11100018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100018.value: In general, the memory encoding and consolidation is initially mediated by the hippocampus (HPC), followed by slow, eventual long-term memory storage in the neocortex. In this way, humans are able to form coherent knowledge frameworks called “mental schemas”. In the current proposal, we establish a rat model to monitor schemas paired associates (PAs) learning and memory retrieval. We will show that the schema acquisition of six PAs (flavor cues and locations) are gradually established. Then, rats learn two new paired-associates that will be encoded and assimilated into the “existing schema” rapidly. The role of HPC and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in different time points of encoding, consolidation and memory recall will be clarified. Using our well established visceral hypersensitive (VH) rat model, we will identify whether the impaired memory in VH state is due to the disruption of encoding, consolidation and (or) the impaired retrieval of stored memory. The dysregulation of schema-linked interactions between HPC and ACC associated with impaired schemas memories will be characterized. To characterize the interactions between the medial prefrontal cortex and the hippocampus, and to elucidate how schema and novelty can facilitate pattern identification after initial encoding, we will perform simultaneous recording of HPC and ACC neural firings and local field potential (LFP) in behavioral animal. Further, the potentiated spike-field coherence (SFC) within HPC and ACC, and increases in the coherent ACC spikes and HPC theta upon PAs learning will be clarified. We plan to demonstrate that memory task-related neuronal spiking patterns are spontaneously “replayed” in the post-encoding period. Moreover, following new PAs training, novelty reactivated the existing schema in the HPC which in turn repossessed ACC phase locking to hippocampal theta LFP, and increased SFC within the ACC suggesting parallel cortical encoding of schema is simultaneously driven in a “bottom-up” manner by the HPC and by the activation of prior knowledge already encoded in cortex. As Reviewers recommended, we added a new Objective to focus on examining the role of astrocyte-neuronal lactate signaling in modulating schematic learning and memory. We expect to confirm that optogenetic stimulation of astrocytes could release lactate, which is able to facilitate neuronal network functions and rescue the impaired schematic memory retrieval under chronic visceral pain state. This finding could hold great promise for the development of novel therapeutics for memory deficits in the chronic pain. 新形成的记忆在海马中编码并得到巩固，随后转化為长时记忆并存储于新皮质。基于这种方式，人类能够在大脑神经网络中形成称为“記憶模式”的知识框架。 在本研究中，我们建立了一种检测配对型 (Paired Associations PAs）学习,鞏因和记忆的大鼠模型。 我们将展示老鼠通过一段時閒學習一系列(六對)食物的嗅,味覺和食物位置之相關, 便能逐步地建立記憶模式，然后，當該動物学习两个新的配对关联時，新的配對之學習及記憶可被快速编码并同化在现有記億图式之中. 我们将阐明海马（HPC）和前扣带皮层（ACC）在记忆编码，巩固和提取等不同时间点的作用。應用我们久巳創建的内脏超过敏 (visceral hypersensitive VH）大鼠模型，我们将研究VH大鼠的记忆受损是否由于阻断學習编码,巩固,或同時伴有记忆提取的障礙. 并進而阐明海马（HPC）与前扣带皮层（ACC）之间的神經元電生理活動的相互協同障礙與行溈記憶模式受损的关系。 为進一步研究内侧前额叶皮质和海马之间的相互作用，并探索巳确立的記憶模式如何促进新的配對學習,和記憶， 我们将在行为学实验的同时记录大鼠海马和前扣带皮层神经元的動作電位及局部场电位（LFP), 並進而分析HPC场电位和ACC动作電位的相關性（SFC).并証實在配對學習,鞏固及重喚記憶過程中ACC动作峰电位及HPC theta波的局部场电位之相關性明顯增加。 本研究将探討學習记忆相关的神经元放电模式在编码后的休止期会自发地重新顯現。更重要的是，短暫的新的配對关联學習后会重新激活海马(HPC)原先已确立的神經元活動模式, 進而再導致海马theta场电位与ACC動作電位的時相锁定，并增強ACC自身动作電位 ̶ 场电位的相關性. 總結以上發現: 那些與已儲存的記憶模式相關的新的學習,記憶之所以能被快速编码并同化在现有記億图式中, 較快地運作是基於海马(HPC) 神經元“自下而上”地重新被激活,同時,記憶模式中已储存於前扣带皮层（ACC)中的知识密碼被冉驱动同时協同作用。 我们將進一步拓展我们的工作，研究星形胶质细胞 ̶̶ 神经元乳酸信号调节在“記憶模式”的形成及運作中的作用。我们將使用光遗传刺激星形胶质细胞並释放乳酸,乳酸可促进腦神经网络的同步協同功能，从而減緩或治癒内脏高敏感大鼠已受损的记忆功能。这一原創性发现,無疑可为治疗慢性疼痛所伴随记忆缺陷带来新的希望。

11100018.label: Realisation of objectives
11100018.value: 1. Utilizing a multiple paired association (PA) behavioral paradigm, we dynamically recorded calcium signals of CA1-ACC projection neurons and ACC neurons during schema formation (Objective 1). The paired associate (PA) behavioral paradigm has been developed to test schematic learning and memory consolidation in rats via the association between place cue and flavored food pellets. The acquisition performance of PAs was measured by performance index (PI). The non-rewarded probe tests (PT) were performed to test the schematic memory retrieval, which was measured by calculating the percentage digging time (dig time %) at the cued location and the percentage digging time at the non-cued locations. Our data are consistent with previous findings that, over the course of training, rats use spatial memory to find the correct flavored food location. We demonstrated that the hippocampus is necessary for the encoding of new PAs and for memory retrieval within a certain time window—24 h following new PA consolidation. The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) plays a critical role in dynamic PA learning and consolidation during training sessions, and is also essential in schema representation and activation. We examine the feature of CA1 ACC interaction during the development and establishment of memory schemas. Fiber photometry studies were performed to assess the Ca2+ signal level in CA1 and ACC, correlating the CA1/ACC activity with PA training in freely behaving rats. Results of recorded calcium signals showed that CA1-ACC projecting neurons excitation gradually decreased along with schema development, while ACC neurons revealed an excitation peak in the middle stage of schema development. 2. CA1 astrocyte Gi pathway activation impairs schema mediated memory acquisition and expression (Objective 1). To specially modulate CA1 astrocyte Gi pathway activation, we employed an AAV2/9 carrying hM4Di fused to mCherry under the control of the astrocytic GFAP promoter. We showed that CA1 astrocytic Gi pathway activation disrupted memory schema development by reducing CA1-ACC projection neuron recruitment in the initial stage and prevented both CA1-ACC projection neurons and ACC neuron excitation in the middle stage. CA1 astrocytes Gi were found to markedly suppress new PA assimilation into the established memory schema. We also showed that CA1 astrocyte Gi activation significantly suppresses new PA assimilation into memory schema in the late stage. 3. Electrophysiological studies in the chronic visceral hypersensitivity (VH) rat model (Objective 2). Multiple-channel electrophysiology recordings were performed. The spike-theta phase distribution of an ACC single unit recorded in VH rats showed desynchronization in the ACC to basolateral amygdala (BLA) neural circuitry. Moreover, activating astrocytic Gq pathway rescued the desynchronization in ACC-BLA circuitry and the impaired decision-making in rats with chronic VH. 4. We performed in vivo microdialysis in the ACC and detected the L-lactate levels in rats with visceral pain-related aversive states. (Objective 3). At this stage we have not completed the study of impairment of schematic memory retrieval in the visceral pain state. However, we showed that multiple paired association (PA) training led to a substantial increase in the extracellular lactate concentration in the ACC. Compared to the untrained group, L-lactate level remained at the baseline. In separate study, we also showed increases of ACC extracellular L-lactate at four consecutive visceral pain-related conditioning training days associated with the establishment of pain aversive memory. These data suggest that the involvement of astrocytic lactate signaling in the modulation of visceral pain aversive memory. Furthermore, local exogenous infusion of lactate into the ACC enhances chronic visceral pain aversive memory and induces the expression of the memory-related plasticity genes pCREB, CREB, and Erk1/2. Pharmacological experiments revealed that the glycogen phosphorylation inhibitor 1,4-dideoxy-1,4-imino-D-arabinitol (DAB) impairs memory consolidation. Moreover, we studied the correlation between astrocyte-neuronal lactate signaling, brain network synchrony and schema memory. The rescue group (CA1 astrocyte Gi activation + local infusion of L-lactate) learned the new PAs within a single PA training session and retrieved the memory of the new PAs during PT4 as evidenced by the significantly higher digging time spent at the correct new cued location. This result confirmed that the rescue group was able to develop the associative schema and assimilate the new PAs into the existing schema in a single trial if CNO+L- lactate is given during the PA training session (S19). However, PT4 without concurrent L-lactate administration showed impaired memory retrieval consistent with the results of PT2 and PT3 of this group, further supporting that ACC astrocytic Gi activation impairs memory retrieval and exogenous L-lactate administration can rescue the retrieval impairment. 5. Using a chronic visceral hypersensitivity (VH) rat model, we characterized the decrease of myelin basic protein, the reduced number of mature oligodendrocytes (OLs), and the hypomyelination in the anterior cingulate cortex. The results of the Rat Gambling Test showed impaired decision-making, and the results of electrophysiological studies showed desynchronization in the ACC to basolateral amygdala (BLA) neural circuitry. These data indicate that ACC hypomyelination is an important component of impaired cognitive performance and ACC neural network desynchronization in the chronic visceral pain state (Objective 2) 6. L-lactate administration increases expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defense (Objective 3). We demonstrated that L-lactate treatment increased level of several proteins including SIRT3, PGC-1α, ATPB, Cyt-c in the neuron of the rat hippocampus and increases mtDNA copy number, which are key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defense. OXR1 mitigates the deleterious effects of oxidative damage in neurons by inducing a resistance response against oxidative stress. 7. Increased myelination may facilitate activated schema model of systems level consolidation (Objective 1). We report for the first time that schematic prolonged multiple PA learning and memory retrieval performances impact myelination by regulating oligodendrocyte (OL) proliferation and differentiation, and are associated with oligodendrogenesis and adaptive myelination within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) network. Furthermore, we determined that ACC demyelination could disrupt schema-like memory formation and retrieval suggesting that myelination is necessary for acquiring schematic learning and memory formation and consolidation. Electrophysiological recordings were performed to examine the role of myelination in ACC band power and spike-field coherence (SFC) and phase-locking. (Hasan, M.,Kanna,et al & Li, Y. Schema-like learning and memory consolidation acting through myelination. FASEB J. 33, 000–000 (2019). Finally, using a chronic visceral hypersensitivity rat model we showed that astrocytic Gq-modulation through expression of hM3Dq facilitated oligodendrocyte progenitor cell proliferation and OL differentiation, and enhanced ACC myelination in rats.

11100018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100018.value: First, we revealed how the neural circuits in CA1-ACC are modulated by CA1 astrocytes during schema establishment. We showed the dynamic information flow in CA1-ACC projecting neurons and ACC neuron activities during schema establishment. The excitation of CA1-ACC projecting neurons decreased along with schema development, while ACC neurons revealed an excitation peak in the middle stage. Through the chemogenetic activation of CA1 astrocytic Gi pathway, we found that schema memory development is disrupted by reducing CA1-ACC projection neuron recruitment in the initial stage and preventing both CA1-ACC projection neurons and ACC neuron excitation in the middle stage (Part C 8. No.1). Moreover, we showed how ACC astrocytes modulate schematic learning via L-Lactate signalling. Activating the ACC astrocytic Gi pathway disrupts schema memory development. We found that ACC astrocytes Gi activation decreases the L-lactate level, reducing neuronal mitochondrial biogenesis and impairing schema memory formation. We also showed that the L-lactate mediating the neuronal mitochondrial biogenesis requires MCT2 and NMDAR activity. With the exogenous L-lactate administration in ACC, the impairment of schema learning and memory retrieval could be rescued (Part C 8. No.2). We also revealed that the exogenous L-Lactate administration increases the expression of SIRT3, PGC-1α, ATPB, Cyt-c in the neurons of the rat hippocampus and increases mtDNA copy number expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defence (Part C 8. No.4). Besides, we found that ACC astrocytes play critical roles in regulating cognitive learning during the chronic visceral pain state. In pain-related aversive learning, we found that ACC astrocytes Gi activation in visceral hypersensitivity (VH) rats before CPA training decreases the lactate level and suppresses pain-related aversive learning. It indicates that astrocytic L-lactate is important in aversive learning and memory retrieval in VH. The L-lactate administration in ACC enhances pain-related aversive learning. It induces the expression of the plasticity-related immediate early genes in the ACC (Part C 8. No.3). Also, we found that hypomyelination and suppressing oligodendrogenesis in ACC occurred in VH rats. The Rat Gambling Test studies showed the impairment of decision-making, and the electrophysiological studies showed the desynchronization in the ACC to BLA neural circuitry in VH rats. Activating ACC astrocytes Gq pathway in VH rats rescued the impaired decision-making and VH-induced desynchronization in ACC-BLA by promoting oligodendrogenesis and remyelination. These results indicate that ACC astrocytes may modulate oligodendrocytes during the chronic visceral pain state (Part C 8. No.5).

11100018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100018.value: We showed that chronic pain disrupts the synchrony of the HPC-ACC neural circuit and causes deficits of cognitive functions (refer to part 7). Our series of findings indicate that astrocytes play a crucial role in the modulation of neuronal activity, circuitry synchrony and myelin plasticity. Astrocytes regulate the release of neurotransmitters and energy substrates such as lactate, which are considered to be involved in learning and memory. Changes in the size and density of astrocytes and reactive astrocytes in ACC and CA1 has been clarified. In addition to our research recent findings in neural-glia interaction, we have also clarified the influence of astrocyte–oligodenrdrocyte signaling in promoting myelination. Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease. A1 reactive astrocytes, neural circuit dysfunction, hypomyelination and dysregulation of glia molecular signaling have all been shown to have a relationship to the AD cognitive deficits. Based on our knowledge and advanced experimental setting, two AD models, 5xFAD and 3-Tg AD mice are applied to characterize the behavioral impairment, reactive astrocytes and myelination deficits. Optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulation of astrocytes will be performed to examine the modulation of brain neuronal network and improving cognitive performances in AD.

11100018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100018.value: Learning of new information was found to be more rapidly assimilated in the presence of schema, a framework of previously acquired knowledge and experiences. We investigated the learning and memory ability of animal models by using the paired association behavioral paradigm to mimic the schematic learning and memory in humans. We showed that the schematic learning is dependent on the dynamic interaction between the hippocampus (HPC) and the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) neurons in rats. The new information is encoded in HPC and then transferred to ACC for storage. We also revealed how astrocytes modulate neural activity to facilitate learning and memory. Astrocytic L-Lactate is responsible for supporting neural activity by acting as neural energy source and as a signalling molecule. Second, we showed that astrocytes promote myelin formation that in turn ameliorates the rate of neural signal transmission and enhances circuitry synchrony and cognitive function. These findings give the potential directions for the study of Alzheimer’s Diseases and its association with reactive astrogliosis, demyelination and cognitive deficits. We plan to perform a series of studies to manipulate astrocytes using in optogenetic and chemogenetic tools to clarify that lactate transport is essential rescuing memory loss in AD patients.

11100218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100218.value: RNA G-四鏈體（rG4）結構在許多基本生物學過程中起關鍵作用，包括轉錄，共轉錄和轉錄後事件的調節。新出現的數據表明rG4s與人類疾病和癌症有關，使rG4成為一個有趣的結構基序，而rG4生物學是一項吸引人的研究熱門話題。 rG4結構的知識 - 特別是它們在轉錄組中的形成及其與順式調控元件的相互作用 - 是進一步探索rG4生物學及其在基礎和應用生物科學中的重要意義的重要方面。 多年來，我們的團隊一直處於調查rG4結構和功能的前沿。最近，我們開發了SHALiPE，DMSLiPE和rG4-seq來檢測轉錄特異性和轉錄組範圍內的rG4，其中數據提供了rG4在人類轉錄組中的普遍性和位置的獨特見解。此外，我們已經進行功能測定以研究rG4s在非翻譯區（UTR）的作用，並證明UTR處的rG4可以抑制翻譯。在這個項目中，我們將改進這些技術以檢測人和小鼠轉錄組中的rG4結構，檢查哺乳動物物種的rG4保守性，評估rG4位點和microRNA（miRNA）靶位點之間的關係，並研究其結構和功能作用。 miRNA中的rG4s靶位點可訪問性和翻譯。與Ting Fung Chan教授合作，將開發新的生物信息學算法來分析rG4-seq數據，這將實現跨轉錄組的rG4的穩健評分和進化分析，以及建立它們與miRNA靶位點的關聯。 一種特異性感興趣的rG4候選物位於APP的3'UTR，這是與阿爾茨海默病相關的基因。使用SHALiPE和DMSLiPE的優化版本，APP RNA的3'UTR處的結構將被表徵以進一步研究rG4和miRNA靶位點之間的串擾，以及其對基因表達的影響。與Andrew Grimson教授合作，將進行廣泛的功能測定以揭示rG4在miRNA介導的翻譯調節中的作用。還將研究如上所述的其他有趣的3'UTR rG4。 通過結合我們在各個領域的跨學科專業知識和獨特經驗，我們相信所提議的項目將揭示新的和重要的發現，將揭示rG4在轉錄後調控中的機製作用，並推進我們對rG4生物學及其的知識醫學意義。

11100218.label: Realisation of objectives
11100218.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives and reported original research findings, and in addition to that, during the course of this project period, we have obtained new research insights that led us to explore a few associated ideas on RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s) (see section 6.1), which altogether yielded a number of high-quality research outputs, and these results are useful for further development of the research in our lab and the related research communities (See section 6.2). In summary, we have published 30 publications, including papers in prestigious journals including Nature Communications (IF 17.69), Nature Protocol (IF 17.021), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 19.16), Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 16.82), Briefings in Bioinformatics (IF 11.622), Genome Biology (IF 17.906), Chemical Science (IF 9.969), ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces (IF 10.383), Cell Reports (IF 9.995), Analytical Chemistry (IF 8.008), Chemical Communications (IF 6.222), etc. Moreover, several awards/patents have been received, several invited talks have been given, a few PhDs have been mentored, several undergraduates have been trained, strong collaboration networks have been established with top institutions in Hong Kong and around the globe, and we have received some press and media coverage (see part C). With regards to research findings and realization of objectives, we have performed rG4 computational prediction and analyzed transcriptome-wide rG4-seq experimental data, and examined the formation and roles of rG4 on messenger RNAs (mRNAs). In particular, we studied the formation of an rG4 within the 3’untranslated regions (3’UTR) of amyloid precursor protein (APP) transcript, which is linked to Alzheimer’s disease. We performed biophysical assays to understand the rG4’s topology and thermostability, structure probing assays to report the structural feature of rG4 at single nucleotide resolution, and cell imaging assays to demonstrate rG4 formation in human cells. Notably, we have also designed different rG4 wildtype and mutant constructs in the luciferase reporter gene system to study the functional role of this APP 3’UTR rG4 and illustrated that it acts as a translational repressor in human cells. UV-melting assays indicated that the translation activity depends on the rG4 thermostability. In a separate study, using rG4-SELEX invented by our lab, we have developed a novel L-RNA aptamer that strongly and specifically recognizes the APP 3’UTR rG4 motif, which in turn suppressed the APP reporter gene and native transcript translation in cells. This result showcased the potential of controlling APP gene expression via targeting the 3’UTR rG4 motif. In plants, we have characterized the rG4 region on 3’UTR of HIRD11 and showed that it serves as an important translational regulator of plant development and growth. Using rG4-seq and SHALiPE-seq, we also reported that hundreds of rG4 structures are strongly folded in Arabidopsis and rice, providing substantial evidence of rG4 formation in living eukaryotic cells for the first time. The nucleotide composition analysis of transcriptomes across 1000 plants (1KP) and their corresponding habitats allowed us to find plants growing in cold climates have G-enriched transcriptomes. Immunofluorescence detection and in vivo structure profiling verified the rG4 formation in plants is globally enhanced in response to cold, and cold-responsive rG4s in the 3′-UTR serve as mRNA stabilizers and delay mRNA decay. We also assessed the formation of an rG4 within the 5’untranslation regions (5’UTR) of Adenosine deaminase acting on RNAs (ADAR) transcript, which is responsible for the editing of RNA and its dysregulation has been associated with cancers. Similarly, we first performed biophysical assays, structure probing, and cell imaging to report the structure feature of this 5’UTR rG4. We then designed rG4 wildtype and mutant constructs in the reporter gene, as well as native transcript to assess the function of rG4, and discovered the down-regulatory role of this rG4 in cells. To investigate the potential binding partners of this rG4, we tested on one of the well-studied rG4 proteins, DHX36, and found that it can bind and unwind ADAR 5’UTR. The in-cell rG4-DHX36 interaction was confirmed by the GTFH (G-quadruplex-triggered fluorogenic hybridization) probes in the DHX36 knockout cells. We also compared the native protein level expressed in DHX36 knockdown and knockout cell lines to verify that DHX36 unwinds ADAR 5’UTR rG4 in cells and regulates gene expression in an rG4-dependent manner. In mouse, we have characterized the 5’UTR rG4 in the Gnai2 mRNA and showed that DHX36 regulates the translation of Gnai2 mRNA by unwinding its 5’UTR rG4 structures and identifying GNAI2 as a downstream effector of DHX36 for skeletal stem cell function. Collectively, as these UTR rG4s are important for gene regulation, they are promising structural targets for controlling their protein production and may be targeted in the future for biological applications. We have also conducted studies to map and characterize CDS rG4s in other biological systems. For bacteria, we have characterized 2 rG4 candidates, bswR and hemL at the CDS region, and found that rG4 plays key regulatory roles in bacterial pathogenicity and metabolic pathways. We also reported that rG4s can be detected in a wide range of bacterial species. For plasmodium, we have characterized the rG4 formation in Rad54 and Ap2 genes and found that the detected rG4s were mostly located in the CDS region in P. falciparum transcriptome of protein-coding genes. We also reported that rG4s control the translation of P. falciparum genes, demonstrating that rG4 can have a functional role in species with highly AT-rich genome/transcriptome (~80% for P. falciparum). These examples clearly indicated the formation and roles of rG4 in different biological systems, underscoring that rG4 has evolutionary and functional role in gene regulation. These findings also provide a repertoire of CDS rG4s for further structural and functional characterization. Last but not the least, as the SAR-CoV2 occurred in late 2019, we predicted rG4 formation in this RNA virus, found about 20 putative rG4, and performed biophysical assays to verify a few cases. In particular, we focused on the top-ranked putative rG4-forming sequences at positions 13385 and 24268 which were shown to form rG4 in vitro, and we reported that they interacted with the nsp13 viral helicase. This finding should provide attractive approaches for inhibiting the pandemic-causing virus via targeting viral rG4s or helicases. Besides coding mRNAs, we also investigated the formation and role of rG4s in non-coding RNAs. Using comparative sequence and biophysical analysis, we reported that MALAT1 lncRNA contains conserved rG4 motifs, forming thermostable rG4 structures with parallel topology. We also showed that rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNA can interact with NONO protein with high specificity and affinity in vitro and in nuclear cell lysate, and we also provided cellular data to support that NONO protein recognizes MALAT1 lncRNA via rG4 motifs. Notably, we demonstrated that rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNA can be targeted by the rG4-specific small molecule, peptide, and L-aptamer, leading to the dissociation of MALAT1 rG4-NONO protein interaction. Altogether, this study uncovered new and important rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNAs, revealed their specific interactions with NONO protein, offered multiple strategies for targeting MALAT1 and its RNA–protein complex via its rG4 structure, and illustrated the prevalence and significance of rG4s in ncRNAs. Also, by using computational prediction, we found a dozen of rG4s were identified in lncRNAs, providing lncRNAs rG4 candidates for future studies.

11100218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100218.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows: First, we determined the formation of rG4 within the 3’UTR of APP transcript and illustrated that it has an important function in suppressing APP translation, providing a target for controlling APP production. This work was published in Chemical Science (IF 9.969). We have invented rG4-SELEX and applied this to develop an L-RNA aptamer that can control APP translation via targeting APP 3’UTR rG4 motif. These works were published in Nature Protocols (IF 17.021) and ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces (IF 10.383). Second, we have demonstrated rG4 formation in 5’UTR of ADAR1 transcript using multi-disciplinary assays. rG4 helicase DHX36, was found to bind and unwind this 5’UTR rG4, which in turn can regulate the ADAR1 protein translation. This work was published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 16.82). Third, we profiled rG4 formation in human, bacteria, plant, plasmodium, and mouse, and detected hundreds to thousands of rG4s. We also showcased the post-transcriptional and/or translation role of several nominated rG4 examples located in the CDS or UTRs. These works were published in Mbio (IF 7.867), Genome Biology (IF 17.906), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 19.16), Nature Communications (IF 17.69), BMC biology (IF 7.364) respectively. We have also predicted the rG4s in the SARS-CoV2 RNA viral genome, and showed that they interacted with viral helicase, which provides potential approaches for inhibiting the virus. This work was published in Briefings in Bioinformatics (IF 11.622). Last, we identified rG4s in long non-coding RNA MALAT1, revealed their interactions with NONO protein, and offered multiple strategies for targeting MALAT1 and its RNA–protein complex via its rG4 structure. This work was published in Nucleic Acid Research (IF 19.16). Our findings and reputations have attracted journals to invite us to write reviews, and we have highlighted the above-mentioned major findings and acknowledged the RGC funding in these publications, including Trends in Biochemical Sciences (IF 14.264), Trends in Biotechnology (IF 21.942), Nucleic Acid Research (IF 19.16), Science China Life Sciences (IF 10.372), etc. All info can be found in part C. Other relevant research activities: We have also published other research articles, including Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 16.82), Nucleic Acid Research (IF 19.16), Cell Reports (IF 9.995), Analytical Chemistry (IF 8.008), Chemical Communications (IF 6.222), and etc, on research topics that are relevant to this project, and acknowledged the RGC funding. All info can be found in part C.

11100218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100218.value: There are at least 3 potentials for further development of the research. First, from an earlier study we have identified thousands of rG4s in the mRNA, however, only a handful of cases were studied so far. In the near future, we will investigate other rG4s in the mRNA on our list and explore their formation and role in cells. Also, we plan to examine the protein interacting partners of APP 3’UTR rG4 and decipher the molecular basis of this rG4-mediated regulatory mechanism. Similarly, other 3’ UTR rG4s can be explored and investigated using the strategies we developed. Second, we have showcased 5’UTR, CDS, lncRNA rG4 examples from this project, and next we plan to investigate more rG4 candidates in these mRNAs and lncRNAs, and examine their effect on translation, ribosome frameshifting, and splicing, protein interacting partners and their underlying biochemical mechanisms. Last, with these rG4 being demonstrated to have a critical role in cells, we plan to develop novel rG4 targeting toolsets to achieve gene control via selective recognition of the rG4 of interest. These are ongoing research in my laboratory, and once promising preliminary data are generated, we will apply for funding support in RGC and other agencies.

11100218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100218.value: G-rich sequences in RNA can form interesting structure motifs referred as RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s), and in this research project, we have investigated rG4s in different regions of messenger RNA (mRNAs), and through the experiments performed, we illustrated their formation and roles in human, mouse, and plant cells. As some of these mRNAs, such as APP, and ADAR1 rG4, are associated with diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease and cancers, these findings supported that untranslated regions (UTRs) rG4 can be a key RNA structural element to regulate translation, and rG4 in mRNAs can be a promising drug target for preventing and controlling disease development. We also reported rG4 formation and functions in different parts of mRNAs and non-coding RNAs in human, mouse, plant, plasmodium, bacteria, and virus, demonstrating that rG4s are ubiquitous across the tree of life. As research on rG4 is currently unexplored, our new data open new doors for future studying and understanding of rG4s’ functions in biology and diseases, which will stimulate further development in biological and biomedical applications.

11100318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100318.value: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide results in neurological deficits. TBI is a progressive disorder that worsens over time due largely to secondary injury occurs days after irreversible mechanical primary injury. Therapeutic intervention therefore focuses on limiting secondary damage caused by inflammatory response that persists for months to years after TBI. Microglia are innate immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS) that possess a double-edge sword function, and play key roles in secondary damage. Following TBI, activated microglia acquire heterogeneous phenotypes namely M1 or M2 microglia secreting cytokines/chemokines either exacerbate (M1) or limit (M2) tissue damage. M1 microglia secrete pro-inflammatory cytokines (neurotoxic). M2 microglia not only produce anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors that are neuroprotective, but also displace increase capacity in chemotaxis and phagocytosis. Unlike the persistent M1 activation of microglia, activation of M2 microglia is transient that phases out within days after TBI. Therefore, there is an urge to develop therapy direct at shifting pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 microglia, to improve neurological function recovery after TBI. Low-dose ionizing radiation (LDIR) such as X-ray enhances adaptive response such as average life expectancy extension, stimulation of immune system, wound healing, cell growth stimulation and neuroprotection in animal models of neurodegenerative diseases, primarily due to immunomodulation. LD X-ray increases anti-inflammatory cytokine production and chemotaxis in human macrophages. LD X-ray (radiotherapy) has been used for decades in treating patients with arthritis. To test the hypothesis that LD X-ray promotes M1 to M2 phenotypic switch after TBI, our results showed that LD X-ray induced upregulation of mRNA expression of M2 markers, a panel of neurotrophic factors, and genes involved in phagocytosis, while keeping the expression of M1 markers unchanged in cultured mouse microglia. In vivo promoting effect of LD X-ray was confirmed by showing increased microglial cell density near the injury site, increased neuronal survival, reduced glial scar, and faster wound healing after TBI in adult and postnatal mice. Current proposal aims to study in vivo functional recovery of TBI mice after LD X-ray irradiation. We first plan to identify the optimal irradiation strategy (partial irradiation of head) to induce maximal motor and cognitive recovery tested by neurobehavioral tests. We will also identify key cytokines/chemokines responsible for the beneficial effect of LD X-ray irradiation by in vivo microdialysis. Our ultimate goal is to establish a microglia-based therapy for TBI and other CNS disorders. 創傷性腦損傷（TBI）是全球致命及引致傷殘的主要原因之一，亦會導致神經功能缺陷。TBI是一種會持續惡化疾病：患者會因受到不可逆轉的機械性原發性損傷所引致的繼發性損傷，隨著時間的推移而惡化下去。因此，介入治療主要集中限制由持續數月至數年不等的炎症反應所引起的繼發性損傷。微膠細胞是中央神經系統裹的先天性免疫細胞，其功能像把雙刃劍，並於繼發性損傷中起了關鍵作用。在TBI之後，微膠細胞會被活化，隨之而獲得異質表現型（即謂M1或M2微膠細胞），並分泌細胞因子或趨化因子，而這些分泌會加劇（M1）抑或限制（M2）組織損傷。M1微膠細胞會分泌具神經毒性的促炎性細胞因子。M2微膠細胞不單分泌保護神經系統的抗炎性細胞因子及神經營養因素，而且具有更強的趨化性和吞噬作用能力。與持續被活化的M1微膠細胞不同，活化M2微膠細胞只會短暫存在，更會於TBI後的數天內慢慢消失。因此有逼切的需要去研究一個治療去把促炎性的M1微膠細胞轉至M2微膠細胞，從而促進TBI後神經功能恢復。 低劑量電離輻射，如X-射線，可增強適應性反應，例如：延長平均壽命、刺激免疫系統、促進傷口癒合和細胞生長、與及於神經退行性疾病的動物模型中對神經系統起保護作用，而其主因是通過對免疫系統進行調節。於人類的巨噬細胞中，低劑量的X-射線增加抗炎性細胞因子的生產及提高趨化性。低劑量的X-射線放射治療亦在數十年前已經於關節炎患者身上開始使用。 為了驗證低劑量的X-射線於TBI後能促進M1至M2的表型轉換這個假設，我們的結果顯示，於培養的小鼠微膠細胞中，低劑量的X-射線能提高M2標記、一組神經營養因子與及參與吞噬作用的信使核糖核酸表達量，而M1標記的表達量則維持不變。而低劑量X-射線的於體內的促進作用，則通過成年及初生小鼠於TBI後，在損傷部位附近的微膠細胞密度增加、神經元存活量增加，神經膠質疤痕減少和傷口癒合速快更快得以證實。 目前的計劃書旨在研究低劑量X-射線對 TBI後的小鼠於體內功能恢復上的影響。我們首先計劃通過神經行為測試來制定一個最佳的照射策略（頭部的局部照射），以達至最大運動和認知功能恢復。我們還會通過體內微透析分析技術來鑑別引致低劑量X-射線有益效果的關鍵細胞因子或趨化因子。我們最終的目標是建立一個以微膠細胞為基礎的治療方案去醫治TBI及其他中央神經系統疾病。

11100318.label: Realisation of objectives
11100318.value: All Objectives were completed. Figures and References are attached in Part C/Section 11 (Low-resolution images were provided due to file size limit). Objective 1.1. was completed and described in the mid-term report (Figs. 1-8). We performed additional experiments to examine if LD X-ray irradiation exhibited neuroprotective effects on a very severe mouse model (irreversible motor deficits )of traumatic brain injury (TBI) by photothrombotic lesion using Rose Bengal (1) (Fig. 9A), which severely damaged the motor cortex (M1 and M2) and the somatosensory area (S1) (Fig. 9B-C). Compared to sham irradiation, X-ray irradiation robustly reduced the wound area by 63% (Fig. 10A). The mean infarct volume (as detected by TTC staining) was markedly reduced in the X-ray-irradiated mice at 1 and 3 dpi (Fig. 10B-C). Also, X-ray-irradiated mice showed a 43-51% reduction of mean infarct volume (as evaluated by magnetic resonance imaging) at 1-7 dpi compared with the sham-irradiated controls (Fig. 10D), demonstrating the therapeutic potential of LD X-ray irradiation in treating TBI and ischemic stroke. Objective 1.2 was completed and described in the mid-term report (Fig. 11). We performed additional experiments to assess motor function recovery after photothrombotic lesion, sham-irradiated mice developed motor deficits that persisted throughout the testing period of 8 weeks (Fig. 12A-B). Strikingly, X-ray-irradiated stroke mice were able to cross the elevated narrow beam at 1 dpi and took only 14 days to return to the baseline latency (Fig. 12C). The number of foot-slip errors was dramatically increased in the sham-irradiated controls compared to X-ray-irradiated mice at 1-7 dpi (Fig. 12D). For pole climbing test, much to our surprise, the time for X-ray-irradiated mice to climb down the pole completely returned to the baseline value within 7 days after stroke. In contrast, sham-irradiated mice struggled to climb down the pole and displayed a significant prolongation of descending latency compared with X-ray-irradiated mice (Fig. 12E-F). At 28 dpi, the grip strength of X-ray-irradiated mice returned to the baseline level and remained unchanged until 56 dpi. In contrast, the sham-irradiated mice were not able to return to baseline level (Fig. 12G-H). Objective 1.3. To assess whether the improved motor functional recovery in LD X-ray-irradiated mice required microglia, we performed intracerebroventricular and intraperitoneally injections of liposomal clodronate to deplete microglia in the motor cortex (2, 3) before we induced stroke in the adult mice (Fig. 13A). In the absence of microglia, LD X-ray-irradiated mice failed to cross the elevated narrow beam during the first 3 days after stroke induction, and developed persistent motor deficits similar to the sham-irradiated mice (Fig. 13B). They took significantly longer time to transverse the narrow beam throughout the entire 2-month testing period, compared with their baseline values before induction of photothrombotic stroke (Fig. 13C). After the photothrombotic stroke, number of foot-slip errors was dramatically increased in the sham-irradiated controls. LD X-ray-irradiated mice with microglia depletion performed equally bad as sham-irradiated counterparts in making frequent foot slip errors 2 months after stroke induction (Fig. 13D). For pole climbing test, microglia-depleted mice spent most of the time at the top of the pole during the first 3 days after stroke and X-ray irradiation (Fig. 13E), and were unable to return to their baseline descending latency (Fig. 13F). Sham-irradiated microglia-depleted and X-ray-irradiated microglia-depleted mice displayed similar low spontaneous recovery of grip strength (Fig. 13G-H), indicating the absence of microglia completely abolishes the beneficial effect of X-ray irradiation. Objective 2. We first examined the molecular dynamics of microglia chemotaxis and phagocytosis after LD X-ray irradiation by qPCR analysis. In LDIR-treated mice, we observed a significant reduction in mRNA expression in several M1 markers (Il-1a, Il-1b, Il-6, Il-12a, Tnf, Cd53, and Cd86) compared with sham-irradiated controls at early time points after ischemic strokes (Figure 14A). In parallel, several M2 markers (Il-4, Il-10, Cd206, and Tgf-b) were up-regulated in LDIR-treated mice. Runx1, a key transcription factor which controls the transition of microglia from amoeboid (activated) state to ramified (resting) state (4) and promoted M1-to-M2 phenotypic switch (5), was significantly elevated only in LDIR-treated mice after ischemic strokes. Clic1, an intracellular ion channel that promoted persistent and chronic inflammatory responses in various neurodegenerative diseases, was significantly down-regulated in LDIR-treated mice after ischemic strokes (Figure 14B). Several chemokines (Ccl2, Ccl6, Ccl9 and Ccl12) also showed significant down-regulation of mRNA expression in LDIR-treated mice after ischemic strokes. The mRNA expression of Regulator of G-protein signaling 1 (Rgs1), a key regulator which controls the resolution of chronic inflammation (6), was markedly attenuated in LDIR-treated mice (Figure 14C). We confirmed our qPCR analysis using Bio-Plex Multiplex Immunoassay System, suggesting a microglial phenotypic switch from a neurotoxic M1 phenotype towards a more neuroprotective M2 phenotype (Figure 15). We validated if low-dose X-ray irradiation could polarize primary mouse microglia towards the M2 phenotype in culture (Figure 16A). X-ray irradiation increased the mRNA expression of several classic M2 markers, including Il-4, Il-10, Tgf-β, Cd206, Ym1 and Ccl-22 without affecting (Tnf-α, Il-1b, Cd32, Cd16, Cd86 and Nos2) or downregulating (Il-6) M1 marker expression (Figure 16B). Our qPCR data are consistent with the results of a previous study on interleukin signalling pathways in that the anti-inflammatory cytokine Il-10 inhibited the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokine Il-6 via activation of the Jak/Stat pathway in X-ray-irradiated microglia (Figure 16C) (7). The protein expression of M2 stimuli, such as IL-4 and IL-10, was significantly upregulated in microglia-conditioned media after X-ray irradiation (Figure 16D). The M2 polarization of X-ray-irradiated microglia was further confirmed by upregulation of a panel of neuroprotective neurotrophic factors and receptors (Igf-1, Irs-1 and Vegf) (Figure 16E) and increased mRNA expression of genes involved in phagocytosis (Mmp2, Mmp9 and Mfge8) (Figure 16F). Exposure of microglia to X-ray irradiation at a dose ranging from 25 mGy to 500 mGy did not have any adverse effects on cell survival (Figure 16G). To validate that X-ray induced M2 polarization, as indicated by enhanced microglial chemotactic and phagocytic capacities, we performed live-cell functional assays to mimic the reactive microglial state observed after injury. Microglial migration in response to ATP, which is a classic chemoattractant released by injured neurons, was measured by a Boyden chamber chemotaxis assay (Figure 17A) (8). Both sham- and X-ray-irradiated microglia responded to ATP by actively moving towards the source of ATP in the lower compartment. Notably, compared to sham irradiation, X-ray irradiation increased the chemotaxis of microglia by 52.9% upon exposure to ATP but had no effect on the basal motility of cultured microglia in the absence of ATP (Figure 17B). To examine the phagocytic capability of these highly mobile microglia after X-ray irradiation, we performed a phagocytosis assay using fluorescent-tagged zymosan particles. We determined the rate at which the zymosan particles were phagocytosed by quantifying the fluorescence intensity of internalized zymosan in microglia after one hour of incubation (Figure 17C). The phagocytic capacity of microglia was assessed based on the average fluorescence intensity of zymosan particles in each IBA-1-positive microglial cell. Compared with sham irradiation, X-ray irradiation enhanced phagocytosis by 23.1% (Figure 17D). We further demonstrated that the increases in microglial chemotactic and phagocytic capacities were not simply due to an increase in the microglial proliferation rate. The number of primary microglia positive for PCNA (a proliferating cell marker) was unchanged between X-ray-irradiated cultures and sham-irradiated controls (9) (Figure 18).

11100318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100318.value: The current study demonstrated for the first time that low-dose (LD) X-ray irradiation markedly accelerated motor function recovery in mouse model of traumatic brain injury (TBI). We first showed that LD X-ray irradiation promoted wound closure in both postnatal and adult mice after cortical stab wound injury. We also confirmed that LD X-ray irradiation significantly reduced the wound size after ischemic stroke by photothrombotic lesion. Compared with sham-irradiated control mice, the mean infarct volume was significantly reduced in LD X-ray-irradiated mice after ischemic stroke as detected by triphenyl tetrazolium chloride staining and magnetic resonance imaging. More strikingly, LD X-ray-irradiated mice displayed remarkable motor function recovery after TBI. The sham-irradiated mice took 28 days to restore motor function completely after TBI and exhibited irreversible motor function deficits after ischemic stroke. Remarkably, LD X-ray-irradiated mice took 7 days to restore to the baseline values of narrow beam walking and pole climbing tests after TBI. For ischemic stroke, LD X-ray-irradiated mice took 14 days to completely reverse the motor coordination impairment as assessed by narrow beam walking and pole climbing test. While sham-irradiated mice displayed significantly lower forelimb and hindlimb grip strength than their baseline values throughout the entire testing period of 56 days, LD X-ray-irradiated mice took 28 days to restore forelimb and hindlimb grip strength to baseline values. We further elucidated the molecular mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of LD X-ray irradiation by RNA-seq. After induction of ischemic stroke, we found that the marker gene expression profile of microglia was markedly elevated in LD X-ray-irradiated mice when compared with their sham-irradiated counterparts. More importantly, we observed a significant down-regulation of key M1 markers and elevated expression of several M2 markers in LD X-ray-irradiated mice. In-depth qPCR analysis and Bio-plex immunoassay confirmed a M1 (pro-inflammatory)-to-M2 (anti-inflammatory) phenotypic switch in microglial polarization, which was consistent with our qPCR and protein analysis on cultured microglia after LD X-ray irradiation. We reasoned those microglia played a crucial role in improving TBI following LD X-ray irradiation. To address this, we depleted microglia in the pre-motor cortex by intracerebroventricular and intraperitoneally injections of liposomal clodronate before we induced TBI in adult mice, and found that all the beneficial effects of LD X-ray irradiation in promoting motor function recovery after stroke were eliminated completely. Finally, we performed a Boyden chamber chemotaxis assay and phagocytosis assay to examine the microglial chemotactic and phagocytic capacities after LD X-ray irradiation. LD X-ray irradiation-induced M2-polarized microglia exhibited enhanced microglial chemotaxis toward ATP (a classic chemoattractant released by injured neurons) and increased phagocytic capacities when compared with sham-irradiated controls. To this end, our proof-of-concept study has provided important pre-clinical evidence that microglia-based therapy is an attractive approach for reversing the progression of functional deficits after TBI and ischemic stroke. One paper was published in top Journals in the area of Neuroscience and one manuscript has been written for submission. Two PhD student (Eugene Xu and Louis Chan) and one postdoc (Bennett Au) are involved and trained in current study. We presented the work at the largest Neuroscience Meeting in the US for two consecutive years (2019-2020). After completion of this study, we filed a patent in the United States Patent and Trademark Office, entitled “Low-Dose Radiation Therapy for Traumatic Brain Injury and Stroke” (reference number US 17/449,959 with its filing date on 23 September 2021).

11100318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100318.value: Our findings here describe a promising approach to achieve full motor function recovery after traumatic brain injury (TBI) by switching microglial polarization using low-dose (LD) X-ray irradiation. Knowledge obtained from this project lays an important conceptual foundation for utilizing anti-inflammatory properties of M2-polarized microglia for severe brain injuries. We believed that our results strongly support the claim that LD X-ray irradiation offers early neuroprotection by limiting the extent of secondary tissue damage (smaller cortical infarct size) results in accelerated motor function recovery at an unprecedented rate after TBI. Further investigation is thus warranted to evaluate the potential clinical application of LD X-ray irradiation on patients with TBI for better motor function recovery. In fact, the clinical success of using LD radiation therapy (0.3-0.7Gy for single dose and 3-10 Gy in total dose) for pain relief and improvement of motor symptoms in treating degenerative osteoarthritis (OA) has been widely used for several decades. The clinical experience of using LD radiation therapy has grown tremendously in recent years regarding its mechanism of action and its low toxicity profile further assures LD radiation therapy as an irreplaceable treatment option for OA patients. Future studies should explore the possibility of developing a portable X-ray irradiator that might offer instant and early intervention to patients with TBI. Additionally, RNA-seq data generated from the current study will certainly initiate new investigations to screen for bioactive small molecules that mimic the protective effects of LD X-ray irradiation using bioinformatic approaches. In general, repurposing an existing FDA-approved drug is regarded as a cost-effective alternative since Phase I clinical trials can be skipped, which makes the existing RNA-seq dataset an attractive tool to the discovery of novel drug targets for TBI.

11100318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100318.value: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is the leading cause of death and disability worldwide, and approximately half of the TBI patients experience lifelong motor impairments and disability. TBI worsens over time due to the secondary tissue injury caused by the microglia-mediated inflammatory responses. Studies focus on pharmacological interventions targeting the complex secondary injury cascades have failed to show efficacy. Here, we demonstrated that a single exposure to low-dose ionizing radiation (LDIR) promoted wound closure and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a significant reduction of infarct volume in LDIR-treated mice after TBI. More strikingly, LDIR completely reversed motor deficits after TBI as demonstrated by a battery of motor function tests. RNA-seq and transcriptomic deconvolution analysis revealed a marked increase in the marker gene profile of microglia in LDIR-treated mice after TBI. In-depth qPCR and protein expression analysis found that LDIR induced M2 microglia polarization characterized by upregulation of M2 neuroprotection- and phagocytosis-related genes and increasing M2 cytokine production. LDIR-induced M2-polarized microglia showed superior chemotactic and phagocytic capability compared with sham-irradiated microglia. Brain microglia depletion completely abolished the beneficial effect of LDIR on motor function recovery in stroke mice. Therapeutic strategy should therefore focus on microglia-based therapy directed at M2 polarization (anti-inflammation).

11100518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100518.value: One increasingly influential idea in neuroscience proposes that one of the most important tasks for the brain is not merely to process incoming sights and sounds, but to predict what will happen next. The brain generates “internal models” of the world that attempt to predict how the imminent future will unfold, and the predictions of the model are constantly compared against new sensory information, and errors in the predictions are flagged to keep the predictions on track with reality and to improve the internal model. Although there is some evidence for this type of “predictive coding”, for example, from bulk brain signals recorded through electrodes on the scalp, as yet there is little examination in single neurons (brain cells). This project will examine the prediction of future sounds which form parts of rhythmic auditory patterns by single neurons recorded in the auditory brains of rats. We will use carefully constructed rhythmic sequences, where, a small, randomly chosen proportion of the sounds deviate from the regular pattern by unpredictable jumps in pitch, duration, loudness or sound source position. Using surface and depth array electrodes we will then identify the location and characteristics of neurons in the animals’ cerebral cortex which register unexpected deviations along each of these perceptual attributes of sound. Predictive coding is now widely thought to be a key principle of brain function, which, if fully understood, could radically improve our capacity to ameliorate sensory deficits. Predictive coding is believed to involve feedback from higher brain areas to lower areas. Some evidence suggests that the auditory system uses predictive adaptation to better encode sounds in noisy environments. Unlike the ear, the action of hearing aids or cochlear implants (remarkable electronic ears that can be surgically implanted to allow hearing in the deaf) does not currently depend on brain activity. With an understanding of predictive neural phenomena, models of these phenomena could be included in the algorithms of hearing prosthetics. 預測編碼是感官大腦的理論，闡述大腦活動會在內部產生代表外界的模型。模型的預測是根據感官的輸入來測量的，而輸入和模型的差異或「誤差」會被最小化，使內部模型與外界的特徵相匹配。儘管有一些證據表明在神經元的總體活動記錄中有預測編碼，例如使用頭皮上的電極，但在單個神經元（腦細胞）層面幾乎沒有研究。對於預測未來刺激的時間尤其如此。此項目將記錄及研究麻醉大鼠腦中的單個神經元活對未來聲音的時間預測。我們將使用精心構造的刺激序列，並在其中小部分隨機選擇的刺激，省略通常在特定時間點發生的特徵，或者令它在不同的時間發生。由於罕見的聲音事件在序列中隨機分散，我們假設它不會被大腦的預測過程預測。因此，代表大腦內部模型（或「誤差」）的神經元應該，對比起在時間上與預期的近似的對照組刺激，出現不同的反應。使用這種方法，我們的目標是精確找出刺激時間的預測編碼中涉及的神經元的位置和特徵。 研究預測編碼的重要之處在於它提供了發掘感知編碼的基本原則的可能性。基本原則影響深遠 — 有如細菌理論對我們治癒疾病的能力的影響。如果充分理解預測編碼這樣的基本原則，我們可以從根本上提高改善感官缺陷的能力，包括聽力缺陷。預測編碼被認為涉及從較高腦區域到較低區域的反饋。一些證據表明，聽覺系統使用預測適應來改善大腦對預期的刺激的編碼 — 這在嘈雜的環境中尤其有用。與耳朵不同，助聽器或人工耳蝸（可以通過手術植入以提供聾人聽力的電子耳朵）的操作目前不能回應大腦的活動。通過對預測神經現象的理解，這些現象的模型可以被編入聽力輔器的演算法中。

11100518.label: Realisation of objectives
11100518.value: Objective 1 was completed. We were able to conduct studies in rodents which tested the auditory cortical signatures of temporal (Auksztulewicz et al., 2023, doi:10.1186/s12915-023-01592-4) and content-based predictions (An et al., 2021a, doi: 10.1016/j.heares.2020.107894) based on simple acoustic stimuli. While these two studies allowed for testing regional specificity of neural signatures of predictions, they were both based on electrophysiological recordings, and the results showed that responses were distributed and heterogeneous rather than forming clear hierarchical gradients. We found a similar pattern of results in an electrophysiological study where content-based predictions were introduced based on repetition of complex stimulus patterns rather than simple acoustic stimuli (Kang et al., 2021, doi: 10.3389/fnins.2021.610978). However, we also tested whether evidence for regional specificity of predictions can be obtained using calcium imaging (Luo et al., 2023; doi: 10.1101/2023.01.18.524413). The latter study showed that higher-order cortical regions (secondary auditory cortex) were uniquely sensitive to more complex forms of content-based and temporal predictions, such that predictable stimulus contents are presented in an unpredictable temporal order. We were also able to substantially build on and extend our findings to decode stimulus predictions from the auditory cortex (Cappotto et al., 2022a, doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.04.022), and show that these decoding effects are modulated by learning (Luo et al., 2021, doi: 10.1016/j.crneur.2021.100019). Objective 2 was partly completed. Our analysis of single-neuron activity accompanying predictions of stimulus timing revealed no significant modulation of activity at the single neuron level, but only at the level of entire populations and field potentials (Auksztulewicz et al., 2023, doi:10.1186/s12915-023-01592-4). As for the analysis of single-neuron activity accompanying predictions of stimulus contents, we have collected a dataset using two-photon calcium imaging which is currently being analyzed. Objective 3, to study the modulation of stimulus-specific adaptation by temporal predictions, is at time of writing largely achieved. All the necessary data have been collected. Data obtained using electroencephalography in humans have been analyzed, uploaded as a preprint (Cappotto et al., 2022b; doi: 10.1101/2022.06.20.496917) and submitted for publication. The results indeed showed that the modulation of prediction error responses by temporal regularity was largely localized to higher-order cortical regions. As for direct cortical recordings in rodents, we have collected two complete datasets - one using electrophysiology, one using calcium imaging - and started the analysis, but publication of these data is not yet completed.

11100518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100518.value: We found robust neural signatures of both content-based (An et al., 2021a, doi: 10.1016/j.heares.2020.107894) and time-based predictions (Auksztulewicz et al., 2023, doi:10.1186/s12915-023-01592-4) in the auditory cortex of rodents, based on simple sequences of repeated stimuli. While these responses were highly comparable to human responses observable in EEG (An et al., 2021b, doi: 10.3389/fnhum.2021.613903), a more detailed analysis of single-neuron activity yielded no evidence for the encoding of time-based predictions and/or errors in spiking activity in the auditory cortex (Auksztulewicz et al., 2023, doi:10.1186/s12915-023-01592-4). This pattern of results brings into the question widely accepted theoretical models of predictive processing, resting on spiking activity, and is instead broadly consistent with alternative accounts resting on dendritic currents. Using more complex stimulus sequences, we found that precise timing of predictable stimulus contents (1) modulates beta-band activity in the auditory cortex in rodents (Kang et al., 2021, doi: 10.3389/fnins.2021.610978); (2) yields prediction error responses in higher-order auditory cortex to temporal violations of stimulus presentation (Luo et al., 2023; doi: 10.1101/2023.01.18.524413); (3) yields successful decoding of prediction contents from the distributed pattern of neural activity in the auditory cortex (Cappotto et al., 2022a, doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.04.022); (4) shows evidence for a boost in decoding following extensive training of rodents exposed to stimulus sequences (Luo et al., 2021, doi: 10.1016/j.crneur.2021.100019). Finally, predictable timing was found to boost mismatch responses to unpredictable stimulus contents, in line with the largely modulatory character of temporal predictions (Cappotto et al., 2022b; doi: 10.1101/2022.06.20.496917). Based on non-invasive data, the interaction between content-based and time-based predictions has been found to be localized largely to higher-order cortical regions, beyond the primary auditory cortex.

11100518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100518.value: Immediate plans involve the completion of the peer-reviewed publication process of submitted preprints (Luo et al., 2023; doi: 10.1101/2023.01.18.524413; Cappotto et al., 2022b; doi: 10.1101/2022.06.20.496917) and of the analysis of collected data (electrophysiological recordings of population activity, and single-neuron two-photon recordings of auditory cortical responses to stimulus-based predictions and their interaction with prediction errors). Beyond that, the studies have generated several important results, specifically in the context of prediction decoding from auditory cortical activity (Cappotto et al., 2022a, doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.04.022). The study found that based on a distributed pattern of activity in response to a neutral impulse, it is possible to decode not only predictions of what stimulus should be currently presented, but also memories of past stimuli. However, the mechanisms of simultaneously encoding memories and predictions in the sensory cortex are not clear. We are currently following up on this finding with a series of studies, including a study in humans using combined EEG and fMRI in which we are testing the involvement of other regions (e.g. the hippocampus) in orchestrating between memory and prediction signalling.

11100518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100518.value: It has been proposed that one of the key functions of the brain is to generate predictions about what and when is likely to occur, and filter incoming sensations through these predictions. However, the neural mechanisms of predictive processing are largely studied using non-invasive recordings in humans, in which activity of millions of neurons is averaged together. In this project, we studied the neural correlates and mechanisms of predicting stimulus contents ("what") and timing ("when") in the rodent auditory cortex. We found that large-scale activity patterns of neurons in the auditory cortex are indeed sensitive to both types of predictions. This enables not only comparisons with human data, but also the decoding of prediction contents from neural activity.

11101518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101518.value: 多重耐藥病原體已對人類健康造成嚴重的威脅。在臨床分離株發現的接合質粒中,抗生素抗性基因通常與移動遺傳元件如插入序列（IS）相關。雖然這種現像已有四十多年的歷史，但IS的調節及其在質粒或細菌中動員和聚集抗生素抗性基因的功能仍不清楚。響應外部刺激而調節細菌基因表達的小RNA是控制某些插入序列轉座的調節方法之一。最近，我們從臨床分離株中分離並測序了幾個攜帶超廣譜β-內酰胺酶基因的多重耐藥病原體質粒，更發現了與轉座酶基因重疊的反義小RNA，其可能調節IS26和ISEcp1的轉座。 IS26和ISEcp1是在多重耐藥病原體質粒中攜帶抗生素抗性基因的常見IS元件。在這個項目中，我們會表徵順式編碼的小RNA，as-tnp26，及它與IS26轉座酶mRNA在控制IS26轉座效率中的相互作用,並闡明通過細菌中的IS26轉座傳播抗生素抗性基因的潛在機制。此外,我們將進一步通過調節as-tnp26來確定可以激活IS26轉座的應激條件。了解IS元素在抗生素抗性基因的動員和聚類偏好中的作用將為細菌中多重耐藥病原體質粒的流行及其在社區中的傳播提供見解。此外，小RNA調節轉座的知識將指導我們更好地控制新出現的多重耐藥病原體，防止抗生素抗性基因的傳播。

11101518.label: Realisation of objectives
11101518.value: In this project, we set out to study and characterize the functional role of small RNA (sRNA) located at the transposon region of the multidrug resistance (MDR) plasmids. We have performed systematic analysis of the plasmid encoded non-coding RNAs using RNA sequencing and transcriptomes profiling. We have characterized the cis-encoded sRNAs, as-tnp26 and two other sRNAs which located at the transposon region, plas2 and ttnpA by various biochemical experiments including Northern blot, electrophoretic mobility shift assay, 3’ and 5’ RACE and so on. The physiology of the bacteria overexpressing these sRNAs were investigated which included growth measurement, minimum inhibition concentration measurement, mobility measurement, biofilm formation, transposition activity and so on. However, although they located in transposon region, they have no effect in the regulation of transposition but other physiological functions, and therefore, we moved forward to study other functions of these sRNAs with the help of transcriptomic analysis and phenotypic experiments. For plas2 which located the 3’ end of tnpA transposon cassette in IncX3 plasmid, we found that this sRNA played significant role in modulating fucose metabolism by controlling the expression of fuc operon. Moreover, it affected the biofilm formation of the bacteria carrying IncX3 plasmid. In addition to plas2, we also identified another sRNA called ttnpA which was a truncated form of Tn3 transposase, and highly conserved in different plasmids. This sRNA possessed its own promoter region which can be transcribed as a stable sRNA in the cell. Moreover, it can modulate the antibiotic persistence. Although the proposed sRNA-regulated transposition was not worked out, we attempted and indeed found other functions of these sRNAs. In addition, during the study of MDR plasmids, we found that the outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) secreted from different uropathogenic E. coli can affect the physiology of the bacteria such as mobility and biofilm formation. Moreover, we found that aroB which is the aromatic amino acid biosynthesis protein presented in OMVs was the key factor to facilitate the movement of the bacteria.

11101518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101518.value: In this project, we studied the physiology of the bacteria upon the introduction of incompatibility group X3 plasmid (IncX3), and determined the functional role of the plasmid as well as their underlying mechanism. We determined the RNA repertoires of the bacteria carrying IncX3 and found that one small RNA at the intragenic region of transposon elements acted as a regulator of fucR which controls the fucose metabolism. This work has been published as an article in the journal of RNA biology. In addition to this small RNA, we identified another new non-coding RNA which is the truncated form of Tn3 family transposon in IncX3 plasmid, and demonstrated that it can modulate that the activity of antibiotics persistence. We are now in the progress of preparing the manuscript for submission (the draft manuscript was attached for reference). Apart from the mechanistic control of small RNA and ncRNA, we also studied the effect of ESBL plasmids in bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs). Intriguingly, we found that OMVs from different strains affect the physiology of the bacteria including biofilm formation and mobility. We further identified the aroB protein in OMV that affect the movement of the bacteria. This work was sent to International Journal of Medical Microbiology and now was under minor revision (The manuscript was included for reference).

11101518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101518.value: We have identified two ncRNAs in IncX3 plasmid and one protein in OMV, which play significant roles in bacterial physiology. However, the detail mechanism remains elucidated. Therefore, the potential for further development of the research is to probe the underlying mechanism of these factors. Since we demonstrated the functions of these ncRNAs and they are specific to ESBL carrying bacteria, they can be used as the biomarkers to identify the drug resistance bacteria. Moreover, understanding the regulation of these factors can facilitate the development of the control strategies for drug resistance dissemination. For example, inhibition of the function of these ncRNAs can be used as therapeutic to target drug resistance bacteria carrying IncX3 plasmid.

11101518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101518.value: The spread of antibiotic resistance has become a critical clinical and public health problem by causing outbreaks as well as sporadic infections worldwide in recent years. Despite the continuous efforts in combating antibiotics resistance, the emerging of new resistance strains is still inevitable and uncontrollable. Therefore, understanding the dissemination of antibiotics resistant microorganisms as well as the development of novel antimicrobial are major focuses of scientific investigation. In the project, we identified the drug resistance bacteria-specific factors that can control the bacterial physiology and facilitate their dissemination, and studied their underlying mechanisms. These factors can be potentially used as druggable target to interrupt the spreading of drug resistance, and to develop the therapeutic for drug resistance bacteria in the future.

11101618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101618.value: High-resolution imaging of oxygen transport in living tissue provides valuable information for many biomedical applications, such as mapping neuron activities in the brain via neurovascular coupling, studying tumor progress via quantitative imaging of oxygen metabolic rate. Most oxygen in the human body binds to hemoglobin and transports through the blood circulation. As an emerging biomedical imaging modality, optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy (OR-PAM) can image oxygen saturation (sO2) of blood with sub-cellular spatial resolution, high imaging speed, and high signal-to-noise ratio. Conventional OR-PAM usually assumes a linear relationship between the measured photoacoustic (PA) amplitude and the absorption coefficient. Based on the linear assumption, OR-PAM determines the sO2 value from PA signals measured at two or more optical wavelengths. Limited by high pulse repetition rate laser technique, most conventional OR-PAM systems use wavelengths in the Q-band. The absorption coefficient of blood in the Q-band is too high and may lead to an absorption saturation problem. With absorption saturation, the measured sO2 value may have a significant systematic error. To avoid the systematic error in sO2 imaging, we propose to develop a new functional OR-PAM imaging technique that can compensate the absorption saturation in sO2 imaging, as well as maintain other performances, such as high imaging speed and high signal-to-noise ratio. We will model the absorption saturation into a nonlinear relationship between the PA amplitude and the absorption coefficient. Via measuring PA signals at three or more wavelengths, we can solve the nonlinear equations and determine the sO2 values without systematic errors. We will develop a new OR-PAM system to test the proposed sO2 imaging method. A multi-wavelength pulsed laser will be built for the OR-PAM system. The new laser will have three or more wavelengths for sO2 imaging, a high pulse repetition rate, and sufficient pulse energy for each wavelength. The accuracy of the new sO2 imaging method will be validated in phantom experiments. In vivo imaging of sO2 will be demonstrated in the mouse brain to show the neurovascular coupling. Combining the sO2 with hemoglobin concentration and blood flow, we may further quantify the metabolic rate of oxygen in a tumor model. The new technical advance in OR-PAM may potentially enable many biomedical applications related to oxygen metabolism. 在活體組織中對血氧輸送進行高分辨率成像能夠為很多生物醫學應用提供有價值的信息，例如通過神經血管耦合對腦神經活動成像，或者通過氧代謝定量成像研究腫瘤的發病過程。人體内大部分氧會與血紅蛋白結合並通過血液循環進行輸送。作爲一種新的生物醫學成像技術，光學分辨率光聲顯微鏡能夠對血氧飽和度進行高分辨率、高速度、和高信噪比成像。傳統光學分辨率光聲顯微鏡通常假定光聲信號和光吸收係數之間呈綫性關係。基於此假定，血氧飽和度的值可以通過測量兩個或以上波長的光聲信號得到。受限于高重頻脈衝激光器技術，大部分光學分辨率光聲顯微鏡使用Q-band範圍内的激光波長。此範圍内的光學吸收係數過高而可能導致光學吸收飽和現象，從而導致測得的血氧飽和度值出現較大的系統誤差。爲了克服這一問題，我們提出了開發一種新的功能光聲顯微鏡技術，補償血氧飽和度測量中的吸收飽和問題，並同時保持高的成像速度和信噪比等。我們將建立吸收飽和的非綫性模型。通過在三個或更多波長進行光聲測量，我們可以解算出血氧飽和度的值而避免引入系統誤差。我們將開發這一新的成像系統，包括具有高重頻、高能量的多波長激光光源。血氧飽和度的測量精度將通過仿躰實驗進行驗證。活體腦功能成像將在小鼠模型中進行演示。將血氧飽和度與血紅蛋白濃度、血流等結合，我們可以進一步對腫瘤的氧代謝進行定量成像。這一新技術有望推動與氧代謝有關的更多生物醫學應用。

11101618.label: Realisation of objectives
11101618.value: All objectives have been achieved. We developed a nonlinear PA model to compensate for the absorption saturation in sO2 imaging. Measurement of PA signals at three wavelengths allows us compute the sO2 value accurately. We developed a high-speed OR-PAM system with a new multi-wavelength pulsed laser. The laser can generate wavelengths at 532, 545, 558 nm. Each wavelength can have higher than ~100nJ pulse energy and 1MHz pulse repetition rate. Switching among different wavelengths was achieved by using different fiber delay lines for different wavelengths. A 2D scanners was used in the OR-PAM to achieve high-speed raster scanning. The new OR-PAM enables multi-wavelength imaging without compromising the imaging speed and signal-to-noise ratio. The improved accuracy in sO2 imaging is validated via phantom experiments. We demonstrated sO2 imaging in the mouse brain and the tumor model.

11101618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101618.value: In this project, we developed new functional OR-PAM that can compensate for the absorption saturation and improve accuracy of sO2 imaging. We developed a nonlinear model to calculate the sO2 based on multi-wavelength PA measurements. To achieve realtime fast imaging, we used a fast optimization algorithm to solve the nonlinear model. The new model has three unknown quantities including the sO2. Solving the nonlinear equations requires measuring PA signals at three or more wavelengths. A new OR-PAM system will be developed to implement multi-wavelength high-speed imaging. Different from linear approaches, the nonlinear model considers the absorption saturation, thus the sO2 can be determined without bias even when the absorption coefficient is high. Via phantom and in vivo experiment, we show that the nonlinear model can significantly reduce errors in sO2 imaging.

11101618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101618.value: In the future, we may further develop a portable imaging system to implement sO2 imaging during surgery. A compact and lightweight imaging probe can be built for handheld applicaitons.

11101618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101618.value: We developed a new optical imaging technique to image the oxygen content in living tissue. A nonlinear model was developed to compensate for the unknown fluence attenuation. A multiwavelength imaging system was developed to implement the oxygen saturation (sO2) measurement. Experimental results show the method is effective. The accurate sO2 imaging may enhance the in vivo applications of functional OR-PAM. For example, high-resolution label-free imaging of sO2 offers key information in the study of neuron diseases or cancer. Enabled by our new method, the biologist or the physician can map the sO2 with higher accuracy even when absorption saturation exists. Because the extent of absorption saturation may vary between trunk vessels and capillaries, the new sO2 imaging can provide more consistent and accurate results. Combining the new sO2 results with hemoglobin concentration and flow, we can further quantify oxygen delivery at a higher accuracy. In addition, this technique does not compromise on other performances, such as imaging speed, resolution, and signal-to-noise ratio. Therefore, this proposed research can significantly enhance the OR-PAM technique and potentially enable many biomedical applications related to oxygen metabolism.
