11101818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101818.value: The thalamocortical network has been shown to be strongly involved in neuronal plasticity and memory consolidation. The thalamocortical network displays tonic, slow wave, spindle, and high-frequency-burst firing modes. Our earlier studies have demonstrated that the auditory thalamus, medial geniculate body (MGB), displays slow-wave, spindle oscillations, and burst firing. Most interestingly, retrograde labeling showed that nearly all the thalamocortical neurons express CCK. In our recent experiments, we found that the medial temporal lobe modulates the neuroplasticity in the auditory cortex through cholecystokinin (CCK) and high-frequency firing of the thalamocortical CCK positive neurons triggers CCK release in the cortex and leads to neuroplasticity in the auditory cortex. This led us to consider whether CCK is involved in thalamocortical neuroplasticity. In the proposed study, our first objective is to confirm whether high-frequency stimulation (HFS) of CCK neurons could induce thalamocortical long-term potentiation (LTP) by activating CCK neurons in the MGB with laser stimulation in Cre-dependent virus injected CCK-Cre mice. CCK-CreER (CCK-/-) mice and low-frequency stimulation (LFS) will be used as control. Specific CCK knockdown in the MGB will be done to further consolidate our hypothesis. Secondly, to investigate whether HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP is age-dependent and to figure out the correlation between thalamocortical LTP and CCK expression levels in the MGB, rats of different ages (from P10 to 2 years old) will be used to induce LTP during the electrophysiological recording. Immunohistochemical staining (IHC) and mRNA quantification will be performed to detect the changes of CCK expression with age. Finally, assuming the loss of thalamocortical neuroplasticity is related to decreased CCK expression in the MGB, we will then test whether local infusion of CCK-8S in the auditory cortex (or intravenous injection of CCK-4) can rescue the thalamocortical LTP formation. An anatomical confirmation of CCKBR expression in the auditory cortex will be carried out with antibodies for CCKBR in the brain slice of the old rats. Based on our preliminary results, thalamocortical LTP is likely CCK-dependent since minimal thalamocortical LTP was induced in the old rats. We hypothesize that the thalamocortical neurons have minimal CCK expression and their CCK receptors in the cortical neurons that receive thalamic projections are still functional in the old rats. To examine these hypotheses, we will confirm whether the minimal thalamocortical LTP we observed in old rats was related to reduced CCK levels and examine whether administration of CCK in the auditory cortex can rescue the HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP in old rats. 丘腦皮層網絡已被證明與神經元可塑性和記憶鞏固密切相關。丘腦皮層網絡顯示強直，慢波和高頻突發震荡模式。我們早期的研究表明，聽覺丘腦，內側膝狀體（MGB）顯示慢波和高頻突發震荡模式。最有趣的是，逆行標記顯示幾乎所有丘腦皮層神經元都表達CCK。在我們最近的實驗中，我們發現內側顳葉通過膽囊收縮素（CCK）調節聽覺皮層中的神經可塑性，並且丘腦皮質CCK陽性神經元的高頻激發觸發皮質中的CCK釋放並導致聽覺皮層中的神經可塑性。這導致我們考慮CCK是否參與了丘腦皮質神經可塑性。在所提出的研究中，我們的第一個目標是確認CCK神經元的高頻刺激（HFS）是否可通過激活刺激在Cre小鼠注射Cre依賴性病毒激活MGB中的CCK神經元來誘導丘腦皮層長時程增強（LTP）。 CCK-CreER（CCK - / - ）小鼠和低頻刺激（LFS）將用作對照。將在MGB中進行特定的CCK擊倒以進一步鞏固我們的假設。其次，為了研究HFS是否誘導丘腦皮質LTP是年齡依賴性的，並且計算出MGB中丘腦皮質LTP和CCK表達水平之間的相關性，不同年齡（從P10到2歲）的大鼠將用於在電生理學期間誘導LTP。 進行免疫組織化學染色（IHC）和mRNA定量以檢測CCK表達隨年齡的變化。最後，假設丘腦皮質神經可塑性的喪失與MGB中CCK表達的降低有關，那麼我們將測試在聽覺皮層中局部輸注CCK-8S（或靜脈注射CCK-4）是否可以挽救丘腦皮質LTP形成。在老年大鼠腦切片中用CCKBR抗體對聽覺皮層中CCKBR表達進行解剖學確認。根據我們的初步結果，丘腦皮質LTP可能是CCK依賴性的在老年大鼠中誘導了最小的丘腦皮質LTP。我們假設了丘腦皮層神經元具有最小的CCK表達，並且它們在接受丘腦突出的皮層神經元中的CCK受體在老年大鼠中仍然起作用。為了檢驗這些假設，我們將確認我們在老年大鼠中觀察到的最小丘腦皮質LTP是否與降低的CCK水平相關，並檢查在聽覺皮層中施用CCK是否可以挽救老年大鼠中HFS誘導的丘腦皮質LTP。

11101818.label: Realisation of objectives
11101818.value: We surmised that the CCK-/- mouse would show deficits in thalamocortical plasticity. HFS induced no LTP in the thalamocortical pathway of CCK-/- mice (CCK-CreER mice), but significant LTP in C57 wild-type mice (CCK-/-, n=9; C57, n=8, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001; post-hoc, Tukey test, CCK-/-, 108.41±3.92% vs. 101.68±11.49%, p=0.983; C57, 103.47±1.85% vs. 159.75±7.23%, p<0.001). In the next experiment, we infused L365,260, a CCK-B receptor antagonist, into the ACx of rats before the HFS in the MGB for the experimental group, and artificial cerebral-spinal fluid (ACSF) for the control group. HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP was totally blocked in the L365,260 infusion group, but not in the ACSF infusion group (L365, 260, n=9; ACSF, n=8, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001, post-hoc, Tukey test, L365, 260, before: 100.43±1.17% vs. after: 94.74±4.20%, p>0.05; ACSF, before: 99.16±1.32% vs. after: 118.31±2.94%, p<0.001), suggesting that the dependence of CCK of the thalamocortical LTP is via CCK-B receptor. Previous studies suggest that electrical stimulation in the MGB, the thalamic radiations or the white matter beneath the sensory cortices may activate not only the thalamocortical projections, but also antidromically the corticothalamic projections that also contain CCK. In order to exclude other possibilities than the thalamocortical CCK-positive projection, we injected a Cre-dependent virus, AAV-EFIa-DIO-hChR2 (E123T/T159C)-EYFP into the MGB of the CCK-Cre mouse. Many MGB neuron were labeled with EYFP, indicating that thalamocortical projection neurons were CCK positive. EYFP labeled thalamocortical projection fibers, mainly targeted layer IV of the ACx. An early study showed a high density of CCK binding sites in layer IV of the ACx, providing the possible targets for thalamocortical CCK projections. After we stained CCKB receptors, we found that CCK-positive thalamocortical terminals (green) were colocalized with CCKB receptors (red; GFP terminal colocalized with CCKB receptors). These results imply that thalamocortical terminals may release CCK targeting at CCKB receptors in layer IV of the ACx. Cortical LTP induced by HFS of entorhino-neocortical projections requires HFS of the CCK terminals to trigger the release of CCK. On the other side, as a key feature of the thalamocortical connections, the thalamocortical responses show strong short-term depression because of decreased glutamate release during repeated thalamic radiation or white matter activation. Therefore, we examined the efficacies of the laser activation of the thalamocortical terminals in the ACx and the laser activation of thalamocortical neurons in the MGB to the five-pulse train. fEPSPs evoked by the second to the fifth pulses of the pulse train laser in the ACx were significantly smaller than the laser in the MGB, both of which had the identical laser power (n=8; two-way ANOVA, p<0.001; 12.37±2.46% vs. 38.24±0.53%; response to the 5th pulse of ACx vs. that of MGB). This result suggests that laser activation of thalamocortical fibers was less effective in eliciting thalamocortical responses in the ACx compared with that in the MGB. We adopted laser activation of the MGB in the following study. We inserted an optic fiber into the MGB and placed the recording electrode in layer IV (350-500 μm) of the ACx. After a stable baseline of 15 min recording of laser-evoked thalamocortical fEPSPs, HF laser stimulation (HFLS) was delivered into the MGB. A robust LTP was achieved after HFLS (before vs. after, 99.29±1.57% vs. 134.19±4.65%, n=8, one-way ANOVA, p<0.001). These findings suggest that HF activation of CCK-positive thalamocortical neurons trigger the release of CCK at the thalamocortical synapses, which in turn enables thalamocortical LTP. Objective 2. Our finding of that thalamocortical plasticity in the young adult rat is CCK-dependent, is different from the mechanism of LTP in the neonatal brains. Our next question was when HFS-induced CCK-dependent plasticity starts to emerge during thalamocortical development. We examined in-vivo thalamocortical plasticity in rats of different postnatal days (P10, P14, P21, P28, P56). In agreement with in vitro experimental results, thalamocortical LTP did not exist in neonatal rats at P10 and P14 (P10, n=9, before vs. after, 102.47±1.21% vs. 99.26±1.97%, one-way ANOVA, p>0.05, P14, n=11, before vs. after, 98.24±0.83% vs. 100.02±3.04% one-way ANOVA, p>0.05). However, a weak potentiation (113±4.8%) after HFS was observed at the end of the third postnatal week (P21, n=13, one-way ANOVA, p<0.05), and the potentiation kept increasing to 137.98±10.28% at P28 (n=7, one-way ANOVA, p<0.001) and 156.77±7.21% at P56 (n=11, one-way ANOVA, p<0.001). The peak latencies of evoked fEPSPs during development were measured. It was 31.55±0.75 ms (n=9) at P10. The peak latency kept shortening as the rat grew and reached 8.82±0.25ms (n=9) at P28 and 7.43±0.18ms (n=9) at P56 (one-way ANOVA, p<0.001, post-hoc, Tukey test, *, p<0.05). These results reflect the progress of the maturation of the thalamocortical projection during development. We examined the level of CCK expression in the MGB during the development. Weak CCK signal was detected at P10 and P14. The expression level increased at P21 and reached high levels at P28 and P56. The higher CCK expression levels are suggestive of a greater level of LTP induction in the thalamocortical pathway after the critical period. We further examined the CCK protein expression level by using Western blot analysis and found that the expression levels of CCK was minimal at P3 and kept increasing to P21 and saturated after that. The results indicate that the protein level of CCK proceeds the LTP induction during the development. Objective 3. Previous studies revealed that altered synaptic plasticity, including LTP, causes age-related impairment of hippocampal-dependent memory. During aging, synapses also become less plastic in the thalamocortical pathway. We examined HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP and CCK expression in the MGB in the rat of >18 months. HFS in the MGB failed to induce LTP in the fEPSP of cortical neurons to the MGB stimulation in the aged rat of >18 m (before vs. after, 99.78±3.62% vs. 91.94±5.47% n=9, one-way ANOVA, p>0.05). This result suggests that the thalamocortical synapses lose their plasticity nature in the aged brain. We speculated that the loss of thalamocortical LTP is correlated with decreased expression of CCK in the MGB. The aged rat showed a minimal level of CCK expression in the MGB, similarly to the negative control CCK-KO group from the western blot results. Western blot results confirmed that the protein expression of CCK in the MGB of the aged brain (12 months) was minimal/void, similar to that of the CCK-/- brain, with a great contrast to that of the young adult brain (8 weeks). If the loss of thalamocortical LTP is the result of the decreased CCK expression in the MGB, an exogenous infusion of CCK should rescue this age-related impairment. We infused CCK-8S or ACSF as the shame control into the ACx and applied low-frequency stimulation (LFS, 200 trials of electrical stimulation at 75% of the saturated current pulse in 0.1 Hz) to the MGB after that. The slopes of evoked fEPSPs showed a significant LTP in the CCK-8S infused rat, but no LTP in the ACSF infused rat (P<0.001, two-way ANOVA; for CCK-8S group, n=8, before vs. after, 98.49±2.37% vs. 126.07±5.11% post-hoc, Tukey test, p<0.001; for ACSF group, n=8, before vs. after, 103.18±4.53% vs. 93.57±4.99% post-hoc, Tukey test, p=0.05). Exogenous application of CCK partially restored the lost thalamocortical LTP in the aged rat. Besides, we examined CCKBR expression in the ACx with anatomical imaging and found no apparent difference between young adult and 18 months old rodents.

11101818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101818.value: During this report period, we continued studying roles of the abundant neuropeptide, cholecystokinin (CCK) in the brain, which were discovered for the modulation of neural plasticity in many brain regions, including auditory cortex (Chen et al., 2019; C-6), and lateral amygdala (Feng et al., 2021). In the present study, we indicated that CCK, which is expressed in the MGB, plays an essential role in the formation of thalamocortical LTP. We then selectively activated with optogenetics the CCK-positive thalamocortical neurons for LTP induction (C-7). Herein, we hypothesize that the thalamocortical neurons have minimal CCK expression and their CCK receptors in the cortical neurons that receive thalamic projections are still functional in the old rats. We further examined 1) whether thalamocortical LTP is with the ontogeny of CCK expression in the MGB during development; 2) whether exogenous application of CCK can rescue the thalamocortical LTP deficit in old animals. From the results, the thalamocortical pathway undergoes neuroplasticity during the critical period and in adulthood. We found that thalamocortical neurons expressed CCK. High-frequency stimulation of the medial geniculate body (MGB) induced thalamocortical long-term potentiation (LTP) in wildtype mice, but not in CCK-/- mice. A CCK-B receptor antagonist completely blocked LTP. Thalamocortical LTP was blocked by either antagonist of mGluR1/5, both of which were found in the CCK terminals, but not NMDA receptor antagonist (C-7). Thalamocortical LTP was induced from week 3 to 7 together with CCK expression in the MGB neurons. However, no thalamocortical LTP was induced neither CCK was detected in rats of >18 months. CCK injection in the auditory cortex of the aged rats partially restored this LTP, implying a potential therapeutic intervention for neurological deficits related to thalamocortical neuroplasticity (C-7). CCK induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to enhance rescue the hearing loss for the old in future. Our main findings on the role of CCK could be generalized in different sensory modalities in learning and memory (Sun et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2020; Gao et al., 2020).

11101818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101818.value: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is of great significance in the long-term potentiation (LTP) of excitatory neurons. Herein, we investigated the mechanism of CCK under the thalamocortical pathway. The primary auditory-responsive proportion of the thalamus, the MGB (medial geniculate body), plays an important role in the information gateway to the auditory cortex. Numerous studies corroborated that the thalamocortical pathway could shape and filter the sound representation to facilitate the proportions of acoustic features to the auditory cortex. Thalamocortical plasticity in the adult brain has been reported to be induced by reversing the critical periods of the sensory cortices in different ways. In our current study, we proposed a novel potential method to trigger thalamocortical plasticity in the adult brain, especially for the aged. Thalamocortical plasticity not only participates in the refinement of the sensory cortices but also learning processes. Thus, our findings may involve different sensory modalities like perception, learning and memory. CCK induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to rescue the hearing loss for the old in future.

11101818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101818.value: In current project, we mainly focused on the role of Cholecystokinin (CCK) in the thalamocortical neuroplasticity. Herein, we found that auditory thalamocortical long-term potentiation (LTP) was CCK-dependent. Besides, there was a time window for the CCK expression level, which was positive correlation with the LTP alterations. Due to the loss of CCK in the old rats, we supplied external CCK to them trying to rescue the loss of LTP. The results showed that CCK could successfully rescued partial thalamocortical LTP in the old rats, which might provide novel treatments for the hearing impairments of the old in future.

11102118.value: 胰腺癌是一種惡性程度高的消化系統腫瘤，其早期診斷率低，發展迅速，預後普遍較差。其中位生存期為6個月，五年生存率低於8％。胰腺導管腺癌（Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC）是最常見的胰腺癌類型，約佔90％。人們對原癌基因以及腫瘤抑制基因在癌症形成中的作用進行了深入的研究，然而表觀遺傳信息改變在癌症中的研究仍處於初始階段。研究表明體細胞原癌基因和腫瘤抑制基因突變與驅動PDAC形成有關。亦有研究發現編碼表觀遺傳修飾因子的基因突變在PDAC形成中發揮關鍵作用。我們曾報導惡性膠質瘤(Glioblastoma multiforme, GBM)病人存在組蛋白基因突變，是腫瘤形成的驅動因素。組蛋白H3變體H3.3第27位賴氨酸K突變為蛋氨酸M，H3.3K27M突變造成基因組H3K27me3分佈紊亂，一方面H3K27me3整體水平下降而使大量基因表達，另一方面局部H3K27me3增多而使部分腫瘤抑制基因沉默，從而驅動腫瘤形成。目前研究發現的組蛋白基因突變僅出現在組蛋白H3，而組蛋白H2A，H2B和H4基因突變在腫瘤中的作用則未見報導。本課題通過分析“癌症基因組圖譜”（TCGA）數據，我們發現許多癌症中存在組蛋白基因突變，在PDAC病人中，除了存在高頻的KRAS和SMAD4等知名腫瘤相關基因突變，還出現了高頻的特定組蛋白基因突變，經前期數據和實驗分析，該組蛋白特定位點突變可能在PDAC形成中發揮重要作用。因此，我們將致力於揭示該組蛋白基因突變的重要性和臨床相關性，將基因突變與表觀遺傳基因調控聯繫起來，深入了解胰腺癌的發生，最終對特定PDAC類型的治療提供策略依據。

11102118.label: Realisation of objectives
11102118.value: We have completed all the three objectives. (* we numbered the position of the Glycine G to Aspartic acid D mutation position 54 "H2BG54D" in the proposal but we have corrected it and changed to H2BG53D in the papers and this report) Objective 1: Investigate the effect of H2BG54D mutation in transcription To examine the effect of the H2BG53D mutation on gene expression we conducted RNA-seq using the CRISPR knock-in H2BG53D mutant and isogenic wild-type clones4. We identified 280 upregulated and 262 downregulated genes which are associated with growth factor signaling, cell adhesion, and pathways involved in cancer development. We have also mapped active RNA polymerases by precision nuclear run-on sequencing (PRO-seq) and identified 559 genes with elevated PRO-seq signals and 426 genes with reduced signals. On a genome-wide scale, we observed significant correlation between differential gene expression and Pol II occupancy alteration between H2BG53D mutant and wild-type cells. We have also perform in vitro transcription elongation assay and using the wildtype and H2BG53D nucleosomes, our results showed that the majority of Pol II stopped at +15, +25, and +45 regions of the nucleosome at 40mM salt condition. As the salt concentration increased, the Pol II’s nucleosomal passage efficiencies increased in both the wild-type and H2BG53D nucleosomes. We observed that significantly more Pol II passed through the H2BG53D nucleosome than the wild-type nucleosome. Together, our data demonstrated that the H2BG53D mutation alters transcription in vitro and in vivo. Objective 2:Define the effects of H2BG54D mutant histone in DNA replication and repair We tested whether the H2BG53D mutation affects DNA damage repair and DNA replication by treating our CRISPR/Cas9 knockin cells with DNA damage agent CPT (topoisomerase 1 inhibitor) and MMS (DNA alkylating agent, generates DNA damage). Using gamma H2AX and 53BP1 as markers of DNA damage, we found that the H2BG53D knockin lines did not exhibit increased sensitivity when compared to the isogenic wild-type knockin clones. We also treated our mutant cells with bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) and performed incorporation assay and our results showed that the mutant lines had no defect in DNA replication. In addition, we found that the H2BG53D mutant cells has no difference in proliferation compared to the isogenic wildtype cells. Objective 3: Elucidate how H2BG54D contributes to oncogenic properties in pancreatic cells Our RNA-seq (objective 1) data showed multiple differentially expressed genes in the H2BG53D mutant cells. Gene ontology analysis of the RNA-seq data showed that genes involved in pathways related to cell migration, such as cell adhesion and focal adhesion, are differentially expressed in the H2BG53D mutant cells, suggesting that the H2BG53D mutation might target cell migration related phenotypes in PDAC. Among these genes we found that ANXA3, an oncogene that has been shown to play important roles in metastasis, is overexpressed in lung, liver and ovarian carcinomas.However, the functional significance and the clinical relevance of ANXA3 in PDAC remain elusive. Hence, we selected ANXA3 and investigated its function in PDAC in the context of the H2BG53D mutation. We investigated the direct effect of the G53D mutant H2B on ANXA3 transcription in vivo, H2BG53D cells were treated with (DRB) to arrest transcription elongation by RNA Pol II. By RT-qPCR we found that the level of ANXA3 primary transcript was reduced significantly in both wildtypes and H2BG53D mutants upon DRB treatment, but gradually increased after released from DRB inhibition. Importantly, substantially more primary ANXA3 transcripts were found at all tested exon–intron junctions along the gene in time course experiments in the two H2BG53D clones, indicating increased transcription elongation on ANXA3. Conversely, SNAP47, a gene that does not have specific FLAG-H2BG53D enrichment,showed comparable recovery after DRB treatment. Together, these results suggested that the H2BG53D plays a direct role in elevating the transcription of ANXA3. We further performed oncogenic assays and found that depletion of ANXA3 by shRNAs reduced the cell migration abilities in both wild-type and H2BG53D clones, when compared with their respective non-targeting controls. However, the H2BG53D mutant cells still exhibited faster migration than wild-type cells, suggesting that other genes or pathways also contribute to the increased oncogenic properties in the H2BG53D cells. More importantly, we found that PDAC patients with high ANXA3 expression had poor overall survival. We also observed that patients harboring the H2BG53D mutation have higher ANXA3 expression and poorer prognosis compared to non-H2BG53D patients , although these are not statistically significant which is likely due to the limited sample size. These findings further support the clinical relevance of the H2BG53D mutation in Pancreatic Ductal Adeno Carcinoma.

11102118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102118.value: We have elucidated that significance of a cancer associated histone mutation H2BG53D in the development of pancreatic cancer. Our data showed that the H2BG53D mutation weakens the interaction between the histone octamer and the nucleosomal DNA and subsequently affects the transcription of its target genes. The transcription of ANXA3, one of the targets of the G53D mutant H2B, is elevated in the H2BG53D mutant cells. The migration ability of H2BG53D mutant cells is enhanced compared to the wildtype control cells and the knockdown of ANXA3 in H2BG53D mutant cells significantly suppressed this oncogenic phenotypes. Our results suggested that the H2BG53D mutation plays a significant role in the development of pancreatic cancer.

11102218.label: Realisation of objectives
11102218.value: We had completed all three objectives. In objective 1, we developed our hydrogels based on clinically-used biomaterials to ensure high potential of clinical translation. These biomaterials include alginate, hyaluronic acid, chitosan and liposomes to provide a sustainable release of drug. Their abundant exchangeable protons, which serve as natural labels, can be detected by molecular MRI contrast, named chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST). Using CEST MRI to track these compositional changes in the hydrogel matrix has the following advantages, no additional labels are required and hence preserve their biocompatibility, and each component generates unique CEST MRI contrast to enable specific imaging of components individually. We measured the rheological and mechanical properties of these CEST-detectable hydrogels, especially those have high syringeability and stiffness comparable to the brain. Among the optimized hydrogel formulations and our experiences with hydrogel fabrication [1,3], eight of them showed promises for local treatment in the brain (some of the formulations are shown in Fig. 1). Findings of the hydrogel formulations were published in Theranostics [1]. The optimized hydrogel formulations have unique contrast for individual components. In CEST MRI, the contrast is measured in ppm, for example, the CEST MRI contrast at -3.4 ppm represents the amount of liposomes within the hydrogel matrix, contrast at 5 ppm represents the amount of intraliposomal drugs (Fig. 2). In objective 2, we have completed the CEST-MRI approach optimization to facilitate the measurement of specific CEST contrast of hydrogels. The aim of developing these CEST MRI approaches is to enhance the sensitivity and specificity of CEST MRI of the components in hydrogels, such as the specific contrast at -3.4 ppm and 5 ppm as mentioned above. Some of the related findings can be found in the published articles [1,3,5,6]. When we injected the hydrogels into the mouse brain, CEST MRI contrast at -3.4 ppm and 5 ppm can be reliably detected in a sensitive and specific manners [1]. Moreover, we demonstrated that the injectable hydrogel can be applied to delivery drug and had favorable rheological properties for local brain treatment, importantly multiple components of the hydrogel can be detected by CEST MRI independently and simultaneously. (Fig. 3) [1,3]. This work was selected as the Supp. Cover of the journal. To facilitate the in vivo imaging of injected hydrogel, we also developed a sequence that could suppressed other contributions to CEST contrast (Fig. 4) [4]. This will be applied to monitor the treatment efficacy in objective 3. In summary, we can use CEST contrast at 1.1 ppm, 5 ppm and -3.4 ppm to image hydrogel-based drug delivery in the mouse brain. In objective 3, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy in five cohorts of mice after brain tumor resection and hydrogel treatment. We have demonstrated tumor and its molecular environment can be revealed by CEST-MRI [7,8]. Data showed that we can detect the drug-loaded hydrogels after injection (Fig. 5). Based on our promising findings, we further showed that the CEST MRI contrast not only can image the drug delivery, but also provides information about treatment responses prior to a decrease in tumor size. We overcome the challenges of other contributions to CEST contrast by injecting the hydrogel next to the tumors. We injected hydrogel loaded with gemcitabine and methotrexate (MTX) (Fig. 6), and monitored the treatment effects using CEST MRI. As shown in Fig. 6C, CEST contrast was significantly different from control on day 3, while tumor size was decrease on day 5. This strongly supported that molecular information detected by CEST MRI that indicated the protein level of tumors could indicate the tumor responses towards the treatment earlier than changes in tumor size [3]. The imaging findings were validated by histology as shown in Fig. 7. We have demonstrated many biomedical applications of CEST MRI, in particular to MR-guided cell or drug delivery [1,3, 4, 8, 9, 15]. In this study, we developed new hydrogels to deliver drug locally and optimized the CEST MRI approach to detect each hydrogel components specifically. We demonstrated that CEST MRI can be a versatile approach to track of compositional changes of the hydrogel matrix with the unique multiparametric readouts of CEST MRI in brain tumors.

11102218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11102218.value: This project aims to develop injectable and MRI-detectable hydrogels for local drug delivery in the brain under MR guidance. We have successfully developed a series of injectable hydrogels with distinctive MR contrast, specific rheological and mechanical properties, and a sustainable drug delivery. These hydrogels have unique molecular MRI contrast, which enables the imaging of individual components in the hydrogel therapeutics simultaneously and independently both in vitro and in vivo at 3T MRI. Moreover, we found that the unique contrast to indicate the release of drug carrier, i.e. liposomes. This is also the first report of label-free tracking of liposomes using MRI. As a result, we can track the drug release and drug carrier to enhance the monitoring of treatment efficacy.[1,4-6] The conventional local brain tumor treatment is based on the Gliadel, which is carmustine loaded wafer, and is indicated for the treatment of patients with high-grade glioma together with surgery and radiation. However, this wafer has a few drawbacks that limited it wide clinical application. First, the wafer cannot provide a full coverage of the surgical site; Second, the degradation of the wafer could lead to side effects. These include impaired neurosurgical wound healing and wafer migration. Thus, another important finding is the development of injectable hydrogel that could provide a comprehensive coverage at the tumor site and hydrogel is known to support wound healing. Our hydrogel has self-healing property that could support such application. Moreover, the mechanical property of the designed hydrogel is injectable, and relatively soft. This further support the local treatment efficacy of brain tumor.[3,9-14] Another major outcome is that the imaging approach enables the monitoring the treatment effect prior to the change in tumor size non-invasively. We observed the change in the tumor CEST MRI contrast two days before the tumor size reduced, which is essential to guide the treatment. We successfully demonstrated a high therapeutic efficacy of suppressing tumor after injection to tumor proximity. This is because of the image-guided local treatment and the specific design of the injectable hydrogel with dual drugs. This approach could be robustly translated to the clinic due to the non-invasive nature of the imaging approach, and the biomaterials have high biocompatibility.[2,7,8,15] We had completed all three objectives successfully. This resulted in 15 published articles, 35 conference proceedings with 8 received the top 5% abstract awards, a young investigator award and a junior fellow award.

11102218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102218.value: The findings of this project had revealed the essential criteria for image-guided local drug delivery to brain tumor. This includes the non-invasive imaging nature to support the interactive refinement of the treatment, a comprehensive coverage at the tumor site, a sustainable release and a relatively soft matrix. Further development to improve the drug loading and release and to fine-tune the mechanical and rheological properties of the hydrogel is expected to enhance the treatment efficacy. Moreover, in the presence of the imaging capability, the therapeutics could be further exploited for treating other neurological disease, such stroke and spinal cord injury. The proposed course of action is the investigation of the mechanical properties of target tissues, such as spinal cord. Then, the examination of the potential CEST MRI contrast of drugs approved for clinical use. The therapeutic efficacy can then be explored in an animal model. After these further development, this additional data perhaps can form a library of potential hydrogel-based drug delivery system for CNS.

11102218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102218.value: Brain tumor is hard to treat due to the challenges of killing remaining cancer cells in a specific and sustainable manner. In this study, a versatile drug delivery system of magnetic resonance imaging(MRI)-detectable injectable hydrogel was presented to treat brain tumor locally. This system has outstanding features, i) the composition of this drug delivery system can be imaged non-invasively using MRI. Notably, the existing MRI scanners at the hospital can be applied for this detection,i.e. no change in the hardware. ii) this injectable hydrogel can provide a comprehensive coverage, and its physical property can prevent tumor growth. iii) Dual anticancer drugs can be carried by this system to provide a sustainable drug release, which resulted in a high therapeutic efficacy in an animal brain tumor model. This MRI-guided drug delivery system can be an alternative to the conventional local treatment using Gliadel. It could overcome the limitation of the delivery vehicle of Gliadel to enhance the treatment efficacy in brain tumor. In particular, the MRI signal indicated the tumor response before the reduction in tumor size. This valuable information can guide the refinement of treatment, especially in the clinical setting where invasive biopsy is not possible during brain tumor treatment.

11102618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102618.value: 在现代社会中，慢性耳鸣是导致残疾的最主要原因。慢性耳鸣好像一种持续不断的铃响声。听力损失引起的耳鸣经常会有各种合并症，包括失眠、注意力下降、焦虑和抑郁，这些合并症会严重地影响生活质量。不幸的是，缓解耳鸣的治疗方法有限。目前，已知耳鸣是与神经元激发/抑(E/I) 的平衡有关。 (E/I) 的平衡主要是靠沿听觉途径上的离子通道和受体的调节。在这里，我们提出了一种沿着皮质神经元并通过激活树突上的A型钾通道（IA）来治疗耳鸣的策略。在听力损失而诱发耳鸣的动物中，我们的初步数据指出听觉神经元中IA通道的数目出现下调。这些通道可以塑造神经元的兴奋性，从而形成耳鸣。我们将采用先进的技术，包括双光子成像、打破MNI-谷氨酸、病毒注射和耳鸣动物模型，这些方法将鉴定IA在耳鸣中的功能。该结果将能够详尽说明导致耳鸣的机制，并有助深入了解IA激动剂在缓解耳鸣中的药理价值。

11102618.label: Realisation of objectives
11102618.value: Objective 1. To demonstrate the role of A-type potassium (IA) channels in a noise-induced tinnitus animal model: We wondered whether noise-induced tinnitus is involved in the expression and function of IA channels. The fact that IA channels are counteracting the activity of NMDARs (known as one of the key factors of tinnitus development) reinforces the involvement of IA channels in tinnitus. Unlike NMDARs which constitutively affect normal signal transmission, the activation of IA channels does not severely influence the normal physiological functions of neurons, which opens new avenues for long-term clinical benefits. For this, tinnitus behavior will be monitored with a conditioned active avoidance method according to our established method. In order to investigate the involvement of IA channels in tinnitus, noise-induced tinnitus animals were generated with the animal behavior test of a conditioned active avoidance method. We tested the expression level of IA channels in the tinnitus animal model. Then, IA channel-mediated dendritic excitability will be measured using two-photon calcium imaging according to our established method. The noise-induced tinnitus animals showed reduced expression of IA channels, thereby leading to hyperexcitable dendritic properties due to aberrant activation of dendritic NMDA spikes. Result: 100 % achieved The reduction of IA channels of cortical neurons in noise-induced tinnitus animals (Noh et al., 2018) Enhanced excitability of cortical neurons in noise-induced tinnitus animals (Noh et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2018; Pak et al., 2023 under review) Objective 2: To investigate the role of A-type potassium channels in a genetically-induced tinnitus animal model A major challenge in tinnitus research is that it is difficult to dissociate the mechanisms underlying tinnitus from the effects of hearing loss. For example, widely used behavioral tests of tinnitus in animal models including both the gap detection and conditioning-based methods rely on the animal’s hearing ability; thus, measurements of tinnitus behaviors could be confounded by hearing loss. Therefore, it remains unclear whether the down-regulation of IA channels is the consequence of tinnitus, hearing loss, or both when it is tested with a hearing loss-induced animal model. To investigate the role of IA channels solely in tinnitus, the effect of hearing loss should be eliminated. Based on our early finding that tinnitus is tightly associated with reduced inhibition in the auditory cortex, it is expected that mice with GAD65 knockdown can demonstrate tinnitus even without hearing loss. Here, we directly tested the role of IA channels in tinnitus by using a genetically-induced tinnitus animal model. This objective is critical for conceptualizing the role of IA channels in tinnitus. Result 2: 100 % achieved Successful establishment of a genetically-induced tinnitus animal model (Miyakawa et al., 2019) Tinnitus behavior is significantly correlated with a reduction of cortical GAD65 level (Miyakawa et al., 2019) Sensory map reorganizations are not necessary for tinnitus development as shown in a genetically-induced tinnitus animal model (Miyakawa et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2021; Pak et al., 2023 under revision) Objective 3. Objective 3: To investigate whether the activation of dendritic IA channels alleviates tinnitus This objective is to provide a mechanistic rationale for the utilization of an IA channel enhancer for tinnitus alleviation. In our early studies, the expression of IA channels was downregulated, plausibly leading to dendritic hyperexcitability of noise-induced tinnitus neurons. For now, it is predictable that the complimentary expression and activation of IA channels can potentially alleviate tinnitus by restoring dendritic excitability. We will test whether overexpression of IA channels in noise-induced mice alleviates tinnitus. For this, we already fabricated Kv4.2 (kcnd2) overexpression under the control of the CaMKII promoter. New, noise-induced tinnitus mice will receive an AAV virus without the IA gene (scrambled gene as a negative control) and with the IA gene under the control of a CamK2α promoter (a molecular marker of the pyramidal neurons). It is expected that the noise-induced tinnitus can be alleviated by cortical administration of IA-containing virus because dendritic excitability will be rescued by restoration of IA channel activity. Virus expression will be monitored with the immunohistochemical reaction for enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (EYFP); see methods for details. Then, we will examine the expression and function of IA channels using rt-PCR and two-photon imaging which accompanies the tinnitus behavior. Result: 100 % achieved Successful fabrication of a virus containing overexpression of the Kv4.2 gene (Noh et al., 2019; Pak et al., 2023 under revision) A framework for the contribution of IA channels on neuron excitability and brain disease (Kwon et al., 2023; Pak et al., 2023 under revision)

11102618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102618.value: Most drugs that are currently used to treat brain diseases directly modulate ion channels and receptors that affect intrinsic and synaptic properties. However, they produce a wide range of nonspecific side effects, leading to the discontinuation of many potential treatments in the past. A recent study reports that the application of 4-AP restores low- and high-threshold dendritic spikes in the distal and apical dendrites, respectively, which can be driven by Ca2+-permeable channels (NMDARs and/or voltage-gated Ca2+ channels). In this respect, IA channels as an indirect modulator can be predominantly activated in a hyperexcitable condition caused by excessive activity of Ca2+-permeable channels, yet having minimal impact on the resting condition of neurons. Furthermore, given the homeostatic regulation of neural networks, the lack of sensory or modulatory inputs likely causes the increment of excitation and/or decrement of inhibition in the affected neurons. These changes seem to be required for maintaining network excitability for neuron survival. Thus, IA channels as a therapeutic target may open an avenue for more sustainable treatments of brain disease with minimal interference in normal physiological function, leading to long-term clinical benefits. Further research is required to delineate the precise contributions of IA channels to brain diseases in humans.

11102618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102618.value: Tinnitus is a ringing in the ear that can be perceived even in the absence of external acoustic stimuli. Tinnitus is induced mainly by environmental factors such as traumatic noise, aging, and ear infection. Environmental damage to cochlear hair cells alters the activity of the neural networks along the ascending auditory pathway, increasing the ratio of excitation to inhibition in central auditory neurons. In this proposal, we hypothesize that dendritic hyperexcitability by down-regulated IA channels can cause tinnitus. We found that there is an apparent reduction of IA channels in tinnitus animals. Furthermore, hearing loss-induced reduction of IA channels was an internal actuator of tinnitus and the activation of IA channels alleviated tinnitus, suggesting a pharmacotherapeutic candidate for tinnitus alleviation.

11102918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102918.value: Fish possess a remarkable multitude of sex determination/differentiation systems to facilitate their adaptation to dynamic changes in the environment. Recent evidence has indicated that the sex-determination/differentiation system in fish is sensitive to a number of extrinsic/environmental factors such as population density, social behaviors, pH and dissolved oxygen levels. Hypoxia is one of the most widespread and pressing environmental problems in aquatic environments worldwide, causing severe habitat loss and interruption of ecosystem balance. Recent studies by our group have shown that hypoxia is an endocrine disruptor that impairs sex differentiation and reproductive functions in fish, leading to male-biased F1 populations of zebrafish and Japanese medaka. Such shifts in sex ratio are likely to have dire consequences for reproduction and recruitment of fish assemblages inhabiting small waterbodies, potentially leading to losses in biodiversity and fishery productivity. Despite this emerging threat, the molecular mechanisms through which hypoxia alters fish sex differentiation, and hence sex ratios, remains poorly understood. As an initial step to investigate the potential role of miRNAs in mediating hypoxia-induced male-biased sex ratios in fish, we recently conducted small RNA sequencing on marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) embryos that were exposed to hypoxia for 6 days (during a critical time window of sex determination). In addition, we successfully established brain and gonadal miRNA transcriptomic libraries from male and female adult medaka fish for comparison and identified a number of tissue- and gonad-specific miRNAs in adult marine medaka as well as specific hypoxia-responsive miRNAs from medaka embryos. Bioinformatic analyses predicted that some of the hypoxia-responsive miRNAs specifically target the 3′-UTR of the androgen receptor (AR) gene. It is widely known that AR is a steroid hormone receptor that plays a critical role in male gonad differentiation and development, and in the maintenance of secondary male characteristics in vertebrates. Using the marine medaka as a fish model, we propose to test the hypothesis that the activation/inhibition of specific hypoxia-responsive miRNAs, directly or indirectly targeting AR expression or AR-associated factors, represent an important regulatory hub controlling sexual differentiation and development in fish and may provide a molecular basis for hypoxia-induced male-biased sex ratios in fish.

11102918.label: Realisation of objectives
11102918.value: The objectives have been achieved based on a series of lab experiments and computer-aided bioinformatics analyses. Details are summarized in the following sections. 1. Investigation of androgen receptor (AR) as a functional target of miR-21-3p, miR-205 and miR-30b, NCOR2 (co-repressor of AR) as a functional target of miR-125b, and SRC (coactivator of AR) as a functional target of miR-1 The 3′-UTRs of the marine medaka AR, NCOR2 and SRC genes were cloned into a firefly luciferase reporter vector (Promega) to generate, respectively, the three luciferase reporter plasmids  pMIR-AR-WT, pMIR-NCOR2-WT, and pMIR-SRC-WT. The pMIR-AR-WT luciferase reporter plasmid was co-transfected with or without pre-miR-21-3p or premiR-205 or pre-miR-30b into HEK293T cells (at a cell density of 1 x 105 cells per well in 24-well plates) using Lipofectamine 3000 reagent (Thermofisher Scientific), followed by luciferase reporter assays to assess the direct binding of these miRNAs to the 3΄-UTR of the medaka AR gene to inhibit its expression. Similarly, the pMIR-NCOR2-WT luciferase plasmid was co-transfected with pre-miR-125b, and the pMIR-SRC-WT plasmid was co-transfected with pre-miR-1 independently into HEK293T cells. Luciferase activity was measured using the Dual-Glo Luciferase Assay System (Promega) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Statistical analyses were performed using the t-test function in GraphPad Prism 9.1.0 (GraphPad Software), for a total of three independent experiments with six replicates. Unfortunately, none of the luciferase assays performed with and without the respective synthetic pre-miR molecules showed any significant difference in luciferase activities despite numerous repeated attempts of transfection studies in HEK293T cells, which suggest that the synthetic pre-miRNAs do not bind to the 3'-UTR of the respective genes. Since no inhibitory activity of the selected miRNAs on the 3′-UTRs of the AR, NCOR2 and SRC genes was observed by transfection studies, further experiments to identify additional hypoxia-responsive miRNA-mRNA pairs by small RNA (miRNA) and mRNA transcriptome sequencing of normoxic/hypoxic embryos was carried out. 2. Molecular mechanisms underlying the interactions between miRNAs/mRNAs and signaling pathways that mediate hypoxia-induced sex differentiation and sex ratio alterations in marine medaka To identify changes to the miRNA profile in hypoxia-exposed medaka embryos (after 40 hours of hypoxia exposure), small RNA and transcriptome sequencing were employed. For miRNAs, we obtained 72.8 and 79.3 million quality-trimmed raw reads from normoxic and hypoxic-exposed embryos, respectively, translating to a total of 4.36 Gb of qualified data. The clean sequencing reads were mapped to the O. melastigma genome to determine the miRNA content of marine medaka embryos. We identified 253 conserved miRNAs and 572 novel miRNAs in the medaka embryo. When we compared the expression level of these miRNAs in the normoxic and hypoxic embryos, we found 131 miRNAs with altered regulation, including 50 upregulated and 81 downregulated miRNAs. Of these, 75 and 56 dysregulated miRNAs corresponded to conserved and novel miRNAs, respectively. As miRNAs are one of the major mediators of gene expression, we applied comparative transcriptomic analysis to determine the differential gene expression occurring as a result of hypoxia exposure. A total of 163.6 million quality-trimmed raw reads, translating to 8.18 Gb of data were obtained from the mRNA sequencing. In the comparative transcriptome analysis, we found 3009 differentially-expressed genes (DEGs), including 1543 upregulated genes and 1466 downregulated genes in the embryos exposed to hypoxia. We then integrated the miRNA and mRNA sequencing results to look at the reversed expression pattern of miRNA and mRNA. Our results indicated that hypoxia could lead to the dysregulation of 167 miRNA–mRNA interaction pairs including 31 downregulated miRNA-upregulated mRNA pairs and 136 upregulated miRNA-downregulated mRNA pairs. The miRNA-targeted mRNA was subjected to DAVID analysis to understand the effect of hypoxia-dysregulated miRNA–mRNA pairs in the embryo. Our results showed that hypoxia exposure could result in alterations to miRNA-mediated genes related to different developmental processes, such as adipose tissue development, skeletal muscle tissue growth, and post-embryonic development. Additionally, hypoxia exposure altered the gene cluster related to neuron migration and amacrine cell differentiation, leading to the interference of brain development through the control of miRNA–mRNA interactions. Finally, we further assessed the possible impact of hypoxia on sex determination and differentiation through miRNA-mRNA regulation. Using gene ontology analysis, we identified miRNA-mRNA pairs that may be involved in biological functions related to sex determination and differentiation including novel miR-145-col9a3 and novel miRNA-94- arid5b in gonad development, novel miRNA-210-ca2, novel miRNA-106-nr2f2, nbr-miR-29c-nr4a1, and ola-miR-92b-akr1d1 in sex hormone response, and novel miRNA-145-mns1, nle-miR-20-sord, and ipu-miR-219b-abcc8 in sex characteristic development (Figure 1A). The differential gene expression was further validated by using quantitative PCR (qPCR), our data showed that the result of qPCR matched with the finding of RNA sequencing (Figure 1B). Taken together, our data suggest that hypoxia may alter sex determination and differentiation through the regulation of miRNA-mRNA pairs. 3. Exposure of medaka embryos to 40-hour hypoxia did not affect the hatchability/survival rate of medaka embryos and the sex ratios of medaka adults Following normoxia (5.8  0.2 mgO2/L) or hypoxia (2.0  0.2 mgO2/L) exposure, the viability and hatchability of the embryos were measured over a 4-week period (28 days). Our results indicated that exposure to the sublethal level of hypoxia did not affect the hatchability and survival rate of the medaka embryos when compared to the normoxic embryos (data not shown). To further determine the effect of embryonic hypoxia exposure on the sex ratio of adult medaka fish, we harvested one hundred 4-month old adult fish (from normoxia- and hypoxia-exposed embryos) for sex characterization at the gonad level. When we compared fish from the normoxic and hypoxic group, no significant difference in sex ratio was observed. 4. Hiring of undergraduate student as lab helper for this project One student helper (undergraduate student) was hired to help out with this project on a part-time basis. The student helper was trained to set up fish culture and fish feeding, perform fish dissection and isolation of total RNA.

11102918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11102918.value: Hypoxia is a widespread and pressing environmental concern in aquatic habitats, causing severe habitat damage and major disruption to aquatic ecosystems worldwide. Aquatic hypoxia has increased globally over the past 30 years due to escalating eutrophication and organic pollution. Presently, over 500 hypoxic areas (< 2 mg O2 L-1) spanning hundreds of thousands of square kilometers have been reported worldwide, and is likely to worsen in the future as a result of rapid coastal development, thereby threatening the sustainability of natural populations. Recent studies by our group have shown hypoxia to be an endocrine disruptor that impairs sex differentiation and reproductive function in fish, leading to male-biased F1 populations of zebrafish and Japanese medaka. Such shifts in sex ratio are likely to have serious consequences for the reproduction and recruitment of fish assemblages inhabiting small water bodies, potentially leading to losses to biodiversity and fishery productivity. Fish possess a multitude of sex determination and differentiation systems to facilitate their adaptation to dynamic changes to the environment. Recent evidence has indicated that the sex-determination and differentiation system in fish is sensitive to several environmental (extrinsic) factors such as population density, social behaviors, pH and dissolved oxygen levels. Despite this, the molecular mechanisms through which hypoxia alters fish sex differentiation, and therefore sex ratios, remains poorly understood. In order to understand the potential role of miRNAs in mediating hypoxia-altered sex determination and differentiation in fish, we carried out (1) luciferase reporter assays to test if AR, NCOR and SRC are targeted by selected miRNAs and we found that the miRNAs to be non-inhibitory by cell transfection studies, and (2) small RNA sequencing and transcriptome sequencing on marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) embryos that were exposed to hypoxia for 40 hours (encompassing a critical window of sex determination). We identified 131 deregulated conserved and novel miRNAs in the hypoxia-exposed embryo, and bioinformatic analysis of the integrative small RNA sequencing and transcriptome sequencing results revealed hypoxia to cause alterations to embryonic development through miRNA and mRNA regulation. Importantly, we have identified miRNA-mRNA pairs that may be involved in hypoxia-altered gonad development, sex hormone response, and sex characteristics. To determine if exposure of fish embryos to hypoxia would alter the sex ratio at adult stage, one hundred normoxia- and hypoxia-exposed adult fish were harvested at 4 months for sex characterization of the gonads. No significant difference in sex ratio was observed in the hypoxia group relative to the normoxia group.

11102918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102918.value: In this project, our integrative analysis of small RNA sequencing and transcriptome sequencing have identified 253 conserved miRNA and 572 novel miRNAs in the medaka embryo. The larger number of novel miRNAs being identified in this study compared to conserved miRNAs suggests that many marine medaka miRNAs are yet to be identified. In particular, we have identified several miRNA-mRNA pairs that were reported to play roles in gonad development (novel miR-145-col9a3 and novel miRNA-94- arid5b), in sex hormone response (novel miRNA-210-ca2, novel miRNA-106-nr2f2, nbr-miR-29c-nr4a1, and ola-miR-92b-akr1d1), and in sex characteristic development (novel miRNA-145-mns1, nle-miR-20-sord, and ipu-miR-219b-abcc8). Our findings highlighted the possible roles of miRNA–mRNA in regulation of embryonic development and sex determination in response to hypoxic stress. The research can be extended to further elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the interactions between the miRNA-mRNA pairs uncovered in this study through gain- and loss-of function mutation studies in medaka embryos to identify prognostic and predictive biomarkers of hypoxia-induced endocrine disruption.

11102918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102918.value: Compared with mammals, fishes possess an exceptional range of sex determination and differentiation processes, which are modulated by a variety of environmental factors such as population density, social behaviors, pH and dissolved oxygen. Hypoxia is a widespread and pressing environmental problem in aquatic habitats, causing severe habitat damage and major changes to aquatic ecosystems worldwide. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) represent an important gene regulatory network that facilitates the epigenetic control of gene expression and protein translation in a tissue-specific manner, making them an important group of regulators of genes involved in sex determination/differentiation during development. In fish, there is a paucity of data on the roles of miRNAs in early sex differentiation and sex determination. This project has investigated the possible roles of miRNAs in mediating sex differentiation and sex determination in fish by transcriptome sequencing of marine medaka embryos that were exposed to continuous hypoxia at the critical time window of sex determination, and we have identified a cluster of miRNA-mRNA pairs that may be involved in regulating the reproductive axis and sex determination/differentiation in fish. Further studies are required to confirm the role of these novel miRNA-mRNA pairs in physiological processes of hypoxia-altered sex determination and differentiation in fish.

11103318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103318.value: 上皮間質轉化是指細胞從上皮細胞特性轉化為間質細胞特性的過程，反映了細胞卓越的可塑性。上皮間質轉化在多細胞生物的發育過程中具有重要作用，但惡性腫瘤細胞也通過這一過程獲得侵襲和轉移的能力。去極性化是上皮間質轉化的一個重要的細胞學特征，受到包括TGF-β通路在內的復雜信號網絡調控。目前已知許多控制細胞極性的分子都參與在上皮間質轉化的調節中，例如頂端-基底極性的蛋白可以控制細胞結構的上皮間質轉化。 平面極性(PCP)控制與頂端-基底軸垂直平面的極性，其在上皮間質轉化中的作用還不清楚。 Vangl2是平面極性信號的核心功能蛋白，在組織結構和形態發育中有重要作用。同時Vangl2的異常升高也常見於惡性腫瘤中，但是機制並不清楚。我們的前期工作發現TGF-β誘導的上皮間質轉化伴隨有Vangl2表達水平的顯著升高，且其對去上皮極性的過程有重要作用。與此同時，過量表達Vangl2可以破壞上皮細胞的極性和促進TGF-β誘導的上皮間質轉化。我們的蛋白組學研究表明Vangl2與PKCζ相互作用並解離PAR極性蛋白復合體。同時我們還發現TGF-β可以誘導Vangl2與PKCζ的結合。這些發現使我們預測Vangl2與PKCζ的復合體在上皮間質轉化中有重要的調節作用。為了驗証這一假設，我們將綜合運用生物化學和顯微成像技術來進行兩個方向的研究。第一個方向是明確Vangl2與PKCζ促進PAR蛋白復合體和細胞極性解離的分子機制。在第二個方向中，我們將研究Vangl2-PKCζ信號與TGF-β通路在上皮間質轉化過程的交叉整合。我們的研究將闡明平面極性信號在上皮間質轉化中的作用，同時可能發現針對腫瘤惡性轉化的新靶點。

11103318.label: Realisation of objectives
11103318.value: Realization of objectives: To elucidate the molecular wiring of planar cell polarity (PCP) signaling in the EMT of cancer cells, it is important to elucidate the interactions of PCP and other polarity signaling components. Our studies pointed to the key role of Vangl2, a core PCP protein, in regulating the stability of PKCzeta-Par6, an essential complex of tight junction and cell polarity. In addition, we have identified that TGF-β signaling regulates Vangl2-PKCzeta in promoting EMT. These studies provide a solid foundation for a major research direction in my laboratory -- to delineate the regulation of cell polarity in cancer progression. The primary goal of this funded project is to dissect the role of Vangl2-PKCzeta in cell polarity regulation and cancer cell EMT. We hypothesize that Vangl2-mediated regulation of cell polarity is critical for EMT. We addressed this hypothesis with two objectives: Objective 1: Map the molecular domains that mediate Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction and determine their functions in epithelial polarity. We dissected the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction in the structural and functional aspects through three subaims. 1.1) To determine the structural basis of Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction. Human Vangl2 is a protein of 521 amino acids with four transmembrane domains and intracellular N- and C- termin. The C-terminal intracellular region (283 amino acids) contains a coiled-coil domain and a PDZ-binding motif. At the same time, PKCzeta (590 amino acids) is a serine/threonine protein kinase with an N-terminal Phox-BEM1 (PB-1) domain and C-terminal AGC domain. To map the interacting domains of Vangl2-PKCzeta, we employed T7- and Flag-tagged deletion mutants of Vangl2 and PKCzeta with the removal of discrete regions. Following co-expressing the deletion mutants and intact counterparts in HEK293T cells, IP and immunoblotting were conducted. The results indicated that deletion of the PDZ binding motif (PBM) inhibited the interaction of Vangl2 with PKCzeta. In contrast, the deletion of the N-terminal PB-1 domain completely abolished the interaction of PKCzeta with Vangl2. Based on these results, we conclude that Vangl2 interacts with PKCzeta through their PDZ binding motif (PBM) and PB-1 domain, respectively. Furthermore, we cloned the PBM and PB-1 domain of Vangl2 and PKCzeta respectively, and validated their direct binding. Based on these results, we conclude that Vangl2 interacts with PKCzeta through the PBM and PB-1 domain, respectively. Therefore, this subaim was completed successfully. 1.2) To define the molecular mechanisms underlying the role of Vangl2-PKCzeta in disassembling the PAR complex. The primary goal of this sub-aim was to test whether the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction is important in mediating the disassembly of the PAR complex. The constructs of PKCzeta-GFP, HA-Par6, and myc-Par3 were co-expressed in HEK293T cells, in the presence and absence of 3xFlag-tagged full-length Vangl2 and the ΔPBM mutant of Vangl2. Anti-HA IP assay was performed to investigate the interactions of the PAR complex. While the full-length Vangl2 disrupted the interaction of Par6 with PKCzeta and Par3, the ΔPBM mutant failed in doing so. These results indicate that the direct interaction between Vangl2 and PKCzeta binding is necessary for interrupting the interactions of Par6-PKCzeta-Par3, potentially through competitive binding. Therefore, this subaim was completed successfully. 1.3) To validate that the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction regulates epithelial polarity. The goal of this aim was to validate whether the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction is implicated in the regulation of epithelial polarity and homeostasis. Therefore, we have established NMuMG cells that stably overexpress 3xFlag-tagged full-length Vangl2 and the ΔPBM mutant of Vangl2. Employing these cells, we showed that overexpression of wild-type Vangl2, but not the ΔPBM mutant that does not interact with PKCzeta, could disrupt the polarity of epithelial cells in 2D and 3D cultures. Therefore, we have successfully completed this objective to dissect the structural-functional mechanisms Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction in epithelial polarity. Objective 2. Delineating the function and regulation of Vangl2-PKCzeta in TGF-β-induced EMT. Based on our previous findings, we hypothesized that the interaction between Vangl2 and PKCzeta plays a key role in TGF-β-induced EMT. To address this, we employed functional genetics and proteomics to evaluate how Vangl2-PKC modulate the organization of signaling networks in TGF-β-induced EMT. 2.1) To define the function of Vangl2-PKCzeta in TGF-β-induced EMT. The original plan was to use a knockout-rescue approach to study the importance of the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction in TGF-β-induced EMT and define the associated cellular reorganizations. Based on the plan, we have applied the CRISPR/Cas9 technology to generate Vangl2-/- NMuMG cells. However, we observed a significantly enhanced expression of Vangl1 in the isolated Vangl2-/- cells, suggesting a potential compensation in certain functions. To avoid complications in interpreting results, we took the alternative approach as planned in the original proposal. Briefly, we established NMuMG cell lines that stably express Flag-tagged full-length or the PBM mutant of Vangl2, which was resistant to the silencing of 3’UTR-targeting siRNA. A control cell line stably transfected with empty control vector was also established. Following the siRNA-mediated knockdown of Vangl2, we observed a significant inhibition of TGF-β-induced EMT, accompanied by stabilization of the PAR complex. Importantly, this inhibition was prevented in cells stably expressing full-length, but not the ΔPBM mutant of Vangl2 that is resistant to siRNA. These results supported the role of Vangl2-PKCzeta in TGF-β-induced EMT and accomplished this subaim. 2.2 To elucidate the mechanism underlying TGF-β-induced assembly of Vangl2-PKCzeta complexes. When silencing different components of TGF-β as planned, we encountered difficulties including redundancies of the components and cross-talks with the Ras-MAPK pathway. Data interpretation was challenging. However, as stated below, we still revealed TGF-β-mediated regulation of Vangl2-PKCzeta via achievements in subaim 2.3. We are preparing a manuscript covering these findings and the draft is attached. 2.3 To dissect the Vangl2-PKCzeta signaling circuits in in TGF-β-induced EMT. We successfully installed the nLC-Q Exactive HF mass spectrometry system in the laboratory. This ensured the successful delineation of signaling circuits using proteomics in this project. After extensive screening and optimization, we obtained antibodies of Vangl2 and PKCzeta that facilitated endogenous IP coupled to LC-MS/MS. This enabled us to establish a network of endogenous proteins that interact with Vangl2-PKCzeta. Among the Vangl2 interactors, we were interested in the E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7. Through collaboration with Dr. GAO Bo (then at HKU), we demonstrated that Vangl proteins are tightly controlled by the ubiquitin-proteasome system through endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD). The key ERAD component p97/VCP directly binds to Vangl at a highly conserved VCP-interacting motif and recruits KBTBD7 via its UBA-UBX adaptors to promote Vangl ubiquitination and degradation. These results were published in the top journal Science Advances in 2021. Interestingly, we further revealed that TGF-β stabilizes Vangl2 by inhibiting its interaction with KBTBD7, which depends on the kinase activity of PKCzeta. The working model is that in parallel to Vangl2-mediated disassembly of PAR complex, PKCzeta may mediate a feedback activity that controls Vangl2 in driving cancer cell EMT. We will consolidate this model in the future and explore different PKCzeta inhibitors for their potential antagonizing EMT and breast cancer metastasis. In summary, we have realized both objectives of the original proposal. This project defined the mechanisms for the novel role and regulation of PCP signaling in cancer cell EMT. Our future studies will continue to investigate the role of PKCzeta and different lncRNAs in cell polarity and cancer progression.

11103318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103318.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP) controls the asymmetric organization of cellular structures and activities across the epithelial plane and is of critical importance to tissue development and health. However, our understanding of the regulation of PCP signaling in human cancer remains rudimentary. With the funding support of this project, we made important findings that advanced our understanding of the regulation of cell polarity in the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of cancer cells. The findings were achieved through addressing the two proposed objectives. Our first major finding is that Vangl2 (a core PCP component) antagonizes the PKCzeta-PAR complex and promotes EMT of breast cancer cells. We delineated the structural and functional aspects of Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction. Our results revealed that the interaction between Vangl2 and PKCzeta is mediated through their PDZ binding motif and the PB-1 domain, respectively. Moreover, we also illustrated that Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction is functionally important for the disassembly of PKCzeta-PAR complex and EMT of breast cancer cells. Another major finding of this project is that Vangl proteins are tightly controlled by the ubiquitin-proteasome system through endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD). The key ERAD component p97/VCP directly binds to Vangl at a highly conserved VCP-interacting motif and recruits the E3 ligase KBTBD7 via its UBA-UBX adaptors to promote Vangl ubiquitination and degradation. We further revealed that TGF-β stabilizes Vangl2 by inhibiting its interaction with KBTBD7, which depends on the kinase activity of PKCzeta. We propose a mechanism that in parallel to Vangl2-mediated disassembly of PAR complex, PKCzeta may mediate a feedback activity that controls Vangl2 in driving cancer cell EMT. In addition to the above findings, we also investigated the functions of pro-cancer lncRNAs in regulating cell polarity and EMT. We have successfully developed a method named CRISPR-Assisted RNA-Protein Interactome Detection (CARPID). It leverages CRISPR/CasRx-based RNA targeting and proximity labeling-enabled affinity purification and mass spectrometry (AP/MS) to identify RBPs of specific RNA molecules in living cells, without depending on chemical- or UV-mediated crosslinking. We have successfully applied CARPID in identifying the interacting proteome of several lncRNAs, including DANCR and MALAT1, revealing their novel implications in cell polarity. We have published this method in the top journal Nature Methods in 2020. Overall, findings from this project defined novel mechanisms for the regulation of PCP signaling and cell polarity during EMT of cancer cells. These results have led to publications in the top journals Science Advances and Nature Methods.

11103318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103318.value: This project defined the mechanisms for the function and regulation of planar cell polarity component Vangl2 in regulating cancer cell EMT. Further developments are undergoing in two aspects to explore the translational value of findings from this project. 1. Although the role of Vangl2 in cancer development has been previously investigated, it remains unclear about how its signaling regulation and implication in vivo. To address this, we will collaborate with Prof. Xiaoyan Qiu at Peking University to confirm the significance of TGFbeta-Vangl2 signaling and breast cancer metastasis using mouse model and patient samples. 2. Inhibitors of PKCzeta are drug candidates for cancer treatment. This project defined a novel functional mechanism of Vangl2-PKCzeta that involves the interacting domains and the importance of PKCzeta kinase activity. Based on our discoveries, we will collaborate with Prof. Jian ZHANG at Shanghai Jiaotong University to develop inhibitors that may target the Vangl2-PKCzeta signaling to inhibit cancer cell EMT.

11103318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103318.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP) controls the organization of cellular structures and activities in our cells and is of critical importance to tissue development and health. However, our understanding of the function and regulation of PCP in cancer remains rudimentary. This project discovered that Vangl2, a core PCP component at cell membrane, interacts with kinase PKCzeta and disrupts the PAR complex, which regulates tight junctions that limit the invasive behaviors of breast cancer cell. We have dissected the Vangl2-PKCzeta interaction and decoded their mutual regulation using functional proteomic studies. In addition, we developed a method to investigate how long non-coding RNAs interact with proteins in cancer progression. The findings of this project provide important insights into how breast cancer cells control the cellular structure during invasion and metastasis. Further studies are undergoing to develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic tools for various cancer.

11103418.value: 发生于中枢神经系统的神经退行性疾病，如阿尔茨海默氏病，十分错综复杂，这是因为大脑中不仅神经元，而且神经胶质细胞（如星形胶质细胞）也受到损伤。这导致各种类型的细胞丢失或获得一些功能，以此对大脑产生保护和/或毒性作用。最近关于星形胶质细胞在神经退行性疾病中的研究证明，反应性星形胶质细胞（星形胶质细胞的活性形式），通过其分子变化（如基因表达），细胞层面的变化（如细胞结构）和功能性变化（如细胞增殖），同时具有神经保护作用和神经毒性作用。然而，现今并不清楚反应性星形胶质细胞，是如何在神经退行性病症中转换它们的功能和状态，以响应来自细胞间隙的信号。 我们的初步结果表明，在神经退化的病理条件下，所有神经细胞的昼夜节律钟都发生了变化。昼夜节律钟存在于大多数组织中，是内源性振荡器，它通过调控成千上万基因的表达，来调节不同的细胞过程和信号传导途径，以此驱动日常生物节律变换。有趣的是，在神经退化的病理条件下，星形胶质细胞中的昼夜节律钟呈现出与其他神经细胞不同的表达模式，即昼夜节律基因的表达首先下调，然后减弱或上调。这暗示了昼夜节律钟可能随着神经退化的进展而变化，并通过改变的昼夜节律基因表达来改变细胞过程或信号传导途径。 基于我们的初步结果和已有的文献，我们提出假说：昼夜节律钟作为反应性星形胶质细胞功能和状态的转换开关。为此，我们将专注于两个主要目标：1）鉴定在神经退化的病理条件下，与反应性星形胶质细胞功能相关的分子机制; 2）验证昼夜节律基因表达变化的模式，以及星形胶质细胞功能的变换：非反应性和反应性形式；神经保护与神经毒性作用。从这个项目，我们将提供明确的证据来说明，昼夜节律钟通过控制星形胶质细胞，从而影响神经退化的进程。
