11103718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103718.value: Ovarian cancer is the leading cause of gynecological cancer-related death among women, with less than 30% 10-year survival from diagnosis. High grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is the most frequent histological subtype of ovarian cancer, and is associated with worse outcome. Although 90% of early stage HGSOC patients could be cured with current therapies, the majority of HGSOC patients have poor prognosis due to the advance stage at diagnosis, widespread metastasis and high recurrence rate. At present HGSOC can be classified by histopathology, FIGO stage and tumor grade, but these characteristics are insufficient to identify clinically relevant subgroups. Furthermore, genetic analysis of HGSOC has identified many genetic alterations, but relatively few consistent driver genes. How to stratify HGSOC patients into molecularly distinct subtypes, in relation to clinical outcomes, is critical for selection of patients for more optimized therapies and design of targeted agents. Gene expression-based subtyping has been widely accepted as a relevant source of disease stratification. Several independent classification systems have identified four largely overlapping HGSOC subtypes, “immunoreactive”, “differentiated”, “proliferative” and “mesenchymal”. The four subtypes have been recapitulated in a recent study, highlighting potential association of the mesenchymal subtype with poor outcome. However, transcriptome-based molecular subtyping has several limitations, hampering its potential clinical translation. First, molecular heterogeneity exists at different (epi-)genetic levels of gene regulation, which may not be fully captured at the transcriptome level. Second, currently classification of HGSOC is only possible for transcriptome data, preventing more efficient use of other type of -omic data. Third, the current HGSOC classification system requires robust measurement of hundreds of signature genes, which cannot be easily realized in the clinic. More clinically accessible markers such as single driver mutations specific to the mesenchymal subtype have not been clearly identified. In this project, we aim to address the abovementioned challenges by integrative analysis of multi-omic data and clinical data involving over 3700 primary tissue samples across 23 public datasets and 2 in-house clinical cohorts. Our 1st objective is to perform unsupervised classification of multi-omic data projected onto a unified space using complete canonical correlation analysis followed by data fusion. Using the established multi-omic classifier, our 2nd objective is to comprehensively characterize identified HGSOC subtypes. Focusing on the mesenchymal subtype, our 3rd objective is to dissect the underlying regulatory mechanisms using a multidimensional network-based approach, and prioritize master regulators followed by biological and clinical validations by our experimental collaborators. 卵巢癌是導致婦科癌症相關死亡的主要原因，診斷後10年生存率低於30％。高級別漿液性腫瘤（HGSOC）是卵巢癌最常見的組織學亞型，並且與較差的臨床結果相關。雖然90％的早期HGSOC患者可以通過現有療法治愈，但大多數HGSOC患者由於診斷時已進入晚期、並出現轉移和高複發，因而預後不良。目前，HGSOC可以通過組織病理學、FIGO分期和腫瘤分級進行分類，但這些特徵不足以鑑定臨床相關的亞型。此外，HGSOC的遺傳分析已經發現了許多基因突變，但其中只有少量的一致驅動基因。如何將HGSOC患者分為不同的、與臨床結果相關的分子亞型，對於優化患者的治療方案和靶向藥物的設計至關重要。 基於基因表達的分子分型方法已被廣泛接受為有效的疾病分類策略。幾個獨立的分類系統已經基本確定了四個HGSOC亞型，即：“免疫反應型”，“分化型”，“增殖型”和“間充質型”。最近的一項研究中重述了這四種亞型，並突出了間充質亞型與不良預後的潛在關聯。然而，基於轉錄組的分子分型具有若干局限性，阻礙了其潛在的臨床轉化。首先，分子異質性存在於不同層次的遺傳和表觀遺傳調控，不能僅僅在轉錄組水平上捕獲。其次，目前HGSOC的分類系統僅可用於轉錄組數據，而不能更有效地應用於其他類型的數據。第三，目前的HGSOC分類系統需要對數百個特徵基因表達水平進行檢測，而這在臨床上是不容易實現的。更多適用於臨床的標誌物，例如對間充質亞型特異的單一驅動突變，尚未被清楚地鑑定。 在這個項目中，我們的目標是通過綜合分析包括23個公共數據集和2個內部臨床隊列的3700多個主要組織樣本的多組學數據和臨床數據來解決上述難題。我們的第一個目標是進行典型相關分析和數據融合，然後對投射到統一空間的多組學數據進行無監督分類。使用已建立的多組學分類器，我們的第二個目標是全面表徵已識別的HGSOC亞型。關注間充質亞型，我們的第三個目標是使用基於多維度網絡推斷的方法來剖析潛在的調節機制，並篩選主調節因子，然後由我們的實驗合作者進行生物學和臨床驗證。

11103718.label: Realisation of objectives
11103718.value: Objective 1. Multi-omic molecular subtyping of HGSOC based on complete conventional correlation analysis followed by data fusion The first goal of this project was to perform molecular subtyping of HGSOC based on multi-omics data. Our fundamental hypothesis was that integrating different types of omics profiles for unsupervised classification will generate more biologically coherent and clinically relevant cancer subtypes. To this end, we developed a multi-omics cancer classification framework—Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis for Cancer Classification (SCCA-CC), which projects each type of single-omics data onto a unified space for data fusion, followed by clustering and classification analysis. To demonstrate the usefulness of SCCA-CC, we first integrated two types of omics data, mRNA and miRNA profiles, for molecular classification of HGSOC using TCGA dataset (n = 462). We performed consensus clustering and identified four HGSOC subtypes (HGSOC1-4), which recapitulated the four subtypes previously defined, i.e., proliferative, immunoreactive, differentiated and mesenchymal. In addition to mRNA and miRNA profiles, we next performed more comprehensive subtyping by incorporating copy number variation (CNV), single nucleotide variant (SNV) and DNA methylation profiles. Using TCGA dataset for discovery, we identified five robust multi-omics HGSOC subtypes (MHGSOC1-5), of which MHGSOC1, 3, and 4 recapitulated immunoreactive, proliferative, and differentiated subtypes, respectively. Interestingly, the previously well-characterized mesenchymal subtype can be further divided into two molecularly distinct subgroups—MHGSOC2 and MHGSOC5. For broad applications, we established a multi-omics classifier, which achieved a high performance (AUC = 0.95) based on 5-fold cross validations. Compared to existing multi-omics subtyping methods, the MHGSOC classifier we established can take as input either a single type of omics data or a combination of any multiple types of data, which greatly extends the applicability of ovarian cancer subtyping to facilitate clinical translations. Objective 2. Comprehensive molecular and clinical characterizations of multi-omic HGSOC subtypes Our second goal was to comprehensively characterize the multi-omics subtypes of HGSOC molecularly and clinically. Using TCGA dataset, we first systematically characterized the CNV, SNV, mRNA and miRNA expression, as well as DNA methylation features in each HGSOC subtype. Between the five subtypes, we found in total 1592 differentially expressed genes, 117 differentially expressed miRNAs, 6448 genes with differential promoter DNA methylation, 11857 genes with differential CNV, and 145 genes with differentially enriched mutations. Compared with the other subtypes, MHGSOC5-mesenchymal tumors had the most differentially expressed mRNAs. MHGSOC1-immunoreactive and MHGSOC3-proliferative tumors had a relatively high prevalence of somatic copy number alterations (SCNAs). MHGSOC2 tumors were featured by higher overall DNA methylation levels. MHGSOC4-differentiated tumors had relatively lower mutation counts. Using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), we found that the five MHGSOC subtypes were characterized by specific biological properties. MHGSOC1 tumors had immune activation, a major feature of the immunoreactive subtype previously defined. MHGSOC3 is associated with cancer stemness, which is a characteristic of the proliferative subtype defined earlier. MHGSOC4 is characterized by upregulated cell differentiation, which is consistent with its significant association with the differentiated subtype. MHGSOC5 is featured with activated TGF-β and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) pathways. Furthermore, assessments of tumor purity, stromal content and immune infiltration by ESTIMATE revealed that the MHGSOC3-proliferative and MHGSOC4-differentiated subtypes were more enriched for tumor epithelial cells. MHGSOC1 and MHGSOC5 tumors had higher immune cell abundance, while MHGSOC5 tumors also contained significantly higher stroma content. More in-depth analysis of the immune microenvironment by CIBERSORT confirmed that MHGSOC1 and MHGSOC5 tumors had higher infiltration of CD8 T cells, M2 macrophages and neutrophils. Interestingly, tumors classified to these two subtypes also had upregulated CD274 and PDCD1LG2, which code for PD-L1 and PD-L2, respectively. Overall, clinical parameters, including age, lymphatic invasion, anatomic neoplasm subdivision were similar among the subtypes. Survival analysis revealed that MHGSOC subtypes were significantly associated with overall survival (OS) (P = 0.0024, log-rank test), where patients classified to the MHGSOC5-mesenchymal subtype displayed the poorest outcomes. However, using the TCGA taxonomy, no significant association was found with OS (P = 0.12). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard regression analysis revealed that patient age and MHGSOC5 were significantly associated with OS, and MHGSOC5 is a more significant risk factor (P = 0.0002, HR = 2.48). For validation, we analyzed eight independent public datasets with single-omics or multi-omics profiles with available clinical information, totaling 981 patient samples. Using the multi-omics classifier trained on the TCGA dataset, we first classified the ICGC-OV-AU dataset (n = 79) with all the five types of omics data. As expected, the subtyping result showed significant association with OS (P = 0.0014), and MHGSOC5 patients had the poorest survival. Compared with MHGSOC2, MHGSOC5 showed much poorer OS (P = 0.00042). Using the merged cohort of the other seven datasets (Cope, Bonome, Tothill, Mateescu, OV133, Bagnoli and Reyes) totaling around 900 patient samples, we validated that MHGSOC5 was also associated with poorer OS (P = 0.0065). Objective 3. Dissecting regulatory mechanisms underlying the mesenchymal subtype of HGSOC using a multidimensional network approach To elucidate subtype-specific regulatory mechanism, we first inferred a miRNA regulatory network by integrative analysis of mRNA and miRNA expression profiles in the TCGA dataset. To identify master regulators for the mesenchymal subtype, master regulator analysis was subsequently performed by testing overrepresentation of each miRNA’s regulon for EMT signature genes. Using the strategy, we found miR-508-3p was the most statistically significant master regulator (P = 0.019, hypergeometric test). Compared to non-mesenchymal subtypes, we observed significantly lower expression of miR-508-3p in the mesenchymal subtype in TCGA dataset. In a combined dataset of Bagnoli (n=130), OV133 (n=133) and OV179 (n=179), miR-508-3p expression was prognostic of both OS and progression-free survival (PFS). As our in-house validation, we examined the expression of miR-508-3p in the FFPE specimens of OvCa patients in West China cohort using qPCR analysis. We observed that lower expression of miR-508-3p was associated with significantly poorer OS and PFS. In both the three public datasets and West China cohort, the expression of miR-508-3p is predictive of survival independent of pathological stages and grades. Based on in vitro and in vivo experimental validations performed by our collaborators, we found that miR-508-3p down-regulation, due to promoter hypermethylation, was directly correlated with metastatic behaviors. Furthermore, focusing on the MHGSOC5-mesenchymal subtype, we inferred a regulatory network by integrating the expression levels of 52 upregulated transcription factors (TFs), seven downregulated miRNAs, and 866 putative target genes that are differentially expressed between MHGSOC5 and the other four subtypes. Master regulator analysis identified ten TFs (EGR2, NKX3-2, MEOX2, HAND2, MEIS3, NR4A3, BARX1, MSC, HEY1, and EGR3) and one miRNA (miR-1287-3p) , whose regulons were significantly enriched for EMT signature genes. Integrating with DNA methylation profiles, we found that the expression of HAND2 was significantly inversely correlated with its promoter methylation, suggesting that HAND2 might promote EMT due to its promoter hypomethylation in the MHGSOC5 subtype specifically. Taken together, our multidimensional network analysis identified miRNAs and TFs as potential master regulators that define the mesenchymal subtype and provide novel prognostic biomarker to improve management of this disease, which warrants more in-depth mechanistic investigations in the future.

11103718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103718.value: 1. We developed SCCA-CC, a computational framework for cancer classification based on sparse canonical correlation analysis of multi-omics profiles (Qi L et al., Frontiers in Genetics 2021). SCCA-CC projects each type of single-omics data onto a unified space for data fusion, followed by clustering and classification analysis. Without loss of generality, as case studies, we integrated two types of omics data, mRNA and miRNA profiles, for molecular classification of HGSOC. The four subtypes we identified recapitulated the subtypes previously defined by TCGA, and displayed a significant association with overall survival, while the TCGA taxonomy did not. The multi-omics classifier we established can not only classify individual types of data but also demonstrated higher accuracies on the fused data. Compared with existing methods, SCCA-CC demonstrated its superiority by identifying subtypes of higher coherence, clinical relevance, and time efficiency. Extending to five types of omics data (mRNA, miRNA, SNV, CNV and DNA methylation), we identified five robust multi-omics subtypes (termed MHGSOC1-5), followed by comprehensive molecular and clinical characterizations. Interestingly, the mesenchymal subtype was subdivided into two subgroups, of which MHGSOC5 is featured by activated TGF-β pathway, EMT, higher immune and stroma infiltration and poorer survival. 2. We elucidated the regulatory mechanism underlying the mesenchymal subtype of HGSOC using a multi-dimensional network approach (Zhao L et al., Oncogene 2018). We inferred a miRNA regulatory network by integrative analysis of mRNA and miRNA expression profiles. miR-508-3p emerged as the most powerful determinant that regulates a cascade of dysregulated genes in the mesenchymal subtype, including core genes involved in EMT program. Moreover, miR-508-3p down-regulation, due to promoter hypermethylation, was directly correlated with metastatic behaviors in vitro and in vivo. Focusing on the MHGSOC5 subgroup, we found ten TFs and one miRNA as potential EMT regulators, of which HAND2 might promote EMT due to its promoter hypomethylation. 3. We also developed OCaMIR—an eight-circulating miRNA signature for non-invasive detection of early-stage ovarian cancer (Kandimalla R et al., Clinical Cancer Research 2021). Due to the lack of effective screening approaches and early detection biomarkers, ovarian cancer has the highest mortality rates among gynecologic cancers. We undertook a genome-wide biomarker discovery followed by large-scale multi-center validations, involving over 1800 patients and healthy participants in four tissue cohorts, three retrospective and one prospective serum cohorts. OCaMIR demonstrated high sensitivities and specificities in all the serum cohorts, and showed a significantly superior diagnostic performance compared with CA125 levels, even in stage I patients.

11103718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103718.value: Several findings in the project have the potential for clinical translation, pending future experimental and clinical validations. (1) We developed a robust HGSOC subtype classification framework—SCCA-CC, which could be applied to both single-omics and multi-omics data types, greatly facilitating the research community and potential clinical translation for precision oncology. (2) We identified miR-508-3p as the determinant of the mesenchymal subtype of HGSOC, as well as its downstream target LOX, which both showed the potential to be prognostic biomarkers and novel therapeutic targets. (3) We developed OCaMIR—an eight-circulating miRNA signature, demonstrating a high potential for early detection of ovarian cancer. To eventually translate these findings into the clinic, in-depth mechanistic studies and large-scale cohort studies with a more rigorous experimental design are needed, which is beyond the scope of this project. However, during the project, we have established close collaborations with multiple research institutions and hospitals such as West China Second Hospital affiliated with Sichuan University and the Beckman Research Institute at City of Hope. We plan to apply for collaborative grants together with these collaborators to support further development of the research, which we believe will eventually benefit patients in the future.

11103718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103718.value: Ovarian cancer is one of the most lethal malignancies in women. In the last two decades, although effective surgery and adjuvant therapy have contributed to improved survival, the overall cure rate remains only about 30%. One critical challenge lies in the heterogeneous nature of this deadly malignancy, resulted in discrepant clinical outcomes to treatment. How to stratify ovarian cancer patients into molecularly distinct subtypes, in relation to clinical outcomes, is critical for selection of patients for more optimized therapies and design of targeted agents. In this project, we interrogated the heterogeneity of high grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most frequent histological subtype of ovarian cancer. Different from previous studies, we performed more comprehensive subtyping by integrating genomics, transcriptomics, and epigenomics profiles based on multi-omics data fusion. We obtained a landscape of subtype-specific molecular properties, tumor microenvironment, and clinical associations. With multiple independent datasets, we demonstrated that our multi-omics HGSOC taxonomy was more biologically coherent and clinically relevant. Focusing on the poor prognosis mesenchymal subtype of HGSOC, we elucidated the regulatory mechanisms based on a multi-dimensional network approach. We identified multiple transcription factors, miRNAs and downstream target genes, showing a great potential as novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, prognosis and therapeutic targets.

11103918.value: Aim 1: Characterizing the exosomes derived from GMs and ECs under hypoxia and normoxia. To investigate the effect of hypoxia on the release, uptake, and composition of the exosomes from GMs and ECs, the analysis of metabolic proteins in exosomal membrane, or intra-exosomal metabolites, will be conducted with sensitive biosensing and metabolomic techniques. Release and uptake assays of the exosomes will be conducted to investigate their correlation with metabolic and phenotypic changes of GMs and ECs. Aim 2: Determining the effect of loss or gain of MCT1 & CD147 function in the exosome-mediated interactions between GMs and ECs under hypoxia. The expression of MCT1 and CD147 will be genetically modulated in the cellular level and the exosomal level by the KD or OE of MCT1 and CD147 in their parental cells. Each group of isolated exosomes will be applied to recipient cells to test their function. Additionally, the exosome-mediated interactions between the two cell types will also be tested in our novel microfluidic co-culture system to gain a better interpretation for the complex mutual interactions. Aim 3: Determining the effect of the inhibitors for MCT1 or CD147 in the exosome-induced phenotypic change of GMs and ECs under hypoxia. To test whether the inhibitors for MCT1 or CD147 with TMZ can prevent the phenotypic change of GMs and ECs via modifying the exosome-mediated interactions between GMs and ECs, the various experiments described in Aim 1 & 2 will be conducted, including the interaction study in the microfluidic co-culture system. Additionally, GMs invasion via using organotypic brain-slice culture from either wild-type- or nude- mice (an ex vivo model) will be tested with or sans pre-treatment with the inhibitors with or without TMZ to GMs before implantation.

Aim 3: Determining the effect of the inhibitors for MCT1 or CD147 in the exosome-induced phenotypic change of GMs and ECs under hypoxia. To test whether the inhibitors for MCT1 or CD147 with TMZ can prevent the phenotypic change of GMs and ECs via modifying the exosome-mediated interactions between GMs and ECs, the various experiments described in Aim 1 & 2 will be conducted, including the interaction study in the microfluidic co-culture system. Additionally, GMs invasion via using organotypic brain-slice culture from either wild-type- or nude- mice (an ex vivo model) will be tested with or sans pre-treatment with the inhibitors with or without TMZ to GMs before implantation.

11103918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103918.value: Malignant glioma is one of the most fatal tumors occurring in the central nervous system (CNS). Despite its common origin in glia and glial stem cells, diverse subtypes of glioma cells (GMs) are generated with various oncogenic mutations. Major types of gliomas include astrocytomas, oligodendrogliomas, and glioblastoma multiform (GBM). Irrespective of the type of glioma, one of the hallmarks of glioma progression is the metabolic shift towards aerobic glycolysis with the enhancement of glycolytic enzymes and transporters, including monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1) and its binding protein CD147, facilitating the movement of lactate across the plasma membrane. Exosomes, cell-secreted vesicles that range from 30-150 nm in size, exert multiple critical biological functions on the intercellular communication and modulation of the tumor microenvironment. Interestingly, GMs in the hypoxic microenvironment secrete tremendous amounts of exosomes, which can spread to distant target cells as well as surrounding stromal cells (SMs). However, the effects of GMs-derived exosomes on glioma progression have not been holistically investigated, particularly through the regulation of the release and uptake of exosomes as well as the production of pro-oncogenic exosomes by metabolic alterations. Our preliminary data revealed that hypoxia-induced exosomes contained significant levels of MCT1 and CD147 which could be detected by sensitive biosensing techniques, including Local Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM). Importantly, we first found that the level of MCT1 and CD147 in the membrane of GMs-derived exosomes reflected the metabolic and phenotypic status of parental GMs, suggesting that exosomal MCT1 and CD147 are great biomarkers for the detection of glioma progression in a liquid biopsy. In further experiments, we found that hypoxia induced GMs-derived and endothelial cell (ECs)-derived exosomes could enter recipient cells, altering their metabolism and phenotype, which was blocked partly by inhibiting the activity of MCT1 and CD147 at the cellular and exosomal level. Thus, we hypothesize that the exosome-mediated interactions between GMs and ECs are important processes for glioma progression, which can be regulated partly by MCT1 and CD147 at the level of cells and exosomes. Therefore, we plan on conducting experiments to determine the effect of loss or gain of MCT1 or CD147 function in the exosome-mediated interactions between GMs and ECs under hypoxia. Eventually, we hope to determine whether the inhibitors for MCT1 or CD147 together with an anti-glioma agent, temozolomide (TMZ), could reduce glioma progression partly by controlling the exosome-mediated phenotypic change of GMs and ECs under hypoxia.

11103918.label: Realisation of objectives
11103918.value: Aim 1 & Aim 2 Glioma cells (GMs) under hypoxia induced by chamber- or chemical- methods significantly increased their proliferation and migration as detected by MTT cell proliferation- and Transwell migration- & Scratch- assays. Importantly, hypoxic GMs’ fast metabolic shift to glycolysis, as detected by Sea-horse experiment, and dramatic upregulation of MCT1 and CD147, as measured by RT-qPCR, ICC, WB, and ELISA, were clearly demonstrated. Hypoxic GMs also significantly enhanced their exosome release, as detected by NTA, confirming the positive correlation of the malignant progression and glycolytic reprogramming of parent GMs and the increased release of daughter exosomes. Particularly, hypoxia-induced enhanced exosome release was dependent on intracellular Ca2+ level in GMs, as detected by Fura-2 & 4 Calcium Imaging. Next question was whether glycolysis-induced enhanced exosome release in GMs could be mediated by MCT1 and CD147. Thus, gain or loss of MCT1 and CD147 function on GMs’ phenotypic change and exosome release was tested by lentiviral overexpression (OE), and shRNA- or GapmeR- knockdown (KD) techniques. Interestingly, MCT1 or CD147 OE in normoxic GMs promoted their proliferation and migration as well as exosome release. In contrast, MCT1 or CD147 KD in hypoxic GMs reduced their proliferation and migration as well as exosome release. Importantly, MCT1 or CD147 KD in hypoxic GMs reduced intracellular Ca2+ level. In contrast, treatment of sodium-L-lactate to GMs increased intracellular Ca2+ level, confirming that enhanced exosome release by MCT1 and CD147 was mediated by increased intracellular Ca2+ level. To determine whether secreted exosomes from GMs could have MCT1 and CD147, exosomes were isolated by a size-exclusion- and ultracentrifugation- method and were characterized by TEM, Immunogold EM, WB, and ELISA. Surprisingly, significant number of MCT1 and CD147 were present in GMs-derived exosomes. Their amount was enhanced in hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes, indicating that exosomal level of MCT1 and CD147 were highly correlated with their level in parent GMs. To validate the data, exosomes from GMs by MCT1- and CD147- OE or KD were utilized as positive and negative controls, further confirming their presence in GMs-derived exosomes. This discovery indicated that MCT1 and CD147 level as well as secretion number of GMs- derived daughter exosomes could be used as surrogate biomarkers to track the metabolic reprogramming and malignant progression in parent GMs. To further characterize GMs-derived exosomes, various techniques, including NTA, AFM, LSPR, TEM, immunogold EM, FAES and etc were used. First, AFM detected 2-D & 3-D topographic image of GMs-derived exosomes, demonstrating their size, 30 to 200 nm in circumference, and morphology. Next, AFM determined biophysical properties of GMs-derived exosomes. NTA and TEM clearly revealed the distinct size and morphology of exosomes. For the precise and sensitive quantitative analysis of MCT1, MCT4, and CD147 level in exosomes from GMs and the blood of glioma-bearing mice, LSFR and AFM were utilized, demonstrating the feasibility that label-free LSPR- and AFM-based detection of exosomal MCT1, MCT4, and CD147 for tracking glioma progression. In the analysis of components of GMs-derived exosomes, tumor-associated proteins, such as EGFRvIII, BIGH3, CD44, CD133, and PD-L1, were identified by various techniques. In the analysis of metabolites and microRNA in exosomes, bioinformatics and molecular experiments indicated that proline, glutamine, glutamate, and lysine as well as microRNA 9, 10, and 21 were enriched in hypoxic GMs. In particular, distinct biomarkers in GMs-derived exosomes, such as exosomal MCT1, MCT4, and CD147, in the blood of mouse models of glioma and human patients (on-going) were detected and quantified by LSPR- and LSPR- biosensors, introducing and establishing new liquid biopsy methods for glioma diagnosis and prognosis. Recently, the enhanced interaction of GMs and ECs via exosomes has been proposed as an important factor to induce angiogenesis. Thus, to characterize ECs and ECs-derived exosomes, various experiments were conducted. Briefly, hypoxic ECs also promoted their proliferation and migration and exosome release. Hypoxia enhanced ECs’ MCT1 & 4, CD147. However, the quantitative analysis of MCT1, MCT4, and CD147 in CD31-postive ECs in the glioma-bearing mice indicated relatively weak expression as detected by immunohistochemistry. Absolute amounts of MCT1 and CD147 in ECs and ECs-derived exosomes were very tiny as compared with those seen in GMs & GMs-derived exosomes, indicating that MCT1- and CD147- associated metabolic reprogramming could be more specific to GMs. Peak size of ECs-derived exosomes was around 150 nm. TEM morphology revealed round shape. Immunogold EM indicated CD9 and CD63. Uptake of ECs-derived exosomes by GMs had a mild influence on GMs’ phenotype. To address whether GMs’ metabolic reprogramming could induce neovascularization via GMs-derived exosomes. uptake (e.g. dye-labeling method) of GMs-derived exosomes by ECs was conducted by a time-dependent and dose-dependent manner, and then its effect on ECs’ tube formation was tested. Enhanced uptake of hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes by ECs was significant, resulting into the promotion of ECs’ tube formation. This observation clearly demonstrated that hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes had a strong capacity to induce angiogenesis. The analysis of angiogenesis factors present in hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes has been under investigation, such as VEGF-A and microRNA21. MCT1 or CD147 KD in hypoxic GMs reduced exosome release and it modified levels of exosomal components, leading to the reduction of tube formation, proliferation, and migration of ECs by their uptake of MCT1- or CD147- KD- GMs-derived exosomes, as detected by exosome uptake-, tube formation-, MTT-, and transwell migration- assays. Co-culture of GMs and ECs under hypoxia also increased tube formation by ECs. Aim 3: In Aim 2, MCT1- and CD147- KD significantly decreased both GMs’ malignant progression and exosome secretion, suggesting that MCT1 and CD147 inhibitors could produce anti-cancer activity at the both cellular and exosomal level. Therefore, in Aim 3, an inhibitor for MCT1, AZD-3695, or MCT1-CD147 interaction, Thalidomide (instead of an inhibitor for CD147, AC73, due to its unavailability from a developer), as well as Temozolomide (TMZ) as a control were tested in their efficacy to produce anti-cancer activity. AZD-3965 and Thalidomide produced similar level of anti-proliferation activity to that of TMZ, and they induced altered cellular and nucleus morphology. Next, anti-migration activity by these agents were tested. AZD-3965 and Thalidomide clearly produced anti-migration effect for 24- and 48- hour- incubation. Combination of AZD-3965 and Thalidomide with TMZ further increased anti-proliferative and anti-migratory activity for GMs. At exosomal level, all three drugs significantly reduced exosome release. The result further supported the potential mechanism of anticancer activity through the inhibition of the release of pro-oncogenic exosomes from GMs and the blocking of uptake of pro-oncogenic exosomes. To investigate the effect of each drug on anti-glioma activity via exosomal communication, co-culture of GMs and ECs, and heterologous uptake of exosomes by GMs and ECs were conducted. All three drugs produced direct anticancer activity in co-culture. In particular, autologous and heterologous uptake of GMs-derived exosomes by GMs and ECs in the uptake assay produced very interesting results. All drugs were uploaded into exosomes after drug treatment. And drug-loaded exosomes significantly inhibited the proliferation and migration of GMs and ECs, and the tube formation of ECs, indicating that exosomes could be utilized as drug-loading vehicles as well as exosome release and uptake could be indeed drug targets for glioma pharmacotherapy. Thus, experiments about exosome-based glioma treatment (e.g. EXO-AZD-3965) using mouse models of glioma rather than exo vivo brain slices have been under investigation.

11103918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103918.value: First, we found enhanced MCT1, MCT4, and CD147 in hypoxic GMs and hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes and exosome secretion in hypoxic GMs. Gain or loss of MCT1 and CD147 function on exosome secretion and their level in GMs-derived exosomes demonstrated that exosomal MCT1 and CD147 could be great biomarkers to track glioma progression and glycolysis. Additionally, biophysical properties from hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes revealed a unique character as a biomarker. Finally, exosomal MCT1, MCT4, and CD147 level could be quantitatively detected by noninvasive LSPR and AFM biosensors as liquid biopsy for glioma progression (Thakur A. et al. Science Advances, 6(26), eaaz6119 & Liu L. et al. Chemical Engineering Journal, 137383). In detailed characterization, biomarker mapping, and biosensing of GMs-derived exosomes, exosomal EGFRvIII, BIGH3, CD44, CD133, and PD-L1 were characterized, and the results were published and some data have been prepared to publish, introducing new concepts and techniques for glioma liquid biopsy (Several articles published in top journals & Manuscripts). The effect of GMs-derived exosomes in GMs’ proliferation and migration and EC’s tube formation were identified, clearly demonstrating that hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes had a strong capacity to induce angiogenesis. The analysis of angiogenesis factors present in hypoxic GMs-derived exosomes has been under investigation, such as VEGF-A and microRNA21. MCT1 or CD147 KD in GMs reduced exosome release and altered exosomal pro-oncogenic components, including angiogenic factors. Furthermore, the effect of ECs-derived exosomes on GMs’ cellular and exosomal phenotype were also found, indicating exosome-based mutual interactions between GMs and ECs could be critical for glioma progression (Thakur A. et al. International Journal of Nanomedicine, 15, 8331 & Manuscripts). In Aim 3, an inhibitor for MCT1 (AZD-3695), MCT1-CD147 interaction (Thalidomide), and a DNA alkylation agent (Temozolomide, TMZ) were tested in their efficacy to produce anti-cancer activity at the cellular and exosomal level. AZD-3965 and Thalidomide produced similar level of anti-proliferation and anti-migration activity to that of TMZ. At exosomal level, all three drug significantly reduced exosome release and they were also loaded into exosomes to produce anticancer activity. The result supported the mechanism of anticancer drugs via blocking the both release of pro-oncogenic exosomes from GMs and their uptake by GMs and ECs (Manuscripts). Some works in Aim 2 & 3 are still on-going with slight modifications. Exosomal interactions between GMs and ECs have been tested via the transwell system and uptake assays. Drug (Exo-AZD-3695) efficacy has been tested through its exosomal delivery to in vitro & vivo GMs.

11103918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103918.value: MCT1 and CD147 play a crucial role in controlling glycolytic reprogramming, exosome release and uptake, and interaction between GMs and ECs. Therefore, inhibitors for MCT1 and CD147 are anti-glioma agents. Interestingly, exosomes can cross the BBB and they can be also delivered to the brain via nasal route. In the current work, we found that exosomes could be great vehicles to load anticancer agents. Therefore, it could be interesting to test the delivery and efficacy of TMZ-, AZD-3965, and Thalidomide-loaded exosomes to the tumor in the mouse model of glioma. Furthermore, the development of smart exosomes by genetic modification or click chemistry targeting to glioma could be synergistic. In the exosome-based glioma liquid biopsy, we found that exosomes contained specific biomarkers for tracking the malignant progression of parent GMs. Particularly, exosomes can cross the BBB into peripheral circulation. Thus, exosomes can be great biomarker-discovery platforms for glioma as well as other neurological diseases. Through development of label-free ultrasensitive LSPR- and AFM-based biosensors for the detection of exosomal biomarkers, we established potential exosome-based liquid biopsy method for glioma diagnosis and prognosis. Therefore, in further experiments, the technique will be verified in patients with glioma and other neurological diseases.

11103918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103918.value: Malignant glioma is an incurable brain tumor, of which a key hallmark fast glycolytic metabolism. Consequently, monocarboxylate transporter1 (MCT1) and its ancillary protein CD147 are significantly upregulated to facilitate the removal of lactate out of glioma cells (GMs). Exosomes, 30-200 nm vesicles, play an important role in the cell-cell communication. GMs via glycolytic reprogramming secrete tremendous amounts of exosomes which can deliver pro-oncogenic components to surrounding cells. In this study, MCT1 and CD147 were found to be essential for glioma survival via enhancing glycolytic reprogramming and exosome communication between GMs and ECs. Importantly, MCT1- and CD147-dependant exosome release and uptake by GMs and ECs, supporting MCT1 and CD147 as promising anti-glioma targets. In addition, high level of MCT1 and CD147 in exosomes from hypoxic malignant GMs indicated that exosomal MCT1 and CD147 could be indeed faithful biomarkers for tracking glioma progression via their detection using label-free LSPR and AFM biosensors. Importantly, inhibitors for MCT1 (AZD-3695) and CD147 (Thalidomide) revealed anti-glioma activity, such as the blocking of the proliferation and migration of GMs and the tube-formation of ECs. Inhibitors for MCT1 and CD147 also significantly reduced exosome secretion, supporting their anticancer activity at the both cellular and exosomal level.

11200218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200218.value: 在人類中，DNA基序在不同發育階段及組織中對於基因調控是普遍且重要的。雖然已經做出了相當大的努力來闡明單個DNA基序模式，但是我們對異源二聚體DNA基序的了解仍然模糊不清（例如，在人類中仍未發現約25,000個異源二聚體DNA基序）。因此，基於每個項目階段的初步初始測試結果, 我們建議開發用於異源二聚體DNA基序合成的新型計算模型，並進行廣泛的驗證。 我們建議開發關於兩個單獨DNA基序如何定向和相互重疊以合成異源二聚體DNA基序的核苷酸預測模型。我們已經在10倍交叉驗證下對618個異源二聚體DNA基序進行了各種不同時間複雜度的分類器和回歸方法的廣泛測試。初步結果（例如AUROCs>0.8和相關係數> 0.75）證明了該預測模型的可行性。 我們建議基於概率圖形建模開發出首個異源二聚體DNA基序(或模體)模式模型。我們的初始輸入輸出隱馬爾可夫模型（IOHMM）已在49個DNA結合家族組合的實驗數據集上得到驗證，並在統計上觀察到合成基序模式與原始基序模式相似（p = 0.003）。其中，我們使用了最大乘積算法，其合成過程的線性複雜性本質，進一步證明了我們提出的方法可以被擴展和應用。 我們的最終目標是整合前階段的模型，以推斷未知的異源二聚體DNA基序。為了評估其潛力，我們進行了初步實驗並發現初始測試方法甚至可以“拯救”現有的異源二聚體DNA基序模式，這些模式以前發表在Nature上。香港大學的宋又强博士同意在這項研究中對新的異源二聚體DNA基序提供生物化學驗證。我們將發布開發的算法和相關數據作為開源軟件和公共數據庫，以實現長期影響和科學再現性。

11200218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200218.value: We developed a computational approach to synthesize a heterodimeric DNA motif from two monomeric DNA motifs. The approach is sequentially divided into two components (Phases A and B). In Phase A, we propose to develop the inference models on how two DNA monomeric motifs can be oriented and overlapped with each other at nucleotide level. In Phase B, given the two monomeric DNA motifs oriented, we further propose to develop DNA-binding family-specific input-output hidden Markov models (IOHMMs) to synthesize a heterodimeric DNA motif. To validate the approach, we execute and cross-validate it with the experimentally verified 618 heterodimeric DNA motifs across 49 DNA-binding family combinations. We observe that our approach can even “rescue" the existing heterodimeric DNA motif pattern (i.e. HOXB2_EOMES) previously published on Nature. Lastly, we apply the proposed approach to infer previously uncharacterized heterodimeric motifs. Their motif instances are supported by DNase accessibility, gene ontology, protein-protein interactions, in vivo ChIP-seq peaks, and even structural data from PDB. A public web-server is built for open accessibility and scientific impact. In addition, we also introduced a deep learning-based approach to synthesize heterodimeric motifs from monomeric motif pairs. Through systematic investigation, we illustrated that our newly developed suite of models, DeepMotifSyn, outperforms the current state-of-the-art method with a transformative way on synthesizing heterodimeric motifs. The previous model generates the heterodimeric motif based on separated predictive spacing length and orientation of the monomeric motif pair. Such a synthesis approach has some substantial limitations, since most of TF-TF pairs’ cooperatively bound sits involves more than one orientation and various spacing preferences [12, 14]. By contrast, DeepMotifSyn generates and scores heterodimeric motif candidates with all potential orientations and spacing preferences (see Figure 1). Our experiment demonstrated that DeepMotifSyn-synthesized heterodimeric motif candidates were able to recover 70% of bona fide heterodimeric motifs validated by CAP-SELEX. In addition, we systematically evaluated MotifKirin on synthesizing heterodimeric motifs given ground true orientation and spacing settings, showing that DeepMotifSyn significantly surpassed MotifKirin on the motif synthesis of 40 heterodimer DNA-binding families. DeepMotifSyn also leverages the motifs of multiple DNA-binding families to synthesize the heterodimeric motif for new family. 11200218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200218.value: In the future, we envision that the proposed approach can be applied to other motif data for heterodimeric DNA motif pattern synthesis, enabling numerous downstream studies. On the other hand, it will be interesting to extend it for hetero-multimeric motif synthesis subject to data availability. The growth in the combinatorial space of multiple motif pattern matching can be a computational challenge. We also expect our DeepMotifSyn can be improved through training on additional heterodimeric motif datasets subject to its availability. We also envision our deep learning-based model can be applied to hetero-multimeric motif synthesis by taking multiple motifs as input in the future.

11200318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200318.value: Optical networks with their tremendous bandwidth capacity, energy efficiency and security advantages have been widely used to power the Internet. Their deployment ranges in size from multi-continental networks to intra-datacenter networks. According to a recent Cisco's White paper [1], the current IP traffic volume is about 4.1 Exabytes/day and is expected to increase to 9.3 Exabytes/day by 2021, a volume that can only be carried by optical networks. Significant research efforts have been directed in recent years towards the development of elastic optical networks (EONs) to improve the efficiency of future networks beyond current WDM networks. Meanwhile, there has been a significant increase in the number of heterogeneous network applications with enormous complexity and resilience requirements supported by optical networks. This turns the management of optical networks into a formidable technical challenge. One key approach to address this challenge is through network virtualization whereby a virtual network operates like a real substrate network, hosted by the virtualized optical networks, in order to offer customized end-to-end services. This enables multiple virtual networks to be accommodated by the same (physical) optical network, thus allowing efficient, robust, reliable and cost effective network management and operations. This project will provide novel network resilience design methodologies to achieve cost effective and energy efficient operations while still meeting the service requirements of future optical networks. For the first time, we will develop methodologies and algorithms for optimizing models that incorporate the integration of substrate optical networks, protection, virtual network embedding (VNE), and EONs. This will provide capabilities necessary for efficient and reliable network operations. Given the enormous complexity and system interdependence associated with virtualization, resilience and reliability are especially important. The project will also compare the benefits of VNE in EONs and in WDM networks. The proposed solutions will scale to realistic network sizes. They will combine new rigorous approaches to iterative LP relaxation with column generation algorithms, and will derive provable bounds on the quality of solutions. We will also provide designs that optimize dynamic network operations loaded by virtual network demands. The project will address both legacy and greenfield scenarios. Under legacy scenarios, a topology is given, and the aim is to optimize the traffic routing and wavelength/spectrum assignment of light paths that support VNE service requirements including performance and service protection. In the greenfield scenarios, the topology is also optimized by minimizing cost subject to meeting VNE service requirements. 光網絡通信能夠提供的巨大帶寬，較高的能源效率和通信安全，現已被廣泛應用於英特網。其應用範圍也從跨洲網絡到數據中心網絡不等。根據思科2016年的白皮書，當前IP流量達到了每天4.1艾字節，2021年將超過9.3艾字節。如此巨大的數據流量，使得光網絡成為唯一的傳輸選擇。 較之傳統WDM網絡，彈性光網絡（EON）具有更高的靈活性，近年來備受關注也被廣泛研究。同時，光網絡支撐的異構網絡應用數量顯著增加，且這些應用具有高度複雜性和彈性的要求，使得光網絡管理成為一項艱鉅的挑戰。網絡虛擬化可以解決這個問題。虛擬網絡像真實物理網絡一樣運行於虛擬光網絡之中，並為用戶提供定制的端到端服務，這種模式使得多個虛擬網絡能夠被同一（物理）光網絡承載，從而實現高效，穩健，可靠且低成本的網絡管理和操作。 該項目將提供創新的網絡彈性機制設計方法，實現低成本並節能的運營，同時滿足未來光網絡的業務要求。我們將首次提出最優化模型綜合考慮物理光網絡，保護，虛擬網絡映射（VNE）和EON，以及提出方法論和算法，為高效可靠的網絡運行提供必要條件。鑑於網絡虛擬化的複雜性以及不同虛擬網絡資源之間的相互依賴性，彈性和可靠性設計顯得尤為重要。該項目還將研究VNE在EON中相比於其在傳統WDM網絡中的優勢。 本項目提出的解決方案將擴展到實際的網絡規模。該方案將結合新的迭代LP鬆弛方法以及列生成算法，並得出目標的可證界限。同時，我們還將研究動態網絡中虛擬網絡請求的建立。該項目將解決傳統網絡場景中，在給定拓撲的前提下，優化流量路由和波長/頻譜分配，在滿足性能和保護等VNE服務要求的前提下降低成本。

11200318.label: Realisation of objectives
11200318.value: Objective 1: We developed an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation for a multicast VNE over an all-optical network, where each Virtual Network (VN) is a Multicast VN (MVN) for the delivery of multicast services. The primary objective is to minimize the system cost (CAPEX) and the total amount of optical bandwidth used (OPEX) to accommodate all given VNs. The objective is subject to the constraints that: 1) the resource demand of each request must be fulfilled (QoS requirement); 2) in each VN, the number of virtual nodes sharing a physical node does not violate a threshold required by this VN, avoiding too many virtual nodes in the VN failing simultaneously (resilience requirement); 3) a connected spanning tree in the physical network is successfully created for each VN; 4) each link on the spanning tree assigns the same wavelength, for a Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) network, or frequency slots, for an Elastic Optical Network (EON), to a certain VN, meeting its bandwidth demand; 5) the amount of resource allocated to all the VNs does not exceed the capacity of each physical node and physical link. Objective 2: We developed a heuristic algorithm for the problem formulated in Objective 1. In the algorithm, we decouple the VNE into two steps, i.e., virtual node embedding and virtual link embedding. In the virtual node embedding, we try to use the fewest physical nodes to host the virtual nodes in a VN while not violating all the requirements. This operation reduces the number of nodes involved to reduce system costs and energy consumption. The virtual link embedding procedure is based on the spectrum window (SW) plane (SWP) scheme. A spectrum window (SW) is made up of one or more consecutive frequency slots, and each link can create multiple SWs based on the required frequency slots number. An SWP is associated with a particular SW and is a graph constructed through 1) constructing an empty graph; 2) adding all the physical nodes to the graph; 3) adding all the links that can provide the SW required by the SWP. If there is a frequency slot within the required SW not available in a link, this link can not provide the SW, so it will not be considered for creating the SWP. Given a VN, a series of SWPs is created based on the physical network and the requested bandwidth. Next, the algorithm runs a spanning tree over an SWP to search for a multicast tree to the VN. Since there are multiple SWPs, we provided two strategies to choose a suitable SWP: min-cost and first-fit strategies. The min-cost strategy chooses the SWP with the least number of active physical nodes among all candidate SWPs, while the first-fit strategy selects the first feasible one. We provided numerical results for the evaluation and found that the proposed algorithm with the min-cost scheme performs very close to the ILP in terms of system cost and network resource consumption. Besides, we also found that the efficiency in an EON is better than in a WDM network. Objective 3 Our proposed heuristic algorithm can be directly applied to the dynamic scenario where the VNs arrive randomly and sequentially. We simulated a Poisson arrival process and an exponential service duration process for the VN requests. The simulation results show that applying the proposed min-cost algorithm to the EON achieves the highest acceptance ratio compared with the situations when applying the first-fit algorithm to an EON or applying the algorithms to a WDM network.

11200318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200318.value: We applied the methodology developed under this project including the ILP models and heuristic algorithms to provide solutions to minimize the system cost and the total amount of spectrum resources used when accommodating the given VNs in a static scenario and minimize the blocking prbability in a dynamic scenario for a given network and link/node capacities and costs. In [Part C/10, number 7], we demonstrated that our proposed solution could significantly improve spectrum efficiency, resource utilization, and dynamic request acceptance ratio. A key application of this project on VNE has been new methodologies for virtual data center (VDC) embedding (VDCE). VDCE is a special kind of VNE dedicated to embedding virtual networks, i.e., VDCs, over a data center network (DCN). The literature uses VDCE instead of a VNE to emphasize that VDCE is much more complicated than the general VNE, and there are two main reasons for this. Firstly, in contrast to a general VNE, which considers a homogenous network with homogeneous nodes, the VDCE considers a DCN consisting of server nodes, switch nodes, and router nodes. Secondly, the network scale of a DCN is quite large, and a DCN often contains hundreds of thousands or even millions of nodes. We have also extended the work to a mixed VDCE, where the VDCs contain a mixture of multicast and unicast virtual links. This work has been published as a journal paper [Part C/8, number 1]. We also provided mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) and a heuristic algorithm to solve the problem. The numerical results show that our solution can significantly reduce the resource efficiency and the dynamic rejection ratio for the traditional DCs. In [Part C/8, number 6], we present a MILP and an algorithm to solve a VDCE to avoid hot spots and improve energy efficiency in DCs. Application of the column generation method to service function chaining embedding in multi-domain networks [Part C/8 number 2]. We studied the benefits of resource disaggregation for service reliability in DCs [Part C/8, number 4]. This also led to a patent application [Part C/10, number 4]. Elastic Optical Network (EON) is the optical application of OFDM. In [Part C/8, number 3], we studied an OFDM-based cognitive radio network. Application to optimization of computation offloading in edge computing was published in [Part C/8, number 6], and in [Part C/10, number 6] we provide an efficient method for job assignments in server farms.

11200318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200318.value: One potential for further development is to combine the several separate research aspects, for example, to consider the hotspots issue in the VNE for the next-generation disaggregated data center connected by an all-optical network, i.e., WDM or EON network. This problem is very challenging as many aspects need to be taken into account, including routing and spectrum allocation, heterogeneity of the DCN, and cooling issues like the hot spots issue related to the placement of hardware in a DC. The work we did under this project was under the assumption that each rack in a rack-scale DDC is a single node, and we did not consider the resource allocation problem within each rack, which also involves latency constraints, making the problem significantly more challenging. The challenges to address these problems will include problem modeling, algorithm development, and simulation study for the evaluation. Another important future direction is to extend our current approach which was mainly based on single objective optimization to multi-objective optimization problems. This is important because it provides the designer with a range of optimal soluions (Pareto front), where choices of preferences made by multiple stakehodders can be discussed and agreed upon.

11200318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200318.value: Optical networks with their tremendous bandwidth capacity, energy efficiency, and security advantages have been widely used to power the Internet and data centers. Considering the enormous volume of data sent every day over the Internet, only optical networks can carry it. Significant research efforts have been directed in recent years toward the development of new optical network technologies of to improve their efficiency. Meanwhile, there has been a significant increase in the number of network applications with enormous complexity and resilience requirements supported by optical networks. This turns the management of optical networks into a formidable technical challenge. One key approach to address this challenge is through network virtualization whereby a virtual network operates like a real substrate network, hosted by the virtualized optical networks, in order to offer customized end-to-end services. This enables multiple virtual networks to be accommodated by the same (physical) optical network, thus allowing efficient, robust, reliable, and cost-effective network management and operations. In this project, we have provided novel network design methodologies to achieve cost-effective and energy-efficient operations while still meeting the service requirements of future optical and data center networks. In our solutions, we have overcome significant challenges associated with optical network virtualization.

11200518.label: Project Objectives
11200518.value: For the single facility case, we plan to investigate strategyproof mechanisms when group externalities exist (In other words, an agent's utility partly depends on other agents' utilities based on whether they are in the same community). We try to show impossibility results when externatility coefficients are large and explore the possible range of coefficients for the existence of strategyproof mechanisms with reasonable performance. For the case of two heterogeneous facilities with arbitrary agent preference where agents may like one facility or both facilities, we have four problems where the government's objective is to minimize either social cost or maximum agent cost and the agent's cost is affected either by the closer facility or the farther facility when it likes both facilities. We introduce the minimum distance constraint into the problem and try to investigate which mechanisms are still strategyproof with good approximation ratios in the new setting and what new mechanisms could be designed for large minimum distance constraint. For our newly proposed fractional model where the agent's cost is the weighted sum of her distance towards the two facilities. We have some initial results obtained and will also extend our study to the variant when there is a minimum distance constraint for the two facilities. For the obnoxious facility games with two facilities, we will investigate both the homogeneous case and the heterogeneous case where the individual agent's utility is either the utility towards the closer facility or the total utility towards both facilities. With the minimum distance constraint for the two facilities, we plan to find strategyproof mechanisms with good approximation ratios and also derive some impossibility results.

11200518.value: 算法博弈論是結合了博弈論和算法設計的研究方向，其主要目標是在復雜的博弈環境中設計好的算法。在本項目中，我們主要研究設施選址博弈問題。在最傳統的模型中，通常假設政府計劃在一條街道上蓋一個設施（比如便利店或者公共汽車站）。街道上住著一些擁有私有信息的住戶。他們希望距離這個設施盡可能的近。政府的目標是收集住戶的信息之後作一個決策，使得住戶報虛假信息不會得到任何好處（具有這種性質的機制叫做可信機制），而同時政府的目標（比如社會代價或最大代價）可以近似優化。機制可以是確定性的，也可以是隨機的，性能的上界可以通過設計一個特定的機制得到，而性能的下界意味著任何可信機制都不能比該界做的更好。如果住戶希望離設施越遠越好，則問題稱為排斥型設施選址問題。 我們把兩種喜好合在一起考慮了耦合模型。並且也研究了住戶既不想太靠近設施又不想太遠離設施的雙峰喜好模型。在實際的社會中，其實住戶之間存在著項目關係，比如同屬某個社團等等，在本項目中我們用團體外部性來刻劃這一類住戶之間的關係並把它第一次引入設施選址博弈問題中來。 除了單設施問題，研究者們也研究過雙設施問題。在同秩雙設施問題中，兩個設施是一樣的，因此住戶只會去好的那個。而在異秩雙設施問題中，住戶會喜歡其中一個設施或者兩個設施都喜歡，當住戶喜歡兩個設施時，之前的研究假設他的代價是到這兩個設施的代價和。我們把該模型擴展為其代價由近的設施決定或者由遠的設施決定。其中一個例子就是巴士站，如果一個住戶兩條巴士路線都喜歡（去同一個目的地），那麼他通常會去近的那個巴士站。在本項目中，我們進一步把模型擴​​展至比例喜好，即兩個設施有類似功能。比如一個超市和一個便利店。住戶會根據他們的喜好決定多少時間去超市及多少時間去便利店，因此他們的代價便可定義為到兩個設施的距離加權和。 我們之前還研究過下述雙設施模型，即所有住戶都喜歡其中一個設施，而排斥另一個設施。比如警察局和看守所。為了保證及時的管控，這兩個設施的距離不能太大。在本項目中，我們研究一個相反的限制，即兩個設施之間的距離不能太小（比如為了考慮堆填區的可擴展性或城市規劃需要。這是最小距離限制在設施選址博弈問題中第一次被研究。

11200518.value: Objective 1 is comprehensively studied and resulted in a publication in COCOON 2022. More specifically, we develop a formal model for facility location games with group externalities where an agent's utility partly depends on other agents' utilities based on whether they join group activities. We consider two social objectives, the social utility and the minimum utility. On the negative side, we show that 1) neither putting the facility at the median agent's location nor putting the facility at the leftmost agent's location is strategyproof; 2) neither the constant approximation ratio for the social utility nor the bounded approximation ratio for the minimum utility can be achieved when an agent can misreport both the location and the preference of the type of activities. On the positive side, the constant ratios can be achieved when an agent can misreport only the location or the preference. We design unanimous strategyproof mechanisms for each pair of social objectives and the types of misreporting information. We also prove their approximation ratios and give the corresponding lower bounds for each setting. Recently we also extended our study to multiple group setting. Objective 2 is explored comprehensively for the objective of minimizing maximum cost and the results is in minor revision in JOCO. We also explored the minimising social cost objective but did not have sufficient findings to form a paper (most of the results in this setting are negative). In the optional preference model for the facility location game with two heterogeneous facilities on a line interval [0, 1], we enforce the requirement of a minimum distance 0 ≤ d ≤ 1 between the two facilities. Each agent has one of three favorable preferences towards the two facilities, i.e., facility 1, facility 2, or optional preference. Here, we consider two variants of the optional preference model: Min (caring for the closer one) and Max (caring for the further one). In both variants, each agent wishes to get close to his preferred facilities, and thus his cost is his distance to his preferred facility. Given any value of d, for both variants, we propose a strategyproof mechanism with an approximation ratio of 2. We also establish lower bounds of any deterministic strategyproof mechanism for both variants and show that the gaps between the lower bounds and the upper bounds are relatively small. Objective 3 is fully studied and the result is published in COCOON 2021. For two-facility location games with fractional preferences and minimum distance constraint. We obtained the following results. For the objective of maximizing the social utility, we designed deterministic strategy-proof mechanisms with a ratio of 4/(2-d), where ‘d’ is the minimum distance constraint between the two facilities, and the lower bound is 2. The proposed mechanism employs a voting method to determine the placement of two facilities based on the agents' preferences. Specifically, if the number of players who prefer facility 1 to be located on the left half [0,1/2] exceeds the number of players who favor the right half [1/2, 1], then facility 1 is placed at (1-d)/2 while facility 2 is placed at (1+d)/2. Additionally, we also proposed randomized strategy-proof mechanisms with an approximation ratio of 2, and the lower bound is 1.06. This mechanism places the 2 facilities at (1-d)/2 and (1+d)/2 with an equal probability of 1/2. For the objective of maximizing the minimum utility, the mechanism mentioned above can achieve an approximation ratio of 4, and the lower bound is 2. Meanwhile, the randomized mechanism can achieve a tight upper bound of 2 for maximizing the minimum utility. Objective 4 is fully studied and the results are published in JAIR. In the obnoxious heterogeneous two-facility location game for maximizing the social utility, we propose new deterministic group strategyproof mechanisms with provable approximation ratios and establish a lower bound (7 − d)/6 for any deterministic strategyproof mechanism. We also design a strategyproof mechanism maximizing the minimum utility. In the obnoxious homogeneous two-facility location game for maximizing the social utility, we propose deterministic group strategyproof mechanisms with provable approximation ratios and establish a lower bound 4/3. Besides, in the two-facility location game with triple-preference, where each facility may be favorable, obnoxious, indifferent for any agent, we further motivate agents to report both their locations and preferences towards the two facilities truthfully, and design a deterministic group strategyproof mechanism with an approximation ratio 4.

11200518.value: We are extending the group externality model to multiple groups and new insights are needed to get reasonable approximation ratios. 11200518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200518.value: The project studies facility location games to elicit true information from agents. The core component of the project is group externality and minimum distance constraint, two very practical elements in reality. Group externality captures agents' group role, namely how an agent's group affect its utility. Minimum distance constraint between two facilities commonly exists in the society when the government plans on the construction of facilities. Mechanisms designed for these models can guarantee good approximation to the best social welfare the system can achieve, while at the same time can prevent agents from misreporting their private information. The lower bounds proved for various models capture the difficulty of the problems and show the effectiveness of our designed mechanisms.

11200618.label: Project Objectives
11200618.value: To demonstrate photonic millimeter-wave generation of up to 100 GHz based on harmonics invoked by chimeras. Both experimentally and numerically, the single-mode laser with feedback will be investigated for chimera-induced switching between stable and oscillation states. The switching transients will enhance the oscillation harmonics of up to at least the fourth order. Optical filtering will be applied for selecting the harmonics for square-envelope modulated millimeter-wave generation. To investigate frequency multiplication for generating millimeter-waves beyond 100 GHz using multiple cascaded lasers. A laser in chimera will be injected to at least three other lasers to obtain sequentially blue-shifted optical spectra. The resultant millimeter-wave frequency will be locked to an increasing multiple of the fundamental oscillation frequency as the number of lasers increases. Nonlinear optical difference frequency generation based on chimeras of low duty cycles will be experimented. To demonstrate millimeter-wave noise squeezing by chimera dynamics. A theoretical framework on noise diffusion will be developed analytically based on the equation-of-motion of the probability density function of the oscillation phase. Squeezing of the probability density function will be investigated through optimizing the state-space trajectories of the chimeras. With numerical verifications, experiments will investigate noise suppression in millimeter-wave generation.

11200618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200618.value: The generation of high-frequency electromagnetic waves has been of central importance for communications in modern cities. The need of increasingly high data bandwidths has prompted most communication systems to keep migrating to higher carrier frequencies. The performances in communications are closely tied to the sources of high frequency, purity, and tunability. The development of signal sources at microwave, millimeter-wave, and even terahertz frequencies has become crucial. Photonic millimeter-wave generation has been a focus of attention because light modulated with millimeter-waves can take advantage of low-loss fiber transmissions. The past decade saw the rapid advancements in photonic millimeter-wave generation using approaches including direct and external modulation, passive mode-locking, dual-wavelength lasers, optoelectronic oscillators, and stable injection-locking using frequency combs. Our group has also investigated optical injection under the steady-state period-one dynamics for widely tunable microwave generation. The above approaches have enabled photonic generation of high frequencies, where applications including radio-over-fiber communications and photonic signal processing have been reported. However, they often demand well-designed high-speed electronic circuitries and are usually challenging at frequencies above 100 GHz. In this proposal, the recently discovered chimera phenomena in semiconductor lasers are considered for photonic millimeter-wave generation. Such photonic chimeras, in a time-delayed feedback system, correspond to the co-existence of different nonlinear dynamical states. They enable temporal switching between a stable state and a microwave oscillatory state, which contains harmonics suitable for millimeter-wave generation. Firstly, chimeras with enhanced harmonics will be considered in a laser with feedback. The enhancement attributed to the switching transients of the chimeras leads to harmonics reaching 100 GHz. The harmonics can be selected by optical filtering that results in millimeter-wave generation with a square-envelope from repeated switching. Secondly, cascaded frequency multiplication will be investigated by using multiple lasers in chimeras. The lasers emit sequentially blue-shifted spectra with the resultant millimeter-wave frequency exceeding 100 GHz. Difference frequency generation by nonlinear organic crystals is possible without damage using chimeras of low duty cycles. Thirdly, noise-squeezed millimeter-wave generation by chimera dynamics will be investigated. The probability density function of the noisy oscillation phase will be analytically studied by developing a diffusive theoretical framework. Reduction of noise will be investigated through optimizing the state-space trajectories of the chimeras for millimeter-waves of high spectral purity. With the completion of the project, the new chimera phenomena will contribute to the exciting development of all-optical, high-frequency, and stable sources for next generation applications. 高頻電磁波的生成在現代城市通信中至關重要。對數據帶寬越來越高的需求促使大多數通信系統不斷改用更高的載波頻率。通信系統的性能與信號源的高頻率、純度及可調諧性密切相關。微波信號源、毫米波信號源、乃至太赫茲電磁波信號源的發展已經變得非常關鍵。由於被毫米波調製的光可以利用其在光纖中傳輸的低損耗特性，光子毫米波生成成為了人們關注的焦點。過去的十年里，光子毫米波生成得到了迅猛發展，生成的方法包括直接調製、外部調製、被動鎖模、雙波長激光器、光電振蕩器、以及基於光頻梳的穩定注入鎖定。我們的團隊也研究了的穩態P1動態下的光注入，以用於廣泛可調諧的微波生成。上述方法已經實現了高頻電磁波的光子方式生成，包括光纖無線電通信和光子信號處理在內的相關應用也得到了報道。然而，這些方法常常對設計精良的高速電路提出要求，並往往在面對100 GHz以上的頻率遇到困難。 在研究計劃中，最近剛被發現的半導體激光器中的嵌合體現象被認為可用於光子毫米波生成。在延時反饋系統中，這種光子嵌合體表現為不同非線性動態狀態的共存。它們能夠在一種穩定狀態和一種微波振盪狀態之間隨着時間進行切換，其中，微波振盪狀態包含的諧波適用於毫米波生成。首先，我們將考量在光反饋激光器中帶有增強諧波的嵌合體動態。歸因於嵌合體狀態的切換瞬態，這種增強作用使諧波頻率可達到100 GHz。諧波可由光學濾波選擇出來，其結果是生成了帶有重複切換的方形包絡的毫米波信號。其次，我們將研究使用多個嵌合體狀態下的激光器以實現級聯倍頻。這些激光器依次發射藍移光譜，由此產生的毫米波頻率超過100 GHz。使用低佔空比的嵌合體狀態，可以通過非線性有機晶體生成差頻。最後，我們將研究基於嵌合體動態的噪聲壓縮毫米波生成。我們將開發一個擴散性理論架構，解析地研究受噪聲影響的振蕩相位的概率密度函數。優化嵌合體動態的狀態空間軌跡，並研究噪聲的降低以得到高譜純度的毫米波。隨着項目的完成，這種新的嵌合體現象將有助於全光學高頻穩定的信號源發展，以推進至下一代應用之中。

11200618.label: Realisation of objectives
11200618.value: The project aims to investigate the dynamics of semiconductor lasers in connection to states related to chimera. The chimera-related phenomenon in semiconductor lasers with a time-delayed optical feedback correspond to the co-existence of different nonlinear dynamical states. Specifically, temporal switching between a stable state and an unstable microwave oscillatory state for the laser with the external cavity was observed in the project. The research focused on the switching between stable and unstable states, applying to photonic millimeter-wave generation, where both optical feedback and injection were considered. The switching transients were investigated for stable-unstable switching such that millimeter-wave generation with a square-envelope was obtained. Moreover, cascaded frequency multiplication was investigated by using additional lasers. Sequentially shifted spectra with the resultant millimeter-wave frequency reaching the order of 100 GHz was attained optically, while the spectral purity of the signal at 72 GHz was studied based on the electrically recorded power spectrum in a dual-stage schematic. Reduction of noise was investigated by locking to a microwave source at a lower subharmonic frequency. Furthermore, a theoretical framework is developed for the stable-unstable switching dynamics. The analytical derivation yielded an expression for the switching period, which was found to slightly expand from the feedback delay time. Such a result interestingly connects to the literature on related chimera phenomena for which the temporal expansion is inversely proportional to the feedback field strength. The effort in addressing the objectives during the project is detailed as follows. Objective 1 was about investigating the chimera-related switching between the stable state and unstable states for photonic millimeter-wave generation with the square-wave envelope. Based on the experimental results on a single-mode laser, a rate-equation modeling was developed for systematically elucidating a precise region in the parameter space, in spite of some previous doubts and discussions on the applicability of the Lang-Kobayashi model in the literature. Such a switching region was identified for feedback strengths above the Hopf bifurcation boundary and below the regions for periodic or chaotic states. Interestingly, the numerical results unveil the need for a gradual adjustment of the feedback strength in order to observe the regular switching of the stable and unstable states. A procedure was developed of yielding the results for every feedback strength, where at least 2000 round-trips were employed to ensure the elimination of residual transients. This avoids the artifacts that are occasionally overlooked in some literatures. Then, as for the spectral behavior, optical spectrograms were obtained using short-time Fourier transform (STFT) on the complex field amplitude, where optical frequency components spanning tens of gigahertz were observed with a duty cycle tunable by the feedback field strength. Additionally, the switching transients were investigated in detail based on the trajectories in the angular frequency-gain plane. By identifying the external cavity modes (ECMs), the stable stage was found to correspond to a spiral into the stable ECM between the maximum gain mode (MGM) and minimum linewidth mode (MLM), as followed by a slow migration to other ECMs, which eventually lead to rapid oscillations with large variations into the unstable stage. Objective 2 was about using multiple cascaded lasers for frequency multiplication to generate photonic millimeter-waves. This was realized by using two slave lasers in the unstable oscillations. Optical injection from a master laser induced period-one oscillations with a fundamental frequency in the primary slave laser, which then injected a secondary slave laser for enhancing the second harmonic of the oscillation. By the antiguidance effect, the cavity resonance of the primary slave laser is redshifted to amplify the first frequency component below the regenerative component, while the cavity resonance of the secondary slave laser was utilized to enhance the second frequency component. By subharmonic locking through modulation at one-fourth of the fundamental oscillation frequency of 36 GHz, photonic millimeter-wave generation at the second harmonic was achieved as observed by the power spectrum at 72 GHz, while higher harmonics were observed optically. Single-sideband (SSB) phase noise was measured to reduce when the modulation power was increased, as long as the modulation frequency had nearly no detuning from the subharmonic frequency. With the availability of high-speed photodetectors, signals up to about 100 GHz can be generated without yet relying on optical conversion. Besides, the millimeter-wave signal power can be strengthened by the coherent addition from the master laser. The modulation depth was maximized when the optical frequency component from the master laser was as strong as that of the second harmonic below the injection. Objective 3 was related to developing a theoretical framework for the stable-unstable switching. The development was based on the groundwork on the Lang-Kobayashi model, as well as the properties of the MGM of maximal gain, MLM of minimum linewidth, and other ECMs and antimodes for the laser with the external cavity. During the investigation of this project, it was identified that the formulation about the ellipse in the frequency-gain plane containing the ECMs continued to have an important role despite the destabilization from a stable self-locking state. Then, by invoking an equation-of-motion based on the switching periodicity, an approximation by fitting at the MLM has led to a conclusion that the switching period has to be slightly greater than the feedback delay time. The MLM least affected by the diffusion of phase noise had the central role in the fitting. Also, the expansion time was theoretically found to be inversely proportional to the cavity decay rate and the feedback field strength. It reduces as the antiguidance factor increases. Most importantly, the period expansion explained the general observation of a shifted frequency component in quasiperiodic laser dynamics that is inversely proportional to the feedback strength. Such a behavior has been observed as drifts of the switching period in early works on laser dynamics, recent works on cavity solitons in relation to temporal dissipative localized states, as well as the spatiotemporal dynamics for chimeras and reservoir computing in lasers under feedback, optoelectronic oscillators, mode-locked lasers, and edge-emitting lasers with polarization-rotated feedback. In other words, the theoretical result based on the ellipse and equation-of-motion in the frequency-gain plane has led to the formulation of the switching period expansion, as a form of an internal reaction time of the laser with the external cavity. Through addressing the above objectives, the project established the understanding for the stable-unstable switching dynamics, while experimental increment of the frequency range was realized. The results paved a way for venturing into regimes of irregular switching, instead of the regular periodic switching, which holds promise for wireless distribution of chaotic signals in future studies.
