11200618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200618.value: The research contributed to 5 journal papers and 3 conference papers, which include one currently under review. It also supported the training of 1 Ph.D. student who has completed the thesis to be examined. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows. For the laser with feedback, the Lang-Kobayashi model was numerically confirmed to agree with experimental observations regarding the stable-unstable switching dynamics, as the feedback strength and delay were both adjusted. The analytical Hopf boundary for the MLM of minimum linewidth was derived to match the boundaries of the switching regions in several maps in the parameter space. The careful adjustment of feedback strength was found to be crucial in avoiding artifacts from noisy initial conditions. An additional systematic study on the correlation dimension in experiments was conducted for the geometric complexity in the state space with feedback. The results were documented in journal publications [3,4] and conference publication [2] in Part C. For the cascading of lasers, the oscillatory behavior was experimentally investigated for photonic millimeter-wave generation. A continuous-wave master laser injected a primary slave laser that in turns injected a secondary one. Photonic millimeter-wave generation at 72 GHz was yielded based on fundamental oscillations at 36 GHz, while subharmonic locking by modulation at only one-eighth of the output signal frequency was investigated in suppressing the phase noise to −87 dBc∕Hz at 10 kHz offset. The millimeter-wave power was maximized by the coherent addition, so that the optical spectrum contained frequency components of nearly the same amplitude. The results were reported in journal publication [1] and conference publication [3] in Part C. For the theory on stable-unstable switching, following the numerical simulations, the trajectory in the frequency-gain plane was analyzed during the stable stage, where the laser is found to follow an ellipse in visiting different ECMs of the external cavity. The analysis yielded the switching period as slightly expanded from the feedback delay, where the expansion was found to be inversely proportional to the feedback strength. Such a result is of importance on the feedback-dependent frequency downshifting, which is commonly observed in other chimera behaviors. As extensions, combining with frequency multiplication in the generation of signals, the dependencies of the detection involving various forms of mixing yielded Gaussian probability density functions and random bit generation utilizing the entropy from state-space trajectories. The results were documented in journal publications [3,2,5] and conference publication [1] in Part C.

11200618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200618.value: Based on the study of the switching between stable and unstable states, other chimera-related behaviors can potentially be developed further for both theoretical understanding and niche applications. Firstly, instead of the regular periodic switching, irregular switching can be developed for wireless distribution of chaotic signals in future studies. There has been interesting recent work by researchers on chaotic bursts for phase-conjugated feedback. Secondly, building on the cascading, adiabatic variation of the parameters can be developed for frequency-modulated continuous-wave signal generation. Such an approach is currently being pursued with a temporally varying frequency beyond 80 GHz. Lastly, there were also reports on the switching dynamics for different kinds of semiconductor lasers such as the discrete-mode lasers. The connection of the laser structure on the stable-unstable switching should worth future investigations. Since the commencement of the project, there have been several interruptions on the experiment due to the unusual circumstances amidst the pandemic, further investigations can nonetheless be continued and extended along the above potential directions.

11200618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200618.value: For the generation of high-frequency electromagnetic waves, microwave photonics have been developed using broadband and low-loss photonic devices. Amongst the many interesting approaches, nonlinear dynamics of semiconductor lasers can yield a number of special waveforms, while not requiring complicated control electronics. In this project, stable-unstable state switching was investigated for a laser with feedback, which supported co-existence of different states as a chimera-related behavior. Numerically, the general Lang-Kobayashi model was established for the specific case of switching. This allowed for detailing the switching region, optical spectrogram, and switching transients in relation to the modes supported by the external cavity. By using additional lasers, cascaded frequency multiplication was investigated for sequentially shifted optical spectra, which increased the millimeter-wave frequencies. An example spectrum at 72 GHz was studied with subharmonic locking that used simply a readily available source at just 9 GHz. Most importantly, a theoretical effort led to an analytical formulation for the switching period that corresponds to the square-envelope frequency. The expansion was found as inversely proportional to the feedback field strength, thereby connecting the switching dynamics to other related chimera phenomena. Progressively, the results contribute to the generation of versatile photonic signals and the understanding of nonlinear laser dynamics.

11200818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200818.value: Lung cancer has the highest mortality rate among all cancer types and results in over a million deaths in the world yearly. Around 85% of lung cancer patients have non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A major cause of NSCLC is the mutation of a protein called the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) in the tyrosine kinase (TK) domain. The first generation drugs, reversible EGFR TK inhibitors (TKIs), are effective initially for treating NSCLC, but almost all patients develop drug resistance after a period of time due to another EGFR mutation. Although recent second and third generation drugs are more effective, drug resistance can still occur, for example, through the activation of a downstream signaling pathway. We have made significant contributions to the analysis of NSCLC drug resistance. We have close collaborations with a genomics technology company and medical doctors at HKU and Queen Mary Hospital. Our research results have already been used by industry and in clinical work. However, our past work focused on EGFR mutants and the TK domain only. This project will address a much more challenging problem, how EGFR related proteins form homodimers and heterodimers and interact with each other, causing resistance even to new generations of drugs through downstream pathways. EGFR is a multi-domain protein and performs its biological functions through various dimerizations. The dimers can be formed due to interactions in different domains. Thus, it is important to investigate how mutations in the TK domain affect functions in other domains. We will develop advanced parametric spectral analysis, projection onto convex sets and probabilistic relaxation labeling based algorithms to identify interactions between EGFR and other proteins. The molecular dynamics data will be treated as non-stationary signals and tensor models will be employed to find the inter-domain relations. We will investigate the structural changes in different domains of EGFR for all known mutations that cause lung cancer and drug resistance. How these changes affect the dimer formation and influence the activities in related signaling pathways will be elucidated. We will study the possibility of targeting one or more proteins in the affected pathways to tackle the drug resistance problem. Through our research work, we can achieve a deep understanding of the drug resistance problem in NSCLC treatment. In addition to scientific contributions to a cutting-edge research area, this project will deliver powerful tools to medical doctors for personalized treatment of lung cancer patients and bring significant benefits to the society.

11201518.label: Project Objectives
11201518.value: We will work on very specific idealized HS-MFG model in the framework of LQ control problems. In this case, Hamiltonian can be explicitly written as a quadratic function, and one may have semi-explicit form optimal trajectories and barrier of a generic player through Ricatti-type equations. In the same period or longer period, given the explicit form being available, we shall conduct Monte-Carlo method to compute its equilibria. Next, based on better understanding of some explicit forms, we shall investigate HS-MFG in a more generalized framework. The distinct features of the existing models are expected: (a) A coalition of different groups triggered by an event; (b) alpha-stable noise in the extension of Brownian motion. We seek for a characterization of a consensus in terms of Nash equilibria. We expect to accomplish the fixed point argument for alpha greater than 1, which will be genuinely new in the MFG field. Indeed, we are very curious how different or to what extent one can improve the classical mean reversion algorithm by incorporating hybrid mean field factor. To test it, analogous to Black-Litterman algorithm, we shall adapt the idealized model into more financially practical one. This may add some additional technical difficulties with some assumption relaxations.

11201518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201518.value: 大型的动态多智能体现象发生在广泛的设计和自然环境中，它们也是经济和金融行为的基础。已有傳統的有限群体博弈理论方法对于這樣大系统的分析被认为是极其困难的。 最近，平均场博弈論（MFG）作为现代控制理论的一部分，于2006年由[Lasry and Lions]和[Huang，Caines，and Malhame]的一系列作品中引入，并且通过渐近分析在大系统的连续极限中提供有效的解决方案。另一方面，自1998年IEEE Transaction on Automatic Control出版混合系统特刊以来，混合系统（HS）在各个领域得到了迅速发展。由于NAHS（非线性分析：混合系统）的编辑工作，PI（副主编）与Caines教授（高级编辑）就这两个快速发展的领域进行了许多讨论。令人惊讶的是，我們發現迄今为止关于MFG和HS（HS-MFG）这两个新兴领域的组合研究的文献非常有限，同时認識到這樣的組合會帶來許多重要应用和有趣的数学挑战。经过更深入的讨论，Caines教授特别感兴趣，并愿意作为Co-I合作开展与事件触发混合平均场博弈論相关的主题，以及许多其他可能的方向。因此，我们期待在此项目期间在完善的（单人）模型之上为大型系统带来新的见解。

11201518.label: Realisation of objectives
11201518.value: The objectives are totally achieved, even it is under a difficult time of communication of Covid19. We did not mange to invite visitors and could not attend face to face conference during this period. Discussions were made through Zoom. Three papers have been published. One in Stochastics(1) , ), one in IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON CYBERNETICS(1) and IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs. Another paper is submitted to ESAIM: Control, Optimisation and Calculus of Variations (re-submitted in Aug 2021 and under review). Objectives 1-3 are realized as follows: (I) DENSITY EVOLUTION OF MEAN FIELD GAME: The density evolution of McKean–Vlasov stochastic differential equations in the presence of an absorbing boundary is analysed where the solution to such equations corresponds to the dynamics of partially killed large populations. By using a fixed point theorem, we show that the density evolution is characterized as the solution of an integro-differential Fokker–Planck equation with Cauchy–Dirichlet data. This problem arises naturally within mean field game theory. Mean Field Game theory attracted a great deal of attention in the control and other fields after it was initiated in a series of founding works by [Huang, Caines, and Malhamé] , and independently in that of [Lasry and Lions]. This led to extensive studies on the density evolution of McKean–Vlasov type stochastic differential equations (MV-SDE). An Fokker–Planck equation (FPK) equation and Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation coupled pair arises naturally in Mean Field Game theory to describe the controlled underlying population dynamics. To better focus on the FPK equation in this work, we presented in the project a motivation from a class of Mean Field particle systems without control. In this work, we showed that under certain assumption on the drift function and the initial density, the killed McKean–Vlasov process solves FPK. That is, there exists a solution of MV-SDE, whose density satisfies FPK. This is an interesting findings for the Mean Field Game theory and brings impact to the development of Mean Field Game theory. (II) GRAPHON MEAN FIELD GAME : It is known that Mean Field Game (MFG) theory establishes Nash equilibrium conditions for large populations of asymptotically negligible non-cooperating agents via an analysis of the infinite limit population. The resulting PDEs consist of a backward Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation and a forward Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FPK) equation for each generic agent. These equations are linked by the state distribution of a generic agent which is called the mean field of the system. The basic structure of standard MFG theory assumes a symmetry in the connections of the agents but not necessarily of their dynamics. However, in the recent studies, asymmetric graph connections in large population games are considered. Large subpopulations (or clusters) of agents are placed at their particular nodes and communicate with the neighbouring subpopulations via the graph edges. The graphs are heterogeneous with the edges having not necessarily identical weights. In the network limit, a graphon gives the communication weights g(α, β), for the Graphon MFG (GMFG) framework and for the graphon theory. Apart from the Mean field game in (I) and Graphon mean field game in(II), the team investigated other network problem stemming out from the main topic. It is useful for future research development in this field as shown below. (III) Estimator for Large Scale Systems with local information [2] In this article, a framework of the distributed linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) estimation for large scale systems with local information (LSLI) has been established. The gains of the LMMSE estimator are effectively constructed by solving linear matrix equations. A gradient descent algorithm is exploited to design the gains of the LMMSE estimator numerically. Sufficient conditions are derived to ensure the boundedness of the estimation error covariance. Compared with the previous works, the main challenge of this work is to handle the sparse structure constraints induced by the local information. The idea of distributed estimation is based on the LQ framework with local information, which provides a new approach of estimation for large scale systems. (IV) Finite-time stability of probability logical networks[3] This brief presents some further results on the finite-time stability of probabilistic logical networks (PLNs). By semi-tensor product technique routinely, the dynamic behavior of a PLN is characterized by its corresponding state transition graph (STG). Then, an irradiative result is found. That is, a PLN is globally stable within finite time, if and only if, its STG is acyclic, except for the self loop at the pre-designated vertex. This is a short note to study the stability issue of logical networks. Overall, parts (I) and (II) have realized the objectives. In addition, parts (III) and (IV) illustrated some related topics such as the construction of the estimator for large scale network based on local information and the stability issues for logical networks, respectively.

11201518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201518.value: Mean Field Game theory attracted a great deal of attention in the control and other fields after it was initiated in a series of founding works by Huang, Caines, and Malhamé , and independently in that of Lasry and Lions. This led to extensive studies on the density evolution of McKean–Vlasov type stochastic differential equations (MV-SDE). In [1], we study a similar integro-differential FPK associated to population density dynamic of the process killed at the boundary of the unit ball. The corresponding study on the solvability and regularity properties of the FPK for the killed population is not available. Our goal is as shown as follows: Under appropriate conditions on the drift function, the density of killed process is the classical solution of its associated integro-differential FPK with initial-boundary data. In this work, we showed that under certain assumption on the drift function and the initial density, the killed McKean–Vlasov process solves FPK. That is, there exists a solution of MV-SDE, whose density satisfies FPK. This is an interesting findings for the Mean Field Game theory. GRAPHON MEAN FIELD GAME [4] In this work, we established the existence of solutions via the application of a fixed point theorem. Our existence proof adopts Schauder’s argument on the fixed point theorem. Our solvability is to answer the existence in H¨older space. In particular, our proof on the continuity of the gradient of the value function with respect to the coefficient functions relies on probabilistic estimates rather than the theory of viscosity solutions. The main advantage of our approach is that, we can conclude the local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map, which is stronger than continuity and beneficial to the subsequent analysis of the GMFG. The major difficulty generalizing existence for MFG to GMFG is to obtain the regularity of the solution with respect to the variable α, which is essential to the existence result by Schauder’s fixed point theorem. This leads to a study of the sensitivity with respect to coefficient functions of corresponding PDEs. Therefore, the local Lipschitz continuity of the HJB solution map becomes essential for this procedure.

11201518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201518.value: (i) We observe in [1] that uniqueness of the solution to the FPK (9) has not been established in this paper and this will be the subject of future work. If the uniqueness were true, as an application, one can approximate the population pth mean(5) of large system in a bounded region by its associated FPK. (ii) From [1], it may also be interesting to consider the estimates of the population pth moment normalized by the number of survivals. Further applications can be found in the connections of non-linear filtering theory with MFG theory. (iii) For [4], One limitation of the current setting is that the running cost in the current setup allows to use Hopf-Cole transformation, which is essential to the subsequent analysis in regularity. To deal with the full generalization of the running cost, one must adopt different approach and it will be definitely in our future research direction. (iv) The current setting in [4] requires the continuity of the graphon. In fact, some graphons are not necessarily continuous. Nevertheless, the continuity condition of the graphon can be relaxed in the future research work.

11201518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201518.value: Large population dynamical multi-agent phenomena occur in a wide range of designed and natural settings and they also underlie much economic and financial behavior. Analysis of such systems with even a moderate number of agents is regarded as being extremely difficult using the finite population game theoretic methods which were developed over several decades for multi-agent control systems. Recently, Mean Field Game (MFG) theory, as a part of the modern control theory, was introduced in a series of founding works by [Lasry and Lions] and by [Huang, Caines, and Malhame] in 2006, and it has been recognized useful to provide an effective solution through asymptotic analysis in the continuum limit for large systems. In this project, extensive studies on the density evolution of McKean–Vlasov type stochastic differential equations (MV-SDE) have been conducted. In addition, asymmetric graph connections in large population games are considered. Large subpopulations (or clusters) of agents are placed at their particular nodes and communicate with the neighbouring subpopulations via the graph edges. The graphs are heterogeneous with the edges having not necessarily identical weights. Thus, in this project, a graphon is developed to give the communication weights and establish Graphon MFG (GMFG) framework and for the graphon theory.

11202318.label: Project Objectives
11202318.value: In view of multiplicity in a fleet of ASVs, the first objective of the proposed research is to develop neurodynamic optimization approaches to neurodynamics-based intelligent task assignment methods to allocate given tasks efficiently among ASVs via centralized or distributed optimization. The proposed methods will enable the fleet of ASVs to optimize their operational capabilities timely with given resources and tasks. 11202318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202318.value: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) are marine vessels capable of performing various marine operations with minimal or without human supervision. Due to their salient features of high autonomy and mobility, they are vitally important tools for numerous applications in marine environment monitoring, hydrographic survey, ocean exploration and exploitation, search and rescue missions, etc. Compared with their counterparts for land and aerial vehicles, the mission planning and motion control of ASVs are more challenging due to the nonlinearity, uncertainty and underactuation of marine vehicle dynamics as well as the strong disturbances of waves and tides between liquid and air media at sea. For complex missions, there are increasing needs for deploying a fleet of ASVs instead of a single one to complete difficult tasks. Cooperative operations among multiple ASVs offer great advantages with enhanced capability and efficiency. Despite various application potentials, mission planning and motion control of swarmed ASVs pose great challenges due to the multiplicity of ASVs, complexity of intra-vehicle interactions and fleet formation with collision avoidance requirements, and scarcity of communication bandage at sea environments. High-performance mission planning and motion control methods are deemed to be highly demanded for widespread applications of ASVs. In recent years, neural computation regained its popularity from academia and industries, due to the numerous successes of deep learning. In addition, the results of our recent research findings in an RGC-funded project indicate that collaborative neurodynamic approaches are effective for distributed and global optimization. These outcomes may play vital roles in coordinated planning and control of ASVs. Systematic investigations on neural-computation-based intelligent mission planning and motion control would be highly interesting and rewarding. In this proposed research, an in-depth investigation of neural-computation-based intelligent ASV mission planning and motion control methodologies will be performed. The research will consist of four coherent parts. The first part will focus on developing neurodynamic approaches to centralized and distributed ASV task assignment in dynamic and uncertain operational environments. The second part will focus on developing collaborative neurodynamic optimization methods for receding-horizon trajectory generation of ASV fleets. The third part will aim at developing intelligent motion control methods based on neural computation. The last part will aim at experimentation and demonstration of the intelligent mission planning and motion control methods on an experimental platform. It is expected that the successful completion of the proposed project will significantly advance the research and development of ASV mission planning and motion control methodologies for both academia and industry. 自主水面无人艇（ASV)是能够在很少或没有人工监督的情况下执行各种水上作业的船舶。由于它们具有高度自治和机动性的显著特征，它们是海洋环境监测，水文测量，海洋勘探和开发，搜救任务等许多应用的重要工具。 与陆地和空中飞行器相比，由于海上船机动力学的非线性，不确定性和欠驱动性以及海上液体和空气介质之间的波浪和潮汐的强烈扰动，ASV的任务规划和运动控制更具挑战性。对于复杂的任务，越来越需要部署一组ASV而不是单个ASV来完成困难的任务。多个ASV之间的协作操作对增强的能力和效率提供了巨大的优势。尽管存在各种应用潜力，但由于ASV的多样性，艇间交互的复杂性以及具有防撞要求的队形形成以及海上环境中通信带宽的狭窄，群体ASV的任务规划和运动控制具有很大的挑战。高性能任务规划和运动控制方法对于ASV的广泛应用被认为是非常需求的。 由于深度学习的众多成功，最近几年神经计算从学术界和工业界重新获得了认可。此外，我们最近在RGC资助项目中的研究结果表明，协作神经动力学方法对分布式和全局优化是非常有效的。这些结果可能在ASV的协调规划和控制中发挥重要作用。基于神经动力学的智能任务规划和运动控制的系统研究将是非常有益的。 这项拟议的研究将对基​​于神经计算的智能ASV任务规划和运动控制方法进行深入研究。该研究将包括四个相关部分。第一部分将重点介绍在动态和不确定的操作环境中开发集中式和分布式ASV任务分配的神经动力学方法。第二部分将重点介绍ASV车队后退轨迹轨迹生成的协同神经动力学优化方法。第三部分旨在开发基于神经计算的智能运动控制方法。最后一部分将针对实验平台上的智能任务规划和运动控制方法的实验和演示。预计成功完成拟议项目将大大推进学术界和工业界ASV任务规划和运动控制方法的研究和开发。

11202318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202318.value: In this project, we developed several neurodynamics-driven meths for the intelligent motion planning and control of marine vessels in general and autonomous surface vehicles in particular. The major research findings are summarized as follows: 1. Several neurodynamic optimization models were developed for solving nonlinear, generalized-convex, and nonconvex optimization problems. In addition, collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches were developed based on the aforementioned neurodynamic models for global and mix-integer optimization. 2. The multistability and synchronization of recurrent neural networks were analyzed theoretically to derive sufficient conditions that may be used as guidelines for designing neurodynamic optimization models and collaborative neurodynamic optimization methodology. 3. Two computationally intelligent algorithms were developed via collaborative neurodynamic optimization for vehicle-task assignment and demonstrated via experimentation to be superior to many mainstream methods. 4. Neurodynamics-driven algorithms were developed for receding-horizon trajectory generation and shown to be applicable to the motion planning of under-actuated vehicles. 5. Several neurodynamics-driven guidance and control methods were developed via neurodynamic optimization and fuzzy approximation for the path-following control, flocking control, and model predictive control of autonomous marine vehicles. 6. Several coordinated control methods were developed for the navigation of multiple autonomous surface vehicles with collision avoidance and desired formation (e.g., targets enclosing or encirclement). 7. A scalable and resilient control method was developed for the platooning of cooperative autonomous vehicles. 8. Data-driven adaptive extended state observers and disturbance observers were developed for the output-feedback flocking control of multiple autonomous marine vehicles. 9. Intelligent control methods were developed for the safety-critical containment maneuvering of underactuated autonomous surface vehicles with collision avoidance. 10. An intelligent control method was developed for the flexible formation tracking of multiple autonomous surface vehicles to navigate through narrow channels with unknown curvatures. 11. A Fault-tolerant control method was developed for the harbor returning of autonomous surface vehicles subject to steer jamming. 12. An event-triggered distributed control method was developed for the formation of autonomous surface vehicles with collision-avoidance capabilities. 13. An intelligent control method was developed for the automatic harbor berthing of maritime autonomous surface ships in constrained water regions. 14. A lightweight and robust deep-learning model was developed for remote sensing image segmentation in aquaculture raft monitoring.

11202318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202318.value: Many avenues are open for future research and development. Specifically, for further investigations of coordinated control of autonomous surface vehicles, we are working on the safety-critical receding-horizon planning and formation control and multi-target circumnavigation via neurodynamics-driven distributed optimization. In addition, further development of the research may include the coordinated motion control of autonomous marine vehicles with drones and its applications for environmental monitoring and surveying.

11202318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202318.value: As a brain-like computationally intelligent paradigm, neurodynamic optimization has been shown to be capable of solving many optimization problems arising in numerous applications, such as the motion planning and control of autonomous underwater vehicles. In this project, we performed systematic investigations on the intelligent motion planning and control of autonomous marine vehicles based on neural computation. The research resulted in many publications that showcase the state of the art of neurodynamics-based methodologies for path planning and motion control of marine vehicles under various physical constraints and requirements. The research covered the analysis and design of neurodynamic optimization models and systems. The main results include many neurodynamics-driven methods for the intelligent planning and control of autonomous marine vehicles. In addition, the research findings also include a machine-learning model with its applications for raft monitoring in aquaculture.

11202418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202418.value: Artificial Intelligence has been enjoying a remarkable resurgence in recent years, which is mainly reinvigorated by a family of machine learning techniques called deep neural networks (DNNs). DNNs feature sophisticated architectures which endow them with exceptionally distinguished learning capabilities, although their performances often heavily depend on good settings of architecture and parameters. Although learning millions of parameters in a DNN is no longer an issue by leveraging on modern high performance computing (HPC) facilities, how to determine the most suitable DNN architecture (prior to parameter learning) to tackle a given task remains an open problem. It has been a common practice to manually design the architecture of an DNN via trial and error. However, this design paradigm is not effective for DNN users with insufficient design experience, and even experienced DNN researchers may not be omnipotent to handle the ever-growing number, variety, scale, and complexity of applications. Design automation thus provides a promising way to address these issues, which should be capable of systematically taking into account the design criteria, methodologies, approaches, and efficiency. With the rapid advancement of computing facilities, design automation for DNNs has become computationally feasible recently. This project aims to make a big step forward in this research area by devising an automatic DNN architecture design framework, which can automatically search for desirable architectures subjected to multiple design criteria that reflect design requirements in different aspects, while exploring and exploiting reusable design knowledge in various forms to a great extent. To make the best use of design knowledge to assist in the current design task, multiple related subtasks will be derived from the current design task and solved simultaneously as a multi-task optimisation problem so that the concurrent solving processes of these subtasks can facilitate one another via design knowledge transfer to ultimately augment the efficiency and effectiveness of solving the current design task. Under this framework, customized approaches will be devised for designing different types of DNNs and implemented in a computationally efficient and scalable way on GPU clusters (a modern HPC facility). The efficacy of the proposed techniques will be demonstrated on both benchmark problems and real-world applications related to sensor and voice signal processing. Ultimately, the project aims at developing automatic design of DNNs into a common choice of techniques in practice such that the pervasive utilities of DNNs can be boosted to generate greater and broader socio-economic benefits. 人工智能近年来再度复兴，其中的一个极为重要的推动力来自一类被称为深度神经网络（Deep Neural Networks, DNNs）的技术。深度神经网络具有极为复杂的结构，正是这种复杂的结构使得它们具备了前所未有的学习能力。然而要想获得超强的学习能力，相当大的程度上取决于如何获得优异的神经网络结构和适合的参数。虽然随着高性能计算装置的普及，通过计算来获得深度神经网络中数以百万计的参数已经变得可行，然而如何确定最优参数依然是极具挑战的研究问题。在这个领域，通过反复试错来手动设计和调整深度神经网络的结构，是一种标准而常见的做法。可是随着应用程序的数量、种类、规模和复杂性的持续增长，这种手动设计的模式，让即便是具备丰富经验的专业研究人员也难以应付，更不用说那些普通用户。因此，一种能够自动设计神经网络的结构并设置最优参数，并综合考虑设计标准和效率的方法，可以为我们克服以上困境提供一种可行的解决方案。 随着计算装置的高速发展，自生成深度神经网络已经具备了实现的可行性。本项目希望通过设计方法来自动搜索满足不同设计需求的网络结构，从获得一个自生成的深度神经网络设计框架。该框架不仅可以满足不同的需求，同时也可以在最大的程度上利用各种形式的可重用知识来加快这一生成过程。最大化的利用已有的设计知识来完成当前的任务，本项目的思路是从当前的设计任务中派生出多个相关的子任务，然后利用多任务优化的方法同时予以解决。在这一并行的过程中，合理的知识迁移能够促进子任务的求解，并最终提高解决当前任务的效率和有效性。在这一框架下，用户可以在GPU集群（一种先进的高性能计算装置）上定制算法，以自动生成不同类型的深度神经网络。为了验证我们所提方法的有效性，本研究项目中所提出的不同算法和技术，不仅会应用于标准测试函数，同时也会用于解决与传感器和语音信号处理相关的现实问题。最终，该项目的目标是使得自生成深度神经网络成为一种实践活动中的普适技术，从而产生更大的社会经济效益。

11202418.label: Realisation of objectives
11202418.value: Overall, the project team has successfully achieved all the objectives by following a rigorous research methodology, including literature review, algorithm design and implementation, and performance evaluation. All the research findings have been published in top-tier international journals and conferences, such as IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, IEEE Computational Intelligence Magazine, IEEE World Congress on Computational Intelligence, etc. In particular, for the first objective, i.e., devising a multi-task multi-objective evolutionary design framework, we have conducted comprehensive literature review, and completed a survey on evolutionary large-scale multi-objective optimization. Based on this, we have developed an evolutionary multitasking paradigm for large-scale multi-objective optimization, which devised a discriminative reconstruction network model to learn and transfer useful traits across large-scale multi-objective optimization tasks towards efficient problem-solving. The efficacy of this developed paradigm has been evaluated on both large-scale multi-objective optimization benchmarks and real-world training of deep neural networks on multiple different classification tasks. In addition, by considering multiple variants of a given multi-objective optimization problem to serve as the multiple optimization tasks, we have extended the evolutionary multitasking paradigm and proposed a multi-variation multifactorial evolutionary algorithm for solving large-scale multi-objective optimization problems. In contrast to the first work, this work considered the cases where no related or similar optimization tasks are available for conducting knowledge transfer, which is a common scenario in most real-world applications. Moreover, we have also improved the evolutionary multitasking paradigm for multi-objective optimization using transfer rank, which is to improve the probability of positive knowledge transfer across optimization tasks. Besides the design of evolutionary multitasking paradigms for multi-objective optimization, we have also developed multi-objective optimization paradigm based on traditional evolutionary search approaches, such as competitive swarm optimizer-based approaches and variable importance-based approaches. Particularly, we have also developed a new competitive decomposition-based multi-objective evolutionary algorithm for multi-objective optimization and a variable importance-based differential evolution approach for large-scale multi-objective optimization. Therefore, we have 100% achieved this objective. For the second objective, i.e., designing customized algorithms under the proposed framework for different types of DNNs, we have first conducted comprehensive literature review on existing learning and optimization approaches for neural architecture search, and completed a survey on evolutionary neural architecture search approaches. With these investigations and reviews, we have developed an evolutionary architecture search approach to automate the entire design process of the generative adversarial network (GAN), in which different objective functions are used in the generator of a GAN as variation operators. This helps to train the generator with various candidate architectures and their associated weights to play adversarial training against the discriminator of the GAN. Following evaluations by the discriminator, superior candidate generators survive to the next generation and evolve for potentially better architectures and their weights simultaneously, leading to more stabilized GANs with improved performance. Moreover, we have also developed a new cell-based architecture search space and new global and local search operators for the automatic design of convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures. In this work, towards efficient optimization performance, we have developed a one-epoch based performance estimation strategy without any pre-trained models, to evaluate each found architecture on the training datasets. To investigate the performance of the developed method, comprehensive empirical studies have been conducted against 34 state-of-the-art peer algorithms, including manual algorithms, reinforcement learning algorithms, gradient-based algorithms, evolutionary algorithms and etc., on widely used CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 datasets. The obtained results confirmed the efficacy of the proposed approach for automated CNN architecture design. Furthermore, we have developed a competitive decomposition-based multi-objective evolutionary algorithm, which decomposes the original problem into several constrained sub-problems, for the architecture search of the dendritic neural model. Besides the design of optimization approaches for neural architecture search, we have also explored the design of new encoding scheme, and developed a new action command encoding for neural architecture search, which defines several action commands to indicate the addition and clone of layers, connections, and local modules, and thus provides a compact and rich search space that can be explored by various optimizers efficiently. Therefore, in designing customized algorithms for different types of DNNs, we have 100% achieved this objective. For the third objective, i.e., developing scalable parallel implementations of the proposed design techniques on GPU clusters, we have explored the temporal-based approaches in a way to advance their accuracy performance by a great margin while keeping the efficiency on the other hand, and developed a new temporal-based framework integrated with the multi-spike learning for efficient recognition of visual patterns. Moreover, we have developed an island-based evolutionary multitasking paradigm using graphics processing unit (GPU), in which the compute unified device architecture (CUDA) that is able to handle a large number of optimization tasks efficiently and effectively is considered for implementing the proposed island-based optimization paradigm. Furthermore, efficient GPU-based knowledge transfer mechanisms for both implicit and explicit evolutionary multitasking have been developed for sharing knowledge among tasks with a high parallelism level. In this work, over 600 times speedup have been obtained by the developed GPU-based evolutionary multitasking paradigm, in contrast to traditional central processing unit (CPU) based evolutionary multitask optimization approaches. Therefore, we have 100% achieved this objective as planned. For the fourth objective, i.e. performance evaluations on benchmark and real-world problems, we have evaluated the developed approaches in this project on both commonly used benchmark problems, including multi-objective optimization benchmarks, large-scale multi-objective optimization tasks, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, LSUN bedroom datasets, ImageNet, etc., and real-world applications, such as real-world large-scale multi-objective optimization test suite (termed RMTF), pattern recognition tasks, and speech recognition tasks. Therefore, we have 100% achieved the objective about performance evaluations on benchmark and real-world problems.

11202418.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202418.value: The project team has achieved the objectives through a rigorous research methodology that includes literature review, algorithm design and implementation, and performance evaluation. The research findings have been published in top-tier international journals and conferences. The project team has made significant progress in developing evolutionary multitasking paradigms for large-scale multi-objective optimization problems. They have also developed customized algorithms under the proposed framework for different types of deep neural networks, including GAN, CNN, and dendritic neural model. Additionally, the team has explored new encoding schemes and developed a new action command encoding for neural architecture search. The project team has also developed scalable parallel implementations of the proposed design techniques on GPU clusters. They have explored temporal-based approaches and developed a new temporal-based framework integrated with multi-spike learning for efficient recognition of visual patterns. The team has also developed an island-based evolutionary multitasking paradigm using GPU, achieving over 600 times speedup compared to traditional CPU-based evolutionary multitask optimization approaches. The team has also evaluated the developed approaches on both benchmark problems and real-world applications, including multi-objective optimization benchmarks, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, LSUN bedroom datasets, ImageNet, real-world large-scale multi-objective optimization test suite (RMTF), pattern recognition tasks, and speech recognition tasks, etc. Overall, the project team has made significant contributions to the fields of multi-objective optimization and neural architecture search. Their developed approaches show promising results in solving large-scale multi-objective optimization problems and designing customized deep neural networks. The team's work on parallel implementations on GPU clusters provides significant speedup and efficiency improvements. Finally, the evaluation results demonstrate the effectiveness of their developed approaches on both benchmark and real-world problems.

11202418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202418.value: There are several directions in which research on neural architecture search (NAS) can be further developed: Scalability: One of the main challenges in NAS is scalability. Most existing methods are computationally expensive, limiting their applicability to small datasets and low-dimensional problems. Developing more efficient and scalable NAS algorithms can enable their use in more complex and larger-scale problems. Transfer Learning: Another area for improvement is transfer learning. NAS methods can be used to search for optimal architectures for a specific task, but these architectures may not be transferable to other tasks. Developing NAS methods that can generate architectures that can be adapted to different tasks can improve their efficiency and generalization. Interpretability: NAS methods often result in complex architectures that are difficult to interpret. Developing methods that generate more interpretable architectures can facilitate their use in practical applications. For the proposed course of action, researchers can explore further development of NAS. This can involve developing new algorithms, improving existing ones, or combining different approaches to enhance their capabilities. Additionally, researchers can also explore the real-word applications of NAS. The goal should be to develop NAS methods that are scalable, transferable, interpretable, robust, and adaptable to new tasks.

11202418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202418.value: This project is about creating a computer program that can design deep neural networks on its own. Deep neural networks are a type of artificial intelligence (AI) that can learn to perform tasks by analyzing data. However, designing a deep neural network is a complex and time-consuming process that requires a lot of expertise. The significance of this research project is that it could make it easier and faster to design deep neural networks, which could lead to more powerful AI applications. Currently, designing a deep neural network requires a human expert to manually choose the architecture and parameters of the network. This process can take a lot of time and may not always result in the most effective network. The value of this research project is that it could help researchers and developers create better AI applications more quickly. By automating the process of designing deep neural networks, more people could access the power of AI without needing to have specialized expertise in the AI design. This could lead to more innovation and more effective AI applications in fields like healthcare, finance, and transportation, etc.

11202718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202718.value: 高熵合金作為一種新興的材料在克服傳統結構材料性能極限方面擁有良好的前景。如我们初步結果顯示，面心立方高熵合金中的多組元納米顆粒的共格析出提供了一種高效的方法以實現優異的強塑性結合。這些精心設計的的L12 型多組元納米顆粒不僅可以顯著提高材料的強度，並且能够同時實現材料的韌化，獲得出色的拉伸塑性。這一独特發現與傳統結構材料的行为截然不同。儘管如此，一些關於L12 型多組元納米顆粒的關鍵問題仍需要進一步地研究與闡明。為了加深對該新型高熵合金的理解與認知，在本提案中我們將重點關注以下兩個科學層面：(1). L12 型多組元納米顆粒的本征結構對合金的宏觀/微觀變形機制的影響; (2) L12 型多組元納米顆粒的熱穩定性及該合金在高溫條件下的力學性能。 首先，基於Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Al-Ti合金體系，我們將設計不同的多組元納米顆粒強化型的高熵合金。借助於原子探針層析，透射電鏡以及X射線衍射技術，對L12 型多組元納米顆粒的本征化學性質及晶格錯配進行精細地测定。隨後，對合金進行拉伸性能測試，并採用透射電鏡和中子衍射結束對其位錯結構的演變進行表征。綜合以上結果， 进一步探討L12 型多組元納米顆粒對該析出強化型高熵合金的塑性變形穩定的影響。 其次，我們計劃對L12 型多組元納米顆粒在高溫條件下的熱穩定性進行系統的研究，包括相轉變行為及動力學粗化等。並且，採用多尺寸的測試方法，對該析出強化高熵合金在高溫條件下的力學性能， 氧化以及蠕變行為進行嚴格的評估。 本提案的成功實施將對該新型L12 型多組元納米顆粒及其對變形機制的影響提供一個綜合和全面的認知。 更為重要的是，本研究成果將提供一種非常有效的指導， 可用於加速工程用析出強化高熵合金的設計， 并獲得更為優異的力學性能。

11202718.label: Realisation of objectives
11202718.value: Object 1: To quantitatively reveal the structural features of the novel L12-type MCNPs and then to elucidate the intrinsic origins of the superb deformation stability and the suppression of the necking behavior in MCNPs-strengthening HEAs. Through tensile load-unload-reload (LUR) tests, We observed a significant increase in effective-stress hardening (short-range forest dislocation hardening), the strengthening contribution of which is almost identical to that of the back-stress hardening (long-range directional dislocations). Therefore, the high work hardening of the (FeCoCr)86Al7Ti7 alloy within this stage was originated from both the back-stress hardening and forest dislocation hardening, which enables this alloy to maintain an unusually higher work-hardening state without the onset of early local necking. By contrast, for the true strain of ~22%, the dislocation structure of the (FeCoCr)86Al8Ti6 alloy was mainly dominated by the planar-slip dislocations. The resultant long-range back-stress hardening is comparable to that of the (FeCoCr)86Al7Ti7 alloy, accompanied by a lower increase in the effective stress. As a result, we ascribed the inferior work-hardening response of the (FeCoCr)86Al8Ti6 alloy to an insufficient short-range effective-stress hardening, leading to a relatively earlier onset of plastic instability. With the further deformation to the true strain in the range of 28%~38% for the (FeCoCr)86Al7Ti7 alloy, the main deformation characteristics are deformation-induced microbands. We detected neither mechanical twinning nor transformation-induced martensite, the formation of these microbands generate a significant increase in back-stress hardening, which is conducive to maintain the work-hardening capacity in the (FeCoCr)86Al7Ti7 alloy for a continuous and stabilized plastic deformation. Moreover, the grain subdivision and refinement induced by these dislocation substructures further contribute to the strength enhancement because of the dynamic Hall-Petch effect. The relatively weaker microband-forming ability of the (FeCoCr)86Al8Ti6 alloy might be ascribed to its lower dislocation accumulation in the early stage, in which the internal stress is insufficient to activate the cross-slip of dislocations as well as the subsequent formation of microbands. Although we observed some microbands in the necking region, the resulting strain hardening in (FeCoCr)86Al8Ti6 alloy comes too late to compensate for the decrease of load-carrying capability caused by the geometric softening. In addition, the relatively higher Ti/Al ratio promotes a substantial increase in the antiphase boundaries energy and a higher work-hardening because of the generation of dislocations cross-slip, which in turn favors the activation of microbands and produces an extended uniform deformation. Some results summarized above have been published in Acta Materialia and Scripta Materialia: BX Cao, WW Xu, CY Yu, SW Wu, HJ Kong, ZY Ding, TL Zhang, JH Luan, B. Xiao, ZB Jiao, Y Liu, T Yang*, CT Liu*. A novel L12-strengthened multicomponent Co-rich high-entropy alloy with both high γ′-solvus temperature and superior high-temperature strength. Acta Materialia 229 (2022): 117763. BX Cao, HJ Kong, ZY Ding, SW Wu, JH Luan, ZB Jiao, J Lu, CT Liu*, T Yang*. A novel L12-strengthened multicomponent Co-rich high-entropy alloy with both high γ′-solvus temperature and superior high-temperature strength. Scripta Materialia 199 (2021): 113826. Object 2: To evaluate the structural stability and mechanical performance of the MCNPs-strengthening HEAs at elevated temperatures. Thermally stable high-entropy alloys (HEAs) consisting of a high density of coherent precipitates show great potential for high-temperature applications. The structural stability of MCNPs predominantly determines the temperature range for the service of the alloys. As a result, we investigated the phase stability and coarsening kinetics of L12-type MCNPs isothermally aged at 800, 900, and 1000 °C. Aged microstructures in the grain interiors under this temperature range were essentially dominated by the uniform precipitation of multicomponent (Ni,Co,Fe)3(Ti,Al)-type precipitates with the L12 structure. The coarsening kinetics of these intragranular L12 precipitates were quantitatively determined and adequately characterized by the classical Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner (LSW) model. The activation energy for coarsening was determined to be 378 kJ/mol, which is relatively higher than that of conventional Ni or Co-based superalloys, suggesting a slower elemental diffusion in the HEA matrix. More importantly, the heterogeneous precipitation and the associated metastable phase transformation mechanism along grain boundaries (GBs) were carefully analyzed. Localized chemical heterogeneity, especially the enrichments of Ti and Al, was identified within the discontinuous L12 phase at the GBs, which thermodynamically destabilizes the L12 structure and encourages the formation of the brittle Heusler phase. These findings will not only shed light on the precipitation mechanisms in compositionally complex HEAs but also generate new opportunities to the interfacial design of HEAs for advanced high-temperature applications with superior properties. Some results summarized above have been published in Acta Materialia and Materials Science and Engineering: A: T. Yang, Y.L. Zhao, L. Fan, J. Wei, J.H. Luan, W.H. Liu, C. Wang, Z.B. Jiao, J.J. Kai, C.T. Liu*. Control of nanoscale precipitation and elimination of intermediate-temperature embrittlement in multicomponent high-entropy alloys. Acta Materialia 189 (2020) 47-59. BX Cao, T Yang, L Fan, JH Luan, ZB Jiao, CT Liu*. Refractory alloying additions on the thermal stability and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys. Materials Science and Engineering: A 797 (2020): 140020. Object 3: To determine the intrinsic mechanical properties of these multi-component L12 alloys. It is known that the intrinsic properties of constituent L12 precipitates play an important role in determining the properties of dual-phase structured alloys. Thus, we carefully evaluated the atomic structures and bulk mechanical properties of the multicomponent L12 alloys. The L12-type ordered structure (a close-packed A3B-type ordered structure) of the grain interior was identified using bright-field transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We conducted aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) analyses to probe the detailed atomic structures and chemistries. The inner grain exhibits a highly L12-type chemical ordering with distinct atomic complexities of the constituent sublattices. We used atomic-resolution energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping to show that Ti and Al atoms mainly occupy the vertices (B sublattice) of the L12 unit cell, whereas the faced centers (A sublattice) are occupied mainly by Ni and Co atoms. Iron atoms occupy both the sublattice sites of the L12 unit cell, allowing the alloy to be stoichiometric. This sorting of the complex atomic site-occupation behavior is remarkably different from that of conventional binary ordered alloys, in which each sublattice is essentially occupied by a single type of element. Partial replacement of Ni with Fe and Co decreases the electron density (the average number of electrons per atom outside the inert gas shell) of the ordered structure. This structure helps suppress the formation of brittle hexagonal or tetragonal ordered phases. The L12‐type intermetallic alloy has ultrahigh strengths of 1.6 gigapascals with tensile ductilities of 25% at ambient temperature. Incorporating these strong and ductile MCNPs allows us to not only effectively impede the dislocation motion for strengthening but also increase the damage tolerance and dislocation storage of the alloys. Some of the results have been published in Science and Scripta Materialia: T Yang, YL Zhao, WP Li, CY Yu, JH Luan, DY Lin, L Fan, ZB Jiao, WH Liu, XJ Liu, JJ Kai, JC Huang, CT Liu*. Ultrahigh-strength and ductile superlattice alloys with nanoscale disordered interfaces. Science 369 (6502), 427-432 T. Yang, Y.L. Zhao, B.X. Cao, J.J. Kai, C.T. Liu*. Towards superior mechanical properties of heterostructured high-entropy alloys via engineering multicomponent intermetallic nanoparticles. Scripta Materialia 183 (2020) 39-44.

11202718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202718.value: The alloy systems strengthened by multi-component nanoparticle (MCNPs) have attracted a great deal of attention due to their unique coherent matrix-nanoparticle interfaces and superb mechanical properties at ambient temperature. The MCNPs-strengthening HEAs are simultaneously ultrastrong and ductile, with no strength-ductility trade-off and plastic instability. Such unique properties mainly originate from their multi-component nature and special chemical structure, compared with conventional alloys. With the aid of theoretical and experimental methods, we have made an impressive achievement, which put some new insights into the fundamental understanding of the structural features, strengthening mechanism, and thermal stability of the MCNPs-strengthening HEAs. The resulting new-generation complex alloys could lead to superior structural properties, which are of great fundamental and applied importance for advanced engineering applications involving automobiles, bullet trains, cryogenic devices, and aircraft and aeronautic systems.

11202718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202718.value: Despite many advances that have been made in the project, widespread application of the multi-component L12 alloys remains elusive, largely limited by the irreconcilable conflict between strength and ductility at ambient temperatures. As the crystalline structure of the L12 alloys becomes highly ordered, catastrophic brittle failure takes place easily at ambient temperatures and demolishes the most desirable properties of the alloys. Consequently, most conventional ordered alloys with ultrahigh strengths (gigapascal levels) are found to be highly brittle during tensile deformation, which severely limits their potential use in structural applications. Therefore, it is critical to developing high-strength L12 alloys with respectable ductility for structural applications in the future.

11202718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202718.value: We demonstrated that coherent precipitation of multi-component nanoparticles (MCNPs) based on the face-centered-cubic (FCC) HEAs offers a highly effective strategy to achieve a superb strength-ductility combination. These elaborately designed L12-type MCNPs can not only significantly strengthen the alloys, but also simultaneously ductilize them with extraordinary plastic stability. We gained a comprehensive understanding of the intrinsic correlation between the innovative MCNPs and deformation mechanisms through successfully implementing this proposal. Of particular importance, the output results provide us with an effective guidance for the accelerated design of novel precipitation-hardening HEAs with superior mechanical properties for engineering applications.

11203218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203218.value: 中風是全球範圍內造成死亡和殘疾的第二大病因。87%的中風是缺血性的，主要由栓塞引發的腦動脈阻塞引起，而栓塞主要來源於頸動脈粥樣硬化。被確診患有頸動脈斑塊的患者易患中風的風險更高，改變飲食結構或者進行藥物干預治療可以顯著降低其卒中風險。因此，對具有高中風險的頸動脈斑塊患者進行更有效的鑒定將會對病患的管理以及中風的預防產生重要影響。本項目的最終目標是研發用於監測頸動脈粥樣硬化變化的三維頸動脈超聲測量工具，並基於測量結果提供準確的中風險評級。 本團隊開創了三維頸動脈超聲技術並驗證了其在風險分級與敏感治療監測中的應用。我們根據頸動脈粥樣硬化的病灶特性對頸動脈粥樣硬化的一些局部特徵進行研究，如血管壁加斑塊厚度（vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness, VWT）的增加或減少以及由於存在潰瘍引起的斑塊表面不規則性。我們研究發現，局部VWT變化測量值與導致斑塊不穩定的主要成分的變化密切相關，並提出測量三維體素-體素體積（voxel-by-voxel volume, ΔVVol）。我們假設，通過聯合VWT、表面不規則性、ΔVVol與斑塊紋理特徵可以有效提高預測準確性以輔助醫療診斷。然而，這些特徵的組合產生了不能通過常規分類器解決的250,000維分類問題。 卷積神經網路（convolutional neural network, CNN）已成功應用於廣泛的電腦視覺任務中。CNN的成功歸功於層級結構，使得其對特徵的表達能力指數性增加。現代圖形處理單元提供的層數，使得CNN具有足夠的表達能力來突破維度的限制。在本項目中，我們計畫開發一個目標敏感度、特異性以及準確率為90%的深度CNN結構，進而用於中風險評級。 本專案提出的CNN結構有許多為三維頸動脈超聲中風險評級量身定制的獨特功能，包括：（1）該結構能夠整合二維和三維頸動脈圖譜上的特徵，相比於只能支援同類型輸入的現有結構更加靈活，並且允許不同類型的特徵組合來提高風險分級性能；（2）該結構基於患者進行分類，相比於對一幅圖像內的一個獨立小圖像塊進行分類的現有CNN醫學應用而言，具有更大的規模，我們不同於已有的技術在小圖像塊中實現易損斑塊定位，而是通過整合數以千計的小圖像塊中不同類型的特徵來評估獨立個體的血管事件發展概率；（3）該結構能夠整合手動提取的斑塊紋理特徵，這些特徵在先前的研究中已經被證實與卒中風險相關；（4）該結構可以對輸入圖像空間中有症狀和無症狀動脈之間的物理差異進行視覺化，視覺化觀察結果可能可以對頸動脈粥樣硬化中的複雜的相互作用提供一定的臨床見解。 本項目的成功不僅可以提高卒中風險分級性能，更加深入地瞭解可以通過三維超聲成像提供的物理風險因數，而且可以提供一個基於CNN的結構化框架，對基於患者的特徵進行整合集成，從而在個性化醫療時代做出更好的管理決策。

11203218.label: Realisation of objectives
11203218.value: The work in Objectives 1 and 2 are highly correlated and discussed together. The works accomplishing these objectives were developed in a few stages. Correspondence alignment of the baseline and follow-up vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness (VWT) map was required for computing VWT-Change (ΔVWT). We developed an algorithm for correspondence alignment of 2D maps [1], but no previous study had been performed to establish that the correspondence optimization would lead to an increased sensitivity in detecting therapeutic effect. In Paper 4, we established that the patient-based, spatially weighted mean of ΔVWT (overline(ΔVWT)_Weighted) measured in the optimized map is more sensitive to treatment effect than the unoptimized map in a randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of a nutritional therapy. This study investigated 120 patients involved in a placebo-controlled trial aiming to evaluate the efficacy of pomegranate supplements. This study establishes a method to properly measure ΔVWT. The same study also showed that overline(ΔVWT)_Weighted can detect the effect of the pomegranate treatment in a statistically significant way, whereas the total plaque volume (ΔTPV) was not able to detect treatment effect. The development of a 3D carotid atlas was first published in Conference Publication 2; the technique was later expanded to a journal publication (Paper 7) in which we developed a more robust approach to compute the change of voxel-based vessel-wall-plus-plaque volume (ΔVVol). We compared the sensitivity of treatment effect of this new biomarker with ΔVWT in the same cohort described in the above placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of a nutritional therapy. The pixel-/voxel-based changes of VWT and ΔVVol were expressed as percentage changes and averaged over the entire carotid atlas to obtain a single metric to evaluate the change of carotid atherosclerosis for each patient. Although both ΔVWT and ΔVVol were able to detect the treatment effect of the nutrition therapy, ΔVVol has a much higher power in discriminating the treatment group from the placebo group. The number of patients required by ΔVVol to establish statistical significance between the treatment and placebo groups was approximately one-third of those required by ΔVWT. Although ΔVVol is a 3D property computed on a voxel-by-voxel basis, the spatial distribution of it was mapped to a 2D carotid atlas to be directly compared with the corresponding ΔVWT distribution. We have developed several deep-learning-based algorithms for evaluating the effect of a nutrition therapy based on ΔVWT and ΔVVol. The first study published as Conference Paper 2 was able to detect the effect of the pomegranate study based on ΔVWT. A deep autoencoder was used to generate the biomarker from VWT measurements represented on the 2D carotid atlas previously developed by our group. This study established that prominent features can be extracted from the ΔVWT maps to detect treatment effects. The second CNN we developed was published by the MICCAI conference (Conference Paper 5), a prestigious conference with an acceptance rate of ~30%. In this study, we developed a Siamese change biomarker generation network (SCBG-Net) to quantify VWV and vessel wall and plaque textural changes. The biomarker was evaluated in a cohort of 120 subjects randomized to pomegranate treatment or placebo. It was shown to have a higher sensitivity in detecting treatment effects than total plaque volume change (ΔTPV) or vessel wall volume change (ΔVWV). We also proposed a visualization framework that allows the highlighting of features contributing to the discriminative power of the biomarker. As this development is more related to Objective 3, this algorithm will be described in more detail later. We have published two journal papers (Papers 1 and 2) on using 3D ultrasound plaque texture to detect the effect of the same nutritional treatment described above. In the two publications, we generated two different biomarkers used to integrate 376 plaque texture features. These two biomarkers can detect the therapeutic effect of pomegranate whereas ΔTPV could not. The requirement of vessel wall segmentation of the 300-patient risk stratification study is a major difficulty in this project. To accomplish Objective 3a, we have developed a deep-learning-based segmentation algorithm (Paper 5) to address this issue. As the algorithm was trained in another dataset, domain adaption techniques were used to segment vessel wall in the 300-patient cohort. Textural features were extracted from the vessel wall using the technique we developed and published in Paper 1. We developed a technique based on a publication in our group [2] to generate a biomarker that indicates the risk level of patients based on 3D ultrasound features. We performed a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis by comparison with the cardiovascular events that occurred. The area under the ROC curve was 0.84, compared to an AUC of 0.79 reported for a similar set of patients in Van Engelen et al. [3]. We note that the major advantage of our method compared with Van Engelen’s method is that only automatically segmented vessel wall boundaries were required for the analysis, whereas manual carotid plaque segmentation was required in Van Engelen’s study. Plaque segmentation is time-consuming and requires a high level of expertise. As manual plaque segmentation is difficult, only a third of candidates could be trained to segment plaques [4]. Although target sensitivity, specificity and accuracy were mentioned in Objective 3a, we later found that it is better to assess a biomarker based on the ROC analysis, instead of reporting the sensitivity and specificity in a specific threshold. Accuracy is not a suitable metric for classification problems with an imbalanced dataset. In our study, only ~10% of patients experienced a cardiovascular event, and therefore, we should not assess the biomarker based on accuracy at an arbitrary threshold. Since the development of the CNN for wall segmentation in the 300-patient cohort took time, we tested the visualization tool stated in Objective 3b with the 120-patient cohort involved in the placebo-controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of pomegranate supplements. The visualization tool we developed was published in Conference Paper 5. We developed a novel activation map to monitor serial changes in the carotid vessel. We showed in the paper that our proposed activation map was more able to identify the location with plaque changes than the gradient-weighted ranking activation map (CG-RAM), a state-of-the-art approach quantifying image differences. This method is equally applicable to the 300-patient cohort. [1] Chen Y, Chiu B. 11203218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203218.value: The key development in this project is the establishment of sensitive and cost-effective tools to measure the progression of regression of carotid atherosclerosis in response to dietary/nutritional therapies. In parallel to the development of novel strategies to treat atherosclerosis, there is a need to develop sensitive and cost-effective image-based tools to assess the efficacy of these treatments. The requirement of sensitivity for detecting dietary/nutritional treatments is especially high because these treatments are not as powerful as intensive medical therapies, and the effects of nutritional treatments are measured on the background of statin therapies. In this project, we have established the change of vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness (ΔVWT) (Paper 4) and the voxel-based volume change (ΔVVol) (Paper 7) as two sensitive tools in assessing progression/regression in carotid atherosclerosis. Although both techniques have sufficient sensitivity in detecting the effect of a nutritional treatment, ΔVVol has a higher sensitivity because it can detect outward expansions of plaques as well as thickness change already detected by ΔVWT. The major advantage of ΔVWT and ΔVVol is that they can be measured only with the vessel wall segmentation. This is in contrast with total plaque volume measurement, which requires subjects to have measurable plaques and needs the plaques to be manually segmented from 3D ultrasound images. Plaque segmentation is time-consuming and prone to observer variability. One of the contributions of this project is the development of an automated vessel wall segmentation algorithm that makes VWT/VVol measurements more efficient (Paper 5). We have further proposed a strategy to improve the accuracy of automatic segmentation by training the segmentation model by baseline images for segmentation of the follow-up images acquired from the same cohort (Paper 8). With the support of this grant, we also pioneered the development of deep-learning approaches to generate biomarkers. We have developed patch-wise autoencoder techniques to quantify VWT measurements mapped on the 2D carotid atlas (Conference paper 2) and an SCBG-Net (Conference paper 5) in quantifying serial changes of vessel wall volume and texture in a cohort involved in the placebo-controlled study of the efficacy of a nutritional treatment. We also developed activation maps for users to visualize the location with major plaque changes. The interpretability of the model afforded by the activation map will help gain the trust of these novel techniques by clinicians, thereby promoting the use of the technique in clinical studies and practice.

11203218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203218.value: There are two important areas of development: 1. The SCBG-Net we published in Conference Paper 5 are 2D-slice based. A more global assessment of plaques along the entire carotid artery would likely benefit the sensitivity in detecting treatment effect and the performance in risk stratification. 2. The published vessel wall segmentation algorithm (Paper 5) segments the common carotid arteries automatically but requires the region of interest (ROI) to be manually identified for segmentation of the internal carotid artery (ICA) segmentation. ROI identification required for ICA segmentation still took a considerable time when we analyzed the 300-patient cohort. We have already developed a more automated carotid segmentation approach as a part of a GRF project funded later (CityU 11205822). This new segmentation approach will be used to improve the efficiency of later analyses.

11203218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203218.value: In parallel with the development of novel medical/dietary/nutritional treatments to prevent stroke, there is a critical need for sensitive and cost-effective image-based biomarkers to monitor serial changes in carotid disease. In this project, we have validated two biomarkers of carotid atherosclerosis: the vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness (ΔVWT) and the voxel-based vessel-wall-plus-plaque volume change (ΔVVol). These two biomarkers were shown to be sensitive to the effect of a nutritional treatment, which has a weaker effect than intensive medical treatment and is difficult to detect. ΔVWT/ΔVVol quantification requires vessel wall segmentation, which if manually performed, is time-consuming and prone to observer variability. We developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automate vessel wall segmentation. Deep learning approaches have also been developed to differentiate the treatment and placebo groups in the evaluation of the efficacy of a nutritional therapy. An approach for generating activation maps based on CNN outputs was developed to allow interpretation of the CNN-generated biomarker. The increased cost-effectiveness afforded by these biomarkers will allow more pilot studies to be performed to establish the effects of novel treatment strategies, thereby shortening the time that effective treatments are withheld from patients needing them.

11204618.label: Project Objectives
11204618.value: To synthesize the highly dense, bottom-up, all-inorganic and air-stable CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br and I) perovskite nanowires with the controlled chemical composition, crystallinity, surface morphology, diameter and length, and optoelectronic properties utilizing cost-effective vapor-phase deposition techniques. To establish the perovskite-compatible lithography process on flexible substrates in order to fabricate phototransistors based on single individual nanowires. To evaluate the performance of fabricated phototransistors for broadband photodetection in the visible to ultraviolet region. The findings would help to optimize the nanowire synthesis condition as well as the corresponding nanowire properties for the enhanced photoresponsivity and other parameters. To assemble the large-scale, uniform and well-aligned parallel arrays of perovskite nanowires on plastics via contact printing technique. These nanowire parallel arrayed films can be next configured into phototransistor arrays for practical utilizations.
