11204618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204618.value: At present, photodetectors have become an important component in modern optoelectronic systems. Despite significant recent progress has been achieved in various photodetector fabrication processes and technologies, the further detector development is still mostly focused on the performance under specific wavelength; however, the ability to respond to light over a broad spectral range on mechanically flexible platforms is essential to many applications in imaging, communication and spectroscopy, etc. The challenge is that there is always a lack of ideal materials with appropriate device structures having the capability to absorb broadband incident radiation with the good optoelectronic transfer efficiency. Recently, the advent of organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite (organohalide) nanomaterials has led to a major step forward in photovoltaics and pathed promising avenues for photodetection. Organohalide perovskites, in general, have been considered as superior light absorbing media and strong sensitizers in the entire visible to ultraviolet region with the absorption rate of light over 90 %, but the complexity of preparing organic components, air instability and incompatibility with conventional integrated circuit processes (e.g. lithography) are major bottlenecks for their practical deployment. As a result, there are still many issues and opportunities in the development and performance assessment of fully bendable, high-performance and broadband photodetectors based on perovskite nanomaterials. In this proposal, we will concentrate on the fabrication of all-inorganic air-stable cesium lead halide perovskite (CsPbX3; X = Cl, Br, I) nanowire parallel arrays as the photoactive channels as well as the development of perovskite-compatible lithography processes to achieve phototransistor devices on flexible plastics. The use of nanowire parallel arrayed films would enlarge the detector output signals and enhance their invariability and reliability. Also, as contrasted to typical perovskite photoconductor or photodiode structures, this unique phototransistor device configuration is employed to modulate carrier concentration of the device channels in order to significantly enhance the performance for broadband photodetection. In the end, we plan to build the large-scale phototransistor arrays and to assess their operation limits with the goal to establish a versatile, low-cost and powerful scheme to realize the fully flexible, high-performance and broadband image sensor arrays based on air-stable CsPbX3 perovskite nanowires for the detection of visible to ultraviolet region. 光电探测器是现代光电系统的重要组成部分。尽管光电探测器制备工艺和技术已经取得了重大的进展，特别是对于特定波长的光探测，但是基于柔性基底的宽光谱响应光电探测器的研究一直滞后，严重限制了其在成像、通信和光谱学等领域的应用。这主要是因为1）缺乏能吸收宽光谱且具有高光电转化效率的的光吸收材料；2）缺乏理想的光电探测器结构。最近，有机-无机杂化钙钛矿材料在光伏领域应用中取得了重要的进展，同样其在光电探测领域也展现了巨大的潜力。众所周知，有机-无机杂化钙钛矿材料可以吸收可见范围和紫外范围的光，且吸收率可以达到90%以上，被认为是一种理想的光吸收介质。但是，复杂的制备工艺、空气中不稳定性、与传统半导体工艺（如，光刻等）不兼容性等缺陷严重限制了有机-无机杂化钙钛矿材料的实际引用。因此，发展可弯曲、高性能、宽光谱响应的钙钛矿光电探测器是困难与机遇共存的。在本项目中，我们将致力于制备空气稳定的无机钙钛矿（CsPbX3; X = Cl, Br, I）纳米线阵列，并且发展与钙钛矿材料兼容的光刻工艺，实现基于柔性基底的光电晶体管。纳米线阵列的应用将会增大光电探测器的输出电流，且改善器件的可靠性和稳定性。与传统的光电导型和光电二极管型的钙钛矿光电探测器相比，我们制备的光电晶体管的三端器件结构可以有效调控载流子的浓度，进而提高宽光谱响应光电探测器的整体性能。最后，我们将制备基于空气稳定无机钙钛矿（CsPbX3; X = Cl, Br, I）纳米线阵列的大面积光电晶体管，实现低成本、可弯曲、高性能、宽光谱响应（紫外至可见范围）的图像传感阵列。

11204618.label: Realisation of objectives
11204618.value: In this project, we have successfully accomplished all the objectives with 100% of completion. Specifically, we developed a direct vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) growth of crystalline all-inorganic CsPbX3 (X =Cl, Br, or I) NWs (Objective 1). Large-area vertical perovskite NW arrays with a uniform diameter of ∼150 nm were successfully synthesized by using Sn catalysts. In order to understand the growth kinetics of these CsPbX3 NWs, the effect of various process conditions (i.e., growth pressure, growth temperature, catalyst density, and growth rate) on the NW growth are thoroughly investigated. In particular, the morphology of grown CsPbBr3 NWs was carefully evaluated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). It is clear that the vertical growth of CsPbBr3 NWs was observed on the substrate, whereas distinctive spherical-like catalytic seeds were witnessed in the tip region of individual NWs, designating the VLS growth process. Based on the other detailed characterization, it is revealed that the NWs were grown with a very narrow process window. It is important that the grown CsPbX3 NWs are defect-free and single-crystalline, being ideal for subsequent device studies. Once the perovskite NWs were optimized, they were then configured into phototransistors based on single individual nanowires (Objective 2). In order to obtain CsPbX3 NWs laid down on the substrates for subsequent device studies, a dry transfer method was used to separate the NWs from the growth substrates. Afterward, shadow masking or perovskite-compatible lithography was utilized to define the source and drain regions, and 5/80 nm thick Ti/Au film electrodes were deposited by electron beam evaporation. The channel lengths were 10 μm for all the devices performed in this study. Device characterizations were performed in an ambient atmosphere with an Agilent 4155C semiconductor analyzer and a standard electrical probe station. Also, laser diodes of 532, 450, and 405 nm were used as the light source for the photodetection measurement of CsPbI3, CsPbBr3, and CsPbCl3 NWs, respectively. The power of the incident irradiation was measured using a power meter (PM400, Thorlabs). To demonstrate their optoelectronic applications on both rigid and mechanically flexible substrates, single CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, or I) NWs were configured into photodetectors (PDs), while corresponding current−voltage (I−V) curves of these NW PDs were measured with and without the light illumination (Objective 3). The linear relationships of I−V indicated that the contacts between the CsPbX3 NW and Au electrodes were ohmic-like. Specifically, all the PDs with similar NW channel diameters of ∼150 nm gave the low dark currents (Idark) of 0.1−1 pA under a bias voltage of 5 V, which probably originated from the minimized free carrier concentration in high-quality VLS-grown NWs. When illuminated at an intensity of 9 mW/cm2 under the same bias conditions, the light current (Ilight) increases by more than 4 orders of magnitude to 8.6nA, 7.4nA, and 2.6nA for CsPbI3, CsPbBr3, and CsPbCl3 NW PDs, respectively. Also, they all exhibited excellent stability and reliability with the on/off switching measurement. The response times (i.e., rise time and recovery time), defined as the time for the photocurrent (Iph = Ilight − Idark) to vary from 10% to 90%ofthe peak current, were found to be less than 50 ms. All these results could indicate the excellent device performance in their corresponding emission band of wavelengths. Responsivity (R) and specific detectivity (D*) are other important figure-of-merits to quantify the device performance and sensitivity of PDs, which are defined as R = Ilight/(PA) and D* = RA1/2/(2eIdark)1/2, where A is the effective irradiated area on the NW and e is the electronic charge. Here, we used the cross-sectional area (A = L × d; L is channel length, d is NW diameter) to estimate the effective irradiated area of the CsPbX3 NW PDs. It is clear that both R and D* increased dramatically with the decreasing light intensity. Under a low light intensity of 0.2 mW/cm2, the R values of the CsPbX3 NW PDs were as high as 4489, 3306, and 1183 A/W, accordingly, while the corresponding D* values were up to 7.9E12, 6.0E12, and 6.6E12 Jones, for CsPbI3, CsPbBr3, and CsPbCl3, respectively. Impressively, these extraordinarily high R and D* values were better than those for other all-inorganic low-dimensional perovskite PDs reported in the literature and even comparable to those of the inorganic−organic hybrid ones, which demonstrate the superior material quality of the VLS-grown single-crystalline CsPbX3 NWs developed in this work. Apart from single NW devices, they were further explored with enhanced device performance as parallel arrays for practical utilization (Objective 4). For instance, the high-mobility CsPbBr3 NW devices could be realized via a simple surface charge transfer doping strategy. Based on the photoemission spectroscopy analysis, it is apparent that the CsPbBr3 NWs are strongly p-type doped by just depositing the molybdenum trioxide (MoO3) shell layer due to the interfacial electron transfer from CsPbBr3 NW core to MoO3 shell. After MoO3 decoration and device fabrication, the hole mobility of the CsPbBr3/MoO3 core−shell NW device is significantly enhanced to 23.3 cm2/(V s), together with a superior responsivity (R) up to 2.36E3 A/W and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of over 5.48E5% toward photodetection in the visible region. Importantly, this MoO3 shell passivation can effectively suppress the environmental degradation of perovskite core as revealed by detailed electron microscopy investigations; as a result, the excellent air stability of CsPbBr3/MoO3 core−shell NW FETs is achieved. All these results evidently indicate that it is promising to employ surface charge transfer doping to improve both the electrical performance and environmental stability of future nanostructured halide perovskite devices. After that, the optimized NWs were fabricated into highly-dense parallel nanowire arrays by a well-developed contact printing method to construct large-scale device arrays on different substrates, including both rigid and mechanically flexible substrates, in order to study their device array performance. Similar to the evaluation of a single NW device, we assessed the detailed detector performances of those arrays and their mechanical flexibility. As a proof of concept, different spatially patterned broadband irradiation had been focused and projected onto the detector arrays. By measuring the output current associated with each pixel, a two-dimensional intensity plot could be obtained to depict the spatial intensity variation across each pixel and to compare against the patterned irradiation evaluating the areal efficiency of the device arrays. On the other hand, for the endurance study, we concentrated on a single-pixel output current when the arrays were bent. During repetitive bending cycles, the normalized change in the output current (∆I/Io, where ∆I = I-Io; I and Io are the output current for the bent and relaxed states, respectively) of a single representative pixel was monitored as a function of the bending curvature as well as the number of bending cycles. All these results have provided valuable information regarding the ultimate performance limits and mechanical robustness of these phototransistor arrays based on CsPbX3 NWs. Overall, we have successfully fabricated high-performance, low-cost, and mechanically flexible phototransistor arrays. The crystalline and inorganic nature of CsPbX3 NWs could enable efficient and sensitive photodetection. More importantly, their nanoscale dimensions resulted in excellent mechanical robustness. Ultimately, we established a versatile and powerful technology platform to develop a robust large-scale integration path to realize highly efficient photodetector arrays beyond conventional thin-film technologies.

11204618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204618.value: Specifically, as reported in ACS Nano 2019, a direct vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) method to obtain CsPbX3 (X=Cl, Br, or I) nanowires (NWs) was developed by using Sn catalysts. The VLS mechanism allowed the synthesis of defect-free single-crystalline CsPbX3 NWs with precise control over the microstructural morphology, nanowire density, and chemical composition. The structural characterization showed that NWs all existed in the stable cubic (for CsPbBr3 and CsPbCl3) or orthorhombic (for CsPbI3) phase at room temperature. In order to demonstrate their optoelectronic applications, single CsPbX3 NWs were configured as photodetectors with respectable photodetection performance (responsivity exceeding 4489 A/W and detectivity exceeding 7.9E12 Jones) toward the visible light regime. Meanwhile, field-effect transistors based on an individual CsPbX3 NW were demonstrated, exhibiting superior hole field effect mobility of 3.05 cm2/(V s) measured at room temperature. Overall, these VLS-grown perovskite NWs provided versatile platforms for evaluating the fundamental properties and exploring the potential applications of one-dimensional perovskite nanostructures. Later, as reported in ACS Nano 2020, effective surface charge transfer doping of VLS-grown single-crystalline CsPbBr3 NWs via surface functionalization with MoO3 shell is established. Utilizing this surface doping scheme, the interfacial hole injection into CsPbBr3 NW cores would provide a high-efficiency modification to their electrical properties, manipulating the conductivity from ambipolar to dominant p-type and even all the way to metallic characteristics. In addition, given the ultra-high carrier concentration and reducing ionized impurity scattering, the hole mobility of CsPbBr3 NW transistors is significantly enhanced to 23.3 cm2/(V s) after 10 nm thick MoO3 modification, indicating a highly improved hole transport of CsPbBr3/MoO3 core−shell NWs. The optimized CsPbBr3/MoO3 core−shell nanowires can yield the enhanced photodetection performance with a superior responsivity (R) up to 2.36E3 A/W and an external quantum efficiency (EQE ) of over 5.48E5 toward the 532 nm regime. Importantly, the enhanced environmental stability of devices against ambient conditions is also demonstrated as a result of the excellent passivation provided by the MoO3 shell. All these results can clearly indicate that surface charge transfer doping is an enabling technology to realize high-performance and air-stable perovskite nanomaterials-based electronics and optoelectronics. In summary, all these major findings are significant and create relevant design guidelines for perovskite nanowires-based electronic and optoelectronic devices, to go beyond the conventional thin-film technologies for future utilizations.

11204618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204618.value: Although there are many important results delivered from this work, different areas are still needed to study these perovskite nanowires-based phototransistors further. For example, phototransistors are preferred to operate in broadband at different wavelengths, such as visible to ultraviolet regimes with low-operating power. In this case, it is essential to understand the spectral selectivity of these devices at different wavelength regimes. The halide composition of X in the CsPbX3 (X=Cl, Br, or I) in the device channel can be further optimized to enhance spectral selectivity and device performance. Another one is to integrate these phototransistor devices in self-powered operation mode and integrate them with other electronic devices. For instance, it is ideal to utilize perovskite nanowires as active channels for both electronics and optoelectronics. Particularly, these two devices can be easily integrated into one platform to perform photodetection and computation in a small form factor. All these further works would push forward nanowire-based systems for practical utilizations.

11204718.label: Project Objectives
11204718.value: Reliability modeling of 3D NAND flash: in order to understand and exploit the reliability characteristics of 3D NAND storage design, we will propose the first public available reliability model. The model will be evaluated on an industry-provided flash testing platform. Program disturbance minimization: program disturbance is magnified for 3D NAND flash. We will propose approaches to minimize its impact on both precise and approximate data to achieve reliability and performance improvement. Read disturbance minimization: read disturbance occurs when there are a large number of read operations. We will design approaches to achieve performance improvement by minimizing its impact on the critical data. Retention loss aware data management: we will investigate retention error characteristics of 3D NAND flash. Potential approaches include detecting the supported retention time and deploying differential refreshes for different data to achieve improved lifetime. Process variation aware data management: we will design approaches to detect the process variation and to judiciously place the data based on the weakness of blocks. With this approach, both the lifetime and performance can be improved.

11204718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204718.value: Due to the reduced technology size and increased number of bits per cell, traditional planar NAND flash memories can no longer offer low cost and increased capacity. Since 2012, 3D NAND flash memories have been developed to combat these limitations. Recently, cloud systems, web servers, and mobile devices are deploying 3D NAND flash memories to satisfy the ever-increasing capacity requirements. However, one critical issue the 3D NAND flash facing is its reliability, especially when it is constructed with high density and a large number of layers. The traditional schemes for solving the reliability issue involve using strong error correction codes (ECC), such as low density parity codes (LDPC). However, these codes have a high cost in power, implementation area, and latency. Moreover, since the reliability issues of the 3D NAND flash differ from those of the traditional planar NAND flash, most of the recent works on the planar flash are not suitable to be applied directly in the 3D flash. During the last few decades, relaxing the reliability of storage using approximate computing has become a hot topic. Many applications in domains like computer vision, media processing, machine learning, and sensor data analysis have achieved great efficiency in exchange for small compromises in computational accuracy. In storage applications, error tolerance has been allowed in a broad range of application domains, from server software to mobile applications. However, few solutions have been proposed to improve the performance and lifetime of the 3D NAND flash considering reliability. This project aims to fill this gap and develop a reliable and robust storage framework for 3D NAND flash. 3D NAND flash suffers from several reliability issues, including program disturbance, read disturbance, retention errors and process variation (PV). We propose to exploit these reliability characteristics to improve performance and lifetime by completing the following tasks. First, unlike the work done on planar flash models, we will develop the first publicly available 3D NAND flash reliability model. Second, we will exploit the specific program and read disturbance characteristics to improve device reliability. Third, we will exploit retention errors and PV to improve device lifetime and performance. Our results will be verified on an industry-provided testing platform and evaluated with widely used simulators and popular workloads. The success of this project will enable 3D NAND flash memories to be adopted extensively for embedded systems, personal computers and clouds, providing a tremendous drive for the innovation industry of Hong Kong. 随着存储元尺寸的缩小和存储密度的增长，传统2D闪存无法进一步满足低价高容量的需求。因此，2012年 3D闪存应运而生，逐渐被应用于云存储、服务器以及移动设备等对容量需求较高的场景。 3D闪存面临的主要问题在于其可靠性，由大量的存储层构成的3D闪存将有较高的错误率。为了解决闪存的可靠性问题，传统的方案主要通过使用更强纠错能力的纠错码来实现，比如LDPC。然而，为了提供更强的纠错能力，这些纠错码通常需要较高的功耗，较大的芯片面积以及较高的解码时延。除此之外，由于3D闪存上的错误特征和2D闪存的错误存在较大差异，现有的针对2D闪存的优化工作，大部分无法直接被应用于3D闪存的优化。近几十年来，通过近似计算来缓解可靠性问题的研究持续升温，包括计算机可视化、多媒体处理、机器学习和传感器数据分析等在内的多个领域取得有效进展。从服务器软件到手机应用，存储领域也有很多容错的应用场景。然而，目前没有工作从可靠性的角度来改善3D闪存的性能和寿命。 本项目将从这个角度出发，建立一个针对3D闪存的可靠存储框架。3D闪存的错误主要包括编程干扰、读干扰、保存时间以及制程差异，我们通过对这些错误进行分析，提取特征用于性能和寿命的优化。本项目内容主要包括以下三个部分：1. 建立一个公开的3D闪存可靠性模型。2. 通过分析编程干扰和读干扰的错误特性，对设备可靠性进行优化。3. 通过分析保存时间错误和制程差异特征，对设备寿命和性能优化。本项目的实验将在业界提供真实测试平台以及通用模拟器上同步进行，以验证提出方法的有效性。 本项目的成功展开必将促使3D闪存未来进一步在嵌入式系统、个人电脑以及云存储系统的应用，为香港的创新产业提供巨大动力。

11204718.label: Realisation of objectives
11204718.value: We conducted extensive experiments on 3D NAND flash in understanding its reliability characteristics. We explored reliability causes including retention time, program/read disturbance, temperature, and constructed models in estimating reliability states for 3D NAND flash memory. To improve read performance for 3D NAND flash, we have proposed several techniques. First, we proposed to use sentinel cells to monitor the reliability changes of a word line and achieve read-retry minimisation to improve read performance. Second, we propose to explore asysmetric error characteristics of 3D NAND flash memory to improve LDPC decoding performance when there is reliability degradation.

11204718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204718.value: The read performance of 3D Flash NAND flash can be improved with implementation of sentinel cells. Sentinel cells monitor the reliability states of a flash word line and provide instant decision on the right voltage to read. Read-retries are minimised and hence flash memory performance is significantly improved. LDPC is commonly apply in 3D NAND flash memory today when there is a presence of reliability issues. Considering the asysmetric characteristics of 3D NAND flash reliability cases, we proposed asymmetric LDPC decoding for 3D NAND flash to improve the performance.

11204718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204718.value: In the future, we plan to continue explore temperature-related reliability issues for 3D NAND flash memory. How to improve read performance after temperature changes is still a challenge.

11204718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204718.value: 3D NAND flash memory is widely used today, from mobile devices to servers, as storage. Understanding the reliability characteristics of 3D NAND flash, with the proposed techniques from this project, we can significantly improve the performance of 3D NAND flash memory. Hence benefit all users who use devices with 3D NAND as storage.

11204918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204918.value: 我們的團隊將開發一種新型可穿戴數字香味生成設備，用於增強虛擬現實用戶體驗。目前，還沒有被廣泛接受的技術可以可靠且準確地按需分配氣味，特別是對於可穿戴設備。我們將使用微機電系統（MEMS）技術來製造陣列式微型加熱器和噴嘴孔，從而實現一種用來生成數字香味的可穿戴粘性流體霧化平台。這個霧化平台的一個重要特徵是它能夠產生10微米（或更小直徑）的液滴作為噴霧，因為大於10微米的液滴不太可能被嗅覺組織吸收。該設備還可以釋放多種氣味，并通過激活嗅覺來增強用戶的體驗。這個設備的其中一個終極目標是將其與ECG（心電圖），EEG（腦電圖）和皮膚電導傳感器相結合，來量化情緒的變化，例如不同氣味被激活時所產生的心率變化，放鬆和壓力。 目前，最普遍的便攜式霧化器是基於使用鋯鈦酸鉛（PZT）作為高頻壓電器，來產生小的流體液滴。這項技術的主要缺點是鉛是一種有害物質，該物質會破壞神經系統并導致腦部疾病，尤其對於幼兒。由基於PZT技術產生的細顆粒可能受到污染，因此不適合日常生活應用。此外，諸如超聲霧化器的普通壓電霧化器不能使粘性流體霧化，同時噴射霧化器效率低且不方便，因為它們需要壓縮空氣。我們的團隊已經證明了無鉛霧化器的可行性，該霧化器可以霧化粘度約為水的200倍的流體。基於該平台，在此項目中，我們將展示一種基於硅的粘性流體霧化器，用於按需生成可以被嗅覺組織有效吸收的液滴。為了實現小尺寸且可靠的粘性流體霧化器，本項目將解決幾個關鍵的工程挑戰和科學問題：1）通過溫度來控制流體粘度，增強霧化器室中的管道流速; 2）確定最佳噴射工作循環，以確保霧化器在沒有顯著減少液滴噴射時間響應的條件下的長期可操作性，; 3）最佳的腔室幾何設計來控制氣泡成核的大小，以確保液滴噴射的穩定模式。提案中讨论了解决这些问题的详细信息

11204918.label: Realisation of objectives
11204918.value: All objectives were achieved in this project as discussed below. In terms of developing a wearable viscous fluid atomization platform for on-demand generation of droplets with diameter of ~10 um, the key components of the atomizer include a microheater array chip, nozzle array chip, firing chamber, and a nanomaterial-coated heater (which also serves as a filter). We integrated the nanomaterial-coated heater (temperature-controllable by providing heating current) into the scent generator in order to increase sorption coefficient of filter, and subsequently increase capillary flow of viscous fluid to the firing chamber. Our team found that carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were much easier to disperse in solutions than graphene, so in the past two years, we have focused on using CNTs to fabricate the sponge heater instead of using graphene. Hence, we will refer to this nanomaterial-coated sponge heater as the “carbon nanotubes-coated polyurethane sponge (CNTPUS) heater” from here on. The atomizer design, its working principle, and the fabrication process for the nanomaterial sponge heater are described below. The lead-free atomizer consists of three key parts: a holder, an atomization unit, and a heating unit. The holder comprised of an upper casing, a lower casing, a spacer, four bolts and nuts. The upper and lower casing is made up of resin fabricated by using 3D printing and held together by using 4 bolts and nuts. Both casings have a thickness of 3.5 mm and an opening with a diameter of 7 mm. The opening served as an outlet for the droplets ejected and a holder for the CNTPUS in upper and lower casing, respectively. Besides, there is a 400 μm thick spacer embedded in the upper casing to ensure a complete sealing. Two pieces of copper tapes on the lower casing act as the electrodes for the conductive CNTPUS. The nickel-cobalt (Ni-Co) nozzle plate has hundreds of cone-shaped micro-sized orifices whose diameters are approximately 20 μm on the bottom side and 95 μm on the top side. The center of the nozzle plate is intentionally designed to be curved inward to increase the rate at which the working fluid can be refilled from the refilling chambers to the firing chamber by capillary action. Additionally, a 300 μm thick PDMS spacer and a microheater plate are used to form a firing chamber and to nucleate bubbles, respectively. Moreover, the heating unit was made up of a CNTPUS which is a cylindrical polyurethane (PU) sponge coated with 0.022 mg/mm3 of multi-wall carbon nanotubes (MWCNT) solution. A cylindrical PU sponge (⌀ 7 mm * 5 mm) was cut and cleaned firstly by alcohol and then by deionized (DI) water with an ultrasonic bath sonicator. The cleaned sponge was then immersed in 5% MWCNT solution and gently vortexed for 10 min to ensure complete coating. Next, the sponge was centrifuged at 1500 rpm for 5 min to remove the excess MWCNT solution away from the pores, leaving only a thin layer of CNT on the skeleton’s surface. Finally, the obtained CNTPUS was dried in oven at 75 °C for 3 h to remove residual water. Consequently, a thin layer of CNT was uniformly coated onto the sponge skeleton. The atomizer can be divided into 3 chambers: firing, refilling, and heating chambers. Three chambers are initially filled with a working fluid. Then, current is applied through the CNTPUS to heat up the fluid in the heating chamber to a desired temperature. The atomizer is then ready to operate after the temperature of the working fluid in three chambers has achieved equilibrium. During operation, the fluid near the surface of the micro-heater is superheated by applying a short current pulse. Heat is spontaneously transferred by convection to the fluid and increases the temperature of the fluid, leading to bubble growth. This instant growth of bubbles is also known as explosive boiling. Firing event is a process when the bubbles act as an actuator to push the fluid out of the orifices. In this manner, a capillary force is initiated by the negative pressure developed between the two chambers. Thus, the firing chamber is refilled with fluid from the refilling chambers and is subsequently ready for the next firing event. Similarly, the empty refilling chamber is refilled through capillary force from the heating chamber and a giant fluid reservoir. In terms of the implementation of a circuit system to digitally generate scent on-demand using the developed wearable atomization platform, the following circuit was realized. A pulse width-modulated (PWM) driving circuit consists of a high-current power source, a signal generator, a n-channel MOSFET transistor (IRFZ44N), and an oscilloscope was used to drive the CNTPUS integrated scent generator. The operating principle of atomization is based on the superheating effect, i.e., for every cycle, a short-duration current pulse (less than one hundred milliseconds) with a peak current of 1–2A was applied to the CNTPUS heater to superheat the fluid. The thermal bubbles generated at micro-cavities and/or sides of the microheater will then pump the fluid in the firing chamber out of the micro-orifices. The period of the driving signal could be adjusted such that the duty cycle always lies lower than 50% to prevent overheating. In terms of exploring scent-mixing capability of the atomization platform to combine at least 4 different scent fluids to produce new scent sensations, the following have been accomplished. Four replaceable and refillable scent cartridges were integrated with the atomizers, i.e., each cartridge containing a particular odor fluid was attached to an atomizer. Each atomizer was controlled by a chip that received the control signals from an audio chip (CM6533) and activated the atomizers accordingly. An EEPROM in each cartridge recorded the scent of smell of the cartridge and detected the amount of liquid inside. We demonstrated that these 4 scent-releasing devices can release mists according to recognized audio effects from a gaming video, e.g., gun fire, forest, ocean, tire-burning, etc.

11204918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204918.value: To summarize, this study presents a lead-free MEMS based atomizer with CNTPUS using the principle of micro-thermal bubble actuation under a pulse heating mode. It consists of holder, nozzle plate, heater plate with microheater lines, a spacer, and a carbon nanotubes-coated polyurethane sponge (CNTPUS) heater. Different experiments were carried out to study the improvement made on the atomization rate by the heating effects of the CNTPUS. With an average power of 1.0 W supplied to the CNTPUS, it can generate heat energy that could increase the temperature of selected scent fluid by 88°C. The novel sponge-heater was used to significantly improve the volume of high-viscosity scent fluid ejected from an atomizer. For example, at room temperature, the atomizer only ejects approximately 0.001 mg droplets of the fluids tested in this work for each atomization cycle. However, when the CNTPUS is heated up to a range of 35 °C to 65 °C, the CNTPUS using an average power of approximately 0.34 W and 0.36 W can achieve an atomization rate of 0.015–0.04 mg for 50%PG/50%VG (PG= propylene glycol; VG=glycerol) fluid, and 0.003–0.01 mg 30%PG/70%VG fluid per atomization cycle, respectively. By comparing the total mass of the droplets ejected after 1 min, the atomizer with the heated CNTPUS sponge (55 °C) ejected 1166% of 50%PG/50%VG and 1400% of 30%PG/70%VG more than the non-heated sponge. The operating principle of atomization is based on superheating effect, i.e., for every cycle, a short-duration current pulse (less than one hundred milliseconds) with a peak current of 1–2A is applied to the CNTPUS microheater to superheat the fluid. The thermal bubbles generated at micro-cavities and/or sides of the microheater will then pump the fluid in the firing chamber out of the micro-orifices. Additionally, with the heating effect of the CNTPUS, our current design has allowed the atomization rate higher than 0.01 mg of 50%PG/50%VG and 0.006 mg of 30%PG/70%VG per atomization cycle without overheating the microheater, which has then improved the refilling efficiency into the fluid reservoir for high-viscosity fluids. Finally, compared to the previous atomizer design that can only eject fluids with viscosity up to 200 cP, the atomizer developed in this project was shown to operate with a wider range of fluid viscosities, i.e., up to 580 cP, at room temperature. Hence, the integration of CNTPUS has advanced our atomizer in terms of an increased mass of droplets ejected, a faster fluid refilling process, and a wider range of applicable fluid viscosities. The development of this novel lead-free MEMS-based atomizer with CNTPUS will benefit the healthcare and well-being industries. For example, the scent generation from miniaturized built-in atomizer in virtual reality (VR) headset may trigger the olfactory bulb, and further enhance the user experience of VR system. We are preparing to publish the technical details of this work soon, especially in applying this new technology to Metaverse apps (see Part C: #11: S. M. Chin, et. Al., “Atomization of High-Viscosity Fluids in Wearable Scent Generator for Applications in Metaverse”, under preparation).

11204918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204918.value: The developed scent generation device can be further improved by reducing its overall volume and energy consumption. It can be further miniaturized to develop integrated scent fluid atomizers for virtual reality systems or Metaverse applications. To advance Metaverse experience, the development of an integrated platform that allows for all five virtual senses to occur, i.e., vision, sound, taste, smell, and touch, will be a key engineering challenge in the coming decade. We propose to advance the this research by enhancing the number of scents the atomizer can generate in the future – that is, much more research effort should be devoted to studying how different mixture ratio of existing scent fluids can be use generate different ‘scent sensations’. About two decades ago, the company Digiscents created a system that supposedly produced thousands of odors daily with a small cartridge containing 128 basic odors. With the advent of micro/nano fabrication and machine learning technologies in the past 20 years, we believe that a wearable scent generation device can now be created to deliver hundreds of different odors. We will apply for GRF and ITF funds to explore this possibility in the next few years.

11204918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204918.value: This project developed a lead-free micro atomizer for high-viscosity scent fluids using microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology. By developing an innovative fabrication process to produce carbon nanotubes-coated polyurethane sponge (CNTPUS) as a heating material, the temperature of high-viscosity scent fluids can be increased by 88°C using only approximately 1.0 W power. This high-efficiency heating capability of the CNTPUS has significantly increased the number of droplets that can be ejected from an atomizer when high viscosity fluids are used. For example, at room temperature, the atomizer can only eject approximately 0.001 mg of fluid droplets during each atomization each cycle. However, when the CNTPUS is heated up in the range of 35 °C to 65 °C, (i.e., consuming approximately 0.34 W and 0.36 W, respectively), the atomization rate increased to 0.015–0.04 mg of droplets for 50%PG/50%VG fluid, and 0.003–0.01 mg of droplets for 30%PG/70%VG fluid per atomization. In addition, compared to previous designs that can only eject fluids up to 200 cP viscosity, our atomizer was shown to operate with a wider range of fluid viscosities, i.e., up to 580 cP. Potential applications of this new atomizer with CNTPUS include healthcare, well-being, and virtual reality industries.

11205018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205018.value: 高熵合金作為近年來新出現的一類新型金屬，通常有四到五種以上的元素等比例或近等比例合成，它的出現引起了材料領域的廣泛關註。由於高熵合金通常具備優異的高溫力學性能，抗腐蝕/氧化性能，它已被提議並成為下一代核能系統的備選結構材料之一。值得強調的是，高熵合金出眾的抗輻照損傷性能也被來自美國橡樹嶺國家實驗室和密歇根大學的研究人員報道。他們的研究表明：在500攝氏度加溫Ni重離子轟擊下，NiCoFeCr和NiFe兩種合金的抗輻照腫脹能力是純Ni金屬的100倍，這種現象的原因歸結於位錯的移動能力在復雜金屬體系中受到弱化，這種效應導致輻照缺陷（如位錯和空洞）的演化被抑制。類似的結果也在FeNiMnCr高熵合金中出現，對比研究發現該合金比Fe-Cr-Ni的奧氏體不銹鋼有更強的抗輻照損傷能力。 在晶體結構的材料中，輻照缺陷是各類材料損傷和性能的退化的來源。在高能粒子撞擊下，輻照產生的空位和間隙原子等點缺陷通常會演化成不同種類的輻照缺陷。取決於輻照劑量和輻照溫度等因素，輻照缺陷的形態最終呈現為：空位/間隙原子團簇（黑點）、位錯環/位錯、層錯四面體和空洞/氣泡等。通常人們認為層錯能是影響材料面缺陷形成能力的關鍵因素，而最近的研究結果發現：高熵合金通常具有很低的層錯能，並導致其在室溫或低溫環境下具有獨特的變形機制，如納米孿晶和層錯等。從這個角度出發，我們很自然的做出假設：層錯能是否會影響高熵合金中輻照缺陷的演化過程。遺憾的是，無論是對於新型高熵合金還是核能產業中廣泛應用的傳統結構材料，層錯能與輻照缺陷演化的因果關系都未被系統研究。 該研究項目旨在揭示層錯能對高熵合金中輻照缺陷演化的影響和作用。長遠來看，我們希望將高熵合金發展成為一類成熟的核能結構材料。基於上文的研究假設，我們首先會設計並合成一系列具備不同層錯能的高熵合金，並使用加速器輻照的手段在材料中制造不同劑量的輻照損傷；之後，使用透射電子顯微鏡和三維原子探針等先進表征手段對材料中產生的輻照缺陷進行精確分析（結構信息和化學成分）；最後，利用分子動力學模擬計算等手段對實驗研究結果進行解釋和預測。該研究項目的完成可以至少解決以下三個科學問題：第一，微量化合金元素對基體層錯能的影響；第二，不同劑量下輻照缺陷在高熵合金中的形成規律；第三，層錯能對輻照缺陷演化過程的作用。最終，我們的研究成果會為設計新型抗輻照材料提供物理冶金方面的理論支撐。

11205018.label: Realisation of objectives
11205018.value: In the project, we designed two groups of multicomponent alloys, FeCoNiCr-based and NiCoCr-based HEAs, to study the influence of intrinsic property of stacking fault energy (SFE) on the radiation defects behavior. The ion irradiation campaigns were carried out at the Institute of Modern Physics, CAS (Lanzhou, China) and National Tsing Hua University (Hsinchu, Taiwan), respectively. The post-irradiation characterizations including TEM and APT analysis were performed at the City University of Hong Kong. All the proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. The details of objectives realization were illustrated one by one, as follows: 1. Evaluate SFE of HEAs with different minor alloying elements and conclude their variation tendency. Two groups of multicomponent alloys, FeCoNiCr-based and NiCoCr-based HEAs were chosen to study the minor alloying effects on the SFE. For the FeCoNiCr system, the minor alloying elements of Ti, Al and Cu were respectively added with the molar ratio of 0.2 into the parent alloy. The SFE of materials were measured by the transmission electron microcopy (TEM), based on the imaging the width of partial dislocations under weak beam dark field technique. The results indicated that the SFE of FeCoNiCr can be reduced by the Ti-addition while the effect of Al and Cu were not so significant. For the NiCoCr system, 0.1 molar ratio of Ti and W were respectively added into the parent alloy. The similar techniques were used to measure the SFE of the series alloys. The results showed that W can increase SFE while Ti lead to a reduction of SFE. In addition, we calculated the SFEs of FeCoNiCr parent alloy and Al/Ti doped FeCoNiCr alloys based on first-principles theory. The axial interaction model (AIM) was adopted to calculate averaged SFEs for the FeCoNiCr-based alloys through the constructed special quasirandom structures (SQS) with optimized short-range order parameters. We employed the slab model to probe the changes near the stacking fault region induced by Al/Ti dopants, the results showed that Ti-doping can significantly decrease the SFE of system, which were consistent with the experimental measurement. 2. Explore the radiation behaviors of HEAs upon ion irradiation at elevated temperature. Three sets of ion irradiation experiments were carried out for the candidate materials of FeCoNiCr-based HEAs and NiCoCr-based HEAs. The first set of ion irradiation was conducted at the material terminal of Low Energy Heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (LEAF) in Institute of Modern Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IMP, CAS). The FeCoNiCr-based HEAs with 0.2 molar ratio of Al/Cu/Ti addition were irradiated by 2 MeV He ions to a peak damage of ~ 0.3 dpa at four different temperatures of 673 K, 773 K, 873 K and 973 K, respectively. The second set of ion irradiation was conducted at the Accelerator Laboratory at National Tsing Hua University. The NiCoCr-based HEAs with 0.1 molar ratio of Ti and W addition were irradiated by 275 keV He ions at 673 K and 973 K to a fluence of 6.4 × 1020 m-2, the nominal peak damage can reach ~ 1.6 dpa. The third set of ion irradiation was performed at Institute of Modern Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IMP, CAS). The FeCoNiCr-based HEAs with 0.2 molar ratio of Al/Cu/Ti addition were irradiated by 3 MeV Ni ions to a al peak damage of ~ 100 dpa at 873 K. Based on the above irradiation campaigns, the radiation defects behaviors were fully explored at various temperatures and the high dose condition. Thus, the evolution of radiation defects at different stage could be investigated at the following characterization. 3. Reveal the effects of SFEs on the evolution of radiation induced defects in HEAs. For the samples of FeCoNiCr-based HEAs irradiated by 2 MeV He ions, two types of radiation defects were observed in the peak damaged region, as He bubbles and dislocation loops. The results showed that minor alloying addition can lead to a slightly effect on the bubble behavior while gave more significant influence on the dislocation loop evolution. Frank dislocation loops in the FeCoNiCr HEA coarsened with increasing irradiation temperature and gradually integrated into a network dislocation structure. Comparing to the parent alloy, the addition of Cu or Ti significantly promoted the growth of faulted loops, while the effect of Al-addition was not so obvious. As the temperature dependent microstructural evolution in the Ti-HEA was always dominated by faulted loops, substantial untangled dislocation lines were observed in the Cu-HEA at 973 K. The heavy ion irradiation by 3 MeV Ni ions at 873 K for the same batch of samples also indicated that the stacking fault featured dislocation loops dominated the microstructures of Ti-addition HEA. In addition, as the faceted void structures were observed in the parent alloy irradiated to ~100 dpa, the abnormal two-dimensional vacancy discs were detected in the Ti-addition HEA. The similar effects of minor alloys addition on the radiation defects behavior were also detected in the NiCoCr-based HEAs. 4. Establish a generalized theoretical model for the relationship between SFE and radiation induced defects. Based on the experimental observations, we found that the SFE played an important role in the radiation defects evolution, in particular for the defects of dislocation loops. Thus, we employed the classical rate-theory models to bridge the correlations between microstructural evolutions and the tuned intrinsic properties. During irradiation, the loop growth is depending on the net flux of point defects towards it and the vacancies thermally dissociated from it. The thermodynamic stability of 1/3<111> Frank loop is essentially controlled by its configuration energy against that of 1/2<011> perfect loop with the same size. During the prolonged irradiation of high dose value, the unstable Frank loop of a/3<111> shall cooperate with a Shockley partial dislocation of a/6<112> to produce a prismatic perfect loop of a/2<110> on the habit plane of {111}, according to the well-known unfaulting reaction: a/3 〈111〉+a/6 〈112〉=a/2 〈011〉. It is noted that a Shockley partial dislocation must be nucleated somewhere to feed the unfaulting reaction. If we considered the internal strain field caused by Frank loop was the dominant source of stress for the Shockley partial nucleation in this study. Since lowering SFE can relax the internal stress and decrease the probability of Shockley partial nucleation, it will be reasonable for the absence of perfect dislocation structures in the Ti-addition HEA. 5. Draw a guideline for the development of the radiation tolerant materials via tuning SFE. Based on the experimental observations and atomistic simulations, the effects of SFE on the radiation defects were obtained that the evolution of dislocation loops were delayed by lowering the SFE of alloy system, which shall further reduce the sink strength of dislocation featured radiation defects and changing the biased factor governing the void swelling. Thus, we draw a guideline for the development of the radiation tolerant materials. 6. Training graduate students to operate the ion accelerator, TEM and APT, and promote undergraduate students understand the materials applied in nuclear industry. During the period of this project, three PhD students in our group were fully or partially related to this project, the major research findings were embodied in their thesis. Their research trainings were also benefit from this project. In addition, several undergraduate students' final year projects (FYP) were involved in the projects, they were training to use the advanced research facilitates.

11205018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205018.value: In this project, we systematically explored the effects of SFE on the radiation defects behavior, including dislocation loops, radiation induced segregation and void swelling. Based on the extensive experimental activities and computational works, some important findings about the correlation between SFE and radiation defects were made as follows: (1) Since the SFE plays an important role in the defect configuration energy in crystalline, the influence of SFE on radiation defects was most direct and significant on the dislocation loop behavior. While lowing the SFE can stabilize the faulted structures, the 1/3<111> featured dislocation loop can grow into a considerable size and did not undergo structural transformation. Furthermore, lowering SFE can relax the internal stress and decrease the probability of Shockley partial nucleation, it will be reasonable for the absence of perfect dislocation structures in the low SFE alloy system, such as Ti-modified HEAs. The delayed dislocation evolution will result in a lower dislocation density which implying a potential mitigated radiation induced hardening. (2) Comparing to the evolution of dislocation loop, the effects of SFE on the radiation induced segregation and void swelling were indirect but being profound. For the RIS behaviors at the faulted planes of dislocation loop, lowering SFE shall reduce the strain field associated with faulted planes, thereby decrease the sink efficiency for point defects absorption and consequently suppress the RIS intensity. The influence of SFE on the void swelling were realized by tailoring the sink strength ratio of dislocations and void structures during irradiation. Since the nature of biased sink of dislocations is the governing factor for the void swelling, a lower total dislocation density will decrease the level of unbalanced point defects and reduce the vacancy supersaturation during elevated temperature irradiation. It will finally suppress the void swelling in the low SFE materials. (3) Minor alloying is an effective strategy for tuning the SFE of multicomponent HEAs. Our experimental results clearly suggested that Ti addition can significantly decrease the SFE of FeCoNiCr-based or NiCoCr-Based HEAs. Through tailoring the SFE of alloy system by minor alloying addition, we successfully alter the radiation defects evolution and obtained a super radiation tolerant multicomponent alloy which can surpass most of candidate alloys for advanced nuclear application. Based on the above findings, the PI have led a dozen of important publications in the prestige journals, such as Nature Communications, Acta Materials, Journal of Nuclear Materials, etc. Please see in Part C.

11205018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205018.value: For the future work, we highly encourage the colleagues in the nuclear material community to do the following works along our track: (1) use the cutting-edge machine learning method to discovery more effective alloying strategy to develop the structure materials for nuclear application, which can balance the factors of phase stability, low activation, and high strength. (2) explore the potential effects of prevailed faulted dislocation loops on the mechanical property of irradiated materials. The nano-mechanical test maybe a feasible way to elucidate the influence of developed radiation defects on the deformation behavior of materials applied in the irradiation environment.

11205018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205018.value: Under the global goal of carbon neutrality in this century, nuclear energy, as a low carbon emission and highly efficient green energy will play a more important role in the future energy system. Considering the advantages of advanced nuclear reactors on the fuel breeding and nuclear waste disposal, Gen. IV reactors are believed to be the priority of next generation nuclear energy. However, the advanced nuclear reactors are usually designed to operate at the higher temperature regime and suffer more extensive radiation damage. Therefore, the structural materials innovation for radiation tolerance will be quite important for the deployment of advanced nuclear reactors. In this project, we successfully employed the minor alloy strategy to tune the SFE of the multicomponent high-entropy alloy and investigate their profound effects on the radiation defects behaviors. We find that the typical radiation defects of dislocation loop and void swelling could be tailored by this method with careful design. Finally, we also developed a superior radiation tolerant alloy for void swelling. The outcome of this project will certainly benefit the development of novel materials for nuclear application and embody the contribution of HK scientists for the nuclear energy.

11205118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205118.value: This project will develop statistical methods that utilize a low-fidelity model to significantly reduce computation cost incurred in estimation of parameters in a high-fidelity model from given physical experiment data. Computer models of a physical system can come in different levels of fidelity. These models are often computer codes that implement numerical algorithms to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) to different levels of accuracy or computer codes that solve systems of PDEs of different levels of complexity. Typically, a high-fidelity model is more time consuming to solve than a low-fidelity model but provides higher prediction accuracy for the real system. For practical problems encountered in geophysical, biomedical, engineering mechanics, and many other applications, parameters in computer models are often uncertain and need to be estimated from data obtained via experiments or observations on the physical system. This class of problems is called inverse problems or parameter calibration problems. Due to the smaller numerical errors and model bias, parameter calibration performed with a high-fidelity model incurs less bias, which can furnish more accurate information to the model user. However, because solving inverse problems can require thousands of runs of the computer model, computational cost is a key consideration in choosing a method to solve inverse problems for a high-fidelity computer model. In this project, we shall develop new statistical methods that utilize one or more low-fidelity models that share the same calibration parameters as a high-fidelity model to reduce computational cost incurred in estimating parameters of the high-fidelity model. We shall link the high and low fidelity models with autoregressive Gaussian process (GP) models, which combines information from the computer models at different fidelity levels to improve prediction of the output of the model with highest fidelity. Expedient Bayesian inference procedures for parameter calibration based a few versions of this model for modeling functional and multiple outputs shall be developed. In addition, we shall also design computationally efficient algorithms specifically for Bayesian inference in large scale inverse problems (problems with a large set of measurements on the physical system observed over a space-time domain). Sequential Bayesian optimal design approaches to reduce the number of high-fidelity simulations for parameter estimation will be developed. Key issues such as the appropriate optimal design criteria to employ, techniques to compute the criteria efficiently and accurately, and expansion or contraction of the experiment region based on the posterior distribution of the calibration parameters shall be addressed.

11205118.label: Realisation of objectives
11205118.value: Objective 1 has been addressed in Article #5, Article #7, Article #1, and Article #6. Article #5 proposes a novel Gaussian process (GP) emulator/model, called the boundary modified autoregressive GP (BMAGP) emulator, for bi-fidelity simulations with boundary information. Bi-fidelity simulations involve simulations at two fidelity levels called the high-fidelity (HF) and low-fidelity (LF) levels, where the HF simulator is more accurate but more time-consuming than the LF simulator. When such simulations are time-consuming, one can replace the HF and LF simulators with the autoregressive GP (AGP) emulator, which is an emulator tailored for pairs of HF and LF simulators (i.e., a bi-fidelity emulator) with identical inputs. Article #5 considers bi-fidelity simulations with two characteristics: (1) the HF simulator contains a vector of inputs absent from the LF simulator, called the augmented input, that captures modeling details neglected by the LF simulator, and (2) the HF simulator output (HF output) converges to the LF simulator output (LF output) when some/all components of the augmented input approach zero, which is information called boundary information (this name arises as it is assumed zero is a boundary point of the domain of each component of the augmented input). The article proposes BMAGP models (obtained by modifying the AGP emulator) that use covariance functions (CFs) constructed from CFs of integrated stochastic processes, called integrated CFs, to incorporate boundary information to improve prediction performance. Numerical examples show that BMAGP models that use CFs constructed from some novel integrated CFs derived in the article consistently predict better than the AGP model. Article #7 applies the BMAGP model proposed in Article #5 to estimate/calibrate simulator inputs whose values are unknown, called calibration parameters. Article #1 proposes a GP emulator for predicting the solution to a HF partial differential equation (PDE) model as a function of the HF PDE model’s parameters. The proposed emulator, which is useful for calibrating PDE model parameters, exploits information from an LF linear PDE model approximation to the HF PDE model to improve prediction performance. Lastly, Article #6 proposes a parameter calibration method that uses a novel bi-fidelity GP emulator for predicting the sum of squared errors (SSE) between the HF output and field data, called the HF SSE. This emulator is an AGP model for identical Box-Cox transformations of the HF SSE and a modified LF SSE (modified SSE between the LF output and field data). It is used to find the maximum likelihood estimate (MLE) of the calibration parameter vector (i.e., vector of calibration parameters), which minimizes the HF SSE. Objective 2 has been addressed in Article #4, Article #2, and Article #3. Article #4 proposes a Bayesian method to solve a large-scale inverse/calibration problem, i.e., calibration/estimation of a functional input/parameter to a time-consuming simulator given field data comprising observations on a physical quantity at a large set S of space-time points predicted by the simulator output. A stochastic process prior is specified for the functional parameter and computation of its posterior distribution is of interest. As a stochastic process prior is commonly represented by a finite but large number of its random values on a grid of points in computations, the calibration problem considered in Article #4 often has a high-dimensional calibration parameter vector with components given by such random values/variables. Moreover, since the simulator yields a high-dimensional output that predicts the field observations at the large number of points in S given any functional input setting, the dataset obtained from multiple simulator runs for building a GP emulator is often large. In Article #4, computational challenges in emulator-based parameter calibration due to the high dimensionality of the calibration parameter vector and the large sizes of the field and simulation datasets are addressed in three ways: First, the stochastic process prior for the functional parameter is reduced via its Karhunen-Loève (KL) expansion to a tractable number of random variables, which serve as the inputs to the GP model/emulator. This mitigates curse-of-dimensionality problems in building the emulator. Second, to keep the computational cost in building the GP emulator and evaluating the emulator-based likelihood of the calibration parameters low, a GP emulator with a constant prior mean and separable prior CF is used. This yields computationally efficient formulas for the MLEs of the GP emulator parameters and the posterior mean and covariance functions of the emulator. Third, a sequential design criterion called the weighted prediction variance (WPV) criterion that is computationally scalable for high-dimensional simulator input and output is proposed for improving the calibration results sequentially. In short, Article #4 proposes a computationally efficient method for calibrating (high-dimensional) functional parameters of time-consuming simulators based on large field and simulation datasets. Additionally, Article #2 proposes an emulator-based method for robust optimization of a simulator with a high-dimensional input, which can be adapted to solve high-dimensional inverse problems, while Article #3 proposes shape-constrained regression models that can be adapted into computationally efficient emulators for solving inverse problems with large datasets. Objective 3 has been addressed in Article #4 and Article #6. Article #4 proposes a GP-emulator-based Bayesian method for calibrating a functional parameter to a time-consuming simulator. The article makes two important methodological developments. First, a flexible prior for the functional parameter is constructed from a GP with random correlation parameters, and this stochastic process prior is reduced via its KL expansion into a vector Z comprising a tractable number of unbounded random variables. Second, the WPV sequential experimental design criterion for decreasing the effect of emulator prediction uncertainty on calibration results is proposed, and the criterion is rigorously proven to yield a sequence of emulator-based likelihoods that converges to the true likelihood. Since convergence of a GP emulator to the function it approximates can only be ensured on bounded domains, Article #4 constructs a GP emulator to approximate the simulator over a compact hypercube that contains Z with high prior probability. Although the proposed method uses a single-fidelity GP emulator, it can be modified to accommodate the use of a multi-fidelity GP emulator. Article #6 proposes a bi-fidelity Bayesian optimization method, i.e., an experimental-design-based optimization method that sequentially adds LF and HF follow-up runs, to find the MLEs of calibration parameters using a bi-fidelity GP emulator. 11205118.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205118.value: Bi-fidelity simulations involve simulations at two fidelity levels called the HF and LF levels. When bi-fidelity simulations are time-consuming, one can predict the HF/LF output using the AGP emulator, which is tailored for HF and LF simulators with identical inputs. However, in many cases, the HF simulator contains a vector of inputs absent from the LF simulator, called the augmented input. In these cases, boundary information, i.e., information that the HF output converges to the LF output when some/all components of the augmented input tend to zero, is often available. A major research outcome of this project is the development of the BMAGP emulator in Article #5 that incorporates boundary information via CFs constructed from integrated CFs. Two novel integrated CFs derived in the article, which are recommended for default use, are shown to each give a BMAGP emulator that consistently predicts better than the AGP emulator, especially when the augmented input is near zero. Calibrating a functional input/parameter of a time-consuming simulator using field observations at a large set of space-time points predicted by the simulator output is a challenging problem due to the high dimensionality of the simulator input and output, and the large sizes of the field and simulation datasets. A major research outcome of this project is the development of a computationally efficient sequential GP-emulator-based method in Article #4 to solve the calibration problem just described. Specifically, Article #4 employs a GP emulator that is computationally efficient to build with large datasets, and uses the KL expansion to reduce the functional parameter’s stochastic process prior to a tractable number of random inputs/parameters. It proposes a sequential design criterion that is computationally scalable for high-dimensional simulator input and output, called the WPV criterion, for reducing the effect of emulator prediction uncertainty on calibration results. Furthermore, Article #4 proves that the WPV criterion gives a sequence of emulator-based likelihoods that converges to the true likelihood, and demonstrates that the proposed method performs well via numerical examples. Another major research outcome of this project is the development of a computationally efficient method in Article #6 that uses a novel bi-fidelity GP emulator for predicting the HF SSE (SSE between the HF output and field data) to calibrate parameters of a time-consuming simulator. The proposed emulator is used to find MLEs of calibration parameters via a Bayesian optimization procedure for minimizing the HF SSE that is shown to perform well.

11205118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205118.value: Two areas have potential for further development. First, it is of interest to extend the BMAGP model proposed in Article #5 to simulations at m>2 fidelity levels with boundary information. In such simulations, the simulator at the (i+1)-th fidelity level contains additional inputs not in the simulator at the i-th fidelity level, where the (i+1)-th fidelity level represents a higher fidelity level than the i-th fidelity level and i=1,…,m-1. Incorporating boundary information, i.e., information that the output of the simulator at the (i+1)-th fidelity level converges to the output of the simulator at the i-th fidelity level as some/all the additional inputs converge to zero, in an extended BMAGP model requires further research. Second, it is of interest to develop a method to calibrate a functional parameter using a multi-fidelity GP emulator by extending the functional parameter calibration method proposed in Article #4, which uses a single-fidelity GP emulator. Replacing the single-fidelity GP emulator in the method proposed in Article #4 with a multi-fidelity GP emulator can yield improved calibration performance as a multi-fidelity GP emulator typically predicts the highest fidelity simulator better than a single-fidelity GP emulator for the simulator if both emulators are built with identical computational budgets.

11205118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205118.value: Parameter calibration based on time-consuming single-fidelity simulations or bi-fidelity simulations (simulations at a high-fidelity (HF) level and a low-fidelity (LF) level) arise frequently in engineering. This project advances the methodology frontier for solving such problems in three ways: (1) it develops improved Gaussian process (GP) emulators for bi-fidelity simulations, (2) it develops a computationally efficient method for calibrating functional inputs/parameters of simulators that yield high-dimensional outputs, and (3) it develops sequential-experimental-design-based procedures for parameter calibration. For (1), this project modifies the standard autoregressive GP (AGP) emulator to obtain a boundary modified AGP (BMAGP) emulator that predicts better by incorporating boundary information, i.e., information that the HF simulator output converges to the LF simulator output when some HF simulator inputs approach zero (which the AGP emulator ignores). For (2)-(3), this project develops a computationally efficient GP-emulator-based method for calibrating a functional parameter of a simulator with a high-dimensional output together with a sequential design criterion for reducing the effect of emulator prediction uncertainty on calibration results. For (1) and (3), this project develops a Bayesian-optimization-based parameter calibration method that uses an improved bi-fidelity GP emulator to sequentially minimize the sum of squared errors between the HF simulator output and field data.

11205318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205318.value: Data in the world is expected to grow to 163 ZB by 2025, which is ten times the data generated in 2016. This rapid growth of new data needs to be stored, which creates a surging demand for data center services. In Hong Kong, the data center sector has been growing fast because of the robust telecommunication infrastructure and reliable power supply. Besides, the HKSAR government has been committed to fostering the city as the prime location for data centers in Asia Pacific. This project aims to develop novel techniques for data storage, which can benefit both local and global data center industries. The unprecedented growth of data poses a formidable challenge to the design of reliable storage systems. The traditional way of providing data reliability is by means of 3-replication, which means that a data file is replicated three times and stored in three different storage nodes, so that it can tolerate simultaneous failures of two storage nodes. Its storage efficiency, however, is only one third, which is too low to cope with the ever-increasing volume of data. To reduce storage cost, novel coding techniques are needed. In practical systems, storage nodes fail frequently. How to replace them at minimum cost is an open problem. Based on existing coding methods, it is often very costly to regenerate the lost portion originally stored in the failed nodes, as the repairing process requires decoding of the entire file by accessing the data in many storage nodes. To speed up the repair process, a mechanism called local repair, which requires the access of only a few storage nodes, has been proposed. The design of locally repairable codes is now of key importance and has attracted much attention from the research community recently. This project distinguishes itself from others in that it takes into account the underlying network topology when designing locally repairable codes. In the literature, most code designs are based on classical algebraic coding methods, which implicitly assume that all storage nodes are identical and fully connected with each other. In a data center network, however, the data centers are geographically distributed and mesh-connected, and the storage nodes within a data center are interconnected often in a tree topology via switches. This project will exploit the network topology. Storage codes with high reliability, low storage cost, and low repair cost will be delivered as the project outcome. 預計到2025年，世界數據將增長到163ZB，這是2016年產生的數據的十倍。需要存儲新數據的快速增長，對數據中心服務產生了巨大的需求。在香港，由於強大的電信基礎設施和可靠的電力供應，數據中心的發展迅速。此外，香港特區政府一直致力將香港發展為亞太地區數據中心的首選地。這個項目旨在開發新的數據存儲技術，以使本地和全球數據中心行業受益。數據的空前增長對可靠存儲系統的設計提出了嚴峻挑戰。提供數據可靠性的傳統方式是通過三次複製，也就是把數據文件複製三份並存儲在三個不同的存儲節點中，使系統可以承受兩個存儲節點同時發生故障。然而，它的存儲效率只有三分之一，不足以應對不斷增加的數據量。為了降低存儲成本，新的編碼技術不可或缺。在實際系統中，存儲節點經常故障，如何以最低成本更換它們是一個懸而未決的問題。基於現有的編碼方法，重新生成本來存儲在故障節點中的丟失部分的成本通常很高，因為修復過程需要通過訪問許多存儲節點中的數據來解碼整個文件。為了加速修復過程，已經有人提出了一種稱為局部修復的機制，過程只需要訪問少數存儲節點。局部可修復碼的設計因而至關重要，最近引起了研究界的廣泛關注。這個項目與其他項目的區別在於，它在設計局部可修復碼時考慮了底層的網絡拓撲。在文獻中，大多數編碼設計基於經典代數編碼方法，其隱含地假設所有存儲節點是相同的並且彼此完全連接。然而，在數據中心網絡中，數據中心在地理上分佈並且網狀連接，並且數據中心內的存儲節點經常通過交換機以樹形拓撲互連。這個項目將基於網絡拓撲，設計出具有高可靠性、低存儲成本和低修復成本的存儲編碼。

11205318.label: Realisation of objectives
11205318.value: This project investigates distributed storage for data centers and other scenarios. There are two major objectives, both of which have been adequately achieved. First, a realistic multi-rack model for data centers has been considered, and a code design framework has been established. Considering the cheaper data transmission within the racks, our code construction method is able to locally repair node failures within the same rack by using only the survived nodes in the same rack. In the case of severe failure patterns when the information content of the survived nodes is not sufficient to repair the failures, other racks will participate in the repair process, resulting in higher repair costs. Therefore, it is critical for a locally repairable code to have multiple repair groups. Robust locally repairable coding schemes are needed, which guarantee that there are multiple distinct alternative local repair groups for any single failure such that the failed node can still be repaired locally even if some of the repair groups are not available. We have addressed how it can be done by appropriate code design. Second, the performance of the proposed codes has been evaluated by information-theoretic analysis and numerical studies. A linear programming bound is obtained to characterize the feasible code rates, which determines the storage efficiency. This practical bound can optimize the trade-off between different parameters of the code such as minimum distance, code length, locality, the number of alternative repair groups, and the number of extra failures. Numerical studies have been carried out to show the effectiveness of our code design. In summary, we have proposed storage codes for different network scenarios and their superior performance has been characterized by theoretical analysis and demonstrated by numerical techniques.

11205318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205318.value: Most works in distributed storage networks assume a simple network model with a collection of identical storage nodes with equal communication costs between the nodes. In this project, we consider a realistic multi-rack distributed data storage network and present a code design framework for this model. By employing the criteria of our multi-rack storage code, we establish a linear programming bound on the size of the code to maximize the code rate. The result was published in Journal Paper 2 of Part C. The above results are generalized to robust locally repairable codes, which provide multiple repair groups to minimize the system repair cost when node failures occur. Furthermore, we address the update efficiency problem of distributed data storage networks. We characterize the update-efficient storage code properties and establish the necessary conditions for the existence of update-efficient locally repairable storage codes. The results were published in Journal Paper 3 of Part C. We have also investigated the distributed storage problems for different network scenarios. Efficient solutions have been proposed for wireless distributed storage systems (Journal Paper 1), edge caching networks (Journal Paper 4 and Conference Paper 1), secure multi-cloud storage systems (Conference Paper 2), and distributed storage networks (Conference Papers 3 and 4). In those works, the superior performance of our proposed methods has been demonstrated by detailed computer simulations.

11205318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205318.value: The research results can be further extended to consider more complex data storage problems in future networks. Indeed, we have gone beyond the project's original scope, applying the ideas to wireless edge caching networks, secure multi-cloud systems, and distributed storage networks as described above.

11205318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205318.value: Due to the vast amount of data that needs to be stored for machine learning applications, how to increase storage efficiency becomes a very important problem to be addressed. Coding techniques thus play a key role in reducing storage space and increasing data reliability. While existing methods often assume all the storage nodes are identical, this project considers the storage nodes connected by a network with specific structures. When node failures occur, node repairs are needed, which requires data transfer from surviving storage nodes. The bandwidth of different network links should be considered to minimize the repair costs. This project addresses this issue by designing storage codes aware of network topology. The study, on the one hand, increases the fundamental understanding of storage code design, and on the other hand, proposes practical code design for various network scenarios, including multi-rack storage networks for data centers, edge caching for wireless networks, and distributed storage over multiple clouds. Our code designs are proven efficient in storage, repair, and update by extensive computer simulations.
