11205418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205418.value: 最新的半導體技術和材料科學降低了現代微電子電路和系統的功耗，例如物聯網和機器對機器設備，並且提高了能量收集產生器的效率，例如太陽能電池，熱電，壓電，電磁和靜電產生器，可將周邊環境中的能量轉換為電能。能量收集的目標是延長電池的充電間距，甚至取代電池。在各種環境能源中，收集由振動所產生的能量具有更穩定，清潔，高功率密度以及微細加工兼容性的優點。 典型的振動能量收集系統主要由三個部份組成，分別是能量收集產生器,交流直流轉換器和能量存儲元件。 交流直流轉換器將由能量收集產生器收集的交流電功率轉換為用於能量存儲元件和負載的直流電功率。在理想的情況下，不論任何負載條件，振動幅度以及頻率均可運行在真實最大功率點上。在數學上而言，轉換器的輸入阻抗需等於能量收集產生器輸出阻抗的複共軛。能量收集產生器的輸出電流應與能量收集產生器的開路電壓具有相同的相位和波形。然而，只有少數研究指出消除能量收集產生器的輸出阻抗對最大化功率輸送的影響。因此，能量收集產生器並不總是在真實最大功率點上運行。在能量收集產生器有相對大的輸出阻抗或振動頻率變化的時候, 問題會變得更加明顯。 此項目旨在研究交流直流轉換器的架構，使能量收集產生器能在真實最大功率點上運行。電力處理單元由混合結構組成，用以處理各種收集到的能量。為了減少功率的損耗， 項目中沒有選用有損二極管橋，而是製定複雜的控制算法，以控制電力處理單元去抵消能量收集產生器的輸出阻抗的影響並與能量收集產生器的輸出阻抗進行匹配，從而實現最大功率傳輸。最後，本項目將製定不同的條件和要求, 以允許負載在能量中性操作裡一系列的消耗模式下操作，使其收集和消耗的平均功率在同一時間間隔中是相同的。

11205418.label: Realisation of objectives
11205418.value: Objective 1 - To model, design, optimize, and implement an architecture for AC/DC conversion An electromagnetic energy harvesting system can be divided into three parts. They are energy harvester, ac /dc converter, and energy storage. Electricity is generated by the harvester by varying the flux linkage on the copper coil. However, the electromagnetic energy harvester, such as Permanent Magnet Generator, has non-negligible output reactance, especially under high frequency and low operation temperature. Most maximum power point trackers (MPPTs) for electromagnetic energy harvesters (EMEHs) are based on resistive matching technology, where the input resistance of the MPPT is made equal to the magnitude of the output impedance of the harvester. This is valid when the output reactance of the EMEH is much smaller than its output resistance. The discrepancy between the power extracted by the resistive matching technology and the maximum extractable power will increase as the output reactance increases. Under high excitation frequency and low operating temperature, the effect of the output reactance will become more dominant. To deal with such an issue, an MPPT that can counteract the effect of the coil inductance and match it with the coil resistance is presented. It does not require knowing coil parameters a priori, and the harvester will be operated at its true maximum power point. A 7-W prototype for testing the proposed algorithm has been built and evaluated. Its performance is favorably compared with the amount of power extracted with the resistive matching technology. The results have been published in [J1]. Two patents have been granted [P1] and [P2]. To further investigate the impact of the modulation technique on the performance of the full-bridge AC/DC converter. A technique that can mitigate leakage current has been studied. It utilizes 1) a virtual ground technique to mitigate ground leakage current, 2) a hybrid pulsewidth modulation (HPWM) scheme to profile the output current and prevent sudden changes in the common-mode voltage, and 3) a nonlinear output inductor to attenuate current ripple around zero crossings and minimize filter size. The HPWM is effectively the same as unipolar PWM (UPWM), but with soft voltage transition modulation introduced around the zero crossings. Apart from low switching losses, the output filter is implemented with a minimum number of components to achieve high attenuation of ripple current. The output current harmonics caused by the nonlinear output inductor is analyzed by the Volterra theory. The technique is evaluated on a 340 W, 380 Vdc/110 V ac, 50 Hz prototype. The results have been published in [J2]. Objective 2 - To investigate into a hybrid energy conversion structure To merge the gap between the low-power output of piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) and the high-power demand of sensors of Internet of Things, researchers recently start to explore PEHs arrays. However, few circuits have been developed to manage the multiple ac inputs from PEHs arrays. A self-powered PEH array interface circuit based on the synchronized switching and discharging to a storage capacitor through an inductor (SSDCI) technique has been developed. The array interface can output a maximum total power greater than the sum of each individual peak power, and achieve a high efficiency when multiple PEHs connect to the SSDCI array circuit. Simulation and experiments are performed to demonstrate the advantages of the SSDCI array interface. The tested results show that the designed SSDCI array circuit achieves an efficiency of 82.3% with three input sources, and allows a gain of up to 300% in terms of maximal output power compared to the full-bridge rectifier. In addition, only the peak detection is utilized for the switching control; therefore, the SSDCI array circuit is realized more easily and with fewer components compared to the existing synchronous electric charge extraction array interfaces. The results have been published in [J3] The research has further extended the work to energy harvesting techniques for IoT applications. Ultrahigh frequency radio-frequency identification (UHF RFID) technology using transducer-integrated antennas provides a cost-effective option for sensing. A novel setup-independent UHF RFID sensing system that can overcome challenges caused by the measurement setup with a priori unknown mutual distance and orientation between the tag and the read/write device (RWD) is proposed. The concept is based on using off-the-shelf radio-frequency identification (RFID) chips having self-tuning capability, which maximizes power transfer coefficient between RFID chip and RFID antenna. An ON-OFF differential (OOD) measurement is implemented to provide setup-independent sensing. The OOD parameters form a 3-D vector that can support more sensing states than prior art using single-dimensional information. Power transfer efficiency (PTE) and tag sensor efficiency (TSE) are defined, where PTE is the minimal power transfer coefficient in all sensing states and TSE is the minimal pairwise Euclidean distance of the OOD parameters. The RFID antenna layout is optimized by optimizing PTE and TSE simultaneously to offer sensing robustness without sacrificing communication performance in all sensing states. A water filling-level sensor has been designed and evaluated. The results have been reported in [J4]. With further enhancement, a multidimensional differential measurement technique for eliminating the effect of the measurement setup, such as unknown mutual distance and orientation between the read/write device (RWD) and sensor tags, and line-of-sight obstruction, on acquiring information from multiple sensor tags simultaneously is proposed. The concept is based on 1) using a channel hopping mechanism to acquire multidimensional data sets and 2) conducting a dissimilarity analysis between offline and online data sets to extract sensor information. The differential measurement, which is activated by the channel hopping mechanism, mitigates the impact of the measurement setup, making the pattern of the multidimensional data sets tightly relate to the sensing state. A sensor tag for measuring the water-filling level of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipes is fabricated. Experiments show that the proposed method can accurately acquire information from three sensor tags simultaneously under different measurement setups. The performances using data sets of different dimensions are compared. The technology has been published in [J5]. References: [J1] K. Tse and H. 11205418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205418.value: A further research can be done for three-dimensional energy harvesting generator. In order to increase the power area density in a confined space with three-dimensional EHG structures and improve the bandwidth, multiple EHGs are connected in series and/or parallel. An ideal operation is that the maximal power harvested from the array of EHGs is equal to the sum of the maximum powers of individual EHG. Apart from having different output impedances, the key challenge is also that each EHG might practically be excited with different amplitudes and frequencies. An equivalent model can be derived to represent the entire circuit and study the interaction of the proposed architecture to the dynamics of the mechanical subsystems and the total output power. The idea can be extended from Ref [J3].

11205418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205418.value: Recent advances in semiconductor technology and material sciences have reduced the power consumption of modern microelectronic circuits and systems, such as Internet-of-Things and machine-to-machine devices. They have also advanced the efficiency of energy harvesting generators (EHGs), such as solar cells, thermoelectric, piezoelectric, electromagnetic, and electrostatic generators, in converting ambient energy into electricity. The goal of energy harvesting is to replace batteries or extend the recharge intervals of batteries. Among various ambient energy sources, vibration energy harvesting owns the merits of being stable, clean, high power density, and compatibility with microfabrication. However, less emphasis is placed on eliminating the effect of the output reactance of the EHG for maximizing power delivery. Thus, the EHG is not always operated at the true maximum power point (TMPP). Such an issue becomes more apparent if the EHG has large output reactance and is subject to a wide variation in the vibration frequency. This project aims to investigate an architecture for the AC/DC converter that can keep operating the EHG at the TMPP. Such architecture also allows to convert energy from an array of EHGs and has each EHG operated at its TMPP.

11205518.label: Realisation of objectives
11205518.value: The objectives of the proposal have been realized. A model to simulate multi-physics coupling between hot air and glass facades has been established and a constitutive model which incorporates the thermal-mechanical (TM) fracture behavior of glass panes has been developed. The overall process of the TM behavior of double skin facades (DSFs) in a fire can be divided into two dynamic stages: The first stage is the direct flame radiation and heat transfer by convection. The second stage is the crack initiation and damage processes of glass panels. In the first stage, several parameters, such as the cavity size in the DSFs and heat release rate, were included. The model of thermal degradation of DSFs under fire conditions was developed by calculating the temperature distribution patterns in the cavity and on both interior and exterior glass. Moreover, the venetian blinds which can affect the temperature distribution on the glass facade through changing hot air flow have also been considered. In the second stage, a simplified thermal-strain transformation technique was proposed to characterize the thermal loading induced by a temperature field. Crack evolution can be predicted using only temperature distributions and multiple cracks distributed in any arbitrary space in the glass panes can be simultaneously predicted. To predict the hot air–glass interaction performance of a DSFs system, a constitutive model was built. The nonlinear multi-physics and fracture characteristics of DSFs were represented and assessed by energy release rates and stress intensity factors. The stress state near the tip of a crack is considered through the stress intensity factor in the development of constitutive relations. A computational framework for the TM performance of DSFs systems during fires has been built. A meshfree method has been applied to solve the problems with an emphasis on the hot air flow and temperature variation during thermal degradation of DSFs under fire conditions. The goal of using a meshfree method is to be better suited to hot air glass interaction problems that involve changing boundaries and large deformations and finally improve the accuracy and efficiency of the simulation. The results obtained using the numerical model and in the experiments are compared well at specific locations, demonstrating the numerical model is capable of predicting the thermal behavior of a fire-exposed DSF. After the meshfree simulation was validated, empirical equations were derived to describe the relationships between the temperature over time and the location variables along the interior and exterior glass panes. The capability of predicting the temperatures in the interior and exterior panes of a DSFs of the empirical equations is clearly demonstrated, through the comparisons of the temperature predictions obtained by the numerical model and these empirical equations at various points. The analysis indicated that the temperature variation in the DSFs depended on the location of the required point relative to the inclined hot air flow. Finally, by incorporating the proposed mathematical model, which calculates the exact deformation of the mesh elements, into the variational phase-field model, the crack evolution can be predicted using only temperature distributions. Numerical experiments have been performed on the thermal behavior of glass facades and heat flux patterns in facade cavities during fires. Heat map plots were generated for the fire room and DSFs cavity at each time step. The heat maps comprehensively illustrate the temperature distributions in the entire configuration, whereas experimental results were only obtained at certain locations. The results obtained using the numerical model and in the actual experiments at specific observation points compared well, demonstrating that the numerical model can predict the thermal behavior of a fire exposed DSFs. Furthermore, some cases with physical methods that can affect hot air flow have been simulated. Venetian blinds can also act as a barrier to prevent the spread of flames and smoke, besides the traditional function of regulating light and air. If the blinds are made of fire-resistant material and properly installed, they can provide an additional layer of protection against the heat and flames. Thus, the validated numerical model was utilized to predict the thermal behavior of a DSFs with venetian blinds under fire exposure conditions. Both the temperature contour plots and the temperature variations at observation points over time for different tilt angles can be generated by the proposed numerical approach easily. Some conclusions of heat flux patterns with the effect of venetian blinds can be summarized based on the analysis. For example, when the tilt angle was 90 °, the temperature of the interior glass was much higher than the temperature of the exterior glass. The probability of the fire jumping and spreading into upper compartments was higher for the interior glass panes because of the breakage due to excessive heating, but not for the exterior glass pane as they were covered by blinds. When the tilt angle was below 30 °, the flow of hot air particles to the upper parts of the DSFs was impeded when the blinds were horizontal or near horizontal. The effects of the venetian blinds on the temperature distribution in the DSFs were lower when the tilt angle was between 45 ° and 60 °. The temperature variation in this tilt angle range approached that in the DSF without venetian blinds because the angle of the hot air flow almost matched the blind tilt angle. This research has led to 3 high-quality research papers published in refereed international journals, 1 conference paper, and trained 1 PhD student.

11205518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205518.value: In this work, an effective numerical framework was proposed for simulating the thermal-mechanical performance of DSFs under fire. The numerical model was validated by comparing the predicted response parameters in a fire exposed DSF system with those measured in fire experiments. Then the validated numerical model was employed to derive empirical equations linking temperature with both the time and location along the interior and exterior glass panes of DSFs. The analysis indicated that the temperature variation in the DSF depended on the location of the required point relative to the inclined hot air flow. Additionally, numerical simulations were conducted for the same DSF configuration but equipped with venetian blinds in order to examine the influence of the blinds on the fire performance of glass DSFs. The simulation results clearly indicated that the “blind tilt angle” can significantly affect the fire spread characteristics and temperature distribution in DSFs. Finally, a simplified thermal-strain transformation technique was proposed to characterize the thermal loading induced by a temperature field. Then we successfully integrated the thermomechanical loading directly into the phase-field model. The proposed model can simultaneously predict multiple cracks distributed in any arbitrary space in the glass panes more realistically than the previous numerical models, regardless of glass pane type and size, fixation method, and thermal loading variation. The study can provide valuable theoretical references in the design of DSF systems for high-rise buildings and significantly improve the fire safety of DSFs. The points mentioned above are the major findings and research outcome of this project.

11205518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205518.value: Further studies on the thermal performance of DSFs and other glass facade structures under fire conditions will benefit from the numerical framework proposed in this work. A numerical framework based on SPH has been validated using experimental data. The validated framework will be applied to predict the temperature distributions in the various configuration. In the later work, different heat release rates, fire locations and DSF geometries will be considered in the simulation. The relevant empirical equations will be derived to satisfy practical engineering needs. At present, the application of empirical equations is limited by variations of specific conditions. This limitation will be broken with the expansion of the empirical equations. In addition, more abundant physical ways to prevent the spread of flame in glass facade structures will also be studied considering related parameters. Through deeper comprehension of the thermal behavior of DSFs in fires, it is anticipated that more practical, inventive, and secure glass facade systems can be created and applied in the modern construction industry.

11205518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205518.value: We have developed a novel computational framework to study the thermal behavior of double skin facades (DSFs) in fires. The accuracy was verified using experimental data. It is worth noting that the simulation developed in this work can provide a whole picture of temperature distribution in the entire configuration, whereas experimental results can only be obtained at certain locations. Then the empirical equations were derived, which link temperature with both the time and location. The empirical equations presented the temperature in interior and exterior glass panes of DSFs and can be easily applied to meet practical engineering needs. Additionally, the DSFs equipped with venetian blinds are considered and the influence of the “blind tilt angle” on the fire performance of double skin facades is examined. Finally, multiple cracks distributed in any arbitrary space in the glass panes can be simultaneously predicted more realistically than the previous numerical models. The study can provide valuable references for the design of DSF systems and significantly improve their fire safety. The development of relevant standards in the field of glass facades can also benefit from this research.

11207718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207718.value: 随着在农业、侦察和运输方面的应用潜力被挖掘，小型、人性化的微型飞行器受到了科学家和工程师们的极大关注。 这些小型机器人（也被称作无人机）有可能彻底改变我们对民用机器人的使用方式。 然而，与传统飞机相比，当小型飞行器的尺寸降低到厘米尺度上时，他们的空气动力学效率会显着降低。 停留在空中的高能量损耗严重限制了这些微型飞行器的续航能力。 在一些常见平台中，旋翼飞行器（例如四旋翼飞行器）由于其简单的设计和悬停能力而变得流行。 不仅机动性极强，这些飞行器还能依靠直接推进力在没有机翼的情况下保持空中悬停。 但是，相较于具有大面积的空气动力学表面的固定翼飞机，旋翼飞行器在空气动力学效率和飞行续航力方面要逊色不少。 虽然现在科学家已经发明出具有旋翼固定翼双飞行模式的混合飞行器，但是这种飞行器仅在向前飞行时，固定翼才产生飞行升力。 在此研究中，我们将展示一个简单的被动变形机制，此机制可以用来实现一类新的可变形飞行器，对于悬停和向前飞行，此种飞行器的能量使用效率都很高。这项研究将分三个阶段来解决这种飞行器的飞行续航力和功能问题。首先，要制造一个能够在两种飞行模式下（悬停，向前飞行）高效飞行的飞行器，我们的灵感来自有翅​​膀的胞果 – 翅果的自转飞行和昆虫中发现的自动俯仰角旋转。在我们的飞行器设计中，我们采用弯曲铰链允许翼型根据空气动力载荷智能地调整其迎角。变形机制使机翼能够在悬停中产生升力（通过旋转），而无需额外的推进力，至此，固定翼可以在悬停和向前飞行两种飞行模式中均产生升力。第二，通过研究悬停状态下飞行器的空气动力和飞行动力学旋转框架，可以设计和制造出能够保证被动姿态稳定性的厘米级机器人，从而简化对主动控制的要求。类似的策略也可以适用于执行向前飞行的飞行器。最后，我们想要展示我们新式飞行器的悬停和向前飞行。在悬停中，要展示位置控制的成果，我们需要一个时变信号来干扰径向对称的标准悬停轨迹来观察飞行器行为。对于向前飞行，我们必须处理高度，俯仰方向的力和纵向动力之间的耦合关系。 可以想象，拟议的研究将通过扩展微型飞行器的飞行时间和功能来促进微型飞行器领域的进步。 该项目有会扩大飞行器的应用范围的潜力。 此研究的科学价值有：（i）能够被动变形的飞行器的设计和相应的航空力学模型的发展; （ii）分析固定翼旋转时悬停飞行的动力学框架和稳定性研究; （iii）实现可以双模型飞行的高能效飞行器。

11207718.label: Realisation of objectives
11207718.value: 1. Characterize and optimize the lift and drag coefficients of a combined hinge-wing system capable of bi-directional camber for a robot that can perform hovering and forward flight. The first objective can be regarded as the aerodynamics and flight dynamics "identification" problem. The aerodynamic properties of the winged seed-inspired aircraft differ from conventional aircraft due to the relatively low Reynolds numbers. While there exist some similarities with flapping wings at intermediate Reynolds numbers, the absence of wing reversal means there is no added mass and wake capture. In order to obtain wings with high efficiency (as measured by power loading or power factor), we must determine the relevant lift and drag coefficients to optimize the wing shape using experimental data. The aerodynamic study was carried out using a benchtop setup as detailed in [1]. We fabricated six wings with different shape parameters under the range of relevant aspect ratios (1 to 6) and span (less than 30 cm). The wings were tested by spinning at different wing pitch angles, corresponding to several angles of attack. The results are consolidated. We obtain a single set of angle-of-attack-dependent lift and drag coefficients. From these empirically fitted models, we can predict the lift produced by the wing as well as the torque and mechanical power required. Furthermore, to ensure that the designed and fabricated wings are compatible with both hovering (revolving) and forward (translational) flights, we decided to simplify the problem of creating bi-directional wings to designing a passive revolute joint that allows the wings to rotate depending on the operating condition. As demonstrated in [3] and below (2nd objective), the vehicle with hinged wings can operate in both revolving and translational modes. 2. Analyze, design, and manufacture the robot capable of both rotating hovering flight and forward flight. This objective follows naturally from the first objective. After the wings are optimized for both operational modes (revolving and translating), we must incorporate them to construct a flight-capable vehicle. In this task, the challenges lie not only in the differences in aerodynamic forces produced by the wings in different modes but more critically in the stability of the vehicle. This is because the centers of mass and aerodynamic pressure shift with the modes of operation. To elaborate, in the revolving-wing mode, the vehicle is stable when the center of pressure on each wing is above the center of mass, and the wing retains the desired configuration when the center of pressure is behind the revolute joint axis. In the forward flight mode, it is more complicated. The pitch stability is generally achieved if a tail is present. The wing sweep angle is also critical to pitch controllability (generation of pitch torque) as it determines the relative location between the center of pressure and the center of mass. Furthermore, to yield roll stability, two wings should be arranged with a dihedral angle. This problem is solved in two steps as described in [2] and [3]. In [2], we showed that to generate pitch torque for controllability without incorporating an extra actuator, we allow the wings to sweep back and force passively, depending on the rotor thrust on the wings. As a result, the robot can effectively manipulate its pitch torque in forward flight through the propelling thrust directly. Second, to allow the wing to rotate about its leading edge to be compatible with both translational and revolving flights, another passive joint is incorporated as shown in [3]. In this setting, the robot does not need an extra actuator for the transformation, and the wing stays in the desired position as it is subject to aerodynamic load and the rotor thrust. That is, both positions are stable after taking into consideration all external torque. Therefore, to allow the wing to switch and the robot to change the mode of operation, it must undergo a maneuver that pushes the wing out of a regular flight envelope. To switch from forward to revolving flight, the robot pitches up and slows down. The changing aerodynamic load induces the wing to rotate, and the robot enters the revolving flight mode. Similarly, from the revolving condition, if the rotor thrust is reduced and the robot descends, the change in the aerodynamic load leads to the desired wing rotation. 3. Develop a control strategy for hovering and forward flight. Demonstrate controlled hovering and forward flight. The outcomes from the previous objectives suggest that the hybrid vehicle can be designed to be passively stable in both revolving and forward flight. This is not only beneficial but critical to the operation of the robot because the degree of actuation of the robot is rather limited as it only has two actuators. Therefore, mechanical design plays a crucial role in the maneuverability of the robot as it is severely underactuated. In the revolving-wing mode, the robot relies primarily on the inherent attitude stability to stay upright. The stability is partially a result of the gyroscopic effect. To travel laterally, the robot directly generates a horizontal force component on a cycle-average basis, leveraging the horziontallly directed propellers. Hence, this is a different mechanism from a regular rotorcraft. For the forward flight, the robot uses the incoming air to generate lift via wings, similar to a conventional fixed-wing aircraft. The air drag is compensated for by two motorized propellers. The roll and yaw control are coupled and can be obtained by the differential thrust between the two rotors on the left and right sides of the fuselage. Without active control surfaces, the pitch dynamics is coupled with the longitudinal dynamics. The robot accelerates to pitch up or decelerates to dive down. The maneuvers are assisted by the fact that the vehicle is inherently stable, thanks to the placement of the center of pressure with respect to the center of mass. [1] Bai, Songnan, Qingning He, and Pakpong Chirarattananon. "A bioinspired revolving-wing drone with passive attitude stability and efficient hovering flight." Science Robotics 7.66 (2022): eabg5913. [2] Bai, Songnan, Runze Ding, and Pakpong Chirarattananon. "A Micro Aircraft with Passive Variable-Sweep Wings." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 7.2 (2022): 4016-4023. [3] Bai, Songnan 2022, ‘Aerodynamics, Dynamics, Control and Application of Revolving Aerial Robots’, PhD thesis, City University of Hong Kong.

11207718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207718.value: In short, we developed a micro aircraft that is capable of hovering efficiently. Imitating the flight principles of samaras, the superior aerodynamic efficiency is obtained by the use of oversized rotating wings which substantially reduces the wing loading. The revolving flight is also advantageous to the flight stability as the large and constantly moving aerodynamic surfaces create torque and force when the robot rotates and translates. The results outlined above were preliminarily published as a conference paper in 2019 IEEE IROS---an internationally recognized robotics conference. The main results was published in Science Robotics (a top journal in the subject category of robotics). During the project, we have trained a few PhD students, with one student taking the main responsibility. The student successfully completed his degree in September 2022. He won an Outstanding Research Thesis Award 2022, which is offered by the Chow Yei Ching School of Graduate Studies in recognition of research students who have produced a thesis of outstanding quality and achievement in their relevant research area. In addition to the mentioned outputs, the second phase of research has been detailed in the dissertation, with some results partially published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (2022).

11207718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207718.value: The revolving-wing platform demonstrates exceptional hovering efficiency compared to other similarly weighted aerial robots. This is a consequence of the large wings (low wing loading). From our feasiblity analysis, if the photovotaic cells with ~20-25% power conversion efficiency are incorporated onto the wing surface, it is possible for the robot to sustain flght under the light intensity of one Sun. If this is realized, the product would contend as the smallest electric vehicle capable of sustained solar-powered flight. To folow up on this, we have discussed with potential collaborators on the development of lightweight and high efficiency solar cells. We expect to submit a proposal for RGC Collaborative Research Fund or other research schemes in the coming months.

11207718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207718.value: In this research, we have developed a novel subclass of micro aerial vehicles. Inspired by maple seeds, we transform the underpinning mechanism of efficient autorotating (gliding) flight of winged seeds to a powered revolving-wing vehicle. This robot is twice as efficient as multirotor vehicles with similar weights. This is thanks to the bio-inspired design that allows the robot to be efficient in both aerodynamic and actuation aspects. As a result, the 35-gram robot is able to fly for almost 15 minutes. The robot is also passively stable, dispensing the need for fast attitude feedback in order to stay aloft. Position control is also achieved despite the robot possessing only two actuators. Beyond that, we equip the robot with an ability to transform and realize forward flight in a configuration of a fixed-wing aircraft. This is accommpished by introducing a rotational joint, allowing one wing to rotate and reverse its wing pitch angle. The robot becomes highly efficient regardless whether it is hovering in place or traveling long distance.

11207818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207818.value: Effective collision avoidance technology that is robust to sensor noise and is scalable to large systems is essential for enabling a large number of robots to collaborate efficiently in cluttered and changing environments, with applications in automated warehouses, self-driving cars, and service robots within the close-proximity of humans. However, existing multi-agent navigation techniques have important limitations. Centralized approaches can generate optimal navigation policies but are disadvantageous in scalability, flexibility, and robustness. Decentralized systems claim to be scalable, but unfortunately, most of them are not fully-decentralized, but rather need additional channels such as WIFI communications to share global knowledge among agents. More importantly, their performance measured by navigation speed and quality is significantly lower than their centralized counterparts. In this project, we will show how a novel end-to-end deep learning framework can generate fully-decentralized and near-optimal navigation policies for large-scale robot systems. Our method is among first few working systems that accomplish fully-distributed navigation applicable to large-scale physical robot systems with hundreds of robots without any inter-agent knowledge sharing. More importantly, our approach greatly reduces the performance gap between decentralized and centralized navigation policies, making our method competitive for high-throughput industrial applications. This research includes two parts. First, to learn a fully-decentralized policy, we formulate each agent's end-to-end navigation strategy as a deep neural network mapping from noisy sensor observation to the agent's steering commands. The policy network is trained in a supervised manner over a large set of navigation data. The learned policy is able to generate reliable navigation behaviors that generalize well in various scenarios. Second, to push the performance of the learned decentralized policy towards the limit of centralized approaches, we refine the learned policy using a multi-scenario multi-stage training framework which exploits a reinforcement learning algorithm based on robust policy gradient. The computed optimal policy is able to outperform the original policy in both navigation speed and quality. It is perceivable that the proposed research will contribute to advances in multi-agent navigation by combining the advantages of fully-decentralized methods in scalability and centralized methods in optimality. The project would transform how robot teams are used in industrial applications. Scientific merits will come from: (i) the development of robust fully-distributed multi-agent systems; (ii) the research into the near-optimal decentralized navigation policy via deep reinforcement learning; (iii) the realization of fully-distributed and near-optimal multi-agent control principles on practical robotic systems with more than 10 physical robots and more than 100 simulated agents. 大規模機器人在擁擠和動態場景中的合作需要高效的機器人避障技術，該技術在自動倉儲、自動駕駛和服務機器人中都有重要的應用。 現有的多機器人導航和避障技術有諸多局限。例如，它們大多是基於全局最優的中心化控制，在系統的可擴展性、靈活性和魯棒性上較差。現有的去中心化系統需要通過通信等機制實現某種程度上的信息交流，因此依然擴展性不佳；同時在機器人運動速度和質量上都顯著低於中心化的系統。 本項目將實現一個新的基於端到端深度學習的框架，以產生一個完全分布式的並接近最優的大規模多機器人的避障和導航策略。我們的方法可以使得數百個機器人在不進行任何相互通信的情況下實現高效的安全的運動，並各自完成不同的任務。通過基於強化學習的優化，學習到的策略的效率和質量接近中心化的策略，但是在靈活性和可擴展性上大為超過。

11207818.label: Realisation of objectives
11207818.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved. For objective 1: we have developed an end-to-end navigation policy using supervised deep learning where the supervision data is collected from a set of different tasks, including holonomic robots, non-holonomic robots, and navigation using various sensors (lidars, cameras, and depth cameras). The trained results can learn navigation policies for holonomic and non-holonomic robots. For objective 2: starting from the learned initial policy from objective 1, we use deep reinforcement learning to learn a high-quality end-to-end navigation policy. The learned policy has much better performance than the supervised learned policy and can easily extend to large-scale robot systems in complex scenes with both dynamic and static obstacles. For objective 3: we have implemented an end-to-end learning framework on more than 10 physical robots in a robotic warehouse. It has been tested on different types of physical robots with different mechanical structures, different shapes, and with different sensors mounted. The system has also been tested in simulation in both 2D (mobile) and 3D (flying) robotic swarms with more than 100 agents. As an extension, our method has also been leveraged in energy control in autonomous trucks and control of a swarm of agents with robotic controllers. All these extensions achieve performance better than state-of-the-art.

Implement the end-to-end learning framework on more than 10 physical robots and more than 100 simulated robots: We will investigate the performance of the learned policies on a set of non-holonomic robots with different dynamics properties, different shapes, and with different sensors mounted.

11207818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207818.value: Major findings: deep reinforcement learning is an ideal tool to achieve fully decentralized and near optimal multi-robot collision avoidance. Thanks to the fully decentralization, our method can scale to swarms of a large number of robots (>1000). Thanks to the collision avoidance capability reinforcement learned via swarm interaction, each robot in the swarm can not only safely avoid all static/dynamic obstacles but also effectively achieve their individual navigation task. We successfully achieved all our planned objectives. Research outputs: We have published 15 journal papers and 8 conference papers, including several top journals in robotics (2 Transactions on Robotics and 1 International Journal on Robotics Research) and top conferences in robotics and machine learning (2 CVPR, 1 ICML, and several ICRA and IROS). The IJRR paper, as one of the first few works about learning-based collision avoidance, has been cited 173 times since its first publication in 2020.

11207818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207818.value: During our conduction of this project, we have found two directions for further development: 1. The reinforcement learned policy is a neural network. It is very difficult for humans to understand and adjust the network’s parameters. As a result, one important research would be how to develop an advanced policy that is Interpretable. One possible solution is using decision tree rather than multi-layer neural networks as the parameterized description of the policy. Once the decision tree is trained, it would be easier for humans to understand the important factors that are accounted for during collision avoidance and can make task-specific adjustments whenever necessary. 2. The reinforcement learned policy lacks guarantees. It is necessary to combine techniques of formal analysis and verification with reinforcement learning to achieve a stack of robust collision avoidance rules that can be verified in simulation and finally safely deployed in the physical world.

11207818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207818.value: In this project, we have used deep reinforcement learning to train a high-quality robotic collision avoidance strategy that can successfully handle challenging scenarios with crowded static and dynamic obstacles. Based on our system, the robot can achieve robust navigation in crowded urban scenarios without a detailed map of the environment and without accurate localization of its location in the scene. This system solves fundamental difficulties in mobile service robots and its prototypes have been deployed in warehouses, airports, canteens, and other urban regions.

11208118.label: Project Objectives
11208118.value: Verify the proposed Doherty power amplifier concept with extended back-off range. This is suitable for high peak-average-power ratio (PAPR) modulated signals used for present and future communication systems such as 5G with a large PAPR. Parameters that limit the performance includes PAPR, efficiency and bandwidth will be studied for the proposed idea. An analytic formulation can then be determined that will allow insight into how to improve performance. To design a broadband Doherty power amplifier with high efficiency for modern wireless communication systems. Its performance should reach the level of state-off-arts in current academic region. Again, parameters that limit the performance will be determined that will allow insight into how to further improve the performance. From previous work, a new configuration is proposed to give an ultra-wide back-off range broadband Doherty power amplifier. This will require an in depth study, to find limitations, optimize, make, improve and verify. The back-off range of the proposed DPA should satisfy a number of scenarios found in 4G (Long term evolution) and the coming 5G wireless system. This would require, Doherty efficiency behaviors over a broad bandwidth.

11208118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208118.value: In the digital era, it would seem that the use of highly inefficient linear amplification would be consigned to the rubbish bin. This would have been true if it wasn’t for the insatiable demand for high data speed, where only the more efficient data modulation formats can satisfy. These more efficient data formats require both linear amplification as well as high efficiency. The requirements in high efficiency, stems from the need for longer battery life in mobile handsets and the reduction of carbon footprint in base station transmitters. There seems to be a never ending proliferation of radio transmitters both indoors and outdoors. Operating costs are also a major factor in the demand for more efficient amplifiers which are the main consumers of electrical power. In the past efficient power amplifiers operating on class C have dictated the modulation format used such as the first generation analogue FM and the second generation GMSK which have a constant signal amplitude. Today and in the future the more efficient modulating signal format now dictates and demands a more efficient power amplifier. As the largest energy consumers in wireless communication systems, the challenge faced by power amplifier (PA) has never been greater. In modern and future systems, the more efficient modulation format signal which has higher peak average power ratio (PAPR) is adopted to give higher data speed. Typical modulation formats comprise of multi-carriers, which requires the PA in base stations to operate with high efficiency from low power to saturation. In the past this could only be achieve using the highly inefficient power amplifiers that biased in class A. The Doherty power amplifier (DPA), due to its additional efficiency peak at lower power, has become the main stream of base station PA design in the past decade. Existing DPAs cannot satisfy the strict requirements of future wireless system (including the low power and bandwidth). In this study, advanced Doherty power amplifiers for 4G/5G wireless communication systems that will meet these future requirements are proposed, studied and optimized. Although the work will centre around future 4G/5G wireless communications systems, the technique used can be applied to any other types of systems. It is envisaged that there be a large improvement in efficiency, translating to a huge reduction in both running costs as well as the carbon footprint. 在數字時代，效率极低的线性放大会被放到歷史的垃圾箱。這將是對的，如果對高數據速度的需求能夠被滿足。然而，只有更高效的数据调制格式能够满足。这些更高效的数据格式既需要线性放大，也需要高效率放大。對於高效率的要求源于手機電池壽命延長的需求和基站發射機碳排放量的減少需求。無論在在戶外還是戶内，无线电发射机的發展似乎永远不会停止。放大器是电力的主要消费者，运行成本也是一個對更高效放大器需求的主要因素。 在過去，工作在C類的高效率功率放大器被用於那些使用恆定信號幅度的調製模式。例如第一代模擬FM調製和二代GMSK調製。在現在與未來，更加高效的信號調製模式已經被制定，這要求更高效的功率放大器。作爲在無綫通信系統中最大的能源消耗組件，功率放大器面臨前所未有的挑戰。在現在和未來的系統中，爲了更高的數據傳輸速率，擁有更高峰均信號功率比的調製信號被使用。傳統的調製模式包含了多載波，這要求基站内的功率放大器從低功率到飽和功率都能維持高效率。在過去，這只能通過使用工作在A類的低效率功率放大器來實現。Doherty功率放大器，得益于它在低功率的額外效率峰值，已經在過去十年成為基站功率放大器的主流設計。然而，現存的Doherty功率放大器難以滿足未來無限系統的苛刻要求（包括更寬的回退區間和帶寬） 在這項研究裏，滿足未來要求的用於4G/5G無綫通信系統的先進Doherty功率放大器被提出，研究和優化。儘管這項研究以未來4G/5G無綫通信系統為中心，這些技術同樣可以應用到其他類型的系統。按照設想，將會帶來巨大的效率改進，同時降低運營成本和碳排放量。

11208218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208218.value: 目前全世界約有2億8千5百萬人患有視覺損傷，其中3千9百萬為失明，而老年黃斑退化所導致的失明大約有2百萬人（世界衛生組織，2010年）。視網膜色素變性是另一類引發進行性視覺退化的眼疾，而在歐美大約3500人中便有1例此類患者。近幾十年來，仿生視覺系統被用來替代失明患者，尤其是老年黃斑退化或視網膜色素變性患者的自然視覺系統。這種仿生視覺系統使用電脈衝來刺激視網膜或視皮層，以期恢復患者的部分視覺功能。其中，視網膜仿生視覺系統已經被證明可以提高患者的生活質量。長期使用這種仿生視覺系統將會不可避免地對大腦產生影響，但是這方面的研究卻為數不多。 對視網膜進行電刺激會對視覺和非視覺等不同的腦區產生調製作用。在優配研究金的資助下（2011/12, CityU123412），我們已經研究了電刺激視網膜後，視皮層神經元的空間相互作用。而尚未探索而又很有意義的問題是，在長期使用視覺假體對視網膜進行電刺激的情況下，視覺和非視覺腦區所發生的調製變化。 本課題中，我們提出了一個新穎的研究方向，即利用跨角膜電刺激研究長期刺激視網膜的效果。第一批的預實驗結果顯示，使用其中一組刺激參數可以同時激活視覺和非視覺腦區。第二批的預實驗結果顯示，視網膜退化的動物模型表現出了類似抑鬱的行為活動。為了進一步研究長期電刺激所引發的功能及行為變化，我們提出使用不同範圍的刺激參數進行刺激，然後詳細探究視覺和非視覺腦區的電生理學變化，比如刺激誘發電位及振盪的延時，幅度，分佈以及功率；同時會開展一系列行為學測試。 本研究將不僅有助於了解在健康和視覺受損人群中，不同腦區間信息的處理和傳遞過程，而且可以從全腦角度揭示長期對視網膜進行電刺激的效果及行為學作用。本課題將會對長期使用仿生視覺系統的最優刺激參數提出深入見解，從而對下一代視覺假體的研發做出貢獻。

11208218.label: Realisation of objectives
11208218.value: Summary - The three objectives have been achieved successfully. Not only have we characterized the TES evoked potentials in visual and non-visual regions, we also investigated the TES-induced cortical excitation under different brain states. For the stimulation types, we have investigated stimulation frequencies and stimulation pulse durations. As for the behavioral outcomes, we studied the depressant-like behaviors in S334ter-line-3 rats, and investigated the antidepressant-like effect of the application of TES in a rat model of retinal degeneration and a rat model of chronic unpredictable stress. Results of Objectives 1 and 2 are reported in three international conference meetings and published in three journal papers. A summary is given below. To characterize electrical evoked responses in the primary visual cortex we first stimulated the right eye of rd10 mice with 19 biphasic current amplitudes (10 μA – 1000 μA) at varying stimulation frequencies (2 Hz, 10 Hz and 20 Hz) and simultaneously analyzed EEPs in both the contralateral (left) and ipsilateral (right) regions of the primary visual cortex (Vcx). For the electrical evoked response experiments, the EEP in the contralateral Vcx was several times higher than the EEP in the ipsilateral Vcx. Specifically, in contralateral Vcx, current amplitudes of 400 μA, 500 μA and 600 μA elicited an effective response amplitude of 50%, 70% and 85% respectively across all applied stimulation frequencies compared to the EEP in the ipsilateral Vcx that did not saturate with increasing current amplitude. Next, to investigate cortical neural excitation responses in awake and anesthetized brain states of rd10 mice under varying stimulation frequencies, we subjected the rd10 mice to pTES (5-7 days) and then recorded resting state ECoG activity in the prefrontal cortex and primary visual cortex after the stimulation at frequencies of 2 Hz, 10 Hz and 20 Hz. We computed the absolute power and coherence of the resting state ECoG activity in the contralateral Vcx and contralateral PFx under awake and anesthetized brain states respectively and compared the results with those obtained in sham control rd10 mice. For the resting-state experiments under varying stimulation frequencies and brain states, contralateral Vcx of awake rd10 mice displayed significantly increased absolute power of theta, alpha and beta oscillations following 10 Hz stimulation compared with sham matched controls. Under the anesthetized brain state the absolute power of medium-, high-, and ultra-high gamma oscillations in the contra PFx, at 2 Hz stimulation, was higher than in the sham controls. Further to this, increased ultra-high gamma band coherence between contra Vcx and contra PFx was observed in rd10 mice stimulated at 10 Hz and 20 Hz frequencies compared with sham matched controls. From this experiment, our findings clearly demonstrate that in RD mice, pTES alters patterns of neural oscillations in the brain circuitry under different brain consciousness states in a frequency and brain state-dependent manner. Furthermore, we learnt that RD mice brain is more responsive to the effects of pTES in the awake state compared to the anesthetized states possibly owing to anesthesia interference. In summary, this experiment provides a starting point to investigate the sustained effect of the prolonged retinal electrical stimulation on brain neural activities. Results of Objective 3 are published in one well-recognized journal in the field of neuromodulation (i.e. Brain Stimulation). A summary is given below. Following neuromodulation of ECoG responses under varying frequencies and pulse durations of pTES in visual and non-visual brain regions, we next aimed to investigate neuromodulatory impact of pTES current amplitudes on behavior outcomes in retinal degeneration animal model. Ten-week-old male S334ter-line-3 rats and Long Evans (LE) rats were used as the retinal degeneration model and healthy controls, respectively. The rats were obtained from the Laboratory Animal Services Centre of the Chinese University of Hong Kong. S334terline- 3 rats were bred from transgenic homozygotes and pigmented LE rats. S334ter-line-3 rats (TES 100 mA, n = 6; TES 200 mA, n = 8; TES 500 mA, n = 6; and sham, n = 12) and LE control rats (TES 100 mA, n = 8; TES 200 mA, n = 6; TES 500 mA, n = 6; and sham, n = 11) received daily TES or sham treatment for 1 week before behavioral assessments. Anxiety-like behaviors were assessed by cylinder exploration, open field, and home cage emergence tests, whereas behavioral despair was assessed by the forced swim test. Our results showed that TES induced antidepressant-like behaviors in S334ter-line-3 rats. The S334ter-line-3 rats exhibited elevated anxiety levels, as demonstrated in the cylinder test, OFT, and HCET. There were no significant differences in the forced swim immobility time between the sham-treated S334terline-3 and control rats, which suggests the retinal degeneration model did not exhibit increased despair compared to control rats. In S334ter-line-3 rats, TES significantly ameliorated anxiety-like behaviors as indicated by the cylinder test, OFT, and HCET. Surprisingly, despite the lack of despair-like behavior in the sham-treated S334ter-line-3 rats, TES at 100 and 200 mA significantly decreased immobility time in the FST, implying an anti-despair-like effect of TES. In the control rats, TES did not generally lead to pronounced behavioral changes, except TES at 100 mA, which increased rearing in the cylinder test and decreased the distance traveled in the OFT. Overall, the effects of TES on control rats were inconclusive, as TES at 200 and 500 uA. Comparing the effects of different stimulation amplitudes, we found that TES at 100 and 200 mA elicited the most profound anxiolytic effects in S334ter-line-3 rats in all behavioral tests, whereas TES at 500 mA failed to induce significant improvements in the OFT and FST. These findings are in agreement with a study investigating the optimal neuroprotective parameters of TES [11], which showed repeated administration of 30e60 min of TES at 100 or 200 mA amplitude, 1 or 2 ms pulse width, and 20 Hz frequency induced the most beneficial effects by enhancing the survival of axotomized retinal ganglion cells in rats. Together with their findings, our current study suggested that TES at a moderate intensity of 100 or 200 mA was optimal for relieving ophthalmological or mental disorders in rats.

11208218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208218.value: In the present study, retinal degeneration 10 (rd10) mice were used as animal models for the human RP disease. Silver wire of diameter 0.4 mm, surface area 0.13 mm^2 and impedance 0.143 ± 0.014 kΩ (in 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline) was used as the stimulating electrode to stimulate the right corneal surface of the rd10 mice via a non-invasive method called prolonged transcorneal electrical stimulation (pTES). Subsequently electrocorticography (ECoG) was employed to record resting state or spontaneous neural signals from the non-visual (prefrontal cortex) and visual (primary visual cortex) regions in both hemispheres of the brain (left hemisphere or contralateral region and right hemisphere or ipsilateral region). In summary, from all the results reported in the aforementioned experiments of the present study, the following conclusions are suggested. Firstly, the awake brain is more responsive to the effects of pTES. Secondly, a short pulse pTES is necessary to enhance narrow band and broad band gamma oscillations which have previously been reported to play key roles in cortical excitatory and inhibitory responses. Thirdly, pTES causes sustained neuromodulatory effects in both the visual region and the non-visual brain region by altering electrophysiological cognitive indices such as functional and directional connectivity measures depending on the parameters of stimulation current amplitude. Fourthly, in S334ter-line-3 rats, TES induced anxiolytic and antidepressant-like behaviors in the cylinder, open field, home cage emergence, and forced swim tests. These behavioural findings suggest a possible neuroplasticity mechanism of the antidepressant-like effects of TES. Overall, we have completed all objectives of this study and published in three journals (Frontiers in Neuroscience, Frontiers in Cellular Neuroscience, HKIE Transactions), three international conferences (9th International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering, 42nd Annual International Conferences of the IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc, and 43rd Annual International Conferences of the IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc), and one review paper (Cells). The analysis of the ECoG responses and local field potentials also yields three other journal publications (IEEE Transactions in Biomedical Engineering, Cerebral Cortex) and one conference proceeding (43rd Annual International Conferences of the IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc).

11208218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208218.value: There are some limitations in the present study, so below we suggested some possible directions for the future work. As an alternative to screw electrodes used in the present study, flexible microelectrode arrays (MEAs) could also be used to capture ECoG activity across an entire population of neurons in more cortical regions beyond the pre-frontal cortex and primary visual cortex. Furthermore, MEAs offer higher spatial resolution and precision of the recorded signal and the unique characteristics of a neural network could be studied via recording neural signals with MEAs. It will also be interesting to go beyond the cortex and explore the effect (if any) of the non-invasive pTES on the neural activities in sub-cortical regions and deep brain structures such as the thalamus, hippocampus and amygdala. In this regard, the possible mechanism of pTES-triggered alteration in neural activities could also be studied by neural tracing. Neural tracing uses the principle of light microscopy with digital-based software to map neural circuits to delineate the neural mechanisms involved in biological systems.

11208218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208218.value: The number of people of all ages around the world with visual impairment is estimated to be 285 million, of whom 39 million are all blind. The cause of global blindness includes Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) where around 2 million are affected (WHO 2010). Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) is another group of eye disorders that cause progressive vision loss, and is estimated to affect 1 in 3,500 people in the United States and Europe. In recent decades, bionic vision system is being developed for use as a substitute for natural vision in blind patients with AMD/RP, where electrical pulses are applied to the retina or the cerebral cortex to restore partial vision to the implant recipients. Bionic vision devices using the retinal approach have proved to provide some improvements to their vision-related life. The long-term use of these devices using both retinal approach and non-retinal approach will inevitably induce modulation to the brain circuitry that is sparsely studied. The present study has systematically characterized the fabricated and characterized the transcorneal electrical stimulation (TES) evoked potentials in visual and non-visual regions by using different stimulation types commonly used in retinal prostheses in awake and anesthetized brain states. This study also reported that animal model with retinal degeneration exhibited depressive-like behaviours. Under electrical stimulation of the corneal region, TES induced antidepressant-like behaviors in retinal degeneration rats.

11208918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208918.value: 目前針對空調系統的優化方法基本都屬於一類基於時間觸發的優化策略,即採用固定頻率的優化機制。 為應對人類日益複雜的功能需求(熱舒適、空氣品質、智慧化、高能效等),空調系統的結構和運行都變得越來越複雜,運行過程中狀態變化的隨機特性或者非規律性顯著增強。 無論在機理還是在應用實踐中,基於時間觸發的優化策略都不能在線上計算量和優化效率之間取得滿意的平衡。 因此,考慮到空調系統的運行本身具有事件驅動的特性,本專案擬針對複雜空調系統,系統地分析其運行特性,從基於事件驅動的視角出發,探索一類新的優化機制來解決目前廣泛使用的基於時間觸發的優化策略所遇到的挑戰。 新的基於事件驅動的優化機制將能夠實現在恰當的時間,執行恰當的優化動作,從而有效應對複雜空調系統中的隨機或者非規律性變化,更好地平衡線上計算量和優化效率。 本專案將為針對複雜空調系統的基於事件驅動的線上優化策略的應用、推廣奠定理論和技術基礎。

11208918.label: Realisation of objectives
11208918.value: (1) Develop a systematic method to define events for the optimal control of central air-conditioning systems The objective was achieved. A systematic method was developed to define events for the optimal control of central air-conditioning systems. In this method, a simulation platform using TRNSYS and MATLAB for the air-conditioning (AC) system that will be optimized is firstly constructed. This platform will be used to run the time-driven optimal control of the AC system over a period to generate necessary data for identifying critical state transitions that affects the optimal control. Using the operation data, sensitivity analysis techniques will be used to analyze the impact of the state transitions on the variations of decision variables’ optimal values, and thus to find the critical state transitions. Then, the mathematical relationship between the critical state transitions and the decision variables will be formatted using linear regression. The regressed linear model actually shows how the decision variables change when the states of the HVAC system change. An event is defined on the change of the states based on the observation that the optimization of the decision variable should be done when the changes of the states will is significant enough to cause a large change in the decision variables. (2) Develop event-based optimal control algorithms for identified events The objective was achieved. After the events were systematically defined, event-driven optimal control laws were formatted to define the event and action spaces as well as the map between them. This map indicates which decision variables needs to be optimized when an event occur. According to the event-action map, the event-based optimal control algorithm was developed. This algorithm has the function of event detection, which monitors the change of the critical states and judges whether an event occurs. It also has an optimization solver, which uses a nonlinear programming method to find the global optimizers of the HVAC optimization problem. Note that a model-based optimization was adopted in this algorithm, in which a grey-box model was used to describe the relationship between the decision variables (including the set points for the chiller water supply temperature, cooling water return temperature and supply air temperature) and the total power of the HVAC system (fans, chillers, and pumps). The algorithm was coded in MATLAB and tested in the simulation platform for a central air-conditioning system constructed using TRNSYS. (3) Evaluate the merits and demerits of event-driven optimal control by comparison with time-driven optimal control The objective was achieved. Using the simulation platform for central air-conditioning systems, we compared the event-driven optimal control and a time-driven optimal control (every 30 minutes) at different seasons of Hong Kong, including spring, summer and autumn, regarding energy use and computation load. The results indicated that the proposed event-driven optimal control had similar energy saving optional with the time-driven optimal control, but was able to reduce computation time significantly. The reasons behind was analyzed, which were identified as (i) the event-driven optimal control can activate optimization actions at more appropriate time, i.e. to do the optimization at the right time, which help to maintain the energy efficiency from the optimal control; (2) the number of optimization actions was reduced when compared with the time-driven optimal control; (3) at each optimization, the number of decision variables that were optimized was reduced. (4) Identify generic events by applying the developed event definition method to the central air-conditioning systems of typical building types The objective was completely achieved. Different configurations of central air-conditioning systems were investigated, for example a chiller plant of single chiller and cooling tower and a chiller plant of multiple chillers and cooling towers. These configurations are used for different types of buildings. Generic events were identified using these configurations. We found that generic events should be defined according to (i) outdoor wet-bulb temperature change Twb, which mainly affect the energy performance of the cooling tower; (ii) the part-load ratio (PLR) charge, which will affect the energy performance of the chiller and air-handling unit; (iii) the stage-on/off of chillers Numchiller, which will affect the energy performance of the chiller, cooling tower and air-handling unit. In the event definition, the weighting factors (for Twb, PLR and Numchiller) should be adjusted accordingly using operation data. (5) Develop a toolbox with demonstration examples using TRNSYS and MATLAB The objective was achieved. We summarized the systematic method of event definition, the event-driven optimal control algorithm, as well as performance analysis in our publications, providing the theoretical development and application examples for easy understanding of the proposed method, as well as guidelines for development and application. We also illustrated the details in the model development (the gray-box model for central air-conditioning system and the procedure in sensitivity analysis for critical state identification). All these details can help engineers understand the propose strategy and guide them to develop suitable tools for applications. The simulation platform (in TRNSYS) and the optimal control algorithms (in MATLAB) could serve as a toolbox to demonstrate how to develop such event-driven optimal control for HVAC systems. It can be given upon requirement.

11208918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208918.value: The main findings and research outcome of this project are summarized as below: (1) The developed event-driven optimal control can significantly reduce the online computational load of the optimal control of HVAC systems without sacrificing the energy-saving potential brought by real-time optimal control. This finding was demonstrated by a case study. Compared with the operation with no optimization, the event-driven optimal control can reduce 4.2-7.4% energy use, which is comparable to that of the time-driven optimal control (4.4–7.5%). However, the developed event-driven optimal control can achieve a significant computation load reduction, up to 75.9–85.2%, compared with the time-driven optimal control (with a frequency of 30 minutes). Details on the case studies are referred to Journal Paper 1 in Part C. (2) Using the developed systematical method to define events, event/action space and event-action map can be determined in a natural and systematic way. This event-action map indicates that not all the decision variables need to be optimized for a given event, which is much different from previous studies that optimize all decision variables simultaneously. To optimize less decision variables can significantly reduce the searching dimension for optimal solutions, thus benefiting to computational efficiency. For example, in our case studies (detailed in Journal Paper 1 in Part C) we defined two events. When Event 1 occurs, only the set-point for the cooling water supply temperature needs to be optimized; and when Event 2 occurs, only the set-points for the chilled water supply and the supply air temperatures are needs to be optimized. (3) The developed event-driven optimal control has better robustness to model errors when compared with the time-driven optimal control. Due to model errors, an optimization shall not always lead to positive rewards, i.e. to reduce the system power. It may lead to negative rewards, and a negative reward will deteriorate the energy efficiency from the optimal control. The event-driven optimal control can significantly reduce the percentage of negative rewards, which can explain why a fewer optimization actions can achieve similar energy performance of the time-driven optimal control. We also demonstrated this finding using case studies, which shows that in the time-driven optimal control have high percentage of negative rewards (as high as 50% when the model error is around 5%); while the event-driven optimal control can reduce this percentage to below 25%. Details on the case studies are referred to Journal Paper 4 in Part C.

11208918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208918.value: We want to apply the proposed event-driven optimal control to systems with thermal storage. We carried out some preliminary studies (Journal Papers 2-3 in Part C). Future development includes the theoretical development on dynamic optimization (such as dynamic modelling of the HVAC systems with significant thermal storage), event definition, and relevant numerical studies.

11208918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208918.value: Optimal control is used to minimize the energy use of central air-conditioning systems, which always present the largest primary energy consumer in buildings. Conventional optimal control always adopts a periodic mechanism with a fixed frequency to trigger optimization actions. However, it has two major limitations in applications. Firstly, most changes in the operating conditions of central air-conditioning systems are aperiodic, such as changes in weather, load and occupancy conditions, and thus a ?clock? is not an ideal trigger. Secondly, real-time optimal control presents a large-scale mathematic programming (high computational load) challenge in a building energy management system. To address the limitations, we developed a new real-time optimal control paradigm known as event-driven optimal control in this project. This new paradigm defines appropriate events to capture the aperiodic changes in the operating conditions of central air-conditioning systems, which ensures that optimization actions are carried out when and only when required. The outputs of this study includes (1) a systematic method of defining events for the optimal control of central air-conditioning systems and (2) the optimal control algorithms corresponding to each event, which can be used to improve the energy efficiency of central air-conditioning systems and thus enhance building energy performance.

11209118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11209118.value: 關於建築糾紛談判中偏見的研究

11209118.label: Project Objectives
11209118.value: The operating objectives of the project therefore include: i) To conceptualize bias in construction dispute negotiation; ii) To develop a validated bias identification inventory; iii) To examine the potency of bias in construction dispute negotiation; iv) To develop bias minimizing measures for construction dispute negotiation and other resolution processes; and v) To share findings with the construction community. The significance and impact of the project can be illustrated from: i) Policy perspective –The Government has repeatedly pledged to make Hong Kong the hub of dispute resolution services in the region. This vision is founded on the Hong Kong strong tradition of independent judiciary and world-class legal services. This study has the potential of contributing to the formulation of policy (Appendix 4a: Policy Addresses on Dispute Resolution Services in Hong Kong). ii) Academic perspective – Study of bias in construction dispute negotiation is largely an uncharted research area. In addition, the development of a validated bias identification is novel per se. The findings will inform bias minimizing measures as well as dispute resolution process design. iii) Industry perspective – Major disputes are anticipated with the disturbing progress and cost reports on the current 10 mega projects in Hong Kong (Appendix 4b: Ten mega projects in Hong Kong). As such, the Society of Construction Law Hong Kong (SCLHK) that has over 300 members of construction dispute resolution experts has endorsed the importance of the study. The SCLHK has agreed to actively participate in the research (Appendix 3). iv) Education perspective – Dispute resolution is an integral part of construction education at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels. An education plan is included in Appendix 1. In sum, the impact can be identified in a) the bias identification inventory can be used as a self-evaluation instrument to remind professionals issue of bias; b) the findings from the experiment will inform the type of bias that may creep into construction dispute negotiation; c) the findings harvested from Stage 4 will inform design of dispute resolution processes. For example, ways to minimise bias in resolution processes like multi-tiered design and appointment arrangement of third party neutral; and d) the findings can be adapted for training of dispute resolution practitioners.

11209118.value: 在當今的建築項目實施過程中不可避免得會產生糾紛。在二零零一年一月份出版的香港首份建築業檢討“為卓越而建”中，減少在糾紛解決過程中對於資源的浪費被重點提出。這份建築業檢討同時鼓勵使用替代糾紛解決機制來處理建築糾紛。針對這份建築業檢討裡面提出的建議，香港政府已經做出相應的舉措：1）于二零零九年的民事司法制度改革中引進庭前自主調解；2）于二零一一年六月生效的《仲裁條例》（第609 章）中加入調解-仲裁規範：3）倡導加入了審裁的法定使用的《付款保障條例》的實施。在二零零五年的公眾諮詢中得到了積極的響應；4） 最新頒布的《道歉条例》（第631章）旨在保護做出道歉的项目方，防止道歉行為被當做是承认错误的行為。這一舉措被認為可以促進糾紛調解的和解。以上的這些舉措共同說明了一個事實：相當數量的糾紛並不能藉助公認低成本的談判實現和解。偏見被認為是一種妨礙和解的心理學障礙。人類判斷過程中存在偏見並不是一個新鮮的話題。即便是經過專業訓練的法官也不能聲稱他們的判決沒有任何偏見存在。當然也就不能排除建築糾紛解決的從業者身上存在偏見的可能性。偏見在建築糾紛談判中是一個鮮有涉及的研究領域。此研究項目旨在填充這個學術空白。 此項目的主要目標就是研究偏見在建築糾紛談判中的影響。 此項目的研究目標包括： 1） 在建築糾紛談判中將偏見概念化； 2） 設計一個驗證有效的偏見識別量表； 3） 確定在建築糾紛談判中的偏見效力； 4） 為建築糾紛談判以及其他糾紛解決機制提供減少偏見的措施； 5） 與建築界分享研究成果。 以上的五個研究目標可以通過五個階段的工作來實現。在第一階段，偏見將會在建築糾紛談判中被概念化。通過前期分析，與建築糾紛解決專家的核心小組討論，一個概念化的框架將會被提出。不同的偏見種類及其內在聯繫、各自的來源以及表現形式都會在框架中得到體現。在第二階段，偏見概念框架會被進一步設計成為偏見識別量表。這個偏見識別量表對於實現第三階段的目標——檢驗偏見是否存在于建築糾紛談判至關重要。本項目會模擬實際的建築糾紛解決過程進行一個實驗并在其中加入可以誘發偏見的因素。建築糾紛解決的從業者將會被邀請參與實驗。實驗參與者的決策將會被記錄和分析以判斷偏見是否存在。實驗參與者將會被邀請接受後續的採訪。言談分析將會被使用來判斷存在的偏見的種類。在第四階段，依據糾紛解決專家的建議，減少偏見的措施將會被提出。本項目將會以與建築業分享研究成果作為結束。

11209118.label: Realisation of objectives
11209118.value: Objective One: To conceptualize bias in construction dispute negotiation Negotiation studies have largely assumed decision makers to be competent and rational. However, this is far from the reality as decision makers are subject to bias. In these regards, this study posits to conceptualize bias in construction dispute negotiation by proposing a bias framework. Manifestations of bias were operationalized from literatures on effects of biases. Data were then collected from construction professionals on their pattern of behaving these manifestations. With the assistance of a PCFA and with reference to the nature of the bias constructs, a four-factor bias framework was developed. Four types of biases were included in the framework: preconception bias, self-affirmation bias, optimism bias and interest-oriented bias. CHEUNG S.O. and LI K. (2019) “Biases in construction project dispute resolution”, Journal of Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management, Vol. 26(2): 321-348. Objective Two: To develop a validated bias identification inventory Bias is a barrier against dispute resolution. This study developed a time-consistent measurement scale to detect the presence of bias. A longitudinal approach was used for this study in which two rounds of data collection were conducted at a 3-month interval. Measurement statements were developed from behavioural manifestations proposed by theories on bias. The statements were further operationalized. Data were collected from the same group of practitioners in construction dispute resolution. With the two sets of data, a paired t-test was performed. A time consistency of the scale was therefore supported. Using the data collected from the round one survey, a four-factor bias structure was obtained from a PCFA. Both rounds of the survey and all the measurement statements were tested to be reliable. All the longitudinal CFA models had good model fits, and when adding equality constraints on the factor loadings across time, the goodness of fit indexes did not change significantly. The development of the scale offered four categories of bias: preconception bias, self-affirmation bias, optimism bias, and interest-oriented bias. Disputing parties could use the scale to evaluate their propensity to bias. LI K. and CHEUNG S.O. (2019) “Bias Measurement Scale for Repeated Dispute Evaluations”, ASCE Journal of Management in Engineering, 34(4):04018016 Objective Three: To examine the potency of bias in construction dispute negotiation Incomplete contract and ambiguous terms are fertile grounds for opportunistic behaviours, which would damage contracting parties’ relationship and underpin construction project disputes. Third-party neutrals are commonly employed to facilitate the communication between the disputing parties has been found to be instrumental. Moreover, to gain trust from the parties, it is imperative for third-party neutrals to be fair and impartial. This study raises an interesting issue of impartiality. It posited to explore the possibility of third-party neutrals being subject to judgmental biases under the influence of opportunism. A simulation was designed to mimic a construction dispute resolution process where the contractor’s opportunistic behaviours were represented by their claim submissions. Respondents were asked to take the role of third-party neutral to rate their observation of the contractor’ opportunism. It was found that two types of bias -anchoring and confirmation were at work. Anchoring bias describes the tendency of overreliance on the previously received information, whereas confirmation bias demonstrates the biased information collection and interpretation for self-affirmation. Cheung S.O., LI K. and LEVINA B. (2019) “Paradox of bias and impartiality in facilitating construction dispute resolution”, ASCE Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction. Vol. 11(3): 0451907. Disputes are common in construction projects. Efficient dispute resolution avoids wasting enormous valuable resources. However, irrational behaviours are impediments to settlement. Reactive devaluation is a well-recognized psychological barrier to successful dispute settlement. This study conceptualized RD in construction dispute negotiation. Twenty-five possible RD manifestations in CDN were developed from the literature. Through a principal component factor analysis, five taxonomies of RD behaviours in CDN were extracted, namely (1) reluctance to change; (2) doubts about counterpart’s ability; (3) overconfidence; (4) biased information processing; and (5) mistrust toward the counterpart. The potency of RD was validated with confirmatory factor analysis. CHEUNG S.O., LI K. and CHOW O.Y. (2020) “Reactive Devaluation as A Psychological Impediment to Construction Dispute Negotiation”, ASCE Journal of Management in Engineering, Vol. 36(4):04020025 Objective Four: To develop bias minimizing measures for construction dispute negotiation and other resolution processes Successful minimizing bias would enhance sustainable construction dispute management and save valuable resources that would be better deployed for productive uses. Going beyond the conventional approach of obtaining self-reflection of biased behaviours by disputants, this study developed robust bias taxonomies in CDN with three different data sets: i) self-reflection of disputants; ii) self-realization of disputants in a dispute resolution simulation; and iii) observations of dispute resolution third party neutrals. Four major types of biases in CDN were conceptualized and these are preconception, self-affirmation, optimism, and interest oriented. Based on this, this study contributes to dispute resolution practices by suggesting bias minimizing measures respective to the bias conceptualization. Categorically, three groups of bias minimizing measures were proposed: i) strategy-based approach is helpful in dealing with preconception bias and self-affirmation bias; ii) attitude-based approach works to alleviate interest-oriented bias and optimism bias; and iii) process-based approach is suitable for preconception bias and interest oriented bias minimization. Curbing biases would minimize the expenses and costs incurred in the protracted dispute resolution processes. LI K. and Cheung S.O. (2020) “Alleviating bias to enhance sustainable construction dispute management, Journal of Cleaner Production, 249: 119311. LI K., CHEUNG S.O. (2020) “Embracing Debiasing in Mediator’s Tactic of Reality Testing”, ASCE Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction, Vol. 12(1): 04519046. Objective Five: To share findings with the construction community Embedded in a network constellation of multi-stakeholders with various professional backgrounds and differing goals, the construction industry is featured with adversarial relationships and inevitable disputes. Therefore, high quality communication and negotiation among the parties are essential in achieving speedy and less costly dispute resolution. As rational evaluation underpins quality negotiation decisions, are construction disputing parties rational as they assumed? Are there any biases that could possibly prohibit them from making prudent judgement? This study seeks to understand the existence and impact of bias in construction dispute negotiation (CDN). The existence of four types of bias in CDN were discussed: preconception, self-affirmation, optimism and interest-oriented. Three categories of de-biasing strategy were also suggested to support the efficient settlement of construction dispute. Vast resources would be saved and amicable relationship among the collaborating parties could be developed when the impact of bias was curbed. Stepping into the digital era, construction dispute resolution professionals should develop the capabilities needed to harness the benefits of technologies for innovative ways of designing a bias-free dispute resolution mechanism. In addition to the sharing through afore-mentioned journal publications, research findings had also been communicated through the following three conference papers. Li K., Chow O. Y. and Cheung S.O. (2019) “Reactive Devaluation as a barrier against amicable construction dispute settlement”, International Structural Engineering and Construction Society, ISEC-10, Chicago, U.S. 20-25 May 2019.
