11209118.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209118.value: This study has four major findings as research outcome: 1. Construction professionals are not immune to bias Faulty judgements were often observed by professional negotiators. This study found construction professionals are influenced by two notable psychological biases include endowment effect and reactive devaluation. Endowment effect phenomenon captures the irrationality in human judgement when people tend to overvalue the items they own. Another bias in construction dispute negotiation is reactive devaluation, representing an unjustified aversion on the proposals and suggestions raised by the opponents. 2. Four main types of bias in construction dispute negotiation Four types of bias in construction dispute negotiation were identified and validated in this study. First, preconception bias describes the preconception disputing parties form before entering or at the commencement of negotiation. Second, self-affirmation bias under which disputing parties are inclined to confine their information collection scope and pay disproportionate attention to the information that confirms their points and arguments. The third is optimism bias that depicts the emotion and attitudes of the disputing parties during the negotiation process. The fourth is interested-oriented bias, which stems from the human nature of self-serving. 3. The caveats in using third-party neutrals When negotiating parties have difficulty in reaching a mutual agreeable settlement, third-party neutrals are the professionals to facilitate the settling process. To better facilitate the communication, it is essential for the third-party neutrals to gain the trust from both parties by upholding their impartiality and neutrality. This study confirmed the possibility for biases to creep in third party neutrals’ decisions, especially under the influence of opportunistic behaviours of the project participants. When third-party neutrals are under the effects of bias, they are unlikely to have a complete picture of the issues in dispute. 4. How to reduce bias? This study suggested three approaches that could be deployed to mitigate biases in construction dispute negotiations, these are strategy-based, attitude-based and process-based. Strategy-based approach was designed for reducing preconception bias and self-affirmation bias. Attitude-based approach was developed mainly to deal with interest-oriented bias and optimism bias. Process-based strategy was found helpful in minimizing preconception bias and interest-oriented bias. It is further suggested that debiasing can be effected through reality testing that is widely used by mediators to steer the disputing parties on rational courses. Reality testing creates more opportunities and environment for the negotiating parties to chew on their assumptions and acknowledge their unrealistic beliefs and expectations.

11209118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209118.value: The emergence of industry 4.0 and relevant continually evolving technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of things, blockchain, etc. are leading business into the digital era. In the construction industry, as huge volumes of data are generated and considered as valuable assets. The landscape of construction dispute resolution would be dramatically changed in both dispute subjects and resolution methods. One simple example could be the use of collaborative technology, like video conferencing in streamlining the process and improving the efficiency of dispute resolution. The disputing parties and expert witnesses will not have to commute to the other side of the world to attend hearing and interviews. Another example is prior commencing a dispute resolution process, the negotiating parties could use AI-based data analytics applications to collect and synthesise data from past arbitrations and trials or gain the knowledge of the behaviours of a particular judge or arbitrator on historical cases. More knowledge, understanding and preparation before entering the dispute resolution process could help achieve early settlement and boost efficiency. The diffusion and application of digital technology surely have brought many new opportunities to avoid human cognitive limitations and eliminate biases in construction dispute negotiations.

11209118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209118.value: Having bias may well be fact of life for most people. However, most decision makers, especially those identified as professionals, will not admit that their decisions have been influenced by bias. This study was inspired by the challenges arising from the use of multi-tiered construction dispute resolution procedure in construction projects. Essentially, a dispute will go through several pre-determined steps typically moving from non-binding mediation to highly legalistic arbitration. This study examines whether this multi-tiered resolution design is futile for bias to happen. The repeated evaluation of a dispute is likely to generate biases that are unintended. This study systemically applied robust research methods to address this uncharted puzzle. The findings confirm the existence of bias in repeated evaluations. The study conceptualizes four types of bias in construction dispute resolution. These are namely: perception, self-affirmation, optimism and interest-oriented. Respectively, a measurement inventory was developed to assist the construction community to detect the existence and extent of biases. Practical strategies to minimize the effect of biases have also been recommended. The conceptualization of biases and contributes to the body of knowledge in construction dispute resolution academically. The bias measurement inventory and the debiasing strategies shall prove invaluable to construction dispute practitioners.

11209418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209418.value: Timber building has becomes an innovative and sustainable architectural solution in view of the research on wood mechanics and bio-spired materials in the past few decades. However, the safety issue related to the wood combustion is still a concern before wood can be applied to building construction extensive. In fact, the question related to wood pyrolysis and decomposition remains unanswered. In particular, little is known with regard to the formation mechanism of toxic carbon monoxide in timber building fire. Prior research studies in this area mainly focus on the experimental approach. It is found that the carbon monoxide yields at least double in wood when there is a vitiation of oxygen supply, which can be easily in tall buildings suffered from fire attacks. However, these findings cannot give any clues upon the formation mechanism of carbon monoxide, which is fundamental and crucial for a comprehensive understanding upon wood combustion. Such mechanism is indeed important for designing the fire safety aspect of the tall timber building, especially related to the evacuation route during fire. Through the recent development of material modeling technique, molecular dynamics simulation equipped with reactive forcefield is capable to reveal the decomposition of the wood constituents from an atomistic perspective, so that the formation mechanism of carbon monoxide under different oxygen content can be explored. The objective of this research is to investigate the formation mechanism of carbon monoxide fundamentally and comprehensively using reactive molecular dynamics simulation equipped with bench-scale fire tests. It is proposed to investigate by means of a synergistic effort that consists of atomistic modeling of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, reactive molecular dynamics simulations of carbon monoxide formation during wood combustion, fire tests from material level, modeling smoke and gas flow in tall timber building during fire using computational fluid mechanics. Synergizing the knowledge developed in these research tasks, this study will form the basis for augmenting existing design specifications for tall timber building by including the quantitative fire safety design related to the carbon monoxide formation during wood combustion, leading to a much more reliable and sustainable design. It is envisioned that this proposed research is crucial for understanding the complete and incomplete combustion processes, which leads to an advancement of thermal and combustion science of timber-based materials, and for understanding the relative rating of their flammability and fire safety, which is crucial when wood is used in tall building design. 在過去幾十年間，木結構建築已成為一種創新和可持續性的建築方案。然而，在木材廣泛應用於建築領域之前，木材燃燒的安全問題仍然有待解決。實際上，有關木材熱解的問題仍懸而未決。特別是對封閉空間火災中有毒一氧化碳的形成機制知之甚少，而這是高層建築火災中導致火災傷亡最重要的因素。此前研究發現，供氧不足時木材中一氧化碳的產生量至少會增加一倍，而遭受火災的高層建築更容易出現此情況。然而，這些研究結果並不能為一氧化碳的形成機制提供任何線索，而這正是全面理解木材燃燒的基礎和關鍵。這種機制對於高層木制建築的消防安全設計非常重要，尤其與火災疏散路線相關。基於納米工程和材料建模技術的發展，結合反應力場的分子動力學模擬能夠從原子角度揭示木材成分的熱解過程，從而進一步探索不同含氧量條件下一氧化碳的形成機制。 本研究旨在利用配備小型防火實驗裝置的分子動力學模擬從原子尺度上全面研究一氧化碳的形成機制。本項目擬通過以下研究任務進行：包括纖維素、半纖維素和木質素的原子建模，木材燃燒過程中一氧化碳形成的反應分子動力學模擬，材料尺度的燃燒試驗，利用計算流體力學模擬火災時高層木制建築中的煙氣流動。通過整合不同研究任務的成果，本研究將通過納入木材燃燒期間一氧化碳形成機理來優化消防安全設計，優化高層木制建築設計規範，從而實現更可靠的可持續設計。可以預見的是，對木材燃燒過程中一氧化碳形成機制的深入研究對於理解完全和不完全燃燒過程至關重要，本研究項目對實現木材材料的熱力學和燃燒科學的進步，加深對木材可燃性和防火安全等級的理解，以及將木材用於高層建築物設計具有重要意義。

11209418.label: Realisation of objectives
11209418.value: Objective 1 has been achieved completely. A reliable full atomistic models for cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin has been created. Such model equipped with reactive forcefield can be used to study the chemistry during combustion process. Objective 2 has been achieved completely. A better understanding on the formation mechanism of carbon monoxide has been obtained through molecular dynamics simulation equipped with reactive forcefield. The intermediate products during the combustion process have been well captured through molecular dynamics simulations. The relationship between the carbon monoxide formation mechanism and the surrounding conditions has also been studied. Objective 3 has been achieved completely. Bench-scale experiments have been conducted and the experimental results show a good agreement with what can be predicted through the full atomistic model. Objective 4 has been achieved completely. A predictive model which can describe the carbon monoxide concentration in tall timber building has been proposed. This predictive model connects the molecular dynamic simulations and fire dynamics simulator in a seamless manner. The developed multiscale and predictive model can accurately predict pyrolysis. The ability to predict fire properties of various wood species by the multiscale model enables to forecast realistic fire scenarios in highrise timber buildings.

11209518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209518.value: 建築能耗占全球發達城市 (如香港、北京、上海、東京、紐約和倫敦等) 能耗的很大一部分。 舉例來說, 2013年香港的商業樓宇能耗約為每年284PJ, 每人均產生2公噸的二氧化碳。 供暖、通風和空調系統至少消耗了香港建築能耗的75%。 有研究證明, 低效控制系統是造成暖通空調系統高能耗的主要原因。 因此, 通過對暖通空調系統的優化控制, 仍有相當大的改進餘地。 本研究旨在開發最佳的控制技術, 以合成一個智慧和經濟高效而不損害個人的舒適程度解決方案。 其關鍵目標是對暖通空調系統進行最佳的監控, 最大限度地減少能源使用, 提高整個系統的效率。 通常, 暖通空調系統對需求反應緩慢。 因此, 模型預測控制 (MPC) 是非常適合用於慢反應系統決策制定。 鑒於暖通空調系統的性能是高度非線性和複雜的, 基於 PENN (Probabilistic Entropy based Neural Network), 一個能夠捕獲系統的動態行為 aNN（adaptive neural network-自我調整神經網路模型）將會被合成為aNNMPC 模型。 本研究會在 TRNSYS 模擬環境下, 建立暖通空調系統的模擬試驗台, 並利用 Matlab 實現 aNNMPC 模型作為系統的控制以評估它的有效性並與常規控制方案作比較。 預計新的控制方案將提高系統的準確性、可靠性和效率, 並能更好地提高作業系統運行速度, 降低維護成本。

11209518.label: Realisation of objectives
11209518.value: Task 1 – Development of Adaptive Neural Network based model of HVAC system (The Task 1 addressing the Objective 1 was completed) For the construction of ANN model, the real HVAC system with a sufficiently adequate history of data had been selected. Its recorded historical data had been used for training of neural network model and also simulation test bed constructed using simulation software TRNSYS had been used for this study to generate and offer supplement data for training and verification of the ANN model for HVAC system. A hyperspace to locate all of the data was established. The probability distribution of the data over this hyperspace was then constructed. A kernel-based artificial neural network model was adopted. In this work, the Probabilistic Entropy based Neural Network (PENN) which was an online learning model with its pre-processor consisting of a novel clustering approach that utilized probabilistic theories and information entropy was developed. Also, it was mathematically proven to be capable of working in noisy environments. We applied the nearest-neighbor approach to upgrade the PENN model to a fully autonomous ANN model that would not require any human intervention with the initialization of a new (proposed) hyper ellipsoidal kernel. After completing the training with training data synthesized, the developed model in this task was used as a part of the complete scheme. Its output was treated as prediction for our HVAC system. Online learning had been performed in batches at appropriate intervals to be determined, to keep the computational load under check. The objective 1 was completed. Task 2 – Verification and validation of Adaptive Neural Network based HVAC model (The Task 2 addressing the Objective 2 was completed) The HVAC prediction model established in Task 1 had been verified. Its performance had been evaluated with the data from real HVAC system (from task 1) the method known as ‘leave-one-out’ validation. This verified prediction aNN model (outcome of currently completed task 2) had been used to predict the response of HVAC system over predictive horizon and incorporated in MPC decision making. Smith Predictor (SP) established in Task 3 also utilized the prediction of aNN HVAC model, in order to provide noise free signal for local loop decision making. The objective 2 was completed. Task 3 – Establishment of dead time compensator for control loops with Smith Predictor (The Task 3 addressing the Objective 3 was completed) In the realization of HVAC systems in high rise buildings, delays (dead time) in control loop were unavoidable, dead time induced noise in the control loop and caused ineffective actuation due to unreliability of data. This erroneous response propagated throughout the system. We considered three types of signal delays in a chilled water loop: (1) sensor and actuator delays due to sampling of data, (2) controller delay accounting for the processing time required by the controller and (3) transport delay over the control loop for chillier to AHU and AHU to chillier transportation delay. These delays caused noise that propagated to air side and were not delayed in this work. The robust control scheme was formulated to enhance stability in the presence of dead time in control loops. The SP which utilized the prediction from aNN model established in task 1 was used as a dead time compensator. This provided noise free signal for local loop control and ensured effective operation of HVAC system. It consisted of two loops (1) the outer loop being actual process which was affected by dead time and (2) the inner loop including the model of the actual process and estimate of dead time through the length of piping and rated chilled water flow rate. The virtual environment provided a compensator/ controller that eliminated the dead time. The objective 3 was completed. Task 4 – Synthesis of aNNMPC scheme for HVAC systems (The Task 4 addressing the Objective 4 was completed) The strategy for ANN model based predictive control (aNNMPC) utilizing the nonlinear trained ANN model to enhance the robustness of controller had been formulated. The ANN model predicted the future plant output over predictive horizon and the optimal control trajectory was then calculated by minimizing desired parameters, such as tracking error of each control loop and constraints formulated into the cost function. With the ANN prediction model, control scheme was found to be more reliable and lower on computational load as compared to first principle model. A powerful aNNMPC scheme for HVAC system which was proven to be robust with respect to model mismatch and time varying disturbances had been developed. This powerful aNNMPC scheme was capable of regulating HVAC system under predefined bonds in an efficient manner. The outcome of this task offered a reliable and energy efficient control with adaptive NNMPC that captured the nonlinear and complex dynamics of HVAC. The objective 4 was completed.

11209518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209518.value: The Model Predictive Control (MPC) as an optimal model based control scheme which utilizes the receding horizon control has been considered as one of the most significant developments in control engineering. It could offer good control for HVAC systems. In MPC, the optimal control law is computed by solving an optimization problem and a plant model is used to predict the future output response of a plant. However, it has been computationally expensive and lacks reliability, since it relies on deterministic models of HVAC systems, which require many assumptions and simplifications. In the current research work, the nonlinear data driven system identification techniques, such as artificial neural network (ANN) which could reduce the computational burden and could be more accurate as compared to conventional deterministic models was utilized to address the above issues. This provided a more potent solution for modelling of HVAC system to be incorporated in MPC scheme. To enhance robustness with respect to model mismatch and time varying disturbances, Probabilistic Entropy based Neural Network (PENN) model could be employed as an adaptive neural network (aNN) model for HVAC systems. The aNN model based predictive control (aNNMPC) worked on the principle of receding horizon to provide enhanced robustness and deal directly with system constraints, nonlinearity and complexity. Furthermore, the Smith Predictor (SP) for dead time compensator of individual control loops was designed to provide noise free feedback for local loop control. The major finding of the current research had been the formulation of the aNNMPC scheme for synthesizing energy conservation models based on optimization control techniques to synthesize an intelligent, cost-effective solution for smart buildings for overall energy usage of HVAC systems, without compromising individual level of comfort. The key research outcome had been the development of an innovative control strategy based on aNNMPC for HVAC systems in MATLAB that dealt with uncertainties, nonlinearities and constraints as an optimal supervisory control solution for HVAC systems to minimize energy costs and improve efficiency of the overall system.

11209518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209518.value: As an immediate further development of this research, case studies may be conducted to show the effectiveness of the aNNMPC by comparison with the conventional control schemes used for HVAC control. Potentially, the research result can be applied and can contribute to the field of HVAC by providing optimal control schemes to reduce energy consumption of HVAC systems in buildings. At the global scale, this will help alleviating carbon emissions and global warming. The established control scheme could be directly implemented in new HVAC designs and systems to create a new generation of products for the local and international industries. Also, this control scheme could be adopted by other process industries for optimising their energy consumption or performance. This will contribute to establishing advanced industrial standards and guidelines for the control industry.

11209518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209518.value: In summary, this research resulted in the development of optimal control techniques to synthesize an intelligent and cost-effective solution for building energy usage without compromising individual level of comfort. As the key finding, an optimal supervisory control solution for HVAC systems to minimize energy use and improve efficiency of the overall system was devised. The Model Predictive Control (MPC) which has been well suited for slow response systems has been adopted quite successfully in HVAC systems control. To further address the highly nonlinear and complex behaviours of HVAC systems, an adaptive neural network (aNN) model based on PENN (Probabilistic Entropy based Neural Network) was formulated to capture its dynamic behaviour. The aNN model could predict the system response and update the MPC efficiently. The aNN model based predictive control (aNNMPC) which worked on the principle of receding horizon had been developed using MATLAB. A simulation test bed of an HVAC system was built in the TRNSYS simulation environment and the aNNMPC implemented with Matlab was used as the control for the system. It was shown that the new control scheme could greatly enhance robustness, accuracy, reliability and efficiency as well as improve system operation and reduce maintenance costs.

11209918.label: Realisation of objectives
11209918.value: Refer to the Objective 1: To study the nanostructural variation and sub-10 nm grain size strengthening behaviors in the Mg alloys produced by PVD under various conditions, and the PVD parameters’ influence on the grain size and volume fraction of glass/crystal ratio; Study the deformation mechanism of the SNDP-GC nanostructure and realization of different deformation behaviors for amorphous phase and nanocrystalline phase. This project objective has been achieved. In this project, we have studied the nanostructural variation and grain size strengthening behaviors in the Mg alloys produced by PVD under various conditions, and the effect of PVD parameters on the grain size and volume fraction of glass/crystal ratio. We have also studied the deformation mechanism of the SNDP-GC nanostructure and realization of different deformation behaviors for amorphous phase and nanocrystalline phase. The findings have been published in the publications, “Near-ideal strength and large compressive deformability of a nano-dual-phase glass-crystal alloy in sub-micron” in Scripta Materialia in 2020. The project team reported a room temperature ultrahigh yield strength (3.0 GPa in compression) and large deformability (above 50% compressive strain) of a magnesium-based nano-dual-phase glass-crystal alloy in sub-micro size, compared with brittle nature of its own structural units. Transmission electron microscope investigation, molecular dynamic simulation and constitutive modeling were conducted, showing that the nanostructure of extremely small sized nanocrystals embedded in the glassy shells results in near-ideal strength; plastic flow of the glassy phase and grain refinement of the crystalline phase contribute to the large deformability. This material design may provide broad implications in wearable flexible devices and high-performance nano-electromechanical systems. Refer to the Objective 2: To study the self-lubrication mechanism under wear for the SNDP-GC nanostructure. Study the different structure evolutions for amorphous phase and nanocrystalline phase under wear. Improve wear property of Mg alloy by depositing the SNDP-GC. This project objective has been achieved. In this project, we showed a superior lubrication performance achieved in the Mg-based nano-dual-phase alloy, where the wear rate under dry sliding conditions can be 1/8 the regular crystalline alloy. By analyzing the detailed micro-structure evolution in both experiments and atomistic simulations, we attributed the unique lubrication behavior to the ultrahigh hardness of the alloy and the easy amorphization that converts the nanocrystalline phase to the low-friction nano-glassy phase. This finding outlined a general scheme where lubricious metal surfaces under dry sliding condition can be designed by tuning the micro- and nano-structures of the constituents. A Mg-based nano-dual-phase glass-crystal (NDP-GC) with an amorphous/nanocrystalline dual-phase structure was fabricated and demonstrated to have striking anti-wear properties throughout the running-in and steady-state wear processes. By inspecting the structural evolution using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, we attribute the superior wear resistance to the ultrahigh hardness of the NDP-GC and the easy amorphization of the nanocrystalline phase. This work has been reported in details in the mid-term report. Refer to the Objective 3: To study the method of increasing plasticity for the SNDP-GC, such as multilayered film design and understand the mechanism for plasticity generation. This project objective has been achieved. Mg alloys can be strengthened by introducing gradient nanograined structure. However, this strategy is unable to provide large ductility in Mg alloys, as restricted by the hcp structure. In this study, we developed a hybrid nanostructured Mg alloy via depositing a Mg-based NDP-MG film on the surface of the gradient nanograined Mg alloy. The ductility can be dramatically increased to 20%, which is comparable to that of the as-received base alloy. Meanwhile, the yield strength maintains at 230 MPa (similar to that of the SMAT-H sample), revealing 31% improvement than the base alloy. The synergistic effects of multiple shear bandings and crystallization of the NDP-MG, crack impediment by the NDP-MG, and grain growth of the SMATed nanograin layer promote the large plastic deformation. These mechanisms facilitate excellent mechanical properties in Mg alloys, overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off dilemma. This hybrid nanostructure alloy design strategy by combining concepts of heterogeneous MG and gradient nanograined structure could be applied to other alloy systems to achieve high strength and large ductility. This work has been published as “Nano-Dual-Phase Metallic Glass Film Enhances Strength and Ductility of a Gradient Nanograined Magnesium Alloy” in Advanced Science in 2020. Refer to the Objective 4: To investigate the corrosion mechanism of SNDP-GC. This project objective has been achieved. In this study, we developed a nanostructured Mg57Zn36Ca7 (at.%) DP-MG and uncovered its corrosion mechanism in simulated body fluid (SBF) at the near-atomic scale utilizing transmission electron microscope (TEM) and atom probe tomography (APT). The 10-nm-wide Ca-rich amorphous phases allow oxygen propagation into the DP-MG, resulting in a micrometer thick hydroxides/oxides layer. This dense corrosion layer protects the DP-MG from further corrosion, enabling a corrosion rate that is 77% lower than that of Mg (99.99% purity). This work has been published as “Second phase effect on corrosion of nanostructured Mg-Zn-Ca dual-phase metallic glasses” in Journal of Magnesium and Alloys in 2021. Refer to the Objective 5: Comparison between experimental results and MD simulation. This project objective has been achieved. In this reporting period, we reported an excellent tensile property of the Mg-based nano-dual-phase glass-crystal alloy in sub-micro size. It shows room temperature large ductility (>50% true strain, resulted from the localized necking deformation) with ultrahigh tensile strength (2.4 GPa), compared with 1.4 GPa strength and limited ductility of its metallic glass counterpart. To unraveling the underlying reasons, we have made transmission electron microscope (TEM) in-situ tensile investigation and molecular dynamic (MD) simulation for the materials, showing that homogenous plastic flow of nano-sized metallic glass phase activated by strain non-localization mechanism is responsible for the large ductility. This woek has been published as “Ductility of an ultrastrong glass-crystal nano-dual-phase alloy in sub-micron” in Scripta Materialia in 2020. A recent work concerning with the constitutive analysis of size-dependent deformation behaviors in micropillars of a NDPGC alloy based on the micromechanics approach has been conducted and published as “Constitutive modeling of size-dependent deformation behavior in nano-dual-phase glass-crystal alloys” in International Journal of Plasticity in 2021. The mechanism-based constitutive models are developed to explore the sample-size dependent mechanical behaviors of NDPGC pillars. An energy-based criterion for shear-band nucleation is employed to predict the diameter-dependent number of shear bands in large micropillars subjected to compression. The flow activation in metallic glass, grain reorganization, and grain refinement are involved in the proposed constitutive model for small micropillars. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed theoretical model can describe the constitutive behaviors of the Mg-based NDPGC alloy. Good agreements between the theoretical and experimental results are achieved for the stress-strain relations and the diameter-dependent number of shear bands in large micropillars.

This finding outlined a general scheme where lubricious metal surfaces under dry sliding condition can be designed by tuning the micro- and nano-structures of the constituents. 3. A hybrid nanostructure concept was presented by combining nano-dual-phase metallic glass (NDP-MG) and gradient nanograin structure in Mg alloys to achieve a higher yield strength (230 MPa, 31% improvement compared with the reference base alloy) and larger ductility (20%, threefold higher than the SMAT-H sample), which breaks the strength–ductility trade-off dilemma. This work has been published as “Nano-Dual-Phase Metallic Glass Film Enhances Strength and Ductility of a Gradient Nanograined Magnesium Alloy” in Advanced Science in 2020. 4. A Mg57 Zn36 Ca7 dual-phase metallic glasses (DP-MG) was developed and it demonstrates a unique passivation performance. The passive layer formed on the Mg57 Zn36 Ca7 DP- MG in simulated body fluid (SBF) is micrometer thick and compact, and its protection ability is enhanced with increasing corrosion duration. This work has been published as “Second phase effect on corrosion of nanostructured Mg-Zn-Ca dual-phase metallic glasses” in Journal of Magnesium and Alloys in 2021. 5. Numerical results of our work demonstrated that the proposed theoretical model can describe the constitutive behaviors of the Mg-based NDPGC alloy. The findings show that a good combination of high yield strength and excellent plasticity can be achieved with small micropillars under compression, and the proposed model can be applied to optimize the mechanical performance of NDPGC alloys by controlling the microstructural size and sample (or feature) size. This work was published as “Constitutive modeling of size-dependent deformation behavior in nano-dual-phase glass-crystal alloys” in International Journal of Plasticity in 2021.

11209918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209918.value: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are good candidates for applications with requirement of energy saving, taking advantage of their low density. In aerospace and automotive industries, the use of magnesium (Mg) alloys is increasing due to their high strength-to-weight ratio. However, conventional Mg alloys show poor plastic formability at room temperature, as their hexagonal-close-packed (hcp) structure cannot provide enough slip systems to deform plastically. In this project, we have successfully employed PVD to deposit a dual-phase glass-crystal (NDPGC) metallic thin film on Mg alloy to allow it possessing excellent mechanical properties and wear resistance. These outstanding mechanical properties of the Mg-based NDPGC alloy encourage it to be employed in many applications, such as aerospace and automotive industries, and biomedical applications. However, the in-depth studies of the feasibility of these applications are still missing. Thus, we will further work on the feasibility studies of the Mg-based NDPGC alloy in different fields after the completion of this project.

11209918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209918.value: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are good candidates for applications with requirement of energy saving, taking advantage of their low density. In aerospace and automotive industries, the use of magnesium (Mg) alloys is increasing due to their high strength-to-weight ratio. However, the conventional Mg alloys show poor plastic formability at room temperature. In this study, we have designed a series of novel Mg-based alloys with dual-phase glass-crystal metallic thin film deposited, which successfully possess outstanding mechanical properties without trading off too much the ductility. We have also uncovered the corrosion mechanism and mechanism of plasticity generation of this type of Mg-based alloy. This project allows us to have a better understanding of the Mg-alloys with NDPGC thin film deposited and demonstrates a few new research strategies to the researchers and engineers for further development of this novel type of materials for real-life applications.

11210218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210218.value: The science and engineering of the optical response of micro- to nano- scale structures can benefit tremendously from far field optical characterization techniques capable to provide quantitative information on the sample’s actual properties: composition, structure, and morphology with sub-wavelength resolution. Among the myriad of applications, ranging from fundamental to technological, where such quantitative characterization capabilities are desirable, the renewed interest in the characterization and control of sub-wavelength temperature distributions presents unique challenges and vast opportunities. The opportunities arise because the control and measure of temperature distributions at the micro- to nano- scale will have profound impact in biology, chemistry, and physics. A major struggle, however, is the difficulty to provide quantitative, contactless, and marker-free experimental measurements of such temperature distributions. Optical techniques can satisfy the requirements for this task and among them, spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) is a leading candidate because of its phase sensitivity and self-referenced characteristics. On multilayered samples SE is routinely used to provide quantitative information on each layers characteristics based on detailed analysis of the spectrally- and depth- resolved sample’s optical functions (n, k) using the well-known Fresnel coefficients and matrix transfer formalism. However, structured non-layered samples require numerical fully vectorial data analysis. The rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) has been highly successful to study the optical critical dimension (OCD) analysis of 1D gratings in the semiconductor industry but so far it faces unresolved difficulties to provide quantitative results for modern nanotechnology applications. For such complex cases, our group recently provided the first systematic validation of an alternative to RCWA: we demonstrated that quantitative SE data analysis can be based on the far-field propagation of the near-field response of the sample calculated using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method. In this project we will use the SE-FDTD strategy developed by our group to enable realistic, quantitative optical characterization of the complete temperature effects in plasmonic metamaterials including changes in refractive index and thermal expansion effects. This project will thus enable the systematic study of sub-micron temperature distributions that will include important characteristics of relevance for the optimization and engineering of thermal fields in plasmonic metamaterials. To this end we will continue the development of advanced polarimetric strategies that are expected to provide much needed optical characterization capabilities of subwavelength - sized structures capable to quantitatively correlate highly sensitive SE measurements with the morphology and optical properties of complex structured materials with applications in nano-optics and nano-photonics. 遠場光學表征技術對微納尺度結構的光響應科學與工程十分有益。該技術能夠提供樣品性質的定量信息，包括其成分、結構及亞波長分辨率的形貌。在從基礎到技術的眾多應用中，研究者十分需要這種定量表征能力。這使得人們對亞波長範圍溫度分布的表征和控制產生極大興趣，並且帶來了獨特的挑戰與巨大的機會，因為微納尺度結構的溫度分佈與測量將對生物學、化學和物理學產生深遠影響。然而，一個主要的困難是難以提供該尺度範圍溫度分佈的定量、無接觸和無標記的實驗測量。 光學技術可以滿足這項任務的要求。其中，光譜橢圓偏振（SE）因其出色的相位靈敏度與自參考特性而備受青睞。基於菲涅爾係數及轉移矩陣方法，光譜橢圓偏振被廣泛應用於定量分析多層樣品結構的光譜及深度分辨光學函數（n, k）。然而，結構化的非層狀樣品的光學函數需要通過全矢量數值模擬分析而獲得。嚴格的耦合波分析（RCWA）被成功地應用于半導體工業中一維光柵的光學臨界尺寸（OCD）分析，但迄今為止，它在為現代納米技術應用提供定量分析方面仍面臨著未解決的困難。 對於該複雜的情況，我們研究團隊最近首次提出并系統地驗證了一項用於替代RCWA的新方案：該方案表明了有限差分時域法（FDTD）所計算的樣品的近場響應之遠場傳播可用於定量光譜橢圓偏振數據之分析。 該項目將使用我們研究組先前所發展的SE-FDTD方法，以實現等離子體超材料中完整溫度效應的定量光學表征，包括折射率及熱膨脹效應的變化。因此，該項目將能夠系統地研究亞微米溫度分佈，這將包括等離子超材料中的熱場優化與工程相關的重要特征。為此，我們將繼續開發先進的極化方法，有望提供亞波長尺寸結構所需的光學表征能力，能夠將高靈敏度SE測量與複雜結構材料的形態和光學性質定量關聯，并應用于納米光學及納米光子學。

11210218.label: Realisation of objectives
11210218.value: OBJECTIVE 1. Mueller Matrix Ellipsometry (MME), is a generalized version of Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE) most suitable to study anisotropic samples. It is also more suitable to study metamaterials, compared to SE, because MME data contains essential optical information about the sample including cross-polarization effects due to linear and circular birefringence (LB and CB, respectively), linear and circular dichroism (LD and CD, respectively), and retardance. We have developed a strategy to model the MME response of arbitrary periodic materials using the Split-Field (SF) FTDT method that: i) enables to model a broad spectral range from a single simulation even at large AoI; and ii) results in faster convergence to a robust, unique solution, due to the additional information provided by the MME data. Using this strategy we model the experimental data, using 11 of the 16 MME elements, measured from a homemade 1D grating. As expected, the MME modeling can fit the experimental data providing much faster convergence compared to the use of SE data when using a particle swarm algorithm. OBJECTIVE 2. This proposal has been of great importance to secure additional funding from the ITC to develop an Imaging and Conoscopic Spectroscopic Ellipsometers: Reference No. ITS/461/18, Project Title: Versatile Polarimetric Platform for Analytical Optical Testing, Funding Year: 2020, Awarded: $1,398,400 HKD. The imaging part of this instrument is a Spectroscopic rotating-compensator Imaging Ellipsometer (SIE) with spectral range from 400 to 750 nm and lateral resolution of ~5 um. The lateral resolution was tested using a USAF 1951 imaging test target which also provides a suitable plasmonic sample as it defines a structured Cr film prepared on glass substrate. The SIE was used to measure the structured Cr layer in an imaging test target USAF-1951. The optical modelling was performed using Fresnel coefficients that enables modelling of the homogenous parts of the sample far away from the Cr/Glass interfaces and FDTD to model the interface part. In the homogeneous regions, calculation of the goodness-of-fit values using the root-mean-squared error (RMSE) confirms the suitability of the optical model (Fresnel equations). From the ellipsometric parameters psi and Delta, we estimate a lateral resolution of ~5.4 um (resolving group 5, element 3) of the test target. Instead, near the interface, FDTD data modeling is required, and we have demonstrated that using the RMSE results in increased ~1.2x increase in lateral resolution (resolving group 5, element 6); this was demonstrated from the RMSE map and is consistent with the numerical FDTD results. OBJECTIVE 3. We have optimized the convergence efficiency of our FDTD approach using multiple strategies that include: i) use of MME to provide additional data information compared to standard SE; ii) optimization of the simulation auto-shut-off (ASF) level that represents the remaining energy enclosed within the modelling region; and iii) use of cross-correlated parameters that take advantage of expected physical relationships between the parameters of an optical model to reduce the total number optical parameters in the simulation. It is noted that such optimization is not universal; for example, one needs to take into consideration the effect of any potential optical or plasmonic resonances in the simulation. In particular, high quality -actor resonances are very efficient to store energy and therefore their decay time is very long. As a consequence, very low ASF levels, 10^(-6), are needed to achieve accurate simulations. However, in such cases, we also demonstrated that it is sufficient to run the simulation for a short period capable to provide high quality quantitative information of the resonance. This additional step then enables the accurate calculation of the resonance decay dynamics which in turns enable to circumvent the need for low ASF levels therefore still achieving high accuracy modelling within reasonably fast computation times. OBJECTIVE 4. We have demonstrated the feasibility to use 1) refractive index changes as function of temperature (dn/dt) and 2) thermal expansion coefficient α for homemade gratings fabricated from gold and PMMA and c-Si substrates. Using these samples, we measured and effectively model the effects of uniform heating, and colling, using a temperature stage during the uniform illumination needed for far-field continuous monitoring of the sample characteristics. This modelling was facilitated with the development of parameter-maps at each temperature stage during the ramp-up and ramp-down. The parameter maps supported the visualization of the evolution of the optical model parameters including refractive index changes as well as structural changes that result from thermal expansion coefficient effects. OBJECTIVE 5. During 2022, this proposal supported part of a sabbatical visit to the Fresnel Institute at Aix Marseille University (AMU), in France hosted by Prof. Claude Amra, Founder of the Institut Fresnel and its Director from 2000 to 2008. During this visit we developed a strong collaboration for multi-physics simulations of i) photothermal heating and ii) photoemission response using Gaussian illumination pulses with temporal ranges in the a) ms, b) ns, and c) ps time scales. These simulations are of great interest in space and other high performance optical coatings. On the French side, the group of Prof. Amra developed a new calculation strategy based on a double Fourier transform (FT) approach to treat the optics and the heat diffusion problems simultaneously. On the other hand, we implemented a Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) and Finite Element Model (FEM) strategy to solve the optical and heat propagation problems, sequentially. We demonstrated excellent agreement between the analytical double FT and FDTD-FEM methods estimated to be within one part in one thousand. These results included the time evolution and depth-profile of the temperature increase resulting from the pulsed illumination. Furthermore, we were also able to calculate the spectral and directional components of the photothermal emission in multilayer photonic systems. While some obvious limitations arise from the sequential use of FDTD-FEM compared to the doble FT strategy, for example difficulties to model train pulses, an important strength of the FDTD/FEM strategy is that it allows the modelling of structured, non-planar, metamaterial samples, which currently cannot be solved analytically. This work highlights the strengths of the approach proposed that were developed during the current project.

11210218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210218.value: We develop the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) model as a powerful approach for the quantitative modelling of far-field photonic and plasmonic effects of great significance in sensing, solar energy conversion, and high-performance optical coating applications. In combination with Finite element modelling (FEM), our studies can then include electrical as well as thermal effects. For the thermal effects we can model the temperature profile, refractive index changes, and thermal expansion, of multilayers and structured samples such as gratings. These results have been verified directly against experimental measurements of homemade plasmonic structured samples subjected to uniform temperature variations. Furthermore, taking advantage of a double FT strategy developed by our collaborators we have been able to model and confirm the temperature increase as well as the spectral- and directional- resolved photothermal emission of thin film multilayers subjected to photothermal effects arising from Gaussian illumination in the ms, us and ps time scales. On the other hand, we also used the FEM to study the electrical effects of multilayers. This takes into consideration important electrical parameters such as charge density and mobility, as well as the effects of bulk and interface recombination. This strategy then becomes a powerful approach to enable the study, for example, of perovskite solar cells in very large detail. For example, we have been able to include the use of structured front contact design to study the resulting photostability effects in single and tandem junction perovskite solar cells. This project has directly supported five major publications, see Par C, and two Phd Students, one of them graduated in March this year and the other expected to submit and defend his PhD thesis later this year (December 2023).

11210218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210218.value: The combination of FDTD model with far field SE is a powerful approach for the quantitative characterization and modelling of photonic and plasmonic effects. This is because the superb precision that is closely matched between both modelling and experimental techniques which currently is estimated to be ~ half monolayer. Furthermore, by adding Multiphysics capabilities in the form of FEM-enables thermal and/or electrical effects, we can add much needed quantitative modelling capabilities to complex, demanding, and important technological problems such as photovoltaics and radiative cooling. Furthermore, the modeling capabilities is not restricted to flat coatings and multilayers, but can include structured micro- and nano- sized structured metamaterials as well as plasmonic effects. The fabricated RCIE (ITF project ITS/461/18) and the results of this project GRF 11210218 are synergic and complimentary: with a current lateral resolution of ~ 5 um it will enable to explore small-area fluctuations of materials properties which is of interest for example in combinatorial materials science, non-uniform structured materials, photonic circuit inspection and many others. On the other hand the results developed by this project GRF 11210218 provide a solid foundation to include the sub-um structure effects in the photonic modeling of such materials and, importantly, to include multiphysics studies to treat heat propagation and electrical properties as demonstrated in our recent publications. Future areas of research to benefit from these capabilities include photovoltaics, thermophotonics, thermoplasmonics, and sensing. In the future we seek to also include magnetic materials in our studies to develop into the emerging interdisciplinary field of magnetoplasmonics.

11210218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210218.value: We have advanced use of the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) model as a powerful approach for the quantitative modelling of far-field photonic and plasmonic effects of great significance in sensing, energy, and high-performance optical coating applications. This is because we have implemented this in combination with Finite element modelling (FEM), in this case, our studies can then include electrical as well as thermal effects. For the thermal effects we can model the temperature profile, refractive index changes, and thermal expansion, of multilayers and structured samples such as gratings, as well as the spectral- and directional- resolved photothermal emission. On the other hand, using FEM to study the electrical effects of multilayers becomes a powerful approach to enable the study of, for example, perovskite solar cells in much greater detail than purely considering optical effects. To this end, we have been able to include the use of structured front contact design and resulting photostability effects in single and tandem junction perovskite solar cells to predict important electrical effects such as short circuit current, fill factor, and open circuit voltage. Importantly, the results achieved open additional avenues to address critical complex applications for which multi-physics modeling is of much importance.

11210818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210818.value: With the rise of cloud computing workloads, much innovation has happened over the recent years to improve the tenant networking performance. Examples range from fair bandwidth allocation among tenants to high performance overlay switches. Despite the progress, the tenant network stack has not seen much innovation; in fact a critical examination of its architecture has not been conducted to date. The tenant network stack is implemented inside the VM in today’s architecture. Applications are written with the standard networking APIs which invoke the network stack as part of the operating system. While this architecture provides strong isolation, when it comes to protocol stack evolution, this architecture presents a barrier due to the tight coupling between the network stack and the guest operating system (OS). In particular, it causes many deployment problems to tenants and management and efficiency problems to the cloud provider. We thus put forth a vision of network stack as a service to facilitate bringing innovations to all layers of the stack. The central thesis of this vision is to decouple the VM network stack from the guest OS and offer it as an independent entity (say a VM) by the cloud provider. We keep the application interfaces in the guest, such as BSD sockets for TCP/IP and Verbs for RDMA, intact and use them as the abstraction boundary instead of the virtual NICs. Packets are then handled outside the guest VM in a network stack module provided by the provider, whose design and implementation are transparent to tenants. Each VM has its own network stack module whose resources are dedicated to providing networking services, and tenants pay for it in addition to the application VM charges. We believe decoupling network stack from the guest OS, thereby enabling network stack as a service, fundamentally solves the problems discussed above. Tenants now can deploy any stack independent of its guest kernel without any effort or expertise. The provider can now offer meaningful SLAs to tenants by gaining control over the network stack. Overall the new architecture allows rapid and flexible deployment of more efficient network stacks, accelerating the innovation in the public cloud. 随着云计算的广泛使用，近年来为改善租户网络性能人们进行了大量创新。例子包括从租户之间的公平带宽分配到高性能overlay交换机。尽管取得了很多进展，租户网络协议栈还没有看到太多创新；事实上，迄今为止大家还没有仔细审视过其架构。在今天的架构中租户网络协议栈在VM内部实现。应用程序使用标准网络API编写，这些API调用作为操作系统一部分的网络协议栈。 虽然这种架构提供了完全的隔离，但在协议栈演进方面，由于网络网络栈和guest OS之间的紧密耦合，这种架构提出了障碍，它会给租户带来许多部署问题，并给云服务商带来管理和效率问题。 因此我们提出了网络协议栈服务化的愿景，以促进协议栈栈的所有层的创新。这一愿景的核心论点是将VM网络协议栈与guest OS分离，并由云服务商将其作为独立实体（比如VM）提供。我们将应用程序接口保留在guest VM中，例如用于TCP / IP的BSD socket和用于RDMA的Verbs，并将它们而不是虚拟NIC用作抽象边界。然后，在服务商提供的网络协议栈模块中，在guest VM外部处理数据包，其设计和实现对租户是透明的。每个VM都有自己的网络栈模块，其资源专用于提供网络服务，并且除了应用程序VM费用外，租户还会为其付费。 我们认为将网络堆栈与guest OS解耦，从而使网络协议栈变成一种云服务，从根本上解决了上面讨论的问题。租户现在可以独立于其VM内核部署任何协议栈，而无需任何努力或专业知识。现在，服务商可以通过控制网络协议栈为租户提供有意义的SLA。总体而言，新架构允许我们快速灵活地部署更高效的协议栈，从而加速公有云的创新。

11210818.label: Realisation of objectives
11210818.value: We achieved the research objectives in this project through several crucial technical innovations. All the design innovations and experimental results mentioned below are published in the two papers related to NetKernel listed in this report. For the first research objective, we propose to separate the network stack from the guest OS and make it a new paradigm, in which the network stack is coupled into the virtualized infrastructure of cloud. Operators can directly deploy, manage, optimize the network stack, and comprehensively promote the efficiency without affecting applications’ execution. As the heavy-lifting is taken care of, applications can just use network stack as a basic service of the infrastructure and focus on their business logic. More concretely, the network stack is offered as a network stack module (NSM) that is chosen by the user, e.g., the kernel-bypass stack mTCP or the improved kernel stack FastSocket. Meantime, Various network stacks can be provided as different NSMs to ensure applications with diverse requirements can work. We propose two critical innovations for the second research objective: transparent socket API redirection and a lightweight semantics channel. First, We designed a new library called GuestLib to redirect socket API calls to the NSM. The GuestLib provides a new socket type with a complete implementation of BSD socket APIs. It replaces all TCP and UDP sockets when they are created with NetKernel sockets, effectively redirecting them without changing applications. Second, we build a lightweight socket semantics channel between the guest VM and its NSM to ensure socket semantics from the VM work properly with the actual NSM stack implementation. The channel relies on small fix-sized queue elements as intermediate representations of socket semantics: Each socket API call in the VM is encapsulated into a queue element and sent to the NSM, who would effectively translate the queue element into the corresponding API call of its network stack. For the third research objective, we refine the lightweight semantics channel and enable the GuestLib to support the epoll event API. We adopt an interrupt-driven polling design for event notification in GuestLib. When an application is waiting for events, the GuestLib will first poll its completion queue and receive queue. If no new NQE comes after a short time period, the GuestLib stops polling and enters an interrupt context. With the extension of event APIs, we implement a popular application called NGINX without any code changes and achieve salient performance benefits by using the mTCP network stack. For the last research objective, we implemented a prototype based on QEMU KVM 2.5.0 and Linux kernel 4.9, with 11K LoC. We implemented the GuestLib as a kernel module and exploited QEMU's IVSHMEM to realized the memory sharing between the guest VM and NSM. We evaluate the prototype on a real testbed, in which each server has two Xeon E5-2698 v3 16-core CPUs clocked at 2.3 GHz, 256 GB memory at 2133 MHz, and a Mellanox ConnectX-4 single port 100G NIC. The results show that our prototype achieves the same scalability and isolation as the current architecture: Using a Linux kernel stack NSM, it reaches 100G send throughput with 3 cores; using an mTCP NSM it achieves 979K RPS with 8 cores which almost doubles that of the kernel stack NSM.

11210818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210818.value: (1). Major findings. The current division of labor between application and network infrastructure is becoming increasingly inadequate, especially in a private cloud setting. The central issue is that the network stack is controlled solely by individual guest VM; the operator has almost zero visibility or control. These limitations can be addressed by making the network stack part of the virtualized infrastructure. This approach has many benefits, it generally achieves better efficiency in management for the operator and deployment and performance gains for users: First, gaining control over the network stack, the operators can orchestrate the resource provisioning strategies more flexibly: For mission-critical workloads, they can dedicate CPU resources to their NSMs to offer performance SLAs in terms of throughput and RPS (requests per second) guarantees. For elastic workloads, on the other hand, they can consolidate their VMs to the same NSM (if they use the same network stack) to improve resource utilization. Second, various kernel stack optimizations, high-performance userspace stacks, and even designs using advanced hardware can now be deployed and maintained transparently without user involvement or application code change. For instance, DCTCP can now be deployed across the board easily in a public cloud. Since the BSD socket is the only abstraction exposed to the applications, it is now feasible to adopt new stack designs independent of the guest kernel or the network API. (2). Research output. We published 7 research papers to the top venues like USENIX ATC and IEEE/ACM ToN throughout this project. Additionally, we designed and implemented a new system called NetKernel that efficiently decouples the network stack from the guest virtual machine and offers it as an independent module.

11210818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210818.value: (1) Isolation. When multiple guest VMs share the same NSM, fine-grained performance isolation is imperative. It is also necessary and interesting to design charging policies that promote fair use of the NSM. In addition, as multiple guest VMs may share the same NSM, complete resource isolation becomes crucial for multi-tenant scenarios. (2) Resource efficiency. Various aspects of our design can be optimized for efficiency and practicality, such as CPU overhead. We will seek hardware offloading approaches for this in the future. (3) API. Our system currently provides BSD socket semantics, but a guest VM might need more network functionalities, such as access control and firewall. Therefore, identifying the minimal API set for guests to efficiently interact with the network stack becomes another future direction. Additionally, applications based on netmap, RDMA and eRPC libraries cannot benefit from NetKernel at present. We aim at supporting these network libraries in the future.

11210818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210818.value: In this project, we present a system called NetKernel that decouples the network stack from the guest virtual machine and offers it as an independent module. NetKernel represents a new paradigm where network stack can be managed as part of the virtualized infrastructure. It provides important efficiency benefits: By gaining control and visibility of the network stack, operators can perform network management more directly and flexibly, such as multiplexing VMs running different applications to the same network stack module to save CPU cores, and enforcing fair bandwidth sharing. Users also benefit from the simplified stack deployment and better performance: For example mTCP can be deployed without API change to support NGINX natively, and shared memory networking can be readily enabled to improve the performance of colocated VMs. Testbed evaluation using 100G NICs shows that NetKernel preserves the performance and scalability of both kernel and userspace network stacks, and provides the same isolation as the current architecture.

11211818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211818.value: The filtering technique plays an important role in a wide range of applications such as target tracking, image processing, signal processing, control, fault diagnosis, and so on. Fault diagnosis, as one of important applications of the filtering technique, becomes more and more critical in a variety of engineering applications such as automation engineering, nuclear engineering, aerospace engineering, and robotic engineering, due to an ever-increasing demand on reliability and safety of these engineering systems. Great effort has been devoted to study of filtering and fault diagnosis for many different kinds of systems during the past decades. Techniques of filtering and fault diagnosis have been well developed for linear systems, and still enjoy significant development for nonlinear systems due to the challenge in dealing with nonlinearities. On the other hand, it is well known that many practical engineering systems can be described or approximated by a special form of nonlinear models, that is, the so-called Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy model. Due to their special features, T-S fuzzy models have been widely exploited for development of filtering and fault diagnosis techniques in addition to control techniques for nonlinear systems in the past decade and many results have been obtained. However, how to reduce design conservatism of filtering and fault diagnosis and how to improve the performance of filtering and fault diagnosis for T-S fuzzy systems are two challenging issues yet to be well addressed. This project will investigate and develop novel approaches to filtering and fault diagnosis to address those two challenging issues for T-S fuzzy systems. In particular, this project will focus on advanced memory filtering techniques in finite frequency domain, and their application to fault diagnosis for T-S fuzzy systems. The outcome of this project is expected to be a number of novel advanced filtering and fault diagnosis approaches with better performance and reduced conservatism in real-world applications. These approaches will enrich theoretical foundation of filtering and fault diagnosis for a class of nonlinear systems described by T-S fuzzy systems, and provide engineers with more tools for filtering and fault diagnosis design. 滤波理论与技术被广泛应用于目标跟踪、图像处理、信号处理、 控制以及故障诊断等众多工程技术领域。作为滤波理论的重要应 用之一，故障诊断在可靠性与安全性要求较高的工程应用中起到 关键作用，其中包括自动化工程、核工程、航空航天工程、以及 机器人工程等。因此在过去的几十年中，科研工作人员针对各类 系统的滤波以及故障诊断方法与技术的研究投入了巨大的精力。 到目前为止，针对线性系统，已经形成了一套较为完善的滤波与 故障诊断理论成果。相比于线性系统，非线性系统的滤波与故障 诊断理论与方法的研究更加富有挑战性，且现有的研究成果并不 完善，亟待进一步的研究。另一方面，研究表明， Takagi-Sugeno (TS) 模糊模型是通用的函数逼近器，其可以在任 意的凸紧集内以任意精度逼近任意光滑非线性函数。因TS模糊 模型的上述特征与优点，在过去的几十年中，基于TS模糊模型 的非线性系统滤波与故障诊断一直是一个热点问题，并且针对 该问题取得了丰富的研究成果。值得指出的是，如何降低设计 保守性以及提高系统性能是基于TS模糊模型的非线性系统滤波 与故障诊断有待解决的重点和难点问题。针对上述TS模糊系统 的滤波与故障诊断中存在的难点和亟待解决的关键科学问题， 本项目拟提出在噪声频域受限情形下，基于过去测量信息的有 记忆滤波器设计方法。在此基础上，进一步研究TS模糊系统的 故障诊断方法，以期提出一套新颖的且较为完整的TS模糊系统 滤波与故障诊断理论及方法，达到有效降低设计保守性，并且 提高系统性能的目的，为工程技术人员提供理论与技术支持。

11211818.label: Realisation of objectives
11211818.value: All of the project objectives have been achieved successfully. More specifically, we have investigated and developed novel memory filtering approaches to T-S fuzzy systems in finite frequency domain. We then have taken into account uncertainties of T-S- fuzzy systems and developed novel robust memory filtering approaches for those systems in finite frequency domain. Based on the results of the first two objectives, we have then investigated and developed novel robust memory fault diagnosis approaches to T-S fuzzy systems with/without uncertainties in finite frequency domain, and have evaluated and consolidated the proposed approaches by extensive simulations and/or experiments on real-world applications.

11211818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211818.value: We have investigated the problems of advanced memory filtering of T-S fuzzy systems and robust memory filtering of uncertain T-S fuzzy systems in finite frequency domain in this project. As a result, a number of novel advanced memory filtering approaches have been developed for T-S fuzzy systems in finite frequency domain by exploiting various optimal filtering techniques, generalized Kalman-Yakuboich-Popov (GKYP) lemma, techniques of linear matrix inequalities, and various Lyapunov functions. The key idea is to utilize the past output measurements of the underlying system and the finite frequency range information of disturbances or noises to design a less conservative memory filter such that the performance of the filter is enhanced. Then uncertainties of T-S fuzzy systems are taken into account, and several novel robust memory filtering approaches have been developed. It is shown that the resulting filter error systems are globally asymptotically stable and the optimal filtering performance can be achieved. Based on the obtained filtering results, we have developed several novel advanced robust memory fault diagnosis approaches to T-S fuzzy systems without/with uncertainties. It is clearly demonstrated that the proposed approaches are less conservative and faults can be well detected. In addition, Extensive simulations over several benchmark systems have been carried out to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. In fact, the proposed approaches have been consolidated throughout the simulation studies. In the process of achieving the objectives of this project, some other results, such as memory output feedback control and fuzzy fault-tolerant control, have also been obtained. As a result of our research effort, 10 journal papers have been either published or accepted.

11211818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211818.value: We have investigated the problems of advanced memory filtering and fault diagnosis of T-S fuzzy systems as well as uncertain T-S fuzzy systems in finite frequency domain in this project. However, T-S fuzzy systems are a special class of nonlinear systems though they can be used to approximate many practical nonlinear systems. It would be interesting to consider more general nonlinear systems. In other words, it is interesting to investigate and develop novel filtering and fault diagnosis approaches to more general nonlinear systems though the topic appears to be very challenging.

11211818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211818.value: The filtering technique plays an important role in a wide range of applications such as target tracking, image processing, signal processing, control, fault diagnosis, and so on. Fault diagnosis, as one of important applications of the filtering technique, becomes more and more important in variety of engineering applications such as chemical engineering, nuclear engineering, aerospace engineering, and automation engineering, due to an ever-increasing demand on reliability and safety of these engineering systems. Great effort has been devoted to study of filtering and fault diagnosis for variety of engineering systems during the past decades. Techniques of filtering and fault diagnosis have been well developed for linear systems, and still enjoy significant development for nonlinear systems due to the challenge in dealing with nonlinearities. By exploiting the special features of Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy model, this project has investigated the problems of robust filtering and fault diagnosis of nonlinear systems. The main focus of the project is to reduce design conservatism of filtering and fault diagnosis and to improve the performance of filtering and fault diagnosis. A number of novel memory filtering and fault diagnosis approaches have been developed for T-S fuzzy systems in finite frequency domain, and then uncertainties of T-S fuzzy systems are taken into account and corresponding novel robust memory filtering and fault diagnosis approaches have been developed. It is shown that the proposed novel filtering and fault diagnosis approaches achieve better performance with reduced design conservatism. These proposed approaches will enrich theoretical foundation of filtering and fault diagnosis for the class of nonlinear systems described by T-S fuzzy systems, and provide engineers with more tools for filtering and fault diagnosis design.

11211918.label: Project Objectives
11211918.value: To study heat transfer through the water wall systems with different water layer thicknesses. To study the possible protection of glass façades using a water wall system. To study the possible protection of glass façades using a water wall system.
To provide guidelines for optimal design of the water wall system with respect to the thickness of the water layer in the system, façade glass type, thickness, etc.

11211918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211918.value: A water wall system (WWS) is an energy efficient green façade design. It can be further exploited as a structure to enhance fire safety. The water layer in the WWS can act as an effective heat absorbent in the case of a room fire due to the high thermal capacity of water. This results in a much lower temperature rise and a more uniform temperature distribution within the window panes. Incorporating a WWS can thus protect large glass façades in a fire, and that is what this proposed project aims to study. Water stored in the system can also be useful to fire suppression once the glass pane is broken during a fire. In this proposed study, a WWS containing two commonly used normal glass panes will be selected for in-depth exploration under post-flashover fire conditions. Physical scale models, an analytical study of heat transfer through glass façades and full-scale burning tests will be used. A hot smoke layer will be formed, simulating the early stage of a room fire. The upper part of the WWS will be exposed to a higher heat flux. A small WWS, 0.1 m × 0.1 m, will be constructed and tested under different radiative heat fluxes emitted by a conical heater in both horizontal and vertical directions. The surface temperatures will be measured under different distributions of heat fluxes to explore the heat removed by the water layer. Medium-scale experiments on the WWS, 1 m × 0.5 m in size, using typical glass panes will be carried out using a thermal radiator developed to emit higher heat fluxes at the upper levels of the glass panes. Changes to the surface temperatures of glass panes that are hotter at the top can then be studied. Burning tests on part of a real WWS will be conducted to study how the water layer protects the glass panes. A 2 m × 2.2 m room with a height of 1.5 m will be constructed and a 2 m × 1.5 m WWS will be built on one wall. The heat removal rate achieved by the water layer will be investigated. Mathematical models simulating heat transfer through glass panes and water layers during fires will be developed based on a thermal network system. The predicted results will be compared with the experimental results to understand how the WWS protects glass panes.

11211918.label: Realisation of objectives
11211918.value: Water wall systems (WWSs) are increasingly being used as glass façades in modern green buildings owing to their enhancement in building energy efficiency. In addition, they can provide fire protection and studied in this completed project with three objectives appeared in the proposal as follows: Objective 1. To study heat transfer through the water wall systems with different water layer thicknesses. 1.1 A mathematical model based on heat balance of the glass layers and water layer of a WWS was developed to study the thermal environment. The model was tested first by studying the impact of WWS on building energy use. The integrated WWS model was validated against two reported experimental studies and showed good agreement. It was applied to study the fire response of WWS using post-flashover room fire simulation results in a model room by the two-layer zone model software Consolidated Model of Fire and Smoke Transport (CFAST). 1.2 Cone calorimeter experiments on glass were carried out at the Department of Architecture and Civil Engineering (ACE) at CityU. The effect of temperature gradient components on cracking behavior of glass panes of WWS under thermal radiation was studied. Medium-scale experiments were conducted on the thermal response of a larger WWS model with a vertical radiant flux gradient. Full-scale burning tests were conducted in a fire laboratory in Heilongjiang, Harbin, China. A flashover was set by burning a 0.35 m square gasoline pool of fire. A WWS with two glass panes was installed in a model room of 2 m × 2.2 m and 1.5 m high. 1.3 During a room fire, the upper part of a vertical glass pane is exposed to higher radiative heat fluxes, producing a large temperature difference between the upper and lower parts. A WWS with two glass panes, each 2 m wide and 1.5 m high, was put in the above model room. The fire behaviour of the WWS was modelled with the results combined to study the fire response of the WWS’s two glass panes. Predictions of the developed mathematical model on WWS were compared with experimental results. 1.4 Numerical fire simulations with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) were developed to investigate the above room fire. The fire simulations were conducted in fire dynamics simulator (FDS) software by taking away the pyrolysis model as WWS is not combustible. The results are useful in understanding the design of a WWS with an optimum water layer thickness and appropriate water flow rate. Objective 2. To study the possible protection of glass façades using a water wall system. 2.1 Glass panes can be protected by applying a water layer, integrating it with the thermal storage of WWS to protect the glass panes against big fires. Heat removed by water to cool the glass panes was studied before in an earlier RGC-GRF project from 2015-2018. The water layer acts as a thermal barrier to reduce thermal radiation from both outdoor fires and indoor fires, and to carry away heat so as to lower glass temperature. 2.2 Experimental study on WWS exposed to fire was carried out and compared to the thermal performance of a single-skin glass façade system. These façade systems were heated an isopropanol pool fire. Results indicated that single skin glass façades are more vulnerable to cracking than water wall systems. Exposed glass pane fallout can easily occur in WWS compared to single skin façades. Since the overall performance is dependent on the failure of the fire unexposed glass pane, WWS are more fire resistant than single skin glass façades. 2.3 Providing adequate water flow at a smartly controlled rate once a fire is detected would remove the heat absorbed by the glass pane more rapidly. Water supplied by breaking the inner glass pane would be able to act on the fire. Activation times of thermal sensing element to start supplying water at appropriate flow rates were proposed and studied using common plunge test with a wind tunnel for sprinkler. Objective 3. To provide guidelines for optimal design of the water wall system with respect to the thickness of the water layer in the system, façade glass type, thickness, etc. 3.1 WWS are not much utilized in the existing green buildings due to their unpopularity and the unavailability of design guidelines. How WWS can have fire safety and reduce energy demand in green buildings as obvious in the literature review. Energy savings of WWS in green buildings was reviewed first. The water layer within the two glass panes of the WWS stores the heat from solar radiation during the daytime, reducing the amount of heat transferred through the building facade. 3.2 Fire protection of WWS green building façade was then reviewed. The water layer acts as a fire safety mechanism in case of a fire. The fire performance of WWS after elevated temperature exposure was investigated. On the basis of the findings of the literature review, stakeholders and the public are encouraged to seriously consider WWS in green building projects as an energy-efficient strategy and a fire safety mechanism. 3.3 Many green projects with new architectural features on glass facades in the rapidly developing Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) have difficulties in complying with the prescriptive fire codes. There are difficulties in specifying fire safety for such glass facades using such prescriptive fire safety building codes. Consequently, performance-based design (PBD) in fire engineering approach (FEA) has to be applied in the GBA. Results deduced from this project can be applied in those fire safety committees in evaluating PBD-FEA projects, and the acceptance criteria to give fire-safe green façades. 3.4 Three possible fire protection mechanisms provided by WWS are: • Water supplied by breaking the inner glass pane would be able to act on the fire. • Glass panes with different properties and thicknesses are recommended in WWS. The glass pane facing fire should be thinner and have higher conductivity than the outer glass, to increase the rate of heating up. • Providing adequate water flow at a smartly controlled rate once a fire is detected would remove the heat absorbed by the glass pane more rapidly. 3.5 In urban areas such as those in GBA, buildings are often used to store large amounts of combustible materials, which can result in long-lasting post-flashover fires using water layer to give a WWSs a viable solution. WWS can provide fire resistance construction and the following possible fire protection. This concluded that WWS can provide both passive and active fire protection.
