11211918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211918.value: This project on WWS was proposed upon completing an earlier project funded by RGC-GRF on “The fire hazards of frameless glass systems in modern workplaces” from 2015-2018. All of the WWS results compiled from the bench-scale cone tests, medium-scale experiments and part of the full-scale model on fire behaviour were integrated. Based on the results of this project, fire protection of WWS on glass façade was recommended. Fire protection possibilities were considered in designing WWS. The inner glass pane facing room fire should be thinner and have higher conductivity than the outer glass. Adequate water flow should be provided at a smartly controlled rate once a fire is detected. Water supplied by breaking the inner glass pane would then be able to act on the fire. A total number of 3 journal papers were published. One of the journal papers appeared in journals in the first quartile (Q1) in Science Citation Index (SCI), Journal of Building Engineering. The other two journals are in SCI Q2, they are Indoor and Built Environment and Sustainability. Another journal paper was submitted for consideration to publish and 1 journal paper on full-scale burning tests on WWS is being drafted. All of the results of the three objectives were also compiled for drafting practical design guides on achieving fire-safe WWS. A summary of the innovative elements of the completed project is: • Mathematical modeling of fire performance of WWS. • Hazardous consequences of single façade used in buildings to be mitigated by WWS. • Assessing WWS using the bench-scale cone calorimeter tests, medium-scale tests and full-scale burning tests. • The WWS approach can provide adequate fire resistance rating values and active fire suppression. One PhD student working on parts of the tasks in this project was registered at CityU. The thesis was submitted in August 2021 working on thermal modeling of WWS based on the heat balance principle. The incorporated model was then utilised to assess the impact of WWS compared to a single skin glass façade on the annual building energy performance of office buildings. The fire performance of WWSs with varying water layer thicknesses was investigated experimentally. The thesis provides a feasibility evaluation of WWS for the integration of buildings in Hong Kong. The overall research exemplifies the convergence of diverse fields, including energy engineering, fire engineering, and life-cycle evaluation, to achieve an innovative green building solution.

11211918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211918.value: Integrating energy-efficient WWS with fire protection in large glazing areas is feasibly a smart and innovative concept in green building designs in the current project. Results of the project provide guidelines on viable design of WWS, including water layer and glass thickness, activation time and appropriate water flow rate to satisfy both its function as thermal energy storage and fire safety construction. Further development can be along the following areas: • More full-scale burning tests on WWS to observe new phenomena and validate the mathematical modelling results. • Drafting acceptance criteria for evaluating PBD-FEA projects on glass facades. • Results and recommendations from this project can be further integrated with the associated literature and existing overseas fire codes for drafting new codes on green building fires with the Hong Kong Fire Services Department and Buildings Department. • The fire protection concept can also be applied by integrating glass panes with vertical greenery system. This concept on WWS would be further considered to integrate with the energy harvest double-skin green façade system. Integrating green façade with WWS would be further developed on ‘fire-safe green façade’.

11211918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211918.value: The energy efficient green façade design, the water wall system (WWS), is shown to enhance fire safety in this completed project. Water stored in the system is also useful for fire suppression once the glass pane is broken during a fire. Thermal behaviour and fire protection possibilities of WWS were investigated through physical scale models, an analytical study of heat transfer through glass façades and full-scale burning tests. Mathematical models simulating heat transfer through glass panes and water layers during fires were developed. The heat removal rate achieved by the water layer was investigated. The predicted results were compared with the experimental results to understand how the WWS protects glass panes. Results compiled in this project are important in deciding acceptance criteria in evaluating performance-based design projects on glass façade. Further, codes and guidelines for protecting glass panes with WWS in buildings can be drafted based on the results of the present project. More importantly, WWS would facilitate better heat removal by supplying water with appropriate flow rate. As a summary, this design can provide both passive protection of adequate fire resistance and active suppression system. Fire-safe green architectural features with WWS be achieved.

11212018.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11212018.value: 關於機器類型通信的隨機接入問題的建模和優化

11212018.label: Project Objectives
11212018.value: To establish a unified and scalable analytical framework for random access of MTC; To characterize the fundamental limits of access performance of MTC, including delay-constrained and energy-constrained rate optimization; To design optimal access strategies for MTC by developing optimal tuning principles of access parameters and criteria for connection initialization and sensing.
rows: To establish a unified and scalable analytical framework for random access of MTC;
To characterize the fundamental limits of access performance of MTC, including delay-constrained and energy-constrained rate optimization;
To design optimal access strategies for MTC by developing optimal tuning principles of access parameters and criteria for connection initialization and sensing.

11212018.label: Realisation of objectives
11212018.value: All the proposed tasks have been successfully completed. 1. For Objective 1, a unified and scalable analytical framework for random access of Machine-Type Communications (MTC) was proposed in [1]. Different from the existing models, which either exclude the device-level input parameters by ignoring the queueing behavior of each Machine-Type Devices (MTD), or become unscalable in the massive access scenarios, a novel MTD-centric model was established, consisting of one request queue and one data queue for each MTD. By characterizing the state transition of each access request, explicit expressions of the network steady-state points can be obtained. The modeling complexity is independent of the number of MTDs even with the queueing behavior of each MTD taken into consideration, which is highly attractive in the massive access scenario. The proposed analytical framework lays a solid foundation for the successful accomplishment of Objectives 2 and 3. 2. For Objective 2, delay and energy constraints were further considered when optimizing the random access performance of MTDs. Two problems of interest are rate-constrained delay optimization and energy-constrained delay optimization. Both have important implications to practical low-latency applications of MTC. Within the proposed analytical framework, various performance metrics, including the throughput, moments of access delay, effective data rate of each MTD can all be evaluated and optimized in a unified manner. Fundamental tradeoffs can therefore be characterized. For rate-constrained delay optimization, for instance, it is found that to minimize the mean access delay, the transmission probability of each MTD should be reduced as the network size increases, leading to a diminishing effective data rate. To achieve the minimum mean access delay for a certain data rate requirement for each MTD, the transmission probability and the information encoding rate of each MTD should be jointly optimized. When the energy constraint is further taken into consideration, the sleeping counter is found to be a key parameter that determines a fundamental tradeoff between lifetime and delay performance, i.e., a larger counter value leads to better delay performance but shorter lifetime for each MTD. For energy-constrained delay optimization, the access parameters should be carefully tuned based on the traffic input rates to optimize the delay performance and meanwhile ensure that each MTD’s lifetime is above a certain threshold. 3. For Objective 3, the effects of two core features of random access, sensing and connection establishment, were examined to see if they are appropriate for MTC. For the first part, the optimal rate performance of sensing-based random access and sensing-free random access, popularly known as Carrier Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) and Aloha, respectively, was compared to establish criteria for beneficial sensing. For the second part, the optimal throughput performance of packet-based random access and connection-based random access was compared to characterize criteria for beneficial connection establishment. The analysis has important implications for optimal access design for MTC. For instance, the throughput and rate comparison of Aloha and CSMA suggests that for MTC where a large amount of low-power MTDs send short packets, sensing could be undesirable as Aloha may achieve better throughput and sum rate performance than CSMA. Whether connection establishment is beneficial also crucially depends on the sensing capability. For given overhead parameters, the connection-establishment threshold of CSMA is found to be much higher than that of Aloha, which suggests that benefits of connection establishment are more pronounced when MTDs have no sensing capability.

11212018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212018.value: A unified and scalable analytical framework for random access of Machine-Type Communications (MTC) was proposed in [1], within which various performance metrics of different random access schemes can be analyzed and optimized. It has been successfully applied to cellular networks and WiFi networks for optimizing the throughput [1], delay [2] and sum rate [5]-[6] performance of MTDs. Rate-constrained delay optimization was further considered in [7], and the effects of sensing and connection establishment on the optimal access performance were analyzed in [3]-[4]. The major findings can be summarized into two parts: 1. Based on the proposed analytical framework, the access performance of MTDs can be optimized by properly tuning the access parameters. In [1]-[2], for instance, the maximum access throughput and minimum mean access delay were derived, respectively. In [7], the data rate requirement of each MTD was further taken into consideration when optimizing the delay performance, where the transmission probability and information encoding rate need to be jointly tuned. The analysis shows that by optimally tuning the access parameters, the minimum mean access delay linearly increases with the number of MTDs, which is in sharp contrast to the exponential growth of mean access delay when the access parameters are fixed. It indicates that adaptive tuning of access parameters is indispensable for massive access of MTC. 2. For the optimal access design of MTC, it is important to understand in what conditions sensing and connection establishment are beneficial. The analysis in [3] shows that that the mini-slot length, i.e., the ratio of the sensing time to the packet length, should be sufficiently small for CSMA to outperform Aloha. The mini-slot length thresholds of throughput and sum rate are characterized, and found to be close to zero at the low SNR region when the capture model is adopted. In [4], the threshold of data packet transmission time for beneficial connection establishment was obtained, and found to be crucially dependent on the sensing capability. With sensing, the threshold is quite large, indicating that the connection-based access mechanism may rarely be activated for MTC featured with small packet size. Without sensing, in contrast, the analysis shows that connection establishment can be beneficial for any packet payload length if the overhead parameters satisfy a certain constraint. It suggests that for Aloha-based LTE networks, when properly designed, connection-based random access protocols may be preferred over packet-based ones for MTC.

11212018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212018.value: The findings of this project have stimulated a number of interesting topics for future research. From the theoretical perspective, the comparisons of connection-free and connection-based random access, as well as sensing-free and sensing-based random access were mainly performed on the optimal throughput and sum rate performance. For low-latency MTC applications, the delay performance is of more interest. It is therefore important to extend the comparative study to the delay perspective, where the slot length needs to be further optimized. Moreover, for monitoring and data measurement applications, the age-of-information (AoI) could be a more pertinent performance metric. Adaptive tuning of access parameters for optimizing AoI deserves much attention in the future study. From the practical perspective, new features have been introduced into the random access protocols of 5G and WiFi 6 networks, which can be incorporated into the proposed analytical framework. The modeling and optimization approaches developed in this project may find wide applications in practical random-access based networks, and provide important insights for the optimal access design of MTC in future networks.

11212018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212018.value: With the growing popularity of the Internet of Things and rapid proliferation of MTDs, MTC is expected to become the dominant communications paradigm in the near future. When facilitating the massive access of MTDs, the existing random access protocols were found to be highly inefficient. Yet due to the lack of scalable and accurate models, how to optimize the random access performance of MTC was little understood. In this project, a unified and scalable analytical framework was established for random access of MTC, where key features of MTC such as a massive number, small packet payload, and diverse QoS requirements can be incorporated. With the proposed framework, fundamental limits of access performance, their tradeoffs and the corresponding optimal tuning of access parameters were characterized. Effects of key factors such as receiver design, sensing capability, and connection establishment on the optimal access performance were also analyzed. The proposed theoretical framework was successfully applied to practical networks such as WiFi networks and cellular networks. The results provide important guidance on the optimal access protocol design for MTC, and demonstrate significant performance gains over the current standards.

11212518.label: Project Objectives

11212518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212518.value: Automatic crowd counting in images has important real-world applications in security, crowd management, urban planning, and retail. For example, in retail, shopper counts could be used to plan staffing schedules to maximize sales and minimize staffing cost, while counts on an MTR subway platform can help managers to improve customer experience and safety. One of the most effective methods for crowd counting is based on crowd-density maps, where summing over a region in the density map yields the count. Current methods have focused on counting from a single camera view of a scene using deep CNNs, and have shown good generalization ability across scenes. However, because of the limited field-of-view of a single camera, single-view counting cannot be applied to wide-area or irregularly-shaped venues (e.g., public parks, event spaces, subway platforms), which are increasingly important places for security control and crowd management in Hong Kong. In this project, we research crowd counting using multiple camera views (i.e., a camera network) to improve its accuracy and applicability to wide-area venues. We formulate our research problem within the context of the inherent challenges of collecting and processing image streams from camera networks in the real-world. First, we assume that bandwidth and computational resources only allow images (and not video) to be transmitted from the camera network and analyzed. Second, we assume that the cameras are loosely synchronized in time, i.e., images are captured roughly at the same time within some temporal threshold (e.g., 3 seconds), which allows situations where precise time synchronization is not possible (e.g., panning cameras). Third, to be deployable in the real-world, the model should generalize across scenes without re-training. Under the above multi-view cross-scene setting, we propose two deep learning architectures that fuse multiple camera views to predict a single density map for the whole scene. We extend our model to handle loosely synchronized images, as well as fine-grain counting where the crowd count is further divided into attributes, such as facing direction and movement type. To train and test our models, we will collect a large-scale dataset for multi-view crowd-counting. The proposed research enables large-scale and wide-area crowd counting of public areas (e.g., subway platforms, public squares, streets, public events), which are of significant interest to Hong Kong due to its large and dense population. The project will also further research in multi-camera fusion methods with deep learning, while the collected dataset will be a benchmark for future work. 圖像自動人群計數（crowd counting）在真實世界中有著重要的應用，諸如安保，人群管理，城市規劃和零售業。譬如在商店中，購物人數可以用來規劃員工的工作安排，以最大化銷量和最小化員工成本。又例如在港鐵地鐵月臺上的人數可以幫助管理者提升乘客的乘坐體驗和安全性。 最有效的人群計數方式之一是基於人群密度圖（density map）的。在基於人群密度圖的方法中，密度圖某一部分的加和即為對應區域的人群數。現今的方法多關注基於深度卷積神經網路（CNN）的單個相機下的人群計數問題。並且此類方法也表現出了較好的跨場景通用能力。然而，由於單個相機覆蓋的視角區域（FOV）有限，單視角的計數方法不能直接應用到大範圍或者形狀不規則的區域（如公園，集會場地，地鐵月臺等）。而在香港，這些區域正越來越需要安全管控和人群管理。 在這一項目中，我們的研究是通過使用多相機視角（相機網路）來提升大範圍人群計數的準確性和可用性。實際相機網路中圖像流資料的收集和處理有著很多內在挑戰。我們的研究問題是在面臨著這些挑戰的背景下制定的。首先，我們假設頻寬與計算資源是有限的，只能傳輸和分析相機網路中的圖像（而非視頻）。其次，我們假設各個相機在時間上是近似同步的，各個相機間的同步誤差在一個較小的閾值內（比如3秒）。這一假設考慮了相機無法精確同步的情形（如掃描式監控相機）。其三，為了能在真實世界中有著可拓展性，模型應該能夠具有跨場景通用能力而無需再訓練。 在以上的多視角跨場景限制下，我們提出兩種可以融合多視角並獲取整個場景的密度圖的深度學習結構。我們將這一模型拓展到處理近似同步的圖像，以及細粒度計數（fine-grain counting）上。其中，細粒度計數是指將人群數目依據不同屬性予以進一步劃分，如臉部朝向、運動類型等。為了訓練和測試我們的模型，我們將收集一個適用于多視角人群計數的大規模資料集。 本文所提出的研究將促進大規模和大範圍公共區域下人群計數問題的解決（如地鐵站，公共廣場，街道，公開集會等）。考慮到香港人口眾多而密集，這一研究對香港社會有著重大意義。這一項目將同時提升基於深度學習的多相機融合方法的研究，而且所收集的資料集也將成為未來研究工作的測試基準。

11212518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212518.value: Improving the performance/accuracy of multi-view counting is still an ongoing task. Future work can also consider performing crowd localization using multi-view images, or multi-view detection of people in the crowd. Since collecting and annotating large crowd datasets is tedious and time-consuming, another area of interest is semi-supervised crowd counting, where only a few annotated images and a larger set of unannotated images are used for model training.

11212518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212518.value: In this project, we develop a system for counting people in large areas, like concert halls, markets, and parks. The system uses multiple cameras to view different parts of the scene from different angles, and then fuses this information to show the density of crowd in the ground-plane map of the scene. Crowd counting can be used for numerous applications, such as safety and crowd management, personnel allocation, and emergency event detection.

11213018.label: Realisation of objectives
11213018.value: In this project, quasi-three-dimensional (3D) and 3D plasmonic photonic crystal (PPC) nanostructures with point-defect cavities were developed and fabricated using direct and reversal nanoimprint lithography. Quasi-3D plasmonic nanoholes were fabricated using the silane-treated intermediate polymer stamp (IPS) soft stamp. TU-7 nanosquares with the width, pitch, and depth of 280, 535, and 500 nm, respectively, were first imprinted on a PMMA-coated Si substrate, then dry etched to the bottom layer. Symmetrical and asymmetrical Cr nanoholes were formed on Si through the normal and 10° tilt angle evaporation of 20 nm Cr and lift-off, respectively. Subsequently, symmetrical and asymmetrical Cr nanoholes were used as masks to etch the Si substrate with a deep reactive ion etching system. Symmetrical and asymmetrical quasi-3D Si nanohole stamps were replicated onto the IPS soft stamps. Using the soft stamp could enable contamination control and prevent damage to the master Si stamp. Symmetrical quasi-3D nanoholes were 350 nm in diameter, 535 nm in pitch, and 350 nm in depth. Asymmetrical quasi-3D nanoholes had radii of 350 nm, pitch of 535 nm, and depth of 350 nm. Finally, 2 nm Cr and 20 nm Au films were thermally evaporated on these quasi-3D nanostructures to form two different plasmonic layers. The 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities were fabricated by stacking SU-8 nanosquares on top of quasi-3D SU-8 nanoholes through reversal nanoimprint lithography. SU-8 polymer was used instead of TU-7 because SU-8 showed better adhesion than TU-7 after cross-linking. The top nanosquares and bottom quasi-3D nanoholes had the same hexagonal arrangement and pitch. Photonic crystals with point-defect cavities could be generated by stacking SU-8 nanosquares on top of the quasi-3D nanoholes because the diameters of the nanosquares are smaller than those of nanoholes. The nanosquares directly on top of the nanoholes were removed because they lacked contact surfaces. 2 nm Cr and 20 nm Au films were thermally evaporated to generate the 3D PPC biosensor with three different plasmonic layers. No metallic films were deposited on the sidewalls of the 3D nanostructures because the metal films were evaporated at low pressure with a long mean free path, and the total film thickness was small. Using the hybrid coupling of localized surface plasmon resonance and Fabry–Perot cavity modes, the quasi-3D plasmonic nanoholes showed higher electromagnetic field intensity and sensitivity than the 2D plasmonic nanoholes. Specifically, the sensitivity of the quasi-3D plasmonic nanoholes was 483 nm/refractive index unit (RIU), whereas that of the 2D plasmonic nanoholes was 276 nm/RIU. In addition, by enhancing the EM field intensity around corners and generating an additional subradiant dark mode, the symmetrical breakage of the quasi-3D plasmonic nanoholes further increased sensitivity to 946 nm/RIU. Among all the nanostructures developed in the study, the 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities showed the highest sensitivity up to 1,376 nm/RIU and the highest figure of merit (FOM) of 11.6 as the result of the hybrid coupling of plasmonics and photonic crystal modes with multilayered plasmonic nanostructures. The spacing between the 3D PPC nanostructures was comparable with the average size of exosomes derived from fibroblast L cells, which allowed the exosomes to spread around the 3D PPC nanostructures with an increased sensing area. This effect further enhanced the detection sensitivity with a large peak shift of 9 nm when using the 3D PPC biosensor to detect exosomes at the concentration of 1 × 10^4 particles/ml, and the peak shift increased to 102 nm as exosome concentration increased to 1 × 10^11 particles/ml. We systematically investigated quasi-3D and 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities. Compared with those of the 2D Au nanoholes, the EM field intensity and sensitivity of the quasi-3D Au nanoholes increased through the hybrid coupling of LSPR and Fabry–Perot cavity modes. At 1,406 nm, the symmetrical quasi-3D Au nanoholes exhibited a sensitivity of 483 nm/RIU. In addition, the symmetry breakage of the quasi-3D Au nanoholes could further increase sensitivity to 946 nm/RIU by enhancing EM field intensity around corners and by generating an additional quadrupole plasmon mode, which is a dark subradiant mode. The 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities showed the highest sensitivity of 1,376 nm/RIU for the resonance peak at 1,232 nm and the highest FOM of 11.6 for the resonance peak at 564 nm. These results are attributed to the hybrid plasmonic and photonic crystal modes in the 3D plasmonic nanostructures. The detection sensitivity of the 3D PPC biosensor increased because the 3D nanostructures increase the sensing area of fibroblast L cell-derived exosomes, allowing even a very low concentration of exosomes to be detected successfully.

11213018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213018.value: Various designs including two-dimensional (2D), quasi-three-dimensional (3D), and 3D plasmonic photonic crystal (PPC) nanostructures with point-defect cavities were developed and fabricated using direct and reversal nanoimprint lithography. The asymmetrical 2D Au nanoholes showed two resonance peaks at 661 and 814 nm that were attributed to surface plasmon polaritons and localized surface plasmon resonance. The measured sensitivity of the resonance peak at 814 nm was 276 nm/RIU. In addition, by enhancing electromagnetic field intensity around corners and generating an additional subradiant dark mode, the symmetrical breakage of the quasi-3D plasmonic nanoholes further increased sensitivity to 946 nm/RIU. To further increase the sensitivity of plasmonic biosensors, we have developed novel 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities to confine and enhance the electromagnetic (EM) field intensity through the hybrid coupling of plasmonic and photonic crystal modes. The sensitivity of these novel nanostructures increased to 1,376 nm/RIU for the resonance peak at 1,232 nm. Moreover, these nanostructures exhibited a high figure of merit of 11.6 for the resonance peak at 564 nm. The spacing between the 3D PPC nanostructures was comparable with the average size of exosomes derived from fibroblast L cells, which allowed the exosomes to spread around the 3D PPC nanostructures with an increased sensing area. The 3D PPC biosensor was used to detect 10 µl of fibroblast L cell-derived exosomes with concentrations of 1 × 10^4 – 1 × 10^11 particles/ml and exhibited a large peak shift of 9 nm during the detection of 1 × 10^4 particles/ml exosomes at very low concentration. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first investigation of 3D PPC nanostructures with point-defect cavities fabricated through reversal nanoimprint lithography and their application in quantitative exosome detection.

11213018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213018.value: Cancer cells often release more exosomes compared to normal cells, and they could be used as biomarkers related to cancer development. However, capturing and detecting exosomes is challenging due to their small size and low buoyant density. The three-dimensional (3D) plasmonic biosensors developed in this project have high sensitivity to detect low concentration exosomes. This sensor array can be integrated with electrodes and nanogratings in a microfluidic platform for effectively capturing and detecting exosomes. Together with the 3D plasmonic biosensors that function with hybrid coupling of the Fano resonance and Fabry-Perot cavity modes, it is expected that exosomes can be captured and detected at very low concentrations. The microsystem with high sensitivity biosensors will be useful for the early detection of tumors.

11213018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213018.value: We have designed and developed three-dimensional (3D) plasmonic biosensors with high sensitivity to capture and detect low concentration exosomes. Exosomes could be used as cancer biomarkers but they are difficult to detect due to their small size and low concentration. Through the design of the 3D nanostructures, the electromagnetic field intensity was enhanced and additional quadrupole plasmon and photonic crystal modes were generated. The 3D plasmonic photonic crystal nanostructures with point-defect cavities had been demonstrated to provide the highest sensitivity of 1,376 nm/RIU and the highest figure of merit of 11.6. These biosensors could detect exosomes at a very low concentration, which will be important for early disease diagnostics and treatments.

11213118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213118.value: Fe-based metallic glasses (MGs) are an important engineering material because of their superior soft magnetic properties. As compared to the traditional soft magnetic crystalline alloys, such as Fe-Si, soft magnetic Fe-based metallic glasses possess higher electric resistance and lower coercive force, thereby leading to extremely low energy loss when they are used for making the next generation of transformer cores. In addition, Fe-based metallic glasses have extraordinary strengths (2-4 GPa) and superior wear resistance. In view of such combination of structural and functional properties of the Fe-based metallic glasses, the central governments worldwide have recently made tremendous investments in the production of the soft magnetic metallic glasses. However, high performing Fe-based metallic glasses are generally brittle at the ambient condition because of a trade-off between magnetization saturation and plasticity. At the current time, this becomes the main roadblock that hurdles their industrial applications. Based on our previous research on metallic glasses, we herein propose several strategies in this proposal to mitigate the room-temperature brittleness in the soft-magnetic metallic glasses without sacrificing their magnetization saturation. These include the carefully selected chemical composition, which leads to a dual-phase amorphous structure, and the use of the recently developed processing methods which enable us to control the rejuvenation and relaxation of metallic glasses over an extended range that is impossible to achieve with the traditional rapid cooling method. In addition, we also design multi-scale experiments to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the brittleness-to-plasticity transition in our dual-phase Fe-based metallic glasses. Once funded, the outcome of our project is expected (1) to help people understand the origin of plasticity in the dual-phase metallic glasses, (2) to provide protocols that can improve the quality of soft-magnetic metallic glasses, and (3) to promote the use of metallic glasses in the energy industries that play a pivotal role to the societal and economic growth in mainland China and Hong Kong. 由于其优越的软磁性能，铁基金属玻璃是一种重要的工程材料。与传统的软磁晶体合金相比,软磁铁基金属玻璃具有较高的电阻和较低的矫顽力, 从而导致极低的能量损耗, 非常适合用于制造下一代的变压器。此外, 铁基金属玻璃具有优异的耐磨性和硬度。鉴于此, 世界各国最近对软磁性金属玻璃的研发进行了巨大的投资。然而, 由于饱和磁化强度和塑性之间存在的矛盾, 高性能的铁基金属玻璃在室温环境条件下通常是脆性的。目前, 这成为阻碍其工业应用的主要障碍。本项课题主要是研究如何在不牺牲饱和磁化强度的前提下减轻软磁金属玻璃室温脆性。

11213118.label: Realisation of objectives
11213118.value: With respect to objective 1, master ingots with the nominal atomic composition of Fe80(Si2B9P3C1)19.25/17Cu0.75 (designated as “Fe80” hereafter) and Fe84.5(Si2B9P3C1)14.75/17Cu0.75 (or “Fe84.5”) were prepared by induction melting in a high vacuum Ar atmosphere. Ribbon samples with width of 1mm and thickness of 20 μm were prepared by re-melting the master ingots through single roller melt-spinning method. The resulting metallic glass ribbons were vacuum-sealed in a quartz tube and then inserted into a preheated tube furnace with a high vacuum of 5×10^(-3) Pa for isothermal annealing. According to the differential scanning calorimetry results, the optimum annealing temperature for synthesizing Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys is around 30 °C above Tp (peak of crystallization temperature). Therefore, based on their crystallization temperature, we chose 480°C and 440 °C as the annealing temperature for Fe80 and Fe84.5 respectively in this study. After the iso-thermal annealing for different durations (up to 96 min), the amorphous nanocrystalline alloys were water quenched to retain their nanostructures, which were then characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). In addition, atom probe tomography (APT) analyses were performed to characterize the nano-scale chemical distribution. With respect to Objective 2, isothermal annealing was carried out in a high vacuum tube furnace at 4200C for different time followed by water-quenching to synthesize the nanocrystalline alloys. The magnetic properties, including saturation magnetic flux density (Bs), coercivity (Hc) and effective permeability (me) were measured with vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM, Lake Shore 7410) under the field of 800 kA/m, B-H loop tracer (EXPH-100) under the field of 800 A/m and impedance analyzer (Agilent 4294 A) under different applied magnetic field, respectively. The mechanical behavior of the Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys was investigated via micropillar compression, which were performed at displacement control and at the nominal strain rate of s-1 on the Hysitron™ nanoindentation system. Micropillars were fabricated following the sequential ion milling method using the focused ion beam (FIB) system. These micropillars had a taper angle less than 2 °, an aspect ratio of 2-3 and an average diameter around 3 ± 0.2 μm in order to avoid a possible size effect and data scattering. To reveal the deformation and fracture mechanisms, post-deformed micropillars were sectioned with FIB and subsequently examined with TEM. Strain-rate sensitivity of these Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys was also measured using strain rate jump nanoindentation. With respect to objective 3, we discovered a ductile-brittle-ductile transition in the Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys through a systematical study of their yielding and plastic deformation behavior over a wide range of volume fraction of nanocrystals. Afterwards, we developed a micromechanical and thermodynamics model to understand the mechanism of yielding and the unusual ductile-brittle-ductile transition which is induced by the controlled crystallization. Based on our current studies, salient conclusions can be drawn as follows: Our amorphous nanocrystalline alloys contain relatively strong nanocrystalline phase and weak amorphous intergranular phase. The overall yielding is caused by the intergranular amorphous phase and this yielding behavior is analogous to grain boundary mediated plasticity commonly observed in nanocrystalline alloys with ultra-small grains. The reduction in the yield strain observed in our Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys is due to the tensile residual stress that originates from the thermal expansion misfit between the amorphous and nanocrystalline phases. Three deformation types, i.e. shear banding, shear-induced cracking and distributed plasticity, were observed in our Fe-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys. According to our model, the transition of the three is controlled essentially by the critical void size (r*) and the thickness () of the intergranular amorphous phase. To determine these two lengths, there is a rather complicated interplay among the mechanical, thermal and kinetic properties of glasses, crystals and liquids, as seen in our theoretical modeling. With respect to objective 4, we developed a processing route to optimize the mechanical properties of the dual-phase Fe-based metallic glass. To facilitate the processing of Fe-based metallic glass ribbon samples, we developed an ultrasound enabled joining approach to synthesize bulk sized metallic glasses. This method allows us to fabricate single or multiple amorphous phases through the activation of the ultra-fast surface atoms. In contrast to conventional monolithic Fe-based metallic glasses, Fe-based metallic glasses with multiple phases and microstructures could be designed based on our current method. We also proposed a novel strategy to enlarge the processing window of high saturation magnetization nanocrystalline alloys (HBNAs) by annealing the partially crystallized precursor Fe-based ribbons via a heterostructured crystallization process. To verify this approach, and to investigate the heterostructured crystallization mechanism with quenched-in crystals, Fe84.75Si2B9P3C0.5Cu0.75 (at.%) alloy ribbons with different thickness were obtained by controlling the spinning rate, and the nanostructure evolution of these as-quenched ribbons were comparatively studied from both the free surface and middle layer. The main conclusions are as follows: Surface crystallization occurs in the low spinning rate ribbons, resulting in the formation of small amount quenched-in crystals in the free surface. Decreasing the spinning rate and avoiding the formation of quenched-in coarse nanocrystallites in precursor ribbons is an effective way to enlarge the processing window and obtain excellent soft-magnetic properties. The quenched-in crystals/clusters smaller than critical size will not grow to coarse grains due to the competitive grain growth and shielding effect from metalloid elements rich interlayer. The heterostructured evolution of the ribbons with quenched-in crystals/clusters has little effect on the uniformity of the nanostructure, since the grains grow to some extent will be retarded and arrested by the shielding and overlapping of the solute-enriched diffusion layers.

11213118.value: We published 12 papers, obtained 1 US patent and trained 1 PhD student with the support of this project over the past years. We studied the deformation mechanisms in high magnetization nanocrystalline Fe-based alloys which can be obtained by fully or partially crystalizing Fe-based metallic glass ribbons. In addition, we also invented a method to fabricate freestanding ultrathin Fe-based metals

11213118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213118.value: In order to further enhance the properties of amorphous -nanocrystalline Fe-based alloys, one promising route is to use generative machine learning models that enable customized alloy design. Our group is working on that and has achieved some promising results on Zr- and Cu-based metallic glasses. Our plan is to extend our machine learning work to Fe-based metallic glasses.

11213518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213518.value: Many applications, such as security and surveillance, environmental monitoring, and intelligent transportation, cannot be easily achieved by a single dynamic system platform if not impossible. A number of single dynamic systems, cooperating with each other through a communication network, are often needed for such applications. Examples of such systems, usually called multi-agent systems, include mobile robot groups, unmanned air vehicle teams, and wireless sensor networks. Each single dynamic system in the group/network is called a subsystem or an agent. In the past two decades, controlling each subsystem to support the cooperative and coordinated behavior of the entire system via distributed control strategies has been a focus in the robotics and control systems communities. The distributed control approach uses only local information. In recent years, controlling each subsystem with intermittent communication, instead of continuous communication, has become equally important. Researchers including the PI have been studying both problems intensively. However, most control strategies developed share a fundamental need to use either some global information about the entire system or continuous communication between neighboring agents, which inevitably leads to excessive consumption of the energy and communication resources. The main objective of this project is to develop a framework for handling the cooperative control problem of multi-agent systems with resources constraints via a fully distributed control strategy. Specifically, this project aims to develop novel adaptive distributed control laws, design aperiodic sampling and communication mechanisms, and conduct stability and consensus analysis of the closed-loop multi-agent systems with different agent dynamics, static or switching communication topologies, parameter uncertainties, and/or external disturbances. In this framework, with the novel adaptive distributed control strategies and well-designed aperiodic sampling and communication mechanisms, no global information will be needed, and information between neighboring agents will be exchanged only when certain conditions are satisfied. In such a way, it is expected that robustness, adaptivity, and efficiency of the closed-loop multi-agent systems will be significantly enhanced. The study will rely on several tools from algebraic graph theory, matrix analysis, and control theory. The developed control strategies will be consolidated and validated via their application to mobile robot formation control. The results from this project will overcome many theoretical hurdles to meet the demanding challenges facing multi-agent systems in real applications. In particular, the results will improve not only the multi-agent systems’ resilience to communication loss and hardware failure, but also their utilization efficiency of energy and communication resources. 為實現安全監視、環境監測和智能交通等眾多應用，往往需要多個動力系統通過通信網絡相互協同。這種系統通常被稱為多智能體系統，常見的例子包括移動機器人群組、無人機隊伍和無線傳感器網絡。此類系統中的單個動力系統被稱為子系統或者智能體。在過去的二十年里，為支持整個系統的協同和協調行為，通過分佈式策略控制每個子系統已經成為機器人和控制系統領域的焦點。近幾年，通過間歇式通信而不是連續通信控制每個子系統也成為另一研究熱點。然而，大部分已構建的控制策略都需要利用關於整個系統的全局信息或者相鄰智能體間的連續通信，這不可避免地導致能量和通信資源的過量消耗。本項目的主要目標是通過完全分佈式控制策略構建一個處理資源受限的多智能體系統的協同控制問題的框架。具體來講，本項目旨在構建新穎的自適應分佈式控制律、設計非週期採樣和通信機制。所提出的框架利用新穎的自適應分佈式控制策略以及精心設計的非週期採樣和通信機制，將不需要全局信息，且僅當一定條件滿足時才會交換相鄰智能體間的信息。採用這種方式，閉環多智能體系統的魯棒性、適應性和效率將會大幅提升。本項目的成果將不僅提高多智能體系統對通信損失和硬件故障的抵禦能力，而且提高它們對能量和通信資源的利用效率。

11213518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213518.value: First, the cooperative output regulation problems of multi-agent systems have been addressed by event-triggered control protocols. The event-triggered control method enables agents to exchange information only when necessary, and the agents involved then update their controllers accordingly. In the cooperative output regulation problem, the exosystem is used to generate both the reference input and the external disturbance for each agent. First, a fully distributed event-triggered control framework has been designed to deal with the concerned problem of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems. Meanwhile, a fully distributed event-triggering mechanism is proposed such that each agent can determine when to broadcast its information. Then, this framework is extended to handle cooperative control problems for several kinds of multi-agent systems. For example, by incorporating the model reference adaptive control method, the proposed event-triggered control protocol has been extended to handle unknown linear agent dynamics. Moreover, the event-triggered cooperative control of uncertain Euler-Lagrange systems has also been studied using the adaptive fuzzy control method. At last, switching communication topologies have also been considered. Then, cooperative control problems subject to quantized measurement and delays have been studied. As a foundation, the research on single systems has been considered. First, the robust output regulation problem of uncertain linear agents subject to limited measurement information has been studied. A novel dynamic quantized control law together with a hybrid quantized feedback control policy has been developed. Then, the stability and stabilization of infinite delay systems have also been studied. In the research, several new Lyapunov theorems for uniform asymptotical stability and exponential stability of delayed systems have been established. At last, the consensus problem of multi-agent systems subject to delays and uncertainties has been solved by distributed control protocols using the abovementioned techniques. Finally, the optimal coverage control problem for a network of mobile sensors on a circle has been investigated. This problem has potential applications including search and rescue by networked multi-robot systems and environmental monitoring using wireless sensor networks. The coverage cost function is defined as the largest arrival time from the mobile sensor network to any point on the circle. Both single-integrator and double-integrator systems have been considered. Distributed coverage control laws have been developed for mobile sensors using the estimated difference. Under the control laws, the sensor network can be driven to the optimal position, and the effect of the measurement errors and velocity constraints on the coverage performance can be handled.

11213518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213518.value: Several results have been obtained and published on the cooperative control for multi-agent systems subject to limited communication resources, quantized measurement, system uncertainties, and delays. At the same time, many intriguing problems in cooperative control of multi-agent systems are identified. For example, during our investigation into the event-triggered cooperative control problem of multi-agent systems, we found that there exist few results considering communication delays when utilizing event-triggered communication among agents. It is hoped that the proposed approaches can provide a deeper understanding and inspire solutions for cooperative control problems under more complex communication constraints. It has been one of our recent interests and could be one of our future research focuses.

11213518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213518.value: Several fundamental problems in cooperative control for multiple dynamic systems under various practical constraints have been studied. Several effective control protocols have been proposed, which can be applied to solve some typical cooperative control problems, such as consensus, formation, and synchronization. One typical example is tracking control of uncertain networked robotic systems subject to resource constraints. Limited communication bandwidths, uncertainties in system dynamics, and delays are all inevitable in real applications and thus should be considered. In this project, event-triggered cooperative control protocols for multiple uncertain linear and nonlinear systems in various practical settings have been addressed. Several challenging issues, such as Zeno behavior, system uncertainties, unknown agent dynamics, and measurement errors have been tackled. The developed techniques and approaches will benefit both academic research and practical engineering applications in cooperative control of multiple dynamical systems. The expected outcomes of this project will advance the current state of cooperative control research and provide a wider scope of applications for the coordination of multiple mobile robots under more practical situations.

11213618.label: Project Objectives
11213618.value: To investigate the nonlinear integrated optical waveguide structures with embedded microstructures consists of highly nonlinear materials, in particular a-Si, SiN and Si-nanocrystal. Critical linear characteristics such as loss, optical mode confinement and propagation constant, along with nonlinear parameters, such as nonlinear phase shift, effective area and gamma will be determined and with their performance compared. To fabricate and characterize highly doped glass waveguide embedded with microstructures composed of highly nonlinear materials for the enhancement of the waveguide nonlinear properties with the goal of a ten-fold improvement of the nonlinear parameters of these waveguides compare with the highly doped glass waveguides without the strip-loaded layer. To design and fabricate optimized nonlinear integrated optical waveguide structure that serves as the building blocks of all optical signal processing device. In particular, structures such as microring resonators and long spiral waveguides that will utilize their nonlinear phenomena for potential applications will be developed.

11213618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213618.value: Complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) compatible nonlinear integrated optical circuits that provide all-optical signal generation and processing offer low cost and low power consumption signal processing capabilities. In high speed applications, they can be far superior then their electronics counterparts. Over the past decade, we have witnessed an array of impressive nonlinear optics achievements with these integrated nonlinear optical circuits ranging from the demonstration of fundamental nonlinear effects to more sophisticated applications [1-7]. Recently, these nonlinear circuits have also shown promises in the field of quantum information with the demonstration of heralded photon sources and QuDits [8-10]. Among the various platforms for nonlinear integrated optical circuits, silicon photonic circuits (SiP) [11-14] initiated the field and has led the research over the years due to the extremely high nonlinearity of silicon and optical confinement in silicon nanowire waveguides. However, with the realization of high nonlinear loss of silicon waveguides in the telecom band it has dampened the enthusiasm of using SiP components in nonlinear application in the telecom band. Besides SiP, there exists other promising CMOS compatible nonlinear integrated optical circuit platforms that the nonlinear optics society is pursuing, two such platforms are the silicon nitride (SiN) and high-index doped silica glass [15,16]. In particular, the SiN platform have drawn immense attention due to the recently reported result of nonlinear enhancement from process improvement [17]. In parallel, the high-index doped silica glass platform has made tremendous stride in quantum optics with the recent demonstrations of multiphoton entanglement and QuDit [9,10]. Although the nonlinearity of high-index doped silica glass is substantially lower than silicon or SiN, It processes one of the highest intrinsic nonlinear figure of merit, the ratio between the nonlinear phase shift and nonlinear absorption coefficient, than among all the CMOS compatible platforms due to its low linear and nonlinear losses [16]. The proposed research will focus on enhancing the nonlinearity optical effect in high-index doped silica glasses waveguides while maintaining its low-loss property for a high efficient nonlinear integrated optical circuit platforms. High-index doped silica glasses waveguides with embedded microstructures that consists of highly nonlinear materials, such as SiN or Si-nanocrystal, will be developed for the improvement in optical confinement, waveguide nonlinearity, and dispersion design flexibility. The proposed research plan is focused on building the foundation of this technology to support future research and innovation in all-optical signal and quantum processing circuits. 互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）兼容的非線性集成光學電路提供全光信號生成和處理，提供低成本和低功耗的信號處理能力。在高速應用中，它們遠遠優於電子產品。在過去十年中，我們目睹了一系列令人印象深刻的非線性光學成就，這些集成非線性光學電路從基本非線性效應的演示到更複雜的應用。最近，這些非線性電路也在量子信息領域展示了前景，並展示了預示光子源和QuDits。 在非線性集成光學電路的各種平台中，矽光子電路（SiP) 引發了該領域，並且由於矽納米線波導中矽的極高非線性和光學限制，多年來一直引領著這項研究。然而，隨著電信頻帶中矽波導的高非線性損耗的實現，它削弱了在電信頻帶中非線性應用中使用SiP元件的熱情。 除SiP外，還存在非線性光學學會所追求的其他有前景的CMOS兼容非線性集成光路平台，其中兩個平台是氮化矽（SiN）和高折射率摻雜石英玻璃。特別是，由於最近報導的過程改進非線性增強的結果，SiN平台引起了極大的關注。與此同時，高指數摻雜石英玻璃平台在量子光學方面取得了巨大進步，最近有多光子糾纏和QuDit演示[9,10]。雖然高折射率摻雜石英玻璃的非線性遠低於矽或SiN，但它處理的是非線性相位和非線性吸收係數之間的最高內在非線性品質因數之一，而不是所有CMOS兼容平台之間的比例。它的低線性和非線性損耗[16]。 所提出的研究將集中於增強高折射率摻雜石英玻璃波導中的非線性光學效應，同時保持其對於高效非線性集成光學電路平台的低損耗特性。將開發具有嵌入式微結構的高折射率摻雜二氧化矽玻璃波導，其由高度非線性材料（例如SiN或Si納米晶體）組​​成，以改善光學限制，波導非線性和色散設計靈活性。擬議的研究計劃側重於構建該技術的基礎，以支持全光信號和量子處理電路的未來研究和創新。

11213618.label: Realisation of objectives
11213618.value: The main objective of the project is to investigate how the nonlinear optical properties of the high-index contrast integrated optical waveguide can be enhanced with embedding microstructures are composed of a separate material. Among the many effects that affect the nonlinear optics properties of the optical waveguide, this project focused on the enhancement of the nonlinear phase shift parameter gamma and on the engineering of the waveguide dispersion for nonlinear applications. We are please to report that at the completion of the project, we have achieved our main objective and resulted in producing one journal publication and two conference publications from the results of this project. It is worth mention that the journal publication was selected as an Editor’s Pick. Regarding our first objective, we have fabricated a number of optical waveguide structures with various embedded microstructures and developed the experimental procedures for the characterization of the waveguide nonlinearity and dispersion. For microstructure composed of highly nonlinear materials such as Silicon Nitride (SiN) and Silicon-nanocrystal (Si-nc), trade-off exists between propagation loss and nonlinear property gamma. Thicker SiN or Si-nc films can increase the nonlinear property gamma, but it also increases the propagation loss. It is found that the Si-nc embedded structure has an overall better performance than the waveguide with embedded SiN film, as the Si-nc layer can be much thinner, with typical thickness of few tens of nm. It is worth noting that one reason that the SiN embedded structure did not perform as well as expected is because the SiN process was not well developed by our collaborator that fabricated the structure. Nevertheless, we have fabricated high-index contrast slot waveguides with lower index PECVD oxide and achieved a flattened dispersion curve of less than 50 ps/km/nm for over 1000 nm that covers both the O, E, S, C and L band and beyond. From the tradeoff between the different waveguide structures and determined the optimal waveguide structure, we have achieved our second objective by characterized the nonlinear efficiency of the optical waveguide circuits with the embedded Si nanocrystal film. By embedded a thin layer of 20 nm Si nanocrystal film at the center of the core of the high-index contrast waveguide, we are obtained a three-fold increases of the nonlinear phase shift parameter gamma. The embedded Si-nc film also increases the propagation loss of the waveguide from 0.10 dB/cm to 0.16 dB/cm. Although one can increase the Si-nc thickness or use a higher nonlinear material such as Si or SiN as the embedded material to achieve a higher gamma however this will also increase the linear propagation loss significantly, making the waveguide ineffective. Our final objective was met with the optical structures such as spirals and ring resonators we developed as building blocks for signal processing devices. Using a Si-nc embedded spiral, we demonstrated an all optical 2-bit analog-to-digital converter that operates in the telecom wavelength band. With the PECVD oxide embedded slot waveguide spiral, we demonstrated an extended supercontinuum spectrum over an octave span from 900 nm to 2200 nm. We further realized slot waveguide ring resonators that double the span of the frequency comb spectrum generated by the optical parametric process compares to the conventional channel waveguide.

11213618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213618.value: The major findings of this project are: 1) Although SiN embedded microstructure waveguide can result in a higher waveguide nonlinearity, it is found that the Si-nc embedded waveguide has a better tradeoff between nonlinearity and loss. 2) It is demonstrated that one can increase the nonlinearity parameter gamma of the waveguide by 300% by embedding only a 20 nm Si-nc in the core but only increases the propagation loss of ~60%. 3) We demonstrated an all optical 2-bit analog-to-digital convertor using the Si-nc embedded waveguide. 4) By embedding the lower index layer at the center of the waveguide core, it is found that one can flatten the waveguide dispersion which enhances its performance in supercontinuum generation and frequency comb generation by the optical parametric process.

11213618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213618.value: We have carried out a thorough investigation on the nonlinear and dispersion effects of placing a thin layer of highly nonlinear or lower index material in the middle of the core region of the conventional channel waveguide. Through the course of the project, we have obtained an understanding of the tradeoff and limitation of the effects of this type of waveguide structures. In view of the achieved findings and outputs, further development of this research will focus on applying these waveguide structures in optical waveguide circuits for all optical processing.

11213618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213618.value: Photonics integrated circuits have found applications in many areas, such as communication, sensing, all optical computing. The performance of these photonics integrated circuits depends on the properties of the optical waveguides that built these components. In this project, we were able to enhance the nonlinear property of the optical waveguides and to optimize the dispersion characteristics. These will benefit the future development of these components.

11214218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214218.value: Naturally occurred or artificially bonded granular geo-materials are encountered in many critical civil, geological and petroleum engineering applications with significant economic, social and environmental impacts locally and internationally. Weakly cemented clastic rocks, weathered rocks/soils, cohesive-frictional geo-materials and cement-treated soils fall within this broad type of geo-materials. There is anecdotal evidence based on research studies by scholars that the complex behavior of geological materials is mainly controlled by the grain interactions. These include contacts between grains and between bonding component-and-grains. Understanding these interactions and quantification of bonded grains behavior is the key to enhance our scientific knowledge and to improve the engineering methods in the safe design and realistic assessment of a broad range of infrastructure. Despite the realization by the scientific community and professional engineers on the need to enhance our understanding of bonded geo-materials behavior at the small scale, i.e. grain-bond-grain interactions, and the significant progress in recent years of numerical methods in the study of geo-materials such as the discrete element method (DEM), there has been little progress in proper experimentation development which would allow observation and quantification of the grain-scale behavior of bonded soils. This has been partly attributed to the relatively slow progress in micromechanical experimentation in the study of geological materials’ interfaces. Recent achievements by researchers, including the proper development of such experimental and scientific methods, provided insights into the micro-mechanical behavior of geological materials. Yet, most of these recent achievements have focused on unbonded grain interfaces and there has been little work investigating the behavior of the broad range of bonded granular geo-materials at the small (or micro) scale. This project aims to enhance our understanding of the complex behavior of bonded granular geo-materials at the grain scale and to develop a novel research in the micromechanical study of these complex geo-materials. This will be achieved through an innovative and comprehensive laboratory study using existing and newly developed cutting-edge facilities which will allow the quantification of bond-soil grain contact behavior. The project will integrate additional research methods, such as element (macro) testing, advanced scanning techniques and numerical analyses linking the micromechanical behavior of bonded grain contacts to the overall macro-scale behavior of geo-materials, to establish a rigorous multi-scale discovery. The outcomes from the project will put an important original contribution to the state-of-the-art research associated with the mechanical behavior of bonded granular geo-materials, enhancing our predictive and designing approaches for critical infrastructure design and assessment.

11214218.label: Realisation of objectives
11214218.value: The project aimed to provide a new contribution to the state-of-the-art knowledge in the field of micromechanics and multi-scale mechanics of variously bonded geological materials. Throughout the project, cutting-edge laboratory facilities and experimental methods were developed and main outcomes of the project were delivered in the form of journal publications addressing all the objectives of the project. This also gave the opportunity for three PhD students to be trained on the project and the PI to develop local and international collaborations with a number of institutes and researches. Preliminary and main outcomes of the projects were also presented in two Keynote Lectures in which PI Senetakis was invited to deliver. Each of the project objectives was fulfilled 100%. Specific descriptions of each individual objective and the way it was achieved are given below with a summary of some of the key works appeared in international journals which contributed to the delivery of project’s objectives. Objective 1: “Investigate the micromechanics of bonded soil-grain interfaces including load transfer, crushing, stiffness, cyclic-hysteretic behavior, thereby, enhancing the current scientific knowledge on the mechanics of these complex geo-materials.” In one of the collaborative works of the PI Senetakis with project’s Co-Is Coop and Zhao (collaborative research between CityU, HKUST and UCL London), a new experimental apparatus was developed which is specifically designed to have high stiffness and apply complex loading paths allowing the examination of the grain-scale contact behavior of cemented particles including weak and strong bonds (Kasyap et al., 2021 appeared in Acta Geotechnica). In that study it was examined the load-displacement constitutive behavior of particles at their contacts in the presence of bonding including hysteretic response as well as the mode of failure of the particle-bond system. Apart from the study by Kasyap et al. (2021, Acta Geotechnica), the stiffness behavior of bonded granular systems at the micro-scale was also examined in the key studies by Ren et al. (2021, appeared in Pure and Applied Geophysics) and Kasyap and Senetakis (2022, appeared in the Journal of Structural Geology). Particularly, the study by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022) provided a new model for the contact stiffness of bonded particle systems using a novel method to bond the particles, while Ren et al. (2021) also examined the crushing behavior of the particle-bond system using this time weaker bonds compared with the study by Kasyap et al. (2021, Acta Geotechnica). Micromechanical insights into the constitutive behavior of bonded granular systems were also obtained in the studies by Kasyap and Senetakis (2021, appeared in the Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering, 2021, appeared in the journal Materials) and Li et al. (2022, appeared in the journal Geomechanics and Geophysics for Geo-Energy and Geo-Resources), in which works the (nano/micro-) indentation method was used. Particularly Kasyap and Senetakis (2021, Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering) provided new insights on the role of creep/time effects on the micro-mechanical properties of naturally cemented soils (shale). Finally, an integrated experimental and analytical study was performed by Kasyap and Senetakis (2021, appeared in the International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics) in which work, the stick-slip instability of bonded granular system was examined as well as the stiffness behavior of bonded systems at the micro-scale. Objective 2: “Understand and quantify the effects of bonding type as well as scale-effects on the mechanics of bond-grain interfaces.”. A key work on the influence of bonding type on the micromechanical behavior of particle-bond systems was presented by Ren et al. (2021, appeared in Pure and Applied Geophysics). Ren et al. developed novel methods to reproduce weak calcite-based bonds, in which case one would mimic a “crystalline” based cement and the second a type of “clastic” based system, simulating in this way bonds of relatively similar strengths, but of different texture. That study showed the significant influence of the cement type/texture on the micromechanical response of particle contacts. Additionally, Kasyap and Senetakis (2022, appeared in the Journal of Structural Geology) examined scale effects of bonded granular systems, particularly the way the sample size (and thereby the size of the cement simulant) influence the constitutive (tribological) behavior of interfaces. That study expanded the scope of the project beyond typical “bonded grains” to flat interfaces which may find additional interest and applications in broader fields of rock mechanics, geophysics and earth sciences (and thereby the article appeared in the reputable journal of Structural Geology). Prior to the work by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022), a more fundamental understanding of scale effects on the tribological behavior of particles was provided by Sandeep, Li and Senetakis (2021, appeared in Tribology International), which focused on non-conforming surfaces of “controlled” roughness. Finally, the influence of bond type was examined in the key study by Kasyap and Senetakis (2020, appeared in Pure and Applied Geophysics), covering a range of light cementing compounds; it was shown in that work that both the initial tangential stiffness but also the rate of decrease of the stiffness with displacement were heavily influenced by the cement type. Objective 3: “Integrally study the mechanics of bonded geo-materials from grain-bond-grain level to assembly of bonded grains by utilizing the analytical tools and observations produced by the micromechanical tests.” Integrated studies using micromechanical-based test results were conducted by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022, appeared in Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment) and Luo et al. (2022, appeared in Int J Numer Anal Methods Geomech). Both of these works developed numerical models which were calibrated based on grain-scale tests and had particular emphasis on the load transfer mechanism, energy dissipation and damage behavior of bonded systems looking this time at the macroscopic level the behavior of the samples. The study by Luo et al. (2022) developed a 2-dimensional theoretical model, in which a distinction of the load transfer mechanism in the “loading” and “unloading” processes was observed and quantified. In this case, the “loading” and “unloading” were defined based on the impact and rebound of a model impactor on a block which was simulated with cemented particles. This model bonded system was originally unfractured, and thus, the work by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022) put particular emphasis to understand the load transfer mechanisms and energy dissipation of bonded system which was initially fractured. Multi-scale insights, from micro-scale to element-size experiments were offered in the work by Kasyap, Li and Senetakis (2021, appeared in Engineering Geology) as the way the bonding type affected the micromechanical behavior of the particle-bond system was further explored based on element-size direct shear tests; the macroscopic results on the constitutive behavior of the “cementing” compound from Kasyap, Li and Senetakis (2021) provided insights (and explanations) in the observed response from the grain-scale tribological tests. Finally, a key work within “objective 3” was conducted by PI Senetakis with two institutes from Iran (Shirmohammadi et al., 2021, appeared in Coatings); that study was predominantly based on macroscopic tests of cemented soils, but additional support of the study’s outcomes were implemented based on micromechanical investigations so that to understand the microstructure of the bonded system and how this influences the observations from the macroscopic tests in terms of system’s strength.

11214218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214218.value: Major outcomes of the project were delivered in the form of international journal publications which included a total of 24 articles appeared in a number of journals covering broader fields of engineering. This included mainstream and reputable journals of Geotechnical/Geological Engineering (e.g., Engineering Geology, Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment, Int. J. for Numerical & Analytical Methods in Geomechanics, Acta Geotechnica, among others) to journals such as Tribology International, Pure and Applied Geophysics, Journal of Structural Geology, Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering, Granular Matter, among others. This also demonstrated the inter-disciplinary nature of the project and the value of its outcomes in different areas of science and engineering, apart from main contributions to Geomechanics and Geotechnical Engineering. This was contributed by the fact that many different types of bonds were examined in both non-conforming and conforming particle-systems. More specifically, micromechanical insights on the load transfer mechanisms including cyclic-hysteretic behavior, damage behavior and stiffness were broadly covered by items no. 1, 5-8, 10, 12-15, 17, 20, 22. Insights into the influence of bonding type covering a wide range of cemented/bonded systems were provided in the key studies by items no. 1, 5-6, 10, 12, 15. Contributions with multi-scale insights on the behavior of bonded systems were majorly delivered by items 6, 9, 11, 19. One of the important new contributions from the project was the integration from small-scale experiments to macroscopic level theoretical models which helped to understand the load transfer mechanisms in bonded systems. Additionally, some important impact of the project’s results is on the development of novel experimental approaches to simulate bonded particles and measure their micro-scale response. Some of the works contributing to project’s objectives had a more fundamental scope to understand the problem of interacting surfaces including scale effects, damage behavior, hysteretic/cyclic response, such as items no. 2-4, 16, 18, 21, 23, thereby providing a solid basis for some of the consecutive works which put particular emphasis on bonded systems and/or provided multi-scale studies. The project provided also the opportunity for the PI (CityU-based) to develop a number of collaborations with institutes from Hong Kong and overseas including Europe, Middle-East Asia and Mainland China and also the PI delivered outcomes of the project through invited keynote lectures.

11214218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214218.value: There is a strong potential for future research developments given that the project opened new directions including inter-disciplinary areas of research. Examples comprise the collision behavior of impactor-cemented block system and the subsequent load/energy transferred to the cemented system involving complex interactions of a particulate material. Future research directions can put particular emphasis to examine in more details the load transfer mechanism in more complex networks of fractures as the present project provided a more fundamental analysis of the problem, i.e., load transfer mechanisms of unfractured bonded system or in the presence of “idealized” fractures. Other direction for future research developments may focus on the role of creep/strain rate effects on the mechanisms and micromechanics of bonded systems more comprehensively as many geo-systems and bonded systems may be susceptible to significant rate effects as some of the outcomes of the project revealed. Perhaps, PI Senetakis could prepare in the near future a “second-phase” proposal for funding as extension of the present completed GRF. As the topic involves significant inter-disciplinary interest, a larger-scale project (CRF or TSR) involving researchers from different areas of science and engineering could be a promising future direction.

11214218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214218.value: Many failures of geo-systems and infrastructures involve bonded geological materials, which exhibit complex behavior and the understanding of their response at the small-scale and multi-scale is a key to provide enhanced predictive tools and design safer infrastructures or take appropriate measurements of stabilization. The present project provided new fundamental insights on the way bonded geo-materials behave and how they transfer the loads via their body. This was mainly achieved through the development of cutting-edge micromechanical-based experimental systems and novel sample preparation techniques in an attempt to mimic variously cemented geo-systems. Additional insights were obtained by performing macroscopic experiments and/or simulations integrating the experimental findings from grain-scale tests to larger-scale problems. The project contributed to a number of high-quality outputs, majorly in the form of international journal publications and allowed for the development of collaborations between different institutes locally and overseas. The PI delivered through invited talks some of the important outcomes of the project, which comprise a solid basis for future promising research directions and direct applications to practical problems. Outcomes of the project also had inter-disciplinary interest as bonded granular systems are of major interest, apart from civil engineering, to petroleum/energy engineering, materials science and geoscience.

11214518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214518.value: 本项目旨在研究个性化安全信息系统的理论基础，为降低个人层面的信息符合提供支持。当今的建筑业越来越依赖于信息技术产生及传输信息。随着这些技术的应用，项目上生成了大量多样性的数据(如工人位置、环境信息等)用于支持工地上的管理活动。尽管这些数据价值高但是数量有时会超出个人的信息处理能力，从而造成了工地上信息过量与个人信息处理能力有限的矛盾。随着信息技术的发展与广泛应用，这一矛盾将继续加剧。因此，需要设计一种安全信息系统，将合适的信息在合适的时间以合适的方式传达给合适的个人，而不是将所有信息推送给个人。因此，建筑项目迫切需要一种可减少信息负载的个性化建筑安全信息系统。 本项目将研究不同的信息如何影响信息处理负荷，从而进一步影响安全决策任务效果。如果成功的话，设计的个性化安全信息系统原型可以减少安全管理人员的负担，提高决策效率。据估计，2020年全球建筑业总值将达10.3兆亿，因此任何提高建筑业效率的努力都能带来巨大的经济效益。尽管本项目聚焦于建筑安全，项目中的理论方法在未来也有望应用到其他行业。

11214518.label: Realisation of objectives
11214518.value: To quantify the impacts of the information loads on cognitive load, two empirical studies were designed and examined. Two of the main challenges are how to quantify and present different levels of information load, and how to measure and quantify cognitive load of subjects. Hence, two tasks closely related to information identification and safety were selected to conduct the experiments, one of which was the crane operator's recognition of the signalman's hand signals, and the other is the safety manager to recognize the information on the safety data panel. In the two scenarios, the researcher designed different levels and forms of information presentation, quantifying the level of information load in terms of the amount of information and previous literature formulas, respectively. In addition, cognitive load is a relatively abstract concept, so subjective questionnaires, objective task performance and measurements of physiological parameters such as electroencephalograph (EEG) and eye-tracking metrics are used to assess the cognitive load of subjects in a comprehensive manner. Through the design and presentation of the information load and the quantification of the subjects' cognitive load, the final results found a connection and relationship between the two concepts. To explore the relationship between cognitive load and construction safety decision making performance, a study was conducted by inducing different levels of cognitive load while evaluating the subjects' construction safety risk identification performance under different levels of cognitive load. From that standpoint, a two-factor (workload versus safety conditions) within-subject N-back design involving the collection of EEG waveforms was carried out. The findings support the assumption that situation awareness will be depleted progressively as cognitive load increases, and increased workload causes a considerable reduction in response latency and accuracy. To develop a personalized construction safety information presentation system prototype for the selected safety task on construction project, the most important part is to find the effect of individual factors on information preference and cognitive load. However, since individual factors include a wide range of demographic factors, and cognitive differences, individual preferences, etc. Therefore, the factor of cognitive style among the cognitive differences was selected for the study in this project. When identifying safety monitoring dashboards, field-dependent individuals took longer to locate information and had a lower accuracy. Cognitive load was significantly higher in the field-dependent group than in the field-independent group as measured by eye-tracking metrics. Although only one factor is investigated, the personalized information presentation system is designed in two stages, the first stage can consider as many individual factors as possible to construct a personal cognitive load matrix mapped with environment setting, task type and individual difference. In the second stage, the personal information load assessment can be used to filter the amount of information and optimize the presentation of information in order to achieve the least cognitive load for the receiver.
