11217018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217018.value: 天線是無線通訊系統中重要的一部分，它可以直接影響信號的傳輸和接收。最近，介質諧振器天線由於其一系列如低損耗、小尺寸，低成本和易激勵的優點，受到了廣泛的研究。 介質諧振器天線的性能取決於它的結構。具有吸引力的介質諧振器天線可以通過設計良好的天線結構來獲得。然而，由於加工技術的限制，目前對介質諧振器天線的研究還是圍繞著基本的形狀展開。隨著3D打印技術的成熟，一些在過去被認為不可行的結構，現在可以用3D打印輕鬆完成，打破了過去一些年傳統方法的限制。本項目將3D打印技術應用於介質諧振器天線設計，獲得一些新穎的陶瓷介質諧振器天線。有了3D打印技術，一些具有創新性的介質諧振器天線將只會受到想像的限制，大大地推進了介質諧振器天線的發展。 本項目將會首次研究各種3D打印的介質諧振器天線。首先，我們將首先研究一款寬帶全向的圓極化介質諧振器天線，隨後是一款寬帶的扭曲的圓極化介質諧振器天線。然後，採用3D打印技術，我們將加工3款各向異性的天線結構。第一款各向異性的天線是全向4層的圓柱介質諧振器天線，它有超過40%的阻抗帶寬。第二款介質諧振器天線的垂直截面被分成了不同的區域，每塊區域都有各自的介電常數。這款天線的兩個主輻射切面有相同的波束寬度，可以用作其它結構的饋電天線。最後一款是3D打印的高增益透鏡集成的介質諧振器天線。由於透鏡和介質諧振器天線具有不同的介電常數，因而整體上它也是各向異性的。各向異性的結構需要各種不用的介電常數，因此，將會使用具有不同等效介電常數的單元來實現。本項目將會給出一些方程來設計這些單元結構。 CST微波工作室將會用來仿真單元結構，而ANSYS HFSS將會被用來仿真3D打印的介質諧振器天線。我們將會使用實驗測試來證實這些仿真結果，也將會提供一些指導要點，使得設計3D打印的介質諧振器天線更加便利。

11217018.label: Realisation of objectives
11217018.value: (i) Objective 1: To investigate 3D-printed wideband circularly polarized DRAs This objective has been achieved successfully. Our wideband circularly polarized (CP) DRA deploys two different 3-D printing dielectric materials. It has a multilayer comb-shaped structure at its top for generating CP fields. The wideband characteristic was obtained by embedding three dielectric strips inside the DRA body to support multiple transverse-electric (TE) DRA modes. Also, the DRA is slightly twisted in the horizontal plane to enhance the 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth. The design was simulated with Ansoft HFSS and then fabricated with a 3-D printer that can prints two different dielectric materials simultaneously. Reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. (ii) Objective 2: To design the unit cell for obtaining different effective dielectric constants To determine the effective dielectric constant, a unit cell with a side length of “a” and a wall thickness of “tc” has been considered. The side length “a” of the cube is fixed as 4 mm or 0.08 wavelengths in air at 6 GHz. The effective dielectric constant of the unit cell can be controlled by simply changing the wall thickness based on the filling-ratio theory. Since our first 3-D printed DRA for this project has a multi-ring structure, the unit cells in each layer have the same wall thickness and dielectric constant. These unit cells can physically support each other and therefore avoid the need to add any extra supporting material in the 3D printing process, saving the printing time and material cost significantly. A retrieval method based on S-parameters has been used to extract the effective dielectric constant of the unit cell. To simulate a periodic structure using ANSYS HFSS, the unit cell is placed in a waveguide with perfect electric and magnetic boundaries. (iii) Objective 3: To investigate a 3D-printed wideband omnidirectional DRA Our 3D-printed wideband omnidirectional DRA consists of four concentric dielectric rings. The central part of the DRA is a solid cylindrical DR, whereas the outer dielectric rings have different air-filling ratios to provide different effective dielectric constants. The effective dielectric constants of the first (central), second, third, and fourth layers are denoted as εr1, εr2, εr3, and εr4, respectively, with εr1 > εr2 > εr3 > εr4. Our 3D-printed DRA is mounted on a circular aluminum ground plane with a radius of Rg and thickness of t. A coaxial probe with a radius of Rp and height of lp axially penetrates into the DRA to excite the transverse-magnetic (TM) modes. To improve the matching, the outermost layer h1 has a slightly higher height whereas the remaining layers have the same height h0 (h0 < h1).

11217018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217018.value: (i) Objective 1: To investigate 3D-printed wideband circularly polarized DRAs A prototype operating in C-band was designed, 3-D-printed, and tested to demonstrate the idea. The prototype was found to have the measured and simulated 10-dB impedance bandwidths of 69.7% and 66.5%. Its measured and simulated AR bandwidths are given by 68.6% and 73.1%, respectively. Our design has a record-high measured operation bandwidth of 63.2%. The work has been summarized in an accepted paper ([1] of Section 8, Part C). (ii) Objective 2: To design the unit cell for obtaining different effective dielectric constants The reflection coefficient of the original design with different dielectric constants (εr = 5, 10, 15, and 20) has been compared with that simulated using the unit cell approach in which only a single dielectric constant (εr = 10) is used. Since the agreement is reasonable, the original result can be used as a preliminary design of the 3D-printed DRA. The work has been published in [2] of Section 8, Part C. The idea has also been used to design 3-D printed multi-layer DRAs, which have been presented in conferences ([1]-[3] of Section 9, Part C). (iii) Objective 3: To investigate a 3D-printed wideband omnidirectional DRA Our DRA prototype was 3-D-printed with a printing material, which has a dielectric constant of εr = 10. The prototype was designed in the WiFi 5GHz band. Its different effective dielectrics in the different regions have been realized by using the unit cell approach as mentioned in (ii) above. The work has been reported in the journal paper given in [2] of Section 8, Part C. In addition, we have studied the 3-D-printed wideband dual-frequency dielectric antenna. Its measured S- and X-band 10-dB impedance bandwidths are 40.2% and 19.5%, respectively, with their high measured port isolations of over 40 dB. The work has been reported in [3] of Section 8, Part C. Also, we have investigated a 3D printed orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) reflectarray with half-wavelength rectangular dielectric elements. Four OAM modes (“l” = 1, 2, 3, 4) have been studied and verified by experiment. At 30 GHz, the measured maximum gain of the reflectarray is 20.4 dBi. The result has been published in [4] of Section 8, Part C. Finally, we have extended the 3D-printed antenna design to obtain a circularly polarized twisted-ridge horn antenna. A pair of twisted ridges have been introduced to convert the LP fields into CP fields. Its measured impedance and AR bandwidths are given by 53% (7.43–12.80 GHz) and 65% (7.63–15.00 GHz), respectively, with an overlapping bandwidth of 51% (7.63–12.80 GHz). The result has been summarized in [5] of Section 8, Part C.

11217018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217018.value: The following two topics can be developed in the future: (a) 3-D-printed pattern-diversity DRA A pattern-diversity DRA needs to be operated at the same frequency for different DRA modes. This can be done by modifying the shape of the DRA and the profile of the dielectric constant. This can be difficult if using the conventional DRA fabrication methods. But with the help of the 3-D printing technology, an arbitrary shape of the DRA can be obtained easily. Also, different dielectric-constant profiles can be realized by using the unit cell approach as studied in this project. (b) 3-D-printed millimeter-wave DRA array At millimeter-wave frequencies, the wavelength and therefore the size of DRA are small, making it difficult to fabricate the DRA accurately. This problem can be solved by using the 3-D printing technology. Also, in fabricating a millimeter-wave DRA array, it is challenging to align the DRA elements precisely. Again, this problem can be solved by 3-D-printing the DRA elements on a thin supporting dielectric layer which is 3-D-printed in one go.

11217018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217018.value: Recently, the dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) has attracted much attention due to its advantages of being low-loss, small-size, low-cost, and easy to be excited. Thus far, most DRA structures do not significantly deviate from the basic ones due to fabrication constraints. By using the 3D-printing technology, new DRA structures that may not be possible before can now be fabricated easily. With 3D printing, innovative DRA structures are now limited by imagination only. In this project, a new 3D-printed wideband DRA has been investigated for the first time. By introducing small air regions to the printed DRA, the effective dielectric constant can be changed at different parts of the DRA. This enables fabrications of inhomogeneous antenna structures. In this project, a wideband omnidirectional 4-layer cylindrical DRA has been designed and fabricated with the 3D-printing technology. It has a wide impedance bandwidth of more than 40%. Also, a new 3-D-printed single-fed inhomogeneous circularly polarized (CP) DRA has been investigated. It consists of two different dielectric materials that can be 3-D-printed at the same time. Our CP DRA has a record-high 3-dB AR bandwidth of 68.6%. Guidelines have been provided to facilitate designs of the 3D-printed DRAs.

11217518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217518.value: Developing electronic diode-like devices that endow the preferential liquid transport is of significant importance. Over the past decade, in spite of extensive progress in the creation of various strategies to rectify liquid transport using the bio-inspired approach, the state-of-the-art devices either involve the use of external energy input or suffer from drawbacks such as low liquid transport velocity and limited transport distance. Recently, we successfully designed a novel silicon-based topological liquid diode that takes advantage of the corner effect to induce a fast spreading precursor film as the driving force and the reentrant structure to pin the liquid in the reverse direction. Although such a device enables the spontaneous and directional transport of virtually any kind of liquids without the need of external energy input, it is still limited by the complexity imposed by the topological structure and manufacturing process. Owing to the hydrophilic nature of surface chemistry, the liquid diode also suffers from severe fouling problem during the long-term operation, which in turn reduces its lifetime and restricts its wide applications. Inspired by the groundbreaking work on the rectification of gas flow in one direction using the Tesla valve, in this project we will propose to develop novel liquid diodes amenable for large-scale manufacturing on a wide range of materials and surface configurations including open surface as well as inner surface by leveraging on Tesla structure. To demonstrate the generality of our design, we will develop facile techniques to fabricate liquid diodes on different materials and surface configurations such as open surface and the inner surface of capillary tube. Furthermore, we will elucidate how the macroscopic transport performances (i.e. rectification coefficient, velocity and transport distance) and the microscopic dynamics are regulated by structural topography. Finally, to address the surface fouling problem encountered in conventional devices, we propose to decorate the as-designed liquid diodes with a special thermal-responsive coating which can switch its wettability in response to an external temperature trigger. Such an active method will be able to remove surface fouling in an on-demand manner, resulting in simultaneous enhancement in liquid directional transport and operation lifetime. If successful, the project will open up a new avenue to design novel fluid devices with advanced functionalities, but also find a wide range of applications such as in biomedical materials and devices, water harvest, and lab on a chip system.

In the following researches, we also optimized the liquid transport performances. 2. We systematically investigated the liquid transport property on the as-proposed liquid diodes. After the design and fabrication of Tesla structures on different materials, we systematically studied how the liquid transport dynamics under different configurations including the spreading rectification coefficient, velocity and distance. 11217518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217518.value: 1. A new mechanism for liquid directionality and long-range transport. Generally, liquid diode intrinsically stems from the multiscale structures on the operation surface, which optimizes and enhances capillary rise in the transport direction, while prevents backflow in the reverse direction. Despite commendable progress, it remains a daunting undertaking to mimic the structural and the functional sophistication inherent in living organisms in a facile and reproducible manner. Moreover, the speed of motion obtained on previous designs is usually slow, the transport distance is limited, and the flow direction is not well controlled with a higher fidelity because of unwanted pinning of contact line by defects on the surface. Our idea is mainly based on the Tesla valve which can rectify gas flow in one direction without the use of any moving parts. The basic principle behind this elegant invention lies in the use of asymmetric recesses to create a large contrast in flow resistance in the forward and backflow directions. 2. A new method for manufacturing liquid diodes that are amenable for a wide range of materials and structural configurations as well as large-scale manufacturing. Previously, researchers have successfully developed some silicon-based liquid diodes with complex topography. In spite of this, the limitation imposed by the complexity in reentrant structure, the substrate materials, as well as manufacturing process, restricts its practical applications in diverse industrial settings. In our project, Tesla-type structures served as a general architecture and can be easily integrated to different materials to enable a distinct diode-like liquid transport. Apart from open surface, we also propose to develop topological liquid diodes on the inner surface of various capillary tubes. 3. A new strategy for realizing liquid diode with enhanced antifouling, superior durability, and elongated lifetime. The long-term operation of liquid diode in various settings will inevitably result in unwanted surface contamination or biofouling. To combat undesirable biofouling, we chose the thermal-responsive polymer as a trigger to dynamically tune the surface wettability of our topological liquid diode. By tuning the wettability of the thermal-responsive liquid diode, we alleviated the colonization of the biofilm in the hydrophobic state and in turn keep the long-term function of liquid transport in the hydrophilic state. The objectives have been fully addressed and several important results have been achieved with publications in leading journals such as Advanced Materials, Nano Letters, Small, ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces.

11217518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217518.value: In this project, we explored the feasibility of developing a general approach to develop liquid diodes with superior transport and antifouling properties. From the fundamental point of view, the idea of leveraging on topological features to achieve preferential liquid transport and thermal-responsive coating to dynamically switch the surface wettability represents an important advance and will stimulate new thinking in the development of bio-inspired devices with exquisite functionalities. From the applied research point of view, we expect that the as-proposed liquid diodes can be large-scale manufactured on a wide range of materials and surface configurations including open surface and inner surface of capillary tube. The easy in mass manufacturing on diverse materials in different configurations as well as its effective antifouling mechanism of our liquid diodes will find a wide range of practical applications such as in various medical devices, vessels, underwater construction, food processing and so on.

11217518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217518.value: The project probed the feasibility of developing a general approach to develop liquid diodes with superior transport and antifouling properties. We believe that this new liquid transport Mechanism and manufacturing method to be identified in this project can dramatically advance our fundamental understanding of the liquid dynamics as well as open up a new avenue for the design and large-scale fabrication of liquid rectifiers for a wide range of applications.

11217618.label: Realisation of objectives
11217618.value: All the objectives have been achieved with the assistance of two Ph.D. students and two postdoc fellows. Major support was from Dr Xin Dai who graduated with outstanding accomplishments in 2021. The project represents a continuing effort to extend the magnetoelectric dipole, invented by the PI in 2006, for millimeter-wave applications. In contrast with the designs at lower microwave frequencies, there are many challenging issues needed to be solved at millimeter-waves which have been used for 5G mobile communications and will be used in many more sensing and radar systems. We have studied different kinds of transmission lines that are suitable for designing low-loss high gain arrays of ME dipoles. Compact ME dipole elements have been developed for array design with wide scan angles. A dual-polarized ME dipole with simple structure that can be fabricated at low cost has also been developed. Compact feed network for antenna-in-package design of ME dipoles has been studied. Technique for reducing the side lobe level of ME dipole array has been proposed with attractive performance. The use of metamaterials for enhancing the performance of ME dipole is also successfully demonstrated. We are so fortunate that we can still find some companies in Shenzhen to fabricate our prototypes under the virus pandemic situation. The advanced equipment available at the State Key Laboratory of Terahertz and Millimeter Waves allowed us to measure the characteristics of our prototypes accurately.

11217618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217618.value: A compact aperture-coupled ME-dipole antenna with a substrate-integrated coaxial-line (SICL) feed was developed. By innovatively etching transverse slots on the electric dipoles, the antenna height can be reduced, and the radiation performance is also improved over a wide band. The antenna height is only about 13 percent wavelength, and the bandwidth is maintained at about 50%. A 1 × 8 linear array of the antenna element with a parallel feed network was designed and tested. Excellent performance is achieved from 24 to 39.5 GHz, and wide beam scan angle (up to ±45◦) over the wide operating band. The antenna is good for antenna-in-package (AiP) implementation. A new dual-polarized ME-dipole antenna with high gain was designed and tested [2]. Using two pairs of orthogonal feed probes, the antenna can be realized on a single-layer substrate. The antenna has 50% impedance bandwidth, 17.8 dB port isolation, and more than 9 dBi gain. A 2 × 2 antenna array based on the proposed wideband element was designed and measured with encouraging performance. The proposed antenna can be easily realized by low-cost PCB fabrication technique and would be attractive for millimeter-wave AiP applications. A novel compact fractal ME dipole antenna loaded with a metasurface was designed and measured [3]. By loading a reactive impedance surface between the electric dipole and ground plane, the operating band can be shifted down and the gain performance at higher frequencies can be improved. The proposed antenna is suitable for mm-wave scanned array designs. A 16-element array of the proposed antenna elements was investigated. Wide beam steering characteristic was found. A novel approach to suppress the side lobe level (SLL) of wideband antenna arrays was introduced [4]. The SLL of the antenna array can be suppressed easily by exciting all elements with same amplitude and a few elements in anti-phase. The anti-phase excitation is realized by rotating an element by 180 degrees so it will not affect the bandwidth of the antenna. As an example, a 16 × 16 array was optimized by the MBPSO algorithm. Based on the optimized array configuration, a 16 × 16 millimeter-wave ME dipole array was designed and tested. It was demonstrated that the SLL is lower than −17 dB from 24 to 35 GHz, and the highest gain is about 26 dBi. With low SLL over a wide operating band and simple feed network, the proposed design would be attractive for many applications

11217618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217618.value: The potential for further development of the ME dipoles is very high. In fact, we have been working on the designs of ME dipoles operating at THz frequencies, ME dipole reflectarrays and transmitarrays and ME dipoles for medical imaging. I am pleased to know that many other overseas research groups are investigating ME dipoles for various applications.

11217618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217618.value: Many new wireless systems including the 5G and 6G mobile communications, automotive radars and medical sensors require wideband antennas with versatile characteristics such as low profile, small size, low cross polarization, stable gain and radiation pattern over the operating band. In general, conventional dipole antennas, slot antennas and microstrip antennas cannot fulfil these stringent requirements. The magneto-electric dipole was proposed by the principal investigator for operation at lower microwave frequencies. Excellent characteristics including wide bandwidth and low back radiation were demonstrated. In this project, we have been able to enhance the ME dipoles for operation at millimeter-wave frequencies. It is just the appropriate time to support the growth of the 5G and 6G mobile communications. In fact, some industrial companies and research institutes have been attracted to apply the ME dipoles in developing their new products and devices for achieving excellent wideband performance including 5G base station antennas, millimeter-wave 5G modules, and satellite antenna arrays for remote sensing. More new applications of ME dipoles are expected to be seen in the near future.

11218018.label: Realisation of objectives
11218018.value: The primary objective of this project is to develop high quality nano-particles enhanced rare earth ions doped glass phosphor materials with efficient sensitization effect and efficient excitability under ultra-violet illumination. In the mid-term progress report for the period ending 31-03-2020 we have completed 40 to 60% of five objectives, as evidenced by the 5 published journal papers: Dy3+ [1, 2], Eu3+ [3], and Pr3+ [4] doped glass phosphor materials, and Er3+/Yb3+ doped fluoride ceramics [5] were synthesized and their properties were studied. In the remaining period, despite the social unrest and pandemic situations ( ~17% of the grant money was unspent and returned to RGC), we have managed to achieve all the objectives. Further work on REIs doped novel materials were carried out, such as Er3+/Yb3+ codoped fluorotellurite glasses [6], Dy3+/Eu3+ codoped borotellurite glass phosphors [9], Sm3+ doped borosilicate glass phosphors with Ce3+ and Sb3+ as sensitizers [12], Eu3+ doped phosphor in glass materials [8], Dy3+ doped phosphate glass phosphors [13], and NPs enhanced glass phosphor materials, such as red emitting CaAlSiN3:Eu2+ phosphor in glass materials [7], Eu3+ doped NaGdF4 nanoparticles in fluoride phosphate phosphors [10], and Eu3+ doped NaYF4 nanocrystals in fluoride phosphate blocky phosphors [11]. In this project, the synthesis of REIs doped and NPs enhanced REIs doped oxide glass phosphor have been studied, simplified, and optimized. Laser-driven white light luminescence properties of these materials have been investigated, and the chromaticity parameters have been studied. White light source using NPs enhanced REIs doped material with high conversion efficiency (79%)and high color rendering index (89) have been demonstrated.

11218018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218018.value: Rare earth ions (REIs) doped oxide glass phosphors suitable for laser driven white light sources have been synthesized and demonstrated. Different REIs have been studied, and both bulk and nanoparticles (NPs) enhanced REI doped phosphor materials show good efficiency, with some of these materials also suitable for light conversion and radiation detection. The introduction of sensitizers and their enhancement properties have also been studied, and it is shown that there is efficient excitation for both low energy ultraviolet (UVA) and high energy ultraviolet (UVC) lights. The intensity parameters (spectral indexes) have been calculated using Judd-Ofelt theory to estimate the luminescence properties of REIs in different host, which are usually derived from the absorption spectra. For NPs enhanced REI materials (for example, Eu doped fluoride-phosphate blocky phosphor embedded with NaYF4 nanocrystals), the multi-peak emissions from the metastable energy levels can be controlled to adjust the color coordinates, with high quantum efficiency (79%), and color rendering index (CRI) as high as 89. For the emission of activators in phosphor-in-glass system, excellent quality white-light with high CRI (91) and low correlated color temperature (CCT) have been achieved in the phosphor-in-glass system. Altogether 13 papers have been published in reputable refereed journals in the research area, such as Science Report, Journal of Luminescence, Journal of Alloys and Compounds, Nanotechnology, and Ceramic International.

11218018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218018.value: Long term reliabilities of the materials developed have not been studied, and this is important for industrial applications.

11218018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218018.value: In this project, pioneering work on white light generation based on a new class of rare earth ions doped glass phosphors has been demonstrated. The glass phosphors developed act as efficient photon converter for solid state lighting applications. The material systems exhibit strong luminescence and high color rendering index (CRI). In addition, the fabricated glass phosphor exhibits glass microspheres, increasing the surface area and making the white light luminescence more suitable for human eyes in daily use.

11218118.label: Realisation of objectives
11218118.value: Microfluidic handling of particles and cells plays a critical role in fundamental biological analyses and biomedical diagnostics applications. The field of acoustofluidics has garnered recent interest by merit of being contactless, label-free, pollution-free, low power (compared to typical optical tweezers), biocompatible, and widely applicable. Traditionally, acoustic tweezers have been based on single-use surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices where the SAW generated on the piezoelectric SAW substrate interacts directly with the sample under manipulation. However, the price of piezoelectric SAW substrates (e.g., LiNbO3) is still rather costly, which poses a significant challenge to lowering costs while also avoiding biological cross-contamination by disposing of part of the device. Therefore, there has been an interest to develop two-chip acoustofluidic platforms comprising of a reusable SAW substrate and a disposable superstrate that is in contact with the sample to be manipulated. This research involves the application of acoustofluidic techniques in a two-chip format for two different functions: (1) acoustic micro-centrifugation for particle concentration and separation in a sessile droplet and (2) patterning and moving particles and cells in two orthogonal directions within a closed microchamber. The concentration of micro to nano bioparticles is an indispensable step for sample preparation in many microfluidic devices. This work advances the state of art currently based on simple plain superstrates by investigating the performance of droplet micro centrifugation on a complex surface micromachined silicon (SMS) superstrate comprising multiple deposited and patterned thin film layers that are meant to mimic a generic microfabricated sensing device. To advance methods to shape waves more efficiently and reliably on a chip to promote micro-centrifugation, we describe the use of low-cost (compared to microfabrication) laser-cut patterned superstrates that enable particle concentration over a wide range of operating frequencies to cover a wide range of particle sizes (several microns to sub-microns). The practical issue of finding a suitable coupling agent was considered by examining four kinds of coupling agents for transmission efficiency and long-term stability. For particle patterning and translation (i.e., acoustic manipulation), we propose a polymer (i.e., Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)) thin film for the coupling agent to balance acoustic coupling efficiency, stability over time, and reusability. As with the case for micro-centrifugation, we studied the feasibility of acoustic manipulation on an SMS superstrate and reported notable alterations in the particle separation distances compared to a plain silicon superstrate, which we attribute to a change of wave type from Lamb wave to Rayleigh wave on SMS superstrate. To demonstrate the biocompatibility of these acoustic techniques, we verified that there was high cell viability after SAW treatment in both the cases of particle concentration in a sessile droplet and particle manipulation in a closed microchamber. The two-chip setup was further explored to demonstrate the integration of two different techniques: acoustic localization of sparse particle and miniaturized mass sensing on a single chip for enhanced detection and minimization of blank measurements. The SAW was coupled into a microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) chip fabricated with a piezoelectric resonant sensor to localize scattered microparticles within a limited detection area, with the added mass resulting in a clear shift in the resonance frequency of the MEMS device, and the mass sensitivity is consistent in different measurements. The most common acoustic tweezers manipulate particles and cells directly on costly piezoelectric LiNbO3 substrates fabricated to form a SAW device. However, disposing of these SAW devices after a single use to prevent chemical and biological cross-contamination is not a viable solution in terms of cost. More recently, two-chip acoustofluidic devices have been proposed to address the issue of cost, comprising a SAW device and a detachable superstrate where the manipulation operations are carried out. The two-chip approach allows the expensive SAW device to be reused while the superstrate contaminated by the biological material is disposed of. But there remain some challenges to the two-chip approach, and this research has endeavored to address some of this. This includes practical issues such as identifying suitable coupling agents that balance function (i.e., acoustic transmissivity) and reusability (i.e., ease of detachment without damaging the device). We have also examined some fundamentals of two-chip acoustofluidic devices such as correlating the separation between patterned particles on a superstrate and the actuation frequency as the acoustic wave couples between different materials. These correlations will be important in the design of two-chip acoustofluidic devices. This research has aimed to push the status of two-chip acoustic actuation from simple plain superstrates to more complex superstrates with multi-layer films and patterned structures that mimic generic microfabricated devices. These efforts were culminated by fusing microscale mass sensing with microcentrifugation aimed at bridging the technical gap from a lack of feasible techniques to localized particles on a miniaturized mass sensor. Thinking beyond complex surface micromachined silicon superstrates to low-cost superstrates that could more effectively promote cell concentration, we have shown a new paradigm based on periodic structures to shape acoustic fields on the chip that is independent of acoustic bandgaps and applicable for a wider range of particle sizes. Specific contributions of this research are summarized as follows: a) We demonstrated the applicability of acoustic microcentrifugation on an SMS superstrate and characterized the underlying performance. With the aim to identify a suitable coupling agent, we examined the transmission efficiency and long-term stability of four kinds of liquid coupling agents for a two-chip setup. We demonstrated ultrasonic isopycnic separation between microbeads differentiated by density on the SMS superstrate. The results herein lay the groundwork for realizing particle concentration on complex superstrates processed with multilayer films that represent a range of microfabricated sensors. b) We demonstrated efficient particle concentration on silicon superstrate patterned with periodic structures fabricated with a laser-cutting tool that is suitable for low-cost and low-volume rapid prototyping in lieu of microfabrication. The advantage lies in being able to operate over a range of frequencies independent of acoustic band gaps and applicable for a wide range of particle diameters from the microscale to the nanoscale. We demonstrated a high degree of biocompatibility for such a two-chip droplet acoustofluidic device. c) Moving from microcentrifugation to manipulation, we described the 2D manipulation of microparticles in a closed microchamber on a silicon superstrate. We applied a polymer thin film as a coupling agent that balances acoustic coupling efficiency, stability over time, and reusability. We verified that standing Lamb waves were formed on the silicon superstrate for the trapping and moving of microparticles. d) We studied the feasibility of acoustic manipulation on an SMS chip by using a two-chip setup. Notable alteration in the particle separation distance was observed on the SMS chip compared to a bare silicon superstrate, which we attribute to a change in wave type. We demonstrated high cell viability on the SMS chip after acoustic manipulation. These results demonstrated the possibility of integrating a suite of microfabricated sensors on a chip with acoustically driven manipulation capabilities for multiplexed sensing and analysis for bio-applications. e) We demonstrated the integration of two different techniques by bringing together the functions of sparse particle localization and miniaturized mass sensing on a MEMS chip for enhanced detection and minimization of blank measurements. As a powerful tool, such a unified platform provides a high-reliability detection for low concentrations of micro-substances like microplastics and insoluble chemical solutions.

11218118.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218118.value: This research has developed a two-chip acoustofluidic platform for two-dimensional (2D) manipulation of microparticles in closed microchambers on reusable surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices. The platform consists of two microfabricated chips: (1) a detachable supersilicate enclosed by a PDMS microfluidic chamber and (2) a reusable SAW device (SSAW) for the generation of a vertical SAW, which is typically an expensive component. The SSAW is transported into the silicon superlayer through the coupling agent to form resident lamb waves (SLW) to capture and move the particles. We exhibit an integrated plug-and-play platform consisting of a reusable SAW device interfaced with a disposable surface-micromachined silicon (SMS) superhigh layer processed with five thin-film layers. To address the shortcomings of existing coupling agents, we examined and compared the transfer efficiency and long-term stability of four coupling agents, with the aim of realizing one-off acoustofluidic applications. To investigate the effect of different superliquids on droplet centrifugation performance, we characterized and compared the centrifugation of different superliquids. Under different conditions such as input power, temperature, droplet volume, particle size and density, SMS super can achieve high performance concentration. In terms of more advanced fluid handling capabilities on the upper layer of a multilayer SMS, we demonstrate ultrasonic isopycnic separation between density-differentiated beads on the SMS. We report a significant change in particle separation distance on SMS chips compared to bare silicon superlayers, which we attribute to changes in wave types by comparing different superlayers prepared. We demonstrate high cell viability after acoustic manipulation of living cells on SMS chips. These results are significant, showing the potential to scale the proposed method from the microscale (e.g., tumor cells) to the nanoscale (e.g., bacteria) by amplifying frequencies without being limited by fabrication capabilities. We demonstrate the concentration of particles in a series of periodic structural patterns fabricated using a laser-cut tool, suitable for low-cost and low-volume rapid prototyping. Experimental results highlight the relaxation of precision that particle concentrations are equally effective outside the bandgap or even in the absence of a bandgap, allowing operation in a frequency range independent of the acoustic bandgap. The key to this two-chip acoustofluidic platform is to select a suitable coupling agent at the interface between the SAW device and the upper layer. We applied a polymer film as a coupling agent to achieve a balance between acoustic coupling efficiency, long-term stability, and reusability. Recycling of SAW devices lowers the cost barrier for acoustofluidic particle manipulation.

11218118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218118.value: The reported method enables the patterning of particles on silicon superlayers, ultimately enabling 2D patterning of particles or cells on functional silicon micromechanical chips. The SMS chip is a complex super-crystalline silicon with a general-purpose thin-film structure made by patterning and etching multiple layers of thin films, whose properties are intended to represent a wide range of microfabricated devices. The reported two-chip strategy enables disposable microfluidic superpowers to avoid chemical and biological contamination while maintaining the non-contact and label-free advantages of acoustofluidic manipulation, and is applicable to devices with different shapes, densities, polarities, and electrical properties. various particles. We demonstrate the high biocompatibility of the device to illustrate the application of this method in biomedical fields such as basic biochemical analysis and in vitro diagnostics. The study here demonstrates the possibility of integrating a suite of microfabricated sensors on a chip with acoustically driven operational functions for multiplexed sensing and analysis in biological applications. This capability will enable functional applications such as diagnostics and biosensing. This non-contact, label-free, and low-cost technique will be widely used in biological applications, regardless of sample shape, size, charge, or polarity.

11218118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218118.value: Particles and cells can be precisely patterned and moved (i.e., manipulated) using acoustic actuation techniques. So far, applications of acoustic particle manipulation have been limited to ordinary surfaces. There is great potential to apply acoustic manipulation techniques to surfaces with microfabricated structures for high-throughput sensing. However, adding thin-film structures may change the operating characteristics compared to normal surfaces. Using a two-chip setup that allows reusable wave generation devices, we investigate the feasibility of acoustofluidic micromanipulation on surface micromachined silicon (SMS) chips. The research for the first demonstrates two-dimensional (2D) patterning of microparticles on silicon superlayers via a plug-and-play reusable acoustofluidic setup. The integrated device consists of two separate parts: (1) a supersilicate enclosed in a PDMS microfluidic chamber (containing particles) and (2) a reusable lithium niobate (LN) piezoelectric substrate. The results obtained in this research lay the foundation for realizing particle concentration in complex superlayers processed with multilayer films representing a family of microfabricated sensors towards the broader goal of integrating acoustically driven concentration capabilities and sensing, used for diagnostics and fundamental analysis.

11218318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218318.value: 在本課題中，我們將探索一些適用於毫米波系統的天線設計。我們將提出利用多層印刷電路板的特殊結構來形成新的寬帶毫米波天線。我們建議應用法布里珀羅諧振器和開放式諧振器的原理來設計出低成本可靠穩健的寬帶高增益雙極化天線。在該提案中，將調查三個確定的研究目標。首先，將對準環形反射器的激勵進行研究，以在法布里珀羅諧振器中產生多模諧振。通過在不同的高頻層壓板上印刷一組金屬環的解決方案地顯示了法布里珀羅諧振器天線。其次，將研究基於寬帶法布里珀羅諧振器天線的波束控制天線。利用多源激發在曲面上的折射率重新分佈電場方法，使天線獲得波束控制特性。最後，將演示雙極化高增益毫米波天線。用於激發本發明的天線結構的正交變換饋源的解決方案實現了優異的電特性，例如高方向性，高端口到端口隔離，低交叉極化，低後瓣，以及在所提出的雙極化的整個工作帶寬上的穩定增益的毫米波天線。

11218318.label: Realisation of objectives
11218318.value: This research project demonstrates new high-gain antenna technologies for millimeter-wave applications. The project is successfully completed with excellent outputs that matched our defined objectives in this GRF project. The outputs of this project have been published in the leading journals of the antenna research area. We here give an overview of this project's achievement. 1. To design a wideband antenna fed for a Fabry-Perot resonator antenna: At the beginning of this research project, we investigated a new wideband resonate structure for a millimeter-wave antenna. We invented a new Fabry-Perot cavity antenna [1] integrated with Fresnel Zone Plate to produce wideband and high-gain antenna features with excellent radiation performance. This antenna achieved an impedance bandwidth of 17.8% from 54 to 64.5 GHz and a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 13.3% from 56 to 64 GHz. The measured peak gain is 21 dBi at the broadside direction. [1] Q.Y. Guo and H. Wong, "A Millimeter-Wave Fabry–Pérot Cavity Antenna Using Fresnel Zone Plate Integrated PRS", IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, vol. 68, no. 1, pp. 564-568, Jan. 2020. 2. To investigate a beam steering planar antenna with offset fed: The second stage of this research project is to suggest a new approach of generating beam steering for antennas. We demonstrated [2] to use a dielectric block on top of a feed source to manipulate the electric field distribution on the radiating aperture of the antenna. This technique is effective to change the shape of the radiating beam from broadside to isoflux beam radiation. We extended a similar idea of manipulating the electric field distribution on a pillbox power divider such that high directive radiations [3] and [4] can be obtained. We further applied an offset feed technique to the antenna design of [1] & [2] to produce re-configurable steering beams [5] and the polarization reconfiguration [6] for millimeter-wave frequencies. 11218318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218318.value: This research has published 6 journals and 7 conferences papers. Two PhD students, Mr. Qing-yi GUO, and Ms. Xuan YI under my supervision completed their PhD degrees in 2019. Parts of their research works were supported by this GRF project. One of our project entitled "A 3D Pinred Polarizer and Its Application for Circularly polarized Fabry-Perot Antenna Design" received the best paper award in 2020 Cross Strait Radio Science & Wireless Technology Conference (CSRSWTC). Major technical findings in this GRF project are listed as follows: 1. A new wideband structure for a Fabry-Perot cavity Antenna. This structure can be easily implemented by printed circuit board technology, which is one of the excellent solutions for producing low-cost and high-performance millimeter-wave antennas. 2. Reconfigurability of multiple radiating beams for a millimeter-wave antenna can be produced by offset-fed sources to excite a Fabry-Perot cavity Antenna. 3. Radiating beam can be manipulated by a loading dielectric block, which is very effective to generate high-efficiency and high-directive radiation patterns for various wireless systems. 4. Metlens designs are practical and good for dual-polarized millimeter-wave antennas. 5. A suggested method of using time analysis for designing a pillbox power distribution network is useful and fast to design a large and complex antenna array.

11218318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218318.value: This research focused on developing newly wideband antenna technologies for millimeter-wave applications. A further work of this research can be extended to terahertz frequency applications, which will be related to 6G communications. In addition, the developed new Fabry-Perot cavity antenna can be applied to other applications such as satellite systems, wireless power transfer devices, and IoT networks, and other emerging wireless systems.

11218318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218318.value: This project proposed a new antenna solution, which is low-cost, wideband and high-gain, for millimeter-wave frequencies. The output of this research can be transferred and applied to 5G/6G communications, in particular to millimeter-wave bands. We successfully develop a new Fabry-Perot cavity antenna, a highly-efficient pillbox power network, and a thin metlens antenna. All these designs can be used in emerging wireless communications. Three defined objectives have been achieved including: 1. To design a wideband antenna fed for a Fabry-Perot resonator antenna; 2. To investigate a beam steering planar antenna with offset fed; and 3. To develop a dual-polarized high-gain planar millimeter-wave antenna.

11300218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11300218.value: 关于圆柱形管道中由激波所造成的不稳定混合界面的研究

11300218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300218.value: The study of unstable interfacial mixing has a very long history. The research on unstable interfacial mixing driven by shock waves started as early as 1960. Since then, due to the importance of this instability in natural processes and industrial applications, the research on this instability has been very active among mathematicians, physicists and engineers. The material interface driven by a shock is unstable. Small disturbances at the material interface grow in size to form fingers. To understand and to predict how these fingers grow in time are the central issues for this unstable interfacial mixing problem. The dynamics of finger growth involves both compressibility and nonlinearity. This makes theoretical studies extremely difficult. Therefore, most theoretical studies carried out in the literature are focused on ideal settings with periodic boundary conditions. However, it is highly desirable to study the dynamics of finger growth in a setting of a shock propagating through a cylindrical tube. Unfortunately, the presence of tube walls complicates the theoretical analysis dramatically. For this reason, no theories are available in the literature for shock-driven interfacial instability of compressible fluids in cylindrical tubes. Most of the theoretical results obtained from studying unstable interfacial mixing in periodic settings cannot be extended to the unstable interfacial mixing in cylindrical tubes. For example, the wave number of the perturbation at the material interface is irrelevant for systems with periodic boundary conditions since the results of different wave numbers can be obtained by a simple linear scaling of the wave number. The situation is very different for unstable interfacial mixing in cylindrical tubes, since the tube walls make the system non-periodic and therefore this scaling approach does not work. In fact, fingers in cylindrical tubes can have many new patterns that do not exist in periodic settings. The purpose of this proposal is to carry out the challenging task of developing quantitative theories for fingers at the shock-driven unstable material interface between two compressible fluids of different densities in cylindrical tubes. 关于不稳定混合界面的研究有着很长久的历史。这些研究始于1960年。基于这种不稳定现象在自然科学和工业应用中都很重要，数学家，物理学家和工程师们在这个领域中的研究非常活跃。受激波撞击的物质界面是不稳定的。界面上的微小扰动会随时间增长。如何理解和预测这些不稳定的增长是一个非常重要和困难的课题。它既牵涉到流体的可压缩性又牵涉到体系的非线性性。这给理论研究带来了很大的困难。因此大部分的理论研究着重于具有周期性边界条件的体系，但这是一种非常理想的情况。人们非常需要关于激波造成的不稳定界面在圆柱形管道中的理论。不幸的是管道壁使理论研究变得非常的复杂。由于这个原因到目前为止还没有关于不稳定可压缩流体界面在圆柱形管道中的理论研究。在周期性边界条件下得到的大部分理论结果是无法推广到圆柱形管道体系中去的。比如，对于具有周期性边界条件的体系来说波数是不重要的。这是因为不同波数的结果可以通过尺度变換来得到。而圆柱形管道体系的情况就完全不同了。由于管道壁的存在体系不再具有周期性。因此尺度变換的方法不适用了。事实上，圆柱形管道能够产生许多新的流体界面形状。这些形状在具有周期性边界条件的体系中是不存在的。本研究课题的目的就是要建立关于在圆柱形管道中两种不同物质密度的可压缩流体之间的不稳定界面的理论。

11300318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300318.value: 本項目的目的是利用發光過渡金屬絡合物修飾的多面聚倍半矽氧烷作為具有一系列不同性能的納米平台，來開發新的細胞試劑。多面聚倍半矽氧烷是最小的二氧化矽納米粒子，具有明確的分子結構。在這些分子中，最被廣泛研究的是八聚倍半矽氧烷，因為它的結構具有高度對稱性，並且可以通過修飾不同的角官能團對其進行改性。多面聚倍半矽氧烷除了具有多功能和三維高分子支架等常見於樹枝狀聚合物的優點外，還具有高熱穩定性、剛性和疏水性等特點。這些有趣的特性使它們成為新型納米複合材料、超分子組裝和功能材料的獨特新穎構件。在生物應用方面，熒光多面聚倍半矽氧烷分子已被用作生物成像探針，納米顆粒的改性劑，生物分子的傳遞系統和光動力治療劑。儘管取得了這些進展，但迄今為止所報導的工作主要集中於熒光有機染料的使用上。最近，發光過渡金屬絡合物的顯著發光性能和生物活性激發了生物成像試劑和抗癌藥物的設計。然而，由於金屬絡合物的低水溶性和高細胞毒性，它們的應用受到嚴重限制。因此，有迫切需要開發一種使發光過渡金屬絡合物既具有良好的生物相容性，又可以保持良好的光物理和光化學性能，還能提供更多的功能化機會的分子平台。鑑於其小尺寸，剛性骨架，疏水表面，高官能團密度，光學透明和非熒光特性，以及無細胞毒性，我們認為多面聚倍半矽氧烷是一種有發展前景的候選物，可用於構建納米分子平台，以開發基於發光過渡金屬絡合物的生物試劑。這種有趣的納米單元將賦予發光過渡金屬絡合物新的化學和生物性能，並進一步增強其在細胞研究中的通用性和應用性。在本項目中，我們將通過共軛修飾具有生物正交標記、細胞器選擇性和腫瘤細胞靶向能力的不同功能團，設計出新的發光多面聚倍半矽氧烷–過渡金屬絡合物，並考察它們的光物理和光化學性能。此外，我們也將研究這些絡合物的細胞毒性、細胞攝取和細胞內定位特性。我們相信，多面聚倍半矽氧烷和發光過渡金屬配合物優勢的整合將發展出可用於一系列生物成像和治療應用的創新試劑。

11300318.label: Realisation of objectives
11300318.value: All four project objectives have been achieved as illustrated by the following results. In the first study, we designed three luminescent molecular hybrids with eight cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes grafted on a polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) unit [POSS-{Ir(N^C)2(py-im)}8](PF6)8. The properties of these complexes were compared with their mononuclear POSS-free counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(py-im)](PF6). Upon photoexcitation, the complexes displayed intense and long-lived orange-red to red emission, which was assigned to a state of mixed 3MLCT/3IL character. Two of the POSS complexes showed enhanced emission intensities in a mixture of CH3CN/H2O when the water portion was increased. This finding was assigned to the reduced molecular motions of the molecules due to aggregation and hence suppression of the nonradiative deactivation pathway. The (photo)cytotoxicity of the complexes was examined using the MTT assay. The POSS complexes exhibited IC50 values > 400 uM, which were much larger than the POSS-free complexes (8.4 to 28.5 uM), indicating minimal cytotoxicity. The IC50 values of POSS complexes on irradiation (145.6 to 280.8 uM) were also much more significant than those of the control complexes (0.3 to 2.7 uM). Since the modification of iridium(III) complexes with a POSS moiety promoted the formation of nanoparticles, the cellular uptake was reduced, leading to lower (photo)cytotoxicity. Confocal microscopy indicated that the POSS complexes stained the whole cytoplasm of live HeLa cells, while the POSS-free complexes were localized in mitochondria. In a related study, we isolated charge-neutral iridium(III) POSS complexes [Ir(N^C)2(L1-POSS)] and their POSS-free counterparts [Ir(N^C)2(L1)] and the PEG derivatives [Ir(N^C)2(L1-PEG)]. Upon irradiation, all the complexes displayed long-lived orange to red emission. The bsn complexes exhibited the highest singlet oxygen (1O2) generation quantum yields (0.85 to 0.86) in aerated CH3CN. The POSS and control complexes showed exclusive lipid droplet-staining upon cellular uptake, while the PEG derivatives displayed lysosomal localization. One of the POSS complexes was utilized to study various lipid droplet-related biological events, including lipid droplet accumulation under oleic acid stimulation, movement of lipid droplets, and preadipocyte differentiation. The number and size of lipid droplets in a panel of cancerous and normal cells were also examined using the same POSS complex. Additionally, the POSS and PEG complexes with the ppy and bt ligands were noncytotoxic in the dark and upon irradiation (IC50 > 200 uM). In comparison, all the bsn complexes showed low dark cytotoxicity (IC50 = 52.9 to > 200 uM) but high photocytotoxicity (IC50 = 1.1 to 5.3 uM). These POSS complexes were promising luminescent probes for lipid droplets and effective 1O2 photosensitizers. In the third study, we designed molecular hybrids composed of a cyclometalated iridium(III) core and a POSS unit [Ir(pqe)2(N^X)](PF6)n (N^X = mbpy-POSS, n = 1; pic-POSS, n = 0; picpy-POSS, n = 1) and their POSS-free counterparts (N^X = dmbpy, n = 1; pic, n = 0; picpy, n = 1). Upon irradiation, all the complexes exhibited intense and long-lived orange-red to deep red emission, which was ascribed to a 3MLCT excited state. The complexes showed relatively moderate to low 1O2 quantum yields (0.52 to 0.15). Experiments involving different ROS scavengers indicated that the complexes were efficient in the photogeneration of superoxide anion radical, and the two bipyridine complexes were also good 1O2 photosensitizers. The POSS complexes were localized in the mitochondria, lipid droplets, and lysosomes, depending on the nature of the N^X ligand. In contrast, the POSS-free complexes stained the endoplasmic reticulum or lysosomes. The cytotoxicity of all the complexes toward the cell lines HepG2, MCF-7, and U87 MG under normoxia and CoCl2-induced hypoxic conditions was evaluated. Upon irradiation, all the complexes became substantially cytotoxic, and both superoxide anion radical and 1O2 contribute to the photoinduced cytotoxicity. The most important finding was that, on changing from normoxia to hypoxia, the IC50 values (irradiation) of the two bipyridine complexes were increased by 4.5 and 4 fold. In comparison, the four picolinate complexes were enhanced by 1.1 to 2.1 fold, indicating that the photocytotoxic activity of the later complexes was much less dependent on oxygen availability, typical of ROS generation through the Type I mechanism. These results are important as the Type I process is effective even under hypoxia due to the lower O2 dependence enabled by the biocatalytic oxygen recycling. Luminescent rhenium(I) complexes containing a benzo[ghi]perylene (BP) unit [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-BP)](CF3SO3) and a perylene diimide (PDI) moiety through a disulfide linker [Re(Ph2phen)(CO)3(py-SS-PDI-TEG)](CF3SO3) were synthesized. The complexes displayed FRET from the rhenium(I) polypyridine to the perylene moiety, resulting in negligible 3MLCT emission from the inorganic unit and predominant short-lived greenish-yellow fluorescence from the perylene. The sensitivity of the PDI complex toward glutathione (GSH) was used to visualize biothiols in live cells. In a related study, we developed rhenium(I) complexes featuring a 2,4-dinitrophenylsulfonamide (DNPS) unit [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-DNPS)](CF3SO3) as phosphorogenic bioimaging reagents and photocytotoxic agents. These complexes exhibited negligible luminescence due to PET to the DNPS unit. However, upon treatment with GSH, the DNPS moiety departed, resulting in emission enhancement and potent photocytotoxicity. Related iridium(III) PEG complexes with a disulfide linkage [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-SS-PEG)](PF6) and a bimetallic iridium(III)-rhenium(I) complex [Ir(pqe)2(bpy-SS-py)(CO)3(Me4-phen)Re](PF6)(CF3SO3) were also designed as sulfhydryl-sensitive biological reagents. Luminescent iridium(III) complexes appended with a perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) moiety [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CH2-OCONH-C2H4-S-C12F9)](PF6) were designed as bioconjugation and bioimaging reagents. The complexes underwent facile reactions with peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence (Phe-Cys-Pro-Phe) to afford highly emissive bioconjugates, which were purified and characterized. The complexes stained the mitochondria of live HeLa cells due to their cationic and lipophilic nature. Conjugation of the complexes to the pi-clamp sequence slightly reduced their cellular uptake due to the polar peptide sequence. We demonstrated that the conjugation of complexes to organelle-targeting peptides is an effective means to modulate their intracellular localization behavior and PDT performance. In a related study, rhenium(I) PFBP complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-C2-PFBP)](CF3SO3) were developed. A conjugate containing a caspase-3 cleavable sequence and a pi-clamp sequence (DEVD-FCPF) was modified with the Ph2phen complex (on the pi-clamp sequence) and an emission quencher QSY-7 (on the N-terminal amine group). Specific enzymatic cleavage of the DEVD sequence led to significant emission turn-on of the complex in extracellular and intracellular environments. Iridium(III) nitrone complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-nitrone)](PF6) were designed as bioorthogonal phosphorogenic probes for a benzylguanine derivative BCN-BG, which was a substrate for the SNAP-tag protein. Upon reaction in an aqueous buffer, the mixtures showed significant emission enhancement and lifetime extension. We also reacted BCN-BG with SNAP-tag protein and isolated the conjugate BCN-SNAP. As expected, the complexes displayed more intense and longer-lived emission upon reaction with the conjugate. These findings were utilized in designing new bioprobes whose luminescence and photocytotoxic activity can be manipulated in live CHO-K1 cells using bioorthogonal reactions. In related studies, we also designed iridium(III) tetrazine complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-tetrazine-Ph)](PF6) and rhenium(I) sydnone complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-sydnone)](CF3SO3) as phosphorogenic bioorthogonal probes for organelle-specific staining and modulated photocytotoxic applications. Overall speaking, there were no significant difficulties encountered in this project. The largest problem would be the low water solubility of the POSS complexes due to the highly hydrophobic POSS unit. However, this eventually became an advantage as the aggregation and nanoparticle formation minimized cytotoxicity and offered additional emission properties that were different from those of individual molecules. Nevertheless, we can highly control the solubility of various complexes by PEGylation and peptide modification. In summary, in this project, a number of transition metal complexes containing a POSS unit and other functional pendants were explored as imaging reagents and modulatable photocytotoxic agents.

11300318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300318.value: In this project, a number of new luminescent iridium(III) POSS complexes with different nuclearity and formal charges were designed, synthesized, and characterized with a range of spectroscopic techniques such as 1H, 13C, and 29Si NMR, ESI-MS, IR, and elemental analysis. The electronic absorption, photophysical, and photochemical properties of the complexes were investigated and compared to those of their POSS-free counterparts. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake properties, and (photo)cytotoxic activity of all the complexes were examined. Our results indicated although the POSS unit is chemically and electronically inert, it can perturb the luminescence properties of octanuclear iridium(III) complexes through aggregation or nanoparticle formation. It substantially reduces the molecular motions of the complexes and increases their emission intensities and lifetimes, offering new opportunities for bioimaging. The reduced cellular uptake also means that the (photo)cytotoxicity of the POSS complexes can be minimized, which is an advantage for bioimaging applications. Another key finding is that neutral iridium(III) POSS complexes do not stain the mitochondria, as commonly observed in their positively-charged counterparts, but displayed a preference for staining lipid droplets in live cells. Our results showed that the neutral POSS complexes maintain higher photostability than the commercial lipid stains Lipi-Blue and BODIPY493/503. As lipid droplets are dynamic and multifunctional organelle involved in physiological activities such as energy homeostasis, lipid metabolism, membrane maintenance, signal transduction, and protein degradation, the charge-neutral iridium(III) POSS complexes show great promise as theranostic reagents. It is imperative to explore ROS photosensitizers with minimal dark cytotoxicity and elevated photocytotoxicity under hypoxia since cancer cells are often starved of oxygen due to uncontrollable cell proliferation and altered metabolisms. Through the manipulation of the structures of the POSS complexes by using different cyclometalating ligands, chelating N^X ligands, and linkers, we afforded efficient photosensitizers for superoxide radicals. This is an important finding as photogeneration of ROS via the Type I mechanism remains effective even under hypoxic conditions due to the lower oxygen-dependence enabled by biocatalytic oxygen recycling. Based on these exciting results, we have extended the studies to the following systems: 1) transition metal disulfide and dinitrophenylsulfonamide complexes that are sensitive to biothiols; 2) perfluorobiphenyl complexes as specific labels for the pi-clamp sequence for bioconjugation and intracellular sensing; 3) metal complexes that are responsive to substrates of protein tags including SNAP-tag and HaloTag; and 4) tetrazine and sydnone complexes that display intriguing phosphorogenicity for live cell imaging and photocytotoxic applications.

11300318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300318.value: We have shown in this project that modifying photofunctional transition metal complexes with a POSS unit can bring new photophysical, photochemical, and biological properties to the conjugates, including aggregate and nanoparticle formation, specific subcellular organelle staining behavior, and effective photosensitization of selective ROS to enhance photocytotoxic efficacies. We believe that additional functional units can be introduced to transition metal POSS complexes to further enrich and control their cellular uptake, biomolecular recognition capability, and (photo)cytotoxic behavior. For example, thiol-sensitive linkers can be incorporated into transition metal POSS complexes to confer thiol-sensing properties. Cancer cells often need a high level of GSH to eradicate excess ROS and detoxify xenobiotic substances, rendering this biothiol a potential target for therapy. Thus, thiol-sensitive transition metal POSS conjugates have a high potential as activatable anticancer drugs. Additionally, transition metal POSS complexes can be modified to react with peptide- and protein tags. This modification will enable the resulting POSS conjugates to exhibit intracellular biomolecular recognition properties and organelle-specific localization characteristics. This structural enrichment, together with the modulatable photophysical and ROS photosensitization properties of transition metal-POSS systems, will pave the way for developing effective biological imaging reagents and photosensitizers for targeted photodynamic therapy.

11300318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300318.value: This project is about using polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) moieties modified with photofunctional transition metal complexes as a nanoplatform for developing new biological probes and cellular reagents. POSS derivatives are the smallest silica nanoparticles with a well-defined molecular structure. The structural characteristics of POSS units allow them to exhibit high thermal stability, rigidity, and hydrophobicity. These molecules can also be multiply-functionalized to afford building blocks for composites, supramolecules, and functional materials. Although fluorescent POSS conjugates have been applied as bioimaging probes, delivery systems, and photodynamic therapy agents, all of these studies were confined to the use of organic dyes. The possibility of applying transition metal POSS conjugates in biological studies has not been explored. Several classes of photofunctional transition metal POSS conjugates have been designed and synthesized in this project. Their photophysical and photosensitization properties have also been examined. Novel conjugates that exhibit: 1) emission enhancement resulting from aggregate and nanoparticle formation; 2) intracellular lipid droplet-targeting behavior; and 3) specific reactive oxygen species photosensitization have been generated. These crucial results highlight the unique features of POSS and transition metal complexes. They will also form the basis of the future development of innovative conjugates for biomedical imaging and cancer therapy.

To examine and study the charge interaction due to charge-transfer and energy-transfer processes among photoactive materials in the ternary systems by comparing UPS results measured with and without the selective wavelength excitation. This objective provides valuable information on the roles of charge-transfer and energy-transfer processes to photocharge generation in ternary systems. To reveal the working mechanisms of the ternary OPV devices.

11300418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300418.value: 由於具有產電成本低，重量輕和機械柔韌性的潛力，有機光伏器件（OPV）最近引起了極大的興趣。盡管OPV器件的功率轉換效率（PCE）已經突破超過10％，但由於光電流提取和光電壓之間的理論折衷，進一步發展仍具有挑戰性。三元OPV器件，即在常規二元D-A異質結中加入額外的供體（D）或受體（A），由於其高PCE（高達12.2％），最近已經成為有潛能的研究對象。雖然三元OPV器件發展迅速，但目前對這種新興技術的理解還遠不夠深切。雖然激發電荷轉移（CT）態的特性是控制傳統二元OPV器件中光電荷產生的關鍵因素，但在三元系統中激發CT態的概念要復雜得多並且仍存在很大爭議。特別是，控制開路電壓（Voc）和電荷復合損失的能量因素仍然存在爭論。在這個項目中，我們的目標是通過探討這些三元系統的能級結構和光電過程，為更好地描述和控制三元OPV器件的性能提供基本的理解。雖然X射線/紫外光電子能譜（XPS / UPS）是測量樣品能級結構和電荷相互作用的有力工具，但測量是在基態條件下進行的。因此，這些技術幾乎不提供關於激發CT態的局部相互作用和能量測量的信息。 最近，項目負責人證明了使用具有外部氙燈照射的UPS系統能直接測量激發CT態的激子結合能。在這個項目中，我們提議通過在UPS分析時選擇性地激發三元OPV中的不同光活性材料來擴展這項技術。

11300418.label: Realisation of objectives
11300418.value: In this reporting period, we have 1) developed a novel photo-modulated UPS (PMUPS) to characterize the charge distributions and electronic interactions of a D/A heterojunction; 2) investigated the mechanism of open-circuit voltage (VOC) loss in binary OPVs; 3) explored the photocurrent generation process of a ternary system; and 4) studied the charge transport properties and interfacial dipole of charge-transfer complexes (CTCs) formed at D/A interfaces. 1) Develop a novel PMUPS to characterize the charge distributions and electronic interactions of a D/A heterojunction Energy offset at the donor (D)/acceptor (A) interface plays an important role in charge separation in organic photovoltaics. Its magnitude determines the charge separation process under illumination. Extensive studies have been carried out for elucidating the charge-transfer (CT) process at different D/A junctions. These works lead to two different views: upon photoexcitation, energies would be (1) consumed in molecular polarization and orientation such that those opposite charges would overcome mutual Coulombic attractive potential at the interface and (2) spent on promoting charges to high-lying delocalized energy states (i.e., hot states), which is necessarily important prior to charge separation. Under these two scheme of studies, the electronic structures and the charge behaviors at the D/A interface should be different under photoexcitation, yet there is so far no direct experimental approach for probing the changes in electronics structures (i.e., Fermi level, vacuum level, frontier molecular orbitals, etc.) upon photoexcitation. In this project, a modified UPS system with an additional solar simulator, i.e. photo-modulated UPS (PMUPS), is used to study the charge distributions and electronic interactions for a standard D/A heterojunction (i.e., copper phthalocyanine (CuPc)/ fullerene (C60)) under photoexcitation. CT states formed as a result of photon energy transfer at the CuPc/C60 junction. Subsequent superpositions of charge transfer and electron polarization effects increase the D/A energy level offsets from 0.75 (ground state measured in the dark) to 1.07 eV (high-lying state measured upon illumination). We showed that there is excess energy consumed for a subtle change in the energy level alignment of the CuPc/C60 junction under illumination, suggesting a new insight for the energy loss mechanism during the photocharge generation processes. The above works have been published in “ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 42992−42996”. 2) Investigate the mechanism of VOC loss in binary OPVs Hybridization between the CT state of a donor–acceptor pair and lowest exciton state of the donor or the acceptor is reported to be effective for reducing recombination loss in OPV devices. Although this approach shows great success in maximizing Voc, it is typically accompanied by low device performance. In this project, “complete boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine devices” with strong hybridization resulting in lower recombination loss (0.47 eV) while not penalizing charge separation dynamics (internal quantum efficiency (IQE) > 80% and fill factor (FF) > 70%) are observed. Interestingly, when boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine is paired with any other active material used in this study (“partial boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine device”), recombination losses are still consistently maintained at lower levels (<0.53 eV). These observations denote the capability of boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine to result in lower recombination loss devices while pairing with other materials. Special intrinsic characteristics of these materials (high dielectric constant, sharp absorption edge, unusually high absorption coefficient) and hybridization collectively result in reduced recombination loss and efficient charge generation in these systems. This work enlightens that how CT process influences the device parameters in binary OPVs. The above works have been published in “Sol. RRL 2020, 4, 2000245”. 3) Explore the photocurrent generation process of a ternary system With the understanding of charge transfer dynamics in D/A bilayer system, we further broaden the scope to ternary systems. A ternary structure of SubPc/C60/MoO3 was fabricated and its charge-transfer processes were studied. We found that SubPc/C60 is a charge-transfer interface and C60/MoO3 is a Schottky junction. This leads to significant enhancements of photocurrent at both forward and reverse biases, while the conventional binary system does not show current enhancement at forward bias. With this novel electric character, we design an organic photodetector (OPD) that overcomes the “color blind” of conventional photodetectrors. The combination of a high or low photocurrent under reverse and forward biases determines the colors of the received light, and that forms the heart of ‘‘non-color blind’’ ability to recognize light colors in the OPD. The energy structure and charge collection pathways in the OPD are investigated with biased external quantum efficiency (EQE), ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and current density–voltage (J–V) studies. The OPD with the ability of color and wavelength determination demonstrates its potential to recognize colors without using additional components and the dual mode operation enables it to work under different conditions via switching its detection ranges with bias voltages. This design principle can be utilized to fabricate multifunctional devices by simply selecting different donor–acceptor materials according to the desired detection ranges. This work reveals the charge generation mechanism in ternary organic heterojunction systems. The above works have been published in “J. Mater. Chem. C, 2021, 9, 3814–3819”. 4) Study the charge transport properties and interfacial dipole of CTCs CTCs show distinguished charge transport properties from their parental materials. In this project, the electron and hole transport properties of co-evaporated MoO3:6T CTC thin film were studied. Using a simple rubbing process, we found that the intermolecular interaction of the CTC material can be tuned such that changes in optical properties, vibrational modes, chemical states and electronic structures are observed. These changes in properties and charge transport behaviors enable us to understand the influences of CTC frontier molecular orbitals and their degree of coupling on the charge transport properties. In addition, while CTCs are most widely known for their much red-shifted energy gaps, there is so far no report on their controllable dipoles. In this project, we achieved device current-change over 2 orders of magnitude by controlling the interfacial dipole with an electrical pre-bias in a MoO3:pentacene CTC-based device. Kelvin probe force microscopy further confirms that surface potential of the MoO3:pentacene film can be modulated by an external electric field. It is shown for the first time that a dipole of controllable direction can be set up inside a CTC layer by pre-biasing. This concept is further tested by incorporating the CTC layer in OPV devices, demonstrating a tunable VOC via changing interfacial dipole. The above works have been published in “J. Mater. Chem. C, 2020, 8, 16725-16729” and “ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 37384−37390”. Other related work: Knowledge and insight from the above works have been further applied to perovskite LEDs and OLEDs. We found that the interfacial charge injection can be improved using a zinc ion chelated polyethylenimine (PEI) interfacial layer in inverted OLEDs. A large centimeter-scale hole diffusion can be achieved with interfacial engineering in OLED, leading to a high efficiency and better stability. The decrease of interfacial charge recombination can enhance the device external quantum efficiency of perovskite LEDs. The charge confinement effect at the interface of perovskite/electron transport layer can tune the color temperature in white perovskite LED. These works have been published in “Sci. Adv. 8, eabm1999 (2022)”, “Adv. Funct. Mater. 2022, 32, 2203962”, “Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 4154−4162” and “ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 44991−45000”.

11300418.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300418.value: In this project, a methodology of measuring UPS under irradiation, is first developed for characterizing the charge distributions and electronic interactions of a standard D/A heterojunction. It is found that different from the CT states in dark condition, the energetic profile of CT states will change under photoexcitation. The result shows that there is excess energy consumption for VOC in OPVs in the energy level alignment condition under illumination, suggesting a new insight for the energy loss mechanism during the photocharge generation processes. (Ref 1: ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 42992−42996) We next investigated that what characteristics of the materials influence the energy loss of VOC in OPVs with a case study on boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine active materials. It is found that strong hybridization between CT states and excitons results in low recombination loss while not penalizing charge separation dynamics. The low VOC loss results from the intrinsic properties of boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine. (Ref 2: Sol. RRL 2020, 4, 2000245) With the understanding of charge transfer dynamics in D/A bilayer system, we further broaden the scope to ternary systems. The photocurrent generation process of a ternary structure of SubPc/C60/MoO3 was explored. It is found that SubPc/C60 is a charge-transfer interface and C60/MoO3 is a Schottky junction. Under light illumination, the photocurrent of this ternary system can be enhanced at both the forward and reverse bias regions. We then apply this novel ternary structure to fabricate a narrowband photodetector with electrically-switchable spectral range and color sensing ability. (Ref 3: J. Mater. Chem. C, 2021, 9, 3814–3819) In addition, the charge transport properties of charge-transfer complexes (CTCs) was also studied. We found that the change of intermolecular interaction in the CTC can tune electronic structures. (Ref 4: J. Mater. Chem. C, 2020, 8, 16725-16729) Moreover, for the first time, we observed that a dipole of controllable direction can be set up inside a CTC layer by pre-biasing, thus the VOC of the OPV can be tuned under different pre-bias values and directions (Ref. 5: ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 37384−37390) The obtained knowledge is further applied to OLEDs and perovskite LEDs for improving performance of different optoelectronic devices. (Ref. 6: Nano‑Micro Lett. (2022) 14:14, Ref. 7: Sci. Adv. 8, eabm1999 (2022), Ref 8: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2022, 32, 2203962, Ref 9: Chem. Mater. 2021, 33, 4154−4162, Ref. 10: ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 44991−45000)

11300418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300418.value: The proposed methodology has been proved to successfully probe charge- and energy-transfer processes at interfaces of binary and ternary systems. It also provides insight on specific issues in OPV devices, such as how to understand the VOC loss and how the charge transport at CTC interface is influenced by external bias during operation. The proposed methodology in characterizing interfaces can also be applied on other ternary systems with different kinds of interfacial combinations. Such investigations on broader configurations are expected to enrich the understanding on ternary OPVs and provide the strategic approaches to control and improve the overall performance.

11300418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300418.value: Performance of many organic optoelectronic devices including OPV devices depends critically on properties of heterojunctions formed between donors and acceptors. In many D/A junctions, charge-transfers and/or energy transfers occur and these processes determine the device performance. This project provides an experimental methodology to directly observe such transfers. In OPV, charge-transfer and/or energy-transfer processes in donor/acceptor interface play a central role in determining device performance. In recent years, ternary systems are emerging as a promising device structure to overcome the efficiency bottleneck. However, an important issue in the research of ternary OPV is that one more interface brings more complex mechanism than traditional binary OPVs. Till now the understanding on charge-transfer and energy-transfer processes in ternary OPV is still limited. In this project, a methodology has been developed by carrying out UPS studies with irradiation of different wavelengths for selective photoexcitation of targeted components. With this newly developed method, the charge-transfer and energy-transfer processes, energy-level alignment condition and electronic structure in ternary OPV have been studied in detail.
