11300718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300718.value: OLED is one of the most important technology for displays and solid state lighting of the 21st century. There is worldwide excitement among technology enthusiasts regarding the launch of the first iPhone with the OLED panel. However, for this industry as well as the academic sector, people are still searching for better OLED phosphors, particularly the blue-emitting materials, as the efficient blue-emitters are expected reduce power consumption and improve color gamut significantly. So far, both the green and red emitters employed by OLED industries are dominated by the Ir(III) based phosphors, except for the blue-emitting Ir(III) materials due to their poor efficiency and inferior stability. As for the molecular designs, majority of the Ir(III) metal complexes possess three bidentate chelates, which are known to be less robust compared to those with two tridentate chelates, for which the stability is provided by the multi-coordination architecture, i.e. tridentate bonding interaction to the central metal atom. Therefore, development of bis-tridentate Ir(III) complexes (or Ir(III) emitter with multi-dentate coordination chelate) with excellent blue emission may solve the important issues of both color gamut and stability, and thus have great significance in the timeline of OLED technology. In this proposal, we intend to set up the generalized synthetic strategy of the vital deep blue-emitting Ir(III) phosphors with novel bis-tridentate structure (or other suitable design such as 4+2 and 4+1+1 modes) from easily synthesized and modified precursors. Therefore, this study should result in notable impact to OLED industries and academic arena, and accordingly, will be important to Hong Kong in building up her scientific strength of the associate research. 有機發光二極管是一項重要的顯示器與照明器件技術。在近期、全世界的消費者都在期待使用有機發光二極管屏幕的蘋果手機上市。但在產業與學術界、研究人員還在搜尋高效的發光材料、特別是藍色磷光材料、因這類型材料將能夠有效地增加色彩對比度、與降低能量耗損。反之、目前主要的屏幕生產廠家雖已在使用銥錯合物的紅與綠色磷光材料、但尚未引入藍色磷光材料以生產屏幕、乃由於該項材料在能源效率與穩定性的指標、皆不符合工業標準。 從分子設計觀點來看、多數銥錯合物皆使用三個雙牙配基用以構建發光分子、但雙牙配基的穩定性皆低於三牙配基、這是由於僅有較少的配位鍵結的緣故。因此、如果能夠發展具有雙三牙配基結構的銥錯合物、將能有效的解決缺乏藍色磷光材料的問題。在這計劃裡、我們將嘗試設計這類高效暨高穩定性的磷光材料、並將分子設計延伸至包含 4+2 與 4+1+1 配位鍵結的新分子設計。預期此項計畫將能部份解決發光材料的設計瓶頸、並增益暨提升香港在此項科技領域的研究水平。

11300718.label: Realisation of objectives
11300718.value: This research proposal contained four main objectives, namely: (1) Changing the coordination geometry from bis-tridentate (3+3) to other geometries such as 4+2, 4+1+1 and others will be executed in seeking for the better molecular architectures that could afford the highest emission quantum efficiencies, plus optimized and desirable optical properties; c.f. the notations 4, 3, 2 and 1 represent the tetra-dentate, tri-dentate, bidentate and mono-dentate ligand, respectively. (2) To synthesize the bis-tridentate Ir(III) metal phosphors or Ir(III) complexes with 4+2 coordination mode that are capable to display various emission hue with excellent quantum yields and reduced radiative lifetime in solution and/or doped thin film state. (3) Modification of the tridentate (or tetra-dentate) chelates will be executed in an attempt to fine-tune the emission color of the above mentioned Ir(III) emitters and looked for their structure-property relationship. (4) Fabrication and optimization of various organic light emitting diodes using the above mentioned phosphorescent materials, particular to those exhibited efficient red, green and blue emission. Chart 1. Drawing of Ir(III) metal complexes bearing the proposed tetradentate chelate. Note: These structures are also available from papers #1 and #2 of our research output. All of these research objectives have been tested and, during our studies, despite of having some important success in preparation of both 4+2 and 4+1+1 emitters and fabrication of corresponding OLED devices. Some of our achievements are listed in Chart 1 and can also be found in our research output #1 and 2, respectively. The mechanistic pathways in giving these Ir(III) based metal complexes were unambiguously clarified. In the first case example, we synthesized mononuclear complexes 1 – 4 and diiridium complexes 5 and 6, all of them have exhibited bright sky blue to green emission with peak wavelength spanning region of 480 – 536 nm. More importantly, removal of the chloride and monodentate ancillary produced the diiridium complexes 5 and 6 with much enhanced emission efficiency. Therefore, the green OLEDs incorporating 5 as the dopant emitter achieved excellent performance with emission peak max. located at 530 nm and with maximum EQE of 25.1% and luminescence of 81.7 cd A-1, confirming their potentials in designing efficient iridium based phosphors for OLED applications. In an another endeavour, we design and prepared another class of Ir(III) emitters bearing the proposed tetradentate chelate by incorporation of greater electron withdrawing -CF3 substituent at the pyridinyl fragment of the tetradentate chelate (among 7a, 7b and 7c), or introduction of better π-donating chloride ligands in reference to the oxygen-based thd donor chelate (between 7c and 8). The isolated mononuclear Ir(III) complexes may be served as adequate dopant emitters in fabrication of phosphorescent OLED devices. According to our data, complex 7a afforded max. EQE of 8.28% with EL peak max. λmax = 530 nm, while complex 8 containing two monodentate chloride ligands gave max. EQE of 8.76%, but with a much red-shifted peak max. λmax = 613 nm, confirming their applicability in fabrication of phosphorescent OLED devices. During this investigation, we also realized that these designs of both 4+2 and 4+1+1 emitters are not particularly suitable in designing of urgently needed blue emissive phosphorescent emitters for commercial OLED applications. As a result, we first completed the proposed task on synthesis of both the 4+2 and 4+1+1 emitters, tuning their emission from sky-blue to orange, and confirmed their feasibility in serving as the efficient phosphors of decent OLED devices. It means that we have completed all of the four proposed research objectives. After then, we diverted our attention to the respective 3+3 and 2+2+2 designs of Ir(III) based metal emitters. This modification turned out to be extremely fruitful, and it has given us an assessment of a new series of efficient blue and true-blue emissive Ir(III) emitters for OLED devices. The respective results will be disclosed in the final report of other GRF proposals.

11300718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300718.value: During this investigation, we discovered that tetradentate chelates, upon conducting necessary revision, are capable to produce Ir(III) metal complexes with distinctive coordination modes, i.e., 4+1+1 and 4+2 and with attachment to either one or two Ir(III) metal centers. Their emission color can be turned from sky-blue to orange red, among which lower is the emission energy, higher is the emission efficiency. Fabrication of OLED devices were also attempted, giving satisfactory but not superior performances suitable for making the commercial viable devices. Hence, for the obtained research results, we gradually understand that, unlike the relevant Pt(II) based complexes bearing tetradentate chelate, our Ir(III) complexes bearing the similar tetradentate coordinative chelate may not be the best design for serving as the efficient OLED emitters. Please be noted that none of these facts have been reported in current literature and we have to figure them out by ourselves. Moreover, we begin to appreciate that Ir(III) emitters with rigidified coordination skeleton (i.e., not necessary to be tetradentate in nature), fine-turned ligand-centered transition energy gap, and reduced intermolecular interaction should be high critical to the ideal designs for future OLED emitters. Overall, we have not only completed all our four proposed objectives, but also find out the best directions to the research works focused on robust and efficient OLED emitters. Finally, I must say that we are privileged to have this opportunity for conducting this work that sponsored by UGC.

11300718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300718.value: Transition-metal phosphors remained as a key component in preparation of light emitting layer for future OLED technology. Hence, it is utmost important to expand their emission wavelengths into the true-blue and near infrared (NIR) regions. Stable true-blue phosphors are expected to excel all commercially available OLED based visual devices, i.e., displays and lighting luminaries, while efficient NIR emitters will enable new applications such as sensing, imaging, and optical communication. In theory, these advanced emitters can be assembled using precious metal elements such as iridium and platinum and judiciously designed chelates. From our current research work on Ir(III) based emitters with tetradentate chelate, i.e., those with 4+2 and 4+1+1 modes, their satisfactory but not the outstanding performances suggested us to seek for an alternative design with 3+3 or 2+2+2 coordination modes as more promising designs for practical applications. These constituted our current and future research endeavours.

11300718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300718.value: This project is a part of our great and combined research goal of finding the most efficient and durable true-blue and near infrared emitters for OLED applications, which will steer and dominate the ongoing development of OLED technology. For building up the demanded emitters with elongated operational lifetime, we need to control the chelate designs and to select a different number and kind of central metal atoms, so that the spin-orbit coupling interaction can be controlled, for achieving the optimal efficiencies. During this investigation, we have unambiguously confirmed that, despite of having tetradentate coordination mode for the chelate, the synthesized Ir(III) emitters are still fall short to the stringent industrial standards. In fact, the lesson learnt from this proposal, have indirectly helped us to publish one Adv. Sci. article (https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202201150) in designing efficient true-blue emitters and two more Nat. Photonics articles (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-020-0653-6 and https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-022-01079-8) in designing efficient near infrared emitters. These successes confirmed the bright future of our research directions.

11300918.label: Project Objectives
11300918.value: In-line electron holography [10] allows one to redistribute the dose of the illuminating electrons to many (20 to 40) focal series images without damaging the sample. From this low-dose image series a high S/N (signal to noise) electron hologram can be reconstructed that preserve the 3D information at atomic resolution (an example is demonstrated in fig. 5). This in-line electron holography can reduce the required dose gap by a factor of 5. The objectives of this proposal are twofold: (a) study of the dynamics of the electron beam sensitive materials MoS2 at atomic resolution. (b) to reveal the 3D conformation of oleic acid molecules at atomic resolution. . In view of the large number of images that have to be recorded to reconstruct an in-line electron hologram, the time resolution for the study of dynamical effects is limited to the order of seconds. The dose rate can be further controlled and the time resolution can be improved to be better than microsecond and even nano-second with other ongoing projects ultra-fast electron microscope [11, 12] that ultilizes a photocathode pulse [13, 14], quantum EM [15, 16, 17, 18, 19] and single electron detector [20]. These developments are currently supported by a starting fund of CityU.

11300918.label: Realisation of objectives
11300918.value: Advancements of aberration-corrected electron optics and data acquisition schemes have made transmission electron microscope (TEM) capable of delivering images and compositional maps with sub-Ångström resolution. However, the high energy electron beam also induces the radiation damage to the observing system. The radiation damage effects include knock-on displacement of atoms, ionization, heating and so on. The common strategy to minimize the radiation damage effect is to lower the accelerating voltage below the knock-on threshold of the objects and/or to reduce the dose of the electron beam. Nevertheless, the use of high electron doses is necessary to gain high enough signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of image for three-dimensional (3D) atomic structure determination. The aim of this research is to develop the in-line electron holography technique to strike a balance between electron beam radiation damage and SNR of image. Conventionally, one image with high electron dose is taken to obtain high SNR. In our method, the focal series images are recorded to evenly distribute the electron dose onto images at different focal planes, instead. Also, the time-resolved exit wave functions can be reconstructed from the sub-groups of focal series images. The information of 3D configuration of atoms can be achieved by analyzing the exit wave function. Two pieces of information, namely the z-height of the atom on the exit surface and the mass of the atom column, can be extracted from the exit wave function to reconstruct the 3D structure. The z-height of atom on the exit surface can be determined from the maximum of propagation intensity criterion and refined with the Big-Bang scheme, while the mass of the atom column can be determined from an Argand plot. This method is merited by the dynamic analysis of Co-Mo-S nanocrystal in 3D. The focal series images at atomic resolution are recorded for the MoS2 nanoparticle operating at 60 kV accelerating voltage with the focuses ranging from -50 nm to 50 nm with 1 nm step and the exposure time of each image is 1 second. The SNR of the images is low, but the signal of the time-resolved reconstructed exit waves is good enough to perform 3D structure analysis. Each exit wave function is reconstructed from 20 through focal images and thus the time interval for each exit wave function is 20 seconds. The time series of the 3D atomic structure of this MoS2 nanoparticle are used for the further analysis of the atom dynamics induced by the electron beam. The analysis reveals a decay of phase image contrast towards the nanocrystal edges and meta-stable edge motifs with crystallographic dependence. These findings are explained by beam-stimulated vibrations that exceed Debye-Waller factors and cause chemical transformations at catalytically relevant edges. The method mentioned above is applicable for the 3D nanomaterial with resolved individual atom column along projection of electron beam. But there are many nanomaterial in which atomic column is not well-resolved and moiré fringe exists, such as carbon nanotube, twisted bilayer graphene, and so on. Therefore, new analytic method is developed for these nanomaterial based on simulated annealing and energy minimization algorithms. Simulated annealing algorithm is implemented to refine structure by comparing the phase of exit wave with the phase of reconstructed exit wave from the focal series images and energy minimization algorithm is applied to correct structural anomalies. By using these two algorithms iteratively, the atomic structure with the phase which is closest to the phase of experimental reconstructed exit wave can be obtained. This method is examined for the carbon nanotube and twisted bilayer graphene. The focal series images at atomic resolution are recorded for the single-walled carbon nanotube operating at 60 kV accelerating voltage with the focuses ranging from -10 nm to 0 nm with 0.17 nm step and the exposure time of each image is 1 second. The atomic structure of single-walled carbon nanotube is obtained from the phase of reconstructed exit wave. From the atomic structure, the displacement map and the corresponding strain can be calculated. The twisted bilayer graphene is observed using the recently installed TEM in City university of Hong Kong, operated at 80kV accelerating voltage. The focuses of focal series image are ranging from -6.8 nm to 6.8 nm with 0.07 nm step and the exposure time of each image is 0.2 second. The time-resolved atomic structures of twisted bilayer graphene is obtained from the phase of time series reconstructed exit waves. The evolution of tilt angle and strain can be achieved from the atomic structures. These results demonstrate the feasibility of this method. The further analysis will be performed to investigate the dynamics of these nanomaterial under the electron beam.

11300918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300918.value: The technique of low voltage/ low dose holography has been developed and demonstrated successfully for a Co-Mo-S nanocrystal, which has been published on Nature Communication. The dynamics in three-dimensions of Co-Mo-S nanocrystal can be retrieved. This ability to relate local excitations and evolutions of atomic motifs is readily applicable and can be beneficially used in phase contrast electron microscopy operating at the limits of electron optics and detection. The analytical method is therefore anticipated to open up possibilities for probing dynamics heterogeneities in nano-scale materials at the single-atom level both inherent and induce by chemically stimuli to advance the fundamental understanding of the structure-sensitive reactivity in clusters, surfaces, and molecules in general. In addition to Co-Mo-S nanocrystal, this technique is also implemented in carbon-based materials, such as single-walled carbon nanotube, bilayer graphene, and fullerene-encapsulated carbon nanotube. These works are in preparation to publish. Carbon is one of the light elements and is sensitive to the electron beam. The feasibility of this method for the carbon-based materials extend the application to other radiation-sensitive materials, especially the biomolecules. Together with our recently developed simulated annealing/ energy minimization algorithm, the atomic structures are not limited to the individual atom column along projection of electron beam. The atomic structures in which atomic column is not well-resolved and moire fringe exists, for example twisted bilayer graphene and carbon nanotube, can be reconstructed successfully. Therefore, this technique demonstrates the potential to widely apply to variety of materials to reveal the underlying mechanisms which is still difficult to achieve.

11300918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300918.value: Although the current transmission electron microscope has reached the atomic resolution, it is still difficult to take images of radiation-sensitive soft matter, which consists of light elements, such as carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Biomolecules, such as proteins and deoxyribonucleic acid, are one of these radiation-sensitive materials. Thus, the development of the low voltage/ low dose electron microscope technique is necessary to avoid the radiation damage on these biomolecules. Our method has demonstrate successfully the feasibility for the carbon-based materials, i.e. single-walled carbon nanotube and graphene. Besides, not only the two-dimensional sheet conformation, but also the three-dimensional helical conformation, i.e. carbon nanotube, can be resolved. Therefore, the further development of this technique can be extended to resolve the structures and dynamics of biomolecules, which will play an important role in the development of life science.

11300918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300918.value: The famous physicist Richard Feynman once said, ‘It would be very easy to make an analysis of any complicated chemical substance; all one would have to do would be to look at it and see where the atoms are.’ The atomic resolution can already be achieved by the current transmission electron microscope. However, there are still some bottlenecks, such as radiation damage, lack of temporal resolution, and lack of three-dimensional information. This technique developed in the research project aims to solve these problems. By the use of this technique, the atoms can be seen in three-dimensions with minimum radiation damage. Besides, the movements of atoms can also be obtained, which is important to further understand the material properties under different stimuli.

11301618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301618.value: This project is concerned with the design, synthesis and reactivity of iron(VI) nitrido complexes. The highest oxidation state known for iron is +6, and there are only two examples of iron(VI) complexes. The iron (VI) oxo complex, FeO42-, is a powerful oxidant that is potentially useful as a green reagent for organic synthesis and wastewater treatment. On the other hand, the other iron(VI) complex, [FeVI(Me3cyclam-acetato)(N)]2+ (Me3cyclam-acetato is an anionic pentadentate N4O ligand), is a highly unstable nitrido complex that decomposes above 77 K. Hence, the search of more stable iron(VI) nitrido species that can exhibit oxidizing properties similar to those of FeO42- is of fundamental interest. Our group has previously found that ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes bearing salen-type ligands are highly electrophilic/oxidizing and they are potentially useful nitrogenation reagents. Selective nitrogentation of organic substrates is an important step in the synthesis of various pharmaceutical and other useful products. However, ruthenium is an expensive and toxic metal. Moreover, in the reaction of RuVI≡N with organic substrates (Ru≡N + Org → Ru-NOrg), the useful nitrogenated product remains tightly bound to the ruthenium centre. On the other hand, iron is cheap and non-toxic, and iron complexes are intrinsically much more labile than ruthenium. Hence, it is anticipated that the nitrogenated product would be readily released from the metal centre if FeVI≡N is employed. More importantly, it is possible to design catalytic nitrogenation processes based on FeVI≡N by using an external nitrogen source. In our preliminary investigation we have successfully synthesized a highly reactive iron(VI) nitrido complex [FeVI(N)(TAML)]- (TAML is a tetraanionic macrocyclic tetra-amido ligand) that readily undergoes nitrogenation reactions at ambient conditions with substrates such as styrene. Moreover, the nitrogenated product (2-phenylaziridine) is readily released from the iron centre, suggesting that it is possible to render this process catalytic by using an external nitrogen source, such as N3- or NH3/NaClO. In this project we propose to design, synthesize and fully characterize a series of iron(VI) nitrido complexes bearing various tetra-anionic and tri-anionic anxilliary ligands. We will investigate their reactivity towards a variety of organic substrates and develop catalytic nitrogenation processes based on these iron(VI) nitrido complexes. Our proposed studies should contribute to a significant advance in high-valent iron chemistry. It should also lead to the development of green and efficient catalytic systems for the selective nitrogenation of organic substrates based on cheap and non-toxic iron(VI) nitrido complexes under mild conditions. 該項目涉及鐵(VI)氮配合物的設計，合成和反應性。已知鐵的最高氧化態為+6，並且僅有兩個鐵(VI)配合物的例子。鐵(VI)氧配合物FeO42-是一種強氧化劑，是可用作有機合成和廢水處理的綠色試劑。另一方面，另一種鐵(VI)絡合物，[鐵(VI)(1-乙酸基-4, 8, 11-三甲基-1, 4, 8, 11-四氮環十四烷) 氮合物]2+ (1-乙酸基-4, 8, 11-三甲基-1, 4, 8, 11-四氮環十四烷是五齒N4O陰離子配體)是高度不穩定的金屬氮配合物，其在77K以上分解。因此，尋找能夠表現出類似於FeO42-的氧化性質的且更穩定的鐵(VI)氮合物具有重要意義。 我們組之前發現，帶有Salen型配體的釕(VI)氮合物是高度親電性/氧化性的，它們是潛在有用的氮化試劑。有機底物的選擇性氮化是合成各種藥物和其他有用項目的重要步驟。然而，釕是一種昂貴且有毒的金屬。此外，在釕氮合物RuVI≡N與有機底物（Ru≡N + Org → Ru-NOrg）的反應中，氮化產物仍然保持與釕中心緊密結合。另一方面，鐵是廉價且無毒的，並且鐵配合物本質上比釕配合物更不穩定。因此，如果使用FeVI≡N，預計氮化產物將容易從金屬中心釋放。更重要的是，可以通過使用外部氮源設計基於FeVI≡N的催化氮化過程。 在我們的初步研究中，我們成功地合成了具有高反應性鐵(VI)氮配合物[FeVI(N)(TAML)]- (TAML是大環四酰胺四陰離子配體)，在室溫環境下容易與苯乙烯等底物發生氮化反應。此外，氮化產物(2-苯基氮丙啶)易於從鐵中心釋放，這表明可以通過使用外部氮源，如N3-或NH3，實現催化氮化。 在這個項目中，我們提出設計，合成和充分錶徵一系列帶有不同的四陰離子和三陰離子配體的鐵(VI)氮配合物。我們將研究它們與各種有機底物的反應性，並基於這些鐵(VI)氮配合物開發催化氮化過程。 我們提出的研究有助於高價鐵化學的顯著進步，它還有助於開發綠色和有效的催化系統，可用於在溫和條件下基於廉價和無毒的鐵(VI)氮配合物選擇性氮化有機低物。

11301618.label: Realisation of objectives
11301618.value: A series of iron(VI) nitrido complexes bearing macrocyclic amido ligands have been synthesized and characterized by various spectroscopic techniques. The reactivity of these complexes towards various nucleophiles, including amines, cyanide and alkenes have been studied. The hydrogen atom transfer reactions of these iron nitrido complexes towards various hydrocarbons have also been investigated. A related, highly luminescent osmium(VI) nitrido complex has also been synthesized and its photochemical reaction with a wide variety of organic substrates has been studied. The hydrogen evolution reaction of a number of related ruthenium materials has been investigated. A series of iron(II) and iron(III) complexes, which are precursors for iron(VI) nitrido complexes, have been synthesized and their magnetic properties studied.

11301718.value: 複雜統計模型中的分佈式估計

11301718.label: Project Objectives
11301718.value: We study how the divide and conquer principle works in high-dimensional partially linear additive models when the dimension of the linear part is large compared to sample size. Due to the existence of nonparametric part, we propose a two-stage approach in which first a debiased profiled estimator for the linear part is averaged to obtain an estimator that has the optimal rate. In the second stage, estimates of the nonparametric functions are obtained and averaged after plugging in the linear part estimate. We aim to establish that the nonparametric part achieved the oracle property in the sense that each, possibly of different smoothness, has the same asymptotic distribution as when the other component functions as well as the linear coefficients are known. We extend the debiasing procedure previously proposed for smooth parametric regression models to quantile regression. Besides the challenges brought by non-differentiability of the loss function, the debiasing procedure involves the unknown conditional density which is hard to estimate directly. By the smoothing technique, we aim to show the matrix inverse involving the conditional density can be replaced with an asymptotically equivalent estimator, without consistently estimating the conditional density. We then derive a divide-and-conquer estimation approach using the debiased estimator which is useful under the big data setting. 1-norm support vector machine (SVM) generally has competitive performance compared to standard 2-norm support vector machine in classification problems, with the advantage of automatically selecting relevant features. We propose a divide-and-conquer approach in the large sample size and high-dimensional setting. Extension of existing theoretical studies to SVM is challenging in estimation of the inverse Hessian matrix that requires approximating the Dirac delta function via smoothing. We will try to show that under appropriate conditions the aggregated estimator can obtain the same convergence rate as the central estimator utilizing all observations.

11301718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301718.value: Given the recent rapid increase in the availability of extremely large datasets, storage, access, and analysis of such data sets becomes critical. This proposed research is concerned with downstream statistical analysis of such big datasets. Since data sets are often too large to load into memory of a single machine, let alone conducting statistical analysis for the whole data sets at once, divide and conquer methodology has received significant attention. Conceptually, this simply involves distributing the entire data to multiple machines, carrying out standard statistical model fitting at each local machine separately to obtain multiple estimates of the same quantities/parameters of interest, and finally pooling the estimates into a single estimate on a central machine by a simple averaging step. This simple but powerful strategy fits into the well-known MapReduce framework of Hadoop and thus can be naturally implemented in a parallel computing environment, although the proposed research is mainly concerned with fundamental theoretical questions rather than detailed implementation. For many models, the simple divide and conquer method can be theoretically shown to achieve the same estimation performance as when the entire data set is analyzed by a single machine, which is called the oracle property of the divide and conquer method. However, for high-dimensional models where the number of parameters to estimate could exceed the number of observations, the case is more complicated. In particular, the naïve averaging fails due to the propagation of bias attributed to the penalty used to make high-dimensional estimation feasible. Thus debiasing is critical before aggregation. In this proposal, we plan to study divide and conquer method for several high-dimensional statistical models, including partially linear models, quantile regression models, and support vector classification. The purpose of this study is to propose debiasing method in these penalized regression models and establish rigorously the optimal convergence rate or even, in some cases, the asymptotic distribution of the aggregated estimates. The technical challenges include dealing with propagation of error from the linear part to the nonlinear part in partially linear models, estimating unknown conditional density function in quantile regression, and approximating the Dirac delta function for support vector classification. Once achieved, it will deepen our understanding of the divide and conquer strategy and significantly expand its applicability. 鉴于最近极大数据集的可用性迅速增加，这些数据集的存储，访问和分析变得至关重要。这个提议的研究是关于这种大数据集的下游统计分析。 由于数据集往往太大而无法加载到单个机器的内存中，更不用说一次对整个数据集进行统计分析，分佈式的方法已经受到了重大的关注。从概念上讲，这只涉及将整个数据分配到多台机器，分别在每台本地机器上进行标准统计模型拟合，以获得相同数量/相关参数的多个估计值，最后将估计值汇集到一个中央机器通过简单的平均步骤。 对于许多模型，理论上可以用简单的分佈式方法来达到与用单机分析整个数据集相同的估计性能，这就是所谓的統計上的预言性质。然而，对于要估计的参数数量可能超过观测数量的高维模型，情况更为复杂。本研究的目的是在惩罚回归模型中提出去偏差的方法，严格地建立最优收敛速度，甚至在某些情况下还可以建立累计估计的渐近分布。一旦实现，将加深对分治策略的理解，并扩大其适用范围。

11301718.label: Realisation of objectives
11301718.value: The current project proposes to study the divide-and-conquer method in the setting with a very large sample size, for some complex models. Using this strategy, the entire data set is partitioned into multiple subsets and some statistical procedure is applied on each subset separately to yield some parameter estimates. Finally these local estimates are aggregated to produce the final estimate. In relatively simple models, it has been demonstrated that such a strategy can produce an estimate as accurate as that obtained when applying the statistical procedure on the entire dataset, when simple average is used in the final stage of aggregation. However, simple average may not work in more complex settings. The main focus is to propose suitable aggregation procedures and to establish their theoretical properties in various situations. Our first objective is to investigate the divide and conquer strategy in the distributed setting for semi-parametric partially linear (additive) models, while existing theoretical studies typically focused on the simpler parametric models. In this direction, we have studied how the divide and conquer principle works in high-dimensional partially linear models when the dimension of the linear part is large compared to sample size. Due to the existence of nonparametric part, we propose a two-stage approach in which first a debiased profiled estimator for the linear part is averaged to obtain an estimator that has the optimal rate. In the second stage, estimates of the nonparametric functions are obtained and averaged after plugging in the linear part estimate. We established that the nonparametric part achieved the oracle property in the sense that each, possibly of different smoothness, has the same asymptotic distribution as when the other component functions as well as the linear coefficients are known. We have also extended the work to partially linear additive models with more than one nonparametric components. For the partially linear additive model, we study how the divide and conquer principle works when the dimension of the linear part is large compared to the sample size. We find that a two-stage approach works well in this setting. Using the lasso penalty, first a debiased profiled estimator for the linear part is averaged to obtain an estimator that has the optimal rate, which is further thresholded to recover sparsity after averaging. In the second stage, estimates of the nonparametric functions are obtained and averaged after plugging in the linear part estimate. However, a well-known difficulty in additive models is to show the local asymptotics of each component function. Our strategy is to carefully control the bias in each component function caused by the estimation of other component functions. This requires more refined analysis than in the existing literature and we are still trying to work out the details. Our second research aim is to extend the debiasing procedure previously proposed for smooth parametric regression models to quantile regression, which is nondifferentiable and thus can cause significant theoretical challenges. In the literature, many studies have been carried out on penalized parametric regression involving smooth loss functions, such as least squares regression and generalized linear regression. For such smooth models, the technical aspects typically involve using Taylor’s expansion around the true parameter to establish the local behavior of the risk minimization, typically characterized by a weighted least square approximation. By decomposing the risk as a sum of bias terms and variance terms, asymptotic theory can be established by dealing with bias and variance separately in the distributed setting. However, for quantile regression which involves a nonsmooth loss, such a strategy will fail. Besides the challenges brought by non-differentiability of the loss function, the debiasing procedure involves the unknown conditional density which is hard to estimate directly. Although the regression function itself is parametric, such a conditional density is a nonparametric target and thus the difficulties are much more significant than other parametric models such as generalized linear models. Even though the density function could be estimated, the estimator’s convergence rate is obviously nonparametric, which may affect the convergence rate of the parameters of interest and leading to sub-optimal asymptotic behavior of the estimator. Thus we cannot directly estimate the density and need to seek an alternative route. By the smoothing technique, we showed the matrix inverse involving the conditional density can be replaced with an asymptotically equivalent estimator, without consistently estimating the conditional density. We then derived a divide-and-conquer estimation approach using the debiased estimator which is useful under the big data setting. Our third objective is to consider 1-norm support vector machine (SVM), which generally has competitive performance compared to standard 2-norm support vector machine in classification problems, with the advantage of automatically selecting relevant features. There are some similarities of the model compared with quantile regression model, especially in that neither loss functions are differentiable but merely Lipschitz continuous. This means in terms of technical tools used, some used in quantile regression can possibly carry over. However, there are two distinct differences. The first one is that the SVM is posed for a classification problem. Unlike the quantile regression problem which has a standard regression function plus additive noise structure, there is no such generating model imposed for classification in SVM. Rather, the generating model in SVM is specified mostly by specifying the conditional distribution of the features given and class label, and the hinge loss used in SVM does not use such a generating model in any way. This lack of generating model usage in the loss makes a clear difference in technical analysis. Secondly, instead of the conditional density that appeared in quantile regression, we now have the delta function in the Hessian, which is not a function in a classical sense, but a function in the distribution sense. Estimating such a generalized function was not studied in the statistical literature. We propose a divide-and-conquer approach in the large sample size and high-dimensional setting. Extension of existing theoretical studies to SVM is challenging in estimation of the inverse Hessian matrix that requires approximating the Dirac delta function via smoothing. We showed that under appropriate conditions the aggregated estimator can obtain the same convergence rate as the central estimator utilizing all observations. In summary, all research objectives as originally proposed are satisfactorily completed.

11301718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301718.value: With the support of GRF funding, we have published several papers. More specifically, we have made the following progress on the project: 1. In the paper “Projected spline estimation of the nonparametric function in high-dimensional partially linear models for massive data” published in Annals of Statistics, we consider the divide-and-conquer method for high-dimensional partially linear additive models with one nonparametric component and established local asymptotics of the nonparametric function. Unlike the fixed-dimensional setting in which the parametric part does not affect the nonparametric part, the high-dimensional setting makes the issue more complicated. In particular, when a sparsity-inducing penalty such as lasso is used to make the estimation of the linear part feasible, the bias introduced will propagate to the nonparametric part. We propose a novel approach for estimation of the nonparametric function and establish the local asymptotics of the estimator. The result is useful for massive data with possibly different linear coefficients in each subpopulation but common nonparametric function. 2. In another paper “Debiased distributed learning for sparse partial linear models in high dimensions” published in Journal of Machine Learning Research, we again take up the subject of divide-and-conquer in partially linear models, but we have used the setting of reproducing kernel Hilbert space and choose to focus on only the high-dimensional linear part. With the proposed method, we theoretically prove that our global parametric estimator can achieve optimal parametric rate in our semi-parametric model given an appropriate partition on the total data. 3. In the paper “Debiasing and Distributed Estimation for High-Dimensional Quantile Regression”, we consider distributed quantile regression in the high-dimensional setting, successfully establishing its optimal estimation property using the debiasing strategy. This theoretical result gives some guidelines on tuning parameter choice in the distributed setting. 4. In the paper “Distributed Estimation of Support Vector Machines for Matrix Data” we further considered support vector machines for classification in the distributed environment. For this we also considered matrix data that can deal with image features, for example, with vector data as a special case. We propose a communication-efficient estimator that can achieve the same convergence rate as the non-distributed estimator.

11301718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301718.value: This project considered three concrete statistical models under the distributed setting using divide-and-conquer, including semi-parametric partially linear models, quantile regression models, and support vector machines for classification. There are several directions one can try to extend the proposed research works. First, one can consider generalized partial linear models, which deals with more general response types including count data and binary data. Second, one can consider matrix or tensor statistical models in which the predictors are matrices/tensors instead of vectors. Such an extension allows us to deal with image/video data, for example, which has important applications in medical research and computer vision. Third, we can combine divide-and-conquer strategy with other efficient computational methods (such as random sketching) to build a more efficient system for distributed learning. We have submitted some grant proposals related to these extensions and some have been funded.

11301718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301718.value: The current project considers a simple and effective strategy for dealing with large data set, based on divide-and-conquer. This is also useful in the distributed setting where data are stored at different locations/machines and sharing of data is restricted by communication constraints and privacy concerns. Although this methodology is attractively simple, blind application of it sometimes results in much worse performances compared to the centralized counterpart, which motivated a more principled investigation of its theoretical properties, especially for complex models for which the mechanism of distributed learning is less clear. In this project, for some statistical models, especially those with a semi-parametric structure or with a non-smooth loss function, we study when such a strategy works theoretically as well as the centralized estimator, and how the performances depend on the number of partitions, on the dimension of the model and on the sample size. This will provide users with deeper understanding and general guidelines of the divide-and-conquer strategy, which is becoming critical in the modern big data era.

11302218.value: 多尺度數據分析：流形與圖上的方向框架小波

11302218.label: Project Objectives
11302218.value: Directional Framelets on Manifolds. Our first objective is to investigate directional framelets on manifolds and their applications. We shall focus on: Objective 1.1 Characterization and construction of directional framelets on spheres. Objective 1.2 Characterization and construction of directional framelets on compact Riemannian manifolds. Objective 1.3 Applications of directional framelets on manifolds. We start from the investigation of directional framelets on the sphere since it is one of the most important non-trivial natural example of compact Riemannian manifolds. The investigation including characterization and construction of directional framelets on the sphere will shed some light on the investigation of directional framelets on general compact Riemannian manifolds, where we first focus on 2-dimensional manifolds and then explore possible approaches of d-dimensional generalization. We shall employ the framework of sequences of affine systems for the study of MRA structures and directional filter banks associated with the directional framelets on manifolds. Fast transform algorithms should then be realized for various applications of multiscale data analysis on manifolds such as manifold data denoising, inpainting, etc. Directional Framelets on Graphs. Our second objective is to investigate directional framelets on graphs and their applications. We shall focus on: Objective 2.1 Characterization and construction of directional framelets on directed graphs. Objective 2.2 Characterization and construction of directional framelets on undirected graphs. Objective 2.3 Applications of directional framelets on graphs. For directed graph, one can associate it with a pair of undirected graphs, where framelets on the directed graphs can be constructed as the tensor product of framelets on the associated pair of undirected graphs. We shall investigate directional framelets on directed graphs under such representation of directed graphs and employ the framework of complex-value framelets. For undirected graphs, we first need to investigate the possible ways of defining directionality on an undirected graph and then focus on the construction of directional framelets on such type of graphs. Applications of directional framelets on directed graphs such as graph clustering, (semi-)supervised or unsupervised learning, etc.

11302218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302218.value: In modern society, data become the centre of people's everyday life, no matter it is objectively or subjectively wanted. In fact, as an individual, we provide tremendous amount of data through web-browsing, smartphone using, daily shopping, entertaining, medical treatments, etc. Huge corporations such as Google, Facebook, and Amazon explore the collection of humongous data sets for their own commercial purpose. Public parties from cities, countries, or international organizations, use such data for better resources distributions and improvement of life quality. Scientific research groups investigate data from various sources for significant scientific discoveries, e.g., new medical treatments, that are supposed to have deep impacts on human race. It has been demonstrated in many areas that applied harmonic analysis using multiscale representation systems plays an important role in data analysis and applications. In this project, we shall focus on the characterizations, construction, and applications of directional framelets on compact Riemannian manifolds and graphs (or networks). The results of this project will provide a general framework for data analysis on manifolds and graphs. Moreover, it will also provide practical algorithms for effective and efficient data analysis on manifolds or graphs. 在現代社會中，數據成為人們日常生活的中心，無論客觀上還是主觀上都是如此。事實上，作為個人，我們通過網絡瀏覽，智能手機使用，日常購物，娛樂，醫療等方式提供大量數據。谷歌，Facebook和亞馬遜等大型企業為他們自己的商業目的探索并收集大量數據集。來自城市，國家或國際等組織使用此類數據來獲得更好的資源分配和生活質量改善。科學研究小組調查來自各種來源的數據做出重要科學發現，例如新的醫學治療，以便對人類生活產生深遠的影響。 在許多領域已經證明，應用调和分析中的多尺度表示系統在數據分析和應用中起著重要作用。在這個項目中，我們將重點關注緊緻黎曼流形和圖（或網絡）上的方向框架小波的特徵，構造和應用。該項目的結果將為流形和圖形的數據分析提供一般框架。此外，它還將提供實用的算法，以便在流形或圖上進行有效和高效的數據分析。

11302218.label: Realisation of objectives
11302218.value: Objectives as per Section 5.1 above. Objective 1: directional framelets on manifolds and their applications. Objective 2: directional framelets on graphs and their applications. To achieve these two objectives, the PI and his collaborators first focusing on the characterization and construction of directional framelets on manifolds and graphs, and then focusing on the applications of directional framelets on manifolds and graphs. For the part of characterizations and construction, the PI and his collaborators mainly investigated two types of directional framelets, that is, the tensor-product type and the non-separable type, which are crucial in the analysis and applications of data defined on simple manifolds such as the intervals, the squares, the cubes, the hypercubes, etc. we showed that compactly supported tight framelets with directionality in arbitrary dimensions exist and can be boiled down to the construction of one-dimensional complex-valued tight framelets. We also proved the existence of directional Haar tight framelets in any dimension. Moreover, we further generalized such directional Haar tight framelets to arbitrary compact sets with hierarchical partitions. With such a generalization, directional framelets can be built not only on manifolds such as the sphere but also on graphs, especially directed graph. The PI and the collaborator also investigated the multiscale transforms for real-valued data based on interpolatory subdivision operators. Such transforms can be used for manifold-valued or graph-valued data. For the part of applications, based on the developed directional framelets, the PI and his collaborators investigated their applications in signal/image processing. For compactly supported tensor product complex tight framelets, we applied them for the image denoising and inpainting. For the directional Haar tight framelets, we built a tailor-made directional Haar framelet system and successfully applied it to the Parallel Magnetic Resonance Imaging (pMRI). For the directional Haar tight framelets on arbitrary compact sets with hierarchical partitions, we realized it on the 2-sphere. We not only applied it for spherical signal denoising using classical transform-based methods but also fused it into a customized convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for further improving its power in spherical signal processing. In summary, the Objectives 1 and 2 have been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcome, we refer to Section 6.1 of this report.

11302218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302218.value: For the tensor-product type system, we showed that by relaxing the real-valued requirement, one could build compactly supported tight framelets with directionality in arbitrary dimensions by the simple tensor product of one-dimensional complex-valued tight framelets. Moreover, we utilized the optimization techniques in the filter design to achieve frequency separation property as in the band-limited case of complex tight framelets. See Part C Sec. 8, the conference paper in SampTA 2019. For the non-separable type, we proved that directional Haar tight framelets in any dimension d, whose high-pass filters have only two filter taps supported on the integer lattice exists. More importantly, such directional Haar tight framelets are closely related to the directional box-spline. Preliminary applications in pMRI were also conducted. See Part C, the journal paper in Applied Mathematics Letters, 2019, 91:213-219. We investigated the multiscale transforms for real-valued data based on interpolatory subdivision operators. We defined even-reversible subdivision operators and proved the existence of an inverse to the linear operator defined by the even part of the subdivision mask. We also analyzed properties of the multiscale transforms based on even-reversible subdivision operators. Such transforms can be used for manifold-valued or graph-valued data. See Part C, the book chapter in “Excursions in Harmonic Analysis, Volume 6. In Honor of John Benedetto's 80th Birthday”, Applied and Numerical Harmonic Analysis, 2021, 297-319. With the carefully reconfiguration that adapted to the setting of pMRI (Parallel Magnetic Resonance Imaging), we proposed a tailor-made 3D directional Haar tight framelet for efficient and effective reconstruction of pMRI images. Moreover, a pMRI optimization model, which we coined l1-3DHSTF, by regularizing the 3DHF features on the 3-D coil image data is proposed to reduce the aliasing artifacts caused by the downsampling operation in the k-space (Fourier). Our numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the superiority and efficiency of our l1-3DHSTF model. See Part C, the conference paper in Proc. SPIE 11138, Wavelets and Sparsity XVIII, and the journal paper in Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis, 2022, 60:446-470. We develop a general theoretical framework for constructing Haar-type tight framelets on any compact set with a hierarchical partition. In particular, we construct a novel area-regular spherical Haar tight framelets with directionality. Moreover, we propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for spherical signal denoising and show that our proposed CNN model outperforms threshold methods. See Part C, the journal paper in IEEE Transaction on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, accepted in 2022.

11302218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302218.value: Potential for further development of the research would be the consideration of framelets on manifolds and graphs in connections to deep learning applications. One can consider the design of framelets on manifolds and graphs with specific consideration of the network architecture and application backgrounds, especially the convolutional operations for data defined beyond the Euclidean domains.

11302218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302218.value: In this project, we focus on the construction, characterizations, and applications of directional framelets on manifolds and graphs. In modern society, data become the centre of people's everyday life and the types of data can come from domains with nice geometric structure (smooth manifolds) or from non-structural domains such as graphs and networks. Directional framelet systems can be developed to cater the needs of various applications such as image/video processing, pMRI reconstructions, spherical data processing, and so on. We provide the constructions of directional framelets with a general framework for data analysis on manifolds and graphs as well as practical algorithms for effective and efficient data analysis on such domains.

11302318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302318.value: The increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration due to intensive consumption of fossil fuel has resulted in an unprecedented warm climate. Post-combustion CO2 capture (PCCC) has been considered as an effective approach to abate the CO2 emissions. In PCCC applications, aqueous solutions of alkaline amines are frequently applied as solvents to absorb CO2, with monoethanolamine (MEA) being the most commonly used species. On the other hand, MEA is released into ambient atmosphere together with the flue gas. The gas-phase MEA concentration can reach as high as ppm-levels, about two orders of magnitude higher than that of ammonia, especially in proximity to PCCC plants. This highlights the importance of MEA in atmospheric chemistry and air pollution. The gas-phase reactions of MEA have been shown to produce toxic gases and new aerosol particles. However, our understanding towards the heterogeneous reactions of MEA with existing aerosol particles remains limited. Heterogeneous reactions change the composition and physicochemical properties of aerosol particles and are important to understand the health impacts, light extinction and climate forcing exerted by aerosol particles. We propose to investigate the heterogeneous uptake of MEA by acidic aerosol particles. Sulfuric acid and oxalic acid are ubiquitous in ambient and used as representatives of inorganic and organic compounds, respectively, contributing to the acidity in aerosol particles. Experiments will be performed using near-source MEA concentration under different relative humidities (RHs) in order to reveal the capacity of MEA to neutralize aerosol acidity. Besides neutralization, it remains unclear whether other reaction pathways (e.g. esterification) are feasible. Therefore, we will carry out computational simulations to evaluate the feasibility of different reaction pathways between MEA and sulfuric (or oxalic) acid molecules at different RHs. These calculations will be used to interpret particle mass and Raman spectral changes during MEA uptake. MEA uptake by acidic particles produces monoethanolaminium (MEAH+) salts, whose water uptake behavior is closely related with the optical properties of aerosol particles. Unfortunately, little information on the hygroscopicities of MEAH+ salts is available. Therefore, we also propose to study the hygroscopicities of MEAH+ salts (sulfate, nitrate, chloride and oxalate due to their ambient ubiquities). Experimental results will be fitted empirically to predict particle-phase water content at any arbitrary RH, which is needed for the thermodynamic and kinetic analysis of MEA uptake. The overall goal of the project is to examine how MEA alters the composition and hygroscopic properties of acidic aerosol particles via heterogeneous uptake. 近年來，為降低二氧化碳（CO2）的排放量並減緩全球變暖的趨勢，燃燒後期的CO2捕集（PCCC）已成為一種切實有效並廣泛應用的工藝流程。在PCCC工藝中，鹼性的有機胺溶液被用作CO2的吸附劑，而乙醇胺（MEA）是最常用的胺類物質。但是，MEA會隨工藝尾氣一同排放至大氣環境中，其濃度可以高至ppm量級，甚至比氨（NH3）在大氣中的濃度高約2個數量級，這說明MEA對大氣化學過程和空氣污染具有重要潛在影響。現有研究結果表明，MEA在氣相中的反應可以產生有毒性的氣體（如亞硝胺）並可促進新粒子生成。另一方面，MEA在氣-顆粒非均相反應歷程中的作用尚不明確，而非均相反應能夠顯著改變顆粒物的化學組成以及物理化學性質。 本項目中，我們計劃研究MEA蒸氣被酸性顆粒物吸收的物理化學過程。硫酸和草酸對大氣顆粒物的酸性貢獻最為顯著，因此將作為酸性顆粒物的代表物。實驗將模擬在不同相對濕度下的MEA吸收過程，以此揭示MEA中和顆粒物酸度的能力。酸鹼中和被認為是MEA和酸性物質的主要反應機理，而除此之外的反應機理尚不明確。我們將利用數值模擬的方法全面考察MEA和硫酸、草酸的反應機理，評估顆粒物化學組分的複雜程度與反應條件的相關性。 MEA和酸性物質的中和反應將產生乙醇胺鹽，其吸濕性與大氣顆粒物的光學性質關係密切，而該類物質的吸濕性在文獻中鮮有報道。因此，我們將研究乙醇胺硫酸鹽、硝酸鹽、草酸鹽和氯化物的吸濕特性，並將實驗數據進行擬合，以預測任意相對濕度下的乙醇胺鹽含水量。本項目的綜合目標是探究MEA如何通過非均相吸收，以改變酸性顆粒物的組分和吸濕特性，進而更深入理解MEA在大氣化學和空氣污染過程中的影響。

11302318.value: Objective 2 (100% completed): Hygroscopic measurements of monoethanolaminium(MEAH+) sulfate, oxalate, nitrate and chloride salts was carried out in an Electrodynamic balance(EDB). Furthermore, hygroscopic measurements of at different molar ratios of MEAH:sulfate and MEAH:oxalate were made. These measurements were used to support the data analysis of the reaction uptake studies. Objective 1 (100% completed) We further investigated the reactive uptake of parts per million-level MEA by sulfuric acid particles in an EDB. The relative mass change of the levitated particles was the combined result of MEA uptake and changes in particle hygroscopicity due to compositional changes. The measured hygroscopicity from Objective 2 was used to analyze the particle composition change during MEA uptake and the uptake kinetics. The uptake coefficients were estimated to be (3.23 ± 0.64) × 10−3 and (9.89 ± 2.62) × 10−4 at 40% and 70% RH, respectively. Equilibrium compositions as a result of the uptake were also determined.

11302318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302318.value: Hygroscopic measurements of monoethanolaminium(MEAH+) sulfate, oxalate, nitrate and chloride salts was carried out in an Electrodynamic balance(EDB). From EDB experiments, no phase change was observed for MEAH+ sulfate, MEAH+ nitrate, MEAH+ chloride aerosol particles. Compared with their ammonium counterparts, these three MEAH+ salts aerosol particles contain more water under the same RH conditions. For MEAH+ oxalate aerosol particles at molar ratio of MEAH+ to oxalate of 2:1 and 1.5:1, efflorescence was observed at RH <10%. The deliquescence relative humidity (DRH) of MEAH+ oxalate aerosol particles at both two molar ratios was observed as ~92%RH. However, MEAH+ oxalate at 1:1 molar ratio does not have phase change, even under the RH as low as 3%. MEAH+ oxalate salts with these three molar ratios are more hygroscopic than their ammonium counterparts. Furthermore, empirical functions were fitted to the experimentally measured hygroscopicity data of monoethanolamine(MEA) salts for analyzing our reactive uptake data discussed below. We further investigated the reactive uptake of parts per million-level MEA by sulfuric acid particles in an EDB. The relative mass change of the levitated particles was the combined result of MEA uptake and changes in particle hygroscopicity due to compositional changes. The measured hygroscopicity was used to analyze the particle composition change during MEA uptake and the uptake kinetics. The uptake coefficients were estimated to be (3.23 ± 0.64) × 10−3 and (9.89 ± 2.62) × 10−4 at 40% and 70% RH, respectively. MEA reactive uptake by acidic particles could be competitive with respect to MEA gas-phase oxidation under high particle concentration conditions near power plants. Publications and presentations derived from the project were listed in Part C.

11302318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302318.value: Further to the uptake of gaseous MEA by sulfuric acid particles, the atmospheric fate of particulate MEA drew our attention. The lifetime of organic species oxidized by OH radicals in aqueous particles can be comparable to those in the gas phase. 1,2 Nitrate is one of the most abundant inorganic components in the atmosphere and found to coexist with amines in ambient particles. 3As a photoactive species, nitrate can be photolyzed to produce a series of oxidants, including OH radicals, NO2, O(3P) and N(III). 4 We have demonstrated in our earlier studies (not related to the current project) that these oxidants exert significant effects on the atmospheric oxidative capacity and promote the transformation of precursors into secondary organic aerosol(SOA). 5Thus, we hypothesize that nitrate photolysis may contribute to the decay of particulate MEA in the atmosphere. Thus, we propose to investigate the particulate MEA decay mediated by nitrate photolysis under different RH and pH, and study the SOA formation potential of MEA during nitrate photolysis in the future.

11302318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302318.value: Monoethanolamine (MEA) has been considered the most promising CO2 absorption solvent in power industries due to its fast absorption rate and low production cost. Given the massive application of MEA in the amine-based post-combustion CO2 capture technology, MEA is inevitably released into the atmosphere. The near-source concentration of MEA is as high as ppm level in the atmosphere. Such a high MEA emission highlights MEA as a potential environmental risk. Heterogeneous reactions change the composition and physicochemical properties of aerosols, and are important to understand the health impacts, light extinction and climate forcing exerted by aerosols. Thus we investigated the heterogeneous reactions of MEA with existing acidic aerosol particles, revealed another effective atmospheric sink pathway of MEA through the reactive uptake by sulfuric acid particles. The water uptake behavior is closely related with the optical properties of aerosol particles. In order to examine how MEA alters the hygroscopic properties of acidic aerosol particles via heterogeneous uptake, we also studied the hygroscopicities of MEAH+ salts. Our study shows that the uptake of MEA decreased the hygroscopicity of sulfuric acid aerosols. It means that heterogeneous reactions between MEA and sulfuric acid aerosols should play an important role in modification of particle properties.

11302418.label: Project Objectives
11302418.value: The only objective of this proposal is to design and analyze a new algorithm to compute the homology (Betti numbers and torsion coefficients) of an arbitrary semialgebraic set, i.e. a set given by a Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities. Algorithms doing this task already exist but they are inefficient (the only explicit upper bound on their performance is doubly exponential in the number n of variables of the defining polynomials) and suspect of numerical instability when finite precision is used. The goal of our proposal is to design an algorithm that should be more efficient (we expect its dependence on n will be single exponential only) and numerically stable.

11302418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302418.value: In the 1970's algorithms with doubly exponential complexity for computing cylindrical algebraic decompositions were designed and analyzed. These algorithms allowed to solve a host of computational problems related to real polynomial systems (of equalities and inequalities) and to their solution sets, known as semialgebraic. Since then, considerable effort was devoted to the design of algorithms for these problems whose complexity would be smaller than doubly exponential. These efforts lead to single exponential time for a good number of them: deciding whether a semialgebraic set is non-empty, computing its dimension, counting the number of its points (once we know the set to be zero-dimensional), or its Euler characteristic. A problem (admittedly, more difficult than the ones just mentioned) for which these efforts have not yet been rewarded is the computation of homology groups. To compute the list of these groups for an arbitrary semialgebraic set we still need doubly exponential time. A recent advance, however, exhibited an algorithm that computes these groups for basic semialgebraic sets in weak exponential time. That is, the algorithm is restricted to a subclass of semialgebraic set (which, unlike the whole class, is not closed under unions or complements) and its complexity is bounded by a single exponential bound provided the input data is not on a negligible set of outliers. The goal of this research proposal is to develop a similar result (i.e., to design and analyze an algorithm with a similar performance) for the whole class of semialgebraic sets. 在1970年代，设计并分析了计算圆柱代数分解的双指数复杂算法。这些算法允许解决许多问题 与实数多项式系统（等式和不等式）及其解集相关的计算问题，称为半代数。 从那以后，人们付出了相当大的努力来设计 这些问题的算法很复杂 小于双指数。 这些努力导致了大量的指数时间：确定半代数集是非空的，计算其维数，计算其点数（一次） 我们知道这个集合是零维的，或者它的欧拉特征。 一个问题（不可否认，比刚才提到的更难）这些努力尚未得到回报的是同源组的计算。计算这些组的列表 任意半代数集我们仍需要双倍指数时间。 然而，最近的进展展示了一种算法，该算法在弱指数时间内计算基本半代数集的这些组。也就是说，算法仅限于半代数的子类 set（与整个类不同，在联合或补语下不会关闭），并且它的复杂性受单个指数界限的限制，前提是输入数据不在一组可忽略的异常值上。 该研究提案的目标是制定类似的结果 （即设计和分析具有类似性能的算法.

11302418.value: Semialgebraic sets are probably the sets most used in applications of geometry to various fields. 11302518.label: Realisation of objectives
11302518.value: The objectives in the project have been fully addressed. The research results were written into four research papers, among them three have been published. First of all, the instability mechanisms for some degenerate PDE systems such as the MHD boundary layer system were investigated. Precisely, for the MHD boundary layer described by the Prandtl type equations derived from the incompressible viscous MHD system without resistivity, under the no-slip boundary condition on the velocity, a local-in-time well-posedness in Sobolev spaces is proved without the monotonicity condition on the velocity field. Moreover, we show that if the tangential magnetic field of shear layer is degenerate at one point, then the linearized MHD boundary layer system around the shear layer profile is ill-posed in the Gevrey function space provided that the initial velocity shear flow is non-degenerately critical at the same point. This shows that without any structural assumption, the Gevrey index for well-posedness is at most 2. Furthermore, we established the well-posedness in Gevrey function space with optimal class of index 2 for the three-dimensional Prandtl system without any structural assumption. More details of the research results will be presented in the next section. Finally, please note that one of the papers, titled `Magneto-micropolar boundary layers theory in Sobolev spaces without monotonicity: well-posedness theory', reported in the midterm report is not reported in this completion report. The reason is that I found that the analysis used in that paper has no significant novelty so that I decided not to continue to work on that manuscript.

11302518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302518.value: The major findings and research outcome will be briefly explained as follows. The first paper concerns with the magnetic effect on the Sobolev solvability of boundary layer equations for the 2D incompressible MHD system without resistivity. The MHD boundary layer is described by the Prandtl type equations derived from the incompressible viscous MHD system without resistivity under the no-slip boundary condition on the velocity. Assuming that the initial tangential magnetic field is not degenerate, a local-in-time well-posedness in Sobolev spaces is proved. Moreover, we show that if the tangential magnetic field of shear layer is degenerate at one point, then the linearized MHD boundary layer system around the shear layer profile is ill-posed in the Gevrey function space provided that the initial velocity shear flow is non-degenerately critical at the same point. In the second paper, we established the well-posedness in Gevrey function space with optimal class of regularity 2 for the three-dimensional Prandtl system without any structural assumption. The proof combines in a novel way a new cancellation in the system with some of the old ideas to overcome the difficulty of the loss of derivatives in the system. This shows that the three-dimensional instabilities in the system leading to ill-posedness are not worse than the two-dimensional ones. The fourth paper is about the vanishing viscosity and magnetic resistivity limit for the two dimensional steady incompressible MHD system on the half plane with no-slip boundary condition on velocity field and perfectly conducting wall condition on magnetic field. We prove the nonlinear stability of shear flow of Prandtl type with non-degenerate tangential magnetic field, but without any positivity or monotonicity assumption on the velocity field. It is in sharp contrast to the steady Navier-Stokes equations and reflects the stabilization effect of magnetic field. The main tools in the analysis are to design an intrinsic weight function to treat the incompatibility of the natural multiplier with the boundary condition as well as to establish critical Hardy type inequalities and proper weighted estimates that lead to an almost optimal convergence rate. In the third paper, we study the diffusion limit of the classical solution to the unipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with initial data near a global Maxwellian. We prove the convergence and obtain the convergence rate of the global strong solution of the unipolar VPB system to the solution of the incompressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson-Fourier system based on the spectral analysis with precise estimation on the initial layer.

11302518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302518.value: The MHD system is a very complicated and it describes rich physical phenomena. In addition to the physical regimes studied in this project, there are many other physical regimes in which the boundary layer may have similar or different behaviour. The analysis developed in this project can be useful for future study on this physical system in different settings, in particular, in three space dimensional case. The well-posedness of the three space dimensional Prandtl system in optimal Gevrey function space is established in this project. This solves a long standing open question for this classical system in fluid dynamics. It is expected that the auxiliary function approach used in the analysis can shed some light on the corresponding study of other physical models with strong boundary layer.

11302518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302518.value: The study on the hydrodynamics stability, instability and the inviscid limit of viscous fluid has a very long history both in physics and mathematics. The earliest systematic mathematical works can be traced back to Rayleigh, Orr, Sommerfeld and Heisendberg among many others. In early years, the spectral approach leads to famous equations like Rayleigh equation and Orr-Sommerfeld equation. As a fundamental system in boundary layer theory, Prandtl equation not only has vast applications in aerodynamics and fluid dynamics, but also provides a challenging mathematical model in the study of degenerate PDEs, in particular in the area of inviscid limit, for which a lot of interesting mathematical problems remain unsolved. The above mentioned problems are related to mathematical study on degenerate PDE systems with loss of tangential derivative property. Hence, we believe the progress in this project not only solves some essential problems in boundary layer theory, but also enriches the mathematical theories for the degenerate mixed type PDE systems.

11302718.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302718.value: 关于 Ginzburg-Landau 方程的高效数值方法及理论分析

11302718.label: Project Objectives
11302718.value: Develop robust and reliable numerical methods for solving time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau problems with emphasises on the equations under the temporal gauge in complicated three-dimensional geometries, including non-single connected regions and defected domains. During this project, we will study both Galerkin type or mixed type approximations in spatial direction and linearized and fully decoupled schemes in time direction. Such schemes are more effective since they only require the solution of linear systems at each time step and these systems can be solved in parallel. For three dimensional models, certain physical conservations, such as Gauss's law, will be conducted and a mesh adaptive technique will be applied to handle the corner singularity and to achieve a better global accuracy. Analysis of time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations has been done extensively under a smooth setting (boundary/initial conditions and domains). However, the problem in a defected superconductor is of high interest in physical and engineering applications since geometric defects seriously influence the generation and motion of vortices. On the other hand, the accuracy of numerical methods also heavily lies on the regularity of the solution of the equations. The regularity of the solution for the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations under both Lorentz gauge and temporal gauge in defected and complicated geometries will be investigated. Finally, we shall present rigorous numerical analysis for proposed numerical methods, including optimal error estimates and unconditional convergence. Due to the strong nonlinearity and coupling, the numerical analysis is not straightforward, although optimal error estimates of several classical methods for two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau equations under Lorentz gauge and smooth setting have been done. More attention will be paid to the three-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau equations under temporal gauge in defected and complicated regions. In this case, the system is degenerate in general.

11302718.value: The project is to develop robust and effective Galerkin type finite element methods and establish rigorous analysis for the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations in a general setting. It is well known that the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations have been widely used for describing physical properties of conventional superconducting materials in a magnetic field.
