11303318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11303318.value: 含CAAC卡賓配體的錸(I)與銥(III)配合物的設計、合成及研究

11303318.label: Project Objectives
11303318.value: To design, synthesize and characterize luminescent Re(I) and Ir(III) complexes with CAAC ligands; To study the reactivity of metal isocyanides for the formation of carbene ligands; To study the photophysical properties of the newly designed transition metal complexes and their uses as photosensitizers and photocatalysts.
rows: To design, synthesize and characterize luminescent Re(I) and Ir(III) complexes with CAAC ligands;
To study the reactivity of metal isocyanides for the formation of carbene ligands;
To study the photophysical properties of the newly designed transition metal complexes and their uses as photosensitizers and photocatalysts.

11303318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303318.value: The unique coordination chemistry and electronic properties of cyclic alkyl amino carbene (CAAC) ligands have led to the discovery of a large number of previously inaccessible main group elements, organometallic compounds and even radicals. Many of these metal CAAC complexes have been demonstrated to show catalytic activities for various important chemical transformations. Moreover, It has also been demonstrated that the replacement of NHC or phosphine ligand in various catalysts with CAAC ligand could lead to improvement on the catalytic performance. In this context, CAAC ligands and their transition metal complexes have received tremendous attention. However, the development of these ligands have been limited by the only feasible synthetic method for the preparation of CAACs, which is incompatible with varieties of functional groups and reaction conditions. In this project, new synthetic strategies for metal complexes with CAAC or acyclic alkyl amino carbene (AAAC) ligands will be developed. Using these methods, new classes of luminescent Re(I) and Ir(III) complexes with unprecedented CAAC or AAAC ligands will be synthesized. These complexes should exhibit intriguing photophysical, photochemical and excited state properties. Their applications in developing emissive materials and photocatalytic systems will also be investigated. It is anticipated that the versatility of the current synthetic methodologies together with the rich coordination chemistry of isocyanide ligands would open up a new avenue for the development of transition metal complexes with many different types of CAAC or AAAC ligands. 利用CAAC卡賓配體及其獨特的配位化學與電子性質，已開發出一些嶄新的化合物。當中有很多含CAAC卡賓的配合物更有不同的催化功用。利用CAAC卡賓配體取替NHC卡賓或膦配體更被証實能有效提升催化作用的功能。因此，CAAC卡賓配體及其配合物的研究引起廣范的關注。由於現時並沒有發展出有效及可廣范應用於合成CAAC卡賓配體的方法，這類的配合物的發展有相當的限制。 本研究項目將發展新的合成手段用於設計及合成含CAAC卡賓配體的配合物。以新發展的合成手段，制備一系列含CAAC及AAAC卡賓配體的錸(I)及銥(III)配合物，同時研究這些配合物用於發光物料及光催化劑的功能。

11303318.label: Realisation of objectives
11303318.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details findings are summarized as follows: Objective 1: New Re(I) and Ir(III) complexes with CAAC ligands derived from the isocyanide precursors have been designed and synthesized. As planned in the proposal, the CAAC ligands can be formed from the reactions of the metal isocyanide The newly synthesized transition metal complexes (both isocyanide precursors and carbene complexes) have been characterized by various spectroscopic techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis. The structures of some of these complexes have also been determined by X-ray crystallography. Some of the results have been reported in journal articles, Inorganic Chemistry Frontier 2020, and the book chapter entitled "Carbonyl and Isocyanide Complexes of Rhenium" in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV, listed in Part C. The results have also been presented in international conferences, 5th EuChemS Inorganic Chemistry Conference. Objective 2: The reactivity of the metal isocyanides for their chemical transformation into the carbene ligands has been investigated in detail through in-depth investigation with NMR, vibrational and time-resolved spectroscopies. The correlation between the isocyanide CN stretches and the reactivity has been established. This enables the development of the synthetic strategy for metal carbene complexes from the rational design of the metal isocyanide precursors. Moreover, we discovered a highly selective reaction between the coordinated isocyanoborato ligand with cyanide anion in the reactivity study. Therefore, the use of the isocyanoborato complex as a cyanide anion sensor has also been explored. Some of these results are reported in ChemPhysChem 2019, Organometallics 2020, and the book chapter entitled "Carbonyl and Isocyanide Complexes of Rhenium" in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV, listed in Part C, and have also been presented in ISPPCC 2019. Objective 3: Many of the newly developed Re(I) and Ir(III) isocyanide and carbene complexes display interesting photophysical and excited state properties. Through studying the absorption, emission, and electrochemical properties of these complexes, the structure-properties relationship has been established. Based on this result, metal complexes with strongly oxidizing and reducing emissive excited states have been developed. The applications of these complexes as photosensitizers and photocatalysts for organic transformations have been explored. Since these metal complexes can harvest visible light due to their strong absorption in the visible region. The visible-light photocatalytic reactions for various organic transformations, such as esterification, amidation, addition reaction and cross-coupling reaction, have been studied. Some of the results have been published in Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry 2020, listed in Part C, and presented in ISPPCC 2019.

11303318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303318.value: The research was conducted following the proposed research plan and methodology outlined in the proposal. Various Re(I) and Ir(III) isocyanide complexes have been designed, synthesized, and their reactivity studied using NMR, vibrational and time-resolved spectroscopies. With the reactivity study, it enables the development of the synthetic strategy for metal carbene complexes from the rational design of the metal isocyanide precursors. Using suitable metal isocyanide precursors, new Re(I) and Ir(III) complexes with CAAC ligands have been synthesized. All the newly synthesized transition metal complexes (both isocyanide precursors and carbene complexes) have been characterized by various spectroscopic techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis. The structures of some of these complexes have also been determined by X-ray crystallography. In addition to the characterization, the reactivity, spectroscopic, electronic, and luminescent properties of the precursor complexes and their acyclic carbene complexes have been investigated to establish the structure-properties relationships. In the reactivity study of the metal isocyanides, a highly selective reaction between the coordinated isocyanoborato ligand with cyanide anion has been discovered. Therefore, the use of the isocyanoborato complex as a cyanide anion sensor has also been explored. Many of the newly developed Re(I) and Ir(III) isocyanide and carbene complexes display interesting photophysical and excited state properties. Based on these properties, metal complexes with strongly oxidizing and reducing emissive excited states have been developed. Their applications as photosensitizers and photocatalysts for organic transformations have been explored. Since these metal complexes can harvest visible light due to their strong absorption in the visible region, the visible-light photocatalytic reactions for various organic transformations, such as esterification, amidation, addition reaction, and cross-coupling reaction, have been studied. Some of these results have been published in internationally refereed journals (Part C), including Inorg. Chem. Frontier, ChemPhysChem, Organometallics, Org. Biomol. Chem., as well as a book chapter in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV. Apart from publications in journal articles and book, the results have also been presented as a number of invited lectures at international conferences (Part C), including the 5th Euchems Inorganic Chemistry Conference and the 23rd International Symposium on the Photochemistry and Photophysics of Coordination Compounds. In short, the results of this project contribute to the development of new classes of transition metal isocyanide and carbene complexes. Many of these complexes display interesting reactivity, luminescence, electrochemical, and excited-state properties. Detailed study shows that these complexes can be used as phosphorescent materials, photosensitizers, photocatalysts, and chemosensors.

11303318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303318.value: As mentioned in 6.1, the results of this project have led to new classes of transition metal isocyanide and carbene complexes with novel properties such as reactivity, phosphorescent, photocatalytic, and chemosensing properties. On the basis of these results, we have initiated new directions to develop photocatalysts for photoredox organic transformation, chemosensors, and luminescent materials. A research proposal on the development of metal-based photochromic systems based on the interconversion between metal-carbene and metal-isocyanide using the results of this work has been supported by RGC. On the other hand, we have also developed a new class of luminescent chemosensors based on the reactivity study of this work.

11303318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303318.value: To meet the increasing demands for new luminescent materials, photocatalysts, and chemosensors, new families of luminescent transition metal isocyanide and carbene complexes with unique photofunctional properties have been developed and studied. Based on these transition metal complexes, new photocatalysts, luminescent materials, and chemical sensors have been designed. The scientific results of these functional properties have been published in internationally refereed journals and presented in several invited lectures at international conferences. In summary, new classes of luminescent transition metal complexes with properties suitable for developing new photofunctional materials have been developed in this project.

11303518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303518.value: 這一個項目是關於三維超音速激波的數學理論，特別是關注於附體激波以及相對論效應下的錐形激波和非相對論極限的數學理論。 當氣體通過契形物體，椎，或者飛行器的頭部的時候，激波經常被觀察到。更多關於定常無旋流的描述能夠在Courant-Friedrich的書上看到([24, p294-297]). 在這個項目中，我們會研究三維具有特殊結構的激波結構。三維激波不同於二維激波，原因在於多了＄x_3＄方向。事實上，三維附體強平面激波是不穩定的「43」。這一個結果和二維穩定性的結果很不一樣「4，21，44」，特別的，據我們所知，三維激波的全局解的結果很少。所以作為一個研究原型，這一個項目的研究可以貢獻於流體力學的數學理論。 自從Von Neumann [40,41]和Courant-Friedrich[24]提出了唯一性的公開問題（即強激波和弱激波哪一個是物理的），衝擊波穩定性的研究經歷了漫長的時間。到目前為止，二維穩定附體衝擊波的研究得到了滿意的結果，強弱激波都得到了唯一性和全局穩定性。然而，對於三維情況，所有的研究都在具有額外假設的條件下，例如，[7,19,22,32,33,34,43]中的圓錐衝擊的穩定性。最近，平面附體強激波的不穩定性，以及跨音速弱激波的穩定性在[8,31]中已經確定。另一方面，對於沒有圓錐形結構的超音速沖擊的全局存在和穩定性，很少有結果。例如（見[18,23]）超音速流過 具有足夠大的頂角的三角翼。因為三維超音速激波結果很少，但因為問題的重要性，對我們來說這個項目是有價值的。 多年來，我們一直致力於相關問題的研究。最近，我們在[28]中確立了二維附體衝擊的唯一性;激波正則反射的凸性[12]; 由非線性波動方程[6]和位勢流方程[11]決定的Lighthill問題。在這個項目中，我們將主要關註於進一步發展相關的方法去研究所提出的問題。

11303518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303518.value: There is a long-time debate on the open question of which of the weak shock and the strong shock is physical in the attached oblique shock structure. Mathematically, it is formulated into the existence, uniqueness, and stability of the shock solutions. The existence, uniqueness, and stability of the shock solutions in two dimensions have been successfully established by many great works. Recently, the instability of the three-dimensional irrotational strong plane shock is obtained by Li-Xu-Yin, which is published in Advances in Maths. Now, in the first objective, we showed the stability of the three-dimensional irrotational weak transonic plane shock. It provides a solid Mathematical understanding that the weak shock should be physical in the attached oblique shock structure. In the second objective, we found a connection between the Euler flows and the relative flows.

11303618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303618.value: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) as one of the emerging PV technologies has drawn a lot of attentions during the last few decades. The low manufacturing cost and unique optical and mechanical properties are attractive in various applications in the PV market. However, OPVs have been suffered from large photovoltage loss (>0.7eV) which limited its efficiency. Recently, OPVs using non-fullerene (NF) molecule as acceptor have achieved remarkable progress in power conversion efficiency(PCE) over 13%. The light absorbing layer in OPV is typically a blend of organic electron-donating polymers and electron-accepting molecules. During the last two decades, numerous highly efficient polymers have been reported, while the acceptors are mainly based on fullerene derivatives. Recently, several promising NF based acceptors have been synthesized which unlocked several engineering limitations in conventional fullerene based devices. They have optical absorption window can be tailored to compromise with the polymer donors to cover a broader absorption spectrum. More importantly, their energy level can be widely tuned to align with the donor to facilitate efficient exciton dissociation and maximize the open-circuit voltage. It is believed that using NF acceptors will be a key strategic approach to tackle the large photovoltage loss issue in OPVs. Despite of the recent encouraging improvement in device efficiency, strikingly, several reported high efficiency NF based OPVs have noticeably small photovoltage loss that apparently contradicts to the previous understanding of the photovoltaic process in OPVs. One has reported that the energy offset between the polymer donor and NF acceptor only 0.1-0.2eV, compared to the general wisdom of the required excess energy of >0.3 eV for efficiency exciton dissociation. In addition, one has found the total photovoltage loss only 0.5eV, compared to the >0.7eV that previously considered the unavoidable energy and recombination losses. Consequently, the energy budget and the origin of photovoltaic loss have become hot debating topics in OPVs. In this proposed project we are aiming at: (1) Theoretically, to develop a model to investigate the impact of energy offset on charge-transfer efficiency across the organic donor/acceptor (D/A) heterointerfaces. (2) Experimentally, to use a set of comprehensive techniques to systematically probe the energetics and charge-recombination of a series of OPVs with different energy offsets. Therefore, the success of this project combining theoretical and experimental results would not only bring insight into the origin of the large photovoltage loss in OPVs, but also provide strategies for further improving the device efficiency by materials engineering. 有机光伏(OPV)作为新兴光伏技术之一，在过去的几十年中已经引起了广泛的关注。低制造成本以及独特的光学和机械性能在光电市场的各种应用中具有吸引力。然而，有机光伏电池遭受大的光电压损失（> 0.7eV）， 这限制了其效率。最近，使用非富勒烯(NF)分子作为受体的有机光伏电池在功率转换效率（PCE)方面已经取得了显著的进步, 超过了13%。在有机光伏电池(OPV)中光吸收层通常是有机电子供体聚合物和电子受体分子的混合物。在过去的二十年里，大量的高效率聚合物已经被报道，而受体主要基于富勒烯衍生物。最近，已经合成了一些有希望的非富勒烯(NF) 基的受体，其解除了常规的富勒烯基器件上的若干工程限制。它们的光学吸收窗口可被调节，以便于和聚合物给体匹配以覆盖更宽的吸收光谱。更重要的是，它们的能级能被广泛地调整以和供体对齐，以促进有效的激子分离和开路电压最大化。相信使用NF受体将是解决有机光伏电池中大光电压损耗问题的一个关键战略方法。 尽管最近器件效率有了令人鼓舞的提高，但令人惊讶的是，一些报道的高效率的基于非富勒烯的有机光伏电池有着明显小的光电压损失，这显然与之前对OPV中光伏工艺的理解相矛盾。有人已报道，在聚合物供体和非富勒烯受体之间的能量偏移仅仅0.1-0.2eV，和通常认为的高效激子解离所需多余能量高于0.3eV形成对比。 此外，有研究发现总的光电压损失仅为0.5eV， 而之前认为的不可避免的能量和复合损耗>0.7eV。因此，能量预算和光伏损耗的起源已成为了有机光伏电池的热门争议话题。 在这个提案中，我们的目标是：（1）在理论上，我们将开发一个模型来探究能量偏移对有机供体/受体(D/A)异质结界面上电荷转移效率的影响。（2）在实验上，我们将使用一套综合技术系统地探测一系列具有不同能量偏移的有机光伏电池的能量和电荷复合。因此，这个课题成功的将理论和实验结果相结合，不仅会深入了解有机光伏电池中大光电压损耗的起源，而且提供通过材料工程对进一步提高器件效率的策略。

11303618.label: Realisation of objectives
11303618.value: O1: To develop a charge-transfer model to investigate the impact of electron back-transfer induced recombination at organic heterojunctions. (Percentage achieved 100%) To understand the back-transfer properties at organic heterojunctions, the charge-transfer (CT) characteristics of individual materials should be first determined. In this project, we developed an analytical model to extract the CT parameters in organic semiconductors measured by electroabsorption spectroscopy.[Liu et al, Nat. Comm. 10, 5089 (2019)] Using the conventional electroabsorption model based on Stark effect, we further incorporated the Kramers-Kronig relation to handle the impact of the optical effect on the resulting electroabsorption spectrum. Details of the derivation and discussion of the new model are available in the published journal attached along with this report. Briefly, using the new model, we are able to extract the polarizability p and dipole moment u of the excited states in organic thin films with high consistency. Resolving the long-term issue of inconsistent values reported in the literature. As shown in Figure 7 in [Liu et al, Nat. Comm. 10, 5089 (2019)], using the new model considering k and n, the extract p and u have excellent agreement in devices with different film thicknesses. Moreover, using the developed model, we successfully extracted the CT parameters in various organic photovoltaic (OPV) materials. In particular, we found that in the recently developed high-efficiency non-fullerene electron acceptor Y6, the strong CT character is attributed to its unique molecular packing. We also found that the conservation of exciton polarizability plays a key role in the strong CT character in Y6, instead of the large increase in dipole moment that commonly observed in other organic systems. As shown in Figure 6 in [Mahadevan et al, submitted to Nat. Comm., under review], an exciton recombination model considering the overlap of the electron-hole wavefunctions is proposed to elucidate the experimental findings. The results of this work have been submitted for publication which is currently under review.[Mahadevan et al, submitted to Nat. Comm., under review] O2: To determine the role of different energetics at organic heterojunctions responsible for the photovoltaic process. (Percentage achieved 100%) We sought to investigate the impact of different energetics in organic materials responsible for the photovoltaic process. We systemically studied five different Y-series non-fullerene acceptors as shown in Figure 1 in [Zhange et al, ACS Energy Lett. 7, 1971 (2022)]. In collaboration with Prof. So in HKBU with their photothermal deflection technique and the highly-sensitive external quantum efficiency (s-EQE) developed in our group, we successfully measured the Urbach energy EU of the Y-series acceptors. It has been shown that the smaller EU is correlated to the smaller carrier recombination in semiconductor devices. We found that the EU around 30 meV in Y-series acceptor is significantly smaller than those previously reported in OPV materials.[Zhange et al, ACS Energy Lett. 7, 1971 (2022)] However, compared to the inorganic counterparts (e.g. Si, GaAs, InP) used in photovoltaics, the EU is still large in Y-series acceptor. To further understand this limitation, we conducted the variable temperature s-EQE measurement, which can differentiate the static (structural) and dynamic (thermal) energy disorder contributions to the EU. Interestingly, we found that the large EU is contributed by the large static disorder, which is three to five folds larger than those in inorganic PV materials. Importantly, the results suggest that better OPV performance can be achieved by further optimizing the side chains and restricting the end-group rotations to reduce the static disorder. O3: To find out the theoretical efficiency limit in OPVs and strategies to reduce photovoltage losses due to energy offset and non-radiative recombination with materials engineering. (Percentage achieved 80%) According to the above studies on the Y-series acceptors, we demonstrated that one strategy to improve the OPV performance is by optimizing the side chains and restricting the end-group rotations to reduce the static energy disorder. Another widely discussed issue in OPV is the large non-radiative recombination. Using the electroabsorption (EA) technique as mentioned in O1, we found that the strong CT character in Y acceptor is due to the conservation of polarizability p from ground to excited states. In fact, the polarizability of molecules is correlated to the delocalization of the wavefunctions of electrons and holes. This suggests that the recombination can be reduced by designing a molecule where its electron and hole orbitals are localized in different moieties within a molecule. In a recent collaboration with theorists, we found that by reducing the overlapping of electron and hole wavefunctions, it can noticeably reduce the non-diabetic coupling between the ground and exciton states, and therefore the non-radiative recombination. Experimentally, as shown in Figure 2c in [Chen et al, submitted to Nat. Energy, under review], we demonstrated that materials having reduced orbital overlapping, such as the Y6 acceptors, their photoluminance (PL) lifetime can as long as nano-second scale, whereas the most typical OPV materials have PL lifetimes in pico-second scale. However, the quantitative correlation between the recombination rate and orbital overlapping parameter are not well established. In addition, other materials characteristics, such as static disorder, which has been recently found to determine photovoltaic performance. These pave challenges to predict the efficiency limit in OPVs. Possibly, a more fundamental model, such as the Marcus theory, should be considered in the future direction of this research.

11303618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303618.value: This project attempted to investigate the correlation between the materials’ electronic properties (charge transfer, energetics, recombination) and the photovoltaic performance. Importantly, as demonstrated in this study, those materials’ properties can be parameterized, such as polarizability, dipole moment, Urbach energy, non-diabetic coupling, overlapping parameters. Therefore, in order to establish a strong correlation systematically and quantitively, future studies should closely collaborate with a chemical synthesis team. A series of materials with finely tuned material parameters should be synthesized and characterized. It would bring insight into the understanding of the theoretical limit in organic solar cells.

11303618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303618.value: In this project, we combined several advanced electronic and optical characterization techniques to investigate the charge-transfer process in organic solar cells. For the first time, we experimentally demonstrated that molecular packing can efficiently facilitate the charge-transfer. Importantly, we demonstrated that achieving efficient charge-transfer not only requires a well separation between the charges, but also the orbitals of the charges moving within the molecules. By further investigating the energy profile and charge orbital in a series of different organic photovoltaic materials, our studies suggest that OPV performance can be further improved by reducing the molecular structure disorder and charge orbital distribution by molecular design.

11303718.value: 不可压缩生物材料的渐进自洽动态板壳模型：理论与应用

11303718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303718.value: 虽然任何物体总是三维的，但是在自然界及工程应用中有很多物 体的结构通常很薄，即它们的厚度尺寸要远小于另外两个维度的 尺寸。在这种情况下， 人们称呼这种结构的物体为板壳。例如， 皮肤，心膜，叶子，花瓣，动脉，飞机机翼和冷却塔都是板壳。 由于厚度很小，人们可以采用一个二维 (2D) 的模型来研究板壳 的行为，而不是三维 (3D) 的模型（由于纵横比非常小，三维模 型的计算量很大）。另一方面，生物材料通常比较柔软。这种类 型材料的一个特征是它们可以在经历有限应变的情况下，发生大 的变形。并且，这种材料一般情况下是不可压缩的（在变形期间 体积不会改变）。通常，为了研究生物材料的力学行为，人们会 使用带有不可压缩约束条件的应变能函数将它们建模为不可压缩 的超弹性材料。文献中已经有很多小应变板壳理论，（例如， Donell的板壳理论和Koiter的板壳理论），这些板壳理论最初是为 了研究硬质材料 （例如钢）而发展起来的。然而，相对来讲，具 有不可压缩约束条件的有限应变板壳理论就要少得多了。特别地 ，还没有文献推导过一致动态有限应变板壳理论来研究同时带有 弯曲和拉伸效应的不可压缩超弹性材料。本课题的主要目的是基 于带有不可压缩约束条件的应变能函数，推导出动态有限应变板 壳理论，以此来研究生物材料。我们的推导将采用一般形式的应 变能函数，而对于特定的生物材料，可以选用特定的应变能函数 （有一些可以在文献中得到）。我们将证明推导出的板壳理论与 三维的Hamilton原理保持渐进一致。理论的推导过程是建立在关 于底平面的级数展开之上的，它的新颖之处在于发现了应力、拉 格朗日常数以及位移（位置）系数之间的一些线性关系（虽然原 先的问题是高度非线性的）。这些线性关系建立了展开系数之间 的递推关系，使得最终的系统只含有三个未知量。在此之后，我 们将提出适当的边界条件，并且为数值计算推导出相关的弱形式 。 此推导出的板壳理论将用于研究与人类动脉相关的几个问题。 第一个问题与固有频率相关。如果环境的频率与人类动脉的频率 相当，那么人们会感到不舒服。另一个问题是通过研究解的分岔 行为来理解人体动脉中血管瘤的形成，这也是近年来的一个研究 热点。以前的研究者通常使用膜管模型来进行后分岔分析，而不 考虑弯曲或者厚度带来的影响。而利用我们推导出的板壳理论， 拉伸和弯曲效应都可以被考虑进来。此外，我们还将考虑由于血 液流动而带来的剪切应力，这在先前的研究中通常是被忽略的， 但是其影响却有可能是重要的。我们希望，推导出来的不可压缩 超弹性材料的动态板壳理论可以在薄生物结构中得到广泛的应用， 并且对血管瘤的研究可以帮助进一步阐明这一重要现象。

11303918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303918.value: 變量選擇是高緯數據分析的一個核心問題，並擁有廣泛的應用。很多現實情景擁有大量的變量，大家廣泛認為其中只有一小部分是與分析的目標真正相關的，所以找出這一小部分真正相關的變量就成了接下來的統計建模的關鍵之所在。在過去二十年，很多變量選擇的方法被提出來，它們或者以來顯式的模型假設，或者需要很大的計算成本。本研究項目旨在提出一個全新的分三步走的變量選擇方法，它包括對於回歸函數及其導數函數的基於核的估計，以及一個硬截斷的變量選擇的標準。這個方法最主要的優勢在於它不需要模型假設，允許一般性的變量效果，允許有效的科學計算，並且可以達到很好的大樣本變量選擇相合性。在關於方法和理論的研究同時，本研究項目主持人也會致力與發展有效的計算算法和平台，以推廣新方法在大規模變量選擇中的應用。

11303918.label: Realisation of objectives
11303918.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators develop an efficient three-step statistical method, involving kernel-based estimation of the regression function and its gradient functions as well as a hard thresholding. The idea is based on the equivalence between whether a variable is informative and whether its corresponding gradient function is substantially non-zero. The proposed method compares favorably with the existing model-free variable selection method in literature. It can be applied to analyze datasets with 100,000 variables on a standard multi-core PC, and its asymptotic consistency can be established without requiring any explicit model assumptions. The proposed method is also extended to discovering interaction structure for partially linear models (PLMs). Particularly, the PI and this collaborator propose a model-free structure selection method for the PLMs, which aims to discover the model structure in the PLMs through automatically identifying variables that have linear or nonlinear effects on the response. The proposed method is formulated in a framework of gradient learning, equipped with a flexible reproducing kernel Hilbert space. The resultant optimization task is solved by an efficient proximal gradient descent algorithm. More importantly, the asymptotic estimation and selection consistencies of the proposed method are established without specifying any explicit model assumption, which assure that the true model structure in the PLMs can be correctly identified with high probability. The effectiveness of the proposed method is also supported by a variety of simulated and real-life examples. The PI and his collaborators further extend the proposed method to recover the sparse structure of the conditional distribution, which plays a crucial role in subsequent statistical analysis such as prediction, forecasting, conditional distribution estimation and others. Unlike most existing methods that often require explicit model assumption or suffer from computational burden, the proposed method shows great advantage by making use of some desirable properties of reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). It can be efficiently implemented by optimizing its dual form and is particularly attractive in dealing with large-scale dataset. The asymptotic consistencies of the proposed method are established under mild conditions. Its effectiveness is also supported by a variety of simulated examples and a real-life supermarket dataset from Northern China. All proposed methods are implemented in R, and available upon request. The PI is also closely working with one of the collaborators to wrap up all the implementations in both Python and R packages for dissemination in the coming year.

11303918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303918.value: The major findings of this project are four-folds. First, the PI and his collaborators develop efficient statistical methods for selecting informative variables in high-dimensional regression and classification (Part C Output 1&2). The key advantages of the proposed method are that it includes no explicit model assumption, admits general predictor effects, allows efficient computation, and attains desirable asymptotic sparsistency. The proposed method can be adapted to any reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with different kernel functions, and its computational cost is only linear in the data dimension. Second, the proposed method is extended to recover the sparse structure of the conditional distribution, which plays a crucial role in subsequent statistical analysis such as prediction, forecasting, conditional distribution estimation and others (Part C Output 6). It focuses on identifying all the covariates acting on the conditional distribution by taking advantages of the nice properties of RKHS. The implementation of the proposed method is computationally efficient by using dual optimization, and is particularly useful to deal with large-scale cases. The asymptotic consistency of the proposed method is established without requiring any explicit model conditions and the numerical experiments illustrate the superior performance of the proposed method against some state-of-the-art competitors. Third, this project also develops tools to bridge classical machine learning framework to modern high-dimensional data analysis (Part C Outputs 3, 4 & 5). Particularly, the regularization techniques developed for the high-dimensional data can be well adapted to various machine learning tasks, leading to interpretable machine learning models, efficient computational schemes, and superior numerical performance.

11303918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303918.value: One potential development is to extend the proposed regularization method to estimation of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) for causal inference. Recovering the directed edges in DAGs can be naturally converted into a series of sparse regression tasks. The PI and his PhD student are now working on this extension, by fully utilizing the desirable properties of the developed regularization method. The preliminary numerical experiments are very promising, and the required computational cost can be substantially reduced without any sacrifice of the estimation accuracy. The PI plans to admit another PhD student or a RA to join the research team and complete the theoretical guarantees of these extensions.

11303918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303918.value: This proposed research project develops novel statistical methods and computing algorithms for high-dimensional regression and classification. All the objectives are achieved, and an efficient machine learning framework is developed, which is in sharp contrast to most existing methods in literature. The research findings have a wide spectrum of applications in practice, ranging from biomedicine, economics and finance, and information technology. The proposed research not only develop a novel perspective of conducting variable selection in regression and classification, but also provide rich opportunities for postgraduate students to participate in cutting-edge researches. With the support of this project, the PI and his collaborators published 6 research articles on leading statistics and machine learning journals, and trained two Ph.D. students Dr. Ben Dai and Dr. Shirong Xu. Dr. Dai is currently Assistant Professor at CUHK, and Dr. Xu is currently Adjunct Assistant Professor at UCLA in US. More importantly, this project also opens up a few potential directions for future research on learning complex structure in large-scale data.

11304018.value: 基於機器學習方法對量子點自旋比特的抗噪操控

11304018.label: Project Objectives
11304018.value: Noise spectroscopy by randomized benchmarking using supervised learning. Quantum state preparation and transfer using reinforcement learning. Gate optimization assisted by reinforcement learning.
rows: Noise spectroscopy by randomized benchmarking using supervised learning.
Quantum state preparation and transfer using reinforcement learning.

11304018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304018.value: The quantum technology is expected to outperform present-day computational technologies in many important classes of problems. Semiconductor spin qubits are being actively studied as one of the leading candidates to host a quantum computer, and accurate control of spin qubits is key to the realization of quantum computing. Among the various techniques to improve the control accuracy, the dynamically corrected gates--which make noises cancelling themselves--are effective means to reduce gate errors. Composite pulse sequences that correct errors dynamically have been developed for both the singlet-triplet qubit and the exchange-only qubit. On the other hand, more and more laborious tasks are conducted by trained machines thanks to the development of artificial intelligence. Machine learning is a powerful tool that allows data analysis or optimization that is beyond the ability of human being or any enumerative methods previously imagined. In this project, we are going to use two methods from machine learning to the quantum control of spin qubits: supervised learning and reinforcement learning. We will develop techniques to measure the noise spectra of quantum devices using supervised learning, in which a neural network is trained with simulated randomized benchmarking results. We will also apply reinforcement learning to two important classes of problems in manipulating quantum states: quantum state preparation and transfer. Last, with the assistance of reinforcement learning, we shall develop quantum control sequences that are optimized as compared to previously found ones, both in terms of their length and complexity but also regarding to specific functions that we desire. In particular, we aim to develop composite pulse sequences that cancel noises with certain spectra which is beyond the low-frequency noises previously studied. As an outcome of this study, we believe the combination of machine learning and quantum control shall offer us new techniques and understanding in controlling spin qubit systems, which may potentially shed light on the endeavor toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation. 量子技術被期待在多類重要問題中勝過當今的計算技術。半導體自旋量子比特作為實現量子計算的候選體系之一，對其精確調控的核心在於如何使 環境噪聲的影響最小化。在多種提高操控精度的方法中，動力學修正量子門較為有效。對單態——三重態量子比特和純交換耦合量子比特，人們發展了抗噪的覆合脈沖序列。另一方面，人工智能的發展為我們提供了全新的思路。機器學習是一個分析和優化數據的強大工具，強過很多傳統的枚舉方法。在本項目中，我們利用兩種機器學習的方法嘗試解決量子比特的抗噪操控的問題：監督學習和強化學習。我們應用監督學習進行測量量子點器件的噪聲譜的一個可行方法。我們還將應用強化學習到兩類問題：量子態制備和量子態轉移。最後，應用強化學習，我們研究對量子控制序列進行優化的方法，包括長度和效率等方面的優化。特別是我們期待發展對特定頻譜噪聲敏感的抗噪控制序列。我們相信，機器學習技術和量子控制的結合可以給我們對自旋量子比特系統的控制提供新的思路。

11304018.label: Realisation of objectives
11304018.value: All objectives set forth in the project have been realized with abundant results. We provide details below. For Task 1, we used supervised learning assisted by randomized benchmarking to study noise spectrum, in particular the 1/f type [1]. A 1/f noise involves a noise exponent alpha (related to the correlation within the noise) and an amplitude A (related to the strength of the noise). We determine the two parameters in two steps. Our method can predict the noise exponent with an absolute error of about ±0.05, and the noise amplitude within a relative error of about 5%, about the same order of magnitude with other methods. [1] Spin-qubit noise spectroscopy from randomized benchmarking by supervised learning, C. Zhang, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A. 99, 042316 (2019). For Task 2, we employed the reinforcement learning technique to study the quantum state preparation and quantum state transfer problem [4]. While we study these problems, we have also made a comparison between reinforcement learning techniques and several other non-machine-learning methods such as GRAPE and Krotov methods. We have found that reinforcement learning is more adaptive and therefore more efficient in some cases. [4] When does reinforcement learning stand out in quantum control? A comparative study on state preparation, X.-M. Zhang, Z. Wei, R. Asad, X.-C. Yang, and X. Wang, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 85 (2019). For Task 3, we considered the decomposition of a general single-qubit gate, especially when the decomposition is optimal, i.e. the resulting combination of elementary operations is minimal [2]. We studied the dependence of this minimal decomposition on available control axes, which shed light on how these gate operations can be optimized. [2] Minimal nonorthogonal gate decomposition for qubits with limited control, X.-M. Zhang, J. Li, X. Wang, and M.-H. Yung, Phys. Rev. A 99, 052339 (2019). We also studied a general error mitigation technique for Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices which only demand minimal resources. In [6] we developed a method to reduce error using quantum autoencoders, which is particularly useful for NISQ devices as it does not require extra qubits, can be applied to various noisy situations, and is more powerful than existing techniques in many cases. [6] Generic detection-based error mitigation using quantum autoencoders, X.-M. Zhang, W. Kong, M. U. Farooq, M.-H. Yung, G. Guo, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 103, L040403 (2021). We have also applied the idea of geometric quantum computation to silicon-based spin qubits, namely the quantum control is realized using geometric phase, a global property that is robust to local fluctuations. We have realized high-fidelity gates in these systems [5]. [5] High-fidelity geometric gate for silicon-based spin qubits, C. Zhang, T. Chen, S. Li, X. Wang, and Z.-Y. Xue, Phys. Rev. A 101, 052302 (2020). We also studied the problem of quantum parameter estimation, an important problem in quantum control and quantum sensing. We have found that as compared to traditional gradient-based methods, reinforcement learning is more generalizable, i.e. an agent trained at one parameter value can be straightforwardly extended to other values, making massive estimations much more efficient. The single-parameter case was studied in [3] and multi-parameter case was studied in [8]. [3] Generalizable control for quantum parameter estimation through reinforcement learning, H. Xu, J. Li, L. Liu, Y. Wang, H. Yuan, and X. Wang, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 82 (2019). [8] Generalizable control for multiparameter quantum metrology, H. Xu, L. Wang, H. Yuan, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. A 103, 042615 (2021). We have also studied quantum devices, in particular the singlet-triplet qubit. For a traditional singlet-triplet qubit hosting two electrons, we have found a method to suppress the charge noise by applying external magnetic fields [7]. We have also found that the robustness of entangling gates can be further enhanced if we allow a singlet-triplet qubit to host more than two electrons [9]. [7] Charge noise suppression in capacitively coupled singlet-triplet spin qubits under magnetic field, G. X. Chan, J. P. Kestner, and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. B 103, 161409 (2021) [9] Robust entangling gate for capacitively coupled few-electron singlet-triplet qubits, G. X. Chan and X. Wang, Phys. Rev. B 106, 075417 (2022)

11304018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304018.value: 1. We used supervised learning assisted by randomized benchmarking to study 1/f noise spectrum, which measures relevant parameters within an error rate on par to other methods. 2. We employed the reinforcement learning technique to study the quantum state preparation and quantum state transfer problem and found that reinforcement learning is more adaptive and efficient compared to traditional methods. 3. We considered the minimal decomposition of a general single-qubit gate which is useful for its optimization. 4. We developed a method to reduce error using quantum autoencoders, which is particularly useful for NISQ devices. 5. We applied geometric quantum computation to silicon-based spin qubits, achieving high-fidelity gates. 6. We studied the problem of quantum parameter estimation and have found that as compared to traditional gradient-based methods, reinforcement learning is more generalizable. This is true in both single- and multi-parameter case. 7. For a traditional singlet-triplet qubit hosting two electrons, we have found a method to suppress the charge noise by applying external magnetic fields. We have also found that the robustness of entangling gates can be further enhanced if we allow a singlet-triplet qubit to host more than two electrons.

11304018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304018.value: Several research directions warrant further study. First, the potential of using reinforcement learning to find optimal quantum control has not been fully explored. Currently most optimal control methods assume that the noise spectrum is quasi-static, while in realistic situations the noise spectrum is complicated. We would like to explore how reinforcement learning can help optimize quantum gates for a general noise. Also, we would like to extend the application of geometric gates to other spin qubit systems. We also want to study how machine-learning methods can be integrated into Shortcut to Adiabaticity, an important method in quantum control.

11304018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304018.value: In this project, we applied machine learning methods to various theoretical problems arising in quantum control. We used supervised learning to measure noise spectrum, resulting in an accuracy comparable to other methods. We employed reinforcement learning to study the quantum state preparation and quantum state transfer problem and found that reinforcement learning is more adaptive and efficient compared to traditional methods. We considered the minimal decomposition of a general single-qubit gate and developed a method to reduce error using quantum autoencoders, particularly useful for recent quantum devices. We realized high-fidelity geometric quantum gates in silicon-based spin qubits. We studied the problem of quantum parameter estimation and have found that as compared to traditional gradient-based methods, reinforcement learning is more generalizable. We have found a method to suppress the charge noise by applying external magnetic fields in traditional singlet-triplet qubit hosting two electrons, and we have also found that the robustness of entangling gates can be further enhanced if we allow a singlet-triplet qubit to host more than two electrons.

11304118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304118.value: Lysine lipoylation is the covalent attachment of a lipoyl group to lysine residues in proteins. Lysine lipoylation has been found in a number of important metabolic enzyme complexes, such as pyruvate deydrogenase (PDH). Literatures have shown that lysine lipoylation is essential for maintaining the activity of these enzyme complexes. A recent study discovered that SIRT4 could serve as lipoamidase and remove the lipoyl group from PDH complex, resulting in the loss of activity of PDH. Till date, research on lysine delipoylation has been very limited. In this project, we seek to develop novel chemical tools to investigate delipoylating enzymes. Such tools will expand our understanding of the roles of lipoamidases in various biological processes. We will first develop fluorescent probes that can report delipoylation activity. A panel of peptide-based fluorescent probes will be designed and synthesized to detect the delipoylation activity of enzymes. Upon incubating the probe with a suitable enzyme, delipoylation will occur and the fluorescence will be “turned on”. We will test the probes with various sirtuins. Through the study, we will generate reaction-based fluorescent probes to detect the activity of delipoylating enzymes for the first time. Our preliminary results demonstrated that SIRT1 and SIRT2 can recognize lipoyl-lysine residue as substrate. In the next step, we will develop mechanism-based inhibitors based on lipoyl-lysine substrate. Previous study has shown that thiolacetyl-lysine-containing peptides can inhibit sirtuin activity by forming a stable ADP ribose adduct. We hypothesize that thiollipoyl-lysine residue could be recognized by SIRT1/2 and form stable ADP ribose adduct as well. A library of inhibitors incorporating thiollipoyl-lysine moiety will be designed and synthesized. Subsequently the inhibitor libraries will be anchored onto microarray to investigate the binding specificity of sirtuins. Through the research, we hope to identify potent sirtuin inhibitors, which can be developed into useful anti-cancer agents. In the third part of the study, we will seek to generate chemical tools both to detect and to identify novel delipoylating enzymes in complex cellular environment. We will introduce a photo-cross-linker diazirine into our model probe. After being synthesized, the probes will first be used to detect the delipoylation activity in cellular lysates. They will then be applied to protein profiling experiments with various cancer cellular lysates. Through these experiments, novel endogenous delipoylating enzymes will be identified. 11304318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304318.value: Platinum-based anticancer drugs including cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin are the first-line clinical treatment against a variety of solid tumors such as testicular, cervical, head and neck, ovarian, and colorectal. These drugs have minimum selectivity against tumors, however, which can lead to severe toxic side effects. Much effort has been devoted to the development of next-generation platinum drugs with an enhanced therapeutic window but with low toxicity. In this proposed project, we aim to obtain a novel series of platinum(IV) prodrugs that can be activated by visible light to overcome the issues of conventional platinum complexes. We make full use of the advantages of octahedral platinum(IV) moiety based on clinically used platinum drugs and offer the drugs photoactivation properties, especially by visible light. Our initial study showed that an oxaliplatin-based platinum(IV) prodrug is remarkably stable in the dark even in the presence of a reducing agent and that the prodrug is quickly photoactivated to release oxaliplatin. This platinum(IV) prodrug is significantly active against platinum-resistant human ovarian cancer cells with cytotoxicity enhanced up to three orders of magnitude over that of oxaliplatin. These data form the basis for the further development of photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs. The complexes will be designed, synthesized, and well characterized. Their photophysical and photochemical properties will be scrutinized, and their photoactivation mechanism will be examined. In vitro biological activity including phototoxicity and the intracellular action mechanism will be tested, and in vivo toxicity and antitumor activity will be revealed. The proposed project will generate a couple of leading prodrugs with high stability and a localized cytotoxic effect, and these prodrugs are expected to have increased selectivity and lowered toxicity. The project will also foster the creation of a new toolkit in the area of medicinal inorganic chemistry for both chemical and biological applications. 铂类抗癌药物包括顺铂、卡铂和奥沙利铂是临床中治疗多种实体瘤的一线药物。然而，这些药物对肿瘤缺乏选择性，容易产生严重的毒副作用。科研工作者一直致力于研发具有更广阔治疗范围并且低毒性的新一代铂类抗肿瘤药物。本项目中，我们设计了一系列利用可见光激活的四价铂前药，从而克服传统铂类药物选择性低、毒副作用高等缺点。我们充分利用了四价铂的八面体空间构型，使这些基于临床用药的四价铂前药具有光敏特性，尤其是可见光激活的光敏特性。前期研究结果显示，基于奥沙利铂的一种四价铂前药在黑暗的还原条件下十分稳定；然而这种四价铂前药能够在光照条件下迅速活化，有效杀死癌细胞。其细胞毒性在耐药性的人源卵巢癌细胞中比奥沙利铂高一千倍以上。这些结果为进一步发展光敏性四价铂前药提供了基础。在本项目中，我们将设计、合成一系列具有光敏活性的四价铂前药，并对这些前药进行充分的化学表征和光激活机理研究。将测试前药的体外光照毒性和细胞内作用机理。本项目致力于研发若干具有高活性和高选择性的抗癌前药，从而为生物无机化学在抗癌药物研发领域的应用提供新的思路和借鉴。

11304318.label: Realisation of objectives
11304318.value: Objective 1: To design, synthesize, and characterize visible light-activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs We used a clinical anticancer drug, oxaliplatin, as the scaffold; with a photosensitizer, pyropheophorbide a, as the photoactivation group, we obtained a Pt(IV) prodrug, phorbiplatin, that can be effectively reduced to oxaliplatin upon 650 nm red light irradiation. Phorbiplatin is fully characterized by ESI-MS, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, 195Pt NMR, and HPLC. Phorbiplatin is the first Pt(IV) complex that can be activated by red light, whereas other reported photoactivable Pt(IV) complexes are activated by UV or blue light. The long activation wavelength brings phorbiplatin enhanced tissue penetration ability, making it more suitable for in vivo cancer treatment. Objective 2: To study photoactivation property and possible activation mechanism We used HPLC, LC-MS, 195Pt NMR, UV-Vis, cyclic voltammetry, fluorescence spectroscopy, and tranisent laser spectroscopy to thoroughly investigate the photoreduction properties of phorbiplatin in the physiological environment. Combined with DFT calculation, a possible photoreduction mechanism of phorbiplatin is proposed. First, phorbiplatin is excited to its singlet excited state under irradiation, and the singlet excited phorbiplatin goes to its triplet excited state through intersystem crossing (ISC). The triplet excited PPA moiety within phorbiplatin can accept an electron from an electron donor (e.g., ascorbate) to generate a Pt(IV) complex containing ground state PPA Π radical anion. Then, PPA radical anion transfers one electron to the Pt(IV) center to yield a Pt(III) complex along with the disassociation of the corresponding axial ligands. The formed Pt(III) complex will then be easily and rapidly reduced to a Pt(II) complex. Objective 3: To test the stability of the photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs The stability of phorbiplatin in both phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH = 7.4) and cancer cells was investigated by HPLC and LC-MS. In the dark condition, phorbiplatin presented great stability; more than 96% of phorbiplatin remained intact in PBS buffer after incubation for 24 h. In the presence of reducing agent (ascorbate), more than 89% of phorbiplatin remained after 24 h. Even in cancer cells, more than 80% of phorbiplatin is kept intact after incubation for 24 h, suggesting phorbiplatin is stable enough in the dark condition. Compared with other reported photoactivatable Pt(IV) complexes, phorbiplatin possesses both great stability and effective photoreduction property. Objective 4: To study in vitro cytotoxicity and action mechanism of the prodrugs in cancer cells The cytotoxicity of phorbiplatin against several cancer cell lines was investigated by MTT assay. Oxaliplatin and PPA were used as the controls. A lung fibroblast cell line, MRC 5, was used as the normal cells to test the toxicity of phorbiplatin towards normal cells. In the dark condition, phorbiplatin is non-toxic towards all the tested cell lines; whereas upon red light irradiation, the cytotoxicity of phorbiplatin is significantly increased. Compared with oxaliplatin, phorbiplatin presented up to 1786-fold increased cytotoxicity. Importantly, phorbiplatin successfully overcame the resistance of cancer cells toward platinum drugs, with the resistance factor as low as 0.68. The mechanism of action of phorbiplatin is studied as well. DNA is the main target of platinum drugs. In the dark condition, only 28 pg Pt per mg DNA was detected in the phorbiplatin-treated cells; whereas after red light irradiation, the Pt-DNA binding level increased to 110 pg Pt per mg DNA and resulting a high level of Pt in genomic DNA. Besides binding to DNA, we confirmed that phorbiplatin generated a huge amount of single oxygen and hydroxyl radicals to damage cancer cells. These results indicate that phorbiplatin could both directly bind to DNA and generate ROS to kill cancer cells after activation by red light. In addition, we also evaluated the toxicity and antitumor activity of the complexes in vivo. The toxicity and antitumor activity of phorbiplatin were examined by using a murine mammary adenocarcinoma 4T1 xenograft model. We first studied the bio-distribution of phorbiplatin in different organs at various time points. BALB/c mice bearing the 4T1 tumor model were treated with PPA or phorbiplatin, by monitoring the fluorescence of complexes, we noticed that 4 h post-injection, most PPA or phorbiplatin were accumulated in the tumor region; therefore 4 h post-injection were chosen for red light irradiation to activate the prodrug. Next, we investigated the antitumor activity of phorbiplatin in vivo. BALB/c mice bearing approximately 40 mm3 4T1 tumors were intravenously injected with phorbiplatin at a dose of 3.5 mmol-Pt/kg every two days for a total of five treatments. PPA, oxaliplatin, and PPA+oxaliplatin were included as controls. Compared with oxaliplatin, the photoactivated porbiplatin presented a more than 2-fold increased antitumor effect, with 67% reduction in tumor volume and 62% reduction in tumor weight compared with the control group. Suggesting that phorbiplatin possesses great antitumor potential. At the same time, no significant body weight in the phorbiplatin-treated group was observed, and the H&E staining indicated that phorbipaltin did not induced damage to main organs, highlighting the safty of this prodrug. In conclusion, we realized the objectives of this project, successfully developed a red light activatable Pt(IV) prodrugs that presented great anticancer potential, and is promising for further development. In addition, this study also provides a novel strategy to design photoactivable Pt(IV) prodrugs with long activation wavelength and high efficiency, which presents valuable information for developing next-generation metal-based anticancer drugs.

11304318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304318.value: The therapeutic outcome of chemotherapy is greatly limited by the drug resistance of cancer cells and various side effects. To address these challenges, we developed a kind of clinical drug-based, red light-activatable Pt(IV) prodrug, designated as phorbiplatin. This prodrug is stable enough in the physiological environment, therefore could minimize the toxicity of drugs towards normal cells to reduce the side effects; whereases upon red light irradiation, this prodrug could rapidly be reduced to oxaliplatin, to effectively kill the cancer cells. In addition, photoactivated phorbiplatin could generate a huge amount of reactive oxygen species (ROS) to synergistically kill the cancer cells and overcome drug resistance. The in vitro experiments indicated that phorbiplatin is non-toxic in the dark condition, whereas after red light activation, phorbiplatin presented up to 1,786-fold increased cytotoxicity than its parent drug, oxaliplatin, and could effectively overcome drug resistance of cancer cells. Subsequently, the in vivo experiments found that phorbiplatin exhibited more than a 2-fold enhanced antitumor effect than oxaliplatin after red light irradiation, suggesting developing photoactivatable platinum(IV) prodrugs is a promising strategy to improve the therapeutic outcomes of cancer chemotherapy. In this project, we thoroughly investigated the reduction mechanism of phorbiplatin, which proved valuable information for designing novel photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs for cancer treatment.

11304318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304318.value: Compared with the parent drug, oxaliplatin, phorbiplatin presented significantly improved cytotoxicity, reduced side effects, and enhanced ability to overcome drug resistance in both in vitro and in vivo models, exhibiting great potential for further development. In the next step, we propose to thoroughly study the pharmaceutical properties of phorbiplatin, such as pharmacokinetic properties, safety, and antitumor activity in different animal models to move this prodrug into the pre-clinical study and further developments. In addition, since some metal drugs, such as oxaliplatin, have been found to activate immune response to improve the treatment effect, we will also evaluate the ability of phorbiplatin to activate the immune system in cell-based and animal models. In the meantime, we will develop next-generation photoactivatable Pt(IV) prodrugs that possess longer activation wavelength to improve the tissue penetration ability, explore the potential treatment types, and further increase the treatment effect.

11304318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304318.value: Platinum-based anticancer drugs are the most widely used anticancer drugs in the clinic; their therapeutic outcome, however, is limited by the drug resistance and various side effects. To address these limitations, we developed phorbiplatin, a Pt(IV) prodrug that can be controllably activated by red light and be reduced to clinical drug oxaliplatin, to kill cancer cells. Compared with oxaliplatin, phorbiplatin is non-toxic in the dark but can be rapidly reduced to oxaliplatin in cancer cells upon red light irradiation. Such a controllable-activation property enables phorbiplatin to effectively reduce the side effects of platinum drugs on normal tissues. Besides directly binding to DNA, phorbiplatin could generate a huge amount of ROS to synergistically damage cancer cells and therefore successfully overcome the drug resistance of cancer cells toward platinum drugs. Especially, compared with other photoactivable Pt(IV) prodrugs, phorbiplatin is activated by red light; the relatively long activation wavelength brings greater tissue penetration ability and makes it more suitable for cancer treatment. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed the superior anticancer activity over conventional platinum drugs, indicating the great potential of phorbiplatin for further development. Our study also provides a new strategy to develop novel photoactivatable Pt prodrugs.

11304518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304518.value: As society moves towards renewables for energy generation, the demand for large batteries for storage applications will increase. Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are widely used in mobile applications such as cell phones, laptops and electric vehicles. However, LIBs are expected to fall short in alleviating this extra demand because of the limited amount of lithium and its high cost. Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) using earth-abundant sodium are therefore an attractive alternative for large energy storage applications. Current SIB have two main drawbacks: low voltage and low capacity compared with LIB. This project aims at developing a new type of sodium transition metal oxide-based cathode material that delivers higher capacity. The strategy is to utilize both the oxidation and reduction of the transition metal and the oxide ions in the material (dual redox) to enable more charge transfer. A similar phenomenon has been investigated in the so-called “lithium-excess material” in LIBs since the early 2000s, but is only observed when Li content in the material is above stoichiometry. In SIB, we have recently discovered that stoichiometric NaVO3 without excess Na can also undergo reversible oxygen charge transfer during sodiation and de-sodiation. This presents new opportunity for dual redox reactions in sodium materials. In this project, we will re-investigate and design a range of materials that are conducive for reversible transition metal (cationic) and oxygen (anionic) redox reactions, then characterize their charge-discharge mechanism, thermal stability and safety. In brief, we will develop a two pronged approach to achieve the goal. The first is to extend our previous work on Na-M-O with chemical doping by adding another transition metal to enable both cationic and anionic reactions. We will start synthesizing a few promising materials with known structures for examination. The second is to explore structural database to look for specific structural markers, and to use density functional theory on a selection of compounds to study their energy bands to identify ones with overlapping oxygen and transition metal states. A few materials will be selected for further characterization and investigation. Expected outcomes of the project will be a new set of sodium-ion cathode materials with higher capacity, and a theoretical model that improves our understanding of oxygen involvement in sodium-ion battery materials during charge and discharge. Successful implementation of the project will enable practical development of SIBs with lower cost and higher storage capacity compared to LIBs. 隨著人類社會向可再生能源時代的邁進，我們對大型儲能電池的需求也將增加。當前鋰離子電池正廣泛應用於手機、筆記本電腦、電動汽車等移動領域，然而，鋰資源的稀缺和高成本使鋰離子電池難以緩解大規模儲能產業的發展，鈉離子電池因採用資源豐富的鈉元素而成為大型儲能係統的極具潛力的選擇。 目前鈉離子電池相對鋰離子電池而言主要有兩個缺點：低電壓和低容量。本項目旨在開發一種具有更高容量的新型過渡金屬氧化物鈉離子正極材料，通過同時利用正極材料中的氧和過渡金屬的氧化還原反應，來獲得更多的電子轉移。我們最近發現NaVO3可以利用氧進行電子轉移，實現可逆脫/嵌鈉過程，這也為鈉離子材料中陰陽離子氧化還原反應提供新的可能。 本項目中，我們將會再研究並設計一系列有利於過渡金屬（陽離子）和氧（陰離子）進行可逆氧化還原反應的材料，然後對其充放電機理進行表徵。簡而言之，我們將同時採用兩種方法以達到目標。第一種是在前期Na-M-O材料的研究基礎上，對其進一步採用化學摻雜以同時獲得陰離子和陽離子氧化還原反應，我們也將合成一些已知晶體結構的具潛力的材料並對其進行表徵。第二種是開發材料的結構數據庫以尋找特定的結構標定，並對採用密度泛函理論研究材料能帶結構，檢驗材料中氧和過渡金屬密度態是否重疊，然後選擇某些材料進行進一步的表徵研究。 本項目的預期結果是獲得一系列新的具有高容量的鈉離子正極材料，並通過理論模型分析提高對其充放電過程中氧的氧化還原反應的深入理解。本項目的成功實行將有助於相對鋰離子電池具有更低價格、更高容量的鈉離子電池的實際發展。

11304518.label: Realisation of objectives
11304518.value: The project has been 100% achieved. Through the project, we have investigated varies sodium metal oxides and lithium metal oxides and discovered that some of them such as Na4V2O7, NaVO3, LiVO3, Na2MoO4, Na2WO4 can undergo both redox reaction of the oxygen and also transition metal (in this case V, Mo and W) to give a high capacity of more than 200 mAh/g. Theoretical calculations using density functional theory were also conducted on the materials by my Co-I Patrick Sit, where we have studied how and why these materials undergo oxygen redox reaction through density of state and spin density analyses. These theoretical calculations help us to identify new materials that can potentially have high capacity so that we can test them in the future. 6 papers were published throughout the course of the project. 4 presentations/posters were also given at international conferences (face-to-face and online). Unfortunately, due to COVID situation and travel restrictions, my students and I were not able to attend more conferences to disseminate the information. One PhD student (Dr. Bizhe Su) was trained under this project. In addition, Dr. Su went onto a study exchange to the University of New South Wales and worked under Dr. Neeraj Sharma to conduct structural analysis of the Na-V-O material upon charge and discharge.

11304518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304518.value: A major finding in the project is that there are many potential sodium metal oxide and lithium metal oxide materials that can undergo oxygen redox reaction, followed by dual-redox reaction with transition metal. In this project, we have mainly worked with V-based materials with VO4 tetrahedra structure. These materials initially have an oxidation state of V5+, but can be charged due to charge transfer of the oxygen atoms in the materials. This mechanism is verified by characterizations such as X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. During discharge, both the oxygen atoms and transition metal atoms are reduced to accommodate extra Na or Li in the material structure. Interestingly, these materials undergo negligible change in lattice constants during Na/Li extraction and insertion. This is attributed to the stable framework formed by the VO4 tetrahedra in the structure. This near zero-strain behavior is important for battery application because it will create less stress within an electrode during charge and discharge, which can improve stability of the electrodes. In addition, these materials with small size change could be used in solid-state batteries in the future where the volume change is a critical issue due to hard interfaces in the solid.

11304518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304518.value: So far, we have only been able to test and optimize a few of the materials. There are many other potential candidates such as Na3SbO4, Li3SbO4, Na5MoO4, Li5MoO4, Na3BiO4, etc. that have suitable crystal structure with Li/Na channels and have the potential to undergo oxygen redox reaction. My group will continue to synthesize new materials and test them to further investigate the mechanism of these materials for battery applications. In addition, I will continue to work with theoretical groups to screen different materials to search for potential ones, which can speed up the discovery of new materials for battery applications.

11304518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304518.value: Battery is an essential device for energy storage in our daily life. For future applications, batteries with higher energy density are desired. This project aims at developing new types of sodium/lithium transition metal oxide-based cathode material that delivers high capacity in sodium/lithium-ion batteries. The strategy is to utilize both the oxidation and reduction of the transition metal and the oxide ions in the material (dual redox) to enable more charge transfer. Through the study, we have found a number of materials (e.g. NaVO3, LiVO3, Na4V2O7, etc.) that can undergo these dual redox reactions, giving capacities of 200 mAh/g or more. Theoretical calculations have supported that oxygen is partially responsible for the capacity. Our work opens up a new category of unexplored materials that can give high capacity in the future for battery applications. Interestingly, these materials have stable framework, where the size of the material does not change during charge and discharge. Currently though, the capacity of the materials decreases with cycling, possibly due to side reactions with the electrolyte. Further work is being conducted on the stability of the material and their interactions with the electrolyte. In addition, the materials may be suitable for solid-state batteries in the future.

11304718.label: Project Objectives
11304718.value: Show the existence of exceptional scales for a Poisson frozen percolation model, where the growth of a connected component is stopped when it is hit by a Poisson process of freezings. This requires the understanding of the cumulative effect of these freezings (of larger and larger connected components) up to the critical time. Understand the effect of such freezings on the self-destructive percolation result of Kiss, Manolescu and Sidoravicius. This result is crucial to understand the behavior of forest fire processes near the critical time. Use the new understanding resulting from 1) and 2) to show the existence of exceptional scales for forest fire processes. This is an important step toward a good description of such processes after the critical time.

11304718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304718.value: 在統計物理中，自組織臨界性是一個十分有趣的現象，可以被用來解釋自然界中復雜性的出現。由Drossel和Schwabl在1992年引入的“森林大火過程”就是這種現象的一個典型。在這一過程中，新樹在格點上以1的強度出現（即普通滲流過程），同時閃電以極小的強度出現：當一棵樹被劈中，此樹及與之相連的所有樹都會被大火燒掉。 雖然森林大火過程引起了許多關註，但人們對這一過程的長期行為所知甚少。研究這類問題極其困難，因為有兩種相對立的效果互相競爭：假如有很多樹，導致出現了大的連通簇，它被燒掉時就會留出大片空地。由於這種非單調性，統計物理中用來研究格點模型的常規方法不能用來研究這類問題，人們需要引入新的技術和想法。 這個研究計劃的目的正是在數學層面上增進對於這類模型的理解，而研究方法來源於近年來在“近臨界性滲流”以及於之相關的其它過程中發展出來的一些突破性想法。特別的，我們想證明，在有限盒裏的森林大火過程，以及與之相關的泊松凍結滲流過程，存在一些特殊的尺度。讓t表示森林大火過程中的普通滲流過程的臨界時間。為得出這類結果，我們將需要對於在t以前出現的大火的累積效應有精確的理解。這些結果也將突顯出最近的關於“體積凍結滲流”的結果（van den Berg, Nolin, 2017）的穩定性。

11304718.label: Realisation of objectives
11304718.value: Objective 1 was completely addressed in the long (80 pages) paper "Near-critical 2D percolation with heavy-tailed impurities, forest fires and frozen percolation", in collaboration with J. van den Berg (CWI and VU University Amsterdam). This work was published in Probability Theory and Related Fields, one of the top journals in the field. In order to understand the cumulative effect of freezings / fires, we introduced and studied an important new percolation process, on a lattice where heavy-tailed impurities are first removed. This yielded several results of independent interest. We then used these results to show the existence of exceptional scales for the Poisson frozen percolation (forest fire) process, as stated in the objective. Our results for percolation with impurities should be very useful to further study forest fire processes, as well as related models. Objectives 2 and 3 are not yet completely addressed, but we have made significant progress toward them. In order to analyze the effect of "recoveries" (trees reappearing at a location where a tree burnt earlier), I have studied carefully the paper of Kiss, Manolescu and Sidoravicius, where the authors establish a key technical result for a process known as self-destructive percolation. It seems possible to adapt this result to forest fires, by considering a more convoluted version of the new percolation process that we introduced to handle Objective 1. In particular, this seems to require a stability result for 6-arm events for a percolation process with impurities / fires. However, even though the stochastic minorant produced by independent impurities was good enough for Objective 1, we have to work with the original forest fire process (or a version of it) for Objective 2. Although this is still technically challenging at the moment, I hope to achieve it in the near future. Objective 3 depends crucially on Objectives 1 and 2. The improved understanding obtained in Objective 1, which allowed us to derive the existence of exceptional scales, should lead in a similar way to a satisfactory answer to Objective 3, unless unexpected technical difficulties arise due to the recovering trees (but I have not found any for the moment). However, this objective can cannot be addressed fully until a result analogous to the Kiss-Manolescu-Sidoravicius result for self-destructive percolation (the goal of Objective 2) is obtained.

11304718.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304718.value: In this project, we introduced a novel percolation model on planar lattices, where impurities are first created. These impurities are not only microscopic, but also allowed to be mesoscopic (“heavy-tailed”, in some sense). They are removed in an independent fashion from the lattice, and we then consider Bernoulli percolation on the remaining part. In particular, we want to understand whether the near-critical regime of Bernoulli percolation is impacted by the presence of impurities. We determined explicitly the range of parameters in the distribution of impurities for which the connectivity properties of percolation remain of the same order as without impurities, for distances below a certain characteristic length, thus generalizing a celebrated result by Kesten for classical near-critical percolation (which can be viewed as critical percolation with single-site impurities). This new process turns out to be crucial to study classical models of forest fires, where vertices become occupied at rate 1, and get ignited at a very small rate (in which case the entire connected component of trees containing the ignited vertex burns immediately). Indeed, the model with impurities provides a very useful stochastic minorant for the configuration of trees, as time approaches (and crosses) the critical time, the time at which an infinite connected component of trees would arise in the absence of fires. In this way, we obtained a good grasp of the connectivity of the forest, i.e. of the way fires spread over long distances. It thus allowed us to obtain the first mathematically rigorous (and surprising) results for the behavior of forest fires near and beyond the critical time, especially the existence of a sequence of "exceptional scales". This unexpected behavior, deeply related to the non-monotonicity of forest fire processes, was not predicted in the physics literature. We hope that these ideas can be further developed to study the impact of recovering trees in a forest, thus yielding a better description of forest fires beyond the critical time. Moreover, this could give insight into their long-term behavior, and into properties of their equilibrium distribution. Furthermore, we believe that the process with impurities could be useful in many other situations where similar impurities are produced by the underlying mechanisms, for example in epidemics models. Finally, our work on these problems, as well as on related questions in percolation theory, also led us to collaborate with V. Tassion (ETH Zürich) and A. Teixeira (IMPA, Rio de Janeiro). In particular, we were able to obtain an answer to a long-standing open question about a problem known as percolation of words, which was introduced by Benjamini and Kesten in 1995. We proved that almost surely, all infinite binary sequences can be embedded into a site percolation configuration on Z^3, as long as the percolation parameter is strictly between p_c and 1-p_c, where p_c is the site percolation threshold on Z^3. We have already completed a paper "No exceptional words for Bernoulli percolation", which is now published online in Journal of the European Mathematical Society.

11304718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304718.value: We hope to extend the results obtained in this project to understand the effect of recovering trees. We also want to look for further applications to other real-world processes, e.g. studied in condensed matter physics, epidemiology or ecology.

11304718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304718.value: In this project, we obtained novel results for a class of models introduced in physics, known as forest fires. These models are still poorly understood, and we were able to obtain the first non-trivial, mathematically rigorous, results about their behavior. Such results are quite surprising and striking, and they were not predicted earlier, neither in the mathematics nor in the physics literature. This provides a better understanding of real-world complex systems with analogous mechanisms.

11304818.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304818.value: 雙碳電池石墨電極層間化合物的第一性原理研究

11304818.label: Project Objectives
11304818.value: To deliver the systematic understanding of the structural, energetic and electronic properties of graphite intercalation compounds with the neutralized anions of prototypical lithium salts. To reveal the microscopic details of lithium salt solvation and the liquid structures of dual-carbon batteries. To provide the mechanistic and kinetic information of the intercalation processes in the cathode of dual-carbon batteries.
rows: To deliver the systematic understanding of the structural, energetic and electronic properties of graphite intercalation compounds with the neutralized anions of prototypical lithium salts.
To reveal the microscopic details of lithium salt solvation and the liquid structures of dual-carbon batteries.
To provide the mechanistic and kinetic information of the intercalation processes in the cathode of dual-carbon batteries.

11304818.label: Realisation of objectives
11304818.value: In this project, we carried out ab initio study of the structural and energetic properties of the graphite intercalation compounds (GICs) with the neutralized anions (BF4, ClO4, PF6, TFSI) and alkali metal atoms (Li, Na, K) of the prototypical salts in dual-carbon batteries. We first focused on the intercalation of one single species. We correlated the extent of the interlayer expansion with the size of the intercalants and examined the interaction between the graphite host and the intercalants. Regarding the roles of GICs in dual-carbon batteries, we identified the trend of the onset voltage with the different salts, which shows good agreement with the experimental trend provided by Co-I Yu’s group. Our study also demonstrated the key roles of the electrolyte as the active material in the dual-carbon batteries. Then, we studied the intercalation processes and staging mechanisms with multiple cation and anion intercalants. We evaluated the stabilities of the different GICs with the formation energy calculations. Moreover, the electronic properties were examined through the electronic band structure calculations of the GICs at different intercalation stages. We compared the voltage profiles of different anion-based batteries upon charging using the Li/Na/K metals as the counter electrodes. The storage capacities of these dual-carbon batteries were also evaluated theoretically which shows good agreement with the experimental values. All the studies discussed above have achieved Objectives 1 and 3. In dual-carbon batteries, the carbonate-based liquid electrolyte is considered to be the active materials as the charging and discharging processes involves ion transport and solvation. In this regard, we performed classical molecular dynamics and ab initio simulations to systemically study the solvation structures and energetics of electrolytes with different solvent types, different salt concentrations, as well as of their mixtures. In particular, we compared the solvation structures of the linear carbonates and cyclic carbonates. The binary mixtures of the solvents commonly used in experiments are also considered. Considering the interaction in the electrolyte, detailed analysis of the relationship between the solvation structure, the free energy of solvation and their effects on the battery properties was performed. This study has achieved Objective 2.
