11304818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304818.value: Considering the intercalation of different anions and cations commonly used in dual-carbon batteries, we identified a direct correlation between interlayer expansion and the size of the intercalants. We also found that the graphene layers interact more strongly with the metal atoms than with the neutralized anions. For the onset voltage, we found that it follows the orders of K+ > Na+ > Li+ for the cations and BF4- ~ ClO4- ~ PF6- > TFSI- for the anions. Compared to the cations, the size of the anion has a smaller effect on the onset voltage due to its large size. On the other hand, the choice of the electrolyte solvent was found to affect significantly the onset voltage. The results of this study were published in the Journal of Physical Chemistry C 2019 123, 18132-18141. In the study of the staging mechanisms with multiple intercalants, we identified that the in-plane intercalant interaction plays the key role in determining the maximum storage capacity. The calculated capacities are in good agreement with the experimental values. Also, we found that initial intercalation is the least favorable step because of the largest energy required for graphene interlayer distance expansion. The subsequent intercalations can then occur more readily. Comparing different stages of intercalation, the interaction between the interactants is only significant when the intercalants are in adjacent layers. This explains the voltage variation of the dual-carbon batteries at different stages of intercalation. The results of this study were published in ACS Omega 2020, 5, 18289−18300. In the study of the solvation and liquid structures of the electrolytes, we found that the Li+···PF6– contact ion pairs are likely to form in the linear carbonate (DEC, EMC and DMC) electrolytes, while the ions are fully solvated in the cyclic carbonate (EC and FEC) electrolytes. Similarly, in the solvent mixtures of linear and cyclic carbonates, the cyclic carbonate molecules play the main role in dissolving the salt ions. Comparing carbonates of the same kind, we found that the interaction of the Li+ cation with the solvents follows a descending trend: DEC > EMC > DMC for the linear carbonates, while for the cyclic carbonates, the order is EC > FEC. Detailed analysis of the relationship between the solvation structure, the free energy of solvation and their effects on the battery properties was also performed. These understandings are important for the development of better electrolytes for DIBs.

11304818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304818.value: Building on the study of the graphite electrodes, future works can include investigation of the effects of doping to the graphite on the intercalation structure, energetics as well as the voltage of the dual-carbon batteries. Moreover, beside graphite, the study can be extended to other 2-demensional materials like MXenes and metal dichalcogenides which have shown promising potential in battery applications by allowing ion intercalation. On the other hand, for the electrolyte, beside the ion solvation structures and energetics, the stability of the electrolyte should also be investigated in detail. Another direction is to explore the use of solid-state electrolytes in this class of batteries.

11304818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304818.value: Dual-carbon batteries (DCBs) have shown great promises in next-generation energy storage application. Charging and discharging of DCBs relies on the reversible formation of the graphite intercalation compounds (GICs) though intercalation and extraction of cations and anions in the anode and cathode, respectively. On the other hand, the carbonate-based liquid electrolyte is an active material as charging and discharging involve ion transport and solvation in the electrolyte. Despite the great promises, in-depth understanding of DCBs like the effects of the choice of salts and solvents on the battery performance is still lacking. In this project, we first performed ab initio study of the effects of different salt ions on the structures and energetics in GICs as well as on the onset voltage of the DCBs. Then, we studied the staging mechanisms with multiple intercalants. The storage capacities of the DCBs were also examined. Moreover, we performed classical molecular dynamics and ab initio simulations to systemically study the salt ion solvation structures and energetics at different concentrations in different solvent types and their mixtures. Considering the interaction in the electrolyte, detailed analysis of the relationship between the solvation structure, the free energy of solvation and the battery properties was performed.

11305218.label: Project Objectives
11305218.value: Developing high performance hydrogel based quasi-solid-state electrolytes with a high ionic conductivity, high stretchability and excellent electrochemical stability. The target ionic conductivity of the developed hydrogel electrolyte should be higher than 1.2 ×10−2 S cm−1 at room temperature. Utilizing these electrolytes to fabricated high-performance quasi-solid-state flexible zinc ion batteries. The developed flexible zinc ion batteries, will have a target capacity of >260 mAh/g based on the cathode, and a cycling stability of 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles, and a target area capacity of 10 mAh/cm2. Successful fabrication of stretchable and self-healable zinc ion batteries based on dual-crosslinked hydrogel electrolytes.

11305218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305218.value: 迅速發展的柔性可穿戴電子器件需要新的可靠的柔性電池來點亮。2015年，柔性電池市場估值6900萬美元，預計到2022年估值將達到9億五千萬美元。柔性電池及柔性系統將會在運動監測，實時健康監察等領域有著廣泛的用途。 柔性電池有很多解決方案，最爲流行的是使用锂電池技術。但是锂電池使用有機電解液和高活性的負極，使得锂電池的安全問題始終無法最終解決。作爲柔性電池，其可靠性和安全性就更加差強人意。 鋅離子電池，使用水系電解液，成本低，高度安全，環境友好，制備容易。使用鋅離子電池制備柔性電池，將會獲得良好的安全性和可靠性。 但是目前鋅離子電池的發展，缺乏高鋅離子導電率的固體電解液。 本項目將會開發新型高鋅離子導電率的水凝膠電解質，並通過水凝膠改性增加其保水性，確保鋅離子電池的高容量，高穩定性和良好的柔性。此外，我們將通過優化和合成新的水凝膠，賦予柔性鋅離子電池可拉伸性和自愈合能力等，拓展其使用範圍，增強其可靠性。

11305218.label: Realisation of objectives
11305218.value: Supported by this project, we intensively investigated a few hydrogel electrolytes, which can effective confine water, providing high stretchability, excellent electrochemical stability (extended electrochemical stability window) and high ionic conductivity. Design, fabrication, mechanical properties and ionic conductivity of hydrogels We developed hydrogels with a remarkable extended electrochemical stability window. we developed two strategies to construct supramolecular hydrogels with remarkably enhanced non-freezable bound water and reduced free water to extend their electrochemical stability windows. Our first strategy is to develop hydrogels containing massive amount of common hydrophilic groups (such as -OH and -NH2, defined as enhanced hydrophilic hydrogels). In specific, D(+)-Glucose monohydrate (DM) is introduced to poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (PSBMA) chains to form the PSBMA@DM. Then, other types of hydrophilic monomers are used to replace part of the PSBMA. The other strategy is to endow superhydrophilic groups (such as NH4+ and SO3-) in the hydrogels (defined as superhydrophilic hydrogels), taking advantage of their super intensive interaction with water molecules than that of common hydrophilic groups. The ionic conductivities of the enhanced hydrophilic hydrogel electrolytes are in the range of 0.7~1.6 ×10-2 S cm‒1. The ionic conductivities of superhydrophilic hydrogel electrolytes are higher, ranging from 1.4×10-2 S cm‒1 to 4.8×10-2 S cm‒1. The superiority of superhydrophilic hydrogels is rooted in the intrinsic zwitterionic groups which provide separated migration channels for ions, largely facilitating the transport of charge carriers. In addition, although free water molecules are attracted in the vicinity of the hydrophilic groups and bound water molecules are formed, the water molecules can still transport ions. It should be noted that the ionic conductivities achieved are comparable with those of conventional hydrogels. However, much more bound water and much less free water exist in our developed hydrogels. In addition, the ionic conductivities achieved are much higher than those of the water-in-salt electrolytes, and the materials cost of fabricated hydrogels is remarkably lower than the water-in-salt. Performance of batteries based on hydrogel electrolyte We fabricated a novel hydrogel electrolyte based on zwitterionic sulfobetaine/cellulose semi-interpenetrating networks (ZSC-gel), which provided superior electrochemical performances and mechanical strengths in flexible aqueous Zn-MnO2 batteries. The hydrogel electrolyte was synthesized by polymerizing the zwitterionic sulfobetaine monomer of [2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl]diethy-(3-sulopropyl) (MAEDS) in a skeleton composed of cellulose nanofibrils. The zwitterionic structure of the MAEDS network provided not only a superior polyelectrolyte water retention owing to the strong electrostatic interactions between zwitterionic groups and water molecules, but also ion migration channels for a large ionic transport, which yielded a higher rate capability. The cellulose nanofibrils significantly improved the mechanical properties. Owing to these synergistic effects, the ZSC-gel electrolyte exhibited an ultrahigh ionic conductivity of 0.0246S cm-1 and high stretchability of 920%. The Zn-MnO2 battery with the polyzwitterion hydrogel electrolyte (polyzwitterion-battery) exhibited a high capacity of 148 mA h g-1at 6.5 C with a retention of 90.42% of the initial capacity after 1200 cycles. Even at 30 C, an ultrafast charging-discharging up to 10000 cycles was achieved with an average capacity of 62 mA h g-1, which further verifies the superior rate capability. Furthermore, flexible planar and fiber-shaped batteries were fabricated using the designed ZSC-gel electrolyte, which exhibited excellent flexibilities and/or weavabilities. The rate performance of the polyzwitterion-battery was measured at 1 to 30 C (1 C = 0.308 mA g-1) in a voltage range of 0.9 to 1.9 V. At 1 C, the polyzwitterion-battery exhibited an average specific capacity of 275 mA h g-1, approximately 91% of the theoretical capacity (308 mA h g-1). With the increase in current density, values of 232, 181, 154, 134, 121, 104, 87, 80, and 74 mA h g-1 were measured when the reversible discharge capacity was stabilized at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 C, respectively. Notably, the specific capacity recovered to 268 mA h g-1 with a small voltage hysteresis when the C-rate was returned from 30 to 1 C, i.e., approximately 97% of the initial capacity was preserved. All galvanostatic charge–discharge profiles exhibit a sloping plateau at 1.4 V owing to the H+ insertion, followed by a flat plateau at 1.3 V dominantly determined by the Zn2+ insertion, which indicates a stable rate capability. Functional batteries based on hydrogel We also developed a quasi-solid-state Zn-δ-NMOH battery based on a developed self-healable polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel electrolyte. With hydrogel electrolyte, the Zn-δ-NMOH cell can still exhibit a rate capability close to that in the liquid electrolyte within 1 C and 12 C. Based on this, a self-healable Zn-δ-NMOH battery was designed, using the self-healing carboxylated-polyurethane as the self-healing substrates. The restoration of electrical conductivity after damage using the healable carboxylated-polyurethane as a substrate was researched based on a fresh planer battery. A multimeter was used to trace the resistance of the anode and cathode. After cut and healing, the resistance of anode and cathode increased slightly to 5.3 and 3.5 Ω, respectively. And the open voltage of the fresh cell was reduced from 1.379 V to 1.355 V. The corresponding EIS and open circuit voltage change relating to healing times were recorded, a rise is observed in both interface resistance (Ri) and charge transfer resistance (Rct), it was caused by the uncompacted contact between the cut ends of the electrodes. The restoration of electrochemical performance on the self-healing aqueous battery was investigated. After each time of cut and healing, a small decrease was observed compared with the original flexible battery. Impressively, the capacity can still be remained around 100 mAh g-1 even at 10 C, with retention of 81.2 % after 4 times of cut and recovery. The discharge-charge profile at 10 C can give a further certification as no significant change was observed, it still delivered a voltage of ca. 1.4 V and the characteristic two-step discharge process.

The discharge-charge profile at 10 C can give a further certification as no significant change was observed, it still delivered a voltage of ca. 1.4 V and the characteristic two-step discharge process.

11305218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305218.value: Hydrogels as electrolytes of aqueous batteries can provide three benefits: 1. Turning a solution-based battery to be quasi-solid state; 2. Endow batteries with multifunctionality; 3. Achieving improved battery performances. My future research on hydrogel electrolytes will be along the following two directions: 1. Stable high-voltage batteries based on the hydrogel. Previously, people used water in salt to achieve expansive electrochemical stability windows and high voltage aqueous batteries. However, they are costly, and they usually deliver limited ionic conductivity. With the support of this project, we have found hydrogel can effectively interact with water molecules through proper design, and then hydrogels can be used to develop high-voltage batteries. Considering the low cost and tunable properties of hydrogels, we will investigate different hydrogels and use them to achieve aqueous batteries with a voltage >2.5 V. 2. We will also use hydrogel to tune the electrochemical activity of different ions. For example, both H+ and Zn2+ contribute to capacity in a Zn-MnO2 battery, we will try to use hydrogel to promote the activity of Zn2+ and suppress the activity of H+.

11305218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305218.value: Hydrogel is helpful as an electrolyte of aqueous electrolyte-based zinc ion batteries due to their high ionic conductivity, mechanical stretchability, self-heal ability, and ability to confine water. By utilizing hydrogel instead of the aqueous solution as an electrolyte, quasi-solid-state zinc ion batteries can be developed, and multifunctionality can be endowed. Here in this project, we developed a few hydrogel electrolytes for zinc ion batteries. The double network-based hydrogel electrolytes possess superior stretchability even under different pHs. With enriched hydrophilic groups and superhydrophilic groups, hydrogels were used to remarkably reduce free water content and achieved an over 3V voltage window. Hydrogel electrolytes based on zwitterionic sulfobetaine/cellulose semi-interpenetrating networks can form different channels for anions and cations, which facilitate the stability and rateability of the developed batteries. These developed hydrogels obtained an ultrahigh ionic conductivity of 0.0246 S cm-1 and a high stretchability of 920%. The Zn-MnO2 battery with the polyzwitterion hydrogel electrolyte (polyzwitterion-battery) exhibited a capacity retention of 90.42% of the initial capacity after 1200 cycles. We also utilized hydrogels to develop a stretchable and self-healable device.

11305318.value: Design numerical methods for deep learning models to explore the low-index saddle point, energy barrier and minimum energy path: We shall explore the differences in energy barriers at various local minima with different generalization errors. The gentlest ascent dynamics (GAD) and string method for saddle points will be improved to handle the large scale problem in deep learning. Construct the stochastic version of the GAD-like methods to improve efficiency of saddle-free optimizations. The saddle-converging methods such as GAD will be modified to the saddle-free methods to improve minimization techniques. The stochastic approximation like the idea of Robbins and Monro in stochastic gradient descent will be exploited both theoretically and numerically. Conduct systematic studies on the relation of energy landscape to the generalization capability of various neural network models. This is to address open problem on generalization of deep learning. We shall use the numerical tools developed above to test our hypothesis on the energy landscape perspective, to investigate the generalization indicator on the complex energy landscape, to understand the consistency or discrepancy of various existing hypotheses, theories, methods and models.

11305318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305318.value: Deep learning has been a great practical success and has a profound impact on the machine learning. Understanding theoretic properties of deep learning is an active research area. In contrast to shallow networks, deep learning is equipped with much more effective parameters than the number of training examples. The loss function of the deep learning quickly becomes very high-dimensional and non-convex. The existence of a huge number of local minima makes the optimization task conceptually challenging. The recent research shows the major optimization difficulty may originate from the proliferation of saddle points and suggests there is a hierarchical structure of the critical points with the various index on the energy landscape (i.e., loss function surface) in deep learning. However, despite the complicated energy landscape and the optimization challenges, many of deep networks with learned locally optimal parameters from stochastic gradient descent exhibit remarkably small generalization error, i.e., the difference between training error and test error. The traditional statistical learning theory on complexity has intrinsic difficulty to explain why this high-capacity network can still obtain low complexity solutions and generalize well. One popular hypothesis is that the characteristic of the landscape of the loss function is one of the important elements to understand the optimization algorithm performance and to explain the good generalization capability in deep learning. This research plan is to conduct substantial investigations of this energy landscape perspective and aims to study the energy landscape of deep learning in an innovative way to gain a better understanding of the geometry of loss surface and its potential connection to the remarkable generalization performance. Our main methodology is based on the previous work of the PI on the rare-event study of random transitions on energy landscape arising from molecular system and energy functional in material sciences. The existing work has built a solid connection between the stochastic gradient descent on the empirical loss function and the modified stochastic differential equation, which is the same equation describing rare events. We propose to use the key concept, energy barrier, in rare-event study as the candidate to measure generalization capability of local minima in deep learning with well-justified reasons. The toolset previously used to explore energy landscape in physics, such as the numerical methods for index-1 saddle points and the minimum energy path, will be carefully modified and applied for the new purpose of deep learning. 深度學習取得了巨大的實際成功，對機器學習產生了深遠的影響。理解深度學習的理論屬性是一個活躍的研究領域。與淺層網絡相比，深度學習配備的參數比訓練樣本的數量更有效。深度學習的損失函數很快變得非常高維和非凸。大量局部最小值的存在使得優化任務在概念上具有挑戰性。最近的研究表明，主要的優化難度可能源於鞍點的增殖，並表明在深度學習中存在能量景觀（即損失函數表面）的各種指數的臨界點的層次結構。 然而，儘管存在復雜的能量格局和優化挑戰，但許多具有隨機梯度下降的學習局部最優參數的深度網絡表現出非常小的泛化誤差，即訓練誤差和測試誤差之間的差異。傳統的複雜性統計學習理論很難解釋為什麼這種高容量網絡仍然可以獲得低複雜度的解決方案並且能夠很好地進行生成。為了解決這個開放性問題，一個流行的假設是損失函數的景觀特徵是理解優化算法性能和解釋深度學習中良好泛化能力的重要因素之一。 該研究計劃旨在對這種能源景觀進行大量調查，旨在以創新的方式研究深度學習的能源格局，以更好地了解損耗表面的幾何形狀及其與顯著的泛化性能的潛在聯繫。 。我們的主要方法是基於PI的先前工作，該研究涉及材料科學中分子系統和能量功能引起的能量景觀隨機轉換的罕見事件研究。現有的工作在經驗損失函數的隨機梯度下降與修正的隨機微分方程之間建立了牢固的聯繫，這是描述罕見事件的相同方程。我們提出在稀有事件研究中使用關鍵概念能量障礙作為衡量深度學習中局部極小值的泛化能力的候選者，並且有充分的理由。先前用於探索物理中能量景觀的工具集，例如指數-1鞍點的數值方法和最小能量路徑，將被仔細修改並應用於深度學習的新目的。

11305318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305318.value: This project identifies the importance of the saddle points on the loss landscape. The algorithms of the index-1 saddle point search can be applied to the landscape of deep learning based on neural networks. The applications of the related saddle point methods and deep learning are also carried on to areas like solving differential equations, and stochastic optimization as well as other practical problems. 11305318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305318.value: We find the geometric landscape is far more complicated if deep learning and neural network are very general. This first project related to machine learning also inspired the PI with a lot of interesting new topics related to control, AI for Science, etc.

11305318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305318.value: How the loss function in deep learning looks in high dimension is not only a visualization problem but also a mathematical problem to understand how the training algorithms and deep neural networks lead to the extraordinary performance of many deep learning and AI methods. This project shows some preliminary progress toward the exploitation and understanding of this loss landscape. It can potentially have acceleration in algorithm and theoretical insight if combined with other techniques from optimization and learning theory.

11305518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305518.value: Eigenvalue problems are important in the study of waves including electromagnetic waves and light. They appear naturally in the analysis of waveguides, resonators and periodic structures. Recently, some fascinating optical wave phenomena such as loss-induced transparency and unidirectional reflectionless transmission, have been discovered in connection with a special class of degenerate eigenvalue problems called Exceptional Points (EPs), of which both the eigenvalues and the eigenfunctions coalesce. In addition, a number of important applications of EPs, such as single-mode lasing and enhanced sensing, have been realized in experiments. However, except for structures satisfying the so-called PT-symmetry, theoretical studies on EPs are limited. In this project, we investigate the existence and robustness of EPs in various eigenvalue problems describing wave phenomena, develop efficient and reliable numerical methods for computing EPs, and analyze the applications of EPs using improved mathematical models and rigorous numerical simulations. Our study can improve the general mathematical understanding on degenerate eigenvalue problems, and help to realize many more practical and innovative applications of EPs. 特徵值問題在包括電磁波及光波的各種波動問題中很重要。它們很自然地出現在波導，共振器及週期結構的分析過程中。異常點（EP）是一種特殊的退化特徵值問題，有著相同的特徵根及合并的特徵函數。最近，很多奇特的光波現象被發現同異常點有關，還實現了一些重要的應用。但是，針對異常點的理論研究非常有限。在本項目中，我們將研究各類波動問題中的異常點的存在性及穩定性，將開發快速可靠的方法來計算異常點，將嚴格深入地研究異常點的各種應用。我們的研究有助于提升對退化特徵值問題的數學理解，也有助于開發異常點更多的實際應用。

11305518.label: Realisation of objectives
11305518.value: The first objective is to understand exceptional points (EPs) in eigenvalue problems governing wave phenomena. The emphasis is on their existence and robustness. For non-Hermitian eigenvalue problems with one or more parameters, an EP is the parameter value at which two or more eigenvalues as well as their corresponding eigenfunctions coalesce. Due to the many applications, we are mostly interested in EPs in eigenvalue problems of resonances for open structures. In that case, the eigenvalue is usually a complex frequency with an imaginary part related to the decay rate in time. Due to the outgoing radiation condition, the eigenvalue problems of resonances are non-Hermitian. It is important to understand basic properties of EPs in eigenvalue problems of resonances. We have made satisfactory progress on this topic, and published two papers, in JOSA B (Vol. 36, pp. 1659-1667, 2019) and Physica Scripta (Vol. 95, 095507, 2022), respectively. In the JOSA B paper, EPs for resonances are analysed for assemblies of circular periodic cylinders. In the Physica Scripta paper, EPs in 2D structures with a single periodic direction are studied. In the latter case, we are able to show that EPs can be classified as continuous sets in parameter space by a pair of integers, and when the periodic structure is tuned to a uniform slab, the limits can be characterised analytically. Existing works on EPs typically only show a few isolated EPs by numerical calculations. Our result is very different. We are able to show that all EPs can be classified into sets with analytically known limits. The second objective is about applications of EPs. We first studied the effect of field enhancement due to EPs in resonance eigenvalue problems. An important parameter for any resonance is the so-called quality-factor (Q). It is related to the ratio between the real and imaginary parts of the complex frequency. For a standard non-degenerate resonance, it is known that the wave field is enhanced by a factor proportional to the square root of Q. At an EP, two resonance modes coalesce. The field enhancement depends on Q differently. We have completed a paper on field enhancement (JOSA B, Vol. 39, pp. 611-618, 2022). We derived a new formula for field enhancement which remains valid when there are more than one radiation channels and when the structure has both radiation and dissipation losses. Another application of EPs is found in open optical waveguides. A complex mode of an open lossless dielectric waveguide is a guided mode confined around the waveguide core, but its propagation constant is complex, even though there is no material absorption or radiation loss. Previously, it is only known that complex modes can exist on 3D waveguides. Recently, we found that complex modes can emerge from EPs for 2D periodic dielectric waveguides. We have published a paper on this topic (Optics Letters, Vol. 45, pp. 5632-5635, 2020).

11305518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305518.value: In Paper 1 (JOSA B, Vol. 36, pp. 1659-1667), we studied EPs for resonances in structures consisting of finite number of parallel dielectric cylinders. An efficient nonlinear eigenvalue formulation is developed to calculate the complex resonant frequency and the structural parameters together. Topological features of the EPs are highlighted. In Paper 2 (Physica Scripta, Vol. 95, 095507, 2020), we find a way to sort and classify EPs in periodic slabs (with one periodic direction). It is shown that when the periodic slab is tuned continuously to a uniform slab, each EP follows a generic path with interesting transition points, and can be characterized by a pair of integers. Unlike existing works that report a few isolated EPs, our study reveals the global picture about all EPs in such a periodic structure. In Paper 3 (Optics Letters, Vol. 45, pp. 5632-5635, 2020), we study the so-called complex modes in 2D open lossless periodic waveguides (with 1D periopdicity). We are able to reveal the formation mechanism of complex modes. In particular, we show that complex modes can emerge from EPs in the bands of regular guided modes. In Paper 4 (PRA, Vol. 103, 043507, 2021), we analyze the robustness of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in 3D structures with two periodic directions). A BIC is a localized eigenmode with a real frequency (or infinite Q factor). Its frequency and wavevector are compatible with scattering solutions with incoming and outgoing waves. We show that under suitable conditions, a BIC in such a structure will continue to exist when the structure is perturbed with small but arbitrary perturbations that preserve the required symmetry. In Paper 5 (PRA, Vol. 103, 043512, 2021), we show that when a BIC is destroyed by a perturbation that breaks the required symmetry, circularly polarized resonant states emege. The work shows that ``conservation of topological charge'' does not imply ``robustness of BICs''. In Paper 6 (Optics Express, Vol. 29, pp. 16695-16709, 2021), we establish the robustness for BICs in optical waveguides with lateral leakage channels. Unlike Paper 4, the structure in this paper in invariant in one spatial variable. BICs in optical waveguides have useful applications. In Paper 7 (PRA, Vol. 104, 023521, 2021), we show that any generic BIC (robust or non-robust) in periodic structures (with 1D periodicity) can be characterized by a single integer n. A BIC is robust if and only if n=0. For a non-robust BIC, n is the minimum number of tunable parameters (in perturbations of the structure) needed to preserve the BIC. We have calculated n for different kind of BICs in the periodic structure. In Paper 8 (JOSA B, Vo. 39, pp. 611-618), we derived a precise formula for field enhancement near a BIC in lossy periodic structures. The formula is valid even for cases with multiple radiation channels, and it takes into account both radiation and absorption losses.

11305518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305518.value: There is currently a significant research interest on EPs in the photonics community. This is mainly due to their applications in lasing, sensing, etc. There are many existing works about these applications, but typically, they are only specific examples. It is desirable to have a general and systematic mathematical study on these applications. To reveal the most useful properties for these applications, we intend to carry out such a study about EPs in the future. We have studied basic properties of EPs for periodic structures and structures with a finite number of cylinders. It is desirable to understand EPs (for the eigenvalue problems of resonances) in general structures.

11305518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305518.value: Eigenvalue problems are important to numerous scientific and enginering applications. For electromagnetic waves (including light), a common eigenvalue problem is concerned with nonzero solutions (eigenfunctions) of the govening Maxwell's equations that only exist at specific values of the frequency (the eigenvalues). When the system contains additional paremeters, it is possible that two or more eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenfunctions coalesce at particular values of the parameters, forming the so-called Exceptional Points (EPs). In recent years, it has been demonstrated that EPs are useful for developing lasers with unusual properties, sensors with ultra sensitivity, wave-guiding structures with robust mode-conversion properties, and devices with uni-directional properties. To help the realization of practical applications of EPs, we study fundamental properties of EPs in this project. We developed an efficient method to calculate the EPs (the special parameter values and the eigenvalues/eigenfunctions), and found a way to sort and classify the EPs. We also analyzed useful resonace effects, such as field enhancement, which are the key to applications such as lasing and sensing. Our study can be used to design novel devices to take advantage of the special properties of EPs.

11305618.label: Project Objectives
11305618.value: To computationally study the effects of nonmetal dopants, such as B, C, N, O, S, P, and halogen atoms, as well as their compounds which are commonly used in experimental doping. Special attention will be paid to the stable doping sites near surface regions, and to any consequent charge transfers caused. Those occurrences may lead to effective doping, in accord with the passivation and transfer doping mechanisms that play a dominant role in nanoscale systems, as we demonstrated in 2009. To reveal the mechanism of stability enhancement in PEC applications, for some dopings, in order to optimize the doping scheme for optimal performace and stability. Recently, we have observed significant stability enhancement upon B doping. We anticipate that the dopant accomulation in the surface region of g-CN could help stablize the structure, due to photoinduced chemical reactions in the enviroment of the electrolyte containing water, H+, OH-, and sacrificial agents. We expect that revealing the underlying mechanism will be helpful for further improving stability.

11305618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305618.value: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) materials are promising photocatalysts for photoelectrochemical (PEC) applications such as splitting water into H2 and O2, which are ideal clean chemical energy carriers that produce only water after combustion. Although recently we successfully achieved depositions of the uniform, large-area, and pinhole-free g-CN thin films that are required for PEC applications, the films’ charge carrier conductivity and stability are still low for PEC applications. Although doping is a straightforward approach for improving conductivity, the complicated results obtained to date often cannot be understood with conventional doping mechanisms. Interestingly, we have recently observed that certain doping not only can improve the conductivity of charge carriers but also can significantly improve the chemical stability of the g-CN films. Systematic computational studies are needed for understanding the underlying mechanisms, in order to guide optimization of the doping and PEC conditions for urgent green energy applications. We believe that surface passivation and charge transfer doping mechanisms play important roles in the doping of g-CN. Thus, in this project we propose to perform computational simulations for an optimal doping design, in order to complement previous researches that were based on substitutional and interstitial doping mechanisms. We will model the doping systems by placing nonmetal dopants such as B, C, N, O, S, P, and halogen atoms, as well as their compounds used in experimental doping, in g-CN nanostructures. We will simulate the accumulation of these atoms and species in the surface regions, as well as the adsorption of water molecules and other possible species, such as H+/OH- and sacrificial agents (e.g., Na2S and triethanolamine), that are used in PEC water splitting. Our calculations will include ground- and excited-state calculations for structural optimizations and molecular dynamics simulations of the model systems, transition state searches of the possible chemical reactions involved, and charge transfers as well as band structure calculations, using the most sophisticated density functional theory methods available and their time-dependent approaches. We expect our computational studies to deliver the needed knowledge about doping types and configurations determined by charge transfers, which provide the carriers for conduction due to the dopant accumulation at the interface and surface as well as the adsorptions onto the g-CN surface with species from the electrolyte. We will also reveal the interfacial chemical reactions involving dopants in PEC applications and will identify the reactions with products that stabilize the intended surface from photoinduced degradation of the g-CN material. 石墨化氮化碳(g-CN)材料是一種很有前途的光催化劑，可用於光電化學(PEC)應用，如將水分解成H2和O2等，這兩種產物是理想的清潔化學能載體，燃燒後只產生水。雖然近年來我們成功地制備了均勻、大面積、無針孔的優質g-CN薄膜，但薄膜的電荷載流子電導率和穩定性仍然很低。雖然摻雜是一種直接提高電導率的方法，但迄今為止所得到的復雜結果往往不能用常規摻雜機制來理解。有趣的是，我們最近觀察到，某些摻雜不僅可以提高載流子的導電性，而且還能顯著提高g-CN薄膜的化學穩定性。尚需要進行系統的計算研究，以了解其潛在機制，以便為其在綠色能源領域的應用提供最佳的摻雜和光電催化條件。 我們認為表面鈍化和電荷轉移摻雜機制在g-CN的摻雜中起著重要的作用，因此本項目建議按照這種機制進行計算模擬，以優化摻雜設計，補充以往基於替代和間隙摻雜機制的探索。我們將通過放置於g-CN納米結構中一些非金屬摻雜物，如B，C，N，O，S，P和鹵素原子，以及用於實驗摻雜的化合物，來模擬摻雜體系。我們將模擬這些原子和物種在表面區域的積累，以及水分子和其他可能的物種的吸附，例如H/OH-和糖化劑(如Na2S和三乙醇胺)在PEC中的應用。我們的計算將包括用於結構優化的基態和激發態計算，並對模型系統進行分子動力學模擬，搜索可能涉及的化學反應的過度態，計算電荷轉移以及能帶結構。將使用最嚴格的密度泛函理論方法及其含時理論方法。我們期望我們的計算研究能提供關於由電荷轉移決定的摻雜類型和構型所需知識。這些電荷轉移提供了在界面和表面的摻雜積累載流子。預計，g-CN表面對電解質中的物種的吸附也為導電提供了載流子。我們還將揭示摻雜物的界面化學反應，並通過探討光誘導降解g-CN材料機理來研究能穩定表面的反應。

11305618.label: Realisation of objectives
11305618.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to reveal the mechanisms of nonmetal doping and doping induced stability enhancement of graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) nanostructures for photoelectrochemical water splitting. Eventually, we have successfully achieved the goal by first studying the electronic properties in both ground states and excited states of related systems including graphene, ZnSe nanorods and dots, as well as g-CN based composite films. We moved on to further study the g-CN systems with oxygen doping, boron doping, iodine doping, pseudo-metal-free dopng, and construction of heterojunctions. We eventually developed a charge transfer doping approach for g-CN using iodine as dopant. Most of our researches for this project were conducted using both computations and experiments to complement to each other.

11305618.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305618.value: We revealed that chemical species on the graphene nanostructure surface perturb the intrinsic electronic structures of the graphene moiety, inspiring our later development of surface charge transfer doping scheme for g-CN. [C8-1] We ascertained the role of epoxide groups in inducing the nonradiative recombination of the excited electron-hole. [C8-2] We showed that it is the water to adenine electron-driven proton transfer barrierless reaction responsible for the ultrafast component of the adenine relaxation. [C8-3] We demonstrated the advantages of the proper passivation of II-VI semiconductor nanocrystals as an efficient approach to tackle the efficient charge transfer and stability of photoelectrochemical cells. [C8-4] By studying the photoelectrochemical performance enhancement of ZnSe nanorods and dots, we proved that size- and shape-tuneable colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals are among the most promising materials for photoelectrochemical water splitting. [C8-5] We further developed an innovative strategy for constructing colorful carbon nitride films by adopting a multiple-steps thermal vapor condensation (MSTVC) method. The films present satisfied photocatalytic activity and the photocurrent densities. [C8-6] We prepared pristine CN and oxygen-doped CN films with in situ textured topography and tuneable electronic structure using the MSTVC method. With the oxygen heteroatom incorporation, the in situ textured OCN film achieves a 15-fold improvement in photocurrent density over pristine CN film. [C8-7] We performed metal-free surface charge transfer doping of g-CN films and achieved a photocurrent density by a factor of 3. [C8-8] We demonstrated that the noncovalent interaction in the case of iodinated g-CN film can also enhance the PEC performance. [C8-9] We proposed a pseudo-metal-free strategy to combine the advantages of metal-free g-CN and metal-containing semiconductor materials with high PEC performance with the photocurrent density as high as 844.6 mA/cm2. [C8-10]. We realized the heterojunction interface by synthesizing sheet-like structures consisting of two semiconductors, facilitating considerably enhanced charge separation under visible light illumination. [C8-11]. We have also extended our research to search for crystal structures of forming unique electrides in the As-Li system. [C8-12]. We reported in detail our development of rapid thermal vapor condensation (RTVC) for growing g-CN films with improved PEC activity. [C8-13]. Finally, we reviewed the researches of PEC cells, our new perspective on the structure of g-CN, the achievements and deficiencies in the development of g-CN based photoelectrodes and some of our suggestions and new ideas about g-CN based films for PEC devices in the future. [C8-14].

11305618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305618.value: The TVC synthesis method is with simple steps and low cost, and thus present great competitiveness and application potential in the field of photoelectrochemical catalysis. Recently, we have achieved a high current density of 3mA/cm2 by forming heterojunction of g-CN with bismuth vanadate. Our further development will be to improve the TVC method to prepare g-CN films with more reactive sites and construct excellent heterojunctions/homojunctions and devote ourselves to designing and manufacturing stable solar hydrogen production systems with improved solar-to-hydrogen energy conversion efficiency. According to the bottom-up principle, we will carry out fundamental research and product development, to establish the structure-property relationship between the two-dimensional thin film microstructure and their electronic properties, to clarify the charge transfer mechanism at the photoanode interface, to propose effective strategies for efficient charge transfer, and finally to industrialize the photocatalytic seawater splitting system and promote its application in green shipping and other areas of applications.

While depositions of uniform, large area, and pinhole free g-CN thin films required for PEC applications have been successfully achieved recently by us, the films’ charge carrier conductivity and stability are still low for PEC applications. Although doping is a straightforward approach for improving the conductivity, the complicated results obtained so far very often could not be understood with conventional doping mechanisms In this project, we have explored dopings by nonmetal dopants through both computational and experimental approaches. 11305818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305818.value: In this project, the PI proposes to study the long time behavior and asymptotic behavior for large sound speed (and thus small Mach number) of solutions to free boundary problems of compressible fluids. Despites the great progress in the study of the long time behavior of solutions to the free boundary problems of incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and the water wave problem which is a free boundary problem of incompressible Euler equations, much less is known on the long time behavior of compressible fluids free boundary problems, in particular, when the effect of heat-conductivity is taken into account. The asymptotic behavior of solutions to compressible fluids equations in the entire space, periodic domains, and bounded domains with fixed boundaries when the Mach number tends to zero has been extensively studied. On the other hand, the only available result on this asymptotic behavior for compressible fluids with free boundaries is only on compressible Euler equation without taking into the effect of heat conductivity, and the liming equations in this case are incompressible Euler equations. When the heat conductivity effect is taken into account, the limiting equations as the Mach number tends to zero of compressible fluids are not incompressible anymore, and the problem becomes much more difficult and subtle. The PI proposes to explore those issues in this project. 在本项目中， 项目主持人提出研究可压缩流体自由边界问题大时间或大声速（因此小马赫数）解的渐进行为。尽管在不可压Navier-Stokes方程自由边界问题及由不可压Euler方程自由边界问题描述的水波问题的解的大时间行为研究有很大进展，但对于可压流体自由边界问题，特别是当把热传导效应纳入考虑时，所知结果甚少。在马赫数趋于零时，可压流体方程在全空间，周期区域以及带固定边界的有界区域解的渐进行为已有很深入的研究。但另一方面，对可压流体自由边界问题，仅有的结果没有把热传导效应纳入考虑。在此情形极限方程为不可压Euler方程。当把热传导效应纳入考虑时，马赫数趋于零时的极限方程不再是不可压缩的，问题因此变得更加困难而微妙。项目主持人提出在本项目中探索这些问题。

11305818.label: Realisation of objectives
11305818.value: For the free boundary problem of the full Navier–Stokes Equations with gravity of compressible fluids in three-dimensional of compressible viscous heat-conducting fluid, first, the global-in-time existence of solutions is proved. Then, we investigated the long time behaviour of the global-in-time solutions , and proved the global-in-time solution tends to a nontrivial equilibrium state of solutions as time tends to infinity. The role played by the heat-conductivity to both the global existence and long time behaviour of solutions is elucidated. This fufill the first objective of the project. For the free boundary problem of a compressible, viscous and heat-conducting fluid occupying an infinite layer, the associated resolvent equations of the linearized problem is studied in this project. An explicit representation of solutions to this boundary value problem, and the unknown boundary values are also well-characterized. The entropy variation and heat-conducting effects are clarified. Our results are essential for investigating the detailed and precise asymptotic behavior in long time or large sound speed (small Mach number) of solutions to the nonlinear free boundary problem. The free boundary problem of full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with small Mach number (thus the large sound speed if the fluid velocity is not small). We first give a formulation of weak solutions without requiring regularity of free surfaces and with the minimal requirement of regularity of fluid variables in any spatial dimension. This formulation accommodates a broad class of solutions with possible singularities. We then define the admissible weak solutions motivated by the entropy inequality of conservation laws. For admissible weak solutions, we obtain some uniform estimates with respect to the Mach number, and prove the asymptotic behavior in the average sense for small Mach number. Moreover, some Lq-estimates are obtained if the Lipschitzian regularity of the flow map is assumed when the initial domain is a bounded, connected and open set with the cone property. We also obtain uniform estimates and prove the asymptotics and convergence of solutions for all time when the Mach number tends to zero in 1d, with detailed convergence rates. The role played by the heat-conductivity to the behaviour of solutions as the Mach number tends to zero is well understood in the above results and their proofs. The above findings accomplish the second objective of this project. We also investigated the other physical effects such as magnetic fields to motion of free boundaries of fluids related partial differential equations.We proved the well-posedness for the linearized free boundary problem of incompressible ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations in a bounded domain. A key idea is to use the Lie derivative of the magnetic field taking the advantage that the magnetic field is tangential to the free boundary and divergence free. Besides the understanding of some physical effects to the motion of fluids related free boundaries, this activity also contributes to the development of geometric approaches for general fluids free boundaries not restricted to graphs. This is closely related to both objectives in this project. In a broader sense, it is very useful to the understanding and tool development of free boundary problems of fluids, among them, the proposed problems and objectives in this project are closely related. We also established the equivalence between Mean Field Game and a class of PDE systems closely related to Navier-Stokes equation of compressible fluids . It offers insights to investigate the behavior of solutions of compressible fluids in an intuitive way. It should be noted that understanding of behaviour of solutions to certain problems of compressible fluids is closely related to the objectives of this project.

For the free boundary problem of a compressible, viscous and heat-conducting fluid occupying an infinite layer, we study the associated resolvent equations of the linearized problem in article 4, we derive an explicit representation of solutions to this boundary value problem, and the unknown boundary values are also well-characterized. The entropy variation and heat-conducting effects make the problem much intricate and challenging. we establish the Lp, 1 < p < ∞, estimates for solutions to the resolvent problem. Our results are essential for investigating the detailed and precise asymptotic behavior in large time or large sound speed (small Mach number) of solutions to the nonlinear free boundary problem. We study the free boundary problem of full Navier-Stokes equations of compressible viscous and heat-conductive fluids with small Mach number in article 5. We first give a formulation of weak solutions without requiring regularity of free surfaces and with the minimal requirement of regularity of fluid variables in any spatial dimension. This formulation accommodates a broad class of solutions with possible singularities. We then define the admissible weak solutions motivated by the entropy inequality of conservation laws. For admissible weak solutions, we obtain some uniform estimates with respect to the Mach number, and prove the asymptotic behavior in the average sense for small Mach number. Moreover, some Lq-estimates are obtained for the Lipschitzian regular flow maps. We also obtain the uniform estimates and prove the asymptotics and convergence of solutions for all time when the Mach number tends to zero in 1d. In article 2, we prove the well-posedness for the linearized free boundary problem of incompressible ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations in a bounded domain. A key idea is to use the Lie derivative of the magnetic field taking the advantage that the magnetic field is tangential to the free boundary and divergence free. This paper contributes to the understanding of some physical effects such as the magnetic to the motion of fluid free boundaries and the development of geometric approaches for general free boundaries not restricted to graphs. 11305818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305818.value: For the weak solutions formulated in article 5 to the free boundary problem of compressible Navier-Stokes equations without requiring regularity of free surfaces to accommodate a broad class of solutions with possible singularities, it is a very challenging and interesting problem to prove the global-in-time existence for large initial data. For large data, even if they are smooth initially, the singularity will very likely develop in a finite time. Therefore, it is necessary to study weak solutions as formulated in this project. It is more realistic to study the isentropic case, as done by P. L. Lions for the initial value problem. This problem is particularly interesting to include singularities on free surfaces, such as splash singularity, wave crests and etc. This problem requires completely new ideas to construct suitable approximations and to establish compactness.

11305818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305818.value: In this project, we use rigorous mathematical analysis to investigate the free boundary problems of compressible viscous and heat-conductive fluids and related models. Free boundary problems of fluids arise in many important physical situations such as water waves, the evolution of the boundary of stars, vortex sheets, interfaces of oil and water, and shock waves. It is challenging to study these free boundary problems both theoretically and numerically. We developed new analytical and geometrical approaches in this project to investigate the behavior of solutions to these problems, in particular, for large time or small Mach number which is the ratio of fluid speed and sound of compressible fluids. The results obtained from this project disclose the behavior of solutions to these problems. The role of some physical effects, in particular, the heat-conductivity, to the behavior of free boundaries, is elucidated. Besides the effect of heat conductivity, we also investigate the role of other physical effects such as magnetic fields to the behavior of fluid free boundaries, and offer some insights to investigate the behavior of solutions of fluid partial differential equations in an intuitive way by using tools from other branches of mathematics.

11306018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306018.value: Rings and circles are fascinating objects for mankind. The humble-looking graphite, for example, contains stacks of 2-dimensional honeycomb sheets made of a great many six-membered carbon rings fused together. Indeed, fused carbon rings as such provides unparalleled stability as well excellent electronic properties: graphite is a mineral persisting on the geological time scale, and the individual honeycomb grid of graphite (called graphene) is a widely acclaimed 2D material for electronics (e.g., the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2010 was awarded on experiments performed on graphene). It remains, however, a grand scientific challenge to produce a crystalline 3D open framework using fused carbon rings, i.e., to build a molecular hotel wherein the walls are made of graphene-like sheets. Such an open scaffold the carbon walls provides structural strength and electronic properties, while the numerous nanoscopic “hotel rooms” serves as well-defined pores for trapping guest molecules for sensing, separation, catalysis and many other applications. The synthetic difficulty arises from the famous conundrum between bond strength and crystallinity: the very strong carbon-carbon bonds often form too fast and irreversibly, and the resultant framework solid tends to be ill-ordered. In other words, once a carbon ring is misplaced, it is difficult to take it out and fit it back in; thus the widely used porous solid, activated charcoal, is very disordered and non-crystalline, with pores of varying sizes and shapes. To resolve this dilemma, we employ a two-step approach that divorces the crystallization step from the formation of carbon grid: first, we crystallize a precursor network using the more reversible metal-carboxyl coordination bonds (i.e., we will use tailor-made organic linker molecules and metal ions as building blocks for templating the nano-hotel); second, we proceed to trigger (e.g., by heating at the right temperature range) massive cyclization reactions within and across the organic linker molecules while preserving the crystalline order dictated by the coordination scaffold. The formation of cyclized carbon links not only serves to strengthen the precursor coordination scaffold, but more importantly, enhance electroactivity and charge transport throughout the fused carbon network. 大家都喜歡圓圓滿滿。在科學研究中，圓形的和環狀的構造常常是很迷人的。其貌不揚的石墨就是由碳原子六元環融合在一起形成的二維蜂窩層狀結構。這種稠環碳環的結構具有獨特的化學穩定性和電子學特性。大家都知道，石墨是一種在自然界中長期稳定存在的礦物，並且石墨的單層蜂窩網絡（即，石墨烯）是一種非常熱門的二維電子材料。2010年諾貝爾物理學獎就授予了從事石墨烯研究的科學家。然而，要用稠環的碳原子的基元來構築三維的（而不是二維的）晶態開放框架仍然是相當困難的。這有點像要運用石墨烯的薄片作為牆體來建造一個分子旅館。在這種開放框架中， 碳原子的牆壁將同時賦予結構強度和電子特性上的種種優良特性； 其眾多精確設計的空穴猶如納米“酒店客房”，可以捕獲客體分子，用於傳感、分離、催化以及其它應用。 構築這種三維有序材料的困難在於，化學鍵強度和結晶有序度通常是一對矛盾。碳-碳鍵的鍵能很大，它的形成通常是極快的而且是一個不可逆的過程，因此，所得到的固態框架材料的結構往往是混亂無序的。換句話說，一旦碳-碳鍵或碳環在錯誤的位置形成以後，將很難將它取出來再裝回去。比如，用途廣泛的活性炭就是一種典型的多孔碳材料；它的結構在微觀上高度地無序，其孔洞的大小和形狀各異，顯示出典型的非結晶態的屬性。為了克服這個困難，我們在此提出一種分兩步走的合成策略，把晶體的生成和碳網的構建這兩個過程分開來實施。第一步，我們運用可逆度更高的金屬-羧酸配位鍵（而不是碳碳共價鍵）得到晶態的前驅框架（即使用靶向設計的有機配體分子和金屬離子作為模板合成納米旅館）；第二步，觸發有機配體分子內和分子間的徹底環化並同時保持配位框架的結晶性。環化後的配體的不僅增強了前驅配位框架的強度， 更重要的是，可以提高電導性和電荷在稠環碳網中的傳輸效率。

11306018.label: Realisation of objectives
11306018.value: The realization of objects 1 and 2, regarding the synthesis of backfolded, phenylalkynyl linker molecules and the construction of porous metal-organic frameworks, was highlighted by all the six papers attached. Therein, we report breakthrough in the synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) extensively equipped with backfolded, phenylalkynyl of diverse functions, ranging from Dense Alkyne Arrays (paper 2), Ferrocene (paper 3), thioether and ether groups (papers 4-6) and strongly Donor–Acceptor units (papers 1). With one eye-opening highlight of the linker design achievements illustrated in paper 2 (Figure 1). Specifically, Paper 2 illustrates the fruitful linker design invoking alkyne side arm functionalization for MOF chemistry: the linker is one of the biggest in molecular weight among MOF linker molecules, and it enables the efficient uptake of reactive metal compounds: the exemplary Co2(CO)8 guest also readily transforms into atomistically dispersed cobalt oxide within the porous solid for catalysis studies. In line with the stated objectives of this project for metal-uptake, catalytic and electronic properties, these diverse molecules for MOF construction achieved with efficient, wide-scope synthetic protocols, lay the foundation for the subsequent functional design/discovery and property studies. These important discoveries, as stated below, serves to fully accomplish the objective 3 and 4. Important discoveries have been made in the the tackling of objective 3, i.e., concerning thermally triggering cyclization and ring fusion in the assembled porous crystals for forming conjugated carbon networks, and objective 4, i.e., concerning studies on porosity (e.g., pore volume/surface area measurement) and electronic properties and electrocatalysis. For example, in paper 4, we described a covalent MOF system with a highest thermal stability among similar systems. The resultant Zr oxide/nanographene hybrid solid is stable in saturated NaOH and concentrated H3PO4, allowing a convenient anchoring of H3PO4 into its porous matrix to enable size-selective heterogeneous acid catalysis. The Zr oxide components can also be removed by strong hydrofluoric acid to further enhance the surface area (up to 650 m2 g−1), without collapsing the nanographene scaffold. In paper 3, we have discovered a high-yield synthetic strategy for iron−nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe−N−C) nanotube materials that emulate the electrocatalysis performance of commercial Pt/C. We have discovered a metal−organic framework (MOF) system that can smoothly convert into both uniform carbon nanotube (CNT) arrays and carbon matrices/CNT composites with promising electrocatalytic properties. The linker system reported here can be flexibly modified in shape and functionality (e.g., regarding the alkyne arrays and the pendant metal units), so as to further explore the carbonization process and to target a broader array of optimized functions and structures (e.g., 3D graphenes/schwarzites). Using this carbon-rich designer metal–organic framework (MOF), we open a high-yield synthetic strategy for iron–nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe–N–C) nanotube materials that emulate the electrocatalysis performance of commercial Pt/C. In paper 5, we expand our linker/MOF chemistry into the topical Ni8-pyrazolate systems. The crystalline Ni8-pyrazolate scaffold also retains the crystalline order even after thermal treatments (up to 300 °C) that served to partially graphitize the neighboring alkyne units. The resultant nanographene components enhance the electroactive properties of the porous hosts, achieving hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity that rivals that of topical nickel/palladium-enabled materials.

11306018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306018.value: The major discoveries are illustrated below. We discovered a covalent MOF system with a highest thermal stability among similar systems (paper 4). This is a curious case study of a Zr(IV)-carboxylate framework, which retains significant crystalline order after cascade thermocyclization of its linker components, and – more notably – after the crucial carboxylate links were severed by heat. Vigorous heat treatment (e.g., 450 °C and above) benzannulates the multiple alkyne groups on the linker to generate linked nanographene blocks and to afford real stability. In paper 5, we expand our linker/MOF chemistry into the topical Ni8-pyrazolate systems. The key discovery here is: unlike the commonly observed full 12 connections of the Ni8(OH)4(H2O)2 clusters in other Ni8-pyrazolate networks, significant linker deficiency was observed here, leaving about half of the Ni(II) sites capped by acetate ligands, which can be potentially removed to open the metal sites for reactivity. The cruciform linker molecule here features two designer functions: the pyrazole donors for framework construction, and the vicinal alkynyl units for benzannulation to form nanographene units into the Ni8-pyrazolate scaffold. In paper 3, we have discovered a high-yield synthetic strategy for iron−nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe−N−C) nanotube materials that emulate the electrocatalysis performance of commercial Pt/C. We have discovered a metal−organic framework (MOF) system that can smoothly convert into both uniform carbon nanotube (CNT) arrays and carbon matrices/CNT composites with promising electrocatalytic properties. The Zr(IV)-based MOF solid boasts multiple key functions: (1) a dense array of alkyne units over the backbone and the side arms, which are primed for extensive graphitization; (2) the open, branched structure helps maintain porosity for absorbing nitrogen dopants; and (3) ferrocene units on the side arms as atomically dispersed precursor catalyst for targeting micropores and for effective iron encapsulation in the carbonized product. As a result, upon pyrolysis, over 89% of the carbon component in the MOF scaffold is successfully converted into carbonized products, thereby contrasting the easily volatilized carbon of most MOFs. Moreover, over 97% of the iron ends up being encased as acid-resistant Fe/Fe3C nanoparticles in carbon nanotubes/carbon matrices.

11306018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306018.value: In pursuing the synthesis and properties of the MOF materials, we have extensively tackled the two central issues: stability and functionalities. But environmentally friendly, green assembly of MOF solids remains a challenge, and proposed course of action includes using water as the sole solvent to form robust metal-organic frameworks; and MOF synthesis without solvents (by mechanical grinding, for example). Advances in these important practical direction shall paves the way for broader/industrial application of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as a growing class of porous materials.

11306118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306118.value: Oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions cover a large and diverse body of familiar chemical and physical processes such as fire, rusting, browning of fruit, respiration and photosynthesis. In the redox reactions such as water oxidation and CO2 reduction catalyzed by electrocatalysts, the efficiency of the electrocatalyst is normally evaluated as a function of two interrelated quantities - rate and overpotential. The overpotential is the difference between the applied potential and the equilibrium potential for the reaction under given reaction conditions. This equilibrium potential is further related to the standard reduction (or oxidation) potential (Ered or Eox), via the Nernst equation. Thus, the Ered (or Eox) is one of the key electrochemical properties governing the efficiency of electrocatalyst. Experimentally, the Ered (or Eox) can be accurately measured by mean of cyclic voltammetry and nevertheless the theoretical determination of Ered or Eox in solvated medium is still in its developing stage. Knowledge on thermochemical properties in both gaseous state and condensed phase is of fundamental importance. By determining the value of thermochemical properties such as ionization energy, bond dissociation energy, proton affinity, activation energy and heat of formation, one can easily foresee the reactivity in chemical reactions. The ab initio predictions of the above thermochemical properties values are so mature that a number of theoretical composite procedures with high reliability and accuracy have been developed in last twenty years. For example, method like the Gaussian-n (Gn, n = 1 - 4), has been implemented in general quantum chemistry software and made available to computational and generic chemists. The accuracy for thermochemistry predictions, in general, is ~2-4 kJ/mol. However, the composite methods are limited to gas-phase molecules; none of them is targeted for predictions of Eored for redox reactions. In spite of the importance of redox reactions in chemistry, the development of composite theoretical method for the Eored predictions in solvent and solution environment, especially for transition metal-containing species is lag behind. This proposal seeks financial support to (i) develop an ab initio composite procedure for the predictions of standard redox potentials in aqueous and non-aqueous medium; (ii) assess the performance of the composite procedure by comparing the results with the available Ered values for metal containing species; (iii) apply the composite procedure to predict Ered of biologically and chemically important redox active species.

11306118.label: Realisation of objectives
11306118.value: We develop a theoretical procedure for accurate determination of reduction potentials for transition-metal containing species. This procedure first computes the gas phase ionization energy (IE) with the explicitly correlated CCSD(T)-F12 method and includes with the zero-point energy correction, core-valence electronic correlation, relativistic and spin-orbit coupling effects. By mean of Born-Haber thermochemical cycle, the one-electron reduction potential (Eabs)is computed by summing up the gas phase IE and the corresponding Gibbs free energies of solvation for both the neutral and cationic species. We have applied this theoretical procedure to two sets of transition-metal compounds: 1) Reduction potentials of ferrocene/ferrocenium and cobaltocene/cobaltocenium, Fe(C5H5)2/Fe(C5H5)2+ and Co(C5H5)2/Co(C5H5)2+ Our theoretical protocol gives reliable predictions (in V) for Eabs(Cp2Fe/Cp2Fe) = 4.616 (water) and 4.644 (acetonitrile) and Eabs(Cp2Co/Cp2Co) = 3.347 (water) and 3.369 (acetonitrile). These predictions compare favorably with available experimental values: Eabs(Cp2Fe/Cp2Fe) = 4.682 (water) and 4.763 V (acetonitrile), Eabs(Cp2Co/Cp2Co+) = 3.321 (water) and 3.369 V (acetonitrile). The maximum absolute deviation for Eabs(Cp2Fe/Cp2Fe+) and Eabs(Cp2Co/Cp2Co+) is ~120 mV. We have tested three solvent models (PCM, SMD and uESE), it turns out that only the SMD model (computed at DFT level) gives the best estimation to the value for “Delta_G of solvation(cation)-Delta_G of solvation(neutral)”, thus the SMD solvation model is adapted in the procedure. This work and results have been written in a manuscript and it is ready for submission. 2. Reduction potentials of [M(H2O)6,18]2+/3+ where M is Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu and Zn To account for solvation effect of aqueous medium, we employ a hybrid solvation model: explicit solvation shell of six and eighteen water molecules surrounding the M2+/M3+ ions and additional solvation effect by implicit solvation model (given by SMD). The IE([M(H2O)6,18]2+-> M(H2O)6,18]3+) are computed with explicitly correlated coupled cluster method, including zero-point energy correction, core-valence electronic correlation, relativistic and spin-orbit coupling effects. Together with the Gibbs free energy of solvation of both the [M(H2O)6,18]2+ and [M(H2O)6,18]3+ species, we obtain the one-electron Eabs for the whole series, [M(H2O)6,18]2+/3+ where M is Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu and Zn. The values of Eabs([M(H2O)6]2+/[M(H2O)6]3+) and Eabs([M(H2O)12]2+/[M(H2O)12]3+) are used to extrapolate the one-electron reduction potential of M2+/3+ in aqueous solution, i.e., Eabs([M(H2O)inf]2+/[M(H2O)inf]3+), where M2+ and M3+ ions are surrounded by “infinite” number of water molecules. The results (in V) are very promising, Eabs(V2+/3+)=-0.28 (our) vs -0.255 (expt), Eabs(Cr2+/3+)=-0.47 (our) vs -0.424 (expt), Eabs(Mn2+/3+)=1.43 (our) vs 1.5 (expt); Eabs(Fe2+/3+)=0.72 (our) vs 0.771 (expt), Eabs(Co2+/3+)=1.99 (our) vs 1.92 (expt). The calculations are finished and we are writing up the manuscript.

11306318.label: Project Objectives
11306318.value: Wavelet analysis of CNNs. We propose a wavelet analysis approach to study the approximation ability of convolutional deep neural networks activated by ReLU. A special convolutional deep net achieved by initial layers of convolutions is expected to reproduce some ridge splines, and to generate a hypothesis space with a strong approximation ability leading to asymptotic universality as the depth tends to infinity. Approximation of radial functions by deep neural networks. The approximation theory problem of approximating a univariate polynomial of degree k by a shallow neural network of width k+1 will be studied through scaling with weights and translating with biases. Then the approximation of a general univariate function by scaled shifts of the activation function in convolutional deep nets or multi-layer nets with tight widths will be investigated. Tight approximation orders are expected and will be used to approximate radial or ridge functions efficiently by fully connected deep neural networks, recurrent neural networks associated with transition functions, and convolutional deep neural networks activated by ReLU and sigmoidal functions.

11306318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306318.value: Deep learning is a powerful tool for artificial intelligence and has demonstrated its power in speech recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, and many other areas of practical applications. Compared with its high efficiency in processing big data, its theoretical understanding is way behind. There is an urgent need to develop rigorous mathematical analysis for deep learning algorithms. The goal of this project is to make some contributions to the mathematical theory of deep learning from the viewpoints of wavelet analysis and approximation theory. Our first target is to develop some wavelet analysis of convolutional deep neural networks activated by ReLU (the rectified linear unit) and to estimate the approximation ability of the generated deep learning algorithm. Our idea is to construct a special convolutional deep net to reproduce some ridge splines which are continuous linear splines composed with homogeneous linear functions, and to study the approximation ability of the generated hypothesis space. This can be achieved by initial layers of convolutions to generate a rich family of homogeneous linear functions and deeper layers of activations to generate linear splines with knot sets depending on the depth of the deep net. Our second target is to investigate the approximation of radial functions by fully connected deep neural networks and convolutional deep neural networks activated by ReLU and sigmoidal functions. We expect to derive approximation orders by approximating a univariate polynomial of degree k by a shallow neural network of width k+1, and then approximate the univariate function generating the radial function by scaled shifts of the activation function in convolutional deep nets or multi-layer nets with tight widths. Methods and ideas from wavelet analysis, learning theory, and approximation by radial basis functions and from shift-invariant spaces play an essential role in our research. 深度學習是一種人工智能方法，已經在語音識別，計算機視覺，自然語言處理和其他領域得以廣泛應用。與其在大數據的高效應用相比，其理論認識遠遠落後,迫切需要發展深度學習算法的嚴格數學分析。這個項目的目標是從小波分析和逼近論的觀點建立一些深度學習的數學理論。我們的第一個目標是發展ReLU激活的卷積型深度神經網絡的小波分析並估計所產生的深度學習算法的逼近能力。我們的第二個目標是通過全連通深度神經網絡和卷積型深度神經網絡研究徑向函數的逼近。來自小波分析，學習理論和在平移不變空間中徑向基函數逼近的方法和思想在我們的研究中起著至關重要的作用。

11306318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306318.value: Deep learning is a powerful tool for artificial intelligence and has demonstrated its power in many practical applications. But its theoretical understanding is way behind, and there is an urgent need to develop rigorous mathematical analysis for deep learning algorithms. In [1] we design deep neural networks of tree structures for realization of radial functions so as to enable rotational invariance in an arbitrarily high-dimensional Euclidean space. It is shown that deep nets have much better performance than shallow nets in terms of approximation accuracy and learning capabilities. In particular, for learning radial functions, it is shown that near-optimal rates can be achieved by deep nets but not by shallow nets. In [2] we aim at rigorous verification of the importance of massive data in embodying the outperformance of deep learning. We prove that the massiveness of data is necessary in realizing the spatial sparseness and deep nets with structures are crucial tools to make full use of massive data. In [3] we carry out wavelet analysis for CNNs when applied to approximate functions on unit spheres. Our analysis presents rates of uniform approximation when the approximated function lies in a Sobolev space or takes an additive ridge form. Our work verifies theoretically the modelling and approximation ability of deep convolutional neural networks followed by an important operation of downsampling from wavelet analysis. Our spherical analysis uses the inner product form of the reproducing kernels of the spaces of spherical harmonics and then to apply convolutional factorizations of filters to realize the generated linear features. In [4] we develop distributed filtered hyperinterpolation for noisy data on the sphere. The distributed strategy allows parallel computing for data processing and model selection. It reduces computational cost for each server while preserving the approximation capability. We prove a quantitative relation between the approximation capability of distributed filtered hyperinterpolation and the numbers of input data and servers. In [5] Information theoretic learning is a learning paradigm that uses concepts of entropies and divergences from information theory. A variety of signal processing and machine learning methods fall into this framework. Minimum error entropy principle is a typical one amongst them. In this paper, we study a kernel version of minimum error entropy methods that can be used to find nonlinear structures in the data. We show by convergence rates that the kernel minimum error entropy can be implemented by kernel based gradient descent algorithms with or without regularization.

11306318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306318.value: The wavelet analysis for CNNs developed in this project can be applied to other deep learning algorithms. This will be explored in our future research activities.

11306318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306318.value: Deep learning is a powerful tool for artificial intelligence and has demonstrated its power in many practical applications. But its theoretical understanding is way behind, and there is an urgent need to develop rigorous mathematical analysis for deep learning algorithms. In this project we develop wavelet analysis for deep convolutional neural networks and analyze the approximation and learning abilities of these networks. Tight approximation and learning rates are derived for approximating radial or ridge functions efficiently by deep convolutional neural networks.

11500118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500118.value: 实验资产市场的信息交流与社会交易

11500118.label: Project Objectives
11500118.value: Implement social trading platform in the laboratory: We plan to design asset market experiments with features that offer interaction and information exchange between investors in real time. This allows for the possibility of sharing knowledge with others and allows investors to trade with the help of others by comparing and copying other traders' strategies. Investigate the impact of social interaction on investment decisions of traders, market liquidity and asset pricing: We intend to study how social trading alters traders’ strategies to invest in the asset. We also plan to focus on the effect of social trading on the overall market liquidity and study various properties of asset prices including whether prices track the fundamental values better in the presence of information exchange among traders. Within this setup, our specific aim is to understand the effect of social trading on the formation, magnitude and duration of asset price bubbles. Analyze the effect of news concerning the underlying value of an asset on its trading price in the presence of social trading: We plan to compare the market reaction to news regarding the fundamental value of the asset with and without the provision of information sharing among investors. Specifically, our goal here is to study whether the duration of over-reaction or under-reaction can be corrected quickly when social communication is possible.
