11502218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502218.value: Industrial suppliers often proactively deal with demands derived from downstream markets (Hillebrand & Biemans, 2011) and offer supplier-generated innovations to B2B customers. Such a strategy enables suppliers to gain favorable supplier status and reap considerable profits. Also, it contributes to customers’ product innovation and success. For example, Coca-Cola’s pioneering supplier Rexam, who “figured out a way to print eight different designs on the same production line and pack 24 variations on a single pallet”, contributed to Coke’s success in the fizzy drink sector in South America (Geraint 2014). Despite the high relevance of supplier-generated innovation in industrial customers’ product innovation and success, extant literature has largely focused on supplier involvement and collaboration in customers’ new product development (Petersen, Handfield, & Ragatz, 2005; Ragatz, Handfield, & Petersen, 2002; Yeniyurt, Henke Jr, & Yalcinkaya, 2014), largely neglecting suppliers’ role as innovation-initiators. We know little about how customers react to supplier-initiated innovations and how suppliers leverage their capabilities or strategies to gain customer adoption. This research gap is significant given manufacturers in many sectors (e.g., food and beverage, automotive) are increasingly depending on innovations from external stakeholders, particularly suppliers, to deal with intensified competition and technological turbulence. To address these concerns, this research draws on the literature of influence strategy, market orientation, and structural balance theory, to understand how suppliers gain customer adoption (intention) of innovations. We first conceptualize two types of supplier capabilities —downstream marketing capability and technological capability as supplier influence strategies. We further examine how supplier influence strategies induce customer adoption (intention) under certain contextual factors (i.e., dependence, trust), and their relationship performance implications. We focus on an under-researched setting—supplier-initiated innovation and customer adoption in the FMCG industry. To test the model, we collect both qualitative cases regarding supplier-generated innovations and customer reactions, and matched survey data from suppliers and customers in China. This study adds to the understanding of the role of downstream marketing in B2B markets. It extends the notion of market orientation (Jaworski & Kohli, 1993; Narver & Slater, 1990) to the downstream market, and the scope of influence strategies in interfirm relationships (Frazier & Summers, 1984; Frazier & Rody, 1991) to the innovation adoption context. The resultant insights could help practitioners in the B2B context find an alternative solution to the common criticism of ‘marketing myopia’ and ‘difficult-to-justify’ for the existence of the marketing function. 工業供應商通常主動應對來自下游市場的需求（Hillebrand＆Biemans，2011），並為B2B客戶提供其創新解決方案。這種策略使供應商在競爭中佔據有利的地位並獲得可觀的利潤。此外，該策略還有助於客戶的產品創新和成功。例如，可口可樂的先驅供應商Rexam “想出了在同一生產線上印刷八種不同設計的方法，並在一個托盤上包裝24種變體”，這促成了可口可樂在南美碳酸飲料領域的成功（Geraint 2014 ）。 儘管供應商主導的創新和工業客戶產品的創新和成功之間具有高度相關性，但現有文獻主要關注供應商參與和協作客戶新產品開發的角色（Petersen，Handfield，＆Ragatz，2005; Ragatz，Handfield，＆Petersen ，2002; Yeniyurt，Henke，和Yalcinkaya，2014），在很大程度上忽視了供應商作為創新發起者的角色。我們對客戶如何應對供應商發起的創新以及供應商如何利用其能力或策略來促使客戶採用其創新知之甚少。鑑於許多行業（例如食品和飲料，汽車）的製造商越來越依賴外部利益相關者（尤其是供應商）的創新來應對激烈的競爭和技術動盪，彌補這一研究差距尤顯重要。 為了解決上述問題，本研究借鑒了影響戰略，市場導向和結構平衡理論的文獻，以了解供應商如何獲得客戶對創新的採用（意圖）。我們首先將兩種作為為供應商影響策略的能力（下游營銷能力和技術能力）概念化。進一步地，我們研究供應商影響策略如何引發客戶在某些背景因素下（即依賴，信任）對創新採用（意圖）以及關係績效的影響。我們專注於一個未得到足夠關注的研究情境 -- 快速消費品行業中供應商發起的創新和客戶採用。為了測試我們的理論模型，我們收集了有關供應商主導的創新和客戶反應的定性案例，以及來自中國市場上供應商和客戶的匹配調查數據。 本研究增進了對下游營銷在B2B市場中之作用的理解。它將市場導向（Jaworski＆Kohli，1993; Narver＆Slater，1990）的概念擴展到下游市場，並將企業間關係中的影響策略（Frazier＆Summers，1984; Frazier＆Rody，1991）擴展到創新採用情境中。由此研究產生的結論可以幫助B2B從業者找到一種替代解決方案，以解決來自營銷實踐普遍中存在的“營銷近視”和“難以證明（營銷價值）”的批評。

11502318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502318.value: This project will explore the dynamics of employment, nonemployment, and hours worked in a search and matching model with heterogeneous workers and will investigate its applications in Hong Kong using quarterly microstructure data of the general household survey from the Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong. The project will first set up a search and matching model with heterogeneous workers and hours worked. Then the model will be generalized to include heterogeneity across the observable personal characteristics in data, such as occupation, industry, educational attainment, and earnings, and the characteristics of the households they belong to, such as type of accommodation, tenure, rent, household size, and household income. Nonemployed workers will be allowed to decide whether to search for jobs and become unemployed or stay out of the labor force in the model. When the opportunity cost of working is different across individuals, some unemployed workers will stop searching for a job (drop out of the labor force) if the optimal hours worked results in a negative job surplus. For example, a low-skilled unemployed mother with a new-born baby may become a home-maker because her home production increases relative to the average revenue she can generate on a job. After solving and analyzing the search and matching model, the results will be fitted into the data from the Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong. The microstructure data from the general household survey will be merged with the data of vacancy posting by occupation, industries, and firm level characteristics. The situations of the labor market will be investigated using the combined data with household characteristics, personal characteristics, and firm vacancy posting. This project will also explore suggestive labor-market policies such as how to regulate hours worked efficiently taking into account both employee benefits and the growth of firms (especially young and productive but financially constrained firms) which is key to the economic growth in Hong Kong. 該項目將探討就業､非就業以及工作時間在異質工人的搜索和匹配模型中的動態，並將使用香港政府統計處的綜合住戶統計調查的季度微觀結構數據調查其在香港的應用。該項目將首先建立一個包含異質工人與工時差異的搜索和匹配模型。然後，該模型將被概括為包括數據中可觀察到的個人屬性的差異，例如職業､工作行業､教育程度和收入，以及他們所屬的家庭的特徵的差異，例如住宅類型､居住年限､租金､家庭規模和家庭收入。在模型中，非就業人士將被允許決定是否尋找工作，從而要么成為失業者，要么不構成勞動力。當個人的工作機會成本不同時，如果最佳工作時間導致工作盈餘負增長，一些失業工人將停止尋找工作（退出勞工市場）。例如，一個擁有新生嬰兒的低技能失業母親可能會成為家庭主婦，因為她在家從事家務的益處相對於她在工作中可以產生的平均收入增加。在分析和求解搜索和匹配模型後，我們將用香港政府統計處的數據應證結果。綜合住戶統計調查的微觀結構數據將與職業､行業和公司層面特徵的空缺職位數據合併，並與家庭特徵､個人特徵和公司空缺職位綜合起來調查勞動力市場的情況。該項目還將探討建議性的勞動力市場政策，例如如何有效地規範工作時間，同時考慮到員工福利和公司（特別是年輕和富有成效但財務受限的初創企業）的增長，這對香港經濟增長至關重要。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502418.value: This project examines the determinants of the relative yields on municipal and taxable bonds. We employ a reduced-form model with default, liquidity and tax factors to price tax-exempt bonds. Using a unique transaction dataset, we directly estimate marginal tax rate and liquidity and default premia from transaction data of municipal bonds. The estimated marginal tax rate is consistent with the statutory income tax rate of wealthy individuals. We find that a substantial portion of the yield spread between municipal and taxable bonds is attributable to liquidity and default premia. Results show that taxes, liquidity and default risk are important factors in the pricing of municipal bonds.

11503318.label: Project Objectives

11503318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11503318.value: The unionization of workers imposes various consequences on corporate policies. For example, through collective bargaining (and potential disruption of operations), labor unions can hamper corporate investment, mergers, and innovations. A growing body of literature shows that firms react strategically to facilitate their bargaining with labor unions. In this proposed study, we carry on this line of research by examining how firms strategically reshape their customer-supplier relationships in response to labor unionization. Specifically, using a regression discontinuity design that takes advantage of union election data, we investigate the causal impact of unionization on the trade credit and other supply contract terms extended to customers. The cost of labor unions could spill over to customers in the form of poor product quality and high input price. To mitigate such costs and retain major customers, unionized firms are expected to extend more trade credit and more favorable supply contract terms to its customers. Consequently, these firms’ accounts receivable would increase, the discount rate they provide for early trade credit repayment would increase, and the supply contract they provide to customers will contain fewer covenants and a less stringent collateral requirement. In other words, supplier firms are expected to provide financial flexibility to their customers to compensate the heightened labor risk borne by these customers. Moreover, allowing customers more trade credits can further benefit supplier firms when they negotiate contracts with their labor unions, since more accounts receivable decreases firms’ cash flows for workers to claim. The contribution of the research is twofold. First, this is one of the first few examinations of how supply chain relationships are affected by labor unions. In a related work, Chen et al. (2017) show that customers of unionized firms tend to shift purchases away from unionized firms. Our paper, instead, examines whether unionized firms offer better supply contract terms to retain their customers. Our potential findings can add to the literature that examines firms’ strategic behaviors in response to the unionization of their workers (Matsa, 2010; Klasa et al., 2009; Yi, 2016). Second, the recent trade credit literature argues that trade credit can be used strategically to deter potential entrants and reduce product market competition (Barrot, 2016; Singh, 2017). We add to this line of literature by showing that trade credit can play a strategic role in retaining customers and in bargaining with workers through working capital management (reducing cash). 工會組織會對企業政策產生各種影響。比如，通過勞資談判（及罷工造成的經營中斷），工會會影響到公司的投資、併購和創新行為。越來越多的文獻發現企業會做出戰略性應對措施來和工會討價還價。為了對這一領域有更深的了解，我們會在本研究中考察企業在應對工會時是如何戰略性地重塑和客戶的關係的。具體來說，通過基於工會選舉數據的斷點回歸方法，我們研究工會組織怎樣影響企業提供給客戶的貿易信用和其他供應合同條款。 工會組織會影響到企業的產品質量和產品價格，從而給客戶帶來成本。為了減輕這部分成本對客戶造成的影響，工會化的企業預計會給客戶提供更多的貿易信用和更優惠的供應條款。這會使得工會化企業的應收賬款提高，其供應合同裡面也可能包括更少的限制條款和更寬松的擔保要求。換句話說，由於工會成立給客戶帶來風險，工會化企業會給這些客戶提供更多的財務彈性來補償他們承擔的風險。另外，為客戶提供更多的貿易信用可以提高企業和工會談判時的議價能力，因為應收賬款增多會減少可供工人索取的現金流。 本研究有兩方面的貢獻。第一，本文是最先研究工會組織是如何影響供應鏈關係的文章之一。在一篇相關文章中，Chen et al. (2017)發現工會化企業的客戶會從工會化企業購買更少的商品。本文則研究工會化企業是否會提供更好的供給合同條款來留住客戶。我們的可能發現可以對企業應對工會運動的戰略性行為這一文獻做出貢獻。第二，最近的貿易信用文獻提出貿易信用可以被用作阻止市場進入、降低競爭的戰略性工具。本文提出貿易信用可以在留住客戶以及和工會討價還價（通過降低現金流）方面起到戰略性作用，從而對這一文獻做出貢獻。

11503318.label: Realisation of objectives
11503318.value: The main objectives, as stated above, has been 100% achieved under the support of the grant. In the paper "LGBT Employment Nondiscrimination and Capital Structure", the principal investigator (PI) and his coauthors study whether promoting workplace equality, i.e., LGBT employment nondiscrimination protection, affects firms' debt contracting and capital structure. The findings of the completed paper are as follows. (1) We start the empirical tests with using the Corporate Equality Index (CEI) published by the Human Rights Campaign Foundation to quantify a firm's LGBT nondiscrimination CSR practices in a cross-sectional analysis. A higher CEI score indicates that the firm has devoted more resources to taking care of LGBT employees' welfare. We find a negative association between firms' CEI scores and financial leverage, consistent with the hypothesis that a good corporate LGBT nondiscrimination practice incorporates the expected cost associated with potential litigations, which increases the cost and the rigidity of labor management. (2) To establish causality from LGBT nondiscrimination CSR practices to firms' financial leverage, we exploit the setting afforded by staggered passages of state LGBT nondiscrimination laws. These laws exogenously increase firms' social responsibility for LGBT workplace equality, increasing LGBT-related labor cost and litigation risk for affected firms. Using a staggered as well as a stacked difference-in-differences approach, we document that after passages of state LGBT nondiscrimination laws, firms headquartered in these states experience a reduction in financial leverage, consistent with the CEI cross-sectional regression result. (3) To demonstrate that LGBT nondiscrimination laws indeed reduce a firm's operating flexibility by increasing the rigidity of labor cost, we directly test whether there is an increase in operating leverage after passages of state LGBT nondiscrimination laws. We show that a firm's operating leverage, proxied by the sensitivity of the change in EBIT to the change in sales, increases after passages of state LGBT nondiscrimination laws. (4) Further, heightened financial distress caused by a higher labor cost can be reflected in firms' borrowing cost. We find that the loan spread for borrowers in states that pass LGBT nondiscrimination laws increases relative to that for borrowers in states not passing similar laws. This finding provides direct evidence on the consequence of an increase in financial distress cost. (5) To further confirm that firms reduce financial leverage in response to a higher labor cost and increased litigation risk due to LGBT nondiscrimination protection, we conduct several cross-sectional tests. We find that firms that are in labor-intensive industries, rely on labor layoffs to manage cost, have been defendants in LGBT-related lawsuits, and are financially distressed, experience a greater reduction in financial leverage in response to LGBT nondiscrimination laws.

11503318.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503318.value: This grant has supported three papers of the PI in the field of debt contracting, the proposed field of the funding application. First, as stated above, the PI has successfully achieved all objectives of the proposed study, and come up with a complete paper "LGBT Employment Nondiscrimination and Capital Structure". The paper is a timely study considering that the U.S. Supreme Court recognized LGBT employment nondiscrimination at the federal level on June 15, 2020. Examining state-level passages of LGBT nondiscrimination laws, the paper contributes to the understanding of how such laws can affect firms' financing cost and capital structure. While the study belongs to the broad literature on the association between labor and leverage, the authors trace LGBT equality, arguably the most important and debated human rights movement of our era, and show how it is changing modern corporations and the society. The paper has been presented in the University of New South Wales and accepted for presentation at the CAAA annual conference 2023, and are ready for submission to a journal in the UTD journal list. Second, the funding scheme of the current grant has lent significant support to PI's two other papers in related field, both papers having been developed, circulated and published during the duration of the grant. One is "The Real Effects of Implicit Government Guarantee: Evidence from Chinese State-Owned Enterprise Defaults", which studies the real effect of debt financing and contracting in China's corporate bond market. The paper has been published in Management Science, with the funding support of the current grant acknowledged. The other is "Labor Mobility and Loan Origination", which studies how labor mobility of loan officers affects the contract outcome of mortgage loans in the U.S. The paper has been accepted for publication in Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, with the funding support of the current grant acknowledged.

11503318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503318.value: First, the PI and his coauthors are aiming at revising the paper according to comments from UNSW and CAAA (and other future seminars/conferences), submitting it to a good journal, and eventually publishing the paper as a research outcome. Second, the PI intends to extend the idea by further exploring the LGBT nondiscrimination policy's labor market implications, asking whether LGBT nondiscrimination employment protection laws stimulate the labor market development and what types of firms or groups of workers are favorably (or unfavorably) affected by LGBT employment nondiscrimination legislations. The labor market implications are an important topic and have to be studied properly, as a law or a public policy can have unintended consequences or its cost can be disproportionately born by a specific types of firms or people. Some preliminary findings have been documented and the PI and his coauthors plan to carry on this line of agenda.

11503318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503318.value: LGBT nondiscrimination is an integral component of workplace equality. To implement LGBT workplace nondiscrimination, firms expend resources on labor adjustment. This can in turn increase firms' borrowing cost, leading to a reduction in financial leverage and increase loan spread. Accordingly, we find a negative association between firms' Corporate Equality Index scores and financial leverage. Further, when a state passes LGBT nondiscrimination laws, firms headquartered in this state reduce their leverage ratio. Leverage reduces more for firms sensitive to LGBT labor related issues, such as those that are labor intensive, prone to mass layoffs, having experienced past LGBT lawsuits, and financially distressed. While it appears that firms are incurring a cost associated with LGBT nondiscrimination, without nondiscrimination, this cost could be unfairly borne by the LGBT community.

11503418.value: 受一個快餐連鎖店面臨的挑戰所啟發，本課題研究面對原材料價格不確定變化下，一個公司應該如何制定自己的最優採購策略。具體而言，考慮一個公司從兩個渠道採購，一個海外供應商和一個本地供應商，前者採購前置時間較長但價格往往較低，後者則恰好相反。兩個供應商的價格相關且隨時間波動。公司的目標是優化採購策略以達到再保證供應不中斷的前提下最小化採購成功。 本課題的挑戰在於較長的採購前置時間以及價格的不確定性。技術上而言，這意味著對於動態規劃的維數災難。為克服這些挑戰，我們提出用魯棒優化的方法處理，用基於中心極限定理的不確定集來建模供應商的價格。類似的思想已經被成功地運用於其它的經典庫存管理問題。我們預期本課題不僅能發掘最優採購策略的結構性質，也能產生可以高效求解的高質量策略。

11503418.label: Realisation of objectives
11503418.value: 1. We have formulated a robust optimization model for the dual-source inventory management problem. The model is motivated and validated by the fast-food restaurant chain we have partnered with. We tested the model with two sets of parameters, and the real-data one is from the fast-food chain. An appealing feature of our approach is that it is data-driven. We have directly produced and chosen constraints like inventory capacity and horizon length from the real data, which are shown to be critical to the final performance. Our back-test on their data shows that our optimization approach can lead to significant cost savings. 2. We have developed two sets of models, a robust optimization one and a distributionally robust one. We have developed the robust counterpart of the robust model and also developed iterative solution approaches to solve the robust optimization model. For the distributionally robust model, we have designed it to validate the idea that originated during the project, which is with respect to how the manager's insight can be converted into a risk constraint and how helpful it could be to the model performance. This model will be further developed and tested for publication shortly. 3. As said above, our robust optimization approach has yielded significant cost savings on the real data; and it performed equally well and robust on the synthetic data on a wide range of parameter settings. For the experiment, in particular, we have designed a data-driven procedure to constraint the uncertainty set, which is an inevitable step in real applications, yet less talked about in the literature, and which has proved to be crucial to the excellent performance of our approach. We benchmarked our approach with the best available methods in the literature, and our approach shows consistently superior performance, often delivering a higher service level at a lower average cost.

11503418.label: Major findings and research outcome
11503418.value: We have developed an actionable data-driven approach to a periodic-review dual sourcing inventory management system in the presence of purchase price and demand uncertainties. The two supply sources differ in their lead times and prices due to, e.g., different transportation modes. We adopt robust optimization because the limited historical data is insufficient to construct meaningful distributions to characterize purchase price and demand fluctuations. Specifically, we build a robust rolling-horizon model and, in particular, construct the uncertainty sets from data and business insights. Major findings: (1) Using a real four-year data set, we show that our approach can yield significant cost savings compared to the other popular methods. (2) Our experiments echo the earlier theoretical finding that a firm may incur a lower cost under a more volatile purchase price process. (3) However, we find that under data-driven decision-making, in comparison with the theoretical results that assume complete distributional information, some interesting results arise. For example, first, considering a longer planning horizon may backfire. Second, some feasible region-reducing business constraints such as limited inventory capacity may lead to unintended benefits. These are consequences of protecting model performance from sampling error and our practically limited forecast ability, as almost always, to characterize uncertainties. Our research, therefore, calls for prudence in extending theoretical insights to data-driven decision-making scenarios. Thus far, one paper out of the project has been published at Transportation Research: Parr E, and a second piece, which, as an extension to the project, covers the distributionally robust idea, is being refined and soon to be submitted for publication. The research was also presented at the POMS-Hong Kong International Conference 2022 recently. The project helped train one PhD student, Xing Xiong, who was under the joint PhD program between City University of Hong Kong and University of China Academy of Science and who is also the first author of the published paper. The student also won the award of Beijing Excellent Graduate because of this research.

11503418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11503418.value: As mentioned above, during the project, an alternative idea to the robust optimization approach arose, namely, a distributionally robust formulation. A distributionally robust approach tends to be more challenging to solve. Nevertheless, it appeals to the manager in terms of interpretability: The idea of service level as a constraint seems intuitive to the manager. In a robust optimization model, service level can be implicitly modeled through the uncertainty set: a feasible solution to the robust optimization model implies that it will reach a certain service level, the exact value of which, however, can only be empirically computed. A distributionally robust approach, in contrast, can incorporate the service level value directly. We will test the alternative approach and publish our findings shortly.

11503418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11503418.value: Purchasing cost often accounts for a significant portion of operating cost for many firms. The purchase price for many raw materials, especially some commodity items, almost always fluctuates over time. Meanwhile, supplies are subject to unexpected interruptions. As a result, managers often prefer to lower the purchasing cost and risk by sourcing from more than one supplier. The real benefit of doing so, however, should be scrutinized. To unlock the true benefit of diversification, managers should bear in mind that the future is uncertain and that the decision should be fact-based. There is indeed some promising benefit of dual sourcing, which, however, can only be reaped through a properly designed data-driven approach. In particular, do not make an excessive bet on a long-term forecast, which can be very wrong and too costly. For example, accumulating a large amount of inventory when anticipating a price spike can be very costly; equally damaging is to delay inventory replenishment when anticipating a price decline. For smooth operations and a good balance of cost efficiency and risk, the manager should restrict the size of the bet and be ready to adjust the bet based on what the data is revealing.

11505018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505018.value: Profitability and investment have recently emerged as two very prominent anomalies. Factors based on profitability and investment are the two vital new factors in newly developed factor models, such as Hou, Xue and Zhang (2015), Fama and French (2015), and Barillas and Shanken (2016). These studies highlight the importance of value, profitability and investment factors in explaining average stock returns. Even though the literature offers motivations and intuitions on why these factors are essential, there is still a lack of a coherent risk-based explanation on how and why these factors drive cross-sectional stock returns. This project intends to investigate whether equity duration can unify these three prominent pricing factors under a risk-based framework. Dechow, Sloan and Soliman (2004) show a duration-based explanation of the value premium: a short duration stock (value) tends to have a higher average return than a long duration stock (growth). Lettau and Wachter (2007, 2011) propose a no-arbitrage model that can generate a downward sloping term structure of equity risk premia, and hence the value premium. Growth stocks tend to have longer horizons of future cash flows than that of value stocks and thus have lower book-to-market ratios by having lower required discount rates. Intuitively, this framework can be extended to include profitability and investment: high profitability may shorten a firm's duration by shifting cash flows relatively close to present, whereas high investment may lengthen a firm's duration by distributing cash flows relatively more in the far future. This project will examine empirically whether equity duration can be the underlying economic force behind the profitability, investment, and other related anomalies. 盈利能力和投資成為兩個非常突出的異常現象。基於盈利能力和投資的因素是新近兩個重要的新因素開發的因子模型，如Hou, Xue and Zhang（2015)，Fama and French（2015)，Barillas和Shanken（2016)。這些研究突出了價值的重要性， 解釋平均股票收益的盈利能力和投資因素。即使文獻提供了關於為什麼這些因素必不可少的動機和直覺對於這些因素的驅動方式和原因，仍然缺乏連貫的基於風險的解釋 橫截面股票收益率。 該項目旨在調查公平持續時間是否可以統一這三者基於風險的框架下的顯著定價因素。 Dechow，Sloan and Soliman (2004）顯示了價值溢價的基於持續時間的解釋：短期股票(價值）往往比長期股票(增長）具有更高的平均回報率。Lettau and Wachter（2007，2011）提出了一種無套利模型，可以生成一個股權風險溢價向下傾斜的期限結構，因此價值溢價。成長型股票的未來現金流往往比價值更長通過降低所需折扣，股票因此具有較低的賬面市值比率率。直觀地說，這個框架可以擴展到包括盈利能力和投資：高盈利率可能會通過改變現金流來縮短公司的持續時間相對接近現在，而高投資可能延長公司的持續時間在遙遠的未來相對更多地分配現金流。該項目將進行審查根據經驗，公平持續時間是否可以成為背後的潛在經濟力量盈利能力，投資和其他相關異常情況。

11505018.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505018.value: Our study provides a risk-based framework to unify the value, profitability, and investment anomalies via the cash flow duration. Our findings show that a short-duration firm tends to have a high book-to-market ratio, high profitability, and low investment. In contrast, a long-duration firm tends to have a low book-to-market ratio, low profitability, and high investment. Thus, a duration-based model can explain the positive relation between profitability and return and the negative relation between investment and return via the duration channel. High profitability or low investment shortens the duration, thus higher returns; low profitability or high investment lengthens the duration, therefore lower returns. With profitability and investment directly determining the horizon distribution of future cash flows, the value premium arises when the term structure of equity returns is downward-sloping. Consequently, a factor model with profitability and investment should explain some duration-related anomalies, and a duration-based factor model should explain the value, profitability, investment factors, and related anomalies. Our analysis shows this is indeed the case. A duration-based model performs reasonably well in explaining the value, profitability, and investment-related anomalies compared to other prominent asset pricing factor models, such as Fama and French (2018), Hou et al. (2015), and Stambaugh and Yuan (2017). These factor models highlight the importance of profitability and investment in explaining the cross-section of equity returns. Instead of directly incorporating the profitability and investment anomalies into a factor model, our duration-based model offers a risk-based economic explanation for the existence of these prominent anomalies. The cash flow duration is a present value-weighted cash flow horizon, depending on a firm’s fundamentals related to profitability and investment. Profitability and investment are the two fundamental drivers determining a firm’s duration. High profitability (investment) decreases (increases) the average horizon of cash flows and hence shortens (lengthens) a firm’s duration. Therefore, a higher (lower) return by the downward sloping term structure of equity risk premiums. The value premium follows directly because value stocks have shorter durations, implying higher expected returns and, thus, lower market values. We find that duration transitions substantially impact the cross-sectional variation of stock returns, and it complements the direct duration-return relation to capturing the cross-sectional effects of duration more completely. A duration-based factor model with both duration and duration transition factors explains most cross-sectional anomalies related to value, profitability, and investment. Thus, these anomalies can arise in a risk-based framework with a downward-sloping term structure of risk premiums.

11505018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505018.value: We offer an economic rationale for the value, profitability, and investment anomalies in a unified risk-based framework. In our duration-based model, profitability and investment affect equity returns by influencing cash flow distribution over time and hence duration. Thus, the profitability, investment, and value premiums arise from the relation that average equity returns decrease with durations. We propose two factors to capture the duration effects on equity returns; one directly measures the return spread between durations; the other measures the return associated with duration transition. Our empirical study shows that duration and duration transition factors present a strong predictive power of future returns and subsumes the value, profitability, and investment effects. Thus, duration, in conjunction with the downward sloping of risk premiums, underpins all these three and other related anomalies. An anomaly may arise when its sorting variable—accounting variables or past returns—picks up the cross-section of duration or duration transition or any combination of both. The complex and dynamic relationship between durations and firms’ fundamentals makes a factor zoo possible in a risk-based pricing model. Our duration measure is by no means perfect. Refinements on VAR (5) may lead to better-estimated equity duration and a more precise term structure of equity returns. Another potential improvement is to construct a better predictive model for the returns associated with duration transitions, leading to a better estimate of duration transition premium. Sharper estimates of these premiums may improve the duration-based factor model’s ability to explain the cross-section of equity returns. We leave these interesting questions for future research.

11505018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505018.value: Two duration factors that arise from the downward-sloping term structure of equity returns explain the value, profitability, and investment premiums. One duration factor captures the spread of returns between short and long durations, and the other measures the difference in risk premiums associated with abnormal duration transitions. The two duration factors, jointly with the market and size, explain many related anomalies comparable to some leading factor models. Our study shows that these three and many other related anomalies can be unified in a risk-based framework. These anomalies may arise from the dynamic relations between firms' durations and their fundamentals.

11505818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505818.value: Website localization has been played an important role in guiding the website design for global e-commerce. This research focuses on web localization strategies that customize a website for a specific country and makes a website seem natural or “local” to their consumers. Drawing on consumer-company identification perspective, we propose two main web localization strategies and their sub-strategies: web similarity strategy (bond-based vs identity-based) and web prosocial strategy (in-role vs extra-role). We hypothesize that web similarity strategy (web pro-social strategy) influences perceived relatedness (perceived support), which, in turn, enhance consumer’s purchase intention. To examine our hypotheses, we plan to recruit our subjects in China and conducted a between-subject laboratory experiment. We expect our findings to have significant theoretical and practical implications. 網站本土化在國際電子商務網站設計中有著重要的作用。這項研究的重點是網站本土化策略。網站本土化策略會針對特定國家定制網站，並使該網站對於本土消費者而言看起來自然或是本土的。基於消費者-公司認同視角，我們提出了兩種主要的網站本土化策略以及它們的子策略：網站相似策略（基於聯結vs基於身份）和網站親社會策略（角色內vs角色外）。我們假設網站相似策略（網站親社會策略）影響感知的關聯性（感知的支持度），轉而影響消費者的購買意向。為了檢驗我們的假設，我們將在中國招募實驗對象並進行被試間的實驗室實驗。我們認為我們的結論有著顯著的理論和實踐意義。

11505918.value: In this research program, I study how the presence of micro-level risks faced by households in developing countries affect their economic decisions, such as choosing where to live and work (i.e. migration decision), choosing what to do for a living (i.e. occupation decision) and choosing how to generate income given an occupation (i.e. technology adoption decision). 11506518.value: Offer a comprehensive examination of the impact of reward disparity on reseller performance by integrating both the benefits and the costs of those upward social comparisons that shape the resellers’ responses to the reward disparity. Enrich the understanding of social comparison within distribution networks by investigating the moderating role of the features of horizontal relationships as well as the vertical relationships within a distribution network. In particular, we examine the contingency effect of 1) the geographic proximity to more highly rewarded peers, 2) the social proximity to more highly rewarded peers, 3) the reward’s legitimacy, and 4) the contract’s customization. 11506518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506518.value: How to attract and retain channel members, and motivate their cooperative behaviors, has been a key question in marketing channel management. Suppliers often reply on varying the level of financial rewards among resellers as a primary tool to motivate them to put in more efforts to attain higher rewards. However, the literature suggests divergent views regarding the effects of promoting a disparity in the levels of reseller rewards. On the one hand, according to agency theory, the use of varying levels of reseller rewards can incite competition for higher levels of payoffs and thus motivate the reseller to exert even more effort and a higher level of productivity. On the other hand, when taking a network perspective, researchers have found that reward variance also fuels social comparisons that confound and complicate incentive outcomes (Larkin et al. 2012). Recently, for example, Vinhas, Heide, and Jap (2012) found that resellers are less satisfied when they perceive an inconsistency in the size of the rewards within a channel system. As such, the incentive benefits of reward disparity can be offset by the costs of social comparisons arising from unequal payoffs. Accordingly, the net effect of reward disparity in incentivizing or inhibiting resellers’ performance remains unclear. To answer this question, we draw from social comparison theory and exchange governance literature to construct a contingency model, explicating how and when the net effect of reward disparity becomes negative or positive. In particular, we examine the moderating roles of (1) physical proximity to peers and (2) social proximity to peers, two important factors in the configuration of the reseller network, and (3) reward legitimacy and (4) contract customization, two factors describing the focal exchange relationship, in the influence of reward disparity on distributor reactions. We predict that reward disparity will be associated with lower levels of reseller performance when the better-rewarded peers are proximate either physically or socially. We also posit that reward disparity will be associated with higher levels of reseller performance when accompanied by legitimate reward rules and/or a higher level of contract customization. Empirically, we plan to match the archival data regarding reseller rewards and performance levels with the reseller survey data in the construction equipment industry to test our hypotheses. The findings will not only contribute to achieving an in-depth understanding of social comparisons within distribution channels, but also will provide an important guideline for firms in their design of more effective reward systems. 如何有效激励经销商，一直是营销渠道管理中的重要问题。厂商经常会使用不同等级的财务奖励来激励经销商努力工作。然而，现有文献对差异化奖励对经销商管理带来的作用意见不一。一方面，基于代理理论，学者们认为差异化的奖励可以激励经销商互相竞争以获取更大收益，这样最终促进经销商更大的投入与产出。另一方面，当采用网络视角时，学者们发现奖励的差异也造成社会比较，从而带来复杂的结果。最近，Sa Vinhas等人（2012）发现经销商感知到的报酬不一致会对其满意度产生负面影响。因此，差异化奖励的激励效果是可以被社会比较带来的负面效应抵销掉的。 分销网络中的差异化奖励到底是会对经销商们产生正激励还是负激励，结论尚未清楚。为了回答这个问题，我们根据社会比较理论和交易治理文献构建了情境模型，分析奖励差异的净效果在什么情况下怎样成为正或者负。我们研究以下几个变量带来的交互作用：1）与同行的地理邻近度；2）与同行的社会邻近度；3）奖励合法性；4）合同定制化。我们推测，在更优奖励同行在地理或社会性上邻近，奖励差异和更差的经销商绩效相关。我们还推测，在奖励合法和合同定制化的情况下，奖励差异和更好的经销商绩效相关。 实证方面，我们计划匹配面板数据和经销商调研数据来验证我们的假设。研究发现将对经销渠道中的社会比较带来更深入的理解，并将为公司设计更有效的奖励系统提供指引。

11506518.label: Realisation of objectives
11506518.value: Regarding the first objective, drawing on social comparison theory, we propose that a dealer’s annual adjustment to its relative engagement in service versus sales is affected by its reward discrepancy: the difference between its annual reward, allocated by the manufacturer based on the dealer’s performance in the past year, and the average reward in the distribution network. We empirically test our hypotheses with an archival dataset from the dealer network of a major automobile manufacturer and a scenario-based experiment. We find a direct relationship between the reward discrepancy and servitization such that the more the dealer’s reward exceeds (falls below) the average, the more the dealer tends to increase (decrease) its engagement in service relative to sales. We also identify the underlying mechanism: the reward discrepancy leads to social comparisons that affect the dealer’s confidence in its capabilities, which affects its subsequent decisions about servitization. Regarding the second objective, we unveil four contingency factors, two each at each step of the causal chain: the absence of a reward and local variation in the reward amount affect the strength of the social comparison effect on confidence, while the dealership group and local economic growth affect the conversion from confidence to engagement in servitization. Again, we used the archival data from the national dealer network of a major automobile manufacturer to test four proposed moderators. We find that characteristics of the reward (local reward dispersion) intensify the effect of social comparisons on the dealer’s confidence in its capabilities, leading to a stronger effect of the reward discrepancy on servitization. We find that the dealership group and local economic growth affect the conversion of confidence into servitization; the effect of the reward discrepancy on servitization is weaker for dealers in groups and stronger in the setting of greater local economic growth. As for the third objective, we concluded valuable insights with which manufacturers can strategically design their dealer reward programs to motivate servitization. We provided practical implications for dealers as well. The above were documented in mainly two papers: “The performance aspiration effect on dealers’ service investment” (with Peng Wang), under the 3rd-round review at International Journal of Research in Marketing. Zeng, Fue, Yunjia Chi, Zhenxin Xiao, and Maggie Chuoyan Dong (2021), “Understanding the Spillover Effects of Channel Reward on Observers’ Commitment: The Mediating Role of Envy,” Industrial Marketing Management, 93, 650-660.

11506518.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506518.value: We find a direct relationship between the reward discrepancy and servitization such that the more the dealer’s reward exceeds (falls below) the average, the more the dealer tends to increase (decrease) its engagement in service relative to sales. We also identify the underlying mechanism: the reward discrepancy leads to social comparisons that affect the dealer’s confidence in its capabilities, which affects its subsequent decisions about servitization. We find that characteristics of the reward (local reward dispersion) intensify the effect of social comparisons on the dealer’s confidence in its capabilities, leading to a stronger effect of the reward discrepancy on servitization. We find that the dealership group and local economic growth affect the conversion of confidence into servitization; the effect of the reward discrepancy on servitization is weaker for dealers in groups and stronger in the setting of greater local economic growth. The findings provide valuable managerial implications. Manufacturers should be aware that the commonly used performance-based reward system may motivate disparate levels of engagement with the servitization process. Such inconsistencies may jeopardize the success of a manufacturer that wants to provide total solutions for customers while maintaining a brand reputation. How can manufacturers unify their dealers’ servitization tracks so as to provide customers with consistent offerings? Our findings suggest several possible tactics. For one, managers can manipulate the “average” that becomes the reference for social comparisons; a manufacturer that wishes to steer more dealers toward servitization could lower the average so that more dealers have a positive reward discrepancy. Our study has practical implications for dealers as well. Constrained by bounded rationality, dealers inevitably will choose myopic strategies to solve urgent problems, as we found among dealers with a negative reward discrepancy. However, it is not wise to “treat the head only when the headaches.” As their capabilities allow, even the dealers with a negative reward discrepancy should devote some attention to long-term service engagement because it is the future of the industry.

11506518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506518.value: 1. It would be worthwhile to explore whether the proposed effects hold in other industries and networks than the automotive industry. 2. Future research can continue the discussion of the role of cultural variation in social comparisons by collecting data in one or more different cultures. 3. We identified confidence in one’s capabilities as a novel mechanism by which the social comparison of channel rewards affects servitization, but other mechanisms might exist as well. Future studies can either collect data from multiple sources or conduct a field experiment to analyze the validity and relative strength of several possible mechanisms.

11506518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506518.value: By examining the effects of performance-based rewards on servitization engagement among dealers in a distribution network, we contribute to and unify the literatures on channel rewards and servitization. We contribute to the channel rewards literature by shifting the focus from relational outcomes (e.g., relationship satisfaction and compliance) to strategic decisions. We argue that social comparisons not only shape relationships but also help with self-assessment, which is important for determining one’s strategy in a competitive environment. We also find a new mechanism, confidence in one’s capabilities, which is distinct from perceived (un)fairness. Fairness is an important consideration when the dealer is evaluating whether the manufacturer treats all dealers consistently, so fairness is a valid mechanism for predicting relational outcomes such as satisfaction and compliance. However, the dealer’s perception of its own capabilities is more relevant than perceived fairness to strategic decisions in a competitive context. The social comparison process provides valuable performance feedback that informs the dealer’s confidence in its capabilities, which informs the dealer’s subsequent strategic decisions.

11506818.label: Realisation of objectives
11506818.value: 1. We find that a quota-linear contract is robust. 2. We find that the firm may be either understock or overstock in the presence of parameter uncertainty. 3. The robustness has adverse impact on firm profit. Specifically, we have the following results. We formulate the problem as a robust principal-agent problem with limited inventory. Facing the model uncertainty, the firm jointly decides the compensation plan and the inventory level to incentivize the salesperson by the worst-case criterion. Notably, the incentive compatibility condition has to hold for any distribution in the uncertainty set. We find that a quota-linear contract that only rewards the salesperson linear commissions for the performance above some threshold is optimal. The optimal commission rate is increasing in the degree of model uncertainty but decreasing in the inventory level. In contrast to the existing literature, we find that the firm has the incentive to understock under the optimal robust contract compared with the first-best inventory level. In particular, under the multiplicative demand model, the firm always understocks while under the general linear demand model, she may first overstock then understock in the demand support range. Finally, we find that the firm has no incentive to screen when the salesperson has asymmetric effort cost information under the optimal robust contract

11506818.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506818.value: We contribute to the extant literature in salesforce compensation with inventory consideration in three different ways. First, our paper characterizes the optimal robust contract in the presence of model uncertainty, i.e., we show that a quota-linear contract with commissions rates decreasing in inventory levels is optimal. Second, as the optimal robust contact is simple and intuitive, it provides guidelines and insights on how to design incentive contracts with inventory consideration. For new seasonal products, quota-linear contracts instead of quota-based contracts are recommended to incentivize salespeople. This is consistent with the empirical findings: according to Joseph and Kalwani (1998), among 266 company surveyed, 35\% of them use the combinations of commissions and bonus to incentivize their salespeople. Third, we obtain new insights on the interplay between the inventory decision and salesforce compensation, which underscores the strategic impacts of model uncertainty on the interplay between the salesforce compensation and inventory considerations. In the presence of model uncertainty, if firms ignore model uncertainty, then it may not only lead to the wrong form of contracts but also overstocking. As a result, the salesforce incentives may fail to incentivize the salespersons. In part due to this fund, I have published two papers at POM, one paper at Operations Research, and two papers at MSOM, and with one paper is currently under review.

11506818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506818.value: Our results provide practitioners guidelines on how to design sales incentives with inventory considerations in the presence of model uncertainty. We find that a simple quota-linear contract is robust. Our results underscore the strategic impacts of model uncertainty on salesforce compensation and inventory decisions.

11506818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506818.value: Consistent with practice, we show a simple quota-linear contract is robust to parameter uncertainty, and the firm may have incentive to overstock or understock under the worst case scenario.

11506918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506918.value: Simulation metamodels have been widely used as computationally inexpensive representations of complex simulation models. While the use of metamodel offers computational advantages, it also causes doubt about the fidelity of the metamodel, i.e., whether the metamodel is a good representation of the simulation model for the intended purpose. Measurement of the performance of a metamodel is therefore a necessary step in simulation metamodeling. The problem is a challenging one because the functional form of the simulation model is typically unknown. In this project, we propose a new measure for simulation metamodel performance that does not require knowing the functional form of the simulation model. The proposed measure serves as an absolute measure of the performance of metamodel that can be used to inform the simulation user about the fidelity of the metamodel. We plan to extend the method to the construction of misspecification tests for metamodels, and two other applications, including input uncertainty quantification and Monte Carlo model calibration. In input uncertainty quantification, we plan to apply the method to estimate the moments of the simulation response as a function of the input modeling data, based on which we may also estimate its quantile and density function by using cumulant-based expansions. In Monte Carlo model calibration, we plan to estimate the error function using the proposed method, minimizing of which leads to an estimate of the calibrated model parameters. This procedure does not require a closed-form formula and is thus generally applicable. We plan to study this procedure in greater detail and compare it to existing calibration methods to better understand its merits and drawbacks. 仿真元模型作爲複雜仿真模型的快速逼近方法，被廣泛運用于複雜仿真模型的分析當中。一方面，元模型具有計算簡便的優點，但另一方面，用戶也會對元模型是不是複雜模型的一個準確逼近存有懷疑。如何確定一個元模型是否一個準確逼近就變成仿真元模型建模的一個關鍵步驟。由於真實仿真模型的函數形式是未知的，這一判定步驟變成一個極具挑戰性的問題。 在此項目中，我們擬提供一種不需要知道真實仿真模型函數形式的判定元模型準確性的新方法，用於提供一種元模型準確性的度量。此外，我們計劃將此方法推廣到統計模型設定檢驗，以及其他兩個應用，包括輸入模型不確定性的度量，和仿真模型的校正。在輸入模型不確定度量方面，我們計劃通過估計仿真輸出的矩來估算它的分位數以及密度函數。在仿真模型校正中，我們計劃通過最小化校正誤差函數來獲得模型參數。在這些應用中，我們並不需要知道複雜仿真模型的函數形式，因而能廣泛應用于實際問題當中。

11506918.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506918.value: We successfully achieved all the project objectives. The outcomes of the research are summarized as follows. We have studied the assessment of metamodels for stochastic simulation. In particular, we conduct an orthogonal decomposition on the residual errors that account for the intrinsic simulation noise inherent to stochastic simulation, based on which we develop an unbiased estimator of the mean squared discrepancy (MSD), a measure of the squared distance between a metamodel and the true functional relationship between the input variables and the simulation output. We further prove central limit theorem for the MSD and develop hypothesis tests. The proposed method can also be applied to model calibration using Monte Carlo simulation. The above results are presented in a paper titled "Assessing metamodels for stochastic simulation: Measurement and hypothesis tests". This paper went through a review by Management Science but got rejected unfortunately. However, the review team did see potential value of the proposed approach with a major comment on how to adapt it to contexts with relatively small sample sizes. We are currently working on a revision and will submit it to another top-tier journal soon. We have also studied the use of assessment methods in quantification of input model uncertainty via the technique of bootstrapping. In particular, we propose algorithms to construct asymptotically valid confidence intervals based on bootstrapping. We show a central limit theorem for the input uncertainty estimator, and estimate the asymptotic variance using non-nested estimators. These results are presented in a paper titled "Input uncertainty quantification via simulation bootstrapping". We are currently polishing this paper, and will submit it soon to INFORMS Journal on Computing.

11506918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506918.value: Currently, the proposed metamodel assessment method focuses on the mean performance of simulation models. It may also be extended to the situation where quantile performance is of interest. We have started an investigation of metamodel assessment under the framework of quantile regression, and preliminary results indicate that it may be a promising future research topic.

11506918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506918.value: Simulation metamodels have been widely used to study the performance of complex stochastic systems, and these metamodels are usually estimated or calibrated using real data. However, due to complexity of the system being studied, how to assess these simulation metamodels has been a challenging problem. In this project, we propose to use mean squared discrepancy (MSD) as a measure of metamodel qualify, and develop efficient methods for estimating MSD. Furthermore, we have analyzed the asymptotic properties of MSD, and proposed hypothesis tests that are helpful in deciding whether a given metamodel is acceptable or not. The proposed method may serve as a viable tool for metamodel assessment in practical applications.

11507218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507218.value: The researches on online reviews are extant in the recent years, while the reviews for services receive little attention. Given the fast development of service economy, especially the development of shared economy where mostly services, including driving services (Uber and DiDi) and medical services (Haodf.com, Chunyu Doctor) or housing services (Airbnb) are transacted, it becomes crucial to evaluate whether our understanding of online review on commodities (such as reviews provided on Amazon.com or Taobao.com) can be applied to service products. Service products have certain unique features that distinguish them from commodity products: (1) the outcome of the service depends on not only the service provider, but also the customer who receives the service. For example, whether or not a disease could be cured depends not only on the doctor’s effort, but also the complexity of the disease and the patient’s own health conditions; (2) service providers, in many scenarios, are able to decide which customers to serve. Such features make it difficult to interpret the service provider’s quality from the review outcome, and inappropriate to interpret the reviews for service the same way as the review for commodity products. This project first proposes a theoretical framework to understand how the reviews for service products are different from those for commodity products. We examine whether, and under what conditions, online reviews for service products can truly reflect the quality of the service provider. We find that reviews for service help differentiate service providers with different quality levels to a certain degree, but not always. Moreover, if the service provider is allowed to select customers to pursue a better review outcome, there exists a deadweight loss in the social welfare where customers who are less likely to produce desirable review outcomes will not be served. We examine the effectiveness of two policies in reducing the deadweight loss. We are also in the process of collecting data from both an online medical service provider and two large offline hospitals to examine whether online reviews help reducing the uncertainties for doctor’s quality, and whether online reviews provide consistent evaluation for the doctors’s offline profile. 鉴于服务经济的快速发展，特别是共享经济的发展，大部分服务被交易，包括驾驶服务（优步和嘀嘀），医疗服务（Haodf.com，春雨医生）或住房服务（Airbnb）。而对于服务的在线评论从前甚少得到关注。我们以往对于商品的在线评论（例如在Amazon.com或Taobao.com上提供的评论）的理解是否可以直接用于对于服务的在线评论呢？ 和普通商品品相比，服务产品具有以下独特性质：（1）服务的结果不仅取决于服务提供商，还取决于接受服务的客户。例如，疾病是否可以治愈，不仅取决于医生的努力，还取决于疾病的复杂性和患者自身的健康状况; （2）在许多情况下，服务提供商能够决定服务哪些客户，拒绝哪些客户。这些特征使得难以从在线评论结果来推断服务提供商的服务质量。 本课题首先提出了一个理论框架，以了解对于服务的评论如何不同于对商品的评论，以及对于服务的在线评论是否以及在何种条件下能真正反映服务提供商的质量。我们还在收集在线医疗服务提供商和两家大型医院的数据，以了解对医生的在线评论是否有助于减少患者对于医生质量的不确定性，以及在线评论是否为医生的真实服务质量提供客观的评估。

11507218.label: Realisation of objectives
11507218.value: The serving of credence goods, such as medical services, auto or house repair, legal services, requires specialized professional knowledge and exhibits significant information asymmetry (Wolinsky 1993,1995, Ely and Valimaki 2003, Dulleck and Kerschbamer 2006, Jiang et al, 2014, Gottschalk 2018). A credence good has “a characteristic that although consumers can observe the utility they derive from the good ex post, they cannot judge whether the type or quality of the good they have received is the needed one. Moreover, consumers may even ex post be unable to observe which type or quality they actually received” (Dulleck et al., 2011, Bafaloutas et al. 2013). Customers experience difficulties in ascertaining such service providers and face considerable risks (Gao et al., 2011). As such, online reviews for credence goods or professional services (e.g., RateMds.com, LegalZoom.com, etc.) become an important information source. Deloitte’s (2011) indicated that 47% of internet users had searched for information about their healthcare providers, and 37% had visited physician rating websites. In addition, many physicians closely monitor their reviews and ratings and try to improve them on review sites such as Yelp, Vitals, and RateMDs (Saifee et al. 2020). Although previous literature has extensively studied online reviews for traditional products such as books or digital games (Chevalier and Mayzlin 2006, Chen et al. 2008, Kuksov et al. 2010, Li et al. 2011), the impact of online reviews on credence goods, however, is uncertain. For example, in the U.S., the American Medical Association (AMA) and some state governments have expressed concerns that online ratings merely reflect disgruntled patients’ opinions and are not representative of the broader population (Gao et al. 2015). Compared to the scenario of purchasing a traditional product (for example, a computer)—in which a transaction can occur as long as a customer is willing to buy—purchasing of a credence good usually requires both the service provider and customer mutually agreeing before the transaction can happen. In addition, credence goods have the following unique features: (1) Customers usually do not have the expertise or specialized knowledge to judge the service provider’s service quality, even after they experience the service (Dulleck et al. 2011, Bafaloutas et al. 2013, Gao et al. 2011, 2015; Saifee et al. 2020). For example, due to the lack of required professional knowledge, a patient may not know whether it is necessary to get a root canal plus a crown or just a crown (Dulleck and Kerschbamer, 2006). An automobile mechanic knows whether the car needs an engine replacement or a simple tune-up, while most likely the car owner does not know (Ely and Valimaki 2003). As a result, customers’ evaluations are most likely based on the service outcomes; for example, whether and how quickly a patient recovers. (2) The service outcome is contingent not only on the provider’s service quality, but also on the customer who receives the service (Sun and Xu 2016). For example, whether a patient recovers depends not only on the physician’s effort, but also on the patient’s own health condition and whether the patient follows the physician’s instructions (Dranove et al. 2003). Given these unique features, how should we understand online reviews for credence goods? Feature (1) implies that the credence goods market exhibits greater uncertainty than traditional commodity markets. So, the existence of online review, which provides information about previous consumers’ experiences, would be extremely useful for latter users; Feature (1) and (2) together, however, also implies that such online reviews, offered by consumers who may not be specialized enough, may not truthfully reveal the quality level of a service provider. So, are reviews for credence goods useful in differentiating service providers? If not, under what conditions are they useless or even harmful? Should we allow service providers to reject certain customers? We propose a theoretical framework to study the impact of reviews for credence goods. We identify three important factors that determine the impact of online reviews for professional services: (1) the gap between jobs’ difficulty levels, (2) the proportion of difficult job requests, and (3) the proportion of informed customers. We find that while online reviews for professional services can help differentiate service providers (SPs) under certain conditions, they fail to do so when the gap between the job difficulty levels is significantly different or when the proportion of easy jobs is in the medium range. As a result, the market can become more undifferentiated in the presence of online reviews. To help resolve this problem, the platform can employ different policies: not allowing SPs to refuse customers; or allowing SPs to set their own prices. We examine the effect of such policies accordingly. In order to empirically examine the impact of online review for credence good, we have also collected dataset from an online service provider platform, Haodf.com, which serves a platform for patients to seek professional services from doctors. Patients also left review comments for the doctors. We examined the impact of online review for doctors on their service volume and identify different impacts on online review for doctors with high credentials in comparison to those with less credentials. It shows complementary evidences to our theoretical results. Overall, all the objectives have been achieved.

11507218.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507218.value: We identify three important factors that determine the impact of online reviews for professional services: (1) the gap between jobs’ difficulty levels, (2) the proportion of difficult job requests, and (3) the proportion of informed customers. We find that while online reviews for professional services can help differentiate service providers (SPs) under certain conditions, they fail to do so when the gap between the job difficulty levels is significantly different or when the proportion of easy jobs is in the medium range. Moreover, SPs may have incentive to reject customers who are less likely to produce desirable review outcomes even when online reviews are helpful. In an industry that requires less specialized knowledge such that the proportion of informed customers is large, it is the low-quality SP rather than the high-quality SP that is more likely to reject customers with difficult job requests. As a result, the market can become more undifferentiated in the presence of online reviews. To help resolve this problem, the platform can employ different policies: not allowing SPs to refuse customers; or allowing SPs to set their own prices. We examine the effect of such policies and find that: first, not allowing SPs to refuse customers helps the market to be more differentiated to some extent, but not completely; second, allowing the SPs to set prices offers one additional lever to eliminating SPs’ service refusal behaviors but not completely. We put part of the research project into one research paper: “Reviews for Credence Goods: A Blessing or Curse?”. This paper is now under review at Information Systems Research, one top journal in the area of Information Systems.

11507218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507218.value: One promising potential is to collaborate with practitioners, say, medical centers or hospitals, whose service is one perfect example of credence good, and consumer review crucially influences the potential consumers’ choices. Meanwhile, the service providers’ incentives to provide a high-quality service is also vital to the society. It will be valuable to perform experiment or collect first-hand data to analyze the relationship between reviews from patients and the service outcome from the doctors.

11507218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507218.value: Recent developments in IT have enabled user-generated contents not only for traditional goods, but also for credence goods, such as professional services provided by physicians, lawyers or auto mechanics. The impact of online reviews on credence goods, however, is uncertain: although the service outcome can be observed, consumers --- they are also the review generators --- usually lack the required specialized knowledge to evaluate the service quality. In addition, as the service outcome is jointly determined by both the service provider and the service receivers, it is even harder for UGC to truly reflect the quality levels of service providers. This paper proposes a theoretical model to understand the impact of online reviews for credence goods. We identify three important factors that critically determine whether online reviews for credence goods help customers differentiate service providers (SPs) with different quality levels: the proportion of informed consumers in the market (which can be understood as how specialized the professional service is, or how much specialized knowledge is required to evaluate the professional service), the proportion of difficult job requests, and the quality gap between the two SPs. We find that the presence of online reviews may hurt consumers if SPs refuse to serve customers with difficult jobs. We then examine different policies: not allowing SPs to refuse customers, or allowing SPs to set their own prices. We find that although these policies cannot completely solve the problems, they help reduce the number of unserved customers and differentiate the market to some extent.

11600018.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600018.value: 耶穌受難記與戲劇性的想像

11600018.label: Project Objectives
11600018.value: To posit an early Christian “melodramatic imagination” that transforms our understanding of early modern representation. To write a new history of melodrama exploring the complex weave of sacred and secular features and how these are codified into a mass art in modern melodrama. To argue for a continuity rather than a break between premodern and modern, based on religion’s presence in secular modernity. To explain the cultural and religious resonances of modern melodrama through the Christianity of Pathos. To understand how the gendered history of “affective piety” illuminates the history and role of gender within modern melodrama. To develop a database of known passion-themed performances (sung or spoken), from the 14th through the 20th centuries, to support the project.

11600018.label: Realisation of objectives
11600018.value: The PI and Co-I were unable to complete their planned trip to the Oberammergau passion play, which was cancelled due to Covid. The Co-I was able to visit Rome in October 2019 to use the Biblioteca Hertziana -- the Max Planck Institute for Art History, in Rome, where she consulted a total of 90 publications unavailable in Hong Kong. However, she was unable to repeat the trip as intended. The PI was unable to undertake any of his planned trips due to the combined impact of his dean’s responsibilities during the social unrest in Hong Kong and subsequent Covid 19 travel restrictions. The PI, especially, had to revise his research outputs as a result and the coverage of research objectives is inevitably less comprehensive than it otherwise would have been. The PI and Co-I have, nevertheless, delivered two concrete research outputs from this GRF. PI, Richard Allen, authored: “Under Capricorn: Hitchcock, Melodrama and the Christian Imagination,” in Sidney Gottlieb ed. Hitchcock Annual 23 (New York: Columbia University Press, 2019). Co-I, Isabelle Frank, is publishing: "Lamentations over the Dead Christ: Emotional Expression, Affective Piety, and the Flagellants," in Ethan Matt Kavaler, ed. Objects of Devotion: Religion and its Instruments (Early Modern Cultural Studies series, Turnhout, Belgium: Brepols Press, forthcoming 2023). Both papers were also delivered at international academic conferences. Objective 1: Posit a melodramatic imagination in the early modern period. Frank’s article demonstrates how full-size Italian Lamentation sculptures and Passion plays from the fourteenth through the sixteenth centuries created a mise-en-scène of corporeal identification with the suffering, mortal body of Christ, manifesting a repertoire of intense emotional gestures by the mostly female mourners. These scenes induced the faithful themselves to be emotionally moved towards spiritual identification with Christ’s suffering and, in the case of the flagellants, they served as a prompt to physically reproduce the conditions of Christ’s suffering. This genre of highly emotional, religious Passion scenes was thus a melodramatic enactment that elicited pathos by soliciting audience identification with the suffering of innocence. To fill out this picture more studies still need to be undertaken that will be focused on the drama and music of the period. Objective 2: Write a new history of melodrama The two published articles for the GRF make significant strides towards this new history. Frank’s GRF contribution fills out in detail the nature of early modern Christian affective piety as a form of melodramatic imagination through analysing the rhetorical form and impact of lamentation sculptures and passion plays. Allen’s essay on Hitchcock, which combines an analysis of literature and film, shows how modern melodrama at once absorbs the Christian imagination of pathos and transforms it within a secular frame. Beyond the remit of the GRF substantial work still needs to be done to fill in the missing parts of this history by analysing early modern music and theatre, the development of opera, and nineteenth century theatre. Objective 3: Propose continuity rather than a break between pre-modern and the modern While following Peter Brooks’ influential argument in The Melodramatic Imagination, that modern secular melodrama emerged from the collapse of what he calls the traditional sacred, the overall argument of Frank’s essay shows how the Christianity of pathos, in the early modern period, generates a new genre of Lamentation Sculptures and Passion plays that, in their rhetoric of pathos and solicitation of the audience’s identification, possess all the lineaments of melodrama. Allen’s essay, in turn, demonstrates how the Christianity of Pathos, derived from the medieval period, informs the very vocabulary of melodrama, even as the religious belief supported by affective piety recedes in the secular world. Objective 4: Explain modern melodrama through the Christianity of Pathos Allen’s published article explains modern melodrama through the Christianity of Pathos in four primary ways. First, the figure of the penitent Magdalene, as the locus of pathos and empathic identification, provides a model for the “fallen woman” heroine of the film. Second, evil is personified through a female character who is directly modelled on the figure of Eve. Third, the redeemed hero is modelled on the figure of Christ. Fourth, the story reconfigures the myth of original sin and the fall as the preservation of female honour in a caste society. This film demonstrates one important general strategy through which pre-modern religious values are preserved in secular modernity. The analysis is incomplete in the sense that more case studies need to be undertaken and this research could not be completed due to COVID 19). This will be a focus of future work. Objective 5: The gendered nature of affective piety and its impact on modern melodrama Frank’s GRF essay analyses how both the written descriptions and visual depictions of the Lamentation focus on female mourning, which includes cries, tears, wringing of hands, but also fainting, tearing of clothes and hair, and scratching of face. Although condemned at secular burials as unseemly behaviour, within the theology of "affective piety", such female comportment was valorised as evidence of emotional identification with the agonies of Christ and the Virgin and led the faithful to contrition and salvation through empathic identification. Medieval theologians adopted the Virgin's persona to express their grief at Christ's sufferings, and the tearful cries voiced in the chants of the mourning Virgin and the agonised, weeping figures served to incite spiritual paroxysms of grief in the members of flagellant confraternities. Allen’s article demonstrates how this gendered, affective piety deeply informs secular melodrama. He shows how in Hitchcock’s Under Capricorn, the figure of Mary Magdalene, the patron saint of penitent sinners, models the central female protagonist as a “fallen woman,” who is the center of pathos and of the spectator’s empathic identification. At the same time, Hitchcock’s film, in accordance with the strategies of secular melodrama, modernises this female archetype by bestowing agency upon the heroine who, unlike the Magdalene, refuses the place society assigns to her. At the same time, the central evil character, Mille, is modelled upon Eve, the temptress with various Biblical allusions. Objective 6: To develop a detailed data base of known passion-themed performances In research for her GRF essay, the Co-I has made the first detailed inventory of Compianti sculptural groups and of known Passion plays, and the Compianti inventory will be published in a second article which will also recognise the support of the GRF. The Co-I was also able to assemble an initial corpus of over twenty five manuscripts and published texts, dating from the 13th to the early seventeenth century, which were written in the format of a play (i.e. with characters speaking their parts, references to scenery or stage directions, different scenes and events). However, Passion plays survived in more remote areas. Frank will thus need more time to gather those in other languages and written in a later period. The research on the Passion plays could not be completed because of COVID 19 travel restrictions. Furthermore, the earliest of these plays in Latin are unavailable in Hong Kong. A difficulty also arose in discerning actual performances from surviving texts, perhaps intended only for reading, and this will require more research.
