12200518.label: Realisation of objectives
12200518.value: The three listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily. Details are discussed as follows. The references [J#] and [C#] refer to the journal and conference paper numbers in Sections 9 and 10 of Part C, respectively. Objective 1: We have developed two source-data-free unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) frameworks from latent feature induction and model inversion perspectives. Framework 1: We have proposed a novel source-data-free feature alignment method (SoFA) [C3], which integrates latent feature learning and cross-dataset feature alignment in an auto-encoding framework. A mixture of Gaussian distributions is induced from the predicted classes as the reference distribution to overcome the lack of source data. Target features are then aligned to the reference distribution for domain adaptation. As the generation process can be embedded in the Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE), we have developed a Latent Alignment Variational Auto-Encoder (LA-VAE), of which the inference and generative processes correspond to the encoding and decoding processes of VAE, respectively. LA-VAE performs cross-domain latent feature alignment in addition to matching target data and label predictions. Experiments are conducted on three cross-dataset classification tasks, achieving encouraging results without accessing the source data. Results of ablation studies further confirm and validate the effectiveness of the proposed soft-data-free feature alignment method. These research findings have been published and presented in the IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision. In addition, we have further investigated the theoretical evidence to learn the cross-domain representations in source-data-free UDA [J1]. A new generalization upper bound on the target-domain prediction error is deduced based on the rigorous domain adaptation model. This new upper bound is represented by a trained source model rather than source data; thus, it is suitable for source-data-free UDA. We further derive an optimization function that minimizes the new generalization upper bound by introducing the information bottleneck theory, which is also a general solution to obtain domain adaptation without accessing the source data. Our study has shown that the LA-VAE is one solution to realize the general optimization function. Quantitive and visualization experiments have been performed on multiple recognition tasks, whose results show the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical model on cross-dataset classification. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. Framework 2: Another framework to achieve source-data-free UDA [J2] is developed based on the model inversion technique that reveals source domain information from a well-trained source model. A Source-Protected Generative Model (SPGM) is developed to distill the inverse process of the source model and generate pseudo data accordingly. We innovatively design a privacy-protected transfer (PPT) metric to supervise the learning of SPGM. The PPT metric measures the transferability and desensitization of the generated data to encourage the SPGM to extract task-relevant information rather than unintended memorization. Hence, the generated pseudo data is desensitized and can be used as substitutes for the real source data in UDA. It is encouraging to see that SPGM is also workable for the black-box source model, which better protects source-domain privacy. The performance of the proposed method has been validated in four cross-dataset recognition applications with encouraging results. This work has been accepted by IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (TIFS) and is currently in press. Objective 2: We have proposed an unsupervised embedding learning [C1]. In this work, we aim at learning discriminative feature representations without using category-wise labels. In the learned low-dimensional embedding space, the visually similar samples are pulled close to each other and dissimilar samples are pushed away. Without any label information, this task faces two primary difficulties: mining reliable and discriminative positive supervision from highly similar fine-grained categories, and generalizing to unseen testing categories, which share similar distribution but different categories to the unlabeled training images. Motivated by the category-wise supervised learning, we introduce a data augmentation invariant and instance spreading feature using the instance-wise supervision to approximate the positive concentration and negative separation properties. The basic idea is that the embedding features of the same instance under different data augmentation operations should be invariant, and the embedding features of different instances should be separated from each other. To achieve this goal, we have proposed a novel instance-wise softmax embedding, which directly performs the network optimization over the augmented instance features with a binary discrmination softmax encoding. A small batch of randomly selected m instances are selected at each training step. By randomly performing the data augmentation to get their positive instances, a Siamese network training strategy is designed to improve the efficiency. These research findings have been presented and published in the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2019. Please refer to Section 8 for details. Objective 3: To achieve objective 3, we have developed a new cross-domain feature alignment algorithm, namely unsupervised graph alignment (UGA) [C2], based on the abovementioned feature embedding learning method. This algorithm aims to solve the cross-domain distribution mismatch problem in UDA by exploring cross-domain invariant representations. We argue that the domain-invariant features learned without consideration of the differences in distribution structures across domains would lead to insufficient representation alignment. To fully disclose the distribution information, data in the source/target domain are linked to building a complete graph with intra-class and inter-class edges to reflect the structural information of data distribution. An adversarial network is then proposed to map both source and target data to a feature space where the data are distributed with a unified structure. We have designed unified criteria for edges in both source and target domains so that the source and target distributions can be aligned without target labels. We have conducted extensive experiments on cross-dataset recognition and cross-modal re-identification to validate the effectiveness of the graph-aligned visual representations. This work has been published and presented in the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 2019.

12200518.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200518.value: In this project, we addressed the issues of unsupervised domain adaptation without source data from several aspects. The major findings and research outcomes are listed as follows. 1. We proposed two approaches, source-data-free feature alignment (SoFA) and pseudo data generation, to obtain UDA with a well-trained source classifier and unlabelled target data under the cases with white-box and black-box source models, respectively. These two approaches address the lacking of source data by estimating source-domain information from two different perspectives. SoFA induces source latent features based on predictive classes, while pseudo data generation reveals source-model memorization. We further summarize source-data-free UDA methods in a theoretical model and derive a general solution accordingly. It is shown that the induced features and generated data are task-discriminative and desensitized, which can protect source-domain privacy and are effective substitutes for source data in UDA. 2. We have also developed an unsupervised feature embedding learning for discriminative low-dimension feature representation. Along this line, we have developed a novel instance-wise softmax embedding. The proposed algorithm not only can be used in the source-data-free unsupervised domain adapation, but also other applications such as person re-identifications. 3. To extract useful information for UDA, we studied the data distribution property in source and target domains. We have observed the structural differences in data distribution across domains and have shown that such differences would damage the cross-domain performance of the source model. An unsupervised graph alignment method is proposed. This method builds a graph with intra-class and inter-class edges to model the distribution structure. The distribution graphs in the source and target domains are then aligned to obtain domain-invariant features that are sufficiently aligned. As labels are unavailable in the target domain, unified criteria for edges are designed as references to facilitate the source and target domain distribution alignment. All the above-proposed algorithms and mathematical models are extensively validated in challenging datasets, showing the effectiveness of the proposed models.

12200518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200518.value: This project has investigated and developed frameworks and algorithms for unsupervised domain adaptation without touching on the source data. This would address the data privacy policy issue, such as general data protection policy (GDPR). These research findings provide good foundation to develop data privacy-preserved applications. To further converting these findings to enabling technology for practical applications, it is necessary to develop some libraries and application prototype. To achieve this, we will try to approach industry and see if they are interested in our research. If so, we would have joint force for applying applied-research funding (e.g. innovation technology fund) for the development.

12200518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200518.value: This project addresses personal data privacy issue when computer makes use of personal data, e.g. facial images, for developing machine learning applications. Because of the new data privacy law, e.g. GDPR, people have the right for forgotten. That means, all individual data have to be deleted and cannot be used for machine learning, if the owner wants to do so. However, data is required for learning a model. To overcome the problem, we have developed frameworks and methods to perform model learning without touching on the original raw personal data. As such, personal data information will not be disclosed. The beauty of this research is that we do not need original data for model learning, and still achieve very similar outcomes. This research findings would increase the public acceptance of using machine learning methods and applications.

12201018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201018.value: 現今的數據流平台，如Twitter、Facebook和比特幣，不斷產生海量的數據。例如，每天超過5億條推文在Twitter上發布，每天新產生的比特幣交易超過20萬筆。為這些平台構建發布/訂閱系統，允許訂閱用戶過濾相關的信息有大量的實際應用，如Twitter用戶可能只想關注某特定事件的推文；比特幣用戶可能想跟踪特定用戶發出的交易。為支持這些數以百萬計的訂閱查詢，將發布/訂閱查詢處理外包給第三方被認為是具擴展性的理想解決方案。但是，外包查詢處理會引起信任問題，使得訂閱用戶必須對收到的查詢結果進行驗證。目前針對外包數據流的查詢驗證研究非常有限，需要克服不少挑戰。首先，數據流的數據是無限的，這使得先前依靠在固定數據集上構建驗證數據結構（ADS）的技術無法應用。我們需要設計新的支持在線增量聚合的ADS。第二，除了正確性之外，訂閱用戶必須能夠驗查詢結果在時間上的完整性，即沒有錯過整個訂閱期間的任何結果。第三，查詢驗證必須是輕量級的，以支持實時流媒體服務。第四，系統應該具備擴展性，可以處理大量同時訂閱的查詢。在本項目中，我們將針對外包數據流的發布/訂閱查詢驗證進行全面的研究。我們將利用區塊鏈的概念設計新穎的數據結構、安全原語和查詢驗證技術。項目的詳細研究計劃如下：1）優化用於支持數據流上可驗證發布/訂閱查詢的區塊鏈結構; 2）開發基於累加器的ADS和查詢驗證算法; 3）研究高效的查詢索引技術; 4）擴展所提出技術至top-k查詢和時間窗查詢;5）對提出的技術方案進行安全性分析和性能評估測試。

12201018.label: Realisation of objectives
12201018.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have investigated the problem of verifiable query processing over outsourced blockchain databases, where data are generated in a streaming fashion. We have proposed a novel framework, called vChain, that alleviates the storage and computing costs of the querying user. To support verifiable Boolean range queries, we proposed an accumulator-based authenticated data structure that enables dynamic aggregation over arbitrary query attributes, including both numerical attributes and set-valued attributes. Two new authenticated indexes were further developed to aggregate intra-block and inter-block data records for efficient query verification. Furthermore, we proposed an inverted prefix tree structure to accelerate the processing of a large number of subscription queries simultaneously. Security analysis and empirical study validate the robustness and practicality of the proposed techniques. While vChain for the first time supports verifiable Boolean range queries in outsourced blockchain databases, it still suffers from several limitations, including linear-scan search performance in the worst case and impractical public key management. To address these issues, we have proposed an optimized scheme, namely vChain+, that supports efficient verifiable Boolean range queries with additional features. Specifically, we proposed a sliding-window accumulator index to achieve efficient query processing even in the worst case. We also designed an object registration index to enable practical public key management without compromising the security guarantee. To support richer queries, we developed tree-based indexes to index both keywords and numerical attributes of the data objects. Several optimizations have also been proposed to further improve the query performance. Compared with vChain, vChain+ improves the query performance by up to 913X. Both vChain and vChain+ support verifiable queries by embedding additional authenticated information into the block structure, which needs to modify the underlying blockchains. To solve this problem, we have designed a decentralized certification framework, called DCert, which is compatible with existing blockchains and achieves constant-cost blockchain integrity validation. The main idea is to leverage a trusted enclave (e.g., Intel SGX) to recursively certify the entire history of the blockchain. With DCert, the blockchain integrity can be easily validated with a secure certificate by the following checks: (i) the integrity of the metadata in the current block header, (ii) the integrity of state transitions from the previous block to the current block, and (iii) the integrity of the previous block’s certificate. Moreover, some novel designs were proposed for certificate construction to mitigate the performance overhead brought by the trusted hardware. Our benchmark-based empirical study shows that DCert incurs a small certification overhead, yet it is capable of supporting efficient verifiable queries with a constant storage size of 2.97 KB and a constant bootstrapping time of 0.14 ms. In addition, we have extended the research to a hybrid blockchain storage model, where only small meta-data is stored on-chain and the raw data are outsourced to off-chain storage. We have designed gas-efficient authenticated data structures to authenticate the query results. We have also studied two types of top-k term subscription queries over streams of spatiotemporal documents: region-based top-k spatial-temporal term (RST) subscriptions and similarity-based top-k spatiotemporal term (SST) subscriptions. To address the problem, we proposed solutions that are capable of supporting real-life location-based publish/subscribe applications that process large numbers of SST and RST subscriptions over a realistic stream of spatiotemporal documents.

12201018.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201018.value: We have investigated a set of related problems on verifiable query processing over outsourced streaming data, in particular in the context of blockchain databases. We have designed novel security primitives and query authentication algorithms for the verification of Boolean range queries. We have proposed space partition-based query indexing techniques for the handling of large-scale subscription queries. To be compatible with existing blockchains, we have developed a new decentralized certification framework capable of supporting rich queries on an as-needed basis while achieving constant-cost blockchain integrity validation. We have also proposed gas-efficient authenticated query algorithms for on-chain/off-chain hybrid blockchains, as well as top-k term subscription queries over spatiotemporal data streams. The research findings have been published in top-tier conferences and journals including SIGMOD 2019, ICDE 2019, SIGMOD 2020, ICDE 2021, ICDE 2022, Middleware 2022, and VLDBJ.

12201018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201018.value: The current works are limited to specific query types such as range queries and keyword searches. A possible future direction is to consider general SQL queries. As SQL queries could be very complicated, involving join and nested operations, it is not easy to verify all operations in a SQL query. As such, instead of verifying SQL operations, an idea is to verify data, making sure the data supplied to the query engine is authenticated so that the correctness of query results can be guaranteed. Moreover, learned index has recently gained a lot of research attention. The basic idea of a learned index is to replace the search keys in each index node with a learned model to reduce storage overhead and improve query efficiency. However, we cannot apply the existing learned indexes directly to blockchain data, because they do not support data authentication and provenance as required in blockchain systems. Also, the index in blockchain systems needs to be persistent in each data block; it would be interesting to explore novel storage designs to support efficient updates of the learned model.

12201018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201018.value: Today’s data streaming platforms, such as Twitter and Bitcoin, continuously generate a massive amount of data at an unprecedented scale. Building query systems for these platforms that allow users to filter relevant data objects has many real-world applications. For example, Bitcoin users may want to find the transactions issued by specific parties. To support millions of queries, outsourcing query processing to a third party has been deemed a desirable solution to scaling up systems. However, the outsourcing of query processing naturally raises the issue of trust, making it indispensable for users to verify the results returned by the server. In this project, we have studied a set of related problems on verifiable query processing over outsourced streaming data, in particular in the context of blockchain databases. We have designed novel security primitives and index-based authentication algorithms to ensure the integrity of query results. We have developed a decentralized certification framework capable of supporting rich queries on an as-needed basis while achieving constant-cost blockchain integrity validation. We have also conducted security analysis and performance evaluation of the proposed solutions in real-world settings.

12201318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201318.value: This project will aim to develop and empirically validate a novel computational framework for active surveillance in the control and prevention of infectious diseases. The large ranges of infectious disease diffusion make comprehensive surveillance challenging or even impossible due to limited surveillance resources during outbreaks. Existing disease surveillance relies on case reporting from existing health agencies; however, this approach is somewhat passive, and can lead to unsatisfactory results because of error-prone observations. Active surveillance is a crucial strategy for addressing the shortcomings of passive surveillance when resources are limited. It proactively determines key locations for surveillance by identifying and utilizing the latent diffusion network inferred from clinically confirmed historical data. Computationally speaking, the problem of inferring the latent diffusion network from historical data for key location selection is very challenging as during the disease diffusion process, the interrelationships between two locations are hidden; what we have in the historical data is only the number of confirmed infected cases at all locations in the past. Moreover, given the limited resources, the goal of diffusion network inference is not merely characterizing the structure of the entire network but identifying key locations from which current/future infected cases at all locations (including unobserved ones) can be predicted. This project will develop a group sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL) framework to address the above problems, i.e., selecting key locations from the inferred latent diffusion network for active surveillance. Under the GSBL framework, we will tackle the following computational challenges: 1) How to model the spatially sparse distribution of infectious disease cases; 2) How to infer latent diffusion networks in a timely fashion; 3) How to characterize the complicated diffusion patterns of infectious diseases. To address those challenges, we will correspondingly propose three novel methods: 1) GSBL with Bernoulli likelihood (GSBL-B); 2) Scalable GSBL (GSBL-S); 3) Nonlinear model embedding for GSBL (GSBL-N). We will carry out both experimental evaluation and onsite validations on multiple scales. Specifically, we will consider two representative real-world disease diffusion scenarios: the influenza outbreak in Hong Kong and the malaria elimination initiative in China. The outcomes of this project will contribute to academic research in computer science and epidemiology, and to the control and prevention of infectious diseases in practice. Results derived from this project will provide a scientific foundation for public health authorities in the development of policies dealing with infectious diseases. 本項目將提出並驗證一種新的主動監測計算框架，用於傳染病的控制和預防。 由於暴發期間監測資源有限，大範圍的傳染病傳播使得全面監測具有挑戰性。現有的疾病監測依賴於現有衛生機構的病例報告;然而這種方法有些被動，並且由於觀察結果容易出錯而導致疾病監測結果不令人滿意。 當資源有限時，主動監視是解決被動監視缺陷的關鍵策略。它通過識別和利用從臨床確認的歷史數據推斷的潛在擴散網絡，主動確定監測的關鍵位置。從計算上講，從關鍵位置選擇的歷史數據推斷潛在擴散網絡的問題是非常具有挑戰性的，因為在疾病擴散過程中，兩個位置之間的相互關係是隱藏的;我們在歷史數據中所擁有的只是過去所有地點確認的感染病例數。此外，鑑於資源有限，擴散網絡推斷的目標不僅僅是表徵整個網絡的結構，而是確定可以預測所有位置（包括未觀察到的）的當前/未來感染病例的關鍵位置。 本項目將開發一組稀疏貝葉斯學習（GSBL）框架，以解決上述問題，即從推斷的潛在擴散網絡中選擇關鍵位置進行主動監視。在GSBL框架下，我們將解決以下計算挑戰：1）如何模擬傳染病病例的空間稀疏分佈; 2）如何及時推斷潛伏擴散網絡; 3）如何表徵傳染病的複雜擴散模式。為了應對這些挑戰，我們將相應地提出三種新方法：1）具有伯努利可能性的GSBL（GSBL-B）; 2）可擴展的GSBL（GSBL-S）; 3）GSBL（GSBL-N）的非線性模型嵌入。 我們將在多個尺度上進行實驗評估和現場驗證。具體而言，我們將考慮兩個具有代表性的現實疾病傳播情景：香港的流感爆發和中國的瘧疾消除倡議。 本項目的成果將有助於計算機科學和流行病學的學術研究，以及在實踐中用於傳染病的控制和預防。本項目取得的成果將為公共衛生部門製定傳染病的防控政策提供科學依據。

12201318.label: Realisation of objectives
12201318.value: In this project, all the objectives have been well achieved. To achieve the three objectives listed in Section 5.1, we made a detailed research plan and strictly followed our plan to complete the set tasks. First, the PI's team initiated a preliminary study to partially test the feasibility of the idea of group sparsity. The result from this preliminary study, which was used to ground the research proposed in this project, was accepted and published in the Proceedings of AAAI 2018 [1] in February 2018, demonstrating the feasibility and potential of our idea and design. We reported this information in the Proposal Update to the RGC in March 2018. To select key locations for active surveillance, a key premise is that the diffusion network should be accurately inferred. However, such a diffusion network is generally not directly observable and thus difficult to infer. To address this challenging issue, we therefore conducted another pilot study in 2018 to investigate the diffusion network modeling problem from the fundamental layer, i.e., analyzing the primitives of the complex networks – motifs. We proposed a new method to mine the motif profile from the node observations and infer the underlying network based on the mined motif profile. Experiments on synthetic and real-world malaria datasets validated the effectiveness of the method. The result of this research was published in [2]. Based on the success of our pilot studies, we systematically carried out a series of research activities to extend the above research from the following three perspectives: (1) Methodology Perspective To develop a comprehensive GSBL framework based on our prototype, we proposed a general sentinel network mining algorithm (SNMA). Specifically, we developed the model with Bernoulli likelihood for the logistic discrete system (GSBL-B). To make the model practically useful, as planned, we validated the effectiveness of our model in two typical disease diffusion scenarios: the H1N1 influenza outbreak in Hong Kong and the malaria transmission in China-Myanmar border. We integrated these new findings into the extended journal version of our AAAI paper. The journal paper was published in the IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence [3]. In order to explore the spatiotemporal nature of disease transmission problems (including but not limited to the disease domain), we developed a new method called interactively and integratively connected deep recurrent neural network (I2DRNN). Under the framework of information theory, this method is a general probabilistic version of the GSBL-B, which allows both discrete or continuous inputs. By characterizing the multi-scale dependency of spatiotemporal data, the developed method consistently outperformed both classical and state-of-the-art machine learning models on disease prediction as well as other spatiotemporal forecasting tasks. The result of this research was published in the IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems [4]. From the viewpoint of machine learning modeling, GSBL is a special case of the multi-task learning (MTL). Therefore, to enhance the applicability of the GSBL, especially the GSBL-S and GSBL-N, we investigated the group sparse learning under the framework of MTL. When the data size is large and the data/task dependencies are nonlinear and complex, a critical challenge in MTL is how to explicitly represent and quantify the distance or similarity of different tasks. To address this challenge, we proposed a novel method of Metric-guided MTL (M2TL), which explicitly measures the task distance using a metric learning strategy. With a metric-guided regularizer incorporated in the proposed objective function, this method was efficient and scalable in computation, and flexible to incorporate the nonlinear embeddings. The result of this research was published in [5]. (2) Application Perspective In addition to the H1N1 and malaria planned in the proposal, we also explored the applicability of our developed technologies in other real-world disease diffusion scenarios. Recently, with the outbreak of COVID-19, there is an urgent need to understand the underlying transmission patterns of the disease, so as to address a series of important questions in controlling the COVID-19 outbreak. To answer this challenging question, we showed that the age-specific [6] and cross-location [7][8] social contact patterns can accurately characterize the interactions among different groups of people, and thus provided explanations on the underlying disease transmission and associated risks in various phases of the outbreak. With a series of retrospective and prospective analyses, this work offered effective tools and insights to other countries or regions for their intervention planning and operational responses. The result of this research was published in The Lancet Discovery Science [6][7] and Infectious Diseases of Poverty [8]. (3) Deployment Perspective To conduct the onsite validation of the developed methods, the PI’s team worked directly with policymakers and practitioners from China CDC and Tengchong CDC to deploy our active surveillance strategies for early warning of imported cases in the malaria elimination and post-elimination phases in China-Myanmar border. In addition to the deployment in China, PI's team aims to transfer the developed technologies for accelerating malaria elimination in the GMS and SEA countries. To do so, we provided a series of deployment planning, priority-specific situation analysis, context-aware technical training, and hands-on practice to the policymakers, public health officials, and practitioners from the WHO Malaria Mekong Elimination (MME) team, the Health Poverty Action (HPA), and the health authorities of eight GMS and SEA countries. After rigorous evaluation, delegates from these countries have recognized the importance and effectiveness of the developed technologies and tools in risk assessment and resource allocation. The Department of Health of Cambodia has already initiated the collaboration with PI’s team to adopt and implement the developed technologies and tools to tackle respective country-specific challenges [9]. 12201318.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201318.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a group sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL) framework and a series of GSBL methods to address the challenging problem of selecting key locations from the inferred latent diffusion network for active surveillance. By systematically validating the performance of the developed framework and methods on both synthetic datasets and real-world scenarios, we demonstrated that GSBL is effective in identifying critical sentinels for disease surveillance, especially when the available resources are limited. Moreover, we have conducted in-depth investigation and analysis of GSBL from both methodological (e.g., the multi-task learning) and application (e.g., spatiotemporal transmission patterns of infectious diseases) perspectives. Such investigation and analysis not only provide the theoretical insight into the model design, but also offer practical guidance for policy making and intervention implementation for disease control. The research outcomes of this project are published on reputable journals and conferences in both computer science and public health domains. We have published nine project-related papers in total, five of which are in computer science while the remaining four are in public health. Specifically, in computer science, we have published: one paper on the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence; one paper on the IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence; one paper on the IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems; one paper on the International Journal of Data Science and Analytics; and one paper on the 25th International Symposium on Methodologies for Intelligent Systems (ISMIS-20). In public health, we have published: two papers on EClinicalMedicine, The Lancet Discovery Science; one paper on Infectious Diseases of Poverty; and one paper on Infectious Disease Modelling. The aforementioned interdisciplinary research outcomes, which are assessed and recognized by experts from both computer science and public health, further demonstrated the usefulness and importance of the developed technologies in resource allocation for risk prediction and surveillance.

12201318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201318.value: Future work will be carried out from the following several aspects. First, we will integrate various machine learning methods into our GSBL framework, such as deep learning architectures and tensor learning algorithms, so as to improve the representation ability of the framework and to adapt to different complex scenarios in practice. Second, we aim to incorporate specific domain knowledge of disease transmission into the GSBL framework, such as the mechanical models that characterize disease dynamics via ordinal differential equations (ODE), so that the learned model could have better interpretability in the real-world context. Third, we would like to integrate active surveillance with other resource (e.g., vaccine and hospital capacity) allocation scenarios, so as to further enhance the framework’s practical applicability. Last but not least, we will continue our collaboration with the health authorities in mainland China and other GMS countries to put the developed technologies and tools into practical use in eliminating malaria, thus contributing to social good.

12201318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201318.value: The extensive ranges of infectious disease diffusion make comprehensive surveillance challenging or even impossible due to limited surveillance resources during outbreaks. Existing disease surveillance relies on case reporting from existing health agencies; however, this approach is somewhat passive, and can lead to unsatisfactory results because of error-prone observations. In this project, we developed and empirically validated a novel framework for active surveillance, which is a crucial strategy for addressing the shortcomings of passive surveillance when resources are limited. The active surveillance strategy proactively determines key locations for surveillance by identifying and utilizing the latent diffusion network inferred from clinically confirmed historical data. By developing a computational framework and new methods, the proposed project contributed to the academic literature in both computer science and epidemiology. By carrying out comprehensive experimental evaluation and onsite validations on two representative real-world disease diffusion scenarios, the project also improved the control and prevention of infectious diseases in practice. Moreover, results derived from the proposed active surveillance framework can provide a scientific foundation for public health authorities in developing policies for infectious disease interventions.

12201518.label: Realisation of objectives
12201518.value: Objective 1. To formally analyze the semantics of different keyword search queries and community search queries. We have analyzed a few semantics of the queries in this project. We have formally defined the keyword search and community search [ICDE2019]; we have analyzed the existing keyword search semantics [ICDE2020, TKDE2021]; and we studied community analysis [PVLDB2022] and subgraph matching [DASFAA2019]. Proc. of the 24th International Conference on Database Systems for Advanced Applications (DASFAA '19), Chiang Mai, Thailand, pages 471-475, 2019. Objective 2. To analyze the critical entity evaluation methods used in cohesive subgraphs. We have considered the problem as the collapsed k-core problem [TKDE2022]. The problem is an NP-hard problem. In the literature, the state-of-the-art approach, a greedy algorithm is proposed with no guarantee on the quality of the solution since there does not exist a submodular function the greedy algorithm can use to get a better answer iteratively. Furthermore, the greedy algorithm is designed to handle k-core in any social network such that it does not consider the structural complexity of a given single graph and cannot get the global optimal by the local optimal found in iterations. Reference: [TKDE2022] K. Zhao, Z. Zhang, Y. Rong, J. Yu, and J. Huang. "Finding Critical Users in Social Communities via Graph Convolutions." IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE), accepted to appear, 2022. Objective 3. To design query processing method to identify critical vertices, keywords, and subgraph patterns. We have achieved this objective by proposing query processing methods of critical vertices, keyword search, and subgraph matching, respectively. Critical vertices. In [TKDE2022], we propose a novel learning-based approach to finding critical vertices. Distinguished from traditional experience-based heuristics, we propose a neural network model called Self-attentive Core Graph Convolution Network (SCGCN), to capture the hidden structure of the criticalness among node combinations that break the engagement of a speciﬁc social community. Supervised by sampling node combinations, SCGCN has the ability to infer the criticalness of unseen combinations of nodes. To further reduce the sampling and inference space, we propose a deterministic strategy to prune unpromising nodes on the graph. Keyword search. In [ICDE2019], we have studied a novel problem of keyword-centric community search (KCCS) over attributed graphs. In contrast to prior studies, no query nodes, but only query keywords, need to be specified to discover relevant communities. Given an attributed graph G, a query Q consisting of query keywords WQ, and an integer k, KCCS serves to find the largest subgraph of k-core of G that achieves the strongest keyword closeness, w.r.t. WQ. We design a new function of keyword closeness and propose efficient algorithms to solve the KCCS problem. Furthermore, a novel core-based inverted index is developed to optimize performance. Subgraph matching. Subgraph matching is to enumerate all the subgraphs of graph G that are isomorphic to the query graph. Most of the existing works design in-memory algorithms assuming that the graph can entirely reside in the memory. However, the real-world attributed graph grows explosively in the big data era, and we have many massive attributed graphs that are much larger than the memory size of the modern machine. Therefore, in [DASFAA19], we study the subgraph matching problem where the graph is stored in multiple disk blocks, and we focus on the I/O efﬁciency. Different from the existing node-matching based approaches, we design a block-based approach, GScan, which investigates the block combinations that contain the subgraph matching candidates. To achieve high I/O efﬁciency, we only use sequential I/O read operations in our approach, which are known to be much faster than the random I/O operations as well as the I/O write operations. The block transfer between the memory and the disk is scheduled by the proposed algorithm effectively to make full use of the limited memory space. 4. To develop a unified system to support various types of graph queries and identify different critical entities. The source code of identifying critical entities can be publicly available here: https://github.com/Kangfei/CoreCollapse

12201518.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201518.value: In this project, we analyzed several query semantics that is relevant to critical entities in a big attributed graph. We started with a new keyword-centric community search [ICDE2019]. Various keyword search semantics have been proposed because graphs are flexible but lack schema information for query formulation. Such search semantics require a small subgraph structure that contains all the keywords [ICDE2020, TKDE2021]. It is then natural to study critical entities in a community whose removal leads to the collapse of the community. In particular, we considered the problem as the collapsed k-core problem [TKDE2022], which is NP-hard. Regarding the solution of the collapse k-core problem, we observe that the state-of-the-art approach is a greedy algorithm. It has no guarantee of the quality of the solution since there does not exist a submodular function the greedy algorithm can use to get a better answer iteratively. Furthermore, the greedy algorithm is designed to handle k-core in any graph such that it does not consider the structural complexity of a given graph and cannot get the global optimal by the local optimal found in iterations. In [TKDE2022], we propose a novel learning-based approach to finding critical vertices. Distinguished from traditional experience-based heuristics, we propose a neural network model called Self-attentive Core Graph Convolution Network (SCGCN) to capture the hidden structure of the criticalness among node combinations that break the engagement of a speciﬁc social community. In a nutshell, we proposed a learning-based approach to solving an NP-hard problem. Regarding the keyword-centric community search [ICDE0219] in an attributed graph, we proposed a new function of keyword closeness and proposed efficient search algorithms. Furthermore, a novel core-based inverted index is developed to optimize performance. The efficiency of various techniques for querying graphs was investigated. For example, in [DASFAA19], we studied the subgraph matching problem where the graph is so large that can only be stored in multiple disk blocks and we focused on the I/O efﬁciency. To achieve high I/O efﬁciency, we only used sequential I/O read operations in our approach. Second, we studied the indexing approach for efficient generic keyword search [TKDE2021]. We found that the attribute hierarchy of attributed graphs (similarly, ontology information of knowledge graphs) can be exploited to index the graphs for efficient keyword search. During the project, we notice that some subgraphs (that may contain critical entities) can be private while the rest are public. We studied the keyword search in the public-private model.

12201518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201518.value: The integration of structural critical entities and more existing keyword search can be further developed. In [TKDE2021], we propose a generic ontology-based indexing framework for representative existing keyword search, called Bisimulation of Generalized Graph Index (BiG-index), to enhance the search performance. The novelties of BiG-index reside in using an ontology graph GOnt to summarize and index a data graph G iteratively, to form a hierarchical index structure G. BiG-index is generic since it only requires keyword search algorithms to generate query answers from summary graphs having two simple properties. It would be technically interesting to investigate if BiG-index can be extended to support structural critical entities. In [VLDB2022], we have studied the D-core decomposition of directed graphs in the distributed settings. In the literature, several peeling-based algorithms have been proposed to handle D-core decomposition. However, the peeling-based algorithms that work in a sequential fashion and require global graph information during processing are mainly designed for centralized settings, which cannot handle large-scale graphs efficiently in distributed settings. Motivated by this, we proposed our novel solution. The support of structural critical entities in the distributed setting.

12201518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201518.value: In this project, we have studied a novel problem of keyword-centric community search (KCCS) over attributed graphs. In the literature, no query nodes, but only query keywords, need to be specified to discover relevant communities. Given an attributed graph G, a query Q consisting of query keywords WQ, and an integer k, KCCS serves to find the largest subgraph of k-core of G that achieves the strongest keyword closeness, w.r.t. WQ. We design a new function of keyword closeness and propose efficient algorithms to solve the KCCS problem. Furthermore, a novel core-based inverted index is developed to optimize performance. We have also studied the problem as the collapsed k-core problem. In brief, it considers a social community as a k-core for a given k and ﬁnds a set of nodes, U, with a given size b, that will trigger the maximum number of nodes to be deleted from the k-core, if all nodes in U are deleted. We have proposed a novel learning-based approach to find such vertices. Our approach captures the hidden structure of the criticalness among node combinations that break the engagement of a speciﬁc social community.

12201818.value: 受細胞中轉錄因子布朗運動的影響，基因轉錄活動必然具有一定的隨機性。這種隨機性導致了轉錄因子信號通路中基因的表達出現隨機波動，進而使得同一基因在相同類型細胞中表現出顯著不同的表達水平，這就是基因表達噪聲。 一種新穎的觀點認為，基因表達噪聲並非是中心法則失效，它可能是細胞為了實現特定功能而主動採取的一種機制。最近有實驗表明，某些基因的噪聲水平是細胞對不同的細胞內/外信號的直接響應，顯示基因噪聲受到細胞的直接控制。 儘管目前單細胞成像技術已經可以細緻觀測細胞內基因轉錄的動態活動，但我們對於細胞控制轉錄噪聲的分子機制仍然知之甚少。最近有單細胞觀測實驗顯示，細胞可以通過調整兩種轉錄因子進出細胞核的相對時序實現對目標基因的組合調控。此外還有研究表明，兩個轉錄因子能形成特定的邏輯關係以實現對其目標基因表達的調控。但是到目前為止，我們仍然未能解析轉錄因子組合調控與目標基因表達噪聲之間的分子機制及定量化模型。 本項目中，我們將以大腸桿菌為研究對象，利用超高分辨率顯微鏡對單細胞中單分子活動進行直接實時的觀測，研究細胞利用轉錄因子組合調控對基因表達噪聲進行控制的分子機制和模型。我們首先建立一個可以描述單細胞中轉錄暴增現象的單轉錄因子模型方程。然後，我們利用組合邏輯將單因子模型擴展為雙因子模型。接著，基於此模型方程及最新的實驗觀測結果，我們提出了研究組合調控對基因噪聲水平控制的三個研究問題。 首先，依據我們的組合調控模型，理論上可以預測，對於相同目標基因而言，雙因子組合調控將比單因子轉錄產生更大的轉錄噪聲。事實上，這一點已經有實驗證據。本項目中，我們將設計單因子及雙因子調控的對比試驗，對這個理論推斷進行進一步驗證。 其次，我們的理論模型預測不同的組合邏輯將導致細胞呈現不同的基因噪聲水平。為了研究這個問題，針對同一個目標基因，我們將構造雙因子組合調控的一組細胞，並對這組細胞的轉錄活動進行實時觀測。基於觀測數據，我們將對每一個細胞中的有關該目標基因的組合調控邏輯進行解析，並根據調控邏輯對細胞進行分類。之後，我們將檢驗不同邏輯類型的細胞之間在基因噪聲水平方面是否存在顯著差異。 最後，我們可以從理論上推導出，不同的細胞間由於在轉錄因子結合目標基因活動上無法實現同步，將導致目標基因的表達上的額外噪聲。本項目中，我們將通過實驗研究這種不同步現象是否會影響目標基因的表達，以及其基因表達噪聲的影響程度。

12201818.label: Realisation of objectives
12201818.value: In this project, we tried to address the mechanistic views of combinatorial gene regulatory logic to transcriptional disturbance and its effects on the related biological phenotypes. We figured out the relevant scopes in mammalian systems. We have specifically opted for it in the biorhythm system since its scalability, complexity, and its transcriptional perturbations under transcriptional combinatorial regulation have a wide range of impacts on living systems. We investigated a key biological research question: (1) how do a few essential transcription factors (TFs) shape such diversified manifestations of transcription activity? (2) How alterations in combinatorial regulatory paradigm affect or produce transcriptional perturbations and phenotypic variations. (3) How to describe and model such paradigm and the perturbations with quantitative approaches. High-time resolution and high-dimensional biorhythm data obtained from mice allowed us to test our hypotheses at both the cellular and tissue level. The mammalian circadian systems consist of indigenous, self-sustained 24-hours rhythm generators. They comprise many genes, molecules, and regulators. To decode their systematic controls, a robust computational approach was employed. It integrated transcription-factor-occupancy and time-series gene-expression data as input. The model equations were constructed and solved to determine the potential transcriptional regulatory logic in the transcription network. This is hypothesized to explore the underlying mechanisms of combinatorial transcriptional regulations for circadian rhythms in mammalian systems. A computational workflow was designed by us to reconstruct the quantitative transcriptional regulatory networks (qTRNs) for combinatorial gene regulation at a dynamic scale. With this workflow, transcriptional perturbations in the qTRNs by altering the transcriptional logic were simulated to estimate their influence on phenotypic variations. The potential mechanism of out-of-synchronization in combinatorial regulation modulating the phenotypic heterogeneity was identified. This quantitative framework offers a quick, robust, and physiologically relevant way to characterize the druggable targets to modulate the combinatorial gene regulation at a dynamic scale effectively. We constructed the qTRNs for the genes under combinatorial regulatory logic, and identified key transcriptional regulatory logic, followed by characterized the transcriptional perturbations upon altered TF-logic. In our results, we have shown that 10 TFs formed 66 combinations which were characterized using logic gates, and they facilitated the prediction of more than 900 genes, out of which 461 genes were well characterized to exhibit circadian fluctuations. Further, we have introduced the concept of TF-logic layers in circadian transcriptional regulations. We found some of the genes were regulated by a single TF/TF-logic, wherein many others were regulated by the various combinations of two-TFs logic. We have shown that different TF-logic formed by the same TFs can produce different dynamic signatures of gene expressions, and genes under the control of the same regulatory logic share similar dynamic profiles also. Next, our qTRN-predicted dynamic expression profiles of those well-characterized genes with circadian fluctuations exhibited an excellent consistency with their original expression signals. It strengthens the biological relevance of qTRNs in interpreting the transcriptional regulations. The group of genes under the control of the same regulatory TF-logic shared similar dynamic fluctuations in their expressions. Interestingly, some of the TF-logic combinations identified in our studies exhibited consistency in regulating the same target genes as predicted and reported to have similar functional roles as we predicted. For example, CRY1 and PER2 formed (CR1.&.PER2) logic to regulate Apoc3 that significantly controls metabolic rhythms in mammalian liver. So, LogicTRN-based transcriptional simulations are quite reliable with experimental evidence. Next, we estimated the influence of vKO on an individual circadian gene. Transcriptional simulation of Spon2 and Prpf19 were shown with all possible combinations of vKO mutant TFs and their corresponding perturbed period lengths were estimated at different vKO conditions. It was found to be consistent with experimentally validated perturbed period lengths (Ray et.al., Science, 2020). It reinforces the concept of the vKO and the underlying quantitative framework. Later, we investigated the tissue-specific circadian transcriptional controls and found that the same target gene expresses differently in different tissues because the underlying TF-logic is different. The same target gene preserves similar expression dynamics across different tissues as regulated by the same TF-logic. So, the versatility of the transcriptional controls govered by TF-logic is tissue-specific. It serves as a clue about the differential molecular interplay of circadian oscillations across tissues. The corresponding cross-dataset validations were reported in our publication. Finally, revisiting all the directions of the results achieved has successfully addressed all the objectives as pursued with this specific study. We developed a framework to reconstruct the qTRNs. The underlying combinatorial transcriptional regulatory logic controlling their expressions were decoded. A wide range of genes with circadian fluctuations were characterized along with their dynamic expressions. We developed the vKO approach to estimate the influence of any TF-combination to perturb the qTRNs. This offers a quick way to generate relevant hypotheses for experimental validation. Besides, in another publication, we have emphasized the transcriptional noise and combinatorial regulation in bacteria. We have discussed the aspects and probable mechanisms of Cis-Regulatory logic in producing gene expression noises which further directs phenotypic heterogeneity in Bacteria. Here, we reviewed the prospects and challenges in validating the quantitative framework of modelling combinatorial gene regulation at cellular and the single-cell level to characterize the bursting patterns and dynamic behaviours of gene transcription. We were able to decipher the role and mechanisms of combinatorial gene regulatory logic to transcriptional noise (100% achieved of the original objective 1) and examined the mechanism of out-of-synchronization of TF binding in different cells in producing phenotypic heterogeneity and gene expression noise that produced different expression variations at dynamic scale (100% achieved of the original objective 2). In addition, with our results, we showed the cross-dataset validation and relevant publication-based validation of the logic concepts and the concepts of cis-regulatory logic-based production of gene-expression noise that describes phenotypic heterogeneity at the systems level (100% achieved of the original objective 3). There is a bit deviation of the objectives met as proposed originally, and we could not deploy this concept in vivo extensively because we missed the cooperation opportunity to test our hypothesis through single-cell experiments by working with Peking University during COVID-19. However, considering those deviations, the scientific rigours pursued in this project were well maintained throughout addressing the principle questions in molecular aspects. To address the lack of experimental validation by direct observation, we reformulated our research strategy. For the observation of intracellular transcription activity, we replaced the method of observing transcriptional activity by monitoring the GFP-tagged MS2 (RNA binding protein) bound mRNA by using the GFP protein expressed by various synthetic promoters. For the estimation of transcriptional noise, we detected the GFP signal within single cells by flow cytometric methods to evaluate cell-to-cell variability within an isogenic population. We apply stochastic control analysis to the synthetic gene expression systems encoded on plasmids that are transformed into E. coli. Based on our proposed model, we computed the parameters of mean and noise levels of GFP fluorescence signals. The computed coefficients show that noise can be controlled efficiently by varying the inactive and active promoter states. The results show that combinatorial control of transcription provides the most efficient way of noise-versus-mean control.

12201818.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201818.value: This project has successfully delivered the following yields: We deployed the LogicTRN approach which was developed based on the well-established theories of -regulatory logic and transcriptional kinetics, which provides an efficient way to infer TF–TF interactions in regulating target genes. Through simulation and comparison studies, our model shows its reliability and robustness in capturing TF regulatory logic, identifying targets of TFs, and constructing transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs). The applications in human breast cancer and the hiPSC-derived CM development demonstrate consistency between the identified TF gene regulation and the previous experiments in our preliminary studies. With an increasing number of dynamic high-throughput data of gene expression and multiple regulator binding signals, our method would provide a powerful tool for interpreting the dynamics and complexity of transcriptional gene regulation. Next, we employed this understanding to reconstruct qTRNs. This helped to decode the underlying transcriptional regulatory logic controlling their expressions. This foundation was deployed to study the transcription disturbance in mammalian systems, and a wide range of genes with phenotypic heterogeneity has been identified and characterized. In addition, the temporal dynamic expression profiles of those genes were simulated. It certainly facilitates understanding of the transcriptional regulatory controls of certain sets of genes having combinatorial control and critically controlling physiological functions by its biological features. To elucidate the role of combinatorial transcriptional regulation and temporal dynamic binding of TFs, we developed a simulation approach to estimate the influence of any TF combinations to perturb the qTRNs. It enlightens in understanding specific mechanisms and the role of dynamic TF-binding on their target genes that eventually controls the expressions of genes having transcription disturbance. Hence, with this publication within this project, we essentially developed a computational approach to modelling combinatorial gene regulation in single cells, which can characterize the bursting patterns and dynamic behaviours of gene transcription. Our approach provides a quick way to generate relevant hypotheses for experimental validation. In this direction, our work facilitated to minimisation of immensely expensive experimental efforts and iterations with smart data-driven decision systems. In another publication in Frontiers in Genetics, we discussed the very fundamental biological problems of gene expression noise to understand the role of genetic circuits in cellular complexity and functions. The emergence of this concept was endorsed as we emphasized the use of synthetic biocomputational approaches to create a holistic roadmap to understand not only the transcriptional noise-driven phenotypic variability but also its underlying regulatory logic. Genetically identical bacteria can behave differently due to variable gene expression patterns, which are noisy. Such spontaneous dynamic performance is pervasive and has been used in microbes and mammalian cells. We have evaluated the contradictory perceptions of the origin of such heterogeneity in terms of its appropriateness in genomic applications. We have indicated that gene expression noise results from randomness in gene circuits, which is tightly dictated by the transcription noise produced via combinatorial gene regulation. This basis offered know-how to indicate the purpose-driven programming of combinatorial regulation to augment phenotypic variability and adapt to fluctuating environments. Such an integrated systems biology approach should help researchers develop more accurate model transcriptional relationships among molecules in a biological system, thus permitting larger consideration of complex biological processes associated with development, ageing, and other complex diseases.

12201818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201818.value: The future development of this research project and course of action can be considered as follow. The current understanding of combinatorial gene regulations can be further refined by integrating other regulatory layers such as translational regulations, histone modifications, DNA methylations and chromatin modifications and their influence on regulating the functional gene expressions. Recent developments in 3D chromatin modelling may serve as a prominent tool along with multimodal omics data integration. Transcriptional noise can be centralised for interpreting phenotypic variations at the cellular level. It can be deployed to understand the unprecedented facets of cell-to-cell variability. The high-resolution temporal and spatio-temporal dynamics of TF binding are two prominent scopes in next-generation evidence-based precision medicine. One of the critical outcomes of this project is vKO which enables an estimation of the temporal effects of TF-binding and its perturbations on gene expressions at a dynamic scale. It can further facilitate decoding the diversified yet intricated molecular interplays stacked across different cells, cell types, and tissues. This can undoubtedly be a unique approach toward establishing robust knowledgebase to support data-backed decision-driven minimization of experimental iterations. The accurate prediction of dynamic behaviours of gene transcriptions through their TF-logic widens an avenue to investigate the functional role of those genes in a time series within a cell and beyond. It may help in decoding the intricated cellular interactome that collaboratively and cumulatively regulate biochemical pathways.

12201818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201818.value: We reinstated the importance of synthetic biocomputational approaches to create a holistic roadmap to understand not only the transcriptional noise-driven phenotypic variability but also its underlying regulatory logic. Our data showed that introducing the TF-logic layer certainly introduces an additional rationale to explain and characterize the gene expression at a dynamic scale. We have shown the same candidate TFs regulate a different group of genes with significantly different trends of dynamic signature as their underlying TF-logic were different. It plausibly answers the complex gene regulation mechanisms and their variations. A few physiologically relevant algorithms have been developed and deployed with relevant biomedical applications as an output of this project. An integrative quantitative framework was constructed that describes mechanistic insights of transcriptional regulations mediated by multiple TFs. It demonstrated the capacity of a few molecules to form a complex genetic circuit that further governs diversified gene expressions. We developed a quantitative framework for modelling combinatorial gene regulation. Based on the framework, the impact of combinatorial regulation on transcriptional perturbations and phenotypic variations can be extensively examined. It facilitates to manipulation of the TF/TFs combinations which is a clue to therapeutically modulating the transcriptional controls. We further extended our concept on patient data to stratify the patients upon rationalizing their diagnosis with personalized genomic signatures which are rooted within transcriptome variations. Largely, this project delivers a refreshed perspective in systems biology from molecules to systems and enables a deeper understanding of complex biological processes involved in various physiologies, and complex diseases.

12300218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300218.value: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) has been used in a variety of real-world applications such as blind signal processing, spectral recovery, pattern recognition, text mining and bioinformatics. NMF is to recover hidden structures or bases from the non-negative input data and compute the linear projection of the data onto the bases keeping with non-negativity property. By adding orthogonal constraints into the factorization, orthogonal non-negative matrix factorization (ONMF) is developed, and ONMF is more challenging and useful because of its uniqueness and rigorous pattern interpretation. However, it is challenging to design efficient solution methods for solving the solution of ONMF especially for large-scale data matrices. Existing techniques include multiplicative update algorithms, gradient calculation in Stiefel manifold, and augmented Lagrangian approach by enforcing orthogonality constraints. The main aim of this project to propose a new formulation of ONMF and design new efficient algorithms for ONMF. Our idea is to analyze the structure of orthogonal constraints, we study similarity matrices in the new formulation and design efficient and structured optimization algorithms to compute ONMF. We will analyze solutions of the new formulation and their error bounds by using matrix theory and probability in perturbation analysis of eigenvectors. Multi-dimensional data is becoming prevalent in many data science applications. The proposed approach and eigenvector analysis will be further investigated into orthogonal non-negative tensor factorization (ONTF). In the project, we plan to apply the proposed ONMF and ONTF models to (i) supervised learning, transfer learning and hyperspectral unmixing frameworks. In supervised learning, prior information can be incorporated in the proposed models and they can used for classification purpose. In transfer learning, knowledge from multiple sources can be transferred to a target domain via the latent features learnt by ONTF, and this new framework can enhance learning capability. (iii) Based on our ONTF model, we can classify pixels in hyperspectral images according to factorized latent features. We will test the numerical performance of the proposed models and algorithms for these applications. 12300218.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300218.value: In [3], we studied a new algorithm for computing nonnegative low rank matrix approximation for a nonnegative matrix based by determining a nonnegative low rank matrix such that the distance between such matrix and the given nonnegative matrix is as small as possible. In [4], we further studied nonnegative tensor data and proposed an orthogonal nonnegative Tucker decomposition, and discussed some properties of orthogonal nonnegative Tucker decomposition. We also developed a convex relaxation algorithm of the augmented Lagrangian function to solve the optimization problem, and analyzed its convergence. In [1], we applied the model and the algorithm to a low rank tensor recovery problem from limited sampling with noisy observations for third-order tensors. We proposed to incorporate a corrected term in the tensor nuclear norm method for tensor completion and provided a nonasymptotic error bound of the corrected tensor nuclear norm model for low-rank tensor completion. In [5], we studied incremental tensors where new data are arriving in the next time step or continuously over time and developed incremental CP decomposition algorithms by adding components in the decomposition. Numerical examples were presented to show the good performance of the proposed algorithms in terms of computational time and data fitting compared with existing methods. In [2,6,7], we deal with tensor data decomposition applications. In [2], we studied a real application in online heterogeneous transfer learning, where the objective is to make predictions for a target data sequence arriving in an online fashion, and some offline labeled instances from a heterogeneous source domain are provided as auxiliary data. In [6], we studied the problem of predicting labels for one type of nodes in a heterogeneous information network which contains multiple types of nodes multiple types of links among them. A tensor-based Markov chain (nonnegative structure) is able to automatically and simultaneously predict the labels for unlabeled nodes and give the relative importance of types of links that actually improve the classiﬁcation accuracy. Theoretical analyses of the existence and uniqueness of probability distributions arising from tensor model are established. In [7], we proposed a blind hyperspectral reconstruction technique exploiting spectral low-rankness and spatial correlation of hyperspectral images. The tensor subspace basis is data-adaptive and provides a more compact representation than other non-adaptive representations. This adaptiveness leads to improved hyperspectral image recovery as illustrated in experiments with real remote sensing data.

12300218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300218.value: The development of the research is to develop a new algorithm for computing a nonnegative low multi-rank tensor approximation for a nonnegative tensor. In the future research, we can study nonnegativity constraints in tensor entries directly, and a low rank approximation for the transformed tensor by using discrete Fourier transformation matrix, discrete cosine transformation matrix or discrete wavelet transformation matrix. This strategy is particular useful in imaging science as nonnegative pixels appear in tensor entries and a low rank structure can be obtained in the transformation domain. We need to study and analyze an alternating projections algorithm for computing such a nonnegative low multi-rank tensor approximation on a set of low rank tensors in the transformation domain and a set of nonnegative tensors in the original domain.

12300218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300218.value: The main aim of this project is to develop new algorithms for computing nonnegative low rank tensor approximations for nonnegative tensors that arise in many multidimensional imaging applications. Nonnegativity is one of the important properties, as each pixel value refers to a nonzero light intensity in image data acquisitions. Our approach is different from classical nonnegative tensor factorization, which requires each factorized matrix, and/or tensor, to be nonnegative. In this project, we determine a nonnegative low rank tensor to approximate a given nonnegative tensor. Both theoretical and experimental results for synthetic data and multidimensional images are presented to demonstrate that the performance of the proposed approach is better than the state-of-the-art methods.
