12303618.value: 隨著領域科學領域的發展，從不同的科學，工程和人文領域收集了許多規模和範圍迅速增長的數據集。它在數據分析中創造了一個挑戰，即如何在統計推斷精度和計算複雜性之間進行權衡。對於大規模數據集，由於其理論計算複雜性，太多不壞的統計方法被宣布無用，但它忽略了計算機的計算結構或編程技術的優點，以及所需的那些實際應用的真實尺度。另一方面，對於經典的統計建模，特別是那些複雜的半參數回歸或非參數回歸建模問題，許多相關的研究文獻都集中在如何在模型估計的偏差和方差之間進行權衡，並試圖找到最優的效率對這些複雜模型的估計或推論。為了獲得那些最佳的有效估計或推論，模型構建必須基於限制性很強的數學條件和復雜的估計或推理過程。它忽略了計算的複雜性和穩定性的代價。因此，它在實踐中大大縮小了那些所謂的最佳有效統計建模方法的應用範圍。如Chanrasekaran和Jordan（2013）所示，為了在統計推斷和計算之間做出良好的平衡，需要將新的基礎觀點與統計學和計算機科學相結合。這是該提案的動機，該項目的主要目標是試圖為統計推斷和計算複雜性之間的權衡提供一些新的見解。 計算機的計算結構基於位操作。比特操作的速度比其他計算操作（例如浮点計算）快得多。該提議的第一個目標是研究如何在統計建模算法中應用這種基本和最簡單的計算機計算操作，以提高計算速度，從而使許多統計建模任務不能或很難通過正常完成計算機來源於理論見解，但可以在實踐中完成。在大多數情況下，觀察是連續的，並且位操作不能容易地應用於直接進行計算。通過數據的離散化，仍然可以應用比特操作來加速統計建模過程。我們考慮如何使用離散化方法來進行分類數據建模的同質性問題，並確定獨立篩選方法，尤其是超高維數據的純交互效應的篩選方法。通過離散化，我們的算法或基於位操作的軟件包可以真正實現大多數真實超高維數據的完全純交互效果篩選任務。 對於許多複雜的經典半參數或非參數回歸模型，非參數組件通常用於減少模型偏差，但參數組件會更感興趣。因此，有效地估計和推斷參數組件將是建模中最重要的任務之一。通過部分一致性的思想（Neyman和Scott 1943），我們將參數組件視為模型中的結構參數組件，但模型中的非參數組件作為偶然參數組件和階梯函數或其他離散化方法用於近似它們無偏。然後，我們將模型更改為高維參數模型。有效的算法可用於估計它們。研究了這些參數分量的效率和漸近正態性。還研究了基於這種估計的推理方法。此外，我們還表明，非參數分量也可以通過兩步估計程序近似最優估計，該程序基於第一步中幾乎無偏但非一致的非參數分量估計。 這項研究的新穎性是從兩個新的基礎觀點發展出來的統計上有效且計算上可行的框架。一個是通過離散化，可以充分利用計算機結構的優點。其次，通過使用部分一致現象，可以大大降低統計建模的計算複雜度，但幾乎可以保持模型估計的效率。

12303618.label: Realisation of objectives
12303618.value: First of all, we have nearly achieved all of the objectives suggested by this proposal. Top or good statistical journals have published most results. For objectives 1-3, we realized our proposed discretization process to transfer the continuous random variables to discrete random variables so that the Boolean bit operation could be applied to make calculations and help us to realize our proposed sure screening methods. We investigated the statistical properties of the discretization process, especially the efficiency loss of such a process. Next, based on the discretized response variable and predicted random variables, we realized our proposed sure screening methods with the Boolean bit operation. We investigated the screening properties of the proposed methods and their asymptotical statistical properties. Furthermore, we built a publicly available R package to realize our screening methods. In particular, we combined with the Rcpp package and applied C++ code to speed up our public R package to deal with large-scale data sets, as shown by our article published by Statistica Sinica. Hence, we believe that we finished the first three objectives of this proposal perfectly. For objectives 4-6, as our proposal shows, we realize the estimation algorithm to estimate the partial linear varying coefficient models. We investigated the asymptotical statistical properties of the estimate. We also compared the computational efficiency of our proposed methods with other classical estimation methods for the partial linear varying coefficient models. As we expected, a trade-off exists between the statistical efficiency and complexity of the estimation computation. We now consider the generalized semiparametric varying coefficient models, but some difficulties have hindered our progress. First of all, the complexity of the calculation is relatively challenging to analyze because there is no closed-form equation for the estimates; as for partial linear varying coefficient models, it depends on the iterative algorithms to find the final estimates. and furthermore, the asymptotic statistical properties of our proposed estimates are not easy to investigate because of step function approximation and high dimensional modeling under generalized linear models. Anyway, we finished most of these three objectives and gave a good understanding of the trade-off between the complexity of computation and optimal statistical efficiency.

12303618.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303618.value: Please see Zhou, et al. (2023). In this paper, we applied our public R package and used the Boolean bit operations to realize the interaction effect screening for the data with nearly 400,000 independent variables with sure screening properties guaranteed by a standard PC. Usually, such a task could not be achieved by classical statistical methods by standard PCs. It is impossible to finish the data analysis task. Hence, we believe that by combining the advantages of computer systems and efficient statistical algorithms, we can complete almost impossible large-scale data analysis tasks with little loss of statistical efficiency. It is one of our significant findings in this project. Please see Peng et al. (2021). We applied the step functions to transfer the partial varying coefficient models to high dimensional linear regression models; then, we can quickly get the model estimations. Though from the theoretical insights, there exists a little loss of statistical efficiency, the computational complexity has been much reduced according to our numerical studies. We believe an exciting trade-off exists between the optimal statistical efficiency of the model estimation and the computational complexity of such an estimation. Scarifying a little statistical efficiency, we can vastly reduce the complexity of the statistical estimation computation. It is the other important finding of our project. As shown by Peng, et al. (2021), the step function approximation provided a nearly unbiased high dimensional approximation to the varying coefficient functions. However, such a nearly unbiased approximation does not affect the consistent estimate of the global parameter estimates. It is our further exciting finding in this project and another partially consistent phenomenon. The basic idea behind such a finding is that we believe that it is because the random errors in the initial high dimensional estimates can be integrated by the following estimating steps for the global parameters estimates, but the bias of the model approximation can never be integrated. Hence our first step for the model estimation is trying to reduce approximation bias as much as possible and then control the variation of the model estimation. It provides another approach to balance the bias and variance of the statistical model estimations.

12303618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303618.value: Discretizing continuous random variables, applying the Boolean bit operations to more generalized statistical models, and speeding up more complex statistical models are our further developments in the research for large-scale data analysis. Investigating more deeply the properties of the discretizing to statistical model estimation and trying to find optimal discretizing ways to speed up different statistical methods. We will first analyze the discretization process for the regularized statistical methods with large-scale data. Investigating the phenomenon of partial consistency more deeply under generalized semiparametric models, providing a deep understanding of the effect of the computational complexity of the statistical model estimation methods on its efficiency loss, and trying to find the optimal approach to make the trade-off between the statistical efficiency and the complexity of the computation for the generalized semiparametric model estimation.

12303618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303618.value: In this research project, we investigate the trade-off between the statistical efficiency and the complexity of the computation of the statistical model estimations from two directions. First, we have shown by combining the advantages of the architecture of the computer system with a little loss of statistical efficiency, and we can use limited computational resources to achieve nearly impossible data analysis tasks. Second, based on partial consistency, we found that if we sacrifice a little statistical efficiency for the model estimation, we can vastly reduce the computational burden of the statistical model estimation. It provided another approach to trade off the statistical efficiency and the complexity of the computation of the statistical model estimations. Furthermore, we offer a new insight into the unbiased approximation for the statistical modeling. Our findings from this project are essential to large-scale data analysis and provide innovative insights or understanding to the statistical model estimations.

12303818.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303818.value: Our midterm report describes our research on developing numerical methods and convergence theories for solving partial differential equations on surfaces. We proposed new algorithms and convergence proofs for embedded and extrinsic solution methods and found that our methods outperformed existing ones, even on evolving and merging surfaces. We also extended our research to coupled bulk-surface PDE systems using kernel-based trial spaces, but some objectives related to bulk-diffusion surface-reaction-diffusion systems remained incomplete. To address the issue of overly accurate spatial approximations in the previous elliptic PDEs focusing greedy approach, we presented a new block-greedy algorithm for kernel-based collocation method combined with time-stepping methods in [3]. We found that using CFL-type conditions is not a good numerical approach for kernel-based methods used in bulk-surface systems. Instead, we developed a new greedy approach for selecting trial subspaces that balances temporal and spatial discretization errors to address Objective 7. Our new algorithm balances temporal and spatial errors in both well- and ill-conditioned scenarios and includes novel residual-based stopping criteria informed by temporal discretization accuracy. We applied our proposed greedy meshfree method to simulate bulk-surface pattern formation in 2D and 3D and demonstrated its ability to automatically select trial centers that balance temporal and spatial errors. Without our greedy selection, numerical results from the same meshfree method are less accurate and computationally more expensive. This addresses Objectives 4 and 6 related to semi-discretizing and extending the methods to bulk-surface systems. Additionally, we also worked on meshfree finite difference method [1] and method of lines [2] for pattern formations. [1] Z. Tang, Z. Fu, M. Chen, and L. Ling. A localized extrinsic collocation method for Turing pattern formations on surfaces. Applied Mathematics Letters. 122:107534. 2021. [2] M. Chen, K.C. Cheung, and L. Ling. A kernel-based least-squares collocation method for surface diffusion. SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis. 61(3): 1386-1404, 2023. [3] Y. Su and L. Ling. Greedy trial subspace selection in meshfree time-stepping schemes. Under Review in SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics.

12303818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303818.value: The research on developing numerical methods for solving partial differential equations on surfaces has great potential for further development. One promising avenue for future work is the application of the proposed methods to more complex systems, such as those involving multiple coupled PDEs or nonlinear equations. Additionally, the proposed methods could be extended to other types of PDEs, such as hyperbolic or integro-differential equations. To continue this research, we propose several courses of action. First, we recommend investigating the use of deep learning techniques to improve the accuracy of the proposed methods for solving PDEs on surfaces. Second, collaborating with experimentalists to apply the proposed methods to real-world problems, such as the simulation of surface chemical reactions or the analysis of fluid flow over surfaces, could be a win-win situation.

12303818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303818.value: Scientists study complex processes where surfaces interact with surrounding volumes, represented by coupled differential equations - one modeling the surface itself and one modeling the surrounding volume (i.e., bulk). Solving these coupled bulk-surface equations can provide insights into how patterns form on surfaces, how surfaces grow and change over time, and the dynamics of systems with interfaces. However, existing numerical techniques struggle to accurately and stably solve bulk-surface systems. The paper presents an adaptive meshless method that uses a greedy algorithm to select the minimum set of basis points needed to balance errors from spatial and temporal discretization. Simulations demonstrate the method's ability to yield stable, accurate solutions for various bulk-surface systems, including moving surfaces, surface reactions and diffusion from surrounding volumes. By efficiently solving coupled bulk-surface equations, the technique offers a way to gain mechanistic understanding of systems where surface phenomena strongly depend on interactions with surrounding volumes, with applications to areas like materials science, biology and chemistry.

12303918.label: Project Objectives
12303918.value: The first project is to propose a new category of the test methods to further advance the existing literature on high-dimensional multivariate testing. Specifically, we will consider a pairwise Hotelling's test to provide a compromise and hence fill the gap between the existing categories of the test methods. For both non-sparse and sparse cases, we will establish the asymptotic null distributions of the test statistics, derive their asymptotic power, evaluate the finite sample performance and compare them with the existing methods. We will also develop a unified R package that integrates the existing and new test methods for high-dimensional multivariate testing and make the package freely available in the R statistical program. The second project is to propose a regularized t distribution and apply it to high-dimensional multiple testing. To advance the research goals, we have the following objectives: (1) study the statistical properties of the regularized t distribution, (2) explore the effects of the regularization parameters on the performance of the regularized t test, (3) define a non-central regularized t distribution and assess the statistical power of the test in both theory and simulation, and (4) develop an R package for the regularized t test and make it freely available in the R statistical program.

12303918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303918.value: The recent flood of high-dimensional data has posed new challenges to the traditional statistical and computational methods. For high-dimensional data, due to the small sample size, there is a large amount of uncertainty associated with the standard estimates of variances and covariances. As a consequence, the classical testing procedures including Student's t test and Hotelling's T2 test may not be reliable, or even applicable, for high-dimensional data analysis. To overcome the problems, researchers have proposed a number of regularization methods to improve the estimation of variances and covariances, and then applied the new estimates to various testing problems to improve the literature. In this research plan, we propose to develop some new test methods for high-dimensional data. Our first project is to propose a new category of the test methods to further advance the existing literature on high-dimensional multivariate testing. Specifically, we will consider a pairwise Hotelling's test to provide a compromise and hence fill the gap between the existing categories of the test methods. For both non-sparse and sparse cases, we will establish the asymptotic null distributions of the test statistics, derive their asymptotic power, evaluate the finite sample performance and compare them with the existing methods. Our second project is to propose a regularized t distribution and apply it to high-dimensional multiple testing. To advance the research goals, we will study the statistical properties of the regularized t distribution, explore the effects of the regularization parameters on the performance of the regularized t test, define a non-central regularized t distribution, and assess the statistical power of the test in both theory and simulation. To cater for the demands of the application, we will also develop two R packages for the proposed testing methods and make them freely available in the R statistical program. Our proposed test methods are expected to have wide applications in different areas including statistical genetics, epidemiology, ecology, and engineering sciences. 高維數據的出現給傳統的統計方法和計算方法帶來了很多新的挑戰。對於高維小樣本數據，我們注意到方差和協方差等參數的估計具有著較大的不確定性，並由此降低了t檢驗和Hotelling檢驗等經典檢驗方法在高維數據分析中的可靠性。為了克服上述的問題，在本研究計劃中我們提出了幾個新穎的基於高維小樣本數據的檢驗方法。我們的第一個題目是關於多元檢驗問題的，針對現有方法的缺陷我們提出了一套全新的pairwise Hotelling檢驗的思想。然後針對非稀疏和稀疏兩種情況，我們將全面研究新構造的檢驗統計量的漸近性質，包括推導出原假設下的漸近分佈和備擇假設下的功效函數，並考慮對新檢驗方法和現有的方法進行大量的比較並得出最後的結論。我們的第二個題目是構造一個全新的正則化t分佈，並探討其在高維多重檢驗中的應用前景。我們將全研究正則化t分佈的統計性質，探討正則化參數對正則化t檢驗的影響，定義非中心正則化的t分佈，並推導出功效函數等眾多問題。最後，我們還將為新提出的檢驗方法開發方便實用的R軟件包並上載到CRAN供大家免費使用。

12303918.label: Realisation of objectives
12303918.value: To realize the first objective, the investigators have taken multiple approaches to propose a series of new test methods for high-dimensional data to further advance the existing literature. Some major developments and contributions are as follows. In Hu, Tong and Genton (2019), we proposed a likelihood ratio test framework for testing normal mean vectors in high-dimensional data for both the one- and two-sample tests, under the assumption that the covariance matrices follow a diagonal matrix structure. In comparison with the diagonal Hotelling’s tests, our proposed test statistics display some interesting characteristics. In particular, they are a summation of the log-transformed squared t-statistics rather than a direct summation of those components, and hence are very ﬂexible and readily applicable for practical implementation. In Ouyang, Liu, Tong and Xu (2022), we tackle the high-dimensional testing problem for equality of mean vectors under the non-normality assumption. To overcome the technical challenges in data sorting, our new statistics were constructed by taking the sum of the Wilcoxon signed-rank or Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test statistics from each dimension of the data. The asymptotic properties of the proposed test statistics were also investigated under the null and local alternative hypotheses. Simulation studies show that the new tests perform as well as the state-of-the-art methods when the high-dimensional data are normally distributed, but they turn out to be more powerful when the normality assumption is violated. In Hu, Tong and Genton (2023), inspired by the fact that most existing methods for high-dimensional testing may have some serious limitations and only work well in certain situations, we proposed a pairwise Hotelling method for testing high-dimensional mean vectors, which, in essence, provides a good balance between the existing approaches. To effectively utilize the correlation information, we construct the new test statistics as the summation of Hotelling’s test statistics for the covariate pairs with strong correlations and the squared t statistics for the individual covariates that have little correlation with others. We further derive the asymptotic null distributions and power functions for the proposed Hotelling’s tests under some regularity conditions. Last but not least, our new tests are able to control the type I error rates, and can achieve a higher statistical power compared to existing methods, especially when the covariates are highly correlated. To realize the second objective, the investigators have taken novel regularization approaches including truncating the p-values or adding the regularization parameters to further advance the existing literature on hypothesis testing. Some major developments and contributions are as follows. In Zhang, Tong, Landers and Wu (2020), we extended the classic Fisher’s combination method to a uniﬁed family of statistics, called TFisher, which allows a general truncation-and-weighting scheme of input p-values of each test. TFisher can signiﬁcantly improve statistical power over the Fisher and related truncation-only methods for detecting both rare and dense signals. We further studied the asymptotic optimal parameters of truncation and weighting based on the Bahadur efﬁciency (BE) and the asymptotic power efﬁciency (APE). Under the Gaussian mixture model in the signal detection problem, both BE and APE indicate that the soft-thresholding scheme is the best, the truncation and weighting parameters should be equal. In Hu, Yang, Li and Tong (2023), we introduced a regularized t distribution to the literature for testing high-dimensional low sample size data. With some interesting motivations, we first given a formal definition of the regularized t distribution, and then systematically studied its statistical properties including the probability density function and the moment generating function. The noncentral regularized t distribution was also introduced for computing the statistical power of hypothesis testing. For practical applications, we further proposed a regularized t-test and applied it to the gene expression detection. Simulation studies and real data analysis show that our newly introduced regularized t-test outperforms the existing competitors in a wide range of settings, in particular when the dimension is high and the sample size is small.

12303918.value: Along with the successful completion of this project, the investigators will continue to develop a series of statistical tools for analyzing high-dimensional data via a regularization approach, ranging from theory, methodology, application and software. 12304018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12304018.value: This research will examine Quaternary (the last 2.6 million years) deposits composed of nearly pure silica (cherts, opaline silica) precipitated from silica-rich waters derived at least in part from springs in the Kenya Rift Valley. Samples will be collected mainly from the central and southern parts of the rift where siliceous deposits are common, with supplementary samples available from previous studies in the Suguta Valley in northern Kenya and from core materials in the southern Kenya Rift. These areas include a variety of silica-rich deposits formed in sublacustrine to playa (saline shallow ephemeral lakes) and wetland settings, as well as in hot springs and adjacent environments. Opaline silica is also widely present in several Pleistocene and Holocene formations, where it appears to be related to permineralisation of spring-fed terrestrial ecosystems. Silica is also present as gels formed in the shore zone of one spring-fed saline lake. The research adopts four broad approaches: 1) an attempt to recognize and describe the major types of silica-rich deposits (excluding biological sediments such as diatomites) that are present in the Kenya Rift, including their physical characteristics in outcrops and hand specimens as well as their microscopic features; 2) a study of their major and trace element geochemistry, including spatial variations between spring, stream, wetland or lake settings; 3) and 4) developing models that should help to explain the formation of the silica-rich deposits that will, in turn, assist with the interpretation of similar sediments elsewhere. The project will achieve these broad aims through systematic field and laboratory studies based on known locations where silica has been deposited and through an exploration of new locations where structural factors (faults, basement trends) favour silica deposition. The deposits available include layered and massive cherts (nearly pure silica rocks), laminated stromatolitic (finely layered with possible biological influences) cherts, probably associated with shallow saline lakes. Other examples include structureless spring cherts formed below former lakes. Cherts have also formed in spring vents and in nearby spring-fed marshes and soils, with silica also accumulating in plant stems following evapotranspiration. The study will include basic descriptions of outcrop setting in relation to other deposits, field geometries of the siliceous sediments as well as their hand specimen characteristics, microscopic features and geochemistry. The resulting data will be used to develop models of deposition and the controlling factors that influence silica formation. Uranium series dating will also assist in determining the timing of deposition. 此項目研究一組位於肯亞裂谷近乎純硅質的第四紀(2.6百萬年前至今)沉積。這些主要是燧石及蛋白石質的硅質岩應最少部份為地下泉水所形成。項目會在硅質沉積普遍的裂谷中部及南部取樣，並佐以早前在北肯亞蘇古塔河谷(Sugata Valley)採集的岩樣及南肯亞裂谷的岩芯樣本。這些地點分佈的硅質沉積主要形成環境在季節性淺鹽湖的湖至湖濱、濕地、以及在溫泉及其附近。在更新世及全新世沉積中，蛋白石質硅質岩也常常出露，其形成應與由泉水支撐的生態系統的完全礦物化有關。此外，在其中一個源頭為地下泉水的鹽湖湖濱，硅質岩以硅凝膠的形式出露。 項目研究分為四個主要方向：(1)辨識及描述在肯亞裂谷的各主要硅質沉積的種類 (生物沉積如硅藻等除外)，包括其露頭及手標的物理性質以及顯微鏡下的特徵。(2) 分析各種沉積的主要及微量元素含量，從而了解其地球化學特徵在地下水泉、地表徑流、濕地及湖相環境的空間分佈。(3) 及 (4) 塑造系統模型，以協助解釋硅質沉積的形成機制，從而有助發展其他地區相似沉積的地質解釋。 研究項目將會透過以下工作達成上述目標。在已知有硅質岩形成的地點進行有系統的田野工作及實驗室分析，以及在大地構造條件(即斷層及基底岩石趨向)有利硅質沉積形成的地點探索新的出露。現時已知的沉積出露包括不分層及分層的燧石 (即接近純硅質沉積)、以及帶紋狀層理疊層石質的燧石(幼紋層及可能經生物擾動)。他們應與淺鹽湖相關。其他出露的例子包括在古湖面以下由泉水作用形成的的無結構燧石。燧石也有在泉水通道及在泉水支持的濕地及泥土中形成。硅質沉積也可以在蒸騰作用下在植物的莖部累積。 研究工作包括在沉積物出露的地點進行基本描述，剖析該些沉積與其他沉積物的關係，以及沉積物在出露點的幾何空間分佈。工作也包括取得沉積的手標及顯微鏡下的特徵以及其地球化學成分。收的資料及數據會用作發展一個解釋可能影響硅質沉積控制因素的沉積模型。項目也會進行鈾系列元素放射定年以協助確定沉積年齡。

12304018.label: Realisation of objectives
12304018.value: There were initial difficulties with progress for this project due to covid-related fieldwork cancellations that significantly delayed studies after a first successful field season. However, we were able to make progress with our initial collections supplemented by old Magadi samples and additional samples from other parts of the Kenya Rift from outcrops and cores. Research was brought back on track when further work was possible in the post-covid period and given a project extension with a final 6 months where Prof Li Jianfeng took on the role of PI following Prof Owen’s retirement. Objective 1 involved identification of different silica forms in the field with supplementary follow-up laboratory analyses. This work was fully successful and resulted in the recognition of nine major silica forms across the study region with results recently published in book chapter form (Renaut and Owen 2023, noted below). Objective 2 related to trace element variability which was explored using bulk geochemical analyses and secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) of cherts from cores. This work showed significant contrasts between otherwise superficially similar-looking cherts with SIMS results already published and a further paper on trace element variability in an early writing stage (hence the 85% estimate below) Objective 3 relates to modelling of silica/chert depositional environments. This work has been published in a series of papers, noted below, and has resulted in new insights into the formation of cherts in continental basins which should be of considerable value to researchers interested in ancient cherts elsewhere. This objective is considered fully achieved.

12304018.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304018.value: The project successfully identified silica in a variety of forms (Objective 1), including (i) opaline silica replacements, (ii) cherts in hydrothermal vents, (iii) cherts in soil profiles, (iv) cherts in marsh settings, (v) Bedded cherts with varying textures (stromatolitic, wave/current ripples etc), (vi) pillow cherts and chert dykes, (vii) silica gels, (viii) sodium silicates such as magadiite and (ix) secondary replacements (cryptocrystalline quartz, chalcedony, megaquartz). Most cherts show high 18O (+41–46‰) indicating hypersaline settings. Magadiite shows lower values (+38–40‰) with megaquartz and cherts associated with gastropods displaying even lower values ((+26–35‰), reflecting fresher waters. REE vary between different chert types with Ce and Eu anomalies, as well as high U, Th, Zr and Nb in hydrothermal cherts. SIMS data have been published (Leet at al. 2021) with trace element data still being written-up. Cherts lack evidence for a Na-silicate precursor suggested by earlier studies. Many originated from primary siliceous gels (Leet et al. 2021). Evaporite pseudomorphs indicate a soft state during accumulation with trona growth in shallow saline water. Rare examples show finely laminated microbial laminae replaced by microcrystalline quartz. Oncoids replaced by silica are found in cherts emplaced along fault ramps (Fig. 20.21a). The models developed emphasise the high silica concentrations in lakes, which is supplied from chemical weathering of volcanics, the high pH of the alkaline lake water, and silica-rich hydrothermal inflow. Precipitation of silica is related to declines in pH, to evapoconcentration, and to the cooling of thermal spring fluids. Microbes may also have been important due to their impact on CO2 and pH, but geothermal CO2 is more important in the Magadi Basin given its high flux along faults. Reduced pH lowered silica solubility. Silica then formed as a precursor of the cherts (e.g. as opaline silica, silica gel, Na-silicate). Evapoconcentration is likely also important in chert formation (see discussion in Buatois et al. 2020). Injected cherts are rare away from obvious faults suggesting they are important through control of geothermal fluids and semi-consolidated cherts. Silica injection may have occurred subaerially or in a shallow sublacustrine setting or below the contemporary land surface. Many diapiric mounds resemble bioherms. Some chert formed as sinter or geyserite mounds with laminated and bedded features including stromatolites, fossil microbes, and brecciation. The hydrothermal silica is usually non-crystalline opal-A (SiO2.nH2O) that alters to quartz during diagenesis.

12304018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304018.value: The research has generated new information on the origins and characteristics of several different chert types. Both Owen and Renaut have now retired although they are still writing as emeritus professors and will be producing more papers on the work already carried out. In terms of further development, we would see this being in the form of other researchers using these results to assist in the understanding of chert formation and chert origins in other basins and former during other time periods.

12304018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304018.value: The geological community has for many years been interested in the origins of nearly pure silica rocks called chert. There have been many types recognized prior to this study but their precise origins have often proved enigmatic. This research has provided new information on how continental cherts in particular develop and the factors that control their formation. Nine different types of chert have been recognized at Magadi and the work shows that the original salinities of the waters from which they formed can be recognized using oxygen isotopes. A range of sedimentary features preserved within most of the cherts also show that they accumulated in shallow silica-rich waters, differing from previous suggestions of deeper lake settings. Geologically recent cherts are rare, which gives the Magadi Basin in the south Kenya Rift a particular significance as a modern analogue for the formation of older chert sequences. We would expect many chert researchers to refer to this work over the coming years.

12500118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500118.value: Reward-based crowdfunding has become the most prevalent form of online crowdfunding. The market size of this innovative funding approach was US$2.68 billion globally in 2015 and it has grown exponentially in recent years (CrowdfundbeatDataCenter 2016). In a reward-based crowdfunding, the fundraisers usually provide a reward scheme, which is a list of reward options with varying funding prices, yields, and the odds of securing the yield, to project backers. Most of the researchers believe that the reward scheme is a key determinant of the reward-based crowdfunding performance (Kunz et al. 2016). They have conducted a series of studies that investigated the impact of reward scheme’s disposition (Ryu and Kim 2017). Amongst them, however, the joint impact of reward option quantity and reward option uncertainty has not been carefully examined. Thus, it creates an empirical vacuum in addressing the research question: how do reward option quantity and reward option uncertainty jointly influence reward-based crowdfunding performance? The reward-based crowdfunding performance can be assessed by examining the effectiveness of fundraising (e.g., fundraising performance), as well as the project backers’ decision-making experience of backing the project (e.g., participation performance) (Du and Wang 2016). Specifically, the reward option quantity and uncertainty are two important antecedents of the crowdfunding performance (Mollick 2014). During the project backers’ decision-making process, the reward option uncertainty could increase their cognitive cost in choosing the preferred option, thus influencing the crowdfunding performance (Pavlou et al. 2007). However, prior literature did not clearly identify the project backers’ decision-making behavior in selecting a reward option under different reward option quantity conditions. This empirical gap impedes scholars and practitioners alike from identifying the deliberate design of the reward scheme that could potentially maximize the crowdfunding performance. Thus, the investigation of the proposed research question could significantly improve our theoretical understanding of the underlying mechanism of the joint impact, which has been largely overlooked in the extant crowdfunding literature. In this project, we adopt the theoretical underpinning of the assortment research and human’s decision-making to conduct a series of studies. The multi-method approach will be applied. Based on the empirical investigations, we will highlight the practical implications for fundraisers and service providers in Hong Kong (but not limited to this area) who are currently engaging in online crowdfunding or contemplating such a move. In addition, the practical implication on designing the reward scheme in crowdfunding would also serve as an important strategic tool for commercial and research purposes. 基於獎勵的眾籌（簡稱為“獎勵眾籌”）已經成為了一種最流行的在線眾籌形式。 2015年，獎勵眾籌的全球市場規模為26.8億美元，且近年來呈指數規模地增長。在獎勵眾籌項目中，籌款人通常會提供一個獎勵計劃給眾籌支持者。這個獎勵計劃是一個獎勵選項列表，其中的每一個選項包括了不同的資金價格，收益率以及確保收益率的可能性。研究人員認為獎勵計劃的設計是獎勵眾籌業績表現的關鍵決定因素。 然而，獎勵選項數量和獎勵收益不確定性的聯合影響尚未經過仔細研究。因此，本研究項目探索的研究問題是：獎勵選項數量和獎勵收益不確定性如何共同影響獎勵眾籌的業績表現？ 獎勵眾籌的業績表現可以通過分析籌款的有效性（例如籌款表現）以及項目支持者支持項目的決策經驗（例如參與表現）來評估。具體而言，獎勵選項數量和獎勵收益不確定性是眾籌業績表現的兩個重要前提。在項目支持者的決策過程中，獎勵收益不確定性可能會增加他們在選擇首選方案時的認知成本，從而影響眾籌的業績表現。然而，先前的文獻沒有清楚地確定項目支持者在不同選項數量條件下選擇獎勵選項時的決策行為。這阻礙了學者和從業者識別有效地最大化眾籌業績表現的獎勵計劃設計。因此，對擬議研究問題的研究可以顯著提高我們對聯合影響潛在機制的理論認識。 在這個項目中，我們將採用分類設計研究和人類決策理論基礎進行一系列多方法研究。我們會強調此項目對香港（但不限於此地區）的籌款人及服務提供者的實際意義。此外，本項目將體現眾籌中設計獎勵計劃如何成為實現商業價值的一種重要戰略工具。

12500118.label: Realisation of objectives
12500118.value: After conducting a series of studies, the majority of the proposed research objectives have been largely addressed. However, due to the social unrest and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019 and 2020, some laboratory experiments that require participants to attend the experimental session in person, as well as the field study, were not able to be done. Thus, the second and third research objectives are not fully addressed. The key findings are summarized below, with an explanation of how these research findings realize the research objectives of this project. Research objective 1: To understand the theoretical mechanism of the joint impact of reward option quantity and uncertainty on reward-based crowdfunding performance. Answer: This research objective has been largely addressed. Anchored on the theories of assortment decisions, we found that the participants of the reward-based crowdfunding project have the bounded processing capacity to estimate the effect of the number of the reward options for influencing the performance of the crowdfunding project. Thus, the number of options has an inverted U-shaped relationship with the participants’ decision on supporting a crowdfunding project. In addition, we investigated the uncertainty of the reward option and its impact on the performance of the crowdfunding project. In specific, we examined the lottery-based reward option, namely, the participants receive the reward with a certain probability (a similar mechanism of lottery) in the crowdfunding context. We found the participants of crowdfunding would be influenced by the reward option with high uncertainty (the lottery option) because participants of crowdfunding projects are considered to be more risk-seeking and variety-seeking than conventional consumers. As a result, the potential of receiving a high level of payback of the lottery option in the crowdfunding would attract participants to engage the crowdfunding project, thus enhancing the performance of the crowdfunding project. Research objective 2: To apply the results of Objective 1 in the consideration of the reward scheme design of the reward-based crowdfunding and to examine the impacts of scheme design by using experiment. Answer: This research objective has been partially addressed (approximately 80% completion). We examined the impacts of the reward scheme design on the performance of crowdfunding projects with the focus on investigating the quantity of the reward options. In specific, we found the number of reward options has an inverted U-shaped relationship with the crowdfunding project’s performance. It is because of a negative impact of the number of options on the participants’ backing centroid. We also found that the impact of the reward scheme design is decoupled with the impact of participants’ willingness to invest, and the participants’ perception of fundraisers’ thoroughness, informedness, or engagement. Particularly, our findings showed that different types of reward scheme design would influence the participants’ search scope and search depth. As such, participants’ backing centroid would be influenced, thus making an impact on the performance of the crowdfunding project. We also examined the impact of a reward scheme design with versus without the lottery option to gauge the uncertainty issue of the reward option. The findings showed that the reward scheme with a lottery option is beneficial to the participants' performance of crowdfunding projects. However, its impacts on the fundraising performance of crowdfunding campaigns are sophisticated, depending on the timing of delivery of the lottery option to the potential participants. Furthermore, the inclusion of the lottery option in the reward scheme design has a cannibalization effect on the potential participants’ selection of other types of options in a reward scheme. We could have done additional examinations on a different level of uncertainties (e.g., with multiple options that contain varying probabilities of receiving a reward) in the laboratory experiments. However, I found it was not possible to conduct the experiments during the period of social unrest and the COVID-19 pandemic. The unprecedented difficulties impeded me from collecting more data from individuals directly through the laboratory experiments, or the experiment with NeuroIS methods. Now the social unrest has been ceased and the COVID-19 pandemic has been largely contained in Hong Kong. I hope we can resume the laboratory experiments in compliance with the social distancing policy as soon as possible. Research objective 3: To apply the results of Objectives 1 and 2 in the real reward-based crowdfunding campaign for a large-scale empirical investigation. This will be followed by a discussion of the empirical and practical implications. Answer: As scheduled, we could have conducted a large-scale empirical investigation in 2020. Unfortunately, this research objective has not been effectively addressed because the second research objective was not completely fulfilled. In addition, it was very difficult to persuade practitioners of the crowdfunding vendors to collaborate with us to conduct a large-scale empirical investigation on reward-based crowdfunding because the local and global economy has been severely undermined by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The majority of the firms are in survival mode with a low level of interest in experimenting with the novel design of the crowdfunding project. Now the COVID-19 pandemic has been effectively contained due to the collaboration of the community and the Hong Kong government. I hope that we can find a pertinent collaborator in the industry to conduct the field study in the near future. It would significantly benefit the development of crowdfunding as an effective financial technology to bring positive outcomes to society.

12500118.label: Major findings and research outcome
12500118.value: After conducting seven studies that revolve around the topic of investigating the impact of reward option quantity and uncertainty on crowdfunding performance, we have the following key research outcomes and research findings. First, we found the participants’ reward-based crowdfunding project will leverage their mental backing centroid to evaluate and make the decision on supporting the crowdfunding project. Importantly, this mechanism is decoupled from the impact of the disposition of a crowdfunding project, such as the number of images or the number of options, is the manifestation of fundraisers’ characteristics. This finding is also corroborated by an eye-tracking experiment, thus confirming the number of reward options influences the participants’ search scope and depth. We reported these research findings in a journal paper published in the leading IS journal, Information & Management. [Zhao, D., Li, M., and Wang, K.L. 2019. “’The More Options, the Better?’ Investigating the Impact of the Number of Options on Backers’ Decisions in Reward-based Crowdfunding Projects”. Information & Management (56:3), pp. 429-444.] Second, we found the uncertainty of the reward option design would significantly influence the performance of the crowdfunding project. A crowdfunding project that has the reward option containing the probability of receiving a reward would outperform the others that don’t. On one hand, the lottery option is beneficial to increase the number of funds raised. On the other hand, it has a detrimental effect on the time to achieve crowdfunding success and the success of crowdfunding campaigns. Moreover, we found the inclusion of a lottery option in the reward scheme has a cannibalization effect on the potential participants’ selection of other options in a reward scheme. We reported these findings in a journal paper published in the leading IS journal, Information & Management. [Zhao, D., Wang, K.L., and Li, M. 2019. “Promoting Crowdfunding with Lottery: The Impact on Campaign Performance”. Information & Management (56:8), 103159.] Third, we also extended our investigation to other types of crowdfunding projects, such as charitable crowdfunding. We examined how the inclusion of self-donation influences the performance of charitable crowdfunding and leveraged the warm-glow theory to explain the underlying mechanism. We reported our research findings in a conference proceeding paper [Du, Z., Wang, K., and Li, M. 2020. “Can Self-Donation Improve the Project Performance? The Impacts of Self-Donation in Charitable Crowdfunding,” in Proceedings of the 41st Annual International Conference on Information Systems (ICIS), India.]

12500118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12500118.value: Based on the current research findings, further development of the research may follow two directions: (1) Extend the research context from reward-based crowdfunding to other types of crowdfunding, such as charitable crowdfunding, equity-based crowdfunding. As our research findings indicate, the nature of the crowdfunding project may significantly influence the participants’ mental mechanism of processing the information in the reward scheme (or selection scheme). As a result, participants may behave differently when facing the different levels of quantity and uncertainty of the option. (2) Conduct the study in different social-economic environments. Cultural cognition theory states that individuals’ mental processing has been significantly influenced by cultural worldviews. Thus, participants with varying cultural worldviews may apply the different methods to mentally process the quantity and uncertainty of the options in crowdfunding projects. Thus, it may moderate the influences on crowdfunding performance. Future studies would collect the data in different countries to investigate this issue further.

12500118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12500118.value: By investigating how the number of the reward options provided in a crowdfunding project, as well as the likelihood of receiving the claimed reward of choosing the option, influences the performance of crowdfunding campaigns, this research project provides an insightful understanding of the mechanism of such impact. We found the quantity of reward options has an inverted U-shaped relationship with the performance of crowdfunding. Moreover, the inclusion of uncertainty-oriented options, such as the lottery option, would deliver varying impacts on the crowdfunding performance with the consideration of the timing and the scale. The research findings would significantly enhance our knowledge on how the design of the reward option (or the selection) scheme influences crowdfunding performance. This research project would provide meaningful implications to the research on financial technology such as individuals’ behavior of participating in online crowdfunding. This research project would also benefit the crowdfunding vendors on how to design an effective reward option scheme.

12500318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500318.value: As established by the World Health Organization and the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (previously Millennium Development Goals), maternal and infant mortality represent major concerns in developing and developed countries. Management of maternal and infant health is complex because it involves the need for (a) professional medical care, which is limited in some contexts and (b) developing and maintaining self-care healthy behaviors. Further, non-communicable or chronic diseases and poverty worldwide augment maternal and infant health issues. With the spread of technologies worldwide, mHealth applications are becoming promising interventions for managing health. However, prior work has focused mainly on the initial adoption of mHealth by examining shorter periods of use and at a broad level without a clear understanding of the utility of particular features. With health situations that are long term, such as chronic diseases, pregnancy, and the first few years from child birth, it is important to understand how mHealth applications are used at the feature level for managing health in different contexts. Our project aims to study the use of mHealth applications for managing complex maternal and infant health conditions in urban poor populations, who are significantly economically disadvantaged, within different geographical locations. We develop a nuanced view of technology use at the feature level. We build on our existing pilot work on mHealth applications by examining how (a) use of features, which we identify inductively based on the design to support particular goals and test using a deductive approach, affect health outcomes and (b) several health and cultural contingencies shape the effects of feature use on health outcomes over time. We will use a longitudinal investigation to track pregnancy and infant health after birth in Hong Kong and the U.S. We focus on two countries to conduct comparative analysis based of different healthcare systems and examine the generalizability of our findings. With the ability to get rich data about mHealth use and health outcomes, we will apply explanatory and predictive analytical approaches to unearth interesting patterns in using mHealth applications and their effectiveness in managing health. We expect that our work will (a) contribute to the literature on healthcare and (b) offer courses of action for the success of mHealth applications.

12500318.label: Realisation of objectives
12500318.value: Objective 1 We developed a theory model of effective use of mHealth applications (see Research Outcome 1). We draw upon two theoretical perspectives that inform the development of our contextualized model: effective use (Burton-Jones and Grange 2013) and health disparity based on the income and race of expectant mothers. In the context of maternal mHealth apps, we (a) developed a contingency model of effective use of mHealth apps from the perspective of expectant mothers encountering income and racial health disparity and (b) developed an instrument for measuring the dimensions of effective use, as effective use focuses on using the system in a way that helps attain the goals of the system, goals vary by context, and different features can be designed to accomplish the overarching goal of managing maternal health, and this instrument was used to empirically test the model in two separate field studies. Our model incorporates the context of underprivileged expectant mothers in general and women of color in particular to examine the effects of the three dimensions of effective use on outcomes and identify heterogeneity that stems from the race of underprivileged expectant mothers. Our instrument development incorporates the context of maternal health to capture the overarching domain of pregnancy management in our operationalization of transparent interaction, representation fidelity, and informed action with getting tips, tracking, and communication features. With our measurement and empirical approaches, effective use produced different impacts on utilitarian, i.e., effectiveness and efficiency, and affective, i.e., satisfaction, outcomes that varied based on the race of expectant mothers. Hence, our findings demonstrate the value of contextualizing effective use of mHealth apps at the feature level by capturing the overarching domain of maternal health and unraveling heterogeneity in the population of underprivileged expectant mothers. Objective 2 The TEU posits that accomplishing the desired goal, i.e., pregnancy management, requires accessing the content needed, obtaining representations needed, and leveraging faithful representations. Hence, the initial wording was formed to reflect the three aspects of effective use in relation to the identified pregnancy management use functions. In other words, we developed initial scales based on the features of maternal mHealth applications as such features reflect the nature and purpose of the application of interest. For example, providing information about pregnancy tips has been incorporated into the three dimensions to capture the extent to which the user perceives difficulty in obtaining pregnancy tips, i.e., transparent interaction, the extent to which the user perceives that the content on pregnancy tips is complete, i.e., representation fidelity, and the extent to which the user acts upon the obtained pregnancy tips, i.e., informed action. The performance dimensions were worded to reflect the effectiveness and efficiency of the mHealth application in pregnancy management. We mapped the context-specific goals of managing maternal health to the illustrative measures that were proposed by Burton-Jones and Grange (2013). Regarding representation fidelity, for instance, Burton-Jones and Grange (2013) suggested evaluating the system’s ability to provide content that is complete, clear, correct, and meaningful. We mapped those evaluation aspects to content that is relevant to managing maternal health (e.g., medication safety, fetal development, fluid intake). This process produced 40 items that capture the most important aspects of the three dimensions, effectiveness, and efficiency. The design features and contextual contingencies have been included in our investigation (see Research Outcome 1). Objective 3 To rule out alternative explanations of the observed effects on pregnancy outcomes, we collected data from a third group of expectant mothers (n=300) who did not use any mHealth apps for managing maternal health. We used the same professional firm to hire this group of expectant mothers. The average age of expectant mothers in this group was 38, with a standard deviation of 5.6 years. The number of prior births was 2.55 with a standard deviation of 1.36. The majority of expectant mothers completed high school and earned an average annual household income of 22,000 USD. About 80% of expectant mothers resided in locations that were less than 10 miles to primary care and 42% resided in locations that were less than 10 miles to specialty care. Finally, 12% of expectant mothers had chronic diseases. The results suggested that expectant mothers who used mHealth apps experienced fewer complications with pregnancy than those who did not use any mHealth app for managing maternal health, i.e., the control group. To examine whether differences between the control group and each of the intervention groups are significant, we created contingency tables and conducted the Fisher’s test of independence on the binary outcomes and t-test for the continuous outcome. The results suggest that the control group and each of the intervention groups were significantly different in the outcomes. Objective 4 From a design perspective, our findings on user heterogeneity can help shape DEI plans for better maternal health for women of color by guiding developers with the design process, content, and assessment of relevant interventions. As scholars note in a recent discourse, practitioners continue to struggle with developing and disseminating interventions that embrace DEI visions, and IS researchers need to tackle this struggle to influence practices and policies that involve important societal outcomes (Sarker 2023). The finding on the weaker effects among women of color suggests a design focus that should go beyond incorporating valid content that could be accessed easily and leveraged throughout the entire duration of pregnancy. Designers could incorporate content through key features like getting tips, tracking, and communication, but the design process needs to be inclusive to ensure equity by addressing challenges and needs that are unique to women of color. Hence, our findings inform practitioners’ thinking about how to enhance the design of technologies and apps. For instance, in cooperation with healthcare professionals and psychologists, designers may conduct more focus groups to elicit user requirements that represent subgroups within a particular user population. As for the assessment, our instrument enables designers to assess the effectiveness of and satisfaction with their app design. Although the measurement approach in this work focuses on content use rather than specific design elements, the instrument will be useful when combined with existing instruments for mobile app usability (e.g., Hoehle and Venkatesh 2015) to obtain patient views—an area that is becoming increasingly critical for developing and disseminating effective patient engagement interventions. For instance, developers will need to decompose their designs and test components, such as tips, tracking, and communication, individually so that they can better identify design issues that might hinder transparent interaction, representation fidelity, and informed action. Our measurement approach will be especially useful for mHealth apps because of the criticality of the content in managing maternal health. For example, maternal deaths in the U.S. are mostly attributed to heart problems and chronic conditions. Hence, developers should focus on designs that emphasize accessing tips, i.e., transparent interaction, protecting against such disorders, and avoiding complications during pregnancy. The courses of action and guidelines can be extended to the context of EDI (see Research Outcome 1). Additionally, a longitudinal online survey was conducted to collect data from pregnant women with experience in using mobile maternal apps in China. The study examined how self-regulated features of mobile maternal apps influence their psychological and physical well-being (see Research Outcome 2).

12500318.label: Major findings and research outcome
12500318.value: In the first paper (Research Outcome 1), we develop a contextualized model of effective use of maternal mHealth apps that identifies user heterogeneity as a key contingency among underprivileged expectant mothers. User heterogeneity that stems from the race of underprivileged expectant mothers could have competing effects such that the direct impacts of the effective use of mHealth apps on the effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction of/with these apps are either strengthened or weakened. The impacts may be stronger for women of color, as the mHealth app is an opportunity to cope with racial health disparity and overcome the burden of accessing professional care; alternatively, a competing hypothesis is that the impacts may be weaker for women of color, as the mHealth app is a constraint that reflects equality in accessing care rather than equity that addresses their unique needs. Second, we identify the overarching goals of mHealth apps for managing maternal health with key features to develop an instrument for measuring the effective use of these apps. In two field studies at a safety-net hospital (n=381 and n=410 expectant mothers), we validated the instrument and tested a model that includes the race of underprivileged expectant mothers over the duration of their entire pregnancy. The scales exhibited good psychometric properties and the model suggested positive impacts of effective use that are contingent on race such that the impacts become weaker for underprivileged women of color. Our findings provide insights that can guide the development and dissemination of inclusive interventions and regulations to improve maternal health in underprivileged groups, thus speaking to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) goals in healthcare and IS research and practice. This paper is built upon the insight from the first Research Outcome and adopts a theory-driven foundation to identify mobile health apps’ features. Rather than using the EDI perspective, we examine the use of mobile maternal apps for pregnant women in China. In the second paper (Research Outcome 2), we adopt a self-regulatory perspective on goal-setting to examine how self-regulated features of mobile maternal apps on pregnant women’s well-being in China. Both the self-analysis feature and self-judgment feature have a significant impact on pregnant women’s psychological well-being and physical well-being. Self-reminder feature only has a significant effect on psychological well-being.

12500318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12500318.value: Several potential future research directions can be explored: Future research can delve deeper into understanding the specific factors that contribute to these varying impacts and explore how different subgroups within the population may experience different outcomes. We can also explore the role of cultural factors (e.g., cultural beliefs, values, and norms) in the effective use of mHealth apps among pregnant women. This could provide valuable insights into designing app features and interventions for specific cultural needs. Both research outcomes focused on the immediate impacts of mHealth app usage on maternal health. Future research could explore the long-term effects of using these apps throughout the pregnancy journey and beyond. This could include assessing the sustainability of positive impacts, tracking postpartum health outcomes, and examining the potential for behavior change maintenance through continued app usage. While the research outcomes focused on the effectiveness of mHealth apps, future research could examine the usability and accessibility aspects of these apps. This could involve evaluating the user interface, design features, and language options to ensure that mHealth apps are user-friendly and accessible to diverse populations, including those with low digital literacy or limited access to technology.

12500318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12500318.value: This research project focuses on the use of mobile health applications (mHealth apps) to improve maternal health, especially among underprivileged expectant mothers. The goal is to understand how these apps can be effectively used and their impact on the well-being of pregnant women, considering factors like race and income disparities. Our results showed that the impacts of using mHealth apps may be stronger for women of color, as it can help them overcome racial health disparities and access professional care. However, there is also a competing hypothesis that suggests the impacts may be weaker for women of color, as the apps may not fully address their unique needs. This project also identified the main goals of mHealth apps for managing maternal health and developed a tool to measure the effectiveness of these apps. The results showed that effective use of mHealth apps had positive impacts, but these impacts were weaker for underprivileged women of color. Overall, this research provides valuable insights that can help improve the development and use of mHealth apps for underprivileged expectant mothers. It contributes to the goals of EDI in healthcare and research, aiming to improve maternal health outcomes for all women, especially those facing challenges.

12500418.value: 入境年齡，經濟同化和社會融合：來自香港童年移民的證據

12500418.label: Project Objectives
12500418.value: To document the native-childhood immigrant differentials in socioeconomic outcomes and their intertemporal changes using census microdata. To extend the reweighting procedure developed by DiNardo, Fortin, and Lemieux (1996) to further incorporate the age-of-entry dimension in decomposing the intertemporal changes in measures of socioeconomic outcomes for childhood immigrants. To apply this extended reweighting approach to decompose the intertemporal changes in the native-childhood immigrant differences in the distribution of the relevant socioeconomic outcomes in Hong Kong after its handover to China. To discuss the policy implications of the research findings for Hong Kong's population policy.

12500418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500418.value: This project aims to study the effect of the age of entry of childhood immigrants on their economic assimilation and social integration in Hong Kong. Using the census microdata, we will utilize the educational attainment and earnings differentials of childhood immigrants to natives to measure economic assimilation, and employ the incidence of intermarriage and differences in spouse’s socioeconomic status and childbearing behaviors to measure social integration. In particular, this project will demonstrate the delay in the age of entry of childhood immigrants after the handover of Hong Kong to China and evaluate the resulting consequences on their economic assimilation and social integration. In other contexts of international migration, for adaptation to the receiving society immigrants need to overcome racial, ethnic and linguistic obstacles, all of which involve the role of age of entry. Since the vast majority of immigrants to Hong Kong are from Mainland China and share the same race, ethnicity and (written) languages as Hong Kong natives, this project can better disentangle the roles of age of entry that are less confounded by its interactions with the racial, ethnic and linguistic background of immigrants. 該課題旨在研究香港童年移民的入境年齡對他們經濟同化和社會融合的影響。使用人口普查微觀數據，我們將利用童年移民相對本地出生人口的教育程度和收入的差異來衡量經濟同化，並應用他們與本地出生人口的通婚率，生育行為以及配偶的社會經濟地位相對本地出生人口的差異來衡量社會融合。本課題將提供兒童移民入境年齡在香港回歸中國後推遲的實證證據並評估入境年齡推遲對這些童年移民經濟同化和社會融合的影響。在其他跨境移民的背景下，移民需要克服種族，民族和語言的障礙以適應新的社會環境，所有這些途徑入境年齡都在其中起到重要作用。因為香港的絕大多數移民都是來自中國大陸，他們和本地出生的人口同膚色，同種族，有共同的（書面）語言，本課題可以更好地分解出入境年齡的直接作用，使之較少參雜移民的種族，民和語言背景差異的影響。

12500418.label: Realisation of objectives
12500418.value: 1. We obtained the micro data sets of the Hong Kong censuses or by-censuses for 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011, and 2016. We defined natives as Hong Kong born and childhood immigrants as those born in Mainland China but had arrived in Hong Kong before age 13. We defined our analysis sample as natives and childhood immigrants born between 1979 and 1993. We documented the changes in the native-childhood immigrant differentials in educational attainment and earnings across birth cohorts, and also documented the evolution of the age-of-entry for childhood immigrants. 2. We extended the reweighting procedure to further incorporate the age-of-entry dimension in decomposing the intertemporal changes in native-immigrant differentials in educational attainments and earnings. Specifically, we first decompose the intertemporal changes in native-immigrant differentials in earnings into a relative endowment change effect attributable to their differences in the changes in endowments and a relative wage change effect attributable to differences in the changes in labour market returns to skills. Furthermore, for the immigrant subsample, we further develop a reweighting approach to perform a detailed decomposition of the relative endowment change effect into that attributable to the relative change in educational attainment conditional on the age-of-entry and that attributable to the change in age-of-entry itself. 3. We first applied the reweighting approach to decompose the intertemporal changes in the native-childhood immigrant differentials in educational attainments and earnings in Hong Kong into a relative wage change effect and a relative endowment change effect. Then, we further applied the extended reweighting approach that we developed in this paper to decompose the relative endowment effect into the relative educational attainment change effect and the age-of-entry change effect. 4. Our research findings have important implications concerning Hong Kong’s population policy. Given that the majority of the childhood immigrants in our sample would be children of Hong Kong permanent residents who would be admitted into Hong Kong anyway. The resulting delays in the age-of-entry of these childhood immigrants due to the quota system, particularly its tightening in the mid-1980s, led to substantial welfare losses of these immigrants in terms of educational attainments and earnings.

12500418.label: Major findings and research outcome
12500418.value: In Zhang and Zhu (2022), we document abrupt changes in the age-of-entry of Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong who had arrived in Hong Kong before age 13 (hereafter childhood immigrants), and relate these changes to the legislative changes in quota of the one-way-permit (OWP) scheme. Meanwhile, we also document hump-shaped patterns for the evolution of native-childhood immigrant differentials in educational attainments and earnings, both of which move in the same direction along the changes in the immigrants’ age-of-entry. The fact that native-childhood immigrant earnings gap moves in the same direction along the changes in the age-of-entry of childhood immigrants motivates us to quantify the role played by changes in the age-at-arrival of childhood immigrants in the evolution of native-childhood immigrant differentials in earnings. Applying an extended reweighting procedure developed in our paper, we find that the delayed age-of-entry for childhood immigrants born 1984-1988, who face the longest queuing time for their entry permit application due to the tightening of the OWP quota in 1983, alone accounts for over one-third of the widening of their mean earnings gap to natives compared to their precedents born 1979-1983. Though much smaller in magnitude, the reduced age-at-entry for childhood immigrants born 1989-1993, who benefited from the relaxing of the OWP quota after 1993, also accounts for nearly one-tenth of the narrowing of their mean earnings gap to natives compared to their precedents born 1984-1988.

12500418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12500418.value: We identify two areas for potential further development of research. 1. We can further extend the reweighting approach to examine the roles of changes in the age-of-entry on the native-childhood immigrant differentials in the entire earnings distribution. 2. We can also extend the analysis to compare the effects of age-of-entry on the socioeconomic assimilation of female childhood immigrants in addition to males.

12500418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12500418.value: The 2006-2016 period witnessed an unusual evolution of the early-career earnings gap between natives and childhood immigrants in Hong Kong. Among 23- to 27-year-old males, the mean earnings gap first almost tripled from about 7.5% in 2006 to 20.9% in 2011, but more than halved thereafter to 9.5% in 2016. Coincide with these changes in the intergroup earnings differential is the hump-shaped evolution of the age-of-entry of childhood immigrants: conditional on having arrived in Hong Kong before age 13, the mean age-of-entry for childhood immigrants increased by 2.5 years for the 1984-1988 birth cohorts compared to their precedents born 1979-1984, owing to the legislative reduction of the one-way permit scheme quota from 150 to 75 per day in 1983. Our decomposition analysis shows that the delayed age-of-entry for the 1984-1988 birth cohorts account for over one-third of the observed widening of their mean earnings gap to natives compared to their precedents born 1979-1984 who had arrived in Hong Kong at earlier ages. Moreover, we also find that when the OWP quota increased subsequently after 1993, the native-childhood immigrant earnings gap also narrowed.

12501618.label: Project Objectives
12501618.value: We will manually collect the identities of auditors from the Capital IQ database, and construct a complete dataset of PCAOB inspections around the world. We try to establish the causal relation between PCAOB international inspection and firms’ foreign institutional ownership by adopting a DiD research design. In cross-sectional analyses, we investigate whether the link between PCAOB inspection and foreign institutional ownership varies with the presence of a strong local regulatory oversight, legal institutions, disclosure institutions, and firms’ information environment. We perform a bunch of additional analyses to substantiate our inference.

12501618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501618.value: Institutional investors are known to underinvest in stocks of foreign firms, as referred to the “home bias puzzle” (French and Poterba, 1991; Coval and Moskowitz, 1999; Chan, Covrig, and Ng, 2005). This study explores the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) international inspection program as an exogenous shock to the stringency of public auditor regulatory oversight. We examine whether a stricter auditor regulatory oversight alleviates the bias that institutional investors exhibit on foreign investments. Specifically, we focus on a sample of international firms that are audited by non-U.S. auditors and adopt a differences-in-differences (DiD) research design. We test whether these firms attract more foreign institutional ownership if their auditors are subject to PCAOB international inspection. Prior studies find that PCAOB international inspections improve audit quality of foreign auditors (Lamoreaux, 2016; Fung, Raman, and Zhu, 2017; Krishnan, Krishnan, and Song, 2017). Literature in home bias has shown that better financial report quality and information environment play important roles in mitigating institutional investors’ bias towards domestic investments (Kang and Stulz, 1997; Dahlquist and Robertsson, 2001; Jeske, 2001; Young and Guenther, 2003; Ahearne, Griever, and Warnock, 2004; Bradshaw, Bushee, and Miller, 2004; Portes and Rey, 2005; Covrig, DeFond, and Huang 2007). As such, we predict that institutional investors will value the additional monitoring and improved audit quality brought about by PCAOB inspections and thus they will be more likely to hold stocks of foreign firms whose auditors are exposed to PCAOB inspections. In cross-sectional analyses, we intend to isolate whether and how the impact of PCAOB international inspection on foreign institutional ownership varies with the presence of a strong local audit oversight system, the strength of legal institutions and disclosure standards in firms’ home countries, and firms’ information environment. This study differs from extant PCAOB inspection literature by investing its impact on firms’ foreign institutional ownership, which is unexplored in prior studies. We complement and extend the recent evidence on the positive externality of PCAOB inspection. Finally, our study contributes the literature examining how accounting choice or accounting regulation impacts institutional investor home bias.
