Finally, our study contributes the literature examining how accounting choice or accounting regulation impacts institutional investor home bias. 眾所周知,機構投資者對外國公司的股票投資不足,我們稱這種行為為「本土偏好之謎」(French and Poterba,1991; Coval and Moskowitz,1999; Chan,Covrig,and Ng,2005)。 本研究探討了上市公司會計監督委員會(PCAOB)國際檢查計畫,認為這是對公共審計監管監督嚴格性的外部衝擊。 我們研究了更嚴格的審計監管監督是否減輕了機構投資者對外國投資的偏見。 具體而言,我們關注的是由非美國審計師審計的國際公司樣本並採用DiD研究設計。 如果他們的審計員接受PCAOB國際檢查,我們測試這些公司是否會吸引更多的外國機構擁有權。 之前的研究發現,PCAOB國際檢查提高了外國審計師的審計品質(Lamoreaux,2016; Fung,Raman and Zhu,2017; Krishnan,Krishnan, and Song,2017)。 本土偏見的文獻表明,更好的財務報告品質和資訊環境在降低機構投資者對國內投資的偏好方面發揮著重要作用(Kang and Stulz,1997; Dahlquist and Robertsson,2001; Jeske,2001; Young and Guenther,2003; Ahearne ,Griever and Warnock,2004; Bradshaw,Bushee, and Miller,2004; Portes and Rey,2005; Covrig,DeFond, and Huang,2007)。 因此,我們預測機構投資者將重視PCAOB檢查帶來的額外監控和提高審計品質,因此他們更有可能持有審計員接受PCAOB檢查的外國公司的股票。 在橫斷面試驗中,我們打算分析PCAOB國際檢查對外國機構擁有權的影響是否以及如何隨著強大的地方審計監督體系,法律機構的強度和公司本國的披露標準的存在以及企業的資訊環境而變化。 這項研究與現有的PCAOB檢查文獻不同,它將研究PCAOB對公司的外國機構擁有權的影響,這在以前的研究中是未被探索過的。 我們補充並擴展了最近關於PCAOB檢查的正外部性的證據。 最後,我們的研究對有關會計選擇或會計監管如何影響機構投資者本土偏見的文獻有一定貢獻。

12501618.label: Realisation of objectives
12501618.value: My co-authors and I have achieved all the above-listed four project objectives in a recent paper “Does the Threat of a PCAOB Inspection Mitigate US Institutional Investors’ Home Bias?”, which was formally published in Contemporary Accounting Research in the Winter of 2021. This publication is based on the combination of two research projects (the current project no. 12501618 and the other project no. 11502017). In this paper, we mainly document a strong positive impact of the PCAOB international inspection on US institutional ownership in the US-listed foreign firms (project no. 11502017) as well the non-US-listed foreign firms (project no. 12501618). Although these two research projects are related, as explained in more detail in the publication, they involve different research questions, sample constructions, and empirical executives. Initially we indeed separately worked on the two research projects. However, the editor and reviewers asked us to undertake both main analyses in the two research projects in one single paper during the revision process at Contemporary Accounting Research. Unfortunately, we must follow the editor’s and reviewers’ suggestions by combining the two research projects into one single paper. Nevertheless, below I detail how we achieve each of the above four project objectives in the current research proposal. First, to examine whether and how PCAOB international inspection impacts US institutional ownership in non-US-listed foreign firms, we manually identify the names of all the non-US-listed firms’ auditors from the S&P Capital IQ database. This involves applying a research design similar to Fung et al. (2017) and Shroff (2020), who examine the impact of actual PCAOB inspections. We follow prior research by extracting all non-US-listed firm-year observations from Compustat Global and Compustat North America (the latter for Canadian companies). Like Aobdia and Shroff (2017), we collect the names of these firms’ auditors from S&P Capital IQ and restrict our sample to firms from countries with at least one PCAOB inspected auditor. The names of international auditors are manually checked and identified because they are often miscoded in Compustat Global (Francis and Wang, 2008; Aobdia and Shroff 2017; Fung et al., 2017). Global institutional holding data are extracted from the FactSet/LionShares database, as it covers the most comprehensive institutional holdings data in the world (Ferreira and Matos, 2008). The final sample period ranges from 1999 to 2015 for this research project. Second, the staggered introduction of the PCAOB inspection regime in different countries at different times allows us to adopt a company and year fixed effects model. As detailed in Bertrand and Mullainathan (2003), Bertrand et al. (2004), and Roberts and Whited (2013), a company fixed effects model with time indicators in settings of staggered law implementation represents a traditional DID research design. We implement this empirical strategy as our main regression model to help establish the causal relation between PCAOB international inspection and firms’ foreign institutional ownership. When extending our analysis to local companies audited by auditors that are subject to the PCAOB inspection threat, we control for any change in a country’s institutional environment/policy across years through the addition of Country * Year fixed effects to these cross-country regressions to further alleviate the endogeneity concern. Complementing Fung et al.’s (2017) and Shroff’s (2020) research on actual inspections, we find strong, robust evidence implying spillover audit quality benefits to non-US auditors’ clients that are not listed in the United States—that is, the home bias that US institutional investors exhibit for non-US-listed clients subsides when their auditors are subject to the PCAOB inspection threat. Overall, the results corroborate our main evidence that US institutional investors perceive—evident in adjustments to their investment portfolios—that the PCAOB’s international inspection program engenders higher audit quality. Third, in cross-sectional analysis, we show that the benefit of the PCAOB inspection threat in constraining US institutional investors’ home bias is concentrated in foreign countries without a strict local auditor oversight system. We also document that the importance of the PCAOB inspection threat to mitigating home bias is concentrated in active US institutional investors relative to their passive counterparts. In addition, we find that the impact of the PCAOB inspection threat on alleviating US institutional investor home bias only applies to firms from countries that grant PCAOB access later—that is, after the onset of the inspection program in 2005 (late adopters). Following the editor’s and the reviewers’ comments, we have removed the cross-sectional tests on the legal institutions, disclosure institutions, and firms’ information environment from the paper as the empirical findings are not that straightforward. Fourth, we undertake several additional analyses that further corroborate our main findings. The parallel trends assumption is critical to drawing reliable inferences from a DID research design in that the treatment and control firms should follow parallel trends absent the PCAOB inspection access. Concerns that may violate the parallel trends assumption include that there may be an upward trend in US institutional ownership in US-listed and non-US-listed foreign firms even before inspection access occurs. For example, a country may elect to become more friendly to US investors by initiating other changes to their institutional infrastructure preceding or concurrent to granting PCAOB inspection access. We rely on three techniques to confront this endogeneity concern: estimating a dynamic effects model, employing a matched sample approach, and conducting a falsification test. We also run a path analysis, which verifies that the impact of PCAOB inspection access on home bias works through improved audit/financial reporting quality.

12501618.label: Major findings and research outcome
12501618.value: We exploit the staggered introduction of the PCAOB’s international inspection program to examine the role that the stringency of public audit oversight plays in shaping US institutional investors’ home bias. Analyzing a sample of US-listed firms and a sample of non-US-listed foreign firms, we evaluate whether US institutional investors hold larger equity stakes in these firms—a longstanding issue that reflects investor portfolio decisions—if their auditors are exposed to the threat of a PCAOB inspection. In a differences-in-differences framework, we find that both US-listed and non-US-listed foreign firms enjoy an increase in US institutional investors’ equity positions after their auditors become subject to PCAOB inspection access. Cross-sectional analysis implies that the benefit of the PCAOB inspection threat in mitigating US institutional investors’ home bias is concentrated in foreign countries without a strict local audit oversight system; active US institutional investors that are known to value accounting transparency; and firms from countries that grant PCAOB access later (after the onset of its international inspection program in 2005). Our evidence suggests that foreign firms become better known in the capital markets under the PCAOB inspection program, which induces US institutional investors to acquire larger equity stakes in both US-listed and non-US-listed foreign firms given the lower information asymmetry that ensues under the PCAOB inspection threat.

12501618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12501618.value: As we have collected a complete set of PCAOB inspection data around the world, we could probably develop a few other potential research projects (either looking at the impact of PCAOB inspection threat or actual PCAOB inspection). We are currently working on them.

12501618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12501618.value: We broaden our understanding of the role that the PCAOB’s international inspection program plays in the capital markets given that empirical research on its impact on US investor perceptions of the assurance value provided by foreign firm auditors remains scarce. From a policy perspective, our analysis lends support to the intuition that helping develop a sound auditing infrastructure by permitting PCAOB inspections enables foreign governments to improve corporate accounting transparency, particularly when these countries have a relatively lax audit oversight system. Our evidence implies that US institutional investors’ home bias subsides after foreign firms’ auditors become subject to the PCAOB inspection threat, which is important given that these firms continue to struggle to attract US investors and some governments continue to resist granting the PCAOB inspection access.

12501818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501818.value: 本項目研究政治事業前景的考慮如何影響專制政府的最優層級設計。 專制政府(例如中國)與民主政府不同之處，在於官員不受選舉制衡。因此，這些官員積極工作的動力主要來自他們對政治事業前景的考慮，而不是連任壓力。政府層級結構的設計必須考慮是否有足夠的事業前景來激勵下層官員努力工作。雖然已有大量文獻研究聯邦制下民主政府的最優分權水平，但這類文獻並未包含政治事業前景的考慮，不足以研究專制政府的最優分權水平。 專制政府也不同於商業公司，因為當我們考慮什麼構成典型官員的回報時，貨幣收益與濫用權力的機會相比，可能顯得蒼白無力。因此，設計這種政府的層級結構時，必須考慮到這樣一個事實，即不同層級政府的權力分配直接影響官員的收益和激勵，但這些影響不容易通過貨幣支付來抵消。雖然有大量文獻研究商業公司的最優層級結構，但過分強調貨幣支付的作用也使得這些文獻不足以研究專制政府的最優分權水平。 本項目旨在建構新的理論框架，以分析專制政府的層級結構。我們的結果將使有關(如中國的)最優政府層級結構的政策辯論更有基礎。我們期望本項目帶來至少一篇國際期刊文章並在多個研討會發表報告。

12501818.label: Realisation of objectives
12501818.value: This project studies how political career concerns affect the optimal design of an autocratic government’s hierarchical structure. We have produced a working paper in which a general theoretical framework for characterizing an incentive compatible and feasible mechanism has been developed. We model the mechanism design problem as finding a personnel policy that allocates authorities to different officials to maximize social welfare, taking into account the incentive compatibility of the agents. In the model, governors can choose actions (work or shirk) in each period which may affect the private and public benefits, and whether they can stay in the same position, be moved to a different position, or be fired in the next period. We invoke the concept of Markov Perfect Equilibrium to analyze the strategy profiles of the agents. Under this framework, we define a mechanism as the combination of an authority allocation, a transition function, and a stationary strategy proﬁle of the agents. We have characterized an incentive compatible and feasible mechanism. This general framework has provided insights that are absent in the literature of federalism and the literature of hierarchical organizations. The ﬁrst generation of this literature treats each government as a benevolent planner, and identiﬁes factors that are in favor or against more decentralization. The second generation of the literature on federalism takes the incentive problems of politicians more seriously, and studies the costs and beneﬁts of decentralization of resources and authorities in terms of how it aﬀects and distorts these politicians’ incentives. However, in all these studies, politicians at subnational governments are always surrogates of their corresponding regions, and represent their regions. They are not appropriate for analyzing career bureaucrats in an autocracy. In the literature of hierarchical organizations, roughly speaking, the key design variables in these studies are the depth and the width of an organization’s hierarchy, with the former referring to the number of vertical layers, and the latter the number of subordinates a supervisor has to oversee in any given layer. Our model investigates how authorities should be allocated. It is different from early studies that only considers the situation of a two-layer of government and specific career path (from the subnational to the national government). The general framework developed in this project allows more complicated hierarchical structures, including ones that look more like a ladder than a pyramid, and ones where career paths potentially contain cycles. We consider that Objectives 1, 2 and 3 have been achieved. We can see that many extensions and detailed work can be done under this framework. This will be left for future work. As for Objective 4, due to the pandemic, we have not been able to disseminate our findings via seminars and conferences. We have circulated our working paper among academic acquaintances. We will continue to look for chances to present and/or publish our paper after collecting comments.

12501818.label: Major findings and research outcome
12501818.value: This project studies how political career concerns affect the optimal design of an autocratic government’s hierarchical structure. We have developed a general theoretical framework for characterizing an incentive compatible and feasible mechanism. In particular, we have not limited our attention to “natural” hierarchical structures such as those resembling a tree or a pyramid, or those where a typical oﬃcial’s career path contains no cycles. Our more general theoretical framework have not presumed any particular oﬃce to be more senior, or of higher-rank, than another oﬃce. Concepts like ”seniority” or ”rank” acquire meaning only when we need to interpret the optimal hierarchical structure that endogenously arises. We expect that lessons we have learned from this exercise will vastly improve the quality of policy debates surrounding, for example, the Chinese government’s optimal hierarchical structure. Specifically, we have identified two properties that an optimal and incentive compatible mechanism must satisfy: - There is a retire position that gives the highest lifetime utility to its holder and its holder must shirk for sure. - All governors that work at least sometimes must be indiﬀerent between working and shirking. Our findings are embodied in three major propositions. We have provided rigorous proofs for all of them. To avoid discussion of complicated notations and definitions, please refer to the attached working paper.

12501818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12501818.value: This project is a theoretical exploration of an important mechanism design question. A natural direction for further exploration is to conduct empirical tests regarding how changes in the allocation of authorities affect the behavior of government officials along the vertical hierarchy. China’s administrative reforms in the past few decades provide a suitable case for investigation. Many studies have tested how performance of local officials affect their promotion. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is none about how promotion probability affects the performance of the local officials.

12501818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12501818.value: This project studies how political career concerns affect the optimal design of an autocratic government’s hierarchical structure. An autocratic government diﬀers from a democratic one in that oﬃcials are not subject to electoral checks and balances. Hence a predominant part of these oﬃcials’ incentives to work hard comes from their political career concerns. An autocratic government also diﬀers from a commercial ﬁrm in that, when we consider what constitutes the payoﬀ of a typical oﬃcial, monetary payments probably pale in comparison with the opportunities to abuse power. The design of such a government’s hierarchical structure therefore has to take into account the fact that the allocation of power across diﬀerent oﬃces directly aﬀects oﬃcials’ payoﬀs and incentives, and these eﬀects cannot be easily counter-balanced by monetary payments. This study has developed a general theoretical framework for a better understanding of how an optimal hierarchical structure should be designed. The findings can shed light on many relevant policy debates, such as those surrounding the Chinese government’s optimal hierarchy structure.

12501918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501918.value: The exponentially increasing yet unjustified executive pay around the world has prompted much debate over how to improve extant corporate governance systems to better align executive pay with shareholders’ interests. One of the most influential proposals to address this issue is to further empower shareholders to voice on executive pay or say-on-pay (SOP). Such proposals have gained widespread support from lawmakers, which have finally been translated to SOP laws in 11 countries as of 2014. Nevertheless, opponents of the law are rather pessimistic for several reasons. To date, studies show mixed results on whether SOP laws could curb executive overpay, enhance pay-for-performance sensitivity and therefore increase firm value. As such, the effectiveness of SOP laws remains controversial and needs further study. In addition, prior studies have not examined how SOP laws affect firms’ financial reporting quality (FRQ), an important factor that is related to several economic consequences and that affects the inferences drawn from pay-for-performance relations in prior studies. The proposed research will aim to contribute to this debate and examine the causal effect of SOP laws on FRQ by taking advantage of the staggered initiation of SOP laws worldwide. Drawing on the existing literature, we propose three possible FRQ consequences following the adoption of SOP laws. We plan to capture FRQ using three proxies that reflect a firm’s involvement in accrual management, income smoothing and real earnings management. To further shed light on how SOP laws affect FRQ, we will further examine the moderating effect of country-level investor protection regimes and firms’ internal/external monitoring mechanisms. To supplement prior studies on the effectiveness of SOP laws, we will examine whether executives are more accountable for their performance after the passage of SOP laws by using a modified pay-for-performance sensitivity model that accounts for earnings quality (Cornett et al. 2008). We expect the proposed research to make the following contributions. First, it could contribute to the debate on the monitoring role of SOP laws from the financial reporting perspective. Second, the proposed research could deepen our understanding of the causal relationship between shareholder protection and FRQ. Finally, it could extend the compensation contracting literature in which shareholders can intervene in the decision-making process concerning executive pay. We believe that our study will be timely as it will provide policy implications to securities regulators, especially those from jurisdictions which plan to adopt SOP laws in the future. 在全球範圍內高級經理人薪酬急速卻又缺乏理據的增長, 已經引發了對如何改善現有公司治理體系以更好的實現將高級經理人薪酬和股東利益一致的討論。 進一步給與股東對高級經理人薪酬以發言權是諸多的具有影響力的提議之一。 該項提議已經獲得了立法者的大範圍支持,並轉化成了全球範圍內截至2014年11個國家的經理人薪酬發言權立法。 儘管如此, 反對者對此項法律是否有效依舊有許多悲觀的理由。 到目前為止,對於該法律能否抑制經理人高薪, 提高業績和經理人薪酬敏感度, 並最終導致公司價值提升的研究, 依然沒有一致的結論。 由此, 該法律是否有效依舊是充滿爭議, 並需要進一步的研究。 過往的研究也沒有探討該法律對於公司財務報告品質的影響。 本研究致力於採用該法律全球範圍內交錯的立法進程來研究該法律對財務報告質量的因果關係。 基於現有的文獻,我們提出該法對於財務報告質量的三種可能性的結果。 我們計畫使用應計制會計操縱, 盈利平穩性和真實盈餘管理作為財務報告質量的計量方法。 為進一步研究該法對於財務報告質量影響, 我們將考慮國家層面的投資者保護法律和公司的內外部治理機制在本主研究課題中的作用。 我們並將拓展過往對於該法有效性的研究,探索在調整了財務報告質量後該法是否提升經理人對公司業績問責。 我們期待我們的研究將有如下貢獻。 第一, 該研究將從財務報告質量角度拓展了經理人薪酬發言權法律的監督作用的文獻。 第二,該研究將加深我們對於股東保護和財務報告質量因果關係的理解。 最後, 該研究將拓展經理人薪酬合同文獻的研究。 我們相信我們的研究是及時的, 因為本研究對於證券監管者, 特別是那些來自計畫採用該法律的國家的監管者, 有政策借鑒意義。

12503018.label: Major findings and research outcome
12503018.value: We have achieved the stated research objectives and further extended it to some timely research areas. Firstly, as proposed, we successfully collected two large-scale survey and experimental data from the field. Specifically, we collected 140 customer-employee teams to testify our hypotheses. We also solicited help from the senior management of two international companies to serve as the coders of each team’s ideation performance. With the data, we reveal the underlying mechanisms and confirm the effects of proposed boundary conditions. In brief, our findings show that team flow emerges when joint collaboration (JointCol) couples with low intra-group efficacy variability or high collective efficacy beliefs. A double-edged sword effect of team flow also emerges: It enhances idea novelty but reduces idea volume and appropriateness. Whereas team depletion arises as an alternative psychological mechanism that drives the effect of JointCol when flow is absent. This line of research thus highlights how crucial psychological processes determine the unique effects of customer–employee JointCol, then offers promising guidance to help managers foster the use of temporary workgroups, encourage customer–employee collaboration, and enhance their innovation development processes. We presented our work in two prestigious conferences, including the EMAC (2021) and AIBSEAR (2020). We also published part of our survey findings in Journal of Business Research (2022) and The Service Industries Journal (2022), as well as another manuscript currently under review at Journal of Service Research. Besides, with the reviewers’ comments and suggestions, we are fortunate to extend our research ideas with more data collection. Specifically, we collected more experimental studies by integrating the ideas of collaboration with employees and service performance in the fields of robotic frontlines. For instance, we develop a project investigating how teaming up the human staff with the robotic employee influences their service creativity, which currently receives an invited revision at Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science. Likewise, we also collect both field and lab data to examine how the presence of robotic frontline influences the consumption behaviors of those solo vs. joint consumers, currently under the 2nd R&R at Journal of Service Research. Overall, all stated objectives have been satisfactorily achieved and with promising extensions of our research.

12503018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12503018.value: Our work generates several directions for future research and potential courses of actions. For instance, our investigation of the effects of joint collaboration centers on temporary workgroups; additional research should seek to replicate these findings in different contexts, to enhance their generalizability. Second, we examine the role of efficacy by using the key concepts of intra-group efficacy variability and collective efficacy beliefs, but we also recognize that other contingencies might be influential, such as shared interpersonal similarity among participants. Third, we adopt an integrative approach to examine customer–employee joint collaboration in terms of their level of effort and participation (e.g., self-reported and objective measures, such as frequency of e-chats), but to gain more insights, further research might address the quality of their collaboration, such as communication quality. Fourth, a flow or depletion state tends to be temporary, so longitudinal research might triangulate our findings and provide more conclusive evidence of causal effects over time. We hope our findings pave the way for more research in areas of customer-employee joint collaboration and creativity so as to establish further valuable insights and implications. We shall also keep exploring additional research topics with the existing datasets that could be developed into publications.

12503018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12503018.value: Our research illuminates a more complete view of the effectiveness of involving the joint collaboration between customers and employees in temporary workgroups. Our work helps provide a finer grained understanding for the effect of Joint collaboration on the group creative performance. In particular, we take a more holistic view by explicating the underlying psychological processes for the effects of joint collaboration basing on Csiksentmihalyi’s (1975) flow theory. Our research also improves understanding of the conditions in which fostering joint collaboration in workgroup drives group flow and thereby influences group creative performance. We further uncover an experiential state of group depletion that might emerge and influence group creative performance when these boundary conditions are not achieved. Exploring these psychological processes should illuminate a clearer picture of the complex relationships between joint collaboration and group creative performance. Finally, we provide fresh insights by uncovering the bright and dark side of the group flow (e.g., reduced usefulness of idea) and depletion state (e.g., increase idea volume) on creative performance outcomes. Our results thus may provide practical evidence of the need to manage and (re)design temporary customer-employee workgroup tasks to allow the groups to arrive at a state of either flow or depletion.

12600718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12600718.value: 中國是一個專制但治理體系很分散的國家。 大部分氣候政策都由中央制度，地方實施，但地方政府有權以當地情況為由重新作出政策決定。 這種治理結構對中國減緩氣候變化的影響尚不清楚。 一部分研究認為，權力下放對成功實施氣候政策至關重要，因為地方政府製定量身定制的政策解決方案必需一定的自主權。 其他研究則認為，地方政府已成為有效氣候治理的主要障礙。 這兩個相反的論點都有證據支持，也是本研究旨在解決的一個重點問題。 兩種不同觀點的存在表明地方實施氣候政策存在重大差異。 然而，以前的研究大多是單一案例研究，側重於單一地點的單一政策，很少有研究充分考慮實施方式和原因。 本項目的主要貢獻是提高我們對中國氣候治理的理解。 基於這些知識，我們可以從政策和治理的角度提出合理的建議，以改善中國的氣候減緩績效。 本項目用嶄新的概念和大量的數據收集研究氣候政策實施的變化，並制定了一個概念框架來解釋了地方政策實施行為差異。 該框架由五個相互關聯的維度組成，包括(1)政策問題的易處理性，(2)政策模糊性，(3)實施能力，(4)利益一致性和(5)中央 - 地方關係。 關於於數據收集，本項目將採用多站點，多案例方法。 我們將研究三個複雜而有影響力的氣候政策:工業節能，建築能源改造和光伏扶貧。 實地調查將在代表中國四個主要經濟區的四個省(吉林，甘肅，山西和江蘇)進行。 將對地方官員和其他相關者進行總共200次訪談。

12600718.label: Realisation of objectives
12600718.value: 1. To understand the variations in climate policy implementation using a multi-case, multi-site approach. This project aimed to investigate the politics of climate policy implementation across various sectors and localities in China, with a focus on coal-mine closure, forest conservation, grassland conservation, and renewable energy development. Despite the challenges posed by COVID-19, we successfully conducted multiple rounds of fieldwork in 2019, 2020, and 2021 to collect first-hand information. Our primary data collection strategies were face-to-face semi-structured interviews and focus groups. We conducted 2 focus groups and 23 interviews in Inner Mongolia for the coal-mine closure policy, 64 face-to-face semi-structured interviews and 5 focus groups in Heilongjiang for the forest conservation policy, 25 interviews in Inner Mongolia for the grassland conservation policy , and 24 interviews both online and onsite in Jilin for the renewable energy policy. The interviews aimed to understand the roles and visions of local officials and other stakeholders in climate policy implementation, the planning, design, and management of policy implementation, the key challenges and barriers hindering stakeholders from fulfilling their roles or achieving their expectations, the actions taken to overcome these barriers, how the actions and visions of stakeholders are embedded in multileveled institutional structures, and the socio-economic impact of climate implementation. We also collected data from secondary sources, such as official documents and reports, media news, and websites. The collection of rich empirical data provided a basis for progressing the theorization work, and we made several new discoveries about China's climate implementation (please see the next section for more details). 2. To develop a conceptual framework of climate policy implementation and apply it to identify the causes of variations in policy implementation. The project has made conceptual advancements in mainly three areas related to the politics of climate policy implementation. First, a series of papers including "Pastoralism and conservation: The politics and notions of environmental justice under the grazing ban policy in Inner Mongolia, China" and "Can authoritarian regimes achieve just energy transition? Evidence from China's solar photovoltaic poverty alleviation initiative" examine the impact of climate policy implementation from the perspective of just transition. These papers contribute to a deeper understanding of the challenges and opportunities for achieving a just transition in China's climate policy implementation. Second, a series of papers including "Political economy of just transition: Disparate impact of coal mine closure on state-owned and private coal workers in Inner Mongolia, China" and "Eco-socialism and the political ecology of forest conservation in the Greater Khingan Range, China" reveal the political economy of climate policy implementation in China. These papers show that the political economy of climate policy implementation in China is complex and multifaceted, and it involves various actors, including the state, private companies, and different social groups. Furthermore, the papers reveal how climate policy implementation is shaped political-economic factors such as eco-socialism and eco-authoritarianism. A third strand of publications, including "Civil society, environmental litigation, and Confucian energy justice: A case study of an environmental NGO in China" and "Chinese environmental activism and the environmental politics of rumors", examine the role and strategies of non-state actors in China's climate policy implementation. These papers contribute to a better understanding of the role and strategies of non-state actors in promoting environmental and social justice in climate policy by holding the government accountable for its implementation practices. 3. To formulate practical recommendations to improve China’s climate governance. China is making rapid transformation to a low-carbon future under the discourse of ecological civilization and the goals of carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutral by 2060. The rapid transformation to a low-carbon future in China presents significant challenges and opportunities for both the climate outcome and the socio-economic well-being of affected communities. By providing evidence-based recommendations, the project aims to contribute to a more just and sustainable transition to a low-carbon future in China. The transition to a low-carbon future has and will continue to create winners and losers. As such, the policy focus should be on protecting the most marginalized groups. One key recommendation is to move beyond the use of quantified indicators such as the reemployment rate to assess the socio-economic impact of climate policy implementation. While such indicators can provide valuable information, they fail to accurately capture the experiences of marginalized groups who may face multiple structural barriers to reemployment, such as lack of education or discrimination. On the one hand, policy implementers should adopt a more nuanced approach to assessing socio-economic impacts that takes into account the specific needs and experiences of different groups affected by the transition. This involves conducting targeted consultations with affected communities, as well as collaborating with civil society organizations and other stakeholders to ensure that the voices of marginalized groups are heard and their needs are addressed. On the other hand, we recommend that implementers prioritize the development of support mechanisms to protect vulnerable groups, such as providing re-training programs to help workers transition to new industries and financial support and to help communities adapt to the changing socio-economic landscape. To disseminate these policy recommendations, the research team will produce a series of policy briefs that summarizes the findings and recommendations. The policy briefs will be distributed online and through established networks to reach policymakers, scholars, practitioners, and other stakeholders working in the area of climate governance and just transition in China. 4. To build and strengthen the research team’s capacity in researching climate governance in China and to publish one academic book and five to six articles in leading journals. The project has exceeded its publication target, resulting in the publication of 13 peer-reviewed journal articles. These articles have been published in highly regarded international journals such as Political Geography, Environmental Politics, Energy Research & Social Science, and Forest Policy and Economics, among others. This demonstrates the high quality and significance of the research conducted by the research team. In addition to the publications, the project has also contributed to the training of the next generation of scholars and practitioners. The project's Principal Investigator (PI) has successfully supervised a PhD student who completed a thesis on climate implementation in China. This achievement highlights the project's impact on developing the expertise and capacity of future scholars and practitioners in this field.

12600718.label: Major findings and research outcome
12600718.value: This project conceptualizes climate policy implementation as a bottom-up political process that is contested by a multitude of local state and non-state actors with diverse interests and priorities. The local politics of policy implementation have a significant impact not only on climate mitigation but also on the socio-economic well-being of local communities. Based on this conceptual framework, the project has generated several specific findings, including: 1. One key finding of the project is that the implementation of climate policy, such as in the closure of coal mines, can both reflect and reinforce deeply rooted unequal socio-economic structures, such as rural-urban inequality and regional inequality. This can leave the most vulnerable groups, such as private coal workers, trapped by the unfair treatment of the climate-political system. 2. Another finding of the project is that state-owned enterprises (SOEs) can play a positive role in reducing the negative socio-economic impact of climate policy in China through eco-restructuring processes, which involve the restructuring of work-units and the development of new sustainable economic activities. These processes can have a significant impact on the state-society relationship. However, the project also highlights that this arrangement can create inequality due to the structural barriers of the SOE system towards the rural population. 3. The project also found that local government officials who are directly responsible for climate policy implementation play a crucial but difficult role in balancing the political pressure from top-down policies and bottom-up realities. This is because local governments in China are rooted in central-local tensions and have limited autonomy and flexibility in implementation, which can make it challenging to protect local socio-economic interests. 4. The project also highlights the important role that affected communities can play in climate policy implementation, particularly in situations where policies are perceived to be unjust. One way that communities can assert their political influence is through rumor-fueled protests. The project finds that poor environmental information governance, driven by a development-first and prejudice-rich official narrative and the strategic behaviors of blame and accountability avoidance, provides an important condition for rumor formulation and circulation. Additionally, the ephemeral nature of communication and group sanctions on government supporters make it difficult for authorities to control rumors.

12600718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12600718.value: From a policy perspective, the project's emphasis on the importance of prioritizing the protection of vulnerable and marginalized groups in climate policy implementation could be further developed through the further elaboration and testing of specific policy interventions, such as job-related training programs and other support mechanisms for affected communities. We suggest the development of an action-oriented research project focused on co-designing and co-implementing interventions with affected communities. The project will use participatory methodologies such as participatory mapping exercises and community-led workshops to develop a deep understanding of the specific challenges faced by different groups and to co-design interventions that are tailored to their needs and priorities. The project would provide an important opportunity for communities to assert their agency and shape the implementation of climate policies in ways that are responsive to their needs and concerns.

12600718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12600718.value: The project has looked at how climate change policies are put into practice in China, and the impact they have on local communities. The study found that the process of implementing climate policies is complex and often involves a range of different local actors, each with their own interests and priorities. One key finding was that the implementation of policies, such as closing coal mines, can reinforce existing inequalities and leave vulnerable groups, such as private coal workers, at a disadvantage. However, the study also found that state-owned enterprises can play a positive role in reducing the negative effects of climate policies on communities through restructuring processes. The study also highlighted the challenges faced by local government officials in balancing the needs of their communities with national policies. Finally, the study found that affected communities can play an important role in climate policy implementation, and that protests can be a way for them to assert their influence. The study suggests that future research should focus on working with affected communities to develop interventions that are tailored to their needs.

12602818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12602818.value: This research adopts an archival approach to the study of the history of medical mission in Hong Kong during the colonial era. Medical mission was a significant aspect in the history of Christian missions in China because it was effective in winning converts and it was a starting point in other modernity projects by missionaries. In Hong Kong history, missionaries made a more direct contribution in these regards. The colonial government of Hong Kong endorsed medical qualifications from Britain. British missionaries commanded instant respect from the government upon which they launched new initiatives. The partnership with the community was a much less irksome journey as compared with their counterparts in China. Hong Kong thus had the largest number of mission hospitals as compared with any other Chinese cities. During the colonial rule, these include Benjamin Hobson’s initiatives in the 1840s, the hospital idea from William Young and John Edge in 1881, the Alice Memorial Hospital in 1887, the Nethersole Hospital in 1893, the Alice Memorial Maternity Hospital in 1904, and the Ho Miu Ling Hospital in 1906. In 1954, the creation of the Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital was to merge these hospitals into one. There were other major Christian medical projects in postwar Hong Kong, including the Junk Bay Medical Relief Council in 1953 (ended in 1986), the Haven of Hope Tuberculosis Sanatorium in 1955, the Baptist Clinic during the 1950s (upgraded to a hospital in 1963), the Evangel Hospital in 1965, and the United Christian Hospital in 1973. After the founding of the Hospital Authority in 1990, the Christian tradition has been preserved and promoted among hospitals with similar backgrounds. Apart from an account of medical missions during the colonial period, this research examines the historical significance of missionary doctors and nurses (and leading Chinese Christian doctors and nurses) in Hong Kong. In doing so, this reveals several salient features that defined their belief and practice in holistic healing. Such an approach echoes well with several current research themes in the field of medical history in modern China, such as power, gender, and community recognition. Specifically, this project explores the historical processes behind the making of a power relationship of “missionary-convert” and “doctor/nurse-patient,” the successes and failures of local partnerships that missionary doctors/nurses established, and the relative importance of Protestant Christian medical missions in the entire sector of medical institutions from the historical perspective. 本研究運用檔案研究的方法，探究殖民香港的基督教醫療服務。傳教士一般認為醫療服務不單較易贏取皈依者的信任，更是現代化其他社會範疇的起點，故視之為是傳播基督教的重要途徑。這可見於他們在殖民香港的醫療貢獻。由於香港政府會認可英國頒授的醫療資格，它大多會接納具備該等資歷的英國傳教士帶來的服務和倡議，如1840年代合信（Benjamin Hobson）在港推動西醫的倡議，以及1881年William Young和John Edge與建醫院的建議。基督教醫院因此相繼建立，如1887年的雅禮氏紀念醫院、1893年的那打素醫院、1904年的雅禮氏婦產醫院以及1906年的何妙齡醫院（後三者於1954年合併為雅麗氏何妙齡那打素醫院）。二次大戰後，基督教會繼續與時並進，建立實踐全人治療概念的醫院，如1953年的將軍澳醫療救濟委員會（1986年結束）、1955年的靈實療養院、1963年由診所升格的浸會信醫院、1965年的播道醫院，以及1973年的基督教聯合醫院。1990年成立的醫院管理局更肯定了基督教醫院的傳統和理念。在殖民地政府的信任下，英國傳教士在港取信於社區組織比中國更為容易，使殖民香港成為擁有最多基督教醫院的中國城市。為理解「傳教士—信徒關係」、「醫患關係」，以及此兩種聯繫構成權力關係的歷史進程，本研究將在整理殖民香港的基督教醫療服務的發展概況後，以傳教士醫生和護士，以及中國基督徒醫生和護士為研究對象，探討他們與社區的夥伴關係，以及基督徒在建立醫療體制的角色，從而回應權力、性別和社區認同等近代中國醫療史的重要課題。

12602818.label: Realisation of objectives
12602818.value: Regarding objective (1), I have achieved it 100%. I explored the roles of the pioneering medical missionary Benjamin Hobson and other leading missionaries under different circumstances: i) handling the 1894 plague and its aftermath (e.g. John Thomson), ii) studying the causes of Beriberi between the 1890s and 1900s (e.g. Robert Gibson), iii) training of nurses from the 1890s to the 1940s (e.g. Alice Sibree), iv) creating the opportunities for the continuation of medical students’ education during WWII (e.g. Gordon King), and v) healing the leprosy patients while making medical discoveries and advances (e.g. Grace Warren). I also included some Chinese Christian doctors whose leadership positions created new opportunities. I examined an understudied aspect of Ho Kai (何啟)’s life -- his fathe’s influence on his religious faith, while assessing his contributions to the founding of the Alice memorial hospital and the Hongkong College of Medicine for Chinese. Besides, Arthur Woo (胡惠德) was instrumental in bringing effective changes in Hong Kong before and during the Japanese occupation. His impact on medicine was at the national level -- the first Chinese president of the China Medical Association. Regarding post-war development, I discussed the impact of some influential Chinese doctors, like Ding Lik-kiu (陳立僑) and Choi Yuen Wan (蔡元雲). Regarding nurses, I sampled from a wide range of selected cases and discussed their respective contributions. These names include the pioneering ones (e.g. Mrs Kwan Lai Shi關黎氏), those who stayed in Christian hospitals (e.g. Lau Mei Yuk 劉美玉in pre-WWII Nethersole Hospital, Grace Chan Wing Han陳永嫻 in post-WWII Nethersole Hospital and Hua Kit-Ying 華潔瑩 in the newly established United Christian Hospital), those who worked in secular hospitals (e.g. Kong Ching-po 江青波in Tung Wah Hospital, and Leung Sheung-chi 梁尚志in Tsan Yuk Hospital), and those who worked primarily in the community (e.g. Law Wai Tak 羅惠德 in Yuen Long, Liv Weber-Aslaksen in the resettlement estates). Regarding objective (2), I have achieved it 100%. Regarding international partners, I assessed their roles and contributions in Hong Kong: the Medical Missionary Society, the London Missionary Society (now known as the Council for World Mission), the Rockefeller Foundation, the Baptist Missionary Society, the Mission to Lepers (now known as the Leprosy Mission in 1965), Southern Baptist Convention, the Evangelical Free Church of America, and the Mission Covenant Church (Norway). I examined their relationship with various local partners through the use of their relevant papers and archives from local and overseas archives. These include the Archives of the Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Charity Foundation, the Hongkong College of Medicine for Chinese materials in the Wellcome Collection, the University of Hong Kong Archives, St. John’s Ambulance, the Tung Wah Museum Archives, and the Hong Kong government reports and archives in the Public Records Office (Hong Kong) National Archives (London), etc. Regarding objective (3), I have achieved 100%. In both the oral history and the historical monograph, I covered all the essential historical features and religious ethos from the vantage points of doctors, nurses and chaplaincy of all significant Christian hospitals in Hong Kong. Specifically, these hospitals include the first hospital (1843-1851) under Benjamin Hobson and Henri J. Hirschberg, the Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospitals (1887- the present), the Hay Ling Chau Leprosarium (1951-1975), the Haven of Hope Hospital and its predecessor (since the 1950s), the Evangel Hospital (since 1954), the Baptist Hospital (since 1962), and the United Christian Hospital (since 1973). I assessed their work under their respective historical circumstances. Given their long history, the history of Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospitals received more attention as they created their impact in various aspects, such as the early history of the Hongkong College of Medicine for Chinese, the 1894 plague, the history of training of Chinese nurses and the introduction of modern maternity services, etc. The Hay Ling Chau Leprosarium had a clear focus on medical service. Its history presents a robust example of the solid doctor-patient relationship. The post-war developments of some of these Christian hospitals contribute to addressing the demands for medical services, and their ethos define specific values in their practice of medical professionalism. Regarding objective (4), I have achieved 75%. I have done four conference/seminar presentations. I did two seminars, one at the Australian National University and the other at the University of Victoria, Canada. I presented at two conferences, where I met up with most scholars in the history of Chinese Christianity and the history of World Christianity, respectively. I produced an oral history (which is of 245 pages in length). The oral history discusses recent developments from the 1960s to the present. Because of this feature, the monograph gives a heavier coverage of the pre-WWII development. The monograph is divided into three parts. The first part is to trace the vision of medical ministry in the nineteenth century. It also laid down the foundation for medical education in Hong Kong through the Hongkong College of Medicine for Chinese and, subsequently, the medical faculty at the University of Hong Kong. The second part assesses the impact of Christian medical ministry in the face of significant challenges such as the 1894 plague, the prevalence of Beriberi, the origin of modern maternity services, and WWII. The last part is to cover the post-WWII developments with two focuses. The issues of refugees and the Cold War are addressed through the Hay Ling Chau Leprosarium case study. The other focus is examining Christian responses to “urban anxieties.” The reasons for underachievement of writing the monograph (which I completed 75%) are (1) lack of time due to new duties at HKBU and (2) severe disruption caused by the pandemic. Regarding (1), I was twice appointed the acting associate at two different periods. These two appointments took up to ten months altogether. In addition to my regular teaching, there were many instances in which I had to handle faculty-related issues. Regarding (2), the pandemic caused severe disruptions to my research as many archives and libraries (local and overseas) were closed or with minimal services. Solution: Regarding the closure of archives, I kept making requests. I slowly got some responses. When international travel became possible and work schedule permitting, I spent two months at Cambridge University between July and August 2022 to catch up with my research and writing. I keep working on the remaining five chapters, each of which I finish 50%. I target December 2023 as the completion date for the full manuscript. I made an initial inquiry with Cambridge University Press, to which I would submit the completed manuscript for their consideration for publication. Unspent Budget: The overseas archives and libraries I planned to visit during the pandemic were closed. The conferences were cancelled or operated only in online mode. I could not spend the budget on trips (conferences: 60,000 [21% of the total budget], and research trips: 29,186 [10.3% of the total budget]). Although I had an extensive research trip in 2022, it fell beyond the project duration. I bore all the expenses. There is an unspent amount of HK$17,920 [0.6% of the total budget] in research staff. The reason is that the staff concerned decided to start his teaching career in September and left HKBU in mid-August. The remaining amount was not significant enough to make any meaningful hiring of research staff.

12602818.label: Major findings and research outcome
12602818.value: 1. This is an oral history of the Christian medical ministry in Hong Kong since the 1960s that I organized, edited, and co-authored. In addition to the records of 21 interviews, I wrote an introduction and 50 annotated entries to explain 50 key concepts. The book consists of the perspectives of doctors, nurses, and hospital chaplains. The scope cover hospital histories, prominent figures’ experiences and contributions, community-based work, and medical professionalism. The oral history book meets objectives 1, 2, and 3. 2. This book chapter examines Gordon King’s work in China and Hong Kong. His papers from the Baptist Missionary Society Archives make possible the writing of a “thick narrative” that covers his inner thoughts about the challenges he went through during the Japanese invasion. This chapter also keeps track of his contribution to continuing HKU medical students’ education in Free China. The interconnectedness shown in his case takes an extraordinary place in the bigger picture of “Christianity and Education in Modern China.” 3. This journal paper attempts to answer the question of how Christian medical missionaries competed with Chinese religions to win over converts. In particular, the paper examines Benjamin Hobson’s translation strategies while producing new medical knowledge. It is a compelling case of East-West interactions in medicine and religions. 4. This monograph intends to complement the oral history book as specified in the report of (1) output, emphasising the history of Christian medical ministry up to 1945. The monograph’s first part answers how the vision of a medical mission was created, promoted, disrupted, and revived in the nineteenth century. In the process, Christian missionaries and Chinese Christians, specifically Benjamin Hobson and Ho Kai, played equally important roles. The second primary focus is to examine how the Christian medical ministry reacted to significant challenges in medicine between 1894 and 1945, namely, the 1894 plague, the prevalence of Beriberi, the birth of modern maternity services, and the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong. The third session of the monograph is to assess the Christian responses to the changing needs in post-WWII Hong Kong. Precisely, it consists of two key questions. First, it is about the surge in the numbers of leprosy patients alongside the refugee problem due to the Cold War between 1949 and the 1970s. Second, it examines the solutions several leading Christian medical professionals suggested regarding the growing “urban anxieties” caused by rapid industrialisation and urbanisation between the 1960s and 1990s.

12602818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12602818.value: First, the history of nursing education in Hong Kong is a topic that has been overlooked for a long time. Historical research could help chart out considerable values and meanings behind the defining ideas of the professionalism of nursing education in Hong Kong. This inspires me to research the history of nursing training at the Kwong Wah Hospital. It ends up with another book that I co-edited and co-authored, namely, Nursing Education at the Kwong Wah Hospital and the Everyday Life History in Hong Kong: An Oral History《提燈者言：廣華醫院護理教育歷史》(Hong Kong: Chung Hwa Books Co., 2022). 243pp. ISBN 978-988-8809-08-0. Second, this research opens up new topics for everyday life history through a long list of individuals whose stories are otherwise neglected. Ho King Mun (何景文), a medical apprentice under Benjamin Hobson, whose life and times made stimulating meanings not only to the history of medical ministry but also to the history of education. I include him in another forthcoming publication entitled “Ying Wa Boys in Early Colonial Hong Kong,” Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies. I am contributing ten short entries to a new edition of Biographical Studies of Eminent Church Figures in Hong Kong (Hong Kong Chinese Churches Union, forthcoming)

12602818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12602818.value: This research examines the history of medical missions in colonial Hong Kong and their significance in Christian missions in modern Chinese history. Drawing on archival research and the oral history method, it analyses how missionary (and Chinese Christian) doctors and nurses introduced modern medical education and holistic healing practices. This research focuses on three purposes. The first is to examine how the vision and mission of Christian medical ministry were made possible in the nineteenth century. Besides healing the sick, the pioneers aimed to establish medical education that created a national impact in China. The second is to assess the effects of Christian medical ministry in the face of significant challenges in Hong Kong between the 1890s and 1945, including the 1894 plague, the prevalence of Beriberi, the demand for modern maternity services, and the threats and damages caused by the Japanese occupation. The third investigates Christian responses to two critical questions confronting post-WWII Hong Kong. The influx of refugees led to the rise of leprosy cases that demanded the creation of a leprosarium offering a holistic cure. The complications of “urban anxieties” caused by rapid industrialization and economic pressure required a new framework to address people’s well-being.

12603318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603318.value: 本項研究採取跨領域視角並運用創新方法進行，從神話和宗教角度對李白（701—762）的一部分相關作品作重新審視和解讀。對於這樣一位唐代最傑出而又在世界文學史上赫赫有名的大詩人的這項研究，其預期成果將在世界文學和人文科學領域作出重要貢獻並產生相當的影響。 本項目的主要研究員（PI）在中國古典文學及道教研究兩個範疇的專業水平為本研究打下穩固的基礎。雖然在李白研究史上神話和宗教因素一直為學人所重視，但研究成果在量和質上均未見突出成就。本研究以跨領域視角和方法，從道教修煉特別是上清派在唐代的新發展（成為茅山派）以及傳說神話題材等角度，運用語文學（philology）和文化研究的方法和思路尋繹這些題材要素，分析李白的相關作品，以見其藝術獨創並評述這種嶄新詩學美學的成就和地位。前賢以中文、日文和其他西方語言發表出版的高論將成為本研究的重要基礎，有利於分析李白獨特詩風的形成，詩人如何善用宗教和文化的知識、技術和語言等因素進行自我塑像以及由此而產生的虛無詩境並引起箋注家的政治寓意解讀（allegorical reading）。 李白在唐代文化史上所扮演的兩重角色尤其重要。他既是個詩人也是個受籙道士，然而學界多忽略後一點，對其宗教背景和思想少有鑽研，即使偶有提及也只限於泛泛而論。本研究集中研討李詩二十來首，除了一般做法把正史、野史、序錄等相關史料作為重要參考外，還參看道教文獻尤其是上清經系作品，力圖還原詩中表達的最可信賴的歷史圖景。 本研究的新視角和新方法將為李白研究和唐代文化研究注入新鮮活力。研究語言為英語，計劃撰寫三篇學術論文，發表於一等漢學和文化研究的學術期刊。這些預期成果將起著橋樑作用，通過它們在文化、文學、宗教等領域產生的影響力，展開香港與西方學界的學術對話。此外，這些成果一方面既能提升PI的學術水平和地位，另一方面也為加強香港相關研究的力量出一分綿薄之力。

12603318.label: Realisation of objectives
12603318.value: 1. To conduct research in alternative, innovative ways, especially using Western Sinology, mythology, and philology, in the research on Li Bai’s poetry by investigating the functions and significance of its religious and mythological elements. The project has successfully realized this objective by means of the PI's academic backgrounds of Western Sinology as well as his training in mythology and philology acquired in the past and during the GRF research period. From these perspectives, the PI reexamined the poetry of Li Bai and discovered some new angles and approaches for research. 2. To practice an interdisciplinary approach and methodology in the reading of Tang poetry. This objective was also implemented as the research involved in interdisciplinary study. It deals with the poetry of Li Bai, but employed a large variety of methods such as mythology, philology, comparative literature, translation, study of editions, and so forth. In its discussion, the project extended its scope of coverage of texts to Western literature and Japanese tradition. 3. Through comparison, to identify and analyze various poetic styles by focusing on certain themes and settings in which the works were composed. This comparison is twofold. One is internal and the other is external. The internal one involves other Chinese texts before Li Bai's time and those contemporaneous with him, including the literary and religious texts, and forms a basis on how Li stood out in the literary and religious tradition in his poetics and poetry. The external one involves texts in the Western tradition, such as the Homeric epic and other mythological tradition, as comparison. 4. To draw attention to the importance of research from new perspectives and thereby to develop dialogue between Chinese and Western scholarship of literary and cultural studies. During the project period, the PI was able to conduct research in overseas institutions where he had interactions with colleagues in the same field. He also presented his findings at different settings on the Mainland, in the US and Australia, although they were mainly done on-line due to the COVID pandemic.

12603318.label: Major findings and research outcome
12603318.value: 1. “Gods Protecting My Physical Form” and Pacing the Void in Jade Capital: Li Bai’s Poetics of the Banished Transcendent Daoist diction and mythological motif elements in Li Bai’s (701-762) poetic works contribute to the formation of a unique poetic style. The essay discusses Li’s diction and imagery derived from the Shangqing and Lingbao meditative methods and rituals as recorded in the two schools’ classic scriptures, as a means to serve his personal poetic purposes. 2. The Transcendent of Poetry’s Quest for Transcendence: Li Bai on Mount Tiantai Mount Penglai and the Peng bird play an important role in Li Bai’s idiosyncrasy and yield crucial hints to the chronology and authenticity of relevant works. The pursuit of transcendence became a metaphorical means for two opposite ideas, namely taking office in response to an imperial summons and leaving office for transcendence-seeking fantasy. 3. Engulfing and Embracing the Vast Earth: Li Bai’s Cosmology in His “Ballad on the Sun Rising and Setting” The essay discusses an aspect of the formation of Li Bai’s poetic style by probing into his cosmology. The theoretical framework of “space-time” offers new insights in the exegesis of Li’s “Ballad on the Sun Rising and Setting,” with a focus on the poet’s treatment of how to deal with the passing of time and how one may transcend the unavoidable ageing process. 4. Li He’s Innovation in Rewriting Traditional Myths of the Sun Li He’s (ca. 790–ca. 816 CE) works recasting and revising the traditional theme of the passing of time are distinct in unique thought and motives. These works mark the debut of unique “spatio-temporal poetics.” Within this framework one finds a variety of creative and grotesque means by which the persona chases after time, as well as a pessimistic narrative on “the death of the transcendents.” 5. A Levee on Mount Jade Capital: From Six-dynasties Rituals of Pacing the Void to Early Tang Poetry on Roaming in Transcendence The essay traces the origin of the image of Mount Jade Capital and outline its development from a religious context to literary creation, by looking into its various functions and allegorical meanings as a key to explore how its sacred status and meaning in religious settings were absorbed and represented in poetry with high aesthetic appeal. The findings enable us to reconstruct the transformation of this poetic image, which eventually became an important “new transcendent realm” in Tang poetry.

12603318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12603318.value: The project lays an important foundation for the PI's long-term research on Tang poetry, especially on Li Bai. The PI has a plan to submit another GRF application in the 2022/23 exercise with a different focus and look forward to conducting more, in-depth study of this Tang poet par excellence. The teaching materials prepared for the PI's course on Li Bai have been taking shape. The PI has a plan to put them together to produce a set of more systematic course materials. In the future, it may become a book manuscript for the general readers. The course materials may well develop into a set that aims at a higher-level as the PI's research findings grow and the course may be offered to post-graduate students.

12603318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12603318.value: The project is a research of one of the greatest Tang poets, Li Bai (701-762), by focusing on the mythological elements and style of his poetic works. By adopting the angles of "mountains," "myth," and "meditation," the research involves these three core elements. Mountains form one most important repertoire of Li Bai's poetry composition. Its significance lies not only in the natural landscape but is related to the other two elements, because the mountains in his life and poetic works are constantly a site of his fantasy of the mythological world; they also serve as settings for his religious meditation practice. These three elements constantly interplay with each other and form the most unique themes of Li's poetic thought and thereby produce the most idiosyncratic poetry in the history of Chinese poetry.

12603418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12603418.value: Near 50% of ethnic minority Yi reside in Liangshan, an area of “concentrated poverty”; some unfortunate Yi youths even lost their parents. To promote Yi youths’ psychological resilience and positive development, since 2006, an international philanthropic foundation, in collaboration with the local government, has been sponsoring them for schooling. Preliminary evidence showed that Yi youths experience positive social and educational outcomes. Furthermore, strong ethnic identity predicts better school grades and higher levels of academic motivation. We assume that ethnic identity can a source for psychological resilience, hence this study focuses on the ethnic identity development among Yi adolescents. Phinney's ethnic identity development theory posits that having an achieved identity during adolescence is necessary for positive adulthood outcomes. International findings showed that strong identity leads to multiple positive developments in adolescents, and peer socialisation builds ethnic identity. Earlier studies of young rural Chinese earthquake victims in Sichuan also showed that positive peer socialisation drives up psychological well-being. Yet, its association with ethnic identity has not been studied in Yi adolescents. Research questions: (1) What is the ethnic identity development of Yi adolescents? (2)What is the effect of peer socialisation on it? (3) What are the associations between psychological and behavioural outcomes with strong ethnic identity? (4) How do Yi adolescents with strong versus weak ethnic identity differ in their socialisation experiences and psychological and behavioural well-being? We will adopt a mixed method research, with quantitative and qualitative strands. Participants are Yi adolescents sponsored by the philanthropic foundation (n=600). Data collection spans from 2018 to 2019. Standardised measurements will be used to collect the quantitative data and analysed with multilevel modelling. Qualitative one-on-one interviews (n=20) will be conducted. 10 Yi adolescents with strong ethnic identity and 10 with weak ethnic identity will be selected for interviews in order to compare their experiences. Last, qualitative findings will be connected with the quantitative results for in-depth analysis. Findings will inform educational strategies to build psychological resilience. The philanthropic organisation and the school management can mobilise peer resources for positive Yi adolescents’ ethnic identity development, which in turn, will drive up their psychological and behavioural well-being. 近半彝族人居住在被列為「貧困縣」的涼山彝族自治州, 當中更有一些不幸的彝族兒童失去他們的父母。為提升彝族兒童的抗逆力及促進他們的發展，一個國際慈善基金會與當地政府合作，自2006年起資助彝族兒童上學。初步數據顯示參與該教育項目的兒童在社交和學業上均有得著。當中，民族認識及認同感促進了他們的成績及學習動力。我們認為民族認識及認同感可提升彝族兒童的抗逆力，所以本研究將探討彝族青少年的民族認同發展。 Phinney的民族認同發展理論指出成年階段的全人健康有賴他們於青年時取得的正面民族認同感。國際研究顯示民族認同為青少年帶來正面發展；而正面的朋輩影響能夠增加青少年的民族認同感。早年研究也發現正面的朋輩關係能提升受四川地震影響的小學生的心理健康，但這關係在彝族青少年身上未被證實。 研究問題： (1)彝族青少年的民族 認識及認同感發展如何？(2)輩關係對民族認識及認同感發展有何影響？(3)民族認識及認同感和心理行為健康有何關係？(4)民族意識較強和較弱的彝族青少年的朋輩經驗和心理行為健康有何差別？ 研究將採用混合方法（包括量性及質性方法），邀請受贊助的彝族青少年參與（共600位）。數據收集將於2018至19年進行。量性研究將收集有關彝族青少年的民族認同感、心理行為健康及朋輩關係的資料。質性部份將以訪談形式進行（共20位），團隊將選出民族意識感較強和較弱的青少年各10位，進行訪談以比較他們的經驗。最後，我們將結合量性及質性的研究數據，深入分析結果。 研究希望幫助慈善基金會和學校管理層設計教育活動加強彝族青少年的抗逆力，善用朋輩資源提升青少年對彝族的認識及認同感，促進他們的心理行為健康。

12603418.label: Major findings and research outcome
12603418.value: The GRF project led to one conference presentation, the publication of 2 research papers. Major findings are: Objective 1. In this project, psychological outcomes are defined as depressive risk, general self efficacy, and ethnic identity. Behavioral outcomes are defined as smoking and drinking behaviors. Quantitative findings showed that the psychological outcomes of depressive risk and general self efficacy did not display a statistically significant change overtime, nor did the behavioral outcomes of smoking and drinking behaviors. As such, these findings were not submitted for publication. On the other hand, the psychological outcomes of ethnic identity showed changes. The ethnic identity exploration of the Yi adolescents increased over time, yet, ethnic identity commitment stayed the same. Those with a disengaged relationship with their caregivers showed the fastest increase in their ethnic identity exploration, while those with secured relationships showed the highest ethnic identity exploration over time. The findings suggest that the process of ethnic identity exploration serves different purposes for Yi students with good versus poor child-caregivers' relationship quality. For those with a secured relationship, ethnic identity exploration is the process of searching for the meaning of their ethnicity, including both positive and negative aspects. For those with disengaged relationships, ethnic identity exploration means searching for a sense of belonging and attachment to their ethnic group, which only acknowledges the positive aspects of their ethnicity (Please see publication no. 1 in Part C). Objective 2. Positive classmate support was associated with high levels of ethnic identity exploration and ethnic identity commitment. Findings underscore the importance of positive interpersonal interaction in building a solid ethnic identity (Please see publications no. 2 in Part C). Objective 3. Ethnic identity exploration was associated with high levels of general self-efficacy, while ethnic identity commitment was not(Please see publications no. 2 in Part C). Yet, the analysis showed that both ethnic identity exploration and commitment were not associated with the smoking and drinking behaviours and depression risk. As such, these findings were not submitted for publication. Objective 4. Analysis using the qualitative data showed that the ethnic socialisation experiences and psychological resilience of Yi adolescents with strong versus weak ethnic identity did not differ much. The team thus took a different approach to explore the experiences of ethnic affirmation (i.e., sense of belonging to ethnicity and positive feelings to own ethnicity) among the Yi adolescents. Nine themes emerged describing how Yi adolescents established their ethnic affirmation in their homes and villages, and then how their connection with their ethnicity changed after their attended secondary school, and how does receiving an education changed their future orientation associated with Yi (Please see publication no. 3 in Part C).

12603418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12603418.value: The research findings carried practical and research implications. Practice-wise, the team has been working closing with Liangshan Psychological Associations to design culturally-oriented programs in school settings to promote multicultural identity among ethnic minority students in the area. The program will focus on facilitating ethnic minority students to understand their ethnic history and traditions and embrace both the positive and negative aspects of it. We will also strive to support ethnic minority students to find their unique cultural selves in mainstream Han-driven school settings. Creating a positive social bonding among school peers is also vital for a strong ethnic identity. Research-wise, the team is building an ethnic asset model featuring ethnic identity as a psychological and cultural asset in the Asian region. We have extended our proposed model among Taiwanese indigenous college students and are also planning to test this model among Mainland ethnic minority university students. The team will continue to test the proposed ethnic asset model among different ethnic minority populations in the long run. We hope to offer additional empirical evidence to guide us on how we can change current narratives of seeing ethnic minorities as a liability instead of an asset to society.

12603418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12603418.value: This study uses Yi adolescents as an example to demonstrate the ethnic identity development of ethnic minorities in China and other Asian regions. Findings led to the establishment of an ethnic asset model featuring ethnic identity as a cultural and psychological asset for the positive well-being of ethnic minority young people. We also identified positive social experiences as a critical source of strong ethnic identity. Results highlight the importance of facilitating ethnic minority youths to search for their ethnic history and understand the meaning of their ethnic practices and traditions. The process of searching for the meaning of own ethnicity and understanding it is the foundation for positive development. Establishing a positive familial and school environment is also crucial for building strong ethnic identity and thus positive well-being in ethnic minority young people.

12604418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12604418.value: 在人際互動中，參與者成功溝通與否，取決於他們能否辨識到大家透過語言和非語言途徑流露的情感訊號。自閉症譜系障礙(ASD)患者有社交和溝通困難。對他們來說，拆解情感訊號甚具挑戰性，因而影響他們在學校、閒暇、工作環境中的人際互動。本研究旨在檢視ASD兒童對比典型發展(TD)兒童在識別情感語氣的能力。就此題目，過往的研究有不一致的結果。雖然部分研究顯示ASD兒童能識別情感語氣(e.g. Lyons et al., 2014) ，但不能排除一個可能性： ASD兒童和TD兒童可能運用不同的內在機制去以處理情感語氣的訊息。為進一步探究其可能性，本研究第二個目的是檢測ASD兒童在辨識情緒刺激時，會否較TD兒童更依賴心理聲學能力，其中包括快速聽覺處理和音調方向辨識能力。最後，本研究會探討心理聲學能力的聽覺訓練能否協助改善ASD兒童的情感語氣辨認能力。本研究將招募年屆十至十二歲的ASD兒童和TD兒童各四十名。於前測階段，我們將檢測參加者的心理聲學能力與情感語氣辨認能力。我們假設，相較TD兒童而言， ASD兒童的心理聲學能力能更準確地預測其情感語氣辨認能力。接著，這些ASD兒童將獲隨機分配至兩組：一組將接受聽覺訓練，另一組將接受非聽覺訓練，以作對照。兩組兒童均需透過手機應用程式接受十二小時訓練。然後，所有兒童將於後測階段再次接受評估。本研究假定只有接受聽覺訓練的兒童，其心理聲學能力會顯著改善，而接受非聽覺訓練的兒童則沒有任何明顯變化；本研究進一步假定，心理聲學能力顯著改善的兒童，他們的情感語氣辨認能力亦會因此提升。以研究重要性而言，本研究初探以實證方法改善ASD兒童的情感語氣辨認能力。我們希望改善ASD兒童拆解聲音中情感訊號的能力，使他們能更有效地與別人溝通，從而改善他們的生活質數。

To explore the daily parental practices of urban singleton parents by specifically investigating how they perform three main parental duties: physical care, emotional care, and the moral discipline of children. To examine conjugal relations in the context of childcare and compare the gendered labor division, conjugal collaboration, negotiation, struggle, and even conflict in childcare between singleton and non-singleton parents in urban China. To investigate how intergenerational relations are reconstructed in childcare and to compare the intergenerational collaboration in childcare between singleton and non-singleton parents. To deepen the understanding of Chinese parenthood, and enrich the theoretical discussion on parenthood in general, by analyzing parenting as relational practices constructed by multiple family members, revealing how gender egalitarian values and increased intergenerational interdependence shape singleton parenting and how gender and intergenerational collaboration is reconciled in their childcare.
