13602818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13602818.value: There is little doubt that causal reasoning and counterfactual reasoning (about what would or might be the case if things were different) are closely related. It is thus reasonable to expect that successful formal tools for the former and those for the latter should bear interesting and illuminating relationships. In this project we aim to carry out in-depth investigations into the relationship between two such formal tools and explore the philosophical implications of our results. Both objects of our study are influential: one is the framework of structural equation models (SEMs), which is widely used to model causal systems and is gaining ground in the philosophical literature; the other is the Stalnaker-Lewis possible-world semantics for counterfactual conditionals, which remains one of the most popular and best known semantics for counterfactuals in philosophy. Broadly speaking, we will pursue two approaches in our investigations. The first is a standard semantical approach, where the two frameworks are compared with respect to what logics of counterfactuals they validate. There are already a few interesting results of this kind in the literature, but most of them are restricted to a special class of SEMs, known as recursive causal models. A distinction of our inquiry is to also consider non-recursive causal models, which are commonly seen in practice. Building on some preliminary results that the PI has established, we plan to attack a number of questions, including at least two questions that we believe may interest a wide audience: (1) Are there methodological justifications for the constraints on SEMs that the PI has identified, and to what extent do the models used in practice conform to them? (2) How to extend SEMs to model non-causal determination (such as "supervenience") alongside causal determination? The second approach will take our inquiry to a higher level of generality and abstraction. We will examine the two formalisms from a category theoretic perspective. Roughly speaking, category theory is the mathematical study of transformations between structures, both within a category (which consists of objects and mappings between objects) and across categories. We aim to construct categories of SEMs and of possible-world models, respectively, and study their relationship by investigating whether certain transformations exist between the categories (called "adjoint functors") that reflect a close relationship. We expect that this mathematically sophisticated approach will also deliver philosophical payoffs by, for example, revealing new and plausible constraints on theorizing about the relationship between causation and counterfactuals. 因果推理同反實推理（即關於與事實不同的假想境況的推理）通常被認爲關係密切。若果如此，適合此兩種推理的形式工具之間多半也有值得探究的關係。基於這個思路，本課題試圖深入探究兩個重要形式工具之間的數學關係以及其哲學意義。其中一個是結構方程模型，乃處理因果推理最重要的工具之一，近來在與因果相關的哲學文獻中常被提及。另一個是處理反實條件句的可能世界模型，是哲學界最廣爲人知的理解反實條件句的工具。 大略説來，本課題的探究會嘗試兩個進路。第一個進路是標準的語義學進路，比較兩個框架下的條件句邏輯。這個進路已經产生了一些有趣的結果，但文獻裏大多數的工作都只考慮一類特殊的結構方程模型，即所謂遞歸的結構方程模型。本課題的一個特點是打破這個限制，不排除在應用中常見的非遞歸的結構方程模型。在此進路下，至少有兩個問題值得關注：一，從此比較中得出的對結構方程模型的一些限制是否有方法論上的依據和意义？二，如何拓寬結構方程模型的框架以便同時處理非因果的依賴關係（比如哲學家經常討論的“隨附”關係）和因果的依賴關係？ 我們期望開拓的第二個進路有更大的一般性和抽象性，會從範疇論的角度來審視這兩個形式工具。範疇論是數學中對結構變換的一種抽象研究，包括同一範疇中結構的變換（一個範疇由一組對象和對象之間的態射構成）和範疇之間的變換。在本課題中我們會分別構造結構方程模型的範疇和可能世界模型的範疇，然後探究是否存在揭示兩範疇間緊密聯係的變換（所謂的“伴隨函子”）。同時我們也會思考如何用此類數學結果來啓發和規範關於因果和反實條件句的哲學理論。

13602818.label: Realisation of objectives
13602818.value: This project was carried out at a rather difficult time, not only because of the pandemic, but also due to a family disaster that occupied the PI for almost a year (December 2019 to November 2020). Fortunately, we took advantage of the additional year after the project officially ended and worked out important results in 2021. We are especially happy with some of these results; they not only sufficiently address the project objectives but also suggest important questions to be further investigated. Regarding the first objective, we worked out an exact characterisation of structural equation models that can be embedded in possible worlds models satisfying Stalnaker's conditions, and an exact characterisation of those that can be embedded in possible worlds models satisfying Lewis's conditions. It is worth noting, however, that these results were obtained in a traditional, combinatorial framework. In view of the new framework developed in connection to the second objective, we now believe that these characterisations should take a much more general and intuitive form, not restricted to deterministic structural equation models. We also developed a generalisation of the standard framework of structural equation models for multi-level causal modelling, with which we hope to illuminate a host of issues in philosophy and in machine learning, including interventionist conditionals, supervenient causation, ambiguous intervention effects, and macro variable construction. The PI presented this generalisation in several international conferences/workshops but discovered that the central idea overlapped significantly with prior work by Joe Halpern and Chris Hitchcock. While we tried to differentiate our proposal from the Hitchcock-Halpern one, we realised that the more important and interesting question is how to choose the right levels of granularity for causal variables. This problem is not only directly relevant to some technical work one of the Co-Is (Eberhardt) has done previously with computer vision researchers at Caltech, but also suggests an interesting spin on the philosophical question of supervenient causation. In particular, we distinguished two questions, the cause-of-effect (COE) question and the effect-of-cause (EOC) question. The former is about choosing the right or best level of granularity for the effect-variable given a cause-variable of interest, whereas the latter is about choosing the right or best level of granularity for the cause-variable given an effect-variable of interest. In the philosophical literature, the COE question (or its variants) have drawn almost all the attention and the EOC question is rarely discussed. This is probably due to an implicit assumption or expectation that they are two sides of the same coin. We think this is a mistake; at least for causal modelling and reasoning in practice, an account to address the COE question does not automatically settle the EOC question. Although the two questions are obviously related, they need separate treatments. With this conviction, we carried out two investigations. On the COE question, the PI collaborated with a philosopher of biology, Wei Fang, and generalised Stephen Yablo's original formulation of the now influential proportionality condition to a probabilistic setting. The resulting account provides a plausible answer to the COE question and has several virtues in comparison to previous proposals, or so we argue in a paper currently under review. On the EOC question, our initial idea was that an account that is dual to the proportionality account for the COE question would fit the bill. While the proportionality account for COE favours more general, higher-level cause-variables over more specific, lower-level ones, provided that a screening-off condition is satisfied, the dual account for EOC favours more specific, lower-level effect-variables over more general, higher-level ones, provided that the same screening-off condition is satisfied. Neat as this idea is (at least as we see it), the proposal actually implies several complications that are not present in the COE question, because fine-graining or coarse-graining an effect-variable involves changes of the relevant interventional probabilities that do not arise in fine-graining or coarse-graining a cause-variable. We believe we have identified all the relevant considerations, and we are finalising a paper to discuss the various complications associated with the dual account. How best to address these complications, however, is an important problem to be further investigated. So much for the first objective. In relation to the second objective, our work experienced more downs than ups until the summer of 2021, when we finally got two breakthroughs. The first breakthrough originated from our decision to carry out a deeper and more thorough analysis of a special kind of morphism constructed by Brendan Fong in a category he calls "causal theory". This turned out to be a very fruitful inquiry. Among other things, we derived a more abstract and generic calculus of interventions, in the sense that its probabilistic intervention yields Judea Pearl's celebrated do-calculus, but it is applicable to all other interpretations of the causal theory. More importantly, it takes a much simpler form than the standard do-calculus, and is conceptually illuminating because it clearly separates causal reasoning and probabilistic reasoning. There is an even more significant fruit borne by this breakthrough. Inspired by our results on the generic do-calculus, we developed a new perspective on a central notion in much of the philosophical and mathematical work on causality, the notion of modularity. In the literature, modularity of causal processes is usually understood as independent manipulability of the processes or some sort of independence (e.g., algorithmic independence) between the processes. But there is no precise formal definition of the notion, and there is no general result on how some facts of modularity entail other facts. By contrast, our new definition of modularity is in terms of composability of a certain kind, which can be rigorously expressed in category theory and intuitively represented by a so-called string diagram. With the precise formal definition in hand, we are able to derive sufficient and necessary conditions for modularity in terms of graphical separation, which is potentially applicable to the practical problem of causal discovery. The second breakthrough was in our attempt to construct a transformation between causal theories to capture the operation of intervention. After trying for a long while, we found an elegant "contravariant" construction of the transformation that proves to be functorial. (By contrast, an existing construction in the literature is "covariant", which we reject because it is not functorial.) With this device, we reformulated the problem of causal effect identification and saw several new open questions that were not apparent in the old framework. Moreover, in trying to prove the functoriality in question (as well as some aforementioned results), we also established a graphical construction of the so-called free Markov categories, which may be of independent interest to category theorists. Finally, regarding the third objective, we produced a number of manuscripts related to the first or second objective, sometimes in collaboration with other computer scientists or philosophers. Some of them were published or submitted, but a couple are currently in the form of a technical report or a first draft, which need a little more work before they are submitted. So, at this point, we take the publication goal to have been 85% achieved rather than 100%.

13602818.label: Major findings and research outcome
13602818.value: 1. We proposed a generalisation of Yablo's influential notion of proportionality to probabilistic settings to answer the COE question (what is the best cause-variable relative to a given effect-variable?), which improved upon the existing accounts, and provided a justification of the answer in terms of informativeness. This finding is reported in a paper coauthored with Wei Fang, which is currently under review. 2. We motivated the EOC question (what is the best effect-variable relative to a given cause-variable?), developed a dual account to address EOC, and identified several important disanalogies between COE and EOC. This finding was presented, either by the PI or by a Co-I (Eberhardt), in several conferences or workshops, including an APA Meeting, a causality conference organised by Harvard University, and a causality forum organised by Shandong University. We are currently revising a rough draft on this finding. 3. We further developed a category-theoretic framework for causal reasoning and derived a generic do-calculus that is simpler, conceptually clearer, and more widely applicable than the standard do-calculus. The PI presented this finding in several conferences, including an occasion of keynote speech (at the 8th International Conference on Logic, Rationality, and Interaction). A paper on this finding has been accepted by the journal Studies in Logic. In addition, the PI published a paper in the journal Theoria arguing that observational and experimental causal inference are unified in that they both amount to finding ways to make the do-calculus applicable. 4. We discovered a new perspective to define and study the notion of modularity for causal systems, which can be rigorously expressed in the language of category theory. We established sufficient and necessary graphical conditions for modularity in a causal theory, which can be used to unify the rules of the do-calculus. The PI presented this finding in a couple of conferences, including one in the industry (Huawei's Strategy and Technology Workshop). This finding is currently presented in a technical report. 5. We found an elegant way to construct transformations between causal theories that incorporates the standard operation of intervention, and we showed how the causal effect identification problem can be fruitfully reformulated in our framework. This finding is currently also presented in the technical report. 6. We also collaborated with computer scientists on practical problems of causal reasoning and inference. Three co-authored papers were published in top conference proceedings in AI (NeurIPS, ICML, and IJCAI), and another one is currently under review.

13602818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13602818.value: We perceive quite some potential for further development of this research, especially in connection to the category-theoretic treatment of reasoning about interventions. Let us highlight four further lines of research suggested by our findings. First, we would like to further explore tradeoffs between different considerations in answering the EOC question. Second, it is our plan to study possibilistic causal models (in contrast to probabilistic causal models and deterministic causal models), which correspond to functors from a causal theory to the category of relations (in contrast to the category of statistical mappings and the category of functions). We suspect our results about the correspondence between structural equation models and Lewisian possible worlds models may be derived more easily and elegantly, and in a more general fashion, from the abstract perspective. Third, another salient possibility of application of our generic do-calculus is to quantum causal models, if such models constitute suitable interpretations of a causal theory. Fourth, our functorial construction of transformations between causal theories probably have more implications or applications than we have pointed out. There is a consensus in the team that we will continue to tackle these questions and seek further funding, if needed.

13602818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13602818.value: This research project is in the main a theoretical - logical, mathematical and philosophical - investigation of a topic that is of utmost practical significance, the topic of reasoning about cause and effect, and about what would happen under hypothetical (or counterfactual) interventions. We all seek causal understandings of the connections among myriad phenomena in life, and we employ reasoning about interventions for the purpose of controlling environments and making changes. It is therefore crucial in many contexts to get causal reasoning right. Among other things, this research project developed a new mathematical framework and perspective to study causal reasoning, and illustrated the power of the new framework by showing how the results obtained in the traditional framework could be generalised, improved and illuminated in the new framework. We expect the new framework to yield many more sights about the logic and science of causal inference. The insights thus obtained, we believe, will be not only theoretically illuminating but also practically useful, as evidenced by the fact that when some of the findings of this project were presented to researchers in the industry, they apparently found the theoretical results exceedingly interesting.

13603718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13603718.value: This project aims to apply the methodology of conceptual engineering to critique several aspects of contemporary analytic epistemology. ‘Conceptual engineering’ is an approach to philosophical methodology which contrasts with the more traditional ‘conceptual analysis’. While the latter might be characterized as a descriptive study of the concepts we employ in ordinary life, the former is a prescriptive enterprise – it recommends modifications of our current concepts, or even replacements. These modifications address deficiencies in our current concepts – for instance, by remedying unclarity or vagueness, or by offering a concept that better serves the purposes of the original. The goal of the project, then, is to ‘re-engineer’ our core epistemological concepts. Contemporary analytic epistemology has been dominated by a focus on knowledge, with a large proportion of the epistemology of the 20th century attempting to provide a conceptual analysis of knowledge. No attempt has yet been successful – all seem to fail to counterexamples – and recent epistemology has been, to some degree, diversifying its aims and approaches. Recent research focuses, for instance, on such topics as the value of knowledge and the nature of epistemic norms. The current project will build on some of this recent work, while simultaneously critiquing its continued attachment to the epistemological framework shaped by analysis-driven approaches of the 20th century. The project will consist of four articles. The first article will employ the conceptual engineering perspective to generate a set of desiderata for revised epistemological concepts. It will, for instance, explore the role that current epistemic concepts play in the regulation of belief formation and evaluation, communication, and so forth, in order to extract plausible ‘functions’ that successor epistemic concepts may more effectively fulfill. The second article will propose a novel theory of knowledge, inspired by the conceptual engineering approach. The view will propose that the levels of justification required for knowing vary depending on the availability of resources and information to the subject. The third and fourth articles will explore the idea that a re-engineered epistemology will reduce current focus on the knowledge concept – that alternate epistemological categories will take on increased importance. The third article will explore whether alternate categories are needed to deal with inquiry conducted at a group level – for instance, in a courtroom, or in academic disciplines. The final article will apply a conceptual engineering perspective to a recently popular, but traditionally philosophically neglected, epistemic category – understanding. 本研究項目旨在應用概念工程的方法來批判現代知識論的一些發展。概念工程與傳統分析哲學的概念分析不同。概念工程主要是規範性的，研究如何修改甚至替換我們現有的概念，用以糾正它們不足的地方。本研究項目正是希望重新設計我們一些有關知識的核心概念。 當代知識論以探討知識為主。二十世紀的研究，集中於如何分析知識這個概念，但至仍然今未有令人滿意的答案。知識論的目的和方法近年開始多樣化，例如會探討知識的價值和規範。本研究項目將會建基於這些新發展，同時延續對二十世紀知識論理論架構的批判。 本研究項目將由四篇文章組成。第一篇討論概念工程對知識概念作出修改時應達到的標準。第二篇對知識提出一套新的理論，指出知識的理據如何因應資源或者信息而有不同程度之分。第三篇文章會討論不同範疇的認知探求會否需要運用知識以外的替代概念。第四篇文章會應用概念工程處理「理解」這一個知識論裡面備受忽略的題目。

13603718.label: Realisation of objectives
13603718.value: The proposed output for this grant was a series of four related papers on the topic of conceptual engineering, particularly as applied to epistemology. Three of the four initial planned papers were completed as planned. My initial ideas for the fourth planned paper, on applications of conceptual engineering to group epistemology, did not end up developing to my satisfaction and I have set this topic aside for the time being. In replacement for this fourth planned paper, however, I have written two additional papers on the methodological underpinnings of the approach I have employed in the three aforementioned 'applied' papers (that is, those originally proposed in the project application). The contents of the five papers are briefly outlined below. The first paper, outlining desiderata for the re-engineering of ‘Knowledge’, is now published at Inquiry under the title “Re-engineering knowledge: A case study in pluralist conceptual engineering”. In addition to exploring the various roles our current concept of knowledge performs, this paper broaches the possibility that optimally satisfying these various roles might call for conceptual features pulling in incompatible directions, thereby raising the possibility of engineering a plurality of successor-concepts. The second paper, co-authored with Joachim Horvath and addressing whether an ideal knowledge-concept ought to be sensitive to the available resources (cognitive and otherwise) of the subject, is now published in Synthese unter the title “Knowledge and Normality”. We discuss the roles our current concept of knowledge performs (echoing conclusions from the paper described above), and argue that one feature that effective fulfilment of these roles demand is a ‘threshold’ that is sensitive to the ‘normal’ level of cognitive support that members of a given epistemic community typically achieve. A threshold that is thus ‘anchored’ to contingent, a posteriori features of the local persons and environment thereby prevents our knowledge-concept from becoming problematically overdemanding. The third paper, exploring a conceptual engineering approach to understanding, will be an invited contribution to a Synthese Library book series volume entitled "New Perspectives on Conceptual Engineering", edited by Manuel Gustavo Isaac. This paper, entitled “Conceptual engineering, the value of knowledge, and the value of understanding”, argues that many of the roles that the knowledge-concept performs for us cannot be equally well filled by the concept of understanding - thereby casting doubt on the idea that epistemologists ought to ‘refocus’ their theoretical efforts on understanding while de-prioritizing knowledge. The paper does, however, argue for distinct yet less common roles that understanding serves more effectively than knowledge, thus supporting the claim that understanding is a currently under-explored concept within epistemology. As mentioned above, I was not satisfied with the current quality of the arguments I had in mind for the paper on group epistemology. As a substitute, I took the opportunity to further develop and refine the ‘functionalist’ theoretical framework for conceptual engineering that has underwritten the above-mentioned core papers for the project (as described in e.g. the ‘research details’ section of the initial proposal). The result was two papers elaborating my own theoretical stance on conceptual engineering, which I know call the ‘practical role account’. The first of these two papers, entitled “Taking control: conceptual engineering without (much) metasemantics”, argues against the common assumption that metasemantics significantly constrains the practice of conceptual engineering. I detail my own ‘practical role account’, which casts engineering as the process of improving a representational device’s ability to serve a variety of purposes which make up its ‘practical role’. I contrast this with standard functionalist accounts, which tend to more narrowly focus on a ‘core’ function. I then argue that my own position is compatible with essentially any metasemantic view, and that the metasemantic facts do not place any constraints on the practice of engineering as conceived by the practical role account. This paper has now been published in Inquiry. The second of the two papers follows up on a feature of the practical role account briefly explored in the previous paper – the claim that the proper target of conceptual engineering is neither concepts nor natural language expressions, but instead ‘classification procedures’. Classification procedures are, very simply, methods for sorting entities into categories; such methods might be associated with various terms or concepts, but we need not commit ourselves to the idea that these methods determine or constitute the meanings of said terms or concepts. By taking classification procedures as our targets, we can successfully keep conceptual engineering metasemantically neutral. This allows us to claim that functions or practical roles determine the conditions for success in conceptual engineering, without tying us to any further claims about the relationship between said functions/roles and meaning or content. One does not, for instance, need to be an inferential role theorist about conceptual content to endorse an approach to conceptual engineering that focuses on inferential roles. This final paper is entitled “Classification procedures as the targets of conceptual engineering”, and has been published in Philosophy and Phenomenological Research. Ultimately, four out of five objectives were fully met; the fifth, which concerned the currently-set-aside paper, I have marked as 10% progress to reflect the initial research (largely, familiarizing myself with relevant literature) that occurred before determining that the paper could not be completed to my satisfaction during the grant time frame. I would, in retrospect, add to these initially proposed objectives a further objective which emerged during the grant period – that of refining and codifying the theoretical characterization of conceptual engineering that undergirds the three core papers of the project. The ‘substituted’ two additional papers, detailing what I now call the practical role account, serve to fulfil this objective.

13603718.label: Major findings and research outcome
13603718.value: Three of the four initial planned papers were completed as planned; two of these are published at Synthese and Inquiry respectively, and a third will be an invited contribution to a Synthese Library book series volume entitled "New Perspectives on Conceptual Engineering", edited by Manuel Gustavo Isaac. My initial ideas for the fourth planned paper, on applications of conceptual engineering to group epistemology, did not end up developing to my satisfaction and I have set this topic aside for the time being. In replacement for this fourth planned paper, however, I have written two additional papers on the methodological underpinnings of the approach I have employed in the three aforementioned 'applied' papers (that is, those originally proposed in the project application). One of these additional papers has been published in Inquiry; another in Philosophy and Phenomenological Research. The output of the project thus consists of two complementary groups of papers - the three 'application' papers, which apply my preferred approach to conceptual engineering to the traditional philosophical concepts of knowledge and understanding, and the two 'theoretical' papers, which provide further exploration of more abstract methodological questions pertaining to the approach I have employed in the application papers. The papers developed during the project period represent a substantial elaboration of the overall theoretical framework that I have defended within the conceptual engineering literature - namely, what I now call the 'practical role' approach. The 'theoretical' papers explore, in greater depth than my previous work, the idea that conceptual 'inventions' should be evaluated by their suitability to a practical role - and the related claim that this evaluation can proceed in the absence of significant metasemantic commitment. The 'applied' papers, meanwhile, make use of this role-driven approach to provide 'case studies' exploring the practical roles the concepts of knowledge and understanding play in our cognitive lives, and ultimately suggesting potential alterations to traditional philosophical approaches to these concepts.

13603718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13603718.value: Though my initial ideas for a paper on group epistemology did not pan out as planned, I have not given up on the idea entirely - one future development for this research will hopefully involve a return to the topic of group epistemology, though perhaps from a different angle. More broadly, the applied 'case study' papers explore a format that I believe could be expanded upon in the future, targeting either additional epistemological concepts or concepts from other philosophical fields. Future papers, then, would attempt to apply the developed 'practical role' approach to conceptual engineering to additional targets. Finally, though I have substantially elaborated the 'practical role' account during the project period, there is still substantial room for further 'theoretical' articles detailing the theory of conceptual engineering that has underpinned the current project.

13603718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13603718.value: Conceptual engineering is a novel approach within philosophy which aims to revise our concepts (rather than merely 'analyze' them, as more traditional approaches aim to do). The current project both elaborates and applies a particular theory of conceptual engineering, which I call the 'practical role' account. On the practical role account, concepts are evaluated by how successfully they perform the practical roles they play in our cognitive lives. This project explores the practical roles of the traditional philosophical concepts of knowledge and understanding; I investigate, for instance, the idea that the knowledge-concept serves a key role in evaluating the assertions and actions of others, that it serves to help identify reliable informants, and so forth. Ultimately, I provide evaluations of the degree to which the concepts of knowledge and understanding succeed in effectively filling these various roles, and suggest potential avenues for revision or even replacement of these familiar concepts.

14100018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100018.value: Skeletal muscle allows voluntary movement and plays a key role in regulating metabolism and homeostasis in the organism. Meanwhile it has a remarkable ability to regenerate after injury thus provides an excellent model to study tissue regeneration. Muscle regeneration relies on its resident muscle stem cells (also called satellite cells, SCs) which normally lie quiescently beneath muscle fiber. SCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergoes self-renewal and returns to quiescent state to replenish the adult stem cell pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulations may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia that are prevalent in our society. As a recently discovered family of cellular regulators, long noncoding RNAs (>200nt non-protein coding RNAs, lncRNAs) are remarkably powerful, flexible, and pervasive in controlling major biological processes. However, despite efforts from our groups and others in the past few years, our understanding of lncRNA participation in SC activities remains largely elusive. Here we propose to study the function of a previously uncharacterized lncRNA, Linc-p27 in promoting myogenic lineage progression. In pilot studies, loss- and gain-of-function assays demonstrated a potential role of Linc-p27 in promoting SC activation and proliferation. Mechanistic elucidation revealed it binds with RNA helicase Dhx36 and facilitates mRNA translation by unwinding 5’UTR quadruplex (rG4) structures. These preliminary results lead us to hypothesize that Linc-p27 plays active role in SC functionality and muscle regeneration. Three aims were proposed to (1) further elucidate how Linc-p27 regulates satellite cell behavior and muscle regeneration; (2) further dissect how Linc-p27 and Dhx36 modulate SC proliferation; (3) examine how Linc-p27 and Dhx36 facilitate translation through unwinding rG4 structures. Once completed, this study will for the first time uncover Linc-p27 as a novel regulator of SC function and muscle regeneration; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. 骨骼肌參與控制自主運動，並在調節代謝及維持體內穩態中起著重要的調控作用。同時骨骼肌在損傷後具有極強的再生能力，為研究組織再生提供了一個非常好的模型。肌肉再生主要歸功於附著於骨骼肌纖維上的幹細胞（也被稱作衛星細胞）。這些細胞通常處於靜息狀態，但當肌肉受損時會迅速激活，增殖並分化形成新的肌纖維來修復受損肌肉。其中一小部分細胞具有自我更新能力，能夠回到靜息狀態，維持肌肉幹細胞群。再生過程中的每一步都受到內源和外源因子構成的基因調控網絡的精確控制,破壞該網絡會導致SC失去再生能力和相關疾病的發生，例如肌肉萎縮，惡病質和骨骼肌衰老等普遍存在的疾病。近年來長非編碼RNA（> 200nt非蛋白質編碼RNA，lncRNA）在多種生理及病理過程中的重要調控作用不斷被發現，但其在骨骼肌幹細胞中的功能及調控機制還鮮有研究。在該課題中，我們將研究一個全新的lncRNA Linc-p27 在調控骨骼肌幹細胞功能中的作用及其機制。在預實驗中，敲除或獲得功能性實驗結果顯示Linc-p27 可能促進骨骼肌幹細胞的激活和增殖。機制研究揭示Linc-p27 能夠和RNA解旋酶Dhx36結合，幫助Dhx36解旋mRNA 5’UTR的G-quaduplex（rG4）結構並促進mRNA的翻譯。這些初步的實驗結果提示Linc-p27 可能在調控骨骼肌幹細胞功能及肌肉再生中有著重要的作用。 為此我們提出以下三個研究目標：（1）進一步分析Linc-p27 如何調控骨骼肌幹細胞功能和肌肉再生。（2）繼續深入分析Linc-p27 和Dhx36在調控骨骼肌幹細胞增殖中的作用。（3）解析Linc-p27 和Dhx36是如何通過解旋rG4結構來對翻譯過程進行調控。課題的實施將首次揭示Linc-p27 對骨骼幹細胞功能和肌肉再生的調控，加強我們對肌肉再生內源調控網絡的認知，可望為相關疾病的治療提供新的思路和靶點。

14100018.label: Realisation of objectives
14100018.value: Objective 1: To further elucidate how Linc-p27 (Lockd) regulates satellite cell behavior and muscle regeneration. 1.1. To examine Linc-p27 (Lockd) KO cells. We inactivated Lockd expression in C2C12 mouse myoblast cell line using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing with both KO (the promoter and the first exon of Lockd were deleted) and KI (a polyA cassette inserted in the immediate downstream of the transcription start site TSS to cause pre-mature termination of the nascent Lockd transcript) strategies. Both homozygous KO and KI lines showed decreased proliferation ability compared to wild type (WT) control examined by EdU and MTS assays. Moreover, WT, Lockd KO and Lockd KI cells were treated with nocodazole to inhibit mitosis and the following cell cycle analysis revealed that both Lockd KO and Lockd KI clones showed obvious G0&G1 arrest compared to the WT cells. 1.2. To analyze Linc-p27 (Lockd) regulation of muscle regeneration in vivo. We knocked down Lockd in the regenerating muscles using an siRNA injection-based strategy. Briefly, siLockd or siNC oligos were intramuscularly injected into the TA muscle at days 1 and 2 after BaCl2 injection. Decreased MyoD mRNA level was examined by qRT-PCR and declined number of MyoD positive cells was observed when IF staining was performed on the above TA sections at 3 dpi. Moreover, the number of newly formed myofibers with CLN on the cross sections was decreased in siLockd vs siNC mice at 7 dpi, indicating the regenerating ability was compromised when Lockd level was decreased. Meanwhile, we also stained the sections for eMyHC at 7dpi, and a higher number of eMyHC+ myofibers was observed in siLockd vs siNC group, suggesting the delayed regeneration process and maturation of fibers. Consistently, a higher level of eMyHC protein was also detected by Western blot from the siLockd injected muscles. To ascertain the above observed proliferative defect of SCs upon Lockd loss, the TA and GAS muscles of Pax7 nGFP mice in which Pax7-expressing SCs are marked by GFP was injured by BaCl2 injection and injected with siNC or siLockd oligos at 1 dpi. EdU was injected intraperitoneally at 2 dpi and the GFP-positive SCs were sorted out 12 hours later for EdU staining. Expectedly, a decreased number of EdU+ cells was detected upon Lockd knock-down. 1.3. To examine human Linc-p27 (Lockd) function. When searching for homologous genes of mouse Lockd in human genome, interestingly, no annotated ncRNAs were found at the downstream of human CDKN1B gene; instead, the exon 1 of mouse Lockd displayed high similarity with the exon of an isoform of human APOLD1 mRNA (NM_001130415) and its exon 2 is also highly similar with the intron of this isoform, suggesting the possible presence of an unannotated ncRNA in human genome. Indeed, transcriptional signals were detected from the regions by examining the RNA-seq data from proliferating human myoblast and differentiated myocyte cells which was significantly decreased upon differentiation, despite the unchanged level of APOLD1 mRNA. Knockdown of the human LOCKD in human myoblast cells by siRNA oligos also hindered cell proliferation, confirming that human LOCKD is functionally conserved with mouse Lockd. Objective 2. To further dissect how Linc-p27 (Lockd) /Dhx36 modulate SC proliferation. 2.1. To further confirm the biochemical interaction between Linc-p27 (Lockd) and Dhx36. We employed selective 2’hydoxyl acylation analyses by primer extension (SHAPE) reagent, 2-methylnicotinic acid imidazolide (NAI), that could selectively acylate the 2’-hydroxyl group of flexible RNA nucleotides, which allows to infer single-stranded regions in RNA molecule at single nucleotide resolution. As Lockd is long (407 nucleotides in length), 6 different Cy5-labeled reverse transcription primers were designed to cover and map the secondary structure of full-length Lockd. Using RNAstructure software, we then delineated the experimentally-guided Lockd secondary structure. In an attempt to identify the region of Lockd that interacts with DHX36, three Lockd RNA fragments, F1 (51-203), F2 (205-310) and F3 (1-48 and 326-407), were designed based on the above derived structural model and their binding with DHX36 was examined using EMSA assay. All three fragments were shown to interact with DHX36 protein, but it appeared that F1 showed the highest binding affinity compared to the F2 and F3 fragments; a complete shifting was observed at 190 nM concentration of DHX36 protein for F1, while both F2 and F3 required at least 950 nM of DHX36 protein. These findings suggest that F1 in the Lockd possesses the highest binding affinity with DHX36 protein. 2.2. To further analyze effects of Dhx36 loss in SCs. In a separate study (Chen et al, Nature Communications, 2021), we demonstrated that inducible deletion of DHX36 in SCs impaired myoblast proliferation and muscle regeneration in vivo. Furthermore, Dhx36 KO cells also displayed an arrest in G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle compared with WT cells when cells were treated with nocodazole and synchronized in G2/M phase, which photocopied the impact of Lockd loss. Objective 3. To examine how Linc-p27 (Lockd) /Dhx36 facilitate translation through unwinding rG4s. 3.1. To high throughput profile rG4 structures in myoblast cells. We profiled the rG4 structure in C2C12 myoblast cells with the help of our collaborator Prof. Kwok. However, due to the depth issue of the sequencing, we used bioinformatic prediction of G4 formation in our publication. 3.2. To high throughput profile Dhx36 binding targets in myoblast cells. We published DHX36 CLIP-seq data in another paper (Chen et al., 2021), with a total of 1262 transcripts were identified to be bound by DHX36 among which 458 were predicted to form 5’UTR rG4s. By GO analysis, 175 of these genes were related to cell proliferation and growth which is in accordance with the demonstrated functionality of Lockd/DHX36, thus considered to be possible downstream effectors of Lockd. 3.3. To test whether Linc-p27 (Lockd) /Dhx36 facilitate target gene translation by unwinding rG4. We identified Anp32e mRNA as a target for Lockd/Dhx36 regulation. The G4 formation at the 5’UTR of Anp32e mRNA was confirmed using CD and G4 intrinsic fluorescence assay. We also found that knockdown of Lockd led to a significant decrease in Anp32 protein but not mRNA. To expand the above study scope, we explored additional translational targets of Lockd/DHX36 by conducting polysome profiling coupled with RNA-seq to examine the global translational status of mRNAs in WT and Lockd KO myoblast cells. Translational efficiency (TE) of each mRNAs was calculated. By integrating with the DHX36 CLIP-seq data, 25 and 601 DHX36 bound mRNAs displayed TE down- or up-regulation respectively, suggesting these mRNAs could be potential translational targets of Lockd/DHX36. Lastly, we elucidated how Lockd/DHX36 interaction affects Anp32e translation in further depth. First, we screened for protein binding partners of DHX36 in myoblast cells by conducting immunoprecipitation followed by MS in WT and Dhx36 KO cells. GO analysis showed genes encoding these proteins were closely related with translation and translational initiation etc. Multiple members of eukaryotic initiation factor 3 (eIF3) complex were included, among which EIF3B caught our attention because it was also immunoprecipitated by Lockd as a potential interacting partner, suggesting an interesting possibility that Lockd may scaffold DHX36 and EIF3B to stabilize their interaction. When Co-IP was conducted in WT, Lockd KI or KO cells, the interaction between DHX36 and EIF3B was impaired, suggesting that Lockd indeed stabilizes their interaction. Knocking down EIF3B significantly inhibited myoblast proliferation, which phenocopied Lockd and DHX36 loss in myoblasts.

14100018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100018.value: In this study we identify a lncRNA, Lockd (named as Linc-p27 when we submitted the proposal) which is induced in activated SCs upon acute muscle injury. We demonstrate that Lockd promotes SC proliferation; deletion of Lockd leads to cell cycle arrest; in vivo repression of Lockd in mouse muscles hinders regeneration process. Mechanistically, we uncover that Lockd directly interacts with RNA helicase DHX36 and the 5’end of Lockd possesses the strongest binding with DHX36. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Lockd stabilizes the interaction between DHX36 and EIF3B proteins, and synergistically this complex unwinds the RNA G-quadruplex (rG4) structure formed at Anp32e mRNA 5’UTR and promotes the translation of ANP32E protein which is required for myoblast proliferation. Altogether, our findings identify a regulatory Lockd/DHX36/Anp32e axis that promotes myoblast proliferation and acute injury induced muscle regeneration. Our findings were published on Cell Reports, Nature Communications and other Journals with high impact. Our work was also presented in international meetings to increase exposure to peer researchers. Moreover, two PhD students obtained their PhD degree with the support of this project.

14100018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100018.value: We characterized the functional role of Lockd in regulating SC activity and muscle regeneration in this study. We demonstrate that Lockd functions to promote the proliferative expansion of myoblasts in vitro and in vivo during the regeneration process. Further mechanistic investigation reveals that Lockd which mainly localizes in the cytoplasm of the myoblasts functions by binding with DHX36 protein and further to stabilize DHX36 interaction with EIF3B protein, together the complex unwinds the rG4 structure formed in the 5’UTR of Anp32e mRNA to promote its translation. Using the CLIP-seq, polysome profiling and Mass spec data of Dhx36 binding proteins, we could further investigate the molecular mechanisms of how Dhx36 regulate mRNA translation. Moreover, since the regenerative capacity of SC declines with aging, which is correlated with muscle aging related disease, e.g. sarcopenia, we could also explore the functional role of Dhx36 regulation of mRNA translation in SC aging process.

14100018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100018.value: Adult muscle stem cells, also known as satellite cells (SCs) play pivotal roles in muscle regeneration and long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) functions in SCs remains largely unknown. 14100118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100118.value: Aim The objective of this project is to explain the immune response moderating mechanisms of the novel fundamental inhibitor of innate immunity, IL-37, in the widely prevalent and chronic disease known as atopic dermatitis (AD). Project Background AD is a chronically relapsing inflammatory skin disease that affects nearly 20% of Hong Kong schoolchildren. Bacterial skin infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus is associated with chronic inflammation and morbidity in AD. Activation of innate lymphoid type 2 cells (ILC2), dysregulation of cytokines and eosinophil/basophil infiltration into the skin lesions are immunological features of AD. Therefore, immunomodulatory therapies can be beneficial in its treatment. Regulatory IL-37 can down-regulate systemic and local inflammation by suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory mediators in both innate and adaptive immunity. IL-37 has been shown to play an anti-inflammatory role in inflammatory diseases including rheumatoid arthritis and allergic asthma. We have demonstrated the putative role of itching-related cytokine IL-31, damage-associated molecular pattern IL-33 and bacterial toll-like receptor and NOD ligands in the activation of eosinophils/basophils through interacting with dermal fibroblasts in AD. Therefore, it will be crucial to step forward to evaluate the regulation of allergic inflammation by anti-inflammatory IL-37 in AD. Brief Project Description We hypothesize that IL-37 is an immunomodulatory cytokine that could exert its anti-allergic inflammatory activities through the suppression of lesion and infection activated eosinophils/basophils upon interacting with dermal fibroblasts, via distinct intracellular signaling pathways. We will study its cellular mechanism in the co-culture of primary human peripheral blood eosinophils/basophils and dermal fibroblasts. High throughput RNA‑sequencing will be applied for the transcriptome analysis of signaling mechanisms for the eosinophils/basophils-mediated allergic inflammation in AD. Both clinical studies using AD patients and animal studies with IL-37 knock-in and AD mice will be used to evaluate the in vivo anti-inflammatory mechanisms and therapeutic application of IL-37 in AD. Advanced intravital multiphoton imaging system will be applied to assess the in vivo interacting mechanisms among eosinophils/basophils/ILC2 cells in AD mice upon IL-37 treatment. Significance of Project The proposed in vitro, clinical and animal studies are expected to identify the novel intracellular and immunological mechanisms for the regulation of basophils/eosinophils-ILC2 axis of IL-37 on skin lesions and bacteria-mediated allergic inflammation in AD. We expect the results can advance our knowledge of the immunoregulatory mechanisms by which anti-inflammatory cytokines can ameliorate AD and help for the development of novel immunotherapy by using immunoregulatory cytokines for the treatment of allergic diseases.

14100118.label: Realisation of objectives
14100118.value: Interaction between eosinophils/basophils and dermal fibroblasts is essential for provoking allergic inflammation in atopic dermatitis (AD). Previous studies have shown that IL-1 family cytokine IL-37/IL-1F7 can downregulate systemic and local inflammation and Th2 cytokines, by suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory mediators and cytokines in innate and adaptive immunity. We have first established the co-culture of human eosinophils, the principal immune effector cells in allergic inflammation, with human primary dermal fibroblasts and setup the MC903-induced AD murine model and CRISPR/Cas9 human IL-37b knock-in mice. As a result, in vitro co-culture of human eosinophils and dermal fibroblasts upon AD-related IL-31 and IL-33 stimulation, and in vivo MC903-induced AD murine model were employed to investigate the anti-inflammatory mechanism of IL-1 family cytokine IL-37 in AD. Results showed that IL-37b could inhibit the in vitro induction of AD-related pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-ɑ, and chemokines CXCL8, CCL2 and CCL5, increase autophagosome biogenesis-related LC3B, and decrease autophagy-associated ubiquitinated protein p62 by regulating intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling pathway. In CRISPR/Cas9 human IL-37b knock-in mice, IL-37b could significantly alleviate MC903-stimulated ear tissue swelling, itching sensation and the level of circulating cytokine IL-6 and ear in situ expression of AD-related TNF-α, CCL5 and transforming growth factor-β. Moreover, IL-37b could significantly upregulate Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Treg) in spleen and ear together with significantly increased serum Treg cytokine IL-10, and decrease eosinophil infiltration in ear lesion. IL-37b knock-in mice showed a distinct intestinal microbiota metabolic pattern upon MC903 stimulation. Furthermore, IL-37b restored the disordered gut microbiota diversity, through regulating the in vivo autophagy mechanism mediated by intestinal metabolite 3-methyladenine, adenosine monophosphate, 2-hydroxyglutarate, purine and melatonin. In summary, IL-37b could significantly ameliorate eosinophils-mediated allergic inflammation via the regulation of autophagy mechanism, intestinal bacterial diversity and their metabolites in AD. Results therefore suggest that IL-37 is a potential anti-inflammatory cytokine for AD treatment, via distinct intracellular signaling pathways. The above results have been published in Frontiers in Immunology 2020; 11: 752. Since innate immune cell basophils are also essential for provoking allergic inflammation in AD, we have further developed the co-culture of basophils and keratinocyte HaCaT cells to further evaluate the roles of novel immunoregulatory cytokine IL-37 in basophils for AD. Therefore, we have employed in vitro co-culture of human basophils and human keratinocyte HaCaT cells and an in vivo MC903-induced AD murine model to investigate the anti-inflammatory mechanism of IL-37 on basophil activation in AD. In the in vitro model, IL-37b significantly decreased Der p1-induced thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) overexpression in HaCaT cells and decreased the expression of TSLP receptor as well as basophil activation marker CD203c on basophils. IL-37 could also reduce Th2 cytokine IL-4 release from TSLP-primed basophils ex vivo. In the in vivo model, alternative depletion of basophils ameliorated AD symptoms and significantly lowered the Th2 cell and eosinophil populations in the ear and spleen of the mice. Blocking TSLP alleviated the AD-like symptoms and reduced the infiltration of basophils in the spleen. In CRISPR/Cas9 human IL-37b knock-in mice or mice with direct treatment by human IL-37b, AD symptoms including ear swelling and itching were significantly alleviated upon MC903 challenge. Notably, IL-37b presence significantly reduced the basophil infiltration in ear lesions. In summary, IL-37b could regulate the TSLP-mediated activation of basophils and reduce the release of AD-related IL-4. The results, therefore, suggest that IL-37 may target TSLP-primed basophils to alleviate AD. The above has been published in Int J Mol Sci 2021, 22, 7393. As planned in the proposal for clinical study, thirty-four patients with moderate-to-severe AD [SCORAD: median (interquartile range) of 44.2 (31.2 - 52.6)] and twenty health controls (HC) were enrolled in this study. Sex and age were comparable between the two groups. Among the study cohort of AD patients, only one AD patient had concurrent mild allergic rhinitis. The percentage of Staphylococcus aureus and Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) colonization of AD patients was 58.5% and 52.9%, respectively. AD patients presented with elevated IgE levels (mean ± SEM, 7615 ± 5764 kIU/L; median, 6310 kIU/L, p < 0.05) compared with HC, who had undetectable IgE levels (< 1 kIU/L) (Table 1). Among the AD subjects, 76.5% (26 of 34) were tested positive in at least two categories of the allergen tests, and 20.6% (7 of 34) were tested positive in six categories of the allergen tests. All the specific-IgE levels were significantly higher in subjects with AD versus HC (all p < 0.05). A majority of the AD subjects reacted to house dust mite (88.2%, 30 of 34) (> 17.5 kUA/L), thereby indicating the AD subjects were mainly allergic to house dust mite in the present study cohort. Serum levels of IL-37 and T helper (Th) 2-related inflammatory mediators were quantified in subjects with or without AD. The expression of IL-37 receptors was determined by flow cytometry. Proteomics with tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) was employed to explore the serum protein profile and novel biomarkers. In vitro cell model, 3D-keratinocytes mimicking skin model, and the serum of subjects with or without AD were investigated to verify the proteomic results. Results showed that AD patients were found to present with higher levels of total and specific IgE as well as Th2 inflammatory mediators including IL-18, IL-33, TSLP, CCL17 and CCL27 compared with healthy controls (HC). IL-37 level and its receptor IL18Rɑ expression on CCR3+ eosinophils in AD patients were significantly decreased, together with increased population of eosinophils, indicating that the signaling of IL37/IL18Rɑ was dampened in AD. In addition, proteomic analysis revealed a significantly differential protein profile of AD patients compared with HC. IL-37 showed the strongest negative correlation with involucrin, a keratinizing epithelia protein. IL-37 was verified to suppress induced involucrin expression in in vitro 2D and 3D skin keratinocyte models. AD patients show a significantly higher serum concentration of involucrin compared with HC. Together, our results demonstrated that IL-37 plays a regulatory role in allergic inflammation and skin barrier function of AD. Its deficiency may lead to the aberrant involucrin expression in AD. The dysregulation of serum protein and skin disruption in AD is related to the insufficiency of IL-37 and its attenuated anti-inflammatory signaling. The above has been published in Allergy 2021, 76:2102-2114. In view of the above, all the three objectives for the in vitro, animal and clinical studies have been totally completed, as shown in the listed three peer-reviewed publications.

14100118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100118.value: Using in vivo and ex vivo co-culture systems, we have elucidated the anti-inflammatory mechanisms for the regulation of basophils/eosinophils axis of IL-37 on skin lesions and allergic inflammation in AD. Since CRISPR/Cas9 IL-37 knock-in and i.p. injection of IL-37 were used for the treatment of AD mice in our project, for further development of therapeutic dimension of IL-37 in translational medicine, together with my colleague Prof Chun-Kit Choi, CUHK, an expert in nanomedicine, we are working on the nanonization of IL-37 protein to be a Metal-organic Framework (MOF) nanoparticles. The development of IL-37 nanoparticles is feasible and effective for the topical treatment of AD in future. This project is being conducted. Since we found that IL-37 restored the disordered gut microbiota diversity, through regulating autophagy mechanism mediated by intestinal metabolites in AD mice, together with Prof. Ting-Fan Leung, a Paediatrician, CUHK, we are planning to evaluate the relationships among gut microbiota and metabolome, IL-37 with skin inflammation of AD patients. Based on the results of the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of IL-1 family member IL-37 in AD, the study of the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of other novel anti-inflammatory IL-1 family cytokine such as IL-38 is also pending.

14100118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100118.value: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronically relapsing inflammatory skin disease, affecting 20% of Hong Kong schoolchildren. Using cell culture, we found that anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-37 can suppress the allergic inflammation of AD. Using mice experiments, the application of IL-37 can suppress the skin inflammation and activities of eosinophils and basophils, which is probably through the modulation of gut microbiota and regulation of bacteria-derived metabolites. In clinical study, IL-37 level in AD patients were significantly decreased. Serum IL-37 level exhibited the strongest negative correlation with involucrin, a keratinizing epithelia protein. AD patients also show a significantly higher serum concentration of involucrin compared with controls. Together, dysregulation of serum protein expression profile and skin disruption in AD is related to the insufficiency of IL-37 and its attenuated anti-inflammatory signaling. The above results not only help for the further evaluation of the novel cellular mechanism of allergic inflammation in AD but also provide a biochemical basis for the development of new therapeutic intervention for the treatment of AD. The results of this AD study have been published in several international peer-reviewed journals and the trained PhD student was awarded the Young Investigator Award in Annual Scientific Meeting, Hong Kong Society for Immunology.

14100218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100218.value: 摘要： 缺少機械應力刺激，特別是在微重力環境下，可引起明顯的骨骼肌萎縮。宇航員暴露於太空微重力環境3-6個月可導致骨骼肌萎縮及功能障礙超過40％。然而宇航員在航天飛行期間的鍛煉不足以預防肌肉力量的丟失。現今藥物方法治療肌肉萎縮也有一定的副作用，比如增加骨吸收，耐藥性以及心血管系統不良反應。肌肉合成代謝受損是造成失負荷性肌肉萎縮的主要原因。目前亟需深入研究失負荷性肌肉萎縮中肌肉合成代謝受損的分子機制，從而發展出有臨床應用前景的肌肉合成代謝治療策略。 長鏈非編碼RNA（lncRNA）被發現在肌肉生成過程中起重要作用。因此我們研究了lncRNA是否在失負荷性肌肉萎縮中發揮作用。我們在尾懸吊肌萎縮小鼠模型的腓腸肌中確定了一種下調最爲顯著的全新的lncRNA（lnc-mar）。在正常小鼠腓腸肌中沉默lnc-mar可顯著降低肌肉重量和力量。而在懸吊前骨骼肌特異性過表達lnc-mar可延緩尾懸吊小鼠肌肉MyoD蛋白水平，肌肉重量，肌纖維橫截面積以及肌肉力量的減少。此外，我們的小樣本量預試驗顯示在已出現肌肉萎縮的尾懸吊小鼠模型中骨骼肌特異性過表達lnc-mar有可能增加肌肉重量。通過機制研究發現，lnc-mar可在C2C12成肌細胞培養中扮演內源性競爭RNA的角色阻止微小RNA-762（miR-762）抑制MyoD蛋白質水平。我們已經成功繁育了骨骼肌特異性miR-762敲入小鼠。與野生型小鼠相比，骨骼肌特異性miR-762敲入小鼠腓腸肌重量，肌纖維橫截面積以及MyoD蛋白水平都顯著降低。綜上所述，我們假設骨骼肌特異性過表達lnc-mar可以促進肌肉合成代謝從而逆轉失負荷所導致骨骼肌肉萎縮。 此項目將完成以下兩個目標。1. 通過在已形成肌肉萎縮的尾懸吊小鼠模型骨骼肌特異性過表達lnc-mar並檢測MyoD蛋白水平以及肌肉重量、結構和功能水平以確定lnc-mar的促合成代謝作用。2.研究在骨骼肌特異性miR-762敲入小鼠中骨骼肌特異性過表達lnc-mar對肌肉MyoD蛋白水平以及肌肉重量、結構和功能水平的影響。 此項目將確立lnc-mar是一個重要的肌肉合成代謝調控因子，從而進一步發展出有應用前景的治療失負荷性肌萎縮的肌肉合成代謝治療策略。研究發現將為處理失負荷性相關的臨床問題提供理論依據。

14100218.label: Realisation of objectives
14100218.value: Both specific aims have been all accomplished. For Specific Aim 1, Six-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to the following four groups: 1) Normal control group: without hindlimb suspension (HLS) and any treatment; 2) HLS group: with HLS but no treatment; 3) HLS+EV group: with HLS and empty vector system treatment; and 4) HLS+lnc-mar group: with HLS and lnc-mar vector system treatment. The mice in all HLS groups were subjected to HLS to induce skeletal muscle atrophy. On day 14 of HLS, the lnc-mar vector system or empty vector system was locally injected once into the mid-portion of the left gastrocnemius muscle (GA) of the mice in HLS+EV and HLS+lnc-mar group, respectively. Ten mice in each group were sacrificed on day 0, 14, 17, 21, 28 and 42 of HLS, respectively. All the mice underwent in situ muscle functional testing before sacrifice to assess the muscle strength. The left GA muscle from each mouse were collected. The wet muscle mass was weighted by scale and normalized to body weight. The muscles were processed for cryosectioning. The muscle cross sections underwent routine histological staining for quantifying the fiber cross-sectional area (CSA). The levels of lnc-mar and MyoD protein were evaluated by real-time PCR and western blot analysis, respectively. The muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength decreased significantly following 14 days of HLS. The above variables in HLS+lnc-mar group started to elevate on Day 14 of HLS. Moreover, the muscle fiber CSA and muscle specific force in lnc-mar vector group were higher than those in EV group on Day 42 of HLS. In addition, the total RNA and proteins in muscle samples were extracted and the expression levels of lnc-mar and MyoD protein were evaluated for by quantitative PCR and western blotting, respectively. Both lnc-mar and MyoD protein levels decreased dramatically during 14-day HLS. After lnc-mar overexpression vector administration on Day 14 of HLS, the expression levels of lnc-mar and MyoD protein started to elevate. Moreover, MyoD protein level in lnc-mar group were higher than those in EV group on Day 42 of HLS. In summary, the skeletal muscle-specific overexpression of lnc-mar could increase MyoD protein level, muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength in established skeletal muscle atrophy during HLS. For Specific Aim 2: Six-month-old male miR-762 knockin mice were injected with the lentiviral vector system once into the mid-portion of the left GA for muscle-specific overexpression of lnc-mar. The right GA were served as the control by injecting empty vector lentivirus (EV) once on the same day. The above mice, together with age-matched control mice without treatment, were sacrificed on day 3, 7, 14 and 28 (n=10 per group at each time point). Ten mice without treatment were sacrificed on day 0 as pre-treatment baseline. All the mice (90 in total) underwent in situ muscle functional testing before sacrifice to assess the muscle strength. Both sides of GA from each mouse were collected. The muscle mass were normalized to body weight. After that, the muscle were processed for cryosectioning. The muscle cross sections underwent the routine histological staining for quantifying the fiber CSA. The levels of lnc-mar and MyoD protein in all muscles were evaluated by real-time PCR and western blot analysis, respectively. Compared to other tissue/organ, the expression level of miR-762 was highly expressed in skeletal muscles of muscle-specific miR-762 knockin mice. The mice also showed lower muscle mass, lower muscle fiber CSA and lower MyoD protein level in GA compared to the wildtype mice. Lnc-mar expression level increased significantly after lnc-mar vector administration. Lnc-mar overexpression increased the muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength in muscle-specific miR-762 mice. In addition, the lnc-mar overexpression elevated the expression level of MyoD protein in GA of muscle-specific miR-762 knockin mice. Taken together, the newly identified lncRNA lnc-mar acts as a miR-762 sponge to regulate MyoD protein, resulting in promoting muscle differentiation. Lnc-mar could be a novel anabolic therapeutic agent to reverse established skeletal muscle atrophy following mechanical unloading.

14100218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100218.value: For Specific Aim 1, the muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength decreased significantly following 14 days of HLS. The above variables in HLS+lnc-mar group started to elevate on Day 14 of HLS. Moreover, the muscle fiber CSA and muscle specific force in lnc-mar vector group were higher than those in EV group on Day 42 of HLS. In addition, both lnc-mar and MyoD protein levels decreased dramatically during 14-day HLS. After lnc-mar overexpression vector administration on Day 14 of HLS, the expression levels of lnc-mar and MyoD protein started to elevate. Moreover, MyoD protein level in lnc-mar group were higher than those in EV group on Day 42 of HLS. The above findings indicated that lnc-mar overexpression in skeletal muscle could reverse HLS-induced skeletal muscle atrophy. For Specific Aim 2, the expression level of miR-762 was highly expressed in skeletal muscles compared to other tissue/organ of muscle-specific miR-762 knockin mice. The mice showed lower muscle mass, lower muscle fiber CSA and lower MyoD protein level in GA compared to the wildtype mice. Lnc-mar expression level increased significantly after lnc-mar vector administration. Lnc-mar overexpression increased the muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA and muscle strength in muscle-specific miR-762 mice. In addition, the lnc-mar overexpression elevated the expression level of MyoD protein in GA of muscle-specific miR-762 knockin mice. The above findings suggested that the suppression of miR-762’s activity was involved in lnc-mar anabolic effect in skeletal muscle. The project helps to increase our understanding of lncRNA in skeletal muscle homeostasis. The findings have inspired more lncRNA-based studies. The related findings have been presented in international conferences.

14100218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100218.value: The current project demonstrated that lnc-mar acts as a miR-762 sponge to regulate MyoD protein, resulting in promoting muscle differentiation. Lnc-mar could be a novel anabolic therapeutic agent to reverse established skeletal muscle atrophy following mechanical unloading. LncRNAs are appealing therapeutic targets because of the following characters, the involvement in disease development, greater tissue, cell and time-specificity than protein-coding genes. However, there is still no lncRNA-based drug brought into clinical trials to date, especially for skeletal muscle atrophy, due to the difficulty in modulation of lncRNAs in human and the potential systematic side effect. Tissue/organ-specific delivery system, such as muscle-targeted aptamer, could be helpful for the lncRNA-based therapy to avoid the potential side effect to other tissue and organs, which could be a research field with great application potential in the future. Another challenge of lncRNA-based therapy is the poor sequence conservation of lncRNA cross species. LncRNA conservation includes four dimensions: the sequence, structure, function, and expression from syntenic loci. Lack of sequence conservation does not directly imply the lack of function. We have demonstrated that lnc-mar is functionally conserved between mouse and human. More extensive studies need to be done in the future.

14100218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100218.value: Reversing established muscle atrophy following mechanical unloading is of great clinical challenge. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been demonstrated to play important roles in myogenesis. Here, we identified a skeletal muscle-enriched lncRNA lnc-mar, which was the most down-regulated lncRNA during muscle atrophy development in hindlimb suspension (HLS) mice. The in vitro and in vivo data demonstrated that the decreased expression levels of lnc-mar closely associated with reduction of myogenesis during mechanical unloading. Mechanistically, lnc-mar promoted myogenic differentiation by functioning as a miR-762 sponge to regulate the core myogenic regulator MyoD in vitro. The enforced expression of lnc-mar relieved the decreases in MyoD protein and muscle mass in miR-762 knock-in mice. Therapeutically, the enforced expression of lnc-mar improved the in vitro myogenic differentiation of myoblasts under microgravity simulation, prevented the muscle atrophy development and reversed the established muscle atrophy in HLS mice. These findings identify lnc-mar as an anabolic regulator to reverse established muscle atrophy following mechanical unloading.

14100818.value: 擬南芥free1抑制子SOF10 的分子機制研究

14100818.label: Project Objectives
14100818.value: To characterize and demonstrate SOF10A as a true FREE1 suppressor. Our recent genetic screening for suppressor of free1 (sof) has identified two sof lines (sof10 and sof641) and the causal locus in these two sof lines was mapped to the same gene SOF10A (At5g10370), indicating that SOF10A is a true suppressor of free1. Both sof10 and sof641 can convert the lethality of FREE1-RNAi plants, we thus hypothesize that SOF10 functions as a suppressor of FREE1 in Arabidopsis. Here we further confirm that SOF10A is the causal mutation of sof10/sof641 via complementation study. We will also exam MVB structure with normal ILVs and normal vacuolar trafficking in sof10/sof641. To illustrate the underlying mechanisms of SOF10A function as a FREE1 suppressor in plant. FREE1 is an essential positive component for MVB and vacuole biogenesis, and autophagosome-vacuole fusion. SOF10A loss-of-function mutants can rescue the FREE1-RNAi lethal phenotype, whereas C-terminus of SOF10A interacts with SH3P2 in puncta structure. We thus also hypothesize that SOF10A may function as FREE1 suppressor through its regulation in secretory-autophagic cross-talk in Arabidopsis. In addition, SOF10 may also act as a negative regulator downstream of FREE1 or act as a positive regulator of FREE1 antagonist.

14100818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100818.value: The plant endomembrane system contains several functionally distinct membrane-bound organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus, trans-Golgi network (TGN)/early endosome, prevacuolar compartment (PVC) or multivesicular body (MVB), and vacuole. We have recently characterized a plant unique ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport) component termed FREE1 (FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting 1). We have demonstrated that FREE1 plays multiple functional roles in regulating protein trafficking, MVB and vacuole biogenesis, as well as autophagic degradation in plants. To further illustrate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 functions in plants, we performed a forward genetic screen for mutants that suppressed the seedling lethal phenotype of FREE1-RNAi transgenic plants and the obtained mutants are termed as suppressors of free1 (sof). Through next-generation sequencing (NGS) of F2 mapping population of the sof mutants, we have identified two interesting sof lines (sof10 and sof641), which were mapped to the same causal gene SOF10A (At5g10370) of unknown function. The sof10 possesses the EMS-induced mutation which results in a premature stop codon, while the sof641 produced a mis-sense mutation (Asp787-to-Asn) in the predicted protein sequence. As expected, both sof10 and sof641 seedlings exhibited reduced FREE1 protein level and normal vacuole morphology. Our preliminary results further showed that SOF10A localized to intracellular punctate dots, likely MVBs in Arabidopsis cells. We also found that the C-terminus of SOF10A (sequence missed in the sof10 mutant) co-localized and interacted directly with a unique plant autophagic regulator termed SH3P2 (SH3 DOMAIN CONTAINING PROTEIN2). We thus hypothesize that SOF10A is a true FREE1-related suppressor that may function in the cross-talk between secretory pathway and autophagic pathway regulate FREE1 function in Arabidopsis. Therefore, the central goal of this research proposal is to illustrate the underlying mechanisms of SOF10A function as a novel suppressor in the FREE1-depenedent membrane trafficking and organelle biogenesis using a combination of cellular, molecular and genetic approaches. 我們最近發現FREE1 (FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting 1)是植物特有的ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport)組分，並且具有多種生物學功能。為了進一步揭示FREE1在植物中的作用機制，我們通過正向遺傳方法篩選抑制FREE1-RNAi轉基因植物致死表型的突變體，該突變體被稱為free1抑制子(sof)。通過對sof 突變體的F2代定位群體進行下一代測序(NGS)，有2個sof 株系(sof10 和sof641)引起了我們的注意，這兩個株係都定位到了同一個功能未知的基因：SOF10A。和預期一樣，sof10 和sof641的FREE1蛋白水平都有所下降並且液泡形態正常。因此，本項目的主要目標就是綜合運用細胞、分子和遺傳學等研究手段，闡明SOF10A作為一個新的free1抑制子在FREE1依賴的膜運輸和細胞器發生中的作用機制。

14100818.label: Realisation of objectives
14100818.value: Objective 1: To characterize and demonstrate SOF10A as a true FREE1 suppressor. To achieve this goal, through the suppressor screening of FREE1-RNAi mutants, we have identified and further characterized the two suppressor of free1 (sof) mutants (sof10 and sof641) using our well-established cellular and genetic approaches, demonstrating that 1) The sof10 and sof641 can reverse the defective phenotype of FREE1-RNAi, including recovery of the defect of central vacuole morphology and protein transport to the vacuole; 2) The sof10 mutant was able to restore the phenotype of FREE1-RNAi plants in terms of membrane protein homeostasis, vacuolar degradation of ubiquitinated membrane cargo proteins, as well as the restore of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) formation in multivesicular body (MVB) at ultrastructural transmission electron microscopy (TEM) levels; 3) Both causal mutations in these two sof lines (sof10 and sof641) were mapped to the SOF10A (At5g10370) gene, resulting in a premature stop codon (Gln996-to-stop) (sof10) or a missense mutation in a conserved amino acid (Asp787-to-Asn) (sof641); and 4) The genetic complementation and recapitulation studies were performed to support the loss of function of SOF10A is responsible for the recovery of the lethal phenotype of FREE1-RNAi and SOF10A is a true FREE1 suppressor as shown by the genetic complementation and recapitulation studies. Taken together, our multiple experiments demonstrated that SOF10A is a true FREE1 suppressor in Arabidopsis. We have thus achieved the original goal successfully and fully. Objective 2: To illustrate the underlying mechanisms of SOF10A function as a FREE1 suppressor in plant. To achieve this goal, we have also identified that the SOF10A has a close homolog SOF10B (At4g01020) in the Arabidopsis genome. To study the functions of SOF10A/B, we have generated Arabidopsis sof10a sof10b double mutant and showed that the embryos of sof10a sof10b double mutant become arrested at the globular stage and formed enlarged MVBs with increased ILVs numbers by 3D electron tomography (ET) analysis. Mechanistically, we further demonstrated biochemically and cellularly that the SOF10A is a membrane associated protein and coordinates with the retromer component sorting nexin 1 (SNX1) to regulate the recycling of PIN-FORMEDs (PINs) in transgenic Arabidopsis plants. In summary, through a combination of genetic, cellular and biochemical approaches, we have identified and demonstrated that the plant-specific protein SOF10A functions as a retromer interactor in regulating the FREE1-mediated ILVs formation of MVBs as well as the vacuolar sorting and degradation of membrane proteins in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. We have thus illustrated the underlying mechanisms of SOF10A function as a FREE1 suppressor in plant, representing a novel and unique mechanism of MVB-mediated protein trafficking and organelle biogenesis in plants. In conclusion, we have achieved all the original objectives in the research project successfully as demonstrated by the research findings summarized above in this completion report. These new findings have been included in the doctoral dissertation completed at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Zhu, 2022). In addition, a manuscript mainly derived from the thesis research (in which Zhu is the first author, and Jiang is the corresponding author) was submitted to The Plant Cell on August 10, 2022 and received the comments of Editors/Reviewers on September 27, 2022. We are now in the process of revising the manuscript to fully address the comments with suggested experiments (mainly related controls) for submission back to the Journal in coming months. We are confident that this revised MS will be accepted for publication in The Plant Cell then. We have thus also attached a copy of the submitted MS to The Plant Cell and decision letter in this report. In addition, in a review article published in Journal of Plant Physiology in 2020, we have also summarized the strategies of genetic suppressor screening approaches related to the identification of unique endomembrane trafficking regulators as well as provided detailed comments on the principles and strategies for the screening of regulators for plant endomembrane trafficking system, and pros and cons for the screening, especially the screening of sof (suppressor of free1). This RGC-funded project sheds new lights on novel regulators in the plant endomembrane system. In addition, the RGC fund has also partially supported several graduate students and related research in the laboratory, resulting in publications of Ph.D. thesis and research article in international journals such as Molecular Plant, PNAS, Autophagy and Nature Plants that are related with protein trafficking and organelle biogenesis and function in the plant endomembrane system and autophagy.
