14100818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100818.value: 1. We have summarized the strategies for the screening of regulators for plant endomembrane trafficking system, and pros and cons for the screening, especially the screening of sof (suppressor of free1) in a review article published in Journal of Plant Physiology in 2020. 2. We have identified a plant-unique ROP8-Sec5 signaling mechanism that positively regulates autophagy in plants. The data was published in Molecular Plant in 2021. 3. We have identified and characterized a unique AtSar1d-AtRabD2a nexus in modulating autophagosome biogenesis in Arabidopsis. The data was pubilished in The Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in 2021. 4. We identified and characterize a novel population of COPII vesicles produced in response to abiotic stresses in plants. This data was pubilished in Nature Plants in 2021. 5. We have identified autophagy-related SNAREs VAMP724 and VAMP726 in regulating autophagy formation in Arabidopsis. The data was published in Autophagy in 2022. 6. We illustrated a lipid-binding protein ORP2A in mediating ER-autophagosomal membrane contact sites and autophagosome formation. The data was published in The Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in 2022. 7. We identified and characterized the plant-specific protein SOF10A as a retromer interactor in regulating the FREE1-mediated ILVs formation of MVBs as well as the vacuolar sorting and degradation of membrane proteins in plants. These new findings have been included in the doctoral dissertation completed at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Zhu, 2022), together with a manuscript currently under revision and resubmission for The Plant Cell in 2022. 8. With partially support from this project, we have also trained several excellent postgraduate students with outstanding research outputs as demonstrated by publications of their thesis work in a number of international journals as shown above.

14100818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100818.value: Our studies have identified and discovered the SOF10A as a novel regulator in plant endomembrane trafficking in orchestrating the FREE1-mediated ILVs formation of MVBs as well as the vacuolar sorting and degradation of membrane proteins in plants. This new finding has expanded our understanding towards the complexity and plasticity of the plant endomembrane system. Future studies include 1) To expand our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the enlarged MVBs and increased ILVs occurred in sof10a sof10b, and illustrate how the SOF10 proteins regulate the SNX1-dependent membrane protein recycling to PM; 2) To understand the roles of the interacting proteins identification with proteomics techniques on the function of the novel regulator; and 3) The identification and characterization of other regulators, the studies of functional relationship between the regulators, as well as structural determination of SOF10A via cryo-EM for expanding our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of the novel players in the plant endomembrane system.

14100818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100818.value: This project identified and illustrated the underlying mechanisms of a novel regulator SOF10A in FREE1/MVB-mediated vacuolar sorting and degradation of membrane proteins in plants using a combination of molecular, cellular, genetic and biochemical approaches. Findings from this study have provided new insights into the molecular machinery of FREE1-related endomembrnae trafficking, which will provide the basis for future study of novel regulators in protein homeostasis, MVB biogenesis, as well as plant endomembrane trafficking.

14101318.value: 背景 “只是傷風吧！” 這是人們對鼻病毒感染最平常的觀感。 然而，鼻病毒感染是兒童因傳染病而住院治療的主要原因。鼻病毒也是在成人社區性感染肺炎中，最常被檢測到的病原體 。 鼻病毒可引致急性呼吸道感染。其中一些鼻病毒品種，與潛在的呼吸系統疾病，如：哮喘和慢性呼吸系統疾病阻塞性肺病的惡化有著密切的關係。流行病學的研究指出，因鼻病毒感染而住院的病童，最少一半是由丙型鼻病毒所引至的。而丙型鼻病毒，相對於另外兩種鼻病毒 --甲型和乙型而言，與兒童哮喘發作及病毒血症病例有更大的相關性。 時至今日，我們仍沒有針對鼻病毒的抗病毒藥物和疫苗。 在過去的50年裡，我們對甲型和乙型的鼻病毒了解很多。相比之下，在二零零六年才被人類發現的丙型鼻病毒，我們對它認識甚少。主要是因為它以往不能在一般實驗室常用的細胞系中複製，所以丙型鼻病毒未能得到充分的研究。 在二零一五年，科學家發現了鈣粘蛋白三是丙型鼻病毒在人類細胞膜上的受體。這項發現有助我們發展分離和複製丙型鼻病毒的細胞系，更能讓我們進一步了解丙型鼻病毒所導致的急性感染和誘發長期性呼吸疾病的病理機制。 目的和假設 在這提議書中，我們將建立和使用不同哺乳動物的呼吸器官作體外培養，並利用它們作為外植體模型來感染鼻病毒。這個外植體方法將提供一個快速和人道的選擇，來測試大量的病毒分離株。這項目的結果能讓我們在 初始階段使用最少量的動物，去預選最合適的病毒品種和動物宿主，以便計劃第二階段活體動物實驗。 先前開發的鼻病毒動物感染模型，都是以病毒的細胞向性研究結果，配合基因改造技術而實踐的。現在，我們假設呼吸器官外植體的易感性，能可靠反映和預測鼻病毒在活體動物實驗的易感性。我們這將會依據實驗結果，改進下一步活體動物實驗實驗。 學習規劃 我們的團隊已在文獻上，發表了能使用人體呼吸器官外植體來研究丙型鼻病毒的可行性。現在，我們將於豬、豚鼠和小鼠的呼吸器官外植體，定義丙型鼻病毒的細胞向性和複製能力。

14101318.label: Realisation of objectives
14101318.value: This project aimed to identify a small animal model to study the pathogenesis of rhinovirus C (RV-C). By utilizing the respiratory explant culture models to substitute the initial phase of live animal studies, the number of animals needed to achieve the same goal was significantly minimized. We hypothesized that the RV susceptibility of the respiratory organ explant culture would serve as a reliable predictor for their susceptibility in vivo. This final report described the RV-C susceptibility of the respiratory explant culture of pigs, mice and ferrets. The euthanized neonatal pigs at seven days old (n=5) were obtained from a local farm. The respiratory organ was dissected out from the body within 2 hours in the laboratory and was done inside a Class II Biosafety Cabinet. In contrast, the intact respiratory organ of adult pigs at six months old (n=5) was obtained in the Hong Kong Sheung Shui Slaughterhouse within four hours after the pigs being slaughtered. The organ was kept in a sterile plastic box at 4°C during transportation to our laboratory. Balb/c and C57bl/6J are the stable colonies established in the animal unit after their first importation from the Animal Resource Center, Australia and Jackson Lab. The lung tissue was obtained from euthanized animals. In addition to the original objective, the intact respiratory organ was also obtained from desexed male ferrets (n=3) at 4–to-8 months old and weighed 1.0–2.0 kg. These ferrets were employed as the control animals in other experiments without any treatments. The preparation of tissue explant culture of the tracheal and alveolar epithelia was previously described (1). Briefly, the tracheal epithelium of pigs and ferrets was peeled from the cartilage carefully by a pair of fine forceps with a sharp scalpel. The tracheal explant (TE) of the adult mouse was prepared by cutting the trachea into rings, and each ring was divided into three pieces. For the lung explant (LE) preparation, the lung of pig and ferret was perfused with a cold wash medium using a tracheal tube 2.0 - 4.0mm (Ruschelit) through the bronchiole, while a 24G - 30G Angiocath (BD) was inserted through the trachea to the lung of the mouse. Then, the wash medium was aspirated and replaced by 1.5% low-melt agarose (Sigma) in DPBS and was kept at 4°C for 5 minutes. This tissue filled with solidified agarose was cut into cubes and embedded in 4% agarose. The agarose-embedded lung tissue was in slices, using a cryotome blade with a thickness snippet was brought to ALI culture after the virus infection and washing steps. RV-A2 or RV-1B (minor), RV-B14 (major), RV-A16 (major) were propagated in H1- HeLa cell line and RV-C15 was generated by reverse genetics. The respiratory explant cultures were washed with PBS before infection to remove the possible cytokine secreted due to the preparation process. The four rhinoviruses were inoculated to the explant preparation with the same viral load (10^5 TCID50/ml) for two hours. Explants were washed three times with 5 ml PBS to remove any unbounded viruses. All TEs and LEs of the mice were incubated at 37°C while the LEs of pig and ferret were incubated at 39°C. At 2, 24, 48, 72 and 120 hour postinfection (hpi), the cell-free supernatant of the infected culture was collected for viral gene quantification and viral load titration in quadruplicate to study the viral kinetic for the RVs in the major and minor groups. In the pig explant study, neonatal pigs at seven days old and adult pigs at six months old were employed. The susceptibility of RVs in the TEs and LEs was examined. The viral titration result showed that RV-A16 replicated extensively in the neonatal pig TE with 20 folds increase in viral load in the first 24 and 48 hours after inoculation but not in the adult pig TE. Moreover, the neonatal and adult pig LEs did not support the replication of RV-A16. In RV-B14 infection, an 8-10 fold increase in viral load was seen in the TE, bronchial explant and LE of the adult pig but not in the TE and LE of the neonatal pig. In RV-C15 infection, the adult pig TE supported a significantly higher viral copy number at 24 hpi (Bonferroni’s multiple comparisons test, p = 0.004) and 48 hpi (p = 0.003) when compared to that at 2hpi, while neonatal TE did not support the RV-C15 replication. The RV-C15 also replicated in the adult pig LE with a significant increase from 2 to 24 hpi (p = 0.03). A subtle increase in RV-C15 gene copy was observed in the neonatal pig LE. However, it did not reach statistical significance. In the mouse study, Balb/c and C57bl/6J were employed. Neonatal mice at five days old were used to prepare the LE as described. RV-A16 did not replicate in the balb/c LE. Surprisingly, in RV-B14 infection, a ten-fold increase in the viral gene was observed from 24 to 48 hpi and retained at a viral titer of 10^2.5 TCID50/ml at 96 hpi. In RV-A2 infection, a prolonged steady viral titer of 10^2.5 TCID50/ml was observed from 48 to 96 h. In RV-C15 infection, a significantly higher level of viral gene copy was detected at 48hpi compared with 2 hpi (Dunn’s test, p = 0.0437). The neonatal C57bl/6J mice did not support RV-A16, RV-B14 and RV-1B and RV-C15 replication. In parallel to this project, a seed funding scheme provided by the Boston University School of Medicine (BUSM) allowed our collaborator in BUSM to perform the RV-C susceptibility test in vivo in the 6-to-8 week-old balb/c and C57bl/6J mice by intratracheal inoculation. The result showed that both mouse strains did not support RV-C replication with decreasing viral gene detected in the supernatant of the lung homogenate harvested from inoculation to 3 days postinfection. As this GRF project aims to extrapolate the result found in the respiratory explant cultures to guide the selection of an RV-C susceptible host for in vivo experiment, the adult mouse respiratory explant cultures were therefore not performed. An additional study in the ferret TE and LE was carried out to assess its susceptibility to RV-C15. RV-A2 and RV-A16 did not replicate in the TE experiment, while RV-B14 replicated with a significant increase in viral titer from 1 to 24 hpi (Bonferroni’s test, p=0.0006). In RV-C15 infection, an average of 1.5 log increase in the viral gene was observed in the first 24 hours after inoculation though it did reach statistical significance (Bonferroni’s test, p=0.07). Strikingly, the LE of ferret supported the replication of RV-A16 with a 50 ± 2.4 fold increase in gene copy at 48 hpi (p = 0.02) with an increased viral titer when compared with those at 2hpi. RV-C15 also had the best replication in the ferret LE and resulted in significant increases in the viral gene copy at 24hpi (p=0.04), 48hpi (p=0.007), 72hpi (p=0.008) and 96hpi (p=0.002) when compared to 2hpi (488±181 copies). The viral load of RV-C15 retained at 10^5 copies/ul at 120 hpi. Nevertheless, RV-B14 and RV-A2 did not replicate in the ferret LE. Reference: 1. Chan RW, Karamanska R, Van Poucke S, et al., Peiris JS, Haslam SM, Guan Y, Nicholls JM. 2013. Infection of swine ex vivo tissues with avian viruses including H7N9 and correlation with glycomic analysis. Influenza and other respiratory viruses 7:1269-1282.

14101318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101318.value: Among the three animal respiratory organ explant models we tested, this data direct our next step in selecting the most appropriate animal model for in vivo inoculation and therefore be used to study the pathogenesis of RV-C. In the pig model, we defined that the respiratory tracts (trachea, bronchus and lung) of the adult pig supports the RV-C15 replication, which is a good indication of a susceptible model. Nevertheless, if we aim to compare the pathogenesis of RV-C15 with another rhinovirus, we cannot include RV-A16 as the control, as it did not replicate in the same model. Although RV-B14 replicated with a ten-fold increase in infectious viral titer along the respiratory tract of the adult pig, the number of RV-B being isolated from human patients contributed to a minor proportion compared with RV-A and RV-C. Therefore, if we set up the adult pig BSL-2 facility to address the research question by comparing RV-B14 and RV-C15, the outcome of the in vivo experiment would be less cost-effective. Obviously, in the neonatal pig model, only RV-A16 could replicate in the tracheal explant while the increase in RV-C15 viral gene copy in the lung explant culture was subtle, no systematic comparison can be made. Therefore, the option of using neonatal pig as an in vivo model for the investigation of RV-C is not desirable. In the mouse model, adult balb/c and C57bl/6J were proven insusceptible to RV-C. The neonatal balb/c lung explant culture supported RV-C15 to replicate from 2 to 48 hours post-infection with an increased viral copy number (p=0.04). There was also a steady infectious viral load detected at a viral titer of 10^2.5 TCID50/ml in the supernatant of the neonatal lung explant after the inoculation of RV-B14 and RV-A2. The neonatal balb/c mouse would be an option for our in vivo testing. Moreover, the availability of specific immunology tools for mice is an important consideration to prioritize our selection. RV-C15 had the broad tropism from the trachea to the lung with a significant increase in viral gene copy number from 2-to-96 hours post-infection in the ferret model. The ferret lung explant culture also supported the RV-A16 replication from 2-to-48 hours post-infection in viral titer. Presumably, the ferret will be an excellent model to work on, as it allows the head to head comparison between the major group RV-A16 and RV-C in the distal lung.

14101318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101318.value: This information suggested that future comparison between RV-A16 and RV-C15 can be done in ferret in vivo in the next stage. This, in turn, provides tools to study chronic outcomes and offers concrete data to assess the health risks of RVs. By then, the study of cross-protection of different RV species by natural infection would be possible, vaccine investigation would become handy, and study of the impact of tissue remodelling by RV-C in the host would become feasible. Nevertheless, the ferret trachea explant, the increment of the RV-C15 gene was limited, and the increase in viral load of RV-A16 was subtle. Careful consideration in the virus inoculation route will be needed, for example, using an intratracheal instead of an intranasal inoculation route or by the nebulization of RV, which generates particles at micrometre scale to achieve an aerosol inoculation with an effective deposition in small airways. This would be a unique model which allows the head to head comparison between the major group RV-A16 and RV-C in the distal lung. It will facilitate our understanding of RV-C induced immunity at the organism level. So far, there is no GMP grade of RV-C available for the inoculation study in human volunteers.

14101318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101318.value: We demonstrated the use of the respiratory organ explant cultures of pig, mouse, and ferret to assess their susceptibility to different rhinovirus species. This approach substitutes the initial phase of live-animal studies and provides a rapid option to reduce the number of animals needed for in vivo work. We identified that the ferret lung explant culture supported the best replication of RV-C amongst all the explant tissues tested with a 100 fold increase in viral load within the first 24 hours after virus inoculation. The ferret lung explant also supported the replication of the major group rhinovirus RV-A16. This data direct our next step in selecting the most appropriate animal model for in vivo inoculation and therefore be used to study the disease mechanism of RV-C infection and at an organism level. Ferrets could be a good option, as it allows the head to head comparison between the major group RV-A16 and RV-C in the distal lung. This is not examined previously, as it was in RV-A16, as there is no GMP grade of RV-C available for the inoculation study in human volunteers.

14101518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101518.value: 青光眼是以視神經節細胞的慢性退行性病變為特征的致不可逆性盲的首要原因。能夠早期發現疾病惡化以用來啟動或擴大降低眼壓的治療對於防止青光眼盲症是至關重要的。在臨床實踐中，評估視神經纖維層（RNFL）的進行性變薄主要是用光學相干斷層掃描（OCT）來實現。然而，眾所周知，OCT用來測量RNFL的進行性變薄的表現是會在RNFL的厚度接近下限的晚期的病人中打折扣的。如果疾病的轉差沒有被及時的發現，那麼治療窗很可能會被錯過。鑒別出能夠提示在所有分期的青光眼病中的疾病轉差的生物標記依然是沒能解決的當務之急。 我們設計了一個新的生物標記，RNFL的光學特質符號，能夠整合用掃頻光源OCT獲得的RNFL的厚度以及RNFL的反射測量值用來偵測以及量化在黃斑區以及視乳頭旁區的RNFL異常。RNFL光學特質符號（ROTA）能夠在晚期青光眼的病人中分辨出不同程度的RNFL異常，而這種能力是其他目前現有的臨床工具所不具備的。更進一步的，對比較于傳統的RNFL厚度分析，ROTA實現了更強的結構功能聯繫以及更高的特異性，以用來檢測RNFL異常。我們提議，ROTA在發現所有分期的青光眼轉差的檢測方面是優於傳統的RNFL厚度分析的。我們提出進行一個為期三年的前瞻性多中心研究計劃，致力於招募469名連續的不同疾病分期（大約20%預計會有視野（VF）平均差 <-18dB）的病人，用於以2個月為間隔的OCT RNFL厚度分析，ROTA，以及視野測量。趨勢進展分析會被用來決定在RNFL厚度分析以及ROTA中是否會存在進行性轉差。 首要目標是比較對於VF轉差的進展性的，在ROTA中的進行性轉差的檢測對比在RNFL厚度的進行性轉差的檢測的基礎上用時間比較的協變量Cox模型來計算得出的危害率。我們預計在所有分期的病人中，對於比RNFL厚度分析來說，在VF進行性轉差的進展中ROTA會顯示出更高的危害率。 該研究項目不僅僅會因為引入了新的診斷性評估以及檢測青光眼的典範而影響青光眼的處理，而且也會使得臨床醫生能夠更有權的去識別在所有疾病分期中的需要接受降低眼壓治療的具有視野損害進行性進展高風險的青光眼病人。

14101518.label: Realisation of objectives
14101518.value: Objective 1 – To compare the hazard ratios for development of visual field progression upon detection of progressive decline in retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical texture signature versus upon detection of progressive RNFL thinning. We performed time-varying Cox proportional hazard modeling to determine the hazard ratios for development of VF progression upon detection of progressive RNFL thinning versus upon detection of progressive RNFL optical texture loss. In the univariable model, eyes with progressive RNFL optical texture loss had 2.29-fold (95% CI: 1.52-3.45) increase in risk for development of VF progression compared with those without whereas eyes with progressive RNFL thinning had 1.78-fold (95% CI: 1.06-2.98) increase in risk for development of VF progression compared with those without. In the multivariable models, the respective hazards ratios were 2.43 (95% CI: 1.59-3.71) (P<0.001) and 1.79 (95% CI: 1.05, 3.05) (P<0.001), respectively, after the adjustment of IOP levels during the study follow-up, and age, axial length, and VF MD at the baseline (please refer to Table 2 in the enclosed manuscript). There were no significant differences in the hazard ratios. Subgroup analyses (i.e., early versus moderate to severe glaucoma) are shown in Table 3 and Table 4 (please refer to the enclosed manuscript). Notably, in eyes with moderate to severe glaucoma, eyes with progressive RNFL optical texture loss remained predictive of VF progression (HR: 3.00, 95% CI: 1.33-6.74, P=0.008) whereas eyes with progressive RNFL thinning was not associated with VF progression (HR: 0.18, 95% CI: -0.02-1.37, P=0.097) (Table 4). Objective 2 – To compare the survival distributions between eyes with progressive RNFL thinning and eyes with progressive decline in RNFL optical texture signature The survival probability of eyes with progressive RNFL optical texture loss was significantly smaller than eyes with progressive RNFL thinning (P<0.001) (please refer to Fig.3 in the enclosed manuscript) because ROTA could detect progressive RNFL change earlier than conventional change analysis of RNFL thickness (please refer to Fig.2 in the enclosed manuscript). Objective 3 – To determine the specificities of Trend-based Progression Analysis (TPA) for detection of progressive decline in RNFL optical texture signature and progressive RNFL thinning The specificity of TPA for assessment of progressive RNFL thinning was 98.8% (95% CI: 95.7-99.7%) whereas the specificity of TPA for assessment of progressive RNFL optical texture loss was 91.6% (95% CI: 86.4-94.9%). Objective 4 – To measure rates of change of VF mean deviation between eyes with and without progressive decline in RNFL thickness/optical texture signature The rate of change of visual field index (VFI) was -1.02%/year (95% CI: -1.66 to -0.37%/year) for eyes with progressive RNFL thinning, and -0.51%/year (95% CI: -0.94 to -0.08%/year) for eyes without progressive RNFL thinning; and it was -0.94%/year (95% CI: -1.50 to -0.39%/year) for eyes with progressive RNFL optical texture loss, and -0.31%/year (95% CI: -0.68 to 0.06%/year) for eyes without progressive RNFL optical texture loss. Objective 5 – To measure age-related rates of change of RNFL thickness/optical texture signature We are still analyzing the data from the normal group in the analysis. We expect the results will be available within one month. Objective 6 – To compare the sensitivity and specificity for detection of glaucoma between RNFL optical texture analysis (ROTA) and conventional OCT analysis We have completed another study to specifically compare the sensitivity and specificity for detection of glaucoma between ROTA and conventional OCT analysis and the results have been published in Nat Biomed Eng (2022;6:593-604). Using VF testing as the reference standard, the specificity of ROTA (94.3%; 95% CI: 91.3–97.2%) was higher than that of the topographic RNFL thickness analysis (87.9%; 95% CI: 83.6–92.3%) and the topographic GCIPL thickness analysis (78.1%; 95% CI: 72.4–83.8%). For the detection of early glaucoma (mean VF MD: −3.40 ± 1.60 dB), the sensitivity of ROTA (97.3%; 95% CI: 94.9–99.6%) was higher than that of the topographic RNFL thickness analysis (91.8%; 95% CI: 87.8–95.8%) and the topographic GCIPL thickness analysis (92.3%; 95% CI: 88.5–96.2%). For the detection of glaucoma (mean VF MD: –11.21 ± 8.31 dB), ROTA had a higher sensitivity (98.7%; 95% CI: 97.7–99.7%) than topographic GCIPL thickness analysis (96.8%; 95% CI: 95.3–98.3%). Although integrating topographic RNFL/GCIPL thickness analysis increased the sensitivities comparable to that of ROTA for the detection of early glaucoma and glaucoma, the specificity decreased to 71.4% (95% CI: 65.4–77.5%).

14101518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101518.value: A total of 773 eyes of 423 patients with glaucoma (735 eyes of 400 patients) or OHT (38 eyes of 23 patients), and 167 eyes of 106 healthy individuals were recruited for visual field (VF) testing and optical coherence tomography retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) imaging at 4-month intervals over a mean of 36.0 months. Progressive RNFL thinning and progressive RNFL optical texture loss were determined by Trend-based Progression Analysis (TPA). Over 3 years, 12.4% of eyes showed VF progression, 13.6% had progressive RNFL thinning, and 45.7% showed progressive RNFL optical texture loss. Progressive RNFL optical texture loss developed earlier than progressive RNFL thinning by an average of 6 months. Eyes with progressive RNFL thinning (HR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.05, 3.05), or progressive RNFL optical texture loss (HR: 2.43, 95% CI: 1.59-3.71, P<0.001) significantly increased the risk of VF progression, after adjusting for intraocular pressure levels, age, axial length, and VF mean deviation. The latter, but not the former, remained predictive of VF progression in eyes with moderate to advanced glaucoma (HR: 3.00, 95% CI: 1.33-6.74, P=0.008). The specificity of TPA was 98.8% (95% CI: 95.7-99.7%) in detecting progressive RNFL thinning, and 91.6% (95% CI: 86.4-94.9%) in detecting progressive RNFL optical texture loss. In conclusion, ROTA was able to detect progressive RNFL change earlier than conventional RNFL thickness analysis. Eyes with progressive RNFL optical texture loss had a high risk of development of VF progression in early, as well as in moderate to advanced glaucoma.

14101518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101518.value: We will conduct a multi-center trial, randomizing patients with advanced primary open-angle glaucoma (visual field (VF) mean deviation ≤-12dB) into two management paradigms with provision of additional intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering treatment upon (I) detection of progressive RNFL loss by ROTA, or (II) detection of progressive RNFL/GCIPL thinning by conventional progression analysis. All patients will have clinical examination, OCT imaging, and perimetry 2-monthly (alternate testing with 24-2 and 10-2 tests) for 36 months. The objectives are to compare the rates of change of VF sensitivity (primary outcome measure), and time to VF progression within 36 months between the two treatment paradigms. We hypothesize that patients managed under Paradigm I to have a slower rate of VF sensitivity decline with a longer time to develop VF progression compared with those managed under Paradigm II.

14101518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101518.value: This study aimed to investigate two methods of detecting disease progression in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. These methods analyze changes in the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), a part of the eye significantly affected by glaucoma. The first method looks at the thinning of the RNFL, while the second examines the loss of optical texture in the RNFL. In simpler terms, imagine the RNFL as the bark of a tree. The first method is like looking at how thin the bark has become, while the second method is more like studying the patterns and textures on the bark that may be lost due to disease. This study, which followed 423 patients over three years, found that 12.4% showed visual field progression, a sign of worsening glaucoma. Additionally, 13.6% had progressive RNFL thinning, and a significant 45.7% showed a progressive loss of RNFL optical texture. Interestingly, this loss of texture was observed six months earlier than the thinning. To summarize, loss of optical texture in the RNFL is a notable early sign of disease progression, potentially even more so than the thinning of the RNFL. Therefore, assessing changes in optical texture could significantly improve early detection and management of glaucoma.

14102418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102418.value: 準確發現和識別糖尿病黃斑水腫並及時治療可以預防視力損害。現時主要通過無創方式進行頻域光學相干斷層（SDOCT）掃描，在數秒內展示三維分層視網膜結構成像，作為診斷及管理糖尿病黃斑水腫的工具。然而，目前的SDOCT分類並未提供有關特定眼疾的訊息，識別糖尿病黃斑水腫時，需要眼科醫生特別是具有視網膜專門知識的眼科醫生來闡釋SDOCT的數據。 由於現階段缺乏對SDOCT分析具有豐富經驗和專門知識的人手，使SDOCT掃描未能達至可行暨有效的篩查。 現時治療糖尿病黃斑水腫的首要方法為抗血管內皮生長因子（anti-VEGF）療法，主要應用於中心性黃斑水腫的患者。不過，患者需要反復地接受侵入性的玻璃體腔注射，並且有近一半的患者對此項治療沒有反應。近期的研究一致表明，SDOCT圖像上的一些特徵（例如橢球帶的完整性）可以前瞻地判斷糖尿病黃斑水腫的患者對anti-VEGF治療是否有效。然而, 目前具有視網膜和SDOCT專門知識的專家仍需要人工閱讀以闡釋SDOCT的特徵。此外, 現時尚未有一個完善的方法結合與視力相關的SDOCT圖像上的特徵，用以指導臨床醫生分辨患者「可能」或「不太可能」對anti-VEGF治療具有效反應。 深度學習是人工智能（AI）機器學習算法的一個分支，現時證明通過訓練人工智能可以處理大數據並且優化圖像分類的工作表現，甚至超越人類水平。在這項研究中，我們將開發深度學習卷積神經網絡（CNN），讓該網絡自動學習SDOCT圖像上糖尿病黃斑水腫的視網膜特徵和模式。我們會回顧地收集香港兩家主要的醫院的糖尿病患者及從大型社區研究中正常對照組之SDOCT圖像數據，以用於CNN的發展。隨後，我們將會用一個從香港、中國大陸、新加坡和美國收集的大型、多中心參與數據庫，以作為CNN的外部驗證。 我們提議的AI-SDOCT系統將用作篩查工具，在當前篩選工作流程下更準確地識別糖尿病黃斑水腫，這將會大大地減少闡釋SDOCT圖像所需的人力。此外，我們提出的系統亦將用作個體化風險評估工具，將病患分類為「可能」或「不太可能」對anti-VEGF治療具有效反應，以輔助治療管理決策。

14102418.label: Realisation of objectives
14102418.value: Accurate identification of diabetic macular edema (DME) and timely treatment can prevent vision loss. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) is widely used as a tool to detect and manage DME. Nevertheless, current OCT classification does not provide information regarding specific eye diseases. Interpretation of OCT data for DME assessment still requires expertise from retinal specialists. This is prohibitively cost-ineffective, and also practically impossible due to the lack of experienced expert manpower to perform screening. In terms of treatment for DME, anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy is now considered first-line treatment for DME involving foveal centre. However, nearly half of patients do not respond to these treatments. Recent studies have consistently shown that features from OCT (e.g. integrity of the ellipsoid zone) have the ability to prospectively determine which individuals with DME would or would not respond to anti-VEGF treatment. However, the current identification of these OCT features is performed manually by experts with specialized knowledge in medical retina and OCT. Furthermore, there is no good way to incorporate the vision-related OCT features to guide clinicians to classify eyes into likely or unlikely to have good response to anti-VEGF treatment for assisting therapeutic management decision. In this study, we first proposed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) convolutional neural network (CNN) using 3D volumetric OCT data cube for the detection of DME with further classification into central-involved DME [CI-DME] versus noncentral-involved DME [non-CI-DME] (Specific Aim 1). We hypothesized that the performance of the CNN for detecting and classifying DME from OCT images is comparable to the human experts in patients with diabetes. For this aim, our objective has been fully achieved. We successfully trained and validated two versions of a multitask CNN to classify DME (CI-DME, non-CI-DME, or absence of DME) using 3D volume scans and 2D B-scans, respectively. For both 3D and 2D CNNs, we used the residual network (ResNet) as the backbone. For the 3D CNN, we used a 3D version of ResNet-34 with the last fully connected layer removed as the feature extraction module. A total of 73,746 OCT images were used for training and primary validation. External testing was performed using 26,981 images across seven independent data sets from Singapore, Hong Kong, the U.S., China, and Australia. Specifically, in classifying the presence or absence of DME, the DL system achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs)> 0.937 for the primary data set obtained from CIRRUS, SPECTRALIS, and Triton OCTs, in addition to AUROCs >0.906 for the external data sets. For further classification of the CI-DME and non-CI-DME subgroups, the AUROCs achieved above 0.951 for the primary data set and >0.894 for the external data sets. Our study substantially extends existing research and studies as follows. First, currently, most reported DL algorithms for DME detection on OCT have mainly been trained and tested using cross-sectional B-scans. In the present study, we trained a CNN model to detect DME using 3D volume-scans obtained from Cirrus OCT, achieving a comparable performance. Application of 3D volume-scan brings about substantial merits on DL algorithms training. For instance, it is labored and time-consuming for experts to label numerous B-scans for conducting supervised system training. Using labeled images from the volume-scan level to train the proposed CNN reduced the burden of labeling work while at the same time maintaining excellent performance. Our study’s second novel feature is the classification of DME into CI-DME and non-CI-DME subgroups by the DL system. This subgroup categorization of DME is clinically important for DR screening, as it determines the re-examination frequency, the necessity and timing for referral to ophthalmologists, and the treatment recommendations in different resource settings, according to the International Council of Ophthalmology (ICO) Guidelines for diabetic eye care. The sub-classification of DME will help to triage patients more effectively in DR screening programs, reducing false-positives, conserving resources—especially in low- or intermediate-resource regions or countries, and enabling ophthalmologists to prioritize patients who need prompt treatment for preventing vision loss, allowing for the better utilization of costly specialist care resources and shorter hospital wait times. Our third novelty is the ability of the DL system to detect non-DME retinal conditions. Most previously reported DL systems only focus on one disease besides DME. Our study goes beyond previously published work by detecting non-DME retinal abnormalities among individuals with DM, enhancing the applicability of our DL system in real-world screening settings. For Specific Aim 2, we trained another DL algorithm to categorize eyes into likely or unlikely to respond if treated with anti-VEGF, among eyes with CI-DME. We hypothesize that DL can further classify eyes with CI-DME based on baseline OCT images into likely or unlikely to have good prognosis if treated with anti-VEGF. Our objective has been achieved with the manuscript being prepared for submission. We successfully trained another integrated DL framework consisting of three networks using pre-treatment OCT images and clinical variables: 1) a segmentation network to segment 4 major features (i.e., intraretinal cysts [IRC], subretinal fluid [SFR], disorganization of retinal inner layers [DRIL], and outer-retinal defects [ORD]) from OCT B-scan; 2) a classification network to detect the presence of 4 features from OCT B-scan; and 3) a multi-modal network that combined the results of segmentation and classification networks, and the clinical variables (visual acuity [VA] and central subfield thickness [CST]) for classifying eyes into “likely” or “unlikely” to have good prognosis if treated with anti-VEGF. A total of 16,477 OCT images were used for primary training and validation. External testing was performed using 5,632 OCT images across three independent data sets from Giridhar Eye Institute, India, Sankara Nethralaya Hospital, India and the Westmead Institute for Medical Research at the University of Sydney, Australia. Based on the best recognition performance of the segmentation and classification model, the prediction of IRC, DRIL and ORD from the classification model, and the prediction of the SRF from the segmentation model were used to facilitate the multi-modal network to classify treatment response. The integrated DL system ultimately achieved an AUROC of 0.731(0.619-0.844) for the primary dataset, and AUROCs >0.629 across three external datasets. Our algorithm has a great potential to be used as an individualized risk assessment tool to predict good or poor response to anti-VEGF treatment for patients with DME. As 40-50% of patients do not respond to anti-VEGF treatment, our proposed algorithm would be very useful for therapeutic selection and thereby reduce the impact of invasive and burdensome treatment for patients in whom anti-VEGF therapy is likely to be ineffective. Furthermore, ophthalmologists can assist in patient counseling on different treatment regimen (e.g. intravitreal steroid injection) or early visual disability support. In conclusion, we demonstrated excellent performance with a DL system for the automated classification of DME. It has a great potential to be implemented as a second-line screening tool to facilitate a more effective triaging mechanism to eye clinics for the detection of DME among DM population. Furthermore, we also trained another DL system that achieved comparable performance to general ophthalmologists for classifying eyes into “likely” or “unlikely” to have good prognosis if treated with anti-VEGF. It has extended the promise to be used as a clinical supporting tool assist therapeutic management decision, benefiting patients with more optimal and economical personalized therapeutic regimen.

14102418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102418.value: For aim 1, as we demonstrated excellent performance with a DL system for the automated classification of DME, our study provided evidence to support the promise of incorporating OCT into current retinal fundus photography–based DR screening programs as a second-line screening tool for facilitating an efficient and reliable detection of DME among patients with diabetes. It might lead to reductions in overreferrals and increased clinical use of DL systems. Thus, in the next phase, we aim to estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of incorporating the DL system into DME screening and to conduct a prospective study to show how the DL system to support DME screening and referral pathways to eye clinics real-world clinical settings. For aim 2, as our proposed algorithm achieved comparable performance to general ophthalmologists for classifying eyes into “likely” or “unlikely” to have good prognosis if treated with anti-VEGF, the integrated system has the potential to be used as a clinical supporting tool assist therapeutic management decision. In the future plan, we aim to implement this system in eye clinics in Hong Kong and further conduct a prospective study to test its accuracies for identifying potential responders and avoiding unnecessary treatment for the non-responders.

14102418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102418.value: Diabetic macular edema (DME) can develop at any stages of diabetic retinopathy. It is a primary cause of irreversible vision loss in individuals with diabetes. In this study, we developed DL systems with good performance to identify DME and categorize eyes into likely or unlikely to respond if treated with anti-VEGF. Our DL systems have huge potential to facilitate DME screening, and be a potential individualized risk assessment tool to predict good or poor response to anti-VEGF treatment for patients with DME. The overall screening model can be made more cost-effective by incorporating the DL system to become more rapid and automated, thereby reducing the need for having a large number of trained personnel on-site. This enhancement would consequently enable the effective stratification of at-risk patients for further investigations, saving medical resources and speeding up the clinical workflow for diabetic eye disease detection and referral/triage. In addition, incorporating the DL systems will enable more accurate DME detection and earlier intervention, thereby further minimizing irreversible losses in vision and quality of life due to DME.

14102718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102718.value: The invasion from marine to freshwater environments is among the most momentous macroevolutionary events in the history of life. Diversification in freshwater biome is often faster than usual, blooming to at least 126,000 species known today. Such transition poses intense physiological challenges to organisms, since freshwater fauna requires innovative mechanisms to actively take up essential ions from the dilute medium against concentration gradient. Osmoregulation – the ability to control fluid and electrolyte balance – is vital for guiding many cellular functions in all life forms. While osmoregulation has been intensively studied in selected taxa, there is a dearth of understanding on the evolution of osmoregulation underpinning marine-freshwater transitions. Many important questions have yet to be answered, such as what molecules are involved in osmoregulation, how they function, what changes give organisms different hyper- and hypo-osmoregulation abilities, and do convergent evolution of freshwater adaptation in evolutionary distinct lineages involve divergent or similar evolution of osmoregulation mechanisms and genetic changes? Nonetheless, these questions cannot be fully answered without vigorous phylogenetic frameworks and comprehensive understanding of the molecules involved in osmoregulatory functions. Caridean shrimp, a very diverse and ecologically important group of decapod crustaceans that inhabit a wide range of salinity, provide an excellent model for investigating the evolution of osmoregulation. In the past decade, our lab has developed multiple molecular markers for phylogenetic analyses and succeeded in reconstructing a robust phylogeny of Caridea. With this phylogeny as the foundation guiding systematic comparisons, and in combination with physiological experiments and high throughput sequencing technology to comprehensively elucidate the molecular changes underlying salinity adaptation, the proposed study will be the first to apply a phylophysiological approach to study the evolution of osmoregulation that instigated freshwater colonization in decapod crustaceans. Findings will not only shed new light on this important macroevolutionary transition, but also yield valuable information that could contribute to advancement of aquaculture of caridean shrimps, which are one of the most commercially important decapods worldwide. 從海洋進入淡水環境是生命進化史上最重要的宏觀進化事件之一。淡水生物種化速度普遍較其他生態系統的生物為高，至今已經有超過126,000種生物在淡水中繁衍。適應淡水環境對生物造成很大的生理壓力──牠們需要演化出一套機制使之能抵抗濃度梯度並從淡水中主動吸收重要離子。生物通過滲透調節來控制體液和電解質平衡，此功能對所有生物都至關重要。雖然現在已經有大量關於特定物種的滲透調節的研究，但我們對海水-淡水轉化過程中滲透調節的進化還缺乏了解，很多重要的問題亟待解答。例如，哪些分子參與了滲透調節以及它們是如何起作用的？物種為甚麼有不同的高滲和低滲調節能力？不同生物適應淡水環境的能力是源自趨同演化還是迴然不同的機制？解答這些問題需要有完備的系統發育框架和對滲透調節相關分子機制的全面理解。 真蝦下目是一群多樣性高、生態地位重要的十足目甲殼類動物。牠們廣泛分布於不同鹽度的環境中，是非常適合研究滲透調節進化的模式生物。在過去十幾年中，我們研究團隊設計了一系列的分子標記以作系統發育分析，並且成功構建了可靠度高的真蝦下目系統發育樹。以此為基礎進行比較，並結合生理實驗和高通量測序技術，我們將全面地闡明鹽度適應過程中的分子調控機制的演化。本研究將成為首次使用系統生理學方法來研究十足目甲殼類動物適應淡水環境的滲透調節的進化機制。本研究的成果不但會揭示這個重要的宏觀進化過程，並將產生許多有價值的訊息，有利於真蝦下目這種高經濟價值的十足動物的養殖。

14102718.label: Realisation of objectives
14102718.value: To achieve objective 1, we first reconstructed the most comprehensive molecular phylogeny of Caridea today based on two different datasets. The first dataset used consisted of five nuclear protein-coding genes, and 12S, 16S, and 18S rRNA from 213 caridean species in 30 families, while the second dataset contains smaller number of taxa, but larger number of marker gene coverage that consisted of the whole mitochondrial genomes plus the five protein coding gene and 18S on 80 species from 28 families. The second dataset include mitogenome from 53 species were newly sequenced in the present study, including 14 families that were sequenced and annotated for the first time. Phylogenetic reconstruction was performed based on the two datasets to obtain a robust phylogenetic framework for subsequent comparative analyses. Subsequently, we review the literature to obtain a matrix for the habitat and lifestyle, as well other major morphological characters of the Caridean species. The characters were then mapped onto our inferred phylogeny for ancestral state reconstructions. We found that there were at least six independent invasions into the freshwater/anchialine habitat with one reversal back to marine conditions (in the genus Palaemon). The family Atyidae (approaching 500 species) and the genus Macrobrachium (Palaemonidae, approximately >250 species) represented the two major radiation following the invasion of freshwater habitat while the remaining freshwater/anchialine lineages all contain fewer than ten species. We further conducted a diversification rate analysis using a fossil calibrated phylogeny, the results showed that invasion into the freshwater habitat result in significant increase in speciation rate, at least twice compared to other habitats. This maybe attributed to the novel ecological once the physiological barriers were overcome as well as the more prominent vicariance in the freshwater environment compared to the marine counterpart. To achieve objective 2, we conducted salinity stress experiments and gill tissue transcriptome sequencing for two freshwater, two achialine and one marine Caridean species. We explore gene expression changes in hypotonic environments and compare protein-coding gene evolution rates among different groups through transcriptome sequencing data. We also performed comparative transcriptomics and adaptive evolution analyses to understand the genetic basis behind this evolution. Differential gene expression We first investigated the regulatory mechanisms of different Caridean groups under hypotonic conditions by analyzing shared GO terms in the enrichment results of five Caridean shrimp species, representing functional differences. Our findings revealed that in the up-regulated gene enrichment results, both anchialine and freshwater carideans possessed terms associated with ion pumps, primarily sodium-potassium pumps. This suggests a universal role for ion pumps in osmoregulation, in line with previous studies. On the other hand, it is noteworthy that in the up-regulated gene enrichment results for anchialine species, GO terms pertaining to muscle-related functions were generally present, while this observation was not made in freshwater species. In the down-regulated gene enrichment results, GO terms appearing in multiple species were primarily restricted to freshwater species, predominantly involving amino acid-ion symporters and similar proteins. This finding implies that in isotonic environments, the expression or activity of such transport proteins in freshwater species might increase. Research has demonstrated that elevated expression of sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporters (SNAT) in the rat brain can lead to cellular amino acid accumulation for adaptation to a hypotonic environment. This mechanism might serve a similar function in freshwater species; however, no studies have reported the relationship between these transport proteins and osmoregulation in decapods. The lack of this phenomenon in anchialine species could suggest either an absence of comparable capabilities or unidentified relevant genes. Freshwater Caridean Exhibit Accelerated Molecular Evolution The evolutionary rate (dN/dS) of protein-coding genes serves as a crucial indicator of the interplay between genotype and environment. Organisms inhabiting mild environments typically exhibit lower evolutionary rates, while those in extreme environments face more rigorous survival challenges, leading to accelerated evolution in protein-coding genes. Using KaKs Calculator and PAML, the ω of 290 one-to-one orthologous genes was calculated, revealing that the ω of freshwater Caridean was significantly higher than that of anchialine Caridean. This finding implies that freshwater species undergo accelerated evolution at the protein level, potentially due to low ion concentration and freshwater infiltration. These factors increase the energy consumption of freshwater organisms, and adaptation to freshwater environments results in an elevated evolutionary rate in freshwater species. Positive Selection of Osmoregulation-related Genes in Freshwater Caridean Detecting positive selection for the two freshwater species species and their ancestral branches revealed significant positive selection in certain osmoregulation-related genes, such as argK and NKA. ArgK is analogous to creatine kinase in vertebrates and can regulate energy metabolism in crustaceans, playing a crucial role in adapting to various environmental stressors. NKA is a vital membrane-bound protein that maintains cellular osmotic balance by pumping sodium and potassium ions, playing an indispensable role in maintaining body fluid and electrolyte homeostasis. Furthermore, significant positive selection was detected in other kinases (e.g., cAMP-dependent protein kinase), which might also be associated with freshwater species adaptation. Besides the previously mentioned genes, significant positive selection was not observed in other osmoregulation-related genes, although some displayed p-values less than 0.05 before BH correction.

14102718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102718.value: Based on the robust and comprehensive phylogeny of Caridean shrimp inferred in the project, we discover multiple independent invasions (at least six) of freshwater habitat by marine ancestors. Furthermore, this results in increased in diversification rate in two lineages, the Atyidae and the Macrobrachium, compared to the shrimp living in other habitats. As a collateral benefit from the phylogeny inferred here, we also provide insights into the taxonomy and evolution in Caridean shrimps by 1/ resolving the taxonomic position of two enigmatic shrimps, Amphionides and Procarididae; 2/ reject the monophyly of a number of families (e.g. Hippolytidae and Pasiphaeidae) and superfamilies (e.g. Alpheoidea) that would provide a framework for future taxonomic revision; and 3/ revealed the evolutionary pattern of morphological characters in relationship to the transition in habitats (e.g. freshwater, deepsea and symbiosis etc). In the second part of the project, we analyzed freshwater and anchialine Caridean to explore gene expression changes in hypotonic environments and compare protein-coding gene evolution rates among different groups through transcriptome sequencing data. We also performed comparative transcriptomics and adaptive evolution analyses to understand the genetic basis behind this evolution. From a gene expression level standpoint, the up-regulated DEGs of both anchialine and freshwater species under hypotonic conditions are enriched in GO terms related to P-type pump activity. This finding suggests that both shrimp species possess osmoregulatory processes driven by various P-type ion pumps, and marine shrimp display the same pattern under hypotonic stress. This observation highlights the ubiquity of this osmoregulatory pattern within Caridean. However, numerous enriched terms found exclusively in a single species or Caridean group indicate that the mRNA expression changes of various genes in shrimp under hypotonic conditions exhibit high species specificity. This observation may apply not only to osmoregulation but also to other physiological responses of Caridean in hypotonic environments. From a genetic change perspective, positive selection was detected in some osmoregulation-related genes in the freshwater species lineage. This finding suggests that osmoregulation of freshwater species has either completed or is still undergoing adaptive evolution under the selective pressure of the freshwater environment. This evolutionary process may have played a critical role in freshwater species adapting to a consistently hypotonic aquatic environment. Investigating how amino acid changes in positive selected osmoregulation-related genes influence Caridean’s osmoregulation can provide further insights into the differences in osmoregulation between various Caridean groups.

14102718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102718.value: In the present project, we revealed the genetic mechanisms of freshwater colonization by Caridean shrimps. It would be interest to conduct further analyses to comparing the genetic basis of freshwater adaptation in other decapod or crustaceans, to determine whether these independent colonization events utilized similar or different genetic mechanisms. This could provide a broader picture on the genetic mechanism for freshwater colonization and adaptation in invertebrate in general, illuminate the molecular toolkit of animal in adapting to new environment. On the other hand, we are attempting to verify the results of comparative transcriptomic analyses using proteomic approach. Some biochemical analyses will be beneficial as we can evaluate the actual performance at protein level for the detected mutation and selection. This could verify the current data and provide another dimension to the issue.

14102718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102718.value: Marine to freshwater colonization represents a significant evolutionary transition in biological history, with the evolution of osmoregulation being a crucial step for aquatic organisms adapting to freshwater environments. Few studies have utilized the phylogenetic framework to compare and examine how adaptive evolution occurred in each lineage during the transition. Here, we reconstructed the most comprehensive phylogeny for Caridean shrimp to date and found at least six independent transitions into freshwater/anchialine habitat, and these transitions result in increase in diversification compared to other lineages. Subsequently, we performed comparative transcriptomics and adaptive evolution analyses to understand the genetic basis behind this evolution. The results revealed that gene expression changes in Caridean exhibit strong species specificity, but freshwater and anchialine species displayed osmoregulatory patterns driven by various ion pumps. A faster protein-coding gene evolution rate was observed in the freshwater Caridean, with some osmoregulation-related genes showing significant positive selection. The positive selection of these genes may have shaped the unique osmoregulatory mechanism in freshwater Caridean. Moreover, this study sheds light on the potential impact of salinity on decapod meat quality and suggests that amino acid transporters may be involved in osmoregulation, with freshwater Caridean displaying a higher metabolic rate.

14103418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103418.value: Sequential waves of follicular development cycling throughout the reproductive years in females mark the dynamic nature of the ovaries for their critical roles in nourishing oocytes. Complex hormonal control is required to guarantee the short-lived and recurring process of folliculogenesis with temporal precision. The drastic changes in ovarian tissue composition dictated by the hormone signals rely on the exquisite spatiotemporal collaboration in proliferation, apoptosis and differentiation among various ovarian cell types, notably granulosa cells (GC). GC is an ovarian somatic cell type of the sex cord closely associated with the developing oocyte. The past decade of rapid boom in genomic technologies facilitated the study of ovarian function by characterizing novel functional genes in GC. Frequent attempts in understanding gene regulation of GC were only up to the transcriptional level. Nevertheless, knowledge in the post-transcriptional control in GC, particularly of its dynamic changes during folliculogenesis, is inadequate. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) were discovered as a group of critical ‘fine-tuning’ post-transcriptional regulators commonly involved in both physiological and pathological conditions. Judging from the dynamic nature of mammalian ovaries, miRNAs are predicted to play a role in the regulation of follicular functions with pioneer success in functional characterization for some of these miRNAs. The miR-10 family is comprised of two member miRNAs, i.e. miR-10a and miR-10b, both located in the Hox cluster, where critical developmental regulators Hox genes were embedded. Intriguingly, miR-10a was identified as a cell type-specific miRNA by small RNA sequencing of human GC while the function of miR-10 family in GC remains elusive. Indeed, our group had confirmed the expression of both members in human and murine GC which suggested their conserved function. The aim of this project is to investigate the specific role of miR-10 family in GC during ovarian follicular development. Our previous results obtained from human, mouse and rat GC transfected with miRNA mimics revealed part of the functional role of the family. In addition, by using in vivo model and miR-10 analogue in C. elegans (Cel-miR-57), the anti-production role of miR-10 were further confirmed. In this project, both miR-10a and miR-10b conditional knockin mice will be recruited to delineate the functions of the miR-10 family during follicle development in vivo while related mechanisms will be explored with the aid of novel sequencing technologies. Elucidating the role of the miR-10 family in GC shall enable us to unravel post-transcriptional regulation during ovarian follicle development and likely presents novel insights for therapeutic interventions. 過往的研究成果指出微RNA (miRNA) 有效調控身體裏不同生理結構的正常運作、發育、代謝或生長各層面，而微RNA表達量異常的情況往往可導致原位疾病。我們研究組針對miR-10家族在卵巢結構的表達水平，佐以人類卵巢顆粒細胞系和動物模型中收集的原代細胞結果分析內，揭示了這些分子在卵泡發育中擔任不可或缺的作用 。 本項目的課題側重於考究miR-10家族在卵泡發育過程中所擔當的分子調控機理。是此研究所得將有賴於轉基因小鼠的顆粒細胞中靶向敲入miR-10家族成員並深入研究這些分子如何影響卵泡發育，繼而影響排卵作用和生殖力等器官功能和衰竭。 課題的宗旨包括以下兩項： 1. 以靶向敲入miR-10的小鼠模型進行體內和體外實驗調查miR-10如何影響卵泡發育； 2. 以高通量測序方式尋找與miR-10互動的分子並引證其如何改變信號通路達致功效。

14104918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104918.value: Globally, tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of mortality. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has, in response, set the goal of eliminating TB by 2050. In places like Hong Kong, reactivation accounts for a majority of TB diseases, the proportion of which has been increasing as a result of population ageing. Host factors aside, environmental pollution has been proposed as one of the potential factors predisposing to TB reactivation, which demands public health attention. As a high-ranking mortality risk factor globally, PM2.5 has been shown in laboratory experiments to adversely affect innate and adaptive immunity mounted by alveolar macrophages. There is however scarcity of population study on the association between ambient PM2.5 and TB reactivation. In this 3-part study, we propose to use, for the first time, high resolution (1km x 1km) PM2.5 spatial data to generate new knowledge on its inter-relationship with TB reactivation, in the territory of Hong Kong. In Part 1, TB notification data spanning between 2005 and 2017 would be collected and converted into a georeferenced dataset for profiling their spatiotemporal association with PM2.5. Seasonality and clustering patterns would be uncovered, and their associations with age and socio-economic factors determined statistically. In Part 2, a cross-sectional study would be conducted to recruit newly diagnosed TB patients, for differentiating between reactivation and non-reactivation TB by the corresponding spatio-temporal pattern of PM2.5. As there is no gold standard for clinically defining reactivation TB, we would apply different working criteria for classifying TB cases enrolled in the study. Using results obtained in Part 1 and 2, the population burden of reactivated TB would be projected in Part 3. This would involve an analysis of the inter-relationship between projected changes of PM2.5 and social-demographic changes of the population in Hong Kong, over the next 10 years. Despite the small size of Hong Kong, the relatively complete TB surveillance data and the availability of corresponding environmental and census data in spatial dimensions would lend support to the conduct of the proposed cross-disciplinary study. The results would be important for informing public health control of reactivation TB, in Hong Kong and places with similar socio-demographic characteristics. While the achievability of WHO’s TB elimination goal remains a concern, the study would highlight the relative importance of ameliorating particulate matter pollution for reducing reactivation TB burden.

14104918.label: Realisation of objectives
14104918.value: Through a 3-part study incorporating high resolution PM2.5 concentration data and real-world data of incident TB cases from an intermediate endemicity city dominated by reactivation diseases – Hong Kong, all the project objectives of the study have been achieved and the relationships between ambient PM2.5 exposure and TB reactivation have been investigated. Small-area spatio-temporal analysis was firstly performed to profile the spatio-temporal pattern of ambient PM2.5 concentrations in contexts of its associations with pulmonary TB (PTB) notifications among population subgroups: the elderly aged ≥ 65 and the working-age population aged 15-64 which have different LTBI prevalence, reactivation risk and proportion of observed TB incidence attributable to reactivation (objective 1). Annual PTB notifications data between 2005 and 2017 in Hong Kong involving 64386 cases were mapped down to District Council Constituency Area (DCCA) level by population subgroups, and correlated with ambient PM2.5 concentration using Bayesian conditional autoregressive model adjusted for other criteria pollutants and socio-economic factors. A cross-sectional study on the clinical epidemiological data of newly reported TB cases registering from May 2019 to August 2020 was followed. After exclusion of cases most likely to have resulted from recent infection, latent class analysis was used to delineate the population phenotypes of active TB cases with various reactivation risk cum clinical profiles. Individuals’ ambient PM2.5 exposure was estimated using a high-resolution (1 km2) satellite-based spatio-temporal model. Differential associations between the ambient PM2.5 exposure and the identified phenotypes were examined (objective 2). Lastly, projection of the population burden of TB reactivation in the future ten years (i.e. 2018-2027) under different scenarios of PM2.5 evolution trend was made based on results obtained in the spatio-temporal analysis and cross-sectional study (objective 3). Seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous factors (SARIMAX) models incorporating ambient PM2.5 of 6-month and 12-month lag were constructed to predict the incidence of elderly TB in Hong Kong, which are largely results of reactivations.

14104918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104918.value: From the spatio-temporal analysis, after accounting for the potential confounding effects from the socio-economic factors, higher ambient PM2.5 concentration was significantly associated with increased pulmonary TB (PTB) notifications among the elderly ( ≥ 65) and the working-age population (15-64). While the effect estimates of PM2.5 for the PTB risk among the elderly were consistently stable to the further adjustments for other criteria pollutants, the association between ambient PM2.5 exposure and PTB risk among the working-age population were less stable and strongly confounded by other criteria pollutants, particularly PM10 and SO2. Four distinct TB population phenotypes with various reactivation risk profiles and clinical presentations: “Elderly male”, “Otherwise healthy younger adult”, “Older female” and “Male smoker” were identified in the cross-sectional study. Exposure to high concentration of ambient PM2.5 at 6 and 12 months prior to notification was significantly associated with increased odds of belonging “Otherwise healthy young adults”, as compared to “Elderly male”. Such association became less evident for other phenotypes. Along with the continuous reduction in ambient PM2.5 concentration in the coming 10 years as predicted, notifications of incident TB cases among the elderly population might experience an overall downward trend in 2018-2022 with a plateau during the subsequent years. Hypothetical scenarios with the reduction rate of PM2.5 concentration increased by 10%, 20% and 30% would result in faster decline in elderly TB at the beginning but the effects would not be sustainable. The overall consistent, stable and significant spatio-temporal associations patterns among the elderly suggested that increased TB reactivations might have occurred after high ambient PM2.5 exposure. The differential associations between ambient PM2.5 exposure and TB population phenotypes with varied reactivation risk profile provided further evidence supporting the role of ambient PM2.5 exposure in TB reactivation, and that its relative contribution varied among different TB population phenotypes. The projected slow decline and subsequent plateau in elderly TB notification under different scenarios of ambient PM2.5 temporal evolution suggested that the burden of reactivation TB in Hong Kong would not be reduced simply by mitigation of PM2.5 pollution, unless the large latent TB infection (LTBI) reservoir is treated with scaled up LTBI management. Study findings provides evidence to inform the development of LTBI management targeting selected subpopulations with high LTBI reservoir, for which attention to environmental factors is advocated beyond the conventional strategy of prioritization by immunocompromised states.

14104918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104918.value: Future research could be conducted to further consolidate the understanding of the role of ambient PM2.5 in TB reactivation, through other angles and approaches. For example, conducting studies in other countries or cities with different ambient PM2.5 concentration level, as well as some specific settings (e.g. subdivided unit in Hong Kong) using similar methodologies. Large-scale cohort studies could be performed to confirm the causality between ambient PM2.5 exposure and TB reactivation, with the dose-response relationship examined. Alternatively, the role of ambient PM2.5 exposure in TB reactivation could be clarified by further incorporating the information from molecular epidemiology tools such as Mycobacterial Interspersed Repetitive Units – Variable Tandem Repeats (MIRU-VNTR) typing or Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS). Generating evidence for other possible risk factors of TB reactivation could be useful. Development and validation of a scoring system for profiling an individuals’ risk of progression from LTBI to active TB could help to determine the potential benefit of LTBI treatment in clinical level and guide the treatment options. In addition, future research could also be performed to investigate the differential effectiveness and harm, acceptability, drug adherence and completion, as well as the potential psychosocial impacts (e.g., stigmatization and fear) related to LTBI testing and treatment in different population subgroups.

14104918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104918.value: Tuberculosis (TB) reactivation accounts for a significant proportion of newly diagnosed TB cases in intermediate endemicity city Hong Kong. It hypothesized that environmental pollution could play a role ion TB reactivation. A 3-part research project was conducted that had made use of high resolution (1km2) PM2.5 concentration data and real-word data of active TB cases notified in Hong Kong, with the aim to explore the relationship between ambient PM2.5 exposure and TB reactivation. The results showed that ambient PM2.5 exposure was associated with TB reactivation. The relative contribution of ambient PM2.5 in TB reactivation varied by population phenotypes as differentiated by reactivation risk and clinical profiles. Study findings highlighted the need in the development and implementation of targeted management of latent TB infection at population level, for which attention to environmental factors is needed beyond the conventional strategy of prioritization by immunocompromised states.

14105418.label: Realisation of objectives
14105418.value: For Objective 1: To address the functional importance of Sox9 in choroid plexus (CP) development and regulation of cerebrospinal fluid secretion, we will analyze the roles of Sox9 in three aspects including (a) CP basal lamina integrity, (b) establishment of CP epithelial polarity, (c) transcytosis across the CP epithelium. Having found that the loss of Sox9 function in the developing choroid plexus (CP) led to aberrant hyperpermeability of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) barrier, we aimed to address the functional importance of Sox9 in CP development and regulation of CSF secretion. To this end, we employed the Cre/loxP approach to obtain conditional mutants that are with Sox9 specifically deleted in the hindbrain CP (Sox9 CKO). (a) Analysis on the role of Sox9 in CP basal lamina integrity Since we observed atypical cell morphology of the Sox9 mutant CP epithelium from H&E sections, we hypothesized that the basal lamina integrity of CP epithelium was hampered by the loss of Sox9. We performed transcriptome analysis with control and Sox9-deleted CP (result for Objective 2). The results obtained suggested that expression of Col9a3, which encodes the alpha-3 chain of type IX collagen, was drastically down-regulated in the Sox9 CKO CP. We further verified this finding by quantitative RT-PCR and in situ hybridization. We demonstrated by in vivo chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) that SOX9 could directly associate with the enhancer element located at Col9a3 intron 1. Therefore, we proceeded to investigate whether the downregulation of Col9a3 expression was accountable for the CP hyperpermeability in Sox9 CKO mutants. To this end, we delivered siRNA targeting Col9a3 into the CP by in utero electroporation at E14.5 prior to the establishment of blood-CSF barrier. Subsequently, we evaluated the permeability of CP epithelium by tracer extravasation assay. Upon the silencing of Col9a3 expression, fluorescent 10 kDa dextran molecules extensively infiltrated into the CP epithelium, whereas the tracers were excluded from the epithelial layer in control CP. Moreover, we further elucidated how loss of Col9a3 interfered the basal lamina integrity. Since previous studies reported that Col9a3 is responsible for maintaining matrix integrity in cartilage by anchoring ECM macromolecules, we studied the expression of major ECM components in the CP epithelial basal lamina by immunostaining. We found that only discontinued patches of collagen I or laminin deposition could be found at the basal lamina 3 days after Col9a3 silencing. Notably, similar phenomenon was observed in the Sox9 CKO mutants. These results together suggest that SOX9 governs the basal lamina integrity of CP epithelium through the regulation of Col9a3 expression. (b) To investigate the role of Sox9 in epithelial polarity and its relevance to CSF secretion Since our preliminary results indicated that the ablation of Sox9 from CP epithelium led to incorrect orientation of apicobasal polarity determinants Par-3, we further investigated whether this would affect the epithelial polarity and cellular junction formation. For this purpose, we performed transmission electron microscopy (TEM) on E18.5 CP from control and Sox9 CKO mutants. We observed the typical tight junction ultrastructure of electron-dense bands forming the apical kissing points between adjacent epithelial cells in normal CP at E18.5. Remarkably, the intercellular space between adjoining CP epithelial cells in Sox9 CKO was substantially wider and without any electron-dense structures, suggesting the absence of tight junctions upon Sox9 inactivation. Next, we examined the expression of the tight junction scaffold protein zonula occludens 1 (ZO-1) by immunohistochemistry. In control CP epithelial cells, ZO-1 was positioned at the apical-most surface. However, ZO-1 was dispersed randomly along the entire apicobasal axis in Sox9 CKO CP. Furthermore, the localization of adherens junction components E-cadherin and β-catenin were both abnormally present on the apical cell surface in the Sox9 CKO mutants at E18.5. Next, to evaluate the impact of perturbations of apicobasal polarity to CP function, we first examined the directional transport system in the CP. By immunostaining of the Na+ K+ ATPase α1 subunit (ATP1A1), we showed that the Na+/K+ pump was diffused towards the basal side in the Sox9 CKO CP epithelium instead of positioned at the apical surface. On the other hand, the basolateral transporter anion exchanger 2 protein (AE2) was displaced from the basal membrane and mislocalized to the apical domain following Sox9 ablation. Quantitative plots of apical/basal transporter subcellular distribution revealed that the membrane asymmetry of CP epithelium was eliminated in the Sox9 CKO mutants. Moreover, we measured CSF electrolyte levels by atomic absorption spectroscopy. Although CSF K+ level was only subtly increased, the concentration of Na+ ions was remarkably reduced by 34% in the Sox9 CKO mutants. In conclusion, our findings demonstrated that SOX9 is critical for defining the correct apicobasal polarity of CP epithelium and is thus essential for CSF homeostasis. (c) To investigate the role of Sox9 in the regulation of transcytosis across CP Another major function of CP is the secretion of extracellular vesicles that contain nutrients, metabolites, RNAs and proteins essential for CNS homeostasis and function. Therefore, we also addressed the importance of SOX9 in the regulation of CP secretion. To address this possibility, we pooled the CSF from multiple embryos and analyzed the concentration and size distribution of extracellular vesicles by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA). The concentration of vesicles with sizes ranging from 30-120 nm in diameter (generally defined as exosomes) was specifically depleted in the CSF of Sox9 CKO. To verify this finding, we performed immunostaining on CP sections with antibodies against the exosome marker protein CD63. The number of CD63 puncta was remarkably fewer in the Sox9-null CP epithelium. The reduction of exosome secretion into mutant CSF could be the consequence of a defective exosome biogenesis machinery or merely a secondary sequel of limitedly available cargoes. To rule out either possibility, we made use of an endotoxemia model which systemic inflammation is induced by in vivo injection of bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS). In the LPS-induced CP, considerably more CD63+ puncta were present in the apical side of epithelium when compared to the non-treated group. In contrast, CD63+ vesicles were absent or only slightly increased in LPS-treated Sox9-null CP. These results suggested that SOX9 is required for the biogenesis of CSF exosomes in the CP epithelium. For Objective 2: To search for novel genetic controls of choroid plexus development and regulation of cerebrospinal fluid secretion, we will identify Sox9 downstream target genes during initial blood-cerebrospinal barrier establishment. From the work described in Objective 1a, we performed transcriptome analysis with control and Sox9-deleted CP. We successfully identified Col9a3 as a novel direct target of SOX9 during CP development for governing the basal lamina integrity of CP epithelium.
