14105418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105418.value: Human mutations in the transcription factor SOX9 are commonly associated with congenital disorders in the CNS including hydrocephalus and ventriculomegaly. The leading causes of hydrocephalus include abnormalities in ependymal cells lining the brain ventricles or, more recently, the dysfunction of the choroid plexus (CP). The CP is a highly vascularized neuroepithelial structure in the brain ventricles that restricts the unauthorized passage of blood-borne molecules into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). However, studies in mouse models with Sox9 loss-of-function in the CNS thus far did not reveal the pathological mechanism underlying hydrocephalus. Moreover, the molecular pathways that regulate the proper sealing of blood-CSF barrier at the CP are completely unknown and represent a major question in the field. In this present study, we demonstrate that SOX9 is vital to the integrity of blood-CSF barrier. The conditional ablation of Sox9 in mouse CP epithelium elicits a cascade of cellular defects that eventually cause the CP to become hyper-permeable. We identified collagen IX as the direct effector of SOX9. Mechanistically, SOX9 activity transcriptionally regulates Col9a3 expression which is required for the anchorage of extracellular matrix (ECM) components at the epithelial basement membrane. Temporal silencing of Col9a3 abolishes the ECM-cytoskeleton interactions necessary for polarized microtubule dynamics. Accordingly, this leads to perturbations in the already-established apicobasal polarity and impediments in tight junction assembly. Loss of Sox9 function in CP ultimately upsets the electrolyte balance and elevates the protein level in CSF, and importantly, such alterations in CSF composition modify the CSF signaling niche at the functional level. Therefore, our findings, published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS) in 2021, identify an unprecedented role of SOX9 as the pivotal player in ensuring the integrity of blood-CSF barrier. The mechanisms identified thus provide a plausible explanation for the pathophysiology of hydrocephalus in patients with SOX9 mutations by establishing a mechanistic linkage between loss of SOX9 function in CP and aberrant protein loading into CSF. Finally, and more broadly, our findings demonstrate a model of in vivo mammalian epithelial polarity regulation that requires homeostatic signaling cues from ECM, which contrasts with the common perception that the importance of ECM becomes negligible once the apical/basal poles are initially specified. While such a paradigm is mainly built upon studies in cell-based systems or invertebrates, our findings may exemplify a mechanism of polarity regulation that represents a generalized phenomenon in other mammalian tissues.

14105418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105418.value: To search for more novel SOX9 downstream transcriptional targets, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing for control and Sox9 CKO hindbrain CP at E16.5. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering identified 18 cell clusters with unique gene expression markers. We used well-established CP epithelial markers (e.g. Ttr, Aqp1, Folr1) to annotate clusters that are epithelial cells. We further cluster the epithelial cells into 12 clusters and identified differential expressed genes (DEGs) specifically found in CP epithelial cells including Col9a3. Interestingly, we found a substantial number of top DEGs are involved in the regulation of ion transport or secretory pathway, including Defb9 (Defensin beta 9), Defb10 (Defensin beta 10), Bloc1s1, and more. Interestingly, we found that the expression of these DEGs displayed remarkable heterogeneity among the 12 epithelial cell clusters, suggesting that the CP can be divided into highly functional specific subdomains. The roles of these secretory proteins in regulating CSF production remain unknown. However, our results suggest that Sox9 is critical for their proper expression in the CP. By analyzing the expression and functions of all these potential target genes in CP, we can decipher the molecular regulation of CP development and function, which is critical for the possible alleviation of CSF-related neurological disorders.

14105418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105418.value: We have discovered that Sox9 protein is an essential regulatory factor of choroid plexus function that ensures the correct composition of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The finding has provided the scientific community with a novel understanding of the molecular regulatory mechanisms behind the function of the blood-CSF barrier and lays the groundwork for developing novel therapeutic strategies for preventing and treating neurodevelopmental disorders. From previous experiments, we have observed the development of hydrocephalus in laboratory mice with genetic deletion of Sox9 from the choroid plexus epithelium, which drew our attention. After further investigation, it was found that the loss of Sox9 function led to an abnormal increase in hyperpermeability of the blood-CSF barrier. In the absence of Sox9 function, there was a dramatic increase in the CSF protein level with abnormal deposition of blood-borne proteins in the CSF of mutant mice, which is a common phenomenon in patients with hydrocephalus. Through RNA sequencing, we found Sox9 is required for the synthesis of collagen IX at the choroid plexus epithelium for maintaining the integrity of the epithelial layer. Based on what we have learned in this research, we are now attempting to harness the choroid plexus function to alleviate CSF-related neurological disorders.

14106218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106218.value: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial aims to evaluate if delayed resumption of aspirin (ASA) in patients with cardiovascular (CV) diseases complicated by peptic ulcer bleeding, as recommended by current international guidelines, will reduce the risk of recurrent bleeding without an increase in mortality. Gastrointestinal bleeding (GI) due to ASA is one of the most common causes of hospitalization worldwide. In China, ASA consumption will rise with the estimated increase of 21 million CV events in the next 20 years. The prevalence of upper GI bleeding in China remains high between 3·9% and 5·5%. In our university center where we manage 800 cases of peptic ulcer bleeding annually, ASA accounts for over 30% of all bleeders. The timing of resuming ASA after peptic ulcer bleeding is a major clinical challenge. Clinicians have to balance the bleeding against thrombo-embolic risks. Early resumption of ASA may increase risk for recurrent bleeding whereas prolonged discontinuation may lead to serious adverse CV outcomes. We have previously shown in a randomized placebo-controlled trial that among ASA users complicated by peptic ulcer bleeding requiring endoscopic treatment, uninterrupted ASA therapy increased risk of recurrent ulcer bleeding by 2-fold within 30 days but reduced all-cause mortality rate by 10-fold compared with patients who discontinued ASA for 8 weeks. The European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Guidelines on Management of Non-variceal Upper GI Bleeding has adopted our findings and recommends that instead of uninterrupted ASA, ASA should be resumed by day 3 following index endoscopy. However, this recommendation is solely based on expert opinion and there are no prospective data to guide optimal timing of ASA resumption. This randomized clinical trial tests the hypothesis that in ASA users complicated by peptic ulcer bleeding, delayed resumption of ASA at day 3 reduces the risk of recurrent bleeding compared with uninterrupted ASA without a significant increase in mortality. Our hypothesis is based on the observation that the risk of early rebleeding is highest within the first 3 days and that anti-platelet (cardioprotective) effect of ASA may last for 5 days after the last dose. The primary endpoint is recurrent ulcer bleeding within 30 days. Secondary endpoints include all-cause mortality and specific-cause mortality. The outcome of this industry-independent trial will not only fill our knowledge gap but also provides invaluable data to international guideline committees on the optimal timing for reinitiation of ASA after peptic ulcer bleeding in terms of GI and CV safety. 根據現行國際指引，患有心血管疾病的病人在出現消化性潰瘍出血後，應延遲恢復阿士匹靈。這項隨機，安慰劑對照試驗旨在評估這樣做是否能減低復發性出血而不增加死亡的風險。阿士匹靈引起的胃腸道出血是全球最常見的其中一個入院原因。在中國，估計在未20年，心血管疾病事件會增加2100萬宗，須要服食阿士匹靈的人會隨此增加。中國上消化道出血的患病率高達3·9％-5.5％。我們的研究中心每年處理500宗消化性潰瘍出血，由阿士匹靈引起的佔30％以上。消化性潰瘍出血後何時恢復阿士匹靈是一個重要的臨床問題。醫生必須平衡出血與血栓栓塞的風險。提前恢復阿士匹靈可能會增加複發性出血的風險，但延長停藥則可能會導致嚴重的不良心血管疾病結果。我們之前在一項隨機安慰劑對照試驗中表明，阿士匹靈使用者在出現需要內鏡治療的消化性潰瘍出血後，與停用阿士匹靈 8週的患者相比，不間斷阿士匹靈治療會增加30天內復發性潰瘍出血的風險達2倍，但全因死亡率則降低至十分一。歐洲胃腸內鏡學會的非靜脈曲張性上消化道出血管理指引採納了我們的研究結果，建議阿士匹靈應在應在內鏡檢查後第3天恢復，而不是不間斷的使用。但是，此建議僅基於專家意見，而非建基於試驗數據。這項隨機臨床試驗旨在驗証這樣的假設：阿士匹靈使用者在消化性潰瘍出血後，延遲3天恢復阿士匹靈與不間斷使用相比，可降低復發性出血，同時不會增加死亡風險。我們的假設是基於以下觀察結果：早期再出血的風險在頭3天內最高，而 阿士匹靈抗血小板（心臟保護）的作用可於最後一次給藥後持續達5天。此研究的主要結果是30天內復發性潰瘍出血。次要結果包括全因死亡率和特定原因死亡率。這項獨立的非藥廠試驗不僅能填補現時數據空白，更能為國際指引委員會說明消化性潰瘍出血後重新恢復阿士匹靈的最佳時機。

14106318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106318.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are phytotoxins widely distributed in plant kingdom worldwide. Ingestion of high doses of PAs causes acute hepatotoxicity. While, for relatively low-level PA exposure, acute hepatotoxic manifestations are often latent, but the resultant chronic diseases, such as liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and cancer, may gradually develop. Due to the extensive distribution of PAs in nature, humans are readily exposed to PAs through the consumption of PA-containing herbs/natural products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Fasting is increasingly and widely adopted in populations nowadays. Considerable evidence from animal and human studies has suggested that fasting, particularly intermittent fasting, can trigger adaptive cellular responses, causing an enhanced ability to resist stress and ameliorate disease processes. Fasting-induced reduction of oxidative stress and inflammation, optimal energy metabolism, and enhancement of autophagy are beneficial to patients with various metabolic and chronic diseases, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancers. On the other hand, fasting even with a short period like overnight can significantly reduce the hepatic concentration of glutathione (GSH), which is vital for detoxifying various exogenous toxins. PA intoxication is caused by hepatic metabolism to generate toxic metabolites, which interact with proteins leading to toxicity, but can be detoxified by hepatic GSH. We anticipated that the fasting-reduced hepatic GSH content could enhance acute hepatotoxicity caused by high doses of PAs. Our preliminary data confirmed that single (overnight) fasting remarkably decreased hepatic basal GSH level by ~45% and significantly enhanced acute hepatotoxicity of a typical toxic PA (retrorsine) in rats. However, whether such a fasting-caused detrimental effect also occurs with prolonged exposure to low doses of PAs is unknown. Considering the high risk of PA exposure and often adopted fasting habit in our daily life, it is significant to study whether and how different fasting patterns would affect PA intoxication. Therefore, our proposed study aims to 1) investigate the impact of single and intermittent fasting on acute hepatotoxicity induced by exposure to high doses of PAs; 2) study the effect of intermittent fasting on chronic hepatotoxicity caused by prolonged exposure to low doses of PAs; and 3) delineate the underlying mechanisms that different fasting patterns may potentiate or reduce hepatotoxicity caused by different PA exposure regimens. The results obtained will provide scientific information for public awareness of benefits or potential risks of different fasting patterns with concurrent intake of PA-containing/PA-contaminated natural products. 吡咯裡西啶類生物鹼（PA）是一類廣泛分佈於自然界的植物毒素。攝入大劑量的PA會引起急性肝毒性，而長期攝入低劑量的PA雖無明顯的急性癥狀，但會逐步引起多種慢性毒性，如：肝纖維化、肝硬化和肝癌。由於PA在自然界中廣泛的分佈，PA很容易通過含有PA的草藥或植物和PA污染的食物而被人們攝入。 近年来節制飲食正被人們廣泛且越來越多地採用。大量來自動物及人體研究表明：禁食，尤其是斷續性禁食，可觸發細胞的適應性反應，從而提升機體對抗壓力及改善疾病進程的能力。禁食引起的氧化應激及炎症水準的降低、能量代謝的改善以及自噬的增強，均對患有多種代謝性及慢性疾病的病人有利，比如：糖尿病、心血管類疾病及癌症。PA中毒是由於其在肝臟中被代謝啟動而形成的毒性代謝產物所致。PA毒性代謝產物可與肝臟中的蛋白共價結合從而引發肝毒性。我們的預試驗已經證明短期禁食可顯著地加重倒千里光堿（一種典型的毒性PA）所致的大鼠急性肝毒性。然而，這種禁食所致的有害影響是否會在長期低劑量PA暴露中發生尚且未知。 考慮到PA攝入的高風險性及禁食習慣的風靡，關於不同禁食模式對PA中毒影響的研究已十分迫切。因此本項目旨在：1）研究單次及斷續性禁食對大劑量PA攝入所致急性肝毒性的影響；2）研究斷續性禁食對長期低劑量PA暴露所致慢性肝毒性的影響；3）闡明不同禁食模式加重或降低不同PA攝入模式所致肝毒性的內在機制。預期取得的研究結果將為提升公眾對不同禁食模式，尤其當禁食過程中同時攝入含有PA或被PA污染的天然產物，所致的有利因素及潛在風險的認識提供科學依據。

14106318.label: Realisation of objectives
14106318.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are phytotoxins widely distributed in ~6000 plant species. Humans are exposed to PAs mainly through the consumption of PA-containing plants used as herbal medicines and dietary supplements, and PA-contaminated foods like wheats, teas, and honeys. Ingestion of high doses of PAs causes acute hepatotoxicity. While, for relatively low level of PA exposure, acute hepatotoxic manifestations are often latent, but the resultant chronic diseases, such as liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and cancer, may gradually develop. Fasting is increasingly and widely adopted in populations nowadays. The results of various well-controlled animal and human studies have suggested that fasting may provide beneficial effects to reduce body weight, delay aging, and optimize health. Fasting has been considered to ameliorate disease processes and improve the functional outcome of a variety of diseases related to aging and metabolic dysregulation. On the other hand, fasting is also known to cause a significant decrease of hepatic glutathione (GSH) concentration, resulting in exacerbated toxicity of hepatotoxic drugs. PA intoxication is caused by hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYPs)-mediated metabolism to generate reactive pyrrolic metabolites, that interact with proteins to form pyrrole-protein adducts (PPAs) leading to PA-induced liver injury (PA-ILI). While the reactive pyrrolic metabolites can be detoxified by GSH via GSH conjugation to produce pyrrole-GSH adducts, which are further degraded and excreted from urine. Therefore, we hypothesize that both single and intermittent fasting may augment acute hepatotoxicity caused by PAs partly due to significant decrease in GSH concentration, weakening GSH detoxification pathway, while intermittent fasting, such as alternate day fasting for a relative longer period, may have beneficial or detrimental effects on PA-ILI. Present project aims to investigate the effects of different fasting patterns on PA-ILI by different PA exposure regimens and their underlying mechanisms. Objective 1—We have investigated the effect of overnight fasting on a representative toxic PA retrorsine (RTS)-induced acute hepatotoxicity. Two treated groups, ad libitum-fed (Feed+RTS) and overnight-fasted (Fast+RTS) male SD rats were orally administered with RTS (40 mg/kg) and sacrificed at 48 h after dosing. RTS did not cause obvious hepatotoxicity in Feed+RTS rats, while significantly elevated serum ALT activity and total bilirubin level, and severe liver hemorrhage were found in Fast+RTS rats. Further, sinusoidal damage, the typical feature of PA-ILI, was observed only in Fast+RTS rats. Our findings demonstrate overnight-fasting significantly augmenting PA-ILI. Further kinetic study demonstrated fasting 1) significantly accelerated absorption time but not alter amount absorbed; 2) remarkably increased clearance resulted in less systemic exposures (AUC); and 3) significantly reduced excretion from urine and feces, reveling that fasting did not alter absorption but significantly reduce excretion of RTS. The results further demonstrate that overnight-fasting causes remarkably faster metabolic elimination, indicating that fasting may significantly accelerate the rate of metabolism which is relevant to metabolic activation of PAs causing PA-ILI. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published in scientific papers (Abstracts 1-2 and Papers 1-2 in Part C). Objective 2—For study of the effects of intermittent fasting on PA-ILI, various models with different fasting patterns were investigated. In an alternate day fasting (ADF) model, rats underwent alternate day fasting for 6 weeks, compared with RTS-treated group, ADF significantly reduced weight gain, caused more severe hepatocellular ballooning and nuclear enlargement in liver parenchymal cells, and further led to the development of liver cirrhosis and progressive hepatic fibrosis, demonstrating exacerbated PA-ILI. Because intermittent fasting may induce autophagy, as a survival mechanism autophagy is a highly conserved intracellular degradation pathway and readily activated in our daily life under adverse conditions, such as nutrient deficiency and intermittent fasting. We further investigated the effects of autophagy on PA-ILI in different models. The results demonstrated that activation of autophagy attenuated PA-ILI in both C57BL/6J mice and human HepaRG cells via removing PPAs and damaged mitochondria, thereby reducing apoptosis in hepatocytes. In addition to fasting patterns, many factors, such as lifestyles and diets, are known to have impacts on PA-ILI. Our study on dietary alcohol revealed that its long-term exposure caused vasculature damage, fibrosis, and steatosis in mouse livers, indicating that co-exposure to PAs with dietary alcohol exacerbated PA-ILI. Furthermore, we revealed that moderate alcohol intake did not affect initial hepatic CYPs-mediated bioactivation of PAs but significantly disturbed hepatic glutathione homeostasis, thereby increasing oxidative stress, and enhancing PA-ILI. Moreover, our study demonstrated that long-time fasting effect has a detrimental impact on small intestine, and intestinal epithelium damage and disruption on intestinal barrier function in acute and chronic situations also significantly exacerbated PA-ILI. Our findings clearly demonstrate significant effects of fasting and dietary patterns on PA-ILI. Such effects can be beneficial or detrimental, therefore precautionary interventions are warranted on hazardous effects of dietary exposure to PAs, particularly with the fasting patterns inhibiting autophagy, concomitant alcohol consumption, and diets disrupting intestinal barrier function, etc. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published in scientific papers (Abstracts 4-5 and Papers 3-4 in Part C). Objective 3—In order to delineate potential mechanism underlying overnight fasting-enhanced PA intoxication, we investigated PPAs formed from different PAs, including RTS. The toxicokinetic profile of PPAs, particularly pyrrole-plasma protein adducts, was also investigated in fed and fasted rats after oral administration of RTS. The results revealed that compared to Feed+RTS rats overnight fasting significantly increased plasma concentration (Cmax ~1.5-fold) and systemic exposure (AUC ~1.6-fold) of PPAs in Fast+RTS rats, confirming that metabolic activation leading to hepatotoxicity is the major and important metabolic pathway of RTS. Moreover, the levels of PPAs in liver and blood of Fast+RTS rats were also significantly higher than that of Feed+RTS rats. All findings revealed that overnight fasting significantly exaggerated PA metabolic activation to generate toxic pyrrolic metabolite, leading to increased formation of PPAs, thus exacerbating hepatotoxicity. Further toxicokinetic studies revealed that overnight fasting signiﬁcantly enhanced CYPs-mediated metabolic activation of RTS leading to significantly increased formation of PPAs. Metabolic studies further demonstrated that fasting induced activities of various CYP enzymes that participated in catalyzing RTS to generate reactive pyrrolic metabolites. Moreover, fasting dramatically decreased hepatic GSH content, which restricted detoxiﬁcation of GSH by neutralizing reactive pyrrolic metabolite of RTS, further contributing to the enhanced hepatotoxicity. Parts of results have been reported in conferences and published in scientific papers (Abstracts 1-2 and Papers 1-2 in Part C). The mechanisms underlying beneficial or detrimental effects of intermittent fasting are much more complicated. In general, mechanisms underlying beneficial effects are fund to be mainly involved in autophagy induction, while mechanism underlying detrimental effects mainly involve GSH detoxification impairment via GSH reduction resulting less detoxification, increased CYPs-mediated metabolic activation leading to increased PPAs formation, prolonged PPAs persistence, and enhanced interactions between upregulated fibrogenesis factors and autophagy. Furthermore, for mechanistic studies, we have developed various LC-MS methods for analyzing PAs and PPAs, the mechanism-based biomarker of PA-ILI. For improving sensitivity and persistence of the biomarker for testing acute and chronic animal models and thus for better clinical usage, we further developed pyrrole-hemoglobin adducts and urinary pyrrole-amino acid adducts as non-invasive biomarker, and successfully applied these newly developed biomarkers for definitive diagnosis of PA-ILI patients. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published in scientific papers (Abstract 3 and Papers 5-6 in Part C).

14106318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14106318.value: Our findings for the first time provide solid evidence and comprehensive information on the effects of fasting on PA-induced liver injury (PA-ILI). Firstly, fasting can cause beneficial or detrimental effects on PA-ILI. Secondly, for the beneficial effect, the fasting-induced activation of autophagy can attenuate PA-ILI via removing PPAs and the damaged mitochondria in hepatocytes. Thirdly, for the detrimental effect, fasting can significantly augmentee PA-ILI, mainly due to the significantly increased formation of toxicity-related pyrrole-protein adducts in the liver through the following two underlying mechanisms: 1) significantly enhancing CYPs-mediated metabolic activation leading to the increased formation of reactive pyrrolic metabolite; 2) remarkably reducing hepatic GSH content resulting in the impairment of GSH detoxification pathway; 3) prolonged PPAs persistence in the body, and 4) enhanced interactions between upregulated fibrogenesis factors and autophagy. Fourthly, different dietary patterns may also significantly affect the severity of PA-ILI. For instances, co-exposure of PAs with alcohol can exacerbate PA-ILI, and co-exposure of PAs with diets which may disrupt intestinal barrier function and/or increase intestinal epithelium permeability can worsen PA-ILI. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences and published in scientific papers (Abstracts 1-5 and Papers 1-6 in Part C). Further, few more manuscripts reporting the above-mentioned findings are currently under preparation for future publication.

14106318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14106318.value: Our findings for the first time provide a comprehensive information on the effects of fasting on PA-ILI and extend the understanding of beneficial and detrimental effects of fasting on PA-ILI and their potential mechanisms. However, the detailed mechanism underlying such effects on PA-ILI via fasting, especially different intermittent fasting patterns are far from fully delineated. Therefore, further in-depth mechanistic investigations are warranted. In addition to fasting patterns, beneficial or detrimental effects of different dietary patterns on PA-ILI are also significant and requested for further in-depth investigation. Apparently, public health education on avoiding the intake of PA-containing herbs and/or dietary supplements for self-health care is warranted. While, if it is unavoidable of these naturally occurring toxins, appropriate regulation for PA exposure is prerequisite. However, currently available regulations for controlling PA exposure via medicinal herbs and contaminated staple foods are mainly build based on animal studies and limited evidence-supported human PA toxication cases. While, such regulations are lacking factors, such as lifestyle and dietary diversities which may significantly affect toxic potency of PA-ILI. Further investigation on effects of human dietary pattens and lifestyles in the daily life on PA-ILI are warranted for establishing better and more realistic regulations for PA exposure.

14106318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14106318.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are natural toxins widely present in ~3% flowering plants worldwide. Humans are readily exposed to PAs by ingestion of PA-containing herbal products or PA-contaminated foodstuffs. PAs are known to cause liver toxicity. The toxicity is caused by liver P450 enzyme-catalyzed metabolism to produce toxic metabolites, which form protein adducts to damage liver. While glutathione in the liver can detoxify PAs by reacting toxic metabolites to form non-toxic conjugate readily excreted from urine. Our findings demonstrate that PA-induced liver toxicity can be significantly reduced or enhanced via human lifestyles and diets. For examples, a short time fasting can dramatically enhance PA-induced liver toxicity because of significant increase in P450 enzyme activity and reduction of glutathione level in the liver. On the other hand, intermittent fasting can induce autophagy to remove the formed protein adducts, thus reduce PA-induced liver toxicity. Furthermore, different lifestyle and dietary patterns can also affect PA-induced liver toxicity. For example, dietary alcohol may worsen PA-induced liver toxicity. Our studies demonstrate that PA-induced liver toxicity is a common phenomenon via consumption of PA-containing herbs and PA-contaminated staple foods in our daily life, and different lifestyle and dietary patterns may significantly reduce or enhance PA-induced liver toxicity.

14106518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14106518.value: Cancer cells are high in heterogeneity, therefore easily adapt to external stresses and lead to drug resistance. Targeting tumor microenvironment (TME) is a new approach for cancer. Recently, we found that Smad3-dependent TME (Smad3-TME) originated from bone marrow and essential for TGF-beta-driven cancer progression by suppressing NK cell immunity against cancer via a E4BP4-dependent mechanism. We finally demonstrated that genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of Smad3 also can protect mice against the lethal progression of invasive lung carcinoma and melanoma via enhancing anticancer immunity. Surprisingly, our preliminary studies also found that TGF-beta/Smad3 can suppress the neutrophil anticancer activities. We detected a dramatic increase in neutrophils in the Smad3-KO TME of two syngeneic mouse cancer models, and Smad3-KO neutrophils show enhanced cancer-killing activity and anticancer N1 phenotypes in vivo and in vitro. By using chromatin immunoprecipitation high-throughput DNA sequencing (ChIP-seq), we further identified a quiescence mediator Prdm2 is markedly up-regulated in the tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN) in a TGF-beta1/Smad3-dependent manner. Interestingly, adaptive transfer of Prdm2-silencing neutrophils can reproduce the anticancer effects of Smad3-KO neutrophils on Smad3-WT mice bearing LLC-tumor. Based on these novel and exciting discoveries, we thus hypothesize that neutrophil suppression is one of the key mechanism thereby Smad3-TME facilitating cancer progression. Thus, we proposed in this study to define a role and mechanisms whereby TGF-beta/Smad3 signalling regulates neutrophil activities against cancer by studying 3 specific aims. 1) We will investigate the role of Smad3-TME in neutrophil suppression in cancer patients and two syngeneic lung carcinoma (LLC) and melanoma (B16F10) mouse cancer models. 2) Then we will investigate the regulatory role and mechanism of TGF-beta1/Smad3 signalling in inhibition of neutrophil anticancer activities. 3) Finally, we will elucidate the downstream mechanism of Smad3-Prdm2-mediated suppression of anticancer neutrophil activation in TME. By completing this study, we expect to identify Smad3 as a key mediator of neutrophil anticancer immunity in TME. Importantly, the inhibitory role of TGF-beta1/Smad3/Prdm2 signalling in cancer immunity specifically on neutrophil will be uncovered. Finally, the working mechanism of Prdm2 on neutrophil immunity at transcriptional level will be identified. Thus, outcomes from this study will be highly innovative and significant both scientifically and clinically. 癌細胞具有高度異質性，因此容易適應外部應力並導致耐藥性。靶向腫瘤微環境（TME）是一種新的癌症治療方法。最近，我們發現Smad3依賴性TME（Smad3-TME）起源於骨髓，並且通過依賴E4BP4的機制抑制NK細胞對癌症的免疫，對TGF-β驅動的癌症進展至關重要。我們最終證明，Smad3的遺傳缺失或藥理學抑制也可以通過增強抗癌免疫力來保護小鼠免受侵襲性肺癌和黑素瘤的致死進展。令人驚訝的是，我們的初步研究還發現TGF-β/ Smad3可以抑制中性粒細胞的抗癌活性。我們檢測到兩種同基因小鼠癌症模型的Smad3-KO TME中的中性粒細胞顯著增加，並且Smad3-KO中性粒細胞在體內和體外顯示出增強的癌症殺傷活性和抗癌N1表型。通過使用染色質免疫沉澱高通量DNA測序（ChIP-seq），我們進一步鑑定了靜止介質Prdm2在腫瘤相關中性粒細胞（TAN）中以TGF-β1/ Smad3依賴性方式顯著上調。有趣的是，Prdm2沉默中性粒細胞的適應性轉移可以再現Smad3-KO中性粒細胞對攜帶LLC腫瘤的Smad3-WT小鼠的抗癌作用。基於這些新穎和令人興奮的發現，我們因此推測中性粒細胞抑制是Smad3-TME促進癌症進展的關鍵機制之一。因此，我們在本研究中提出通過研究3個特定目標來定義TGF-β/ Smad3信號通過調節中性粒細胞抗癌活性的作用和機制。 1）我們將研究Smad3-TME在癌症患者和兩種同基因肺癌（LLC）和黑素瘤（B16F10）小鼠癌症模型中的中性粒細胞抑制中的作用。 2）然後我們將研究TGF-β1/ Smad3信號傳導在抑制中性粒細胞抗癌活性中的調節作用和機制。 3）最後，我們將闡明Smad3-Prdm2介導的TME中抗癌中性粒細胞活化抑制的下游機制。通過完成這項研究，我們期望將Smad3鑑定為TME中中性粒細胞抗癌免疫的關鍵介質。重要的是，將揭示TGF-β1/ Smad3 / Prdm2信號傳導在癌症免疫中對中性粒細胞的抑制作用。最後，將鑑定Prdm2在轉錄水平上對中性粒細胞免疫的工作機制。因此，本研究的結果將具有高度的科學創新性及臨床參考性。

14107118.value: 聚谷氨酰胺（polyQ）疾病是一組神經退行性疾病，包括亨廷頓舞蹈病（HD），脊髓和延髓肌萎縮，牙本質蒼白球萎縮和罕見疾病，如各種類型的脊髓小腦性共濟失調。 PolyQ疾病是由各疾病基因的編碼區中擴增的CAG重複引起的。眾所周知，擴增的CAG重複序列在蛋白質水平上發揮其致病作用;而它們在RNA水平上的毒性作用近年來才剛剛開始被認識到。為了有效治療polyQ疾病患者，了解蛋白質和RNA毒性的機制至關重要。我們的項目旨在闡明polyQ疾病中RNA毒性的潛在機制。我們將poly(A) RNA polymerase D5 （PAPD5）鑑定為通過擴增的CAG RNA穩健上調的基因。我們通過驗證polyQ患者腦樣本中的異常上調，以及in vitro和in vivo 的HD模型，證實了其在人類polyQ疾病中的相關性。我們進一步證明，降低PAPD5足以拯救體內HD模型中的神經變性。已知PAPD5在微小RNA（miRNA）的降解中起作用，微小RNA是基因表達的重要轉錄後調節因子。我們發現擴增的CAG RNA改變了神經元中眾多miRNA的水平。這些miRNA之一的miR-125b響應於CAG重複誘導的PAPD5上調而降解，繼而導致程序性細胞死亡。在該建議書中，我們試圖確定polyQ疾病中的RNA毒性如何增加PAPD5表達，以及增加了的PAPD5如何導致polyQ疾病中的miRNA變化､神經退化及細胞死亡。在目標1中，我們將確定擴增的CAG RNA如何調節PAPD5的轉錄。我們將使用熒光素酶測定來證明兩種轉錄調節因子YY1和AP2-α在正常條件下負調節PAPD5，並且這種負調節被CAG RNA消除。我們將進行染色質免疫沉澱以研究YY1和AP2-α與它們在PAPD5啟動子上預測的結合位點的結合，並檢查它們如何通過DNA甲基化沉默PAPD5啟動子。在目標2中，我們將確定幾種miRNA如何被CAG RNA下調，以及它們如何在polyQ疾病中導致細胞死亡。該項目將為我們提供有關RNA毒性誘導的polyQ疾病發病機制的機制見解，並確定治療發展的潛在分子靶點。

14107118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107118.value: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNA that are responsible for RNA silencing and posttranscriptional regulation of gene expression. They also play crucial roles in the cellular pathogenesis of polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases, including Huntington’s disease (HD). Poly(A) RNA polymerase D5 mediates the degradation of microRNAs (miRNAs). In this study, we showed that the PAPD5 level was induced in cell and animal models of HD. We further demonstrated the Yin Yang 1 (YY1) protein repressed PAPD5 expression at the transcription level. Further, the YY1 protein was recruited to both RNA foci and protein aggregates, which caused PAPD5 transcriptional de-repression in our HD models. By means of miRNA-seq, we identified a subset of PAPD5-regulated miRNAs whose levels were downregulated in our disease model. Upon PAPD5 knockdown, the levels of these miRNA species were restored. We focused on miR-504-5p and miR-7-5p in this study. The gene targets of these two miRNAs are transforming growth factor-beta activated kinase 1 (TAK1)-binding protein 1 (TAB1) and TAB2. The TAB1 and TAB2 proteins form a trimeric complex with TAK1 to regulate its MAPK kinase kinase activity. We found that the downregulation of miR-504-5p and miR-7-5p caused the activation of the TAK1-MKK4-JNK signaling axis and induced cellular apoptosis. Furthermore, we discovered that the PAPD5 small molecular inhibitor, BCH001, could mitigate neuronal defects and cell death in our disease models. This work establishes PAPD5 dysregulation as a novel pathogenic mechanism of HD, and as a potential therapeutic direction for the treatment of HD and other polyQ diseases.

14107118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107118.value: As a noncanonical poly(A) polymerase, PAPD5 possesses enzymatic activity. In general, enzymes are considered to be desirable drug targets. The small molecule BCH001 was recently reported to be able to specifically target PAPD5 enzyme activity. Upon treatment, 3’ adenylation of the non-coding RNA template telomerase RNA component was reduced. We showed that this compound does not induce cell death at 400 nM. When used at 200 nM concentration, BCH001 is sufficient to suppress PAPD5-induced cell death. This highlights the potential of BCH001 to be adopted as a therapeutic for PAPD5-mediated cellular toxicities, and can be further considered as a new therapeutic direction for polyQ diseases treatment.

14107118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107118.value: Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases are caused by the abnormal expansion of CAG repeats in the protein-coding region of genes related to the disease. The CAG repeats encode polyQ tract which becomes the pathogenic part of the disease protein. Patients with polyQ diseases often develop progressive neurodegeneration and motor impairment. MicroRNAs are component of the miRNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) responsible for silencing mRNA targets. Supplementing polyQ disease model animals with miRNAs has been proved to be a possible therapeutic strategy. Understanding how miRNAs are regulated in neurons and why they are dysregulated in polyQ diseases will provide insights into the pathogenesis of diseases and may help with the identification of new therapeutic targets. Our work highlights the importance of a pathway that involves the PAPD5 poly(A) polymerase in polyQ disease pathogenesis. We further identified a compound that can alleviate miRNA dysregulation in polyQ diseases.

14107418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107418.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is a very common sports injury in athletes. As a ruptured ACL does not heal, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) is the standard treatment to restore knee function, but an unpredictable healing and a long rehabilitation period are unavoidable. It is well-known that quadriceps muscle weakness after ACLR is the major limiting factor for functional recovery. Quadriceps muscle weakness is contributed by arthrogenic muscle inhibition and muscle atrophy, which are resulted from joint swelling, pain, inflammation and damage of neuro-receptors in the joint after the surgery. The unfavorable muscular changes can thus be reduced by alleviating joint swelling, pain and inflammation after ACLR. Magnesium emerges as a potential intra-articular analgesic agent to control joint pain and inflammation after surgery, and intra-articular injection of magnesium sulphate after knee surgery has been used clinically. On the other hand, we also showed that vitamin C-containing surgical irrigation solution can reduce post-operative inflammation and reduce excessive knee laxity in ACLR. It is possible that a combination of magnesium and vitamin C in irrigation saline could exert effective peri-operative control on pain, inflammation and knee swelling, which may help to alleviate the extent muscle weakness after ACLR, hence shorten the time of rehabilitation and promote earlier returns to full activities and sports. Our pilot study in a well-established rat model of ACLR revealed that magnesium vitamin C irrigation saline can reduce knee swelling and reduce muscle fibre necrosis; it supports a full scale study to confirm the findings, to optimize the formulation of the irrigation saline and to examine its effects on muscle weakness. We have filed US and China patents for vitamin C irrigation saline with a number of possible electrolytes, including magnesium sulphate. The proposed investigation will further explore the added-values of the patented irrigation saline by combining vitamin C and magnesium. 14108718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108718.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common cancer worldwide. CRC evolves through a sequence of genetic events that triggers malignant transformation. Loss of adenomatous polyposis coli (APC), a tumor suppressor, followed by the activation of oncogenic KRAS are the two pivotal events that initiate colorectal carcinogenesis in humans. KRAS-mutant CRC is an unmet clinical need due to a lack of effective agents targeting activated KRAS. KRAS-mutant CRC exhibits a metabolic phenotype distinct from that of normal colon tissues. Our analyses of gene expression profiles unraveled Steroid Biosynthesis as the top metabolic pathway activated in KRAS-mutant CRC as compared to adjacent normal tissues. Using isogenic cell lines and mice models with concurrent APC loss and mutant KRAS expression, we demonstrated that these genetic alterations co-operatively induced mTOR-SREBP2 activation. Consequently, de novo cholesterol biosynthesis was consistently up-regulated, whereas lipoprotein transport was suppressed. PCSK9, a repressor of lipoprotein uptake, was also acutely induced. This mediated a profound shift in cholesterol homeostasis in APC-silenced, KRAS-mutant cells from transcellular uptake (via lipoproteins) towards de novo cholesterol biosynthesis. Our preliminary work also unveiled PCSK9 as a molecular mechanism that links aberrant cholesterol metabolism to increased proliferation in KRAS-mutant CRC. PCSK9 silencing selectively suppressed proliferation of APC-silenced, KRAS-mutant cells, but had no effect on normal colonic cells. Integrative pathway analysis showed that PCSK9 is essential for cell cycle progression by activating MAPK/ERK cascade. Moreover, PCSK9 expression specifically predicts greater risk of recurrence in KRAS-mutant CRC, but not KRAS wild-type CRC, indicating that PCSK9 plays an oncogenic role in CRC with KRAS mutations. Finally, targeting of co-dependencies of KRAS-mutant CRC on de novo cholesterol synthesis and PCSK9 effectively abolished cell growth. We hypothesize that combinatorial targeting of cholesterol metabolism will be a novel therapeutic approach for KRAS-mutant CRC. To evaluate this, we propose three specific aims: 1) to quantitatively evaluate the effect of APC loss plus oncogenic KRAS expression on cholesterol homeostasis in CRC in vitro and in vivo; 2) to elucidate the molecular mechanism linking deregulated cholesterol metabolism and tumorigenesis of KRAS-mutant CRC; and 3) to assess the therapeutic efficacy of co-targeting de novo cholesterol biosynthesis and PCSK9 in KRAS-mutant CRC. These aims will evaluate the aberrant cholesterol metabolism in KRAS-mutant CRC and how to harass its unique dependencies to achieve a synergistic killing effect. This work will set the stage for developing novel strategies targeting KRAS-mutant, drug resistance subset of CRC. 結直腸癌（CRC）是世界上最常見的癌症之一。 APC的沉默和KRAS的激活是CRC發生的關鍵機制。由於缺乏靶向KRAS的有效藥物，治療KRAS突變型CRC是一個臨床的難題。 KRAS突變體型CRC與正常結腸組織有著不同的代謝表型。通過基因表達譜的分析，我們揭示了類固醇生物合成通路在KRAS突變型CRC比正常結腸組織有異常的激活。使用具有同時APC沉默和突變KRAS表達的細胞系和小鼠模型，我們證明這些遺傳改變共同誘導mTOR-SREBP2活化。因此，膽固醇合成基因一致上調，而脂蛋白轉運基因被抑制。 PCSK9，一種脂蛋白攝取的抑制因子，也被急性誘導。這一系列的改變促進了APC沉默和KRAS突變型細胞的新生膽固醇的合成，卻抑制了外來的膽固醇攝取。我們的初步工作還揭示了PCSK9是一個促進癌細胞生長的因子。 PCSK9沉默選擇性地抑制APC沉默和KRAS突變型細胞的增殖，但對正常結腸細胞沒有影響。整合途徑分析顯示PCSK9通過激活MAPK / ERK通路促進細胞生長。此外PCSK9表達可以預測KRAS突變型CRC的複發風險，表明PCSK9在具有KRAS突變的CRC中發揮致癌作用。最後，共同靶向膽固醇合成和PCSK9可以有效的抑制KRAS突變型CRC的生長。所以我們假設膽固醇代謝的組合靶向將是KRAS突變體CRC的新型治療方法。為了評估這一點，我們提出了三個具體目標：1）定量評估APC沉默加上突變型KRAS表達對體外和體內膽固醇體內平衡的影響; 2）闡明膽固醇代謝失調和KRAS突變型CRC的腫瘤發生的分子機制; 3）評估共同靶向膽固醇生物合成和PCSK9在KRAS突變型CRC中的治療效果。這項工作將為開發針對KRAS突變型CRC的藥物研究奠定基礎。

14108818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108818.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is endemic in Southern China and Southeast Asia with an annual incidence of 15-50 cases per 100,000. Treatment primarily involves radiotherapy +/- chemotherapy. Local recurrent or persistent disease in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) patients typically requires surgical salvage, however local control rates remain poor despite surgical intervention with or without further postoperative radiotherapy. Early detection of local failures are important to permit surgical salvage before locally aggressive lesions are deemed un-resectable. However, detection of local failures are challenging in the nasopharynx, after radiotherapy and in the absence of obvious mucosal lesions. Both nasopharyngeal brush biopsies and plasma EBV DNA have been used in the detection of primary nasopharyngeal carcinoma, but they have not been extensively evaluated individually for the detection of local failure, more importantly a combination of the two modalities to detect local failures of nasopharyngeal carcinoma has never been examined. We hypothesize that the combination of both brush biopsy of the nasopharynx and plasma evaluation of EBV DNA for local failure of nasopharyngeal carcinoma will be superior to the individual tests in detecting a local failure of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. 14108818.label: Realisation of objectives
14108818.value: The achievement of the objectives were extremely difficult during the COVID pandemic as part of the study involved nasopharyngeal swabs and also examination of the nasopharynx with an endoscope. All aerosol generating procedures that severely hampered this study, particularly in patient recruitment, given the location of the bio samples. Furthermore, QEH which was out collaborative partner was also transformed into a COVID hospital during part of the pandemic. We have however, continued to strive to recruit patients from multiple sites to achieve the objectives during periods of quiescence, in between waves of COVID, and when COVID restrictions within the hospitals permitted the samples to be collected for research purposes. At the conclusion of the study we were able to recruit a total of eighty-five patients as part of the study. There were twenty-seven patients in the local-failure group and fifty-eight patients without a local failure. There were no significant differences between the groups in regard to age, gender, primary stage, primary radiotherapy and primary chemotherapy. The transoral nasopharyngeal brush was well tolerated by all patients without complications for the detection of EBV DNA. Results were unavailable in 7 out of the eighty-five patients due to inadequate EBV DNA for detection and a sample loss during delivery. For objective 1: To evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of EBV DNA in the detection of locally recurrent/persistent nasopharyngeal carcinoma through a nasopharyngeal brush biopsy. A transoral NP brush biopsy with the NP screen (NPC Screen, Markham, Ontario, Canada) with proprietary primers and probes to detect EBV EBNA-1 gene, was performed as previously described. The transoral brush is a patented device that requires minimal operator training, is easy to use, and well tolerated by patients. With the use of NP Screen®, EBV will be detected by real-time polymerase chain reaction (rt-PCR) for the EBV-EBNA-1 gene with proprietary primers and probes. The results were reported in the form of EBV Detection Level (EDL). The transoral nasopharyngeal brush was well tolerated by all patients without complications for the detection of EBV DNA. Results were unavailable in 7 out of the eighty-five patients due to inadequate EBV DNA for detection, possible explanations include nasopharyngeal crusting following radiotherapy that may have prevented an adequate contact between the mucosa and the transoral NP brush, and one sample was loss during delivery. For the 7 patients with an inadequate DNA level on transoral brush biopsy, we were unable to obtain patients’ approval for a repeated sample. The median EDL of the local-failure group was 2.77 (IQR = 1.29), while that of the control group was 0 (IQR = 0.63). There was a significant difference in the EDLs between the 2 groups (p<0.01). ROC analysis showed an area under curve (AUC) of 0.89 (95% CI 0.80 – 0.98) with an optimal cut-off for the EDL at 1.98, which suggested that the NP brush is a reliable tool in outcome prediction. With this cut-off, the sensitivity and specificity were 79.17% (95% CI 57.85 – 92.87%) and 94.44% (95% CI 84.61 – 98.84%) respectively. The positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 86.36% (95% CI 67.43 – 95.09%) and 91.07% (95% CI 82.34 – 95.71%) respectively. There was no significant correlation between the recurrent T-classification and the EDL of NP Brush (Spearman Rho = - 0.02, p = 0.93). For objective 2: To evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of EBV DNA in the detection of locally recurrent/persistent nasopharyngeal carcinoma through plasma. A sample containing 10 ml of venous blood in EDTA was obtained from each participant. EBV DNA in plasma was analysed by means of real-time polymerase-chain-reaction (PCR) assay that targeted at the BamHI-W fragment of the EBV genome, as described previously4. All the samples were analysed in duplicate. For plasma detection of EBV DNA, results were available for all patients. For plasma detection of EBV DNA, results were available for all patients. The median EBV DNA level in the local-failure group was 17 (IQR = 54), while that in the control group was 0 (IQR = 0). There was a significant difference in the EBV DNA levels between the 2 groups (p<0.01). ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.79 (95% CI 0.68 – 0.91) with an optimal cut-off of 9 copies/ml. With this cut-off value, the sensitivity and specificity were 59.26% (95% CI 38.80 – 77.61%) and 91.38% (95% CI 81.02 – 97.14%) respectively. The PPV and NPV were 76.19% (95% CI 56.68 – 88.68%) and 82.81% (95% CI 75.23 – 88.43%) respectively. There was a significant correlation between recurrent T-classification and plasma EBV DNA level (Spearman Rho = 0.39, p = 0.04). For objective 3: A combination of both of the optimal cut-offs for the transoral nasopharyngeal brush and plasma for the detection of EBV DNA showed a sensitivity and specificity of 84.62% (95% CI 65.13 – 95.64%) and 85.19% (95% CI 72.88 – 93.38%) respectively. The PPV was 73.33% (95% CI 58.69 – 84.18%) and the NPV was 92.0% (95% CI 82.26 – 96.61%) . In conclusion, despite the setbacks we have been able to achieve the objectives .This novel case – control study evaluated a combination of a transoral brush biopsy and plasma detection of EBV DNA in identifying local failures in NPC. The results showed high specificities for both the transoral NP brush biopsy and plasma EBV DNA in detecting local failures in NPC. More importantly, a combination of both the transoral NP brush biopsy and plasma for the detection of EBV DNA showed an overall improved sensitivity and NPV in the detection of local failures in NPC.

14108818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108818.value: Objective To evaluate the sensitivities and specificities of EBV DNA in the detection of locally recurrent or persistent NPC through NP brush biopsy and plasma respectively, and whether a combination of both would be superior to the individual tests. Design A case-control study conducted from September 2016 to June 2022. Setting A multicentre study at tertiary referral centres was conducted by the department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head & Neck Surgery, the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Studied subjects were recruited from Prince of Wales Hospital, United Christian Hospital and Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Hong Kong SAR. Participants Twenty-seven patients with biopsy-confirmed locally recurrent NPC were recruited as studied subjects. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed to rule out regional recurrence. The control group consisted of 58 patients with a prior history of NPC who were now disease-free based on endoscopic and MRI findings. Intervention Patients underwent both the transoral NP brush (NP Screen®) and blood collection for plasma EBV DNA levels. Main Outcomes and Measures Transoral NP brush biopsy with the NP screen (NPC Screen, Markham, Ontario, Canada) was used. EBV DNA levels were reported as EBV Detection Level (EDL) from the study. Plasma EBV DNA was measured with real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and was reported as copies/ml. Sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV) and positive predictive value (PPV) were reported for the tests individually and in combination. Results The optimal EDLs were 1.98 (Area Under Curve [AUC] = 0.89) for NP brush and 9.0 (AUC = 0.79) for plasma EBV DNA respectively. The sensitivity and specificity of NP brush were 79.17% and 94.44% respectively, while the sensitivity and specificity of plasma EBV DNA were 59.26% and 91.38% respectively. When the above EDLs were implemented with a combination of the NP brush and plasma EBV DNA, the sensitivity and specificity in combination were 84.6% and 85.2% respectively, with PPV of 73.3% and NPV of 92.0%. Conclusions The high sensitivity of NP brush biopsy and high specificity of EBV DNA in detecting locally recurrent NPC may provide additional surveillance modalities besides current practice when used in combination. Further study with a larger sample size would be required to validate the cut-off values.

14108818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108818.value: The research indicates that the combination of a transoral brush and plasma for EBV DNA are useful in detecting local failures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This offers further potential for development in the aspects of timing of these tests for disease surveillance of patients as part of their survivorship. This will also potentially mitigate the need for regular imaging such as MRI/PET, reducing the cost of providing safe care to patients and relieving the burden of imaging needs on the public hospital system. Furthermore with refinements in circulating tumor DNA also need to be evaluated if the updated technologies can further improve disease surveillance. To do this the proposed course of action would be to seek funding support to pursue a prospective cohort study of patients following completion of treatment of primary nasopharyngeal carcinoma with defined time points of performing the transoral brush and plasma EBV DNA followed by imaging and endoscopy as needed for disease surveillance.

14108818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108818.value: This study sought to evaluate the use of a brush that could reach the nasopharynx and a blood test that would both look for raised levels of the Epstein Barr Virus that would suggest the presence of a recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma, with a focus on only patients who have a recurrence at the original site in the nasopharynx. This study showed that individually the tests were reasonable in identifying patients with a recurrence of the disease and very good at identifying patients who did not have disease recurrence. More importantly, a combination of the brush and blood test significantly improved the tests at picking up patients who had a recurrence of the disease at the original site in the nasopharynx

14109218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109218.value: 慢性肝病是全世界重主要的公共衛生問題。 肝纖維化是 慢性肝病早期階段的一個關鍵特徵。 臨床上患者在發展成為肝硬化前可以無症狀或只有輕微的非特異性症狀。因此檢出患有肝纖維化的患者以在相對早期階段控制疾病進展非常重要。 至今肝活檢仍然是肝纖維化診斷和分期的參考標準。然而肝活檢是一種侵入性手術，受制於抽樣誤差，判斷也有其固有的主觀性。 超聲彈性成像目前在臨床上使用，但它適用於早期肝纖維化（S1）的表現不是很好。為了更好地處理有進展性纖維化的患者，特別是那些可能從早期干預中受益的患者，一種無創、可重複的、而且可靠的肝纖維化診斷方法非常重要。 自2011年我們的初始論文（Radiology 2011; 259:712）發表以來，作為有希望用於 瀰漫性肝病的早期檢測和分級的MR技術 ，T1rho引起了很多關注。 最近我們開發了黑血單次憋氣快速自旋回波（BB / Fast）T1rho技術， 以克服與呼吸運動相關及血管高信號的T1rho測量欠精確的問題。這個方法可以滿意地抑制血液信號，並可以在單次憋氣時間內採集多個自旋鎖定時間 (spinlock time) 圖像。 這種方法為患者更廣泛的接受肝T1rho MRI 鋪平了道路。 對比以前的技術，BB / Fast T1rho技術在我們的健康志願者中呈現了更高的測量準確性測和可重複性。 由於近年來該領域的進展，MRI生產商 Philips Healthcare表達了希望進行更多臨床試驗，如果結果良好，他們就 將肝T1rho開發為臨床產品。 但是，目前 肝T1rho的磁共振對比機制尚不完全清楚。 我們在本研究中的目的是通過一系列動物模型的研究以回答一下問題：調查1）什麼導致了 大鼠肝T1rho的個體間差異？2）雖然解剖組織學表現為肝硬化但是功能正常的肝臟的 T1rho值會是怎麼樣？3）卵巢切除術（OVX）能否影響大鼠肝臟T1rho？4） 在生理性衰老過程中，肝臟T1rho會改變嗎？ 5）BB / Fast T1rho技術 診斷大鼠肝臟脂肪變性/肝臟脂肪性肝炎模型的診斷性能如何？ 目前T1rho序列尚是實驗序列。 我們的目標是 開發這個序列為臨床應用。在應用於患者之前，這裡提出的實驗研究將會幫助進一步了解早期肝纖維化的T1rho對比機制。

14109218.label: Realisation of objectives
14109218.value: In an animal model, we demonstrate that our blood suppressed T1rho imaging can completely separate livers with fibrosis and livers without fibrosis. We conclusively demonstrated that collagen in the liver will lead to T2rho elongation. Functionally normal while anatomically cirrhotic liver is associated with increased T1rho due to its higher collagen content in the liver. Iron, in the range of physiological concentration, does not affect T2rho measurement in the liver. Menopause, and its directly related liver iron increase, does not affect liver T1ho in a major way (does not affect liver T1rho’s diagnostic application). For mechanisms probably we do not fully understand yet, aging is associated with T1rho reduction for women, but less so for men. Inter-subject variation of liver T1trho is notable, and it appears that this point does not affect its application as a sensitive diagnostic tool, at least in the experimental settings.

14109218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109218.value: We have satisfactorily completed this project, and published 14 journal articles (there is one more article related to this project remaining to be published). In an animal model, we demonstrate that our blood-suppressed T1rho imaging can completely separate livers with fibrosis and livers without fibrosis. We conclusively demonstrated that collagen in the liver will lead to T2rho elongation. We also proved that fat in the liver contributes to T2rho time shortening. On the other hand, it appears that Iron, in the range of physiological concentration, does not affect T2rho measurement in the liver. We demonstrated that age and gender have a significant impact on normal liver values.

14109218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109218.value: Our results continue to suggest that MRI T1rho has been shown to be very promising as a non-invasive technique for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis. We conclusively demonstrated that collagen in the liver will lead to T2rho elongation. Iron, in the range of physiological concentration, does not affect T2rho measurement in the liver. However, we noted that fat in the liver contributes to T2rho time shortening. This should be taken into account when interpreting T1rho result from patients with liver steatosis. In fact, we proposed a method to first measure fat concentration in the liver, and then use this information to correct T1rho value. Regarding the age-related differences in T1rho for healthy livers, we recommend that we need to sample large normal livers’ value from different age groups.

14109218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109218.value: Liver fibrosis is a major disease associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Early detection and diagnosis are very important. However, a definite diagnosis currently requires an invasive biopsy. A non-invasive diagnosis technique is highly desirable. MRI T1rho has been shown to be very promising as a non-invasive technique for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis. However, till now how the confounders of T1rho measurement remain to be clarified. Our study elucidated a number of important factors concerning liver T1rho quantification. We conclusively demonstrated that collagen in the liver will lead to T2rho elongation. We also proved that fat in the liver contributes to T2rho time shortening. Iron, in the range of physiological concentration, does not affect T2rho measurement in the liver. We demonstrated that age and gender have a significant impact on normal liver values. In an animal model, we demonstrated that our blood-suppressed T1rho imaging can completely separate livers with early stage fibrosis and livers without fibrosis. Our findings pave the way for further clinical translation of T1rho for liver fibrosis early diagnosis.

14109618.value: We compared the mRNA expression level of BMP4 and BMPER in the mouse aortas with and without intact endothelium. Our results revealed that endothelial cells removal significantly reduced the mRNA level of BMP4 and BMPER in the aortas, indicating that BMP4 and BMPER are mainly expressed in vascular endothelium of the artery, suggesting a significant role of BMP signaling in endothelial homeostasis. The SMAD signaling pathway is activated by oscillatory shear stress while suppressed by laminar shear stress. The YAP/TAZ and SMAD pathways share a similar regulatory pattern by shear forces, implying the two pathways are associated. SMAD1 knockdown suppressed the expression of the YAP/TAZ target genes, implying that the SMAD pathway reversely affects the YAP/TAZ activity, thus suggesting that a feedback loop might exist in the YAP/TAZ-SMAD signaling cascade. The present study shows that the BMP-SMAD pathway plays an important role in endothelium homeostasis. Shear forces have similar regulatory patterns on the activity of the SMAD pathway and YAP/TAZ implying cross-talking might present in these two pathways. Indeed, gene knockdown of SMAD1 reduced the expression of YAP/TAZ target genes. Indicating the SMAD pathway can reversely regulate YAP/TAZ activity. 14109618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109618.value: Vascular endothelial cells lining the lumen of blood vessels are directly exposed to such high level of blood glucose, triggering dysfunction of endothelial cells, a key initial harmful event that ultimately causes formation of atherosclerotic plagues and thrombosis often leading to fatal cardiovascular complications. We previously demonstrated that increased activity of a pro-inflammatory bone morphogenetic proteins 4 (Bmp4)-Smad signaling pathway is closely associated with vascular dysfunction. However, how metabolic disorder activates Bmp4-Smad pathway is still unclear. The Hippo pathway is a highly conserved kinase cascade, which has been identified as the central regulator of multiple pathways. Being a newly found signaling regulator, investigation into both physiological and pathological roles of the Hippo pathway in the cardiovascular system has just started. We were the first to reveal that inhibition of Hippo pathway plays an important role in atherogenesis in athero-prone mice through promoting endothelial cell inflammation, implying that the Hippo signaling is likely to involve metabolic control of vascular function. We have established a drug screening platform aiming to identify drugs with potent inhibitory effects on the BMP/Smad signaling axis and activators of the Hippo pathway in human endothelial cells. We have identified several drugs which are being further investigated.

14110418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110418.value: Associative learning, the ability to link two otherwise unrelated events, is one of the most intensely studied learning behaviors. In higher order animals, attempts to decipher the mechanism underlying this capability is hampered by the rather complicated organization and connectivities of the brain. The fruit fly Drosophila is an ideal model organism for investigation because of its much simpler brain while population-level encoding of neural information comparable to that of the mammalian brain is retained, allowing investigators to gain important insight into the neuronal architecture and logic for associative learning. Previous attempts have identified the mushroom body of Drosophila as a key integrating center for aversive olfactory memory formation. However, most studies have focused on understanding the neural organization and neuroplasticity mechanism occurring at the output structure, namely the axons, of the mushroom body neurons, and especially the role of dopamine D1 receptor. As a result, there are still major gaps in our understanding of the neural circuitry and its operational principles underlying aversive olfactory memory formation in this organism. Based on a number of findings in our preliminary studies, we hypothesized that important neuroplasticity processes occur at the cell body and dendrites of mushroom body neurons to facilitate associative learning. Also, dopaminergic input mediated by D2 receptors from yet to be identified area could serve as an essential reinforcing signal. Here, we propose a comprehensive series of experiments to dissect in details the expressions, actions, and roles of D2 receptor on the mushroom body in particular with respect to its neuronal subtypes that are known to participate in different phases of memory formation. By exploiting the transgenic lines available, we will apply electrophysiological, behavioral and neuronal circuit tracing techniques to answer some key questions. We will establish the roles of D2 receptors on different mushroom body subtypes in short-term and long-term aversive memory formation. We will also identify the source of dopaminergic input that serves as the potential reinforcing signal in the process of memory formation. Finally, we will examine the functions of D2 receptor in modulating long-term synaptic plasticity in the mushroom body critical for associative learning. Learning and memory are cornerstones of animal behavior, forming the basis of the ability of the nervous system to respond to changes in the environment and in part, define almost all forms of exhibited behavior. Our results would further our understanding of the working mechanisms of associative memory exhibited by most animals. 聯想學習是將兩個不相關的事件聯繫起來的能力，是研究最深入的學習行為之一。在高階動物中，試圖破譯這種能力背後的機制受到大腦相當複雜的組織和連接性的阻礙。果蠅是一種理想的模型生物，因為它更簡單的大腦，同時保留了與哺乳動物大腦相當的神經信息的群體級編碼，使研究人員能夠獲得關於神經元結構和關聯學習邏輯的重要見解。 。 以前的嘗試已經確定果蠅的蘑菇體是厭惡嗅覺記憶形成的關鍵整合中心。然而，大多數研究都集中在理解在輸出結構上發生的神經組織和神經可塑性機制，即蘑菇體神經元的軸突，尤其是多巴胺D1受體的作用。因此，我們對神經迴路及其在該生物體中厭惡嗅覺記憶形成的操作原理的理解仍存在重大差距。根據我們初步研究中的一些研究結果，我們假設重要的神經可塑性過程發生在細胞體和蘑菇體神經元的樹突上，以促進聯想學習。此外，由待識別區域的D2受體介導的多巴胺能輸入可以作為必要的增強信號。 在這裡，我們提出了一系列全面的實驗來詳細剖析D2受體在蘑菇體上的表達，作用和作用，特別是關於其已知參與記憶形成的不同階段的神經元亞型。通過利用可用的轉基因品系，我們將應用電生理學，行為學和神經元電路追踪技術來回答一些關鍵問題。我們將在不同的蘑菇體亞型中建立D2受體在短期和長期厭惡記憶形成中的作用。我們還將確定多巴胺能輸入的來源，其作為記憶形成過程中的潛在強化信號。最後，我們將研究D2受體在調節對關聯學習至關重要的蘑菇體中的長期突觸可塑性中的功能。 學習和記憶是動物行為的基石，是神經系統應對環境變化的能力的基礎，部分地定義了幾乎所有形式的展示行為。我們的結果將進一步了解大多數動物表現出的聯想記憶的工作機制。

14110418.label: Realisation of objectives
14110418.value: We have fully address and realise the objectives of the present proposal, and generated results are of significance and worthy of publication. (Objective 1: To investigate the roles of D2 receptors in different Kenyon cell subtypes in long-term aversive memory formation) We conducted a series of experiments to investigate the roles of D2-like receptors in different Kenyon cell subtypes in long-term aversive memory formation. Based on a conventional T-maze paradigm, we studied the effect of dopamine D2 receptor (DD2R) knockdown on aversive long-term memory formation of Drosophila. We observed that the shock response, motor abilities and sensitivity to the test odors, namely 3-octanol and 4-methylcyclohexanol, were normal in these different control and DD2R knockdown lines. When compared with the UAS-Dop2R-RNAi control and the respective GAL4 control, all the Dop2R-RNAi knockdown groups showed similar performance in short-term memory test. In contrast, flies with DD2R receptor suppressed in their γ neurons showed deficits in this ability while those with DD2R knocked down in either α’/β’neurons or α/β neurons could still establish normal long-term memory (LTM). These results confirmed that expression of DD2R receptors in γ neurons contribute critically to the formation of aversive long-term memory induced by the pairing of an odor with electric shock. Since the 1471 GAL4 driver is known to also label some neurons outside the mushroom body, we also employed another split-Gal4 driver based Dop2R-RNAi line, MB009>Dop2R-RNAi, which is more specific to γ neurons, to confirm the role of DD2R in these neurons. We found that while knockdown of DD2R did not affect the shock response, odor sensitivity (Figure S7B) and motor ability, formation of LTM was impaired, confirming the results of 1471 GAL4 driver experiments. Together, our results implicate a particular importance of γ neurons in receiving dopaminergic input that mediates aversive unconditioned signal via D2-like receptor. (Objective 2: To elucidate the source of dopaminergic input onto Kenyon cells and their connectivity) It has been reported that three dopamine clusters, namely protocerebral anterior medial (PAM), paired posterior lateral 1 (PPL1) and paired posterior lateral 2ab (PPL2ab), terminate in the mushroom body (MB). We employed the Drosophila brain preparation from a genotype that combined 1471-GAL4, TH-GAL4 and UAS-GFP by double balancer, labelling both dopamine neurons and γ neurons. Electrophysiological characterization of PPL1 neurons was conducted showing that these neurons are spontaneously active. Intriguingly, electrical stimulation targeting fluorescent neuronal cluster at PPL1 evoked synaptic potentials in γ neurons that were sensitive to TTX and the D2 receptor antagonist sulpiride, with a reversal potential at 0 to 20mV suggesting the involvement of non-selective cation channels. Successive stimulation of the PPL1 cluster could lead to superimposition of the DD2R-mediated synaptic potentials, significantly depolarizing the γ neurons. These results suggested an excitatory projection from PPL1 to MB γ neurons, directly or indirectly. (Objective 3 - To elucidate the actions and mechanisms of D2 receptors in modulating long-term synaptic plasticity) To address this question, we conducted several sets of experiments. First, we adopted an electrophysiological approach that allowed us to directly gauge synaptic events of MB neurons. We first generated flies with mGFP expressed in distinct Kenyon cell subtypes by crossing males with different GAL4 drivers to UAS-mCD8::GFP females. In the dissected brains in which specific Kenyon cell subtypes could be identified by fluorescence, we were able to record EPSPs originating from the projection neurons. Importantly, we found that by pairing this stimulation with subsequent postsynaptic depolarization of Kenyon cells at an interval of 65-80ms for 25 times, we were able to induce long-lasting potentiation of the EPSPs by more than 150%, which typically lasted for more than 60 mins. This phenomenon was found in γ neurons only. We further confirmed the requirement of the plasticity on associated pre- and post-synaptic activities. We then applied an RNAi strategy to test the effect of DD1R and DD2R knockdown on the synaptic plasticity that we observed. By crossing fly lines with GAL4 driver for γ neurons to a line with UAS-dopamine DD1R (DopR1) RNAi or UAS-dopamine DD2R (Dop2R) RNAi, the expression of DD1R or DD2R in the γ subpopulation was suppressed. We found that while DD1R knockdown had no effect on the input-timing dependent potentiation of EPSPs originated from projection neurons, DD2R knockdown completely abolished this plasticity. These results confirmed a critical role of dopamine in activating DD2R underlying the plasticity. Finally, we confirmed confocal imaging experiments to demonstrate that voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCC) may contribute to DD2R-mediated long-term synaptic plasticity and aversive olfactory memory formation. In VGCC knockdown flies, DD2R activation failed to evoke calcium response in γ neurons, input-timing dependent plasticity and LTM formation.

14110418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110418.value: In the drosophila model, by electrophysiological recordings from mushroom body (MB) neurons, we discovered a form of input-timing dependent plasticity at the incoming synapses from projection neurons in the antennal lobe that controls the efficacy of aversive olfactory memory formation. Importantly, this plasticity is facilitated by activity of a group of dopaminergic neurons called PPL1, the neuronal cluster that also modulates mushroom body-mushroom body output neurons (MB-MBON) connections at the output stage of the mushroom body. Unlike the MB-MBON synapses that probably utilize dopamine D1-like receptors, this neuroplasticity is dependent on D2-like receptors that are expressed mainly by γ Kenyon cells and confined to their somato-dendritic region. The D2-like receptors recruit voltage-gated calcium channels, leading to calcium influx in the soma and dendrites of γ neurons. Together, our results reveal a previously unrecognized synaptic component of the MB circuit architecture that not only could increase the salience of a conditioning odor but also couples the process of memory encoding and valency mapping to drive associative learning. Our findings promote a better understanding of how the central nervous system integrates efficiently the tasks of processing the values of sensory stimuli to guide behavior and storing the association.

14110418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110418.value: Our results established that the fruit fly is a highly useful model for studying the mechanism of memory formation. Future works could further utilise this model to investigate other fundamental neuroscience questions.

14110418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110418.value: Associative learning is the basis of more complex forms of learning and also behaviours. Among the different popular model organisms, the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster is a favourite model in the pursuit of the working principles of associative memory formation. Recent studies provide evidence that the circuit for olfactory associative memory formation in Drosophila is more complex than previously thought, and involves not only D1-like but also D2-like receptors and in locations other than the output site of the mushroom body, the key structure of memory formation in Drosophila. The results of our study strongly indicate that the representations of the conditioning odour at the upstream input synapses of the mushroom body is another key component in addition to signals valency remapping. This represents a previously unrecognised circuit component of the complex mushroom body architecture that helps to drive olfactory learning, further enriching our understanding of mechanism of associative learning. Our findings thus promote a better understanding of how the central nervous system integrates efficiently the tasks of processing the values of sensory stimuli to guide behaviour and storing the association.

14110918.label: Realisation of objectives
14110918.value: We have accomplished the four research objectives as originally proposed in this project. Our major findings as realized in this study are summarized as follows: 1. Objective 1: As planned in this study objective, we employed three different methods based on the unique features of cancer stem-like cells (including anchorage-independent growth, expressions of specific membrane markers and stem cells-specific transcription factors) to isolate prostate cancer stem cells (PCSCs) from various sources: including prostate cancer cell lines, tumor xenografts and also primary cultures of human prostate cancer tissues. Methods include our newly established agar agar-based non-adherent 3D-culture method (Gao et al., Stem Cell Res Ther 2018;9:243), CD133-based MACS/FACS and also a reporter gene-based FACS sorting (SORE6-reporter driven by the transactivation of stem cell-specific transcription factors SOX2 and OCT4). Our results confirmed that the isolated PCSCs, derived from various sources and isolated by different methods, consistently exhibited increased expressions of TLX and also three master stem cell-associated transcription factors (SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG). Based on these expression patterns, we then generated prostate cancer cells with either stable TLX-overexpression or its knockdown/knockout for further growth characterization studies. In vitro phenotype growth analyses showed that TLX could play roles in the promotion of clonogenicity, stemness and migration/invasion capacity in prostate cancer cells. Expression analyses on the generated prostate cancer infectants with either TLX-overexpression or its knockdown/knockout validated that TLX could function to up-regulate the expressions of both cancer stem cells (CSCs) and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) -associated markers at both mRNA and protein levels, suggesting that TLX could play roles in these processes. 2. Objective 2: As planned in this study objective, we have determined the oncogenic roles of TLX on the in vivo tumor growth of generated prostate cancer cells with either TLX-overexpression or its knockout. Results of in vivo tumorigenicity and metastasis analyses showed that prostate cancer cells with TLX-overexpression formed significant larger tumors whereas prostate cancer cells with TLX-knockout formed significant smaller tumors and also abrogated their distal metastasis to lungs in the host mice, suggesting that TLX could perform roles in promotion of tumorigenicity and metastasis in prostate cancer. In summary, results as obtained from Objectives 1 and 2 show that TLX could play positive roles in the growth regulation of PCSCs (cancer stemness) and promotion of EMT and metastasis in prostate cancer. 3. Objective 3: As planned in this part of study, we have determined by molecular analyses whether some of the up-regulated PCSCs- and EMT-associated markers as induced by TLX would be its direct down-stream molecular targets in mediating both cancer stemness and EMT in prostate cancer cells regardless of their androgen receptor status. By promoter sequence analysis (including ChIP-seq) and reporter gene assays, we have characterized that TLX could transcriptionally up-regulate genes of CD44, SOX2, POU5F1 (OCT4) and NANOG in prostate cancer cells. On the other hand, we still need to further confirm whether TLX could also regulate the TGF-β/SMAD-dependent signaling pathway in prostate cancer cells. Results as shown in this part of study indicate that TLX could act as a key up-stream regulator to activate or enhance the cellular processes involved in both cancer stemness and EMT via its direct transcriptional control of gene networks involved in these processes. 4. Objective 4: In this study objective, besides the plans to evaluate the anti-tumor effects of knockdown of TLX in prostate cancer cells, it is also planned to determine whether the ligand-independent nuclear receptor TLX would be druggable in order to provide insight into the therapeutic potential of targeting TLX in prostate cancer. Results obtained so far by reporter gene assays showed that treatment with a TLX ligand (all-trans retinal) could further potentiate the transactivation of CD44-gene promoter activity while treatment with another TLX ligand (famprofazone or ccrp1) could moderately suppress the CD44-driven reporter activity, suggesting that the orphan nuclear receptor TLX is druggable. Together, results as obtained in Objectives 2 and 4 implicate a potential therapeutic value of targeting TLX as an adjuvant therapy or in combination with hormone-therapy for the management of advanced prostate cancer via its control of cancer stemness and EMT. However, it still needs to further evaluate its therapeutic potential by in vitro and in vivo growth analyses using different clinically relevant organoid models and tumor xenograft models and pharmacologic approach with the use of novel synthetic TLX inverse agonists or ligands.
