14110918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110918.value: Our major findings as derived from this GRF-funded study on the study of nuclear receptor TLX in prostate cancer are summarized as follows: 1. TLX (NR2E1) is a ligand-independent orphan nuclear receptor, with previously characterized roles in regulation and maintenance of embryonic and adult neural stem cells via its transcriptional control of gene signals involved in multiple cell processes and is also implicated in oncogenesis. In prostate cancer, we have previously shown that TLX can play roles in prostate carcinogenesis by overcoming the oncogene-induced cellular senescence via its differential regulation of CDKN1A and SIRT1 genes and also induction of androgen insensitivity in CRPC by direct repression of androgen receptor (AR) gene transcription via an epigenetic mechanism (results reviewed recently in Wang et al., Mol Asp Med 2021;78:100921; Zhou et al., Oncogene 2021:40:2625-2634). In this study, we continued to characterize the specific roles of TLX in the regulation of cancer stemness and EMT in prostate cancer. Our results showed that the isolated PCSCs, with their enhanced 3D-spheroid formation capacity (stemness) and in vivo tumorigenicity, exhibited significant increased expressions of TLX and also three master stem cell-associated transcription factors (SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG). Expression correlation analysis also revealed that up-regulation of TLX was significantly associated with increased expressions of multiple CSCs- and EMT-associated markers in isolated PCSCs, further suggesting that TLX plays regulatory roles in both cancer stemness and EMT. 2. Results of in vitro growth analyses demonstrated that TLX could support clonogenicity, cancer stemnesss and migration or invasion capacities in prostate cancer cells. In vivo tumorigenicity studies confirmed that TLX could promote both the tumor growth and metastasis potential in prostate cancer cells. Together, these results suggest that TLX could function to promote both cancer stemness and EMT in prostate cancer cells. 3. Molecular analyses characterized the signaling as mediated by TLX that TLX could act as the up-stream transcriptional regulator of CD44, SOX2, POU5F1 (OCT4) and NANOG so as to mediate or enhance the cellular processes of cancer stemness and EMT in prostate cancer. 4. Furthermore, reporter gene analysis showed that the CD44-driven reporter activity could be potentiated by two synthetic TLX ligands (all-trans retinal and famprofazone), implicating that TLX activity could be targeted by small molecules in prostate cancer cells and also its potential value as a therapeutic target in the suppression or eradication of PCSCs and management of prostate cancer. 5. These major findings have been submitted for publication.

14110918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110918.value: 1. In this GRF-supported study, we have elucidated the oncogenic roles of nuclear receptor TLX in the advanced growth regulation of prostate cancer, particularly therapy-resistance and metastasis, via its promotion of PCSC growth and EMT process by its direct transcriptional control of multiple target genes involved in these two processes. Our findings also provide an insight into the transcriptional control as mediated by TLX in linking both the maintenance of PCSCs and EMT in prostate cancer. 2. Besides, we also demonstrated that transcriptional activity of TLX could be modulated by small molecules in prostate cancer cells, implicating that TLX could be druggable. However, there is still a need to develop potent TLX antagonists that can suppress its dysregulated activity in diseases including cancers. Recent study shows that oleic acid, rich in olive oil and other edible oils, can act to activate TLX in neural stem cells and can promote neurogenesis in mice. However, this raises a concern that whether increased dietary consumption of oleic acid-rich edible oils will impose any negative impact on the risk of prostate cancer or its enhanced growth, at least the potential TLX activation in PCSCs. These areas of research are of value to further explore.

14110918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110918.value: Prostate cancer is a leading male-specific cancer in many countries and regions, including Hong Kong. This cancer is unique in its hormone-dependence. Surgery and hormone-therapy are the current mainstay treatment options. Unfortunately, most patients under hormone-therapy will inevitably advance to a metastatic therapy-resistant stage (metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer/mCRPC), which remains the major cause of death. Recent studies indicate that prostate cancer stem cells (PCSCs) being unique in their enhanced self-renewal and tumor growth capacities, and also an embryonic process epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) play important roles in the progression of mCRPC. Hormone-therapy can induce EMT that in turn can promote the PCSC growth, through the synergic interactions between two processes, leading to therapy resistance and metastasis of prostate cancer. However, the molecular pathways and signals linking between such two processes are still unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that nuclear receptor TLX can act as an upstream regulator in the control of both PCSCs and EMT through its direct transcriptional regulation of gene networks involved in these two processes. Moreover, we also show that TLX activity could be modulated by small molecules, implicating that TLX is druggable and its pharmacologic targeting could be a potential adjuvant therapy for mCRPC.

14111318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111318.value: Post ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) occurs in 4 to 5% of patients and is associated with significant morbidities and occasional mortalities. The use of rectally administered indomethacin and pancreatic duct stent (PDS) placement have independently been proven to reduce PEP. The comparative effectiveness of the two methods has however not been studied. It is argued that in the context of indomethacin, the placement of a PDS is unnecessary. Advocates for PDS insertion however believe that mechanical decompression of the pancreatic duct is critical in the prevention of pancreatitis. We propose a multi-centre randomised controlled trial to compare the use of rectal indomethacin to PDS insertion in high risk patients in the prevention of PEP. 經內鏡逆行胰膽管造影（ERCP）術後胰腺炎發生率為4%-5% 並且會導致嚴重的病患 甚至死亡。 研究證明吲哚美辛塞肛和胰腺導管內支架（PDS）置入這兩種方法 對減少ERCP術後胰腺炎都有效。 但尚未有研究比較上述兩種方法哪一種更有效。 對於是否需要在應用吲哚美辛塞肛后再置入PDS存在爭議。 PDS置入的提倡者認為機械性的解壓胰腺導管是 預防胰腺炎的關鍵。因此我們提議做一個多中心的隨機對照 研究比較在高危病人中應用吲哚美辛塞肛與PDS置入預防術後 胰腺炎的效果。

14111318.label: Realisation of objectives
14111318.value: We started the randomized controlled trial in 2019. To date, a total of 552 have been enrolled in the study. Our trial commencement coincided with the onslaught of COVID. Because of the persistent COVID situation, many centers could not recruit patients, and there were periods when enrollment was stopped in many centers. The only centers with active participation have been Xijing hospital, Xian, Prince of Wales Hospital Hong Kong, and King Chulalongkorn University Hospital in Thailand. We have conducted an unplanned analysis based on the 552 patients. 1. The overall incidence of post-ERCP pancreatitis was 9.4% (52 out of 552), and the incidences in the three groups were comparable. 9.3% (17 of 183) in the rectal indomethacin alone group, 9,7% (18 of 185) in the pancreatic stent group (PDS), and 9.2% (17 of 184) in the combined indomethacin and PDS group. 2. The failure rate in the insertion of PDS was 21.1% in the PDS alone group and 19% in the combined treatment group. 3. An exploratory analysis suggests that >5 cannulation attempts and double wire technique were predictors of PEP. 4. The 3 strategies appear comparable in the prevention of PEP. A planned analysis will be conducted when we reach n=600 (1/3 of the planned total enrolment).

14111318.value: The primary endpoint i.e. post ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) was seen in 17 (9.3%),18 (9.7%) and 17 (9.2%) patients in the indomethacin alone group, pancreatic duct stent (PDS) and the combined indomethacin and PDS group. 14111318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111318.value: The risk of ERCP-related pancreatitis is high in patients after difficult bile duct access (multiple attempts and inadvertent pancreatic duct cannulation or contrast injection). The optimal strategy has not been defined. Many endoscopists would administer rectal indomethacin after ERCP. Some would insert a pancreatic duct and others would combine both strategies. Our preliminary findings indicate that outcomes i.e. PEP are similar with all 3 strategies. Rectal indomethacin after ERCP is likely to be the best strategy for its simplicity. Insertion of PDS will require a follow-up endoscopy for removal of the stent.

14111918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111918.value: 肉質果實成熟是開花植物特有的發育過程，其中種子器官的化學和生理特性被顯著改變，以吸引作為種子分散器的食果動物。由於它們現在是人類和動物飲食的重要組成部分，因此了解果實成熟對於全球糧食安全越來越重要。通過對番茄的研究，已經獲得了對肉質果實成熟的深刻見解。由於許多肉質水果基因組現已被測序，因此對番茄模型本身以及它是否具有普遍性提出了疑問。番茄轉錄因子在控制果實成熟中起著不可或缺的作用。我們從桃，甜瓜，擬南芥和水稻的初步數據顯示，它們的直接直系同源物參與成熟，葉子衰老或花器官發育。有趣的是，我們發現這些基因都與組織特異性H3K27me3標記有關。由於肉質果實成熟在多個被子植物譜系中獨立進化，這可能表明番茄中利用的基因和表觀遺傳標記可能起源於控制葉和花組織發育中的基因表達的現有機制，尤其是衰老。為了測試這一點，我們建議：1）鑑定和克隆上述番茄成熟調節劑在其他植物物種中的直接直向同源物。 2）在衰老過程中檢查它們的表達和表觀基因組的變化。 3）通過ChIP-Seq比較它們的下游目標。 4）通過Crispr / Cas9敲除或使用現有的突變體和變種研究它們的生物學功能。

14111918.label: Realisation of objectives
14111918.value: In short, we have successfully achieved the main objectives of this GRF proposal. Our TF ChIP-seq story have been published in Nature Communications (Tu et al 2020). The key findings from this project are: 1) TF binding is strongly influenced by the genome cis-regulatory elements (cistrome). Most of the TF binding sites are not conserved among species. 2) The conserved TF binding sites often carried more regulatory potential based on the analysis of TF target gene expression in TF knockout mutant. 3) Cross-species comparison could help to identify “important” TF target genes only if the function of the TF is conserved. Newly evolved function would be missed. Objective 1 and 2: Identify and clone the direct orthologs of the tomato ripening regulators in other plant species & Examine their gene expression and epigenome change during senescence. We first generated transcription factor (TF) gene expression data during fruit development for 11 fleshy fruit species using RNA-seq. Since there are always a large number of differentially expressed genes, we selected those that are associated with epigenome changes such as promoter DNA methylation change, promoter chromatin accessibility change and gene body H3K27me3 change for further analysis. The rationale behind this is that plants, as well as animals, often control the expression of those key regulators using epigenome to prevent them from mis-expression in the wrong tissues or developmental stages. We choose two fruit species, apple and tomato, for comparison. We selected the top 20 apple TF genes and 50 tomato TF genes based on the gene expression and epigenome data for cloning. Because apple transformation would take years, we expressed their TFs in e coli for protein purification and raised antibody for ChIP-seq. The tomato ones are cloned into binary vector with C-terminal GFP tag, and transformed into tomato to generate stable transgenic lines for ChIP-seq. We also developed transient expression system to expressed TF fused to either biotin tag in maize protoplast and HA tag in tobacco (N benthamiana) leaf for ChIP-seq. Objective 3 and 4: Compare their downstream targets by ChIP-Seq. & Examine their biological function by Crispr/Cas9 knockout or using existing mutants and varieties. We have generated a large collection of TF ChIP-seq data in each species. For example, 6 apple TFs’ ChIP-seq passed the ENCODE2 QC, including MADS7 and NAC5 that are highly expressed in the ripen fruit tissues. In another fleshy fruit tomato, we have ChIP-seq data for their orthologous genes such as MADS-RIN and NAC-NOR. For non-fleshy fruit species, we have generated over 100 maize TF ChIP-seq using protoplast and over 50 tobacco TF ChIP-seq using leaf agro-infiltration. To identify homologous genes in these species, we used Orthofinder to generate ortholog groups for all protein coding genes in these species. This enabled us to examine how many TF target genes are conserved in different plants. For example, we compared GLK TF binding in five species and found that around 15% of the target genes are conserved. To test the role of these TF genes in fruit development, we also generated Crisper/Cas9 mutant lines for tomato TF genes such as MADS-RIN, NAC-NOR and CNR. Some of the result has been published in horticulture research. We also transformed TF genes from different plants species into their Arabidopsis ortholog’s t-DNA or Crisper/cas9 mutant, which enabled us to test whether they have similar biological function. For example, when we transformed an HA-tagged maize TF into the Arabidopsis mutant, we found that although it can complement the mutant phenotype, its binding pattern changed in the heterologous genome environment. This suggest that TF binding is largely determined in cis by DNA sequence variation rather than in trans, and we have published this finding last year in nature communication.

14111918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111918.value: We have used ChIP-seq to analyze tomato TF (RIN/NOR/CNR) binding site genome-wide, We found that they bind to the promoter of key ripening gene. We also found that TF EIL3, which is controlled by the plant hormone ethylene, can bind to the promoter of MADS-RIN. This forms a positive feedback loop to amplify the ethylene and ripening signal. We also generated Crisper/Cas9 mutant lines and examined their phenotypes. Several ChIP-seq and mutant analysis have been published in Nature Plant and Horticulture Research. We also performed a large-scale TF ChIP-seq using maize, which has been published in Nature Communications. The genome-wide cross-species analysis of the maize and tomato TF is in progress, while the cross-species comparison of two individual TFs have been completed, and published last year also in Nature Communications.

14111918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111918.value: 1) With a large collection of TF ChIP-seq data, we are performing cross-species cis-regulatory element (cistrome) comparison. This analysis will enable us to assign the ancestral function for all TFs in different species. 2) Because ChIP-seq data is still difficult to generate, we are trying to use ATAC-seq and DAP-seq data coupled with deep learning to predict TF binding and cis-regulatory elements without ChIP-seq data.

14111918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111918.value: Our study show that genome cis-variation caused wide-spread TF binding divergence, and most of the TF binding sites are genetically redundant. This poses a new challenge for interpreting the effect of individual sites and highlights the importance of quantitatively measuring TF occupancy. Many plant TF studies, particularly those in crops that are hard to transform, have often inferred gene function based on mutant complementation or over-expression in a model plant like tomato and Arabidopsis. Our finding gives reason for caution in interpreting the result of such studies. If TF binding could be influenced by the genome cis-regulatory dynamics, one might have missed the novel function of a TF when expressed in a foreign genome. For example, ETHYLENE INSENSITIVE3 class TFs are key regulators of the conserved ethylene signaling pathway40.

14112618.value: 我們的研究目標是闡明Zinc finger SWIM-type containing 4（Zswim4）通過調節Bone Morphogenetic Protein (骨形態發生蛋白，BMP）信號通路傳導，來調控胚胎圖示形成的分子機制。胚胎圖示形成是指在早期胚胎髮育過程中，細胞受到在時間和空間協同作用的各種信號通路的調節，分化並形成高度有序個體的過程。 BMP信號通路是參與調控胚胎體軸形成˙重要的信號通路。已有研究表明，這一信號通路在調節外胚層，中胚層和內胚層的分化，維持成體組織的穩態平衡中發揮重要作用。我們通過使用Affymetrix DNA基因芯片篩選出Zswim4 在Spemann-Mangold組織者中差異表達。此外，整體原位雜交顯示Zswim4在神經胚的神經板中高度表達。進一步研究表明Chordin可以誘導Zswim4表達上調。過表達Zswim4能夠抑制BMP熒光素酶報告基因活性，並且降低Vent1和Sizzled兩個BMP靶基因的表達。然而Zswim4在胚胎圖示形成過程中調節BMP信號傳導的機制尚未不清楚。在此項研究中，我們將研究Zswim4在胚胎髮育過程中的作用，並闡明其調控BMP信號通路中的分子機制。基於我們的前期工作，我們提出以下假說： Zswim4通過抑制BMP-Smad1 / 5/8信號通路來調節胚胎圖示形成。我們將通過三個方面的工作來驗證我們的假說：1）利用基因敲低或敲除手段來研究Zswim4在胚胎圖示形成中的作用; 2）闡明Zswim4調節BMP信號通路中的分子機制; 3）使用RNAseq鑒定Zswim4靶基因。通過以上研究，我們將明晰Zswim4在胚胎圖示形成中的作用，更加深入地了解胚胎模式中的調控網絡，闡明Zswim4調節BMP信號的分子機制。

14112618.label: Realisation of objectives
14112618.value: Zswim4 is expressed in Spemann Mangold organizer (SMO) with nuclear localization. Zswim4 is a maternal factor with high expression levels at the cleavage stage. At the onset of gastrulation, intensive zswim4 signals appeared in the dorsal blastopore lip, the SMO, and Its expression was detected in the anterior edge of the neural plate at neural stages. The temporal expression pattern revealed by quantitative RT-PCR showed that zswim4 is highly expressed and maintained at a constant level before gastrulation. Immunostaining showed that ZSWIM4 is predominantly localized in the nucleus. The overexpression of either bmp4, fgf8, or wnt3a suppressed the expression of zswim4. The zswim4 expression is increased upon overexpression of chordin in animal cap assay. Dysregulation of zswim4 disturbs anterioposterior axis formation. Overexpression of zswim4 mRNA can cause an apparent disturbance of body axis formation in embryos when examined at the tailbud stages. These embryos showed a phenotype characterized by a shortened, and bent body axis with tails curved to the dorsal side. Severely affected embryos showed strong inhibition of head formation. We designed two antisense morpholino (MO) oligonucleotides (zswim4MO1 and zswim4MO2) to knock down zswim4 in X. tropicalis embryos. The injection of zswim4MO1 or zswim4MO2 caused a similar phenotype of the anterior axis inhibition and shortened body axis in embryos at stage 28 with varying severities. Embryos in the moderate group just showed only a shortened body axis, while those in severe group showed a ventralization phenotype with an extremely short body axis and the loss of head structures. The phenotype caused by zswim4MOs can be partially rescued by co-injection of Zswim4 mRNA, indicating the phenotype is specific. We designed four sgRNAs targeting zswim4 (sgRNA1-4) and co-injected them with Cas9 protein into X. tropicalis embryos. CRISPR/Cas9 disruption of zswim4 caused a short tail and trunk, as well as loss of head structures, including eyes and brain. This phenotype was highly similar to the phenotype induced by the MOs. Taken together, these results indicate the critical roles of Zswim4 in body axis formation and head development. Zswim4 restricts the ventrolateral mesoderm and promotes neural formation by inhibiting BMP signaling. Overexpression of zswim4 severely inhibited the expression of sizzled and vent1 in X. laevis embryos. The expression of neural ectoderm marker genes, otx2, and sox2, was both decreased after the knockdown of zswim4. Meanwhile, the ventral mesoderm marker genes, sizzled and vent1, were increased in zswim4 morphants in a dose-dependent manner. Collectively, these results indicate that Zswim4 is required to restrict the ventral mesoderm formation and promote neural fate in the early gastrula. We found that Zswim4 inhibits BMP signaling transduction. In animal cap assay, the expression levels of xhox3, xbra, and wnt8 induced by BMP4 were attenuated by the co-injection of a high dose of zswim4 mRNA, suggesting the suppression of BMP signaling by zswim4. Co-injection of zswim4MO1 with bmp4 mRNA, more injected embryos showed an increase of sizzled expression, compared to those by bmp4 mRNA alone. These results suggested that Zswim4 restricts ventral mesoderm formation by antagonizing BMP signaling. Overexpression of zswim4 in the whole embryo apparently reduced the level of p-Smad1 and total Smad1. Conversely, the knockdown of zswim4 caused a moderate increase in total Smad1 levels and an apparent elevation of p-Smad1 levels. These results indicated that Zswim4 inhibits BMP signaling activity in both whole embryos and animal caps. ZSWIM4 attenuates BMP signaling in the HEK293T cell line. We found that BMP4-induced luciferase activity was inhibited by transfected ZSWIM4 in a dose-dependent manner. Similarly, the expression of ID1 and ID2 induced by BMP treatment was also downregulated in ZSWIM4 transfected cells. Knockdown of ZSWIM4 promoted BMP4-induced luciferase activity, and the expression of ID1 and ID2. Moreover, we established ZSWIM4 mutant HEK293T cell lines using CRISPR/Cas9. Two ZSWIM4 mutant clones, Z7 (Δ25/Δ16) and Z9 (Δ2/+375), exhibited increased ID1 expression with or without BMP treatment compared with wild-type cells. Consistent with this observation, the levels of p-Smad1 and total Smad1 were upregulated in the two mutant cell lines. Collectively, these results indicate that the endogenous ZSWIM4 functions attenuate the BMP signaling in HEK293T cells. ZSWIM4 promotes the ubiquitination and degradation of SMAD1. To examine the regulatory level of ZSWIM4 in the BMP signaling hierarchy, we transfected HEK293T cells with either constitutively active BMP receptor, BMPR1A_CA, or constitutively phosphorylated SMAD1, SMAD1-DVD. Both of the components increased the BRE-luciferase activity, and this effect was blocked by overexpression of ZSWIM4. This result suggests that ZSWIM4 acts downstream of SMAD1 phosphorylation, and its function is independent of de-phosphorylation process of Smad1, or at least, does not entirely rely on SMAD1 de-phosphorylation. In Xenopus zswim4 morphants, the endogenous Smad1 protein was also upregulated compared with that in control embryos. Thus, Zswim4 decreases Smad1 protein levels in both Xenopus embryos and mammalian cells. The mRNA levels of smad1 were not affected by zswim4 overexpression in either Xenopus embryos or HEK293T cells. SMAD1 protein stability was measured following the treatment of HEK293T cells with cycloheximide (CHX) to inhibit protein synthesis. Indeed, the protein stability of SMAD1-FLAG was markedly reduced in the presence of ZSWIM4 compared with its stability in control cells. We conclude that ZSWIM4 regulates the protein stability of SMAD1. We also observed that SMAD1 ubiquitination was reduced in the ZSWIM4 mutant cell lines, Z7 or Z9. Taken together, these results indicate that Zswim4 attenuates BMP signaling by promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of SMAD1. ZSWIM4 forms a complex with SMAD1 and Elongin B/C-containing ubiquitin ligase. We found that the MH1 domain in SMAD1 is essential for its interaction with ZSWIM4 using Co-immunoprecipitation. To identify the possible interaction partners of Zswim4 in regulating SMAD1 stability, stable isotope labeling by amino acid in cell culture (SILAC)-IP was performed. After LC-MS/MS analysis of the immunoprecipitates, ELONGIN B (ELOB) and ELONGIN C (ELOC) were identified among the 10 most abundant proteins in forward and reverse SILAC. The interaction between Zswim4 and ELOB or ELOC was then confirmed by Co-IP in HEK293T cells The ELOB and ELOC have been identified to interact with Cullin and the RING domain protein Rbx to form Cullin-RING ligase (CRL) complex, which promotes the ubiquitination of its targets by binding to different substrate-recognition components. Indeed, we found that Zswim4 has a physical interaction with CUL2, the scaffold protein in the CRL complex. We further determined that the amino acids 1-99 are essential for binding to ELOB and ELOC using Co-IP. Taken together, these results indicate that ZSWIM4 forms a complex with CRL and SMAD1. ZSWIM4 functions in the CRL complex to regulate SMAD1 stability. To examine whether ZSWIM4 regulates SMAD1 protein degradation by cooperating with CRL, we co-expressed Zswim4 and the components of the CRL complex. Compared with the single transfection of ZSWIM4-Myc or cul2, co-transfection of both showed a stronger effect at reducing the stability of Myc-tagged SMAD1. Further co-transfection of ELOB and ELOC caused the highest degree of degradation of SMAD1-Myc. Consistent with these results, the ubiquitination assay of SMAD1-HA showed the strongest signals in the cells co-overexpressing Zswim4-FLAG, Cul2, ELOB, and ELOC. Taken together, these results indicate that ZSWIM4 and the CRL complex work synergistically to attenuate SMAD1 protein stability and BMP signaling.

14112618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112618.value: Zswim4 is expressed in the Spemann-Mangold organizer during gastrulation. During neurulation, Zswim4 is expressed in the anterior border of the neural plate and neural crest. Immunostaining revealed that the Zswim4 protein is localized in the nucleus. Dysregulation of Zswim4 disturbs anterioposterior axis formation and affects ventrolateral mesoderm and neural formation. Overexpression of Zswim4 attenuates, while knockdown and disruption of Zswim4 promotes BMP signaling in Xenopus embryos and HEK293T cells. We found that Zswim4 physically interacts with Smad1 and attenuates Smad1 stability. The MH1 domain of Smad1 is responsible for binding with Zswim4. Overexpression of Zswim4 enhances the ubiquitination of Smad1, while knockdown or disruption of Zswim4 attenuates the ubiquitination level of Smad1. We used stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture (SILAC) to identify interaction partners of Zswim4. Zswim4 can interact with Culin2, Elongin B (ELOB), and Elongin C (ELOC) to form a protein disruption complex that ubiquitinates Smad1, leading to its degradation. In addition to Zswim4, we identified nine ZSWIM genes in the humanand mouse genome, eight in the Xenopus genome, and five in the zebrafish genome. We examined the temporal and spatial expression patterns of zswim family genes in Xenopus embryos. Both zswim1 and zswim3 were maternally expressed genes. Zswim5 and zswim6 were expressed throughout embryogenesis and showed dynamic expression in the brain, eyes, somite, and bronchial arch at the late tailbud stages. Zswim7 was detected in the eye area, while zswim8 showed dynamic expression in the brain, eyes, and somite during the tailbud stages. Zswim9 was faintly expressed throughout embryonic development. We published seven papers, and one manuscript is under revision in EMBO Report. We trained four Ph.D. students with this fund and participated in four conferences to present our research supported by this grant.

14112618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112618.value: Our research aims to investigate the underlying mechanism of Zswim4 as to how Zswim4 regulates neural crest development. We identified Prohibitin1 (Phb1) as a Zswim4 interaction partner using SILAC, and Prohibitin1 was implicated in regulating neural crest formation. Our next step is to investigate how Zswim4 and Prohibitin1 coordinate to regulate neural crest development. We also plan to study the function of Zswim4 during neural stem cell (NSC) differentiation. To do this, we have generated knockout Zswim4 mice in which exon 2 is flanked by the loxP sequence. We will cross the Zswim4 loxP mice with Nestin-Cre mice to generate Nestin-Cre: Zswim4-/- mice, in which we expect Zswim4 to be knocked out in NSCs and intermediate neural progenitor cells (NPCs). We will study the brain morphology of these mice and test whether they display any changes in nervous behavior.

14112618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112618.value: All vertebrates share a conserved body plan, i.e., the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis with head, trunk, and tail, and dorsoventral (D-V) axis with the backbone and belly of the animal. We found that Zinc Finger SWIM-Type Containing 4 (zswim4) is expressed in the Spemann-Mangold organizer at the onset of Xenopus gastrulation and then enriched in the developing neuroectoderm at the mid-gastrula stages. Knockdown or knockout of zswim4 caused ventralization. Overexpression of zswim4 decreased, whereas knockdown of zswim4 increased, and the expression levels of ventrolateral mesoderm marker genes. Mechanistically Zswim4 attenuates the BMP signal pathways by decreasing the protein stability of Smad1 in the nucleus. In order to elucidate the Zswim4 function, we utilized the stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture (SILAC) to identify its interaction partners and found that Elongin B (ELOB) and Elongin C (ELOC) physically interact with Zswim4. Indeed, Zswim4 forms a complex with the Cul2-RING ubiquitin ligase and ELOB and ELOC, promoting the ubiquitination and degradation of Smad1 in the nucleus. Our study identified a novel mechanism that restricts BMP signaling in the nucleus.

14112718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112718.value: The primary aim of this project is to determine the effectiveness of low-dose ketamine, given during surgery and continuing for the first postoperative day, to prevent chronic pain over the surgical wound in patients receiving major abdominal, thoracic, breast and orthopedic surgery. Chronic postsurgical pain is now recognized as one of the commonest and most debilitating complications after major surgery. In previous RGC-funded studies, we found that around 12% of patients continued to suffer chronic postsurgical pain for months to years after surgery. This was associated with significant interference of daily activities and poorer quality of life. Ketamine, an inhibitor of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors, prevents central sensitization in the pain pathways and may therefore reduce the risk of chronic postsurgical pain. A meta-analysis of earlier ketamine trials, reinforced by our pilot study showed a non-significant decrease in the incidence of chronic postsurgical pain, pooled relative risk (95% confidence intervals): 0.68 (0.43-1.09), p = 0.11. Although these results are encouraging, research in this area has been limited in its methodology and generalizability. A large adequately powered trial to investigate the effectiveness of ketamine for the prevention of chronic postsurgical pain is urgently required, and is rated as the top priority for future research in anesthesia. We propose to conduct an international, randomized, pragmatic trial to compare the effect of low-dose ketamine with a placebo (normal saline) on chronic postsurgical pain in 4,884 patients at 12 months after major surgery. Our secondary goals are to determine the effect of ketamine on quality of recovery, mood and functional disability during the year after surgery. The findings of this study are expected to have considerable scientific, social and economic significance. As enormous numbers of patients undergoing surgery worldwide every year, an effective prophylactic strategy to prevent chronic postsurgical pain would spare millions of patients from the distress of devastating wound pain, life-long medication and repeat interventions. The findings could also be readily translated into contemporary clinical practice, because all anesthetists are familiar with the use of ketamine. 本項目的主要目的是確定低劑量氯胺酮在手術期間和術後第一天持續性使用的有效性，以預防接受大型腹部、胸、乳房和整形外科手術的患者的慢性術後痛。 慢性術後痛是公認的大型手術後最常見和最折磨的並發症之一。研資局曾資助的研究中，我們發現大約12%的患者在手術後數月至數年內持續遭受慢性術後痛，這顯著影響了日常活動，並與生活質量下降顯著相關。氯胺酮是一種NMDA受體抑制劑，可防止疼痛途徑中的中樞敏化，因此可降低慢性術後痛的風險。對之前的氯胺酮試驗進行薈萃分析，以及我們的初步研究也証實，術後早期使用氯胺酮非顯著性地降低慢性術後痛的發生率，合並的相對風險（95%CI）為0.68（0.43-1.09），P＝0.11。雖然這些結果是令人鼓舞的，但在這方面的研究在其方法和可推廣性方面受到限制，因此迫切需要一個樣本量充足、論証有力的試驗來研究氯胺酮預防慢性術後疼痛的有效性，這被認為是未來麻醉研究的重中之重。 我們倡議進行一項國際性、隨機、有時效性的試驗，比較小劑量氯胺酮和安慰劑（生理鹽水）對4884例大型手術后12個月患者術後疼痛的影響。我們的次要目標是確定氯胺酮在術後一年內對恢復質量、情緒和機體功能殘疾的影響。 這項研究的結果很可能具有相當的科學、社會和經濟意義。每年在世界范圍內進行手術的患者數量巨大，預防慢性術后痛的有效預防策略將使數百萬患者受益，使他們免於遭受傷口疼痛、終身服藥和重復干預等痛苦的折磨 。這些發現也很容易地轉化為當代臨床實踐，因為所有麻醉醫生都已熟悉氯胺酮的使用。

14112718.label: Realisation of objectives
14112718.value: Trial recruitment has been severely interrupted by the arrival of the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent healthcare system response. This included mandated interruption of clinical trial activity by hospital authorities from 2020, prolonged reductions in elective surgery throughput in the public hospital system, and severe strains on research staffs and productivity associated with staff redeployments and furloughing. Recruitment has fluctuated with successive COVID waves and lockdowns through to the end of 2022. Trial recruitment is consequently running at least 18-24 months behind schedule. COVID-19 pandemic has presented an unprecedented challenge to multicentre clinical trial conduct. Throughout the period, we have been working hard to maintain trial recruitment and follow-up. Consistent resumption of elective surgery started in 2022 and recruitment recover again substantially, with an overall recruitment rate of approximately 60-70 patients/month. There is also financial challenge to the trial management. Nevertheless, we have been successful in obtaining top-up funding from the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (#2023989, AU$967,000) to help supporting trial completion. Our achievement to date of over 4,000 recruited patients is testament to the perseverance of our team, and the enthusiasm of the trial network for the important clinical question being investigated by the ROCKet trial. With the recovery in recruitment rates, we are confident that the trial will be able to achieve its planned sample size and report in early 2025. Since we are determined to continue with the trial, we are unable to report the results as yet. However, we are committed to recruit the remaining 15% of patients required and will report the definitive results of whether low dose ketamine will prevent the development of chronic postsurgical pain. In addition, the proposed trial will provide a wealth of prospective data on the epidemiology of chronic postsurgical pain and its associated mental health and economic burdens.

14112718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112718.value: The Reduction Of Chronic Postsurgical Pain with Ketamine (ROCKet) Trial is a large (n=4,884), multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial evaluating the effect of low-dose ketamine infusion on the incidence and severity of chronic postsurgical pain among patients having major abdominal and thoracic surgery. As of 11 October, 2023, a total of 4,183 patients (85.6%) were enrolled to the trial. In Hong Kong, we proposed to enroll 600 patients. On 29 November, 2023, we have exceeded our target and have recruited 724 patients (17.3% of total enrolment). We anticipate to complete patient enrolment by the third quarter of 2024 and reporting the 3-month results in early 2025. The trial is currently blinded. Nevertheless, we are able to report the results from the interim analysis, performed after collection of 12-month data from 1,856 patients. The rate of loss to follow up was 4.0%, The incidence of chronic postsurgical pain was 19.7% at 12 months. This exceeded the expected rate of 12%, for which the trial was powered. The incidence of confirmed chronic pain at 3 months was 26%. Forty-eight percent reported moderate pain (with pain score ≥3/10) and 24% reported severe pain (pain score ≥5/10). Patients with chronic postsurgical pain were more likely to develop moderate or worse psychological distress on the K-10 scale (52% vs 25%, p<0.0001) and reported poorer EQ-5D VAS scores (mean 62 vs 82, p<0.0001), compared with those without pain. A total of 37% of these patients had neuropathic characteristics. Clinically important pain catastrophising scale score were reported in 8.3% of patients. These data suggest that chronic postsurgical pain after major surgery is substantial and adversely affect psychological indices and quality of life. The ROCket trial is well powered to demonstrate a clinically significant treatment effect, if present, from the trial intervention.

14112718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112718.value: In addition to the investigation of treatment effect, we have collected blood samples before and after surgery in over 300 patients. We will evaluate the biomolecular determinants for acute and chronic postsurgical pain. In this study, we aim to explore the genetic and epigenetic influences on the risk of progression from acute to chronic postsurgical pain. Furthermore, we will determine the association between ketamine efficacy, side effects, and inter-individual differences in drug kinetics and metabolism of the drug. This study will allow us to develop a cost-effective precision medicine for the diagnostic and treatment of chronic postsurgical pain. This will ultimately improve community health, productivity and economic savings.

14112718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112718.value: Chronic postsurgical pain is one of the most common and debilitating complications after major surgery, accounting for 10% of the overall chronic pain prevalence in the community. Our ROCket trial tested whether a commonly used anesthetic/analgesic agent – ketamine will help to prevent hypersensitivity and “wind-up” of the pain pathway and spinal cord. Currently, we have recruited 85% of the target patient sample. In the coming 12 months, we will complete data collection and will be able to report definitively whether ketamine will help to avoid the progression of acute postoperative pain progresses to chronic postsurgical pain.

14112818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112818.value: Background: The epidemics of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) in Hong Kong and Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) in the Middle East and South Korea generate the need to evaluate the effectiveness of control measures. Hong Kong is a densely populated international city with strong communication links between residents which facilitate the rapid spread of infectious diseases. In the early phase of outbreaks, contact tracing followed by quarantine or isolation is an important infection control measure. Ideally, epidemics are better contained with direct control over the whole population, but that involves high cost and sometimes it may not be achievable with limited resources in a short period of time. The benefit of contact tracing will be substantially reduced with tight schedules. Given that resources were top stretched to the limit over a short period of time in early phase of outbreak, resources need to be prioritized and allocated to trace number of identified physical contacts. Aims and methods: The aim of this study is to develop a tool to assess the likely effectiveness of a contact tracing process during an epidemic of a novel pathogen. An individual-based mathematical model will be developed alongside a resource-constrained contact tracing process. This simulation environment will be tested in scenarios that reflect both actual uncertainties of two prior epidemics that affected Hong Kong (SARS and pandemic influenza). One recent emerging infectious disease (MERS) will also be considered. We will test a number of plausible future scenarios during which contact tracing may be important and where there may be substantial uncertainty in subsequent interventions after tracing. Expected results and implication: With a developed tool to assess the contact tracing process effectiveness, we can estimate the probability and the average duration of disease containment, the average time to trace one contact per day and proportion of actual contact to be traced in given contact tracing strategies for different transmission scenarios. The optimal number of traced identified contacts and optimal combination of traced contacts at home and school/workplace to control the outbreak can also be estimated given there is no resource constraint on contact tracing. The relationship between contact tracing resources and mitigation effectiveness for different proposed infectious diseases outbreaks can thus be identified. The potential marginal benefit of improved contact tracing will be particular substantial in the near future with the availability of vaccine against novel pathogens (such as influenza) within short period of time after initial isolation. 14112918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112918.value: Ghrelin (acyl ghrelin) is a peptide that stimulates feeding and gastrointestinal motility mainly via growth hormone secretagogue receptors (GHS-R1A). The ability of acyl ghrelin and/or its metabolite, des-acyl ghrelin, to induce a sensation of hunger may reduce the tendency to perceive the feeling of nausea. Plasma levels of ghrelin correlate inversely with nausea and/or vomiting in patients with diabetic gastroparesis or postoperative ileus and in those who undergo chemotherapy. In these situations, ghrelin, ghrelin mimetics, and treatments that elevate ghrelin levels can increase appetite, restore gastric propulsion, and/or reduce nausea and vomiting. However, evidence shows that acyl ghrelin and des-acyl ghrelin activate an unacetylated ghrelin receptor (UGR). The relative importance of these receptors to the mechanisms that control nausea and emesis is unknown. Chemotherapy with agents such as cisplatin induces not only an acute phase, but also a delayed phase of nausea and emesis that is mechanistically different and poorly understood. Our studies have shown that acyl ghrelin and a ghrelin mimetic, HM01, can antagonize the “acute” response via mechanisms in the brain that probably involve GHS-R1A. However, no studies have examined a potential for ghrelin or ghrelin mimetics to reduce the “delayed” phase of emesis. Furthermore, the contribution of UGR to the emetic mechanism involved in the acute and delayed phases is unknown. Recently, we showed that the antiemetic effects of HM01 extend to cyclophosphamide and the emesis induced by the free radical generator pyrogallol, but not to fluoxetine, which increases the extracellular levels of 5-HT; this suggests that stimulation of GHS-R1A or UGR prevents the production of free radicals, which is hypothesized to be a starting point from which chemotherapy initiates a cascade of cellular events that lead to emesis. Furthermore, HM01 antagonized motion-induced emesis via a mechanism that may involve an ability to reduce c-Fos expression in medial vestibular nuclei and/or by potentiating c-Fos in hypothalamic nuclei. The recommended antiemetic agents for chemotherapy-induced emesis do not prevent motion-induced nausea and emesis in man, but a history of motion sickness is a risk factor for nausea and emesis induced by chemotherapy. The spectrum of action of ghrelin and ghrelin mimetics to reduce emesis and their mechanism of action is therefore unique. The proposed studies will investigate whether GHS-R1A and/or the UGR are involved in the mechanism of cisplatin-induced acute and delayed emesis necessary for the development of ghrelin mimetics as novel antiemetic drugs. 胃飢餓素（酰基化的胃飢餓素）是一種主要通過生長激素促分泌素受體來刺激攝食和胃腸蠕動的肽。酰基化的胃飢餓素和/或其代謝產物，去酰基化的胃飢餓素誘導飢餓感的能力可能會有降低感知噁心感的傾向。血漿胃飢餓素水平與糖尿病引起的胃輕癱，術後腸梗阻和治療後化療患者的噁心和/或嘔吐呈負相關。 在這些情況下，胃飢餓素及其類似物和提高胃飢餓素水平的治療可以增加食慾，恢復胃蠕動和/或減少噁心和嘔吐。 然而，已有的證據表明酰基化的胃飢餓素和去酰基化胃飢餓素會激活未乙酰化的胃飢餓素受體。這些受體對控制噁心和嘔吐機制的重要性目前還不清楚。 使用順鉑等藥物進行的化療不僅可誘導急性期的惡心和嘔吐，還可誘導延遲期噁心和嘔吐，但兩者在機制上有所不同，相關機制也不完全清楚。我們已有的研究表明，酰基化的胃飢餓素及其類似物HM01可以通過可能涉及腦內生長激素促分泌素受體的機制來拮抗“急性”反應。然而，沒有研究檢測過胃飢餓素或胃飢餓素類似物可能會減少延遲期間的噁心和嘔吐的潛在作用。此外，未乙酰化的胃飢餓素受體在急性期和延遲期所涉及的催吐機制的作用也不清楚。最近，我們的研究發現HM01的止吐作用擴展到環磷酰胺和由自由基生成劑連苯三酚引起的嘔吐，但不是氟西汀，這增加了細胞外水平的五羥色胺，表明了生長激素促分泌素受體或乙酰化的胃飢餓素受體的激活抑制了自由基的產生。自由基的產生被假設為化療的引發一系列細胞事件從而導致嘔吐的起點。此外，HM01可能通過降低內側前庭核中fos蛋白的表達和/或通過增強下丘腦核中fos蛋白的能力的機制來拮抗運動誘導的嘔吐。推薦用於化療引起的嘔吐的止吐藥可以預防運動引起的噁心和嘔吐，而暈車病的病史是化療引起的噁心和嘔吐的一個危險因素。因此，胃飢餓素及其類似物減少嘔吐的作用範圍及其作用機制是獨特的。擬議的研究將調查生長激素促分泌素受體和/或未乙酰化的胃飢餓素受體是否參與順鉑誘導的急性和延遲性嘔吐機制，這是利用其開發作為新型止吐藥必需的研究內容和範疇。

14112918.label: Realisation of objectives
14112918.value: The major aim of the project was to determine if ghrelin could activate a novel mechanism to reduce chemotherapy-induced mechanism. It has been postulated that AG may have low potency actions at a distinct DAG or un-acetylated ghrelin receptor (UGR), but the receptors remain to be cloned. The studies would be the first to see if DAG could affect emesis and mechanisms involved in feeding and ‘nausea’ in a more potent manner than AG un an animal with an emetic reflex. As animals are unable to communicate their emotional/nausea status, they were implanted with radiotelemetry devices to record biopotentials and experiments also looked at neurotransmitter profiles against a backdrop of standard experimental techniques and effects on respiration. AG and DAG had similar effects against most of the readouts that were recorded particularly during the acute phase of emesis, but there was a tendency for DAG to be more active during the delayed phase. We demonstrated that AG and DAG had a trend to enhance food intake before cisplatin administration. However, both AG and DAG failed to reverse the reduction of food intake, body weight induced by cisplatin. Cisplatin induced 15.7±9.2 episodes; latency to onset was 36.4±2.9-min. AG and DAG [μg/kg/day] prevented emesis completely during the 12-72-h period: AG 0.2:1/6; AG 1:2/5; AG 5:2/5 and DAG 1:3/5; DAG 5:1/5. AG and DAG reduced the emetic intensity. AG decreased frequency in the acute emetic period, while DAG reduced frequency in both acute and delayed period. This indicates that DAG has additional affects that may not exclusively involve GHSR-1A. Cisplatin caused a small degree of hypothermia, which was not reversed by AG or DAG. Cisplatin reduced blood pressure, but this was not significantly affected by AG or DAG. Cisplatin reduced respiration rate but this also was not affected by AG or DAG. Baseline GMA for animals before randomization was DF=10.9±0.6cpm; DP+7.4±2.1*10−3mv2; and 51.7±2.7% of power was in the bradygastria range; 24.9±1.7% of power was in the normogastria range, and 16.5±1.1% of power was in the tachygastria range (n=42). Cisplatin decreased the DF and DP during acute emesis; there was a reduction of %power of tachygastria. DF decreased further during delayed emesis, where the %power of bradygastria increased. AG/DAG prevented the cisplatin-induced DP reduction and DF alterations indicating animals may have experienced less nausea. To better observe the slow waves of GMA, Running Spectrum Analysis was created to obtain the 3D plots of GMA, which demonstrated that both AG and DAG administrated higher than 1mg/kg/day, could rescue the Dominant Power of GMA. To examine this further, DFA and Entropy analysis were applied to characterize the gastric effects of cisplatin during the acute and delayed phase of emesis. Western blot detected cisplatin-induced changes in Bcl2, Bax, and cytochrome C/ β-actin levels, which regulate cell apoptosis pathways. DAG had a better anti-apoptotic activity than AG within the GI tract. Other signatures relative to nausea and emesis relate to neurochemical profiles in tissues. Cisplatin treated animals had higher levels of substance P in plasma which was not reduced by AG or DAG suggesting the stimulus to drive the emetic response was still ongoing. A liquid chromatography-mass-spectrometry (LC-MS) protocol enabled the quantitative analysis of neurotransmitters/metabolites including acetylcholine, norepinephrine, dopamine, tyrosine, 5-HT, tryptophan, 5-HIAA, GABA, and glutamate, in different brain areas. A Pearson coefficient correlation analysis was performed revealing significance between 9-neurotransmitter/metabolite in 5-different brain areas. Compared to the vehicle-treated group, cisplatin transformed positive correlations into negative correlations. AG and DAG were both found to reverse these changes to different degrees. This work has been presented internally at a CUHK during a Postgraduate Research Day, 2022, meeting, as a poster communication and an abstract has been submitted to the 19th World Congress of Basic & Clinical Pharmacology 2023. We have not yet written up the work for full publication as some data are still being held back for analysis. This is because the system software used for the respiratory analysis was upgraded but failed to synchronize with other telemetry software in our setup. The software developer assures us that this would be fixed in the next software update. We do need to access data on inspiratory/expiratory rates and volumes. A template to write up the studies has been published by us (Tu et al., 2021. Front Pharmacol. 2021; 12: 746053). The original project was disrupted by several times. only Aims 1 and 2 could reasonably be addressed using the funding that was available. Social unrest in November-2019 disrupted access to the University and laboratory. The University closed and the Laboratory Animal Services Centre (LASEC) was cut off from main campus. LASEC reported that the Suncus murinus colony had also been relocated twice in the year due to renovation and building works, which impacted negatively on breeding performance. The COVID-19 pandemic also impacted on access of personnel to CUHK and breeding in LASEC with several laboratory team members contracting SARS-CoV-2 leading to further periods where research was suspended. We were not able to take delivery of osmotic minipumps and other experimental consumables due to suspension of the postal system. In the meantime, our Research Assistant resigned, and it has taken time to find a replacement and retrain the new individual. Evidence we obtained from the main experiments did indicate differences between AG and DAG, but we did not fully progress during the allotted time to focus experiments to the hypothalamic/limbic forebrain areas (Aim 3). To compensate, even though the project has officially ended, work is continuing using a PhD studentship which has one year to run. This would give us time to complete the studies up to Aim 3. This would not be covered in this report. Certainly, we have shown some evidence that AG and DAG may also differentially reverse some indicators of ‘nausea’ which is very encouraging. In summary, burst analysis for emesis episodes, RSA for GMA signals, and LCMS for the changes of neurotransmitters in different brain areas demonstrated that AG and DAG have different patterns to affect emesis. The social disruption and Covid pandemic impacted on Hong Kong severely, and laboratory time was cut short by many months (above). Animals could not be surgically prepared or left alone in the middle of experimentation. When an experimental run is disrupted, 3-4 weeks of laboratory time is lost between the occurrence of an event and then to have overlap of experiments that were planned. Originally, we estimated that 6-months had been lost, but the suspension of breeding of Suncus murinus added a further 6-months. The loss of personnel of the project through resignation was also impactful. To address this, a PhD studentship was acquired, and she began work on the project as part of her studies. This means the studies will be completed, as the funding for PhD studentship is from elsewhere and manuscripts submitted by end of 2023.

14112918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112918.value: Ghrelin is a peptide that stimulates feeding and gastrointestinal motility via growth hormone secretagogue receptors (GHS-R). Ghrelin levels increase in the plasma when the stomach is empty and is thought to provide a signal to eat signal. In addition, a wealth of evidence now shows that low plasma levels of ghrelin correlate with nausea and vomiting in patients with diabetic gastroparesis, postoperative ileus, and following treatment chemotherapy. Our previous study showed that ghrelin and ghrelin mimetics could antagonize cisplatin-induced early emesis through mechanisms probably involving GHS-R1A in the brain. Ghrelin can exist in two forms: acyl ghrelin (AG) and des-acyl ghrelin (DAG). Many studies suggested AG receptor is GHS-R1a. However, it has been hypothesized that there may be a DAG receptor mediating some of the effects of ghrelin, although most of the evidence is circumstantial, as the DAG receptor has not been cloned. In the present studies, we compared the potency of AG and DAG to stimulate feeding and to reverse the detrimental effect of cisplatin to induce emesis and ‘nausea’. We demonstrated that AG and DAG had a trend to enhance food intake before cisplatin administration but both forms of ghrelin were ineffective to reverse the reduction of food intake, body weight induced by cisplatin although they did reduce the emetic action of cisplatin. The approach of using radiotelemetry in conjunction with whole body plethysmography was to permit access to physiological data indicative of ‘nausea’ where respiration is slowed and temperature, cardiovascular and gastrointestinal readouts shift to a pattern representative of a predominant sympathetic tone following treatment with cisplatin. AG and DAG did not impact on the thermal or cardiovascular readouts to indicate that nausea had been abated. However, the profile on the gastrointestinal readouts were more positive, with DAG having a greater protective effect during the delayed emetic response. It is possible that this may have been due to protective effects against cell death in gastrointestinal tissues, but evidence was also found for a protective effect against cisplatin-induced disturbance of neurotransmitter levels in several brain areas. Indeed, AG and DAG had protective effects, but the patterns of protection were different. This suggests that AG and DAG may indeed have different mechanisms against emesis and ‘nausea’ readouts in Suncus murinus. The data are encouraging to suggest that DAG mimetics could be synthesized in the future as novel anti-‘nausea’ drugs to be used in conjunction with standard anti-emetics.

14112918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112918.value: To further explore the central nervous system mechanisms, drugs would be infused into the amygdala, hypothalamus, and dorsal vagal complex before the administration to delineate between emesis and mechanisms controlling ‘nausea’. We have already established the coordinates for injecting into the hypothalamus and studies on GLP-1 receptor mechanisms on an unrelated project show that this brain region can modulate emesis and feeding. Our studies with AG and DAG should be pivotal in delineating these mechanisms as they build on neurotransmitter patterns of ‘nausea’ following cisplatin treatment and differential effects on sympathetically mediated markers of nausea, with GMA being most affected. We shall administer AG, DAG, and vehicle groups using Alzet® Osmotic infusion pumps into the hypothalamus and amygdala to avoid handing the animals and achieve better recordings. Cisplatin (30 mg/kg, i.p.) will be administered and animals will be followed for another 72 h to assess behavioral change and food and water intake. Animals will be killed, and brainstem DVC and GI tissue (stomach and ileum) will be taken for neurochemical and immunohistochemical analysis. Blood will be taken to determine plasma vasopressin and substance P, important markers of ‘nausea’.

14112918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112918.value: Chemotherapy-induced acute and delayed emesis remains a significant problem for some cancer patients. Our previous study showed that the gut hormone, ghrelin, and ghrelin mimetics could antagonize the early emesis induced by chemotherapy through mechanisms probably involving receptors in the brain. However, as ghrelin can exist in two forms: acyl ghrelin (AG) and des-acyl ghrelin (DAG), it is possible that multiple receptors are involved. The present studies compared the potential of AG and DAG to inhibit the acute and delayed emesis induced by the chemotherapeutic drug, cisplatin, in Suncus murinus. Emesis was antagonized by both forms of ghrelin and there was also evidence for an ability of AG and DAG to reduce some of the physiological readouts of nausea including an ability to protect against the action of cisplatin in the gastrointestinal tract. There was also evidence that both AG and DAG could antagonize the imbalance of neurotransmitter functions in brain areas associated with emesis and those involved in mechanisms thought to be involved in nausea. The differential activity between AG and DAG, however, may suggest that a novel ghrelin receptor exists. It may be possible to target this unidentified receptor/mechanism to specifically treat nausea and emesis.

14113018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113018.value: 該項目旨在研究骨質疏鬆骨折癒合過程中給予循環機械負荷後骨細胞的骨陷窩－骨小管網絡、礦化程度及DMP1作用的改變，並與正常骨折進行比較。 骨質疏鬆骨折在老年人中十分常見，並有著相當高的發病率和死亡率。長期以來的普遍觀點認爲疏鬆骨對機械負荷的反應會降低。但是越來越多的體內實驗證據表明無論是完整的還是已經發生骨折的疏鬆骨都對機械負荷有著良好的反應。我們的前期研究也顯示在給予低幅高頻振動（LMHFV）的循環機械負荷後，相較於年齡匹配的正常骨折，骨質疏鬆骨折的愈合速度更快。 我們已證實的機制包括骨折後骨痂処間充質幹細胞募集及雌激素受體表達增加，這改善了骨的機械反應及骨折的癒合。然而這只是下游的通路，發生骨折的疏鬆骨是如何感應並對機械信號作出反應的仍需要進一步探究。由於骨細胞的功能包括機械感應和礦化調節，這或許可以解釋爲什麽發生骨折後，疏鬆骨相較於正常骨有著更好的機械反應。除此之外，表達在骨細胞樹突的DMP1是骨細胞對對機械負荷作出反應並調節礦化的重要通路，然而在骨質疏鬆骨折癒合中卻很少被提及。我們早期的研究顯示：骨折後疏鬆骨的LCN超微結構相較於正常骨更差，而LMHFV可顯著誘導兩組形成骨細胞樹突。此外，在骨折後第４周（機械敏感階段），骨質疏鬆骨折LMHFV治療組的骨痂処礦化程度和ＤＭＰ１的表達量都要高於未予治療的對照組。 在這項研究中，我們假設（１）相較於正常骨折，機械負荷能更大程度地改變骨質疏鬆性乾骺端骨折的骨細胞LCN和礦化程度；（２）骨質疏鬆性骨折癒合過程中，循環機械負荷可增加骨痂処DMP1的表達，而阻斷DMP1則將抵消LMHFV誘導的礦化增加。 本研究是我們之前GRF資助項目的延續（參考編號：462811, 462708；研究骨質疏鬆骨折的機械反應機制）。這項研究的結果將解釋爲什麽骨質疏鬆骨折比正常骨折有更好的機械反應，進而幫助我們進一步瞭解骨質疏鬆骨折癒合過程中骨細胞的作用，從而最終開展新的加速骨折癒合的治療策略。

14113018.label: Realisation of objectives
14113018.value: Objective 1: • A clinically relevant ovariectomy (OVX)-induced osteoporotic metaphyseal fracture rat model was used, which is an FDA-approved osteoporosis animal model and the metaphyseal region can mimic osteoporotic bone well. Sham and osteoporotic rats were randomized into 4 groups: (1) Sham control (Sham-CT), (2) Sham vibration (Sham-VT), (3) Osteoporosis control (OVX-CT), (4) Osteoporosis vibration (OVX-VT). Vibration treatment (V-Health Ltd, Hong Kong; 35Hz, 0.3g; 20min/day, 5days/week) was given to VT groups, while control animals were put on vibration platform with power off. Assessment timepoints were day 7, 14 and 42 post-fracture, including radiography, bone microarchitecture, dynamic histomorphology, acid-etched SEM (scanning electron microscopy), FITC staining / Imaris analysis of osteocyte morphology and mechanical testing. • Vibration treatment could significantly improve lacuna-canalicular network (LCN) osteocytes with a substantial increase in the canaliculi number and length and the effect on the osteocytes related morphology was greater in OVX group than Sham group. Quantitatively, OVX-VT showed increased dendritic branch points at day 14 and 42 than OVX-CT (day 14: +65.3%, p=0.03; day 42: +50.6%, p>0.05). Also, canalicular length was increased in OVX-VT than in OVX-CT at day 14 and 42 (day 14: +93%, p=0.019; day 42: +68%, p>0.05). For lacunar surface area, OVX-VT showed an increase than OVX-CT at day 7 and 42 (day 7: +8.4%, day 42: +46.7%), while lacunar volume increased in OVX-VT than in OVX-CT at day 7, 14 and 42 (day 7: +44.9%, day 14: +47.8%, day 42: +56.4%). The enhancement effect was also observed in Sham-VT group, yet the magnitude of increase was not as high as in OVX-VT. In summary, with vibration treatment, the osteocyte LCN exhibited a more vibrant morphology with an exuberant outgrowth of canaliculi in both Sham-VT and OVX-VT groups. (Reported in interim report) Objective 2: • MAR and BFR were measured by dynamic histomorphology; Ca/P ratio was assessed by energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry analysis; BV/TV and mechanical properties were evaluated by microCT and mechanical testing respectively. • A significant increase of mineral apposition rate (MAR) (p=0.007) and bone formation rate (BFR/BS) (p=0.018) were found in OVX-VT group than in OVX-CT group at day 42. Yet, there was no significant change of them in Sham-VT group. For Ca/P ratio, a significant enhancement was also found in OVX-VT than in OVX-CT group (p=0.05), while no change of Ca/P ratio was detected in Sham-VT. Meanwhile, BV/TV of microCT increased from day 7 to day 42 in all groups. OVX-VT group exhibited an increase steadily compared with OVX-CT group at all time points. A significant increase in BV/TV was found in OVX-VT at day 14 (p=0.008). At day 42, both OVX-VT and Sham-VT groups showed significantly higher BV/TV values, as compared with their corresponding control groups (p=0.01 for both). Mechanically, OVX-VT group exhibited a significantly higher ultimate load by 105% (p=0.036) and stiffness by 151% (p=0.024) than OVX-CT group at day 14. Higher energy-to-failure was also observed in all vibration groups (p=0.016). A significant increase of energy-to-failure by 113% was found at day 42 in OVX-VT group (p=0.022) than in OVX-CT group. In contrast, there was no significant difference between Sham-VT and Sham-CT groups at all time points. (Reported in interim report) • From Objectives 1 and 2, vibration treatment was found to enhance osteocytes’ morphology, mineralization status and bone healing in the osteoporotic metaphyseal fracture animal model. The revitalized osteocyte LCN implies a better connectivity and transduction of mechanical signals between osteocytes, thus fostering the osteoporotic fracture healing process through enhanced mineralization. These results highlight the importance of osteocyte LCN in response to mechanical signal during osteoporotic fracture healing. Objective 3: • Only OVX rats were used, while OVX metaphyseal fracture rats were randomized to 5 groups: (1) vehicle control (CT), (2) vehicle control vibration (VT), (3) DMP1 knockdown (KD), (4) DMP1 knockdown vibration (KD+VT) and (5) scramble control vibration (Sb+VT). Vibration treatment regime remained the same. Knockdown was performed by injecting AAV9 vector (1x10^11 titer) to femoral condyle 2 weeks before fracture creation allowing sufficient time for effective knockdown, while shRNA sequences (Division of Life Science, HKUST, HK) were packaged into AAV9 vector. Timepoints and assessments were same as Objective 1 and 2. • Radiologically, Sb+VT group (0.248 ± 0.056) had significantly higher mean radiopacity than KD+VT group (0.169 ± 0.064) at day 7 (p=0.004). KD+VT group (0.383 ± 0.041) had significantly lower mean radiopacity than Sb+VT group (0.481 ± 0.011) and VT group (0.476 ± 0.02) at day 42 (p=0.013 and 0.012 respectively). DMP1 knockdown groups had lower relative radiopacity than control groups at all time points. • In dynamic histomorphology, knockdown groups showed decreased MAR and BFR at all timepoints, which KD+VT group had significantly lower MAR and BFR than VT group (p<0.05 for both) at day 42. For microCT, tissue volume (TV) of VT and Sb+VT groups were significantly higher than KD+VT group (p=0.012 and 0.007 respectively) at day 7. For bone volume (BV), knockdown groups had less bone at day 14 and 42 compared with VT and Sb+VT groups, where KD+VT group had significantly lower BV than Sb+VT group at day 14 (p=0.01). BV/TV of Sb+VT group was significantly higher than that of KD+VT group (p=0.034) at day 14. Ca/P ratio also showed significantly higher value in VT than in KD-VT group (p<0.05) at day 42. Morphologically, less outgrowth of osteocyte LCN was observed in KD and KD+VT groups than other groups. Quantitatively, VT and Sb+VT groups demonstrated significantly higher canalicular number and length of osteocytes than KD and KD+VT groups (p<0.05). • In immunohistochemistry, DMP1 expression of knockdown groups remained at a low level across all timepoints. CT, VT and Sb+VT groups showed steady increase of DMP1 towards day 42 where significant difference was reached between CT group and KD group (p=0.033). VT group had significantly higher DMP1 expression than KD+VT group at both day 14 and 42 (p=0.008 and 0.000 respectively). Significant difference was also found between Sb+VT and KD+VT groups at day 42 (p=0.03). The expression of SOST in knockdown groups was higher at all timepoints compared to the other 3 groups. Vibration groups generally had lower SOST expression but KD+VT group had an opposite result, which was significantly higher than VT and Sb+VT groups (p=0.001 and 0.007 respectively) at day 42. There was a decreasing trend of E11 expression among all groups towards the end of healing process at day 42 post-fracture. KD group had significantly higher E11 expression than CT group at day 7 (p=0.05). KD+VT group also showed significantly increased expression of E11 than Sb+VT group at both day 7 and 14 (p=0.024 and 0.008 respectively) and VT group at day 14 (p=0.048). The expression of FGF23 followed an increasing trend towards day 14 and decreased at day 42. KD groups had comparatively higher FGF23 expression at all time points. Vibration treatment had reduced the FGF23 expression in VT and Sb+VT groups compared to CT group, but the same effect was not found in the KD+VT group. • In summary, Objective 3 revealed an impaired mineralization and fracture healing after knockdown of DMP1. These confirm the important role of DMP1 in osteoporotic fracture healing augmented by vibration treatment through altering osteocyte specific protein expression. This is the first study demonstrating the role of DMP1 in response to mechanical stimulation in osteoporotic fracture healing.

14113018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113018.value: • Two systematic reviews on the roles of osteocytes in fracture healing and in mechanotransduction regulation were conducted. This generated two journal articles [8.1, 8.3]. • The changes of osteocyte lacuno-canalicular network, mineralization and healing status were comprehensively measured after vibration treatment. Morphological analysis revealed that vibration treatment enhanced dendritic branch points (+65.3%, +50.6%) and length (+93%, +68%) of osteocytes extensively in osteoporotic fracture group at day 14 and 42 respectively than its control group. Meanwhile, vibration increased the lacunar surface area and volume at all time points (lacunar volume: +44.9%, +47.8%, +56.4% at day 7, 14, 42 respectively). Sham group (non-osteoporotic) also demonstrated an enhancement effect on osteocyte morphology, but not as good as in osteoporotic group. At tissue level, an increase of mineralization was found after vibration, as reflected by significant increases of MAR, BFR and Ca/P ratio at day 42. Furthermore, microCT also showed a significant increase of bone volume fraction (BV/TV) in osteoporotic fracture group at day 14 and 42. Mechanical properties of osteoporotic fracture bone also became significantly stronger after vibration – ultimate load (+105%), stiffness (+151%) at day 14 and energy-to-failure (+113%) at day 42. In contrast, Sham group did not show significant enhancement in most parameters at tissue level after vibration, except BV/TV at day 42. These results indicated that vibration revitalized osteocyte lacuno-canalicular network, leading to better transduction of mechanical signals among osteocytes, improved mechanosensitivity and hence osteoporotic fracture healing through promoted mineralization. These generated 1 original article [8.2], 1 review article [8.4], 5 conference abstracts [9.1-9.5] and 1 invited talk [9.9]. • The role of DMP1 in osteoporotic fracture healing augmented by vibration treatment was investigated. At tissue level, knockdown of DMP1 showed inferior results, including decrease of MAR and BFR (KD+VTVT and Sb+VT at day 42), significantly higher E11 (KD>CT at day 7, KD+VT>Sb+VT at day 7 and 14 and VT at day 14). These confirm the critical role of DMP1 in osteoporotic fracture healing augmented by vibration treatment. This part generated 3 conference abstracts [9.6-9.8] and 1 original article under review [8.5].

14113018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113018.value: • This study confirmed the enhanced effect of vibration treatment on osteocyte and mechanosensitivity in osteoporotic fracture healing. Combined with our previous positive evidence of vibration treatment on downstream mechanisms of osteoporotic fracture healing, the effect of vibration treatment on osteoporotic fracture healing has been confirmed. The next step is to conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) for translation. Our research team is working in this direction on trochanteric hip fracture (https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT04063891). • Our patented vibration platform has been commercialized (www.v-health.com.hk) for fall prevention, muscle training and osteoporosis prevention. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, USA) is approaching us to include our vibration treatment into upcoming issue of fall prevention compendium in 2022. If the RCT on fracture healing is proven, this will add one more indication to our vibration platform for wider clinical applications. • We have also investigated the in vitro effect of vibration treatment on osteocyte-like cells (MLO-Y4). RNA-Seq was performed to evaluate the gene expressions and showed that vibration treatment increased the expression of Wnt10b remarkably. Knockdown of beta-catenin also abolished the enhancement effect of vibration treatment; hence, Wnt/beta-catenin should be the major pathway. Wnt10b may be developed as a potential therapeutic target for fragility fracture enhancement in the future.

14113018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113018.value: With increasing ageing population, osteoporotic fracture is a common geriatric problem in orthopaedic wards, which is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Osteoporosis impairs fracture healing, leading to extended healing time and high complication rates. Therefore, there is a pressing need to search for an effective and non-invasive intervention for osteoporotic fracture healing. This study is the first to investigate the changes of osteocytes, mineralization and the role of osteocyte-specific dentin matrix protein 1 (DMP1) in osteoporotic fracture healing augmented by vibration treatment. Results showed vibration treatment could induce more vibrant osteocytes’ morphology with extensive dendritic outgrowth, enhance mineralization status and bone healing in an osteoporotic metaphyseal fracture rat model. The revitalized osteocyte network implies a better connectivity and transduction of mechanical signals among osteocytes, which may foster the osteoporotic fracture healing through promoted mineralization. Meanwhile, knockdown of DMP1 negated the vibration-induced enhancement effect, leading to impaired mineralization and hence fracture healing, which confirmed the critical role of DMP1 in osteoporotic fracture through altering osteocyte specific protein expression. In summary, vibration treatment can enhance osteoporotic fracture healing through revitalizing osteocytes. It is of high potential to be applied clinically to accelerate osteoporotic fracture healing in the future.
