14113618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113618.value: Aberrant amyloid-β peptide (Aβ) production derived from amyloid precursor protein (APP) is a crucial event in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis. Although various strategies to reduce Aβ level have been proposed/tested, severe side effects and/or unsatisfying effectiveness are reported for some approaches. Therefore, alternative strategies for lowering Aβ level are desirable. Further understanding of the mechanisms that influence APP processing could reveal novel therapeutic targets. FE65 is brain-enriched adaptor which has been shown to interact with APP and to alter APP processing. One critical question in the field is how FE65 participates in APP processing. A function of FE65 is to recruit interactors to form functional complexes. It is therefore essential to establish FE65 interaction network and to evaluate the roles of the identified FE65 interacting proteins (FIPs) in FE65-mediated APP processing. Owing to different limitations of the classical identification approaches, some crucial FIPs may yet to be identified. To this end, proximity-dependent biotin identification (BioID) is performed in FE65 knockout mouse primary neurons and has identified ARF nucleotide-binding-site opener (ARNO) and engulfment and cell motility protein 1 (Elmo1) as novel FIPs which are the regulators for ARF6-Rac1 signaling. ARNO is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for ARF6 while Elmo1 is the regulatory subunit of Elmo1/Dock180 bipartite GEF complex for Rac1. ARF6-Rac1 signaling is essential for endocytic trafficking, a process that plays a significant role in APP processing. Noteworthy, there is evidence that FE65 alters APP localization. Therefore, it is possible that FE65 orchestrates ARNO and Elmo1 in the ARF6-Rac1 signaling pathway to regulate APP endocytic trafficking and in turn APP processing. On the other hand, FE65 phosphorylation is shown to modulate APP processing. Since phosphorylation is a common mechanism to regulate protein-protein interaction and aberrant phosphorylation is strongly associated with AD, FE65 kinases may regulate/dysregulate APP processing via ARF6-Rac1 signaling, possibly by altering FE65-ARNO and/or FE65-ELMO1 interactions. In this project, we will evaluate the above hypotheses in cell and transgenic models, and the mechanism(s) behind will also be investigated. In a preliminary study, FE65 potentiated the effect of ARNO on ARF6 activation and Elmo1 on Rac1 activation. Moreover, Elmo1 could enhance FE65-mediated APP processing. The proposed work will shed important light on the roles of FE65, ARNO and Elmo1 in ARF6-Rac1 signaling and the mechanism by which FE65 modulates APP processing, and may provide essential information for the therapeutic development of AD. 從澱粉樣前體蛋白（APP）異常裂解產生的β-澱粉樣蛋白（Aβ）是阿爾茲海默病（AD）發病的關鍵因素。然而，多種降低Aβ生成的治療方案會產生嚴重的副作用，治療效果並不理想。因此，進壹步理解調控APP裂解過程的作用機理會提供新的治療方向。FE65是壹種腦富集銜接蛋白，它可以APP蛋白結合並影響其裂解過程。而FE65如何調控APP裂解過程是壹個研究重點。多項研究表明FE65的結合蛋白(FIP)影響FE65多種生理功能。我們運用BioID，在FE65敲除小鼠的原代神經元細胞實驗中發現了FE65新型結合蛋白(FIP)：ARNO 和ELMO1。這兩個新型FIP是調控ARF6-Rac1信號通路的重要因子。ARNO是ARF6的鳥票呤核甘酸交換因子，而ELMO1是ELMO1/DOCK180復合體中調控Rac1活性的關鍵亞基。ARF6-Rac1信號通路在細胞內吞運輸中至關重要，而這個過程顯著影響APP裂解。值得註意的是。FE65調控APP在細胞內的定位。因此，我們假設FE65結合ARNO和ELMO1，通過影響ARF6-Rac1信號通路調控APP內吞運輸，從而影響其蛋白裂解。另壹方面，FE65的磷酸化也參與APP裂解調控。磷酸化是調節蛋白-蛋白相互作用的常見機制，而異常的磷酸化過程與AD密切相關。因此，調控FE65磷酸化的激酶有可能影響FE65-ARNO，或者FE65-ELMO1相互作用，從而通過影響ARF6-Rac1信號通路參與調控APP裂解。本課題計劃用細胞和轉基因模型驗證以上假設並研究其中機制。初步研究發現，FE65分別增強了ARNO對ARF6, ELMO1對Rac1的激活作用。此外，ELMO1可增強FE65介導的APP裂解。擬議的工作將重點闡明FE65，ARNO和ELMO1 在ARF6-Rac1信號通路中的作用以及FE65如何調節APP裂解的機制，並為AD的治療發展提供重要資訊。

14113618.label: Realisation of objectives
14113618.value: Objective 1: ELMO1 and ARNO are novel FE65 interacting protein that is found in our laboratory from various screening approaches. In this part of the project, their interaction with FE65 was confirmed by different biochemical assays including GST-fusion protein pull-down and co-immunoprecipitation assays. To facilitate further analysis of the project, we then determined the regions in FE65 and ELMO1 that mediate their interaction. In yeast two-hybrid analysis, that the first sixty residues of FE65 are essential for FE65-ELMO1 interaction. We then determined the residue(s) in FE65 that is critical for mediating FE65-ELMO1 interaction by generating a number of FE65 mutants and tested their abilities to interact with ELMO1 in co-immunoprecipitation assays. We found that FE65 K48 and R51 are crucial for FE65-ELMO1 interaction as the interaction was markedly reduced by FE65 K48A/R51A double mutation. On the other hand, ELMO1 626-680 could not interact with FE651-217 in yeast two-hybrid assay. This suggests that amino acids 681 to 727 of ELMO1, which contain ELMO autoregulatory domain (EAD) and PXXP, are required for the interaction. We further demonstrated that ELMO1 M692A/E693A, within EAD, double mutation abolished the interaction between ELMO1and FE65 in the yeast two-hybrid and co-immunoprecipitation assays. Our previous study reveals the interaction between FE65 and the small GTPase ARF6. It has been suggested that ARF6 functions as an upstream regulator of ELMO1-Dock180-mediated Rac1 signaling, a process implicated in APP processing. However, the mechanism by which ARF6 associates with ELMO1-Dock180 to trigger this signalling remains elusive. FE65 has been shown to interact with both ARF6 and ELMO1 via its PTB1 domain and N-terminal region, respectively, we anticipated that FE65 serves as a hub to recruit ARF6 and ELMO1 and modulate Rac1 signaling. In GST-fusion protein pull-down and co-immunoprecipitation assays, FE65 potentiated the interaction of ARF6 and ELMO1. Together, our data suggests that FE65 functions, at least in part, to connect ARF6 and ELMO1 and form a tripartite protein complex. We also determined the regions in ARNO and FE65 that are responsible for their interaction. Deletion of the FE65 PTB2 domain abolished the FE65–ARNO interaction in pulldown assay using GST-ARNO as bait. The importance of the FE65 PTB2 domain was further confirmed by a co-immunoprecipitation assay in which FE65, but not FE65ΔPTB2, co-immunoprecipitated with ARNO. Using alanine screening mutagenesis, we found that the arginine 605 residue (R605) of FE65 was critical for the FE65–ARNO interaction, as the interaction was markedly weakened by an R605A mutation (FE65 R605A) as determined in a co-immunoprecipitation assay. Objective 2: FE65 has been implicated in amyloid precursor protein (APP) processing. FE65 interacts with the APP intracellular domain (AICD) and promotes APP processing. However, how FE65 controls APP processing is not fully understood. In the second part of this research, the possible roles of the FE65-ARNO interaction on APP processing were investigated. We demonstrated that FE65 promotes APP processing while ARNO and ARF6 inhibit APP processing. However, the stimulating effect of the ARNO-noninteracting FE65 mutant shows no substantial differences from the wild-type FE65. Moreover, the potency of FE65 stimulation on APP processing remains unaffected in the ARNO knockout cell line. These data suggests that the two proteins work independently on APP processing. Increasing evidence suggests that APP is also implicated in neurite development. Notably Aberrant neurites were observed in many neurodegenerative disorders including Alzheimer’s disease. As FE65 is an APP interactor and ARF6, ARNO and ELMO1 are implicated in Rac1 signalling which is an important process for neurite outgrowth, we enquired if their interactions with FE65 affect neurite outgrowth. In fact, FE65 potentiates the stimulatory effect of ARNO on ARF6-mediated neurite outgrowth, and the effect of FE65 is abrogated by an FE65 mutation that disrupts FE65–ARNO interaction. As stated above FE65 serves as a hub for ARF6 and ELMO1, allowing the formation of a multimeric signaling complex. Interestingly, interfering with the formation of this complex by transfecting either FE65-binding-defective mutants or FE65 siRNA attenuates both ARF6-ELMO1-mediated Rac1 activation and neurite elongation. Objective 3: Endosomal recycling is essential for membrane trafficking between the recycling endosome and the plasma membrane (PM). Endosome is a compartment for trafficking of APP and APP processing. Moreover, the PM is a compartment where ARF6 and/or ARNO regulate the dynamics of the cytoskeleton through Rac1 activation. We, therefore, enquired whether FE65 influences endosomal protein recycling. Notably, the PM trafficking of ELMO1 is markedly decreased in cells with suppressed expression of either FE65 or ARF6. Likewise, this process is attenuated in the FE65-binding-defective mutants transfected cells. Moreover, overexpression of FE65 increases the amount of ELMO1 in the recycling endosome, an organelle responsible for returning proteins to the PM, whereas knockout of FE65 shows the opposite effect. Together, our data indicates that FE65 potentiates ARF6-Rac1 signaling by orchestrating ARF6 and ELMO1 to promote the PM trafficking of ELMO1 via the endosomal recycling pathway. Furthermore, FE65 potentiates the stimulatory effect of ARNO on ARF6-mediated neurite outgrowth, and the effect of FE65 is abrogated by an FE65 mutation that disrupts FE65–ARNO interaction. Autoinhibition is a reported mechanism for regulating the activity of several families of GEFs. It usually involves an intramolecular interaction(s) in the GEF domain to hinder the access of the corresponding small GTPase. Cytohesin family proteins, including ARNO, have been shown to adopt autoinhibited conformation. Therefore, we determined whether FE65 alters the intramolecular association of ARNO. His-ARNO1-270 and GST-ARNO 271-399 fragments consisting of the CC + Sec7 + Sec7-PH linker and the PH + CtH/PBR domains, respectively, were expressed and purified from E. coli for GST-pulldown assays., GST-ARNO 271-399 pulled down ARNO 1-270. Of note, the interaction between the two fragments was significantly inhibited in the presence of the recombinant FE65 PTB2 domain, but not the FE65 PTB2R605A mutant. To confirm the above observation, PLAs were performed in cells transfected with myc-ARNO1-270 and GST-ARNO271-399. Fluorescent PLA signals were observed in the transfected cells, indicating the interaction between the two ARNO fragments. The number of PLA signals was reduced by approximately 40% in the cells co-transfected with FE65 but not FE65R605A (Fig 3B). Conversely, the association between the two ARNO fragments increased significantly in FE65 KO cells compared with wildtype cells (Fig 3C). Collectively, these findings indicate that the FE65–ARNO interaction plays a role, at least in part, in relieving ARNO autoinhibition. As the interaction of FE65 and ARF6 influences endocytic trafficking, we determined the mechanism by which the interaction is regulated. We found that FE65 serine 459 (S459) residue with the PTB1 domain is a target for PKCι/λ. FE65 phosphorylation has been shown to modulate the function of FE65 by altering binding to its interactors. As ARF6 is an FE65 PTB1 interactor and the binding of ARF6 to FE65 triggers neurite outgrowth, we postulated that FE65 S459 phosphorylation alters the FE65-ARF6 interaction. In a co-immunoprecipitation assay, the FE65–ARF6 interaction was markedly enhanced by the S459E phosphomimetic mutation. A similar result was observed in GST-pulldown assays, in which a recombinant GST-FE65 S459E bait pulled down more ARF6 than the wild-type protein. We further performed proximity ligation assays (PLAs) in which increased PLA signal counts were observed in cells co-transfected with ARF6+FE65 S459E compared with those transfected with ARF6+FE65.

14113618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113618.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that altered production of amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is crucial to AD pathogenesis. APP is also implicated in many physiological processes such as neurite outgrowth. Neurite damage and atrophy are observed in various brain injuries and neurodegenerative disorders including AD. FE65 is a brain-enriched “scaffold” protein that has been shown to interact with APP and influences APP metabolism/functions. Increasing evidence suggests the role of Rac1 signaling in regulating the functions of APP. In this study, we have identified two novel FE65 interacting proteins namely ARNO and ELMO1. To note, ARNO is a guanine exchange factor (GEF) for the small GTPase ARF6 that we have identified from a previous study. We have fully characterized the FE65-ARNO and FE65-ELMO1 interactions. Moreover, ARF6-FE65-ELMO1 and ARF6-FE65-ARNO multimeric complexes were detected. It has been long proposed that ARF6 activation stimulates Rac1 signaling through the ELMO1-DOCK180 complex, the association between ARF6 and ELMO1-DOCK180 complex was not known. Our findings reveal that the neuronal scaffold protein FE65 serves as a functional link between ARF6 and ELMO1 to activate Rac1 (publication 2 and 3 in part C). Likewise, we have found that FE65 potentiates the activation of ARF6 by ARNO. We have demonstrated that FE65 activates ARF6 by attenuating the autoinhibited conformation of ARNO (publication 4 in part C). We have also demonstrated that FE65 promotes APP processing while ARNO and ARF6 inhibit APP processing. However, the stimulating effect of the ARNO-noninteracting FE65 mutant shows no substantial differences from the wild-type FE65. Moreover, the potency of FE65 stimulation on APP processing remains unaffected in the ARNO knockout cell line. These data suggests that the two proteins work independently on APP processing. On the other hand, we have found that the multimeric complexes could stimulate neurite outgrowth. FE65 is found required for PM, a site for Rac1 activation, targeting of ARF6, ELMO1 and ARNO through the endosomal recycling pathway. Evidence suggests that FE65 functions can be regulated by phosphorylation including its interaction with its interactors. In order to understand, how FE65-ARF6 interaction is regulated, we have attempted to identify FE65 phosphorylation sites. In this study, we have identified FE65 S459 as PKCι/λ phosphorylation sites. Such phosphorylation potentiates FE65-ARF6 interaction and triggers neurite outgrowth (publication 5 in part C).

14113618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113618.value: In this project, we have explored the roles of the novel FE65 interactors in APP processing and neurite outgrowth. Our findings suggest a role of FE65 neurite outgrowth. Neurite damage and atrophy are observed in various brain injuries and neurodegenerative disorders. We attributed this stimulatory effect to the interaction of FE65 with ELMO1, ARF6 and/or ARNO. FE65 has been found to disrupt the autoinhibited conformation of both ELMO1 and ARNO. Thus, targeting these autoinhibited conformations by designed peptides derived from FE65 may stimulate Rac1-mediated neurite outgrowth. This strategy to stimulate neurite outgrowth may trigger the reconnection of injured neurons, consequently the recovery of the nervous system.

14113618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113618.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that the over-production of toxic amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is an important process for the disease. Moreover, damaged nerve cell structures namely neurites are commonly observed in AD. Recent studies have shown that the brain-enriched protein FE65 binds to APP to modulate the production of Aβ and influences neurite outgrowth. In this study, we have identified two new FE65 binding proteins namely ARNO and ELMO1. We have shown that both FE65 and ARNO affect APP processing. However, our data suggests that the two proteins work independently on APP processing. On the other hand, we have found that FE65-ARNO and FE65-ELMO1 interactions potentiate neurite outgrowth. Our findings lay a foundation for exploring the potential of triggering FE65-ARNO and FE65-ELMO1 mediated neurite outgrowth as a therapeutic approach for AD.

14114918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114918.value: In Hong Kong, 20% of adults with diabetes were diagnosed below the age of 40 years, with substantial heterogeneity in aetiology and disease trajectory. Type 1 diabetes is reliably distinguished from other subtypes by acute presentation with diabetic ketoacidosis and presence of auto-antibodies. However, it remains a clinical challenge to differentiate patients with young-onset type 2 diabetes from monogenic diabetes, due to commonalities in initial clinical presentation. Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) is the most frequently encountered group of monogenic diabetes and clinical course varies depending on subtypes of MODY. Notably, responses to treatment also differ and first-line glucose lowering drugs may not be appropriate. Early detection of MODY is therefore important to project clinical course, guide treatment, offer genetic counselling, and conduct screening. Despite strong clinical indications, MODY remains underdiagnosed. Conventional criteria based on age of presentation, parental history of diabetes and non-use of insulin have low sensitivity and specificity when used alone to select cases for genetic testing. Risk algorithms to identify high-risk cases for molecular testing have been developed in Caucasians but are not applicable to Chinese, in whom prevalence of MODY may differ and clinical phenotypes vary. Diagnostic confirmation requires sequencing of known MODY genes and Sanger sequencing, which analyses one gene at a time, has been the gold standard to identify putative mutation. Unlike Caucasian counterparts in whom mutations were found in up to 50% of young subjects with non-type 1 diabetes, detection rate is significantly lower at only 10% in matched Chinese population using traditional sequencing techniques. Next generation sequencing (NGS) is a revolutionary approach to uncover mutations in a larger pool of genes simultaneously, significantly enhancing detection rate. We postulate that the composition of genes causing monogenic diabetes differ between ethnic groups, and that NGS as a comprehensive test platform will uncover additional mutations in genes that were not previously implicated in Chinese. We propose to sequence a panel of monogenic diabetes gene using NGS in stored serum of a prospective cohort of 1,100 Chinese patients with diabetes diagnosed <40 years recruited between 2000-2012 with available information on baseline clinical variables including C-peptide and auto-immune status, and incident cardiovascular-renal events and mortality. We aim to estimate the prevalence of MODY and to characterise patients with MODY by their metabolic attributes and incidence of diabetes complications. We will also construct and evaluate performance of a Chinese-specific risk algorithm for prediction of MODY.

14115418.value: 研究背景：不明原因的反覆流產的流產物作為遺傳學研究的對象，能夠為我們解釋流產和胚胎停育的遺傳學原因。雖然目前染色體異常與反覆流產相關，這類病人中的平衡或非平衡異位或者致病性的拷貝數變異的發生率如何尚未得到全面的研究。我們通過前期研究已經證明了低深度全基因組測序檢測方法，可以應用於未存活或腐爛的組織樣本；這個方法可以同時檢測染色體非整倍體、微小的缺失和重複（稱為拷貝數變異，通常通過染色體微陣列芯片檢測）、平衡型染色體重排。染色體低深度全基因組測序技術與核型分析、染色體微陣列芯片分析相比，能夠獲得基因組的單鹼基突變信息與微小的插入缺失。對此類樣本進行低深度全基因組測序研究，能夠為確診致病性染色體異常的患者夫婦提供下一步干預的手段，如進行植入前基因診斷來提高生育率。 研究目標：旨在證明低深度全基因組測序在檢測流產組織的遺傳學變異上能夠優勝於傳統的核型分析。 研究方法：收集200個來源於反覆流產夫婦的流產組織，其核型分析結果正常，並應用已建立的低深度全基因組測序技術進行研究分析，最終結果將與其原始的常規核型分析進行比較分析。 預期研究結果與影響：通過此項目的研究，我們旨在（1）驗證在流產組織的產前診斷方面，低深度全基因組測序的臨床診斷效能；（2）研究反覆流產夫婦的流產組織中染色體異位的整體頻譜；（3）全基因組範圍研究流產組織中潛在的致病性變異。從此研究中，我們通過全基因組測序方法全面分析獲得的遺傳信息將從根本上協助對流產原因進行診斷，而獲知流產原因能夠有效的降低自責，同時評估下一次流產的概率並提供下一步干預的方案。我們本項研究的方案將為高效的應用低深度全基因組測序技術在臨床應用和基礎研究上提供一個經驗支持，從而能最大化的影響到香港地區的臨床應用機制和操作指南的指定與執行。

14115418.label: Realisation of objectives
14115418.value: With the funding from GRF, we have completed the tasks of applying 10-fold genome sequencing retrospectively for 200 products of conception from the couples with idiopathic recurrent miscarriage to (1). To study and validate the clinical utility of the low-pass whole genome sequencing technique on diagnosis of abortus; and (2) To identify the spectrum of chromosomal rearrangements among abortus from idiopathic recurrent miscarriages; and (3) To investigate the incidence and type of genomic variants (BCAs and CNVs) in the abortus. Overall, we achieved an average of 10.4-fold of genome sequencing for each sample and performed genomic variants analysis including point mutations (single-nucleotide variants [SNVs], and small insertions/deletions [InDels]), copy-number variants (CNVs) and structural rearrangements (SVs) with our inhouse analytical algorithms and pipelines. After data analysis, variant interpretation and confirmation of parental assignment, the results indicated there were 24% (48/200) cases with clinically significant (pathogenic, likely pathogenic) variants identified among these 200 products of conception. It includes 32 compound heterozygosity (SNVs+SNVs, CNVs+SNVs) or de novo SNVs in autosomal dominant disease-causing genes, 12 CNVs and 4 SVs. For instance: (1) Case 15C0069, miscarriage occurred at 10 gestational weeks, ultrasound indicated anencephaly. GS and data analysis indicated there was a 4bp small deletion in the donor site of splicing in exon 1 of gene LZTR1 ([GRCh37/hg19] chr22:g.21,337,379-21,337,380). In-silico prediction indicated a truncated mutation. Gene LZTR1 is known to cause Noonan Syndrome (http://omim.org/entry/600574) in an autosomal dominant manner. Sanger sequencing indicated the mutation was not presented in the parents confirming the de novo inheritance. (2) Case 17C0964, miscarriage occurred at 11+3 gestational weeks. GS and data analysis reported a G to C missense mutation in the 14th exon of gene TP63 ([GRCh37/hg19] chr3:g.189612055). Sanger sequencing confirmed a de novo inheritance. The incidence of this mutation in gnomAD was only 3.23144e-05, while SIFT and Polyphen predictions both indicated it was a pathogenic mutation. InterVAR data base based on ACMG guidelines also reported that it was a likely pathogenic mutation. OMIM databases revealed mutations in TP63 were strongly correlated with ADULT syndrome (https://omim.org/entry/103285), Ectrodactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip/palate syndrome 3 (https://omim.org/entry/604292), which might indicate the pathogenicity of this mutation and the miscarriage. (3) Case 17BA0296, first trimester miscarriage. CNV analysis reported a heterozygous deletion of 86kb in size in the terminal region of the q arm of chromosome 16: seq[GRCh37/hg19] del(16)(q24.3) chr16:g.89269040_89355182del. qPCR experiment confirmed the deletion occurred in de novo inheritance. Gene ANKRD11 was involved in the deletion and it has been reported to be likely haploinsufficient (https://www.nature.com/articles/ejhg2011105), resulting in KBG syndrome. Although KBG syndrome has been also reported in prenatal cases with multiple ultrasound anomalies (visible), further study is warranted to investigate how it contributed to the miscarriage. (4) Case 17C1690, first trimester miscarriage. CNV analysis identified a mosaic copy number gain with 1.5Mb in size in the q arm of chromosome 22 seq[GRCh37/hg19] dup(22)(q12.3) chr22.g. 35880201_37359631dup[0.4], the mosaic level of which was approximately 35%. qPCR confirmed it was a de novo event. There were multiple OMIM disease-causing genes involved including APOL1, MYH9, TXN2, CACNG2, IFT27, NCF4 and CSF2RB, while there were some cases with intellectual disabilities and with similar size of duplications reported in DECIPHER database. (5) Case 19C1493, first trimester miscarriage. Ultrasound examination indicated 7.11 mm nuchal translucency. Genome sequencing and data analysis reported a compound heterozygosity in gene DNAH11 including a heterozygous mutation in c.3020T>G (classified as pathogenic) and a heterozygous mutation in c.3470T>G (classified as VUS). Sanger sequencing confirmed both mutations were inherited from each of the parents. Gene DNAH11 is known to cause primary ciliary dyskinesia, further study is warranted to investigate the contribution to first trimester miscarriage. (6) Case 19C2255, first trimester miscarriage. A heterozygous deletion 103kb in size seq[GRCh37/hg19] del(10)(q26.3) chr10:g.128985159_129088977del and a 7kb heterozygous seq[GRCh37/hg19] del(10)(q26.3) chr10:g.129154690_129161792del were identified in the product of conception, both of them were locating in gene DOCK1. By qPCR, we confirmed the former deletion was from the mother, while the later cryptic deletion was from the father indicating a compound heterozygosity. Although DNA methylation was found in genes including DOCK1 in patients with recurrent miscarriage (PMID: 31938574), it is unclear how completely loss of function for this gene contribute to early pregnancy loss. The three objectives from the proposed project have been achieved successfully. However, we encountered some problems warranting for new proposal to further investigate: (1) Correlation of mutations identified in products of conception and the miscarriage: as described above, low-pass genome sequencing and data analysis with our inhouse pipeline have reported 24% additional clinically significant genomic mutations in cases with normal karyotype. However, the majority of current existing databases was established based on the data from paediatrics, adult diseases and to a lesser extent, prenatal cases. As such, many of these disease correlations are curated in conditions that are compatible with livebirth. Genetic mutations that are incompatible with livebirth and those that cause embryonic lethality may not be properly annotated and curated in these databases. This limits our investigation and correlation of how some of the genetic variants detected in this study contribute to the clinical consequence (miscarriage). Large-scale sample size might be warranted in future study to better correlate genetic findings to miscarriage. (2) Part of the variants were found to be in de novo manner. The possibility that some of them were contributed by germline mosaicism in one of the parents is still largely unknown. Further study might be warranted to investigate the contribution of germline mosaicisms in parents with a method of significant higher sensitivity of mutation detection (e.g. digital PCR) to investigate the genetic contributions from the parents. (3) RNA-seq study. Although in this proposal we didn’t propose to perform RNA-seq analysis, we performed RNA-seq in several cases with candidate mutations identified. However, due to fetal demise, the quality of RNA was poor in most of the cases. In addition, the genes interested were not expressed in the tissue sample. It might be a challenge to confirm expression changes via RNA-seq in products of conception. In future studies, we will use mouse models to create knock-in or knock-out the mutations as an alternative plan.

14115418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115418.value: In this study, low-pass genome sequencing and data analysis with our inhouse pipeline among 200 products of conception reported 24% additional clinically significant genomic mutations in cases with normal karyotype. Investigation of the presence of clinically relevant genomic variants among 200 abortuses from couples with recurrent miscarriage using low-pass whole genome sequencing revealed a spectrum of genetic abnormalities beyond aberrations that can be detected by karyotyping. This approach yielded 24% additional clinically significant findings in a cohort that had received negative results by conventional karyotyping. We demonstrated pathogenic and likely pathogenic mutations can be detected by low-pass whole genome sequencing across a broad spectrum of types of mutations which included SNVs, cryptic copy number variants, and structural rearrangements. Traditionally, different types of genetic variants required specific molecular tests. Genome sequencing showed its advantage by comprehensive delineation of compound heterozygosity of different types of genetic variants in a single test. Investigation of pathogenic/likely pathogenic mutations in abortuses is important because it identifies and establishes the genetic etiology. The parents can also be tested to accurately assess the recurrence risk in subsequent pregnancies. Having knowledge of the genetic etiology not only provides informed management options and prognostic information, but also provides potential reproductive options including prenatal genetic diagnosis in subsequent pregnancies, or preimplantation genetic testing and assisted reproductive technologies. We have translated our research findings into clinical practice by the implementation of a clinical genetic test based on this low-pass genome sequencing approach (ChromoSeq) at the CUHK Prenatal Genetic Diagnosis Laboratory for recurrent miscarriage couples and their abortuses

14115418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115418.value: Abortuses with high suspicion of underlying genetic etiologies but previously undiagnosed by low-pass whole genome sequencing may be of interest for further investigation by long-read genome sequencing to study genetic variants that may contribute to pathogenic consequences, particularly in regions of the genome that are inaccessible by limitations of short read sequencing. These include mutation in: regions with GC% bias, low or high complexity regions, repetitive elements, and repeat expansions. Long-read sequencing may also be used to phase cis and trans variants to resolve compound variants of different mutation types. This will enable us to better understand more about the advantages and disadvantages of low-pass WGS and to better guide clinical testing and management. Based on this dataset, we are applying for CRF grant the project title “Recurrent First Trimester Miscarriage: Genetic Etiology, Diagnosis and Prevention”

14115418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115418.value: We investigated the contribution of disease-causing genetic variants in a cohort of 200 abortuses from couples who experienced recurrent miscarriage using advanced genome sequencing technologies. We studied and identified a spectrum of genetic variants, including copy number variants, chromosome rearrangements, and single nucleotide variations in this cohort. Our approach detected an extra 24% clinically significant genetic variants which could explain the abortuses’ phenotype for miscarriage. Compared to conventional karyotype, low-pass genome sequencing significantly increased the genetic diagnostic rate in the genetic investigation of abortuses in couples with recurrent miscarriage. Our research findings led to the implementation of low-pass genome sequencing at our genetic diagnostic laboratory as a clinical service, for abortuses and couples with recurrent miscarriage.

14116218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116218.value: The prevalence of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), which is associated with heightened risks for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, is increasing in many Asian countries. The pathogenic mechanisms governing the progression from simple steatosis to necroinflammation in the liver are unclear, rendering limited therapeutic options for patients with NASH. Emerging studies have demonstrated the protective function of autophagy, a cellular self-cannibalistic process hallmarked by the formation of double-membrane autophagosomes, in NASH. Recently, we reported that endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress could inhibit lysosome acidification and autophagic flux to aggravate NASH. Our preliminary findings further suggest that, in a murine model of methionine-choline deficiency (MCD)-induced NASH, administration of the short-chain fatty acid butyrate could (i) reduce hepatic lipid accumulation and inflammation; (ii) restore lysosomal acidification, lysosomal enzyme activities, and autophagic flux; (iii) activate the transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master gene for lysosomal biogenesis. However, the molecular mechanism mediating the therapeutic effect of butyrate in relation to restoration of autophagosomal-lysosomal system in NASH has not been defined. Herein, we hypothesize that (1) butyrate could protect against NASH development in another murine model of NASH (i.e. insulin-resistant Alms1 mutant (foz/foz) mice fed with high-fat diet); (2) the butyrate receptors GRP41, GRP43 and/or GRP109A mediate the activation of TFEB and restoration of lysosomal activity to protect against NASH development; (3) normalization of autophagosomal-lysosomal impairment by butyrate would be accompanied by rectification of mitochondrial dysfunction and ER stress. Such therapeutic manipulation of the autophagosomal-lysosomal system by butyrate is expected to alleviate steatosis and necroinflammation in both murine models of NASH and thereby paving the way for clinical trials of butyrate on NASH in humans. The findings of this study are also expected to open up new therapeutic avenues by identifying novel druggable targets in the GRP41/43/109A-TFEB-autophagy pathway. 在許多亞洲國家，非酒精性脂肪性肝炎（NASH）的患病率正在增加，這與肝硬化和肝細胞癌的風險增加有關。控制肝臟中從單純性脂肪變性到壞死性炎症的進展的致病機制尚不清楚，為NASH患者提供了有限的治療選擇。新興研究已經證明了自噬在NASH中的保護功能，自噬是一種由雙膜自噬體形成的細胞自同化過程。最近，我們報導內質網（ER）壓力可以抑制溶酶體酸化和自噬通量加重NASH。我們的初步研究結果進一步表明，在甲硫氨酸 - 膽鹼缺乏（MCD）誘導的NASH的小鼠模型中，短鏈脂肪酸丁酸鹽的給藥可以 (i) 減少肝臟脂質積聚和炎症; (ii) 恢復溶酶體酸化、溶酶體酶活性和自噬通量; (iii) 激活轉錄因子EB（TFEB），這是製造溶酶體的主要調控基因。然而，我們尚未確定介導丁酸鹽治療NASH中自噬體 - 溶酶體系統恢復的治療效果的分子機制。我們假設 (1)丁酸可以預防另一種NASH模型的NASH發展 （即胰島素耐、受高脂飲食的Alms1突變體 (foz / foz）小鼠); (2) 丁酸受體GRP41，GRP43和/或GRP109A介導TFEB的活化和溶酶體活性的恢復，以防止NASH發展; (3) 丁酸鹽對自噬體 - 溶酶體損傷的正常化將伴隨線粒體功能障礙和ER應激的矯正。預期丁酸鹽對自噬體 - 溶酶體系統的這種治療性操作可減輕NASH的兩種鼠模型中的脂肪變性和壞死性炎症，從而為人體中NASH的丁酸鹽的臨床試驗的開展奠定根基。通過在GRP41 / 43 / 109A-TFEB-自噬途徑中鑑定新的可藥物靶標，預計此研究的發現也將開闢新的治療途徑。

Characterize the tumor-suppressive role of GGT7 in gastric cancer in vivo 1.1 GGT7 inhibits the growth of subcutaneous xenograft tumors in nude mice We subcutaneously injected BGC823 cells stably transfected with GGT7 or a control vector into the left and right dorsal flanks of nude mice, respectively. GGT7 markedly reduced tumor size (P<0.01) and weight (P<0.001) of BGC823 xenografts. GGT7 expression in xenograft tumors was confirmed by immunohistochemistry. In concordance with the in vitro findings, fewer proliferating cells were concomitantly detected by Ki-67 staining in GGT7-expressing xenografts as compared to controls (P<0.05). 1.2 GGT7 inhibits metastasis of gastric cancer cells to the lung in vivo We further assessed the effect of GGT7 on tumor metastasis in vivo. The BGC823 cells stably overexpressing GGT7 or transfected with control vector were injected through the tail vein of nude mice. After four weeks, histological examinations demonstrated that 100% (5/5) of the mice bearing control cells exhibited lung metastases, while only 20% (1/5) of the mice bearing GGT7-expressing cells showed lung metastasis (P<0.05). Moreover, the number of metastatic lesions was significantly fewer in GGT7 group than in control group (P<0.05). 2. Investigate the mechanisms underlying the tumor-suppressive role of GGT7 2.1 GGT7 dysregulated MAPK/ERK signaling cascade KEGG pathway enrichment analysis on RNA-sequencing data revealed that GGT7 significantly dysregulated steroid biosynthesis, endocytosis, MAPK signaling, cytokine-receptor interaction, metabolic pathways, and pathways in cancer. MAPK signaling has been reported to be associated with ROS. We further showed that GGT7 significantly inhibited MAPK activity in both BGC823 and AGS cells by luciferase SRE reporter assays (both P<=0.01), accompanied by decreased protein levels of p-c-Jun and p-ERK1/2, but not p-p38 or the total proteins of c-Jun, ERK1/2, and p38, as shown by western blot. 2.2 RAB7 is a direct effector of GGT7 In comparison of the co-IP products by GGT7 antibody and IgG, RAB7 and RAB1 were found to interact with GGT7 with the highest Mascot score and the most Matched queries by mass spectrometry. To validate the interaction between GGT7 and RAB7/RAB1, co-IP using GGT7 antibody and IgG followed by western blot using RAB7/RAB1 antibodies was performed in cells with GGT7 overexpression, and the results further confirmed the interaction of GGT7 with RAB7, while the interaction with RAB1 was not so strong as with RAB7. 2.3 GGT7 mediates the translocation of RAB7 from the nucleus to the cytoplasm GGT7 is mainly localized in the cytoplasm, and RAB7 is also localized in the cytoplasm and co-localized with GGT7 in cells stably overexpressing GGT7 by immunofluorescence staining under confocal microscopy. However, in cells without GGT7 expression, RAB7 was observed mainly in the nucleus or both cytoplasm and nucleus. We further found that the relative level of RAB7 (vs GAPDH) was significantly higher in the cytoplasm of GGT7-overexpressing cells, while the relative level in the nucleus (vs Lamin A/C) was significantly decreased with GGT7 expression by western blot. 2.4 The tumor-suppressive function of GGT7 is dependent on RAB7 We overexpressed GGT7 and/or knocked down RAB7 in AGS and BCG823 cells. GGT7 significantly suppressed cell growth of both cell lines (P<0.05), while when RAB7 was knocked down, the growth-suppressing effect of GGT7 was diminished. Moreover, GGT7 significantly decreased clonogenicity (all P<0.05). The extent of decrease in clonogenicity by GGT7 was smaller in cells with RAB7 knockdown compared to those without RAB7 knockdown in both cell lines (P<0.05). 2.5 GGT7 promotes autophagy/mitophagy and protects against oxidative stress GGT7 was not effective on cell apoptosis by flow cytometry. Transmission electron microscopy revealed an increased number of autophagic vacuoles in GGT7-overexpressing cells. Considering the crosstalk between ROS and autophagy/mitophagy, we examined the effect of GGT7 on oxidative stress. Cells were treated with an ROS inducer, and then intracellular ROS was measured using the DCF-DA oxidation kit on a flow cytometer. The results showed that GGT7 expression significantly inhibited induction of ROS in AGS and BGC823 cells (both P<0.0001), suggesting a protective effect against oxidative stress. 2.6 GGT7 promotes mitophagy In concordance with increased autophagy, increased LC3-I-to-LC3-II conversion and decreased level of the autophagy substrate SQSTM1/p62 were detected in GGT7-overexpressing cells by western blot. GGT7 induced LC3B accumulation and a decrease of SQSTM1/p62 by confocal fluorescence microscopy. We further transfected a tandem mCherry-GFP-tagged LC3 expression vector into cells to monitor autophagy flux. GGT7 increased mCherry signals without GFP, indicative of acidified autophagosomal structures. No increase in Atg5 or Atg12 was observed. Increased levels of BNIP3, BNIP3L, PINK1, and Parkin were detected in cells with stable GGT7 overexpression by western blot. Further confocal fluorescence microscopy showed obvious upregulation of BNIP3 (with specific accumulation in the cytoplasm) and BNIP3L by GGT7 overexpression. 3. GGT7 was significantly downregulated in gastric tumors as compared to their matched adjacent non-tumor tissues at both mRNA and protein levels (both P<0.0001). 14116418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116418.value: Functionally we demonstrated that GGT7 played an important tumor-suppressive role in suppressing gastric tumor growth and inhibiting tumor metastasis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, we elucidated that GGT7 recruited RAB7 by direct binding and drove RAB7 to translocate from nucleus to cytoplasm, subsequently mediating mitophagy by increasing mitophagy mediators/inducers. GGT7 further inhibited intracellular ROS via the increased mitophagy, and subsequently suppressed MAPK signaling. Regarding clinical significance, we demonstrated that down-regulation of GGT7 in adjacent non-tumor tissues is associated with metastasis. The expression of GGT7 in adjacent non-tumor tissues is an independent predictor for survival of patients with gastric cancer. The research outputs of this project include publication of a peer-reviewed research article in Oncogene, an oral presentation invited to the Distinguished Abstract Plenary of Digestive Disease Week (the most prestigious meeting in the world for GI professionals) on May 23, 2021,training of two PhD students and three undergraduates, and awards at international conferences, new collaborations with national and international collaborators, etc.

14116418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116418.value: GGT7 protein expression in adjacent non-tumor tissues, but not primary tumors, was associated with a favorable prognosis of gastric cancer patients independently of their clinicopathological features. A commercial test based on the detection of GGT7 protein, such as immunohistochemical staining using FFPE blocks, can be developed for clinical application to predict patient prognosis. GGT7 may also serve as a promising therapeutic target, by activating which could induce mitophagy so as to prevent gastric tumorigenesis or improve patient outcomes.

14116418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116418.value: We demonstrated that gamma-glutamyltransferase 7 (GGT7) was mainly downregulated by promoter methylation in gastric cancer, while genetic alterations including copy number change contributed to <5% of cases. GGT7 methylation inversely correlated with its expression. High-expression of GGT7 in adjacent non-tumor tissues was significantly associated with favorable survival in gastric cancer patients, and was an independent prognostic factor. GGT7 significantly inhibited gastric cancer cell growth, G1-S transition, and migration and invasion abilities. GGT7 also significantly attenuated the growth of subcutaneous xenograft tumors and reduced metastasis to the lung in nude mice. The mitophagy regulator RAB7 was identified as a direct downstream co-player of GGT7. Growth suppression effect of GGT7 was dependent on RAB7. GGT7 induced autophagy as shown by electron microscopy and confirmed by autophagy markers (LC3B and p62). GGT7 recruited RAB7 by direct binding and drove RAB7 to translocate from nucleus to cytoplasm, subsequently mediating mitophagy by increasing mitophagy mediators/inducers. GGT7 inhibited intracellular ROS, which was associated with increased mitophagy, and subsequently suppressed MAPK signaling. Collectively, GGT7 plays a pivotal tumor-suppressing role in gastric cancer by binding with RAB7 to induce mitophagy and inhibit ROS and MAPK cascades. GGT7 is an independent prognostic factor for gastric cancer patients.

14116918.label: Realisation of objectives
14116918.value: Three objectives were proposed in the original proposal. For AIM 1, we developed a computational framework for predicting key TFs using the specific type of hotspots namely super-enhancers (SEs), a subset of enhancers with clusters of key TFs, and other key regulators marked by the epigenetic marks such as H3K27ac et al.. Using this framework, we successfully identified a distinct list of key TFs in the early stages of SC fate transition and ex vivo tested selected key TFs in AIM 2. For AIM3, we experimentally screened the predicted key TFs using in vivo CRISPR mediated editing. The detailed progress is summarized below: AIM 1: To develop a computational framework for predicting TF hotspots and key TFs In this aim, we have developed a pipeline to predict key TFs regulating SC lineage progression by using integrated gene regulatory networks involving a specific subset of TF hotspots called SEs, and their downstream interacting promoters and gene. In the pipeline, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data were used in the SE identification and key TF inference. AIM 2: To establish TF hotspot atlas and identify key TFs regulating SC lineage progression To establish TF hotspots atlas defined by the SEs, we performed H3K27ac ChIP-seq in freshly isolated SCs (FISCs) from Pax7-nGFP mice and activate SCs (ASCs) cultured in growth medium for 24 hrs. We applied a slightly modified ROSE algorithm to define SEs in both FISCs and ASCs leading to the identification of a total of 57 and 163 SEs, respectively. By using the computational framework implemented in AIM1, We predicted 12 auto-regulated TFs, among which 10 were determined as key TFs based on the activity and expression level of each candidate; the list includes Pax7, Runx1, Mef2d, Cebpb, Klf9, Sox4, Esr1, Six1, Bcl6 and Rora. Similarly, in ASCs, a total of 11 key TFs including Pax7, Tgif1, Runx1, Nfix, MyoD, Six1, Cebpb, Myc, Nfia, Pknox2,and Bcl6 were defined. To test the functions of the selected key TFs ex vivo, we picked up 6 TF candidates based on their expression levels and known relevancy in muscle cells, including Myc, Bcl6, Rora, Esr1, Pknox2, Sox4. To test the functionality of these key TFs, we employed loss-of-function assays by siRNAs in cultured SCs. To this end, FISCs from Pax7-nGFP mice were cultured for two hrs followed by transfecting of siRNAs against each TF. Knockdown of Myc, Bcl6 or Pknox2 led to reduced EdU incorporation thus the delay of SC activation, which however was not observed in the cases of Rora, Sox4 or Esr1 knockdown. Together, our data suggested that Myc, Bcl6, Pknox2 may potentially play a role in SC activation. AIM 3: To experimentally screen key TFs using in vivo CRISPR mediated editing To establish a versatile in vivo platform that allows muscle restricted genome editing, we crossed homozygous Cre dependent Rosa26Cas9-EGFP knockin mouse with a Pax7Cre mouse and the resulting progenies were referred to as Pax7Cas9 mice. After obtaining the above mouse expressing Cas9 in SCs, we sought to test if it can be used for gene editing of the identified TFs in SCs in vivo. As a proof-of-concept, the MyoD gene was selected due to the wealth of knowledge of its functions in SC as a master TF orchestrating myogenic program. To deliver the sgRNA in vivo, AAV9 virus was employed because it displays tropism to skeletal muscle and allows transgene expression during a long period of time. The AAV9-sgMyoD plasmid was packed into virus and intramuscularly (IM) injected into the Pax7Cas9 mice at postnatal day 10 (P10). Our results demonstrated the Pax7Cas9/AAV9-sgRNA system can be used for effective gene editing in SCs in vivo. Although the application of single sgRNA exhibited high efficiency in editing MyoD locus, several studies have demonstrated that simultaneous use of dual sgRNAs could induce indel as well as large deletion at target loci to further enhance editing efficiency. We thus developed an AAV9-dual sgRNA system expressing two sgRNAs from a single vector. Using MyoD as a paradigm, our findings demonstrated the dual sgRNAs editing system yielded higher editing efficiency than single sgRNA. We also tested if it is possible to edit QSCs. However, our results demonstrated that the in vivo CRISPR/Cas9/AAV9 system failed to induce efficient genome editing at the MyoD locus in QSCs. After the above in-depth evaluation of the performance of the CRISPR/Cas9/AAV9 mediated genome editing at MyoD locus, we next employed this system to study the key TF functions in SC quiescence maintenance and activation. Our findings demonstrated the critical requirement of Myc for proper muscle regeneration after acute injury. To further solidify the usefulness of our system in editing TFs and studying their functions in vivo, we also applied it to Bcl6 and Pknox2 which led to distinct effects on SC activation and muscle regeneration.

14116918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116918.value: Skeletal muscle satellite cells (SCs) are adult muscle stem cells responsible for injury induced muscle regeneration. Despite advances in the knowledge of molecular mechanisms regulating SC lineage progression, our understanding of key transcription factors (TFs) and their regulatory functions in SCs in particularly the quiescent and early activation stages remains incomplete due to the lack of efficient method to screen and investigate the stage-specific key TFs. In this study, we succeeded in defining a distinct list of key TFs in early stages of SC fate transition using the paradigm of super enhancers (SEs). Particularly, leveraging the Cre-dependent Cas9 knockin mice and AAV9 mediated sgRNAs delivery, we generated a facile muscle specific genome editing system which allows gene depletion in SCs in vivo. Using MyoD locus as a proof of concept, we demonstrated that this CRISPR/Cas9/AAV9-sgRNA system can efficiently introduce mutagenesis at target locus and recapture the phenotypes reported in knockout mice. Further application of the system on key TFs, Myc, Bcl6 and Pknox2, revealed their distinct functions in the early stage of SC activation and damage induced muscle regeneration. Altogether our findings have proven the CRISPR/Cas9/AAV9-sgRNA system as a robust way for in vivo genome editing and elucidation of key factors governing SC activities.

14116918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116918.value: Of note, our recent in vivo genome editing system has several limitations. One caveat is that the AAV9 administration can also edit muscle fibers. Since Pax7 expression emerges as early as embryonic day 10.5 (E10.5) in the muscle progenitor cells to drive the formation of muscle compartments, Cas9 is expressed not only in SCs but also fibers in Pax7Cas9 mice. We attempted to solve this problem by using inducible Pax7ER-Cas9 mice that will allow SC restricted expression of Cas9 but the results were not compelling at the current stage. So it will be interesting to generate a facile platform for edting quiescent muscle stem cell in vivo. Second, this system does not generate a uniform knockout mouse. Although the transduction efficiency appeared to be close to 100%, the editing efficiency per SC and the editing events largely varied, leading to mosaic mutagenesis. Mosaic editing for some genes, for example, Pknox2, may not be sufficient to elicit any phenotypical alterations, in which case the traditional knockout models are needed to confirm the findings. So it is necessary to further improve the editing efficiency in the future.

14116918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116918.value: In this study, we defined distinct lists of key TFs in SC lineage progression particularly in the early stage of SC quiescence and activation. With the help of the Cre-dependent Cas9 knockin mouse and AAV9 mediated sgRNA delivery, we created a muscle specific in vivo genome editing system. Using MyoD locus as a proof of concept, we demonstrated that this CRISPR/Cas9/AAV9 system can efficiently introduce mutagenesis at target TF locus and reduce its expression in SCs. Further application of the system on Myc, Bcl6 and Pknox2 revealed their distinct functions in the early stage of SC activation and damage induced muscle regeneration. Overall, this system manifests several advantages. First, compared with commonly employed transgenic and gene knockout-based models that necessitate significant investment of both time and resources, our approach can accelerate the pace at which gene function and interactions can be interrogated in SCs in vivo. In addition to coding genes, it is also possible to interrogate non-coding genome such as enhancers and lncRNAs, therefore further expanding the application of this system. Another interesting fact is that Cas9 expression is present at birth in Pax7Cas9 mouse and the administration of AAV9 virus at P10 enables the investigation of postnatal myogenesis.

14117418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117418.value: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a major cause of chronic kidney disease but treatment remains no specific and ineffective. We and other investigators have recently identified that M1 macrophages play a pivotal role in AKI; however, treatment for AKI by targeting macrophages remains yet to be developed. A novel and surprising finding from our preliminary study was that the neuropeptide Y (NPY) plays a protective role in AKI by switching the inflammatory M1 macrophages to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. We found that NPY was primarily produced by resident immune cells including macrophages/dendritic cells (DC) in the normal kidney, which was lost in ischemia-reperfusion-injury (IRI) and cisplatin cytotoxic-induced AKI. Treatment with NPY restored the NPY-producing cells and therefore protected kidneys from cisplatin and IRI-induced AKI. In contrast, blockade of NPY signaling with the Y1 receptor antagonist largely promoted AKI. Mechanistically, our preliminary results found that NPY was downregulated on macrophages by LPS or TNFa via the NF-kB-dependent mechanism. In contrast, NPY acted via its receptor Y1 to inhibit LPS-induced NF-kB-Mincle-Syk signaling and proinflammatory cytokine production by switcing the M1 macrophages to the M2 phenotype. Based on these preliminary observations, we hypothesize that the NPY-neuroimmunity axis occurs in the kidney and may play a protective role in AKI. Modulating this axis may represent as a novel and specific therapy for AKI. We plan to test this hypothesis in IRI and cisplatin–induced AKI by 4 Specific Aims. 1) We will first characterize the expression profile of NPY and its receptors in both normal and AKI kidneys, peripheral blood, and urine. 2) We will then investigate the functional role and therapeutic potential of NPY for AKI in NPY knockout (KO) mice and in AKI mice treated with NPY and/or the Y1 receptor antagonist. 3) The specific role of macrophage/DC-derived NPY in AKI will be determined by adoptive transfer of NPY KO or overexpressing macrophages. 4) Finally, the counter-regulatory mechanisms of NPY in renal inflammation and M1 macrophage activation via the NF-kB-Mincle-Syk circuit will be investigated in vivo and in vivo. We expect that results obtained from this study will be for the first time to identify and establish the NPY-neuroimmunity axis in AKI, to detect the protective role and regulatory mechanisms of NYP in AKI, and to develop a novel and specific therapy for AKI by modulating this axis with NPY. Thus, the outcomes from this study will be highly significant both scientifically and clinically. 急性腎損傷（AKI）是慢性腎病的主要原因，但治療仍然沒有特異性和無效。我們初步研究發現神經肽Y（NPY）通過滅活M1巨噬細胞在AKI中起保護作用。我們發現NPY主要由正常腎臟中的常駐免疫細胞產生，包括巨噬細胞/樹突細胞（DC），其在缺血 - 再灌注損傷（IRI）和順鉑誘導的AKI腎中喪失。用NPY治療恢復了產生NPY的細胞並保護腎脏免於順鉑或IRI誘導的AKI。相反，用Y1受體拮抗劑阻斷NPY信號傳導阻止了NPY的保護作用，從而大大促進了AKI。在機理上，我們的初步結果發現NPY通過其受體Y1抑制LPS誘導的NF-kB-Mincle-Syk信號和促进M1轉換為M2巨噬細胞表型而抑制炎症。基於這些初步觀察，我們假設腎臟NPY-神經免疫軸可能在AKI中起保護作用。調節該軸可能是AKI的新型療法。我們計劃通過4個特定目標在IRI和順鉑誘導的AKI中檢驗這一假設。 1）明确NPY及其受體在正常和AKI腎臟以及外周血中的表達譜。 2）在NPY敲除（KO）小鼠研究NPY在AKI的保护作用， 并探讨NPY或Y1受體拮抗劑治療AKI的作用。 3）阐明NPY防治AKI的机制。 我们拟通過NF-kB-Mincle-Syk信号通路在體內和體內研究NPY在AKI和M1巨噬細胞活化中的反調節機制。 本研究结果將首次在AKI建立NPY神經免疫軸在AKI中的保護作用和調節機制。 我们期待，应用NPY调节NPY神經免疫軸可能是防治AKI的新方法。因此，本研究的結果在科學和臨床上都具有重要意義

14117418.label: Realisation of objectives
14117418.value: We have successfully completed all 3 objectives of this study with several novel findings. 1) We found that NPY was constitutively expressed in blood, urinary, and resident kidney macrophages by co-expressing NPY and CD68+ markers in normal human and mice, which was lost in patients and mice when AKI was developed, and macrophages became activated with M1 phenotype. This was further confirmed in vitro that more than 80% of NPY-expressing were bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) but was lost in response to LPS stimulation. This novel observation provided the first evidence for involvement of immunologically-derived NPY in AKI. In addition, we also found that NPY was not expressed by renal tubular epithelial cells, which argues against the previous report that kidney tubular cells can expressed NPY. Thus, we concluded that macrophages are a major source of NPY-expressing cells in physiologic conditions, however, it is lost when AKI developed and macrophages became activated. These observations suggest that in contrast to never-derived NPY, macrophage-derived NPY may be protective in AKI. 2) A novel and most significant finding from this study is that NPY plays a protective role in AKI and is a novel therapeutic agent for AKI. This was demonstrated in two mouse models of AKI induced by cisplatin or ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) in which mice lacking NPY developed much more severe AKI with worsening tubular necrosis and renal dysfunction when compared to NPY WT mice. In contrast, treatment with exogenous NPY was able to dose-dependently inhibit AKI by improving renal dysfunction and tubular necrosis. Results from these experiments clearly demonstrated that NPY is protective in AKI and is a novel therapeutic agent for AKI. 3) Mechanistically, we uncovered that NPY protected kidney from AKI by inactivating M1 macrophages via the Y1R-NF-κB-Mincle-dependent mechanism. This was supported by the findings that a loss of NPY in NPY KO mice and BMDMs inhibited Y1R but increased in NF-κB-Mincle signaling, resulting in overactivation of M1 macrophages (F4/80+iNOS+Mincle+ cells) and the development of severe necroinflammation in AKI. In contrast, addition of NPY to the AKI mice and LPS-stimulated BMDMs was capable of dose-dependently upregulating Y1R signaling, thereby blocking NF-κB-Mincle-mediated M1 macrophage activation and expression of proinflammatory cytokines, which was reversed by silencing NPY in LPS-stimulated BMDMs. More importantly, Targeting Y1R signaling with addition of a Y1R antagonist BIBP3226 was able to block NPY-induced upregulation of Y1R signaling, thereby enhancing NF-κB-Mincle-mediated M1 macrophage activation and renal necroinflammation in AKI mice and in vitro. Furthermore, the regulatory role for Mincle on M1 macrophage activation was further confirmed by silencing Mincle to inhibit LPS-induced M1 macrophage activation and expression of proinflammatory cytokines. Taken together, we can conclude that NPY signals through the Y1R to exert its inhibitory effect on M1 macrophage-mediated AKI by blocking NF-κB-Mincle signaling.

14117418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117418.value: There are several novel findings from this study. 1) In contrast to previous finding that neuropeptide Y (NPY) is produced by the nerve system, in this study, we found that NPY can be produced by blood and resident kidney macrophages in normal human and mice. However this is lost when macrophages become activated with M1 phenotype in patients and mice with acute kidney injury (AKI), which is also confirmed in bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM). This novel observation provided the first evidence for the immunologically-derived NPY in AKI. 2) A novel and most significant finding from this study is that NPY plays a protective role in AKI and is a novel therapeutic agent for AKI. In two mouse models of AKI induced by cisplatin or ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI), mice lacking NPY develop much more severe AKI with worsening tubular necrosis and renal dysfunction. In contrast, treatment with exogenous NPY is able to dose-dependently inhibit AKI. Thus, NPY plays a protective role in AKI and is a novel therapeutic agent for AKI, which is contradictory to previous reports that the never-derived NPY is harmful in patients with chronic kidney disease. 3) We also uncovered that NPY protects kidney from AKI by inactivating M1 macrophages via the Y1R-NF-κB-Mincle-dependent mechanism. This was supported by the findings that mice and BMDM lacking NPY can impair Y1R but increase NF-κB-Mincle signaling, resulting in M1 macrophage-mediated necroinflammation in AKI. All these changes are reversed by addition of NPY but become worse by blocking Y1R signaling with a Y1R antagonist BIBP3226. Thus, we conclude that NPY signals through the Y1R to exert its inhibitory effect on M1 macrophage-mediated AKI by blocking NF-κB-Mincle signaling. All these findings have just been accepted by Int J Biol Sci (Research Output #1) and have also resulted in a successful HMRF grant application to study the role of NPY in acute myocardial infarction as published in Molecular Therapy (2022;30:881-897). Furthermore, the novel finding of macrophage-derived neural property has also resulted in the new discovery of neural transcription factor Pou4f1 in progression of kidney disease by regulating macrophage-myofibroblast transition (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2020;117:20741-20752). Totally, 16 publications and two institutional collaborations associated with this project have been obtained as indicated in Part C Research Output.

14117418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117418.value: The major finding in this study is that NPY is renoprotective and has therapeutic effect on AKI, which is highly significant clinically. However, the vasoconstriction caused by NPY may also induce ischemic renal injury if it is long-term use, particularly in CKD patients with sympathetic hyperactivity. This challenges the application of NPY in AKI on CKD patients. Thus, the clinical application by using NPY as a therapeutic agent for AKI remains to be determined.

14117418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117418.value: In contrast to previous findings that neuropeptide Y (NPY) is produced by the nerve system and contributes to the progression of chronic kidney disease, the present study found that NPY is constitutively produced by blood and resident kidney macrophages, but this is lost when macrophages become activated with proinflammatory phenotype in patients and mice with acute kidney injury (AKI). The new and most significant finding from this study is that NPY is protective in AKI and has therapeutic effect on AKI. This is strongly supported by the findings that mice lacking NPY develop worse renal necroinflammation in cisplatin and ischemic-induced AKI. In contrast, treatment with exogenous NPY dose-dependently inhibits AKI by largely improving tubular necrosis and renal failure. Mechanistically, we uncovered that NPY functions to protect kidney from AKI by inactivating M1 macrophages via the Y1R-NF-κB-Mincle-dependent mechanism. In conclusion, we identify that NPY plays a protective role in AKI and may be a novel therapeutic agent for AKI. Thus, findings from this study are highly significant both scientifically and clinically.

14118118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118118.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an important cancer in mainland China and Hong Kong, with most patients presented with metastasis and relapse, and very low 5-y survival rate (~20%). Molecular study to understand its metastasis and pathogenesis is urgently needed, in order to develop better biomarkers and therapeutic strategy. Cancer is caused by abnormities of multiple cancer genes inactivated/or activated by genetic and/or epigenetic alterations. These alterations play important roles in tumor initiation and progression, via causing aberrant cell signaling regulation including Ras signaling. In normal cells, finely-tuned RAS signaling is important to normal cell physiology, critically involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)/cell stemness, cell cytoskeleton and migration. Aberrantly activated RAS signaling is frequently detected in most cancers including ESCC, which could be caused by hyperactive Ras mutations. However in ESCC, Ras mutations are rarely detected, highlighting the importance of epigenetic disruption of Ras signaling balance in ESCC pathogenesis. Through epigenome study previously, I identified a novel Ras-GTPase-activating protein (RasGAP), RASAL3, as a methylated and downregulated target in ESCC. RASAL3 is a very recently identified gene with homology to known RasGAPs like RASAL1 which we studied before. I further found RASAL3 to be frequently methylated and downregulated in ESCC cell lines and tumors, while low RASAL3 level was correlated with poorer survival of cancer patients. Thus in this proposal, I propose to further study its epigenetic and genetic alterations in ESCC cell lines and primary tumors, and examine its function as a potential RasGAP antagonizing Ras signaling cascade. I will also examine its functions and mechanisms in regulating ESCC cell proliferation and apoptosis, EMT/stemness, cell cytoskeleton and metastasis. I will determine the association of methylation and expression of RASAL3 with ESCC patient clinical features and tumor EMT marker, to develop RASAL3 methylation as an epigenetic biomarker for ESCC. Through this study, I will elucidate the molecular functions and epigenetic mechanism of aberrant activation of RAS signaling related to the metastasis of ESCC, and develop potential epigenetic biomarker to benefit ESCC patients.

14118118.label: Realisation of objectives
14118118.value: In this project, through epigenome study, we identified a novel Ras-GTPase-activating protein (RasGAP), RASAL3, as a methylated and downregulated target in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We further found RASAL3 to be frequently methylated and downregulated in ESCC cell lines and primary tumors, but rare in normal esophageal epithelial cells. Pharmacological (using Aza or combined with TSA) restored RASAL3 expression, along with increased unmethylated promoter alleles, indicating that methylation directly mediates its repression in tumors. RASAL3 promoter methylation was further confirmed by bisulfite genomic sequencing (BGS). CGI methylation played a dominant role in RASAL3 silencing and deletion played a partial role. Importantly, low RASAL3 level was correlated with poorer survival of ESCC tumor patients. RASAL3 was validated to be a typical RasGAP, and regulates RAS activity and its downstream signaling through the RasGAP activity. Ectopic expression of RASAL3 inhibited tumor cell proliferation and induced apoptosis. We also found that RASAL3 overexpression suppressed cell metastasis by inhibiting EMT and stemness, further disrupting the cell cytoskeleton of ESCC. Interestingly, reduction of RASAL3 expression co-occurred with RAS mutation, and RASAL3 showed unexpected roles that it suppressed tumor growth and RAS downstream signaling in tumor cell lines that contained not only wild-type but also mutant RAS. Ectopic expression of RASAL3 suppressed remaining wild-type RAS activity in tumor cells harboring RAS mutations. Thus, our study identified RASAL3 as a new suppressive RasGAP, highlighted the expanding role of RasGAPs and supplied a new sight into the therapeutic strategy for overcoming RAS-driven cancer. All the proposed objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. The results obtained directly from this project have been described in our publications/manuscripts listed below. Overall, the findings from this project have provided a significant understanding of the contribution of regulating tumor cell invasion/metastasis and EMT/stemness by a new Ras antagonist which is silenced by CpG methylation in esophageal cancer.

14118118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118118.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an important cancer for mainland China including Hong Kong, with metastasis and recurrence as the major cause of patient death. Molecular mechanistic studies (including epigenetics) on its metastasis pathogenesis are urgently needed. Our study will provide new insights into the critical role of Ras signaling in the regulation of ESCC metastasis and recurrence, through epigenetic inactivation of a novel Ras antagonist RASAL3 by promoter CpG methylation silencing. Moreover, the tumor-specific methylation of the RASAL3 promoter could serve as an epigenetic biomarker for ESCC diagnosis and prognosis prediction, benefiting the patients in China including Hong Kong and the world.

14118718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118718.value: It is estimated that 16.9% of pregnancies globally are affected by hyperglycaemia, with total burden of around 21 million births affected per year. Furthermore, younger onset of diabetes means an increasing proportion of women of reproductive age are now affected by diabetes. It is well known that offspring born to mothers with diabetes or gestational diabetes have increased risk of obesity, diabetes and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) later in life. Epigenetic modification of fetal gene expression has been suggested to contribute to this persistent phenotypic change following transient exposure to intra-uterine hyperglycaemia. In a pilot project, we have demonstrated persistent epigenetic changes up to 15 years in offspring of mothers with gestational diabetes. In this proposal, we aim to extend this observation by undertaking a genome-wide search for methylation changes after maternal hyperglycaemia, using a unique collection of samples. We aim to identify and validate a panel of differentially methylated markers in cord blood from offspring born to mothers with untreated gestational diabetes from the Hyperglycaemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome (HAPO) Study, for which we have already completed detailed metabolic evaluation at age 7. Epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) will be performed to identify differentially methylated loci and regions in cord blood DNA in offspring with or without exposure to intrauterine hyperglycaemia. Validation and replication of the identified methylation markers will be performed using i) an alternative method to evaluate methylation in the same cohort; ii) independent samples available from the HAPO study; iii) a prospective Chinese GDM cohort from Tianjin, China. Association between the novel methylation markers at birth and adiposity and cardiometabolic trait in childhood will be examined, in conjunction with available genotyping information and additional expression profile from collected placenta and cord tissue already available. Relationship between the identified marker and maternal glycaemic parameters will be quantified. Biological function of the identified genes will be explored using bioinformatics approaches utilising available data, as well as readily available dataset of methylation and gene expression changes in subcutaneous and visceral fat to highlight key regulatory pathways perturbed by intra-uterine hyperglycaemia. Finally, we plan to incorporate the epigenetic markers into prediction models of future risk of childhood obesity. This comprehensive and systematic evaluation of differentially methylated sites associated with GDM should uncover important pathways in fetal programming of future adiposity. This will provide a new approach and new tools to help predict and prevent the current epidemic of diabetes and obesity. 據估計，全球有16.9％的妊娠婦女有高血糖症，影響每年約2100萬新生兒。此外，年輕的糖尿病發病率增加，意味著越來越多的育齡婦女將會受到糖尿病的影響。眾所周知，患有糖尿病或妊娠糖尿病的母親所生的後代在以後的生活中肥胖，糖尿病和其他非傳染性疾病（NCD）的風險均增加。胎兒基因表達的表觀遺傳修飾已被認定有助解釋短暫母胎內高血糖後導致胎兒各種持續的表型變化。在一個試點項目中，我們證實了母親患有糖尿病的後代的表觀基因變化持續可長達15年或以上。 在本研究項目中，我們旨在通過使用獨特的樣本，對母體高血糖症進行全基因組範圍內的甲基化變化來擴展這一研究。我們計劃鑑定和驗證來自高血糖和不良妊娠結局（HAPO）研究的未被治療妊娠糖尿病母親所生的後代臍帶血中搜索甲基化標記差異。我們將進行表觀基因組範圍的關聯研究（EWAS）以鑑定後代臍帶血DNA中甲基化位點和區域的差異。我們將 1）以替代方法驗證同一群組中的甲基化變化，2）使用HAPO研究提供的獨立樣本; 及 3）利用來自中國天津的妊娠糖尿病樣本以進行甲基化標記物的驗證和確認。我們將檢查出生時的甲基化標記和兒童時期的肥胖和心臟代謝特徵之間的關聯，並結合已收集的胎盤和臍帶組織的基因表達譜和基因分型信息。表觀基因標誌與母體血糖值的關係將被量化。並使用生物信息學方法利用現有數據探索已鑑定基因的生物學功能，以及皮下和內臟脂肪中甲基化和基因表達變化的現成數據集，以突出由子宮內高血糖症擾亂的關鍵調節途徑。 最後，我們計劃將這些表觀基因標記納入未來兒童肥胖風險的預測程式中。這項全面與有系統性評估妊娠糖尿病相關的甲基化差異位點的研究項目中，應該能夠揭示編程胎兒未來肥胖的重要途徑，並提供新方法和新工具，以幫助預測和預防糖尿病和肥胖症。
