14118818.label: Realisation of objectives
14118818.value: We hypothesized that (1) enteric neural progenitors (ENPs) can be induced from mouse induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and (2) enteric neurons can be generated from ENPs after transplanted to the gastrointestinal tract of the Dominant megacolon mutant (Dom), an animal model of Hirschsprung’s disease with congenital gastrointestinal motility disorder. To determine the feasibility of using ENPs in the autologous cell transplantation therapy, we proposed to first correct the mutant gene sequence in iPSCs derived from the Dom mutant before iPSCs were induced to form ENPs (Objective One), then establish a protocol to induce ENPs from mouse iPSCs (Objective Two), and finally assess the ability of iPSC-derived ENPs to form enteric neurons in the gastrointestinal tract (Objective Three). All three objectives have been fully achieved. Objective One: To correct mutant Sox10 sequence in iPSCs using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (a) Reprogramming of mouse skin fibroblasts to iPSCs: Mouse skin fibroblasts isolated from E13.5 wild type (Sox10+/+) and homozygous Dom (Sox10Dom/Dom) embryos were reprogrammed to iPSCs with retroviral transduction of four Yamanaka transcription factors (Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc). iPSCs exhibited embryonic stem (ES) cells-like morphology, and expressed pluripotent stem cell markers Sox2, Oct3/4 and SSEA-1 after immunofluorescence localization and qPCR. Their pluripotency was confirmed by the formation of teratoma containing derivatives of three germ cell layers in non-obese-severe combined immunodeficiency (NOD-SCID) mice. (b) In silico design, construction and transfection of both guide sequences targeting the mutant Sox10 sequence and donor templates for gene correction into iPSCs from the Sox10Dom/Dom mutant: Four guide sequences and donor templates carrying the normal Sox10 sequence were designed in silico, constructed for targeting the Sox10 mutation site, and cloned individually into vectors. (c) Determination of Cleavage efficiencies with T7EI: Two days after transfection of Cas9-sgRNA-Puro into Sox10+/+ and Sox10Dom/Dom iPSCs, transfected cells were selected with puromycin and genomic DNA extracted. The genomic DNA sequence surrounding the sgRNAs targeting sites was amplified for the T7EI assay. sgRNA-1, 2 and 3 showed higher indel efficiencies, so they were selected for subsequent experiments. (d) Gene correction with homology-directed repair (HDR): Both Cas9-sgRNA-1/2/3-GFP and donor plasmids were transfected into Sox10Dom/Dom iPSCs, and genomic DNA was extracted from FAC-sorted GFP-positive cells. The average HDR efficiency was found to be 23.05%. Eight of the 42 clones showed both alleles corrected whereas 4 clones showed one allele corrected. (e) Corrected sequence confirmed by Sanger sequencing: Sequencing results confirmed that the corrected sequence in the 8 homozygous and 4 heterozygous clones. (f) Analysis of off-target activities: The off-target cleavage activities were analyzed with the online CRISPR Design Tool which computationally predicted off-target sites for each sgRNA guide sequence. 3 clones showed the lowest number of off-target sites and all of them did not have any known functional implication, so these three clones were used in subsequent experiments. In summary, mutant skin fibroblasts were successfully reprogrammed to iPSCs which were gene-edited by CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Three iPSC isogenic cell lines carrying the corrected Sox10 sequence in both alleles (Sox10Cor/Cor iPSCs) with minimal off-target activities were established. Objective two: To establish a protocol to induce formation of enteric neural progenitors from iPSCs in vitro (a) Modification of the three-step to two-step induction protocol: After painstaking trials with different culture conditions in vitro, we developed a three-step induction protocol which included (1) neurosphere formation from iPSCs, (2) emigration of cells from neurospheres, and (3) expansion of emigrated cells. To monitor the induction process, we examined at different induction stages the morphologies of induced cells, expression of neural crest markers (during normal development, neural crest cells form the enteric neural progenitors) including Sox10, p75, nestin, Ednrb, FoxD3, AP-alpha2, Snail and Slug with immunofluorescence staining and/or qPCR, migration abilities in vitro and developmental potentials in different differentiation culture media. Eventually, we established the optimal induction medium containing epidermal growth factor, fibroblast growth factor, retinoic acid, BMP4 and a Wnt pathway activator, and most importantly, simplified the induction protocol to two steps: (1) neurosphere formation and (2) expansion of neurospheres. Three induced ENP cell lines were established: Sox10+/+ENPs, Sox10Dom/DomENPs and Sox10Cor/CorENPs (gene corrected) with induction efficiencies at 60%, 11% and 18%, respectively. (b) Characterization of induced enteric neural progenitors: The induced ENPs were characterized with immunofluorescence staining and qPCR for marker gene expression, wound healing and Boyden migration assays, directed differentiation assays for neurogenic, osteogenic, chondrogenic and myogenic potentials, time-lapse live cell imaging for studies of migration speed, directionality and migration behaviors in vitro and transcriptomic profiling with RNA sequencing. The characteristics of induced ENPs were compared with those of E8.5 vagal neural crest cells (i.e. embryonic enteric neural progenitors). Expression of critical marker genes within the neural crest gene regulatory network (e.g. Tfap2a, Ednrb, Sox10, id2, Snail1, Arpc1b, nestin, Bmi1), cell markers of neural crest subtypes (e.g. Ets1, Lhx5, Tbx2, Rarb/g, Hes6, Moxd1, Prox1) and a whole range of Hox genes (marker genes of the neural crest at different axial levels) were examined with immunofluorescence staining and qPCR. Bioinformatic analyses with transcriptome datasets from induced ENPs and vagal neural crest cells were performed. Our findings showed that the two-step protocol was able to induce ENPs from mouse iPSCs. In summary, a two-step induction protocol was established to induce formation of ENPs from wild type iPSCs, mutant Sox10 iPSCs and gene-corrected Sox10 iPSCs in vitro. Objective three: To assess the development of iPSC-derived enteric neural progenitors following transplantation to the hindgut explants cultured ex vivo (a) Ex vivo gut explant culture: Small agarose blocks of 5 mm3 were prepared to serve as holding platforms for gut explants. Hindgut segments were dissected from E13.5 Dom (Sox10+/+, Sox10Dom/+ and Sox10Dom/Dom) embryos and fixed with fine tungsten needles to the agarose blocks for organ culture. The expression of various cell markers of enteric neurons, glia and muscles indicated that the development of the gut explants ex vivo was normal for up to 7 days. (b) Cell transplantation to the gut explants: Fibroblast-reprogrammed iPSCs from Dom mice were labelled with GFP using CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in technology, whereas primary vagal neural crest cells were isolated from B6/EGFP mouse embryos where all nucleated cells were genetically labelled with GFP. GFP-labelled iPSCs were then induced to form GFP-labelled ENPs before cell transplantation by microinjection to normoganglionic, hypoganglionic or aganglionic region of the gut explants. GFP-labelled vagal neural crest cells were also transplanted for comparison purposes. About 4000 cells in less than 0.1 microliter PBS were microinjected with a hand-held micro-aspirator tube fitted with a microcapillary pipette under a high-power stereomicroscope. (c) Cell migration and differentiation of transplanted cells ex vivo: At different time points after cell transplantation, the embryonic gut explants cultured ex vivo (up to 5 days) were examined for (i) the gradual cellular changes of transplanted ENPs and vagal neural crest cells within the gut tubes including migration distances, directionalities and speeds and cell morphology, distribution and organization with special attention to any possible formation of tumor tissues; and (ii) the expression of various markers of enteric neural crest cells (p75, Ret, Sox10, Ednrb and Phox2b), neurons (PGP9.5, TuJ1, NOS, HuC-D, ChAT), glia (B-FABP, GFAP), mitosis (PH3) and muscle (SMA). In summary, an ex vivo embryonic gut explant system was established, and GFP-labelled ENPs and vagal neural crest cells were successfully transplanted to the normoganglionic, hypoganglionic and aganglionic regions of the gut explant. The migration and differentiation of transplanted cells were monitored at different time points with live cell imaging and immunofluorescence localization.

14118818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14118818.value: Autologous transplantation of patient-derived iPSCs (induced pluripotent stem cells) could be a personalized treatment option where patient’s own cells are used for transplantation to reduce the risk of immune rejection. In this study, as a proof-of-principle experiment, the Dominant megacolon mouse mutant (Dom) was used as an animal model to investigate the feasibility of using iPSCs in the cell therapy for Hirschsprung’s disease, a common congenital gastrointestinal motility disorder in newborn babies with regional absence or reduction of enteric neurons in the distal colon. Skin fibroblasts from the Dom mutant were first reprogrammed into iPSCs where the mutant Sox10 was then corrected with CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing before iPSCs were induced to form enteric neural progenitors (ENPs) for cell transplantation to gut regions with missing neurons. Our results showed that skin fibroblasts from 3 different genotypes (Sox10+/+, Sox10Dom/+and Sox10Dom/Dom) were successfully reprogrammed with four Yamanaka factors (Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) to iPSCs which possessed stem cell characteristics in vitro and in vivo. To correct the mutant Sox10 in iPSCs with CRISPR/Cas9, guide RNAs and donor templates carrying the normal Sox10 sequence for homology-directed repair were designed in silico, cloned into vectors, and transfected to Sox10Dom/DomiPSCs. Eight homozygous clones with both alleles corrected and 4 heterozygous clones with one allele corrected were identified, and eventually three iPSC lines with the corrected Sox10 were established. Sox10+/+iPSCs, Sox10Dom/DomiPSCs and Sox10Cor/CoriPSCs (iPSCs with the corrected sequence) were then induced with a two-step protocol to form ENPs which were further characterized by a multitude of bioassays including morphological assessments, live-cell imaging, migration and multipotency assays, expression profiling with qPCR and RNA sequencing, and bioinformatic analysis. Induced ENPs showed characteristics of vagal neural crest cells which are the embryological origin of enteric neurons, indicating that induced cells were very likely to be ENPs. Induced ENPs were then examined for their migration and differentiation abilities after transplanted to the embryonic gut explants cultured ex vivo. When they were transplanted to the gut region with normal neurons/ganglia (normoganglionic), they formed intricate neuronal network with the recipient’s enteric neurons, but however, they were not able to form normal neuronal network in hypoganglionic or aganglionic gut regions despite that they could still form enteric neurons. Our results indicated that both transplanted iPSC-derived ENPs (cell autonomous effect) and recipient’s gut microenvironment (non-cell autonomous effect) play roles in the formation of normal neuronal network after cell transplantation to the gut.

14118818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118818.value: 1. The present study showed that differentiated skin fibroblasts could be reprogrammed to iPSCs and that iPSCs could be induced to form enteric neural progenitors (ENPs) which were able to form enteric neurons after transplanted to the embryonic gut explant. However, the gut explant culture was an ex vivo system which did not have a blood supply and an immune system. For cell therapy, induced ENPs should be transplanted to the mutant’s distal colon with absence or reduction of enteric neurons. This in vivo experiment was proposed in the original application, but because of the budget and time constraints, this part was removed after revision. Our follow-up studies with in vivo transplantation showed that ENPs in hypoganglionic or aganglionic regions could still form subtype neurons (e.g. ChAT and nNOS neurons) but neuronal network was defective. These important data will be combined with the findings from the present study for publication in a high-impact journal. 2. As recipient’s gut microenvironment also plays roles in the neuronal network formation, single cell transcriptome datasets for normoganglionic and hypoganglionic/aganglionic gut regions should be generated and compared to identify molecules/genes that are important for the normal network formation so as to improve the transplantation outcome.

14118818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118818.value: One of the most promising applications of stem cells is to replace damaged or lost cells in the body, and transplantation of patient’s own cells could be a personalized treatment option to evade immune rejection. Using an animal model, the present study aimed to show in principle the application of stem cell transplantation in patients with Hirschsprung’s disease, a common congenital gut motility disorder in newborn babies with missing neurons in the colon. Our results showed that skin cells from the animal model could be reprogrammed to stem cells which could then be gene-edited and induced to form progenitor cells with potentials to form neurons in the gut. When these progenitor cells were transplanted to the normal gut tube isolated from the animal model and grown in a culture medium, the transplanted cells were able to form neurons closely associated with the recipient’s normal neuronal network. However, when they were transplanted to gut regions with reduction or absence of neurons, the neuronal network formation was abnormal, implicating that the diseased gut could also affect the neuronal network formation after cell transplantation. This also implicated that to treat the congenital disorder, the diseased gut should also be modified before cell transplantation.

14119518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119518.value: Understanding on retaining the broad differentiation propensity of early embryos in cell culture is fundamental in stem cell research and critical to development of technologies that are required for robust expansion of stem cells. Totipotency refers to the unique cellular property observed in early embryos, exampled by mouse zygotes and 2-cell embryos, which can support broad differentiation to both embryonic and extraembryonic lineages. While the pluripotent embryonic stem cells (ESC) derived from late blastocysts have been successfully established in culture conditions and supported extensive research on complex pluripotency network, understanding on totipotency and its regulatory mechanism still remains very limited. Interestingly, rare totipotent-like cells have been observed among mouse ESCs cultured with GSK3b and MEK inhibitors (termed 2i). Furthermore, recent intensive single-cell RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis has uncovered broad heterogeneity among cultured mouse ESCs. These provide excellent opportunities to capture the totipotent-like cell state in vitro. We have initiated a research work to identify totipotency-associated genes, through gene co-expression analysis using published mouse ESC single-cell RNA-seq data. Very interestingly, we identified a distinct co-expressed gene module which is highly correlated to totipotency. This module contains 188 lincRNAs and 263 protein coding genes, which include several previously reported 2-cell stage markers. Furthermore, our bioinformatics analysis revealed that these genes display distinct transcriptional and epigenetic features which highly resemble the characters of totipotency genes. These results suggest that we have successfully identified a large number of totipotency-related genes, many of which are lincRNAs. In this project, we propose to further study these previously uninvestigated totipotency-related lincRNAs. We aim to use both in vivo and in vitro models to dissect their functions and gain insights into totipotency mechanisms. We will first validate the expression of candidate lincRNAs in 2i-ESCs and mouse early embryos using qRT-PCR and RNA-FISH technology. Furthermore, we will assess their roles in mouse early embryo development as well as in reconstituting totipotency in cultured cells, through gain/loss-of-function analyses. We will utilize our well-established platforms including lentivirus production, CRISPR technology and microinjection to conduct our proposed experiments. We believe our data generated through this research will establish lincRNAs as novel totipotency regulators. Our results will lead to better understanding on totipotency and underlying molecular mechanisms. In the long-run, it will have significant impact on establishment of totipotent stem cells in culture and development of regenerative medicine to a more advanced level.

14119518.label: Realisation of objectives
14119518.value: Long non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) are emerging as important regulators during the very early stage of embryonic development of mammals, controlling the totipotency and pluripotency properties in blastomeres. However, many lincRNAs remain unidentified. Mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and epiblast stem cells (EpiSCs) are derived from mouse early embryos and maintain different pluripotency properties in culture. To identify and investigate the functional roles of lincRNAs in regulating pluripotency, we carried out this research and present a large discovery of novel lincRNAs, from ab initio assembly of 15 high-depth transcriptome datasets generated in mouse ESCs and EpiSCs. Among the 5995 candidate lincRNAs, 75.7% were detected among mESC single-cell RNA-seq data, showing expression correlation with known genes and forming 43 co-expression modules. Further analysis of these lincRNAs and co-expression modules yielded important findings listed below. 1. Our study found that lincRNAs could be divided into two classes, with and without transposable elements (TEs), which implicate their distinct evolution and functions. The lincRNAs discovered from mESC and EpiSC transcriptome data showed a general enrichment of all types of TEs among the newly identified lincRNAs, with ERVK and LINE-L1 elements showing significantly higher enrichment than others. Analysis of the ChIP-seq data in previous publications further revealed the extensive binding of ERVK-type lincRNAs by the core pluripotency transcription factors, Oct4 and Nanog, suggesting that these ERVK-type lincRNAs may play specific roles in regulating pluripotency. 2. The study identified several co-expression modules and clusters of lincRNAs, and Gene Ontology (GO) analysis based on known genes in co-expression modules revealed distinct enrichment of specific functional terms in individual modules, as well as in clusters/sub-clusters. Among the four major clusters of lincRNAs, Cluster-A was composed of three sub-clusters, each showing moderate to strong association with specific GO terms related to mRNA processing, energy metabolic process, and cell cycle/mitosis control. Cluster-B contained two sub-clusters highly associated with Erk and TGFβ signaling, chromatin organization, DNA replication, trophectoderm development, and naïve-to-primed pluripotency state transition. Cluster-C was associated with histone/protein acetylation, stem cell maintenance, and blastocyst development, and Cluster-D was weakly expressed in 2i and largely silenced in a2i/serum conditions, with genes specifically expressed in 2-cell stage embryos. 3. The specific functions of the co-expression modules and clusters of lincRNAs identified in the study provide insights into the roles of lincRNAs in regulating pluripotency and totipotency properties. In particular, the novel lincRNAs identified in sub-cluster A3 of Cluster-A are strongly associated with specific GO terms related to cell cycle and mitosis control, mRNA processing, and energy metabolic process. These lincRNAs are likely to play roles in regulating the proliferation and differentiation of stem cells, which could have implications for stem cell research and regenerative medicine. The lincRNAs identified in sub-cluster B1 of Cluster-B are highly associated with Erk and TGFβ signaling, suggesting their involvement in the control of cell fate and differentiation. The lincRNAs identified in sub-cluster B2 are associated with specific GO terms related to trophectoderm development and naïve-to-primed pluripotency state transition. These lincRNAs could play a role in regulating the differentiation of embryonic stem cells into different cell types, which could have implications for the development of new therapies for diseases that involve pluripotent stem cells. The lincRNAs identified in Cluster-C are associated with specific GO terms related to histone/protein acetylation, stem cell maintenance, and blastocyst development. These lincRNAs could play a role in regulating the maintenance of pluripotency and the early stages of embryonic development. The lincRNAs identified in Cluster-D are weakly expressed in 2i and largely silenced in a2i/serum conditions, with genes specifically expressed in 2-cell stage embryos. These lincRNAs could play a role in regulating the totipotency property of 2-cell stage embryos. 4. This study aimed to identify and investigate the functional roles of lincRNAs in regulating pluripotency and totipotency properties. The unique co-expression module ES-M17 in Cluster-D highlighted a significant finding related to totipotency regulation. The module ES-M17 consisted of 106 novel lincRNAs, 82 annotated lincRNAs, and 263 protein-coding genes. The module exhibited high and specific expression at the 2-cell stage of mouse embryos, followed by a rapid decrease and persistent repression in later stages. Further analysis of the expression profiles of lincRNAs in module ES-M17 using single-cell RNA-seq data collected during preimplantation development of mouse embryos revealed distinct and prominent activation of ES-M17 lincRNAs in the 2-cell stage mouse embryos, confirming their association with totipotency state. Previous research on totipotency markers has identified several genes associated with the totipotent state, including Zscan4, Tcstv1, and Dux. The study's findings on lincRNAs in module ES-M17 add to this body of research by identifying a novel set of lincRNAs specifically expressed at the 2-cell stage of mouse embryos, which is a critical stage for totipotency. These lincRNAs are then confirmed to be associated with several previously reported totipotency markers, including Zscan4f, Zfp352, Abcb5, Tcstv1, Tcstv3, and Cml2. The study's findings also provide new insights into the regulation of totipotency. The identification of a unique co-expression module ES-M17, consisting of novel lincRNAs associated with totipotency markers, suggests that lincRNAs may play a significant role in regulating totipotency and early embryonic development. Collectively, we have completed the proposed project objectives, and the outcome of this research has yielded important and interesting findings that provided new insights into the roles of lincRNAs in regulating pluripotency and totipotency properties and could have implications for stem cell research and regenerative medicine.

14119518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119518.value: In this research, we investigated into ab initio assembly of 15 high-depth transcriptome datasets generated in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and epiblast stem cells (EpiSCs), and presented a large discovery of novel lincRNAs related to pluripotency and totipotency regulations. Among the 5995 candidate lincRNAs identified, 75.7% were detected among mESC single-cell RNA-seq data, showing expression correlation with known genes and forming 43 co-expression modules. Distinct functional potentials uncovered in individual co-expression modules are highly consistent with their epigenetic features and binding patterns by key pluripotency factors. Interestingly, two groups of novel lincRNAs were found to be closely associated with cellular states representing recently recognized naïve pluripotency or totipotency, and single-cell transcriptome data in preimplantation mouse embryos verified the specific enrichment of totipotency-lincRNAs at the 2-cell stage. Hence, our study provides wealthy information to elucidate functions of lincRNAs and mechanisms controlling mammalian pluripotency, and yielded manuscript ready for submission. In order to delineate the functions of the newly discovered lincRNAs, we also explored the CRISPR technologies that can be used to introduce loss-of-function effect of lincRNAs and published a review article on the recent findings regarding the expending CRISPR toolbox and technologies, as well as their impactful applications in biomedicine (Wang et al., J Cell Mol Med. 2020; 24:3256-3270). An extended effort in summarizing the potentials of CRISPR technologies in clinical applications and recent updates of gene therapy technologies yielded another review article published in 2021 (He et al., J Mol Med. 2021; 99, 593–617). One postdoc (Dr WANG Yaofeng) and Two PhD students (MA Xun graduated in 2019; DAI Liujiang graduated in 2021) were trained during this research. The student’s work also contributed to the construction of new CRISPR targeting systems and generation of human and mouse embryonic stem cell lines that carried the knockout of β-catenin, E-cadherin, JUP, or TCF family factors, and knock-in of fluorescence reporters (unpublished). These cells provided important tools to study the molecular mechanism underlying the lineage formation of definitive endoderm (DE), an important prevenient stage during embryonic development, which revealed new insights into the regulatory function of WNT/β-catenin signaling at the early differentiation and further clarified that it is the transcriptional regulation mediated by the nuclear activity of β-catenin playing essential role. The study on this topic yielded another manuscript ready for submission.

14119518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119518.value: LincRNAs are emerging regulators of totipotency and pluripotency property, and their transcriptions undergo drastic changes alongside the rapid cell fate transition and differentiation process. However, many of the LincRNA remains unidentified and their expressions and functions during early differentiation have not been fully understood. Recent studies employed the high-throughput single cell sequencing technology to investigate and map the cell fate changes and lineage specification during early embryonic development of mouse and human, which yielded a wealthy data that can provide an excellent resource for discovery of novel LincRNAs and studying their expression changes. Hence, we will continue the study and seeking for collaboration with scientists in Guangzhou Institute of Biomedicine and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences and Guangzhou Laboratory, who have documented studies on mapping the early lineages of mouse and human embryos. Potentially, a research proposal on the collaboration work will be submitted to RGC-NSFC joint scheme in the next round of exercise.

14119518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119518.value: Our study identified two classes of lincRNAs, with and without transposable elements (TEs), which imply their distinct evolution and functions. This finding could help researchers better understand the regulation and evolution of non-coding RNAs, which could further our understanding of the functional and evolutionary aspects of the genome. Furthermore, totipotency refers to the unique cellular property observed in early embryos, exampled by mouse zygotes and 2-cell embryos, while has not been successfully recapsulated in culture and its regulatory mechanism still remains poorly understood. Our finding on lincRNAs in the distinct co-expression module, ES-M17, add to the limited existing research on totipotency a novel set of lincRNAs, which specifically expressed at the 2-cell stage of mouse embryos and associated with previously reported totipotency markers, including Zscan4f, Zfp352, Abcb5, Tcstv1, Tcstv3, and Cml2. This finding provides new insights into the regulation of totipotency and suggests that lincRNAs may play a significant role in regulating totipotency and early embryonic development. Overall, the study's findings on lincRNAs could have significant implications for our understanding of gene regulation, evolution, and functional genomics, as well as for stem cell research and regenerative medicine.

14120118.label: Realisation of objectives
14120118.value: Milestone 1: Characterize the phenotype of joint articular cartilage and subchondral bone, compare the functional properties of chondrocytes and bone marrow-derived MSCs in Smad3- and Smad7-deficient mice. The research work of milestone 1 has been finished. From the results, we found that intact Smad7-deficient (KO) mice showed spontaneous cartilage degeneration changes including lower unmineralized cartilage/mineralized cartilage (UC/MC) ratio (p < 0.01), higher MMP13 expression in the cartilage, and subchondral bone hardening (higher BV/TV, p < 0.05) at 6 months, when comparing with those of wild type controls. We also found that intact Smad3-deficient (KO) mice have different phenotype in the articular cartilage, showing reduced cartilage thickness (significantly lower UC/MC ratio, p < 0.01) and degenerative changes (MMP13) mainly on the articular cartilage surface rather than the whole cartilage, comparing to the wild type mice at 6 months. However, there is no significant change in the subchondral bone structure. The chondrogenic differentiation potentials of the BM-MSCs isolated from Smad7-deficient (Smad7 KO) and Smad3-deficient (Smad3 KO) mice at 6-month-old were both impaired, showing lighter stain of Safranin O in the cell pellets after 21d of culture, and lower expression of chondrogenic markers (Sox9, Col2a1, and Aggrecan) as determined by qRT-PCR, when compared to the BM-MSCs of the wild type (WT) mice. In addition, we have generated a cartilage-specific Smad7 knockout mice through crossbreeding of Collagen2a1-CreERT2 and Smad7-flox mice. We have obtained several breeding pairs of Smad7-flox mice, the genotype is confirmed. We have also measured the cartilage phenotype in the Smad-7 cartilage conditional KO mice. Collagen2a1-driven Smad7 conditional knockout mice were generated through intraperitoneal injection of 60 mg/kg per mice for 5 days continuously for 8-week-old male mice, which were generated from crossbreeding between Smad7-flox and Collagen-2a1-CreERT2 mice according to the following protocol as shown below. After treatment with Tamoxifen, we found that cartilage matrix was impaired in the Smad-7 cKO mice at 4 weeks, showing lighter stain of Safranin O and more MMP13 expression. At 14 weeks, more significant OA phenotype was observed in the Smad-7 cKO mice. These results suggest that Smad-7 chondrocyte-specific knockout mice display OA-like phenotype. Smad7 cKO mice may become a spontaneous OA animal model for future research. Milestone 2: Perform sequencing analysis of chondrocytes to identify the key downstream genes that may regulate chondrocyte homeostasis in Smad3- and Smad7-deficient mice. Based on the sequencing analysis, we have performed some verification studies to identify the potential targets for OA therapy. We demonstrated that long intergenic non-coding RNA regulator of reprogramming (linc-ROR) plays an important role in chondrogenesis processes. Linc-ROR expression pattern in articular cartilage tissue sample from OA patients were studied by real-time PCR. Linc-ROR lentivirus mediated BMSCs were constructed and in vitro/ in vivo MeHA hydrogel encapsulated BMSCs cartilage formation activity were studied. Results showed that Linc-ROR was down-regulated in articular cartilage tissue from OA patients and was positively correlated with the expression level of SOX9 (R2 = 0.43). Linc-ROR ectopic expression significantly promoted in vitro BMSCs chondrogenesis and in vivo cartilage formation activities as revealed by safranin O, alcian blue and COL II staining. (Osteoarthritis and Cartilage. 2021). In our previous studies, we found that miR-378 repressed BMSCs osteogenesis and bone regeneration. We have also investigated the role of miR-378 in OA progression and its potential as a target of OA treatment. Upon in vitro OA induction, miR-378 expression was upregulated and correlated with elevated inflammation and chondrocyte hypertrophy. Chondrocytes isolated from articular cartilage from miR-378 TG mice showed impaired chondrogenic differentiation. These results suggested that miR-378 amplified OA development via repressing chondrocyte autophagy, thus indicating miR-378 may be a potential therapeutic target for OA treatments (Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2022). Milestone 3: Examine the effects of Smad3 activator, Smad7 activator, or combined treatment in modulating cartilage degenerative changes in Smad3- and Smad7-deficient mice with or without surgery-induced OA model. We have finished an animal study to test of effect of Asiatic acid (AA, Smad-7 activator) on OA progression and development. We confirmed that Asiatic acid attenuates OA development in the OA mice model. The surgery-induced OA animals were treated with AA (which is a potential regulator of TGF-β signalling and activator of Smad-7) or saline for 6 weeks. Result showed that, significant bone lost was seen in the OA animals comparing to the sham group (-38.1% in BV/TV, p < 0.001). Interestingly, AA treatment efficiently inhibited abnormal bone remodelling within the subchondral bone, whereas OA mice exhibited a higher BV/TV (-15.3 % in BV/TV, p < 0.001). Moreover, results of the IHC staining showed that Ostrix expression was suppressed in the OA subchondral bone (87.7%, p < 0.001) in the AA treatment group comparing to the non-treatment group. AA treatment significantly promoted the expression of Osterix (+67.6%, p < 0.001). (European Journal of Pharmacology. 2021). Safranin O & fast green staining result indicated an obvious cartilage degradation characterized by significantly higher OA scores (0.25 vs 16.125, P < 0.001) as well as higher expression level of MMP13 (0.375 vs 23.5, p < 0.001) and Col X (17 vs 94.5, p < 0.001) in the articular cartilage of OA group compared to the sham-operated group at week 6 post-operation. However, the systemic application of AA significantly retarded the articular cartilage degeneration in OA animals (16.125 vs 5.25, p < 0.001). IHC staining result showed that AA significantly inhibited expression of MMP13 (23.5 vs 2.375, p < 0.001) and Col X (94.5 vs 18.125, p < 0.001). These results indicate a protective effect of AA on cartilage and adjunct tissues including the synovium in OA animal model. (European Journal of Pharmacology, 2021). Furthermore, based on our previous finding on the protective effect of asiatic acid on cartilage, we also observed the effect of TGF-β1 in the Smad-7 cKO mice (4 weeks treatment). The 3D reconstruction images of subchondral bone indicated that Smad-7 cKO mice have a more dense bone structure when compared with a control group, while the TGF-β treatment decreased the bone mass. On the other hand, histological staining showed there were more hypertrophic chondrocytes on the cartilage surface after 4 weeks of Tamoxifen treatment. An even worse cartilage quality (cartilage destruction) and higher OARSI score were observed within Smad-7 cKO mice with the TGF-β treatment group, which indicates an obvious OA phenotye in the cartilage.

14120118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120118.value: We have the following major findings through this study: 1.We found that intact Smad7-deficient (KO) mice showed spontaneous cartilage degeneration changes in the whole articular cartilage. We also found that intact Smad3-deficient (KO) mice have different phenotype in the articular cartilage, showing reduced cartilage thickness and degenerative changes (MMP13) mainly on the articular cartilage surface. The chondrogenic differentiation potentials of the BM-MSCs isolated from Smad7-deficient (Smad7 KO) and Smad3-deficient (Smad3 KO) mice at 6-month-old were both impaired. 2.We have also constructed a Smad-7 cartilage conditional KO mice. Results suggest that Smad-7 chondrocyte-specific knockout mice display OA-like phenotype. Smad7 cKO mice may become a spontaneous OA animal model for future research. 3. We demonstrated that long intergenic non-coding RNA regulator of reprogramming (linc-ROR) plays an important role in chondrogenesis processes (Linc-ROR promotes mesenchymal stem cells chondrogenesis and cartilage formation via regulating SOX9 expression. Osteoarthritis and Cartilage. 2021). We also identified miR-378 amplified OA development via repressing chondrocyte autophagy, thus indicating miR-378 may be a potential therapeutic target for OA treatments (MicroRNA-378 contributes to osteoarthritis by regulating chondrocyte autophagy and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell chondrogenesis. Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2022). 4. We also identified Asiatic acid (AA, Smad-7 activator) as a ptential therapeutic small molecule which attenuates OA progression and development (Asiatic acid protects articular cartilage through promoting chondrogenesis and inhibiting inflammation and hypertrophy in osteoarthritis. European Journal of Pharmacology, 2021). We also observed a deteriorated effect of TGF-β1 in the Smad-7 cKO mice. In summary, the proposed project has been finished smoothly and significant research progress and output have been made accordingly to the proposed plans. A total of ten peer reviewed SCI-indexed articles have been published with the support from this funding. Most of the papers are published in journals with high reputation, including Osteoarthritis and Cartilage, Bone and Joint Research, Mol Ther Nucleic Acids, etc. Two PhD students (Dr. Yang Zhengmeng and Dr. Lin Weiping) have been trained and graduated from CUHK.

14120118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120118.value: We have generated a cartilage-specific Smad7 knockout mice through crossbreeding of Collagen2a1-CreERT2 and Smad7-flox mice. Our preliminary results suggest that Smad-7 chondrocyte-specific knockout mice display OA-like phenotype. Smad7 cKO mice may become a spontaneous OA animal model for future research. In addition, this Smad7-flox mice can be used to generate osteoclast-specific knockout mice with CTSK-Cre or osteocyte-specific knockout mice with DMP1-Cre mice. Animal models of osteoporosis, fracture or distraction osteogenesis can be applied using this model, to investigate the effect of Smad7 specific knockout in osteoclasts or osteocytes in bone homoeostasis and diseases.

14120118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120118.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive and degenerative joint disorder. There is no effective medical therapy. It was reported that TGF-β pathways play an important role in regulating subchondral bone quantity and quality which are closely related to OA development. Our previous study indicated that two important TGF-β pathway regulators, Smad7 (inhibitory Smad) and Smad3 (receptor-regulated Smad) play important role in regulating OA development. We hypothesize that depletion of Smad7 and Smad3 expression may alter the development and progression of OA. Our results found that Smad3- and Smad7-deficient mice showed spontaneous cartilage degenerative changes and abnormal subchondral bone, they are vulnerable for OA development. The bone marrow derived MSCs in Smad3-and Smad7-deficient mice showed impaired chondrogenesis. We demonstrated that long intergenic non-coding RNA regulator of reprogramming (linc-ROR) and mir-378 play important roles in promoting or inhibiting chondrogenesis processes. We also identified Asiatic acid (Smad-7 activator) as a ptential therapeutic small molecule which attenuates OA progression and development. This study suggests that both Smad3 and Smad7 are important regulators for maintaining chondrocyte homeostasis and cartilage health. The findings from this study not only inform the biology of OA development but also have translational potentials for the management of OA.

14120218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14120218.value: 功能近紅外光譜儀(FNIRS)的臨床用途-查找與rTMS抗抑鬰療效相關的治療前腦部功能性網絡及療程中的改變

14120218.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14120218.value: Dr Chau, Wai-ho Prof Chu, Winnie Chiu-wing Dr TSE, Chun Yu

14120218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120218.value: Background: Long-term sufferers from Major Depressive Disorder are challenged with chronic, recurrent and treatment refractory course of illness that requires multi-modal treatment alternatives. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a safe, non-invasive non-convulsive brain stimulation therapy that proves to be efficacious for major depressive disorder not responding to at least one course of prior antidepressant therapy. Combining clinical treatment protocol with TMS and non-invasive neuroimaging may directly inform and refine targeted neuro-modulatory treatment for major depressive disorder. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (FNIRS), being a new non-invasive brain imaging method based on optical signals, offers an equally safe, non-invasive, patient-friendly alternative to other hospital-based functional imaging at much lower cost for measuring TMS related neuro-modulatory changes in brain. Methods: In patients who receive 4-week daily neuronavigated 10Hz rTMS to left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (left DLPFC) as clinical treatment for treatment refractory major depressive disorder, our primary objectives are: i) to measure the changes in hemodynamic responses in left DLPFC by measuring the offline FNIRS resting state signals of left DLPFC in pre-treatment phase (7-10 days before first treatment session), week 2, week 4, week 6 and week 12; ii) to evaluate if FNIRS signals in left DLPFC detected in week 2 correlate with the treatment outcomes in week 4, 6, 8, 12, in order to look for early biomarkers for treatment response. Secondary objectives: i) to cross-validate the prediction of clinical response to rTMS in a 12-week depressive symptom trajectory using two biomarkers, i.e. pre-treatment resting state connectivity of left DLPFC measured with fMRI and resting state FNIRS signals in left DLPFC; ii) to evaluate the concordance of changes in connectivity of left DLPFC on resting state functional MRI and changes in resting state FNIRS signals in left DLPFC in post-treatment phase (at week 6 and week 12). Specific hypotheses: i) Detection of increase in resting state FNIRS signal in left DLPFC in week 2 is an early biomarker for positive treatment outcome in the subsequent symptom trajectory up to week 12; ii) Pre-treatment resting state connectivity measured with fMRI and FNIRS resting state signal in left DLPFC classifies clinical response status in week 6 and 12 consistently; iii) Resting state functional connectivity of left DLPFC on functional MRI and changes in resting state FNIRS signals in left DLPFC in post-treatment phase (at week 6 and week 12) are highly concordant. 背景: 抑鬱症長期患者面對頑強及復發的困擾，需要不同模式的治療方法。連環透顱磁力刺激治療 （rTMS） 是一種安全和非入侵性、非抽搐性的腦刺激治療，其效能已被證實用於曾接受一種或以上抗抑鬱藥物治療而未有成效的病人。透過結合連環透顱磁力刺激治療和非入侵性腦造影，希望能直接理解和改進磁場對腦部細胞的定位，以便更掌握治療前腦部功能性網絡如何影響治療效果，為改良未來的rTMS技術提供科學證據。FNIRS 是一種利用光學訊號檢測大腦區域性帶氧活動的神經造影技術。它設計輕便，讓研究人員能在磁力共振中心以外的地方為病人作多次的區域性腦功能檢查，大大提升數據收集效能同時減低成本。我們收集這些數據是為了增加了解rTMS的療效預測生物指標及療程中相關的腦神經活動機理。 方法: 抗藥性抑鬱症病人會接受四星期高頻定位連環透顱磁力刺激治療於左腦前額葉，以下為四項主要研究目標: 1. 通過測量治療前（治療前7-10天），第2、4，6、12週左腦前額葉的離線FNIRS靜止狀態信號來測量左腦前額葉血流動力學反應的變化。 2. 評估第2週FNIRS信號於左腦前額葉是否與第4、6、8、12週的治療結果相關，以便尋找治療反應的早期生物指標。 3. 驗證兩種方法（功能性網絡磁力共振和FNIRS）對於預測抗藥性抑鬱症病人對連環透顱磁力刺激治療的反應。 4. 評估兩者（rTMS和FNIRS）在治療後（第6週和第12週）左腦前額葉與大腦靜止狀態下的連接性變化的一致性。 假設: 1. 在第2週，左腦前額葉中靜止狀態FNIRS信號的增加是早期生物指標直至第12週隨後症狀。 2. 治療前左腦前額葉的靜止狀態（以功能性網絡磁力共振和FNIRS方法量度）都能一致地反映第6週和第12週的臨床反應。 3. 兩者（rTMS和FNIRS）在治療後（第6週和第12週）左腦前額葉與大腦靜止狀態下的連接性變化是高度一致。

14120318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120318.value: 背景 超聲內鏡引導胃空腸吻合術（EPASS）是一種治療惡性胃出口阻塞的新興技術。然而，這種方式與傳統内鏡十二指腸支架術，誰療效比較好尚不確定。 目的和假設 本研究的目的是比較EPASS與未覆蓋的十二指腸支架術（DS）在不可切除的惡性胃出口梗阻中的療效。我們假設與，相比DS，EPASS可以降低再干預率。 方法 這將是一項前瞻性多中心隨機對照研究，比較EPASS與DS在不可切除的惡性胃出口梗阻患者中的應用。研究將招募患有不可切除胃十二指腸或胰膽管惡性腫瘤導致的胃出口梗阻病人。主要測量結果是6個月的再干預率。次要測量結果包括技術和臨床成功率，並發症率，死亡率，支架前和術後胃出口梗阻評分（GOOS），支架功能障礙的原因，支架通暢的持續時間，成本和生活質量評估分數。 分析 所有結果將根據意向治療原則分析。比較將通過Chi-square或Fisher精確檢驗進行分類數據分析，Mann-Whitney U檢驗分析非參數連續數據。Kaplan-Meier方法分析累積支架通暢和患者存活時間，並使用對數秩檢驗進行比較。 病人量計算 病人量是根據我們的回顧性研究和已發表的研究結果計算出來的。假設EPASS和DS之間的再干預率差異為20％，雙側P值為0.05，功效為80％，則每組需要58名患者。如果根據我們自己的數據，假設再乾預率差異為29.2％，則每組需要26名患者。因此，取兩個數字之間的平均值，每組需要42名患者。考慮到10％的退出率，每組需要46名患者。 時間表和可行性 這項研究將包括4至6個高病人量機構參與，每個機構招募20至30名患者。在威爾斯親王醫院，每年約有20名患者需要進行十二指腸支架術，他們可以被招募參加該研究。因此，我們預計研究招募可在1至2年內完成。然後在手術後跟踪患者狀況6個月。

14120318.value: Major findings Between Dec 1, 2020, and Feb 28, 2022, 185 patients were screened and 97 (46 men and 51 women) were recruited and randomly allocated (48 to the EPASS group and 49 to the duodenal stent group). Mean age was 69·5 years (SD 12·6) in the EPASS group and 64·8 years (13·0) in the duodenal stent group. All randomly allocated patients completed follow-up and were analysed. Reintervention within 6 months was required in two (4%) patients in the EPASS group and 14 (29%) in the duodenal stent group [p=0·0020; risk ratio 0·15 [95% CI 0·04–0·61]). Stent patency was longer in the EUS-GE group (median not reached in either group; HR 0·13 [95% CI 0·08–0·22], log-rank p<0·0001). 1-month GOOS was significantly better in the EPASS group (mean 2·41 [SD 0·7]) than the duodenal stent group (1·91 [0·9], p=0·012). There were no statistically significant differences between the EPASS and duodenal stent groups in death within 30 days (ten [21%] vs six [12%] patients, respectively, p=0·286), technical success, clinical success, or quality of-life scores at 1 month. Adverse events occurred 11 (23%) patients in the EPASS group and 12 (24%) in the duodenal stent group within 30 days (p=1·00); three cases of pneumonia (two in the EPASS group and one in the duodenal stent group) were considered to be procedure related. We conclude In patients with malignant gastric outlet obstruction, EPASS can reduce the frequency of reintervention, improve stent patency, and result in better patient-reported eating habits compared with duodenal stenting, and the procedure should be used preferentially over duodenal stenting when expertise and required devices are available

14120318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120318.value: Since we have demonstrated superiority of EPASS as compared to conventional endoscopic stenting, the next step would be to assess if the new treatment could provide superior results as compared to conventional surgical bypass. Furthermore, a cost effective analysis could also be performed to see if EPASS is cost effective in managing patients with malignant gastric outlet obstruction as compared to duodenal stenting.

14120318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120318.value: "Malignant gastric outlet obstruction" occurs in patients with advanced cancer affecting the pancreas, bile ducts, or stomach. It results in vomiting, malnutrition, and poor health outcomes. To alleviate this obstruction, several treatment options are available. One option is to create a surgical connection between the stomach and the small intestine, called surgical gastrojejunostomy. Another option is to place a metal tube called duodenal stenting to widen the narrowed area in the intestine. A newer procedure called EPASS can also be used. This involves using special stents to create a connection between the stomach and the intestine under endoscopic guidance. Comparative studies have shown that EPASS has better outcomes compared to duodenal stenting. However, results from randomised controlled trials are lacking. This study is the first randomised study comparing EPASS with duodenal stenting. The results showed EPASS had a significantly lower rate of reintervention, shorter hospital stays, longer stent durability, and better eating habits by patients. There were no significant differences in other outcome parameters. Based on the available evidence, for patients with malignant gastric outlet obstruction and a reasonable life expectancy, EPASS should be the preferred treatment option when expertise is available.

14120418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120418.value: 據世界衛生組織統計數據顯示，全世界範圍內患有不孕不育的人群達到了8 千萬，其中男性不育占50%。 在哺乳動物睪丸中，雄性生殖系幹細胞表現出精確的細胞和表觀遺傳調節。 它們的自我更新和分化是男性生育能力的關鍵基礎。它們還具有通過轉分化為非胚細胞譜系而在再生細胞療法中作為替代性多能幹細胞來源的潛力。5-甲基胞嘧啶（5mC）的表觀遺傳修飾對細胞發育具有深遠的影響。 盡管進行了多年的研究，只有少數表觀遺傳因子被證明會導致精子發生缺陷，其他表觀遺傳原因或風險因素的鑒定也非常困難。 以前5mC被認為是穩定存在並可通過被動去甲基化去除。 然而最近的研究表明，TDG可介導活性DNA去甲基化，這一過程對於小鼠胚胎和幹細胞發育是十分重要。為了研究TDG在雄性生殖系幹細胞中的功能作用，本實驗室成功培育及鑒定TDG生殖細胞特異性敲除小鼠 。與野生型和雜合子組相比，敲除動物顯示出顯著更少的後代和表觀遺傳標記的差異表達。 重要的是，我們在精原細胞分化的初始階段（P8）使用分化的精原細胞標記物KIT追蹤精原細胞分化，並觀察到敲除動物的睪丸中KIT陽性細胞顯著減少。 初步研究表明，Tdg調節參與雄性生殖系幹細胞發育和衰老的長非編碼RNA（http://germage.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk/），以及正常幹性維持中的關鍵編碼基因，包括Oct4和Stra8。 這些觀察結果表明TDG可能與精原幹細胞維持及老化有關。基於這些新穎和令人興奮的發現，我們推測TDG介導主動去甲基化有助於雄性生殖系幹細胞的維持和分化。 我們計劃通過以下步驟來檢驗這一假設：1）調查Tdg缺失導致的生精缺陷及潛在機制; 2）闡明RAR / TDG復合物介導的去甲基化在RA誘導生殖細胞分化過程中的作用; 3）最後，我們將使用全基因組方法系統地研究TDG介導的去甲基化在雄性生殖系幹細胞維持中的作用。

14120418.label: Realisation of objectives
14120418.value: Objective 1: To investigate the spermatogenic defect resulted from Tdg deletion and its underlying mechanism using germline-specific Tdg knockout mice. We have successfully shown the spermatogenic defect resulted from Tdg deletion using germline specific Tdg knockout mice. Since Tdg knockout caused embryonic lethality in mouse, we have generated male germline-specific Tdg knockout mice in C57BL/6 background by crossing mice carrying recombinant Tdg floxed alleles and Oct4-EGFP (Tdgfl/fl) with mice carrying a Stra8-Cre allele (Stra8-Cre+/-). The loxP sites were located before exon 3 and after exon 7 of Tdg genes, which generate a truncated protein in the presence of Cre recombinase. The generation of successful knockout of target Tdg exons was confirmed by Sanger sequencing, while the genotypes of pups we used in subsequent experiments were all confirmed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The reduction in expression level of Tdg exons was verified by real-time PCR. Typically, the expression of Tdg significantly reduced by over 60% in P8 and over 99% in 1-month mice. The expression of the self-renewal and differentiation-related genes, including Plzf, Gfra1, and Rarg, during the first wave of spermatogenesis (P8), adult stage (2-month old) and aged animal (15-month old) were decreased in CKO testes, which agreed with the fertility decline observation. Next, we studied the epigenetic landscape of Tdg null SSC, we found significant increase in CpG methylation in imprinting genes, including H19 and Igf2, as well as genes involved in SSC maintenance (Ngn, Nanos3, Fgfr1) and differentiation (Stra8, Kit, Dmrt1). The only challenge we encountered was the infection rate of rescue construct in CKO SSC culture was low (10-16%), which is common for SSC culture. Therefore, the potential rescue effect could not be examined. Objective 2: To elucidate the role of RAR/TDG complex in retinoic acid-dependent active demethylation during germ cell differentiation. Since Tdg null embryonic stem cells (ESCs) failed to differentiate in response to retinoic acid, and recent study suggesting TDG-mediated active demethylation may involve retinoic acid signaling. We hypothesized that a similar mechanism may underlay the SSC differentiation regulation. To our surprise, we found TDG does not involve in SSC differentiation induced by retinoic acid. We first attempted to test if TDG is involved in RA-induced response in spermatogonial stem cell (SSC) differentiation by treating SSC with different concentrations of RA. Tdg null SSC culture showed 13% decrease in differentiated SSC (KIT-positive cells). This is associated with repression of all the differentiation targets (9/9) and 58% (7/12) of SSC stemness genes. To show if physical interaction between RAR and TDG proteins, examined the presence of Stra8-TDG and RAR gamma (RARG)-TDG complex in SSC culture derived from Oct4-EGFP mice by co-immunoprecipitation. However, the signal showed no interaction of TDG with either RAR. Therefore the role of Tdg in regulating RA-dependent differentiation of SSC through Stra8 is not supported. To further elucidate the potential gene targets regulated by Tdg and underlying molecular regulation of in Tdg-KO SSC during differentiation, we resorted to profile the transcriptomes of both PND8 undifferentiated (KIT-) and differentiating (KIT+) SSC of Tdg-WT/-HT/-KO genotypes by RNA-seq analysis. We are intrigued that this alternative approach led to identification of FGF and GDNF signaling would be the key signaling pathways regulated by Tdg in RA-induced SSC differentiation. Objective 3: To investigate the role of active demethylation in the regulation of RAR/TDG-targeting genes identified in Aim 2. We first examined the global of 5fC/5caC marks in Tdg-WT and Tdg-CKO cells by extracting the genomic DNA. The 5fc and 5caC marks were quantified by dot blot. However, we found the 5fC and 5caC levels in genomic DNA were comparable in WT and KO SSC isolated from 4-week-old mice, suggesting Tdg knockout may not affect the 5fC and 5caC in global level. The equivalent global 5caC levels between WT and KO SSC were also cross validated by immunostaining and flow cytometry. To continue the systematic investigation about the role of TDG-mediated demethylation in SSC. We thus turn to convention CpG DNA methylation marks, as Tdg is also involved in the active demethylation of cytosine. We asked if TDG could directly regulate the methylation status of differentiation related genes. We confirmed Tdg-null SSC showed methylation repression by 30%-43% in the 9 candidate genes during KIT transition in postnatal day 8 (P8) SSC. Over 60% of CpG sites in targeted promoter regions of four important spermatogenesis regulators Stra8, Apaf1, Ptpn11, and Sox2 were hypo-demethylated in Tdg null SSCs during KIT transition. Taken together, our results suggested although TDG depletion did not altered the global 5fC and 5caC levels, it may play a regulatory role in demethylation of specific gene loci. With this intriguing finding, we further the examined methylation changes on P8 SSCs with ATAC-Me, a novel technique which profiles cytosine methylation at single nucleotide level in accessible chromatin, which provide a better idea about the methylation dynamics information. Over 4.2 millions of statistically significant differential methylated loci (DML) were identified during KIT transition for both wild-type and Tdg-null SSCs. These DML were contributed to 1,244 and 1,365 DMRs during KIT transition of wild-type and Tdg-null SSCs respectively. Gene ontology analysis results showed loss of Tdg may lead to changes in essential pathways in SSC development through regulating gene specific DNA methylation or demethylation. Gene pathway analysis highlighted a list of signaling pathways potentially affected by the global methylation changes induced by Tdg. Taken together, both gene-centric and global approaches suggested of Tdg contributed to essential pathways in SSC development. These novel pathways will be the focus of subsequent study.

14120418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120418.value: We found that Tdg knockout mice were subfertile, the fertility was reduced progressively and reflected in the lower number of progenies. Despite we detected subfertility in Tdg-CKO mice, we did not observe any difference in testis size and sperm count in adult mice. H&E staining on testis sections revealed a depletion trend in the number of leptotene/zygotene spermatocytes, which are characterized by their deeply-stained nuclei along the outermost cell layer in a cross-section, in Tdg-CKO adult mice across sexually active ages. This is accompanied by an increase of apoptotic germ cells by over 50% in Tdg-CKO testes. Despite retinoic acid signaling is involved in male germline stem cell differentiation, Tdg does not involve retinoic acid (RA) regulation. To further elucidate the underlying molecular regulation of changes observed in Tdg-KO SSC at undifferentiated stage and during KIT transition, we resorted to profile the transcriptomes of both PND8 undifferentiated (KIT-) and differentiating (KIT+) SSC of Tdg-WT/-HT/-KO genotypes. Gene ontology analysis on 81 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between KO and WT showed that these genes were enriched in terms related to protein functions, including post-translational protein modification, oxidative phosphorylation, translational initiation and intracellular protein transport, suggesting Tdg plays a wide-ranged role in regulating protein metabolism-related functions. Our results suggested although TDG depletion did not alter the global 5fC and 5caC levels. Examining SSCs with ATAC-Me, a novel technique which profiles cytosine methylation at single nucleotide level in accessible chromatin, the results suggested loss of Tdg may lead to changes in some essential pathways in SSC development through regulating gene-specific DNA methylation or demethylation.

14120418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120418.value: Our study identified the TDG-regulated targets using ATAC-seq in SSCs for the first time. The epigenetic regulations of these gene targets are potentially crucial for the proper maintenance and differentiation of SSCs. Therefore, elucidating the epigenetic programs would be a major direction in the subsequent study.

14120418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120418.value: Recent studies have shown that active DNA demethylation through 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) by Thymine DNA Glycosylase (TDG) is essential for embryonic and stem cell development. Spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) are male germline stem cells that provide the foundation for continuous production of male gamete (sperm) throughout a male's lifespan. Only few epigenetic factors have clearly been shown to cause spermatogenic failure. To examine the functional role of TDG in male germline stem cells, we have successfully generated Tdg germline-specific knockout mice. The knockout animal showed significantly fewer progenies and differences on epigenetic marks in testes when compared to wild-type and heterozygote groups. We observed that the differentiated cells were significantly reduced in the testes in the knockout animal, suggesting TDG plays an indispensable role in SSC development and maintenance.

14120618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120618.value: The aim of this project is to identify novel therapeutic target kinase for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). PDAC is aggressive and the available therapies are ineffective. Overall survival of patients has little improvement in the past 20 years. Therefore, it is of urgent significance to identify novel therapeutic targets. KRAS mutations occur in over 90% of PDAC and has been recognized as the fundamental driver. However, inhibiting mutant KRAS has been challenging. Kinases are recognized as good druggable targets and have been intensively involved in KRAS-driven cancers. In an attempt to identify kinases essential for KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth, we conducted kinome-wide RNAi screening in KRAS mutant and wild-type PDAC cell lines. Our screening demonstrated that knock-down of three kinases: Pyruvate Dehydrogenases Kinase Isozyme 2 (PDK2), Serine/Threonine Kinase 31 (STK31) and Serine/Threonine Kinase 32B (STK32B) selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth. Amongst, the role of STK32B in cancer remains largely unknown. Therefore, we focused on STK32B in this proposal. STK32B inhibition selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth, cell proliferation, colony formation, cell transformation and in vivo tumor formation in nude mice. Intra-tumoral injection of siRNAs targeting STK32B selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC xenografted tumor growth while showing no effect in KRAS wild-type tumor mouse model. Moreover, STK32B was dramatically overexpressed in a large portion of PDAC tissues. Increased level of STK32B was positively correlated to shorter survival of PDAC patients. Our preliminary results suggested that transcription factor Sp1 which has been well implicated in PDAC may play important roles in regulating STK32B expression. We further identified two proteins Importin 7 and Talin 1 with oncogenic potential as the downstream targets of STK32B by proteomic approaches. Our promising preliminary results prompted us to believe that STK32B played critic roles in PDAC and represented a promising therapeutic target. In this proposal, we intend to 1) identify the functional domains and validate the kinase activity of STK32B; 2) delineate the mechanisms underlying the oncogenic roles of STK32B; 3) characterize the role of Sp1 in regulating STK32B expression; 4) identify potential STK32B inhibitors. Knowledge gained from this project will reveal the roles of STK32B and its targets in PDAC and potentially lead to novel therapeutic target for KRAS mutant cancers. 本項目的目的是鑒定胰腺導管腺癌（PDAC）的新型治療靶激酶。PDAC具有攻擊性，而現時並缺乏有效的療法。因此，在過去20年，患者的總體存活率幾乎沒有改善。所以，尋找新的治療靶點具有重要的意義。 在超過九成的患者中，都發生了KRAS的突變，所以KRAS突變體一直被認為是PDAC的驅動基因。然而，抑制KRAS突變體一直具有挑戰性，而激酶則被認為是良好的可藥物靶標，以治療KRAS驅動的癌症。 為了認出讓KRAS突變體PDAC細胞生長所需的激酶，我們在KRAS突變體和野生型的PDAC細胞系中進行了全激酶敲除篩選。我們發現敲除三種激酶：丙酮酸脫氫酶激酶同工酶2（PDK2），絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶31（STK31）和絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶32B（STK32B）能選擇性地抑制KRAS突變PDAC細胞生長，而對KRAS野生型PDAC細胞則沒有影響。其中，STK32B在癌症中的作用仍然未知。因此，我們在本項目中集中研究STK32B。 抑制STK32B選擇性地抑制裸鼠中KRAS突變體PDAC細胞的生長、細胞增殖、集落形成、細胞轉化和體內腫瘤形成。在腫瘤內注射靶向STK32B的siRNA能選擇性地抑制KRAS突變體PDAC異種移植腫瘤的生長，而對KRAS野生型腫瘤小鼠模型則沒有影響。此外， STK32B在大部分PDAC組織中都顯著上調，亦與PDAC患者生存期短成正比。一方面，我們發現與PDAC有關的轉錄因子Sp1在調節STK32B表達中起重要作用。另一方面，我們通過蛋白質組學的方法發現了兩種致癌蛋白Importin 7和Talin 1作為STK32B的下游目標。我們的初步結果促使我們相信STK32B在PDAC中發揮了重要作用，並且STK32B可能成為新的治療目標。 在本計劃書中，我們計劃1）鑑定並驗證STK32B激酶活性的結構域; 2）研究STK32B的致癌機制; 3）研究Sp1在調節STK32B表達中的作用; 4）尋找潛在的STK32B抑制劑。從本項目中獲得的知識將揭示STK32B及其下游目標在PDAC中的作用，並有助發展治療KRAS突變的胰腺導管腺癌。

14120618.label: Realisation of objectives
14120618.value: All the objectives were achieved. 1. To identify the functional domains and validate the kinase activity of STK32B. Although STK32B was a putative kinase according to the conservative sequences of the protein, there was no experiment-based kinase activity analysis of the enzyme. To prove that STK32B was exhibiting genuine kinase activity, we conducted the kinase activity assay to measure the kinase activity of STK32B. In addition to full length STK32B recombinant protein, we also tested kinase activity of the STK32B recombinant protein with truncated kinase domain. The result showed that STK32B had kinase activity with EC50 of 110.6ng, while the truncated protein with kinase domain deletion had no kinase activity. It suggested that the kinase domain of STK32B exhibited potent kinase activity. 2. To delineate the mechanisms underlying the oncogenic roles of STK32B. 2.1 FKBP8, ACAA1, IPO7 and TLN1 were potential target genes regulated by STK32B To identify target genes regulating by STK32B, we used quantitative proteomic analysis to measure differential protein expression in SW1990 ShSTK32B and ShSCRAMBLE. The cutoff of fold change was two-fold down-regulated. Then we validated the results by q-PCR and measure the mRNA levels of these potential target genes. In these differential expressing genes, FKBP8, ACAA1, IPO7 and TLN1 were frequently correlated to cancer development in a broad range of cancer types. They participated in the biological process of cell proliferation and cancer cell survival, which were consistent with the phenotypical changes of knock-out STK32B. As such, we believed they might contribute to the aggressiveness of PDAC in the STK32B pathway. These four genes were chosen for further investigation as potential functional target genes of STK32B. 2.2 Knock-down of STK32B in SW1990 and CAPAN2 cells significantly decreased TLN1 and IPO7 at mRNA and protein levels To prove that the expressions of TLN1 and IPO7 were regulated by STK32B, we knocked-down STK32B in SW1990 cells and CAPAN2 cells by shSTK32B. Total RNA was extracted for measurement the mRNA levels of TLN1 and IPO7 by Q-PCR. Knock-down efficiency was validated by western blotting. We found knock-down of STK32B significantly reduced TLN1 and IPO7 at mRNA levels and protein levels. 2.3 Overexpression of STK32B in BXPC3 cells significantly increased TLN1 and IPO7 at mRNA and protein levels Expression levels of TLN1 and IPO7 were measured in BXPC3 cells with overexpression of STK32B. We showed that they were upregulated at mRNA levels and protein levels when STK32B was overexpressed in BXPC3 cells. Based on the above results, it was clear that TLN1 and IPO7 were regulated by STK32B, either directly or indirectly. However, it was still elusive that how a protein kinase regulated gene expression. There should be other substrate proteins of STK32B contributing to this biological process. Nonetheless, our results showed thatTLN1 and IPO7 were the functional target genes of STK32B 3. To characterize the role of Sp1 in regulating STK32B expression. 3.1 Expression of STK32B was modulated by oncogenic KRAS To demonstrate that oncogenic KRAS could transactivation STK32B in PDAC cells, we transfected siRNA targeting KRAS G12V and KRAS G12D in CAPAN2 cells and SW1990 cells respectively. Q-PCR was performed to validate Knock-down efficiency, and showed that STK32B was down-regulated upon siKRAS treatment compared to siNC at mRNA levels and protein levels. In parallel, forced expression of mutant KRAS protein in HPDE and BXPC3 cells significantly up-regulated STK32B at mRNA level and protein level. These results proved that STK32B was a downstream effector of the oncogenic KRAS signaling. 3.2 Expression of STK32B was regulated by transcriptional factor SP1 By searching the Eukaryotic Promoter Database (EPD) , we found that there was a GC rich region in the STK32B promoter. In parallel, by using an online transcriptional factor prediction software (PROMO), we found that the promoter of STK32B harbored transcriptional factor SP1 binding sites, and thus STK32B might be regulated by SP1 transactivation. Therefore, we used the SP1 inhibitor Mithramycin A to treat the cells for 48 hours. We found that Mithramycin A significantly reduced mRNA level of STK32B. To further prove that SP1 was involved in the regulation of STK32B, we inhibited SP1 by transfecting SP1 siRNA in SW1990 cells. Inhibition of SP1 by siRNA could also significantly reduce the mRNA level of STK32B in SW1990 cells. Taken together, we showed that STK32B was transactivated by SP1 pathway. 3.3 Oncogenic KRAS signaling activated SP1 Previous studies revealed SP1 could be phosphorylated by ERK, while phosphor-SP1 was the active component enabling DNA binding and facilitating transcription of its target genes. However, evidence showing direct interaction of oncogenic KRAS and SP1 in PDAC was elusive. We profiled the phosphor-SP1, as the active fraction of the protein, in PDAC cell lines, and found phosphor-SP1 was specific to KRAS mutation cells, with similar expression pattern with STK32B in PDAC cell lines. ChIP assay followed by q-PCR showed there was a significant enrichment in the promoter region of STK32B. Pol II also significantly enriched to this promoter region as well, indicating direct transcription of STK32B. By using siRNA targeting KRAS and SP1, and by using MAPK inhibitor and ERK inhibitor, p-SP1 enrichment was significantly reduced. 4. To identify potential STK32B inhibitors with anti-cancer activity. 4.1 Homology modeling of STK32B for virtual screening To develop a kinase inhibitor of STK32B, we adopted the virtual screening method to identify potential small molecule inhibitor candidates. Virtual screening could be divided into structure-based virtual screening and ligand-based virtual screening. The former one was suitable for the situation to identify potential inhibitors for a known protein target, meanwhile the later one was a bottom-up method in which the potential protein targets were predicted based on a known small molecule inhibitor. For our case, the structure-based method was more appropriate as we attempted to identify potential inhibitors for STK32B. To run the virtual screening, the architecture of the molecules should be available. Up till now, the architecture of STK32B had not been investigated by any other research groups, and there was not any experimental based data for STK32B. As such, we built up a homology model of STK32B by SWISS-MODEL. Figure 28 showed the report of STK32B structure modeling. Z-score was used to evaluate the efficiency of the template we used for modeling. Figure 28A showed Z score for all-atom, which was ∣Z score∣< 1, indicating the similarity of the template was acceptable. Fig 28B. showed the coverage of query protein and the template, with a sequence identity of 71.27%. 4.2 Virtual screening for potential inhibitors of STK32B To identify potential inhibitors targeting STK32B, we ran a virtual screening by using iDOCK 2.2 software. As we attempted to target the regulatory motif of STK32B, we ran the program by importing the ATP binding site and mTOR binding site of the STK32B proteins separately. After filtering the compound by Rule-of-five, we got a list of candidate inhibitors targeting ATP binding site and candidate inhibitors targeting mTOR binding site.

14120618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120618.value: STK32B was selectively expressed in KRAS mutant PDAC cells. The expression of STK32B was significantly higher in PDAC tumor tissues compared to paired adjacent non-tumor tissues (p=0.0061). Knockout of STK32B dramatically inhibited cell proliferation, colony formation rate and cell transformation ability in KRAS mutant cells. Overexpression of STK32B in BXPC3 cells with wild-type KRAS significantly increased cell proliferation, colony formation rate, and cell transformation ability. Knockdown of KRAS reduced the expression of STK32B. MAPK/ERK pathway inhibitors significantly suppressed the expression of STK32B, meanwhile SP1 inhibitor and siRNA targeting SP1 inhibited STK32B expression. ChIP assay showed p-SP1 was enriched at STK32B promoter region. These results suggested that STK32B expression was regulated by the KRAS/MAPK/SP1 axis. Quantitative proteomic analysis suggested that IPO7 and TLN1 as the target genes regulated by STK32B. Our results demonstrated that mTOR was an interacting protein of STK32B through phosphorylating the 378th Serine of STK32B. Correlation analysis showed TLN1 and IPO7 had a better correlation with p-STK32B than total STK32B, suggesting p-STK32B was played a more important role in regulating IPO7 and TLN1 expression. Intratumoral injection of siSTK32B selectively inhibited the KRAS mutant xenograft tumor growth. Lastly, a structure-based virtual screening identified potential inhibitors targeting STK32B.

14120618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120618.value: PDAC is aggressive and the available therapies are ineffective. Overall survival of patients has little improvement in the past 20 years. Therefore, it is of urgent significance to identify novel therapeutic targets. KRAS mutations occur in over 90% of PDAC and has been recognized as the fundamental driver. However, inhibiting mutant KRAS has been challenging. Kinases are recognized as good druggable targets and have been intensively involved in KRAS-driven cancers. Knowledge gained from this project revealed the roles of STK32B and its targets in PDAC and will potentially lead to novel therapeutic target for KRAS mutant cancers.

14120618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120618.value: In an attempt to identify kinases essential for KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth, we conducted kinome-wide RNAi screening in KRAS mutant and wild-type PDAC cell lines. Our screening demonstrated that RNAi targeting Serine/Threonine Kinase 32B (STK32B) selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth. STK32B inhibition selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC cell growth, cell proliferation, colony formation, cell transformation and in vivo tumor formation in nude mice. Intra-tumoral injection of siRNAs targeting STK32B selectively inhibited KRAS mutant PDAC xenografted tumor growth while showing no effect in KRAS wild-type tumor mouse model. Moreover, STK32B was dramatically overexpressed in a large portion of PDAC tissues. Increased level of STK32B was positively correlated to shorter survival of PDAC patients. In this proposal, we have 1) identified the functional domains and validate the kinase activity of STK32B; 2) delineated the mechanisms underlying the oncogenic roles of STK32B; 3) characterized the role of Sp1 in regulating STK32B expression; and 4) identified potential STK32B inhibitors. Knowledge gained from this project revealed the roles of STK32B and its targets in PDAC and will potentially lead to novel therapeutic target for KRAS mutant cancers.
