14120818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120818.value: This project aims to elucidate the biological action of a newly identified Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS)-associated lncRNA, namely LBX-AS1, on osteocytogenesis and osteocyte function, and to explore its potential clinical implication in a case-control study on bone biopsies obtained intra-operatively from AIS Vs non-AIS control subjects. AIS is a global prevalent three-dimensional spinal deformity that could be associated with serious functional morbidities, cardiopulmonary compromise, early spinal degenerative changes and psychosocial disturbance. Systemic low bone mineral density (BMD) affecting multiple skeletal sites is a significant clinical association reported in different ethnic studies. Our team reported that low BMD, defined as Z-score of femoral neck BMD ≤ -1 with reference to the age and ethnic matched population, found in over 30% of the AIS patients is an independent prognostic factor for curve progression. Our most recent randomized controlled clinical trial shows that progression to surgical threshold could be reduced significantly by vitamin D supplementation in low BMD AIS patients. Based on our pilot study, we hypothesize that the aberrant high expression of lncRNA LBX1-AS1 in AIS could be an intrinsic factor affecting osteocytogenesis and osteocyte function and its response to physiological mechanical stimulation. This could result in abnormal and disproportionate bone mineralization between the convex and concave sides of the early deformed spine, which might contribute to further curve progression. It is also hypothesized that such abnormal osteocyte function could be restored through medical pharmacological and/or genetic approach. In this proposed case-control study, osteocyte number, lacuno-canalicular network (LCN) and bone mineralization will be evaluated with histomorphometry, FITC-Imaris technique and microCT, the expression level of LBX1-AS1 and osteocyte markers with in situ hybridization/qPCR and immunostaining. These parameters will be correlated with the curve severity measured as Cobb angle of the major curve and other clinical parameters. Primary human osteocytes culture will be used to study the biological function of LBX1-AS1 and to explore the possibility to restore AIS osteocyte function through pharmacological and genetic intervention. This study is complementary to our previous GRF funded studies (Project Number 463113 and 14116415) and help to advance our understanding on the possible association between genetic factor and impaired osteocyte function (manifested as abnormal bone qualities) in AIS. It has the potential to shed light on future development of novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies in preventing the occurrence or progression of the scoliosis deformity via targeting on the bone cells and bone mineralization pathway in AIS through timely non-invasive intervention. 該項目旨在闡明新鑑定的AIS相關lncRNA（即LBX-AS1）對骨細胞分化和骨細胞功能的生物學作用，並探討其在青少年術中獲得的骨活檢病例對照研究中的潛在臨床意義。特發性脊柱側彎（AIS）與非AIS對照受試者。AIS是一種全球流行的三維脊柱畸形，可能與嚴重的功能性疾病，心肺損害，早期脊柱退行性改變和社會心理障礙有關。影響多個骨骼部位的全身低骨密度（BMD）。我們的研究小組報導，與年齡和種族匹配人群相比，超過30％的AIS患者有低BMD（定義為股骨頸BMD的Z評分≤1）。我們最新的隨機對照臨床試驗表明，低BMD AIS患者補充維生素D可顯著降低脊柱畸形的惡化。基於我們的初步研究，我們假設lncRNA LBX1-AS1在AIS中的異常高表達可能是影響骨細胞分化和骨細胞功能及其對生理機械刺激的反應的內在因素。這可能導致早期變形脊柱的凸面和凹面之間的異常和不成比例的骨礦化，這可能有助於進一步的脊柱側彎的致病機制。在這項提議的病例對照研究中，將使用FITC-Imaris技術和microCT評估骨細胞密度，腔隙 - 小管網絡（LCN）和骨礦化，LBX1-AS1和骨細胞標記物的表達水平與原位雜交/ qPCR和免疫染色， 分別。這些參數將與作為主曲線的Cobb角和其他臨床參數測量的曲線嚴重性相關聯。原代人骨細胞培養將用於研究LBX1-AS1的生物學功能，並探索通過藥理學和遺傳干預恢復AIS骨細胞功能的可能性。同時假設通過醫學藥理學和/或遺傳學方法可以恢復這種異常的骨細胞功能。這項研究將補充我們之前的GRF資助研究（項目編號463113和14116415），並有助於促進我們對AIS中遺傳因素與受損骨細胞功能（表現為異常骨質）之間可能關聯的理解。通過及時的非侵入性干預，通過靶向AIS中的骨細胞和骨礦化途徑，有可能揭示新型預後生物標誌物的未來發展和預防脊柱側彎發生或發展的治療策略。

14120818.label: Realisation of objectives
14120818.value: For Objective 1a, we recruited 312 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) girls and 201 control female subjects in accordance with our inclusion and exclusion criteria. Blood sample was taken from all subjects and genotyping assays were performed to determine their LBX1-AS1 single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) variants. For Objective 1a, bone mass, bone density and bone qualities were assessed with Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT). For objective 1b, Cobb angle was measured with the Cobb method on standing full-spine X-ray. Stage of puberty was assessed using Tanner stages. Anthropometric parameters were measured standard protocols, and chronological age and monarchal age were self-reported by the subjects. The project Objective 1a and 1b have been fully achieved. For Objective 2a, 28 pairs (concave and convex sides) of facet joint bone biopsies were collected from AIS patients intra-operatively. Five pairs of biopsies from congenital scoliosis (CS) patients and seven biopsies from non-scoliosis (NS) subjects were included. The CS and NS groups serve as positive and negative control groups, respectively. For Objective 2b, among those collected biopsies, four pairs from AIS group, five pairs from CS group and three pairs from NS group were scanned by the ultra-high-resolution desktop micro-computer tomography (Scanco, μCT50, Switzerland) for morphological features of osteocyte lacunae. For Objective 2c, all collected facet joint bone biopsies were scanned with micro-computer tomography (Scanco, μCT40, Switzerland) for volumetric bone mineral density (BMD) and bone microstructure. Primary bone cells cultures derived from the facet bone samples is collected and determined by qPCR (Applied Biosystems, QS12, United States) for the expression of LBX1-AS1 level. The project Objective 2a, 2b and 2c have been completed. Objective 3 For Objective 3a, Cell proliferation of primary bone cells is determined by MTT assay (Sigma-aldrich, M2128, United States). The proliferation rate will be quantified by measuring the absorbance at 570nm, with reference wavelength at 690nm using plate reader from Day 1 to Day 4 (Bio-Tek, µQuant Universal Microplate Spectrophotometer, United States) Delayed delivery of load cell due to the COVID pandemic. we are not able to purchase BrdU assay. Three control primary bone cells and nine AIS primary bone cells are determined for cell proliferation. The level of osteocyte markers from total soluble protein is measured by Western blot from three control samples and nine AIS samples. Only DMP1 (Abclonal, A16832, United States) and SOST(Abcam, ab99340, United Kingdom) antibodies are available on the market due to global shortage of other three antibodies (MEPE, E11 and DSTN). The protein band intensity analyzed with Image J. For objective 3b, overexpression of LBX1-AS1 in osteocyte did not alter the cellular response to mechanical stimulation. For Objective 3c, due to technical difficulty of CRISPR-Cas9 method, an alternative appraoch was used to compare the cellular response of human primary osteocytes consisting of major or high risk allel of LBX1-AS1. 54 primary osteocytes culture samples from AIS group were collected and determined by Sanger Sequencing (BGI Genomics, CHINA) for the LBX1-AS1 genotyping frequency distribution. Those in good condition were subjected to examination on the the expression of osteocyte markers upon treamtent with vitamin D ,1,25(OH)2Vit-D3 (Sigma-Aldrich), at 1, 10 and 100 nM with or without vibration treatment at Day 10. The project Objective 3a, 3b and 3c have been completed.

14120818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120818.value: For Objective 1, our results show significantly lower femoral neck areal BMD (P < 0.001), total volumetric BMD (P = 0.016), trabecular volumetric BMD (P < 0.001), trabecular number (P < 0.001), and trabecular thickness (P = 0.012), and significantly higher trabecular separation (P < 0.001) in AIS group than that in control group. The genotype frequency of LBX1-AS1 SNP (rs678741) is differently distributed in AIS (genotype AA: 37.5% in AIS group vs 22.1% in control group, P < 0.001). There is no significant difference between different rs678741 genotypes (AA vs GA vs GG) observed in bone density, bone qualities, and maximal Cobb angle. For Objective 2, a total of 230,076 osteocyte lacunae from facet joints of apical vertebra of scoliotic curve were included in the analysis of osteocyte lacuna morphology with μCT50. Our results show that lacunar stretch (Lc.St) is higher, and lacunar equancy (Lc.Eq), lacunar oblateness (Lc.Ob), and lacunar sphericity (Lc.Sr) are lower in AIS and CS groups when compared with NS group). All collected facet joint bone biopsies were scanned by μCT40 for bone volumetric BMD and microstructure parameters. The density of bone volume is significantly higher in both concave (P = 0.011) and convex (P = 0.006) sides in AIS group when compared with NS group. The expression level of LBX1-AS1 cannot be detected by in situ hybridization due to low staining intensity. Therefore, primary bone cells cultures derived from the facet bone samples were collected and determined by qPCR. There is no significant difference between AIS and NS groups. For Objective 3, The cell proliferation is normalized to Day 1 result respectively and there is no significant difference shown between control and AIS groups from MTT assay. For protein expression, our results shown the expression level of DMP1 is significantly higher (P<0.01) in AIS group than that in control group. However, no significant difference in SOST expression level between two groups. For exploration of restoring AIS osteocyte function, vitamin D treatment in different concentration and vibration treatment were studied. There is no significant difference of osteocyte markers expression between control and AIS group among 3 different concentrations (1,10,100 nM) of vitamin D treatment after with or without vibration treatment. For the sequencing, there is no significant difference among three genotypes of LBX1-AS1 SNP (rs678741) P =0.17867.

14120818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120818.value: In 2015, our group reported a novel AIS associated single nucleotide polymorphism in the intron of LBX1-AS1, which is the head-to-head long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) transcribed in an antisense direction to protein-coding gene LBX1. To the best of our knwoledge, this is the first post-GWAS study aiming to demonstrate the assoication between LBX1-AS1 major/high risk allels and clinical and bone related parameters, and the biological effect of LBX1-AS1 on osteocyte functions. Despite we have confirmed the structural and functional abnormalities of AIS osteocytes with more advanced imaging technology and larger sample size, the biological function of the LBX1-AS1 appears to be subtle when compared with other reported factors. However, through this project, we discovered the new biological function of LBX1 which was supposed to be interacted with LBX1-AS1, and published the unreported function of LBX1 in terms of modulating energy metabolism in AIS. Therefore, the PI and collaborator of Joint Scoliosis Research Centre has initialized a new joint study proposal for NSFC/RGC 2023/24 exercise to continue research of this GRF project. Furthermore, with the newly established animal model of scoliosis, we aim to provide more evidence on how does LBX1 contribute to the onset and progression of AIS.

14120818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120818.value: Musculoskeletal health and spinal well being, albeit important, are often ignored by the general public, both children and adult alike. As for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), it predominantly affects adolescent girls aged 10-16. The causes for this back problem remain unknown. Our group has found that low bone mineral density (BMD) is a systemic and persistent phenomenon that correlates with the curve severity and a significant prognostic factor for predicting curve progression in AIS. Based on recent discoveries, it is postulated that lncRNA could be an alternative transcriptional regulatory mechanism which modulate the expression of AIS associated genes and their biological functions in AIS. This study will be complementary to our previous GRF funded studies (Project Number 463113 and 14116415) and help to advance our understanding on the possible association between genetic factor and impaired osteocyte function (manifested as abnormal bone qualities) in AIS. It has the potential to shed light on future development of novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies in preventing the occurrence or progression of the scoliosis deformity via targeting on the bone cells and bone mineralization pathway in AIS through timely non-invasive intervention.

14121018.label: Realisation of objectives
14121018.value: The study has been completed as planned, though the progress was delayed by COVID-19. Out of the 271 subjects with diabetes mellitus (DM), who had participated the randomized trial of vitamin B12 supplementation, 145 subjects (52.0 %) were further followed up at month 72. The reasons for drop outs were refusal 78, death 38, frailty 6, loss in contact 4. Clinical dementia rating scale (CDR), Neurocognitive tests (NTB) in memory, executive and memory function, psychomotor speed and fasting blood tests were repeated. Serum samples at baseline, month 9, 27 and 72 were analyzed for ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) mediated cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) of HDL in the laboratory of Co-I Tan and Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) in a commercial accredited laboratory. Volumetric MRI brain scans were performed in 171 subject at baseline, month 27 and 45. Of these, 70 subjects had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) which quantified small vessel disease more reliably by Peak Width of Skeletonized Mean Diffusivity (PSMD). The serial MRI scans were analyzed for whole brain atrophy rate atrophy by SIENA, hippocampal volume and white matter density (WMH) by a validated AI assisted analysis programme “ACCUBRAIN”.

14121018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121018.value: Vitamin B12 supplementation had no significant effect on CEC at month 9, 27 and 72. All the trial subjects were therefore regarded as cohort subjects. Serum HDL at baseline was associated with better executive function at 18, 27, 36 and 45 months (P = 0.014, <0.001, 0.001 and 0.039, respectively), and also better memory function at 9, 27 and 36 months (P = 0.042, 0.012 and 0.025, respectively). Serum ApoA1 was associated with better memory Z score at month 18 only (P=0.042). CEC correlated significantly with female gender, serum HDL, ApoA1 and sodium, and mean corpuscular volume (R2 0.256, 0.177, 0.253, 0.204, -0.168; P<0.01). CEC was not associated with cognitive function, hippocampal volume and white matter disease (WMH, PSMD) at baseline. All subjects were categorized by tertiles of CEC at baseline. Higher CEC was associated with an increase in clinical dementia rating scale (CDR) sum of boxes (estimate average 0.0498, 0.1660, 0.1135 per year for low, mid, high tertiles respectively, suggesting greater impairment, P=0.001) but a significant increase in memory (0.0208, 0.0006, 0.0326 per year respectively, P=0.043). In addition, CEC tertiles were not associated with global cognitive decline as defined by an increase in CDR global score by Poisson regression (P= 0.378), and not associated with changes in executive function, psychomotor speed, hippocampal volume, WMH, PSMD and whole brain atrophy rate. The correlations between baseline CEC and those at follow-up were significant but weak (correlation coefficients 0.219, 0.195 and 0.165, and P = <0.001, 0.004 and 0.049 at month 9, 27 and 72 respectively). CEC declined significantly in the first 27 months (-7.46 ± SD 8.15% at month 9; -13.11 ± 7.91% at month 27; P<0.0001 on Paired t test), but not between month 27 and month 72. On the other hand, serum ApoA1 decreased significantly at each follow-up (-5.16 ±28.57; -7.47 ±23.60; -11.40 ±24.50 mg/L at month 9, 27 and 72 respectively; P<0.0001 Paired test), but serum HDL did not change significantly at follow-up. No clinical factors at baseline correlated significantly with CEC decline. (P>0.01) The fast decliners in CEC (-12.5% or more), when compared with slower decliners in the first 27 months, had significantly greater increase in PSMD (0.641 ± 0.313 versus -0.314 ±0.281; P =0.025). There were no significant group differences in changes in cognitive function, whole brain atrophy rate, WMH, serum ApoA1 or HDL.

14121018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121018.value: Higher serum HDL was associated with more favourable changes in memory and executive function in older people with DM. But this could not be explained by ApoA1 or ABCA1 mediated CEC. This suggested that the reverse cholesterol transport function by HDL in systemic circulation may not reflect HDL function in the brain. In addition, HDL has many lipid and protein components with functions other than reverse cholesterol transport e.g. anti-oxidative, anti-inflammatory effects. Future studies may examine the effects of other HDL functions on cognitive decline in older people with DM. Relative to CEC and ApoA1, serum HDL was a relatively stable trait. It has been known that 50-60% of variations in serum HDL is due to genetic factors. It would be interesting to explore if genetic factors of serum HDL are associated with cognitive decline in older people with DM. CEC decreased significantly in older people with DM and this was associated with small vessel disease in the brain. Future studies on the biochemical, lifestyle or clinical factors of CEC decline in older people with DM may shed light on potential interventions to prevent small vessel brain disease which is associated with stroke and dementia in older people with DM.

14121018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121018.value: Our study found that higher serum high density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) was associated with less cognitive decline in older people with diabetes mellitus (DM) over four years. On the other hand, we found that the important function of HDL in reversal cholesterol transport from periphery tissues to the liver, which is important to vascular health, was not related to changes in cognitive function and brain structures in older people with diabetes mellitus (DM). Further studies are required to ascertain the component(s) and other functions of HDL-C which may be neuroprotective in older people with DM. Another important finding was that CEC decreased significantly in older people with DM and this was associated with small vessel disease in the brain. Future studies on the biochemical, lifestyle or clinical factors of CEC decline in older people with DM may shed light on potential interventions to prevent small vessel brain disease which is associated with stroke and dementia in older people with DM.

14121618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121618.value: Aim: The aim of this project is to elucidate the mechanistic origin of the premature vascular aging in Werner syndrome (WS), thus providing a basis for the rational design of new therapeutics. Background: WS is an autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by premature aging. Progressive degeneration is found in a variety of tissues indicated by symptoms such as premature graying and loss of hairs, osteoporosis, arteriosclerosis, early onset of bilateral cataracts, type 2 diabetes, skin atrophy and ulcers. Arteriosclerosis, malignancies and the associated abnormalities result in potentially life-threatening complications. Premature arteriosclerosis, caused by thickening, hardening and loss of elasticity of artery walls, gives rise to a number of vascular diseases such as myocardial infarction, ischemic legs, skin atrophy and ulcers. Chronic ulcers are complicated with high incidence of diabetes (diabetic ulcer), leading to necrosis and eventually requiring amputation. These clinical symptoms suggest a predisposed vascular disorder, whereas the mechanistic origin remains largely unclear. Our current work employs reprogramming and gene editing technologies to generate patient-specific mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and the isogenic MSCs with the causative mutation corrected. The gene-corrected MSC has an enhanced function in the angiogenesis of endothelial cells (ECs). We compared the pro-angiogenic trophic factors secreted by these MSCs, and found hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) diminished in WS MSC. HGF plays a central role in supporting angiogenesis, morphogenesis, tissue regeneration and homeostasis. Knockdown of HGF in MSC decreased angiogenesis of ECs. Therefore, we hypothesize that deficit of HGF engenders the impaired pro-angiogenesis function of stem cells, signifying a mechanism for the pathogenesis of vascular aging in WS. Objectives: 1) to examine the proangiogenic trophic effect exerted by WS MSC on EC angiogenesis and clarify the underlying mechanism. 2) to employ an in vivo model of vascularization using MSC and EC of WS. Significance of the project: The current work under this grant suggests a novel mechanism that HGF deficit in WS MSC is connected with impaired blood vessel regeneration. This work will not only elucidate the mechanistic origin of premature vascular aging in WS, but it will also have direct applications in regenerative medicine and anti-aging research, some of which have been already pursued in clinical trials. 目標： 該項目的目的是闡明成人早衰症（WS）血管早衰老的機制來源，從而為合理設計新療法提供依據。 背景： WS是一種以過早衰老為特徵的常染色體隱性遺傳疾病。在不同組織中出現逐漸退化，例如過早白髮和脫髮、骨質疏鬆、動脈硬化、雙側白內障早期發作、2型糖尿病、皮膚萎縮和潰瘍等症狀。動脈硬化、惡性腫瘤和相關的異常導致可能危及生命的並發症。由於動脈壁的增厚、硬化和失去彈性引起的過早動脈硬化而產起許多血管疾病，例如心肌梗塞、腿部缺血、皮膚萎縮和潰瘍。慢性皮膚潰瘍及高發病率的糖尿病（即糖尿病性潰瘍），導致皮膚組織壞死並最終需要截肢。這些臨床症狀表明WS病人易患血管疾病，而機械起源仍然很不清楚。 我們目前的工作是採用細胞重編程和基因編輯等技術來生成患者特異性的間充質幹細胞（MSC）和同基因的MSC，並糾正了其致病突變。基因修改的MSC對內皮細胞（EC）的血管生成具有增強的功能。我們比較了這些MSC所分泌的促血管生成因子，發現肝細胞生長因子（HGF）在WS MSC中減少。 HGF在支持血管生成、形態發生、組織再生和體內平衡中起重要作用。 HGF的敲減降低了EC的血管生成。因此，我們假設HGF的缺陷導致幹細胞的促血管生成功能受損，以表明WS中血管衰老的發病機制。 目標： 1）檢測WS MSC對EC血管生成的作用，並闡明其機制。 2）在體內模型中研究WS的MSC和EC的血管形成。 項目意義： 本項工作提出了一種新的機制，即WS MSC中的HGF缺乏與血管再生受損有關。這項工作不僅闡明了WS早期血管老化的機制來源，而且還將直接應用於再生醫學和抗衰老研究，其中一些已經在臨床試驗中得到應用。

14121618.label: Realisation of objectives
14121618.value: In this project, we proposed two objectives. Objective 1 is to examine the proangiogenic trophic effect exerted by Werner syndrome (WS) MSC on EC angiogenesis and clarify the underlying mechanism. To achieve this goal, we first performed gene editing to correct the pathogenic WRN mutation in WS iPSC. The corrected iPSC lines (C21 & C24) were isogenic and restored the expression of the normal WRN protein. They were subsequently differentiated to mesenchymal stem cell (MSC). C21/C24-MSC showed higher proliferation rate, enhanced clonogenicity, lack of premature senescence, decreased apoptosis rate and improved mesodermal differentiation. We next investigated whether gene correction of WRN in MSCs could promote angiogenesis, a paracrine function of MSC. HUVEC tube formation assay showed that conditioned medium (CM) collected from C21/C24-MSCs exhibited enhanced pro-angiogenic activity compared with CM from WS-MSCs. Moreover, the C21/C24-MSC CM showed enhanced mitogenic and motogenic effects on HUVEC, suggesting that gene correction increased the paracrine effect on stimulating HUVEC tubulogenesis, mitogenesis, and motogenesis, which is indicative of an improved pro-angiogenic function of MSCs. We also performed animal experiments to demonstrate the effect of gene correction on MSC function in vivo. Physiological angiogenesis was simulated using a femur segmental bone defect model. In this model, we transplanted WS or C21 MSCs preloaded in a 3D alginate-gelfoam scaffold into the surgically created bone defect cleft in adult mice. Collagen formation and bone regeneration were clearly indicated through Masson's trichrome staining. In the WS-MSC transplant group, less collagen deposition was found, and bone regeneration was poor. Immunohistochemistry analysis of endomucin and CD31, two markers of vessels, indicated neovascularization at the bone defect area. These data suggested that gene correction of WRN improved the pro-angiogenic function of MSCs and enhances tissue regeneration in vivo. We asked why gene-corrected MSCs promoted angiogenesis. We screened a number of MSC-released trophic factors and cytokines by RNA-seq. We found HGF, a growth factor known to stimulate angiogenesis, mitogenesis, motogenesis and morphogenesis, was significantly downregulated in WS-MSCs. Through gene silencing and gene rescue experiments performed in other primary MSC, we concluded that downregulation of HGF in WS-MSCs appeared WRN-dependent and not cell line-specific. Next, we tested the effects of HGF on angiogenesis in vitro. Recombinant HGF protein added to the CM of WS-MSCs increased HUVEC tube formation and migration/invasion, whereas knockdown of HGF in C21/C24-MSCs reversed these effects. These results indicated that downregulation of HGF in WS impairs the pro-angiogenic function of MSCs. WS patients frequently experience chronic skin ulcers, which are difficult to heal. In addition, the recurrence rate in WS patients is considerably higher than in nonsyndromic patients. Skin atrophy and type-2 diabetes are the common phenotypes of WS, further challenging wound healing and tissue regeneration. MSCs have been demonstrated to enhance wound healing through differentiation and angiogenesis. To demonstrate whether a deficiency of HGF expression in WS-MSCs results in impaired therapeutic potential of MSCs, we transplanted WS or C21/C24-MSCs onto surgically created cutaneous wounds in diabetic mice. Normal iPSC-derived MSCs and primary human MSCs were included as additional controls. On stem cell treatment, C21/C24-MSC or normal MSCs promoted wound healing at a faster rate than WS-MSCs. Notably, the addition of HGF recombinant protein significantly enhanced the wound healing rate than using WS-MSCs alone. Histological examination of the skin biopsy specimens revealed abundant CD31-positive staining and thicker epidermal/dermal layers in the C21/C24 MSC-treated skin than in the untreated or WS-MSC-treated skin. VEGF (an angiogenesis marker) and alpha-SMA (a myofibroblast marker) were also detected at higher levels in the C21/C24 MSC-treated wounds than in the WS-MSC-treated wounds. Remarkably, the addition of HGF to WS-MSCs enhanced the expressions of all these markers in the healing wounds. How the loss of WRN resulted in HGF deficiency remained unanswered. We examined signaling pathways that were altered in WS MSCs. Three major pathways, Ras/Raf, PI3K/Akt, and MAPK/p38, were identified and relevant to MSC functionality. To examine which pathway is critical for HGF expression, we used small molecules to block each pathway. Although all the tested inhibitors could suppress HGF expression in WRN+/+ cells, only LY294002 (a PI3K inhibitor) showed a differential effect. WS-MSCs appeared less sensitive to LY294002 than C21/C24 did. The amount of phosphorylated AKT protein in WS-MSC was remarkably reduced, suggesting that the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway was impaired. In MSCs, PI3K/Akt signaling can be activated by mitogenic factors to stimulate cell survival, proliferation, migration, and pro-angiogenic activity. We found that PI3K/Akt signaling in WRN+/+ MSCs could be activated by mitogenic factors (as expected). However, mitogenic factors failed to activate PI3K/Akt signaling in WS-MSCs, nor they could stimulate cell proliferation. Under normal culture conditions, WS-MSCs exhibited higher apoptosis. The addition of HGF promoted MSC survival, whereas the addition of LY294002 reduced cell survival in WRN+/+ but not in WRN−/− cells. Together, these results suggested that inactive PI3K/Akt signaling in WS-MSCs compromised cell proliferation and survival. Lastly, we evaluated the role of the PI3K/Akt pathway in the therapeutic potential of stem cells. The inhibition of PI3K/Akt signaling by LY294002 in WRN+/+ MSCs resulted in a poor wound healing. WS-MSCs, regardless of the presence of an inhibitor, showed poor wound healing. All these results suggested that the PI3K/Akt pathway is critical for mediating the (trophic) function of MSCs, whereas in WS stem cells, this pathway is inactivated, which accounts for the poor therapeutic outcome of WS stem cells. We concluded that Objective 1 was 100% achieved (Research output #1, 2). Objective 2 is to employ an in vivo model of vascularization using MSC and EC of WS. To achieve this goal, we generated WRN-knockdown MSC by shRNA via lentivirus. Umbilical cord blood-derived MSC was used in this study. As expected, knockdown of WRN in MSC resulted in reduced Akt phosphorylation, as well as the Akt downstream targets such as phosphorylated mTORC1 and GSK3B. Further analysis revealed that src homology 2 (SH2) – containing inositol 5-phosphatase (SHIP) were upregulated upon WRN depletion. SHIP is a negative regulator of Akt signaling by dephosphorylation of PIP3. Thus, inhibition of SHIP activity could stimulate WRN-deficient MSC to proliferate faster and reduced senescence. SHIP inhibition could also promote HGF secretion by MSC. Furthermore, SHIP inhibition could rescue the impaired differentiation of chondrocyte and adipocyte in WRN-deficient MSC. These results suggested that SHIP upregulation was a cause of inactive Akt signaling in WS MSC. Following these experiments, we performed in vivo experiments to demonstrate the effect of WRN loss in vascularization. WRN-knockdown MSC or scramble control MSC were mixed with HUVEC and embedded in growth factor-reduced matrigel. The cell/matrigel mixtures were then transplanted to NOD/SCID mice. Two weeks after transplantation, immunohistochemistry was performed to analyze vascularization. As expected, no tubule structures were observed when HUVEC were transplanted alone, as human endothelial cells require stromal cells such as MSC and pericytes for their survival. HUVEC co-transplanted with scramble control MSC could develop a vascular network. However, for HUVEC co-transplanted with WRN-KD MSC, we observed poor vascularization. We confirmed this result by using human specific anti-CD31 antibodies. The poor tubule formation in WRN-KD MSC group might be explained by the low survival of the MSC in vivo, as fewer of these cells could be detected by anti-GFP antibodies (MSC were labeled by GFP before transplantation). We concluded that Objective 2 was 100% achieved (Research output #6).

14121618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121618.value: In this project, we have found that loss of WRN in mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) resulted in impaired pro-angiogenesis, which compromised endothelial cells to form blood vessels and vascular network. Transcriptional analysis revealed hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) was one of significantly downregulated paracrine factors secreted by stromal cells such as MSC. As a result of this growth factor deficiency, MSC displayed poor pro-angiogenic function in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, WRN-/- MSC showed impaired function in promoting cutaneous wound healing when being transplanted to diabetic mice. These results indicated that WS MSC has an impaired function to stimulate angiogenesis during tissue repair or regeneration. Next, we found that the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway was suppressed in WRN-deficient cells. As Akt signaling (through phosphorylation of AKT protein) plays multiple roles in stem cell survival, proliferation, migration, cytokine production, angiogenesis and differentiation, the suppression of this pathway has a direct impact on MSC function. Indeed, inhibition of Akt signaling by LY294002 resulted in reduced HGF production and slower cutaneous wound healing. Further mechanistic study revealed that the upstream regulator SHIP was significantly expressed in WRN-deficient MSC. SHIP is a PIP3 phosphatase that negatively regulates Akt phosphorylation. Inhibition or knockdown of SHIP in WRN-/- MSC rescued cell senescence, stimulated cell proliferation and increased HGF production. Thus, these findings connected SHIP upregulation, Akt signaling, HGF downregulation to explain the impaired pro-angiogenesis function of MSC in WS. Besides, our published data also showed that WRN-deficient MSC had attenuated function to promote vascularization when HUVEC and MSC cells were co-transplanted into mice. In summary, the results from this research project highlighted the importance of HGF in mediating the trophic function of MSC. When normal HGF synthesis is suppressed in WS MSC, it may lead to pathological conditions that worsen tissue repair and regeneration due to the lack of angiogenesis and reduced cell proliferation.

14121618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121618.value: Through this project, we discovered that WS MSC showed impaired pro-angiogenic function because of suppressed HGF production. Furthermore, HGF expression was dependent on the Akt signaling, which was also suppressed in WS MSC. Genetic rescue by, for instance, CRISPR/Cas9-based gene editing, could restore the expression of normal WRN protein and therefore restored the functions of MSC in promoting angiogenesis, increased proliferation, reduced senescence, and better differentiation to skeletal tissues. However, many technical challenges still remain if gene editing were to be applied to clinic setting. We found that, however, if the Akt upstream (negative) regulator SHIP was inhibited, it could reactivate the Akt signaling and rescued some of the attenuated function such as the HGF expression, cell proliferation and apoptosis. This approach was appealing because it does not require gene editing of the pathogenic WRN mutation. Therefore, the future research can focus on how to apply SHIP inhibitors to promote MSC functions by reactivating the Akt signaling pathway. SHIP inhibitors can also potentially enhance MSC survival by suppressing apoptosis and senescence. Animal research using SHIP inhibitors to treat aging and age-related diseases are in urgent need and could be our next research milestone.

14121618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121618.value: Aging has become a public health concern because many aging-associated diseases, such as atherosclerosis, stroke, cardiovascular disease and cancer, have directly impacted on the human’s health and lifespan. Our project studies stem cell aging in a genetic disease called Werner syndrome (WS), which displays accelerated aging. Most of the WS patients die early due to heart disease and cancer. In this project, we focused on the function of an adult stem cell called mesenchymal stem cell (MSC). We found that WS MSC could not perform well because they could not produce sufficient growth factor (HGF) to stimulate new blood vessel formation and therefore WS patients generally show poor healing outcome. Although the pathogenesis of accelerated aging in WS is complicated, our current study highlighted a molecular origin that leads to the growth factor deficiency. This finding could be potentially translated to treat aging-associated diseases because drugs that interfere with this molecular signal could stimulate the stem cells to proliferate faster and release more growth factors to heal, for example, chronic wound that requires the formation of new blood vessels. New therapeutic drugs can be designed to target this molecular signal so as to promote stem cell functions.

14121918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121918.value: 近年來，雙膦酸鹽類（BPs）藥物已被廣泛用於臨床治療骨質疏鬆，但長期使用BPs有較高的骨折風險。在使用BPs超過10年的西方人群中，每10萬人中將有約110人遭遇一種新型骨折，即股骨非典型性骨折（AFF）。因其骨折延遲愈合或不愈合的概率非常高，AFF已引起了高度關注。 由於BPs與無機磷的結構高度相似，它可與ATP結合并形成非水解型的ATP類似物，因此導致ATP依賴性的細胞活動受到抑制。同時，臨床發現BPs治療后的患者血液中Sclerostin的含量升高數倍。此外，BPs會抑制巨噬細胞清除衰老/凋亡的細胞及甚至是骨折邊緣的無血管組織的功能。我們推測這些都是影響AFF愈合的不利因素。 為解決上述臨床問題，我們致力於尋求新型而有效的固定材料來改善AFF愈合。鎂金屬特具良好生物兼容性和促進成骨的作用。本課題組近來研發了載鎂髓內釘系統并利用其顯著促進骨質疏鬆骨折的愈合（發表于Nature Medicine, 2016）。我們已經證實鎂離子可促進ATP表達。鎂離子可顯著升高細胞外的ATP濃度，提示這些ATP是水溶性的。有趣的是，Science雜誌最近報道了ATP的生物溶劑作用。也曾有關於ATP抑制異位成骨及Sclerostin表達的報道。另一方面，鎂對巨噬細胞的極化亦有較多文獻支持。在本研究中，我們假設鎂可通過升高ATP依賴性的Sclerostin水解作用來下調Scleorstin表達水平、巨噬細胞極化，從而有效地改善AFF愈合。

14121918.label: Realisation of objectives
14121918.value: 1. To investigate the pathological characteristics in AFF model of OVX rats with BPs pre-treatment in terms of 1) effect on the differentiation of BMSCs; 2) expression of ATP and sclerostin; 3) status of macrophages polarization: In this part, long-term BPs treatment (zoledronate, at both a high dosage of 0.3 mg/kg/week for 3 months and a low dosage of 0.1 mg/kg/3 months for 6 months) in OVX rats has been demonstrated to contribute to delayed femoral fracture healing or even nonunion. In non-OVX rats, long-term BPs treatment at a dosage of 0.3 mg/kg/week for 3 months also has been demonstrated to induce delayed femoral fracture healing or nonunion. In both OVX and non-OVX rats, long-term BPs treatment significantly increased callus volume as shown by quantitative measurement of X-rays. Accordingly, the phenotype of delayed femoral fracture healing induced by long-term BPs treatment is of high reproducibility and independent of OVX. Therefore, to save the time and cost related to animal feeding and holding, the delayed healing model established by long-term BPs treatment in non-OVX rats was used in the following experiments. We detected the effects of BPs on the mechanical properties of intact femora in rats and found that long-term BPs treatment significantly elevated the ultimate load and stiffness of intact femora, while decreased the energy to failure. For fractured femora at 12wpf, the biomechanical properties in BP group are significantly impaired as compared to that in Ctrl group, which was characterized as the decreased ultimate load, stiffness, and energy to failure. Quantitative micro-CT analysis indicated that long-term BPs treatment increased mineralized bone volume fraction (BV/TV), bone mineral content (BMC), and bone mineral density (BMD), suggesting that the enlarged fracture callus is predominantly filled with bone tissues. Nonetheless, H&E and Safranin O-Fast Green staining showed that there was a fibrous layer between the fracture gap of external callus, which is believed to prevent the bilateral bony end from bridging. The expression of sclerostin (SOST), which is a secreted glycoprotein that has anti-anabolic effects on bone formation, within fracture gap (predominantly at the region of fibrous tissues) in BPs-treated rats was much higher than that in BPs-naïve rats, indicating the extremely inhibited bone formation at this region. Cellular senescence within fracture callus was further detected, while no significant difference was observed between BPs-treated and BPs-naïve rats. We further isolated the BMSCs from both intact and fractured (4wpf) femora of either BPs-treated or BPs-naïve rats, differentiation test showed that BMSCs harvested from both intact and fractured femora of BPs-treated rats exhibited increased osteogenic and fibrogenic potential as compared to the control group. Given that ATP has been demonstrated to hydrolyze SOST in a dose-dependent manner, the highly expressed SOST in the fracture callus of BPs-treated rats may be caused by the insufficient secretion of ATP. Since in vitro studies have demonstrated that Mg ions induced BMSCs to release ATP and elevates mitochondria function via magnesium transporter 1 (MagT1), we further investigated whether implantation of Mg-IMN could rescue long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing in the second part of this study. We have achieved all the objectives listed in Part I, except for the part about senescent macrophages which was not obviously observed in the BPs-treated rats. 2. To validate if the Mg ions to be released from Mg-IMN will facilitate AFF healing in terms of both histological and biomechanical outcomes. In this part, the therapeutic effect of Mg-IMN on long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing was comprehensively investigated. Rats were administrated with ZOL subcutaneously at a dosage of 0.3 mg/kg/week for three months and followed by establishment of closed femur fracture fixed by either stainless steel IMN or Mg-IMN. Radiographic data showed that implantation of Mg-IMN rescued the long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing which was characterized by decreased callus volume and non-bridging rate at 12wpf as compared to BPs-treated rats. Quantitative micro-CT analysis revealed that implantation of Mg-IMN decreased values of callus BV/TV and BMD at 12wpf in contrast to BPs-treated group, although there was no statistical significance. Above results suggested that the impaired callus remodeling process induced by long-term BPs treatment was recovered by implantation of Mg-IMN to some extent. Biomechanical test demonstrated that implantation of Mg-IMN significantly increased the mechanical properties (including ultimate load, stiffness, energy to failure, and hardness) of fractured femora at 12wpf. H&E, Safranin O-Fast Green, and Picrosirius Red staining showed that implantation of Mg-IMN rescued the aberrant callus fibrosis induced by long-term BPs treatment. Masson’s Trichrome staining demonstrated that the impeded bony callus formation and remodeling under long-term BPs treatment was rescued by Mg-IMN. By calculating the proportion of bone, cartilage, and fibrous tissues in callus, we could conclude that Mg promotes long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing through inhibiting callus fibrosis and accelerating bony callus formation (callus bridging). In addition, the expression of SOST in fracture callus of BP-Mg group was also detected at 8wpf. It turned out that the upregulated expression of SOST in BP group was reverted by Mg-IMN. We further isolated BMSCs to detect their differentiation potential and found that Mg-IMN significantly suppressed fibrogenic potential of the BMSCs harvested from the fracture callus of rat femora at 4 weeks post-fracture. Thus, Mg-IMN may rescue the impaired fracture healing under long-term BPs treatment through augmenting ATP-mediated degradation of SOST. To further validate above assumption, we investigated whether supplementation of ATP or SOST antibody could rescue long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing in vivo in the third part of this project. Collectively, we have achieved all the objectives listed in Part II. 3. To explore the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by which Mg ions enhance BPs-impaired AFF healing with focuses on: 1) the roles of ATP and sclerostin and their relationship; 2) the polarization status of macrophages at the fracture site. In this part, we investigated whether local supplementation of ATP (10mM, 200µl/week, injection of ATP targeting soft tissues adjacent to the fracture callus) or systemic supplementation of SOST monoclonal antibodies (SOSTAb, 25mg/kg, twice per week) could rescue long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing at 8 weeks post-fracture. Radiographic and micro-CT data showed that local supplementation of ATP alone accelerated the long-term BPs treatment-delayed fracture healing as implantation of Mg-IMN did, while local supplementation of ATP to rats fixed by Mg-IMN did not promote BPs-impaired fracture healing. Furthermore, biomechanical and histological analyses reinforced above findings. These data suggested that the therapeutic effect of Mg-IMN on long-term BPs treatment-impaired fracture healing was indeed associated with the concentration of ATP, which decreased the expression of anti-osteogenic SOST. It is noted that excessive concentration of ATP might inhibit fracture healing through modulating other relevant pathways. We further demonstrated the detrimental role of SOST in BPs-impaired fracture healing by verifying that systemic supplementation of SOST antibodies accelerated delayed fracture healing in BPs-treated rats. In summary, we have achieved all the objectives listed in Part III. The present study demonstrated that magnesium reverses impaired fracture healing in rats receiving long-term bisphosphonates treatment partly due to facilitate ATP-mediated decrease of SOST.

14121918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121918.value: The present research has expanded our understanding in long-term BPs pretreatment-impaired fracture healing in three aspects: (1) we successfully established an impaired fracture healing model in rats receiving long-term BPs pre-treatment, which was consistent to AFF patients who had a history of long-term BPs use. Our established animal model offered a great tool for researchers to explore the potential mechanisms and treatments of AFF; (2) we have identified Mg-IMN as a potential bioactive implant for enhancing AFF healing in rats receiving long-term BPs pre-treatment. Further translation from bench to bedside will in turn reduce the huge burdens on patients, families, and our healthcare system and society; (3) we have demonstrated that Mg-IMN reversed impaired fracture healing in rats receiving long-term bisphosphonates treatment partly due to facilitate ATP-mediated decrease of SOST. Based on above research outcome, a total of 2 peer-reviewed papers have been published in Materials Today (Zheng et al., 2022) (WoS IF26.943) with research highlighted by Science (https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ada1187) and Advanced Science (Wang et al., 2020) (WoS IF17.521). In addition, two conference abstracts related to this research project have been delivered to Annual Meeting of Orthopaedics Research Society (2020) and ICORS (2022), respectively.

14121918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121918.value: The present project aimed to investigate the pathological characteristics in atypical femur fracture (AFF) model of rats receiving long-term bisphosphonates (BPs) pre-treatment and further verify the potential therapeutic effect and mechanisms of magnesium-containing intramedullary nail (Mg-IMN). We have successfully established an impaired fracture healing model in rats receiving long-term BPs pre-treatment, which was consistent to AFF patients who had a history of long-term BPs adminstration. Our established animal model offered a great tool for researchers to explore the potential mechanisms and treatments of AFF. Furthermore, we have identified Mg-IMN as a potential bioactive implant for enhancing AFF healing in rats receiving long-term BPs pre-treatment. Further translation from bench to bedside will in turn reduce the huge burdens on patients, families, and our healthcare system and society. Regarding to the mechanisms, we have demonstrated that Mg-IMN rescued impaired AFF healing in rats partly through facilitating adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-induced sclerostin (SOST) degradation.

14123618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14123618.value: Background: Childhood obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with a variety of cardiovascular, metabolic and neurobehavioural morbidities. Children with OSA are also heavy users of health care services. Timely diagnosis and treatment of childhood OSA are important to lessen health care resource burden and risk of developing future morbidities. Although overnight polysomnography (PSG) is the current diagnostic gold standard, its limited availability and costly nature can potentially lead to delay in managing children suspected to have OSA. There is a need of a reliable screening tool for OSA risk stratification allowing prioritization of patients for PSG assessment and treatment. In our pilot study, a point-of-care model combining childhood OSA symptoms, anthropometric measures, upper airway size and craniofacial parameter was developed to predict severity of OSA in children. Objective: To evaluate the validity of a point-of-care model in predicting the severity of OSA in a prospective cohort of prepubertal children. Hypothesis: This model can be an effective screening tool by reliably predicting the severity of OSA in prepubertal children. Study Design: A prospective cohort study. Subjects: Two hundred and fifty healthy prepubertal Chinese children aged 6-11 years old suspected to have OSA will be recruited from two paediatric centres. Methods: Eligible subjects will undergo evaluation of clinical profile including completion of demographic and OSA symptoms questionnaire, anthropometric measurements, nocturnal PSG, tonsil size evaluation, x-ray cephalometry and sonographic measurement of lateral parapharyngeal wall (LPW) thickness. Using our prediction model which consists of the following parameters: age, gender, BMI z-score, neck circumference, habitual snoring, witnessed apnoea, tonsil size, LPW thickness and the distance from mandibular plane to hyoid bone (MP-H), each subject will be categorised into either moderate-to-severe OSA (as defined by OAHI ≥5 events/h) or non-moderate-to-severe OSA (OAHI<5 events/h) group. The performance of the prediction model in differentiating participants into either group will be assessed against the gold standard diagnostic test, namely PSG. This discrimination ability will be evaluated by both conventional analysis using dichotomous outcomes as well as the receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Expected results: If proven to be useful with satisfactory predictive values, this model will potentially improve the efficacy of our current management strategy for childhood OSA. 背景：兒童阻塞性睡眠窒息症（OSA）是一種常見的睡眠疾病，並與多種疾病有關，包括心血管，代謝和認知行為併發症等。因此，及時診斷和治療兒童睡眠窒息症可有助減少未來的疾病風險，以及降低醫療保健資源負擔。目前，多導睡眠監測（PSG）是診斷睡眠窒息症的黃金標準。然而，這是非常昂貴的檢查而且需要住院。因此PSG的等候時間通常很長 。在缺乏資源的中心，往往因而導致延遲診斷和治療，並可能增加睡眠窒息症相關併發症的風險。所以研究人員一直在探索各種替代的篩選或診斷工具。我們的研究小組之前進行了一項先導研究，擬定了一套預測模型，綜合兒童睡眠窒息症相關因素(包括症狀，人體測量，上呼吸道大小和顱面參數)，以預測兒童睡眠窒息症的存在和嚴重程度。此先導研究顯示這預測模型能有效預測兒童睡眠窒息症的嚴重程度。可是，這項先導研究由小樣本組成。因此，我們要再進行是次驗證研究，以足夠的樣本量驗證這預測模型，以確定其臨床有效性。 目的：本研究的目的是驗證預測模型的有效性。我們假設這預測模型可以可靠地預測兒童阻塞性睡眠窒息症（OSA）的嚴重程度，來成為一種有效的篩選工具。 研究設計：這是一項前瞻性的研究。 對象：將從兩個兒科中心招募250名年齡介乎6至11歲；懷疑患有阻塞性睡眠窒息症健康的青春期前中國兒童。 方法：符合條件的參加者將接受臨床特徵評估，包括OSA症狀問卷，人體測量，PSG，扁桃體大小評估，X射線頭影測量和側咽壁厚度（LPW）的超聲測量。我們的預測模型包括以下參數：年齡，性別，體重指標 （BMI z-score），頸圍，習慣性打鼾，見證性呼吸暫停，扁桃體大小，LPW厚度和從下頜平面到舌骨（MP-H）的距離。我們會使用預測模型將每個參加者分類為中度至重度OSA（由OAHI定義≥5/ h）或非中度至重度OSA（OAHI < 5/ h）。將根據黃金標準診斷測試即PSG的結果評估預測模型將參加者區分的準確度。 預期結果：如果證明我們的預測模型有效且具有令人滿意的預測值，該模型將有可能改善我們治療兒童阻塞性睡眠窒息症的策略和效律。

14123618.label: Realisation of objectives
14123618.value: Objectives and study design Our study aimed to evaluate the validity of a point-of-care prediction model in predicting the severity of obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) in a prospective cohort of prepubertal children. Based on our previous work on alternative diagnostic tools for childhood OSA, we developed and compared prediction models built from different combinations of clinical data from prepubertal children suspected of OSA, together with X-ray cephalometry and ultrasonographic measurement of lateral parapharyngeal wall (LPW) thickness. The polysomnographic index, obstructive apnoea hypopnoea index (OAHI) is regarded as the diagnostic gold standard to evaluate the accuracy of the prediction models. The outcomes of interest were the presence of OSA (defined as an OAHI ≥ 1 event/hour) and the presence of moderate-to-severe (MS) OSA (with an OAHI ≥ 5 events/hour). The current first-line treatment of paediatric OSA is adenotonsillectomy (AT), particularly for children with moderate-to-severe OSA. Therefore, besides predicting OSA, the accuracy of prediction models for MS OSA was also investigated, which can guide the management plan. Prediction model development The following models were developed and investigated for their accuracies. Model 1a predicted the presence of OSA (OAHI ≥ 1), constructed from data collected from clinical exams and questionnaires (basic data). Model 1b also predicted the presence of OSA but incorporated cephalometric and ultrasonographic data (point-of-care data) into model 1a. Models 2a and 2b predicted the presence of moderate-to-severe OSA (OAHI ≥ 5) built from basic data (2a) and point-of-care data (2b), respectively. The recruited subjects were randomly split into either the training or test datasets, with 75% as training data for model development and the remaining 25% as the test data for validation. The proportion of disease/non-disease in the training and test datasets was ensured to be as equal as possible. Multivariate logistic regression, a commonly used method for developing prediction models was used for model specification. Variables selection was performed based on their clinical importance and the empirical model performance. Model performance evaluation Model performance was evaluated based on discrimination, calibration, and accuracy. Discrimination indicates how well the model can distinguish between subjects with and without OSA. It was represented by Harrell’s c-statistic which is equal to the area under the receiver operator curve (AUC) for logistic regression analysis. DeLong tests were performed to compare the AUC of the receiver operator curve (ROC) curves. ROC curves with a 95% confidence interval (C.I.) were plotted. Calibration indicates how well the model’s predictions agree with the observed outcomes. It was represented by the calibration slope, which is the regression coefficient of the logistic regression model. If a model showed a calibration slope that largely deviated from the ideal calibration curve, it indicated high bias and was excluded. Accuracy is calculated as the sum of true positive and true negative over the total number of cases. A 2x2 confusion matrix was created using the optimal cut-off determined by the Youden index. Ten-fold fold cross-validation was performed. The numerical performance matrices including AUC and accuracy were calculated and the average values were presented. Results 213 children were recruited but 30 were excluded from analysis due to the following reasons: history of upper airway surgery (n=6), congenital disease (n=1), post-pubertal (n=9), missing data (n=13), and withdrawal (n=1). 173 children (mean age of 8.26 ± 1.62 years, 67.6% male) were included in the model development and performance evaluation. Fifty-eight did not have OSA, while 63 and 52 had mild (OAHI 1-5 events/hour) and MS OSA respectively. Overall, 12% of the participants were obese and 42% of them had large tonsils. The MS OSA group had more obese children and presented with a higher prevalence of large tonsils. Model 1 – Predict the presence of OSA Model 1a included age, gender, neck circumference, BMI z-score, and the presence of large tonsils, habitual snoring, and nocturnal oral breathing as predictors of the presence of OSA. After 10-fold cross-validation, the mean AUC and accuracy were 0.726 and 0.745 respectively. Model 1b included hyoid position (MP-H/Go-Gn) from cephalometry, LPW thickness, age, gender, BMI z-score, and the presence of large tonsils, habitual snoring, and nocturnal oral breathing as predictors. After 10-fold cross-validation, the mean AUC and accuracy were 0.743 and 0.759 respectively. Model 1b had a better performance than model 1a. However, the difference in the AUC of the two ROC curves did not reach a statistical significance (p = 0.163, 95% C.I. = -0.15 - 0.025). Model 2 – Predict the presence of MS-OSA Model 2a included age, gender, BMI z-score, neck circumference, the presence of large tonsils, habitual snoring, and nocturnal oral breathing as predictors of the presence of MS OSA. After 10-fold cross-validation, the mean AUC and accuracy were 0.744 and 0.770. Model 2b included hyoid position (MP-H/GoGn), large ANR (defined as >0.73), LPW thickness, age, gender, BMI z-score, and the presence of large tonsils and habitual snoring as predictors. The mean AUC and accuracy were 0.749 and 0.777 respectively. Similar to models 1a and 1b, selecting the cephalometric and sonographic variables improved the model performance more than solely using clinical variables. However, the difference of AUC was not significant when compared using DeLong’s test (p = 0.348, 95% C.I. = -0.15 - 0.05). Summary Two point-of-care prediction models for childhood OSA and MS-OSA were developed based on cephalometry, ultrasonography, questionnaire, and anthropometric data. Both models achieved a good accuracy of more than 75% when incorporating cephalometric and ultrasonographic data. These data can be collected from a point-of-care setting which is faster, cheaper, and more available compared to a conventional PSG diagnosis. The prediction models can be a useful tool in predicting high-risk patients. Although the proposed point-of-care prediction models did not achieve a significantly better performance in terms of matrices like AUC when compared with the model built from the anthropometric, clinical and questionnaire data, the clinical relevance should not be underestimated. One of the challenges in managing childhood OSA is the heterogeneous aetiologies of the disease in children. The craniofacial and parapharyngeal structural morphology obtained from cephalometry and LPW thickness can provide insights into the aetiology of individual OSA patients. In some children, the major causes of OSA may remain adenotonsillar hypertrophy and obesity, while the role of cephalometric parameters or LPW thickness contributing to the OSA development may be more important in other children who do not have adenotonsillar hypertrophy or obesity. Therefore, the point-of-care prediction model can provide additional information on the anatomical risk factors, and potentially aid the development of personalized OSA management. In future studies, if a larger sample size is available, subgroup analysis may allow a better appreciation of what patient group, cephalometric measurements and LPW assessment have higher diagnostic values to guide management approaches. The clinical usefulness of incorporating cephalometry and ultrasonography into routine OSA management should also be further examined. Whether and how will these parameters benefit the development of personalised OSA management plans should be further explored.

14123718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14123718.value: 目前的提案將研究神經膠質細胞在阿爾茨海默病（AD）中的功能作用。AD 是一種癡呆症，患者腦部會出現異常澱粉樣β（Ab）病原體的沉積。 AD的特徵是續 步丟失神經元導致多個腦區域萎縮。另外，Ab驅使炎症反應可能在疾病的早期無症狀階段發揮作用。神經炎症是一個非常複雜的過程，可以是神經保護的或神經毒性。它涉及神經元和炎症細胞之間的互動，如小膠質細胞和星形膠質細胞。許多免疫調節劑包括趨化因子和細胞因子都會參與其中。我們的實驗室和其他人已經確定了PTEN基因對AD能長期抑制小鼠海馬腦突觸是非常重要的。我們進一步介定PTEN的PDZ結構域能在小鼠導至認知障礙。 我們最近發現了PTEN能控制一種神經炎症生物標誌物，YKL-40。大腦脊髓液的YKL-40水平會在癡呆症惡化的階段會慢慢增加。此外，YKL-40具有廣泛的功能包括增殖，遷移，免疫反應和血管生長。然而，YKL-40如何受到監管並不完全清楚。此外，其在AD中的功能尚未完全闡明。我們有以下兩個假設。首先，PTEN / PI3-K能直接調節YKL-40在星形膠質細胞的水平。第二，PTEN / PI3-K能導致Ab誘導的神經炎症和認知障礙。目前的提案建議了解PTEN如何在AD小鼠模型中調節YKL-40的水平。通過在特定的神經細胞消除PTEN，其對神經炎症和發病機制的影響會被澄清。目前，AD是不能治愈的。加上人口老化，這導致對治療這種病的藥物有巨大的需求。使用PI3-K抑製劑來治療AD是一個可能性。但是，增加對PTEN和AD的基本機制理解先可以充分利用這些化合物來進行AD治療。

14123718.label: Realisation of objectives
14123718.value: See Part C in section 8 for figures indicated below Objective 1: To examine the expression patterns of YKL-40 and PTEN/PI3-K in 5xFAD mouse model (We have completed this objective) Increased astrocytic YKL-40 expression in 5xFAD mice - We used the 5xFAD mouse strain as an AD model in an attempt to unravel the role of YKL-40 in AD. Immunostaining revealed extensive Abeta plaques in 5xFAD mice, even in the presymptomatic phase at 4-month-old (Fig. S1A). As expected, the plaque numbers in multiple brain regions were significantly increased in 7- and 9-month-old 5xFAD mice (Fig. S1B-H). Co-staining experiments revealed extensive overlapping signals of GFAP and YKL-40 in the DG and CA1 regions of 5xFAD mice (Fig. 1A). The YKL-40 levels showed a progressive increase with age from 4- to 9-month-old (Fig. 1B and S2A-D). These results imply a strong association between YKL-40 expression in astrocytes and amyloid plaque deposition. Because YKL-40 is a prognostic biomarker for AD, CSF and plasma were collected from 4-, 7-, 9-, and 16-month-old wild-type and 5xFAD mice. Using ELISA, we observed a significant (~3-fold) increase in soluble YKL-40 in the CSF of 5xFAD mice from 7 months onward (Fig. 1C). Elevated YKL-40 expression correlated with signaling events in 5xFAD mice - We observed an age-dependent progressive elevation of p-AKT and p-STAT3 in either cortices or hippocampi in 4-, 7-, and 9-month-old 5xFAD mice compared with WT mice (Fig. 2A). Immunofluorescence analysis revealed increased staining intensities of p-AKT and p-STAT3 in DG region in 5xFAD mice relative to WT mice (Fig. 2B–E). GFAP image analysis of the DG, MOC, and TH regions of 7-month-old 5xFAD mice revealed hypertrophic activated astrocytes compared with WT mice (Fig. S3A–J). In addition, Western blotting analysis revealed 1.5- to 2.5-fold increases in GFAP expression levels in 5xFAD mice compared with WT mice (Fig. S3K–M). Taken together, the activation of both PI3-K and STAT3 signaling in reactive glial cells may contribute to Abeta-driven YKL-40 production in 5xFAD mice. Objective 2: To test if PTEN/PI3-K pathway is required for Aβ-regulated YKL-40 expression in astrocytes (We have completed this objective) To delineate the role of the PI3-K pathway in controlling YKL-40 expression and secretion, we established primary cortical astrocytes from Nes-Cre;Pten+/+, Nes-Cre;Ptenfl/+ (HET) and Nes-Cre;Ptenfl/fl (KO) primary astrocytes. By Western blotting analysis and RT-qPCR, we observed a 2- to 3-fold increase in YKL-40 protein expression and a 16-fold increase in YKL-40/Chi3l1 mRNA expression in Pten-KO astrocytes compared with WT (Fig. 3A-D). Next, these primary astrocytes were treated with Abeta(1-42) to mimic the in vivo condition of 5xFAD. Abeta(1-42) induced a dose-dependent upregulation of intracellular and secreted YKL-40 in WT astrocytes (Fig. 3A–D), which was correlated with robust activation of p-AKT (Fig. 3F–G). While Pten-HET astrocytes have elevated YKL-40 expression, Abeta(1-42) treatment failed to further stimulate its expression. Similar results were also observed with Pten-KO astrocytes (Fig. 3A–D). Overall, the activation states of AKT correlated well with YKL-40 expression (Fig. 3F–G). We conclude that PI3-K activation may be involved in maintaining the basal level of YKL-40. Moreover, the ability of Abeta(1-42) to increase YKL-40 expression appears to be correlated with p-AKT levels in astrocytes with different PTEN genotypes. Objective 3: To test the functional role of PTEN/PI3-K in activated astrocytes of 5xFAD (We have partially completed this objective) Prior to generating the required animal groups for this objective, we performed several preliminary studies to test the PTEN/PI3-K status following YKL-40 and Abeta(1-42) treatments. Treatments with either Abeta(1-42) or YKL-40 resulted in significant loss of cell viability and neurite attrition (Fig. 4 and S5). Furthermore, synaptic density and electrical properties of treated primary neurons were suppressed (Fig. 5). In terms of signaling effects, Abeta(1-42) significantly increased p-AKT473, p-P70S6K, p-S6, and p-STAT3 expression levels (Fig. S6A–B). However, YKL-40 only generated a modest effect and marginally enhanced p-P70S6K and p-S6 expression. No synergistic effect between Abeta(1-42) and YKL-40 was observed for the PI3-K/AKT pathway. However, the expression levels of p-P70S6K, p-S6, and p-Erk1/2 were significantly elevated following both treatments (Fig. S6A-B). PTEN expression was unchanged in different treatment groups. Reasons for underperformance for Objective 3: We proposed extensive mating between Pten knockout and 5XFAD mice. However, there were multiple events that had negatively impacted on our progress including, social movement, MHV-infection, followed by COVID-19 pandemic. Despite an extension of our project for 6 months, we simply did not have enough mice to support the mating experiments. Remedial actions taken: We uncovered that YKL-40 negatively regulates calcium signaling. There is a link between PI3-K and calcium signaling in astrocytes. Also, phagocytosis of Abeta by astrocytes is mediated by calcium signaling. Therefore, we have explored the interaction between YKL-40 and Abeta in regulating calcium signaling. The intracellular calcium levels [Ca2+]i in primary astrocytes treated with Abeta(1-42) or YKL-40 was monitored. Interestingly, while Abeta(1-42) could elevate [Ca2+]i levels, YKL-40 repressed it. Thus, knockout of YKL-40 would elevate [Ca2+]i and enhances phagocytosis of Abeta(1-42) resulting in its clearance and restoration of cognitive functions in AD mice. This is indeed what we observed in objective 4. Objective 4: To test the functional role of YKL-40 in activated astrocytes of 5xFAD (We have completed this objective) YKL-40 knockout reduces Abeta plaques and neuronal loss in 5xFAD mice - To explore the role of YKL-40 in 5xFAD, the Chi3l1 (YKL-40) gene was conditionally deleted in astrocytes of 5xFAD mice. The exon 5 of Chi3l1 was deleted by tamoxifen injection one week prior to the experiment (Fig. S7B, E). WT (Aldh-Cre;Chi3l1+/+) and heterozygous (Aldh-Cre;Chi3l1+/fl) mice had detectable YKL-40 expression in GFAP+ cells in both DG and TH regions (Fig. S7F-G). In contrast, YKL-40 knockout mice (Aldh-Cre;Chi3l1fl/fl) had drastically reduced YKL-40 expression in GFAP+ cells, suggesting effective knockout of this gene (Fig. S7F-G). By IF analysis, significant reductions in Abeta plaque numbers and sizes were observed in the DG region of 5xFAD;Aldh-cre;Chi3l1fl/fl mice (Fig. 6C-D, Fig. S8B). Immunostaining further showed significant restoration of NEUN immunoreactivity in 5xFAD;Aldh-cre;Chi3l1fl/fl knockout mice to a level similar to the WT (Fig. 7A–B). Also, significant increases in p-AMAPR in both cortical and hippocampal regions were observed in YKL-40 knockout 5xFAD mice compared with control 5xFAD mice (Fig. S9A–B). Furthermore, we observed significant decreases in glial activation in multiple brain regions of YKL-40 knockout 5xFAD mice via confocal microscopy (Fig. S10A–D). YKL-40 astrocyte-conditional knockout rescued cognitive deficits in 5xFAD mice - Morris water maze tests were conducted to examine whether the knockout of YKL-40 in astrocytes could rescue the memory deficits of 5xFAD mice. Memory deficits were defined by a reduced number of entries plus shortened latency to find the platform on day 5 (probe trial). No differences in escape latency between groups were observed on day 0 and day 1 (Fig. 8A&B). After four days of training, the escape latency of 5xFAD;Aldh-cre;Chi3l1fl/fl mice was significantly shortened compared with 5xFAD mice (Fig. 8C). On day 5, mice were allowed to explore the tank for 60 s following release from a fixed location (Fig. 8H). Deletion of YKL-40 increased the number of entries and reduced the escape latency of 5xFAD mice. Taken together, the improvement in spatial memory and learning ability of YKL-40 knockout 5xFAD mice support the detrimental effects of YKL-40 in the Abeta deposition.

14123718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14123718.value: There are three major outcomes from this funded proposal. First, we have established 5XFAD mouse line as an appropriate model to study the role of YKL-40 in Alzheimer’s Disease. Specifically, we observed increased YKL-40 expression in the cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, and hippocampal lysates of 7-month-old 5XFAD mice. Upregulated YKL-40 expression was correlated with activated astrocytes and heightened PI3-K/AKT signaling. In primary astrocytes, Abeta1-42 upregulated YKL-40 in a dose-dependent manner and was correlated with PI3-K signaling pathway activation and increased cytokine release. Second, we have uncovered the neurotoxic effects of YKL-40 by either acting alone or together with Abeta1-42. Specifically, primary neuron treatment with YKL-40 and/or Abeta1-42 resulted in significant synaptic degeneration, reduced dendritic complexity, and impaired electrical parameters. Indeed, the combination treatment with YKL-40 and Abeta1-42 appeared to exert synergistic effects in diminishing the electrical activities of primary cultured neurons. Thirdly and more importantly, the amyloid-beta burden was significantly reduced in multiple brain regions of 5xFAD mice with conditional knockout of Chi3l1 in their astrocytes compared with 5xFAD mice with functional Chi3l1. Furthermore, YKL-40 knockout attenuated glial activation, reduced neuronal attrition, and restored cognitive function. Our results provide new insights into the role of YKL-40 in AD pathogenesis and demonstrate the potential of this soluble biomarker as a therapeutic target to alleviate cognitive decline in AD patients.

14123718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14123718.value: The main finding of this funded project is that the knockout of YKL-40 in astrocytes caused a dramatic elimination of amyloid beta plaques and restoration of memory functions in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease, 5XFAD. We observed that YKL-40 knockout in astrocytes is associated with less activated astrocytes and reduced microglia. We would like to delineate the underlying mechanisms by which YKL-40 can exert its effects on astrocytes and microglia and particularly in the clearance of amyloid beta. We made the novel finding that while amyloid beta stimulates intracellular calcium levels in astrocytes, YKL-40 suppresses it. Since calcium signalling stimulates phagocytosis, we hypothesize that YKL-40 has a role in suppressing amyloid beta clearance in the brains of 5XFAD mice. Therefore, the knockout of YKL-40 enhances amyloid beta clearance and improves cognitive functions in 5XFAD mice. These new findings formed a part of a GRF grant proposal that was submitted in the GRF23/24 funding cycle. A more exciting aspect of our findings is the possibility of developing novel therapeutics targeting YKL-40 in the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. For this, we are planning to apply for funding to screen for small molecules that can block the action of YKL-40.

14123718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14123718.value: Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that afflicts the elderly population and poses considerable health care challenges in aging population. The main culprit of this disease is the deposition of toxic amyloid proteins in the brain. Previous studies have uncovered that the level of the YKL-40 protein present in the cerebral spinal fluid showed a significant association with the severity of Alzheimer’s disease. YKL-40 has been used as biomarker to predict disease outcome but little is known of its regulation and its biological actions in the brain. Our studies have identified a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease that recapitulates the association between YKL-40 and amyloid beta deposition. We further identified a key signalling molecule that could modulate YKL-40 expression in a specialized brain cell type called astrocyte. Further experiments demonstrated YKL-40 has destructive effects on neurons by damaging their elaborated synapses and ability to transmit electrical signals. More importantly, when we eliminated the YKL-40 gene in mice with Alzheimer’s disease, the toxic amyloid deposits were greatly reduced and the memory and cognitive functions were restored. Thus, we have identified a potential drug target for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
