14200218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200218.value: Human languages present natural forms of big data. They are highly complex and dynamic in nature, variable in form, and produced in massive volume everyday with vital economic and social value. Statistical language models (LMs) form key components of many human language technology applications such as speech recognition and machine translation. A central part of language modelling research is to appropriately model long-distance context dependencies. In recent years deep learning based techniques represented by recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are becoming increasingly popular. The successful application of deep learning techniques for language modelling also opens up a number of key research problems. In particular, the computational cost incurred in training and evaluation significantly limits their scalability and the number of applications. State-of-the-art deep neural network language models are becoming increasingly larger in size and complex in structure as the amount of training available increases. This presents a major challenge to speech technology based commercial products such as voice controlled virtual assistants and chatbots. In these product systems, computational efficiency and model compactness are crucial to reduce the latency in processing user requests as well as necessary storage demand. In contrast to our previous research focused on building large and complex RNN LMs using big data sets, this project aims to significantly improve their compactness and efficiency using novel compression techniques and model architectures. These include student-teacher based transfer learning from larger to smaller models, structured neural network weight matrices to reduce the overall number of parameters, temporal and between layer gating to dynamically compress the network’s depth. Multi-task adaptive training will be used to improve their robustness to varying contextual factors such as speech styles and topics without increasing the number of parameters. Efficient discriminative training techniques will also be used to further enhance their performance. An analysis of the trade-off between language model complexity and accuracy over proposed techniques on multiple speech recognition tasks will be performed. By exploiting varying amounts and styles of Big Data that are commonly used in commercial speech technology products, this analysis is expected to provide useful insights for designing compact deep language models in these practical systems. This proposal is the first attempt in the international speech technology community to derive compact and efficient forms of deep neural network language models to allow their wider application in commercial products. The proposed research will also contribute to other fields including machine learning, machine translation and natural language processing. 自然語言日常生活中被大量使用，高度複雜，結構異化，用法更新頻繁，是最常見的大數據種類。統計語言模型是眾多語音語言技術產品的重要組成部分。語言模型研究的核心問題是對長距離上下文信息的準確建模。近年來以第歸神經網絡為代表的基於深度學習語言模型已得到廣泛使用。同時也由此產生了眾多亟需解決的研究課題。特別是此類模型在大數據應用場景下結構愈發複雜。在訓練和使用時的產生的運算耗費嚴重制約其應用領域。難以在對模型緊湊性和計算效率有較高要求的商用產品系統中大規模使用。針對上述問題，本研究項目致力於有效提升深度學習語言模型緊湊型和計算效率的一系列新方法研究。研究內容包括基於轉移學習的深度語言模型壓縮技術，結構化深度語言模型參數共享算法，以及動態調整神經網絡語言模型有效複雜度的方法。上述算法在一系列語言模型公開數據集上的壓縮率和準確性能的分析和共享將為商用系統開發中緊湊型語言模型的設計提供指引和借鑑，因此兼具研究和實用價值。此外本研究項目還會對包括機器學習，機器翻譯和自然語言理解的相關領域研究有所幫助。

14200218.label: Realisation of objectives
14200218.value: 1. Optimising the trade-off between language model complexity, speed up and accuracy performance for Big Data of varying volumes and styles By formulating quantized RNNLMs training as an optimization problem, our research explored the use of a novel method to train quantized RNNLMs from scratch using alternating direction methods of multipliers (ADMM) [C1, Xu et al. IEEE ICASSP2020]. This method can also flexibly adjust the trade-off between the compression ratio and model performance using locally varying low-bit quantization tables learned among different groups of hidden layers or nodes. Experiments on two tasks: Penn Treebank (PTB), and Switchboard (SWBD) suggest the proposed ADMM quantization achieved a model size compression factor of up to 31 times over the full precision baseline RNNLMs. Faster convergence of 5 times in model training over the baseline binarized RNNLM quantization was also obtained. 2. Derive novel model architectures to improve the compactness and efficiency deep learning language models on large data sets When deploying deep neural network based language models in many application systems, another challenge arises from the sparsity of the limited training data. For deep neural networks, and many machine learning algorithms in general, this leads to modelling uncertainty and generalisation issues, when deterministic model structures and fixed valued parameter estimates are used. In order to address these issues, our recent research focused on deriving novel Bayesian deep learning approaches for language models. These approaches allow compact deep neural networks language models to be constructed on diverse and variable data by learning compactly shared distributions over DNN parameters, or their hidden outputs, rather than directly increase the underlying DNN model size as is prone to over-fitting and less efficient. First, the deterministic parameter estimates in LSTM RNNLMs are prone to over-fitting and poor generalisation when given limited training data. Furthermore, the precise forms of activations in LSTM have been largely empirically set for all cells at a global level. In order to address these issues, our research introduced Gaussian process (GP) LSTM RNNLMs [C2, Lam et al. IEEE ICASSP2019]. In addition to modelling parameter uncertainty under a Bayesian framework, it also allows the optimal forms of gates being automatically learned for individual LSTM cells. An efficient variational inference based training algorithm for GP-LSTM RNNLMs is also proposed. Experiments were conducted on three tasks: Penn Treebank (PTB) corpus, Switchboard conversational telephone speech (SWBD) and the AMI meeting room data. The proposed GP-LSTM RNNLMs consistently outperform the baseline LSTM RNNLMs in terms of both perplexity and word error rate. Second, another source of modelling uncertainty in deep neural networks can be found in the hidden layer representations. However, the deterministic model parameters and fixed hidden vectors in conventional RNNLMs have limited power in modeling the uncertainty over hidden representations. In order to address this issue, our recently published research at ISCA Interspeech2019 conducted a comparative study of parametric and hidden representation uncertainty modelling approaches based on Bayesian gates and variational RNNLMs [C3, Yu et al. ISCA INTERSPEECH2019]. Such comparative study is performed on long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent units (GRU) LMs. Experimental results were obtained on two tasks: PennTreebank (PTB) corpus, and Switchboard conversational telephone speech (SWBD). Consistent performance improvements were obtained over conventional RNNLMs in terms of both perplexity and word error rate. Furthermore, the Bayesian and Gaussian Process deep neural network modelling approaches were also extended to and studied in the context of the acoustic modelling and speaker adaptation tasks for speech recognition systems. Specifically, our research developed a novel full Bayesian framework to account for model uncertainty in sequence discriminative training of factored TDNN acoustic models [C4, C5, Hu et al. IEEE ICASSP2019, ISCA INTERSPEECH2019, J2, Hu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2021]. Model-based speaker adaptation approaches often require sufficient amounts of target speaker data to ensure robustness. Our research also developed a Bayesian learning based robust DNN speaker adaptation framework to model SD parameter uncertainty given limited speaker specific data [C8, Xie et al. IEEE ICASSP2019, IEEE ICASSP2019 Best Student Paper Award, J3, Xie et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2021]. 3. Efficient second order optimization methods for deep neural network language models Recurrent neural network language models (RNNLMs) are normally trained by minimizing the cross entropy (CE) using the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm. However, the SGD method doesn’t consider the correlation between parameters and therefore can lead to unstable and slow convergence in the training. Second order optimization methods such as limited memory BFGS (L-BFGS) provide a possible solution to this issue, but these methods are often computationally expensive. In our research (C6, Yu et al. IEEE ICASSP2019), a novel optimization method, stochastic natural gradient based on minimum variance assumption (SNGM) is proposed for training RNNLMs. It allows the natural gradient method to operate at a comparable training efficiency to the SGD method. By modifying the gradient according to the local curvature of the KL-divergence, the proposed SNGM approach is shown to outperform both the SGD and L-BFGS based second-order optimization methods across three tasks: Penn Treebank, Switchboard conversational speech recognition and AMI meeting room transcription in terms of both perplexity and word error rate. 4. provide insights and guidance for designing deep language models in practical systems developed by the industry. State-of-the-art neural network language models (NNLMs) represented by long short term memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNNs) and Transformers are becoming highly complex. They are prone to overfitting and poor generalization when given limited training data. To this end, an overarching full Bayesian learning framework encompassing three methods is developed in our research (J1, Xue et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP, C7, Xue et al. IEEE ICASSP2021) to account for the underlying uncertainty in both LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs. Experiments are conducted on multiple tasks: Switchboard conversational telephone speech, AMI meeting transcription and Oxford-BBC LipReading Sentences 2 (LRS2) overlapped speech recognition using state-of-the-art LF-MMI trained factored TDNN systems featuring data augmentation, speaker adaptation and audio-visual multi-channel beamforming for overlapped speech [J4, Yu et al. IEEE/ACM TASLP2021]. Consistent performance improvements over the baseline LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs with point estimated model parameters and drop-out regularization were obtained across both tasks in terms of perplexity and word error rate (WER). In particular, on the LRS2 data, statistically significant WER reductions up to 1.3% and 1.2% absolute (12.1% and 11.3% relative) were obtained over the baseline LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs respectively. In addition, the advantages of our Bayesian learning neural network language techniques were further illustrated in a series of ablation conducted across different training data quantity versus model complexity trade-off points. The performance improvements they produced were also found to be strongly correlated with the median signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the Gaussian approximated latent Transformer or LSTM-RMM language model parameter distributions. The accompanying software and example recipe have also been made publicly available. All the above efforts were made to provide insights and guidance for designing deep language models in practical industry systems target speech applications in a naturalistic user or task environment.

14200218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200218.value: State-of-the-art neural network language models (NNLMs) represented by long short term memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNNs) and Transformers are becoming highly complex. They are resource intensive in terms of both the quantity of training data and computation cost required to construct and practically deploy them in practical industry applications. In order to handle their data intensive nature, an overarching full Bayesian learning framework encompassing three methods is developed in our to account for the underlying uncertainty in both LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs [C2, C3, C7, J1]. The uncertainty over their model parameters, choice of neural activations and hidden output representations are modelled using Bayesian, Gaussian Process and variational LSTM-RNN or Transformer LMs respectively. Efficient inference approaches were used to allow the computational costs incurred in Bayesian NNLM training and evaluation to be minimized. Experiments are conducted on multiple state-of-the-art speech recognition tasks including Switchboard conversational telephone speech, AMI meeting transcription and Oxford-BBC LipReading Sentences 2 (LRS2) overlapped speech recognition using state-of-the-art LF-MMI trained factored TDNN systems featuring data augmentation, speaker adaptation and audio-visual multi-channel beamforming for overlapped speech [J4]. Consistent performance improvements over the baseline LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs with point estimated model parameters and drop-out regularization were obtained across all three tasks in terms of perplexity and word error rate (WER). Furthermore, the Bayesian and Gaussian Process deep neural network modelling approaches were also successfully applied to the acoustic modelling [J2, C4, C5] and speaker adaptation [J3, C8, C9] tasks for speech recognition systems. The second issue concerning the computational cost required have been addressed on two fronts in our research. First, a novel method to train low-bit quantized RNNLMs from scratch using alternating direction methods of multipliers (ADMM) [C1] was developed. This method can also flexibly adjust the trade-off between the compression ratio and model performance using locally varying low-bit quantization tables among different groups of hidden layers or nodes. Experiments on two tasks: Penn Treebank (PTB), and Switchboard (SWBD) suggest the proposed ADMM quantization achieved a model size compression factor of up to 31 times over the full precision baseline RNNLMs. Second, an efficient second order optimization method based on stochastic natural gradient was developed in our research [C6]. The approach is shown to outperform both the conventional SGD and L-BFGS based second-order optimization methods across three tasks: Penn Treebank, Switchboard conversational speech recognition and AMI meeting transcription in terms of both perplexity and word error rate.

14200218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200218.value: State-of-the-art neural network language models are highly resource intensive in terms of both the quantity of training data and computation cost required to construct and practically deploy them in practical industry applications. In order to handle their data intensive nature that makes them prone to overfitting, a full Bayesian learning neural language modelling framework encompassing three methods was developed to account for the underlying uncertainty in both LSTM-RNN and Transformer LMs. The advantages and genericity of the proposed approaches were extensively validated on language modelling, acoustic modelling and speaker adaptation tasks for speech recognition systems. The second issue concerning the computational cost required was addressed on two fronts in our research. First, our research explored the use of a novel method to train quantized RNNLMs from scratch using alternating direction methods of multipliers (ADMM). This method can also flexibly adjust the trade-off between compression ratio and performance using layer or node level locally varying low-bit quantization tables. Second, an efficient second order optimization method based on stochastic natural gradient was developed. These research outputs together with exemplar recipe system developments provide insights for designing deep language models in practical industry speech recognition systems targeting naturalistic user or task environments.

14200618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200618.value: Service robots have been attracting more and more attention in recent years. They are expected to carry out labor-intensive tasks in human-living environments, such as cleaning floors, mowing lawns, and delivering parcels. Unfortunately, it is usually difficult to achieve the desired performance for service robots due to immature robotics technologies. Recent progress in computer vision and artificial intelligence have made it possible to investigate feasible solutions for the immature robotic technologies that are of significance to service-robot applications. In the proposed research, we will focus on the scenario intelligence for service robots, and investigate the underlining theories as well as develop the enabling technologies to facilitate a robotic system. We constrain the scenario to autonomous untrained elevator operations in indoor office environments. The intelligence refers to the robotic capabilities to support autonomous operations. The innovative features in this project are the proposed solutions to the scenario intelligence. The key issues of the scenario intelligence in this project include the problems in environment perception, autonomous navigation, and robot-elevator interaction. The environment perception mainly involves the problem of robust Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) in dynamic environments. The autonomous navigation mainly concerns the problem of robotic exploration and the problem of the human-friendly motion planning in office environments. The robot-elevator interaction mainly comprises the problem of the visual detection and recognition of elevator buttons. The service robot is able to autonomously take the elevator to the destination floor without any modification to the elevator system in buildings. In order to test and evaluate the proposed solutions to the scenario intelligence, we will develop a service robot prototype in this proposed research. 近年來，服務機器人越來越受到關注。預計他們將在人類生活環境中執行勞動密集型任務，例如清潔地板，修剪草坪和交付包裹。遺憾的是，由於機器人技術的不成熟，服務機器人通常很難達到理想的性能。計算機視覺和人工智能的最新進展使我們有可能研究對服務機器人應用具有重要意義的機器人技術的可行解決方案。 在這項研究中，我們將重點關注服務機器人的場景智能，並研究強調理論以及開發支持機器人系統的關鍵技術。我們將場景限制在室內辦公環境中的自主未經訓練的電梯操作。智能指的是能夠支持自主操作的機器人能力。 該項目中情景智能的關鍵問題包括環境感知，自主導航和機器人-電梯交互等問題。環境感知主要涉及動態環境中的SLAM問題。自主導航主要涉及機器人探索的問題以及辦公環境中人性化運動規劃的問題。機器人-電梯交互主要包括視覺檢測和電梯按鈕識別的問題。服務機器人能夠自動地操作電梯到達目的地樓層而無需修改建築物中的電梯系統。為了測試和評估方案所提出的智能解決方案，我們將在此研究中開發服務機器人原型完成實驗驗證。

14200618.label: Realisation of objectives
14200618.value: Firstly, we propose a robust visual localization system based on a feature-based visual simultaneous localization and mapping algorithm to address the moving object issue. Because in practice, there are always some moving objects in the scenes, which significantly degrades the accuracy of the localization. In order to detect the dynamic part in the input frame, we designe a dynamic region detection method and used it to preprocess the input frame. The object detection process is implemented in a Bayesian framework that takes into account both prior knowledge and observational data generated by the process. Next, we explain the object detection process in detail. We generate object proposals using a deep neural network and an input frame named F_cur captured by the camera. We identify reliable frame regions based on the dynamic properties of each object. A Bayesian framework is fed with dynamic region proposals and prior regions obtained from object detection. Only the feature points extracted from the static region are used for further visual localization after the detection results are obtained. We run experiments on public TUM datasets as well as our own recorded datasets depicting daily dynamic scenarios. To demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method, qualitative and quantitative results are provided. Secondly, we develop an autonomous robotic exploration algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Most previous algorithms were greedy, with little regard for long-term forecasting. With our algorithm, the robot can predict the long-term visit order of unexplored subregions. With the help of DRL, our algorithm can learn exploration experience over building blueprints. Besides, we designed an exploration architecture that integrates a DRL model, a next-best-view (NBV) selection approach, and a structural integrity measurement to further improve the exploration performance. The workflow of our method is as follows: 1) The trained DRL model predicts a candidate subregion for the next-step visit based on the current states of the agent and grid map; 2) At the same time, a greedy strategy is used to include the closest subregion as a candidate; 3) The structural integrity measurement assigns a score to the two subregions; 4) A waypoint in the winner subregion is specified by the NBV selection algorithm; 5) The agent uses the A* algorithm to determine a local path from its current location to the waypoint. We compare our method to others on several new maps, demonstrating that the robot can efficiently explore uncertain regions with a shorter path and smarter behaviors. We also build a large-scale indoor layout dataset with 35,126 2D floor plans and 252,550 rooms to train the method. In addition, we create a lightweight and efficient simulation platform to accelerate the training process. Thirdly, we design a button recognition framework powered by a CNN-based semantic segmentation module and an attention-RNN-based Optical Character Recognition (OCR) module to address the elevator button recognition. The framework mainly consists of three modules, the segmentation module, the cropping module, and the OCR module. Firstly, the segmentation module segments the region of elevator buttons on the elevator panel image captured by the robot's RGB image sensor. Secondly, the cropping module finds each button's area by a density-based clustering algorithm. Image patches will be cropped based on the result of segmentation mask clustering. The OCR module will identify the corresponding button's label and function. We open source our dataset and simulation platform to the public to facilitate related research. Our proposed framework doesn't rely on the pre-defined button labels, which facilitate the capability of handling unseen panel structures and unseen button types. With the proposed framework, our autonomous system can recognize the buttons on an untrained elevator panel quickly and correctly. Finally, we designed and built a service robot prototype for autonomous operation in an indoor office environment. The prototype consists of a Kinova robotic arm with a three-finger grasping hand attached to the tip, a Segway RMP mobile platform, and a RealSense D435 camera. The Segway RMP mobile platform is equipped with a Hokuyo lidar for localization and mapping. The RealSense camera is mounted on the robotic arm right behind the grasping hand, and it is used to recognize the button labels and estimate the position of the buttons with respect to the arm. The mobile platform enables the robot to explore and navigate autonomously in the indoor environment. The robot arm enables the robot to manipulate the objects and operate the elevator. We implemented our method on the prototype and implemented a demo where the robot operated the elevator.

14200618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200618.value: We present a novel dynamic region detection method based on a Bayesian framework and considered both the intrinsic properties of objects and their current state. The proposed detection method is integrated into a feature-based visual SLAM system. The system as a whole improves positioning accuracy in a dynamic environment. We have released an Office dataset for the benefit of the community. This dataset represents the dynamic environment of daily work well and can be used for method validation. We propose a novel approach that combines the benefits of high-level global access order inference and low-level cross-regional planning. We use a DRL model to learn the common sense of office floor plans and successfully generalize the model to new cases by defining MDP on a heuristic graph. Furthermore, we design an NBV algorithm as a waypoint selection method that can be integrated into the exploration architecture. Compared with the traditional random sampling method, the algorithm has higher efficiency and accuracy. We also open source our training dataset and a simulation platform for the training of the model. We release the first large-scale publicly available elevator panel dataset, containing high-quality 3,718-panel images and 35,100 button labels. To benchmark future methods and facilitate related research on escalator operation, we also publish baseline implementations and evaluation metrics for button segmentation and recognition. In order to provide a reference for other researchers in this field, we also design a robot prototype that can be used for indoor navigation and elevator operation and also implement a demo for operating elevators.

14200618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200618.value: In the future, we will improve the current algorithm to make it more robust in extremely difficult environments. Combining the dynamic localization problem with other challenges, such as low-texture environments, is another way to improve our method. In addition, we will create a deep model to learn the relationship between the settings and scene information, allowing us to apply our method to a wider range of environments. As for the future work of the autonomous exploration system, first, the MDP formulation and A3C training process can be improved further by employing inverse reinforcement learning techniques; data scale and network capacity must also be increased. Second, the time efficiency of exploring the architecture should be greatly improved, leaving us plenty of room for further improvement. For elevator button recognition and pose estimation, we will use a new network with stronger feature extraction capability for feature extraction and optimize the network structure to improve accuracy. Finally, the currently designed robot prototype still has a lot of room for improvement. In future work, we will simplify its hardware structure and add new sensors to enable it to perform more complex tasks.

14200618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200618.value: This project designs an intelligent robot system, including software designs and a hardware prototype. The research of this project provides several new methods to solve the problems in the real-world application of the robot. The proposed methods enable the robot to perform complex tasks more efficiently and smartly. Undoubtedly, the deployment of indoor service robots will significantly facilitate human life, and this project shows the possibility that the service robot can be helpful in the daily life of people. Besides, this project also provides a reference for future research in this field.

14200718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200718.value: Remanufacturing is an industrial process that restores end-of-life goods to their original working condition. Due to its large economic and environmental values, remanufacturing has been widely adopted in many industries (e.g., consumer products, electrical apparatus, machinery, and motor vehicle parts) in recent years. In response to the industrial needs, researchers started to study hybrid manufacturing and remanufacturing inventory systems as early as 1970s. Most of the existing studies assume that the manufacturing and remanufacturing operations have identical lead times. While facilitating technical tractability, this assumption can only be justified for systems where manufacturing and remanufacturing have comparable lead times. In many realistic systems, however, the remanufacturing lead time can be significantly shorter or longer than the manufacturing lead time. Thus, it is practically very important to study hybrid manufacturing/remanufacturing systems with different lead times. Motivated by the observations that the studies on systems with different lead times are very limited and there exist few analytical results and effective heuristics, in this project we propose to conduct a comprehensive and in-depth study on periodic-review finite-horizon hybrid manufacturing/remanufacturing systems with different lead times. Depending on the lead-time relation, we separately study the systems with longer manufacturing lead time and the systems with longer remanufacturing lead time. For each class of the systems, we further divide it into two subclasses: the systems with consecutive lead times (i.e., the lead-time difference is one period) and the systems with nonconsecutive lead times. For the first subclass, since the system state only consists of two variables, we propose to characterize the detailed structure of the optimal policy to better understand and more efficiently compute it. For the second subclass, the system state is high-dimensional and the optimal policy is intractable due to the curse of dimensionality. Hence, we propose to develop effective heuristics for managing this subclass of systems. If successful, this project will not only significantly contribute to the literature on hybrid manufacturing/remanufacturing inventory systems, but also have a broad impact on practitioners by providing effective decision tools for managing these systems. 再製造是一種將報廢產品恢復至最初工作狀態的工業過程。由於其巨大的經濟和環境價值，近年來再製造已廣泛應用于許多行業（如：消費品、電器設備、機械和自動車部件）。為滿足工業需求，研究人員早在二十世紀七十年代便開始研究混合製造與再製造庫存系統。大多數現有文獻都假定製造和再製造過程具有相同的提前期。儘管便於技術上的處理，這一假定只適用於製造提前期和再製造提前期差不多相同的系統。然而，在許多實際系統中，再製造提前期可以顯著地長或者短與製造提前期。因此，研究具有不同提前期的混合製造與再製造库存系统具有重要的實踐意義。考慮到現有文獻對具有不同提前期的混合系統的研究非常有限並且非常缺乏相關的理論結果和有效的啟發式算法，我們建議在這一項目中對按週期盤點的有限週期的具有不同提前期的混合製造與再製造系統進行全面深入的研究。根據提前期的大小關係，我們將分別研究具有較長製造提前期的系統和具有較長再製造提前期的系統。對每一類系統，我們進一步將其分為兩個子類：具有連續提前期（即提前期相差一個週期）的系統和具有非連續提前期的系統。對于第一個子類，由於系統狀態可以通過兩個變量來描述，我們建議詳細刻畫最優控制策略的結構以便更好地理解及更有效地計算它。對于第二個子類，系統的狀態變量是高維的；受限於維數災難，最優策略在計算上是不可行的。因此，我們建議開發有效的啟發式算法來管理這類系統。如果獲得成功，這一項目將不僅在學術上對混合製造與再製造庫存系統的研究產生重要貢獻，而且通過提供有效的管理這些系統的決策工具對行業實踐者產生積極影響。

14200718.label: Realisation of objectives
14200718.value: First, I, the project Co-I and another collaborator, characterize the structures of the optimal policy for the two systems where manufacturing lead times are one period longer or shorter than remanufacturing lead times. For the system with longer manufacturing lead times, we fully characterize the optimal policy by two control curves and identify conditions under which one or both control curves have a simple structure. For the system with longer remanufacturing lead times, we also fully characterize the optimal policy by two control curves and connect it with the optimal policy for an auxiliary dual-sourcing system with consecutive lead times. These results satisfactorily achieve our objectives 1 and 2. Second, for the general system with longer manufacturing lead times, we construct an auxiliary two-echelon inventory system. We show that the optimal cost of the original hybrid system is lower bounded by that of the auxiliary system minus a linear function of pipeline inventories. Further, we identify conditions under which the two systems are equivalent or asymptotically equivalent. Based on these results, we apply the optimal policy for the auxiliary two-echelon system (i.e., an echelon base-stock policy) as a heuristic policy for controlling the original hybrid system. Our extensive numerical study shows that this heuristic policy performs very close to optimal over a wide range of parameter settings. In addition, the lower bound we develop via the auxiliary system is also consistently close to the optimal cost of the original system. These results satisfactorily achieve objective 3. Third, for the general system with longer remanufacturing lead times, we construct an auxiliary dual-sourcing system with general lead times and further approximate its optimal ordering quantities by using two dual-sourcing systems with consecutive lead times. Then, we construct a heuristic policy for the original system based on the connections between the original and auxiliary systems. Our numerical studies show that this heuristic policy performs close to optimal when the lead-time difference between manufacturing and remanufacturing operations is small. When the lead-time difference is large, it performs comparably well to an existing heuristic policy in the literature. These results satisfactorily achieve our objective 4. It is important to mention that this project was severely affected by the outbreak of COVID-19. It started in January 2019 and ended in June 2022. During this period, the project PI was unable to visit Co-I and attend conferences physically as planned. As a result, the proposed budget for general expenses and conference expenses was left largely unspent. COVID-19 also made it very difficult to hire research assistants and invite collaborators to work on this project as planned. Consequently, around 40 percent of the proposed budget for the staff cost was also left unspent by the end of the project. On the other hand, COVID-19 also largely slowed down the progress of the project. While we are now satisfied with the results of the project, we are still in the process of writing a high-quality paper for publication in a top-tier journal in my field.

14200718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200718.value: For the system where the manufacturing lead times are one period longer than the remanufacturing lead times, we fully characterize the optimal policy and identify conditions under which it has a simple structure. For the general system with longer manufacturing lead times, we construct an auxiliary two-echelon inventory system. Based on this auxiliary system, we derive a lower bound on the optimal cost for the original system and propose a simple heuristic policy. Our extensive numerical results show that both the lower bound and our proposed heuristic policy perform very well. For the system where the remanufacturing lead times are one period longer than the manufacturing lead times, we also fully characterize the optimal policy and connect it with the optimal policy for an auxiliary dual-sourcing system with consecutive lead times. For the general system with longer remanufacturing lead times, we develop a heuristic policy based on its connections to an auxiliary dual-sourcing system with general lead times. Our numerical studies show that this heuristic policy performs comparably well to an existing heuristic policy in the literature. My co-authors and I are working hard to write a high-quality paper to report the above results. We expect to complete a working paper by the end of this year and then submit it for publication in the journal Operations Research (a top-tier journal in my field). This project directly led to two other outcomes as follows. First, as mentioned in the mid-term report, my Ph.D. student, Ms. Suting Liu, and I have been working on a related project on hybrid manufacturing and remanufacturing systems with random capacities. We have finished a working paper from this project, and the paper is currently under Major Revision in Production and Operations Management (a top-tier journal in my field). Second, this project also motivated me to collaborate with my colleague, Prof. Sean X. Zhou to write an invited review chapter titled “Inventory Models with Returns and Remanufacturing” for the book “Research Handbook on Inventory Management” edited by Prof. Jeannette Song. The book is scheduled to be published by Edward Elgar Publishing in August 2023. Please refer to Part C for details. Finally, this project also partially funded the PI’s four other related projects, which led to several top-tier research publications. All these publications have acknowledged the partial funding support from this research project. Please refer to the “Other Impact” section of Part C for details.

14200718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200718.value: First, there is still room for further investigating the general hybrid inventory with longer remanufacturing lead times. In this project, we approximate this system by an auxiliary dual-sourcing inventory system with general lead times (which is in turn further approximated by two dual-sourcing inventory systems with consecutive lead times). This approximation enables us to develop a simple heuristic policy for the original system. However, we believe that there is still room for developing more effective heuristic policies (preferably with theoretical performance guarantees) for this system. To this end, new ideas and insights into hybrid inventory systems with longer remanufacturing lead times are needed. We leave this investigation as future research. Second, it is valuable to investigate infinite-horizon inventory systems under a discounted or long-run-average cost criterion. This project has focused on finite-horizon systems with non-stationary data. Some but limited existing studies considered infinite-horizon systems with non-identical lead times and stationary data. In some sense, these systems are simpler than the finite-horizon systems studied in this project because the former assumes stationary data. We expect that our research findings in this project can be partly extended to the infinite-horizon systems. We also leave this investigation as future research.

14200718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200718.value: Hybrid manufacturing/remanufacturing inventory systems are a class of practically important yet challenging inventory systems. For tractability, most of the existing studies consider systems with identical manufacturing and remanufacturing lead times. In many realistic systems, however, the two lead times are non-identical and can differ significantly. This project conducts a comprehensive study on periodic-review inventory systems with different manufacturing and remanufacturing lead times. For systems with consecutive lead times, we characterize the structures of the optimal inventory policy. By extending the insights derived from these simpler systems, we propose simple heuristic inventory policies for systems with general non-identical lead times. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed heuristic policies through analytical and numerical studies. Our research findings provide new insights into the control of hybrid manufacturing/remanufacturing inventory systems with non-identical lead times, and they also provide effective tools for practitioners to manage these systems.

14201118.label: Project Objectives
14201118.value: Different multiuser relay networks with SWIPT We would first consider a general relay network model, and would then specialize into different network models according to different intended applications. Our general model can cover many commonly encountered networks, e.g. the downlink of an access point, the uplink of an access point, multiple access points, the two-way relay network, and etc. Feasibility and optimization in SWIPT multiuser relay networks We would investigate the feasibility and the optimization problems in SWIPT multiuser relay networks. Practical constraints, such as transmission power limits, signal-to-noise ratio requirements, harvested energy requirements, and etc., would determine whether a system is feasible. For feasible systems, the optimization of transmission power, transmitting beamformers, receiving beamformers, and etc., would enhance the performance of the system. Admission control and scheduling in SWIPT multiuser relay networks When the system is not feasible, we cannot support all the users simultaneously. We would have to perform admission control and/or scheduling. Admission control can be applied to remove users that cannot be satisfied by the system while scheduling can be used to put users into different appropriate time slots to be served. SWIPT multiuser relay networks for mobile edge computing (MEC) As more and more devices supply get connected (e.g., with the development of Internet of Things), new applications emerge. Some of these applications could require intensive computation where mobile edge computing (MEC) has been perceived as the solution. MEC models may also be covered under our general model. Besides the previously mentioned optimization problems, devices, especially those with limited energy supply, would also need to decide which tasks to offload to MEC servers, giving an additional dimension for the system to be optimized.

Admission control can be applied to remove users that cannot be satisfied by the system while scheduling can be used to put users into different appropriate time slots to be served.

SWIPT multiuser relay networks for mobile edge computing (MEC) As more and more devices supply get connected (e.g., with the development of Internet of Things), new applications emerge. Some of these applications could require intensive computation where mobile edge computing (MEC) has been perceived as the solution. MEC models may also be covered under our general model. Besides the previously mentioned optimization problems, devices, especially those with limited energy supply, would also need to decide which tasks to offload to MEC servers, giving an additional dimension for the system to be optimized.

In many cases, relays would be employed to enhance the communication, resulting in relay networks. Of particular interest is the multiuser relay network where multiple users or nodes share the same relays. While many devices require communication, not all of them have a steady supply of power. Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) has been considered in a number of situations in the literature. In this project, we would like to perform a thorough investigation of SWIPT in multiuser relay networks. We would investigate different scenarios where SWIPT can be employed in multiuser relay networks. We would look into the feasibility, the optimization, the admission control, and the scheduling problems in these networks. We would also explore its potential application in mobile edge computing. 14201118.label: Realisation of objectives
14201118.value: According to our first and fourth objectives, we have investigated many different systems with simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) and mobile edge computing (MEC). Throughout this project, we have worked on broadcast networks with SWIPT, relay networks with SWIPT, MEC systems with SWIPT, etc. Indeed, our related publications [1 – 4, 6,7] are on SWIPT and/or MEC systems. According to our second objective, for each system, we have investigated feasibility and strategies to optimize the performance of the relevant system. For example, in [1], we optimized the sum offloading rate or the sum mobile energy consumption by joint radio-and-computation resource allocation. User scheduling, offloading data size control, and time allocation were also among the optimization variables involved. In [4], we increased the total harvested energy with a new design to manage interference. Our scheme employed network coding to cancel the undesired effects of the interfering signals over a finite field during demodulation while it preserved the physical interfering signals, which were used as energy sources for energy harvesting. By optimizing the network code, we tried to maximized the energy harvested. In [7], we investigated how short packets should be jointly coded to improve the age of information (AoI). By optimizing the number of packets to be jointly coded, we optimize the AoI without sacrificing the amount of energy harvested. Actually, in all our systems, we strived to optimize the performance where the objective could be the maximization of the throughput, the maximization of the harvested energy, the minimization of mobile energy consumption, or the minimization of migration costs, etc. Depending on the system model, the optimization variables can be the data precoding, the transmit beamformers, the relay processing matrices, the receive beamformers, scheduling, data size control, bandwidth allocation, etc. We also considered a number of admission control and scheduling problems, according to our third objective, especially for MEC systems or for systems with service migration. For example, in [1], we considered the optimization of an MEC system. The offloading decision was an admission problem, and the users admitted to offload data were scheduled properly for optimal system performance. The resultant algorithms jointly scheduled offloading users, controlled their offloading sizes, and divided time for communication (offloading and downloading) and computation. In [2], we considered service migration where the decision to perform service migration (or not) involved an admission problem, and actual migration also involved a scheduling problem. The policy design was formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem that maximized the sum offloading rate, quantifying MEC throughput, and minimized the migration cost, where the issues of virtualization, I/O interference between virtual machines (VMs), and wireless multi-access were taken into account. In [3], we tackled the mobility management problem in MEC systems where the potential service migration again involved admission and scheduling problems. We employed a Lyapunov-based framework to decompose the problem into different timescales, based on which a low complexity two-timescale online algorithm was developed by exploiting the problem structure. 14201118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201118.value: The project has resulted in seven international journal and conference papers, including four IEEE Transactions full papers, one IEEE letter and two IEEE conference papers. One postgraduate student, who was heavily involved in this project, has graduated with his Ph. D. degree. In [1,2,3,6], we have published significant results on mobile edge computing (MEC) systems. In [1], we studied the problem of joint radio-and-computation resource allocation in multiuser MEC systems in the presence of I/O interference, which was largely ignored before. In [2,6], we considered user mobility so that the offloaded tasks could be seamlessly migrated between MEC servers without compromising the resource-utilization efficiency and link reliability. In [3], we proposed a two-timescale mobility management framework by joint control of service migration and transmission power. The service migration operated at a large timescale to support user mobility in the multi-cell network, while the power control was performed at a small timescale for real-time task offloading. In [4], we proposed a novel way to manage interference in simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) systems by utilizing physical-layer network coding (PNC). Our scheme cancelled the undesired effects of the interfering signals over a finite field during PNC demodulation for while preserving the physical interfering signals which were beneficial energy sources for energy harvesting. In [7], we investigated the information freshness and energy harvesting (EH) in downlink Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Information freshness was measured by Age of Information (AoI). We demonstrated the tradeoff between AoI and EH by examining the number of packets to be jointly coded. The techniques developed in this project were also useful in other areas and resulted in [5].

14201318.value: Wireless communications are the transfer of information or power between two or more points that are not connected. Wireless technologies use radio frequency (RF) waves or microwaves and operate in the megahertz to gigahertz frequency (GHz) ranges. 5th generation (5G) wireless systems are the proposed next mobile standards beyond the current 4G/LTE. Not only will 5G improve smartphones capabilities and introduce new high bandwidth applications, it will drive the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) — billions of connected devices. The idea of Internet of Space (IoS) is the natural progression of the vision to extend Internet access to all members of humans. The 5G radio access network will be a combination of technologies, nodes and frequencies. More bandwidth will be needed, which will require new and better microwave components. These new technological challenges call for an increasing number of elements per device and higher level of integration. Thus, it is important that the size and cost of the elements continue to decrease. Wireless communications using satellites are experiencing a very similar technological revolution. The global satellite industry has introduced high throughput satellites (HTS) with spot beams to provide wireless IoS. Companies like SpaceX (founded by Elon Musk), Oneweb (backed by Softbank), LEOSAT and many others around the world (including China) have detailed ambitious plans to bring IoS to the entire world with a new satellite system that offers greater speeds and lower latency than the existing networks. It will launch thousands of small satellites into low-Earth orbits, with altitudes less than 1000 miles. The microwave subsystem in each satellite functions like a wireless base station, which requires mass production capabilities. This paradigm shift drives the technology convergence from ground to space. 14201418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201418.value: Multi-agent control systems arise from numerous engineering applications such as synchronized motion of multiple robots, formation flying of multiple fight vehicles, mobile sensor area coverage, control of power grids, etc. It has been a central control problem since the early 2000s. A typical multi-agent system contains a follower system consisting of multiple subsystems called followers and a leader system that provides the reference signals to the followers. What makes the control of multi-agent systems challenging is that the control law has to be distributed in order to satisfy communication constraints. Recently, the PI has developed a so-called distributed observe based framework for designing the distributed control law for complex multi-agent systems. This framework reduces the almost intractable task of designing a distributed control law for complex systems to the task of designing a conventional control law for a single system and a much more trackable task of designing an adaptive distributed observer for a leader system. The adaptive distributed observer for a leader system is a dynamic compensator that is capable of providing both the system’s dynamics and the state of the leader to each follower while satisfying communications constraints. It turns out that this framework is quite effective in dealing with several cooperative control problems for complex multi-agent systems. Nevertheless, the existing adaptive distributed observer has two drawbacks. First, it relies on the state of the leader system, which is impractical in some applications when only the output of the leader system is available. Second, the observer is over-parameterized in the sense that it needs to estimate excessively many parameters. To overcome the first drawback, we first propose a so-called output-based adaptive distributed observer for the leader system, which only relies on the output instead of the state of the leader. To overcome the second drawback, we further propose a minimal dimensional output based adaptive distributed observer for the leader system. Among many merits, the second observer only needs to estimate the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of the system matrix of the leader instead of the system matrix of the leader, thus drastically reducing the dimension of the observer. Moreover, we will apply these two observers to several cooperative control problems such as the cooperative output regulation problem for heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems, the leader-following consensus problem for Euler-Lagrange systems, and the attitude synchronization of multiple spacecraft systems.

All the three objectives are achieved as reported in 4 journal papers and 4 conference papers. Specifically, the major findings are summarized as follows: The conference paper 4 has developed an output based adaptive distributed observer over switching networks, and has thus achieved the first objective. The main findings of journal paper 2 are summarized as follows: A minimal dimension output based adaptive distributed output observer has been developed, which, in contrast to the existing adaptive distributed observer, can drastically reduce the dimension of the observer as well as the information exchange among agents. As a direct application, we solve the attitude consensus problem of multiple rigid body systems utilizing this minimal dimension output based adaptive distributed output observer. Thus, these two papers have successfully achieved the first two objectives. We have also achieved the third objective and the main finding are reported in journal papers 1 to 3 and conference paper 1. 14201418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201418.value: We will expand the scope of the research in the following two directions. 1. This project has only considered the design of the continuous-time control law. As almost all control laws are implemented by digital control law, the first expansion is the digital implementation of the control law by the sampled-data control law. This expansion is ongoing. 2. In this project, we have established an output-based adaptive-distributed-observer for a known leader system. It is more interesting and more practical to establish an output-based adaptive-distributed-observer for an unknown leader system. This generalization is under way.

14201418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201418.value: The cooperative control of multi-agent systems has been one of the central control problems since the 2000, and it includes but is not limited to such problems as consensus/synchronization, formation, and cooperative output regulation. A specific challenge to the control of a multi-agent system is that the control law must satisfy disconnected switching communication constraints. Such a control law is called distributed control law. To overcome this challenge, we proposed a so-called adaptive distributed observer approach, which systematically converted the design of the distributed control law to the so-called decentralized control law and a dynamic compensator called adaptive-distributed-observer. Nevertheless, the existing adaptive-distributed-observer has two drawbacks. First, it relies on the state of the leader system, which is impractical in some applications when only the output of the leader system is available. Second, the observer is over-parameterized in the sense that it needs to estimate excessively many parameters. To overcome these two drawbacks, we have developed a minimal dimensional output-based adaptive-distributed-observer for the leader system. This novel adaptive-distributed-observer effectively overcomes the two drawbacks. The outcome of this project has been applied to the cooperative output regulation problem for linear multi-agent systems, and the attitude synchronization of multiple spacecraft systems.

14201818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201818.value: The explosive growth of the number of multimedia-capable and Internet-connected mobile devices has led to the tremendous increase in wireless data traffic in recent years. Given the looming radio-frequency (RF) spectrum crunch, great efforts have been made to explore supplementary techniques for future wireless communications. Due to the low atmospheric attenuation and license-free regulation in visible light frequencies, visible light communication (VLC), also known as light fidelity (LiFi), has drawn extensive research interests from both academia and industry. One main attraction of VLC is that we can equip the widely-deployed light source with communication capability, yet not affecting its primary lighting function. Similarly, most of the prior works on VLC utilize photodiodes (PDs) for the purpose of signal reception. Is it possible to use widely-deployed but non-communication-oriented optical detectors for VLC receiver? Solar-panel is one attractive candidate because of its worldwide rapid deployment in various scenarios, including buildings, transportations, the “Internet of Things” (IoT), and aerospace applications. By using the photovoltaic effect of solar-panel, dual functionality of data communication and energy harvesting can be realized, thus enabling seamless communication function of self-powered IoT devices for smart cities. Another potential candidate for the signal detection in VLC is the complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor, which has been widely used in smartphones, tablets, dashboard cameras and surveillance cameras. Image-sensor based VLC provides a promising solution for ubiquitous data communication when integrated with real-time surveillance/video recording in future smart cities. In the literature, the investigation of solar-panel/image-sensor based VLC, especially the systematic transceiver design and the advanced signal processing, is still in a relatively nascent stage. To unleash its full potential, systematic and extensive research is required. In this project, the topics to be addressed include the following. (1) Theoretical modeling of solar-panel and image-sensor based VLC, aiming to provide frameworks to analyze and evaluate the system performance. (2) System design and advanced signal processing for solar-panel based VLC. The joint optimization of optical wireless energy harvesting and data communication will be investigated. (3) Capacity maximization techniques including advanced modulation and multi-dimensional multiplexing for image-sensor based VLC. Investigations of both the in-lab and realistic scenarios will be performed for the latter two topics. This project will also strengthen the research collaboration with internal and overseas institutions, including Tianjin University on the solar-panel based VLC and National Chiao Tung University on the image-sensor based VLC, to ensure the successful delivery of this project. 近年來，具有聯網功能的多媒體移動終端的數量顯著增加，移動數據流量也因此不斷地急劇增長。鑑於有限的無線射頻頻譜資源，在研發未來無線通信的替代/補充技術方面，學界和工業界均付出了巨大的努力。由於可見光波段具有低大氣損耗和免頻譜許可等特性，可見光通信技術（亦稱為LiFi技術）引起了廣泛的研究興趣。可見光通信技術的一大優勢在於它可以在不影響基本照明功能的前提下，通過現已普及的LED光源實現高速無線通信。當前，大部分關於可見光通信的研究均採用光電二極管來實現信號接收。是否可以同樣利用現已普及但未用於通信用途的光接收器來實現可見光通信的信號檢測呢？太陽能電池板是一種有吸引力的候選，因其已在全球範圍內的建築物、交通系統、物聯網及航天等諸多應用中被廣泛使用。通過利用太陽能電池板的光伏效應，可以實現數據通信和能量收集的雙重功能，從而為智慧城市中的自主供電的物聯網設備實現無縫通信提供了可能。另一種可行的光接收器是圖像傳感器，其亦已廣泛應用於智能手機、平板電腦、行車記錄儀及監控攝像頭等產品中。基於圖像傳感器的可見光通信技術為實現無處不在的數據通信提供了一種非常有前景的解決方案，因其可以與未來智慧城市中的實時視頻監測/拍攝系統結合。目前，針對基於太陽能電池板/圖像傳感器的可見光通信的研究，特別是在系統收發器的設計和先進信號處理等方面，仍相對處於初期階段。為了發掘該技術的應用潛力，仍需進行廣泛的研究。 本項目將系統地研究以下課題：（1）基於太陽能電池板和圖像傳感器的可見光通信技術的理論建模，旨在建立一個有效的系統架構以分析和評估系統性能；（2）關於基於太陽能電池板的可見光通信系統的系統設計及先進信號處理，以及針對系統能量儲存功能及數據通信能力的聯合優化。（3）關於基於圖像傳感器的可見光通信系統的容量最大化技術的研究，包括先進調製技術及多維復用技術等。本項目的研究將包括實驗室演示以及實際環境驗證等。 本項目也將加強課題組與海內外高校的科研合作，包括將與天津大學開展基於太陽能電池板的可見光通信系統的聯合研究，以及將與國立交通大學合作研究基於圖像傳感器的可見光通信系統，確保本項目的順利實施。

14201818.label: Realisation of objectives
14201818.value: Objective 1 To understand and model the solar-panel-based and the image-sensor-based VLC systems, aiming to develop the theoretical framework and identify the dominant factors that affect the system performance. • [Solar-panel-based VLC system] We characterized the solar panel as a photodetector for VLC. In this study, we have theoretically analyzed the nonlinear distortion of the self-powered solar panel (working in photovoltaic mode), showing that it suffers from nonlinear distortion because the output voltage increases logarithmically with the illuminance [1]. It is shown that the nonlinear distortion is more exacerbated when illuminance is low, covering the indoor illuminance region. To overcome this issue, we have proposed four types of compensation methods, namely, distortion compensation local-light, post-distortion compensation, passive diode compensation, and programmable anti-logarithm linearization circuit (PALC). • [Image-sensor-based VLC system] We have investigated the rolling shutter mechanism and developed a theoretical model [2]. The time-domain channel response and frequency-domain channel response can be simulated for given exposure time and readout time. We have also derived an SNR model for the image-sensor-based VLC system. The optical power of the LED light source was derived based on the Lambertian emission pattern. Multiple noise sources are considered in the SNR model, including photon shot noise, dark current shot noise, read noise, dark signal non-uniformity, and photon response non-uniformity. However, since the current smartphone employs powerful post-processing techniques and these algorithms are not disclosed, it is infeasible to derive a precise SNR model for the image-sensor-based VLC system and verify the effectiveness. Objective 2 To design and develop solar panel-based self-powered VLC receiver, with emphasis on (1) Joint optimization of energy harvesting and data communication. (2) Advanced DSP to boost the achievable speed. • We have implemented a supercapacitor-based charger circuit to collect power from a solar panel. It was demonstrated that a single charged supercapacitor could power a microprocessor with a display feature for one minute. The MCU system can continuously work if the solar panel is constantly exposed to a large illuminance. • As stated in objective 1, solar panels employed for simultaneous energy harvesting and communication devices suffer from nonlinear distortion. In addition, the bandwidth is severely limited in solar panels due to the large physical area. The severe bandwidth limit in solar panels was overcome by employing multilevel PAM4 signals with linear equalization. This bandwidth-efficient communication requires high signal linearity. We proposed two compensation methods to achieve higher device linearity: local light compensation and post distortion compensation. Based on the proposed DSP techniques, a 1.0-Mbit/s transmission link was demonstrated using a solar panel with six kHz 3-dB bandwidth [1]. We proposed a compensation scheme using a passive diode array in advance for solar panel receivers with a limited power budget and achieved one order BER reduction for a 1.0-Mbit/s transmission link [3]. Objective 3 To investigate and develop advanced DSP techniques for capacity maximization in image-sensor-based VLC. The integration of the developed solutions and the existing infrastructure networks will be studied. We target to achieve more than Mbit/s transmissions using the built-in camera of smart devices. • We proposed a DSP algorithm, double equalization, to improve the performance of the monochromatic-LED-to-camera system [4,5]. The double equalization targets amplitude-variation mitigation due to nonuniform illuminance and the inter-symbol interference induced by the rolling shutter effect, thus leading to BER performance improvement for the adaptive thresholding scheme. This realized the objective of developing advanced DSP techniques for data rate maximization. • To resolve the capacity limitation issue, we investigated the performance enhancement of the multiplexing scheme in the image-sensor-based system. For the color-division multiplexing scheme, 2D CNN was employed and experimentally demonstrated to address the ISI and ICI issue, attaining the best BER performance among the state-of-the-art techniques [6]. Furthermore, we proposed an XOR-based coding scheme for data loss compensation to fully leverage the effective image capturing duration and maximize the system capacity. To optimize the transmission performance, we also employed the color space conversion to transfer RGB signals to YCbCr/CIElab color space to maximize the minimum Euclidean distance [7]. An optical companding scheme that accommodates three RGB LEDs was proposed to realize spatial and color multiplexing, which attained a high data rate of 111 kbit/s [8]. • We also demonstrated a real-time NLOS image-sensor-based system to transmit text information [9]. To improve the efficiency of the algorithms, the decoding process is divided into multiple steps running in multithreading and asynchronous mode. Moreover, we proposed an efficient four-level flicker mitigation coding scheme and achieved comparable flicker detection probability but with a higher transmission data rate than the OOK signals[10]. • We realized a 1.2-Mbit/s screen-to-camera communication system that transmits 201×201 barcodes on a 14-inch laptop monitor at 30 fps. A smartphone captures the barcode at 120 fps with a frame resolution of 1080ⅹ1920. This realized the objective of achieving Mbps image-sensor-based VLC system. The drawback of the scheme is that the fast-changing barcodes will cause visual flickers to human eyes. Therefore, we focused more on LED-to-camera communication system because LED lighting is widely distributed and can combine illumination and communication simultaneously. [1] S. Chen, L. Liu, and L. 14201818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201818.value: In this project, we investigated DSP, coding schemes, and multiplexing schemes for image-sensor-based VLC systems to improve the data rate and robustness. We have also characterized the linearity characteristic of a solar panel and verified it experimentally. It is shown that the linearity strongly depends on the illuminance and direct current (DC) bias of the PV module. The main findings and outcomes are: • DSP and coding schemes To mitigate amplitude fluctuation, we have proposed a double-equalization algorithm to compensate for the spatial and temporal dispersion, realizing 14-kbit/s transmission over 1 m [J1, C2]. In [C1], a 10.74-kb/s 4-color shift keying transmission has been achieved with the assistance of a QPSK-like 2D constellation in YCbCr/CIElab color space. Furthermore, we have proposed an XOR-based data loss compensation scheme to restore the data loss during the gap time, realizing a 21% data rate improvement compared with the conventional repetitive transmission [J2]. For visual flicker, we have proposed a four-level flicker mitigation scheme that realized a data rate of 13.72 kbit/s with a 65% improvement compared with the two-level scheme [C5]. • Data rate enhancement schemes To further increase the data rate, we have developed a color multiplexing system augmenting the RGB LEDs and proposed a convolutional neural network to resolve inter-color and inter-symbol interference [J2]. We also have demonstrated an optical companding scheme to accommodate multiple RGB LEDs, effectively boosting the transmission data rate from 37 kbit/s to 111 kbit/s [C3]. Moreover, we have proposed and experimentally demonstrated a 156.50-kbit/s image-sensor-based VLC system using a name-card size plastic fiber array for spatial multiplexing. This work was submitted to IPC 2022. • Real-time implementation We have developed a real-time NLOS image-sensor-based VLC system, Li-poster, allowing retrieval of descriptions from complex optical signals reflected by an exhibition poster or artwork using a hand-held smartphone [C4]. • Nonlinear compensation for solar-panel-based VLC We showed that PV modules exhibit nonlinear optical-to-electrical conversion in VLC receivers under low illuminance [J3]. Degradation in communication performance was investigated under different illuminance. The reduction of distortion-induced BER degradation was realized via DSP approaches. Nonlinear compensation was also realized by a passive diode array for low energy consumption scenarios [C6]. Please note that the papers [J3] and [C6] did not acknowledge RGC but both papers were accepted in November and December, within 6 months after the project completion date (June 30, 2021), and well before the deadline of the completion report (June 30, 2022). RGC's acknowledgment was not included due to PI's negligence.

14201818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201818.value: For solar panel-based VLC systems, the switching circuit between energy harvesting and communication can be implemented. Moreover, nonlinear compensation technologies can be well selected to fit indoor/outdoor scenarios. For further solar panel modeling, we can investigate the effect of solar panel layout (serial/parallel) connection and the effect on signal detection when the solar panel is partly shaded. Such modeling will give a clearer picture of how to optimize the layout of the solar cells and how to mitigate related degradations. For image-sensor-based VLC, the user mobility issue will be considered when designing the transmission system, aiming to support several users simultaneously. In the latest smartphones, significant improvement has been achieved for image stabilization in a video to allow the light source to stay at a more static location in the image sensor. The proposed signal processing algorithms, like FAST and double equalization, also need modification to make them adaptive to the user movement. Nowadays, mainstream smartphones are equipped with multiple rear cameras to improve the quality of photos. Albeit preliminary results have been obtained for multicamera OCC, it is interesting to research methods to unleash the full potential of multi-camera architecture to improve communication performance.

14201818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201818.value: For solar panel VLC systems, it is of high interest to use solar panels as VLC receivers since solar panels are now widely used in several applications such as satellites, power plants, and mobile IoT devices. The transmission link built-in solar panel allows a simultaneous energy harvesting feature. It is also a substitution for scenarios where radio frequency does not perform well and requires high alignment tolerance between transmitter and receiver. Our investigation allows performance enhancement when solar panels experience illumination variation indoors or outdoors by using adaptive nonlinear compensation techniques to decrease the probability of transmission error. Th image-sensor-based VLC system is a promising technology to provide location-based service for users in time using a camera as the receiver. Nowadays, there are 5.22 billion unique mobile phone users in the world. The image-sensor-based VLC links can be established ubiquitously by using widely distributed LEDs and smartphones. For example, in museums or galleries, users can obtain data for augmented reality applications by capturing the reflected light that embeds content-related information. In this project, we investigated the limiting factors of image-sensor-based VLC systems and proposed various signal processing, coding, and multiplexing schemes to significantly improve data rate and robustness.

14201918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201918.value: Computational design generally refers to the applications of science and computational methods to support object design and fabrication. It is a multi-disciplinary topic, emerging not only in computer graphics research, but also in architecture and manufacturing. This project explores a novel computational design problem. Our target is the LEGO Technic system. Its assembly is very different from those with regular LEGO bricks, since LEGO Technic models involve complex connections in beam structures, a diverse set of bricks, and a very different building style. Over decades, they have been shown to be highly inspiring and valuable for STEM-based education with LEGO robotics and for constructing a wide variety of nontrivial LEGO machines. However, designing Technic models is very challenging and requires tedious manual effort due to their complexity. The goal of this project is to develop computational methods and tools to support the design and construction of LEGO Technic models for both static and dynamic assemblies, as well as for various application scenarios. We will approach the problem in four tasks, each focusing on one particular aspect in designing LEGO Technic models. In Task 1, we aim to develop methods with optimization models to arrange and connect Technic bricks into a static frame that resembles user input sketches. In Task 2, we will focus on enhancing the structural integrity through a force analysis and by developing methods to maximize the rigid connections and to add in reinforcement beams. In Task 3, we will enumerate existing Technic motion patterns and develop methods to compute and realize them with Technic bricks such as gears. In Task 4, we will explore and demonstrate the power of computational design in three application scenarios. In the end, we will evaluate our results by producing both virtual and physical Technic models and by conducting physical experiments on the resulting models. 設計計算(Computational Design)是通過科學方法和計算方法的應用，以支持對象物件的設計和製造。這是一個多學科的專業，不僅應用在計算機圖形學研究中，還應用在建築和製造業中。該學科探索一種新穎的設計計算問題。在這項研究工作中，我們的目標是樂高技術(LEGO Technic)系統的三維構造設計。由於樂高技術模型涉及複雜的結構連接，多種磚塊，以及非常不同的構造風格，因此，其裝配與常規樂高積木是非常不同的。幾十年來，由於樂高技術模型具有極高的啟發性和價值，它已經被使用於機器人技術，STEM教育以及構建各種複雜的樂高機器。然而，設計樂高技術模型是非常具挑戰性且相當複雜，故通常需要繁瑣的人手設計。 這研究項目的目標是開發樂高技術模型的自動計算方法和工具，以支持該模型的設計和構建，當中包括靜態和動態組件，以及各種應用情況。我們將在四個任務中解決各個不同的相關問題，而每個任務都將集中於設計樂高技術模型的一個特定範籌。在任務一中，我們的目標是開發具有優化樂高技術模型的方法，以根據用戶輸入草圖的框架，自動設計樂高技術模型磚塊的三維排列和連接。在任務二中，我們將重點關注於力學分析和計算方法，以優化結構完整性和連接並增加加固結構。在任務三中，我們將羅列樂高技術模型的運動模式，並開發使用動態磚塊（如齒輪）的計算和實現它們的自動化設計方法。在任務四中，我們將在不同應用場景中探索和實現設計計算的強大功能。最後，我們將通過生成虛擬和真實三維模型以及對生成模型進行物理實驗來評估我們的結果。

14201918.label: Realisation of objectives
14201918.value: This project aims for developing computational methods for constructing LEGO Technic models, so the project involves 3D designs, 3D object creation, and also 3D geometry analysis and processing. First, we design the world's first computational method that is able to automatically compute and design LEGO Technic models from user input sketches, optionally with motion annotations. The LEGO Technical models generated by our method resemble the input sketches with coherently-connected bricks and simple layouts, while respecting the intended symmetry and mechanical properties expressed in the inputs. The challenge of the research work is that the computational assembly problem involves an immense search space and a very rich set of bricks and connection mechanisms more than regular LEGO bricks. In this project, we first comprehensively model the brick properties and connection mechanisms, then formulate the construction requirements into an objective function, accounting for the faithfulness of the generated model to the input sketch, model simplicity, and structural integrity. Further, we model the problem as a sketch cover by iteratively refining a random initial layout to cover the input sketch. Also, we create a working system to analyze the balance, stress, and assemblability of the generated model. In the end, we evaluate our approach by comparing it with baselines and professional designs to demonstrate the superiority of our automatic designs. We produced a collection of LEGO models, built most of them, and showcased our results and method in several university and department demonstrations, a television programme, and some newspaper media. Besides, we innovated a new computational solution for cost-efficient 3D fabrication, in which our idea is to automatically partition a 3D model into a thin shell of residual volume and internal core, with universal blocks such as LEGO bricks to fill the internal and 3D-printed parts to fill the external shell. By this means, we can quickly construct the internal core with massively-prefabricated bricks at a low cost (compared with 3D printing material) and improve the cost and speed to fabricate 3D-printed objects. Further, we begin to explore deep-learning-based approaches and introduce the first neural optimization framework to solve a classical instance of the tiling problem. The core idea is to is reformulate tiling as a graph problem by modeling candidate tile locations in the target shape as graph nodes and connectivity between adjacent tile locations as edges, such that object assembly becomes a graph node selection problem. Hence, we formulate a graph convolutional neural network (GNN) to propagate and aggregate features over graph edges for predicting which potential tiles to be selected for producing the final object assembly. Further, we study a general form of gears called non-circular gears (NCG) for transferring periodic motion with variable speed through their irregular shapes and eccentric rotation centers. In this work, we model the geometry, kinematics, and dynamics of non-circular gears, formulate the design problem for NCG as a shape optimization, and identify necessary independent variables in the optimization search. Our optimized models not only resemble the inputs but can also drive the motion with relatively small torques. Also, we explore various methods on geometry analysis and learning-based computation. First, we derive a novel approach to learn and detect distinctive regions on 3D shapes by analyzing point sets sampled from 3D shapes and formulating a deep neural network for unsupervised shape clustering to learn local and global features. Also, we formulate an encoding-and-decoding framework with pyramidal deformable fusion to exploit long-range correspondences between views, a quantization layer to suppress the restoring artifacts, and the compression noise simulation module to resist the compression noise in a self-supervised fashion. Next, we design a novel approach for augmented virtual reality by analyzing the physical environment in the user's egocentric view through depth sensing and deep learning, acquiring the layout and geometry of the surrounding objects, and further exploring their affordance, for creating visual guidance and hybrid user interfaces to augment the user interaction. Further, we derive an edge branch in our point cloud processing framework to predict semantic labels on points by hierarchically integrating point features and generating edge features and enabling the feature interactions between the edge branch and point branch. Also, we innovate the idea of automatically augmenting 3D point clouds for neural network framework, such that we can automatically optimize and augment point cloud samples to enrich the data diversity when we train a downstream classification network. Besides, we developed a fast and accurate single-stage 3D object detector and a novel disentanglement approach for the 3D point cloud upsampling task by formulating two cascaded sub-networks.
