14201918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201918.value: This project produced 6 journal and 10 conference papers: five papers in ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG) and one in Eurographics (Computer Graphics Forum (CGF)), as well as some in CVPR and ICCV. Note that top-tier conferences such as SIGGRAPH/SIGGRAPH Asia and Eurographics publish the accepted papers in ACM TOG and CGF, respectively. First, we summarize major findings in 3D fabrication and LEGO construction: - [J01]/[C01] presents the world's first fully automatic method that is capable of constructing LEGO Technic designs that resemble user input sketches, such that the generated designs are built by coherently-connected LEGO Technic bricks that respect the symmetry and structural integrity of the models, while aiming for minimalistic layouts. - [J02]/[C02] introduces a new solution for cost-efficient 3D fabrication by employing universal blocks (including LEGO bricks), levering massive prefabrication at low cost to quickly assemble and constitute a significant internal core of the target object. - [J03]/[C03] presents the first neural optimization framework to solve a classical instance of the tiling problem; we explore deep learning to construct tile-based and LEGO-based computational assembly. - [J06]/[C05] presents a novel computational method for designing non-circular gears by modeling the geometry, kinematics, and dynamics, and formulating a shape optimization with necessary independent variables. Second, we summarize major findings on geometry analysis and learning-based computation: - [J04] presents a novel approach to learn and detect distinctive regions on 3D shapes by formulating an analysis on point samples and a neural network for unsupervised shape clustering. - [J05]/[C04] presents an encoding-and-decoding framework with the pyramidal-deformable-fusion module, a quantization layer, and compression noise simulation module. - [C06] proposes a novel approach that analyzes the environment in user's egocentric view, acquires the layout and geometry of surrounding objects and further explores their affordance. - [C07] presents an edge branch to predicting labels on 3D points by hierarchically integrating point features and generating edge features, enabling feature interactions between the edge and point branches. - [C08] presents a novel auto-augmentation framework that automatically optimizes and augments point cloud samples to enrich the data diversity when training a downstream network. - [C09] proposes a fast and accurate single-stage 3D object detector with the lightweight module to fuse high- and low-level features, rectify predicted confidence, smooth regressions, and avoid redundant predictions. - [C10] presents a novel disentanglement approach for point cloud upsampling by formulating two cascaded sub-networks to infer a coarse but dense result and further fine-tune it.

14201918.value: This project aims for developing computational fabrication methods for designing LEGO Technic models. We have successfully developed the first method that can automatically compute and design LEGO Technic models from user input sketches, optionally with motion annotations. The LEGO Technic models generated by our method resemble the input sketches with coherently-connected bricks and simple layouts, while respecting the intended symmetry and mechanical properties expressed in the inputs. 14202218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202218.value: Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) has become increasingly important since the soar of the machine learning popularity and the tremendous speedup of machine learning algorithms with FPGA implementations. With its flexibility in re-programming and the availability of an unprecedentedly massive amount of computational logic, FPGA has found to be very useful in application specific implementations such as deep learning and data center. However, the place and route of FPGA is a crucial step affecting the performance of the circuit. While the FPGA architectures become more complex, more sophisticated placement methods are needed. We propose to develop a flat analytical routability-driven and multi-clock domain aware placer for today’s heterogeneous FPGAs. As the computational logic in FPGAs has increased tremendously, its gap with ASICs (Application Specific Integrated Circuits) is significantly reduced, and it is challenging to study how the analytical placement approaches, which have been successfully applied in general ASIC placements, can be applied in FPGA designs. Multi-clock domains, routability and timing are issues to be considered in order to secure performance. The impact of machine learning on artificial intelligence and our everyday life has become far-reaching. FPGAs, with high performance per unit power and high ability in customization for different applications, are ideal choices to serve as hardware acceleration platforms for machine learning problems. FPGA architectures can be reconfigured and tailored for different machine learning algorithms. Techniques that explore low-level hardware controlled operations can be realized with FPGAs. However, all these advantages come at a cost of relatively longer FPGA compilation (includes placement and routing) time comparing with GPU and CPU. Users will definitely need to iterate a number of times during the design cycle. With analytical placement, we target at shortening the placement time and also to favor incremental placement that allows re-use of some pre-compiled kernels which are common in deep learning applications. The success of this project will contribute to the AI community and also will definitely move forward the advancement of the EDA community. 隨著機器學習的迅速普及以及基於FPGA實現的對機器學習算法的大量加速，現場可編程門陣列（FPGA）變得越來越重要。憑借其在重新編程方面的靈活性以及超大量計算邏輯的可用性，FPGA已經發現在例如深度學習和數據中心等特定的應用中非常有用。然而，FPGA的布局和布線是影響電路性能的關鍵步驟。隨著FPGA架構變得越來越復雜，我們需要更復雜的布局方法。我們提出為當今的異構FPGA開發一個扁平化的可分析的由繞線驅動和多時鐘域感知的布線器。隨著FPGA中計算邏輯的不斷增加，其與ASIC（專用集成電路）的差距顯著縮小，研究如何將已成功應用於通用ASIC布局的分析型布局方法應用於FPGA設計是具有挑戰性的。以確保性能，多時鐘領域，可繞線和時序都是需要考慮的問題。 機器學習對人工智能和日常生活已經有很深遠的影響。具有單位功率下的高性能表現和適用於不同的應用的高定制能力的FPGA是機器學習問題的硬件加速平臺的最佳選擇。FPGA架構可以針對不同的機器學習算法進行重新配置和定制。探索低級硬件控制操作的技術可以通過FPGA實現。然而，與GPU和CPU相比，所有這些優勢都需要相對較長的FPGA編譯（包括布局和布線）時間。在設計周期中，用戶肯定需要多次叠代。通過分析布局，我們的目標是縮短布局時間，並且支持逐步更新的布局，並允許重復使用深度學習應用程序中常見的一些預編譯內核。該項目的成功實現將為AI做出貢獻，並且肯定會推動EDA的發展。

14202218.label: Realisation of objectives
14202218.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved. We developed a routability-driven FPGA placer, called RippleFPGA, based on our ASIC placer Ripple. As a good tradeoff between central processing unit (CPU) and application specific integrated circuit (ASIC), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) become widely used in both industry and academia. The increasing complexity and scale of modern FPGAs impose great challenges on the FPGA placement and packing problem. We developed RippleFPGA to solve the packing and placement problem simultaneously through a set of novel techniques: 1) smooth stair-step flow; 2) implicit packing similar to ASIC legalization (LG); and 3) two-level detailed placement (DP). To enable the flow, an efficient legality check is proposed. Some FPGA-routing-architecture-aware optimization techniques are proposed to improve routability. When evaluated by ISPD 2016 Contest benchmarks, RippleFPGA has 5.1% better routed wirelength and 5.5× speedup compared to the state-of-the-art academia FPGA placers. We have also worked on the problem of clock domain-driven placement on FPGAs. As the complexity and scale of circuits keep growing, clocking architectures of FPGAs have become more complex to meet the timing requirement. To optimize wirelength and to meet emerging clocking architectural constraints, we propose several detailed placement techniques: two-step clock constraint legalization and chain move. After integrating these techniques into our FPGA placement framework, experimental results on ISPD 2017 benchmarks show that our proposed approach yields 2.3% shorter routed wirelength and the running time is 2× faster compared to the first place winner in the ISPD 2017 contest. We have also explored the possibilities to use machine learning-based methods to predict routing congestion in UltraScale FPGAs. Experimental results on both ISPD 2016 and ISPD 2017 benchmarks show that our proposed congestion estimation model is a good approximation to the one obtained from a popular commercial tool and can improve the placement results. For data path driven placement problem, we study and develop an effective bus routing method named MARCH which can efficiently route data paths handling practical issues like minimum spacing and minimum wire width on metal layers with irregular track structures. The objective is to finish routing all the buses which can represent data paths, maintaining the same topology for different bits of a bus while optimizing metrics like wire length, wire segment number and compactness of the buses. We propose MARCH, which routes all the bits in a bus concurrently, instead of processing bit after bit. Such concurrency directly captures the topology consistency constraint together with other objectives (e.g. wire length) and constraints (e.g. spacing) in a correct-by-construction manner. A hierarchical framework is designed for efficiency, consisting of a Topology-Aware Path planning stage (TAP) and a Track Assignment for Bits stage (TAB). TAP is efficient as it works on a coarse-grained solution space. TAB generates fine-grained routing solution, but it also gains efficiency by searching on the regions provided by TAB only.

14202218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202218.value: An analytical framework is proposed and developed to optimize the system clock period globally for the multi-FPGA TDM optimization problem. It first generates a continuous result of the TDM ratios with minimized system clock period under relaxed constraints. A discretization algorithm is then applied to remove all the constraint violations. Finally, a swapping-based post refinement is performed to further optimize the TDM ratios. Compared to previous works, our approach supports wires with a user given set of TDM ratios, which is more practical in modern FPGA systems. Experimental results show that our framework can achieve high quality with short runtime compared to the optimal LP-based methods. Our framework scales for designs with over 45,000 inter-FPGA nets while the running time and memory usage of the LP-based methods will increase dramatically for large designs. In terms of multi-clock domain constraint on FPGA placement, as the complexity and scale of circuits keep growing, clocking architectures of FPGAs have become more complex to meet the timing requirement. In order to optimize wirelength and to meet emerging clocking architectural constraints, we propose several detailed placement techniques, i.e., two-step clock constraint legalization and chain move. After integrating these techniques into our FPGA placement framework, experimental results on ISPD 2017 benchmarks show that our proposed approach yields shorter routed wirelength and faster running time compared to other academia placers. We also used machine learning-based methods to predict routing congestion in UltraScale FPGAs. Experimental results on both ISPD 2016 and ISPD 2017 benchmarks show a good approximation of these machine learning based methods to the real congestion measures obtained by Vivado and can lead to better placement results compared to other previous methods. [Please refer to 8.1 in Part C, 9.1-2 in Part C] The continuous development of modern VLSI and AI technology has brought new challenges for on-chip interconnections with data paths. Different from classic net-by-net routing, data path routing requires all the nets (bits) in the same bus to share similar or even the same topology, forming a very regular path, besides considering wire length, via count, and other design rules. We developed an efficient maze routing method under a concurrent and hierarchical scheme for buses. In order to achieve the same topology, all the bits in a bus are routed concurrently like marching in a path. For efficiency, our method is hierarchical, consisting of a coarse-grained topology-aware path planning and a fine-grained track assignment for bits. An effective rip-up and reroute scheme is applied to further improve the solution quality. In experimental results, MARCH significantly outperforms others in both quality and running time. [Please refer 8.2 in Part C, 9.3-5 in Part C]

14202218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202218.value: Some applications like circuit emulation and large AI network model training require placing a huge circuit in a many-FPGA system. Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM) is a widely used method for transferring multiple signals over a common wire in multiple FPGA systems. The circuit performance will be significantly influenced by this inter-FPGA delay. Some inter-FPGA nets are driven by different clocks, in which case they cannot share the same wire. Future works can be on placement and routing on these many-FPGA systems. First, a TDM-aware partitioning algorithm is needed to minimize the maximum cut size between FPGA-pairs. A TDM ratio assignment method is needed to assign TDM ratio for each inter-FPGA net effectively. Further research and development in this direction of handling systems with many FPGAs will be very much needed.

14202218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202218.value: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA) is an integrated circuit designed to be reconfigurable by a customer after manufacturing. FPGA is a good trade-off between performance and cost due to its faster time-to-market and simpler design cycle, and is becoming more important for applications such as deep learning, data center and circuit emulation. Routability is always an issue in placement for FPGAs. We developed several placement techniques for ultrascale heterogeneous FPGAs to meet the challenges of clock constraints, routability and wirelength. We integrate all the techniques into our framework RippleFPGA. The experimental results show that our algorithm can achieve better quality and running time compared to other academia FPGA placers. Moreover, our machine learning-based congestion model can approximate the routing estimation of a commercial tool well and can guide RippleFPGA to generate good placement results.

14202518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202518.value: Continuous-time (CT) Delta-Sigma modulators (DSMs) offer benefits of constant input impedance, anti-aliasing capability and high power efficiency, and are extensively used for high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion in a variety of applications including audio and mobile communications. This project will investigate a new class of CT DSMs with a revolutionary design capable of solving a number of major problems simultaneously. We intend to investigate the potential of CT DSMs which employ a passive switched-capacitor (SC) low-pass filter (LPF) in the feedback. CT DSMs with a feedback LPF have been reported before, but our new class is distinguished from its predecessors that the feedback LPF is a passive SC one. The feedback SC LPF realizes a pole for the modulator’s loop filter and produces a very small signal at the first integrator’s input, thereby reducing the number of amplifiers required and relaxing the speed and linearity requirements of the crucial first amplifier. For these reasons, it has the potential to significantly improve the power efficiency of a CT DSM. We also intend to resolve the circuit non-idealities of clock jitter and inter-symbol interference (ISI). Clock jitter is a critical performance barrier to wide bandwidth CT DSMs. Existing solutions have sacrificed the modulator’s anti-aliasing capability and power efficiency. We expect our proposed SC LPF approach to achieve an optimal solution by delivering immunity to clock jitter while retaining anti-aliasing capability and reducing power consumption. It will also be immune to the ISI arising from asymmetric rising and falling clock edges, enabling a very high performance to be achieved without the need for calibration. This approach will resolve almost every major design problem in a CT DSM, leaving thermal noise as the ultimate performance limit of the modulator. We will test our theories in this project by developing two prototypes of the new class of CT DSMs in CMOS, one for high-performance audio applications and the other for wideband mobile communications. In both cases we intend to surpass existing records for power efficiency. We will also develop a new active-RC CT DSM architecture with a passive RC LPF in the feedback, which will offer high power efficiency, anti-aliasing ability and simplicity, but not immunities to clock jitter and ISI. Our findings are expected to place Hong Kong at the forefront of R&D on DSMs. They will also spur further research into this new class of CT DSMs, aimed at developing new industry standards.

14202518.label: Realisation of objectives
14202518.value: We have fully realized the four project objectives. First, we have developed a new CT DSM architecture that features a passive SC LPF for both the feedback signal and the input signal. The new architecture solves the degraded aliasing performance and power efficiency when an SC type of DAC is applied in the main feedback path of a CT DSM, while retaining the immunities of the SC DAC to clock jitter and ISI. It is the first time that high power efficiency and immunities to clock jitter, ISI and aliasing are achieved simultaneously for a CT DSM. Second, we have designed an audio-band Gm-C CT DSM with a passive SC LPF as the first stage in a 0.18-µm CMOS. Operating from a 1.8V supply, the CT DSM consumes only 49µW, and achieves an SNDR of 95dB over a 25kHz bandwidth at a sampling rate of 12.8MHz in post-layout simulations. Its energy efficiency is 182dB in terms of Schreier’s figure of merit, and 21.3fJ/conversion-step in terms of Warden’s figure of merit, which were the best among the state-of-the-art audio-band CT DSMs at the time of publication (2019). It achieves this performance under a relaxed clock jitter requirement. The modulator was not fabricated, as the design has been published by us with rigorous post-layout simulations that confirmed these properties. Third, we have realized and fabricated a 200kHz bandwidth Gm-C CT DSM with a passive SC LPF as the first stage in a 65-nm CMOS process for applications in Bluetooth transceivers. The CT DSM employs a novel intrinsically-highly linear multi-level SC DAC. The modulator was designed with 40× oversampling. The Gm-C CT DSM consumes 22.8 μW from a 1.2-V supply, and achieves an SFDR of 86.6dB, a DR of 85.1dB, and an SNDR of 78.8dB. It measured an alias rejection of 52dB and 58dB at the sampling frequency (fs) and twice the fs, respectively, and can tolerate a clock jitter of 3ns. Its Warden’s and Schreier’s figure of merits, representing its power efficiency, were 16fJ/conversion-step and 181.5dB, respectively, being the best among state-of-the-art CT DSMs at the time of publication (2019). It is noted that the bandwidth of this design is different from the original planning (2MHz). This is because we realized a 2MHz CT DSM by another architecture and wished to test the Gm-C architecture for Internet-of-things applications (200kHz). Fourth, we have developed a new active-RC CT DSM architecture with a passive RC LPF as the first stage. The new architecture employs a large capacitor at the virtual ground node of the first amplifier in the active-RC DSM to form the passive LPF. With this new circuit structure, the transconductance and output swing requirements of the crucial first amplifier can be significantly relaxed. In addition, the technique reduces an amplifier and eliminates the problems associated with the parasitic pole. We have realized and demonstrated such a DSM with 2-MHz bandwidth in a 0.18-µm CMOS technology for Bluetooth transceiver applications. Clocked at 320 MHz, the DSM achieves a measured SNDR of 78.7 dB, a DR of 79.8dB and an SFDR of 88.4 dB while consuming 0.59 mW from a 1.8V supply. The recorded Warden's and Schreier's figures of merit were 20.1 fJ/Conv-step and 174 dB, respectively, which is among the best of the state-of-the-art CT DSM with similar bandwidth. The alias rejection is greater than 60dB as a resistive feedback DAC was adopted. In addition, we have developed low-power circuit techniques for respiratory monitoring and always-on voice activity detection.

14202518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202518.value: In this project, we have produced the following circuit and system techniques for CT DSMs and beyond. First, we have proposed a new circuit architecture for CT DSMs that features a passive lowpass filter (LPF) as the first stage. The new architecture leads to improved performance and power efficiency. It solves the long-lasting problem of alias rejection degradation of a CT DSM when an SC DAC is applied. An SC DAC is well known for its immunities to clock jitter and ISI, but damages the power efficiency and inherent anti-aliasing property, two major advantages of CT DSMs. With the proposed system technique, a CT DSM can maintain the alias rejection for the first time while taking the benefits of an SC DAC. The proposed system technique further improves the power efficiency of a CT DSM. In this project, we have reported several variants of the new CT CSM architecture with the common essential feature of a passive LPF first stage. These discoveries are reported in Papers 8.1, 8.2, and 8.5. Second, we have developed a number of linearization techniques for a multi-level DAC in a CT DSM. The DAC is the performance-defining element in a DSM, so many techniques have been reported in the literature to improve the linearity when the DAC is of multiple levels.. However, the existing technique always comes at a price, such as extra testing cost, excessive loop delay, and increased power consumption. In this project, we have developed the world’s first 5-level SC DAC circuit that is intrinsically highly linear. We have reported the technique in Paper 8.2. The technique is not limited to the use in CT DSMs, but can be applied in other DAC applications in general. Furthermore, we have developed a power-saving technique for the proposed 5-level DAC and reported the technique in Paper 9.2. Apart from the 5-level DAC, we have reported other DAC linearization techniques in Papers 8.3 and 9.1. The new system and circuit techniques enabled us to develop CT DSMs in standard low-cost CMOS processed with record-breaking power efficiency, as reported in Papers 8.2 and 8.5. The project has also led to low-power circuit techniques for respiratory monitoring and always-on voice activity detection. A highly efficient envelope-to-digital converter circuit was discovered for respiratory monitoring, as reported in Paper 8.4. A low-power SC acoustic feature extraction circuit was developed for always-on voice activity detection, as reported in Paper 8.6.

14202518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202518.value: The circuit and system techniques developed in this project have been successfully demonstrated in CT DSMs with bandwidth lower than 10MHz. However, both the CT DSM circuit architecture of a passive LPF first stage and the multi-level DAC circuit have great potential to enable high performance and power efficiency in CT DSMs with a much wider bandwidth, e.g., 100MHz. It will be highly valuable to extend this research into the wideband regime.

14202518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202518.value: This project is about developing continuous-time Delta-Sigma modulators (CT DSMs), an important type of analog-to-digital converters for high resolution and low power consumption over a moderate bandwidth. This project has discovered several new circuit- and system- techniques that significantly improve the performance and power efficiency of CT DSMs. We solved some important long-lasting problems in the design of CT DSMs. They include: (a) the aliasing rejection degradation caused by the use of a switched-capacitor digital-to-analog converter (DAC); (b) a DAC could not achieve a high intrinsic linearity when the number of its conversion levels exceeds three. The developed techniques enabled us to demonstrate high-performance CT DSMs (fabricated in standard low-cost CMOS processes) with record-breaking power efficiency. The developed techniques can help extend the battery life of many electronic devices that need a CT DSM, including internet-of-things devices, Bluetooth ear sets, etc. The proposed DAC techniques can be applied in applications beyond CT DSMs for reduced cost, power, and latency. Furthermore, the project has discovered circuit techniques to achieve ultra-low power consumption for devices with respiratory monitoring and voice activity detection functions, which are increasingly popular in intelligent internet-of-things devices.

14202818.label: Realisation of objectives
14202818.value: We have fully accomplished the objectives of the proposal. - We have synthesized single crystalline bismuth selenide (Bi2Se3) nanoribbons via the Au-catalyzed vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) method in a three-zone horizontal tube furnace. Bi2Se3 powders (99.999%) were placed in the hot center of the tube furnace. A silicon wafer coated with Au nanoparticles with a diameter of roughly 20 nm was used as the growth substrate, which was placed in the cold zone of the furnace, i.e., 12 cm away from the center. The tube was initially pumped down to a base pressure of about 10^-2 mbar. With an argon gas flow of 50 sccm, the hot center of the furnace was heated to 580°C and then held at this temperature for about 1 hour with a pressure of 100 mbar. After that, the furnace was naturally cooled down and a layer of Bi2Se3 nanoribbons was formed on the silicon substrate. In this project, we have tried to tune the thermoelectric properties of Bi2Se3 nanoribbons through helium ion irradiation and copper intercalation/deintercalation. - We have performed helium ion irradiation and reversible copper intercalation/deintercalation on individual Bi2Se3 nanoribbons to tune their thermal and electrical transport properties. An as-synthesized Bi2Se3 nanoribbon (the pristine nanoribbon) was placed onto a suspended micro-device. Then, the micro-device with the nanoribbon was irradiated under a 15 keV helium ion beam with a dose of 10^16 ions/cm2. As high-energy helium ions penetrate through the thin Bi2Se3 nanoribbon, Bi and Se vacancies will be generated in the nanoribbon, which will affect the carrier concentration, mobility, and thermoelectric properties of the nanoribbon. Moreover, Cu atoms were intercalated into the layered chalcogenide Bi2Se3 nanoribbons by using a solution-based chemical method. To allow for comparison, a uniform Bi2Se3 nanoribbon with a length of tens of microns was cut into three segments using an in-house built micromanipulator. One segment was directly transferred onto a suspended micro-device for thermal and electrical measurements (i.e., the pristine nanoribbon). The other two segments were placed onto a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate for subsequent Cu intercalation. Quintuple layers of alternating Bi and Se planes stack along the thickness direction of the Bi2Se3 nanoribbon via van der Waals forces. The large van der Waals gaps are suitable sites for Cu intercalation. Cu intercalation proceeds through the generation of metal atoms in a dilute precursor solution by a disproportionation redox reaction. In a typical Cu intercalation process, the substrate was soaked into a 10 mM solution of tetrakis(acetonitrile)copper(I) hexafluorophosphate (J&K Scientific) in acetone (Sigma-Aldrich) and was kept at 50°C under reflux for 5 min. Then, the PDMS substrate was removed from the solution and washed immediately by hot ethanol (Sigma-Aldrich) and hot acetone. One intercalated nanoribbon was transferred onto a micro-device for measurements (i.e., the intercalated one). The de-intercalation reaction was performed on the remaining segment for comparison. Specifically, a small amount of 0.6 M hydrochloric acid (HCl, Sigma-Aldrich) was dropped onto the intercalated nanoribbon on top of a PDMS substrate and kept at room temperature for 1 hour under static condition. The intercalated Cu atoms were gradually dissolved in the acidic solution. The substrate was washed by ethanol and acetone to remove excess Cu ions and acidic solution and then dried naturally. Finally, the de-intercalated nanoribbon was also transferred onto a micro-device for electrical and thermal conductivity measurements. All the chemicals and solvents are of analytical grade and used as-received without any further purification. Prior to the intercalation/de-intercalation reaction, all glass vessels were soaked in an alkaline bath composed of isopropyl alcohol (Sigma-Aldrich) and supersaturated sodium hydroxide (Showa) overnight and washed by distilled water until reaching the neutral condition. - We have systematically investigated thermal and electrical transport properties of the pristine, irradiated, intercalated, and de-intercalated Bi2Se3 nanoribbons via a suspended thermal bridge method to fully understand the effects of helium ion irradiation and copper intercalation/de-intercalation on their thermoelectric properties. A novel batch-fabricated micro-device was developed to characterize the carrier concentration of individual nanoribbons in a physical properties measurement system (PPMS) to better understand the effect of Bi and Se vacancies on electron transport in the Bi2Se3 nanoribbon. - In this project, we have collaborated with Prof. Oleg V. Prezhdo’s group at University of Southern California and conducted the first-principles calculations to understand the mechanisms of how Bi and Se vacancies affect electron transport in the Bi2Se3 nanoribbon. The electronic band structure calculations were performed with the Vienna ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The Perdew−Burke−Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange−correlation functional and the projector augmented wave (PAW) method were employed in the first-principle density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The van der Waals interactions were treated using the DFT-D3 method. PBE + U was used to describe the strongly localized Cu 3d electrons with U = 6.0 eV. A system with 1*1*1 hexagonal unit cell was used to represent the Bi2Se3 crystal. The plane wave cutoff energy was set to 400 eV, and 13*13*7 Gamma-centered Monkhorst-Pack grids were used to sample the Brillouin zone. We first performed the structure optimization for the pristine Bi2Se3 and the four designed systems with various levels of Cu intercalants in the van der Waals gaps and Cu substitutes on Bi sites in the host lattice. Non-self-consistent calculations were then performed to obtain the electronic properties of the optimized structures. Bader was used for atomic charge analysis and the electron localization function was calculated with VASP for bond analysis. The BoltzTraP package was used to calculate the Seebeck coefficient with the obtained electronic properties. BoltzTraP adopts the constant relaxation time approximation and has been successfully used to quantitatively predict transport properties of various materials in the literature. An experimentally determined electron concentration of 10^19 cm-3 was adopted for calculating the Seebeck coefficient of the pristine Bi2Se3. - By combining the experimental and first-principles calculations studies, we have extensively investigated the effects of defects such as Bi and Se vacancies and intercalated and substituted Cu atoms on the thermal and electronic transport properties of individual Bi2Se3 nanoribbon. The successful completion of this project provides new insights on how to tune the doping level and transport properties of low-dimensional thermoelectric materials. We further demonstrated a nanoscale thermoelectric generator based on the pristine n-type and intercalated p-type Bi2Se3 nanoribbons, which opened a new avenue for on-chip cooling applications.

14202818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202818.value: - We have experimentally investigated the effects of reversible copper intercalation/de-intercalation on the thermal transport properties of individual Bi2Se3 nanoribbons. Distinct from prior studies that have shown reduced thermal conductivity after intercalation, a crossover in the total thermal conductivity was observed over the measured temperature range, i.e., the thermal conductivity is significantly suppressed at low temperatures but enhanced above 250 K by copper intercalation. This intriguing crossover phenomenon is attributed to the interplay between the enhanced electronic thermal conductivity and the reduced lattice thermal conductivity, both of which result from the intercalated Cu atoms. Moreover, we showed that thermal conductivity could be further tuned by de-intercalation of Cu atoms. Compared to the pristine nanoribbon, a dramatically lower in-plane lattice thermal conductivity was observed for intercalated and de-intercalated nanoribbons due to the formation of the Cu/Bi2Se3 superlattice structure. Theoretical modeling revealed that the reduced lattice thermal conductivity was primarily owing to the enhancement of phonon boundary scattering and point defect scattering. This project provides a facile approach to tune thermal transport properties at nanoscale, which can be potentially used in thermal switch and thermoelectric applications. (Publication on International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer) - We further investigated the effects of intercalated and substituted Cu atoms on the electron transport properties of Bi2Se3 nanoribbons through both experimental studies and the first-principles calculations. Realizing switchable n-type and p-type conduction in Bi2Se3, a traditional thermoelectric material and a topological insulator, is highly beneficial for the development of thermoelectric devices and also of great interest for spintronics and quantum computing. In this project, we demonstrated switching between n-type and p-type conduction in single Bi2Se3 nanoribbons through a reversible copper intercalation method. DFT calculations reveal that such a switchable behavior arises from the electronic band structure distortion caused by the high-concentration copper intercalation and the copper substitution for Bi sites in the host lattice. A proof-of-concept in-plane thermoelectric generator is fabricated with one pair of the pristine n-type and intercalated p-type Bi2Se3 nanoribbons on a microfabricated device, which gives rise to an open-circuit voltage of 4.8 mV and a maximum output power of 0.3 nW under a temperature difference of 29.2 K. This project achieves switchable n-type and p-type electrical conduction in Bi2Se3 nanoribbons via a facile chemical approach and the practical application of nanoribbons in a thermoelectric device. (Publication on ACS Nano)

14202818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202818.value: The success of the project shows that defect engineering such as helium ion irradiation and copper intercalation/de-intercalation can effectively tune the thermal and electrical transport properties of low-dimensional thermoelectric materials. Based on these two approaches, we have observed very intriguing phenomena in Bi2Se3 nanoribbons including the crossover in the thermal conductivity over the temperature range and switchable n-type and p-type electrical conduction through copper intercalation/de-intercalation. However, it is still challenging to tune the doping level of individual nanoribbons for optimizing thermoelectric figure of merit. In this project, we have fabricated a batch-fabricated microdevice to characterize the carrier concentration of individual nanoribbons. Based on this technique, we will further investigate how to optimize the power factor of individual nanoribbons through tuning the size and doping level. It might lead to new design rule on how to optimize the thermoelectric properties of low-dimensional nanostructures.

14202818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202818.value: In this project, we have demonstrated two effective approaches (helium ion irradiation and copper intercalation/de-intercalation) to tune the thermal and electrical transport properties of one-dimensional bismuth selenide nanoribbons for thermoelectric energy conversion applications. High-energy helium ions can penetrate through the thin bismuth selenide nanoribbon and thus generate Bi and Se vacancies, while Cu atoms can be intercalated into or de-intercalated from the van der Waals gaps of the layered bismuth selenide nanoribbon. The Bi and Se vacancies and intercalated and substituted Cu atoms will affect the carrier concentration, mobility, and thermoelectric properties of the nanoribbon. Distinct from prior studies that have shown reduced thermal conductivity after intercalation, a crossover in the thermal conductivity was observed over the measured temperature range, i.e., the thermal conductivity is significantly suppressed at low temperatures but enhanced above 250 K by copper intercalation. More interestingly, we observed switching between n-type and p-type conduction in bismuth selenide nanoribbons through the reversible copper intercalation. Such a switchable behavior arises from the electronic band structure distortion caused by the high-concentration copper intercalation and the copper substitution for Bi sites in the host lattice. We further demonstrated the practical application of nanoribbons in a nanoscale thermoelectric generator.

14202918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202918.value: Deforming soft objects using robots to desired 3D shapes is highly demanded in many industrial and service applications such as robotic surgery, food processing, soldering and assembly of cables and flexible PCBs, etc. There are several challenges for a robot to automatically control deformation of a soft object. First, the kinematics and dynamics of the deformation can be hardly modelled in practice, so it is desirable but challenging to control the deformation without using any kinematic and dynamic models. Second, the deformation leads to difficulties and complications in the controller design and stability analysis. In particular, stability based on full dynamics of the system is yet a problem to be solved. Third, it is not a trivial task to characterize/represent 3D deformation of a soft object. Despite of tremendous effort made to robotic deformation control, existing methods suffer from one or several problems: strong assumptions on the object, the use of exact deformation model, neglecting dynamic forces, weak to measurement noises, etc., and hence they are not really suitable for real-world applications. In this project, we aim to develop innovative solutions to robotic 3D deformation control of soft objects using real-time 3D imaging feedback. The basic ideas for developing such solutions include 1) use of surface curvatures of areas of interests of the object as the feedback of the controller, 2) design of on-line algorithms for estimating the deformation Jacobian matrix between the 3D deformation and motion of the robot so as to realize model-free control, 3) introduction of force feedback for stabilizing the deformation dynamics, 4) use of energy-based Lyapunov functions to design the controller, and 5) proof of the asymptotic stability based on full dynamics of the system. Compared to our previous works, in addition to 3D deformation control, this project also copes with deformation trajectory control, i.e. deforming the 3D shape along a desired trajectory, and designs torque controllers based on the dynamics of the system. Our previous controllers were based on the kinematics only. We will validate performance of the controllers by experiments on soft objects such as soft foam, cleaning sponges and soft tissues of animals. This project, if successfully developed, will significantly advance the research on deformation control of soft objects, and the research outputs will have potential applications in robotic surgery, food and textile industries. 利用機械人的柔性物體變形操作在製造業和服務業有許多應用，如機械人手術、食物加工、線材和柔性電路板安裝等。利用機械人操作柔性物體有幾個技術挑戰。首先，柔性物體的運動學和動力學建模非常困難，所以不使用運動學和動力學模型設計控制器就非常重要，但是也極其挑戰。其次，變形使控制器的設計和穩定行分析變得異常複雜，基於完整動力學的穩定性分析還是一個未解決的難題。第三，柔性物體的三維變形表述也是一個挑戰的問題。現有的控制方法具有各種局限性，如很強且不合實際的假設、需要準確的變形模型、沒有考慮動力學、測量誤差影響大等等。本項目將基於實時三維圖像反饋設計新的柔性物體變形控制器。我們的主要思路如下：1）利用三維表面的曲率作為控制反饋量；2）在線估計機械人運動與柔性物體三維變形的關係以實現不利用模型的變形控制；3）利用力反饋鎮定變形動力學；4）利用基於能量的Lyapunov函數設計控制器；5）基於系統的動力學分析穩定性。相對於我們以前的工作，本項目主要考慮動力學設計機械人的力矩及解決變形跟蹤問題。我們將通過在軟組織等柔性物體上的實驗驗證控制器的性能。本項目的成果將不僅推進柔性物體操作控制技術的發展，也在機械人手術、食品加工和製衣等行業有很好的應用前景。

14202918.label: Realisation of objectives
14202918.value: 1. To develop an algorithm for online estimating the deformation Jacobian matrix between the 3D shape descriptor and motion of the robot： We have fully achieved this objective. To address this challenge, we have designed different 3D shape descriptors for deformable linear, planar, and volumetric objects. Given these shape descriptors, we have designed a series of model-free controllers with online estimations of the deformation Jacobian matrices between the 3D shape descriptor and the motion of the robot. We have designed different on-line estimation algorithms using adaptive laws, robust laws, and neural-network-based methods. In these methods, the unknown deformation Jacobian matrices are online updated using sensor measurements. We do not need to calibrate both the physical properties and the geometric models of the objects. 2. To design a dynamic controller for controlling the shape of a soft object to a desired shape using real-time 3D image feedback when the force feedback is used and when the force feedback is not available： We have fully achieved this objective. To address the related technical issues, we have developed several dynamic control laws that allow for the deformation of soft wires to desired shapes while ensuring proper contact forces are maintained. This is achieved through the use of model-free controllers that incorporate hybrid vision and force feedback. We used deep network structures to approximate the relationships among the shape deformation, the robot manipulation, and the interaction forces between the object and the manipulators. Then, based on the deep network structures, we have designed offline and online learning methods to control the object shape and the deformation forces using visual and force feedback. On the other hand, for applications where force feedback is not available, we have designed adaptive neural networks for online force compensations using real-time 3D image measurements. In these approaches, we used deep network structures to approximate the deformation forces from visual measurements of the object’s shape deformation. Then, we designed adaptive laws to online adjust the incremental motion of the robot to compensate for the interaction forces. 3. To design a controller for deforming 3D shape of a soft object along a desired deformation trajectory using 3D image feedback： We have fully achieved this objective. To solve the problem, we have developed vision-based tracking control laws to manipulate deformable linear objects such that their shape deformation can track desired trajectories. To formulate the control laws, we first developed a dynamic-region-based controller to sequentially manipulate the object to desired configurations while avoiding local minima and overstretching; Then, we used deep network structures to learn shape transition functions along the desired trajectories. Based on the shape transition functions, we designed model-free control laws for the active shape transition of soft cables with unknown deformation models; Third, we developed a hierarchical scheme for vision-guided planning and control of multiwire cables according to the desired trajectories or profiles. At the low level, the vision-based control laws are used to manipulate the deformable objects to local targets. At higher levels, more complex tasks including path planning and obstacle avoidance are performed using optimal-based control algorithms. These control laws have been integrated into a hierarchical manipulation scheme for robotic cable sorting. 4. To investigate the asymptotic stability and robustness of the controllers using energy-like Lyapunov functions based on the full dynamics of the system: We have fully achieved this objective. To investigate the stability and robustness of our controllers, we have constructed energy-like functions and used Lyapunov theories to analyze the stabilities of the dynamical systems. We have rigorously proved the asymptotic stability and robustness of our deformation controllers based on the full closed-loop system dynamics. 5. To develop an experimental setup and validate the performance of the controllers by experiments： We have fully achieved this objective. We have built experimental platforms using different 3D vision sensors (including stereo cameras, point cloud cameras, and hybrid visual sensors) and different robotic manipulators (including industrial robot arms and the da Vinci surgical robotic systems). On these platforms, we have validated our controllers using different linear, planar, and volumetric objects and under different settings.

14202918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202918.value: In the research project, we have developed different deformation controllers using 3D image feedback. The major findings and outcome are summarized as follows: (1) We have developed a series of novel controllers for deformable linear object manipulation. First, we developed a dynamic-region-based controller to sequentially manipulate the object to desired configurations while avoiding local minima and overstretching; Second, we designed a deep-network-based controller for the active shape transition of soft cables with unknown models; Third, we developed a hierarchical planning and control scheme to manipulate multiwire cables to follow desired trajectories or profiles. These works led to one conference paper (Part C-9-1), two published journal papers (Part C-8-2 and Part C-8-3), and one journal paper submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine (Part C-8-1). (2) We have developed fully automated robotic manipulation systems for deforming and sorting multi-wire cables. First, we have developed new mechanical modules with embedded control algorithms and a deep-vision network to achieve active transition; In addition, we have designed a novel two-level planning scheme for the robotic sorting of multi-wire cables using hybrid sensor measurements. The high-level planner outputs optimal grasping sequences, while the low-level planner controls grasping trajectories while maintaining proper contact forces. These works led to two published journal papers (Part C-8-2 and Part C-8-3). (3) We have designed novel 3D shape descriptors based on modal analysis for deformable object manipulation. These descriptors compute low-frequency deformation of the object and are robust to sensor noises and measurement irregularities. Based on the descriptors, we have designed a series of model-free 3D shape deformation controllers using different stereo image feedback and raw point cloud measurements. These works led to one published journal paper (Part C-8-4), and one journal paper submitted to the International Journal of Robotics Research (Part C-8-5). (4) We have developed online estimating algorithms for the deformation Jacobian matrices between different shape descriptors and the robot motion. Different model-free controllers have been designed using adaptive, robust, and neural network-based methods. We have rigorously proved the asymptotic stability and robustness of the controllers.

14202918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202918.value: Automatic manipulation and control of soft objects have significant potential for medical robotics, industrial robotics, and service robotics. Further development of this research can improve the flexibility, complexity, and accuracy of the manipulation tasks, and promote task autonomy in various industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and transportation. To further develop this research topic, the following course of action is proposed: (1) Develop more advanced control and planning algorithms for global deformation control in longer-horizon tasks; (2) Integrate more machine intelligence techniques such as deep learning and reinforcement learning into the control system for better environment understanding and task planning; (3) Developing more efficient real-time control and sensing algorithms for high-speed manipulation of soft objects; (4) Explore new applications and develop new use cases for robotic deformation control of soft objects.

14202918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202918.value: This research studies the robotic deformation control of soft objects, which can promote significant developments in industrial manufacturing, medical robotics, and service robotics. However, it is technically challenging as deformation is complex and high-dimensional. We have developed a series of deformation controllers for linear, planar, and volumetric objects without the need to know their deformation models. Our controllers use 3D visual measurements to guide the motion of the robot while on-line estimating the relationship between the object’s shape changes and the robot motion. We have conducted extensive experiments to validate our controllers on both industrial and surgical robotic platforms with different objects and visual measurements. The results show superior performances of the controllers. Based on the control methods, we have further developed robotic systems for soft wire manipulation that can achieve fully automated sorting tasks. The results confirm high accuracy and efficiency. In summary, our research has addressed an important and challenging robotic topic and shows great application potential.

14203018.label: Project Objectives
14203018.value: To design and fabricate optical structures in support of chiral photonic modes for excitons of TMD materials, e.g., Tamm-plasmonic structure, metasurface, metamaterials, etc., and to realize and manipulate polarization-sensitive Rabi splitting of exciton-polaritons at room temperature. To explore exciton-polariton based on non-cavity resonance. In the excitonic resonance, the permittivity of monolayer MoS2 is up to 25. The large impedance mismatch between MoS2 monolayer and air enables MoS2 itself to be a natural mirror. Therefore, it is possible to construct a non-cavity resonance mode only by constituting one mirror and one monolayer of MoS2. With this non-cavity resonance mode, valley-polarized exciton–polaritons are highly anticipated. To develop electrically exciton-polariton emission diodes with circular polarization. As an atomically-thick material, a layered TMD material (e.g., WSe2 monolayer) can be tuned from p-type to n-type. Therefore, we envisage that a TMD-based diode sandwiched into chiral photonic cavity will generate exciton-polariton emission with chiral polarization. To explore novel physical properties based on the polarization of exciton-polariton, such as the life time and diffusion length.

14203018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203018.value: An exciton-polariton is a hybrid light-matter quasi-particle that is formed in semiconductor when an exciton interacts sufficiently strongly with a photonic/plasmonic mode. In particular, exciton–polariton has attracted tremendous attention not only because of its compelling physical properties of Bose–Einstein condensation, but also its potential applications for devices in quantum-information processing, such as spin switch and polaritonic lasing. However, these interesting characteristics normally require very low operation temperatures (< 77 K), which is largely limited by the small binding energy of exciton in conventional semiconductors. Monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are an emerging class of two-dimensional electronic/optoelectronic materials with unusually startling properties. Their two-dimensional nature results in a very large exciton binding energy, theoretically ~ 550 meV, which allows the strong coupling of exciton-polariton at room temperature. Moreover, the exciton (or trion) presence in the atomically-thick monolayers can be facilely controlled with externally applied electric fields, which could be used to optoelectronic devices, e.g., active polaritonic devices. Despite the large amount of research effort deployed on the exciton of TMD (e.g., MoS2) coupled to cavity photonic mode and plasmonic mode, little attempt has been extended to the polarization selectivity of exciton-polaritons in TMD materials. The polarization selectivity is a new dimension for exciton–polariton coupling systems and can be utilized for polarization-dependent polaritonic devices. It is known that the inversion asymmetry and strong spin–orbit coupling in TMD layered materials lead to the spin–valley properties, in which excitons with different spins can spatially coexist in separate regions in the momentum space, and can be selectively excited by chiral polarization of light. This unique characteristic makes it possible to manipulate the polarization selectivity of exciton-polaritons by coupling chirally polarized photonic/plasmonic modes with the spin polarized excitons of TMD materials. In this proposed project, our aim is to have a systematic understanding of the interactions between photonic/plasmonic modes and spin-polarized excitons in two-dimensional TMD materials, to manipulate valley-spin exciton-polaritons by chiral photonic nanostructures, and ultimately to realize polarization-selective polaritonic devices. While the Hong Kong Government has identified that nanotechnology is one of the major intended areas to be supported by the Innovation and Technology Commission in recognition of the potential future market, the theme of this project apparently has close relevance to such initiative. It will also provide training of R&D personnel for local electronics industry. 利用外部施加的電場容易地控制原子厚度單層中的激子（或trion）存在，可以用於光電器件，例如有源極化器件。儘管人们对耦合到腔光子模式和等離子體模式中硫系过渡金属（TMD）的激子（例如，二硫化鉬 MoS2）進行了大量研究工作，但很少嘗試擴展到TMD材料中激子-極化子的極化選擇性。極化選擇性是激子-極化子耦合系統的新維度，並且可以用於偏振相關的極化器件。眾所周知，TMD層狀材料中的反轉不對稱性和強自旋 - 軌道耦合導致自旋谷特性，其中具有不同自旋的激子可以在動量空間中的不同區域中空間共存，並且可以通過手性極化選擇性地激發。光這種獨特的特性使得可以通過將手性偏振光子/等離子體模式與TMD材料的自旋極化激子耦合來操縱激子 - 極化子的偏振選擇性。 在本的項目中，我們的目標是系統地理解光子/等離子體模式和二維硫系过渡金属（TMD）材料中的自旋極化激子之間的相互作用，通過手性光子納米結構操縱谷 自旋激子-極化子，並最終實現偏振選擇性極化器件。

14203018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203018.value: We have interrogated the Fano-type asymmetry in the open plasmon-exciton system (non-resonant scenario). We find that different from the Rabi-type process, where the internal plasmon–exciton coupling dominates, the Fano-type process is highly dependent on the external excitations on the exciton and plasmon components. (See J3) We have developed a bulk MoS2 metaphotonic platform by CVD method. We demonstrate magnetic surface lattice resonances (M-SLRs) and their energy-momentum dispersions in 1D MoS2 gratings. We observe anti-crossing behaviour with Rabi splitting up to 170 meV, when the M-SLRs are hybridized with the excitons in multilayer MoS2. We show the distinct Mie modes and anapole-exciton polaritons in 2D MoS2 disk arrays. (See J5) We have proposed the heterostructures of graphene on a biaxial crystal (α-MoO3) slab and theoretically investigated the hybridized plasmon-phonon polaritons with dependence on the Fermi level of graphene. We demonstrate the distinct wavelength tunability of the plasmon-phonon polaritons modes and the optical topologic transitions from open (hyperbolic) to closed (bow-tie-like) iso-frequency contours as the increase of the Fermi level of graphene. Furthermore, we observe the tunable quantum spin Hall effects of the plasmon-phonon polaritons. (see J4) We devise a graphene-based electrically reconfigurable polarization conversion across a broadband THz region (0.3-0.9 THz) for controlling the chiral polarization of terahertz pulse. By electrically controlling the graphene conductivity, we can switch the device reflection in-between total internal reflection and metal mirror reflection to realize a frequency-independent phase change. We achieve tunable chiral polarization THz waveforms in the time domain for the first time, from right-handed to left-handed polarization. (See J6) We have proposed a synergistic effect of chiral near-field and hot carrier injection for actively controlling the valley polarization of WSe2 at RT. The degree of valley polarization emission is enhanced from near zero (for pure WSe2) to 20% under non-resonant optical excitation (532 nm) when monolayer WSe2 is integrated with the chiral near-field by the plasmonic metasurface. By applying a near-infrared light (wavelength of 970 nm to 1600 nm) illumination, the valley polarization can be further enhanced from 20% to 30%, which contributes to plasmonic induced hot carrier injection from metasurface in infrared region. (See J1-J2, J4, J7)

14203018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203018.value: An exciton-polariton is a hybrid light-matter quasi-particle that forms in semiconductor when an exciton interacts sufficiently strong with a photonic/plasmonic mode. In particular, exciton–polariton has attracted tremendous attention not only because of its compelling physical properties , but also its potential applications for devices in quantum-information processing, such as spin switch and polaritonic lasing. Monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) is an emerging class of two-dimensional electronic/optoelectronic materials with unusually startling properties. Its two-dimensional nature results in a very large exciton binding energy, which allows the strong coupling of exciton-polariton at room temperature. In this proposed project, we have accomplished a systematic understanding of the interactions between photonic/plasmonic modes and spin-polarized excitons in TMDs, and have manipulated valley-spin exciton-polaritons by chiral photonic nanostructures.

14203118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203118.value: The goal of this project is to develop a structured deep learning framework, which can simultaneously model the structures of supervisory signals in different modalities as well as the structures of feature maps in hidden layers in a probabilistic way. Such structural information can effectively improve the visual representations learned by deep neural networks. The proposed structural deep learning will be applied to scene understanding, which is a fundamental computer vision problem and has a broad range of applications to image search engines, automated driving, and human computer interactions. Deep learning has achieved great success in deep learning. A typical neural network passes information from lower layers to higher layers in a feedforward way, while the interactions among neurons in the same layers are not modeled. Beyond image labels, which have no structures, more and more vision problems require deep neural networks predicting signals with complex structures, such as semantic graphs, sentences, skeletons of bodies, and 3D scene layout. In this project, we will propose a novel structured deep learning framework which can model interactions among neurons in the same layers and message passing schemes are proposed to pass structural information in feature maps with gate control. The structures of supervisory signals in different modalities also guide massage passing. The structures among multi-modality supervisory signals and feature maps are jointly learned in an end-to-end manner. This proposed structured multi-modality deep learning will be applied to scene understanding. Given an image as input, the network can predict a scene graph with rich structural semantic information, including detected objects, their class labels and attributes, and the visual relationship between objects (called phrases). Each detected object has multiple class labels in a hierarchy from WorldNet which defines classes/subclasses at different levels. Based on the scene graph, language description for each region (called region captioning) will also be generated. Object detection, phrase detection and region captions are jointly predicted by exploring structural information in different layers. The outcome of this project will have substantial impact on scene understanding and deep learning. It will significantly advance the state-of-the-art of scene understanding by predicting rich structural multi-modality supervisory signals and modeling structural information in different hidden layers. Structured deep learning is a fundamental problem. Besides scene understanding, the theories and algorithms developed from this project also have the potential to be generalized to other domains, such as human pose estimation, video analysis, and 3D vision. 本項目旨在研究結構化的深度學習框架，能夠同時對跨模態的監督信號和隱含層特徵圖進行概率化的建模。該類結構化的信息能夠使深度神經網絡更有效的學習更優的視覺特徵表達。本項目提出的結構化深度學習方法將被應用於場景理解，其是計算機視覺中的基礎問題之一，在圖像搜索引擎、自動駕駛、以及人際交互中有著廣泛的應用。深度學習在不同研究領域獲得了巨大的成功，經典神經網絡通常從低層向高層前向的傳遞信息，但是同層神經元之間的關係並未進行有效建模。傳統使用的神經網絡訓練監督信號，如圖像標籤，並沒有結構化信息。但是，越來越多的視覺問題要求神經網絡輸出帶結構的複雜優化目標，如語義圖、自然語句、人體骨骼框架以及三維場景佈局等。在本項目中，我們提出一種創新的結構化深度學習框架，其能夠有效的建模同層神經元之間的關係，並且有效的在不同特徵圖之間傳遞由門控制的結構化信息。不同模態的監督信號同樣能夠指揮神經網絡中的信息傳遞。跨模態監督信號以及特徵圖之間的結構能夠有效的通過端對端訓練進行學習。本項目提出的結構化深度學習方法將被應用場景理解。給定一幅圖像作為輸入，本項目提出的神經網絡能夠估計帶有豐富語義結構信息的場景圖，其包括被檢測物體和類別、屬性標籤以及物體之間的視覺關係。每個被檢測物體均有在WordNet的種類/子種類的層級標籤。基於場景圖，每個圖像區域的自然語言描述能夠被有效的生成。提出的方法能夠通過使用不同網絡層級之間的結構化信息，聯合輸出物體檢測結果、關係檢測結果、以及區域自然語言描述結果。本項目的成果對場景理解和深度學習領域將有重要的影響，通過估計預測多模態監督信號之間的關係，以及不同層級關係的建模，能夠極大的增強現有場景理解算法的性能。結構化深度學習是深度學習中的基礎問題之一，本項目研究的理論和算法，除了場景理解，也能夠擴展和應用於其它領域，包括人體姿態估計、視頻分析、以及三維視覺。

14203118.label: Realisation of objectives
14203118.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) Development of the theoretical structured deep learning framework and the message passing scheme. We have proposed the deformable mechanism for modeling interactions between neurons and passing structure information not just within the feature maps of the same layer but also across feature maps of different layers. Transformers with self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms have shown promising performances in various learning problems. They can be used for passing information between different neurons. We proposed the deformable attention mechanism for effective and efficient message passing, which attends to a small set of sampling locations as a pre-filter for prominent key elements out of all the feature map pixels. Specifically, given a feature map, we adopt 1x1 convolution blocks to predict the locations to be attended beforehand, which can save much computations, leads to faster convergence, as well as improved performances for visual understanding tasks. (2) Joint prediction of scene graphs and class hierarchy. We observe that previous methods on scene graph generation needs to consider a large number of candidate pairs. We observe that multiple phrase features can refer to some highly-overlapped regions. Prior to constructing different subject-object pairs, these features are of similar representations as they correspond to the same overlapped regions. Thus, a natural idea is to construct a shared representation for the phrase features of similar regions in the early stage. Then the shared representation is refined to learn a general representation of the are by passing the message from the connected objects. In the final stage, we can extract the required information from this shared representation to predict object relations by combining with different subject-object pairs. Based on this observation, we propose a subgraph-based scene graph generation approach, where the object pairs referring to the similar interacting regions are clustered into a subgraph and share the phrase representation (termed as subgraph features). In this pipeline, all the feature refining processes are done on the shared subgraph features. This design significantly reduces the number of the phrase features in the intermediate stage and speed up the model both in training and inference. Three prominent novelties reside in this work. 1) A bottom-up clustering method is proposed to factorize the image into subgraphs. By sharing the region representations within the subgraph, our method could significantly reduce the redundant computation and accelerate the inference speed. 2) spatial weighted message passing (SMP) structure is proposed to pass message between object feature vectors and sub-graph feature maps. 3) A Spatial-sensitive Relation Inference (SRI) module is proposed to use the features from subject, object and subgraph representations for recognizing the relationship between objects. (3) Joint prediction of scene graphs and region captions. On top of the work in (2), we also propose the joint prediction of dense captions of regions. We found that contextual correlated visual cues (i.e., local, neighboring, global) permits multi-scale contextual message passing to reinforce regional description generation. To achieve dense region captioning, we propose a Context and Attribute Grounded Network (CAG-Net) consists of two vital modules. 1) Contextual Feature Extractor, establishing a non-local similarity graph for the feature interaction between the target ROI and its neighboring ROIs based on their feature affinity and spatial nearness, allows adaptive contextual information sharing from multiple adjacent ROIs (i.e., global and neighbors) to interact with the target ROI. 2) Attribute-Grounded Caption Generator adopts LSTM as the fundamental unit and fuses contextual features to generate the description for the target ROI. To reinforce the coarse-to-fine structure of description generation, we adopt coarse-level and fined-level linguistic attribute losses as the additional supervision respectively at the sequential LSTM cells. Without sequential restrictions from the ground-truth captions, such keywords or attributes are more recognizable by the content in the target ROI, and thus own a more stable discriminative power for the extraction of visual patterns. To some extent, it is similar with the visual attributes of objects in multi-label classification. The resulting CAG-Net achieves top performance in dense captioning.

14203118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203118.value: As research outcomes, 20 conference papers are published in top conferences on computer vision and machine learning (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and NeurIPS). In this project, we have proposed novel approaches on multi-modal structured learning for modeling relations between images, natural language, semantic maps and audio. Learning complex relations between natural language and images has extensive applications, including visual question answering, expression referring, language-based image generation, etc. Structured learning between multi-modal information is crucial for recovering such complex relations. In (Part C.9 No.11), we proposed a novel structured learning algorithm for tackling the visual question answering problem. We proposed a multi-modality latent interaction module, which learns the cross-modality relationships between latent visual and language summarizations. The cross-modality information between the latent summarizations are propagated to fuse valuable information from both modalities and are used to update the visual and word features. In (Part C.9 No.2), we tried to tackle the multi-modal problem on locating certain objects or persons in an image with a referring expression, where the key challenge is to comprehend and align various types of information between the visual and textual domains. We designed a novel cross-modal attention-guided erasing approach, where we discard the most dominant information from either textual or visual domains to generate difficult training samples online, and to drive the model to discover complementary textual-visual correspondences. In (Part C.9 No.14), to discover the relations between scene graphs and natural images, we propose a semi-parametric method, PasteGAN, for generating the image from the scene graph and the image crops. Spatial arrangements of the objects and their pair-wise relationships are defined by the scene graph. To enhance the interactions of the objects in the output image, we designed a crop refining network and an object-image fuser to embed the objects as well as their relationships into a joint map to generating realistic images. In (Part C.9 No.17), We propose a novel algorithm, Open-Edit, which is the first attempt on open-domain image manipulation with open-vocabulary instructions. It is a challenging cross-modal task considering the large variation of image domains and the lack of training supervision. Our approach takes advantage of the unified visual-semantic embedding space pretrained on a general image-caption dataset, and manipulates the embedded visual features by applying text-guided vector arithmetic on the image feature maps. Our approach shows promising results in manipulating open-vocabulary color, texture, and high-level attributes for various scenarios of open-domain images.

14203118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203118.value: In our study, we found that the joint learning of multiple tasks on graphs can be beneficial to the multiple tasks' performances, if the hyper-parameters are properly and carefully tuned for different multi-task settings. However, manually tuning the hyperparameters is also time-consuming and tedious. We will further conduct research on automatically search of multi-task learning hyper-parameters. In addition, we will also investigate how to design more advanced transformer-based network architectures for joint scene graph generation and region captioning.

Such structural information can effectively improve the visual representations learned by deep neural networks. The proposed structural deep learning will be applied to scene understanding, which is a fundamental computer vision problem and has a broad range of applications to image search engines, automated driving, and human-computer interactions. We have developed novel scene graph generation algorithms, based on which, object detection, phrase detection and region captions are jointly predicted by exploring structural information. The outcomes of the project have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art performance of scene understanding.

14203218.value: 以誤差界方法對二階求解具結構優化問題算法的收斂性分析

14203218.label: Project Objectives
14203218.value: Develop techniques to analyze the convergence rates of the standard trust-region method and cubic regularization method when they are applied to structured optimization problems that possess the error bound property using exact Hessian information. Develop error bound-based techniques to analyze the convergence rates of the inexact regularized proximal Newton method and cubic regularization method when sub-sampling and quasi-Newton strategies are used to approximate the Hessian.
rows: Develop techniques to analyze the convergence rates of the standard trust-region method and cubic regularization method when they are applied to structured optimization problems that possess the error bound property using exact Hessian information.

Develop error bound-based techniques to analyze the convergence rates of the inexact regularized proximal Newton method and cubic regularization method when sub-sampling and quasi-Newton strategies are used to approximate the Hessian.

14203218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203218.value: 雖然二階求解算法的計算複雜度一般比較高，但因很多從實際應用衍生出來的優化問題有著特殊的結構，所以二階求解算法還是有一定的優勢, 並在近幾年越來越受到重視。可是，現有的理論分析並未能解釋二階算法在求解這類具結構優化問題時候所展現的快速收斂性。這個研究項目的目標就是要填補這個理論方面的不足。我們提出以誤差界方法去分析二階算法在求解具結構優化問題時的收斂率。這項目的成果將能為二階求解算法的優越收斂性能提供理論基礎，並能推動針對大規模具結構優化問題的二階求解算法的設計和發展。

14203218.label: Realisation of objectives
14203218.value: To achieve Objective 1, we first developed techniques to obtain a sharper convergence analysis of the classic cubic regularization method (CRM) proposed by Griewank and, independently, by Nesterov and Polyak. Specifically, we proposed a new error bound (EB) condition that captures the distance to the set of second-order critical points of an unconstrained (non-convex) optimization problem and showed, for the first time, that the CRM has a quadratic rate of convergence when applied to problems that satisfy this EB condition. This improves upon the decade-old sub-quadratic convergence result in Yu. Nesterov, B. T. Polyak. Cubic Regularization of Newton Method and Its Global Performance. Math. Prog., Ser. A 108(1): 177-205, 2006. Furthermore, we showed that the aforementioned EB condition is satisfied by a number of recent applications, such as matrix completion and phase retrieval. This demonstrates the relevance of our proposed EB condition. Next, we considered linear and quadratic optimization problems over the Stiefel manifold, which encapsulate the trust-region problem, and established EBs for them. These EBs imply the linear convergence of a host of iterative methods for solving variants of the trust-region problem. Our results have been further developed by the following recent work: R. Jiang, X. Li. Hölderian Error Bounds and Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz Inequality for the Trust Region Subproblem. Math. OR 47(4): 3025-3050, 2022. To achieve Objective 2, we first focused on a family of non-smooth optimization problems over the Stiefel manifold, in which the objective can be expressed as the sum of a smooth (but possibly non-convex) function and a non-smooth convex function. To tackle the sub-problems that arise during the course of computation, we proposed a highly efficient regularized semismooth Newton method and established its global convergence. Our work is the first to give a practically efficient and provably convergent algorithm for solving a large class of non-smooth optimization problems. Next, we applied the aforementioned algorithmic framework to two fundamental problems in signal processing and machine learning, namely orthogonal dictionary learning and robust subspace recovery. Due to the structure of these problems, we were able to develop an inexact version of the semismooth Newton method for the sub-problem and showed, using EB techniques, that it converges superlinearly to the optimal solution to the sub-problem. Lastly, we explored how our techniques can be extended to decentralized settings, which are highly relevant in applications and have attracted much attention in recent years. In particular, we developed a novel Newton tracking algorithm for decentralized optimization of a network, in which each node holds a strongly convex and twice-differentiable local objective function. We showed, for the first time, that our algorithm achieves exact convergence to the optimal solution to the problem. Furthermore, based on the EB property of strongly convex functions, we established the linear convergence rate of our algorithm. The result reveals the impact of the condition number of the objective function and the connectivity of the network on the convergence rate of our algorithm, which provides further insights into the design of efficient second-order methods for decentralized optimization.

14203218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203218.value: The major findings of the project have already been summarized in Section 5.3 above. The research outcomes for Objective 1 have led to the publication of one journal article in SIAM Journal on Optimization, in which the grant from the current project is acknowledged, and the following journal article, which appears after the end date of the current project: P. Wang, H. Liu, A. M.-C. So. Linear Convergence of a Proximal Alternating Minimization Method with Extrapolation for ℓ_1-Norm Principal Component Analysis. Accepted for publication in SIAM Journal on Optimization, November 2022. The research outcomes for Objective 2 have led to the publication of three journal articles --- one in SIAM Journal on Optimization, one in IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks, and one in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. In addition, the outcomes have been disseminated in two refereed conference articles. We remark that SIAM Journal on Optimization is a top-ranked journal in the field of mathematical optimization, while IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks and IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing are top-ranked journals in the field of signal processing.

14203218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203218.value: There has been much interest lately in the design and analysis of efficient second-order methods for solving large-scale machine learning problems. The outcomes of this project provide a set of powerful tools for further investigation in this direction. In particular, given our work on EB theory and manifold optimization, it would be interesting to design second-order methods for structured manifold optimization problems that arise in machine learning applications (such as orthogonal dictionary learning and robust subspace recovery) and develop EB-based analysis of their convergence rates. It would also be interesting to study second-order methods for decentralized manifold optimization, which so far has barely been investigated in the literature.

14203218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203218.value: Motivated by the observation that many contemporary applications in data science, machine learning, and signal processing call for the optimization of objective functions with specific structures, we designed novel optimization algorithms that can exploit those structures to achieve fast computation in practice. To provide a better understanding of the performance of our proposed algorithms, we developed mathematical tools to rigorously analyze their efficiency and obtained the best-known theoretical efficiency guarantees to date for them. The outcomes of this project provide a broad set of algorithm design and analysis techniques for modern large-scale optimization and open up a number of new directions for further research.
