14203318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203318.value: Despite advances in CMOS transistors that now enable their switching at tens of gigahertz frequencies, the clock frequency at which the central processing units (cpu) of computers can operate are limited to less than one tenth of this because of the heat that would be generated from the CMOS interconnects if they were operated at higher frequencies. The bottleneck comes from the copper interconnects which connect the billions of transistors, and the heat produced from the interconnects which rises in proportion to frequency. The high number density of transistors in the cpu leads to high density of heat generation that can exceed the thermal density limit for practical cooling if the switching frequency were increased. If the problem from excessive power consumption (heat generation) at high frequencies were solved it would immediately result in computers that are more energy efficient and more than ten times faster. A possible solution to reduce the heat generation from the interconnects is to use on-chip optical instead of electrical interconnects for the global interconnects in high performance computers. The small size of state-of-the art CMOS transistors however introduces a challenge of how to integrate the large sized silicon optical waveguides with the tiny transistors. We pursue the approach of using dielectric (silicon nitride based) optical waveguides integrated at the upper level of the back-end interconnect hierarchy of CMOS interconnects as the way to replace the global electrical interconnects with optical interconnects. However silicon nitride waveguides do not yet have the devices to convert the high speed optical signal in silicon nitride waveguide to electrical signals. In this project we aim to develop the high quantum efficiency and high speed photodetectors which can be integrated with silicon nitride waveguides for use in future on-chip optical interconnects. We shall investigate the use of two dimensional materials such as graphene, hexagonal boron nitride and molybdenum disulfide, and their combination in artificial van der Waals heterostructures to make hybrid integrated photodetectors which have the speed and quantum efficiency needed for on-chip optical interconnects. By taking advantage of the different properties of different 2D materials, we can engineer perpendicular electric fields in 2D van der Waals heterostructures which serve to efficiently separate the photo-generated electrons and holes in a photodetector. Using appropriate 2D materials for optical absorption and extracting the photocurrent, we shall create novel structures for the high speed and high quantum efficiency photodetectors on silicon nitride. 在本項目中，我們尋求探索介電（氮化矽基）光學波導在片上光學 互連的潛在應用，以用於高速CMOS全域互連的後端工藝。基於氮 化矽平臺至今還未有器件可以將波導中的高速光信號轉換成電信號， 本項目旨在開發易於集成在氮化矽波導上具有高量子效率的高速光 電探測器。我們將研究利用二維材料（如石墨烯，六方氮化硼和 二硫化鉬）以及由它們組成的層狀範德華異質結所製備而成的複 合集成光電探測器，以滿足片上光學互連所需的速度和量子效率。 我們將構建二維範德瓦爾斯異質結構，通過利用不同二維材料的獨 特特性有效地分離光電探測器中的光生電子和空穴。通過合理選 擇二維材料我們將製造滿足未來光學互連所需用於高速 CMOS微處理器的高速和高量子效率的新型光電探測器。

14203318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203318.value: In this project we developed the wet and dry transfer methods to place 2D materials onto optical waveguides. We demonstrated the successful application of these techniques to fabricate high speed photodetectors formed by a van der Waals heterostructure comprised of 2D layers of hexagonal boron nitride, molybdenum disulphide and graphene. These waveguide integrated photodetectors had measured bandwidths of 28GHz and 0.24A/W responsivity on the silicon nitride waveguides and fully met objectives 1 and 3 of the project. We also studied the carrier dynamics in high speed photodetectors formed by placing graphene on silicon nitride waveguides and using asymmetrically positioned metal contacts. We modelled the carrier diffusion of electrons and holes and showed that resulted in differential arrival times at the electrodes and producing a voltage from the charge imbalance that further improved the hole transport in order to produce impulse responses as fast as 11.5ps. This work addressed, addressed objective 2 of the project in improving our understanding of the optolectronic properties of the device. To further improve the light matter interaction in the hybrid integration of 2D materials with dielectric optical waveguides, we also developed a new low-loss plasmonic slot waveguide to dielectric waveguide mode converter. The structure exploited the concentration of the optical field in the plasmonic mode to increase the overlap of the optical field with the thin 2D material. Low loss was achieved by making use of the constructive interference of the symmetric and antisymmetric modes in the 2D material while there is destructive interference in the dielectric waveguide. The interface loss was less than 1.68dB and improved the optical absorption in the 2D material by a factor of 15 compared with simple placement of the 2D material on the silicon nitride waveguide. This work was published in Journal of Lightwave Technology. We also studied the optoelectronic properties of platinum diselenide for use in high speed waveguide integrated photodetectors (APL 2020) and showed that this 2D material could be used for making 35GHz bandwidth photodetectors on silicon nitride waveguides (ACS Photonics 2020). These works were the first demonstration of high speed photodetectors using this new 2D material on optical waveguides. A PhD student, Yi Wang, completed her PhD dissertation on the hybrid integration of 2D materials for photonic devices and graduated in 2020.

14203318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203318.value: There is excellent potential for further development of high speed and high responsivity photodetectors using the hybrid integrated 2D materials, especially for making near and mid infrared photodetectors.

14203318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203318.value: In this project we advanced the technology of using atomically thin two dimensional materials for making high speed photodetectors on dielectric waveguides. We developed the experimental techniques to fabricate devices by stacking different 2D materials, held together by vander Waals forces. This enabled the combination of large bandgap insulators such as hexagonal boron nitride with semimetals, such as graphene, and semiconductors such as molybdenum disulphide or platinum diselenide, to make high speed photodetectors, operating with bandwidths of over 35GHz. We also developed a plasmonic metal slot waveguide to dielectric waveguide interface that was low loss and enabled enhancement of the optical absorption in the 2D material by a fifteen times, because of the light concentration into the 2D material layer by the plasmonic mode. This project may lead to new photodetectors for use in the near and mid-infrared for applications in high speed communications.

14203418.label: Project Objectives
14203418.value: We will develop efficient algorithms based on multidimensional Hilbert transform for pricing popular path-dependent multi-asset options written on a medium number of assets in Lévy-driven asset price models, as well as for computing joint survival/default probabilities in Lévy-driven structural credit risk models. We will develop error analysis of our algorithms.

14203418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203418.value: Derivatives market is a major component of today’s financial markets and options form an important class of derivatives. In the options business, typically an asset price model is calibrated to the prices of plain vanilla options traded on regulated exchanges, which is then used to price exotic options that are traded over the counter. These exotic options are created to meet the diverse needs of investors, e.g., hedging, risk management and speculation. There exist many complex exotic options, and developing efficient computational methods to price them is a major problem in financial engineering research. Multi-asset exotic options, whose payoffs depend on the prices of multiple assets, are very popular products in the over-the-counter market for equities, currencies and commodities. The barrier, lookback or early exercise feature embedded in them makes the pricing problem particularly challenging. Some standard numerical methods are available for solving the problem, but they are often too time-consuming for obtaining good accuracy. One-dimensional Hilbert transform based method is highly efficient for pricing single-asset exotic options with barrier, lookback or early exercise feature in Lévy-driven asset price models, which are widely used to capture jump risk and fit option implied volatility smiles/skews. The great success of this approach for single-asset options motivates us to develop its multidimensional generalization for multi-asset options. In this project, we will undertake this nontrivial task and develop a novel approach based on multidimensional Hilbert transform for pricing multi-asset options with barrier, lookback or early exercise feature in Lévy-driven asset price models. The method can also be applied to compute joint survival probability in popular structural credit risk models, which is crucial for credit risk management. We anticipate that the proposed research will contribute a highly efficient method for solving such computationally challenging problems in practice. 衍生品市場是現代金融市場重要組成部分，其中期權是主要的衍生產品。在期權行業中，通常將某個定價模型用交易所交易的普通期權作校正，然後使用該模型去定價場外交易的奇異期權。這些奇異期權是用來滿足投資者的各種需要， 例如對衝， 風險管理以及投機。市場上有很多複雜的奇異期權， 如果開發有傚的算法對它們定價是金融工程研究中的主要問題。基於多個資產的奇異期權在股票，外匯以及商品的場外交易市場很普遍。一些奇異期權帶有障礙或者回看或者提前執行的特徵，這使得對它們定價特別具有挑戰性。一些標準的數值方法可以用在這些問題上，但是要得到好的精度它們通常都太慢了。 一維希爾伯特變換在處理基於列維的資產模型中定價單個資產帶障礙或回看或提前執行的期權時特別有效。這些模型被普遍用來捕捉跳躍風險以及擬合市場波動率曲綫。希爾伯特變換方法在單個資產期權定價中取得的巨大成功鼓舞我們去研究如何使用它來定價多個資產的期權。 在本項目中， 我們致力於開發一種基於多維希爾伯特變換的新方法來定價基於多維列維過程的價格模型中多個資產的帶有障礙或者回看或者提前執行的期權。 這個方法也可以被用來計算在普遍使用的結構化信用風險模型中公司的共同生存概率。這對信用風險管理很重要。我們期待本項目的研究將會為現實中解決這類具有挑戰性的計算問題提供一種新的有效方法。

14203418.label: Realisation of objectives
14203418.value: We have solved a series of problems and achieved objective 1 fully. (1) We have developed an efficient method based on multidimensional Sinc approximation to compute multidimensional Hilbert transform. This built the foundation for solving other problems in this project. (2) We have considered multi-asset barrier options which is a popular class of multi-asset path-dependent options. We have developed an efficient algorithm based on multidimensional Hilbert transform to price them in exponential Levy models. The algorithm performs well for options on two or three assets, which are the typical cases for such options in the market, under many popular exponential Levy models. It also outperforms some standard algorithms for such problems in the literature. (3) In addition, we have developed an efficient algorithm based on multidimensional Hilbert transform to compute joint survival probabilities in Levy-driven structural credit risk models. This algorithm also outperforms some standard methods in the literature. Results obtained in (1), (2), and (3) can be found in output 1. We have also achieved objective 2 fully by developing rigorous error analysis of Sinc approximation for multidimensional Hilbert transform as well as the error analysis of the algorithm for pricing barrier options and computing survival probabilities. These results are reported in output 1. After the project began, we identified some other important problems that can be solved by the methods we had developed. Thus, we went beyond the original scope of the project and contributed in the following ways. (1) We solved stochastic control problems in a class of jump-diffusions using multidimensional Hilbert transform and Sinc approximation and successfully applied our method to deliver computationally efficient solutions in various financial applications including multi-asset option pricing and optimal investment. The results can be found in output 2. (2) We developed a Fourier transform based method for solving backward stochastic differential equations which appear in many financial applications. Fourier transform and Hilbert transform are two commonly used transforms in science and engineering. We initially tried Hilbert transform, but it turned out Fourier transform is more suitable for solving backward stochastic differential equations. Our method is applied to obtain computationally efficient solutions to various option pricing problems in models with realistic features. See output 3. During the project, I trained two Ph.D. students, whose dissertations are directly related to the topics of the project. Output 1 became the first part of the dissertation of Jie Chen, and outputs 2 and 3 constituted the dissertation of Yingming Ge. Both students successfully defended their dissertations and graduated. They are now working in investment companies in Hong Kong and Shanghai. I would like to explain the unspent balance for this project. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, many conferences were cancelled in 2020 and 2021 and it was difficult to attract scholars to come to Hong Kong for research visits to work on the project. Thus, some balance was left.

14203418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203418.value: 1. In output 1, we first studied Sinc approximation of multidimenisional Hilbert transform. For a class of complex-valued analytic functions in a tube, we derived estimates of the errors of Sinc approximation for several quantities. These results generalize the standard one-dimensional results in the literature. We then considered the problems of pricing multi-asset barrier options in exponential Levy asset price models and calculating joint survival probabilities in Levy-driven structural credit risk models. To solve them, we developed a recursive algorithm by utilizing multidimensional Hilbert transform and its Sinc approximation and showed how to implement it efficiently. Furthermore, we performed a comprehensive error analysis of the algorithm, demonstrating its convergence and rate of convergence. We tested our algorithm in various important financial models for the two-asset and three-asset cases. It performs very well in most cases and outperforms some standard benchmark methods. For the Variance Gamma model where our method fails to converge fast, we applied a multidimensional spectral filter in our algorithm that successfully accelerated its convergence. 2. In output 2, we developed a new computational method for finite horizon control problems for a class of jump-diffusions. We apply piecewise constant policy approximation and develop a Hilbert transform approach to solve a discrete time dynamic programming problem. We provide rigorous error bounds for the piecewise constant policy approximation for controlled jump-diffusions, generalizing previous results for diffusions. We also apply our method to solve several financial problems: pricing single-asset options in uncertain volatility models and spread options in models with uncertain volatility and correlation, and optimal investment, including utility maximization and mean-variance portfolio selection when asset prices follow jump-diffusions. Through various numerical examples, we demonstrate the properties of our method and show that it is a computationally efficient choice for low-dimensional problems. Our method also compares favorably with some popular approaches. 3. In output 3, we propose a method based on the Fourier transform for numerically solving backward stochastic differential equations. We apply time discretization to the forward equation of the state variable as well as the backward equation to yield a recursive system with terminal conditions. By assuming the integrability of the functions in the terminal conditions and applying truncation, we derive recursions in the Fourier space. The fractional FFT algorithm is applied to efficiently compute the Fourier and inverse Fourier transforms. We showcase the efficiency of our method through various numerical examples in option pricing applications.

14203418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203418.value: 1. In the project, we focused on two types of multi-asset options: barrier options and spread options. We can extend our method to price other types of multi-asset options, such as double lookback options and multi-asset Bermudan options in future research. We can also consider the problem of valuation adjustments for credit derivatives in Levy-driven structural credit risk models. 2. We can extend our method to solve more challenging backward stochastic differential equations, such as those with jumps and coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations.

14203418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203418.value: Fast and accurate computational methods are needed for solving many problems in financial markets, such as pricing complex financial products like options, assessing the credit risk of companies, and making investment decisions. In this project, we study how to compute multidimensional Hilbert transform efficiently and use this result to develop fast and accurate methods for solving these problems in sophisticated financial models with realistic features. We also provide rigorous convergence analysis of our methods. The outputs of the project equip financial market participants with computationally efficient tools for pricing, credit risk assessment, and investment.

14203518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203518.value: Along with the thriving of social networks, photos have become an increasingly popular media for people to share and communicate. The stories behind such photos convey valuable information about our life, our world, and perhaps more importantly commercial opportunities. Whereas the computer vision community has made remarkable progress in tasks like face recognition and object detection, we are still far from being able to understand the stories behind images — recognizing objects of certain categories is only the first step. In the proposed project, we aim to move beyond conventional tasks and develop a new methodology to extract high-level messages, instead of object categories, from real-world photos. This task requires not only recognizing what can be observed visually but also connecting them to background knowledges. For example, to understand an image which shows Obama talking to Putin, one has to know that their conversation is likely to be related to US-Russia relations. To tackle this problem, we plan to explore a framework that can incorporate a knowledge base with visual analysis. Here, the knowledge base can provide useful information hidden behind the scene. At the heart of this framework is a joint reasoning process, which will construct a graph that connects visual elements and real-world entities (from the knowledge base) given a photo and then reason about the associations among them. It is important to note that this exploration differs fundamentally from previous work in computer vision, and therefore a new dataset is needed. However, this is nontrivial. Whereas one can readily collect a large number of story photos from the Internet, it is prohibitive to acquire detailed annotations for them. To overcome this difficulty, we propose to develop a weakly supervised learning framework that combines both the local context (e.g. news articles and user descriptions) and the knowledge base to provide supervision. This project has impacts on both academic study and real-world practice. From an academic standpoint, it may lead to new insight into the question of how to incorporate background knowledge with visual analysis, which is important to image understanding but often overlooked in previous studies. From a practical standpoint, it brings visual understanding from object level to story level, and thus opens up a number of exciting applications, e.g. vision-based news retrieval and automatic news synthesis. 隨著社交網絡的蓬勃發展，照片已成為人們分享和交流的越來越受歡迎的媒介。這些照片背後的故事傳達了有關我們的生活，我們的世界，以及也許更重要的商業機會的寶貴信息。雖然計算機視覺在人臉識別和物體檢測等任務方面取得了顯著進步，但我們仍然無法理解圖像背後的故事。目前我們能做到物體識別，只是朝著這個目標的第一步。 在此項目中，我們的目標是超越傳統任務，並開發一種新方法，從真實世界的照片中提取高層次的信息，而不是僅僅是物體類別。 此任務不僅需要識別可以在視覺上觀察到的內容，還需要將它們與背景知識聯繫起來。 例如，為了理解奧巴馬與普京談話的新聞圖片，人們必須知道他們的談話可能與美俄關係有關。 為了解決這個問題，我們計劃探索一個可以將知識庫與可視化分析相結合的框架。 在這裡，知識庫可以提供隱藏在場景後面的有用信息。 該框架的核心是一個聯合推理過程，它將構建一個可以連接視覺元素和真實世界實體的關係圖。基於這個關係圖，給出照片，然後推斷它們之間的關聯。 這種探索與以前的計算機視覺工作有著根本的不同，因此需要一個新的數據集。 但是，構造這個數據集並不容易。 雖然人們可以隨時從互聯網上收集大量的故事照片，但卻無法獲得詳細的註釋。 為了克服這個困難，我們將開發一個弱監督學習框架，結合圖片的語境（例如新聞文章和用戶描述）和知識庫來監督模型訓練的過程。 該項目對學術研究和實際應用都有影響。 從學術角度來看，它可能會引發對如何將背景知識與視覺分析相結合的問題的新思考。這對於圖像理解很重要，但在以前的研究中往往被忽視。 從實用角度來看，它帶來了從對象層面到故事層面的視覺理解，從而可以開闢了許多令人興奮的應用，例如： 基於視覺的新聞檢索和自動新聞合成。

14203518.label: Realisation of objectives
14203518.value: For Objective 1: Understanding scenes from vision clues requires a unified formulation that integrates both elements and background knowledge. To achieve this goal, object detection and instance segmentation are the key challenges that localize each element in the scene and enables hierarchical scene understanding. According, we develop several object detection and instance segmentation frameworks to leverage both element and background knowledge, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Specifically, for object detection, we noticed state-of-the-art detectors mostly rely on predefined anchors that limit their localization quality. We propose a Guided Anchoring scheme, which leverages semantic features to guide the anchoring. We also carefully revisited the standard training practice of detectors and find the imbalance often limits the detection performance during the training process. We proposed Libra R-CNN, a simple but effective framework for balanced learning for object detection. We observed that precise localization requires careful placement of each side of the bounding box. Thus, we propose Side-Aware Boundary Localization (SABL), where each side of the bounding box is respectively localized with a dedicated network branch, bringing much more precise bounding localization results. Beyond object detection, we further explore instance segmentation for more detailed descriptions of elements and backgrounds in scenes. We proposed Hybrid Task Cascade (HTC), which interweaves multi-tasks for joint multi-stage processing, and adopts a fully convolutional branch to provide the spatial context of the background. With the proposed works, we successfully integrate both visual elements and background knowledge into a unified formulation, facilitating the exploration of scene understanding. For Objective 2: Vision, language, and audio are three major modalities for human perception and reasoning. They convey distinct yet complementary semantics that can be combined together to achieve next-level context understanding and reasoning, which is hard to accomplish when each of this modality is adopted in isolation. However, since the data format and granularity of these modalities are completely different, the key to combine these modalities is how to efficiently extract and fuse semantics across modalities for downstream tasks. In this direction, we made several successful attempts. We developed an efficient framework to jointly reason over movie videos and movie synopses via event dynamics and character interactions. The proposed framework is a graph-based architecture consisting of two modules, namely an event flow module for aligning the sequence of shots in a movie segment, each showing a particular event, to the sequence of sentences in a synopsis paragraph. And a character interaction module for capturing characters and their behaviors (both actions and interactions) and associating them with the corresponding descriptions. By jointly reasoning across vision and language, the proposed framework is shown to remarkably improves the matching accuracy over conventional feature-based methods. Similar frameworks that integrate movie videos and corresponding text have been successfully applied to movie scene segmentation, movie shot classification, movie person association, and movie face recognition. In terms of joint inference over vision and audio. We also developed efficient frameworks to integrate semantics across vision and audio for sound separation and generation. Specifically, thanks to the integrated semantics, it can recursively pick out the most salient sound and remove it from the mixture, until the mixture becomes empty or contains only noise, so that it can be applied to sound mixtures with arbitrary numbers and types of sounds, and sounds with small energy can emerge and be separated more accurately. For Objective 3: Current advances in computer vision mostly require rich annotations for supervised learning. However, richly annotated data are expensive to acquire. Therefore, it is critical to explore weakly supervised learning, bringing benefits in two aspects. First, it can help to learn more representative features from a large amount of weakly annotated data, boosting the performance of downstream tasks. Second, it can transfer the knowledge of models from one domain to another one without requiring extra annotations, increasing the generalizability of vision algorithms. Specifically, for learning more representative features, we leveraged motion cues to learn visual representations without relying on annotations. We design a new learning-from-motion paradigm that seeks to recover the full-image motion from the input image and several sparse flow guidance, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several downstream tasks. We proposed a novel framework for leveraging web data to train video recognition models that learn from noisy and weakly annotated web data. Experiments show that our method is more data-efficient in training by utilizing data from multiple sources and formats. For transferring from a source domain to target domains without requiring extra annotations, we proposed a novel approach to domain adaption for object detection to handle the issues in “where to look” and “how to align”. Our key idea is to mine the discriminative regions and focus on aligning them across both domains. We studied an open compound domain adaptation (OCDA) problem, in which the target is a compound of multiple homogeneous domains without domain labels. We propose a new approach based on a curriculum domain adaptation strategy and a memory module to increase the model’s agility towards novel domains. In summary, these proposed research work effectively leverages weakly supervised learning strategies for representation learning and domain adaption from photos and their contexts. For Objective 4: To facilitate the research of exploring algorithms that can reason across different modalities and under weak supervision, a high-quality and large-scale dataset that faithfully reflect the challenges raised in this direction is necessary. However, while existing datasets hardly meet our need in terms of data quality and the coverage of modalities, constructing such a new dataset is also very hard, since we need to find a domain that have multiple modalities and each modality convey informative and complementary semantics. We adopted gymnastic actions as the target domain and successfully built FineGym, a new dataset that consists of gymnastic videos performed by Olympic athletes and text descriptions of each individual action. Besides, it also provides temporal annotations at both action and sub-action levels with a three-level semantic hierarchy. Through experiments we found FineGym raises significant new challenges for action recognition, e.g., how to parse the temporal structures from a coherent action, and how to distinguish between subtly different action classes according to their action descriptions. We adopted place as the target domain and successfully built Placepedia, a new large-scale dataset with more than 35 million photos and meta-information of 240K unique places. Specifically, place is an important element in visual understanding. People can often tell a place’s functionality, e.g. a restaurant or a shop, its cultural style, e.g. Asian or European, as well as its economic type, e.g. industry oriented or tourism oriented. While place recognition has been widely studied in previous work, there remains a long way towards comprehensive place understanding, which is far beyond categorizing a place with an image and requires information of multiple aspects. Placepedia cover massive multi-faceted information including place photos, place GDP, place population and so on, allowing various multi-modality and semi-supervised studies to be conducted. For Objective 5: We have constructed a prototype photo and video retrieval system and a demo system for visual summary, which shows the strength of our methods. Overall, the works mentioned above have resulted in 20+ papers published on top conferences on computer vision.

14203518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203518.value: Overall, we found that 1) high-level understanding of scenes or stories require effective integration of multiple kinds of elements, e.g. human action, objects, environments, and the interactions among them; and that 2) unannotated data contain valuable information, which, if effectively leveraged, can lead to notable performance improvement without a huge cost for data annotation. Below, we summarize key findings in several aspects: 1) Despite remarkable progress in the past decade, detecting objects in the wild remains a very challenging problem. Errors in detection, to a large extent, would impair the performance of higher-level understanding. Nowadays, modern object detectors have been very sophisticated. To make further improvement on detection, we need a more balanced perspective that covers different stages of the detection pipeline (Libra R-CNN at CVPR’19); stronger capability of domain adaptation (Selective Cross-Domain Alignment at CVPR’19); effective ways to integrate information from different aspects (Hybrid Task Cascade at CVPR’19); and more accurate localization of boundaries (Side-Aware Boundary Localization at ECCV’20). 2) New learning paradigms are promising especially in the context where not all the data are annotated. Our work on conditional motion propagation (CVPR’19) shows that motion hints, which are widely available in videos, are significant for learning visual representation. Our work on learning to cluster (CVPR’20) shows that clustering structures overall the entire data set are an important complement to the information contained within individual samples. Our work on omni-sourced video recognition (ECCV’20) shows that images and videos can be effectively combined when learning visual representation, where they play complementary roles. Our work on caption-supervised recognition (ECCV’20) image captions together with reliable information parsing can be used as userful supervisory signal in the place of human labels. 3) There exist multiple kinds of semantic connections among visual elements (e.g. persons, objects, and scenes). Such connections convey important messages in beyond the labels of individual elements. Our graph-based framework that bridges movies and synopses (ICCV’19) clearly demonstrates the benefits of leveraging such connections, which not only lead to better understanding of the whole stories but also benefit the recognition of individual elements. Our work on visual-sound separation & association (ICCV’19, ECCV’20) shows the interesting connections between the visual and the audio domains. We also explored the combination of various elements in temporal action parsing (CVPR’20) and have obtained promising results.

14203518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203518.value: This project brings up several topics that are worthy of further exploration. 1. The connections across time, i.e. those connections that link between the future and the past, play significant roles in developing higher-level understanding. However, discovering and exploiting such connections remain challenging. New modeling technologies, e.g. transformer, provide more powerful tools. It is interesting to see how such latest techniques can help. 2. Recently, there have been remarkable advances in natural language processing and information extraction. Such advances can potentially lead to more versatile and powerful methods to connect visual and linguistic domains. These new language models, if effectively utilized, may take the performance to a new level. 3. Academic research is just a beginning part of this work. To see the value of this research, it is important to use it in practical applications. In recent years, a number of new application domains emerge, e.g. metaverse, interactive healthcare, and smart cities, which may benefit from the improved capability of whole-scene understanding.

14203518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203518.value: The primary goal of this project is to develop a new framework to integrate visual elements together with their inter-connections. Such a new framework allows us to move beyond the limitation of current visual recognition techniques, which focus on specific aspects of a visual scene, to form a whole understanding at a higher level. To achieve the goal mentioned above, we face several key challenges: 1) the accuracy and reliability of visual recognition, e.g. detecting visual objects; 2) the capability of learning from unannotated or partly annotated data; and 3) the capability of discovering and exploiting the relationships among different elements. With the methods developed under the support of this project, we made significant progress in all these aspects. Specificially, we significantly improved the efficiency and accuracy of visual recognition and detection in challenging settings; we developed semi-supervised and unsupervised methods that can effectively leverage unannotated data, thus greatly reducing the cost of data preparation; we developed a novel framework that allows various visual elements to be integrated for higher-level understanding.

14203618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203618.value: Over years, graph processing has been extensively studied. On one hand, there are many graph algorithms being developed to deal with large real graphs using database techniques. Such algorithms include reachability queries, graph traversal, subgraph matching, maximal weight matching, dense subgraphs finding, connected components, community detection and searching, influential maximization, ranking (e.g. PageRank), etc. On the other hand, there are many graph processing systems developed on different platforms using different optimization techniques: from multi-core shared memory to distributed computing, from MapReduce to BSP (Bulk Synchronous Parallel), from synchronous to asynchronous, from pushing styled message passing to polling styled message passing and hybrid styled of pushing/polling, from naive graph processing systems to graph processing systems built on some existing data processing systems. In such graph processing systems, many different programming models have been used (e.g. vertex-centric, block-centric, and subgraph-centric). Some systems design a domain-specific language to be used. For both graph algorithms and systems, the important issue is efficiency. But, there are some key issues that are not well addressed. For graph algorithms, they are designed to deal with individual graph problems. A question that arises is how to conduct some complex tasks which needs more than one graph algorithms. In other words, the question is how we support users to query graphs in a flexible manner, given a large collection of graph algorithms available. For graph processing systems, they are developed to allow users to write any programs to process graphs. But, they require users to fully understand the mechanisms and the optimization techniques adopted in the underneath system in order to achieve efficiency. A user cannot achieve high efficiency in a system, even if he/she knows how to achieve high efficiency in another system for the same graph algorithm. In this project, we focus on SQL, and aim at extending SQL to be a graph query language to support a large range of graph processing tasks in different computing platforms which can be standalone/distributed. By such a language, we achieve separation to separate what to query from how to query efficiently. A key issue is recursive SQL handling from all perspectives from relational algebra, to recursive SQL, and its optimization/implementation on distributed computing platforms. The academic significance of the project is of two folds. In addition to publications reporting the project finding, the methodology and techniques developed will be implemented to demonstrate the strength of our approach. 多年來，圖處理已成為一個廣泛研究的領域。一方面，有許多圖算法利用數據庫技術處理大圖問題。這些算法包括可達性查詢，圖遍曆，子圖疋配，極大權重疋配，密集子圖查找，連通分量計算，社區偵測和查找，影響力最大化，節點排名（例如PageRank）等。另一方面，有許多運用了不同優化技術的圖處理系統部署在不同的平臺上：從多核共享記憶體到分布式計算平臺，從MapReduce到BSP(批量同步並行)，從同步執行到異步執行，從主動推送的消息傳遞模式到輪詢消息傳遞模式和混合的消息傳遞模式。在這些圖處理系統中，已經使用了許多不同的編程模型（例如，以節點為中心，以塊為中心，以子圖為中心）。還有一些系統設計了領域專用語言來編程。 在圖算法和圖系統中，效率是一個重要的問題。然而仍有一些關鍵問題尚未得到很好的解決。對於圖算法，它們旨在處理一個單一的圖問題，這裏需要考慮的問題是如何執行一系列由多個圖算法組成的復雜任務。換句話說，我們應該如何為用戶提供一種靈活的方式來查詢圖。對於圖處理系統，它們的開發允許用戶編寫任意的程式來處理圖數據。為了實現高效的處理，用戶在編寫程式時必須充分理解底層系統中復雜的實現和優化機制。這就意味着，即使用戶知道如何在某個圖系統中實現一個高效的圖算法，他也無法將這一實現直接地遷移到另一個系統中。 在這個項目中，我們的研究專註於SQL語言，旨在將SQL擴展為圖查詢語言，從而在單機和分布式平臺上支持大量的圖處理任務。透過擴展的SQL查詢語言，我們實現了將如何制定查詢内容和如何執行高效的查詢之間的隔離。其中關鍵的問題是反映了關係代數、遞歸的SQL查詢和其在分布式系統上的實現和優化的所有角度的遞歸SQL處理機制。該項目的學術意義在於兩個方面。我們會在學術文章中報告我們的項目所使用的技術，此外還會透過高效的實現來驗證這些方法的優勢。

14203618.label: Realisation of objectives
14203618.value: The two objectives of this project on efficient SQL-based graph processing are: to enhance SQL to support a large number of graph algorithms that can be executed efficiently in graph processing platforms including RDBMSs, and to investigate query processing and query optimization techniques to support graph algorithms in distributed graph processing platforms. To support both graph analytics and graph algorithms (e.g., subgraph matching), we have provided systematic approaches by enhancing RDBMS on a distributed platform. To integrate graph analytics together with data analytics in a system, first, we show that any graph algorithms that can be supported by linear algebra (e.g., semi-ring) can be supported by relational algebra and therefore SQL, and any graph analytics (e.g., PageRank), that need iterative computing, can be supported by our enhanced recursive SQL, which is impossible by SQL’99. Second, we have developed our approach on Spark, the distributed platform for large-scale data processing, by integrating SparkSQL and GraphX. For any graph algorithms that are issued by SQL with enhanced recursive SQL, we are able to optimize them and execute them like a graph algorithm on top of GraphX. To support subgraph matching, which is an NP-hard problem having been extensively studied, we support it as a special case of complex joins processing in RDBMSs. We have developed a general approach to support subgraph counting for any k-node graph patterns, and have developed a system that can efficiently support complex joins and any other relational algebra operators by separating communication from computation in a distributed system. We have also developed new approaches to support various of graph algorithms, as summarized in the major findings and research outcome.

14203618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203618.value: We summarize the main results below. First, we have developed a system called SQL-G on top of SparkSQL and GraphX on Spark which is a well-known open-source distributed platform for large-scale data processing. We can support any graph analytics/algorithms that can be specified by linear algebra (semi-ring) using SQL with our enhanced with clause. This work is reported in TKDE 2021. We also show that our enhanced recursive SQL can be used to support machine learning (e.g., expectation-maximization), which is reported in DASFAA’21. Second, we study local subgraph counting, which is to count the occurrences of a user-given pattern graph p around every node v in a data graph G. This problem is a variant of subgraph isomorphism by enumeration, an NP-hard problem. We develop a new general approach to count any k pattern graphs. The key idea behind is that we do local subgraph counting by homomorphism counting, which can be solved by relational algebra using joins, group-by and aggregation. By homomorphism counting, we do local subgraph counting by eliminating counts for those that are not subgraph isomorphism matchings from the total count for any possible matchings. We have developed a distributed system named DISC on Spark. This is reported in PVLDB’20. Third, we process subgraph matching (or subgraph isomorphism) by complex joins, and propose new approaches to make it efficient. In particular, we study parallel query processing with a focus on reducing the communication cost, which is the dominating factor in parallel query processing. The communication cost becomes large if the intermediate results between operators are large in intra-operator parallelism. To reduce communication cost, we separate communication from computation using several new operators. We have developed a distributed system named Secco by revamping SparkSQL on Spark, and confirmed the efficiency of our approach in our performance studies using real datasets. The works are reported in ICDE’2, ICDE’22, and SIGMOD’22. Fourth, we also study how to accurately estimate cardinality in query processing by Neural Network Gaussian Process, which is a lightweight approach that can learn very fast. The work is reported in SIGMOD’22. Sixth, we study new graph algorithms to support distributed subgraph enumeration (PVLDB’19), near-maximum independent set computing in dynamic graphs (ICDE’19), maximal clique search in uncertain networks (ICDE’19), unboundedness and efficiency of truss maintenance in evolving graphs (SIGMOD’19), and skyline cohesive group queries (ICDE’20).

14203618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203618.value: With the rapid growth of social networks and new applications, the needs to support both big graph and data analytics in a unified way on a distributed platform are high. There are still many difficult issues from the language perspective, to the system design/optimization/implementation. We will continue to work on these issues.

14203618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203618.value: With the rapid growth of social networks and new applications, there are increasing needs to support big graph processing. A main issue in this project entitled “efficient SQL-based graph processing” is to find a unified way to support graph analytics in a similar manner like data analytics over relational database management systems (RDBMSs), due to the fact that RDBMSs are the major players used in industries to deal with big data. It needs to support both graph/data analytics in a single system, as the hidden cost of transferring graph/data between two systems (one for graph processing and one for data processing) is very high. To make it possible, we show a way to support graph algorithms that can be supported by linear algebra (semi-ring) based on relational algebra and therefore SQL, and we propose a new enhanced with clause to support recursive SQL queries by which we can support graph analytics (e.g., PageRank) by SQL in RDBMSs. To deal with efficiency issue for graph analytics by SQL, we have developed a system SQL-G by integrating SparkSQL and GraphX on Spark. In brief, for graph analytics that are specified by SQL, we can convert them to GraphX using graph processing techniques on Spark. To further deal with efficiency for graph analytics and graph algorithms (e.g., subgraph isomorphism, subgraph matching, subgraph counting), we have developed new techniques to support complex join processing by distributed computing on Spark. We also study many new graph algorithms to deal with different graph problems, and confirm the efficiency. All works are reported in major international conferences and journals.

14204118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204118.value: 香港約有320,000家中小企業，佔所有商業機構的98％以上。他們中的許多人，特別是擁有在線溝通渠道的商店，在很大程度上依賴社交媒體（微信，應用程序，Facebook等）每天回答類似的問題，如營業時間，餐桌預訂，產品規格，運輸方式等。從理論上講，聊天機器人可以用來自動回答這些問題並減輕員工的工作量，使他們能夠專注於其他業務活動。然而，在實踐中，中小企業幾乎不能負擔現有的聊天機器人系統。最新的聊天機器人主要基於深度強化學習（DRL）開發。 DRL無法在抽象層面進行推理，使得聊天機器人很難直接整合商業邏輯。為了緩解這種困境，訓練聊天機器人需要大量數據，這是中小企業無法負擔的。因此，我們迫切需要一種用於構建聊天機器人的有效且廉價的方法。 我們觀察到經典的符號人工智能（AI）可以充分利用抽象層次推理來基於現有的有限數據對知識進行編碼，即它可以將業務邏輯編碼到其學習模型中。然而，符號人工智能存在一些缺點，包括處理矛盾的效率低；然而，這些缺點通常可以由DRL有效地處理。事實上，我們的初步實驗表明，通過將符號人工智能集成到DRL中而開發的聊天機器人，可以大大超越傳統的聊天機器人。這就奠定了項目的主要目標：研究和開發一種有效且適應性強的方法，來構建一個適用於不同業務領域，並且中小企業能夠負擔得起的聊天機器人。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種稱為DRILLED（有限數據的深度強化學習）的方法，通過將符號人工智能集成到深度強化學習中來構建聊天機器人，這樣我們不僅可以將不同的業務邏輯合併到聊天機器人中，還可以使用有用的聊天機器人來構建有限的數據。 DRILLED由3個新功能組件組成：即（1）策略整形器（PS），（2）獎勵整形器（RS），以及（3）專家分析器（EP）。 PS和RS包含邏輯推理，它們是通過符號人工智能學習獲得的。 EP提取對話的核心特徵和屬性，它通過自然語言處理技術學習。基於EP並在PS和RS的指導下，DRILLED使用DRL構建聊天機器人。 值得注意的是：現有的聊天機器人研究的公開數據非常有限。在這個項目中，我們將構建一個用於訓練和評估聊天機器人的數據集，數據集將供公眾下載。

14204118.label: Realisation of objectives
14204118.value: For objective 1 "Build effective and adaptive chatbots by integrate symbolic AI into deep reinforcement learning": Our two published papers trying to solve this problem: "Re-entry Prediction for Online Conversations via self-supervised Learning" in Proceedings of the 2021 Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EMNLP 2021) and "Dynamic Online Conversation Recommendation" in Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL2020). Topics in social media content evolve over time, and it is crucial to understand social media users and their interpersonal communications in a dynamic manner. In these two papers, we studied dynamic online conversation recommendations, to help users engage in conversations that satisfy their evolving interests. Different from works in conversation recommendation which assume static user interests, our model captures the temporal aspects of user interests. Moreover, our model can cater to cold start problems where conversations are new and unseen in training. We propose a neural architecture with the capability of incorporating human-defined rules (i.e. symbolic rules) to analyze changes in user interactions and interests over time, whose result is used to predict which discussions the users are likely to enter. We conduct experiments on large-scale collections of Reddit conversations. Results on three subreddits show that our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models based on a static assumptions of user interests. We further evaluate performance in cold start and observe consistently better performance by our model when considering various degrees of the sparsity of user’s chatting history and conversation contexts. Lastly, our analysis also confirms the change of user interests. This further justifies the advantage and efficacy of our model. For objective 2 "Build affordable chatbots using limited training data and minimum human intervention": In our published paper "Learning Efficient Dialogue Policy from Demonstrations through Shaping" in the proceeding of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, we have presented this problem and derived a solution. Specifically, training a task-oriented dialogue agent is prohibitively expensive since it requires a large volume of data and needs frequent interactions with users. Even though human demonstrations can be used to accelerate learning progress, how to effectively leverage demonstrations to learn dialogue policy remains a critical problem. In this paper, we have presented that efficiently learns dialogue policy through policy shaping and reward shaping. We have used an imitation model to distill knowledge based on which policy-shaping estimates feedback on how the agent should act in policy space. Reward shaping is then incorporated into bonus state-actions similar to demonstrations explicitly in value space encouraging better exploration. The effectiveness of the proposed method in three dialogue domains and a challenging domain adaptation task with both user simulator evaluation and human evaluation has been presented. For objective 3 "Build chatbots that are applicable to SMEs in different business domains by incorporate business logics into the chatbots": In our published paper "Continuity of Topic, Interaction, and Query: Learning to Quote in Online Conversations" in the Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, we have presented this problem and derived a solution. Specifically, we observed that incorporating business logic is important in continuing a topic and properly quoting (or recommending) information to the user so as to successfully explain and convince a user. However, such a task is challenging for both humans and machines. This paper studies automatic quotation generation in an online conversation and explores how language consistency affects whether a quotation fits the given context. Here, we capture the contextual consistency of a quotation in terms of latent topics, interactions with the dialogue history, and coherence to the query turn’s existing content. Further, an encoder-decoder neural framework is employed to continue the context with a quotation via language generation. Experiment results on two large-scale datasets in English and Chinese demonstrate that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art models. Further analysis shows that topic, interaction, and query consistency are all helpful to this task. For objective 4 "Construct a dataset for training and evaluating a chatbot. The dataset will be made available for public to download": Compared with CrossWOZ (Chinese) and MultiWOZ (English) datasets which have coarse-grained information, there is no dataset that handles fine-grained and hierarchical level information properly. In this paper, we publish the first Cantonese knowledge-driven Dialogue Dataset for REStaurant (KddRES) in Hong Kong, which grounds the information in multi-turn conversations to one specific restaurant. Our corpus contains 8,000 conversations that derive from 10 restaurants with various styles in different regions. In addition to that, we designed fine-grained slots and intents to better capture semantic information. The benchmark experiments and data statistic analysis show the diversity and rich annotations of our dataset. We believe the publish of KddRES can be a necessary supplement of current dialogue datasets and more suitable and valuable for small and middle enterprises (SMEs) of society, such as building a customized dialogue system for each restaurant. The corpus and benchmark models are publicly available. Detail can be referred to the paper: Hongru Wang, Min Li, Zimo Zhou, Gabriel Pui Cheong Fung, Kam-Fai Wong: KddRES: A Multi-level Knowledge-driven Dialogue Dataset for Restaurant Towards Customized Dialogue System. CoRR abs/2011.08772 (2020)

14204118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204118.value: Our experiments show that a chatbot developed with limited training and testing data by integrating symbolic AI into DRL can dramatically outperform conventional chatbots. But the current research was prototypical in nature and domain-specific limiting its scalability and universality. Future work can focus on chatbot generalization. In addition, the chatbot developed by using the existing algorithm is hard to visualize its decision logic. Research on explainable AI in the chatbot domain is necessary in order to further improve its ease of use.

14204118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204118.value: This project aims for building low-cost data-limited intelligent chatbots which can incorporate different business logics effectively and efficiently. This is essential for SMEs, such as online stores. According to the Hong Kong Trade and Industry Department, there are approximately 320.000 small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Hong Kong, which constitute over 98% of all business establishments. For this reason, this research is significant to the advancement of the global Internet Economy at large, and that of Hong Kong in particular.

14204418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204418.value: 自動摘要文本文檔具有廣泛的應用，用於處理文本內容的現有方法基本上利 用一袋詞及擴展含實體信息 但是，這種表示方式只能表達很少的語義信息。現有的依賴關係語法和Universal Dependencies提供依賴關係清單。然而，核心概和頭部依賴關係只能被視為膚淺的語義信息。最近提出了諸如遞歸神經網 絡（RNN）的深度神經網絡模型來處理文本摘要。一個特點是它可以直接處理利用文本中出現的詞序的詞序列。然而，這些方法仍然考慮非常有限的語義信息。此外，用單詞序列表達的自然語言文本包含句法特性。 我們提出了一個利用更深層語義信息的框架。對於每個句子，文本內容被轉換為精細粒度的語義圖，捕獲精細的概念和關係，這些概念和關係從最近提出的語義形式主義抽象意義表示擴展而來。雖然最近一些關於語義分析的工作試圖解決這個問題，但轉換質量仍然不夠。此外，我們打算結合知識圖表以新穎的方式豐富語義。從句子生成語義圖可以表示為序列到圖的轉換問題。我們建議通過結構化預測學習和新穎的深度神經模型來解決這個問題。這比標準結構化預測更具挑戰性，因為在每個輸入字和由圖形結構組成的預測輸出之間不存在一對一的對應關係。 在獲得語義表示之後，用於消化文本內容的一種有用機制是發掘隱藏的或潛在的方面/主題。現有的主題建模僅假設基於單詞的主題表示和基於單詞的主題與文本內容的關聯。在對精細粒度方面進行建模時，它具有局限性。我們提出的主題發掘提供了更豐富的主題語義表示。此外，可以基於文本數據的特徵自動確定諸如主題數量之類的模型複雜度。這種能力可以避免現有方法的共同缺點，其中需要提前提供方面/主題的數量，從而導致不期望的結果。另一個新穎性是能夠將知識圖中的語義知識結合起來，從而發掘出更好的主題。 我們打算在互聯網文檔搜索利用多文檔摘要和結構化摘要中應用我們的框架。

14204418.label: Realisation of objectives
14204418.value: We conduct research with the goal of developing a new framework that can exploit deeper semantic information for natural language texts. As mentioned in the proposal, we focus on a fine-grained semantic graph structure known as Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) which is derived from semantic parsing research. We exploit the graph fragments including nodes, links, and paths which can capture different levels of semantic information. We explore the formalism of structured prediction and deep neural models. We have achieved all the three objectives stated in our proposal. More detailed information is presented below. We propose a new model for AMR parsing which takes a piece of text such as a sentence and transforms the text into an AMR graph capturing the essential semantic meaning. We develop a new end-to-end neural model that treats AMR parsing as a series of dual decisions on the input sentence and the incrementally constructed graph. It addresses two critical questions for parsing. The first question is which part of the input sequence to abstract. The second question is where in the output graph to construct the new concept. We design a new algorithm based on iterative inference that helps achieve better answers for both questions. We also investigate the detection of hidden aspects from the text content. Through the semantic representation developed above, we propose an aspect discovery model that can offer richer semantic representation of aspects. Recall that each sentence has been transformed into a semantic graph. The graph contains all the meaningful fine-grained concepts. For any two concepts in the graph, they are connected by a graph fragment embodying a relation. Consequently, a document can be viewed as a bag of concepts and relations. In principle, such representation does not lose any information compared with bag of words in existing topic modeling approaches. We employ AMR as semantic graph representation and tackle the problem of multi-hop question answering (QA), which can be considered as a summarization application. To take advantages of both rich textual corpora and explicit graph structure and make it compatible to all textual knowledge, we explore the usefulness of Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) as a graph annotation to a textual fact. The aim of AMR is to capture every meaningful content in high-level abstraction while removing away inflections and function words in a sentence. As a result, AMR allows us to explore textual facts and simultaneously attributes them with explicit graph structure for explainable fact quality assessment and reasoning. We also investigate a number of summarization applications, namely aspect-based sentiment analysis, legal contract document understanding, and text-to-SQL transformation. The aim of aspect-based sentiment analysis is to summarize fine-grained sentiment information including aspect category, aspect term, opinion term, and sentiment polarity. The aim of legal contract understanding is to identify key clauses from legal contracts. Such summarized information can support review and risk assessment. The aim of text-to-SQL transformation is to conduct transformation from natural language texts into SQL queries via a learning model inspired by automatic summarization.

14204418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204418.value: The research work has produced some successful results. We have published several papers in ACL (Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics) and EMNLP (Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing), both of which are prestigious conferences in natural language processing area. More detailed information is given below. A new end-to-end model treats AMR parsing as a series of dual decisions on the input sequence and the incrementally constructed graph. At each time step, our model performs multiple rounds of attention, reasoning, and composition that aim to answer two critical questions: (1) which part of the input sequence to abstract; and (2) where in the output graph to construct the new concept. We show that the answers to these two questions are mutually causalities. We design a model based on iterative inference that helps achieve better answers in both perspectives, leading to greatly improved parsing accuracy. This work, published in ACL 2020, is the first paper shown in Part C. We also propose a new framework to exploit more valid facts while obtaining explainability for multi-hop QA by dynamically constructing a semantic graph and reasoning over it. We employ AMR as semantic graph representation. Our framework contains three new ideas, namely, an AMR-based Semantic Graph, constructed by candidate fact AMRs to uncover any hop relations among question, answer and multiple facts; a novel path-based fact analytics approach exploiting AMR-SG to extract active facts from a large fact pool to answer questions; a fact-level relation modeling leveraging graph convolution network (GCN) to guide the reasoning process. This work, published in ACL 2021, is the second paper shown in Part C. Regarding aspect-based sentiment analysis, a novel paraphrase modeling paradigm is developed. We further consider the unsupervised cross-lingual transfer setting and develop a new model. We have published two papers in EMNLP 2021, which are the third and the fourth paper shown in Pact C. We also investigate two tasks, namely, legal contract document understanding, and text-to-SQL. For legal contract document understanding, three semantic relations commonly found in legal documents are distilled and modeled leading to better contract understanding and analysis. For text-to-SQL, our proposed model is generalizable and robust. The research findings of both tasks are published in EMNLP 2022.

14204418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204418.value: The research produced in this grant enables potential further development. We intend to investigate the usage of AMR in low-resource settings. This is particularly useful for machine processing and understanding of low-resource languages. We may construct a small amount of parallel texts in different low-resource languages together with the corresponding AMR representation. Such kind of knowledge resource will be beneficial to tackling minority languages facilitating better automated understanding and digest.

14204418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204418.value: Automatic digesting and understanding text documents have a wide range of applications. Existing methods for processing text content basically treat it as a bag of words possibly enriched with entity information. However, such representation can only express little semantic information. We have developed a new framework that exploits deeper semantic information. For each sentence, the text content is transformed into a fine-grained semantic graph capturing fine-grained concepts and relations which are expanded from the recently proposed semantic formalism Abstract Meaning Representation. We propose to tackle this problem via the formalism of structured prediction and novel deep neural models. This is more challenging than standard structured prediction because there is no one-to-one correspondence between each input word and the prediction output composed of a graph structure. We also apply our research finding for information digest and summarization tasks related to sentiment analysis and contract clause understanding in legal contract documents.

14204618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204618.value: The aim of this study is to develop dynamic hydrogels containing single chain nanoparticles as the unfoldable and energy dissipative cross-linkers and to study the effect of biomimetic energy dissipation of such hydrogels on encapsulated cells. Hydrogels are promising delivery vehicle of therapeutic cells for repairing diseased/injured tissues by providing a biomimetic 3D environment for the encapsulated cells. Furthermore, 3D cultures of cells in hydrogels with defined properties also yield critical additional insights into the effect of cell-matrix interactions on cellular behaviors not attainable in traditional 2D cell cultures. Therefore, there exists a huge demand for novel hydrogels with tailor-made physical properties that emulate the natural extracellular matrix (ECM). However, conventional chemically-crosslinked hydrogels generally do not possess the dynamic structures typically found in ECMs due to the static nature of covalently cross-linked networks. Therefore, the mechanical behaviors of conventional hydrogels, such as energy dissipation and viscoelasticity, are very different from that of the natural tissues. The incorporation of reversible physical cross-linking affords the hydrogels with biomimetic mechanical properties. However, it is still challenging to accurately control the structure, distribution, and dynamics of such physical cross-linking in hydrogels, and therefore the overall bulk physical properties of such hydrogels. These limitations restrict the application of conventional hydrogels in fundamental and translational research into cells in 3D cultures. This proposed study aims to develop hydrogels containing unfoldable single chain nanoparticles (SCNPs) as the dynamic crosslinkers. We have developed an effective strategy to scale up the synthesis of SCNPs, which traditional synthesis methods have hitherto restricted to low yields. In this study, we will synthesize unfoldable SCNPs containing reversible host-guest complexations for the folding of SCNPs. Such SCNPs (bearing end reactive groups) will be used to crosslink 4-arm PEG polymers to form hydrogels with spatially controlled distributions of unfoldable SCNP cross-linkers. The fast and reversible binding kinetics of host-guest complexation in the SCNP cross-linkers facilitate rapid recovery and enhances the energy dissipation capacity of hydrogels under cyclic loading. Adjusting the number of reversible host-guest complexations in the SCNP crosslinkers allows the fine tuning of the energy dissipation capacity of hydrogels from a molecular bottom-up approach. This study will also evaluate the behavior of cells encapsulated in such hydrogels under intense and cyclic loading and the efficacy of such hydrogels for in vivo tissue repair. The findings from this project will demonstrate a unique molecularly-tailored approach for designing novel biomaterial carriers for cell therapies. 本研究的目的是開發含有單鏈納米粒子作為可展開和能量耗散交聯劑的動態水凝膠，並研究這種水凝膠的仿生能量耗散對包封細胞的影響。 水凝膠是治療性細胞的優良遞送載體，可以為包封的細胞提供仿生3D環境來修復患病/受損組織。此外，在具有確定化學成分的水凝膠中進行細胞的3D培養也利於對細胞 - 基質相互作用行為的研究，這是傳統2D細胞培養中無法獲得的信息。因此，對具有模擬天然細胞外基質（ECM）的定制物理交聯的新型水凝膠存在巨大需求。然而，由於共價交聯網絡的靜態性質，常規的化學交聯水凝膠通常不具有通常在ECM中發現的動態結構。因此，常規水凝膠的機械性能，例如能量耗散和粘彈性，與天然組織的機械性能非常不同。摻入可逆的物理交聯爲水凝膠提供了仿生機械性能。然而，精確控制水凝膠中這種物理交聯的結構，分佈和動力學以及這種水凝膠的整體物理性質仍然是具有挑戰性的。這些限制限制了常規水凝膠在基礎和轉化研究中應用。 本項目旨在開發含有可展開的單鏈納米顆粒（SCNP）作為動態交聯劑的水凝膠。我們已經制定了一種有效的策略來擴大SCNP的合成，傳統的合成方法迄今為止僅限於低產量合成SCNP。在這項研究中，我們將合成可展開的SCNP，其含有可逆的宿主 - 客體複合物，用於SCNP的折疊。此類SCNP（帶有末端反應性基團）將用於交聯4-臂PEG聚合物以形成具有空間控制的可展開SCNP交聯劑的水凝膠。 SCNP交聯劑中主客體絡合的快速且可逆的結合動力學促進了快速恢復並增強了水凝膠在循環加載下的能量耗散能力。調整SCNP交聯劑中可逆的主客體絡合物的數量允許從分子層面自下而上得微調水凝膠的能量消散能力。該研究還將評估在劇烈的循環負荷下包封在這種水凝膠中的細胞的行為以及這種水凝膠在體內組織修復中的功效。 該項目的研究結果將展示一種獨特的分子定制方法，用於設計可用於細胞療法的新型生物材料載體。

14204618.label: Realisation of objectives
14204618.value: Objective 1: We used S,S’-bis(ɑ’ɑ’-dimethyl-ɑ’’-propargyl acetate) trithiocarbonate (BDPT), an alkynyl-functionalized symmetrical CTA, reported stable in the presence of amines in neutral environment, to mediate the polymerization of N,N-dimethyl acrylamide (DMA). The obtained alkynyl-functionalized macromolecular CTA with two wing blocks of varying molecular weights (macro-CTA-m, m represents the feed molar ratio between DMA and BDPT). The success of RAFT polymerization and control over the polymer structures of macro-CTAs were demonstrated. For the scaled-up preparation of unfoldable dynamic supramolecular SCNGs, we synthesized vinyl-adamantane (V-ADA) as the guest monomer and vinyl-β-cyclodextrin (V-CD) as the host monomer to assemble a water-soluble supramolecular divinyl crosslinker (V-ADA@CD-V) via host-guest complexation. Macro-CTA-m was used to mediate the RAFT polymerization of DMA as the second block monomer and V-ADA@CD-V as the intrachain crosslinker to yield the final product, ADA@CD-SCNGs, and the reactant concentration was as high as 100 mg/mL for the scaled-up production. The obtained ADA@CD-SCNGs have a structure of PDMA0.5m-b-(DMAn-co-ADA@CDx)-b-PDMA0.5m (n and x represent the feed molar ratios of DMA and V-ADA@CD-V to macro-CTA-m, respectively. x is fixed at 1/30th of n. The product is denoted as ADA@CD-nm-SCNGs). The GPC curves of synthesised ADA@CD-100200-SCNGs showed unimodal molecular weight distributions with low PDI (PDI = 1.26), indicating the absence of multi-chain species. The water-phase GPC data showed that the treatment with free ADA led to the unfolding and conformational expansion of ADA@CD-SCNGs, as evidenced by a decrease in the elution time and a slight increase in the apparent molecular weight, while there is no obvious change in the absolute weight-averaged molecular weight. The addition of free ADA (1 mM) did not cleave polymer backbone as evidenced by GPC tests after 7 days incubation with ADA. Furthermore, amines cannot effectively degrade the CTA used for synthesizing SCNGs at the almost neutral pH of cell culture media in which our experiments were conducted. Consistent with the GPC data, DLS confirmed an increase in the hydrodynamic radius of the ADA@CD-100200-SCNGs after unfolding in water. Previous studies have shown that the unfolding of traditional SCNPs or cyclized/knotted SCNGs leads to expansion of the polymer chains, thus increasing their overall size and apparent molecular weights. The obtained ADA@CD-100200-SCNGs were also characterized by AFM. SCNGs deposited on silica exhibited an average height of 10±3 nm. After the unfolding of SCNGs, some linear structures with reduced height are observed. These results confirmed that macro-CTA-200 effectively minimized interchain crosslinking and facilitated intrachain folding of the second central block with V-ADA@CD-V as supramolecular intrachain crosslinker. For comparison with the unfoldable dynamic supramolecular ADA@CD-SCNGs, we prepared non-unfoldable control SCNGs (MBA-SCNGs) by using N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA) as the covalent intrachain crosslinker and the same preparation steps. We also prepared a linear ABA block copolymer without the folded central domain by using V-CD instead of V-ADA@CD-V supramolecular crosslinker during the second block polymerization. The obtained product (CD-LCPs) served as the non-foldable linear control of ADA@CD-SCNGs. From GPC data, MBA-100100-SCNGs and CD-100100-LCPs had similar molecular weights as ADA@CD-100100-SCNGs, and the addition of free ADA had no influence on the molecular weight of these control polymers. We further tested our method with the acrylamide-type divinyl ADA@CD crosslinker. The resultant SCNGs showed narrowly distributed molecular weight with low PDIs and conformational change in response to the addition of free ADA. These findings demonstrate the simplicity, efficacy, and versatility of our method for scaling up the synthesis of SCNGs based on diverse building blocks. Objective 2: The successful scaled-up preparation enables the fabrication of bulk materials, as a mimetic of the natural tissues. The β-cyclodextrin and adamantane (βCD-ADA) host-guest complex has a high equilibrium binding constant (Keq ~105 m −1) and rapid binding kinetics (ka ~108 m−1s−1, kd ~103 s−1) in aqueous conditions. Therefore, analogous to the muscle proteins which dissipate loading energy through force-induced temporary rupture of secondary structures, the ADA@CD-SCNGs are ideal molecular energy dissipaters and network recovery actuators during rapid cyclic loading of hydrogels. We used alkynyl-functionalized and intramolecular-folded ADA@CD-SCNGs as crosslinkers to react with 4-arm poly (ethylene glycol) thiol (4-arm-SH-PEG, Mn 10k, 20% v/w) in a molar ratio of 1:1 via the thiol-alkynyl “click” reaction. The obtained hydrogels possessed a regular network with uniformly distributed folded SCNGs domains (ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogel). A control group of hydrogels without folded domains was also prepared by using the non-foldable linear block polymers, CD-LCPs, to crosslink 4-arm-SH-PEG. Compared with ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogels, CD-LCPs hydrogels showed a comparable shear modulus, as revealed by in situ rheological analysis. Both ADA@CD-SCNGs and CD-LCPs hydrogels exhibited similar mechanical properties under a compression test after being fully swollen to a final solid content of 5% w/v. Live/dead staining revealed that the majority (over 90%) of the hMSCs encapsulated in both ADA@CD-SCNGs and CD-LCPs hydrogels remained viable throughout 14-day static culture, while both hydrogels remained stable. We then subjected the fully swollen cell-laden hydrogels to cyclic compression at a frequency of 0.5 Hz and different peak strains of 0% (static control group), 30% (moderate compression), and 60% (excessive compression). During the 3-hour non-resting cyclic compression, the strain-stress curves of ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogels remained almost identical and showed an evident hysteresis loop, indicating the occurrence of consistent and substantial energy dissipation during the loading period. In contrast, CD-LCPs hydrogels without the folded domains showed a minimal hysteresis loops and energy dissipation. ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogels dissipated 48.5% of the total loading energy under the excessive compressions corresponding to 22-fold higher dissipation ratios than CD-LCPs hydrogels under the same test conditions. Objective 3: We applied the dynamic SCNGs to fabricate bulk materials to precisely tune the dynamic mechanical properties of the bulk material from a molecularly-tailored approach. In contrast to the elastomeric proteins, which have variable and less-defined structure, dynamic SCNGs are ideal molecular energy dissipaters and network recovery actuators during rapid cyclic loading of hydrogels. Thus, dynamic SCNG hydrogels can effectively dissipate substantial loading energy during rapid cyclic compression via reversible conformational change thereby shielding the encapsulated stem cells from excessive mechanical shocks. After 3-hour cyclic compression, live/dead staining revealed that the cell viabilities in ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogels under moderate and excessive compression were 16% and 28% higher, respectively, than those in CD-LCPs hydrogels. ADA@CD-SCNGs group also showed 51% and 48% lower production of reactive oxygen species by the encapsulated cells than that of the CD-LCPs control groups under moderate and excessive compression, respectively. From RT-PCR data, the expression of interleukin-1, a major pro-inflammatory cytokine produced by cells under distress, in ADA@CD-SCNGs group was only 35% and 54% of those in CD-LCPs group. Furthermore, the effective protection of cells by SCNG hydrogels enabled the investigations into the stem cell responses under large compression strains such as differentiations, which is difficult to implement with conventional hydrogels. We analysed the expression of a major chondrogenic gene, SOX9, in the encapsulated stem cell subjected to daily cyclic compressions for 3 hours at 0.5 Hz with the peak strain of 60%. After 3-day chondrogenic culture, qPCR data revealed that the high-strain cyclic compression (60%) significantly promoted the expression of SOX9 in the encapsulated hMSCs compared with the other groups while maintaining good cell viability. These findings suggest that ADA@CD-SCNGs hydrogels can effectively dissipated the loading energy during rapid cyclic compression due to the conformational change of dynamic SCNGs crosslinkers, thereby protecting the encapsulated stem cells from excessive mechanical insults.

14204618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204618.value: Folded single chain polymeric nano-objects are the molecular level soft material with ultra-small size. In this project, we developed a simple but effective strategy for scaling up the synthesis of dynamically-crosslinked supramolecular SCNGs by using a symmetrical trithiocarbonate chain transfer agent (CTA). Our strategy allows the preparation of customized SCNGs with varying chemical structures and different stimuli-responsiveness by using different monomers and intra-chain crosslinkers. Furthermore, the successful scaled-up preparation of supramolecular SCNGs enables us to capitalize on the unique controllable conformational change of dynamic SCNGs to construct multiscale biomimetic functional materials and investigate cellular responses to the molecular-level dynamics of polymeric materials. We proved that the folded conformation of the dynamic SCNGs is critical for their uptake by stem cells as a molecular gene delivery vehicle. We also demonstrated that the SCNGs as the dynamic ligand tether linker can precisely regulate cell mechanosensing on 2D culture surfaces. We showed that the dynamic SCNGs function as the molecular energy dissipaters to effectively shield the encapsulated stem cells in the 3D hydrogel matrix from excessive mechanical shocks. These biomedical studies consistently reveal the critical role of the molecular conformational dynamics of SCNGs in regulating the polymer-cell interactions. We further utilized the bio-functional single polymeric chain-based nanogels which can accommodate easy conjugation of multiple bioactive ligands for ligand presentation. We evaluated the efficacy of such polymeric SCNGs in mediating the controlled dynamic nanoscale presentation of dual bioactive ligands in a single synthetic molecule. Based on this SCNG-based dynamic regulator, we further investigate the potential synergistic action on stem cells by the proximal co-presentation of two model ligands, i.e., RGD peptide, a widely used integrin-binding peptide, and the Foxy5 peptide, a Wnt5a biomimetic peptide capable of initiating noncanonical Wnt signaling upon ligation to its receptor. Such carefully-designed SCNG is capable of mediating triggered co-presentation of the master and cryptic ligands in a single molecule to elicit the synergistic crosstalk between different intracellular signaling pathways, thereby considerably boosting the bioactivity of the presented ligands. This controllable nanoswitching-on of cell‐adhesive ligands' presentation allows regulation of cell adhesion and fate from molecular scale.

14204618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204618.value: The scalable synthesis of dynamic supramolecular SCNGs enables many potential biomedical applications of SCNGs. We will further develop custom SCNGs as molecular delivery system, ligand presentation structure, and components of biomedical hydrogels with dynamic structures as detailed in the following. As an effective molecular delivery vehicle, these dynamic SCNGs show conformation-dependent entry into stem cells and therefore can efficiently deliver genetic materials to regulate stem cell differentiation. When immobilized on substrates as the tether linker of bioactive ligands, the controllable conformational change of the dynamic SCNGs will facilitate manipulation of the nanoscale presentation of bioactive ligands and the temporal regulation of cellular behaviours such as adhesion and mechanosensing. Moreover, the successful scaled-up preparation of SCNGs enables molecular tailoring of the bulk hydrogel materials to achieve biomimetic properties. The obtained hydrogels can provide effective protection of encapsulated cells from deleterious mechanical shock and provide a platform to investigate the stem cell behaviour under large compression strains. The modular nature of this synthetic macromolecular nano-regulator makes it a versatile nanomaterial platform to assist basic and fundamental studies in a wide array of research topics. We anticipate that such a bottom-up molecular tailoring strategy will inspire further applications of SCNGs in the fabrication of a wide range of multiscale materials with unique functionalities for biomedical applications.

14204618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204618.value: Folded single chain polymeric nano-objects are the molecular level soft material with ultra-small size. Here we report a easy and scalable method for preparing single chain nanogels (SCNGs) with improved efficiency. We further investigate the impact of the dynamic molecular conformational change of SCNGs on cellular interactions from molecular to bulk scale. First, the supramolecular unfoldable SCNGs efficiently deliver siRNAs into stem cells as a molecular drug carrier in a conformation-dependent manner. Furthermore, the conformation changes of SCNGs enable dynamic and precise manipulation of ligand tether structure on 2D biomaterial interfaces to regulate the ligand?receptor ligation and mechanosensing of cells. Lastly, the dynamic SCNGs as the building blocks provide effective energy dissipation to bulk biomaterials such hydrogels, thereby protecting the encapsulated stem cells from deleterious mechanical shocks in 3D matrix. Such a bottom-up molecular tailoring strategy will inspire further applications of single chain nano-objects in the biomedical area.
