14204918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204918.value: Real time epileptic seizure detection is a complex pattern recognition task aiming to detect potential seizure activity within several seconds once it occurs. Since epilepsy patients may get seriously hurt during seizure, prompt intervention such as deep brain stimulation and vagus nerve stimulation is vital and can greatly lower the risks. Electroencephalography or EEG is an efficient diagnosis method on epilepsy patients, experienced neurologists can recognize seizure activity from background EEG signal. Decoding the EEG signal accurately is the key for seizure detection since the electrical onset from EEG can indicate clinical onset. Traditional numerical methods explore multi-domain features from EEG signal to represent seizure activity and normal activity, however, it is difficult to identify those truly important indicative features due to the complex nature of human EEG. Inspired by the recent achievements of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in image classification and video understanding tasks, using CNN as an analysis model to decode EEG signal is being investigated. Given a large set of EEG signals, CNN can learn and identify the representative features automatically. Due to its strong generalization capability, CNN is more robust than other traditional methods in detecting seizure activity from EEG signal. Our work will focus on building a CNN-compatible model from multichannel EEG signal. We propose an innovative method to transform the one dimensional (1D) EEG signal to three dimensional (3D) video clips, then 3D CNN models will be used to evaluate each video clip. By taking advantage of three dimensional convolution, the frequency domain, spatial domain and time domain information can be fully utilized. This will achieve great improvements over traditional methods since the geometrical relationship and changing dynamics of brain activities are considered simultaneously. Moreover, we will further explore the impact of different input frame lengths on false detection rate (FDR), seizure onset detection latency and sensitivity. Finally, a fusion network based on model ensemble will be exploited to achieve the best overall performance. The fusion network will be migrated to FPGA platform to allow building a wearable device. This process will include platform based design space exploration (DSE), hardware and software co-optimization and context-aware power reduction. The final system can be used as a warning device to help epilepsy patients avoid danger in everyday life. Our objective of this work is to develop a low latency, low false detection rate and high sensitivity real time seizure detection algorithm with 3D CNN. 實時癲癇檢測是一項復雜的模式識別任務，它的作用是在癲癇發生的數秒之內進行自動識別。由於癲癇病人在病發時可能受到嚴重傷害，使用深部腦刺激術和迷走神經刺激進行及時干預非常重要，可以極大減小病人的受傷風險。腦電圖是一項針對癲癇病人的有效診斷手段，經驗豐富的神經內科醫師可以從腦電波背景信號中准確識別出癲癇症狀。由於腦電中的發病信號可以指明臨床的發病信號，准確對腦電信號進行解碼是癲癇檢測的關鍵。傳統的數值分析方法試圖從腦電中提取多維度的信息來表征癲癇和正常的腦電活動，然而由於人類腦電信號的復雜本質，識別出真正重要的指示性特征是很困難的。受到最近卷積神經網絡在圖像分類和視頻理解任務中成功應用的啟發，人們開始探索利用卷積神經網絡作為分析模型來解碼腦電信號。考慮一個大型的腦電數據集，卷積神經網絡可以自動學習並識別出代表性的特征。同時受益於其強大的泛化能力，卷積神經網絡比傳統方法在識別癲癇任務上要更加穩健可靠。 我們的工作致力於從多通道腦電信號中建立一個和卷積神經網絡相兼容的模型。我們提出了一種創新方法將一維的腦電信號轉化成三維的視頻片段，然后利用三維卷積神經網絡評估每一片段的屬性。受益於三維的卷積操作，頻域、時域和空間域的信息可以被完整提取利用。這將使得我們的方法大幅優於傳統方法，因為大腦活動的幾何關系和時域變化被同時考慮。此外，我們將會進一步地探究輸入視頻片段的時長對誤檢率、檢測延時和敏感度的影響。最終，我們將利用模型集成技術建立一個融合網絡以獲取最佳性能。這個融合網絡將被移植到FPGA平台並建立一套可穿戴設備。移植過程將包含平台級的設計空間搜索，軟硬件協同優化以及基於情境感知的低功耗技術。最終的系統將被用作幫助癲癇病人預防日常風險的預警設備。 我們的設計目標：開發一套基於三維卷積神經網絡的低延時，低誤檢率以及高靈敏度的實時癲癇檢測算法。

14204918.label: Realisation of objectives
14204918.value: We aim to develop efficient seizure detection algorithms and their hardware implementations as part of the future wearable neuromodulation devices. Firstly, we propose an off-line seizure detection algorithm to help analyze the long-term EEG monitoring. Correlation integral is adopted as the discriminative feature to locate every seizure event We integrate a pre-processing stage and post-processing stage to filter the input data and smooth the output. The three-stage algorithm is verified on a scalp EEG database and achieves 84.6% sensitivity and 0.087/h false detection rate. Secondly, a real time seizure detection algorithm and its hardware implementation with FPGA are proposed. Short time Fourier transform is used to extract the spectral energy from multiple channels of the scalp EEG and support vector machine classifies the input signal as normal or ictal state. With this approach, we achieve a seizure onset detection latency of 6 seconds with 98.4% sensitivity and 0.356/h false detection rate. Thirdly, we propose a frame work to transform the 1D EEG time series to 3D video clips and use 3D convolutional neural network to build an end-to-end learning system. 3D CNN is used for its demonstrated learning capability of the spatio-temporal features from video clips.

14204918.value: Epilepsy is a serious brain disease caused by abnormal neuronal discharges. Patients can experience loss of consciousness or convulsions during epileptic seizure, which could easily cause accidents like falling or drowning in daily life. Epilepsy affects about 50 million people in the world and most of the patients live in developing countries. Although antiepileptic drugs can help about 70 percent patients get rid of seizure, the rest patients may be advised to take surgical resection to remove the epileptogenic focus permanently. As an alternative treatment to risky brain surgery, closed-loop neural stimulation is proved to be an effective approach to suppress the recurrent seizure activities. However, this approach requires an instant detection of each seizure event within seconds to trigger the stimulation device, which poses challenges in both algorithm design and hardware implementation. We successfully developed an efficient seizure detection algorithms and their hardware implementations. The new techniques can be applied in future wearable neuromodulation devices.

14205018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205018.value: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have gained mainstream adoption in the past ten years for many artificial intelligence (AI) applications including computer vision, speech recognition and natural language processing. While being able to produce state-of-the-art results that often exceed human accuracy, the computational complexity of DNNs is extremely high. Consequently, efficient processing of DNNs with dedicated hardware accelerators has attracted lots of attention from both academia and industry and it is expected to be widely deployed in the near future, especially for DNN inference engines. Many DNN applications (e.g., biometric authentication and autonomous driving) are safety- and security-critical. In the literature, many researchers have studied the so-called adversarial example attacks, which generate malicious results by making slight perturbations to the DNNs' inputs. An interesting question is whether attackers could achieve the same goal by attacking the DNN accelerators directly without changing their inputs. To the best of our knowledge, this problem has not been studied in the literature. Motivated by the above, in this project, we plan to investigate the confidentiality and integrity issues of DNN accelerators. To be specific, for the confidentiality of DNNs, we study side-channel attacks to recover the inputs to DNNs without knowing the detailed parameters used in the neural network. In our preliminary results, we are able to achieve more than 80% accuracy for the MNIST dataset with power side channel analysis (SCA). This project will develop more advanced SCA techniques to achieve highly-accurate recovery for general inputs to DNNs. We shall also develop efficient and effective countermeasures to mitigate such attacks. For the integrity issues of DNNs, we study fault-injection attacks on DNN accelerators that result in malfunction and/or denial-of-service. In our preliminary results, we are able to achieve misclassification for targeted inputs with some impact on other input patterns. In this project, we plan to further develop more practical attacks that are be easily launched with high efficiency. We shall also design novel defense mechanisms to ensure the runtime integrity of DNN accelerators to mitigate fault-injection attacks. 深度神經網路 (DNNs) 在過去十年中得到廣泛應用, 包括電腦視覺, 語音辨識和自然語言處理等人工智慧領域。然而, 深度神經網路的計算複雜性是非常高的。因此, 用專用的硬體加速器對DNNs進行高效處理, 引起了學術界和工業界的廣泛關注,。預計在不久的將來, 它將得到大量的部署, 特別是針對DNN推理引擎的加速器。 許多 DNN應用 (例如, 生物特徵認證和自主駕駛) 要求極高的安全性和可靠性。然而，近期的研究文獻表明，通過對DNNs的輸入進行輕微的擾動可以生成所謂的對抗樣本攻擊, 產生惡意的結果。一個相關問題是，如果攻擊者無法改變輸入，他們是否可以通過直接攻擊DNN加速器來實現同樣的目標。據我們所知, 這一問題尚未有人研究。 本項目計畫針對DNN加速器做攻防研究。具體而言, 對於DNNs的保密性, 我們研究如何在不清楚神經網路的詳細參數條件下，利用側通道攻擊來恢復DNNs的輸入。初步研究結果表明對於簡單的MNIST數字資料庫，使用電源側通道分析能夠達到80% 以上的精度。本項目將進一步開發更先進的手段以實現對複雜DNNs的攻擊。此外，我們還將研究減輕這種攻擊效果的對策。針對DNNs的完整性問題, 我們研究針對DNN加速器的故障注入攻擊。初步研究結果表明, 我們能夠實現目標輸入的誤判, 並對其他輸入模式產生一定的影響。在本項目中, 我們計畫進一步開發更實際的攻擊手段。我們還將設計新的防禦機制, 以確保DNN加速器運行時的完整性, 以減輕故障注入攻擊的效果。

14205018.label: Realisation of objectives
14205018.value: We have realized the project objectives in the following aspects. We demonstrated the first power side-channel attack on an FPGA-based convolutional neural network accelerator. Its input image is successfully recovered using the power traces measured for the inferencing operation. In the attack, we first filter out the noises and distortions in the power measurement process. Then we consider two attacking scenarios for adversaries of different abilities. They can either passively eavesdrop on the power side channel, profiling the correlation between power signals and image pixels. For the two adversaries, we propose two methods respectively: background detection and power template, to recover the input image in different granularity. We demonstrate the practicality of our proposed attack on an accelerator executing classification task for hand-written digits in MNIST datasets and the experimental results show we achieve high recognition accuracy. We also investigated the impact of fault injection attacks on deep neural networks (DNNs), wherein attackers try to misclassify a specified input pattern into an adversarial class by modifying the parameters used in DNNs via fault injection. We propose two kinds of fault injection attacks to achieve this objective. Without considering stealthiness of the attack, single bias attack (SBA) only requires to modify one parameter in DNN for misclassification, based on the observation that the outputs of DNN may linearly depend on some parameters. Gradient descent attack (GDA) takes stealthiness into consideration. By controlling the amount of modification to DNN parameters, GDA is able to minimize the fault injection impact on input patterns other than the specified one. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed attacks. In terms of defense, we first proposed a fine-grained redundancy framework, named D2NN, for deep neural networks against hardware vulnerabilities including fault injection attacks and hardware faults. D2NN efficiently utilizes the external and internal redundancy of DNN models to trade-off system robustness and hardware overhead. The overhead of D2NN, however, is relatively large. To tackle this problem, we later developed a novel lightweight fault-tolerant solution for DNN-based systems, named DeepDyve, which employs pre-trained neural networks that are far simpler and smaller than the original DNN for dynamic verification. The key to enabling such lightweight checking is that the smaller neural network only needs to produce approximate results for the initial task without sacrificing fault coverage much. We also developed efficient and effective architecture and task exploration techniques to achieve optimized risk/overhead trade-off in DeepDyve. Experimental results show that DeepDyve can reduce 90% of the risks at around 10% overhead. Moreover, we also proposed a novel edge/cloud collaborative architecture that can be used to defend against attacks on edge AI models.

14205018.value: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have gained mainstream adoption in the past ten years in various artificial intelligence (AI) applications, many of which (e.g., biometric authentication and autonomous driving) are safety- and security-critical. In this project, we investigate the confidentiality and integrity issues of DNN accelerators. To be specific, for the confidentiality of DNNs, we study side-channel attacks to recover the inputs to DNNs without knowing the detailed parameters used in the neural network. As shown in our results, we are able to achieve more than 80% accuracy for some AI datasets with power side-channel analysis (SCA). For the integrity issues of DNNs, we study fault-injection attacks on DNN accelerators that result in malfunction and/or denial of service. In our results, we are able to achieve misclassification by injecting very few faults. To tackle the above security issues, we develop several defense mechanisms that can effectively mitigate these threats.

14205318.label: Realisation of objectives
14205318.value: Secondary organic aerosol (SOA), generated from oxidation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by ozone (O3), hydroxyl radical (OH), or nitrate radical (NO3), is an important source of particulate matter (PM) globally. Although about 70% of the total global organic aerosol (OA) production is due to secondary sources, the toxicological implications of SOA are not yet fully understood. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the relative toxicity of particles generated from NO3 or OH-initiated oxidation of VOCs. The aim of this study was to investigate the oxidative potential and inflammatory responses of particles generated from NO3 or OH-initiated oxidation of biogenic and anthropogenic VOC precursors by identifying the components responsible for PM toxicity on a cellular level. SOA precursors, including isoprene, α-pinene, toluene, and m-xylene, representing major classes of biogenic and anthropogenic VOCs known to produce SOA under atmospheric oxidation, were selected. Photooxidation experiments were carried out in a Potential Aerosol Mass (PAM) oxidation flow reactor (OFR) and an experimental smog chamber for OH- and NO3-initiated oxidation, respectively. Moreover, vehicle exhaust was oxidized in PAM reactor also. In the PAM study, the reactor is 45.7 cm long with an inner diameter of 19.7 cm and has a volume of around 13 L. A UV lamp is mounted inside the reactor, providing UV radiation at 254 nm only. The main oxidant (OH radical) in the PAM reactor is generated by the reaction between water vapor and excited oxygen [O(1D)] atom (which is produced by the irradiation of O3 with UV light inside the reactor). The relative humidity (RH) and temperature of the outflow of the PAM OFR were monitored by a temperature/humidity sensor. The VOC precursors used in the current study were prepared in the gas phase and were directly injected into the PAM OFR. In experiments using seed particles, ammonium sulfate powder (~99%, Missouri Sigma-Aldrich, Inc., St. Louis, MO, USA) was dissolved in milli-Q water and then atomized by an atomizer (3076, TSI, Shoreview, MN, USA). Particle number and mass concentration at the outlet of the PAM OFR were monitored by a scanning mobility particle sizer (SMPS). SOA generated was collected for offline chemical and toxicological analysis on quartz and Teflon filters, respectively, with an ozone denuder installed before the filter to prevent prolonged oxidation of SOA samples on the filter by O3 In the chamber study, the simulation of VOC oxidation was conducted in a smog chamber made of Teflon film under atmospheric pressure. Zero air produced from a zero-air generator (Model 111, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.) was used as bath gas. Before each experiment, the smog chamber was flushed with zero air until all pollutants in the chamber were below the detection limit of instruments. The temperature in the chamber was controlled and stable at ~ 300 ± 5 K, and the relative humidity (RH) in the smog chamber was manually adjusted to ~20-30% in the experiments by adjusting the ratio of dry zero air and humid air produced from a water bubbler. NO2 was added to the chamber with variable volumes to simulate different oxidation conditions. O3 generated by an ozone generator (Model NO 2001, Jellght Company Inc.) was introduced into the smog chamber. After NO2 and O3 mixed for about 15 min, a certain volume of VOC was injected into a three-way tube into the chamber. The generated aerosols in the chamber were monitored by a SMPS. The particles formed in the chamber were collected on Teflon filters under an air flow rate of 1.0 L/min for toxicological analysis, and their chemical compositions were determined with a high-resolution time-of-flight aerosol mass spectrometer (HR-ToF-AMS, Aerodyne Research, USA). The weight of each SOA sample collected on a pre-weighed filter was determined gravimetrically using a microbalance (Sartorius, Germany; with a readability of 0.001 mg). Organic compounds detected in the filter samples were directly analyzed using a solvent extraction-gas chromatography/electron ionization-mass spectrometry (GC/EI-MS) system. The quartz filter sample was cut and extracted with dichloromethane and methanol (2:1, v/v) under ultrasonication. The extracts were concentrated using a rotary evaporator under vacuum conditions and then dried with pure nitrogen gas. The dried extract was reacted with N,O-bis-(trimethylsilyl) trifluoroacetamide (BSTFA) at 70°C for 3 hours, and the resulting derivatives were determined using GC/EI-MS. For chamber study with the HR-ToF-AMS, the sample gas passed through a Nafion drying tube and reduced the RH below 20%. Then, particles with an aerodynamic equivalent diameter below 1 µm were focused into a narrow beam by an aerodynamic lens at the injection port. The particles were ionized by electron collision (70 eV) after being impacted on a flash vaporizer (600°C) and converted into vapors. The positively charged ions were separated in the ToF section and then detected by a quadrupole mass spectrometer with scans across m/z 1 to 300. V-mode (m/Δm ~ 2000), which has a higher signal-to-noise ratio, was used in the AMS ToF section. For mass concentration calculations, 1.4 was used for the default relative ionization efficiency (RIE) values for organic compounds. The chemical composition data from AMS was analyzed through SQUIRREL 1.63B coupled with PIKA 1.23B in the Igor Pro (WaveMetrics, Inc., Portland, Oregon). Note that the elemental ratios (i.e., O/C, H/C, N/C) were calculated using the Aiken-Ambient method for comparison with previous studies. Toxicological analysis was carried out using human lung epithelial cells (A549) to assess the oxidative potential and inflammatory response of particles generated from NO3- or OH-initiated oxidation of the SOA precursors. The cells were exposed to various concentrations of the collected particles, and cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, as well as pro-inflammatory cytokine (lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and interleukin-6 (IL-6)) release were measured. A sulforhodamine B (SRB) colorimetric assay was used to assess cell viability. In brief, cells were stained with 10% (wt/vol) trichloroacetic acid, followed by incubation with a 10 mM Tris base solution. Optical density (OD) at 510 nm was measured using a microplate reader (Bio-Rad Model 680, CA, US). Cell viability (%) was calculated after adjusting for the control. For the determination of ROS production, the cells were exposed to 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (DCFH-DA). The reaction between cell-bound ROS and DCFH-DA produces the highly fluorescent 2',7'-dichlorofluorescin (DCFH). The fluorescent intensity served as a surrogate for ROS concentration and was measured using a Light Luminescence Plate Reader (VICTOR X, Waltham, MA, USA). The supernatants of the cell culture were used to determine the lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) released by the cells. The concentrations of LDH and IL-6 were determined using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit (BD Biosciences, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Inflammatory and oxidative responses were found after PM exposure, and the crucial organic compounds for the cell responses were also identified. Spearman’s rank correlation was used for the correlation analysis, while the Kruskal-Wallis H test was employed to identify significant differences among datasets. The proposed targets have been achieved, albeit with some delays caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, certain outcomes have been published in peer-reviewed journals. More results are anticipated and expected for further article submissions in due course.

14205318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205318.value: The results showed that particle mass concentration increases with increasing OH or NO3 exposure in most experiments, indicating the formation of SOA under high OH or NO3 exposure conditions. Off-line chemical analysis of the SOA sample generated by OH-initiated oxidation in PAM revealed the dominance of highly oxidized products. The well-known toluene, m-xylene and isoprene SOA markers were also detected in SOA sample. Our results showed good agreement with the results of previous smog chamber studies. It was found that the SOA mass concentration formed decreased when NOx concentration increased during the oxidation of toluene and α-pinene in the chamber study. The reaction between NO and RO2, which produces higher volatility products, can suppress SOA formation in high NOx conditions. HR-ToF-AMS results showed that the m/z 43 was dominated by ion C2H3O+, moreover, organic nitrates formed by photooxidation in this study were highly oxidized organic molecules containing multifunctional groups (CHON and CHOxN family). The toxicity results revealed that all SOA generated had higher bioreactivities than the control, indicating that they caused a certain degree of oxidative stress to the human body and could potentially trigger proinflammatory responses. For SOA generated by OH-oxidation of isoprene, an approximate 10% decrease in cell viability was observed. By contrast, the SOA from OH-oxidation of toluene and m-xylene retained high cell viability under the same dosage. These findings suggest that the isoprene-derived SOA can lead to decreased cell viability. In most cases, ROS, IL-6, and LDH levels measured from isoprene-derived and toluene-derived SOA were significantly higher than those from m-xylene-derived SOA. It was found that toluene and α-pinene SOA formed under high NOx oxidation conditions have lower cell viability and higher LDH than those formed under no or low-NOx conditions which matched with our vehicle exhaust experiments under high NOx conditions. However, ROS and IL-6 levels were similar regardless of NOx concentration. Strong correlations were identified between methylglycerol and tartaric acid with cell viability and LDH levels, as well as between m-toluic acid, oxalic acid and succinic acid with IL-6 levels in SOA samples from OH-oxidation. Results suggested that CHON and CHOxN family are the major contributors to the increase in LDH, IL-6, and ROS levels in NO3-oxidation samples. This study demonstrated that SOA samples derived from VOC oxidation play a critical role in PM-induced oxidative stress and inflammation.

14205318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205318.value: The current study focused on the chemical and toxicological characterization of biogenic and anthropogenic VOCs derived SOA and their corresponding toxicity. The cytotoxicity caused by SOA was investigated and compared. In the future, VOC emissions from different non-vehicular sources (e.g., volatile chemical products (VCPs) such as paints, consumer products, adhesives, sealants, and other solvents) and their secondary organic aerosol formation mechanisms by photo-oxidation reactions can be further studied. Moreover, it is important to compare the health effects triggered by VCPs and their associated SOA. In this study, only part of the organic components were identified, and many organic fractions of aerosol were not resolved in detail. Therefore, the detailed chemical compositions of aged aerosol from different VCPs can be investigated and compared. The results are important for further air pollution control (e.g. ozone control) strategies in Hong Kong. Additionally, human health effects could be studied based on the current results, such as cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases. When SOA is inhaled by humans, there will be a series of body reactions triggered and spread throughout the whole body, which can ultimately lead to different diseases. This is also important for further studies on PM health research.

14205318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205318.value: This study aimed to investigate the components responsible for SOA toxicity on a cellular level by comparing the toxicity of particles generated from NO3- and OH-initiated oxidation of VOCs. SOA is a major contributor to particulate matter globally, but its toxicological implications are not yet fully understood. To simulate the atmospheric conditions under which SOA is generated, the study employed a Potential Aerosol Mass (PAM) oxidation flow reactor and an experimental smog chamber. The particles produced in the experiments were then collected and analyzed to identify the components responsible for their toxicity on a cellular level. The results showed that particles generated from both NO3- and OH-initiated oxidation of the SOA precursors were able to induce ROS production and pro-inflammatory cytokine release in the A549 cells. However, the magnitude of the response varied depending on the precursor used and the type of oxidation. The study is important because SOA is a significant contributor to air pollution and can have negative impacts on human health. By understanding the toxicity of particles generated from different types of VOCs, policymakers can take steps to reduce the amount of harmful pollutants in the atmosphere and improve public health.

14205618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205618.value: Networked data are ubiquitous in different application domains, for example, social networks, biological networks, and so on. In many scenarios, multiple networks in a certain domain may relate to each other. For example, when users of one social networking service use their accounts to sign into another social networking service instead of creating a new login account specifically for the latter (a feature known as “social login”), such users are common between the two social networks. The one-to-one correspondence of common users between two networks is called cross-network node correspondence. For another example, consider the English Wikipedia and Chinese Wikipedia, which are two language editions of the free online encyclopedia Wikipedia. A Chinese wiki page may contain a hyperlink to an English wiki page. Such cross-language hyperlinks widely exist among different Wikipedia language editions and may create barriers for readers who cannot understand the two languages involved. If each language edition of Wikipedia is viewed as a network, the link that involves a Chinese wiki page depending on an English wiki page is called cross-network link dependence. In this project, we propose to study the relation across multiple information networks. Specifically, we investigate two problems: (1) cross-network node correspondence inference, and (2) cross-network link dependence minimization. Cross-network node correspondence is very useful for various downstream applications such as network alignment, link prediction, community detection and transfer learning. Cross-network link dependence, on the other hand, may cause undesirable effects due to the coupling of the networks, thus should be eliminated as much as possible. We propose to take a deep graph learning approach to solve the above two problems. Theoretically, the deep learning approach is an efficient architecture to infer complex non-linear structures. The underlying structures in networks, such as cliques, trusses and graphlets, are very complex and highly non-linear due to the coordinate-free relation among vertices. The deep learning approach is very suitable for capturing the complex structures in graphs. Practically, many deep learning frameworks, such as TensorFlow, Caffe and MXNet have been developed, which provide a comprehensive solution to querying, maintaining and processing large volume of data. With these existing frameworks as a basis, we aim to design a unified, special-purpose deep graph learning platform to model and infer the relation across multiple information networks. The success of this project will facilitate the management and analysis of multiple inter-related information networks, and make impact in both research and industrial communities.

14205618.label: Realisation of objectives
14205618.value: All project objectives have been achieved satisfactorily with research results appearing in top-tier journal and conference paper publications. The realisation of each objective is described below. 1. We developed a deep graph learning solution to model and infer the relation across multiple information networks. The framework consists of learning graph embedding and inferring node correspondence by leveraging both the topological structure and node features. In particular, we considered different types of relations between multiple information networks, e.g., interconnection, temporal relation, and designed corresponding solutions. 2. We designed a network representation learning framework to incorporate both the topological information and side information of information networks into a unified representation, and then take a minimization approach for inferring the cross-network node correspondence. In our WWW'19 paper, we used a hierarchical graph to model multiple information networks and their relation. To learn the representation of the hierarchical graph, we proposed a novel supervised, self-attentive graph embedding method called SAGE, which embeds graph instances of arbitrary size into fixed-length vectors. In our KDD'19 paper, we considered multiple information networks that have a temporal dependency, and designed a relational GCN and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to model the temporal dependency between them. In our Information Sciences paper, we built a node-feature bipartite graph and exploited the bipartite graph convolutional network to model node-feature relations. By aligning results from the original graph structure and node-feature relations, we can make a more accurate prediction for each node in an end-to-end manner. 3. We designed efficient algorithms and side information encoding strategies for minimizing the cross-network link dependence. In our SIGMOD'21 paper, we studied graph isomorphism as it is useful for aligning two information networks and inferring cross-network correspondence. To test two graphs for isomorphism, canonical labeling has been studied to relabel a graph in such a way that isomorphic graphs are identical after relabeling. We designed a new efficient canonical labeling algorithm DviCL based on the observation that we can use the k-th minimum permutation as the canonical labeling. Different from previous algorithms, we take a divide-and-conquer approach to partition a graph and construct an AutoTree, which preserves symmetric structures as well as the automorphism group of the graph. The canonical labeling for a tree node can be obtained by composing those of its child nodes, and the canonical labeling for the root is the one for the graph. In addition, we studied how to recover a graph structure (i.e., one information network) that removes irrelevant edges and adds missing edges by referring to its counterpart (i.e., another information network). As in practice noisy-clean graph pairs are rare, we proposed to de-noise the input noisy graph without any supervision from its clean counterpart, which is referred to as blind graph denoising. Our method, called Mask-GVAE, makes use of the robustness in low eigenvectors of graph Laplacian against random noise and decomposes the input graph into several stable clusters. It then harnesses the huge computations by decoding probabilistic smoothed subgraphs in a variational manner. This was published in WWW'21.

14205618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205618.value: The research outcome is as follows. Overall, there are 4 journal papers and 10 conference papers published from the research investigations in this project. 2 PhD students were trained during the project duration. The major findings are, given complex information networks from real applications, how to learn graph representation to incorporate both the topological information and side information of information networks into a unified representation. We used a hierarchical graph representation to capture both the topology of the information networks and the interconnection between them. A supervised, self-attentive graph embedding method is designed for the hierarchical graph model (in WWW'19). We also designed a relational GCN with LSTM to model the temporal dependency between multiple information networks (in KDD'19). In order to unify both the topological structure and node features, we built a node-feature bipartite graph and used the bipartite graph convolutional network to model node-feature relations (in Information Sciences'23). To efficiently infer the node correspondence between information networks, we designed a new efficient canonical labeling algorithm DviCLusing a divide-and-conquer approach. This can enable efficient and robust graph isomorphism test (in SIGMOD'21). We also studied how to de-noise information networks by removing irrelevant edges and adding missing edges by referring to its counterpart and proposed the first variational generative model for blind denoising large graphs (in WWW'21). We also studied the application of our proposed methodology to downstream tasks, such as community search (in PVLDB'22) and adversarial attack on community detection (in WWW'20), and demonstrated the superiority of our methods.

14205618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205618.value: We believe there will be more opportunities and challenges arising from this topic, thus there is a lot of potential for further investigation and development in this direction. On one hand, we may use different graph models, for example, use hypergraph as a more expressive model to represent the information networks and study the graph representation learning problem using hypergraphs. On the other hand, we may seek more real-world problems, e.g., network alignment, data integration and imputation, community detection, to which our proposed algorithms can be applied.

14205618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205618.value: In this project, we studied the relationship between multiple information networks (e.g., node to node correspondence) and how to minimize the cross-network dependence. We designed graph matching algorithms to compute node to node correspondence, and we designed machine learning methods for representing a graph by encoding both its topology and attributes. Theoretically, this research advances our understanding of large-scale information networks, how to represent them and how to infer their relationship. Practically, our designed algorithms can be applied to real-world social networks, communication networks, biological networks for alignment, matching and link prediction.

14205718.label: Project Objectives
14205718.value: We plan to propose a dynamic version of the first-loss scheme that includes current practices in the hedge fund industry, such as those in Topwater Capital, as special cases. We plan to consider both a discrete-time setting and a continuous-time setting. We plan to propose a new decision model that generalizes stochastic differential utility by allowing for infinite elasticity of intertemporal substitution. This new model is used to represent fund managers’ preferences for continuous-time cash flow streams. We plan to use tools from stochastic control, such as dynamic programming, from differential equations, such as the theory of viscosity solutions, and from functional analysis, such as the contraction mapping theorem, to solve the manager’s decision problem in our model. We plan to study the impact of two contract components in the first-loss scheme, namely the incentive rate and the liquidation boundary, on managers’ risk taking behavior. We plan to compare the first-loss scheme to the high-water mark scheme in terms of the manager’s risk-taking behavior, the manager’s utility, and the investors’ utility.

14205718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205718.value: In the U.S., the manager of a hedge fund typically takes a portion, named incentive rate, of the fund investors’ profits as a performance fee, but does not share the investors’ losses. The manager can also put her stakes in the fund and takes any gain and loss induced by her stakes. Many US hedge funds also have a high-water mark provision: fund managers are entitled to a performance fee only when the investors’ stakes exceed a high-water mark value that is equal to the historical high of the net value of the investors’ stakes, and the performance fee is calculated as the difference in these two values multiplied by the incentive rate. A scheme known as the first-loss scheme has recently become popular in China and is also emerging in the U.S. For instance, Topwater Capital, an asset management company, has been using first-loss managed accounts since 2002. In this scheme, fund managers typically put up 10% of the fund capital from their own money as a “first-loss” deposit. Any fund losses, even those induced by the investors’ stakes, will be covered by this deposit before investors take a hit. As compensation for covering losses first, the incentive rate for the manager can be higher, such as 40%. In a recent work by the principal investigator, the authors study profit sharing between fund managers and investors in the first-loss scheme for the first time in the literature. They, however, essentially assume that fund managers take performance fees at one time only, whereas in practice fund managers take performance fees at multiple times, such as annually. In this project, we propose a dynamic version of the first-loss scheme in which the first-loss deposit is managed dynamically and the manager is paid performance fees at a predetermined set of dates, and this model includes the current practices in Topwater Capital as a special case. By using tools from decision analysis and stochastic control, we plan to study the connection between risk taking and performance fees in the first-loss scheme, such as whether an increase in the incentive rate induces the manager to take on more risk. We also plan to compare the first-loss scheme and the high-water mark scheme in terms of the manager’s risk-taking behavior, the manager’s utility, and the investors’ utility. 在美國，通常一個對沖基金的經理可以收取基金投資者收益的一個百分比作為提成，這個百分比稱為提成率。然而該經理卻不會承擔投資者的任何損失。基金經理也可以將自己的一部分錢投入他管理的基金。對於這部分投資，他自負盈虧。許多美國的對沖基金會採用高水位線條款。在該條款下，基金經理只能在所管理的投資者資產的淨值超過其歷史最高點的時候才能收取提成。提成的計算通常為投資者資產淨值超過歷史最高點的那部分乘以提成率。 第一損失機制是一個在中國私募基金常用的基金經理提成的辦法，最近在美國也日漸流行。例如一家名為Topwater Capital的美國資產管理公司從2002年起就開始使用第一損失機制來管理其名下的資產管理賬戶。在該機制下，基金經理通常配資10%作為第一損失資本。所有投資賬戶的損失，包括投資者資本產生的損失，都會由第一損失資本承擔。只有當該資本全部被消耗的時候，投資者才會承擔損失。因為基金經理先於投資者承擔損失，通常他們會收取一個比較高的提成率，譬如40%。 項目主要研究人的一個近期工作首次研究了在第一損失機制下的基金經理和投資者之間的收益分配問題。然而在該研究中，研究人員假設基金經理只收取一次提成。在實際中，基金經理會收取多次提成，譬如在每年年底基於當年的基金收益情況收取提成。 在這個項目中，我們提出一個動態的第一損失機制。在該機制下，第一損失資本需要動態的調整，而且基金經理可以在給定的多個時間點，譬如每年年底，收取提成。Topwater Capital現在使用的基金賬戶管理機制是我們提出的動態第一損失機制的一個特例。通過應用決策分析以及隨機控制中的一些工具，我們計劃研究在該機制下基金經理與投資者之間的風險分擔和基金經理提成之間的聯繫。特別的，我們計劃研究是否更高的提成會導致基金經理選擇風險更大的投資策略。我們還計劃比較動態第一損失機制和傳統的高水位線條款。

14205718.label: Realisation of objectives
14205718.value: The PI has realised Objective 1 as follows: First, the PI studied Topwater Capital as a case study in Research Output 8 Item 1. This study shows the popularity of the first-loss scheme in the market and the effectiveness of the dynamic version of the first-loss scheme in attracting skilled managers to the market. Second, the PI has trained a PhD student for this proposal. The PI and the student have proposed a dynamic version of the first-loss scheme both in the discrete-time setting and in the continuous-time setting. The PhD student is expected to submit his thesis in August 2023; see Research Output 13. The PI has realised Objective 2. More precisely, the PI and the PhD student have proposed a preference model in which the agent’s utility of a consumption stream is represented by a backward stochastic differential equation. This model can be regarded as stochastic differential utility by allowing for infinite elasticity of intertemporal substitution. The result is included in the PhD student’s thesis, which is to be submitted in Aug 2023; see Research Output 13. The PI has realised Objective 3. More precisely, the PI and the PhD student have established the well-posedness and proved the dynamic programming principle for the hedge fund management problem under the first-loss scheme in the discrete-time setting. The PI and the PhD student have also developed numerical algorithm to solve the HJB equation to derive the manager’s optimal decision. The results are included in the PhD student’s thesis, which is to be submitted in Aug 2023; see Research Output 13. The PI has realized Objectives 4 and 5. The PI has studied the effectiveness of the first-loss scheme in screening out hedge fund managers that are not appealing to fund investors. More precisely, the PI considered a model in which there are multiple managers with various skill levels and different risk appetite. The fund investors do not know the managers’ risk levels or risk appetite, so asymmetric information arises. The PI showed that traditional incentive schemes for hedge fund management, such as the high-water mark provision, cannot screen out all managers who are unappealing to the investors while attracting at least some managers who are attractive to the managers. The first-loss scheme, together with a liquidation boundary, can achieve the screening. The above results also show that the first-loss scheme is better than the high-water mark provision in terms of addressing the issue of asymmetric information in the hedge fund industry. These results lead to Research Output 8 Item 1. The PI has also completed another three publications that are by-products of the proposed project. In Research Output 8 Item 2, the PI and his coauthors studied a contract design problem, which is similar to the contract design problem for hedge funds proposed in the project but is applied to security underwriting. In Research Output 8 Item 3, the PI and his coauthors study a portfolio selection problem with reference-dependent utility. The managerial payoffs of both the first-loss scheme and the high-water mark scheme can be regarded as payoffs relative to certain reference points. Thus, the study of hedge fund management in the proposed project motivated us to consider portfolio selection problems with a general reference-dependent utility model. The results have been published in a top journal. In Research Output 9 Item 2, we published a conference paper, which is to study reinforcement learning of risk-sensitive control. This study is motivated by the proposed project, where we need to develop numerical algorithms to solve a stochastic control problem faced by fund managers.

14205718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205718.value: First, the PI studied the effectiveness of the first-loss scheme in screening out hedge fund managers that are not appealing to fund investors. More precisely, the PI considered a model in which there are multiple managers with various skill levels and different risk appetite. The fund investors do not know the managers’ risk levels or risk appetite, so asymmetric information arises. The PI showed that traditional incentive schemes for hedge fund management, such as the high-water mark provision, cannot screen out all managers who are unappealing to the investors while attracting at least some managers who are attractive to the managers. The first-loss scheme, together with a liquidation boundary, can achieve the screening. The above results also show that the first-loss scheme is better than the high-water mark provision in terms of addressing the issue of asymmetric information in the hedge fund industry. These findings lead to a paper, which is currently under major revision in a top journal. For details, see Research Output 8 Item 1. Second, in the study of contract design for security underwriting, which is closely related to contract design in hedge funds, the PI found that a firm-commitment contract is optimal if and only if the issuing company is more pessimistic than the underwriter. This finding leads to a paper published in Insurance: Mathematics and Economics, a top journal in the area of insurance; see Research Output 8 Item 2. Third, the PI studied portfolio selection under reference-dependent preferences, which can be regarded as a generalisation of the hedge fund management problem under the first-loss and high-watermark schemes. The PI found that agents become less averse to losses if they endogenize their reference points. This finding leads to a publication in Operations Research, a top journal in the field of operations research and management science; see Research Output 8 Item 3. Fourth, the PI found that with the same incentive rate, the first-loss scheme leads to less risk taking by the fund manager than the high-water mark scheme does. This finding, together with many others, are included in the PhD thesis supervised by the PI that is to be submitted in Aug 2023; Research Output 13. A related finding is a regret bound on reinforcement learning of risk-sensitive control arising from the manager’s control problem. This finding leads to a publication in ICML, a top conference; see Research Output 9 Item 2.

14205718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205718.value: In the first-loss scheme, the manager shares the investor’s loss, in contrast to the traditional scheme in which the loss is not shared. In the proposed project, the PI has showed that the first-loss scheme is able to reduce risk taking and to solve the issue of asymmetric information in the hedge fund industry. Note that the first-loss scheme is a specific contract that features loss sharing. A natural research problem is to study other types of contracts that have loss sharing. In particular, it would be interesting to find optimal contracts under certain criteria.

14205718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205718.value: Hedge funds are popular investment options in the market. Traditionally, hedge fund managers tend to take excessive risk because they do not share investors’ losses. A natural question is whether having a feature of loss sharing in managerial contracts can alleviate the issue of excessive risk taking. In this project, the PI considered a specific contract, known as first-loss contract, that is emerging in the market. In this contract, the manager of a fund covers the fund’s investors losses using her stake in the fund. The PI found that the first-loss scheme indeed leads to less risk taking by the manager than traditional schemes, such as the high-water-mark scheme, do. This finding shows the importance of having loss sharing in hedge fund managerial incentive design.

14206318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206318.value: This proposal aims to experimentally investigate bound states in the continuum (BICs) in integrated photonics and develop BIC-based photonic devices for applications in photonic integrated circuits. A bound state in the continuum is a wave that remains localized even though its frequency lies inside the continuous spectrum of extended radiating waves that can carry energy away. The concept of BIC was first proposed by von Neumann and Wigner in quantum mechanics in 1929. Recently, it has been realized that BICs are intrinsically a wave phenomenon and not restricted to the realm of quantum mechanics. They have many interesting physical properties and have been studied in many material systems such as piezoelectric materials, dielectric photonic crystals, optical waveguides and fibers, quantum dots, graphene, and topological insulators. The fundamental research on BICs has also led to many applications, for example, lasers, sensors, and filters. On the other hand, the area of integrated photonics has witnessed rapid development in incorporating new optical functional materials, such as silicon carbide, lithium niobate, and diamond, which have opened new avenues for integrated photonics applications due to their unique material properties. However, those functional materials usually have very stable physical and chemical properties, and thus it is challenging to etch them and fabricate devices of high quality, which has largely limited their applications in integrated photonics. To overcome this difficulty, we propose to experimentally investigate the BICs in integrated photonics and develop a new type of photonic integrated circuits which operate under the principle of BICs. By carefully designing the pattern geometry of a low-index material silicon dioxide above a thin-film functional material, we can obtain a confined optical mode (i.e., the BIC mode) in the functional material without etching it. Since the pattern definition and etching process of silicon dioxide are CMOS compatible and very mature, the fabrication of such photonic structures is expected to reach the highest quality. This proposal has far-reaching significance to both fundamental physics and practical applications. Fundamentally, the idea of BICs will be explored in a new area with new material systems. The experimental results will be used to test, verify, and enrich the BIC theories. Technology-wise, harnessing BICs in photonic integrated circuits will overcome the difficulty in etching of some functional materials for photonic integration and thus may provide a new paradigm of functional photonic integrated circuits for applications in high-power photonics, nonlinear optics, and quantum photonics. 本項目旨在實驗研究集成光子學裏連續區束縛態（BIC），並開發用於光子集成回路的基於BIC的光子器件。 連續區束縛態是一種波，即使其頻率位於可以帶走能量的延展輻射波的連續譜內也會保持局域化。BIC的概念最初由von Neumann和Wigner於1929年在量子力學裏提出。最近，人們已經認識到BIC本質上是一種波動現象，且並不局限於量子力學領域。它們具有許多有趣的物理性質，並且在許多材料體系裏已被研究，例如壓電材料、介電光子晶體、光波導和光纖、量子點、石墨烯和拓撲絕緣體。對BIC的基礎研究也導致了許多應用，例如激光、傳感器和濾波器。另一方面，集成光子學領域在結合新的光學功能材料（例如碳化矽、鈮酸鋰和金剛石）方面取得了快速發展。由於其獨特的材料特性，這些材料為集成光子學應用開闢了新的途徑。然而，這些功能材料通常具有非常穩定的物理和化學性質，因此蝕刻它們並製造高品質的器件頗具挑戰性，這在很大程度上限制了它們在集成光子學裏的應用。 為克服這一困難，我們提議實驗研究集成光子學裏的BIC，並開發一種在BIC原理下工作的新型光子集成回路。通過仔細設計功能材料薄膜上的低折射率材料二氧化矽的圖案幾何形狀，我們無需蝕刻功能材料就可以在其中獲得局域的光學模式（即BIC模式）。由於二氧化矽的圖案定型和蝕刻工藝是CMOS兼容的且非常成熟，因此制備這種光子結構可以達到最高品質。 本項目對基礎物理和實際應用都具有深遠的意義。從根本上說，BIC的概念將會在一個新領域利用新的材料體系進行探索。實驗結果將用於測試、驗證和豐富BIC的理論。在技術方面，利用光子集成回路裏的BIC將克服蝕刻某些光子集成功能材料的困難，因此可以為高功率光子學、非線性光學和量子光子學的應用提供功能光子集成回路的新範例。

14206318.label: Realisation of objectives
14206318.value: 1. (Objective 1) To design a BIC mode in a photonic structure on the integrated photonics platform and simulate the modal performance. We have fully achieved this objective by designing a fundamentally new architecture supporting BICs on integrated photonics platform at both telecom and near-visible wavelengths. (1) We experimentally demonstrated BICs in a fundamentally new photonic architecture by patterning a low-refractive-index material on a high-refractive-index substrate, where dissipation to the substrate continuum is eliminated by engineering the geometric parameters [J1, J5, C1, C8]. By utilizing the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and finite-element method (FEM), we simulated the propagation loss of the BIC mode in both straight and bent waveguides, and the Q factor in both microdisk and microring cavities. The simulation results show that the BIC mode can achieve zero propagation loss and infinite Q factor at certain geometric parameters. This platform breaks through the fundamental limitation of photonic architectures, allowing the exploration of high-refractive-index dielectric materials on an integrated platform without the need for patterning micro- or nanostructures in these materials. (2) We have also designed BIC modes of different orders by engineering the structure parameters [J4, C4], which was further used for demonstrating mode (de)multiplexing and high-dimensional communication with an insertion loss <4.0 dB and a crosstalk <−9.5 dB in a 70-nm wavelength band. 2. (Objective 2) To fabricate and measure the photonic structure to characterize the behavior of the BIC mode. We have fully achieved this objective by developing a standard laboratory fabrication process for fabricating the BIC-based integrated photonic circuits and a basic experimental setup for characterizing the behavior of the BIC mode. (1) We have fabricated the basic elements of integrated photonic circuits on a lithium niobate-on-insulator (LNOI) platform. A thin film of e-beam resist (ZEP520A) was adopted as the upper low-refractive-index material and was patterned with only one step of e-beam lithography to create the optical structures, including waveguides and microcavities [J1]. Waveguides with different widths and microcavities with different bend radii were fabricated on the same chip for characterization of the BIC mode. (2) We have measured the propagation loss of waveguides and Q factors of microcavities. The photonic devices were characterized by coupling light from an optical fiber into and out of the devices via polarization-sensitive grating couplers and measuring the transmission spectra. The experimental results show that the propagation loss of waveguides varies periodically with waveguide width and achieves minima at certain geometric parameters, and the Q factor of microcavities varies periodically with bend radius and achieves maxima at certain geometric parameters [J1, J5]. (3) We have also exploited dissipative coupling between photonic waveguides on the BIC-based integrated platform, and for the first time, experimentally observed supermode BICs on a chip. We verified the dissipative nature of coupling between the photonic waveguides by demonstrating the complementarily varied loss rates of the two supermodes. [J10] 3. (Objective 3) To develop basic optical components for a BIC-based photonic integrated circuit. We have fully achieved this objective by developing a BIC-based photonic integrated circuit with basic components such as waveguides, microcavities, grating couplers, directional couplers, power splitters, and Mach–Zehnder interferometers. (1) We have demonstrated ultralow-loss guidance of light on the BIC-based photonic integrated circuit. We measured a minimal propagation loss of 2.0 dB/cm from waveguides and a maximal intrinsic Q factor of 1.1 × 106 from microcavities operating at the wavelength of 773 nm [J5], and a minimal propagation loss of 1.8 dB/cm from waveguides and a maximal intrinsic Q factor of 5.8 × 105 from microcavities operating at the wavelength of 1550 nm [J1]. (2) We have demonstrated a directional coupler where light can efficiently be delivered from one port to another in the wavelength range of 1450–1600 nm. We have also demonstrated an MZI constructed from two 3-dB power splitters. The length difference between the two arms of the MZI leads to the beating pattern in the spectrum, where the large extinction ratio indicates that the 3-dB power splitters in the MZI can divide optical power evenly. [J1] 4. (Objective 4) To develop a BIC-based hybrid-integrated photonic device with unique functionality pertaining to an optical functional material. We have fully achieved this objective by investigating the excellent nonlinear properties of lithium niobate and integrating the BIC-based platform with 2D materials to demonstrate various applications. (1) We have introduced a practical scheme for integrating 2D materials with BIC-based platforms, which can maintain large optical overlap with the 2D material by harnessing BICs. By the hybrid integration with graphene, we have demonstrated thermos-optic switches and filters, ultrafast photodetectors with 40-GHz detection bandwidth, and ultrafast electro-optic modulators with 5-GHz modulation bandwidth [J2, C3, C5]. By the hybrid integration with monolayer WS2, we have demonstrated the coupling of photon emitters in monolayer WS2 with a BIC waveguide with simulated coupling efficiency of 10.9 % and 2.3% for out-of-plane-oriented and in-plane-oriented dipole, respectively [J9]. (2) We have demonstrated acousto-optic modulation of the photonic BIC modes in high-quality integrated lithium niobate microcavities by using piezoelectrically actuated surface acoustic waves. The modulation frequency can be designed by choosing an appropriate finger period of the interdigital transducer (IDT). Modulation frequency up to 4 GHz was obtained with an IDT finger period of 3.7 µm at telecom wavelengths [J3, C2]. Modulation frequency up to 2.44 GHz was obtained with an IDT finger period of 3 µm at near-visible wavelengths [J6, C6]. Based on the strong acousto-optic modulation, we further demonstrated high-performance surface acoustic microwave photonic filters, which consist of a high-quality multitap photonic microcavity and an IDT. We have achieved acoustic time delays of 21–106 ns and passbands with bandwidth as narrow as 0.89 MHz [C9]. (3) We have demonstrated a four-channel TM mode (de)multiplexer by cascading multimode directional couplers on the BIC-based platform. The measured insertion loss of the TM0, TM1, TM2, and TM3 mode channels is <1.7, 3.4, 4.0, and 3.3 dB, respectively, the crosstalk is <−9.5 dB in the wavelength range of 1.51–1.58 μm. We also performed high-dimensional data transmission through the four-channel TM mode (de)multiplexer at 40 Gbps/channel and observed error-free eye diagrams for all the channels [J4, C4]. (4) We have demonstrated second-harmonic generation from telecom to near-visible wavelengths on the BIC-based platform. The devices feature second-harmonic conversion efficiency of 0.175% W−1 cm−2 and excellent thermal stability with a wavelength shift of only 1.7 nm from 25 to 100°C [J7, C7].

14206318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206318.value: The research outcome in the science aspect is shown as follows: (1) We designed BIC modes in a fundamentally new architecture by patterning a low-refractive-index material on a high-refractive-index substrate. This architecture avoids the etching of single-crystal material and allows ultralow-loss guiding of light at both telecom and near-visible wavelengths, which facilitates development of functional photonic integrated circuits [J1, J5, C1, C8]. (2) We demonstrated GHz acousto-optic modulation of the low-loss BIC modes in integrated lithium niobate microcavities by using piezoelectrically actuated surface acoustic waves. The structure harnessing BICs enables strong interactions of optical and acoustic waves and holds great promise for achieving high performance in Brillouin-effect-based applications [J3, J6, C2, C6]. (3) We realized second-harmonic generation from telecom to near-visible wavelengths with BIC-based waveguides. Our results will enable a broad range of on-chip applications such as optical parametric generation, signal processing, and quantum photonics [J7, C7]. (4) We achieved BICs in anti-PT-symmetric systems by using a cascaded-resonator system. The proposed structure can enable many applications that benefit from the advantages of both BICs and anti-PT symmetry, such as optical delay and storage, all-optical nonlinear processing, high-sensitivity sensing, and chiral mode switching [J8]. (5) We investigated the coupling between the photon emitters in monolayer WS2 and BIC waveguides, which paves the way for building on-chip single-photon emitters and offers new insight into on-chip integrated quantum light sources [J9]. (6) We have verified the dissipative nature of coupling between photonic waveguides by demonstrating the complementarily varied loss rates of the two supermodes. The observed supermode BICs open the way for a new category of dissipatively coupled BICs that may enable new applications in signal processing, sensing, chiral transmission, and topological physics [J10]. The research outcome in the engineering aspect is shown as follows: (7) We have demonstrated a BIC-based photonic integrated circuit with basic components such as waveguides, microcavities, grating couplers, directional couplers, power splitters, and Mach–Zehnder interferometers [J1, J5]. (8) We have demonstrated thermo-optic switches and filters, ultrafast photodetectors with 40-GHz detection bandwidth, ultrafast electro-optic modulators with 5-GHz modulation bandwidth by integrating 2D materials on the BIC-based platform [J2, C3, C5]. (9) We have demonstrated a four-channel TM mode (de)multiplexer by cascading multimode directional couplers on the BIC-based platform. The demonstrated device can meet the increasing demand for high capacity in on-chip optical communication [J4, C4]. (10) We have demonstrated high-performance surface acoustic microwave photonic filters on the BIC-based platform. Our demonstration may open up new applications in microwave photonics on the lithium niobate integrated platform, such as optical communication, signal processing, and beam steering [C9].

14206318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206318.value: In this project, we have demonstrated BICs in a fundamentally new photonic architecture by patterning a low-refractive-index material on a high-refractive-index substrate and developed a series of devices for applications in different areas. Further development of the research can include the following aspects: (1) Exploration of BIC in many other physical domains. For example, by applying the principles of BIC in building acoustic waveguides, one can realize low-loss guiding of phonons and thus enable a new type of phononic integrated circuitry for mechanical sensing and optoelectronic signal processing. (2) Extension of the hybrid integrated platform to other functional materials. For example, by mixing dye molecules as well as quantum dots with the polymer, it is possible to realize on-chip optical amplifiers and low-threshold lasers at various wavelengths. (3) Studying many advanced physical topics with the dissipatively coupled BICs, such as quantum physics, non-Hermitian physics, and topological physics. For example, the supermode BICs can be employed to construct a non-Hermitian system by varying the waveguide widths, which enables chiral dynamics and high-sensitivity sensing. (4) Nonlinear optics at the single-photon level as well as scalable photonic quantum information processing. For example, the ultralow-loss BIC mode leads to high-Q microcavities, which can realize strong single-photon nonlinear coupling strength and enable optical quantum state engineering. With the strong acousto-optic modulation, one can develop a wide range of Brillouin-scattering-based photonic applications, such as delay lines, light storage, microwave signal processing, Brillouin lasers and amplifiers, and nonreciprocal light transmission. (5) Development of high-performance lithium niobate optoelectronic chip by integrating all the individual components and modules onto the BIC-based platform.

14206318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206318.value: The research project focuses on the development and characterization of a BIC-based platform in integrated photonics. The project successfully achieved the four objectives, by designing the BIC modes, fabricating and measuring the BIC-based photonic structures, developing basic optical components, and producing hybrid-integrated photonic devices with unique functionalities. The demonstrated platform breaks through the fundamental limitation of photonic architectures, allowing the exploration of high-refractive-index dielectric materials on an integrated platform without the need for patterning micro- or nanostructures in these materials. This project shows a great impact on both BIC physics and practical applications. Fundamentally, the demonstration of BIC in photonic structure enriches the BIC theories and will inspire the exploration of BIC in other physical domains to reduce dissipation loss. Practically, the BIC mode with theoretical zero loss can enable advanced photonic devices with enhanced functionality and performance. Moreover, due to the generic mechanism of BIC, this strategy can be adopted for other functional materials as well as integration with 2D materials, which offers high versatility and potential for applications in high-power photonics, nonlinear optics, and quantum photonics. In the long term, the demonstrated platform paves the way for developing next-generation high-performance optoelectronic chips.

14206518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206518.value: The field of multiuser (or network) information theory deals with determining optimal rates of communication or compression in a multi-user setting such as wireless networks. Unlike the point-to-point setting, many of the fundamental problems remain unsolved. The PI has been actively working towards solving some of these ``open" problems and is excited by some of our recent results in this area. The proposal intends to pursue the new directions that are motivated by these results. The first direction is motivated by the following result. The optimality of superposition coding region for a three receiver broadcast channel with two degraded message sets was an open problem (Open problem 8.2) in the book Network Information Theory. The PI was able to resolve this open problem last year and show that superposition coding was strictly sub-optimal for this setting. This problem is intimately related to open problems 1 and 2 (in Chapter 3.1) posed by Csiszar in the book "Open problems in communication and computation". The counterexample demonstrated that dependent coding across space (independent channels) and time can strictly improve on memoryless coding. By investigating the multi-letter expressions, the PI was able to compute an outer bound to the capacity region. The proposal seeks to build on this work and explore its ramifications: understand why it outperforms the traditional codes, and come up with effective outer bounds to this family of problems. The second direction that the proposal wishes to investigate is the behavior of the capacity regions around the corner points for some basic problem settings. The corner point of the capacity region in a multi-terminal point refers to a point where only the rate to one receiver is maximized while ignoring all other rates. These points lie usually on the axis and their value is determined by the point-to-point capacity of the intended receiver. In this proposal we wish to study the first order (slope) behavior of the capacity region around the known corner points. This question has been recently solved by the PI for a generic discrete memoryless broadcast channel; however the corresponding question for the interference channel and other more general settings remain open. Thus the proposal intends to make use of some very interesting and promising breakthroughs that the PI has obtained recently to make further forays into solving these long standing, fundamental, and central problems in multiuser information theory. 多用戶信息論（或網絡信息論）主要研究在多用戶情況（如無線網絡）下的最優通訊或壓縮速率。不同於點對點情況，該領域的許多基礎問題至今依然未被解決。主要研究員一直以來為解決一些這樣的未解決的問題積極工作，並在最近獲得了一些振奮人心的成果。這個提案將陳述被這些成果啟發的新的方向。 第一個方向來自於以下的成果。在一個有著兩個退化信息集合的三個接收者廣播信道中，疊加編碼是否是最佳通訊方案曾是《網絡信息論》中的一個懸而未決的問題（未解問題8.2）。主要研究員去年成功解決了這個問題，並用反例證明了疊加編碼在這種情況下並不是最佳通訊方案。該問題也與Csiszar的書《通訊與計算中的未解決問題》章節3.1的未解決問題1和2密切相關。 上述用到的反例表明時空耦合編碼能夠提高無記憶編碼。通過研究多字母的表達式，主要研究員能夠計算出信道容量的外界。這份提案將嘗試繼續延伸上述工作：理解為什麼時空耦合編碼的性能可以比傳統編碼更優秀，並對這一類問題提出有效的信道容量的外界。 第二個方向則希望能研究一些基本問題中的信道容量在頂點處的表現。在多端口情形下的信道容量的頂點處，給某一個接收者的通訊速率能得到最大化，而其他的接收者的通訊速率則被忽視。在多端口情形下，所謂信道容量的頂點處，即忽視其他接收者的通訊速率時，使某一個接收者的通訊速率最大化的點。這些點通常在坐標軸上，而且它們的值是由從發送者到目標接受者的點對點信道容量決定的。在這份提案中，我們想研究信道容量在已知的頂點處的切線斜率表現。最近主要研究員解決了一般的離散無記憶廣播信道下的這個問題；然而干擾信道和其他更普遍的情況下的對應問題依然未被解決。 因此這份提案意欲使用主要研究員最近取得的一些非常有吸引力並且有前瞻性的突破性工作，來嘗試解決那些多用戶信息論中長期以來懸而未決的重要基礎問題。

14206518.label: Realisation of objectives
14206518.value: Traditional coding schemes in network information theory use ideas from the probabilistic method to show existence of codes with certain rates. They use ideas such as random binning and superposition coding to achieve these rates. In one sense, these can be viewed as single-letter achievable schemes as the achievable rate regions can be expressed in terms of expressions involving a single use of the channel. The outer bounds in the literature too, aim to arrive at such a conclusion. Objectives 1-3 were directly trying to question this strategy based on preliminary evidence. It was stated as an open question in the book, network information theory, whether superposition coding is optimal for a broadcast channel with three receivers where all of them want a common message and two of them want a another (shared) message. The intuition was that single-letter superposition (with the cloud centre denoting the common message) would be the optimal region. In a preliminary work that motivated this proposal, the PI realised that two-letter superposition coding region (this was known to tend to the capacity region) for a product erasure channel strictly improved on the single-letter region. Further the optimal two-letter superposition coding region could be viewed as a linear code of block two. During this proposal, the PI and his student did similar analysis for larger and larger block-lengths and found that the set of achievable rates did increase. However, by working on a limiting object we could also derive outer bounds to the capacity region. This was done by generalising the concentration result that was derived for the erasure channel. This formed the early part of the investigations of this report and these results are found in an ISIT paper as well as in the PhD thesis of Mehdi Yazdanpanah (graduated in August 2019). There was a main issue with going beyond block size 3. There was a gap between the achievable rates and the bounds obtained using information inequalities. This led us to surmise that while linear codes are useful, this may not exhaust the entire capacity region for product erasure channels. Therefore, we reverted to another problem for which linear codes were already known to be optimal for some regimes, the modulo two sum source coding problem. The difficulty in going beyond small block-sizes related to non-convex nature of the associated optimisation problems. Therefore, with my doctoral student Dustin Wang, we tried to investigate non-convex optimisation problems and how to solve and evaluate them more efficiently. In the process we came up with new converses for the modulo two sum problem, obtained new lower bounds for source coding problems. Further we also realised the the concentration type results perhaps indicated that we have to capture the rate tradeoff using extraneous receivers. This led us to a gradual investigation process of the use of auxiliary receivers. This was the start of a tour de force in network information-theoretic machinery (thanks to the pandemic for giving Amin Gohari and me lots of free time) to develop new and better-than-the-state-of-the-art outer bounds for *all* the three fundamental settings for which the capacity region is still undetermined: the broadcast channel, the interference channel, and the relay channel. This has led to the two journal publications mentioned in the outcome. (There are conference publications also listed related to this that has some of the ideas). Prior to this work, there was a rather infamous open problem related to the corner point of a Gaussian interference channel (infamous because the original proof had a small issue in one of the parts, which was only discovered after many years). This was solved using ideas from functional analysis and high dimensional probability theory such as HWI inequalities by Polyanskiy and Wu. However, even these techniques only showed a flat behaviour at the corner point; quite different from a discontinuity in slope predicted by the inner bounds. As a result of the new ideas for outer bounds, we could do better and not only demonstrate the corner point but also show a discontinuity of the slope at the corner point. Further, in a later paper we also managed to improve the slope. This is related to Objective 4 in this proposal. The link between functional analysis, geometric inequalities and information inequalities were also investigated during this time - motivated in part by the connections to interference channels. This is the third journal publication. With my doctoral student, David Ng, we mainly investigated block Gaussian codes for interference (and showed that it does not improve on single-letter regions), and on developing new bounds for the Gaussian interference channels by incorporating new ideas. This also had a collaboration with Prof. Max Costa.

14206518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206518.value: From the context of the capacity region of a broadcast channel or a 2 receiver interference channel, it was not clear whether structured codes could be really beneficial over optimal random codes. In this work, we show that there are instance where linear codes do outperform standard ideas even in these settings. Further as the block size of the linear codes increase, the rate regions seem to improve. This prompted us to think of novel ideas for outer bounds. Consequently this project has led to at least two novel ideas for outer bounds (in a field where such ideas are very rare). One is to use properties of functions and submodularity type inequalities directly applied to limiting objects to obtain computable outer bounds without corresponding single letter expressions. The second important idea the came out was the use of auxiliary receivers to fashion outer bounds that in some settings were tight; but more importantly, led to strict improvements in the known outer bounds to the capacity region in all the three basic settings of broadcast channel, interference channel, and the relay channel.

14206518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206518.value: The use of linear codes in various contexts have been getting increasing exposure in the community. However, previously, they were used in the context of different sender so as to achieve some kind of spatial dimension collapse. In this work we showed that even in single sender settings, linear codes can improve the set of achievable rates. Further, numerical simulations also showed that the achievable rates increase along with the block size. One potential direction is to explore limits of certain expressions and see if it can be alternately expressed in terms of other functionals. One could potentially investigate a similar idea such as "graphons" in graph limits to information theory. Another potential direction is to use some of these techniques developed in the context of the outer bounds to functional analysis and geometric methods. This is because state of the art inequalities from functional analysis could yield certain bounds; however, the new ideas strictly outperformed these.

14206518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206518.value: It is imperative that we maximize the rate of reliable communication over the scarce physical resources. However as a first order of business, one needs to know the fundamental limits of communication (which is technology independent) so that one can determine how close one is to the physical limits. This research proposal showed that certain mathematical methods (like structured codes) do outperform (in a rate sense) random codes even in regimes that were previously unsuspected. This is important as it can lead to new implementable coding ideas. The second main contribution is to develop new methods to bound the capacity region from outside. For some of the basic settings such as certain relay channels, these techniques give tight expressions and resolve long standing open problems. Further these ideas show a completely unexplored paradigm of the use of auxiliary receivers to capture certain information tradeoffs.
