14206818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206818.value: Aim The aim of this proposed project will be to using coupled meteorological and glacier energy and mass balance model to re-analyse multi-platform observed geodetic glacier mass balance and reconstruct its time series in the Eastern Nyainqêntanglha, Tibetan Plateau. Project Background Glaciers play an essential role in global and regional climate change, and their mass lost is a proxy for global warming. Glaciers located in the high mountains of Asia (HMA) have presented a heterogeneous pattern of mass lost over the last decade. The Eastern Nyainqêntanglha (Southeastern of HMA), where the only maritime glaciers in China are found, have experienced a more rapid mass loss rate than the continental glaciers distributed throughout other parts of the HMA. However, specific glacier mass balance rates have remained on debates according to results derived from different techniques. Because there have been almost no space-borne instruments that have been specifically designed for glacier mass balances observation, the different spatial coverages, revisiting periods and observation principles that have induced large disagreements. It is, therefore, necessary and essential to re-analyse these data and reconstruct the time series of glacier mass balance that observed by multiple platforms for the benefit of further glaciology and hydrology study. A coupled mesoscale distributed weather and glacier energy and mass balance model can be established for use in evaluating and removing these biases. Brief Project Description In this proposed project, we aim to establish a distributed water and enthalpy Budget-based glacier mass balance model (WEB-GM) and couple it with a weather research and forecasting model (WRF). We will also obtain earth observation data including satellite altimetry data, bistatic SAR images and optical stereo images to derive glacier mass balance information for the Eastern Nyainqêntanglha. The seasonal to inter-annual fluctuations and spatially heterogeneity of glacier mass balance show in the coupled model outputs will help to remove bias from the multiple sources observations. Hence a glacier mass balance pattern time series will be provided for the Eastern Nyainqêntanglha region. Parameter sensitivity analysis of the coupled model will also help us understand the factors triggering the rapid glacier mass loss rate in the Eastern Nyainqêntanglha. Significance of the Proposed Project The outcomes from this proposed study will include a strategy to integrate glacier mass balance observed from different observational platforms. The proposed glacier model will help us to understand the physical processes of rapid lost of maritime glaciers in the HMA.

14206818.label: Realisation of objectives
14206818.value: We established the offline coupling model that only considers feedback from WRF's land cover model for the sake of accuracy and efficiency. Parameter sensitivity analysis, involving the temporal resolution of the forcing data, maximum number of iterations of the enthalpy budget calculation, sensitivity to surface albedo scheme and precipitation type discrimination, was performed and the coupled model was established. We utilized the coupling model to derive glacier height changes for 2000 - ~2012. After removing the flat earth and topographic phase evaluated with TSX/TDX orbital information and SRTM. We also proposed three different processing methods to derive glacier height changes for the period of ~2012 to 2017. We generated the mosaicked TanDEM-X DEM of 2017 for the first method which aligned to the same datum and projection of SRTM. Second method followed an iterative D-InSAR procudure that found phase difference in the iteration. The third method is roughly similar to the first one, but considered DLR TanDEM-X DEM as reference. The output of the coupling model was the glacier height changes which were transferred to glacier mass balance with scenarios of glacier density assumption. In order to derive decadal mass balance, a seasonal fluctuation pattern of glacier mass balance was extracted through simulation first. Then, the annual glacier mass balance fluctuations were evaluated with scenarios of glacier density assumption. The procedure was iterated several times until the value was stable. Finally, a distributed glacier surface energy mass balance model from the point like model was released. The accuracy of the model for two period was estimated basically followed error propagation. Finally, to derive the annual glacier mass balance, a similar procedure was followed and the distributed monthly to long-term products of glacier mass balance pattern was determined and released from different earth observation platforms. The re-analysis meteorological result presented that the temperature increased during 1990 to 2009 then followed by a decline trend to 2017 may be the reason responsible for the quick glacier mass loss rate around eastern Nyainqentanglha. Meanwhile, precipitation showed a decline trend from 1995 is another inducing factor.

14207018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207018.value: Modern wireless communication systems often employ advanced modulation techniques (such as OFDM) for increased channel capacity and spectrum utilization. However, the attained high data-rate results in envelope-varying signal waveform that exhibits large Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR). Indeed, advanced modulation schemes also demand high linearity amplification. In practice, power amplifier (PA) operated well below saturation (to avoid signal distortion) will eventually lead to significant impairment in power efficiency. Further, due to the co-existence of different wireless standards (e.g. 2G/3G/4G) with multiple frequency bands, broadband operation of PA is found to be highly desirable for compact and low-cost realization of RF transmitters and base-stations. This project aims to realize advanced microwave power amplifier architectures with both broadband and high efficiency characteristics. Its major principle is based on the adoption of a new Doherty PA configuration in conjunction with the novel design of signal splitting/combining networks. This study also attempts to develop a low-cost solution that features compact size, simple construction and ease of use. This research is essential to existing 4G and future 5G markets and will, in the long run, have a significant impact on the implementation of base-stations and mobile terminals.

14207018.label: Realisation of objectives
14207018.value: All objectives (1-2) have been fully realized. There are three major accomplishments relating to the design and realization of broadband and dual-band high efficiency RF power amplifiers: 1. In this research, a new design method of dual-band OBO-enhanced symmetrical Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) has been studied. Based on the Generalized Combining Network (GCN) theory, a versatile output combiner has been demonstrated in supporting Doherty operation with two widely separated frequency bands. The proposed combiner network is simple in structure, compact in size and flexible in design. A DPA prototype operating at 1.4 and 3.5 GHz has been verified experimentally with Drain Efficiency (DE) of over 68% at saturation (>42 dBm) and 55% at 9-dB back-off being achieved at both frequency bands. Moreover, it exhibits an average DE of over 51% under 9-dB-PAPR modulated signal excitation. Compared to the state-of-the-art dual-band DPA designs, the proposed circuit can offer high-efficiency operation, large frequency band ratio (k > 2), extended OBO, and cost-effective solution (single type of power device, high PUF, and low complexity). 2. In the second work, a new DPA design approach with enlarged operating bandwidth (BW) and high Power Utilization Factor (PUF) has been explored. Through an analytical study, the excessive phase dispersion of quasi-TL (Transmission Line) networks has been identified as the major BW limiting factor of conventional broadband DPA design. By the introduction of optimized adaptive combining load, the available BW of dispersive DPA has reached 60% (theoretical value of ideal-TL DPA) with both high efficiency and PUF. Experimental verification revealed that the proposed DPA can achieve excellent efficiency and high PUF over an extended frequency range (1.4–2.55 GHz). 3. In the final design, a novel fully-integrated CMOS PA that can offer reconfigurable frequency bands and power modes with simple switching scheme and high efficiency has been developed. Compared to prior works, the proposed circuit does not involve multi-chip solution, off-chip components, mixed-semiconductor technologies or advanced efficiency enhancement techniques.

14207018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207018.value: The major findings concerning the design and implementation of wideband and dual-band high efficiency RF power amplifiers include: 1. Design of Generalized Equal-cell Dual-band Doherty Power Amplifier with Extended Power Back-off Range: Owing to the adoption of equal-cell architecture and extended power output back-off (OBO > 6 dB) operation, the conventional dual-band impedance-transformer approach cannot be applied. Because of this, a novel output combiner is proposed for the provision of load modulation at two widely spaced frequency bands. A 9-dB-OBO DPA design operating at 1.4- and 3.5-GHz was prototyped. Simulation and measurement results indicate excellent Doherty efficiency behavior with back-off (9 dB) efficiency of over 55% and saturation efficiency of over 68% at both frequencies. Under 9-dB-peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) WCDMA signal excitation, average efficiency of 52.1% and 51.3% was achieved at 1.4 and 3.5 GHz, respectively. Out of this work, a peer-reviewed journal article (J1) was published in 2020 (IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques) with a citation index of over 15 (dated Feb. 2022). 2. Design of Bandwidth Enhancement of Frequency Dispersive Doherty Power Amplifier: For the first time, the impact of the excessive phase dispersion of matching networks on the performance of conventional broadband DPA was analytically revealed. For dispersion compensation, an optimized adaptive combining load was introduced to enhance the achievable DPA BW and PUF. For verification, a 42-dBm equal-cell DPA was prototyped to cover 1.4–2.55 GHz. Measurement results indicate that, over the prescribed frequency range, a PUF of over 0.95, back-off efficiency (6 dB) of 48%–58%, and saturation efficiency of 62%–74% can be achieved. Moreover, under WCDMA excitation, the adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) was found to be better than −32 dBc with average efficiency of over 45% (without applying digital predistortion). Out of this research, a journal article (J2) has been published in IEEE Microwave and Wireless Components Letters (2020). 3. Design of Single-Chip CMOS Dual-band Tri-Power-Mode Reconfigurable High Efficiency RF Power Amplifier: The proposed architecture utilizes a novel switched-capacitor based output network to facilitate differential signal combining and impedance transformation at two widely separated frequency bands. It can offer three distinct output power levels (saturation) to be selected for multi-power-mode applications. Besides, closed-form explicit equations are readily available for the evaluation of component values. For validation, a PA operating at 1.8/2.6 GHz (non-concurrent), with three distinct saturation power levels (21, 23, 26 dBm) and peak efficiency of about 30%, was designed and fabricated using 0.35 µm CMOS process. Out of this finding, a peer-reviewed article (J3) has been published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits & Systems-II: Express Briefs (2021).

14207018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207018.value: With the explosive growth of wireless market (e.g., cellular, WLAN), RF transmitters that can support multiple communication standards (e.g. widely-separated frequency bands, advanced modulation formats) are in great demand. To date, there have been significant efforts to develop wideband or multi-band power amplifier (PA) with enhanced efficiency and small footprint, operating at sub-6GHz and mm-wave frequencies. Monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC) based upon CMOS and/or Compound semiconductor technologies are potential candidates for existing 5G and future 6G applications. The PA solutions developed here can be further extended and combined with MMIC technology for increased integration, higher operating frequency (e.g. mm-wave) as well as cost reduction.

14207018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207018.value: To accommodate the increasing demand for wireless communication, the cellular system underwent rapid development in the past decades. Among the wireless communication spectra, the sub-6 GHz is regarded the primary frequency band to offer the best compromise between capacity and coverage. However, because of the coexistence of various communication standards (such as 4G-LTE, and 5G-NR), the available spectrum below 6 GHz displays more scattering, which makes it very challenging to design a transmitter covering all frequency bands. Furthermore, to provide higher data rate and massive system capacity, multicarrier techniques (e.g., orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing) and spectrum-efficient modulation schemes (e.g., quadrature amplitude modulation) have been widely used in modern wireless communications, thus leading to transmitted signal with large peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and hence degraded power efficiency of RF transmitter. This research work aims to explore advanced microwave power amplifier architectures with both broadband and high efficiency characteristics. This study also attempts to develop a low-cost solution that features compact size and simple construction. This research outcome is essential to emerging 5G markets and will, in the long run, have a significant impact on the development of wireless communication system infrastructure (e.g. base-stations and mobile handsets).

14207118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207118.value: 定參數算法是解决不可解問題在其參數較小時的有效方法。本項目旨在開發一種基於間接驗證的新方法用於定參數算法設計。此新方法是對作者等十年前所發明的隨機分離法之擴充。用這一新方法，作者已成功地設計出了解决經典的點覆蓋問題的數個新算法。我們相信本項目會産生有影響力的成果， 並對定參數算法的設計作出重要貢獻。

14207118.label: Realisation of objectives
14207118.value: The main objective of this project is to develop the following indirect certificating method for designing FPT algorithms to find k-solutions, i.e., solutions of size k of NP-hard problems: Discover a small-size structure x in the input I that is disjoint from a k-solution X of I and can be used as a certificate for a yes-instance, and then use random partition to find a k-solution with the aid of this small indirect certificate x. This novel idea was initially motivated by my well-known random separation method, and my obsession of using the method to solve the classical vertex cover problem. It turns out that this indirect certificating method is more general than the random separation method, and is a general tool for designing FPT algorithms. Here are some highlights of my major findings in realizing the objective of the project: 1. Every yes-instance (G,k) of Vertex Cover admits an indirect certificate of size at most k/3. The theorem implies that at most k/3 vertices, instead of k vertices, are sufficient to convince others that the input graph G admits a vertex cover of size k, and lays the foundation of an O(kn)-time algorithm that uses the indirect certificating method and achieves success probability at least 1.6633^{-k}. 2. For any positive integer constant t, there are NP-hard problems that admit certificates of size at most k^{1/t}. This is quite surprising as a natural certificate of an NP-hard problems has size k, and we need much less information, k^{1/t} instead of k, to convince others yes-instances of such NP-hard problems. We note that it is very unlikely that NP-hard problems have certificates of size O(log(k)). 3. A large class of FPT problems solvable by bounded search tree can also be solved by indirect certificating. Since bounded search tree is a fundamental tool for designing FPT algorithms, this is a clear indication that indirect certificating is also a general tool for designing FPT algorithms and therefore quite potential for solving NP-hard problems in FPT time. Indeed it is extremely challenging to develop a new method for designing algorithms, and my encouragement for this novel indirect certificating method comes from the success of the method for Vertex Cover and my experience in inventing the well-kown random separation method, which happens to be a special case of indirect certificating. I tried to explore the possibility of indirect certificating as a general tool for designing FPT algorithms, instead of just a clever trick for some isolated problems. With this idea of general tool in mind, I have tried to use this indirect certificating method to design FPT algorithms for several classical problems such as Feedback Vertex Set, Multicut and Hitting Set. Initially, I was unsuccessful for Feedback Vertex Set, Multicut for Trees, but managed to solve Hitting Set for Triples by a complicated ad hoc approach. The main difficulty lies in determining the existence of indirect certificates and computing a k-solution with undesired noise in a partition. A breakthrough was made when I realized that the ad hoc approach I used for Hitting Set for Triples can be generalized to other problems, and indeed I have used a similar idea to solve Multicut for Trees. After these two successful applications, I have noticed that the method can be viewed as one orthogonal to the fundamental method of bounded search tree. With this point of view, I have successfully proved that a large class of FPT algorithms based on bounded search tree can be transformed into FPT algorithms based on indirect certificating. This confirms my initial view that indirect certificating is a general tool for designing FPT algorithms.

14207118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207118.value: The project has developed an innovative method, indirect certificating, for designing FPT algorithms, and the following four papers summarize main results from this project. Paper 1 (CAI, Vertex Covers ...) The classical Vertex Cover can be solved in FPT time by various techniques, but it seemed almost impossible to do so by approaches based on random partition. I prove that every graph with a k-vertex cover admits an indirect certificate of size at most k/3 (surprising and perhaps best possible), which enables us to obtain an FPT algorithm using random partition and having success probability of 1.6633^{-k}. This indirect certificate also leads to several other new FPT algorithms for Vertex Cover based on random partition and random selection. Furthermore, I have also explored other structural properties of vertex covers and use them to obtain new FPT algorithms by iterative compression and color coding. Paper 2 (CAI, Indirect Certificating ...) I have obtained indirect certificates for several other problems, including Colored Clustering, Hitting Set, and Multicut, and developed FPT algorithms by utilizing these indirect certificates. Furthermore, I have shown that indirect certificating is a general tool for designing FPT algorithms, as it can be viewed as a method orthogonal to bounded search-tree method, which enables us to transform many search-tree based FPT algorithms into FPT algorithms based on indirect certificating. Paper 3 (CAI, FPT and Exact Algorithms ...) We consider FPT algorithms and exact algorithms for the weighted version of the classical Maximum 2-Satisfiability problem. The problem is NP-complete and W[1]-hard, and we present an exact algorithm with running time roughly O(n^{0.792k}) by transforming the problem into finding a maximum-weight triangle in a graph with carefully chosen edge weights. We also give an FPT algorithm running in time 2^O(k) n log(n) when each literal appears a constant number of times. Our FPT algorithm transforms the problem into a maximum vertex cover problem and apply the random separation method, a special case of indirect certificating, in a clever way. Paper 4 (CAI and Leung, Colored Clustering ...) Further to my direct work on the indirect certificating method, we also used the general idea of random partition to obtain an FPT algorithm for the Colored Clustering problem, where we wish to color vertices of an edge colored graph to produce as many stable edges as possible, i.e., edges with the same color as their ends. In this paper, we reveal that the problem is in fact a maximum subgraph problem concerning monochromatic subgraphs and alternating paths, and demonstrate the usefulness of such connection in studying these problems. We obtain a faster algorithm to solve the problem for edge-bicolored graphs by reducing the problem to a minimum cut problem, and we also give FPT algorithms for the problem when we take the numbers of stable edges and unstable edges, respectively, as parameters.

14207118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207118.value: The project has demonstrated that the existence of indirect certificates of NP-hard problems can be surprisingly useful for developing FPT algorithms to solve parameterized versions of these hard problems, and indicated the wide applicability of the indirect certificating method in designing FPT algorithms. It will be interesting to see if we can also use the method to obtain FPT algorithms when no search-tree based algorithms are available. In particular, can we also use the method to obtain an FPT algorithm for the classical bipartite graph deletion problem? The usefulness of indirect certificates also calls for the study of smaller certificates for NP-hard problems as they are useful to reduce communication cost. A more demanding direction is to develop tools for obtaining smaller certificates as well as tools for establishing lower bounds of certificate size. In particular, is k/3 the lower bound for certificates of k-Vertex Cover?

14207118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207118.value: FPT algorithms are useful and effective in solving intractable problems in practice when certain parts of inputs are relatively small, and we have developed an innovative method, indirect certificating, for design FPT algorithms. Although intractable problems are extremely hard to solve, it is usually easy to convince others that an instance of an intractable problem is a yes-instance by presenting a certificate of the instance. Typically, we use solutions of yes-instances as certificates. In this project, we demonstrate that intractable problems can possess indirect certificates, which can be smaller than natural certificates. And, very surprisingly, the existence of indirect certificates can be very useful in finding solutions, even without actually knowing indirect certificates. We are able to develop FPT algorithms based on existence of indirect certificates, and also relate our indirect certificating method to the fundamental bounded search tree method for designing FPT algorithms. It is a rare occasion to invent a new method for designing algorithms, and this innovative method of indirect certificating provides us with a new and general tool for designing FPT algorithms. In view of this, the project has made a significant contribution to the field of FPT algorithms.

14207318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207318.value: 最近，深度學習在許多應用中取得了巨大成功。它在諸多領域引發了模式上的轉變，尤其是在自然語言處理和計算機視覺領域上。這很自然引發出一個問題：深度學習能否也會在信號處理的基礎研究中發揮作用，進而拓展到，優化，統計和機器學習領域？ 我們應該更嚴謹地定義這一類問題的範圍：這是一類基於模型的研究分支，而且此分支中的問題重視利用模型的內在結構來設計有效的解決方案。它也尋求從理論意義上更好地理解問題本質。舉一個重要的例子，優化技術作為一個十多年來處理基於模型的信號處理問題的關鍵方法，可以極其有效地處理基於模型的信號處理問題，並極大地拓展了我們的科研視野。從處理問題的角度來說，基於模型的技術與深度學習的技術在很多方面非常不同。一些學者批判性地稱深度學習為黑盒方法。但是我們能否在基於模型的問題中將深度學習轉化為優勢加以利用，而不是抗拒它？最近，一些研究開始注意到這個科研方向，但是現有結果仍然寥寥無幾。 這個項目旨在研究利用兩個不同的研究方法，即優化和深度學習，來建立新的基於模型的信號處理技術。簡單來說，對於基於模型的信號處理問題，我們會嘗試用深度學習技術來進一步學習目前最代表性的優化算法，並通過它找到對於相同問題的更好算法。這個想法通常被稱為深度展開。深度展開繼承了優化算法利用問題結構和本質的特點，所以它並不是一個黑盒的方法。目前，深度展開只被應用在少數特殊的問題上，比如 l1 稀疏問題。而我們的目標是開發一個深度展開的框架來處理一大類通用的問題。這個目標一旦成功，將能極大地影響到很多現有應用。這個問題裡有挑戰的地方是確定什麼是最值得用深度學習來學習的優化算法，以及如何將一些現有技術細節融入到學習這些算法的過程中。因此，這研究也會和一些基本優化問題有很緊密的聯繫。除此之外，這個項目也將會探討運用深度展開到兩個前沿的應用---大型MIMO的1-比特量化信號檢測和結構性低秩矩陣模型。

14207318.label: Realisation of objectives
14207318.value: The realization of the objectives was successful. By the end of this project we are able to establish a homotopy optimization framework for deep unfolding, which provides a variety of deep unfolding possibilities (e.g., proximal gradient deep nets, Frank-Wolfe deep nets, ADMM deep nets, and expectation-maximization deep nets). We are also successful with our application to challenging MIMO detection problems. By the end of the project, we are able to tackle the very challenging problem of one-bit MIMO-OFDM detection.

14207318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207318.value: In our first major investigation, we considered MIMO detection with coarsely-quantized (one-bit) received signals. This is a well-motivated problem in massive MIMO. We devised a deep unfolding-based neural network by taking insight from the homotopy optimization principle and from the structure of the proximal gradient method. The deep networks built outperform many of the state of the arts. The work was published in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. In our second major investigation, we considered MIMO-OFDM detection with coarsely-quantized received signals. There are only a few algorithms for this problem, and deep learning was not considered in prior work. The new challenge lies in the significantly larger problem dimension than MIMO detection. We had to first develop a new class of model-based techniques, in order to overcome the challenges. Using the new model-based techniques built, we employed deep unfolding to build a deep network that smartly uses OFDM problem structures to efficiently perform MIMO-OFDM detection. The result is very promising as indicated by our empirical experiments. While the project focuses on deep unfolding, it is worthwhile to note that even the model-based part of our developments has significant contributions. The work was submitted to IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. Currently it is under revision, and the comments received seem to suggest that the work has a good chance to be accepted. In the third major investigation, we built on our past experiences and accomplishments to return to the basics. We were interested in whether we can provide an explanation of why our deep unfolding-based methods work, and, from that explanation, how we may expand and generalize the principles. This turns out to be possible in the context of MIMO detection. We provide an explanation from the perspective of homotopy optimization. That explanation explains why we want to use certain nonlinear activation functions in deep networks, and it led us to new possibilities such as Frank-Wolfe deep nets, ADMM deep nets, adaptation to the more challenging multi-level constellations cases, etc. The work was published in IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing (OJSP). The paper stands as the most popular paper in OJSP, as of May 2023. The PI should report that the GRF project reference number with all the journal and conference publications was consistently misquoted as "142017318"; the correct one is "14207318". Unfortunately, no amendment is allowed for these published papers. The PI apologizes this oversight.

14207318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207318.value: There is great potential for further development. In particular, the major finding by the end of the project has essentially established a framework based on homotopy optimization. That framework provides an explanation of why deep unfolding may lead to beneficial results. It will be very interesting to further study how this homotopy optimization framework can be leveraged to build more powerful deep networks, how the homotopy optimization framework can be applied to other signal processing applications, and how the new insights gained from the homotopy optimization framework can be used to design better training schemes. We see many possibilities.

14207318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207318.value: Machine learning and artificial intelligence are making tremendous impact on different fields, and this is particularly so in natural language processing and computer vision, which interface with people closer. The success is largely due to deep learning techniques, which rely on massive computations and massive data. Signal processing, a field for inventing “stealth technology” for improving human life, has had its success largely with model-based techniques—we build computationally efficient solutions through understanding of the underlying problem nature. In this project we studied deep learning methods that leverage our understanding from model-based signal processing. Our study demonstrated that model-based deep learning methods are beneficial, particularly, for MIMO detection (an important signal processing problem and an essential component for wireless communications). We built efficient high-performance solutions for complex and challenging MIMO detection problems, which is attractive from an industry point of view. Our investigation also gave new explanations of why model-based deep learning methods would work in MIMO detection, which is intriguing from an academic perspective. The significance of this project lies in providing new fundamental insights and better practical solutions for model-based deep learning techniques for signal processing, which has now become a key topic.

14207518.label: Project Objectives
14207518.value: Design and analysis of efficient classical/quantum "modulators" and quantum/classical "demodulators" that can be used as interface for quantum--quantum channels with memory. Such "modulators" and "demodulators" have the potential to take advantage of the superadditivity of some classes of quantum channels. In previous work, the PI and his collaborators have come up with algorithms for efficiently maximizing the mismatch information rate by optimizing the law of the auxiliary channel within some class of classical channels with memory. We want to consider the, as it turns out, non-trivial, generalization of these algorithms to maximizing the mismatch information rate by optimizing the law of the auxiliary channel within some class of quantum channels with memory. Design and analysis of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes suitable for the quantum channels under consideration. An intriguing aspect will be to see if the different parts can be designed separately or if they have to be designed jointly towards improving the reliability of the system. So far, all stochastic techniques for estimating information rates do calculations based on running the sum-product algorithm on a cycle-free factor graph. In order to be able to deal efficiently with complicated channels, we want to explore how far calculations that have been done so far on cycle-free factor graphs can also be accomplished by running the sum-product algorithm (and more sophisticated variants thereof) on factor graphs with cycles, thereby significantly reducing the complexity. Explore if and how the results of the above projects can be extended to quantum channels beyond point-to-point quantum channels.

14207518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207518.value: 我們生活的世界是量子的——這一點並不會因為我們局限于經典力學的感官體驗所改變。然而感官與直覺上的不足不因成為我們在工程學中利用量子現象的絆腳石。 量子資訊處理是指基於並利用量子現象的資訊處理技術。它涉及到量子資訊的處理、傳輸及儲存。量子信道(quantum channel)——作為該項技術中的一大基本概念——主要用於描述傳輸問題中的收發(receiver-transmitter)關係，但也常常被用於描述量子資訊的處理和儲存問題。在下文中，我們將主要考慮信道在傳輸問題中的角色。 無記憶量子信道(memoryless quantum channels)是過去的主流量子通信模型；而近年來有憶量子信道(memory quantum channels)逐漸受到關注。一大原因在於前者對於描述某些物理模型的局限性。在本專案中, 我們致力於研究某些類別的有憶量子信道，從而實現基於此類信道的可靠而高效的通信。 是次研究提議始於一篇由專案負責人(PI)及其一位博士生近期撰寫的期刊。該文討論了一種高效估計有憶量子信道的經典資訊率(classical information rate)的方法。這篇論文同時為相關信道的非匹配解碼(mismatched decoding)提供了依據；而後者基於優化後的輔助有憶經典信道。 是次研究提議將計畫大幅度超越以上結果：尤其考慮到有憶量子信道的編碼及解碼器的設計領域中的大幅空白。我們將會考慮經典及量子輸入輸出的多種情況。除了要設計高效的編碼及解碼器，我們更會考慮利用量子信道的某些獨特性質，例如超可加性(superadditivity)。 在其科研生涯中，專案負責人是使用圖模型(graphical models)表達及視覺化數學結果的專家。他成功地將此技巧運用在了經典有憶信道和基於消息傳遞(message-passing)的解碼器的研究中。事實上，合適的圖模型對於處理有憶量子信道的問題也多有裨益——它們不僅可以用於描述及表徵信道，更可以説明構建有效的編碼及解碼器。故而，圖模型將會是本專案中的關鍵角色。 此外, 圖模型還為（估）算某些數值提供了新方法。目前，有憶（經典）信道信息量的估算基於無環圖上的和積演算法(sum-product algorithm)。（對於有環圖，我們會將其轉換成等效的無環圖。）而如何構建合適的有環圖以配合和積演算法(或其變種)來估算有憶量子信道的資訊率是一個極具吸引力的命題。這一方向的研究有希望大幅削短相關問題的計算時間。 總之，是次專案的核心目標是利用上述手段在量子資訊處理領域做出基本、深入和實用的貢獻。

14207518.label: Realisation of objectives
14207518.value: Two of my PhD students and one postdoc have worked on topics related to this project: (1) Michael X. Cao (CAO Xuan) (PhD, supported by this grant Jan. 2019 - Feb. 2021) (2) Anthony Huang (HUANG Yuwen) (PhD, supported by PGS, not supported by this grant) (3) Shashank Vatedka (postdoc, not supported by this grant) For all of the above students and the postdoc, I directly supervised their research by having individual weekly meetings, giving them advice on how to proceed, telling them about relevant papers, sometimes outlining potential solutions, sometimes proving results and writing computer programs myself, and giving guidance while writing papers. Contributions toward objectives (more details below): (1) Michael X. Cao has mainly contributed to Objectives 1-5. (2) Anthony Huang has mainly contributed to Objective 4. (3) Shashank Vatedka has mainly contributed to Objective 4. The unifying theme of this project was to gain a better understanding of graphical models (GMs) and the sum-product algorithm (SPA). GMs and the SPA have been successfully used for classical information processing (CIP). In this project we explored the use of GMs in quantum information processing (QIP), in particular in the context of reliable communication over quantum channels. Here the concept of a quantum channel serves not only as a primitive for quantum information transmission, but also for QIP more generally. (On the side, the PI has been elevated to IEEE Fellow (class of 2021) "for contributions to graphical models for channel coding".) (1) Some of Michael X. Cao's contributions are as follows: (a) Characterizing of the classical information rate of quantum channels with memory with the help of variations of the SPA. Here the SPA is not used for decoding, but for estimating the information rate of such channels. While the basic idea came from techniques (devised by the PI and collaborators in earlier work) for classical channels with memory, it turned out that the proofs of the statements in the quantum channel setup required rather non-trivial generalizations and novel ideas. (b) Optimizing the information rate of so-called mismatched decoders that have low complexity, and along with that also the design of efficient classical/quantum "modulators" and "demodulators". While the basic idea came from techniques (devised by the PI and a different set of collaborators in earlier work) for classical channels with memories, also here the generalization to quantum channels with memory turned out to be non-trivial and requiring novel ideas. A notable (and from the perspective of applications very valuable) aspect of the obtained techniques is the fact that they are data-driven, i.e., only input/output sequences of the true channel are needed, but not the channel model of the true channel itself. (c) Investigating GMs for QIP. When generalizing GMs from CIP to GMs that can be used for QIP, different avenues can be taken. One possibility is to generalize non-negative-valued function nodes to pairs of complex-valued function nodes that have to satisfy some positive-definiteness constraint. Another possibility is to generalize non-negative-valued function nodes to positive-semidefinite-matrix-valued function nodes. While the generalization of the multiplication of function nodes in the first approach is a straightforward extension of real multiplication to complex multiplication, the generalization of the multiplication of function nodes in the second approach requires the use of a special matrix product that is associative and commutative. Both approaches have their advantages (and disadvantages) for actual calculations. Results were obtained that characterized the approximations obtained by the sum-product algorithm (and variants) on these GMs when computing quantities of interest. (2) Anthony Huang's main focus was on understanding the approximation obtained by the SPA, known as the Bethe approximation, in the context of GMs motivated by QIP. For context: for GMs, the partition sum (or partition function) Z is the sum of the global function over all configurations. For scenarios of interest, the partition sum is usually intractable and so one has to approximate it. In the context of CIP, Yedidia et al. defined the Bethe approximation Z_Bethe to the partition sum Z via the solution of an optimization problem and showed that fixed points of the SPA correspond to stationary points of the function appearing in the above-mentioned optimization problem. Later, the PI showed a combinatorial interpretation of Z_Bethe in terms of graph covers. While the expression of Z_Bethe in terms of an optimization problem is useful for numerical purposes, the latter result has proven beneficial for analytically relating the values of Z and Z_Bethe. Anthony investigated the generalization of the above results to GMs motivated by QIP. In particular, he analyzed if the combinatorial interpretation of Z_Bethe in terms of graph covers still holds. This is non-trivial because the proof technique that was used in the classical setup breaks down in the quantum setup. We were able to show that for certain classes of GMs (which satisfy an easily checkable condition) the result still holds. In fact, based on numerical results, we conjecture that the result holds much more generally. In another research direction, Anthony considered the local marginal polytope associated with GMs. For context: the local marginal polytope is the domain of the above optimization problem and collects all the relevant variable-based and function-based marginals for the GM under consideration. For most GMs with cycles, the local marginal polytope is such that there are collections of marginals that cannot be written as marginals of a joint probability mass function. This is an important aspect when understanding and quantifying the suboptimality of the SPA. As we discovered, interestingly enough, the same mathematical structures appear when trying to understand the benefits of entanglement in QIP (cf. Bell's inequalities). (3) Shashank Vatedka's main focus was on the approximation of the permanent for non-negative matrices. (The permanent of a non-negative, square matrix is one of the most prototypical (weighted) counting problems in theoretical computer science and appears naturally in many information processing scenarios.) However, he introduced a novel GM, i.e., a GM that is different than the traditionally used GM for approximating the permanent via the SPA. Interestingly enough, because of the particular structure of the novel GM, running the SPA on this novel GM has many similarities to running the SPA on GMs used in QIP, thereby allowing for a cross-fertilization of techniques for the efficient implementation of the SPA in the classical and the quantum domains. He studied the resulting Bethe approximation and showed that for some classes of matrices, with a slight increase in computational complexity compared with the traditionally used GM, better approximation guarantees can be given. Some of the insights gained in the above research have be weaved into my post-graduate course IERG5200 (Channel Coding and Modulation) in Spring 2020 and Spring 2022 and my post-graduate course IERG6120 (QIP) in Spring 2021 and (upcoming) Spring 2023. Concerning Objectives 3 and 5 with less than 100% completion: this is due to more focus being spent on the other objectives than originally planned. (This refocusing is not due to fundamental problems, but due to pursuing the most promising directions based on the capabilities and knowledge of the students and postdocs. Note that in the research area of this project it takes a significant amount of training beyond the typical undergraduate education in order for a student to do meaningful research.)

14207518.value: (References below are w.r.t. to Part C.) (1) Michael X. Cao: the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem states under what conditions on some process X_1, X_2, X_3, ..., the entropy rate lim_{n -> infinity} (1/n) H(X_1, ..., X_n) equals lim_{n -> infinity} - (1/n) log(p(x_1, ...,x_n)) with probability 1, where x_1, ..., x_n, is a sample sequence of the above process. This is the key results that was used by the PI and his collaborators in earlier work to efficiently estimate (with the help of the SPA) the information rate of classical channels with memory. A central technical result in the investigations by Michael was the generalization of this result to quantum channels with memory. Another result is the optimization of the information rate of so-called mismatched decoders that have low complexity, and along with that also the design of efficient classical/quantum "modulators" and "demodulators". A central technical result was how to efficiently approximate the gradient of a function whose function values can only be estimated. Section 8, No. 1 Section 9, No. 1 Section 10, No. 1 -------------------------------------------------- (2) Anthony Huang: Some results (and their proofs) for graphical models generalize straightforwardly from the classical setup to the quantum setup, however, some results (and their proofs) do not generalize straightforwardly. A central theme of Anthony's research was to address the second type of results and devise techniques to deal with them. Section 9, No. 2 Section 9, No. 3 -------------------------------------------------- (3) Shashank Vatedka: in general, the Bethe approximation of the partition sum of a graphical model can be improved by removing cycles by suitably merging parts of a graphical model. However, usually this comes at a significant computational cost when running the SPA on the modified graphical model. A key result of Shashank's research was on how to remove cycles in the graphical model that is typically used for estimating the permanent, yet not to incur a large computational penalty, along with analyzing the modified graphical model. Section 9, No. 4 Section 11, No. 2 -------------------------------------------------- (4) Work with my collaborator Hans-Andrea Loeliger: investigation of graphical models for quantum information processing, in particular toward understanding of when "quantum variables" are jointly classicable. The concept of jointly classicable variables allows a unifying perspective on various "paradoxes" in quantum information processing. This concept was also at the basis of some of the investigations by Anthony Huang mentioned above. Section 8, No. 2

14207518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207518.value: Further investigation of the Objectives 3 and 5 with less than 100% completion: we expect that insights gained in by the PI and collaborators on finite-input intersymbol interference wiretap channels (see Part C, Section 11, No. 1), in particular w.r.t. the constrained secrecy capacity and coding schemes for such channels, will also significantly benefit these lines of research. Extension of the results that were obtained by Anthony Huang. We want to show that in the quantum setup the combinatorial characterization of the Bethe approximation of the partition sum holds more generally than we were able to prove so far. At the same time, we want to search for counter-examples (we do not have a counter-example so far), which would show limitations to the generality of the conjecture.

14207518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207518.value: Quantum information processing is about understanding the quantum-mechanical aspects of our world and use it to our advantage to process, transmit, and store information. A fundamental concept in quantum information processing is a quantum channel, a concept that is useful not only in the context of transmission of information, but also in the context of processing and storing of information. In order to efficiently do the relevant computations when processing information, graphical models and the sum-product algorithm are very beneficial. (For example, reliable data communication in the recent 5G telecommunications standard is achieved with the help of low-density parity-check codes, which are decoded by running the sum-product algorithm on a suitably formulated graphical model.) The aim of this project was to enhance our knowledge of graphical models that can be used for quantum information processing in general, and for quantum channels with memory in particular. While results for graphical models for classical information processing (in particular results by the PI and collaborators) have inspired various research directions in this project, the generalization of these results to graphical models for quantum information processing was often non-trivial and required novel ideas to deal with the more challenging setup.

14207618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207618.value: 布林函數（Boolean functions）的近似次數（approximate degree）是一個與他們的查詢複雜性（query complexity）及可學習性（learnability）有密切關係的量。給定一函數，如何證實其近似次數算高呢？過去廿年的研究受到量子算法研究的大力推動，得出某些函數近似次數的緊密界限。這些結果已被證明難以一般化，部分原因是沒有適合的複合定理。最近有了一項突破，Bun和Thaler（FOCS 2017）擬出一個嶄新的複合法（composition method）並首次得出了一個n參數、n^{1-\epsilon}次數的AC0函數例子。 最近另一範疇的研究建立了函數近似次數和它重建密碼學中秘密分享（secret sharing）的份額（shares）的能力。這些成果激發對高近似次數和針對密碼學應用的複合法給出替代定義。我們有興趣研究這些工具在獲得近似次數的新下限的適用性。為了說明它們的威力，我們顯示已知的複合定理及其證明有著自然的秘密共享解釋。我們在這範疇研究的一類例子是de Morgan公式，包括不平衡深度2和/或樹這個特殊情況。 在部分函數的情況有兩種近似次數的定義。在文獻中多數採用的那個，多項式在域外的參數是不受約束的（超越有界）。我們觀察到對這些參數施加更強的整數約束可得出更強的下限。我們提出以凸鬆弛研究這兩個概念的間隙，並以近似多數函數為實際例子。

14207618.label: Realisation of objectives
14207618.value: The theme of this project is the duality between approximate degree and secret sharing. The initial ideas were to leverage results from secret sharing to improve approximate degree bounds. Some of the results obtained also rely on connections in the other direction, i.e., applications of methods from approximate degree bounds for secret sharing. We found it more productive to partly change the focus as some of the open problems mentioned in the proposal were resolved by other researchers (Sherstov, Bun and Thaler) using different methods. Objective 1: This objective was largely addressed in the progress report. The work [3] contains some new results on the approximate degree of AC0 under some restriction that is natural from a cryptographic perspective. It also derives a general result about leakage-resilience to a large class of multiparty computation protocols. In contrast, the work [2] gives a much stronger leakage-resilience result, but one that applies to a specific protocol. Objective 2: The work [3] proposes and systematically studies a new relaxation of secret sharing where the complexity of the distribution on shares is restricted. This analysis leads to a finer understanding of the approximate degree of the OR function as parametrized by the degree of the dual distributions as polynomial maps. Objective 3: The manuscript https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2021/115/ (other impact, [2]) arose out of an investigation of lower bounds for partial functions using methods from quantum query complexity. In the process we discovered a major error in one of the foundational works in this area and corrected it using methods developed in the project.

14207618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207618.value: One accomplishment of this project is a deeper understanding of the approximate degree of the OR function and its impact on secure multiparty computation. * In [1] we bound the approximate degree by a novel argument and show a general tradeoff between the parameters of the dual witness (the number of parties vs. the distinguishing advantage) that extend to all symmetric functions. * In [2] we leverage these and other insights to resolve an open problem about leakage-resilience of private circuts * In [3] we carry out a systematic study of indistinguishability of *simple* distributions inspired by cryptographic applications. We obtain new bounds from the OR functions from this perspective and identify complexity-theoretic barriers to extending these results to more complex functions. * In (other impact, [2]) and Cheug Tsun Ming's M.Phil. Thesis we identify an error in a construction of an instance of a partial function with large gap between quantum and classical query complexity, a notion closely related to approximate degre, in work of Aaronson and Ambainis. We also demonstrate that the error can be fixed for the case of a single quantum query by a different analysis. A general analysis for multiple queries was obtained independently by Bravyi, Gosset, and Grier.

14207618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207618.value: This project, in conjunction with independent progress by other researchers, largely settles the questions that motivated the proposal. One exception is the approximate degree of partial functions like "approximate majority" which remains unknown. Resolving that problem might require advances in other areas. It is difficult to recommend a specific course of action at this point.

14207618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207618.value: The "approximate degree" of a function is a mathematical concept that gives an indication how difficult the function may be to compute. Calculating the approximate degree of various functions of interest is a challeging task. Surprisingly, this concepts turns out to be closely related to "indistinguishability of probability distributions", a key primitive behind secure multiparty computations. These are protocols that allow computers to jointly compute something of interest without revealing unintended private information. The main takeaway of this project is that insights about approximate degree lead to advances in indistinguishability, in some cases leading to better protocols, or enhanced security guarantees of existing protocols. In the other direction, insights from indistinguishability give a finer understanding of approximate degree. As a byproduct we also discovered a major error in a result about the power of quantum computers and developed tools for repairing this error.

14207718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207718.value: The problem of identifying geometric deformation between images is regularly encountered in a wealth of applications like medical image alignment (MRI, CT, eye fundus etc.), video stabilization, panorama generation, image super-resolution. The literature on this topic is abundant but most algorithms are unable to align images accurately in the presence of significant intensity distortions (caused by blurring, global intensity variations, noise etc.), or for large distortions. We propose to develop a new approach to image registration by combining our Local All-Pass (LAP) elastic registration agorithm (fast and accurate, when intensity distortions are minimal), with a linear parametric fitting strategy that allows both to refine the deformation found so that it abides by an expected model, and to predict the intensity changes. This LAP + refinement process is iterated until some stabilisation is achieved. Preliminary results demonstrate the high accuracy and high robustness of this strategy, while still not compromising the algorithmic efficiency. In this proposal, we plan to develop and test our parametric approach to address difficult registration problems: when the images to align are corrupted with significant intensity distortions or have limited overlap. We also plan to investigate how much our approach is able to address multimodal registration problems. 在諸如醫學圖像對齊（核磁共振成像、电脑断层扫描、眼底圖像等）、視頻穩像、全景生成、圖像超分辨率等大量應用中經常會遇到需要確定圖像之間的幾何形變的問題。雖然關於此問題的文獻非常豐富，但是在亮度變化（由圖像模糊、全局亮度變化、噪聲等引起）或大的幾何形變存在的情況下，多數算法不能將圖像準確對齊。 我們提出了一種新的圖像配准算法，此算法通過結合我們的局部全通（LAP）彈性配准算法（在亮度變化很小的情況下具有快速、準確的特點）和線性參數擬合方法（對通過LAP得到的形變進行精化）使得圖像形變遵循一個期望模型，並且預測圖像之間的亮度變化。LAP和精化過程不斷迭代，直到穩定為止。 初步結果證明了我們的算法的高準確性和強魯棒性，並且沒有損害算法效率。在此研究計劃中，我們將開發并測試我們的參數化方法，來解決困難的配准問題：要對齊的圖像之間有明顯的亮度變化或重疊區域有限。我們還計劃研究我們的算法對與解決多模態圖像配准問題的有效程度。

14207718.label: Realisation of objectives
14207718.value: Objectives 1, 3 and 5 had already been attained at the time of the midterm report. This resulted in a conference paper (ICIP 2019) and an IEEE TIP journal paper published in 2020. Later (November 14, 2020), the PI was invited to give a keynote speech at the International Conference on Graphics and Image Processing (ICGIP: http://www.icgip.org/icgip20.html) on parametric image registration. Objectives 2 has also been fully attained and resulted in a collaborated IEEE TMI journal paper (grant not acknowledged, unfortunately) on 3D MRI image registration from k-space data (i.e., directly from the raw data acquired by the scanner). More specifically, the PI's german collaborator Dr. Thomas Küstner (University Hospital Tübingen, http://www.midaslab.org/people.html) had the idea of training a neural network to learn the output of our 3D LAP image registration algorithm directly from k-space MRI acquisitions (i.e., multi-slice 2D Fourier transforms of the 3D volume image). The goal was to use the CNN directly on downsampled k-space data (for faster acquisition, reducing motion artifacts substantially), and our collaborator was able demonstrate the robustness of this approach. In addition to the TMI paper, objective 5 can be considered fully attained with an application to eye fundus alignment that was already mentioned in the midterm report. Unfortunately, the paper corresponding to this study has not been submitted yet: the PhD student (Xinxin Zhang) who worked on it has successfully passed her oral defense (June 2020), but has been severely perturbed by the covid pandemics and lost her motivation for this work. The study is available in her thesis document (Chapter 5).

14207718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207718.value: The major finding of the work performed during the project is that a quadratic parametrization of geometric transformations is essentially sufficient to represent most practical distortions with a very good approximation. Of course, the major outcome of the project is to provide a computationally efficient and very accurate approach to identify this quadratic transformation. We have also shown in the TIP paper how it would be possible to go beyond this quadratic model (e.g., using Fourier series expansions, or polynomial splines) at limited increased computational cost. Also, an original contribution of the work done is the definition of two "no reference" metrics (i.e., without the need to know the ground-truth) that characterize the quality of an alignment algorithm: the "salience correlation", which compares the salient features of the aligned images; and, importantly, the "parsimony" of the geometric transformation (i.e., a measure of its simplicity), outlining that an alignment field should be as simple as possible, while still aligning features as closely as possible.

14207718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207718.value: The current version of the algorithm still depends on the Local All-pass (LAP) algorithm which first finds an elastic displacement field, that is then reduced to few parameters. We realized that it is possible to bypass completely the LAP, and this is what a current PhD student is doing. Following the keynote speech at ICGIP 2020, there has been regular requests for the code of our algorithm. In order to make sure that the implementation is foolproof, it is necessary to go through the program very carefully, which unfortunately requires quite some time.

14207718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207718.value: The problem of aligning images is ubiquitous: identification of subtle changes between two satellite images, accurate comparisons between medical scanner images taken at different times (indicating the progress of an illness, or the effect of a therapy), stabilization of shaking videos, panorama images by stitching multiple smaller images, super-resolution from multiple less resolved images etc. We propose a flexible but robust approach to this problem by combining our very efficient (but sensitive to image inaccuracies) elastic alignment algorithm, and a parametric description of the alignment field. We show that this combination makes it possible to align real images (e.g., from mobile phones, or medical scanners) for which intensity variations can be substantially large, or even unrelated (multimodal image alignment). Moreover, the algorithm that we have developed is very efficient, providing an accurate result within a few seconds on a standard desktop computer.

14207918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207918.value: In the presence of market frictions, transacting one class of financial assets to another is usually costly. In addition to the commissions and other types of direct costs that most investors pay on each trade, two kinds of indirect costs, particularly the bid-ask spreads and the market impact costs, have profound implications in investment decisions and asset evaluation. The former one refers to the difference between the price quoted for immediate sale and purchase. It is a transaction cost that investors pay for small-sized trades. Significant amounts of market impact costs will arise when investors try to transact large-sized portfolios within a limited time framework. In the absence of enough liquidity providers presenting in the market at the same time to absorb them, such transactions will often lead to adverse price movements against investors, i.e., upward when buying and downward when selling. Hence prudential investors must carefully choose their investment strategies on the basis of the current risk exposure, expected returns, and transaction costs, as well as the future evolution of all these factors. However, the classical paradigm of financial engineering, including Markowitz’s portfolio theory and Black-Scholes option pricing theory, often ignores the impacts of such transaction costs and thus yields realistically infeasible solutions. As pointed by numerous empirical studies, investors’ concerns on the asset illiquidity also change their evaluation, creating statistically significant deviations in asset pricing from what the classical theory predicts. These motivations pose a challenging research problem about understanding the implications of the dynamic of price impacts to portfolio selection and contingent claim pricing. Nowadays most trading venues of various financial assets converge to the form of electronic limit order books (LOB) and grant investors real-time access to the LOB data. This enables us to gauge the dynamics of price impacts from a microscopic perspective. The proposed research aims to develop a stochastic control based approach, in junction with the LOB modeling, to quantify the effects of the above two indirect costs in portfolio selection and contingent claim pricing. The outcomes will produce quantitative characterizations on the optimal trading strategy, enhancing our understanding of investors behaviors in the presence of market frictions. They also will help us distinguish the risk premium of illiquidity from the risk premium caused by the fundamental risk so that we can acquire new insights into the liquidity-caused systemic risk. New computational tools will be produced from the investigation for liquidity risk management purposes. 在市場摩擦的影響下，金融資產間的交易往往代價高昂。除了大多數交易參與者支付的佣金等直接費用外，兩種間接費用，即買賣價差和市場衝擊成本，也會對投資決策和資產定價產生深刻影響。前者是指完成即刻買賣時的價格差異，它是投資人進行小額交易所支付的成本。而當投資人試圖在有限時間內完成大宗交易時，市場衝擊成本便會顯著的體現出來。如果此時恰好又缺少足夠的流動性提供者吸納這些交易要求，那麼市場上就會出現不利於投資人的價格波動：當他買入時，價格上升；賣出時，價格下跌。因此審慎的投資人必須基於當前的風險敞口，預期收益，交易成本，以及這些因素的未來走勢，仔細權衡他們的交易策略。然而經典的金融工程基本理論，包括著名的Markowitz 投資組合理論和Black-Scholes期權定價理論，卻往往忽視這些重要的因素，從而給出了在實踐上並不可行的方案。無數的實證研究表明，現實市場中交易者對於流動性的關注會改變他們對金融資產的價值判斷，造成金融資產的實際市場價格在統計意義上顯著的背離這些理論的預期。如何刻畫價格衝擊對於投資組合以及資產定價因而成為一個極具現實意義的研究課題。 現今多數金融資產的交易平台實行基於限價訂單簿的電子交易，並且允許交易參與者實時獲取交易數據。這使得我們有可能從微觀角度度量市場摩擦的動態變化。本研究項目通過對訂單簿的建模，建立一套隨機控制的方法，用以定量分析上述兩種間接交易成本對於投資組合以及資產定價的影響。研究成果能夠給出最優交易策略的定量刻畫，增強我們對於在有市場摩擦下的交易人行為的理解。同時，我們也能夠進一步區分由於流動性而引起的風險溢價和由於基本面而引起的風險溢價，從而獲得對流動性產生的系統風險更新的洞見。本研究也會產生出用於流動性風險管理的計算工具。

14207918.label: Realisation of objectives
14207918.value: 1. To fulfil the first research objective, the PI has developed a dynamic model for the market operated with a limit order book (LOB) when he carried out the research supported by this grant. The new model features a block-shaped LOB as the first-order approximation to the real-life market. It consists of four key elements: i) a Bachelier process to capture the dynamics of the security’s fundamental value; ii) the distance between the best bid/ask prices and the fundamental value to capture the instantaneous liquidity provided by the market; iii) the heights of the limit buy and sell orders to capture the market depth; and iv) a finite refill rate to capture the market resilience after a large block of trading. Compared with the existing literature, our model can better reflect the key characteristics of market microstructure, such as the bid-ask spread, transient and permanent price impacts, and market resilience. In addition, the model is highly flexible to accommodate the predictive signals in the dynamics of the security’s fundamental value, which enables us to investigate the important tradeoff between the optimal risk exposure and the transaction costs. In this way, the PI has successfully achieved the first research objective. 2. To fulfil the first research objective, the PI formulated the optimal investment problem based on the above LOB model. In other words, consider a trader who intends to buy and sell with market orders in such a market to maximize her terminal utility. Mathematically, the PI managed to transform this optimization problem into a high-dimensional variational inequality system and to show the existence of the viscosity solutions. Under the assumption of the aforementioned Bachelier process, an explicit solution to the variational inequality system have been obtained. The solution clearly quantifies the tradeoff between the optimal risk exposure and the transaction costs. On the one hand, the trader should maintain her portfolio close to the optimal portfolio in the absence of market illiquidity to catch up with the optimal risk exposure implied by the fundamental value. On the other hand, to avoid the excessive impact costs from too frequent trading activities, the trader should slow down the speed of trading, sometimes even temporarily halt transactions to wait for better trading prices. In this process, the PI finds that the market resilience should play an essential role in the trader’s decision. Hence the PI has successfully achieved the second research objective. 3. To fulfil the third objective, the PI investigated the evaluation of options, one of the most important contingent claims traded in the market. In the presence of limit order books, the market is not complete any more and the classical risk neutral pricing does not work. Hence, the PI took the utility indifference approach to overcome this obstacle. To this end, we need to solve two optimal control problems for option traders, one of which is endowed with the nonlinear payoff function associated with the option. Both problems are difficulty to solve because of the high dimensionality. The PI thus proposed a deep neural network based numerical approach to tackle them. The numerical experiments clearly demonstrate that, in addition to the Black-Scholes type option price based on the fundamental value of the underlying asset, the liquidity premium contributes significantly to the option prices. In this way, the PI has successfully achieved the third research objective.

14207918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207918.value: There are several research outcomes related to this project. One paper (Research output 4 in Part C) has been submitted to Management Science, one of the top journal in the area of financial engineering, based on the findings detailed in Item 5.3 of Part B. In that paper, we develop a dynamic model for limit order books that synergizes three key features of market microstructure: the bid-ask spread, the market depth, and a finite market resilience, and we present an explicit characterization on the trader’s optimal trading strategies. Both the theoretical and numerical results shed managerial insights on how an investor should strike the balance among several competing goals, such as achieving the optimal risk exposure currently, incorporating signals about the future, and minimizing trading costs, in a market of limited liquidity. Before the submission, the major outcomes have been presented orally in several major conferences such as SIAM Conference in Financial Mathematics and Engineering, the World Congress of Bachelier Finance Society, and INFORMS Annual Meeting (Conferences 4, 5, 6 in Part C). Part of the fund was used to support three related researches. The first one is to propose a duality driven learning algorithm to solve stochastic dynamic programming problems. As an important application domain, the algorithm works efficiently for dynamic portfolio selection problems, the main topic of this project. Publication 2 in Part C is based on these results. The paper received a minor revision from Operations Research, the flagship journal in the area, after several rounds of revisions. The second one (Publication 3, Part C) studies the shock propagation effect of financial network in the crises. In it, we develop a robust estimate on systemic capital requirement and thus provides an analytical tool in systemic risk management. We submitted the 2nd round major revision of the paper back to Operations Research. The acceptance likelihood is high according to the comments of the editor. The third output (Publication 1, Part C) investigates the role of market liquidity in the 2015-2016 Chinese Stock Market Turbulence. The outcomes reveal that different market participants may react differently in a crisis, providing new insights about the systemic risk regulation. The paper is under 1st round major revision under Pacific-Basin Finance Journal, one main publication outlet for high quality research on capital markets within the Asia-Pacific region (US market excluded). Three PhD students have (expected) finished their thesis under the grant support.

14207918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207918.value: Market liquidity refers to how easily assets can be bought or sold without inflicting significant transaction costs. Hence, it yields important influences in investors’ trading decisions. In the extreme, a deterioration in market liquidity amplifies price swings, leading to instability for the financial system as shown in the recent financial crises. The research outcomes from this project are of two levels. At the micro level, the PI developed efficient numerical algorithms to solve for optimal trading strategies to incorporate the effects of market illiquidity; at the macro level, the PI constructed robust estimation on the probability of the network caused and liquidity caused systemic defaults, which provides a scientific basis for the regulation on financial systemic risk. In addition, some empirical investigations have been done on the 2015-2016 Chinese Stock Market Turbulence. Adequate evidence from the research points to the essential role of market liquidity in this event, shedding valuable managerial insights onto how to regulate such risks when the liquidity deteriorates. Results from this study contribute fundamental understandings and insights into the liquidity risk, along with practical tools to support the decision making for market participants.
