14208118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208118.value: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disabilities, commonly associated with abnormal muscle coordination and loss of dexterity, particularly in the hand function. Paired associative stimulation (PAS) has recently been shown as potential therapeutic intervention for promoting recovery from brain injury/disease. PAS is a kind of stimulation protocol of originally pairing an electrical stimulus to a peripheral nerve with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over the contralateral primary motor cortex (M1). It is assumed that the effects from the two sources of stimulations could be synchronized at the M1 by adjusting an appropriate latency between the two stimuli over the central and peripheral nervous systems. A novel form of associative stimulation is now proposed by pairing peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) with transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) over the M1. The tACS has the potential to directly induce cortical alternations in intrinsic neural oscillation at specific frequencies, and the brain would mirror the induced frequencies of external source of oscillations to potentially induce synaptic plasticity. However, stroke often encounters a wide variation in lesion profiles and creates critical challenge to apply this PAS technique by finding the appropriate latency and frequency to induce excitability. In this proposal, subject-specific stimulation frequency and latency will be identified. The frequency is using neurophysiological findings by applying TMS stimulation at M1 and then analyzing the brain oscillation activities through electroencephalography(EEG); and the latency is identified by signal processing the latency from stimulus using ascending peripheral nerve stimulation(PNS) to reach the M1 using EEG. With both frequency and latency, we can achieve corresponding neuronal resynchronization to induce cortical excitability in damaged brain. Recently, high-definition tACS (HD-tACS) has emerged to have better spatial focality, greater influence on cortical excitability than conventional tACS. HD-tACS will be applied to evaluate the effects of cortical excitability on stroke subjects. Computational modeling of neuromodulation will be developed to allow a detailed examination of HD-tACS-induced changes in brain cortical excitability and to enable the visualization of how stimulation modulates brain oscillations. A randomized controlled trial will be conducted with three groups of stroke survivors: customized tACS+PNS at subject-specific stimulation frequency and latency; standard tACS+PNS at fixed frequency and latency; and sham stimulation. A 10-session training will be provided to evaluate the neuromodulation effects of the protocols with clinical assessment scores. Neuroimaging(EEG&MRI) and neurophysiological evaluations will be conducted before and after 10-session training and at 3-month follow-up, to investigate stimulation-induced neuroplasticity and hand function recovery. 中風是長期殘疾的主要原因，通常與異常肌肉有關，特別是在手部功能方面。最近已將使用配對關聯刺激（PAS）促進腦損傷恢復。 PAS是一種刺激方案，其最初將電刺激與周圍神經配對，並通過運動皮層（M1）進行經顱磁刺激（TMS）。假設通過中樞和外周神經系統上的兩個刺激源可以在M1處同步。現在通過在M1上將外周神經刺激（PNS）與經顱交流電刺激（tACS）配對來提出一種新形式的關聯刺激。 tACS有可能在特定頻率下直接誘導內在神經振蕩的皮質交替。然而，中風通常會在病變特徵中遇到很大的變化，並且通過找到適當的潛伏期和頻率來誘導興奮性。在該提議中，將識別受試者刺激頻率和潛伏期。頻率是通過在M1應用TMS刺激然後通過腦電圖（EEG）分析;並且通過使用周圍神經刺激（PNS）從EEG到達M1的刺激的延遲信號處理來識別潛伏期。通過頻率和潛伏期，我們可以實現相應的神經元再同步，以在受損腦中誘導皮質興奮性。最近，高密度tACS（HD-tACS）已經出現具有比常規tACS更好的空間焦點，對皮質興奮性的更大影響。 HD-tACS將用於評估皮質興奮性對中風受試者的影響。將開發神經調節的計算模型，以允許詳細檢查HD-tACS誘導的大腦皮質興奮性的變化，並且能夠調節腦振盪。將對三組中風倖存者進行隨機對照試驗：針對受試者刺激頻率和潛伏期的定制tACS + PNS;固定頻率和延遲的標準tACS + PNS;和假刺激。將提供10節培訓，以評估臨床效果。神經影像學（EEG和MRI）和神經生理學評估將在10個療程的訓練之前和之後以及3個月進行，以研究刺激誘導的神經可塑性和手功能康復。

14208118.label: Realisation of objectives
14208118.value: The first objective of the project has been completed and published in IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering. Thirteen chronic stroke subjects, who suffered from their first-ever stroke and had a time since stroke of more than one year, were recruited to participate in concurrent tACS-fMRI experiments. Subjects with a history of epilepsy, serious cognitive deficits, comprehensive aphasia, and/or metal implants were excluded from the study. This was a randomized, single-blinded (subjects), sham-controlled crossover study. Each subject received three stimulation experiments (10 Hz, 20 Hz, and Sham) in a random order, with at least a one-week washout period between sessions to prevent confusion effects. Concurrent tACS and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) were conducted on all 13 chronic stroke individuals. Resting-state and task-based fMRI were collected for each subject under different frequencies (10 Hz, 20 Hz, and Sham). Two tACS electrodes (5 × 5 cm2) were attached to each subject's scalp and fixed with straps. The electrodes were positioned over the ipsilesional M1 (C3/C4) and the contralesional supraorbital ridge (FP1/FP2), respectively. For 10 Hz and 20 Hz tACS, a current of 1 mA (peak-to-peak) was delivered for 20 minutes by an MRI-compatible DC stimulator (NeuroConn GmbH, Ilmenau, Germany) with 30 seconds' ramp-up and 30 seconds' ramp-down. For the sham stimulation, only 30 seconds' ramp-up and 30 seconds' ramp-down were applied. MRI data were acquired using a 3T Philips MR scanner with an 8-channel head coil (Achieva TX, Philips Medical System, Best, Netherlands). T1-weighted anatomical images and blood-oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) fMRI images were collected for each subject. During rs-fMRI acquisition, the participants were instructed to focus on a white fixation cross on a black background. rs-fMRI data were collected before, during, and after tACS, with one 6-minute run before stimulation, three 6-minute runs during stimulation, and one 6-minute run after stimulation. Each 6-minute fMRI run consisted of 180 volumes. During task-based fMRI acquisition, subjects were asked to grasp their hand with maximum force using either their paretic or non-paretic hand when a letter "L" or "R" (indicating left or right hand) was displayed on the screen. They were also instructed to maintain this grip for 6 seconds until the letter disappeared from the screen. The second objective of the research has been completed and published in Brain Sciences. The MRI data from the thirteen chronic stroke subjects in the previous part were used to develop computational models of neuromodulation to understand tACS. In order to investigate the modification of brain functioning induced by tACS located at the lesioned motor area, the whole brain was first parcelled into 116 regions based on Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas to construct the network at the whole brain level, and 20 regions of interest (ROIs) related to motor function were extracted to constitute the nodes of the network in motor-related regions. The mean time series of each ROI was averaged. The temporal correlation matrix for each subject under each condition was obtained by calculating the Pearson correlation coefficients between the time courses of each pair of regions. In graph theory, an adjacency matrix was often adopted to characterize the structure of the graph. In the present study, we would threshold the fMRI temporal correlation matrix to acquire group adjacency matrix as well as individual adjacency matrix for each time point under each stimulation condition. First of all, a Fisher’s r-to-z transform was utilized to map correlation r value to z score value for all individual correlation matrices to improve normality. After constructions of brain networks, several measures that characterize the property of modular organization and nodes were evaluated. All graph theory analysis was conducted while using Brain Connectivity Toolbox that was implemented in MATLAB (The MathWorks Inc., Natick, MA, USA). Based on the community assignment of all nodes, the role of a specific node could be determined with respect to its own community as well as other communities. The within-module degree z-score is a classical measure to characterize how ‘well-connected’ a specific node is to other nodes that belong to the same community. Normally speaking, a high value of within-module z-score indicates dense within-module linking. Some of the nodes might not merely connect with nodes near them within the same community, but also have connections with nodes in other communities. The participation coefficient is used to evaluate such diversity of intermodular interconnection for an individual node. Complementary to within-module degree z-score, the participation coefficient characterizes ‘how-distributed’ the links of a specific node among various communities. For the third objective, we conducted a preliminary randomized controlled trial to evaluate the training effectiveness of subject-specific stimulation. Nineteen chronic stroke survivors were recruited for this study and randomized into a stimulation group and a sham group. We conducted a monocenter, randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomized into a personalized stimulation plus EMG robot hand training group (Stimulation group) or an EMG robot hand training alone group (Control group). Individualized finite element head (FEM) models were generated from subject’s structural T1 and T2 images. Each head model consists of 6 compartments, including the grey matter(GM), white matter(WM), cerebrospinal fluid(CSF), skull, scalp and stroke lesions. Stroke lesions were manually labelled by trained professionals using individual T1 and T2 images To accurately model the brain of stroke subjects, stroke lesions were manually labelled by trained professional, and modelled as CSF in the FEM. Individual stimulation targets were determined using activation map obtained from hand function based fMRI map. The preprocessing and generation of the target map was described in the supplementary materials. The contralesional hemisphere and non motor-related brain region were excluded from the target definition to minimize the effect of stimulation on developing maladaptive plasticity or other neurophysiological factors that impacts the motor recovery. Target map were co-registered onto the individual FEM model. Each subject completed 20 sessions of EMG-driven robot hand training at the local community center. Prior to training, subjects wore the robotic hand and were seated in a comfortable position facing a computer screen. They were instructed to keep their elbow at rest and slightly flexed at approximately 130◦. EMG signals were recorded from the Flexor Digitorum (FD) and Extensor Digitorum (ED) muscles, with reference electrodes placed over the olecranon process of the paretic arm. To measure voluntary motor intention, subjects were instructed to perform maximum voluntary contraction (MVC). EMG signals from the FD and ED muscles were used to trigger robot-assisted hand grasping and opening powered by a linear actuator. Assistance was triggered when the EMG amplitudes of the corresponding muscle exceeded a percentage threshold of their respective MVC amplitudes. Based on individual training performances, a minimum threshold of 10% was set and adjusted as necessary. The EMG amplitudes were displayed on the screen as feedback, and subjects were instructed to continue contracting their muscles until the robot hand movement was completed. The training was divided into three blocks, each lasting 15 minutes, with a 5-minute break in between.

14208118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208118.value: This first part of the study aimed to investigate the effects of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) on chronic stroke patients. tACS is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique that could potentially improve stroke rehabilitation. The study conducted concurrent tACS and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) on 13 chronic stroke individuals. The subjects underwent resting-state and task-based fMRI under different frequencies, including 10 Hz, 20 Hz, and sham. The results showed that tACS had frequency-specific modulation effects in the chronic stroke population. Specifically, 20 Hz tACS enhanced functional interaction between sensorimotor regions and brain regions involved in executive control, while 10 Hz and sham tACS had limited impact on motor-related brain activity. The study's findings provide insight into the neural response process under external current stimulation and offer new perspectives on tACS neuromodulation mechanisms in a lesioned brain. Furthermore, these findings have implications for the design of stimulation protocols for stroke patients. In the second part of this study, we aimed to investigate the frequency-specific stimulation effect of tACS in chronic stroke. Thirteen chronic stroke patients underwent tACS intervention, while resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were collected under various frequencies (sham, 10 Hz and 20 Hz). The graph theoretical analysis indicated that 20 Hz tACS might facilitate local segregation in motor-related regions and global integration at the whole-brain level. However, 10 Hz was only observed to increase the segregation from whole-brain level. Additionally, it is also observed that, for the network in motor-related regions, the nodal clustering characteristic was decreased after 10 Hz tACS, but increased after 20 Hz tACS. Taken together, our results suggested that tACS in various frequencies might induce heterogeneous modulation effects in lesioned brains. Specifically, 20 Hz tACS might induce more modulation effects, especially in motor-related regions, and they have the potential to be applied in rehabilitation therapies to facilitate neuromodulation. In the third part of this study, after receiving personalized transcranial current stimulation montages based on individual fMRI activation maps, the stimulation group demonstrated greater improvement in motor function and neuromuscular control compared to the Control group. This was indicated by significant improvements in clinical function score (FMAUE), co-contraction between flexor digitorum (FD) and extensor digitorum during opening hand (P = 0.02), involuntary muscle activation of FD during opening hand (P = 0.027), and CMC value of FD during opening hand. In conclusion, personalized multisite stimulation has therapeutic potential for post-stroke upper extremity motor rehabilitation.

Firstly, the study could be expanded to include a larger sample size to increase the statistical power of the results and improve generalizability. Additionally, the optimized tACS therapy developed through this research can be applied to other neurological conditions beyond stroke such as traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease. Furthermore, the study could be extended to investigate the effects of different stimulation frequencies and intensities on stroke patients. This would help to determine the optimal parameters for tACS therapy in stroke patients and may provide insights into personalized treatment approaches. Another area for future research is the exploration of combined treatment approaches, such as pairing tACS with other rehabilitation intervention (e.g. rehabilitation robotics). Overall, the proposed course of action offers promising avenues for research that could significantly improve our understanding of tACS therapy in stroke patients and ultimately lead to the development of more effective treatment approaches for stroke and other neurological conditions.

14208118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208118.value: This research project explored the potential of a non-invasive brain stimulation technique called tACS to improve brain function in stroke patients. Researchers used brain scans and computer models to investigate how tACS affects brain activity and developed customized treatment plans for individual patients. They also combined tACS with robot-assisted hand training to help stroke patients regain motor function more quickly. Overall, the study showed that tACS has promising potential as a therapy for stroke patients and could lead to improved outcomes for those recovering from this condition.

14208318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208318.value: Graph analytics has received much attention thanks to the proliferation of graph data in a wide range of application domains today. Subgraph-centric problems (e.g., subgraph mining, subgraph matching, clique/triangle listing or counting, graph clustering, community detection) form a very important class of problems for effective graph analytics. However, scalable solutions for subgraph-centric problems, especially for processing massive graphs in today's applications, are severely lacking since existing studies mainly focused on sequential algorithms. Many graph systems have been proposed in recent years, which allow scalable graph algorithms to be implemented under a unified programming framework. Unfortunately, existing graph systems are mainly designed for implementing vertex-centric algorithms (e.g., PageRank, BFS, connected components) that have linear computational complexity, while algorithms for subgraph-centric problems normally have much higher complexity and cannot scale with existing vertex-centric graph systems. This project proposes to design and develop an efficient distributed framework for solving subgraph-centric problems. We identify the key design criteria for building an efficient and scalable system for subgraph-centric problems, and propose a unified programming framework to allow a wide range of subgraph-centric algorithms to be easily implemented. With the proposed system, we will also build a library of subgraph-centric algorithms for graph analytics in real-world applications. 近年來，由圖模型構成的資料在各個領域中廣泛增長，大規模圖分析技術因此受到了越來越多的關注。以子圖為中心的圖計算問題（例如，子圖匹配，子團/三角形計數/枚舉，子圖聚類，社區發現，等等）已經演化成為了圖分析領域的重要分支之一。然而，該領域目前的研究方向仍然著重於對挖掘演算法的有效性提高上，對於如何在超大規模圖資料上並行化、可擴展化這一類演算法依然缺乏關注，當前無論是工業界還是學術界都沒有一套高效、可靠的分散式方案存在。雖然許多已經被提出的分散式圖計算框架/系統可使得其某一類圖計算問題可以被統一的程式設計介面所實現，但這些系統所服務的圖計算問題主要是以點為中心的（例如，PageRank，廣度優先遍歷，聯通分支計算），其演算法複雜度低（線性）。與之對應地，以子圖為中心的圖計算問題往往具有更高的演算法複雜度，也很難在當前眾多服務於以點為中心的圖計算問題的分散式系統上做到並行和擴展化。 在這個專案中，我們將設計、開發一套高效的分散式圖計算框架以服務於這類以子圖為中心的圖計算問題。具體地，我們調研並總結出了這類圖計算問題的共性和針對於其的分散式系統設計關鍵，提出了一套通用的程式設計介面以使得眾多屬於此類型的圖演算法可以得到輕鬆實現。除此以外，我們也將基於這個系統開發出一套以子圖為中心的圖計算應用場景演算法庫，以服務於大圖挖掘/分析技術在真實世界中的應用。

14208718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208718.value: Voice biometrics is among the most natural, non-intrusive and convenient means of identity authentication. Hence, speaker verification (SV) technology contributes significantly towards security in human-centric user interfaces. Rapid technological advancements, accelerated by the pervasive use of mobile devices, especially smartphones, has brought voice biometric authentication into common, everyday use. Examples include call centers, phone-banking, device unlocking, etc. Previous studies in SV primarily focus on discrimination between enrolled target speakers and imposters. However, remarkable progress made in several key technologies has enabled sophisticated deception that induces false acceptance of the imposter’s spoofed speech by the SV system. The four major types of spoofing techniques are: (i) impersonation, where the imposter mimics the target speaker; (ii) replay – where pre-recorded speech is presented for identity verification; (iii) text-to-speech synthesis (TTS) – where synthetic speech generated from input text incorporates the target speaker’s characteristics; and (iv) voice conversion, where an imposter’s speech input is converted to sound like the target speaker’s. Research on the vulnerabilities of SV technologies towards different spoofing techniques is nascent. Impersonation may not easily confuse machine perception unless the imposter’s voice is very similar to the target speaker’s. Replay is difficult because the spoofed speech and genuine speech have the same voice characteristics, and so countermeasures need to rely on channel differences between the signals. The effectiveness of TTS and VC as spoofing technologies have yet to be fully investigated, but recent technological advancements can generate very high quality synthetic and converted speech outputs that pose a real security threat to SV systems. It is therefore critical to develop effective anti-spoofing techniques as countermeasures. The countermeasures need to competently discriminate between genuine speech and spoofed speech, and may rely on signal artefacts introduced by the spoofing techniques and algorithms, be it TTS, VC or others. If the countermeasure can leverage prior knowledge of the spoofing technique, then we are faced with a “known attack”. Contrarily, if the spoofing technique is unseen previously, we are faced with an “unknown attack”. Studies have indicated that performance levels of countermeasures to spoofing can drastically degrade from known to unknown attacks. We propose to investigate the vulnerabilities of SV systems towards spoofing by various TTS and VC techniques, and to develop effective countermeasures that can generalize across known and unknown spoofing attacks. Generalized countermeasures can reinforce SV systems and uphold security protection in a diversity of real-world applications that use voice biometric authentication.

14208718.label: Realisation of objectives
14208718.value: Objective 1: Initiate Anti-spoofing Investigation We investigated anti-spoofing based on the ASVspoof 2019 challenge, where high-performance spoofing countermeasure systems for automatic speaker verification (ASV) were proposed. However, robustness of such systems under adversarial attacks has not previously been studied yet. More specifically, we investigated the vulnerability of spoofing countermeasures for ASV under both white-box and black-box adversarial attacks with the fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and the projected gradient descent (PGD) method. We implemented high-performing countermeasure models in the ASVspoof 2019 challenge and conducted adversarial attacks on them. We compared performance of black-box attacks across spoofing countermeasure models with different network architectures and different amount of model parameters. The experimental results show that all implemented countermeasure models are vulnerable to FGSM and PGD attacks under the scenario of white-box attack. The more dangerous black-box attacks also prove to be effective by the experimental results. Objective 2: Comparative Study of Spoofing Techniques and Countermeasures Performance We investigated spoofing detection performance across different countermeasures. We analysed performance degradations observed as one migrates from known attacks to unknown attacks. We investigated adversarial speech to spoof ASV systems in terms of the vulnerability of Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) i-vector based speaker verification systems, and the transferability of adversarial samples crafted from GMM i-vector based systems to x-vector based systems. More specifically, we formulated the GMM i-vector system as a scoring function of enrolment and testing utterance pairs. Then we leveraged the fast gradient sign method (FGSM) to optimize testing utterances for adversarial samples generation. These adversarial samples are used to attack both GMM ivector and x-vector systems. We measure the system vulnerability by the degradation of equal error rate and false acceptance rate. Experiment results show that GMM i-vector systems are seriously vulnerable to adversarial attacks, and the crafted adversarial samples prove to be transferable and pose threats to neural network speaker embedding based systems (e.g. x-vector systems). Another point is that speaker verification systems usually suffer from the mismatch problem between the training and evaluation data, such as the speaker-identity set mismatch, the channel and environment variations. In order to address this issue, the system must have good generalization ability on unseen data. Hence, we incorporated Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) into the DNN x-vector speaker verification system to improve the system’s generalization ability. With the weight uncertainty modelling provided by BNNs, we expect the system could generalize better on the evaluation data and make verification decisions more accurately. Our experiment results indicate that the DNN x-vector system could benefit from BNNs especially when the mismatch problem is severe in out-of-domain evaluation. Specifically, results show that the system could benefit from BNNs by a relative EER decrease of 2.66% and 2.32% respectively for short- and long-utterance in-domain evaluation. Additionally, the fusion of DNN x-vector and Bayesian x-vector systems could achieve further improvement. Moreover, the evaluation conducted with a larger mismatch, suggested that BNNs could bring a more relative EER decrease of over 4.5%. Objective 3: Deep Learning Generalized Countermeasures in Spoofing We also investigate methods of defense against adversarial attacks on spoofing countermeasures of ASV. Various forefront countermeasure methods for automatic speaker verification (ASV) with considerable performance in anti-spoofing are proposed in recent years. However, previous work has shown that countermeasure models are vulnerable to adversarial examples indistinguishable from natural data. A good countermeasure model should not only be robust against spoofing audio, including synthetic, converted, and replayed audios; but counteract deliberately generated examples by malicious adversaries. We introduced a passive defense method, spatial smoothing, and a proactive defense method, adversarial training, to mitigate the vulnerability of ASV spoofing countermeasure models against adversarial examples. Our work is among the first to use defense methods to improve the robustness of ASV spoofing countermeasure models under adversarial attacks. The experimental results show that these two defense methods positively help spoofing countermeasure models counter adversarial examples. We further investigated using self-supervised learning models for adversarial defense for ASV, to guard against increasingly malicious attackers who attempt to launch adversarial attacks at ASV systems. Our work is among the first to perform adversarial defense for ASV without knowing the specific attack algorithms. Inspired by self-supervised learning models (SSLMs) that possess the merits of alleviating the superficial noise in the inputs and reconstructing clean samples from the interrupted ones, this work regards adversarial perturbations as one kind of noise and conducts adversarial defense for ASV by SSLMs. Specifically, we proposed to perform adversarial defense from two perspectives: 1) adversarial perturbation purification and 2) adversarial perturbation detection. The purification module aims at alleviating the adversarial perturbations in the samples and pulling the contaminated adversarial inputs back towards the decision boundary. Experimental results show that our proposed purification module effectively counters adversarial attacks and outperforms traditional filters from both alleviating the adversarial noise and maintaining the performance of genuine samples. The detection module aims at detecting adversarial samples from genuine ones based on the statistical properties of ASV scores derived by a unique ASV integrating with different number of SSLMs. Experimental results show that our detection module helps shield the ASV by detecting adversarial samples. Both purification and detection methods are helpful for defending against different kinds of attack algorithms. Moreover, since there is no common metric for evaluating the ASV performance under adversarial attacks, our work also formalizes evaluation metrics for adversarial defense considering both purification and detection based approaches into account.

14208718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208718.value: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) technology contributes significantly towards security in human-centric user interfaces. However, it has been shown that recent technological progress has enabled sophisticated deception that leads to false acceptance of an imposter’s spoofed speech by the ASV system. This project is among the first to investigate the robustness of high-performance spoofing countermeasure for ASV under adversarial attacks. We investigated both white-box and black-box adversarial attacks with the fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and the projected gradient descent (PGD) method. The experimental results show that all implemented countermeasure models are vulnerable to FGSM and PGD attacks [Liu et al. ASRU 2019 in Part C, Section 9, Item 1]. We further investigated the vulnerability of GMM i-vector systems to adversarial attacks and the adversarial transferability from the i-vector systems to x-vector systems. Experimental results show that the GMM i-vector systems are vulnerable to both white and black box attacks and the generated adversarial samples also prove to be transferable to neural network speaker embedding based systems [Li et al. ICASSP2020 in Part C, Section 9, Item 2]. As ASV systems usually suffer from mismatch between training and evaluation system, such as speaker population, channel and environmental mismatch. We incorporated Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) into the deep neural network x-vector system, which showed performance benefits in face of the mismatch problem [Li et al. Speech Odyssey 2020 in Part C, Section 9, Item 4]. Next, we investigate methods of defense to improve the robustness of ASV spoofing countermeasure models under adversarial attacks, which is among the first studies of its kind. We introduced a passive defense method, spatial smoothing, and a proactive defense method, adversarial training, to mitigate the vulnerability of ASV spoofing countermeasure models against adversarial examples. Experimental results show that both methods positively help spoofing countermeasure models counter adversarial examples [Wu, Liu et al. ICASSP 2020 in Part C, Section 9, Item 3]. We are also among the first to investigate self-supervised learning models for adversarial defense for ASV. We proposed to perform adversarial defense from two perspectives: 1) adversarial perturbation purification and 2) adversarial perturbation detection, together with formalized evaluation metrics. Experimental results show that both purification and detection methods are helpful for defending against different kinds of attack algorithms [Wu, Li et al. ICASSP 2021 and TASLP 2021 listed respectively in Part C, Section 9, Item 5, and Section 8, Item 1].

14208818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208818.value: 本項目旨在提升人們對計算機系統中模擬組件安全性的理解，進而能夠更好的增強系統安全性，防禦潛在的威脅。除了中央處理器等數字組件之外，計算機系統中通常會包含非數字模塊，比如LCD顯示屏、麥克風、揚聲器等，而這些非數字模塊對於系統安全性的影響則通常被人們所忽略。本項目擬通過一系列的實例研究，深入理解非數字模塊在系統安全方面的影響，總結其中的內在規律，並研究它們在系統安全攻擊與防禦方面的潛在應用。本項目是首次對該類問題進行系統化研究，對於提升計算機系統的安全性有着積極的作用。

14208818.label: Realisation of objectives
14208818.value: * Realization of Objective 1: Our first object is to perform real world case studies on the security implications of non-digital components. We have completed this objective. (1)We first studied the non-digital features of screens on mobile devices. We investigated the characteristics of screens of mobile devices, including the LCD and AMOLED screens. Both of these two screen types work in analog domain and are non-digital components. Our studies showed that the brightness of these screens actually not uniform, even though it is expected to be evenly bright at every pixel. We developed an algorithm to calculate the brightness of each pixel, then draw a contour line by connecting all pixels with equal brightness. It turns out that every mobile's screen will have different shapes of contour lines, even for two mobiles with the same brand and screen model. This study has approved that fingerprints can be generated from the screens of mobile devices by using its physical characteristics. We also extended this work and investigated the possible applications of such screen fingerprints in the context of mobile payment, i.e., use such fingerprints as an extra authentication factor. This work was related to the publication "Be aware of Your Screen: Anonymous Fingerprint of Device Screens for Off-line Payment Protection". (2) We also studied the Bluetooth in the real-world settings. We have built devices to sniff Bluetooth traffic, inspected the wave forms in the analog domain, hoping to find some features in the non-digital domains and further extend it to security applications. Unfortunately, due to the Frequency hopping of Bluetooth protocol at physical layer and bandwidth limitation of our existing equipment, we could not capture the signal of the whole communication process in the analog domain. So we give up our original plan and switch to perform security analysis in the digital domain for the Bluetooth protocol. This decision later turns out to be correct because we indeed found some weakness in existing Bluetooth protocol: a Bluetooth device, during the connection (pairing) phase, needs to declare its device type (i.e. profile) and get an explicit approval from device owner, however, the protocol did not forbidden a malicious Bluetooth device to change its profile in future connections after having been paired successfully. Such a loophole in the Bluetooth protocol can lead to dangerous attacks, including private data leakage, or even complete control of victim’s device. This work was published in paper “BadBluetooth: Breaking Android Security Mechanisms via Malicious Bluetooth Peripherals” on NDSS, one of the top conferences in security area. * Realization of Objective 2 In objective 2, we planned to explore the possible characteristics of non-digital components in conventional computing systems. Towards this objective, we studied several different types of the system and try to understand the possible non-digital characteristics. (1) We explored the technique to generate high quality random numbers using data from sensors, which is the other case study stated in our proposal. Currently, we have developed an Android app that can collect data from several sensors like accelerometer, gyroscope, ambient light sensor, and magnetic sensor, etc. We found that there are some correlations among the data from different sensors, which means the numbers generated from a single source sensor, as was proposed in previous studies, may not be secure enough. Now we are studying the method to see if we could remove the common and correlated data from two or more sensors, and hopefully we could come up with a new algorithm that can output better random numbers from those data residues. (2) As an extension to above work, we investigated the randomness feature inside Integrated Circuit (IC), and how to use such kind of non-digital features to construct a secure PUF (Physical Unclonable Function). Due to the manufacturing imperfections, every IC chip will always have something different from the others, and such kind of randomness is unique to each chip, thus is called "unclonable". We studied how to exploit such analog (non-digital) characteristics to build a secure PUF, especially under the attack of machine learning techniques. We designed a new architecture called "FLAM-PUF" which combined the unique feature of each chip as well as the Galois LFSR structure to mix and hide original PUF information but at the same time can generate correct response. According to our test, such a new architecture is much stronger in terms of existing machine-learning based attacks. This work was published in paper "FLAM-PUF: A Response–Feedback-Based Lightweight Anti-Machine-Learning-Attack PUF", and it was nominated as the runner-up award for the best-paper award. (3) We also studied the smart meters and investigated the possible non-digital features inside them. We found that: smart meters circuit contains many analog components, including the capacitors, resistors, and inductors. Due to the manufacturing, such basic components may not be identical, e.g., 1K ohm resistors may not always be 1K ohm exactly. Such kind of variations lead to the different pulse responses of each smart meters. Our studies shows that it is possible to generate hardware fingerprints for each smart meters so that we are able to recognize each smart meter. This technique may have several security applications. For example, it can be used to detect modifications smart meters, and use of illegal smart meters, and then find electricity theft or other improper uses of electricity. Part of this research work was published in paper "Hidden Electricity Theft by Exploiting Multiple-Pricing Scheme in Smart Grids".

14208818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208818.value: As we previously expected in the project proposal, it is inevitable for many existing computing systems to include some non-digital components, and such non-digital components may have important security implications, either for attacks or defenses. (1) We found that the screens of mobile devices are not perfectly manufactures, so its brightness of each screen is not uniformly distributed across pixels. By drawing a contour line of equal brightness, we found that each screen will have its unique shape of such contour lines. Such a unique feature of screens can be used as an extra authentication factor to enhance the security many applications like mobile payment, etc. Please refer to paper "Be aware of Your Screen: Anonymous Fingerprint of Device Screens for Off-line Payment Protection" in Part C for more details. (2) We found that the imperfection of IC (Integrated Circuit) chips at the physical (i.e., non-digital) layer also have big security implications. Our research showed that it is possible to construct a PUF (Physical Unclonable Function) for device authentication. Since the raw PUF function built directly on such non-digital features can be easily defeated by machine learning algorithms (mainly due to the limited entropy from the manufacturing imperfections), we further proposed a new PUF architecture called "FLAM-PUF" that are more robust to various attacks. This work was published in paper "FLAM-PUF: A Response–Feedback-Based Lightweight Anti-Machine-Learning-Attack PUF", and it was nominated as the runner-up award for the best-paper award. (3) We found existing smart meters could be exploited, and the non-digital feature of smart meters (at the basic circuit components level) can be used to generate hardware fingerprints to authentication smart meters. The fundamental idea comes from the variations of electronic components (such as resistors, capacitors, inductors, etc.) due to the manufacturing process. Normally, such variations are acceptable due to the budget when designing the circuit, however, in our studies, we showed that it can also be used to enhance the security of smart meters and smart grid. Part of this research work was published in paper "Hidden Electricity Theft by Exploiting Multiple-Pricing Scheme in Smart Grids". (4) Finally, we also investigated the non-digital properties of Bluetooth, but we found that it hard to extract useful information due to limited capacity of equipment. We then extend the research and found some security loops inside the Bluetooth protocol. This work was published in paper “BadBluetooth: Breaking Android Security Mechanisms via Malicious Bluetooth Peripherals”.

14208818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208818.value: There are several possible future developments along this line. (1) Random number generator. Random numbers have important security impacts, especially for IoT devices, where the entropy sources are very limited. It should be possible to exploit the environment variations in terms of sound, lights, temperature, etc. to collect entropy and generate strong random numbers. (2) Build strong authentication protocols based on information from existing non-digital information sources. We have explored the idea of using screens on mobile devices to generate fingerprints and to enhance the authentication process. There are many other works can be done along this directions too.

14208818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208818.value: It is a common sense that computers are based on digital technologies. However, a computer system may also contain non-digital components to interact with users and other devices. In this project, we studied the security implications of these non-digital components. We found that those non-digital components may have huge impacts on computer system security. On one hand, when designed improperly, a non-digital component could be exploited to by attackers (e.g., to steal victim's private data). On the other hand, such non-digital components can also be used to enhance system security (e.g., be used as an extra authentication factor). The biggest contribution of this project is pointing the non-digital components out as a new attacking surface that was previously unknown. Our work may attract many new follow-up works toward this direction to better protect the general public by fortifying the computing systems used in our daily works and lives.

14209018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209018.value: This proposal aims to develop a high throughput laser nanofabrication method based on two-photon polymerization using a digital micromirror device (DMD). To achieve the goal, multiple focal points from a single femtosecond laser will be generated, controlled, and engineered individually to realize high-precision 3-D parallel fabrication via computer generated holograms. As the holograms programmed to the DMD can be rapidly updated at a speed up to 32.5 kHz, high-speed multi-focus arbitrary scanning can be realized, achieving high precision and high-throughput additive manufacturing. Two-photon polymerization is an important additive manufacturing method that is typically performed via raster-scanning the focus of a femtosecond laser in photoresists, thereby inducing a nonlinear absorption process to polymerize submicron features as nanoscale building blocks. Although it enables nanoscale features to be additively created, the processing rate is limited by the point-by-point and layer-by-later serial scanning procedure. While parallel processing methods have been proposed, e.g., microlens array or spatial light modulator, they are often limited to fabricating periodic structures or have compromised resolution. Accordingly, there is a compelling need to develop new fabrication methods with improved throughput and flexibility without compromising the fabrication resolution. To realize high precision and high-throughput two-photon polymerization, we propose to develop a multi-focus DMD random-access scanner based on binary holography. Specifically, the DMD will be used as a programmable binary mask, coded with holograms, to modulate the incident femtosecond laser wavefront. 3-D scanning can be achieved by using holographic patterns of spherical wavefronts with adjusted tilted phases. To enhance the scanning resolution, holograms for wavefront correction will be designed and superposed to the scanning holograms, realizing simultaneous arbitrary beam shaping and 3-D laser scanning via a single DMD. By combining the individual focal points via superposition, multi-focus random-access scanning can be achieved. Multi-focus scanning trajectory will be optimized. Parametric models will be developed to deterministically link the system performance to DMD parameters. Fabrication experiments will be designed and performed to validate the predicted results. The result of this work will substantially improve the throughput and resolution of two-photon polymerization processes, enabling multi-focus 3-D additive manufacturing with high resolution. The random-access scanner has tremendous advantages for fabricating complex structures, e.g., octet truss, as the fabrication time will only be proportional to the total solid volume regardless of the structure complexity. The new system may fabricate large-scale devices at a much lower cost and improved rate, generating impact in the nanomanufacturing industry. 本項目旨在開發基於使用數字微鏡器件（DMD）的雙光子聚合的高通量激光納米製造方法。為了實現這一目標，將單獨生成，控制和設計來自單個飛秒激光器的多個焦點，以通過計算機生成的全息圖實現高精度3-D並行製造。由於編程到DMD的全息圖可以以高達32.5 kHz的速度快速更新，因此可以實現高速多焦點任意掃描，實現高精度和高通量的增材製造。 雙光子聚合是一種重要的增材製造方法，通常通過線掃描飛秒激光在光刻膠中的焦點來進行，從而引發非線性吸收過程以聚合亞微米特徵作為納米級構建塊。雖然它可以附加地創建納米級特徵，但是處理速率受到逐點和逐層串行掃描過程的限制。雖然已經提出了並行處理方法，例如微透鏡陣列或空間光調製器，但它們通常限於製造週期性結構或具有受損的分辨率。因此，迫切需要開發具有改進的生產量和靈活性的新製造方法而不損害製造分辨率。 為了實現高精度和高通量的雙光子聚合，我們提出開發基於二元全息術的多焦點DMD隨機存取掃描儀。具體而言，DMD將用作可編程二進制掩模，用全息圖編碼，以調製入射飛秒激光波前。通過使用具有調整的傾斜相位的球面波前的全息圖案可以實現3-D掃描。為了提高掃描分辨率，將設計用於波前校正的全息圖並疊加到掃描全息圖上，通過單個DMD實現同時任意光束整形和3-D激光掃描。通過疊加組合各個焦點，可以實現多焦點隨機訪問掃描。將優化多焦點掃描軌跡。將開發參數模型以確定性地將系統性能與DMD參數相關聯。將設計並執行製造實驗以驗證預測結果。 這項工作的結果將提高雙光子聚合工藝的產量和分辨率，實現高分辨率的多焦點3-D增材製造。隨機存取掃描器對於製造複雜結構（例如八位組桁架）具有巨大優勢，因為無論結構複雜性如何，製造時間將僅與總固體體積成比例。新系統可以以低得多的成本和提高的速率製造大型設備，從而在納米製造業中產生影響。

14209018.label: Realisation of objectives
14209018.value: All research objectives have been fully achieved within the project duration. Specifically, we have developed a multi-focus random-access DMD scanner based on a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography; the DMD scanner can operate at the DMD pattern rate (22.7 kHz); each hologram contains the location, amplitude, and phase of the designed laser foci (up to hundreds of laser foci can be described in a single hologram without compromising the quality of the point spread function). Thus, by sequentially displaying the synthesized holograms on the DMD, the laser foci will perform multi-focus scanning at the DMD pattern rate. We have developed parametric models to deterministically link the system performance (i.e., resolution, range, and number of focal points) and the DMD parameters (i.e., number of pixels, pixel size, and aperture), which precisely predicts the minimum step size, maximum scanning range in different axes, and the point spread function at different depths. (See details in Research Output #2). We have also developed parametric models and control methods to precisely control the intensity of each scanning focus; the discrete sampling errors associated with the DMD and large number of focal points have been investigated via both accurate parametric model and experimental characterization. (See details in Research Output #7). Lastly, models and algorithms to perform wavefront correction, simultaneous beam shaping, and 3-D scanning using a single DMD have been developed; experiments with optimal multi-focus scanning paths have been performed to verify the effectiveness of the methods to improve the fabrication results. (See details in Research Output #4, #6 and #7).

14209018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209018.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a multi-focus random-access scanner for two-photon polymerization (TPP) based on a digital micromirror device (DMD) and binary holography. Specifically, the DMD is used as a programmable binary mask, coded with holograms, to modulate the incident femtosecond laser wavefront. Accordingly, we achieved 3D random-access scanning by rapidly displaying custom-synthesized holographic patterns, where holograms of spherical wavefronts and tilted phases respectively control to axial and lateral positions of a laser focus. Multi-focus scanning is realized by superposing holograms containing individual laser focus (Research Output #2). To enhance the fabrication resolution, holograms for wavefront correction is designed and superposed to the scanning holograms, realizing simultaneous arbitrary beam shaping and 3-D laser scanning via a single DMD. (Research Output #4 & #6) We have also developed parametric models to deterministically link the system parameters (pixel size, aperture, laser parameters) to the performance of the DMD scanner (minimal step size in different directions, work volume, errors induced by the discrete wavefront sampling processes etc.), the results are reported in (Research Output #7). The result of this work has substantially improved the throughput and resolution of TPP processes, enabling multi-focus 3D additive manufacturing with high resolution. The random-access scanner has tremendous advantages for fabricating complex structures, e.g., octet truss, as the fabrication time will only be proportional to the total solid volume regardless of the structure complexity. The new system may fabricate large-scale devices at a much lower cost and improved rate, generating impact in the nanomanufacturing industry. In terms of impact, two US patents have been awarded to protect the DMD-based laser scanning technology (Research Output Patent #2 and #3). The patents have been licensed to Precision Instruments and Optics Limited for technology transfer; and the first DMD-based TPP 3D printed was made commercially available in 2020. In parallel, inspired by the concept of temporal focusing, we have developed a projection-based two-photon polymerization system based on DMD for fast 3D nanofabrication, achieving record-breaking speed and resolution. The results have been published in Science (Research Output #1). By applying binary hologram-based multi-focus scanning, our team has constructed a random-access pump-probe microscopy, achieving highly flexible ultrafast spectroscopy (Research Output #4). With the project fund support, we have published two review papers about emerging micro-additive manufacturing methods as well as the design and manufacturing of flexible pressure sensors (Research Output #3 & #5).

14209018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209018.value: In this study, the number of laser focus is limited by the laser power, which is around 10 foci. If a regenerative laser amplifier is applied to the DMD-scanner, we can practically generate up to 4,000 laser foci for parallel processing, where the position, amplitude and phase of each focus can be individually controlled, i.e., fabrication rate increases 100 times. In our preliminary experiments, we have proved the idea works and the resolution will not be compromised when less than 400 laser foci are used. Owning to the ultrahigh laser peak power of the laser amplifier, we also found new kinetics of the TPP process, which enables the best resolution to be written within the least exposure time. A GRF proposal based on this idea was award in 2021. (?Development and Mechanistic Study of Multi-focus Two-photon Lithography based on Dual-comb Spectroscopy,? CUHK 14209421, 8/2021 - 7/2024.)

The result of this work has substantially improved the throughput and resolution of TPP processes. Notably, the random-access DMD scanner has tremendous advantages for fabricating complex structures, e.g., octet truss, as the fabrication time is only proportional to the total solid volume regardless of the structure complexity. 14209118.label: Realisation of objectives
14209118.value: For Aim 1, the PI and his collaborators have developed a novel compliant, articulated, and adjustable robotic retractor with force sensing capability. Its tip was based on the buckling principle of a Nitinol beam that can provide inherent compliance to minimize inadvertent tissue damage. To enable articulation for dexterity, an articulated wristed mechanism consisting of two rolling gears and a “dumbbell” structure was developed. It can prevent any transverse and axial split of the contact to ensure high torsional stiffness and large holding force. Adjustability is required for surgical needs. A telescopic and push-pull rod was designed to adjust the expansion of the retraction tip surface. When pulling the rod backward, the retractor would be folded to its collapsed state, allowing it insert through a cannula. Once it reaches the surgical site, the rod would move forward to expand the retraction. To provide safe robot-organ interaction, identifying the contact point and estimating the contact force are crucial. FBG-based sensors were integrated into the retractor tip with optimized geometry and dimensions. After processing the signals from FBGs, encoders, and motor currents, the interaction force information can be estimated. For Aim 2, the PI and his collaborators have developed the control framework to support the semi-automatic hybrid position/force control, including low-level multi-tendon actuator control and high-level “model-less” organ manipulation scheme. For the designed coupled multi-tendon-driven retractor, the torque disturbance at one of the distal joints can “spill” over to other joints at the steady state, resulting in potential instability. Instead of tuning the controller gains individually, a scheme of searching a diagonal scaling matrix was designed and such a matrix can guarantee the stability of the coupled low-level tendon-actuator control. To alleviate the burdens of physicians from prolonged usage of the retractor, a high-level semi-autonomous organ manipulation scheme was created. Specifically, a hybrid position/force optimal control formulation was designed based on the feedback from camera images. It does not require a priori knowledge of the deformation object and can also manage the interaction force and organ manipulation simultaneously. For Aim 3, the overall system performance has been evaluated from a clinical perspective. The system has been integrated into the dVRK robot and clinical evaluation, force sensing, and semi-autonomous control have been conducted. During this work, to reduce the effect the gravity on the dVRK master, a reliable gravity compensation control strategy for dVRK has been developed. This by-product work has been developed into an open-source software package and published in the dVRK community. The overall system has also been evaluated with the human phantom. The user simulated the organ (a kidney silicon phantom) retraction process. The results demonstrated the effectiveness and reliability of the overall system.

14209118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209118.value: This research enables us to investigate the development of safe and reliable surgical instruments, especially a common yet important organ retraction. Different from existing manual and rigid robotic retractors, a compliant, articulated, and adjustable robotic retractor with force sensing and semi-autonomous manipulation capabilities has been developed. This instrument has been integrated into the dVRK platform and evaluated with the manipulation of the human phantom. While integrating the retractor into the dVRK robot, analytical and learning-based gravity compensation algorithms have been developed to reduce the gravity effect while manipulating the master device (see the papers: Hongbin Lin et al., 2019 [RAL journal paper] and Hongbin Lin et al., 2021 [RAL journal paper]). While developing visual-based semi-autonomous manipulation control, a non-fixed contact manipulation control framework for deformable objects with active contact adjustment has been proposed (see the paper: Jing Huang et al., 2021[RAL journal paper]). While designing low-level controllers for coupled mechanical systems, two papers on control design for classical mechanical systems subject to coupling were published (see Xiangyu Chu et al., 2020 [ACC conference paper] and Xiangyu Chu et al., 2021 [ICRA conference paper]).

14209118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209118.value: Although the main goal of developing an organ retractor has been achieved, there are still some potentials: 1) The payload of the retractor can be further increased. To increase the dexterity, an articulated wristed joint was used, but this also limits the overall payload. Optimizing the joint parameters or developing a new joint with different structures would help improve the torsional stiffness, thus reinforcing the overall payload. 2) The speed of interaction force estimation algorithms can be further improved. The numerical iterative estimation algorithm was used, but it was applied to a series of segments and the inverse problem of the analytical model needs to be solved. 3) The low-level multi-tendon actuator control can be further improved. The scaling matrix was assumed to be diagonal for the easy formulation, but this may constrain the search of an optimal scaling matrix. A potential way is to release the assumption and use non-convex optimization methods considering the rapid development of numerical solvers. 4) The application scenarios can be more versatile. The proposed organ retractor has built up a systematic design process for surgical instrument development from the perspectives of safety, dexterity, and usability. In the future, the retractor can be adapted to many different applications. For example, its tip can be replaced by other end-effectors like drills. Although the additional design is required, the overall framework can be followed.

14209118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209118.value: This research was motivated by the previous rigid and manual instruments for organ manipulation. To advance this technology, a compliant, articulated, and adjustable robotic retractor with force sensing and semi-autonomous manipulation capabilities has been developed. This allows users to manipulate organs easily and safely, leading to safer and more comfortable operations in minimally invasive surgery. Besides the device itself, this research project also inspires instrument development in terms of safety, dexterity, and usability. For example, the instrument for other purposes like drilling can be designed by following the overall framework of this research project and even re-using some components like the articulated wrist joint with high torsional stiffness.

14209818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209818.value: We propose to investigate two complexity questions regarding conic optimization algorithms: (1) Recently a few new randomized optimization algorithms have appeared, such as Gram--Schmidt walk of Bansal et al and subdeterminant maximization algorithm of Ebrahimi et al. Can these algorithms be derandomized? How to derandomize similar approximation algorithms systematically? (2) Can combinatorial methods prove new upper and lower bounds of conic optimization algorithms? Lower bounds of general linear or semidefinite programs, known as extended formulations, are known for a few problems, and the proof do not reflect the computational complexity of such problems. Can combinatorial methods help prove stronger lower bounds and upper bounds? Can such lower bounds be shown for almost all NP-hard problems? These questions will deepen our understanding of power of conic optimization as a computation model. Their answers may guide us in designing new optimization algorithms. 本人計劃礸研兩條問題，關於錐優化算法的複雜度： （一）最近出現幾種新式隨機優化算法，如 Bansal 等人的葛蘭–史密特遊走及 Ebrahimi 等人的求最大子行列式算法。這些算法能否變得不再隨機？能否找出規律，令類似的近似算法無須隨機？ （二）能否用組合技巧去證明錐優化算法的更多優點與限制？普遍的線性或半正定規劃（叫做擴充陳述）亦有局限，但已知有局限的問題寥寥可數，而且相關證明並不反映解決該問題有多複雜。能否用組合技巧證明更強的優點、限制？能否證明擴充陳述對於幾乎所有 NP 困難的問題，都受制於相同的局限？ 解答上述問題，就會更透徹了解錐優化這個計算模型有幾強大，或會啟發出新的優化算法。

14209818.label: Realisation of objectives
14209818.value: The project consists of two unrelated parts: derandomization and extension complexity lower bound. Derandomization turns out to be much more challenging than expected. I discussed with my MPhil student Sing Hei LI and another PhD student Yihan ZHANG for 3--4 months to try to improve Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett (STOC 2018) and Dadush-Garg-Lovett-Nikolov (APPROX-RANDOM 2016). We identified the obstacles but didn't manage to improve on the former. For the extension complexity lower bound for CSPs such as 3XOR, I have been working on the problem for years and is still working on it. This problem is interesting because the computational model is vastly more general than Sherali-Adams (or sum-of-squares for the case of SDP). This is a necessary step towards understanding general conic computation lower bounds, beyond ad hoc hierarchies such as Sherali-Adams or sum-of-squares. It is natural to guess that the smallest extended formulation must be based on simulating resolution refutations of unsatisfiable 3XOR. A challenge is to properly define a step/subcomputation of the extended formulation that would hopefully correspond to a resolution step. For a long time I even looked into whether the definition of "half a resolution step" would be helpful for proving a lower bound (I mentioned this possibility in a very brief discussion with Madhur Tulsiani). Later I realized "half a resolution step" may not exist and makes no sense for semidefinite extended formulation.

14209818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209818.value: The best way to define a common step, at least for linear extended formulation, is to consider the maximum common subrefutation (also known as meet) of different unsatisfiable XOR instances. For linear extended formulation, if the refutations for four unsatisfiable XOR instances A, B, C, and D are linearly dependent, then common subrefutations of (A,B), of (A,C), of (D,B), and of (D,C) all exist, and the sum of two complementary subrefutations equals the refutation of an instance. Further, each of these common subrefutations is linearly independent of the span of refutations of A, B, C, and D (at least for unsatisfiable instances consisting of four clauses). Such subrefutations do not exist in general for weak refutations in semidefinite extended formulation, because semidefinite matrices do not form a lattice and meet and join operations are not defined. Later, I gave a concrete proof that such subrefutations do not exist using Bell states.

14209818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209818.value: Complete the lower bound for linear extended formulation strong refutations of minimally unsatisfiable XOR. After that, try to prove the same lower bound for weak refutations as well, which will then imply lower bounds for NP-hard problems as well.

14209818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209818.value: Understand why general linear programs are unable to solve a large class of problems conjectured to be hard, by studying the structure of these programs and decomposing these programs into elementary steps.

14209918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209918.value: 我們愈來愈依賴互聯網服務。 這些服務背後的數據儲存伺服器（DSS）通常儲存許多其用戶的敏感數據，例如信用卡信息。但是不少大型的互聯網服務在這十年中發生了多次數據洩露。一種很自然的解決方法是加密這些數據；然而，DSS仍然需要在使用這些數據之前解密，但顯然把解密密鑰儲存在DSS是同樣危險。 與此同時，很多用戶自己不會做很多事情去保證安全性，例如他們經常會選擇容易猜到的密碼，更不會儲存解密密鑰來採用任何公鑰加密方案。 密碼強化（PH）是Facebook在使用的一種有前景的解決方案，它利用外部加密伺服器來強化儲存在DSS中的認證密碼數據庫。 用戶身份驗證仍然基於認證密碼，但DSS需要與加密伺服器互通以驗證密碼。 只要加密伺服器保持安全，就算攻擊者控制了DSS，任何離線字典攻擊亦會變得無效。 每個驗證請求僅適用於單個驗證密碼，因此加密伺服器可以限制在線字典攻擊。最近的研究實現了許多有趣的功能，包括部分模糊性（加密伺服器無法得知任何驗證密碼）和高效的密鑰輪換（兩個伺服器都可以更新其密鑰，DSS可以相應地更新數據庫，使先前的攻擊無效）。 此提案旨在解決一些針對實際需求的問題。1）即使DSS遭到入侵，用戶如何只通過記住一個弱的密碼來保護DSS儲存的敏感數據？ 但是PH本身只會加密驗證密碼數據庫，無法保護其他數據。2）傳統的PH方案需要加密伺服器知道用戶名稱來限制其驗證速率。我們可否設計一個匿名PH協議，在不洩漏用戶名稱的情況下仍可進行限速驗證？3）如何提高PH的可靠性，允許動態的加密伺服器組，同時盡量減少它們之間的交互？ 4）如何應用PH來開發新的安全服務／程式？ 解決這些問題也會帶來理論上的貢獻。 1.我們會制定一個新的元件---強化認證密碼的密鑰封裝機制（PKEM）。 2.我們會解決一個公開問題---構造一個基於雙線性配對的密鑰同態偽隨機函數，而不需要隨機預言模型。 3.我們會研究支持密鑰輪換的多伺服器PH/PKEM。 4.我們開辟一種處理加密數據的方法，在保持效率的前提下，提供更豐富的查詢。 此提案的成功將充分發揮密碼強化服務在實際使用案例的潛力，並推動應用密碼學領域的發展。

14209918.label: Realisation of objectives
14209918.value: Objective 1: Objective 1 has been achieved with work co-authored by the PI that constitutes an early but integral part of the investigation [UsenixSec18] (Please also see the note at the end.) -- password-hardened encryption (PHE) and (more specifically) password-hardened key encapsulation mechanism (PHKEM). PHKEM enables users to employ a password for the encryption and decryption of encapsulated keys, subsequently used for securing sensitive user data. Our contributions to password-hardened storage extended beyond the initial scope through research into advanced encryption notions, including identity-based encryption (IBE) and access control encryption (ACE). Notably, the ACE encryption key or IBE/ACE's decryption key can be encapsulated by PHKEM. We propose IBE schemes with related-key security in [ACNS22] and anonymous (hierarchical) IBE from broader assumptions in [ACNS23a]. In [S&P21], [ACNS21], and [ISIT23], we propose i) the first cross-domain ACE which supports arbitrary policy, constant size ciphertext, and practical efficiency without using heavyweight primitives, ii) the first post-quantum secure ACE, and iii) the first information-theoretic-secure ACE. Objective 2: Our manuscript "Key-Homomorphic randomized pseudorandom functions" introduces a variant of the (oblivious) pseudorandom function, a foundational primitive underlying password hardening or PHE for anonymous authentication with (anonymous) rate-limiting assurance. Our proposed generic construction allows adaptability to integrate various anonymous rate-limiting mechanisms proposed in our recent works ([ACNS23b], [CSF23], [EuroS&P23]). Objective 2 is not fully achieved as the manuscript awaits acceptance from an appropriate venue. While the foundational protocol has been established, the intricate balance required between anonymity and effective rate-limiting presented unexpected challenges. Anonymous rate-limiting without trusted third parties by itself (before integrating with other authentication services) proves to be a formidable problem. Our series of work addresses critical issues in rate-limiting, offering pioneering solutions that prevent global halting in the presence of one problematic user and ensure sustainability by managing the cryptographic data structure's growth for anonymous rate-limiting across all users. To enhance the prospects for publication, a strategic focus is placed on refining the balance between formalism needed by provable security and practicality (e.g., the efficiency of the overall solution) in the integration of a password-hardening service. Objective 3: For extending password-hardening services to multiple servers, an integral step involves obtaining authorization from a sufficient number of servers, which can be done via threshold signatures. We delve into threshold ECDSA, for it is a standard and has been deployed in many decentralized systems like blockchain, cryptocurrency, and domain name services. In [NDSS23], we propose the first robust threshold ECDSA scheme that achieves t-out-of-n threshold flexibility throughout the entire pre-signing and signing phases without assuming an honest majority among participating users. Notably, our scheme eliminates the need to restart from scratch, a vulnerability in prior schemes that becomes pronounced in resource-constrained environments and decentralized settings where faults are more likely. Our proposal of multi-client oblivious RAM in [AsiaCrypt20], particularly the multi-server realization, provides a solid foundation contributing towards Objective 3. Our solution can ensure that users can log in without the server(s) gaining knowledge of the specific enrollment record storing the user's registered password. The client-obliviousness feature aligns with the goal of extending password-hardening services to multiple servers while maintaining user privacy and confidentiality. Objective 3 has been notably influenced by external factors, specifically the realization that aspects of our work have been preempted by another paper from our prior collaborators, initiated by a student not originally part of the collaborative team. This independent discovery prompts the need for a reassessment and redirection of our approach. Faced with similar efforts, we are strategically shifting our trajectory to make a unique and compelling contribution to the field. In response to this circumstance, our revised strategy involves accentuating distinctive elements of our work and exploring alternative avenues for impact. Instead of extending existing solutions, we focus on innovative features, refine implementation details, and seek opportunities to differentiate our work within the broader landscape. Emphasizing the incorporation of digital signature schemes published as standards and widely deployed further underscores our commitment to making a significant and distinct contribution. Another alternative for Objective 3 involves addressing the absence of anonymous rate-limiting (Objective 2) in the existing work. Our strategy now includes incorporating anonymous rate-limiting mechanisms into the extended password-hardening service for multiple servers, enhancing both security and privacy aspects. This direction aims to provide a comprehensive solution, effectively combining access control with the ability to mitigate potential misuse through rate-limiting. Objective 4: Upon successful user authentication and recovery of the encapsulated key, the applicabilities of PHE become versatile. It can serve as the private key in cryptocurrency or e-payment systems, as explored in [CCS19, ACSAC21, ICDCS21]. More generally, the key, along with any user data encrypted under the key, can undergo secret-sharing between two servers, facilitating efficient secure computation for diverse pragmatic tasks. Our series of works delve into private set interaction (PSI) for data analytics [AsiaCCS22], searchable encryption [DBSEC21], privacy-preserving skyline queries [DASFAA20], range queries [PoPETS22], graph analytics [TDSC23], and privacy-preserving machine learning [SCC19, ADMA23]. Still, we faced challenges in getting a full-blown paper published in a decent conference when the integration of these with PHE at the moment is rather direct. Hence, we consider this 99% completed. Our next goal aims to propose a practical system that tightly integrates PHE with secure two-party computation, focusing on addressing a prominent, pragmatic task of typical daily users. An idea is the implementation of spam filtering in encrypted email communications, in which we have explored techniques in oblivious evaluation of automata, an extension of oblivious graph evaluation underlying our PSI protocol [AsiaCCS22]. (P.S. As explained in the Mid-Term Progress Report, one paper was accepted before the start of this project. The reasons are: i) There are external collaborators (who are not co-investigators) involved. In particular, they would like to do a start-up (the PI is not involved) and submit a patent application (more details later) as early as possible. ii) We also got a travel grant (DAAD/ G-CUHK406/17) under DAAD Germany / Hong Kong Joint Research Scheme" starting on January 1 2018, which is before the original starting date (January 1 2019) of the project. iii) Due to managerial issues of the PI, the starting date of this project is deferred to June 28 2019. )

14209918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209918.value: Our research has yielded significant contributions across multiple objectives. Objective 1 has been successfully achieved, focused on PHE and PHKEM [UsenixSec18]. Our advancements extend to exploring IBE and ACE, offering schemes with related-key security [ACNS22], hierarchical IBE [ACNS23a], and novel ACE designs being the first of their kind [ISIT23, S&P21, ACNS21]. Objective 2 contributes to anonymous rate-limiting and reputation/revocation. We present two novel anonymous credentials [ACNS23b, EuroS&P23] for securely maintaining credits for rewarding or penalizing user behavior. We eliminate the global halting issue in the prevalent designs. We also proposed a general technique for achieving sustainability in decentralized ring-based anonymous systems [CSF23]. Objective 3 has produced groundbreaking proposals. Multi-client oblivious RAM [AsiaCrypt20] provides a collaborative but untrusted environment for private anonymous data access, addressing efficiency and trust-assumption limitations in existing solutions. We proposed a robust threshold ECDSA scheme [NDSS23], overcoming denial-of-service vulnerabilities in state-of-the-art designs. It achieves t-out-of-n threshold flexibility throughout pre-signing and signing phases, even in a decentralized setting, with significant communication-efficiency improvements. Objective 4 underscores the versatile and impactful applications of privacy-enhancing technologies, focusing on secure two-party computation and queries over encrypted data. Our results collectively showcase broad applicability, extending beyond fundamental cryptographic tasks to advanced applications like private set intersection for data analytics [AsiaCCS22], searchable encryption [DBSEC21], queries over encrypted data structures [PoPETS22, DASFAA20], and privacy-preserving graph analytics [TDSC23] and machine learning [ADMA23, SCC19]. The outcomes of Objective 4 also make significant strides in the domain of financial privacy and secure electronic transactions [CCS19]. "Sipster" [ACSAC21] pioneers a novel method for private and swift IOU settlements using smart meters, ensuring user privacy and even concealing payment amounts. Our LDSP (Leadership-Driven Secure Payment) [ICDCS21] ensures user privacy in retail transactions and extends to central bank digital currencies. These achievements directly address concerns related to the inadvertent disclosure of user-profiles through payment patterns, offering nuanced solutions that prioritize privacy protection in electronic transactions. Our forward-looking approach, exemplified by processing encrypted data and confidential transactions, marks a pragmatic shift in leveraging password-hardened encryption. This aims for an evolution that makes advanced cryptographic techniques accessible to everyday Internet users, addresses real-world needs, and paves the way for the widespread adoption of privacy-centric technologies.

14209918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209918.value: The research outcomes set the stage for further development and refinement. For Objective 1, one potential is the development of lattice-based PHE, enhancing security alongside emerging quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques. Leveraging our existing lattice-based ACE constructions and even unconditionally secure ACE constructions will be our starting point. Objective 2's foundational protocol awaits acceptance, prompting a strategic focus on balancing formalism and practicality for publication. For Objective 3, incorporating anonymous rate-limiting into multi-server password-hardening services emerges as a novel direction. Our proposed course of action involves refining integration strategies, seeking publication in suitable venues, and exploring innovative features to enhance the overall impact. For Objective 4, the next research phase aims to tightly integrate PHE with secure two-party computation for seamless and secure user experiences of some killer applications. In summary, the major findings from Objective 4 underscore the transformative potential of PHE in diverse domains, positioning it as a key enabler for practical and privacy-preserving applications beyond conventional cryptographic use cases. Our research here also contributes to the development of robust financial systems that prioritize user privacy, which we will continue to explore in the future landscape of secure and confidential digital transactions.

14209918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209918.value: Our research breakthrough focuses on reinforcing user data security and privacy in practical scenarios, where we not only emphasize the use of passwords but also introduce innovative techniques that leverage password usage to achieve security goals beyond the capabilities of passwords alone. Our advances in password-hardened encryption ensure robust security for communication and diverse applications. Innovations extend to safeguarding user privacy in collaborative environments through access control encryption with novel features. Our work also addresses challenges in privacy-preserving authentication, anonymous reputation, and rate-limiting while ensuring long-term system sustainability. In practical applications, we emphasize security in everyday tasks. This includes techniques like private set intersection for private matchmaking and contact tracing, searchable encryption for secure queries to outsourced data, and secure big data analytics. We aim to extend these secure systems to multiple users and/or servers settings for enhanced scalability and utility. We also prioritize privacy in daily digital interactions, covering financial transactions such as utility payments and retail transactions. We envision a digital landscape where users navigate and interact online with enhanced safety and heightened privacy. As our research continues, our commitment is unwavering, providing practical solutions for secure and private online experiences and shaping the future of digital interactions.

14300018.label: Project Objectives
14300018.value: Study contact manifolds resulted from contact surgeries on links and determine whether they support overtwisted, tight or symplectically fillable contact structures. Study geometrically simply-connected 4-manifolds and obtain obstructions to the existence of symplectic structures in terms of their intersection forms.
