14300018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300018.value: This project mainly studies 3-dimensional contact topology and 4-dimensional symplectic topology. We address the basic questions of which 3-manifolds admit tight contact structures and which 4-manifolds admit symplectic structures. Gauge theoretical methods will be applied. In particular, we compute Ozsvath-Szabo's contact invariant and use link surgery formula to understand how they change under contact surgeries. We apply similar techniques to compute Heegaard Floer 4-manifold invariant of closed geometrically simply-connected 4-manifolds. Last but not least, we explore the possibility of refining the classical Seiberg-Witten or Heegaard Floer invariant in a way so that their values on 4-manifolds resulted from Fintushel and Stern's knot surgery contain additional information besides Alexander polynomial of knot, such as Alexander modules. If this approach is successful, we may use the new invariant to construct pairs of simply-connected nondiffeomorphic manifolds of the same Seiberg-Witten invariant. 該項目主要研究三維接觸拓撲和四維辛拓撲。其中的主要問題包括哪類三維流體允許緊接觸結構以及哪些四維流形允許辛結構。 我們將應用規範場論的方法。我們會計算Ozsvath-Szabo的接觸不變量，並通過鏈環手術公式來計算此不變量在接觸手術下的變化。我們還會應用類似的技術來計算幾何單連通的閉四維流形的Heegaard Floer不變量。 最後，我們還會嘗試改進經典的Seiberg-Witten及Heegaard-Floer不變量，希望能在Fintushel和Stern的紐結手術情況下看到除亞歷山大多項式之外更多的信息。此類新的不變量可以用於構造很多相同Seiberg-Witten不變量，但非微分同胚的單連通四維流形。

14300018.label: Realisation of objectives
14300018.value: All objectives were investigated and realized partly by the 3 publications of the PI. For the contact aspect of the project, the PI used the surgery formula from Heegaard Floer homology to compute the contact invariants. These invariants can be used to determined overtwistness, tightness and fillability of contact manifolds. Rather than focusing on the well-established knot surgery in the 3-sphere case described in the literature, the PI investigated the wider and more complex scenario of link surgeries in rational homology spheres. Further details regarding the significance and impact of the research will be given in subsequent sections of this report. For the symplectic aspects of the project, the PI has been collaborating with Prof. Jongil Park, a renowned topologist, ICM speaker and current president of the Korean Mathematical Society. We had managed to reformulate our questions in a much more user-friendly manner before being interrupted by the COVID pandemic. The project resumed in early 2023. It is worth noting that some of our ideas appeared in a recent preprint by Levine-Lidman-Piccirillo titled "New construction and invariants of closed exotic 4-manifolds". In addition, while working on smooth structures in 4-manifolds, the PI made unanticipated progress on minimal genus problems in 4-manifolds. The ideas emerged in 2022, but both paper (arXiv: 2307.06807, arXiv: 2311.11507) were written after the expiration date of the project.

14300018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300018.value: The major breakthrough concern research on contact topology and geometry, among which the most important piece of work is presented in the paper "Contact (+1) surgeries along Legendrian two-component link" published in the journal "Quantum Topology", in which we utilized the link surgery formula of Manolescu-Ozsvath to compute the contact invariant of the resulting contact manifold from contact surgeries on links. It is the first new result of this kind to address a wide class of links instead of knots, and it is also an intriguing and pioneering application of the intricate link surgery formula to tackle a classical and fundamental question in contact topology. The PI's other two papers addressed different aspects of contact surgeries. One of them explored contact surgeries in rational homology spheres, which was previously far less extensively studied as knots in the 3-sphere. The paper is published in "Journal of Symplectic Geometry". The other paper constructed infinitely many hyperbolic closed 3-manigolds which admit no symplectic fillable contact structure. This provides new evidence for the "high surgery conjecture" raised by Stipsicz.

14300018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300018.value: The link surgery formula developed by Manolescu and Ozsvath for the Heegaard Floer homology of integral surgeries on link is significantly more complicated than a similar formula developed by Ozsvath-Szabo for knots, which has been a powerful tool in low dimensional topology and contact geometry. Likewise, it is very likely that a better understanding of this link surgery formula will in turn play an important role in our understanding of contact geometry in three dimensions. Our paper represents an initial effort in this direction, with the tool utilized in its simplest form. We totally expect further development in this area and also in symplectic geometry. Indeed, the paper has stimulated researchers to explore similar questions in symplectic field theory (arXiv:2307.12635). The PI knows the author and a potential collaboration appears feasible in the near future. Additionally, the PI is also working on minimal genus type problems in low-dimensional topology, which are crucial for understanding smooth structures in 4-manifold.

14300018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300018.value: Manolescu and Ozsvath developed a potentially powerful tool called the "link surgery formula", but for nearly a decade it was deemed impractical for solving classical problems in low-dimensional topology or contact surgery by many experts due to its intimidating length of 200 pages. The PI and his collaborators have taken the first step in this direction, demonstrating boldness and innovation that could inspire and boost the confidence of other researchers who want to use this tool. From a more technical (but less Layman) point of view, our work were able to extend previous work from knots to links (from one-component embedded circle to multi-components), and from the standard 3-sphere to rational homology spheres. Both generalizations are highly non-trivial and of great theoretical significance.

14300118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300118.value: Isoprene is a volatile organic compound (VOC) emitted from terrestrial vegetation that contributes to the greatest fraction of global VOC emission. Forests and remote environments are often characterized by high isoprene emissions and low NOx concentrations due to large vegetation cover and low human activity. In these regions, a significant fraction of isoprene reacts with hydroxyl (OH) radicals to generate isoprene epoxydiols (IEPOX). The reactive uptake of gas-phase IEPOX onto aqueous sulfate seed aerosols is a key pathway for the formation of isoprene epoxydiols derived secondary organic aerosols (termed IEPOX-SOA). While the mechanisms of IEPOX-SOA formation have become clearer, how it chemically transforms or ages over time in the atmosphere remains unclear. After formation, IEPOX-SOA can continuously evolve through oxidation with gas-phase oxidants (e.g. OH radicals) at or near the aerosol surface. These heterogeneous oxidative processes can change the abundance, composition, and properties of the aerosols, but it is unclear how and to what extent this occurs. This proposed study will investigate the chemical transformation of laboratory-generated IEPOX-SOA through heterogeneous OH oxidation and will examine how the variation of both aerosol composition and relative humidity (RH) affect kinetics, products, and reaction mechanisms. IEPOX-SOA will be first generated through the uptake of the two most predominant gas-phase IEPOX isomers (cis- and trans-β-IEPOX) onto different types of aqueous inorganic seed aerosols in a glass flow tube reactor. The aerosols will be introduced into an oxidation flow reactor, in which they will be oxidized by gas-phase OH radicals over a range of RH values. The size, mass, and chemical composition of IEPOX-SOA before and after oxidation will be measured using a variety of online and offline analytical techniques. The molecular information of reaction products will provide new insights regarding heterogeneous reaction mechanisms. Oxidation kinetics will be quantified by monitoring the change in the aerosol composition upon oxidation. These kinetic data will allow us to evaluate whether heterogeneous OH oxidation contributes to the chemical transformation of IEPOX-SOA. In particular, the heterogeneous OH oxidation of specific IEPOX-SOA tracers will be quantified, which will determine the efficacy of these tracers to predict the atmospheric abundance of IEPOX-SOA in aerosol source apportionment studies. Overall, the results from this proposed study will contribute to a better understanding of the abundance, transformation, and environmental fates of IEPOX-SOA. 14300118.label: Realisation of objectives
14300118.value: In this project, we investigated how IEPOX-SOA and its tracers chemically transform through heterogeneous OH oxidation. We gratefully acknowledge that the two objectives have been fully addressed. The details of the realization of objectives are given below. 2-methyltetrol sulfates (2-MTS) and 2-methyltetrols have been widely used as tracers for IEPOX-SOA. While they are often assumed to be relatively unreactive, many organic compounds are known to be heterogeneously oxidized by gas-phase OH radicals at a significant rate. This may question the efficacy of these two species as tracers in aerosol source-apportionment studies. To address this question (objective 2), we assessed the stability of 2-MTS and erythritol (an analog of 2-methyltetrols) upon heterogeneous OH oxidation using an atmospheric pressure oxidation flow reactor (OFR). The molecular composition of the aerosols before and after oxidation were characterized using mass spectrometric techniques (Xu et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2020). Our kinetic data revealed that the e-folding lifetimes of these two tracers against heterogeneous OH oxidation were about 12-16 days. Considering atmospheric aerosols with a typical lifetime of two weeks in the atmosphere, our results suggest that these two IEPOX-SOA tracers were likely chemically stable. This finding supported the use of these two tracers in aerosol source apportionment studies for qualifying the amount of IEPOX-SOA. We would also like to note that oxygenated derivatives formed upon heterogeneous OH oxidation of 2-MTS had been detected in ambient aerosols of which formation pathways were previously unexplained (Chen et al., 2020). This suggested that the chemical transformation of IEPOX-SOA tracers and possibly other components of IEPOX-SOA initiated by heterogeneous OH oxidation could represent one of the overlooked sources of previously unidentified species (e.g. organosulfates) in atmosphere aerosols. Beyond IEPOX-SOA tracers, we investigated the heterogeneous OH oxidation of IEPOX-SOA freshly generated from the reactive uptake of β-IEPOX onto acidic sulfate seed aerosols (Objective 1) and examined the molecular-level compositional changes before and after oxidation using mass spectrometric techniques (e.g. LC-ESI-MS) (Cazimir Armstrong et al., 2022). Aerosol speciation data revealed that sulfated and nonsulfated oligomers are the major components of IEPOX-SOA prior to oxidation. Upon oxidation, the oligomeric species were fragmented into lower molecular weight products. We found that 2-methytetrols and 2-MTS were generated upon fragmentation of the oligomers, explaining a minimal change in their concentrations upon oxidation. Since most of these products were non-volatile and remain in the aerosol phase, we argued that IEPOX-SOA could be resistant to mass loss by the production of low-volatility products, and decomposition of oligomeric species upon oxidation could likely extend the atmospheric lifetime of IEPOX-SOA and its tracers (i.e. 2-methyltetrols and 2-MTS). This further supported the use of these two tracers for aerosol source apportionment studies for quantifying the amount of IEPOX-SOA in the atmosphere. We also observed some reaction products with the same molecular weights and retention times as those in chamber samples and ambient aerosol samples. We suggested that some compounds in ambient aerosols that may have been previously identified as monoterpene-derived compounds could likely be attributed to IEPOX-SOA. All these results address the needs to characterize the compositional evolution of IEPOX-SOA upon heterogeneous OH oxidation in order to better understand the sources and composition of atmospheric aerosols. We would like to note that the findings of this project had clearly demonstrated that the organosulfates (e.g. 2-MTS and sulfated oligomers) are the important components of IEPOX-SOA and can play a crucial role in determining the heterogeneous reactivity. This led to a new research direction on the heterogeneous OH reactivity of organosulfates that are surface-active and preferentially partition near the aerosol surface for oxidation. From that, we published a review paper entitled “Organosulfates in Ambient Aerosol: State of Knowledge and Future Research Directions on Formation, Abundance, Fate, and Importance” (Bruggemann et al., 2020). Particularly, in this review, we addressed the importance to study the chemical transformation of 2-MTS, a chemical tracer of IEPOX-SOA, through heterogeneous OH oxidation and other atmospheric processes. We also advocated our atmospheric community to investigate how and to what extent atmospheric aerosols (including IEPOX-SOA) chemically transform through heterogeneous oxidation in order to better understand the fate of atmospheric aerosols. From the study of 2-MTS (Chen et al., 2020), we demonstrated that chemical transformation of 2-MTS and possibly other organosulfates can potentially produce new products which are previously unclassified in atmospheric aerosols. With the support of this project, we tested this hypothesis by studying the heterogeneous OH oxidation of an atmospheric relevant organosulfate originated from photochemical oxidation of α-pinene (αpOS-249) (Xu et al., 2022). Product analysis showed that more oxygenated organosulfates were formed with the addition of one or two hydroxyl and carbonyl functional groups to αpOS-249. Furthermore, most of these reaction products had been detected in laboratory-generated α-pinene-derived aerosols as well as in atmospheric aerosols. These results further supported the hypothesis that organosulfates freshly formed from the photochemical oxidation of biogenic volatile organic compounds (e.g. IEPOX and α-pinene) could react further to form organosulfates commonly detected in atmospheric aerosols through heterogeneous OH oxidation. Lastly, we also acknowledge that inorganic salts were always present in the atmospheric aerosols and can potentially affect the heterogeneous reactivity. To examine the salt effects on heterogeneous reactivity, we observed a phenomenon whereby ammonium sulfate (AS), an typical inorganic salt in atmospheric aerosols, acts to enhance the heterogeneous OH reaction rate for surface active organosulfates (Ng et al., 2022). We postulated that AS may exhibit an ion-specific effect on modifying interactions between dodecyl sulfate, a model compound for organosulfates and OH radical, which subsequently altered their reactivities. Our all-atom non-reactive molecular dynamic (MD) simulation revealed that upon the addition of AS, ammonium ion (NH4+) tended to accumulate near the air-water interface, while sulfate ion (SO42–) was dispersed near the aerosol interior. Inferred by ab initio calculation, a strong attraction exists between NH4+ and OH radical, while repulsive force dominated between OH radical and SO42–. Altogether, the enhanced reaction rate was likely due to the affinity of both NH4+ and organosulfates for the air-water interface and the strong interaction between NH4+ and OH, which brought the diffused OH closer to dodecyl sulfate. In essence, this indicates that the abundance and identity of counterions (e.g. NH4+ and other cations) would affect the reaction kinetics. We anticipated observing a similar enhancement in reactivity of other oragnosulfates if another cations sharing a surface propensity and exhibiting a strong attraction to OH radical was present. Future studies on the heterogeneous OH oxidation of organosulfates shall therefore take into careful consideration the effect of their counterions , which may together affect the interpretation of experimental kinetics outcomes. We encouraged future experimental and MD simulation studies on the effects of counterions on the heterogeneous OH oxidation, which provide mechanistic insight to improve our understanding of heterogeneous reactivity of organosulfates. We acknowledge that there was an unspent balance. The reasons for this are we had reserved the money for the chemical analysis and eventually got a discount for the charges. Also, we decided not to recruit undergraduate students to work in the lab due to the pandemic.

14300118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300118.value: In this work, we have experimentally examined the chemical transformation of IEPOX-SOA and its tracers through heterogeneous OH oxidation. The major findings were summarized below IEPOX-SOA tracers. We found that 2-methyltetrol sulfates (2-MTS) and 2-methyltetrols, two important IEPOX-SOA tracers, had e-folding lifetimes to be less than 16 days. Considering atmospheric aerosols with a lifetime of two weeks, these two IEPOX-SOA tracers were likely chemically stable in the atmosphere Furthermore, we observed that these two tracers were generated from the fragmentation of the oligomeric species upon heterogeneous OH oxidation of IEPOX-SOA, and decomposition of oligomeric species upon oxidation could likely extend the atmospheric lifetimes of these two tracers. Altogether these results supported the use of these two tracers for aerosol source apportionment studies for quantifying the amount of IEPOX-SOA in the atmosphere. We also found that transformation of 2-MTS into their oxygenated derivatives, which the resultant products had been detected in ambient aerosols of which formation pathways were previously unexplained. These suggested that transformation of IEPOX-SOA initiated by heterogeneous OH oxidation could represent one of the overlooked origins of some previously unidentified species in atmosphere aerosols. IEPOX-SOA. We investigated the heterogeneous oxidation of freshly generated IEPOX-SOA by gas-phase OH radical and examined the aerosol composition changes at a molecular level before and after oxidation. Product analysis revealed that sulfated and nonsulfated oligomers were the major components of IEPOX-SOA before oxidation. Upon oxidation, these oligomeric species were fragmented into lower-molecular weight nonvolatile species. Decomposition of oligomers by heterogeneous OH oxidation could act as serve a reservoir of low-volatility species and extend the atmospheric lifetime of IEPOX-SOA. While IEPOX-SOA remained longer in the atmosphere, they may also become more oxygenated and more efficient in cloud and ice nucleation, potentially having larger climatic impacts. We also observed reaction products with the same molecular weight and retention time patterns as those in chamber samples and ambient aerosol samples. We argued that some compounds in ambient aerosols that may have been previously identified as monoterpene-derived compounds, were likely be attributed to IEPOX-SOA. All these results addressed the needs to characterize the compositional evolution of IEPOX-SOA upon heterogeneous OH oxidation in order to improve the prediction of their sources and impacts on air quality and climate. Overall, the findings of the project provided us a better mechanistic understanding of the sources, composition, transformation and environmental impacts of IEPOX-SOA.

14300118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300118.value: We would like to propose that further development in two directions. To date, one of the major challenges in quantifying the composition of IEPOX-SOA is a lack of authentic standards. With numerous organosulfates detected, only few authentic standards are available for accurate identification. Successfully synthesized a variety of atmospheric organosulfates before in this project, we propose to continue to develop reaction pathways to synthesize new authentic standards, especially for those poorly uncharacterized ones (e.g. sulfated oligomers). With standards, we can develop analytical methods for better separation, identification, and quantification of organosulfates, which are the important components of IEPOX-SOA. These newly developed methods can help us to obtain much needed accurate composition and concentration of organosulfates in atmospheric aerosols. Until recently, the formation pathways of IEPOX-SOA have become more well-understood and incorporated into some photochemical box models (e.g. GAMMA and UNIPAR) and chemical transport models (e.g. CMAQ and ECHAM-HAMMOZ). However, the transformation pathways of IEPOX-SOA have not been considered in all of these models. Now we acknowledge IEPOX-SOA can undergo chemical transformation. Implementing transformation schemes based on kinetic parameters and mechanisms obtained in this project will enable more accurate prediction of the composition and abundance of IEPOX-SOA.

14300118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300118.value: Secondary organic aerosols (SOA) originating from this multiphase chemistry of IEPOX (termed IEPOX-SOA) can account for a significant mass fraction of the aerosol mass in the atmosphere and can play a significant role in determining the environmental and climatic impacts of atmospheric aerosols. The formation mechanisms of IEPOX-SOA have become clearer in recent studies. However, the chemical transformation of IEPOX-SOA is largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally investigated the heterogeneous OH oxidation of IEPOX-SOA and its tracers using an aerosol flow tube reactor by quantifying the kinetics and identifying the reaction products and mechanisms. We showed that IEPOX-SOA and its tracers were chemically stable against oxidation. This supported the use of tracer method in the aerosol source apportionment studies for quantifying the concentration of IEPOX-SOA in the atmosphere. In addition, we reported that heterogeneous OH oxidation of IEPOX-SOA led to new reaction products that were previously unclassified in field studies and could represent one of the overlooked sources of unidentified compounds in atmosphere aerosols. Overall, the findings of this project demonstrated that heterogeneous oxidative process shall be considered when understanding the sources, composition, and abundance of IEPOX-SOA and atmospheric aerosols.

14300218.label: Project Objectives
14300218.value: To synthesize the proposed nanographenes using the ring expansion reaction as a key step for construction of the seven-membered rings. To investigate synthesis of the proposed carbon nanobelts, which will take advantage of the curved nature of the building blocks. To study molecular geometries, stereochemical dynamics and electronic structures of the proposed molecules with experimental and computational methods. 14300218.label: Realisation of objectives
14300218.value: We have successfully realized all the objectives as detailed below. 1. We synthesized two negatively curved nanographenes containing seven membered rings. In particular, the synthesis of heptabenzo[7]circulene involves a ring expansion reaction to form the seven-membered ring and a Scholl reaction to form the fully conjugated framework. 2. We proposed a new negatively curved carbon nanobelt and investigated its synthesis. We expanded the scope of this project to zigzag carbon nanobelts, which are not only a long-sought-after target of organic synthesis but also a key step toward precise synthesis of carbon nanotubes, and successfully synthesized a few zigzag carbon nanobelts using the Scholl reaction as a key step. 3. We studied molecular geometries, stereochemical dynamics, strains and electronic structures of the synthesized nanographenes and carbon nanobelts using both experimental and computational methods. 4. We tested the capability of the synthesized nanographenes and carbon nanobelts to co-crystallize with fullerenes, and found that an oxanorbornene-fused dibenzo[de,qr]tetracene nanobox can accommodate a fullerene (C70 or C60) in its cavity in both crystals and solution.

14300218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300218.value: 1. We synthesized two negatively curved nanographenes containing seven membered rings. One of them is heptabenzo[7]circulene, a new member of fully orthobenzannulated [n]circulene after three smaller analogues; and the other consists of 72 sp2 carbon atoms and is functionalized with ketone groups, which can in principle allow further expansion of the π-system. These results were reported in Publications 1 and 3 (Part C). 2. We designed and synthesized tribenzo[a,c,e]cyclooctene oligomers, which are potential precursors for synthesis of negatively curved nanographenes and nanobelts. These results were reported in Publication 2 (Part C). 3. We expanded the scope of this project to zigzag carbon nanobelts, which are not only a long-sought-after target of organic synthesis but also a key step toward precise synthesis of carbon nanotubes. We investigated two ways to synthesize zigzag carbon nanobelts. The first is repetitive Diels-Alder reactions followed by reductive aromatization, and the second is the Scholl reaction of macrocyclic precursors. Using the first way, we synthesized two oxanorbornene-fused nanoboxes, which, under reductive aromatization conditions, either led to a hydrogenated carbon nanobelt as identified by X-ray crystallography or observation of the corresponding zigzag carbon nanobelt by mass spectroscopy. Using the second method, we synthesized three unprecedented zigzag carbon nanobelts, which present a wave-like arrangement of hexagons in the unrolled lattice of (n,0) single wall carbon nanotubes (n=16 or 24). We calculated the strain of these carbon nanobelts and analyzed the change of strain during formation of the nanobelts. This analysis sheds light on rational design and efficient synthesis of new carbon nanobelts. These results were reported in Publications 5-7 (Part C). 4. We studied interactions between fullerenes and the synthesized molecular nanocarbons (negatively nanographenes and carbon nanobelts) in solid state and in solution. It is found that one of the zigzag carbon nanobelts can bind C60 strongly and a nanobox (the precursor of a zigzag carbon nanobelt) can selectively bind C70 over C60. These results were reported in Publications 6 and 7 (Part C). 5. We also published an invited review (Publication 4 in Part C) on the synthesis of different types of carbon nanobelts.

14300218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300218.value: In this project, we investigated the Scholl reaction as a powerful tool for synthesis of curved molecular nanocarbons. The recent successful syntheses of a series of curved molecular nanocarbons by us and other research groups have changed the earlier assumption that the Scholl reaction is not capable of synthesizing polycyclic aromatics in accompany with the introduction of significant steric strain. The success of this project encourages us to expand the scope of Scholl reactions, and the deeper understanding on the Scholl reaction as obtained from this project will allow us to investigate precise synthesis of more challenging nanocarbon structures using this method. For example, we plan to explore direct formation of seven- and eight-membered rings by Scholl reactions, which, however, commonly form six-membered rings in polycyclic aromatics.

14300218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300218.value: Carbon schwarzites are long-sought-after carbon allotropes that are predicted to have interesting electronic and magnetic properties, but have not been realized unambiguously yet. Fragments of carbon schwarzites containing their key structural information are negatively curved nanographenes, which can in principle be used as units in a bottom-up approach to carbon schwarzites. Carbon nanobelts are not only a long-sought-after target of organic synthesis due to their appealing structures, but also regarded as a key step in the bottom-up approach to precise synthesis of carbon nanotubes, which remains the top challenge in science of carbon nanotubes and a bottleneck limiting their applications. In this project funded by the RGC, we successfully synthesized a series of negatively curved nanographenes and carbon nanobelts, investigated Scholl reactions as a powerful tool for synthesis of these curved molecular nanocarbons, and explored their interesting properties and applications. This project has led to seven peer-reviewed publications on top journals of chemistry, and the results of this project were also presented at two international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project, and one of them has recently joined Cologne University, Germany as an assistant professor.

14300418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300418.value: This project aims to conduct quantum transport studies of topological semimetals under high pressures, with a varying magnetic field strength and direction, down to millikelvin temperatures. Quantum transport measurements at ambient pressure have revealed a string of interesting in-field behaviours, including the observations of a negative magnetoresistance, a large and unsaturated positive magnetoresistance as well as the phase shift in Shubnikov-de Haas quantum oscillations. These behaviours are the direct results of the unusual electronic band structure of topological semimetals. Hence, high quality quantum transport data provide a powerful avenue to probe the electronic states of topological semimetals. Pressure can drive transitions to other phases in a continuous manner. Certain effects that are believed to be unique in topological semimetals, e.g. the above-mentioned negative magnetoresistance associated with the chiral anomaly, can thus be tested systematically by varying pressure. Furthermore, the Fermi energy can be varied by pressure, which can lead to Lifshitz transitions. With quantum transport measurements under pressure, we can track the pressure evolution of the electronic structure, including the size, shape and the anisotropy of the Fermi surfaces. The established pressure evolution will enable a deeper understanding of transport properties of topological semimetals as well as their temperature-pressure phase diagrams. We believe the joint Hong Kong-Shenzhen team is in an advantageous position to carry out this project owing to the close geographical proximity of the teams, our well-established capability to investigate materials under multiple extreme conditions, our extensive theoretical experience in this class of materials and our ability in the growth of high quality topological semimetals. This ambitious project is a systematic high-pressure magnetotransport study of topological semimetals that explicitly includes the field angle as an independent parameter. Therefore, the project promises to contribute unique data and insight to advance the understanding of topological semimetals.

14300718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300718.value: Hydrocarbons are prevalent in engineered bionanomaterials used for many intracellular biomedical applications, like phospholipid-coated quantum dots for molecular imaging, lipid nanoparticles for gene delivery, and cholesterol-coated or vitamin E-coated nanoparticles for drug delivery. When elucidating the fundamental "bio-nano" interactions between hydrocarbyl-containing nanoparticles and the cell, previous researchers mostly treated hydrocarbyl-containing nanoparticles as a single hydrophobic entity and studied how hydrophobicity dictates the interactions between nanoparticles and mammalian cells. Yet the effects of hydrocarbons as functional groups (e.g., linear, cyclic, branched, unsaturated, and aromatic) remain incomprehensively investigated. We propose a platform for specifically addressing the role of hydrocarbyl groups in the interactions between nanoparticles and the cell. Termed “hydrocarbyl-PEG-AuNP", this largely hydrophillic platform contains a gold nanoparticle (AuNP) core, a shell of polyethylene glycol (PEG) strands, and minute amounts of hydrocarbyl groups at the periphery. Its key advantage lies in modularity, allowing for flexible adjustment of the density and type of hydrocarbyl groups to be attached. Recently, we have constructed this platform to elucidate the effect of alkylation on endocytosis, serum adsorption, and trafficking (Ho LWC et al., ACS Nano, 2017). Remarkably, with only 4 mole % of alkyl groups in the PEG shell, dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs and octadecyl-PEG-AuNPs can enter skin cells 30 times more abundantly than hexyl-PEG-AuNPs and methoxy-PEG-AuNPs (without alkyl chains). Dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs enter skin cells via the filopodia-mediated pathway, and remain stable during their trafficking along the “endo-lysosomal” route. Additional preliminary data reveal higher amount and variety of serum proteins adsorbed onto dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs, attenuating the uptake of dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs by 70%. Upon cellular entry, dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs leave the cell 50-fold more readily than methoxy-PEG-AuNPs. These results provide exciting opportunities for studying exocytosis, a topic rarely examined in mechanistic detail; many bionanomaterials internalized by the cell rarely leave in abundant amounts due to their entrapment or degradation inside organelles. As evidenced by the elevated levels of endocytosis and exocytosis as well as intracellular stability of dodecyl-PEG-AuNPs, our platform is suitable for elucidating how various hydrocarbyl groups influence the entire journey of nanoparticles into, en route, and out of the cell. We will derive mechanistic knowledge in how different hydrocarbons as functional groups affect "bio-nano" interactions, by leveraging our established experience in alkyl groups. Our research foci are the mechanism for endocytosis, extracellular and intracellular protein corona, intracellular trafficking, and the mechanism for exocytosis. Our data will offer insights into the incorporation of hydrocarbons for designing bionanomaterials for intracellular biomedical applications. 碳氫化合物（又稱烴）常見於用作胞內生物醫學應用的生物納米材料，例如用作分子成像的磷脂包裹的量子點、用作基因遞送的脂類納米粒子和用作藥物遞送的膽固醇或維生素E包裹的納米粒子。在闡釋包含烴類的納米顆粒與細胞之間的基礎「生物-納米」相互作用時，以往的學者大多數把包含烴類的納米顆粒看作疏水的單一實體，並研究疏水性如何主宰納米顆粒與哺乳動物細胞之間的相互作用。然而，烴基作為官能基團（例如: 直鏈、環狀、支鏈、非飽和及芳香環）的影響，至今尚未被全面地研究。 我們提出一個命名為「烴基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」的平台，從而具體解答烴基如何影響納米顆粒與細胞之間的相互作用。這個相對親水的平台，包含一顆金納米顆粒的核心和一個由聚乙二醇鏈組成的外殼，其外圍也裝飾了微小份量的烴基。其主要優勢在於模塊化的結構，可以彈性地調整被連接烴基的密度和種類。最近，我們建造了這平台以闡釋烷化對內吞作用、血清吸附及胞內運輸的影響（Ho LWC et al., ACS Nano, 2017）。 值得注意的是，當聚乙二醇外殼中只含有4個摩爾百分比的烷基時，「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」和「十八烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」能比「己基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」及「甲氧基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」（沒有烷基鏈）進入皮膚細胞多30倍。「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」以絲狀偽足主導的路徑進入皮膚細胞，並在胞內體至溶酶體的運輸中保持穩定的結構。額外的初步數據顯示，相對於「甲氧基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」，更多數量和種類的血清蛋白吸附在「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」上，讓「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」的細胞內吞減少百分之七十。進入細胞之後，「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」比「甲氧基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」更容易離開細胞50倍。胞吐作用甚少被深入研究，而這些結果提供了研究此課題的契機。很多生物納米材料進入細胞以後難以大量離開細胞，因為它們於細胞器中被困或降解。有見於「十二烷基-聚乙二醇-金納米顆粒」的高度內吞、 胞吐及其胞內穩定性，我們的平台適用於闡釋不同烴基如何影響納米顆粒進入細胞、胞內運輸和離開細胞的整個過程。 借鏡我們對烷基已經掌握的經驗，我們將會獲取有關不同的烴官能基如何影響「生物-納米」相互作用的機理性知識。我們的研究焦點在於內吞作用、胞內及胞外的蛋白冠、胞內運輸及胞吐作用的機理。我們的數據將揭示如何把烴納入生物納米材料的設計，從而推廣至胞內的生物醫學應用。

14300718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300718.value: We prepared a collection of gold nanoparticles (NPs) functionalized with different hydrocarbyl groups on the surface. Initially, we investigated the biological mechanism for their endocytosis and intracellular trafficking route as a function of hydrocarbyl group in vitro. Upon seeding cells on a substrate with sub-10 nm surface roughness, we also demonstrated the elevated uptake of hydrocarbyl-terminated NPs via clathrin-mediated endocytosis in cells compared to their counterparts that are seeded on a conventional flat culture plate, because conditioning cells to nanoscale surface roughness in the extracellular environment upregulates endocytosis-related genes (Yin et al., Nano Lett., 2021). Modification of NPs with straight-chain dodecanes enhanced cellular uptake than all other types of hydrocarbyl groups tested (Ho et al., Biochem., 2021). Upon cellular entry, these NPs mostly reside in the late endosomes or lysosomes. We further studied the bio-nano interaction of the NPs in vivo. By subjecting mice to inhalation of aerosolized NPs with different hydrocarbyl functional groups, we mapped the intrapulmonary distribution of NPs among the various types of cells (Yin et al., ACS Nano, 2019). We revealed strong correlations between the fractions of protein corona (albumin or carbonyl reductase) bound to NPs and associations of inhaled NPs to neutrophils or macrophages. In another study, when AuNPs modified with octadecyl chains are applied to psoriatic mice, we showed that the NP can cross the stratum corneum and enter keratinocytes (Han et al., Nano Lett, 2021). With an anti-inflammatory gold core, the alkylated gold NPs prevented psoriasis and downregulated genes that are linked to epidermis hyperproliferation and inflammation. Applying the NPs treats the psoriatic skin as effectively as standard therapy but without hair loss and skin wrinkling. We investigated the exocytosis of NPs as a function of hydrocarbyl group in vitro and found that the probability of exocytosis of NPs depends on the cell type and type of hydrocarbyl group (Ho et al., Biochem., 2021). Notably, NPs modified with cyclododecanes are most likely to be exocytosed by RAW264.7 macrophages and C166 endothelial cells. We elucidated the biological mechanism for the exocytosis of dodecyl-terminated NPs (Ho et al., ACS Nano, 2022). After entering Kera-308 keratinocytes and trafficking to multivesicular bodies and lysosomes, the dodecyl-terminated NPs exit the cell predominantly via unconventional exocytosis, accompanied by enhanced secretion of sub-100 nm, CD81-enriched exosomes. The pathway for NP exocytosis and subpopulation of extracellular vesicles that are secreted alongside the exocytosed NPs depends on dodecyl loading.

14300718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300718.value: We discovered that modifying nanoparticles with straight-chain alkanes of 12 carbons or more leads to drastically higher uptake than all other types of hydrocarbyl groups tested (Ho et al., Biochem., 2021; Yin et al., Nano Lett., 2021). We will study how surface engineering of nanoparticles with other functional groups may overcome delivery hurdles of nanoparticles to other disease destinations. In addition, we showed that these alkylated nanoparticles effectively enter epidermal keratinocytes for treating psoriasis in vivo and treat psoriasis as eﬀectively as standard steroid/vitamin D analog therapy, but without long-term retention in major internal organs or toxicity (Han et al., Nano Lett, 2021). As our present alkylated nanoparticle is of high translational value, we will apply for a Research Impact Fund (RIF) to determine its toxicity and anti-inflammatory efficacy in humans. Finally, we proved the role of extracellular vesicles in nanoparticle exocytosis (Ho et al., Biochem., 2021; Ho et al., ACS Nano, 2022). By tuning the alkyl content of nanoparticles, we may design nanoparticles that can lead to joint secretion of exosomes for building skin nanomedicines because keratinocyte-derived exosomes could facilitate wound healing. Our data also suggest NP-based methods for the production, isolation, and puriﬁcation of exosomes.

14300718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300718.value: This project has expanded our understanding in how hydrocarbyl-terminated nanoparticles interact with mammalian cells in vitro and in vivo. These are valuable data because hydrocarbons are prevalent in engineered bionanomaterials used for many intracellular applications. On endocytosis, we learn that modification with straight-chain alkanes with more than 12 carbons leads to drastically higher uptake than all other types of hydrocarbyl groups tested. On exocytosis, we show that surface alkylation of nanoparticles aﬀects their fraction of exocytosis and prove the role of unconventional secretion and extracellular vesicles in nanoparticle exocytosis. Modification of nanoparticles with optimal amounts of alkyl groups leads to enhanced secretion of exosomes, extracellular vesicles that are under active investigation for diagnosing and treating diﬀerent diseases. Further, we show in vivo that when mice are subjected to inhalation of NPs, there are strong correlations between the amounts of protein bound to NPs and associations of inhaled NPs to neutrophils or macrophages. We also show that anti-inflammatory gold nanoparticles modified with alkyl chains can cross the stratum corneum, enter keratinocytes, and treat the psoriatic skin as effectively as standard therapy. These mechanistic insights will benefit the design of nanomedicines with tunable cellular uptake and exocytosis for treating other inflammatory diseases.

14301118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301118.value: 在臨床試驗中，病人們通常不會同時進入試驗，研究者可以序貫地收集治療效果數據。在這種情況下，採用臨床反應自適應設計比常用的均衡設計（即在每個治療方案中分配相同的病人數量）在倫理道德方面具有明顯的優勢。這個倫理道德方面的優勢具體體現在，臨床反應自適應設計能夠將病人以較大的概率分配到更好的治療方案中。在臨床試驗的各個階段，已知的治療效果方面的統計信息能夠為下一位病人治療方案的分配提供有價值的信息。在近年來主流的藥物研發中，臨床反應自適應設計得到了越來越廣泛的關注。 目前，大家已認識到臨床反應自適應設計能夠為參與試驗的病人帶來好處，儘管如此，還是只有很少的臨床研究不使用傳統的均衡設計方案。一個不可忽視的原因是，在實際的臨床研究中，缺少合適的基於臨床反應自適應設計框架的分配過程研究。本項目的主要任務就是，在幾個常見的臨床試驗環境下，利用臨床反應自適應設計框架中主要的分配原則構造有價值的試驗設計算法。臨床反應自適應設計有多種不同設計框架，其中雙重自適應有偏硬幣設計是一個優異的設計方法。因此，本項目中主要採用雙重自適應有偏硬幣設計框架。 在臨床反應數據類型較為簡單的情況下，臨床反應自適應設計已經得到了充分的研究，如響應變量為二項分布或正態分布等。生存數據和屬性數據是兩種重要的響應變量數據類型，在本項目中，我們專注於對這兩類響應變量推導出有效的設計過程。針對生存數據，我們主要考慮群組生存數據和復發數據，這在目前的臨床研究中是兩類重要的響應變量數據類型。屬性數據，如疼痛等級、生活質量等有序的響應數據，也是臨床中一類常見的數據類型。 在本項目中，我們研究團隊致力於在常見的臨床試驗中為重要的倫理道德問題尋找科學的解決方法。我們相信通過本項目，能夠促使自適應設計方面的統計學者更加深入地理解更加複雜條件下的分配過程，同時能夠提出符合倫理道德的分配過程，使較少的人分配到療效較差的治療方案中。

14301118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301118.value: In clinical studies, patients usually accrued sequentially, thus enabling the incorporation of adaptive schemes: adjustments of the study roadmap after the assessment of the available patient responses thus far in the trial. Here in this research, we focus on two valuable design methodologies, adaptive in nature, that tremendously benefit drug developers as well as trial participant. The first is response-adaptive treatment randomisation and the second is stage-wise designs. The response-adaptive treatment allocation mechanism enables more patients to be allocated to the superior treatments with information of accumulative outcomes. For stage-wise procedures, the focus is on non-inferiority trials. It provides a paradigm within which interim analysis can be performed in order to determine if the next stage will be required and hence the trial can be terminated in a much earlier stage. The major research findings are summarised in three refereed papers, with all of them related to practical procedures in medical researches. Two different types of response variables are being examined, namely, ordinal and normal data. Nevertheless, our proposed method can easily be extended to other types of response variables, such as survival data and multivariate data. For response-adaptive design, we have offer useful and pragmatic treatment allocation randomisation schemes that outperform the conventional balanced design option for ordinal outcomes. For the comparison of the efficacies of two treatments, we show that a response-adaptive treatment allocation scheme is more ethical because it allows more patients to undergo the better treatment. In addition, each of the discussed allocation procedures has very similar test power. For modelling of the ordinal data, the latent Weibull model is an adopted for the proposed treatment allocation scheme. This is the first attempt in the literature to have applied the latent Weibull model for the derivation of response-adaptive treatment allocation schemes for ordinal responses. The allocation rules are derived using very general basic principles in the doubly biased coin design framework. The asymptotic variance of the allocation proportion is also provided. For stage-wise adaptive designs, simultaneous tests of non inferiority and superiority in three-arm clinical studies are provided. Furthermore, the information of misclassification is also examined in non inferiority trials. The use of misclassification in some of the non inferiority trials is able to improve the precision in estimation. Besides referred publications, we have also disseminate our findings in international conferences in order to share with the clinical community useful designs.

14301118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301118.value: Various interesting future research topics have also been generated. For example, we are trying to explore the likelihood to include sequential monitoring procedures in the design process. This will enable earlier termination of the trial if some of the treatments are found to be superior. In these cases, both the financial and human costs will be able to reduced substantially. Another future direction of research is to generalise our proposed methods to mixed responses which comprise different types of variables, including categorical, survival and continuous. The related testing methods will be more complex and the computational task will be much more complicated. For response-adaptive treatment randomisation, a practical concern is the existence of delayed response. That is, some of the observation may take a much longer time frame to collect and that will jeopardise the integrity of the proposed methods. In such cases, we have to adjust the existing method so as to provide a more stable estimate in the process of treatment allocation. The current project not only produces several important paradigms for response-adaptive designs, it also lays out an important foundation on which more influential and general classes of statistical methods could be developed.

14301118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301118.value: Clinical research is an expensive and time-consuming scientific endeavour that requires cautious planning and ethical considerations. The response-adaptive strategies on the one hand are capable of lowering the exorbitant financial cost in drug development, and on the other reducing the risk-exposure period of trial participants. Even though both response-adaptive randomisation and stage-wise designs have been reported to have some remarkable success in clinical researches, limited achievements have been attained with more complex trials and outcome structures, mainly because the corresponding theoretical and computational issues are by no means straightforward. In this project, we seek to explore and investigate response-adaptive clinical designs for more complex, but popular, responses (ordinal data) and multi-arm trials. Further, owing to the rising importance of non-inferiority (NI) trials, stage-wise testing framework in NI trials are also studied. This project is not merely a scientific venture, it bears an immense practical significance in our search of more effective therapy to combat various diseases.

14301218.label: Project Objectives
14301218.value: It is proposed to investigate the dimensional properties of ergodic invariant measures for IFSs. These measures are the images of ergodic invariant measures in the symbolic space under the coding map. A key issue in this investigation is to study the problems whether these measures are exact dimensional, and how their dimensions relate to other dynamical invariants associated to the IFSs, like entropies and Lyapunov exponents. 14301218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301218.value: In the 1970's, Mandelbrot introduced the revolutionary concept of ``fractal'' to describe the geometry of highly irregular objects in nature, such as mountains, clouds and coastlines. Since then, the idea of fractals has been widely used in numerous areas of natural sciences, as well as in engineering, life sciences, economy and arts. In recent 40 years, fractals have arisen in most areas in mathematics, such as geometric measure theory, dynamical systems, number theory and probability. The most essential features of fractals are self-similarity and fractional dimension. In mathematics, iterated function system (IFS) is a basic scheme to generate fractal sets. Formally, an iterated function system consists of a finite set of contractive transformations. By repeatedly iterating these transformations, we obtain a fractal set, which is called the attractor of the IFS. When we assign a probability in the iteration, we get an invariant measure for the IFS. In this project, we plan to investigate the fractal dimensions of invariant measures for IFSs. These measures are supported on the attractors of the IFSs, and reflect their geometric and dynamical structures. We aim to study the local dimensions of these measures and reveal their connections to other dynamical invariants (like entropy and Lyapunov exponent) associated to the IFSs. As a closely related topic, we also plan to study the dimension of stationary measures associated with random matrices. These investigations will improve our understanding of dimension theory of IFSs. 在上世紀70年代, Mandelbrot 引入了分形這一全新概念, 用之來研究自然界中極不規則的幾何對象,例如山峰,雲彩及海岸線.自此,分形的概念被廣泛應用到自然科學的諸多領域以及工程,經濟,藝術等學科中. 近40年以來, 分形已得到數學各分支的廣泛研究,例如幾何測度論,動力系統,數論及概率. 分形的最本質特徵是自相似性及分數維數.在數學上, 迭代函數係統是生成分形集合的主要模式之一. 每個迭代函數係統由有限多個壓縮映射所生成. 反复迭代這些映射,我們便得到分形集,即迭代函數係統的吸引子. 如果賦予迭代的概率,我們便得到相應的分形測度. 在本研究計劃中, 我們打算研究迭代函數係統不變測度的維數. 這些測度支撐在迭代函數係統吸引子上, 並攜帶了迭代系統的諸多幾何與動力系統結構. 我們主要目的在於研究這些測度的局部維數，並分析它們與其它動力系統不變量（例如熵與Lyapunov指數）之間的內在聯繫。作為相關課題，我們也計劃研究隨機矩陣平穩測度的維數性質。這些研究將加深我們對迭代函數係統維數理論的進一步理解。

14301218.label: Realisation of objectives
14301218.value: The main focus of this project is to investigate the dimensional properties of invariant measures associated with iterated functions systems (IFSs), as well as that of Furstenberg measures corresponding to random product of measures. We achieve the following results. Firstly we succeeded in proving that every ergodic stationary measure associated to an average-contracting affine IFS is always exact dimensional, and the dimension of this measure can be expressed in terms of Layapunov exponents and conditional entropies. This resolves a longstanding open problem in the community of fractals. To achieve this result, we applied abstract measure theory, ergodic theory of IFSs and the techniques of density estimates. A key part lies in the estimation of transverse dimensions of conditional measures, where we used the techniques of induced dynamical systems. Secondly we investigate the dimensional properties of non-linear and nonconformal IFSs. We achieved two main results: (a) the upper box-counting dimension of the attractor of any non-linear and nonconformal IFS is less than or equal to its singularity dimension; (b) the upper packing dimension of any ergodic stationary measure on such an attractor is bounded above by its Lyapunov dimension. The results are obtained by applying some new counting techniques and the mathematical theory of thermodynamic formalism. Using some transversality arguments, we show that, in some random upper triangular case, the dimension of the attractor is equal to its singularity dimension, and moreover, each ergodic stationary measure is exact dimensional with dimension equal to the Lyapunov dimension. Thirdly we succeeded in determining the Hausdorff and packing dimension of a class of (random) self-affine sets in the Euclidean spaces, by using the theory of probability, in particular, the theory of Mandelbrot cascades. Furthermore, we investigated the dimensional properties of Furstenberg measures associated with high dimensional matrices. Under a very general setting, we proved the exact dimensionality of every Furstenberg measure on Grassmannian manifolds or more generally, on flag manifolds. A key part of this study is done by analyzing the geometric and ergodic properties of the action of random matrices on P(Rd) or Grassmannian manifolds. Our main tools are the limiting theorems on products of random matrices.

14301218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301218.value: In [1], we investigate the local dimensions of stationary invariant measures for affine iterated function systems in Euclidean spaces. We prove that the local dimensions of these measures always exist almost everywhere. Moreover, we succeed in proving that every ergodic stationary measure for an average-contracting affine iterated function system is exact dimensional (that is, the local dimension of such measure is equal to a constant almost everywhere). This gives an affirmative answer to a longstanding open problem in the community of fractal geometry. In [2] we investigate the dimensional property of C^1 smooth iterated function systems and repellers. We prove that the upper box-counting dimension of the attractor of any C^1 iterated function system (IFS) on the Euclidean space is bounded above by its singularity dimension, and the upper packing dimension of any ergodic invariant measure associated with this IFS is bounded above by its Lyapunov dimension. Similar results are obtained for the repellers for C^1 expanding maps on Riemannian manifolds. In [3], we are dealing with dimensional properties of a natural class of random statistically self-affine sets and measures in R^k (k ≥ 2), namely random Sierpinski sponges and related Mandelbrot measures, as well as certain of their projections and related fibres and conditional measures. These random sponges can be also viewed as limit sets of some percolation process on the unit cube endowed with an (m1, . . . ,mk)-adic grid, where m1 ≥ · · · ≥ mk ≥ 2 are integers. We compute the Hausdorff dimension of any random statistically self-affine Sierpinski sponge K in Rk (k ≥ 2) obtained by using some percolation process in [0, 1]^k. In a paper in preparation, we investigate the dimensional properties of the Furstenberg-Oseledets measures generated by the random products of matrices. We show that all the Furstenberg-Oseledets measures generated by the random products of a finite family of invertible matrices are exact dimensional and their dimension is given by a Ledrappier-Young type formula.

We successfully give a quantitative characterisation of the local dimensions of these measures and reveal their connections to other dynamical invariants (like entropy and Lyapunov exponent) associated to the IFSs. Similarly we obtain some analogous results for the dimension of stationary measures associated with random matrices. These investigations will improve our understanding of dimension theory of IFSs.

14301318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301318.value: 現今在光伏發電的全球太瓦級能源部署中存在兩個主要的挑戰，一個是光電能量轉換效率，另一個是太陽能發電的總成本。在許多吸收層材料中，無機薄膜材料因其良好的穩定性，超過20年的使用壽命、低耗材，與其他材料相比具有很大的隱性成本優勢。其中CdTe和Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS) 就是兩個成功的例子。它們分別具有22.1％和22.6％的高實驗室轉換效率和16-18％的商業模組效率。然而，由於Te和In的地殼中的元素豐度很低，CdTe和CIGS的供應受到了限制。受限於世界儲量，CdTe和CIGS無法滿足太瓦級能源發展的需求。 為了解決上述原料供應問題， Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) 作為替代方案被提出。這種材料具有許多優點：Zn, Sn及S在地殼中蘊含量多，具有單結太陽能電池的最佳帶隙（1.5 eV），104 cm-1的高吸收係數，以及與CIGS太陽能電池兼容的器件結構，原理上是理想的太陽能光吸收層。然而，經過十多年的研究努力，純CZTS的最佳效率約為9％，而部分Se取代S的CZTSSe的效率為12.6％，均遠低於CdTe和CIGS的效率。 在CZTS中的主要問題是與其帶隙相比開路電壓不足。對於大多數良好的吸收層，帶隙和開路電壓之間的差異可以降至0.4-0.5 eV，而CZTS僅能達到0.8-0.9eV。許多研究表明，開路電壓不足的原因很可能與具有相似的原子尺寸Cu和Zn之間形成的大量反位缺陷有關。為了解決這個問題，在保持帶隙基本不變的情況下，我們提出用其他陽離子如Cd和Mg部分替代Zn的方案。由於Cu與Cd和Mg的原子尺寸差異很大， Cu和Zn之間反位缺陷的形成將得到抑制。此外，CZTS的固有局限性，例如二次相的存在，能帶不匹配和載流子收集長度短等問題亦可以通過Cd或 Mg的替代得到緩解。 隨著我們實驗室和其他研究組的Cd替代嘗試的初步成功，我們將使用Cd和Mg進行系統研究。儘管前者仍受限於世界儲量，同時也受到環境的關注，後者自然豐富且環境友好，但我們的目標是合成高質量的陽離子（包括Cd和Mg）取代的CZTS薄膜，並製造基於這種薄膜的高效太陽能電池。因此，我們將1）使用共蒸發和前驅體/硫化方法，通過優化找到該類薄膜的最佳反應/生長條件。 2）優化這些陽離子與Zn之間的比率以實現最大轉換效率。 3）設計並調控帶隙結構進一步提高電池性能。 4）研究該類薄膜的結構，光學和電學性質，並闡明陽離子取代和抑制反位取代的機制。上述Cd和Mg取代的實現，不僅能證明這些方案的可行性，而且有助於揭示這些複雜半導體薄膜中缺陷的物理特性。

14301318.label: Realisation of objectives
14301318.value: To realize objective 1, We successfully synthesized high quality Cu2Zn1-xMxSnS4 (M=Cd, Mg) thin films. The unique advantages of single-step co-evaporation for CZTS are demonstrated. Zn gradient was introduced to CZTS absorbers fabricated via this method. Self-compromised behavior of Sn content is investigated. To realize objective 2 ZnTe layer was used as a rear interface passivation layer for Cd alloyed CZTS thin-film solar cells. This layer was found to suppress the detrimental rear interface via a physical separating absorber and Mo and finally fuse with the absorber. With a 5 nm-thick ZnTe layer, we gain around 9% absolute increase in power conversion efficiency for the passivated cell, which is attributed to the increase in VOC and FF. To realize objective 3 We have systematically investigated the Rb incorporation effects on the quality of Cu2(Cd,Zn)SnS4 (CCZTS) thin films and related solar devices. The Rb incorporation could engineer both the bulk and interface significantly, specifically improving bulk quality with enhanced grains and suppressed defects, passivating the rear interface with less secondary phase accumulation, and forming a favorable front band alignment. Benefiting from these multifunctional benefits, carrier collection efficiency is greatly improved with the enhancement of short-circuit current density (JSC) and open-circuit voltage (VOC). As a result, a champion efficiency of 10.64% is achieved, which is the highest value for pure sulfide CZTS solar cells made by the thermal evaporation method. In addition, using SEM imaging, EDX mapping, and SIMS analysis, we have identified the locations of secondary ZnS particles formed in CZTS absorbers. While ZnS particles both near the rear interface and within the interior of the CZTS absorber were demonstrated to greatly reduce the photocurrent, they were also found to reduce the open circuit voltage, although to a lesser extent. To eliminate/reduce Zinc element aggregation near the rear interface of CZTS/Mo and avoid formation of ZnS particles, delaying Zn supply for a few minutes in preparing the precursors via thermal coevaporation of Cu, Zn, Sn, and S has been found to be an effective approach. By delaying Zn deposition for 2 min in the precursor, the diffusion of Zn to the Zn depletion region during the annealing/sulfuration process could well compensate for the aggregation effect of Zn and render Zn uniform in the resultant CZTS layer. The conversion efficiency was increased from ≈6.34% to ≈8.31%. To reallize objective 4 By intentionally controlling the precursor composition, the surface of CZTS can be modified to improve the quality of the Zn(O,S)/CZTS junction for the chemical bath-deposited Zn(O,S) buffer. Such a CZTS solar cell reaches a high conversion efficiency of 7.28%, the highest among all Zn(O,S)-based kesterite solar cells so far. The CZTS surface that can jointly work well with the Zn(O,S) buffer is further investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy. The results indicate that an ultrathin SnS layer exists on the CZTS surface and effectively raises the conduction band edge of the absorber surface to form a conduction band offset barrier of ≈0.40 eV, significantly better than that without the assistance of SnS layer. In addition, we demonstrated the qualitative similarity of defect thermodynamics and electronic properties in Cu2MgSnS4 (CMTS) to CZTS. We show SnMg to be abundant when in Sn- and Cu-rich condition, which can be detrimental, while defect properties are largely similar to CZTS in Sn- and Cu-poor. Under Sn- and Cu-poor chemical potential, there is a general increase in formation energy in most defects except SnMg, CuMg remains as the main contribution to p-type carriers, and SnMg may be detrimental because of a deep defect level in the mid gap and the possibility of forming defect complex SnMg+MgSn. Vacancy diffusion is studied using generalized gradient approximation, and we find similar vacancy diffusion properties for Cu vacancy and lower diffusion barrier for Mg vacancy, which may reduce possible Cu-Mg disorder in CMTS. These findings further confirm the feasibility of CMTS as an alternative absorber material to CZTS and suggest the possibility for tuning defect properties of CZTS, which is crucial for high photovoltaic performance. Also, we conducted diffusivity and band offset analysis of a graphene interlayer at the back contact of a copper zinc tin sulphide solar cell. The kinetics processes of S atom diffusion on and across the graphene plane with various defects are considered. While an S atom can easily diffuse on graphene with a diffusion barrier of 0.355 eV, it is hard to diffuse across the graphene plane with or without defects, with diffusion barriers ranging from 1.19 eV through a double vacancy to 8.66 eV across pristine graphene. In addition, a band offset calculation using a local potential alignment method was performed to understand the role of graphene in hole transport. We discover that the interpolation of Hartree potential data can largely improve the stability of the band offset algorithm, comparable to a core level alignment method. The band offset calculation results show that the Fermi level of graphene is 0.664 eV higher than the valence band maximum of CZTS. Therefore, graphene is a benign interlayer in the back contact that can facilitate hole collection. Our calculations suggest that graphene is a promising protective interlayer.

14301318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301318.value: We conducted important theoretical and experimental investigations on various strategies to tune the metal contents in both front contact and back contact to obtain optimized band structure and achieved record high solar conversion efficiencies. 1 High quality thin film of CZTS with different metal (Mg, Cd, Rb) alloyed are obtained. Zn gradient was successfully obtained to tune the band structure. See details in the research outputs 1, 2, 3 in part C. 2 ZnTe interlayer was found to be effective to protect the back contact in Cd alloyed CZTS cell. With this strategy, 9% increase in power conversion was achieved. See details in research outputs 4 in part C. 3 Rb was found to be very important metal element that largely enhance the solar cell efficiency. A champion efficiency of 10.64% CZTS cell was achieved with Rb incorporation that helps passivate the rear interface. See details in research outputs 5 in part C. 4 A delayed Zn incorporation strategy was discovered that improve the power conversion efficiency from 6.34% to 8.31%. The existence of the detrimental properties of Zn rich secondary phase was confirmed. See details in research outputs 6 in part C. 5 Extra Sn incorporation largely enhance the front interface quality and improved the efficiency of a new structure with ZnSO as buffer layer. See details in research outputs 7 in part C. 6 The CMTS defect and diffusion properties was found and CMTS was confirmed to have superior electronic properties than CZTS. The detrimental defects were discovered, and the vacancy mediated diffusion study was conducted. See details in research outputs 8 in part C. 7 Back contact of graphene was investigated and confirmed to protect the Mo contact. New algorithm based on the non-linear fitting of local potential largely improved the accuracy of the band offset calculations. See details in research outputs 9 in part C.

14301318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301318.value: Experimental studies of CMTS with accurate defect measurement can further illustrate the superior properties of CMTS cell. The physical origin of Sn on the front contact should be further investigated with the help of first principles calculations. There could be interesting codoping phenomena that largely reduce the interface lattice mismatch and provide intermediate states for electron collection. Various interface configurations should be tested and their electronic properties should be investigated.

14301318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301318.value: We have conducted new experimental strategies of co-evaporation that yields high quality CZTS cells with Cd/Mg and group one or group two metal alloyed. Several new strategies were tested and found to be effective to improve the band structure, back contact and front contact qualities: 1 A gradient of Zn was found to be effective to improve solar cell efficiency. 2 With Rb passivation, ZnTe insertion, the back contact was found to be largely improved. A record high CZTS cell efficiency was achieved with the alloy and passivation strategy. 3 Zn delayed incorporation was found to be effective to improve the power conversion. 4 Extra Sn incorporation showed an interesting efficiency enhancement in Cd free cell which can have very good impact in environment. Theoretical investigation was conducted to illustrate interesting defect physics of CMTS and novel strategies on back contact passivation. 1 The defect physics of CMTS is clear now with our theoretical investigation and the kinetic process was investigated. 2 New algorithm was discovered during our theoretical investigation on the graphene interlayer insertion strategy which is confirmed to be effective to protect the back contact and reduce back contact defects.

14301418.value: 磷基材料在鈉離子電池負極的應用

14301418.label: Project Objectives
14301418.value: To fabricate a series of composite materials composed of transition metal (e.g. Ti), phosphorus, and carbon using high energy mechanical milling. The ratio of transition metal/phosphorus/carbon, and the ball milling parameters will be varied in a systematic manner to obtain a wide range of transition metal/phosphorus/carbon composite materials with different phase composition and microstructure, in particular, to obtain composite material with and without the formation of transition metal phosphides. To characterize the as-fabricated composite materials for comprehensive information on the chemical composition, bonding and/or interaction between compositional elements, phase composition, size of individual phases, and microstructure/electronic structure of the composite materials. Correlation will be established between the material design/fabrication parameters and the resulted chemical/structural characteristics of the composite materials. To evaluate the electrochemical properties of the composite anode. Coin cells will be assembled for the measuring the electrochemical properties of the respective composite anodes. Correlation will be established between the electrochemical performance of the composite anode and its chemical/structural characteristics. Ex situ experiments will be carried out on representative samples to understand the dynamical evolution of chemical composition, bonding, phases, and microstructure of the composite material upon sodiation/desodiation. Key factors to achieve high reversible capacity and long cycle stability in the phosphorous based composite anode will be identified.

14301418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301418.value: Phosphorus is a most promising candidate for anode applications in sodium ion batteries due to its highest theoretical capacity （2596 mA h/g）and reasonably low redox voltage (~0.6 V vs. Na/Na+), implying achievable high energy density. Nevertheless, experimentally pure phosphorous anode suffers from fast capacity decay during cycling and low initial coulomb efficiency. These are caused by intrinsic characteristics of the phosphorous, including (1) low electrical conductivity (~10-14 S/cm); (2) instability of the Na-P phases; and (3) possible electrode pulverization due to sodiation induced volume expansion (390% to its original volume). Methods employed to tackle the above outstanding issues include making phosphorus/carbon composite and/or forming phosphide. However, the outcomes are either unsatisfactory or technically challenging for practical applications. In our preliminary work of Ti-P-C composite development for sodium ion battery anode, we have found that formation of stable Ti-P compound leads to low capacity. Nevertheless, when deliberately avoiding the compound formation between Ti and P, while maintaining the same chemical composition of the composite, a high reversible capacity and excellent cyclability with reasonable initial Coulomb efficiency can be obtained. Although the sodiation/desodiation details and the underlying mechanism(s) of such a composite anode remain unclear, our preliminary results suggest that the interplay among compositional elements in the phosphorus based composite is critical in determining its sodiation/desodiation chemistry and thus the electrochemical performance of the anode. Based on the preliminary results, we propose in the present work to develop phosphorus based anode materials composed of transition metal, phosphorus, and carbon. We will systematically vary both the material parameters (such as the choice of the transition metal, and the ratio of the compositional elements) and the fabrication conditions, in order to obtain a series of phosphorus based composites with different chemical composition, phase composition, and microstructural characteristics, and investigate their corresponding electrochemical properties. We aim at (1) identifying the optimum material/phase compositions and the microstructure of the composites for high reversible capacity and long cyclability; and (2) unravelling the underlying mechanisms that lead to the excellent electrochemical performance of such phosphorus based composite anode. The present proposal, if successful, will not only result in a novel family of phosphorous based composite materials with high reversible capacity and excellent cycle stability for anode applications in sodium ion batteries, but would also shed light on the design of a new electrode materials for energy storage applications in general. 在鈉離子電池中負極材料的開發中， 磷是最有希望的候選材料之一。它有極高的理論容量（2596 mA h / g）和相當低的氧化還原電壓（~0.6 V vs. Na / Na +）。然而，純磷負極的循環穩定性極差。製備磷/碳複合物和/或形成磷化物是兩類最普遍的提高磷負極的循環穩定性的方法。但兩者各有問題， 不是電極容量太低，就是在技術上不易普及。 在前期工作中，我們發現穩定的Ti-P化合物的形成導致低容量。然而，如果避免Ti和P之間的化合物形成， 便可以在保持複合物的相同化學組成的同時獲得具有合理的初始庫侖效率的高可逆容量和優異的循環穩定性。 基於前期工作的進展，我們提出開發由過渡金屬，磷和碳組成的磷基負極材料。我們將系統地改變材料參數（例如過渡金屬的選擇和組成元素的比例）和合成條件，以獲得具有不同化學組份和相組成的一系列磷基複合材料。表徵其微觀結構特徵，並研究其相應的電化學性質。我們的目標是（1）確定最佳的材料組份，相組成，和微觀結構，以實現高可逆容量和高循環穩定性; （2）揭示決定這種磷基複合電極優異電化學性能的機理。

14301418.label: Realisation of objectives
14301418.value: All three objective are fully addressed. For the first objective, we have fabricated a series of composite materials composed of transition metal, phosphorous, and carbon using high energy mechanical milling. Ti, Mn and Fe have been employed as the transition metal candidate. In each of the material system, the ratio of transition metal/phosphorus/carbon, and the ball milling parameters have been varied in a systematic manner. Composite materials with and without the formation of transition metal phosphides have been obtained. In realizing the second objective, the as-fabricated phosphorous containing materials are characterized using x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), energy dispersive x-ray (EDX) for their chemical composition; x-ray diffraction (XRD) and a few transmission electron microscopy based techniques for their microstructure and phase compositions. Correlation has been established between the material design/fabrication parameters and the resulted chemical/structural characteristics of the composite materials. To address the third objective, coin cells have been assembled for the measuring the electrochemical properties of the respective composite anodes. Ex situ TEM based methods are being developed to provide information for understanding the dynamical evolution of chemical composition, bonding, phases, and microstructure of the composite material upon sodiation/desodiation.

14301418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301418.value: The electrochemical performance of the P-based electrodes relies on both the activity of P in sodiation/desodiation and the its stability against other reactions. Among the several transition metal-P-C system tested, the phosphorous-Titanium-carbon system demonstrated the best cycle performance--we found that forming P−TiO2−C composites leads to changes of local chemistry in both titanium oxide and phosphorus, improving the electronic conductivity of the former and stabilizing the latter during repeated sodiation/desodiation cycles. The resulting composite anode thus delivers a high reversible capacity of 1147 mA h/g at a current density of 100 mA/g with reasonably good cyclability. Such a composite electrode also shows excellent rate performance by maintaining 81.5% of its original capacity when the discharge rate increased from 100 to 1000 mA/g. [Thesis, D. Lan, 2019] Similar results have been obtained in the P-Fe-C, and P-Mn-C system but with inferior electrochemical properties. In summary, all composite materials without phosphide formation have high reversible capacity (around 1000 mA/g) and improved cycling performance (compared to pure phosphorous or corresponding phosphides). However, the improvement on the cycling stability of these P based materials remains limited. A number of hypotheses can be found in the literature, trying to explain the major reason for the poor cycle performance of P-based materials, but its origin remains arguable. In this regard, we have developed an ex situ TEM based characterization method, trying to monitor the evolution of the respective P-based electrode material in a cycle dependent manner [Lin et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2022]. By taking a phosphide material of Cu4SnP10 nanowire electrode as an example, we show that the electrode's phase/structural change can be systematically investigated using a comprehensive set of ex situ transmission electron microscopy-based techniques, which are ideal for decay mechanism analysis of electrode materials of amorphous nature and with nanoscale structural evolution. The compositional elements of Cu4SnP10 nanowires are found to be spatially redistributed at a nanometer scale upon the initial sodiation, and this is partially reversible in the following desodiation process. Damage accumulates until a critical size of phase separation/segregation is reached, when the active material loss takes place, leading to fast deterioration of the entire Cu4SnP10 nanowire structure and thus its electrochemical performance. The phase segregation driven-active material loss is found to dominate the cycle-dependent capacity decay of the Cu4SnP10 nanowire electrode.

14301418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301418.value: In the failure analysis of Cu4SnP10 nanowires anode, we identified nanoscale spatial redistribution of the compositional element in the electrode materials and their partial reversibility upon electrochemical cycling. Effects of phase segregation accumulates and eventually results in the active material loss upon cycling, being the major cause of the drastic capacity decay of the phosphide anode. The finding in the present work suggests that suppression of phase separation and stabilization of the SEI (to retain the separated phase) can be effective methods for improving the cycle performance phosphide electrode. In this regard, we will attempt both artificial SEI formation or adjusting the electrolyte composition for in situ SEI manipulation in future works, in order to extend the cycle life of P-based anode for Na-ion batteries.

14301418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301418.value: The present project shows that chemical stabilization of P is important for this electrochemical performance. The P-based chemistry must allow effective sodiation and at the same time avoid P loss upon desodiation. In this regard, composite materials of P, transition metal oxide, and C have demonstrated improved cycle performance when P is uniformly dispersed in a matrix of carbon and transition metal oxide. However, the requirement on the uniformity is challenging with the current technology, limiting the amount of active materials (P) allowed in the composite. On the other hand, transition metal phosphide materials allows effective sodiation, but suffers from loss of P in the following desodiation due to the phase separation. The developed cycle-dependent ex situ TEM-based chemical and structural characterization provides a feasible method for studying the degradation mechanism of electrode materials. The excellent spatial resolution associated with the microscopy-based method enables the disclosure of compositional/structural evolution at a finite length scale, being important for failure analysis of electrode materials in general. It is particularly useful for accessing the structural/phase change of amorphous materials at nanoscale, providing a promising method for dynamic analysis of electrode failure in batteries.
