14301618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301618.value: 本研究的各課題旨在拓展帶有刪失數據的分位數迴歸模型，以處理在各類抽樣機制下與時間相關的協變量有關的問題。這類問題由於（右）刪失的存在而變得複雜，因為刪失帶來了部分觀測不到的數據。 在給定自變量的值的情況下，傳統迴歸試圖估計因變量的條件期望值，而分位數迴歸的目的則是估計因變量的條件分位數。相比均值迴歸僅通過中心量度提供的偏面總結，分位數迴歸模型提供了一個靈活而全面的替代方法，這體現在，如果我們估計了足夠數量的分位數，那麽因變量的分佈也能被隨之估計。此外，與均值迴歸模型相比，分位數迴歸也被認為是對離群值更加穩健的模型。 這些優點也解釋了為何分位數迴歸作為標準的建模工具之一，在經濟學、生物或醫學統計學，以及其他學科中受到廣泛應用。在統計學的各個研究領域裡面，分位數迴歸也經常出現在生存分析的研究中，並且正受到越來越多的關注。 除了在先前的研究中討論和分析的問題，包括全域綫性假設之外，還存在著例如如何處理與時間相關的協變量等的諸多挑戰；對偏倚數據的處理也缺乏相應的工具。考慮到這些開放性問題的重要性，本研究嘗試在更少限制性假設的情況下提供解決方案，以期補充文獻上相關的討論。 由於帶刪失數據的分位數迴歸模型已被廣泛應用於解決各學科中的各種問題，本研究有望為生存分析和分位數迴歸的研究前沿作出貢獻。

14301618.label: Realisation of objectives
14301618.value: The three objectives of the project have been achieved in this proposal for various projects. 1. One publication output entitled “Censored Interquantile Regression Model with Time-Dependent Covariates” (see Publication #5 in Part C) proposes a new class of quantile-based regression models with time-dependent covariates for censored data. Conventionally, censored quantile regression stipulates a specific, pointwise conditional quantile of the survival time given covariates. Despite its model flexibility and straightforward interpretation, the pointwise formulation oftentimes yields rather unstable estimates across neighbouring quantile levels with large variances. The models proposed aim to capture the relationship between the failure time and the covariate processes of a target population that falls within a specific quantile bracket. The pooling of information within a homogeneous neighbourhood facilitates more efficient estimates hence more consistent conclusion on statistical significances of the variables concerned. This new formulation can also be regarded as a generalization of the accelerated failure time model for survival data in the sense that it relaxes the assumption of global homogeneity for the error at all quantile levels. By introducing a class of weighted rank-based estimation procedure, our framework allows a quantile-based inference on the covariate effect with a less restrictive set of assumptions. Consistency and weak convergence of the proposed estimator are established via empirical process theory. The first objective, is therefore, achieved for this work. Numerical studies demonstrate that the proposed estimator outperforms existing alternatives under various settings in terms of smaller empirical biases and standard deviations. A perturbation-based resampling method is also developed to reconcile the asymptotic distribution of the parameter estimates. The second and the third objectives of this project are also achieved. There are some follow-up extensions that are currently under investigation. Some preliminary studies show promising results along this line of research. 2. Another publication entitled “On asymptotic equivalence of the NPMLE of a monotone density and a Grenander-type estimator in multi-sample biased sampling models” show thats the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) of the decreasing density function in the s-sample biased sampling models, is asymptotically equivalent to a Grenander-type estimator, namely the left-continuous slope of the least concave majorant of the NPMLE of the distribution function in the larger model without imposing the monotonicity assumption. Since the two estimators favor different proof directions in establishing weak convergence, we require additional results for both estimators so that the two estimators can be considered jointly in a unified approach. For instance, we employ an analytic argument for showing the tightness of an inverse processes associated with the NPMLE, since a conventional geometric approach used in the literature cannot be employed due to multiple biased samples. The first objective of the proposal is hence satisfied also for this related project. We demonstrate other results using numerical simulation and a real data illustration which makes us hopefully fulfil the objectives #2 and #3 of the proposal. We are currently finishing a manuscript with results that are based on this work and Chan et al. (2018). The s-sample biased sampling problem is something worthwhile to investigate further. 3. The three objectives are also achieved for another paper entitled " Variance Reduction for Risk Measure Estimation with Importance Sampling" (see Publication #4). In the field of risk management, Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) are two standard risk measures that are widely adopted. Simulation-based approaches including nested simulation and least-squares Monte Carlo are effective strategies to yield reliable estimates of these risk measures, but there remain open questions on how importance sampling can be incorporated to improve estimation efficiency. In this paper, we extend the scope of importance sampling from simple Monte Carlo to nested simulation settings and its adaptations for American-type options; we also establish the asymptotic consistency of importance sampling. Numerical results consistent with our theoretical analysis are provided to verify its effectiveness. Other projects, say Publications #8 and 9, also achieve the three objectives stated for portfolio optimization and censored quantile regression in a distributed context. All of these results are presented in regional/international conferences also. Reference: Chan, K. C. G., Ling, H. K., Sit, T. and Yam, S. C. P. (2018). Estimation of a monotone density in s-sample biased sampling models. The Annals of Statistics 46 2125–2152.

14301618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301618.value: The main focus of this research project is to develop proper treatments for handling various issues related to censored quantile regression. Existing methods, although have been recognised as effective tools in modelling specific quantile level(s) of event time distribution given covariates, some of the technical issues remain unanswered. A novel and insightful idea in the literature reframes the conventional quantile regression check function framework (see Koenker and Bassett, 1978; Econometrica and Koenker, 2005) into a martingle-based, counting process formulation (see Peng and Huang, 2008; JASA and Wang and Wang, 2009; JASA). While this idea intricately and naturally makes use of the conventional techniques in survival analysis, there was, however, to the best of our knowledge, no discussion on how the inferential efficiency can be improved under the said martingale framework. We (see Publication #7) have established a computable weight function which achieves the most efficient estimates under a very broad class of possible Z-measureable weight functions. The first version of the manuscript was finalized in Q4 2019. Unfortunately, possibly because of the COVID-19 pandemic, we experienced a long response time from the journal during which some substantial extra work was added to enrich the manuscript. Another main work developed for this project is Publication #5 in which local homogeneity was first studied in the literature. Our work attempts to fill up the gap between the cases with global homogeneity (AFT) and point-wise heterogeneity (CQR). The pooling of information within a homogeneous neighbourhood facilitates more efficient estimates hence more consistent conclusion on statistical significances of the variables concerned. This interquantile regression model can also handle time-dependent covariates, which ccur frequently in biomedical and epidemiological research. These are covariates whose values change over the duration of follow‐up. Examples include biomarkers that change over follow‐up or cumulative exposure to medications. The methodology developed can yield more stable results and possibly more meaningful interpretation. As discussed in the paper, the new perspective provided can give physicians and researchers a set of more representative statistics to describe the distributions of interest. Other publications including Publications #2, 6 and 9 discuss other various issues related to censored observations under the network context, non-parametric MLE consideration and a distributed setting, respectively. Some works on quantile-related risk management models are also published (see, e.g. #4 and #8). They appear in reputable journals and/or book series. All the aforementioned results are also presented in various regional/international conferences.

14301618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301618.value: Despite the desirable results that we have developed in this proposal, one of the limitations that many of the projects discussed share is its inability of handling time-dependent covariates under conditionally independent assumption between the failure time and the censoring time given covariates under an online manner without local homogeneity. In various medical studies, it is very often to encounter situations where subjects’ attributes vary as time proceeds and the vast volume of records may enter the study in a streaming manner. It is interesting to extend or generalise the current settings so that time-dependent covariates can be incorporated in an online inference model in which case the applicability of the models concerned will be much more expanded. Given the fact that under the big data era, the volume of data has immensely increased along with the development of data-generating, extracting, addressing, storage, and output technologies, particularly the connected Internet of Things (IoT) devices along as well as new database technologies, e.g., NoSQL, it is a research direction with good potential. Some preliminary work including simulations and theoretical analysis have been carried out.

14301618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301618.value: While traditionally means and medians are typical summary statistics to describe distributions concerned, it is more informative to model the quantiles concerned through quantile regression. Another benefit that quantile regression estimates enjoy is their robustness against outliers in the response measurements. All these desirable features make quantile regression valuable tools for modelling. In medical studies, censored observations are frequently observed, it is therefore useful to expand the current literature on censored quantile regression. Existing methods may result in unstable numerical results, for instance, or do not discuss possible solutions of improving numerical efficiency (accuracy). Through the extensions introduced in this project, censored quantile regression model can be an effective tool for more settings with better efficiency. It is expected that the methodologies developed can benefit various different end users who are interested in efficient, and accurate quantiles modelling for time-to-event data.

14301718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301718.value: Image segmentation is one of the fundamental tasks in image processing. It is to outline different objects of interest in a given image so that high-level programs or experts can identify and analyze the objects more easily and accurately. It has numerous engineering, medical, and commercial applications. For examples, ophthalmologists can diagnose diabetes patients more efficiently if the blood vessels in retina angiography images can be segmented automatically and biologists may predict the rate of deforestation more accurately if the forest regions are identified correctly in hyperspectral images obtained from remote sensing satellites. Since there are many different types of images and they are usually corrupted by different kinds of noises and blurs, the segmentation task is intrinsically difficult. Our proposal is to design new efficient and accurate segmentation methods for two major fields in image processing: vessel segmentation in angiography imaging and hyperspectral image classification. In angiography image segmentation, the aim is to correctly detect big and small vessels in a patient’s body and repair small occlusions. The images are usually degraded by non-Gaussian noise and blurred by the patients' motions. Hyperspectral images (HSI) measure the spectral responses of terrains on the surface of the Earth. HSI classification is to use the spectral responses of the pixels to identify which classes the pixels belong to (e.g. road, tree or water). Spectral methods that use only spectral responses may give noisy results. A segmentation map that exploits spatial information among neighboring pixels can be added to increase the accuracy of the classification. The segmentation approach we use is based on an effective variational methodology that we developed recently. Its idea is to separate the segmentation into two stages. In the first stage, we denoise and deblur the given image by a restoration model to get a clean and smooth approximation of the given image. In the second stage, we threshold this approximation to get the segmented solution. For general images, our approach produces results that are better than most existing methods under various blurs and noises. It has been extended to color images and sophisticated convex models with nonconvex terms. We will modify and adapt our methodology to design novel efficient and accurate methods for the two fields. We will provide new theory such as convergence of our new algorithms and compare them with state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness for publicly available databases in the two fields. 圖像分割是圖像處理中的基本任務之一。它指的是將給定圖像中的各個感興趣的部分細分出來，以便高級程序或專家可以更容易和準確地識別和分析它們。圖像分割在工程，醫療和商業中有着广泛的應用。例如，如果視網膜血管造影图像中的血管可以被自動分割，则有助于眼科醫生更有效地診斷糖尿病患者；如果能從遙感衛星獲得的高光譜圖像中正確的識別森林區域，那麼生物學家則可以更準確地預測滥伐森林的速率。由於圖像有很多不同的類型，而且它們通常被不同類型的噪音和模糊所破壞，所以分割任務本質上來說很困難。我們的計劃是對兩個圖像處理中的主要領域-- 血管造影成像的血管分割和高光譜圖像的分類 -- 設計新的高效準確的圖像分割方法。 血管造影圖像分割的主要目的是如何能正確地檢測患者身體中的大小血管以及修復其中的小閉塞。這些圖像通常會被高斯噪聲和患者運動引起的模糊所破壞。高光譜圖像是測量地球表面地形的光譜響應。此類圖像的分類是使用像素的光譜響應來識別像素屬於哪些類別（例如道路，樹木或水）。僅使用光譜響應的光譜方法有可能給出帶噪音的結果。利用相鄰像素點之間的空間信息將有助於提高分類的準確性。 我們使用的分割方法是基於我們最近提出的一種有效的變分方法。它的想法是將分割分為兩個階段。在第一個階段，我們通過求解修復模型對給定圖像進行去噪和去模糊，以獲得給定圖像的乾淨且平滑的近似。在第二個階段，我們對此近似進行閾值處理來得到最終的分割結果。對於一般的具有各種模糊和噪音的圖像，我們的方法得到的結果比大多數現有的方法更優。此方法已經被擴展到處理彩色圖像和復雜的擁有非凸項的凸模型中。在此計劃書中，我們將改進和調整我們的方法，對上述提到的兩個應用領域設計新穎高效和準確的方法。我們將提供新的理論，例如算法的收斂性，並將其與最新的算法在速度，準確性和穩健性方面用上述兩個領域的公開的測試數據進行比較。

14301718.label: Realisation of objectives
14301718.value: In Paper 1 listed in Part C, Item 8, we have developed with the first co-I (who unfortunately died in the summer of 2019) a new two-stage method for LiDAR and hyperspectral image classification by combining pixel-wise classifiers from machine learning, such as the classical support vector machine (SVM), with a convex variant of the classical variational segmentation method, the Mumford–Shah model. Our proposed method effectively utilizes both spectral and spatial information of the data sets and is fast because only convex minimization is needed in addition to the SVMs. Experimental results on three widely utilized real hyperspectral data sets indicate that our method is very competitive in accuracy, timing, and the number of parameters when compared with current state-of-the-art methods. Hyperspectral images are usually obtained by satellites flying over the Earth, which are subject to atmospheric blur. Adaptive optics is a commonly used technique to correct the phase distortions caused by the Earth’s atmosphere to improve the image quality of ground-based imaging systems. However, the observed images still suffer from the blur caused by the adaptive optics residual wavefront. In Paper 2, we propose a model for reconstructing the residual phase in high resolution from a sequence of deformable mirror data. Our model is based on turbulence statistics and the Taylor frozen flow hypothesis with knowledge of the wind velocities in atmospheric turbulence layers. A tomography problem for the phase distortions from different altitudes is solved to get a high-quality phase reconstruction. We provide a theoretical analysis of the existence of a minimizer of the objective function. Numerical simulations are carried out to show the effectiveness of our approach. Paper 3 presents a probabilistic semi-supervised learning (SSL) framework based on sparse graph structure learning. Our proposed SSL model can learn a sparse weighted graph from the unlabeled high-dimensional data and a small amount of labeled data and deal with the noise of the input data. This will be precisely the case for hyperspectral image classification, where we have many images from satellites while labeling of pixels is tedious and costly. Extensive experiments on various data sets show promising results in the setting of SSL compared with many existing methods and significant improvements on small amounts of labeled data. Paper 4 examined the degree to which two machine learning approaches can better characterize change detection in the context of a current conservation challenge, artisanal small-scale gold mining (ASGM). We obtained Sentinel-2 imagery and consulted with domain experts to construct an open-source labeled land-cover change dataset. This dataset focuses on the Madre de Dios (MDD) region in Peru, a hotspot of ASGM activity. We also generated datasets of active ASGM areas in other countries (Venezuela, Indonesia, and Myanmar) for out-of-sample testing. With these labeled data, we utilized a supervised (E-ReCNN) and semi-supervised (SVM-STV) approach to study binary and multi-class change within mining ponds in the MDD region. The results showed that E-ReCNN could accurately detect specific and object-oriented environmental changes related to ASGM. E-ReCNN is scalable to areas outside the focal area and is a method of change detection that can be extended to other forms of land-use modification. Paper 5 proposed a novel framework that utilizes both spatial and spectral information for classifying pixels in hyperspectral images. The method consists of three stages. In the first stage, the pre-processing stage, the Nested SlidingWindow algorithm is used to reconstruct the original data by enhancing the consistency of neighboring pixels, and then Principal Component Analysis is used to reduce the dimension of data. In the second stage, Support Vector Machines are trained to estimate each class's pixel-wise probability map using the images' spectral information. Finally, a smoothed total variation model is applied to ensure spatial connectivity in the classification map by smoothing the class probability tensor. We demonstrate the superiority of our method against three state-of-the-art algorithms on six benchmark hyperspectral datasets with 10 to 50 training labels for each class. The results show that our method gives the overall best performance in accuracy even with a very small set of labeled pixels. Especially, the gain in accuracy with respect to other state-of-the-art algorithms increases when the number of labeled pixels decreases, and, therefore, our method is more advantageous to be applied to problems with a small training set. Hence, it is of great practical significance since expert annotations are often expensive and difficult to collect.

14301718.value: Image segmentation is one of the fundamental tasks in image processing. It is to outline different objects of interest in a given image so that high-level programs or experts can identify and analyze the objects more easily and accurately. It has numerous engineering, medical, and commercial applications. For example, biologists may predict the rate of deforestation more accurately if the forest regions are identified correctly in hyperspectral images obtained from remote sensing satellites. 14301818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301818.value: 在超冷(<10-9 開耳文)溫度下，粒子德布羅意的波長會變長，此時，粒子的量子性質就會變得重要。與傳統觀念相反，很多理論工作已經表明，借助量子力學效應，如隧道效應和共振，在超冷溫度下化學反應仍然可以有效地發生。在2010年JILA的KRb實驗中已經觀察到了超冷化學反應，但由於製備超冷分子樣品非常困難，目前還沒有用其他超冷分子樣品研究超冷化學的報到。同時，與超冷化學反應相關的很多問題很沒有答案，在沒有化學反應通道時超冷分子的碰撞動力學就是其中之一。 在2016年，我們小組成功實現了高密度超冷絕對基態NaRb分子樣品的製備。在本課題中，基於這一成就和一些最近的進展，我們將對原子+ NaRb的基本碰撞過程進行一系列詳細的研究。我們調查的重點是了解非反應性Rb + NaRb的碰撞及其對溫度，塞曼和斯塔克效應的依賴。利用由超冷溫度提供的高能量分辨率和我們對實驗參數的精確控制能力，我們將在超冷碰撞中研究目前還未觀測到涉及基態雙鹼分子的散射共振。同時，我們也計劃研究碰撞中混沌行為的可能性。為了充分理解實驗結果，我們的理論合作者將計算我們體系的ab initio勢能面，並將基於此計算的碰撞性質和我們的實驗結果進行比較。

14301818.label: Realisation of objectives
14301818.value: The main purpose of this project is to investigate collisions between ultracold atoms and ultracold ground-state diatomic molecules. This is a system just one atom more than the well-understood atom-atom system, but it is already complicated enough for the current brute force computation methods. In addition, knowledges gain from atom-molecule collisions are also expected to shed light on the more complicated molecule-molecule collisions. This project is based on the previous works supported by RGC in which we have successfully prepared the ultracold ground-state NaRb molecule by association of ultracold Na and Rb atoms. There are four objectives in this project. All of them have been addressed. Based on these investigations, several papers have been published or are under preparation. 1. Technical improvement of the apparatus We built a pancake shaped crossed beam 1064 nm optical trap and added two additional low-power 852 nm beams to fine tune the overlap between Na and Rb. This two-color optical trap works more robust than the single frequency magic wavelength 946 nm trap used previously. This also saved us from the transfer from the 1064 nm trap to the 946 nm trap and reduced the instability of the atom and molecule numbers. In the new system, we are now routinely producing 2*10^4 Feshbach molecules. We also improved the atom removal by replacing the magnetic field gradient and microwave with all light pulses. This shortened the time of the removal procedure to within 1 ms which gives us a lot more flexibility in preparing the atom-molecule mixture with larger molecule numbers. We also studied the anisotropic polarizability of NaRb and realized tuning of the rotational coherence with the polarization angle. A paper on this work was published in PRA. To study the magnetic field dependence of the atom-molecule collisions, it is necessary to be able to stabilize the B field in the ms time scale. To this end, we developed a feedward scheme and added a pair of fast small coils. This has allowed us to change the magnetic field from 20 G to 600 G (starting from 335 G) within 4.5 ms. The magnetic field fluctuation is less than 150 mG. 2. We have created the Na + NaRb or Rb + NaRb atom and molecule mixtures in a controllable way. We first studied the difference between the reactive Na + NaRb case and the non-reactive Rb + NaRb case at 335 G. We did not find evidence that the reactive Na + NaRb and the non-reactive Rb + NaRb collisions are difference due to the different reactivity. Instead, the measured loss rates are both close their universal limits. The temperature dependence of the atom-molecule is difficult to study since the temperature is very difficult to control due to the heating following the association of molecules. 3. We then focus on the magnetic field dependence of the Rb + NaRb collisions. With the fast magnetic field ramping technique, we studied the collisions of Rb in |F=1, mF =1> with NaRb prepared in two different nuclear spin states. Within the range of magnetic field from 20 G to 600 G, we discovered more than 50 resonances in each of the scattering channel. We performed a statistical analysis and extracted the three-atom density of states (DOS). We also compared the resonance distribution to the Wigner-Dyson model and found preliminary evidence of chaotic behavior. We are now finishing the data analysis and a paper is under preparation. 4. We also studied the possibility of tuning the Rb + NaRb collisions with electric field. As our electrodes are placed outside the glass vacuum cell, this turns out to be difficult as the glass cell can be charged at electric field above ~ 800 V/cm. This results in residual electric field and makes the Raman transfer unreliable. We then decided to halt the control of NaRb with dc electric field and pursue other ways to see the dipolar effect. We studied the resonant dipolar collision between NaRb molecule in difference rotational states. The loss rates with resonant dipolar interaction are found to be 10 to 100 times higher than that between identical molecules. For collision channel not of the lowest energy threshold, the loss contribution from hyperfine changing is also observed. A paper on this work was published in Physical Review Research.

14301818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301818.value: 1. Observation of resonant dipolar collisions in ultracold 23Na87Rb rotational mixtures. NaRb prepared in rotational levels of opposite parities can interaction via the resonant dipolar interaction. This couples many partial waves into the collision and opens many additional loss channels. We observed 10-to-100-fold enhancement of the loss rate. This work has been published in Phys. Rev. Research 3, 013016 (2021). 2. Anisotropic polarizability of ultracold ground-state 23Na87Rb molecules. We studied the anisotropic polarizability of NaRb and realized tuning of the rotational coherence with the polarization angle. This capability will enable us to probe dipolar effects with longer coherence time. This work was published in Phys. Rev. A 103, 023332 (2021). 3. Measuring of the Feshbach molecule binding energy. We measured the binding energy of Feshbach molecules by the dissociation method. Based on this, we performed a precise calibration of the parameters for the 347.64 G Feshbach resonance. A paper based on this work has been published in Phys. Rev. A 105, 023313 (2022). 4. Probing Photoinduced Two-Body Loss of Ultracold Molecules. In collaboration with Silke Ospelkaus’ group in Germany, we studied the loss mechanism of non-reactive ground-state molecules. Our results shows that the two-molecule complex lifetime is still not fully understood. This is pushing the frontier of the theory and has triggered many interests. A joint paper is published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 163401 (2021). 5. NaRb in optical lattices. We realized a long-lived NaRb sample by loading them into a deep 3D optical lattice potential. We also obtained a nuclear spin coherence time of several seconds. This work is published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 223201 (2022).

14301818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301818.value: At extremely low temperatures of about a millionth of a degree above absolute zero, when the de Broglie wavelengths of particles become long, their quantum nature becomes important. At these ultracold temperatures, contrary to conventional conceptions, many theoretical works have shown that chemical reactions can still happen efficiently with the help of quantum mechanical effects such as tunneling and resonances. While this ultracold chemical reaction was already observed in 2010, few new experiments have been reported since then due to the challenge in creating high density and ultracold samples of ground-state molecules. Meanwhile, many questions, such as the collision dynamics with ultracold molecules when no chemical reaction is allowed, remain to be clarified. In this proposal, based on our previous work on creating a high-density sample of ground-state NaRb molecules, we carried out a series of detailed collision investigations on the atoms + NaRb elementary processes. The focus of our investigation is on understanding the non-reactive Rb + NaRb collision and its dependence on magnetic field. We found many scattering resonances between Rb and NaRb and discovered evidence of quantum chaos. We also performed several other works with pure NaRb molecules and developed various ways to control their collisions and coherences. Our work will help to understand the ultracold molecular collisions and finally enable ultracold molecules as a new system for studying quantum many-body physics.

14301918.label: Project Objectives
14301918.value: To establish novel regression models in the presence of imaging predictors, latent variables, and nonignorable nonresponses. The models under consideration include cross-sectional/longitudinal scalar-on-image (SoI) regression and latent factor-on-image regression (LoI). To develop novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model selection. Efficient FPCA techniques are proposed to reduce the dimensionality of imaging predictors. Bayesian approaches, coupled with various efficient sampling schemes and model/variable selection procedures, are also developed to conduct statistical inference. To develop efficient and freely available computer programs/packages for producing statistical results. We utilize freely available software, such as R and C++, to ensure that the codes are user friendly. To apply the developed methodologies in the analysis of real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and other settings. The current project is motivated by a longitudinal study of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Its main purpose is to investigate the associations between clinical outcomes (e.g., cognitive decline) and MRI brain images/biomarker variables. Various test scores for characterizing cognitive decline from different perspectives are collected longitudinally and subjected to missingness. The proposed models and methodologies allow for a systematic investigation of the association between MRI brain images and other covariates and AD progression. Such comprehensive studies can provide new insights into the treatment and prevention of AD.

14301918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301918.value: Medical imaging data are widely used in modern healthcare, especially in the prognosis, screening, diagnosis, and treatment of various diseases. Revealing the association between medical images and clinical outcomes is critical because medical images can be translated into clinically useful information that facilitates clinical decision making. However, imaging observations are characterized by high dimensionalities, which hinder regression analyses. Despite numerous studies on regression analyses with functional/imaging predictors, previous work present limitations. First, they often assumed that responses are complete or missing at random. This assumption is violated when the characteristics of nonresponses affect their missingness. Disregarding this feature may lead to biased estimation results. Thus, appropriately modeling nonresponses is important but challenging because the missingness mechanism is generally unknown and may introduce additional model identifiability issues. Second, available methods usually consider a scalar response. However, the outcome of interest may be a latent factor (e.g., cognitive/non-cognitive ability) that should be measured by multiple observed variables. Therefore, latent factors should be accommodated by using a joint modeling approach that integrates factor analysis for characterizing the latent factor and a regression model for examining the association between imaging predictors and the latent factor. Third, the majority of existing scalar-on-function/image regression analyses focused on mean regression. However, covariates may exert different effects at different quantiles of the response variable. Quantile regression offers a complete view of covariate effects on the entire distribution, including the upper and lower tails, of the response. A comprehensive view of covariate effects on response distribution may be of particular interest in substantive research. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to develop novel methodologies to address the aforementioned problems systematically. This study aims to develop scalar- and latent factor-on-image regression in the presence of nonignorable nonresponses. Mean and quantile regressions are considered. We propose a two-stage procedure for statistical inference. The first stage uses functional principal component analysis to reduce model dimensionality. The second stage incorporates the extracted major principal imaging scores into the regression. A Bayesian approach is developed for regression analysis due to the following reasons. First, the Bayesian approach can powerfully and efficiently manage complex models with latent variables and can utilize prior knowledge. Second, relevant developments in the Bayesian framework are extremely limited. Computer programs/packages for statistical analysis are also developed and made freely available to practitioners. The developed methodologies are applied to real problems in Hong Kong and other settings.

14301918.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. We have established novel regression models in the presence of imaging predictors, latent variables, and nonignorable nonresponses. The models under consideration include cross-sectional/longitudinal scalar-on-image (SoI) and latent factor-on-image regression (LoI). The objective in Item 1 of Section 5.2 (related to the model establishment) is fully achieved. 2. We have developed novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model selection. Efficient FPCA techniques are proposed to reduce the dimensionality of imaging predictors. Bayesian approaches, various efficient sampling schemes, and model/variable selection procedures are also developed for statistical inference. The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 (related to inference methodology) are fully accomplished. 3. We have developed efficient and freely available computer programs/packages for producing statistical results. We utilize freely available software, such as R and C++, to ensure the codes are user-friendly. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to computer programs) are fully achieved. 4. 14301918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301918.value: Our main findings and research outcomes are represented by 17 research papers (16 published and one under revision) (see “Research Outputs” in Section 8 of Part C). Specifically, 1. We have established novel regression models in the presence of imaging predictors, latent variables, and nonignorable nonresponses. The models under consideration include cross-sectional/longitudinal scalar-on-image (SoI), image-on-scalar (IoS), and latent factor-on-image regression (LoI). Please refer to Items 1, 2, 12, 13, and 16 in Section 8. In addition, we have developed many valuable extensions of the proposed model to cope with complex research settings. In particular, we have extended the proposed model to general functional and mixed-mode data and considered mean, quantile, and expectile regression. Please refer to Items 3, 6, 7, 9, 12, 15, 16, and 17 in Section 8. 2. We have developed novel and sound statistical methods for estimation and model selection. In particular, we have applied FPCA techniques to reduce the dimensionality of imaging predictors and developed efficient Bayesian approaches, coupled with various sampling schemes, for statistical inference. Please refer to Items 1, 2, 11, 12, 15, 16, and 17 in Section 8. In addition, we have developed frequentist approaches as valuable alternatives to the problems considered and developed novel procedures to tackle nonignorable or blockwise missingness. Please refer to Items 2, 3, 4, 9, 11, and 14 in Section 8. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs for producing estimation and model selection results. All the computer codes have been published or provided on websites that are freely accessible to practitioners (see the corresponding papers in Section 8). 4. We have applied the developed methodologies in analyzing real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and other settings. The real-life applications include but are not limited to (1) type 2 diabetes and its complications data collected by the Prince of Wales Hospital at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Items 6 and 13 in Section 8), (2) Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data (Items 1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 12, 16, and 17 in Section 8), (3) general health survey study concerning the cognitive impairment and mortality of Chinese elders (Item 8 in Section 8), (4) the medical cost study data for chronic heart failure patients from the University of Virginia Health System (Item 4 in Section 8), (5) Tecator and cookie dough data (Item 9 in Section 8), (6) Chinese air pollution and meteorological dataset (Item 15 in Section 8), (7) patient data from the Aerobics Center Longitudinal Study conducted at the Cooper Clinic in Dallas, Texas (Item 10 in Section 8), and (8) the Boston housing data (Item 5 in Section 8).

14301918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301918.value: The models considered in this project can be extended to simultaneously incorporate multivariate longitudinal, imaging, and time-to-event data. Although such an extension is out of this project's scope, we have considered this vital extension and submitted a paper to the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C. A revision of this paper was invited and submitted; see Item 17 in Section 8. Moreover, considering high-dimensional genetic data together with imaging predictors is of considerable interest and worth investigating. We will consider this further development in the future.

14301918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301918.value: Medical imaging data are widely used in modern healthcare, especially in the prognosis, screening, diagnosis, and treatment of various diseases. Revealing the association between medical images and clinical outcomes is critical because medical images can be translated into useful information that facilitates clinical decision-making. This study proposed novel scalar- and latent factor-on-image regression in the presence of nonignorable nonresponses. Compared to conventional regression analysis with imaging predictors, the newly proposed models have several unique features, such as accommodating latent responses, addressing nonignorable missingness, and constructing quantile and expectile regression. The proposed models and developed methodologies are original and applicable to various problems in medical, behavioral, social, and psychological research settings. The novel methods developed in this project have addressed the most challenging issues in regression with imaging data and thus contribute significantly to complex imaging and mixed-mode data analysis. The applications of the developed methodologies have produced essential findings and new insights into vital problems in different research areas. A total of 17 papers (16 were published, and one was revised and resubmitted) in international journals represent the primary outputs. Some extensions of the proposed methods beyond the project objectives have also been considered.

14302018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302018.value: A large number of scientific applications involve the inversion of heterogeneous properties represented by multiscale coefficients in the mathematical models. Examples include the identification of underground features in subsurface flows, heat conductivies in geothermal systems and permeability in shale gas transport. The inversion of heterogeneous material properties require efficient numerical solutions to the multiscale systems as well as appropriate regularized inversion procedure. Existing inversion techniques are based on the recovery of upscaled quantities on a coarse grid, and they generally need the assumption on the existence of a homogenized representation of the fine-scale properties of the unknown coefficient on a coarser scale mesh. While there are cases in which these assumptions hold, they do not generally hold for more realistic problems in which the multiscale coefficients contain high contrast channels and fractures. These channels and fractures produce some longer range effects, which cannot be represented by local upscaling techniques. The multi-continuum model, which uses multiple upscaled coefficients to represent complex media, requires some physical assumptions that are difficult to verify in practice. Therefore, fine scale discretization of the problem is necessary when channels and fractures are present. However, this leads to large scale discrete systems which are ill-posed and are expensive to solve, and this way is therefore not desirable. The proposed research develops a class of multiscale model reduction techniques for the inversion of heterogeneous media in multiscale systems. The novelties of the work are the representation of the global features arising from channels and fractures by local multiscale basis functions as well as the inversion algorithm for the recovery of coarse scale features of heterogeneous coefficients without the assumption on the existence of homogenization. In order to capture global features by local multiscale basis functions, we will use the recently developed constraint energy minimization technique which gives exponential decay of basis functions outside certain oversampling regions. For the inversion process, we will regularize the problem by discretization. In particular, we use the fact that the solutions of the multiscale systems can be represented well by our local multiscale basis functions. We will then construct coarse scale model for the simultaneous inversion of coarse scale properties of the unknown multiscale coefficients as well as the corresponding multiscale basis functions. Our proposed research will provide a new insight and a significant advance for the inversion of multiscale coefficients involving channels and fractures, and provides an effective tool for practical applications. 大量的科學應用涉及由數學模型中的多尺度係數表示的異質性質的反演。例子包括識別地下水流中的地下特徵，地熱系統中的熱導率和頁岩氣輸送中的滲透率。異質材料特性的反演需要多尺度系統的有效數值解以及適當的正則化反演程序。現有的反演技術基於粗網格上的放大量的恢復，並且它們通常需要假設在較粗尺度的網格上存在未知係數的精細尺度屬性的均勻化表示。雖然存在這些假設的情況，但它們通常不適用於多尺度係數包含高對比度通道和裂縫的更現實的問題。這些通道和裂縫產生一些較長距離的效應，這些效應無法通過局部放大技術來表示。多連續體模型使用多個放大係數來表示複雜介質，需要一些在實踐中難以驗證的物理假設。因此，當存在通道和裂縫時，需要對問題進行精細尺度離散化。然而，這導致大規模的離散系統，這些系統是不適合的並且解決起來很昂貴，因此這種方式是不希望的。 所提出的研究開發了一類多尺度模型簡化技術，用於多尺度系統中異構介質的反演。該工作的新穎性是通過局部多尺度基函數表示由通道和裂縫引起的全局特徵，以及用於恢復異質係數的粗尺度特徵的反演算法，而不假設存在均勻化。為了通過局部多尺度基函數捕獲全局特徵，我們將使用最近開發的約束能量最小化技術，該技術在某些過採樣區域之外給出基函數的指數衰減。對於反演過程，我們將通過離散化來規範化問題。特別是，我們使用的事實是多尺度系統的解決方案可以通過我們的本地多尺度基礎函數很好地表示。然後，我們將構建粗尺度模型，用於同時反演未知多尺度係數的粗尺度特性以及相應的多尺度基函數。我們提出的研究將為涉及通道和裂縫的多尺度係數的反演提供新的見解和重大進展，並為實際應用提供有效的工具。

14302018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302018.value: We have developed some novel multiscale approaches for challenging applications involving inversion. One key element of the developed method is the construction of reduced spaces. The reduced space should be able to capture most of the solution features and gives accurate approximations. This is particularly important for inversion process as one has to solve the direct problem many times. Our idea is based on the generalized multiscale finite element method. The method is based on the use of local spectral decomposition and construction of localized basis functions. Our multiscale space gives a good latent space for the learning process, which give efficient methods for inversion. We have developed several schemes in the learning of unknown coefficients in computational models and various sampling approaches. Our results show that the developed method can give very efficient, accurate and stable schemes for finding unknown coefficient in computational model and solving real challenging applications.

14302018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302018.value: Based on the convincing findings of the project, there are many opportunities for future research. One possibility is the investigation of other challenging applications in coupled flow and mechanics, where the poroelasticity system is needed. In this case, there are some unknown parameters in the model such as the fracture distributions. One can develop multiscale approaches for such problem and design strategies to learn the unknown fracture distributions. Another possibility is the construction of more advanced multiscale spaces. In particular, one can design multiscale spaces that are based on the coupled system. Such space will be useful in the learning process as it provides a good latent space.

14302018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302018.value: The project investigates an important problem in computational mathematics. The problem is to identify key and unknown parameters in a given model. Such problem is known to be challenging as it is typically ill-posed, namely, solution may not exist and is unstable with respect to perturbation in the data. We have developed novel and robust multiscale approach to solve such problems. The idea is based on finding a smaller approximation space that gives accurate approximation. As the problem can be solved in a smaller space, the problem becomes less ill-posed. We have illustrated the success of the developed idea in some applications. For example, we have developed inversion techniques to identify unknown parameters in computational models for coupled flow and transport. We have also developed multiscale sampling methods with applications to inversion.

14302218.label: Project Objectives
14302218.value: We shall develop a phase field approximation of an abstract shape optimization problem with a PDE constraint, and under specific settings we recover previous applications to drag minimization and structural topology optimization studied in the literature. We shall analyze the phase field approximation of the PDE constraint, and identify a suitable notion of solutions. We shall provide analytical results concerning the existence of solutions to the PDE constraint and the existence of a minimizer (optimal shape) to the abstract optimization problem in Objective 1. We shall use the results obtain in Objective 2 to derive optimality conditions (often in the form of a coupled system of nonlinear PDEs or inequalities) with the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, we employ asymptotic analysis to connect the optimality conditions from the phase field approach and the classical formulation for shape optimization. We shall apply the results obtained in Objectives 1, 2 and 3 to two specific inverse problems: inverse acoustic scattering and electrical impedance tomography. In both applications, we shall carry out a systematic analysis for minimizers and optimality conditions. Furthermore, we shall investigate the stability of optimal shapes with respect to changes in the data. We shall numerically realize the optimal shapes for the problems studied in Objective 4 by solving the corresponding optimality conditions, and compare the results from the phase field approach to those obtained from the current state-of-the-art solution methods for these inverse problems.

14302218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302218.value: In shape optimization problems, the aim is to find a class of shapes that optimizes some prescribed goals under a partial differential equation (PDE) constraint. One example is drag minimization, seeking the shape of an impermeable object exhibiting the least drag while flowing through a fluid. The classical formulation for such problems involves representing the unknown shape as a mathematical surface, and seeks to derive optimality conditions (equations/inequalities involving nonlinear PDEs). The optimal shapes can then be realized numerically by solving the optimality conditions. However, shape optimization problems are often severely ill-posed (as the existence of optimal shapes is not guaranteed in general) and can be computationally intensive (due to the requirement of a new approximation of the computational domain at every numerical iteration). We propose to use a phase field approach to overcome the above problems, and for drag minimization, it has several important mathematical and numerical advantages over the classical approach; namely the phase field method can be justified (in the sense that existence of optimal shapes can be proved rigorously) and in addition both the PDE constraint and the optimality conditions are solved on the same fixed domain throughout the optimization procedure. Furthermore, by sending a small parameter to zero, the optimality conditions from the classical formulation are recovered. Hence, one may view the phase field approach as a consistent approximation for shape optimization problems. The goal of this proposal is to develop phase field approximations to study nonlinear inverse problems that can be casted as shape optimization problems. In light of the mathematical advantages outlined above, we believe that the proposed phase field approach may offer novel and alternative resolution strategies for such problems. Firstly, we consider an abstract shape optimization problem with the aim of providing analytical results for the PDE constraint and establish the existence of optimal shapes, the derivation of optimality conditions, as well as the connection with the classical formulation. Then, we apply this theory to two important examples of inverse problems: inverse acoustic scattering and electrical impedance tomography. Numerical simulations will be carried out to compare the proposed phase field approach with current state-of-the-art methods, and successful investigations will serve to enhance the applicability of the phase field approach. 形狀優化問題的目標是找到一類在偏微分方程（PDE）約束下優化某些規定目標的形狀。一個例子是尋求在流體內表現出最小阻力的物體的形狀。針對這些問題的經典方法涉及將未知的形狀表示為數學表面，並尋求導出最優性條件（涉及非線性PDE的方程/不等式）。然後，通過求解最優性條件，可以在數值上實現最佳形狀。然而，形狀優化問題往往是嚴重不適（因為通常不能保證最優形狀的存在）並且可以是計算密集型的（由於在每次數值迭代時需要新的計算域）。我們建議使用相場模式方法來克服上述問題，並且對於拖曳最小化的形狀優化問題，它比傳統方法具有幾個重要的數學和數值優勢: 相場模式方法可以有進一步分析（可以嚴格證明最佳形狀的存在）並且另外通過優化過程在相同的計算域上解決PDE約束和最優性條件。此外，通過發送一個小參數為零，就獲得了經典方法的最優性條件。因此，可以將相場模式方法視為形狀優化問題的一致近似。本計畫提議的目標是開發相場模式近似以研究可以作為形狀優化問題的非線性反問題。鑑於上述的數學優勢，我們認為所提出的相場模式方法可以為這些問題提供新穎的解決方案策略。首先，我們考慮一個抽象的形狀優化問題，目的是為PDE約束提供分析結果，建立最優形狀的存在，最優性條件的推導，以及與經典方法的聯繫。然後，我們將這個理論應用於兩個重要的反問題：逆聲散射和電阻抗斷層成像。 將進行數值模擬以將所提出的相場模式方法與當前最先進的方法進行比較，並且成功的研究將有助於增強相場模式方法的適用性。

14302218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302218.value: We proposed a phase field shape optimization approach to study two types of problems: (i) a geometric inverse problem involving quasilinear magnetostatic equations, (ii) design problems in 3D and 4D printing involving linear elasticity equations. In both topics, we recast these shape optimization problems in terms of PDE-constrained minimizer problems and performed a systematic analysis for minimizers and optimality conditions. Furthermore, we studied the so-called sharp interface limit that allows us to relate our phase field optimality conditions to optimality conditions of a corresponding shape optimization approach in a rigorous setting. Numerical simulations of the phase field optimality conditions also demonstrated some novel and interesting designs for the application to 3D printing. In particular, our research results are among the first to apply this phase field methodology to quasilinear Maxwell equations and the field of additive manufacturing. These were published in some of the best applied mathematics journals, such as Inverse Problems, Applied Mathematics & Optimization, and ESAIM: Control, Optimization and Calculus of Variations.

14302218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302218.value: While the connection between the proposed phase field methodology and classical shape optimization has been clearly established, we have observed that the proposed methodology can also perform some degree of topology optimization. The connection between the two is less clear, and so it would be very interesting to mathematically investigate whether the optimality conditions from topology optimization problems can be obtained from the phase field approach. Another direction worthy of pursuit is the application to the emerging field of 3D printing. In one of our works we focused on creating designs that do not require support structures during construction, but one can equally cast a shape optimization problem that optimizes the shape of the support structures during printing. These topics would make very good PhD research projects.

14302218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302218.value: Inverse problems involving geometry and design commonly appear in many areas of applications, and due to their importance, it is essential to develop mathematical approaches that can accurately and efficiently obtain a reasonable solution. In this project, we demonstrated that our proposed phase field methodology is able to tackle highly challenging design and detection problems appearing in 3D printing and magnetic tomography. In the former application we are able to develop some novel designs of 3D structures that change their shape in response to an external stimulus. Our theoretical investigations showed that the phase field approach is mathematically sound, and it can be related to other mathematical approaches in the literature studied previously. Based on our observations, it is possible to apply our phase field approach to other problems in shape and topology optimization.

14302318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302318.value: In this proposal, we aim to produce charged microdroplets containing organic reactants for the purpose of reaction acceleration. We will develop a microfluidic system to study the accelerated organic chemical reactions and a reactor for large scale accelerated organic reactions. Comparing to the previous research on accelerated reactions in charged microdroplets suspended in air, the proposed charged microdroplets are surrounded by perfluorinated oil. We expect that the resulting droplet interfaces have distinctly different properties and effects on the reaction rate. We will first construct and validate the microfluidic system to generate the charged microdroplets in perfluorinated oil. We will study three typical organic reactions in the charged microdroplets: the Pomeranz-Fritsch synthesis of isoquinoline, the Claisen-Schmidt condensation, and the reaction of Girard’s reagent T with ketosteroids. We will study the interfacial factors including the microdroplet size, charge density, and surface tension as the contributes to acceleration effect. Once validated, the microfluidic system will be a useful platform in the mechanism research and in the small-scale organic synthesis. Secondly, we will develop the reactor capable of large scale reaction in charged microdroplets. We plan to integrate ultrasound method with electric field to achieve the goal. We will use ultrasonic bath to produce large amount of emulsion, and use the electric field to induce charges on the microdroplet surface in the emulsion. We will measure the reaction production by mass spectrometry, and use the production as the feedback to optimize the reactor design. 我們計劃製備帶電荷內含有機反應物的液滴用於加速反應速率。我們將發展一套微流系統來研究液滴里的反應加速以及一個用於大規模加速的有機反應的反應器。不同於之前在炫富在空氣中的帶電荷液滴加速反應的研究，我們這裏的帶電荷液滴是在氟油中。我們預計兩種液滴的界面有不同，對於反應速率的效果也會不同。 首先我們會建造并驗證微流系統在氟油中來產生帶電荷液滴。在液滴里我們會研究三類典型的有機反應：Pomeranz-Fritsch反應合成異喹啉，Claisen-Schmidt縮合反應，以及Girard試劑與酮類固醇的反應。我們會研究各類界面效應對反應加速的影響，包括液滴大小，電荷密度，以及表面張力。驗證過的微流系統將是一個在反應機理研究和小規模有機合成方面有用的平臺。 然後我們將發展一個能夠進行大規模液滴反應的反應器。我們計劃把超聲和電場結合起來。我們將用超聲池來產生大量乳液，然後用外加電場來誘導乳液中的液滴表面產生電荷。我們將用質譜來評估反應速率，并以此作為反饋信息來優化反應器的設計。

14302318.label: Realisation of objectives
14302318.value: The first objective has been fully achieved. We have developed the microfluidic device which can generate uniform microdroplets in fluorinated oil and also generate charges on the surface of the microdroplets. We have performed organic reactions in the charged microdroplets, and analyzed the content of the microdroplets after controlled reaction time by using mass spectrometry. More specifically, we accomplished the following tasks. We succeeded in producing the microdroplets containing the organic reactants in perfluorinated oil in microfluidic devices using T-junction configuration. The resulting microdroplets are uniform in diameter, and the size can be controlled by changing the flow rate of the organic reagents and the perfluorinated oil in the microfluidic device. We also introduced liquid metals into the microchannels to act as microelectrodes, which substantially simplified the device fabrication and operation. We succeeded in controlling the surface charge density of the microdroplets by varying the strength of the applied charging voltage from 0 to 3000 V at the charging area. By integrating a deflecting zone in the microfluidic devices, we proved that the microdroplets were negatively charged. We developed a new method of evaluating the charge number of each microdroplets by analyzing the size, deflecting time, and the amount of deflection under controlled deflecting voltage. We succeeded in using LC-MS to analyze the products in the microdroplets after controlled reaction time. The separation of the perfluorinated oil from the reaction mixture was found to be crucial to obtaining high-quality mass spectrometry data. In the three model reactions we studied, we found various levels of yield enhancement. For example, in the Pomeranz-Fritsch synthesis of isoquinoline in microdroplets, we achieved the yield of more than 95%, which was substantially higher than the previously reported 1% yield in bulk solution under the same mild reaction condition. The second objective has been fully achieved. We integrated a pair of plate electrodes with an ultrasound bath to produce the reactor. Large scale organic synthesis of isoquinoline from benzaldehyde and 2,2-dialkoxyethylamine was performed in the reactor. The reactant mixture dissolved in methanol was mixed with the perfluorinated oil to become an emulsion. The electric field produced by the two plate electrode would charge the droplets of the emulsion. The ultrasound cavitation caused bubble formation, growth and implosion, which provide extremely high localized pressure and temperature. The generated huge energy provided sufficient force to break the large droplets into nanodroplets. The methanol nanodroplets were neutral initially, and would go through polarization, fission, and coalescence under the high electric field intensity. We used light scattering to characterize the size distribution of the droplets, which were mostly in the range of a few nanometers. LC-MS showed that the yield of isoquinoline was more than 95%, substantially higher than the previously reported 1% yield in bulk solution under the same mild reaction condition. The result was consistent with our result in the microdroplet in the first objective., demonstrating that the reaction was significantly accelerated in charged droplets in the scaled-up reactor. The work validated the scaled-up reactor for the large scale synthesis of isoquinoline using charged droplets. Currently, we attributed the rate acceleration to the protons at the interface due to the solvent oxidation induced by the charges on the nanodroplet surface.

14302318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302318.value: We established a microfluidic platform which generated uniform microdroplets in oil. In the microfluidic device, we were able to generate charges on the surface of the microdroplets. We have performed organic reactions in the charged microdroplets, and analyzed the content of the microdroplets after controlled reaction time by using mass spectrometry. The yield of the organic reaction was significantly higher than that from bulk solution under the same reaction conditions. We also used the droplets produced in the microfluidic device to measure the kinetics of DNA replication and to detect single nucleotide variation (SNV). We found that the crowding conditions in the droplets generally enhanced the specificity in the detection of SNV (M. Cui, X. Zhou, X. Chen, W. Zheng, L. Bian, Z. Li, and B. Zheng, Chem. Commun., 2019, 55, 12052). We tried a different approach of producing uniform microdroplets on patterned perfluorinated surfaces to perform the organic reactions in the microdroplets. Using this patterned perfluorinated surface we developed new methods of immunoassay with high sensitivity (Q. Liu, X. Zhou, H. Wu, L. Wu, B. Zheng, Sens. Actuators B Chem., 2019, 287, 306; S. Qian, H. Wu, Q. Liu, B. Huang, Y. Chen, B. Zheng, Sens. Actuators B Chem., 2021, 345, 130341). We built and validated a reactor for scaled-up organic synthesis in charged droplets. The reactor consisted of an ultrasound bath and a pair of plate electrodes. The combination of ultrasound and high-intensity electric field produced charged nanodroplets inside the reactor, and the reaction yield was consistent with the yield from the reaction in the microfluidic device. For measuring the yield of the reaction in the droplets, in addition to LC-MS, we tried a different approach of using an electronic nose to monitor the yield in real time, and developed a new type of electronic nose which was specifically sensitive to acetone (Q. Fu, P. Lyu, S. Handschuh-Wang, L. Teng, B. Zheng, Ceram. Int., 2022, 48, 28419). One student, Baishu Liu, obtained his PhD for his work on this project. Research collaboration has been established based on the research work. We are collaborating with Professor Xuechang Zhou of Shenzhen University, who is an expert in polymer chemistry. Professor Barry Sharpless is also very interested in our work, and from time to time offering his insight on the project. We are developing new microfluidic techniques to investigate organic reactions on interfaces.

14302318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302318.value: The research paves the way for further study of organic reactions in microdroplets. We plan to further our research work on reactions in microdroplets in the following aspects: (1) We will integrate microfluidic devices with mass spectrometry (MS), especially electrospray ionization (ESI) MS to study the mechanism of reactions in microdroplets; (2) We will try different approaches of scaling up the reactions in microdroplets, e.g., using mechanical force instead of ultrasound to produce large amount of emulsion; (3) We will apply the reactor for scaled-up reaction to more organic synthesis. We will study several critical parameters, including bath temperature, strength of the electric field, the choice of the immiscible liquid in the emulsion, and etc., to optimize the reaction condition and enhance the yield; (4) We will extend the application of the microdroplets to biosynthesis under biocompatible conditions. More specifically, we are interested in performing the synthesis of proteins and high value natural compounds in microdroplets and studying the interface effect on the biosynthesis.

14302318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302318.value: In this project we designed and built a microdevice for producing charged uniform microdroplets. We performed several organic reactions in the microdroplets, and we measured the content of the microdroplets after the reaction. We found the reaction rate and the yield were enhanced in the charged microdroplets. In the project we also built and validated a reactor for scaled-up organic synthesis in charged droplets. The reactor consisted of an ultrasound bath and a pair of plate electrodes. The combination of ultrasound and high-intensity electric field produced charged nanodroplets inside the reactor. We measured the size of the droplets and the content of the droplets after the reaction. The reaction yield was greatly enhanced, which was consisted with the result in the microdroplets from the microdevice.

14302418.label: Project Objectives
14302418.value: Propose suitable higher-order approximations for tail probabilities of dependent random variables with smaller-order relative errors. Develop Stein's method for higher-order moderate deviations to justify the approximations. 14302418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302418.value: A central theme in probability theory is approximating the distribution of a random variable of interest by a suitable limiting distribution. The approximation is commonly justified by providing an absolute error bound for the difference between the cumulative distribution functions. However, a small absolute error bound cannot guarantee the accuracy of tail probability approximations when these tail probabilities themselves are smaller than the error bound. Such tail probability approximations are of significant interest in various disciplines such as statistics and operations research. If we are interested in approximating tail probabilities, it would be more useful to provide an upper bound for the relative error in the approximation. We use the term "moderate deviation" to refer to the approximation of tail probabilities with a small relative error. Moderate deviations date back to Cramér (1938), who obtained expansions for tail probabilities for sums of independent random variables about the normal distribution. On the other hand, Stein's method provides a powerful tool to deal with dependent random variables. In this project, we plan to investigate the theory of Stein's method with regard to Cramér-type moderate deviations. In particular, based on our previous work, we will further study moderate deviations for (i) higher-order approximations, (ii) local limit theorems, and (iii) multivariate approximations. The general theory developed in this project will equip us with the necessary techniques to deal with complex problems arising from various areas of study. In particular, we plan to explore applications in operations research, statistical physics, and statistics. 概率論的一個中心課題是通過合適的極限分佈來近似某個感興趣的隨機變量的分佈。這種近似通常通過控制兩個分佈函數的絕對誤差來保證。但是，小的絕對誤差並不能保證尾概率近似的精確性。這種尾概率近似在統計和運籌學等各種學科中有廣泛的應用。 如果我們對尾概率近似感興趣，控制相對誤差更為有用。我們用“中偏差”這個詞來指具有較小的相對誤差的尾概率近似。中偏差可以追溯Cramér（1938），後者獲得了獨立隨機變量和的尾概率關於正態分佈的相對誤差的展開。另一方面，Stein方法提供了一個強大的工具來處理相關的隨機變量。在這個項目中，我們計劃研究關於Cramér型中偏差理論的Stein方法。具體來說，基於我們之前的工作，我們將進一步研究（i）高階的尾概率近似（ii）局部極限定理，以及（iii）高維近似。這個項目得到的一般理論將有利於我們處理來自運籌學、統計物理和統計學等各個領域的複雜問題。

14302418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302418.value: It is of wide interest to bound the relative error in probability approximations and this is the main topic of this project. Our main tool is Stein’s method. In Fang, Luo and Shao (2020, Bernoulli), we proposed skewness-corrected normal approximations for tail probabilities of sums of local statistics and theoretically justified the accuracy of the approximations. We applied the main result to U-statistics and subgraph counts in random graph models. In Braverman, Dai and Fang (2022, Operations Research), we proposed and justified high-order steady state diffusion approximations where the limit is non-normal. We considered applications to queuing models. In Fang, Liu and Shao (2022, Bernoulli), we obtained a moderate deviation result with a fast rate for Esseen’s chi-square approximation. In Fang and Liu (2022, under review) and Fang and Zhang (2022, manuscript), we developed Stein’s method for local central limit theorems and the corresponding moderate deviation results for integer-valued random variables. In Fang and Koike (2022, under review), we developed Stein’s method to prove moderate deviation results for multivariate normal approximations. Other related work includes: (i) Arcsine laws for random walks generated from random permutations with applications to genomics (Fang et al. (2021)), (ii) High-dimensional central limit theorems (Fang and Koike (2021)), (iii) New error bounds in multivariate normal approximations via exchangeable pairs with applications to Wishart matrices and fourth moment theorems (Fang and Koike (2022)), (iv) Normal approximation and fourth moment theorems for monochromatic triangles (Bhattacharya, Fang and Yan (2022)), (v) Large-dimensional central limit theorem with fourth-moment error bounds on convex sets and balls (Fang and Koike (2022)), (vi) Sharp high-dimensional central limit theorems for log-concave distributions (Fang and Koike (2022)).

14302418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302418.value: Several problems are left open by this project. (i) Skewness correction in high-dimensional central limit theorems. High-dimensional CLT is a relatively new topic, but has already attracted researchers from the fields of probability, statistics, and econometrics. One open problem in high-dimensional CLT is whether skewness correction brings any benefit to the approximation accuracy. We believe this is the case in tail probability approximations and we are currently working in this direction. (ii) Functional approximations. Gaussian process approximations have been well studied in the literature. However, tail probability accuracy in Gaussian process approximations is less developed. We believe it is an interesting potential direction to work on.

14302418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302418.value: A central theme in probability theory is approximating the distribution of a random variable of interest by a suitable limiting distribution. The approximation is commonly justified by providing an absolute error bound for the difference between the cumulative distribution functions. However, it is of significant interest to obtain a small relative error bound in tail probability approximations. In this project, we have proposed skewness-corrected normal approximations for tail probabilities of sums of local statistics and theoretically justified the accuracy of the approximations. We applied the main result to U-statistics and subgraph counts in random graph models. We have also proposed and justified high-order steady state diffusion approximations where the limit is non-normal. We considered applications to queuing models. Moreover, we have obtained a moderate deviation result with a fast rate for Esseen’s chi-square approximation and developed Stein’s method for local central limit theorems and the corresponding moderate deviation results for integer-valued random variables. Finally, we have developed Stein’s method to prove moderate deviation results for multivariate normal approximations. We expect these new theoretical developments as well as applications will enrich the asymptotic theory in probability and large sample theory in statistics and many other areas.

14302518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302518.value: Entropy is one of the fundamental states of the compressible fluids including but not limit to the ideal gases. The main difficulties of the mathematical analysis of the entropy are: (i) The entropy satisfies a highly singular equation near the vacuum region; (ii) As the entropy is defined as some combination of the logarithms of the density and temperature, the regularities of the density and temperature do not imply any desired regularities of the corresponding entropy in the vacuum region. This project is devoted to some analysis on the entropy of the ideal gases in the presence of vacuum at the far field only. Precisely, we will consider the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations, with positive constant viscosities and nonnegative constant heat conductivity, and we are going to study the local or global existence and uniqueness of such solutions that have bounded entropy to the Cauchy problem. 14302718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302718.value: Poisson-Nernst-Planck 方程被用來描述離子在生物環境裡的傳輸。這個方程以及其相應的電動力學方程組在電池領域和生物化學領域有著重要的應用。最近幾十年，關於PNP方程數學方面的分析和研究取得了很多進展（參考[2]-[3], [15], [25]-[26])。在這些工作裡面永久負載電荷被假設成某些空間裡面的函數。在我們這個課題裡面，我們感興趣的是當永久負載電荷具有某些奇異特性。比如它可以被看作成Dirac 測度，或者是Radon意義下的測度。具體來說我們感興趣的問題可以分成兩類。第一部分，我們希望研究當具有帶奇性的永久負載電荷時，PNP方程的穩態解具有什麼特徵。這個問題跟半線性橢圓方程有很大關係。我們計劃具體研究解的存在性以及當某些參數取極限時，解的漸進行為。在第二部分，我們希望討論動力系統。特別的我們希望考慮動力系統解的長時間行為。這些問題跟第一部分裡面得到的穩態解有很多關係。事實上，我們希望研究這些穩態解在動態條件下的穩定性。我們相信通過對這些問題的討論能為我們在橢圓和拋物性方程領域開闢新的研究方向。同時我們的研究也能吸引生物化學領域專家的興趣。我們期望我們的研究能夠在更多實用領域帶來應用。

14302718.label: Realisation of objectives
14302718.value: PI has studied all the problems proposed in the project objectives. Around 80% of the goals in the objectives are achieved. More than that, some unexpected results have also been obtained, e.g. resolutions to the Debye layer problem, Rubinstein problem, and unconditional long-time dynamics of Keller-Segel equation, etc. Objective 1: In 2D, we fully classify the singular equilibrium solutions to the PNP equation, in terms of the charges carried by the defects. In higher dimensional case, we prove that there is no equilibrium solutions to the PNP equation with defects of Dirac type, provided that all ions in the solution have finite total mass. Moreover, based on the nonlocal charge conserved Poisson-Boltzmann equation (the equation satisfied by the equilibrium solutions to the PNP equation), we rigorously verify the prediction proposed by Gouy-Chapman on the existence of Debye layer. All goals in objective 1 have been achieved. Objective 2: Right after I finished the objective 1, I began to explore singular equilibrium solutions to the PNP equation in higher dimensions. Since there cannot have solutions with Dirac type singularities when the spatial dimension is not less than 3, a natural extension is to introduce some defects concentrated on a codimension 2 submanifold in the domain. However, except some technical difficulties arising from the geometries of defects, and some complexities when one applies gluing argument, the existence and Debye layer results are all the same as the 2D case. Therefore, I switched to consider the dynamical problems, and planned to finish one article on the codimension 2 defect measure problem after the dynamical problems were solved. However, the dynamical problems are pretty amazing, and I spent almost all my remaining time in this project on the dynamical system. The codimension 2 defect measure problem is hence left unfinished. Though there is no journal publication related to this objective, we have made some attempts to construct solutions with codimension 2 defects. In fall 2020, my Ph.D student Ho-Man Tai, my postdoc Chia-Yu Hsieh and I organized an online working seminar. We systematically studied the following paper by Mazzeo-Paccard: A construction of singular solutions for a semilinear elliptic equation using asymptotic analysis. Some gluing arguments due to Del-Pino and Wei were also studied. Objective 3: The goals in this objective have been achieved. We considered a generalized Rubinstein problem by introducing multiple defects. The charges of the defects might have different signs. Under some assumptions, we obtained both local and global solutions to the singular PNP equation in 2D. We also extended to studying a similar system, Keller-Segel system, arising in the theory of chemotaxis. With both nutrition and poison, we prove the existence of bounded global solutions to the Keller-Segel system in 2D, under the subcritical regime. Our result is optimal and contains all the subcritical cases. Objective 4: The goals in this objective have been achieved. Indeed, we are not only concerned about the PNP equation, but also the Keller-Segel equation. To some extent, it is harder to describe the asymptotic behavior of global solutions to the Keller-Segel equation, than to the PNP equation. Our approaches used to study the Keller-Segel equation can be successfully applied to the PNP equation. For the Keller-Segel system, we have two results on the asymptotic behavior of global solutions. For 2D subcritical regime, we proved an unconditional long-time asymptotic result on the global mild solutions. For higher dimensional case, we studied the asymptotic behavior of the global solutions found by Iwabuchi-Nakamura. Objective 5: This objective is NOT finished satisfactorily. In 2019, Constantin-Ignatova published their paper: On the Nernst–Planck–Navier–Stokes system. In this paper, our suggested 2D problem was successfully studied by Constantin-Ignatova. Thereafter, we spent a lot of time on the 3D case, and hoped to find out the mechanism on stabilizing the PNP-NS system with the electric force. However, this attempt is not successful. Main reason still lies in our limited understanding of the 3D Navier-Stokes equation. Objective 6: The goals in this objective are fully achieved. When we studied the Debye layer problem, we have introduced two different ions whose charges have different signs. In the stationary case, the result can be extended easily to the case with multiple ions.
