14302718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302718.value: [1]. We study the open problem on the Debye layer phenomenon, in terms of the charge conserved Poisson-Boltzmann equation (CCPB for short). The limit of the electric potential in the thin layer limiting process is explicitly determined via a novel log-exponential mean integral on Dirichlet data. The convergence rate is estimated by a quantity depending on the thickness of the layer. The behavior of the electric potential in the boundary layer regime is also quantitatively studied. As is well known, CCPB is non-local. The non-locality of CCPB yields difficulties in its numerical simulations. We provide a local model, by which CCPB can be efficiently approximated. The results are valid in all dimensions. [2]. We study the classical Keller-Segel equations in all dimensions. In 2D subcritical regime, we give an unconditional long-time asymptotics of the global mild solutions. Our results only require the finiteness of the total mass, and drop the usual assumptions in literature on the finiteness of free energy and second moment. This result can be compared with the one due to Gallay-Wayne on 2D Navier-Stokes equation. In higher dimensions, we extend to studying the global solutions obtained by Iwabuchi-Nakamura. Different from 2D case, in higher dimensions, the long-time asymptotics are governed by the standard heat kernel. The higher-order approximations are also obtained. They are separately studied when spatial dimensions are 3, 4, and no less than 5. [3]. We introduce a shrinking hole argument and a novel Born-Infeld approximation scheme to study the singular solutions to the semilinear elliptic equations with exponential nonlinearities. The sizes of the holes are determined via an inverse problem. The approach has physics background. As a byproduct of our arguments, we show that Born-Infeld-Higgs model can be used to approximate the Abelian-Higgs model in 2D when the Born-Infeld parameter is large. [4]. We generalize Poincare inequality to a weighted version. The weights are of Muckenhoupt type. By this result, we obtain the global solutions to the 2D PNP equation when there are finitely many fixed defects in the domain. This result partially solves an open problem proposed by Rubinstein. [5]. We study the uniform boundedness of global mild solutions to the Keller-Segel equation with nutrition and poison. Nagai-Yamada obtained similar result before. However, their result is valid only in part of the subcritical regime. Our consequence extends the uniform boundedness result of the global mild solutions to the full subcritical regime.

14302718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302718.value: [1]. It is worth to study the dynamical boundary layer problem for the original PNP equation. When the layer thickness is small, we may find nice approximation to the solution of PNP equation in both interior region, and near the boundary layer. [2]. For the classical Keller-Segel equation, the blow-up problem in higher dimensions are largely open. We plan to study the formation of type-I singularities in solutions to the classical nD Keller-Segel equation. [3]. The Born-Infeld scheme are powerful. It not only can construct solutions to semilinear elliptic equations with Dirac type singularities. In higher dimensions, it can also help construct singular solutions with codimension 2 singularities. This is an interesting topic and needs follow up in the future. [4]. Generalized Rubinstein problem is just partially answered. The range of defect charges studied in our dynamical system cannot cover the full range of the stationary case. The reason is due to the singular-degenerate parabolic system derived from the original PNP system. It is worth to study systematically the parabolic system with general singular and degenerate coefficients. [5]. Similar to the classical Keller-Segel equation, it is interesting to study the formation of type-II singularities in solutions to the attraction-repulsion model.

14302718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302718.value: The project finishes with many significant and valuable results. With these results, we obtain better understanding of various phenomena observed in ion channels, membrane electrochemstry, chemotaxis, and so on. Moreover, successfully solving part of the problems in the project also help us motivate several new and exciting research topics that are worthy of further study in the future. The research in this project is at the junction areas between mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. Along this direction, some interdisciplinary collaborations may be promoted with different units, faculties, and universities.

14303518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303518.value: Mirror Symmetry conjecture was originated in the study of String theory in Physics. Mathematically speaking, this is a highly nontrivial identification between two different kinds of Geometry, namely Symplectic Geometry and Complex Geometry. The conjecture was originally stated for pairs of Calabi-Yau manifolds and it has been generalized to other spaces and LG models. Strominger-Yau-Zaslow proposed an explanation of the Mirror Symmetry in terms of a fiberwise Fourier-Mukai type transformation. In this proposal, the PI plans to continue the studies of the SYZ transformation. These includes the studies of scattering diagrams and categorification, geometry of coisotropic A-branes, quantum cohomology of flag varieties via wonderful compactifications and so on. This research will enhance our understanding of mirror symmetry, complex geometry and symplectic geometry. 鏡對稱本源自物理中弦理論的研究。從數學角度來說， 這是一個有關兩種不同的幾何之間的等同關係。 它們是辛幾何和復幾何。這猜想已從本來有關卡拉比空間 推廣到其他空間及LG模型。SYZ用Fourier-Mukai形的變換提出 解釋鏡對稱的辦法。 在這建議書中，研究員計劃繼續有關SYZ變換的研究。 其中包括散射圖及範疇化的研究、A-膜的幾何、旗空間 量子上同調、完美緊致化等等。這項研究項目提高對鏡對稱、 復幾何和辛幾何的理解。

14303518.label: Realisation of objectives
14303518.value: The PI has obtained results enhancing our understanding of SYZ transformation in Mirror Symmetry. This includes a differential geometric approach via the Maurer-Cartan equation; 3d mirror symmetry for elliptic hypertoric varieties, cyclic group actions on Fukaya categories mirror to divisibility of first Chern class and so on. Mirror symmetry conjecture has inspired many new predictions in both symplectic geometry and complex geometry. This enables us to discover new geometric structures, including relationships among different quantization schemes on Kahler manifolds, new example satisfying DK conjecture for derived categories for flips and so on.

14303518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303518.value: In the paper 'Elliptic hypertoric varieties', we introduced elliptic hypertoric varieties, which is an elliptic analogue of hypertoric varieties and multiplicative hypertoric varieties. We proved an elliptic version of Hikita conjecture, which relates elliptic (resp. additive and mulitplicative) hypertoric varieties to the equivariant elliptic cohomology (resp. ordinary cohomology and K-theory) of their 3d mirror hypertoric varieties in 3d mirror symmetry. In the paper 'A cyclic group action on Fukaya categories from mirror symmetry', we studied mirror symmetry for symplectic manifolds whose first Chern class is divisible by a positive integer n. We showed that its mirror admits a natural Zn-action. More generally, We construct a Z2n-action on its Fukaya category Fuk(X) and a Zn-action on the local models of its moduli of Lagrangian branes. We showed that this action is compatible with the gluing functions for different local models. In the paper 'A geometric construction of representations of the Berezin-Toeplitz quantization', we give a geometric construction of a family of representations of the Berezin-Toeplitz deformation quantization algebra parametrized by points in X. The key idea is to use peak sections to suitably localize the Hilbert spaces around any fixed point in the large volume limit. In the paper 'Kapranov's L-infinity structure, Fedosov's star products, and 1-loop exact BV quantizations on Kahler manifolds', we studied quantization schemes on a Kähler manifold and relate several interesting structures. We first construct Fedosov's star products on a Kähler manifold X as quantizations of Kapranov's L∞-algebra structure. Then we investigate the Batalin-Vilkovisky quantizations associated to these star products. A remarkable feature is that they are all one-loop exact, meaning that the Feynman weights associated to graphs with two or more loops all vanish. This leads to a succinct cochain level formula in de Rham cohomology for the algebraic index. In the paper 'Geometric quantization and quantum moment maps on coadjoint orbits and Kähler-Einstein manifolds', we studies both deformation quantization and geometric quantization on Kähler manifolds, they give the mathematical description of the algebra of quantum observables and the Hilbert spaces respectively, where the later forms a representation of quantum observables asymptotically via Toeplitz operators. When there is a Hamiltonian G-action on a Kähler manifold, there are associated symmetries on both the quantum algebra and representation aspects. We show that in nice cases of coadjoint orbits and Kähler-Einstein manifolds, these symmetries are strictly compatible (not only asymptotically). In the paper 'DK conjecture for derived categories of some Grassmannian flips', we studied the DK Flip Conjecture of Bondal-Orlov and Kawamata, which states that there should be an embedding of derived categories for any flip, which is known to be true for toroidal flips. In this paper, we construct new examples of Grassmannian flips that satisfy the DK Flip Conjecture.

14303818.label: Project Objectives
14303818.value: Determine the long-term trends in MSL and tidal amplitudes, and the interannual and seasonal variability in tides correlated to the short-term MSL variability (TACs and δ-HATs) in Hong Kong and the SCS, garnered from both ground-based tide gauges and altimeter-based open water observations. Determine the historical water level exceedance and extreme high-water events at all tide gauges in the SCS and Hong Kong as well as in open water using satellite altimetry data from multiple missions. Determine future probability of nuisance flooding events in HK and the SCS based on past behavior of tidal and sea level variability, tidal predictions, frequency of high water exceedance, and future representative carbon pathway (RCP) emission scenarios of sea level rise to generate an ensemble of possible inundation scenarios. Use a digital elevation model (DEM) from the Hong Kong Lands Department to estimate future inundation areas based on the spatial field of calculated nuisance flooding probabilities, and use results to inform relevant coastal management authorities, which may assist with future planning.

14303818.label: Realisation of objectives
14303818.value: Objectives (1) and (2) were mainly addressed through the publication of a paper in the Ocean Science journal, entitled “Tidal Variability in the Hong Kong region”, which was accepted in 2019. This paper performed analyses of multiple tide gauges of the Hong Kong monitoring network, with data acquired from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) and the Hong Kong Marine Department (HKMD). The intention of this paper was to better understand the long-term trends of mean sea level (MSL) and tidal variability over the past 30 years. The results of these investigations clearly demonstrated that there is significant tidal variability associated with MSL variability over the time period considered, especially at locations in highly developed harbors (e.g., Quarry Bay in Victoria Harbour, and Tai Po Kau in Tolo Harbour). This article first considered the individual variabilities of the four largest tidal constituents, M2, S2, K1, and O1. Methods employed included the novel TAC method which calculates the changes in tides possible for a unit change in MSL. This method has been repeatedly demonstrated to be able to reveal important information about local tidal sensitivities. There were significant sensitivities of tidal amplitudes and phases seen at nearly all locations in Hong Kong. The second task was to combine the variabilities of all four tides as a proxy for the highest astronomical tide and its sensitivity to MSL fluctuations, which was denoted as δ-HAT. These analyses showed that the combined tidal fluctuations associated with sea level variability with extremely strong at the two harbour locations mentioned above; numerical results showed that at Quarry Bay, e.g., the increase of tidal range as parameterized by δ-HAT can be up to 655 mm for a 1 m MSL change, or a 65% positive amplification on top of sea level rise. It is hypothesized in the paper that this phenomenon is likely related to the significant anthropogenic modifications that have occurred in these locations over the past half century or so. Finally, it was also observed that there are significant correlations between diurnal (once-a-day; D1) and semidiurnal (twice-a-day; D2) tides, especially at the developed harbours. All these results demonstrate that tides in sensitive harbour locations may be partially dependent on the frequency of the forcing tides and partially dependent on local resonance changes due to modifications. In either case, the results show that the observed tidal sensitivity to changing sea levels may greatly increase future total water levels, nuisance flooding levels, coastal inundation, and other related secondary hazards. All of these may have significant impacts to coastal infrastructure, regional logistics, economics, and society. In addition, the results reveal important foundational information which can assist in future efforts to better determine water level exceedance and extreme high-water events. This foundation will be employed in future investigations which will consider the coastal response to different typhoon events and storm surge at all relevant locations in and around Hong Kong. Related to this work, another paper was published in 2020, which performed a modified version of TAC analyses which were especially designed for short-record tide gauges. This paper was focused on locations in the Indian Ocean (which are mostly very short records) and was entitled “Multi-Timescale Analysis of Tidal Variability in the Indian Ocean Using Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition”. This approach used a novel combination of the TAC and EEMD methods to separate different modes of variability and correlations between tides and MSL and individually compare them. These results showed that most locations in the Indian Ocean have significant correlations between MSL and tides, especially so for the yearly and annual timescales, which is hypothesized to be related to seasonal monsoon cycles. These results demonstrate a method which can be applied to other regions of the world, especially Hong Kong, which has several shorter-record tide gauges which were not considered in previous investigations. Finally, attempts were made to determine sensitivities of tides to MSL using altimetry data, though these tasks were found to not be so straightforward due to the longer sampling period of altimetry observations as compared to ground-based tide gauges (i.e., once every ten days vs. once every hour). However, a new set of papers are currently being worked on with colleagues at Ocean University of China in Qingdao, Shandong which uses the novel S-TIDE analysis package to understand open-ocean tidal changes and variability on both short- and long-term scales. These results are currently being finalized for submission. Objective (3) was realized through a recently-published paper in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans by Devlin et al. which was accepted in 2021 and was entitled “Extended Water Level Trends at Long-Record Tide Gauges Via Moving Window Averaging and Implications for Future Coastal Flooding”. In this work, the objectives originally laid out for Hong Kong and the SCS were applied globally to a large set of long-period tide gauges. Consideration was given to extended water levels, which included classical mean sea levels (MSL) in addition to time-variable components such as tides and annual cycles or seasonal variability. This paper described a new way to determine long-term trends of peak water levels (i.e., the highest “still-water” levels achievable over a given time era, not involving waves or very short-frequency variability) and compared these peak levels (PEWL) to mean levels of extended water levels (MEWL). Results showed that PEWL has a larger and more rapid trend of increase than MEWL at a majority of locations considered, with some locations having a PEWL trend nearly double that of MEWL. Notably, the strongest and largest trends were seen in the western margins of both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the latter of which includes Hong Kong and other nearby locations. These results suggest that the dynamics of sea level and tides, as well as seasonal variability, and highly sensitive in the Western Pacific, and closer examination is still required to better understand the characteristics and likely future increases. These results further analyzed in the context of IPCC projections and RCP scenarios to demonstrate that increased rates of PEWL may have additional implications for future flood levels at locations which have large projected increases in SLR. For Objective (4), the results from the 2019 paper (Ocean Science journal, entitled “Tidal Variability in the Hong Kong region”), discussed above for Objectives (1) and (2) helped to clearly demonstrate the locations of the Hong Kong regions which are most sensitive to increased MSL rise and extreme tidal variability. This information is now being used to instruct the construction of enhanced flood and inundation maps for future scenarios of sea level rise and tidal sensitivity as well as increased seasonal variability (Objective 3), and will be integrated into GIS-based maps using a DEM which will be overlain on various map layers to determine likely inundation zones from nuisance flooding and storm-surge flooding in the future and how these disasters may affect different public and private sector infrastructure, logistics, and society.

14303818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303818.value: 1. Mean sea level (MSL) is rising worldwide, and correlated changes in ocean tides are also occurring. This combination may influence future extreme sea levels, possibly increasing coastal inundation and nuisance flooding events in sensitive regions. Analyses of a set of tide gauges in Hong Kong reveal complex tidal behavior. Most prominent in the results are strong correlations of MSL variability to tidal variability over the 31-year period of 1986–2016; these tidal anomaly correlations (TACs) express the sensitivity of tidal amplitudes and phases (M2, S2, K1, O1) to MSL fluctuations and are widely observed across the Hong Kong region. It is demonstrated here that tidal changes in the Hong Kong coastal waters may be important in combination with MSL rise in impacting future total water levels. 2. Quantifying the nature and patterns of sea level rise (SLR) is a critical challenge for the sustainability and resilience of coastal zones. Studies of SLR typically consider time-averaged mean sea level (MSL) trends; however, coastal flooding is more sensitive to extended water level (EWL). Our results suggest that in the context of IPCC projections to demonstrate that increased rates of PEWL may have additional implications for future flood levels at locations which have large projected increases in SLR. 3. Tidal mixing in the coastal waters of Hong Kong was investigated using a combination of in situ observations and high-resolution satellite-derived sea surface temperature (SST) data. The study shows that both the near-fortnightly (Mf) and fortnightly (MSf) tides are enhanced due to nonlinear tidal signal interactions. Tidal constituent properties vary by space and depth, and high-resolution SST plays a pivotal role in resolving the spatial characteristics of tidal mixing. 4. Global sea level rise understanding is critical for coastal zones, and estuaries are particularly vulnerable to water level changes. A basin-wide survey of Pacific and Atlantic Ocean tide gauges shows that tidal changes due to sea level rise is present at most locations surveyed. A focused regional study of Hong Kong is also described as an example of how tidal evolution can impact high population density coastal zones.

14303818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303818.value: 1) The storm surge combining with larger tides and higher MSL may be explored in future that may amplify flood risk, coastal inundation, damage to infrastructure, and population displacement. 2) The tidal variability in multiple constituents may be additive and may reinforce MSL changes at some locations, aggravating coastal flooding, which may be further studied.

14303818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303818.value: 1) Mean sea level (MSL) is rising worldwide, and correlated changes in ocean tides are also occurring. This combination may influence future extreme sea levels, possibly increasing coastal inundation and nuisance flooding events in sensitive regions. 2) Sea level rise is a critical concern for coastal locations and has been extensively studied. Most previous approaches rely on the analysis of mean sea level (MSL) trends over long time periods. These estimates, however, typically neglect the evolution of tides as well as the influence of changing short-term (e.g., annual and seasonal) variability. Accurate assessments of potential future flood risks are better provided by the consideration of extended water levels (EWL), which includes MSL and tides, and the long-term changes in peak extended water levels (PEWL), which allows examination of long-term evolution in rates of MSL, tides, and annual or seasonal cycles.

14303918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303918.value: In this project we will investigate a novel form of collective oscillation recently discovered in bacterial swarms, aiming to control this phenomenon and to understand its potential role in active matter self-organization. Collective oscillatory behavior is ubiquitous in nature and it plays a vital role in many biological processes, such as embryogenesis, organ development, and pace-making in neuron networks. Collective oscillations in physical and biological systems studied to date often arise from coupling between individual units that display inherent oscillations. In stark contrast, we recently discovered a novel form of self-organized collective oscillatory motion in bacterial swarms that does not require inherent oscillation of individual units. Instead, it results from weak coupling between nearby cells and only emerges when averaging large numbers of erratic trajectories of single cells. Based on the established findings, in this project we aim to investigate potential means of modulating the dynamics of collective oscillation in bacterial swarms. We will also explore whether the collective oscillatory motion promotes self-assembly and phase separation in bacterial swarms, thereby influencing the spatial structure of biofilms. For the proposed studies we will combine genetic engineering and high-spatiotemporal-resolution cell manipulation techniques to perturb the behavior of cells, and to manipulate their interaction pattern as well as the self-organization dynamics. The project lies at the interface of physics and biology, and the obtained results will be of great interest to both fields. Bacterial swarms provide a model system for the study of active matter and complex fluids. Manipulating the dynamics of collective oscillation in bacterial swarms will provide new insights to the control of collective dynamics in general active matter systems. In addition, bacterial swarming is closely related to bacterial surface colonization and biofilm formation. Therefore understanding the collective behavior during bacterial swarming is of relevance to multicellularity and invasiveness. 此項目將研究最近在細菌集群中發現的自組織集體振蕩現象，並探討這一現象的可控性及其對於活性物質自組織的潛在應用。 周期性集體振盪現象廣泛存在於自然界中，並且在諸如胚胎發育、器官生長和神經網絡信號同步等許多生物過程中起到重要的作用。生物體系中的集體振盪通常需要在自身具有振盪行為的細胞個體之間建立長距離的相互作用。與之截然不同，我們最近在細菌集群中發現不需要局域振子的周期性集體振盪現象。這一現象的根源是大量無規則運動的細菌的弱同步和擴散式耦合。 基於已有的發現，我們在此項目中計劃研究如何控制集體振蕩行為，並探索集體振蕩行為是否有助於細菌集群的自組織和相分離，從而影響微生物膜的空間結構。為此我們計劃結合基因工程和高時空解析度細菌控制技術來操縱細菌的行為，它們的相互作用模式，以及它們的自組織動力學。 此項目涉及物理學和生物學的交叉領域，所得到的結果對相關領域都有重要的意義。細菌集群運動可以認為是自驅動或者活性物質體系的典型例子，因此此項目的研究結果會加深我們對活性物質體系的認識。同時，細菌集群運動與細菌表面定植和微生物膜的形成初期行為相似，因此對細菌集群運動的研究有助於理解細菌的多細胞狀態和致病過程。

14303918.label: Realisation of objectives
14303918.value: With the funding from this grant, we have realized both objectives. For Objective 1, we have developed a method to simultaneously control the spatial and temporal self-organization of bacterial active fluids by tuning the viscoelasticity of the suspending fluid through the addition of purified genomic DNA; we also developed means to control the collective modes of bacterial active solid by varying the activity of cells with light. For Objective 2, we discovered that confined dense active suspensions of Escherichia coli cells display self-driven spatial and temporal organization in the form of a millimetre-scale rotating vortex with periodically oscillating global chirality of tunable frequency, reminiscent of a torsional pendulum. Also we discovered that mass elements in bacterial active solids are self-driven into local oscillatory motion. Under two-dimensional isotropic confinement, the local oscillation self-organizes into a pair of topologically distinct global motion modes; surprisingly, the two modes transit between each other with a sharp, step-like frequency jump at certain activity threshold. Under anisotropic confinement with a major axis of symmetry, the local oscillation of mass elements is organized in space as self-sustained elastic standing waves.

14303918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303918.value: Two major research outputs arose from this project: 1. Liu S, Shankar S, Marchetti MC, Wu Y (2021) Viscoelastic control of spatiotemporal order in bacterial active matter. Nature 590: 80–84. By manipulating one single macroscopic parameter, i.e. the viscoelasticity of confined bacterial active fluids, we observed that the collective flows of cell-fluid assemblage undergo disorder-to-order transition in space, forming a gigantic millimeter-scale rotating vortex; more strikingly, the giant vortex can switch its global chirality periodically with tunable frequencies, reminiscent of a torsional pendulum – a self-driven one. Meanwhile, individual cells move erratically despite the global order. We explain the phenomena in terms of interplay between active forcing and viscoelastic stress relaxation. 2. Xu H., Huang Y., Zhang R., Wu Y (2022) Autonomous waves and global motion modes in living active solids. Nature Physics. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-022-01836-0 Elastic active matter or active solid consists of self-propelled units embedded in an elastic matrix. Active solid resists deformation; the shape-preserving property and the intrinsic non-equilibrium nature make active solids a superior component for self-driven devices. Nonetheless, the mechanical properties and emergent behavior of active solids are poorly understood. Using a biofilm-based bacterial active solid, here we discovered self-sustained elastic waves with unique wave properties not seen in passive solids, such as power-law scaling of wave speed with activity. Under isotropic confinement, the active solid develops two topologically distinct global motion modes that can be selectively excited, with a surprising step-like frequency jump at mode transition. Our findings reveal novel spatiotemporal order in elastic active matter and may guide the development of solid-state adaptive or living materials.

14303918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303918.value: Our findings on viscoelastic control of bacterial active fluids provide insight into the influence of bacterial motile behaviour in complex fluids, which may be of interest in health- and ecology-related research, and demonstrate experimentally that rheological properties can be harnessed to control active-matter flows. We envisage that our millimetre-scale, tunable, self-oscillating bacterial vortex may be coupled to actuation systems to act a ‘clock generator’ capable of providing timing signals for rhythmic locomotion of soft robots and for programmed microfluidic pumping, for example, by triggering the action of a shift register in soft-robotic logic devices. Our discovery of biofilm-derived bacterial active solid pave the way for investigating the non-equilibrium physics of elastic active matter in continuum, and may guide the development of solid-state adaptive or living materials, such as autonomous actuators for soft robotics, programmable tissues, and synthetic microbial consortia with mechanical functionalities.

14303918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303918.value: A central goal of active matter research is to understand and control the self-organization of active assemblies in space and time. We have discovered a simple technique to simultaneously control the spatial and temporal self-organization of bacterial active matter. This reveals self-driven spatial and temporal organization in the form of a millimetre-scale rotating vortex with periodically oscillating global chirality of tunable frequency, reminiscent of a torsional pendulum. Understanding the mechanical functionality of active matter as a continuum (i.e. the ability to generate forces or extract work at length scales much larger than the individual unit) is an essential step to bridge the gap between practical applications and a myriad of fundamental science knowledge in the field learned over the past two decades. Using a biofilm-based bacterial active solid, we discovered self-sustained elastic waves with unique wave properties not seen in passive solids, such as power-law scaling of wave speed with activity. Our findings reveal novel spatiotemporal order in elastic active matter and may guide the development of solid-state adaptive or living materials.

14304418.label: Project Objectives
14304418.value: Novel code designs for group-testing: For a variety of group-testing problems most (but not all) of the literature focuses on “random pooling designs” for group-testing. Recent work has begun to demonstrate that for some models one needs to go beyond this class of designs to improve performance (e.g., reduce the number of tests to guarantee recovery, or reduce computational complexity). We aim to systematically examine new ensembles of designs for group-testing problems. Understanding fundamental limits for group-testing: For many group-testing problems generally speaking the tightest known lower bounds on the number of tests required to guarantee recovery relies on a straightforward counting argument. While such bounds are tight in several models, there is now mounting evidence that in other models of interest these bounds are loose. We aim to examine recently developed information-theoretic techniques to tighten existing impossibility results. Understanding the effect of noise: A variety of existing algorithms in the literature are not robust to the impact of noise in test outcomes. Conversely, while existing information- theoretic bounds can be extended to scenarios with noisy tests, in some scenarios the naive extensions tend to underestimate the impact of noise in degrading performance. We aim to examine the impact of noise on group-testing problems by considering both noise-aware information-theoretic lower bounds on the number of tests required, and combinatorial optimization-based algorithms to provide robust recovery guarantees for a variety of group- testing problems. Computationally efficient algorithms/bounds: In some group-testing problems there are gaps between what is known to be information-theoretically possible, and what is known to be computationally possible. We aim to bring results from algorithmics/computational complexity to bear on the group-testing literature, and on the one hand design algorithms that are faster than those in the current literature, and on the other hand understand the fundamental limits of computationally efficient group-testing. Understanding implications for general non-linear inverse problems: A variety of natural non-linear inverse problems (e.g., network tomography) can be described in terms of generalizations of group-testing. We aim to investigate the generalizations of the previous objectives for these more general inverse problems.

14304418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304418.value: 分組檢測問題研究的是如何用非線性的分組方法從一個大的集合中檢測出一個隻包含一種特殊元素的子集。在最常探索的分組檢測問題中，每當完成一次檢測，檢測者都會得知被檢測的小組是否包含特殊元素。分組檢測可以運用到許多實際的問題中，例如，如何通過血液測試從大規模的人群中篩選出某種疾病的患者。一種可行的方法是對所有個體的血液樣本分別進行測試，但此方法需要的測試數量十分巨大。在一些情況下，若先將所有個體巧妙地分組，然后匯集並混合各組包含的個體的血液樣本，並對混合之后的血液樣本進行測試，則可以在保証檢測可靠性的基礎上顯著減少測試數量。除此之外，分組檢測的思想同樣可以運用到其他領域中，例如劣質工業產品檢測，特定的低速率無線通信協議，以及某些數據壓縮算法等等。分組檢測問題可以被視為一類最簡單的非線性估計問題。在本項目中，我們的目標是系統的研究分組檢測問題以及相關的拓展。 新型算法/基本極限：即使是最簡單的分組檢測問題，在理論上，各種性能（包括：精確估計所需的最低測試數量，以及可以逼近該最低測試數量的低復雜度算法）的基本極限依然未被解決。我們的目標是通過運用信息論、復雜度理論、以及算法領域的最新進展，從而解決目前尚未被完全理解的分組檢測問題。 噪聲的影響：在目前的文獻中，絕大部分文章都忽略了噪聲對測試結果的影響。然而在許多實際的估計問題中，檢測的結果並不是完全可靠地。因此，我們將在本項目中詳細的考慮分析噪聲對分組檢測算法的影響。 向一般非線性估計問題的拓展：我們注意到許多有關分組檢測的文獻都專注於如何匯集樣本進行檢測，但其中蘊含的思想同樣可以拓展並運用到更廣泛的存在限制的非線性估計問題中（例如已知元素的先驗統計，可進行測試的類型受限，以及测试中不同类型的非线性性）。我们力求广泛考察此类问题。 項目領導者和其他研究人員針對上述模型的一系列最新結果表明，前述的研究具有可觀的前景。鑒於所考慮問題（非線性估計問題）的廣泛而根本的特性，該提案中獲得的研究成果也會為其他懸而未決的基本問題的解決帶來曙光。 關鍵詞：分組檢測，信息論，編碼理論，非線性估計，圖編碼

14304418.label: Realisation of objectives
14304418.value: In this work the PI and his collaborators were able to make significant progress on understanding various aspects of non-linear sparse recovery problems. In particular, we designed novel algorithms in a variety of settings (such as when the testing itself is required to be sparse, motivated by physical considerations), prove information-theoretic near-optimality of these algorithms, further demonstrate the robustness to noise and computational tractability of these algorithms. We were also able to generalize many of these notions to broad classes of non-adaptive non-linear sparse recovery problems beyond just the classical group-testing setting.

14304418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304418.value: Broadly speaking, significant progress was made on the major objectives of this project. 1. In "Nearly Optimal Sparse Group Testing" (Research output journal paper), novel sparse group-testing schemes were designed (Research Objective 1), it was shown that these schemes approached fundamental limits (Research Objective 2), their robustness to noise was demonstrated in some scenarios (Research Objective 3), and they were shown to be computationally tractable (Research Objective 4). (While the original submission was in August 2017, the revisions included significant new materials arising from this project -- in particular, tighter information-theoretic lower bounds, faster group-testing algorithms, and the impact of noise on group-testing) 2. In "Generalized non-adaptive group-testing" (Research output under preparation, a topic that was initiated in the early summer of 2020, and is now being polished for submission to a journal, with a pre-print on ArXiV), we demonstrated that a large class of non-linear sparse recovery problems could be handled by a single group-testing-inspired algorithm (Research objective 5). In further ongoing work we believe we can show the universal optimality of this algorithm. (Research objective 2) 3. In "A Novel Computationally Efficient Decoding Algorithm for Group Testing" (Research output conference paper), we showed computationally efficient decoding algorithms for non-adaptive group-testing that could improve upon the performance of the baseline COMP algorithm in the literature with minimal additional cost in computational complexity. (GRF funding was acknowledged during the presentation.)

14304418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304418.value: The ongoing work on "Generalized Non-Adaptive Group Testing" is of particular interest. In our current version being polished, we are able to handle quite general binary-input binary-output stochastic measurement functions (with "natural" minor restrictions -- requiring them to be symmetric, and monotone in the test positivity probability). Further extensions that seem within reach that would be particularly interesting include settings where there are non-binary inputs and non-binary outputs (with partial orders on both input and output alphabets), and suitably defined versions of monotonicity. In this setting we believe our existing algorithm should be order-optimal.

14304418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304418.value: Classical group-testing considers the mathematical problem of identifying a "few" diseased individuals from a large population via "pooled" tests (where due to various reasons the time or cost of testing every individual in the population would be prohibitive, but pooling samples from multiple people in different combinations, testing these groups, and then analyzing the results to infer which individuals are diseased, significantly reduces the number of tests required). While classical group-testing is reasonably well-understood mathematically, to make it applicable in real-world settings, one should examine settings where the variable accuracy/sensitivity of these pooled tests needs to be taken into account in designing testing schemes, computationally efficient methods of analyzing the results of these tests are required, and ideally one should also understand the fundamental limits of what is possible and what is not via these pooled tests. In this project we were able to make significant headway in all of our related research objectives. In light of the COVID pandemic this research is particularly topical.

14304618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304618.value: Solid state quantum systems are playing a huge role in the development of practical quantum technologies, ranging from quantum information processing devices to high-precision quantum sensing technologies. For both applications, each individual qubit should be controlled with high fidelity over many rounds of operations. However, these solid-state qubits are under the influence of the random magnetic noise caused by other spins within the host material. This process causes decoherence that limits the quantum sensing sensitivity and loss of quantum information during quantum communication or in a quantum computation. Methods such as dynamical decoupling has been traditionally used to control this decoherence, and as well to isolate spins from the spin bath for useful applications. Alternatively, by measuring the spin bath states and projecting them into known states, we not only can reduce decoherence caused by the spin-bath, but also use it as a resource for quantum technologies, for example as quantum memories, quantum buffer, etc. We propose to explore this new feature using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. We have chosen this system, because high fidelity and fast single shot readout of both electron spin and nuclear spin states is possible and has been experimentally demonstrated. By performing quantum non-demolition measurements on the bath nuclear spins, we not only measure the spin bath trajectory, but also project the bath spins into certain system eigenstates. Thus, by carefully optimizing the experimental parameters, we can engineer the quantum states of the spin-bath that are previously undetermined. These states can be well-defined single spin states which then can be used as qubits for scalable quantum computation, a many-body singlet paired state that has no magnetic projection on central qubit thereby enhancing its life time, or can be used for many-body physics research or as a quantum repository for quantum information exchange. We will also use these qubits to prepare the 5-qubit Steane codes to perform quantum error correction with high fidelity to enhance the coherent storage time of single qubit information in a single NV center beyond 1 second. Instead of just being a source of decoherence, the spin bath will be explored in this proposal as a new resource for quantum applications. This would provide the key step for scaling up quantum devices in quantum technologies. 固體量子體系在應用量子科技上有著重要的位置。實際的應用需要量子比特能在多次測量之後仍有很高的保真度。但是量子比特周圍的自旋環境產生隨機的噪音，影響著量子比特的相幹性。很多方法比如動態去耦已經被用來對抗這種噪音，把量子比特從環境噪音裏孤立出來。我們這裏提出，通過量子測量，把自旋環境投影到已知的量子態，這樣不僅能夠減少噪音，而且還能把自旋環境作為量子科技的新資源。 我們提出用鉆石裏的氮缺陷來實現這個設想，因為這個體系可以單次讀出電子和核自旋的狀態。通過對於核自旋環境做量子非破壞測量，我們不僅可以知道核自旋環境的狀態，而且還可以把它們投影到特定的狀態。通過對於實驗參數的優化，我們可以制備以前無法制作的核自旋環境態。我們會進一步，用這些態來做多比特的量子操作，比如5比特的量子糾錯。 量子自旋環境一直是量子錯誤的來源，通過這個研究，我們把它作為一種新的量子資源。這個會對量子科技的發展起到很大的作用。

14304618.label: Realisation of objectives
14304618.value: In this project, we have explored in several directions on quantum spin bath engineering to minimize its influence on central qubit as noise sources and manipulate them as auxiliary qubits. (1) We have realized the purification of spin bath via quantum probe measurements (Nature Communications 13, 7527(2022)). This was realized in diamond samples with lowest impurity level. The residue magnetic noise is from the C-13 nuclear spin bath. The C-13 spin bath was projected into pure states. This greatly helps the improvement of decoherence time of the central NV center spin. The T2* time of NV center increases by a factor of 2 and the linewidth of the spin resonance decreases. Furthermore, by repetitive quantum measurements, the C-13 spin bath state stays beyond milliseconds under Anti-Zeno purification, this greatly reduces the error generated by nuclear spin bath on central qubit. These results addresses Objective 1,2 and 3. (2) Diamond samples which are commonly used for quantum sensing and quantum simulations have much stronger spin bath. The method in part 1 alone is not enough to suppress these noise sources. We developed two novel methods to solve this bottle neck problem: (a) purify spin baths of NV center by manipulating local electronic environment (Nature Physics 18, 1317(2022)). By using a "push-pull" driving method, electron spins around NV center spin were depleted. The decoherence time of NV center was increased by several times, up to 20 folds. After this optimization, we were able to use dynamical decoupling to probe and manipulate weakly coupled C-13 nuclear spins for shallow NV centers. This work addresses Objective 1 and 2. (b) purify spin baths of NV center via thermally driven recombination of paramagnetic defects (Physical Review Applied 18, 024044 (2022)). In this work, we triggered the recombination processes of paramagnetic defects into less magnetic or nonmagnetic defects in ultra high temperature. Therefore the spin bath is greatly suppressed. The decoherence time increases 4 times. By using dynamical decoupling and double electron electron resonance, we can probe and manipulate both C-13 nuclear spin and residue electron spins. This work addresses Objective 1 and 2.

14304618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304618.value: In this project, we have developed three novel methods for quantum spin bath engineering in NV center in diamond. All these methods can be adapted in other physical systems in solids. Since these spin baths are the major noise sources in quantum information in solids, these new methods have big importance in these fields. 1. By using repetitive quantum measurements, nuclear spin bath around central qubit can be projected into pure states. This is a new way of manipulating weakly coupled nuclear spins. This method leads to the frozen of corresponding nuclear spin bath up to millisecond. This greatly reduces the quantum errors, and significantly increases the decoherence time. 2. By using a "push-pull" driving method, we depleted most electron spins around NV center spin. This method shines light on the electronic environments around NV center. This method increases decoherence time for all NV centers under study, up to 20 folds. This method not only makes the manipulation of single nuclear spin inside diamond near shallow implanted NV center possible, but also paves the way for manipulate single external nuclear spin. 3. By using thermally driven recombination of paramagnetic defects, we increased decoherence times of diamond samples with a vast range of qubit concentrations, up to 4 times.

14304618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304618.value: With these three methods ready, we can explore nuclear spins unreachable before. We can further increase the performance for the repetitive quantum measurement method by increasing the fidelity of single shot readout. For better control of the spin bath, one would need to perform the readout faster than the evolution time of the bath. We can optimize the readout time needed for each measurement and develop a novel realtime feedback method for realizing quantum algorithms.

14304618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304618.value: Solid state qubits are one of the most promising physical systems to realize quantum technology, as they have good quantum properties and can adapt many well-established semiconductor technologies. The bottle neck of this field is to reduce noise and boost up the decoherence time, as the qubit cannot hold its quantum properties beyond decoherence time due to various paramagnetic defects around it. These defects are currently hard to remove and some of them can be useful if one can manipulate them. In this project, we developed three new methods to solve this challenge. We developed two methods to greatly reduce these noise sources via thermal or electrical manipulations. The decoherence time can be boosted up to nearly two orders of magnitude. We also took advantaged of quantum measurement which is not only just a readout but also an operation. We can project residue weak spin bath into pure quantum state, thus converting harmful noise into useful auxiliary qubits. All these methods can be adapted widely and thus be useful for the whole community of quantum information science.

14304918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304918.value: 這項提議的工作的目的,是使用環萜基硫屬元素化物作為軟路易斯鹼性有機催化劑，來開發有效的不飽和化合物的親電子官能化反應。 不飽和化合物的親電官能化是一種非常有用的有機反應。軟路易斯鹼性硫屬元素化物（例如硫化物，硒化物）的有機催化劑被認為是金屬催化劑的更環保的替代物，並已經使用於一系列親電子官能化反應。軟路易斯鹼性硫屬元素化物可以與軟親電子試劑配位，得到高度極化的絡合物;這可以加速不飽和化合物的親電子官能化。然而，在文獻中，由於有機催化劑的路易斯鹼度相對較弱，反應通常都需要高催化劑量。 環丙烯亞胺是一種新興的布朗斯台德鹼催化劑，已被證明在催化各種有機轉化方面具有很高的效力。由於芳族環萜烯體系穩定了環丙烯亞胺的共軛酸，因此增強了胺的鹼性。環丙烯鹽系統具有穩定的結構。然而，到目前尚未有研究將環丙烯系統結合到軟路易斯鹼性硫屬元素化物, 並應用於路易斯鹼性有機催化的反應。 我們的研究小組多年來一直致力於開發軟路易斯鹼性硫代氨基甲酸酯（含硫化物的化合物）有機催化劑（例如Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 5161; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2013, 52, 8597; Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 7985）。雖然硫代氨基甲酸酯可以催化一系列親電官能化反應，但它們的催化性能仍然不夠高。我們還開發了一種相關的兩性離子路易斯鹼系統，但這種催化劑存在結構不穩定性。因此，開發更有效的軟路易斯鹼性硫屬元素化物有機催化體系有一定的需要。 最近，在一項未發表的研究中，我們發現環丙烯硫醚有機催化劑可以催化一系列親電子官能化反應，包括烯烴的分子間鹵代乙酰氧基化，鹵代氨基化和芳族鹵化。環萜硫屬元素化物的催化性能明顯優於一般結構相關的軟路易斯鹼性硫屬元素化物有機催化劑。基於這些試驗結果，在這項擬議的工作中，我們計劃進一步開發和探索環丙烯硫屬元素化物有機催化劑在不飽和化合物的各種親電子官能化中的應用。預計新的催化平台將成為有機合成的重要工具。

14305018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305018.value: Carboranes, carbon-boron molecular clusters, are finding increasing and valuable applications in coordination/organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents, in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks, and in optoelectronic materials as unique electron sinks. It is noteworthy that the overwhelming majority of carborane-based functional molecules are substituted at cage carbon positions, due to the facile functionalization of acidic cage C-H bonds (pKa ~ 23), which precludes the progression of the application of carboranes. Though a considerable progress in transition metal catalyzed regioselective B-H functionalization of carboranes has recently been made, only a few methods are available. Regioselective multi-functionalization of carboranes, with different functional groups in a one-pot process, is still a very challenging subject. The Xie group previously reported a conversion from metal-carbon to metal-boron bond in o-carborane, and very recently the Spokoyny and Peryshkov groups described halogen and metal migrations among BH vertices in m-carborane, respectively. Such “cage-walking” processes might provide a promising alternative strategy for cage B-H functionalization. We plan, in this proposal, to develop new methodologies for the selective multi-functionalization of o-carboranes via a “cage-walking” strategy and to study the mechanisms of these processes. It is anticipated that the project would generate a wide variety of cage B-substituted o-carborane derivatives, which might find valuable applications in many areas. Reaction mechanism investigation is intrinsic to this proposal, aiming to improve the fundamental understanding of “cage-walking” phenomena in o-carboranes. This would in turn shed light on how to control the selectivity of “cage-walking” processes for the effective synthesis of target products. 碳硼烷是一類由碳和硼原子組成的簇合物，它們在配位化學、超分子設計、材料及醫藥領域有廣泛而重要的應用。因此，發展直接而高效的方法來構築新型碳硼烷功能分子尤為重要。由於缺乏有效的修飾硼氫頂點的方法，絕大多數碳硼烷功能分子是籠碳取代的碳硼烷衍生物。儘管過渡金屬催化為選擇性硼氫活化提供了可靠的策略，十個硼氫頂點選擇性多官能團化仍然是極大的挑戰。謝作偉教授課題組率先報導了碳硼烷金屬碳鍵到金屬硼鍵的轉化反應。最近，Spokoyny和Peryshkov課題組分別發現鹵素及過渡金屬在碳硼烷不同硼氫頂點間的遷移現象。我們認為可以發展“籠遷移”的策略實現碳硼烷選擇性多官能團化。可以期待，此研究將會產生一系列具有潛在應用價值的新型硼取代碳硼烷功能分子。細緻的機理研究將提高我們對“籠遷移”現象的基本理解，同時引導更加高效的“籠遷移”合成策略的發展。

14305018.label: Realisation of objectives
14305018.value: Carboranes are finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry, and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed toward the area of carborane functionalization. In this project, we have developed new methodologies for the selective mono- or multi-functionalization of o-carboranes via a “cage-walking” strategy. Under the help of an acylamino directing group at cage B(3), a series of B(8)-arylated, B(4,7,8)-triarylated and B(4,7,8)-trifluorinated o-carborane derivatives were conveniently prepared. On the basis of isolation of a key intermediate, deuterium labeling experiments, and DFT calculations, a reaction mechanism involving high-valent palladium induced “cage-walking” from B(4) to B(7) and B(8) vertices was proposed to account for the regioselective B(4,7,8)-H activation and functionalization. We then developed a cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with readily available benzamide, resulting in the facile synthesis of previously inaccessible carborano-isoquinolinone derivatives in a simple one-pot process, in which two cage B-H, one aryl C-H and one N-H bond were sequentially activated to construct efficiently new B-C and B-N bonds, respectively, via “cage-walking” of Ir catalyst. The CV results combined with control experiments indicate that high-valent Ir(V)-species may be involved in the reaction pathways, which is crucial for such cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling reactions. The isolation and structural identification of a key intermediate, its controlled transformations, and deuterium labeling experiments support a new Ir-nitrene mediated amination for B-H/N-H dehydrocoupling. Having achieved Ir-catalyzed cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with readily available benzamide, we extended this reaction to include benzoic acids. Subsequently, an Ir-catalyzed cascade dehydrogenative CH/BH and BH/OH cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with readily available benzoic acid was achieved, leading to the facile synthesis of previously unavailable carborano-coumarin in a simple one-pot process via the migration of Ir catalyst from B(4) to B(5). Two cage B-H, one aryl C-H and one O-H bond are activated to construct efficiently new B-C and B-O bonds. The cascade cyclization can stop at the first B-H/C-H cross-coupling step by tuning the reaction conditions, resulting in a series of α-carboranyl benzoic acid and aryl carborane derivatives. Control experiments indicate that B-H/C-H dehydrocoupling proceeds preferentially over B-H/O-H dehydrocoupling, and both directing groups and oxidants are crucial for this reaction. An iridium(V) intermediate is proposed to be involved in the catalytic cycle. We also developed a rhodium-catalyzed one-pot trifunctionalization of o-carboranes with three different substituents via a carboxy group directed sequential B(5)-alkenylation, B(4)-alkyne annulation and B(3)-acyloxylation via “cage-walking” of Rh catalyst, leading to the synthesis of a new class of B(3,4,5) trisubstituted o-carborane derivatives. Treatment of 1-COOH-2-CH3-o-C2B10H10 with ArC≡CAr in the presence of [Cp*RhCl2]2 catalyst and Cu(OPiv)2 oxidant gave 1,4-[COOC(Ar)=C(Ar)]-2-Me-3-OPiv-5-[C(Ar)=CH(Ar)-o-C2B10H7 in good to high yields. This protocol represents a new strategy for catalytic selective polyfunctionalization of carboranes with different substituents via “cage-walking” of a metal catalyst. A Pd-catalyzed 3,4-bifunctionalization of 3-I-o-carborane was achieved, leading to the synthesis of a new class of 3-alkenyl-4-R-o-carboranes (R = alkyl, alkynyl, aryl, allyl, CN and amido) in high to excellent yields. This highly regioselective bifunctionalization protocol combines the sequential activation of cage B−I and B(4)−H bonds to furnish cage B(3) and B(4) functionalization with different substituents in a one-pot manner. The walking of Pd from exo-alkenyl sp2 carbon to cage B(4) serves as a key step in this new process, which is thermodynamically very favorable as indicated by DFT results. This work represents a new route for regioselective bifunctionalization of o-carborane with different substituents. In a similar manner, a Pd-catalyzed sequential B(3)−I and B(4)−H bonds activation has been achieved for the synthesis of 3,4-benzo-o-carboranes via a formal [2 + 2 + 2] cycloaddition of 3-I-o-carborane with 2 equiv of arylalkynes. This work not only presents a new route for the preparation of o-carborane-fused cyclics, but also describes another pathway of metal migration on the cage (cage-walking). Following the same strategy, a Pd-catalyzed highly selective tetrafunctionalization of 3,6-I2-o-carborane and 4,7-I2-o-carborane has been developed, leading to the preparation of 3,6-dialkenyl-4,11-R2-o-carboranes and 4,7-dialkenyl-5,11-R2-o-carboranes (R = alkyl, allyl, and aryl) in moderate to excellent yields. This represents another route for selective synthesis of polyfunctionalized o-carborane derivatives via the walking of Pd catalyst. Finally, we moved to base metal catalysis and invented a traceless bidentate directing group guided copper-catalyzed direct cage B(4,5)−H disulfenylation of o-carboranes via migration of Cu catalyst, leading to a series of B(4,5)−disulfenylated o-carborane derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity. The in-situ departure of the 8-aminoquinoline bidentate auxiliary circumvents additional processes for directing group removal, thus enhancing the atom-/step-economy. In summary, we have developed several new methods on the basis of the “cage walking” strategy for the preparation of a wide range of functionalized carborane molecules via transition metal catalysis, which might find valuable applications in many realms. The associated reaction mechanisms have also been investigated via the combination of control experiments and DFT calculations. The results offer a better fundamental understanding of the “cage-walking” phenomenon in o-carboranes, which in turn would shed light on how to control the selectivity of “cage-walking” processes for the effective synthesis of target products. This project has been very successfully carried out and all objectives have been achieved.

14305018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305018.value: (1) Development of Directing Group-Assisted “Cage-Walking” of Metal Catalyst for Selective Functionalization of o-Carboranes (Pub. #1, #4, #5, #8 and #14) Under the assistance of an acylamino directing group at cage B(3), a series of B(8)-arylated, B(4,7,8)-triarylated and B(4,7,8)-trifluorinated o-carborane derivatives were conveniently prepared via “cage-walking” of Pd catalyst from B(4) to B(7) and B(8) vertices for the regioselective B(4,7,8)-H activation and functionalization. A carboxy group assisted Ir-catalyzed cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with benzamide was developed, resulting in the facile synthesis of previously inaccessible carborano-isoquinolinone derivatives in a simple one-pot process, in which two cage B-H, one aryl C-H and one N-H bond were sequentially activated to construct efficiently new B-C and B-N bonds, respectively, via “cage-walking” of Ir catalyst. Subsequently, a carboxy group-assisted Ir-catalyzed cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with benzoic acids was invented, resulting in the facile synthesis of carborano-coumarin in a simple one-pot process via the migration of Ir catalyst from B(4) to B(5). In addition, a rhodium-catalyzed one-pot trifunctionalization of o-carboranes with three different substituents was achieved through a carboxy group directed sequential B(5)-alkenylation, B(4)-alkyne annulation, and B(3)-acyloxylation via “cage-walking” of Rh catalyst, leading to the synthesis of a new class of B(3,4,5) trisubstituted o-carborane derivatives. Finally, we developed a traceless bidentate directing group guided copper catalyzed direct cage B(4,5)−H disulfenylation of o-carboranes via migration of Cu catalyst, leading to a series of B(4,5)−disulfenylated o-carborane derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity. (2) Development of Directing-Group-Free Multi-functionalization of Carboranes via “Cage-Walking” of Metal Catalyst (Pub. #6, #9, and #12) A Pd-catalyzed 3,4-bifunctionalization of 3-I-o-carborane was achieved, leading to the synthesis of a new class of 3-alkenyl-4-R-o-carboranes (R = alkyl, alkynyl, aryl, allyl, CN and amido) in high to excellent yields. This highly regioselective bifunctionalization protocol combines the sequential activation of cage B−I and B(4)−H bonds to furnish cage B(3) and B(4) functionalization with different substituents via “cage-walking” of Pd from B(3) to B(4). This work represents a new route for regioselective bifunctionalization of o-carborane with different substituents. Subsequently, it was found that alternation of the reaction conditions resulted in a formal [2 + 2 + 2] cycloaddition of 3-I-o-carborane with 2 equiv of arylalkynes for the synthesis of 3,4-benzo-o-carboranes via a Pd-catalyzed sequential B(3)−I and B(4)−H bonds activation. Following the same strategy, a Pd-catalyzed highly selective tetrafunctionalization of 3,6-I2-o-carborane and 4,7-I2-o-carborane was also developed, leading to the preparation of 3,6-dialkenyl-4,11-R2-o-carboranes and 4,7-dialkenyl-5,11-R2-o-carboranes (R = alkyl, allyl, and aryl) in moderate to excellent yields via the walking of Pd catalyst. In summary, this original work has resulted in 14 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x 2), Angew. Che. Int. Ed. (x 1), ACS Catal. (x 1), Chem. Commun. (x 4), Dalton Trans. (x 2), Chin. J. Chem. (x 1), Chem. Soc. Rev. (x 1), Chem. Asian J. (x 1), and Bull. Chem. Soc. Jpn. (x 1). PI was invited to give one plenary, one keynote, and two invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students have been trained, of which two have graduated.

14305018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305018.value: Regioselective metal-catalyst migration has been achieved. We wonder if enantioselective metal-catalyst migration would be possible with the assistance of chiral ligands. If so, chiral-at-cage carborane derivatives could be prepared via asymmetrical catalysis. We will explore such asymmetrical catalysis in the future.

14305018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305018.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, can be viewed as three-dimensional analogs of benzene. They are finding many applications in coordination/ organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents and in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks. All this has recently drawn considerable attention to carborane chemistry. However, the exceptional thermal and chemical stable 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, limiting their application scope. The development of an efficient and general technique to functionalize carboranes will be one of the main issues in this field. In this project, we have developed a new "cage walking" strategy for the functionalization of carboranes, leading to the invention of several methods for the efficient synthesis of a large class of poly cage B-functionalized o-carboranes under mild conditions with high yields. These functionalized o-carboranes may find applications in materials and medicine.

14305318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305318.value: The aim of this project is to develop statistical methods to analyze time-to-event data on a social network. A social network depicts the interactions among a set of social actors. With the rise of social media and electronic commerce, social network data are prevalent today. Consequently, there has been extensive research on social network analysis over the past two decades. However, most research focused on network data for which the edges between actors are binary or coded with continuous weights. In contrast, more and more social networks can now record a sequence of time-to-event data for a pair of actors, which often provides alternative perspectives into interpersonal relationships. For instance, an employee may have many more emails with a secretary than with the CEO but replies to emails from the CEO much faster than to those from the secretary. Modeling the reply time instead of the number of emails between employees can offer novel insights into the company organization and leadership style. Similarly, we have recently collaborated with a Hong-Kong-based electronic document management company to understand employees' priorities in dealing with assigned tasks. However, despite the abundant information encoded in time-to-event data on a social network, their analyses are challenging. Given a social network, the pairs of actors having time-to-event data are usually sparse, and the number of data points for each pair is often small. Moreover, the interaction patterns are heterogeneous across actor pairs. So far, statistical methods for analyzing time-to-event data on a social network are still lacking. In this project, we propose a novel Bayesian framework to analyze time-to-event data on a social network, which borrows information across all actor pairs while enables pair-specific inference. Globally, our proposed model will be able to detect the social clusters in a network and characterize the between-cluster and within-cluster interaction patterns; locally, our model will be capable of identifying the social roles for each actor pair and predicting their interaction patterns. For posterior inference, we will develop efficient parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms and make them freely available. We will use the proposed methods to study company emails, and the scientific discoveries will directly benefit business problems in Hong Kong. The proposed statistical methods will make profound contributions to network analysis, survival analysis, and parallel computing. The application to company emails will greatly deepen our understanding of company organization, improve communication and business efficiency, and ultimately enhance economic development in Hong Kong and elsewhere. 本項目旨在開發統計方法來分析社交網絡上的生存數據。 社交網絡描繪了一組社交角色之間的互動關係。隨著社交媒體和電子商務的興起，社交網絡數據如今已非常普遍。因此，在過去二十年中已有大量對社交網絡的研究。然而，大多數研究都只針對網絡中的邊是二元數據或連續權重的網絡數據。 最近，越來越多的社交網絡可以為一對參與者記錄一系列時間到事件數據--即統計學所說的生存數據，這為研究人際關係提供了新的視角。例如，員工可能收到的秘書電子郵件遠多於首席執行官的電子郵件，但回复首席執行官的郵件的速度遠遠快於回复秘書的郵件。對回复時間而不是僅對員工之間的電子郵件數量進行建模可以為了解公司組織和領導模式提供新的見解。與之相類似，我們最近與一家總部位於香港的電子文檔管理公司合作來研究員工處理指定任務的優先級。 然而，儘管社交網絡上的生存數據中包含了豐富的信息，但他們的分析具有挑戰性。給定一個社交網絡，具有生存數據的參與者對通常是稀疏的，並且每對參與者所擁有的樣本量通常很小。此外，不同參與者對之間的交互模式常常不同。到目前為止，分析社交網絡上生存數據的統計方法任然十分匱乏。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一個新穎的貝葉斯框架來分析社交網絡上的生存數據。該方法充分利用所有參與者對的信息來進行統計推斷。就整個網絡而言，我們提出的模型將能夠檢測網絡中的社交群集，並描述群集間和群集內的交互模式; 對每個參與者對，我們的模型將能夠識別每個參與者所扮演的社會角色並預測他們的交互模式。對於後驗推理，我們將開發有效的並行算法並提供免費的軟件包。我們會使用所提出的方法來研究公司的電子郵件。得出的科學發現將直接有利於香港的商業問題。 本項目所提出的統計方法將為網絡分析、生存分析和並行計算做出重要貢獻。對公司電子郵件的研究將大大加深我們對公司組織的了解、改善溝通和業務效率、並最終促進香港和其他地方的經濟發展。

14305318.label: Realisation of objectives
14305318.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the proposal. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed in Part C. We have developed a Bayesian hierarchical model—the survival mixed membership blockmodel (SMMB)—by integrating the mixed membership stochastic blockmodel (MMSB) for binary networks with semiparametric cure rate models to model the time-to-event data observed for node pairs in a social network [1]. We have proven the model identifiability of SMMB. Noteworthy, the identifiability of the MMSB is a challenging theoretical problem with emerging results such as the recent paper by Mao et al. (JASA 2020). We have developed a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct posterior inference, and we provide our C++ code and instructions of how to apply the algorithm to time-to-event data freely available at https://github.com/songfd2018/SurNet. We have applied our algorithm to analyze the famous Enron e-mail corpus datasets and find communication patterns missed by traditional MMSB models. Moreover, the proof of the model identifiability of the proposed SMMB model enables us to investigate a related problem for Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs)—whether a peer review scheme for a MOOC is valid so that the true score for each homework submission can be recovered despite the grader-specific bias [2]. We have developed a linear-time-complexity algorithm, BFS-MOOCs, built upon the breadth-first search (BFS) algorithm to quickly determine the validity of a given peer assessment scheme. Compared with an alternative approach, the speed of BFS-MOOCs accelerates over 1,000 times. Moreover, when the peer assessment scheme is invalid, BFS-MOOCs provides a strategy for the instructor to remedy an invalid observed assessment grid by grading a small number of additional submissions as suggested by the algorithm. We provide our C++ code and instructions of how to apply the algorithm freely available at https://github.com/songfd2018/MOOCs.

14305318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305318.value: Whenever we send a message via a channel such as e-mail, Facebook, WhatsApp, or WeChat, we care about the response rate—the probability that our message will receive a response—and the response time—how long it will take to receive a reply. Recent studies have made considerable efforts to model the sending behaviors of messages in social networks. However, statistical research on modeling response rates and response times on social networks is still lacking. Compared with sending behaviors, which are often determined by the sender's characteristics, response rates and response times further depend on the relationship between the sender and the receiver. In this project, we develop a survival mixed membership blockmodel (SMMB) that integrates semiparametric cure rate models with a mixed membership stochastic blockmodel (MMSB) to analyze time-to-event data observed for node pairs in a social network [1]. The SMMB also allows the response time to depend on covariates. The SMMB simultaneously learns the network structure from the data and uses the learned structure to improve user-pair-specific inference. The identifiability of the MMSB is already a challenging theoretical problem with only recent results. Mao et al. (JASA 2020) prove that the existence of pure nodes in the network who play one and only one latent role is not only sufficient but also necessary for the MMSB for binary networks to be identifiable. Fortunately, as time-to-event data encode more information, we are able to prove that the SMMB is identifiable up to label switching without the pure node assumption. We develop a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct posterior inference and select the number of social clusters using the conditional deviance information criterion. Applying the SMMB to the Enron e-mail corpus reveals interesting leadership patterns. Employees play distinct roles depending on whether they are communicating with superiors or subordinates. In addition, we find that junior employees replied to e-mails sent by other junior employees more slowly at weekends than on weekdays. However, if an e-mail was sent by a senior employee to a junior employee, then whether the e-mail was sent at the weekend or during the weekdays did not affect the junior employee’s response time. Meanwhile, the identifiability proof of the SMMB also enable us to develop an algorithm, BFS-MOOCs to check the validity of a peer review scheme for a MOOC so that the true score for each homework submission can be recovered despite the grader-specific bias [2].

14305318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305318.value: With the rapid development of social media and electronic commerce, many social networks now encompass time-to-event data. Although we focus on an e-mail network, many other social networks have similar time-to-event data. For example, the times taken for users to re-post messages from other users are available for Twitter and Sina Weibo. Moreover, in web-based electronic document management systems such as the services provided by Dropbox and ParaDM, the time that a team member or an employee spends on an assigned task can also be recorded, and the question of how soon a user responds to the action of another user is also of great interest in this context. We envision that the proposed SMMB can help to analyze these networks and provide insights into information flow, company organization, and working efficiency.

14305318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305318.value: People are relying more and more on social media for communication. Whenever we send a message via e-mail, Facebook, WhatsApp, WeChat, or LinkedIn, we always care about how soon our message will receive a response from its recipient, namely the response time. However, statistical research on modeling response times on social networks is still lacking. Compared with sending behaviors, which are often determined by the sender's characteristics, response times further depend on the relationship between the sender and the receiver. Moreover, some messages may never be replied to; thus, it is also important to model non-response events, which are overlooked in previous studies. In this project, we propose a survival mixed membership blockmodel to model the response time between actors on a social network. Application of our proposed model to emails within a company shows that the response rate and response time of an employee depends on whether the sender of the email is a superior or subordinate of the recipient, and we can infer people’s seniority within the company according to their response rates and response times. Therefore, by modeling response times between node pairs on a social network, the proposed model can reveal important social interaction patterns.

14305518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305518.value: We propose to make a systematic study of Iwasawa algebras of a large class of open compact subgroups of a p-adic reductive groups which are uniform pro-p groups, and are defined in terms of Bruhat-Tits theory. The studying of these objects is of fundamental importance in Iwasawa theory of p-adic Langlands program, and has been investigated in the past 20 years by many authors, often in the generality of all uniform pro-p groups. However, we believe that more significant results can only be obtained when we restrict to the class mentioned above. Most expected applications to number theory pertain to this class. The PI already has preliminary results showing the richness of the structure theory, including generators and relations and integral group scheme structures. 我們提議系統研究某些緊緻 p-群的岩澤代數，這些緊緻 p-群是 p-adic 可約群的開緊子群，來自於 Bruhat-Tits 理論，並且滿足群論上的一致條件。研究這些是對 Langlands 綱領和岩澤理論的關係有基本重要性的，而在過去二十年已經被很多學者討論過，但通常是對完全一般的一致群討論。但我們認為更有意義的結果必須把條件限制成上述類型的 p-群才能獲得，而且對於預期中的數論應用，上述限制也是完全合理的。我們已經有一些初步結果顯示會有很豐富的結構理論，包括生成元，關係，以及群概型的結構。

14305618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305618.value: The aim of this project is to study elevation changes in permafrost areas by using global navigation satellite system (GNSS) reflectometry. In areas underlain by permafrost, the ground surface undergoes vertical movements caused by seasonal freeze and thaw processes and secularly (decades or longer) due to the degradation and possibly aggradation of permafrost. Such elevation changes affect ecosystems, hydrologic and landscape processes, infrastructure stability, and living conditions in cold regions. However, elevation changes in vast permafrost areas are poorly resolved, either from a limited number of in situ campaign measurements or from remote sensing datasets. More than 200 GNSS sites have been continuously operating in the Northern Hemisphere permafrost areas for several years up to two decades. The reflected GNSS signals recorded by these sites have great potential for uncovering the near-surface dynamics of the underlying permafrost. Therefore, we propose the GNSS-RECIPE project that innovatively uses GNSS Reflectometry to study elevation changes in permafrost areas. We will conduct a systematic and comprehensive assessment of the quality of reflected GNSS signals from these permafrost-region sites. We will retrieve time series of daily elevation changes and estimate their uncertainties at the sites that we will identify as suitable for studying permafrost. We will use this unique dataset to quantitatively model and investigate the temporal variability of elevation changes at seasonal, inter-annual, and decadal timescales. We will further examine whether regional factors, including climatic conditions, permafrost zonation, and ground ice conditions, can explain the spatial variability of our retrieved elevation changes at different sites. GNSS-RECIPE will exploit the full potential of the existing geodetic infrastructure and extend the use of long-term, widely distributed GNSS data for permafrost studies. This study will be complementary to the on-going permafrost monitoring efforts by providing new observables, namely, the time series of elevation changes, that will also fill in the spatial and temporal gaps of permafrost observations. Our measurements will provide key validation/calibration datasets and baseline information for historical, current, and future remote sensing measurements from air and space. GNSS-RECIPE項目旨在利用GNSS反射測量技術（GNSS Reflectometry，GNSS-R）獲取多年凍土區域的地表高程變化，進而探求凍土的變化機理。 在多年凍土區域，由於活動層的季節性融化或凍結以及多年凍土的退化或擴張，地面出現下沉或隆起現象。這樣的地表形變對寒區的生態系統，水文及地形地貌的演化，基礎設施的穩固以及人們的生產生活造成影響。但是，不論是基於實地測量數據，還是衛星遙感數據，目前大部分多年凍土區域的地表形變仍沒有經過測量及評估。 目前，超過200個GNSS連續運行觀測站廣泛分佈於北半球多年凍土區域。其中，某些GNSS站已經運行了將近20年。利用GNSS-R獲取長期、連續、高時間分辨率的地表高程變化有助於研究多年凍土的動態變化。 GNSS-RECIPE項目將對現有的位於多年凍土區域的GNSS站進行全面系統的評估，找出適合於應用GNSS-R的GNSS站點。然後，獲取這些站點處的地表高程變化，並對它們進行季節性、年際以及年代際等時序分析。另外，通過分析區域影響因子，包括氣候、多年凍土的分佈類型和地下冰的情況等，解釋不同站點處地表形變的空間差異，探究多年凍土的變化機理。 GNSS-RECIPE項目將充分利用現有的且分佈廣泛的GNSS連續運行觀測站，獲取長期、連續、高時間分辨率的地表形變測量值，對現有的多年凍土觀測值在時間和空間上進行補充，也為多年凍土的觀測研究提供新的角度。另外，此地表形變測量值可以為遙感數據提供基本信息，並對其進行驗證及校正。

14305618.label: Realisation of objectives
14305618.value: I have completed all the proposed research tasks and realized all the objectives. "Objective 1: To assess which terrestrial continuous GNSS sites can provide reflected signals that are suitable for measuring the elevation changes in permafrost areas in the Northern Hemisphere." We have conducted a thorough assessment to screen all open-access GNSS data provided through seven major GNSS networks: the International GNSS Service (IGS), the Plate Boundary Observatory (PBO), the Canadian Active Control System (CACS), the Portable Observatories for Lithospheric Analysis and Research Investigating Seismicity (POLARIS), the Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Network (CHAIN), the EUREF Permanent GNSS Network (EPN), and the Greenland Network (GNET). We have identified 23 sites suitable for measuring elevation changes using GNSS interferometric reflectometry. At each site, we also have estimated GNSS reflector heights, from which surface elevation changes on snow-free days and snow depth otherwise have been obtained. "Objective 2: To improve GNSS-Reflectometry retrieval algorithms to obtain time series of daily elevation changes and their uncertainties at selected high-quality sites." We have improved the commonly-used GNSS-IR algorithm for estimating surface soil moisture in permafrost areas, by introducing modeled surface elevation changes to mitigate the biases introduced by the seasonal surface vertical deformation. We have validated our method by using the GNSS signal-to-noise-ratio data and in situ observations at a permafrost site in the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and showed that our new algorithm had achieved higher accuracies in both elevation and soil moisture estimates than conventional methods. We have also proposed a new framework to integrate the GNSS-IR estimates of three key variables, i.e., surface elevation changes, soil moisture, and snow depth, at a single site.
