14305618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305618.value: The project has produced three journal papers on GNSS-IR studies of frozen ground in the Arctic and Tibet, three associated datasets, one Ph.D. dissertation, and a few conference papers. Please refer to Part C for detailed citation information and the full papers. Below I summarize our major findings as reported in the three GNSS-IR papers. Zhang and Liu (2021) conducted the first comprehensive data mining study in which we screened seven major open-data GNSS networks to identify what sites are suitable for using GNSS-IR for permafrost studies. From the 186 continuously operating sites located in the Arctic permafrost areas, we identified 23 usable ones, the majority of which are located in northern Canada and Alaska. We also obtained their reflector heights by GNSS-IR, which can be converted into surface elevation changes in snow-free seasons, otherwise snow depth. Together, the sites identified in this study help to fill some spatial gaps in the existing permafrost monitoring programs and provide complementary measurements to active layer thickness and permafrost temperature. In a detailed study focusing on the Canadian Arctic, Zhang et al. (The Cryosphere, 2020) used GNSS-IR to retrieve vertical surface movement at Alert, Resolute Bay, Repulse Bay, Baker Lake, and Iqaluit to investigate their multi-year linear trends. We revealed that the ground surface underwent subsidence at these sites, except Repulse Bay; and the subsidence trends were possibly caused by near-surface permafrost degradation induced by warming air temperatures. This study highlights that the multiple GNSS stations in northern Canada offer multi-year, continuous, and daily surface deformation, and provide new insights into frozen-ground dynamics at seasonal, inter-annual, and decadal time scales and across a broad region. Zhang et al. (The Cryosphere, 2021) elucidated that the commonly-used GNSS-IR algorithm for estimating soil moisture content cannot be directly used in permafrost areas because it does not consider the bias introduced by the seasonal surface elevation changes due to active layer thawing. We proposed a solution by introducing modeled surface elevation changes. We validated our method by using the GNSS signal-to-noise-ratio data and in situ observations at a permafrost site in the northeastern Tibet Plateau and achieved moderate improvement in the retrieved soil moisture. We also introduced a new framework (dubbed three-in-one) to integrate the GNSS-IR estimates of surface elevation changes, soil moisture, and snow depth at one site. This study is also the first to use GNSS-IR to estimate environmental variables on the Tibet Plateau.

14305618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305618.value: 1. Automated data mining. The identified suitable and unsuitable sites and their features, including topography, land cover, and vegetation, can be utilized to build a machine-learning-based model, to assess the suitability of a site for GNSS-IR applications automatically. 2. Synergy between GNSS-IR and InSAR. Since both methods have been used to study frozen ground, a synergy can combine their strengths and compensate for the limitations. For instance, daily and continuous GNSS-IR measurements help to tie InSAR measurements with gaps in time and between missions. The GNSS sites can provide reference points for InSAR measurements. Zhang and Liu (IGARSS 2021) laid out the general principles, yet detailed implementation plans remain to be developed. 3. Establishing supersites for permafrost monitoring. As indicated by our studies, vegetation, soil type, soil moisture, and ground ice content moderate the impact of air temperature on frozen ground, consequently affecting its thermal regime. To gain comprehensive and detailed quantifications and understandings of all these inter-played properties and processes, a few ‘supersites’ with various sensors installed from above and below ground need to be established, warranting collaborations under the International Association of Permafrost and the International Association of Geodesy.

14305618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305618.value: Permafrost on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and in the Arctic is thawing rapidly as the climate is warming. The ground surface in a permafrost region is subject to uplift/subsidence, due to seasonal freezing/thawing of the near-surface layer called the active layer. This project innovated the use of reflected Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals recorded by ground-based receivers located in cold regions for studying permafrost. Using improved interferometric reflectometry (IR) algorithms, we obtained time series of three key variables: elevation changes, soil moisture, and snow depth. We found trends of subsidence in several Arctic sites, likely due to thawing of the underground permafrost. Taken together, the multi-year, continuous, and daily GNSS-IR measurements as generated from this work at 23 sites constitute a new set of observations that complement the existing in situ measurements of as active layer thickness and ground temperature, fill in the spatial and temporal gaps in the existing permafrost monitoring networks, and help to quantify frozen ground dynamics in a warming climate.

14305918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305918.value: Carboranes, a class of three-dimensional relatives of benzene, have proven as very useful functional blocks in boron neutron capture therapy agents, in supramolecular design/materials, and in coordination/organometallic chemistry. Thus, the functionalization of carboranes has drawn growing interests. Over the decades, the research activity in this area has focused on cage carbon functionalization due to facile deprotonation of the weakly acidic cage C-H proton. In sharp contrast, selective cage B-H functionalization among chemically very similar ten B-H vertices is very challenging. The known methods for cage B-H functionalization are generally based on electrophilic substitution of cage B-H bonds by strong electrophiles. It is well established that strong nucleophiles such as alkoxides and fluoride anion lead to the deboration reaction of carboranes, giving nido-carborane anions. Very recently, by introducing electron-withdrawing groups to the cage carbon atoms to decrease the electron density of cage B-H vertices, we have achieved, for the first time, direct regioselective nucleophilic cage B-H substitution reaction of o-carboranes by Grignard reagents (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2017, 56, 8642-8646). This represents a brand new way to functionalize o-carboranes via a transition-metal-free process. In this proposal, we plan to investigate systematically such nucleophilic substitution reactions, aiming at the development of new methodologies for selective cage BH functionalization of carboranes via direct nucleophilic cage BH substitution process. Studies of the reaction mechanism are also an important part of this proposal. It is anticipated that this research will result in a new toolbox for the preparation of a large class of cage B-substituted carborane derivatives and expand our fundamental understanding of the nature of o-carboranes. It will also be fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 碳硼烷，作為苯環的三維近似物，是十分有用的功能塊，被廣泛應用於硼中子捕獲治療劑，超分子設計/材料，以及配位化學/金屬有機化學。因此，碳硼烷的官能團化越发引人关注。由於碳硼烷中碳氫的微弱酸性，易於实现去質子化，在過去的十年之中，該領域的研究主要集中於碳硼烷笼碳的官能團化。與此相反，對碳硼烷中具有相似化學性質的十個硼氫鍵進行選擇性活化，則極具挑戰性。已知的硼氫活化方法大致基於強親電試劑對於硼氫的親電取代。強親核試劑，如烷氧基負離子與氟負離子往往會引起碳硼烷的脫硼反應，导致巢式碳硼烷的形成。近來，通過在碳硼烷的碳上安裝拉電子基團從而降低碳硼烷的電荷密度，利用格氏試劑，我們首次完成了碳硼烷的選擇性親核取代 (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2017, 56, 8642-8646)。這是一個全新的無過度金屬參與的碳硼烷官能團化的方法。在這個提案中，我們將系統地研究該親核反應，發展通過親核取代反應過程實現碳硼烷選擇性硼氫官能團化的新方法學。該提案中，反應機理的研究也是十分重要的一部分。我們希望該研究可以為制备硼上多种取代的碳硼烷衍生物構築工具箱，同時拓寬我們對於碳硼烷的基本認識。此外，我們也期待有其它的新發現。

14305918.label: Realisation of objectives
14305918.value: Carboranes are finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed towards the area of carborane functionalization. In this project, we have developed new methodologies for the selective mono- or multi-functionalization of o-carboranes via nucleophilic substitution reaction or transition metal catalysis strategies. It has been well documented that hard nucleophiles such as O-, N- and F- attack the most electron-deficient B(3)-H that is bonded to both cage carbon atoms. Subsequently, the attack of a second equivalent of the nucleophile occurs on the same boron atom to remove one BH vertex from o-carborane framework, resulting in the formation of the dicarbollide ion [nido-C2B9H112−]. On the other hand, carbenes, soft carbon nucleophiles, are also able to attack the B(3)-H vertex to generate 1 : 2 or 1 : 1 nido-carborane–carbene adducts, depending on the steric demand of carbenes. It is rational to propose that nucleophilic cage B-H substitution could be achieved if the departure of H− from the cage boron could be promoted by a hydride abstractor after the first attack of a proper nucleophile, and the second attack of the nucleophile could be efficiently blocked. However, there are no reactions between 1,2-Me2-o-carboranes and RMgX (or RLi), suggesting that it is essential to lower the electron density of o-carboranes in order to promote cage B-H nucleophilic substitution reaction. Accordingly, we proposed the following strategy for realizing selective cage B-H nucleophilic substitution reactions: (1) using less bulky electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., alkynyls) on the cage carbons for selective B(3,6)-H nucleophilic substitution; (2) using electron-withdrawing substituents with an appropriate size (e.g., aryls) on both cage carbons for B(4,5,7,11)-H nucleophilic substitution; and (3) employing very sterically hindered groups (e.g., silyls) on both cage carbons to block B(3,4,5,6,7,11)-H vertices for the remote B(9,12)-H nucleophilic substitution. Due to the difference in electronegativity of carbon and boron elements, the electron density of ten BH vertices of o-carborane follows the order B(9,12)-H > B(8,10)-H > B(4,5,7,11)-H > B(3,6)-H. Cage B(3,6)-H, bonded to both cage carbons, are the most electron-deficient. According to our proposed strategy, less bulky electron-withdrawing substituents on the cage carbons are required to enhance the electron deficiency of B(3,6)-H vertices, promoting nucleophilic reactions. With this in mind, 1-methyl-2-phenylethynyl-o-carborane was prepared as a model substrate, since alkynyl group is electron-withdrawing yet less sterically demanding. Reaction of such substrate with 2.1 equiv of alkyl Grignard reagents in toluene at room temperature for 18 h generated the B(3,6)-dialkylated carborane derivatives in high yields. Both primary and secondary alkyl Grignard reagents served as competent coupling partners. Such nucleophilic substitution provides a convenient and efficient complementary protocol for selective functionalization of o-carboranes. Different from the proximal B(3,6)-H and B(4,5,7,11)-H vertices, the distal B(8,9,10,12)-H ones are much more electron-rich. Furthermore, the electronic properties of cage carbon substituents have little impact on these vertices in such σ system of o-carborane. These analyses indicate that sterically hindered functional groups should be installed onto cage carbons to block the adjacent B(3,4,5,6,7,11)H vertices, so as to realize the nucleophilic substitution at distal position. In this regard, two DMPS (DMPS = dimethylphenylsilyl) groups were introduced to cage carbons of o-carborane. Treatment of 1,2-(DMPS)2-o-carborane with 1.3 equiv of alkyl Grignard reagents in diethyl ether at 40 oC for 24 h, followed by desilylation with K2CO3 in acetone, afforded the B(9)-alkylated o-carboranes in moderate to good yields. Primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl Grignard reagents were all compatible. Interestingly, aryl Grignard reagents also worked well, though decreased isolated yields were obtained for B(9)-arylated o-carboranes, due probably to the relatively weak nucleophilicity of aryl Grignard reagents. Control experiments confirmed the formation of MgHCl. DFT calculations showed (1) the proximal B(3,4,5,6,7,11)-H vertices were sterically protected by two bulky DMPS groups at cage carbons; and (2) the calculated charge of B(9)-H (ca. -0.06) was slightly less negative than that of B(8)-H (ca. -0.08), suggesting the preference of B(9)-H to be attacked by nucleophiles. Having achieved the selective construction of cage B-C bond(s) via nucleophilic substitution using Grignard reagents, we wondered if amido-Grignard reagents could undergo nucleophilic aromatic cage BH substitution reaction to realize transition-metal-free B-H amination of o-carboranes. Accordingly, a pyridine-enabled transition metal-free regioselective nucleophilic cage B(4)−H amination of 1,2-diaryl-o-carboranes with magnesium bisamides has been developed for facile synthesis of 4-NR1R2-1,2-diaryl-o-carboranes in moderate to high yields. Unprecedentedly, these o-carboranes can undergo cage isomerization at as low as 100 oC in the presence of bispyridine and magnesium complex to give 2-NR1R2-1,7-diaryl-m-carboranes, offering a new route for the synthesis of B(2)-aminated m-carboranes in high yields. A reaction mechanism for nucleophilic cage BH amination has been proposed on the basis of DFT calculations. It is a stepwise B-N formation/B-H cleavage process, in which Mg-H formation/cage closure is the rate-determining step. This work not only offers a transition metal-free method for direct, efficient, and regioselective B-H amination of o-carboranes, but also opens a new avenue for developing nucleophilic cage BH functionalization and synthesizing functionalized m-carboranes. During the course of the above studies, we discovered an unprecedented cascade cyclization of 1-arylethynyl-2-alkyl-o-carboranes initiated by nucleophilic cage BH substitution using Grignard reagents for highly efficient synthesis of various carborane-fused cyclopentanes. On the basis of D-labelling and control experiments, a HMgBr-initiated reaction mechanism is proposed, in which the magnesium-mediated intramolecular sp3 C−H activation serves as a key step. These results not only shed some light on magnesium-promoted C−H activation and functionalization, but also offer references for the design of cascade reactions involving o-carboranes. In addition, we also extended the research scope to develop the methods for transition metal catalyzed selective cage BH functionalization, including B(8)-arylation, B(4)-amination, B(4)-oxygenation, and B(4)-sulfenylation. In summary, we have developed several new methods on the basis of nucleophilic reaction or transition metal catalysis strategies for the preparation of a wide range of functionalized carborane molecules, which might find valuable applications in many realms. The associated reaction mechanisms have also been investigated via the combination of control experiments and DFT calculations. The results offer a better fundamental understanding of nucleophilic substitution reaction in o-carboranes, which in turn would shed light on how to control the selectivity for the effective synthesis of target products. This project has been very successfully carried out and all objectives have been achieved.

14305918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305918.value: (1) To develop selective cage B-H functionalization of carboranes via direct nucleophilic substitution reactions (Pub. #1, #3, #11 and #19) A new protocol for regioselective nucleophilic cage B-H substitution in o-carboranes has been proposed and validated: (1) for B(3,6)-H nucleophilic substitution, less bulky electron-withdrawing substituents on cage carbons is necessary, (2) for B(4,5,7,11)-H nucleophilic substitution, an appropriate size of electron-withdrawing substituents (such as aryls) on both cage carbons are required, and (3) for B(9,12)-H nucleophilic substitution, very sterically hindered groups (such as silyls) on both cage carbons are needed to block B(3,4,5,6,7,11)-H vertices. This transition-metal-free strategy is complementary to those of transition metal-catalyzed regioselective functionalization of o-carboranes, and electrophilic substitution reactions, enabling the facile synthesis of cage B-alkylated/arylated/aminated carboranes in a regioselective and controlled manner. This work opens a new window to the controlled functionalization of boron clusters. (2) To study and understand the reaction mechanisms (Pub. #3 and #19) On the basis of control experiments and DFT calculations, a reaction mechanism for nucleophilic cage BH substitution reaction has been proposed. It is a stepwise B-C/N formation/B-H cleavage process, in which Mg-H formation/cage closure is the rate-determining step. This mechanism can explain the role of electron-withdrawing groups, nucleophiles, [Mg]2+ and steric effects in the reactions. (3) To develop methods for transition metal catalyzed selective functionalization of o-carboranes (Pub. #2, #5-10, #12, and #14-#17) Under the assistance of an acylamino directing group at cage B(3), a series of B(8)-arylated, B(4,7,8)-triarylated and B(4,7,8)-trifluorinated o-carborane derivatives were conveniently prepared via “cage-walking” of Pd catalyst from B(4) to B(7) and B(8) vertices for the regioselective B(4,7,8)-H activation and functionalization. A carboxy group assisted Ir-catalyzed cascade dehydrogenative cross-coupling of carboranyl carboxylic acid with benzamide was developed, resulting in the facile synthesis of previously inaccessible carborano-isoquinolinone derivatives in a simple one-pot process, in which two cage B-H, one aryl C-H and one N-H bonds were sequentially activated to construct efficiently new B-C and B-N bonds, respectively, via “cage-walking” of Ir catalyst. A rhodium-catalyzed one-pot trifunctionalization of o-carboranes with three different substituents was achieved through a carboxy group directed sequential B(5)-alkenylation, B(4)-alkyne annulation and B(3)-acyloxylation via “cage-walking” of Rh catalyst, leading to the synthesis of a new class of B(3,4,5) trisubstituted o-carborane derivatives. Finally, we developed a traceless bidentate directing group guided copper catalyzed direct cage B(4,5)−H disulfenylation of o-carboranes via migration of Cu catalyst, leading to a series of B(4,5)−disulfenylated o-carborane derivatives in high yields with excellent regioselectivity. In summary, this original work has resulted in 19 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x 4), Angew. Che. Int. Ed. (x 2), Acc. Chem. Res. (x 1), Nat. Commun. (x 1), Chem. Sci. (x 1), J. Org. Chem. (x 1), Chem. Commun. (x 2), Dalton Trans. (x 1), Chin. J. Chem. (x 1), Chem. Soc. Rev. (x 2), Chem. Asian J. (x 1), Chin. Chem. Lett. (x 1) and Bull. Chem. Soc. Jpn. (x 1). PI was invited to give three keynote and one invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students have been trained, of which two have been graduated.

14305918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305918.value: Regioselective cage BH functionalization has been achieved. We wonder if enantioselective version of these reactions would be possible with the assistance of chiral ligands. If so, chiral-at-cage carborane derivatives could be prepared via asymmetrical reactions. We will explore such asymmetrical synthesis in the future.

14305918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305918.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, can be viewed as three-dimensional analogues of benzene. They are finding many applications in coordination/ organometallic chemistry as versatile ligands, in medicine as boron neutron capture therapy agents and in supramolecular design/nanomaterials as useful building blocks. All this has recently drawn considerable attention to carborane chemistry. However, the exceptional thermal and chemical stable 3D structures of carboranes make their derivatization difficult, limiting their application scope. The development of an efficient and general technique to functionalize carboranes will be one of the main issues in this field. In this project, we have developed nucleophilic cage BH substitution reaction and transition metal catalysis strategies for the functionalization of carboranes, leading to the invention of several methods for the efficient synthesis of a large class of cage B-functionalized o-carboranes under mild conditions with high yields. These functionalized o-carboranes may find applications in materials and medicine.

14306218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306218.value: The aim of this proposal is to find and study a population of hidden compact objects and other structures that cause significant distortion of spacetime through its effects on gravitational waves. I propose a programme of studies to model the effects of gravitational lenses and use them to find and interpret lensed gravitational-wave signals. Recent detections of gravitational waves by the LIGO detectors herald a new era where invisible black holes and neutron stars can be discovered throughout the Universe. Similar to electromagnetic waves, gravitational waves can be distorted by massive objects between the observer and the source, i.e. gravitational lensing. Neglecting the effects of lensing can lead to missing gravitational-wave events or a biased measurement of the individual source and the population of sources. In particular, in the geometrical-optics limits, lensing may give rise to repeated signals from the same source that are (de-)magnified. This effect may lead to a so-called lensing bias, i.e. preference to seeing signals that are gravitationally lensed. In the wave-optics limit, effects like diffraction, interference and dispersion may deform the signal morphology to an extent that they cannot be matched with our standard templates. However, if these challenges are successfully addressed then, the effects of gravitational lensing have the ability to uncover a population of objects or structures that are intrinsically faint and can otherwise not be found. Moreover, they provide us with a way to study the large-scale structure of the Universe or even probe fundamental aspects of gravity. I propose to systematically study the effects of lensing on the detection and interpretation of gravitational-wave signals. Moreover, I will extend existing LIGO infrastructure to account for the effects of lensing. Any hints of lensing will then be followed up with detailed lens modelling and Monte Carlo simulations to provide the best possible insight into the nature of the lens. These studies allow Hong Kong scientists to participate at the forefront of astrophysics and astronomy and pave the way for a strong and thriving gravitational-physics community. This proposal also has the ability to contribute to the local high-tech sector by developing cutting-edge statistics and big-data techniques, and by training students for creative and abstract problem solving. 該研究計劃的目的是找到並研究一群隱藏的緊湊物體和其他結構，這些物體對時空有顯著扭曲導致對重力波的影響。我提出了一個研究方案來模擬重力透鏡的效應，並用它來發現和解釋通過重力透鏡後之重力波信號。 最近LIGO探測器對重力波的探測預示著一個新的時代，在整個宇宙中可以發現隱形黑洞和中子星。類似於電磁波，重力波可以被觀察者和源之間的大質量物體（即重力透鏡）扭曲。忽視透鏡效應可能導致缺失重力波事件或對個體源和源群進行偏差測量。特別地，在近似幾何光學的情況下，透鏡可以放大（或縮小）來自相同光源的信號。這種效應可能導致所謂的透鏡偏差，即我們看到的為被重力透鏡影響過的信號。在波動光學極限中，衍射，干涉和色散等效應可能會使信號形態變形到不能與我們的標準波型匹配。 然而，如果成功地解決了這些難題，那麼重力透鏡的效果就能夠揭示本質上微弱且無法找到的物體或結構。此外，它們為我們提供了一種研究宇宙大規模結構的方法，甚至可以探索重力的基本方面。 我提出去系統地研究透鏡效應對重力波信號的檢測和解釋的影響。此外，我將擴展現有的LIGO基礎研究工具，以解決重力透鏡的影響。然後，將通過建立詳細的重力透鏡模型和進行蒙特卡羅模擬來提出重力透鏡的性質。 這些研究使香港科學家能夠參與天體物理學和天文學的最前沿的研究，為強大而繁榮的重力物理學界鋪平了道路。該提案還有能力通過開發尖端的統計數據和大數據技術，以及培訓學生進行創造性和抽象的問題解決，為當地高科技領域做出貢獻。

14306218.label: Realisation of objectives
14306218.value: NB: Citations from the (numbered) research output (Part C) are denoted with curly brackets {}, whereas external citations are denoted with square brackets [] and can be found at the end of the text. The overall achievement of the objectives has been very successful, leading to 13 published articles, X presentations at international conferences or seminars and 5 postgraduate theses. It should be further noted that the PI is an active member of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, which is a scientific collaboration of international physics institutes and research groups dedicated to the search for gravitational waves using the United States-based LIGO detectors. As stated in the proposal, the work of this project is therefore also in part for publications of the collaborations. These publications have not been included in the research output, because it is impossible to acknowledge individual project codes in an author list with more than 2000 authors. However, in the assessment of the realisation of the research objectives, work done for the collaboration is taken into account. 1. Refs. {2, 6, 7, 10, 12} all study the effects of lensing on gravitational-wave observables. These include the effects of microlensing {2, 6, 7}, alternative theories of gravity {10} and populations of colliding black holes {12}. While the entire landscape of gravitational-wave lensing effects is too vast for a single institute to study, we have made major contributions to the most interesting effects that we can expect to see. 2. Ref. {6} describe a software package that is developed under the auspices of this proposal to calculate gravitational waveforms from complex fields of lenses. This software is used to calculate lensing signatures and serves as input for objective 3. Moreover, simplified models have been constructed as part of Ref. {11}, which are also used in collaboration-wide papers [1]. 3. Refs. {3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 13} all describe the development of algorithms to find or interpret lensed gravitational waves. These range from search algorithms to identify strong or microlensing {3, 5, 8, 13} using either traditional Bayesian or machine-learning methods, to studies improving our understanding of what physics can be extracted from lensed gravitational waves {4, 9, 11}. 4. This proposal yields 6 postgraduate theses either solely or largely devoted to the topic of this proposal. Moreover, around 10 research projects involving undergraduate students were conducted on the theme of this proposal. [1] R. Abbott et al. ApJ 923 14 (2021)

14306218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306218.value: The major finding and research outcomes can be categorised as follows: STUDIES OF EFFECTS OF GRAVITATIONAL-WAVE LENSING - We find that stellar mass microlenses, permeating the lens plane, and near critical curves, can introduce interference distortions in strongly lensed gravitational waves. In particular, we show when these diffraction effects are important when we consider GWs in the LIGO frequency band lensed by objects. - We find that the waveform morphology of lensed gravitational waves depends may yield sensitive information about the nature of the propagation nature of gravitational waves. MODELS FOR GRAVITATIONAL-WAVE LENSING - We developed an open-source code for the fast and accurate calculation of gravitational waves lensed by a complex configuration of lenses. IDENTIFICATION OR INTERPRETATION OF LENSED GRAVITATIONAL WAVES - Strongly lensed signals can enhance the inference of the microlensing effects. - Gravitational-wave sources can be accurately localised from strongly lensed events. - The type of strong lensing can be directly inferred from a gravitational-wave measurement. SEARCHES FOR GRAVITATIONAL-WAVE LENSING (IN REAL DATA) - We have developed fast and accurate algorithms to identify lensed gravitational-wave signals through traditional matched filtering and machine learning. - No gravitational-wave lensing effects have been observed in existing gravitational-wave data

14306218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306218.value: The field of gravitational-wave lensing is still in its early stages, but major progress has been made by our group (through this proposal) specifically. Further development is ongoing and focuses on the areas of waveforms from complex lensing configurations, and identification of repeated lensed signals from a vast number of candidates and through multiple messengers.

14306218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306218.value: Gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of spacetime, are predicted by Einstein's theory of General Relativity. These waves encode accurate information about the movement of massive celestial objects but also any spacetime distortion due to massive objects in between the source and the observer. This project mapped out potential distortions from massive objects and devised algorithms to recognise the occurence of these distortions in gravitational-wave data.

14306418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306418.value: Earthquakes have caused significant damage and casualty in human history and accordingly there is a critical need to advance our understanding of earthquake physics. Frictional properties of seismogenic faults and stress fields before and after earthquakes, play critical roles in earthquake generation, rupture propagation and termination, as well as slip distribution and ground shaking. Yet frictional parameters are mostly obtained either from laboratory measurements or indirect estimates from seismic and geodetic recordings. Constraining frictional properties on seismogenic faults from seismological methods is challenging, but is of critical significance to advance our understanding of earthquake physics and thus of better seismic hazard preparation and mitigation. We propose to develop a framework to infer frictional parameters on faults that are ruptured in large earthquakes by integrating both kinematic and dynamic source descriptions for earthquakes, as well as constraint on dynamic friction from laboratory measurements. We will estimate the frictional parameters not only using near-field observations, but also from far-field data, as demonstrated in our studies of the 2015 Nepal Mw7.8 earthquake. To utilize the far-field data, we will develop a method to compute far-field synthetic seismogram from the dynamic rupture models and then investigate how far-field data may resolve dynamic source parameters of large earthquakes with constraints from the back-projection method. Here we will not only demonstrate how we may for the first time robustly determine frictional parameters on seismogenic faults using near-field data, but will also develop a new method to directly link spontaneous rupture simulations with far-field seismic waveform records. Furthermore, the propose work will integrate seismological methods (e.g. finite fault inversion and back-projection) with dynamic rupture simulation, as well as rock-sliding experiments in the laboratory. The anticipated results of in-situ frictional properties can be used for future ground motion prediction based on dynamic rupture simulations, which is crucial for seismic hazard assessment. One graduate student at CUHK will be supported and trained in different perspectives during the project, including spontaneous rupture simulation and seismic data analysis. All research from this project will be presented at professional meetings, and the work will be integrated into the teaching curriculum of H. Yang and S. Wei. 人類歷史上曾遭受多次地震災害，防震減災需要深入認識地震物理。發震斷層上震前、震后的應力狀態和同震摩擦性質不僅對破裂開始、傳播和終止具有關鍵影響，也是影響斷層同震滑移和地表運動的關鍵因素。目前，斷層上的摩擦性質數據主要來自於實驗室岩石摩擦實驗，或者基於地震學和大地測量學數據的間接測量。直接基於地震學和大地測量學方法約束斷層摩擦參數極具挑戰，但這對於加深震源物理的認識和防震减灾工作有重大意义。 這裡我們提出一個新的研究方法：結合運動學和動力學震源模型，並利用實驗室摩擦實驗數據的約束，研究斷層上的同震摩擦性質。如在2015年尼泊爾7.8級地震的研究中所阐述，除了近場數據，遠場數據也會被用來約束摩擦參數。為了利用遠場數據，我們將建立新方法，合成動力學破裂模型的理論遠場響應，并研究如何在基於反投影方法的原理下，利用遠場響應约束震源動力學破裂參數。 我們不僅將證明利用近場數據直接約束破裂斷層同震摩擦參數的可行性，並且會建立聯繫遠場數據和震源動力學破裂模型參數的方法。本項目將震源運動學的研究方法 （有限斷層反演和反投影），與動力學地震破裂模擬和岩石摩擦實驗相結合。我們期待能將得到的斷層摩擦性質應用到未來地震動力學破裂情景模擬中，對區域地表破壞程度進行預估，這對於地震危险性评估意義重大。 一位香港中文大學的研究生將會參與到這個項目中，根據項目要求接受不同方面的研究訓練，包括動力學破裂模擬和地震學數據處理技術。項目得到的結果將會在專業會議上展示，項目進行的工作將會整合到楊宏峰教授和韋生吉教授的教學课程中。

14306418.label: Realisation of objectives
14306418.value: We have conducted a variety of investigations targeting at the above objectives. Two PhD students are trained to conduct numerical modeling of earthquake rupture propagations, who had both graduated. Two postdoc fellows are involved in this project. We have first developed a framework to robustly constrain the coseismic frictional properties with kinematic source models and near-field observations by conducting spontaneous dynamic rupture simulations. To do so, we first estimate static stress drops from kinematic slip distributions, which then serve as initial conditions on stress patterns and frictional properties on faults. A linear slip-weakening law is adopted as the constitutive law on faults. After conducting spontaneous rupture simulations with frictional parameters varying in wide ranges, we compare synthetic ground motions with coseismic near-field observations to constrain the parameters. We apply this approach on the 2015 Nepal Mw 7.8 earthquake (Weng and Yang, 2018, J. Geophys. Res.) and the 2012 Nicoya Mw 7.6 earthquake (Yao and Yang, 2020, Geophys. Res. Lett.; Yao and Yang, 2018, CGU, DEEP, AGU conference presentations; Yao and Yang, 2019, NMEM conference presentation; Yang and Yao, 2019, EGU conference presentations). The two earthquakes are chosen by considering their extensive near-field observations, which offer good resolutions on the rupture process. By developing a new method to remove parameter trade-off, for the first time, we robustly determine the frictional properties on seismogenic faults. In addition, we infer the strength on the Nicoya megathrust prior to the Mw 7.6 earthquake to be extremely low (< 10 MPa in average) (Yao and Yang, 2020, Geophys. Res. Lett.). Such low strength on the seismogenic fault is critical in understanding recurrence intervals for future large earthquakes. These results have addressed the objective 1. We have also investigated the effects of fault zone structures on the ground motions and the consequent impacts on estimating frictional parameters (Chen and Yang, 2019, AGU conference presentation; Chen and Yang, 2020, Geophys. J. Int.). The critical weakening distance (D_c), a key parameter in slip-weakening friction law, has been proposed to be approximated to the twice of fault-parallel displacement (D_c'') at the time of the maximum slip rate on off-fault stations for strike-slip faults. We conduct 3-D dynamic rupture simulations considering different seismogenic widths and a shallow low velocity zone (LVZ). Then we find that near-fault ground motions are strongly affected by the seismogenic width and the LVZ structure, causing large uncertainties in D_c estimation. The estimated D_c'' increases with the seismogenic width. Furthermore, we apply this approach on the 2014 Mw 6.2 Ludian earthquake and inferred D_c'' from the acceleration data (Chen et al., 2021, Seismo. Res. Lett.). Based on our dynamic rupture models, we’ve also derived far-field ground motions by treating the dynamic models as a group of point sources, which are then convolved with Green’s functions that are computed by the frequency-wavenumber method from a 1D Earth model. Such approach has been conducted jointly with our collaborator at NTU. We also apply the back projection technique on recent large earthquakes to resolve their rupture kinematics. For example, the 2021 Mw 8.1 Kermadec earthquake showed different frequency-dependent radiation features than previous megathrust earthquakes, with high-frequency energy radiated from up-dip region of the megathrust. With well-constrained frequency radiation pattern, we then infer that such feature was originated from the changes in frictional property along the megathrust. These results have addressed the objectives 2 and 3. We have extended a bit from the original objectives to derive rupture scenarios for future earthquakes from interseismic locking models (Yang et al., 2019, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.; Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.; Yao and Yang., 2022, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.), using our determined frictional properties. We find that the earthquake magnitudes and shallow slip distribution are dependent on hypocentral locations, which are unfortunately not known for future earthquakes. Such results hold significant implications on seismic hazard assessment from interseismic locking models, which requires a good understanding of frictional properties on seismogenic faults. These results have also addressed the objective 3.

14306418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306418.value: One of the challenges in earthquake seismology is to determine frictional parameters and stress state on seismogenic faults. We developed a new method to remove trade-off between frictional parameters (Weng and Yang, 2018, J. Geophys. Res.) and thus can robustly determine frictional properties on faults. With constraints of near-field data, we find an extremely low strength on the Nicoya megathrust (Yao and Yang, 2020, Geophys. Res. Lett.), which was resulted from overpressured fluids. In addition, we find location-dependent magnitudes and rupture extents of earthquakes on faults with heterogeneous initial stress (Yang et al., 2019, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.; Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.; Yao and Yang., 2022, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.). The results of hypocentre-dependent earthquake magnitudes lead to a new perspective in physics-based earthquake hazard evaluation and shed lights on foreshock-mainshock relationships that have been in debate for a long time. Through our collaboration, the Co-I in this project has been motivated to submit a proposal entitled “New constraints on fault geometry and propagation of megathrust earthquakes”, which was funded by Ministry of Education in Singapore.

14306418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306418.value: Our findings from this project show that, even with well-determined frictional parameters on seismogenic faults, we may not be able to accurately predict future earthquake magnitudes unless we can identify future earthquake hypocenters. How to identify the potential nucleation region on a fault where future large earthquakes may occur becomes critical. In regions with good network coverage, we may construct high-resolution catalog and analyze the spatial-temporal evolution of seismicity, trying to determine the likelihood where future large earthquakes may nucleate.

14306418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306418.value: Earthquakes have caused significant damage and casualty in human history and accordingly there is a critical need to advance our understanding of earthquake physics. Frictional properties of seismogenic faults play critical roles in earthquake generation, rupture propagation and termination, as well as slip distribution and ground shaking. Yet constraining frictional properties on seismogenic faults from seismological methods is challenging. In this project, we have developed a new method to constrain frictional parameters by removing the trade-off between parameters. By doing so, we identify an extremely low strength on the Nicoya megathrust, which was attributed to overpressured fluids. Furthermore, using the well determined frictional parameters on seismogenic faults, we derive future earthquake scenarios with constraints from interseismic locking distribution. We find location-dependent magnitudes and rupture extents of earthquakes on faults with heterogeneous initial stress. The results of hypocentre-dependent earthquake magnitudes lead to a new perspective in physics-based earthquake hazard evaluation and shed lights on foreshock-mainshock relationships that have been in debate for a long time.

14306518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306518.value: This project aims to identify the origin of nucleation precursors, probe its structural evolutions, and explore its distinct roles in the formation of all three types of solids: crystal, quasicrystal, and glass. Crystallization is ubiquitous in condensed matter physics and materials science. However, its exact kinetics has been under intensive debate for more than a century. In the classical nucleation theory, the kinetics of crystallization proceeds as nucleation and growth of nuclei: small crystals, which have the same symmetry and density as the final solid, directly emerge from the liquid through spontaneous thermal fluctuation. In contrast, however, the Ostwald’s step rule (1897) and many recent studies suggest the appearance of various intermediate states [1-12]. To clarify this discrepancy, we experimentally revealed (Nature Physics 2014 [Xu1]) the existence of relatively-ordered special structures, which behave as nucleation precursors and out of which different intermediate states can emerge. However, a critical question is still open: what breaks the disordered liquid state and produces these precursors in the first place? This question touches on the extremely fundamental topic of how order can initially emerge from a disordered environment, and its answer will fill up the important knowledge gap of crystallization kinetics at the very beginning. Besides crystallization, moreover, it may even shed new light on the formation of quasicrystals, in which only orientational order develops; and the formation of glass where ordered structures never reach a significant amount throughout the entire system. To illustrate this fundamental question, it is ideal to measure the structural and dynamical evolutions of every single particle throughout the crystallization process, and extract essential physics from large statistics. This is the expertise we are particularly good at [Xu1, Xu2]. Using colloidal systems with single-particle resolution, we plan to visualize the kinetic evolutions of about 500,000 to 1,000,000 colloids. In particular, we will focus on the early-stage transformation from supercooled liquid to nucleation precursors and aim to solve the following three outstanding issues: (1) identify the origin of nucleation precursors, (2) probe such an origin’s structural and dynamical roles in initiating the crystallization process, and (3) explore its distinct behaviors in other solidification-initiation processes such as the formation of quasicrystal and glass. Our goal is to not only clarify the initial crystallization kinetics, but also illuminate the onset kinetics of all three types of solids: crystal, quasicrystal, and glass. 本項目主要目的是找到結晶前驅體的產生原因，探索它的結構和動力學演化，以及探討它在各種固體結構比如準晶和玻璃態結構中的作用。眾所周知，結晶是一個非常重要的物理過程，在凝聚態物理和材料學中有著廣泛的應用。但是結晶的具體動力學路徑仍然不夠清楚。在經典結晶理論描述下，這一過程分為兩步：成核以及生長。在初始的結晶過程中，與最後的固體態完全一樣的結構先凝結成晶核，然後進一步長大變成大塊的晶體。 這一描述卻與很多最近的實驗和模擬相違背：最近結果中經常在晶核產生前出現一些前驅體，並在結晶過程中出現很多中間態。在本研究計劃中，我們主要探索晶核的前驅體是怎麼出現的。這個問題非常的基本和重要，它可以幫我們了解在無序的液體態中，有序的結構最初是怎樣從中出現的。為了研究這一問題，我們計劃用50萬到100萬膠體顆粒組成實驗體系，用共聚焦顯微鏡對顆粒們進行單顆粒的跟踪，收集它們從液體態到固體態的動力學轉化過程。 通過對它們最早期的轉變行為的仔細研究，我們可以探索前驅體的產生機制和影響。我們將重點研究以下三個具體問題：（1）找出晶核前驅體的產生機制，（2）探討它們的結構與動力學演化過程，（3）探索它們對固體結構的影響。通過這一研究，我們希望能夠對晶體以及其他各種固體的產生有一個深入的了解。

14306518.label: Realisation of objectives
14306518.value: The two objectives are fully realized. 1. Based on our study, we have discovered two-step crystallization process of the charged-colloidal system at high super-cooling, which has very low diffusion. The two steps are: (1) the step-like advancement of the rough interface that disintegrates frustration, followed by (2) defect repairing inside the newly formed solid phase. The former is a diffusionless collective process, whereas the latter controls crystal quality. We further show that the intrinsic mechanical instability of a disordered glassy state subject to the crystal growth front allows for domino-like fast crystal growth even at ultra-low temperatures. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of fast crystal growth and may be useful for applications related to vitrification prevention and crystal-quality control. These results are published in the prestigeous journal of Nature Materials (Nature Materials, 20, 1431–1439, 2021). 2. Moreover, in another structure similar to crystal, the hyper-uniform packing system, which is uniform in density but without translational order, we discover a topological transition. This transition enables a powerful tuning in system elasticity. Within one system, we achieve solid-like affine response, liquid-like non-affine response and a continuous tunability in between. Moreover, the system also exhibits a broadly tunable Poisson’s ratio from positive to negative values, which is of practical interest for energy absorption and for fracture-resistant materials. Our study reveals a fundamental connection between elasticity and network topology, and demonstrates its practical potential for designing mechanical systems and metamaterials. These results are published in another publication in Nature Materials (Nature Materials, 20, 1635–1642, 2021).

14306518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306518.value: 1. We discover fast crystal growth in charged colloidal systems under deep supercooling, where liquid diffusion is extremely low. We show that this process occurs via wall-induced barrierless ordering consisting of two coupled steps: the step-like advancement of the rough interface that disintegrates frustration, followed by defect repairing inside the newly formed solid phase. The former is a diffusionless collective process, whereas the latter controls crystal quality. We further show that the intrinsic mechanical instability of a disordered glassy state subject to the crystal growth front allows for domino-like fast crystal growth even at ultra-low temperatures. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of fast crystal growth and may be useful for applications related to vitrification prevention and crystal-quality control. These results are published in the journal of Nature Materials (Nature Materials, 20, 1431–1439, 2021). 2. In a structure similar to crystal, the hyper-uniform packing system, which is uniform in density but without translational order, we discover a topological transition. This transition enables a powerful tuning in system elasticity. Within one system, we achieve solid-like affine response, liquid-like non-affine response and a continuous tunability in between. Moreover, the system also exhibits a broadly tunable Poisson’s ratio from positive to negative values, which is of practical interest for energy absorption and for fracture-resistant materials. Our study reveals a fundamental connection between elasticity and network topology, and demonstrates its practical potential for designing mechanical systems and metamaterials. These results are published in the journal of Nature Materials (Nature Materials, 20, 1635–1642, 2021).

14306518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306518.value: The research results can be further applied for the design of materials with different Poisson's ratio, which has good anti-fracture and energy absorption properties. The course of action is to first numerically design structures with various Poisson's ratio, and then manufacture prototype structures with 3D-printing. After that, we will test the energy absorption and fracture resistance properties of these prototype systems. The final goal is to provide guidance for real anti-fracture and energy absorption materials.

14306518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306518.value: This project aims to identify the origin of nucleation precursors, probe their structural evolutions, and explore their role in forming crystals. Crystallization is ubiquitous in condensed matter physics and materials science. However, its exact kinetics has been under intensive debate for more than a century. In the classical nucleation theory, the kinetics of crystallization proceeds as nucleation and growth of nuclei: small crystals, which have the same symmetry and density as the final solid, directly emerge from the liquid through spontaneous thermal fluctuation. In contrast, however, the Ostwald?s step rule (1897) and many recent studies suggest the appearance of various intermediate states. To clarify this discrepancy, we have experimentally studied the early evolution of crystals. Our study has successfully illustrated the fast crystallization process under high super-cooling; moreover, we further revealed the powerful tuning of elasticity in a crystal-like hyper-uniform packing system. The related results are published in two publications in the prestigious journal of Nature Materials (Nature Materials, 20, 1431-1439, 2021 and Nature Materials, 20, 1635-1642, 2021).

14306718.value: 無界區域上數學模型的預處理方法的構造和分析

14306718.label: Project Objectives
14306718.value: We formulate a general complex-valued discrete variational system to a real-valued saddle-point system of special structure, then construct general preconditioning systems in variational form under the finite element setting. We formulate the general conditions for the preconditioning systems, under which the spectrum of the preconditioned systems can be estimated in terms of some crucial parameters involved in the discrete variational systems. We apply our general frameworks to the large-scale discrete systems arising from some important and representative PDE models. We conduct numerical experiments to check the preconditioning effects of the new preconditioners and improve them based on the numerical results.

14306718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306718.value: 許多重要應用問題的數學模型都是通過無界域中的偏微分方程來表示的。為了數值上穩定，快速求偏這些微分方程， 必須通過一些特殊的數學途徑將它們化為一些有界域中的偏微分方程來近似 (稱為近似模型)。有許多這樣的特殊的數學理論工具，例如，完全匹配層（PML）技術被證明是最流行和最有效的技術之一。通過PML技術將無界域中的數學模型轉換得到的有界域上的模型，稱為PML近似系統。對於各種不同的偏微分方程模型，大量的數學研究已經證明了PML系統的近似解相對於PML的厚度將以指數級的速度收斂於無界域中原始模型的真實解。 但是，幾乎所有現有的高效求解偏微分方程模型的數值方法都是基於本身就是在有界域中建立的微分方程模型，它们不能應用於PML系統。雖然PML系統也是有界域中的偏微分方程，但它們在數學上完全不同於原始的無界域中的偏微分方程。新的有效求解PML系統的數值方法必須是基於PML系統的各項特徵來構造的。離散化的PML系統規模龐大且缺乏在無界域中原始偏微分方程的一些好的特徵和結構，所以為這些大規模和不適定的離散化系統構造有效的數值求解方法一直是工程，物理和計算數學界的一個巨大的挑戰。雖然這個問題對許多實際應用問題至關重要，目前在數學上和數值上的研究都極少。而這正是我們這個三年的研究項目的重點。我們將設計一些有效的有限元離散方法將 PML系統離散化得到大規模和不適定的代數係統， 再構造一系列高校及穩定的預處理方法求解這些代數係統。並研究一般的條件，使得預處理方法的有效性可以根據所涉及的關鍵參數進行評估，例如網格尺寸，PML參數和PML系統中係數的跳躍等。

14306718.label: Realisation of objectives
14306718.value: During this RGC project, we have made a very successful effort and realized all our project objectives. We have also achieved a series of very encouraging and exciting theoretical and numerical results in several aspects that are closely related to the project objectives but were not expected in our original proposal. Various PDE models on unbounded domains have been explored, including both their mathematical formulations and analytical understanding as well as their efficient numerical methods and simulations. Many mathematical models on unbounded domains from wide applications, such as medicine, underwater acoustics, earthquake modelling, and seismic imaging, can be reduced to models on bounded domains effectively and accurately, e.g., by PML, ABC and DtN techniques. Efficient numerical solutions of these reduced models are then of tremendous interest. In our work [2], we took a typical acoustic wave model with high frequencies as an example to discuss a systematic framework to help construct efficient numerical solvers, especially preconditioning-type iterative methods. We considered a family of complex-valued indefinite Helmholtz problems with absorption and increasing wavenumber and studied some highly parallel and optimal preconditioners for solving the large-scale discrete systems arising from general finite element approximations of the model. More specifically, we formulated and analysed a new parallel preconditioner for solving the complex-valued indefinite Helmholtz problems. We presented a rigorous theory to justify that our preconditioners remain highly parallel and efficient even when the wavenumber is very large. It is remarkable that the additive Schwarz method is proved to be also robust when the number of subdomains grow quickly. This new method is proved to be very powerful and effective, and can be applicable to many other wave type PDE models. In order to more stably and accurately approximate the solutions of the reduced models on bounded domains, adaptive methods are very reliable choices and also the focus of this project, see [3][4]. But the development and justifications of adaptive methods are challenging. We proposed in [3] an adaptive method and established its full convergence for an important electromagnetic optimal control model problem. An efficient strategy is introduced to approximate the state variable and adjoint state by edge elements, and the control variable by the simplest piecewise constants. We established the reliability and efficiency of the a posteriori error estimator and the strong convergence of the adaptive solutions for both the state and control variables. More interestingly, our preconditioners in [2] can be directly and effectively applied to the resulting large-scale systems during the adaptive iteration. Many important physical phenomena, including the Bingham fluid, the friction, and type-II high-temperature superconductivity can be modelled by the mechanic or elastic or electromagnetic variational inequalities. We proposed in [4] an efficient adaptive method for solving this type of electromagnetic variational inequalities. Type-II superconductors are characterized by the loss of electrical resistance and the repulsion of weak magnetic fields when they are cooled down below a certain critical temperature. For describing the penetration and exit of the magnetic flux in a type-II superconductor, the critical state Bean model is most popular to relate the electrical field and the current density. By combining this smodel with the electromagnetic system, we obtained a nonlinear hyperbolic mixed variational inequality. This is the first work to design and analyse adaptive methods for electromagnetic variational inequalities. We established both the reliability and the efficiency of these estimators, by means of a special linear auxiliary problem involving the discrete Moreau-Yosida-regularized dual formulation, along with a local regular H(curl) decomposition. We also demonstrated strong convergence of adaptive edge element solutions. All the mathematical models that were addressed in this RGC project are important forward models in many physical or medical inverse problems. Numerical solutions of inverse problems are computationally much more expensive than the solution of the corresponding forward problems. In the work [5], we took the popular elliptic model as a general example to construct a series of novel direct sampling methods (DSMs) for simultaneously reconstructing two different types of physical inhomogeneities inside a sampling domain when very limited measurement data, available from only one or two measurement events. This inverse problem is highly unstable and ill-posed. Our new sampling method can decouple the respective signals coming from the monopole-type and dipole-type sources located in the sampling domain so that it enables to decouple the boundary measurements and achieves desired simultaneous reconstructions. This sampling method can be computed in a fast, stable and highly parallel manner, and is a special type of efficient preconditioners for many inverse problems of PDEs. Furthermore, we proposed in [7] a DSM for the effective and stable inversion of the Radon transform. The fractional order duality product can greatly enhance the robustness of the reconstructions in many physically important but severely ill-posed inverse problems. A systematic analysis is conducted to help understand the performance of the new DSM for stable and efficient numerical reconstructions of inhomogeneous media. Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) type methods are proved to be effective in solving various large-scale systems arising from wide applications. But no mathematical analysis was developed on the stability and convergence of SGDs for ill-posed inverse problems. In our recent works [9][10], we provided a systematical mathematical study to understand how, why and under what conditions different variants of SGDs are effective and efficient for general linear and nonlinear inverse problems, by means of the classical regularization theory and a priori stopping rules. Another fundamental mathematical issue to inverse problems is their unique identifiability, which has also been a key component in this RGC project; see [8][11][12]. We studied in [8] the shape identification and coefficient determination associated with two time-dependent PDE models, determining an obstacle and a coefficient involved in the PDEs from a single dynamical near-field data. We proved that the sound speed together with its contrast support of a polygon type can be uniquely determined, and also established a unique identifiability for recovering an electric potential as well as its support in a second PDE. These results enable us to develop a uniqueness result for recovering the refractive index of a medium from a single far-field at a fixed frequency in the time-harmonic case. In [11] [12], we studied unique identifiability of inhomogeneous media by finitely far-field measurements, which is a long-standing fundamental mathematical problem in inverse scattering problems. We provided a systematic investigation and characterization of qualitative behaviors of eigenfunctions of a PDE operator at a corner point and the geometric quantities of that corner for various geometric cases. These results and observations are applied to establish unique identifiability for several physically important problems, including the inverse obstacle scattering and diffraction grating problems by far-field measurements. These results discovered that in a polyhedral setup, we can recover the unknown scatterer and the surface impedance parameter by finitely far-field patterns, even two far-field data for some important cases. For all the numerical methods we proposed and nearly all typical PDE models discussed in this project, we have carried out a large number of numerical simulations to show their stability, efficiency and convergence for various PDE models, which can be found in all the publications listed in this completion report.

14306718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306718.value: As we know, many mathematical models on unbounded domains from wide applications can be reduced to models on bounded domains effectively and accurately. Efficient numerical solutions of these reduced models are then of tremendous interest. In this project, we focused only on some standard elliptic and wave PDE models to develop a systematic framework to help construct efficient numerical solvers, especially preconditioning-type iterative methods. But with different PDE models, the constructions and analyses of preconditioning-type solvers are very different. It will be a practically and mathematically important direction to construct and analyse preconditioning-type iterative solvers for more general PDEs, such as time-harmonic electromagnetic Maxwell systems and nonlinear acoustic Helmholtz model equations. In order to more stably and accurately approximate the solutions of the reduced models on bounded domains, adaptive methods are very reliable choices. But the development and justifications of adaptive methods are challenging, and we focused only on two typical PDE models in this project, namely electromagnetic optimal control model problem and electromagnetic variational inequalities for Type-II superconductors, and present some mathematical theories to help understand the stability and convergence of these adaptive methods. But for practical applications, it is also extremely important to understand if the adaptive methods can really reduce stable and accurate numerical solutions with least degrees of freedom in comparison with other popular non-adaptive methods. This will be a very important and challenging topic for general adaptive methods.

14306718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306718.value: Popular and effective mathematical models for many important real applications are often described by partial differential equations (PDEs) in unbounded domains. For numerical solutions, these PDE models must be approximated by some effectively transformed and equivalent PDEs in bounded domains. There are many such approximation techniques, including two popular ones, i.e., perfectly matched layers (PMLs) and absorbing boundary conditions (ABCs). Nearly all existing efficient numerical solvers are developed for PDE models that are defined originally in bounded domains, and can not apply to the PML or ABC systems. New efficient numerical methods should be constructed for these PDE systems, and it is a big challenge to design efficient and stable numerical solvers for these large-scale and ill-conditioned discrete systems. Although this is a fundamental area in applied and computational mathematics, little has been done both mathematically and numerically. And it is the main focus of this RGC project. We have constructed a series of efficient solvers for the large-scale and ill-conditioned systems arising from finite element discretizations of the PML or ABC systems. General conditions are formulated under which the effectiveness of the solvers can be assessed in terms of the crucial parameters involved. The framework and its general conditions are demonstrated for several important PDE models in unbounded domains.

14306918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306918.value: 2016年諾貝獎的頒發承認了拓撲相和拓撲相變是過去三十年中現代凝聚態物理學的重大突破。1982年，一些不為人們所預期的平臺首次被人們在分數填充的二維電子氣霍爾電阻測量中發現。這一現象被稱為分數量子霍爾效應。隨後人們意識到不同的分數量子霍爾態具有同樣的對稱性卻屬於不同的物質相，因此它們不能被通常的對稱性破缺相變理論所描述。因此分數量霍爾效應代表了一種全新的超越對稱性破缺序的新型量子物質態，人們把它叫做拓撲序。拓撲物質中的分數化激發，分數化統計，非阿貝尓統計等現象在量子多體系統中的湧現揭開了現代凝聚態物理學的新篇章。 拓撲絕緣體在三維無相互作用或弱相互作用電子系統中的理論預言和實驗實現進一步把我們對拓撲序的認知推向了高維空間。三維空間中拓撲激發最獨特的特點是不僅存在點粒子的激發，還可以存在具有延展性的閉弦激發。然後在無相互作用作用或者弱相互作用電子系統中的閉弦激發並不具有分數化統計。 因此，我們要構造和研究一類全新的無法在三維無相互作用或弱相互作用系統中實現的拓撲超導體。我們發現在三維超導體的渦旋線上陷入馬約拉納鏈可以導致一類全新的強關聯電子系統拓撲超導體。這類超導體的渦旋線具有分數化的非阿貝尓統計。將來這類新型超導體可能幫助我們實現常溫拓撲量子計算機。

14306918.label: Realisation of objectives
14306918.value: (a) Very recently, we have made important progress on the classification of fermionic symmetry protected topological (FSPT) phases based on the concept of equivalence class of finite depth fermionic symmetric local unitary (FSLU) transformations and decorating symmetry domain wall picture, subjected to certain obstructions. The obstruction-free and trivialization-free constructions naturally lead to a classification of FSPT phases. Each fixed-point wave function admits an exactly solvable commuting-projector Hamiltonian. By gauging these FSPT phases, we can realize all topological phases in 3D interacting fermion systems. (b) In another very important work, we systematically study the so-called three-loop braiding statistics for 3D interacting fermion systems. Most surprisingly, we discover new types of non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics that can only be realized in fermionic systems (or equivalently bosonic systems with emergent fermionic particles). On the other hand, due to the correspondence between gauge theories with fermionic particles and classifying fermionic symmetry-protected topological (FSPT) phases with unitary symmetries, our study also gives rise to an alternative way to classify FSPT phases. We further compare the classification results for FSPT phases with arbitrary Abelian unitary total symmetry Gf and find systematical agreement with previous studies. (c) We also established a topological quantum field theory(TQFT) framework to understand the quantum statistics of particle and loop like excitation in 3 + 1D. In particular, based on the dimension reduction picture, we generalize the 2+1D Chern Simons theory into 3+1D to describe three-loop braiding statistics.

14306918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306918.value: Based on the equivalent class of symmetric fermionic local unitary (FLU) transformation and decorating domain wall picture, that is, decorating (subject to certain obstructions) 2D (p+ip) topological superconductors to 2D symmetry domain walls, 1D Majorana chains to 1D symmetry domain walls or intersection lines of domain walls, complex fermion modes to 0D symmetry domain walls or intersection points of domain walls, we explicitly construct all the fixed point wavefunctions of SPT phases for 3D interacting fermion systems. Our paper was published on Physical Review X(Qing-Rui Wang and Zheng-Cheng Gu Phys. Rev. X 10, 031055) and recognized as a major breaking through in the research of topological order. By gauging intrinsic interacting fermionic SPT phases, new types of topological phase was discovered in 3D. Among many different examples, one of the most interesting case is characterized by flux line with Ising non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics, which can be interpreted as the 2D generalization of Ising non-Abelian braiding statistics for p+ip TSC. However, very different from the 2D case, it is easy to see that the flux line decorated with a Majorana zero mode must be linked to another flux line, otherwise one can always smoothly shrink a flux line into a point point-like excitation with a Majorana zero mode on it. It is well known that in 3D, a point point-like object can only be boson or fermion, and it is impossible to carry non-Abelian statistics induced by the Majorana zero mode. Actually, one should regard the two Majorana zero modes on the linked flux as the two open ends of a 1D Majorana chain. Thus, it is will be much easier to understand the non-Abelian nature of the three-loop braiding statistics, since as a pair of linked flux lines with two topological Majorana zero modes which will generate two-fold degeneracy. Similar to the 2D case, the braiding statistics between two loops linked with a third loop should will be characterized by an SU(2) matrix instead of a U(1) phase factor. Our paper was published on Nature Communication(Zhou, JR., Wang, QR., Wang, C. Zheng-Cheng Gu, Nat Commun 12, 3191 (2021). ) and was highlighted as a major breakthrough for topological phase of quantum matter in 3D.

14306918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306918.value: For future research, there are a few interesting directions based on our current results. (a) It will be very important and interesting to study symmetry enriched topological phases in 3+1D. (b) The 3D topological phase with Ising non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics might provide us with a new understanding for the origin of three generations of elementary particles. (c) It will also be very important to work out the topological quantum field theory(TQFT) that describes topological phase with Ising non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics.

14306918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306918.value: The discovery of topological insulators?exotic materials in which electrons can move only along the surface?has led to a search for similar underlying phenomena in a range of systems. It turns out that topological insulators are just one example of a broader class of materials known as symmetry-protected topological phases (SPT), where properties are protected by topology and certain global symmetries. Here, we propose a way to construct and classify SPT phases in systems of interacting fermions. Until now, the understanding of SPT phases in systems of interacting fermions has been very limited. Researchers have found much greater success in classifying SPT phases in systems of interacting bosons and free fermions. Previous efforts to extend this success to interacting fermions have largely relied on modifications to existing mathematical descriptions of interacting bosons and free fermions, but such attempts end up missing many fermionic phases. Rather than use existing math, we develop new mathematical structures that allow us to fully characterize the many SPT phases that can arise in systems of interacting fermions. By gauging these newly discovered fermioic SPT phases, we further discovered new types of 3D topological phases with Ising non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics.

14307018.label: Project Objectives
14307018.value: We’ll try to understand the stability of SCO2, SCO2.5 and SCO3 by calculating their stable structure, related phase diagram, projected density of states, magnetic coupling strength with GGA+U exchange correlation functional. Such analysis will be combined with the ECM, tight binding theory, crystal field splitting theory, and molecular orbital theory to illustrate the physical origin of this surprising stability in the porous material. Meanwhile, the calculated phase diagram will be shared with our experimental collaborator to further improve the crystal quality of BM-SCO. Such information will be extremely valuable since our collaborator will adopt epitaxial growth technique to grow high quality BM-SCO single crystals. Also, the phase diagram will be checked by our experimental collaborators. We’ll further conduct investigations of band structure and tune SCO with group I, II, VII elements. ECM will be conducted to help replacing Co with other transition metals and O concentration may be tuned to preserve the porous and single crystal nature. Various diffusion barriers of different elements along different diffusion channels will be calculated by the climbing image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) method. Magnetic order will also be studied. All these results will be rapidly shared with our experimental collaborators to largely enhance the tuning, searching and development of SCO related devices.

14307018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307018.value: The aim of this project is to investigate the stability and seeking for tuning strategies to largely enhance the device performance of SrCoO2.5, using density functional theory approach. SrCoO2.5 is a promising magnetic semiconducting oxide material, with superior stability and flexible tuning strategy for energy applications. Particularly, as pointed out by our collaborators in a recent Nature article, by using a dual-ion switch, a reversible, electric-field-controlled phase transformation among three distinct crystalline phases in this system can be realized. In this way, it may have promising potential in applications such as fuel cell, ion batteries, catalysis, magnetic, and information devices. However, fundamental physical understanding lacks for the stability and semiconducting nature with the presence of a large amount of oxygen vacancies. Such vacancies also make it very attractive to incorporate various ions or metallic elements to dramatically change the electronic or magnetic properties. Yet, the general understanding for such strategies lacks and limited kinetic studies have been performed. Therefore, a investigation of stability and fundamental tuning strategy is highly desirable in this material. . Density functional theory is a well-established technique to accurately calculate electronic, magnetic and kinetic properties. By applying this approach, we have studied and proposed many novel strategies to control defects concentrations and types in GaP, ZnO, Si, Cu2ZnSnS4, and Cu2ZnSnSe4. In this project, we plan to, (1) investigate the physical origin of the stability, construct phase diagram and stable chemical potential range; (2) tuning electronic, magnetic, kinetic, defect properties by incorporating various ions, metallic elements in the context of potential energy applications. Our findings will help to improve basic scientific understandings of the electronic properties and the controlling schemes of SrCoO2.5. We expect that our results will provide important theoretical predictions on property tuning and new materials with porous and semiconducting nature and improve the efficiency of various potential applications. These results will directly impact the field of energy devices. The general strategy of property tuning in porous single crystal will help to improve other similar semiconductor devices, which have played or will play important roles in our daily life. 本項目的目的是使用密度泛函理論研究SrCoO2.5的穩定性，並找出可以調整優化SrCoO2.5器件性能的方法。 SrCoO2.5是一種很有前景的磁性半導體氧化物材料，具有出色的穩定性和靈活的調節策略，適用于能源應用。值得一提的是，我們的合作者最近發表了一篇Nature文章，文中指出：通 過使用雙離子開關，SrCoO2.5系統中的三個不同結晶相之間可以達到可逆的由電場控制的相 變。通過這種方式，SrCoO2.5在諸如燃料電池、離子電池、催化、磁性和信息設備等領域中 具有很大的應用空間。然而，由于SrCoO2.5存在大量氧空位，人們對該材料的穩定性和半導 體性質還缺乏基礎物理上的理解。這些氧空位還導致SrCoO2.5非常容易與各種離子或金屬元 素結合，從而顯著改變材料的電子或磁性特性。目前尚沒有針對這些策略的的整體理解，對 SrCoO2.5的動力學研究亦非常不足，有鑒于此，針對該材料的穩定性和基本調整策略的研究迫在眉睫。 密度泛函理論是一項可以精確計算電子、磁性和動力學特性的成熟技術。通過密度泛函理論方法，我們研究並提出了許多新策略，用以控制GaP，ZnO，Si，Cu2ZnSnS4和Cu2ZnSnSe4 等材料的缺陷濃度和種類。在這個項目中，我們計劃，1）研究穩定性的物理起源，構建相 圖和穩定化學勢範圍; 2）針對能源方面的應用，通過摻入各種離子和金屬元素，來調節電子、磁性、動力學，以及缺陷性質。 我們的研究結果將有助于從基礎科學角度出發，提高對SrCoO2的電子特性和調節策略的基本科學認識。預計我們的研究成果將爲多孔半導體性質的新材料提供重要的 理論預測，並提高相關器件效率。這些結果將直接關系到能源領域各種應用的設計。“另外，對多孔晶體的理解和調節也將有助于改進其他類似的半導體器件，而這些器件已經或將在我們的日常生活中發揮重要作用。

14307018.label: Realisation of objectives
14307018.value: We successfully computed the phase diagram of SCO related phases, obtained the density of states, magnetic coupling strength. In addition to GGA+U method, we also achieved more accurate results based on SCAN functional. In our analysis, we invented an extended version of electron counting model (ECM), applied it to six fold symmetry, which is significantly different from the original ECM. In addition, in our thin film and surface stability analysis of SCO related phases, we invented a new approach to take one whole layer as a unit to calculate the electron supply and electron shortage on each layer. This new model is very successful in SCO systems. Based on this new model, stable surface reconstructions are discovered and found to match with experimental results. Previously, it was found to be challenging to remove the long range coupling in calculations between the top and bottom surface. We discovered a new passivation scheme to passivate the bottom surface and isolate the states of top surface. Based on this new scheme, we discovered the most stable surface orientation, the most stable surface reconstructions, and important H passivation scheme on the top surface of SCO. Additioanly, we found that the magnetic order of the system is sensitive to the concentration of the H on the top surface. This finding may provide important insights to the long-standing puzzle on the inconsistency of magnetic order between theory and experiment and also match with the experimental facts that slight excess of H may provide ferromagnetic order to the system. Also, it paved way for future analysis on the stability of H attachment in the hydrogenic phases of SCO. The related results are published as "Surface Stability Analysis with H Adsorption Affected the Magnetic Fluctuation of Brownmillerite SrCoO2.5 Based on the Electron Counting Model by Layers", Yupu Wang, Gaofeng Teng, and Junyi Zhu* at J. Phys. Chem. C 2022, 126, 29, 12251–12263. In addition, we discovered a new algorithm to largely improve the accuracy of defect studies based on SCAN functional structure and HSE electronic structure calculations and applied it in a similar perovskite system and to achieve very accurate results that is comparable with pure hybrid functional study, which is computationally expensive. This new method can be adopted as a standard approach in future defect studies. In addition, we also find that the bond orbital coupling is very important to the defect charge states and stability in ionic compound semiconductors. The related research works are published as "Defect calculations using a combined SCAN and hybrid functional in γ-CsPbI3" by Shengyuan Wang, Kin Fai Tse, Alena Boyko and Junyi Zhu* at Phys Chem Chem Phys, 2022 Feb 2;24(5):3420-3428. doi: 10.1039/d1cp04449d. Note that Alena Boyko is an undergraduate student. At the same time, since the local and crystal symmetry is very important in the defect studies of SCO related compounds, we adopted a machine learning approach and successfully predict the crystal symmetry based the input of band structure data with a deep neural network. The accuracy for cubic lattice like SCO systems are very high, more than 90%. This find also paves ways in the future ARPES related studies of complexed oxides. The research results are published as "Machine-Learning-Assisted Acceleration on High-Symmetry Materials Search: Space Group Predictions from Band Structures", by Bin Xi, Kin Fai Tse, Tsz Fung Kok, Ho Ming Chan, Man Kit Chan, Ho Yin Chan, Kwan Yue Clinton Wong, Shing Hei Robin Yuen, and Junyi Zhu*, at J. Phys. Chem. C 2022, 126, 29, 12264–12273. Note that Tsz Fung Kok, Ho Ming Chan, Man Kit Chan, Ho Yin Chan, Kwan Yue Clinton Wong, Shing Hei Robin Yuen are all undergraduate students. Finally, we systematically investigated the H diffusion in SCO and computed the diffusion barrier of H at different charge states of the system with spin polarized nature. In our research, we discovered various diffusion pathways and find out the most important pathway, which is consistent with experimental findings by our collaborators. Also, we found out interesting charge transfer mechanism from the H to various Co sites based on local symmetry arguments of the crystal field splitting theory. The findings are published as "Diffusion Studies of H of Different Charge States and Their Interplay with Co Spin States in SrCoO2.5. " by Gaofeng Teng Gaofeng Teng, Yupu Wang, Jingzhao Zhang, Sze-Chun Tsang, and Junyi Zhu* at J. Phys. Chem. C 2022, 126, 38, 16315–16331. We also made APS presentations on all the research results.
