14307018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307018.value: In terms of surface science, we have constructed new model of electron counting and applied it successfully on the complexed structure of SCO with oxygen vacancy channels. Previously, ECM is only applied in conventional semiconductors and whether it is applicable to a very complexed system of SCO with oxygen vacancy channel is highly unclear. In our work, we found that a modification in terms of coordination works very well for surface studies of SCO. Without this new model, it is almost impossible to quickly find the most stable surface reconstructions of complexed oxides. In the field of magnetism and diffusion, we discovered that atomic and ion diffusion of H may affect the magnetic system in a surprising way by transfer the charge to nearby or faraway Co atoms to fulfill the local symmetry requirement and lower the system energy. Previously, most studies of diffusion ignored the charge states and spin polarization. We are the first to discover that the charge states and spin configuration are critical to predict the diffusion pathways. The general diffusion study for such a low symmetry system is very difficult and we set up our leading positions in this field by accomplish the interesting investigation of H and proton diffusion and their effects on the magnetism. The machine learning algorithm is also very original. It is the first ever practice to train machine intelligence with the band structure as inputs to figure out symmetry properties and may lead to very interesting future development in both theory and also experimental studies with ARPES. In addition, it accelerates the material search for at least one order of magnitude based on symmetry information. The general defect algorithm we discovered largely accelerate the defect formation and transition energy calculation. Also, during the studies, it was the first time to realize the bond orbital coupling is the driving mechanism in the understanding of semiconductor defects with their surrounding electronic environment. We have published three papers at JPCC, one paper at PCCP and four conference talks at APS March meeting.

14307018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307018.value: The new extension of electron counting model can be widely applied in most compound semiconductors and will be taken as a standard. The newly discovered algorithm of neural network can be especially important in the searching of new materials based on electronic properties. The new algorithm of defect studies based on SCAN and hybrid functional can easily become the standard approach in defect stability studies. Based on this new algorithm, we are also working on a new paper on the H effects in both SCO and HSCO, which may explain the interesting phenomenon of weak ferromagnetism in HSCO. Please see section C, publication 5 for details.

14307018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307018.value: We have developed multiple important algorithms to investigate the phase stability, defect stability of SCO related systems. The new algorithm reduces the computing cost for at least one order of magnitude. In addition, we proposed a highly accurate neural network algorithm to train machine intelligence to understand the crystal symmetry from band structure inputs which may accelerate the searching speed of new materials by at least one order of magnitude. In addition to these computational discoveries, we constructed new electron counting models that are applicable for highly complexed oxides with internal surfaces. With this approach, phase stability, surface stability, surface reconstructions, H passivation effects are all obtained. With these new findings, interesting intercoupling mechanism between surface states and magnetism is discovered with the help of bond orbital coupling. Our diffusion studies also illustrate the importance of charge states and spin polarization for the first time in complexed oxides and with the help of symmetry analysis, we obtain the important insights of bond orbital coupling that may strongly affect the diffusion barrier of neutral and ionic defects. These finding may pave the way to further fine-tune the strategies of liquid ion gating and lead to new devices.

14307118.value: Having proved that the optical components can really work together, now is the time to work on the practical issues of un/installation. The plan is to manually un/install the wire grid and the half-wave plate and to leave the torque motor plus the entire supporting frame permanently on the telescope. We will replace the current wire grid with a smaller one to be installed on the window of the TES (transition edge sensor) camera cryostat. A smaller grid can be manually un/install easily. Installing right on the window can minimize the possibility for the ambient noise to enter the cryostat through the wire grid. Software - We need software to coordinate the operation of APol, the TES camera and ASTE. The software also needs to save useful information in a synchronised time sequence, e.g., pointing, intensity, sky noise, wave-plate position, etc. The data analysis pipeline will also be finished before APol deployment 2020-2021.

14307118.value: Aim To upgrade the Polarimeter for the Atacama Submillimetre Telescope Experiment (APol) in order to gather the data necessary to improve the understanding of the role of magnetic fields in star formation. Project Background There is currently no agreement among astronomers on important aspects of how stars form, especially the role played by B-fields. Our previous work in this area has led to important advances, but in order to make further progress it is necessary to have equipment that can study the faint magnetic fields in prestellar gas clouds. This means having an efficient polarimeter, working at more than one frequency, in an excellent sub-mm observation site. Significance of Project This project will provide the equipment necessary to gain a better understanding of the role B-fields play in the formation of stars. B-fields are still the most mysterious player in star formation. This will be the first instrument of this kind led by an Asian institute. The number of astronomers acknowledging the importance of magnetic fields (B-field) in star formation is rapidly growing. This is reflected in the growing number of millimeter and sub-millimeter polarimeters, the instrument for mapping B-field morphologies in molecular clouds. For example, the IRAM-30M telescope, the Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy and the Large Millimeter Telescope all have new or up-coming polarimeters. Thanks to the support from RGC (GRF14600915), we are leading the international collaboration over APol, the polarimeter for the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE). APol will be the second sub-mm polarimeter located in the best sub-mm observing site, the Atacama desert, and the first led by Asia. In this proposal, we first report the current status of APol, including the software development and hardware testing. We then propose plans for improvement, which include a semi-automatic method to un/install APol on the telescope. The method will also improve the signal-to-noise ratio. Also, APol can currently work only at 350 GHz. We propose to extend the working frequency to 270 and 670 GHz. The spectrum of polarization of thermal dust emission is an important method for studying dust properties which, in turn, will help build a more precise understanding of the relationship between polarization and B-field orientations. 目標: 優化APol亞毫米波偏振儀以覌測分子雲磁場, 幫助了解恆星生成機制. 背景: 磁場會如何影響恆星生成仍無定論. 中大恆星生成研究小組在本領域已作出重要貢獻. 而進一步的研究須要更靈敏的儀器和更優良的觀測環境. 計劃重點: 完成APol的優化, 至Atacama沙漠的部署及䦕始觀測. APol是世界第一個由亞洲大學領導完成的亞毫米波偏振儀. Atacama沙漠有全球最佳的亞毫米波觀測環境, 而偏振儀是測量分子雲磁場的唯一手段.

14307218.label: Realisation of objectives
14307218.value: In this project, we proposed to develop lysine-selective site-specific reactions for the modification of autophagy proteins, to probe autophagosome formation, and to study the content of the autophagosomes. We also proposed to study the molecular mechanism of autophagosome formation by newly designed chemical probes and inhibitors to protein-protein interactions. Both objectives have been successfully realized. (1) We have significantly advanced lysine-selective conjugation reactions. (2) We designed a new method to label LC3 and autophagosomes. (3) We developed new chemical biological tools to study the protein-protein interactions in autophagy. (4) We developed covalent blockers for USP30. The center of this project is the development of site-selective lysine reactions, covalent conjugation reactions, and chemical probes. Site-selective lysine reactions are challenging because of the difficulty of identifying one lysine residue among many in the same protein. By screening different amine-reactive groups fluorodinitrobenzene, isothiocyanate, and phenyl ester reactions, we developed site-selective lysine reactions first on model proteins: Crk SH3 domain and the ubiquitin-like protein SUMO. Next, we designed Atg8/LC3-specific lysine reaction based on the crystal structure and texted the reaction using a library of reactive peptides containing the unnatural amino acids. This led to the discovery of peptides that can covalently react with Atg8 and LC3 for the first time. Mass spectrometric analysis of the peptide fragments of ATG8d-peptide conjugates after proteolysis gave evidence that peptides A6 and A8 exhibit different reaction patterns. For one peptide, Lys50 is the reaction site, whereas, for another peptide, Lys51 or Lys65 may serve as the nucleophile in this conjugation reaction. These experiments show that we successfully achieved the objective of developing site-selective reactive peptides for Atg8 proteins. To our knowledge, this is the first Atg8-specific, lysine-selective reaction developed. This reaction could also be developed to be a dual-functional peptide for covalent labeling or pull-down of LC3 from complex protein mixtures, for example, a cell lysate. Also, it allowed us to covalently label autophagosomes. For this purpose, we first purified GFP-LC3 positive autophagosome (LC3+ puncta) from HeLa cells and performed covalent labeling reactions on autophagosome particles using A20 and A8-TMR peptides. Colocalization of the GFP signal with the TMR signal can be clearly visualized. When we zoomed in on each particle under a super-resolution microscope, we observed heterogeneity of the labeling reactions. For example, some of the LG3+ puncta showed very bright TMR signals, whereas some are less bright and some showed unsymmetrical distribution. This suggests that the distribution of Atg8 on autophagosomes may not be homogeneous, although the final confirmation awaits further proof. We also attempted the semi-synthesis of Atg8 through native protein ligation and made significant progress on forming Atg7-Atg8 complexes. Protein semi-synthesis represents a powerful tool to acquire functional proteins with unnatural amino acids that enable following chemical biological experiments. We explored two different methods to synthesize ubiquitin-like small proteins: a native chemical ligation (NCL) method, and an enzymatic ligation using sortase. The key of the NCL is the generation of reactive thioester, which will ligate with N-terminal cysteine-containing peptides. A different method of generating reactive thioester using the naturally-existing intein chemistry resulted in expressed protein ligation (EPL). We synthesized a peptide with N-terminal cysteine residue and generated a construct to express 6xHistag-MBP-Atg8H-intein. Adding an excess of small molecule thiol to the protein produces 6xHistag-MBP-Atg8H-thioester. This thioester spontaneously reacted with the peptide NH2-CQETFGK(5(6)-FAM)-CONH2 and produced Atg8H-FAM. The Atg8H-FAM protein is visible on the fluorescent scanning image, indicating successful conjugation of the peptide with the protein thioester. We also explored different methods to synthesize C-terminally modified peptides. One new method we developed was an on-resin Passerini reaction to produce C-terminal photocaged peptides. This method will enable optical control of the autophagy events. Also, we developed synthetic methods to produce peptides with C-terminal Dha or propargyl-groups that can react with an active cysteine residue in the processing enzyme. We also acquired the technology of cryoEM and single particle analysis for protein structure determination. In addition, we also conducted research on the development of peptide inhibitors of USP30 (Ubiquitin-specific protease 30), a key protein in the regulation of autophagy of mitochondria and a potential drug target for the treatment of Parkinson's Disease. We first PCR-amplified the catalytic domain of human USP30 57-517, inserted the sequence into different vectors, and expressed GST-USP30, SUMO-His-USP30, and His-USP30 in pure forms. We then developed methylpyridinium ester-containing peptides with the ester installed at the terminus of the peptide to enable a covalent conjugation with the active site cysteine of USP30. We observed a peptide-USP30 complex on an SDS-PAGE gel, proving a covalent conjugation between the peptide and USP30. The methylpyridinium ester-containing peptides also can act as selective covalent inhibitors of USP30 and promote the autophagy of mitochondria. Summary We have developed a set of lysine-reactive peptide probes for the Atg8 protein family. Although Atg8 proteins have highly similar structures and at least eight lysine residues closely aligned on the surface, the lysine-reactive probe peptides can differentiate these lysine residues. This enables a site-specific reaction at only two lysine residues of Atg8, based on mass spectrometry analysis. The site-specific lysine reactions result in Atg8-specific covalent probes, that can be used to label autophagosomes in vitro. The most popularly used Atg8 labeling method is the genetic fusion of GFP or other fluorescent proteins on Atg8. But because of the small size of the Atg8 protein, a large GFP often changes the distribution of Atg8 protein and causes artifacts. Our peptide probe is significantly smaller than a GFP protein and thus may represent a new tool to study autophagosome formation. Aiming at developing Atg8 proteins with unnatural C-termini, we also expressed semisynthesis of the Atg8 proteins, both NCL, and sortase-mediated ligation methods were able to produce semisynthetic proteins. We also explored the synthesis of C-terminal-modified peptides and developed several methods that enable an unnatural C-terminus to be synthesized on peptides. This work paved the foundation for the generation of unnatural Atg8 proteins with reactive C-terminus for probing the Atg8 processing enzymes. Lastly, we developed reactive peptide blockers/probes for USP30, a key protein related to autophagy and degenerative diseases. Altogether, this work showcases the power of chemical biology in studying autophagy, develops various probes and blockers for essential proteins in the autophagy process, and significantly advances both peptide chemistry and Atg8 protein chemistry.

14307218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307218.value: Site-selective lysine reaction in a multi-lysine protein is challenging. By screening different amine-reactive groups and selecting a panel of protein-binding peptides, we developed Atg8 reactive peptides for the first time. The Atg8-reactive peptide can successfully label autophagosomes. We have established new synthetic methods of peptide C-terminal functionalization. It is relatively easy to install functional groups at the N-termini of peptides, but installing functional groups at the C-termini is challenging. Implementing multicomponent reactions in solid-phase peptide synthesis develops new linkers that, upon photolysis, will give peptides with different C-terminal groups. Alternatively, C-terminal functionalization may be enabled by an in-solution reaction of pre-synthesized peptides, or the direct derivatization of natural amino acid at the C-terminal end. Our research advanced the area of peptide C-terminal functionalization; combined with protein semisynthesis, it leads to new methods of acquiring C-terminally functionalized proteins. Other discoveries, including Atg7-Atg8 complexes, USP30 probes and blockers, and cryoEM structures of protein complexes, have also made significant contributions to the field of chemical biology. Several papers have been published to report the results above. This work was also reported at international conferences as invited talks. Several Ph.D. students received training under this project, and three graduated with a Ph.D. degree during the period.

14307218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307218.value: This research project significantly advanced the study of site-selective lysine reactions. Besides using this type of reaction on small, lysine-rich proteins, we are also motivated to apply the same strategy to therapeutic proteins, such as enzymes and antibodies. This new direction will not only develop tools to study biological processes but also devise new molecules that can impact biomedical research. Another inspiring direction is infection-induced autophagy. We and others notice that bacterial infection in mammalian cells may cause an increase in autophagy. With the tools that we developed in this project, we could use them to study E. coli-infection-induced autophagy, and to explore new anti-infection methods and tools. These two directions will lead to new research projects and new proposals in the future.

14307218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307218.value: Autophagy is a process that cells utilize to clear unwanted junk and rejuvenize the intracellular environment. The formation of autophagosomes, a new type of organelles, during the process, is hard to monitor and study, due to the lack of tools. Here in this project, we are dedicated to the development of peptide and protein tools for the study of this process. Utilizing proximity-guided reactions, we developed site-selective lysine conjugation that can selectively label Atg8 proteins. Together with other tool development, this research will lead to a better understanding of autophagosome formation and may eventually lead to new therapeutics for treating diseases such as bacterial infection.

14307318.label: Project Objectives
14307318.value: This project aims to investigate the degradation mechanisms of the water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries and the effects of surface modifications on electrode-electrolyte stability by a systematic model system approach to decouple combinatory effects at the water-in-salt electrode-electrolyte interfaces. The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows: We will fabricate thin-film model electrodes and composite electrodes of two positive electrodes, lithium manganese oxide (LiMn2O4)/lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2), and two negative electrodes, titanium sulphide (TiS2)/lithium titanium oxide (Li4Ti5O12), as model electrodes considering their distinct electrode potentials and cycling stabilities in water-in-salt electrolytes. We will employ comprehensive spectroscopic and microscopic techniques to decouple processes responsible for combinatory effects at the water-in-salt electrode-electrolyte interfaces. We will investigate the role of the three hypotheses on the degradation mechanisms of water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries: (i) parasitic reactions involving or triggered by the highly-concentrated bis(trifluoromethane)sulfonimide lithium salt (LiTFSI); (ii) electrode materials that have high oxygen evolution reaction (OER)/hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalytic activity catalyse water decomposition, which prevents the formation of stable passivation layer; (iii) electrode material that is prone to electrode protonation and metal dissolution will degrade in water-in-salt electrolyte even operating within the stable window of water. We will develop two electrode modifications including (1) employing a polymer coating using hydrophobic polymers with intrinsic microporosity on electrodes to repel water molecules while allowing the transport of lithium ions; (2) applying inorganic surface coatings of Al2O3 and AlF3 on electrode surface to reduce metal dissolution and electrode protonation. We will investigate the effects of the electrode surface modifications on the electrochemical stability of water, OER/HER, parasitic reactions as well as the natures of the solid-electrolyte-interface including its chemical composition, morphology, solubility and ionic conductivity.

14307318.value: 此項目採用模型系統的方法探究高濃度水溶鹽(WiS)水系鋰離子電池的衰減機制，並檢測電極表面修飾對水的穩定性、庫倫效率以及WiS水系鋰離子電池循環穩定性的影響。 非水系鋰離子電池採用易燃的電解質，存在巨大的安全隱患。水系鋰離子電池採用非易燃的水系電解質，顯著地提高了安全性能，但是其電池電壓受限于水的電化學穩定性(1.23V)，能量密度較低（<80 Wh/kg）。 高濃度水溶鹽（WiS）電解質可以顯著提高水系鋰離子電池的工作電壓（>3.0V）。然而，即使是在WiS電解質的穩定窗口内，對于不同的電極，WiS電機-電解質的界面穩定性也非常不同。這種與電極相關衰減的背後機制尚未被很好的理解。另外，高濃度鹽增加了成本，存在量產問題，這需要我們採取新的策略，在低濃度鹽溶液中創造類似的穩定電極-電解質界面。 在這一研究項目中，我們將研究模型電極-電解質的系統，探究WiS鋰離子電池的副反應及衰減機制，並解耦對電極-電解質界面有協同影響的過程。由於正極LiMn2O4/LiCoO2及負極TiS2/Li4Ti5O12具有較好的電勢優勢及在WiS電解質（21m双三氟甲烷磺酰亚胺锂(21m LiTFSI）-H2O）的循環穩定性，我們選擇這兩組正負極進行研究。具體而言，我們將(1)設計並製備LiMn2O4，LiCoO2, TiS2，Li4Ti5O12的薄膜模型電極與複合電極；（2）通過全面的非原位與原位光譜及微觀技術探究WiS水系鋰離子電池衰減機制的三種假說；（3）發展兩種電極修飾方法，包括(i)包覆具有微孔能夠斥水且導鋰離子的疏水聚合物，與(ii)在電極表面包覆無機Al2O3和AlF3薄膜，減少金屬元素在WiS電解質中的溶出及電極的質子化；（4）調研電極表面修飾對水的電化學穩定性、析氧、析氫反應、副反應以及固體電解質膜的化學組成、形貌、溶解度和離子電導率的影響。 通過此項目的研究，我們將更深入地理解水溶鹽水系鋰離子電池的衰減機制，這些將對未來設計安全、穩定、高能量密度的水系鋰離子電池提供指導。

14307318.label: Realisation of objectives
14307318.value: We fabricated composite electrodes of lithium manganese oxide (LiMn¬2O4, denotes LMO), lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2, denotes LCO) and lithium titanium oxide (Li4Ti5O12, denotes LTO) as model electrodes. We assembled LTO//LMO and LTO//LCO full Li-ion batteries to evaluate the degradation mechanism in water-in-salt aqueous electrolytes. To study the stability of the electrolytes, we performed tests of linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic cycling, scanning electron microscope (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), online electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). We investigated the role of three hypotheses on the degradation mechanisms of water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries: (i) to reveal parasitic reactions involving in the water-in-salt aqueous electrolyte with highly concentrated bis(trifluoromethane)sulfonimide lithium salt (LiTFSI), we selected 21 m LiTFSI and 19.4 m LiTFSI-8.3 m lithium bis(pentafluoroethanesulfonyl)imide (LiBETI) as model electrolytes. We detected the generation of CO, CO2, O2, H2 gas in the LTO//LMO and LTO//LCO full batteries during cycling with these two electrolytes using OEMS method. The evolved gas could indicate the type of parasitic reaction; (ii) we investigated the role of catalytic capability of electrode materials on the degradation in aqueous batteries. We selected LTO as model electrode since it has been reported that Ti is catalytic for HER. We conducted LSV on blank stainless steel (S.S.) current collector and LTO coated S.S. current collector to reveal the influence of LTO on the formation of passivating layer and electrochemical stability. (iii)To evaluate the influence of the electrode material that is prone to electrode protonation and metal dissolution, we selected LMO as model electrode because it’s reported that Mn dissolution is common for LMO in non-aqueous electrolyte. We performed galvanostatic cycling at 0.5 C with Ag/AgCl as reference electrode, 21 m LiTFSI as electrolyte, and monitored the capacity decay of LMO in 21m LiTFSI aqueous electrolyte during cycling. To improve the cycle performance of aqueous batteries, we developed both polymer and inorganic coating on the electrode surface to suppress the degradation behaviors. We tested a series of polymer coating layers on stainless steel (S.S.) current collectors, including Nafion (a sulfonated tetrafluoroethylene-based fluoropolymer-copolymer), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and polymer of intrinsic microporosity (PIM). We chose these polymers based on their micro-porosity, hydrophobicity, and good Li-ion conductivity. We employed inorganic surface coating of Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), LiAlO2 and Al2O3 on the surface of LTO powders due to their stability towards water and fast Li-ion transport. We also applied carbon coating on LiTi2(PO4)3 (LTP) electrode and fabricated free-standing 3D electrodes for flexible aqueous LTP//LMO batteries with ultrahigh areal capacity (3-23 mAh cm-2). To investigate the effects of polymer and inorganic coating, we performed SEM and TEM to observe the morphology and structure of the coating layer, we adopted LSV test to compare the stability of the coatings in aqueous electrolyte and analyzed the result of CV measurements to verify the electrochemical reversibility of the coated electrodes. We also performed OEMS to monitor the gas evolution (especially HER) during charge and discharge process of the full batteries to further verify whether water decomposition was virtually eliminated. In addition, we probed the nature of the solid-electrolyte-interface (SEI) derived from the aqueous electrolyte. We characterized the SEI composition by XPS analysis of different signals (C 1s, O 1s, F 1s, Cl 2p, etc.) for both surface and internal distribution of SEI on LTO and LMO electrode. We compared the structure of SEI derived from different electrolytes/electrodes by TEM. Based on the combined results, we correlated electrochemical stability to the composition and structure of the SEI and reveal the key species for building stable and robust SEI in aqueous batteries.

rows: This project aims to investigate the degradation mechanisms of the water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries and the effects of surface modifications on electrode-electrolyte stability by a systematic model system approach to decouple combinatory effects at the water-in-salt electrode-electrolyte interfaces. The technical objectives subordinate to our overall objective are as follows:

We will fabricate thin-film model electrodes and composite electrodes of two positive electrodes, lithium manganese oxide (LiMn2O4)/lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2), and two negative electrodes, titanium sulphide (TiS2)/lithium titanium oxide (Li4Ti5O12), as model electrodes considering their distinct electrode potentials and cycling stabilities in water-in-salt electrolytes. We will employ comprehensive spectroscopic and microscopic techniques to decouple processes responsible for combinatory effects at the water-in-salt electrode-electrolyte interfaces.

We will investigate the role of the three hypotheses on the degradation mechanisms of water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries: (i) parasitic reactions involving or triggered by the highly-concentrated bis(trifluoromethane)sulfonimide lithium salt (LiTFSI); (ii) electrode materials that have high oxygen evolution reaction (OER)/hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalytic activity catalyse water decomposition, which prevents the formation of stable passivation layer; (iii) electrode material that is prone to electrode protonation and metal dissolution will degrade in water-in-salt electrolyte even operating within the stable window of water.

We will develop two electrode modifications including (1) employing a polymer coating using hydrophobic polymers with intrinsic microporosity on electrodes to repel water molecules while allowing the transport of lithium ions; (2) applying inorganic surface coatings of Al2O3 and AlF3 on electrode surface to reduce metal dissolution and electrode protonation.

We will investigate the effects of the electrode surface modifications on the electrochemical stability of water, OER/HER, parasitic reactions as well as the natures of the solid-electrolyte-interface including its chemical composition, morphology, solubility and ionic conductivity.

14307318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307318.value: We assembled LTO//LMO full Li-ion batteries with 21 m LiTFSI and 19.4 m LiTFSI-8.3 m LiBETI electrolytes and performed OEMS test. We detected significant hydrogen gas in the cell with 21 m LiTFSI electrolyte, the low discharge capacities can be attributed to severe water decomposition. Furthermore, the hydrogen gas evolution in 19.4 m LiTFSI-8.3 m LiBETI can explain the results shown in previous study that a lower capacity was achieved at low C-rates (0.2 C, 0.5 C) compared with that at high C-rates (10 C) in hydrate-melt electrolytes owing to water decomposition. The combined results show that the main parasitic reaction in LTO//LMO cell with 21 m LiTFSI and 19.4 m LiTFSI-8.3 m LiBETI is hydrogen evolution reaction, indicating that the cathodic stability of these two highly concentrated LiTFSI aqueous electrolyte is not high enough to support LTO (Part C-1: Nature Materials, 2020, 19, 1006–1011). We also revealed that the LTO has a strong catalytic effect for HER due to the titanate-rich surface. Kinetic suppression of the HER on the catalytic electrode surface is therefore critical to achieve high coulombic efficiency and long cycle life for aqueous Li-ion batteries. In addition, we observed a continuous decay of LMO capacity in aqueous 21m LiTFSI electrolyte, which can be attributed to Mn dissolution of LMO owing to the presence of H+ (ppm level) in the electrolytes. To suppress water decomposition on the electrode surface, we adopted polymer and inorganic coating on the electrode. The LSV result showed that water decomposition could be suppressed due to the hydrophobicity and micro-porosity of polymer layer (Nafion, PVDF, PIM). For inorganic coating, we observed that the amount of the generated H2 gas decreased when applying coatings of LATP, LiAlO2 and Al2O3, and the suppression effect of H2 evolution is the best with LiAlO2 coating (Part C-2: Matter, 2022, 5,1, 162-179). Furthermore, carbon coating is also effective to support excellent rate capability (6.5 mAh cm-2 at 12 mA cm-2) and extraordinary cycling stability (72% capacity retention after 3000 cycles at 4C) for LTP//LMO batteries (Part C-4: Materials Today Energy, 2021, 19, 100570). We analyzed the chemical composition and morphology of SEI in aqueous electrolytes, the combined LSV, OEMS, XPS and TEM results indicate that the formation of a LiF-rich SEI layer is critical to the improved electrochemical stability of aqueous electrolytes (Part C-3: Chemistry of Materials, 2022, 34, 11, 5176–5183).

14307318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307318.value: Future work on improving water-in-salt aqueous electrolytes includes extending the electrochemical stability window to over 4.0 V, increasing ionic conductivity and decreasing the cost as well as the toxicity of the electrolytes with high safety. Several effective modifications should be applied, for instance, add cheap and green co-solvent or additive which could master hydrogen bond interactions, alter SEI composition, and tailor the water reactivity at electrified interfaces from both thermodynamic and kinetics, design more effective coating layer to eliminate water decomposition on the electrode surface. To further verify the safety of the designed aqueous batteries, systematic tests such as flammability test (self-extinguishing time, flash point), thermal analysis (differential scanning calorimetry, accelerating rate calorimeter), abuse test (electrical abuse, thermal abuse, nail penetration) should be combined to exam the safety in the levels of materials, electrolyte/electrode, and battery. In addition, more in-depth mechanistic investigation including both experimental and computational methods (density functional theory calculation, machine learning) should be performed to provide a comprehensive understanding of degradation reaction in the aqueous batteries.

14307318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307318.value: The use of non-flammable aqueous electrolyte is an effective approach to alleviate the safety concerns of the nonaqueous Li-ion batteries. However, the voltage window of aqueous Li-ion batteries is limited by the narrow electrochemical stability of water, which limits the energy density of the aqueous Li-ion batteries. Water-in-salt electrolytes were proposed as a new approach to expand the voltage window of the aqueous Li-ion batteries using highly concentrated salts. However, the mechanism behind the degradation phenomena of water-in-salt system is not yet fully understood. In this project, we investigate the degradation mechanisms in water-in-salt aqueous Li-ion batteries including the parasitic reactions in the highly concentrated LiTFSI aqueous electrolyte, HER catalytic activity and metal dissolution of electrode materials. We also develop polymer and inorganic coating on electrode to further improve the electrochemical stability of the aqueous batteries. This project offers a deeper understanding of the degradation mechanism in the water-in-salt aqueous batteries, and a new path for designing high-voltage, safe and sustainable energy storage system.

14307418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307418.value: Catalytic cross-coupling process has emerged as one of the most straightforward and widespread used protocols for scientists to produce chemical modifications for assembling structurally unprecedented, yet materially and pharmaceutically attractive compounds. Indeed, these methods have revolutionized the way chemists to perform complex organic synthesis. At the center of these synthetic technologies, catalyst development which allows difficult or problematic bond construction process to be proceeded smoothly would be highly attractive. Thus, catalyst exploration and development is particularly central to contemporary catalysis research for innovative organic synthesis. The new development of aromatic bond-construction methodology would advance the current coupling process and put forward of catalysis research. The purpose of this project are (1) to rationally design and explore a new family of tunable phosphine ligands via a facile approach; (2) to investigate the difficult sterically congested coupling process; (3) to establish a ligand-enabled approach for enantioselective cross-couplings and related processes; (4) to investigate the unexplored asymmetric direct C-H bond arylation reactions. This project is expected to explore a new field in cross-coupling reactions. The fundamental knowledge obtained during the course of catalyst development and the rationale of stereocommunication of chiral metal complex to cross coupling partners would be of significant value for academic interest and potential applications. The proposed study is based on our previous success in the ligand/catalyst design and synthesis, and our extensive experiences in aromatic bond-construction research. These new areas will offer us an excellent opportunity in making a substantial advancement to the frontier of catalysis research and may help us to establish a foundation for fine-chemical industry in Hong Kong. 催化交叉偶聯過程已成為科學家最直接和廣泛使用的協議之一，用於生產化學修飾，用於組裝結構上前所未有但具有實質性和藥學吸引力的化合物。實際上，這些方法徹底改變了化學家進行複雜有機合成的方式。在這些合成技術的中心，催化劑開發使得難以或有問題的鍵合構造過程順利進行將是非常有吸引力的。因此，催化劑的勘探和開發對於創新有機合成的當代催化研究尤其重要。 芳香鍵構建方法的新發展將推動當前的耦合過程，並提出催化研究。該項目的目的是（1）通過簡便的方法合理設計和探索新的可調膦配體家族; （2）研究困難的空間擁擠耦合過程; （3）建立配體使能方法，用於對映選擇性交叉偶聯和相關過程; （4）研究未探索的不對稱直接C-H鍵芳基化反應。 該項目有望探索交叉偶聯反應的新領域。在催化劑開發過程中獲得的基礎知識以及手性金屬配合物與交叉偶聯配偶體的立體通信的基本原理對於學術興趣和潛在應用具有重要價值。擬議的研究基於我們之前在配體/催化劑設計和合成方面取得的成功，以及我們在芳香鍵合構建研究方面的豐富經驗。這些新領域將為我們提供一個在催化研究前沿方面取得實質性進展的絕佳機會，並有助於我們為香港的精細化工業奠定基礎。

14307418.label: Realisation of objectives
14307418.value: This is the completion report of the project 14307418-18P. Although we encountered social unrest in late 2019 and COVID-19 since early 2020, we had done our best to carry out the research activities in the project period of 1/1/2019 to 31/12/2021. The proposed project objectives are in the area of new phosphine ligand design and synthesis, as well as the applications of these newly invented ligands in promoting asymmetric cross-coupling and related reactions. During the research period, we had explored straightforward strategies for attaining various phosphine ligands with high diversity and thus structural tunability. In the course of our investigations, we had found new synthetic methods for reaching complex heterocycles, which are useful core-templates for the ligand skeleton. Part of these results were published in SCI-peer-reviewed journals (e.g. Organic Letters, 2020, 22, 4306; Organic Letters, 2020, 22, 7348; Organic Letters, 2021, 23, 6520). Most of these new methods employed organocatalytic pathways, which circumvented the expensive transition metal-catalyzed routes. Particularly noteworthy is that one of our abovementioned findings (Organic Letters, 2020, 22, 7348) showed an innovative strategy for resembling existing Sonogashira and Heck-type cross-coupling of coumarin triflate with nucleophiles, yet can avoid the drawback of these original synthetic pathways. We had developed a new series of axially chiral ligand for enantioselective reactions. In particular, we showed the chiral ligand featuring interesting C-N axial chirality. We indeed overcame the less restricted rotational barrier of aromatic C-N bond, compared with documented aromatic C-C bonds. This interesting C-N axis offered unique transient N-coordination to the metal center, and provided a flexible environment particularly fit for facilitating highly sterically hindered cross-coupling processes (i.e. tetra-ortho-substituted biaryl syntheses). This innovative finding is believed to open a new area of chiral ligand design and synthesis. The aforementioned research contributions was published in high calibre journal, the Journal of the American Chemical Society in mid 2022 (J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2022, 144, 14864). Remarkably, this paper was also highlighted by JACS Spotlights (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 14403). Some of other relevant heterocyclic phosphine ligands were examined in C-H arylation and related cross-coupling under ppm Pd loading as well (Chem. Sci., 2020, 11, 1411 and Eur. J. Org. Chem. 2020, 2846). Overall, even though we had encountered social unrest 2019 and COVID-19, we had accomplished the proposed objectives during the project period successfully. A Ph.D student was also trained.

14307418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307418.value: The major findings of this GRF project (14307418-18P) are described below. Developing new strategies for achieving diversified heterocylces are of high importance in modern synthetic methodology. In this research period, we developed an organocatalytic cascade reaction between propargylamines with environmental friendly water for affording oxygen-heterocycles. This finding is highly versatile for accessing structurally varied flavanone framework, and would be useful for the heterocyclic phosphine ligand synthesis at later stage. This research contribution was published in Organic Letters in 2020 (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 4306). In continuing this promising synthetic transformation investigation, we found that by modifying the starting material from water to pyridinium methylide, we were able to resemble the existing Sonogashira coupling. Particular noteworthy is that this protocol was found compatible to -Br group where the traditional cross-coupling process is inherently not permissible. This achievement was published in Organic Letters in 2020 (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 7348). In addition to oxygen-heterocycles, we found an expeditious metal-free [2+2+1] cyclization process for delivering versatile N,N,N,O-heterocycles. This annulation pathway is versatile and DFT calculation (theoretical study) revealed the early cyclization step is completely different from previous established late-stage cyclization mechanism. This contribution was published in Organic Letters in 2021 (Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6520). With part of the abovementioned synthetic strategies, we embarked the heterocyclic phosphine ligand synthesis. We designed and developed a new collection of chiral ligands bearing unique C-N chiral axis, in which it was sporadically studied because of its intrinsically flexible C-N bond rotation. We overcame the existing challenges and showed the atropisomeric phosphine ligand having C-N axial chirality is highly useful in exceedingly sterically hindered enantioselective cross-coupling. Particularly noteworthy is that this out-of-the-box design offered unique fleeting Pd-N coordination and the Pd-pi-arene-walking. These outcomes allow exceedingly steric hindered coupling to approach the catalyst/metal center in facilitating the reaction. This new concept was published in high calibre journal in 2022 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 14864). Moreover, this finding was also highlighted by JACS Spotlights. With some of the new phosphine entities, we examined their efficacy in C-H arylation process. Part of these results were published in Chemical Science in 2020 (Chem. Sci. 2020, 11, 1411). Moreover, we were able to show the heterocyclic phosphines which can promote the cross-coupling reaction under ppm level of Pd (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 2020, 2846).

14307418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307418.value: There are rich potentials for further development of new catalyst systems in promoting challenging chemical transformations. In view of atropisomeric phosphine bearing C-N axial chirality, this is entirely a new area of investigation, in which it would attract other scientists in field to establish more frontier catalysis using our landmark finding (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 148644). With a collection of catalyst, we are able to fundamentally study the previous problematic reactions, as well as other unprecedented chemical transformations. This potential outcome would be highly beneficial towards an array of pharmaceutical synthesis and aromatic material manufactoring.

14307518.label: Project Objectives
14307518.value: To design, synthesize, and characterize a series of beta-galactosidase-activated BODIPY-based photosensitizers. To study the electronic absorption and photophysical properties, as well as the photostability of these conjugates. The cleavage kinetics induced by beta-galactosidase will also be studied by monitoring the recovery of the fluorescence of and singlet oxygen generation by the distyryl BODIPY unit. To examine the beta-galactosidase-responsive behavior of these photosensitizers in SK-MEL-103 (human melanoma) and WI-38 (human lung fibroblast) cells which have been treated with palbociclib and doxorubicin, respectively, to induce cellular senescence, in terms of fluorescence emission, reactive oxygen species generation, and photocytotoxicity. The results will be compared with those for the corresponding non-senescent cells and in the presence of a competitive beta-galactosidase inhibitor. To extend the study to tumor-bearing nude mice which have been treated with senescence-inducing chemotherapy. The in vivo response of these conjugates, including their time-dependent distribution in the tumor and major organs examined by whole-body fluorescence imaging, and therapeutic efficacy reflected by the ability to inhibit the growth of tumor will be examined and compared with suitable controls.

14307518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307518.value: Aging is the main risk factor for human diseases. It represents the progressive loss of tissue and organ function along with time. It has been revealed that this natural process is closely related to cellular senescence, which is a permanent state of cell cycle arrest induced by disparate stress factors. Apart from not being able to contribute to tissue repair through cell division, the senescent cells disrupt normal tissue function by promoting secretion of a range of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors. Accumulation of senescent cells during the aging process also damages the tissues in which they reside. Hence, selective detection and elimination of senescent cells are crucial in tackling this universal problem from the biomedical perspective. As part of our continued effort in the development of novel and efficient photosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT) of cancer, we propose herein an extension of the studies for selective photodynamic eradication of senescent cells with “smart” photosensitizers. To our knowledge, senotherapy for selective elimination of senescent cells has not yet been applied to humans, and the use of PDT to eliminate senescent cells is virtually unexplored. In this proposal, we plan to design and synthesize a series of boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) based photosensitizers that can be specifically activated by beta-galactosidase, which is a common biomarker of senescence. Although a number of fluorescent probes have been developed for detection of beta-galactosidase activity, selective killing of beta-galactosidase-expressing cells has rarely been reported. We intend to use distyryl BODIPYs as the photosensitizers due to their various desirable features, such as tunable absorption and photophysical properties, ease of chemical modification, and relatively high photostability. These photosensitizing units will be conjugated to a beta-galactosyl substrate and a black hole quencher through a skeleton that can be cleaved by quinone methide chemistry induced by beta-galactosidase. The disassembly will result in restoration of the fluorescence and photosensitizing properties of the distyryl BODIPY units. The beta-galactosidase-responsive behavior of these photosensitizers will then be demonstrated using SK-MEL-103 (human melanoma) and WI-38 (human lung fibroblast) cells which have been treated with the anticancer drugs palbociclib and doxorubicin, respectively, to induce cellular senescence, and with tumor-bearing nude mice treated with senescence-inducing chemotherapy. Finally, the photocytotoxicity of these activatable photosensitizers and their in vivo PDT efficacy in inhibition of the tumor growth will be studied and compared with suitable controls. 衰老是人類疾病的主要危險因素，它代表了組織與器官功能隨著時間的逐漸喪失。經證明，這個自然過程與細胞衰老緊密相關，細胞衰老是由不同的壓力因素誘導產生的細胞週期永久停滯狀態。除了不能通過細胞分裂促進組織修復外，衰老的細胞會通過促進一系列的衰老相關的分泌表型因子的分泌而破壞正常的組織功能。隨著衰老過程累積的衰老細胞還會對它們所處的組織造成傷害。因此，衰老細胞的選擇性檢測與消除對於從生物醫藥角度解決這一普遍問題至關重要。作為我們持續性開發用於癌症的光動力學治療（PDT）的新型且有效的光敏劑的一部分，我們在此提案用“智能”光敏劑選擇性光動力根除衰老細胞作為以上研究的擴展。據我們所知，對於衰老細胞的選擇性消除療法尚未應用於人體，並且PDT對衰老細胞的消除幾乎未被研究。在該提案中，我們計劃設計并合成一系列可被β-半乳糖苷酶特異性激活的硼二吡咯甲烷（BODIPY）光敏劑，其中，β-半乳糖苷酶是衰老的常見生物標誌物。儘管已有許多熒光探針可以用於檢測β-半乳糖苷酶活性，但選擇性殺死表達β-半乳糖苷酶的細胞卻鮮有報道。我們打算使用二苯乙烯基BODIPY作為光敏劑，因為它們具備各種所需的性質，例如可調的吸收和光物理性質，易於化學修飾和相對高的光穩定性。這些光敏單元將通過骨架與β-半乳糖基底物和一個黑洞淬滅劑相連，該骨架可通過β-半乳糖苷酶誘導進行醌甲基化物化學裂解。裂解將導致二苯乙烯基BODIPY單元的熒光和光敏性質的恢復。隨後，將使用分別經抗癌藥物帕博西尼和多柔比星處理過從而誘發細胞衰老的SK-MEL-103（人黑色素瘤）和WI-38（人肺成纖維細胞）細胞以及用衰老誘導化療的荷瘤裸鼠來驗證這些光敏劑的β-半乳糖苷酶反應行為。最後，將研究這些可活化光敏劑的光細胞毒性及其抑制腫瘤生長的體內PDT功效，並與合適的對照進行比較。

14307518.label: Realisation of objectives
14307518.value: This project aims to develop a series of β-galactosidase-activated photosensitizers that can be used for selective photodynamic eradication of senescent cells. As galactose is the substrate of β-galactosidase, to establish the chemistry of this monosaccharide, we first prepared a series of di-α-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanines with different number of galactose moieties, ranging from 1 to 8, namely Pc-Galn (n = 1, 2, 4, and 8) (ChemPlusChem doi.org/10.1002/cplu.e202200285, which has been selected as the Front Cover of an upcoming issue; see the Cover Profile at doi.org/10.1002/cplu.e202200406). These galactosyl phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers were purified by repeated precipitation followed by reverse-phase liquid chromatography (HPLC) and characterized with various spectroscopic methods. After this pilot study, we designed and synthesized a β-galactosidase-responsive photosensitizer through a convergent approach. It contained a galactosyl substrate, a boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY)-based photosensitizing unit, and a black hole quencher 2 (BHQ-2) connected via an AB2-type self-immolative linker (Chem. Commun. Submitted). Owing to the close proximity of the BODIPY and BHQ-2 moieties and the large spectral overlap between the fluorescence emission of the former and the absorption of the latter, which favors the fluorescence resonance energy transfer, this compound (labeled as Gal-BODIPY-BHQ2) was largely quenched in the native form. In the presence of β-galactosidase, the glycosidic bond was cleaved, which subsequently triggered the self-immolation via the quinone-methide elimination. The separation of the BODIPY and BHQ-2 moieties led to restoration of the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen production of the BODIPY unit. To extend this study further, we replaced the BODIPY and BHQ-2 moieties with two zinc(II) phthalocyanine units, which were also connected to a galactose group via the same AB2-type self-immolative linker (Biomater. Sci. To be submitted). To exaggerate the self-quenching effect, this compound (labeled as Gal-dZnPc) was self-assembled in water with 2.5% dimethylsulfoxide (v/v), forming a β-galactosidase-responsive nanophotosensitizer (labeled as Gal-dZnPc NP) with a hydrodynamic diameter of 67.9 ± 4.8 nm as determined by dynamic light scattering. In addition, we also prepared another smart photosensitizer in which a pyridinium diiodo BODIPY was connected to a galactose group via a self-immolative linker. Similarly, this compound (labeled as Gal-PyBODIPY) was quenched by photoinduced electron transfer to the pyridinium group and could release a photodynamically active pyridyl BODIPY after hydrolysis by β-galactosidase (manuscript in preparation). With all these β-galactosidase-activated photosensitizers, the first objective was deemed to be fully achieved. The electronic absorption and fluorescence spectra of all these compounds were recorded in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), water, and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) (pH = 7.4). For the molecular photosensitizers, Tween 80 (0.1% v/v) was also added to the aqueous media to increase their water solubility. In addition, their singlet oxygen generation efficiency upon light irradiation was also studied by a steady-state spectroscopic method using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as a singlet oxygen scavenger. During the irradiation, these photosensitizers were found to be stable. For Gal-dZnPc NP, its stability in water and culture medium was also examined by monitoring the change in hydrodynamic diameter over a period of 5 days and 24 h, respectively. The activation effect of β-galactosidase was first studied by monitoring the change in fluorescence spectra of these photosensitizers (1-2 μM) in the presence of this enzyme (10 unit mL-1) along with time and in different concentrations of this enzyme (0 to 10 unit mL-1). To further examine the specificity of the activation, the fluorescence spectra of Gal-BODIPY-BHQ2 and Gal-PyBODIPY were recorded in the presence of various biologically interfering species and compared with those in the presence of β-galactosidase. In addition, the restoration in singlet oxygen generation by β-galactosidase was also studied for all the photosensitizers using DPBF as the probe. Therefore, the second objective was also accomplished. For the in vitro studies, we first determined the intrinsic β-galactosidase levels of a range of cell lines using the commercial fluorogenic probe C12FDG. As a positive control, the well-known β-galactosidase-overexpressing OVCAR-3 human ovarian carcinoma cells were used for comparison. It was found that HeLa human cervical cancer cells and HT29 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells showed negligible β-galactosidase inside the cells and therefore they were suitable candidates to induce cellular senescence. According to a previously described procedure, the cells were treated with different concentrations of doxorubicin for 72 h, followed by incubation in a doxorubicin-free medium for further 24 h. The induced cellular senescence was evaluated by a X-Gal assay for monitoring the increased β-galactosidase activity. After optimization, it was found that 50 and 25 nM of doxorubicin was sufficient to induce significant cellular senescence for HeLa and HepG2 cells, respectively. After the establishment of these senescent cellular models, we first studied the activation in fluorescence emission of these photosensitizers in these senescent cells under different incubation conditions, using the native cells for comparison. By using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, the extent of activation was monitored, quantified, and optimized. The subcellular localization of Gal-dZnPc NP and Gal-PyBODIPY was also examined using confocal microscopy. Apart from the fluorescence restoration, the recovery of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation of these two photosensitizers in senescent HeLa cells was also investigated using 2’,7’-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate and the CellROX Deep Red Reagent, respectively, as the ROS probe to match their spectroscopic features. In addition, the activation in photocytotoxicity of all the photosensitizers in senescent cells was also investigated. In this study, the cells were treated with different concentrations of the photosensitizers both with and without light irradiation, and then the cell viabilities were determined and compared using the CellTiter-Glo luminescent cell viability assay or annexin V-red fluorescent protein (for Gal-BODIPY-BHQ2) for detecting the extent of cell apoptosis. Again, the results were compared with those for the native cells. Apart from these senescent cellular models, in collaboration with the research group of Prof. Ramón Martínez-Máñez of Universitat Politècnica de València, we also used the senescent SK-MEL-103 (human melanoma) cells obtained by treating the native cells with palbociclib to study the β-galactosidase-responsive properties of Gal-PyBODIPY. The activation in intracellular and subcellular fluorescence emission, ROS generation, and photocytotoxicity, as well as the cell death mechanism were also investigated. All these studies showed that the third objective was also achieved. The last objective of this project is to extend the study to senescent tumor-bearing mice. This part of study is also in collaboration with Prof. Martínez-Máñez as his group has extensive experience in senescent animal models and the related studies. Unfortunately, there was delay in this study due to various reasons, including the COVID-19 pandemic. Nevertheless, we successfully established the animal model by treating the SK-MEL-103 tumor-bearing mice with palbociclib and performed an initial study of the in vivo response of Gal-PyBODIPY. In this study, Gal-PyBODIPY was injected intravenously into the mice. After 2 h, the tumor was irradiated with a laser operated at 1 W cm-2 for 5 min. This treatment was performed twice a week for a total of 21 days. The tumor volume was monitored during the course of the treatment. Although we were not able to see differences between the palbociclib (or senescent) group and the palbociclib group treated with Gal-PyBODIPY (plus laser irradiation), we could clearly detect the BODIPY-associated fluorescence in the tumor sections of the mice being treated with Gal-PyBODIPY. The intensity was significantly higher for the mice pre-treated with palbociclib, showing that the compound could also be activated in vivo.

14307518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307518.value: A series of galactosyl photosensitizers were designed and synthesized, including a series of di-α-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanines with 1, 2, 4 or 8 galactose moieties [Pc-Galn (n = 1, 2, 4, and 8)], a diiodo BODIPY conjugated with a galactose group and a BHQ-2 moiety via an AB2-type self-immolative linker (Gal-BODIPY-BHQ2), a bis(phthalocyanine) system connected to a galactose moiety via the same linker (Gal-dZnPc), and another diiodo BODIPY substituted with a meso pyridinium group connected to a galactose unit via a self-immolative linker (Gal-PyBODIPY). These compounds were fully characterized with various spectroscopic methods and/or HPLC analysis. Their spectroscopic and photophysical properties, including fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation, were studied in DMF, water, and PBS (pH = 7.4). With an amphiphilic character, Gal-dZnPc could self-assemble in water forming stable nanoparticles with a hydrodynamic diameter of 67.9 ± 4.8 nm. This nanosystem and the molecular photosensitizers Gal-BODIPY-BHQ2 and Gal-PyBODIPY were also quenched in their photoactivities in the native state by various mechanisms. Upon interactions with β-galactosidase, the galactosyl substrate of these compounds was detached, which subsequently triggered the self-immolation via the quinone-methide elimination and the release of an activated form of the photosensitizers, thereby restoring the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation. The activation effects of β-galactosidase were first demonstrated in aqueous media spectroscopically. The specificity of the activation was also revealed using a range of biologically interfering species. The results showed that only β-galactosidase could activate the fluorescence emission of the photosensitizers, while all the species being studied could not induce a significant change in the fluorescence intensity. Hence, these three photosensitizing systems are β-galactosidase-responsive and are promising candidates for photodynamic eradication of senescent cells. To reveal their potential for this application, several senescent cell models were first established, which included the doxorubicin-treated HeLa and HT29 cells, as well as the palbociclib-treated SK-MEL-103 cells. The elevated β-galactosidase levels after the chemotherapeutic treatment were confirmed by a X-Gal assay and the fluorogenic probe C12FDG. These senescent cells were then used to examine the activation of the three photosensitizing systems by senescence-associated β-galactosidase. It was found that all the photosensitizers could be activated remarkably inside the senescent cells in terms of fluorescence emission, ROS generation, and photocytotoxicity. By using SK-MEL-103 tumor-bearing mice pre-treated with palbociclib, we could demonstrate that Gal-PyBODIPY could also be activated in the tumor. Based on these studies, one paper in ChemPlusChem (with a Front Cover and a Cover Profile) has been published online, one paper has been submitted to Chem. Commun., and two other papers are now in preparation.

14307518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307518.value: This research project involves the design and synthesis of novel photosensitizers that can be activated selectively by senescence-associated β-galactosidase and the use of this unique biomarker to trigger the photodynamic action of these smart photosensitizers for elimination of these cells. To date, a number of fluorescent probes have been developed for detection of β-galactosidase activity. In contrast, only a few β-galactosidase-activated prodrugs have been reported for eradication of senescent cells. To the best of our knowledge, elimination of senescent cells by photodynamic therapy is virtually unexplored, and only one methylene blue-based photosensitizer has been reported for this application during the course of this study (Lee et al. RSC Adv. 2022, 12, 4543-4549 and Yang et al. Anal. Chem. 2022, 94, 5425-5431). Hence, there is much room for further development in this field, including the design of more advanced β-galactosidase-activated photosensitizers, the development of more efficient synthetic methodologies to these compounds, the establishment of improved senescent cellular and animal models that can facilitate the biological studies, and the extension of the application to other senescent objects, etc. It is believed that this new application of photodynamic therapy will attract more attention in the time to come.

14307518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307518.value: Aging is a major risk factor for human diseases. It represents the progressive loss of tissue and organ function along with time. It has been revealed that this natural process is closely related to cellular senescence, which is a permanent state of cell cycle arrest induced by disparate stress factors. Apart from not being able to contribute to tissue repair through cell division, the senescent cells disrupt normal tissue function by promoting secretion of a range of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors. Accumulation of senescent cells during the aging process also damages the tissues in which they reside. Hence, selective detection and elimination of senescent cells are crucial in tackling this universal problem. In this research project, we have designed, synthesized, and characterized a series of photosensitizers that can be selectively activated by β-galactosidase, which is the most common senescence biomarker. By using different controls, we have demonstrated the remarkable activation in fluorescence emission, reactive oxygen species generation, and photocytotoxicity of these photosensitizers in senescent cells. The overall results show that these tailor-made compounds can serve as promising therapeutic agents for photodynamic elimination of senescent cells, which are virtually unexplored.

14307718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307718.value: The proposed research aims to investigate the effect of CO2 adsorption on carbon gasification in dry reforming of methane, an important factor combating catalyst deactivation due to carbon deposition. Dry reforming of methane, or carbon dioxide reforming of methane, has received much attention worldwide for its promising potential to convert two greenhouse gases (CH4 and CO2) to valuable fuels or feedstock for producing valuable chemicals. Ni-based catalysts are most commonly used, and the biggest problem is catalyst deactivation due to carbon deposition. Extensive efforts have been devoted to understanding the carbon formation mechanism and to developing catalyst formulations that mitigate catalyst deactivation. In this project, we will develop robust Ni catalysts to mitigate carbon deposition by addressing a key surface reaction, carbon gasification, which removes carbon atoms that have been generated in CH4 dissociation. Little attention has been paid to CO2 adsorption, which provides the oxidant for carbon gasification. Our approach is to use a CO2 adsorbent to enhance CO2 adsorption so that an adequate amount of CO2 is available for the carbon gasification. The main research goals are to identify a suitable catalyst support from known high-temperature CO2 adsorbents; and to determine catalyst deactivation mechanisms by various characterization techniques. The knowledge obtained from the deactivation mechanistic study will be used to guide the synthesis of dry reforming catalysts. If successful, it will help to develop completely different catalyst formulations for highly carbon-resistant Ni catalysts to overcome one of the major technical barriers for dry reforming of methane. 甲烷的幹重整指的是甲烷和二氧化碳相互作用生成合成氣（氫氣、一氧化碳混合氣）的反應，該反應令人關註是因為它將兩種溫室氣體轉化為燃料或用於生產有價值化學品的原料。該反應需要催化劑，其中最常用的是Ni基催化劑，目前該反應最大的問題是由於碳沈積導致的催化劑失活。本領域的研究主要集中於理解碳形成機理和開發減輕催化劑失活的配方。碳沈積是受碳生成和碳氣化共同影響，不像碳形成，本領域對於碳氣化的研究非常少。本項目的研究重點在二氧化碳吸附對甲烷幹重整過程中催化劑失活的影響，原因是二氧化碳吸附是碳氣化的第一步。我們的思路是使用二氧化碳吸附劑來作為催化劑的載體以增強二氧化碳的吸附，希望可以為碳氣化提供足夠量的二氧化碳從而減少碳沈積。主要的研究方法是從已知的高溫二氧化碳吸附劑裏篩選出合適的催化劑載體，並通過各種表征技術確定催化劑失活機理，這些機理研究反過來可以指導幹重整催化劑的合成。如果項目成功的話，它將有助於開發出高耐碳的Ni基催化劑從而克服甲烷幹重整技術的一個主要障礙。

14308018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308018.value: Hydrogen is an environmentally attractive fuel because it has very high energy density and it does not cause global warming. However, sustainable methods for hydrogen production must be developed for H2 to replace the traditional fossil fuels. Solar-driven photocatalytic H2 formation from water splitting seems to be a promising approach. The major problem with this approach is the need of an efficient photocatalyst to drive the water splitting reaction. A number of photocatalysts including TiO2, CdS, Ta3N5 and g-C3N4 have been studied extensively. Among them, CdS is one of the most promising candidates for solar-driven hydrogen evolution due to its excellent visible light response and narrow band gap. However, CdS undergoes photocorrosion easily and suffers from a fast charge recombination. This project will develop novel CdS-based photocatalysts to overcome these problems. The new photocatalyst will be based on a hollow CdS structure. Hollow structures promise high flexibility for the material design, and many co-catalysts can be added onto the inner and/or outer surfaces. These arrangements should protect CdS from photocorrosion and it would also enhance charge separation. Metallic species will be used as co-catalysts to improve the photocatalytic performance of CdS. This project aims to prepare different kinds of ultrasmall metallic nanoparticles confined within hollow CdS by ligand-stabilized and hard-template approaches for highly-efficient H2 evolution in photocatalytic water splitting. Moreover, we will also explore multi-component hollow CdS catalysts with spatially separated reduction and oxidation surfaces including metal@CdS@metal sulfide, metal@CdS@metal phosphide, and metal@CdS@metal nitride. Highly active photocatalysts with more efficient electron migration and better charge recombination will be realized. We believe that our research will not only open new perspective for the controllable synthesis of hybrid metallic species-containing CdS with hollow structure, spatially separated surfaces, and superior photocatalytic H2 evolution performance, but also provide some guidance for the fabricating of other hybrid hollow photocatalysts. 氫氣是一種極具吸引力的環境友好型的燃料，因為它具有很高的能量密度，且不會引起全球變暖。然而，開發出更多的可持續制氫方法，用以取代傳統的化石燃料是一項非常重要的課題。太陽能驅動的光催化水裂解制氫是一種極具前途的方法。光催化水裂解制氫面臨的最主要問題是開發並製備高效的光催化劑。目前，包括TiO2、CdS、Ta3N5及g-C3N4在內的許多光催化劑已經得到了廣泛的研究，其中CdS以其優異的可見光回應和較窄的帶隙結構，成為最具吸引力的太陽能驅動光催化水裂解制氫的催化劑之一。然而，CdS催化劑在光催化過程中很容易發生光腐蝕，且極易發生光生電子和空穴的快速複合。本課題擬開發新型的CdS基光催化劑來克服上述問題。擬製備的新型CdS光催化劑具有中空結構。具有空心結構的催化劑在材料設計方面具有很高的靈活性，在其內部和(或)外表面可以引入許多助催化劑。這些設計既可以保護CdS催化劑抵禦光腐蝕，又可以增強電荷分離。通常情況下，金屬物種是做常用的助催化劑，用以提升CdS的光催化性能。本專案旨在通過配體保護法和硬質範本法，在中空CdS催化劑上擔載各種超小的金屬納米粒子助催化劑，以提升其太陽能驅動的光催化水裂解制氫性能。此外，我們還將探索具有空間分離還原和氧化表面的多組分空心CdS催化劑，其中包括金屬@CdS@金屬硫化物、金屬@CdS@金屬磷化物、及金屬@CdS@金屬氮化物，實現製備具有更高效電子遷移和更好電荷複合的高活性光催化劑。我們相信，我們的研究將不僅為可控合成具有雜化金屬助催化劑、空間分離表面和優異的光催化析氫性能的中空CdS光催化劑開闢新的前景，也為製備其他具有空心雜化結構光催化劑提供了一定的指導。

14308018.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308018.value: A novel hollow porous CdS photocatalyst with effectively restrained electron–hole recombination was developed with this funding. By using microporous zeolites as a host and a hard template, ultrasmall Pd and PdS nanoparticles can be anchored separately onto the inner and outer surfaces of a hollow CdS structure. The metallic Pd pulls the photoexcited electrons away from CdS while PdS pushes the holes for more thorough oxidation of the sacrificial agent. The final Pd@CdS/PdS product exhibits superior visible-light-driven photocatalytic H2 evolution rate of up to 144.8 mmol h−1 g−1. This is among the highest values of all the reported CdS-based catalysts. The CdS material is found to be biocompatible, and it can be coated on the living cell surface of a versatile photoheterotrophic bacterium, Rhodopseudomonas palustris. The photo-induced electrons from the CdS NPs significantly improve the biological nitrogen fixation in pure cultures of R. palustris. The biohybrid cells continuously fix N2 when sufficient N is available, thus revealing excessive reducing power. The Calvin cycle also contributes 28.1% to the additional solid biomass in the presence of available CO2. The CdS-coated photoheterotrophic cells exhibit excellent practical feasibility with an industrial waste carbon source under a solar/dark cycle. The idea of spatially separated reduction and oxidation surfaces was also used in the design of high-performance electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). It is by introducing cerium into Co3O4. This electrode requires a much lower overpotential than that of Co3O4 nanosheets to reach a current density of 100 mA cm−2, and it is stable for at least 100 h with high intrinsic activity. The structure becomes partially disordered after Ce doping, thus exposing more active sites. Photocatalytic oxygen reduction is a potentially sustainable route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). By optimizing the charge separation and polarization, a covalent organic framework (COF)-based photocatalyst has been developed. It can reduce O2 to H2O2 efficiently in pure water under visible-light irradiation is reported. A solar-to-chemical conversion of 0.76% is achieved for H2O2 generation. More importantly, the hydrophobic and mesoporous properties of triphenylbenzene-dimethoxyterephthaldehyde-COF allow the formation of a triphase interface (gas–liquid–solid) when loading this catalyst onto a porous substrate. The H2O2 production rate reaches ≈2.9 mmol gcat−1 h−1 at the triphase interface by overcoming the mass-transfer limitation of O2 in water. The triphenylbenzene part is identified as the reactive site based on theoretical calculations.

14308018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308018.value: This synthetic approach may be used to fabricate other highly efficient catalysts with spatially separated cocatalysts. The CdS-containing hybrid cells may provide a facile and expandable strategy for future studies of visible-light-driven ambient N2 fixation and even advanced systems for solar-to-chemical conversion.

14308018.value: Photocatalysis is an emerging technology for clean energy production. In this project, catalysts with great potential have been prepared for solar-induced formation of hydrogen, oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. Ideas from this investigation would be useful for future development of other sunlight driven chemical conversion systems.

14308218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14308218.value: 高維時間序列多重變點的統計推斷

14308218.label: Project Objectives
14308218.value: The main objective of the proposed study is to develop useful statistical methodologies for the change-point analysis of high-dimensional piecewise stationary time series. In particular, by casting the piecewise stationary model in a high-dimensional regression context, we propose to apply a new technique, known as group orthogonal greedy algorithm (GOGA) developed in the machine learning literature, to identify and analyze the genuine change-points for these high-dimensional time series. The second important goal is to develop the so-called oracle properties of the proposed technique. It is well known that many high-dimensional regression methods, such as the celebrated LASSO, SCAD, MCP or OGA enjoy certain optimality (oracle) properties under the independent settings. Many of these properties, however, remain to be determined for serially correlated data, let alone piecewise stationary data. To further understand these properties in a high-dimensional setting, subtle asymptotic techniques to analyze the underlying structure are required so that both local and global oracle properties can be assessed. As the asymptotic results involve evaluating subtle probability bounds for the underlying structure, we aim to develop efficient algorithms to compute these bounds in real time. Using the asymptotic results established in the proposed study, we will develop efficient numerical procedures that can be applied empirically. Risk management is a rapidly developing discipline. Because practitioners are constantly faced with the challenge of handling multiple abrupt changes, it is of crucial importance to develop efficient statistical procedures to identify the genuine change-points and filter out apparent change-points that are artifacts of cross serial dependence. Successful completion of this project will lead to a deeper understanding of the underlying change-points, which in turn will enhance the applicability of high-dimensional time series to risk management and other disciplines.

14308218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308218.value: The recent surge of activity in health and risk management has led to a huge demand for non-standard statistical procedures to be developed for the modeling of piecewise stationary and non-regular time series. It is now generally accepted that the dynamic nature of diverse physical and financial phenomena requires one to take into account the ever-changing piecewise stationary and abrupt change behavior. During the past decade, a cascade of theoretical research on the inference for high-dimensional regression problems has been developed. It was found that many of the standard tools for low-dimensional problems are not applicable and that there is a need to develop new ideas to deal with the challenges of high-dimensional data. In particular, the idea of penalized least squares method and its variants play a central role in this new endeavor from which certain optimal (oracle) properties are derived. The corresponding counter part of these problems for serially correlated data, however, remains to be a challenge. With the concerted efforts of many scholars, it is now high time to study high-dimensional time series regression in order to offer a more comprehensive treatment of the penalized optimization criterion. One major objective of the proposed study is to pursue a comprehensive treatment of these results for the change-points problem of high-dimensional time series. Establishing an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional time series only constitutes the first stage in statistical inference. To further understand the procedure, one also needs to consider the underlying optimality (oracle) properties of the algorithm. Recently, Chan, Yau and Zhang (2014) proposed to cast the change-point detection problem for piecewise stationary time series into a high-dimensional regression context, from which LASSO type procedure can then be applied to identify and estimate the underlying change points. The second objective of this study is to extend this idea to high-dimensional time series in which genuine and apparent change-points exist. Specifically, we intend to pursue using the idea of GOGA to develop a fast and effective on-line estimation procedure for multiple change-points of a high dimensional time series. This result will be studied not only for the finite-dimensional situation, but also for the big-data scenario, that is, small $n$ and big $p$ situation where the dimension of the time series increases with the sample size. Such a research will be of interest not only to statisticians, but also to practitioners who need to handle high-dimensional multiple change-point problems.

14308218.label: Realisation of objectives
14308218.value: The main research objectives of this proposal have been realized. New statistical techniques for high-dimensional change-points estimations and their related properties have been established. These methodologies include GOGA techniques for piecewise stationary time series as well as high-dimensional time series. Consistency and asymptotic results related to oracle properties have been obtained. The findings of this project cover a wide scope of statistical inference for change-points problems encountered in high-dimensional piecewise stationary time series. Together they cover objectives 1-3 to a large extent. In the course of these findings, new numerical procedures have to be developed and some of these methods have been reported in the relevant publications, which addresses objective 4.

14308218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308218.value: The major finding of this proposal is to employ group orthogonal greedy algorithm (GOGA) techniques to conduct statistical inference for chang-points problems for high-dimensional piecewise stationary time series models. In particular, by making use of the GOGA, consistency and oracle properties of the estimates are established. Further, by means of a high-dimensional regression framework, new techniques about inference of change-point for piecewise stationary time series were established. Numerical methods have also been developed in the course of this project to handle the convergence properties and the nested GOGA techniques. The collected research outcomes not only offer an novel method to analyze change-point of high-dimensional time series, but also provide a new method to estimate thresholds in non-linear time series. Important research findings from this project were reported in major international conferences and published in premiere refereed journals, as stipulated in Part C: Tables 8 and 9.

14308218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308218.value: As GOGA techniques are high-dimensional in nature, the results obtained in this proposal can be used in many other contexts. In particular, by introducing the idea nested GOGA, results from this project offer a novel way to analyze high-dimensional time series with change-points, which is of huge potential interest in financial risk management. The techniques developed in this project can be applied both to linear and non-linear time series. Further, by combining with a high-dimensional regression framework, this project offers new insight into the inference not only for the change-points themselves, but also for revealing structural changes in piecewise stationary time series. In summary, with the established theoretical properties of the change-points estimates, the pursuit of high-dimensional time series will be greatly enhanced. In areas such as financial risk management and network engineering, where change-points in high-dimensional situations are rules rather than exceptions, results of this project offer a viable means to handle structural changes that often occur in finance and economics.

14308218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14308218.value: All of the major objectives have been realized in this project. By virtue of the GOGA techniques, advances in model estimation and calibration of change-points can now be efficiently conducted. This will bring significant impacts in modeling important features not only for a single time series, but also for several series jointly such as in the case of portfolio management and network traffic, where the joint effects of different assets have to be taken into account. In particular, the four objectives achieved in this proposal offer a platform and new direction that will lead to important advances in the pursuit of modeling high-dimensional multivariate financial data. Finally, by publishing relevant papers in statistics as indicated in objective four, important research developments can be disseminated to practitioners timely and effectively.
