14502718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502718.value: Evaluating China’s economic performance by official statistics is often open to question. The controversy begins with the quality of the basic statistics such as GDP. The problem becomes much more serious when it comes to regional statistics. One famous example is that the real GDP growth rate averaged across provinces is always above the national rate by two to three percentage points. An equally disturbing (if not more) but less well-known case is investment data. According to the national statistics, China’s investment (fixed capital formation) accounts for roughly 43% of its GDP from 2005 to 2015. In contrast, the sum of provincial fixed capital formation is about 54% of GDP, 11 percentage points higher than the national statistics. On the one hand, these statistical discrepancies reflect the tensions between local governments that are incentivized to over-report local economic growth and the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS henceforth) that is held accountable for data quality at the national level. On the other hand, it is also clear that NBS does not correct regional statistics to the extent that they are consistent with their national counterparts. This is detrimental to academic and policy research on regional issues in China: Even the basic statistics are likely to be manipulated or even fabricated. This project aims to achieve three goals. Using publicly available data, we will develop a few accounting restrictions to identify the potential biases in the regional investment statistics. Our preliminary study suggests that at least a third of fixed asset investment (the primary data source for NBS to calculate fixed capital formation) is fabricated by exaggerating construction and installation. Second, based on the accounting restrictions, we propose three approaches to re-measure fixed asset investment and regional fixed capital formation. The first is to use publicly available data, while the other two approaches will explore the confidential micro-level datasets at China’s State Administration of Taxation (SAT henceforth). We will have access to the datasets through the institutional collaborations among CUHK, Tsinghua, NBS and SAT. Finally, we will apply the corrected statistics to re-estimate China’s regional TFP growth and the degree of resource misallocation at the regional level. Some preliminary studies show that under-developed regions tend to manipulate data more than what rich regions would do. An immediate implication is that we would have to adjust upwards TFP growth for under-developed regions and downwards the degree of capital misallocation across regions. 中國官方經濟資料存在一些嚴重問題。本項研究旨在重新測算中國地區的投資資料。我們將使用多方面的微觀和宏觀資料對官方資料進行系統的評估和調整。

14502718.label: Realisation of objectives
14502718.value: Objective 1: Identifying manipulation and fabrication in China's regional investment statistics The main output of this project is “A Forensic Examination of China’s National Accounts”, published by Brookings Papers on Economic Activities in 2019. While the paper was motivated and funded by the project, it goes well beyond the scope of the project by investigating not only regional investment statistics, but also all the major statistics in China’s national accounts, including potential manipulation and fabrication on GDP and consumption data. In the paper, we check which of the numbers provided by local governments are more likely to be inaccurate. First, we show that the sum of local GDP frequently exceeds national GDP. Second, we compare the sum of the local consumption, investment, and net exports with national consumption, investment and net exports reported by the National Bureau of Statistics. We find little discrepancy between local and national consumption, but find a large discrepancy between local and national statistics of investment and net exports. Third, we compare the sum of value-added of sectors as reported at the local level with the same sectors at the national level. We find large discrepancies for the industrial sector and smaller gaps in the non-industrial sectors. Objective 2: Using three different approaches to remeasure China's regional investment statistics We use different approaches to determine the accuracy of adjustments to the local numbers by the NBS. First, we adjust national GDP by the difference between value added growth reported by NBS and value added tax revenue growth reported by the State Administration of Taxation in the sectors where value added tax is a major type of taxation. Our estimate suggests that the adjustments made by the National Bureau of Statistics were roughly accurate until 2007/8. However, the adjustments made after this date no longer appear to be accurate. Our baseline estimate of GDP growth from 2008 to 2016 is 1.7 percentage points lower than the official growth rate. Furthermore, our estimate of the aggregate investment and savings rate in 2016 is 7 percentage points lower than the official numbers. We use the same approach to adjust local production and expenditure GDP for each Chinese province. There is a strong positive relation between our adjustments to local GDP and investment across provinces, with a correlation of 0.61. This evidence suggests that local governments inflate local GDP by overestimating local production as well as local investment. An alternative approach is to estimate a statistical model where we estimate the relationship between a set of economic indicators (which are less likely to be manipulated) and local GDP prior to 2008. We then use parameters of the estimated model along with the same set of the indicators after 2008 to predict local GDP after 2008. The indicators include satellite night lights, national tax revenue, electricity consumption, railway cargo flow, exports and imports. We use the method developed by Su, Shi and Phillips (2016) to control for (hidden) economic structure heterogeneities across regions. Using this method, we also find that the corrections made to national GDP no longer appear appropriate after 2008. Objective 3: Exploring novel micro-level data at China's National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and China's State Administration of Taxation (SAT) and building a bridge to connect NBS and SAT to take full advantage of the extraordinarily rich micro-level data in both institutions We document that the NBS has access to the micro-data of the surveys used by local governments and supplements this data with economic censuses and administrative data such as land sales, vehicle registration and foreign trade. On the former, for example, NBS conducted a census of industrial firms in 1995 and censuses of all firms (in all sectors) in 2004, 2008, 2013, and 2018 (although the latter has not yet been processed). Based on this data, it adjusts the reports by local governments to arrive at a number for national GDP and its components on the production and expenditure sides. The main data that NBS uses for industrial firms is ASIF (Annual Survey on Industrial Firms), which only provides information for above-scale firms. For below-scale firms and the self-employed, the local statistical bureaus and the NBS rely on survey of these two types of establishments. Another way to gauge whether the accuracy of the NBS’ estimate of industrial GDP is to use information on revenues from value added taxes on industrial firms. China imposes a 17% value added tax on essentially all industrial firms. The State Administration of Taxation (SAT) implemented the so-called “Golden Taxation Project” since 1994, making tax fraud and evasion difficult. We find that the growth rate of revenues from value-added taxes exceeds that of industrial GDP prior to the mid-2000s, consistent with the improved enforcement of value-added taxes. However, after 2007, the growth rate of tax revenues is lower than the growth rate of industrial GDP. Furthermore, the gap has been widening over time. In 2010 to 2012, for instance, value added tax revenue growth is about two-thirds that of industrial GDP. The growth in tax revenues dropped to half the growth rate of industrial GDP growth in 2013 and 2014 and even became negative for 2015 and 2016. Objective 4: Re-estimation China's regional TFP growth, capital returns and misallocation China’s real GDP Growth: The annual real GDP growth was overstated by 2 percentage points between 2008 and 2016. The official real GDP is 16% above our estimate in 2016. China’s capital returns: While our estimated capital returns are about one to two percentage points higher than those using official data, the dramatic decline in aggregate returns to capital in the post-2007 period turns out to be a robust phenomenon. China’s TFP growth: The aggregate TFP growth rates by our estimates appear to be more volatile than those by official data. Yet, it remains obvious that China’s aggregate TFP growth slowed down substantially after 2007. China’s Debt-GDP ratio: The debt to GDP ratio with our revised estimate of nominal GDP. The bottom line is that our revised numbers suggest that the debt to GDP ratio has increased by more than suggested by the official numbers. Our estimate of the debt to GDP ratio in 2016 is 2.4 – the official number is 2.1. All the regional statistics are reported in our online appendix.

14502718.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502718.value: The possibility that local governments misreport local GDP is well known, and the Central Government’s National Bureau of Statistics adjusts the numbers reported by local governments. Prior to 2003, the NBS adjusted upwards local GDP but after 2003, the NBS adjusted local GDP downwards. However, our estimates suggest that the extent by which local governments exaggerate local GDP accelerated after 2008, but the magnitude of the adjustment by the NBS did not change in tandem. As a consequence, our best estimate is that the true growth rate of GDP is probably overstated by almost 2 percentage points from 2008 to 2016. "A Forensic Examination of China’s National Accounts" (coauthored with Xilu Chen, Wei Chen and Chang-Tai Hsieh), published by Brookings Papers on Economic Activities, Spring 2019, 77-127. 14502718.value: The impact of this study is obvious. We expect our corrected statistics on China’s national accounts to be leading indices in academic and policy research for years to come.

14502718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502718.value: China’s national accounts are based on data collected by local governments. However, since local governments are rewarded for meeting growth and investment targets, they have an incentive to skew local statistics. China’s National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) adjusts the data provided by local governments to calculate GDP at the national level. The adjustments made by the NBS average 5% of GDP since the mid-2000s. On the production side, the discrepancy between local and aggregate GDP is entirely driven by the gap between local and national estimates of industrial output. On the expenditure side, the gap is in investment. Local statistics increasingly misrepresent the true numbers after 2008, but there was no corresponding change in the adjustment made by the NBS. Using publicly available data, we provide revised estimates of local and national GDP by re-estimating output of industrial, construction, wholesale and retail firms using data on value-added taxes. We also use several local economic indicators that are less likely to be manipulated by local governments to estimate local and aggregate GDP. The estimates also suggest that the adjustments by the NBS were insufficient after 2008. Relative to the official numbers, we estimate that GDP growth from 2008-2016 is 1.7 percentage points lower and the investment and savings rate in 2016 is 7 percentage points lower.

14503018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503018.value: Young people in many countries work less now than at any time in the history. While rising rates of college going at non-selective institutions explains some portion of the increase, a rising share of young workers is idle, disconnected from school and the labor force. In sum, labor market entry appears to be increasingly difficult for workers on the employment margin. This project studies the role of post-secondary education and community college policies in helping young workers threatened by idleness through the process of labor market entry. To conduct the analysis, we estimate a model of labor market transitions that allow for observed and unobserved individual-specific characteristics. These individual characteristics affect the probability of status changes, such as school to work or work to being idle. The model delivers estimates of state dependence (the probability that a given person remains in a labor market state once they enter it), stepping stone effects (the usefulness of a labor market state, such as going to community college, in helping workers transition to other states, such as employment), and individual-specific heterogeneity. Once estimated, we can use the model to perform counterfactual simulations to examine the effect of unemployment and policies to combat idleness. We begin by asking whether young workers experience an ``idleness trap'' when they spend extended periods of time out of work and school. This analysis follows on previous work examining traps in unemployment, poor health, and drug use. As the model accounts for individual heterogeneity, our finding will tell whether idleness mostly reflects bad luck or laziness, which has profound implications for labor policies. We then turn to the role of rising rates of college attendance at the community college. Community colleges are important, both because of the trend towards the replacement of employment with attendance at these institutions, but also because enrollment barriers are modest. We use our model of labor market transitions to investigate whether enrollment at community colleges provides a meaningful stepping stone out of the ``idleness trap'' into both employment and enrollment at more intensive educational institutions. We also can use the estimates for counter-factual policy simulations, such as examining the effectiveness of community college as a stepping stone during times of high and low unemployment, using variation in economic conditions provided by the Great Recession. 許多國家的年輕人現在的工作量比歷史上任何時候都少。雖然年輕人上大學的比率在上升，還是有越來越多的年輕人與學校和勞動市場脫節。進入勞動力市場對於年輕工人來說似乎越來越困難。該項目是研究社區學院和高等教育政策是如何幫助待業的年輕工人進入勞動力市場。我們估計了一個個體就業狀態的動態模型， 模型中包含允許觀察到的和未觀察到的個體特徵（這些個人特徵影響就業狀態變化的概率）。該模型提供了對狀態依賴性的估計和不同狀態對進入勞動力市場的有用性，例如此模型可以在排除個人特定的異質性以後，估計去社區大學多大程度幫助待業年輕人找到工作。該模型的估計結果可以模擬經濟危機中失業和高等教育政策對年輕工人的影響。

14503018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503018.value: This paper studies idleness among men in their first decade after leaving high school in the United States. Using a dynamic multinomial choice model, we estimate the transition among work, idleness, low-commitment schooling (community college or training programs) and high-commitment schooling (bachelor's degree program) for a cohort of young men who experienced the Great Recession in their early job market years. After controlling for economic environment and time-invariant observable and unobservable individual characteristics, we find evidence of an idleness trap. Our state dependence estimates show that compared to those employed in a given six-month period, idle young men are six times more likely to stay idle than to work in the next period. In addition, our cross-state dependence estimates suggest that low-commitment school options rarely serve as a stepping-stone to work. During a recession, schooling keeps existing attendees in school but absorbs little to no youth idleness.

14503318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503318.value: The theory of dynamic mechanism design has been successfully applied to study various economic settings, in which agents may possess private information evolving over time and a sequence of decisions need to be made. Examples include auctions, nonlinear pricing, taxation, public good provision, and the design of institutions. Most works in the literature assume an exogenous information evolution process. That is, the information arriving in the subsequent stage only depends on the information in the previous stage, but not on the decisions made before. However, it is necessary to incorporate the endogenous information evolution process in many important economic applications, such as experience goods, addiction, and learning-by-doing. This project aims to study the optimal contract for a revenue-maximizing monopolist in a general dynamic setting, where the agent’s private information evolution could be completely endogenous. We plan to provide a full characterization of the optimal mechanism, and demonstrate how to implement the mechanism via a realistic contract. More importantly, we shall describe the optimal information provision rule, and analyze the influence of different information structures on the revenue quantitatively. As a byproduct, we expect to give novel predictions that are absent in the setting with an exogenous information process. Thus, this project may provide new explanations on the marketing/sale strategy in a wide class of industries. 機制設計理論能夠幫助決策者分析實際生活中應用的各種機制，並在拍賣機制，稅收機制，保險條款等的設計中發揮重要作用。此外，機制設計理論也能夠幫助人們理解決策者們是為何選擇各種現有機制的。過去二十年中，動態機制設計理論的發展得到了廣泛重視並取得了巨大成功。在先前的研究中，絕大多數理論都假設儘管代理人可能會有隨著時間變化的個人信息，這些信息是外生給定的。也就是說，代理人的當期現有信息并不能依賴委託人之前的決策。然而在實際生活中，有大量的實例表明個人決策可能會影響以後信息獲取的變化，比如體驗品，各種易讓人上癮的商品，以及在行動中邊做邊學獲得新信息的現象。 本項研究旨在分析在有內生信息的動態環境下目的為利潤最大化的委託人如何設計最優機制。我們希望能夠將這項研究成果應用在現有理論無法適用的實際經濟案例中。因此，本項研究的一個重要意義是擴展現有的利潤最優機制理論能夠適用的實際環境。從應用的角度出發，本項研究的一個直接意義是分析基於信息結構的市場營銷和銷售策略，刻畫最優機制並給出實際可行的實施方案。因為對於信息的有效控制和利潤最優化是商業社會的常見現象，我們希望本項研究會幫助提升我們對於很多行業內各種市場營銷和銷售策略的理解。

14503318.label: Realisation of objectives
14503318.value: This project tries to understand the role of information in economic design problems. The theory of mechanism design aims to help the designers understand many real-world institutions, in which the information evolution are typically very common. For example, people often prefer to take trial sessions before registering Gym classes, and consumers often experience multiple cosmetic samples before deciding which brand to buy. As discussed in the proposal, almost all the previous studies in the literature work with the assumption that the agents have evolving private types, while the process is exogenous in the sense that the current type does not depend on the decisions made before. Such a framework clearly cannot cover the setting in which consumers could choose to actively acquire information. In this project, I study models with endogenous information process, in both static and dynamic settings. In the dynamic setting, I model the feature of learning-by-consuming in a sequential screening environment. The key modelling assumption is that the future information may depend on the consumption in the current stage. In the static setting, I study a novel robust auction design problem in which the designer may be lack of the information about the correlation among bidders’ valuations. I show that the optimal mechanisms in these two settings are the try-and-decide contract and the second-price auction, respectively (Objective 1). I further study how the seller’s revenue may depend on the information structure by allowing agents’ informativeness to vary slightly (Objectively 2). Importantly, we demonstrate that the mechanisms that are often used in practice, the try-and-decide contract and second-price auction, are indeed optimal. In this sense, we provide a possible theoretical justification for those common sales strategies in a variety of economic applications (Objectively 3).

14503318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503318.value: We have studied two settings in which the information structure may play a significant role in determining the seller’s revenue. First, in the working paper “Learning by consuming: Optimal pricing with endogenous information provision”, we study the revenue-maximizing mechanism when a buyer’s value evolves endogenously because of learning-by-consuming. In particular, the consumer may choose to experience a portion of the good, through which he better understands how well the good fits him and then decides the subsequent consumption. We identify the optimum revenue-maximizing mechanism as a menu of try-and-decide contracts. It is shown that a larger first-stage consumption level is paired with a higher first-stage price but a lower per-unit second-stage price for the remaining portion of the good. Moreover, if the buyer ends up buying the entire good, a higher first-stage consumption leads to a lower total payment. In another paper “Correlation-robust auction design” (Journal of Economic Theory, 2022), we study the design of auctions when the auctioneer has limited statistical information about the joint distribution of the bidders’ valuations. More specifically, we assume that the auctioneer only has an estimate of the marginal distribution of a generic bidder’s valuation, but is lack of reliable information about the correlation structure. The performance of mechanisms is evaluated in terms of the revenue guarantee - the greatest lower bound of revenue across all joint distributions that are consistent with the marginals. It is shown that the second-price auction with no reserve price is asymptotically optimal. Furthermore, in a finite-bidder market, a second-price auction with a random reserve price generates the highest revenue guarantee among all standard dominant-strategy mechanisms.

14503318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503318.value: Regarding the revenue-maximizing problem where buyers acquire information via learning-by-consuming, we plan to study a more general setting in which consumers can learn information over time rather than only once. Such an extension tries to capture the observation that in real life consumers often obtain information gradually; for example, buyers can lease cars for a long time to gain some information, and new customers may want to experience a few trial sessions before deciding whether to register the Gym membership. We have done some preliminary analysis for this extension, and proposed to study this question in the 2022-2023 RGC funding application. The paper “Correlation-robust auction design” focuses on the single-unit auction setting, while in realistic environments auctioneer often conducts combinatorial auctions where multiple heterogeneous objects are sold to a group of bidders; for example,, two of the most profitable auctions, the Google Ads Auction and the Meta Ads Auction, are combinatorial and involve highly correlated valuations. We plan to extend our current framework to cover this important setting. To do so, we need to develop new methodology to estimate the order statistics from a robust perspective, and link such a mathematical approach to the complicated economic auction environment.

14503318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503318.value: The feature of learning-by-consuming is prevalent in the daily selling environment. It is widely observed that consumers may be uncertain about whether the goods match with their preferences or not, and thus prefer to experience some trials in order to obtain additional information about the goods. A revenue-maximizing seller would take such learning behavior from buyers into consideration, and design accordingly the optimal contract with a suitable learning process. This project studies the revenue-maximizing contract in the setting with the feature of learning-by-consuming. We have identified the optimal mechanism and shown that it can be implemented via the common try-and-decide contract. In practice, a monopolist can often influence the consumers via various pre-sale information-provision options, such as advertisement and consumer education. Our results provide novel explanations for some common marketing/sale strategies.

14503518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503518.value: 在線知識共享（比如Quora, 知乎，StackOverflow）已經成為人們在互聯網上相互獲取知識的一個很流行的方式。與傳統的傳授知識的機構（比如學校和其他組織）相比，在線知識共享提供了一個開放的平臺。在這個平臺上，知識可以更大規模地得以傳播，而傳播的成本卻是很低的。這也是在線共享知識平臺在近幾年蓬勃發展的原因。數以百萬的人在短短幾年的時間內分享了大量的知識在這些平臺上，而這些平臺也被估值超過百億美元。在這些在線知識共享平臺迅速發展的同時，他們也面臨著一個巨大的挑戰：如何激勵人們更多地分享高質量的知識？如何應對這個挑戰至關重要，因為如果每個人都坐等別人分享的知識，或者每個人都分享低質量的知識，那麽最終沒有人會使用這些平臺。 我們的研究希望通過探究人們在中國最大的在線知識共享平臺“知乎”上分享知識的行為來回答以上這個問題。我們采集了257631個用戶7年以來在“知乎”上分享知識以及和其他用戶社交互動的所有面板數據。利用這些數據，我們希望研究用戶的社交互動是如何激勵他們共享知識的。我們的數據有三個特別的地方：首先，我們追蹤了這些用戶從第一天使用這個平臺開始的所有活動；第二，我們的數據涵蓋了共享知識的數量和質量；第三，我們的數據包括了社交互動的三個方面。因此我們可以研究三個問題：（1）如何量化社交互動對共享知識的數量和質量的影響；（2）哪種社交互動對於共享知識的數量/質量有著更大的影響；（3）哪種社交互動對於哪種用戶有著更大的影響。 由於我們的研究著重回答如何激勵人們更多地分享質量更高的知識，我們的研究結論將對在線知識共享的文獻有所貢獻。我們是第一個利用大數據研究社交互動對知識共享的影響的研究。通過比較不同社交互動的影響，我們的研究還將為在線知識共享平臺提供指導，尤其是如何設計共享平臺使之更好地激勵人們分享知識。

14503518.label: Realisation of objectives
14503518.value: Overall, our project achieved all four objectives with the efforts of all authors and a group of research assistants. To achieve all four objectives, we collected data for 896 crowdfunding projects on DemoHour (i.e., one of the earliest crowdfunding platforms in China with a similar setting as Kickstarter) that were launched and concluded between July 31, 2011, and August 30, 2014. For each project, we collected the project-related information such as funding goal, funding duration, and industry. We also obtained the full detailed investment history, i.e., who (investors’ usernames) invested how much money to what project at what time. Our dataset comprises 821 entrepreneurs who initiated 896 crowdfunding projects and 68,015 investors who made 116,104 contributions. Most importantly, as DemoHour allows people to sign up with their online social network accounts (Weibo, China’s Twitter), we accessed their Weibo accounts of 669 entrepreneurs and 32,560 investors who sed their Weibo accounts to sign up for DemoHour and collected their Weibo connections. To achieve Objective 1: the information role of crowdsourcing from entrepreneurs’ social networks (e.g., friends and family), we examined the funding outcomes of projects which had a higher vs. lower proportion of investments from Weibo friends in the early stage (e.g., first day and first week of project launch). We found that early contributions from Weibo friends are negatively correlated with the funding outcome (defined as the ratio of the total amount of funds raised to the funding goal), the likelihood of “funding success” (defined as having met the funding goal) and the number of investors (controlling for the funding goal, the funding duration, and the number and amount of funding on the first day/week). The results suggest crowdsourcing from entrepreneurs’ social networks as a negative signal of the quality of a crowdfunding project. To achieve Objective 2: identify entrepreneurs’ manipulation of funding from their social networks and Objective 3: what kind of crowdfunding projects manipulate funding from entrepreneur’s social networks, we zoomed in on the first day of the fundraising campaign, which is critical for the campaign's success, and carefully examined the intra-day time pattern of contributions. we carefully examined the investments from entrepreneurs’ Weibo connections in the first day of project launch. We compared the proportion of investments from entrepreneurs’ social connections in every hour among three groups of crowdfunding projects—good quality projects, moderate quality projects, and bad quality projects. We found that in the last three hours of the first day, connected contributions for moderate quality projects increase relative to those for good quality projects. This suggests that while entrepreneurs of good projects may receive favorable early signals about their projects and therefore do not need to call in connected individuals to boost the first day fundraising outcome, entrepreneurs of moderate quality projects may receive worse signals. Facing more uncertainty about their projects being able to reach the funding goal, they may therefore start calling on their social connections late at night on the first day to boost the first day fundraising outcome. This contribution time pattern thus rules out the possibility that the entrepreneur’s social connections voluntarily contribute to entrepreneurs’ projects because otherwise, their contributions at nighttime should illustrate the same pattern across all projects. To achieve Objective 4: what kind of funders are manipulated by entrepreneurs, we classified investors into two groups, sophisticated investors versus naïve investors, based on the average fundraising outcomes of the projects they invest in. We found that sophisticated and naïve investors have different investment behavior. Sophisticated investors invest almost three times the amount of money per project as do the naïve investors, and they tend to wait and make investments at a later stage than do the naïve investors, which suggests that sophisticated investors are more rational and are willing to wait and learn. Most interestingly, we find that if a project has a high percentage of early contributions from the entrepreneur’s social connections, it attracts fewer sophisticated investors but more naïve investors later on, suggesting that sophisticated investors may identify the strategic financing in the early stage of a fundraising campaign and avoid those projects, while naïve investors do not.

14503518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503518.value: Major findings: 1. We found that early investment from entrepreneurs’ social connections (e.g., friends, family) is a negative signal of the quality of entrepreneurs’ crowdfunding projects. That is, the crowdfunding projects with early investment from entrepreneurs’ social connections deliver poorer funding performance eventually. Those findings meet Objective 1 of our study. 2. We also found the entrepreneurs with moderate early funding performance strategically solicit investments from social connections in the early stage (e.g., first day of a project launch) to encourage naïve investors to herd. Specifically, in those crowdfunding projects with moderate early funding performance, the funding from entrepreneurs’ social connections is disproportionally high in the late night of the first day of project launch, compared with those in crowdfunding projects with good or bad early funding performance. It suggests that those entrepreneurs with moderate early funding performance carefully monitor the funding progress on the first day of project launch, and when the funding is not progressing well, they ask funding supports from their social connections before the closure of the first day of project launch. Their manipulation is to “fake” the good funding performance and attract external investors to invest. Those findings meet Objectives 2 and 3 of our study. 3. In addition, we found that the market has two segments of investors, naïve and sophisticated investors. Entrepreneurs’ strategic manipulation of finance can only influence naïve investors, who herd the crowd. On the other hand, sophisticated investors wait and observe the funding progress, and invest in the later stage with less money. They also discern entrepreneurs’ manipulation of financing from social connections. Those findings meet Objective 4 of our study. 4. Lastly, we found that entrepreneurs’ manipulation of financing from social connections exists even when a majority of investors are sophisticated investors because eventually the manipulated projects deliver poorer funding performance. Those findings meet Objective 1 of our study. Research Outcomes: 1. We presented our paper at Asia-Pacific Corporate Finance Online Workshop, May 2020, and Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance Annual Conference, June 2020 2. Our paper has been submitted to the top finance journals: Journal of Finance, Journal of Financial Economics, The Reviews of Financial Economics, and Review of Finance. We also submitted our paper to Management Science. Based on all the reviews, we are revising our paper and aim to submit it to other top journals.

14503518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503518.value: 1. Our measures of social connections between entrepreneurs and investors are based on the online social media data, i.e., whether an entrepreneur’s list of Weibo friends has the individual investor. This does not measure the closeness of the social connections. As entrepreneurs are likely to solicit finance from close friends and family, future work can enrich the measure by examining the interactions between entrepreneurs and investors on Weibo. Although it is beyond the scope of our study, we made extra efforts to collect online interaction data on a sample of randomly selected entrepreneurs and investors. We found the majority of the social connections identified with our measure indeed had interactions (e.g., comments on posts, like posts) with entrepreneurs on Weibo. 2. We measure the quality of crowdfunding projects with the success of a project meeting the funding goal. This measure, even though has been commonly used in literature on crowdfunding, has its limitation of not able to measure the outcomes of the crowdfunding projects, e.g., whether the project successfully delivers its products, whether the project gains commercial success in market. Future work can track the outcomes of crowdfunding projects and measure its success by the eventual deliverables.

14503518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503518.value: Conventional wisdom suggests that if an entrepreneur gets finance from investors connected to her (e.g., entrepreneur’s friends and family), it signals good quality of her business to the external investors. However, it also creates an opportunity for entrepreneurs to influence external investors’ perceptions by “carefully” manipulating the finance from investors they know (e.g., entrepreneur’s friends and family). Our research study the information role of financing from individual investors connected to entrepreneurs by examining the investment behavior on a crowdfunding platform and the social relationship between investors and entrepreneurs based on data from a crowdfunding platform and online social media data. We found that financing from connected individuals might be a signal of funding performance manipulation. With two segments of investors in the market, naïve and sophisticated investors, entrepreneurs with moderate early funding performance strategically solicit investments from their friends and family in the early stage to encourage naïve investors to herd. However, sophisticated investors discern entrepreneurs’ manipulation and invest less to those projects. We also found that entrepreneurs’ manipulation of financing exists even when sophisticated investors have significant market power as manipulated projects deliver poorer funding performance eventually.

14503618.value: 個人和組織通常需要把固定數量的資源（例如，時間，金錢）分配到多個項目中。在這項研究中，我們將審查兩種分配方法：（1）同步分配，即決策者把所有資源同一時間統一分配，以及（2）順序分配，決策者首先將總資源分成單位金額然後按順序分配每個單位金額。我們發現，在資源總量和候選項目數量不變的情況下，順序分配導致資源分配更加多樣化。 我們的研究結果違反了經濟理論中程序不變性的原則，表明不同的資源分配方法導致了分配結果的系統性偏差。這種效應也與經典行為決策研究的結果相矛盾，因為之前的研究表明同步決策通常會比順序決策導致更高的結果多樣性（例如，Read and Lowenstein, 1995; Simonson, 1990; Simonson and Winer, 1992）。因此，這項研究旨在記錄這種新的現象並解釋其潛在的機制。 我們發現，與同步分配相比，順序分配更有可能引導人們進行淺層處理，並主要關注於“選擇哪個項目？”而不是“應該給已選擇的項目分配多少資源？”因此，順序分配的決策者更有可能選擇更多項目。為了全面了解這些資源分配決策的心理機制，我們將研究以下問題： •人們如何做出資源分配決策？ •同步和順序分配如何影響人們的多樣性需求？ •與同步分配相比，為什麼順序分配會導致更高的結果多樣性？ •這種現象是否可以在現實環境中複製（在現實生活而不是在實驗室中）？ •可以在跨文化環境中和不同性格特徵的人中間觀察到同樣的现象嗎？

14503618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503618.value: The project highlights the importance of decision-making procedures on resource allocation outcomes. Our findings add to our understanding of the factors that influence human variety-seeking behavior. Our research suggests that an attentional focus may drive the variety-seeking tendency in a resource allocation setting. Our research implies that, if a decision-maker thinks that efficiency should outweigh equality, then the allocation-by-target procedure would serve the goal better. By contrast, if a decision-maker favors equality over efficiency, then the allocation-by-unit procedure is better. Our research also implies that individuals, organizations, or policymakers can choose the allocation procedure strategically, depending on the goal (equality vs. efficiency) of the decision task. At the same time, they should be wary of the unintended influence of procedure dependence and constantly remind themselves of their allocation criteria, and if necessary, check whether following another procedure would lead to the same allocation outcome.

14503718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503718.value: Studies on explosive autoregressive (AR) processes with a root greater than unity have attracted tremendous attention in econometrics. This is because explosive processes are useful for modeling periods of extreme movements in economic and financial variables. Empirical evidence of mildly explosive behavior has been found in many macroeconomic variables in the well-known Nelson-Plosser data set. Other examples of explosive behavior include financial bubbles in asset prices. The recent global financial crisis, commonly believed to be caused by the birth and burst of the U.S. real estate bubble, provides a rich new environment for empirical research and has led to growing interest among economists in studying financial bubbles and their catastrophic effects across markets and nations. The proposed project will aim to provide new econometric tools to improve understanding of explosive behaviors in economic and financial variables. From asset pricing theory, the price of an asset is composed of two unobservable components, the “fundamental” component and the “bubble” component. This project will first propose an econometric model and a Bayesian estimation procedure to separately identify and estimate these two components. Hence it will become possible to investigate whether and how the“bubble”components in various periods and markets differ from each other. A new approach will be proposed for detecting bubbles and estimating the origination date and termination date of each detected bubble. Then, does the detection of a bubble aid in time series forecasting in a univariate setting? In spite of the importance of forecasting in time series, to the best of our knowledge this question has not been addressed in the literature of bubbles. Hence, as the second objective, this project will first show that conventional methods generating time series forecasts cannot work well for explosive processes, then propose an alternative three-step procedure to generate better forecasts for time series during bubble episodes. Econometric properties of model selection criteria for determining the best forecasting model will be studied. Another question related to bubbles is whether and how bubbles across markets and countries interact with each other. To answer this question, regressions among explosive processes must be involved. The third objective of this project will be to design econometric tests to effectively distinguish between the non-sense regressions among explosive processes and the co-integrating regressions. 14503818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503818.value: The rapid development of digital technologies driven by the drastic reduction in the cost of storing, searching and retrieving information, promotes more and increasingly sophisticated digital environments for the accumulation of publicly available knowledge. The reduced cost of coordination and communication allows remotely located users to collaborate on complex joint projects, such as writing an online encyclopedia. In this project we will analyze generation of public knowledge on collaborative online platforms, concretely, mechanisms underlying survival and growth of collaborative online platforms. We evaluate individual utility from access to online public goods and its relationship with individual willingness to contribute to this knowledge, exerting effort and time, or contributing money. Despite some progress in the recent literature on specific aspects, the relationship between the value of the produced online public goods and the incentive mechanisms to contribute remain largely opaque. We propose a research design, that allows quantifying productivity gains from using online resources and the price, that users would be willing to pay for access to a resource. Moreover, we analyze how users’ valuation interacts with their willingness to contribute to the public good. We propose a field experiment to recreate in the lab an environment, where individuals would have to reveal their utility from getting access to online public knowledge for the search of information. Our subjects will make decisions regarding time, effort and money they would wish to spend for contributing to online encyclopedia Wikipedia. For this field experiment, we will exploit an emerging form of labor, which is also facilitated online: micro- and crowd working platforms. They will allow us to guarantee a large number of participants, and so a representative sample of the population, and an appropriate amount of economic resources used in our research project. The PI and Co-I’s have worked together on related topics and have been successful in producing working papers on the relationship between the economic downturn and private provision of an online public good Wikipedia, which has been presented in several conferences from 2015 to 2016. We expect that the study we propose will generate a significant contribution to the economics of IS literature on private provision of public goods. 由於存儲，搜索和檢索信息的成本急劇下降而推動的數字技術的快速發展促進了更多和越來越複雜的數字環境，以積累公開可用的知識。協調和通信的成本降低使遠程用戶能夠在復雜的聯合項目上進行協作，例如編寫在線百科全書。 在這個項目中，我們將分析協作在線平台上公共知識的產生，具體而言，是協作在線平台生存和發展的機制。我們評估從訪問在線公共產品的個人效用及其與個人願意為這種知識做出貢獻，付出努力和時間，或貢獻金錢的關係。 儘管最近關於具體方面的文獻取得了一些進展，但在線公共產品的價值與提供捐助的激勵機制之間的關係仍然很大程度上不透明。我們提出了一種研究設計，可以通過使用在線資源和價格來量化生產率，這是用戶願意為訪問資源而支付的。此外，我們還分析了用戶的估值如何與他們為公共利益做出貢獻的意願相互作用。 我們提出了一個現場實驗，在實驗室中重新創建一個環境，​​個人必須通過訪問在線公共知識來展示其實用性，以便搜索信息。我們的主題將決定他們希望用於貢獻在線百科全書維基百科的時間，精力和金錢。對於這個現場實驗，我們將利用一種新興的勞動形式：眾包工作平台。它們將使我們能夠保證大量參與者，以及代表性的人口樣本，以及我們研究項目中使用的適當數量的經濟資源。 PI和Co-I已經就相關主題進行了合作，並成功地研究了關於經濟衰退與私人提供在線公共物品維基百科之間關係的工作論文，該論文已於2015年至2016年在多個會議上宣講并在期刊接受評審。我們我們希望我們提出的研究將對私人提供公共產品的文獻產生重大貢獻。

14503818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503818.value: In a natural field experiment setting, we find that job displacement leads to higher participation by volunteers and increased content generation on public goods. On Wikipedia, both the number of participating editors and the number of highly active users increase. The number of edits to Wikipedia articles increases, and we also find evidence for increased growth of overall content. When facing empirical identification challenges, we also collected a country-level dataset. The results for the country-level dataset are consistent with those at the district level. We find even stronger effects on content generation.

14503818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503818.value: Despite the success of achieving all planned objectives, there are still many potential ways for further development. For example, it remains unclear as to whether the employed users increase their activity during leisure hours or whether the unemployed prefer to contribute during the hours that we classified as leisure times. Even if our identifying assumptions are satisfied, we can only provide indicative evidence on whether the additional content generation is driven by unemployed or employed users. Another fruitful avenue for further research could investigate the content of the contributions. Further research could analyze the nature of contributions and the type of articles that are edited.

14503818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503818.value: Economic crises often result in massive job loss. However, although reduced employment has been shown to have many negative consequences for the affected individuals, it may also push them into new activities, such as provision of service to their communities. In this project, we show how individuals engage in socially useful activities after an increase in unemployment. Specifically we document increased online content generation at Wikipedia, the world’s largest user generated knowledge repository. Leveraging German district-level and European country-level unemployment data we analyze the relationship between the economic crisis in 2008–2010 and contributions to Wikipedia. For both data sets we find increased socially valuable activity in the form of knowledge acquisition and contributions to Wikipedia. For German districts, we observe an increased rate of content generation on Wikipedia in districts that faced greater increases in unemployment. The effect of unemployment on content generation is even stronger at the European country level. Our findings suggest that private provision of public goods increases as a positive side effect of economic crises.

14504318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504318.value: A growing body of literature in accounting, beginning with Anderson, Banker, and Janakiraman (2003) (ABJ), studies cost stickiness. Costs are considered sticky if “they increase more when activity rises than they decrease when activity falls by an equivalent amount.” Cost stickiness captures the asymmetry in managers’ decision to commit resources when they face uncertain future activity levels and resource adjustment costs (Banker and Byzalov 2014). We extend this literature by decomposing cost stickiness into its main components and studying their information content. In particular, we study three different aspects of cost stickiness: (a) the elasticity of costs in response to an increase in sales; (b) the elasticity of costs in response to a decrease in sales; and (c) the proportion of firms experiencing a decrease in sales at any given point in time. In the ABJ model, cost stickiness is the difference between (a) and (b). Since the ABJ model is typically conducted in a cross-sectional fashion, the averages of (a) and (b) reflect the cost structure of the economy or industry. Unlike most of the existing literature on cost stickiness, which focuses almost exclusively on component (b), we examine the information content of each of these components. We expect (a) to be higher in magnitude if the increase in demand is expected to be more permanent. Hence, (a) is determined by the production function (increasing, decreasing or constant return to sales) and whether adjustment costs are increasing (convex) or decreasing (concave) in size. We expect (b) to be higher in absolute value if the decrease in demand is expected to be permanent. We expect (c) to be informative about the importance of cost stickiness at any given time. The higher the proportion of firms that experienced a decrease in sales, the greater the importance of cost stickiness. Using data from corporate filings, we will study the information content of the three components of cost stickiness. For many firms, labor is a major resource and this is reflected in the significant proportion of operating costs that are comprised of labor. We build on prior research and we examine, in particular, the usefulness of the different components of cost stickiness in forecasting macrolevel unemployment rate. 源於Anderson, Banker, Janakiraman (ABJ) 2003年的研究，越來越多的文章開始關注成本粘性這個話題。成本粘性可以解釋為：經營活動增加一定單位時所增加的成本超過經營活動減少相應單位時所減少的成本。管理層在做成本決策時需要面對未來經營活動的不確定性以及資源的調整成本，成本粘性反映了管理層成本決策的不對稱性。我們的研究貢獻是，對成本粘性進行主成分分解並分析它們相應的信息含量。 具體而言，我們研究了成本粘性的三方面內容：(a) 銷售收入增加時的成本彈性；(b) 銷售收入減少時的成本彈性; (c) 在某一時點上銷售收入減少的公司佔比。在ABJ模型中，成本粘性定義為(a)和(b)的差值。由於經典的ABJ模型是採用橫截面數據估計的，因此(a)和(b)的平均值反映了經濟系統或者行業的成本結構。與已有的幾乎全部關注(b)的成本粘性研究不同，我們同時探究了以上三個組成部分的信息含量。我們預測當需求更加持續穩定的時候，(a)更高。因此，(a)是由生產函數（遞增、遞減或者不變的收益率）和調整成本的規模遞增（凸性）或規模遞減（凹性）所決定的。我們預期當需求的減少是穩定持續的時候，(b)的絕對值更高。我們預期(c)在所有情況下都反映了成本粘性的重要性。當銷售收入下降的企業佔比越高時，成本粘性的重要性愈加凸顯。 我們將通過上市公司財務報告中的數據探究以上三個方面內容的信息含量。對於大量公司而言，人力是一項重要的資源，反映為公司的經營成本中包含了大量的有關人力資源的成本。在已有研究的基礎上，我們重點研究了成本粘性的不同組成部分對於預測宏觀失業率的有用性。

14504618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504618.value: To pursue low labor and material costs, Western brandname companies choose to source from suppliers located in developing countries. But sourcing from those countries brings concerns and problems related to product quality and ethics. On one hand, some suppliers don’t own the capability to produce units that meet quality/safety specifications set by Western brands. On the other hand, lack of ethical awareness leads to many suppliers paying little attention to social considerations, including overtime policy, facility security, environmental protection, and child labor use. Those problems are latent in the stage of contract negotiation between brandname companies and suppliers. However, when they arise in later stages, they cause severe consequences to the brands, yielding substantial losses both financially and reputationally. Thus, it is for the best interest of brandname companies that supplier audit is conducted before contract negotiation. Those companies oftentimes rely on third-party audit firms for supplier audit because auditing is not their core competence and suppliers are located far away. However, it is possible that an audit report doesn’t reveal true conditions of an auditee. There are two reasons for this phenomenon. First, there are imperfections associated with auditing technologies. Second, realizing their difficulty to pass audits, low-quality suppliers may offer bribes to auditors sent by audit firms in exchange for favorable audit results. Such auditor-auditee collusion greatly reduces the credibility of audit results. To prevent the auditor-auditee collusion, an audit firm may audit an auditee for a second time (re-audit the auditee) to examine whether the first audit report of the auditee is accurate. But the implementation of re-auditing is unlikely to be applicable to all the auditees due to limited budgets. Besides, a long preparation needed for re-audit may render leakage of some information regarding parties to be re-audited. We will build a game-theoretic model that considers imperfection of auditing technology, possibility of auditor-auditee collusion, and information leakage related to probable re-audit. We will study how an audit firm designs an incentive payment scheme that prevents the auditor-auditee collusion. This research is relevant to the economy of the region. Hong Kong has the convenience and advantages of providing audit and certification services to manufacturers in China. This research can contribute to such practices by providing insights into improving efficiency of auditing processes. This research may also help promote cross-border trades and global supply chain management by examining mechanisms to reduce collusive behavior in sourcing from emerging economies. 為了追求低廉的勞動力和材料成本，西方的許多品牌公司選擇從發展中國家的供應商採購。但是，從這些國家採購會帶來與品質和道德相關的問題。一方面，一些供應商不具備生產達到西方品牌所設之質量/安全的設備與能力。另一方面，由於道德意識的欠缺，許多供應商很少關注社會因素，包括超時政策，設施安全，環境保護和童工使用。在品牌公司與供應商之間的合同談判階段，這些問題往往潛伏著。然而，當它們真正出現時，會對品牌造成嚴重後果，使之在財務和聲譽上蒙受重大損失。 因此，品牌公司為了其最佳利益，通常選擇在合同談判之前進行供應商審核。因為審計不是他們的核心競爭力，同時供應商通常位於遠方，這些品牌公司往往依賴審計公司進行供應商審計。但是，審計報告可能無法揭示受審核方的真實情況。這種現像有兩個原因。首先，審計技術存在不完善之處。其次，由於難以通過審計，低質量的供應商可能會向審計公司派出的審計員行賄，以換取有利的審計結果這種審核員 - 受審核方的串通大大降低了審核結果的可信度。 為了防止審核員 - 受審核方的串通，審核公司可以進行第二次審核（即重新審核受審核方），以檢查第一份審核報告是否準確。但是由於預算有限，不可能對所有的受審核方進行重新審核。此外，重新審核需要一定時間的準備工作，從而可能會導致一些信息洩漏。我們將構建一個遊戲理論的模型。該模型將考慮審查技術的不完善性，審計師 - 受審計方串通的可能性，以及重新審計相關信息所可能的洩漏。我們將研究審計公司是否可以設計一個薪酬方案，以防止審計師 - 受審計方的串通。 我們相信這項研究與本地區的經濟相關。香港具備為中國大陸的製造商提供審計和認證服務的便利和優勢。最近，兩地政府之間實施了CEPA（更緊密經貿關係協議）。這項研究可以提供有關預防串通行為和提高審計過程效率，從而促進該協議的實施。

14504618.label: Realisation of objectives
14504618.value: Realisation of Objective 1: We consider a supply chain in which a buyer (he) sources from a supplier (she) for the production of a product. The unit retail price of the product is p. The buyer offers to the supplier a “take-it-or-leave-it” sourcing contract, which specifies an order quantity q and a transfer payment t. In addition, to produce q units, the supplier needs to incur a production cost cq. The supplier's production process is subject to probable violations of either government regulations or ethical requirements (such as usage of child labour or inferior working conditions). If some violation occurs, it will be reported by the news media and will eventually be known by consumers in the market. Thus, the product can be no longer sold due to news reports of such violation. The buyer's sourcing contract demands that the supplier exerts an effort to improve its production process, thus reducing the probability of the occurrence of violation. The violation probability at the supplier is reduced by the effort exerted by the supplier. We assume that the supplier's effort is hardly observable to the buyer. But the buyer can hire an auditor to perform an audit of the supplier's facility by reviewing documents, interviewing employees, and inspecting the facility. The auditor will in turn report whether the supplier has exerted the effort. The sourcing contract will be nullified if the supplier fails to pass the audit. We assume that the audit is imperfect. Specifically, following the inspection literature, we assume that the supplier always passes the audit if the supplier has exerted the effort. However, when there is no effort exerted, the probability that the auditor finds out the actual situation is less than one. If that is the case, the supplier may offer a side contract in exchange for a passing result from the audit (note that such collusion occurs only when the auditor agrees on this side contract). The supplier-auditor collusion could be discovered with some probability. After being discovered, the auditor will be subjected to a positive penalty, which can be imposed by the law enforcement by regulatory authorities. Given that the auditor may not detect the supplier exerting no effort and may even choose to collude, the supplier can consider choosing not to exert any effort, if doing so is economically attractive to her. We first consider a benchmark case in which the buyer has no other levers to hinder the probable supplier-auditor collusion. Hence, to hedge against the collusion risk, all that the buyer can do is to adjust his order quantity. We then incorporate the reaudit into our model and denote by r the cost of the reaudit. Adopting the reaudit strategy increases the buyer’s chance to detect the supplier exerting no effort (if it is the case), which leads to, on average, a higher price for the supplier and the auditor of the first audit to engage in any collusion. On the other hand, the reaudit brings to the buyer an additional expense spent on auditing the supplier. Realisation of Objective 2: We consider the sequence of events as follows: 1) The buyer devises the sourcing contract and offers it to the supplier. 2) The supplier decides on her effort level. 3) The auditor carries out an audit at the supplier. 4) The supplier offers a side contract if she has not exerted any effort and does not pass the audit. The auditor decides on whether or not to accept the side contract. 5) The buyer carries out reaudit if he chooses that strategy 6) The sourcing contract is executed if the supplier passes the audit (and the reaudit, if applicable) Based on the sequence of events, we are able to derive the IR (Individual Rationality) and IC (Incentive Compatibility) constraints, which in turn leads to a contract-design optimization problem for the buyer. By solving the optimization problem (via making the IC constraint binding), we can thus obtain incentive payment schemes for the benchmark case and the reaudit strategy, which can effectively prevent the auditors from collusion. Realisation of Objective 3: We examine how the collusion penalty may influence the equilibrium outcome. Specifically, when the collusion penalty is sufficiently large, it is effective in preventing the supplier and the auditor from colluding with each other. In other words, the buyer behaves as if all the parties were indeed ethical and can do business as usual. Recall that the equilibrium solution is gained from making the IC constraint binding. Thus, when the collusion penalty becomes lighter, maintaining the same sourcing contract will make it economically attractive for the supplier to choose not to exert any effort but to collude with the auditor. Consequently, the buyer would respond by reducing the business with the supplier, which yields a smaller order quantity and a decreased expected profit. In short, our result shows that the conclusion penalty does play a critical role in responsible sourcing. This observation explains why buyers from the West oftentimes lobby local governments in developing countries to increase penalties on illegal activities including collusion and reinforce their legal enforcement. For example, several global brands (such as Starbucks, Nike, and Gap) signed the Anti-Corruption Call to Action with the local governments, driving the latter to address corruption problems and foster effective governance. Another example comes from the fact that Disney stopped sourcing garments from Bangladesh due to safety concerns raised from the building collapse in 2013, but returned after a successful negotiation with the local government there, coupled with charges of criminal negligence that led to the building collapse, the first ever in the history of Bangladesh. Realisation of Objective 4: We examine another strategy that the buyer can utilize to deter the probable supplier-auditor collusion, dual sourcing. Dual sourcing has been widely used in reality to improve the resilience of sourcing practices. Presumably, dual sourcing can play a role in preventing the collusion studied in our model. That is, when the buyer splits his order quantity to two (or more) suppliers, the order quantity placed with an individual supplier would become smaller, thus reducing her incentive to collude with the auditor. Of course, the buyer needs to pay attention to the fact that if any supplier is involved in certain violation, the buyer will suffer from a reputation damage and thus an overall revenue loss, even though the supplier provides only a small portion of units ordered by the buyer. Accordingly, we assume that the buyer source from two homogeneous suppliers. To focus on interesting cases, we assume that violation probability is nontrivial. Given the fact that the two suppliers are homogeneous, it is straightforward that the buyer will offer the same outsourcing contract to them. To be consistent with our previous discussion, we continue to denote the contract by (t,q), where q is the order quantity placed with either supplier and t is the transfer price. Note that with our previous discussion of the buyer's brand reputation, we assume that the buyer sells his product successfully only if no violation occurs at either supplier. Our previous analysis can be modified to treat this two-supplier problem, from which we derive insights related to deterring supplier-auditor collusion via dual sourcing.

14504618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14504618.value: Our analysis of the model offers interesting observations and insights. First, we find that the buyer should reduce the order quantity to deter the supplier-auditor collusion when the penalty of the collusion is relatively low. This result confirms the negative impact of the collusion, that is, reducing order quantities placed by MNCs when outsourcing to emerging economies with lax legal enforcements on bribery activities. It also justifies the attempt made by some buyers to bring the production in-house. For instance, Ravensburger, a European toy brand, decides to manufacture 90% of its products in its own factories in Czech Republic, while outsourcing only 10% of its goods, a significant decrease compared to the past. Second, in mitigating the risk of collusion, one may conjecture that a reaudit serves as a substitute for the penalty imposed on the supplier-auditor collusion. However, our analysis reveals that this is not necessarily the case. Instead, under certain conditions, the reaudit complements the collusion penalty. This result implies that buyers cannot choose auditing their suppliers and then fully relying on local governments' efforts of enforcing stricter laws to punish supplier-auditor collusion. It is true that to sustain the volume of sourcing contracts from their Western buyers, emerging economies have raised penalties for collusive behaviours. In that case, adopting the reaudit strategy continues to be attractive to the buyers as it can improve their profitability further, as supported by some industrial evidence. For example, suppliers need to undertake a social audit to be approved as Inditex's partners, but some of the suppliers are subjected to a more stringent second audit (in addition to the previous social audit) that evaluates specific aspects related to worker health and safety. Third, we find that using dual sourcing to deter collusion is viable only in these countries where law regulations are lax but reliable suppliers are present. Once the law enforcement has been strengthened, MNCs should leverage more on the strengthened law enforcement and switch back to sourcing from a single supplier.

14504618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14504618.value: Our research serves as a starting point for further investigations of related problems faced by practitioners of responsible sourcing. Some extensions to our model are worthy of studying. In our model, we have assumed that the buyer's auditing plan is known by the supplier (that is, whether the buyer will implement the reaudit is public knowledge to the supplier). We can generalize the model to the case in which the supplier may not have such knowledge, because the buyer adopts a randomized auditing schedule in which the number and the timing of audits are not revealed to the supplier in advance. We have also assumed that the buyer may source from two homogeneous non-competing suppliers. In practice, suppliers can be heterogeneous, ranging from reliable to unreliable, long-term to short-term, incumbent to entrant ones, not to mention the possible competition among the suppliers. It would be interesting to investigate how the heterogeneity of suppliers may influence the buyer's strategy to mitigate the collusion risk.

14504618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504618.value: We have developed a stylized model to study the supplier-auditor collusion and approaches to deterring such collusion. Our work contributes to the growing literature on responsible sourcing by taking into account the reaudit strategy and endogenizing the decision on order quantity. Our analysis reveals important insights that can provide theoretical supports the responsible sourcing practices that may face risks caused by the probable supplier-auditor collusion. Specifically, our analysis indicates that the buyer should reduce the order quantity to prevent the supplier from colluding with the auditor when the penalty imposed on the collusive parties is low. This result suggests that if local governments want to restore the business volumes with foreign buyers, there does exist a need to strengthen the law enforcement (such as heightening punishments on collusive behaviour). Our model also reveals that reaudits do not just serve as a substitute for the penalty imposed on collusion. Instead, under certain conditions, a reaudit can complement the collusion penalty, thus improving the buyer's profit. Furthermore, we find that dual sourcing is optimal only in these countries with lax law regulation but reliable suppliers. However, once the law enforcement has been improved, brands should switch back to sourcing from a single supplier.

14504918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504918.value: The proliferation of Internet based platforms has created an emerging channel of funding – crowdfunding. In crowdfunding, an individual requests funding for an idea and a large number of unaffiliated individuals contribute to fund the project. Crowdfunded projects range from small creative projects to entrepreneurial ventures seeking millions of dollars in funding. The crowdfunding marketplaces have grown rapidly in recent years, attracting an estimated $34.4 billion worldwide in 2015. Online crowdfunding markets provide a platform where market participants can easily access diverse information to help assess different projects available for contribution. However, despite the potential benefits associated with crowdfunding, legitimate concerns include the potential for fraud and creator incompetence. According to a study, a significant number of projects are delivered late or even fail to deliver. In decentralized online crowdfunding with a lack of strict reporting and accounting, crowdfunders are thus subject to an unusually high degree of information asymmetry. While information disclosure is believed to help reduce information asymmetry, we are aware of no empirical evidence regarding how crowdfunders respond to the disclosure of risk information of early-stage projects. In this project, we aim to examine how crowdfunders respond to the disclosure of project risk in crowdfunding. To examine this, we first use a crowdfunding platform's new policy to require creators to disclose potential risks and challenges associated with their projects. Second, we will collect all the actual disclosure data for technology projects on the platform and develop a machine learning-based prediction algorithm to predict a risk level of a project based on its risk disclosure. This will be then used to see if this predicted risk level is associated with the funding success and actual reward delivery. This project will make several implications. First, we are first to examine the effect of the disclosure of project risks in crowdfunding. More broadly, our study will add to the literature on disclosure, which has largely focused on its role for public firms. While previous studies suggest that disclosure requirements are largely beneficial for such firms, we should not expect that the finding will still hold for small ventures in a crowdfunding market. Finally, answering the questions can have implications for policy makers and platform providers. A better understanding of how participants react to risk disclosure will help crowdfunding platforms to implement better strategies to reduce information asymmetry between creators and crowdfunders, which is the most critical issue in any funding market. 基於互聯網平台的普及，一個新的資金渠道應運而生——眾籌。在眾籌中，個人要求為一個創意項目提供資金，並且大量與此項目無關聯的人去為這個項目提供資金。眾籌項目包括從小型創意項目到尋求數百萬美元資金的創業企業。眾籌市場近年來迅速增長，在2015年期間全球吸引了大約344億美元的資金。在線眾籌市場提供了一個平台，市場參與者可以輕鬆訪問各種信息，這些信息用來幫助評估可以參與貢獻的不同項目。然而，儘管存在諸多與眾籌相關的潛在好處，但也存在很多合法化的擔憂，比如潛在欺詐和發起人無法勝任的能力。根據研究表明，大量項目出現交付延遲或者無法交付的情況。在分散的在線眾籌中缺乏嚴格的報告和會計，因此多數眾籌者的信 息不對稱程度異常高。儘管信息披露被認為是有助於減少信息披露的不對稱，但我們還沒有關於大眾對早期項目風險信息披露的反應的經驗證據。在這個項目中，我們的目的是研究眾籌者如何應對眾籌項目風險的披露。為了檢驗這一點，我們首先應該使用眾籌平台的新政策，要求發起人披露與其項目相關的潛在風險和挑戰。其次，我們將要收集平台上所有技術項目的實際披露數據，並開發基於機器學習的預測算法，以根據風險披露來預測項目的風險等級。這將用於查看此預測風險等級是否與資金成功和實際獎勵交付相關聯。此項目將會產生以下一些影響。第一，我們首先考察了項目風險披露對眾籌的影響。更廣泛地說，我們的研究將會增加關於披露的文獻，其中主要關注其對上市公司的影響。雖然先前的研究表明，披露要求對這樣的公司大有裨益，但我們不應該期待這一發現對眾籌市場中的小型企業仍然試用。最後，回答這些問題可能會對決策者和平台提供者產生影響。更好的了解參與者如何應對風險披露將會有助於眾籌平台實施更好的策略，以減少發起人和眾籌者之間的信息不對稱，這是所有融資市場最關鍵的問題。

14504918.label: Realisation of objectives
14504918.value: This project has been going successfully so far. I'm going to explain what I have done to achieve the three objectives. The first objective is to examine the response of crowdfunders to the disclosure of project risks by using a new disclosure policy implemented on a leading crowdfunding platform. For this, leveraging a policy change as an exogenous event, I adopted a difference-in-differences empirical strategy with a matching sample to compare funding decisions before and after the regulation was mandated and show differential effects between high- and low-risk projects. In addition, to strengthen the causality, I directly tested individuals’ intention to pledge after reading project descriptions with and without risk disclosure in online experiments. The second objective was to mine textual information about the disclosure of project risk in a crowdfunding platform and apply machine learning techniques to predict the risk level of the project with mined textual information. Because risk disclosure is self-disclosed and only available in projects after the policy introduction, I relied on a more objective measure of risk from several ex-ante observable characteristics rather than risk disclosure. Furthermore, I examined how the content and the presentation of risk disclosure could mitigate the negative effect by using text mining to show that authenticity, sentiment, and consistency are essential if the disclosure is to appear credible. Finally, the last objective is to propose some implications for platform providers and market participants in crowdfunding. This project provides several implications. It shows that disclosure policies may make crowdfunding markets more sustainable by reducing information asymmetry and helping crowdfunders make more informed decisions. Also, mandatory risk disclosure is less harmful and more credible if creators write risk disclosures that appear authentic and are appropriately balanced regarding negativity and positivity and consistent with the main description of the project. The key is to write risk disclosures strategically.

14504918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14504918.value: We find that increasing the awareness of project risks is associated with inferior funding outcomes of crowdfunding projects, and the effect exists mainly for high-risk projects but not much for low-risk projects. In addition, high-risk projects benefit from a risk disclosure with relevant information, authentic language, and balanced tones that are not overly negative or optimistic. Despite the negative short-term effects, technology funders tend to interpret risk disclosures rationally over time, suggesting a positive long-term effect.

14504918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14504918.value: Our work bears limitations, which also inspires opportunities for future research. For instance, the observed divergence in trends of funding amount between high- and low-risk projects started even before the policy, which could imply funders might have already been aware of potential risks and acted accordingly in months closer to the actual policy introduction date. It could be a small proportion of funders starting to avoid investing in high-risk projects when a number of questions about accountability on Kickstarter emerged before the mandatory risk disclosure policy was formally introduced. We use multiple methodologies in our paper to account for this shortage and strengthen our findings. In future, researchers could conduct randomized field experiments on project risk disclosure and prevent a contaminated samples by sound experiment design. Using the low-risk projects as the control group is not ideal because low-risk projects are also influenced by the policy if small and compete with high-risk projects for funding. Whereas we believe that the project risk index is a reliable and consistent project risk measure that reflects the inherent project risk meaningfully, we do not claim that our current approach is the best. Future research can improve the measure of project risks.

14504918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504918.value: Online crowdfunding markets often lack quality assurance mechanisms and feature significant information asymmetry between project creators and funders. As a result, platform providers frequently endeavor to devise policies to ensure sound transactions and reduce associated risks, but they also need to understand how project creators and funders will respond. In this project, we investigate a policy change instigated to increase the salience of project risk at Kickstarter, a leading crowdfunding platform. Our study shows that Kickstarter’s new risk disclosure policy generally hurts project outcomes by reducing funding and success, especially for high-risk projects but less so for low-risk projects. Although the policy increases the salience of risk information, creators can reduce negative effects by writing relevant, authentic content and avoiding tones that are too negative or too optimistic. Also, the negative effects persist for nontechnology projects, but gradually dissipate for technology projects. Together, we show that the new policy reduces information asymmetry and potentially makes crowdfunding markets more sustainable by helping funders identify risks and make wiser contributions. Also, we encourage managers and policymakers to balance the pros and cons before enacting platform regulations.
