14505318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505318.value: A well-known finance theory, by Jensen and Meckling (1974), states that, due to limited liability, the equity holders of a distressed firm have an incentive to take on new high-risk investments to increase their firm’s asset risk. If the high-risk investment fails, the equity holders don’t have to pay back the debt holders from their own pockets during bankruptcy. This strategy, called the risk-shifting problem, essentially shifts the risk to the debt holders. However, finance researchers have difficulty finding empirical evidence that illustrates that troubled firms make real high-risk investments. A well-circulated classroom story on the risk-taking theory involves the founder of FedEx, Fred Smith. In 1971, he saved his company by taking its last $5,000 and turning it into $32,000 by gambling in Las Vegas. This lucky money allowed FedEx to keep operating for another week. As a result, FedEx is still in business today. What do we learn from this story? How is this story different from the aforementioned finance theory? There are at least two discrepancies: 1) the instrument of investments and 2) the time required to make an investment. Firstly, Fred Smith was gambling with $5,000 in cash for immediate cash payoffs. As such, the investment instrument is the financial instrument (i.e., cash), instead of real investments. Second, Fred Smith was desperate and short of time to figure out or take on another business strategy (e.g., a new delivery route), to save his firm. Instead, he took on financial risk in Las Vegas and make some quick dirty money, because he needed the money immediately to keep his company running for another week. With the aforementioned insights, we believe that most troubled firms are prone to take on financial risk, instead of real investment risk. Therefore, we examine the change in the taking of a financial asset risk, instead of an operating risk, for the distressed firms in the proposed research project. More specifically, the 2009 Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (SFAS), No. 157, requires all ﬁrms to report the fair value of major asset classes on their balance sheet. Consequently, financial asset holdings were hand-collected in our preliminary test. Strong evidence illustrated that firms increase their holdings in risky financial assets prior to a downgrade in their credit rating. With this encouraging evidence, we plan to collect more financial asset information for a large sample of distressed firms and study their opportunistic risk-shifting behavior. Jensen and Meckling (1974)曾提出一經典的金融理論，認為由於有限負債的存在，一個危機公司的股權持有者有激勵去進行高風險的投資活動來增加他們公司的資產風險。如果高風險投資活動失敗，這些股權持有者並不需要在公司破產時，用自身資金來償還公司債權人。這種策略即稱為風險轉移問題，並且基本上多為將風險轉移到債權人。但是金融學者們發現這在實證上難以找到相關證據，即難以驗證處於危機的公司會進行實質的高風險投資活動。支持“風險承擔理論”的一個典型案例涉及到聯邦快遞（FedEx）的創始人弗雷德·史密斯（Fred Smith）。在1971年，他將公司最後的$5,000美元投入到拉斯維加斯的博彩活動中，並最終贏得了$32,000美元，挽救了他的公司。這些幸運的資金是的聯邦快遞可以繼續運行一個週。而最終，聯邦快遞公司至今依舊在運行。我們從這個故事中可以學到什麼？這個故事和上文提及的金融理論有何區別？這其中至少有兩個區別：1）投資活動中投資工具的選擇和2）進行投資活動的時機選擇。首先，弗雷德·史密斯將$5,000美元現金投入到博彩活動來得到即時的現金回報。此時，投資工具即為金融性的投資工具，而不是實質性的投資活動，比如：現金。其二，弗雷德·史密斯處於非常沮喪和絕望的處境中，缺乏足夠的時間來處理公司困境或者從事新的商業業務來挽救公司，比如：開發一條新的物流鏈。相替代的是，他在拉斯維加斯進行了金融風險活動，並且賺取了快錢，目的在於他需要即時的資金來維持他的公司可以運營一周。 鑑於上述的現象，我們相信大部分的危機公司都會傾向於承擔金融性風險，而不是實質性的投資活動風險。因此，我們在研究方案中考察了危機公司承擔金融性資產風險而不是營運風險的變化。更具體而言，2009年的財務會計標準(SFAS)中的第157條要求所有的公司公開披露其資產負債表上主要資產類別的公允價值。因此，在我們初步測試中，我們手動收集了金融性資產的持有情況。有力的證明表明，公司會在他們的信用評級出現降級調整之前，增加他們對高風險的金融性資產的持有。因為有這些證據，我們計劃收集更多大樣本下的危機公司金融性資產持有情況的信息，並且學習他們機會主義的風險轉移行為。

14505318.label: Realisation of objectives
14505318.value: Objective 1. Build a new financial asset holding dataset for non-financial firms To study the composition of firms’ financial assets, we follow DGHH (2017) and collect data on ﬁrms’ ﬁnancial portfolios that comprise: (1) the balance sheet accounts “cash and cash equivalents” and “short-term investments,” which constitute Compustat’s data item CHE, the standard measure of cash holdings in the literature, and (2) any additional ﬁnancial assets reported as “long-term investments” or “other assets”. We hand-collect detailed information on the asset classes that constitute ﬁrms’ ﬁnancial portfolios from the footnotes of annual reports. To classify the riskiness of firms’ financial assets, we follow DGHH (2017) and define safe financial assets as those that fall into the following asset classes: cash, cash equivalents, demand deposits, money market securities, treasury bills, treasury notes and treasury bonds. We consider all other financial assets as risky. We exclude from the analyses restricted assets, deferred executive compensation, and derivative hedging. Objective 2. Collect real investment information for oil and gas firms We construct a measure of firms’ risky real assets by hand-collecting data on investment risk from the 10-K reports of the Crude Oil & Natural Gas ﬁrms (SIC 1311) in the sample. These data are collected from firms’ disclosures on “Costs Incurred in Natural Gas and Oil Exploration and Development, Acquisitions and Divestitures,” which provide information related to expenditures on exploratory wells and development wells. Exploratory wells are those drilled to ﬁnd a new ﬁeld or to ﬁnd a new reservoir in a ﬁeld in which another reservoir has previously produced oil or gas. Development wells are those drilled within the proven area of an oil or gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive. We follow Gilje (2016) and categorize all activities associated with exploratory drilling as risky investments. This includes both the capital to drill and the capital to acquire unproven acreage in which to drill. All activities associated with development drilling, which include the drilling of development wells and the acquisition of proven/producing acreage for development drilling are classified as safe investments. Using these data, we construct two measures of risky real assets investments. Objective 3. Investigate the risk-shifting behavior of these firms entering distress In the main analyses, we find that following the onset of the 2014 oil price crisis, firms with high short-term liabilities (in the top tercile) increase their investments in risky financial assets, on average, from $1.06 billion to $1.43 billion – an increase of $370 million, or 34.8%. Consequently, their ratio of risky financial assets to total financial assets increases from 20.5% in 2013 to 37.2% in 2016. The significant economic increase in risky financial assets is also highly statistically significant and continues to hold in difference-in-differences panel regressions that include year and firm fixed effects as well as time-varying firm-level attributes such as capital expenditures and sales. We conduct extensive robustness tests. First, we demonstrate that our results hold across alternative measures of short-term liabilities: debt maturities of one, two, or three years; short-term liabilities scaled by total assets; and both dichotomous and continuous measrues of short-term liabilities. Second, we show that the results hold in a subsample of oil producers that excludes firms with diversified operations such as oil refinement, which entails a directionally opposite exposure to oil price declines. Third, we provide estimates from two-stage least-squares regressions, where the first-stage regressions identify exogenous changes in profitability based on the oil price shock, and the second-stage regressions use the fitted changes in profitability from the first-stage regressions to explain changes in risk-taking. These estimates show that the decline in profitability following the oil price crisis is accompanied by an increase in financial risk-taking at highly levered firms. Lastly, we further validate our measure of debt rollover risk by providing direct evidence on firms that actually went bankrupt following the 2014 oil price crisis. Using hand-collected data on bankruptcy filings, we find that soon-to-be-bankrupt firms increase their financial risk-taking. The estimates suggest a significant increase of 25.1% in the ratio of risky financial assets to total financial assets in the year before filing for bankruptcy. Overall, these estimates imply that distressed firms, with high levels of short-term liabilities and rollover risk before the oil price crisis, gravitated considerably toward riskier financial investments following the onset of the crisis. By the end of 2016, their risky financial investments accounted for a nontrivial fraction of both their financial and total operations. I very much appreciate financial support from the GRF and has acknowledged this funding in the paper.

14505318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505318.value: Using hand-collected data on financial asset portfolios and exploiting the 2014 oil price crisis as an exogenous cash flow shock, we investigate financial risk-taking at distressed firms. We find that distressed firms, with high debt rollover risk proxied by short-term liabilities, substantially increase their investments in risky financial assets, including corporate debt, equity, and mortgage-backed securities. The effects are stronger for unhedged firms with low collateral assets. Overall, we provide new evidence that distressed firms take risk using financial assets camouflaged as cash reserves, which, compared to real assets, are less visible and carry lower transaction costs and accelerated payoffs.

14505318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505318.value: Our study limits to the oil and gas industry, not only because we would like to exploit the exogenous shock of the 2012 oil price drop, but also because the manual classification of risky and safe financial assets is very time consuming. It would be of interest to extend it to other industries.

14505318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505318.value: Risk-shifting theory states that, due to limited liability, the equity holders of a distressed firm have an incentive to take on new high risk investments to increase their firm’s asset risk. If the high-risk investment fails, the equity holders don’t have to pay back the debt holders from their own pockets during bankruptcy. We attempt to shed new light on this topic in several ways. First, this paper investigates firms’ financial investments as a novel conduit for risk-taking. We argue that financial assets can be better conduits for risk-taking than real assets. Compared with traditional real assets, trading in risky financial assets does not require an upfront investment in physical or human capital, can generate immediate/accelerated payoffs, and is less visible. In fact, financial assets are typically reported on the balance sheet as corporate cash holdings, and consequently, allow firms to camouflage their risk-taking as holdings of seemingly safe assets. Second, we highlight the importance of debt maturity and rollover risk in risk-taking. Third, we also provide novel evidence on the role of hedging in weakening the incentives to take risk and gamble for resurrection, complementing prior studies on hedging and firm policies or value.

14505418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505418.value: In 2013, the Financial Reporting Council (FRC), the United Kingdom’s independent audit regulator, issued a new standard increasing the information required to be included in the independent auditor’s report on financial statements (ISA700). Among other things, the new standard requires auditors to 1) describe the “assessed risks of material misstatement that were identified by the auditor”, 2) provide “an explanation of how the auditor applied the concept of materiality in planning and performing the audit”, and 3) provide “an overview of the scope of the audit…” While the new standard was issued with the aim of providing useful and important information for financial statement users, the FRC admittedly “deliberately set [the reporting requirements] at a high level with the view of encouraging auditors to innovate in their approach to reporting” (FRC 2016). As a result, the standing did not provide much detailed guidance on the substance or form of the auditor’s report. This flexibility and vague language makes it unclear what effect, if any, the new standard has on financial reporting. This paper examines the determinants and consequences of audit report changes following the extended disclosures requirements set forth by the FRC in 2013. The auditor’s report discloses the auditor’s opinion on whether the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. In practice, most audit reports give an unqualified opinion without additional explanatory language, so provide limited information to users of financial statements. Since ISA700 requires auditors to discuss material misstatements, materiality, and an overview of the scope of the audit, one likely direct consequence is that auditors’ reports increase in length. What is less clear, and the focus of this project is to examine whether difference in auditing and reporting quality prior to the implementation of ISA 700 result in difference in how ISA700 is applied, and whether ISA 700 disclosures subsequently improve reporting quality. 2013年，英國獨立審計監管機構財務報告委員會（FRC）發布了一項新標準，增加了包含在獨立審計師財務報表報告（ISA 700）中所需的信息。當中新準則要求審計師1）描述“審計師確定的重大錯報評估風險”，2）解釋“審計師如何在計劃和執行審計時應用重要性概念” ，3）在審計報告中提供“審計範圍的概述”。雖然頒布新標準的目的是向財務報表使用者提供有用和重要的信息，但FRC承認“故意將[報告要求] 概括列出，以鼓勵審計師用創新的報告方法”（ FRC 2016）。因此，該聲明並未就審計報告的內容或形式提供詳盡的指導。這種靈活性和模糊的語言使人們難以清楚新標準對財務報告的影響（如果有的話）。本文根據FRC在2013年提出的擴展披露要求，審查了審計報告變更的決定因素和後果。 審計師的報告披露了審計師對財務報表是否按照公認會計原則編制的意見。在實踐中，大多數審計報告在沒有附加解釋性語言的情況下給出了無保留意見，因此向財務報表使用者提供有限的信息。由於ISA700要求審計師討論重大錯誤陳述，重要性以及審計範圍的概述，因此可能直接導致審計師報告的長度增加。該項目的重點是檢查在實施ISA 700之前審計和報告質量的差異是否導致ISA700的應用方式不同，以及ISA 700披露是否隨後提高了報告質量。

14505418.label: Realisation of objectives
14505418.value: We have achieved all four objectives addressed in the proposal. I address each objective and its realization as follows: We hired two research assistants to assist in data collection and assist with empirical analysis. Since the reporting requirement is new, there is currently no database that captures the necessary data in machine readable form. We have located and retained a copy of annual reports for a large subset of companies publicly listed in the United Kingdom. We hired research assistants to extract and code information contained in the auditor’s report. ISA 700 requires auditors to disclose risks, materiality, and the scope of the audit. Therefore, collected data is related to these characteristics, such as FOG, bag of words, and similarity of auditor’s report. We collected the data from the largest 350 companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, but other data will be collected if available. We have collected total 1,593 firm-year auditor’s reports for 231 firms from 2010 to 2016. We extract and code information contained in the auditor’s report. ISA 700 requires auditors to disclose risks, materiality, and the scope of the audit, so collected data will related to these characteristics. We then use this information to examine the determinants and consequences of auditors’ report disclosures in relation to pre- and post-ISA 700 financial statement reporting quality. The first two objectives are to (1) locate and retain a copy of annual reports for a large subset of companies publicly listed in the United Kingdom and (2) extract and code auditor's report information for such firms. We have completed the first two objectives. The third objective is to examine pre-ISA 700 financial reporting quality to determine whether differences in pre-ISA 700 reporting quality is associated with differences in auditors' report disclosures under ISA 700. To examine the relation between pre-ISA 700 financial reporting quality and differences in auditor’s report disclosures under ISA 700, we estimate the following model: ISA_700_disclosure = α0 + α1*Pre_Quality + Controls + ε. (1) ISA_700_disclosure includes and the characteristics of the disclosures. We use FOG as the readability measure to compare the audit reports from the pre and post ISA 700 implementation periods. The Fog Index (FOG) is a widely used readability measure developed by Gunning (1952). In addition, we use similarity score of auditor’s reports (Similarity) to measure how auditor’s reports are qualitatively changed over time. We find that that differences in pre-ISA 700 reporting quality is associated with differences in auditors' report disclosures under ISA 700. Pre-ISA 700 earnings quality measured by the absolute value of discretionary accruals by Dechow et al. (1995) and accruals quality by Dechow and Dichev (2002) is positively associated with auditor’s report FOG index, suggesting that as earnings quality is poorer in the pre-ISA 700 period, auditors are more likely to write their reports in a more complicated way. In addition, we find a positive relation between pre-ISA 700 earnings quality and similarity score of auditor’s reports within the same industry, suggesting that auditors are more likely to write similar reports. The fourth objective is to examine whether differences in auditors' report disclosures under ISA 700 is associated with differences in reporting quality after ISA 700 adoption. To examine whether differences in the auditors’ reports disclosures under ISA 700 are associated with differences in reporting quality after ISA 700 adoption, the following model will be employed: Post_Quality = α0 + α1* ISA_700_disclosure + Controls + ε. (2) Post_Quality is measured using discretionary accruals based on Dechow and Dichev (2002) and Wysocki (2009). We find that auditor reports’ FOG index becomes more positively related to earnings quality in the post ISA 700 period, relative to the pre-period when we measure reporting quality with the absolute value of discretionary accruals. Similarly, we find that auditor reports’ similarity score becomes more positively related to earnings quality in the post ISA 700 period, relative to the pre-period when we measure reporting quality with accruals quality (Dechow and Dichev 2002). Our findings suggest that auditor reports’ complexity and similarity influence firms’ financial reporting period.

14505418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505418.value: We find that that differences in pre-ISA 700 reporting quality is associated with differences in auditors' report disclosures under ISA 700. Pre-ISA 700 earnings quality measured by the absolute value of discretionary accruals by Dechow et al. (1995) and accruals quality by Dechow and Dichev (2002) is positively associated with auditor’s report FOG index, suggesting that as earnings quality is poorer in the pre-ISA 700 period, auditors are more likely to write their reports in a more complicated way. In addition, we find a positive relation between pre-ISA 700 earnings quality and similarity score of auditor’s reports within the same industry, suggesting that auditors are more likely to write similar reports. Next, we examine whether differences in the auditors’ reports disclosures under ISA 700 are associated with differences in reporting quality after ISA 700 adoption. We find that auditor reports’ FOG index becomes more positively related to earnings quality in the post ISA 700 period, relative to the pre-period when we measure reporting quality with the absolute value of discretionary accruals. Similarly, we find that auditor reports’ similarity score becomes more positively related to earnings quality in the post ISA 700 period, relative to the pre-period when we measure reporting quality with accruals quality (Dechow and Dichev 2002). Our findings suggest that auditor reports’ complexity and similarity influence firms’ financial reporting period.

14505418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505418.value: Currently, we test for the association between ISA 700 implementation and financial reporting quality. To provide a causal evidence, we need some exogenous shocks.

14505418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505418.value: In this study, we provide insight that is useful to standard-setters on the effect of the new audit reporting standard. By expanding auditor reporting expanding across the globe, our findings on the disclosure effect of ISA 700 could influence standard-setters in other jurisdictions as the usefulness of client-specific information in the audit report is confirmed. Our project suggests that standard-setters monitor the long-term implementation of expanded auditor reporting and ensure that auditors do not revert to creating stale and boilerplate disclosures which may decrease the processing ability of the financial statement user.

14506218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506218.value: This project will analyse the entry of new investors during an asset bubble episode. Anecdotal evidence suggests that during the run-up a large number of residents who never trade before participate into the market; but they quit quickly when the bubble bursts. In this sense, bubble can be viewed as a socially viral event, which attracts an abnormally large amount of attention and participation of inexperienced investors. While it is widely observed, this phenomenon is to some extent neglected – the research has mainly focused on over-valuation and high trading volume during a bubble. One limitation is the lack of detailed data on participation of the population. This project aims to fill the gap by providing, to my knowledge, the first systematic evidence on the correlation between the entry of new investors and asset valuation. I plan to use the proprietary trading account data from the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SSE). The dataset, which covers the trading recording for all investors who have ever traded in SSE, allows me to accurately measure the participation of the population. With the detailed data, I can also extend the analysis to the individual stock level. In addition, the Chinese stock market experiences two bubble episodes in the recent decade, providing an ideal setting to study this topic. The project will begin with an analysis at the aggregate market level to confirm whether a bubble episode features a large number of newly registered investors. Next, I will extend the analysis to the cross-section of individual stocks; that is, whether an increase in new entries can predict higher subsequent returns during the booming period, but larger price drops when the bubble collapses. In addition, I will categorize new investors based on their account size, and examine which group exhibits the strongest tendency. The findings in the project will add important new evidence to the bubble literature. If the measure on the entry of new investors appears to be significantly correlated with asset over-valuation, it can be used as an early warning indicator for regulators.

14506218.label: Realisation of objectives
14506218.value: All five objectives have been well achieved. The results are generally consistent with the hypotheses that I developed in the proposal. In addition to the five objectives, we further design two tests to further highlight the importance of new investors in the pricing dynamics in the Chinese market. We examine whether the presence of new investors can explain return anomalies in China, and whether the trading by new investors induces some China-specific phenomenon, e.g., daily momentum. Please see the working paper for more detail.

14506218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14506218.value: The main research outcome of the project is the research paper, titled "New Investors and Anomalies in an Emerging Stock Market," (coauthored Zhenyu Gao, Wei A. Xiong, and Wei Xiong). In this paper, we analyze how large inflows of new investors and small presence of institutional investors differentiate an emerging stock market from more developed markets. By using account-level data of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, we find substantial heterogeneity among retail investors. The trading behaviors of new investors—not all retail investors— help to explain several anomalies in the Chinese stock market, including two China- specific phenomena—the lack of medium term price momentum and the presence of daily price momentum. Our results caution against treating all retail investors as noise traders and instead highlight the sharp effects of new investors. We find that new investors’ entries can negatively predict future market returns over different horizons. A flux of new investors appears to signal the overheating of the stock market and predict the reversal of subsequent market returns, implying that new investors are noise traders who contribute to the overall market sentiment. Furthermore, after entering stock markets, new investors’ trading plays an important role in the individual stock pricing dynamics. New investors’ net buying predicts negative stock returns cross-sectionally in the future one-, three-, six-, and twelve-month windows. Next, we examine whether the trading of new investors is one of the drivers of the anomalies in the Chinese market. We find this is indeed the case for value, turnover, and volatility effects. For example, the return predictability of EP decreases by 38%, Abn_Turnover by 34%, one-month return reversal by 17%, and Vol to insignificant. By comparison, controlling for net buying of experienced small or large retail investors does not change the return predictability of those variables. Furthermore, we link new investors to a China-specific phenomena: daily momentum. It is well known that the intermediate-term momentum effect does not exist in China. We document that, for the first time in the literature to our knowledge, Chinese stock prices do exhibit daily, i.e., stocks with high returns today tend to outperform tomorrow. But such price continuation pattern starts to reverse in a few days (less than a week). We show evidence that such patterns can be explained by the unique trading behavior of new investors.

14506218.value: This working paper has been presented at the University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Baptist University, University of Notre Dame, CKGSB, and Miami behavioral finance conference. We plan to continue to circulate and present this manuscript in various seminars and conferences over the next three months to collect more feedback. After another round of revision and polishing, we will submit the paper to one of the top 3 financial journals for publication in six months.

14506418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506418.value: 摘要 本項目中，本研究探討了分析師對於I/B/E/S共識實際收益不同意見的影響。眾所周知，I/B/E/S數據將不同意I/B/E/S共識收益的分析師排除在外（Gu & Chen，2004），這一行為很可能對使用預測準確性、偏差以及市場對收益不符預期反應的相關研究產生影響（Brown & Larocque，2013）。囙此，本研究以期對（1）I/B/E/S數據的選擇偏差（I/B/E/S中的分析師覆蓋率），（2）數據的局限性（共識抑制性收益）展開研究。 首先，文章檢驗了I/B/E/S資料庫系統排除/包含某些分析師是否影響使用I/B/E/S實際收益和預期收益的研究結論。進一步，本研究預期提出一種减少由於IBES數據中預測準確性或收益不符預期的使用給研究帶來的選擇性偏差。其次，已有研究假設所有分析師預測的收益都相同（共識實際收益），即使分析師預測的收益可能不同。本研究試圖檢驗，個人分析師對實際收益的定義是否與I/B/E/S提供的共識實際收益不同，以及他們的動機或特徵是否與共識實際收益的偏離有關。本研究證實了Brown和Larocque（2013）提出的措施，對已有文獻的貢獻在於提出一種更可靠的程式來糾正I/B/E/S帶來的偏差。

14506418.label: Realisation of objectives
14506418.value: 1. We find that I/B/E/S excludes analysts who disagree with the majority decision in their database. 2. We find that the difference in actual earnings between Investext and I/B/E/S is significantly different while the differences between inferred actual earnings and I/B/E/S or Investext are not significantly different. However, the comparison with inferred actual earnings should be interpreted with caution because the number of observations are only 85 observations. The estimation process of inferred actual earnings results in large drops in the number of observations because it requires 3 quarters’ earnings forecasts and annual earnings forecast to calculate the inferred actual earnings. Therefore, the use of inferred actual earnings can result in selection problem because many analysts do not issue quarterly earnings forecasts every quarter. 3. We document that the propensity that analysts issue actual earnings deviated from the I/B/E/S consensus actual earnings is associated with their incentives, ability, resources, and firm characteristics, missing forecasts, the number of industries following, brokerage size, all star status, recommendation upgrade, analyst following, growth opportunities, earnings volatility, number of business segments, institutional holdings and the number of institutional investors.

14506418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14506418.value: In this paper, we investigate the determinants and consequences of analysts’ issuing actual earnings deviated from I/B/E/S consensus actual earnings. We document that the propensity that analysts issue actual earnings deviated from the I/B/E/S consensus actual earnings is associated with their incentives, ability, resources, and firm characteristics, missing forecasts, the number of industries following, brokerage size, all star status, recommendation upgrade, analyst following, growth opportunities, earnings volatility, number of business segments, institutional holdings and the number of institutional investors. We show that the use of I/B/E/S actual earnings result in greater forecast errors than actual forecast errors, resulting in overestimating the effects of measures when researchers use I/B/E/S actual earnings. We call for future research on correcting the estimation bias arisen from the use I/B/E/S actual earnings.

14506418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14506418.value: We plan to expand the data by collecting excluded items further to provide more comprehensive evidence. We also plan to provide a way to adjust for the bias introduced by the I/B/E/S in a more efficient and effective manner.

14506418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14506418.value: Our paper finds that there is a systematic selection by the database provider (I/B/E/S). We recommend that researchers using the data from I/B/E/S should understand that the use of I/B/E/S actual earnings may result in a false conclusion at most or overestimate the effect.

14507018.label: Project Objectives
14507018.value: Advance risk perception theory by examining how people perceive their risks for noncommunicable diseases and disease risk factors. Examine how the current form of health education affects people's mental models noncommunicable diseases and their motivation to prevent the diseases. 14507018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14507018.value: Weight loss, exercise, and diet change are important means of disease prevention. A large body of research has explored how people pursue their weight loss goals, exercise plans, and diet changes (e.g., Fishbach, Dhar & Zhang 2006; Mead and Patrick 2016; Patrick & Hagtvedt 2012; Shiv and Fedorikhin 1999; Toure-Tillery & Fishback 2015; Woolley and Fishbach 2016). In the proposed research, we will examine behavioral changes from a new perspective: how people create mental models of such behaviors as a way to prevent disease. Because diet changes, weight loss, and exercise are best known for their effectiveness in reducing the risk of noncommunicable diseases, the study of mental models of disease prevention offers an excellent perspective to understand people’s decision to pursue diet changes and weight loss. More importantly, noncommunicable diseases have some idiosyncratic characteristics that make the studying of mental models of disease prevention a theoretically and practically meaningful topic. Specifically, noncommunicable diseases are not associated with one cause, but rather a set of “risk factors,” and the set of risk factors causes multiple diseases and disease outcomes. As a result, there could be great variations in the way people judge (1) the risk of a disease, (2) the severity of a disease, and (3) the causality between behavioral changes (e.g., weight loss, exercise, and diet change) and disease prevention. The primary objectives of this research will be to (a) identify systematic patterns of how people make the above judgments, (b) explain those patterns using research on risk perceptions and mental model theories, and (c) develop and test effective interventions that help people to form accurate judgments, thereby cultivating stronger motivation and persistence in their pursuit of disease prevention through lifestyle changes.

14600118.label: Project Objectives
14600118.value: Collect first-hand data of excavated turquoise artifacts at Jiahu and Erlitou through close-up photography and digital microscopy to document tool marks. Conduct geological provenance studies across well-known turquoise mines in China using Raman spectroscopy, XRF, LA-ICP-AES, and TIMS. The mines are located across the Luonan County in Shaanxi, Yungaisi in Hubei, and Xichuan County in Henan. Two prehistoric mines discovered by Co-I Yanxiang Li (Co-I Li), Laziya and Hekou in Luonan County, will be central to our project. Lead and strontium isotope analysis will be the main methodology used to source the geological origins of these artifacts. Systematically compare the stone tools used to make turquoise objects at Jiahu and Erlitou with those at Alta Vista in Mexico, such as hammers, grinding stones, and abrasives, to better understand turquoise production processes. Conduct in-depth experiments to replicate the turquoise round disks found at Jiahu, and the beveled-edge and inlay technology of ancient mosaics of the Erlitou culture, in order to understand turquoise production technology of ancient China. Conduct chemical analyses to determine the chemical composition of the binding agents on bronze plaques of the Erlitou culture. Currently, there is very little information in the western literature for prehistoric turquoise in China. The result of this project will be compiled in multilingual archaeological publications, with a high-resolution photographic database of the prehistoric turquoise artifacts and production technologies studied.

14600118.label: Realisation of objectives
14600118.value: When the pandemic began in early 2020, restrictions on international travel made it impossible to conduct field trips. Research in mainland China and overseas was largely affected due to the closure of institutions, universities, and laboratories. Co-investigators and research assistants were forced to work remotely. Nonetheless, we produced fruitful archaeological findings and completed the core work of this project. We completed the most comprehensive techno-typological categorization of the Jiahu and Erlitou turquoises. We extensively documented the earliest turquoises known in the world (dated to ~9,000 years BP) by using high-resolution close-up photography. Co-I Chung Tang (Co-I Tang) and Co-I Juzhong Zhang (Co-I J. Zhang) visited the Henan Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology, and systematically documented 293 objects. We focused on burial M55, where over 200 pieces of turquoise (3-5mm) were unearthed on the neck and upper thighs of a child. The largest and oldest turquoise pendant, dated to 8,800 BP, was thoroughly documented. Through technological analysis, we concluded that Jiahu turquoise beads were likely made in situ; indicating a workshop could be discovered in future excavations. Moreover, the large pendant and flat beads were sophisticated made, requiring refined production technology; showcasing the advancement of the locally developed turquoise culture in the Yellow River Basin. Additionally, we (including Co-Is Tang, Hong Xu, and Haitao Zhao) categorized over 10,000 Erlitou turquoise workshop artifacts by using high-resolution close-up photography and digital microscopy. Other associated tools, including lithics and tesserae polishing stones, were heavily documented. We conducted archaeological experiments to produce turquoise tesserae, and recreated the beveled-edge technology found in Erlitou culture. With a massive amount of archaeological data, we completed over 300 pages of the monograph “二里頭龍形器與綠松石作坊". Overall, we photographed over 100,000 high-resolution images of Jiahu and Erlitou artifacts and its tool marks, making it the largest database of prehistoric turquoise in China. Our collaborators yielded fruitful research in regards to turquoise geological provenance. Co-I J. Zhang’s PhD student Wang Hou conducted non-destructive X-Ray Fluorescence analysis (XRF) and X-ray crystallography (XRD) on 279 Jiahu artifacts and 35 Zhushan samples to determine its mineral compositions and to compare the result with mines in China. The result indicated that Jiahu turquoise was perhaps procured from multiple sources. As Jiahu is near Lushan where phosphate and copper mines are present, this might have provided the geological condition for turquoise mineralization. Co-Is Yanxiang Li (Co-I Li) and Dengyi Zhang (Co-I D. Zhang) measured stable lead and strontium isotopes of Erlitou turquoise using thermal ionization mass spectrometry, and conducted on-site investigations of ancient mines. They clarified the relationship between Erlitou and the prehistoric mines in Hubei, Henan, and northern Shaanxi, and concluded that the Luonan mines were associated with Erlitou. Professor Yang Mingxing of the China University of Geosciences (Wuhan) also participated in our project. He performed scientific and technological analyses (Infrared, Raman, and Ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy) on 20 Erlitou turquoise artifacts. He stated that Erlitou had possibly procured material from Hubei, Henan, and northern Shaanxi. In March 2021, along with Prof. Yang, Co-Is Tang, Xu, H. Zhao investigated a modern turquoise mine in Zhushan, Hubei. Turquoise in this region were not only found in caves, but they were also formed visibly outside at the mountain rocks; some of them were over 10 centimeters. However, due to the natural formation of turquoise in this region, raw materials could only be found at an elevation of approximately 900 meters, while there was virtually no turquoise formed at the foot of the mountain. A miner stated that although rare, turquoise could also be procured in the nearby rivers. Interestingly, upon analyzing the Erlitou raw materials, we noted that a small amount of them could have been procured from the river basin. Chemical analyses and investigation of prehistoric and modern mines aided our understanding in ancient resource procurement strategies. Due to the pandemic and Chinese museum policies, we were unable to collect binding agent samples from prehistoric turquoise inlaid objects. China has also imposed stricter regulation in recent years. We tried to overcome this by investigating the production technology of tesserae morphology and its relation to the binding agent. Using close-up photography and microscopy, we observed that Erlitou tesserae had a larger upper face than its lower counterpart, with the side being slated and wedge shaped. The beveled-edge allowed the tesserae to be seamlessly aligned on a three-dimensional base. Using many scattered tesserae in the Erlitou turquoise workshop, we sorted the pieces by its geometry and used rice glue to connect these experimental tesserae. These archaeological experiments gave us a deeper understanding of prehistoric tessellation technology. Closure of international borders affected our comparative analysis between prehistoric China and Mesoamerica. Fortunately, before Covid-19, Co-I Emiliano Melgar (Co-I Melgar) and Research Assistant Tang Hok Man Maya (RA Tang) met and discussed our project. RA Tang visited museums including Chaco Culture National Historical Park, the Turquoise Museum, and a Native American flea market to document pre-Columbian and modern Native American turquoise objects. In particular, Chaco Canyon is a significant pre-Columbian archaeological site of the ancient Pueblos. It served as the largest turquoise trading network in North America, where over 56,000 pieces were discovered. Even though we were unable to visit each other’s respective institutions, we continuously conducted research separately, and kept in close touch with Co-I Melgar for academic exchange. He is collaborating with us on the monograph, where his research will be translated. This will strengthen our comparative study between East and West. Additionally, we found other ways to enrich our Mesoamerican archaeology research. In June 2022, Co-I Tang met with Professor David Freidel of Washington University in Saint Louis to discuss Mayan turquoise culture. Prof. Freidel is an archaeologist specializing in the emergence of government in the lowland Maya of southeastern Mexico and Central America. Furthermore, we extensively documented literature regarding Mesoamerican turquoise at the Orlando Museum of Art in Florida, US. Kin Sum LI took the PI’s role in 2020. Although he could not conduct any field trips, he also prepared several publications based on co-I Tang Chung’s research findings. He mainly summarized the research progress thus far and indicated future major orientations for studying the relationship between turquoise and jade processing techniques and bronze post-casting processing. Our research thus far has been compiled in multilingual archaeological publications. In particular, our monograph will be the first publication on the subject matter in China. This book will be the first comprehensive publication regarding turquoise workshop in Chinese academia and perhaps the world’s first comprehensive turquoise archaeological report. Although our research progress suffered from some setbacks, we received significant support from our Chinese collaborators. Some of our collaborators have even taken the initiative to cover the cost for chemical analyses, accommodation, and travel expenses. Despite many uncertainties since early 2020, we were able to complete all of our objectives. We created the most comprehensive categorization of the Jiahu and Erlitou turquoises. Chemical analyses and on-site investigations provided us with clues to prehistoric procurement strategies. Extensive documentation of Erlitou stone tools combined with data from the American Southwest and Mesoamerica enriched our understanding of turquoise production processes. Experiments were conducted to replicate turquoise pieces and its beveled-edge technology. Multilingual publications regarding Jiahu and Erlitou are being edited.

14600118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600118.value: Our research outcome has completely redefined the study of turquoise culture in prehistory. We completed the most comprehensive database of turquoise unearthed from Jiahu and Erlitou. Jiahu turquoise is dated close to 9,000 years BP. The study in Jiahu serves as a pioneering research on turquoise production technology. We speculate that in future, even earlier turquoise objects could be found in sites dated to 10,000 years BP in China. For the first time, we established a model of procurement and production technology found in the Erlitou turquoise workshop. We comprehensively documented over 10,000 pieces of turquoise tubes, beads, tesserae, and special ornaments, and completed over 300 pages of the Erlitou monograph. This book is the first comprehensive publication regarding turquoise workshops in Chinese academia. In 2021, many exciting artifacts were unearthed. In an Erlitou elite tomb, we excavated thousands of tesserae formed into a clothing-like object, and over ten cicada-shaped turquoise and earrings were unearthed. Co-I Qin Xiaoli studied the production and consumption pattern of Erlitou turquoise tube beads and inlays to better understand the social and political system of the Erlitou political system. Erlitou turquoise objects, pottery ceremonial vessels, and jade yazhang were simultaneously transported over long distances, showing the regional political impact of Erlitou culture. We performed chemical analyses and on-site investigations to determine the turquoise geological provenances. Co-I J. Zhang and his team conducted XRF and XRD on Jiahu artifacts, and found that Jiahu turquoise might have been sourced from multiple mines. Using Pb-Sr isotope analysis, Co-I D. Zhang concluded that Erlitou turquoise has a relatively single source, one of which is from Laziya, Luonan. Prof. Yang conducted non-destructive analyses on 20 Erlitou turquoise, and found that Erlitou turquoise was perhaps procured from Hubei, Henan, and northern Shaanxi. We conducted comparative analysis on the social values and consumption pattern of turquoise in Central Asia, the Middle East, and Central America. Since the earliest turquoise ornament found in Jiahu in the early Neolithic to the Erlitou phase in the Bronze Age, the combination of turquoise and bronze was a distinctive characteristic in China; while in the West, in Egypt, turquoise was inlaid onto gold and silver. Later in Mesoamerica, turquoise was incorporated with a variety of minerals and shellfish; showcasing the emergence of traditional characteristics across the world.

14600118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600118.value: From the prehistoric to the historic period, turquoise played a significant role for its cultural, symbolic, economic, and religious importance across the world. The combination of turquoise with bronze technology found in the pre-Qin period became a distinctive feature of Chinese civilization. Our research shows that turquoise inlay technology in China and Central America share similarities, thus the production technology in respective regions require further in-depth research. As turquoise technologies also existed in Central Asia and the Middle East, our findings formed a holistic picture of the early history of turquoise. International collaborations will be needed to continue strengthening our understanding of the role turquoise played in the emergence of ancient civilizations. As turquoise is highly prized in modern society, it holds a great interest for many. We now can educate the public regarding the history of turquoise and its role in the formation of Chinese civilization. In March 2022, we participated in the exhibition ???????????? in Panlongcheng Museum, Wuhan. It attracted a large audience and received rave reviews. In the future, it is of great significance to further promote the history of Chinese turquoise culture across the world.

14600118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600118.value: This project sheds light on the history of turquoise from the early Neolithic in Jiahu (9,000BP) to the Bronze Age in Erlitou (1750-1540BC) in China. As technological analyses of turquoise production are scarce, our approach using lithic analysis was an important breakthrough. Jiahu turquoise is currently the oldest archaeological discovery in the world. Its objects are sophisticated, showcasing the advancement of the locally developed turquoise culture in the Yellow River Basin since the early Neolithic. In Bronze Age Erlitou, turquoise was incorporated with bronze technology. As only elites could own such precious objects, it manifested as one of the material symbols of prestige. In the turquoise workshop situated in the Erlitou palace, we analyzed over 10,000 artifacts, and studied the chain of operation from its resource procurement to the final polishment. We performed chemical analyses to better understand procurement strategies, and concluded that the Jiahu and Erlitou turquoises were likely mined in Hubei, Henan, and northern Shaanxi. We conducted comparative analyses of turquoise for its social value and consumption pattern with other ancient civilizations. China is currently the world?s largest exporter of turquoise. The research on ancient turquoise has the potential for decades of studies.

14600218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14600218.value: 同行評審在數學界中的實踐

14600218.label: Project Objectives
14600218.value: Firstly, to challenge widely held beliefs about mathematical practice. While mathematics is often portrayed as the paradigm of absolute certainty, it is also acknowledged that almost every published paper contains mistakes. Furthermore, while mathematicians often claim that ‘in principle’ it should be possible to check the correctness of mathematical results, they also acknowledge that ‘in practice’ this is difficult to do and that there are only a few people who actually can understand many proofs. This project will respecify our understanding of mathematical certainty as admitting ‘degrees of correctness’ (for, e.g., ‘Philosophia Mathematica’). Secondly, to understand the relation between establishing the ‘significance’ and checking the ‘correctness’ of results in modern science. Some new journals (e.g., ‘PLOS ONE’) have argued against judging the perceived significance of scientific papers and only assess their technical soundness. In almost direct contrast, mathematicians at elite journals have established the practice of ‘quick opinions’ that asks referees to judge the importance of a paper before even considering its correctness. The project will investigate how mathematicians distinguish between judging the significance and correctness of a paper and investigate whether this is handed differently at journals of different ‘levels’ (for, e.g., ‘Social Studies of Science’). Finally, to demonstrate the role of trust in modern science. Recent studies have shown that despite the many criticisms of peer review, scientists in general still trust ‘in’ peer review. However, what about the role of trust ‘within’ the process of peer review? Refereeing is single-blind, and since checking technical arguments is very challenging, referees acknowledge that they rely on authors’ reputation in checking the correctness of their arguments. In turn, editors are trying to find referees they trust, relying on both personal contacts and the reputation of potential referees, but also assessing referees’ perceived ‘closeness’ to the subject area of an author. Editors also rely on ‘trusted experts’ to extend their trust to technical referees, thereby creating networks of trust. While modern epistemology has characterised the nature of scientific knowledge through the absence of trust, this project will follow Shapin (1994) to investigate in which sense modern science has become more trusting (for, e.g., ‘American Sociological Review’).

14600218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600218.value: All academics have deeply held, sometimes vitriolic, opinions on peer review. Many grudgingly accept that peer review remains the main (if not the best) form of evaluating the merits of academic research and grant proposals. But a growing movement views peer review with the same incredulity that Albert Einstein once did when he retracted his paper from a journal that deigned to send it out to ‘specialists’. They argue that peer review stifles true creativity and meaningful research. Due to its importance, peer review has been studied extensively. Scholarship has paid particular attention to whether single-blind peer review is biased, and to whether peer review is scientific and reliable. Yet the lion’s share of these studies are quantitative, which provide a fascinating bird’s eye view of peer review, but do not deal with how the tensions and contradictions of peer review are managed in practice. How are referees chosen? How do journals evaluate the referees’ evaluations? These questions can only be properly addressed by a qualitative study on peer review. This project explores the peer review process in journals in pure mathematics. Mathematics offers a fascinating case for two reasons. First, peer review in mathematics works well. Mathematicians appreciate peer review as a stamp of approval—a form of professional validation of the significance and correctness of their research. Second, peer review in mathematics offers an extreme case of peer review. The stakes are higher than in other disciplines, because published results are treated as settled (there are no calls for replication in mathematics). The process also takes more time and effort than in any other discipline. Furthermore, the organisation of peer review in mathematics separates the evaluation of the result’s significance from checking its correctness. A qualitative study of such an extreme case brings into stark focus aspects of peer review that are present across any discipline. My preliminary research highlights the extent to which trust pervades the entire process of peer review in mathematics. Owing to the laborious nature of peer review in mathematics, referees need to trust the authors. Likewise, editors need to find ‘trustworthy’ referees to determine both the significance and correctness of the research. Peer review in mathematics highlights the existence of networks of trust and is thus an ideal setting to study what Shapin (1994: 16) has termed “the invisibility of trust-relationships in modern science”. 所有學者都對同行評審機制有其堅信的（有時甚至是嚴苛的）意見。許多人勉強接受同行評審仍然是評估學術研究的優劣、以及申請研究補助金的主要（雖然並不是最好）形式。然而，現時也出現了一種趨勢，以懷疑態度看待同行評審，就像阿爾伯特·愛因斯坦（Albert Einstein）也曾撤回他一篇期刊文章，這文章原本是以所謂的「專家」為對象。這些質疑的聲音認為，同行評審會扼殺真正有創意、有意義的研究。 由於其重要性，同行評審已被廣泛研究。過去學者們已特別關注到以下兩個方面的問題：單盲同行評審是否存有偏見，以及同行評審是否科學與可靠。這些研究大部分以定量作為方法，為我們提供了一幅對同行評審絕佳的鳥瞰圖。然而，這些研究並沒有涉及如何處理在運作中同行評審存在的張力和矛盾。如何選擇專家學者作為評審人？期刊如何評估評審人的評估？這些問題只能通過定性研究才能妥善處理。 是次研究是探討純數學期刊中的同行評審過程。數學界是研究此現象的上佳個案，原因有二：首先，數學同行評審運作良好。數學家欣然將同行評審視為一種獲得認可的標誌，即一種對其研究重要性和正確性的專業認證。其次，數學界的同行評審是同行評審機制的極端個案。相對於其他學科，同行評審對數學家關係重大，因為發表的研究結果就會被視為最終極（在數學界中並不可以要求重複驗證其研究結果）。與其他學科相比，數學期刊中的評審過程也需要花費更多時間和精力。此外，數學界的同行評審的組織形式還將評估研究發現的重要性與檢查研究的正確性這兩部分分開。對這種極端個案的定性研究，將引導我們看到同行評審的重要層面，這些層面是存在於各個學科中。 我的初步研究成果展示了在多大程度上，信任是貫穿在整個數學同行評審過程中。由於數學同行評審需要耗費大量精力，評審人需要信任作者。同樣，編輯也需要找到“值得信賴的”評審人，以此來確定研究的重要性和正確性。這一發現昭示了數學領域中同伴評審中信任網絡的存在，為研究Shapin (1994:16) “現代科學中信任關係的隱形特質”提供理想的環境。

14600218.label: Realisation of objectives
14600218.value: DATA COLLECTION As stated in my proposal, “The aim is to conduct semi‐structured interviews with 80 editors (i.e., members of editorial boards) of mathematics journals from different ‘levels’ in the perceived hierarchy of journals (in order to see whether peer review is handled differently at the ‘top’ or ‘bottom’ level of the spectrum).” In the end, I conducted even more interviews than planned: I conducted 95 interviews, both in‐ person (N=49) and via telephone/video‐conferencing (N=46). In‐person interviews were conducted in Hong Kong (N=5), during a two‐week trip to the US (N=21) and during several trips to Europe (N=23). 87 interviewees had worked as editors (often of more than one journal), while 8 worked for journal publishers. The majority of the editors worked in North America (N=39) and Europe (N=37), while some worked in Asia or Africa (N=10) and one in Australia. The 95 interviews were all transcribed and formatted, producing 1600 pages of double‐spaced interview transcripts. The materials served as the main data for the analysis. I also collected 120 ‘quick opinions’, 100 technical reports, and 50 emails. In total 600 pages of written reports, which supplemented the interviews for the analysis. ANALYSIS The aim of this analysis has been to explore the interviews from the perspective of three objectives, namely (1) ‘mathematical correctness in practice’, (2) ‘the separation of judging significance and checking correctness’, and (3) ‘the role of trust within peer review’. For the first objective, ‘mathematical correctness in practice’, I have approached this from two directions. On the one hand, I have collected accounts of my interviewees in their role as reviewers discussing the variety of ways in which they would check the correctness of the results and proofs of papers they have reviewed. On the other hand, I have assembled the ways that my interviewees describe the difference in the ‘perceived certainty’ of results published in peer‐reviewed journals and those that are available on (non‐peer‐reviewed) pre‐print servers. For the second objective, ‘the separation of judging significance and checking correctness’, I have structured the analysis around the unique practice of ‘quick opinions’ in mathematical peer review. I have collected accounts of the emergence of quick opinions, the reasons for using them, the status and recipiency of quick opinions (are they written for authors, editors, or editorial boards), as well as general views of the benefits and dangers of using quick opinions. For the third objective, ‘the role of trust within peer review’, I have explored this from the perspective of both authors and referees. On the one hand, refereeing in mathematics is single‐blind and the name of the author is thus taken into account in judging the paper’s importance and correctness. As one of my interviewees put it: “in areas like this you create a name for yourself not for nothing”. However, authors also do not just gain a ‘positive’ reputation, but also a ‘negative’ one, e.g., for being hasty and frequently making mistakes. On the other hand, editors frequently spoke about the challenge of finding “referees I trust”. It seems that editors often personally know the experts that they ask for quick opinions, or are at least familiar with their work. Editors also distinguish in what respects to trust referees. In particular, although they may not trust someone ‘close’ to an author with judging the significance of a paper, that same person may be trusted to check its correctness. Finally, editors may extend their trust. A common practice is for a handling editor to ask a (senior) expert for an initial quick opinion, as well as a suggestion for another (junior) expert who would be able to check the correctness of a paper, resulting in a situation in which “you trust the person recommending the person” (as one of my interviewees put it).

This project will respecify our understanding of mathematical certainty as admitting ‘degrees of correctness’ (for, e.g., ‘Philosophia Mathematica’).

Secondly, to understand the relation between establishing the ‘significance’ and checking the ‘correctness’ of results in modern science. Some new journals (e.g., ‘PLOS ONE’) have argued against judging the perceived significance of scientific papers and only assess their technical soundness. In almost direct contrast, mathematicians at elite journals have established the practice of ‘quick opinions’ that asks referees to judge the importance of a paper before even considering its correctness. The project will investigate how mathematicians distinguish between judging the significance and correctness of a paper and investigate whether this is handed differently at journals of different ‘levels’ (for, e.g., ‘Social Studies of Science’).

Finally, to demonstrate the role of trust in modern science. Recent studies have shown that despite the many criticisms of peer review, scientists in general still trust ‘in’ peer review. However, what about the role of trust ‘within’ the process of peer review? Refereeing is single-blind, and since checking technical arguments is very challenging, referees acknowledge that they rely on authors’ reputation in checking the correctness of their arguments. In turn, editors are trying to find referees they trust, relying on both personal contacts and the reputation of potential referees, but also assessing referees’ perceived ‘closeness’ to the subject area of an author. Editors also rely on ‘trusted experts’ to extend their trust to technical referees, thereby creating networks of trust. While modern epistemology has characterised the nature of scientific knowledge through the absence of trust, this project will follow Shapin (1994) to investigate [...].

14600218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600218.value: Peer review has never been a uniform practice, but is now more diverse than ever. Despite a vast literature, little is known of how different disciplines organise peer review. This project has been the first in-depth sociological study of how peer review is organized in pure mathematics. On the basis of 95 qualitative interviews with editors and publishers and several hundred written reports the project has analysed the organisation of peer review in pure mathematics. There have made two major contributions: Firstly, to the sociology of mathematics: Mathematics is often seen as the only academic discipline that can provide absolute certainty, since arguments in mathematics rely on deductive proof rather than empirical evidence as in the natural sciences. Yet mathematicians acknowledge that the published literature contains many mistakes. The place where errors could, and perhaps should, be discovered is when they go through peer review. In practice, mathematicians attach different degrees of certainty to different papers. They value peer review, because it “adds a bit of certainty” to papers. Mathematicians also attach degrees of certainty depending on the reputation of authors, whose track record can be both positive and negative. This project has shown that there can be disagreement among mathematicians. Such disagreement not only concerns the importance of a paper (which is often seen as a more ‘subjective’ judgement), but also the question whether a particular argument constitutes a proof or not. This project highlights the importance of the role of the mathematical community when it comes accepting arguments as proofs and assigning certainty to results. Publishing an argument in a peer-reviewed journal is often only the first step in getting a result accepted. Results get accepted if they stand the test of time and are used by other mathematicians. Secondly, to the sociology of evaluation and peer review. This project has uncovered a discipline-specific form of peer review in mathematics referred to as ‘quick opinions’. This involves asking (senior) experts about a paper’s importance, and only after positive evaluation sending the paper for a full review (which most importantly means checking the paper’s correctness). Quick opinions constitute a form of ‘importance only’ peer review and are thus the opposite of the ‘soundness only’ approach at mega-journals such as PLOS ONE. Quick opinions emerged in response to increasing submissions and the fact that checking correctness in mathematics is particularly time-consuming. Quick opinions are informal and are often only addressed to editors. They trade on, indeed reinforce, a journal hierarchy, where journal names are often used as a ‘members’ measurement system’ to characterise importance. Finally, quick opinions highlight that a key function of the peer-reviewed journal today, apart from validation and filtration, is ‘designation’ – giving authors items on their CV.

14600218.value: To finish the third objective, ‘the role of trust within peer review’, which I plan to do in 2023.

14600218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600218.value: Journal peer review consists of the evaluation of manuscripts by others working in the same field. It is widely acknowledged that peer review is not a uniform practice, but differs from discipline to discipline. Yet little is known of how different disciplines organise peer review. This project has been the first to study peer review in pure mathematics on the basis of 95 qualitative interviews with editors and several hundred written reports. There have been two major findings: Firstly, mathematicians attach different degrees of certainty to different papers. They value peer review, because it “adds a bit of certainty, but publishing an paper in a peer-reviewed journal is often only the first step in getting a result accepted. Results get accepted if they stand the test of time and are used by other mathematicians. Secondly, mathematicians have institutionalized a discipline-specific form of peer review, which they term ‘quick opinions’: asking experts only about a paper’s importance in order to decide whether to send out the paper for a ‘full review’ (which most importantly means checking the paper’s correctness). These ‘quick opinions’ are thus almost the opposite of the ‘soundness only’ peer review approach at mega-journals such as PLOS ONE.

14600618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600618.value: This project will examine one of the most popular forms of youth entertainment in China, namely, online fiction. For this new form of literature, youth are not only readers or fans; they can be amateur or full-time professional writers. Based on in-depth interviews with writers and fans, study of text of online novel and a one-year virtual ethnography, this project will analyze the cultural production and consumption of online fiction and the how youth identity crystallizes around popular fiction. Starting with Chinese fiction from the tomb-raiding genre, The Lost Tomb (online on Qidian since 2006 and with a record 200 million hit rate online), online fiction has become a major cultural and commercial form, attracting capital investment and translating into other commercial forms. Writing online novels has also become trendy for young amateur writers, some of whom aspire to be professional and celebrity writers. First, for media capital, purchasing the intellectual property (IP) of online fiction and developing it into other popular cultural forms constitutes a new form of cultural production. For example, the original IP of The Lost Tomb was developed into online animation (2015); an online television series (2015-2017) (in Aqiyi’s portal, with 160 million watching the first five minutes of release); and movies (2016) (with ticket sales of RMB1 billion) in addition to its printed version (over 12 million sales). The fandom of The Lost Tomb continues to evolve. Second, online fiction is less restricted than printed publications such as books and magazines. For young readers, with their active reading, they consume cultural content that exhibits rich imagination and occasionally goes beyond the confined hegemonic discourse of the Internet and social media, which are closely monitored by the state. Third, for young writers, they narrate their perception of China and relatively free to express their personal and social pleasure and frustration, imagination and fantasy, and utopia and ideals by contributing their fictional writings, and in general they enjoy a higher degree of creative freedom. In theoretical terms, this project will examine the new digital habitat of online fiction, the blurred boundaries between cultural consumption and production, the values and imaginations embedded in these online fictional texts, and the development of youth identity around online fiction, and animation, television series and movies adapted from online fiction. By doing so, this project will shed light on the formation of Chinese youth culture in the current socio-political landscape of China. 研究試圖闡釋當代中國青少年的網絡小說消費和生產行為。在這網絡年代，青少年不僅是作為讀者或粉絲閱讀網上內容，他們也可投身成為網上作家或文化的生產者，是次研究通過網上作家/青少年的訪問，網絡小說內容的文本分析和一整年的虛擬(網絡)民族誌的方法，研究青少年網上社群的形式和身份認同，其中一個最明顯例子是網上的《盜墓筆記》，自2006年以來《盜墓筆記》在網絡小說平台《起點》已經累積超過二百萬的點擊。網絡小說已經成為其中一種最商業化的文化行為，不少資本紛紛投資網上小說平台。第一，對青少年人來說，可以成為業餘寫手是一種文化活動和娛樂行為，當中，也有不少成為專業作家。對於媒介資本，購買、轉授和開發網絡小說的知識版權成為新興的媒介和文化投資。同一個版權，已經可轉化成《愛奇藝》上的網劇(2015-2017)、電影(2016)和一千二百萬本的實體小說。第二，網絡小說是中國年青人的最主要文化消費之一，當中，有多少閱讀者的詮釋是符合或跟主流的意識形態衝突是研究問題所在。第三，青少年作為主體，他們究竟透過網絡寫作如何表示他們對中國的觀感和想象，也可透過他們的網上創作體現出來。在理論層面，這研究分析新的網絡小說的生態，文化消費和生產的模糊邊界、網絡文本內的價值觀和世界觀、以及青少年網絡社群和身份的形成。長遠來說，這研究有助理解中國的青少年文化的趨勢和發展。

14600618.label: Realisation of objectives
14600618.value: This completed project is a successful research collaboration among the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), Beijing Normal University (BNU), and Tsinghua University (TU). It examines the production/consumption of online novel writing, which is one of the most popular forms of youth entertainment and creative industries in China. The research also the cooperation among research students from three universities (Boris Pun from CUHK, Lei Lin from BNU, and Yue Wang from TU). The importance of the study is evidenced by the fact that by the time the project was approved, users of online novel writing in China had reached 460 million readers. However, since 2020, the entire research plan has been affected by the pandemic. The research team then devised research plans to conduct interviews in a mixed mode. Thanks to the research collaborators who are in mainland China, we were able to conduct most of the interviews face-to-face and online across the country, while we also had a clear division of labor to tackle different fieldwork online and offline. With these newly planned strategies, we successfully completed all fieldwork as stated and responded to all three research objectives: (1) To meet Objective 1, it required the study of (i) a major site of production/consumption of online fiction, (ii) the extended production sites of animation, television dramas, and movies, and (iii) the study of fans and fandom formation. (i) The study of Yuewen, a holding of Tencent which owns major online writing platforms, including Qidian, QQ Reading, Chuangshi, and Hongxiu, represents major fieldwork done to meet this first objective. While most academics have no access to this largest online novel company, the Co-Is had a connection with Yuewen at the management level. The research team visited Yuewen’s headquarter, spending three days interviewing all levels of personnel—including the managing editor who liaises with the authors so they can understand how Yuewen manages cultural production on an industry scale. The actual production of online fiction depends on writers whom we conceptualize as a new form of worker, namely, creative labor. In 2019, we began the research with 10 in-depth interviews with writers in Beijing, Nanjing, and Suzhou. Next, in 2020, a national survey of 399 online fiction writers was conducted to give a comprehensive view of their production; this represented additional fieldwork beyond the study’s original proposal to better understand the phenomenon. With the consent of the writers in the survey, we further completed nine in-depth online interviews of different types (with variances in gender, age, fame, genres of writing, and geographic location) of writers. In short, combining the data from the industry and those from the authors, we were able to accurately describe this mode of platformized production by the authors. (ii) The study of extended cultural forms necessitated access to IP experts and illustrated how the IP of online novels is being developed and used by the existing creative industries. In this regard, the research team interviewed IP developers in Hong Kong, Beijing, and Chengdu, where IP businesses are very active, and the producers, managers, directors in Changsha, an entertainment hub where Hunan Satellite Television is located. With around 15 high-level personnel interviews, the team gained important insights into the process and business logic of IP production and the consequence of such production/consumption. (iii) In terms of our investigation of cultural consumption, this involved identification of and then interviewing fans online who followed these writers. The research team focused on those fans considered in our case studies of writers. The number of fans varied in different cases. The strategy aimed to analyze fans’ interactions with the writers, what content they are interested in, and their imagination of the lifestyle of those writers. Their perception constitutes part of the youth culture as reflected by online writing production/consumption. To meet Objective 2 which is about the content/theme in the novels, the research team explored more than 20 online novels and finally selected three important cases for textual analysis: (i) The first case study chosen was Chunzhen Niandai (literally meaning the age of innocence), which is the young author’s self-exploration of the meaning of life. The research team conducted a textual analysis of the story (and interview with the author and fans), and explored how the story rationalizes and conceives of environmental change in order to reveal the contradictions involved in the relationship between citizenship and social development. (ii) The second case was Lingaoqiming, a story of modern people going back into the past to build a new empire that illustrates the utopian ideals in the minds of contemporary Chinese. However, the governance, law, and culture of the new empire was far from ideal and reflected a dystopian theme that the team discussed with the author and his fans for two days in our fieldwork. The contradiction between the ideal and the actual dystopian world is what the team illustrated in this case study. (iii) In addition to exploring the theme of contradiction, the team illustrated that literature in modern China, even in the digital age, does not necessarily reveal social contradiction. In the study, we also looked at how traditional classic literature, such as Shanhaijing, which has been newly reinterpreted, represented, repackaged, and reproduced, not just for commercial purposes, but for innovating, perpetuating, and rejuvenating traditional values. To meet Objective 3, which is about the long-term impact of this culture, it required multiple levels of data, triangulation, and theoretical synthesis. We identified three basic factors related to Chinese youth culture: (i) youth as creative labor working online, (ii) formation of a new lifestyle as a result of the new working mode, and (iii) the impact from the everyday use of digital platforms: (i) The new mode of working as online writers—relatively free from institutional constraints—was studied utilizing a survey questionnaire and in-depth interviews that gauged the writers self-perceived creativity and working conditions (e.g., income, hours of working, etc.). With the assistance from ByteDance (owner of TikTok), the same questionnaire survey we used previously (with 1,000 samples and 50 interviews) was applied to short video online producers on Douyin in China for the purpose of comparing the nature of creative labor among different cultural forms. In addition, 20 interviews with Hong Kong and Guangzhou online animators/comic illustrators were conducted for comparison. This was to ensure that the study had covered all extended cultural forms, as stated in the proposal. (ii) Chinese youth’s new lifestyle was mainly captured by the survey, which was designed not to just measure the working conditions of online writers. Writers’ satisfaction with their living conditions, mental and physical health, and lifestyle were also measured by the questionnaire. The data were then triangulated with the follow-up in-depth interviews previously mentioned. (iii) The study of the impact of digital platforms required, on the macro level, the study of youth’s consumption on digital platforms in general, their (dis)continuity of using traditional media, and the transformation of traditional media to digital platforms; on the micro level, it required the formation of online communities, the algorithm of the platform, and online subscription strategies/models, among other things. In the 2020 follow-up interviews, the research team conducted 20 informal interviews with industry personnel to more fully understand this subtle long-term impact.
