14600618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600618.value: The study revealed a new popular culture which Chinese youth have adapted to, where they are not just consuming online, but also producing novels/literature (however, not limited to writing, also including video and animation). It has become a new form of labor (or occupation) by which youth can earn a living. It represents a new lifestyle or slash culture in which youth live relatively free and unrestrained lives, while remaining outside of the formal system of work/controls in the workplace (both planned state and commercial jobs) in China (Part C 8.5, 8.8, 8.9, 9.4, and 9.5). Such a new mode of labor has also been proven to exist in different extended cultural forms (Douyin as shown in Part C 8.3, 8.10; comic platform as described in Part C 10.1). Consistent with the existing literature on platformization, data suggest that the nature of the work is not at all fancy, idealistic, or “unlikely creative.” However, the research did identify that a few of the novels that have been written (e.g., Chunzhen Niandai and Lingaoqiming) represent contradictions and dilemmas between the ideals conceived by youth and the vicissitudes of everyday life in contemporary China (Part C 9.1/ 9.8). On a social level, the case of online writing is the epitome of youth’s platformized life, in which entertainment, information seeking, and self-expression all take place on digital platforms in China and other parts of Asia. Consequently, we have witnessed a digital transformation of the traditional media industry in which the development of IP and response to the taste of the online community/audience play a significant role in accelerating the reformation of traditional media and their transformation to an online/platform business that meets the needs of the networked digital generation (Part C 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, and 8.7). The project resulted in six published articles (with both SSCI and CSSCI articles, thereby creating impacts internationally and in China), four articles under review, and five conference papers. The project trained two local PhD students whose theses focused on online female youth writers and young comic artists as creative labor on digital platforms in China. The project itself is a collaboration among the Chinese University of Hong Kong and two top-tier universities in China. In addition, this project has attracted international attention, resulting in a joint Australian National Grant application with researchers from the University of New South Wales who study online literature.

14600618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600618.value: First, the current study provides an overall picture of the field by highlighting a few relevant case studies. More emerging writing platforms (e.g., Tomato under ByteDance, which owns TikTok) are coming up for further study. In fact, the presentation of the data at international conferences has received positive feedback. Dr. Elaine Zhao of the University of New South Wales, the first scholar to study the Chinese online writing platform, has invited the PI for further collaboration (as stated in Part C 11.3). Second, the extended cultural forms of IP of online fiction for the production of television/video online, movies, and animation are vast unexplored fields. This is not just the case in China. IP investment and development in Japan and South Korea can be considered for potential comparative studies. Third, the research has also led to the study of online writers as creative labor whose working conditions, desires, and social, cultural, and symbolic capitals are investigated. In this way, the same framework can be extended to other platform studies, such as independent artist/musicians (e.g., Tencent Music), online celebrities/key opinion leaders producing short videos (e.g., TikTok), and fans making secondary productions (e.g., Bilibili/YouTube), to name a few.

14600618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600618.value: Online fiction writing in this study manifests the gradual replacement of traditional printed literature with fiction writing on online platforms. Like traditional novels, online fiction has now become the source of IP conversion, investment, and development for the entire entertainment industry in China and globally, ranging from dramas/movies watched on Netflix and other online TV platforms to digital games and even VR entertainment. Our study indicates that this phenomenon has also resulted in the formation of a new generation of slash writers. These are writers who are committed to working differently as creative labor on platforms where they write content and produce video animation and who are open to adopting a new and unconventional lifestyle. In this study, various published papers have empirically revealed cases and formulated concepts/theories about (1) the new forms and genres of writing, cultural production, and consumption and the formation of youth culture out of these platforms and other media on an individual level and (2) the strategic development of online platform and the IPs, the new assessment of cultural markets and audiences, and the cultural reorganization and transformation of the traditional media industries to accommodate IP-based and digital production on macro and global levels.

14600718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600718.value: 本項目旨在探索如何提升對香港和中國大陸“卡特爾”聯盟的威懾措施，所採用的方法是將更加成熟法域的傳統監測措施加以改善，使之符合香港和大陸本土需求。 “卡特爾”聯盟，指的是競爭者之間為了消除競爭的而組成的聯盟，對經濟有巨大的傷害。當受監測的風險較低時，此傷害可能會翻番。中國大陸和香港在近十年都制定了反不正當競爭法，其反壟斷機構依法打擊“卡特爾”聯盟。雖然違法，但因為豐厚的利潤誘惑，“卡特爾”是很難監測的，因為涉事方通常會極力掩蓋它們的行為。因此，任何有效打擊“卡特爾”的制度都需要有強力的監測手段作為支撐。世界各地的執法者通常採取兩種手段：（1）回應性措施，即競爭主管部門針對從他方（來自競爭者或消費者，或者作為對“卡特爾”成員尋求懲罰豁免的寬大處理）獲取的信息作出回應；（2）主動性措施，即主管部門採取市場調查等主動性措施調查發現串通行為。相較而言，前者比後者的應用的更多。儘管二者都有缺陷，但是通過研究其他法域的執法經驗發現，它們對打擊串通行為是至關重要的。但是，它們在香港和中國大陸的環境下能夠取得多大的成功，是完全沒有被研究的。 本項目匯集了一群本地和國際上的知名學者，他們在從法律和經濟角度對“卡特爾”進行監測和威懾具有豐富的理論和實踐經驗。在香港競爭事務委員會和中國反壟斷執法部門的支持下，研究小組將會評估國際實踐做法的價值，以期提出適用於香港和大陸的、“卡特爾”監測以及威懾方面的、規制措施和政策建議。本項目分為三期。第一期將會關注一些精選的法域打擊“卡特爾”的實踐經驗，主要是歐盟和韓國，並且將會採訪一些業內人士和執法者。第二期將會關注香港和大陸的獨特性，評估其到目前為止所採取的“卡特爾”監測措施的有效性。本期也將會調查公眾對“卡特爾”及其懲罰措施的態度。第三期將衡量各種措施和政策建議的優點，已明確它們的可行性，並會將研究結果進行傳播。 尋求最佳的“卡特爾”監測和威懾措施對本地以及全世界而言有著根本性的意義。就本地而言，本項目的研究成果將會對香港和大陸通過保護競爭以促進地區繁榮有重大貢獻。就全球而言，本地對“卡特爾”的規制，預示著全球打擊串通的行動是有廣泛前景的。

14600818.label: Project Objectives
14600818.value: To identify those second and third graders who are defined as dyslexic in each of the three cultures and to clarify which cognitive-linguistic correlates are most strongly associated with dyslexia in each location. To determine the extent to which the characteristics of those identified in each culture are the same as or different from one another. To develop a character/word reading test that can be administered across all three cultures in order to examine the overlap between this “universal” word reading test of Chinese and the traditional methods of identifying children with dyslexia in each place. To highlight the neuromarkers of dyslexia in each of the three locations, particularly across scripts, and to map these neuromarkers onto cognitive-linguistic abilities.

14600818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600818.value: Research on reading development and impairment in Chinese has become increasingly strong and multifaceted in the last two decades or so. At the same time, Chinese literacy might involve somewhat different skills in different contexts. In the proposed project, we seek to compare reading-related skills, cognitive-linguistic processing, and neurocorrelates among children in grades 2-3 with and without dyslexia across Hong Kong, Beijing (Mainland China), and Taipei (Taiwan). These three cities have, arguably, the best developed research on dyslexia in Chinese children in their respective regions. In addition, across these cities, there are similarities and differences that make direct comparisons theoretically intriguing and practically important. For example, Hong Kong and Taipei share use of the traditional script (but Beijing uses simplified). Taipei and Beijing both make use of phonological coding systems (Zhuyin vs. Pinyin) to help to teach Chinese; they teach in Putonghua (Mandarin). In Hong Kong, Chinese is typically taught using a look-and-say method and mapped onto Cantonese. Hong Kong and Taipei share a well-developed system of identifying children with developmental dyslexia in Chinese, whereas Beijing’s system of identification is less focused. In the proposed study, we will compare children with and without dyslexia across all three cities using locally developed identification methods. We will then administer to all children across cities a test of word reading in Chinese developed jointly to examine the extent to which the children are equally distinguishable based on this test for the purpose of cross-validation of the concept of dyslexia in Chinese across regions. In each city, we will administer tasks of phonological sensitivity (segmental and suprasegmental phonological awareness), verbal memory, rapid automatized naming, morphological awareness, orthographic knowledge, and vocabulary knowledge, as well as nonverbal IQ, to all participating children to assess the extent to which each of these skills is helpful in distinguishing those with and without dyslexia. In addition to these behavioral measures, the children will be tested using event-related potential (ERP) methodology to explore whether tasks of print tuning, radical sensitivity within compound single characters, and character sensitivity within compound (2-character) words can distinguish children with dyslexia from those who do not have dyslexia. Results will highlight the theoretical underpinnings of reading development and impairment in Chinese across Chinese societies. These results will also be practically useful for understanding the most important correlates of Chinese dyslexia in each society. 在過去的二十年左右，有關中文閱讀發展和障礙的研究逐漸增加、以及變得多元化。與此同時，中文讀寫能力在不同情景之下可能涉及不同的技巧。在此計劃中，我們將會比較香港、北京（中國大陸）、台北（台灣）2至3年級有讀寫障礙以及沒有讀寫障礙的兒童在有關閱讀相關的技能、認知-語言加工過程以及神經關聯指標。相比其各自地區中的其他城市，這三個城市在發展性的讀寫障礙的研究最完善。除此以外，直接比較這三個城市之間的相同與不同之處，在理論上和實用性上皆引人入勝。例如，香港和台北共用繁體字；但北京使用簡體字。台北及北京都使用語音編碼系統（分別是注音和拼音）協助中文教學；他們都使用普通話（國語）教學。而香港則使用廣東話，並配合看圖說話的方式教授中文。香港和台北共用一個完善的系統來鑒別中文發展性的讀寫障礙的兒童，北京的讀寫障礙鑒別系統則並不統一。在此計劃中，我們會運用當地研發的閱讀障礙鑒別系統，比較三個城市有讀寫障礙和沒有讀寫障礙的兒童。為了探討不同地區的中文發展性的讀寫障礙的交叉效度，我們會為這三個城市的兒童進行一個共同研發的中文閱讀測試，包括語音敏感性（單一音段和超音段音位語音意識）、言語記憶、快速命名、詞素意識、字型結構知識和詞語知識的測試，以及非語言智力測試，以檢視各個能力用作區分兒童為中文發展性的讀寫障礙的有效程度。在每個城市，除了以上的行為測試以外，我們將會使用事件相關電位的方法測試兒童，來了解中文單字的字體調諧和部首敏感度，以及中文雙字詞語中的中文單字敏感度是否能夠辨別中文發展性的讀寫障礙的兒童。研究結果會突出中文發展性的讀寫障礙在華裔社會中的理論重要性。在實際應用上，研究結果亦有助於了解中文發展性讀寫障礙在各個社會情景下最重要的相關變量。

14600818.label: Realisation of objectives
14600818.value: During the reporting period, we have recruited and conducted behavioural assessments on 148 Hong Kong Chinese primary school students from Grades 2-6, 64 Chinese primary school students from Beijing from Grades 2-3, and 67 Chinese primary school students from Grades 2-3 in Taipei. Among the 279 participants, 121 children were reported to have dyslexia. The behavioural assessment across three cities comprised the following tasks: Chinese dictation, pinyin writing, Chinese delayed copying, Chinese morphological awareness, Chinese phonological awareness, Chinese character reading, Chinese word reading, Chinese rapid automatized naming, Chinese orthographic knowledge, arithmetic, and English silent word reading test. This battery was very broad and allowed us to explore a variety of behavioral skills of children with or without dyslexia across Chinese cultures. We have developed a character reading task and a word reading test that can be administered across all three cities in the study. The items in the Chinese character reading and Chinese word reading task we used were identical in both traditional and simplified Chinese, which allowed us to compare the cognitive-linguistic profiles of Chinese dyslexia across three cities. The items in the Chinese dictation task were also identical in both traditional and simplified Chinese as well. Due to the COVID-19 situation, schools were suspended for most of the time in 2020, and online teaching was conducted most of the time in the academic year 2020-2021. As face-to-face data collection posed potential health risks both to experimenters and participants, online testing was conducted in Hong Kong, with the same behavioral tasks planned. We have several ERP tests that have been ready to test for neuro-responses in the sample in the project. We also have tried to schedule the ERP tests in 2020. However, the pandemic has obstructed our project progress and we were not able to collect EEG data in the three cities to highlight the neuromarkers of dyslexia in each of the three locations due to the health risk. Therefore, objective 4 could not be 100% complete. We did pilot a couple of tasks on a couple of students in Hong Kong, however, and this was useful for another application to build on this application (Senior Research Fellowship Scheme) which was funded in 2021. In summary, we have established “universal” character reading and word reading tests with good reliability that can be administered across all three cultures. Our findings with the behavioural data have also addressed Objectives 1 and 2 and highlighted the fundamental importance of phonological sensitivity, semantic awareness, and orthographic knowledge for word recognition in Chinese and the potential cross-cultural effects of Chinese dyslexia.

14600818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600818.value: The present project yielded many findings that are potentially important for understanding dyslexia in Chinese primary school children across cultures. 1) Chinese children with dyslexia performed more poorly in phonological awareness than typically developing children in all three cities. In addition, pinyin writing was found to be one of the two critical cognitive-linguistic skills that best-distinguished children with and without dyslexia in Hong Kong (Pan et al., under review). Previous studies (e.g., Ding et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2010) have demonstrated that Pinyin writing is significantly associated with Chinese reading performance. The present project extended the findings to show that Pinyin/Zhu-Yin-Fu-Hao writing appears to be important for understanding Chinese reading and writing in Hong Kong and Taipei (Ng et al., under review). 2) Chinese children with dyslexia in both Taipei and Hong Kong performed more poorly in morphological awareness, delayed copying, and spelling than their peers in the control group (Pan et al., under review). Morphological awareness was found to be one of the few dominant cognitive-linguistic skills that significantly distinguished children with and without dyslexia in these two places (Pan et al., under review). Children with dyslexia were found to perform less well in word spelling in both Hong Kong and Taipei than typically developing children (Pan et al., under review). These findings highlight the importance of semantic and orthographic skills in Chinese reading across different societies. 3) The character reading task was better than the word reading task in distinguishing children with and without dyslexia in Hong Kong and Taipei (Pan et al., under review). When word reading and character reading were included in the same logistic regression equation, only character reading remained in the final model. This finding might be clinically significant for developing a universal test battery to diagnose Chinese dyslexia across cultures. We need to follow up on these findings in future work. 4) Children with dyslexia in Hong Kong and Beijing performed significantly less well than typically developing children in English word reading (Pan et al., under review). This is in line with some previous studies demonstrating a co-occurrence of reading difficulties in L1 Chinese and L2 English across cultures (Gao et al., 2019; McBride-Chang et al., 2013). 5) Children with dyslexia were found to have more difficulties in mathematics performance than typically developing children in Hong Kong and Taipei (Pan et al., under review). This finding is somewhat consistent with the suggested association between Chinese word reading and arithmetic calculation (e.g., Peng et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2017). However, this result was not found in our Beijing sample. Future research should focus on additional cross-cultural comparisons to understand Chinese children’s arithmetic skills. Together, these findings are both theoretically and practically important for understanding the fundamental similarities and differences in the nature of Chinese dyslexia across Chinese cultures. The unique findings of the character reading task and morphological awareness test can help us to develop a “universal” test battery that would be potentially useful for educational or clinical psychologists to diagnose Chinese children with dyslexia across different societies.

14600818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600818.value: The current work inspired us to further investigate the nature of Chinese dyslexia across cultures, at the behavioral, neuroscience, and molecular genetics levels. We proposed to continue to explore more on these issues in the Senior Research Fellowship Scheme (SRFS) and it has been funded. In our SRFS, we will recruit more participants in each city. We will further investigate the nature of Chinese dyslexia across three prominent cities by expanding the current work to test newly identified correlates of Chinese and English literacy longitudinally. The neural signatures and genetics of the targeted, specific behavioral correlates as well as basic, potentially universal processes, such as resting state (using evoked-response potentials in the brain), in both Chinese and English will also be tested. Combining the results from behavioral, neural, and genetic levels, our transdisciplinary approach should facilitate optimization of early identification of risk for reading impairment in both Chinese and English, across Chinese-speaking societies.

14600818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600818.value: Research on Chinese dyslexia has often underscored the importance of cultural contexts and learning environments for understanding Chinese reading development and impairment. The current study compared the reading-related skills of children across three prominent Chinese cities, namely, Hong Kong, Beijing, and Taipei. The results have helped us to understand the importance of sensitivity to phonemes in distinguishing Chinese children with and without dyslexia across Chinese cultures. Character reading and morphological awareness can also be important for identifying reading impairment in Chinese across societies. Overall, the findings in the current project have extended our understanding of dyslexia in Chinese societies. The “universal” test battery developed in this project can potentially be used by educational or clinical psychologists to diagnose Chinese children with dyslexia across different societies.

To further develop the framework of transcendental functionalism put forward by the PI and to offer a coherent reconstruction of Kant’s theoretical philosophy. To clarify and explain Kant’s position on major metaphysical issues such as the nature of transcendental idealism and the ontological status of things in themselves as well as the transcendental subject. To reconsider and evaluate the possible contributions of Kant’s philosophy to the contemporary philosophy of mind and cognitive science. To present the work at international conferences and to publish the results in journals and/or books.

14601518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601518.value: A conceptual framework will be developed in this project to unify two dimensions of Kant’s theoretical philosophy widely considered to be incompatible. A critic of traditional metaphysics, Kant attempted to lay a new foundation for human knowledge and to redefine the nature and scope of metaphysics in his Critique of Pure Reason, which is a critical examination of our faculty of cognition. However, in pursuing this strategy of revolutionizing metaphysics by investigating our cognitive faculties, Kant has often been accused of psychologism. In response, a dominant camp of Kant scholars has advocated separating Kant’s metaphysics from his psychology, and focusing on his analytical arguments concerning the conditions of knowledge. Another camp of Kant scholars has pointed to Kant’s reflections on cognitive psychology as being the more valuable for contemporary philosophy and cognitive science. Although these two camps locate Kant’s major contribution in different areas, both see a strong tension between Kant’s psychology and metaphysics. The project will show that not only have the two major interpretations failed to do justice to Kant’s strategy, but that it is entirely possible to resolve the tension that they see as existing between the two dimensions of Kant’s philosophy. The PI has published a few papers outlining a framework that allows Kant’s psychology and metaphysics to be systematically unified. This framework, which can be called “transcendental functionalism,” describes a functionalist theory of mind and cognition that can fit into Kant’s transcendental idealism and provide clues to explaining the basic structure of reality. The aim in this project is to fully develop the framework of transcendental functionalism and carry out a thorough reconstruction of Kant’s theoretical philosophy on that basis. It will then be possible to offer a more coherent interpretation of Kant’s philosophy from a contemporary standpoint, as well as to give Kant’s valuable insights for cognitive psychology a deeper metaphysical foundation. A further aim is to identify Kant’s possible contributions to contemporary debates on metaphysical issues of the mind and cognition as well as on philosophical presuppositions of cognitive science and psychology. With the GRF grant, the PI plans to conduct research visits to the cooperating partners, organize a workshop with leading Kant scholars, present the results at international conferences, and publish a number of papers in journals. The main goal will be to publish a monograph on the unity of Kant’s transcendental psychology and metaphysics with an international publisher. 形上學與心理學是康德理論哲學裏的兩個主要部份，但不少學者認為兩者互不相容，而本研究計劃旨在建立一個可統合兩者的理論框架。康德在《纯粹理性批判》中嘗試透過審視我們的認知功能，為人類的知識奠定基礎，以及重新界定形上學的性質與範圍。然而，康德的研究進路不時被批評為「心理主義」。有一派學者認為我們應把康德的形上學視為其哲學的核心，把它從心理學中抽離出來，並集中研究康德對知識的條件的分析和論證。另一派學者則主張我們可聚焦康德的心理學，認為這部分才是康德對當代哲學與認知科學的貢獻所在。儘管兩派學者對康德哲學有不同的判斷，但他們均同意康德的形上學與心理學之間有明顯的張力。 這兩派的詮釋都未能恰當評價康德哲學，康德哲學中形上學與心理學的表面矛盾完全是可以化解的。計劃主持人在一些論文中已經勾勒出一個理論框架，展示如何統合康德的形上學與心理學。此框架可稱為「超驗功能主義」，因為它是在康德的超驗觀念論下，以功能主義的方式理解康德的認知心理學。本研究計劃正是要進一步發揮這個理論框架，並以此重建康德的理論哲學。這不單容許我們在當代哲學的背境下更融貫地詮釋整套康德哲學，也有助我們明白其對認知科學和形上學的貢獻。本研究計劃會嘗試把康德的深刻洞見，帶進當代形上學和心靈哲學的討論，並審視相關的理論預設。

14601518.label: Realisation of objectives
14601518.value: The GRF-project was conducted during a period in which external circumstances have made a lot of things including academic research difficult. The project was launched on October 8, 2018, when it was still possible to travel without restrictions, and I immediately attended two conferences on Kant’s philosophy which were held in Europe, first the 8th Multilateral Kant Colloquium “Kant and the Contemporary World: Philosophy, Science, Politics” in Italy and then the 4th International Congress of the Society for Kantian Studies (SEKLE) on the “Current Relevance of the Critique of Pure Reason” in Spain. With leading Kant scholars from all over the world in these two big events, I was able to exchange ideas and receive useful feedback for my Kant project. With the funding from the GRF-project, my Department was able to hire a relief teacher to take over some of my teaching duties so that I could spare time for the project. The work began with a critical analysis of the central principles of Kant’s philosophy and a detailed reassessment of Kant’s major writings in theoretical philosophy. In addition to Kant’s own writings, a significant amount of secondary literature on Kant’s theoretical philosophy has been reviewed. This part of the work was assisted by a research associate hired with the funding from the GRF-project. The research associate, Dr. Chun-Yip Lowe, is himself a recognized Kant scholar with a PhD from Free University of Berlin and has published papers on Kant’s philosophy in international journals. Based on a careful study, a radical new reading of Kant’s noumena as thought, or rather abstract, entities has been developed. This interpretation allows a more coherent solution to intractable problems in Kant’s philosophy, especially a more intelligible account of how noumena can be understood as grounding phenomena. It shows that there is neither an identity nor a one-to-one correspondence between a phenomenal being and its noumenal ground. Instead, the grounding relation is to be understood in the sense of an abstract entity being the ground of its multiple instances of concrete instantiation. Under this interpretation, phenomena are spatiotemporally instantiated concrete entities, whereas noumena are divided in two ontologically distinctive senses: noumena in their permissible negative sense are non-instantiated abstract entities, while noumena in their impermissible positive sense are non-spatiotemporally instantiated concrete entities, the conceivability of which would require a kind of non-sensible intuition that goes beyond the limits of human cognition. The result was presented as a Keynote Speech titled “Kant’s Concept of Negative Noumena,” at the Conference “The Concept of Negation in Classical German Philosophy,” organized at the Chinese University of Hong Kong in conjunction with the International Research Network on Transcendental Philosophy in February, 2019. From the start of the project in October 2018 until the beginning of the global pandemic in early 2020, I made nine conference presentations in Asia, Europe and North America, where the results of my research were presented to a wide range of audiences from leading Kant experts to philosophers in various fields. Exchange and discussion with scholars from different background is vital for the success of this kind of otherwise solitary academic research. With the outbreak of the global pandemic in early 2020, almost all academic conferences that scheduled for the past two years were cancelled, which also affected my GRF-project. I not only had to cancel a number of planned conference trips and research visits, but also a workshop on Kant’s psychology and metaphysics with participation of leading Kant scholars such as Paul Guyer and Patricia Kitcher. As stated in the project proposal, the workshop was originally scheduled for 2020. During the preparation of the conference, the global pandemic suddenly broke out and the conference had to be postponed. As no one could have foreseen that the pandemic would last for a few years, I initially postponed the workshop for a year to 2021. In order to finance the postponed workshop and other research works, I applied for an extension of the GRF-project twice, each for a period of 6 months, resulting in an overall extension of one year. The hope was that the pandemic would be over by 2021 and academic activities could be resumed by then, but the pandemic turned out to last much longer than expected, and it was impossible to organize the workshop in 2021. The workshop had to be cancelled in the end, which also affected the associated publication plan. Originally, an edited volume on Kant’s psychology and metaphysics with contributions from the workshop participants including Paul Guyer and Patricia Kitcher was planned, but the publication had to be cancelled together with the workshop. Due to the unexpected circumstances, the funding that was reserved for the workshop and the publication of an edited volume became available for other purposes. After careful consideration, I decided to extend the contract of the research associate for a few months so that more research-related supporting tasks could be completed. In addition, Dr. Lowe and I also co-authored two academic papers: a paper in Chinese published in a top philosophy journal in Taiwan and another in English forthcoming in the “Oxford Handbook of Kant” to be published by the Oxford University Press. With the extension of his contract, Dr. Lowe was able to accomplish some more research work that will be useful for the new HSSPFS-project. Although the external circumstances have made academic research difficult, the project realized all the objectives set out in the project proposal. The difficult travel situation made some changes necessary, especially the cancellation of some research trips and the above-mentioned workshop, but I did manage to explore alternative ways to complete the project. The results of the project were communicated through the standard academic vehicles, including academic papers and conference presentations. Six papers were published or are forthcoming in peer-reviewed journals or books in two languages (English and Chinese). Around half of a 350-page book manuscript on Kant’s transcendental psychology and metaphysics has been completed. All the major objectives, as stipulated in the project proposal, have been achieved. Yet, what is more important is the potential for further development and new research possibility that is made possible by the GRF-project. As described in 6.2 below, based on the results of the GRF-project, I successfully applied for the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme (HSSPFS) 2022/23. The HSSPFS-project is an extension of the research completed with the current GRF-project and will become the focus of my research in the coming year, with the publication of a monograph in English titled “Kant without Thing-in-Itself: The Unity of Kant’s Transcendental Psychology and Metaphysics” in an internationally renowned publisher as its major objective.

14601518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601518.value: There are a number of peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations resulted directly from the GRF-project, among which the forthcoming paper titled “Kant’s Negative Noumena as Abstracta” (#4) stands out, among the completed results, as philosophically the most important one. As the lead article in a volume on “The Being of Negation in Post-Kantian Philosophy” (Springer) with contributions from leading experts on German philosophy, the paper develops a novel interpretation of Kant’s noumena as abstract entities, which makes a further development of a deflationary reading of Kant’s transcendental idealism possible. The paper titled “The Unity of Kant’s Transcendental Psychology and Metaphysics” (#7) is a thematic presentation of the core results of the GRF-project, while its fuller exposition will be a monograph titled “Kant Without Thing-In-Itself: The Unity of Transcendental Psychology and Metaphysics” (#6). The monograph, which extends substantially beyond the scope presented in the original proposal of this GRF-project, will consist of around 350 pages, around two-thirds of which have been completed. In order to complete this larger project, a funding from the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme (HSSPFS) 2022/23 has been secured (see 6.2). The paper titled “Kant’s Transcendental Idealism and Empirical Realism” (#1) argues that Kant’s ontological position is not, as usually thought, determined by transcendental idealism, but rather by empirical realism, whereas transcendental idealism should be understood as an epistemological framework under which ontology is thoroughly transformed. The paper titled “From the Kantian to the Hegelian Court of Reason” (#2) discusses in what way Kant’s Critique of Pure Reason paths the way for the development of Hegel’s thought, which can be viewed as a Critique of Historical Reason. There are two co-authored papers (both with Dr. Chun-Yip Lowe) resulted from the GRF-project: the first one is titled “From the Realization of Freedom to a World Government: On Kant’s and Hegel’s Conceptions of International Order” (#3), and the second one titled “Kant on Community” (#5) is forthcoming in the “Oxford Handbook of Kant” to be published by Oxford University Press next year. With the support of the funding, ten conference presentations were made in different continents, and a one-month research visit at the Kant Research Lab of Aarhus University, Denmark was conducted. Further research outcome including a 350-page monograph in English will be produced from the HSSPFS-funded continuation project titled “Kant Without Thing-In-Itself: The Unity of Transcendental Psychology and Metaphysics.”

14601518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601518.value: The project has proven to be successful, not only with the reported publications in which the framework for the unification of Kant?s transcendental psychology and metaphysics was presented, but also in breaking new ground for a larger project that is built on its results. The completed GRF-project provides a promising framework for a thoroughly deflationary interpretation of Kant?s transcendental idealism without the commitment to the existence of things in themselves. This is not only a substantially new way of understanding Kant?s philosophy, but will also make Kant?s foundation for human cognition more secure. In order to be able to devote myself fully to this more ambitious project, I applied successfully for the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme (HSSPFS) 2022/23 with a proposal titled ?Kant without Thing-in-Itself: The Unity of Kant?s Transcendental Psychology and Metaphysics.? With a total of funding of $848,900, my project is the highest funded HSSPFS-project in the last three years. The funding not only allows my Department to hire a relief teacher for one year, but also allows me to conduct research visits to leading Kant scholars in different continents. The result will be a monograph on Kant?s philosophy published by an internationally renowned publisher.

14601518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601518.value: Kant is arguably the most important philosopher in the modern age. He attempted to answer those ultimate questions about reality that mankind has been seeking since the dawn of thought. Many philosophical debates today are profoundly influenced by his thought. Kant launched a Copernican revolution in philosophy, fundamentally rethinking the very possibility and limits of metaphysical inquiry. Kant is well-known for his critique of traditional metaphysics, but the metaphysical position in his philosophy is ambiguous. This is because, for Kant, metaphysical questions cannot even be asked in a way that was previously taken for granted, but must be thoroughly reformulated and transformed. Although Kant?s strategy was to transform metaphysics through an investigation into the faculty of cognition, there is a long tradition in Kant scholarship that insists on a strict separation of Kant?s metaphysics from his psychology. The project developed a new interpretation that allows Kant?s transcendental psychology and metaphysics to be systematically unified. With a distinction between transcendental cognitive functions and their empirical realizations, the framework reads Kant?s faculty of cognition and the transcendental subject as abstract or thought entities, whereas real-world cognizers such as human beings can be understood as concrete realizations or instantiations of the transcendental subject.

14602418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602418.value: The human brain constantly and unconsciously monitors the environment for unexpected changes. For example, even when we are driving and focusing on the traffic in front of us, we can detect a pedestrian jumping onto the road from the side. The ability to detect changes from the environment without paying attention is essential to our survival. The pre-attentive change detection ability is typically studied using an event-related brain potential (ERP) component, the mismatch negativity (MMN). The MMN has also been used as biomarkers for normal aging and disease populations, such as schizophrenia. Given the central importance of the pre-attentive change detection system in survival, it is highly desirable if we can improve this system in healthy individuals, and even more critically, to provide rehabilitative training for individuals who have a compromised change detection system, e.g., schizophrenia patients. Previous studies have shown that MMN can be improved through long term experience. However, years of experiences or an intensive training scheme are required to change the MMN response; the application of modulating the pre-attentive process through training is limited. In this proposal, our first objective is to use motivational value association training to improve pre-attentive change detection ability. Recent studies have found that a task irrelevant stimuli feature, e.g., color, associated with reward or punishment during a training session, affects task performance in a subsequent testing session. This learning effect can last for months without retraining. As attention is not required to process the rewards or punishments associated stimuli during training, populations having difficulties in following instructions, e.g., children with attention problems and disease groups with low compliance, can also greatly benefit from this training scheme. Furthermore, for people with different sensitivities to rewards and punishments, training focusing on rewards or punishments can be tailor-made to the individual. The second objective of the proposed study is to investigate how individuals’ sensitivity to reward and punishment modulates the motivational-value association training effect on pre-attentive change detection. From a theoretical perspective, the proposed study will be the first that demonstrates longitudinal training effect in the pre-attentive change detection system, at both behavioral and neural levels. From a practical perspective, such a training scheme can be further developed to help road users to improve driving safety, and disease populations whose compromised visual pre-attentive change detection ability impairs their daily life, but nonetheless can benefit from such training because their reward/punishment learning system is intact.

14602418.label: Realisation of objectives
14602418.value: The objectives of the current project are 1) to improve the sensitivity of the pre-attentive change detection system by using a task-irrelevant motivational value-association training scheme.; 2) to investigate how individuals’ sensitivity to reward and punishment modulates the motivational-value association training effect on pre-attentive change detection. The two objectives were fully realized by five experiments. Experiment 1 to 3 demonstrated a basic and generic frontal sensory brain dynamics of the pre-attentive change detection and the causal relationship between frontal and sensory cortices. Experiment 4 showed long term experience effect (culture) on the pre-attentive change detection. Experiment 5 showed short term implicit reward association learning improved participants’ pre-attentive change detection, and which is modulated by individuals’ sensitivity to reward and punishment. Experiment 1 (Tse et al., 2021,Neuroimage) postulated a generic fronto-sensory cortical network underlying the prediction violation mechanism in pre-attentive change detection. This study examined the involvement of the IFC-occipital cortex (OC) network in visual pre-attentive change detection and the modulation of the IFC-OC mismatch response pattern by regularity abstractness and amount of information for establishing the prediction. Modulations of the IFC-OC mismatch responses similar to that of the IFC-STC network were found. The results demonstrated that the fronto-sensory cortical network is not unique to auditory pre-attentive change detection and provided supports for a universal neural mechanism across sensory modalities as suggested by the prediction violation hypothesis. Experiment 2 (Xiao et al., 2022, Neuropsychologia) examined the EROS mismatch responses of the IFC-STC network when detecting the violation of an abstract rule. The rule “the higher the frequency of a tone, the stronger the intensity” established by standards was violated by deviants of 12 deviance levels. When deviants were preceded by a short train of standards, early IFC, STC, and late IFC EROS mismatch responses linearly increased with the deviance levels. When deviants were preceded by a longer train of standards, the STC but not the early or late IFC EROS mismatch responses were elicited by all the deviants without modulation by deviance levels. These results demonstrate a functional role of the IFC in the abstract change detection when insufficient rule-conforming information could be extracted from the preceding standards and are consistent with the predictive violation account of pre-attentive change detection. Experiment 3 (Lui et al., 2021, Brain Stimulation) investigated the critical role of the IFC in establishing a prediction model during pre-attentive change detection. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) was applied at the IFC to disrupt the processing of the initial 2 or 5 standards of a 3-, 6-, or 9-standard train, while the MMN responses to pitch deviant pre-sented after the standard trains were recorded and compared. during standards processing for subsequent deviant detection. An abolishment of MMN was only observed when TMS was delivered to the IFC at the initial 2 standards of the 3-standard train, but not at the initial 5 standards, or when TMS at the vertex or TMS sound recording was applied. The MMNs were also preserved when IFC TMS, vertex TMS, or TMS sound recording was applied at the initial 2 or 5 standards of longer trains. The IFC plays a critical role in processing the initial standards of a short standard train for subsequent deviant detection which is consistent with the prediction violation account of pre-attentive change detection Experiment 4 (Zeng et al., 2022, scientific report) examined the long-term experience (culture) effect on pre-attentive change detection. More specifically, it investigated whether cultural information could be spontaneously categorized, and the modulation of this process by the belief in the biological origin of race (i.e., racial essentialism) with an event-related brain potential, the visual Mismatch Negativity (vMMN). Deviant pictures of Eastern (Western) culture were randomly presented in a stream of standard Western (Eastern) pictures while participants were playing a video game. Participants who endorse racial essentialism (high group) showed vMMNs to the deviants with high relevance to the Eastern or Western culture and the deviant with low Eastern relevance; while participants with low racial essentialism showed vMMN to the deviant with high Eastern relevance only. These results revealed spontaneous cultural categorization with vMMN and the top-down modulation of spontaneous categorization by personal belief. Experiment 5 (Wang et al., in preparation) demonstrated a short-term (4 days) implicit reward association learning would be able to increase our sensitivity to certain visual feature (i.e., orientation). Moreover, such process is modulated by participants’ sensitivity to reward and punishment measured by BAS and BIS questionnaires. The experiment including three types of phases: 1) In training phase, participants learnt to build the association between the task irrelevant stimuli feature (i.e., orientation) and different monetary values (i.e., high, low, and zero amount of reward); 2) In the testing phase, participants were also asked to respond to the task relevant stimuli feature (i.e, color and spatial frequencies) while a task irrelevant distractor with either a high or low reward associated orientation were also presented; 3) The MMN phase employed a visual equal probability paradigm to examine whether participants’ sensitivity to reward associated stimuli feature would differ from other random orientations at pre-attentive level. The experiment consisted of 5 sessions carried out in 5 consecutive days. The first day (Day 0), which acted as a pre-training baseline, only had the testing and MMN phases while in the subsequent days (Day 1 to Day 4), participants underwent all three phases. The behavioral results of the testing phase showed that participants learned to facilitate their response (shorter reaction time) when there were high or low reward associated distractors from day 1 to day 4 compared to day 0. More importantly, their respond to target were quicker when there was a high reward distractor compare to a low reward distractor on day 3. In MMN phase, the low and high reward MMN were neither significantly differ from zero nor differ from each other on day 0. As on day 0, participants have not learnt the association yet. These two orientations did not significantly differ from other filler orientations. On day 3, high and low reward MMN showed significant difference which is similar as behavioral results in testing phase. These results suggested that participants were able to learn reward association with the orientations at behavioral and pre-attentive level with a maximization on day 3. Participants’ sensitivity to reward relative to punishment (BAS minus BIS score) modulates the differential sensitivity to high versus low reward. For relatively high BIS group (BIS minus BAS score > 0), the differentiation between high versus low reward start to show up on day 2 and this differentiation continued to day 3. Whereas for relatively high BAS group (BIS minus BAS score < 0), the differentiation between high versus low reward start to show up on day 3 and this differentiation continued to day 4. High BIS group participants learnt the value attached to different orientations (i.e., high versus low reward) earlier than high BAS group. High BIS people tend to suppress their response in order to avoid punishment, while the training phase is actually training participants to suppress their response to reward associated and task irrelevant features. Thus, they learnt the high versus low reward differentiations earlier than high BAS group in which people are better at approaching behavior.

14602418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14602418.value: The current project demonstrated 1) a generic fronto-sensory network of pre-attentive change detection. Furthermore, the causal connections and activation sequence of the fronto-temporal network in pre-attentive change detection and the functional role of frontal cortex consistent with predictive model hypothesis were also reported; 2) top-down influence on MMN including long-term experience (culture) and short-term experience (implicit reward association learning) effect on MMN which are modulated by individual differences. The generic brain foundations of MMN suggested pre-attentive change detection is a generic mechanism for detecting changes in the environment, while the top-down influence (long-term experience and short-term experience) on MMN suggest the mechanism is also flexible. Future studies can use 1) further explore the generic pre-attentive change system in other modality e.g., somatosensory, etc; 2) using implicit reward association learning to improve pre-attentive change detection sensitivity in other modalities, e.g., auditory, somatosensory, etc; 3) The passive oddball paradigm which are usually used in pre-attentive change detection does not require participant to engage in an active task which is suitable for examining cognitive processing in special population, e.g., ASD. The mismatch brain response elicited in pre-attentive change detection can potentially be used as biomarker in some clinical populations.

14602418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14602418.value: The human brain is capable of monitoring signals in the environment (e.g., appearance of a car passing by) and making predictions of future events without focus of attention. When this automatic system detects a salient change out of expectation (e.g., an incoming car), the brain will orient attention to the change, and carry out remedial action if required (e.g., jump out of the way). This pre-attentive change detection process reflects a predictive nature of human brain which is a fundamental principle in human cognition. The findings from this project 1) demonstrated a generic fronto-sensory network during pre-attentive change detection. Furthermore, the causal connection of fronto-temporal network in pre-attentive change detection and the functional role of frontal cortex which consistent with prediction violation hypothesis were also found using combined neuroimaging technique: TMS-EROS, EROS-EEG, and TMS-EEG methods; 2) pre-attentive change detection is also a flexible mechanism and can be changed by top-down influences (e.g., culture, training, individual differences). These findings allow us to understand the generic and flexibility of pre-attentive change detection and provide a new way (i.e., implicit reward association training) to modify our pre-attentive change detection sensitivity.

14603218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603218.value: 中國民間信仰在德川日本的神道化研究

14603218.label: Project Objectives
14603218.value: To trace the origins and history of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan based on primary sources. To investigate how Chinese folk beliefs were included in the Shinto framework through the lens of localization and cultural appropriation, and document how Chinese gods were enshrined in Shinto shrines as manifestations of Japanese deities. To explain how the cultural policy of the bakufu (military government) and the changing intellectual atmosphere influenced the reception of Chinese folk religion among Tokugawa Japanese, and to demonstrate how Chinese culture was domesticated to fit in the Tokugawa setting. To examine the images of Chinese mythological characters in Tokugawa art, literature, theatre, and architecture, and investigate how they were incorporated into Japanese festivals and folklore. To identify the characteristics of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan and to compare them with the original Chinese folk beliefs and practices.

14603218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603218.value: Aim: This is a pioneering study on the reception and localization of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan (1603-1868) conducted through textual analysis and ethnographic fieldwork. Project Background: Chinese cultural influence reached its zenith in Tokugawa Japan. Different schools of Chinese thought and religion were introduced to Japan and played an important role in shaping Tokugawa culture. The impact of Chinese Neo-Confucianism and Chan (Zen) Buddhism in Tokugawa Japan has been widely researched, whereas the historical reception of Chinese folk religion during this period remains largely uncharted territory for researchers. This project will be a historical study of major Chinese folk beliefs and practices in Tokugawa Japan, using Shintoization as the main analytical framework. Brief Project Description: Through textual analysis of Tokugawa sources and ethnographic fieldwork conducted at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples in Japan, the proposed project will be a pioneering study of the popularization and localization of various Chinese folk beliefs and practices in Tokugawa Japan. The reception and adaptation of major Chinese folk religion surrounding figures, such as Mazu, Zhong Kui, Shennong, Yu the Great, Fuxi, and Guan Yu, and items like Shigandang, will be closely examined to understand how they were naturalized to enrich indigenous Japanese religion. Most of those Chinese figures were transformed into Shinto deities, given Shinto titles, enshrined in Shinto shrines, and worshiped in the Shinto manner. Shintoization became a device for Japanese to overcome the psychological barriers caused by the worship of foreign gods. The naturalization of Chinese folk religion was also reflected in Tokugawa art, literature, and folklore. This project will demonstrate how Chinese folk religion was incorporated into Japan’s Shinto framework and how Chinese elements were used to enrich Japanese culture. Project Significance: This study will break new ground in Sino-Japanese studies and Tokugawa intellectual and cultural history through the following aspects. First, it will provide an original study of the history of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan. Second, it will be based mainly on Tokugawa primary sources, many of which have never been cited for research. Third, it will supplement and at times challenge existing literature on Sino-Japanese cultural interchange that overemphasizes the Chinese influence on Tokugawa Japan. It aims to show that Chinese elements were creatively and selectively used by Tokugawa Japanese to construct and enrich Japanese culture. Fourth, it will make an academic impact through publication of journals articles and eventually a monograph in English. 以文獻分析及民族學調查為基礎，本研究討論中國民間信仰在德川日本(1603-1868)的本地化。中國文化在日本的影響在德川時代達高峰，不同派別的中國思想及宗教均被引進，納入德川文化體系之內。儒學及禪宗的相關研究豐碩，但中國民間信仰仍是研究上不毛之地。本研究以神道化為分析架構，探討中國民間信仰在德川日本的發展。 透過原始史料及走訪日本神社寺院，本計畫是對中國民間信仰在德川日本本地化的開拓性研究。媽祖、鐘馗、關帝、神農、大禹、伏羲等在德川日本都經過本地化洗禮，化身神道神祇，以神道儀式被供奉於神社。神道化化令日人解除接受外來信仰的心理障礙。神道化在德川文藝及民間風俗亦可窺見一斑。此研究探討中國民間信仰如何在德川日本被編入神道系統及豐富日本文化。 此研究對中日文化交流史及德川思想史有以下貢獻：第一，提供中國民間信仰在德川日本的開拓性研究。第二，以日本原始史料為基礎，部分至今從未被使用過。第三，挑戰學界過分強調中國影響，主張日本在吸收中國文化時保持主體性。第四，研究成果將在國際學術期刊發刊，最終目的是學術專書。

14603218.label: Realisation of objectives
14603218.value: All five objectives have been basically achieved. (1) To trace the origins and history of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan based on primary sources. A large amount of Japanese and Chinese primary sources have been used to trace the introduction of Chinese folk religions in early and medieval Japan and their popularization and localization in the Tokugawa period. Some historical data have never been used. (2) To investigate how Chinese folk beliefs were included in the Shinto framework Based on primary sources and field-work based research, different Chinese deities were found to be enshrined in Japanese Shinto shrines, received Shinto titles and worshipped in the Shinto way throughout different parts of Japan. (3) To demonstrate how Chinese culture was domesticated to fit in the Tokugawa setting. This study shows that Chinese folk beliefs were domesticated to accommodate Tokugawa bakufu and domain's religious policies and the rise of nationalist sentiments among Tokugawa intellectuals. (4) To examine the images of Chinese deities in Tokugawa art, literature, theatre, architecture and festivals. Based on fieldwork and visit to museums, art galleries and libraries in Japan, the PI have taken many pictures of Chinese deities in Japan and their representation in Tokugawa art and culture. The PI participated in cultural and religious festivals to understand the localization of Chinese deities in Tokugawa Japan. (5) To identify the characteristics of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan and to compare them with the original Chinese folk beliefs and practices. This study underlines of the characteristics of Chinese folk religion in Tokugawa Japan from a comparative perspective. The comparison between the Chinese prototype and the Japanese version is conducted. The PI also compares the reception of Chinese deities in Japan, Korea, and Vietnam.

14603218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603218.value: Major Findings: (1) Chinese folk beliefs were domesticated in Tokugawa Japan and were included in the Shinto framework. (2) The popularization and the localization of Chinese folk religion were two sides of the same coin. Localization (or Shintoization) became the major reason behind popularization. (3) Chinese culture was used as a set of "building block" to construct and enhance Japanese indigenous culture and religion. 14603918.value: 原始閩語與上古漢語的音韻比較研究

14603918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603918.value: This project aims at comparing the phonological system of Proto-Min (‘PM’), the putative ancestor of all modern Min varieties, with that of Old Chinese (‘OC’), the oldest attested stage of the Chinese language used in the pre-Han period, from a historical perspective. The Min dialect group is well known for keeping a rich layer of pre-Middle Chinese elements, and its relationship with OC is basically unquestioned. Yet, recent advances in linguistic reconstruction have not been fully reflected in existing comparative studies of Min and OC. For example, modifications have been proposed since the PM phonological system was first reconstructed in the 1970s. It will be timely to review and incorporate some of these proposals in an updated PM phonological system. There is a lack of consensus over the number of vocalic nuclei in OC. In this project, we consider PM to be an objective criterion for evaluating OC reconstruction. We will compare the vowel systems of OC (where the main difference of the two camps lies) with that of PM, and examine which OC system is more compatible with PM. This project will be able to settle fundamental debates in the question about whether there are 4 or 6 vocalic nuclei in OC. Unlike previous studies which compare OC and PM, the present research will approach the reconstruction of PM and OC phonological systems without making any presumptions about the two languages’ relationships (‘mother-son’ or ‘sisters’). In addition, this project will draw on new Min data and more robust methods in the comparison of OC and PM. More specifically, we will investigate and suggest interpretations for the OC reflexes of (a) the PM voiceless sonorant initials; (b) the PM ‘softened’ initials; (c) the distinctions between PM ‘close’ and ‘open’ vocalic nuclei; and (d) the PM final *-al. Attention will be paid to the connections between PM and OC dialects such as those spoken in the ancient Qi and Chu regions. This study will deepen our understanding of not only Chinese dialectology, but also Old Chinese reconstruction and historical linguistics. 本計劃擬從歷時角度比較原始閩語 (‘PM’) 和上古漢語 (‘OC’) 的音韻系統。所謂「原始閩語」，是指用比較法推訂出來、所有現代閩語方言的共同祖先。閩語的存古性質相當明顯，保留了大量超越中古漢語的成份。學界一般相信它在兩漢時期就已經脫離主流漢語。我們一方面會引用新語料，另一方面會採用比以往更嚴謹的方法，在不假定 PM 和 OC 具體關係的前提下，探索以下幾個 PM 的特徵在 OC 裡的反映，並尋求解釋：(a) 清響音聲母；(b)「弱化聲母」；(c) 「開韻核」及「閉韻核」的分野；(d) 韻尾 *-al。我們也會以修訂過的原始閩語音系作為基準，對上古音擬構的「四元音方案」和「六元音方案」作出檢測。

14603918.label: Realisation of objectives
14603918.value: Objective 1: 通過比較，探索上古漢語和共同閩語在音系上的對應，從而增加我們對彼此關係的認識。 1a. Collation of the Common Min forms: The Common Min 共同閩語 system by late Professor Jerry Norman is a reconstructed ancestor of all modern Min dialects by the comparative method. Incorporating more Northern Min materials available to him, Norman treats Common Min as a revised and improved version of Proto-Min 原始閩語. Unfortunately, the reconstruction of the whole Common Min had never been made public. In 2017, I received a list containing several hundred reconstructed Common forms from Professor W. South Coblin. This list is of paramount importance to this project. In order to make the subsequent comparisons easier, the Common Min forms were put into three Excel files, grouped by their initials, rhymes and tones. I make use of 14 modern Min dialects including Ningde 寧德, Yong’an 永安, Quanzhou 泉州, Putian 莆田, Shibei 石陂 and Shaowu 邵武 to elicit the sound correspondence between Common Min and its modern descendants. In doing so, I was able to expand the lexicons of Common Min to around 700 items. 1b. Input of the Old Chinese forms: The Old Chinese forms reconstructed by Baxter and Sagart (2014a, 2014b) and their Middle Chinese transcriptions were input into the Excel file compiled in phase 1a. 1c. Working out the sound correspondence between Common Min and Old Chinese: It is generally agreed that Common Min (or Proto-Min) contains at least two Sinitic lexical layers from different historical origins: one can be dated back to the Han Dynasty and the other the Sixth Dynasties (cf. Norman 1991; Akitani 2020). To work out the sound correspondence between Common Min and Old Chinese, we need to fully understand the sound changes between Old Chinese and Middle Chinese. In Common Min, only those elements that cannot be fully explained under the Middle Chinese framework would be taken into comparisons with Old Chinese. The following two examples illustrate this. (i) The word for ‘carp’ 鯉 in Common Min has two variants, reconstructed as *dəi and *di (Proto-Min *-dəi~*-di). Its modern reflexes are as follows: Quanzhou /tai4/; Shibei /di5/; Yong’an /ti4/. In Middle Chinese, however, the word for ‘carp’ is liX. This form seems to be accountable only for the literary forms of Min (cf. Quanzhou /li3/; Yong’an /ni3/). Baxter and Sagart (2014a) give the Old Chinese form for ‘carp’ as *mə-rəʔ. In their proposal, the former part of *mə-r- would drop without a trace in most of the modern Sinitic languages but would give rise to *-d- in Proto-Min (=Common Min *d-). Other examples which fit in this correspondence include ‘deer’ 鹿 and ‘oyster’ 蠣. We hypothesize the sound change as *mə-r- > *mbr- (by epenthesis) > *ndr- (by backward assimilation) > Common Min *d- > Shibei /d-/. (ii) We found that the words for ‘river’ 江 and ‘work’ 工 are homophonous in most of the modern Min dialects, e.g. Xiamen /kaŋ1/; Putian /kaŋ1/; Fuzhou /koyŋ1/. Their common forms can be readily reconstructed as *kuŋ. It should be noted that the phonetic element of 江 *kˁroŋ is 工 *kˁoŋ, but only 江 underwent a diphthongization process and became kaewng in Middle Chinese (Baxter and Sagart 2014a:244). This Middle Chinese form can basically account for the reflexes of most of the modern Sinitic languages. However, for the case of Min, it is more likely that 江 *kˁroŋ had dropped the *-r- and eventually merged with *kˁoŋ. Words with Old Chinese *-ˁrok such as ‘horn’ 角 (MC kaewk < OC *C.[k]ˁrok) also experienced a similar change in Min (i.e. *-ˁrok > *-ˁok). The result is that the word for ‘horn’ 角 shares the same rhyme with words like ‘to read’ 讀 (MC duwk < *C.lˁok). Compare, for example, 角 Xiamen /kak7/; Jian’ou /ku7/; 讀 Xiamen /thak8/; Jian’ou /tu7/. Objective 2: 審視各種修訂共同閩語的方案，並整理出最終方案在現代閩語方言中的對應關係。 2a. The revisions of Common Min initials and tone classes: One of the main differences between Common Min and Proto-Min is the treatment of tone classes: Proto-Min had only four tone classes, roughly corresponding to tradition Chinese ping 平, shang 上, qu 去 and ru 入. In Common Min, the original tone classes were divided one by one into the yin 陰 category and yang 陽 category. The result is that Common Min had eight tone classes, similar to what we observe in the modern Chaoyang 潮陽 Southern Min. While this revision is not unreasonable, we found that it can hardly accommodate various important sound change in Eastern Min, particularly *dz- > s-, e.g. ‘to sit’ 坐 Fuzhou /soy6/; Huba 虎浿 /θoi6/; ‘stone’ 石 Fuzhou /suoʔ8/; Huba /θiʌʔ8/. We are inclined to a 4-tone system for the ancestral language of Min. It also means the so-called ‘softened stops’ as proposed in Norman (1973, 1974) should be maintained. 2b. The revision of Common Min rhymes: Norman (1981) proposed vocalic alternations for several rhymes in Proto-Min, and this feature is basically maintained in the Common Min reconstruction. In this project, we resolved the so-called ‘*-əi ~ *-i alternations’ by assigning the words for ‘eyebrows’ 眉, ‘kill’ 治 and ‘come’ 來 to *-əi, and the words for ‘dung’ 屎 and ‘sharp’ 利 to *-i. Under the new assignment, words with Common Min *-əi have regular correspondence with Old Chinese *-ə, e.g. ‘to kill’ Common Min *trhəi : Old Chinese *C.lrə. The lack of consistence in correspondences of those rhymes between Old Chinese and Common Min is partially caused by the replacement of the old forms by the new forms from the literary layer in some of the Min dialects. Objective 3: 提出以共同閩語檢驗上古音擬構的方法。 3a. Taking the Min reflexes as an important material for Old Chinese reconstruction: We treat the Min reflexes as an important additional material for Old Chinese reconstruction, especially the initials. For instance, an aspirated affricate initial is observed in the word for ‘flesh’ 鮮 in Min: Xiamen /tshĩ1/; Fuzhou /tshieŋ1/. These reflexes are unlikely to be derived from Middle Chinese form sjen. We proposed the Old Chinese initial for this word as *s.ŋ-, which became *s.n- and then *tsh- in Min. This reconstruction also helps us better explain why the Han scholar Zheng Xuan (127-200CE) regarded 鮮 as an ‘error in pronunciation’ of xian 獻 in his comment of Liji 禮記 (鮮當為獻，聲之誤也), since the Old Chinese form of xian 獻 was reconstructed with a voiceless velar nasal *ŋ̊-. 3b. Examination of the ‘round-vowel hypothesis’: Unlike F.K. Li (1971) who proposed a 4-vowel system for Old Chinese, Baxter (1992) and Baxter and Sagart (2014a) argued for a 6-vowel system, including a round-vowel *o. With reference to Akitani and Nohara (2018), we studied the Old Chinese rhymes with *o and their modern reflexes in Min. It is found that after acute codas, the correspondence between Old Chinese *o and Common Min *o is highly regular, which can be exemplified by: ‘short’ 短 *OC *tˁorʔ : *CM *-oi; ‘cut off’ 絕 OC *[dz]ot: CM *-ot; ‘egg’ 卵 OC *k.rˁorʔ : CM *-on. It is assumed that the Middle Chinese forms for the above words would evolve to -wa- or -we-, e.g. 短 twan; 卵 lwan. In this regard, the Min forms to a certain extent are supportive to a reconstruction of an *o vocalism in Old Chinese. While we encountered several difficulties caused by COVID-19 during the research period, overall speaking, the three objectives stated in the proposal have been fully achieved.

14603918.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603918.value: Major findings of this project include the followings: (1) Revisions of the reconstruction of several Old Chinese initials in light of Proto-Min reflexes [Part C, 8, No.1, 3, 4, 5, 7; 9, No.1, 3, 5]: We found that words reconstructed with voiceless nasals in Proto-Min (‘PM’) have frequent contact with Old Chinese (‘OC’) phonetic series with voiceless nasal initials. After compared the PM forms and their cognates in Proto-Tibeto-Burman, we suggested to adjust the OC reconstruction of *C.N- (N=nasal) by Baxter & Sagart (2014a) to *sə.N-, e.g. ‘hemp’ 麻 *sə.mˁ-. In our proposal, the minor syllable would drop without a trace in the ancestor of most of the modern Sinitic languages; in Min, the development would be: *sə.mˁ- > *s.m- > PM *mh-. Another finding of this project is the multiple origins for Middle Chinese s-. Baxter & Sagart (2014a) noticed that some OC origins of s- have special reflexes only observable in Min, e.g. ‘shame’ 羞 OC *s.n- : Xiamen /tshiu/. On top of their study, we were able to add two sound changes from OC to PM, namely, *s.ŋ- > *tsh- (e.g. ‘fresh’ 鮮) and *sr- > *tšh- (e.g. ‘search’ 搜). The Min reflexes also support the OC reconstruction for the word 腥 ‘rank smell (of fish)’ as *nə.s- put forward by Jacques (2020), who based chiefly on early loanwords in the Mien language from Chinese. (2) Identifications of correspondences in several rhymes between Old Chinese and Proto-Min [Part C, 8, No.3, 6; 9, No.4, 8]: Norman (1981) proposed vocalic alternation *-əi ~ *-i for words like ‘kill’ 治 , ‘sharp’ 利 and ‘come’ 來. Our suggestion is to assign *-əi for 治 and 來 but *-i for 利. In so doing the correspondence between PM *-əi and OC *-ə (i.e. 之部) will become more apparent, e.g. 來 OC *mə.rˁək : PM *ləi. The modern reflexes of PM *-əi and *-i in modern dialects are illustrated by examples in my papers. The correspondence between OC *o and its reflexes in PM is also a highlight of this project. We found that after acute codas, the correspondence between *OC o and PM *o is highly regular. After back codas, OC rhymes *-rˁoŋ and *-rˁok would behave like those of *-ˁoŋ and *-ˁok respectively in PM (result: 工 ‘work’ and 江 ‘river’ became homophonous). Such behaviors, maintaining the OC structure to a certain extent, are rarely attested across Sinitic languages.

14603918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603918.value: Potential development of this research is of twofold: (1) Separated reconstructions of Proto-Coastal Min and Proto-Inland Min: In his later years, Professor Jerry Norman advocated to reconstruct the proto-languages of Coastal Min (Eastern Min, Southern Min and Pu-Xian) and Inland Min (Northern Min, Central Min and Shao-Jiang Min) separately. In so doing one can have a clearer picture on how the Min dialects were formed. It may also shed new light on the historical connections between Old Chinese and the Min languages. My new GRF project on Pu-Xian Min (CUHK14603222) will partially follow this trend, with an attempt of reconstructing Proto-Coastal Min by incorporating the established Proto-Eastern Min (Akitani 2018, 2020) and Proto-Southern Min (Kwok 2018). (2) An investigation on the connection between Old Chinese and Southern Sinitic languages: On top of Min, it is found that a number of Old Chinese phonological relics can also be found in other Southern Sinitic languages like Hakka, Yue and Waxiang. For instance, various OC origins of Middle Chinese sy- would yield aspirated affricates in Southern Sinitic, a phenomenon that cannot be explained under Middle Chinese. How to interpret this would be of great interest of historical linguists as well as Chinese dialectologists.

14603918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603918.value: Min refers to a group of Sinitic languages spoken mainly in Southeast China, including the Xiamen and the Chaozhou dialects (both affiliated to Southern Min), and the Fuzhou dialect (Eastern Min). While it is generally agreed that Min preserves a good number of archaic phonological features that were lost in other members of Sinitic, the sound correspondences between Old Chinese, the earliest attested forms of Chinese, and Min have yet to be worked out. In this project, we attempted to explore the Old Chinese elements of Min by taking the Old Chinese forms reconstructed by Baxter & Sagart and the Proto-Min/Common-Min forms reconstructed by Norman into comparison. Our target is to gain a better understanding on the historical connections between the two sides. It is found that the Proto-Min forms are basically supportive to the ‘round-vowel hypothesis’ in Old Chinese as pioneered by Yakhontov (1960), who laid an important foundation for a six-vowel system. On the other hand, the Min reflexes also call for revisions for some of the established Old Chinese forms, especially the initials. For instance, we suggested to adjust the reconstruction of ‘fresh’ 鮮 to *s.ŋ-, which would eventually evolve to Proto-Min *tsh-.

14604218.label: Project Objectives
14604218.value: The goal of the research is to re-examine ‘tso-tong’ land in NT with the concept of ‘commons’, focusing on exploring the challenges and possibilities of devising sustainable means to use this resource. Specific objectives are as follows. Finding the commons: systematically examining the heritage of ‘tso-tong’ land in NT and how colonial governance, territorial development such as the building of reservoirs, urban expansion and the evolving regional context have changed the fate of this land resource. Internal challenges in reinventing the commons: through case studies, examine the characteristics of ‘tso-tong’ land; the characteristics of the group ‘owning’ the land resource and their interrelationships; the internal operational rules and institutional set up of these commons; and impacts of commons on members. External challenges in reinventing the commons: with reference to the above case studies, examine state-related regulatory regimes and market-related forces that affect the survival, operation and evolution of ‘tso-tong’ land. Synthesise the internal and external challenges of the above cases over time and assess the potential of reinventing ‘tso-tong’ land as ‘commons’ in rural Hong Kong. Formulate policy and planning recommendations to overcome challenges to reinventing commons in NT that will benefit the sustainable development of both the rural and urban sectors.
