14604218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604218.value: This research aims to use the concept of ‘commons’ (a shared resource that should be managed sustainably) to examine the ‘tso-tong’ land (clan-based customary land trusts) collectively-owned by indigenous villagers in the New Territories (NT), exploring the constraints and possibilities of utilising this little known resource to meet sustainably Hong Kong’s future needs. It is always believed that Hong Kong is short of land. However, built-up area made up only 24.3% of land and discounting country parks in largely rugged terrain (40%), the city should still have 35% of land for use. The majority of land in Hong Kong lies in NT. Indigenous villagers (who were in NT before 1898) used to own the land. It is reported that 6,000 acres (24km2) of land resources are owned collectively by clan-based customary land trusts (called ‘tsos’ if named after an ancestor or ‘tongs’ if it transcends a kin group). This amount is larger than the 16km2 Hong Kong used to build public housing, accommodating 45% (3.3 million) of her population. It is also puzzling why indigenous villagers opt turning their private and ‘tso-tong’ land to brownfield sites (13km2) or selling them to developers (10km2) rather than developing them sustainably. As ‘tso-tong’ land is grossly under-researched in urban planning, this study will attempt to locate ‘tso-tong’ land through the Rural Council (Heung Yee Kuk) and its 27 Rural Committee representatives. Through semi-structured interviews with these representatives, at least one ‘tso’ or ‘tong’ will be studied in detail in each of the 27 Rural Committee jurisdictions. Using a synthesised framework to study ‘commons’, ‘tso’ or ‘tong’ managers, village heads and villagers will be interviewed to gather information on the land resource, the group owning it and the institutional arrangements in the operation of these land trusts. Government, developers and NGOs concerning land development in NT will also be interviewed to trace the impacts of policies, urbanisation and other developments on this land resource. The research findings will be synthesised and ecological and humane planning approaches advocated by the United Nations will be adopted to formulate feasible pathways of re-commoning this land resource. Theoretically, the research provides rare and valuable inputs to understanding ‘commons’ in traditional Chinese culture that has been affected by colonialism and capitalist developments. Practically, it will help the city understand better the state of ‘tso-tong’ land and contribute to a more informed debate about their future sustainable use. 這項研究嘗試用「共有資源」的概念（可持續管理的共享資源）來研究新界原居民擁有的「祖、堂」土地（一種以宗族為本的土地信託），以探討永續利用這鮮為人知的資源來滿足香港未來土地需求的限制和可能性。 人們一直認為香港缺少土地。但是，香港的建成區只佔用了24.3％的土地，而覆蓋大部分崎嶇地勢的郊野公園佔了大約40％。換言之，香港應該還有大概３５％的土地可供使用。香港的大部分土地都在新界，一直由新界原居民（1898年之前已經住在新界的人）擁有。據報導，由宗族集體所有的土地信託（以祖先命名者為「祖」，如果超過一房的，則稱為「堂」）為6,000英畝（即24平方公里）。香港市區只用了16平方公里去建公共房屋，容納了三百三十萬（４５％）的人口。令人費解的是為什麼原居民會選擇把他們的私人和「祖、堂」土地變成棕土（13平方公里）或者將它們賣給開發商（10平方公里）而不是以可持續發展的原則來使用這些資源。 城市規劃對「祖、堂」地的研究嚴重不足，本研究希望可以填補這空白。通過訪談鄉議局和27個鄉鄉事委員會，我們會以「共有資源」的概念來詳細研究其中最少一個「祖或堂」的土地。我們將訪談「祖、堂」地司理，村長和村民以收集有關土地擁有權的信息以及這些土地信託的運作和制度安排。我們也會走訪政府，開發商和非政府組織以追踪政策，城市化及其他發展對有關土地的影響。整合研究結果後，我們會基於聯合國倡導的以生態和人為本的規劃方法來製定「重新共同享用」這一土地資源的可行途徑。 理論上，這研究為理解中國傳統的「共有土地」如何受到殖民主義和資本主義的影響提供了重要和珍貴的材料。實際上，本研究會整理「祖、堂」地的相關資訊，以便我們可以更有效地討論如何能夠持續使用這些土地資源。

14604218.label: Realisation of objectives
14604218.value: TSO-TONG LAND AS A SIGNIFICANT RURAL COMMONS The goal of the research is to re-examine ‘tso-tong’ land in the NT with the concept of ‘commons’, focusing on exploring the challenges and possibilities of devising sustainable means to use this resource. This proves to be extremely fruitful research as Hong Kong is probably the only place on earth that still houses rural commons such as the ‘tso-tong’ land. Tso-tong land refers to land set aside by an ancestor to benefit every living male descendant. It is supposed to be perpetual, not to be divided or sold, unless with unanimous consent. Proceeds from the tso-tong land are used for ancestral worship, maintenance of the ancestral halls, payment of scholarships and red packets for the aged members etc. However, given the unique historical developments of Hong Kong as a post-colonial city, there are considerable challenges to conserving this unique rural commons. There are two types of villages in the NT: Punti (local) villages that occupy the best and flat land in the north and northwestern part of the NT, and Hakka (guest) villages occupying narrow valleys in the hilly areas in the east. The Punti villages were first established in the Song Dynasty. The Hakka villages were developed later and hence had to settle in less favourable land. These villages have their respective ‘tso tong’ land. Yet their fates have changed over the years. DIFFERENT FATES OF THE RURAL COMMONS IN HONG KONG A considerable amount of the ‘tso-tong’ land was once managed according to a ‘one lot two owners’ system: the subsoil was owned by the landlord and the surface soil by the tenant farmers. Given the history of migration of the Puntis and the Hakkas, the former were usually landlords and the latter tenant farmers. However, the British colonial government initiated a ‘land reform’ in the early 1900s, abolished the ‘one lot two owners’ system and granted ownership rights to the active farmers whenever the landlords could not produce their land deeds or received compensation from the government. While rice cropping was the primary farming activity in the NT before WWII, political changes in China in the late 1940s led to an influx of refugees from the mainland. Many of them became vegetable farmers for the land, including ‘tso-tong’ land, in the best parts of the NT. However, life for the Hakka villagers became more difficult. With Hong Kong’s urban expansion, many moved to the city or even overseas. Significant urban expansion took place in Hong Kong in the late 1960s and 1970s. The urban riots in 1966 and 1967 led to the colonial government’s plan to launch a 10-year housing programme to be achieved through new town development. Hence, tso-tong land in the identified new town areas was almost all resumed. Since China’s open door policy in the late 1970s and the integration of Hong Kong’s economy with the mainland, a lot of the agricultural land, including tso-tong land, in the flat Punti village areas has been transformed into brownfield sites. Such transformation has led to different socio-economic and environmental issues in those villages though this also means that their respective tso-tong land can raise handsome operational funds. INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL CHALLENGES OF THE RURAL COMMONS The research undertook a few typical case studies of the tso-tong land in different Punti and Hakka villages and confirm that the internal and external challenges are intertwined. Due to the locational variations and the history of the city’s spatial expansion, the challenges faced by the Punti and Hakka villages are different. There are different kinds of Punti villages in Yuen Long and North districts where tso-tong land has been put to various kinds of uses such as farming, housing and brownfield developments etc. Given their strategic location, the government constantly targets their land for land resumption for infrastructure development; the private sector for real estate development; and land use changes to enhance financial gain. As a result, the tsos and tongs have received a lot of financial benefits. A typical challenge of these commons is how to share the proceeds from land resumption or land sale fairly. Some villages have a policy of not selling their tso-tong land and others have sold most of their tso-tong land in the past due to poor economic situation. In most of the villages that we visited, the representatives were receptive to the idea of land resumption by the government. To those tsos and tongs that have serious internal conflicts, they actually prefer land resumption by the government so that they can ‘liquidate’ their benefits now held in the hands of the powerful ones. SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS AND POLICY AND PLANNING RECOMMENDATIONS Although the research had been seriously affected by the social movements in 2019 and then the world pandemic, the research team managed to visit enough villages and study their cases. A total of 30 village representatives from 18 villagers in 14 Rural Committees were interviewed and the contents were transcribed for analysis. The impossibility of field research was compensated by using geographical information system techniques and purchasing demarcation district sheets of the old schedule lots to identify the rural commons. Though tso-tong land in the NT only makes up about 2,400 hectares, the NT occupies over 80% of the land areas in Hong Kong. For a city so short of land and affordable housing, proper re-planning of the NT will offer the opportunity to resolve deep-seated development issues in the city. However, unfortunately, the reluctance of the colonial government to perform integrated planning between its ceded land in Hong Kong island and Kowloon and the leased New Territories seems to have continued in the Hong Kong SAR Government until recently. And even the announcement of the Northern Metropolis has not tackled the rural heartland but instead has focused on strategic development nodes at the boundary with Shenzhen. The government is studying the relaxation of the threshold for indigenous villagers to sell their tso-tong land. This is rather unfortunate and will further weaken this unique rural commons. The research findings suggest that the fates of the rural commons also depend on how the commoners react and respond to external challenges. Those who value their commons, whether in Punti or Hakka villages and exercise collective actions to maintain their traditions and social cohesion, will find a way to maintain the integrity of their commons. Unfortunately, they seem to be the minority in my studied samples. This study of the tso-tong land reveals an important gap in the city’s spatial planning. There is an urgent need to have proper integrated, holistic and comprehensive planning of the rural NT with a view to encouraging the continuation and flourishing of the rural commons, probably the only such land institution on earth, for the benefits of their respective commoners. Proper re-planning of the rural NT in general and the conservation of tso-tong land for the collective well-being of the indigenous population in particular will also benefit the city. The plan will also provide much needed land for innovative and creative industries, co-working spaces and opportunities to provide housing options that offer alternative lifestyles.

14604218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604218.value: The lack of integrated territorial planning for the rural NT including among other natural and cultural heritage, tso-tong land, is one of the most under-researched factors for Hong Kong’s deep-seated development problems, an argument that I have tried to repeatedly emphasise in all the journal articles, book chapters and newspaper pieces generated from this project (see below). Without proper integration of the rural NT in the city’s overall development strategy, urban development has continued to take place in the ultra-high-density Hong Kong island and Kowloon peninsula (11.3% of land areas in the city) and new towns (15.7% of land area) making more humane and ecological developments difficult if not impossible (Ng, 2020; Ng, Lau, Chen and He, 2021). The failure to integrate the rural NT into the planning landscape has produced two density regimes (Ng et al, 2021; Ng, 2022, 2023; Ng, Yeung, Cheng and Ma, 2023). While urban density ranges from 20,000 to 40,000 per km2, population density in the rural NT is less than 1,200 per km2. The lack of proper planning has also produced unnecessary arguments and conflicts among indigenous and non-indigenous villagers in rural areas (Ng, 2020, 2022). Since there is no record of tso-tong land in the public domain, we have used old schedule lots issued in 1905 in the North and Yuen Long districts to identify the situation of tso-tong land (Ng, under review; Ng, Cheng and Li, 2022). Although the source is old and it is not possible to identify the ownership of tso-tong land without conducting a land record search, we still considered the exercise meaningful because unanimous consent is required for selling tso-tong land except for land resumption. We manage to offer some overall ideas of the spatial distribution, and existing and planned uses of the tso-tong land (Ng, under review). The information provides essential clues for considering the future of tso-tong land (Ng, Cheng and Li, 2022) and the spatial planning for the rural NT (Ng, forthcoming). The research adds to the international literature on the commons by offering a framework to examine the spatial and management outcomes of individual commons. While tso-tong land has its attributes with associated rules and norms, the fate of individual commons also depends on the capability, knowledge, values, goals and strategies of the commoners as they react to the broader political and economic developments and related policies, discourses and rules (Ng, under review; Ng et al, 2023).

14604218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604218.value: The research points to an urgent need to study the rural NT. The rural NT embedding the world’s unique rural commons, tso-tong land, should become part of an integrated territorial plan, strategically integrating the new Northern Metropolis and the old Harbour Metropolis. Both the Punti and Hakka villages deserve more in-depth studies. Currently, the government’s Countryside Conservation Office is providing funding for revitalising and conserving remote villages which are mainly Hakka ones. More resources are required to document the history and potential of regenerating those villages. And the Punti villages in the north and northwestern NT require immediate attention too because while they face tremendous development pressure, the planning and development regime fails to steer its development in an integrated, holistic and sustainable manner. Indeed, if done right, a development that respects natural and cultural heritage can take place, revitalising the rural commons, providing essential spaces for necessary economic activities, decommissioning the small house policy through higher density developments in rural settlements, and turning brownfield sites into integrated developments that provide quality living and working spaces etc. A proposal will be submitted to the Public Policy Research Fund Scheme to apply for funding to undertake such a study.

14604218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604218.value: Tso-tong land in Hong Kong is a unique rural commons that probably cannot be found elsewhere. The clan-based customary land trusts are established to sustain traditional practices and the welfare of their male descendants. Unlike private agricultural land, tso-tong land still exists because selling it requires unanimous agreement among members. Our research shows that tso-tong land is fragmented. While tso-tong land may not be optimally utilised in the more remote Hakka villages, tso-tong land in the flat land of north and northwestern Punti (local) villages have undergone dramatic changes. Some tso-tong land has become brownfield sites while others are used for farming, housing development etc. As the rural New Territories constitutes a critical zone between the new Northern Metropolis and the old Harbour Metropolis, it is high time this area be re-planned appropriately regarding its natural and cultural heritage including tso-tong land. An integrated territorial plan for the rural New Territories will boost its urban-rural linkage functions, consolidating existing sporadic developments, rationalising the distribution of brownfield and rural industrial activities, increasing development densities in specific strategic locations, revitalising fertile agricultural land and offering quality living and working environments for the local population and urbanites who aspire for alternative living environments.

14604318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604318.value: By comparing mortuary ritual and patterns of memorialization in cemeteries in five southern Chinese cities, this research will underpin a book on urbanization and socio-economic transformation during the reform era. Three lenses on socioeconomic transformation will be utilized. The first is economic. Funerary ritual involves considerable economic expenditure as well as the settling of the economic accounts of the deceased. At funerals, gifts are exchanged between friends and families, battles emerge over inheritance, government offices make payouts to families of pensioners, stigmatized forms of small businesses provide short-term cash services to grieving families, and large state-capitalist corporations sell long-term forms of memorialization. The evolution of these forms of economic transaction will be compared and contrasted among the five cities and across class lines. The second is familial. On tombstones and in funerary ritual familial relationships are staged for public display. The evolution of these displays will likewise be compared and contrasted among the five cities and along class lines. Finally, acts of memorialization are forms of remembrance and memory is a highly political arena in the People’s Republic of China. What about the deceased is memorialized and how this varies across class lines, among different cities, and over time will be analysed to illuminate both the politics of memorialization and the cultural dynamics of urbanization in China. 通過研究殯葬業在五個華南城市，這個項目要提供關於城市化的社會轉變的資料。本項目研究社會轉變的三個方面。第一是經濟方面。殯葬業涉及好幾種經濟，包括禮儀經濟，遺傳經濟，商業經濟等等。第二是家庭轉變。 墓碑和葬禮顯示家庭關係。第三是政治轉變。在中國，紀念活動非常政治化。本項目要比較這三種轉變在不同城市， 不同社會階層， 和不同歷史階段。

14604318.label: Realisation of objectives
14604318.value: The project objectives were mostly achieved, despite the fact that I was not able to travel to China after the start of the pandemic in late 2019. The most important objective, the writing of a book that integrated the discussion of various aspects of social change in urban China through the lens of funerary ritual was achieved through the publication of The Funeral of Mr. Wang with the University of California Press in the second half of 2021. I am very pleased with this outcome. I still would like to visit more cemeteries and interview more people in the funerary industry in China some day, in order to complete research objectives one through four. I will attempt to do so once the pandemic and related travel restrictions ease, though it will no longer be with money from this grant. Completing those research objectives will help me write additional research articles related to this project. I note that I did not spend a substantial portion of the research funds allotted by this grant. The amount of money that I am returning does not really reflect the amount of research that I was able to complete. I was able to complete 65-85% of the field research, but I spent much less than 75% of the budgeted amount for field research because a university in China provided free accommodation and many other forms of support to me at an important research site in exchange for my giving several lectures there. This free accommodation reduced the cost of the field research that I did complete. Obviously the field research I did not complete relates to pandemic travel restrictions.

14604318.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604318.value: Some of the major research findings of this project include understanding how the shrinking of family size and community integration in urban China is reflected through funerary ritual. For example, reduction in household size has made relationships between related households more important and made the distinction between family and non-family members more distinct. The distinction between family and non-family members is reflected in gift giving patterns at funerals. A second important finding relates to the stigmatization of those who work in the funerary industry. This stigmatization also relates to the family non-family distinction discussed above as funerary workers are strangers who are involved in an intimate aspect of familial life. A third finding relates to the placement of funerary service providers at the outskirts of the city. This makes the experience of death ever more remote in urbanizing China and leads to heightened levels of fear and discomfort with death, cemeteries, ghosts, and strangers. A fourth finding relates to the increasingly negative environment for the funerary services industry in China. It is a matter of both land use policy and a politically negative attitude by the government towards forms of memorialization that do not glorify the Party. The most important outcome of this project is the publication of the book _The Funeral of Mr. Wang: Life, Death and Ghosts in Urbanizing China_ .(University of California Press, 2021). the book is open acess and may be dowloaded for free at the press's website.

14604318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604318.value: As mentioned above, I would like to complete research objectives 1-4 by visiting more cemeteries in China and interviewing more people in the funerary industry. Further tracing patterns of class differentiation in mortuary ritual would be fascinating. I would also like to develop a future research project on the reasons why so many Hong Kong residents choose to memorialize their ancestors in columbaria niches rather than other means. This preference is both a pressing practical issue for Hong Kong (as there is a shortage of columbaria niches), and speaks to issues of imagining Hong Kong as a home in turbulent political times.

14604318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604318.value: In rural China funerals are conducted locally, on village land by village elders. But in urban areas, people have neither land for burials nor elder relatives to conduct funerals. Chinese urbanization, which has increased drastically in recent decades, involves the creation of cemeteries, state-run funeral homes, and small private funerary businesses. This projects examined social change in urbanizing China through the lens of funerals, the funerary industry, and practices of memorialization. It analyzed changes in family life, patterns of urban sociality, transformations in economic relations, the politics of memorialization, and echoes of these changes in beliefs about the dead and ghosts.

To explore how and why the intervention affects health outcomes from the patients’ perspectives.

14604418.label: Realisation of objectives
14604418.value: For Objective 1, the investigation team used the first three months to develop the initial draft of the intervention for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), titled “the nurse-led multi-component behavioural activation (N-MBA) program. Then, a group of 11 AF patients with various socio-demographic background was invited to comment on the comprehensiveness of the intervention. Based on their comments and suggestions, the N-MBA program was finalized. It comprised four care components to activate self-care behaviours in patients with AF: (i) risk profile assessment and shared decision-making regarding oral anticoagulant (OAC) use; (ii) empowerment-based educational module on AF self-care; (iii) nurse-initiated telephone support; and (iv) patient-initiated contact for professional advice. The nurse first conducted individualized risk assessments before their next medical appointment to make patients aware of their stroke risks with and without OACs and bleeding risks with OACs, using numeric and graphical pictograms as decision aids. The decision aids organized treatment options as option grids to facilitate comparison and clarification of the options. The nurse then encouraged the patients to discuss the use of OACs with their physicians. Assertive communication skills in asking questions, expressing concerns, and stating preferences regarding OACs for stroke prevention were highlighted. Scenario-based videos and role play rehearsals were used to enhance skill acquisition. This was followed by a 5-weekly group-based educational module that covered all of the major topics related to AF self-care: medication management, symptom monitoring, crisis management, activities and exercise, and risk factor management to reduce the risks of stroke and bleeding. The educational content of each session complied with the major practice guidelines for AF management. To enhance effective learning, the nurse delivered each session using an empowerment model. During these sessions, the nurse used interactive teaching strategies, experiential learning, goal setting, and action planning, with an emphasis on helping patients to understand the links between their self-care behaviours and health consequences. Upon completion of the educational module, the nurse monitored patients’ adherence to suggested self-care actions, symptom profiles, treatment efficacies, adverse effects, and goal attainment progress; identified barriers to self-care; and provided resolutions and continued support via regular telephone calls (four calls over 6 weeks). The participants were provided telephone access to the nurse for inquiries regarding disease management. The nurse provided health advice and counselling accordingly. The content of the intervention was reviewed by an expert panel that consisted of five members including cardiologists, cardiac nurses and nursing academia specializing in cardiovascular care. The panel members rated the appropriateness and relevance of the content on a 10-item content validity survey, each item to be rated on a 1 - 4 Likert scale, with a higher score representing better quality. The mean score for the content validation was 3.91, indicating excellent content validity. They commented the intervention content was highly relevant to equip patients to take an active role in communicant their concerns about AF and its health risks to their physicians. In view of the strong paternalism of the healthcare system and the power dynamic of the physician-patient relationship, the panel members suggested enhancing the intervention content relating to assertive communication skills, so as to minimize patients’ reluctance to discuss their concerns with the physicians. Scenario-based teaching strategy with role play was added to strengthen the acquisition of communication skills. In addition, the panel members suggested other than crisis management relating to major bleeding and stroke, patients should also be educated on how to handle more common treatment and disease-related side effects and complications, such as gastrointestinal bleeding and fast AF attacks. These suggestions were taken to fine tune the intervention. The full-scale randomized controlled trial was commenced in May 2019. The research nurse used two approaches to identify eligible subjects for evaluating the effects of the N-MBA program. First, a single-lead electrocardiographic device was used to screen for AF among those subjects with unknown AF status. The research nurse also identified potential participants from the Clinical Management System of the study hospital. The project implementation was negatively affected by the social unrest happened from June 2019 to January 2020. Participants expressed concerns about safety issues for attending the intervention sessions. The progress was further influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic since February 2020. The study was suspended periodically according to the infection control measures of the study hospital. With the approval of RGC, the research collaboration was extended to more sectors for subject recruitment and project extension of 6 months in June 2021. Throughout the study period, 5,341 individuals underwent eligibility evaluation, of which 4,949 were excluded. The primary reason was that they did not have AF. Among those with confirmed AF (n=529), reasons for exclusion from the study were having a low CHA2DS2-VASc score, being younger than 60 years, and having cognitive impairment. Fifty-eight patients (11.0%) met the eligibility criteria but declined to join, mostly because of scheduling, willingness, or being physically unfit to travel. The remaining 392 were randomized into the intervention (n = 198) or control group (n = 194). The attrition rates immediately after the completion of the intervention (T1) and at the 6-month follow-up (T2) were 11.7% and 14.3%, respectively. Objective 2: Patients who have participated in the N-MBA program were invited to attend a qualitative interview to solicit their in-depth comments on their engagement experience in the intervention, perceived effects from their perspectives to explain the quantitative findings. They were selected on the basis of the changes in the primary outcome, that is health-related quality of life (HRQoL). In addition, patients with different demographic and clinical background (i.e., gender, education attainment, and CHA2DS2-VASc score) were invited. A total of 32 participants completed the qualitative interview. Guided by a semi-structured interview guide, these participants were elicited to discuss how the intervention affected their understanding about AF and its health consequences, and perceived impacts of the intervention on their health outcomes. Each interview lasted from 40 to 78 minutes. All the audio-taped interviews were transcribed verbatim and checked for accuracy, before subjecting to analysis.

14604418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604418.value: The intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in HRQoL measured by the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on QualiTy-of-life questionnaire than the control group at T1 [β=-6.702, 95% confidence interval (CI)=-9.556 to -3.847, p <0.001], and this positive effect was sustained at T2 (β=-5.593, 95% CI=-8.491 to -2.695, p <0.001). The Hedges’ g values at T1 and T2 were 0.346 and 0.225, respectively, indicating small effect sizes. No significant between-group difference was found for the decision concordance between patients and physicians regarding the use of OAC. A higher proportion of the participants in the intervention group were prescribed an OAC than those in the control group at T2 (odds ratio=5.870, 95% CI=1.957 – 12.331, p=0.012). The intervention group demonstrated significantly better medication adherence than the control group at T1 (β=0.340, 95% CI=0.148–0.532, p<0.001) and T2 (β=0.265, 95% CI=0.081–0.449, p =0.005), with small effect sizes at both time points (Hedges’ g=-0.228 and -0.151, respectively). No significant between-group differences were found in anxiety and depression at T1 or T2. A sensitivity analysis was conducted by including participants with a CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 for male patients and ≥3 for female patients, as the clinical guidelines suggest OAC as a Class 1A recommendation for these patients. The analyses indicated consistent results with the main analyses on all primary and secondary outcomes. The qualitative phase found that participants were highly satisfied with the intervention content. Most of them did not have much understanding about AF before attending the intervention. Six of them even did not realize that they have AF. The intervention has significantly raised their awareness about AF and its associated health risks, particularly ischemic stroke. In particular, they found that the decision aid booklet was very effective to empower them in making decision relating to stroke prevention, as the decision aid facilitated them to compare and contrast the pros and cons of different treatments. They were also assisted to understand their individualized stroke risk, which served as a crucial information to guide their decision-making. All these improved illness and treatment perception, together with the enhanced communication skill, rendered them to be more assertive in communicating their treatment concern with the physicians. The participants further highlighted the availability of the nurse via the telephone for prompt professional advice, which was crucial to booster their confidence in AF management. Among those patients with minimal changes in HRQoL, their baseline scores were high, rendering limited room for improvement.

14604418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604418.value: The investigation team is planning to adopt this evidence-based intervention to benefit a wider range of population by submitting an application to the Research Impact Fund in 2024/25’s round. For this translational research project, we will aim to apply the established intervention materials to benefit a larger population beyond the cohort with confirmed diagnosis. AF is often underdiagnosed, as up to 40% of the patients are asymptomatic. Despite the symptom status, these asymptomatic patients bear the same health risks as the symptomatic patients. Therefore, identifying these individuals from the community is of crucial importance to reduce the healthcare burden. The translational research project has two preliminary objectives: 1) to increase the awareness of the general public and high-risk population about AF and its health risks; 2) to increase the accessibility of our intervention to the asymptomatic patients hidden in the community through massive screening. Furthermore, the investigation team is conducting a follow-up study to capture objective clinical and patient-reported outcomes of the participants in this GRF study, including stroke and bleeding rates, long-term adherence to OAC and mortality. The findings of this follow-up study would provide valuable evidence on the longer-term effects of the intervention on clinically meaningful outcomes.

14604418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14604418.value: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common abnormal cardiac rhythm. AF patients are prone to develop adverse health outcomes, including ischemic stroke, heart failure and deaths. Despite the existence of guideline-based indications for preventing stroke by using oral anticoagulants (OAC), under-prescription is a prominent problem, mainly resulting from inadequate patient–physician communication on treatment preference and risk analysis, as well as limited self-care by patients. We developed a nurse-led multi-component behavioural activation intervention. It consisted of four care components to activate self-care behaviours in AF patients, including risk profile assessment and shared decision-making regarding OAC use, educational module on AF self-care, nurse-initiated telephone support, and patient-initiated contact for professional advice. By randomly assigning 392 patients with AF who had high stroke risk but not using OAC to the multi-component behavioural activation intervention or standard care, we found that the intervention was effective to improve health-related quality of life, medication adherence and, more importantly, increase OAC prescription among patients with AF. The study provided empirical evidence on an effective nurse-led intervention to activate AF patients to become an active agent in disease management, which is of great significance in curtaining the healthcare burden associated with AF- and treatment-related complications.

14604618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604618.value: A combination of vernacular bamboo craftsmanship and digital design technology enables radically unique and spatially versatile architectural solutions rooted in local culture and sustainable building practices. This action research project will build on earlier fundamental research on the digital design and implementation of bending-active bamboo shell structures in Hong Kong and will aim at developing 1) an expanded ‘Taxonomy Overview’ and 2) ‘Guidelines for Best Practice’ for their computation-driven architectural design. The study will combine research in 1) architectural design with digital physics-simulation engines, 2) low-tech, light-weight construction systems and 3) vernacular bamboo building traditions. Bamboo is a material of high environmental and socio-cultural importance. It is one of the fastest growing, widely available, low-cost, carbon-sequestering natural resources suitable for direct implementation in construction. It has globally been part of vernacular construction for centuries. Expanding its design solution space with contemporary answers will positively impact the development of the built environment and the locally significant but dwindling cultural craftsmanship. Bending-active shells are amongst the most material-efficient, hyper-light-weight structures. They rely for strength and construction implementation on the overall geometrical double curvature and elastic bending properties of their components. Their nonstandard geometries provide unique spatial design opportunities, and their material efficiency results in a reduced need for natural resources. Two types of bending-active gridshell structures exist. 1) ‘Flatbed’ structures employ initially flat, prefabricated, regular grids with no shear rigidity, and elastically deform and brace those into place. 2) The ‘lay-up’ method additively bends and joins individual members into a final shape onsite. Both types present important opportunities and restrictions. Prior research illustrates that computational tools considerably facilitate their development; yet, no scholarly study exists on hybrid structures, and limited research exists on bamboo applications. Following a pragmatic ‘Reflective Practice’ and ‘Action Research’ methodology, the proposed project’s two-year research plan will follow a ‘Plan-Act-Observe-Reflect’ spiral centring on digital design tool development and physical prototyping testing. Supported by a team of specialists, the iterative project stages will result in a comprehensive ‘Taxonomy Overview’, and verified ‘Guidelines for Best Practice’ for the design and construction of bamboo bending-active shell structures. The studied structures will present a spatially versatile and practically applicable, eco-friendly tectonic system, suitable for the low-tech, labour-driven, onsite construction contexts found in most rapidly developing parts of the world. The combination of a ‘Taxonomy Overview’ and ‘Best Practice Guidelines’ will practically expand their potential by increasing accessibility and applicability in real-world construction. 通過結合本地竹手工藝和數字設計技術，建築設計可以將獨具特色且空間靈活的方案融入到當地文化和可持續建設當中。此行動研究項目基於前期在香港進行的基礎研究，包括對於彎曲主導的圓竹殼體結構的數字設計和實踐，并致力於進一步1）擴大“分類綜述”和2）制定數字化建築設計的“最佳實踐準則”。 本研究將會包括1）數字物理模擬引擎引導下的建築設計，2）低技術和輕型建造系統，以及3）本地竹建築傳統。 竹子是一種對環保和社會文化具有極高重要性的材料。其生長迅速、散佈地區廣泛、廉價、碳吸收的特性使其作為一種自然材料可以直接用於建造施工。數百年來許多地區已將竹子用作本地建設。通過擴展竹材料的設計可能性來應對當代的需求，將會對建造環境和正在消逝的本地竹手工藝產生積極的影響。 彎曲主導的殼體結構是一種材料效率高、超輕型的結構體系。結構的強度和建造關鍵在於其雙曲率的幾何形式和具有彎曲彈性的構件。非標準化的形式提供了創造獨特空間感受的機會，同時，高材料效率將有效減少對自然資源的需求。 目前共有兩種彎曲主導的殼體結構。1）“平板”結構指的是將初始狀態是平面的，無切向強度的等距網格通過彈性彎曲支撐到位。2）“鋪疊”方法則是通過現場逐步添加、彎曲、固定桿件單元從而得到最終的結構形式。兩種結構形式各有利弊。之前的研究強調了數字技術有助於此類結構形式的發展，但是對於混合結構體系還沒有相關學術研究，並且對於竹材料的應用的研究更是少之甚少。 本研究採用一套參數化“反思性實踐”和“行動研究”的方法。以兩年為週期的項目將遵循一套“計劃-執行-觀察-反思”的循環邏輯，研究重心在於數字化工具的研發和實體大樣的測試。項目團隊由專家組成，并通過不同階段的反復實踐，最終結果將會得到一套對設計和建造彎曲主導的圓竹殼體結構體系的完整 “分類綜述”以及測試過的“最佳實踐準則”。 本研究將會展現一種空間多樣、實施性強、環保的建構體系。此種建構體系將適用於世界上普遍面臨低技術、多人力勞動，現場作業多的快速發展地區。通過在現實實踐中增加通用性和適用性，“分類綜述”和“最佳實踐準則”的結合將會得到最大的發揮。

14604618.label: Realisation of objectives
14604618.value: Objectives of this grant have been largely realised despite the substantial disruptions and delays the project has experienced due to the pandemic. As these are being overcome as we speak, all objectives will be fully achieved in coming months. 1) “Objective 1: Compile and develop a comprehensive overview of computation-driven methods and tools for the architectural design and implementation of bamboo bending-active shell structures in Hong Kong, including ‘flatbed’, ‘lay-up’ and ‘hybrid’ setups” has been achieved for 95%. The remaining 5% reflects the need to revise and update any possible items following recently-completed/upcoming full-scale testing and prototyping. 2) “Objective 2: Develop a ‘Taxonomy Overview’ of obj. 1’s design solution space” has also been achieved for 95%. Feedback from recently- completed/upcoming full-scale built prototypes will allow us to refine the taxonomy in response to a comprehensive practical feasibility assessment. This assessment may possibly filter out some sectors of the design solution space, or may provide those with practical constraint requirements, for example in terms of feasible scale or size of the overall structure or used materials. 3) “Objective 3: Test objs. 1 and 2 through design workshops and physical prototyping” has been achieved 90%. The final 10% will be reached in coming months as the evaluation is taking place of a built prototype that was completed in November 2022 following extensive COVID-delays and of upcoming full-scale construction of key prototypes scheduled for 2023. 4) “Objective 4: Compile ‘Guidelines for Best Practice’, including inferring how findings can be expanded beyond the local into broader generalisations and applications” has been completed for 90% and has been made available on the publicly accessible website https://bsl.hku.hk/babss/. The remaining 10% reflects the need to revise and update the content following assessment of the full-scale testing and prototypes. This is scheduled for 2023 and time and resources are made available for this. The project centred on the testing of developed methods, tools, and techniques, and the system’s associated expanded design solution space through design workshops and physical prototype construction. These were scheduled to take place outdoors in Hong Kong in collaboration with bamboo scaffolding masters of the Construction Industry Council (CIC) and overseas (a.o. in Bali, Indonesia (see original education plan)). However, due to COVID 19 restrictions on international travel and on public outdoor gathering in Hong Kong, this testing has not been possible in time. An alternative research plan was forcibly implemented in line with the original objectives and taking on the one-year granted extension of the project. This modified research plan since early 2020 includes following key items: 1. In the summer of 2020, a summer course, titled “ARCH7478 - Bending Bamboo Rules”, was taught by the PI at HKU in which preliminary methods and guidelines for best architectural design practice of bending-active bamboo shell structures were taught to a group of 13 Master of Architecture students, who tested them out through the production of a series of physical 1:20 scale models (see the course planner in Appendix). 2. In June 2021, an international online workshop was taught by the PI for the organisation “Digital Futures 2021”, in which a group of 16 international architecture students were taught a next iteration of the methods and guidelines for best architectural design practice of bending-active bamboo shell structures (see teaching certificate in Appendix). 3. In the fall of 2021, the PI accepted the invite to design a “Rural Construction Studio” in Anji, China, using our methods developed for the design of bending-active bamboo grid shell. This project was scheduled to be constructed in 2022, but is to this day delayed due to COVID restrictions. We hope this will take place in 2023. This design was done in collaboration with the architecture design practice Laboratory for Explorative Architecture and Design Ltd. (LEAD) (see project images in Appendix). 4. In July 2022, the PI was invited by the Architectural Association, London (UK) to teach a Visiting School Programme for them in São Paulo (Brazil) on bending-active bamboo shell structures. In this workshop, an early version of the online tutorial platform with methods and guidelines for best architectural design practice of bending-active bamboo shell structures was used to teach a group of 17 international student and workshop assistants. This workshop also resulted in the construction of the "Belas Bambu". 5. In November 2022, following a delay of over 1 year due to COVID, the PI completed the construction of the "Somewhere Bamboo Pavilion" in Hong Kong, which uses some of the methods developed for the design of bending-active bamboo grid shell. This design was done in collaboration with the architecture design practice Laboratory for Explorative Architecture and Design Ltd. (LEAD). Processing and evaluation of the research outcome is still taking place, with publication of the results scheduled for 2023 (see project images in Appendix). 6. In December 2022, a first version of the online tutorial platform with methods and guidelines for best architectural design practice of bending-active bamboo shell structures was launched on https://bsl.hku.hk/babss/. This platform will continue to be expanded and developed in 2023. 7. (upcoming) In March 2023, the PI is scheduled to teach a design-and-build workshop in Ubud (Bali, Indonesia) in collaboration with Bamboo U (https://www.bamboou.com/) where the aim is to build a full-scale bending-active bamboo gridshell using our developed methods. Research finding from this experience will be published in 2023. 8. (upcoming) In Summer 2023, the PI is again invited by the Architectural Association, London (UK) to teach a second Visiting School Programme for them in São Paulo (Brazil) on bending-active bamboo shell structures. In this workshop, we will again use the online tutorial platform to teach and then build a bamboo shell structure. Research finding from this experience will be published in 2023/2024. 9. (upcoming) The PI has been preliminary invited to design one of the three major bamboo architecture pieces that will operate as the highlight for the World Bamboo Conference, which will take place in Taiwan in spring 2024. This provides us with a major full-scale demonstrator opportunity for this research project. As several large-scale prototypes recently have or are only now about to be completed, the qualitative data and quantitative information from the assessment of both the digital tools and built output still requires to be further extracted and incorporated in updated guidelines for best practice. The delay also resulted in a lack of data needed to produce the anticipated peer-reviewed journal article research output. Originally scheduled to take place in the Phase 2 of the project in the summer of 2020, these tasks are only now gradually starting to become possible as the research data becomes available. Note that the project extension did not come with additional funding to provide extension of the needed research assistance required in that period of time. Nonetheless, the PI is on track to catch up with outstanding items: In 2023, all four objectives will be met 100% and at least two further research article submissions will be made to academic journals.

14604618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604618.value: The major finding and research outcome from this project are the architectural design practice methods and guidelines for the design of bending-active bamboo shell structures, as published on https://bsl.hku.hk/babss/. They comprise of an extensive series of digital design tools that provide architects access to the radically new and different mode of working that is required for these structures. Using the popular 3D NURBS modelling platform Rhinoceros and its procedural modelling plugin Grasshopper, a methodology has been iteratively developed through numerous design case studies, prototypes, and educational courses, and refined and distilled to be as easily accessible for architects with prior platform knowledge. Rather than “drawing” designs, the technique requires designers to “generate” shell structures: after defining specific topology setups and boundary conditions, a digital simulation engine is used to have equilibrium structures “emerge” in response to specific bamboo material- and context-specific loading properties. The two major types of bending-active gridshell structures are covered, as well as a hybrid between them. The first type, “flatbed” structures, employs initially flat, prefabricated, regular grids with no shear rigidity, and elastically deforms and braces those into place. This technique is combined with methods from structures using the “lay-up” method, which additively bends and joins individual members into a final shape onsite. The topology setups consist of interconnected curve networks, representing the axis lines of bamboo culms, that are given a material behaviour similar to that of bamboo when it is bent. Geometry restrictions are then defined that reflect the structure foundations and anchors that will hold the final design project in place. Once defined, the final curved geometric structures are then generated using a digital spring-particle-based physics simulation engine. Outcomes can then be subjected to various bamboo material- and building context- specific performance criteria tests. These includes tests to assess whether or not designs fall within permissible curvatures, analyse the structural behaviour under wind loads, self-weight, and initial strain from curvature, analyse deflection, etc. All of these analysis results can be visualised in real-time, allowing designers to quickly design structures for selected bamboo materials and project locations. The method has and is currently being further tested at full scale, prototypes of which confirmed validity.

14604618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604618.value: The study identified a wide potential for further development and research: 1. Future built applications of the methods in practice will provide valuable feedback on how to further optimise, develop and refine the tools and techniques. Several projects are currently lined up for this (e.g. Bali, 2023; Brazil, 2023; Taiwan, 2024). 2. An opportunity has been identified for interdisciplinary research related to the field Extended Reality (XR). Pilot studies, like the São Paulo workshop, explored the incorporation of Augmented Reality (AR) technology in project implementation to ease real-time building model information and data communication to craftsman operating onsite. A former RA of this research currently pursues a Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme-sponsored doctoral study on this topic, supervised by the PI. 3. The study revealed a global knowledge gap in bamboo-specific material properties for structural evaluation of bent bamboo structures. The PI has secured HK$1,000,000 in funding from the Seed Funding for Strategic Interdisciplinary Research Scheme 2021/22 (University Research Committee with matching by Faculty of Architecture) for the project titled “Empowering High-Performance Bamboo Construction: A Low-Cost, Material Informatics-driven, Culm Structural Properties Definition System”, for which a Collaborative Research Fund application is scheduled for 2023.

14605218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605218.value: The aim of this project is to explore empirically the important question: what is the role and workings of corporate boards in mainland Chinese listed firms. Corporate boards play a central role in the governance of public companies. The board takes important decisions on such matters as the undertaking of major projects and the hiring of senior executives. It also controls and monitors, so as to align managerial interests more closely with shareholder (and stakeholder) interests. In the past two decades, a string of corporate scandals has thrust the board into the very centre of corporate governance reforms in China and worldwide. Although the comparative literature on the changing board characteristics has been rapidly expanding, the role and workings of Chinese corporate boards remain seriously understudied and under-theorised. This project aims to fill this important lacuna, and thereby to enhance significantly our understanding of corporate governance reforms both in mainland China and more generally. The project will investigate both types of board – the board of directors and the supervisory board – used in China’s management-supervisory dual-board structure. Drawing on two unique, hand-collected datasets on the dual-boards of Chinese listed firms, as well as qualitative data on the behavioural strategies of board members to be obtained with the support of a network of collaborating PRC securities regulators, this project will present new insights into, among other things, the pattern of board composition, structure and independence, the determinants of board members’ observable behavior (such as voting behavior), and the impact of recent board reforms on the governance of Chinese listed firms. It is anticipated that the systematic, empirical and comparative analysis of corporate boards in China, which this project offers, will inform and help to generate a more grounded theory for better understanding the role that board reforms play in the protection of shareholder interests and the development of national securities markets, with particular reference to China but also more generally. The importance of such understanding is enhanced by the fact that major China-based corporations are now becoming significant global players as well. The theoretical and empirical findings of this project will also contribute to better minority shareholder protection in China, as the effectiveness of the legal and regulatory reforms aimed at strengthening shareholder rights is critically dependent on the manner in which boards are held accountable to shareholders. 本研究旨在通過實證方法研究中國上市公司董監事會的作用和運作方式。 董監事會在上市公司治理中扮演至關重要的角色。一方面，董監事會承擔決策職責，決定公司重大投資項目，招聘高級管理人員。另一方面，董監事會還扮演監督者的角色，督促公司管理人員勤勉履職，對公司股東和利益相關方負責。近年來，在中國和世界其他國家不時出現上市公司醜聞，使得董監事會制度成為公司治理改革的重中之重。對於董監事會制度的比較法學研究日益增多，然而對中國董監事會作用和運作方式的實證研究尚付闕如。本課題試圖填補此研究空白，以期加深對公司治理改革的理論和實證研究。 本課題研究對象包括中國上市公司的董事會和監事會。根據定量研究需要，本課題創建兩個特別的資料庫，並系統收集董監事行為特徵的定量資料，希冀在此基礎上研究若干重要問題，例如中國董監事會的組成、結構和獨立性，董監事行為（特別是表決行為）的決定因素，董監事會改革舉措對中國上市公司治理的影響等。 本研究通過系統性的實證和比較分析，將在理論上進一步揭示董監事會制度改革在保護中小股東利益和發展證券市場中的作用。

14605218.label: Realisation of objectives
14605218.value: Quantitative and qualitative investigation undertaken under the project has been guided by, and directed to fulfill, its five objectives. All five objectives have been successfully and fully achieved. Objective 1: To articulate the historical, economic and political contexts in which the legal and regulatory framework for China’s management-supervisory dual-board structure has evolved This component of the project has relied primarily on materials derived from secondary sources. A comprehensive documentary archive has been created, tracing the evolution and functioning of corporate boards under Chinese law. This archive collects not only published materials that are more readily accessible (such as research monographs, yearbooks, journal articles, and newspaper entries), but also materials that are ‘internal’ in nature, yet are not classified or otherwise confidential. The latter include ‘internal’ policy reports, and ‘internal’ policy addresses. They are particularly useful for gaining an insight into the academic and policy debates on how best to reform China’s corporate board structure, composition, and independence, among others. These secondary materials are supplemented, importantly, by elite interviews. Interviews have been conducted with senior and rank-and-file officials, both serving and former, at the regulatory bodies who were involved in the development of China’ corporate board legal regime. These interviews have shed light on the underlying, often times undocumented, considerations that account for the regulatory initiatives taken on improving board independence and accountability, as well as their institutional constraints. Objective 2: To examine empirically the composition, structure and independence of both boards of directors and supervisory boards in Chinese listed companies; Objective 3: To discern empirically the determinants of the behavioural patterns exhibited by board members of Chinese listed firms; and Objective 4: To determine empirically the impact of recent board reforms on the governance of Chinese listed firms; In order to achieve Objectives 2, 3 and 4, two distinct, albeit related datasets have been constructed, one focusing on the characteristics of the boards of directors (BoDs) of all Chinese listed firms during the 2004-2017 period, and the other on the attributes of these firms’ supervisory boards (SBs) during the same period. Board of Directors Dataset The BoD Dataset comprises data on board memberships, board committees, and board resolutions and the results of voting thereon. Construction of the BoD Dataset is based primarily on company disclosures of BoD meetings, collected from CNInfo, an officially designated source for Chinese listed firms to make disclosures. These disclosures contain useful quantitative data on, inter alia, the dates and venues of BoD meetings, the number of board members present or represented, the nature of each of the resolutions voted on, and the voting results of each resolution (the numbers of “for” votes, votes “against”, and votes “withheld”). The BoD Dataset includes, additionally, data on a cohort of selected independent variables, including firm’s characteristics (including market capitalisation, ownership structure, identity of the controlling shareholder, financial performance, level of institutional shareholdings, and voting arrangements) and the complex set of constraints facing board members (including, inter alias, any prior enforcement actions taken by securities regulatory authorities against directors, and board members’ prior professional experience). Supervisory Board Dataset The SB Dataset comprises data on board memberships, and board resolutions and the results of voting thereon. Similar to the BoD Dataset, construction of the SB Dataset is based on company disclosures, including votes cast at SB meetings. It also shares with the BoD Dataset data on a similar cohort of selected independent variables, including the aforementioned firm characteristics and other constraints, that might impact on SB members’ behaviour. Elite Interviews The private, confidential nature of the behind-the-scenes interactions of corporate boards means that they are usually unobservable in studies that rely entirely on publicly available data. Therefore, in addition to the quantitative data described above, elite interviews have also been carried out to acquire valuable qualitative data that help achieve the objectives 2, 3 and 4. I have interviewed BoD and SB members of the Chinese listed firms, as well as the controlling shareholders of those firms (or their representatives in the case of state-owned firms). Lines of questioning will include, among others: how do inside BoD and SB members interact with the shareholders that appoint them in setting board agendas; how do outside/ independent directors get identified and nominated; how do inside members of BoD and SB interact with outside/independent directors on issues susceptible to majority-minority conflict, particularly in the face of the majority-of-the-minority rule as applicable to related party transactions; how do outside/ independent directors balance the appointer-appointee relationship and the risks of being targeted by law enforcement for corporate wrongdoings; and so on. Interviews have also been conducted to gain a greater understanding of how listed firms and their controlling/ significant shareholders have been affected by, and have reacted to, recent board reforms. The interviewees included rank-and-file bureaucrats of the government agencies controlling the identified listed firms (in the case of state-owned firms) as well as institutional investors (in the case of firms with a significant institutional shareholder presence). Moreover, interviews have also been carried out with officials of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, as well as executives of the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges, who are responsible for the making and enforcement of the rules and regulations on corporate boards. Quantitative observations arising from the two hand-collected Datasets above have been discussed during the interviews. Objective 5: To propose a more grounded theory for better understanding the role that board reforms play in the development of national securities markets, with particular reference to China but also more generally Building on the quantitative and qualitative research described above, I have successfully engaged in work of conceptualization and generalization, and have developed a theoretical framework that enriches the comparative discourse on corporate board reforms. The theoretical findings form the basis of two journal articles currently under review, one of which is now at an advanced stage, with R&R offered by a top-ranked peer-reviewed journal (acceptance rate standing at 8%) in January 2023 and re-submission scheduled in summer 2023. It is anticipated that the publication result of the other submission to a leading peer-reviewed journal in the field will become known in H2 2023.

14605218.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605218.value: Research outputs of the project include: • Five articles have been published or accepted for publication in leading/respectable peer-reviewed journals, all acknowledging support from the present project (see Part C, section 8). • Three journal articles are currently under review, one of which is presently at an advanced stage, with R&R offered by a top-ranked peer-reviewed journal (acceptance rate standing at 8%) in January 2023 and re-submission scheduled in summer 2023. It is anticipated that the publication results of the other two submissions to leading peer-reviewed journals will become known in H2 2023. • One chapter contribution has been accepted by the editors of an edited volume, which I understand is being actively considered by a top-rated academic publisher. • Five conference/seminar presentations have been delivered at international or regional academic events. In addition, one knowledge transfer event has been organised to disseminate the project’s research outcomes. The major findings of the project include: • Board-level governance reforms have been central and core to China’s corporate governance movements in the past two decades. The focus has been on enhancing board independence and accountability, particularly by assigning an increasingly wider range of governance roles to independent directors. A notable example is to place independent directions at the centre of policing transactions that are susceptible to majority-minority conflict (e.g. related-party transactions). • China’s board legal regime differs importantly from most other jurisdictions by imposing out-of-pocket (financial) liability on independent directors by way of securities enforcement actions, in addition to reputational sanctions. This finding helps to enrich the comparative discourse on director liability. • There is empirical evidence that observable (e.g. voting) and unobservable (e.g. behind-the-scenes dynamics) behaviour patterns of board members are sensitive to not only the nature of specific board resolutions, but also to a range of firm-level attributes (e.g. identity of the controlling shareholder) and institutional constraints (e.g. securities enforcement actions). This finding adds to the emerging strand of comparative legal scholarship on the role and workings of corporate boards. • There is no conclusive evidence that regulatory interventions aiming at curbing perceived directorial entrenchment (including such arrangements as staggered board) helped to enhance shareholder wealth, a finding that challenges received wisdom in the legal scholarship.

14605218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605218.value: The project’s findings help to lay a strong foundation for a teamwork-based comparative study on corporate board legal reforms around the world, potentially leading to a research handbook or edited volume on the topic. I plan to draw on my earlier editorial experience (as a co-editor of the Cambridge Handbook of Shareholder Engagement and Voting, Cambridge University Press, 2022) and to explore the scope of such an international collaborative project.

14605218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605218.value: Corporate boards play a central role in the governance of public companies. The board takes important decisions on such matters as the undertaking of major projects and the hiring of senior executives. It also controls and monitors, so as to align managerial interests more closely with shareholder (and stakeholder) interests. In the past two decades, a string of corporate scandals has thrust the board into the very centre of corporate governance reforms in China and worldwide. Although the comparative literature on the changing board characteristics has been rapidly expanding, the role and workings of Chinese corporate boards remain seriously understudied and under-theorised. The present project helps to fill this important lacuna. It has investigated both types of board – the board of directors and the supervisory board – used in China’s management-supervisory dual-board structure. Drawing on two unique, hand-collected datasets on the dual-boards of Chinese listed firms, as well as qualitative data gleaned from interviews, this project has presented new insights into the role and workings of corporate boards in mainland Chinese listed firms. Overall, the project helps to enhance significantly our understanding of corporate governance reforms both in mainland China and more generally.

14606318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606318.value: 本研究紮根並旨於貢獻於三大研究領域： 人口遷移與同化、人口遷移與性，以及男女同性戀外藉人士。本研究採用混合式研究，了解男女同性戀商業人士，由承認同性關係的地方，遷移到將同性性行為列為刑事罪行的地方（俄羅斯、印度和新加坡），和遷移到對基於性傾向歧視缺乏法律保障的地方 （香港）的經驗。 本研究提出以下的問題： 在全球同性戀權益不斷發展，但發展程度不相等的時代下，男女同性戀的外藉商業人士如何與當地社會互動？ 當他們由一個對同性戀權益較多保障的地方遷移到較少保障的地方（甚至去到極端的情況，同性性行為刑事化），他們是會隱藏自己的身份、保持沉默，繼而與當地社會文化進行「同化」，還是他們會參與當地的社會運動，進行政策倡導，甚至開展新的社會運動，去爭取自己的權益？ 理論層面的有趣問題是： 有甚麼因素影響男女同性戀專業人士評估「當地文化」？ 他們如何評估不同機遇和代價？ 短暫居留和長期居住如何影響他們的評估？甚麼的文化接觸會影響他們的決定？ 他們的決定（隱藏、保持沉默、爭取自己權益）是如何被看待？特別的是，當他們爭取自己的權益時，當地的男女同性戀團體是如何看待他們的參與？ 當地團體會樂於得到他們的幫忙，還是會抱著不歡迎的態度，甚至認為他們為「外國勢力」，過於政治敏感而需要避免？ 本研究旨在回應最基本的「結構」與「能動性」的問題，當男女同性戀者遷移時，他們會「接受」還是「挑戰」當地的社會？ 這引申到以下問題，當商業人士（其中包括男女同性戀者）在全球遷移情況增加時，他們會帶來多大程度的文化和社會改變？ 這研究不只是為理論層面作出貢獻，亦會帶來重要的實際及政策應用。全球商業世界越來越重視多元和接納，特別關注男女同性戀、雙性戀和跨性別議題。這研究會為跨國企業的管理層和人力資源部門作出參考。首席研究員已經與不同商業機構建立了連繫，可以一同合作推動社會改變。 混合式研究包括： 1) 與居於海外的男女同性戀商業人士進行網上問卷調查 (目標數目為1000人) 2) 網上問卷調查的結果會為之後進行的深入訪談建立基礎： 會與由承認同性關係的地方，遷移到將同性性行為列為刑事罪行的地方和和遷移到對基於性傾向的歧視缺乏法律保障的地方的男女同性戀商業人士進行深入訪談 （目標人數為60人）

14606518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606518.value: We move our hands spontaneously when speaking. Such hand movements are gestures. Intransitive gesture is crucial for communication and social interaction(e.g., HANDS-CLAPPING for awesome). Early studies by others and the PI have found delay in development of intransitive gesture in young and school-aged children with Autism Spectrum Disorders(ASD). Thus, intervention is needed to promote gestural communication skills in children with ASD. However, these children have difficulty in imitating gestures produced by humans as they prefer attending to objects to human beings. The PI pioneered the use of social robots in teaching Chinese-speaking school-aged children with low-functioning ASD (IQs<70) gesture use (So et al., 2016b; 2017). Her results reported that children recognized and imitated more gestures as well as producing them in appropriate social contexts after training (2016b). However, it is not clear whether robots are more effective than humans in teaching children with ASD gesture use. In the present study, we aim to 1) compare the effectiveness of a robot-based intervention(RBI) to that of a human-based intervention program(HBI) on gestural learning; 2) investigate whether the beneficial effect of RBI on gestural learning is moderated by children’s cognitive and social skills; 3) examine whether RBI, in comparison to HBI, would yield long-lasting learning effect and help children with low-functioning ASD to generalize the acquired skills to novel contexts. Fourteen sets of conversations are created, with each containing one gesture. We recruit 150 six- to twelve-year-old Cantonese-speaking children with low-functioning ASD. Children are randomly assigned to three conditions: two intervention conditions (RBI, HBI), and a care-as-usual condition, with fifty children in each condition. Both intervention conditions will last for twelve weeks and teach children the meanings of the gestures used in the specific conversations. Children’s learning outcomes will be measured by immediate and one follow-up standardized tests and their ability to generalize acquired gestural skills to novel contexts. We hypothesize that RBI is more effective than HBI in helping children with low-functioning ASD to acquire gestural communication skills. The beneficial effect of RBI may be more salient for children especially for those with weak attention abilities and communication and social interaction skills. Children in the RBI condition are also able to transfer the acquired gestural skills to novel contexts. Moreover, the beneficial learning outcome of RBI is still evident in the second posttest. Our results provide recommendation for therapists in applying RBI to foster the social and communicative skills of children with ASD. 我們說話時會自發地活動雙手。這些手部動作就是手勢。不及物手勢（Intransitive gesture）對於溝通和社交互動至關重要（例如拍手代表「很好」）。主要研究者及其團隊的早期研究發現，患有自閉症譜系障礙（Autism Spectrum Disorders, ASD）的幼兒和學齡兒童，其不及物手勢的發展較為遲緩。因此，自閉症兒童有需要接受干預治療以促進他們的手勢溝通技巧。然而，這些孩子難以模仿人類產生的手勢，因為他們更喜歡專注於物件多於人類。 主要研究者率先使用社交機械人，向患有低功能自閉症並說廣東話的學齡兒童（智商低於70）教導手勢的運用（蘇及其他，2016b; 2017）。 她的研究結果表明，兒童在訓練後能辨認及模仿更多的手勢，以及能在適當的社交環境中運用這些手勢（2016b）。 然而，目前尚不清楚機械人在教導自閉症兒童使用手勢方面是否比人類更為有效。 在本研究中，我們的目標是1）比較基於機械人的（robot-based intervention , RBI）與基於人類的（human-based intervention , HBI）手勢學習干預計劃的有效性; 2）研究RBI對於手勢學習的有利影響是否受到兒童的認知和社交能力的調節; 3）調查與HBI相比，RBI是否會產生更持久的學習效果，並更能幫助患有低功能自閉症的兒童將獲得的技巧應用到新的情景中。 我們創作了14組對話，每組包含了一個手勢。 我們招募了150名六至十二歲的患有低功能自閉症並說廣東話的兒童。兒童被隨機分配到三個組別：兩個干預組別（RBI，HBI）和常規照顧組別。每個組別分別有50個兒童。這兩個干預組別將持續12週，並教導兒童在特定對話中使用的手勢的含義。兒童的學習成果將透過即時的和一個後續的標準化測試，及其將獲得的手勢技巧應用到新情景的能力來衡量。 我們預計RBI比HBI能更有效地幫助患有低功能自閉症的兒童習得手勢溝通技巧。RBI的有利影響可能對兒童更為顯著，特別是對於那些專注力、溝通和社交能力弱的兒童。 在RBI組別的兒童也能夠將獲得的手勢技巧應用到新的情境中。此外，RBI在第二次後測中的有利學習成果仍然顯著。 我們的研究結果將為治療師如何應用RBI，以促進自閉症兒童的社交和溝通提供建議。

14606518.label: Realisation of objectives
14606518.value: This project aimed to compare the learning effectivness of robot-based intervention to that of human-based intervention in improving social skills, with the focus on joint attention, autistic children. Given the pandemic from 2020 to 2022, the team had difficulties in data collection, which was conducted in a special school. The objectives were revised and achieved. 1) To compare effectiveness of robot-based intervention(RBI) to that of human-based intervention(HBI) on the gestures produced during joint attention among children with ASD and 3) To examine whether RBI, in comparison to HBI, would yield long-lasting learning effect and transferability to novel contexts. Two studies were conducted and published. Study 1 examined the learning effectiveness of RBI in joint attention. We designed a robot drama intervention for promoting responses to joint attention abilities (RJA) of children with low-functioning autism (IQs <70). Using a stepped wedge design, Chinese-speaking children aged six to eight were randomly assigned to three tiers. Children of all three tiers had comparable autism severity, language and cognitive function, and joint attention abilities. Tier 1 first received intervention, followed by Tiers 2 and 3. They watched six dramas in which social robots demonstrated RJA behaviours. The RJA of children of all tiers improved after intervention and such improvement was maintained over time. Despite initiation of joint attention (IJA) not being explicitly taught, IJA of all children was found to improve after intervention. It was, therefore, concluded that a robot drama could enhance the joint attention of children with low-functioning ASD. Based on the findings of Study 1, Study 2 further compared the learning effectiveness of RBI to that of HBI. Chinese-speaking children with autism aged 6 to 9 years were randomly assigned to RBI and HBI groups. Before intervention, their autism severity, cognitive abilities, and language skills were assessed. Each child received six 30-minute training sessions over three weeks. During training, he/she watched one or two robot/human dramas twice where two robot/human actors demonstrated eye contact and RJA. Children in the RBI (but not HBI) group produced more RJA and IJA behaviors in the delayed post-test than in the pre-test. Parents of the RBI children rated the program more positively than those of the HBI children. Implications: RBI may be more effective than HBI in promoting JA in autistic children with high support needs. 2) To illustrate the moderating effects of individual differences in cognitive and social skills on learning gestures produced during joint attention in RBI. Study 1 and Study 2 assessed the participating children's autism severity, cognitive abilities, and language skills, did not find any significant effects of cognitive and social skills in affecting joint attention learning

14606518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606518.value: Study 1: The responses to joint attention of children with low- functioning autism improved after taking six robot drama lessons at staggered time points. What was more promising was that their positive learning outcomes were maintained for approximately 1–2 months. Besides, their number of RJA behaviours in the delayed post-tests was comparable to those who had just received training. In addition to RJA, the IJA ability of all children was enhanced after intervention despite IJA not being explicitly taught. As was the case with RJA, the improvement of IJA was maintained over time. So, W.C., Cheng, C.H., Law, W.W., Wong, T., Lee, C., Kwok, F.Y., Lee, S.H., Lam, K.Y. (2023). Robot dramas may improve joint attention of Chinese-speaking low-functioning children with autism: Stepped wedge trials. Disabilities and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, 18:2, 195-204 Study 2: During training, children in the robot-based intervention required fewer prompts than their peers in the human-based intervention. After taking six drama lessons, children in the robot-based intervention produced more RJA behaviors in the delayed post-test than in the pre-test. They were also found to have an increase in IJA behaviors in the immediate post-test compared to the pre-test despite IJA not having been explicitly taught. More promisingly, their increase was maintained in the delayed post-test. However, those improvements were not evident in the children taking human-based drama lessons. These findings were in line with parents’ ratings of both kinds of intervention. Parents of the children receiving the robot-based intervention rated the program more positively than those of the children receiving the human-based intervention, suggesting that the positive learning outcomes of the robot-based interventions could be generalized to human-to-human interactions. So, W.C., Law, W.W., Cheng C.H., Lee C., Ng K.C., Kwok F.Y., Lam H.W., & Lam, K.Y. (accepted). Comparing the effectiveness of robot-based to human-based intervention in improving joint attention in children with autism. Frontiers in Psychiatry - Autism.

14606518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606518.value: The intervention protocols established in Study 1 and Study 2 could be integrated to the current therapies for autistic children. The PI is delivering robot-based intervention to autistic children aged 3 to 18. She plans to include the intervention on joint attention to her established program.

14606518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606518.value: Children with autism have impairments in the initiation of joint attention (IJA) and response to joint attention (RJA). Social robots are widely used in autism therapy. Previous studies have examined whether social robots could improve joint attention (JA) but have reported mix findings. Our project found that robot dramas promote JA in autistic children with high support needs. Robot dramas are also more effective than human dramas in promoting JA. Autistic children in the robot drama group generalize their acquired JA to daily life. Since robot dramas can facilitate the development of JA skills in autistic children with high support needs, practitioners or therapists may implement robot dramas in this domain and design and test whether robot dramas can enhance other domains of social communication skills
