14616418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14616418.value: Accumulating evidence suggests that the brain is a prediction machine that predicts sensory input in a top-down manner across different levels of the perceptual hierarchy. A recent model of visual object recognition proposes that such predictions are generated based on stimulus information that is quickly available through fast magnocellular projections. Despite similarities between objects and visual words, this model has yet to be extended to reading. The current project intends to lay the groundwork for this extension. We plan to use Chinese characters to test whether magnocellular information (information biasing the magnocellular pathway), but not parvocellular information, leads to neural facilitation in subsequent processing of the same character. In Aim 1, we present magnocellular information as a preview to the parafoveal region of the visual field and measure neural facilitation in fixation-related potentials using combined EEG/eye-tracking. In Aim 2, we present magnocellular information to the fovea and measure neural facilitation in event-related potentials of the EEG with masked priming. In both cases, we expect to see neural facilitation in the form of a reduced late N1/N250 component along with behavioral facilitation after a same-character preview/prime in the magnocellular, but not parvocellular conditions. EEG is the method of choice in Aims 1/2, because preview benefits and masked priming effects have been most robustly detected with EEG. In Aim 3, we plan to test which brain regions underlie neural facilitation and the pattern of connectivity between them. To this end, we will adapt the experiments from Aims 1/2 for use with fast optical imaging (EROS) and lagged correlation path modelling. We expect to find early frontal and parietal activation and early frontal/parietal-to-occipitotemporal modulation in the magnocellular, but not parvocellular conditions. The rationale for the proposed research is that it is expected to provide evidence for the use of fast magnocellular information in reading in agreement with a predictive coding model. The proposed research is innovative, as it extends an influential model from object recognition to reading and tests it with advanced neuroimaging techniques (simultaneous EEG/eye-tracking, EEG with masked priming, EROS). The proposed research is significant as it is expected to challenge bottom-up theories of reading and extend interactive accounts by linking them to basic physiological properties of the visual system. Such a model, embedded in the powerful theoretical and statistical framework of predictive coding, is likely to strongly influence our future understanding of reading development, cross-linguistic differences in reading, and developmental dyslexia. 近年有很多證據顯示腦袋是一個預測的機器，它能以由上而下的方式，跨越不同的感知階層，來預測感官的輸入，根據近年一個有關視覺物件辨認的模型，這些預測是透過快速巨細胞(magnocellular)投射來快速地獲取物件資訊而產生。雖然物件與視覺上的文字有相似性，但此模型並未曾廷伸至閱讀層面，而這研究計劃將作為此廷伸的基礎。我們打算利用中文單字來測試巨細胞資訊（傾向巨細胞路徑的資訊），而非小細胞(parvocellular)資訊，能否在隨後同一單字的運作過程中，導致神經元激發(neural facilitation) 。在目標一，我們會向視野周邊區域展示巨細胞資訊作預視，以及使用腦電技術(EEG)和眼球追蹤(eye-tracking)來量度在定視相關電位(fixation-related potentials)的神經元激發。 在目標二，我們向中央凹(fovea)展示巨細胞資訊，以及使用腦電技術和隱閉促發(masked priming)來量度在事件相關電位(event-related potentials)的神經元激發。在兩個目標中，我們都期望可看到以減弱而且廷遲的N1/N250 腦電成分形式出現的神經元激發，以及在巨細胞，而非小細胞的情況下，可看到同一單字的預視或促發後的行為刺激。腦電技術被採用為達成目標一和二的方法，是因為它能強烈偵測預視優勢(preview benefits)和隱閉促發的影響。至於目標三，我們打算檢測作為神經元激發基礎的腦部區域以及它們的關聯模式。為了達到此目的，我們將採用目標一和二的實驗，並結合快速光學成像(fast optical imaging)（事件相關光學信息(EROS)）和滯後相關路徑模型 (lagged correlation path modelling)，我們期望在巨細胞而非小細胞情況中找到早期額葉和頂葉的激發和早期額葉和頂葉至枕顳區的調制。有關是次研究的原理，我們期望找到在閱讀時使用快速巨細胞資訊的證據，並符合預測編碼模型(predictive coding model)。是次研究是創新的，因為它把一個有影響力的模型從物件辨認延伸至閱讀，並以先進的神經成像技術（同時進行的腦電技術與眼球追蹤、腦電技術與隱閉促發、事件相關光學信息）作檢測。是次研究是有意義的，因為我們期望透過此研究挑戰由下而上的閱讀理論，並透過與視覺系統的基本生理特性連繫而廷伸交互的理論。這個具強大理論和統計學基礎的預測編碼模型，很有可能將會深遠地影響我們將來對閱讀發展、閱讀的跨語言相異之處，以及發展性的讀寫障礙的理解。

14616418.label: Realisation of objectives
14616418.value: Objective 2 was the first one that was completed. As planned, the objective was tested with two experiments that manipulated magnocelluar and parvocellular sensitivity of the stimuli in different ways (experiment 1: low vs. high spatial frequency; experiment 2: luminance vs. isoluminant color contrasts). The paper containing the results of this objective has been published last year. Objective 1 was completed after Objective 2, as pursuing this objective required the development of the lab infrastructure to conduct concurrent EEG – eye-tracking experiments. We achieved this technological development through the input of Dr. Dimigen who visited our lab in Hong Kong and helped us run and interpret the necessary timing tests and making adjustments in the setup and experiment program. These timing tests were critical to ensure that the boundary paradigm was working properly and that previews only occurred in the parafoveal region, but never in the fovea. Finally, the objective was tested as planned with 2 experiments that used the same manipulation of magnocellular vs. parvocellular sensitivity, as described for Objective 2. The manuscript containing the results of this objective is in an advanced stage of preparation and is going to be submitted within a few weeks. The period during which this project was conducted was also the period of the social unrest in Hong Kong and the subsequent pandemic. These events affected the progress of the project and lead to substantial delays, which were accounted for by extensions of the project duration. In addition, Objective 3 was originally planned to be conducted by the application of the fNIRS technique at our Department. Unfortunately, the Co-investigator with fNIRS expertise left the Department, and conducting an experiment with his remote expertise turned out to be difficult. At the same time, CUHK opened a new MR center that offered the opportunity to address Objective 3 with a spatially more accurate technique. We therefore submitted a project revision to change the technique for Objective 3 from fNIRS to fMRI. After we had obtained approval, we collected data that was completed in August 2022. A new PhD student in my lab has now analysed the data, and after some more checking of the results, we are going to write up the results. When working on the objectives of the project, we realized that it would be interesting to compare the basic effects of the techniques used in Objectives 1 and 2. We therefore conducted an additional study as part of a pilot study. The results of that study are written up as a manuscript that is also in an advanced stage of preparation and should be submitted within a few weeks.

14616418.label: Major findings and research outcome
14616418.value: An important aspect of this project was to establish concurrent EEG – eye-tracking data collection and analysis, as this was necessary for Objective 2. We were very successful in doing so. We used the boundary paradigm in 4 experiments now (3 as part of this grant), and found very consistent facilitation effects during the late N1/N250 component of the fixation-related potentials (FRP). These effects could also be found in the masked repetition experiment. And we corroborated the similarity of the preview benefits effects and the masked priming effects in an additional experiment. Aside from these technical aspects, the project was written to test a model according to which the magnocellular system is critically involved in reading by providing fast “gist” information about upcoming stimuli that can facilitate subsequent processing. The results of the studies in Objectives 1 and 2 were clear by showing that the preview benefit and masked priming effects were not mediated by magnocellular information. The absence of such an effect was consistent across both types of manipulations of the magnocellular vs. parvocellular sensitivity, and across both the masked priming and the preview benefit manipulation. Given the absence of this effect, we focused on a repetition and expectation manipulation in the fMRI experiment to test assumptions of predictive processing in reading. Preliminary results suggest that expectation effects differ from repetition effects regarding the direction and location in the brain suggesting that repetition effects cannot be explained by expectations based on previous stimuli.

14616418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14616418.value: The research project helped us to establish a new technique in the lab (concurrent EEG – eye-tracking recordings). This technique turned out to work very well, and could already be used in another project. The technique is promising and can be used in additional projects in the future that require EEG recordings in the context of natural eye movements. Although the original idea of an involvement of the magnocellular system was fascinating, such a model was clearly not supported. It still seems plausible that visual properties of upcoming stimuli in the parafovea may bias subsequent processing. Future studies may look at other visual aspects, such as outlines rather than along the magnocellular vs. parvocellular division.

14616418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14616418.value: The human visual system consists of a magnocellular system that is fast, but contains poor spatial information, and of a parvocellular system that is slower, but contains detailed information. The current study tested the idea that the magnocellular system is involved in reading by providing the brain with rough “gist” information about upcoming words that makes processing of these words more efficient. We tested this idea by providing words as masked (invisible) primes in the center of the visual field, or as previews in the parafoveal area slightly to the right of the fixation in the center. We combined EEG with eye-tracking to measure the brain processes involved in visual word processing and to measure facilitation effects. While we could consistently measure facilitation in visual word processing between about 200 and 300 ms in both the masked priming and parafoveal preview experiments, we could not find any evidence that the magnocellular system plays a special role for this facilitation effect. This suggests that the magnocellular system does not uniquely mediate facilitation effects in reading, such as those underlying preview benefits in reading. The technique of concurrent EEG – eye-tracking recording that was developed for this study is useful to study brain processes involved in natural reading in future studies.

14617418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617418.value: Abstract In the last 15 years, overseas study has become more accessible to many Chinese students of architecture. These students were mostly born in the 1980s, and now, with newly completed architectural projects to their names, some have been recognized as “emerging architects.” In common with many of their generation, their careers started with projects in small towns and villages because major cities such as Beijing and Shanghai are already well served by many established architectural companies and design institutes. When architectural journals limit the presentation of complex buildings to 6 to 8 pages, much of the special circumstances of smaller and unfamiliar locales, and significant aspects of innovative work remain hidden. The link between architectural fame and the understanding of architectural merit becomes loosened, to the detriment of the discipline of architecture. Central to this problem is the role of architectural images. Can proper interest in the work of emerging Chinese architects be invigorated by renewed thinking about their architectural plans and photographs? This research project will focus on two emerging Chinese architects, Natural Build (in Shanghai) and Zhao Yang Architects (in Dali, Yunnan Province). The sketchy and open-ended nature of clients’ briefs, the topographical settings of the sites, the fluid condition of rural areas in development, local expectations on aesthetic treatment of new buildings, construction teams with informal training, the increasing homogeneity of the supply chain for building materials—when these aspects are occluded in brief presentations of new projects, it becomes difficult to understand how great outcomes are achieved in challenging circumstances. Can the innovative of merit these architects be understood in terms of a shift from self-centred professional imagination to a dialogic and purposeful improvisation? Using detailed interviews to probe large archives of images for what they demonstrate as well as imply, this research will attempt to show how architectural plans and photographs be read in multiple ways to articulate challenging circumstances and innovative design thinking in these architects’ work. This will be the first study of Chinese architects that goes beyond conventional narratives that presents architectural design in terms of the correspondence of concept, intuition and outcomes. It will offer new readings showing how challenging conditions of design projects can shake up preconceptions and lead to unexpected and innovative outcomes. This will invigorate our understanding of architectural innovation and offer new materials for comparative studies of contemporary architecture. 最近15年來，中國建築學生在國外留學並歸國的人數漸增。這些學生大部分出生於20世紀80年代，其中有些人已有建成作品並成為 “新銳建築師” 了。這一代建築師的初期項目往往是在小城鎮裡的，因為像北京、上海等大城市的建築市場幾乎已被眾多經驗豐富的建築事務所和設計院所佔據。當下中國建築期刊介紹新建築的篇幅一般為6-8頁，這通常使得小城鎮相對獨特但少為人知的情況以及新銳建築師的創新性貢獻沒有得到充分的展示。因此，建築名望與建築成就的關聯就變得鬆散了；這對建築學科而言，不無遺憾。此中，建築圖像的角色是至關重要的。我們能否重新思考建築圖紙和照片，從而深化對中國新銳建築師作品的理解呢？ 本研究將關注兩個中國新銳建築事務所：上海直造建築事務所以及雲南大理的趙揚建築工作室。在過於簡短的項目說明中，眾多因素被省略——甲方提供的籠統而多變的任務書、多樣的場地地貌特征、鄉下開發的各種變數、當地對新建築的唯美願景、非專業的施工團隊、建材供應鏈的單一化——這讓讀者很難明白高質量的建築成果是如何在艱難的情況下取得的。我們能否把注意力從建築師自我為主的專業想象轉到有意識的、對話式的即興創作，從而為這些建築作品的成就謀求一種新的理解呢？ 本研究計劃利用詳細的採訪來挖掘大量圖檔，並探討圖檔直接呈現的以及暗含的意向與見解，企圖從多種角度解讀建築圖紙和照片，突顯建築師工作中的各種具體挑戰與創新性的設計思維。 在中國建築師的相关研究中，本研究是首次摒棄一般建築設計研究中建築概念、直覺與結果三者之間的簡單等同的。本研究將發展一系列新的解讀，並說明設計項目中挑戰性的條件如何能動搖各種先入為主的見解並引發意料之外的、創新性的結果。最后，本研究計劃希望更新我們對建築創新的理解，並為當代建築學的比較研究提供新的材料。

14618118.label: Realisation of objectives
14618118.value: 1. This first objective has been perfectly realized in the project. As revealed in the results of the project, students' profile of motivation and engagement demonstrated that there was a notable decrease in the scores from adaptive to maladaptive factors of students' cognitive, emotional, and behavioral engagement, echoing the characteristics of engaged learners suggested by researcher in general. Meanwhile, there were significant differences in student engagement between groups with various demographic characteristics and types of learners. For example, students at research-oriented universities scored significantly higher than their counterparts at teaching-oriented universities. Male students scored significantly lower on adaptive motivation and adaptive engagement, but significantly higher on maladaptive motivation and maladaptive engagement (e.g., Yin, 2022). 2. This second objective has been perfectly achieved in the project. As revealed in the research outcomes of the project, there were various types learners who had distinctive characteristics in terms of their motivation and engagement (e.g., Tian et al., 2021; Yin, 2022). In addition, our results showed that students who engaged more in face-to-face synchronous interactions yielded greater positive effects on student learning and had significant gains on all the constructs of academic learning outcomes and development. As for students' perceived learning environments, face-to-face synchronous interactions were supportive to increase the level of teacher academic assistance. Moreover, it contributed to shaping an interpersonally connected and cognitively aroused environment in terms of teacher affective support, peer collaboration, students' feeling of belonging, and teachers emphasizing creativity. It was also positively associated with both the academic and nonacademic outcomes. In contrast, the engagement in online asynchronous interactions were more helpful for motivating students cognitively, as indicated by its relationship with teachers' academic assistance and emphasizing creativity. However, it had a minimum or even no effect on the social aspects of the learning environment (Yin & Shi, 2022). 3. The third objective has been perfectly fulfilled in the project. The results of the project revealed that personal, classroom, and institutional factors played significant roles in influencing student motivation and engagement in mathematics. For personal factors, the results showed that students' perceptions of the difficulty of learning mathematics promoted their fragmented conceptions of mathematics, while at the same time demotivating their cohesive conceptions, academic efficacy as well as mathematics grade (Yin et al., 2020). Moreover, gender was significantly related to students' motivation, engagement, and satisfaction with their learning. For example, male students scored significantly lower on adaptive motivation and adaptive engagement, but significantly higher on maladaptive motivation and maladaptive engagement (Yin 2022). Meanwhile, female students were more satisfied with their online learning experiences during the COVID-19 (Yin et al., 2022). Classroom environments were significantly related to students' beliefs of mathematics learning and mathematics achievement. As indicated in the results of the project, students' perceptions of the classroom environments characterized by teacher support, student autonomy, cooperation among students, and classroom discipline positively predicted their cohesive conceptions of mathematics and academic efficacy in mathematics, and were weakly associated with their fragmented conceptions of mathematics. Furthermore, the results displayed significant positive mediation effects on paths from students' perceptions of classroom environments to their mathematics achievement via academic efficacy and via both cohesive conceptions and academic efficacy (Yin et al., 2020). Institutional factors played different roles in influencing students' perceptions of learning environments at the programme level and student engagement at the individual level. On the one hand, university type (teaching- or research-oriented universities) was not significantly related to students' perceptions of programme-level learning environments, but students in research-oriented universities were more satisfied with their learning experiences during the COVID-19 (Yin et al., 2022). On the other hand, under the context of online learning during the COVID-19, the advantage of students from research-oriented universities disappeared. There was no significant main difference between students from research and teaching-oriented universities on adaptive motivation, adaptive engagement or maladaptive motivation. Moreover, students from research-oriented universities scored higher than those from teaching-oriented universities on maladaptive engagement (Yin, 2022). In addition, teachers' perceived characteristics of the university environments, such as job demands and resources, stress from organizational inadequacy and new challenges of technologies, were significantly associated with self-efficacy to teach, which further influenced their commitment and well-being (Han et al., 2020; Huang et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2020; Yin et al., 2020). 4. For the fourth objective, influence by the COVID-19 pandemic, all universities in China changed to online teaching in early February 2020. This sudden and dramatic change of learning mode brought tremendous challenges to the project which strived for a longitudinal study on student engagement in mathematics learning. However, we overcome the difficulties through various means and collected data at different time points and situations to address this objective. The fourth objective has been satisfactorily realized in the project. Our results indicated that university students' prior experiences of mathematics learning during their secondary education had a prolonged impact on their engagement in university mathematics learning. Emotions and affects played important roles in different stages of mathematics problem solving consisting of understanding, planning, enacting, and evaluating (Fu & Yin, 2021; Lin et al., 2020), which highlights the significance to comprehensively cultivate student engagement from multiple dimensions. Moreover, the changes of learning and teaching mode before and during the COVID-19made a difference in student engagement. The results showed that students from research-oriented universities were more engaged in face-to-face learning contexts than those from teaching-oriented universities. However, the advantage of students from research-oriented universities in terms of motivation and engagement disappeared during the COVID-19 due to the adoption of online learning. In addition, although in the online teaching mode, the number of 'adaptive learners' increased, the adoption of online teaching mode during the COVID-19 also led to a small group of 'extremely maladaptive learners' in university learning. (Yin, 2022) 5. The fifth objective has been perfectly fulfilled in the project. The cultural contexts in Chinasignificantly influenced these students' motivation, engagement, and achievement in mathematics learning. The unique features of Chinese mathematics classrooms have led to various debates. As indicated by our results, mathematics classrooms in Chinese universities feature high teacher support and frequent teacher-student and student-student interactions, Chinese students, in some sense, tend to be obedient and appear to be passive learners, which is quite consistent with the 'Chinese learners' paradox' (Lin et al., 2020; Yin et al., 2020). Our research outcomes tend to suggest that the Chinese cultural model of learning —haoxuexin, referring to 'the heart and mind for wanting to learn' — learning is a lifelong process of self-perfection for Chinese students, which requires them to study hard regardless of obstacles. In the Chinese haoxuexin ideal, poor learning is associated with some painful, depressing experiences, but these negative emotions do not necessarily lead to a retreat from learning. Instead, a desire to learn in order to make up for one's inadequacies usually comes from the negative affect, and the focus is 'on the positive course of action under way' after the negative affect. In view of this cultural model of learning, the underlying cultural beliefs held by Chinese university students may account for the characteristics of their motivation and engagement in learning (Yin, 2020).

14618118.label: Major findings and research outcome
14618118.value: 1. Students' perceptions of mathematics classroom environment were associated with both affective and cognitive mathematics outcomes, which was mediated by students' mathematics beliefs consisting of conceptions of mathematics and academic efficacy in mathematics learning. Specifically, a desirable classroom environment was related to students' cohesive conceptions, enhanced self-efficacy, and higher mathematics achievement. In contrast, students' perceived difficulty of learning mathematics was connected to their fragmented conceptions, reduced self-efficacy and lower mathematics achievement (Yin, Shi, Tam, & Lu, 2020). 2. Student engagement in two types of interactions (face-to-face vs. online) had different effects on their learning and development. The face-to-face synchronous interaction generated more desirable academic learning, perceptions of the learning environment, and higher satisfaction than the online asynchronous interaction in most aspects. However, the asynchronous online interaction fostered student autonomy and contributed to students' completion of an in-depth thesis (Yin & Shi, 2022). 3. University students varied in their types of motivation and engagement in different learning contexts. Before the COVID-19, there were four types of learners among these students: ‘active interactors’, ‘realistic interactors’, ‘digital interactors’, and ‘passive interactor’ (Yin & Shi, 2022). In contrast, another four types of learners emerged in the context of online learning during the COVID-19: ‘adaptive learners’, ‘engaged but maladaptive learners’, ‘moderately maladaptive learners’, and ‘extremely maladaptive learners’ (Yin, 2022). For international students studying in Chinese universities, three types of learners (i.e., actively engaged, insufficiently engaged, and passively engaged) were differentiated (Tian, Lu, Li, & Yin, 2021). 4. Institutional and cultural contexts influenced student engagement. Specifically, students in research-oriented universities held a more favorable views of their efficacy in completing academic tasks (Yin, Lu, & Meng, 2022). Although students from research-oriented universities performed better in motivation engagement, this advantage disappeared in online learning during the COVID-19 (Yin, 2022). In addition, the underlying cultural beliefs held by Chinese students may account for the characteristics of their motivation and engagement in mathematics learning (Yin, 2020, 2021; Yin, Shi, Tam, & Lu, 2020). 5. Teacher matters in students' mathematics learning. Teachers’ perceived stress from organizational inadequacy and new challenges were negatively associated with self-efficacy (Yin, Han, & Perron, 2020). Teachers' self-efficacy mediated the effect of challenge job demands and job resources on work engagement (Han, Yin, Wang, & Bai, 2020). Teachers' technological pedagogical content knowledge contributed to their satisfaction with teaching experiences, which was moderated by faculty members’ work engagement and mediated by their self-efficacy (Huang, Yin, Jin, & Wang, 2022).

14618118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14618118.value: The project elicits two directions worthy of further research in future: First, our project focuses on student engagement in mathematics learning in universities in mainland China. The findings have endorsed the importance of contextual factor at different levels such as classroom, institution, and sociocultural traditions. Considering the similarities (the dominant proportion of Chinese students, the importance attached to education, and students' outstanding performance in mathematics in schools) and difference between mainland China universities and those in Hong Kong, for example, different teaching languages at the classroom level, different management styles at the institution level, and the fusion of East and West academic traditions in Hong Kong, some comparative research on student engagement in mainland China versus Hong Kong universities will be meaningful and insightful. Second, the COVID-19 pandemic heavily influenced the implementation of this longitudinal study, which made the trace of participants and comparison between individual students difficult. However, it also brought some new ideas in deepening this research topic. Future research on student engagement in mathematics or other disciplines are advised to take into consideration the adoption of educational technologies such as hybrid learning and virtual reality, because our findings have revealed that student engagement in different learning contexts varied.

14618118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14618118.value: To reveal the complexities of student engagement in university learning, the project examined university student engagement in mathematics learning and its transformation from multiple angles, including behavioral, psychological and socio-cultural perspectives. The findings revealed different types of learners who had distinctive characteristics in terms of their motivation and engagement. Students' variation in their motivation and engagement further influenced their cognitive and affective mathematics achievement. Meanwhile, the contextual factors at the classroom, institutional, and sociocultural levels were closed related to university students' engagement in and approaches to mathematics learning which were subject to the changes in the learning contexts and educational stages. This is one of the first group of attempts to investigate university student engagement from multiple perspectives. The findings are meaningful for the development of theoretical understandings of student engagement research and the improvement of mathematics learning in university teaching. Theoretically, the project endorses the importance for adopt a comprehensive, situational, and dynamic perspective of student engagement. Practically, the findings of the project highlight the significance of creating a supportive classroom environment, enhancing teachers? self-efficacy and desirable conceptions of mathematics, and promoting beneficial faculty-student interaction and Chinese cultural beliefs in motivating and sustaining university student engagement in mathematics learning.

14618618.label: Realisation of objectives
14618618.value: All project objectives have been achieved. We have developed three research papers to address these objectives and presented the research findings at regional and international conferences. One of the research papers has been revised and resubmitted to a high-ranking international journal. The project has trained one PhD student. Below we detail how the objectives were addressed. 1. Describe the distribution of individuals’ subjective power positions in 30 countries with diverse configurations of political and social institutions We worked with the Gallup World Poll to field two items on perceive power and wealth status in 30 societies with diverse political and social institutions in 2019/20. Because of unexpected circumstances, data collection was not completed in the Czech Republic, and when this happened, it was too late to replace the Czech Republic with a similar country. We therefore received data from 29 countries, totaling around 32,000 observations. We then created the analytical dataset by merging the survey data with macro-level variables measuring political and social institutions. The analytical dataset is used in analyses that fulfill the objectives of this project. We assessed the distribution of individuals’ subjective power positions and found that first, on average, people’s subjective power status is much lower than their subjective wealth status, similar to what we found in a previous study done in China. Second, we identified a significant amount of variation in people’s perceived power status in different societies. For example, whereas 81% of the respondents in Zimbabwe placed themselves on the lowest rungs of the power hierarchy (levels 1-3), only 38% did so in Germany. These descriptive findings have been included in all three manuscripts developed for this project. 2. Examine the relationship between features of the political system and individuals’ subjective power positions We conducted extensive analyses examining the relationship between features of the political system and individuals’ subjective power positions. We identified two broad features of political institutions that are significant predictors of people’s perceived power status, i.e. the rule of law and democracy. In general, individuals living in societies with more functional democratic and legal institutions were more likely to report higher positions in the power hierarchy. These findings were reported in two manuscripts, the focuses of which are on the relationships between power status and psychological well-being across different societies. The two manuscripts are described in more details under objective three. 3. Investigate the relationship between power perception and physical and psychological well-being and assess the extent to which people’s power perception mediates the relationship between the political system and well-being Two manuscripts have been developed to address this objective. The first examined the link between power perception and well-being and showed that people who placed themselves higher in the power hierarchy tended to report greater well-being. Moreover, it showed that an important feature of the institutional context, i.e. the rule of law, fosters greater political power. Furthermore, it also revealed that the rule of law moderate the link between power perception and well-being; well-defined, universally applicable, and fair laws reduce the power position’s effect on well-being. Taken together, this paper showed that the rule of law influences individual well-being through its effects on people’s power perception; it also ameliorate the effects of power perception on well-being. The findings have been presented at both regional and national workshops and conferences. This paper was submitted to European Societies, which is the official journal of the European Sociological Society and ranks in the top 25% in the JCR category of Sociology by impact factor, and received an invitation to revise and resubmit. We have recently resubmitted the paper. This paper was developed in collaboration with a PhD student at our department, for whom I served as a member of the thesis committee. The student has graduated and is now a Research Assistant Professor at Lingnan University. The second manuscript further extended the theme highlighted in the first paper, i.e. the role of the institutional context in shaping both the level and distribution of population health. As the COVID-19 pandemic ravaged the world, we have become interested in assessing the role of the institutional context during the pandemic. We hypothesizedthat during the pandemic, well-functioning institutions may ameliorate the harmful effects of the pandemic on individual well-being and mitigate the extent to which the pandemic exacerbate social inequalities in well-being. To investigate this hypothesis, we collaborated with the GWP to do another round of data collection in 2021/22, which was then combined with the data collected before the pandemic. Our analysis first showed that both people’s power status and wealth status are important predictors of well-being. Moreover, an indicator of institutional quality, the democracy index are positive associated with people’s evaluation of their power status, suggesting that the effects of democracy index on well-being is mediated by power perception. Finally, functioning democratic institutions may have mitigated the widening socioeconomic gaps in well-being during the pandemic. A manuscript has been developed based on these findings and we plan to submit it to an academic journal early next year. We have presented some of the findings at a local conference. The manuscript has been accepted for presentation at the annual meeting of the International Sociological Association, which will be held in June 2023 in Melbourne, Australia. Both manuscripts address this objective by illuminating the relationship between power perception and well-being and how power perception mediated the link between the institutional context and well-being. They also contributed to an “institutional turn” in the study of population health that emphasizes the role of the institutional context in shaping both the level and distribution of population health. 4. Study the effects of the discrepancies between subjective power and wealth positions on well-being We have developed a manuscript that examined the effects of the discrepancies between subjective power and wealth positions on well-being in different social contexts. In a previous paper, we found that although Chinese people perceived substantial gaps in their power and wealth status, the incongruence between power and wealth status matters little to their psychological well-being. Rather, individuals tend to emphasize the status dimension in which they enjoy advantages and discount the dimension in which they suffer detriments. In the current project, we extended the study and hypothesized that political institutions in a society may influence the relevance of the incongruence between power and wealth status and condition its consequences. We apply the diagonal mobility model to the cross-national data generated in the current project. We found that political institutions moderate the relationship between the incongruence and well-being. The incongruence is only detrimental to psychological well-being in hybrid democracies; it does not matter in authoritarian regimes or full democracies. It is conceivable that in hybrid democracies, the mismatch between expectations and realities of the political processes may be acutely felt and the gaps between power and wealth status are psychological relevant and consequential. This study is the first to provide rigorous empirical evidence on how macro institutions conditioned the relevance of status incongruence. This paper has been accepted for presentation at the Annual Conference of the American Sociological Association in August 2022. Because of the pandemic travel restrictions, we were not able to present the paper. We are now finalizing the manuscript and plan to submit it in a month.

14618618.label: Major findings and research outcome
14618618.value: The findings center on power perception and its well-being consequences. The first set of findings describes people’s power perception in 29 societies with diverse political and social institutions and reveals its institutional antecedents. Compared with positions in the wealth hierarchy, people tended to place them much lower in the power hierarchy. Moreover, there is a significant amount of variation in people’s perceived power status in different societies. We also identified two broad features of political institutions that are significant predictors of people’s perceived power status, i.e. the rule of law and democracy. In general, individuals living in societies with more functional democratic and legal institutions were more likely to report higher positions in the power hierarchy. The second set of findings illuminates the link between power perception and well-being and how the institutional context interacts with individual power and wealth status to influence well-being. We found that people who placed themselves higher in the power hierarchy tended to report greater well-being. Moreover, as people in societies with more functional legal and democratic institutions were more likely to reported greater power perception, our findings suggest that power perception mediates the relationship between the institutional context and well-being. Furthermore, well-functioning institutions ameliorates the effects of individuals’ access to power and wealth on well-being and reduces social disparities in well-being. More specifically, well-defined, universally applicable, and fair laws reduced the power position’s effect on well-being. In addition, functioning democratic institutions may have mitigated the widening socioeconomic gaps in well-being during the pandemic. Finally, we examined the effects of the incongruence between subjective power and wealth positions on well-being and found that political institutions moderate the relationship between the incongruence and well-being. The incongruence is only consequential to psychological well-being in hybrid democracies; it does not have well-being consequences in authoritarian regimes or full democracies. It is conceivable that in hybrid democracies, the mismatch between expectations and realities of the political processes may be acutely felt and the gaps between power and wealth status are psychological relevant and consequential. This study is the first to provide rigorous empirical evidence on how the well-being effects of status incongruence is conditioned by macro institutions. We have presented the research findings at regional and international conferences. Three papers have been developed based on the findings, one of which has been revised and resubmitted to a high-ranking international journal. This project also trained one PhD student.

14618618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14618618.value: As the COVID-19 pandemic has been ravaging the world, the findings of this project has led us to think about the role of institutions in influencing the level and distribution of population health and well-being during the pandemic. Socially disadvantaged groups are at greater risks to the devastating consequences of disasters. Higher-quality institutions may better at protecting their citizens, especially the vulnerable ones, from the harms of disasters. It is therefore conceivable that during the pandemic, well-functioning institutions may ameliorate the harmful effects of the pandemic on individual well-being and mitigate the extent to which the pandemic exacerbate social inequalities in well-being. To investigate this hypothesis, we did another round of data collection in 2021/22, which was then combined with the data collected before the pandemic, so as to investigate the pandemic effects and the role of the institutional context during the pandemic. Our analysis provides evidence that functioning democratic institutions may have mitigated the widening socioeconomic gaps in well-being during the pandemic. We will also investigate other features of the institutional context. We will aim to collect data after the pandemic so as to assess the role of the institutional context throughout the pandemic.

14618618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14618618.value: Power constitutes an important dimension of social stratification. Yet empirical research on individuals’ access to power is relatively rare. This project seeks to understand the distribution, institutional antecedents and well-being consequences of access to power. We collaborated with a well-established international survey to collect data on people’s perceived power status in 29 societies with diverse social and political institutions. We found that first, compared with positions in the wealth hierarchy, people tended to place them much lower in the power hierarchy. There is a significant amount of variation in people’s perceived power status across different societies. Functional democratic and legal institutions tended to foster greater power perception. Second, power perception is positively linked to well-being and it mediates the relationship between the institutional context and well-being. Moreover, well-functioning institutions ameliorates the effects of individuals’ access to power and wealth on well-being and reduces social disparities. Finally, the incongruence between power and wealth positions on well-being is only consequential to psychological well-being in hybrid democracies; it does not have well-being consequences in authoritarian regimes or full democracies. This project deepens our understanding of social stratification by focusing on power, a distinct but understudied aspect of social stratification.

14618918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618918.value: The Qin and Han empires (221 B.C.–A.D. 220) were the early unified empires in China. The jun (郡 Commndery) and xian (縣 Prefecture) were their local administrative systems that ruled the vast territories effectively for more than four hundred years. The imperial authority penetrated into the local society was always challenged by the corruption of the bureaucratic system and the interest groups of the eminent families in the bottom of the local society. How imperial court rule such an vast empire is worth for studying. This project aims at a thorough understanding of the Han governance on the Linxiang Prefecture 臨湘縣, Changsha Commandery 長沙郡. Through a microhistorical approach, I shall explore the newly unearthed bamboo slips and wooden documents, excavated in the Wuyi Square, Changsha, Hunan Province, which recorded the enforcement of Han laws and concrete judicial issues, such as criminal and civil lawsuits on juridical and taxation, debt disputes among individual, local officers and public affairs, dated back to the Mid-Eastern Han Dynasty. Significantly, the analysis of concrete cases from these archives will shed new light on the microhistory of the Linxiang society as well the governance of Han local administrative mechanism, especially the function and the role of the bureaus (cao 曹) in the Linxiang Prefecture. The implement of Han laws to the local society was the prominent indicator for the evaluations of the government efficiency in the Linxiang Prefecture. Truthfulness and honesty of the law enforcement officials was the key to achieve successful governance. Obviously, a high frequency of the violation of imperial laws and dereliction of duty by local officials would definitely an alarm to Han governance in prefecture level. This project also evaluate how corruption affected the Han ruling machine, why the officers violated imperial laws and failed to perform their missions as Confucian literati. In brief, the objectives of this project are as follows: i) To reconstruct the various of bureaus in the Linxiang Prefecture of Eastern Han China; ii) To evaluate how the bureaus operated and their governance in reference to the enforcement of Han laws and imperial decrees; iii) To evaluate imperial penetration to the local society: how various bureaus involved and associate with the daily life of the bianhu qimin 編戶齊民. 郡縣制度是秦漢帝國地方行政的管理系統。在幅員廣大的帝國內，此制度有效地統治了超過四百年的歷史。但從上而下的帝國權力，往往受到地方社會的挑戰，這些挑戰來自地方的利益集團，例如地方官僚的腐敗和豪族大姓的抗拒等。本研究計劃旨在深入了解東漢長沙郡臨湘縣的管治問題。本計劃通過微觀歷史的方法，以長沙市五一廣場新出土的簡牘文書為中心，探討長沙郡各曹執行漢帝國律令的具體情況。漢代郡府縣廷分曹辦事，出土的簡牘文書是當時使用的官府檔案，主要包含長沙郡及門下諸曹、臨湘縣及門下諸曹的下行文書，臨湘縣、臨湘縣下屬諸鄉、亭的上行文書，亦有與外郡縣的往來文書。筆者透過文書所示的民事訴訟案例了解長沙郡臨湘縣各曹的司法情況。五一廣場的官府文書，顯示東漢編戶民與地方官員，在公共事務之間的各種糾紛。本計劃對上述檔案的具體分析，將為臨湘社會的微觀歷史，以及漢帝國地方行政機制，尤其為臨湘縣廷各曹的組織及其功能提供新的視角。另方面，漢國帝法令的實施是評估臨湘縣廷效率的重要指標。執法掾吏的奉公守法是成功治理的關鍵，反之，地方官員違法瀆職頻率飆升，肯定是帝國管治的警號。 簡而言之，本項目研究目標如下： i） 重建東漢臨湘縣各曹的組織及評估各曹在臨湘縣的管治能力; ii） 評估帝國對當地社會的滲透，各曹如何應對和聯繫編戶齊民的日常生活。

14618918.label: Realisation of objectives
14618918.value: 1 The first objective of this project is to reconstruct the various bureaus in the Linxiang Prefecture of Eastern Han China; and to evaluate their operation and their governance. I analyzed concrete cases from the archives excavated at the Wuyi Square of Changsha. Historians realized that there were nearly twenty bureaus which in charge of most civil affairs at the commandery and county offices during Han times. I adopted micro analysis on the bureau of statement Ci Cao 辤曹, which in charge of statements of legal cases and examination of the evidence put forward by the suspects, plaintiffs and defendants during the processes of the accusation. By evaluating the testimony samples and the biographies of the Ci Cao officers in Han Shu and Hou Han Shu, I found that Ci Cao officers, not only transcribing the confessions of the both sides of the defendants and the plaintiffs, but also responsible for identifying factuality of the statements, giving judgment and suggestions for punishing guilty defendant under the existing legal framework. In case of doubtful, Ci Cao officers could question the affairs involved and presented by both sides of the plaintiff and defendant. A typical example was Chen Chong 陳寵, the former Ci Cao officer in the central government. He was praise by the people for judging accusation convincingly and putting fair and just penalty to criminals. The exploration of the responsibilities of bureau of Ci Cao reflected the governance of Han empire, especially the implement of law to achieve public order. More details please see my article, “Changsha Wuyi Guangchang chutu Dong Han jiandu Zhong de Ci Cao 長沙五一廣場出土東漢簡牘中的辭曹” (in Zhou Dongping 周東平 and 朱騰 Zhu Teng, 法律史譯評 Legal History Studies, Vol 7 (2019), Shanghai: Zhongxi Shuchu, pp104-132). 2. In terms of the second objective, that is to evaluate imperial penetration to the local society, how various bureaus involved and associate with the daily life of the bianhu qimin. My second paper, namely Shi xi ji mei Wuyi Guangchang Dong Han jiandu 試析幾枚五一廣場東漢簡牘 A Tentative Analysis of Three Eastern Han Documents from the Wuyi Guangchang Hoard, which was published in 簡帛研究 Jianbo Yanjiu 2018 (Guilin: Guangxi shifan daxuechubanshe, 2019, pp345-357), analyzed the floating of common peoples, such as merchants, crew, hired workers and coolies in shipping industry along the Xiang River 湘水. With the implement of the Han law and the efficiency of local administration, this paper exhibited the prosperity of human resources, exchange of commodities with the Cangwu Jun 蒼梧郡, Lingling Jun 零陵郡, Guiyang Jun 桂陽郡 and Jiaozhi Jun 交趾郡 acrossing the southern China, and even the Kuaiji Jun 會稽郡 and 下邳郡 Xiapi Jun in the eastern China. Changsha was one of common regions where convicts were sent for hard labour. The tablet CWJ1③:314 indicated 168 Kunqian 髡鉗 convicts were sent from Jiyin Jun 濟陰郡for labour works in Changsha. These non-Native people together with refugees, migrant population, hungry people and even opportunist all come to the metropolitan Changsha. During Eastern Han period, to a certain extent, Changsha became a complex city with several metropolitan characteristics, such huge population with active mobility, highly developed commercial exchanges, convenience of both water and land transportation, etc. 3. In terms of the daily life of the bianhu qimin, Changsha provided sufficiency of agricultural land, abundant of natural resources, and a lot of trade opportunities, such as silk weaving, grain trading and wholesale transshipment. My view is that all these provided plenty engagementto the Changsha populations, such as job opportunities in water navigation and wage employment. My third paper, Changsha Wuyi Guangchang Dong Han jiandu tansuo: Shangmao huodong, shuidao yu lulu jiaotongxian 長沙五一廣場東漢簡牘探索：商貿活動、水道與陸路交通線 explored the commercial activities, water navigation and land transportation of the Changsha commandery and its hinterland. As reflected from the documents, some theft accusations involved huge number of cargoes. Changsha was a commercial and distribution center of the silk weaving product and grain trade crossing southern and northern China. With the establishment of Lingqu 靈渠, which linked the Xiang River and Lishui 灕水 in the southwest China, the communication between Jiaozhi and Jingzhuo 荊州 became more convenience. In counting the water navigation and land transportation, floating people from neighboring county and commandery were attracted to Changsha, particularly the Linxiang city.

14618918.value: I shall continue and analyze in-deep on the manuscripts excavated from Wuyi Square of the Changsha Province, especially the social life and local community of the Linxiang county. 14619418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619418.value: According to the most recent government statistics, more than 200 million Chinese rural residents have migrated from largely agricultural areas to cities. Of these migrants, about 34.5% are female workers. With such a large-scale movement of people, and the resulting imbalance in the gender composition of the sending communities, an important question that remains under studied is how rural people’s livelihood choices have been changing over time. In particular, studies often treat those left-behind as a homogeneous group, and little attention is paid to the variety of off-farm work performed in the home area. To move beyond the sole focus on migration and understand the heterogeneity of rural people’s livelihoods, a systematic study that accounts for the changes to local farm, local off-farm and migration activities is required. Drawing on theories on the gender division of labor, life course, and household labor allocation, the proposed research goes beyond migration and its consequences to examine both local and non-local livelihood choices from a gender perspective. The aim of the project is to study how rural people’s livelihoods have been changing and how their household economic and individual well-being has been affected by these changes. Specifically, we ask the following questions. First, have the livelihood choices of men and women been diverging or converging over two decades of drastic transitions taking place within Chinese society? Second, are gender patterns in livelihood choices shaped by men and women’s life course stages? Third, how do the livelihood choices of household heads impact household economic and individual well-being? The proposed project will use data from two national, large-scale panel surveys: the China Health and Nutrition Survey (CHNS) and the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). CHNS covers a period of over 21 years, i.e., from 1991-2011; CFPS was initiated in 2010 and contains four waves of data to date. Both data sets capture detailed work and household information for all adults. The survey instruments from both sources are deemed to complement each other for the purposes of this study. Innovative statistical methods will be used to take advantage of the panel data design to disentangle the confounding impacts of age and cohorts with period on gender difference in livelihood choices over time, and household heterogeneity in work choice and consequences for rural households and their members. In addition, an ethnographic study will be conducted with a view to providing substantive insights on the statistical results. 隨著女性在城鄉遷移人口中的比例增加，農村家庭戶和個人的生計模式分別發生何種變化在學術研究中還有很大的空缺。本研究運用性別分工理論，生命歷程以及家庭戶勞動分工的理論試圖超越目前多數研究中的簡單的遷移和留守農村的二分生存模式，來研究生計模式在生命歷程中的變化，性別的差異以及對家庭戶和個人福祉的影響。數據將來自兩個全國性的大型調查，一個是中國營養健康調查，另一個是中國家庭追蹤調查，兩者都是縱向調研數據。除此之外，我們也將做一些家庭戶的訪談數據來補充量化研究的不足。

To investigate the neural mechanism of auditory category learning, we will employ both functional and structural MRI to characterize the neural circuitry underlying acquisition of a speech-like auditory category structure. We hypothesize that auditory category learning results in the emergence of categorical representations in the STG. We predict that STG representational changes are an outcome of learning processes in both rule-based frontal-subcortical and reward-based cortical-striatal learning systems. uncovering brain systems mediating different type of supervised learning and design optimal learning protocol. We investigate neural recruitments accompanying the acquisition of non-native speech categories using fMRI by manipulating the speech-like sound category presentation structure (rule-based [RB] or information-integration [II] focus) and type of feedback. Adult participants will be trained to categorize novel sounds with RB category structure at the early stage while with II category structure at the later stage. Neural function across RB and II learning stages will be probed using fMRI and analyzed using univariate neuroimaging analyses and hypothesis-driven multivariate representational similarity analyses (RSA). We predict that the rule-based system is utilized during novice learning, the reward-based system is utilized during the late stage of learning. We further uncover the neural basis underlying two type feedback processes (implicit vs. explicit feedback). Across learning paradigms and neuroimaging modalities, we predict RB representations during novice-learning, driven by the rule-based learning network. As learning progresses to experienced-levels, we hypothesize that representations become multidimensional along the distinctive features of the stimuli, which will be reflected in selective evoked responses in the high-level auditory cortex. Such learning processes and auditory category acquisition could be facilitated and improved by using reward-based feedback processing.

14619518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14619518.value: Learning a foreign language in adulthood is a challenging task, especially learning to map novel auditory signals into abstract categories (e.g., phonetic categories). Despite its challenge, it is possible, even efficient to acquire novel speech signals via feedback-guided training procedure. Previous behavioral and neuroimaging studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of such supervised learning processing and provided possible but vague neural accounts for speech category learning. In this proposal, we attempt to establish a holistic mechanistic account of how the mature human brain functionally reorganizes to acquire and represent speechlike novel auditory categories. We hypothesize two complementary learning systems, rule-based and reward-based streams, are critical during the acquisition. Specifically, we hypothesized that the superior temporal cortex (STG) is a key auditory area in coding speech categories. As learning progress, the two learning systems would interact with the STG differently, and both the functional activation and the neural representation pattern of the STG in response to newly acquired auditory categories are reconfigured. More precisely, we hypothesis that corticostriatal networks, which are sensitive to the reward value of feedback during supervised learning, mediate the STG plasticity and the acquisition of new auditory categories in adulthood. In a series of experiments, we will collect both behavioral learning data and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data to examine the brain dynamics that accompany acquisition of auditory categories with or without feedback. We predict that both rule-based frontal-subcortical and reward-based auditory-striatal learning system are involved in feedback learning while the two systems are less involved in the no-feedback context. We further test the prediction that the rule-based system would be recruited more in the early stage of learning while reward-based circuitry would be involved more in the later stage of learning. Finally, we investigate both behavioral and neural differences between two type of feedback training procedures (minimal vs. full feedback). We aim to design an optimal learning protocol and provide a possible neural mechanistic account for such optimal learning processing. To test these hypotheses, we will use univariate brain activation and multivariate pattern analysis as well as connectivity analysis to characterize the neurobiological dynamics during learning. In summary, we will integrate several lines of research to provide a mechanistic account of novel speech category acquisition. Potential findings derived from these experiments could uncover the role of the corticostriatal circuitry in supervised speech learning, which could be a scientific basis for designing optimal speech training procedure. 成年人學習外語是非常困難和有挑戰性的，尤其是要求學習新的言語聽覺信號並區分出不同的抽象聲音類別（例如，語音類別）。儘管存在困難和挑戰，但通過使用反饋性的監督訓練程式是有可能促進學習者習得新的言語類別。先前的行為和神經影像學研究展示了這種監督性學習程式的有效性，並為言語類別範疇學習的認知神經機制提供了初步的證據。在本研究項目中，我們團隊試圖闡述和建立一個完整的言語類別學習的認知神經機制，並進一步探明成人大腦在功能上如何重組以習得新的聽覺言語類別。我們根據先前的研究發現認為存在兩個互補的大腦學習系統（基於規則和基於反饋的系統）在言語習得過程中起到重要作用。具體來說，我們假設顳上皮層（STG）是編碼語音類別的關鍵聽覺區域。在學習過程中，兩個學習系統會以不同方式與STG進行交互，而且對新的聽覺刺激相關的STG啟動模式會隨著不同學習階段而發生改變。更準確地說，我們假設，在監督學習期間對反饋敏感的大腦皮質-紋狀體系統會調節STG的神經可塑性，這一機制使成年學習者獲得區分新聽覺類別的能力。在一系列實驗中，我們將收集行為學習數據和功能磁共振腦成像（fMRI）數據，用於研究聽覺類別學習過程中的大腦動態改變，並對比有或沒有反饋條件下大腦改變的差異。我們預測基於規則學習的前額葉皮質-皮質下系統和基於反饋的聽覺-紋狀體學習系統都參與到反饋性言語學習中，而兩個系統較少參與到無反饋的學習條件。我們進一步檢驗，在早期學習階段，規則學習系統會有更多的參與；而在後期學習階段，基於反饋的學習系統會更多參與。最後，我們計畫研究兩種類型的反饋訓練程式（最小與完全反饋）之間的行為和神經差異。我們的目標是設計一個最佳的指導性學習程式，並為對這種最佳學習程式提供可能的神經機制解釋。為了測試這些假設，我們將使用多種先進的神經建模分析方法，包括單變數大腦啟動和多變數模式分析，以及腦功能連接分析技術來研究學習過程中的神經生物學機制。總之，我們將整合幾個不同的研究領域和技術，以發現獲取新語音類別的認知神經機制。這些實驗得出的潛在發現可以揭示皮質-紋狀體系統在指導性語音學習中的作用，這可能是設計最佳言語訓練程式的神經科學依據。

14619518.label: Realisation of objectives
14619518.value: The aim of this project is to characterize the mechanical role of human corticostriatal systems in acquiring various types of auditory category structures (Objective 1) and to manipulate different training-related factors to examine their impact on learning success and responses of corticostriatal systems (Objective 2). This study could provide valuable insights into designing optimal learning protocols for adult learners. To achieve the above project objectives, the PI’s research team hired three research staff for the implementation of the proposed experiments, including one full-time Postdoctoral Fellow (with additional funding support from the CUHK Research Fellowship Scheme) and two part-time research assistants (hired in Mainland in Guangzhou for subject recruitment and neuroimaging data collection). Unfortunately, we faced significant challenges in executing the proposed experiments during the 2020-2021 period, primarily due to the global COVID-19 pandemic. These hurdles encompassed the shutdown of neuroimaging facilities, complexity of commuting between collaborative locations, and a restricted personnel budget that impeded us from gathering an adequate number of samples (due to the project's extension). In 2020, the neuroimaging facilities were temporarily shut down, resulting in a significant delay to the research plan and an impact on the research budget. The facilities resumed normal operation in mid-2021 but with limited access initially. Thanks to the assistance of one of our Co-Investigators, Prof. Suiping Wang at SCNU, we were able to receive support in project administration and manpower. With their help, we successfully conducted all of our planned experiments, analyzed all neuroimaging data, and published some of our research findings. In summary, we have conducted three planned fMRI studies with well-controlled experimental designs, advanced fMRI protocols, and state-of-the-art multivariate neural analytics to achieve the two objectives. In study 1, we conducted auditory category training experiments with speech (tones) and speech-like ripple sounds, where we asked participants to categorize or learn to categorize sounds during fMRI scanning. To overcome the impact of scanning noise on our auditory experiments, we designed a customized fMRI sparse-sampling sequence with a high spatial and temporal resolution where the sounds can be displayed during the silent scanning period. With the novel experimental design and scanning sequence, we identified the key neural systems that are related to feedback-based auditory category learning and determined the neural representations of category information in the auditory-speech cortical systems that emerge during learning with feedback. We published three papers in high-profile journals and conference proceedings for the data (Please refer to Part C for details). In study 2, we manipulated the feedback type that we presented to participants after each categorization attempt during training and also focused on individual differences in learning success, which enabled us to examine to which extent different types of feedback would result in different learning outcomes at both group and individual learner levels. To achieve objective 2 and understand why learners learn differently, we constructed predictive models with leaner’s neuroimaging data to predict how well they would learn in the future. This also helps uncover the neural mechanisms underlying successful learning in general. We found that multivariate neural responses across multiple brain networks, including dorsal and ventral auditory streams, frontoparietal control network, and corticostriatal network, contribute to explaining the individual differences in learning success. Some of the data and findings derived from this study have been published in the high-profile journals Neurobiology of Language and Journal of Neuroscience (Feng et al., 2021[2] and 2021[3]). In study 3, we manipulated the training procedure to examine whether a new procedure (easy-to-hard training) would enhance learning outcomes and investigated how the corticostriatal system responded to the switching from learning a rule-based (easy-to-learn) structure to learning an information-integration (hard-to-learn) structure in the middle of training. This modified learning procedure helped learners transfer their learning strategy to the multidimensional information-integration strategy and yielded better behavioral learning outcomes. Also, this design enables us to examine the neural mechanisms underlying the more efficient learning procedure for auditory category learning. At the neural level, we used advanced multivariate neural encoding modeling and functional connectivity approaches to examine the relationship between the striatum and auditory superior temporal regions in different learning phases and determined the inter-regional interactions contributing to learning success. We found that more successful learners have more efficient corticostriatal neural dynamics during learning. We are finalizing the research manuscripts for this data and its findings.

14619518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14619518.value: This multi-site collaborative project focused on examining neural mechanisms of human auditory category learning. Three carefully designed functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) studies explored the role of corticostriatal systems and different training-related factors in learning to categorize sounds with various category structures. In the first study, participants underwent auditory category training with speech and speech-like stimuli during fMRI scanning. Utilizing a customized fMRI sparse-sampling sequence to minimize the influence of scanning noise, the study identified key corticostriatal neural systems associated with feedback-based auditory category learning. Results further showed that feedback-dependent neural representations of category information emerged in auditory-speech cortical systems during the learning process. The emerging neural representations are tightly linked with the striatal feedback-related activations. We published three research papers in high-profile journals (i.e., Feng et al., 2021[1], 2021[4], NeuroImage; Gan .. Feng, 2023[5], Data in Brief) and conference presentations for the data (refer to Part C for details). In the second study, participants were given different types of feedback after each categorization attempt during training to see how it affected their learning outcomes. The focus was on individual learning success variations, and this approach helped researchers understand the impact of different feedback types on learning success. By analyzing neuroimaging data, predictive models were created to forecast each participant's future performance. Multivariate neural responses across multiple brain networks played a significant role in explaining individual differences in learning. These findings were published in the high-profile journals Neurobiology of Language and Journal of Neuroscience (Feng et al., 2021[2], 2021[3]). In the third study, the training procedure was altered to assess its effects on learning outcomes and the corticostriatal system's response. The study moved from a traditional training procedure to a new easy-to-hard switching training paradigm that resulted in improved behavioral learning outcomes and a more efficient transfer of learning strategies. Successful learners exhibited more efficient corticostriatal neural dynamics during learning at the neural level. We are preparing manuscripts to report these findings. In summary, auditory category learning yielded multidimensional perceptual feature representations in the corticostriatal neural network, encompassing the superior temporal cortex, inferior frontal gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, and striatal regions. Feedback and learning procedure played critical roles in modulating behavioral performance and neural involvement in corticostriatal learning systems. By manipulating feedback and learning protocols, the study offered insights into the neural mechanisms underpinning feedback-based auditory category learning, potentially informing the design of optimal learning protocols in speech category learning.

14619518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14619518.value: Based on the current findings and framework, our team plan to deepen our understanding of the neural mechanisms of auditory category learning and optimize learning protocols based on the neurocognitive mechanisms of learning. Our findings highlight the significant potential to utilize brain imaging techniques, such as fMRI, to enhance personalized learning strategies based on individual neural patterns. We propose a two-pronged course of action for future research. First, we aim to refine our predictive models to further our understanding of how specific neural networks contribute to individual learning success. These refined models could potentially be used to design personalized learning protocols, enhancing learning outcomes in areas such as language learning and music education. Second, we plan to delve deeper into the impact of varying training procedures and feedback types on the corticostriatal system's responses and generalization of learned knowledge. We will examine how these changes affect the transfer of learning strategies and overall learning success. Our goal is to optimize the learning process by identifying the most effective training procedures and feedback types. These further developments will not only advance our understanding of auditory category learning but could also have broad applications in educational and therapeutic settings.

14619518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14619518.value: The capacity to learn to categorize sounds is crucial for humans to learn and comprehend different spoken languages. The objectives of this project are to understand how the brain recognizes and classifies various sounds, as well as how to enhance these processes. Similar to how a personal trainer utilizes various exercises and feedback methods to assist individuals in improving their skills in a sport, this study utilized different techniques and feedback types to aid participants in improving their sound categorization abilities and to understand the underlying neural principles. Using neuroimaging techniques, this project found that a corticostriatal system in the brain lit up as participants learned to categorize sounds. This neural system further creates a kind of mental map for these sounds when training with feedback. Switching up the training method, starting from easy tasks and moving to harder ones, further improved learning outcomes and made the learning strategies more efficient. In addition, the researchers also created prediction models that could even forecast how well someone would learn based on their brain scans. This research could help design better learning programs, making it easier for us to learn new languages or musical instruments.
