14623518.label: Major findings and research outcome
14623518.value: Under the current Chinese college admissions system, universities assign admissions quotas to provinces and admit applicants with the highest test scores in each province to fill the quotas. To understand the quota-setting process, we develop a theoretical model that captures key features of the Chinese system. In our model, universities prefer applicants with higher test scores. But controlling for test scores, universities also have preferences over students' provincial backgrounds. The preference may reflect the interests of the universities or the central government. We show that universities should set admission quotas to equalize the value of marginal students in different provinces in equilibrium. As a result, the equilibrium allocation of places reflects not only the central government's and universities' preferences over students but also students' preferences over universities. We collect a unique data set of admissions quotas and cutoffs of one hundred top Chinese universities from 2013 to 2017. Using a methodology developed from the theoretical model, we estimate the universities' preferences over provinces and applicants' preferences over universities. The main findings are as follows: 1. Universities in our sample have remarkably similar preferences. Regardless of rank and location, they consistently favor students from richer provinces. One possible explanation is that richer provinces spend more on pre-college education. 2. Universities, especially those higher ranked or under provincial governments, tend to favor home-province applicants. However, the magnitude of this bias is small compared to the preferences for richer provinces. 3. Applicants have a strong preference for universities in their home provinces. This preference, rather than universities' home bias, explains why many students attend universities in their home provinces. 4. Counterfactual simulations suggest that universities' preferences mainly cause the current unequal provincial allocation of places for richer provinces. The contribution of home biases of universities in richer provinces is small. In fact, universities in Shanghai tend to be biased against home-province applicants. Overall, our results suggest that the long-term solution to the unequal distribution of university places is to raise the education spending in poorer provinces. However, forcing universities to reduce quotas to home provinces may result in a substantial welfare loss as students prefer universities closer to home.

14623518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14623518.value: The allocation of places at the top Chinese universities is a highly contentious issue in China. Under the current system, applicants do not compete across provinces. Instead, universities assign admissions quotas to provinces and admit applicants with the highest test scores in each province to fill the quotas. A common grievance is that universities in Beijing, Shanghai, and other rich provinces are biased in favor of home-province applicants. In this project, we collect a unique data set of admissions quotas and cutoffs of one hundred top Chinese universities from 2013 to 2017. Using a methodology we develop from a theoretical model, we estimate the universities’ preferences over provinces and applicants’ preferences over universities. We find that universities have remarkably similar preferences. Regardless of rank and location, they consistently favor students from richer provinces. The preference explains why applicants from richer provinces are more likely to be admitted to a top university in China. Universities, especially those higher ranked or under provincial governments, tend to favor home-province applicants. However, the magnitude of this bias is small. Contrary to popular beliefs, universities’ home biases have little impact on the overall allocation of places.

14623818.label: Project Objectives
14623818.value: To study the demographic dimension of ‘Lo Wai Luen’s Hong Kong Literature Archives’ by visualizing a detailed account of cross-border writers within the 2,000 files and 38,000 pieces of documents, investigating what kinds of socio-political as well as cultural activities are involved in the formulation of Hong Kong literature, and how Hong Kong is conceptualized in literary studies through layers of China experiences cultivated by various populations. To study the spatial dimension of the Hong Kong Literature Archives by visualizing geographically on the development of localism and China related sentiments by examining the origins where southern-bound writers came from and the (de)territorization of literary organizations and printed works, mapping the development of the Hong Kong literary field since the borderless and non-hierarchical experiences of the early twentieth century. Combining the above two tasks, this study can generate a digital database for us to understand Hong Kong-China literary relations synchronically and diachronically with the functions of timeline (1920's to 2010's) and different filters and layers (number, movement and relations of people, places and time), visualizing Hong Kong’s nodal significance in the crossroads of empires. (see fig.1 and 2 for suggested layouts of the perspective outputs)

14623818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14623818.value: The research is intended to provide an in-depth analysis of the ‘Hong Kong Literature Archives’ compiled by Lo Wai Luen (Xiao Si) (1939- ), who is acknowledged as 'the most qualified writer on Hong Kong literary history', through tools of digital humanities as well as interactive interviews. There are two main objectives in the study: 1. Providing a historical survey of Hong Kong-China cultural interactions in ‘Lo Wai Luen's Hong Kong Literature Archives’; and 2. Visualizing the relations between Hong Kong and China in the context of Hong Kong literary activities since the 1920s with the help of analytic tools of digital humanities. Combining the two perspectives, we shall be able to learn more about the changing understanding of relations between Hong Kong and China in terms of literary history over the last ten decades, including Hong Kong's initiatives in advocating an independent cultural identity. The research will focus on archival studies of literary activities of the "Southern-bound writers' from mainland China and their interactions with local Hong Kong writers, a field where discourse and concrete documents meet, and will have a wide impact on our understanding of the complex relations between Hong Kong and Mainland China as well as the literary field of Hong Kong literature and its sociopolitical contexts. The actual history of Hong Kong, from the rule of colonial British empire to People's Republic of China, will also provide a valuable perspective from which to study how literature is manifested in different political situations. Above all, this research demonstrate the advantages of archival studies and long term interviews with the most accomplished scholar and archivist of Hong Kong literature. It will also assist scholars to understand the actual meanings, impacts, and specificities of 'Hong Kong-China Relations' in the context of Hong Kong literature, a pertinent amendment to a burgeoning academic area of studies in recent years. 本計劃旨在透過數位人文與親身訪談，深入研究盧瑋鑾教授（小思）（1939—）「香港文學檔案」之「中港關係」。盧氏被譽為「最有資格撰寫香港文學史」的人，從她所蒐集的材料與口述文學史，本研究目的有二︰ 一、為盧氏之「香港文學研究檔案」梳理出一套中港文學文化關係史 二、以數位人文分析工具多元呈現1920年代以來中港文學活動及人物的圖景 結合上述兩項研究，可以為近十年的中港文學關係以至香港的獨特文化身份帶來啟示；此外，亦會重點論及「南來作家」的論述與史料、內地文化人與香港文學場域的關係，以至由英殖至中國管治下社會政治語境之轉變。總括而言，本研究凸顯對重要學人之個人檔案及口述歷史之重視，並期望透過香港文學，了解日趨熾熱之「中港關係」論述當中，確實之意義、影響與內涵。

14623818.label: Realisation of objectives
14623818.value: As for Objective 1, the demographic data of 38,000 pieces of documents from more than 2,000 file were reviewed and input in a dataset which was attached in the last progress report. The data include near 6,000 cultural interactions among 500 literati and we produced clusters of documents on them and generated networks of the clusters and grouped them into six categories: publication business, journalism, writers’ associations, education institutions, political parties as well as government departments, thus remapped the literary field of Hong Kong, which was usually misread as a small group of reclusive literary writers and poets. The vibrant cultural exchanges consolidated not only the mainlanders and Hongkongers, but sometimes also the lobbyists from adversary political forces. The dataset is basically ready for various task with visualization tools like Palladio which was developed by the “Stanford Humanities + Design” team. Network theory is particularly useful in analyzing people’s affiliations, as in the example of ‘Literati and Organizations in 1948 Hong Kong’ shown in fig.1 in the appendix. We can see the literati from mainland actively participated in the ‘China Literary Association (Hong Kong Division)’, ‘The Hong Kong and Kowloon Overseas Chinese Teachers Welfare Association’, and the ‘Representatives meeting of American Citizens’ China Policy’. These events concern not only local literary issues, but also have an international aspect towards sociopolitical situation in Hong Kong. Over 1,500 organizations and 3,000 names are documented and ready to be further appraised with visualization tools. The complex literary field of Hong Kong and the participations of mainland literati is represented, especially from the 1930s to 1960s. Hong Kong was used as a platform of dissemination of ideas, and sometimes the clash of ideas nurtured the burgeoned literature development in the 1970s. The practice of network theory in this project further benefits the study of Lu Lun 侶倫, arguably the first local literary writer in Hong Kong, on a recently unearthed movie script archived in the Chinese University Library. The relations and conflict among Chinese immigrants project a mixed feeling towards mainlanders from a local writer. As for Objective 2, since the concept of ‘Chinese mainlanders’ is not monolithic, as well as Hong Konger’s, the study of Lo’s archive demonstrates the construction of Hong Kong literary field as well as Hong Kong community, which warrant a close, deep and continued understanding of mainlanders, especially from a cultural point of view. From the dataset mentioned above, literati from over 300 places in mainland China visited Hong Kong with cultural or political agendas. Their birthplaces, working places, arrival points (Hong Kong and other) are recorded and ready for visualization as in fig.2, in which the routes of mainland literati in 1948 is mapped with their frequencies shown while mouse overed. Numbers of mainland visitors could be compared with different periods of time, groups of people or individuals. While the influxes of mainlanders are apparent during the outbroke of WWII and 1949, some underrepresented cultural exchanges are recorded in the archives, such as the Japanese Occupation period of 1941-1945, the activities of mainland writers such as Ye Lingfeng and Dai Wangshu is crucial and well documented. Their metaphorical writings and reluctant cultural exchange with the Greater East Asia region during the occupation period is essential for highlighting Hong Kong’s ambivalent cultural position and the commitment of the literati. The birthplaces or original provinces of mainland literati in Hong Kong can also be examined in the visualization process. As shown in fig.2, most of the mainland writers came from Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces rather than the adjacent Guangdong provinces or the more politically central Beijing. This contributes to the ‘Shanghai influence’ or Haipai in Hong Kong literature. Those writers who are deeply related to Hong Kong like Dai Wangshu, Ye Lingfeng and Mu Shiying are from the JiangZhe area, and the phenomenon is clearly shown in the visualization in fig.2. As for Objective 3, on the whole, the data of Lo’s digital archive, including people, place and time from various events has been completely input to the dataset. From the visualization process, we discover the importance of official units such as ‘China Literary Association (Hong Kong Division)’ in the end of 1940s and 1950s, the dominant activities of the ‘United States Information Service (USIS)’ and the reactive strategies of the mainland literati in the 1960s, the opposing of the quintessential nationalism and localism after the stormy year of 1967, a historical turning point which I mark the power of mainland cultural influence fading away in the 1970s. Reason for under-achievements and attempts to overcome problems While “archival studies is a subfield of information studies that is concerned with records as persistent representations of human activity that travel across space and time” (Carbajal, Itza A; Caswell, Michelle, 1103), the archivist and other archival creators are ethically responsible for what they collect and make available digitally. The project was intended to have all the data files open for public use and further visualization experiments right after the completion of it. However, on the suggestions of the archive builder Lo Wai-luen, the existing archive covers only materials before 2003 which need to be updated as well as cross-checked with information beyond the archive itself, to materials such as almanacs, collected essays and index cards compiled by Lo over the years. The base of the research thus increased extensively and the “data massage” process is much longer than we expected. We take heed here from the concept of “slow archives”, which are “about focusing differently, listening carefully, and acting ethically” (Kim Christen; Jane Anderson, 90). With careful intent and care, digital archives do not need to be approached haphazardly in order to be used, enjoyed, and exposed. We believe the completed dataset will be released in mid-2022. Moreover, the ‘digital archive’ in this project is actually analogue records, such as those created in paper, analogue film, recording tape and other nondigital formats, that have been selectively digitized, selectively collected by Lo, the archive founder; and the CUHK library, the archival institutions selectively preserved. An oral history with Lo is an indispensable complement of the project. However, due to the social upheaval and pandemic situation in 2019 and 2020, many of the planned visits to Lo’s home was either postponed or changed to emails. There were still five face-to-face discussions conducted during the project period with numerous exchanges on emails. The complete record will be used in the exhibition of the 20th Anniversary of Hong Kong Literary Research Centre in May 2022. Carbajal, Itza A, and Michelle Caswell. “Critical Digital Archives: A Review from Archival Studies.” The American Historical Review, vol. 126, no. 3, 2021, pp. 1102–1120., https://doi.org/10.1093/ahr/rhab359. Christen, Kimberly, and Jane Anderson. “Toward Slow Archives.” Archival Science, vol. 19, no. 2, 2019, pp. 87–116., https://doi.org/10.1007/s10502-019-09307-x.

14623818.label: Major findings and research outcome
14623818.value: The intention of this project is to trace the outlines of a cultural presence of the last century (1920s-2020s) by means of the study of literary archives in which certain mainland literati groups and movements were involved in Hong Kong. The major finding of this project is the establishment of mainland cultural influences against the Hong Kong literature background, and the vanquishment of that establishment. Such a study is attempted by simultaneously tracing the course of the most important activities by mainland and local literati. The comparative view possesses the double mainland literature so near to us that we can understand it, and of removing our own Hong Kong literature until we are enabled to see it in its true perspective. The scientific view of visualization of mainland literati’s activities in Hong Kong provides us with a vision that they have only to a very limited extent been able to benefit by each other’s production. In ‘Negotiating Theories of Affect and Diaspora: The Potentialities of Chinese Writers as Hong Kong Flâneur’ (Wong, 2022a), I argue that southbound mainland literati were not always descend from the superior ‘North’ in a high-profile way. They can act as a Flâneur in Hong Kong and the scattered networks of visualized this. There political agendas were sound, but the affect and diaspora were still everywhere mingled with the local forces. Visualization can also help reading literary text. The local born writer Lu Lun, named as the first local writer in Hong Kong, had fled to mainland during the occupation period and came back after the war ended. His most famous novel “Dead End” was written after returning from mainland. With the inspiration of network theory, the paper ‘Network Theory, Plot Analysis: A case study of Lu Lun's "Poverty-Stricken Alley/Dead End"’ (Wong, 2019) demonstrates the complicated struggle of a writer between the identification of China and Hong Kong through a well-made network of plots and characters. The acknowledgement of RGC's support was not found in the printed version of the paper. However, the support is fully acknowledged in the conference presentation and paper. While the above cases come from the 40s and 50s of Hong Kong, the paper on popular writer Yida依達 (Wong, 2022b) focuses on the cultural scene of 60s and 70s, and the one on Xi Xi西西 investigates the personal correspondences between Xi Xi and mainland writers including Mo Yan莫言, Yu Hua余華 and Wang Anyi王安憶.

14623818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14623818.value: While the study presents the spectacle of many scattered and apparently disconnected literary efforts and phenomena by mainland literati, one who carefully observe the current of mainland influence perceives that their movements are conditioned by the interactive movement of the local Hong Kong literati. We cannot comprehend the intellectual idiosyncrasy of the Hong Kong authors without some acquaintance with the mainland intellects which influenced their development. This is proven with the help of data visualization, and the vast background gained from this project will cast a sharp contrast to the existing Hong Kong literature discourse. And it would be is ready for compilation as a book of "Hong Kong Literary History" in the scale of Margret Atwood's "Survival: A Thematic Guide to Canadian Literature", which echoes with the 'survival history of Hong Kong literature' over the past century.

14623818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14623818.value: As intellectual phenomena condition, elucidate and explain each other, a thorough study of Hong Kong literature cannot be complete without some acquaintance with mainland intellects which influenced the development of Hong Kong authors, and the spiritual atmosphere which they breathed in. Archival study, like other disciplines, is evolving into more specific interdisciplinary subfields. This project demonstrates the above statements by processing more than 38,000 pieces of data in “Lo Wai Luen’s Hong Kong Literary Archives” to be visualization ready. Clusters of authors names, places, dates and organizations are produced using the visualization tool. The project generated pathways to various studies regarding “mainland writers and Hong Kong” including literati networks, political adversary in literary activities, transformation of the “Shanghai style” and the personal acquaintances between Hong Kong and Mainland writers. Dataset to be openly shared online for research.

15100018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15100018.value: Major depressive disorder is a devastating condition that disables millions of people worldwide. Current antidepressant treatments are limited by both low response rates and delayed onset of action. Recent evidence indicates that ketamine has rapid antidepressant properties. Its antidepressant effects are likely due to its promoting effects on glutamate transmission and synaptic plasticity in the prefrontal cortex. Unfortunately, despite its rapid antidepressant properties, ketamine is also a drug of abuse and is associated with significant adverse events. Thus, there continues to be a need to identify alternative effective antidepressants. Physical exercise is an effective and safe non-drug antidepressant treatment. Our previous research has found that an adipocyte-secreted hormone adiponectin plays a key role in mediating the antidepressant effects of physical exercise. Specifically, we found that it mediates exercise-promoted adult neurogenesis (adult-born neuron in the dentate gyrus [DG] of the hippocampus), and that by initiating adiponectin receptor-triggered cellular signal transduction in the hippocampus it can also improve mood. Recently, adiponectin has been shown to exert rapid antidepressant actions that are independent of hippocampal neurogenesis. Our electrophysiological data have shown that adiponectin restores synaptic deficits and potentiates glutamate receptors—specifically, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in the hippocampus—suggesting that adiponectin’s beneficial effects occur via its effects on NMDA receptor-dependent synaptic plasticity in the DG. We hypothesize that adiponectin exerts its rapid antidepressant effect through its direct action on activating NMDA receptor in glutamatergic neurons in the DG. These activate downstream signal transduction that promotes hippocampal synaptogenesis and synaptic plasticity. By using a multi-method approach, including electrophysiology, molecular, spine morphology, behavioral studies, and transgenic mice in combination of viral vectors, we will build on previous research by: (1) determining whether adiponectin elicits rapid antidepressant effects by enhancing hippocampal synaptic plasticity in depressed mice; (2) determining whether adiponectin’s antidepressant effect involves activation of NMDA receptors in glutamatergic neurons; and (3) identifying the molecular and cellular pathways underlying adiponectin’s action on NMDA receptor activation and its rapid antidepressant effect. The proposed study will not only provide mechanistic data illustrating the novel roles of adiponectin, but also provide evidence showing how NMDA receptor function on glutamatergic neurons is linked to depression. Ultimately, this program of research will identify novel therapeutic targets for developing effective rapid antidepressants with minimal side effects.

15100018.label: Realisation of objectives
15100018.value: Aim 1: To determine if adiponectin deficiency impairs synaptic plasticity or increase in adiponectin levels induces synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus Results achieved: We have demonstrated that animals subjected to chronic unpredictable stress showed depression-like behaviour as indicated by significant increase in immobility time in forced swim test, sucrose splash test . Long term potentiation measurement has indicated that chronic stress did not affect presynaptic neurotransmission efficient , but impaired synaptic plasticity in the both the ventral and dorsal hippocampal dentate gyrus. We utilized electrophysiological recording to examine the effects of adiponectin on modulating synaptic plasticity. Results from field recording of the long-term potentiation has shown that bath application of adiponectin on synaptic impairment in the hippocampal dorsal and ventral dentate gyrus in the acute hippocampal slices from animals subjected to chronic unpredictable stress, suggesting increasing adiponectin levels in the hippocampus could restore synaptic impairment in an animal model of depression. Adiponectin knockout mice breeding pairs bred in Laboratory Animal Unit at University of Hong Kong cannot be transferred to the central animal facilities, because of viral infection in the breeding pairs at HKU. Therefore, we could not test whether adiponectin deficiency in adiponectin knockout mice impaired hippocampal plasticity; however, we have shown that depressed animals showed impaired synaptic plasticity and it is known that depression reduces adiponectin levels in clinical patients in the literature. We have demonstrated that animal with depressive behaviour showed impaired synaptic plasticity and adiponectin restored this impairment. Aim 2: To determine if adiponectin exerts its rapid antidepressant effect on depressed mice by enhancing hippocampal synaptic plasticity Results achieved: We started with control health animals based on previous report showing that intraventricular infusion with recombinant globular or low molecular adiponectin showed rapid antidepressant effects in the mice. Our results showed that 30-min post intra-hippocampal dentate gyrus infusion with 0.5 ng and 5 ng recombinant trimeric form of adiponectin increased depression-like behaviour in a dose dependent manner. Acute treatment with 50 nM adiponectin or 50 nM adiponectin receptor agonist: AdipoRon reduced spine maturation in hippocampal primary culture expressing green fluorescent protein. Acute bath application with trimeric adiponectin at the dosage of 500nM suppressed long-term potentiation, indicating an impairment in synaptic plasticity at a high dosage of adiponectin treatment . So far, the data has suggested that in physiological condition, acute treatment with adiponectin at a dosage leading to excessive increase in adiponectin levels in the hippocampal dentate gyrus could lead to detrimental effect on hippocampal synaptic plasticity in physiological condition. Since acute increase in adiponectin levels at the dosage of 50nM in the hippocampal dentate gyrus caused detrimental effect on synaptic plasticity and spine formation and induced depression-like behaviour in normal animals. However, in stressed animals, we have observed that intraventricular infusion with recombinant adiponectin elicits rapid antidepressant effects in mice with chronic unpredictable stress, showing the direction action of adiponectin in triggering rapid antidepressant response in the mouse model of depression. Furthermore, we conducted a sub-chronic treatment with adiponectin receptor agonist to activating adiponectin downstream signalling. AdipoRon treatment to activate adiponectin signalling in the normal mice, because our previous pilot data showed that blood levels of adiponectin could be reduced with 7-day treatment with 20 mg/kg AdipoRon treatment, suggesting a homeostatic feedback regulation in adipogenergic signalling.Since adiponectin levels in the blood was decreased following 7-day acute treatment. Our results has been published (Formolo et al.. 2022 Biomedicine) showed that 7-day treatment with 20 mg/kg AdipoRon elicited significant antidepressant effects as evidenced by (1) decreased in decreased anxiety-like behaviour represented by increased latency, increased time spent and number of visits to the center in the open field test; (2) depression/anhedonia-like behaviour in novelty suppressed feeding, sucrose preference test and forced swim test , but decreased adiponectin levels in the blood. Taken the currently available data together, low levels of adiponectin increase may be required to elicit positive influence on hippocampal function. As we expected, our in vivo experiment showed that increasing adiponectin levels in the brain elicits rapid antidepressant effects of mice with chronic unpredictable, showing increasing adiponectin in pathological condition can elicits rapid antidepressant response. Aim 3: To better understand the underlying mechanisms of adiponectin action on inducing hippocampal synaptic plasticity and antidepressant effects Results achieved: As rapid antidepressant effect was shown after activating adiponectin receptor signalling in the hippocampus, we performed synaptoneurosome extraction of hippocampal dentate tissues to examine whether changes of synaptic proteins in synaptic compartment is involved in the behavioural response after the rapid treatment. In physiological condition, adiponectin at the concentration of 50 nM did not affect the NMDA receptor EPSP in the field recording (Fig 10), we will further investigate whether adiponectin modulates AMPA EPSP in both physiological or depressed condition. We speculate that adiponectin in physiological condition (with intact adiponectin signalling) affects hippocampal function differently from the diseased state when adiponectin levels or signalling is impaired. Using transgenic mice, we specifically knockdown NMDA receptor subunit GluN2A or GluN2B, results showed no changes in depressive behavior in mice treated with AdipoRon, suggesting that antidepressant and anxiolytic effects of sub-chronic AdipoRon are independent of hippocampal NMDA receptors. The effects of acute (7 days) AdipoRon treatment are not significantly affected by knockdown of the NMDA receptor subunit (GluN2A and GluN2B), as no significant alteration is observed in (a) the sucrose preference in the SPT, (b) immobility time in the FST, (c) latency to eat in the NSF test, and (d) time spent and (e) number of visits to the light compartment of the LDB test, compared with AdipoRon-treated animals with intact NMDA receptor subunits (Control). Furthermore, sub-chronic AdipoRon treatment reduces protein levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor in the hippocampus. (a) 7-days AdipoRon treatment significantly reduces hippocampal BDNF levels, although with no changes in the level of (b) hippocampal adiponectin. (c) Protein expression of (d) hippocampal AdipoR1 or (d) AdipoR2 is not significantly affected. Activating adiponectin signaling by AdipoRon treatment did not change the expression of the protein expression of (b) PSD-95, (c) GluA1 subunit of AMPA receptors, (d) GluN2A, or (e) GluN2B subunits of NMDA receptors in the hippocampus.

15100018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15100018.value: We have discovered that increasing adiponectin elicits rapid antidepressant effects, which is independent to changes of hippocampal synaptic plasticity. Therefore, we plan to further investigate whether rapid antidepressant response required activation of medial prefrontal cortex, since we have evidence showing that mPFC plays in key role with significant increase in neuronal activation marker which is absent in the hippocampus. The future work will extend to PFC to further investigate the neural circuit remodeling by activation of adiponectin receptor in the mPFC and its projecting key brain regions that involved in rapid antidepressant response.

15100018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15100018.value: Major depressive disorder is a devastating condition that disables millions of people worldwide. Current antidepressant treatments are limited by low response rates and delayed onset of action. Rapid antidepressant properties could due to its inhibitory effects on N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in inhibitory interneurons. Our previous research has found that an adipocyte-secreted hormone adiponectin plays a key role in mediating the antidepressant effects of physical exercise. We have found that increasing adiponectin levels in the brain exerts rapid antidepressant actions. Our data have shown that adiponectin restores synaptic deficits in the hippocampal dentate gyrus of depressed animals. Activating adiponectin signaling with acute treatment (post 30 min) of its receptor agonist AdipoRon elicits rapid antidepressant response but increased anxiety levels, while acute treatment with 7 days elicits both antidepressant and anxiety behaviors. While blocking NMDA receptor NR2A or NR2B subunits using transgenic mice did not block the antidepressant effects of adiponectin, suggesting rapid antidepressant response may not necessarily involved the hippocampus. Future study should extend to the medial prefrontal cortex. Our molecular studies showed that increasing adiponectin levels in physiological condition could reduce spine density and maturation, and NMDA receptor function, suggesting adiponectin could have a bidirectional role in regulating synaptic plasticity.

15100418.label: Realisation of objectives
15100418.value: The primary goal of this project was to extend current understanding on how the presence of two common astigmatic subtypes (With-The-Rule, WTR; and Against-The-Rule, ATR) alter refractive development, using a well-established animal model (chickens) sensitive and responsive to alterations in early visual experience. First, we hypothesized that WTR astigmatism was more potent than ATR astigmatism in slowing eye growth. To answer this, objective 1 investigated the ocular biometric changes in chicks developing abnormal refractive error in the presence of WTR and ATR astigmatism. Second, we hypothesized that the magnitude of WTR astigmatism is more potent than that of ATR astigmatism in modulating ametropic development; objective 2 tested the limit to which each astigmatic subtype could alter ocular biometric parameters. With this research fund, the project generated two original scientific publications (1xIOVS and 1xScientific Reports) and three reports presented at international conferences (1xInternational Myopia Conference and 2xARVO), providing convincing evidence on the influential role of astigmatism during myopic (or short-sightedness) eye growth. 1st paper: Vyas SA and Kee CS (2021). Early Astigmatism Can Alter Myopia Development in Chickens. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 62(2): 27. To answer how and to what extent the presence of WTR and ATR astigmatic defocus influence ametropic development during early eye growth, chicks were randomly assigned to wear either spherical (hyperopic defocus) or sphero-cylindrical lenses (hyperopic-astigmatic defocus, with 2 magnitudes and 4 axes). Refractions, corneal curvature, and axial dimensions were measured and compared across groups. Results showed that mixing the optical blur with the presence of astigmatism significantly slowed the myopia development induced by spherical defocus alone. In addition, hyperopic-ATR defocus induced a higher myopia but lower astigmatism compared to hyperopic-WTR defocus. Importantly, the effects of imposing different magnitudes and different axes of WTR and ATR defocus on ocular parameters were consistently found in a relatively large number of birds, suggesting a complex neural mechanism that integrates the optical properties of astigmatic error signal in regulating early eye growth. There were also substantial differences at the anterior and posterior ocular segments depending on the axis of astigmatic blur. These results provide important foundation work on myopic-astigmatic development in an excellent animal model for eye research and open the possibility to test the effectiveness of different optical interventions on astigmatic eye growth. 2nd paper: Vyas SA, Lakshmanan Y, Chan HH, Leung TW and Kee CS (2022). Experimentally induced myopia and myopic astigmatism alter retinal electrophysiology in chickens. Sci Rep 12(1): 21180. The foundation works established by 1st paper above showed that myopia and myopic astigmatism were associated with abnormal ocular structural changes in both anterior and posterior segments, the 2nd published paper here reported on how these common refractive errors alter retinal functions – the primary station in the signaling pathway controlling eye growth. This study adopted the established experimental protocol in 1st paper to induce myopia and myopic-astigmatism in chickens, and investigated the influence of these abnormal refractive development on retinal electrophysiology by using a novel image-guided, multifocal global flash stimulation. Three treated groups wore spherical or sphero-cylindrical lenses (fixed magnitude with different axes) monocularly and an aged-matched control group without any lens treatment provided normal data. Multifocal electrophysiological results revealed significant regional variation in the amplitude of induced component in the normal and hyperopic-ATR (H-ATR) groups, but not in the hyperopic and hyperopic-WTR (H-WTR) groups. Most importantly, for the first time, our results showed that both H-WTR and H-ATR groups exhibited a significantly longer implicit time at the central retinal region when compared to the normal and hyperopic groups, highlighting a significant role of astigmatism in retinal physiology during abnormal ametropic development. Using this novel methodological approach, our findings suggest a significant role of astigmatic properties in signal processing pathway within the central retinal region. Because early eye growth mechanism is regulated by retinal signaling pathway, our results highlight the importance of understanding the characteristics of astigmatic defocus during normal and abnormal refractive development. In summary, the two objectives proposed in this project were successfully completed and results reported in internationally accessible journals. The foundation works on the operational properties of the mechanism regulating eye growth in the presence of astigmatism provide a new way to study astigmatism development in a widely used animal model. This established protocols to study the retinal signaling pathways on astigmatic eye growth can guide the development of ophthalmic interventions for controlling this highly prevalent refractive error.

15100418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15100418.value: There are two major findings in this project: 1. The magnitude and axis of astigmatism clearly have an influence in the signaling pathway to direct early refractive development. The vision-dependent eye growth mechanism takes these astigmatic properties into account to regulate early eye growth in chicks. In this project, two astigmatic magnitudes (4DC and 8DC) and 4 axes (0, 45, 90, 135) were combined with both hyperopic and myopic defocus; ocular biometric parameters including refractions, corneal shape, and axial ocular components were investigated and the results compared with spherical defocus alone as well as age-matched normal birds. Our results extended the current understanding on the influential role of astigmatic properties, even mixed with spherical defocus, in early eye growth. The differential effects of astigmatic subtypes on anterior and posterior ocular components have significant clinical implications and should be followed up. 2. Retinal signal processing pathway in the central region shows differential responses in chicks developing different astigmatic subtypes (With-The-Rule vs. Against-The-Rule astigmatism). Animals with astigmatism also demonstrated significantly longer processing time in the inner retinal layer. These results support the use of chicks as a cost-effective animal model in understanding the retinal neural mechanism regulating astigmatic eye growth.

15100418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15100418.value: 1. Biometric changes (refractive, corneal, and axial) in response to astigmatic development provide strong foundation for further investigations into the mechanism regulating early eye growth at micro-structural and molecular levels. Compared to ocular parametric changes in response to spherical defocus alone, the ocular changes under astigmatic blur show a larger intersubject variability but the “open-loop” conditions similar to form-deprived high-myopia development did not occur. Our results add to yet another advantage of using chicks as an excellent animal model to predict/control refractive development in response to environmental risk factors. 2. The impacts of astigmatic subtypes on early refractive development should be followed-up closely. Specifically, the clinical impacts of early With-The-Rule and Against-The-Rule astigmatism on later myopia development have been documented in literature but the exact mechanism remains elusive. Our results from chicks suggest that the early signaling pathway at the retinal level is affected by astigmatic errors and is region specific. While the new approach in this project allowed region-specific analysis, the extend of the visual field tested was limited to the mid-peripheral region only. Extending the analysis to far peripheral region, where natural off-axis astigmatism dominates, awaits technological advancement and further investigations.

15100418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15100418.value: Astigmatism has been associated with myopia progression in humans but how the astigmatic properties interfere with refractive development received little attention. Building on our earlier findings in chicks as an animal model for early eye growth, this project investigated how WTR and ATR astigmatism, the two most frequently observed forms of astigmatism in clinical practice, influenced the structural and functional properties during ametropic development. Objective 1 showed that both the axis and magnitude of astigmatism can interfere myopia and hyperopia development using a relatively large sample size. Objective 2 further showed that the induced myopic-astigmatic eye exhibited altered retinal electrophysiology at the central region. Understanding the pattern of change in essential biometric parameters during the course of astigmatic development is crucial in formulating clinical interventions. Our results significantly advanced current understanding of the impacts of early astigmatism on ametropia progression and provide ground-breaking information for follow-up experiments at the structural and molecular levels.

15102118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15102118.value: Primary liver cancer is a leading cause of cancer related deaths in Hong Kong and worldwide. Liver metastases from solid malignancies (such as colorectal cancer, one of the commonest cancers in Hong Kong) are a primary cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality. The role of radiation therapy for liver cancer (including primary and metastatic liver tumors) has been limited due to radiation-induced liver disease. Respiratory motion is a major obstacle to achieving more effective radiation therapy for liver cancer. It is critically important to manage respiratory motion in radiotherapy of liver cancer. If not properly managed, respiratory motion can lead to significant treatment errors. This becomes especially crucial in stereotactic body radiation therapy, a modern radiotherapy technology that can precisely deliver radiation treatment using a much higher radiation dose (10 times higher) than conventional radiotherapy, because improper respiratory motion management can lead to mistreatment in a much greater degree than in conventional radiotherapy. Four-dimensional (4D) imaging plays a key role in radiotherapy of mobile tumors. The current clinical standard of 4D imaging is 4D computed tomography (4D-CT). However, 4D-CT does not show tumor clearly in the abdomen due to the low soft-tissue contrast of CT, indicating there is a need of better 4D imaging techniques for imaging liver cancer. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is known for its superior tumor and soft-tissue contrast compared to CT. It is therefore highly desirable to develop 4D-MRI technique for imaging liver cancer motion for radiotherapy. It is expected that 4D-MRI can provide more accurate and reliable results in measurements of mobile liver tumor volumes for radiotherapy than 4D-CT. The present study aims to develop a new methodology for generating ultra-quality 4D-MRI images, and to evaluate its clinical efficacy in radiotherapy planning of liver cancer. The ultra-quality 4D-MRI images are featured with high tumor contrast, high spatiotemporal resolutions, and minimal motion artifacts. We will achieve this goal by optimizing and logically synergizing a number of novel image processing and reconstruction methods that we have recently developed. Once fully developed, the 4D-MRI methodology will allow us to better visualize liver tumor and its respiratory motion. 15102118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15102118.value: Current 4D-MRI techniques are limited by insufficient image quality and long acquisition times or require specially designed sequences or hardware that are not available in the clinic, which greatly hinders the clinical implementation of 4D-MRI. We developed a fast ultra-quality 4D-MRI (UQ-4D-MRI) method based on a commercial low-resolution 4D-MRI sequence (lr-4D-MRI) and a novel dual-supervised deformation estimation model (DDEM). We tested the UQ 4D-MRI method in 39 liver tumor patients who underwent regular MR imaging for radiotherapy treatment planning. Results showed that our UQ-4D-MRI method based on DDEM successfully generated clinically implementable multi-parametric high quality 4D-MRI. The UQ-4D-MRI yielded small tumor tracking errors: 0.79 ± 0.65, 0.50 ± 0.55, and 0.51 ± 0.58 mm in the superior–inferior, anterior–posterior, and mid–lateral directions, respectively. As compared to lr-4D-MRI, the UQ-4D-MRI significantly improved the tumor contrast-to-noise ratio from 7.25 ± 4.89 to 18.86 ± 15.81. We further validated the UQ 4D-MRI method in a separate patient cohort with 12 patients with upper GI (5 liver, 5 pancreatic and 2 abdominal) tumors, diaphragm motion estimated from UQ 4D-MRI and lr-4D-MRI was compared. Furthermore, tumor internal target volume (ITV) defined based on UQ-4D-MRI was compared with those contoured based on conventional CT/MR simulation images. In this study, excessive motion artifact in 1 patient failed UQ-4D-MRI reconstruction. In other 11 patients, diaphragm motion profiles measured by UQ- and lr-4D-MRI matched well (absolute differences 2.06 ± 1.76 mm). ITV volumes contoured on UQ-4D-MRI were smaller than 3D-MRI but largely different than those drawn on 4D-CT. Overall, these results showed that UQ-4D-MRI with flexibility in image contrast was successfully deployed in our clinical practice. It significantly improved image quality compared with that of commercial 4D-MRI and yielded accurate tumor motion measurements with a fast processing time. The UQ-4D-MRI method also has advantages over other current 4D-MRI methods, which often produce images with compromised quality, have limited image contrast choices, and are sensitive to field inhomogeneity. The UQ-4D-MRI method improves physician’s confidence in target motion assessment and tumor volume delineation for radiotherapy, offering the potential to reduce safety margin in upper GI cancer patients, and holding great promises for improving liver tumor motion management during radiation therapy.

15102118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102118.value: The current study has only included T1w and T2w MRI for UQ-4D-MRI, our method can be further extended to multiple types of image contrast if corresponding 3D MR images are provided. For example, diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MR can potentially facilitate the localization of liver tumors and metastases. In future research, we can enroll patients with DWI and DCE images, to further verify the generalizability of our method. In future study, we will further improve the temporal resolution of UQ-4D-MRI. Currently, the acquisition time of conventional 4D-MRI is 0.69 s per frame to achieve good image quality, which yields around six frames per typical respiratory cycle (~4 s). In the future, we will further reduce the acquisition time of the original commercial 4D-MRI scans to improve the temporal resolution. Furthermore, the UQ-4D-MRI method will benefit from more validation and testing for its wide clinical implementation. In future studies, we will use digital human phantoms to comprehensively and thoroughly evaluate the robustness and accuracy of our proposed method. We will also enroll more patients at other hospitals that use different scanning protocols to further evaluate the generalizability of our method.

15102118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102118.value: Respiratory motion is a main source of targeting uncertainty in cancer radiotherapy, especially in the thorax and abdomen. Accurate assessment and management of tumor motion helps define an accurate target volume to deliver precise radiation dose to the tumor and minimize radiation toxicity to the surrounding normal tissues. This project developed and clinically evaluated a novel, ultra-quality four-dimensional magnetic resonance imaging (UQ-4D-MRI) method for imaging moving tumors in radiotherapy. Compared to current methods, the UQ-4D-MRI method offers significantly improved image quality, versatile image contrasts, accurate tumor motion trajectories, and faster processing time. The use of MRI in radiotherapy has been steadily increasing in the past decade, and will likely to accelerate in the next decade. It is clear that MRI will lead to a paradigm shift in radiotherapy in the near future. The UQ-4D-MRI may play an essential role in this paradigm shifting process. It will lead to true MRI-based precision radiotherapy for abdominal cancers, as well as many new developments and applications using 4D-MRI such as response assessment and functional guided treatment planning. Ultimately, the UQ-4D-MRI will improve dose conformity and advance precision radiotherapy by reducing geometric uncertainties in target identification, motion-induced geographic misses, and inter-fractional changes.

15103118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103118.value: The longitudinal cohort study showed that the bone strength on the paretic distal radius continues to deteriorate in people with chronic stroke, primarily as a result of declined cortical bone thickness and volumetric BMD (vBMD). A lesser decline in failure load (indicator of bone strength) over the 2-year follow-up period was predicted by better baseline hand sensation and better vascular health as indicated by a larger blood flow volume. Therefore, vascular health and sensory function can be potential targets for future intervention studies aimed at improving upper extremity bone health in people with chronic stroke. Similar to distal radius, we found that even for individuals who had regained independent walking during chronic stroke stage, decline in bone strength still occurred in the distal tibia on the paretic side during the follow-up period and was mainly attributable to a decrease in cortical vBMD, trabecular vBMD and cortical thickness. The modifiable clinical factors that were identified as significant predictors of the decline of tibia strength included lower limb vascular health, walking velocity, muscle strength, and physical activity level. Future intervention studies are recommended to target these outcome measures to improve lower limb bone health for chronic stroke.

15103118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103118.value: Better baseline vascular health are useful predictors of better bone outcomes in the distal radius, while better lower limb vascular health, walking velocity, muscle strength, and greater physical activity level are predictors of less decline in bone strength of the distal tibia. We plan to formulate an intervention study to examine the effects of cardiovascular and mobility exercises on bone properties in people with stroke.

15103118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103118.value: Secondary hemi-osteoporosis is one of the health issues experienced by stroke survivors that is often overlooked in both research and clinical practice. The risk of fragility fractures becomes higher when bone health is compromised, especially in a population with compromised balance function. Considering the adverse impact of post-stroke fractures to its survivors, their caregivers and the society, there is great need to conduct research on post-stroke bone health. Before establishing effective intervention program to alleviate the bone loss post stroke, knowing the specific targets is crucial. Thus, the aim of the current thesis project was to know how the bone characteristic changes after stroke and what are the modifiable clinical variables that influence bone health in people with stroke. We found that bone strength of the distal radius and tibia on the affected limbs continue to deteriorate during a 2-year follow-up period in individuals with chronic stroke. The useful predictors of better bone outcomes at follow-up are better vascular health and muscle strength, higher walking velocity and greater physical activity level. These findings have important implications because they provide insights into the possible targets of intervention to improve bone health post-stroke.

15103418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103418.value: Liver is an important metabolic and immunologic organ constantly receiving nutrients and microbiota antigens from the gut. Its metabolic function mainly accomplished by hepatocytes which make up about 80% of the liver mass. Liver also contains numerous immune cells specialized in capturing pathogens from circulation and protect the host from antigenic overload by facilitating immunologic tolerance. Tissue-infiltrating immune cells have been shown to also regulate metabolic functions through the actions of their secreted cytokines in various metabolic organs such as adipose tissues. Similar mechanism of metabolic regulation in liver has been described, however, a large gap remains in the understanding how intrahepatic B cells regulate liver metabolic homeostasis to be filled. Based on the recent findings by our team and others, we hypothesize that intrahepatic B cells produce cytokines to regulate the expression of hepatic genes required for glucose and lipid metabolism in response to nutrient availability. The population and subset of intrahepatic B cells as well as their cytokines production are altered in obese subjects in ways to cope with the extra nutrients. To test our hypothesis: In objective 1, we propose fully document the changes in intrahepatic B cells subsets and their cytokine profiles in obese mice and to dissect the mechanism of B cell recruitment to liver. In objective 2, we will explore the crosstalk between B cells and hepatocytes in maintaining liver metabolic homeostasis by providing compelling evidence to show the importance of the cytokines secreted from intrahepatic B cells in regulating hepatocyte gene expression. In objective 3, we will investigate the role of the B cell receptor signalling pathway in the regulation of intrahepatic B cells function in response to high-fat diet and fasting conditions. Given that chronic inflammation promotes the progression of fatty liver and liver cancer, the proposed research will provide a complete picture of the importance of intrahepatic B cells in liver metabolic homeostasis. In addition, B cells targeted therapy is being increasingly used in the management of leukaemia and autoimmune diseases, e.g. systemic lupus erythematosus and type 1 diabetes. 15103418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103418.value: The key findings are: 1. Intrahepatic B cells are the main source of anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-10 (IL-10) to reduce liver inflammation and hepatic steatosis in HFD fed mice. 2. HFD treatment did not change the intrahepatic B cell population but increased the expression of STAP1 in intrahepatic B cells. 3. The induction of STAP1 expression is required to provide energy for B cells to production cytokines and antibodies, especially under stimulations. 4. Knockout STAP1 in mice increased circulating cholesterol and triglyceride levels as compared with their WT littermates under standard chow feeding, and overexpressing STAP1 in B cells improves lipid metabolism and protects against high-fat diet-induced glucose intolerance in mice. 5. Knockout STAP1 in mice also decreased antibody production as compared with their WT littermates after vaccination. 6. Knockout or knockdown STAP1 in B cells lowered their oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR). In contrast, overexpressing STAP1 could induce OCR and ECAR in B. 7. Mechanically, STAP1 binds to mitochondrial chaperone prohibitins (PHBs) that increases mitochondrial respiration to meet the energy demands for cytokine and antibody productions. 8. As prohibitins bind to the major mitochondrial phospholipid cardiolipid and we developed unbiased lipidomic analysis using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry imaging to reveal the changes of lipid composition and distribution in liver. The method is very successful for kidney but not sensitive enough to check the changes of lipid composition and distribution in the micro-environment of intrahepatic B cells. Please find the attached manuscript under preparation for the key data mentioned above. As recent publication “Dual roles of B lymphocytes in mouse models of NAFLD” in Hepatology 2022 demonstrated that B lymphocytes have both detrimental and protective effects in HFD-induced NAFLD. The lack of secreted pathogenic antibodies protects partially from NAFLD, whereas the presence of certain B cell subsets provides additional protection. IL-10-producing regulatory B cells may represent such a protective B cell subset by the restricted B cell function IgMi and a complete lack of B cells JHT mice. There is some overlapping with our study in term of their IgMi and JHT mice with much obvious effects then using antibodies to deplete B cells in mice in our study. Therefore, for the manuscript, we focus on the discuss of the linking B cell metabolism to immune regulation by STAP1 with our STAP1 KO and B cell specific overexpressing in B cell mice.

15103418.value: 1. We plan to reinvestigate possibility of STAP1 be a causative gene for familial hypercholesterolemia and other lipid dys-homeostasis. In addition to polymorphism, we will also check the expression level of STAP1 in B cells of the patients. 2. Data reported in the literature suggest that many factors, including age and gender, can be associated with differences in immune responses to vaccines. We plan to explore whether STAP1 can be act as potential immunogenetic factor to predict host responses to vaccination. 3. As overexpressing STAP1 can increase the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) in non-STAP1 expressing cells such as HEK293 cells (data not shown). 15103418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103418.value: Vaccination is one of the most successful and sustainable tactics to prevent and counteract disease-causing pathogens affecting human health. Vaccines prime our immune system to recognise these pathogens in advance by imitating an infection. However, vaccine performance varies significantly between individuals, both in terms of safety and efficacy. In my study, I explored the novel function of an immune cell-specific gene STAP1 in antibody and cytokine production by B cells via metabolism reprogramming. In brief, knockout of STAP1 in B cells reduced antibody production after vaccination. On the other hand, STAP1 is suggested to be the fourth causative gene for familial hypercholesterolemia, but the mechanism is not yet defined. My study has revealed a molecular mechanism that explains the protective role of STAP1 against hyperlipidemia by enhancing B cell production of IL-10, an anti-inflammatory cytokine. Collectively, my work has shed initial light on the elucidation of a missing link between immunity and energy metabolism through the expression of STAP1 in B cells. Novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for B cell-related immunometabolic diseases can be designed by targeting STAP1. Furthermore, STAP1 may be exploited as a marker for predicting vaccine efficacy.

15104218.label: Project Objectives
15104218.value: In this proposed study, we aim to elucidate the mechanisms underlying enhanced intramacrophage survivability of hypervirulent M. tuberculosis clinical strains. There are four objectives: i) To identify genetic mutations that are specific to hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strains using whole-genome sequencing; ii) To snapshot the transcriptomes from hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strains and control strains of the same phylogenetic lineage during macrophage challenge using RNA-seq technology; iii) To unveil the co-expressed gene networks associated with the mutations specific to hypervirulent M. tuberculosis using a novel structural co-expression analysis; and iv) To validate the role of the genetic mutations in dysregulated expression profiles and enhanced intramacrophage growth by knock-in mutant construction or gene overexpression.

There are four objectives: i) To identify genetic mutations that are specific to hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strains using whole-genome sequencing;
ii) To snapshot the transcriptomes from hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strains and control strains of the same phylogenetic lineage during macrophage challenge using RNA-seq technology;
iii) To unveil the co-expressed gene networks associated with the mutations specific to hypervirulent M. tuberculosis using a novel structural co-expression analysis; and
iv) To validate the role of the genetic mutations in dysregulated expression profiles and enhanced intramacrophage growth by knock-in mutant construction or gene overexpression.

15104218.label: Realisation of objectives
15104218.value: Objective 1 Whole-genome sequencing were done for the hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strain, named as H112 (Beijing Lineage 2.2.1), and its low-virulent comparator strain, named as H54, using PacBio Single Molecule Real-Time (SMRT) sequencing platform. The run yielded high-quality (quality score > 0.8) reads, with sub-reads N-50 value greater than 10Kb. Fully closed circular genomes assembled into a single contig with an average sequencing depth of ~150X were obtained for both M. tuberculosis strains. Sequencing data revealed that there were 139 SNPs and 45 Indels present in H112 only. These genetic mutations were then used to screen all of the published genomes of M. tuberculosis of L2 lineage (n=384). Our search identified that 33 strains collected from 13 countries also harboured at least one of these mutations. WGS-based phylogeny found that four hypervirulent strains of L2 lineage isolated from different countries were clustered together and formed a novel phylogenetic clade (known as H112-clade). All hypervirulent strains in the clade shared 12 SNPs and 3 SVs. The close relationship between these highly virulent strains implied that genetic factors common to them are more likely to contribute to their hypervirulence. The SIFT algorithm were used to predict the effect of nonsynonymous SNPs on protein function. Notably, a SNP, D30E, located in higB, a transcriptional regulator of iron uptake pathway, was found to be deleterious. In addition, a 2-bp deletion was found in intergenic region rv0759c-rv0760c, which was identified to be a binding target for a sigma factor, Sigma F, a putative regulator of phoP. PhoP is a global transcriptional regulator of lipid metabolism and hypoxic response and controls the expression of ~2% of the genes in M. tuberculosis. A previous study showed that phoP upregulation was capable of restoring the virulence in H37Ra during macrophage infection. We hypothesized that these mutations could modulate the expressions of the transcriptional regulators, leading to a massive change in the downstream expression profile and contributing to the hypervirulence. The objective 1 has been fully achieved. Objective 2 and 3 In order to investigate how the hypervirulent-specific mutations may alter the expression profile of M. tuberculosis during macrophage infection, the expression profile of H112 and H54 during macrophage challenge were characterized using RNA-seq with Illumina HiSeq platform. Three biological replicates have been done in this study. The RNA sequencing runs yielded on average 33.71 million high quality (>Q30) reads, of which, 87.15% mapped uniquely to the reference genome M. tuberculosis H37Rv (NC_000962.3). Overall, the sequencing result was consistent between replicates as indicated by close clustering of the replicates in hierarchical clustering and principal-component-analysis (PCA). The clustering analysis also uncovered that the genetic mutations between the strains were important factors in shaping the transcriptional profiles of the studied strains. Pairwise comparison of the DESeq2 normalized read-counts per gene between strain H112 and strain H54 revealed that there were 493 differentially abundant transcripts (false-discovery-rate [FDR] lower than 5%) between the two strains. Notably, eight of fifteen genes that harboured hypervirulent-specific mutations were significantly differentially expressed, including higB, fadE5, Rv3371, pip, Rv0480c, Rv0633c, Rv0178 and Rv0760c. Structural co-expression analysis algorithm showed that the up-regulation of higB led to universal repression of at least 8 genes that are responsible for iron acquisition in M. tuberculosis. Moreover, phoP which is next to rv0759c-rv0760c intergenic deletion, was also upregulated in H112. Notably, the expression of various key reporter genes regulated by phop were greatly suppressed, including those encoded for sulfolipid and polyacyltrehaloses. Strain H112 harboured a hypervirulent-specific mutation (D150E) in Rv0178, which constitutes the mce1 opeon with 8 addition upstream genes. All the transcripts of the mce1 operon were shown to be under-expressed (median of log2 fold changes for all genes = > −0.72) in H112. The results demonstrated that the mutations switched on certain co-expressed gene networks specific to H112. Genomic sequencing identified 1S6110 insertion in pip gene of strain H112. Consistent with the genomic data, the entire transcripts for rocA-rv1188, encoding proline utilization pathway, were also under-expressed in H112. Our study revealed that at least 4 hypervirulent-specific mutations could lead to dysregulation in expression of a network of genes associated with mycobacterial virulence. This is particularly important when selecting the candidate mutations from a pool of genetic variants obtained from WGS for further functional validation. Objectives 2 and 3 have been achieved completely. Objective 4 To validate the causative roles of these mutations in enhanced intra-macrophage survivability, strain H112 was complemented with wildtype higB, phop, pip and Rv0178 genes. In briefly, the wildtype genes were cloned to a tetracycline (Tc)-inducible expression vector pUV15tetORM. The ligated plasmids were introduced into H112 by electroporation. As confirmed by RT-qPCR, the expression level of the transformed genes was evelated when the concentration of tetracycline was increased from 2ng/mL to 128ng/mL. The expression level of all the five genes were found to be comparable to H54 (i.e. wildtype level) when tetracycline concentration was at 60 ng/mL. The transformants were then challenged with the THP-1 macrophage. The results showed that overexpression of wildtype higB and phop genes in strain H112 significantly impaired intra-macrophage growth. The growth index of the parent strain H112 and H37Rv were increased by 2.5 and 1.4 fold, whereas the phop and higB transformants were reduced by 0.45 and 0.8 fold, after 10-day of macrophage infection. The pip and Rv0178 transformants showed no signficant difference in growth index when compared to H112 parent strain, indicating that the genetic variation of these genes have no impact on intra-macrophage surivial. The finding demonstrated that the SNP D30E in higB and 2-bp deletion in rv0759c-rv0760c (regulator of Phop) are responsible for enhanced intracellular survivability in macrophages. The study unveiled the virulence mechanisms of M. tuberculosis during the early stages of infection. Objective 4 has been achieved completely.

15104218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104218.value: Major findings We demonstrated that a hypervirulent strain isolated from cerebral spinal fluid exhibited significantly better intracellular survivability than the reference virulent strain H37Rv and 124 other clinical isolates in human macrophages. Comparative whole-genome sequencing identified 12 SNPs and 3 indels which were commonly shared by strain H112 and other hypervirulent strains isolated from various countries. Among these mutations, a deleterious SNP, D30E, located in higB and a 2bp deletion in the intergenic region rv0759c-rv0760c are of interest. higB is a transcriptional regulator of the iron uptake pathway, which is essential for intracellular survival. rv0759crv0760c is a binding target for a sigma factor, Sigma F, a putative regulator of phoP (21). PhoP is a global transcriptional regulator of lipid metabolism and hypoxic response and controls the expression of ~2% of the genes in M. tuberculosis. The expression profile of H112 and H54 during macrophage challenge were characterized using RNA-seq. A total of 493 genes were differentially expressed in H112 when compared to H54. Eight of fifteen genes that harboured hypervirulent-specific SNPs were significantly differentially expressed, including higB. The up-regulation of higB led to universal repression of at least 8 genes that are responsible for iron acquisition in M. tuberculosis. Moreover, phoP, which is next to rv0759c-rv0760c intergenic deletion, was also up-regulated in H112. Notably, the expression of various key reporter genes regulated by phop were greatly suppressed, including those encoded for sulfolipid and polyacyltrehaloses. To validate the causative roles of these mutations in enhanced intra-macrophage survivability, whildtype higB and phop were overexpressed in strain H112. The overexpressed mutants were then challenged with the THP-1 macrophage. The results clearly showed that the overexpression of higB and phop had signifcantly reduced macrophage survival compared with the parent strain H112 and H37Rv. The study showed that the SNP D30E in higB and 2-bp deletion in rv0759c-rv0760c are responsible for enhanced intracellular survivability in macrophages, it explained the virulence mechanisms of M. tuberculosis during the early stages of infection. Research Outcome Two research articles were published in peer-reviewed journals. The first paper is to report our findings on multi-omic analysis and to highlight the mutations that are likely to cause the dysregulation in RNA expression of a network of genes associated with mycobacterial virulence. The second paper is to identify a anti-virulence agent for TB by screening repurposed small molecules that can suppress the expression of phop gene in using a lux-based promoter-reporter platform.

15104218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104218.value: The present study identified the causative role of genetic mutations that account for enhanced intra-marcophage survivial of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolated from patients with TB meningitis. It explained the virulence mechanisms of M. tuberculosis during the early stages of infection. How these factors facilitate the subsequent development of tuberculous meningitis inside the host is still unknown. Therefore, we proposed a follow-up study to investigate if these mutations are responsible for the genetic mechanisms underlying the neurotropism of the hypervirulent M. tuberculosis strains using a multiple fluorescent zebrafish infection model. The study was funded by RGC (GRF#15102220). It has been well-known that antibiotic resistance is the major challenge for TB treatment. The spread of drug resistant and hypervirulent MTB raises the need for innovative therapeutic strategies to restrict bacterial resistance. Anti-virulence therapy is a promising approach that focuses on disarming bacterial virulence factors that facilitate disease development instead of killing the bacteria. Notably, development of anti-virulence drugs requires an in-depth understanding of the roles that diverse virulence factors have in disease processes. Therefore, our findings in this study serve as the knowledge basis for the development of new anti-virulence drugs against TB. The proposed study was also funded by RGC (GRF#15102220).

15104218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104218.value: Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading cause of death among infectious diseases. Certain Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains are reported to preferentially invade the central nervous system, thus earning the label “hypervirulent strains”. Our previous study demonstrated that these strains had better survivability inside human macrophage. In this study, we used multi-omic (i.e. genomic and transcriptomic) analysis to identify genetic mutations that are (i) specific to hypervirulent strains only and (ii) can cause dysregulation of RNA expression in a network of genes associated with virulence in M. tuberculosis. As a result, two genes, namely higB and phop were selected for functional validation. Overexpression of wildtype higB and phoP in hypervirulent strain successfully impaired the intra-macrophage survival and restored inhibitory growth as wildtype strain. These mutations could be used as epidemiological markers for the rapid tracing of infections with M. tuberculosis strains of high-level infectivity, facilitating better infection control and patient management. In addition, our finding also serves as the knowledge basis for the development of new anti-virulence drugs against TB.

15104418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104418.value: 肥大细胞是人体内一类重要的免疫细胞，其主要功能是进行免疫调节。肥大细胞能释放多种免疫活性介质，如组胺，促进血管通透性增强，介导炎症反应。肥大细胞参与多种人类病理生理过程，其中研究最透彻的是其在过敏发生发展中的促进作用。肥大细胞可以分成两大亚类，结缔组织肥大细胞（Connective Tissue Mast Cell, CTMC）和粘膜组织肥大细胞（Mucosal Mast Cell, MMC）。前人研究发现CTMC的体内存活时间远较MMC长，但其机制不明。我们已知CTMC表面表达两种IgG受体，即FcgammaRIIB和FcgammaRIIIA，而MMC表面只表达一种IgG受体即FcgammaRIIB。本课题组的研究工作表明，体外培养的CTMC能抵抗IgG免疫复合物作用后导致的细胞凋亡（凋亡为一种细胞自我控制的有计划的死亡过程），其抵抗机制即因其表达两种IgG受体。若利用基因工程方法让CTMC失去任何一种受体，仅表达一种受体的CTMC将对IgG免疫复合物介导的凋亡敏感。MMC本身只表达一种IgG受体，所以MMC可被IgG免疫复合物刺激后导致细胞凋亡。本研究基于上述观察，提出体内肥大细胞的存活周期也是受Fcgamma受体和IgG免疫复合物的相互作用而导致的细胞凋亡的调控。本研究拟选用小鼠模型，开展一系列体内和体外实验，来验证该假说。本研究属于肥大细胞生物学的基础研究，其结果将进一步丰富我们对肥大细胞寿命和存活机制的了解，有助于未来以诱导肥大细胞凋亡的思路设计过敏类疾病（比如过敏性哮喘）的预防及治疗措施。

15104418.label: Realisation of objectives
15104418.value: Rodent mast cells can be divided into two major subtypes: the mucosal mast cell (MMC) and connective tissue mast cell (CTMC). It was reported back in the 1980s that connective tissue mast cells (CTMC) have a longer life span compared with mucosal mast cells (MMC) in rodents, a phenomenon that still lacks proper mechanistic explanation. The precise mechanisms underlying such differential tissue persistence of mast cell subsets had never been described prior to our research. In this study, we have discovered that mast cells expressing only one receptor, either FcgRIIB or FcgRIIIA, underwent caspase-independent apoptosis in response to IgG immune complex treatment (Objective 1). Lower frequencies of CTMC in mice that lacked either FcgRIIB or FcgRIIIA compared with wild-type mice were recorded, especially in aged mice. We proposed that this paradigm of FcgR-mediated mast cell apoptosis could account for the more robust persistence of CTMC, which express both FcgRIIB and FcgRIIIA, than MMC, which express only FcgRIIB. Importantly, we reproduced these results using a mast cell engraftment model, which ruled out possible confounding effects of mast cell recruitment or FcgR expression by other cells on mast cell number regulation. In conclusion, our work has uncovered an FcgR-dependent mast cell number regulation paradigm that might provide a mechanistic explanation for the long-observed differential mast cell subset persistence in tissues (Objective 2).

15104418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104418.value: In this study, our data support an FcR-mediated mast cell apoptosis as a mechanistic account for the long-observed differential tissue persistence of CTMC and MMC. However, we have not provided direct evidence demonstrating that constitutive IgG immune complex-mediated crosslinking of FcgR, which is assumed to result in cell death, is a critical regulatory machinery underlying mast cell persistence. Transfer of congenically marked FcgRIIB-deficient and FcgRIIIA-deficient BMMC into B cell-deficient mice, which do not have IgG immune complexes, may possibly reveal whether the IgG immune complex-FcgR axis is fundamentally required for the regulation of mast cell tissue persistence. This engraftment model can also reveal whether any FcgR-dependent, but IgG immune complex-independent, mechanisms might also play a role in regulating mast cell tissue persistence.

15104418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104418.value: Specialized immune cells called mast cells are important effector cells in allergic pathology as these cells can secrete allergic mediators such as histamine. Mast cells can be divided into two major subtypes: mucosal mast cells (MMC) and connective tissue mast cells (CTMC). While the exact functionality of these two mast cell subtypes has not been fully contrasted, an interesting observation was made at least five decades ago which revealed that rodent CTMC have a longer lifespan (tissue persistence) than MMC. The mechanism accounting for this differential tissue persistence had not been explained prior to our study. In the current project supported by RGC, we have provided solid experimental evidence confirming that crosslinking of a particular cell surface receptor called FcgRIIB by antibody complexes can induce mast cell death. This finding can explain the vulnerability of MMC to cell death induction in the tissues. Although CTMC also express FcgRIIB, these cells also express another molecule called FcgRIIIA, which counteracts the cell death-inducing effect of FcgRIIB. Our study may have expanded our knowledge base about mast cell biology, which has implications for the future development of therapeutic strategies for treating allergic disorders.
