15104618.label: Realisation of objectives
15104618.value: 1. To functionally characterize the role of UBE2T in the regulation of liver T-ICs (100%) i. To study the effects of EPHB2 modulation on the T-IC phenotypes We performed UBE2T-knockdown and UBE2T-overexpression experiments using a lentivirus-based approach. We found high expression of UBE2T in a panel of HCC cell lines, including MHCC-97L and PLC/PRF/5; therefore, these two cell lines were chosen for the knockdown experiment, while Huh7 cells were chosen for the overexpression experiment due to relatively low UBE2T expression. Knockdown of UBE2T reduced the spheroid-forming ability of both PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells, while UBE2T overexpression was shown to enhance the spheroid-forming ability of Huh7 cells. In both PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells, knockdown of UBE2T reduced the size and number of tumors formed. Conversely, UBE2T overexpression in Huh7 cells significantly enhanced tumorigenicity, with an increase in the estimated CSC frequency. Accompanied with the above changes, suppression of UBE2T reduced the percentages of CD47-, CD133- and CD90-positive PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells, while UBE2T-overexpressing Huh7 cells exhibited increases in the percentages of these markers. ii. To study the effects of UBE2T modulation on HCC metastasis and drug resistance We explored the effect of UBE2T alteration on the chemoresistance of HCC cells. Knockdown of UBE2T enhanced the cell death of HCC cells upon doxorubicin treatment. Similar findings were observed in shUBE2T cells in response to sorafenib and lenvatinib treatments. Next, we investigated whether the role of UBE2T in sorafenib resistance is clinically relevant by analyzing 30 HCC patients who received prior sorafenib treatment in TCGA-LIHC dataset. Consistently, patients with high UBE2T expression were correlated with shorter overall survival (p=0.0299, log rank test). Transwell assays showed that UBE2T knockdown decreased the migration and invasion abilities of PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells, while UBE2T overexpression exerted the opposite. To further confirm whether UBE2T promotes metastatic potential in vivo, an orthotopic HCC xenograft model was employed in which luciferase-labeled MHCC-97L cells derived from shUBE2T and corresponding control cells were directly implanted into the left lobe of the liver. When compared with control tumors, we found that UBE2T-repressed MHCC-97L cells exhibited a drastic reduction in tumor volume, as well as lung metastasis in this orthotopic HCC xenograft model. 2. To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which UBE2T functionally contributes to tumor initiation, self-renewal, and drug resistance. (100%) i. To study UBE2T-mediated regulation of HUWE1 via ubiquitination By tandem affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry (TAP-MS), we identified Mcl-1 ubiquitin ligase E3 (Mule; also known as HUWE1, ARF-BP1 or HectH9) with a size of ~ 480 kDa and 3 unique peptide sequences that have been recognized by mass spectrometry analysis. We confirmed the interaction between UBE2T and Mule by reciprocal immunoprecipitation. Interestingly, we found that UBE2T not only binds to Mule but also directly regulates Mule expression by ubiquitination. By Western blot analysis, UBE2T expression was found to be inversely correlated with Mule upon overexpression and suppression of UBE2T. Treatment with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 restored the expression of Mule in UBE2T-overexpressing Huh7 cells, indicating that UBE2T controls the protein level of Mule by proteasomal degradation. Further co-localization between UBE2T and Mule was observed with the presence of MG132. To further demonstrate whether UBE2T mediates the degradation of Mule by ubiquitination, a vector harboring UBE2T with defective E2 activity (UBE2T C86A mutant) was constructed by substituting cysteine at the 86th active site with alanine by site-directed mutagenesis. Impaired ubiquitination of Myc-DDK-tagged UBE2T was observed in the C86A mutant compared to the wild-type UBE2T due to diminished E2 activity. Western blot analysis showed that the C86A mutation significantly reversed the suppressive effect of UBE2T overexpression on Mule in Huh7 cells. Furthermore, the regulatory role of UBE2T on Mule via ubiquitination was examined by ubiquitination assay. Finally, we found that UBE2T regulated Mule degradation specifically through K48-linked ubiquitination. ii. To study the effects of UBE2T/HUWE1 on ubiquitination and activity of β-catenin We first examined the effect of Mule suppression on the expression of β-catenin in Huh7 cells. ShMule Huh7 cells showed an increase in β-catenin expression compared with control cells. Knockdown of UBE2T was found to stabilize Mule, which led to a concomitant decrease in β-catenin expression in both PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells. IF staining revealed less cytoplasmic and nuclear β-catenin protein expression in shUBE2T PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells than in control cells. Western blot analysis showed that the expression of β-catenin protein was increased in UBE2T OE Huh7 cells, and this effect was abolished in UBE2T-C86A-expressing counterparts. This result was further confirmed by IF staining. Furthermore, the TOP/FOP reporter assay showed that the transactivation ability of β-catenin was suppressed when UBE2T was repressed, while its activity was elevated in UBE2T-overexpressing cells. iii. To evaluate β-catenin as the downstream effector of UBE2T-mediated CSC function To confirm the regulatory role of UBE2T on β-catenin in vivo, the role of UBE2T in regulating β-catenin expression in human HCC clinical samples was explored by correlating UBE2T and β-catenin protein expression by IHC staining. We showed correlation between UBE2T and β-catenin expression in a cohort of 51 HCC samples (p<0. 001, Fisher’s exact test). Addition of CHIR99021, a GSK3β inhibitor, restored the inhibitory effects of UBE2T knockdown on sphere formation and expression of liver CSC markers. This result demonstrated that UBE2T may regulate liver CSC function, at least in part through the β-catenin signaling cascade. 3. To evaluate the clinical relevance of UBE2T expression and its correlation with liver T-ICs in human HCC. (100%) In the analysis of another dataset (GSE25097), UBE2T was significantly upregulated in tumor specimens from normal to cirrhotic to tumor tissues in a stepwise manner, suggesting an oncogenic role for UBE2T in liver carcinogenesis. In addition, the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data analysis of 442 HCC patients showed that patients with high UBE2T expression (above the median level) had poorer overall survival (p = 0.0016, log rank test) and disease-free survival (p = 0.0013, log rank test) than patients with low UBE2T expression. To further validate the results, we evaluated UBE2T mRNA expression in a cohort of 82 patients via qPCR analysis. 91% (75/82) of the patients showed >2-fold upregulation of UBE2T mRNA levels, while 55% (45/82) of the patients showed >8-fold upregulation in HCC samples compared to normal samples. Statistical analysis by SPSS software revealed that higher expression of UBE2T was associated with larger tumor size (p = 0.023), venous invasion (p = 0.049), and advanced tumor stage (p = 0.045). Consistently, UBE2T was found to be overexpressed at the protein level by IHC staining and Western blot analysis. Collectively, these results provide solid evidence that UBE2T is upregulated in liver CSCs and has clinical significance in HCC. 15104618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104618.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is one of the deadliest diseases and is the 4th leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Treatment modalities of HCC commonly include surgical resection, transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), chemotherapy, and molecularly targeted drugs2. However, the survival benefits are modest, attributed to frequent tumor recurrence and the development of chemoresistance. Compelling evidence has emerged in support of the vast contribution of cancer stem cells (CSCs; also known as tumor-initiating cells, T-ICs) to the poor survival of cancer patients as they promote chemoresistance, tumorigenicity and metastasis. Therefore, it is critical to identify new therapeutic targets against CSCs for the benefit of HCC patients. Identification of critical molecules/pathways involved in the regulation of liver CSCs may prolong the survival of HCC patients. In this study, we have employed an integrative analysis of publicly available datasets involving HCC clinical and stemness-related data to select genes and identified ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 T (UBE2T) was drastically upregulated and activated in self-renewing HCC cells compared to control cells. However, the molecular mechanism by which UBE2T regulates stemness properties is poorly understood. Whether UBE2T regulates liver CSCs also remains unexplored. First, we found that overexpression of UBE2T at both the mRNA and protein levels was associated with advanced tumor stages and poor patient survival. UBE2T was found to regulate the phenotypes of liver CSCs, including self-renewal, drug resistance, tumorigenicity and metastasis. By tandem affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry, we identified Mcl-1 ubiquitin ligase E3 (Mule) as the direct binding partner of UBE2T, which regulates ubiquitination of β-catenin. Our study identified a novel noncanonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascade mediated by the UBE2T/Mule complex. Our findings are scientifically important and clinically relevant and will definitely appeal to the readership in different scientific research field. Our finding will convey several important messages to the readers: (1) UBE2T is strikingly increased during liver carcinogenesis and correlated with aggressive tumor phenotypes and patients’ survival; (2) UBE2T plays a crucial role in regulation of liver CSCs; (3) Mule, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, was first identified to be the direct protein binding partner of UBE2T; (4) we first identified the non-canonical role of UBE2T which directly mediate ubiquitination of substrate; (5) the interplay of UBE2T and Mule was found to be critically involved in the regulation of the noncanonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascade. Our data suggest that targeting Targeting the UBE2T/Mule/β-catenin signaling cascade is a new potential therapeutic approach for HCC.

15104618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104618.value: Although the role of UBE2T in regulation of liver T-ICs has been suggested, the exact mechanism of how UBE2T mediates this effect is unknown. In this study, we provide solid evidence of how UBE2T regulates liver T-ICs via direct regulation of mule-mediated beta-catenin regulation This information provides a useful mechanistic insight for the role of UBE2T in regulation of cancer stemness and drug resistance in HCC. Based on this interesting finding, it is of great interest to determine the combination effect of UBE2T inhibitor and targeted therapies for potential treatment of HCC patients at advanced stages. Thus far, the use of specific inhibitor against UBE2T is limited in commercial market. Based on the 3D crystal structure of UBE2T and its interaction with UBE2T, I am currently collaborating with Dr. Ma Cong (ABCT, PolyU) and synthesized several UBE2T specific inhibitors. We have synthesized different compounds and now testing their in vitro therapeutic efficacies against HCC cells. Ultimately, we would like to synthesize the novel UBE2T inhibitor with high specificity and hope to translate the results generated in this grant proposal.

15104618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104618.value: Liver cancer (HCC) is the fifth most common cancer worldwide. The 5 year-survival for this disease is not satisfactory due to tumor relapse and refractory to the current targeted therapy including sorafenib. Therefore, it is of great importance to identify the factors leading to these tumor behaviors. Recently, cancer stem cells (CSCs) are regarded as the root of tumor relapse and therapeutic resistance. Thus, targeting these cells may be a novel therapeutic strategy against HCC. In the current proposal, In the current proposal, findings presented in this study not only provide evidence to show the clinical relevance of and functional role of ubiquitin conjugating enzyme E2 T (UBE2T) in liver cancer but also demonstrated its pivotal role and mechanistic action in regulation of liver CSCs and resistance to chemotherapy and targeted therapies. Specifically, UBE2T regulates the liver CSCs and drug resistance by turning on Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, a well-known pathway in stem cells through direct interaction of Mule protein. Targeting a novel UBE2T/Mule/β-catenin signaling cascade provides an attractive potential therapeutic target for HCC.

15105618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15105618.value: 視網膜色素變性（RP）是由基因突變引起的視網膜光感受器功能障礙和死亡的眼科疾病。全世界每3000人中就有1人因光感受器的死亡導致部分或完全失明。遺憾的是，光感受器死亡的機制目前尚未完全了解。目前也尚無有效的方法可以治療人類視網膜色素變性。我們研究小組和世界其他研究小組已證實慢性神經炎症可惡化視網膜色素變性的進程。然而，引發神經炎症的機制尚不清楚。 CD33是一種結合唾液酸的免疫球蛋白凝集素。腦中小膠質細胞特異性表達CD33。據報導，CD33可抑制小膠質細胞的吞噬功能，刺激促炎細胞因子的產生，導致阿爾茨海默病中的異常神經炎症。該研究結果證明了CD33在調節神經炎症中的重要作用。在我們的初步研究中，我們也發現CD33在rd10視網膜色素變性小鼠模型中的小膠質細胞的表達顯著增加。不過，CD33在視網膜色素變性中的具體功能仍不清楚。 我們的實驗假設是CD33參與調節RP中的小膠質細胞吞噬作用。抑制 CD33可以增強小膠質細胞的吞噬活性，抑制神經炎症和減輕RP疾病。為了檢驗我們的假設，我們用siRNA在rd10小鼠中敲除CD33基因。我們發現CD33基因敲除後，導致神經炎症顯著減少，並促進了rd10視網膜中的光感受器存活。我們計劃用CD33基因缺失的小鼠與rd10小鼠雜交，來研究CD33基因缺失對小膠質細胞吞噬作用，促炎細胞因子的產生和光感受器存活和功能的影響。此外，我們將闡明在視網膜rd10中CD33失活的保護作用的機制。我們也將研究CD33失活是否有效恢復TREM2 / DAP12信號介導的小膠質細胞吞噬活性。 該研究對理解CD33在RP發病過程中的作用具有重要意義。了解CD33在RP中的功能可以幫助我們開發以CD33抑制為中心的一種新型的治療視網膜變性的方法。

15105618.label: Realisation of objectives
15105618.value: In this project, we investigated our hypothesis that CD33 was associated with microglial phagocytosis in RP, and that CD33 inhibition enhanced the phagocytic activity of microglia, suppressed damage-induced neuroinflammation, and subsequently mitigated the disease. We examined the expression and cellular localization of CD33 in the rd10 mouse model of RP using immunohistochemistry, qPCR and ELISA. We observed upregulation of CD33 expression at both mRNA and protein levels in rd10 mice at postnatal 19 (P19), P22 and P25. To identify the cellular localization of CD33, we performed immunohistochemistry using a CD33-specific antibody and Iba1, a microglial marker. We found that CD33 signal colocalized with Iba1-lablled microglial cells, and that CD33-positive microglia were significantly increased in rd10 retinas relative to WT controls. To confirm whether CD33 was upregulated in microglia, we backcrossed transgenic CX3CR1GFP/GFP mice, in which microglia are fluorescently labeled after replacing the Cx3cr1 gene with the gene encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), with rd10 mice and generated a new line of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice, and performed qPCR in sorted primary microglia from rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP by using flow cytometry. Indeed, qPCR analysis confirmed upregulation of CD33 transcripts in microglia of CX3CR1+/GFP/rd10 mouse retinas relative to those in CX3CR1+/GFP WT retinas. Together, our data demonstrated CD33 upregulation in microglia of the rd10 retina, suggesting the possible involvement of CD33 in regulating neuroinflammation in the rd10 retina. To confirm the functional role of CD33, we backcrossed CD33 knockout mice (CD33-/-) onto rd10 background and investigated the effect of CD33 deletion on microglia phagocytic activity, production of inflammatory cytokines and photoreceptor survival and function in the resulting mouse line (CD33-/-/rd10) at several time points (P19, P25 and P30). To study whether CD33 knockout reduced microglia activation, we stained rd10 retinas with antibodies against Iba1 and CD68, a marker for microglia activation. We found that CD68 immunoreactivity was reduced in the rd10 retina with CD33 knockout in comparison with rd10 control retinas. Consistently, western blot analysis confirmed the results from immunohistochemistry. To examine the effect of CD33 knockout on microglial proliferation, we did intraperitoneal BrdU injection before animal sacrifice. We found a reduction in the proliferation of microglia to the photoreceptor cell layer of rd10 retinas after CD33 knockout. By using qPCR and ELISA, we observed downregulation of inflammatory mediators including tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) in the rd10 retina, which confirmed a significant reduction in neuroinflammation after CD33 knockdown. Similarly, we purified microglial cells from CD33-/-/rd10 mouse retinas using FACS and verified the lower RNA expression levels of CD33, TNF-α and IL-1β in microglial cells after CD33 knockdown by qPCR. Taken together, our results showed suppression of microglia activation and alleviation of neuroinflammation in rd10 mice after CD33 knockdown, suggesting that CD33 is an important regulator of microglia activation states in RP. We then investigated the effect of CD33 knockout on photoreceptor survival and function. Rods occupy about 97% of photoreceptor nuclei in the outer nuclear layer (ONL) of the mouse retina. Therefore, we measured the ONL thickness in retinal vertical sections for rod survival. We found a higher number of nuclear rows in the ONL revealed by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining in P25 CD33-/-/rd10 mouse retinas than in age-matched rd10 control retinas. The similar trend was observed at P30 between CD33-/-/rd10 retinas and rd10 control retinas, indicating the preservation of rods after CD33 deletion. For the assessment of cone survival, we stained cones using an antibody against red/green opsin for quantification of cone density at P30 and P40. we observed much higher cone densities in P30 and P40 CD33-/-/rd10 mice than those in age-matched rd10 retinas, indicating the preservation of cones after CD33 deletion. Together, our data demonstrated the morphological preservation of rod and cone photoreceptors in the rd10 retina with CD33 deletion. We next assessed the effect of CD33 deletion on photoreceptor function by measuring electroretinography (ERG) and optomotor responses on CD33-/-/rd10 mice. We observed markedly greater amplitudes of scotopic a-waves and b-waves on P25 and P30 CD33-/-/rd10 mice relative to age-matched rd10 controls. Similarly, higher photopic ERG b-wave amplitudes were recorded on CD33-/-/rd10 mice at the two time points in comparison with age-matched rd10 controls. Our data suggested that CD33 deletion preserved photoreceptor function in rd10 mice. Together, our data confirmed the pathological role of CD33. Moreover, we elucidated the mechanisms underlying the protective effects of CD33 inactivation in the rd10 retina. To examine whether CD33 deficiency affected microglial phagocytosis, we cultured primary microglia and CD33-deficient microglia and assessed phagocytic activity. Primary microglia were collected from retinas using FACS from rd10/CX3CR1GFP/+ mice and CD33-/-/rd10/CX3CR1GFP/+ mice and were incubated with fluorescent bio-particles at 37°C for 2 hours. Microglial phagocytosis was imaged on an epifluorescence microscope and the internalization of fluorescent beads by phagocytosis were scored. We found that CD33-deficient microglial cells uptook more fluorescent microspheres than microglial cell controls. The percentage of phagocytic cells after CD33 deficiency was significantly higher than microglial cell controls. These results suggest that microglial phagocytic function was impaired in rd10 retinas, which may subsequently impact the capacity of microglia to clear tissue debris in the retina. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is specifically expressed by microglia. TREM2 couples with the signal transduction partner DAP12 for its signalling function. TREM2/DAP12 signalling on microglia is found to facilitate phagocytosis of cell debris and clear the degenerative environment. CD33 and TREM2/DAP12 signalling have opposing effects on microglial phagocytosis. We thus investigated whether CD33 inactivation restored effective TREM2/DAP12 signaling-mediated phagocytic activity. To this end, we investigated whether CD33 inactivation upregulated the expression of TREM2/DAP12 signalling in the CD33-/-/rd10 retina at P16, P19 and P21 using a combination of immunohistochemistry, qPCR and western blot analysis. Three different approaches consistently confirmed that CD33 inactivation upregulated the expression of TREM2/DAP12 signalling, indicating the potential restoration of effective TREM2/DAP12 signalling-mediated phagocytic activity of microglia. Additionally, we examined whether CD33 inhibition promoted a unique subtype of disease-associated microglia (DAM) with phagocytic activity. Previous study demonstrates that microglia with a DAM signature are CD11c positive, which has been used as a DAM marker for enriching the DAM population from the brain. Similarly, we isolated CD11c- positive microglia from rd10 mice and CD33-/-/rd10 mice at P16, P19, and P21 and gated positive for CD45 and CD11c. We calculated the percentage of CD11c-positive microglia over total CD45 microglia. Interestingly, we observed a higher percentage of CD11c-positive microglia in CD33-/-/rd10 mice than rd10 mice at all three time points. To further confirm and quantify DAM, we labelled sorted CD11c-positive microglia with two DAM-specific markers: tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases and lipoprotein lipase. We found that CD11c-positive microglia were positive for both tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases or lipoprotein lipase, indicating that CD11c-positive microglia in the CD33-/-/rd10 retina were DAM. Taken together, we demonstrated that CD33 is a key regulator in proinflammatory cytokine-driven signaling pathways in RP, and that CD33 deficiency resulted in a skewing of activated microglial cells towards DAM activation, which trigger secretion of anti-inflammatory cytokines, and neurotrophic factors, and promoted a strong phagocytic activity by upregulating the TREM2/DAP12 signalling in the rd10 retina. Targeting CD33 may be a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating neuroinflammation and photoreceptor degeneration in RP. Manuscript from this project is currently under preparation.

15105618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15105618.value: In this project, we investigated our hypothesis that CD33 was associated with microglial phagocytosis in RP, and that CD33 inhibition enhanced the phagocytic activity of microglia, suppressed damage-induced neuroinflammation, and subsequently mitigated the disease. We examined the expression and cellular localization of CD33 in the rd10 mouse model of RP and found that CD33 upregulation in microglia during photoreceptor degeneration in the rd10 retina. To confirm the functional role of CD33 in the rd10 retina, we investigated the effect of CD33 deletion on microglia phagocytic activity, production of inflammatory cytokines and photoreceptor survival and function in the rd10 retina. We observed downregulation of inflammatory mediators including tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) in the rd10 retina after CD33 knockout, suggesting suppression of microglia activation and alleviation of neuroinflammation in rd10 mice after CD33 knockdown. Additionally, we observed a reduction in microglia proliferation to the photoreceptor cell layer of rd10 retinas after CD33 knockout. Together, our data suggest that CD33 is an important regulator of microglia activation states in RP. Moreover, we assessed the effect of CD33 deletion on photoreceptor survival and function by measuring electroretinography (ERG) and optomotor responses on CD33-/-/rd10 mice. We found that CD33 deletion led to morphological and functional preservation of rod and cone photoreceptors in the rd10 retina, indicating microglial neurotoxicity mediated by CD33. Furthermore, we elucidated the mechanisms underlying the protective effects of CD33 inactivation in the rd10 retina. We found that that CD33 upregulation impaired microglial phagocytic function through downregulating the TREM2/DAP12 signalling, which facilitates phagocytosis of cell debris and clear the degenerative environment, in rd10 retinas. Conversely, CD33 inactivation restored effective TREM2/DAP12 signalling-mediated phagocytic activity of microglia, which subsequently improved the capacity of microglia to clear tissue debris in the rd10 retina. Additionally, we found that CD33 deletion promoted a unique subtype of disease-associated microglia (DAM) with phagocytic activity and stimulates secretion of both anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors to combat the disease.

15105618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15105618.value: Based on the findings from this project on the functional role of CD33 in regulating neuroinflammation and photoreceptor degeneration in RP, we have expanded our research to further investigate the mechanisms underlying CD33 activity in the rd10 retina. We have preformed proteomic analysis using the Liquid Chromatograph Triple Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (LC-MS/MS) to detect differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between rd10 retinas and CD33-/-/rd10 retinas. LC-MS/MS demonstrated significant changes in proteins related to retinal degeneration, inflammatory response, synthesis of ROS, and phagocytosis in the rd10 background. More importantly, we identified the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) as a potential downstream effector of CD33 signaling in regulating microglial neurotoxicity. Moreover, we observed that some microglial cells express a high level of CD33, while the other microglial cells express a very low level of CD33 in the rd10 retina, indicating potential heterogeneity of microglia and their differential roles in the rd10 retina. To explore further on the issue, we have applied single-cell gene expression profiling to reveal subtype of disease-associated microglia (DAM) in the rd10 retina and to identify unique subtypes of DAM with accelerating development of RP. Further investigations of these multiple microglia subsets may lead to novel therapeutic approaches to treat RP pathology.

15105618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15105618.value: Neuroinflammation plays a pathological role in photoreceptor death in RP. However, the mechanisms underlying the chronic neuroinflammation in RP are poorly understood. The transmembrane protein CD33 is specifically expressed in microglia and regulates innate immunity in the brain. However, the functional role of CD33 in regulating inflammation in RP remains unknown. In this project, we observed CD33 upregulation in microglia during photoreceptor degeneration in the rd10 retina. After CD33 knockout, we found suppression of neuroinflammation and preservation of photoreceptor survival and function in the rd10 retina. Our data suggest that CD33 is an important regulator of microglia activation and neurotoxicity in RP. Mechanically, we demonstrated that that CD33 impaired microglial phagocytic function through downregulating the TREM2/DAP12 signalling in the rd10 retina. Additionally, we found that CD33 deletion promoted a unique subtype of disease-associated microglia with phagocytic activity and stimulates secretion of both anti-inflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors to combat the disease. In summary, a better understanding of the microglial regulator CD33 action in RP might lead to the development of a novel therapeutic approach centered around CD33 inhibition for the prevention and treatment of this devastating disease.

15106018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106018.value: This project will investigate the pathogenesis of myopia (short-sightedness) — one of the leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide. It is estimated that nearly half of the global population may be myopic by 2050, of whom 10% will be highly myopic. At present, myopia is commonly managed by optical correction of vision only. With limited understanding of the underlying pathogenesis, emerging treatments, such as defocus incorporated lenses or atropine eye drops are far from 100% effective or free from undesirable side effects. With an increasing prevalence of myopia in the adult and aged populations of Hong Kong and China, a high incidence of myopia-associated complications are anticipated in the near future, leading to enormous losses in productivity and increasing rehabilitation costs to the society. Therefore, there is an urgent need for research to unravel the mechanism of myopia development and to devise improved preventative and therapeutic approaches for its management. The present study will examine the mechanism by which the retina processes visual information to modulate ocular growth. Recent studies have shown that myopic eye growth may be accelerated or decelerated by several optical (e.g. defocus or bright light) or pharmacologic interventions (e.g. atropine). Increasing evidence suggests that the effects of these interventions are associate with a transcription factor termed Early Growth Response (EGR1). Despite the fact that EGR1 may play a central role in myopia development, the exact identity of EGR1 expressing neurons remains unknown. We hypothesize that these neurons are the key players in the retinal circuitry that processes visual information for modulating myopia. To test the hypotheses, we will investigate the physiology, morphology, and neurochemistry of EGR1 neurons using whole-cell patch clamping, confocal microscopy, and immunohistochemistry, respectively. The project will take technological advantage of visualizing the EGR1 neurons by genetically tagging with green florescence. Our pilot data indicated that EGR1 is selectively expressed in subsets of amacrine cells.Some of the subtypes, of which there are at least four, responded to myopia promoting/inhibiting optical or pharmacological interventions by down-regulating EGR1 expression or altered electrical responses. It is expected that a full-scale study will reveal the location and cellular identity of the myopia-specific retinal circuit. The results will advance knowledge of the mechanisms of myopia development helping to provide a basis for developing novel therapeutics that could potentially benefit many people. 該項目將調查近視的發病機制 - 深近視是全球不可逆視力喪失的主要原因之一。據估計，到2050年，將近一半的全球人口可能會患近視，其中10％將是高度近視。目前，近視通常僅通過光學矯正視力來管理。由於對潛在發病機理的理解有限，最近的治療方法，例如散焦眼鏡或阿托品滴眼液遠非100％有效，或伴隨有不良副作用。隨著近視在香港和中國成年人和老年人群中的近視患病率增加，預計近視相關併發症在不久的將來會大幅增加，導致社會生產力的損失和康復成本的增加。因此，迫切需要進行研究以揭示近視發展的機制並改進其預防和治療方法。 本研究將探討視網膜處理視覺信息以調節眼睛生長的機制。最近的研究表明，近視眼生長速度可以通過幾種光學（例如散焦或亮光）或藥理學干預（例如阿托品）。越來越多的證據表明，這些干預措施的效果與稱為早期生長反應1（EGR1）的轉錄因子有關。儘管EGR1在近視發展中起核心作用，但表達EGR1的神經元的確切身份仍然未知。我們假設這些神經元是視網膜電路中的關鍵參與者，其處理視覺信息以調節近視。 為了驗證這些假設，我們將分別使用全細胞膜片鉗，共聚焦顯微鏡和免疫組織化學來研究EGR1神經元的生理學，形態學和神經化學。該項目將利用綠色熒光基因標記可視化EGR1神經元的技術。我們的試驗數據表明EGR1在無長突細胞亞群中選擇性表達。其中一些亞型通過下調EGR1表達或改變電生理來響應光學或藥理學干預。預計該項目研究將揭示與近視有關的視網膜電路的位置和其細胞特徵。該結果將推進對近視發展機制的了解，為開發新療法提供基礎。

15106018.label: Realisation of objectives
15106018.value: All the objectives have been achieved. Animal preparation. Transgenic EGR1-eGFP +/- mice were obtained from the Jackson Laboratory and backcrossed with C57BI/6J mice for more than 5 generations. Genotyping was performed to ensure the presence of the desired GFP gene and the absence of rd1 and rd8 mutation in the offspring. EGR1-eGFP +/+ mice of both genders at 4 weeks of age were subsequently used in our experiments. Optical interventions. To apply optical diffusers and -30D lens onto mice eyes, we have crafted -30D and diffuser lenses in our lab and 3D printed spectacle frames and mounting system specifically for the mice. The mounting system blueprint was a gift from a research group in Keio University in Japan, as a result of new collaboration. To control light-dark cycle without being affected by ambient illumination, a dedicated cabinet is made for housing animals under controlled experimental lighting conditions including brightness, flickering frequency, on-off cycle etc. Immunohistochemistry and confocal microscopy. We aim to study the neurochemistry of EGR1 expressing cells. More specifically, we tested whether there would be double labeling of the GFP+ cells with a list of known biomarkers for amacrine cells, transporters, receptors, and synapses. We have tested more than 30 primary antibodies for amacrine cells including tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), calretinin, ChAT, neuropeptide Y, neuropeptide vasoactive intestinal peptide, serotonin, enzyme nitric oxide synthesis (NOS), expressed in some GABAergic cells., parvalbumin, Fam81a, SNAT, glycine transporters and connexin. After primary antibody staining, whole-mount retinae or sections were stained free floating in PBS buffer system at 4℃ for overnight for donkey oriented secondary antibody staining conjugated with Dy405 (1:200), AF488 (1:500), AF546 (1:400) and AF647 (1:400) and chemical dye DAPI (1:4000, Abcam, Cambridge, United Kingdom). After that, the specimens were mounted on glass slides where the distribution pattern and density of those dual labelled cells on flat-mounted retina were characterized using a confocal microscope (Carl Zeiss, LSM800, Thornwood, NY, USA) in tile-scan mode. Cells of interest was further imaged from 60-µm vertical sections separately prepared using a vibratome (Carl Zeiss VT1200S) to obtain higher resolution images, z-stacks, and 3D morphology when indicated. qPCR. RNAs were converted to cDNA using a PrimeScript RT reagent kit with gDNA Eraser (Takara Bio). qPCR was performed using the PowerUp Sybr Green Master Mix (Thermo Fisher Scientific) on QuantStudio 3 Real-Time PCR stems (Applied Biosystems). Gapdh was used as the normalizing control. Generalized linear models (GLM), which can capture stimulus-dependent changes in real neurons with spike timing precision and reliability, were used to predict RGCs responses to focused and defocused images in the retinas of wild-type (normal) and Lens-Induced Myopia (LIM) mice. As the predominant subunit of gap junctions in the mouse retina and a plausible modulator in myopia development, Cx36 knockout (KO) mice were used as a control for an intact retinal circuit. Selected findings. We found that about 15-20% of EGR1+ amacrine cells in the inner nuclear layer co-express TH. In contrast, TH-expressing retinal amacrine cells always co-express EGR1. Interestingly, while NOS+ cells and EGR+ cells are mutually exclusive, NOS+ cells are often found to be conjugated to EGR-TH expressing cells. Judging from the morphology, it is highly likely that they are electrically coupled through gap junctions such as connexins (e.g. Cx36). Although EGR1, dopamine, and NOS have been separately reported to modulate ocular growth signals, our results is the first to describe the linkage between these pathways. The presence of EGR1+ / TH- amacrine cells indicated that EGR1 may not solely be “switching on” the dopaminergic amacrine cells, but the possibility of a EGR1-dopamine-EGR1 looped feedback. Dopaminergic amacrine cells are known to receive synaptic inputs from photoreceptors and ipRGC and response to a wide range of illumination. The electrical synapse between TH and NOS amacrine cells suggests that NOS amacrine cells are possibly the downstream target of the dopaminergic cell which in turn modulates VEGF, MAPK and provide feedback on EGR1 though a EGR1-dopamine-NOS-VEGF-MAPK-EGR1 axis. In addition, we also compared retinal tissues harvested at different time points of the light-dark cycle and found the expression pattern of EGR+ cells being consistent across samples. In light of the above findings, we have shortlisted a number of drug candidates to be tested. Eventually, two drugs that acts on the above axis were found to be effective in inhibiting experimental myopia in animal model. The first drug is latanoprost, which is a prostaglandin that is commonly used to treat glaucoma clinically through lowering intraocular pressure. We found that latanoprost eye drop substantially inhibited form deprivation myopia and lens induced myopia in a chicken model. The result was presented at the ARVO conference in 2022. The second drug is binimetinib, which is an inhibitor of Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase Kinase (MAP2K). Our data demonstrated that intravitreal injection of Binimetinib effectively suppressed lens-induced myopia and suggested that the MAPK pathway is a pharmacologically viable molecular targets to alter ocular growth, implying its potential for treating myopia. We are applying for a patent application on the drug and the molecular target. We found that the kinetics of excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) of a single αRGC could reflect projection of both focused and defocused images in the retinas of normal and LIM, but not in the Cx36 knockout mice. Moreover, Poisson GLMs revealed that encoding of visual stimuli in the LIM retina was similar to that of the normal retina. In the LIM retinas, the linear-Gaussian GLM model with offset was a better fit for predicting the spike count under a focused image than the defocused image. Furthermore, Akaike information criterion (AIC) indicated that nonparametric GLM (np-GLM) model predicted focused/defocused images better in both LIM and normal retinas. However, the spike counts in 33% of αRGCs in LIM retinas were better fitted by exponential GLM (exp-GLM) under defocus, compared to only 13% αRGCs in normal retinas. A difference in encoding performance between LIM and normal retinas indicated the possible amendment and plasticity of the retinal circuit in myopic retinas. The absence of a similar response between Cx36 KO mice and normal/LIM mice might suggest that Cx36, which is associated with myopia development, plays a role in encoding focused and defocused images. We also found that the lipogenic transcription factor sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2) transcriptionally represses low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 2 (Lrp2), which has been shown to restrict eye overgrowth. Furthermore, bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) is the downstream effector of Srebp2 and Lrp2 which is suppressed by SREBP2 transcriptionally but activated by Lrp2. During normal postnatal development, SREBP2 protein expression decreases whereas that of Lrp2 and Bmp2 increases as the eye growth rate reduces. Collectively, our data suggested that Bmp2 is the key determinant of eye size such that its level inversely correlates with eye size. Remarks Due to the social unrest and COVID-19 in Hong Kong, research laboratories and offices of research personnel were inaccessible for research personnel for a prolonged period. Research activities were officially suspended. Furthermore, more than half of the EGR1-eGFP mice died because the central animal facility was understaffed when the PolyU campus was under complete lockdown in Nov and Dec 2019. Unfortunately, the above events have substantially hindered the progress of the present project.

15106018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15106018.value: Translational studies. Our project filled important gaps in the literature by suggesting a signaling pathway comprised of new molecular targets for modulating ocular growth. Candidates such as MAPK, Cx36, and EGR1 are promising targets that warranty further investigation. Among this direction, we have tested and shown that latanoprost and binimetinib are effective in inhibiting experimental myopia in animal models. Lataoprost as an approved drug for glaucoma, has the potential to be repurposed for treating myopia following appropriate clinical testing. Binimetinib and its derivative is a novel drug for ophthalmic application and will need to go through formulation and toxicology testing. Mechanistic studies. Our findings highlighted the central role of dopaminergic amacrine cells in modulating myopic eye growth. It is known that dopaminergic amacrine cells received synaptic inputs from photoreceptors and ipRGC. However, its detailed receptive field and optical tuning property of remains unknown. Intuitively, it may contribute to the directional sensitivity to discern the sign of optical defocus. Therefore, further study by performing single-cell recording under patterned optical stimulus is warranted.

15106018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15106018.value: This research project aimed to understand how certain retinal cells and signalling molecules in the eyes may affect vision, specifically in relation to myopia, a condition that increases risks of vision-threatening diseases. The team used advanced techniques in immunohistochemistry, imaging, and molecular biology to study the effects of these cells and molecules in special mouse models. Additionally, the team made special lenses and frames for the mice to use in their experiments. The team found that early growth factor (EGR1) expressing cells, dopamine-secreting cells and nitrite oxide-secreting cells in the eyes form a signalling pathway that may be involved in the development of myopia. Moreover, the roles of gap junction and MAPK pathway are highlighted. This research may lead to the development of new pharmacological treatments for myopia and the associated vision-related conditions. The findings of this research project are significant because they contribute to our understanding how we can potentially prevent or treat myopia.

15106218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106218.value: 布氏錐蟲（Trypanosoma brucei，T. brucei）是一種原生動物寄生蟲。它可引起人類非洲錐蟲病（也稱為昏睡病）、大型動物的納加納病等傳染性疾病。晚期的非洲錐蟲病嚴重威脅生命健康, 然而目前暫未研製出抵抗此種疾病的疫苗。慢性感染引起的反復發作是非洲錐蟲病的治療難點。研究表明，T. brucei通過持續轉換錶面可變糖蛋白（Variable Surface Glycoproteins，VSGs）的單等位基因表達引發抗原變異，從而逃避宿主免疫系統的清除。目前，由VSG轉換引起的抗原變異的機制尚不清楚。 T. brucei端粒蛋白TbTRF和TbRap1是Shelterin複合物的主要組成部分。它們通過與端粒結合來維持端粒的穩定性。同時，兩者都具有調節VSG轉換的功能。我們的前期研究表明，TbTRF可以特異性結合雙鏈端粒TTAGGG重複序列，該DNA結合活性對於其調節VSG轉換的功能至關重要。而且我們的合作夥伴首次發現TbRap1是TbTRF共定位於端粒的結合因子，也是沉默VSG表達的關鍵調節因子。 含有端粒重複序列的RNA（Telomeric repeat-containing RNA，TERRA）是一種新發現的由端粒轉錄的長鏈非編碼RNA。研究表明TERRA具有端粒保護和染色質狀態調節的功能。我們假設TbTRF和TbRap1可以通過調控TERRA來發揮維持端粒結構、調節抗原變異的功能。對於TbTRF而言，我們猜測它可以與TERRA直接相互作用並幫助TERRA與端粒基因座連接，以便TERRA維持端粒穩定並抑制VSG轉換。對於TbRap1，我們認為它可能具有DNA / RNA結合活性，從而乾擾TERRA介導的端粒RNA:DNA雜交體的形成，從而保護端粒的完整性並減少VSG轉換。 為了驗證我們的假設，首先我們計劃進行一系列的體外實驗，以確定TbTRF和TERRA相互作用的區域以及TbRap1和DNA / RNA的結合區域。第二步，我們將分別對TbTRF-TERRA複合物和TbRap1-DNA / RNA複合物的結構進行表徵。為了進一步描述TbTRF和TbRap1對TERRA調控的分子機制，我們將與合作夥伴進行基於結構信息的功能研究，並評估TERRA對端粒穩態和VSG調節的影響。總而言之，我們的生化、結構和功能研究將有助於理解T. brucei中的TERRA調節機制，並為由這種寄生蟲引起的各類疾病提供新的治療思路。

15106218.label: Realisation of objectives
15106218.value: The project has progressed very well through the period of 1-1-2019 to 30-6-2022 with all objectives realized to 100%. We would like to report our activities and results obtained according to the four proposed objectives. Objective 1. Biochemical characterization of TERRA-binding activity in TbTRF, the duplex TTAGGG Repeat Binding Factor We carried out RNA immunoprecipitation (IP) experiments to test whether TbTRF associates with TERRA in vivo. We used IP to pull down endogenous TbTRF and subjected the pulldown lysate to slot blot hybridization using (CCCTAA)n probe to detect the presence of TERRA. Our results show that endogenous TbTRF pulled down detectable amount of TERRA but not the highly abundant ribosomal RNA (rRNA). These results suggest that TbTRF specifically associates with TERRA in vivo. We also conducted biochemical assays to characterize the TbTRF-TERRA interaction in vitro. Our EMSA results showed that full-length TbTRF “shifted” a 144 nt RNA transcript that contained 12 repeats of UUAGGG but not a same-length RNA with 12 repeats of CCCUAA. Additionally, we tested different constructs of TbTRF and confirmed that its Myb domain is required and sufficient for TERRA binding. Furthermore, we used competitive EMSA studies to confirm that the DNA- and TERRA-binding activities in the Myb domain act independently because TbTRF Myb could “shift” TERRA probes in presence of duplex TTAGGG repeats and vice versa. In summary, Objective 1 is 100% accomplished with the TERRA-binding activity of TbTRF confirmed both in vivo and in vitro. We also identified the TbTRF Myb domain as required and sufficient for TERRA binding. Furthermore, for TbTRF Myb domain, its duplex telomeric DNA binding activity and TERRA binding activity act independent of each other. Objective 2. Biochemical mapping of key regions responsible for DNA/RNA-binding in TbRap1, a TERRA suppressor and silencer of VSG expression To map the DNA/RNA-binding region(s) in TbRAP1, we proposed to focus on the middle region (aa500-765), which contains a long stretch of disordered region (aa500-633); a putative Myb-like domain (aa663-733); and a K/R-rich segment with clusters of Lys and Arg residues (aa734-761). We have generated over ten constructs covering various segments within this middle region and tested their DNA/RNA-binding activity by EMSA using various DNA/RNA probes. Our EMSA studies show that the K/R-rich segment “shifted” multiple DNA molecules, including the double-stranded (ds) DNA with 12 TTAGGG telomeric repeats, 100-nt dsDNA with random sequence and 100-nt single-stranded (ss) DNA with random sequence. These results suggest that the K/R-rich segment possesses an unusual DNA binding activity that is electrostatics-based and sequence-non-specific. We also carried out NMR studies of the putative Myb-like domain (aa 639-733) and confirmed that it is actually an RNA Recognition Module (RRM) despite low sequence similarity. We then carried out a series of biochemical assays to assess whether TbRAP1 RRM binds to TERRA and VSG mRNA, two dominant RNA species at telomere. Our fluorescent polarization results showed that TbRAP1 RRM interacted with both (UUAGGG)4, an oligo that represents TERRA; and 34-VSG-UTR, a 34-nt oligo representing the consensus sequence of VSG 3’ UTR. However, such interaction was of moderate affinity with Kd estimated to be of ~300-500 μM. In summary, Objective 2 is 100% accomplished. Our in vitro biochemical results confirm that the K/R-rich region of TbRAP1 possesses unusual DNA-binding activity that is based on electrostatics, sequence non-specific and length dependent. The RRM module of TbRAP1 binds telomeric RNA including TERRA and 34-VSG-UTR with moderate affinity. Objective 3. Structural study of TbTRF-TERRA and TbRap1-DNA/RNA interactions to delineate the molecular mechanism of their TERRA regulation We used NMR for our structural studies to delineate the molecular determinants of the TbTRF-TERRA and TbRap1-DNA/RNA interactions. For the TbTRF-TERRA interaction, we observed that the TbTRF Myb protein started to precipitate when increasing amount of TERRA RNA oligo was added. As a result, we couldn’t obtain reliable data to identify the TbTRF residues responsible for TERRA binding. We reason that TERRA may induce conformational changes in the TbTRF Myb domain that renders it structurally unstable. Thus, it may not be feasible to identify the key residues for the TbTRF-TERRA interaction in vitro. For the TbRAP1-DNA interaction, we observed that a collection of dsDNA and ssDNA substrates induced notable chemical shifts in the HSQC spectra of 15N-labeled TbRAP1 RRM+R/K-rich region (aa 639 – 761), most notably for positively charged residues K738 and R741 within the R/K patch (aa 737 – 741). Additionally, mutating the R/K-patch to Ala abolished these chemical shifts. For the TbRAP1-RNA interaction, we conducted similar NMR titration studies and found that only 34-VSG-UTR induced noticeable chemical shifts in the HSQC spectra of TbRAP1 RRM while (UUAGGG)4 failed to do so. This data suggests that 34-VSG-UTR is the preferred substrate for TbRAP1 RRM. Notably, 34-VSG-UTR induced significant concentration-dependent chemical shifts for residues located in the conserved RNP1 and RNP2 motifs of RRM, particularly F655 and F694. A few residues in the R/K-rich region also showed noticeable chemical shifts, although at much lower magnitudes. These results suggest that both the RRM module and the R/K-rich region interact with the 34-VSG-UTR, with RRM playing a major role. In summary, Objective 3 is 100% accomplished with the molecular determinants for the TbRap1-DNA/RNA interaction mapped to the K/R-rich region and the RRM module respectively. For the TbTRF-TERRA interaction, it seems that TbTRF Myb domain may undergo structural unfolding to associate with TERRA. Future studies are needed to investigate how such unfolding and TERRA association occurs in vivo and whether it is assisted by other telomeric proteins. Objective 4. Structure-based functional study to elucidate the significance of TERRA regulation by TbTRF and TbRap1 in telomere maintenance and VSG regulation In collaboration with Prof. Bibo Li, we carried out a series of structure-based functional studies to elucidate the significance of the TbRAP1-DNA/RNA interaction. Prof. Li’s lab have established a Cre-loxP-mediated conditional deletion system to remove one copy of the TbRAP1 allele by Cre and replace the other with designed mutants (TbRAP1-F/mut). To investigate the functional significance of the TbRAP1-DNA interaction, we generated mutant strains that deleted the R/K-rich patch (delRK) or replaced it with Ala (5A). Both mutant strains showed reduced telomere localization of TbRAP1, which led to growth arrest, more telomeric DNA damage and VSG de-repression. These results confirm that the TbRAP1-DNA interaction is essential for telomere integrity and VSG silencing. To delineate the molecular function of the TbRAP1-VSG interaction, we generated mutant strains that deleted the RRM region (delRRM) or mutated the conserved aromatic residues F655 and F694 (2FA, 2FQ, 2FL). Unexpectedly, all mutant strains showed ~50% reduction in the transcription level of the active VSG2 with concomitant de-repression of silent VSGs. This unique phenotype suggests that the TbRAP1-VSG interaction is critical for sustaining the high-level transcription of the single active VSG. Thus TbRAP1 plays a dual role in VSG regulation by sustaining the transcription of the active VSG while silencing the other VSGs. Overall, Objective 4 is 100% accomplished with two important mechanistic findings. First of all, the R/K-rich region of TbRap1 is responsible for its electrostatics-based DNA-binding activity. This activity is critical for the localization of TbRAP1 to telomere and for VSG silencing. Secondly, the RRM region of TbRAP1 binds to the consensus 3’ UTR sequence with moderate affinity. This RNA-binding activity is essential for sustaining the full-level transcription of active VSG to maintain its monoallelic expression.

15106218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15106218.value: During this project, we obtained two important findings regarding the DNA- and RNA-binding activities of TbRAP1. First of all, we find that the R/K-rich patch in TbRAP1 (737RKRRR741) has an unconventional DNA binding activity that binds to both single- and double-stranded DNA in electrostatics-based and sequence-non-specific manner. We show that this region is required for the association of TbRAP1 with the telomere chromatin, VSG silencing, telomere integrity, and normal cell growth. Mutations that replace the positively charged R/K residues with A substantially diminish TbRAP1’s dsDNA binding activity in vitro and abolish TbRAP1’s telomere localization in vivo. These mutations also cause VSG derepression, accumulate telomere/subtelomere DNA damage, and lead to cell growth arrest. Our results indicate that the unconventional dsDNA binding activity of TbRAP1 is essential for its telomere localization and VSG silencing. A manuscript reporting these findings have been published in Science Advances in 2020 (Part C, item 8[1]). Secondly, we carried out NMR studies of the putative Myb-like domain of TbRAP1 and made the unexpected finding that this domain was actually an RNA Recognition Motif (RRM). This finding is novel because no RAP1 homologs have been reported to have a RRM domain. Our biochemical and structural studies reveal that, assisted by the R/K-rich patch, TbRAP1 RRM binds the consensus sequence of VSG 3’UTR in vitro, while TbRAP1 binds the active VSG RNA in vivo. Mutations in the RRM domain that specifically abolish its RNA binding activity lead to an acute decrease in the active VSG RNA level by ~50% and subsequent derepression of all silent VSGs, thus disrupting both aspects of VSG monoallelic expression. A manuscript reporting these findings have been published in Nature Communications in 2023 (Part C, item 8[5]). Prof. Zhao (PI of this project) and Prof. Li (Collaborator of this project) were invited by the trypanosome community to write a review f to discuss the role of the Shelterin Complex in VSG regulation. This review article has been published in Pathogens (Part C, item 8[2]). Two more research output items, including one manuscript published in BBRC in 2022 (Part C, item 8[3]) and another manuscript published in BB Reports in 2023 (Part C, item 8[4]), are also included in this completion report because they benefited from resources provided by this project.

15106218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15106218.value: Our research team is interested in pursuing the following two initiatives in our future study. First of all, while we have shown that the unconventional DNA binding activity in TbRAP1 mediated by its K/R-rich region is required for localization to telomere, this TbRAP1-DNA interaction is electrostatics-based and thus not telomere-specific. We reason there are additional proteins that help to recruit TbRAP1 to telomere in specific manner. One possible candidate is TbTRF, which binds to telomeric DNA repeats and also has been shown to associate with TbRAP1. We plan to carry out biochemical and structural studies to delineate the molecular determinants of the TbTRF-TbRAP1 interaction. Secondly, while we have uncovered an unexpected RRM region in TbRAP1 and showed that it binds to the short consensus sequence in the 3’ UTR of VSG mRNA, we are keenly aware that TbRAP1 RRM may recognize multiple RNA sequences as this is a notable feature shared by many RRMs reported in the literature. We plan to conduct systematic screening using both rationally designed RNA oligos and a pool of random RNA sequences to identify the most preferred RNA sequences for TbRAP1 RRM.

15106218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15106218.value: Trypanosoma brucei is a protozoan parasite that causes human African trypanosomiasis. It evades host immune surveillance by regularly switching its major surface antigen, the Variant Surface Glycoproteins (VSG). From a genetic repertoire of ~2,000 genes and pseudogenes, only one VSG is monoallelically transcribed by RNA polymerase I from a subtelomeric expression site (ES) while the others are silences. The molecular mechanism of this process is poorly understood. Here our studies reveal that the telomeric protein TbRAP1 plays an essential role in VSG regulation through its novel DNA/RNA-binding activities. Our biochemical and structural studies show that TbRAP1 has an unconventional DNA binding activity mediated by a cluster of positively charged in the R/K-rich region. This DNA binding activity is critical for locating TbRAP1 to the telomere and for silencing VSG. We also uncovered an unexpected RNA Recognition Module (RRM) in TbRAP1, which allows TbRAP1 to bind to VSG mRNA. This RRM-mediated RNA binding activity is required to sustain the full-level expression of the single active VSG by competing against the silencing effect exerted by the R/K-mediated DNA binding activity. Our findings contribute to better understanding of VSG-mediated antigenic variation in T. brucei and help battle devastating diseases caused by this parasite.

15107118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15107118.value: Terahertz waves (0.1 THz ~ 10 THz) have attracted great interest with recent technological advances and are now the subject of interdisciplinary researches. A variety of applications have shown initial promise for their biomedical use, particularly in broadband Terahertz based imaging including noninvasive or intraoperative cancer imaging and skin and cornea hydration sensing. However, efforts to reveal the Terahertz-induced effects at cellular and molecular levels, especially how biological objects interact with Terahertz wave having specific frequency and intensity, is scarce and remains challenging. Recent progress in Terahertz spectroscopy have shown that many important biomolecules have intrinsic vibrational resonances in the Terahertz range, implicating that appropriate Terahertz irradiation may direct biochemical reactions and biological energy transport. In addition, mild inflammation response in mouse skin under Terahertz irradiation was reported recently, suggesting possibility of immune response mediated skin regeneration. In this project, we aim to investigate biological effects of Terahertz irradiation for skin regeneration and hair growth to develop a novel therapeutic technique for dermatological diseases. Hair loss, or alopecia, is a markedly increasing dermatological disease in aging society, involving an annual global market revenue of US$85 billion and a growth rate of 5%. Unfortunately, currently available therapeutic drugs such as Minoxidil and Finasteride have either low efficacy or significant adverse effects. Focusing on capability of Terahertz wave for nonionizing local irradiation and deep penetration to cover a whole hair follicle, we identified skin exposure to Terahertz (0.2 THz) promotes hair stem cell proliferation in the preliminary study. Based on such compelling evidence, we will investigate the optimized Terahertz irradiation condition to maximize hair stem cell regeneration and greatly induce growth cycle of hair follicle using novel time-lapse in vivo imaging technologies. Then, we will compare stimulatory effect of the determined Terahertz irradiation over conventional red-light therapy by quantitative and long-term analysis of hair growth. Immune reaction coupled regeneration by Terahertz will be also rigorously investigated as one of major underlying mechanism. Finally, we will showcase overall biosafety and absence of adverse effect of Terahertz by measurement of temperature change, blood vessel dilation, DNA damage, and tissue viability. To this end, we provide, for the first time, a powerful strategy to treat hair loss with high efficacy and no side effect using a new promising frequency regime, i.e., Terahertz wave. Such Terahertz medicine will eventually revolutionize current clinical practice in dermatological treatment to improve overall patient outcome and reduce health care cost. 太赫茲波（0.1 THz~10 THz）是近來跨學科研究的熱點和主題。其五花八門的應用，如利用寬帶太赫茲成像技術來建立非侵入性或術中癌症成像或用於皮膚及角膜含水量檢測等，都初步證實了他在生物醫學方面的應用性。然而，針對太赫茲波在細胞及分子層面造成的效應，特別是就特定頻率和強度的太赫茲波對生物組織的影響，仍然未知且充滿挑戰。近來太赫茲光譜學的相關研究發現，許多重要的生物分子處於太赫茲波的環境時，會與太赫茲波振動產生共振頻率，這暗示著適當的太赫茲輻射或將誘發生化反應和生物能量轉移。此外，最近研究發現小鼠皮膚在接受太赫茲輻射照射後呈現輕度發炎反應，而此現象可能來自於免疫反應誘發的皮膚再生。 脫髮或圓禿在逐步老齡化的現代社會中，是一種常見的皮膚病。全球每年用於治療脫髮的市值高達850億美元，並以5％的成長率逐年增長。不幸的是，目前可用的治療藥物如米諾地爾和非那雄胺效果不彰且有著明顯的副作用。所以，在這個項目中，我們將研究太赫茲輻射對皮膚再生和毛髮生長的效應，用以開發一種新的皮膚病治療技術。 針對太赫茲波產生的局部非電離輻射及其穿透深度是否能覆蓋整個毛囊的能力，我們的前期成果證實當皮膚暴露於太赫茲（0.2THz）時，能夠促進毛髮幹細胞增殖。基於此證據，我們將利用新型延時體內成像技術，優化太赫茲輻照條件，以達成毛髮幹細胞再生的最大化並誘導毛囊生長。然後，我們將針對皮膚於太赫茲輻照或常規紅光治療對促進生長毛髮數量的影響，進行定量與長期的比較與分析。另外，我們也會探討太赫茲波引發相關免疫反應來印證太赫茲波促進皮膚再生之機轉。最後，我們將通過測量溫度變化、血管擴張程度、DNA損傷、和組織存活度，展示太赫茲波的高安全性和低副作用。 為此，我們首次提供了一種高效率、無副作用且有效的脫髮治療策略，即太赫茲波。這種太赫茲波醫學治療或將徹底改變目前的臨床皮膚病治療，以提高整體患者的痊癒水平，並降低相關的醫療成本。

15107118.label: Realisation of objectives
15107118.value: Objective 1. Investigation of the optimized condition for T-ray irradiation to enhance hair stem cell regeneration and induce growth cycle of hair follicle (anagen) The objective 1 was 100% achieved by finding the best condition for T-ray irradiation to enhance hair stem cell regeneration and induce hair follicle growth (0.2 THz, 10min). A portable and powerful continuous wave (CW) terahertz (THz) wave source was developed and used to irradiate a large area in mice with various radiation time and intensity. A CW THz gyrotron with a compact cryogen-free magnet could generate 10 mW of THz power at 0.2 THz and 0.4 THz and illuminate a large field-of-view (up to 5cm x 5cm) with uniform beam density. Leveraging the capabilities to control illumination area, illumination time and interval, and light intensity with superior beam quality at tunable wavelengths, i.e., 0.2 THz and 0.4 THz, we tested different combinations of exposure condition and found the best condition of 0.2 THz exposure for 10 min to induce skin and hair regeneration. T-ray induced cell proliferation using Ki-67 marker was observed in the different aged mice (4- and 6-week-old balb/c male mice, each 3-4 mice per experimental group). Immunofluorescence staining and statistical analysis showed significantly increased expression of proliferation marker, Ki-67 over hair follicles and neighboring skin regions in the T-ray illuminated group (0.2 THz wave for 10 min) compared to the room-light illuminated control group. Interestingly, elevated enhancement was reported in 6-week old mice (more telogen and categen phases) compared to 4-week old mice (more anagen phases). This result indicates T-ray can promote proliferation of hair follicle cell components especially in the resting or regression phases of hair cycle. Hair stem cell regeneration was also measured with various hair stem cell markers, CD34 (bulge stem cell marker), β-catenin (Wnt/β-catenin activity), P-cadherin (hair germ stem cell marker) in 6-week old balb/c mice using intravital microscopic imaging of time-lapse hair stem cell dynamics and following immunofluorescence staining. All three markers were upregulated within hair follicles, but not in the extra-follicular dermal macro-environment. Particularly increased expression of β-catenin spur future study of T-ray’s regeneration capability because it is well proven that cyclic activation of hair stem cell involves periodic β-catenin activity and the eventual anagen initiation requires activation of Wnt/β-catenin. Hair follicle is highly accessible and its stem cells and progeny, located in the bulge and hair germ, respectively, are anatomically and molecularly well-defined. New hair growths can be identified with signatures of P-cadherin+ and proliferative (Ki-67+). Figure 4 clearly shows that local stimulation by THz irradiation in skin generates new hair growth. The increased number of new hair follicle by THz irradiation was statistically significant. Objective 2. Identification of the mechanism underlying T-ray-induced skin and hair regeneration through a multi-step immune cascade The objective 2 was 100% achieved via measurements of sequential biological events following T-ray irradiation, i.e., apoptosis of hair follicle component cells and recruitment of inflammatory macrophages to induce hair regeneration using intravital imaging and ex vivo analysis. For the mechanism underlying T-ray-induced skin and hair regeneration, we hypothesized that T-ray with high tissue penetration up to several hundred microns (sufficient enough to affect the whole hair follicle with typical length of ~100 µm) can induce micro-injury in hair follicles and neighboring skin tissues that can potentially lead to full-scale hair stem cell activation through the coupling immune response with cooperative regeneration. Appropriate micro-injury has shown as a critical stimulus to induce full-scale hair regeneration through a multi-step cascade, i.e., 1) microinjury induces apoptosis of hair follicle component cells and neighboring skin cells, 2) slightly injured hair follicle secrete CCL2 that recruit TNF-α-secreting inflammatory macrophages, 3) TNF-α activates regeneration of all hair follicles in the relatively large area, 4) Secondary hair growth-propagation induces extensive hair regeneration beyond the injured region. We accomplished several measurements of T-ray irradiated mice over time (immediately before and after T-ray irradiation, 4-, 8-, 12-hours after irradiation, 1-, 2-, 3-, 5-, 7-dyas after irradiation) over comparison with room light irradiated control groups. T-ray irradiation was performed using the best condition to enhance hair regeneration which was found in the experiments to achieve objective 1. Tunel assay and Annexin V staining were carried out to measure apoptosis after T-ray irradiation, which showed a peak value ~4 hr after T-ray irradiation. Then, CCL2 production was checked using immunofluorescence staining and real-time PCR. A significant high expression of CCL2 production was found at 1day after T-ray irradiation. Infiltration of macrophages were observed using intravital imaging of the Dextran-coated nanoparticles injected mice for fluorescent targeting of macrophages at 2 days after T-ray irradiation. Additional histological analysis also confirmed inflammation stimuli by T-ray irradiation showing infiltration of inflammatory macrophages (CD86 high macrophages) and pan-macrophages (CD11b high macrophages). Overall, a clear sign of macrophages’ recruitment was observed at 2days after T-ray irradiation. Objective 3. Demonstration of biosafety of T-ray irradiation by assessment of possible skin toxicity The objective 3 was 100% achieved by demonstration of no temperature change, high viability of hair follicle component cells and neighboring skin cells, no acute inflammatory response, and no blood vessel dilation after T-ray irradiation (0.2 THz, 85mW/cm2) up to 100 mins. Demonstration of safety and absence of side effects of T-ray irradiation is essential to increase its clinical effectiveness. Temperature increase has always been a major concern for T-ray’s biomedical application. To resolve such concern, we monitored temperature changes over time after T-ray irradiation using Infrared (IR) camera. Although the best condition to induce hair regeneration was found to be 0.2THz for 10mins, we tested T-ray (0.2THz) irradiation up to 3hrs with 10mins’ duration variation at high power density (85mW/cm2). No significant temperature change was observed by IR camera until 100 mins’ irradiation due to protective epidermal layer and efficient heat dissipation via blood circulation. Over 100mins, a linear increase in temperature was observed showing high absorption of T-ray by water in mice. Utilizing our established intravital microscopy technique, we measured high viability of hair follicle component cells and neighboring skin cells using Ki-67 marker, no acute inflammatory response using CD11b marker, and no blood vessel dilation using high molecule fluorescent dextran injection in mice. Enhanced proliferation was consistently observed at the best T-ray irradiation condition (0.2THz, 10min) by in vivo immunofluorescent staining with anti-Ki-67 antibodies and intravital microscopy. Although slight recruitment of macrophages was observed, no significant acute inflammation was found by CD11b based in vivo immunofluorescent staining and intravital microscopy. These data confirm biosafety of T-ray irradiation. Erythema is one of the common side effect of pharmacologic therapies for alopecia, which is triggered by blood dilation. Intravital imaging can perform three-dimensional measurement of blood vessels up to several hundred microns. Instead of Tie2-GFP mice (original plan), we used high molecule fluorescent dextran injection to Balb/c mice because supply of transgenic mice was not smooth due to COVID-19 outbreak. Injection of Dextran-Alex Flour 680 (molecular weight of 2.3kD) delineated blood vessel dynamics well and provided easy measurement by 3D intravital microscopy. Blood vessel diameter changes over time up to 2 days after T-ray irradiation was measured in vivo using dextran based intravital imaging of blood vessels and showed no evidence of induction of erythema. In conclusion, no significant toxicity was found by T-ray irradiation in mice.

15107118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15107118.value: We successfully found the best condition for T-ray irradiation to enhance hair stem cell regeneration and induce hair follicle growth (0.2 THz, 10min). Focusing on capability of Terahertz wave for nonionizing local irradiation and deep penetration to cover a whole hair follicle, skin exposure to Terahertz (0.2 THz, 10 min) was identified as an effective tool to promote cell proliferation and to activate hair stem cells. Through extensive ex vivo tissue analysis work, we could demonstrate active cell proliferation (Increased expression of Ki-67 marker), hair stem cell regeneration (Increased expression of CD34, β-catenin, and P-cadherin), and growth morphology of hair follicle (Increased number of hair follicle with Ki-67+P-cadherin+). Particularly increased expression of β-catenin proves T-ray’s regeneration capability because it is well reported that cyclic activation of hair stem cell involves periodic β-catenin activity and the eventual anagen initiation requires activation of Wnt/β-catenin. We also revealed the mechanism underlying T-ray-induced skin and hair regeneration through a multi-step immune cascade. We observed sequential events, i.e., 1) microinjury induced apoptosis of hair follicle component cells and neighboring skin cells by T-ray irradiation and 2) increase expression of CCL2 production and following infiltration of macrophages which can induce hair regeneration. Lastly, we demonstrated biosafety of T-ray irradiation by detection of high cell viability, no acute inflammatory response, and no blood vessel dilation after T-ray irradiation (0.2 THz, 85mW/cm2) up to 100 mins. Overall, we showed that T-ray irradiation (0.2 THz, 10 min) could provide an effective tool for hair regeneration with no toxicity for future clinical applications in dermatology medicine. We presented our research in many renowned international conferences including World Molecular Imaging Congress 2020. One PhD (Dr. Minfeng Yang) was successfully completed through this project and she also awarded a “Women in Molecular Imaging Network Scholar Award” for her scientific research presented at the WMIC Virtual 2021. Her PhD topic is about to establish intravital microscopy technique which was a key technique to complete this project. She applied this developed in vivo time-lapse intravital imaging technique for immunotherapy response monitoring as well as hair regeneration monitoring by T-ray irradiation. Dr. Minfeng Yang was also appointed as research assistant professor at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University and she will start her duty from September 1, 2023. Successful collaboration was made with Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute and Seoul National University Bundang Hospital in Republic of Korea via this project. This research was performed using a compact T-ray gyrotron system capable of producing high output in 0.2 THz and 0.4 THz which was developed by Dr. Seong-Tae Han from Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute. Dr. Chang-Hun Huh, MD PhD contributed to accurate analysis of histological data after THz irradiation with his professional expertise as dermatological doctor and stem-cell research scientist. Recently, we submitted the manuscript with our research to the journal “Science Advances” which is under revision now. There have been lots of difficulties due to the COVID-19 pandemic situation. Due to collaborative characteristic of this study between Hong Kong and South Korea, we had to visit Korea for T-ray irradiation research. However, it was not possible to visit Korea or invite our collaborators to Hong Kong due to the pandemic situation. That is why publication was delayed. Although journal paper publication was a bit late due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we strongly believe the paper will be published soon with high impact to the field of Terahertz research.

15107118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15107118.value: The presented research has high translational value to provide a new treatment tool for dermatological diseases such as hair loss. Hair loss, or alopecia, is a markedly increasing dermatological disease in aging society, involving an annual global market revenue of US$85 billion and a growth rate of 5%. Unfortunately, currently available therapeutic drugs such as Minoxidil and Finasteride have either low efficacy or significant adverse effects. With known efficacy in hair regeneration and safety of T-ray medicine in this project, we hope this T-ray technique helps people suffering with hair loss and reduce overall health care cost. To maximize clinical potential of our results, we will further test why 0.2 THz showed a good efficacy to enhance hair regeneration to provide more persuading evidence of using T-ray medicine. There is a possibility of T-ray modulation of vibrational resonance of regeneration contributing biomolecules. Moreover, we will compare stimulatory effect of the determined T-ray irradiation (0.2 THz, 10 min) over conventional red-light therapy for quantitative and long-term analysis of anagen induction and hair growth. Finally, we will find clinical collaborators and move into clinical trial study. Patent application in various countries is also essential to maximize benefits of this development.

15107118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15107118.value: Terahertz waves (0.1 THz ~ 10 THz) have attracted great interest with recent technological advances and are now the subject of interdisciplinary research. However, efforts to reveal the Terahertz-induced effects at cellular and molecular levels, especially how biological objects interact with Terahertz wave having specific frequency and intensity, is scarce and remains challenging. Herein, biological effects of Terahertz irradiation for skin regeneration and hair growth were investigated to develop a novel therapeutic technique for dermatological diseases such as hair loss. Focusing on capability of Terahertz wave for nonionizing local irradiation and deep penetration to cover a whole hair follicle, skin exposure to Terahertz (0.2 THz, 10 min) was identified as an effective tool to promote cell proliferation and to activate hair stem cells. The underlying mechanism of T-ray induced regeneration via mild inflammation induction was also revealed. Lastly, biosafety of T-ray irradiation was confirmed with high cell viability and no temperature change. Altogether, we provide, for the first time, a powerful strategy to treat hair loss with high efficacy and no side effect using a new promising frequency regime, i.e., Terahertz wave. Such Terahertz medicine will eventually revolutionize current clinical practice in dermatological treatment to improve overall patient outcome.
