15200218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200218.value: Cyber-physical systems (CPSs) are the result of the inevitable convergence between computers (correspondingly, the cyber subsystems) and the physical world (correspondingly, the physical subsystems). A major application domain of CPSs is control applications. CPSs for control applications (simplified as “control-CPSs”) include avionics, smart vehicles, power grids, robotics etc. These control-CPSs are often mission/life critical, hence demand high dependability. To ensure the dependability of control-CPSs, their cyber subsystems need software debugging. A key step of software debugging is bug localization, i.e. to find the buggy source code lines. State-of-the-art bug localization tools typically demand a large number of labeled (as “correct” / “incorrect”) source code execution traces as inputs (see Fig. 1). The labeling mechanism is called the “oracle”. In other words, oracle is the mechanism to judge the correctness of source code execution traces (before bugs are located). However, it is well known that designs of oracles are application dependent, and can often be difficult. The challenge on how to design oracles is called the “oracle problem”. For control-CPSs, the oracle problem faces new challenges, as well as new solution opportunities. Unlike pure cyber systems, whose outputs are discrete, control-CPS outputs are continuous physical trajectories (e.g. missile/airplane flight trajectories, vehicle driving trajectories, power grid voltage-over-time curves, robot movement trajectories etc.). Unlike pure continuous physical systems, a control-CPS undergoes discrete mode changes when outputting its continuous physical trajectories (e.g. an airplane switches from takeoff mode to cruise mode during a continuous flight). These new challenges call for new solutions for the control-CPS oracle problem. On the other hand, we can exploit various control theories to help judge the correctness of control-CPS outputs. Specifically, by exploiting the state-of-the-art hybrid-systems-stability theories and model-predictive-control theories, we aim to discover rules governing control-CPS outputs’ behaviors. We shall use these rules to design oracles for control-CPSs, so as to solve the control-CPS oracle problem. Our pilot study shows encouraging results: a preliminary version of our control-CPS oracle design improves bug localization quality (in terms of accuracy etc., see Part II-2(b)(i)-6) by 100~300% on one test-bed compared to the conventional oracle design. With more in-depth studies, this project shall achieve even better results, and shall propose a comprehensive set of solutions to the control-CPS oracle problem. This shall benefit not only control-CPSs, but also the bigger area of software/system engineering, dependability, and the many social domains served by control-CPSs. 信息-物理融合系統（CPS）是計算機信息系統和物理世界不斷融合的必然產物。自動控制是CPS的一大主要應用領域。用於自動控制的信息-物理系統（簡稱為“自動控制CPS”）涵蓋航空航天、智能汽車、智能電網、機器人等多種應用。這些自動控制CPS應用多為任務攸關或安全攸關，因此需要高可靠性。為了達到高可靠性，自動控制CPS信息子系統的軟件除錯就必不可少。而軟件除錯的一個關鍵步驟即是軟件錯誤定位：我們必須找到哪一行程序包含錯誤。目前前沿的軟件錯誤定位工具普遍需要大量的（自動）標註（“對”還是“錯”）過的程序運行紀錄作為輸入。而執行標註的機制被稱為“預言家”。也就是說，“預言家”即是（在程序錯誤被發現前即能）自動判斷程序執行對錯的工具。 “預言家”的設計是與應用緊密相關的。其難度會隨應用的不同而有巨大的差別。對於很多應用，“預言家”設計極具挑戰，被稱為“預言家問題”。對於自動控制CPS，其預言家問題面臨新的挑戰，同時也蘊含創新的機遇。一方面，與輸出離散結果的純軟件系統不同，自動控制CPS系統的輸出是連續的物理軌跡（例如飛行軌跡、行車軌跡、電網的電壓-時間軌跡、機器人的行動軌跡等）。另一方面，自動控制CPS與傳統的連續物理系統亦有不同：在輸出連續物理軌跡時，自動控制CPS會經歷離散的軟件模態變化（例如，再一次連續的飛行中，飛機會由起飛模態切換到巡航模態）。這些新的挑戰意味著自動控制CPS預言家問題需要新的解決方案。為此，我們注意到，我們可以利用各種自動控制理論來幫助判斷自動控制CPS的輸出軌跡是否正常。特別的，我們可以利用前沿的混成系統穩定性理論和模型預測控制理論來發掘自動控制CPS輸出軌跡的行為規律，並利用這些行為規律作為預言家。 根據這個想法，我們開展了預研，設計了一個預言家原型。結果顯示，對於我們的各種測試床應用，相較於傳統的方法，我們的原型預言家可以將軟件錯誤定位的品質（準確性等指標）提升100～300%。本項目計劃將我們的預研深入下去，以期得到更好的結果，並提出一套完整的解決方案，來解決自動控制CPS的預言家問題。這不但會助力自動控制CPS的諸多應用，還會大大有利於軟件工程/系統工程、可靠性等學科的發展，以及牽涉到自動控制CPS的社會的各個方面。

15200218.label: Realisation of objectives
15200218.value: For Objective 1, we made two discoveries. Discovery 1: One of the common behavioural rule governing control-CPSs is that their trajectories usually comply with the predictions of auto-regressive system-identification (AR-SI). The basic idea of AR-SI is to use linear regression of recent trajectories to predict the near future trajectories of the controlled plant. Supposedly, most man-made control-CPS’s physical trajectories should comply with the predictions of the AR-SI. This is because linear control is empirically the most widely adopted control strategy. Even non-linear control systems are usually designed to move their plants smoothly, so as to comply with temporal local linearity. Discovery 2: Many control-CPSs are required to be verifiably safe. That is, they must have an idealized math model, which satisfies certain properties. Such properties can be used as oracles. For Objective 2, based on the Discovery 1 of Objective 1, we propose an AR-SI based oracle. It continuously predicts the near future trajectories of a control-CPS, and if the predicted trajectory deviates too far away from the actual trajectory, we claim the control-CPS encounters a fault. We evaluated the above proposed oracle on various control-CPS testbeds, specially, the ArduPilot UAV platform, and a computer vision guided inverted pendulum system (IP). We injected various well-known bugs into these control-CPS testbeds, measure the following metrics: 1. Software Fault Localization (SFL) accuracy (percentage of suspects that are truly buggy in the list of top 10 suspects reported by SFL, the bigger the value the better). 2. SFL Latency (the rank of the first truly buggy suspect in the list of top 10 suspects reported by SFL, the smaller the value the better). 3. Oracle False Positive Rate (FPR) 4. Oracle False Negative Rate (FNR) We also compare the above metrics with a human flesh oracle (proposed by a panel of control-CPS experts). The results show that our proposed AR-SI oracle can significantly outperform the human oracle in terms of SFL accuracy, latency for spectrum based and statistics based SFL, and the in terms of oracle FPR and FNR. The corresponding results are published in [ICSE19]. In our publication of [RTCSA23], we further investigate the possibility of using the recently very hot AI time series generation tool of transformer as oracle, and compare its performance with the AR-SI oracle. Results show that the transformer oracle does not significantly outperform the AR-SI oracle in terms of SFL accuracy and latency. In terms of FPR, the AR-SI oracle performs better; and in terms of FNR, the transformer oracle performs better. Also for Objective 2, based on the Discovery 2 of Objective 1, we focus on designing verifiably safe formal models of control-CPS, and hope these can be used in the future as oracles. One of the focus application is the collaborative driving of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) on dedicated lanes. We proposed a set of wireless CAV collaborative driving protocols that can guarantee Constant-Time-Headway (CTH) safety and liveness (i.e. no deadlock) under arbitrary wireless communications failures [TCPS23][THESIS22][ICCPS20]. In the future, we can use these safety and liveness guarantee properties as oracles to test the correctness of the CAV collaborative driving implementations. 15200218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200218.value: We discovered that autoregressive system identification (AR-SI) can be used as an effective oracle for detecting faulty trajectories of control-CPS. Empirical evaluations on typical control-CPS testbeds show that compared to the conventional human oracles, the AR-SI can significantly improve software fault localization (SFL) accuracy and latency, and improve oracle’s false positive rate (FPR) and false negative rate (FNR). These results are published in [ICSE19]. Furthermore, the recently hot transformer time series generator can also be used as an oracle for control-CPS. Empirical evaluation on our testbeds show that the transformer oracle is not significantly better than the AR-SI oracle in terms of SFL accuracy and latency. However, the transformer oracle outperforms the AR-SI oracle in terms of the oracle FNR, while the AR-SI oracle outperforms the transformer oracle in terms of the oracle FPR. These results are published in [RTCSA23]. We also notice that many safety critical control-CPSs require verifiably safe design, whose formal properties can be used as oracles. Hence we further investigated the possibility of such designs using formal model for control-CPS. Our focus application is collaborative driving of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) in dedicated lanes. We propose a CAV collaborative driving protocol that guarantees the Constant-Time-Headway (CTH) safety and liveness under arbitrary wireless communications failures. In the future, we can use this CTH safety guarantee and the liveness guarantee as oracles to discover faults in the CAV collaborative driving. The corresponding results are published in [ICCPS20][THESIS22][TCPS23].

15200218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200218.value: The oracles designed can help further our research on program automatic repair. For example, in our publication of [TSE23], we can use oracles to label the correctness of millions of test case outputs, hence to get automatic feedback of program repair during runtime, and use these feedback to train a better program repair decision maker. In our publication of [TCAD20], we explored the possibility of using scenario based online reachability validation for control-CPS fault prediction. Same heuristics may be applied to design new control-CPS oracles: instead of using AR-SI to linearly predict the trajectories of a control-CPS, we can use [TCAD20]’s proposed scenario based reachability idea, to check if a family of scenario trajectories are possible to reach certain forbidden regions in the control-CPS’s state space, to decide the quality of the current control. If the quality is bad enough, we can label the current trajectories as faulty, and vice versa.

15200218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200218.value: Testing and debugging are critical for any software systems. Nowadays software testing and debugging need millions of test case execution traces, which need to be labelled correct or wrong. With such large number of test case execution traces, manually labelling them is impossible. We need an automatic labelling algorithm, aka oracle, to do the job. Design of oracles is a well-known hard problem for regular software. The problem is even harder for control-CPS, where complex software is used to control physical machineries. This project is among the first to explore the oracle problem for control-CPSs. The output of this project lays the foundation for future control-CPS oracle research, hence also lays the foundation for future control-CPS testing and debugging research.

15200318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200318.value: 該方案旨在開發用於生產智慧致動器的具有自傳感與自修復功能的新型透明柔性電活性聚合物複合材料。這些複合材料將為生產如仿生鏡頭與隱形設備等創新設計提供新的機會。此方法衍生于納米技術、聚合物複合材料、微波焊接與按需噴墨列印的最新進展，通過增強離子聚合物金屬複合材料致動器的導電性、介面粘附性以及結構完整性，從而克服了目前這種材料的局限性。 目標材料是一類重要的離子電活性聚合物，適用于製備可用于包括機器人、電子及生物醫學領域的不同長度尺寸智慧致動器。然而目前的技術不能使這些致動器同時實現高透明度、高柔性、低驅動電壓及自愈性能。激發這些致動器時的反復應變會導致電極與金屬-聚合物介面的劣變，這對它們的導電性、電荷遷移率和迴圈壽命均有不利影響。 在此方法中，電活性聚合物複合材料將基於這種材料的工作原理與結構配置，從而擁有其相同的獨特優勢。材料性能的增強將通過以下三條路徑實現：一、 微波焊接透明柔性電極能將材料的連線性與導電性最大化，從而提高其機電性能；二、 將納米網電極與自愈型離子液體聚合物凝膠電解質結合形成具有延長迴圈壽命的複合材料； 三、 三維列印將實現具有最小局部應力的致動器設計。功能性分級的納米網電極材料能減少不同材料相之間的介面應力。因其具有一定電容量，這種複合材料可以產生由機械輸出而引起的電信號，用於閉環傳感或控制。 項目組在智慧聚合物納米複合材料領域有著相關的研究經驗，包括增強型納米碳材料的製備，電活性聚合物複合材料的有限元分析，納米複合材料的微波處理以及開發新的複合材料。這項研究的可交付成果將主要致力於：一、 增加用於開發透明柔性智慧致動器並具有增強機電性能的分級結構設計中的科學知識；二、開發克服現有這種複合材料局限性的方法。研究組前期研究工作為成功開展此研究方案並取得預期結果奠定了堅實基礎。

15200318.label: Realisation of objectives
15200318.value: Realization of Revised Objective 1 A series of experiments was carried out to determine the suitable composition and processing conditions for fabricating transparent iEAP actuators, covering the following two main parts: (1) Design and fabrication of transparent iEAPs The electrolyte membrane of iEAPs used PVDF or PVA as the polymer matrix and imidazolium ionic liquid (IL) as the mobile ions. For PVDF/IL electrolyte membranes, methods of reducing crystallinity by copolymerization and sacrificing water-soluble templates were designed to improve optical transmittance. For PVA/IL electrolyte membranes, solution casting and freeze-thaw cycling methods were employed to prepare solid or gel electrolytes. The polymer electrode (PEDOT:PSS) was deposited onto the electrolyte membrane surfaces to form the iEAPs by direct casting. An electromechanical response of the iEAPs was generated due to the directional motion of ions in an electrical field. The redistribution of ions in electrolyte membranes under external force would allow the generation of electrical signals, which would realize the sensing function. PVA/IL demonstrated higher optical transparency (as high as 96% transmittance) than PVDF/IL. (2) Preparation and characterization of PVA/PEDOT:PSS conductive film PVA/PEDOT:PSS composite hydrogels were prepared for transparent, flexible electrodes with self-sensitive capability. The hydrogels were prepared by cross-linking PVA and PEDOT:PSS using glutaraldehyde. After forming the PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogel films, the chemical structure, morphology, and electrical properties were determined by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and four-point probe conductivity measurement. The PVA and the cross-linking agent formed a stable chemically semi-interpenetrating network structure through the acetal reaction. The composite hydrogel exhibited rubber-like behavior with a conductivity of 0.36 S/m, then applied as the transparent electrode to fabricate the transparent and flexible electroactive polymer composites. Realization of Revised Objective 2 Precursor solutions for the transparent electrolyte were used to develop composite inks for layer-by-layer printing of smart actuators. The PVA/IL solution was used as the electrolyte ink for the ion conductive membranes, and the pretreated PEDOT:PSS membranes were used as the transparent electrode for transfer printing. The experimental details are explained below: (1) Preparation and characterization of PVA/IL electrolyte membranes After determining the suitable material composition for the electrolyte, PVA/IL composite inks with different rheological properties were developed. Due to the good compatibility, the optical transmittance of the membrane was not affected and was maintained above 95%. The crystallinity of the electrolyte membrane formed using the composite inks was characterized by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and the results showed the inhibitory effect of IL on PVA crystallization. A lower crystallinity will be beneficial for the bending performance of the iEAP. Tensile tests further demonstrated that the flexibility of the electrolyte membrane increases with IL loading. Electrochemical characterization revealed fast and reversible ion transport. In addition, PVDF/IL composite inks were also prepared for comparison. A copolymer (PVDF-HFP) with lower crystallinity was used to improve transparency. Unfortunately, the membrane became opaque, ascribed to phase separation and phase inversion after PVDF exposure to the solvent. For these reasons, PVDF and PVDF-HFP were not considered in follow-up studies. (2) Coating of electrodes and preparation of transparent iEAP The methods and parameters for coating the electrodes were studied. The transparent PEDOT:PSS electrode was made by spin-coating on a glass plate. Taking advantage of the weak interfacial bonding between the conductive polymer and the substrate, a transparent electrode can be suspended in water and transfer-printed to the PVA/IL electrolyte membrane. The PEDOT:PSS electrodes were washed with nitric acid to remove the PSS so that the electrical conductivity can be further enhanced. A series of coating methods was also designed, including spray-, blade-, spin-, and dip coating. The transfer printing method was found to be the most successful strategy for fabricating transparent iEAP actuators. The transparent iEAPs were assembled through the following procedure. First, the PEDOT:PSS ink was poured into a petri dish to form a transparent electrode with a thickness of 0.1 um after drying. The PVA/IL composite ink was then added to the surface of the dried PEDOT:PSS electrode. Finally, the top PEDOT:PSS electrode layer was transfer-printed onto the surface of the PVA/IL electrolyte. The resulting iEAP actuators exhibited optical transmittance as high as 90.2%. Realization of Revised Objective 3 The main factors, including the composition and processing conditions of the electrolyte membrane and the PEDOT:PSS electrode, were analyzed for their impact on optical transmittance, mechanical properties, and sensing-actuating electrochemical performance. The research activities and the results are summarized below: (1) Characterization and actuation of electrolyte membranes Different electrolyte membranes with varying IL and water content were prepared to investigate the effect of IL hygroscopicity on the actuator's performance. Regardless of the water content, the PVA/IL electrolyte membrane demonstrated good compatibility without phase separation between PVA and IL. All electrolyte membranes also showed a reduced crystallinity, resulting in optical transmittances >96%. The absorbed water by IL widened the migration channels in the electrolyte, enhancing the smart actuator's actuation performance. A universal test machine was used to characterize the mechanical properties of the electrolyte membranes, and it was found that samples with higher IL and water content exhibited greater flexibility. The actuation properties of trip-type iEAPs made of PVA/IL electrolytes with gold electrodes were assessed. To obtain a reliable comparison of the actuation performance, an analytic method based on B-spline interpolation and the circular regression equation was developed to obtain the bending profile of the iEAP actuators and calculate their bending curvature. Compared to the imidazolium IL-containing iEAPs reported in the literature, the PVA/IL iEAP actuators fabricated in this study showed at least a 35% improvement in bending performance. Interestingly, the PVA/IL iEAP actuators showed an unusual anion-controlled actuation behavior, and further investigations were conducted. It was found that the possible formation of hydrogen bonds between the IL cations and PVA chains immobilized the cation and therefore realized an anion-controlled bending behavior. The highest bending curvature of 40.27 m-1 at 2 V was achieved, attributed to the hygroscopicity of IL and the unique actuation mechanism. (2) Actuation and sensitivity performance of transparent iEAP The PVA/IL electrolyte membrane with 1:1 PVA:IL mass fraction was selected to achieve better actuation performance of the iEAPs. PEDOT:PSS thin film electrodes were applied to fabricated transparent iEAP. Despite having lower conductivity than metal electrodes, the fabricated electroactive polymer composite actuators exhibited a fast response time (<1 s) to voltages below 1 V due to their inherent electrochemical redox. At 0.5 V, the highest bending curvature of the transparent iEAP reached 17.36 m^-1. To assess the self-sensing ability of the transparent iEAP using PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogel as an electrode, the strain sensitivity of the electrode was examined. PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogels showed elastic behavior. Increased strain enlarged the spaces between the conducting material within the PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogel, reducing its conductivity. The gauge factor (GF) was used to evaluate the sensitivity of PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogels as strain sensors. At the same strain, GF increased with increasing PEDOT:PSS content in the hydrogel. Additionally, the GF also increased with increasing strain. The highest GF reached up to 4.4 at 100% strain, demonstrating great potential for transparent iEAPs with self-sensing function.

15200318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200318.value: The major findings and outcomes are listed below: (1) A method for preparing a transparent and flexible PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogel electrode was developed. The material composition and properties of the composite hydrogel were thoroughly investigated. The conductive hydrogel demonstrated stain-sensitive behavior, which can be used for fabricating transparent iEAPs with self-sensing functions. The highest gauge factor of the PVA/PEDOT:PSS hydrogel strain sensor reached as high as 4.4. (2) A new PVA/IL electrolyte membrane for fabricating transparent iEAPs was developed. The suitable material composition and processing conditions were determined. The PVA/IL demonstrated good compatibility without phase separation. Enhanced actuation performance was achieved due to the hygroscopicity of IL, which facilitated the ion migration in the electrolyte membrane. The effects of the IL and water contents within the membranes on the mechanical and electrochemical properties and actuation performance of transparent smart actuators were studied. (3) The fabricated transparent PVA/IL iEAPs exhibited unusual anion-controlled bending deformation due to the hydrogen bonding between PVA and IL, further enhancing the actuation performance. This finding provides new knowledge in designing advanced smart actuators. In addition, the process for assembling transparent iEAPs with PEDOT:PSS electrodes was developed. The adopted method can overcome problems such as high surface energy and low conductivity of conductive polymers that hinder the deposition of the electrode film. This also avoided disruption of the ionization equilibrium of the conducting polymer. (4) A reliable evaluation method was developed for quantitatively evaluating the bending deformation of strip-type actuators. This method allows researchers to study the bending behavior consistently and offers a better method for comparing the actuation performance of smart actuators. (5) A layer-by-layer formation scheme of transparent iEAPs was established. A transfer-printing strategy was developed to avoid the precipitation of PEDOT:PSS. Referring to Part C of this report, the major findings have led to 4 journal publications and 1 conference paper. The findings/outcomes mainly related to Items (1) and (4) were published in Polymer Testing, and some of the results were presented at the 27th Annual International Conference on Composites and Nano Engineering. Items (2) and (3) were published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry C. Item (5) was covered by one journal paper in Nanotechnology Reviews.

15200318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200318.value: This study developed electrolyte and electrode materials and fabrication methods for transparent electroactive polymer actuators. Future work is required to achieve programmable actuation responses and explore their applications in electrochemical devices. This may involve an in-depth study of the interaction between various imidazole rings and polymers. Fabrication of smart PVA/IL actuators with predesigned structures using 3D printing technologies is curial to realize multimode responses for endowing the ability to perform complicated tasks. Additionally, a comprehensive study of the electromechanical sensing and electrochromic functions of transparent iEAPs with polymer electrodes is recommended. These proposed works can lead to the production of sensors with multiple sensing and the implementation of more complex actuators for the development of transparent smart devices.

15200318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200318.value: Our team has developed a new transparent and flexible smart actuator using electroactive polymer composites. The smart actuators demonstrated fast response and enhanced performance under a low actuation voltage. Compared to other similar electroactive polymers reported in the literature, the smart actuator showed at least a 35% enhancement of the bending performance. Moreover, the developed transparent conductive hydrogel electrode could also sense external stimuli. The main factors for enhancing flexibility and actuation performance were also thoroughly studied. A layer-by-layer printing method was proposed for fabricating smart actuators. Composite inks with suitable rheological properties were developed based on the optimal material composition for achieving enhanced actuator performance. The method can overcome some processing challenges and allows precise control over the thickness of the electrode to enhance transparency. The research outcomes led to new transparent composite materials and an innovative approach for fabricating smart actuators. The innovations can be applied to develop smart devices covering electronics, aerospace applications, and biomedical devices. The project also generated new knowledge that is useful to guide the design of advanced smart devices or the development of future technologies.

15200418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200418.value: With the rapid development of renewable energy, energy storage, EVs, FACTS and HVDC, increasing number of power electronic converter (PEC)-connected equipment has penetrated into the conventional power system, which enhances the system flexibility and controllability, but also considerably complicates the dynamics of transmission and distribution systems. The PEC system, on one hand, participates in the conventional power oscillations and makes problems more complex; On the other hand, it also brings some new types of oscillation/interaction among various converters in different-level power networks (e.g., under/over-frequency oscillations are observed in wind-connected systems, and their dynamics are associated with PECs. How exactly such oscillations happen and how to damp them remain an open problem for grid connections of wind power). Both aspects above have posed a critical threat and enormous challenge to power system operation and thus deserve a careful examination. To investigate these emerging oscillation problems, a precise system modeling would be crucial if traditional model-based analysis is used. However, large quantities of PEC systems with complex structures, time-varying parameters and ‘black-box’ controllers not only make system modeling nearly an impossible task, but also significantly increase model dimension and computational burden especially for a resource-constrained real-time operation. Hence, due to these ‘new features’, traditional methods might be no longer suitable for modern system operation. The transition from model-based to data-based analysis enabled by the wide-area measurement system and big data analytics provides an effective solution to the above-mentioned challenge. Nevertheless, most existing data-based research only examines the conventional power oscillations of transmission system without considering the impact of high penetrating converters. Additionally, most of data-based methods perform like a black box and are lack of a deep physical explanation. Therefore, this project aims to develop a new model-independent monitoring and analyzing system by combining two proposed data-based techniques (i.e., energy flow dissipation monitoring technique and damping flow distribution learning technique), which can simultaneously visualize and study all types of oscillations including new emerging or potentially undiscovered oscillations brought by PECs with a clear physical understanding for the first time, since whatever oscillations are essentially related to energy flow fluctuation. Then some efficient preventive&emergency control strategies will be proposed and the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed system and control strategies will be validated by real system operation. The project will undoubtedly bring significant benefits to secure operation of future smart grid characterized by large-scale integration of converter-controlled components worldwide including Hong Kong. 隨著新能源、儲能、電動汽車、靈活交直流輸電技術的快速發展，越來越多電力電子換流器連接的設備（後簡稱電力電子換流器系統）滲透進傳統的電力系統，這一方面提高了系統的靈活性和可控性，但同時也使得輸配電系統的動態更加複雜。電力電子換流器系統一方面參與電力系統傳統振盪，並且使得問題更加複雜；另一方面不同電壓等級電網中由於各種換流器間相互作用又引發了新的振盪問題（例如，在含有風電場的系統中已觀測到的高/低頻振盪現象，並且這種動態過程與電力電子換流器緊密相關。這種振盪究竟是如何產生的，怎樣抑制這種振盪，仍然是風電併網所面臨的重要問題）。以上涉及到的兩方面影響給電力系統運行帶來了嚴重的威脅和巨大的挑戰，因此值得深入研究。為了研究這些突現的振盪問題，如果採用基於模型的傳統分析方法，建立系統模型將至關重要。然而，對於大量含有複雜結構，時變參數和黑箱控制器的電力電子換流器系統來說，不僅建立精確的系統模型幾乎不可能，而且極大地增加系統模型維數和計算量，尤其對於一個實時運行系統來說不太可行。因此，正是由於這些系統“新特性”，傳統方法將不再適用於現代電力系統運行的分析。由廣域測量技術和大數據分析技術所推動的基於數據的分析方法正在逐步取代傳統分析方法的地位，是解決上述挑戰的一個有效途徑。然而，現有大多數基於數據的研究僅僅集中於輸電網傳統功率振盪方面，沒有考慮系統中高滲透的電力電子換流器的影響。此外大多數基於數據的研究方法像一個黑箱，缺少深入的物理解釋。因此，本項目旨在研發兩種關鍵技術，即能量流耗散監測技術和阻尼流分佈學習技術，並有效結合兩種技術開發一個新型不基於模型的監測與分析系統。由於任何振盪的本質都是系統中能量流的波動，該系統將首次對所有類型的振盪模式，包括由電力電子換流器引起的新型振盪模式和未發現的潛在振盪模式，進行可視化分析，並給出了清晰的物理解釋。然後本項目將提出了一些有效的預防和緊急控制策略，並在真實系統的運行中檢驗其準確性和有效性。本項目將進一步保障大規模換流器併網為標誌的未來智能電網的安全運行，無疑對香港乃至世界範圍內智能電網的發展有著重要的意義。

15200418.label: Realisation of objectives
15200418.value: The original project objectives have been revised after the project is granted based on the actual given funding and resources as well as the comments from the reviewers. To date, all the revised objectives of the project have been achieved. Part of the original objective 5 has also been achieved. The details are provided as follows. Revised objective 1: Oscillation energy flow dissipation tracking, analyzing and visualizing techniques for different oscillation modes and sources based on WAMS Two oscillation energy flow dissipation assessment methods have been proposed to analyze and visualize different oscillation modes and sources based on the PMU measurements in a real-time manner without acquiring detailed system models and information. The mathematical equivalence between the two proposed methods and conventional damping torque analysis (DTA) and modal analysis (MA) have been strictly proved regardless of arbitrary generator models in the multi-machine power systems. Then, the methods have been extended to power electronics-dominated power systems from the traditional synchronous generator-centered power systems to deal with the emerging power electronic converter associated/induced wideband oscillations and the quasi-oscillation loop is identified and constructed to be used by the proposed energy flow methods. Modal analysis in the frequency domain and time domain simulation are also used to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method and index. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1-3 and 7-12, and Conference Paper 1 in Part C. Revised objective 2: Machine learning techniques to predict damping flow channel weighting factors and determine relation between local oscillation energy dissipation and system oscillatory stability margin Deep learning techniques such as CNN and LSTM are employed to develop advanced situation awareness method to monitor and predict the power system oscillatory stability margin and damping. CNN and LSTM can effectively extract the special spatial (e.g., nodes and branches to form a topology) and temporal (e.g., time series dynamics) features of the power system for better prediction results. The deployment of PMU measurements are also studied to determine the best and most cost-effective deployment plan. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1, 4 and 7 in Part C. Revised objective 3: Data pre-processing (error tolerance and correction) techniques to deal with incomplete and false data due to communication failure and cyberattack Random matrix theory is employed with deep learning techniques such as LSTM to deal with the multiple data corruptions such as false and insufficient measurements caused by cyberattack and communication failure in a complex environment with massive fluctuating renewable power generation. The developed technique can be used as a data pre-processing measure for the advanced situation awareness assessment to detect any anomaly in system security and oscillatory stability. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1, 5 and 7, and Conference Paper 2 in Part C. Revised objective 4: Application of developed system in investigating impact mechanism of PEC systems on oscillatory stability The oscillation energy flow dissipation theory can effectively help to understand the impact mechanism of power electronic converter (PEC) systems on oscillatory stability. It has been rigorously proved that the oscillation energy flow dissipation speed should be equivalent to the damping ratio of the relevant oscillation mode. The oscillation is essentially caused or reflected by a second-order oscillation loop, which is associated with a pair of conjugate eigenvalues. The second-order oscillation loop can be easily identified not only in the conventional synchronous generator (rotor angle and rotor speed loop) but also in many PEC control loops, which correspond to the oscillation modes of PEC systems. Quite a few research efforts have been devoted to formulating a generic second-order oscillation loop model in the PEC systems. Hence, the proposed oscillation energy flow dissipation assessment methods can be used in large-scale power electronics-dominated power systems as long as the PMU equipment can be deployed at the interface of these PEC systems and the impact mechanism (damping contribution path) of PEC systems on the concerned oscillation modes can be revealed. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 2, 3, 6 and 8-12, and Conference Paper 1 in Part C. Part of original objective 5: Design of effective preventive & emergency control strategies to damp multiple types of critical oscillations/resonances Based on the damping evaluation and mechanism analysis of oscillatory stability, some offline/online oscillation mitigation and damping control strategies have been proposed. The optimization techniques can be utilized in a real-time manner based on the collected PMU data, which is very adaptive and robust considering different operational conditions. Sometimes the oscillation is called modal resonance if it is related to the dynamic interactions between two oscillation modes with a closer frequency. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1, 6 and 7 in Part C.

15200418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200418.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized associated with the selected research outputs of the project. The various measurement-based model-independent methods in monitoring and analyzing the oscillatory stability of transmission and distribution systems are extensively reviewed to gain an in-depth understanding and knowledge in this field (Associated with Journal Paper 1 and 7 in Part C). It is revealed that the proposed energy flow analysis method using the angular frequency of the oscillation mode in the calculation is equivalent to damping torque analysis in damping performance evaluation regardless of generator models (Associated with Journal Paper 2 in Part C). It is also revealed when using the whole oscillation mode in the calculation, the proposed energy flow analysis method is equivalent to modal analysis in assessing the oscillatory stability margin regardless of generator models (i.e., the real part of the eigenvalue) (Associated with Journal Paper 8 and Conference Paper 1 in Part C). Then, it is discovered that the proposed methods can be also extended to the power electronized power systems when the quasi second-order oscillation loop can be identified and constructed (Associated with Journal Paper 9 in Part C). It can be found that all the oscillation modes have their associated mathematical second-order differential equation formulation and this formulation is also called the second-order oscillation loop. The generic second-order oscillation loop is studied and constructed in PEC systems with different converter control schemes (Associated with Journal Paper 3, 10, 11 and 12 in Part C). Based on the analysis, some real-time measurement-based mitigation strategies are designed for wideband oscillations without the need of system models and information with sound adaptability and robustness (Associated with Journal Paper 6 in Part C). Another major finding is that deep learning algorithms are very suitable for the spatiotemporal dynamic feature extraction of power systems and hence the relevant situation awareness methods are developed accordingly (Associated with Journal Paper 4 and 5, and Conference Paper 2 in Part C).

15200418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200418.value: Firstly, the methodology developed in this project will be packed into relevant software and implemented in the industry with its accuracy and efficiency validated and improved in the real environment for further commercialization. Secondly, the theory and methodology proposed in the project can be applied to the monitoring and impact mechanism investigation of wideband oscillations/resonances induced by different types of PEC-interfaced resources (sometimes called inverter-based resources) and their dynamic interactions, e.g., renewable power generation, energy storage system, HVDC and FACTS. Thirdly, the oscillatory stability problems and their impact mechanisms in the active distribution networks (ADNs) should also be more focused compared with those of traditional transmission grids that have been well studied, as the oscillatory dynamics become more complex in ADNs due to the massive integration of distributed energy resources interfaced by PECs.

15200418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200418.value: To limit global warming to 1.5 degrees compared to pre-industrial levels, the Carbon Neutrality target by 2050 has become a consensus among many countries and regions worldwide. Renewable energy will gradually replace conventional fossil fuels and finally account for a dominant proportion of future global power generations. Since the majority of renewable energy is interfaced by power electronic converter (PEC), a significant increase in PEC-connected resources in the transmission and distribution grids can be certainly foreseen, also considering the wide utilization of energy storage, electric vehicles, FACTS and HVDC. Therefore, power system dynamics will be considerably changed and a precise system modeling would become almost impossible to analyze these emerging and complex dynamics unfortunately. This project aims to provide an effective and economical solution to power system dynamic issues induced by massive PEC-connected resources and tackle the technical bottleneck of the existing model-dependent assessment methods. The project outcomes have been very fruitful and of both substantial theoretical and practical values. The project has provided theoretical guidance and technical support to power system operators for the secure operation of future power grids. The theoretical method and findings of the project can also be extended to other relevant fields for future research.

15200518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200518.value: Rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), which is based on interactions and communication of huge numbers of microsensors and microprocessors, is producing dramatic changes across many facets of daily life. Nano-sized objects, with unique or size-dependent properties, are being used across many disciplines to provide efficient and innovative solutions that may not be achievable using bulk materials. For example, nanosensors can be small enough to circulate in the blood stream or be embedded into other structures (e.g. construction materials, solar panels, or disposable food service items). This drives strong interest in the research community to apply nanotechnology within IoT architectures. This proposal aims at developing a new type of nanosensor, with enhanced sensitivity to the changes in its surrounding environment. A sensitive detection mechanism is an essential component of any reliable nanosensor. Over the past two decades, many nanoparticle-based sensing approaches have been developed. Among them, plasmonic sensing has emerged as a particularly useful and promising approach. Traditionally, plasmonic sensors employ the resonant oscillation of free electrons on metal surfaces, usually gold and silver. This oscillation of electrons produces strong light absorption at the resonant frequency and is strongly sensitive to the surrounding environment. This sensitivity provides a mechanism of detecting changes in the environment. Contact of substances (e.g. chemicals or biomolecules) with the metal surface induces a change of local refractive index that changes the resonant wavelength. However, the sensitivity achieved in this refractive index based detection scheme remains insufficient for many applications. To address these issues, we will employ a new type of plasmonic material based on semiconductor nanocrystals. The resonant condition in this class of materials is supported by the oscillation of free holes (positive charge carriers) rather than electrons. Their optical properties are very sensitive to both the surrounding medium and to the concentration of free holes in the semiconductor nanocrystal. With this additional effect, we hypothesize that the sensitivity of these materials can be manipulated by modulating the number of free holes per nanostructure. To verify this hypothesis and understand the "nanoparticles structure-plasmonic-detection sensitivity" relationship, hetero-nanostructures will be produced by attaching an electron-rich moiety to the plasmonic semiconductor nanocrystal. A new sensing mechanism, “plasmonic quenching” is also proposed to evaluate the enhanced sensitivity by optical measurements. The outcomes of this project will advance fundamental understanding these new plasmonic materials and sensing mechanism, and will facilitate the development of the new “Internet of Nano Things (IoNT)” paradigm. 大量微傳感器和微處理器的技術革新，大大促使了物聯網（IoT）的快速發展，使得我們日常生活的各個方面都發生了巨大的變化。納米材料由於其獨特的尺寸依賴性，已經被應用在許多領域，實現傳統材料無法實現的性能，甚至提供了更多的創新方案。譬如說，納米傳感器可以做到足夠微型，使其能在不影響機能的情況下嵌入血液循環系統中，或者融合進各種不同的結構中，如建築材料，太陽能電池板或一次性食品包裝盒。這些特性，都激起了研究領域將納米科技應用在IoT的興趣。本項目旨在開發一種新型的納米傳感器，大大增強傳感器對周圍環境變化的靈敏度。一個傳感器的感應機制是其可靠性最重要保障。在過去的二十年中，研究人員已經開發出許多基於納米材料的傳感手段，其中基於等離子效應的傳感器已經展現出其卓越的穩定性。傳統的等離子效應傳感器，通常利用金和銀作為主體，利用其金屬表面的自由電子共振現像傳感。這種電子振盪在共振頻率下會強烈的光吸收，並且共振條件對周圍的環境非常敏感，使得利用等離子效應製作檢測環境變化的傳感其成為可能。例如，物質（化學品或生物分子）與金屬表面的接觸會引起物質局部表面的折射率變化，通過觀察共振波長的變化，便可以達到檢測的目的。即便如此，這種基於折射率變化的檢測手法在靈敏度上仍有待提高。 為了解決這個問題，我們將採用一種基於半導體納米晶體的新型等離子體材料。這種材料的等離子共振由自由空穴（正電荷載流子）而不是電子的振盪引起的。它的光學特性對周圍環境介質和半導體納米晶體中的自由空穴濃度都非常敏感。利用這種額外的效應，我們設想這種材料的靈敏度可以通過調節每個納米結構中自由空穴的數量來控制。為了驗證並研究這種“納米結構與等離子靈敏度”的關係，我們將用富電子部分連接到等離子體半導體納米晶體來製造異質結構，並還使用一種新的機制“等離子體猝滅”來評估其靈敏度。該項目的成果將促進對我們新型等離子體材料和傳感機制的認知，並促進“納米物聯網（IoNT）”發展。

15200518.label: Realisation of objectives
15200518.value: Objective 1 have been achieved by developing a facile method to synthesize controllable size and shape copper sulfide nanocrystals (Cu2−xS NCs) in an aqueous solution. In this case, the Cu2−xS NC is a p-type semiconductor material, which has strong near infrared (NIR) absorption originated from localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of free holes. Commonly used chemicals copper (II) chloride and sodium sulfide were used as the copper source and sulfur source, respectively. One of the important steps is to use low-molecular-weight branched polyethylenimine (PEI), which is cationic and highly soluble in water, was utilized as the reducing and capping agents. Transmission electron microscope (TEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) techniques were used to characterize the as-synthesized nanocrystals and revealed that structures ranging from copper-deficient covellite (CuS), spionkopite (Cu1.1S), roxbyite (Cu1.75S), to copper-rich djurleite (Cu1.94S). The size and morphology of Cu2−xS NCs can also be able to adjust with lengths from 6.5 to 46.5 nm and the aspect ratio from 2.2 to 7.5 by simply varying the concentrations of PEI (see Research Output 1). In this work, we found that the Cu2-xS NCs are very stable in aqueous solution and highly responsive to the NIR irradiation. We discovered that the heat conversion efficiency (HCE) of these NCs is remarkable. A range of 34.9 to 49.0% of HCE were obtained in different Cu2−xS NCs with distinct morphology under 1064 nm laser irradiation (1.33 W/cm2) (see Research Output 1). Another nanostructures prepared for Objective 1 is AuNR/Cu2-xS core shell nanohybrids. They were prepared by first introducing AuNR/Cu2O NPs as templates and then converting the outer layer into Cu2-xS through an anion exchange reaction. The AuNR cores were synthesized by a silver ion-assisted seed mediated method. The size and aspect ratio of AuNRs were carefully controlled to enable efficient PRET with Cu2-xS layers. The Cu2O coating of the AuNRs was achieved by reducing Cu(OH)42- with NH2OH, while applying sodium dodecyl sulfate as a stabilized agent. In the growth process, the color of the reaction mixture gradually turned green, indicating growth of Cu2O. The conversion from Cu2O to Cu2-xS can be achieved by reaction with Na2S followed by HCl etching of residual Cu2O. AuNR/Cu2-xS core shell nanohybrids were used for in-vivo cancer therapy applications (manuscript under preparation, see Part C). To produce Cu2-xS thin films, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA, molecular weight of 54,000) was used and Cu2-xS NCs-PVA gel was prepared to address Objective 2 and 3. The synthesis is very simple. PVA power was dissolved in water with constant stirring at 90 ℃. After the PVA solution cooled down to room temperature, Cu2-xS dispersion, glutaraldehyde and hydrochloric acid were further added to obtain Cu2-xS NCs-PVA gel. Samples containing different types and concentrations of Cu2-xS NCs were prepared and the microstructure of the film can be found in Research Output 2. A plasmonic quenching effect was demonstrated by the use of o-phenylendiamine (OPD). OPD is a compound which emitted yellow fluorescence (568 nm) when it was oxidized (electrons donator) by the Cu2-xS NCs-PVA nanocrystals (electrons acceptor). As the concentration of OPD increased, more Cu2-xS NCs were quenched and the fluorescence was enhanced, therefore the plasmonic quenching effect could be observed. It was shown that the LSPR of Cu₂-xS nanocrystals was quenched effectively in the rod shape of Cu2-xS nanocrystals with higher (2-x) value. The results showed a satisfying signal-to-noise ratio and sensing capability, revealing the potential for the future development of the Cu2-xS film based sensors.

15200518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200518.value: Potential for Further Development: The synthesis, LSPR properties and sensing capability of copper based nanocrystal film have been comprehensively studied in this project. As we found that a small variation of carrier density will lead to a significant shift in the LSPR peak, one of the future research directions could be a design and fabrication of plasmonic hetero-nanostructures. By using the interaction between two different plasmonic regimes (i.e. electrons and holes), the number of free hole carriers can be manipulated by growing hetero-nanostructures with metallic nanoparticles. When an electron rich moiety contacts with the sensing substrate, the vacancies in the sensing substrate will be filled by electrons from the donor moiety, decreasing the number of free holes in the semiconductor and creating an additional red shift and damping of the LSPR peak. Through this mechanism, the detection sensitivity can be potentially enhanced. In this project, the researchers have developed a sensing and photothermal based on nanotechnology. The technique can be applied in creating a range of applications for public and environment. For example, the developed structures can be modified with biomarkers that can be specified to particular infected site in our body (e.g. tumor). External laser can be used to trigger the photothermal effect of nanostructure to achieve a therapeutic outcome. In addition, the solar-to-vapor generation of the Cu2-xS NCs-PVA was also capable of producing pure water under natural sunlight, as well as suitable for environmental cooling, pollution abatement and moisture management.

15200518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200518.value: Nanotechnology is producing dramatic changes across many facets of daily life. Nano-sized objects, with unique or size-dependent properties, are being used across many disciplines to provide efficient and innovative solutions that may not be achievable using bulk materials. For example, nanosensors can be small enough to circulate in the blood stream or be embedded into other structures (e.g. construction materials, solar panels, or disposable food service items). This drives strong interest in this work to apply in surrounding environment. Over the past two decades, many nanoparticle-based sensing approaches has been developed. A sensitive detection mechanism is an essential component of any reliable sensor. To address these issues, we employed a new type of plasmonic nanomaterial. Plasmonic sensing has emerged as a particularly useful and promising approach. We employed a different approach to produce sensing films, which can be applied in a wide range of applications. The film could also generate heat when exposing to nature light. By using the thin film developed in this work, we developed a high efficiency solar-to-vapor thin film system, which provided a “green” solution for producing pure water under natural sunlight.

15200718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200718.value: With the exponential increase in data traffic, especially the demand for ultra-broad bandwidth driven by multimedia applications, ultra-high-speed optical fiber communication system has become the indispensable backbone of Internet and modern information infrastructures. Coherent optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) has recently received much attention as a candidate for high-speed long-haul transmission due to its key advantages: resilience to chromatic dispersion (CD) and polarization mode dispersion (PMD), high spectral efficiency, and low digital computation complexity. However, the CO-OFDM system is highly sensitive to the carrier frequency offset (CFO), which is induced by the incoherence between the signal laser at the transmitter and the local oscillator (LO) at the receiver. The frequency offset normalized by the OFDM subcarrier spacing can be divided into a fraction part and an integer part. If the CFO is not compensated properly, even 0.01 normalized CFO can result in severe performance degradation. Therefore, the CFO estimation and mitigation is an inevitable step for the digital signal processing at the receiver. In addition to the CFO compensation, timing synchronization is another essential step to find the correct starting position of the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) window. The occurrence of timing estimation error will cause the shift of OFDM sequence, thus leads to severe BER performance degradation. Various approaches have been applied to realize the timing and frequency synchronization, which have drawbacks of limited estimation accuracy, large overhead, or high complexity though. We will develop our timing and frequency synchronization algorithms for CO-OFDM systems to improve the estimation performance. We will be the first to apply the matched filtering (MF) technique for carrier recovery, to estimate the timing offset and frequency offset jointly for CO-OFDM systems, which can theoretically obtain the optimal solution with low complexity. Based on MF, we propose to design both data-aided and blind algorithms, which can reduce the computational complexity by more than 50%, double the effective transmission bit rate, and improve the Mean Square Error (MSE) performance of both timing and frequency synchronization, compared with the conventional synchronization algorithms. We will also design novel coding structures to produce the code words in certain format, which is convenient and efficient for the joint timing and frequency synchronization, increasing the estimation accuracy, and at the same time improving BER performance. We will study the details of our proposed techniques by both simulations and experiments. The research has both academic impacts and practical applications. 隨著數據流量的指數增長，尤其是多媒體應用對超寬頻寬的需求，超高速光纖通信系統已經成為互聯網和現代信息基礎設施不可或缺的支柱。相干光正交頻分復用 (CO-OFDM) 作為高速長途傳輸的候選者，受到了很多關注，因為它具有以下關鍵優勢：對於色散 (CD) 和偏振模色散 (PMD) 的容忍性、高光譜效率和低數字計算複雜度。相干光正交頻分復用系統對載波頻率偏移 (CFO) 非常敏感，而頻率偏移是由發射機的信號激光器與接收機的本地振盪器 (LO) 之間的不相干引起的。由OFDM子載波間隔歸一化的頻率偏移可分為分數部分和整數部分。如果CFO沒有得到適當的補償，即便是0.01倍歸一化CFO也會導致嚴重的性能下降。因此，對接收機進行數字信號處理時，CFO的估計和補償是不可避免的步驟。另外，找到正確的離散傅里葉變換 (DFT) 窗口，也就是說定時同步，是在接收機信號處理時另一個必要的步驟。定時估計的誤差會導致OFDM序列的移位，從而導致誤碼率性能的嚴重下降。迄今為止，已有很多種方法來實現定時和頻率同步，但仍存在估計精度不高、開銷大、複雜度高等缺點。 我們提出用於CO-OFDM系統的聯合定時與頻率同步算法，以提高系統估計性能。首先，我們利用匹配濾波 (MF) 技術來進行載波恢復，聯合估計CO-OFDM 系統中的時間偏移與頻率偏移，從而得到可用低複雜度實現的理論上的最優解。基於匹配濾波技術，我們進一步提出盲估及非盲估算法，以實現50%以上的複雜度降低，並將有效傳輸速率提高一倍且提高時頻同步的均方誤差 (MSE)性能。我們還將設計新的編碼結構來生成特定格式的碼字，以實現方便高效的時頻估計，以及提高估計精度以及誤碼性能。我們將通過仿真及實驗來驗證所提出的算法。該研究兼具理論意義和實際應用價值。

15200718.label: Realisation of objectives
15200718.value: Until now, we have successfully achieved the goals of this project, and both the experiment and simulation works have been conducted to obtain significant results and achieve the corresponding objectives. The project until now is completed in accordance with the schedule and arrangements, and we believe that the completion of this project can bring contributions to the coherent optical frequency-division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) systems, especially for achieving ultra-high speed, ultra-large capacity and ultra-long distance optical transmissions. For objectives 1, 2 and 5, we start conceptually with the idea of first computing L replicas of the original orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) spectrum, where L is a power of two and is assumed sufficiently large. This is done by padding (L-1)N zeros to the end of the N received noisy OFDM samples, where N is the number of OFDM subcarriers. By computing the LN-point discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of these LN samples, we get L replicas of the DFT of the original OFDM spectrum, where each replica corresponds to the DFT for one hypothesized value of the carrier frequency offset (CFO) and the set of possible CFO values is 〖{l/L}〗_(l=0)^(L-1) . We select the most probable replica by choosing the one that is at the minimum Euclidean distance from the original OFDM spectrum, which leads to a matched filter (MF) operation in the frequency domain in either a blind or a data-aided manner. Building on this MF concept, we then develop a joint maximum likelihood (ML) estimator for the timing offset (TO), CFO and carrier phase offset (CPO) for CO-OFDM system. The novelty here is that the TO and the CPO are estimated efficiently as the frequency and phase of a complex sinusoid observed in noise via either a time-domain or a frequency-domain approach. The resulting joint CFO, CPO and TO estimator is simpler than existing estimators, both conceptually and in implementation. A much simpler sequential approach in which we first decide on the CFO and then perform a joint TO and CPO estimation is also proposed. Also, we derive the Cramer-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) to give benchmarks of the performance of our proposed algorithms. For objectives 3 to 5, we start from the concept of matched filter, then design a likelihood ratio test (LRT)-based blind CFO estimator. Firstly, we compensate for the time-domain received signal by using a hypothesized value of CFO. Then the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is performed to obtain the spectrum. Next, the zero-information in real and imaginary parts of the effective data subcarriers is detected by LRT. Finally, the power fluctuations of zero-information are used to estimate CFO, which is the one that minimizes the average power of the detected zero-information in the real parts and imaginary parts. To further simplify the CFO estimation algorithm, we propose an LRT-based simplified fine CFO estimator (LRT-SFE), which reduces complexity by approximating the cost function as a cosine function and deriving the closed-form expression of CFO estimate using three arbitrary test values. The blind zero-information detection procedure transfers the LRT-based methods to a sort of semi-blind estimator, which improves estimation accuracy, and the optimal threshold derived by LRT makes the proposed methods robust to various modulation formats. The simulation and experiment results verify that the proposed methods are computationally efficient, accurate, flexible to different modulation formats, and can tolerate LPN, AWGN, and CD. At the mean squared error (MSE) of 10−4, the SNR gain of LRT-SFE is up to 6.5 dB compared to other blind estimators. Apart from the above static estimation algorithms, we also investigate the dynamic tracking schemes. We propose a dynamic joint FO and LPN tracking method using a number-theoretic net-based Gaussian particle filter (NT-GPF). The NT-net generates particles on an ellipse for a given bivariate normal distribution, which can help to improve the estimation efficiency and noise tolerance of the proposed algorithm compared to conventional Bayesian filtering-based methods. The proposed method achieves accurate FO and LPN tracking with only a small number of particles. Additionally, a recursive signal detection algorithm is proposed to enhance system performance. The results demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the NT-GPF, which outperforms the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and Gaussian particle filter (GPF) methods under 4/16-QAM modulation and the combined laser linewidth of 200 kHz and 1 MHz. Then, we further propose an H∞ filter-based approach to dynamically and jointly track the CFO and LPN for CO-OFDM systems. Firstly, by solving the min-max optimization problem with a given threshold, we can recursively update the prior state information and the H∞ gain, thereby obtaining the posterior state estimate. The min-max optimization problem protects the tracking performance from severe noise disturbances, which illustrates the robustness of the proposed H∞ filter algorithm. Secondly, after compensating for the CFO in the received signal, we apply a decision-feedback method to accurately detect the bit sequence. The unknown transmitted OFDM symbol is firstly determined by compensating the coarse LPN estimate based on the averaged phase estimates on the previous OFDM symbol. A fine LPN estimation is then conducted by utilizing the H∞ filter according to the newly determined OFDM transmitted symbol. Thirdly, the CRLBs and Bayesian CRLB (BCRLB) are derived to evaluate and verify the state estimation performance of the proposed H∞ filter. Finally, comparing with conventional Bayesian filters such as EKF and GPF, as well as the classical Schmidl’s method, experiment results demonstrate that the proposed H∞ filter can obtain the MSEs of CFO and LPN converging to the CRLBs and BCRLB even in the appearance of 20 dB external noise disturbance and residual CD. For objectives 6 and 7, we try to solve the problem that the previously proposed MF-based blind algorithm is sensitive to the modulation format, especially the MQAM and MAPSK formats. The Trellis code is utilized to firstly divide the MQAM or MAPSK-modulated signal to several subsets based on their radius inside the constellations. Then, the modulated symbols that are on the same constellation circle will be modulated to a QPSK modulation format. The advantage of conducting such a modulation manner is to enlarge the Euclidean distance between the constellation points, thus improving its robustness to the disturbances such as CD, residual CFO, laser phase noise and AWGN. In addition to the robustness, the utilization of Trellis code can also overcome the drawback of the MF-based blind algorithm by reorganizing the received spectrum with different amplitude levels, which can help to obtain the MSE performance under MQAM or MAPSK the same as that of MPSK. The performance of the proposed algorithm is verified in a 16-QAM-modulated 88.9 Gb/s CO-OFDM system. The simulation results show that under 16-QAM modulation, the MSE of the proposed Trellis-coded CFO estimator is nearly one-order lower than that of the traditional MF-based blind estimator and possesses a better tolerance to the CD, LPN and AWGN. In conclusion, the proposed joint timing and frequency synchronization algorithms for CO-OFDM have met up with the objective of this project and some extended results were also obtained, which are not only useful for carrier recovery in CO-OFDM systems, but also applicable for visible light communications and optical fiber sensing.

15200718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200718.value: 1. A joint ML estimator for the CFO, CPO and TO of CO-OFDM system is proposed. The resulting receiver is straightforward to implement, although it can be computationally heavy. But the sequential estimator is much simpler computationally, and its performance loss is small compared to the performance of the optimum joint estimator at high SNR. Also, the experimental results show that the estimation performance of the sequential approach is more robust to the CD and the fiber nonlinearity. (No. 12 conference paper) 2. An LRT-based blind CFO estimator for CO-OFDM is proposed. To further simplify CFO estimation algorithm, we also propose LRT-SFE by approximating the cost function as a cosine function. The blind zero-information detection procedure transfers the LRT-based methods to a sort of semi-blind estimator, which improves estimation accuracy, and the optimal threshold derived by LRT makes the proposed methods robust to various modulation formats. The simulation and experiment results verify that the proposed methods are computationally efficient, accurate, flexible to different modulation formats, and can tolerate LPN, AWGN, and CD. (No. 14 journal paper) 3. An NT-GPF for dynamic estimation of FO and LPN is developed. Based on the concept of uniform design, the NT-net can uniformly generate particles on an ellipse for a given bivariate normal distribution. As a result, the NT-GPF can achieve accurate FO and LPN tracking with only a small number of particles, which greatly improves the estimation efficiency and noise tolerance compared with the conventional GPF. The results demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the NT-GPF, which outperforms the EKF and GPF methods under 4/16-QAM modulation and the combined laser linewidth of 200 kHz and 1 MHz. (No. 12 journal paper) 4. An H∞ filter-based approach is proposed to dynamically and jointly track the CFO and LPN for CO-OFDM systems. The results show that the proposed H∞ filter algorithm not only has a fast steady-state convergence rate, but also possess excellent tolerance to the external noise disturbance and CD. The MSE of H∞ filter is nearly 10 dB lower than that of EKF with the appearance of 20 dB noise disturbance, and H∞ filter can always achieve the best performance of CFO and LPN estimation, which converges to the CRLBs and BCRLB, under uncertain noise statistics. After 400-km transmission, the BER of H∞ filter is close to 1E−3 due to its accurate estimation and compensation for the CFO and LPN. (No. 11 journal paper)

15200718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200718.value: Based on the successful completion of this research, there is significant potential for further development not only in CO-OFDM systems but also in other optical communication systems like single carrier systems, polarization-division multiplexing (PDM) systems, and so on. One further development is implementing the proposed algorithms in practical systems. This would involve investigating the performance of the proposed algorithms in more complex and realistic scenarios, considering practical impairments such as fiber nonlinearities, phase noise, and polarization effects. Another potential area for development is the investigation of more advanced tracking schemes for dynamic synchronization in CO-OFDM/ single carrier/ PDM systems. While the proposed algorithms have demonstrated accuracy and efficiency in tracking timing offset, carrier frequency offset and laser phase noise, there may be room for improvement in terms of tracking speed and noise tolerance. Further research could explore the use of machine learning algorithms or deep learning models to improve accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, the proposed Trellis coding techniques have shown promising results in improving the estimation accuracy and MSE performance of the algorithms. Additional research could explore the use of more advanced coding techniques, such as LDPC coding, Turbo coding, or Cyclic codes.

15200718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200718.value: This project focuses on improving the performance of coherent optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) communication system, which takes the advantages of coherent detection and high spectral efficiency but is sensitive to frequency and timing offset. Thus, we develop matched filtering and coding algorithms to achieve the timing and frequency synchronization of the signals being transmitted to reduce signal detection errors and improve the overall system performance. This can significantly increase the accuracy and reliability of the optical communication systems. Our research involved both theoretical analysis and practical experiments to test the algorithms in different scenarios. The developed algorithms and techniques can be implemented to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of communication systems that rely on CO-OFDM, which are used in a wide range of applications such as Internet and telephone networks. By improving the accuracy and reliability of these systems, the research can help to support faster, more reliable communication and enable new applications and services that rely on high-speed data transfer. Overall, this research has the potential to contribute to ultra-high speed, ultra-large capacity and ultra-long distance optical transmissions.

15201118.label: Realisation of objectives
15201118.value: With respect to Objective 1, we have studied the application of physical-layer network coding (PNC) in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications to accommodate the time-critical nature of vehicular networks in [1]. The idea can theoretically reduce the transmission latency by 50%, thus alleviating the short contact time issues caused by high-speed vehicle motion. Our proposed scheme has been validated through empirical on-road measurements with software radio peripherals. In [4], the implementation of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in 3GPP Cellular-V2X (CV2X) systems was preliminarily investigated. Specifically, we have proposed two NOMA receivers for C-V2X communications based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) and joint decoding (JD) respectively, where the JD method is closely related to the PNC and MUD method. The NOMA schemes offer significant improvement as compared with the conventional orthogonal multiple access (OMA) scheme, and the block error rate (BLER) can be reduced by up to 93.6%. We further extended the work in [6] through proposing a tractable network model to analyze V2X broadcast performance operating in an uncoordinated network with both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) communication links. We have analytically derived the packet delivery ratio (PDR) expressions of these two types of communications for various receiving techniques including the conventional OMA receiver, SIC receiver, and JD receiver. The analytical and simulation results reveal that the NOMA schemes generally outperform the OMA scheme, especially for users suffering from NLOS propagation and long transmission distance. Besides the performance analysis, we have also proposed a data rate optimization scheme to maximize the aggregated goodput. The goodput distribution among the users implies that both the SIC and JD schemes offer good fairness among multiple users, which cannot be achieved by the OMA scheme due to the low PDR of weak users. The choice of receivers is a tradeoff between communication efficiency and computation complexity as a function of the SINR condition and the number of users. The use of network coding (index coding algorithm) for efficient 3D road map data dissemination among intelligent connected vehicles in city-wide vehicular networks was also studied in [2]. The proposed algorithm was validated with empirical mobility traces, 3D LiDAR data, and experimental multi-robotic testbed. The corresponding roadside unit (RSU) deployment strategy for optimizing the amount of information shared from RSU to vehicles was investigated in [7]. In addition, full-duplex two-way relaying cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access based on spectrum sensing (CNOMA-SS) was investigated in [3]. We have derived the analytical ergodic rate and outage probability and validated them via extensive simulation. The corresponding problem on relay selection was studied in [8], which proposed a three-stage relay selection strategy with power allocation (TRSPA) for a spectrum-sensing-based full duplex (FD) user relaying cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (CNOMA) scheme. Such two-way relaying NOMA scheme can be applied in vehicular networks when the line of sight (LOS) between vehicles is blocked by buildings or other obstacles. With respect to Objective 2, we have proposed an ICI-aware approach that jointly achieves accurate channel estimation, signal detection, and channel decoding in [1]. We considered the channel estimation and signal decoding as two optimization problems and resolved them with the expectation maximization algorithm and the belief propagation algorithm, respectively. The proposed approach can efficiently mitigate the negative effect of inter-carrier interference (ICI) (caused by carrier frequency offset) by exploiting both pilot and data tones in channel estimation, detection, and decoding. Both simulation and experiment were conducted to evaluate the proposed approach, and the results reveal that the proposed algorithm outperforms the benchmark that simply treats ICI as Gaussian noise. In [5], We studied carrier frequency offset (CFO) compensation in a two-way relay channel (TWRC) that adjusts the CFO values of the end nodes simultaneously and found that an optimal choice is to yield opposite CFO values in PNC. Particularly, we reveal that pilot insertion could play an important role against the CFO effect, indicating that we may trade more pilots for not just a better channel estimation but also a lower BER at the relay in PNC. With our proposed measures, we conduct simulation using repeat-accumulate (RA) codes and QPSK modulation to show that PNC can achieve a BER at the relay comparable to that of point-to-point transmissions for low to medium CFO levels. We also proposed in [9] a channel estimation method for vehicular networks based on a realistic city model and radio propagation in digital twin simulation and deep neural networks (DNN). Compared with traditional algorithms such as least square and linear minimum mean square error that use 8 pilots at 15 dB SNR, the bit error rate (BER) performance of the proposed city-model-aware (CMA) deep learning method is greatly improved by more than 92.23% and 88.50%, respectively. The performance boost is also more than 32.38% when compared with other generic deep learning based estimators. In addition, we considered the use of the basis expansion model (BEM) to simplify the simulation process of dynamic vehicular channels in the digital twin so that large-scale training data for the deep learning model can be acquired efficiently. Our results show that the CMA DNN method with BEM-approximated dynamic channels sacrifices a small level (i.e., 6.50%) of BER performance, but with greatly reduced computational complexity and runtime (i.e., 33.38%) for efficient operation of the digital twin. The proposed digital twin and deep learning investigation framework in this pioneering work will open up many other research opportunities for connected autonomous vehicles and cooperative driving in future smart cities. 15201118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201118.value: Research Outcomes: 1. We have rigorously studied and optimized the joint-decoding (JD) and successive-interference-cancellation (SIC) NOMA V2X schemes. 2. NOMA V2X scheme applied to index coding at roadside units (RSU) for 3D point cloud data exchange and the corresponding optimal RSU deployment scheme based on vehicles’ trajectories have been developed. 3. Full-duplex two-way relaying cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access based on spectrum sensing (CNOMA-SS) has been investigated 4. The potential of using large-scale joint traffic-network simulation with 3D building models in a digital twin environment for accurate channel estimation in urban vehicular networks has been evaluated. Overall, a number of interesting findings are obtained from the results regarding non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in vehicular networks: 1) for applications requiring a high data rate, the joint-decoding (JD) scheme is always the best choice; 2) for low data rate applications, the successive-interference-cancellation (SIC) scheme requires relatively low complexity and has similar performance compared with the JD scheme; 3) in the extremely low SINR regime, all the three receiving schemes have similar performance and thus the OMA receiver should be applied due to the lowest complexity; 4) when there are a large number of users, JD is the best solution to provide high goodput; 5) as implied from points (1) to (4), we note that the development of a hybrid protocol for NOMA‑based V2X communications is critical to meet the requirements of diverse scenarios; and 6) the random access‑based NOMA schemes can achieve lower transmission latency than the Collision‑Free Scheduled Access (CFSA) scheme in dense vehicular networks.

15201118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201118.value: We believe that our findings on NOMA V2X communications will provide insights into the further development of existing V2X multiple access protocols. This together with the proposed digital twin and deep learning investigation framework are expected to open up a whole new dimension in real‑time vehicular networking for enhancing safety and efficiency in future autonomous cooperative driving, as well as many other research opportunities for connected autonomous vehicles in future smart cities.

15201118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201118.value: With the increasing popularity of inter-vehicle communications and the development of new protocol standards, the city will likely be filled with high-speed wireless users in the future. As the vehicular network gets crowded, the radio bandwidth and other signaling dimensions need to be allocated among multiple users more judiciously so that real-time data can be successfully delivered. The research in this project attempted to harness the interfered or overlapped signals such that multiple users can access the same channel simultaneously and precious contact intervals in vehicular networks can be fully utilized. In essence, we proposed two non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) based vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication schemes, namely, NO-V2X decoded by successive interference cancellation (SIC-V2X) and decoded by joint decoding (JD-V2X). Based on stochastic geometry, we derived and compared the communication performance of both NOMA schemes and the conventional scheme under line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions. In addition, field trials with software-defined radio were performed to experimentally verify the performance of NO-V2X. Our results indicate that the proposed NOMA schemes significantly outperform the conventional scheme, and JD-V2X provides further enhancement compared with SIC-V2X in the high data rate regime. The research outcomes in this project have led to the publication of 7 journal papers (5 of them are in Q1 according to Scopus CiteScore) and 2 conference papers.
