15201418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201418.value: Civil infrastructure systems serve as essential components in a society and therefore their safety and serviceability are of great importance to maintain a civilized society and a productive economy. In the interest of ensuring a safe and reliable operation of the structures and issuing early warnings on damage or deterioration prior to costly repair or even catastrophic failure, structural health monitoring (SHM) technology has been developed and implemented to critical infrastructure systems worldwide in the past two decades. It enables to gain information about the in-service performance of civil structures by offering continuous monitoring with an array of permanently deployed sensors. With the great advances in sensing, communication and signal processing technologies, online SHM systems have been increasingly applied to various civil infrastructure systems in recent years. Central to SHM is the extraction of health-relevant knowledge from sensed data. Despite continuous evolution and development of SHM technology in past years, interpreting a great deal of monitoring data from a sophisticated SHM system to obtain useful information about structural health condition remains a challenge. Due to the complexity of civil structures and various uncertainties arising from environmental variability, modeling error and measurement noise as well as inherent in monitoring data, physical models reflecting the authentic performance of structural systems are difficult to create precisely. As a result, data-driven approaches that use only monitoring data to evaluate structural health status have received much attention recently. Novel model-free, data-interpretation methods which can accommodate and account for uncertainties from various sources are highly desirable in SHM. The research proposed in this project aims to develop a novel damage detection methodology in the context of variational sparse Bayesian learning. The proposed methodology features the following merits: (i) it is model-free without needing a physical model of the structure; (ii) it uses only dynamic response measurements while exempting from excitation/loading information; (iii) data-driven, non-parametric reference models in need for structural damage detection can be formulated using only monitoring data from healthy state in the absence of monitoring data from damaged state; (iv) the formulated models have good generalization (prediction) capability while sparse representation; (v) damage identification is executed in a fully Bayesian framework; and (vi) uncertainties involved in both monitoring data and identification results can be quantified. Real-world monitoring data from an instrumented bridge and from an in-service high-speed train will be utilized to verify the damage/fault detection and discrimination capabilities of the proposed methodology. 本项目將開展以下三個方面的研究：1、通過在稀疏貝葉斯學習中引入確定性的基函數係數，發展基於變分稀疏貝葉斯學習僅利用響應的無模型結構損傷監測方法；2、通過在稀疏貝葉斯學習中引入自適應的基函數係數，發展基於變分稀疏貝葉斯學習僅利用響應的無模型結構損傷監測方法；3、利用斜拉橋和高速列車損傷前后採集到的響應數據，檢驗上述方法的可行性及損傷區分能力。

15201418.label: Realisation of objectives
15201418.value: Objective 1: A framework of Bayesian blind source separation (BSS) was proposed to remedy the deficiencies of traditional BSS techniques. In this framework, the uncertainty and the indeterminacy which have restricted the standard BSS techniques can be quantitatively characterized. By embedding the Gaussian process (GP) prior to this flexible Bayesian model, the source’s temporal characteristic that is usually remarkable in real-time structural health monitoring (SHM) problems is fully captured. To lessen the computational burden of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)-based sampling methods and accelerate the estimation of the GP-BSS model, a variational Bayesian (VB) learning method is developed as a fast alternative to the MCMC approach. A BSS method based on variational autoencoder (VAE) was proposed. This method embeds the Gaussian process regression (GPR) into the latent space of VAE for increasing the separation ability of temporal structure sources. Meanwhile, the length-scale parameters of covariance functions that are difficult to determine are treated as trainable parameters during the model training process, so that suitable covariance functions of the GP can be adaptively obtained. Experimental results show that the proposed method has significant advantages in dealing with source separation tasks under noisy conditions. Two Bayesian approaches, Bayesian generalized linear model (BGLM) and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL), were proposed for characterizing the wind-induced lateral displacement responses of long-span bridges with SHM data. They are fully model-free data-driven approaches, preferable for reckoning the wind-induced total displacement intended for wind-resistant performance assessment. With the measured displacement responses and wind speeds, a BGLM is developed to characterize the nonlinear relationship between the total displacement response and wind speed, where the Bayesian model class selection criterion is adopted to determine the optimal model. In the formulation of SBL, both wind speed and wind direction are treated as explanatory variables to elicit a probabilistic model with sparse structure. A method in the context of SBL was proposed for online assessment of railway wheel conditions using trackside monitoring data. It is a fully data-driven, nonparametric approach without needing a physical model. To enable defect identification using only response measurement, the measured dynamic strain responses of rail tracks during the passage of trains are processed to elicit the normalized cumulative distribution function values representative of the effect of individual wheels, which in conjunction with the frequency points are used to formulate a probabilistic reference model in terms of SBL. Through cleverly realizing sparsity by introducing hyper-parameters and their priors, the SBL makes the resulting model exempt from overfitting and generalize well on unseen data. Only the monitoring data in healthy state are needed in formulating the reference model. A novel Bayesian null hypothesis significance testing in terms of scale-invariant intrinsic Bayes factor is then pursued in the presence of new monitoring data collected from possibly defective wheel(s) to detect wheel defects. Objective 2: Capitalizing on adversarial-training-aided variational autoencoder, a method for tackling both linear and nonlinear BSS problems was proposed in the context of variational inference. To enable the description of possible temporal structure of sources, this approach discards the standard normal prior in latent space commonly used in VAE and instead adopts a parameter-adaptive Gaussian process (GP). By setting trainable variables as the parameters of kernel functions, a suitable covariance matrix of the GP can be adaptively elicited. The nonlinear representation capability of neural networks in VAE endows the proposed approach with the ability to solve nonlinear mixtures. Furthermore, an adversarial-training-based shuffling strategy is embedded in VAE to enhance the independence between the inferred sources in an adversarial manner. Experimental results show that the proposed approach performs well in separating the sources with temporal structure. A novel adaptive modelling framework for sparse polynomial chaos expansion was proposed, which can automatically determine adequate truncation degree and training sample set simultaneously. In this framework, a new basis selection strategy, which leverages basis expansion, pruning and refinement, is pursued to adaptively select the polynomial terms of proper degree during the modelling process. Besides, an outstanding sequential sampling strategy is adopted to collect samples of high quality and in relatively small quantity for training polynomial chaos expansion model, and a sparse representation method, Bayesian compressive sensing, is employed for regression calculation. To reconcile the sequential sampling and adaptive basis selection in a consistent framework, a stability evaluation process which works in parallel with the sequential sampling process is performed. The performance of the proposed adaptive modelling framework is evaluated on two benchmark functions and a physical model. A data-driven, speed-tolerant, and response-only Bayesian-based wheel condition evaluation method is proposed in the context of relevance vector machine (RVM). With the dynamic strain responses collected by a trackside monitoring system, the cumulative Fourier amplitudes (CFA) characterizing the effect of individual wheels are extracted to formulate multiple probabilistic regression models (MPRMs) in terms of multi-kernel RVM, which accommodate both variables of vibration frequency and running speed. Compared with the general single-kernel RVM-based model, the proposed multi-kernel MPRM approach bears better local and global representation ability and generalization performance, which are prerequisite for reliable wheel defect detection by means of data acquired under different running-speed conditions. Objective 3: The two Bayesian models (BGLM and SBL) developed in Objective 1 were applied to forecast the wind-induced displacement responses in extreme typhoon events beyond the monitoring scope, and the predicted displacement responses are contrasted to the finite element analysis results and the design maximum allowable displacement under the serviceability limit state (SLS). The proposed methods are demonstrated using the monitoring data acquired by GPS sensors and anemometers instrumented on a long-span suspension bridge. The results show that the SBL model is superior to the BGLM for wind-induced displacement response prediction and is amenable to SHM-based evaluation of wind-resistant performance under extreme typhoon conditions. The SBL method (Objective 1) and the Bayesian-based RVM method (Objective 2) for online assessment of railway wheel conditions were verified by utilizing real-world monitoring data acquired by a distributed fiber Bragg grating-based trackside monitoring system and comparing with the offline inspection results. In the devised monitoring system, two FBG arrays are deployed along the foot of rail tracks on both sides. Each array contains 21 FBG strain sensors evenly distributed on the rail foot with 0.15m intervals, and such a dense arrangement can characterize abundant wheel defect detection performance. The rail strain data collected under different train speeds are used to verify the above methods. A new statistical decision philosophy was developed to tackle structural damage detection problems defined in the context of novelty detection. In this philosophy, structural damage detection is achieved by deriving the posterior probability of damage presence from the Bayesian testing of two competing hypotheses where the null and alternative hypotheses represent the undamaged and damaged states, respectively. To resolve the tricky problem of prior appropriateness in Bayesian hypothesis testing, a general prior specification criterion is devised based on the notion of risk management, including the risk of false positive indication and the risk of false negative indication. To determine an optimal risk level, the principles of posterior probability difference minimization (PPDM) and posterior probability product maximization (PPPM) are defined. Experimental verification has been conducted by using data obtained from a 5-story steel frame model and a 38-story concrete building model to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed philosophy.

15201418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201418.value: 1. A variational Bayesian (VB) learning-based Bayesian blind source separation (BSS) method, which is able to quantitatively characterize the uncertainty and the indeterminacy and capture the sources’ temporal structure (Patent 1 in Part C); 2. A method capable of tackling both linear and nonlinear BSS problems based on adversarial-training-aided variational autoencoder and a shuffling strategy (Patents 2 and 3 in Part C); 3. A sparse Bayesian learning (SBL)-based approach for train wheel defect detection. It is shown that with the use of dynamic strain measurement data from a trackside monitoring system, this method can reliably detect the defect/fault of train wheels in an online manner (Journal paper 2 in Part C); 4. A sparse Bayesian learning (SBL)-based fully model-free data-driven approach for characterizing wind-induced lateral displacement responses of long-span bridges with SHM data and assessing the wind-resistant performance in extreme typhoon events. It is shown that this method is superior to the Bayesian generalized linear model (BGLM) in wind-induced displacement response prediction (Journal paper 3 in Part C); 5. A method to explore the BSS of heterogeneous structural health monitoring (SHM) data containing non-stationary and temporally discontinuous components (Journal paper 6 in Part C); 6. A data-driven, response-only wheel condition evaluation approach in the context of relevance vector machine (RVM). It is shown that this method is capable of detecting the defect/fault of train wheels using trackside monitoring data obtained under varying train running speeds (Journal paper 7 in Part C); 7. A new statistical decision philosophy tackling structural damage detection problems defined in the context of novelty detection with the proposed principle of posterior probability difference minimization (PPDM) and the principle of posterior probability product maximization (PPPM). It is shown that both the PPDM and PPPM principles can consistently determine the optimal false positive risk in damage detection (Journal paper 10 in Part C); 8. A adaptive modelling framework for sparse polynomial chaos expansion, which can automatically determine adequate truncation degree and training sample set simultaneously. It is shown that the proposed framework outperforms the existing adaptive polynomial chaos expansion modelling technique in terms of modelling precision and convergence rate, and it has similar performance with the sequential sampling-only method while lessening the burden in regression calculation and enabling adaptive determination of the truncation degree (Journal paper 11 in Part C).

15201418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201418.value: 1. In this project, various sparse Bayesian learning-based and variational autoencoder-based blind source separation (BSS) methods have been developed. They are powerful for separating and extracting inherent sources from heterogeneous data, and their use in combination with SHM methods would greatly help improve damage identification accuracy and prevent false alarms. In addition to train wheel fault detection and bridge deck damage detection addressed in this project, the applicability and efficiency of the proposed methods in helping SHM for broader infrastructure systems would be examined in the future; 2. In this project, a Bayesian hypothesis testing (BHT)-based statistical decision philosophy has been put forward to optimally distinguish between undamaged and damaged states of a structure, where a damage-sensitive feature (DSF) is extracted from the collected monitoring data to indicate the health condition of the structure. However, a scalar DSF may not be able to effectively discriminate between undamaged and damaged states of the target structure and a vectorial DSF of high dimension would be favorable. Towards this direction, the BHT-based statistical decision philosophy for structural damage detection will be extended to accommodate high-dimensional DSF in the future.

15201718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201718.value: Marine ports have long been the main gateways for global trade and are critical to economies around the world. However, they are major sources of ship pollution, cargo handling equipment emissions, and noise. When berthing at ports, ships use their diesel auxiliary engines to generate electricity for hoteling, unloading, and loading activities, and they emit huge amounts of greenhouse gases (GHGs), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter (PM), and other harmful pollutants. These emissions can cause adverse impacts on the environment (e.g., climate change, acid rain, water contamination) and contribute to significant health problems for local communities (e.g., premature mortality, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). One effective measure to reduce at-berth emissions is to provide electricity to the ships from the shore-side national grid while turning off the ships’ auxiliary diesel engines at ports, which can significantly reduce the emissions of air pollutants and GHGs. Several issues must be tackled before shore-side power (SP) can be adopted on a global scale. A major issue is the expensive retrofitting process―shore-side electricity supply infrastructure is required at ports, and ships should be retrofitted with equipment that enables the connection to SP. To incentivize SP installation, governments in many countries/regions offer subsidies to ports to promote SP implementation. Another fundamental and inherent issue is the “chicken and egg” dilemma―ports do not install SP infrastructure until ships are SP equipment ready, while ships wait for SP infrastructure to be set up prior to being retrofitted. An effective SP subsidy plan by government should take into account this interactive effect between ports and shipping lines. Concern over the adverse environmental impact calls for scientific approaches in dealing with this problem. The aim of this project is to develop a subsidy program for government that could be a managerial tool to achieve utmost reduction of at-berth emissions. An integrated multistage game theoretic framework will be developed to capture the interaction between government and stakeholders (ports and shipping companies). As the Ministry of Transport of the People’s Republic of China has planned to deploy SP for 50% of berths at major sea ports by 2020, a case study of ports in China (including the Port of Hong Kong) will be conducted to formulate policy measures. This project will be of tremendous value in improving the sustainability of ports and in promoting environmentally friendly, sustainable practices. 海港是國際貿易的門戶，對經濟發展至關重要。與此同時，海港內部的靠泊船舶排放、貨物裝卸設備的排放和噪音也不容忽視。船舶靠泊期間輔機仍然需要消耗柴油為船舶提供電能，並釋放大量的溫室氣體、二氧化硫、氮氧化物、可吸入顆粒物。這些污染物對環境和人類健康造成極大損害。港口為靠港船舶提供岸電，即船舶靠泊後關閉發動機通過城市電網為船舶設備提供電能，能夠有效降低船舶排放。然而，要使用岸電，港口必須安裝昂貴的岸電設備，船舶也必須進行昂貴的岸電改造。為了鼓勵岸電安裝，很多政府機構都提供相應的補貼。推廣岸電的另一個困難是“雞生蛋蛋生雞”問題：如果沒有大量船舶進行岸電改造則港口不願意安裝岸電，而如果沒有大量港口安裝了岸電則船舶不願意進行岸電改造。本課題致力於為政府提供有效的岸電補貼機制以促進岸電的推廣降低靠泊排放。本課題將採用多階段的博弈論對政府、港口、航運公司的相關作用進行建模分析。考慮到中國交通部計畫在2020年底之前在全國50%的主要海港安裝岸電設備，本課題將以中國（包括香港特區）為例做一個案例分析。本課題對提高港口的可持續性發展有積極意義。

15201718.label: Realisation of objectives
15201718.value: The three objectives of this project have been realized on time through the joint effort of all participants. To achieve Objective 1, we first conducted a thorough literature review on shore power management for maritime transportation. From the port and shipping company’s perspectives, decision models were summarized to analyze under what scenarios would the two parties invest in and adopt shore power. Results show that the lack of economic incentives is one of the remained barriers to the application of shore power. Based on the analyses, we have investigated the shore power investment decision making problems from both the shipping line and port authority’s aspects. From the shipping line’s aspect, we have studied the fleet deployment problem including green technology adoption decisions in a shipping network with Emission Control Areas (ECAs). A nonlinear mixed integer programming model was proposed to optimize the fleet deployment, sailing speeds on all legs, timetables, cargo allocation among routes, and berth allocation considering shore power availability. A customized heuristic solution method containing three phases was developed. Numerical experiments were conducted to validate the model and algorithm originally proposed. It is revealed by the results that the three-phase algorithm performs better than the CPLEX method and the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, which are frequently used to solve similar nonlinear problems. Sensitivity analyses show that the price gap between heavy fuel oil (HFO) and marine gas oil (MGO) and the initial installation costs have significant impacts on the adoption of scrubbers and shore power facilities onboard. Meanwhile, the extension of ECAs will encourage the application of scrubbers. From the port authority’s aspect, we have investigated the subsidy plan optimization problem to encourage ships to use shore power while berthing. Considering the uncertainty in energy requirements of ships, we built a stochastic optimization model to balance the environmental benefits and subsidy expenses and recognize the optimal subsidy amounts. Taking advantage of the problem structure, the model was converted into a deterministic one by applying sample average approximation and a binomial distribution. Numerical experiments with government-operated port validate that favorable shore power price and subsidy for visits that use shore power significantly improve the shore power usage ratio. Meanwhile, due to the uncertainty in power demand, an unrealistically high expectation of shore power usage ratio may lead to an extremely high subsidy expenditure and a negative total profit, which are obviously undesirable. Experiments of self-operated port, which does not consider the environmental benefits, reveal that compared to government-operated port, self-operated port makes less effort improving the shore power usage ratio. When the usage ratio reaches a high level, namely most of ship visits choose to use shore power while berthing, the availability of port-side shore power becomes a new problem. Therefore, we have conducted the shore power allocation problem at port to schedule the shore power usage. Considering the limited total power and different proficiencies of seafarers in operating shore power on and off, an integer programming model was proposed to allocate the shore power sockets to users. Results of numerical experiments indicate that the total power limit is a potential bottleneck in shore power management of port. Results obtained in Phase 1 suggest that government subsidies and favorable shore power price are two critical elements in the promotion of shore power. Therefore, in Phase 2, we investigated the shore power deployment problem in maritime transportation and shore power price competition between ports. First, we studied the shore power deployment problem for a government aiming at achieving the utmost reduction of at-berth emissions from ships in a container shipping network. Considering the reaction of port operators and shipping lines’ reaction to shore power deployment, a two-stage optimization model was developed to describe the problem. The shore power application would reach its long-term equilibrium after the network effect brought by the initial deployment. A tailored labeling algorithm was developed based on the decision process of the government, port operators, and shipping lines to obtain the deployment plan that can maximize shore power usage. Various numerical experiments validate our model and algorithm. The significant impacts of the government subsidy and network effect on shore power promotion were also verified. Meanwhile, we also explored the shore power price competition between ports and tried to figure out the impact of shore power price on port selection. A Bertrand model was proposed to identify the optimal shore power price to maximize a port’s total benefits in the competition with other ports in the same group. It turns out that the port authority needs to balance between the marginal profit of selling shore power and the customer loyalty of shipping lines. In Phase 3, to validate the models, algorithms, and analyses obtained, we conducted a case study of the shore power deployment problem based on the real container shipping network in China. From the perspective of the government, we made an effort to identify an effective subsidy plan for shore power installation for the Chinese case. In this case study, the electricity grid is operated by the local government, which sells electricity at a predetermined price to the port authorities. Meanwhile, the purchasing price of shore power for ships are decided by ports. To promote shore power usage, the government provides subsidy to certain ports and shipping routes to fully cover the facility construction cost/ship retrofitting cost. The container shipping network was built based on the shipping lines operated by the biggest shipping company in China, the China Ocean Shipping (Group) Company. Problem scale in this case study exceeds previous ones. Specifically, 91 liner shipping routes from four types, namely the domestic coastal routes, the Yangtze River routes, the Pearl River routes, and the cross-strait routes, and 85 ports (including the Port of Hong Kong) were covered. To justify the subsidy policy, we also estimated the environmental benefits of marine fuels saved by using shore power and conducted cost-benefit analyses. Results show that with three ports and nine routes receiving subsidies, 82 ports, including the Port of Hong Kong, and 88 routes will ultimately choose to construct and use shore power facilities, due to the network effect. This shows the effectiveness of our subsidy plan. Moreover, the environmental benefits achieved are way above the total subsidy expenditure, which validates the subsidy plan from the cost–benefit aspect. Numerical experiments with different subsidy budgets were carried out to analyze its influence on the optimal subsidy plan. Useful managerial insights were obtained. First, a relatively small budget would accomplish the emission reduction task excellently, and it might be unnecessary to spend a large amount of budget on the subsidization. Second, a significantly higher budget will be required for further fuel usage reduction. The subsidy expenditure needs to be considered together with the final bunker reduction, while making the budget. In conclusion, all three objectives haven been finished on schedule. Fruitful results have been obtained to provide constructive suggestions for the government on shore power deployment and subsidy plan decisions. The case study of a Chinese container shipping network validates our models, algorithms, and analyses, yielding a practical deployment plan and managerial insights.

15201718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201718.value: We have proposed a nonlinear mixed integer programming model to identify the optimal fleet deployment along routes (including green technology adoption), sailing speeds on various leges, timetables, cargo allocation among routes, and berth allocation considering the availability of shore power, which minimize the total costs. Due to complexity, we proposed a three-phase heuristic algorithm to solve the model. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our solution method. Influences of marine fuel price, facility installation costs, and ECAs boundary on the adoption of green technologies, including shore power, were also analyzed. A stochastic optimization model considering the uncertainty of electricity requirement of ship visits was developed to optimize the subsidy design for shore power promotion. Taking advantage of historical ship visits, binomial distribution was adopted to handle the chance constraint in the model. Optimal subsidy amounts were obtained for government-operated port, which takes the environmental benefits into consideration, and self-operated port, which only focuses on its own profits, respectively. In addition to the effectiveness of different subsidy policies, we also explored the impacts of unit environmental benefits, electricity cost, fuel price, and shore power usage ratio expectation on the subsidy design. Moreover, an integer programming model was proposed to investigate the shore power scheduling problem at port and identify the optimal allocation plan of shore power sockets. Considering the limited total power and different proficiencies of seafarers, the model maximizes the total shore power usage. A two-stage optimization model was proposed to describe the shore power deployment problem, which identifies the ports and shipping lines to be subsidized. A tailored labeling algorithm was proposed to obtain the optimal solution. Numerical experiments validated our model and solution method. The shore power price competition between ports was also explored, and a Bertrand model was developed to describe the relationship between two adjacent ports in shore power pricing. It is revealed that the marginal profit of selling shore power and the customer loyalty of shipping lines should be considered simultaneously by the port. We conducted a case study of the shore power deployment problem based on a real container shipping network in China. An effective subsidy plan for shore power installation was obtained from the government’s perspective. Results and analyses show the necessity of government subsidy and the significance of the Port of Hong Kong in the Chinese case. This phase validates the models, algorithms, and analyses in Phase 1 and 2.

15201718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201718.value: Freight rate decision can be integrated into the fleet deployment problem considering green technology adoption. In practice, higher freight rate will be acceptable with greener logistics service. Therefore, the freight rate decision and green technology adoption should be considered simultaneously. The integrated problem aims to maximize the total profit and can yield a more profitable fleet deployment plan. To investigate the integrated fleet deployment problem, optimization model considering the pricing strategy will be developed. Game theory will be adopted to describe the relationship between freight rate and shipping demand. A tailored algorithm based on the problem structure and the specific price-demand function will be proposed. Joint optimization of shore power subsidy design of multiple ports can be investigated. If various ports of call along the route provide subsidies to ship visits for using shore power, the shipping company may decide to equip their vessels with shore power facilities or charter in ships already with such equipment. Meanwhile, the shore power price competition under this scenario can be explored. With the joint optimization of various ports, the problem complexity will increase. Game theory models will be developed. More efficient solution methods will be required to handle the interrelationships between ports.

15201718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201718.value: For port areas, for example Hong Kong, ship emissions while berthing has significant impacts on social welfare, due to the dirty marine fuel consumed to power ships at port. Shore power, which refers to providing electricity for ships, is an effective measure to reduce at-berth emissions. However, the installation of shore power systems is barriered by the high construction costs. Meanwhile, existing shore power facilities are facing low usage ratios due to the low cost-effectiveness. To promote shore power and reduce ship emissions in port areas, this research project investigated the shore power deployment problem with the aim to minimize total emissions. We have investigated shore power installation and utilization decisions of shipping lines. Studies on green technology adoption for fleet deployment and subsidy design for shore power usage were conducted, and instructive suggestions were obtained for shipping companies and port authorities. Moreover, we have identified which ports and shipping lines should be equipped with shore power systems and come up with optimal deployment plan for the government. A case study of a Chinese container shipping network, including Hong Kong, was conducted to validate the models and algorithms proposed in this project and yield practical suggestions on shore power deployment.

15203618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203618.value: The thermo-acoustic oscillation (TAO), a self-excited phenomenon generated by the interaction between a heat source and acoustic waves, remains one of the most important and challenging problems, pertinent to numerous applications. Arousing persistent interest in the scientific community, the problem has mostly been addressed using simplified models with assumptions made on particular system configurations, due to the complex and multi-disciplinary nature of the problem and the limited methods available. A thorough literature review shows that the lack of (or the insufficient) consideration of the multiple time delays as well as the coupling among various system components including TAO control devices is one of the major flaws in the existing work. Recent work also shows that these factors significantly impact on the system behavior. Therefore, their proper apprehension in the modelling and analyses is of paramount importance for the thorough understanding of the underlying physics and the development of control means for TAO suppressions. Capitalizing on our previous work on the delay differential equation theories and acoustic coupling analyses, this project sets the objective of establishing a general modelling and analysis framework in which both the multi-delay and the full coupling are meticulously considered. The proposed general methodology is first demonstrated using the classical 1D configuration as a benchmark, along with the explorations and analyses of some key physical phenomena. The methodology is then extended to general 3D cases in which various TAO control devices are included in the modelling framework through a unified boundary impedance description. The proposed model allows the prediction and characterization of typical TAO phenomena such as instability onset, limit cycle behavior and mode classifications. Meanwhile, it allows the examination and the tuning of various control devices, exemplified by passive acoustic resonators, micro-perforated liners and active feedback controls, for TAO suppressions. The model and the revealed phenomena are finally validated and verified by experiments. The significance of the project lies in its direct applicability to a wide range of problems related to engine combustion systems and domestic devices, which are of direct benefit to both Hong Kong and beyond. 热声振动(Thermo-Acoustic Oscillation，简记为TAO)是一种因热源和声波相互作用而产生的一种自激振荡现象，它会对系统的结构和性能等造成重要影响。在工程实际中存在有大量的热声振动系统，从家用设备到大型引擎，这些系统往往构型复杂，对其进行深入的科学研究需要多种学科知识交叉，是极富挑战性的工作。现有关于热声振动的研究工作中，往往将热声振动系统简化为一维的简单构型，而对于对热声振动系统中的复杂构型、多时滞效应、子系统相互耦合以及热声振动控制等问题，研究还相当缺乏。本项目组成员具有长期关于时滞现象和声学耦合现象的研究背景，已有的研究发现，上述现象对于热声振动具有重要的影响。基于此，本项目以能量法为基础，致力于建立一般化的系统建模方法，着重考虑多时滞效应和声学耦合效应，在此基础上对热声振荡的物理本质和产生机理进行研究，并提出相应的热声振动控制方法。项目的研究工作将首先以经典的一维构型为主，对热声振动的稳定性和极限环等关键物理现象进行机理解释和分析，着重研究多时滞效应和声学耦合效应等对系统行为的影响；然后将该能量建模和分析方法拓展到一般性的、包含控制元件的多维系统，其中控制元件以边界阻抗的形式进行描述，以保证对多种控制方法如声共振器、微穿孔板甚至主动控制方法等的统一建模，并实现建模的模块化。项目的建模和机理研究等工作，将同时进行理论分析和实验验证。

15203618.label: Realisation of objectives
15203618.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out, in relation to the research objectives are summarized as follows: We first focuse on 1D Rijke tube. For that, a modified Fourier series solution for the thermo-acoustic modal characteristics analyses is established. The proposed model tackles the arbitrary impedance boundaries by introducing two boundary smooth auxiliary polynomials to the traditional Fourier series, which overcomes the differential discontinuity issue encountered at the impedance boundaries. The coupled thermo-acoustic system is then characterized and cast into a quartic matrix characteristic equation, which gives the modal parameters with high computational efficiency, rather than solving a transcendental equation or resorting to FEM method. The effectiveness of the proposed model is demonstrated and validated against the results from the literature, in terms of modal parameters like frequencies, growth rates and mode shapes. This part of the work has been published in a few journals as listed in the outcome section. The potential use of micro-perforated-panel absorbers (either as liners or absorbers) in a flow duct has been systematically investigated. This part of the work is then directly used to alter or control the thermo-instability in the duct and a later stage. More specifically, 3D CFD simulations are conducted on a MPP hole with a backing space in a flow duct. Numerical results allow identifying the flow velocity gradient in the viscous sublayer as the intrinsic flow parameter and show its linear relationship with a flow-related term in the acoustic resistance formula. Through a linear regression analysis, a new acoustic resistance formula is established. The validity of the impedance formula is demonstrated through comparisons with existing results and experimental data, showing good agreement and superiority in terms of the prediction accuracy over existing model. Extensive experimental validation in terms of acoustic impedance as well as sound absorption inside a tube are carried out. This part of work has been published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, and Applied Acoustics. We have developed the efficient computation methods by considering the time delay effects and verified its accuracy using typical examples with a paper published in Journal of Scientific Computing. More specifically, time delay modelling and system solution have been investigated. In particular, a mathematical framework has been established, which extends the definite integral stability method to calculate the characteristic roots of both retarded and neutral multi-delay systems. Based on the root shifting technique, the extended method first identifies the closely approximate real parts of the characteristic roots, and then calculate the complete characteristic roots by using the iteration method. Two algorithms are proposed to carry out the extended definite integral method, of which the latter one is more recommended for use. Other than MPP control, the concept of using metamaterials, in form of lined membrane and resonators have also been exploited, providing a series of effective TAO control methods, verified numerically and against other experimental results reported in the literature. More specifically, we studied the acoustic bandgap formation in a duct with periodically flush-mounted flexible walls, subject to a stream-wise temperature variation. A numerical model, based on a piecewise treatment of the arbitrary temperature gradient, is proposed for the accurate prediction of sound propagation in a complex thermal environment. Effects of the system quasi-periodicity due to the temperature change on the bandgap formation, as well as possible mitigation measures through parameter tuning, are revealed. Then, thermoacoustic oscillation and instability are systematically explored. Investigations on the interplay among different types of modes, their evolution process and coupling with add-on control devices are of vital importance to guide the development of proper control strategies. Using a linear heat release n-τ model inside a duct, these issues are investigated in this paper based on a fully coupled energy-based model. Studies allow the classification and quantification of different types of eigen-modes, as well as their stability and controllability features. Using flush-mounted flexible membranes over the duct wall, possible suppressions of unstable modes and the underlying control mechanisms are revealed with particular focus on cases involving small time delay and interaction indices. This part of the work was published in the very top journal in Combustion.

15203618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203618.value: The proposed modified Fourier series method allows establishing a quantitative relationship between the modal stability of the IE tube with the heat release position and the pure acoustic mode shape (without heat source). It is shown that the TAI is triggered when the heat source is placed at those locations where the sound pressure is strengthened for lossless boundaries. For the non-dissipative case, an abrupt change of thermo-acoustic stability appears around the characteristic impedance of the acoustic medium; and for its dissipative counterpart, a common stable zone for the first two thermo-acoustic modes can be achieved through an appropriate matching combination of real and imaginary parts of the boundary impedance. Thus, to obtain an enlarged stable range of the thermo-acoustic modes in a combustion system, a due consideration of the whole set of system parameters, such as the heating position and boundary impedance variation range as well as their interaction, is of paramount importance for the TAI control. The proposed computational method with time delay proves to be accurate and efficient in dealing with TAO problems. The original definite integral stability method is derived and simplified from the Argument Principle. It holds the advantages of easy coding and high efficiency, and increasing the number of delays does not raise the difficulty for its implementation. Compared to the original method, the extended one calculates all the rightmost and non-rightmost roots in an arbitrary and bounded area in the complex plane, no matter the strong stability condition holds or not; also, it is of even simpler testing integrand and smaller integral interval, and hence improves the computational efficiency more. Moreover, the proposed method calculates all the roots in a uniform way with no extra strategies being used, it is not needed to determine the accumulation points, or to find the rightmost roots’ boundary; in a contrary, this method poses an efficient way to find the accumulation points of a multi-delayed NDDE. This part of the work lays the theoretical foundation for dealing with any system with delay, including the thermos-acoustic systems which are investigated in this project. Studies on meta-material TAO control show that, on the top of the resonance bandgap, Bragg reflection bandgap can still be created despite the system quasi-periodicity. In addition to an alteration to the bandgap central frequency due to the temperature-induced acoustic wavelength changes inside the duct, the bandwidths of the bandgaps are also adversely affected, especially when the temperature gradient is large. Numerical analyses show the possibility of tuning and customizing the bandgap formation through a proper selection of the lattice distance and the structural parameters. A combined tuning strategy would warrant a merging of the bandgaps, adjustment of their central frequencies as well as an enlargement of the bandwidth for a given temperature variation range through creating a favorable coupling between the Bragg reflections and the local resonances of the flexible walls. TAO analysis shows that thermoacoustic instability of the system can be controlled via creating strong vibro-acoustic coupling, via two different physical processes for acoustic and intrinsic modes. For the former, the acoustic modal pressure distribution should be positively altered in the vicinity of the heat source to create a favorable pressure state scenario, in agreement with Rayleigh criterion. For the latter, control is achieved indirectly through a proper alteration of the nearby acoustic modes, thus affecting their coupling with the targeted intrinsic mode. In both cases, a successful suppression of the thermoacoustic modal instability can be materialized through a proper adjustment of the physical parameters of the membranes and their installation locations.

15203618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203618.value: Through four years of research, our group is now regarded as one of the most active research groups in the vibration and acoustic area. Apart from the academic reputation gained out of this effort, we have successfully attracted strong interest from a number of companies, who decided to support our research through collaborative/consulting projects, which shows the huge application potentials of the technology. This includes our on-going collaborations with Midea Ltd, one of the largest houseware products in China. The company is interested in exploring the technology for conceiving better and sound-proofing products and thermos-acoustic instability control. On-going collaboration is taking place with more opportunities to be materialized. The potential application of the technology goes way beyond this. In fact, vibration and noise reduction based on TAO technology start to flourish in recent years, with significant impact in many application areas ranging from mechanical, civil, aeronautical and naval engineering. We’ll explore these opportunities in years to come.

15203918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203918.value: Conventional design assumes joints as pinned, rigid or occasionally partially rigid to determine the bending moment and force diagrams for member design after which the joints are designed accordingly to satisfy the moment and shear forces at joints. This approach was noted to be inefficient and unreliable because the stiffness of the joints may not be the same as the assumed joint stiffness commonly as pinned or rigid. The proposer notices that many collapses of shallow domes such the ones in Netherland on 7th July 2011, among others, during heavy snow, and recently on 2nd May 2016 in City University in Hong Kong showed the danger of this structural form could be related to the joint stiffness assumptions. The second-order direct analysis has been included in the local design code of which the proposer is the first principal consultant (see http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/index_crlist.html ). This project proposes a new and alternative design approach of designing the joints first and evaluate it stiffness based on which the members are designed in size to suit the moment and buckling requirement via the section capacity check embedded in the concept of second-order direct analysis. Secondly, a new joint type of using pre-load high strength bolts with welds is developed with properties including strength, stiffness and ductility documented for uses by engineers in future. This new joint type using pre-load bolts and welds simultaneously to share load is proposed and it could allow more room for constructing an innovative structure. For some buckling sensitive structures like space frames, the effects of joint stiffness affects greatly the buckling loads and this investigation was not much focused in the past since most semi-rigid frame analysis is concentrated on beam-to-column connections. Therefore, the present project proposes designing a structure based on pre-designed joints and applied it to not only conventional steel buildings, but also to space frames and domes. Although some research was conducted on load sharing of weld and high-strength bolt, the work mostly did not include stiffness and ductility so the present study is to fill this important gap. The objectives of this project can be summarized below. 1. Develop a joint-based design philosophy for future structural engineering design 2. Creation of design for joints composed of welds and high-strength bolts in terms of strength, stiffness and ductility and 3. Enhance the power and applicability of second-order direct analysis for frame with semi-rigid joints. 傳統的設計中通常首先假設結構中的節點是鉸接，剛接或者半剛接 再通過計算分析得到構件所承受的内力后，對構件進行設計，最後 根據受力情況設計節點。但是這一設計方法不僅效率低下，而且存 在安全隱患；因為實際的節點剛度其實並不是像設計中通常假設的 那樣完全鉸接或者完全剛接。申請人註意到很多淺穹頂結構倒塌事 故的發生都和節點剛度的不合理假設有關，例如2011年7月7日發生 在荷蘭由大雪引起的事故和2016年5月2日發生在香港城市大學的事 故。二階直接分析法已被納入到本地規範，在該規範的編寫過程 中，申請人作為首席顧問參與其中 詳見 http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/index_crlist.html 本項目將會提出一個新的結構設計方法，該方法先對節點進行設計 再根據節點的實際剛度得到結構構件的受力情況，然後結合二階直 接分析法對構件進行設計。本項目也將研發一種新型節點形式 這一新型的節點形式將會綜合性地使用預應力高強螺栓和焊接來 控制節點的強度、剛度和延展性以供未來的工程使用。這一新型 的節點因為結合了預應力高強螺栓和焊接的優點，所以所占空間 小，因而可以節省大量建築空間，並且有利於未來新型結構體系 的發展和應用。對於一些對構件屈曲較為敏感的結構，例如空間 框架，節點剛度將會對構件的屈服承載力產生很大影響。現有的 大多數半鋼節點研究的研究重點都是集中在梁上，因而此方面將 不會是本項目的研究內容。本項目的研究重點在於提出一個新的 基於預設計節點的結構設計方法，且該結構設計方法不僅可以適 用於傳統的鋼結構還能應用於空間框架和穹頂結構。雖然已經有 個別學者對焊縫和高強螺栓的結合進行了研究但是他們的工作很 少會涉及到節點的剛度和延展性，而本項目將會通過研究來填補 這一空缺。總之，本項目的目標可以總結如下：1. 為未來的工程 設計提供一個基於節點設計的新型設計理論；2. 發明一個綜合使 用預應力高強螺栓和焊接來控制節點的強度、剛度和延展性的新 型節點設計方法；以及，3.加強二階直接分析法在含有半鋼節點 的框架中的應用。

15203918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203918.value: The findings from this project show joint stiffness is important in affecting the safety of a building and a frame. Its consideration is important if safety and economy of designing a frame are targeted to achieve. Its review further indicates that very few, if not nil, structures to date are designed to allow for finite joint stiffness and the current design only assumes pinned or rigid joint stiffness which are unrealistic in practice. The method developed in this project could be applied to bolted and welded joints. The work was used in design of the MGM roof in Macau which is currently recorded as the world's longest roof in Guinness record. A research paper published in the proceedings of an European conference attached with this report describes this project with acknowledgement to GRF and this project.

15203918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203918.value: The work should be expanded and adopted in code of practice for structural design of steel and composite structures so engineers could make use of it for designing structures more safely and economically. Very often, engineers over-design a structure by using more materials in order to ensure safety but it is cost-ineffective with safety level not enhanced as more materials are put to wrong locations. This is because the joint stiffness is not considered in the engineers' design and it affects the design accuracy considerably. So the engineers may base on wrong and inaccurate analysis results for their design which then becomes unsafe and uneconomical. The research outcome should be shared with all engineers involved in structural design.

15203918.value: The project introduces a new concept of semi-rigid design to account for realistic joint behaviour in designing a structure and it will significantly not only lower the weight of materials used and subsequently the cost of a structure, but also enhance the safety level of the structure as we could know more accurately and realistically the structural behaviour and load carrying capacity of a structure which can be a building, a bridge, a stadium etc. The research outcome was used in design of the MGM roof in Macau which is currently recorded as the world's longest roof in Guinness record and a research paper about the design was published in the proceedings of an European conference.

15204018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204018.value: Thanks to the rapid advance of artificial intelligence technologies, there is a recent explosion of interest in research and development of social conversation machines (aka. chatting machines) that can freely and appropriately converse to humans in a natural language. As the underlying support, natural language understanding and generation techniques undoubtedly play the central role. To equip machines with conversational intelligence, considerable efforts have been made to develop neural conversation models to generate fluent and relevant responses to the past conversation utterance(s). Despite the remarkable progress, it is still far from the level of human communication. In our opinion, an import but currently overlooked aspect of social conversation is emotion. Emotional interaction plays an important role in human conversations especially for social purpose. It directly affects the way people interact with each other. Thus a human-like chatting machine must be empowered with the necessary emotional intelligence in order to offer the continuous and enjoyable conversation experience. Not to mention how significant it is in the applications like accompanying lonely elderly, providing consulting services and appeasing angry customers. There is a practical need to develop novel emotion-enhanced social conversation models that enable machines to converse to humans properly in both content and emotion. This is exactly what this project is targeted to. However, effectively enhancing the state-of-the-art conversation models with the emotion element is nontrivial. The expected models must be able to perceive and express emotion in words. They should also have certain mechanisms to incorporate emotion inference, reasoning and control capabilities. To develop emotion-enhanced models, we focus on emotion management and emotion-directed text generation. In particular, we explore (1) how to wisely determine the favorite machine emotions that directly react to human expressed emotions and/or potentially trigger/avoid certain human emotional consequences in the future; (2) how to integrate commonsense knowledge that connects causes and consequences to facilitate emotion reasoning; (3) how to accurately reflect the desired emotions in machine-generated utterances depending on the conversation contexts. To promote continuous and harmonious emotional interactions, it is also our aim to move forward from mainstream context-oriented response modeling towards far-sighted interaction-oriented conversation modeling. Our research contributes to build the anticipated emotional chatting machines that can engage people in the nice and thoughtful conversations. It has values in a wide range of applications involving emotion care and also facilitates the research development of machine emotional intelligence. 鑑於先進人工智能技術的迅猛發展，近年來，人們對可以自由運用自然語言恰當地與人進行交談的社交會話機器人（又稱聊天機器人）的研究和開發產生了濃厚興趣。其中，自然語言理解和自然語言生成技術無疑起著核心支持作用。為了使機器人具有會話智能，研究人員已做出相當努力，開發出一系列基於神經網的對話模型以達到自動生成符合對話語境的相關機器回應。儘管取得了顯著進展，但機器人的聊天能力仍遠未達到人類交流的水平。 我們認為，目前研究尚缺少對情緒因素（社交對話中的一個非常重要的因素）的重視，眾所周知，情感互動在人類對話中起著重要作用，尤其是以社交為目的對話。它直接影響著人們相互交流的方式。因此，必須賦予聊天機器一定的類似於人類的情商，才能為用戶提供持續且愉快的對話體驗。機器情商在伴隨孤獨老人、提供諮詢服務和安撫情緒激動顧客等應用中的重要性更是毋庸置疑。開發新型情感社交對話模型令機器人能夠在內容和情感中正確地與人交談具有廣泛的實際應用價值。 然而，利用情感元素有效地增強對話模型並非易事。預期的模型必須能夠感知和表達情感，還應該具備相應機制來提升情感推理和管控能力。為了開發情感增強對話模型，我們將聚焦於情感管理和情感導向的文本生成。我們將重點探索（1）如何智能地確定機器情感，以對人所表達的情感作出恰當的反應，並且能夠有意識地主動激發或者避免人在聽到機器話語之後的情感後果;（2）如何整合連接因果關係的常識知識，實現情感推理;（3）如何根據會話背景知識準確地反映機器話語中的所需情感，以促進持續和諧的情感互動。 我們的研究有助於構建情感聊天機器，得以讓人享受與機器的愉快對話。該研究對其他涉及情感護理的應用開發亦具有價值，並有助於機器情感智能的研究發展。

15204018.label: Realisation of objectives
15204018.value: The project “Towards Emotion-Enhanced Social Conversation Machines” was proposed in November 2017, funded in June 2018, commenced in January 2019, and competed in December 2022. Since the proposal was submitted to RGC in 2017, the research on machine response generation has been rapidly developed. The neural network sequence-to-sequence (aka. encoder-decoder) framework has become the de facto standard setup. Based upon the sequence-to-sequence framework, two main research issues have been addressed in this project: (1) how to identify human’s emotions in his/her conversation utterances, how to infer machine’s suitable response emotions and how to incorporate the emotion information into response generation; (2) how to improve existing sequence-to-sequence models to allow effective reasoning over the external knowledge, including both emotion knowledge and other common-sense knowledge that is relevant to emotion causality. Our researches were mainly developed along these two directions. Despite the significant impact of COVID-19, the dedicated efforts of PhD students and research assistants ensured the smooth and successful completion of these two objectives. Furthermore, we utilized the extended one-year period effectively to expand our research. We progressed from context-oriented response modeling to interaction-oriented dialogue modeling, and from reactive dialogue modeling to proactive dialogue modeling, which emphasizes more on the importance of dialogue strategies. Below, we summarize our primary efforts to achieve the project objectives. Emotional and Empathetic Response Generation We first proposed to integrate emotion classification, emotion prediction and response generation based on a typical sequence-to-sequence framework. Recognizing that various underlying factors influence people’s communication patterns, we tried to capture and utilize these factors to enable conversational machines to generate favorable responses and establish amicable connections with users. We investigated two significant factors in response generation, i.e., emotion and intention. To explore their dependency, we developed a hierarchical variational model that sequentially predicted the emotion and intention to be conveyed in the response. The response was then generated word-by-word based on these predictions. To enhance model training, we proposed a novel adversarial-augmented inference network. The aforementioned work primarily focused on how machines can generate emotional responses by effectively expressing emotions through language. However, this aspect alone is not sufficient. Human communication involves a deeper understanding of the other party’s emotions, the context in which emotions arise, and even the underlying reasons behind those emotions. This understanding enables individuals to provide more appropriate responses, which may not necessarily be emotionally charged but aim to effectively alleviate the other person’s mood. The early work on emotional response generation quickly motivated a new task called empathetic response generation, which aims to understand emotional experience of a user and then reply to acknowledge it appropriately. The key issue was how to extend the encoder to facilitate the better understanding of user emotions and feelings explicitly or implicitly expressed in their utterances. We contributed to this line of research by emphasizing on emotional cause. To capture semantic relationships between emotions and their causes, we began by identifying emotion concepts from the emotion clause in the latest user utterance and the cause concepts from the cause clauses extracted from the conversation context. Armed with these emotion and cause concepts, we employed a multi-hop reasoning strategy to infer paths from cause concepts to emotion concepts using ConceptNet. Our response generation model followed the typical encoder-decoder architecture but incorporated an additional emotional causality graph encoder. Knowledge-Grounded Response Generation We believed that external knowledge, encompassing both emotional and non-emotional knowledge, provide necessary background for understanding human communication intents and generating responses supported by knowledge. Our early work in this respect tried to equip conversation machines with an external knowledge graph. To achieve this, we devised a new encoder-decoder architecture that leveraged contextual attributes and entities to determine when to mention an entity in a response. Subsequently, we advanced our research by organizing conversation utterances and contextual knowledge into a unified context graph. To enhance the understanding of the conversation context, we develop a novel graph-based encoder. Specifically, the encoder fused the information from the entire context graph, providing global context-graph-aware representations of each node in the graph. These representations facilitated knowledge-grounded response generation. For empathetic response generation, we explored potential emotional causes and effects that may be relevant to the dialogue context, even if not explicitly mentioned. Our initial simple solution involved identifying potentially relevant causes and effects using external causal knowledge, such as a cause-effect graph. We then distilled the most pertinent information with an emotion-guided context filter. To incorporate both emotional causality information and the dialogue context into response generation, we employed a multi-source attention scheme and a copy mechanism. However, we identified two limitations in existing approaches, which (1) mainly considered causalities between user emotions and user experiences, overlooking causalities between user’s experiences themselves; and (2) inferred causalities independently, disregarding interdependence among these causalities, resulting in limited accuracy in causality detection. To address these issues, we proposed a solution that reasoned all plausible causalities, i.e., causalities stated explicitly stated in the dialogue history and potentially in future dialogue, interdependently and simultaneously. We formulated this reasoning task as conditional graph generation. In particular, we developed a conditional variational graph auto-encoder framework dedicated to causality reasoning, and implemented a multi-source attention mechanism in the decoder to facilitate the infusion of causality information. Supportive Response Generation and Goal-Oriented Dialogue Planning Previous research on emotional conversion machines primarily focused on understanding the user’s emotion and passively responding with appropriate empathy. We took pioneering steps in this field by exploring how to proactively evoke positive emotions in users. We argued that strategic planning in emotional support conversations extend over a longer planning horizon. To this end, we proposed an A*-like strategy selection algorithm that estimated the extent to much an adopted strategy could contribute to reduction of the user’s emotional distress in the long run. We further introduced innovative techniques to dynamically track the user’s subtle emotion changes, by incorporating external knowledge sourced from the NRC VAD lexicon into the emotion embedding layer of the encoder. We also extensively explored the effective utilization of Large Language Models (LLM) in emotional support conversations. While LLMs demonstrated impressive performance, they often they often lacked a comprehensive understanding of the overall dialogue progression and struggled to strategically accomplish complex dialogue goals, such as emotional support, through multi-turns of interaction. To overcome this challenge, we introduced a dialogue framework that coordinated multiple specialized LLM-based agents, with each agent focusing exclusively on a specific aspect of the dialogue goal. By collectively working together, these agents aimed to achieve the global goal. This divide-and-conquer approach made the complex dialogue goal more manageable, and harnesses greater intelligence compared to a single LLM, thanks to the collaborative efforts of individual agents. Moreover, we allocated additional efforts towards the development of another type of goal-oriented, proactive dialogue system. Specifically, we focused on target-driven dialogue generation in the context of conversational recommendation, with a specific emphasis on addressing dialogue planning. In overall, the objectives of this project were successfully achieved. Some research results have been reported in top conferences and prestige journals in natural language processing and artificial intelligence, with RGC funding acknowledgments.

15204018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204018.value: Emotional and Empathetic Response Generation With a focus on emotion classification, emotion prediction and response generation, we incorporated two significant factors in emotional response generation, which were recognized to influence people’s communication patterns. They are emotion and intention. We developed a hierarchical variational model to predict the emotion and intention to be conveyed in a response and then generated the response based on prediction. The proposed hierarchical prediction and adversarial learning model was published in TKDE’2022. Moving from emotional response generation to empathetic response generation, in addition to identify the emotion expressions in the user utterance, we also extracted the cause expressions from the dialogue context and captured their semantic relationship via multi-hop reasoning over ConceptNet. The research results were published in KBS’2021. Knowledge-Grounded Response Generation We were among the pioneer researchers who worked on knowledge-grounded response generation. We constructed a domain knowledge graph and explored various approaches to leverage the entity knowledge graph. We aimed to enhance the content and coherence of responses at both the utterance-level and dialogue-level. Some of our research findings could be found in AAAI’2019 and SIGIR’2021. Based on causal knowledge, such as a cause-effect graph, we explored potential emotional causes and effects relevant to the dialogue context but not explicitly mentioned. We proposed several graph-based reasoning approaches, making use of causal knowledge to better understand emotional experience of the user and the underlying reasons behind his/her emotion. The details can be found in EMNLP’2022, NeurIPS’2023 and a submission to ACL’2024. Supportive Response Generation and Goal-Oriented Dialogue Planning The objective of supportive response generation is to offer emotional support to users experiencing emotional distress by engaging in actions such as reflective listening or providing suggestions to alleviate negative feelings when they seek assistance for their problems. By transitioning from reactive to proactive goal-oriented dialogue, strategic planning and coordination have been emphasized. Two papers were published on this topic, one in EMNLP’2022 and another in AAAI’2024. Additionally, the issue of user satisfaction was investigated, resulting in a publication in NeurIPS’2023 and a submission to ACL’2024. We also extended our work on dialogue planning to target-driven dialogue generation in context of conversational recommendation, leading to publications in TNNLS’2023, AAAI’2023, ACL’2023 and EMNLP’2023.

15204018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204018.value: Emotion interaction is essential in human social communication. It directly affects the way people interact with each other, and plays an even more important role in the applications like accompanying lonely elderly people, providing consulting services, and appeasing dissatisfied customers or anxious patients. Hence, a good conversation machine must respect emotional aspects of conversation. It should be equipped with the essential emotional intelligence to strengthen the social bond and emotional connection to human for comfortable conversations. With these objectives in our mind, during the period from 2019 to 2021, our primary research endeavors revolved around emotional understanding, emotional reasoning utilizing the external knowledge graph, and emotional (or empathetic) response generation. We soon realized that the scope of emotional intelligence in machines extends beyond entertainment and social conversations. In today’s fast-paced and stressful world, offering timely emotional support becomes vital for individuals to navigate daily distress and replenish their resilience to confront life’s hurdles. Motivated by this, we embarked on further exploration of methods and strategies to develop emotional support conversation machines. Expanding on our efforts, we submitted another GRF proposal in 2022 and successfully obtained funding support from RGC this year.

15204018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204018.value: The advancement of artificial intelligence has led to the development of social conversation machines that can converse naturally with humans. However, while significant progress has been made in generating fluent and relevant responses, the incorporation of emotion in these models has been overlooked, despite its significance in fostering enjoyable experiences. This project aimed to develop emotion-enhanced social conversation models that effectively engage humans in both content and emotion. However, enhancing existing models with emotion was challenging, requiring perception and expression of emotions in words, emotion inference and reasoning, and control of emotional responses. The goal of this project was to move beyond context-oriented response modeling and towards interaction-oriented conversation modeling to foster continuous and harmonious emotional interactions. The research contributed to building emotional conversation machines in a wide range of applications involving emotion care, such as providing companionship to the lonely elderly, offering consulting services, and handling angry customers. It also facilitated the research development of machine emotional intelligence. Our research achievements have been published in a number of top conferences and prestige journals in natural language processing and artificial intelligence.

15204118.label: Realisation of objectives
15204118.value: The project has been completed successfully. All the project objectives have been achieved. For the objective 1, we have studied fundamental mechanisms of the hypersonic boundary layer instabilities with and without ultrasonic porous coating (UAC), especially Mach first and second modes, using linear stability theory (LST) and direct numerical simulation (DNS). The DNS using (1) the acoustic admittance boundary condition and (2) the faithful plate geometry with different pores (or slits) configuration were conducted. For objective 2, the fundamental characteristics of the acoustic fields in the pore (or slit) and near the porous surface were also studied theoretically and validated. A theoretical acoustic model of porous coatings with consideration of interactions of neighboring pores (or slits) and sound waves induced at the pore (or slit) corners was developed, which provide a better porous boundary conditions used in LST and DNS. For objective 3, four kinds of optimal layout of porous coatings were proposed for the engineering applications and validated through the numerical experiments - (1) A UAC design with gradient pore (or slit) depths to stabilize the second mode in a wide frequency range with the first mode little amplified; (2) Absorptive acoustic metasurface; (3) Impedance-near-zero acoustic metasurface; and (4) Reflection-controlled acoustic metasurface. For objective 4, the real gas effects on the performance of porous coatings in hypersonic vibrational and chemical nonequilibrium flows were studied by LST and DNS. The project has successfully developed many theoretical and numerical tools for the study of hypersonic boundary layer instabilities and the outcomes have advanced the understanding of the underlining instability mechanisms, leading to different acoustic meta-surfaces for the delay of hypersonic boundary layer transition.

15204118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204118.value: The outcome of the project includes (1) 11 published journal papers and 1 journal paper under review, (2) One conference paper won the best paper award in an international conference, (3) 3 PhD students were nurtured. The major findings are listed below: 1.The change of fluctuating internal energy is sustained by the advection of perturbed thermal energy in the vicinity of the critical layer and by the dilatation fluctuation near the wall. The energy transport by the wall-normal velocity fluctuation accounts for the growth of second-mode instability, and the growth rate depends on the relative phase of the energy transport by the wall-normal velocity fluctuation to the total time rate of change of fluctuating internal energy in the vicinity of the critical layer. Moreover, this relative phase is associated with the mutual interaction between the critical-layer fluctuation and the near-wall fluctuation. Porous walls recast this mutual interaction by delaying the phase of the wall-normal energy transport near the wall, resulting in the stabilization of the second mode. 2. An improved theoretical acoustic model describing how a porous coating affects the control of the hypersonic boundary-layer transition is proposed, taking into account the higher-order diffraction waves generated at the porous surface. 3. Whether Mack modes are stabilized or destabilized closely depends on the UAC admittance phase θ and the corresponding stabilization or destabilization effect is intensified by the increase of the admittance magnitude. The first mode will be marginally stabilized if phase angle θ approaches 0.5π, and greatly destabilized in the vicinity of θ=π. On the contrary, the second mode is restrained when θ ≥ 0.75π and amplified as θ approaches 0.5π. Based on the current analyses, a reverse design strategy is proposed, and a UAC composed of constant spacing slits with increased width and depth is proposed. It is found that the designed UAC can substantially stabilize the second mode across a wide frequency band without amplifying the first mode distinctly. 4. The direct numerical simulation of the spatial evolution of disturbances that interact with the coating microstructure is conducted, and it emphasizes the coating effect on the outflow fields, accuracy of the theoretical model, and the effect of coating locations. Flow quantities fluctuate in the coating region because of alternating expansion and compression at the cavity corners. The effect of the porous coating on the mean flowfield is small enough to satisfy the “aerodynamically smooth” hypothesis. The impedance boundary method can accurately model the porous coating stabilization effect, by providing an average treatment of the acoustic characteristics of microcavities when comparing fluctuating pressure in the coating region. The Mack second mode is destabilized or stabilized when a porous coating is located upstream or downstream of the synchronization point, and this trend is slightly overpredicted by the theoretical mode. 5. Three other meta surfaces were proposed for the engineering applications and validated through the numerical experiments - (1) Absorptive acoustic metasurface; (2) Impedance-near-zero acoustic metasurface; and (3) Reflection-controlled acoustic metasurface. Their effectiveness on delaying the hypersonic boundary layer transition are demonstrated.

15204118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204118.value: In the future study, more meta surface designs will be proposed in order to stabilize the second mode in a wide frequency range and without amplifying the first mode much. Experimental validations in the PolyU's hypersonic Ludwieg tube will be conducted. We have just recently upgrade our Ludwieg tube from Mach 4 to Mach 6. Also, in the real hypersonic flight scenarios, many other instabilities may occur, such as Gotler mode, crossflow mode, oblique first mode, ...etc. The mechanisms of these modes will be studies using LST and DNS. More control designs to delay the hypersonic boundary layer transition will be proposed for the real flight conditions. Passive flow control using the metasurfaces and active flow control using the blow/suction pores (slits) may be integrated to tackle different instability modes at the same time.

15204118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204118.value: Hypersonic boundary layer (HBL) transition generates a significant increase in viscous drag and heat flux, which leads to severe restrictions on the performance and thermal protection systems of hypersonic vehicles. Among various passive/active transition control strategies, acoustic metasurfaces demonstrate minimal effects on the mean flow but significantly suppress the Mack second mode. Therefore, it can be considered one of the most promising transition control technologies. Acoustic metasurfaces are planar metamaterial structures that comprise monolayer or multilayer stacks of subwavelength microstructures, which affect unstable modes via acoustic wave manipulations. In this project, acoustic characteristics of acoustic metasurfaces and their corresponding stabilization effects on the first and second modes are revealed and discussed. Improvements in the mathematical modeling of acoustic metasurfaces have been made. The theoretical linear stability theory (LST) and direct numerical simulation (DNS) investigations are then provided. Four different metasurfaces are proposed for delaying the HBL transition. Finally, the suppression of the instability of HBL transition under thermochemical nonequilibrium (TCNE) using a porous coating configuration is examined through LST and DNS. The TCNE effect exerts little impact on the acoustic attenuation of the instability inside the cavity.
