15204918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204918.value: A fire whirl (FW) can be generated during a room fire under certain appropriate ventilation conditions. A hot smoke layer is observed to form above the cool air layer. Heat and mass transfer to the upper smoke layer through the FW is faster than with a normal fire plume, giving a more hazardous environment. An FW remains fixed above the fire source if there is only one burning object, but the FW can move around the room if there are several combustible objects located next to the burning object. Ignition of the adjacent objects with a moving FW will give a very hazardous environment. In this proposed project, the above two key scientific hazardous phenomena associated with FW in a room fire will be studied. Firstly, the higher air entrainment rate due to the FW and hence the faster development of the smoke layer; and secondly, the FW movement over different combustibles in a room will be focused upon. A typical room of size 4 m by 3 m and height 2.8 m is selected for this study. Experiments with a smaller physical model of size 0.4 m by 0.3 m and height 0.28 m will be carried out first to study FW generation and its characteristics. Different sizes of ceiling vents and sidewall ventilation provisions will be adopted. Liquid pool propanol fires of three different diameters will be placed inside the small room model. Air flow along the FW swirling flame surface will be studied experimentally in the small model together with analytical studies on heat transfer, swirling fluid flow, combustion and fire-induced aerodynamics. Computational Fluid Dynamics, integrating air flow simulation and appropriate combustion models for liquid pool fires will also be applied, together with physical modelling results to study FW air entrainment in a room fire. Results on FW swirling air entrainment will be used to develop a two-layer zone fire model using symbolic mathematics. The movement of FWs over an array of combustible items will also be studied. Full-scale burning tests on the room will be carried out to validate the scale model observations and mathematical modelling results. Scaling laws on key parameters including room dimensions and opening sizes will be explored by applying dimensional analysis to the experimental results. These two key FW characteristics will be included to increase our fire hazard assessment capabilities in relation to fires in small rooms. 在適當的通風條件下，在室內發生火災期間可能產生火旋風（FW）。能夠觀察到熱煙層在冷空氣層上方形成。 通過火旋風傳遞到上部煙霧層的熱量和質量比使用正常的火焰羽流更快，從而造成相對更危險的環境。 如果室內只有一個燃燒物體，則火旋風會保持固定在火源上方，但如果燃燒物體旁邊有多個可燃物體，則火旋風可以在房間內移動。移動的火旋風點燃相鄰物體將產生非常危險的環境。 上述兩個關鍵的火旋風科學危險現象將會在這個擬議的項目中研究。首先，由於火旋風導致更高的空氣吸入率，因此煙層下降得更快; 其次，將再研究火旋風在房間內不同可燃物之間的移動。 這項研究選擇了一個典型的房間。先進行較小尺度物理模型的實驗，以研究火旋風的產生及其特性。將採用不同尺碼的天花板通風口和側壁通風設施。 不同直徑的液體池丙醇火將放置在小房間模型內。沿著火旋風旋轉火焰表面的氣流將在小模型中進行實驗研究，同時對傳熱，旋流流動，燃燒和火災引起的空氣動力學進行分析研究。 計算流體動力學，集合氣流模擬和液池火災的適當燃燒模型，以及物理模擬結果，以研究室內火災中的火旋風空氣含量。火旋風的旋轉空氣含量的結果將用於開發一個使用符號數學的雙層區域火災模型。還將研究火旋風在一組可燃物品上的移動。將對房間進行全尺寸燃燒測試，以驗證比例模型的觀測和數學模型結果。通過對實驗結果應用尺寸分析，將探索關鍵參數（包括房間尺寸和開口尺寸）的尺度定律。包括在內的這兩個關鍵的火旋風特性將會提高我們在相關的小房間火災中的火災危險評估能力。

15204918.label: Realisation of objectives
15204918.value: Three objectives were achieved as following: 1. To study the generation mechanism and the characteristics of fire whirls in a room. Fire whirls (FW) generated by a gasoline pool fire in a vertical shaft were studied experimentally. Vortex motions of swirling flame induced by buoyancy above the pool fires were observed. Buoyancy-induced upward flame motions were described mathematically by solving the vorticity transport equation. Swirling attenuation along the vertical direction was determined. Heat release rates and fire whirl diameters at different heights were measured to obtain the vertical variation of circular speeds of the FW. Velocity distribution and motion of a whirling flame in a room fire with vent were then studied analytically. Whirling flame models with and without decay of the rotation velocity were established by using Rankine vortex model. The whirling flame model and the cross-wind velocity boundary conditions were used to study the velocity distribution of the rotating flame under the action of side wind. In the rotation velocity attenuation model, the axis of the whirling flame deviates from a straight line. The change of the shape of the whirling flame is related to the flame height, the rotational angular velocity, and the maximum wind velocity. Uniform lateral wind and lateral wind with linear velocity gradient can only affect the position and shape of the whirling flame axis but not change the rotational angular velocity. The above results were applied to study the possibility of FW in two examples: short vehicular tunnel (SVT) and refuge floor (RF). A new SVT opened recently in the eastern part of downtown Hong Kong was taken as an example. Fire can also spread easier between vehicles when an SVT has heavy traffic congestion through a FW. RF is a fire safety requirement for tall buildings in many Asia-Oceania areas including Hong Kong. Example buildings with RF were reviewed. RFs for buildings are allowed to be opened and drencher systems are waived for residential buildings. Fire safety issues in relation to natural ventilation across RFs in tall buildings related to FW were explored. 2. To develop a two-layer zone model for a room fire with higher amounts of air entrainment due to the presence of fire whirl. The two parts of this objective in developing a two-layer fire model with symbolic mathematics were met. The first was to review the key equations for a two-layer zone model and their simplification to a simpler model. The ordinary differential equations of the simplified model were then solved by symbolic mathematics. Programming with symbolic mathematics enables flexible changing of the equations and parameters concerned describing the physics behind. Results on FW characteristics were put in a two-layer zone model with appropriate mathematical formulation. The differential equations based on a two-layer zone model have no analytical solutions and numerical methods are required. Stiffness in using numerical methods to solve these differential equations was investigated. Analytical solution for the clear height in the zone model was studied in the past. Predicted values of smoke layer height in the present approach are shown to be in good agreement with experimental results reported in the literature. The present work would provide insight in modeling FW in a compartment fire. The action of driving air to generate FW in a room fire was studied by physical scale modelling tests. A 1:7 room scale model of a typical room was constructed to study the fire environment resulting from different ventilation arrangements. 3. To study the movements of fire whirls around a room when there are several combustible objects. The spinning motion of the FW that ignites adjacent combustibles was studied in this project along an array of combustible fuel sources. Nine propanol pools (without ignition) were placed as an array on the floor in the small room model. The behavior of FW above a pool fire under cross-wind was studied using a small wind tunnel. The effect of different wind speeds on the FW with different heat release rates was studied. Lateral images of the whirling flame collected were analyzed. Results show that under cross flow, the FW was deflected along the direction of incoming flow. With the increase in wind speed, the deflection angle increased gradually. The angle also increased with the increase in pool diameter. When the cross flow increased to a certain value, the flame stopped swirling, and changed to an irregular shape. Cross wind with lower speed would raise the temperature of the FW. Results of wind effects on FW would provide some information on the possible hazards and fire environment in several case studies of industrial building fires. With many industrial areas developing rapidly in Southern China, more industrial fires occurred and are expected to occur with FW generated. Industrial fires in Hong Kong up to 1980s were reviewed as the background, because many factories at there were moved from Hong Kong and invested by local citizens. Further, there are many big construction projects with new green architectural designs and green style of living for achieving sustainability. Fire safety challenges to green constructions including FW in shafts for ventilation, access and even other special purposes, are of concern. Results on FW in this project were applied to study possible fire hazards in big cities with manufacturing areas including the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GHMGBA). Wind action on supertall building fires might lead to mass fires due to entrainment resulting from complicated urban geometry. Wind-fire interaction will be introduced as FW might be generated. Six tasks were carried out to achieve the three objectives with a summary as follows: Task 1: Scale model experiments were carried out in the PolyU-BSE Fire Engineering Laboratory. Task 2: Full-scale burning tests including scale models with a wind tunnel were carried out at Lanxi, Harbin, Heilongjiang, China. The behavior of whirling flame under lateral wind is of great significance in fire hazard assessment in a combustion wind tunnel with one of size 6 m x 1.55 m x 1.55 m. Task 3: Swirling flame inside the room model was studied numerically by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) in room fire for generating FW. Task 4: Air entrainment to the FW was explored based on the physical experimental observations and results, and predictions from mathematical CFD modelling. Task 5: The two-layer zone model was reviewed and simplified to a simpler model. An equation for flow through vertical openings at height was applied together with the FW entrainment equation. The ordinary differential equations of the simplified model were solved by symbolic mathematics. Task 6: Movement of FW over the combustibles along an array of combustible fuel sources. As a summary, scientific research carried out for better understanding the potential fire hazards of fire whirl in this project can be transferred to practical design guides and fire regulations for green buildings with vertical shafts, supertall buildings with refuge floors and short vehicular tunnels integrated with other green designs such as green roof. The results and conclusions in this project would definitely provide a solid foundation for the government in the evaluation and approval process of projects involving buildings and designs mentioned above with respect to fire safety.

15204918.value: This project was worked out after completing two FW projects funded by RGC-GRF on “Onsetting of internal fire whirls in buildings and associated safety provisions” (2007-2010); and “A study of internal fire whirl in vertical shafts with open roofs” (2013-2014). Although the original Principal Investigator (PI), Professor W.K. Chow was retired in November, 2019, he continued working closely with the new PI, Dr Joseph Lai, who agreed to take up the responsibility. Experiments on a small physical model on air exchange flows through the sidewall openings and horizontal ceiling vent in a room model with small propanol pool fires were carried out. The core structure of an internal fire whirl was studied to investigate whether vortex breakdown occurs in the fire whirl. The maximum swirling velocity and its location were determined. Asymmetries in the core flow were investigated based on the observed flame motions. A total of 5 journal papers were published in this project. One journal paper is under review and another one is under preparation but submission is delayed slightly because of the incident of occupying PolyU campus and closure of campus for coronavirus COVID-19 control. Further, 5 conference presentations were made. New challenges on fire safety of existing buildings were outlined with examples of FW reported in some talks at local professional institutions. All key findings above were communicated to the Hong Kong Government Fire Services Department as part of our mentorship programme. Under the scheme, a fire officer carried out a research project as part-time PhD student on supertall buildings with refuge floor fires. Research results will be made use of by the new set of fire codes on room fires for better fire safety provisions. For example, the derived correlation expression relating heat release rate of the pool fire to the flame height of the FW is useful for hazard assessment when determining fire safety provisions in a room fire. The codes will be drafted under the leadership of the original PI, Professor Chow, with reference to existing local codes, updated overseas codes and associated fire research literature. Two part-time PhD students working parts of the tasks in this project were graduated. One is a fire officer just promoted recently to divisional officer working on supertall building fires, assessing fire hazards of swirling flame at refuge floor. The other is a building services consultant engineer, with the PhD thesis on fire whirl generation mechanism.

15204918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204918.value: The impact of fire whirl (FW) on fire hazard assessment following a scientific understanding of vertical shafts, green buildings, supertall buildings and short vehicular tunnels were illustrated. Research on exploring the effects of FW to new projects proposed on these buildings and short vehicular tunnels should be further developed. More full-scale burning tests with FW in vertical shafts and room models should be carried out to validate the scale model observations and mathematical modelling results. Results and recommendations from this project can be further integrated with the associated literature and existing overseas fire codes in order to then draft new codes with the Hong Kong Fire Services Department and Buildings Department. Government fire officers who are updating the local codes for new challenges encountered in buildings can learn to work on a special section on FW phenomenon that will be drafted under the leadership of the retired PI, who is still active in fire and explosion research, and leading international activities. Another important part recommended to further study thoroughly is to work out appropriate firefighting scheme to control fire with whirling flame. More efficient firefighting operational schemes should be worked out to better protect firemen when fighting big building fires.

15204918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204918.value: A fire whirl (FW) can be generated during a room fire under appropriate ventilation conditions. Hazardous consequences such as faster heat and mass transfer to the upper smoke layer through the FW will be resulted. Further, the generated FW can move around the room if there are several combustible objects. Two key hazardous phenomena associated with FW in a room fire on the faster development of the smoke layer due to higher air entrainment rate and movement over different combustibles were studied scientifically with scaled model, Computational Fluid Dynamics, and full-scale burning tests in this project. A total of 5 journal papers were published. Two part-time PhD students working on parts of the tasks in this project were graduated. One is a fire officer assessing the hazard of FW in supertall buildings. The other is a building services engineer working on flame swirling generation mechanism. The long-term benefits achieved from this research are that the results will be applicable and available to the urban public in general, and in particular to the government and regulatory bodies responsible for building fire safety. Fire officers can be trained better on working out firefighting schemes against FW.

15205318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205318.value: 基於Si CMOS技術和Von Neumann結構的傳統計算機系統正在接近於其物理極限，處理器和存儲器單元在物理上分離，它們之間的數據傳輸極大地限制了計算速度並增加了功耗，而物聯網的發展需要用於邊緣計算系統的超低功率電子設備。人腦是一種信息處理系統，具有高度並行計算、事件驅動和低功耗的特點。我們的大腦由1000億個神經元組成，每個神經元通過突觸與其他神經元形成數千個連接，我們將采用具有多個輸入和輸出端的電子器件來模擬單個神經元的生物突觸的基本特征，這是一個基本的科學問題。 二維層狀半導體表面沒有懸掛鍵，有助於減少表面態和陷阱態，二維半導體的超薄厚度還能夠有效地實現靜電柵極控制和亞閾值擺幅。二維材料半導體溝道的使用有望實現低功率場效應晶體管，這對於實現類腦計算非常重要。此外，一些二維材料具有很高的各向異性電學特性，在相同的突觸尖峰刺激下，各向異性二維材料可以沿不同方向表現出不同水平的興奮性突觸後電流或抑制性突觸後電流。通常，每個神經元只有一個軸突，但軸突是高度分支的，並連接了數千個目標神經元。各向異性的二維材料提供了一個模擬具有多輸出功能的神經元的平臺。 在這個項目中，我們將展示基於高度各向異性的二 維材料的高性能和高穩定二維材料電子器件，並模擬具有多個輸入和輸出端的單個神經元的生物學行為。首先，我們將使用氣相法或液相法生長高度各向異性的二維材料，並使用這些二維材料制造高性能和低功率場效應晶體管。其次，我們將研究具有多個輸入端的神經晶體管的基本特性，例如，EPSC，IPSC，成對脈沖促進和取向選擇性。最後，我們將研究二維材料的各向異性電學特性，以模擬具有多個輸出端的單個神經元。

15205318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205318.value: We adopted van der Waals trigonal-selenium (vdW t-Se) with two-dimensional (2D) form as a channel material of electrolyte-gated transistors (EGT) devices, which present low energy consumption of 0.1 pJ. The transition from short-term plasticity (STP) to long-term plasticity (LTP) can also be selectively realized by tuning the amplitude of gate voltage. More importantly, a large anisotropic factor of electrical resistance (~8.6) in t-Se was demonstrated, which is among the highest in other reported 2D anisotropic materials. Due to the intrinsic anisotropy in electronic properties, we demonstrated the dissimilar synaptic response of multi-terminal EGT devices, exhibiting its great potential for developing artificial systems to mimic the behaviors of the human brain. We can observe a clear transition from STP to LTP by employing a voltage pulse with large amplitude or width, which can be well explained by the Li+ ion intercalations into a t-Se lattice. The energy consumption of neuromorphic networks is mainly determined by the “read” process due to the relatively small leakage current and large width of the voltage stimulation. The smallest energy consumption was calculated to be only 0.1 pJ for a single pulse (2.0 V) event. This value is among the lowest of reported synaptic EGT devices with similar device configurations. Due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of electrical conductance, the EGT device based on a t-Se nanosheet exhibits a high anisotropy in the modulation of synaptic weight as well as temporal filtering ability. The function of the biological axon−multisynapse network was also successfully emulated. This finding provides an attractive approach to realize the complex artificial neural system for mimicking the behaviors of the human brain. We have published these research results in ACS Nano, Science Advances, etc. We also trained a PhD student.

15205318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205318.value: To further develop the research in this specific direction, we can use this materials system and device structure to demonstrate multimodal in-sensor computing. The multiple terminals of the device can respond to different stimuli, including light, electronic, electrochemical, etc. Highly anisotropic 2D materials not only provide a channel material with excellent electrostatic control to minimize power consumption but also enables to mimic biological behaviors of a single neuron with multiple input and output terminals.

15205318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205318.value: Conventional computer systems based on Si CMOS technology and Von Neumann architecture are running into their physical limits. The data transfer between the physically separated processor and memory units greatly limits the computation speed and energy efficiency. The development of the Internet of Things (IoT) requires ultralow power electron devices for edge computing systems. Human brains are an information processing system with the characteristics of highly parallel computation, energy efficient, and event-driven. Our brain consists of 100 billion neurons, and each individual neuron can form thousands of links with other neurons through synapses. It is a fundamental research interest to adopt the electron device with multiple input and output terminals to mimic the basic characteristics of biological synapses at the single neuron level. We demonstrate high-performance and air-stable 2D devices based on highly anisotropic 2D materials, and mimic the biological behavior of a single neuron with multiple input and output terminals.

15206318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206318.value: Light sources used for general illumination produce “white” light ranging from yellowish white to bluish white. Standards typically restrict their colour coordinates (i.e., chromaticities) within a defined region (i.e., on or near the Planckian locus) in colour spaces, so that their colour appearance matches incandescent lamps or daylight. These specifications are made on the assumption that only daylight and incandescent lamps appear white, but without an explicit rationale. Such a tradition was simply followed in LED industry; most commercially-available LEDs have their chromaticities on or near the Planckian locus. As the adjustment of chromaticities is becoming easier for LED sources—especially to colour tuneable LEDs—manufacturers, specifiers, and designers are looking for opportunities to exploit this potential to enhance lighting quality and standardization bodies are making efforts to revise relevant standards. In May 2017, American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and National Electric Manufacturers Association (NEMA) revised the specifications for LED product chromaticities in ANSI/NEMA C78.377-2017 and expect further review and revision as LED technologies and research advance. Recent studies found that light sources with chromaticities located off the Planckian locus (known as “off-Planckian sources”) can produce an un-tinted white perception and preferred illumination, which has led to the popularity and the development of off-Planckian LED sources. The applicants’ early works, however, revealed weaknesses in these studies (e.g., the unrealistic presentation of lighting in a viewing booth, the failure to isolate chromaticity, and the assumption of complete chromatic adaptation under off-Planckian sources). This project aims to comprehensively investigate human perception under off-Planckian illumination, focusing on perception of white, chromatic adaptation, and preference, in a full-size space. It will fully immerse observers in a space and create more realistic lighting conditions, in comparison to the viewing booths employed in past studies. In addition, an 11-channel spectrally-tuneable LED lighting system will be developed to realize a wider range of light stimuli and to explicitly isolate chromaticity from other variables. This project is timely and is of interest to lighting community. It makes important scientific contributions by furthering understanding about human perception to light stimuli. It will also have a great impact on LED industry, especially to that in the Pearl River Delta Area, which is adjacent to Hong Kong and has the largest LED industry in China, by guiding manufacturers to develop high-quality white LEDs, standardization bodies to update LED specifications, and designers/users to make better use of colour tuneable LEDs and enhance lighting environment. f虽然用于通用照明的光源可以产生从偏黄到偏蓝的各种白光，但这些光源的色坐标在各种标准中都被限制在黑体辐射线上来产生与白炽灯和日光相近的白光。尽管这样的限制都是基于未经严格论证的假设——仅有白炽灯和日光可以产生白光，但这样的限制目前仍然在LED行业被广泛应用。随着LED的色坐标调节以及光谱调节变得越来越容易，LED制造商和照明设计师开始探究这一假设的科学性，并且希望可以通过改变LED色坐标来进一步提高照明品质。另一方面，LED行业也开始修改标准中对LED光源色坐标的限制。2017年5月，美国国家标准技术局ANSI和美国国家电器协会NEMA修改了LED色坐标限制的标准ANSI/NEMA C78.377-2017，并且表示会在将来随着LED技术的发展和新的研究进一步修改该标准。若干最新的研究表明将光源的色坐标远离黑体辐射线可以产生纯白光以及提升光品质，这一结果引起了整个LED行业的关注。但是，项目申请人的前期研究表明这些研究都存在缺陷，例如使用不真实的实验场景以及未能区分色坐标与光源显色性的影响。本项目将研究在色坐标远离黑体辐射线光源下的颜色视觉，并将重点研究白色视觉、色适应以及颜色偏好。通过搭建全光谱可调空间来实现各种光源，并在研究中完全独立色坐标的影响。本项目对于照明行业具有重要的意义，尤其是珠江三角洲地区的LED产业以及建筑行业。本项目也具有重要的科学意义，将帮助我们进一步了解人类视觉系统对光刺激的反应。

15206318.label: Realisation of objectives
15206318.value: The project aims to better understand how chromaticities of the stimuli affect the color perception of the human beings, which can be used to guide the development of lighting products. Overall, all the objectives have been achieved. A large-size experiment area has been built, which allows the accurate achievement of lighting conditions at a wide range of chromaticities and spectral compositions. In the experiment area, several experiments were carefully designed and conducted to understand how the chromaticities of the stimuli affect the perception of the colors of human beings. In particular, we investigated the range of the chromaticities to produce a white appearance, and also how the degree of chromatic adaptation was affected by the chromaticities of the adapting conditions.

15206318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206318.value: Chromaticity ranges to produce a white appearance of stimulus were identified under various lighting conditions, which can be used to define the chromaticities of white light sources. In addition, the importance of the spectral compositions of the stimuli in producing a matched white appearance was clearly found. Based on the perception of white, the effect of the chromaticities on the degree of chromatic adaptation was clearly found, which was the most significant finding of this project. An interaction between the adapting chromaticities of white illumination and the adapting luminance was found. In particular, an incomplete chromatic adaptation was found under the lighting conditions having a lower CCT level (e.g., 2700K) regardless of the adapting luminance, which was never found in the past.

15206318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206318.value: The findings of this research have led to the further investigations of color appearance of highlights under different adapting conditions, which can further help us to understand the role of the illumination chromaticities. In addition, the importance of the spectral compositions revealed in this research has suggested the necessity to investigate the underlying mechanism of color matching functions, which is the fundamental of color science and color perception.

15206318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206318.value: The color of illumination is commonly specified using a set of coordinates in a color space. For general illumination, the light source has been always designed to have coordinates along a curve, so that the color tone of the light source appears similar to daylight, from warm to cool. The development of the LED technology has allowed the shift of the coordinates. In this project, we investigated the range of the coordinates for producing a white illumination. In addition, it was found that when the white illumination has a warm tone, the color appearance of the objects under the illumination always has a large shift, especially when the light level is low. The findings of this project provide a much better understanding about how the color of the illumination affects the perception of color, and also how the spectral compositions of the illumination need to be adjusted to compensate the changes of the object color appearance under certain lighting conditions.

15206418.label: Realisation of objectives
15206418.value: Project Title: New perovskite anodes for solid oxide fuel cells running on hydrogen/carbon monoxide mixture Objectives: • To develop novel perovskite BFO-based materials as SOFC anodes for syngas (H2/CO mixture) oxidation. • To understand the bulk and surface properties of the newly developed BFO-based materials at atomic level by first-principle calculation. • To develop high performance SOFCs with newly developed anode materials using syngas (H2/CO mixture) as fuel. Activities conducted: We have developed novel perovskite BFO-based materials for SOFCs (Objective 1 and 3). We developed B-site doped BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ), which was characterized systematically using XRD, SEM TEM etc. The BFZ at 800°C exhibits a cubic perovskite structure (space group P m 3 m) with a unit cell parameter of a = 4.09 Å. The converged reliability factors are Rp = 11.4%, Rwp = 15%, χ2 = 2.60. After annealing in humidified H2 atmosphere at 800°C for 10 h, no additional phase is found and the cubic perovskite structure is retained even at room temperature, implying sufficient chemical structural stability. The electrical conductivities of BFZ in air and humidified H2 atmosphere are studied. The oxide demonstrates lower values in reducing atmosphere, which may be attributed to the electronic holes loss in reducing condition. We studied the area specific resistances (ASRs) of BFZ at various temperatures in air and humidified H2. The sample delivers excellent electrocatalytic activity in oxidizing atmosphere, and as low as 0.005, 0.02 and 0.14 Ω cm2 ASRs are obtained at 800, 700 and 600°C respectively. The results are better than many existing perovskite materials. We also evaluated the performance of solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) using the newly developed perovskite oxide as both the anode and cathode. Good performance was obtained. We measured the current density-voltage curves and the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) (Objective 1 and 3) Peak power densities of 1097, 886, 636 and 398 mW cm-2 are obtained at 800, 750, 700, 650°C, respectively. In addition, we also tested the long-term stability of the material for 100 hours. The cell was stable for 100 hours. After a few thermal cycling, the cell is still stable. We also developed other BFO-based perovskite, such as Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ (BSFG) and we achieved very low area-specific resistance of 0.074Ωcm2 and a high power density of 1.145W/cm2 at 600oC (objective 1 and 3). To gain insights into the material properties of BSFG, we conducted first principle calculations (objective 2). To achieve good phase stability, we partly replaced Ba with Bi and Pr, and developed Bi0.7Pr0.1Ba0.2FeO3-δ (BPBF). The BPBF showed good oxygen transport properties and electrocatalytic activity, which delivered a polarization resistance of 0.056Ωcm2 at 700oC and a good stability in CO2 containing environment (objective 1). We replaced Ba with La and developed La0.3Sr0.7Fe0.1Ti0.9O3-δ (LSFT) anode for oxidation of H2 and CO. Electrolyte-supported SOFC with LSFT anode and CO fuel achieved a power density of 0.292W/cm2 at 850oC (objective 1 and 3). The low power density is caused by high ohmic loss of the thick electrolyte. Further, we developed A-site deficient and Ni-doped La0.7Sr0.3Cr0.5Mn0.5Ni0.1O3-δ (N-LSCM) for CO oxidation in SOFC and achieved a polarization resistance of 0.54Ωcm2 and power density of 0.153W/cm2 at 850oC (Objective 1 and 3). By replacing Ba by La (for the sake of phase stability), we developed LaFeO3-δ and further composite it with CeO2 to evaluate the electrocatalytic activity (Objective 1). We reported La diffusion from LaFeO3-δ to CeO2. The redistribution of cations triggered the change of chemical environment of interface elements, which increased oxygen vacancies and high valent Fe species, leading to increased electrocatalytic activity. We also developed atomic models based on density functional theory (DFT) for studying the electrocataytic performance of different materials (Objective 2). We studied the O2 adsorption pathways on various oxide materials and the PDOS of the adsorbate O* atoms on the catalyst surface. In summary, we developed BFO-based materials for use as anode. We also tested the new materials for use as cathode. In general, we found that the performance of the anode for CO oxidation can be improved by various doping strategies at the A-site or B-site of BFO-based perovskite. However, the polarization for CO oxidation is still high and needs to be further improved. For comparison, when the BFO-based perovskite oxides are used as SOFC cathode, they show very good performance for oxygen reduction reaction. We employed the DFT computations to understand the material properties and to explain the experimental results. We completed the project, and the 3 objectives are well achieved (100%).

15206418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206418.value: We developed a series of BFO-based materials, such as BaFe0.9Zr0.1O3-δ (BFZ), Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ (BSFG), and Bi0.7Pr0.1Ba0.2FeO3-δ (BPBF). We also substituted Ba with La and developed La0.3Sr0.7Fe0.1Ti0.9O3-δ (LSFT) and LaFeO3-δ. These materials are characterized and tested to evaluate their bulk transport properties and surface electrocatalytic activity. We also employed DFT calculations to understand the material properties. Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) were fabricated using the newly developed electrode materials. It was found that the BFO-based perovskite oxides in general showed good oxygen transport properties and surface electrocatalytic activities. In an oxidizing environment, we achieved a low area-specific resistance (ASR) of 0.14 Ω cm2 at 600°C (BFZ). The SOFC delivered a peak power density of 1097 mW cm-2 at 800°C (BFZ). Ba0.75Sr0.25Fe0.875Ga0.125O3-δ (BSFG) also showed very good electrocatalytic activity without Co. Based on first principle DFT computations, we found that the local structural units in the Ba-Fe-O materials play a critical role in the redox process and participation of oxygen in them. There are 3 types of structural unit around oxygen (O1-type, O2-type, and O3-type), see Journal of Energy Chemistry 62(2021)653-659. A larger integral size near Fermi level of BSFG over oxygen-stoichiometric BSFG was observed, showing excellent electrocatalytic activity. In addition, the O p-band center is a good descriptor for predicting experimental values of surface exchange coefficient of perovskite oxides. The calculated O p-band center for BSFG (δ in the range of [0.13, 0.17]) lies in the range of -1.48 to -1.59 eV, which exceeds that of LSCF and is comparable to that of BSCF, both are popular SOFC cathode materials. The DFT calculations showed insights into the materials properties. When La0.3Sr0.7Fe0.1Ti0.9O3-δ (LSFT) A-site deficient and Ni-doped La0.7Sr0.3Cr0.5Mn0.5Ni0.1O3-δ (N-LSCM) are used as SOFC anode for CO oxidation, good electrochemical performance was achieved, with good stability as well, indicating their good anti-coking properties. Due to thick electrolyte used, the SOFC delivered a power density of 0.292W/cm2 at 850oC for LSFT and 0.153W/cm2 at 850oC for N-LSCM. From this project, we can see that the BFO-based perovskite oxides showed good oxygen transport properties and very good electrocatalytic activities for oxygen reduction and CO oxidation reactions. However, the performance for CO oxidation should be further improved. Future research can be conducted to develop nanostructured electrodes by in-situ exsolution techniques or infiltration techniques to improve the surface activity of the electrode materials. The project has been successfully completed and more than 10 journal papers have been generated.

15206418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206418.value: This project has been successfully completed. A series of BFO-based perovskite oxides were developed, which showed very good performance for oxygen reaction reaction and reasonably good performance for CO oxidation. Therefore, continued efforts should be made to further reduce the polarization loss of the anode for CO oxidation. Apart from doping strategies to improve the bulk transport properties, more strategies to improve the surface electrocatalytic activities are needed. For example, in-situ exsolution of nanoparticles from the perovskite bulk can be employed to enhance the surface electrocatalytic activity of the anode. Or nanostructured anode can be fabricated by infiltration technique. With the surface modification by nanoparticles, we believe the performance of anode can be greatly improved. Our group will conduct the above mentioned research to further improve the electrocatalytic activity of the SOFC electrode material.

15206418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206418.value: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising clean power sources with high efficiency, low emission, and quiet operation. One distinct feature of SOFC is fuel flexibility, as not only hydrogen but also hydrocarbon fuels can be used as fuels for power generation. When hydrocarbon fuels are used, CO oxidation in SOFC plays a critical role. Therefore, to develop high performance and durable electrode materials for CO oxidation is essential for the success of SOFC. In this project, we developed a series of BaFeO3-based perovskite oxides for use as SOFC anode and cathode. Through systematical characterizations and electrochemical testing, we evaluated the electrocatalytic activity of the newly developed materials. We also employed first principle computations to understand the material properties and to explain experimental results. SOFCs with the newly developed anode delivered good power density and demonstrated the effectiveness of the BaFeO3-based perovskite oxides for use as SOFC anode. Future works can be conducted to develop nanostructured electrodes by in-situ exsolution of nanoparticles or infiltration to further improve the electrochemical performance of SOFC. This project has been successfully completed. All the 3 objective have been achieved. More than 10 papers have been published in excellent academic journals.

15206818.label: Realisation of objectives
15206818.value: Objective 1: Tin-based perovskites with excellent optoelectronic properties and suitable band gaps are promising candidates for the preparation of efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, it is challenging to prepare highly stable and efficient tin-based PSCs because Sn2+ in perovskites can be easily oxidized to Sn4+ upon air exposure. We enabled the fabrication of air-stable FASnI3 solar cells by introducing hydroxybenzene sulfonic acid or its salt as an antioxidant additive into the perovskite precursor solution along with excess SnCl2. The interaction between the sulfonate group and the Sn2+ ion enables the in situ encapsulation of the perovskite grains with a SnCl2–additive complex layer, which results in greatly enhanced oxidation stability of the perovskite film. The corresponding PSCs are able to maintain 80%of the efficiency over 500 h upon air exposure without encapsulation, which is over ten times longer than the best result reported previously. Our results suggest a possible strategy for the future design of efficient and stable tin-based PSCs. Objective 2: Adding extra SnX2 (X = F, Cl, or Br) in the precursor solution to inhibit Sn2+ oxidation is an essential strategy to improve device efficiency and stability. However, SnX2 on the surface of perovskite grains tends to prohibit charge transfer across perovskite films. Hence, we developed a coadditive engineering approach by introducing antioxidant gallic acid (GA) together with SnCl2 to improve the performance of tin-based PSCs. The SnCl2−GA complex can not only protect the perovskite grains but also more effectively conduct electrons across it, leading to highly stable and efficient PSCs. The unencapsulated devices can maintain ∼80% of their initial efficiency after 1000h of storage in ambient air with a relative humidity of 20%, which is the best air stability achieved in tin-based PSCs to date. It is challenging to obtain high-quality Sn-based perovskite films by solution process. We find that liquid-exfoliated 2D transition-metal dichalcogenides (i.e., MoS2, WS2, and WSe2) with smooth and defect-free surfaces can be applied as growth templates for spin-coated FASnI3 perovskite films, leading to van der Waals epitaxial growth of perovskite grains with a growth orientation along (100). We also find that WSe2 has better energy alignment with FASnI3 than MoS2 and WS2 and results in a cascade band structure in resultant perovskite solar cells (PSCs), which can facilitate hole extraction and suppress interfacial charge recombination in the devices. The WSe2-modified PSCs show a power conversion efficiency up to 10.47%, which is among the highest efficiency of FASnI3-based PSCs. The appealing solution phase epitaxial growth of FASnI3 perovskite on 2D WSe2 flakes is expected to find broad applications in optoelectronic devices. Objective 3: 2D–3D mixed tin halide perovskites are outstanding candidate materials for lead-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs) due to their improved stability and decreased trap density in comparison with their pure 3D counterparts. However, the mixture of multiple phases may lead to poor charge transfer across the films and limit the device efficiency. Herein, a stacked quasi-2D (down)–3D (top) double-layered structure in perovskite films prepared via vacuum treatment is demonstrated by us, which can result in a planar bilayer heterojunction. In addition, it is found that the introduction of guanidinium thiocyanate (GuaSCN) additive can improve the crystallinity and carrier mobility in the 2D perovskite layer and passivate defects in the whole film, leading to a long carrier lifetime (>140 ns) in photoluminescence measurements. As a result, the PSCs show a high open circuit voltage (VOC) up to 1.01 V with a voltage loss of only 0.39 V, which represents the record values ever reported for tin-based PSCs. The champion device exhibits a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.79% with decent stability, retaining 90% of the initial PCE for 1200h storage in N2-filled glovebox.

15206918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206918.value: 360度視頻的高效編碼技術及其快速編碼框架

15206918.label: Project Objectives
15206918.value: Each frame of spherical 360-degree video is projected on a 2D plane in order to adapt it to the input format of the existing video codecs. So far, various 2D projection representations have been investigating intensively in literature and JVET. All these projections evidently cause geometric distortion, and make the conventional motion-compensated prediction, which assumes the translational motion model, is not appropriate for exploiting the temporal correlation between these 2D projection planes. Therefore, one of the objectives in this proposal is to focus on designing a new model for motion compensation(MC) on a spherical domain other than the 2D projection domain for the inter-frame coding purposes. Results of our preliminary study show that the new MC model provides impact gains compared with the state-of-the-art HEVC codec for 360-degree video. However, the new MC model depends on block-based motion estimation(ME) in the 2D projection domain. In this proposal, we will evaluate the impact of the conventional ME on the new MC model in 360-degree video coding, and explore the characteristics of non-linearity between the spherical and 2D projection domains. This motivate us to adopt the spherical-domain distortion criterion for ME, which avoids the problem of non-linearity when ME is performed in the 2D projection planes. This ME strategy with the new MC model provides high coding efficiency and is tailor-made for inter-frame coding in 360-degree video. The geometric distortion induces many curves in the 2D projection plane, which makes the conventional intra-prediction inefficient. A further need for new intra modes, which are specifically designed for the curve coming from geometric distortion, may arise. The trajectory of the curve due to the non-linear mapping will be studied for the purpose of contriving curve prediction, instead of straight edge prediction in intra-prediction mode.

15206918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206918.value: 隨著顯示器，網絡和計算技術的不斷發展， 工業的重心開始向360度/全向視頻轉變，正如虛擬現實（VR）和增強現實（AR）的興起。計算機視覺和圖形對於VR / AR的興趣現已經轉移到360度視頻並給用戶帶來360度全景視覺體驗和身臨其境般的體驗。因此，360度視頻流成為VR實現的重要支撐技術。這些視頻服務最近變得非常流行，並在Facebook，YouTube等幾個主要視頻平台上推出。因此，高效率和低複雜度的360度視頻編碼是減少巨大數據傳輸量的關鍵技術。目前360度視頻的編碼解決方案主要來源於傳統視頻。然而，360度視頻並不能通過簡單地將球形信息投影到平面圖像進行編碼，因為該投影引起幾何失真並顯著影響當前標準中的傳統幀間/幀內編碼技術的編碼效率。因此，ITU-T VCEG和ISO / IEC MPEG的聯合視頻探索小組（JVET）正在研究在未來視頻編碼標準中包含360度視頻編碼技術的潛在需求。這項研究將在球面域中探索並用於360度視頻編碼的新的幀間/幀內預測工具，並且將研究一些有效的算法以解決這些具有挑戰性的問題。 360度視頻的特徵與傳統的2D視頻有著巨大差異。然而，目前最先進的視頻編解碼器專為具有平移運動和直線邊界的2D視頻而設計，並不適合360度視頻。因此，新的360度視頻編碼方法是很有必要的。在文獻中，各種2D投影表示和採樣方法已經被提出，但是它們仍處於技術發展的早期階段，特別是在幀間/幀內編碼中。由於不同的2D投影平面引起的曲線，非平移運動和幾何失真來都自從球面到2D投影域的映射，這個研究計劃是利用我們的經驗和幀間/幀內編碼的強大背景來開發一個新的MC運動模型，將2D投影平面的特定運動行為結合到到我們提出的球面域運動估計中，並考慮從球面域到2D投影域的非線性映射。作為初步研究，與球面域運動估計結合而成的新運動補償模型可以僅用一個運動矢量對塊內具有不同運動的像素進行建模，這對於處理360度視頻的幾何失真至關重要。此外，我們提出了一種新的基於曲線的幀內預測，用於編碼在2D投影平面中具有不同曲線的塊。在本次探究中，我們的初步公式表明360度視頻投影空間中的幾何失真和曲線可以被解決。隨著各種新模式的引入，它將擁有巨大的計算複雜度。為了緩解這種情況，我們利用360度視頻中的一些特徵提出了一種快速模式決策分類器。我們相信我們是第一個在360度視頻編碼中考慮這種決策的小組。通過這項研究，我們將實現360度視頻內容的編碼框架。它不僅對理論研究具有重要價值，而且還可以為許多需要360度視頻的商業VR / AR產品奠定堅實的基礎。

15206918.label: Realisation of objectives
15206918.value: Objective 1: To realize the proposed idea, we first implemented the new intra/inter-prediction framework in 360-degree video coding. A 360-degree video records a location from all possible angles around a central point, allowing viewers to freely access the content from any direction. The viewing directions are assumed to be uniformly distributed, creating an isotropic observation space similar to a sphere. This video data is represented using various projection formats, which are essentially 2D planes that capture different perspectives of the spherical domain. These projection formats are collectively referred to as representation space. However, mapping from the spherical domain (observation space) to 2D projection domain (representation space) involves nonlinear transformation resulting in the non-perspective nature of 2D projection plane. It causes large deformation of the video content. Our work investigated a possible trend in the near future of performing intra/inter-prediction by exploring the geometric distortion due to the specific projection of a 360-degree video format to a 2D plane. For example, all these projections evidently cause geometric distortion and make the conventional inter/intra-prediction in video coding not appropriate for exploiting the temporal/spatial correlation between these 2D projection planes. After the investigation, we designed new models for motion compensation (MC)/intra prediction on a spherical domain other than the 2D projection domain for inter/intra-frame coding purposes, respectively. Objective 1 has then been achieved by effectively designing the frameworks for MC/intra prediction. Objective 2: For inter-prediction, we developed a new MC motion model that incorporates the specific motion behavior to the 2D projection plane into our proposed spherical domain motion estimation. The model takes non-linear mapping from the spherical domain to the 2D projection domain into consideration. Based on this concept, the new motion compensation model integrated with the spherical-domain motion estimation can model all pixels inside the block having different motion, but only one motion vector is required. This is crucial to handle the geometric distortion for 360-degree video. As compared to previous works, our new MC model does not require additional motion vectors, and is independent of camera parameters. We implemented this MC model into the HEVC encoder for coding equirectangular projection (ERP) of various 360-degree videos. This novel advanced MC model can finally handle the geometric distortion in the 2D projection plane of 360-degree video by projecting the pixels in the ERP to the sphere. Besides, by making use of the uniform motion characteristic in the sphere, the relationship between the motion vectors among various pixels in ERP can be derived. In this way, the geometric distortion in ERP can be handled efficiently. Remarkable gains have been achieved in 360-degree interframe coding. Objective 2 has then been fully accomplished with significant progress made towards the goal. Objective 3: Geometric distortion in ERP always turns lines that should be straight into curve. Numerous curves are then generated for 360-degree images due to the lens curvature and projection format. Conventional intra-prediction tools are not optimal for compressing 360-degree content since there are many curved structures. Studying the geometric distortion for 360-degree video after projection motivates us to adopt curve-based prediction tools into the 360-degree video coding scheme. The investigation of a curve-based intra-prediction tool was conducted in this project. In the proposed algorithm, inspired by Spherical Linear Interpolation (Slerp), which was originally used in computer graphics animation, our proposed 360-degree intra mode can efficiently encode those curved structures. By taking the geometric distortion, we studied the trajectory of the curve for intra-prediction based on the locations of coding units. With our novel coding mode and carefully selected coding parameters, the coding efficiency is improved with 0.32% on average and up to 0.74% BD-rate reduction using S-PSNR. As compared with the recent development of 360-degree video compression, our approach can achieve a more reasonable increase in both encoding and decoding complexities. Some other factors, such as foreground/background regions, were also considered in the new coding tools. It is noted that only the horizontal line is changed to a curve in ERP. In the case of other types of projections, the vertical line may also be affected. Therefore, various models have then been successfully made to develop more intricate curve-based intra-prediction modes for these projections. As a result, different intra-prediction has been designed for different projections to achieve a good trade-off between coding efficiency and complexity for 360-degree videos. This progress has been made toward our goal, resulting in the complete accomplishment of Objective 3.

15206918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206918.value: Recent technological advancements in displays, networking, and computing have shifted industry focus towards 360-degree/omnidirectional video, particularly for virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR). Streaming 360-degree videos has become crucial to realizing the true-to-life VR experience with immersive 360-degree views. As a result, high-efficiency and low-complexity 360-degree video coding is essential to reduce data transmission. However, traditional video coding techniques are insufficient due to geometric distortion caused by projecting spherical information onto a planar image. This research work designed a number of efficient algorithms/models to implement the required components and address challenging issues, which has contributed to the advancement of 360-degree video coding technology. Conventional video codecs designed for natural 2D sequences are not suitable for 360-degree videos, which have unique characteristics such as non-translational motions and geometric distortion caused by the mapping from the spherical surface to 2D projection domains. Although various 2D projection representations methods were proposed, but they were still in the early stages of development, particularly in inter/intra-frame coding. This research aim is to develop a new MC motion model that incorporates the specific motion behavior of 2D projection planes and the non-linear mapping from the spherical domain to the 2D projection domain. To handle geometric distortion, a new motion compensation model integrated with spherical-domain motion estimation has been developed, which models all pixels inside the block with different motion but only requires one motion vector. Additionally, a novel curve-based intra-prediction method has been proposed to encode blocks with various curves in 2D projection planes. The newly proposed model shows that these methods can handle the geometric distortion and curves in the projection space of 360-degree videos. Therefore, this research has successfully addressed the specific requirements of 360-degree videos and improved their coding efficiency, contributing to the development of a promising approach for 360-degree video coding standards. As a result, five journal papers and five conference papers have been published in this project.

15206918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206918.value: The newly introduced inter/intra modes have significantly increased the exhaustive mode decision process, posing a challenge. To address this issue, our research team plans to explore the use of machine learning (ML) classifiers, which can be trained based on specific features tailored for 360-degree video. The investigation of these features is crucial for the development of effective ML classifiers. The introduction of using ML in 360-degree video coding is a brand new concept to optimize the trade-off among quality, bitrate, and complexity. We expect the work in the standard organization will also adopt new coding tools in the future video coding standard. In our plan, we will also plan to make a comparative study with the new tools. When the performance of the proposed algorithm is proven to be better than the future approaches in the coding standardization activities. The core techniques in this research will be submitted to JVET for their consideration and possible inclusion in future video coding standards. Therefore, in the long term, we should participate in JVET meetings to promote our techniques in future video coding standards. Our present study will have a remarkable long-term and significant impact on the advancement of future 360-degree video coding technology.

15206918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206918.value: The research project is focused on improving the way 360-degree videos are created and stored. With the rise of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), 360-degree videos have become increasingly popular as they offer users a more immersive experience. However, the characteristics of 360-degree video sequences differ substantially from the conventional 2D sequences. Thus, the current video codecs that are used to store and transmit traditional 2D videos are not well-suited for 360-degree videos. It is due to the fact that 360-degree videos have unique characteristics such as non-translational motions and geometric distortion, which make them difficult to encode efficiently. To address this challenge, this research project is to develop new and novel motion models that take into account the specific motion behavior of 2D projection planes and the non-linear mapping from the spherical domain to the 2D projection domain. For intra-prediction, this research work also designs a novel curve-based model to encode blocks with various curves in 2D projection planes. The goal of this research is to create an encoding framework for 360-degree videos that is efficient and effective, which is valuable for theoretical studies and commercial VR/AR products that require 360-degree videos.

15207318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207318.value: With low volatility, low biodegradation rate and high bioaccumulation, pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) have recently aroused worldwide concern as emerging contaminants. PPCP pollution is a particularly serious environmental problem in China which is the largest producer and consumer of pharmaceutical ingredients of the world and one of the top three countries with the largest personal care product consumption. For the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region and Hong Kong with dense population and high urbanization in China, the pollution of PPCPs is more acute. Recent studies have confirmed that several antibiotics are widely distributed in the main rivers and sewage treatment plants of Hong Kong, which are often eliminated incompletely during treatments. Thus, efficient remediation technologies are urged to develop for the removal of PPCPs from aquatic environment. This project will propose a novel composite catalyst for persulfate (PS) activation to remove PPCPs in the aqueous environment, by using porous minerals as support for spinel oxide particles. The spinel oxide will be tailored by two of active metals (e.g., Co, Cu, Mn, Fe and Zn) to obtain efficient catalysts for PS activation towards PPCP degradation. Then the spinle oxide with optimized activity will be loaded on the porous minerals with different pore distribution and morphology as supports, e.g., montmorillonite, palygorskite, halloysite and diatomite, to improve the dispersion of spine oxide particles. The used porous minerals are abundant resource in China. At last, the reaction parameters (pH, catalyst dosage, PS concentration, mineralization time and cation leaching) will be optimized, while the degradation pathways of typical PPCPs, e.g., loxacin, tetracycline and sulfamethoxazole, and the biological toxicity of degradation products will be determined. Based on catalyst characterization and batch degradation experiment, the relationship between local structure of transition metals (e.g., species, valence and occupancy) and activity (e.g., surface properties and catalytic activity) of spinel-based catalysts will be illustrated. Moreover, the effects of porous mineral types, and content and microstructure of spinel oxides on the adsorption and catalytic activity of composite catalyst will also be discussed. The obtained results will be beneficial to the development of on-going treatment technology for the removal of PPCPs. 藥物及個人護理用品（PPCPs）作為新興污染物，由於其穩定、低生物降解率以及高生物累積率等特點，引起了全世界的廣泛關注。中國作為世界上最大的藥物生產國、消費國以及全球三大個人護理用品消費國之一，PPCPs污染問題尤為嚴重。在珠三角地區及香港，由於人口密集及城市化較高，PPCPs污染形勢更為嚴峻。已有研究表明，由於降解不徹底，抗生素廣泛分佈於香港的主要河流及汙水處理系統中。因此，亟待開發有效去除水體中PPCPs的新型技術。 本專案擬通過多孔礦物負載在尖晶石氧化物顆粒上製備得到一種新型催化劑，應用該催化劑活化過二硫酸鹽（persulfate，PS）來降解PPCPs。應用兩種活性金屬（如Co，Cu，Mn，Fe及Zn）來調適尖晶石氧化物，從而獲得能夠有效活化PS以降解PPCPs的催化劑。之後，選取活性最高的尖晶石氧化物負載到具有不同孔徑分佈及形貌的多孔礦物（如蒙脫石、坡縷石、矽藻土等） ，以提高尖晶石氧化物顆粒的分散性。專案中所應用的多孔礦物在中國均儲備豐富。最後，優化反應參數（如pH值、催化劑劑量、PS濃度、礦化時間及陽離子淋溶）。同時，揭示典型PPCPs（如氧氟沙星、四環素、磺胺甲惡唑）的降解路徑及反應產物的生物毒性。 根據催化劑表徵及實驗室降解實驗，揭示製備所得催化劑中過渡金屬的局部結構（如物種、價位及占位）與催化劑活性（如表面性質及催化活性）的關係。此外，討論多孔礦物的類型、內容物及尖晶石氧化物的微結構對複合催化劑的吸附、催化活性的影響。該專案所得結果對改進已有PPCPs處理技術具有重大意義。

15207318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207318.value: Two composite catalysts with CoMn2O4 loaded on different natural clay minerals, kaolinite (Kln) and halloysite (Hal), were successfully fabricated through co-precipitation method. To clarify the effect from the content of CMO within the composite catalysts towards their PMS activation, 20, 40, and 60-CMO/Hal were investigated and compared with bare CMO spontaneously. With outstanding performance, 40-CMO/Hal was selected for further studies under the optimal working conditions, i.e., proper pH, dosage of PMS, and initial concentrations of the target pharmaceuticals (carbamazepine, CBZ). The stability and durability of 40-CMO/Hal and bare CMO were explored through a three-time reuse, while the metal leakage during them were determined by ICP-OES. The potential PMS activation mechanism was proposed according to traditional trapping experiments and results obtained from electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The possible degradation pathways and final products of CBZ were determined based on the intermediates detected by LC-MS and the TOC results. The possible application of 40-CMO/Hal in removing common antibiotics was verified by targeting tetracycline (TC), ofloxacin (OFX) and sulfamethoxazole (SMZ). The positive results promise the development of an effective treatment technology for the removal of common pharmaceuticals. To investigate the impacts from clay mineral substrates with different morphologies, CMO/Hal and CMO/Kln with the same CMO loading percentage (40%), were chosen for further comparisons and investigations. The results indicated that both Hal and Kln helped to control the crystallinity of CMO spontaneously with induce oxygen vacancies (OVs), which significantly enhanced the working efficiency. The reaction rate constants of Hal/CMO and Kln/CMO towards OFX degradation were nearly triple and twice that of bare CMO, respectively. CMO/Hal and CMO/Kln exhibited higher stability and durability than CMO, while CMO/Kln showed higher structural stability with lower metal leaching after 3 rounds of reaction. This work revealed the effectiveness and efficiency of the SR-AOPs using PMS activated by CMO loaded on natural clay. The modified catalysts, either CMO/Hal or CMO/Kln, both overcame the disadvantages of bare CMO, spontaneously with promoting their PMS activation efficiency for the degradation of pharmaceuticals. The presence of Hal and Kln contributed to the regulation of CMO particles’ grain size and crystallinity, the promotion of specific surface area by the evenly distribution of CMO particles, and the induction of more active OVs. Hal was advantageous in the generation of more OVs, while CMO/Kln with higher crystallinity and ordered structure maintained higher structural stability with less metal leakage.

15207318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207318.value: The experiments were generally performed in laboratory using batch reactors, and focused more on the elimination of single target compound each time. It is necessary to conduct continuous tests with more relevant elements, e.g., coexistence of multi chemicals or pharmaceutical contaminants, and the effects of some naturally occurring microorganisms and algae in water. In addition, although CMO/Hal and CMO/Kln catalysts both showed superior PMS activity in degrading pharmaceuticals than bare CMO, they still had some limitations, e.g., the unbalanced improvement of both catalytic activity and structural stability, and the unavoidable metal leaching. Thus, these catalysts could be further modified via hybrid processes combining the catalyst/PMS system with membrane and/or ultrasonic technologies. For example, nano-sized catalysts with extremely small grain size are generally considered with hard, time-consuming, and high mass loss during their separation from water. By entrapping nano-catalysts directly into the pores of porous catalytic membranes may promote the collaborative separation simultaneously with enhanced catalytic efficiency. Among various membrane materials, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), an electroactive semicrystalline thermoplastic material, has received increasing attention with high practicality in water purification. It might be feasible to immobilize the CMO/Hal and/or CMO/Kln catalysts into PVDF membrane for pharmaceutical degradation via PMS activation.

15207318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207318.value: This research shed lights on the application of natural minerals in the modification of transition metal catalysts aimed at heterogeneous PMS activation with enhanced catalytic ability and low-impact remediation of pharmaceuticals. Spinel oxide was tailored by two active metals to obtain higher activity, and then loaded on porous minerals to improve the particle dispersion, decrease particle size, and reduce cation dissolution. The PMS activation ability of the catalyst were investigated thoroughly and separately towards the degradation of some typical pharmaceuticals which were frequently detected in water environment. The utilization of spinel oxides on porous clay minerals can solve several key technical challenges to optimize the catalytic performance of transition metals via increased the treatment performance with synergistic effect of mixed transition metals, improved surface properties and stability of catalyst for real application, enhanced adsorption properties of catalyst, and feasible reusing of the catalyst in real applications with minimized metal loss. Clay minerals, halloysite and kaolinite, are abundant mineral resources in China. The outcomes of the projects imposed significant long-term benefits to reduce the potential environmental risk of PPCPs in Hong Kong, as evidenced in the attached supporting letters from the government and industry.

15207918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207918.value: The District Cooling System (DCS) concept has attracted increasing attention in many cities, such as Singapore, Tokyo, Hong Kong and cities in South China. The Hong Kong government has adopted DCS as one of the main energy efficiency measures within its “smart city” development initiative. In particular, DCS has been adopted for the new district development in Kowloon East and will also be adopted in the North East NT development area. Although DCS is very attractive and has good potential for achieving high energy efficiency in high-density districts, the actual achievement of the energy saving potential is not automatic. One of the biggest challenges is how to deal with the impacts of uncertainties and reliability issue. Uncertainties widely exist in the design inputs and construction process, resulting in that the actual working conditions are often very different from that projected at the design stage. Reliability issue refers the risks of equipment failures/degradations during operation. To ensure the actual DCS performance reaches expectations, these uncertainties and reliability issue should be properly taken into account at the design and testing & commissioning (T&C) stages. However, in current design practice, these complex issues are handled usually in a very simple fashion by means of introducing safety factors and standby provision. Current T&C simply aims to meet an intended design target, even though the actual operating conditions deviate significantly from the design conditions. Thus, systems are usually deliberately oversized at the design stage and the energy saving potentials accruing from these oversized designs are ignored at T&C and operation stages. This project therefore proposes two new design concepts (i.e., “probabilistic optimal & adaptive design” and “on-site adaptive T&C”), to address the uncertainty and reliability issues and achieve maximum energy saving. A “probabilistic optimal design method” for chiller plants and a “probabilistic optimal & adaptive design method” for water circulation systems will be developed. The proposed design methods will enable designers to make the best predictions and flexible designs which take the impacts of possible uncertainties and the probabilities of component failures into account by quantitative means. On-site adaptive T&C allows engineers to adjust the actual systems constructed according to the actual system characteristic uncovered during the T&C stage and therefore realize the energy saving potential as much as possible. The project outputs will help to provide significant and meaningful improvements to the current design and T&C standards/practices of DCSs and centralized air-conditioning systems. 區域供冷系統的概念吸引了越來越多城市的關注，比如新加坡，東京，香港和中國南方的城市。香港政府已經將區域供冷系統作為它智慧城市發展計劃中主要的節能措施之一。特別是區域供冷系統已經應用於九龍東部的新區發展建設中，並且將會用於新界东北的發展建設中。儘管區域供冷系統很吸引人而且在高密度區域有很好的節能潛力，但在實際應用中這種節能潛力並不是必然的。最大的挑戰之一是怎樣處理不確定性和可靠性問題的影響。不確定性普遍存在于設計輸入數據和建造過程中，這導致實際工況和在設計時預計的工況相差很大。可靠性的問題是指在運行過程中設備故障或性能下降的風險。 為了確保實際的區域供冷系統到預期的效果，在設計和調試階段應該考慮這些不確定性和可靠性問題。但是，目前的系統設計經常只是通過引入安全係數和提供備用的方法簡單地處理了這些複雜的問題。目前的調試只是將系統調至設計狀態，不管實際運行工況和設計工況相差很多。所以，在設計階段系統一般會故意選大，在調試階段由於過大設計導致的節能潛力也被忽略了。 因此本項目提出了兩個新的設計概念用於解決不確定性和可靠性問題並且將節能最大化。這兩個設計概念分別是概率優化和自適應設計以及現場自適應調試。這個項目將會开發製冷機組的概率優化設計方法以及水循環系統的概率優化及自適應設計方法。该的設計方法能讓設計師定量化地考慮潛在的不確定性和設備故障的影響并做出最佳的和靈活的設計。現場自適調試能讓工程師在試驗調試階段根據實際的系統特點調整系統從而實現盡可能多的節能。本項目將會使區域供冷系統和集中式空調系統目前的設計及試驗調試標準和實踐得到顯著和有意義的提高。

15207918.label: Realisation of objectives
15207918.value: 5 research objectives have been fully addressed. More details are elaborated as below. First, we developed the method of probabilistic optimal design for chiller plants by integrating uncertainty and reliability quantifications into the optimal design process. Secondly, we have developed the method of probabilistic optimal and adaptive design for water circulation systems facilitating the adaptive T&C of the systems at the T&C stage, aiming to achieve their best performance according to actual system characteristics. Thirdly, we have analyzed the interaction between system design and T&C processes, and developed the on-site adaptive T&C method to fully utilize the energy saving potentials of typical and normally oversized water circulation systems in coordination with the probabilistic optimal and adaptive design method developed. Then, we have developed an automated method and tool for selecting of the best pump models and development of adaptive T&C schemes. Finally, we have validated the probabilistic optimal and adaptive design methods as well as the on-site adaptive T&C method in two buildings in Hong Kong.

15207918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207918.value: 10 research papers published. The main research work and achievements are summarized as follows. Developed the method of probabilistic optimal design for chiller plants by integrating uncertainty and reliability quantifications into the design process. A systematic approach of probabilistic optimal design and adaptive commissioning for central cooling systems of buildings to minimize the actual impact (energy waste and increased life-cycle cost) of oversizing in operation. Developed the method of probabilistic optimal and adaptive design for water circulation systems to facilitate the adaptive T&C of the systems at the T&C stage, aiming to achieve their best performance in tune with actual system characteristics. The probabilistic optimal design considers both the uncertainties of design inputs and the flexibility of on-site adaptive commissioning, while adaptive commissioning enables flexible balancing to maximize energy saving according to characteristics of constructed systems. Explored the interaction between system design and T&C processes, and develop the on-site adaptive T&C approach to fully utilize the energy saving potential of an oversized water circulation system in coordination with the probabilistic optimal and adaptive design method developed. Developed a robust optimal design method to efficiently identify the global optimal design solutions for the entire zero/low energy buildings under uncertainties, including two stages: robust design optimizations of building envelope and energy systems considering uncertainties. Developed an agent-based distributed real-time control strategy for building HVAC systems with the objective to be deployed in the local control devices with limited programming and computation capacities, i.e., smart sensors integrated in future IoT-based field networks and local controllers in field networks of current LAN-based building automation systems. Investigated new challenges of nearly and net ZEB design under the post-occupancy performance-based design standards. Propose a risk-benefit based optimal design method to facilitate the achievement of nearly and net ZEBs under these standards.
