15208018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208018.value: Adult degenerative (de novo) scoliosis (ADS) is a condition of the ageing population caused by degenerative changes without pre-existing spinal deformity. Pain is the most frequent problem, especially low back pain and radicular pain, and seriously affects the daily activities and health of ADS patients. The current treatment for ADS is not well defined. The main intervention for ADS treatment is surgical, but surgery is clearly not appropriate for every patient. Custom-fabricated rigid torso braces similar to those used for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) are occasionally used in adults. The goal of these braces is to correct and/or sustain the sagittal plane of the patients. However, previous literature has demonstrated that bracing can only help relieve pain temporarily and does not prevent curve progression in the adult population. Clearly, our knowledge about how ADS may be alleviated with conservative treatment is lacking. This study is a multi-disciplinary collaborative study that includes experts in orthopaedics, physiotherapy, materials science and textiles, garment technology, engineering and biomechanics. The first objective is to establish a thorough scientific basis for ADS pathophysiology and gait pattern as well as the myoelectric activities of the trunk and lower limb muscles in relation to various clinical situations. The morphology and asymmetry of the body, kinematic profiles of the spine and locomotor skills of mature adults with ADS will be analysed. Active bodysuits will then be designed based on body alignment and pain management using special design components and incorporating active posture training from a biofeedback system. Back pain is often localized along the convexity of the curve, and passive support to the areas of pain, most likely in the lower trunk, hip and lower extremities, should be provided. The biomechanical efficiency of the bodysuits will be evaluated with finite element (FE) modelling of ADS patient spines. The effects of bodysuit design components will be computed in terms of the compressive stresses produced at different body parts, and corrections to the 3D clinical indices (pelvic tilt, sacral slope, pelvic incidence, lumbar lordosis and the sagittal vertical axis) will be determined. Older adults are predicted to benefit from wearing these bodysuits, which maintain their current levels of function while minimizing symptom progression. The output of this project would extend to the development of other orthotic products and will add a new dimension to medical clothing for patients.

15208018.label: Realisation of objectives
15208018.value: Adult degenerative scoliosis (ADS), which is also known as de novo scoliosis, is a condition of the ageing population caused by degenerative changes of spine in individuals who do not have any pre-existing spinal deformities, with a Cobb angle that exceeds 10° in the coronal plane. Globally, there is an approximate overall incidence rate of ADS of 6% for people aged 50 or older, and the average progression of the spinal curvature is 3.3° each year. Patients with ADS usually suffer from progressive lower back pain with radiculopathy and neurogenic claudication, spinal stenosis, and progression of the spinal curve which negatively affect the health-related quality of life. Patients are required to wear a rigid brace to relieve pain, correct their posture and reduce the progression of the spinal curvature, which could lead to the problems of discomfort and pressure sores, and cause psychological barriers to compliance with treatment. In response, this project aims to develop a novel flexible brace that provides adequate corrective forces, as well as improves the wear comfort and aesthetics perspective towards bracing treatment. To achieve the project goal, this study will carry out three tasks, including: (1) To establish a thorough scientific understanding of ADS pathophysiology, gait patterns, and the myoelectric activities of the trunk and lower limb muscles in relation to various clinical situations. The morphology and asymmetry of the body, the kinematic profile of the spine and the locomotor skills of older adults with ADS will be analysed in relation to body alignment and posture training to provide three-dimensional re-equilibration of the spine. (2) To facilitate FE modelling of ADS patient spines to evaluate the shear and compressive stresses between the spine and the brace. Achieving this objective would allow us to compare the biomechanical efficiency of different designs for treating ADS patients using the developed FE model. (3) To design and develop active bodysuits for older ADS patients based on clinical applications, materials science, garments, and wearable technologies that focus on core strengthening, postural training, reducing lower back pain, and addressing the needs of the elderly while considering their physiological concerns. We also seek to perform laboratory tests and clinical trials to evaluate whether the intended objectives of the active bodysuits can be achieved. Objective 1) The posture, balance and muscle utilisation of ADS patients are still unclear. To enhance current understanding of how ADS contributes to the posture, balance and muscle activity, a total of 10 ADS subjects and 10 asymptomatic subjects are recruited to perform habitual standing and sitting. A three-dimensional (3D) motion capturing system, force platform and surface electromyography are used in this study. The ADS subjects demonstrated higher knee flexion in the standing posture and increased hip and knee flexion in the sitting posture at the convex side of their spinal curvature. Moreover, the paraspinal muscles and lower extremities at the convex side of the spine generally showed increase in muscle activity compared to the concave side. The findings demonstrated that ADS patients change their balance pattern to compensate for the shift of the gravity line caused by spinal deformity and have asymmetrical muscles that are elongated and stretched at the convex side of the curvature. Objective 2) An FE model is constructed to simulate the wear process of the active bodysuit through the torso of an ADS patient which demonstrates its biomechanics and corrective effect. The result shows that the waistband is the most critical component for correcting the spinal curvature, followed by the side struts, shoulder straps and finally the middle strut. The optimized design of the proposed active bodysuit should have woven shoulder straps with a Young’s Modulus of 243 MPa, waistband with a Young’s Modulus of 0.45 MPa, 6061 aluminium alloy middle struts and polyoxymethylene side struts should be used to reduce the predicted in-brace Cobb angle from 29.2° to 27°. Objective 3) Active bodysuits for older ADS patients was design and developed. The active corrective forces are produced through a vibrotactile feedback (VTF) system during posture training sessions. Meanwhile, passive forces are produced by the bracewear with spinal support which eliminates the adversities of conventional hard braces by offering increased flexibility and comfort. Finally, a clinical study is conducted to investigate the efficacy of the existing active bodysuit in terms of the in-brace correction, health-related quality of life and feedback from the recruited subjects. Most of the subjects experience a reduction of Cobb angle greater than 5 degrees while the pain score is reduced after 3-months of brace wear. However, the initial in-brace correction effect of the 2-hour clinical study is not adequate due to possible influential variables, such as a low compliance rate and the material used for the bodysuit. Therefore, the correction effect of the active bodysuit should be enhanced in order to prevent the progression of spinal curvature as well as maintain the ability of ADS patients to perform daily activities. Based on the results of the clinical study, the thermal comfort and corrective effect of the proposed active bodysuit are the areas that require more attention. First, different fabrics are sourced, and material tests are conducted for the inner vest. A biomechanical model is then developed and validated by comparing the results with those of an actual radiographic examination. The model also eliminates the problems of repeated radiation exposure, subject involvement, long manufacturing time, and brace wear time when conducting a wear trial. The biomechanical model shows a trend of spinal correction with good accuracy. To optimise the spinal corrective effect of the proposed active bodysuit, the different material properties of the shoulder straps, waistband, and side and middle struts are modified by using a D-optimal design. It is found that the design combination of woven shoulder straps with Young's Modulus of 243 MPa, elastics Young's Modulus of 0.45 MPa, 6061 aluminum alloy and polyoxymethylene provides the highest in-brace spinal correction which reduces the predicted in-brace Cobb angle from 29.2° to 27°. The stiffness of the waistband is regarded as the most important factor in reducing the Cobb angle, followed by stiffness of the side struts, shoulder straps and lastly the middle strut. The research results in this study enhance current knowledge on the balance, posture and muscle activity of ADS patients, as well as provide useful information for the design, thermal comfort and mechanics of flexible braces to control spinal deformities and maintain daily activities of ADS patients. The use of FEM and D-optimal design provides an objective, efficient and reliable methodology to evaluate the performance of different brace materials in correcting spinal deformities and optimising the effectiveness of the proposed active bodysuit. The output of this project can be extended to the development of similar orthotic devices and textile medical products.

15208018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208018.value: 1) Establishment of new knowledge characterizing standing balance and gait of older adults with ADS Experimental evaluation has showed that ADS patients (N=10, 60.67 ± 4.23 years, Cobb angle 38.1° ± 22.7°) have much poorer standing balance in the antero-posterior (AP) direction when compared to asymptomatic individuals. This observation agrees with the study by Yagi et al., where older subjects (65.4 ± 6.7 years) with more serious scoliosis (Cobb angle 48.6° ± 20.28°) were involved. Our findings suggest that the patients with ADS might encounter balancing problem at an earlier age. Also, our result showed that the patient group has a longer double support time and higher % of stance phase in a stride cycle, indicating that ADS patients might spend more effort to stabilize their gait. 2) New FE sub-models are developed to evaluate the compressive stresses produced between the spine and the bodysuit. An FE model is constructed to simulate the wear process of the active bodysuit through the torso of an ADS patient which demonstrates its biomechanics and corrective effect. The result shows that the waistband is the most critical component for correcting the spinal curvature, followed by the side struts, shoulder straps and finally the middle strut. The optimized design of the proposed active bodysuit should have woven shoulder straps with a Young’s Modulus of 243 MPa, waistband with a Young’s Modulus of 0.45 MPa, 6061 aluminium alloy middle struts and polyoxymethylene side struts should be used to reduce the predicted in-brace Cobb angle from 29.2° to 27°. 3) Newly designed active training bodysuits for ADS that incorporate both passive and active correction. In response to the drawbacks of bracing and the special needs of older ADS patients, an active training bodywear that incorporates both passive and active corrective forces with a more age-friendly design was developed and evaluated in this study. At the end of the 3-month intervention, all the eight domains defined by the Brace Questionnaire (BrQ) showed improvements, with the highest percentage increase in vitality (+19.5%), followed by emotional functioning (+13.91%) and physical functioning (+11.09%). As for Scoliosis Research Society-22 (SRS-22) questionnaire, improvements were shown in all domains of the health-related quality of life, among which pain (+9.5%) and mental health (+7.2%) domains experienced the greatest improvement. The mean Oswestry Low Back Pain Disability questionnaire (ODI) score has been reduced from 23.29% to 18.17% after the 3-month intervention.

15208018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208018.value: Based on the established research findings and limitations, the recommendations for future work are as follows: • Sensorimotor function assessment, and external perturbations are not included in the study. To gain a better understanding of the balance control strategies adopted by ADS patients, further research work is required. • A torso model with organs, ligaments, tendons, muscles and skin and skeletal model with rib cage and posterior elements should be developed in the future. Moreover, FE simulations with more design factors such as the thickness of the materials can be carried out to predict their performance for in-brace spinal curvature reduction. • A randomised controlled trial with a large sample size for the proposed active bodysuit is recommended to evaluate the actual efficacy of the proposed active bodysuit which the subjects are randomly assigned to wear the existing active bodysuit and the proposed active bodysuit for 1 year. Moreover, monitoring devices like temperature loggers or IMU sensors can be embedded in the active bodysuit to check the compliance rate. • Active games have its own unique values and benefits in postural / motor learning of older adults. Future studies could be focus on the efficiency of transferring the benefits obtained in the video gameplay training to postural control in daily life.

15208018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208018.value: Patients with adult degenerative scoliosis (ADS) usually suffer from progressive lower back pain, progressive deformity and symptoms of sagittal imbalance. Bracing is the most typical non-invasive treatment recommended for ADS. However, related studies have revealed that extended periods of bracing of older patients can cause deconditioning of the paraspinal muscles and overall worsening of the deformity and symptoms. In response to the drawbacks of bracing and also the special needs of older ADS patients, an active training bodywear that incorporates both passive and active corrective forces with a more age-friendly design was developed in this study. The active bodysuit successfully incorporated active self-correction into passive bracing, which will be very helpful for maintaining the level of bodily function of patients while minimizing the symptom progression of ADS, as well as improving the current problems of brace-wearing experiences through the design and development of the posture training bodywear. It is anticipated that this project will contribute as a new breakthrough in brace development especially for older ADS patients and provide a healthier lifestyle to them.

15208418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208418.value: 正如现今的复杂系统依赖于各种控制机制一样，毫无疑问，量子控制理论也将在推动量子工程技术创新方面发挥不可或缺的作用。 从经典工程实践中可以看出，线性系统模型通常允许对控制系统进行严格的研究，所以它具有可分析性和计算易处理性。 此外，成熟的线性系统理论通常是研究更一般的非线性系统理论的重要基础。 次项目的目的是通过研究以下三个主题，为量子线性系统的结构分析及其在量子信息科学中的应用开发强大而严格的数学方法： 1：量子线性系统的卡尔曼规范的结构分析。 2：量子线性系统的一种新的参数化方法。 3：应用于量子信息科学，特别是无消相干系统（DFS）和量子非破坏（QND）变量的设计 主题1通过由研究者（PI）和合作者提出的卡尔曼规范形式来揭示量子线性系统的结构。推导出卡尔曼规范形式的物理可实现性条件，并阐明卡尔曼规范形式的系统矩阵的各个组件之间的各种关系。这些关系对于探索量子线性系统的谱理论很有用。 主题2提出一种新的量子线性系统参数化方法。这个新的参数化是直接基于卡尔曼规范形式设计的。因此，所涉及的参数是对应于卡尔曼规范形式的块状结构的块状形式。该参数结构可用于简化各种控制设计问题，这些问题是主题3的焦点。 主题3研究量子线性系统理论在量子信息科学中的应用。如研究人员最近所示，卡尔曼规范形式明确地表征了DFS，QND变量和BAE测量。通过主题2中提出的参数化方法，DFS和QND变量的设计以及BAE测量的实现都可以根据指定卡尔曼规范形式的这些新参数来制定。由于它们的块状性质，每个给定任务需要很少量的参数。 总之，拟议的研究主要是为量子器件工程提供强大且数学上严格的工具，从而推动量子控制工程学科的发展。

15208418.label: Realisation of objectives
15208418.value: All the three objectives have been realized. In the following we describe them in detail. In paper [4], we investigated the structure of quantum linear systems by analyzing their Kalman canonical form. We explored the spectral structure of quantum linear systems, revealing that a system is both controllable and observable if it is Hurwitz stable. We proposed a new parameterization method specifically designed for the Kalman canonical form. This parameterization represents the parameters in a blockwise form, corresponding to the blockwise structure of the Kalman canonical form. This parameter structure simplifies various quantum control design problems. For instance, we provided necessary and sufficient conditions for the realization of quantum back-action evading (BAE) measurements based on these new parameters. Due to their blockwise nature, only a few parameters are required to achieve quantum BAE measurements. In paper [5], we applied the linear systems theory to study the dynamics of a quantum coherent feedback network composed of two two-level systems (qubits) driven by counter-propagating photons in each input channel. The coherent feedback network enhances the nonlinear photon-photon interaction within the feedback loop. Using quantum stochastic calculus and the input-output framework, we derived the analytical form of the steady-state output two-photon state. Based on this analytical form, we demonstrated applications of the coherent feedback structure in the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometer and marginally stable single-photon devices. In paper [7], we addressed the problem of an input-output model of a two-level quantum system in the Heisenberg picture, which takes a bilinear form with constant system matrices. This form allows us to introduce the concepts of controllability and observability, analogous to those in quantum linear systems. By utilizing these notions, we constructed explicit coordinate transformations, represented by rotation matrices, that convert an input-output model into a new one. The new input-output model enables the investigation of various interesting properties of the two-level quantum system, such as steady-state solutions to the Lindblad master equation, quantum decoherence-free (DF) subspaces, quantum non-demolition (QND) variables, and the realization of quantum back-action evading (BAE) measurements. We re-examined the physical system in Wang and Wiseman (2001) to illustrate the presented results. In [12], we conducted a comprehensive study of the Tavis-Cummings model from a system-theoretic perspective using linear systems theory. The Tavis-Cummings model typically consists of a collection of noninteracting two-level systems (TLSs) collectively coupled to a common cavity resonator. We proposed an associated quantum linear passive system, whose canonical form exhibits typical features of the Tavis-Cummings model, including Sqrt{N}-scaling, dark states, bright states, single-excitation superradiant and subradiant states. The passivity of this linear system is related to the vacuum Rabi mode splitting phenomenon in Tavis-Cummings systems. Based on the linear model, we presented an analytical form for the steady-state output state of the Tavis-Cummings model driven by a single-photon state. We utilized master equations to study the excitation properties of the Tavis-Cummings model in scenarios with multiple excitations. Additionally, we proposed a computational framework for calculating the state of the Tavis-Cummings model, applicable to cases with multiple excitations, based on the transition matrix for a linear time-varying system. In paper [16], we proposed and analyzed a scheme for generating large-size Schrödinger cat states through linear operations involving Fock states, squeezed vacuum states, and conditional measurements. By performing conditional measurements using photon number detectors, we amplified two unbalanced small-amplitude Schrödinger kitten states combined by a beam splitter into a large-size cat state with the same parity. Simulation results demonstrated the amplification of two Schrödinger odd kitten states with amplitudes of |β|=1.06 and |β|=1.11, generated from one-photon-subtracted 3 dB squeezed vacuum states, to an odd cat state of |β|=1.73 with a fidelity of 99%. Furthermore, we predicted the generation of a large-size Schrödinger odd cat state with |β|=2.51 and fidelity of 97.30% using 5.91 dB squeezed vacuum states. We also analyzed the impact of experimental imperfections and concluded that Schrödinger odd cat states with |β|>2 are feasible. We proposed a feasible configuration based on a quantum frequency comb to realize the large-size cat state generation scheme.

15208418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208418.value: The proposal aims to investigate the structure and potential applications of quantum linear systems, which are fundamental in the development of quantum technologies such as quantum computing, cryptography, metrology, and sensing. Quantum linear systems are considered essential for their simplicity and approximation capabilities in quantum optics and networks. The research project focuses on three main topics: understanding the structure of quantum linear systems, developing a new parameterization method for these systems, and exploring their application in quantum information science. The project's long-term impact lies in advancing quantum device engineering and contributing to the rapidly evolving field of quantum control engineering. By uncovering the structure of quantum linear systems and their mathematical properties, researchers aim to provide powerful tools for the design and realization of decoherence-free systems (DFSs), quantum nondemolition (QND) variables, and back-action evasion (BAE) measurements. These advancements will facilitate the development of quantum technologies and pave the way for future technological innovations.

15208518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208518.value: Hong Kong (HK) is a crowded city which heavily relies on highways for moving people and goods. HK recently updated its highway pavement design guide with an objective that load-carrying asphalt pavement layers last at least 40 years, so that traffic disruptions caused by road reconstruction activities can be minimized. Investigations on existing highway pavements in HK, however, revealed that the oxidative aging of asphalt binders in asphalt pavements is one of the main concerns for their long-term durability. Motivated by the findings, this study proposes to: 1) analyze oxygen transport in compacted asphalt mixtures, 2) examine factors that affect asphalt binder aging in the mixtures, 3) monitor aging-related environmental factors inside field pavements, and 4) develop an integrated procedure for predicting field asphalt pavement aging. Although asphalt binder aging has been extensively studied, it remains unclear how asphalt mixture designs interact with environmental factors to affect field asphalt pavement aging. Recently, the mechanisms of asphalt mixture aging and prediction of pavement aging based on such mechanisms have aroused much interest. The proposed study, however, differs from existing ones in the basic methodologies to be used for investigation. In the proposed research, a newly developed method will be used to measure and calculate the oxygen diffusion coefficients of compacted asphalt mixtures prepared with different design formulas. The coefficients will be used as one of the key parameters to predict binder aging in asphalt mixtures and will be used to model oxygen flows in field pavements. Full-scale pavement sections will be built and monitored to gain insights on aging-related environmental factors inside pavements, including oxygen content, moisture content, and temperature. Asphalt mixture aging models and data gained from field pavement monitoring will be synthesized to develop an integrated procedure for predicting pavement aging. The procedure will be validated by aging data, with possible calibration to enhance the accuracy and robustness of the prediction procedure. It is anticipated that this “new angle” of studying asphalt mixture aging will generate the following outcomes: 1) models for the estimation of the oxygen diffusion coefficients of asphalt mixtures, 2) models for the prediction of asphalt binder aging in asphalt mixtures, 3) models and data for the estimation of the aging-related environmental factors inside pavements, and 4) an integrated procedure for predicting field pavement aging. The outcomes are anticipated to help develop more aging-resistant asphalt mixture designs and improve pavement structural design and maintenance strategies. 香港是一座繁忙的城市。 她緊密依賴四通八達的公路系統來運輸人員和貨物。 為了降低公路建設對交通的影響,香港近年來更新了瀝青公路設計規範,其目標是道路承載層的壽命可以達到40年以上。 通過對已有道路的研究發現,瀝青道路的氧化老化是瀝青公路長期耐久性的主要因素之一。 基於這項發現,本課題將集中研究瀝青道路的氧化老化問題,它包括以下主要內容:1)分析氧氣在壓實的瀝青混合料內的傳導機理,2)確定影響瀝青老化的主要因素,3)觀察、研究環境因素對瀝青老化的影響, 4) 發展一套基於機理的瀝青道路老化預測方法。 現有的研究主要集中在瀝青本身的老化,而忽略瀝青在混合料內的老化機理。 儘管近年來國外對瀝青混合料的老化問題有所涉獵,但是,本研究與已有的研究有很大的區別。 在本研究中,我們將使用一種新的方法來測量和計算氧氣在壓實的瀝青混合料裡的擴散係數。 此係數是預測瀝青老化的關鍵指標。 它將被用來預測瀝青混合料的老化和類比氧氣在瀝青道路內部的流動。 本研究將建造一處足尺的瀝青道路,埋設感應器,分析影響瀝青老化的環境因素,如氧氣濃度,濕度,溫度等。 混合料老化模型和實測的資料將被共同用來預測瀝青混合料的老化。 關於瀝青混合料的研究預期取得如下成果: 1)預測瀝青混合料氧氣擴散係數的模型;2)預測瀝青混合料氧化耐久性的模型; 3)影響老化的環境因素的模型和資料;4)預測瀝青道路老化的綜合模型。 這些成果可以説明發現更耐久、更抗老化的瀝青混合料。 此外,這些成果也可以説明改善道路設計和養護的方法。

15208518.label: Realisation of objectives
15208518.value: The principal investigator would like to thank the RGC panel members for providing us the opportunity to implement this project. This research focuses on the fundamental mechanism of asphalt binder aging in a porous medium—asphalt mixtures. Some very important research findings have been made from this study. With supports from RGC and other stakeholders such as Hong Kong Highways Department, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the paving industry in Hong Kong, the project has been satisfactorily completed. All the original proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. Fundamental and significant findings have been made based on this project. The realisation of objectives is explained as follows. Objective one: Measure and model the oxygen diffusion coefficients of dry and moist compacted asphalt mixtures; For the first time, our research group have developed methods to measure and model the oxygen diffusion coefficients of dry and moist compacted asphalt mixtures. Traditionally, asphalt pavement mix design is focused on the mechanical properties and volumetric properties of the asphalt mixtures. While the mechanical properties and volumetric properties prescribe the asphalt mixture performance immediately after construction, they do not determine the long-term performance of asphalt mixtures. This is because asphalt binder as an organic material is subject to severe oxidative aging in the usage conditions. Using our method, the material property evolution in a long term can be predicted. Objective two: Measure and model the oxidative aging susceptibility of dry and moist compacted asphalt mixtures; We have measured and modeled the oxidative aging susceptibility of dry and moist compacted asphalt mixtures. We found that the oxidative aging susceptibility of asphalt mixtures can be well predicted by oxygen diffusion coefficients of the asphalt mixtures. The findings are published in a very selective conference series—The Association of Asphalt Paving Technologists 2022. The paper was also selected for special promotion by Transportation Research Board of US. The research was deemed by TRB to be able to fundamentally affect asphalt mixture design practice. Objective three: Construct testing asphalt pavement sections and monitor oxygen, moisture, and temperature variations inside the pavements; We built full-scale asphalt pavement sections, designed the entire monitoring system with oxygen, moisture, and temperature sensors. Such information enables us to fully understand the in-service environment of asphalt pavements. Objective four: Develop an integrated procedure for predicting asphalt pavement aging with calibrations and validations. We developed integrated procedure for predicting asphalt pavement aging and other property changes. The aging and property changes are calibrated and validated through a large database—The long-term pavement performance program (LTPP). With partial contribution from this study, we have prepared a paper (Truck platooning reshapes GHG emissions of the integrated vehicle-road infrastructure system) for “Nature: Communications.” The paper has completed the first round of the review and the reviewers favorably commented on the paper. Overall, the research objectives are realised through well-planned experiments, theoretical and methodological developments. The research findings from the experiments are reported in several papers that are well recognized.

15208518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208518.value: The oxidative aging of asphalt binder affects the long-term performance of asphalt pavement. Aside from the intrinsic property of asphalt binder, binder aging in an asphalt mixture is affected by the mixture’s oxygen transport efficiency. In this study, the mixture’s oxygen transport efficiency is characterized by the oxygen diffusion coefficient (Ds). We found that asphalt mixtures’ long-term integrity is highly affected by the oxygen diffusion coefficient. In addition, we developed accelerated aging methods to age asphalt mixtures. Some of the major findings are summarized as follows. (1) The Ds values of asphalt mixtures are influenced by mixtures’ volumetric characteristics including gradation, air void content, and the nominal maximum aggregate size. It is a comprehensive indicator of the oxygen transportation efficiency of compacted asphalt mixtures. (2) The majority of the asphalt mixture samples subjected to aging treatment demonstrate a similar pattern of the aging gradient along the depth profile. Asphalt binders in the top and bottom surface layers of the mixture samples are more severely aged than those in the middle layers. (3) For each mixture type, the aging gradients of asphalt binders in the mixture samples are closely related to AV contents. Such a relationship, however, is specific to mixture type. On the other hand, the Ds values are closely and universally related to the aging gradients of all asphalt mixture types. (4) The aging extent of asphalt binder in the inner portion of an asphalt mixture is closely related to the Ds value of the mixture. (5) In view of the close relationships between Ds and aging gradient and between Ds and aging severity of asphalt mixtures, the Ds value of an asphalt mixture may serve as a useful surrogate to assess the aging susceptibility of the asphalt mixture. The determination of Ds does not demand expensive equipment and complicated test procedure. Therefore, it can serve as a promising parameter in designing more aging-resistant mixtures, modeling and predicting field pavement aging. (6) Ds is a very useful indicator to quantitatively represent the oxygen retarding capacity of the preventive maintenance methods. (7) The oxygen retarding capacity of preventive maintenance methods significantly affects the aging susceptibility of asphalt mixtures. (8) Most physicochemical properties of the naturally aged binders exhibited two stages. The properties changed more rapidly at the first stage than at the second stage. At the second stage, commonly used properties can be well predicted through linear models. (9) The long-term aging trends of asphalt binders in a more natural condition may be well predicted by using a proposed linear model based on data collected in a short period after binder’s “spurt” reaction stage. This research has led to the following major research outcomes: (1) A new piece of equipment (initially developed by our research group) is further improved for accurately and reliably testing the oxygen diffusion coefficient of asphalt mixtures. (2) A new method was developed to evaluate the long-term durability of asphalt mixtures against oxidative aging. (3) The new method can be used for optimizing asphalt mixture design as well as pavement maintenance design. (4) A new procedure was developed to predict the long-term aging of asphalt binder in more naturally aging conditions.

15208518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208518.value: This study, for the first time, clearly reveals the mix-design factors that affect asphalt binder aging in asphalt mixtures. As shown in our published paper, for both new asphalt mixture design and maintenance design, the relationships between oxygen diffusion coefficients and aging-susceptibility of asphalt mixtures are very strong (R-square>90%). This indicates that our method and models well capture the aging phenomenon of asphalt binders in asphalt mixtures. Such findings have significantly implications in pavement design and maintenance. In addition, our new methods can well predict the long-term aging of asphalt binder. We have communicated our findings with local highway agencies and international peers. The research was also selected by TRB for promotion. In the future, we will try to promote the new methods to be adopted for mixture design standards and specifications as well as quality acceptance test.

15208518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208518.value: Asphalt pavement is an important group of transport assets. Driven by traffic loading and aging-induced material deterioration, roads made of asphalt pavements are in bad conditions in many places around the world. Severely degraded pavements are often demolished and sometimes recycled. On the other hand, if we can design an asphalt mixture that is very resistant to aging, or use effective preventive maintenance methods to conserve the asphalt pavement, the performance life of road pavements can be significantly increased. This would result in significant savings on costs, energy, resources and help mitigate negative environmental impacts. In this research, we found the key parameter that affects asphalt aging. This parameter is called the oxygen diffusion coeffect. This parameter is essentially determined by the interconnected voids in asphalt mixtures. It is well related to aging of asphalt mixtures—newly paved and maintained. This parameter can be used for new mix design, pavement maintenance design, and quality control and quality assurance practices of road pavements.

15208718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208718.value: Fibre-optics sensors based on fibre Bragg gratings (FBGs) are extremely versatile and are used in a multitude of industries ranging from structural health monitoring of civil structures to medical devices such as in-vivo sensors and patient monitoring wearable smart fabrics. FBGs are being used as MRI-compatible sensors in catheterization procedures or integrated in surgical tools to provide 3-degree of freedom force sensing capability for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery. FBG arrays embedded in smart fabrics were used for respiratory monitoring, and prevention of sudden infant death syndrome. Fibre Bragg gratings are usually fabricated in optical fibres made of silica glass. Silica is fragile, has high stiffness, and produces shards when breaks. These properties render fabrics embedded with glass FBG sensors difficult to handle. Polymer optical fibre (POF) is a good alternative and POF sensors are generally accepted as a promising sensing technology for the biomedical industry because POFs are biocompatible, flexible, shatter resistant, has smaller stiffness, and inexpensive to produce. Single-mode optical fibres with high photosensitivity are needed for FBG inscriptions. However, photosensitive single-mode POF suitable for FBG fabrication is not readily available. This is because of dopant diffusion during the POF fabrication process, making it difficult to control the refractive-index profile of single-mode POFs. Furthermore, writing FBGs in POFs can take extremely long UV exposure time – could be more than 60 minutes. In comparison, FBGs are routinely written in standard single-mode silica glass optical fibres in tens of seconds. Low-cost FBGs in silica optical fibres has opened up a wide range of applications. The availability of low-cost polymer FBGs could open up many new applications. They could also provide significant improvement in existing applications. This is made possible by the recent discovery of a dopant by the PI, permitting rapid fabrication of FBGs in POFs several orders of magnitude faster that previously reported results. This proposal concerns the development of single-mode polymer optical fibres, and systematic investigation of different dopants and polymers in single-mode POFs, with the ultimate objective to develop low-cost photosensitive single-mode POFs that allow rapid FBG inscription during the fibre drawing process. The three key issues to be addressed in this proposed project are to: (1) design and fabricate single-mode photosensitive polymer optical fibres with lower loss; (2) investigate the properties of the rapidly inscribed FBGs in these POFs and characterize their long-term stability; and (3) investigate potential materials to reduce cross-sensitivity of different sensing measurands. 基于光纤光栅（FBG）的光纤传感器用途广泛，已经用于从土木结构的健康监测到医疗设备，诸如体内传感器和用于患者监测的可穿戴智能纺织物等 。光纤光栅也被用作导管插入过程中兼容MRI的传感器或集成在外科手术器械中，为机器人辅助微创手术提供三个自由度的力感知能力。另外，嵌入在智能纺织物的光纤光栅阵列也已经用于呼吸监测，以及预防婴儿猝死综合症。 该提议包括单模聚合物光纤的制备，以及对单模聚合物光纤中不同掺杂材料和聚合物的系统性研究，最终目标是开发低成本的光敏单模聚合物光纤，并实现在光纤拉丝过程中在线刻写光纤光栅。

15208718.label: Realisation of objectives
15208718.value: All the objectives were completed successfully. New materials were discovered for the fabrication of new types of optical fibers suitable for medical applications, opening up new opportunities to do exciting research related to smart cochlear implants, human vital-sign monitoring, and also in battery monitoring. It is worth noting that the early encouraging results of this project provided the support to a later successful GRF project which is funding the collaborative project with Melbourne University and the Royal Victoria Eye & Ear Hospital in Melbourne. A US patent on the smart cochlear implant integrated with polymer optical fiber sensors was granted in February 2023. Objective 1: New polymer optical fiber fabrication facility An entirely new facility for fabrication of high-quality polymer optical fibre suitable for FBG sensors inscription was developed. This includes the construction of a new fiber drawing tower, and a new processing technique in the fabrication of polymer preforms for the fabrication of multicore as well as polymeric micro-structured optical fibers. The fiber drawing tower was equipped with all the necessary monitoring sensors and feedback control for the fabrication of high-quality polymer optical fibers. The performance of the fiber drawing tower is very good and is now being developed into a commercial product for other universities. Objective 2: Investigate the optimal condition to rapidly inscribe FBGs in these POFs. Several kinds of polymeric optical fibers were developed based on two different materials systems: (1) PMMA doped with photosensitive materials to enhance FBG sensors fabrication, and (2) Cyclo Olefin polymer (COP) optical fibers, using ZEONEX pellets produced by ZEON Ltd, without any dopant and therefore lower transmission. Although the PMMA based optical fiber is quite efficient for FBG-inscription and strong FBGs can be inscribed in the fiber in just 7 msec using 325-nm He-Cd laser, but its loss at the 1550-nm transmission window is very high. Single and multicore ZEONEX polymer optical fibers were fabricated and FBG sensors can be inscribed in them with one 20-ns pulse of 248-nm excimer laser or in several seconds using femto-second laser. We have successful tailored the FBG inscription conditions to rapidly write FBG sensors in all our fabricated polymer optical fibers. Objective 3: Growth evolution of FBG and the behavior, including long-term stability, of gratings inscribed in the various POFs. We demonstrated for the first-time fabrication of FBGs in all ZEONEX (COP)-based SMPOFs with a single 25 ns pulse of 248 nm UV irradiation and studied their temperature and tensile behaviour over a 12-month period. The FBG sensors exhibited good long-term stability, and this opens up new frontiers in optics and photonics for the effective fabrication of polymer optical fiber Bragg gratings (POFBGs), permitting mass producibility of them. POFBGs were characterized by subjecting them to various physical parameters including temperature and tensile strain. Strain responses of FBGs with similar grating strengths fabricated with 248 nm and 325 nm He-Cd laser irradiations were explored over a year to demonstrate their long-term stability and applicability. PMMA doped with photosensitive fibers were irradiated with high fluence of 325 nm and 248 nm lasers and the fibers properties are investigated using dynamic mechanical analysis and tensile strain for potential use of these fibers past the yield point. It is demonstrated that the UV sources shifted the ultimate tensile strength and changed the strain hardening behavior. Tensile strain measurements show excellent repeatability for gratings inscribed with these two sources with similar sensitivity of 1.305 nm/µstrain for FBG inscribe with 325 nm laser, and 1.345 nm/ µstrain for grating written with 248 nm laser in the range 0 to 1.5% elongation. Furthermore, tests far beyond the yield point (up to 2.8% elongation) show that grating inscribed with lower UV wavelength exhibit hysteresis. We demonstrated that 248 nm laser fluence shall be chosen carefully whereas even high 325 nm laser fluence do not critically impact the sensor properties. Objective 4: Fabrication and characterize of POFs' performance in terms of cross-sensitivity of measurands. We discovered and fabricated highly photosensitivity DPDS-doped PMMA optical fibers that strong FBG sensors can be inscribed in the fibers in less than 7 msec with low-irradiation intensity 325-nm He-Cd laser. However, the transmission loss of the doped fiber is very high at the 1550-nm window which limited their usable fiber length to just a few cm. The discovery of the use of two different grades of Cyclo Olefin Polymer (COP) to fabricate single-mode polymer optical fibers which FBG sensors can be inscribed in the fibers with just a single 20-ns 248-nm UV laser pulse without degrading the COP fibers open up many new opportunities in medical applications. Attenuation of the COP optical fibers at the 1550-nm window is significantly lower, and the workable fiber length is extended to over 20 cm. It is important to note that with the availability of 850-nm FBG-integrators, the COP optical fiber’s workable length can be up to 3-m which is adequate for most medical applications. The long-term stability of the COP optical fibers in strain and temperature measurements, as well as capability to operate in temperature as high as 120°C were investigated, demonstrating their superior performance in comparison to PMMA. Objective 5: Conduct experiments on health monitoring using polymer FBGs. The unique features of the wearable pulse-wave measurement device fabricated by embedding polymer optical fibre Bragg gratings (POFBGs) in silicone rubber resulted in much better performance in the detection of human heart rate compared to that of silica single mode fiber (SMF). The response of the sensing device during a human respiration process was also explored where exhalation and inhalation were monitored and distinguished. These revelations signify the importance of ZEONEX (COP)-based POFBGs, which allow consistent and effective grating fabrication and are highly promising in the foreseeable future for biomedical applications. The Pulse wave signals of human subjects were measured by POF-FBG and silica-FBG sensors. After signal processing, a calibration curve was constructed by partial least squares regression, then blood pressure was calculated from the calibration curve. The POFBG sensor could measure the pulse wave signals with a signal to noise ratio at least eight times higher than that with the silica-FBG sensor. Further, the measured signals were substantially similar to those of an acceleration plethysmograph. The collaborative research activities with Shinshu University of Japan in the use of our fabricated polymer optical fibers with inscribed FBG sensors resulted in two joint publications. Objective 6: Investigate the suitability of FBG sensors for real time monitoring of the dynamic internal state of battery cells. This new objective was added to the project after we were approached by Prof. Tarascon of College de France who was interested to use our optical fibers, including micro-structured optical fibers and FBG sensors inscribed in polymer optical fibers for battery monitoring purposes. Jean-Marie Tarascon FRSC is Professor of Chemistry at the Collège de France in Paris and Director of the French Research Network on Electrochemical Energy Storage. He is a globally renowned researcher in the area of energy storage and was awarded the most prestigious CNRS GOLD Medal in 2022. This led to a long-term collaboration and new discoveries by monitoring the chemical and thermal activities inside cell batteries using FBG sensors with enhanced sensitivity, enabled by the novel optical fibers. Some of the collaborative work was published in Nature Energy, the highest ranked journal in the area with an impact factor of 60.8.

15208718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208718.value: List of Major finding and research outcome 1. The discovery of using two different grades of Cyclo Olefin Polymer (COP) to fabricate polymer optical fibers for rapid FBG sensor inscription [Cheng, 2020] opens many opportunities to establish multi-disciplinary research collaborations in medical as well as renewable such as battery monitoring. 2. The use of COP for the core as well as the cladding permits easy fabrication of the COP optical fibers due to similar glass transition temperature which makes the fiber drawing process easier. It is important to note that COP exhibit very low water affinity and can operate at much higher temperature as compared to PMMA-based polymer optical fibers. These attributes are critical in many practical applications. 3. Polymer starts to degrade when exposed to UV light below the wavelength of 300 nm. FBG sensors can be inscribed in the COP optical fibers using just one 20-ns pulse of 248-nm laser irradiation [Cheng, 2020]. It was found that exposure of the fibers to 248-nm irradiation during the FBG fabrication process did not affect the long-term reliability of the FBG sensors [Boneficino, 2020]. 4. Developed rectangular cladding with single- or multi-cores COP optical fibers provide a flat surface for ultra-short 1-2 mm FBG sensors using femto-second laser. The novel fiber design eliminated the use of index-matching oil and permits strong gratings to be written more rapidly [Dash, 2020]. 5. The application of COP optical fibers in pulse-wave monitoring to derive all the essential human vital-signs open the opportunity to integrate polymer optical fiber Bragg grating sensors in wearable devices as polymer unlike glass is not easy to break and much more sensitive. We demonstrated that the signal-to-noise ratio is eight times better using polymer fiber Bragg grating sensors than with that using glass optical fibers [Haseda, 2019 and Koyama, 2021] 6. Use of COP optical fibers in smart cochlear implants offers a potential solution to improve the surgical procedure of cochlear implantation as the embedded polymer optical fibre sensors provide real-time contact force to surgeons which could help to reduce trauma in patients. The finding of this project led to collaboration with Melbourne University and the Victoria Eye and Ear Hospital and the award of a joint US patent in February 2023. 7. The finding of this project helped to establish a collaboration with College de France in batter monitoring and the research outcome was published in Nature Energy which has impact factor of 60.8 [Huang, 2020]

15208718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208718.value: Medical grade polymer materials for making single-mode optical fibers were discovered for the fabrication of high-quality polymer optical fiber Bragg grating sensors. Strong FBG sensors can be rapidly inscribed in the novel polymer optical fibers using one 20-ns pulses of a 248-nm excimer laser. Ultra-short strong and stable FBG sensors of 1-2 mm can also be fabricated in the novel fibers using femto-second lasers. The materials have very low water-affinity and are suitable for medical applications as well as for battery monitoring. The novel polymer optical fibers open up opportunities for several new research topics, including: 1) the use of the fiber sensors in smart cochlear implants, 2) attach to bone and implantable metal fixtures and screws to monitor bone healing process; and 3) monitoring the chemical and thermal events in batteries.

15208718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208718.value: Optical fiber sensors fabricated with medical grade Cyclo Olefin Polymer (COP) materials were developed to measure pulse waves on the wrist or fingertips to derive the essential human vital signs such as pulse rate, respiration rate, blood pressure, stress, etc. The polymeric optical fiber sensors offer eight times better performance than sensors fabricated in standard fused silica fibers. The non-brittle nature of polymer offers a practical solution for the development of wearable device to provide continue real-time monitoring of the vital signs of elderly. Fiber sensors fabricated in COP optical fibers were also successfully embedded in cochlear implants to measure the contact force between the implants and walls of cochlea to provide vital information to help surgeons to reduce trauma during surgical operation. In addition, the ultra-low water affinity of COP and its ability to operate in high temperature made them an ideal candidate to monitor the dynamic chemical and thermal state of batteries during operation which offer a scalable solution to design battery thermal management systems with enhanced safety.

15209318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209318.value: 光电探测技术是将光信号转换为电信号的关键技术。它对于社会有很大的影响力，甚至能够实现以及提升诸多关键技术，例如通讯，成像，远距离传感，安全等。最近，基于二维材料的光电探测技术在全球范围内广泛研究，因为二维材料在一代微纳光子器件中提供了新的研究前景。因此，在顶尖杂志中不断有诸多的研究报道。本研究组有着良好的制作加工条件和研究修改二维材料的光学性质以适用于不同的光子器件和光电探测器。 在这个研究计划中， 我们将会制备并研究Group-10 过渡金属硫化物二维材料，例如PdSe2 以及氧化物二维材料，例如TiO2. PdSe2具有较宽的光吸收，高载流子迁移率，可调的带隙，以及在光电探测器上的潜在应用。另一方面，是一种廉价普遍，在紫外（265 nm）具有很强的吸收，化学稳定且无毒的二维氧化物材料。这两种结构可以构成很多异质结结构，以产生高性能的可以在多个不同波段工作的自驱动紫外光电探测器。 本项目将会采用多种方法研究上述二维材料的生长机制，例如脉冲激光沉积、磁控溅射和Langmuir Blodgett薄膜提拉技术。这些技术耗费合理，可以大面积成规模的在商业产品中应用。本研究将会开辟上述二维材料新的制作工艺以及将其应用于光电探测上。更重要的是，从本研究中获得的知识与经验将会有助于材料科学家和工程师来制作和设计各种新颖的二维材料来应用于具有优异性能的光电探测器。 根据本研究组的良好记录，这个项目在风险和结果之间取得了正确的平衡，将会发表一系列高水平文章以及潜在的专利。具有专业素养的研究员将会促进香港的经济和科技发展，并填补该领域的空白。

15209318.label: Realisation of objectives
15209318.value: Publication summary: It is my third GRF since I came back Hong Kong in 2009. I have used the money very carefully. This project has been carrying out successfully and producing many high-quality publications 32 SCI journal in total. All objectives are achieved. Some of these publications even rated top 1% ESI highly cited paper. This grant helps me a lot in securing the top 2% of the world's most-cited scientists in the field of optoelectronics and photonics (upto 2019). Most of the works are done mainly by my PhD students and RA, which positioned as first author in the publication. These publications, demonstrating the research output, including 1 × IF, Impact Factor = 30 Advanced Materials, “cover”, 12 × (IF > 10), e.g., Advanced Functional Materials, ACS Nano, Advanced Science, Nano Energy, Small Methods, Nano Micro-Letters, Chemical Engineering Journal, Applied Materials Today, 14 × (IF > 5), ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, Nano Research, Journal of Materials Chemistry C, Advanced Optical Materials, Solar RRL, Solar Energy, Advanced Materials Interface, Advanced Sustainable Systems, 5 × (IF >2) e.g., RSC Advances, Nanomaterials, Nanotechnology, Optics and Laser Technology, Thin Solid Films, etc. Research activities in relation to the project objectives that were carried out during this reporting period We have tried various fabrication technique, e.g., sputtering, Langmuir-Blodgett film deposition methods for fabricating various 2D materials-based photodetectors. This research focus on exploring the novel 2D material’s optoelectronic properties and used for broadband photodetection. The long-term stability is tested and reported for various 2D materials based broadband photodetectors. In correspondence to that, we have successfully optimized and characterized the performance of the fabricated photodetector. PdSe2 with distinct optical and tunable electrical properties have exhibited great potential for various optoelectronic applications. Some PdSe2 samples have been successfully prepared and fabricated with GaAs substrates for broadband photodetection. However, the photodetection performance is not very good. Therefore, a self-powered photodetector is developed with broadband response ranging from deep ultraviolet to near-infrared by combining FA1−xCsxPbI3 perovskite with PdSe2 layer. The as-assembled PdSe2/perovskite Schottky junction is sensitive to light illumination ranging from 200 to 1550 nm. Our research finding related to this PdSe2/perovskite Schottky junction photodetector was published in Advanced Science and selected as ESI highly cited paper. [1] Owing to a puckered pentagonal structure of PdSe2, polarization-sensitive, high-speed, and broadband photodetector based on a graphene/PdSe2/germanium heterojunction are fabricated, and it exhibits a wide spectral response from 200 nm to 4.55 μm with an ultrahigh polarization sensitivity of 112.2.[2] What’s more, a large-size PdSe2/CdTe mixed-dimensional van der Waals (vdW) heterojunction for room-temperature infrared detection was demonstrated. [20] Furthermore, high-quality perovskite thin films and the wafer-scale other group-10 TMDs materials like PtTe2 have been used to fabricate high-quality photodetector as well [8] and [14]. 2D layered PtTe2/Si with graphene transparent electrode for high-performance, broadband, infrared photodetector. [14] The fabrication of ultrathin TiO2 film via a Langmuir-Blodgett film deposition approach is developed. Some TiO2 samples have been successfully prepared and fabricated for deep ultraviolet (DUV) photodetection. However, we did not find any UV response based on TiO2 films. Therefore, other attractive materials like PtSe2 with unique electrical and optical properties has been proposed for novel mix-dimensional heterojunction based on few-layer PtSe2 on prepatterned Ga2O3 substrate. In this project, we demonstrate the successful fabrication of two-/three-dimensional (2D/3D) graphene (Gr)/PtSe2/β-Ga2O3 Schottky junction devices for high-sensitivity solar-blind DUV photodetectors is demonstrated. Benefitting from the high-quality 2D/3D Schottky junction, the vertically stacked structure, and the superior-quality transparent graphene electrode for effective carrier collection, the photodetector is highly sensitive to DUV light illumination and achieves a high responsivity of 76.2 mA/W, a large on/off current ratio of ~105, along with an ultra-high UV/visible rejection ratio of 1.8×104. More importantly, it has an ultra-fast response time of 12 s and a remarkable speciﬁc detectivity of ~1013 Jones. Finally, an excellent DUV imaging capability has been identified based on the Gr/PtSe2/β-Ga2O3 Schottky junction photodetector, demonstrating its great potential application in DUV imaging systems.[19] This publication attract high level of citation after it is published and also awarded “Top Paper Award in 2021 by Nano Research and 10000 RMB cash to the team”. A novel approach for realizing an efficient color imaging detector will be studied. Conventional RGB sensor uses a set of color filter arrays (CFA) for extracting blue, green, and red color, leading to lower the efficiency to only 33%. In the CFA based color sensor, individual filter detects only one color at a time (blue or green or red); hence, almost 66% solar spectrum remains unused. We propose a vertically stacked color sensor design with perovskite alloys with distinct bandgaps, which is able to detect all three colors at a time. The blue color is detected by the top cell, green by middle cell, and finally, bottom cell absorptions red region lights. Consequently, as compared to the conventional parallel CFA based sensor, the proposed sensor or detector design could exhibit high efficiency. Additionally, we have also found that some of 2D layered materials exhibit favorable optical properties for laser applications. PdSe2 flakes and tin telluride quantum dots as nonlinear optical materials to generate Q-switch pulses [16][17]. Moreover, some novel 2D materials including PdS2, SnTe QDs, GaS, and PdTe2 were produced and investigated. [15] [23] [26] [27] We have found that there have broadband saturable absorption features and excellent optoelectronic properties for saturable absorbers applications. Finally, this project also partly supports some other works related to novel materials used for development of perovskite photovoltaic, [3][12][21][22][24][25], perovskite multispectral optical sensors [29], renewable energy generation [28] [30] [31], ultrahigh adsorption 2D materials for water pollutant removals [18], solar cells related development [5][6][7][9][10][11][13] and nonlinear optical activities of the novel 2D Gallium Sulfide [32]. 15209318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209318.value: We are the pioneer research group focusing on the growth of all kinds of group-10 2D materials for optoelectronic devices and systems. These novel 2D materials is featured with attractive optical and electrical properties, more importantly, it is very stable under air conditions. We have demonstrated the great potential of these novel materials for application in high-sensitivity broadband light detection. These obtained device parameters are very competitive, which can be compared with photodetectors based on other 2D materials, even are close to commercial photodiodes. Some of the journal publications resulted from this project rated as Top1% highly cited paper in the field.

15209318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209318.value: The 2D layered materials based optoelectronic devices are expected to bring some revolutionary changes into the field. Therefore, it attracts great attention globally and has significant importance in modern society from practical aspects including medical imaging, optical communication, sensors for safety monitoring, and display technology to fundamental science applications. Further research on properties of other new and unexplored 2D materials will continue to be a hot research area. Additionally, the growth of large-area group-10 TMDs materials through a simple vapor phase deposition process allows the minimization of device in the micro-scale, which is realized and studied.

15209318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209318.value: The project allows us to probe some novel materials including perovskite and graphene-like two-dimensional group-10 TMDs materials, e.g. PtSe2, PdSe2, and PtTe2. These materials with atomic thicknesses exhibit unique optical and optoelectronic properties like widely tunable bandgap, high air stability, and wide light absorption. Therefore, the optoelectronics devices based on these materials with high-performance could offer revolutionary changes in performance and function. By using these newly developed materials, we have first demonstrated some practical applications e.g., high performance broadband (ultraviolet to infrared) photo-detection and room-temperature image sensing. Additionally, the funding also supports some completed research works for solar thermal energy conversion for freshwater generation and solar cells development. This project opens new research directions and opportunities for these novel materials.

15209718.label: Project Objectives
15209718.value: To develop a reliable and efficient scanning approach for building of 3D geometric hand models. Particular attention will be given to the geometric features of the hand, skin deformation and finger web surface in relation to hand postures, thus providing a consistent amount of pressure on the scar-glove interface. To evaluate the dynamic stress-strain and recovery behavior of warp-knitted glove materials so as to incorporate the dynamic pressure attenuation of the fabric into the design of finite-element glove sub-model. The structural design of glove and reduction factor in pattern making, as well as the design and properties of pressure reinforcement materials will also be taken into consideration. To formulate a biomechanical model to simulate the amount of stress on the glove and the interface pressure distribution between the hand and the glove in relation to fabric type and tensile behaviour, geometric features of anatomic sites, change of hand postures, etc. To undertake laboratory wear trials that validate the analysis and simulation of the finite element models to facilitate the administration of pressure induced by pressure therapy gloves for effective scar reduction and optimal treatment efficacy.

To undertake laboratory wear trials that validate the analysis and simulation of the finite element models to facilitate the administration of pressure induced by pressure therapy gloves for effective scar reduction and optimal treatment efficacy.

15209718.label: Realisation of objectives
15209718.value: In this project, the 4 objectives stated in the project proposal have been fully achieved. In this study, the impact of postural variations on hand anthropometry and distribution of skin strain ratios has been investigated. Full-color three-dimensional scans of the hands are captured with thirty healthy subjects (20 females, 10 males) to analyze the hand measurements and skin deformation with various postures. The hand measurements are then statistically analyzed. Amongst the 57 hand dimensions studied, a total of 34 dimensions of the circumference, length, and surface area showed significant differences among the postures. More than 88% of the dimensions are significantly correlated to height, weight, and BMI, respectively. However, less than half of the angle measurements are significantly correlated to gender, height, weight, and BMI, respectively. A negative skin strain ratio means that the dimension has a higher value in the ball grip posture than the relaxed or splayed postures and vice versa. The skin strain ratios between the ball grip and the relaxed postures, and between the ball grip and the splayed postures ranged from -6.6% to 30.8% and from -12.2% to 65.5% respectively. As compared to the ball grip posture, the level of skin deformation obtained from the splayed hand posture is consistently higher than the relaxed posture, especially in the slants of web space and the length dimensions. Results also indicated that 85% of the female measurements and 87.5% of the male measurements have greater skin deformation when changed from gripping to the splayed posture when compared to the relaxed posture. The skin strain ratio of most palm-length dimensions is negative, while the skin strain ratio of most dorsal-length is positive. Conventional glove pattern designs which are based on hand dimensions with a splayed posture therefore limit the movement of gloved hands, particularly with a gripping posture. Consideration should be given to hand measurements in dynamic postures for optimal fit and comfort. This study also creates the possibility of computer automatic generation of a glove pattern with improved fit based on 3D hand images. The skin strain ratios can be used for comparison with the nominal plots of the stress-stretch ratio of different types of fabrics for gloves to examine the effect of the fabric properties, and further develop gloves with materials that cater to different occupations and professions. Hypertrophic scars (HS) are considered to be the greatest unmet challenge in wound and burn rehabilitation. The most common treatment for HS is pressure therapy but pressure garments may not be able to exert adequate pressure onto HS due to the complexities of the human body. In this study, the development of three-dimensional (3D) scanning and direct digital manufacturing (DDM) technologies has facilitated the customized placement of additively manufactured silicone gel onto fabric as a component of the pressure therapy garment. It provides a novel and customized fabrication approach to treat HS and discusses the mechanical properties of 3D printed fabric reinforced with a silicone composite. For further demonstration of the suggested HS therapy with customised silicone insert, silicone inserts for the finger webs and HS are additively manufactured onto the fabric. Through the pressure evaluation by Pliance X system, it is proved the silicone insert increases the pressure exertion to the HS. Moreover, the mechanical properties of the additively manufactured fabric silicone composites are characterized. The findings suggest that as compared with single viscosity print materials, the adhesive force of the additively manufactured silicone and fabric shows a remarkable improvement of 600% when print materials with different viscosities are applied onto elevated fabric. In consideration of the problem of fluctuated pressure exertion during the hand movement, a series of 3D printed auxetic thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) inserts were developed to substitute the conventional polyethylene inserts. Auxetic structures including re-entrant (RE) and double-arrowhead (DAH) were investigated regarding their shape formability, structural deformation and auextic response experimentally and numerically by finite element analysis (FEA). The result reveals DAH structure has superior shape formability verses that the re-entrant and conventional polyethylene (PE) foam insert. A wear trial was conducted to further evaluate the effect of a more formable insert on the pressure delivery. Based on the result of wear trial, the application of DAH insert is able to maintain a stable pressure level at the centre part of the insert, even during the wrist flexion and extension. In this study, a fabrication approach was developed to combine a small silicone insert and pressure garment together. Medical grade silicone is directly three-dimensional (3D) printed on the knitted fabric. The geometry of silicone insert is based on the 3D scanned HS data, so that the customized insert can be securely placed onto the HS, fitting the needs and pressure dosage required of individual patients. The silicone insert attached pressure garment also facilitates the use of scars treating gel into the HS therapy that combines pressure, silicone sheet and scars treating gel. A novel 3D multi-viscosity printing approach was developed for developing the silicone-fabric composite. By adopting the new approach that using a lower viscosity of print solution for the first layer of printing, the shearing strength between the silicone and fabric increased around 600% when comparing with the conventional 3D printing method. Apart from the application of HS therapy, the approach could be adopted by any type of 3D printed fabric reinforced composite development. To further evaluate the feasibility of the proposed pressure garment with silicone insert attachment, a wear trial has been conducted. A patient with HS on the right wrist was invited for the wear trial. Finite element models (FEM) have been developed to investigate the parameter of garment size and thickness of insert to the pressure delivery for the patient. Throughout the FEA, the parameters with optimal performance that provides suitable amount of pressure to the HS with minimal pressure exertion to the healthy skin was determined. The pressure garment was produced based on the best parameters and provided to the patient. After one year of wear, it can be observed that the HS has shown a significant reduction in thickness and pigmentation without creating any negative effect. The consolidated design framework of the proposed HS therapy demonstrates the application of various novel technologies into HS therapy and provides a new insight to advance the design of customised products.

15209718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209718.value: This study starts with an investigation on impact of postural variation on hand measurement. In this part, various measurements of hand during 3 different postures are systematically evaluated. Results show that 40 out of 57 measurements of hand have statistically difference regarding to hand postures. The findings of this study provide valuable guidelines to enhance the anatomically engineered design for the pattern of pressure gloves which relates to the practical function of hand. Considering the problem of fluctuated pressure exertion during the hand movement, a series of 3D printed auxetic thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) inserts were developed to substitute the conventional PE inserts. Two widely discussed auxetic structures including re-entrant (RE) and double-arrowhead (DAH) were investigated regarding their shape formability, structural deformation and auextic response experimentally and numerically by finite element analysis (FEA). The result reveals DAH structure has superior shape formability verses that the RE and PE foam insert. Based on the result of wear trial, the application of DAH insert is able to maintain a stable pressure level at the centre part of the insert, even during the wrist flexion and extension. In consideration of HS in small dimensions and/or specific body regions, a new fabrication approach that combines a silicone insert and pressure garment has been developed. A medical grade silicone is directly three-dimensional (3D) printed on the knitted fabric. The geometry of silicone insert is based on the 3D scanned HS data. The silicone insert attached pressure garment also facilitates the use of scars treating gel into the HS therapy that combines pressure, silicone sheet and scars treating gel. To increase the feasibility of the suggested therapy, a novel 3D multi-viscosity printing approach was developed for developing the silicone-fabric composite. Apart from HS therapy, the proposed method can also be adopted at various types of 3D printed fabric reinforced composite development for customized clinical and healthcare products. To further evaluate the feasibility of the proposed pressure garment with silicone insert attachment, a wear trial has been conducted. Finite element models (FEMs) have been developed to investigate the parameter of garment size and thickness of insert to the pressure delivery for the patient. Satisfactory results were observed between the simulated and experimental data. The consolidated design framework of the proposed HS therapy demonstrates the application of various novel technologies into HS therapy and provides a new insight to advance the design of customised products.

15209718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209718.value: To further study regarding the treatment for HS, various perspectives can be investigated to facilitate a better treatment. To optimise the auxetic insert, different type of auxetic structure can be analysed its shape formability and mathematical model related to the out-of-plane blending. Various materials such as silicone and hydrogen can be applied as insert materials and evaluated their mechanical properties which can directly affects the contact pressure received by HS. On the other hand, micro-capsulation of therapeutic material for HS can be explored and added in the 3D printed material which directly contacts with the HS. As a result, different type of research proved therapy might be able to be combined together. Wear trials or animal test can also be carried out to evaluate the effect of auxetic insert to the recovery of HS. When considering the suggested hybrid therapy, the effects of various type of scar treating gel can be further evaluated through a randomised controlled trial. Thus, the best combination of treatment can be determined.

15209718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209718.value: Hypertrophic Scar (HS) is one of the most critical problems in the wound healing process and burn rehabilitation. The patient usually suffer the problem of scarring which limiting the range of motion and affect their self-esteem. Because of the distant hard, raised and dark red appearance of HS, the patients usually encounter the psychological problem, especially the female patient. To improve the quality of life of HS patients, this study aims to improve the pressure therapy which is the most common treatment to prevent the grow of HS and speed up the maturation of HS. In this study, the finding on the geometric features of hand, skin deformation and finger surface in relation to hand postures provides a scientific basis for further pressure therapy glove engineering that provides a better fit, performance and comfort of gloves. In order to distribute the pressure to the ideal position, while ensure the stable pressure level during various motions of hand, the state-of-the-art technologies that integrating 3D scanning, 3D printing and FEA were analysed. Customised pressure inserts were designed and developed, providing a new insight for optimal fit and control of hand-glove interfacial pressures in treatment of HS.
