15209818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209818.value: Walking does not only alleviate the problems of traffic congestion and emission, but also improve the well-being of citizen. Walkability has been increasingly promoted. This is particularly true for Hong Kong, where 90% of daily commuter trips are made by public transport and almost all of the public transport trips rely on walking as the primary access. Safety is one of the important attributes to walkability. Pedestrian safety has been a concern in Hong Kong. In 2016, of the 20,132 people who were injured in the road crashes, 17% were pedestrian. In contrast, of those who were killed and seriously injured on roads, 64% and 30% were pedestrian respectively. The problem was particularly significant at the signalized intersections in the urban area, where the population density, activity level, and frequency of vehicle-pedestrian conflict were high. There is a need to develop a comprehensive safety management framework, to improve the design of road facilities and traffic control measures, considering the pedestrian crash and injury characteristics. To estimate the pedestrian crash risk, it is necessary to have robust exposure measure, accurately quantifying the potential to collision between pedestrian and motor vehicle. For the macro-level (zonal and regional) safety analysis, aggregated exposure based on the population socio-demographics, land use pattern and traffic composition; and disaggregated exposure based on the individual walking path choice were estimated. For the micro-level analysis (individual intersection and crosswalk), exposure based on the volume, density and speed, for either pedestrian or vehicular traffic mode only, was estimated. It was rare that the multimodal (both pedestrian and motor vehicle) exposure was measured for the micro-level pedestrian safety analysis. It is necessary to take into account the interactions between pedestrian and motor vehicles, by incorporating the vehicular traffic volume, speed and density, into the pedestrian behavior model for the exposure estimate. In addition, the effects of unobserved heterogeneity and spatial correlation on the association between pedestrian crash, exposure and possible factors should be considered. This project aims to address the fundamental problem on how to measure the relationship between pedestrian crash risk and possible factors, taking into account the multimodal exposure, at the signalized intersections. Hong Kong is a compact city with high level of pedestrian activity. Results of this project should influence the planning and management of road facilities, and thus enhance the pedestrian safety and walkability in the long run. 步行不僅能夠舒緩交通擠塞和車輛排放的問題，更可提升市民的生活質素。易行度在世界各地日漸流行，香港也不例外。在香港，每天大約有百分之九十的通勤活動使用公共交通工具，而步行乃公共運輸的主要可達方法。安全是易行度的其中一個重要指標，行人安全在香港備受關注。在2016年，共有20132人在交通意外中傷亡，其中行人佔百分之十七。然而，在交通意外中嚴重受傷和死亡的道路使用者中，行人分別佔百分之三十和六十四。行人安全問題在市區的交通燈路口尤為嚴重，因為市區人口密度高，活動頻繁，車輛與行人的衝突更是頻繁。因此，建立一套考慮行人意外和傷亡風險的綜合安全管理框架，對改善道路設計和交通控制非常重要。 為了準確計算行人意外風險，需要可靠的曝光評估方法，量化行人與車輛的碰撞潛在可能。在宏觀（區域性）層面，傳統上以人口普查資料、土地利用分佈和交通組成等計算整體曝光，或以個人步行路徑選擇分析計算個別曝光。在微觀（路口或行人過路處）層面，則以行人或車輛其中之一的流量，利用交通量、密度和速度去計算曝光。可是，更準確的方法應該是結合行人與車輛的流量、密度和速度綜合分析，以考慮行人和車輛間的互動對安全的影響。此外，曝光估計還需要考慮無法觀測的異質性和空間相關性等對行人行為、曝光和其他可能因素間的關係的影響。

15209818.label: Realisation of objectives
15209818.value: All project objectives have been achieved. Research outcomes are published in the top journal in the related subject areas. Overall, 15 research papers have been published in SCI journals (see J1-J15 in Part C). Objective 1: In this project, pedestrian and vehicular traffic flow data were collected at the signalized intersections using video observation surveys. Sampled intersections were widely distributed in the whole territory of Hong Kong. Additionally, variations in traffic pattern in term of traffic volume, vehicle mix, pedestrian volume and behaviours across different time periods, e.g., weekday peak, weekday non-peak and weekend, were accounted. Furthermore, different crossing types including single direction, two-direction, single stage and multi-stage (split of pedestrian green time) crossings are considered [J5, J7 and J9 in Part C]. Overall, 10118 pedestrians were captured in the video observation surveys. Information on personal characteristics including gender, age group and presence of pedestrian group was collected. Additionally, other factors including road environment (width and distance of crossing, land use and road class), traffic condition (traffic volume, percentage of heavy vehicles and vehicular speed) and traffic management (signal phase, green time, red time and cycle time) are accounted [J5 in Part C]. For the multi-stage signalized crossings, which are commonly found in Hong Kong to cater high vehicular and pedestrian flow, changes in pedestrian behaviour across different stages, i.e., waiting at the kerbside versus waiting at the central island, of the same individual were also accounted [J7 in Part C]. Furthermore, to extract the trajectories of pedestrians and vehicles from video images, advanced image processing and recognition algorithms including YOLO and Deep Sort are adopted. Validity of YOLO and Deep Sort algorithms for object detection and tracking were assessed using deep learning approach [J9 in Part C]. Last but not least, pedestrian flow counts at the road segment level were also obtained using automatic counting system. Therefore, efficiency and precision of pedestrian flow estimation could be enhanced [J12 in Part C]. Objective 2: In this project, multimodal crash exposure was estimated using the data obtained from multiple sources including observation surveys, population census, household travel survey, Annual Traffic Census, digital road network and Transport Information System of Hong Kong [J1, J5, J6, J7, J9, J10 and J15 in Part C]. For example, household travel survey captured the trip data of 35,400 households (1.5% of overall) in Hong Kong. Then, trip data including trip generation, distribution and modal split of 101385 individuals were used to estimate the walking frequency and total walking time at both aggregated [J6 and J15 in Part C] and disaggregated levels (by time period and transport mode) [J1 and J10 in Part C] in 289 Tertiary Planning Units in Hong Kong. Additionally, as the definition of exposure in existing pedestrian safety studies was vague, pedestrian crash involvement, relative to overall walking trips, was modeled simultaneously with crash occurrence, using joint probability framework [J2 and J6 in Part C]. For example, walking distance and number of roads crossed of pedestrians were estimated using an integrated trip assignment model, to better proxy the exposure for pedestrian crash [J2 in Part C]. Furthermore, propensity of red light running of pedestrians and pedestrian-vehicle interactions can also be used to proxy pedestrian crash exposure at the microscopic level [J8 and J14 in Part C]. For example, effect of the trade-off between safety and time on red light running behaviour was estimated using stated preference method, with which the effects of pedestrian characteristics (attitude, social norms and perceived behavioural control), traffic condition (traffic flow, vehicular speed and vehicle class) [J8 in Part C], crossing facilities (underpasses and footbridges) and weather condition [J14 in Part C] were accounted. On the other hand, effects of built environment, transport network, and human factors on multimodal crash exposure were investigated [J1, J2, J6, J9, J11, J12 and J15 in Part C]. For the built environment, factors including land use, points of interest (POIs) including restaurants, hotels and shops, and urban street tree (tree density and tree canopy cover) were considered [J6, J9, J12 and J15 in Part C]. For the transport network and facilities, factors including road density, road class, road connectivity, accessibility of crossing facilities (signalized crossing, footbridges and underpasses), traffic operation characteristics (traffic flow, vehicle class and vehicle speed), and public transport stations were considered [J2, J9, J11, J12 and J15 in Part C]. Furthermore, personal characteristics including demographics, socioeconomics and household structure were considered [J1 and J6 in Part C]. Last but not least, as the pedestrian-vehicle interaction can proxy the multimodal exposure, interference of the decisions between driver and pedestrian was modeled as simultaneous two-player game using game theory, with which human error and irrationality were incorporated using the quantal response equilibrium method [J9 in Part C]. Objective 3: In this project, relationship between pedestrian-vehicle crash and factors including built environment, road network, traffic characteristics and human factors was examined using advanced econometric models including negative binomial regression, multinomial logit regression and Poisson lognormal regression models, with Full Bayesian approach [J1, J3, J6, J7, J8, J10, J14 and J15 in Part C]. To eliminate the bias by selection of treatment and control group in safety evaluation, Propensity Score Matching approach was adopted [J4 in Part C]. Additionally, to account for the effect of unobserved heterogeneity on the association, novel mathematical formulations including random parameters [J1, J7 and J15 in Part C], and random regret minimization [J8 and J14 in Part C] are considered. For the spatial analysis of pedestrian crash, spatial correlation among neighbouring geographical units are controlled using Bayesian spatial approach [J11, J12 and J15 in Part C] with conditional autoregressive prior [J10 in Part C]. Furthermore, multivariate and panel data approaches were adopted to eliminate the bias in parameter estimation by repeated observations of the same individuals [J14 in Part C] and multivariate correlation between crash counts of different injury severity levels [J12 and J15 in Part C]. Last but not least, boundary crash problem (crashes occur at or near the boundary of a geographical unit may correlate with the characteristics of the neighbouring units) is prevalent in the spatial analysis of pedestrian-vehicle crash. Therefore, a data-driven approach is proposed to optimize the boundary crash allocation process. Therefore, accuracy of crash estimation in terms of root-mean-square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) could be improved [J13 in Part C].

15209818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209818.value: This research indicates that it is viable to estimate the pedestrian crash exposure based on multiple data collections including video observation surveys [J5, J7 and J9 in Part C], household travel surveys [J1, J2, J6, J10 and J15 in Part C] and automatic counting system [J12 in Part C]. For example, walking trip frequency, total walking time and walking distance estimated based on trip generation and assignment model can be used to proxy the aggregated pedestrian exposure at the zonal (macro) level [J1, J2 and J6 in Part C]. Additionally, disaggregated pedestrian exposure at the road segment (micro) level with respect to time period and transport mode can also be estimated [J1, J10 and J12 in Part C]. Furthermore, crossing behaviours of pedestrians and pedestrian-vehicle interactions captured using video image can also be adopted to reflect the pedestrian exposure to traffic crash in the real-time [J5, J7 and J9 in Part C]. On the other hand, this research finds that there are significant effects for built environment (land use, point of interest and green vegetation) [J6, J9 and J12 in Part C], transport infrastructure (road network configuration, public transport and crossing facilities) [J1, J6, J10 and J15 in Part C], traffic characteristics (traffic flow, vehicle class and vehicular speed) [J5, J7 and J9 in Part C] and personal characteristics (socio-demographics, safety attitude and household structure) [J1, J6, J8, J14 in Part C] on pedestrian crash risk, with which pedestrian crash exposure is controlled. Furthermore, novel data acquisition techniques including image processing, object detection, trajectory tracking and remote sensing are adopted to collect the disaggregated pedestrian flow and speed data in this research [J9, J12 and J15 in Part C]. In the econometric models for the association between pedestrian crash risk and possible influencing factors, prevalent modelling issues including unobserved heterogeneity, spatial correlation, panel data and boundary crash allocation were addressed using novel approaches including random parameters, conditional autoregressive prior and data-driven method [J1, J7, J10, J11, J12, J13 and J15 in Part C]. This project can indicate effective transport policy, optimal urban transport planning, and targeted traffic management strategies that improve pedestrian safety, and promote walkability in Hong Kong in the long run [J3, J4, J8 and J14 in Part C].

15209818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209818.value: For the collection of pedestrian and vehicle flow data, future research can be focused on the training and validation of computer vision-based object detection and trajectory tracking algorithms that can accurately capture the pedestrian and vehicle characteristics in Hong Kong. For example, characteristics of individuals with impaired physical mobility and commercial vehicles (taxis, buses and goods vehicles) should be considered. Regarding the statistical models, it is worth exploring the advanced modelling framework that can address the issues including imbalanced data, endogeneity and under reporting using data-driven approaches. It is because crashes that involve non-motorised transport are less likely reported. Last but not least, future research could be extended to pedestrian simulation model using advanced mixed reality technology. In particular, high definition 3D road environment, dynamic traffic flow, and adverse weather could be incorporated into the simulation model. Hence, relationship between road environment, traffic condition, pedestrian behaviour and safety risk can be examined.

15209818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209818.value: In the previous studies, pedestrian flow data is normally not available for the estimation of pedestrian exposure and safety risk. This project has applied novel data acquisition and analysis methods to estimate pedestrian flow for pedestrian safety analysis at both micro- and macro-levels. For example, pedestrian volumes at individual signalized intersections and road segments can be estimated based on video images, with which the pedestrians are detected and tracked using advanced computer algorithms. Also, it is possible to estimate pedestrian walking trips, time and distance based on household survey data using advanced econometric models. Then, both macro-level factors including land use, green area, road network, public transport and crossing facilities, and micro-level factors including gender, age, safety attitude and travel habit that would affect pedestrian crash risk are identified. In particular, precision of crash estimation can be enhanced and bias in parameter estimation can be eliminated using advanced mathematical formulations. Last but not least, findings can shed light on future urban and transport planning, traffic management and transport policy strategies that can reduce pedestrian injury risk. Hence, walking can be promoted as a green transport mode in the future sustainable urban development strategy.

15209918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209918.value: Fall accidents are serious threats to construction workers. Previous fall protection methods have either been heavily relying on invasive methods or passive measures. In this project, we developed a method to use unobtrusive wearable insole technology to alleviate MSD risk factors and fall hazards. Specifically, we developed a method for MSD risk factor classification/recognition using foot plantar pressure distribution collected from insole sensors; we developed a risk index to assess the gait of construction workers from insole sensor data (poor gait having been found to increase the likelihood of falls); and 3) we validated the methods developed in the project through laboratory tests and site trials. Overall, the project has equipped the construction industry with a non-invasive tool to recognize MSD risk factors and workers with poor gaits. Most importantly, this method enables intervention before any suffering or misfortune occurs.

15209918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209918.value: We will seek relevant governmental bodies and major industrial organizations to apply this method in managing and mitigating fall accidents on construction sites.

15209918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209918.value: Construction tasks expose workers to various occupational hazards. Consequently, the labour component is adversely affecting the occupational safety and health of the construction workers. Among those health and safety hazards, work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and falls are a significant burden to the construction industry. To mitigate these hazards, it is imperative to proactively identify the risk factors of MSDs and fall-prone construction workers. Previous efforts for identifying MSD risk factors have relied on either very invasive methods or various sensor technologies which have their own limitations. Moreover, fall protection on construction sites has heavily relied on passive measures, which will need to be replaced with proactive measures to identify workers at risk. Given the above problems, this project aims to make use of the unobtrusive wearable insole technology to alleviate MSD risk factors and fall hazards.

15210018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210018.value: Lightning is a natural phenomenon. It may occur within clouds or from a cloud to the ground. A cloud-to-ground lightning flash usually starts with a downward process followed by a return stroke. The return stroke is considered as a neutralization process of opposite charges on the lightning channel and the ground surface. It is the return stroke current that causes fatal casualties, severe damage to facilities and mal-function of electrical and electronic systems. Lightning protection, therefore, becomes indispensable for the live beings, facilities and systems at the ground. To provide effective lightning protection, both system modelling and transient simulation are the essential prerequisites. In past decades research on lightning physics has been carried out extensively. The physical knowledge on lightning mechanism have been built up continuously. It is found that parameters in physical models that describe lightning phenomena may vary temporally and spatially, and could be mutually coupled. Recently, a number of return stroke models have been proposed for engineering applications. These models, however, have not considered some of key issues addressed in the physical models, for example, the ground surface charge. This project aims to develop an integrated electromagnetic model for a system incorporating the lightning return stroke, the cloud, the ground surface charge and wire systems during a negative CG lightning flash. This model will be constructed with a partial electrical equivalent circuit approach by making use of our physical knowledge of lightning. Mutual coupling among different parts will be taken into account. A simulation procedure will be developed for evaluating the lightning transients in the systems at the ground, as well as the lightning-induced electromagnetic field at a distance. These transients include transient voltages and currents in the overhead line and underground cables, lightning currents on the grounded structure, and ground potential rise and its subsequent effects. This procedure will help to evaluate the influence of tall structures on the lightning return stroke current. The effect of ground surface charge could be addressed further by comparing the results with existing return stroke models. The proposed procedure as well as the results obtained could be used further for updating our knowledge on lightning-generated effects and improving existing design principles and guidelines for effective protection. 閃電是一種自然現象。它可能發生在雲與雲之間或者雲與地之間。雲對地閃電由向下過程和隨後的閃電回擊組成。閃電回擊被認為是一種閃電通道和地面上電荷的中和過程。這個中和過程會產生巨大的回擊電流從而造成人員傷亡、設施受損和電氣系統非正常工作。因此，雷電防護對保護人員安全、設施和系統正常運行來說,變得不可缺少。為提供有效的防雷保護，有必要建立一套電腦摸擬系統，以便能預測潛在的災害或損害。 近幾十年來, 閃電物理學的研究得到了廣泛的開展,雷電機理的物理知識不斷更新。研究表明，描述閃電現象的物理模型中的參數在時間和空間上不斷變化，並且相互耦合。最近，有人提出了一些用於工程應用的閃電回擊模型。然而, 這些模型並沒有考慮物理模型中的一些關鍵問題，例如，地面電荷的影響。 該專案的目的是建立一個集成的電磁模型系統。該系統包括閃電回擊通道、雲、地面電荷和導線系統。該模型將利用現有的閃電物理知識，用部分電氣等效電路方法構造。不同部分之間的相互耦合會得到考慮。 這項研究將會為評估地面系統中的閃電瞬變，以及閃電引起的電磁場建立模擬程式。這些瞬態包括架空線和地下電纜的瞬態電壓和電流、接地結構上的雷電電流、地面電位抬升及其附隨的影響。這一過程將有助於評估高層結構對閃電回擊通道電流的影響。通過將結果與現有的閃電回擊模型進行比較，可以進一步討論地表電荷的影響。擬議的程式以及取得的成果可進一步用於更新我們對閃電產生的影響的認識, 並改進現有的設計原則和有效保護的準則。

15210018.label: Realisation of objectives
15210018.value: The PEEC modeling of a lightning channel was addressed. A thorough review of lightning channels was conducted first, which covered the physical phenomena of a lightning flash, and various physical and electromagnetic lightning channel models for lightning strikes on the ground or lightning strikes on elevated structures. The PEEC modeling of a lightning channel is formulated based on the mixed potential integral equation and the current continuity equation. Based on the PEEC method, all the lightning physical parameters are transferred into the circuit domain. The lumped physical evolution of a lightning channel is described with circuit elements in each PEEC segment. The nonlinear resistance, inductance, potential coefficient, and conductance have been integrated into the PEEC model to describe the lightning channel physical behavior. Firstly, the lightning strikes on the ground issue were settled. The channel heating effect is modeled with nonlinear resistance. The channel radius expansion is modeled with nonlinear inductance and core potential coefficient. The channel dynamic corona effect based on the most recent physical research is modeled with the nonlinear sheath potential coefficient and lumped conductance. It is found that the nonlinear resistance affects only the rising part of the lightning return stroke current. The propagating speed and attenuation of return stroke current are decided respectively by the nonlinear sheath potential coefficient and lumped conductance. Meanwhile the nonlinear inductance and core potential coefficient have little influence on the return stroke current. The algorithms for building the PEEC model of a lightning channel have been implemented on the platform of MATLAB. The coding work has been carried out to produce an in-house program for our simulation of lightning strikes. Theoretical work on the modeling of lossy ground has been carried out. By considering the ground surface charge, the PEEC method was modified to consider the effect of lossy ground and indirect lightning. The corresponding theoretical analysis and numerical algorithm were well-developed and published. This model is based on the scattering PEEC method and dyadic Green’s function for the multi-layer ground structure. An equivalent circuit was derived for the first time by including correction terms arising from the lossy. The low-frequency model of the lossy ground was derived, and was depicted using the mirror image of source elements, The computational burden in the time-domain simulation can be significantly relieved. Because of the characteristics of the PEEC method, mutual coupling among different sub-systems is automatically incorporated in the modeling of these systems. The objectives 1 and 2 have been successfully achieved. The theories and models developed have been applied to analyze lightning transients in different cases. Computer simulations have been performed to investigate the lightning transients in electrical systems and steel structures in several ground objects, including buildings and photovoltaic power stations. Simulations were performed under lightning strikes to tall towers. The integrated model was verified by comparing the currents and electric fields with the experiment data. This proposed model also was applied to evaluate lightning surges on a wind turbine system. A significant difference is found between the proposed method and the simplified lightning channel model. Both the current and voltage on the system are overestimated if the simplified lightning channel model is used. Significant oscillation is found with this simplified model as well, which is not in correspondence with the observation result under natural lightning. The coupling effects between return stroke and ground or grounded wire structures were comprehensively analyzed. The coupling effects include lightning-induced overvoltage on overhead power lines. It is found that the coupling from a lightning channel has a significant impact on the surge response of the tower. This coupling specifically brings a 12.7% higher insulator voltage and a difference of nearly 28% in the ratio of ground wire current to tower foot current. Ignoring this effect in numerical simulations will lead to noticeable deviations in lightning surges and weaken the hazard of lightning strikes. The coupling effects also include the ground potential rise in the lightning-stroked or adjacent independent grounding grid. The results of step voltage distribution for several typical grounding structures under different lightning current waveforms and physical environments are studied, such as the configuration of the grounding grid, the conductivity of the earth, and the rise time of the lightning current waveform. An advance in traveling wave theory was made in this project. It presents a theoretical time-domain analysis of lightning surge propagation on a multistage and multi-conductor tower, where the non-TEM wave propagation in the tower is characterized by time/position-variant transient impedance. It was found that the traditional transmission line theory could lead to a significant error in the current in the tower. The influence of grounding structures under a lightning strike, particularly those for protecting the PV power generation system was addressed. The surge voltage on the PV cables, potential rise, and transfer voltage caused by the lightning surge current were investigated. Recommendations have been provided to mitigate these lightning-generated problems. An integrated model has been worked out for the system that contains both lightning channel and ground structure. An extended distributed circuit was developed for modeling the lightning channel, by including the physical behavior of the lightning corona effect. Meanwhile, the wire structure on the ground was modeled with the partial element equivalent circuit method. They were integrated into an integrated model. The interaction between the lightning channel and ground structures was included in the integrated model. A lumped voltage source was introduced to ensure an “undisturbed” current waveform at the attachment point. A procedure was provided to determine this voltage source in a nonlinear circuit. A direct lightning strike to the 553 m tall CN tower was recorded. The lightning current on the tower top was measured. It is observed that the waveform has two distinct peaks. The second peak is primarily caused by the current wave reflected from the ground. This cannot be simulated with a hard current source. With the proposed model we can reconstruct the lightning return stroke current in the channel and replicate the lightning current on the tower. Simulations were performed under lightning strikes to tall towers. The proposed model was verified by comparing the currents and electric fields with the experiment data. This proposed model also was applied to evaluate lightning surges on a wind turbine system. A significant difference was found between the proposed method and the simplified lightning channel model. Both the current and voltage on the system are overestimated if the simplified lightning channel model is used. Significant oscillation is found with this simplified model as well, which is not in correspondence with the observation result under natural lightning. An instability problem was encountered when evaluating induced voltage caused by incident lightning electromagnetic pulses. It becomes a hurdle in the application of PEEC for evaluating induced transient currents in closed wire loops and is primarily caused by the discretization of the electric field in the numerical evaluation of external voltage sources. An algorithm is provided to solve this instability problem, It is also found that Uman’s formula is generally incapable of producing stable induced currents in a wire loop structure. The objectives 3 and 4 have been successfully achieved.

15210018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210018.value: In this project, the theory of PEEC for wires above lossy ground was further developed. This theory is particularly important for transient analysis of a wire structure on the ground by considering the effect of lightning channel, structure, and ground surface charge. The PEEC model is formulated with dyadic Green’s functions. An equivalent circuit is derived for the first time by including correction terms arising from the lossy ground. Circuit parameters are expressed using Sommerfeld integrals. The low-frequency model of the lossy ground is derived and is depicted using the mirror image of source elements. An extension of the ground model was further developed by considering wires in any layer of the air-ground space. Closed-form expressions are derived for the quasi-static and asymptotic approximation of Sommerfeld integrals. These results are particularly important in developing circuit models of the wire structures under lightning. In this project, an extended traveling wave theory using electric scalar potential is introduced to analyze lightning transients on a structure without a returning current path or that does not support TEM-mode wave propagation. It is considered supplementary to the existing traveling wave theory based on the TEM-mode wave propagation. The concept of transient impedance is introduced, which is the position/time variant. With this, characteristics of wave propagation on a line, at a discontinuity, and at an open/short end are presented. This theory provides a simple tool for analyzing wave propagation conceptually on a vertical structure. In this project, an integrated model of the lightning channel, tall structure, and ground surface for lightning analysis was developed by considering their mutual interaction. An extended distributed circuit is employed to model the lightning channel, by including the dynamic behavior of the corona sheath. The non-linear, non-uniform, and time evolution characteristics of the lightning channel are taken into account. The wire structure on the ground is modeled with the PEEC method. A lumped voltage source is introduced to ensure an “undisturbed” current waveform at the attachment point. This model is particularly important for studying the mutual coupling effect between the lightning channel and ground structure. The developed theories and models have been applied to different cases, including buildings, power distribution systems, transmission or wind turbine towers, grounding of photovoltaic power stations, etc. Nine journal papers have been published in IEEE Transactions Journals, and one Ph.D. student was trained with the support of this project.

15210018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210018.value: The PEEC theory has been successfully applied to model ground structures (e.g., power systems, buildings, railway systems, telecommunication systems) for transient analysis under lightning. Note that the lightning-generated electromagnetic impulse has a frequency spectrum up to MHz. It is noted that these systems are very vulnerable under high-power electromagnetic pulses (lightning, nuclear explosion, solar storm, etc.), which have a frequency spectrum up to GHz. Currently, there is no effective simulation method to address transients in these systems caused by such high-frequency EM pulses. It would be necessary to carry out a study of extending the existing PEEC theory to this new application.

15210018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210018.value: Lightning is a natural phenomenon. A cloud-to-ground lightning flash usually starts with a downward process followed by a return stroke. The return stroke is considered a neutralization process of opposite charges on the lightning channel and the ground surface. It is the return stroke current that causes fatal casualties, severe damage to facilities, and malfunction of electrical and electronic systems. To provide effective lightning protection, system modeling and transient simulation are essential prerequisites. This project developed an integrated electromagnetic model for a system incorporating the lightning return stroke, the cloud, the ground surface charge, and wire systems during a negative CG lightning stroke. This model is constructed with a partial electrical equivalent circuit approach by making use of our physical knowledge of lightning. A simulation procedure was developed for evaluating the lightning transients in the systems at the ground, as well as the lightning-induced electromagnetic field at a distance. The developed theories and models have been applied to evaluate lightning transients in different systems on the ground, power systems, railway systems, telecommunication systems, renewable energy systems, buildings, etc. The results can be used to update our knowledge of lightning-generated effects and improve existing design principles and guidelines for effective protection.

15210618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15210618.value: 中國不同城市群空氣PM2.5化學混合污染物與毒性的差異

15210618.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15210618.value: Prof Fu, Pingqing Prof Wong, Chris Kong Chu

15210618.label: Project Objectives
15210618.value: We will conduct cell-based bioassays to determine if location- and season-specific PM2.5 can trigger cellular responses in different dose-response ways. We will explore an integrative transcriptomics and proteomics platform to elucidate whether the same mass concentrations of PM2.5 from different locations/seasons would act on different toxic mechanisms. We will try targeted and non-targeted instrumental techniques and mixture toxicity modeling to determine what key components in PM2.5 account for the different toxic actions.

15210618.label: Realisation of objectives
15210618.value: To determine if location- and season-specific PM2.5 can trigger cellular responses in different dose-response ways using cell-based bioassays, we conducted the BEAS-2b cell viability assay and ROS assay using representative samples from different seasons throughout a year across different regions in China, including Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Beijing, and other urban, rural, and industrial areas in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) and Pearl River Delta (PRD) regions. This allowed us to determine the corresponding effect concentrations (EC10 and ECIR1.5) of location- and season-specific PM2.5 in a large scale. It was observed that location- and season-specific PM2.5 can trigger cellular responses in different dose-response ways, and there was no clear correlation between toxicity and seasonal variations. Furthermore, it was found that high PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily indicate high toxicity, while low PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily imply low toxicity. It is highly likely that the toxicity is influenced by the specific types and concentrations of toxic compounds from different emission sources present in the complex mixture of PM2.5. The findings motivated us to explore the compositions, sources, seasonal variations, and health risks associated with key toxic compounds in PM2.5, as well as assess their biological toxicity. We tested the organic carbon (OC), elemental carbon (EC, or black carbon (BC)), major metals, endotoxins, water-soluble ions (WSI), hopanes, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from PM2.5 samples collected using targeted instrumental techniques. Taking Hong Kong as an example, the major sources of total PM2.5 were identified as secondary aerosols, shipping emissions, traffic-related dust, combustion, vehicle emissions, and sea salt. A 24-hour back trajectory cluster analysis, based on meteorological data, revealed regional effects: second sulfate aerosol and shipping emissions may increase with southeast oceanic trajectories in the warm season, while northern continental trajectories significantly contribute to combustion emissions in the cold season. Moreover, northeast trajectories notably enhance the second nitrate aerosol during the cold season. With the obtained profile and composition of PM2.5, we further ranked the contributions of different emission sources to the health risks posed by hazardous metal components in airborne PM2.5 using the positive matrix factorization (PMF) model. Firstly, we performed an integrated source apportionment to quantify the contributions of the major source categories underlying metal-induced health risks with information on the bioaccessibility (using simulated lung fluid) and speciation (using synchrotron-based techniques) of metals. The results showed that the particulate trace metal profiles reflected the land-use gradient within each region, with the highest concentrations of anthropogenically enriched metals at the industrial sites in the study regions. The resulting carcinogenic risk that these elements posed was higher in the YRD than in the PRD. Chromium was the dominant contributor to the total excessive cancer risks posed by metals while manganese accounted for a large proportion of non-carcinogenic risks. An elevated contribution from industrial emissions was found in the YRD, while traffic emissions and non-traffic combustion (the burning of coal/waste/biomass) were the common dominant sources of cancer and non-cancer risks posed by metals in both regions. Moreover, the risk-oriented source apportionment of metals did not mirror the mass concentration-based one, suggesting the insufficiency of the latter to inform emission mitigation in favor of public health. Secondly, we compared heavy metal- and PAHs-induced health risks of urban PM2.5 of Hong Kong. In both roadside and ambient PM2.5 samples, the calculated carcinogenic risk attributed to PAHs was significantly lower than that posed by heavy metals. The vehicle emission source was regarded as the primary contributor of heavy metal and PAHs, however, non-fossil fuel combustion affected by regional diffusion emerged as a more significant factor for total toxic component-related cancer risk. While providing region-specific insights into the quantitative contribution of major source categories to the health risks of PM2.5-associated trace metals and PAHs, our studies highlighted the need to consider the health protection goal-based source apportionment and emission mitigation in supplement to the current mass concentration-based framework. Beyond the application of source apportionment and carcinogenic risk modeling, we explored an integrative transcriptomics and proteomics platform to elucidate whether the same mass concentrations of PM2.5 from different locations/seasons would act on different toxic mechanisms. Growing literature has documented varying toxic potencies of source- or site-specific fine particulate matter (PM2.5), as opposed to the practice that treats particle toxicities as independent of composition given the incomplete understanding of the toxicity of the constituents. Quantifying component-specific contribution is the key to unlocking the geographical disparities of particle toxicity from a mixture perspective. In this study, we performed integrated mixture–toxicity experiments and modeling to quantify the contribution of metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), two default culprit component groups of PM2.5 toxicity, to in vitro oxidative stress caused by wintertime PM2.5 from Beijing and Guangzhou, two megacities in China. PM2.5 from Beijing exhibited greater toxic potencies at equal mass concentrations. The targeted chemical analysis revealed higher burden of metals and PAHs per unit mass of PM2.5 in Beijing. These chemicals together explained 38 and 24% on average of PM2.5-induced reactive oxygen species in Beijing and Guangzhou, respectively, while >60% of the effects remained to be resolved in terms of contributing chemicals. PAHs contributed approximately twice the share of the PM2.5 mixture effects as metals. Fe, Cu, and Mn were the dominant metals, constituting >80% of the metal-shared proportion of the PM2.5 effects. Dibenzo[a,l]pyrene alone explained >65% of the PAH-shared proportion of the PM2.5 toxicity effects. The significant contribution from coal combustion and vehicular emissions in Beijing suggested the major source disparities of toxicologically active PAHs between the two cities. Our study provided novel quantitative insights into the role of varying toxic component profiles in shaping the differential toxic potencies of city-specific PM2.5 pollution. To unravel the unknown fractions in urban PM2.5 that contribute to the unexplained toxicity contributions, we applied non-targeted instrumental techniques and mixture toxicity modeling to identify non-targeted components and determine what key components in PM2.5 account for the different toxic actions. We employed pre-treatment methods, such as organic solvent extraction to isolate organic fractions from PM2.5. Using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry, along with data analysis software like Progenesis QI, we established a non-targeted analysis method for identification of organic pollutants in the PM2.5 mixture. With this approach, unknown organic compounds in the PM2.5 samples were screened and identified. Through molecular composition analysis, multivariate statistical analysis, and structure matching analysis, we systematically elucidated 45 compounds with high instrument response. By comparing them with standard substances, we identified new pollutants such as N-dodecyl ethanolamine, as well as organic pollutants with relatively high concentrations, including phthalates, carboxylic acids, and nitroaromatic compounds. To assess the toxicity risk of organic pollutants in PM2.5, we employed toxicological calculation software such as ADMET lab and utilized quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models for toxicity prediction. This approach allowed us to narrow down the search targets for highly toxic byproducts. Furthermore, using human lung epithelial cells as test subjects, we investigated the toxic effects of organic pollutants at different levels, including cell viability and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. We found that nitroaromatic compounds and certain fatty amine compounds exhibited high toxic effects, highlighting the need for further attention and more systematic studies.

15210618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210618.value: Beyond the current mass concentration-based framework in air quality management, our studies indicated location- and season-specific PM2.5 can trigger cellular responses in different dose-response ways, and it was found that high PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily indicate high toxicity, while low PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily imply low toxicity. The findings suggested PM2.5 toxicity is influenced by the specific types and concentrations of toxic compounds from different emission sources present in the complex PM mixture. Researchers must find the particles that are most dangerous to health in each place so policies can reduce levels of those pollutants first. To this end, we established an integrative transcriptomics and proteomics platform to elucidate the contribution of each PM2.5 component to total PM2.5 toxicity. Using targeted chemical analysis and mixture toxicity modeling, we revealed metals and PAHs together explained 20-40% on average of PM2.5-induced reactive oxygen species in urban areas, while >60% of the effects remained to be resolved in terms of contributing chemicals. Our study provided novel quantitative insights into the role of varying toxic component profiles in shaping the differential toxic potencies of city-specific PM2.5 pollution and highlighted the need to consider the health protection goal-based source apportionment and emission mitigation in supplement to the current mass concentration-based framework. To unravel the unknown fractions in urban PM2.5 that contribute to the unexplained toxicity contributions, we invented an ultra-performance liquid chromatography-Orbitrap mass spectrometry-based method to identify organic compounds in PM2.5 from urban areas in Hong Kong and found organic compounds in the CHO, CHON, CHN, CHOS, and CHONS subgroups were major components of the PM2.5. We used Kendrick mass defect and van Krevelen analyses combined with structural characterization to identify 45 structures with high signal abundances in 13 classes. Quantitative structure–property relationships predicted different toxic effects, highlighting the potential hazard of nitrogenous compounds (e.g., nitrophenols) and (condensed) aromatic compounds [e.g., oxygenated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (OPAHs)]. Although selecting different toxicity endpoints led to different toxicity values, results from in vitro cytotoxicity and intracellular reactive oxygen species generation assays also indicated that nitrogenous compounds (e.g., N-lauryldiethanolamine) and OPAHs (e.g., acenaphthenequinone) had high toxic potencies. Our studies provide an efficient method in classification and structure identification of key toxic components in the complex PM2.5 mixture.

15210618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210618.value: Following the significant research outcomes, we will continue to identify the key toxicity contributors in urban ambient PM2.5 using real air exposure methods. Firstly, we will conduct research particularly concerns the bio-accessibility and cytotoxicity contribution of heavy metals and PAHs to avoid overestimating the health risks. The methods for assessing bio-accessibility of heavy metals and PAHs have been developed. To mimic the real exposure condition, we have established a state-of-the-art platform, i.e., Air-liquid Interface Exposure Systems, for simultaneous air pollutant monitoring and in vitro toxicity assessment. We will conduct exposure experiments concerning the toxicity of PM2.5 in Hong Kong. Furthermore, we will establish an in vivo exposure chamber to perform toxicity evaluation on acute dust and long-term PM2.5 exposures, integrate in vitro and in vivo studies under real air exposure scenarios in Hong Kong and the region, and synchronize the results from in vitro and in vivo studies on air exposure and human health. Last but not least, we will apply our non-targeted analysis method to identify the largely unknown nitrogenous compounds and (condensed) aromatic compounds in various PM2.5 samples and to extend our understanding of the toxicological significance of unknown compounds in PM2.5.

15210618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210618.value: Current air quality management on ambient PM2.5 is largely based on the mass concentrations, our studies suggested that high PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily indicate high toxicity, while low PM2.5 mass concentrations did not necessarily imply low toxicity. The findings suggested PM2.5 toxicity is determined by the specific types and concentrations of toxic compounds from different emission sources present in the complex PM mixture. Researchers must identify the particles that are most dangerous to health in each place so policies can reduce levels of those pollutants in priority. To this end, we established an integrative transcriptomics and proteomics platform to elucidate the contribution of each PM2.5 component to total PM2.5 toxicity. Our study highlighted the need to consider the health protection goal-based source apportionment and emission mitigation in supplement to the current mass concentration-based framework. To unravel the unknown fractions in urban PM2.5 that contribute to the unexplained toxicity contributions, we invented a non-targeted analyzing method to identify organic compounds in PM2.5 from urban areas in Hong Kong. This efficient method provides a powerful tool in classification and structure identification of key toxic components in the complex PM2.5 mixture.

15210718.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15210718.value: 尺寸和温度对NASICON类材料在脱嵌锂离子和钠离子过程中的相变的影响

15210718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210718.value: Rechargeable batteries are widely used in digital devices, electric vehicles (EVs), stationary energy storage wells, and aerospace applications. Apart from the requirements of high energy density and extended life cycles, rechargeable batteries also need to provide stable output and fast charge/discharge cycling over a wide temperature range (e.g., −40 °C ≤ T ≤ 60 °C), especially for powering an EV or a hybrid EV. But the truth is that the rechargeable batteries including both Li-ion batteries and Na-ion batteries often experience significant capacity loss at low temperatures and capacity fade during cycles at high temperatures, which severely restricts their applications. Current efforts to expand the service temperatures focus on improving the composition of the electrolyte. However, the phase transition of electrode materials at extended temperature ranges is poorly understood, which limits the development of electrode materials with wider temperature compatibility. The nature of phase transition of the electrode material directly affects its performance. Although the phase transition mechanism is inherent in the electrode materials, it can be substantially influenced by particle size and working temperature. NASICON (NAtrium Super Ionic CONductor)-structured materials represent a family of attractive electrodes and solid electrolytes for LIBs and NIBs due to their great structural stability and superior ionic conductivity, and thus become the model material system of present research. By combing experimental studies and theoretical analysis and calculations, the proposed project will systematically investigate the phase transitions of NASICON-structured electrode materials with different particle sizes in their operating environments at extended temperature ranges. The project will have three main components: (i) adopting in-operando techniques including in-operando XRD and in-operando Raman spectroscopy to investigate the phase transitions and electrochemical properties of electrode materials with different sizes during electrochemical cycling at various temperatures (e.g., -40 °C to 60 °C), and clarifying the correlation between the phase transition and the electrochemical properties; (ii) establishing phase diagrams for the phase transition mechanism as a function of size and temperature; and (iii) proposing a new rationale to explain the coupled size- and temperature-dependent phase transition induced by electrochemical Li+ or Na+-(de)intercalation through phase field modeling and density functional theory calculations. We expect that the results will provide guidance for the design of all-climate rechargeable batteries, and will significantly improve the understanding of the impact of nanosizing on solid-state phase transitions in lithium or sodium storage devices at various temperatures.

15210818.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15210818.value: 研發用於在血腦屏障微流體芯片中光治療阿爾茨海默病的混合納米系統

15210818.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15210818.value: Dr Chan, Koon-Ho Prof Zhao, Xin

15210818.label: Project Objectives
15210818.value: Aim 1: Synthesis and characterization of MOF photosensitizer nanoparticle and MoS2 nanosheet. MOF photosensitizing nanoparticles will be synthesized by a hydrothermal approach with various photosensitizer linkers. The synthesis conditions will be optimized to achieve controllable size, ultra-stable structure and good singlet oxygen generation in NIR window. MoS2 nanosheet will be ultrasonically synthesized from bulk material with controlled nanosize and good photothermal property. Aim 2: Establishment of hybrid MOF/MoS2 nanoprobe for combinational photo treatment. The hybrid aptamer-MOF/MoS2 nanoprobe will be established with target-selective photo-activation and combinational photo-thermal and photo-oxygenation capability for Aβ aggregation. The photo-quenching/photo-activation efficiency with various molar ratio of aptamer-MOF and MoS2 nanosheet will be explored. Aim 3: Testing of the hybrid MOF/MoS2 nanoprobe for photo-treatment in cerebrospinal fluid. The synthesized hybrid nanoprobe will be evaluated for photo-stability and photo-treatment in cerebrospinal fluid under laser irradiation. The effect of hybrid nano-system on inhibition of Aβ monomer aggregation and disaggregation of Aβ fibrils under laser irradiation will be tested. The results will also be compared among hybrid MOF/MoS2 nanoprobes, MOF nanoparticle, and MoS2 nanosheet. Aim 4: Testing of the hybrid MOF/MoS2 nanoprobe in the in-vitro blood-brain barrier on-a-chip model. The blood-brain barrier on-a-chip in-vitro model will be established on a polymeric microfluidic chip to mimic the blood-central nervous system interface. The permeability of the hybrid nano-probe to across BBB will be tested in this chip model. Cell viability of neuron cells incubated with Aβ monomers/fibrils inside the chip model will be explored before and after laser treatment with hybrid nanosystem. The results will also be compared among hybrid MOF/MoS2 nanosystem, MOF nanoparticle, and MoS2 nanosheet.

15210818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210818.value: 阿爾茨海默病（AD）是導致癡呆的主要原因，全世界有超過4700萬例登記病例。越來越多的證據表明，AD的一個可能原因是將細胞外澱粉樣蛋白-β（Aβ）肽錯誤折疊成腦中具有β-折疊結構的神經毒性聚集體。因此，抑制Aβ聚集是AD治療的一種有希望的預防性治療方法。然而，大多數目前的抑製劑分子受制於抑制能力較弱，Aβ聚集體的弱解離能力，生理環境中容易降解，以及血腦屏障（BBB）的滲透性差等缺点。在針對Aβ聚集的新興治療方法中，由於其時間和空間可控性以及減少的副作用，光處理是一種有吸引力的選擇。發現通過近紅外激光（NIR）照射的光熱處理可以有效地解離Aβ聚集體，並且通過有機光敏劑的光氧化可以導致氧化的Aβ肽的聚集能力差。然而，光熱處理只能暫時抑制Aβ聚集，有機光敏劑的生物環境穩定性低，缺乏靶選擇性光激活能力。因此，開發新的組合光處理方法以同時抑制Aβ單體聚集和預先形成的Aβ聚集體的去穩定化具有高穩定性和良好的BBB滲透性是非常重要的。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種基於混合金屬 - 有機骨架（MOF）/二硫化鉬（MoS2）的組合光處理納米探針，用於有效抑制血腦屏障芯片中的Aβ聚集和神經毒性。這將是體外AD治療的組合光療的第一個試驗。由於納米尺寸和功能化，這種混合納米探針保留了紅色熒光成像，靶選擇性光激活和良好的BBB滲透性。利用MOF納米粒子作為成像探針和光敏劑，以及納米級MoS2片材作為光熱劑和光淬基底，建立混合納米探針。 MoS2納米片用Aβ聚集體靶向抗體功能化，用於靶向光熱解離。在Aβ單體存在下，Aβ單體和適體之間更強的結合親和力將從MoS2表面分離適體-MOF，導致MOF的熒光恢復和光活化，用於Aβ單體的靶向光氧化。基於上述機理，建立的混合MOF / MoS2納米探針將用於測試跨BBB屏障的滲透性，抑制Aβ抑制和神經毒性的功能在血腦屏障芯片體外模型中。該提出的混合納米探針可以是潛在的成像引導組合光療平台，具有優異的生物相容性和高穩定性，用於AD的靶向預防性治療方法。

15210818.label: Realisation of objectives
15210818.value: During the whole project period, all the 4 objectives have been realized. 1) MOF nanoparticles and MoS2 nanosheets were both successfully synthesized and characterized. MOF photosensitizing nanoparticles were synthesized by a hydrothermal approach with various photosensitizer linkers. Various MOF nanomaterials have been synthesized including MOF-525 nanodots, PCN-222 MOF nanoparticles and PCN-222 MOF nanosheets. The synthesis conditions were optimized to achieve controllable size, ultra-stable structure and good singlet oxygen generation in NIR window. The singlet oxygen generation capability of PCN-222 MOF nano-materials were characterized by singlet oxygen sensor green assay (SOSG), which showed good photodynamic properties under NIR 600 nm and 808 nm irradiation. MoS2 nanosheet was ultrasonically synthesized from bulk material with controlled nanosize and good photothermal property. Nanosized MoS2-PEG was synthesized by an ultrasonic exploration approach from bulk MoS2. After PEGlation and sonication, the size of MoS2 nanosheets could be reduced to tens of nanometers. The MoS2 nanosheets showed good absorption and photothermal properties in the NIR window. 2) Hybrid nanoprobe for combinational photothermal/photodynamic was synthesized. This hybrid nanoprobe was established with modified the brain-targeting peptide RVG with target-selective photo-activation and combinational photo-thermal and photo-oxygenation capability for Aβ aggregation. The N2 absorption/desorption spectrum demonstrated the good porous structure of hybrid nanoprobe, which was beneficial for molecular oxygen diffusion. The photothermal properties of the hybrid nanoprobe under NIR irradiation was demonstrated by the thermal camera imaging. The photothermally enhanced photo-oxygenation capabilities was demonstrated by MALDI-TOF MS spectra. 3) The hybrid MOF nanoprobe for photo-inhibition of Aβ in cerebrospinal fluid was successfully demonstrated. The synthesized hybrid nanoprobe was evaluated for photo-stability and photo-treatment in cerebrospinal fluid under laser irradiation. The effect of hybrid nano-system on inhibition of Aβ monomer aggregation and disaggregation of Aβ fibrils under laser irradiation was tested. A photothermally assisted photo-oxygenation treatment based on the hybrid nanoprbe could largely enhance the photo-inhibition effect on Aβ42 aggregation and lead to much lower neurotoxicity upon near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at 808 nm compared with a single modality of photo-treatment in both cell-free and in vitro experiments. Generally, local photothermal heat increases the instability of Aβ aggregates and keeps Aβ in the status of monomers, which facilitates the photo-oxygenation process of generating oxidized Aβ monomers with low aggregation capability. 4) The hybrid MOF nanoprobe for photo-inhibition of Aβ was demonstrated in a in-vitro blood-brain barrier on-a-chip model. The blood-brain barrier on-a-chip in-vitro model was established on a polymeric microfluidic chip to mimic the blood-central nervous system interface. This brain-on-a-chip was composed of two polymeric polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) compartments with channels separated by a thin and porous PET membrane. The membrane was sandwiched between two PDMS compartments. Brain endothelial phenotype HUVECs cells was co-cultured with astrocytes on the membrane to establish the BBB model. The permeability of the hybrid nano-probe to across BBB was tested in this chip model. The hybrid MOF nanoprobe showed an enhanced BBB permeability with RVG peptide modification. The hybrid nanoprobe has proven its good human BBB permeability in a microfluidic brain-on-a-chip model under a continuous flow that mimics the in vivo brain micro-environment of Alzheimer’s disease. Finally, the enhanced dissociation of Aβ plaques via NIR-stimulated hybrid nanoprobes was also observed in an ex vivo AD mouse model.

15210818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210818.value: We firstly explored the synthesis methods of Metal-organic-framework (MOF) nanomaterials. A new facile and environment-friendly hydrothermal synthesis process was developed to synthesize red-florescent MOF-525 nanodot. (Refer to Analyst, 2020,145, 797-804 in Part C, impact factor: 5.227). The synthesized MOF-525 nanodots showed good fluorescence properties and good water dispersion properties. We also synthesized PCN-222 MOF nanoparticles as dual-modal fluorescent/colorimetric “Signal-On” nanoprobe for phosphate detection in solution and cells for the first time. (Refer to ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 2020, 12, 26391−26398, in Part C, impact factor: 10.383). The present work would greatly extend the potential of nanostructured MOFs in the sensing and biological fields. We also developed MoS2-based hybrid nanoprobe based on aggregation-induced emission (AIE) effect and Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) for in situ detection of miR-125b biomarker in early Alzheimer's disease. (Refer to Biosensors & Bioelectronics, 2023, 230, 115270 in Part C, impact factor: 12.545). Our nanoprobes exhibited excellent imaging capabilities to aid real-time monitoring of the endogenous miR-125b in PC12 cells and brain tissues of mice AD model. This nanoprobe could be a promising tool for in situ and real-time monitoring of the AD-related microRNAs and also provide mechanistic insight into the early prognosis of AD. To establish the combination of MOF nanoprobes with microfluidic chip for cell-based study, we established a digital droplet microfluidic platform based on biofunctionalized 2D MOF nanosensor for detection of dual micoRNAs in single cells. (Refer to Small, 2022, 18(32), 2201779 in Part C, impact factor: 15.153). The fabricated MOF nanosensor-based microfluidic chip could be a promising platform for single cell-based study. Finally, we report a novel combinational photothermally assisted photo-oxygenation treatment based on a nano-platform of the brain-targeting peptide RVG conjugated with the 2D porphyrinic PCN−222 MOF and indocyanine green (PCN−222@ICG@RVG) with enhanced photo-inhibition in Alzheimer’s Aβ aggregation. (Refer to International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2022, 23(18), 10885 in Part C, impact factor: 6.208). In addition, combined with the brain-targeting peptide RVG, the PCN−222@ICG@RVG nanoprobe shows high permeability of the human blood–brain barrier (BBB) on a human brain-on-a-chip platform. The ex vivo study also demonstrates that NIR-activated PCN−222@ICG@RVG could efficiently dissemble Aβ plaques. Our work suggests that the combination of photothermal treatment with photo-oxygenation can synergistically enhance the inhibition of Aβ aggregation, which may boost NIR-based combinational phototherapy of AD in the future.

15210818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210818.value: The further development of nanoprobe-based combinational phototherapy for AD disease will not only based on amyloid beta aggregation mechanism but also other more promising mechanism such as Tau phosphorylation. New nanoprobes can be designed based on Tau phosphorylation mechanism to inhibit Tau phosphorylation process and reduce the related neurotoxicity. Moreover, imaging-guided nanoprobes can also be developed by integrating the multi-functions of diagnostics and therapy in one nanoplatform. The current study is based on NIR-I window laser treatment. The future study can be extended to NIR-II window with deeper penetration and low diffraction in brain.

15210818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210818.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia with over 47 million registered cases in the world. Accumulating evidence has suggested that one possible cause for AD is the misfolding of extracellular amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptide into neurotoxic aggregates with β-sheet-rich structures in the brain. Therefore, inhibiting Aβ aggregation is one promising preventative therapeutic approach for AD treatment. In this project, we propose a hybrid nanomaterials-based combinatorial photo-treatment nanoprobe for efficient suppression of Aβ aggregation and neurotoxicity in a blood-brain barrier on-a-chip. This hybrid nanoprobe preserves red fluorescence imaging, target-selective photo-activation, and good BBB permeability due to nanosize and functionalization. This will be the first trial of combinatorial photo-treatment for AD therapy in vitro. This proposed hybrid nanoprobe can be a potential imaging guided combinatorial photo-therapy platform with advantages of excellent biocompatibility and high stability for targeted preventative therapeutic approach for AD.

15211518.label: Realisation of objectives
15211518.value: As far as the project Objective I is concerned, the project team made a thorough and comprehensive comparison among the existing macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) models (Task I). The comparison involves three main MFD models: the accumulation-based model, the trip-based model, and the time delay model. The MFD model with time delay integrated state-dependent regional travel time function as an endogenous time-varying delay to describe the traffic dynamics within a region. Comparison with existing models shows that the MFD model with time delay provides a good approximation in both free-flow and saturation scenarios without violating strict causality. Thus, the time delay model is a promising alternative for dynamic network loading in large-scale network applications to consider departure time and route choices (Task I & II). Based on the multi-region MFD system with time delay, Object II incorporates network travel delay and route choice into the multi-region time delay MFD systems. Then the dynamic user equilibrium (DUE) and dynamic system optimum (DSO) models are proposed in Object III to support the MFD-based car-sharing vehicle relocation problem. The DUE problems with both inflow capacity and accumulation constraints were formulated using the DVI framework while the DSO problem was captured by a constrained optimal control framework. Inflow capacity constraints are imposed to prevent the network from over-saturation and thus the “gridlock”. The additional cost caused by the inflow capacity constraint can be regarded as the price to prevent the network from entering over-saturated conditions. Additional cost induced by the inflow capacity constraints can be regarded as the price to prevent the network from over-saturation and thus the “gridlock” while the dynamic marginal cost can be implemented as a hybrid incentivizing strategy that prices a portion of the peak time and subsidizes the rest (Task III&IV). Numerical schemes for calculating various dynamic external costs were proposed which provide some guidelines on dynamic road pricing design for network-wide access control. To alleviate the serious roadside pollution problem in congested urban areas, the project team introduced second-best road pricing schemes by imposing environmental capacity constraints for network traffic mixed with EVs and FVs and formulated as multiple vehicle-class user equilibrium problems with nonlinear environmental capacity constraints for both fixed demand and elastic demand cases. Both the tailpipe emission of FVs and the energy consumption of EVs are assumed to depend nonlinearly on network traffic conditions. Although the EVs do not contribute to the tailpipe emission, all vehicles contribute to congestion externality that induces more emission of FVs. Therefore, both types of vehicles are charged, but the toll on FVs is significantly higher than that on EVs. A new projected dynamics-based algorithm is introduced to solve the toll from the Lagrange multiplier associated with the environmental constraint apart from the equilibrium flow. Numerical examples indicate that the tolling schemes can efficiently suppress the FVs from accessing the protected area by charging them with the corresponding environmental externality while both the tolls imposed on FVs and EVs decrease with respect to the growing market penetration of EVs. With respect to Object IV, optimal relocation of idle vehicles to high-demand regions can enhance its efficiency, improving the quality of service and reducing the overall congestion of the whole network in the long run. Enforcing vehicle relocating with link-node representation or grid-based representation is hard to capture the interrelated dynamics with private vehicles in addition to its computationally intensive nature. Macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) provides a powerful tool to model those dynamics. Therefore, we propose a bi-level rebalancing scheme to maximize the served orders in the system. For the upper level (network -level), an MFD based bi-modal traffic flow model was developed in (Task IV) to consider the interrelated dynamics between private vehicles and car-sharing vehicles. It is solved using the Approximate Dynamic Programming (ADP) algorithm to determine the number of desired vehicles in each subregion and cross-border. For the lower level (i.e., vehicle-level), a Voronoi-based distributed coverage control algorithm is implemented by each vehicle to obtain position guidance efficiently. Simulation results based on Shenzhen, China, demonstrate that the proposed approach can serve more requests with less waiting time while reducing the overall congestion/externalities of the network. To support the data-driven adaptive vehicle relocation strategy in Task IV, the project team developed an integral reinforcement learning (IRL) approach to solving the optimal perimeter control and regional route guidance problems without requirement of any knowledge on the system dynamics, i.e., model-free. Perimeter control (maximizing the network traffic efficiency) and regional route guidance (homogenizing the traffic density distribution) are the most significant applications of the accumulation-based MFD in urban traffic control. Note that the urban traffic network is usually subject to uncertain time-varying traffic demand and MFD model error. Moreover, due to the unknown MFD system dynamics and the strong nonlinear relationship between the control inputs to the model (the dynamics model for solving the optimization problem) and the actual management policies implemented in the plant (the real-world/simulated traffic network to be controlled), one should take into account the dissimilarity between the model and the plant. The IRL approach stems from the adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) method, which gives rise to a promising solution to the complex MFD-based traffic management problem and the car-sharing vehicle relocation problem that are subject to the “curse of dimensionality”. The outcome of these studies can assist in the dynamic system optimum analysis of the MFD-based vehicle relocation system in Task III and the development of the bi-level data-driven adaptive vehicle relocation strategy in Task IV. To support the information prerequisite for real-time vehicle dispatching and relocation in Task V, the project team developed traffic state prediction methods from various traffic data. To be specific, short-term travel time prediction in multimodal transportation systems is essential for real-time vehicle dispatching while suffering from various sources of uncertainties. Noting that the quantification of uncertainty is vital for robust performance, this paper proposes two data-driven approaches based on the Functional Data Analysis (FDA) and Bayesian Support Vector Regression (BSVR) for short-term travel time prediction while anticipating various uncertainties. A probabilistic nested delay operator is used to capture spatial-temporal dynamic traffic conditions along the route. The skewness of dynamic journey time distribution is well captured. Journey time reliability analysis is then conducted using the skewness of dynamic journey time distribution. With respect to Object V, current literature usually bases the design of dispatching and relocation strategies on the time-independent traffic condition (speed) assumption to reduce the problem dimension while uncertain demand and travel time subject to traffic congestion can significantly affect the optimal solutions. Therefore, we first propose a network-level traffic state estimation algorithm using functional data analysis. Then a multi-stage decision model is proposed to address the matching and repositioning of a centralized car-sharing platform controlling a fleet of vehicles in Task V. Further, the customer spatial-temporal uncertainty is considered under the formulation of a stochastic programming problem. Then, an ADP based approach is developed for solving the multi-stage decisions efficiently. Our algorithm is evaluated in a designed simulator based on NYC yellow taxi data and the Manhattan Road network. Simulation results show that the total profit can be enhanced compared with traditional time-independent traffic assumption strategies and several decision strategies.

15211518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211518.value: Sharing service providers face strategic, tactical, and operational issues ranging from the decisions on the number of vehicles to acquire, price and distribution of service, parking location, allocation of vehicles, to relocation operations which enable the departure time and route assignments. Thus, optimization of vehicle dispatching and relocation can be formulated as generalized dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) problems while facing similar computational challenges with link-based representations. Macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD), describing the aggregate relationship between the network flow accumulation and the space-mean traffic variables at the network level, initiates a promising solution to the challenge of spatial dimensionality. To adapt the MFD framework to time-varying travel demand, this project modified the MFD to consider state-dependent travel delay and applied it to consider route choice into the multi-region trip-based MFD systems. Publication no. 7 identified that the MFD with time delay model provides a good approximation in both free-flow and saturation scenarios without violating strict causality. Thus, the time delay model is a promising alternative for dynamic network loading in large-scale network applications. With regard to different choice behavior assumptions, optimal control formulations for the MFD-based car-sharing vehicle relocation problem by dynamic user equilibrium (DUE) and dynamic system optimum (DSO) were developed and analyzed in Publication nos. 1, 2, and 4, respectively. An MFD-based bi-modal traffic flow model was developed in Publication no. 8 to consider the interrelated dynamics between private vehicles and car-sharing vehicles. And Publication no. 3 introduced second-best road pricing schemes to enable dynamic tolls to protect the network from congestion and pollution. Based on the adaptive dynamic programming approach developed by Publication nos. 6 and 10, a bi-level approach was proposed in Publication no. 8 to determine the number of rebalancing vehicles between regions, which can serve more passenger demand with less waiting time. To adapt to the dynamic travel times and spatial-temporal demand, Publication no. 9 adopted a functional data analysis algorithm from Publication no. 5 for short-term traffic state estimation and trained the proactive vehicle relocation algorithm under different demand scenarios. Experimental results using New York City yellow taxi data demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively improved the system's profit.

15211518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211518.value: Taxi is one of the main transport modes in Hong Kong and hence the operation of taxi fleets (e.g., ride-sourcing services) can significantly influence the traffic efficiency of the road network. Existing studies on taxi dispatching cannot capture the impact of taxis on normal traffic flows and the reverse relationship due to the heavy computational burden brought by the complex dynamic modeling. Few studies focus on optimizing the road network efficiency while improving the operation of taxi fleets. Therefore, a hierarchical framework that optimizes the matching rate of the ride-sourcing system and minimizes the total travel delay of the road network is desired to achieve collaboration optimization of network system performance and user experience. It may contain three parts: 1) a computationally efficient traffic model for complex network dynamics with private vehicles and taxis; 2) a hierarchical optimization framework for traffic management integrated with taxi fleet operation; 3) and a general simulation platform integrating dispatching of ride-sourcing services and route guidance of private vehicles. On top of the framework, an efficient traffic management system can be developed as the centralized transport operator to implement traffic flow control at a macroscopic level and disseminate personalized route guidance information to road users.

15211518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211518.value: The rise of shared mobility has transformed transportation services in Hong Kong. However, its effectiveness as an alternative to personal and public transport remains uncertain. Operators of vehicle sharing services face strategic, tactical, and operational issues ranging from asset ownership to distribution and relocation operations. To realise the vision of future shared mobility, this project is dedicated to the cost optimization of the service minimizing the relocation cost of vehicles to meet with demand. To tackle the challenge of modelling complexity, the project integrates both strategic and operational level decisions in a computation-efficient framework, macroscopic fundamental diagram. A data-efficient adaptive dynamic programming algorithm is developed to ease the heavy computational burden. The proposed framework enables the operator to utilize the price scheme or vehicle assignment to adjust or interact with demand such that the vehicle supply will be adjusted over time and space to satisfy the demand. The significance of this research project lies in its potential to provide a cost-effective and efficient alternative to traditional transportation methods, while promoting sustainability and reducing congestion.
