15211918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211918.value: The successful development of hypersonic vehicles is essential to the construction of next generation global transportation system, enabling air travel and freight at highly supersonic speed. When a vehicle travels at hypersonic speed, laminar-turbulent transition of boundary layer increases surface thermal heating and aerodynamic drag, posing a serious threat to its stability. This transition process is not completely understood yet, but the acoustic (second or Mack) mode is well known as the most significant incentive for boundary layers when free stream Mach number is larger than 4. Recent experiments have reported the delay of such acoustic mode transition with certain surface structures. However, no clear physics model is available to explain the mechanisms, and more importantly, to support the design optimization. To deal with such destructive acoustic mode, this proposed study aims at developing a guiding model for the design of broadband acoustic mode transition delay material for hypersonic vehicles, by introducing the theory of acoustic metasurface to the linear stability analysis of hypersonic flow. The unique capability of gradient index metasurface to slow down, trap and contain broadband acoustic waves will play a critical role in realizing turbulent boundary layer transition delay, for hypersonic vehicles travelling at speeds of different Mach numbers. This proposed study shall ultimately result in a methodology of prescriptive principles to correlate the profile of gradient index metasurface with the transition delay of specific acoustic mode, paving the way towards realizing the practical transition delay and stability control device. The proposed research will be implemented in three phases including: (1) Theoretical investigation on evolving the analytical and mathematics models of acoustic metasurface in the linear stability analysis of hypersonic flow, and adjusting the models’ parameters accordingly. (2) Numerical simulation and calculation to evaluate the acoustic wave trapping performance of designed gradient index acoustic metasurface under hypersonic flow. (3) Experimental measurement of fabricated acoustic metasurface samples and reference samples in the hypersonic Ludwieg tube. We plan to perform the measurements in various scenarios with different tube Mach numbers. It is expected that this project can achieve two accomplishments. First, the analytical acoustic metasurface model will help to explain the fundamental physics behind current transition delay method with porous coating. Second, the new broadband gradient index acoustic metasurface design that can provide a universal solution to control the Mack mode: one design suitable for vehicles traveling at different hypersonic speeds. 高超音速飛行體的成功開發對於下一代全球運輸系統的建設至關重要，可以使航空旅行和空運以高超音速進行。當飛行體以高超音速飛行時，邊界層的層流 - 湍流過渡增加了表面熱和氣動阻力，對其穩定性構成嚴重威脅。目前整個過程中發生的事情尚未完全被理解，但當自由流馬赫數大於4時，聲學（第二或Mack）模式是眾所周知的邊界層最重要的激勵模式。近幾年的實驗已經證實:用某些表面結構延遲這種聲模式轉變。但是，沒有明確的物理模型可用於解釋機制，更重要的是，支持設計優化。 本研究旨在通過將聲學超構表面理論引入高超聲速流動的線性穩定性分析，開發物理模型來指導高超聲速飛行體寬帶轉捩延遲材料的設計。對於以不同馬赫數的速度行進的高超聲速飛行體，梯度折射率聲學超構表面的減速，束縛寬帶聲波的獨特能力將對實現湍流邊界層轉捩延遲起到關鍵作用。該提議的研究最終將產生一種具有指導性的物理方法，將梯度折射率聲超構表面與特定聲學模式的轉捩延遲相關聯，為實現實際的轉捩延遲和穩定性控制裝置鋪平道路。 擬進行的研究將分三個階段進行：（1）在高超聲速流線性穩定性分析中演化聲學表面分析和數學模型的理論研究，並相應調整模型參數。 （2）高超聲速下評估梯度指數聲超構表面俘獲聲波性能的數值模擬與計算。 （3）高超聲速流環境下的實驗測量。製造的聲超構表面材料樣品將在高超聲速管中進行測試。我們計劃用不同的馬赫數來檢查各種情況下的性能。 預計該項目可以取得兩項成就。首先，經驗證的聲超構表面模型將有助於解釋當前具有多孔塗層的轉變延遲方法背後的基本物理。其次，新的寬帶梯度指數聲學表面設計可以提供控制Mack模式的通用解決方案：一種適用於以不同高超音速行駛的飛行體的設計。

15212418.label: Project Objectives
15212418.value: To develop an approach for sensitivity analyses involving spatially varying geotechnical parameters, and to identify influential zones in deep excavations that require additional soil sampling or instrumentation. System sensitivity functions will be developed for efficient evaluation of the predictive distribution of system response, and design charts will be established for optimal sample locations for typical shoring layouts. To extend the Bayesian updating framework to include effects of spatial correlation in geological profiles and geotechnical parameters. With this approach, the parameters characterising spatial variability can be updated based on inclinometer and settlement measurements as the excavation progresses. To incorporate model bias and temporal correlation factors into the updating procedure, accounting for the prediction discrepancies that cannot be attributed to geotechnical spatial variations. The individual proportions of the two elements provide indications on the relative influence due to geotechnical variability and other design conditions.

15212418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212418.value: In many geotechnical engineering projects, predictions of system performance at the design stage can deviate from actual site response during construction, due to various sources of geotechnical uncertainty. The observational method, initially proposed as a qualitative framework, emphasises the needs to incorporate new knowledge of site conditions as construction progresses and, if necessary, revise the original assumptions during the process. This is particularly important for deep excavation projects, which are often located at the city centres, where geotechnical failures can lead to catastrophic results. Meanwhile, the multiple stages of shoring installation offer opportunities for fine adjustments of the layout if such needs are revealed from the monitoring data. The Bayesian approach provides a quantitative framework by which initial assumptions on material property (prior probability) are updated to obtain the posterior probability, through observations made during construction. However, in most applications of the Bayesian approach, the spatial variability of geotechnical properties is not explicitly accounted for during the updating process. This is partly due to a lack of numerical tools for systematic analyses of spatial correlation features based on existing data from geotechnical investigation. The excessive computational demands associated with conditional random field modelling also exacerbate the difficulty of updating the posterior probability of spatially varying parameters. The proposed research aims to extend the existing Bayesian approach, taking into consideration the spatial variability of geotechnical parameters as an inherent source of model uncertainty. Recent findings on characterising and modelling spatially correlated fields will be incorporated into the prior distribution and likelihood function under the Bayesian framework. To enhance its efficiency, a high-accuracy surrogate modelling technique will be coupled with variance-based sensitivity indices to account for spatially correlated random variables representing the geotechnical properties. This will be utilised to identify the high-risk or sensitive zones pertaining to the unique features of soil-structure interaction in deep excavations. These zones can then be targeted for optimal instrumentation or soil sampling plans. The approach aims to maximise the value of instrumentation in deep excavations, where inclinometer or settlement measurement data can be utilised to update the subsurface spatial correlation structure as the construction progresses. The goal of the research is to ensure that ground investigation, instrumentation planning and interpretation of measurement data are properly assimilated into the design and construction phases of excavation projects, achieving synergy among the components, meanwhile adding value to facilitate the decision-making process. 在許多岩土工程項目中，由於各種岩土工程不確定性來源，在設計階段對系統性能的預測可能會偏離施工期間的實際現場狀況。因此，「岩土工程觀察法」強調在施工過程中透過實地監測納入新的岩土條件資料，並在必要時修改原設計中的假設。這框架對於深坑挖掘項目尤為重要，因為這些項目通常位於市中心地區，故工程事故可能導致災難性後果。故此，當監測數據與原來的設計評估出現重大偏差，便有必要適時調整支撐的設計與裝置。在概率與統計學上，貝葉斯方法提供了一個定量框架，可以此根據施工期間進行的觀察，更新工程物料特性的初始假設（先驗概率）以獲得後驗概率。然而，在以往的貝葉斯方法應用中，其更新過程一般沒有明確考慮岩土性質的空間變異及空關聯性。 部分原因是由於缺乏適當的數值模擬工具，用來對現有岩土數據及其空間關聯特性進行有系統的分析。另外，此類空間變化參數的分析亦往往需要龐大的計算量，增加了計算後驗概率的難度。 本研究項目旨在擴展現有的貝葉斯方法，並同時考慮岩土參數的空間變異性作為模型不確定性的來源。為提高計算效率，本項目將結合高精度代理模型及靈敏度指數分析，以識別基坑工程中的高風險或敏感區域，作為監測儀器或岩土採樣計劃的目標區域。此方法旨在提高深基坑工程中監測數據的實用價值，其中傾斜儀或沉降測量數據更可用於更新地下空間關聯結構的模擬。此研究的長遠目標是結合岩土磡探及現場監測的規劃，並適時將施工階段獲得的數據跟設計評估作比較，為工程決策提供重要資訊，並在需要時完善支撐設計。

15212418.label: Realisation of objectives
15212418.value: Objective 1 involves determination of geotechnical system sensitivity through a suite of new surrogate modelling techniques, and the use of quantitative sensitivity methods to determine system sensitivity of geotechnical problems. In this project, new and efficient probabilistic approaches have been established to evaluate propagation of geotechnical uncertainty to system response of deep excavation problems and other geotechnical problems including slopes and deep foundations. The new approaches include combination of the relevance vector machine (RVM), which is a machine learning approach, with polynomial chaos expansions (PCE), which is a surrogate modelling method in the publication by Pan, Leung & Hsu (2020). This proposed RVM-PCE approach is shown to be more effective in estimating response uncertainty and failure probabilities in geotechnical systems, compared with previous surrogate models. This is mainly because the existing surrogate methods, such as PCE, normally involved a large number of unknown coefficients to be determined through numerical analyses, while the RVM method is effective in the selection of the most important coefficients, rendering the surrogate model much simpler yet more accurate at the same time. Using this new RVM-PCE approach, the sensitivity and relative influence of each random input parameter (e.g. soil stiffness, soil strength and/or loading pattern) to the system response can be assessed effectively, as demonstrated in the said publication. Another new approach developed in this study is the extension of the variability response function (VRF) approach to nonlinear soil-structure interaction problems, which can be applied to foundation engineering or excavations, as demonstrated in the publication by Lo, Leung & Ku (2020). This VRF method is shown to be particularly useful for geotechnical engineering with spatially variable soils, because spatial variability parameters (e.g. scales of fluctuation) are very difficult to characterize with precision, due to limited information from geotechnical investigations. Therefore, previous attempts of geotechnical reliability assessment would involve various combinations of random field parameters to be analysed, which led to excessive computational demands, because for each set of parameters, hundreds to thousands of realizations would be involved through Monte Carlo-type methods. Using this extended VRF method developed in this research project, a single set of realizations becomes adequate for a reliability assessment for multiple sets of spatial correlation features. Therefore, this approach greatly reduces the computational demands for probabilistic analyses of geotechnical systems. These newly developed numerical methods are illustrated and validated for various geotechnical problems and geometry domains, including excavations (Lo and Leung, 2019), slopes (Mori et al., 2020), shallow and deep foundations (Lo, Leung and Ku, 2020) published under this research project. A set of design charts were also established for problems with spatially variable soils. To achieve Objective 2, this project developed an approach (Lo and Leung 2019) to utilize field measurements to update the parameters characterizing spatial variability of soil properties, leading to refined predictions for subsequent construction stages based on data from the preceding construction stages. It incorporates random field simulations and PCE modeling technique into the Bayesian updating framework, which updates the principal components that characterize the spatial variability features. With the updated variability features, the response predictions for the subsequent stages can be continuously refined as the construction progresses. Two deep excavation cases have been presented in various publications associated with this project, to illustrate the capabilities of the approach. Firstly, a hypothetical case shows that using separate 2D analysis models, the approach can capture the distortion phenomenon along the longitudinal direction of the retaining wall, which arises due to spatial variability of the soils in lateral directions. The second illustration involved an excavation case study in Hong Kong (Lo and Leung 2019), where the updating approach is able to envelop the measured deflection response and nearby ground settlements, considering site-specific data that reveal the variability features in soil properties. The two cases also revealed the merits and limitations of the stage correlation model for bias factor: while stage correlation improves the prediction accuracy when the excavation is conducted within a statistically homogeneous material, it is less effective when the excavation involves multiple soil layers with abruptly changing properties, as in the real case scenario. The approach can be useful for deep excavation projects where the observational method is to be adopted. For example, the key requirements from Eurocode 7 about the observational method include (i) definition of acceptable limits of the system behavior; (ii) assessment on the range of possible behavior, with an acceptable probability that the actual behaviour will be within acceptable limits; (iii) monitoring plan with frequent measurements so that contingency measures can be implemented if and when necessary; (iv) rapid response time for instruments and analyses of monitoring results; and (v) plans of contingency actions if the monitoring reveals behavior outside acceptable limits. With the analytical components developed in this study, the proposed approach can serve as a quantitative tool under the framework of the observational method, as the proposed Bayesian approach allows the probabilistic estimates to be progressively refined and updated through monitoring results such as inclinometer readings. For example, based on inclinometer reading at a certain stage, the prediction intervals of wall deflection at subsequent stages can be updated. The prediction intervals can be presented as mean estimate plus–minus one standard deviation, which corresponds to confidence interval of roughly 68%. These intervals provide quantitative indicators on the probability of system behavior exceeding certain limits. It would be a cause for concern, or warning sign, if field measurements exceed the prediction intervals, as this implies that some elements of uncertainty may not have been properly accounted for. These intervals can be rapidly evaluated using the proposed approach, to facilitate contingency measures if warning levels are reached. Objective 3 involves the incorporation of model bias, temporal correlation and other sources of prediction discrepancies in updating. The Bayesian approach described earlier in Objective 2 had incorporated model bias into the updating process (Lo and Leung 2018; 2019). It has been found that by incorporating model bias, and the spatial and temporal features of such bias, there is marked improvement in the prediction capabilities. The approach and findings from this study also reveal other aspects of uncertainty in site-specific applications that may lead to several additional sources of discrepancy between modelling and site measurements. One of these includes the statistical uncertainty in spatial variability parameters such as the scale of fluctuation in various directions. While the VRF approach is efficient for multiple combinations of spatial variability parameters, this technique also has the potential to be fully assimilated into the Bayesian approach. Currently, some ‘best estimates’ for scales of fluctuation were adopted prior to the Bayesian updating using site data. It is possible that further refinements can be made so that the site data is also utilized to provide insights into the spatial variability parameters themselves.

15212418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212418.value: This research project developed new probabilistic approaches to evaluate propagation of geotechnical uncertainty to system response of deep excavation and other geotechnical problems. One of those include combination of the relevance vector machine (RVM) with polynomial chaos expansions (PCE) by Pan, Leung & Hsu (2020). This proposed RVM-PCE approach is shown to be more effective in estimating response uncertainty and failure probabilities in geotechnical systems, as RVM facilitates selection of the most important coefficients, rendering the surrogate model simpler yet more accurate at the same time. Using this new RVM-PCE approach, the sensitivity and relative influence of each random input parameter (i.e. soil properties) to the system response can be assessed effectively. Another new probabilistic analysis approach developed in this study is the extension of the variability response function (VRF) approach to nonlinear soil-structure interaction problems, which can be applied to foundation engineering or excavations, as demonstrated in the publication by Lo, Leung & Ku (2020). The VRF method is shown to be particularly useful for geotechnical engineering with spatially variable soils, because spatial variability parameters (e.g. scales of fluctuation) are difficult to characterize with precision, due to limited information from geotechnical investigations. Using the extended VRF method developed in this research project, a single set of realizations becomes adequate for a reliability assessment for multiple sets of spatial correlation features, leading to a set of design charts and greatly reducing the computational demands for probabilistic analyses of geotechnical systems and parametric studies to determine the worst-case scale of fluctuation. The advances in surrogate modelling methods enabled this project to incorporate them into the Bayesian framework (Lo and Leung 2019), utilizing field measurements to update the parameters that characterize spatial variability of soil properties, and leading to refined predictions for subsequent construction stages based on data from earlier stages of the project. With the updated variability features, the response predictions for the subsequent stages can then be continuously refined as the construction progresses. With the analytical components developed in this study, the proposed approach can serve as a quantitative tool under the framework of the observational method, as the proposed Bayesian approach allows the probabilistic estimates of excavation system performance to be progressively refined and updated through monitoring results such as inclinometer or ground settlement readings. These advocates the implementation of observational method to ultimately result in a flexible design/construction cycle to ensure economical and safe underground infrastructure constructions.

15212418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212418.value: The project extends the Bayesian approach for updating of geomaterials properties and their spatial variability features, making use of common field measurements including inclinometer and ground settlement readings obtained during deep excavation projects. As practitioners are familiar with these monitoring techniques, the knowledge gap in the application, from the instrumentation point of view, is not large. On the other hand, distributed fibre optic sensing (DFOS) techniques open up new opportunities as they provide continuous measurements of strains and temperatures along the infrastructure that is being instrumented, which lead to much larger volume of response data at various stages of construction, and potentially enhanced effectiveness in probabilistic back analyses and Bayesian inference of subsurface geomaterials properties. The PI and research team are currently working with various government departments, developers and stakeholders to identify suitable excavation and foundation projects as testbeds for the use of DFOS techniques in health monitoring of the subsurface structure and Bayesian updating and refinement of system response using data obtained throughout construction phase. The advancements in Bayesian analysis techniques and field instrumentation aspects are expected to complement each other during the course of the infrastructure developments.

15212418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212418.value: Uncertainty and variability in geotechnical properties are known to be a significant source of risk in major infrastructure projects, especially those involving deep excavations. Despite advances in theories governing soil mechanics and geomaterial behaviour, predictions on the performance of excavations and retaining structures made at the design stage can deviate from measured site response during construction because of such uncertainty. This project establishes a numerical Bayesian analysis method that utilizes the response measurements during construction, such as ground movement and inclinometer readings of retaining walls, to refine estimates of geomaterial properties and their variability features, thereby reducing the uncertainty and enhancing the accuracy of performance predictions as construction progresses. The significance and strengths of the approach have been demonstrated through reanalyses of a deep excavation case study in Hong Kong, where the method is shown to be able to envelop the measured deflection response effectively as site-specific geotechnical data are progressively incorporated into the analyses. This can become a useful quantitative tool for practitioners, to ensure that ground investigation, instrumentation planning and interpretation of measurement data are assimilated into the design and construction phases of excavation projects, achieving synergy among the components, meanwhile adding value to the decision-making process.

15212518.label: Realisation of objectives
15212518.value: Ultra-precision machining of difficult-to-cut materials is a topic with important research and engineering values. Improving the machinability and machining quality of difficult-to-cut materials in ultra-precision machining is still a problem that needs to be solved. Therefore, this project develops a magnetic field-assisted machining strategy and successfully improves the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials in ultra-precision machining. For objective (1) of this project, two kinds of magnetic field systems were established for ultra-precision machining. The first system was developed with two sets of permanent magnets. The magnetic field intensity in the cutting zone was adjusted by changing the distance between the two permanent magnets or the magnetic properties of the magnets. The second system was developed by two electromagnets. By inputting voltages of varying amplitudes, the magnetic field intensity in the cutting zone was adjusted in real-time. The magnetic field intensity can change continuously from 0 T to 0.2 T, which lays the foundation for research on improving the machining performance of difficult-to-cut materials under different magnetic field strengths. Based on the developed magnetic field system, the effects of the magnetic field on the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials were investigated under different cutting conditions. The thermal conductivity of the workpiece with magnetic field assistance was analyzed directly or indirectly through the arrangement of particles in the workpiece and the chip morphology related to thermal melting, and it was found to be enhanced. The vibration of the cutting system affects the machined surface quality but is difficult to measure directly in ultra-precision machining. So, it was demonstrated through the eddy current damping effect and measurable cutting forces whose frequency components can reflect the vibration characteristics of the cutting system. The machining vibration was found to be mitigated. Through the cutting forces, chatter (i.e., a kind of self-excited vibration) was also proved to be suppressed with magnetic field assistance. Material recovery causes shape and accuracy errors. Its characteristics were measured through groove-cutting tests. Based on the above changes in characteristics of the material and the cutting system, tool wear during ultra-precision machining with magnetic field assistance was compared with that without magnetic field assistance, which was found to be reduced. In summary, magnetic field-induced changes in the thermal conductivity of the workpiece, machining vibration, material recovery, and tool wear under different cutting conditions were studied through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations (Objective (2)). According to the simulation results, experiments under various cutting conditions and magnetic field intensities from 0 T to 0.03 T were designed and carried out. During these processes, the cutting forces, the machined surface roughness and morphonology, the chip morphonology, and the tool wear were measured and recorded. The experimental results validated that the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials is improved by the developed magnetic field. The optimal magnetic field intensity is related to the material and the cutting parameters. But, under most cutting conditions, a magnetic field density of 0.02T is most conducive to improving the machining quality of the workpieces (Objective (3)). As a whole, all the objectives of the project have been fully achieved. Based on the research results, more than eight SCI papers have been published in international journals such as the Journal of Materials Processing Technology, Journal of Manufacturing Processes, Journal of Magnesium and Alloys, etc.

15212518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212518.value: Ultra-precision parts made of difficult-to-cut materials are widely used in fields such as national defense, medical care, and optics, placing higher requirements on ultra-precision machining. Thus, a magnetic field system for ultra-precision machining is developed to improve the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials in this project. The major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: (1) In this project, two kinds of magnetic field systems were developed for the assistance of ultra-precision machining of difficult-to-cut materials (Yip and To, 2019 (a)). Both magnetic field systems can be easily integrated into the machine tools. The magnetic field intensity in the cutting zone can be adjusted from 0 T to 0.2 T, which provides the most suitable assistance for the machining of different materials under varying cutting conditions. (2) This project studied the thermal conductivity of difficult-to-cut materials with magnetic field assistance. The experimental results showed that the thermal conductivity of the material is enhanced by forming the chained structures in the liquid state of melted materials in the ultra-precision machining process (Yip and To, 2019 (b)). In this way, surface damages induced by the brittle deformation are remarkably suppressed and the surface quality of both ductile and brittle deformation areas is enhanced. (3) This project studied the effect of magnetic fields on the vibration of the cutting system. Eddy current is generated in the rotating workpiece with magnetic field assistance, which applies a damping effect to the cutting system and reduces its vibration, thereby resulting in better surface quality (Yip and To, 2019 (c)). Self-excited vibration (i.e., chatter) can be also suppressed by the eddy current damping effect and the enhanced thermal conductivity, leading to stable and high-efficiency machining (Li et al., 2023). (4) This project studied the material recovery characteristics with and without magnetic field assistance. In the absence of a magnetic field, there is an error of almost 25% - 37% between the assigned and actual results for all form accuracy indicators of the machined surface of titanium alloys. After applying a magnetic field, these errors were reduced to less than 4% (Yip et al., 2021). (5) This project also studied the tool wear of ultra-precision machining of difficult-to-cut materials. With the help of the above-mentioned improved characteristics of the material and cutting system, damage to diamond tools caused by high cutting temperature and vibration is mitigated. Therefore, diamond tool life is significantly increased with magnetic field assistance (Khalil et al. 2022; Khalil et al. 2023). As a whole, the developed magnetic field system improves the machinability and surface quality of difficult-to-cut materials. Their mechanical properties after machining are also enhanced (Yip and To, 2019 (d)). These findings have been disseminated through publications in top international journals. More than eight SCI journal papers have been published.

15212518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212518.value: Ultra-precision machining of difficult-to-cut materials plays an increasingly important role in various important and high-value-added industries. However, the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials is limited by their characteristics such as low thermal conductivity, high material recovery, and so on. Thus, it is meaningful to develop the magnetic field system to improve the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials, which is also an environmentally friendly machining strategy. The magnetic field system developed in this project has significantly improved the machinability and surface quality of the titanium alloy, a representative of paramagnetic materials, in diamond turning. Based on its working mechanism, in the next, this system can be extended to nonmagnetic/anti-ferromagnetic materials, such as bulk metallic glass, to improve their machinability and machining accuracy. The magnetic field system can be also applied to other machining types, such as milling and grinding. In this way, various machining needs of different difficult-to-cut materials can be met. Artificial and functional surfaces are increasingly used in a range of modern industries. With the effectiveness of uplifting the machining performance and machinability of machined materials using a magnetic field, some micro-patterns are planned to be fabricated under the magnetic field to increase form accuracy and the precise level of the micro patterns. It is also a promising and executable strategy to combine magnetic fields with other auxiliary processing methods such as ultrasound and laser for ultra-precision machining to further improve the machining accuracy of difficult-to-cut materials.

15212518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212518.value: Ultra-precision parts made of difficult-to-cut materials are drawing ever-increasing attention due to their outstanding characteristics. However, the machinability of difficult-to-cut materials is usually limited by their mechanical properties. Therefore, this project proposes magnetic field systems to improve the machinability and surface quality of difficult-to-cut materials in ultra-precision machining. Using the magnetic field system developed in this project, the cutting heat is lowered by the enhanced thermal conductivity of the material; the recovery level of the material is decreased; and the vibration of the cutting system is also mitigated during the cutting process. All of these are conducive to improving the machinability and machining accuracy of difficult-to-cut materials in ultra-precision machining. Tool wear during this process is also reduced, thereby increasing tool life and reducing machining costs. This project not only provides an environmentally friendly processing strategy for ultra-precision machining of difficult-to-cut materials but also significantly improves their machining accuracy, and is conducive to promoting the development of ultra-precision machining and its upstream and downstream industries.

15212618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212618.value: This project seeks to control the divergence and convergence of light in an optofluidic waveguide using the laser-induced thermal lensing effect. It is motivated by the rising demand to manipulate the light in optofluidic systems, which is essential for many applications such as input/output coupling, optical switching and optofluidic laser/light sources. Previous studies on the optofluidic tunable lenses have obtained the in-plane beam shaping but they mostly rely on external flow pumps to adjust the fluidic geometry (e.g., size, volume ratio, curvature) or contents (e.g., fluid type, concentration), causing a slow response (~ 1 s). In contrast, this project will exploit a much faster mechanism – thermal lensing effect (tuning speed 10 us – 10 ms). It is accomplished by irradiating a continuous-wave pump laser onto a metal structure on the substrate of optofluidic waveguide. The metal absorbs the laser to heat up the moving fluid and thus generates a gradient-index lens. Pilot study using a straight chromium strip has shown that the divergent angle of the probe laser can be adjusted from 11.6 to 29.1 degrees, obtaining a change of 2.5 times. Another pilot study using a pair of straight metal strips has tuned the probe laser from collimation to different focusing states, with a minimum focal length of 1.4 mm. In the proposed effort, we will focus mainly on three tasks: (i) conceptual designs of the optofluidic devices and multiphysics models of the fluidic motion, thermal diffusion and optical transformation; (ii) device development for the basic diverging/focusing functions using simple straight metal strips; and (iii) advanced study of aberration-free diverging/focusing functions using complicated metal patterns. Compared with the prevailing optofluidic tunable lenses, the laser-induced thermal lens method possesses distinctive features. (1) The mechanism is unique. (2) The tuning speed is much faster than the other tunable lenses (10 ms versus 1 s). (3) Both the focal length and the steering direction can be tuned independently. (4) It allows the use of a homogeneous fluid rather than different fluids required by the tunable lenses. (5) The pump laser irradiation is remote and non-contact, and can be conveniently relocated to other points of interest. (6) The use of metal absorption significantly lowers the pump power. To the PI’s best knowledge, this is the first attempt to develop aberration-free thermal lenses in a running microflow. 本項目旨在利用激光誘導的熱透鏡效應來控制光流控波導中光的發散和會聚。隨著光流控技術的發展，越來越需要對光束進行精確操縱，這對於輸入/輸出耦合、光學切換和光流控激光/光源等許多應用至關重要。之前關於光流體可調透鏡的研究已經獲得了平面內光束成形，但它們主要依靠外部流量泵來調節流體幾何形狀（如尺寸、體積比、曲率）或內容物（如流體類型、濃度），從而導致反應速度比較緩慢（~1秒）。相比之下，本項目將利用一個更快的機制 ‒ 熱透鏡效應（響應速度10 us ‒ 10 ms），通過將連續泵浦激光照射到光流控波導基板上的金屬結構上，以加熱流動的液體，從而產生梯度折射率透鏡。在預驗實驗我們使用鍍鉻直條，將激光束的發散角可以從11.6度調整到29.1度，獲得2.5倍的變化。在另一個預研實驗中，我們使用一對金屬直條s實現將光束從准直狀態調節到不同的聚焦狀態，其最小焦距可達1.4 mm。 在本項目的工作中，我們將主要關註三個任務：（1）光流控裝置的概念設計和流體運動、熱擴散和光學變換的多物理場模型; （2）使用簡單的金屬直條實現基本發散/聚焦功能; （3）研究發散/聚焦狀態的像差。與現有的光流控可調透鏡相比，激光誘導熱透鏡方法具有其獨特性和優點：（1）機理獨特；（2）調節速度比其他可調透鏡快得多（10 ms對1 s）；（3）焦距和轉向方向都可以獨立調節；（4）允許使用均勻的流體而不是其它可調透鏡所需的不同流體；（5）泵浦激光照射實現遠程非接觸控制，易於重新定位到其他感興趣的工作點；（6）使用金屬吸收可以顯著降低泵功率。因此本項目具有工作機理的原創性，為需要進行光束精確調控的應用如微粒操控、液體光源等提供一個新技術。

15212618.label: Realisation of objectives
15212618.value: In relation to Objective 1, we have successfully developed a multiphysics model that includes the interactions of heat transfer, flow dynamics, refractive index distribution and optical fields by coupling the Fourier law, Navier-Stokes equation and ray tracing in 3D space. In relation to Objective 2, we have conducted numerical simulations of the laser beam field pattern under different conditions of chamber dimensions, flow velocity, liquid materials, irradiation laser power density. The results show that when the thickness of liquid layer is below 20 um, the convections of heat and flow in the vertical direction are negligible. This downgrades the 3D model into 2D model and significantly simplifies the optical analysis. In relation to Objective 3, we have designed an optical device that use a pair of chromium straight bars as the laser absorber and thus the heat source, and use the generated heat to form a gradient-index liquid waveguide for laser focusing. The liquid chamber has the dimensions of 3 mm x 500 um x 30 um (LxWxH). The liquid can be water, glycerol or ethylene glycol. The device has 3 layers, the top layer is a transparent glass slide, in the middle is a layer of microchamber that is fabricated by photolithographic patterning and mold transfer. The bottom layer has two Cr straight bars deposited on another glass slide. The three layers are bonded and sealed using NOA81 optical epoxy. We have used this pair of chromium straight lines to generate a gradient distribution of temperature and thus a refractive index gradient field, which in turn forms a thermal lens to focus the light in a controllable manner. Experiments show the build-up time of thermal lens is 200 ms, and the focal length is tuned from initially infinite to the minimum 1.3 mm. The thermal lens has one additional function of off-axis focusing by offsetting the pump laser spot. This is a new finding of this project. In addition, the fabrication process developed for this project has been applied to microfluidic reactors, which has produced 3 journal articles in Nature Communications, Micromachines, and Reaction Chemistry & Engineering, respectively. Particularly, the paper in Reaction Chemistry & Engineering is elected as the front cover. In relation to Objective 4, we have assembled a home-made optofluidic test platform that consists of a tube-shaped long-objective distance inspection microscope, two sets of high-precision syringe pumps, a fiber-pigtailed green laser (as probe light), a 980-nm fiber-coupled laser (as pump light), and a 5-dimension precision micropositioner. This platform has been used to characterize the field pattern of probe light under the irradiation of the pump light. Experiments have shown continuous tuning from biconcave to biconvex with the focal length from −0.5 mm to infinite to +0.5 mm. This part of work has produced 3 conference papers. Among them, once received Best Paper Award and another received Best Poster Award, both in The 9th International Multidisciplinary Conference on Optofluidics (IMCO2019) held in June 2019. In relation to Objective 5, we have presented a novel design of tunable in-plane liquid lenses that has no aberration by regulating local curvatures. Experiments using a silicone oil droplet demonstrate the tuning of focal length over 500–1400 μm and obtain a longitudinal spherical aberration (LSA) of ∼3.5 um, which is only 1/24 of the LSA (85 um) of the spherical lens. Fine adjustment allows even elimination of the LSA to no aberration. It is the first time that local curvature regulation is used to compensate for the aberration within one liquid lens. This part of work has directly produced 1 journal paper in Lab on a Chip. The related thin-film deposition technique has led to another journal paper in Optics Express. It produces 1 conference paper as well.

15212618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212618.value: Major findings: (1) We have developed a 2D theoretical multi-physical model. This is the first 2D model for in-plan thermal lenses. It was based on our previous model in the journal paper (“Q.M. Chen, Optofluidic tunable lenses using laser-induced thermal gradient, Lab on a Chip 16(1) 104 – 111, 2016,” not reported for this project) and further used in the journal paper in Lab on a Chip in 2020 (reported for this project). (2) We have conducted the multi-physical simulations using COMSOL and the ray tracing simulation using Zemax to study the focusing/diverging effects and the optical aberration. The results were presented in the journal paper in Lab on a Chip in 2020 (reported for this project). (3) We have fabricated a thermal lens that uses the laser light to illuminate a pair of chromium lines deposited in a microfluidic chamber to obtain the focusing/defocusing functions. This is the first design that generates a 2D refractive index gradient remotely for in-plane light manipulation. The results were reported in a conference paper in 2019 (reported for this project). (4) We have reported a reconfigurable optofluidic lens with two air–liquid (silicone oil) interfaces. It obtains continuous tuning from biconcave to biconvex with the focal length from −0.5 mm to infinite to +0.5 mm. Its wide tunability, low power consumption and easy operation make it suitable for light manipulation in microfluidic networks. The results were reported in 1 conference paper in 2019 (reported for this work). (5) We have presented a novel design of tunable in-plane liquid lenses that can compensate the spherical aberration by regulating local curvatures. It is the first design of aberration-free liquid lens. Experiments demonstrate the tuning of focal length over 500–1400 μm with a longitudinal spherical aberration of ∼3.5 um, only 1/24 of that of a spherical lens. Fine adjustment can obtain no aberration. This part of work has produced 1 journal paper in Lab on a Chip in 2020 (reported for this project). Research outputs: (1) Published 5 journal articles and 4 conference papers. (2) Obtained 1 Best Paper Award and 1 Best Poster Award. (3) Established close research collaborations with other institutions, for example, with Prof. Yu Weixing of Xi'an institute of Optics and Precision Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), and with Abdel El Abed of Université Paris-Saclay, France. The PI worked with Prof. Yu to obtain an NSFC/RGC joint project (N_PolyU511/20) and is collaborating with Prof. Abdel El Abed to apply for ANR/RGC joint project.

15212618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212618.value: Manipulation of light in optofluidic systems is essential for many applications such as input/output coupling, optical switching and optofluidic laser/light sources. Previous studies on the optofluidic tunable lenses have obtained the in-plane beam shaping, but they mostly rely on external flow pumps to adjust the fluidic geometry (e.g., size, volume ratio, curvature) or contents (e.g., fluid type, concentration), causing a slow response (~ 1 s). This project has presented a new design that controls the divergence and convergence of light in an optofluidic waveguide using the laser-induced thermal lensing effect. When a continuous-wave pump laser irradiates onto a metal structure on the substrate of optofluidic waveguide, the absorbed heat generates a gradient-index lens in the moving fluid. 15213118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213118.value: In bone fracture surgery, implants are commonly used for internal fixation to provide mechanical support and stability during the first few months of bone reunion. Current fixation implants are normally made of stainless steels and Ti-based alloys. Such implants might have to be removed by a second surgery after bone healing as the long-term presence of implant might cause undesirable problems. Active research has been pursued recently to develop biodegradable metallic implants which would degrade and disappear in vivo after bone reunion is completed, without removal surgery. Among many alloys, Magnesium(Mg)-alloy is the most promising because it has excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability and elastic modulus close to that of cortical bone. However, Mg-alloys normally have intermetallic phases dispersed in the Mg-matrix and galvanic corrosion occurs when the implant is in vivo. The high degradation rate of Mg-implant in vivo is the biggest hurdle to be overcome. In addition, an implant should have patient-specific 3-d profile and shape for best surgical outcomes. Laser additive manufacturing via selective laser melting (SLM), or commonly known as 3-d printing, is an ideal process for this purpose. Only a few researchers have started recently investigating SLM of Mg-alloys and identified major issues such as insufficient fusion of metal powders, vaporization of alloying elements, presence of large pores, thermal cracks and precipitation of large intermetallic phases. These are the results of poor understanding and process control during the laser-powder interaction and melt pool solidification. This project aims to solve these issues in three innovative steps. To start with, a most promising Mg-alloy, Mg-Zn-Mn, will be chosen based on publication results. Then, the effect of laser power, powder sizes, melting efficiency and melt track integrity will be correlated by monitoring the melt pool temperature (MPT) using a patented “On-line monitoring system for high speed laser spot welding” developed by the PI three years ago. The system can record the MPT profile with time of laser incidence and enable the optimum MPT and solidification time to be established. The second innovative step is to use a second laser beam to control the cooling rate and reduce the thermal stress and cracks. Thirdly, the SLM process will be carried out in a pressurized chamber containing Argon in order to achieve an isostatic effect for enhanced quality. Finally, the 3d-printed implants will be coated with Zn by electrodeposition in an ionic liquid followed by phosphating to enhance corrosion resistance and/or osseointegration.

15213118.label: Realisation of objectives
15213118.value: Achievement of Objective 1 and 2 Starting from magnesium alloy Mg-Zn-Zr (ZK60) powder ZK60 samples were prepared by selective laser melting (SLM). It is well known that laser processing of Mg alloy powder presents technical difficulties due to the high reactivity of Mg and thus a thorough investigation of the processing parameters is needed for fabricating SLM samples with good quality. The preparation of SLM ZK60 samples was thoroughly investigated via varying the laser processing parameters. Experimental results show that laser power and scan velocity played an important role in determining the quality of SLM ZK60. SLM ZK60 with minimal defects and high dimensional accuracy could be obtained at a laser power of 50 W and scanning velocity of 500–800 mm/s. The formation mechanisms of pores were also identified and illustrated thoroughly. A second trailing beam to slow down the cooling rate was attempted but the experiment was not successful due to the rapid scanning speed and multi-directional scanning direction of the first laser beam made the trailing mechanism of the second beam impractical. However, by optimising the process parameters of the main laser beam, high quality printed parts could be obtained. Achievement of Objective 3 and 4 It is a common practice to gauge the success of the SLM process by comparing the properties of the SLM samples with their cast counterpart. In this respect, the hardness of cast ZK60 and SLM ZK60 was 0.55 and 0.78 GPa, respectively, with similar elastic modulus. The corrosion resistance of the SLM ZK60 samples was studied using hydrogen evolution experiment and potentiodynamic polarization tests. SLM ZK60 exhibited a higher corrosion resistance in Hanks’ solution compared with cast ZK60 as indicated by a decrease of about 30% in hydrogen evolution rate and of about 50% in the corrosion current density. These results show that SLM ZK60 samples with good quality can be prepared with carefully chosen processing parameters. Owing to the high corrosion rate of Mg alloys in human body fluids, Mg implants are commonly surface treated by some methods to reduce the degradation rate and also to enhance bioactivity. In this project a series of calcium phosphate (CaP) coatings were synthesized on Mg alloy substrate via electrodeposition using different electrodeposition voltages. Zn coating was explored but it was found that Zn coating is not as bioactive as CaP. Electrochemical tests (both potentiodynamic test and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy) in Hanks’ solution showed that sample CaP-3.5V exhibited the best corrosion resistance, that is, a much lower corrosion current density, about 6 times lower than the Mg alloy substrate. Long-term immersion test also showed the formation of hydroxyapatite like precipitates on the CaP coated sample surface, indicating enhanced bioactivity. Besides degradation rate and bioactivity, implants are expected to process high biocompatibility for successful osseointegration. In this respect the biocompatibility of the printed surfaces was evaluated by in-vitro culturing of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) at different time points up to 96 h. The printed surfaces were found to be hospitable for MSCs, and healthy cell response was recorded throughout the 96-h culture periods. These findings can be instrumental in optimizing the surface features of SLM in order to improve cell response.

15213118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213118.value: The present project aims at fabricating Mg alloy implants for applications as degradable orthopaedic applications using selective laser melting (SLM), a popular laser additive manufacturing process. The major findings of the project are listed below: 1. The laser processing window, which describes the feasible combination of laser scanning speed and laser power for fabrication high quality SLM Mg samples, has been determined. [Publications 1 and 2] 2. As compared with the cast counterpart, the SLM samples has similar elastic modulus but with a higher hardness. SLM samples exhibited a higher corrosion resistance in Hanks’ solution as indicated by a decrease of about 30% in hydrogen evolution rate and of about 50% in the corrosion current density. [Publications 1 and 2] 3. Further enhancement in corrosion resistance and bioactivity could be achieved via electrodeposition of CaP coatings on the Mg sample as evidenced by the formation of hydroxyapatite-like precipitates in immersion tests. [Publication 3] 4. With proper selection of laser scanning strategy SLM samples were shown to be biocompatible as indicated by in vitro tests using mesenchymal stem cells response. [Publication 4] Coupled with the unique advantages of laser additive manufacturing, which includes the ability to tailor make implants to suit individual patients, the findings of the present project are bringing the realization of degradable orthopaedic implants a big step forward.

15213118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213118.value: The present project has addressed the feasibility of fabricating Mg implants by employing selective laser melting. The basic requirements for a degradable orthopaedic implant, namely, a reasonable corrosion rate, good bioactivity and biocompatibility, have been achieved. However, the mechanical behaviour of the SLM implants, has not been fully studied. Only the microhardness and elastic modulus have been studied in comparison with the cast counterpart. Future studies naturally should focus on the mechanical behaviour of the SLM parts, such as fatigue strength and corrosion fatigue, both of these important aspects have not been reported in the literature. Another issue which might cause trouble in the degradation of Mg implants is the formation of hydrogen. The effect of these hydrogen bubbles on the surrounding tissues has not been studied, even for animal models. Thus this is another research direction for the final realization of successful SLM Mg degradable implants.

15213118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213118.value: In surgical treatment of bone fracture, internal fixation implants are required for providing mechanical support during the bone reunion period. The current practice uses permanent metallic implants for fixation. Bone healing period is of the order of a few months and after that the presence of an implant is a nuisance. Thus, in some cases, a second surgery to remove the implant is required. This would incur extra risk and expenditure. It would be very attractive if one can design biodegradable implants that will disappear in the human body after bone healing is completed. In this respect Mg alloy is potential candidate as it is non-toxic, degradable, and biocompatible. The problem to tackle is to control the degradation rate. In addition, orthopaedic implants are tailor-made for individual patients. In this connection laser 3D printing would offer a feasible fabrication route. The present study has thoroughly investigated the processing parameters in selective laser melting (SLM), which is a laser 3d printing process, in fabricating Mg alloy samples. Results of mechanical, degradation and bioactivity tests show that the method proposed in the project exhibits a great potential for applications in implants.

15213218.label: Project Objectives
15213218.value: While the field of mean-field stochastic control has been well explored, little has been done to address problems with mixed state-control constraints. This research project aims to fill out this gap and investigate issues with practical relevance rooted in portfolio selection models. The first problem is a general optimal control problem for mean-field stochastic systems with mixed state-control constraints under random coefficients. We shall apply Ekeland's variational principle to derive a Pontryagin type stochastic maximum principle for this problem. The second problem is an optimal mean-field linear-quadratic optimal control problem with the linear dynamic system and the quadratic cost functional, in which mixed constraints follow linear inequalities. We plan to study this problem using coupled backward stochastic differential Riccati-like equations as well as the general results established in objective (2). The third problem is a dynamic portfolio selection problem involving a non-smooth cost functional with no-shorting, borrowing and terminal wealth constraints based on mean--semi-variance criteria. We plan to extend the findings obtained in objectives (2) and (3) to address this research question.

The second problem is an optimal mean-field linear-quadratic optimal control problem with the linear dynamic system and the quadratic cost functional, in which mixed constraints follow linear inequalities. The third problem is a dynamic portfolio selection problem involving a non-smooth cost functional with no-shorting, borrowing and terminal wealth constraints based on mean--semi-variance criteria. We plan to extend the findings obtained in objectives (2) and (3) to address this research question.

15213218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213218.value: 带混合約束的最優隨機控制問題在科學，工程，經濟學和金融投資的各個領域中不僅有意義而且非常重要。最近，人們越來越關注研究這类隨機控制問題及它們的應用問題。幾十年來，對於該領域的研究在標準隨機動力系統中已經得到了很好的發展。然而，在平均場隨機控制框架中，動力系統，代价泛函或兩者中都不僅涉及狀態而且涉及它的期望值 。引入平均場之后所产生的一些主要技术难题包含了导致动态规划方法失败的时间不一致性問題。本项目旨在解决带有随机系数及混合约束的这类难题，因为其理论和实际意义是否重要 。在本研究项目中，为克服上述問題中产生的困难，我们将发展一些新的方法，其与标准随机控制理论中的方法有相当大的不同 。此外，我们也会将理论结果应用于一些具有挑战性且实际相关的重要决策模型，比如金融投资中不可卖空，借贷限制和终端财富约束問題。该模型将帮助投资者更好地理解和有效管理风险资产，以便在有限的投资范围内实现更高的回报。

15213218.label: Realisation of objectives
15213218.value: This project mainly investigated a class of dynamic optimization problems featuring both stochastic control and mean-field stochastic systems with constraints over a finite/infinite time horizon. We developed new methodologies, which are significantly different from those in the existing literature's standard control theory. In our models, the inclusion of constraints introduces significant technical difficulties, including random coefficients, which lead to its theoretical significance and its practical importance. We considered a class of optimal investment problems with a nonsmooth and nonconcave utility function under mixed constraints, further developed the theory and presented the numerical examples (papers 1 and 12 in Part C). We proved that the value function is strictly increasing yet strictly concave in the wealth variable. In particular, comparing with the existing literature, the utility measures the difference between the control and its running maximum, and a nonnegativity constraint on consumption is imposed. Also, we studied indefinite stochastic mean-field linear-quadratic (LQ, for short) optimal control problems, which allow the weighting matrices for state and control in the cost functional to be indefinite (papers 2 and 11 in Part C). We developed two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games over an infinite horizon. The existence of an open-loop Nash equilibrium is characterized by the solvability of a system of mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations over an infinite horizon and the convexity of the cost functionals, and the closed-loop representation of an open-loop Nash equilibrium is given through the solution to a system of two coupled non-symmetric algebraic Riccati equations. The existence of a closed-loop Nash equilibrium is characterized by the solvability of a system of two coupled symmetric algebraic Riccati equations (paper 5 in Part C). Besides the above works, we studied the solvability of anticipated backward stochastic differential equations (ABSDEs, for short) with quadratic growth over a finite time horizon (paper 6 in Part C). ABSDE are path-dependent stochastic differential equations and a vital analysis tool when one deals with delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients. We further developed this theoretical result to tackle delayed control problems (papers 9 and 13 in Part C). We adopted a reinforcement learning (RL) method to solve infinite horizon continuous-time stochastic linear quadratic problems, where the drift and diffusion terms in the dynamics may depend on both the state and control. Based on the Bellman’s dynamic programming principle, we presented an online RL algorithm to attain optimal control with partial system information. This algorithm only requires local trajectory information, which significantly simplifies the calculation process (paper 2 in Part C) During this project period, we also investigated open-loop and weak closed-loop solvabilities of stochastic LQ optimal control problems of the Markovian regime-switching system (paper 4 in Part C). We provided an alternative characterization of the open-loop solvability of the LQ problem using a perturbation approach. Then we studied the weak closed-loop solvability of the LQ problem of the Markovian regime-switching system. In particular, we established the equivalence between the open-loop (closed-loop, resp.) solvability and the existence of an adapted solution to the corresponding forward-backward stochastic differential equation with constraint (paper 7 in Part C). The results obtained from our work are expected to help readers have a better understanding of stochastic LQ control based on the Markov chain model. In paper 9 in Part C, we analyzed optimal control and stabilization problems for continuous-time mean-field systems with input delay, which are the fundamental development of control and stabilization problems for mean-field systems. We established the necessary and sufficient solvability condition for this kind of optimal control problem with input delay, and derived the analytical form of an optimal controller through overcoming the obstacle that separation principle no longer holds for multiplicative-noise systems. In paper 13 in Part C, we studied partially-observed optimal control problems for the state governed by stochastic differential equation with delay. We developed a stochastic maximum principle for this kind of optimal control problems using a variational method and a filtering technique. Also, we established a sufficient condition without assumption of the concavity. Besides these, we also introduced the above methods to study continuous-time and discrete-time portfolio selection problems in financial investment (papers 3, 8, 10 and 14 in Part C). In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our research has important and practical significance. With the alarm bell's sounding and the ongoing financial crisis, risk hedging has attracted more attention than ever before. Among various hedging methods and managing risks, institutional investors prefer consumption cost, non-smooth utility, and mean-variance portfolio selections under stochastic systems. We performed a sensitivity analysis of the value function, the optimal consumption and portfolio on some model parameters, namely the reference degree parameter, the mean return and the volatility of the risky asset, and discussed some quantitative properties and their financial implications. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions.

15213218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213218.value: This project is to deal with stochastic control problems with constraints in many fields such as science, engineering, economics, management, and especially financial investment. We mainly revisited some challenging, yet practically important wealth management models over a finite/infinite time investment horizon, reformulated them as stochastic control problems with constraints, and derived their optimal analytical strategies. Also, we analyzed stochastic differential games over an infinite time horizon using coupled Riccati equations within a game-theoretic framework during this project period. Besides these, we further studied a class of anticipated backward stochastic differential equations with quadratic growth and developed this theoretical result to tackle delayed control problems. Although we did not project expenses for graduate student training in the original GRF proposal submitted to RGC in October 2017, our university appointed Miss Li Hongdan as a Research Assistant to work with us on this GRF-sponsored project in the period of 15 October 2019 – 15 April 2020. On or before 31 December 2019, she was a PhD student of Shandong University. She, together with us, published one paper on Automatica (paper 8 in Part C). On or after 1 January 2020, she obtained PhD degree and continued her research works with us. We also supported our PhD student Ms. Zhou Wenxin’s study (beyond normal period). On or after 1 November 2018, we use this GRF-sponsored project to support her study until she completed oral defense on 1 February 2019. She, together with us, studied optimal investment problems with nonsmooth and nonconcave utility over a finite time horizon (paper 12 in Part C). During this project period, I attended the 9th International Colloquium on BSDEs and Mean Field in Annecy, France from 26 June to 1 July 2022. This conference invited specialists from various universities, including those from Princeton University, University of California at Berkeley, University of Texas at Austin, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College, ETH Zurich, etc. Also, I served on the organizing committee of the 11th World Congress of Bachelier Finance Society and gave a talk in Hong Kong from 13 to 17 June 2022. In addition, I presented a keynote talk at 2019 SYSU Forum on Financial Engineering and Risk Management in Zhuhai from 9 to 10 November 2019. I attended Quantitative Finance – Workshop 1: Stochastic Control in Finance at NUS in Singapore from 22 to 26 July 2019. It provided a forum for researchers and practitioners to present and discuss on risk management and stochastic control so that I can communicate with peers about our research works. Besides these, I participated in SIAM Conference on Control and Its Applications and introduced our research works in Chengdu, China from 19 to 21 June 2019. In addition, we obtained 2018 Outstanding Achievement Award in Scientific Research for Institution of Higher Education (Second Prize) in January 15, 2019.

15213218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213218.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for constrained control problems under mean-field stochastic differential equations, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for standard and non-standard time-inconsistent problems within the more general stochastic system framework, such as path-dependent, delayed, and partially-observed stochastic differential equations. We will further study these potential research works in the future. [1] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze behavioral portfolio selection, while one encounters investment problem with reference to the historical consumption maximum over his/her investment time horizon. We will further develop those results established in papers 1 and 12 of Part C in the future. [2] Our methods developed in this project can be applied to two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games with random coefficients over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will further study the corresponding techniques in papers 4, 5, 7, 9 and 11 of Part C so that we solve the above problems. [3] Reinforcement learning method proposed in this project (paper 2 in Part C) can be further employed to study more general stochastic control problems over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will present the results in another project report after we complete it.

15213218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213218.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as optimal policy and consumption cost in portfolio selection (papers 1, 11 and 12 in Part C), mean-variance portfolio selection, fund management and agency theory (papers 3, 10 and 14 in Part C) within the multi-period framework. Specific to the literature on portfolio theory and investment, we expect the results to help shed light on the investment strategies on the basis of financial underlying assets over the investment time horizon (papers 1, 3, 10, 12 and 14 in Part C). In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve the optimal control studied and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic control constraints (papers 9, 11 and 13 in Part C) and under the regime-switching system (papers 4 and 7 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings provides a fundamental tool (paper 9 in Part C) to study a class of delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients in the future. We also studied two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games over an infinite horizon using open-loop and closed-loop Nash equilibria (paper 5 in Part C). Besides these, introducing reinforcement learning method paves the avenue for analyzing a class of optimal stochastic control problems (paper 2 in Part C). Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance, and it helps provide risk-management advice for policy makers and institutional investors.

15213318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213318.value: 物聯網（IoT）中設備和數據的增加促使研究人員將邊緣計算用於諸如智慧家居，智慧城市，工業物聯網等的新興應用。邊緣計算使計算能夠更接近數據來源。然而，僅僅將計算推送到邊緣設備是不夠的，許多物聯網應用還需要在不同設備之間進行協作和數據交換，從而導致了協作邊緣計算的出現。 我們提出了一種名為Edge Mesh的新型計算模型。該模型利用自組織網狀網路來支援終端設備的連接和邊緣設備之間的智慧決策。 Edge Mesh中的一個重要問題是如何有效地將應用程式內計算任務分配給邊緣設備。本專案中，我們研究了Edge Mesh中的數據感知任務分配（DATA）問題。該問題同時考慮了數據複製和數據傳輸對任務分配中的影響。在Edge Mesh中，數據在終端設備上動態生成，然後由邊緣設備上的計算任務處理。考慮到邊緣設備的異構容量，該問題將決定每個計算任務由哪些邊緣設備來執行，同時決定哪些邊緣設備複製數據，以及如何將有限的網路頻寬資源配置給任務之間，以及數據副本到任務之間的數據傳輸流。其目標是最小化任務完成時間或節省能量消耗。 據我們所知，之前尚未存在數據感知任務分配的研究工作。傳統的任務分配僅考慮計算任務的位置，在當今具有海量數據的物聯網應用中無法實現較好性能。我們提出的任務分配框架考慮到底層數據複製和數據傳輸。此外，我們還考慮了數據和網路動態特性，即設備和鏈路故障會隨時發生。數據感知、以及數據和網路動態特性使該問題比傳統任務分配更具挑戰性。 我們將通過聯合考慮任務分配與數據複製和數據傳對該問題建模，並開發有效的演算法來估計和預測動態協作邊緣計算環境中的網路和設備資源以及工作負載。 然後，我們將開發用於數據感知任務分配的新演算法，以解決數據和網路動態的挑戰。 該專案有助於推動邊緣計算的前沿研究，同時也將推動邊緣計算技術在諸如智慧家居、多機器人系統、車載網路和物聯網中的應用。

15213318.label: Realisation of objectives
15213318.value: We have finished the main objectives listed in the proposal. The first objective is to investigate the new requirements and challenges of designing a data-aware task allocation framework, and design its system models. We have comprehensively investigated and identified the main challenging issue of joint task and network flow scheduling for the data-aware task allocation problem. We have designed the system model of Edge Mesh as an abstraction of collaborative edge computing, where multiple edge devices collaborate by sharing data, computation, and other resources, and are managed by a centralized controller. Our research results for this objective are published in [J2019] [J2020c]. We have also investigated challenges for model learning in Edge AI with the Edge Mesh system model. We have proposed E-tree learning, a decentralized model learning framework for Edge AI [J2021]. The second objective is to design algorithms and mechanisms for the identified issues and evaluate the proposed solutions using theoretical analysis and simulations. We have studied four specific research problems. The first problem is the joint task and network flow scheduling in a collaborative edge computing environment while considering different application models of multiple dependent tasks [J2019] and multiple directed acyclic graph tasks [J2020c]. The second problem is the bandwidth allocation among multiple concurrent live VM migrations in edge clouds [J2020a]. The third one is the hybrid data dissemination problem in edge-assisted automated driving [J2020b]. The fourth problem is the reliability-aware dynamic service function chain scheduling in NFV-enabled 5G networks [C2021] [J2022c]. The details of the results on these problems are as follows: First, in terms of joint task and network flows scheduling in a collaborative edge computing, we have studied the problem under two different application models, i.e., multiple dependent tasks and multiple DAG tasks. For the dependent task model, we have studied the data-aware task allocation problem that considers each dependent task requires input data from multiple sources. This problem makes the decision on when and where each task is allocated, and the start time of data flows based on the placement of input data. We have mathematically formulated the problem as a mixed-integer non-linear programming problem with the objective of minimizing the average completion time of tasks. We have proposed a multi-stage greedy adjustment (MSGA) heuristic that considers both placements of tasks and start time of flows to make schedule adjustments for resolving network flow conflicts. Performance comparison done using simulation shows up to a 27% reduction in average completion time compared to benchmark solutions that do not make a joint decision. For the multiple DAG task model, we have studied the problem of multi-hop offloading of multiple DAG tasks generated at different edge devices at different release times with the objective of minimizing the average completion of all DAG tasks. Compared to existing task offloading problems, this problem makes the joint decision of task offloading, i.e., when and where each subtask within the DAG task is offloaded, and network flow scheduling, i.e., start time of flows. The problem is challenging to formulate and solve due to complex dependency among different decision variables. We have mathematically formulated the problem that is shown to be NP-hard. We have proposed a joint dependent task offloading and flow scheduling heuristic (JDOFH) that leverages the information of both parallelism and dependency within each DAG task to make a joint decision. Performance comparison using simulation experiments shows up to 85% reduction in the average completion time of tasks compared to benchmark solutions not making a joint decision. Second, in terms of resource allocation for multiple live VM migrations across edge clouds, we study the bandwidth allocation problem with the aim of maximizing the average QoS while meeting the deadline constraint of each VM migration task. Compared to existing works, this problem considers concurrent multiple VM migrations caused by the user mobility in edge clouds. We have formulated the problem as a non-linear programming problem that is shown to be NP-hard. We propose an initial solution for the transformed LP problem that is iteratively adjusted with the aim to with the aim of maximizing the increase of average QoS. Since the initial solution can affect the final results, we propose evolutionary algorithms including the genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) to find a good initial solution. Performance evaluation using extensive simulation experiments shows that our proposed solution can achieve both good QoS and fast convergence speed. Third, in terms of data dissemination among vehicles in the edge-assisted automated driving scenario, we study the hybrid data dissemination problem of determining when and which vehicle the data are injected into, and whether the vehicle acquires the demanded data directly from the edge or from nearby neighbors, with the aim of minimizing the traffic cost on the edge and meeting the deadlines of acquiring the data. We have proposed an offline algorithm for hybrid data dissemination (OFDD) that selects the V2V broadcasts by first making estimation and then choosing feasible V2I disseminations. Based on OFDD, we have also proposed two online algorithms, i.e., snapshot online data dissemination (SODD) and online data dissemination algorithm with ∆t-step (∆t-ONDD). Performance evaluations are done using simulation for the Tianhe District, Guangzhou, China using the real-world road map from the OpenStreetMap. The results show that our algorithms significantly outperform the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of data acquisition rate and traffic cost. Fourth, in terms of reliability-aware online scheduling in dynamic 5G networks, we study the service function chain (SFC) scheduling problem that includes deciding the redundancy, deployment, and redeployment of virtual network functions (VNF) in SFC on computation nodes with the objective of maximizing the number of SFC requests satisfying the latency and reliability constraints. The problem considers that SFC requests can arrive randomly following a certain distribution. We mathematically formulate the problem that is shown to be NP-hard by reducing it to a flexible job-shop scheduling problem. We propose a heuristic solution to first determine the redundancy of VNFs while minimizing delay. Then, we further propose a reinforcement learning solution to decide the placement of VNFs on computing nodes to maximize the success rate of SFC requests. Performance evaluation using simulations shows an increase in the success rate by 18.7% compared to the benchmark methods. The third objective is to build a prototype and develop applications to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed solutions. We have developed two different prototypes corresponding to two different application domains, i.e. distributed machine learning and multi-robot systems. For the distributed machine learning at the edge, we implement a novel hybrid testbed EdgeTB, which provides numerous emulated nodes to generate large-scale and network-flexible test environments while incorporating physical devices to guarantee fidelity [J2022a]. We have tested the efficacy of deploying different distributed machine learning solutions on EdgeTB including federated learning, gossip learning, and E-tree learning. We have also tested our proposed solution to optimize aggregation frequency for hierarchical model training in heterogeneous edge computing on EdgeTB [J2022b]. For the multi-robot system application domain, we have designed and implemented a middleware solution, GraphWare [J2022d], that uses a graph modeling approach to construct a logical graph of functions that are mapped to physical robots using an auction-based approach. GraphWare has been tested with a group of robots for performing different ball collection missions.
