15217018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217018.value: In [1], we developed an efficient linear programming (LP) decoding algorithm for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. In the proposed algorithm, the Euclidean projection onto the check polytope is eliminated. Complexity analysis showed that our proposed LP decoder in each iteration has a lower complexity than the state-of-the-art alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based LP decoders. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed LP decoder achieved better performance than other competing ADMM-based LP decoders in terms of decoding time. In [2], we have proposed a joint shuffled scheduling decoding algorithm to speed up the convergence speed of the DP-LDPC system. The algorithm can mitigate unequal convergence rate phenomenon, effectively reduce the number of iterations required for convergence, and hence lower the decoding complexity and power consumption. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves faster convergence speeds and better error performances in both the waterfall region and the error-floor region compared with the joint BP algorithm and the partial shuffled algorithm. Moreover, our proposed algorithm is applicable to other D-LDPC systems. In [3], we investigated the error-floor issue of DPLDPC codes. We proposed a GSP-EXIT algorithm for evaluating the source decoding threshold of DP-LDPC codes. With the GSP-EXIT algorithm, we optimized DP-LDPC code structures (with both regular or irregular source protomatrices) and achieved lower error floors. Our analytical findings were also validated by simulations results. Our study again shown dependency between error-floor levels and waterfall region performances of DP-LDPC codes. In [4], we implemented our JSCC encoder and decoder onto hardware. A 6-bit quantization scheme is adopted to make this JSCC system implementable. Two designs are included, which is software-simulated JSCC system using floating-point and FPGA-version one using 6-bit fixed-point. It is assumed that the coded bits are transmitted using binary-phase-shift- keying (BPSK) modulation. An additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with a region of noise power is applied to test Bit Error Rate (BER) and Frame Error Rate (FER) of two designs. Results show that the hardware error results are only slightly degraded compared with the floating-point results. In [5,6,7], we proposed a novel type of ultimate-Shannon-limit-approaching codes, namely protograph-based low-density parity-check Hadamard (PLDPC-Hadamard) codes. We extended and modified the aforementioned analytical techniques to investigate and optimize the performance of PLDPC-Hadamard codes. Simulation results show that PLDPC-Hadamard codes produce very good error performance even when very close to the ultimate Shannon limit. [1] Jing Bai, Yongchao Wang*, and F.C.M. 15217018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217018.value: The DP-LDPC codes for JSCC has a high potential to be applied in IoT devices, which can be regarded as electronic devices with simple sensors, low computing power and limited power supply. The use of DP-LDPC codes in such IoT devices can optimize the communication reliability and power consumption. To continue our investigation, we have submitted a follow-up General Research Fund in Oct. 2022. We propose to investigate a novel type of JSCC based on a generic protograph, and propose a unified framework to analyze all types of protograph-based JSCCs. With the new framework, the design of protograph-based JSCC is generalized and the error performance of different designs can be more readily compared and optimized. Moreover, the tradeoff between performance in the waterfall region and error floor is expected to improve. Second, we will extend the generic JSCC to other practical environments such as rate compatibility, coded modulation, spatial coupling, and iterative decoding. The ultimate goal of the new project is to design protograph-based JSCCs and the corresponding encoder/decoder architectures that are readily used in IoT devices/systems to store, transmit and protect source information more effectively and efficiently.

15217018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217018.value: This project investigates techniques that improve the reliability and efficiency of the data transmission. The main idea is to jointly consider the representation of data and the data protection mechanism. The techniques allow more efficient use of bandwidth as well as available power. They can be applied to small devices (e.g. IoT devices) that have limited computing power and power supply.

15217818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217818.value: 生物煉製是指利用生物質為原料製備增值產品，在過去十年中備受關注。生物基化學品可以取代傳統的石化產品，用作生產常見的消費品，如藥物、聚合物和生物燃料，以緩和以往煉油工業帶來的全球暖化等問題。生物煉製的重要性已得到全世界的認可，如歐洲和美國正積極實施國家級生物經濟策略，而中國和香港亦正引入相關的環境政策，可見全球生物基產品市場將會蓬勃地發展。因此，社會必須推進現有的科技，並重點研發可持續工藝技術，以實踐符合環境和社會效益的生物質精煉工業。 催化劑通常用於生物精煉以加速化學過程。常規的液體催化劑（例如無機酸）可導致設備的嚴重腐蝕並且難以循環再用，而固體催化劑（例如聚合物）可能需要復雜並且高成本的製備方法。考慮到欠缺環境和經濟友好的選擇，本項目提出使用生物質炭（如木材廢料和咖啡渣）為可再生原料製作催化劑，使用於兩種常見的生物精煉工藝 - 酸和鹼催化作用。生物質炭是通過熱解從生物質產生的碳質材料，可以透過不同化學改性來設計其性能。本項目將合成和定制分別負載酸和鹼的生物質炭催化劑，並對它們的催化效能作出評估。 為了識別生物質炭催化劑的有利特性，其表面化學對催化效率的影響具有研究的必要性。酸鹼量和酸鹼強度可能決定催化活性，而芳香性、疏水性、相鄰官能團和氧化物礦物可改變化學相互作用。此外，透過控制熱解和改性條件來改善孔結構，以提高活性位点的可達性及加快基質和產物的傳質。基質和產物的大小和分子結構，以及生物質炭催化劑的物理性質如孔徑分佈、總孔體積和孔形態，都可能影響吸咐過程與後其的催化作用。 本項目提倡利用可再生資源（即生物質炭）於催化劑製造和化學合成的新興應用，以實踐可持續生物煉製。研究結果將促進我們理解表面化學和孔隙結構對生物質炭催化劑性能的重要性，為研製高效能綠色催化劑奠定基礎。

15218518.label: Project Objectives
15218518.value: A general structure screening and design method of multi-PM-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors will be developed. At the first step, general topology models will be presented to describe machines’ structures. An optimization strategy will be developed. An analytical method will be first applied to check whether the design can output effective torque. Only the effective designs will be further optimized using finite-element method. A computer program for the implementation of the proposed screening and design method will be developed; then, the design process can be finished automatically. A database of machine topologies with their performances will be established and be automatically updated by running the developed computer program so the system has a self-learning ability. To validate the proposed methodology, an electric motor for direct drive in industrial robots will be designed and analyzed. It will have high torque density compared with those of conventional versions.

A computer program for the implementation of the proposed screening and design method will be developed; then, the design process can be finished automatically.
A database of machine topologies with their performances will be established and be automatically updated by running the developed computer program so the system has a self-learning ability.

To validate the proposed methodology, an electric motor for direct drive in industrial robots will be designed and analyzed. It will have high torque density compared with those of conventional versions.

15218518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218518.value: 電機在機電能量轉換中起著關鍵作用。在許多直驅應用中，如在工業機器人中，能夠以低速輸出高轉矩密度的電機，是十分令人期待的。然而，使用普通電磁材料增加轉矩密度並且不犧牲效率，是非常困難的。眾所周知，如果電流相同，氣隙中的強磁場會產生較大的電磁轉矩。永磁體可以在不消耗運行能量的情況下產生磁場，適當地在電機內部使用更多的永磁體是提高電機性能的有效途徑。另一方面，如果在不增加電樞繞組極對數的情況下磁場以較高的頻率交變，能量轉換將更有效。 基於這些思想，用於直接驅動工業機器人的雙永磁激勵電機已被研究。這些電機的轉子和定子上都裝有永磁體，它們比傳統的永磁同步電機具有更高的轉矩密度。但是，大家只嘗試了有限的極槽配合，可能會有其它更好的拓撲結構。我們也嘗試搜索不同的拓撲結構，但這種手動搜索和測試非常有限，因為它們嚴重依賴於研究人員的經驗並消耗太多時間。所以，如果這樣的人類探索、比較和選擇可以通過計算機程序來完成是特別令人期待的。在此項目中，我們將開發一種用計算機程序搜索可能結構的通用篩選方法。磁阻耦合的多永磁體激勵結構在更高的交變頻率下具有更強的磁場，因而具有優越的性能。首先，我們將提出通用拓撲模型(GTMs)來表示可能的結構。 GTMs中的不同設計標籤代表不同的電機結構。採用組合優化方法選擇GTMs中的設計標籤和設計參數，並使用諧波分析方法定性檢查是否可以產生有效的電磁轉矩，可以快速識別出具有不同極槽配合併可以產生有效轉矩的合理結構。然後，我們將開發一種基於概率模型的實用的多目標進化優化方法來改進設計。為了確定局部結構，我們將提出一種基於廣義多邊形的新型拓撲優化方法，該方法比傳統的拓撲優化方法快得多。所有這些方法都將在計算機程序中實現，所有篩选和設計都將在計算機中自動完成。與傳統的尺寸優化方法相比，該方法具有找到最佳或新穎結構的潛力。我們將建立一個動態數據庫，其中包含機器的現有拓撲結構及其性能。如果程序找到新的拓撲，它將自動添加到數據庫中，從而使系統具有自學習能力。如果系統運行時間越長，它將變得越有智能，越有效。 在我們的初步研究中，通過人工使用所提出的篩選方法，已經發現了幾種用於工業機器人中的低速直驅新型多永磁激勵磁阻耦合電機。例如，在一種新型的三重永磁激勵電動機中，轉子槽、定子槽和定子的內表面上都安裝有永磁體。有限元分析表明，在相同總體積和相同總損耗的條件下，與傳統的永磁同步電機相比，所提出的電機可以額外輸出199％的轉矩。

15218518.label: Realisation of objectives
15218518.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors has been developed to search for possible structures by a computer program for applications in low-speed direct drive. A proposed optimization method has also been implemented in the program to achieve full automation. Various structures are represented by general topology models (GTMs). The developed program automatically converts the data of GTMs to the finite-element method (FEM) input data. The performances of the effective GTMs verified by the analytical method are further analyzed and optimized computed using FEM. A self-learning database has been established and automatically updated by running the developed program. GTMs have been proposed to describe the geometric structures of possible typologies, which make it easy to implement different machines in computer programs. Not only the geometric structures but also the magnetomotive force (MMF) and magnetic reluctance of each object have been expressed. A series of classes in c++ computer programs have been developed to express the GTMs. The design indicators are adopted in GTMs. With different design indicators and design parameters in GTMs, the different structures of the machines are produced. A multi-stage optimization strategy has been developed. A harmonic analysis method is first applied to check whether the design can output effective torque with combinatorial optimization to select sample points. The effective designs are further optimized based on the multi-objective functions computed using FEM. Local topologies are further explored using our proposed topology optimization method. A database of existing structures with their performances has been established, and novel structures are automatically added to the database. A low-speed motor for the direct drive of industrial robots has been proposed based on the screening method. The performance, including torque density, losses, and efficiency of the proposed motor, has been well analyzed by FEM analysis. The prototype is manufactured and tested to validate the results. An experiment has been conducted to validate the performance of the proposed motor and compare it to the FEA results.

15218518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218518.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors is developed to search for possible structures by a computer program. In this program, different structures are presented by the GTMs. The proposed optimization method is implemented in the program as well. The analytical harmonic analysis is employed to verify the effectiveness of GTMs. The effective GTMs are analyzed and optimized based on the optimization method by using FEA. The advantages of this proposed method are summarized as follows (1) GTMs provide general expressions of machine structures which simplifies the implementation of the structure in the computer program. (2) The computation efficiency is improved due to the multi-stage optimization strategy. (3) The program can automatically offer possible designs and more unexpected novel structures are proposed. (4) The database is smart and effective since the system is dynamically updated with a self-learning ability. Several novel multi-PM-excited reluctance-coupled motors for a low-speed direct drive in industrial robots have been screened and proposed [1-6]. On the one hand, more PMs inside electric machines are properly applied with the assistance of the proposed program, which is an effective way to improve the performance of the machines [1, 2]. Three sets of PMs are applied in the proposed motor. The output torque improves by 100.3% compared to the conventional machine while the volume of the motor keeps the same. In addition, efficiency is also improved, which achieves as high as 94.5%[1]. On the other hand, the energy conversion efficiency of the proposed motor also improved due to the stronger magnetic field with higher alternating frequency [6]. The reluctance coupling method is well employed in machine structure so that the frequency increase of the coupled magnetic field for power generation does not lead to the increase of pole pairs of the windings. As a result, the electromagnetic performance of the machines utilizing this design principle can be significantly improved. All the proposed machines well validate the effectiveness of our proposed screening method. The topology optimization is also well investigated [3-5]. The optimization algorithm is coupled directly to the FEM analysis to achieve a completely automatic process. Various topologies can be obtained by changing the parameters. With the optimization program, asymmetric rotor structures with better performance are obtained [3,4]. A unique PM arrangement that utilizes an asymmetric Halbach array is also obtained [5]. The results show that with the topology optimization, the performance of the machines has notable improvement.

15218518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218518.value: Firstly, for the general screening method program, the computational efficiency can be further improved by using surrogate models. The multi-stage optimization strategy is a key part of the currently proposed method, which involves numerous FEM analyses to analyze motor performance. The computing time is highly affected by the mesh quality in the FEM analysis. On the one hand, good mesh quality can produce a more accurate result. However, the whole process is time-consuming. On the other hand, if the mesh quality is reduced, the computing time can be shortened. Nonetheless, the accuracy of the result will be influenced. The surrogate model can improve the computing time and keep the accuracy simultaneously. The well-trained surrogate model can produce accurate results in a short time. Secondly, the scope of the general screening method program can be extended. Nowadays, the demand for electric machines with high rotation speeds is huge. Similar to the employment of the proposed method in low-speed direct drive applications, the topologies, and design parameters are also required a comprehensive investigation in high-speed machines. Thus, the proposed method can be applied to high-speed machines and other motors with different operation statuses.

15218518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218518.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors has been developed to search for possible structures by a computer program for applications in low-speed direct drive. The proposed computer program highly improves the diversity and efficiency of different typologies designs. The full automatic program is realized by combining the screening and design method and the proposed topology optimization method. Additionally, the FEM is embedded in this program to calculate electromagnetic performance. Several novel structures have been proposed to showcase the effectiveness of this method. The performance of the proposed structure based on the screening method is investigated by simulation and validated by the prototype experiments. The torque density, ripple, losses, and efficiency are computed using the magnetic field computation of FEM. The results show that the proposed motor has an enhanced performance compared to the conventional designs, which further validates the practicability of the proposed method. The application of this research is not only limited to low-speed direct drive machines, but can also be extended to high-speed electric machines or other electromagnetic devices with minor modifications of the general screening method. In the future, the proposed method can be further developed by continuously updating the database to include more application situations.

15218918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218918.value: This project proposes to investigate the cross-section capacity of fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow section stub columns under monotonic compression and combined compression and bending. This structural component is fabricated from high strength steel plates. The high strength steel plates are first cold-formed to shape different geometries and dimensions and then are welded together through robotic welding machine to form a user defined shape. The application of this type of high strength steel fabricated tubular cross-section has offered versatility for architects and engineers to fabricate different geometries that can suit their design and engineering purposes. In addition, the multiple flat surfaces of the polygonal shape can also facilitate the connections with the in-coming members. The potential to have concrete-in fill also enhance the loading carrying capacity with the beneficial effects to promote fast-track construction as the polygonal steel tube can eliminate the need of temporary formwork for concrete-casting. However, there are currently no design rules to characterise the cross-section behaviour of such fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow sections. Therefore, this project targets firstly the characterization of cross-section resistance under axial compression with an aim to developing the cross-section slenderness parameters and limits and, secondly, the examination of the behaviour of the fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow sections under combined compression and bending at cross-section level. Both experimental and numerical investigations will be conducted to advance the current understanding on the behaviour of these high strength steel component. Such output is of extreme relevance for the structural engineering community to exploit the use of high strength steel materials. 本項目計劃研究高强鋼冷彎多邊形管截面短柱受單調壓力荷載及壓彎荷載下的承載力。短柱結構利用高强鋼板冷彎製成，在製作過程中，鋼板首先冷彎製成不同形狀及尺寸的單元，這些冷彎單元再使用機撲焊接工藝製成所需要的多邊形管狀結構。應用高强鋼冷彎多邊形管截面結構有助於建築師及工程師選用不同的結構形狀及尺寸以適應多樣的工程及設計需要。此外，多邊形管結構具有多個平面，使這類結構與其他結構較容易通過結點連接。多邊形管結構亦有前景用於構成鋼管混凝土結構以獲得更大承載力，并且將多邊形鋼管用作混凝土澆築外模可以實現快速施工的目的。然而針對高强鋼冷彎多邊形管截面局部穩定性的判斷和承載力預測尚未有設計方法。所以，此項目首先研究截面在軸壓荷載下的結構受力性能並提出截面徑厚比參數及局部失穩臨界值，然後研究高强鋼冷彎多邊形管截面在壓彎荷載下的結構受力性能。針對高强鋼冷彎多邊形管截面展開實驗及數值分析研究有助於瞭解此種結構在荷載下的承載力及局部穩定性，這些研究成果將對在工程領域使用高强鋼材料有極大幫助

15218918.label: Realisation of objectives
15218918.value: Objective 1 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations: An experimental investigation on the material properties variation and residual stress distribution within the high strength steel (HSS) hexagonal hollow sections was carried out in this project. Three different fabrication routes encompassing welding or combinations of welding and press-braking were used for fabricating the HSS hexagonal sections. HSS plates of grade Q690 with two thicknesses of 6 mm and 10 mm were employed. A new material model describing the material properties for the flat portion was proposed while the existing material model for cold-formed steel was modified for the materials at the press-braked corners. In addition, residual stresses measurements for five HSS hexagonal sections with different fabrication routes and varying section slenderness were subsequently performed. Based on the measurement results, predictive models for residual stresses were developed and can be applied to estimate residual stresses for predicting the structural behaviour of the HSS hexagonal hollow sections. Similarly, an experimental investigation on the material properties variation and residual stress distribution within the cold-formed high strength steel (HSS) irregular hexagonal hollow sections (IHexHS) with two different fabrication methods was conducted. The test specimens were manufactured through press-braking and gas metal arc welding (GMAW). Tensile coupons tests were conducted on specimens fabricated from the critical locations within cold-formed HSS irregular hexagonal hollow sections. New material models to predict the material properties for the tensile coupons with both rounded responses and yield plateau followed by significant strain hardening were proposed. Moreover, the residual stresses measurements for HSS IHexHS were also performed, membrane and bending residual stresses distributions on the investigated sections were measured in longitudinal directions. Based on the measurement results, predictive models for residual stress distribution were developed and can be subsequently applied for predicting structural behaviour of the cold-formed HSS IHexHS. Objective 2 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations. A comprehensive experimental investigation into the structural behaviour of the high strength steel (HSS) hexagonal hollow sections (HexHS) stub columns under concentric compression was conducted in this project. The HSS plates used to fabricate the specimen were delivered in Quenched and Tempered (QT) condition. The cross-section slenderness yield limits in the existing design codes of the EN 1993-1-12, ANSI/AISC 360-16, AS 4100 and ASCE/SEI 48-11 were compared and assessed against the experimental results. It was found that the current limits for internal compression plates in HSS rectangular and square sections cannot be extended to cover the cross-section classification for HSS HexHS. In terms of the cross-sectional resistance predictions, all the design codes tend to under-estimate the resistance of HSS HexHS under axial compression. For sections failed by local buckling prior to the attainment of yield load, the AS 4100 yields more accurate predictions compared with those predictions based on the other design codes. Compared with the design approach of Direct Strength Method (DSM), Continuous Strength Method (CSM) provides more consistent and satisfactorily predictions, particularly for stocky sections due to the consideration of strain hardening. In addition, comprehensive experimental investigations into the material properties and stub column behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel (HSS) irregular hexagonal hollow sections (IHexHS) are presented in this project. A series of HSS IHexHS stub column specimens were tested under axial compression and the cross-section classification from the existing structural steel design codes of EN 1993-1-12, ANSI/AISC 360-16, AS 4100, AISI S100-16 and design approaches of DSM and CSM were compared and assessed against the obtained results. It was found that the design provisions of cross-section classification in current design codes cannot be extended to the HSS IHexHS stub columns. Based on current codified yield slenderness limits, the strength predictions from design codes exhibit conservatism without the consideration of strain hardening and beneficial effect of element interaction whereas cross-sections with intermediate slenderness values were over-predicted. Furthermore, comprehensive experimental and numerical investigations into the structural behaviour of cold-formed high-strength steel (HSS) irregular octagonal hollow sections (IOctHS) were also conducted in this project. In conjunction with experimental tests on the stub columns, finite element (FE) models were developed to replicate the test results and failure modes. Afterwards, the validated FE models were employed to conduct parametric studies to supplement the experimental data. Cross-section slenderness limits set out in design codes such as EN 1993-1-1, ANSI/AISC 360-16, AS 4100 as well as ASCE/SEI 48, and design methods of DSM as well as CSM were evaluated against the experimental and numerical data. It was found that the current limits for internal compression plate elements of rectangular hollow sections set out in the design standards are not suitable for the design of cold-formed HSS IOctHS under compression load. Cross-section strength predictions obtained from EN 1993-1-12, ANSI/AISC 360-16, AS 4100, ASCE/SEI 48, DSM, CSM and modified design methods were also compared with the tests and numerical results. Relatively accurate predictions are provided by design codes. Non-conservative results are obtained from DSM and the CSM yields more consistent and precise results than DSM. The modified design approaches were also assessed and discussed. Objective 3 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations. Cross-section behaviour for cold-formed high strength steel (HSS) irregular hexagonal hollow section (IHexHS) stub columns under combined compression and bending was studied in this project. Finite element models were developed and validated using the existing experimental data collated from the previous research. Upon the validated finite element models, extensive parametric studies were subsequently carried out to generate more numerical data covering a wider range of parameters. The obtained numerical results were utilised to assess the accuracy and the applicability of the current design codes, such as Eurocode of EN 1993-1-12 (EC3) and the North American code of ANSI/AISC 360-16 (AISC) for cold-formed HSS IHexHS stub columns under combined loading. It was demonstrated that the existing design codes can be safely applied and can be extended for cold-formed HSS IHexHS stub columns design under combined loading. In cross-sectional resistance predictions, conservative results were provided from the existing design codes.The employment of CSM leads to improved accuracy in cross-sectional resistance prediction with updated end points in the interaction curve. More consistent and reliable predictions were revealed by carrying out reliability analysis in accordance with EN 1990. In addition, an experimental and numerical study on the octagonal high-strength steel tubular stub columns under combined compression and bending was conducted in this project. Octagonal high-strength steel tubular stub column specimens with different sizes were prepared. Experiments were performed on these specimens under concentric compression or eccentric compression, which induced various combinations of compression and bending on the structures. In addition, a numerical study through finite-element modelling was also conducted. A finite-element model was developed and validated to be capable of accurately replicating the experimental results. Subsequent parametric studies using the validated model were performed on the structures with a wide range of dimensions and under various combinations of compression and bending. Based on both experimental and parametric studies results, the applicability of existing design approaches in European and American Standards to the structures subject to combined compression and bending was evaluated. The evaluation results show that the design approaches from the standards, especially the compression and bending interaction relationship, provide conservative strength predictions and can be safely applied to the structures.

15218918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218918.value: Fabricated polygonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections from different fabrication routes, including welding and press-braking, were examined. Effect of welding and press-braking on the material properties were also investigated. Material models with due considerations on strength enhancements for fabricated polygonal shaped high strength steel hollow sections were proposed. A comprehensive experimental program was conducted to measure residual stresses to evaluate both the distributions and magnitudes of them. Simplified residual stress patterns for fabricated polygonal shaped high strength steel hollow section due to cold forming and welding are proposed. Detailed findings are summarized in Liu et al. (2022a, b, Part C-1,2). Experimental and numerical investigations were conducted on polygonal shaped S690 steel hollow section stub column specimens. A range of cross-sectional slenderness parameters and aspect ratios were carefully selected to examine their effect on the structural behavior. Experimental and numerical data including, load-deformation histories and failure modes were reported. Existing design approaches in European codes, North American standards were discussed and assessed against structural performance data. Based on the structural performance date, design provisions on the cross-section classification parameters and limits for fabricated S690 hexagonal and octagonal hollow sections with different aspect ratios as well as the design rules for the fabricated S690 hexagonal and octagonal hollow section stub columns under combined compression and bending are proposed. Detailed findings are summarized in Liu et al. (2022c, d, e, Part C-3,4,5) and Liu et al. [submitted with minor revision), Part C-6] and Fang et al. (2021, Part C-7).

15218918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218918.value: This research focuses on the cross-sectional behavior of cross-section capacity of fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow section stub columns. There is a potential to have concrete-in fill which can also enhance the loading carrying capacity with the beneficial effects to promote fast-track construction as the polygonal steel tube can eliminate the need of temporary formwork for concrete-casting. The corresponding design provisions can be further developed based on experimental and numerical investigations. To complement the reported research, specimens can be formed by using high strength steel plates together with high strength concrete with nominal compressive cylinder strength of 90 MPa. Polygonal shaped steel hollow sections can be fabricated by cold-forming steel plates into half-sections and subsequently welding half-sections together to form the target shapes. Concrete-filled steel tubular specimens will then be formed by in-filling high strength concrete. This future development has the potential to further contribute and facilitate the applications of high strength concrete-filled polygonal shaped steel hollow sections in construction.

15218918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218918.value: This project proposes to investigate the cross-section capacity of fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow section stub columns under monotonic compression and combined compression and bending. This structural component is fabricated from high strength steel plates. The high strength steel plates are first cold-formed to shape different geometries and dimensions and then are welded together to form a user defined shape. The application of this type of high strength steel fabricated tubular cross-section has offered versatility for architects and engineers to fabricate different geometries that can suit their design and engineering purposes. In addition, the multiple flat surfaces of the polygonal shape can also facilitate the connections with the in-coming members. However, there are currently no design rules to characterise the cross-section behaviour. Therefore, this project targets firstly the characterization of cross-section resistance under axial compression with an aim to developing the cross-section slenderness parameters and limits and, secondly, the examination of the behaviour of the fabricated high strength steel polygonal hollow sections under combined compression and bending at cross-section level. Both experimental and numerical investigations will be conducted. Such output is of extreme relevance for the structural engineering community to exploit the use of high strength steel materials.

15219018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219018.value: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have attracted much attention in the past decay because of their extraordinary properties such as the superior fracture toughness, ultra-high specific yield strength, excellent wear, fatigue and corrosion resistances. Those physical, mechanical and chemical properties of HEAs can be even effectively tuned by adjusting their compositions and microstructures. Although HEAs containing generic nanostructures have been developed to achieve superior mechanical properties, there is a lack of understanding on the deformation mechanisms in these novel multi-component alloys which are chemically disordered. In this proposed research, quasi-continuum simulations on dislocation plasticity are implemented to explore the deformation mechanisms in HEAs. The computer simulation is based on the modifications on the Frenkel-Kontorova model, which has been successfully employed to investigate the dislocation plasticity in atomistic scales in conventional alloys since 1939. In the simulation on the dislocation plasticity of HEAs, all essential parameters of the modified Frenkel-Kontorova model such as the periodic potential reliefs on the dislocation slip planes and the stiffness of interatomic bonds among the nearest-neighbor atoms are determined comprehensively from the first-principles calculations on the HEAs. The simulation approach developed in this proposed research is unique and robust in apprehending the relations between the macroscopic mechanical properties and the atomistic details of crystal structures and nanostructures in HEAs, which have not been well investigated by other theoretical or simulation methods available to date, e.g., ab inito molecular dynamics, classical molecular dynamics and constitutive modeling. Subsequently, it is employed to investigate the deformation mechanisms in nanostructured HEAs containing nano-sized secondary solid-solution phases or precipitates. The deformation mechanisms in nanostructured HAEs closely related with the dynamics of dislocation kinks and their interaction, multiplication and annihilation at the twin boundaries or interfaces of precipitates are systematically investigated. Besides providing an in-depth understanding on the temperature-dependent mechanical strength, the proposed research opens up further potentials to optimize the fatigue and creep behaviors of nanostructured HAEs, which could have tremendous value for their structural applications in nuclear, automotive, aerospace and military industries. More importantly, this proposed research bridges the gap of knowledge about the deformation mechanisms for multi-component alloys without long-range chemical ordering, and will make a significant contribution to the development of nonlinear models for the simulation of dislocation plasticity. 作為先進結構材料的高熵合金的設計和應用目前面臨著巨大的挑戰。其中一個關鍵問題在於高熵合金所固有的合金組份的無序性使得現有的位錯理論難以從原子尺度分析其塑性形變機制和機械性能。本研究專案利用結晶固體中位錯線的準連續模型即Frenkel-Kontorova模型，研究高熵合金的宏觀力學性能與微觀結構特性如化學組份無序性、晶格畸變等的關係。通過第一性原理計算確定高熵合金位錯滑移面內Frenkel-Kontorova模型的參量，基於此模擬位錯彎結與多組元合金原子的相互作用，從而研究高熵合金的塑性形變特性。本研究專案還模擬高熵合金中固有的第二相納米顆粒或析出物、孿晶、雙相複合片層等納米結構與位錯線的相互作用規律，從而為設計具有優異力學性能的高熵合金打下堅實的基礎。

15219018.label: Realisation of objectives
15219018.value: 1. To develop simulation approaches combining the Frenkel-Kontorova dislocation model and first-principles calculation on the chemically disordered crystal structures for the investigation of dislocation plasticity of HEAs, has been achieved by 100%. There are two steps in achieving this objective, as follows (a) Peierls potentials in (Ti, Zr)-based high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are determined by first-principles calculation. An orthorhombic supercell with lattice vectors aligned in the crystallographic directions of [-12-10], [10-10] and [0001] was used to model the hexagonal close-packed (HCP) HEAs. Special quasirandom structure technique implemented in Alloy Theoretic Automated Toolkit was used to simulate the HEAs with chemical disorder. First-principles computations were performed using the Vienna ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) codes. The slips of partial dislocations a/3[10-10] could lead to different deformation mechanisms, while in HEA the Burgers vector has to be determined by the energy landscape for dislocation motion on (0001) slip plane (the x-y plane), which is described by the garmma-surface and can be determined by fitting the energy change with the shear deformation at the slip plane. From the garmma-surface, the Burgers vector b_p for the partial dislocation can be determined. Therefore, the Peierls potentials Up(x,y) for dislocation motions in HEAs can be obtained. Consequently, Frenkel-Kontorova model can be applied to investigate the dislocation motion in HEAs. (b) Dislocation plasticity of HEAs is simulated by using Frenkel-Kontorova model. The simulation on dislocation kinetics at a slip plane is carried out by using a two-dimensional (2D) Frenkel-Kontorova kink dislocation model. The displacements of atoms located at the 2D hexagonal lattice sites (i, j) are denoted as u_ij=(u_i,j, v_i,j)a, which describe the positions of a dislocation line lying at the (0001) slip plane. The equations of motion of the dislocation line could be determined for the 2D hexagonal lattice. The Runge-Kutta method is used to solve the equations of motion, and periodic boundary conditions are applied at x- and y-directions. The activation of dislocation kinks and the motion of dislocation are simulated by acting forces of f=[-F/2, (3^1/2)F/2] on the dislocation line, which measure the applied shear stress on the slip plane. With the force F increased from 0, kinks are generated while parts of dislocation line may remain static or the kinks are at rest. It is no until F reaches a critical value Fcr that the whole dislocation line moves along f with a distant larger than bp=(3^1/2)a/3 or the kinks have moved across the slip plane. Therefore, by solving the equation of motion, Fcr can be determined for the HEA systems, which could measure the shear strength τy of the HEAs, respectively. 2. To elucidate the characteristics of dislocations and mechanisms of dislocation motions affected by the chemical disorder of HEAs under various thermal and mechanical activation conditions, has been achieved by 100%, respectively, by using the following simulation approaches. (a) The effects of chemical disorder on dislocation motions under thermal activation are studied by using Frenkel-Kontorova model at the mesoscopic scales. In the (Ti, Zr)-based HCP concentrated solid-solution alloys (CASs), i.e., TiZr, TiZrHf, TiZrHfSc, TiZrHfY and TiZrHfScY, the Peierls potentials Up(x,y) for dislocation motions are determined by first-principles calculations, respectively. The thermal activation condition is simulated by acting randoms forces on the dislocation lines, which are approximated by Gaussian white noises. By using Frenkel-Kontorova model, the equations of motion of the dislocation line are solved numerically in a 2D hexagonal lattice with as large as 50000*50000 sites. For the CSAs with various entropic values, the effects of temperature on profiles and velocities of kinks on the dislocation line are measured. (b) The characteristics of dislocations and deformation mechanisms in HEAs are analyzed by the generalized stacking fault energy (GSFE) and generalized planar fault energy (GPFE) curves as determined by first-principles calculation. The first-principles calculations are employed to determine the GSFE and GPFE curves, elucidating their phase stability and deformation mechanisms. Consequently, energy barriers for the formations of stacking faults, twin faults and face centered cubic (FCC) faults are determined from the curves, which are meaningful in analyzing the characteristics of dislocations and deformation mechanisms in HEAs. 3. To predict the temperature-dependent mechanical properties of HEAs containing nano-sized secondary solid-solution phases or precipitates, has been achieved by 100%. There are two steps in achieving this objective, as follows (a) A composite model containing AlCoCrFeNi bcc-HEA and fcc-Al is established for ab initio simulation at T=0 K. First, the lattice parameters for the b.c.c AlCoCrFeNi HEA and f.c.c Al are determined to be 2.89 ± 0.05 Å and 4.059 Å by first-principles calculation, respectively. In order to accommodate the lattice mismatch at the Al/AlCoCrFeNi interfaces, the (001)fcc-Al|(001)bcc-HEA interface that alignes along [110]fcc-Al/[100]bcc-HEA and [1–10]fcc-Al/[010]bcc-HEA, is built. Second, first-principles calculations are employed to investigate the interfacial behaviors and mechanical properties of the bcc-HEAs containing secondary fcc-Al phases at T=0 K. (b) The mechanical behaviors of the composite models at T=300-1200 K are simulated. The lattice parameters for the b.c.c AlCoCrFeNi HEA and f.c.c Al at T=300-1200 K are taken from previous experimental studies, which are used to build the HEA/Al composite model in ab initio simulations. After the equilibrium composite model systems are obtained, first-principles calculations are employed to investigate the interfacial behaviors and mechanical properties, reflecting the mechanical behaviors of the composite models at T=300-1200 K. Consequently, the temperature-dependent mechanical properties of bcc-HEAs containing secondary fcc-Al phase are predicted.

15219018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219018.value: (a) A multi-scale simulation approach combining first-principles calculations and Frenkel-Kontonova kink-dislocation model is employed to investigate dislocation plasticity of TiZr-based HCP CSAs. In the HEA formed through adding HCP elements in TiZrHf CSA, it is found that the dislocation mediated slip is promoted or reduced by the addition of Y or Sc, respectively, while it is significantly enhanced by the addition of Y and Sc. The mechanical properties of TiZr-based HCP CSAs are quantitatively predicted by the Frenkel-Kontorova kink-dislocation model, which are well consistent with experimental results. These findings are published in Research Outcome #6 in section 8. (b) The interfacial behaviors and mechanical properties of the composites containing AlCoCrFeNi bcc-HEA and fcc-Al are investigated by first-principles calculations. It is found that the stability of Al/HEA interfaces would be enhanced when the interfacial regions contain more Ni atoms or fewer Al atoms. In an Al-matrix composites (AMC), the introduction of HEA reinforcements would cause a loss of yield strength while leads to a much enhanced Young’s modulus and good plasticity of Al matrix as compared to those of pure aluminum. It is suggested the HEA-reinforced AMCs with enhanced mechanical properties could be developed for structural applications. These findings are published in Research Outcome #4 in section 8. (c) Short-range chemical and structural ordering related to oxygen interstitials in CrCoFeNi fcc-HEAs is studied by first-principles calculations. It is found that the octahedral sites with a high local concentration of Cr or low local concentration of Ni are energetically favorable for the insertion of interstitial oxygen. The influences of interstitial oxygen on the mechanical properties are found to depend on the content and the ordered structures of oxygen interstitials in HEAs. The yield strength is enhanced by about 26% with the addition of 0.926 at.% oxygen interstitials randomly distributed in HEAs, while it is reduced by about 14% with an oxygen content higher than 3 at.%. The HEAs containing ordered structures of interstitial oxygen could have improved yield strength when the ordered structures are formed with low formation energy, which resemble the rock salt crystal structure with a composition of (CrCoFeNi)O4. These findings are published in Research Outcome #1 in section 8. (d) The generalized planar fault energy curves are utilized to analyze the competition between the transformation and deformation twining in the HEA. It is found that the transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) could occur in CrCoFeNi HEA through the reversible HCP-to-FCC transformation under hydrostatic pressures or uniaxial tensions, which is enhanced in the regions with high or low local concentration of Co or Ni, respectively. These findings well explain on the TRIP in CrCoFeNi HEAs from an energetics perspective, and provide useful information on the effects of chemical disorder on dislocation activities in HEAs. The results reported in this work could facilitate the development of HEAs with structural transformation accommodated plasticity. These findings are published in Research Outcome #3 and #5 in section 8.

15219018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219018.value: In this project, dislocation plasticity has been successfully simulated by using Frenkel-Kontorova kink-dislocation model in (Ti,Zr)-based HEAs without magnetisms, which depends on the successfully determination of Peierls potentials by first-principles calculation. For magnetic HEAs such as CoCrFeNi HEA, it is suggested local magnetisms have to be considered in the construction of Peierls potentials for the dislocation model. However, in some magnetic HEAs, the magnetisms may affect the phase stability of HEAs. Hence, in further applying the computational approached developed in this project to simulate the mechanical properties of magnetic HEAs, before first-principles calculations are carrier out to determine the GPFE, GSFE and Peierls potentials, it is desirable to obtain the ground state or equilibrium crystal structure of the HEA at T=0 K by ab initio simulation.

15219018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219018.value: Multi-scale computational methods are developed in this project to investigate the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys. It is the first work that the simulation approach based on a mesoscopic kink-dislocation model is used to predict and design the high-entropy alloys with desirable mechanical properties. The mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys revealed from the simulation approaches combining the mesoscopic kink-dislocation model and quantum mechanics have extensive implications for the design of high-entropy alloys with high strength and excellent ductility and thermal stability. The research project paves a new avenue for the development of high-entropy alloys and high-entropy alloy based composites for structural applications.

15219318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219318.value: Urban regeneration programs in more and more Chinese cities have attempted to modernize their city fabric through “village-in-the-city (VIC)” clearance. Recently, VIC redevelopment has caused widespread social conflicts, as many redevelopment projects could not finish on schedule. These emerging conflicts point to the need for a refocused inquiry into an under-explored question. That is, why many VIC redevelopment projects were seriously delayed or suspended, despite strong policy support and the fact that the booming property market has created favourable conditions for their implementation. Existing studies on urban regeneration and VIC redevelopment primarily focus on the coalitions between the local state and private developers, but with little attention paid to the role of villagers. In this study, the Principal Investigator (PI) will treat villagers as collective actors equal in importance to others, and examine their actual influence on VIC redevelopment. In the past year, the PI conducted intensive research in 14 VICs of Guangzhou to investigate the processes and outcomes of their redevelopment projects. A key finding of her qualitative research is that an in-depth analysis of how villagers engage with their Shareholding Cooperatives (SCs) to make decisions in supporting or rejecting redevelopment is critical to explaining the power of villagers in VIC redevelopment. In this GRF project, the PI intends to extend the scope of the study to cover 57 VICs. Using sets of longitudinal and cross-sectional data gathered from 637 SCs in these VICs, the core of the study will combine qualitative analysis with quantitative modelling to examine (1) what factors are critical in influencing villager consensus on redevelopment and (2) how villager decisions affect the implementation progress of VIC redevelopment. By bringing the role of villagers back into the theorizing of the state-society relationships in VIC redevelopment, this study will develop a heuristic framework for analysing the institutional complexities (both formal and informal) of urban regeneration in China. The findings of this study will offer a solid foundation for the advancement of theories on urban development planning and governance. On the practical front, this study will offer insights, critical to redevelopment project management and policy review for a better balance of economic, social and political concerns in urban regeneration. As participatory urban development is not a theme unique to Guangzhou, the analytical framework and lessons drawn from this study are of relevance to other Chinese cities and beyond. 中國城市中越來越多的城市更新項目通過拆除“城中村”使城市面貌變得更加現代化。但是近年來，大量的城中村重建項目無法按期完工導致了越來越多的社會衝突。這些新型的衝突表明有些問題有待進一步的深入研究——城中村重建項目不僅有著強力的政策支持，而且近年來繁榮的房地產市場為其實施創造了良好條件，但為什麼如此多的項目卻嚴重延期甚至停工呢？已有相關研究主要聚焦于地方政府與開發商的勾結，卻很少關注村民在項目實施中的作用。 本研究將村民視為具有同等重要作用的集體行動者，並檢驗他們對城中村重建項目的實際影響。在過去的一年中，項目負責人已經在廣州市的14個城中村中開展了大量的田野調查，充分瞭解這些項目的進展與結果。項目負責人基於定性研究的重要發現是，深入分析村民如何與其股份合作社（SC）互動並做出支持或拒絕重建的決策，對於解釋村民在重建項目中的權力至關重要。在該GRF項目中，項目負責人希望擴大研究範圍，全面覆蓋廣州市的57個城中村，搜集並整理這些城中村中637個股份合作社的時間序列資料與橫截面資料，結合採用質性與量性研究方法回答本研究的核心問題：（1）哪些關鍵因素影響村民對重建項目達成一致？（2）村民的決策如何影響城中村重建項目的實施進度？ 通過將村民的角色納入到城中村重建項目中“國家——社會”關係的理論中，本研究將提出具有借鑒意義的研究框架用於分析中國城市更新中的制度複雜性（正式和非正式制度兩方面）。本研究的成果也將為城市規劃與治理的相關理論的發展與完善打下堅實的基礎。在實踐層面，本研究將為重建項目管理和政策審議提供重要見解，以更好地平衡城市更新中的經濟、社會和政治問題。隨著參與式城市發展被越來越多的城市所採用，這項研究的分析框架與經驗教訓總結對其他城市有借鑒價值。

15219318.label: Realisation of objectives
15219318.value: Project Objective #1 has been achieved. Four major categories of data relating to VIC redevelopment project were collected. They included locations, site areas, development scheme, and compensation arrangement. This database was collected through a number of channels. They included: (1) the Office of Three Categories of Old Areas (now the Urban Renewal Bureau); (2) Villagers’ Committees which show the redevelopment plans for public inspection; and (3) the Google Map and Baidu Map. Project Objective #2 has been achieved. A database of VICs and their SCs, including demographic features, socio-economic conditions and organizational structures, was assembled. This database was collected through a number of channels. They included: (1) the Platform of Village Information Disclosure which is an online system built by the Guangzhou Municipality for the public to oversee the operation of SCs and village governance; (2) the archival records kept by the Villagers’ Committees; and (3) the documentary sources such as government working papers, government policy notices, leader speeches, past development layout plans and aerial photographs. Moreover, the PI conducted more than 90 face-to-face interviews with local actors, including local officials, village cadres and villagers, to collect and clarify this database. Moreover, intensive field research was conducted in some of the villages to investigate how these local actors interacted on the ground to shape the process and outcome of their village redevelopment project. Project Objective #3 has been achieved. The PI identified the most important factor affecting villager consensus-building in redevelopment were identified. That is, the leadership of the village community. Conventional wisdoms suggested that a range of the related factors, such as the design of redevelopment scheme, compensation assessment, and compensation offers. In in this study, the PI found that the solidarity and cohesion of the villagers under a strong lineage leader was the key factor for the villagers to reach consensus and mobilize collective actions in the planning and implementation of VIC redevelopment. Project Objective #4 has been achieved. The PI found that villager decisions affected VIC redevelopment planning and implementation in two significant ways. First, if villagers were united to research collective decisions on project planning, compensation offers rehousing arrangement, they were able to have effective collaboration with the private developers, leading to the success of the redevelopment project. Second, if villagers were divided and failed to make collective decisions, private developers were often forced to retreat, and state interventions to provide strong political and financial support were necessary to “save” the project. Project Objective #5 has been achieved. The PI highlighted the following theoretical and practical implications of this study for urban planning and governance. (1) This study contributed to advancing the research methods for the studies of state-society power relations in urban regeneration. It illustrated how to bring the role of village community back into the theorizing of the state-society relationships in urban regeneration by the development of three heuristic frameworks, namely state-led model, community-led model, and market-led model, for analysing the institutional complexities (both formal and informal) of VIC redevelopment in urbanizing China. (2) This study contributed to advancing the existing theoretical debates on China’s urban regeneration through an empirical study of VIC redevelopment in Guangzhou. It argued that VIC redevelopment represented a neoliberal transformation of the local state, but by no means indicate a neoliberal paradigm shift from a “state-led” to a “market-led” approach in China’s urban regeneration. Existing scholarships on state–society relationship suggested that state control is the obstacle of urban China to embrace a neoliberal, market-led approach in its urban redevelopment programs; the government continued to dominate in development process, giving the market force a very limited space to grow. This study put forward an alternative argument: what really holds the reins of the shift of urban China to neoliberal growth is the power of the indigenous village communities. (3) This study offered new insights critical to redevelopment project management and policy review for a better balance of economic, social and political concerns in urban regeneration. It suggested that the state, communities, and markets are equally important in urban regeneration. They are complements but not substitutes. The effective participation of market players in urban redevelopment requires both policy support and community cooperation. However, in the real-life situations, not all communities have sufficient capacity to take up the duties of project planning and implementation. To this end, state intervention for community building is often necessary, as it can help produce a right power balance, that can benefit communities and preserve the effective contribution of market institutions under decentralization. As participatory urban development is not a theme unique to Guangzhou, the analytical framework and lessons drawn from this study are of relevance to other Chinese cities and beyond.

15219318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219318.value: As stated in Section 5.3, the key findings of this project addressed the power of village community, which has been under-explored by the existing studies on the state-society relations. The PI linked her research finding into a set of inter-related development planning issues, including urban-rural planning and governance for sustainable development, rural property rights reforms for social equities, participatory community planning for capacity building. Drawing from these findings, the PI has achieved the following three categories of outcomes: The first is publication of academic journal papers. Four papers have been published in top international academic journals, including (1) Journal of Planning and Education and Research, (2) Environment and Planning A: Economy and Space, (3) Journal of Urban History; (4) Land Use Policy. The PI served as both the first author and the corresponding author for all these papers. The copies of these papers are attached in Part C. The second is conference presentations. The PI made three presentations (including one keynote speech). The PI made a presentation about VIC redevelopment at the 15th International Congress of APSA in Seoul (22-23 August 2019) in the international conferences to discuss the implications of the findings of this project. The PI made another conference on rural property rights reform in 2019 Joint Forum for Land Use Policy - Urban-rural Coordinated Development and Land Use Policy (27 April 2019). The PI made a keynote speech related to the restructuring of state-community-market relationship in China’s urban regeneration at the International Conference on National Spatial Planning and Advanced Urban Development in Zhejiang (18-19 June 2022). The Invitation Letter and presentation PPT are attached in Part C. The presentation abstract and/or PPTs is attached in Part C. The third is organization of symposia/seminars on the topics related to this project with the aims of providing a platform for knowledge exchange. The PI organized three symposia in Renmin University of China, Nanjing University and University of Hong Kong Respective. Moreover, the PI organized one digital symposium and three webinar CIURG seminars. More details about these symposia/seminars are provided in Part C. They are also available at the website of the China Innovative Urban-rural Governance (GIURG) Research Network (http://ciurgpolyu.wixsite.com/home).

15219318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219318.value: How the public and the private sector can work together to make urban development not only economically viable, but also socially equitable, has presented a big challenge to many cities around the world. This project provided both new theoretical perspectives and methodological insights into studying the power of the community and the complexity of state-community-market relationships in China’s urban regeneration. It led the PI to succeed in the applications of two research projects as follows: (1) Ford Foundation Grant 2019: Community Development and Grassroots Governance for Urbanizing Villages: Case Studies, Best Practices and East-West Dialogue (Ford Foundation Grant No. 131778 ) (2) UGC Matching Grant Scheme: A Comparative Study of Indigenous Community Planning and Governance in Periurban Regions (Project ID: P0034814) Moreover, a new GRF proposal, which proposed to extend the geographical scope of the research on community and used a new research methodology, was prepared and submitted to the Research Grants Council in 2021. This new proposal should be able to complement the current one, which focused entirely and only on urban regeneration.

15219318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219318.value: Urban regeneration programs in many Chinese cities have attempted to modernize their city fabric through “village-in-the-city (VIC)” clearance. Recently, VIC redevelopment has caused widespread social conflicts, as many redevelopment projects could not finish on schedule. These emerging conflicts point to the need for a refocused inquiry into an under-explored question. That is, why many VIC redevelopment projects were seriously delayed or suspended, despite strong policy support and the fact that the booming property market has created favourable conditions for their implementation. Existing studies on urban regeneration and VIC redevelopment primarily focus on the coalitions between the local state and private developers, but with little attention paid to the role of villagers. By bringing the role of villagers back into the theorizing of the state-society relationships in VIC redevelopment, this study will develop a heuristic framework for analysing the institutional complexities (both formal and informal) of urban regeneration in China. As participatory urban development is not a theme unique to Guangzhou, the analytical framework and lessons drawn from this study are of relevance to other Chinese cities and beyond.

15220318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220318.value: Concrete filled steel tubes (CFSTs) are a popular form of columns and have also been widely used as the main arch ribs in arch bridges due to various advantages, including their good structural performance, ease of construction and athletically pleasing appearance. This project is proposed to develop a new sectional form for arches to improve their long-term durability and strength-to-weight ratio. In the proposed sectional form, an annular layer of concrete is sandwiched between an outer tube made of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) and an inner steel tube with a set of external T-section longitudinal stiffeners. The new sectional form differs from that of existing hybrid FRP-concrete-steel double-skin tubular members (DSTMs) previously proposed by the PI in the addition of large T-section stiffeners, which fulfil the following important roles with regard to the construction and performance of the arch: 1) substantially increase the section capacity of hybrid DSTMs; 2) enhance the composite action between the steel tube and the concrete as shear connectors; 3) provide additional restraints against the local buckling of the steel tube; 4) facilitate the placement of the FRP tube during construction and connection to hangars/spandrel columns. Arches with such a stiffened DSTM section are referred to as hybrid stiffened double-skin tubular arches (hybrid S-DSTAs or simply S-DSTAs). Such arches are superior to CFST arches in a number of aspects, including much better corrosion resistance and a much higher strength-to-weight ratio. The proposed project has the following objectives: (a) optimization of the stiffened steel tube section to prevent premature local buckling of the steel tube and to ensure full composite action between the steel tube and the concrete; (b) development of a reliable finite element (FE) approach employing beam-column elements for the nonlinear analysis of S-DSTAs to determine their load-carrying capacity; (c) development of a simple procedure for the design of S-DSTAs for both the construction and the service/operation stages. To achieve these objectives, a large experimental programme in combination with an in-depth theoretical programme will be carried out. The proposed project will lead to a new type of arches that is of higher performance, higher material efficiency and better construability than CFST arches. Substantial cost savings can be expected by replacing CFST arches with S-DSTAs in many applications. The project has special relevance to Hong Kong and the rest of China due to their huge demands for cost-effective and sustainable civil infrastructure. 鋼管混凝土（CFST）構件由於其結構性能優越、施工方便、外形美觀等優點，常被作為結構柱使用，同時也被廣泛應用於拱橋的主拱肋結構。本項目擬開發一種新型拱截面形式，以提高拱結構的耐久性及強度-自重比。該新型拱截面由複材（FRP）外管、帶“T”型加勁肋的鋼內管以及內外管之間的環形混凝土夾心層三部分組成。與本項目負責人此前提出的複材-混凝土-鋼雙壁空心構件（DSTM）的區別是，該新型截面在其鋼內管的外側（與混凝土接觸的一側）沿拱軸線方向增設了一系列大尺寸的“T”型加勁肋。這些加勁肋將對拱結構的施工工藝與整體受力性能起到重要作用：1）能夠顯著提高雙壁空心構件（DSTM）的截面承載力；2）能夠作為剪力連接件強化鋼管與混凝土之間的共同作用；3）為鋼內管的局部屈曲提供附加約束；4）可在施工過程中輔助複材外管的定位以及方便主拱肋與拱肩柱或吊杆等構件的連接。採用此類新型截面的拱結構（命名為雙壁空心加勁拱，S-DSTA），將在諸多方面優於鋼管混凝土（CFST）拱結構，例如具有更好的抗腐蝕性能和更高的強度-自重比。 本項目的目標為：（a）優化帶加勁肋的鋼內管截面，以防止鋼管過早出現局部屈曲，並確保鋼管與混凝土之間的共同作用；（b）為雙壁空心加勁拱（S-DSTA）建立可靠的梁-柱單元非線性有限元模型，預測其承載力；（c）建立一套簡易的方法，用於雙壁空心加勁拱（S-DSTA）施工和使用階段的設計。為此，本項目將對雙壁空心加勁拱（S-DSTA）進行大量的試驗研究與深入的理論研究。 本項目提出的雙壁空心加勁拱（S-DSTA）將比傳統鋼管混凝土（CFST）拱具有更優的結構性能、更高的材料利用率以及更簡易的施工過程。可以預期的是，採用該雙壁空心加勁拱（S-DSTA）替代鋼管混凝土（CFST）拱在許多情況下將顯著節約成本。由於中國香港及內地對造價經濟、可持續的基礎設施有巨大的需求，本項目對於這些地區有著尤其重要的意義。

15220318.label: Realisation of objectives
15220318.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed the two objectives. Realization of Objective 1: (1) Tensile tests were conducted on forty-two steel coupons cut from steel tubes and stiffeners. The tensile properties of the stiffened steel tubes with different manufacturing methods, stiffener shapes, and stiffener quantities were investigated. (2) The geometric imperfections of twenty-three unstiffened steel tubes and sixty stiffened steel tubes were measured. The effects of diameter-to-thickness ratio, manufacturing method, stiffener shape, and stiffener quantity on the geometric imperfections of the steel tubes were examined. (3) The residual stress distributions of five unstiffened steel tubes and eight stiffened steel tubes were measured. The effects of diameter-to-thickness ratio, manufacturing method, and stiffener quantity on the residual stresses of the steel tubes were examined. (4) Six unstiffened steel tubes and twenty-one stiffened steel tubes were tested under axial compression. The effects of diameter-to-thickness ratio, manufacturing method, and stiffener quantity on the buckling resistance of the steel tubes were investigated. (5) Ten double-skin tubular columns (DSTCs) and twenty-seven stiffened DSTCs (S-DSTCs) were tested under axial compression. The relative slips between concrete and steel tube in DSTCs were compared with those of the corresponding S-DSTCs. (6) The predictions based on Yu et al.’s (2010) model for FRP-confined concrete were compared with the test results of concentrically loaded DSTCs and S-DSTCs. (7) Three DSTCs and four S-DSTCs were tested under eccentric compression. The test results of these eccentrically loaded specimens were compared with the predictions based on existing stress-strain models for FRP-confined concrete. (8) The rupture failure process of FRP tube in a DSTC or S-DSTC is complex, but the prediction of this ultimate condition is important for understanding the behaviour of DSTCs or S-DSTCs. A numerical approach aimed at predicting this ultimate condition based on the lattice discrete particle model (LDPM) was studied. (9) An improved theoretical model for the axial compressive behaviour of concrete-filled FRP tubes with the nonlinear biaxial behaviour of the FRP tube duly taken into account was proposed. The proposed model led to more accurate predictions of test results than the existing ones in which the biaxial nonlinearity of the FRP tube was ignored. (10) A robust plasticity constitutive model has been developed for the modelling of FRP-confined non-circular concrete columns using ABAQUS, which can be applied to the modelling of S-DSTAs in this project. Realization of Objective 2: (1) Five DSTAs of 3.6 m in span were fabricated and tested under three- or four-point loading. The effects of eccentricity of the steel tube position in the section, thickness of the FRP tube, and diameter of steel tube on the behaviour of DSTAs were investigated. A numerical model was also developed in OpenSees to predict the behaviour of DSTAs. (2) The design procedure of DSTAs based on existing design codes and the research outcomes of this project was established in connection with the design of two pedestrian deck arch bridges. (3) A comparative study was conducted on the structural and economic performance of a DSTA versus that of a steel tubular arch (STA) and a concrete-filled steel tubular arch (CFSTA). (4) A parametric study was conducted with an emphasis on the effects of FRP tube thickness and stiffeners on the structural and economic performance of DSTAs. A PhD student, Mr. Wei Xiong, has been trained in this research project. He started his PhD study program on 31/08/2018 and submitted his PhD thesis to The Hong Kong Polytechnic University on 30/11/2023. The title of his Ph.D. thesis is: FRP-concrete-steel tubular columns and arches with a stiffened steel tube. Reference: Yu, T., Teng, J.G. & Wong, Y.L. (2010). Stress-strain behavior of concrete in hybrid double-skin tubular columns. Journal of Structural Engineering, ASCE. Vol. 136(4), pp.379-389.

15220318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220318.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: (1) DSTCs and S-DSTCs with steel tubes of relatively large diameter-to-thickness ratios were more likely to exhibit serious buckling deformation of the inner steel tube prior to the rupture of FRP tube. (2) The stiffeners, which served as the shear connectors between the concrete and the steel tube, could effectively suppress the slips between the concrete and the steel tube in a S-DSTC. (3) The stiffeners could enhance the buckling resistance of the steel tube, and provide extra confinement for the concrete annulus, and improve the load-carrying capacity of a DSTC. (4) The comparisons between test results and predictions for the concentrically- and eccentrically-loaded S-DSTCs revealed that the consideration of steel tube buckling and stiffener confinement effect are necessary for achieving more accurate predictions. Findings Related to Objective 2: (1) All the DSTA test specimens showed a ductile behaviour. DSTAs were found to provide a significantly higher ultimate load than corresponding reinforced concrete arches of a similar cross-section. (2) DSTAs possessed structural performance significantly better than the corresponding STAs and CFSTAs with the same quantity of steel or steel and concrete. (3) The load-carrying capacity of a DSTA at the ULS was enhanced by the inclusion of T-shaped stiffeners. A sufficiently large thickness of the FRP tube was critical for providing necessary ductility for the annular concrete layer; such an FRP tube ensured the composite action between the concrete and the steel tube, but further increasing the thickness of the FRP tube had a marginal effect on the load carrying capacity.

15220318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220318.value: More research is needed on the numerical simulation of concentrically- and eccentrically-loaded stiffened steel tubes, and the behaviour of concentrically- and eccentrically-loaded DSTCs and S-DSTCs. Based on results from such studies, together with the existing results, the respective effects of FRP confinement stiffness ratio, void ratio, diameter-to-thickness ratio of steel tube, and confinement provided by stiffeners could then be better identified and a more robust and accurate stress-strain model for confined concrete in S-DSTCs could next be developed. More research is also needed for the establishment of a reliable and reasonably simple analysis method for the load carrying capacities of DSTAs and S-DSTAs for the practical design of these novel arches.

15220318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220318.value: Hybrid FRP-concrete-steel double-skin tubular members with a stiffened steel tube (referred to as hybrid stiffened DSTMs or simply S-DSTMs) represent an enhanced form of hybrid DSTMs originally invented by the PI. Compared to hybrid DSTMs without stiffeners, the introduction of stiffeners: 1) substantially enhances the sectional capacity; 2) provides additional restraints against the local buckling of the steel tube; 3) enhances the composite action between the steel tube and the concrete. Arches with such a stiffened DSTM section are referred to as hybrid stiffened double-skin tubular arches (hybrid S-DSTAs or simply S-DSTAs). Such arches are superior to concrete filled steel tubular arches in a number of aspects, including much better corrosion resistance and a much higher strength-to-weight ratio. This project was undertaken to gain an in-depth understanding of the behaviour of S-DSTMs as columns (S-DSTCs) and arches (S-DSTAs), with a particular focus on the buckling behaviour of the steel tube. Systematic experimental studies including axial compression tests on stiffened steel tubes, concentric/eccentric compression tests on DSTCs and S-DSTCs, as well as theoretical analyses, were conducted. A design procedure of DSTAs was established in connection with the design of two pedestrian deck arch bridges. The results conclusively demonstrated the superior structural performance of DSTAs and S-DSTAs.

15220618.value: To develop a generic middleware framework that would enable coupling of CFD based fire simulation software FDS with FEM based heat transfer and structural response simulation software, OpenSees. Initiate work on applying the middleware framework developed to also couple FireFOAM (based on OpenFOAM) with OpenSees. To validate the integrated computational framework using documented experiments such as: the Dalmarnock fire tests to validate the CFD-HT (heat transfer) component; the Cardington tests to validate the HT-TM (thermo-mechanical) component. To use the framework to study the whole structure response (including progressive collapse simulation) for a range of realistic fire scenarios (such as post flashover compartment fires, localised fires, travelling fires in large open plan compartments and vertically travelling fires); and to simulate fire induced collapses such as WTC towers and the Plasco building in Tehran.
