15222018.label: Realisation of objectives
15222018.value: During this project, we have achieved the three objectives as follows: Objective #1: To design and fabricate an efficient light absorption and charge separation composite structure with a UV-light-sensitive TiO2 nanowire array on a UV-light-sensitive WO3 layer, coated by a visible-light-sensitive CdS/CdSe/g-C3N4 layer and then a thin carbon layer. Realisation: A highly efficient TiO2 nanotube array photoanode prepared by anodizing treatment of titanium foil is developed for an all-vanadium photoelectrochemical cell with a miniaturized design for solar energy storage. The highly ordered structure and miniaturization design have the intrinsic advantages of not only providing a large active surface area and plentiful pores but also enhancing mass and electron transport. Consequently, the developed photoanode exhibits both good photoresponse and operation stability under irradiation. The photoanodes prepared at higher anodizing voltages have larger active surface area and photocatalyst loading, thus leading to the improved performance. Nanosheets are synthesized with a unique two-dimensional layered architecture exposing oriented crystalline (101) facets as a majority for efficient electrochemical reactions. Objective #2: To develop an advanced model that incorporates the charge generation, separation and recombination, the transport of electroactive ions, holes and electrons, as well as the electroactive ion-conversion reactions at solid-electrolyte interfaces, which allows the charge transport to be numerically studied so that the structural design parameters can be optimized. Realisation: A mathematical model is developed, involving charge generation, separation and recombination, redox ion transport through the porous electrodes, ion-conversion reactions at the solid/electrolyte interfaces, and ion migration through the membrane. Different from the previous models that typically treated the catalyst layer as an interface, our model also considers the thickness of the catalyst layer and examine the effect of various structural and operating parameters on concentration and potential/current distributions. Therefore, this model is not only capable of predicting the redox ion conversion rate, but also able to give more in-depth insights into physical and chemical phenomena occurring in the photoelectrochemical storage single cell, e.g., the concentration distributions of charges/redox ions, the distribution of local photocurrent density, and the distribution of electrode potential. Objective #3: To devise a characterization and diagnostic system with which the light absorption, light response, photocurrent, voltage-current curves can be measured and characterized. Realisation: A three-electrode testing system with an electrochemical workstation is developed to conduct characterizations at electrode level, where the photoanode, an Ag/AgCl electrode and a platinum plate were used as the working electrode, the reference electrode and the counter electrode, respectively. The testing conditions are light intensity of 130 mW cm-2 and ion concentration of 100 mM. Objective #4: To design and fabricate a photoelectrochemical storage single cell to investigate the effects of different electroactive redox couples, cell structural design parameters, and operating conditions on the cell performance. Realisation: A photoelectrochemical storage single cell is fabricated as follows: The as synthesized TiO2 nanotube array with an electrode area of 1 cm × 1 cm is used as the photoanode. Commercial Pt-coated carbon paper with an exposed active area of 1 cm × 1 cm is used as the cathode. Two reaction microchambers with depth of 1 mm are used as the flow channels for the photoanode and cathode electrolytes. A Nafion®115 proton exchange membrane is used to separate the photoanode microchamber from the cathode microchamber. Both the electrolytes are injected using a syringe pump. A 300 W Xe lamp is used as simulated sunlight to illuminate the photoanode. The cell fixture is made of PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate). Moreover, the arrangement of the photoanode and cathode is not exactly face-to-face. They are misaligned with a minimal edge distance of 15 mm to ensure light transmission. Besides, a visible radiometer is utilized to measure the light intensity. Real-time monitoring of the current is realized by a data collecting instrument.

15222018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222018.value: With this project, we have the following major findings and research outcome: 1) The solar energy storage performance of the microfluidic all-vanadium photoelectrochemical cell with the developed TiO2 nanotube array photoanode is evaluated under various light intensities and vanadium ion concentrations. The performances of TiO2 nanotube array photoanodes prepared with different anodizing voltages are also investigated. The obtained results show that an increase in both the light intensity and vanadium ion concentration can improve the performance in terms of photocurrent density and vanadium ion conversion rate. The photoanodes prepared at higher anodizing voltages have larger active surface area and photocatalyst loading, thus leading to the improved performance. Major part of this find is included in paper titled “One-dimensional TiO2 nanotube array photoanode for a microfluidic all-vanadium photoelectrochemical cell for solar energy storage” published in Catalysis Science & Technology included in Part C. It is also utilized in other related work in Part C. 2) Nanosheets, a thickness of few nanometers, with a unique two-dimensional layered architecture exposing oriented crystalline (101) facets as a majority for efficient electrochemical reactions. The presence of oxygen vacancies in nanosheets creates defective nanostructures with dangling bonds, which can significantly enhance the reactant adsorption via strengthening the local binding effect. The two-dimensional architecture enables the presence of abundant uncoordinated surface atoms that are thermodynamically unstable, in which reactant adsorption and dissociation mostly take place, thus greatly enhancing the catalytic reactivity. Major part of this find is included in paper titled “Two-dimensional layered SnO2 nanosheets for ambient ammonia synthesis” published in ACS Applied Energy Materials included in Part C. It is also utilized in other related work in Part C. 3) Performance enhancement of adsorption-type carbon materials after ammonia treatment is revealed. As ammonia post-treatment temperature increases from 600 oC to 1200 oC, a simultaneous increase of specific surface area (8.6-1155 m2 g-1) and active nitrogen dopants (0.75-6.47 wt.%) is observed. This results in a transition of sodium storage behavior from electrochemical double-layer capacitor dominant behavior via physisorption to dominant surface redox behavior via chemisorption. Major part of this finding is included in paper titled “Revealing the sodium-storage performance enhancement of adsorption-type carbon materials after ammonia treatment: Active nitrogen dopants or specific surface area?” published in International Journal of Energy Research included in Part C. It is also utilized in other related work in Part C.

15222018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222018.value: With the results from the project, the further development of the research and the proposed course of action will be to scale up the microfluidic all-vanadium photoelectrochemical cell system with the TiO2 nanotube array photoanode. It consists of a TiO2 nanotube array photoanode, a proton exchange membrane, and Pt-coated carbon paper cathode. Both the electrolytes are fed into the anode and cathode by syringe pumps. During all experiments, the liquid flow rates at both electrodes are always the same to ensure the laminar flow.

15222018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222018.value: Photoelectrochemical storage cells (PESC), which are capable of converting the solar energy to chemical energy and electrical energy simultaneously, meet the global demands on the storage of solar energy. Although promising, the conventional stationary cell exhibited extremely low performance. Our solution to this issue is to introduce microfluidics technology to the PESC system, forming a thin layer-by-layer structure. The miniaturization design effectively enhances the light absorption via shortening the pathway of the light transport and improving the uniformity of the light distribution, enhances the transport of redox ions via tuning the flow rate, as well as facilitates the ionic migration via miniaturizing the chamber. In term of cell resistance, it is shown that the use of this novel design results in a more than 200% reduction. In terms of photoanode performance, the photocurrent is upgraded by ~170%. This performance improvement is mainly attributed to the unique design of the microfluidic cell and the use of the robust model. This project has achieved a substantial improvement in the PESC performance, making the technology closer to reality.

15222118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222118.value: 隨著電動車和互聯汽車的日益盛行，車載遠程資訊在車輛安全、交通運輸以及環境保護上獲得了廣泛的應用。隨著這些數據的重要性逐步提升，如何保護它們的可靠性防止非授權的篡改已成為一個重要課題。本項目基於系統級安全硬件所遵從的可信執行環境（Trusted Execution Environment, TEE）標準，設計并實現一套可靠實用的車載遠程資訊匯報系統，解決惡意軟體及系統入侵所帶來的數據可靠性被破壞的問題，為下一代智能車輛的設計和實施提供安全和可靠性基礎。同時，我們也期望這項研究成果能廣泛應用于物聯網、移動互聯網等新興行業。

15222118.label: Realisation of objectives
15222118.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, we report that most objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have achieved objectives 1-2 by the end of year 2020, and objectives 3 and 4 by the end of year 2021, and mid 2022, respectively. First, we study the problem that is presented in the first task of the original proposal (objectives 1 and 3) by putting in a wireless sensor network (WSN), which is an essential network infrastructure to deliver vehicular telematics data. We set out to study the confidentiality and integrity issue of data aggregation in WSN. Existing approaches adopt homomorphic encryptions where confidentiality and integrity can be protected against untrusted or compromised aggregators. However, such techniques cannot protect against untrusted or compromised sources, i.e., wireless sensors, as homomorphic encryptions require all sources to share a common encryption key. We propose Onion Homomorphic Encryptionbased Aggregation (OHEA), where sources form groups with their dedicated encryption keys, a.k.a., the group keys. OHEA has a nice property that group keys themselves can be aggregated, so it can work recursively with any level of aggregation hierarchy. In terms of security, we show that even if multiple aggregators or sources are compromised, an adversary is still unable to compromise the data of other nodes in the same or upper levels of the hierarchy. In terms of performance, the experimental results show that OHEA incurs low computation and communication cost, and is thus scalable to large WSNs. This work has been published in ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM2020) as a full research paper. Second, we study an integrity assurance problem that is presented in the objective 2 for trusted TU. The problem we try to tackle is password-based authentication. Such services are essential in many vehicular and IoT systems. In many cases, B-tree has been adopted as a fast retrieval index for a large user account database. However, such design leaves the system vulnerable against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. We propose to use a Bloom filter, with O(1) query complexity, as a pre-screener to reject bad requests quickly. Effectively, we have designed a firewall architecture to clean out these requests before they arrive at the authentication service. The main challenge of such design is the security issue of this additional pre-screener. More specifically, we need to develop mechanism to protect against attackers who break in the vehicular or IoT systems and obtain the hashed password list, trying to gain the password plaintexts from a brute-force attack. To this end, we design a keybased semantic secure Bloom filter (KSSBF) as a secure pre-screener. For objective 3 of untrusted TU, we also design a generically secure Bloom filter (GSBF) whose security is nontrivial, strictly provable and key-independent. This work has been published in IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS '20). Third, we design and propose an integrity assurance scheme for untrusted clients under TEE in the objective 3. The main issue we address is the access frequency pattern leakage problem, which reveals sensitive information over encrypted cloud data, such as query inclinations and interests. Even worse, adversaries can infer the content of storage with the help of auxiliary knowledge. It jeopardizes the mutual trust between the client users and the server as reported in many cases. In this task, we study the threats model in which adversaries know both the exact in-memory flow of accessed blocks and the processing boundary of each request. Under these settings, he can precisely observe the access frequency patterns in both aggregated and independent perspectives over queries. We then propose the ReFlat module as a counter solution through the K-duplication obfuscation mechanism. ReFlat securely runs inside the hardware enclave provided by Intel SGX and requires no modifications on query processors. Comparing with the state-of-the-art schemes using the similar idea, that is, fake query injection, ReFlat eliminates the security risk of involving intermediate proxy and achieves higher robustness under the proposed threat model. This work has been accepted and published in IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing (TCC), 2023. We also extend this idea to textual and document data, the work has been published in Journal of Computer Security, 2023. Fourth, we study the integrity assurance problem in objective 4 without trusted TEEs. First, we address the message integrity issue in IoT and vehicular network, In particular, these messages may contain sensitive information, and a portion of the information in the message needs to be authenticated. In a previous work, we have proposed PMAC to work under such scenario, but it only works if the portion to be authenticated is a prefix of the message. In this work, we propose a more general scheme called Scalable Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code (SPMAC). It inherits the advantage of PMAC while overcoming the drawbacks. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management (TNSM), 2022. Second, we also study the integrity assurance problem for another vehicular telematics data type, namely, videos. Video cameras have been widely deployed in autonomous vehicles. But the authenticity of a video faces a great challenge due to the ease of tampering with video data without leaving visible traces. Unfortunately, existing authentication schemes are not efficient for emerging high-resolution videos. In this work, we propose stateful correlation coefficient sampling-based hash (Stateful-CCSH), which adopts correlation coefficient sampling in image hash and learns from previous frames to sample those blocks with more dynamic contents and thus, more likely to be tampered in a video forgery. This work has been published in IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 2022. Third, we also attempt to adopt blockchain for integrity assurance on multidimensional data with historical values. In blockchain systems, existing works only consider one-dimensional data to implement indexing approaches, so these approaches perform poorly when extended to multi-dimensional and historical data. To overcome these issues, in this work we propose two new indexing models for blockchain. The first model is Two-tier Deterministic Appended Only Skip List (TDASL) that improves from LineageChain by using an additional indexing layer on top of a skip list and by using prefixes to query multi-dimensional state versions. The second model is Predefined Partitioned B-plus Tree. This work has been published in Future Generation Computer Systems, 2023. Fifth, we have also produced a demo for integrity assurance for cloud vehicular telematics and IoT data. We provided a web-based GUI to demonstrate the integrity mechanism does not incur high computational overhead even for a portable device such as iPad. The demo has been published in 35th IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '19). Last but not the least, since telematics on vehicles also have privacy issues together with integrity assurance, we also investigate the application of local differential privacy (LDP) techniques to various telematics data types. For example, we stduy the vehicular trajectory data (accepted to appear in MDM '19, PVLDB '23 and TKDE '23), multi-dimensional numerical value (published in IEEE SECON '21, ICDE '22 and TIFS '23), continuous data (published in TKDE '23), time series data (published in IEEE INFOCOM '21 and '23), and aggregate data under untrusted users (published in IEEE ICDE '23).

15222118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222118.value: Our major research findings and outcome are listed as below. Due to space limitation, more technical details are presented in Section 5.3 as above. 1. A secure aggregation mechanism which support group-based integrity assurance in sensor network. This paper has been published as a full research paper in ACM CIKM '20. 2. A Bloom filter-based, O(1) time complexity, authentication system for vehicular and IoT systems. This paper has been published in IEEE ICDCS '20. 3. An integration scheme of hardware security (or more specifically CPU enclaves such as Intel SGX) with oblivious RAM for authenticable aggregation operations such as OLAP queries. The paper has been published in Information Systems, 2021. 4. A ReFlat module as a counter solution through the K-duplication obfuscation mechanism for access pattern hiding under TEE. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing (TCC), 2023. 5. An access pattern hiding and authentication scheme for textual and document data under TEE. This work has been published in Journal of Computer Security, 2023. 6. A Scalable Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code (SPMAC) scheme for integrity assurance in vehicular and IoT systems. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management (TNSM), 2022. 7. An active video integrity authentication system for high-resolution video camera data in vehicular and surveillance systems. This work has been published in IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 2022. 8. A lightweight and efficient indexing schemes for historical data retrieval in a blockchain system. This work has been published in Future Generation Computer Systems, 2023. 9. A demo for integrity assurance for cloud vehicular telematics and IoT data. This work has been published in 35th IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '19). 10. Various local differential privacy schemes for various vehicular telematics and IoT data types. These works have been published in many top-tier conferences and journals, including INFOCOM '21, 23', PVLDB '23, ICDE '22, '23, TKDE '23, and TIFS '23.

15222118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222118.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our existing schemes to make it suitable for commercial demonstration and knowledge transfer. We believe that the promotion of these protection schemes will further make an impact on both research and industry community regarding our integrity assurance for vehicular telematics.

15222118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222118.value: Vehicular telematics combine telecommunications and informatics to send, receive, and store information related to vehicles. With the increasing role of computers in automobiles and the prevalence of electric vehicles, telematics data become essential in the automobile and transportation industry. As such, the integrity of such data must be assured to guarantee vehicular safety and intelligent transportation. Fortunately, system-on-chip manufacturers have made hardware security freely and ubiquitously available through the Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) specification. In this project, we have seized this opportunity to assure vehicular telematics integrity against malicious subjects. With the provision of TEE and/or peer vehicles, vehicles are enforced to report their true telematics data for the mission-critical tasks. Based on whether the clients are trusted and such TEEs exist in the system, we have proposed various integrity assurance solutions for various types of vehicular telematics data, such as high-dimensional sensor data, time series data, video camera data, and key-value data. We believe the outcomes of this project can lay the security foundation for the next-generation applications using vehicular telematics, and benefit the research community, the vehicular industry, and the city of Hong Kong, a “beacon city for electric vehicles”, called by Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla.

15222318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222318.value: 隧道是香港常見的設施。使用無GPS的自主，精確，低成本的導航 的隧道測量系統具有廣泛的應用前景。本項目提出壹種以無人機和 低成本RGB-D傳感器組合的自動隧道測量系統。利用RGB-D的 SLAM系統，我們可以同時得到無人機位置和周邊三維環境。 這樣無人機就可以實現自主導航和避障的功能。 本項目旨在提高低成本RGB-D傳感器的實時定位精度和定位穩定 性，實時性以適應無人機地下隧道的應用環境。主要研究內容包括 ：RGB-D的精密校正，實時三維場景算法研究， 和障礙無自動 檢測。

Multiple features (i.e. point, line, and plane) are used in the new SLAM algorithms developed in this research project. New robust estimation methods have been proposed to improve the robustness of pose estimation in SLAM algorithms. 3) Objective 3: Developing RGB-D sensor based integrated navigation system for UAV auto-piloting in tunnels for robust navigation and obstacle avoidance. A prototype system is developed to include real-time operation for 3D modelling. New exploration method is developed to enhance the quality of 3D model.

15222318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222318.value: The RGB-D errors are distance related and normally it can only be used within 2 m for SLAM. IN this study, we developed a new calibration model for RGB-D sensor. It is shown that the previous study was wrong to assume that the distortion center of the RGB-D system is at a fixed point. Based on our new model, the accuracy of RGB-D sensor can improve more than 60%, and the operation range of RGB-D sensor can extend to 7 m from original 2 m. The proper statistical models are developed for the 3D point cloud from RGB-D sensors, which will be used in the optimal estimation of pose parameters of the sensor. We developed robust SLAM algorithms with the multiple features (i.e. point, line, and plane). Other geometrical constraints can also be included in the optimization model. It is shown that the performance of our SLAM algorithms is significantly better than the existing methods, particularly in the environments with low textures. A prototype system is developed for real-time operation and a new exploration algorithm is proposed to improve the survey quality.

15222318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222318.value: The demand for precise 3D models for indoor environments is increasing for diversified applications. Currently there are many technologies can be used for collect 3D point cloud in the indoor environment. In this study, we developed a low cost RGB-D system for indoor /tunnel 3D surveying. The results demonstrate that decimeter level 3D model accuracy can be achieved with this type of low cost sensors. In the future study, fast generation of 3D model in near real-time will be the challenge. Installing the RGB-D SLAM system on moving platforms, if we can obtain 3D model in real-time, there will be many potential applications, such as rescue operation. We will try to work with industry for this type of application.

15222318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222318.value: 3D model is the basic information for many diversified applications, such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), indoor navigation, and rescue operation. Currently most of the surveying equipment includes Lidar which is expensive. In this study, we try to use a low cost sensor, RGB-D senor, to replace Lidar for 3D modeling. We have developed new calibration models which significantly improve the accuracy and operation range of RGB-D sensor. The results show that in typical indoor/tunnel environments, decimeter level 3D model can be obtained by RGB-D sensor in near real-time. Together with an autonomous platform, we can survey the tunnel space without human intervention which will significantly improving survey efficiency.

15223018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223018.value: Falls on the same level are the leading cause of non-fatal injuries in construction. To prevent these injuries, it is important to eliminate any intrinsic (e.g., worker age, fatigue) and extrinsic (e.g., unsafe conditions) risk factors that could lead to a loss of balance in a timely manner. This study aims to develop a wearable sensor (i.e., pressure insole sensor)-based approach to detect 1) slips, 2) trips, 3) unexpected step-downs and 4) twisted ankles that are major loss of balance events. This approach enables us to identify1) construction workers who are more vulnerable to falls on the same level under given conditions; and 2) potential risk factors (i.e., types of unsafe conditions) that could lead to falls on the same level. The central hypothesis of this study is that each loss of balance event creates unique foot pressure patterns from the insole sensors, and thus by using machine learning algorithms, each event can be classified. To develop the machine learning algorithms, foot pressure data from wearable insole sensors will be collected from 10 healthy subjects by simulating four loss of balance events at the laboratory. Then, sequential supervised learning algorithms that consist of data segmentation, feature extraction and classifiers will be tested using collected pressure data to determine the optimal combination of algorithms. The developed algorithms will be validated through field data collection to test the feasibility of real-time fall risk detection at real construction sites. The proposed approach for loss of balance event detection could open the door to more proactive monitoring of fall risks by taking appropriate interventions. Specifically, by providing warnings or precautions to vulnerable workers or by removing any unsafe conditions on sites, falls on the same level can be reduced. 在建築業施工過程中，在同一高度跌倒是造成僱員非致命傷害的主要原因之一。為了預防上述傷害，極為重要的是消除易造成工人瞬間失去平衡的內在風險（如工人年齡，疲勞程度）和外在風險（如危險的工作環境）。本研究旨在開發基於可穿戴設備（即足部壓力傳感器）的方法以檢測失去平衡的誘因，包括：1）滑倒；2）絆倒；3）意外踩空；4）腳踝扭傷。本檢測方法可輔助甄別：1）在指定工作環境下更容易發生同層墜落的工人； 2）易造成同層墜落的潛在風險因素（即危險環境的類型）。該研究的中心假設认为失去平衡時，足部壓力傳感器將會檢測到特定的足部壓力。因此單個失去平衡的事件可以通過機器學習的算法分類。為了開發機器學習的算法，科研人員將通過可穿戴的足部壓力傳感器收集10位健康試驗員在實驗室模擬的四種失去平衡情況下的足部壓力數據。之後將進行數據分割，特徵提取和製作分類器，完成順序監督學習算法並使用試驗採集的壓力數據進行測試，以此確定最優的組合算法。所開發的算法將用施工現場採集的數據進行驗證，以測試其在實際施工环境下检测實時墜落風險的可行性。本研究提出的失去平衡檢測方法可通過適當的干預，為更積極主動地監墜落風險打開大門。具體而言，通過向弱勢工人提供警告或預防措施，或通過消除現場的危險因素，工人同層摔倒的幾率得以降低。

15223018.label: Realisation of objectives
15223018.value: Objective 1. Develop machine learning algorithms that can automatically classify different types of loss of balance events by using foot plantar pressure distribution data from insole sensors 0bjective #1 is to develop a methodology for automated fall risk detection. Based on this research, one journal paper (Antwi-Afari et al. (2018)) and one conference paper (Antwi-Afari et al. (2019)) were published. Antwi-Afari et al. (2018) presents the methodology described below. In Antwi-Afari et al. (2019), the research team extended the scope of the application area of the proposed study by applying the algorithms developed from Objective #1 to general construction activities. (Please note that Dr. Antwi-Afari has worked with the PI for this project, but was not financially supported by this project during his Ph.D study as he was already supported by another project when this project was awarded.) 1.1. Mechanisms and Prevention Measures of Falls on the Same Level There are four major types of loss of balance events that could lead to falls on the same level: 1) slips; 2) trips; 3) unexpected step-downs; and 4) twisted ankles. These four events account for more than 90% of underfoot events that resulted in falls on the same level. They are directly associated with specific underfoot surface conditions such as a slippery surface, an obstacle on a walkway, and an uneven surface. 1.2. Designing Machine Learning Algorithms for Loss of Balance Event Classification Data Segmentation: Data segmentation is a data preprocessing strategy to convert sequential supervised learning problems into traditional supervised learning problems. A sliding window technique is one of the widely used methods for time-series data segmentation. From the previous research efforts, it has been concluded that short window sizes (e.g., less than 3s) lead to better classification performance. Also, the window sizes can be affected by types of features used in the algorithms. For example, one of the features widely used for sequential supervised learning is frequency-domain features using the fast Fourier transform (FFT) function. One of the limitations of using the FFT function is that the number of sample data points in the segment must be a power of two. Considering the use of the frequency-domain features, we selected four different window sizes of 0.32s, 0.64s, 1.28s and 2.56s that corresponds to 16 (24), 32 (25), 64 (26) and 128 (27) data samples, respectively. Feature Extraction: For time-domain features, we used seven time domain features (i.e., mean pressure, variance, maximum pressure, minimum pressure, range, standard deviation, and kurtosis) that have been commonly used for activity recognition and classification. Also, to extract frequency-domain features, the raw data in time domain will be converted into frequency domain by using the FFT function, and then spectral energy and entropy were computed to be used as two frequency domain features. In addition to time and frequency domain features, we applied a new feature extraction method based on pressure time integral (PTI). PTI is a variable that describes the cumulative foot loading over time, providing useful information on chronic foot problems. Supervised Machine Learning Classification: To classify different loss of balance events, machine learning classifiers learned unique signal patterns from pressure data based on extracted features. As the classifier performance could vary depending on types of data, window sizes and types of features, it is necessary to test diverse classifiers that fit best for detecting loss of balance events from pressure data. In this research, classifiers to be tested include but not limited to 1) Artificial Neural Network (ANN), 2) Decision Tree (DT), 3) Random Forest (RF), 4) K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and 5) Support Vector Machine (SVM). Classifier Model Assessment and Performance Evaluation: The performance of the classifiers is evaluated by a 10-fold cross-validation, which is a model validation technique to assess the accuracy and validity of statistical models. In the 10-folds cross-validation, the dataset is randomly split into 10 approximately equal size exclusive subsets. Then, each part is reserved as test datasets, and the remaining parts are performed as training datasets with a particular classifier. Objective #2. Test the developed algorithms on construction sites to prove the feasibility of real-time detection of loss of balance events The objective #2 is to validate and refine the proposed algorithms by applying them to data collected on construction sites. In 2019, the PI tried to collect the data at the construction sites for 3 months. However, we were not able to collect meaningful datasets from loss of balance events as these events rarely occurred in a real condition. Also, even though some workers reported these events, it was not possible to extract the data during that events due to significant noisy signals. From 2020, our team wanted to collect more data, but unfortunately, due to the pandemic situation, site access was not allowed for further data collection. Due to this reason, the PI would like to report our validation results from laboratory experiments in this final report. However, the data collection in 2019 at construction sites enabled us to collect additional data from construction workers, which led us to publish one journal paper titled “Wearable acceleration-based action recognition for long-term and continuous activity analysis in a construction site (Gong et al. (2022)).” 2.1. Data Collection Foot plantar pressure distribution data of each loss of balance event was collected at laboratory settings by using Moticon SCIENCE (Moticon GmbH, Munich, Germany, http://www.moticon.de/), a wearable insole pressure sensor system. It provides a novelty in conducting research based on foot plantar pressure distributions in both laboratory and field conditions. It consists of two sensor insoles (containing 13 capacitive sensors each) that measure the foot plantar pressure distribution. Each insole sensor incorporates a wireless module for data transmission and sensor configuration control. For data collection, a convenience sample (n = 10) of healthy male volunteers ranging in age between 20 and 35 years were recruited from the student population of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Exclusion criteria were: 1) a history of injuries on upper extremities, a low back and lower extremities; and 2) a history of neurological disabilities or other conditions that could affect body balance functionality. Ten repeated data collection sessions for each participant were conducted to collect foot plantar pressure distributions data while simulating four different types of loss of balance events. To simulate loss of balance events similar to real conditions, all participants were asked to wear safety boots and a hard hat during the sessions. Also, a safety harness and a 30-cm thick layer of high-density gymnasium mattress were provided to prevent any possible injuries. 2.2. Testing Results From the comparative evaluation based on cross validation, it was found that the Random Forest classifier achieved the best performance for detecting and classifying loss of balance events with an accuracy of 97.1%, and the sensitivity of more than 94% for each event using all feature groups and a window size of 0.32s. Additionally, we performed hold-out validation by randomly splitting the data into two parts (70% for training, 30% for testing). The result also showed 95.9% overall accuracy when using same algorithm parameters, supporting the robustness of the proposed approach for independent test datasets. This result implies that signals obtained from wearable insole pressure sensors can effectively detect and classify loss of balance events, which may help to understand the causes of falls on the same level.

15223018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223018.value: Wearable sensor-based approaches have been reported to provide information-rich and reliable sensor data for assessing construction workers’ activity recognition and fall risk detections. In particular, despite its great potential, wearable insole pressure sensors for measuring foot plantar pressure distribution have not been yet explored for monitoring falls on the same level in construction. This study introduces a novel methodology for automated classification and detection of different types of loss of balance events that may lead to falls on the same level. Toward this goal, wearable insole pressure sensors that are light-weight and can be inserted in workers’ safety boots were employed to collect their foot plantar pressure distribution data. Based on our experimental trials, the Random Forest classifier obtained the best results with the accuracy of 97.1% and sensitivity of each loss of balance event above 94.00% using the window size of 0.32s. The foot plantar pressure distribution data contain valuable information relating to specific loss of balance events, which can be used to understand the causes of falls on the same level in a timely manner. Overall, the wearable insole pressure sensors may encourage more intensive and regular workplace inspections to check workplace factors having the potential to cause fall injuries to workers, i.e., materials, activities, and the environment, to identify safety hazards and recommend a preventive measure.

15223018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223018.value: Despite the promising result of the proposed approach, there are several potential issues when applying it in practice, which includes 1) data collection issues and 2) need for location data. Identifying and removing existing risk factors (e.g., slippery floors) in a timely manner is essential to minimize falls on the same level. Toward this goal, continuous data transfer and real-time analysis are required. Most wearable sensors including pressure insole sensors uses direct wireless network or a smartphone for data transfer. However, the issues related to internet disconnection could occur in wearable sensors, failing to transfer data in real time. As a result, the reliability of wearable sensors for data transfer needs to be tested, especially at construction sites where signal blockage commonly exists. Also, even though the proposed system can detect instances of loss of balance events, the location information where the event occurs is also required to implement necessary interventions, and thus additional location tracking systems may be required for more proactive control of fall risks at construction sites.

15223018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223018.value: Fall on the same level is the leading cause of non-fatal injuries in construction workers; however, identifying the causes of falls in a timely manner remains challenging. The objective of this study was to develop a method to detect and classify loss of balance events that could lead to falls on the same level by using foot plantar pressure distribution data captured from wearable insole pressure sensors. The types of loss of balance events were classified into four categories, including slip, trip, step-down, and twisted ankle, and corresponding foot plantar pressure data were collected by simulating these events at a laboratory setting. Machine learning algorithms were used to learn the unique pressure data patterns, and then to automatically detect loss of balance events. We compared classification performance by varying model parameters, and the best classification accuracy (97.1%) was achieved. This study is of value as the proposed approach enables to identify potential causes of falls on the same level as each loss of balance event is associated with specific unsafe conditions at construction sites. The proposed approach can serve as an automated fall risk assessment tool to eliminate the fundamental causes of falls on the same level.

15223918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223918.value: 大约84亿联网的IoT设备将会在一年内于全球部署，这个数字将于2020年达到204亿。与此同时，这些设备变成了黑客新的攻击热点。因为相比于普通的PC/服务器，IoT设备往往缺乏足够的安全保护。这个安全问题对于基于App及裸程序控制的IoT系统来说更加严重，因为这些IoT系统有更大的攻击面（如，移动App)，而且它们通常使用低端的没有操作系统支持而且缺乏安全机制的微控制器。虽然已有不少关于这类IoT设备的漏洞的报道，但这些发现大多是基于手动分析的，缺乏系统的方法和工具来评价这类IoT设备的安全性。本项目尝试来解决这个问题。我们将设计新的方法并研发实用的工具来有效的发现这类IoT设备上的三类漏洞，包括认证被绕过漏洞，固件被修改漏洞，以及内存被破坏漏洞。这项研究要解决一些挑战性的问题，包括对认证机制的整体建模，设计系统的方法来检测固件被修改漏洞，以及逆向IoT设备的私有协议和App。基于我们在App分析及漏洞发现的经验，我们将设计新颖的方法并开发使用的系统来解决这些问题。这个研究将从理论和实践两个角度进行，其成果将深化对这类IoT设备的安全性的认识。预期成果包括新的方法来寻找这类IoT设备的漏洞以及实用的分析工具和数据集。

15223918.label: Realisation of objectives
15223918.value: We have realized the three objectives. 1. Identifying authentication bypass vulnerability. We proposed a new approach to detect authentication bypass vulnerabilities in appified IoT systems by inspecting both the app and the firmware of IoT device. The corresponding paper entitled “Update If You Dare: Demystifying Bare-metal Device Firmware Update Security of Appified IoT Systems”, which also covers the firmware modification vulnerability, will be submitted to TDSC soon. To identify more vulnerabilities, we propose a new framework to learn deep feature representation from software defect data. The corresponding paper entitled “LDFR: Learning Deep Feature Representation for Software Defect Prediction” appeared in JSS. We performed an empirical study on clustering-based defect prediction models. The corresponding paper entitled “A comprehensive comparative study of clustering-based unsupervised defect prediction models” appeared in JSS. When analyzing the apps, we tackled several important issues. First, many apps use application performance management libraries to collect information, which may leak the authentication information. We summarized our observations in an ASE’19 paper entitled “Demystifying Application Performance Management Libraries for Android”. Second, many apps use native framework APIs, but their permission specification is poorly documented. We proposed PSGen that statically analyzes Android framework and Android kernel to correlate native framework APIs with their required permissions. The corresponding paper entitled “Finding the Missing Piece: Permission Specification Analysis for Android NDK” appeared in ASE’21. Third, the inconsistent access control enforcement in Android can be exploited to bypass access controls. We proposed IAceFinder to detect such inconsistent access control. The corresponding paper entitle “Uncovering Cross-Context Inconsistent Access Control Enforcement in Android” appeared in NDSS’22. Fourth, we tried to design deep learning approaches to detect vulnerability from Apps. However, we found deep learning based approaches can be misled by modifying the app’s CFG. The corresponding paper entitled “Structural Attack against Graph Based Android Malware Detection” appeared in CCS’21. We further investigated adversarial inputs and poisoned models within a unified framework and revealed there exist intriguing mutual reinforcement effects between the two attack vectors. The corresponding paper entitled “A Tale of Evil Twins: Adversarial Inputs versus Poisoned Models” appeared in CCS’20. We developed a hardware-assisted cross-layer analysis tool, which uses ARM’s ETM to collect execution traces and combines the app’s oat file and the waypoints to reconstruct the execution paths. The corresponding paper entitled “Happer: Unpacking Android Apps via a Hardware-Assisted Approach” appeared in IEEE Symposiums on Security and Privacy’21. We further developed a hardware-assisted tool to detect various implementation bugs and memory corruption vulnerabilities. The corresponding paper entitled “Alligator In Vest: A Practical Failure-Diagnosis Framework via Arm Hardware Features” was submitted to NDSS’23. We investigated the IoT malware evolution by leveraging the information from online articles about IoT malware and malware samples collected by our honeypots and constructed a lineage graph for 72 IoT malware. The corresponding paper entitled “An Evolutionary Study of IoT Malware” appeared in IEEE Internet of Things Journal. To analyze the traffic generated by apps or IoT devices, we designed a novel neural network that can classify network flows by examining the first few packets and outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. The corresponding paper entitled “EBSNN: Extended Byte Segment Neural Network for Network Traffic Classification” appeared in TDSC. 2. Detecting firmware modification vulnerability. We developed a new approach to analyze bootloaders to find firmware modification vulnerability. After applying our tool to the bootloaders extracted from a set of appified IoT systems, we found their vulnerabilities. The corresponding paper entitled “Update If You Dare: Demystifying Bare-metal Device Firmware Update Security of Appified IoT Systems” will be submitted to TDSC soon. Since most IoT devices use ARM architecture, we conducted the first study on ARM disassembly tools and uncovered their limitations. The corresponding paper entitled “An Empirical Study on ARM Disassembly Tools” appeared in ISSTA’20. We further investigated whether emulators are consistent with real devices by developing a new approach to automatically locate instructions that behave differently between emulators and real devices. The corresponding paper entitled “EXAMINER: Automatically Locating Inconsistent Instructions between Real Devices and CPU Emulators for ARM” appeared in ASPLOS’22. Performing dynamic analysis on a full-system emulator can facilitate discovering vulnerabilities in firmware, but many IoT systems are not supported by QEMU. Hence, we proposed FirmGuide that combines the peripheral abstractions in the Linux kernel and kernel-peripheral interactions to semi-automatically generate peripheral models to synthesize QEMU virtual machines. The corresponding paper entitled “FIRMGUIDE: Boosting the Capability of Rehosting Embedded Linux Kernels through Model-Guided Kernel Execution” appeared in ASE’21. We further proposed a new technique that transplants the device drivers of designated peripherals into the Linux kernel binary, thus making the Linux kernel rehostable. The corresponding paper entitled “ECMO: Peripheral Transplantation to Rehost Embedded Linux Kernels” appeared in CCS’21. We conducted the first empirical study on the (in)security of End-of-Life devices and discovered many vulnerable IoT devices. The corresponding paper entitled “An Empirical Study on the Insecurity of End-of-Life (EoL) IoT Devices” was submitted to TDSC. Moreover, by landing reinforcement learning onto a system capable of smartly scanning IoT devices in a principled way, we disclosed key parameters affecting the effectiveness of different scanning strategies. The corresponding paper entitled “Landing Reinforcement Learning onto Smart Scanning of The Internet of Things” appeared in INFOCOM’22. 3. Discovering implementation bugs and memory corruption vulnerability. We designed a new approach to reverse engineer the proprietary protocol used by an IoT device and the app, and then use such information to guide the fuzzing. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art fuzzer for appified IoT systems. The corresponding paper entitled “Aidfuzz: App-assisted Vulnerability Detection for IoT Devices” will be submitted to ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM) soon. We extended this research in two aspects. First, we designed an extended method to reverse engineer the diagnostic protocols used by vehicles. The corresponding paper entitled “Towards Automatically Reverse Engineering Vehicle Diagnostic Protocols” appeared in USENIX Security’22. Second, we developed PrIntFuzz, an efficient and universal fuzzing framework for driver codes. By applying PrIntFuzz to simulated virtual PCI/I2C/USB devices, we found 150 bugs. The corresponding paper entitled “PrIntFuzz: Fuzzing Linux Drivers via Automated Virtual Device Simulation” appeared in ISSTA’22. We proposed a novel approach to detect concurrency memory vulnerabilities based on partial orders of events and proposed new algorithms to extract vulnerability-potential event pairs for three kinds of memory vulnerabilities. The corresponding paper entitled “Detecting Concurrency Vulnerabilities Based on Partial Orders of Memory and Thread Events” appeared in ESEC/FSE’21. For the Identification of Crashing Fault Residence(ICFR) of newly submitted crashes, we developed a novel cross project ICFR framework, and the corresponding paper entitled “Feature selection and embedding based cross project framework for identifying crashing fault residence” appeared in Information and Software Technology. By exploiting the bugs in firmware, we obtained information from the lane detection module used by autonomous driving and proposed a novel two-stage approach to determine how to fool the lane detection model. The corresponding paper entitled “Too Good to Be Safe: Tricking Lane Detection in Autonomous Driving with Crafted Perturbations” appeared in USENIX Security’21. To defend against such attack and other injection attacks, we propose a new state-aware defense approach, which detects the abnormal data by considering the data semantics and the vehicle dynamics. The corresponding paper entitled “SAID: State-aware Defense Against Injection Attacks on In-vehicle Network” appeared in USENIX Security’22.

15223918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223918.value: We proposed novel approaches and developed practical systems to identify various vulnerabilities with a focus on authentication bypass vulnerability, firmware modification vulnerability, memory corruption vulnerability, and implementation bugs in appified IoT systems. We uncovered various vulnerabilities in popular IoT and relevant systems and reported them to the vendors, and we found that these vulnerabilities are caused by many reasons, especially incorrect threat model (security assumptions), insufficient protection mechanisms, insecure software development, and inadequate software testing adopted by developers. We identified the challenging issues in inspecting apps/Android, firmware, and traffic exchanged among IoT devices, their apps, and cloud servers to detect vulnerabilities and proposed new techniques to tackled them. We pointed out many limitations in existing approaches and tools and designed solutions to overcome them. Moreover, our large-scale measurement studies showed that adversaries keep trying to compromise IoT devices connected to the Internet and then launch other activities. We also found that there are many End-of-Life (EoL) IoT Devices, whose vendors no longer maintain their firmware or software and thus make EoL devices susceptible to attacks. Our findings can facilitate developers to enhance the security of their IoT products. First, developers should adopt correct security assumptions and strong protection mechanisms as suggested in our papers. For example, developers should not assume that the smartphone running the accompany app is secure, adversaries cannot sniffer messages sent through mobile communication, the secrete embedded in binary through obfuscation cannot be recovered, to name a few. The reason is our research demonstrates that the native functions used by apps and the firmware of IoT devices can be reserve-engineered to identify important messages via hardware-assisted approaches and/or full-system emulators. Adversaries can use pseudo base station/ fake wireless AP to capture messages exchanged and infer the information of encrypted packets according to their observable features. Second, developers should follow the best practices of secure software development and conduct adequate software testing. They can use our proposed techniques and systems to test their product for finding potential security loopholes. In this project, we published 5 journal papers and 16 conferences papers. One journal paper was submitted to IEEE TDSC, and one conference paper was submitted to NDSS'23. Two papers are going to be submitted to TDSC and TOSEM, respectively. We trained one Ph.D. student, two M.Sc. students, and several undergraduate students. Moreover, we have been collaborating with the researchers in a number of universities on this research.

15223918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223918.value: We proposed new techniques and systems to detect several kinds of vulnerabilities in appified IoT systems by scrutinising their apps, firmware, and traffic. There are three directions for further investigation. First, while we focus on the security issues in individual IoT system, nowadays many IoT systems are connected through various channels and communicate with each other to make decision and conduct activities. Since there are new security issues in such a group of IoT systems, our proposed techniques and systems can be extended to investigate their security. Second, more and more IoT devices adopt various machine learning algorithms to provide rich services. Unfortunately, their machine learning algorithms may be attacked by adversarial samples or be poisoned. How to detect the weaknesses in the deployed machine learning algorithms and characterize the effect of the corresponding attacks would be an interesting and promising direction. Third, as IoT devices have been widely used in our daily life, there are many sophisticated IoT systems that have not been carefully investigated, such as devices in vehicles, planes, vessels, and industrial IoT systems. An important direction is to automatically identify unique vulnerabilities in them and design innovative approaches to protect them.

15223918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223918.value: Billions of connected IoT devices have been in use worldwide, which become the new lucrative and profitable targets for attackers because IoT devices usually lack sufficient security protection and the compromised IoT devices will pose severe threats to cybersecurity. This problem becomes worse on appified bare-metal IoT systems, which allow users to control them through mobile apps. In this project, we proposed new approaches and developed practical tools to effectively detect several kinds of vulnerabilities in such systems with a focus on the authentication bypass vulnerability, firmware modification vulnerability, memory corruption vulnerability and implementation bugs. By using our new techniques to identify vulnerabilities in popular IoT produces and characterize vulnerable IoT devices, we showed the security situation of IoT systems. Our research also provided new methodology and approaches to developers and security analysts to enhance the security of IoT systems. In particular, for their IoT systems, developers should adopt correct security assumptions and strong protection mechanisms and follow the best practices of secure software development and conduct adequate software testing. Moreover, they can use our proposed new techniques and tools carry out static analysis and dynamic analysis on their products to detect potential security loopholes before releasing them.

15224118.label: Project Objectives
15224118.value: Novel designs of dual comb source based on microresonators and bus waveguides will be developed. We will investigate different configurations using a single or dual microresonators, and a single or dual bus waveguides. For dual microresonators, we will investigate the effect of coupling between the two microrings on dual comb generation. For single microresonator, we will consider using the two orthogonal polarizations or counter propagating direction of the CW beams. Microring parameters such as ring diameters, Q-factors, dispersion, and nonlinear coefficients, etc., will be varied for optimal performance. Modeling of dual comb generation using pump frequency scanning approach: For each of the dual comb source configuration, we will model the dynamics of dual comb generation using the appropriate theoretical model. The conventional pump frequency tuning and “power kicking” approach will be used to achieve the dual single-soliton states in each design. Deterministic dual comb generation: we will investigate deterministic generation of dual combs for each of the design by the novel pulse trigger approach proposed by the PI. The use of pulse train, dual, and single trigger pulses will be investigated. Thermal effect: we will investigate the thermal effect on the generation of dual frequency combs by using either the conventional pump frequency tuning or the trigger approach. We will also study the long term thermal stability of the dual combs generated. Fabrication, characterization, and dual comb generation: The optimum designs of the dual comb sources will be fabricated and characterized. Experiments will be carried to generate dual frequency combs. The experimental results will be compared with the modeling results for further optimization of the designs and fabrication process.

15224118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224118.value: Optical frequency combs consist of equally spaced sharp lines in the frequency domain. Coherent octave spanning optical frequency combs have important applications in high precision infrared spectroscopy for molecular finger printing. The main obstacles in widespread application of optical frequency combs are the availability of robust optical frequency comb sources outside state-of-the-art laboratories and low cost detection of the frequency comb lines. The latter can be tackled by using dual comb spectroscopy in which two optical frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates are mixed. The beat frequencies of each pair of comb lines are in the radio frequency domain and can be detected in the electrical domain directly. Optical frequency combs with bandwidths of a few terahertz can be compressed to electric combs of a few hundred megahertz only. Thus real time, high resolution, high requisition rate detection of the optical spectra in the near- to mid-infrared wavelength regime is possible. For frequency comb sources, recent advances in microresonator-based optical frequency combs promise robust on-chip generation of frequency combs, which is an attractive platform for dual comb frequency spectroscopy. However, the Kerr nonlinearity in the microcavities that makes soliton frequency combs possible in the microresonators also gives rise to scores of nonlinear dynamical phenomena including modulation instabilities, chaos, and multiple soliton states. Furthermore, because of the small heat capacity of the nanoscale microresonators, the energy dissipated by the optical beam injected into the microring resonsators for the formation of soliton frequency combs also heats up the microcavities and induces changes in the refractive indices. The thermal effect affects the soliton formation process and the long term stability of the soliton frequency combs formed. Current soliton optical frequency combs generation using microresonators typically go through different nonlinear dynamical states including the chaotic state which makes the frequency comb formation processes not predictable. Recently, we proposed a novel deterministic soliton frequency comb generation approach by using a pulse train or even a single pulse as a trigger. The proposed trigger scheme has been analyzed by using numerical simulation taking into account both the nonlinear and thermal effects. In this project, we propose to carry out a comprehensive study to determine the optimal designs for microresonator-based dual comb sources, and investigate deterministic generation of dual frequency combs using the trigger approach. The outcome of the project will be photonic chip microresonator-based dual comb sources for near- to mid-infrared spectroscopy. 光頻率梳由頻域中等間隔的窄線寬梳狀頻率線組成。相干的倍頻程光頻率梳在高精度紅外光譜學（覆蓋分子指紋區）具有重要的應用。目前光頻率梳在應用方面的主要障礙包括脫離實驗室層面的實用性、高性能光頻率梳源以及低成本的頻率線探測技術。其中頻率線探測技術可通過雙頻率梳光譜學方法來解決。此方法將兩支頻率間隔稍有不同的頻率梳混頻，每一對頻率線拍頻得到的頻率成分屬於射頻範疇，可在電域直接探測獲得。因此可將頻寬為幾個太赫茲的光頻率梳壓縮成頻寬只有幾百兆赫茲的電頻率梳。這使得即時、高解析度、高利用率的近紅外到中紅外波長區域的光譜探測成為可能。 就頻率梳源而言，近期研究進展表明基於微諧振腔的光頻率梳在片上光頻率梳源的產生方面具備良好前景，這同樣也為雙頻率梳光譜學提供了極具吸引力的雙頻率梳光源產生平臺。但是，微腔中的Kerr非線性效應在產生孤子態光頻率梳的同時，也會同時引入複雜的非線性動態，比如調製不穩定性、混沌態、多孤子態等等。此外， 由於納米尺寸的微諧振腔的熱容很小，腔內光所耗散的能量很容易將微腔加熱並導致腔的折射率發生變化。這一熱效應會影響產生的孤子態光頻率梳的長時間穩定性。目前產生孤子態光頻率梳的主要方法要求微腔在進入孤子態前首先經過混沌態，這一演化過程使得所產生的孤子態光頻率梳中孤子的個數不可預估。最近，本研究組提出了一種新穎的確定性孤子態光頻率梳產生方法，即利用一光脈衝串或者僅僅一發單一光脈衝作為孤子頻率梳產生的觸發器，可確定性地獲得單腔孤子態頻率梳。我們已通過數值模擬驗證及分析了此觸發方法，模擬中充分考慮了包括熱效應和Kerr非線性效應在內的多種情況。 在此課題中，我們計畫通過綜合性的研究分析以確定基於微諧振腔的雙頻率梳源的最優設計，以及研究利用脈衝觸發方法來產生確定性的雙頻率梳源。課題成果將產出面向近紅外到中紅外光譜學的光子晶片上的微腔雙頻率梳源。

15224118.label: Realisation of objectives
15224118.value: we proposed a novel method to achieve soliton comb generation without the use of tunable lasers by adjusting the coupling coefficient between two coupled nonlinear microcavities. Besides two coupled microcavities, we also propose a Sagnac loop-like structure with simple and easy fabrication to analyze the soliton region and numerically simulate soliton comb generation by tuning the coupling coefficient between the clockwise (CW) and counterclockwise (CCW) modes. We find that both the coupling coefficient of the coupled microcavities and the Sagnac loop-like structure can be tuned by adjusting the gap at the coupling region. We first study deterministic soliton frequency comb generation in LiNbO3 microcavities. The Kerr comb generation with a single-shot pulse trigger is investigated. The trigger pulse is launched at the 5000-th roundtrip. Figure 2(b) shows the soliton number counts of comb generation with different coupling strengths. By using the trigger pulse, the single soliton state is obtained in all 50 simulations for either weak coupling or strong coupling. The central one with the highest peak power eventually evolves to a soliton and the others are all suppressed. The evolution does not experience modulation instability or chaotic states. The generated FD comb corresponds to a single soliton and both FD and SH combs have relatively large spectral range. We note the single-shot trigger method is not applicable to ultrahigh-speed optical clock recovery applications. Instead of using a single-shot pulse to trigger comb generation, we further propose to use a train of pulses for single dissipative Kerr soliton generation. This method releases the ability of subharmonic operation compared with the pulsed pumping method. The proposed pulse train triggering method can also be harnessed for ultrahigh speed all-optical clock recovery with a potential rate of up to terahertz. Our results open up a new path for manipulating single and multi-DKS in microresonators and a robust optical clock recovery module simultaneously possessing ultrahigh speed, on-chip integration, and cost-efficiency. The thermal effect in the formation of dissipative Kerr soliton generation in a LiNbO3 microresonator is studied using the model developed in a recent publication by our research group (Zhe Kang et al., Opt. Express 26, 18563-18577 (2018).) We find that even under strong thermal effect the trigger approach can excite dissipative Kerr solitons in practically fabricated LiNbO3 microresonators. No additional complex engineering is required for thermal compensation. Because of the fast triggering process and relatively slow thermal dynamics caused by the intracavity optical heating, single cavity solitons can be easily excited within a broad parameters range and thermally self-stabilized in long-term evolutions. We propose the MI generation in coupled microcavities with a blue-detuned CW pump laser in this report. We discovered the existence of a new MI region in the blue-detuned pumping regime when an auxiliary cavity with negligible Kerr nonlinearity is coupled to the main nonlinear cavity, which has little thermal effect and is thermally self-stabilized in long-term evolutions. We utilized an auxiliary ring to generate a new bistability regime in the blue-detuned side of the resonance peak by controlling the coupling between the auxiliary and the main ring. We found that a new bistability regime appears on the blue-detuned side. This new bistability regime promises MI and OFC generation on the blue-detuned side which is thermally stable. We found that normal dispersion red-shifts the new bistability regime and anomalous dispersion blue-shifts this regime. The proposed structure is thermally stable when compared with a single-ring cavity. we propose a new dual-comb generation scheme based on coupled nonlinear microcavities with a single pump. By theoretical analysis, we find that the bistability region in coupled microcavities depends on the coupling between the two microcavities. By making use of the tunability of the bistability region in coupled nonlinear microcavities, we numerically simulate dual soliton comb generation by tuning the coupling coefficient with a single frequency cw pump laser. We also investigate a new dual-microcomb generation scheme by using coupled microcavities pumped by two separate pumps. When the coupling coefficient increases, two microcombs emerge from the cw background and the generated combs are in soliton crystal states. The two microcombs have different carrier frequencies and different repetition rates. we propose and demonstrate a novel discrete Fourier domain mode locked (FDML) laser by using intracavity optical intensity modulation. Swept signals with comb lines uniformly distributed in the frequency domain is generated with tailor-made pulse patterns according to the sweep trace of the swept filter. Discrete k-space uniform swept signals with different FSRs and pulse durations are generated in the same laser.

15224118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224118.value: 1) We demonstrate that it is possible to induce MI in normal dispersion microresonators with a coupled-ring structure. The proposed structure is thermally stable when compared with a single-ring cavity. An auxiliary ring also avoids the need to control mode-crossing in a dual-ring structure for anomalous dispersion. 2) We also propose a Sagnac loop-like structure with simple and easy fabrication to analyze the soliton region and numerically simulate soliton comb generation by tuning the coupling coefficient between the clockwise (CW) and counterclockwise (CCW) modes. We find that both the coupling coefficient of the coupled microcavities and Sagnac loop like structure can be tuned by adjusting the gap at the coupling region. 3) We first study deterministic soliton frequency comb generation in LiNbO3 microcavities by single shot pulse trigger. We found that the evolution does not experience modulation instability or chaotic states. We further propose to use a train of pulses for single dissipative Kerr soliton generation. This method releases the ability of subharmonic operation and can also be harnessed for ultrahigh speed all-optical clock recovery with a potential rate up to terahertz. 4) We find that even under strong thermal effect the trigger approach can excite dissipative Kerr solitons in practically fabricated LiNbO3 microresonators. No additional complex engineering is required for thermal compensation. 5) We propose the MI generation in coupled microcavities with blue-detuned CW pump laser in this report. We discovered the existence of a new MI region in the blue-detuned pumping regime when an auxiliary cavity with negligible Kerr nonlinearity is coupled to the main nonlinear cavity, which has little thermal effect and is thermally self-stabilized in long-term evolutions. 6) We proposed a new dual-comb generation scheme based on coupled nonlinear microcavities with a single pump. By theoretical analysis, we find that the bistability region in coupled microcavities depends on the coupling between the two microcavities. We also investigate a new dual-micro comb generation scheme by using coupled microcavities pumped by two separate pumps. The two micro combs have different carrier frequencies and different repetition rates. 7) We propose the use microresonator comb filter in the Fourier domain mode-locked laser to generate a frequency comb-swept laser, which can improve the coherence length to around 100 mm. We also propose and demonstrate a novel discrete FDML laser by using intracavity optical intensity modulation. Discrete k-space uniform swept signals with different FSRs and pulse durations are generated in the same laser.

15224118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224118.value: When studying the coupled microresonators, we found that the blue-detuned MI region and the red-detuned MI region originate from the figure-8 cavity optical path and the main cavity optical path, respectively. The merging means that we can use a single cw pump to excite MI generation with the optical fields in the main cavity optical path and the figure-8 cavity optical path. In this case, there are a number of questions worth exploring. Firstly, are the two MI fields are generated in separate optical path coherent? Secondly, how is the intensity of the MI field generated at this point compared to that of a single microcavity with the same parameters? Thirdly, since a single pump CW laser is used to excite two MI generations, will this regime increase the pump-to-MI conversion efficiency? These questions are to be investigated in our future work. For the ease of numerical simulations, we assume the auxiliary cavity size is identical to the main cavity. The size of the auxiliary cavity determines the FSR of the figure-8 cavity optical path induced by the coupling. In the future, we will investigate how to model the coupled microresonators with different sizes.

15224118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224118.value: In this project, we propose a novel coupled microresonators scheme for frequency comb and dual-comb generation. We find that it is possible to induce MI in normal dispersion microresonators with a coupled-ring structure, which is thermally stable when compared with a single-ring cavity. We also investigate a new dual-microcomb generation scheme by using coupled microcavities pumped by two separate pumps. The two microcombs have different carrier frequencies and different repetition rates. Besides, the deterministic dual comb generation and thermal effect are also systematically investigated. The microresonator comb filter is also applied in Fourier domain mode locked (FDML) laser to improve the coherence length. Intensity modulation is also utilized to generate k-space uniform swept signals with different FSRs. Our findings provides a theoretical understanding and experimental guidance for optical frequency comb and dual comb generation in single microcavity or coupled nonlinear microcavities, which benefit the development of chip-scale comb sources. The microresonator comb filters and intensity modulation for FDML laser also opens up new insights into realized high coherent FDML laser with high flexibility.

15224518.label: Project Objectives
15224518.value: 1. Develop novel inverse problems for calibration of array configurations. In the localization problem for sound source, by reverting the role of dependence, we can formulate the optimization problem of array locations using a set of known source locations. We will study this inverse problem and develop novel optimization methods, including hybrid descent and convex relaxation, in solving for the array configuration. Moreover, we will address the problem with sampling rate offsets by embedding an additional objective function based on the coherence between channels into the inverse problem. In order to understand the theoretical aspect of the problem, we will also investigate the well-posedness of the inverse problem by studying the ambiguity problem caused by the locations of the microphones relative to the source location. Study the distributed beamformer design problem with subband processing. By decomposing the signal into different frequency bands, we will study the near field effect and explore the beamforming capability of individual sensor node and the performance enhancement when they are employed collectively. For certain subband frequencies, we will design suitable distributed beamforming algorithms to optimize on the beamformer performance, including using the generalized eigenvalue decomposition, and study the convergence property of the algorithms comparing with the centralized algorithm when all signals are available simultaneously. Develop non-uniform filter bank for distributed beamforming algorithms. We will develop prototype filter designs with different passband widths, and the window is optimized in the sense that stopband energy is minimized subject to the specification of the passband requirement on distortion. Trade-off between performance including aliasing effect and signal distortion will be addressed in a multi-criteria manner to optimize with respect to a set of filter bank parameters. For the final beamforming output, we will formulate and optimize on the speech quality measures and speech recognition accuracy directly by refining on the subband gains and the variation in the passband widths.
