15224518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224518.value: In this project, we consider the design of broadband acoustic beamformers over distributed acoustic array networks. In our environment, many smart devices with wireless capability are scattered around. If properly deployed, they can form a very powerful sensor array network and many innovative applications can be developed. One important application is to enhance speech signals and suppress unwanted noise via beamforming techniques. If successful, this can enhance significantly the capability of voice control device for the development of intelligent man-machine speech interactive systems. Indeed, voice control is an attractive feature that provides a natural mean of remote control and has the potential to change our lifestyle. However, it is well known that the performance of speech recognition engine diminishes rapidly when there is a mismatch between the training and testing conditions. In order to design such a system with smooth operations, acoustic noise should be suppressed so that the enhanced speech can be recognized accurately. There is a pressing need to conduct research in this area to ensure accuracy and efficiency. The formation of this kind of microphone array network is a very new concept. The design of beamforming algorithms over such a network is very different from the conventional one in which all signals are available simultaneously. For a successful distributed algorithm, it should avoid energy inefficient data centralization and allow distributing the processing load over different nodes, as each node only contains partial data with limited energy supplies. Moreover, the array configuration is important when it comes to localization applications, but is rather difficult to calibration due to the fact that sensors are being distributed arbitrarily in the surrounding. In view of this, we propose to study the optimization of distributed beamformer systems and calibration of array configurations, which can operate in the near field to enhance signals in a region with distributed sensor arrays. First of all, a set of inverse problems will be developed for finding array configurations. Sampling rate offsets and synchronization errors will also be addressed. To develop efficient distributed algorithms, subband processing will be investigated to derive schemes for distributing updates of filters. Finally, both speech quality and speech recognition accuracy will be optimized using the beamforming output with respect to a set of subband parameters. The research outcomes will significantly enhance the capability of distributed beamforming system and localization accuracy. We believe this research will benefit academia as well as industry. 在這個項目中，我們考慮分佈式陣列網絡的寬帶聲波束形成器的設計。在我們的環境中，有很多智能設備具有無線功能分散在各地。如果部署得當，它們可以組成一個非常好的強大的傳感器陣列網絡和許多創新應用可以開發。一重要的應用是增強語音信號並抑制不需要的噪聲波束形成技術。如果成功，這可以顯著提高其能力用於智能的語音控制裝置系統上。實際上，語音控制是一個很有吸引力的功能，提供了自然的遙控器，有可能改變我們的生活方式。然而，眾所周知當存在噪音時，語音識別引擎的性能會迅速下降。為了設計這樣一個系統擁有順暢的操作，應抑制噪聲，使語音增強可以準確識別。迫切需要在這方面進行研究確保准確性和效率。 這種麥克風陣列網絡的形成是一個非常新的概念。該這種網絡上的波束形成算法的設計與傳統的非常不同。為了成功分佈式算法，應避免能量低效的數據集中和允許在不同節點上分配處理負載，因為每個節點僅包含部分節點能源供應有限的數據。而且，陣列配置很重要來自本地化應用程序，但由於事實，很難校準傳感器在周圍任意分佈。 有鑑於此，我們建議研究分佈式波束形成器系統的優化和陣列配置的校準，可以在近場操作以增強具有分佈式傳感器陣列的區域中的信號。首先，一組反問題將開發用於查找陣列配置。採樣率偏移和同步錯誤也將得到解決。要開發高效的分佈式算法，將調查子帶處理以導出用於分發更新的方案過濾器。最後，將優化語音質量和語音識別準確度使用關於一組子帶參數的波束成形輸出。該研究成果將顯著提高分佈式波束成形的能力系統和本地化準確性。我們相信這項研究也將有利於學術界作為行業。

15224518.label: Realisation of objectives
15224518.value: In this project, our main objectives are to investigate different distributed beamformer design problems and develop beamforming algorithms. We also want to study novel inverse problems for calibration of array configurations. Following the objectives of the proposal, we have published 5 journal papers, 1 paper under major revision and 1 conference presentation to achieve all the objectives. To summarize, the research team has investigated and proposed several distributed beamforming methods with convergence analysis. Novel inverse problems for calibration of array configurations have been explored. The details are in the following. In distributed beamforming, with the advent of wireless smart devices equipped with microphones, a wireless acoustic sensor network (WASN) can be formed to enhance the speech signals. There are several challenges. First, although the sensor coverage becomes larger and speech signal can be enhanced with the increment of microphone arrays, the increased computational burden cannot be ignored. Therefore, decentralized schemes such as distributed or blockwise iterative techniques and subband processing are essential for the success of the design so that computational burden is shared by all the nodes and the entire sampling data is fused iteratively in the WASN. Second, reliability of data transmission determines the performance of the designed beamformers, since faulty data will drift the filter coefficients quickly and deviated from the target location. In view of this, we have investigated the gossip algorithm in which information exchanges between adjacent nodes constantly and successively. The gossip algorithm has the advantages that it is computationally efficient and it does not require the WASN to remain to be the same throughout the whole process. In solving the data reliability issue, we have proposed a novel framework of the compound distributed beamformer where nodes are grouped and the system are embedded with blockchain technology. This is a two-level communication scheme containing the intra-group data sharing based on blockchain technique as well as the inter-group data communication via gossip algorithms. We propose three distributed MMSE beamformers using gossip algorithms. Our proposed distributed MMSE beamformers outperform the distributed delay-and-sum beamformer and MVDR beamformer in a simulated reverberation environment. Based on the blockchain technique, a data protection scheme is also proposed to avoid faulty data transmissions. We have evaluated the results by the noise suppression measure and speech distortion measure [1]. Another distributed beamforming method is based on convex optimization. In the literature, it is noted that most of the distributed approaches for speech enhancement are based on blockwise optimization techniques, such as the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). However, the convergence results on ADMM-like algorithms for such multi-block optimization problems is problematic except for the two-block optimization model. In view of this, we have developed a randomly permuted alternating direction method (RP-ADMM) of multipliers for distributed beamforming [3]. This method transforms the original optimization problem into a class of sequential subproblems, and then distributes the computational workload to each node of the sensor array. It obtains a great reduction in the computational complexity and makes parallel computing achievable. We have shown that the proposed method is applicable to cases with blocks bigger than 3 and we have established the expected convergence of the proposed algorithm. We prove that the necessary condition for convergence is satisfied without further assumption. The segmental signal-to-noise-plus-interference ratio (SNIRseg) and the PESQ score to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm for wireless acoustic sensor network. We have further studied the use of a fixed equalizer for speech enhancement applications. Two of the most widely used objective measures in speech enhancement are perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) and the short-time objective intelligibility (STOI). An improvement in PESQ gives an overall improvement in speech quality, and STOI provides an indication of how much speech intelligibility is improved. We pose these two measures as evaluation criteria in a multi-objective optimal problem setting. The Pareto optimality is then used to produce a set of candidate solutions for the multi-objective problem. Experimental results with various real-world noises show that the trained fixed equalizer improves both the PESQ and STOI scores [5]. In the design process, the beamformer design problem is often formulated as an optimization problem to get close to a given target response function. Under this framework, we have studied a general semi-finite optimization problem parametrized by frequency bands. In order to understand the performance limit of the designed beamformers for different frequency bands, we have discovered that the frequency response function can be optimized directly instead of the filter coefficients, which represents the performance limit when the filter length is infinite. To compute the limit efficiently, we proposed a novel method which decomposes the problem into a series of simplified subproblems. By taking the maximum of these optimal values, the final limit can be obtained. It is very useful to know and analyze the limit of the optimal value series as filter length increases. This will provide guidance to determine if a problem is posed properly and to set the filter length and the filterbank in order to achieve a desired performance [2]. We have studied another popular method for signal enhancement over distributed arrays, namely blind signal separation (BSS) method, which separates the desired signals from a mixed observed signal by making full use of spatial information. Spatial information refers the fact that the sources originate from different location in space and thus provides the diversity for the separation. This diversity can be further enhanced by optimizing the different array configurations as opposed to a fixed location. We attempt to fill the research gap by studying the effect of sensor array configuration on the performance of BSS [4]. Such study will enable the incorporation of optimized placement for improved spatial information to enable the best source separation performance. As opposed to focusing on a specific configuration, a hybrid descent method is proposed to optimize the performance of BSS for the best sensor array configuration on the allowable placement space as the number of sensors and the reverberation time (RT) change. Results show that the optimized sensor array placement greatly improves the separation performance of the BSS system across the different reverberation times. The results also reveal that the sensors tend to cluster on the desired source when the RT is less than 200 ms and spread out otherwise. Finally, we have studied the sensor array localization problem when the array configuration and locations are decision variables, with some sound sources at the designated location. In our method, firstly, the TDOA between each pair of microphones is estimated and transformed into distance measurements between sensors. It results in a set of nonlinear hyperbolic equations. Then, we can estimate the location by solving the set of equations. However, it is a highly nonlinear problem to find the intersection of hyperbolic equations. To convert the localization problem into a convex optimization problem, we employ a convex relaxation method for solving the group microphone localization problem extensively and propose a novel mixed relaxation model. In this way, very efficient algorithms can be derived by exploring the properties of semi-definite programming (SDP) and second-order cone programming (SOCP). We have studied the theoretical structure and the characteristics of the optimal solution. Then, in the experimental part, we have tested the method with simulated and real data [6].

15224518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224518.value: In the formulation of distributed beamformer design problems, we have studied various approaches to obtain beamforming algorithms. The first one is based on convex optimization via ADMM-like algorithms. It is known that the convergence results on ADMM-like algorithms for such multi-block optimization problems is problematic except for the two-block optimization model. We have developed a randomly permuted alternating direction method (RP-ADMM) of multipliers for distributed beamforming [2]. We have shown that the proposed method is applicable to cases with blocks bigger than 3 and we have established the expected convergence of the proposed algorithm. In addition to the development of decentralized schemes, reliability of data transmission determines the performance of the designed beamformers, since faulty data will drift the filter coefficients quickly and deviated from the target location. We have proposed a novel framework of the compound distributed beamformer where nodes are grouped and the system are embedded with blockchain technology [1]. Based on the blockchain technique, a data protection scheme is also proposed to avoid faulty data transmissions. We have studied blind signal separation (BSS) method for signal enhancement over wireless sensors. We attempt to fill the research gap by studying the effect of sensors placement on the performance of BSS. Such study will enable the incorporation of optimized placement for improved spatial information to enable the best source separation performance. Results show that the optimized sensor placement greatly improves the separation performance of the BSS system across the different reverberation times. As for performance indicator, we have developed optimization methods to optimize objective measures directly, including perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) and the short-time objective intelligibility (STOI). In acoustic localization, we have studied the sensor array localization problem when the array configuration and locations are decision variables, with some sound sources at the designated location. We have proposed a novel mixed SDP-SOCP relaxation model and derive the characteristics of the optimal solution.

15224518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224518.value: In the present project, we have studied the design of distributed beamformers and developed several distributed beamforming algorithms. In addition, we have developed a localization method for array calibration with a given set of anchor sound sources. As a future extension, it would be of interest to investigate how to combine both approaches to form an automatic calibrated beamforming system with microphone array scattering around and with multiple sound sources. Also, we have studied extensively how to apply the hybrid descent method for optimizing the configuration of wireless sensor arrays to achieve better performance. Currently we have carried out the study for blind signal separation. The approach can be applied to general beamforming system in order to under if a subset of wireless sensors will provide sufficient accuracy. Finally, it is possible to study the optimization of objective measures directly for beamforming system.

15224618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224618.value: 地震的驚人破壞力常常給城市鄉村帶來巨大的生命財產損失。針對地震的各種防災減災技術，在全世界範圍內都受到了廣泛的關注。其中，隔震支座作為一個成功地範例，已應用于許多實際的土木工程項目中，用來增加土木結構的抗震能力。但是基於過往的研究和工程經驗，傳統的隔震支座也存在一些問題，譬如，一旦隔震支座在強震下出現永久變形，修復的技術難度和經濟費用都將非常高昂。 本項目將研究和開發一種全新的隔震支座，通過利用板式橡膠支座和U形形狀記憶合金阻尼器的新穎組合，實現震後極小的殘餘變形。這種新型的隔震支座，除了具有傳統隔震支座保護結構的功能之外，還擁有震後自復位的功能和可以重複使用的優良特性，因此可以最大程度的降低地震后的修復費用和修復時間。申請人的前期研究已經初步顯示了這種新型隔震支座的優勢。本項目將通過系統的試驗研究和理論分析，進一步對這種自復位的隔震支座在中低層房屋結構中的行為模擬、抗震性能以及抗震設計進行研究。而這種自復位隔震技術的開發，將能夠進一步提升關鍵性結構的抗震能力，以確保它們能在強震后能夠快速恢復并投入使用，這將對災后的救援產生重要的意義。

15224618.label: Realisation of objectives
15224618.value: This project proposed and investigated a novel type of self-centering seismic base isolator with shape memory alloy (SMA) U-shaped dampers, termed SMAUDs, and investigated seismic performance and design of building structures with SMAUDs. The proposed four objectives have been fully achieved during the 3.5-year project period. The significant achievements of this completed project include: 1. Cyclic tests and finite element modeling of SMAUDs [Objectives 1 & 4] The mechanical properties of SMAUDs, such as the strength, self-centering (SC) ability, and energy-dissipating ability, were systematically investigated through experimental and numerical studies. The results demonstrated that SMAUDs exhibited ideal flag-shaped SC behavior even under large displacement amplitude. In particular, the low temperature effect was studied to evaluated the practicability of SMAUDs in cold outdoor environments. 2. Cyclic tests and finite element modeling of SMA angles [Objective 1] In addition to SMAUDs, another promising type of SMA elements, namely SMA angles, were systematically investigated as well. The FE simulations and mechanical tests of SMA angles were conducted to explore the feasibility of SMA angles as seismic-resistant SC devices. 3. Development, tests and simulations of SMAUD isolators [Objective 1] SMAUD isolator prototypes with different configurations were designed, fabricated, and experimentally tested. Quasi-static cyclic loading tests were carried out on the SMAUD isolators to evaluate cyclic behaviors and performances. Results showed that the proposed SMAUD isolators can achieve flag-shaped hysteresis loops associated with evidently reduced residual deformation under cyclic loading. Refined Bouc-Wen models were developed to simulate the hysteresis behaviors of SMAUD isolators and traditional base isolators. 4. Shake table tests of steel frame equipped with SMAUD isolators [Objectives 2 & 4] Shake table tests of a 1/4-scaled two-story one-bay steel moment resisting frame (MRF) equipped with SMAUD isolators were conducted. The seismic performance of the frame with SMAUD isolators was systematically evaluated under a series of seismic ground motions covering frequency earthquakes (FE), design basis earthquakes (DBE), maximum considered earthquakes (MCE), and near-fault earthquakes. In particular, its seismic performance was compared with another MRF equipped with conventional base isolators. 5. Seismic analysis of multis-story buildings equipped with SMAUD isolators [Objectives 2 & 4] The seismic performances of six-story reinforced concrete (RC) frame buildings with traditional base isolators and SMAUD isolators were simulated and compared under far- and near-field earthquakes. Seismic fragility analyses were carried out through incremental dynamic analysis (IDA). Compared with the considerable residual deformation of the traditional isolated system, the SMAUD isolated system exhibits negligible residual deformation that can significantly avoid normal serviceability disruption while achieving high performance objectives. 6. Performance-based seismic design (PBSD) of frame buildings equipped with SMAUD isolators [Objective 3] A two-level PBSD approach for frame structures isolated by SMAUD isolator was proposed to enable the accurate control of seismic performance objectives at two different seismic intensity levels (i.e., DBE and MCE) during the design process. Design examples demonstrated that the two-level PBSD approach can satisfactorily achieve the predefined performance objectives at both levels. The PBSD approach was further extended to the design of other types of SC structures, including SC braced frames and hybrid frame systems, to guarantee the desired high-performance objectives through advanced design approaches. 7. Other types of SMA-based SC structural systems [Objectives 1-4] In addition to buildings with SMAUD isolators, a variety of SMA-enabled SC structural elements and systems have been explored during the project, including but not limited to, SC steel beam-column connections, SC timber beam-column connections, SC RC walls, SC precast segmental columns, SC braced frames, and hybrid braced frames. They show very promising seismic performance in terms of earthquake resilience and life-cycle benefits.

15224618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224618.value: The major findings and outcome of this project include: (1) Test and numerical results demonstrated that SMAUDs could exhibit excellent SC capability and stable energy dissipation under both in-plane and out-of-plane loadings. The adjacent plate has a positive role in the deformation mechanism under in-plane loading, whereas it has a slight effect under out-of-plane loading. Two detailed FE models validated global hysteresis loops and deformation shapes through the comparisons with experimental results. [Research Output: Journal Papers 1,6] (2) Two novel designs of SC seismic base isolator utilizing SMAUD have been proposed, fabricated and tested. Test results demonstrated that these SC base isolators can exhibit satisfactory SC capability and stable energy dissipation. The hysteresis characteristics of the SC base isolators are nearly isotropic, enabling the SC base isolators to resist seismic actions in any horizontal direction. [Research Output: Journal Paper 3] (3) Shake table tests of a 1/4-scaled two-story one-bay steel MRF equipped with SMAUD isolators indicated that the MRF equipped with SMAUD isolators could exhibit superior seismic performance under multiple seismic hazard levels. Under MCE, an obvious residual deformation was observed in the traditional base isolators, whereas almost no residual deformation was observed in the SMAUD isolators. A numerical study of the MRF equipped with SMAUD isolators was also conducted and agreed well with the experimental results. [Research Output: Journal Paper 17] (4) IDA of RC frames with SMAUD isolators clearly indicated that compared with the conventional isolators, the SMAUD isolators can improve the response of the traditional isolated building in terms of isolator displacement ductility without incurring any residual deformation. SMAUD isolators can return to the original position rapidly after earthquake shakings, which can maintain the normal serviceability of the superstructure and the isolation function to withstand immediate aftershocks or future earthquakes. [Research Output: Journal Paper 16] (5) The proposed PBSD approach can accurately control structural performance objectives at DBE and MCE seismic intensity levels. A four-story frame structure equipped with SMAUD isolators was designed as an example, which indicated the effectiveness of the proposed PBSD approach. Later on, the PBSD approach was upgraded to a machine learning-based PBSD approach, which can control the peak displacement, residual displacement and floor accelerations of the SC frames with SMA elements. [Research Output: Journal Papers 10, 13, 14] (6) In addition to SMAUD isolators, a variety of interesting applications of SMA materials in earthquake engineering have been proposed and investigated. [Research Output: Journal Papers 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15]

15224618.value: The following promising research directions can be explored in the future: 1. The seismic applications of SMAUD isolators in bridge structures will be systematically explored; and 2. The low temperature effect on SMAUD isolators will be systematically investigated to enable applications of SMAUD isolators in extremely cold environment.

15224618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224618.value: Among a variety of seismic response mitigation technologies, seismic base isolators have been widely adopted in the protection of real-world civil engineering structures from severe seismic damage. However, past studies and implementations identified a potential problem associated with conventional base isolators: permanent isolator deformation after earthquakes may lead to a difficult and costly repair. This project developed and investigated a novel type of SC seismic base isolators using shape memory alloy U-shaped dampers (SMAUDs) as critical components. A systematic research program, including the modelling and testing of SMAUD isolators, numerical and experimental studies of frame buildings installed with SMAUD isolators, and seismic fragility analyses and performance-based seismic design of multi-story frames with SMAUD isolators, has been completed in this project. The research outcome indicated that SMAUD isolators can achieve unparalleled performance in controlling residual displacement compared with conventional base isolators. Therefore, SMAUD isolators will be a promising device for the seismic protection of structural systems.

15224818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224818.value: We propose to develop an optimal trunk-feeder network for a city with demand that varies over space, where the trunk (backbone) network is operated by rapid transit (e.g. rail) and the feeder systems are operated by bus, mini-bus, or van, which transport transit patrons between the local area and the neighbouring trunk station. This type of network can be efficient because the type, strategy, and design of the localised feeder systems can vary over the city. We propose to formulate continuum approximation (CA) models for the trunk network, fixed-route feeder, and flex-route feeder (a.k.a. demand-responsive connector, DRC). In particular, we will model a number of operating strategies for the DRC systems under stochastic demand. The solution of the trunk-feeder model will be used to layout trunk lines, specify the service regions of each feeder system, and the feeder service types, strategies and other design features. Built upon the CA solutions, we will further develop discrete models that account for local geometric irregularities and physical constraints, to refine the feeder designs and operating strategies. We will also incorporate the optimal selection of DRC stops and the patrons' preferred pick-up time windows into the model. Efficient heuristic methods will be developed to solve the complicated mathematical programs in reasonable computation time. The results can be directly used by the agency to operate the vehicles. These customised DRC design models will be implemented in the web- and app-based systems, and be tested via real-world case studies. 本項目將建立城市的“幹線－支線”公共交通網絡的最優設計理論与模型。幹線公交服務將由鐵路或快速巴士提供，而支線（接駁）公交服務將由普通巴士、小巴、或商務車提供。此類支線公交服務將負責將在幹線站點与乘客的起點或最終目的地之間運送乘客。由於支線的車型、運營方式（固定線路或需求回應）、線路設計等均可隨城市內等不同地點而變化，此類幹支線網絡的設計有相當大大自由度，從而保證了設計的高效性。項目中將應用連續近似理論（Continuum Approximation, CA）進行優化設計，並將特別關注需求回應式支線服務（demand responsive connector, DRC）在多種運營策略下的最優設計。我們將考慮實際的，隨空間變化的隨機需求。優化的結果將用於布設幹線公交線路、設定支線公交的服務範圍、支線類型及其運營策略等。 本項目還將基於連續近似模型的最優解繼續建立更為細緻準確的離散模型，用以求解各類支線公交（特別是DRC）的最優設計方案。離散模型將考慮支線服務的空間範圍的不規則性、道路的實際約束（如路口等），從而得到準確并能立即實用的設計方案。我們並將在離散模型中加入用戶預約服務的考量，并據此選擇最優的公交停靠站點、服務時間等。我們將採用準確調試的啓發式算法來求解離散模型。結果將可用於安排支線公交，尤其是DRC的線路設計、調度、運營等實際工作。最后，本項目將探索如何研發基於互聯網和手機應用的軟件以供公交服務商和乘客使用，并嘗試展開實際或仿真項目測試。

15224818.label: Realisation of objectives
15224818.value: Objective 1: Developing continuum approximation models for jointly optimizing a trunk (e.g. rail) network with a localized feeder system consisting of a mix of fixed- and flex-route feeder services. We have developed continuum approximation models for: (i) optimizing a fixed-route feeder service network serving a trunk station; (ii) optimizing a flex-route feeder service network serving a trunk station; (iii) optimizing a trunk-feeder network consisting of a trunk transit network and many feeder systems of fixed- and flex-route services and bike-sharing services. We also consider various trunk-line services such as skip-stop services. Results are compared against previous transit network designs under spatially heterogeneous demand. Two papers have been published on top journals and two are submitted. Objective 2: Developing continuum approximation models for comparing the optimal flex-route feeder designs under various strategies and stochastic demand. We have developed continuum approximation models for flex-route service design with: (i) a strategy involving the optimal travel-salesman-problem tours; and (ii) a strategy using the sweeping method of Daganzo (1984). We compared their system costs and identified the best design under various operating conditions and stochastic demand. One paper is in preparation. We have also extended the work to investigate similar problems that can also be solved using the continuum approximation approach, for example, the fleet management problem. Another paper has been published. Objective 3: Developing discrete models for optimizing the routing and scheduling of DRCs that consider the patrons’ preferred boarding locations and time windows, and efficient solution algorithms. We have developed discrete optimization models that jointly optimize the routing, scheduling and meeting points of flex-route feeder service (demand-responsive connectors), which are solve by the genetic algorithm. We have also extended the work to model the scheduling problem of vessels using a similar approach. One paper has been published and another is near completion. Objective 4: Developing prototype simulation programs (and if time permitting, web- and app-based systems) for testing the customized DRC optimization models. We have developed simulation programs to implement the optimal continuum-approximation design and calculate the overall system cost of the concrete transit network design. Results have verified the accuracy of our continuum approximation models. The simulation programs can also be used for examining the cost estimates of the discrete models for flex-route transit optimization. References: Daganzo, C. F. (1984). The length of tours in zones of different shapes. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, 18(2), 135-145.

15224818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224818.value: The major findings are summarized as follows: 1. For fixed-route feeder networks, optimizing heterogeneous line, stop spacings and headways under heterogeneous demand produces significant cost savings compared to homogeneous designs and favors the use of smaller buses. Greater demand heterogeneity renders more cost savings. Feeder lines should be designed for buses to travel along the shorter side of the service region to pick up and drop off patrons and travel nonstop along the longer side to the rail station. When conditions permit, trunk and feeder schedules should be coordinated in both service directions (each direction yields a distinct but substantial cost saving). 2. For flex-route feeder networks, accounting for passengers’ wait times at home results in distinct benefits for the optimal-TSP-tour strategy and the sweeping strategy. The two strategies’ dominating conditions are identified. Considering the second-order effect of random demand largely affects the optimal designs. More flexible designs involving a hybrid strategy, spatially varying service zones, and pre-defined meeting points are developed. The threshold demand between fixed-route and flex-route feeder designs is derived. 3. An optimal trunk-feeder network with the optimal trunk line layout and the optimal choice and design of mixed feeder services would render a greater cost savings compared to previous transit network designs under spatially heterogeneous demand. 4. Integrating shared-bikes as a feeder mode, and skip-stop service scheme as a trunk design would further reduce the generalized system cost. 5. Similar methodologies can be applied to transportation research questions beyond the trunk-feeder network design, e.g., the fleet management problem and the vessel scheduling problem.

15224818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224818.value: Potential future extensions of the present project include: 1. Optimal trunk-and-feeder transit network designs considering more flexible and cost-effective trunk designs, like the designs involving: (i) a hybrid structure; (ii) line bifurcating and merging; (iii) irregular city shapes; and (iv) irregular street network layouts. The first two extensions can be developed by using more complicated continuum approximation models and more advanced solution methods. The third extension can be explored using a hybrid methodology of analytical and simulation. The last one may employ simulation-based optimization techniques. 2. Novel designs involving emerging technologies, e.g., autonomous modular buses, electric buses, etc. These research extensions can be explored by extending the continuum approximation methods to account for the electric bus charging needs (including both plug-in charging and opportunistic charging) and the modular bus features. 3. Real-world implementations of the design methods. We will seek collaborations with local, Chinese mainland, and overseas transit agencies and bus companies for potential collaborations. Research works can be pursued by applying for future research projects like General Research Fund and Collaborative Research Fund. Collaboration with the industry can be pursued by applying for Innovation and Technology Fund or Smart Traffic Fund.

15224818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224818.value: We have developed advanced continuum approximation models for optimally designing the fixed-route feeder bus systems (where each bus line follows a fixed route and set of stops), flex-route feeder bus systems (where a bus does not follow a fixed route and set of stops), and various types of trunk-and-feeder networks (where a rail transit network serves as the trunk service and feeder buses and shared bikes carry passengers to and from rail stations). These network designs capture more realistic operating details. For example, they are heterogeneous in that the line, stop spacings, and headway vary with locations and bus lines. They can be implemented to design optimal transit networks for cities where the passenger demand is not evenly distributed. Our models are simpler, more general, and easier to calculate. These designs are shown to be more cost-effective than previous transit network designs. The models are validated via simulation tools. Many insights are generated, which inform practical designs and operations of urban transit networks.

15224918.label: Project Objectives
15224918.value: Develop new storage techniques for spatial-temporal data stores with high-throughput processing and minimum storage footprint. We aim to achieve significant improvement on the write throughput (more than one million inserts per second per server) and storage footprint (more than 10 times space reduction) without compromising query performance compared with state-of-the-art techniques. Develop cloud-storage-aware optimization techniques to reduce the storage access latencies. Specially, we will study how to determine the best file sizes for different types of files, and how to exploit different reliability schemes and new opportunities introduced by SSDs. Integrate the above two studies to develop an experimental framework for evaluation.

15224918.label: Realisation of objectives
15224918.value: The project has been going very well, and all objectives have been 100% achieved. With the support of this fund, two PhD students (WANG, Tianyu and GUO, Yang) at CUHK were recruited/enrolled in August 2019 and are expected to graduated in July 2024. Three undergraduate students, Zhilin YAN (graduated in 2020), Yi JI (graduated in 2022) and Yifan Zhou (graduated in 2022), at CUHK, were recruited to conduct undergraduate research. In total, 3 journal papers and 4 conference papers have been published. Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 1, in [C3], we have proposed a novel storage model with query-aware indexing, called Cymo, that can adapt different query patterns for spatio-temporal big data systems. Our basic idea is to divide the spatio-temporal space into multiple subspaces so each subspace can effectively exploit its query characteristics to obtain the best storage model. Specifically, Cymo includes a learning model that can predict query patterns for each subspace based on historical workloads. Also, in Cymo, a virtual layer is proposed to hide the heterogeneity of different storage models with a unified query interface, by which different storage models can be hidden and transparent from applications while different query patterns can be effectively exploited in query optimization. We have implemented Cymo based on HBase and further integrated it into GeoMesa, a representative spatio-temporal big data system. Experimental results based on real taxi datasets show that Cymo improves query latencies significantly (1.53× to 10×) compared with GeoMesa. We have released the open source code of Cymo for public access. We also investigate effective key-value caching as it is one of critical components in a spatial database system. By effectively caching spatial data, we can enhance the system throughput and query performance. Specifically, in [J1], we present a dynamic on-line compression scheme, called SlimCache, to improve the cache hit ratio by virtually expanding the usable cache space through data compression. We have investigated various compression granularities to achieve a balance between compression ratio and speed, and also leveraged the unique workload characteristics to efficiently identify and separate hot and cold data. In order to dynamically adapt to workload changes during runtime, we have designed an adaptive hot/cold area partitioning method based on a cost model. To avoid unnecessary compression, SlimCache also estimates data compressibility to determine whether the data are suitable for compression or not. We have implemented a prototype based on Twitter's Fatcache. Our experimental results show that SlimCache can accommodate more key-value items in flash by up to 223.4%, effectively increasing throughput and reducing average latency by up to 380.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 2, in [C4], we present TimeUnion, an efficient timeseries management system tailored for hybrid cloud storage services (e.g. fast cloud block stores and slow cloud object stores). TimeUnion contains a novel unified data model to represent both independent timeseries and groups of timeseries, which is capable of handling diverse use cases of timeseries. In TimeUnion, since the main bottleneck of the current timeseries systems is the overuse of memory, we also propose a memory-efficient data structures for timeseries to maximize the number of timeseries a compute instance can maintain. To absorb the memory data chunks quickly, we present our time-partitioned LSM-tree with tailored architecture, compaction mechanism, out-of-order data handling, and dynamic level size adjustment for timeseries data. We prototype TimeUnion with C++ from scratch and evaluate it on AWS EC2 with AWS EBS (cloud block store) and AWS S3 (cloud object store). Compared to the storage engine of Cortex, TimeUnion can handle at least 5x more timeseries, and achieve at least 24.8% higher insertion throughput and 49.8% lower query latency. We have released the open-source code of TimeUnion for public access. We also propose a new storage model with effective data flushing for timeseries big data systems [J3]. It contains two techniques: (1) a new storage model, which enables efficient queries on compressed data by utilizing the shared timestamp column to easily locate corresponding metric values; (2) a novel two-level epoch-based memory manager, which allows the system to gradually flush and reclaim in-memory data while unreclaimed data can still serve queries. We have implemented a fully functional prototype based on Prometheus tsdb, a representative open-source performance monitoring system, and conducted extensive experiments with real and synthetic timeseries data. Experimental results show that, compared with Prometheus, our techniques can significantly improve the insertion throughput, query latency and space usage. Furthermore, we have investigated various SSD techniques to reduce the IO latency. Specifically, in [C1], to optimize big data workloads such as spatial big data, we propose a holistic solution to address several important and challenging issues in storage data management in light of emerging NVDIMM-based architecture: namely, new performance modelling, NVDIMM-based migration, and architectural support for NVDIMMs on migration optimization. In [C2], we propose a flexible storage interface called Prism-SSD that exports the SSD hardware in three levels of abstraction: as a raw flash media with its low-level details, as a group of functions to manage flash capacity, or as a configurable block device. This multi-level abstraction allows developers to choose the degree in which they desire to control the flash hardware in a manner that best suits their applications' semantics and performance objectives. In [J2], as SMR has huge potential to significantly increase the disk capacity and reduce the storage cost, we also investigated effective techniques to optimized SMR disks. Specifically, we for the first time propose an approach called Tiler to manage SMR disks by dividing the physical space into small autonomous regions (ARs). Each AR can manage its space allocation, address mapping and cleaning independently. By managing these ARs in a log-structured way, RMWs can be avoided; besides, ARs can also help update data when the adjacent tracks contain no valid data. Tiler is capable of partitioning a large-scale cleaning into self-contained-small-scale cleaning and thus, the data that need to be relocated are limited inside independent ARs, which further minimizes the performance overhead. Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. Specifically, we have developed various experimental platforms and prototypes. Our experiments are conducted on a cluster with MongoDB in [J1], and the evaluations are based on simulation environments in [J2, C1] and an Open-Channel SSD in [C2]. In [J3, C3, C4], three prototypes have been open-sourced and released for public access. Specifically, in [C3], we have implemented one prototype based on HBase as a library with 6,269 lines of code, and a spatial-temporal system is further developed by integrating our prototype into GeoMesa, a representative spatio-temporal big data system, with another 286 lines of code. Both the prototype and the query dataset have been released for public access. In [C4], our prototype is developed with C++ from scratch and is evaluated with Amazon cloud services including AWS EC2 with AWS EBS (cloud block store) and AWS S3 (cloud object store). In [J3], we have implemented our storage model based on Prometheus tsdb v0.8.0 (the storage engine of Prometheus) where we replace the storage model and add our memory manager.

15224918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224918.value: For spatio-temporal big data systems, we propose a novel storage model with query-aware indexing that can adapt different query patterns, and a dynamic on-line compression scheme to improve the cache hit ratio by virtually expanding the usable cache space through data compression. One direction for future work is to integrate these techniques into one system to further optimize the system performance. For cloud-storage-aware optimization with SSDs, we have proposed various techniques to exploit hybrid cloud storage services and developed new SSD-based storage techniques. It will be an interesting direction to further explore the trade-offs and characteristics of the memory and storage systems in cloud environments (such as local memory, local SSD storage, local HDD storage, and cloud storage). It is also a promising direction to integrate in-storage computing into our techniques to optimize spatial-temporal big data systems.

15224918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224918.value: Spatial-temporal data are emerging to become a major big-data workload with the rapid growth of GPS-embedded mobile devices and the rise of the Internet of Things. In such kind of big data systems, high-performance, space-efficient storage with the support for real-time spatial-temporal queries is urgently needed. However, spatial-temporal data cannot be efficient processed by spatial or temporal databases that focus on either spatial or time-series data. Existing solutions for spatial-temporal big-data applications all adopt a database-centric approach in which existing distributed databases, such as HBase, are used to store records. This practice, though simple, limits the exploitation of the characteristics of spatial-temporal data, and cannot cope with the continuously-growing throughput and space demands. On the other hand, with simple structures and WORM (Write Once Read Many), spatial-temporal data are suitable for specially-tailored data stores. Thus, in this project, we aim to investigate new storage techniques with ground-up spatial-temporal data stores. Specially, for spatial-temporal data stores, we have two objectives, namely, handling high-throughput and reducing storage footprint. For cloud-storage-aware optimization, we will focus on reducing the access latencies introduced by underlying cloud storage systems. Our techniques can be applied to a large variety of spatial-temporal data.

15300018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300018.value: 撓曲電效應描述了在機械應變梯度下產生電極化響應。由於應變梯度可以破壞空間反轉對稱性，因此撓曲電流允許從所有介電材料中的晶格變形產生電極化。柔性電子學的研究對於理解背後的物理學很有意義，這種物理學迄今尚不清楚，並且在諸如傳感器和能量採集器等電子設備的應用中很有前途。目前對柔性電子學的研究主要集中在從多晶陶瓷到有機聚合物和單晶的塊狀材料，但對於薄膜來說仍然非常罕見，而對於氧化物異質結構的界面則是空白的。然而，由於薄膜中存在顯著的應變梯度，薄膜中的撓曲電可能更顯著。因此，薄膜撓曲電性的研究及其與界面態的相互作用是非常有趣的，特別是在異質結構的界面上。 在這個項目中，我們將使用我們的定制儀器將應變梯度應用於外延生長的氧化物薄膜，並研究薄膜中產生的柔性電子以及界面處的撓電感應電傳輸調製。特別是，將對LaAlO3 / SrTiO3（LAO / STO）界面的柔性電子及其對電輸運性質的調製進行深入研究。 LAO / STO異質結構是在非極性STO基板上包含非常薄且電極化的LAO層的模型系統，其具有金屬導電界面，其被廣泛接受為二維電子氣（2DEG）。通過表徵響應於施加的應變梯度在薄膜上產生的界面傳輸調製和撓曲電流，我們可以在這樣一個有趣的界面系統中深入理解撓曲電的形成機理以及撓曲電和界面態之間的相互作用。 本項目將重點關注以下幾個方面： （1）存在應變梯度時外延氧化物薄膜產生撓曲電的機理; （2）彎曲電感應電遷移性質調製到薄膜和氧化物異質結構的界面; （3）晶體取向和溫度依賴的撓曲電性及其誘導的界面傳輸調製; （4）薄膜中的撓曲電性和鐵電性之間的相互作用以及氧化物異質結構的界面。 該項目的成果將促進人們對理解氧化物薄膜中柔性電子物理學的興趣，從而為複雜的氧化物理學開闢了一條新途徑，並最終為氧化物電子設備（如傳感器和能量採集器）的設計設計。

15300018.label: Realisation of objectives
15300018.value: 1. Deep understanding of the flexoelectricity formation mechanism in oxide heterostructures; By inducing a strain gradient to the (001) LAO/STO heterostructure, large electrical transport modulation to the interfacial 2DEG has been realized. The enhanced interfacial flexoelectricity is believed to play a crucial role in a scenario of electric field effect modulation. Coupled with intrinsic polarization of the LAO thin film, flexoelectric polarization shows its ability to stimulate an electron density and mobility change at the interfacial 2DEG. This result illustrates how the flexoelectricity can influence the complex oxide interface based electronic devices. 2.Deep understanding of flexoelectric effect on electrical transport properties of oxide heterostructures; The flexoelectricity modulated (110) LAO/STO samples grown at different oxygen partial pressures was investigated. The samples’ interfacial electric transport property change is affected by oxygen vacancies introduced during PLD growth. For the samples with relatively low oxygen vacancies, the resistance of the 2DEG changes according to the variation of interfacial charge carrier concentration. For samples with higher oxygen vacancies, the resistance change is much smaller and determined by the change of charge mobility. Such a modulation effect can be explained by the electric field effect. These findings further clarify the physical picture of flexoelectric modulation in oxide heterostructures and render us more application possibilities with the flexoelectricity in oxides. 3. To understand interplay between flexoelectricity and other factors in oxide heterostructures such as ferroelectricity, domain structure and phase change, etc. The flexoelectric coefficient of BTO thin films was characterized. It demonstrated that the flexoelectric polarization of the Pt/BTO/NSTO structure is purely generated from the BTO thin film layer. Multi-level control of the capacitance was achieved by combining both ferroelectric and flexoelectric polarizations. The flexoelectric response of BTO thin film grown on mica was also measured. Compared with STO films on mica, the flexoelectric response didn’t show the large difference observed in single crystal or ceramic bulk materials.

15300018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300018.value: We found that, in a thin film heterostructure, the ferroelectricity is usually much larger than its bulk form. This enhance flexoelectricity is due to the existence of interfacial strain which may generate ferroelectric effect and contribute to the flexoelectric effect. The interfacial electrical band structure also favor the flexoelectricity, leading to enhanced photovoltaic effect. The photo-generated electron hole pairs also contribute to the flexoelectricity. This is due to the fact that, these movable charge carries can be driven to the electrode by the flexoelectric field, giving rise to the measured current. This is not intrinsic flexoelectric effect, but a kind of extrinsic effect.

15300018.value: The existence of flexoelectric enhanced photovoltaic effect and photocurrent enhanced flexoelectric effect may promote the research of so-called flexophotovoltaic effect or photoflexoelectric effect. The enlarged flexoelectricity by this effect may eventually make it applicable in sensing and energy harvesting.

15300118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300118.value: 兩階段隨機變分不等式的最優化理論和算法

15300118.label: Project Objectives
15300118.value: We will develop comprehensive theoretical results on the existence of solutions of the two-stage SVI. We will provide meaningful sufficient conditions to ensure that the solution set is nonempty, bounded, and the sequence of solutions generated by sample average approximations converges. We will use the special structure of the functions and sets in the two-stage SVI to develop efficient algorithms for finding its approximate solutions with discrete random variables, including the progressive hedging algorithm and the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm. These algorithms can be used to solve the two-stage SVI with large samples in parallel computing environment. We will establish the error bounds for the computed solution which include the error from sample average approximations and the error from numerical computation. We will apply the perturbation theory in optimization and variational analysis to give useful error bounds. We will explore deep theoretical properties of the two-stage stochastic linear variational inequality, which is a special case of the two-stage SVI and presents the first-order optimality condition of the two-stage stochastic linear programming. We will develop efficient distributionally robust optimization approaches when the distribution of random variables can only be guessed with limited information. We will extensively test the proposed methods and compare them with the existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data from transportation network assignment will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms for the two-stage SVI.

15300118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300118.value: The variational inequality (VI) provides a powerful framework for optimality conditions of optimization problems and equilibria of many kinds in engineering, science and economics. The VI includes the nonlinear complementarity problem and the system of nonlinear equations as special cases. Many important problems can be solved efficiently via the framework of the VI. Given a nonempty closed set and a continuous function, the VI is to find a vector satisfying a system of inequalities. In real applications, the set and the function in the VI often involve uncertainties and errors. Over the past years, there have been efforts to extend the VI to the stochastic variational inequality (SVI) which uses random variables to describe uncertainties, data errors and/or dynamic scenarios. Finding a solution of the SVI has attracted significant attention in various fields and has an increasing number of applications. Moreover, applications of the SVI urgently need innovative theory and efficient algorithms, due to their complex configuration, uncertainties and dynamics in the new data era. In this project, we focus on systematic study of the two-stage SVI, which is to find a pair of here-and-now and wait-and-see solutions. The here-and-now solution represents now-decisions, while the wait-and-see solution depends on future events described by random variables. A typical example is transportation/communication network designs under uncertainties. The travel cost and travel demand fluctuate randomly with different time periods. The here-and-now solution can be an optimal network design based on the average of the past travel costs and travel demands. The wait-and-see solution minimizes the loss for all possible occurrences due to failure of the equilibrium of the network at future uncertain events. Motivated by numerous applications of the two-stage SVI, in this project, we will develop innovative theory and efficient algorithms for the two-stage SVI. We will derive new necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions of the two-stage SVI. Moreover, we will develop efficient optimization algorithms for solving the two-stage SVI using sample average approximation and splitting methods. We will establish convergence theorems of the algorithm and error bounds for solutions of the approximation problem. We will apply our theory and algorithms to transportation/communication network designs. The outcomes of this project will have long-term, high impact, because the two-stage SVI arises naturally in numerous applications and our theory and algorithms will provide urgently needed theory and algorithms for these applications. 變分不等式（VI）為優化問題的最優性條件和工程，科學和經濟學中的多種均衡問題提供了強有力的研究框架.非線性互補問題和非線性方程組是VI的特例。通過VI的框架可以有效地解決許多優化問題和均衡問題。 給定非空閉集和連續函數，VI將找到滿足相应不等式系統的向量。在實際應用中，VI中的集合和函数通常包含有不確定性和误差。在過去幾年中，將VI擴展到隨機變分不等式（SVI）的努力已經做出。SVI使用隨機變量來描述不確定性，數據誤差和/或動態情景，並提供隨機優化問題的最優性條件。求解SVI已經在各個領域引起了極大關注並且具有越來越多的應用。此外，由於新數據時代問題的複雜性，不確定性和動態性，迫切需要SVI的創新理論和有效算法。在這個項目中，我們專注於對兩階段SVI進行系統研究。兩階段SVI求解一對here-and-now和wait-and-see解，here-and-now解代表現在的決策，而wait-and-see解取決於隨機變量描述的未來事件。一個典型的例子是不確定性下的運輸/通信網絡設計。旅行成本和旅行需求隨著不同的時間段隨機波動。here-and-now解可以是基於過去旅行成本和旅行需求的平均值的最佳網絡設計。wait-and-see解最小化了由於未來不確定事件中網絡均衡失敗導致的所有可能發生的損失。 受兩階段SVI的眾多應用的推動，在這個項目中，我們將為兩階段SVI開發創新理論和高效算法。 我們將為兩階段SVI解的存在性和唯一性推導出新的充分必要條件。 此外，我們將開發有效的優化算法，使用樣本平均近似和分裂方法來解決兩階段SVI。 我們將建立算法的收斂定理和近似問題解的誤差界。 我們將新理論和高效算法應用於交通/通信網絡設計。 該項目的成果具有長期的高影響，這是因為兩階段SVI在許多應用中自然產生，而我們的成果將為這些應用提供迫切需要的理論和算法。

15300418.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300418.value: 大規模帶結構優化問題算法的加速方法

15300418.label: Project Objectives
15300418.value: Analyze the convergence and iteration complexity of some extrapolated variants of popular first-order methods such as the proximal gradient algorithm and the Douglas-Rachford splitting method in some nonconvex settings. The techniques developed will likely shed lights on how to analyze various extrapolation based first-order methods in the literature in the general nonconvex settings. Develop and analyze new envelope functions that can be defined under more general / relaxed assumptions on the objective function of the optimization problem than those existing envelopes such as the forward-backward envelope. Based on the new envelope functions, it is conceivable that one can develop new variants of first-order methods that can solve a larger class of optimization problems and incorporate some degree of second-order information for faster convergence.

15300418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300418.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will develop techniques for accelerating first-order methods to solve large-scale structured optimization models that arise in various applications such as compressed sensing. Such techniques are supposed to maintain the low computational cost per iteration of first-order methods, while reducing the number of iterations required for achieving the desired accuracy. In the literature, a common technique for acceleration is to incorporate extrapolation, such as the use of Nesterov's extrapolation techniques. Another recent approach is based on developing and studying envelope functions that encode the first-order methods under consideration, in the sense that the first-order methods applied to solving the original problem are equivalent to some specific algorithms applied to minimizing the envelope functions. In this project, based on the PI and the co-I's recent work on convergence analysis of the Douglas-Rachford splitting method in the nonconvex setting, we will study the effect of extrapolation on some popular first-order methods in the nonconvex setting and analyze their iteration complexity. The tools developed can be applied for investigating the effect of extrapolation on other first-order methods. We will also design new envelope functions under more general settings so that these functions can be used for developing fast solution methods for a larger class of structured optimization problems. The acceleration techniques developed in this project can provide guidelines for the development of fast algorithms in various applications. 本項目將研究如何加速用於求解大規模帶結構優化問題的一階算法，既降低算法迭代次數，同時又不增加每次迭代的計算量。目前常用的加速法包括外插法及構造適當的包絡函數。本項目將循兩方面進行。首先，我們將研究外插技巧如何用以加速一階算法以求解非凸優化問題，並分析其複雜度。另外，我們亦會針對一大類帶結構的優化問題設計新的包絡函數以便發展新的優化算法。這些新的加速技巧可望為不同優化問題設計快速算法提供指引。

15300418.label: Realisation of objectives
15300418.value: One of the goals of this project is to analyze the convergence of some extrapolated variants of popular first-order methods. In this regard, we studied in “A strictly contractive Peaceman-Rachford splitting method for the doubly nonnegative relaxation of the minimum cut problem” the application of the Peaceman-Rachford (PR) splitting method for solving convex relaxations of some NP-hard nonconvex minimum cut optimization problems. Peaceman-Rachford splitting method can be viewed as an extrapolated variant of the classical Douglas-Rachford (DR) splitting method. This work was initiated during a visit to Professor Henry Wolkowicz in University of Waterloo in June 2019. Besides, the Frank-Wolfe (FW) algorithm, a popular first-order method in the convex setting, has been extended in the work “Frank-Wolfe type methods for nonconvex inequality-constrained problems” to some nonconvex settings, and the away-step strategy has been adapted from the convex setting to accelerate empirically this nonconvex extension. The away-step strategy can be viewed as a version of extrapolation techniques, in which the next iterate is generated as either “a convex combination of the current iterate and the output of the FW linear optimization oracle”, or “an extrapolation of the current iterate against the output of the away-step oracle”. The subsequential convergence of this nonconvex FW algorithm and its away-step variant were established under suitable assumptions. In summary, we have studied the convergence of some extrapolated variants of popular first-order methods, such as the PR splitting method (variant of the DR splitting) and the FW algorithm, for solving some nonconvex problems and their relaxations. The other aim of this project is to develop new variants of first-order methods based on the study of suitable envelope functions. In this regard, we studied in “A hybrid penalty method for a class of optimization problems with multiple rank constraints” how the Moreau envelopes of multiple regularizers can be used in an integrated manner to deal with a class of optimization problems involving multiple rank constraints from the system identification literature. An iterative algorithm was then developed based on the fact that the Moreau envelope can be written as a difference-of-convex (DC) function. To handle the rank constraints explicitly, we proposed a new concept called pseudo-projection and showed that, under mild conditions, the subproblem solvers we use will return pseudo-projections. Global subsequential convergence of our proposed algorithm involving these subproblem solvers was then established. This work was initiated during the PI’s visit to Professor Akiko Takeda in University of Tokyo in April 2019, which was supported under this funding. In addition, in the work “Frank-Wolfe type methods for nonconvex inequality-constrained problems”, we extended the FW algorithm to solve constrained optimization problems with constraints defined as the level sets of DC functions satisfying certain regularity conditions. The proposed algorithm involves what we call the generalized linear optimization oracle (GLO). When the first component of the DC function is strongly convex, the corresponding GLO involves the computation of the so-called proximal map, which is essentially the gradient of the Moreau envelope function. In our numerical experiments, the version of FW algorithm that made implicit use of such an envelope function is the fastest. Our nonconvex extension of the FW algorithm largely complements the vast literature of FW algorithm in the convex setting, and the envelope idea led to the fastest variant of nonconvex FW algorithms in our numerical tests. In summary, we have studied new variants of DC optimization algorithm and the FW algorithm, and efficient implementation was made possible upon identification of the role of envelope functions in the design of algorithm.

15300418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300418.value: Three papers were submitted and two of them have already been published. The first paper is “A hybrid penalty method for a class of optimization problems with multiple rank constraints”, which was reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications. This paper proposed an algorithm for optimization problems with multiple rank constraints based on Moreau envelope and a new concept called pseudo-projection. The second paper is “A strictly contractive Peaceman-Rachford splitting method for the doubly nonnegative relaxation of the minimum cut problem”, which was also reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in Computational Optimization and Applications. The algorithm under study of this paper is an extrapolated variant of the Douglas-Rachford splitting method. The paper investigated how this variant can be efficiently applied to solving doubly nonnegative relaxation of the minimum cut problem. Finally, towards the end of the project period, a third paper “Frank-Wolfe type methods for nonconvex inequality-constrained problems” was submitted. This paper is currently still under review. It extended the classical Frank-Wolfe algorithm from the convex setting to some nonconvex settings, and studied how classical acceleration techniques such as away-step can be extended to this general nonconvex setting. A talk entitled “Polar envelope and polar proximal map” was given in the 6th International Conference on Continuous Optimization in Berlin in 2019. This talk contained studies concerning envelope functions related to the findings of this project.

15300418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300418.value: There are several avenues for potential further development. First, other than away-step strategies, there are other recently proposed extrapolation techniques for accelerating the FW algorithm in the convex setting. It will be interesting to test out these techniques for FW algorithm in some nonconvex settings. Next, the envelope function implicitly used in accelerating the FW algorithm was not explicitly identified and analyzed. These are possible avenues for future research.

15300418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300418.value: In this project, the PI and his coworkers studied acceleration techniques for some optimization algorithms. In details, we developed several first-order methods with tailored acceleration techniques and studied their convergence in some nonconvex settings. Empirical acceleration was achieved by either incorporating extrapolation techniques or leveraging suitably constructed envelope functions. The techniques developed will shed lights on how to analyze the convergence of various extrapolation based first-order methods in the literature in the general nonconvex settings, and help develop new variants of first-order methods that can take advantage of extrapolation techniques or envelope function constructions (implicitly or explicitly) for acceleration.

15301218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301218.value: Panel count data usually refer to data arising from studies on recurrent events in which the study subjects are observed only at discrete time points rather than under continuous observations. Most of the previous research has focused on situations where there is no terminal event. In this project, we investigate a more complicated but realistic situation in biomedical studies where a recurrent event process will be eventually terminated by a terminal event. The effect of terminal event on recurrent events should be considered for this case, and thus the analysis of panel count data becomes more challenging since the data structure is more complicated. The aim of this project is to develop new nonparametric and semiparametric methods for panel count data with a terminal event. First, we propose a reversed mean model anchoring at a terminal event, develop a two-stage sieve likelihood-based estimation procedure for nonparametric estimation of mean function of a recurrent event process, and discuss the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Second, we consider a multi-sample nonparametric comparison problem for panel count data with a terminal event, construct new tests for the problem, and establish the asymptotic theory of the proposed test statistics. Third, we propose a reversed proportional mean model anchoring at terminal event, develop a two-stage likelihood-based inference procedure for estimation of both a terminal event-dependent mean function and regression coefficients, and investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators. Furthermore, we propose a reversed nonparametric regression model anchoring at terminal event and develop the corresponding inference procedure. The novel models can intuitively and clearly explain the relationship between the recurrent current process and terminal event. However, these novel models result in complicated likelihood functions and bring new challenging theoretical and computational questions in statistics that require more innovative research effort. These challenges will be addressed by using the modern empirical process theory for asymptotics and adapting a generalized gradient projection algorithm for optimizing a nonlinear objective function with linear inequality for computation. The performance of the proposed new models and estimation procedures will be evaluated by Monte Carlo simulations. Some real data sets, such as the bladder tumor data and care utilization data for subjects with mitral regurgitation prior to death that motivate the proposed research, will be analyzed and presented as illustrative examples. The proposed project will yield new methods for the analysis of panel count data in the presence of terminal event. 面板計數數據通常是指對複發事件的研究產生的數據，其中研究對象僅在離散時間點而不是在連續觀察下觀察。以前的大部分研究都集中在沒有終端事件的情況。在這個項目中，我們研究了生物醫學研究中一個更複雜但更現實的情況，其中復發事件過程最終會被終端事件終止。對於這種情況，應該考慮終端事件對複發事件的影響，數據結構更複雜, 因此面板計數數據的分析變得更具挑戰性。該項目的目的是利用終端事件為面板計數數據開發新的非參數和半參數方法。首先，我們提出了一個反向錨定在終端事件的平均模型，開發一個基於兩階段篩選似然的估計程序，用於復發事件過程的平均函數的非參數估計，並討論所得估計的漸近性質。其次，我們考慮面板計數數據與終端事件的多樣本非參數比較問題，構建問題的新檢驗統計量，並建立所提出的檢驗統計量的漸近理論。第三，我們提出了一個反向錨定在終端事件比例平均模型，開發一個兩階段基於似然的推斷程序，用於估計終端事件依賴平均函數和回歸係數，並研究所提出的估計的理論性質。此外，我們提出了一個反向錨定在終端事件的非參數回歸模型，並開發相應的推斷程序。新穎的模型可以直觀而清晰地解釋複發事件過程和終端事件之間的關係。然而，這些新穎的模型導致複雜的似然函數，帶來新的挑戰性的理論和計算問題，需要更多創新研究。這些挑戰將通過使用現代經驗過程理論導出漸近性質，調整廣義梯度投影算法來優化具有線性不等式的非線性目標函數來解決計算問題。蒙特卡羅模擬將評估擬議的新模型和估算程序的性能。一些真實數據集，例如激勵所提議的研究的膀胱腫瘤數據和死亡前二尖瓣關閉不全的受試者的護理利用數據，將作為說明性示例進行分析和呈現。擬議的項目將產生用於在終端事件存在的情況下分析面板計數數據的新方法。

15301218.label: Realisation of objectives
15301218.value: We have worked on all four objectives of this project. First, we developed a likelihood-based two-stage estimation procedure under a reversed conditional nonparametric mean model for panel count data with a terminal event, and established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator. Second, to relax the Poisson assumption on the counting process, we developed a least squares-based two stage estimation procedure for estimation of an unknown mean function under a reversed conditional nonparametric mean model based on panel count data with a terminal event, and established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator. Third, we discussed the problem of the multi-sample comparison of point processes with a terminal event. Using the results from the likelihood-based approach and least squares-based approach and the asymptotic properties of the corresponding estimators, we constructed more powerful nonparametric tests for the problem. Two classes of nonparametric test procedures based on two new nonparametric estimators were proposed for the problem and the asymptotic properties of the test statistics were established. Extensive simulation studies were carried out and suggested that the proposed approaches work well for practical situations. Fourth, we also considered simultaneous variable selection and parameter estimation as well as hypothesis testing in censored survival models where a parametric likelihood is not available. For the problem, we utilized certain growing dimensional general estimating equations and proposed a penalized generalized empirical likelihood based on the semiparametric efficiency bound of estimation with given moment conditions. The proposed penalized generalized empirical likelihood estimators enjoy the oracle properties, and the penalized generalized empirical likelihood ratio test statistic has an asymptotic central chi-square distribution. We also discussed the conditions of local and restricted global optimality of weighted penalized generalized empirical likelihood estimators. Finally, we proposed a class of reversed semiparametric regression models for panel count data with covariates and a terminal event. We have developed two-stage nonparametric sieve likelihood-based and least squares-based estimation procedures for estimating both unknown functions and regression parameters, which overcome the computational difficulties arising from a nuisance functional parameter involved in the likelihood function and least squares loss function. We established the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators from two estimation methods. Extensive simulation studies and application results demonstrated that the proposed methods perform well. We have achieved all the objectives of this project.

15301218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301218.value: For nonparametric inference of panel count data with terminal events, we have proposed a flexible and intuitive nonparametric reversed conditional mean model. We have established the asymptotic properties of the proposed two-stage nonparametric sieve likelihood-based and least squares-based estimation methods. In particular, we have developed a general theorem for the asymptotic normality of nonparametric M-estimators with a nuisance functional parameter when estimators have a convergence rate slower than the standard rate. We have designed two classes of new nonparametric tests for comparing mean functions of recurrent event processes with panel count data in the presence of an informative terminal event. For semiparametric inference of panel count data with terminal events, we have developed a semiparametric reversed mean model anchoring at a terminal event to explicitly quantify its effect on the recurrent event process. We have formulated the log-likelihood for panel count data conditional on censored terminal event time data as an objective function, and designed a two-stage estimation procedure. We have established a general framework of the asymptotic distributional theory of semiparametric M-estimators with a nuisance functional parameter that can be applied to derive the asymptotic normality of functionals of two-stage semiparametric M-estimators. In particular, the asymptotic results of the proposed estimator do not rely on the working model of the Poisson process assumption. For robust analysis of panel count data with an informative terminal event, we have investigated a semiparametric regression model, where the stochastic mechanism for the underlying counting process arising from recurrent events is completely unspecified. We have proposed a predicted least squares-based two-stage estimation procedure with the spline-based sieve estimation technique and further established the asymptotic normality for the estimator of the finite-dimensional parameter and functionals of the estimator of the infinite-dimensional parameter. For the problem of simultaneous variable selection and parameter estimation as well as hypothesis testing in censored survival models where a parametric likelihood is not available, we have developed a penalized generalized empirical likelihood. We have found that the estimator of any fixed dimensional vector of nonzero parameters achieves the semiparametric efficiency bound asymptotically and the penalized generalized empirical likelihood ratio test statistic has an asymptotic central chi-square distribution. In summary, the nine research papers associated with this project have been published in international peer-reviewed journals (The Annals of Statistics, Journal of the American Statistical Association, Bernoulli, Statistica Sinica), and also presented in the international conferences.

15301218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301218.value: (1) Our new models developed in this project can be used to make better understanding of important features from recurrent event processes. (2) Our developed nonparametric and semiparametric inference procedures can be extended to analyze panel count data in the presence of informative observation and censoring times as well as terminal events. (3) Our developed general theory on the asymptotic normality of M-estimators with nuisance functional parameters can be widely used to derive the asymptotic distributions of two-stage estimators no matter whether the convergence rate of an estimator is standard or slower.

15301218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301218.value: In this project, we have investigated nonparametric and semiparametric inference problems with a general situation where a recurrent event process is eventually truncated by an informative terminal event and we are particularly interested in behaviors of the recurrent event process near the terminal event. This research is significant in that it addresses more general situations which often occur in the real world but have not been adequately studied in the literature. A key advantage of our developed approach over existing methods is that it provides the explicit relationship between a recurrent event process and a terminal event. The results of this project have a significant impact because they have filled the gap in the literature on panel count survival data analysis, and are also important to practical applications in economics, genetics, medicine, and public health. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to develop nonparametric tests for panel count data in the presence of an informative terminal event. From the simulation studies and the applications, we conclude that one needs to be careful in choosing a nonparametric comparison procedure as many existing procedures apply only to situations where no terminal event is considered.

15301418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301418.value: In this proposal, we shall focus on solving an important class of large scale convex composite optimization (CCO) problems with double regularizers arising from science, engineering, statistical learning, finance and risk management, etc. This class of problems includes a number of regularized statistical regression models and nonlinear doubly nonnegative semidefinite programming problems. Concerned with the inherent huge computational burdens of the interior point methods for solving these optimization problems of large scales, many researchers and practitioners tend to the first order methods such as the accelerated proximal gradient methods and the alternating direction methods of multipliers for the rescue. While these first order methods have been successful in a number of interesting applications, they also encounter enormous numerical difficulties in dealing with many real data optimization problems of large scales even only with a low or moderate solution quality. For the purpose of overcoming the numerical difficulties either in the second order interior point methods or in the first order methods, we plan to design an efficient and robust augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) to solve the large scale CCO problems with double regularizers. This proposal is highly motivated by our recent progress in solving the fused lasso problem, the convex quadratic programming problem with the Birkhoff polytope constraint, and those appeared in the earlier works of the PI and his co-authors for solving semidefinite programming problems. In order to make our approach successful, we shall first analyze the sparsity and low (or high) rank structures in the generalized Jacobian of the proximal mapping of the sum of the two regularizers that are conducive for numerical implementations. Then we shall study the question when the constraint nondegenerate conditions and error bound results hold for the CCO problems. The answer to this question is of critical importance for the employed (inexact) semismooth Newton methods for solving the subproblems in the ALM framework to be efficient and robust. Finally, we shall propose a bi-level ALM to handle the case when the proximal mapping of the sum of the two regularizers does not admit an efficient algorithm. The subproblems in the first level ALM are always constraint nondegenerate and can be solved by the second level ALM applied to the dual of these subproblems. The developed software packages will be made publicly available for practitioners and academic researchers to use. 在本項目中，我們將著重解決源於科學，工程，統計學習，財務和風險管理等領域的一類重要的含有雙正則項的大規模凸複合優化（CCO）問題。這類問題包括許多正則化的統計回歸模型和非線性雙非負半定規劃問題。考慮到求解這些大規模優化問題的內點法固有的巨大計算負擔，許多研究人員和從業者傾向於採用一階方法，如加速鄰近梯度法和交替方向法乘子法等。雖然這些一階方法已經在許多有意義的應用中取得了成功，但它們在處理許多大規模的實際數據優化問題時也遇到了巨大的數值困難，即使所追求的僅僅是只有低或中等品質的解。為了克服二階內點法或一階法中的數值困難，我們計畫設計一種有效且穩健的增廣拉格朗日方法（ALM）來求解含有雙正則項的大規模CCO問題。本項目研究的提出深受我們最近在求解融合lasso問題、含有Birkhoff多面體約束的凸二次規劃問題，以及專案負責人及其合作者早先的求解半定規劃問題等方面取得的進展的啟發。為了使我們的方法獲得成功，我們將首先分析兩個正則項之和的鄰近映射的廣義雅可比中有助於數值實現的稀疏性和低（或高）秩結構。接下來，我們將研究在什麼情況下適用於CCO問題的約束非退化條件和誤差界條件成立。這個問題的答案對於用來求解ALM框架中的子問題的（不精確的）半光滑牛頓法的有效性和穩健性至關重要。最後，我們將提出一個兩級ALM來處理兩個正則項之和的鄰近映射缺失有效演算法的這一情況。第一級ALM中的子問題總是約束非退化的，並且可以通過第二級ALM來求解這些子問題的對偶。本项目開發的套裝軟體將公開供從業人員和學術研究人員使用。
