15301418.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301418.value: All the objectives proposed for this research project have been achieved. Eleven papers based on the research of this project have been written. Among them, eight papers have been published in top journals in the area of optimization and data science. Moreover, three open-sourced solvers have been developed and released. Some major findings are summarized below. (1) Design the highly efficient semismooth Newton method for a class of problems. The PI has extensively investigated the generalized Jacobian of the proximal mapping of several given proper, closed, and convex functions These generalized Jacobians have contributed to the design of the highly efficient semismooth Newton method for solving a class of important optimization problems, including the second-order cone (SOC) programming [C8.6], optimization problems with doubly nonnegative cone constraints [C8.5, C8.7], the sparse graphical lasso model [C8.1, C8.9], the squared-root lasso model [C8.2], the exclusive lasso model [C8.11], and the convex clustering model [C8.8]. One key to the success of the algorithms is the second-order sparsity induced by the generalized Jacobians. (2) Investigate the constraint nondegeneracy conditions and error bounds. The constraint nondegeneracy of the primal problem implies the nonsingularity of the generalized Jacobian for the corresponding dual problem, which is crucial for designing Newton’s method. The PI has established the constraint nondegeneracy condition for a class of problems, including the squared-root lasso [C8.2], and the SOC problem arising from the minimal enclosing ball problems [C8.6]. Moreover, the PI has established the error bound conditions for a sequence of problems, in particular, the metrically sub-regularity of the normal cone associated with the positive semidefinite cone [C8.7]. Such error bound conditions are crucial to establish the asymptotically superlinear convergence rates of the augmented Lagrangian method (ALM). (3) A proximal/bi-level ALM method for solving doubly regularized composite problems. When the proximal mapping of the regularizer in the problem is difficult to compute, the PI investigated the proximal ALM and the bi-level ALM method to overcome the potential constraint degeneracy issue. In particular, the PI investigated the error bound conditions for establishing the fast convergence rates of the proximal ALM and the bi-level ALM methods [C8.6, C8.7, C8.9]. (4) Open-sourced optimization solvers. The PI has developed and released three open-sourced solvers with his collaborators and students based on the algorithms designed in this project [C11.2, C11.3, C11.4]. These solvers have made significant impacts in the academic community and beyond.

15301418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301418.value: In the future, the PI plans to further investigate the topic of solving large-scale degenerate conic programming problems. As a possible future research direction, the PI will further investigate the error bound conditions for the large-scale nonlinear conic programming problems.

15301418.value: In this project, we focus on solving an important class of large-scale convex composite optimization problems with double regularizers arising from science, engineering, statistical learning, finance, and risk management, and so on. We designed a highly efficient semismooth Newton based augmented Lagrangian method for solving a class of important optimization problems, including the second-order cone programming, optimization problems with doubly nonnegative cone constraints, the sparse graphical lasso model, the squared-root lasso model, the exclusive lasso model, and the convex clustering model. We further investigated the constraint nondegeneracy condition and the error bound conditions to establish the fast convergence rate of the designed algorithm. Three open-sourced solvers have been developed and released, which have made significant impacts in the academic community and beyond.

15301818.label: Project Objectives
15301818.value: For parabolic equations with real and symmetric coefficients, we shall prove discrete maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions with A(α)-stable multistep BDF methods up to order 6. This is equivalent to characterizing the angle of analyticity and R-boundedness (uniform with respect to the mesh size of the finite elements) of the semigroup generated by a discrete elliptic operator (discretized by the finite element method) with complex and non-symmetric coefficients. In the mean time, we shall also obtain maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions with A-stable time discretizations for parabolic equations with complex and non-symmetric coefficients. As an application of the above result, we present analysis for the stability and accuracy of the finite element solutions of nonlinear parabolic equations describing gradient flows with strongly nonlinear energy functionals, including minimal surface flow and regularized total variational flow, by high-order multistep BDF methods linearized by Newton’s method. We investigate the convergence rate of the fully discrete finite element solutions given by a fixed number of Newton iterations at each time step. As an application of discrete maximal Lp-regularity, we shall study time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations in nonsmooth nonconvex polygonal domains, and fully discrete finite element methods for the partial differential equations governing miscible displacement in porous media with the commonly-used Bear-Scheidegger model of diffusion-dispersion tensor. We shall fill in the gap between existing numerical experiments and error analysis by using the discrete maximal Lp-regularity approach.

15301818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301818.value: Discrete maximal Lp-regularity is an important mathematical tool for analyzing the stability and accuracy of numerical solutions of nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations. The theory of discrete maximal Lp-regularity has been established for semidiscretization in time by implicit A-stable Runge-Kutta methods and A(α)-stable multistep methods. However, the current maximal Lp-regularity theory for fully discrete finite element solutions is limited to parabolic equations with real symmetric diffusion coefficients and A-stable time discretization methods. This rules out many interesting nonlinear problems as well as high-order multistep time discretization methods. In this project, we shall establish maximal Lp-regularity for semidiscirete finite element solutions of parabolic equations with possibly complex and non-symmetric coefficients, and apply the result to derive the maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions with A(α)-stable multistep time discretization methods for solving parabolic equations. As an application of the established results, we present analysis for the stability and accuracy of the numerical solutions of some nonlinear parabolic equations, including gradient flow and miscible fluids mixture flow in porous media. We shall fill in the gap between existing numerical results and numerical analysis by using the discrete maximal Lp-regularity approach. 离散最大 L^p 正则性是分析非线性抛物型偏微分方程数值解的稳定性和精度的重要数学工具。隐式 A-稳定 Runge-Kutta 法和 A(α)-稳定多步法的时间半离散最大 L^p 正则性的理论目前已经建立起来。然而，目前的全离散有限元解的最大 L^p 正则性理论仅限于具有实对称扩散系数和 A-稳定时间离散方法的抛物型方程。这排除了许多有重要的非线性问题以及高阶多步时间离散化方法。这个项目旨在对具有复数值和非对称系数的抛物型方程的半离散有限元解的最大 L^p 正则性，并应用所得的结果对采用 A(α)-稳定的多步法进行时间离散的全离散有限元解的最大 L^p 正则性。此外，我们拟分析一些非线性抛物型方程的数值解的稳定性和精确性，包括梯度流和混相流体在多孔介质中的流动，利用离散最大 L^p 正则性分析来填补现有数值结果与数值分析之间的空隙。

15301818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301818.value: We have proved discrete maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions with A(alpha)-stable multistep BDF methods up to order 6. This is equivalent to characterizing the angle of analyticity and R-boundedness (uniform with respect to the mesh size of the finite elements) of the semigroup generated by a discrete elliptic operator (discretized by the finite element method) with complex and non-symmetric coefficients. The paper is published in "B. Li: Maximal regularity of multistep fully discrete finite element methods for parabolic equations. IMA J. Numer. Anal. 42 (2022), pp. 1700–1734." We have presented analysis for the stability and accuracy of the finite element solutions of nonlinear parabolic equations describing gradient flows with strongly nonlinear energy functionals, by the backward Euler method linearized by Newton’s method, and have investigated the convergence rate of the fully discrete finite element solutions given by a fixed number of Newton iterations at each time step. The paper is published in "G. Akrivis and B. Li: Linearization of the finite element method for gradient flows by Newton’s method. IMA J. Numer. Anal. (2020), DOI: 10.1093/imanum/draa016" As an application of discrete maximal Lp-regularity, we have studied time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations in nonsmooth nonconvex polygonal domains with holes, and proved convergence of numerical solutions under minimal regularity conditions. The paper is published in "B. Li, K. Wang, and Z. Zhang: A Hodge decomposition method for dynamic Ginzburg–Landau equations in nonsmooth domains -— a second approach. Commun. Comput. Phys. 28 (2020), pp. 768-802."

15301818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301818.value: The theory of discrete maximal L^p-regularity of time discretizations and finite element methods for parabolic equations has potential application in the numerical analysis for many other nonlinear partial differential equations from geometry, physics and engineering applications, including nonlinear partial differential equations on evolving surfaces, geometric flows and so on. The corresponding research will be further developed in the following years.

15301818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301818.value: Nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations appear in a variety of applications, such as fluid dynamics, superconductivity, magnetization, quantum dynamics, image processing, and oil exploration, just to name a few. In all of these applications, numerical treatment of nonlinear partial differential equations plays an important role. Therefore, developing stable and high-order accurate numerical methods for solving such nonlinear problems is of great practical importance. Discrete maximal Lp-regularity is a mathematical tool for analyzing the stability and ac curacy of numerical solutions of nonlinear parabolic equations. In this project, we have established some fundamental results and tools of discrete maximal Lp-regularity for people to analyze the stability and convergence of numerical solutions to nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations from geometry, physics and engineering applications.

15302118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302118.value: Cancer has dated back over centuries and still remains as one of the major causes of death to date. One virus, Epstein Barr virus (EBV), occupies a prominent place because it acts as a carcinogenic cofactor in the development of several lymphoid and epithelial malignancies. EBV was discovered 53 years ago and since then, has been linked conclusively to infectious mononucleosis as well as found to have a direct link to a wide range of human malignancies. To date, there is still no approved therapies directly targeting EBV or EBV-expressed proteins. One major reason is that it seems to take on numerous roles in lymphoid and epithelial malignancies hence the mechanism regarding these virus is extremely complicated and elusive. To try to resolve such issues, a deeper understand is necessary by combining and integrating expertise that crosses multidisciplinary fields. In this project, by collaborating with biologists, we work to design small lanthanide molecular probes that can help to elucidate our understanding in this area. Over the last two decades, lanthanide materials have been significant and flourishing in cancer research, such as in cancer diagnosis and therapy, with extensive applications in detection and imaging of various biomolecules in-vitro/in-vivo due to the versatile chemical and magnetic properties of the lanthanide-ion 4f electronic configuration. The unique photophysical properties of the lanthanides includes: distinctly long emission and characteristic hypersensitive emissions (provides real-time information about the effect of coordination environment from surrounding entities), which makes time-resolved measurements crucially accessible and thus is a more attractive alternative to the conventional organic fluorophores. Hence, in our probe designs we will incorporate lanthanide ions, in order to exploit the favourable optical properties for use in various imaging techniques such as multiphoton confocal imaging as well as circular polarized emission imaging. In this project, our target is to develop a new class of therapeutic compounds – that can be a responsive and selective sensor to Zn2+ as well as being specific to EBNA1. We are interested to see if the probe can compete with the Zn2+, hence allowing us to elucidate its role in the protein dimer as well as in the dimerization process. We hypothesis that the coherent effect of inhibition of dimerization and co-factor function, will help to further improve the selectivity and dosed concentration to inhibit EBV associated tumor growth. 儘管在癌症治療方面做出了巨大的努力，但癌症仍然是迄今為止死亡的主要原因之一。一種病毒，Epstein Barr病毒（EBV）佔據顯著位置，因為它在幾種淋巴和上皮惡性腫瘤的發展中充當致癌輔助因子。 EBV是在53年前被發現的，從那時起，它已經與傳染性單核細胞增多症最終聯繫起來，並且發現它與廣泛的人類惡性腫瘤有直接聯繫。迄今為止，仍然沒有直接針對EBV或EBV表達的蛋白質的批准療法。一個主要原因是它似乎在淋巴和上皮惡性腫瘤中扮演了許多角色，因此關於這些病毒的機制非常複雜和難以捉摸。為了嘗試解決這些問題，需要通過結合和整合跨越多學科領域的專業知識來加深理解。在這個項目中，通過與生物學家的合作，我們致力於設計小分子探針，以幫助闡明我們在這一領域的理解。

15302118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302118.value: Two publications has been the output from this grant. 1.) Dual-Targeting Peptide-Guided Approach for Precision Delivery and Cancer Monitoring by Using a Safe Upconversion Nanoplatform, Advanced Science, 2021, 8, 5, 2002919 2.) Reactivation of Epstein–Barr virus by a dual-responsive fluorescent EBNA1-targeting agent with Zn2+-chelating function, PNAS, 2019, 116, 52, 26614 The grounds of this project is based on developing a probe that is selective to EBV and induces inhibition by investigating the roles of Zinc ion which is essential for oligomerization of the function of EBNA1. In our first work, we explored different EBNA1 binding peptides with a Zn2+ chelator to create an EBNA1-specific inhibitor. This probe, was found to emit unique responsive fluorescent signals once it binds with EBNA1 and a Zn2+ ion. Biological and cellular studies also shown that the EBNA1 oligomerization can cause nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) tumor shrinkage, possibly due to EBV lytic induction. In this work, we found that Zn2+ is an important cofactor for EBNA1 function and have constructed a series of EBNA1 probes with a Zn2+ chelator and an EBNA1-binding peptide. The Zn2+ chelator can preferentially suppress the higher-order form of EBNA1 complex to further enhance the inhibitory activities of our new-generation of compounds . As EBNA1 is a foreign protein to the host, in theory this strategy of elimination of EBV-associated tumor cells provides absolute specificity over other lytic induction therapies. The current lytic analysis results also suggest that the function of EBNA1 as well as the role of EBV latent infection is associated with the maintenance of tumor cell survival through the suppression of the lytic cycle reactivation. We postulate from this work that by exhaustion of Zn2+ in the microenvironment in protein molecules, this can be a new potential strategy in designing inhibitory agents to target pathogenic proteins in cancer development and other diseases. In further studies based on these probes, we developed a nanoparticle platform integrating the EBV probes to create a dual modal responsive platform for trafficking the inhibition in EBV associated cancer. Here several dual-EBV-oncoproteins-targeting and pH-responsive luminescent nanoprobes with up-conversion properties were synthesized. In these probes, a pH-responsive linker were prepared by Schiff base reaction to link the UCNP and the dual-EBNA1/LMP1-targeting peptides. These nanoparticles with the up-conversion properties is designed to allow specific and sensitive emission enhancement responses toward EBV-positive cell lines.

15302118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302118.value: The work in creating a nanoplatform for dual imaging is important as it opens a new pathway for use of dual-functional peptide agents for precision therapy/medicine. In addition, such nanoplatform can function as an imaging agent due to its responsive photophysical properties. Results of our current study have shown the successful use of EBV proteins as drug targets, as well as demonstrated a dual-targeting peptide-guided approach which could be conveniently translated to be applied to other types of cancers.

15302118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302118.value: EBNA1 is the only Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) latent protein responsible for viral genome maintenance and is expressed in all EBV-infected cells. The metal ion, Zn2+ is shown to be essential for oligomerization of the functional EBNA1. Hence, focusing on this property, specific EBNA1 binding peptides was selected and incorporated with a Zn2+ chelator to develop an new EBNA1-specific inhibitor . Our designed probes was found to be responsive with ‘on’ fluorescence emission upon binding with EBNA1 and a Zn2+ ion.

15302318.label: Project Objectives
15302318.value: To design and fabricate heterostructures based on the selected two-dimensional (2D) III-VI compounds (e.g., In2Se3 and InSe) suitable for the incorporation of piezo-phototronic effect. To observe piezo-phototronic effect in the selected 2D III-VI compound based heterostructures (e.g., Schottky barrier and p-n junction). To investigate photoexcited charge carrier behaviors through three-way coupling among electrical, optical and mechanical properties in the heterostructures. To demonstrate the enhanced performance of 2D heterostructure optoelectronic devices (e.g., photoresponsivity of the photodetector is enhanced 10 times under strain compared to strain free condition), and to develop a new concept of strain-gated atomically thin flexible optoelectronic devices by piezo-phototronic effect.

15302318.label: Realisation of objectives
15302318.value: 1. In order to achieve the objective 1, we have employed a variety of techniques to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) III-VI compounds-based heterostructures. These heterostructures have been carefully designed to suit for the observation and application of piezo-phototronic effect. Typically, multilayer III-VI compound α-In2Se3 and WSe2 flakes were mechanically exfoliated from bulk crystals. After the alignment, the heterostructure device was heated to achieve good contacts between materials and electrodes. Then, the PVA film was removed using the deionization water. Finally, a layer of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) was spincoated above the heterostructure device to avoid the movement of 2D materials during measurements. For chemical vapor deposition (CVD), the 2D In2Se3 nanoflakes were grown. Se and In2O3 powders were used as the precursors with 10% H2/Ar mix gas as the carrier gas. The Se and In2O3 powders were heated to 300 and 660 oC, respectively, and the temperature was held for 40 min in atmospheric pressure with carrier gas. For pulsed laser deposition (PLD), the bulk InSe target was placed 4 cm in front of the substrates. The substrate temperature was controlled at 500 °C-600 °C. Both InSe target and substrates were rotated during the deposition process for achieving uniform film growth. We fabricated high quality InSe thin film on piezoelectric PMN-PT substrate by PLD to form heterostructures suitable for the incorporation of piezo-phototronic effect. The PLD growth conditions, including growth temperature, pressure, growth rate, annealing temperature and duration have been studied. These works have been published in Adv. Opt. Mater. (2021), Phys. Rev. B (2020). 2. To achieve the objective 2, we have made attempts to characterize the interfacial structures and optical spectra using a variety of advanced measurement tools. Furthermore, we used flexible PET substrate with electrodes to make strain-gated piezo-phototronic samples. We have optimized the samples’ design and fabrication. Mechanical exfoliated flakes of III-V compound In2Se3 were transferred onto different substrates. A pair of 10 nm Ti/50 nm Au electrodes were pre-deposited onto PET substrate through standard photolithography and electron-beam evaporation. The sample flakes were lifted up from the SiO2/Si substrates using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) film. Meanwhile, the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film was used as stamp attached between PVA film and the glass slide. In addition, atomic force microscopy was used to characterize the surface topography and the thickness of the samples. X-ray diffraction was used to study the structural phase of the fabricated samples. The obtained samples were then transferred onto a copper grid for TEM characterization. Raman spectra and photoluminescence were obtained by a high-resolution confocal μ-Raman system. For observing piezo-phototronic effect, the Raman and PL spectra of nanosheets under biaxial strain triggered by the PMN-PT substrate have been studied, which provides an effective method to modulate and investigate 2D material properties via an in situ and dynamical approach. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) was taken to produce a surface potential image operating in AC mode and NAP mode. In order to observe piezo-phototronic effect in the 2D III-VI compound based heterostructures on the flexible substrates, we have set up a system for characterizing the heterostructures under tensile or compressive strain condition under optical illumination. With the home-made system, we can determine the optical response varied by the external strains, the performance of the photodetector under different strains and illumination intensity. These works have been published in Appl. Phys. Lett. (2020), Adv. Mater. (2021). 3. To achieve the objective 3, the I–V characteristics of the flexible photodetectors under tensile and compressive strains were systematically investigated with the light source. We have measured the time-dependent photocurrent curves at bias tailored by applied strains under identical illumination intensity. Typically, the photodetection behavior of III-VI compound α-In2Se3/WSe2-based heterostructure photodetector was tested under 620 nm LED light illumination with varied intensities. The photodetection performance of 2D-based photodetectors have been be modulated by strain engineering due to the piezo-phototronic effect. Under identical strain conditions, the performance of photodetector enhanced under light illumination compared to the dark condition, which rules out the possibility of photoresistive effect that is considered as “volume effect” and should be independent of the optical power. Furthermore, we adopted a careful design of the α-In2Se3/Pt/PMN-PT/Au heterostructure. Photoexcited charge carrier behaviors are studied through three-way coupling among electrical, optical and mechanical strain properties in the heterostructures. In order to investigate the effect of photoexcited carriers on the piezoelectric field, a semi-quantitative estimation of the number of electron-hole pairs present in α -In2Se3 is performed. In order to understand the coupling mechanism of the piezo-phototronic effect, the energy band diagrams near the metal–semiconductor or PN junction interface are analyzed under mechanical tensile and compressive strains. In combination with experiments, we performed DFT calculation using the plane-wave pseudopotential code quantum espresso. The generalized gradient approximation with Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof parametrization was used for the exchange and correlation functionals. These works have been published in Adv. Opt. Mater. (2021), Adv. Mater. (2021) and Book Chapter (2022). 4. To achieve the objective 4, we have made various types of ultrathin heterostructure optoelectronic devices such as photodetectors, which are published in Nano Lett (2020), Adv. Opt. Mater. (2021) and Adv. Mater. (2021). Typically, the optoelectronic devices have been fabricated by photolithography and lift-off techniques. Electrical transport characteristics were measured. all the electronic and photoelectronic measurements were carried out at room temperature. LED at the specific wavelength was used as an illumination source, where the intensity of illumination light was calibrated via a commercial power meter. A home-made bending apparatus was employed to apply proper strains onto the device. The electrical characterization was measured and collected by a semiconductor analyzer Keithley 4200 through a probe station. The device under bending was considered as a circular arc for the calculation of the applied strains. To avoid any unfavorable sample movements, the strains applied to the plastic substrates were carefully controlled to be less than 0.5%. The enhanced output current of the photodetectors was tested and evaluated under strain. The photoresponsivity and detectivity of the devices are evaluated under optical illumination power and strain. 5. In summary, we have fully achieved the four objectives of the RGC GRF project. One postgraduate student, Yuqian Zhao financially supported by the GRF grant has been well trained in the project period and received MPhil degree. Regarding the GRF project’s research, the postgraduate student has published international journal paper entitled “Piezo-Phototronic Effect in 2D α-In2Se3/WSe2 van der Waals Heterostructure for Photodetector with Enhanced Photoresponse” in Adv. Opt. Mater. as the first author, and co-authored in other papers in Adv. Mater., Appl. Phys. Lett. She is also the first author in Wiley Book Chapter entitled “Progress in Piezo-Phototronic Effect on 2D Nanomaterial-Based Heterostructure Photodetectors”. Totally, 8 high-quality journal papers (Adv. Mater., Nano Lett., Adv. Opt. Mater., Appl. Phys. Rev., Appl. Phys. Lett., etc.) including invited reviews are published with acknowledgements of this project. To disseminate our results, the PI has given 4 keynote or invited talks in the recognized international conferences. In addition, the PI has collaborated with the Co-I, Dr. Wenzhuo Wu in Purdue University through piezo-phototronic sample synthesis, measurements, data analysis and discussion. The PI and Co-I have co-authored two published journal papers in Appl. Phys. Lett. And Adv. Opt. Mater..

15302318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302318.value: 1. We found that III–VI compounds of α-In2Se3 and InSe are ideal piezo-phototronic materials for the construction of flexible heterostructure devices via combining metals or other 2D layered materials. In our representative work of the project, the type-II band alignment can be formed in the vdW heterojunction based on the difference in the bandgap and work function between α-In2Se3 and WSe2. These piezo-phototronic heterostructures can be made by a variety of fabrication techniques such as ME, chemical and physical deposition methods. (see: Part C: Journal 1,2,3,5,6, Conference 3,4). 2. We observed piezo-phototronic effect in the selected 2D III-VI compound and other 2D material based heterostructures in both Schottky barrier and p-n junction. Owing to the noncentrosymmetric structure of 2D III–VI compounds, the strain-induced piezo-potential is able to modulate the band slope near the interface, improving the transfer characteristics and separation efficiency of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. By applying the mechanical strain, the photocurrent of the photodetector can be enhanced by about 18 times. The research outcome can bridge electrical, optical and mechanical properties of 2D materials via piezo-phototronic effect. (see: Part C: Journal 6,8,9, Conference 2,3). 3. In our designed 2D III-V compound α-In2Se3/Pt/PMN-PT/Au heterostructure, we found two factors can influence the bandgap of nanosheets, namely, biaxial compressive strain and strain induced piezoelectric field. Photoluminescence shows a blueshift, which can reach up to 215 meV per 1% strain. Such tunability of optical characteristics observed from 2D III–VI compounds of α-In2Se3 nanosheets is larger than that from conventional semiconductors. This finding is related to the variations in the energy band and photoexcited carriers under a piezoelectric field and laser power. (see: Part C: Journal 2,4,9, Conference 1,4). 4. Regarding the enhanced performance of 2D heterostructure optoelectronic devices, we demonstrate that the photoresponsivity of the 2D III-V compound α-In2Se3/WSe2 heterojunction photodetector can be significantly enhanced to about 1800% under 0.433% tensile strain compared to strain free condition. The maximum photoresponsivity and detectivity can reach up to 4.61 × 10^5 A W−1 and 4.34 × 10^14 Jones under a low optical illumination power with 0.069 μW cm^−2 and 0.433% tensile strain. Our findings suggest that the feasibility of the heterostructures can be widely extended to other ultrathin materials, which may provide insights to develop high-performance and new concept of strain-gated atomically thin flexible optoelectronic devices by piezo-phototronic effect. (see: Part C: Journal 6,7,8, Conference 3,4).

15302318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302318.value: Firstly, we have mainly used mechanical exfoliation, chemical and physical vapor deposition methods to make 2D heterostructures in this project. Most recently, a moire pattern induced by twist angles between different layers in vdW heterostructures is emerging. There is a new possibility to introduce the approach to investigate the strain-modulated optoelectronic vdW heterostructures, which will provide an insightful design of 2D vdW heterostructures for further device development. Particularly, the inheritance of valley physics in twisted heterostructures is expected to offer the potential in excitonic optoelectronic modulation. Secondly, our results suggest that the feasibility of vdW heterostructures can be widely extended to other piezoelectric 2D materials beyond III-V compounds, which needs further development of high-performance flexible nano-optoelectronics. Compared with bulk materials, the surface conditions of 2D materials become significant during the fabrication process as they only have an atomically thin thickness. Although vdW heterostructure-based piezo-photonic devices have been achieved in our study, the coordination of interfacial charge behaviors and the piezo-photonic performance still need further theoretical investigation and application development. Further investigations on band alignment engineering and 2D piezo-photonic behaviors should be expected before the realization of the novel device into practical applications in the future.

15302318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302318.value: Thanks to the generation of piezoelectric potential in the materials under strain, piezo-phototronic effect offers new means of manipulating photoexcited carrier transport, generation, separation and recombination behaviors via mechanical stimuli. Such novel optoelectronic devices employ mechanical strain-induced interfacial polarization as the controlling signal, differing from conventional electronically controlled devices. In this project, we have designed and fabricated heterostructures based on 2D III-VI compounds possessing superior optoelectronic and piezoelectric properties, offering an opportunity to investigate both piezo-phototronic effect and material physics of 2D materials. We developed heterojunction optoelectronic devices on flexible substrates. Strain-regulated photoresponse of the heterostructures can sufficiently modulate the device’s performance. We investigate the influence of piezo-phototronic effect on the flexible heterostructures such as 2D III-VI compound α-In2Se3/WSe2 vdW heterojunction, and further examined the strain-modulated photodetection performance of the device. With applying the mechanical strain, the performance of the photodetector can be greatly enhanced by the piezo-phototronic effect and the approach can be extended to other piezoelectric ultrathin materials beyond 2D III-V compounds. Our results of materials processing and various characterizations enable us not only to observe interesting piezo-phototronic effect in the 2D heterostructure, but also to pave the new way for enhancing 2D optoelectronic device performance.

15302418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302418.value: There are many important applications that involve a fluid flow and a porous medium flow occurring in separate but abutting domains, with the two flows coupled at the interface between the two domains. Therefore, a number of scientists and engineers have investigated the corresponding Stokes-Darcy and Navier-Stokes-Darcy models. However, most of these works consider only single-phase models, which are not applicable in many real world applications that involve multi-phase flows. In this project, we plan to utilize the Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard equation to describe multi-phase fluid flow and Darcy-Cahn-Hilliard equation to govern multi-phase flow in porous media; then we will couple the two flows with appropriately proposed interface conditions to form the Cahn-Hilliard-Navierr-Stokes-Darcy model. Although one might think that it should not be very difficult to extend the existing works for the single-phase model to the multi-phase scenario, the reality is quite the opposite. Major difficulties arise at the domain interface, which plays a key role in the interface models, especially the Beavers-Joseph interface condition. Coupling two constituent models leads to a complex system involving vastly different scales in the fluid flow and porous media flow, which demands new accurate and efficient numerical methods. The defective boundary condition increases the complexity of the coupled system even further. Therefore, this project is to carry out systematic mathematical research on the coupled multi-phase fluid flow and porous media flow. The goal of this project is to: 1) analyze the well-posedness of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navierr-Stokes-Darcy model, 2) develop a parallel non-iterative multi-physics domain decomposition method (MPDDM) to solve the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes-Darcy model, 3) mathematically analyze the stability and convergence of the proposed parallel non-iterative MPDDM, and 4) develop and analyze a Lagrange multiplier method to deal with the defective boundary condition with the proposed parallel non-iterative MPDDM. 有許多重要的應用涉及流體流動和多孔介質流動發生在分開但鄰接的區域中，兩個流動在兩個區域之間的界面處耦合。因此，許多科學家和工程師研究了相應的Stokes-Darcy和Navier-Stokes-Darcy模型。然而，這些工作中的大多數僅考慮單相模型，這些模型不適用於涉及多相流的許多現實世界應用。在這個項目中，我們計劃利用Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard方程描述多相流體流動和Darcy-Cahn-Hilliard方程來控制多孔介質中的多相流動;然後我們將兩個流程與適當提出的接口條件耦合，形成Cahn-Hilliard-Navierr-Stokes-Darcy模型。 雖然人們可能認為將單相模型的現有工作擴展到多階段方案應該不是很困難，但事實恰恰相反。域接口出現了主要困難，在接口模型中起著關鍵作用，尤其是Beavers-Joseph接口條件。耦合兩個組成模型導致一個複雜的系統，涉及流體流動和多孔介質流動的大小不同的尺度，這需要新的準確和有效的數值方法。有缺陷的邊界條件甚至進一步增加了耦合系統的複雜性。 因此，本項目是對耦合多相流體流動和多孔介質流動進行系統數學研究。該項目的目標是：1）分析Cahn-Hilliard-Navierr-Stokes-Darcy模型的適定性，2）開發並行非迭代多物理域分解方法（MPDDM）來解決Cahn- Hilliard-Navier-Stokes-Darcy模型，3）數學分析所提出的並行非迭代MPDDM的穩定性和收斂性，以及4）開發和分析拉格朗日乘數法以處理所提出的並行非迭代

15302418.label: Realisation of objectives
15302418.value: We have worked on our objectives of this project. We addressed all questions, for example, using for the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes-Darcy model and elliptic systems with interfaces. Our focuses are on the error estimates, domain decompositions techniques, convergences and stabilities for newly proposed numerical schemes. In addition the extensive numerical simulations are carried out, which are the essential parts in all publications. The immersed element spaces are used for solving a group of inverse geometric problems for recovering the material interface of a linear elasticity system, which is key part for engineering designs. The main difficulty is for 3D shape optimization of Maxwell type systems, that is very challenging topic. We are continuing work on, hopefully, it can be solved soon. In multiscale numerical techniques all coefficients are assumed to be smooth. Recently we begin investigate the multiscale numerical methods for Maxwell type systems with piece-wise rapidly oscillating coefficients. For multi-interface problems with nonlinear models involving magnetic fields our current research methods and directions lead to our next project. A domain decomposition method is proposed to solve a time-dependent Navier-Stokes-Darcy model with Beavers-Joseph interface condition and defective boundary condition. Robin boundary conditions between the Navier-Stokes domain and Darcy domain are constructed by directly re-organizing the terms in the three interface conditions, including the Beavers-Joseph condition. In order to avoid the traditional iteration for the domain decomposition method at each time step, the interface information, which is needed for the Robin type transmission conditions at the current time step, is directly predicted based on the numerical solution of the previous time steps. Backward Euler scheme is first utilized for the temporal discretization while finite elements are used for the spatial discretization. The convergences of this domain decomposition method are rigorously analyzed for the time-dependent Navier-Stokes-Darcy model with Beavers-Joseph interface condition. The major difficulties in the analysis arise from nonlinear terms and Beavers-Joseph interface condition, including a series of technical treatments and the final special norm used in the discrete Gronwall's inequality for the analysis of full discretization. Based on the above preparation, we further develop a Lagrange multiplier method under the framework of the domain decomposition method to overcome the difficulty of non-unique solutions arising from the defective boundary condition. One interesting finding of this paper is that the Lagrange multipliers are time dependent functions instead of constants. In order to improve the accuracy order for the temporal discretization, a three-step backward differentiation scheme is used to replace the backward Euler scheme. Compared with the first scheme, the second one allows us to use the relative larger time step to reduce the computational cost while keeping the same accuracy. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the features of the proposed method. Fully discrete Galerkin finite element methods are studied for the equations of miscible displacement in porous media with the commonly-used Bear–Scheidegger diffusion– dispersion tensor cases. Previous works on optimal-order L∞(0, T ; L2)-norm error estimate required the regularity assumptions, while the Bear Scheidegger diffusion–dispersion tensor is only Lipschitz continuous even for a smooth velocity field. In terms of the maximal L p-regularity of fully discrete finite element solutions of parabolic equations, optimal error estimate in Lp(0, T ; Lq)-norm and almost optimal error estimate in L∞(0, T ; Lq )-norm are established under the assumption of matrix tensor D(u) being Lipschitz continuous with respect to the solution u. This is a newly theoretical technique leading to nontrivial results, which may be applied to more wide real engineering problems. A finite element method on a fixed mesh for solving a group of inverse geometric problems for recovering the material interface of a linear elasticity system. A partially penalized immersed finite element method is used to discretize both the elasticity interface problems and the objective shape functionals accurately regardless of the shape and location of the interface. Explicit formulas for both the velocity fields and the shape derivatives of IFE shape functions are derived on a fixed mesh and they are employed in the shape sensitivity framework through the discretized adjoint method for accurately and efficiently computing the gradients of objective shape functions with respect to the parameters of the interface curve. The shape optimization for solving an inverse geometric problem is therefore accurately reduced to a constrained optimization that can be implemented efficiently within the IFE framework together with a standard optimization algorithm. We demonstrate features and advantages of the proposed IFE- based shape optimization method by several typical inverse geometric problems for linear elasticity system. This methods may be applied easily to the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes-Darcy models with two or multi interfaces. As usual for Schrödinger system with rapidly oscillating discontinuous coefficients, the multiscale asymptotic method for the system is studied. We propose a novel multiscale asymptotic expansion for the vector potential to capture the oscillations caused by the quantum current density. To solve the homogenized Maxwell--Schrödinger system, we present an alternating Crank--Nicolson finite element method. The stability estimates and the solvability of the discrete system are established. An iteration algorithm together with its convergence analysis is given. Numerical examples are carried out to demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the multiscale algorithms.

15302418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302418.value: Numerical analysis and simulation of Maxwell type equations offer many challenges in terms of mathematical and numerical issues. For example the multiscale computations for the Maxwell-Schrodinger system with rapidly oscillating coefficients under the dipole approximation that describes light-matter interaction in heterogeneous nanostructures. The immersed finite element methods are to be used to for saving many intermediate calculations at adaptive refinements along the material interfaces. In near future we are to study efficient and higher order numerical schemes for Maxwell type equations which may potentially provide engineers with better numerical tools in new smart material designs. In recent years, the study on the interaction of electromagnetic fields with two incompressible, immiscible and electrically conducting fluids is of great signification in the engineering, such as the Aluminum electrolysis cells, metallurgical industry, pump accelerators, MHD generators and fusion reactors. The results and techniques generated from this study may be the starting point for the new directions. We will continue our studies on mathematical analysis for the wellposedness and energy law of the Cahn-Hilliard-ferrohydrodynamics model, development of linear, decoupled, unconditionally stable schemes with finite element discretization for the Cahn-Hilliard-ferrohydrodynamics model, energy stability analysis for the linear decoupled scheme and convergence analysis for the linear decoupled schemes.

15302418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302418.value: This project provides a solid mathematical foundation in both modeling and numerical simulation for understanding the dynamics of the coupled multi-phase fluid flow and porous media flow, which is important for many realistic applications. In this project, extensive research are carried out for different types of efficient numerical methods for the Cahn-Hilliard-Navierr-Stokes-Darcy model, the results maybe used for the comparisons between the numerical simulations and lab experiment results for a wide range of realistic applications of the coupled multi-phase fluid flow and porous media flow. This project also provides undergraduate and graduate students many valuable training opportunities in mathematical modeling, development of numerical methods and code techniques, and mathematical analysis. They can gain solid foundation in both computational mathematics and valuable research experience.

15302518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302518.value: The goal of this project is to develop and study various types of numerical methods for solving an asymptotic coupled model of groundwater flow in fractured aquifer system. In order to simplify the model, we treat the fracture as a two-dimensional hyperplane embedded in a three-dimensional surrounding medium domain. Such procedure greatly reduces the computational cost while preserving the physical properties of groundwater flow in fractured media. Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods can easily handle meshes made of general shaped polygons or polyhedra, due to the fact that their elements are discontinuous in nature. Hence they are ideal methods for solving the asymptotic coupled flow model on complicated domains. In this project, we will study DG methods for the coupled model and derive optimal order error estimates based on general polyhedral meshes. The use of general shaped meshes allows us to simulate the flow more efficiently in the presence of intersecting fractures. A proper mesh grading technique is critical to the success of the convergence analysis of DG methods. More precisely, the mesh will be graded near the fracture hyperplane, where the flow velocity and pressure change rapidly. This is a new approach to improve the convergence properties of numerical schemes in the presence of singular solutions. In this project, we will introduce and analyze multigrid methods for the coupled model problem based on DG discretization. We aim to show the uniform convergence of multigrid algorithms on general meshes. We will also apply adaptive methods to solve the model problem when exact solutions are not available. We would like to derive a reliable and efficient a posteriori error estimator for the adaptive mesh refinement algorithm. Other types of numerical methods, such as nonconforming finite element methods and hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods, will also be studied for the steady model problem. The numerical methods proposed in this project can be further extended to simulate the unsteady fluid flow in fractured media. 本項目的主要目標是研究求解裂縫含水土層介質中地下水流模型的多種數值方法。為簡化模型以及模擬計算的方便，我們將含水土層中的裂縫視為嵌入三維周邊介質中的二維平面。此舉措可在保持裂縫介質中地下水流物理性質的基礎上，極大的降低計算量，從而提升計算速度。 間斷Galerkin方法 (DG方法) 因其自身具有的間斷有限元性質，能夠被有效的應用於一般形狀的多邊形或多面體網格。因此，DG方法是處理復雜區域上流體模型的一類非常理想的數值方法。在本項目中，我們主要研究求解裂縫介質中地下水模型的DG方法，並在多面體網格上證明其具有最優收斂速率。不規則多面體網格的應用使得我們能夠更有效的模擬交叉裂縫中的地下水流。關於此模型問題的DG方法收斂性的理論分析，很大程度上依賴於一項關鍵性技術，我們稱之為等級網格技術。具體來講，我們將對地下水流速快、壓力變化大的裂縫周邊區域做局部的等級網格剖分。這是一項能夠在奇異解存在的情況下有效提高數值方法收斂速度的新技術。 在本項目中，我們還將進一步研究基於DG方法的多重網格快速算法。我們的目標是在一般型多面體網格上證明多重網格算法的一致收斂性。另外，在模型真實解未知的情況下，我們擬使用自適應有限元方法對模型問題進行數值模擬。我們將構建一類可靠且有效的後驗誤差估計子，進而對計算區域進行自適應網格剖分。在本項目中我們還將研究求解裂縫介質中穩態地下水流模型的其它多種數值方法，包括非協調有限元方法、雜交間斷Galerkin方法 (HDG方法)等。以上提到的幾類數值方法也可以應用於非穩態地下水流模型的數值模擬，這也將是本項目的研究內容。

15302718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302718.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the most common form of liver dysfunction. It affects 20-30% of the adult population around the world. Under the current obesity epidemic, NAFLD prevalence is increaseing and imposes a huge burden to our society. Although the pathogenesis of NAFLD is not completely understood, it is generally believed that dysregulated metabolism of free fatty acids leading to insulin resistance is an essential requirement for the accumulation of hepatocellular fat and cell dysfunction in the initiation and progression of NAFLD. This proposal studies the use of piceatannol a natural analog of a well-known dietary supplement, resveratrol. It is more bioavailable and potent (in terms of antioxidant activity) than resveratrol. In our preliminary study, high-fat diet (HFD) was shown to successfully induce NAFLD and hyperlipidemia in rats and a 4-week piceatannol treatment could significantly reduce hepatic lipid content, atherogenic index, LDL-cholesterol and triacylglycerol. Secondary bile acids, which are metabolites of gut microbiota, differ significantly between disease and piceatannol treatment groups. Our data suggest that piceatannol’s beneficial effects may be a result of gut microbiota modulation. Thus, the major focus of this project is to examine whether piceatannol exerts its beneficial effects solely or partly via modulating the gut microbiota in HFD-induced NAFLD rats. Examination on the changes of endogenous and bacterial metabolites will be performed using mass spectrometry based metabolomics to reveal details about the underlying metabolic processes involved. The mechanistic pathway(s) of piceatannol in various metabolic organs, such as liver, skeletal muscle and adipose tissues, will be investigated. The proposed study will (1) determine the influences of the presence of gut microbiota on the treatment of HFD-induced NAFLD in rats using piceatannol; (2) identify the underlying mechanisms of the beneficial effects of piceatannol on HFD-induced NAFLD rats by determining the major metabolite changes in the serum, liver, skeletal muscle and adipose tissues of NAFLD rats upon the treatment of piceatannol with or without the presence of gut microbiota using a metabolomics approach; and (3) investigate whether the beneficial effects of piceatannol on NAFLD rats are via activating silent information regulation-2 homolog 1 (SIRT1)-mediated signaling pathways in various metabolic tissues, modulating gut microbiota and their metabolites or both. Data about the NAFLD pathogenesis, the role of gut microbiota on piceatannol’s effects on treating NAFLD and the mechanism of action of piceatannol could improve the existing strategies for NAFLD prevention and treatment.

15302718.label: Realisation of objectives
15302718.value: Objective 1: One of the major goals of this project is to examine the role of gut microbiota on the effect of piceatannol treatment of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced NAFLD. The basic study design is to use HFD to induced NAFLD and compare the effects of piceatannol treatments in animals with intact or depleted gut microbiota. A combination of antibiotics [ampicillin (1 g/L), vancomycin (500 mg/L), and ciprofloxacin HCl (20 mg/L), imipenem (250 mg/L) and metronidazole (1 g/L)] is used to depleted the gut microbiota in the animals. A preliminary animal study was conducted to evaluate the effect of the antibiotics treatment on the animals. The total number of bacteria after anti-biotics consumption was reduced to one-tenth of that of the normal rats. Results showed that the antibiotics consumptions do not cause significant changes on serum TG, TC, ALT and AST levels, liver lipid content and liver histology of HFD-fed SD rats. These data suggesting that the antibiotics formulation used are effective in depleting the gut-microbiota of the animals without significant effect on NAFLD. The full animal study has been conducted as proposed to evaluate the effect of piceatannol on HFD-induced NAFLD. The animals were evenly distributed into 7 groups: 1) control, 2) HFD, 3) HFD + pioglitazone (positive control), 4) HFD + piceatannol (low dose), 5) HFD + piceatannol (high dose), 6) HFD + resveratrol (low dose), and 7) HFD + resveratrol (high dose). Half of them consumed antibiotics mixture containing drinking water while the other half taking pure autoclaved drinking water. For SD rats with intact gut microbiota, treatment of HFD-fed rats with piceatannol and pioglitazone once daily via oral gavage for 8 weeks, the livers of rats were less yellowish and had less macrosteatosis, microsteatosis, ballooning and lobular inﬂammation in hepatocytes. Piceatannol and pioglitazone supplementation significantly reduced serum TC, TG and total lipid content in the HFD-fed rats when compared to those treated with control. These results demonstrate that piceatannol could alleviate NAFLD. However, resveratrol-treated rats didn’t show any effects. For the SD rats with gut microbiota depleted, Piceatannol and pioglitazone supplementation significantly reduced serum TC and total lipid content in the HFD-fed rats when compared to those treated with control. These results demonstrate that piceatannol could alleviate NAFLD in the presence of antibiotics. However, resveratrol -treated rats didn’t show any effects. When we designed the animal study, we anticipate the effects of piceatannol on treating NAFLD in rats with and without gut microbiota would be different. However, it seems that piceatannol stills exhibits anti-NALFD effects when gut microbiota was depleted. The results suggested that the effect of piceatannol on NAFLD may not be due to its modulation of the gut microbiota composition and population. There is one limitation in this study as the gut microbiota was not completed removed. Perhaps, a gem free study may be needed to further confirm the results. Objective 2: Targeted metabolomics analysis has been performed on the serum and liver collected from the animal study to quantitative the bile acid profiles in the samples collected as the project was designed based on our previous observation of substantial changes in the bile acid profiles, particularly, the secondary bile acid profiles. For the serum samples collected from rats with intact gut microbiota, the bile acid profiles of the control, HFD, piceatannol-L and piceatannol-H groups showed some differences. Some of the differences observed in previous study have been reproduced in this animal study. For the serum and liver samples collected from animals with gut microbiota depleted, the secondary bile acids were depleted as expected. Surprising, there are some differences in the primary bile acid profile observed in animals with and without gut microbiota. The bile acid profiles in animals with gut microbiota depleted was very different from those with intact gut microbiota and the bile acid profiles difference in the HFD, piceatannol groups observed for animals with intact gut microbiota were no longer observed and the differences are not significant. As the piceatannol could alleviate NAFLD in animals with gut microbiota (and secondary bile acid profiles) depleted, the data suggested that the bile acid profiles changes observed before may be associated with the effects of piceatannol, but probably not the cause of the anti-NAFLD effects of the compound. Untargeted metabolomics analysis focused on the lipid profiles (lipidomics) were further conducted to further evaluate the effects of piceatannol to liver in order to identify possible pathways related to the beneficial effects of the compound towards NAFLD. The lipid profiles of the serum with gut microbiota depleted show some distinct pattern. The major differences include the fatty acids (such as C18:1, C18:3, C20:4, C20:5, C22:6, and C24:0). Interestingly, these changes are consistent in both animals with and without gut-microbiota suggesting the effect of piceatannol may be modulating fatty acid metabolism in liver and slow down the development of NAFLD. Objective 3 and related research works To better understand the mechanism by which piceatannol suppresses the development of NAFLD, the levels of SIRT1 in rat various metabolic tissues were determined by Western blot assays. However, no significant difference in SIRI1 protein level in all groups was detected. As the animal study was delayed because of the COVID-19 pandemic and the results were sort of unexpected. The lipidomics results of the liver samples are quite promising and we would try to identify more lipid species in the analysis to further evaluate the role of fatty acid metabolism in the activities of piceatannol before we report the findings of this study. As the animal study was delayed, we have employed the metabolomics platform to study clinical samples of a different disease, adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), collected by some of our collaborators to better utilize the available resources. The metabolomics analysis identified 46 metabolites to be changed significantly among the non-progressing, processing and healthy subjects. Seven of the differential metabolites are related to dysregulated galactose metabolism and glycolysis pathways, suggesting the presence of abnormal energy metabolism at early stage of AIS. The results have been reported in international renowned journal. Piceatannol is one of the phytochemicals in the dried rhizome and root of Polygonum cuspidatum Sieb. et Zucc. (PCRR). Our study showed that PCRR-treated rats displayed significant reduction of serum TC and LDL-C, hepatic TG, TC levels and total liver lipid contents under a HFD feeding condition. In view of this, we tried to see whether we could observe similar metabolite changes as those observed in this piceatannol study in those samples. Untargeted metabolomics showed that PCRR significantly restored overall levels of eight lipid classes in liver tissues and elevates the bile acids levels in the serum. We demonstrated that PCRR protected from steatosis by promoting hepatic triglyceride export and decreasing de novo lipogenesis via regulating AMPK/ACC/FAS/PPARα signalling pathways. This is also inline with our observation in the animal study of the piceatannol which hepatic TG and lipid metabolisms would a responsible for the anti-NAFLD of the compound.

15302718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302718.value: Piceatannol and an anti-diabetes drug pioglitazone is capable to reduce macrosteatosis, microsteatosis, ballooning and lobular inﬂammation in hepatocytes and to reduce the serum triglycerides, total cholesterol and total lipid content in animals taking high fat diet. When the gut microbiota has been depleted, the reduction of macrosteatosis, microsteatosis, ballooning and lobular inﬂammation in hepatocytes are still observed. This clearly confirms the beneficial effects of piceatannol towards NAFLD and suggested that the beneficial effects do not depend on the presence of the gut microbiota in the animals. The targeted metabolomics bile acid analysis on the serum and liver samples suggested that there are consistent changes in bile acid profiles for HFD rats treated with piceatannol. When the gut microbiota depleted, the biological activities on hepatocytes are still exited despites the differences of the bile acid profiles of the disease and treatment groups are no longer observed. The experiment suggested that perhaps the lowering in triglycerides in liver would be a more important cue for the biological activities of piceatannol. The lipidomics studies showing a more detailed changes in the fatty acid profiles suggesting the liver lipid metabolism may be responsible for the beneficial effect of piceatannol. A similar metabolomics study was performed on the serum and liver samples collected from a previous animal study with treatment of dried rhizome and root of Polygonum cuspidatum Sieb. et Zucc. (PCRR) which contained piceatannol. The animals with intact gut microbiota and PCRR-treated rats displayed significant reduction of serum TC and LDL-C, hepatic TG, TC levels and total liver lipid contents under a high-fat diet feeding condition. Untargeted metabolomics showed that PCRR significantly restored overall levels of eight lipid classes in liver tissues and elevates the bile acids levels in the serum. These results have been submitted to an international renowned journal for publication (Item 3 of Section 8). These are consistent with the observation of the animal study conducted in here using piceatannol. Our data on piceatannol and PCRR clearly demonstrated hepatic triglyceride export and de novo lipogenesis in liver are involved. Metabolomics analysis has been conducted on clinical samples of a different disease, adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Seven metabolites related to dysregulated galactose metabolism and glycolysis pathways are identified to be significantly affected, suggesting the presence of abnormal energy metabolism at early stage of AIS. The results have been reported in international renowned journal. (Item 2 of Section 8).

15302718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302718.value: The lipidomics data of liver and serum from gut microbiota depleted groups would be important to further understand the mechanisms involved. Some changes in fatty acids have been identified. More detailed analysis of the lipidomics data would certainly helpful in understanding the mechanism of the piceatannol. The de novo lipogenesis via regulating AMPK/ACC/FAS/PPARα signalling pathway have been observed in PCRR. Thus, further study to investigate the underlying mechanism behind decreased lipid level by piceatannol, particularly the pathway related to TG metabolism, such as AMPK, FAS, ACC, and PPARα as well as TC metabolism (including ABCG5/G8, CYP7A1, LDLR, NPC1L1 would be our subsequent plan.

15302718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302718.value: Piceatannol and an anti-diabetes drug pioglitazone is capable reducing liver inflammation and the development of NAFLD in animal model. A similar reduction in serum triglycerides, total cholesterol and total lipid content are also observed. The beneficial effects of piceatannol is not through modulation of gut microbiota. In the absence of gut microbiota, piceatannol is still beneficial towards NAFLD. The study clearly confirms the beneficial effects of piceatannol towards NAFLD as the effects has been shown in multiple animal experiments with different experimental conditions. The metabolomics study showing that although the bile acid profiles are being modulated, but the changes is probably not the cause of the beneficial effects. In the experiment using animal without gut microbiota, the liver fatty acid profile has been changed significantly suggested modulation of liver lipid metabolism such as de novo lipogenesis would probably be one of the biological actions of piceatannol. More studies are need to further confirmed this.

15303018.label: Project Objectives
15303018.value: We propose to develop an overall experimental protocol that we plan to couple our ultrafast broadband TRF with TA to enable direct probe of temporal evolution of GQs excited-states in timescale ranging seamlessly from femtoseconds to hundreds nanoseconds after excitation. The protocol is proposed also to examine change as time of the fluorescence anisotropy and solvent effect on the dynamics of excited-state. The protocol is designed to assess identity and determine lifetime and efficiency of the transient species, thereby to establish a comprehensive picture for deactivation pathways with emphasizing on the charge-transfer and Hoogsteen hydrogen-bonding related proton-transfer in the selected systems. We propose to utilize the protocol in (1) to perform systematic ultrafast study for GQs with the varied typical structure and different molecularity from a set of G-rich sequences including among others a number of human telomeric DNAs and RNAs, in dilute solution with stabilizing cations. The results will allow acquisition of the hitherto unknown spectra, dynamics, and excited-state pathways signature to the various GQ structures in the systems chosen. The ultrafast study proposed in (2) is planned also for the purpose to allow direct comparison between the excited-state behaviors of the various GQs. By comparing the results from GQs with the varied topology stabilized by the different agent, this work will provide concert evidence for addressing how the stabilizing cation, molecularity, structural polymorphism in terms of, e.g. the varied loop structure, rigidity, and different strand orientation on the dynamics and excited-states of GQs. We propose to perform parallel ultrafast experiments on GQs from the selected sequences in cell-mimicking molecular crowding condition in nanosized water pool encapsulated by reverse-micelle or solution containing varied crowding and/or dehydrating agent. With the results in the dilute solution as a benchmark reference, the finding of this work will enable to evaluate property and dynamics of GQs in the biologically relevant condition. In particular, comparing the results in the reverse-micelle vs cosolute condition will observe solid evidence for clarifying effects of volume exclusion, dehydration, and environmental confinement on the excited-state dynamics of GQs. The proposed ultrafast study on GQs from the chosen human telomeric DNAs and the counterpart RNAs in the dilute and molecular crowding condition is also designed aiming to seek experimental evidence for understanding the fundamentally different function of DNA vs RNA GQs in genomic stability and cellular processes. The overall results of the proposed works on GQs will contribute importantly to the photophysics and especially the understanding of structure-property relationship of nucleic acids. The dynamics of charge-transfer and proton-transfer in GQs should prove relevant to the vulnerability of GQs towards the DNA oxidative damage and to the anticancer drug design as well as the application of GQs in molecular devices and nanotechnology.

15303018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303018.value: In addition to the canonical double helix, nucleic acids can adopt several noncanonical structures including the four-stranded G-quadruplexes (GQs). Formed in guanine(G)-rich sequences, GQs comprise stacks of planar-square G-tetrad composed of four G bases linked by Hoogsteen H-bonding interactions. G-rich sequences, likely form GQs in vitro and in vivo, are abundant throughout human genome, play important roles in genetic processes and as therapeutic target for anti-cancer drug design. Concentrated with G base, the known oxidative hotspot in nucleic acids, GQs may also contribute to oxidative stress responsible for DNA strand breaks, aging, and cancer. Besides, with their structure controllable and highly polymorphic, GQs have potent applications in nanotechnology and fabrication of molecular devices. Despite of the enormous research interests and rich information on their structures, thermo-stability, and thermo-dynamics, little is currently known about electronic property and dynamics of electronically excited-states of GQs. This arises due to the intrinsic complex nature of GQs excited-states and thus the great difficulty for direct study of these systems. The excited-state processes, governed by inter-base electronic coupling and controlled by both the GQs structure and environmental condition, contain however key information for understanding at molecular level the photostability vs photodamage of GQs and the properties rendering their biomedical and material related applications. To decipher the interplay between the structure, environment, and excited-state dynamics is nowadays one of the major frontiers in the photophysics and photochemistry study of GQs. Aiming to explore this largely unknown area, herein we propose to use our state-of-the-art ultrafast time-resolved spectroscopy to develop a protocol for systematic and in-depth investigation of excited-states of GQs with diverse structures formed from a series of carefully chosen G-rich sequences including a number of human telomeric DNAs and RNAs in controlled condition, e.g. cell-mimicking environments. The proposed research will enable the first real-time probe and comprehensive characterization of GQs excite-states and will allow acquisition of dynamic and spectral parameters signature to the varied GQs under the designated conditions. Making comparison between results from the proposed work on the varied systems will allow unveiling the molecular origins for impacts of the structural polymorphism and the molecular crowding on excited-state dynamics of GQs. The ultrafast study proposed in (2) is planned also for the purpose to allow direct comparison between the excited-state behaviors of the various GQs. By comparing the results from GQs with the varied topology stabilized by the different agent, this work will provide concert evidence for addressing how the stabilizing cation, molecularity, structural polymorphism in terms of, e.g. the varied loop structure, rigidity, and different strand orientation on the dynamics and excited-states of GQs.

We propose to perform parallel ultrafast experiments on GQs from the selected sequences in cell-mimicking molecular crowding condition in nanosized water pool encapsulated by reverse-micelle or solution containing varied crowding and/or dehydrating agent. In particular, comparing the results in the reverse-micelle vs cosolute condition will observe solid evidence for clarifying effects of volume exclusion, dehydration, and environmental confinement on the excited-state dynamics of GQs.

The proposed ultrafast study on GQs from the chosen human telomeric DNAs and the counterpart RNAs in the dilute and molecular crowding condition is also designed aiming to seek experimental evidence for understanding the fundamentally different function of DNA vs RNA GQs in genomic stability and cellular processes.

The overall results of the proposed works on GQs will contribute importantly to the photophysics and especially the understanding of structure-property relationship of nucleic acids. The dynamics of charge-transfer and proton-transfer in GQs should prove relevant to the vulnerability of GQs towards the DNA oxidative damage and to the anticancer drug design as well as the application of GQs in molecular devices and nanotechnology.

15303018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303018.value: We have conducted most of the experiments planned in this project. Through these measurements, expected evidences have been obtained for addressing most of the questions posed in the proposal. Our study shows, for the first time, that a direct probe of excited state spectra and quantitative observation of a multi-channel nonradiative pathway for human telomeric (HT) DNA formed antiparallel basket-type G-quadruplex (BGQ) with the presence of Na+ ions. The pathway is dominated by proton transfer (PT) coupled with varied degree of inter-tetrad charge transfer from two types of states lasting, respectively, in the ten and hundreds picosecond timescales. These states, being almost equally important, contribute altogether the overwhelming ~85% of the entire nonradiative deactivation. Our comparative study with hybrid-type G-quadruplex (HGQ) in K+ solution suggests a leading role of structural rigidity in governing inter-base coupling and nature of electronic excitation while with the metal ions and glycosidic bond conformation to affect merely the quantitative energies and lifetimes of the long living states involved in the unimolecularly folded GQs. We also demonstrate that the peculiar hydration and confined condition imposed by the reverse-micelle nano-cavity water pool prolong the excited state lifetimes and inhibit the nonradiative processes. Our study demonstrates the first direct and comprehensive detection of the fluorescence dynamics and deactivation cascades for a bimolecular GQ formed from a HT repeat-containing RNA 5'-[UAG3U]2-3’ (TERRA12 GQ) in the parallel folding structure. The results observed multi-pathway decay containing the hitherto unknown high energy excimer with charge transfer (CT) between stacked Gs in the tetrad core that deactivates through PT with the time constant of ~7.4 ps. Our data also show the participation of low energy exciplex formed by CT in the loop region featuring the deeply red shifted weak emission not seen in BGQ/Na+ and HGQ/K+ from the telomeric DNA. The study highlights important differences in the excited states between TERRA12 GQ and the DNA GQs examined in the past studies, underscores decisive role of the distinct structure, sequence content, and loop conformation in accounting for the particular energy, electronic property, and decay dynamics of the TERRA12 GQ excited states. The finding of this work shed light into the structure-property relationship of GQ after photo-excitation, providing new insight into the mechanism for photo-stability and the origin of the intrinsic fluorescence of GQs. This may encourage further investigations into the molecular details and structural diversity on the nonradiative pathways of DNA and RNA GQs.

15303018.value: Based on the outcome of this project, further research will be attempted to perform more combined fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments to directly probe the dynamics and spectra of the excited-states for more GQs formed from RNAs in reverse-micelle with molecular crowding condition.

15303018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303018.value: The structure and electronic property of nucleic acids determines their biological functions and material related applications. G-quadruplex (GQ) represents a four-stranded structure formed in guanine(G)-rich sequence by stacking of G-tetrad composed by four G bases. GQs exist not only in vitro but also in vivo, they play important parts in genome stability. With their structure highly polymorphic and formation controllable by factors like content of G-rich sequence, identity of stabilizing agent, and environmental condition, GQs have found potent applications in nanomaterial and molecular electronics fabrication. Following the research plan suggested in the proposal, some GQs formed from DNAs and RNAs in dilute solution with stabilizing cations condition as well as in reverse-micelle with molecular crowding condition were investigated using femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy and steady-state method. The results help establish an overall description of excited state cascades for the GQs and advance our knowledge on the electronic and dynamic characteristics of GQs in varied structure and condition including the cell-mimicking environment. The outcomes of this project have led to several publications in top international journals. The research grant allows training of several students, at both undergraduate and post graduated levels.

15303218.label: Realisation of objectives
15303218.value: This project aims for developing multi-material thermal drawing process for the fabrication of stretchable and conductive fibers, and exploring their application in flexible/wearable electronics. All the research objectives have been achieved. The detailed description of the realization of objectives are discussed below. Objective 1. To develop multi-material thermal drawing for the continuous fabrication of elastomeric fibers with diameter tuneable in the range of 5 µm-1000 µm. We have developed a core-shell preform, which is drawn into core-shell fibers with diameters ranging from a few tens of micrometers to millimeters. The core was made of stretchable polymer Poly(styrene-butadiene-styrene) (SBS), and the shell was made of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA). The core diameter was controlled to be much smaller than the thickness of the shell. The thermal drawing temperature was tuned so that continuous drawing was achieved. After getting the core-shell fiber, the PMMA shell was dissolved with acids. The final stretchable SBS fiber with a diameter in the range of 5 µm-1000 µm was then obtained after some brief rinsing and drying. The fiber can be stretched up to ~1000%. Objective 2. To functionalize the elastomeric fibers with electrical conductivity by loading metallic nano/micro materials and metal coatings through post modifications. We have developed a chemical process to load the Ag+ ions onto the SBS fibers, followed by a chemical reduction of the Ag+ ions to form Ag particles. We tuned the degree of adsorption and reduction. The Ag coating endowed high conductivity of the SBS fibers, even when they were stretched to large strains. These fibers could be stretched by few hundred times without significant deterioration of the performance. Objective 3. To fabricate stretchable conductive yarns and fabrics using the as-made elastomeric conductive fibers through spinning and weaving. Based on the achievement learned from objective 1 and 2, we have developed a multi-core fiber fabrication. We first did a normal thermal drawing to produce the single-core-shell (SBS-PMMA) fiber following procedures developed in objective 1. We then parallelly packed the single core fiber as a new preform, and then drew the fiber for a second time so as to produce a multi-core-shell fiber. We then followed the same procedures to wash away the PMMA, to load the Ag ions and to form the Ag particles by chemical reduction, so as to form the multi-filament SBS fibers. Finally, we twisted the multi-filament fibers to form yarns. These yarns were then used as building blocks for braiding, weaving and knitting process. In some cases, we also coated the surface of fibrous substrates with liquid metal, e.g., EGaIn, which can further improve the conductivity upon stretching. Objective 4. To study the chemical, mechanical, electrical of the stretchable conductors, and to optimize it to high stretchability, high conductivity, and high stability. We have setup house-made testing system to evaluate the stretchability and conductivity of the fibers, yarns, and fabrics. The system was able to measure both the strain and the resistance at the same time, with a precise control using electric motors. We were able to tune the stretchability and conductivity by changing the fiber diameter, the fiber numbers (single or multi-filaments), the twist of yarns, and the weaving/knitting parameters. The textiles can be generally stretched to a few hundred percent to more than one thousand percent, with a good conductivity. Objective 5. To do proof-of-concept demonstration of fiber-based stretchable supercapacitors with the as-made fibers, yarns and fabrics as conductive substrates. We have made use of the fibers and yarns as building blocks to assemble wearable devices including wearable strain sensors, heaters, ECG sensors. All these devices are highly permeable; the permeability is similar to normal fabrics. We also tested the washing ability of the ECG device using standard laundry procedures. The ECG device can be washed for more than 20 times, without obvious deterioration of the performance. We also use the fiber and yarns as electrodes for making wearable capacitors and batteries. We coated the conductive yarns and fabrics with cathodic and anodic materials, and then sealed them with electrolytes. We successfully fabricated wire-type and pouch-type wearable lithium batteries showing high energy density, good cycling stability, and outstanding flexibility.
