15303218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303218.value: We have developed stretchable liquid metal based conductors and Ag-SBS based conductors. Based on these materials, we developed wearable and permeable types of strain sensors, ECG sensors, heaters, as well as wearable wire-type and pouch-type batteries. Eight peer-reviewed journal articles have been published in high-impact journals including Nature Materials (1 article), Advanced Functional Materials (3 articles), Advanced Energy Materials (2 articles), and Small Structures (1 article). One paper is in the revised review process (revised submission to be submitted to Cell Report Physical Science. PI has also been invited to deliver oral and keynote lectures in many international symposiums, conferences, and workshops.

15303218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303218.value: The as-developed stretchable conductive fibers, yarns, and fabrics are very durable. They are suitable for low-speed weaving and knitting process. Therefore, these materials should have very wide application potential for wearable electronics in general. In the future, we hope to further develop a larger scale of fabrication capability to continuously fabricate a large quantity of these materials, and to improve their uniformity. And then, we would like to build full-body wearable electronics using these electrodes as fundamental building blocks. We should also work on integrating other functional materials with these electrode materials to realize high levels of device functions. The third direction is to try wireless communications using these fibrous building blocks.

15303218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303218.value: The development of stretchable electronics opens up a wide range of applications including robotic skins, wearable electronics, medical implants for health monitoring and disease diagnostics, point-of-care treatment, and biological actuation. One critical challenge to address in this field is how to fabricate high-performance and highly stretchable conductors, because they are essential components of all kinds of electronic devices. To date, most reported elastomeric conductors are developed on thin-film formats. When compared with elastic thin films, elastic fibers show obvious advantages in stretchability, durability, drape, and integrability into different 3D shapes. This project has developed scalable methods to fabricate high-performance fibrous stretchable conductors. Metals such as liquid metal, or Ag particles are fabricated on stretchable fibers, yarns, and fabrics through methods such as coating, printing, and chemical depositions. These fibrous conductors show outstanding conductivity even under large tensile strains up to 1000%. Wearable electronic devices including strain sensors, ECG sensors, heaters, and batteries have been developed based on these highly stretchable fibrous conductors. The fabrication methods and the advanced fibrous conductors developed in this project can find a broad range of applications for wearable, on-skin, and even implantable electronics in the future.

15303718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303718.value: Column-bound electron and hole pairs, known as excitons, are primary photo-excitations in semiconductors. The inversion symmetry breaking and strong spin-orbit coupling in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) results in the splitting of their conduction bands, allowing the presence of optically bright and dark intra-valley excitons. The bright excitons are featured with parallel electron spin polarization, which can directly couple to the light with an in-plane polarization. Yet, the dark excitons with anti-parallel spin polarization have a longer lifetime than the bright counterparts but a zero in-plane dipole moment, making such optical transitions spin-forbidden and silent at conventional normal-incidence illumination. Recently, several elegant approaches, including near-field coupling, edge detection, magnetic brightening and optical antenna coupling have been developed to detect the dark excitons in monolayer TMDCs. They either involve extreme detection, intense magnetic field or strong tip-enhancement. Moreover, coupling such dark excitons with other types of optical excitations like localized surface plasmons remains unexplored although in the past decades the plasmon-bright-exciton coupling has been extensively studied in various systems to reach the strong coupling regime. This proposal aims to probe the dark excitons in monolayer TMDCs with plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities and also realize plasmon-dark-exciton strong coupling. Such plasmonic nanocavities can be readily formed by placing single metallic nanoparticles (monomers or dimers) atop a metal film with tiny gaps in between. Our earlier studies have demonstrated that such nanocavities can sustain both out-of-plane-polarized and in-plane-polarized plasmon modes and also higher-order hybridized modes, exhibiting ultra-strong local field enhancement and extremely small mode volume. Upon introducing a TMDC monolayer in the gap region, the dark excitons can be invoked through near-field coupling to out-of-plane polarized gap plasmons to generate a photoluminescence peak accordingly. In addition, upon tuning the gap plasmon resonance to spectrally overlap with the dark exciton energy (either by changing particle size or gap thickness), the plasmon-dark-exciton coupling is expected to occur in the scattering response of the hybrid system. Subsequently, active control over this coupling by temperature scanning can further quantify the Rabi splitting of the new plexciton state. The project will be carried out in collaboration with Professor Peter Nordlander at Rice University, and he is responsible for partial theoretical understanding of our experimental results. This joint study will certainly deepen our understanding of the optical and electronic properties of TMDCs and could pave the way for employing these materials in quantum information and optoelectronics devices. 受庫侖作用束縛的電子-空穴對是半導體材料中的主要光學激發模式。單層過渡金屬硫化物的晶格中心對稱破缺和強電子自旋-軌道耦合造成其導帶劈裂，允許光學亮和暗的谷內激子同時存在。亮激子具有平行電子自旋極化，可以直接與面內偏振的入射光耦合。然而，反平行自旋極化的暗激子具有極小的面內偶極矩和更長的壽命，使得其無法與正入射的光束耦合，成為自旋禁阻躍遷。最近，一些巧妙的方案被用來探測單層過渡金屬硫化物中的暗激子，包括近場耦合，邊緣激發，磁致亮化和光學天線耦合。這些方法有的需要極端探測條件，有的使用強磁場誘導或者納米針尖增強。盡管過去數十年間在多種系統中都觀察到金屬表面等離激元和亮激子的光學耦合和強耦合現象，然而暗激子和其它光學激發模式的耦合還鮮有研究。 本項目旨在利用表面等離激元顆粒-薄膜納米光學腔來探測單層硫化物中的暗激子，並實現等離激元和暗激子的強耦合。這種納米光學腔可以通過在單個金屬納米顆粒（單聚體或雙聚體）和金屬薄膜之間生成一個納米尺度的間隙而形成。我們早期的研究表明這種納米光學腔支持一個垂直於表面極化和一個面內極化的共振模式，以及一個高階的雜化模式。一旦把單層過渡金屬硫化嵌入在這種納米光學腔內，暗激子可以通過近場耦合與垂直於表面的間隙表面等離激元共振相互作用從而發光。通過調控間隙等離激元共振能量與暗激子能級匹配，有望在此雜化系統的散射譜上觀測到等離激元和暗激子的耦合。此外，通過調節溫度可以實現對此耦合的主動控制，從而量化此雜化系統的拉比分裂。我們將和萊斯大學的Peter Nordlander教授合作開展本項目，對方將會負責理論解釋我們的實驗結果。我們期望這個聯合項目可以加深對過渡金屬硫化物在金屬納米光學腔中的電學和光學行為理解，同時為把這些材料和結構用在量子信息和光電子器件中做好基礎研究。

15303718.label: Realisation of objectives
15303718.value: We have achieved the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities, with details summarized as follows. Results achieved (1) We have successfully probed the existence of dark excitons in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) with single plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities at room temperature (objective 1), and demonstrated control over the radiative properties of the dark excitons with localized surface plasmons, such as Purcell-enhanced emission rate and plasmonic nanoantenna induced direction radiation (objective 2). To achieve the above-described project objectives, we have demonstrated the nanocavity coupling of the spin-forbidden dark excitons in monolayer WSe2 using the plasmonic gap mode of a metal nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) geometry. The gap plasmon mode of the cavity has a large out-of-plane electric field component and ultra-small mode volume, enhancing the radiative decay rate of the dark excitons with an out-of-plane dipole, while the weak in-plane field component in the cavity center has less impact on the radiation from the bright excitons with an in-plane dipole. We have observed the photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy of such hybrid system shows a pronounced emission peak below the bright exciton energy, which is a phenomena not observed in the PL spectrum of bare WSe2. Numerical aperture dependent signal collection reveals clear signatures of the out-of-plane dipole radiation from the dark exciton. We have also found that double-Lorentz fitting of the PL spectra quantifies the respective radiation energy and intensity of the bright and dark excitons, showing an energy splitting of about 60 meV. To fully understand the above-described experimental observations, on the one hand, we have performed full-wave electrodynamics simulations on the hybrid system, and found that the sub-wavelength plasmonic NPoM cavity supports a Purcell enhancement of over 10^6 for the dark exciton emission intensity. This significantly exceeds the previously reported enhancement of 2×10^3 in the vicinity of a gold nanotip, and overcomes the intrinsic weakly-radiative nature of the dark excitons. On the other hand, we have developed a full-quantum model consisting of three states and quantum radiations to provide a microscopic description of the measured dark-exciton emission spectrum. We believe that the nanoplasmonic approach described above provides an efficient and easy-to-implement method for brightening the excitonic dark states in two-dimensional semiconductors and understanding their room-temperature dynamics. A manuscript reporting the above results is currently under revision with Nano Letters (2022). Objectives 1 and 2 achieved. (2) We have successfully demonstrated temperature-controlled plasmon-bright-exciton coupling in two typical monolayer TMDCs both coupled with single plasmonic nanostructures (objective 3), and revealed the effect of dark excitons in the plasmon-bright-exciton coupling strength by analyzing their temperature-dependent single-particle scattering spectra (objective 4). To achieve the abovementioned project objectives, we have developed an indirect spectroscopic method to probe the dark excitons in two representative TMDCs (for WS2 and MoS2 monolayers), namely thermal tuning of plasmon-bright-exciton coupling spectroscopy. In experiment, we have coupled respectively monolayer WS2 and MoS2 with an open plasmonic nanocavity (an Au@Ag nanocuboid) and covered the whole system with an Al2O3 protection layer. By carrying out temperature-dependent differential reflectance and single-particle dark-field scattering spectroscopy on these hybrid systems, we have found the presence of the excitonic dark states modiﬁes the temperature-dependent plasmon-bright-exciton coupling strength of each monolayer TMDC-plasmonic nanocavity coupling system. Specifically, we have observed that the modiﬁcations show an opposite manner for WS2 and MoS2 monolayers. In theory, we performed coupled-oscillator model analysis to reveal that the monolayer WS2-nanocavity coupling strength increases with rising temperature, yet that for the monolayer MoS2-nanocavity diminishes, which both follow the temperature evolution of the respective exciton oscillator strength obtained by ﬁtting the reﬂectance spectra of each pristine TMDC monolayer with a multi-Lorentz oscillator model. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations with experimentally determined exciton resonance energies and line widths at elevated temperatures further reveal a quantitative proportionality between the plasmon−bright-exciton coupling strength and the bright exciton oscillator strength as predicted by a simplified two-level Boltzmann thermodynamic model. On the basis of these experimental, theoretical, and numerical results, we propose that such a dramatic difference in the temperature-dependent plasmon-bright-exciton coupling strengths of the two systems is due to the reversed sign of energy diﬀerence between the bright and dark excitons in WS2 and MoS2 monolayers, which consequently leads to opposite redistribution of their exciton population (proportional to their respective oscillator strength) under thermal tuning. We believe that our comparative study provides a uniﬁed physics scenario of recent experimental results on the exciton oscillator strengths of these two typical TMDC monolayers, which is of critical importance for fundamental studies such as high-temperature stable polaritons and also for thermally robust photonic applications and nanoscale thermal switching in optical devices. These results have been published in ACS Photonics 2019, 6, 411-421. Objectives 3 and 4 achieved. (3) Beyond the approved revised project objectives, we have also carried out studies on the effects of particle-film gap thickness and emitter location in the photoluminescence (PL) intensity of TMDC monolayers sandwiched in plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities in the weak coupling regime. Briefly, we have investigated the Purcell effect-enhanced PL of monolayer MoS2 inserted in the gap of a gold nanoparticle (AuNP)–alumina (Al2O3)–gold film (Au Film) structure. Under confocal illumination by a 532 nm CW laser, we observed a 7-fold PL peak intensity enhancement for the cavity-sandwiched MoS2 at an optimal Al2O3 thickness of 5 nm, corresponding to a local PL intensity enhancement of ∼350 by normalizing the actual illumination area to the cavity’s effective near-field enhancement area. To understand these experimental results, we have performed full-wave electromagnetic simulations to reveal a counterintuitive fact that radiation enhancement comes from the non-central area of the cavity rather than the cavity center. By scanning an electric dipole across the nanocavity, we obtained an average radiation enhancement factor of about 65 for an Al2O3 spacer thickness of 4 nm, agreeing well with the experimental thickness. Our results indicate the importance of configuration optimization, emitter location and excitation condition when using such plasmonic nanocavities to modulate the radiation properties of quantum emitters. These results have been published in Nanophotonics 2020, 9 (7), 2097-2105, representing an excellent extension work pertinent to Objectives 3 and 4. (4) Finally, we have employed a phenomenological tight-binding model to understand layer number-dependent excitonic responses of monolayer and few-layered WS2, and used the Varshni formula to describe the temperature-dependent A-exciton emission energy of monolayer WS2. In experiment, we have used micro-Raman mapping and spectroscopy methods to precisely determine the layer number of each region in a triangle WS2 flake prepared by chemical vapor deposition; we have then combined differential reflectance and photoluminescence spectroscopies to measure the layer number-dependent excitonic resonance energies of the WS2 flake. In theory, we have applied density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the layer number-dependent band structure of WS2 and extract their corresponding bandgap energies; we have then developed a phenomenological tight-binding model to make theoretical fitting of the measured layer-dependent exciton responses of WS2, showing good agreement with the DFT results. Finally, we have found out that the temperature-dependent emission intensity variation of monolayer WS2 be probably associated with thermal redistribution of bright-dark exciton populations at intermediate temperatures and increased non-radiative damping due to the enhanced electron-phonon interaction at elevated temperatures. These results have been published in Nanoscale Horizons 2019, 4, 969-974, representing an excellent extension work pertinent to Objective 1.

15303718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303718.value: Major findings and research outcome of this GRF research project are summarized in the following 4 aspects: (1) We have experimentally demonstrated that coupling spin-forbidden dark excitons of 2D TMDCs to a metal nanoparticle-on-mirror cavity leads to plasmon-induced resonant emission with the intensity comparable to that of spin-allowed bright excitons. Furthermore, we have developed a three-state quantum model combined with full-wave electrodynamic calculations to interpret the experimental results, revealing that the radiative decay rate of the dark excitons can be enhanced by nearly six orders of magnitude through the Purcell effect, therefore compensating their intrinsically weakly radiative nature (refer to item 1 in Part C). (2) We have experimentally demonstrated temperature-controlled plasmon-bright-exciton coupling between two typical monolayer TMDCs and single plasmonic nanostructures, and measured their temperature-dependent single-particle scattering spectra and differential reflectance spectra of uncoupled monolayer TMDCs. By analyzing the scattering spectra with a coupled-oscillator model and the reflectance spectra with a multi-Lorentz oscillator model, we have revealed the presence of dark excitons in the two monolayer TMDCs and their effect in the plasmon-bright-exciton coupling strength based on a two-level Boltzmann model (refer to item 2 in Part C). (3) We have maximized the Purcell effect-enhanced photoluminescence (PL) of an MoS2 monolayer sandwiched in a metal particle-on-film nanocavity through precise tuning of the thicknesses of two dielectric spacers between the metal particle and TMDC and between the metal film and TMDC, showing a 7-fold PL peak intensity enhancement at an optimal spacer thickness of 5 nm. Moreover, we have employed full-wave electromagnetic simulations to reveal a counterintuitive fact that radiation enhancement comes from the non-central area of the cavity rather than the cavity center. By scanning an electric dipole across the nanocavity, we obtained an average radiation enhancement factor of about 65 for an Al2O3 spacer thickness of 4 nm, agreeing well with the experimental thickness (refer to item 3 in Part C). (4) We have developed a phenomenological tight-binding model to describe the excitonic response of 2D WS2 as a function of layer number, showing good agreement with both experimentally measured excitonic resonance energies and the results by density-functional theory calculations. We have revealed that the temperature-dependent emission intensity variation of monolayer WS2 be related to thermal-induced population redistribution of bright and dark excitons at intermediate temperatures and increased non-radiative damping due to the significant electron-phonon interaction at elevated temperatures (refer to item 4 in Part C).

15303718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303718.value: While carrying out this GRF research project, we have come up with a new idea about using the high-Q magnetic plasmon resonance mode of an ultra-compact metal nanocube-on-mirror cavity to realize selective brightening of the interlayer excitons in a sandwiched transition metal dichalcogenide vdW heterostructure. Based on this new idea and some preliminary results, the PI has developed and submitted a GRF proposal in 2021. Compared to the low-Q bonding electric dipolar mode in the plasmonic nanosphere-on-mirror cavity employed in the present project, the high-Q (~25) magnetic dipole (MD) plasmon mode allows for spectrally-selective radiative enhancement of interlayer excitons, being almost off-resonant with intralayer excitons; the small MD mode volume (~10^4 nm3) enables spatially selective interrogation of photo-excited interlayer excitons within the cavity, avoiding the contribution from the surrounding heterostructure area. The PI expects that this new project will develop a novel plasmonic approach for manipulating radiative and non-radiative relaxation of interlayer excitons, including competing decay pathways and relaxation dynamics. Results could pave the way for further investigating the elusive dynamics of multi-excitonic systems within the framework of plasmonic nanocavity quantum electrodynamics and also for exploiting TMDC vdW heterostructures to build up high-performance ultra-compact nanophotonic and optoelectronic devices.

15303718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303718.value: In monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the significant spin-orbit coupling induces splitting of their valence and conduction bands, resulting in optically bright and dark intra-valley excitons. Compared to the spin-allowed bright excitons featuring an in-plane dipole moment, the spin-forbidden dark excitons have an out-of-plane dipole moment and longer lifetimes, making them optically silent at conventional normal-incidence illumination. Through carrying out this project, on the one hand, we have theoretically developed and experimentally demonstrated a nanoplasmonic approach to control the radiative properties of dark excitons by coupling TMDCs monolayers with several plasmonic nanocavities. Briefly, we have shown that coupling the dark excitons of a TMDC monolayer to an ultra-compact metal nanoparticle-on-mirror cavity leads to plasmon-induced resonant emission with the intensity comparable to that of the bright excitons, and their radiation directionality can be manipulated by the cavity gap plasmon mode. On the other hand, we have developed two indirect spectroscopic methods to probe the presence of dark excitons in monolayer TMDCs, their relative energy states and population exchange between the dark and bright excitons under temperature variation. Our nanoplasmonic approaches have overcome the limitations of many previous methods like near-field coupling, edge detection, magnetic brightening and antenna coupling.

15304418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304418.value: Large and high-dimensional data arise in many diverse fields of sciences and humanities, including biology, economics, finance, information technology and health sciences. In this project, we propose a unified parallel computing framework for fitting high-dimensional models. The proposed parallel framework will be applied to several important statistical models in high dimensions, including the linear regression models, generalized linear models and covariance matrix estimation problems. For the algorithms to be developed, we will study their numerical convergence and implement them in computer software. This project aims to develop novel computational algorithms and theories for high-dimensional models, and is expected to stimulate new research directions in computational statistics. Statistical properties including the estimation error bound and oracle selection properties of the solution sequences from the proposed algorithms will be studied. Extensive simulation studies will be carried to evaluate the algorithms and compare with the existing methods. 高維數據出現在許多不同的自然科學和人文科學領域，包括生物醫學學，經濟學，和信息技術科學。本項目提出一個適用用於高維模型的併行計算方法，並將提出的並行方法應用於幾個高維情形下重要的統計模型，包括線性回歸模型，廣義線性模型和協方差矩陣估計問題。對於所提出的的並行算法，將研究其數值收斂性質並在計算機軟件中實現它們。也將研究所提出的算法的數值解的統計性質，包括解序列的估計誤差和變量選擇的相合性， 該項目旨在發展新穎的計算算法和高維模型理論，並有望激發計算統計學裡新的研究方向。

15305018.label: Project Objectives
15305018.value: Analysis of the kernel-based pairwise learning algorithms. We shall develop analysis for a class of pairwise reproducing kernels and the algorithms based on the kernels. We shall consider the relations between pairwise learning and pointwise learning, and the relations between the hypothesis spaces of these two classes of algorithms. For least squares loss, we shall consider the method for decomposing pairwise learning to pointwise learning. We shall consider the pointwise regularized least squares with offset term. We shall consider the relations between empirical features for pointwise learning, and for pairwise learning, and develop analysis for empirical feature-based pairwise learning algorithms with l^1 regularization, and then consider the general folded-concave regularization. 15305018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305018.value: Pairwise learning is a large family of supervised learning algorithms for the problems that provide no (real-valued) labels, but only the differences between labels of each pair of sample points. Pairwise learning is widely applied and studied for the problems of ranking, AUC maximization, metric learning, gradient learning, learning with minimum error entropy principle, and so on. Existing kernel-based algorithms either try to fit the regression function of the labels, but suffer from the unknown of offset which vanishes in the observations of label differences; or try to fit the pairwise regression function of label differences, therefore suffer from the big computational complexity caused by a large number of kernel coefficients in the model. Moreover, these algorithms are hard to parallelize. In this project, we shall provide a new analysis of a class of pairwise kernels. Based on the analysis, we shall develop and analyze a fast implementation of the pairwise learning algorithms with least squares loss. We shall develop the parallelization of the pairwise learning algorithms with both least squares and general convex loss functions, to meet the demand of applications with large-scale data. We shall study the empirical feature-based pairwise learning schemes that drive sparse approximations. As an application of our analysis on the pairwise kernels, we shall provide analysis to the classical regularized least squares algorithm with offset terms. 成對學習是一大類監督學習算法，被用於處理不帶有（實值）監督標籤，只包含兩兩樣本點標籤差值的問題。成對學習被廣泛應用於排序，AUC最大化，度量學習，梯度學習，最小誤差熵算法等問題，並得到研究。文獻中已有的基於核方法的算法要麼試圖擬合監督標籤對應的回歸函數，因而苦於無從推斷在標籤差值採樣中消失的回歸函數偏移量；要麼試圖擬合標籤差值對應的成對回歸函數，因而需要面對巨大的核方法係數矩陣帶來的極大計算複雜度。更重要地，已有的算法很難實現並行計算。在這個研究項目中，我們將提供對一類成對學習核的全新分析。基於這些分析，我們發展並分析使用最小二乘損失函數的成對學習算法的快速實現。我們將就最小二乘損失和更一般的凸損失函數，發展成對學習算法的並行實現，以回應分析大規模數據的殷切需求。我們將研究可產生稀疏逼近的基於經驗特徵的成對學習框架。做為我們對成對學習核的分析的一個應用，我們將提供含偏移量的經典正則化最小二乘算法的分析。

15305018.label: Realisation of objectives
15305018.value: In [1], we studied generalized linear models for large-scale grouped and right-censored count data. In the model, observed variables are group indexes (for example, observations 1, 2, and 3 corresponding to the original yet unknown integer sets 0~2, 3~5, and 6+, respectively). This is strongly motivated by many applications in social sciences, where questionnaires are designed to collect category indexes instead of integers, for dependent variables. For both Poisson and zero-inflated Poisson models, we proved the existence, asymptotic consistency, and asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimators of the generalized linear model coefficients. Since grouping and right-censoring destroys the nice algebraic structure of likelihood function of exponential family distributions, MLE is prone to severe numerical stability problems. So, in [1], we designed a hybrid algorithm for line search along two directions. The one direction is specified by the numerical gradient, which is stable yet not efficient; and the other is the direction for Newton iteration, with both gradient and Hessian computed analytically. The latter direction is numerically unstable at the beginning of iterations but becomes stable and provides fast convergence at the late stage when the output vector is close to the maximizer of the likelihood function. Implementation of the algorithm works smoothly for both artificial and real data in [1]. In [2], we designed and analyzed a new reproducing kernel-based boosting regression learning algorithm, called kernel-based re-scaled boosting with truncation (KReBooT). With truncation, KReBooT is more resistant to over-fitting. Applying a recently developed integral operator approach, and a variant of Talagrand's concentration inequality, we proved the state-of-the-art convergence rates of KReBooT among the boosting-type kernel-based learning algorithms. The convergence rates are derived based on the assumptions on the regularity of target function, and the rates of decay of integral operator eigenvalues. In [3], we employed deep-learning-based approach and studied a large-scale data set with 280,000 articles published in six mainstream newspapers in North America. First, we used the hierarchical Dirichlet process model to identify topics, and assign the articles to their corresponding topics. Sentiment scores are predicted for each newspaper article by deep learning (namely, the bidirectional encoder representations from transformers), which was trained on binary-labeled reviews of movies in the Internet Movie Database (IMDb). The scientific findings include, first, sentiments across different topics show distinct trajectories over the period of study, and topics form a much more powerful predictor to explain the variation of sentiments, than other predictors such as publisher, year of publication, and country of publisher. Second, while less positive sentiments are more relevant to material concerns than to ethnic considerations, more positive sentiments are associated with an appreciation of culture. Third, the United States and Canada each displays different temporal patterns of sentiments, even for the same or similar topics. Besides these findings, our research results also call for a paradigm shift for studying the intertwined sociodiscursive interactions with big data, and across a long period of time. In [4], we studied kernel-based online stochastic gradient descent algorithm for the inference of functional linear models. Two settings of step-sizes are discussed. In the first setting, step-sizes are taking as a sequence of decreasing positive numbers, and the iteration moves on as long as new data come. In the second setting, step-sizes are set as a fixed number depending on the fixed sample size. Both of the estimation and the prediction problems are studied, where the estimation problem seeks inference of slope and prediction problem seeks inference of the predicted linear functional. We show that when the reproducing kernel is properly selected, capacity assumptions can compensate for the regularity assumption for the prediction problem. That is, convergence is guaranteed even when the slope function is only square integrable without further regularity assumption. This shows significant difference between prediction and estimation problems. Comprehensive mathematical analysis on the rates of convergence are carried out. The near-equivalent relation among effective dimension assumptions, the assumption on finite trace of fraction power of integral operator, and the rates of integral operator eigenvalue decay, is established. For our Object 1 of the analysis of the kernel-based pairwise learning algorithms, first, in [2] the structure of KReBooT and the convergence analysis include kernel-based pairwise learning as a special case and provide an efficient algorithmic design. In [1] GRC data provide an important model for ranking and pairwise learning, since comparison data is usually given from a finite set (e.g. -3, -2, ..., 3), while GRC Poisson variable (multiplied by a random sign) provides a much finer underground model for pairwise learning, compared against traditional approaches such as ordinal logistic regression. In [4], we obtained the near-equivalent relation among three characterizations of the kernel-based hypothesis space complexity: effective dimension, integral operator eigenvalue decay, and the finite trace assumption of fraction power of the kernel integral operator. For our Object 2 of the analysis of the distributed pairwise learning algorithms, our work [1] provides a sufficient foundation. Based on the proved asymptotic consistency and normality [1], a distributed pairwise learning algorithm could be obtained by divide-and-conquer. That is, MLE estimators are computed locally, and synthesized to the global estimator by weighted (with weights proportional to the sizes of sub-samples) averaging. As elaborated in our recent work (Xin Guo, Ting Hu, and Qiang Wu, Distributed Minimum Error Entropy Algorithms, Journal of Machine Learning Research 2020), kernel-based pairwise learning could be implemented via point-wise learning through a special kernel design which does not narrow down the generality too much.

15305018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305018.value: The research outcome of this project includes four papers on international leading journals (with two under review). In [1], we developed and implemented a new optimization algorithm which resolves the numerical instability problem for generalized linear models with grouped and right-censored count data. We developed the existence, asymptotic consistency, and asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimators of generalized linear model coefficients. In [2], we designed and analyzed a new reproducing kernel-based boosting regression learning algorithm, called kernel-based re-scaled boosting with truncation (KReBooT). KReBooT is designed to control over-fitting by truncation of boosting step-size. We proved the state-of-the-art convergence rates of KReBooT among the boosting-type kernel-based learning algorithms. In [3], we apply hierarchical Dirichlet process model and a deep neural network named bidirectional encoder representations from transformers, to analyze 280,000 articles published in six mainstream newspapers in North America. The scientific findings include the temporal patterns of sentiments across 1978--2019 in different topics, and the insights of using large-scale text data for the research on social science problems. In [4], we studied the performance of online stochastic gradient descent algorithm for functional data analysis. State-of-the-art convergence rates of both expected excess prediction error, and expected estimation error are derived. We compared and obtained near-equivalent relation between our capacity assumption of finite trace of fraction power of kernel integral operator, with the assumption on effective dimension, and the assumption on rates of integral operator eigenvalue decay. Our analysis shows that with properly selected kernel, the prediction problem does not require any regularity assumption on slope. This demonstrates the significant difference between prediction problem and estimation problem of functional linear models.

15305018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305018.value: The PI is working on extending the methodology developed in [1], to general mixture models of count data. This includes learning the mixing density or the mixing distribution. The analysis of online and boosting algorithms we developed in [2] and [4] would be extended to deep-learning-based function data analysis, and deep operator learning problems. The natural language processing problem we studied in [3] is a part of the paradigm shift of social science research. Motivated by this paper, our team is working on further improvement of deep learning-based sentiment classification of long text, and non-English text.

15305018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305018.value: Kernel-based machine learning algorithms are widely applied for the analysis of data with large scales. In this project, we developed the convergence theory of kernel based boosting for regression learning, and kernel-based online algorithm for functional linear model with large-scale data. Grouped and right-censored count data with large scale are widely collected in many branches of social sciences, including criminology, demography, epidemiology, marketing, sociology, psychology, and so forth. Traditional algorithms developed for count data does not work for the grouped and right-censored format. We designed and implemented a hybrid line search for the inference with maximum likelihood algorithm. Mathematical theory on the algorithm performance is established. We also explored the application of deep learning to sentiment analysis of a large-scale newspaper text data set, with many exciting findings which are also of significant social scientific values.

15305518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305518.value: How to incorporate microscopic details (including spatial or temporal or both) into kinetic models describing the individual behaviors of species and then derive the relevant macroscopic limit models is a challenging and important question in the mathematical modeling. The investigation of such question involves complicated modeling ideas and deep analysis. The major finding of this project is to show that when temporal sensing mechanism is included in the kinetic model of chemotaxis, the macroscopic (like parabolic) limit equation will not contain temporal parts but flux-limited effect may arise. The resulting macroscopic models have globally bounded solutions and spatial patterns, which are different from the classical chemotaxis models where solutions may blow up. Therefore such macroscopic chemotaxis models derived from the kinetic models with specific individual details may be more relevant to applications compared to the phenomenological models. In our research results, we have shown that the hyperbolic-parabolic chemotaxis system can be rederived as the macroscopic limits of kinetic models and they may generate possible network patterns interpreting the vasculargenesis.

15305518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305518.value: Using the idea of deriving the macroscopic limits of kinetic chemotaxis models with temporal sensing mechanism in our published works mentioned above, we may further develop some relevant macroscopic chemotaxis models from the microscopic (like kinetic) models and study the properties of their qualitative behaviors to interpret their underlying biological implications.

15305518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305518.value: This research project is mainly focused on the rigorous derivation of macroscopic limit of kinetic (mesoscopic) chemotaxis models with temporal sensing mechanism incorporated in the turning kernel and qualitative analysis of the resulting macroscopic chemotaxis models. The significance of this project we show that temporal variations in the individual species are included in the kinetic models will not be carried over to the related macroscopic limit models due to the bottom-up scalings, but flux-limited effect of chemotaxis will appear instead. These flux-limited chemotaxis models will admit globally bounded solution, and in particular can generate spatial patterns which can be possibly used to interpret some experimental observations like the network formation in the vasculargenesis.

15305718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305718.value: 二維鐵電材料有望在單層晶胞厚度上展現超薄鐵電性，無論對於基礎科學還是器件應用都有重要意義。最近的理論和實驗研究都表明二維硒化銦材料具有室溫鐵電性，使其成爲超薄鐵電器件的熱門選擇。然而目前對硒化銦的二維鉄電性研究仍然在初級階段，尤其是理論和實驗在硒化銦的鐵電相以及其具體原子結構上仍有分歧。由於硒化銦材料裏普遍存在調製和孿晶結構，傳統方法比如X射綫衍射難以準確解出其原子結構。爲了解決這一問題，本項目旨在使用原子分辨率的透射電子顯微鏡深入研究硒化銦的鉄電相原子結構，包括使用≤0.1納米的分辨率直接表徵硒化銦的鐵電極化方向和分佈，進而推出其鐵電性的結構根源。我們還將在透射電鏡中使用原位加熱/冷卻技術，實時研究鐵電轉變的過程機制。本研究有望全面理解硒化銦二維鉄電性，徹底解決目前這一領域的分歧，從而為基於新型二維材料的超薄鐵電器件鋪平道路。

15305718.label: Realisation of objectives
15305718.value: Objective 1: We have fully achieved this objective, by demonstrating experimentally the first discovery of in-plane antiferroelectricity in 2D In2Se3, with no out-of-plane component, using atomic-resolution TEM imaging, polarized light microscopy, as well as PFM. We identified that such antiferroelectriciy manifests as a unique nano-stripe superstructure: the individual nano-stripes exhibit local ferroelectric polarization, whereas the neighboring nano-stripes are antipolar with zero net polarization. It reflects the intriguing competition between 2D ferroelectric and antiferroelectric ordering in In2Se3, which can be preserved down to single-layer thickness. These results have been published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 047601 (2020) with 27 citations already. Objective 2: We have fully achieved this objective, by performing first-principles calculations and quantitatively comparing with TEM-imaged structure. An excellent agreement was obtained between experimental image and theoretical model. The theoretical model further identified the origin of spontaneous polarization as the collective displacement of central-layer Se atoms in each In2Se3 unit cell. The Se displacement is purely in-plane and can generate spontaneous polarization ~23-26 μC/cm2. On the other hand, such spontaneous polarization is modulated by structural instability detected by phonon dispersion of 2D In2Se3, which gives rise to the observed nano-stripe superstructure. These results have also been reported in Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 047601. The derived structure model of 2D In2Se3 from a combination of TEM and first-principles calculations is unprecedented and has been requested by and shared with several researchers in the field. Objective 3: We have fully achieved this objective, by carrying out in situ heating in both TEM and X-ray diffraction (XRD) to explore the phase transformation from non-polar to polar In2Se3. Not only have we identified the transition temperature and the associated latent heat, but also we detected a subtle lattice distortion accompanied with the spontaneous polarization. Such lattice distortion effectively breaks the symmetry, which leads to anisotropic lattice strain and the first experimental demonstration of 2D ferroelasticity. These results have been published in Nature Commun. 12, 3665 (2021) with 18 citations already.

15305718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305718.value: Through accomplishing this project, we have achieved the first experimental discovery of 2D antiferroelectricity in In2Se3, using optical and electron microscopy which is in quantitative agreement with first-principles calculations. The revealed antiferroelectriciy manifests as an unusual nano-stripe superstructure: the individual nano-stripes exhibit local ferroelectric polarization, whereas the neighboring nano-stripes are antipolar with zero net polarization. It is unique in the following aspects: (1) It is in-plane dominated and confined in the single β’-In2Se3 quintuple layer, as opposed to conventional 3D antiferroelectrics such as PbZrO3, and other 2D materials whose antiferroelectric ordering arises from antipolar stacking along the out-of-plane direction. Such 2D confined nature also enables the preservation of antiferroelectricity down to the single-layer thickness. (2) The observed nano-stripe superstructure reflects the unprecedented competition between 2D ferroelectric and antiferroelectric ordering, with the nano-stripe width representing the balance of the competition. It suggests bright prospects for realizing antiferroelectric-ferroelectric phase switching in In2Se3. Even though the nano-stripe superstructure has been observed in In2Se3 since 1975, its structural origin remains unknown for over four decades. Our work resolves the true nature of this intriguing superstructure as 2D antiferroelectricity. In2Se3 is also known as a semiconductor with the bandgap ~0.8 eV and was demonstrated to make phase-switching memory devices. The accurate structure model achieved in our work is essential for better understanding its emerging functionalities as a low-bandgap 2D antiferroelectric material. All above results have been published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 047601 (2020). (C: Research Output No. 1). Furthermore, we have also achieved the first experimental demonstration of 2D ferroelasticity in the fascinating In2Se3 material. Using the cutting-edge electron microscopy consolidated by in situ XRD and optical measurements, we identified quantitatively 2D spontaneous strain originating from in-plane antiferroelectric distortion, in contrast to the conventional 3D ferroelastics. The symmetry-equivalent strain orientations give rise to three domain variants separated by 60° and 120° domain walls (DWs). Mechanical switching between these ferroelastic domains is achieved under ≤0.5% external strain, demonstrating the feasibility to tailor the antiferroelectric polar structure as well as DW patterns through mechanical stimuli. The detailed domain switching mechanism through both DW propagation and domain nucleation is unraveled. In addition, the effects of 3D stacking on such 2D ferroelasticity, such as surface wrinkles and inclined DWs, have also been revealed. These results have been published in Nature Commun. 12, 3665 (2021). (C: Research Output No. 2).

15305718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305718.value: With the demonstrated competition between 2D ferroelectric and antiferroelectric ordering, it suggests bright prospects for realizing antiferroelectric-ferroelectric phase switching in In2Se3. We are currently working on achieving repeatable phase switching in In2Se3, which may lead to an ultrathin phase-switching memory for device applications. Also the coupling between 2D antiferroelectricity and ferroelasticity indicates an effective route to tune polarization in In2Se3 through strain engineering, which we are currently investigating. Furthermore, the identified 2D ferroelasticity should be widely available in 2D materials with anisotropic lattice distortion, including the 1T' transition metal dichalcogenides with Peierls distortion and 2D ferroelectrics such as the SnTe family. Applying our established approaches to explore ferroelastic behaviour in these materials renders tantalizing potential to tune 2D functionalities through strain or DW engineering, with promising application in making ultrathin electromechanical devices.

15305718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305718.value: Today's trend of device miniaturization requires active materials to be smaller or thinner while maintaining their functionalities. However, when the dimension of conventional materials is reduced to the atomic level, surface effects such as broken bonds or surface reconstruction usually dominate and undermine the bulk functionalities, which sets a fundamental limit on the modern device miniaturization. Two-dimensional (2D) materials with the layered structure, on the other hand, do not suffer the surface effects and thus can preserve functionalities from 3D bulk down to single-layer thickness. Exploring emerging functionalities in 2D materials with ultrathin thickness has become an exciting frontier for both fundamental physics and ultrathin device applications. Along this direction, in this project we have successfully demonstrated the first 2D antiferroelectricity and ferroelasticity in ultrathin In2Se3 material. Using cutting-edge microscopy techniques, we have unravelled the in-plane nature of both functionalities that have never been discovered in other materials. It enables the functionalities to be maintained down to single-layer thickness, which enriches 2D physics for fundamental research at reduced dimensionality. Our results also indicate bright prospects for making ultrathin phase-change memories and electromechanical devices based on In2Se3.

15305818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305818.value: The sensitive detection of biomolecules plays a crucial role in early disease diagnosis and pathogen identification. Aptamer-graphene oxide is a promising next-generation assay platform due to its applicability for a wide range of analytes and simplicity. Nucleic acid aptamers, which are short single-stranded DNA or RNA molecules that bind to non-nucleic acid targets (e.g., ions, small molecules, proteins, and cells) with high affinity and specificity, have enabled the development of numerous novel biosensing platforms since mid 1990s. Among them, the coupling of aptamer with graphene oxide (GO; a single layer of carbon atoms containing oxygenated functional groups) has received considerable attention in recent years. The assay involves the use of a fluorophore-labeled aptamer bound to GO (via pi-stacking interaction and hydrogen bonding), by which the fluorescence is quenched (GO is a superior quencher). Upon the addition of the specific target analyte, the fluorophore-labeled aptamer is released from GO (driven by the formation of target-aptamer complex) and thus the fluorescence is restored. Importantly, by adding a nuclease (e.g., DNase I) into the assay mixture, the sensitivity can be improved by two orders of magnitude. The nuclease cleaves the aptamer of the target-aptamer complex, thereby recycling the target for signal amplification. Another vital function of GO is to protect the bound aptamer from nuclease cleavage through steric hindrance. However, the inclusion of nuclease has inherent drawbacks of being expensive and heat-labile, limiting its usage in resource-rich central laboratories. In this proposal, the project team aims at developing a first-of-its-kind nuclease-free target recycling strategy by means of Fenton-like reagents. Our preliminary data demonstrates that Cu(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide can efficiently cleave aptamer in the target-bound state but not in the GO-bound state. We hypothesize that, supported by previous relevant research work, hydroxyl radical generated by Cu(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide is responsible for the aptamer cleavage in the target-bound state and GO serves as an efficient hydroxyl radical scavenger to protect the GO-bound aptamer against cleavage. Efforts will be devoted to investigate the cleavage and protection phenomena/mechanisms, to achieve signal amplification through Cu(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide-mediated target recycling (model targets of adenosine triphosphate, insulin, and Plasmodium falciparum lactate dehydrogenase), to study the performance of some other Fenton-like reagents, and to extend beyond fluorescence readout (colorimetry and electrochemistry). Given the versatility, simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and robustness of the proposed assay platform, we believe that it will become a useful tool for diverse applications (both centralized and point-of-care/on-site testing). 生物分子的靈敏檢測在早期疾病診斷和病原體鑒定中起着至關重要的作用。適體 - 氧化石墨烯由於其廣泛的適用性和簡便性，成為了具有前景的新一代檢測平台。自九十年代中期起，核酸適體作為一種能和其他非核酸靶標（例如，離子，小分子，蛋白質，細胞）高親和性高特異性地結合的短的單鏈DNA或者RNA，已經促成了眾多新型生物傳感器平台的開發。這其中，適體與氧化石墨烯（GO；一種具有含氧官能團的碳原子單層）平台尤為矚目。該平台的檢測採用熒光基團標記的適體。熒光適體通過π-π堆積和氫鍵作用，被吸附在氧化石墨烯表面，發生熒光淬滅（氧化石墨烯是極強的淬滅劑）。加入特定目標分析物後，由於靶標-適體複合物的形成，熒光標記的適體從GO釋放，熒光恢復。若通過將核酸酶（例如，DNase I）添加到測定混合物中，檢測的靈敏度可以提高兩個數量級。酶可以將適體從靶標-適體複合物中剪切，從而循環使用靶標來達到信號擴增的目的。GO的另一個重要功能是通過空間位阻保護結合的適體免受核酸酶切割。然而，核酸酶昂貴不耐熱的固有缺點限制了它只能用在資源豐富的重要實驗室。在此提案中，項目團隊旨在通過類Fenton試劑開發出首個無核酸酶靶標循環平台。我們的初步數據表明，Cu（II）/抗壞血酸/過氧化氫可以在靶結合狀態下有效切割適體，但不能在GO結合狀態下切割適體。在先前的相關研究工作的支持下，我們提出假設，Cu（II）/抗壞血酸/過氧化氫產生的羥基自由基導致了靶結合狀態下的適體裂解，GO作為有效的羥基自由基清除劑可以保護連在其上的適體不被切割。進一步的研究我們將致力於探索切割和保護現象產生的機理，通過Cu（II）/抗壞血酸/過氧化氫對三磷酸腺苷，胰島素和惡性瘧原蟲乳酸脫氫酶作為模型靶標的適體氧化石墨烯平台進行信號擴增，研究其他類芬頓試劑的性能，將熒光讀數擴展至比色法和電化學法。鑒於所提出的分析平台的多功能性，簡單性，成本效益和穩健性，我們相信它將成為各種應用（集中式床旁檢測/戶外檢測）的有用工具。

15305818.label: Realisation of objectives
15305818.value: Objective 1: Experiments were carried out to confirm the protection of aptamer against cleavage by chemical nuclease (redox-active transition metal ion-mediated aptamer cleavage; copper(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide and iron(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide) when bound to graphene oxide (GO), as well as the stability of GO and aptamer targets (insulin, Plasmodium falciparum lactate dehydrogenase, alpha-fetoprotein, and adenosine) in copper(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide and iron(II)/ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide. Objective 2: Target recycling by chemical nuclease in aptamer-GO assay platform was achieved. The results showed a 100-fold improvement in the limit of detection (LoD) as compared with that without target recycling. In fact, we encountered one major technical issue. Some proteins give rise to high nonspecific signal due to the nonspecific displacement of GO-bound aptamer, which is an unanticipated technical challenge that has not been well studied in the literature. Toward practical human sample testing applications (e.g., serum), it is important to confirm the source(s) of the nonspecific displacement and find effective strategy to address the issue. We employed ultracentrifugation (molecular weight cutoff of 3 kDa) to separate serum into 2 portions (small and large molecular weights). It was found that the large molecular weight portion was the source(s) of the nonspecific displacement whereas the small molecular weight portion did not contribute to the nonspecific displacement at all. Since then, we have focused on small-molecule target (i.e., with small-molecule target in serum, the nonspecific displacement issue can be fully addressed by a simple ultracentrifugation step). Instead of adenosine triphosphate in the original proposal, we switched to adenosine because adenosine–aptamer in recently published works had higher specificity than adenosine triphosphate–aptamer. Excellent specificity was achieved with nonspecific interferences of adenosine monophosphate, cytidine triphosphate, and uridine triphosphate. We tried 2 other strategies in an attempt to minimize the nonspecific displacement by serum. The first strategy was GO passivation by poly(ethylene glycol), pyrenebutyric acid, and surfactants (more precisely aptamer-GO treated with these reagents individually). The second strategy was heat treatment of aptamer-GO. Although both strategies could significantly reduce the nonspecific displacement/signal (negative sample), target spiked in serum (positive sample) could not be distinguished from the negative sample. Objective 3: We optimized the chemical nuclease formulation. The highest target recycling efficiency was achieved with 0.1 mM iron(II), 25 µM ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (chelator), and 1 M hydrogen peroxide. It was found that ascorbic acid had negative effect on the target recycling efficiency. Objective 4: Gold nanoparticles supported on graphene (AuNPs/graphene) was synthesized. Results showed that a positive sample (with aptamer-bound AuNPs/graphene, chemical nuclease, and adenosine) appeared blue in color upon the addition of 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine and hydrogen peroxide whereas a negative sample (with aptamer-bound AuNPs/graphene and chemical nuclease; i.e., absence of adenosine) appeared colorless.

15305818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305818.value: DNA-based aptamers are synthetic single-stranded oligonucleotides that can bind to various target analytes with high affinity and specificity. The use of aptamers as recognition probes has offered new avenues for the detection of small molecule biomarkers. Fluorophore-labelled aptamer coupled with graphene oxide (GO) has provided a quantitative fluorescence-based assay platform. Nevertheless, a sensitive, simple, general, and cost-effective aptamer/GO fluorescence assay for small molecules is required. In this project, adenosine (a signaling metabolite) was used as a model biomarker. The key focus is to design an adenosine aptamer/GO fluorescence assay to detect adenosine in human serum. With direct detection of adenosine in serum, the specific signal could not be distinguished from the background serum signal. This was due to the severe nonspecific aptamer probe desorption from GO by the interference molecules (such as proteins) in serum. A 3,000 Da ultrafiltration centrifugal device was then used to fractionate human serum specimens based on their molecular weights. By doing so, the issue of the undesirable false-positive signal was resolved and selective adenosine detection in ultrafiltered serum was achieved. Apart from the assay specificity improvement, the sensitivity enhancement is another important aspect of detection. Fenton reagents, comprising ferrous iron, ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, and hydrogen peroxide were added to the assay. A mixture of these chemicals generated hydroxyl radicals that triggered the target recycling signal amplification. The limit of detection in buffer and ultrafiltered serum was enhanced by a factor of 100 and 9, respectively. In conclusion, the “protein-free” reagent assay (i.e., no antibodies and nucleases involved) developed herein can be an alternative to conventional protein-based biosensing methods.

15305818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305818.value: Further development of this project includes: • The physisorption and desorption of fluorophore-labeled aptamer on GO surface present a simple biosensing platform. The effects of GO surface properties (such as surface charges, hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions, and temperature) on the adsorption and desorption of aptamer should be investigated. Since commercially available GO was utilized in this study, synthesizing custom GO and modifying its surface properties would yield better insights into aptamer/GO sensing mechanism as well as the nonspecific displacement of aptamer by serum. • Further investigation to figure out the exact large molecules in serum (larger than 3,000 Da) responsible for the nonspecific displacement of aptamer from GO. • Apart from GO, future study should include other 2D materials such as molybdenum disulfide and tungsten disulfide. These materials exhibit a single-layer nonaromatic surface, allowing for interaction with aptamers through van der Waals forces. It is intriguing to compare the assay sensitivity and specificity of these materials with GO. • Apart from adenosine, the developed new assay platform should be applied to a wider spectrum of small-molecule targets.

15305818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305818.value: Fluorescent bioassays using aptamer–graphene oxide (GO) adsorption/desorption coupled with target recycling signal amplification have been developed for detecting various targets. Nucleases are commonly used to amplify signals by cleaving desorbed aptamers and recycling the target for additional aptamer binding. However, nucleases have limitations of low-temperature storage and high cost. To address these challenges, we developed a new target recycling signal amplification method driven by hydroxyl radicals (•OH). This enzyme-free assay uses Fenton reagents (FR) to generate •OH for signal amplification, enabling sensitive and specific adenosine detection. The process involves quenching the fluorescence of adsorbed fluorophore-labeled adenosine aptamers with GO. The signal is then restored by adding adenosine and the FR mixture, comprising iron(II) sulfate, EDTA, and hydrogen peroxide. The •OH generated by the FR cleaved the adenosine aptamer within the aptamer–adenosine hybrid, releasing adenosine to bind more adsorbed aptamers, and therefore amplifying the signal. This fluorescent amplification assay achieved a 100-fold sensitivity improvement in the limit of detection from 0.5 mM to 0.005 mM in buffer solution. When tested in ultrafiltered human serum, a 9-fold enhancement in the limit of detection from 0.8 mM to 0.09 mM was exhibited.

15306218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15306218.value: Various hard magnetic bimetallic alloy nanoparticles (NPs) can be prepared from single-source heterobimetallic molecular and polymeric precursors. A series of bimetallic phase-separated block copolymers (BCPs) was synthesized by incorporating a complex containing Fe and Pt centers into the coordinating block of different poly(styrene-b-4-vinylpyridine)s. The bulk and thin-film self-assembly of these BCPs was studied. The products from the pyrolysis of the BCPs in bulk indicated that the FePt NPs exist in the face-centred tetragonal phase with average particle sizes of ca. 4−8 nm within a carbonaceous matrix. The use of a nanostructured BCP approach is important for the synthesis of ferromagnetic FePt NPs with a smaller average NP size and a ~1:1 Fe/Pt stoichiometric ratio (paper 1). A new FePt-containing polymer with amphiphilic (paper 4) ligand design can be used as the single-source precursor to prepare FePt NPs with very high crystallinity. The polyethylene glycol (PEG) tails could act as the protective layer during pyrolysis, which would make the resultant NPs disperse more evenly in the carbon matrix and the size can be controlled by tuning the length of the PEG tails. Those highly crystalline FePt NPs can be used as electrocatalysts to catalyze oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) with much better performance than commercial Pt/C, and showed high stability after 10,000 cycles (paper 3). Efforts were made to develop new synthetic routes to various Pt(II) precursors (papers 5-6, 8-9). Self-assembly driven by external electric field represents a highly efficient strategy to regulate the supramolecular nanostructures of some square-planar Pt complexes (paper 2). We also describe the use of high-throughput nanoimprint lithography (NIL) to direct the self-assembly of the bimetallic FePt and FePd complexes. More importantly, when top-down NIL is coupled with the bottom-up self-assembly of the organometallic building blocks, regular arrays of nanorods can be accessed and the patterns can be controlled by changing the lithographic stamp. The resulting arrays of ferromagnetic FeM alloy nanorods suggest promising potential for the scalable production of ordered magnetic arrays and fabrication of magnetic bit-patterned media (paper 7). A new bimetallic complex containing a 4'-ferrocenyl-(2,2':6',2'' terpyridine)palladium core with PEG-based pyridine is applied in seeded-growth self-assembled supramolecular polymerization, which affords nanoribbons with controllable lengths and the process follows a first-order reaction kinetics. This approach is demonstrated for a bimetallic organic complex for the first time (paper 10). We were also invited to contribute a chapter in "Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV" on conjugated poly(metalla-ynes) (paper 11).

15306218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15306218.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future. (i) Extension of the approaches to other metal and ligand systems. (ii) Improvement of the areal density of the bit-patterned media based on the magnetic NP nanopatterns. (iii) Enhancement of the electrocatalytic activities of the metal alloy nanoparticles in energy conversion applications.

15306218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15306218.value: Some hard magnetic bimetallic alloy nanoparticles can be conveniently prepared via one-step pyrolysis of a single-source molecular precursor. The use of a bimetallic block copolymer (BCP) to ferromagnetic FePt NPs has been studied. The use of a phase-separated BCP can give rise to a smaller average NP size and a nearly 1:1 Fe:Pt ratio. Metallo-BCP lithography is proved to be a coalescence-free approach to convert a single bimetallic source into FePt NPs without the need of surfactants of weak binding strength or a complicated addition sequence of monometallic salts. The organic skeletons could protect the NPs from sintering during pyrolysis, and H2 gas is useful to avoid the possible oxidation and reduce part of the carbon. The use of electric field is also a reliable method to help construct nanostructures in charged self-assembling systems. When the top-down lithography is coupled with the bottom-up molecular self-assembly, the self-assembly of heterobimetallic complexes can be precisely controlled to prepare ordered patterns of assemblies with high throughput. A bimetallic FePd complex with polyethylene glycol-based pyridine is also applied in the seeded-growth self-assembled polymerization, which affords nanoribbons with a controllable dimension. The resultant FePt NPs can find useful applications in magnetic data recording and electrocatalysis.
