15504918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504918.value: Customer demands depend on prices but also on other characteristics of goods and services. In the case of public transport such as bus, train, and ferry services, passengers care about (ticket) prices and also about waiting times. Both prices as well as waiting times can be controlled by carriers. More specifically, waiting times are controlled by schedules and the implied headways, where headways describe the time distance between vehicle departures. The proposed project concentrates on two dimensions in which schedules can differ: information strategies and headway choices. In the case of fully reliable schedules, vehicles depart exactly at pre-determined, “advertised” departure times. For instance, every 30 minutes starting at 8 am until 8 pm. The implementation of a fully reliable schedule can be costly because it may involve more complex planning procedures and buffer capacity which reduces overall vehicle utilization. The implementation of an unreliable schedule, which we describe as a “hidden” schedule, could therefore help to reduce costs and increase vehicle utilization. In our case, hidden schedules leave passengers uninformed about exact departure times, while they are informed about average waiting times. The aim is to identify and analyze fundamental properties of passenger arrival processes (passenger demands) that determine optimal information, headway, and pricing strategies. The mathematical model involves strategic passengers in the sense that they decide whether “to wait or not to wait” depending on the sum of the price and waiting time costs, where this sum is called the “generalized price of traveling.” A crucial feature of the proposed model is that it uses general functional forms to describe the relationship between passenger demands and the generalized price of traveling. This feature allows us to study optimal information, headway, and pricing decisions depending on whether passengers with long or short waiting times are more sensitive with respect to waiting time changes. Other parts of the proposed study cover passenger types that differ in terms of time valuations and the price elasticity of their demands, endogenous passenger arrival times to the station, and generalized prices that are non-linear functions of passenger waiting times. 客户需求取决于价格，也取决于商品和服务的其他特征。在公共交通工具如公共汽车，火车和渡轮服务的情况下，乘客关心（票）价格以及等待时间。价格和等待时间都可以由运营商控制。具体地说，等待时间由时间表和隐含的交通工具的到达时距控制，其中到达时距描述了相邻车辆离开之间的时间跨度。 拟议的项目集中在两个方面，其中时间表可以有所不同：进度选择和进度可靠性。在完全可靠的时间表的情况下，车辆准确地在预定的，固定的时间离开。例如，从早上8点到晚上8点每30分钟一班。实施完全可靠的时间表可能成本很高，因为它可能涉及更复杂的规划程序和缓冲能力，从而降低整体车辆利用率。因此，实施不可靠的时间表（我们称之为“随机化”）可以帮助降低成本并提高车辆利用率。在我们的案例中，随机化涉及对随机车辆离开时间和表示预期交通工具的到达时距的平均交通工具的到达时距的公告，并确定预期的乘客等待时间。 目的是确定和分析确定最优定价，进度和进度随机化策略的乘客到达过程（乘客需求）的基本属性。数学模型涉及战略乘客，他们决定“等待还是不等待”取决于价格和等待时间成本的总和，其中这个总和被称为“旅行的广义价格”。所提出的模型是它使用一般函数形式来描述（预期）乘客需求与旅行广义价格之间的关系。这一特征使我们能够研究（i）定价随机化如何影响定价和交通工具的到达时距决策，（ii）随机化的好处如何取决于乘客需求功能的特性，特别是在需求曲率方面，以及（iii）在什么条件下某些需求属性可能会出现。拟议研究的其他部分包括乘客类型，这些乘客类型在时间估值和需求的价格弹性方面，内生到达时间以及最小化长度偏差的随机结构方面不同。

15504918.label: Realisation of objectives
15504918.value: Objective 1: A stylized transport market with a monopoly company that charges a uniform price to its passengers is considered. The transportation service involves a trip from one origin station to one destination station. The demand-rate functions are time-homogenous and decreasing in waiting times. If the waiting time information is advertised, demand rates are therefore high or low depending on whether passengers arrive shortly before or shortly after vehicle departures, respectively. If the exact waiting time information is hidden, passengers' expected waiting times are independent of the passengers' arrival times at the station because vehicle inter-departure times (headways) are assumed to be constant in time, which leads to constant demand rates. General functional forms, specific functional forms in which one specific parameter controls for the curvature of the demand-rate function, and time-homogenous demand-rate functions are used to clearly identify the role of curvatures for information, pricing and headway strategies by abstracting away from shifts in the demand-rate function. Objective 2: We find that that both the profit- and welfare-maximizing choices of information strategies in terms of hiding or advertising waiting time information rely on the curvature of the (time-homogenous) demand-rate function. The discussion of curvatures is meaningful because they help to distinguish two types of passengers who differ in their valuation of small changes in (expected) waiting depending on whether the (expected) waiting time is short or long. One type involves passengers who do not care much about a small change in (expected) waiting time if the (expected) waiting time is short but care much about a small change in (expected) waiting time if the (expected) waiting time is long. This type is captured by the consideration of concave demand-rate functions. The other type involves passengers who care much about a small change in (expected) waiting time if the (expected) waiting time is short but do not care much about a small change in (expected) waiting time if the (expected) waiting time is long. This type is captured by the consideration of convex demand-rate functions. In reality, one type of passengers could be dominating in some markets whereas the other type of passengers could be dominating in other markets. None of these two scenarios can be ruled out a priory. For the profit maximization case, it is shown that, if the demand-rate function is concave, hiding is the profit-maximizing information strategy, whereas advertising is the profit-maximizing information strategy if the demand-rate function is convex. This conclusion holds, independent of whether prices and headways are exogenously given or any of them is endogenously determined by the carrier. Concave demand rates favor the use of hidden schedules because they increase passenger demand per ride when passengers with long waiting times are more sensitive with respect to waiting time changes than those with short waiting times. This is because expected waiting times in the case of hidden schedules are lower than actual waiting times for passengers with long waiting times. Convex demand rates favor the use of advertised schedules because they increase passenger demand per ride when passengers with short waiting times are more sensitive with respect to waiting time changes than those with long waiting times. This is because actual waiting times in the case of advertised schedules are lower than expected waiting times for passengers with short waiting times. The comparison result of the two information scenarios under welfare maximization, where welfare is determined by the sum of the carrier's profit and consumer surplus, is more complicated. It is shown that the demand-rate function must be sufficiently concave to ensure that welfare can be higher with hidden relative to advertised schedules, where the level of concavity is measured by the waiting time elasticity of the slope of the demand-rate function (simply called slope elasticity). While consumers prefer advertised schedules, the possibly positive effect of hidden schedules on welfare can be explained by the fact that it can boost demand per ride and welfare when demand rates are strictly concave and prices exceed marginal costs and, thus, are excessive from the welfare viewpoint. When the demand-rate function is concave but not sufficiently concave (that is, the slope elasticity is given by an intermediate range), the profit-maximizing strategy is to hide schedules and the welfare-maximizing strategy is to advertise schedules. Therefore, profit maximization can lead to an excessive use of hidden schedules. This indicates a potential discrepancy between profit- and welfare-maximizing choices of information strategies. Numerical examples indicate the crucial role of demand rate curvatures for the profit-maximizing headway and price choices and that information strategies can be used to save transport costs by increasing headway lengths. Objective 3: Capturing the non-linear and, more specifically, convex relationship between the full price (called “generalized price of travelling” in the proposal), which is the sum of the fare and the waiting time costs, had been of crucial importance. The convexity captures the trade-off between travel time and the time spent at, for example, home and work and that the inconvenience of the absence from home and work places increases in travel time including waiting time. We show, amongs other results, that the slope elasticity of the demand-rate function, which is a measure for its curvature, can be written as the weighted sum of the waiting time cost function's slope elasticity and the slope elasticity of the demand-rate function in the full price.

15504918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504918.value: This project has led to six papers. Four are already published in Journal of Transport Economics and Policy, Economics of Transportation, Transportation Research Part E, and Journal of Air Transport Management. One paper has been submitted to Research in Transportation Economics. Minor revisions are required for acceptance according to the corresponding editor. One PhD student (Zhang, H.) is the first author of this study. Another paper has been submitted to Transportation Research Part B. Major revisions are required for according to the corresponding editor. In addition, the paper has led to 1 PhD thesis (Lang, H., 2021) and 1 presentation. The limited number of presentations is due to the travel restrictions associated with the Covid-19 pandemic. The corresponding studies involve theoretical and empirical contributions. These contributions are related to the strategic use of information strategies and their role for prices and service quality in terms of waiting times (Czerny, Guo and Hassin, under review: major revisions). They are further related to other transport problems involving congestion management (Lang and Czerny, 2021), resilient airline schedules (Brueckner, Czerny and Gaggero, 2x2021), airline mergers (Czerny, Jost, Lang, and Mantin, 2021), and airline networks and competition (Zhang (PhD student), Czerny, Grimme, and Niemeier; under review: minor revisions).

15504918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504918.value: The study by Czerny, Guo and Hassin (under review) assumes deterministic vehicle ride times. A natural extension would be to consider stochastic vehicle ride times. If ride times are randomly drawn, this increases the expected waiting time of a random passenger relative to a scenario in which vehicle ride times are deterministic. Analyzing the role of random ride times for information strategies, prices and service quality in terms of service frequencies would be a natural and worthwhile avenue for future research. Based on the studies by Brueckner, Czerny, and Gaggero (2x2021), another study considering the measuring and determinants of airline delay propagation has recently been published in Transportation Research Part B. Further studies on related topics considering airline schedule management by integrating stochasticity in aircraft ground and flight times is currently in progress. The study by Zhang, Czerny, Grimme, and Niemeier (under review) concentrates on the airline networks of low-cost carriers. Extending this study so that the analysis captures not only the networks and competition among low-cost carriers but also those among full-service carriers and between low-cost and full-service carriers is currently in progress.

15504918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504918.value: Apps which allow customers to check waiting times in real time on their smartphones are popular across many industries. Waiting time information is good or bad news for customers depending on whether they get to know that they have to wait short or long times, respectively. The main objective of the proposed study was to analyze the strategic choice of information strategies in the context of transport where waiting times are determined by headways which are given by the time difference between vehicle departures and the sum of the price and waiting time costs represent the full price of traveling which vary among passengers depending on arrival times at the station. Passengers respond to variations in the full price by adjusting their demand rates. Two types of information strategies are considered. The company can advertise the exact schedule or advertise only the average lengths of inter-departure times (headways). The analysis shows that the curvature of the demand-rate function in the waiting time is crucial for the choice of information strategies, prices and headways in both the case of profit-maximizing companies and the case of welfare-maximizing companies where welfare is calculated by the sum of profit and consumer surplus.

15505218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505218.value: This paper studies the capital market effects of news articles that cite anonymous sources. A growing literature has documented how the media affect stock prices, corporate governance and capital allocation. Most prior papers have not explored one of the media’s most unique features relative to the other information intermediaries—naming sources. About one third of newspaper articles quote anonymous sources (Culbertson, 1978) and 80% of national and international stories in Time and Newsweek use anonymous sources (Wulfemeyer, 1985). The importance of studying the sources of news articles is that the sources automatically solve a key question in research on the media—who initiates the news, firms or the media? Producing or discovering private information is a central theme in capital market research. Many market participants can possess private information and help impound the information into stock prices either through trading activities or broadcasting the information that spurs others to trade on it. Corporate insiders, short-sellers, syndicated loan participants or sophisticated traders are more likely to trade on their private information quietly, whereas other players such as analysts, activist short-sellers (e.g. Muddy Waters, see Zhao, 2017) and the media publicize private information. Most studies on the effects of private information rely on the patterns of stock price variations to infer that private information is being produced. This study explores a unique feature of the media and proposes a new approach to directly and clearly identify private information—the use of anonymous sources. Unlike other information intermediaries, citing the sources of information is a standard industry practice for the media. News stories citing anonymous sources reliable enough to pass the editorial process reveal information that is not previously public. Exploiting the sources makes it possible to single out new information that presumably matters more for the capital market, holding information dissemination constant. This new approach also enables us to identify the media’s information discovery on a variety of topics that are of interest to investors. This study aims to explicitly address how investigative journalism and “scoops” affect the capital market. I expect to document more significant stock price adjustments and trading activities in response to news reports citing anonymous sources than news reports without such sources. I also expect to find reduced information asymmetry and speedier stock price discovery when the media use anonymous sources more on reporting a certain firm, above and beyond the effects of general media coverage. 本論文研究媒體使用匿名消息來源對資本市場的影響。已有的文獻研究過媒體對股票價格，公司治理和資本配置的影響，但是沒有研究過媒體相對於其他市場中介的獨到特點—指出信息來源。三分之壹的報紙文章使用匿名來源，時代周刊和商業周刊百分之八十的文章使用匿名來源。研究媒體的信息來源可以解決媒體研究的壹個重要問題—誰制造了新聞，公司還是媒體？ 制造還是挖掘私有信息是資本市場研究的中心課題。很多市場參與者擁有私有信息並幫助信息融入股票價格，通過自己的交易或者傳播信息供他人交易。公司內部人，空頭，聯合貸款參與者或者成熟交易者傾向於默默交易，而其他資產市場參與者比如分析師，積極空頭和媒體則公布傳播私有信息。 大部分研究私有信息的文章依賴股價變動的規律來推測私有信息被交易。本文提出壹種直接、清楚地確認私有信息的方式—文章的匿名來源。與其他信息中介不同，指出信息來源是媒體的行業習慣。文章使用匿名來源說明信息是以前沒有公開過的，而且匿名來源的可信度通過了審稿標準。通過有匿名來源的文章，我們可以挖掘出對市場更為重要的全新信息，假設信息傳播程度等同。這個方法還可以讓我們研究股價對壹系列話題的信息發現。 本論文旨在研究調查性新聞報道對資本市場的影響。我預期股價波動和股票交易量在有匿名消息的文章發表之後變動更顯著。相對媒體報道對市場的壹般影響，媒體積極使用匿名消息報道公司會降低信息不對稱，加速股價發掘速度。

15505318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505318.value: Nowadays, with the development of advanced information and mobile technology, there is rapid growth in on-demand service platforms that match customers with specific service needs with self-employed independent agents. Both the customers and independent agents are generally heterogeneous and exhibit different preferences. The services provided by independent agents often exhibit different quality levels; that is, the services are vertically differentiated (e.g., UberX vs UberBlack). In addition, when matching customers with independent agents, the platforms sometimes upgrade the service for free when there is a mismatch of supply and demand. How do these factors interact with each other and affect the performance of the on-demand service? This is the research question we plan to investigate in this proposal. Specifically, we are going to investigate how user heterogeneity and service differentiation affect the design of the service and operational policy of the on-demand platforms. First, we plan to consider a vertical differentiation setting in which the platforms offer both regular- and high-type services. We then derive the customers’ joining (or service selection) decisions, the agents’ participation incentives and the platform’s pricing and wage decisions under four scenarios, depending on whether a platform operates the two services dedicatedly or jointly (with free-service upgrades) and whether the platform adopts a fixed commission pricing or not. A comparison of the equilibrium outcomes under the above four scenarios can help us answer the following questions: What is the effect of service dedication on the performance of the on-demand service? Under which conditions is fixed commission pricing optimal? How does the free service upgrade affect customers’ strategic service selection decisions, agents’ participation incentives, the platform’s pricing and wage decisions and the performance of the on-demand service? Under what conditions will the platform operate its services in a dedicated manner? What is the effect on customer surplus, agents’ welfare and platform profitability if the platform manages its on-demand services dedicatedly instead of jointly? We then analyze a horizontal differentiation setting in which the customers and agents exhibit gender preferences toward each other. For example, female customers might prefer cars with female drivers. A platform, when designing its services, can either ignore this type preference or group agents into their specific types. Again, we examine the equilibrium decisions of the three parties, the customers, the agents and the on-demand platform, to investigate under which conditions the platform will operate the service according to the users’ type preferences. 近来，随着先进信息和移动技术的发展，把有特定服务需求的顾客与自雇独立代理商相匹配的按需服务平台快速增长。顾客和自雇独立代理商通常都是异质的并且表现出不同的偏好。独立代理商提供的服务往往有不同的质量水平;也就是说，服务是可垂直区分的。此外，当对顾客和独立代理商进行匹配时，如果出现供需不平衡， 平台有时会进行免费升级服务。这些因素如何相互影响并影响按需服务平台的表现？这是我们计划进行研究的问题。 具体而言，我们将研究用户异质性和服务差异化如何影响按需服务平台的服务和运营策略的设计。首先，我们考虑平台的垂直差异化设置。平台可以提供常规服务以及高质量类型服务。然后，根据平台是否采用固定佣金定价 和平台是分别专门地还是同时一起地（通过免费服务升级）提供这两项服务，我们考虑四种情况，推导相关顾客的加入（或服务选择）决策，代理商的参与提供服务决策以及平台的定价和工资决策。对四种情况的均衡结果进行比较可以帮助我们回答以下问题：专门化服务如何影响按需服务平台的表现？在哪些条件下固定佣金定价最优？免费服务升级如何影响战略顾客的服务选择决策，代理商的参与决策，按需服务平台的定价和工资决策以及平台的绩效？平台会在什么条件下提供专门化服务？如果平台对其服务进行专门化管理而不是联合管理，这会如何影响消费者剩余，代理商福利和平台的盈利水平？其次，我们考虑水平差异化, 如顾客和代理商之间展现出性别偏好。平台在设计其服务时， 可以忽略此类偏好，也可以把用户按其偏好进行分组。我们会重新推导顾客，代理商和平台的均衡决策， 然后找出平台会在哪些条件下根据用户的类型偏好运营其服务。

15505318.label: Realisation of objectives
15505318.value: All the objectives have been achieved. This research project focuses on the customer’ heterogeneity and the platform firms’ operational/service decisions. We aim to examine how customers’ heterogeneous preferences affect the firms’ pricing decisions and service provision and the operational system design. We have considered an on-demand ride-hailing platform in which riders are price- and waiting-time-sensitive and drivers are wage-sensitive. The riders and drivers exhibit heterogeneous gender-based safety concerns. Some female users exhibit safety concerns when matched with male counterparts and incur a mismatch cost. We then construct a two-stage queueing game model to analyze the performance of the following two systems: 1) a pooling system that matches riders and drivers without considering gender, where the platform adopts a gender-neutral policy for its pricing and wage decisions; and 2) a hybrid system consisting of two gender-specific driver subsystems – a male-driver subsystem and a female-driver subsystem, where the platform adopts a subsystem-based pricing and wage policy for its pricing and wage decisions. In the hybrid system, male riders can join the male-driver subsystem only; however, each female rider has the option to choose between two subsystems. For each system, we derive the corresponding equilibrium joining and participating behavior of riders and drivers, respectively and the platform’s optimal pricing and wage decisions. For the pooling system, we show that reducing the mismatch cost for those safety-concerned female users has an increasing marginal effect on the platform’s profit. This result implies that it is beneficial for the ride-hailing platform to develop initiatives for reducing the mis-match cost and safety concern. Also, we obtain two seemingly interesting results. First, in the pooling system, we show that reducing the mismatch cost for female drivers does not necessarily lead to more female riders joining the pooling system because of the pricing decision of the platform. Second, in the hybrid system, female riders do not necessarily pay a higher price when they opt for female drivers instead of male drivers. When the mismatch cost of safety-concerned female riders is either sufficiently high or sufficiently low, we show that female riders will end up paying less when they opt for female drivers. We compare the equilibrium outcomes associated with the pooling and the hybrid systems by focusing on three issues: (1) accessibility of safety-concerned female users, (2) other users’ utility, and (3) platform profit. Our comparisons yield the following results. First, relative to the pooling system, the hybrid system reduces the mismatch cost incurred by safety-concerned female users and increases their accessibility. Second, while the hybrid system suffers from a slight loss of the pooling effect, the hybrid system renders a higher profit than the pooling system when the mismatch cost of safety-concerned female users is sufficiently high. Third, from the perspective of those safety-unconcerned users, i.e., all male and safety-unconcerned female users, their utility may deteriorate slightly when the platform switches from the pooling system to the hybrid system. These findings imply that the hybrid system benefits safety-concerned female users and the platform. We also illustrate how our analytical results are congruent with different ride-hailing systems adopted in different countries by considering different mismatch costs that female users incur in different countries. We further consider a shared micromobility system in which the platform micromoboility operator needs to properly determine a total number of vehicles and allocate them to each service region to satisfy demand and generate profitability. Riders in the shared micromobility system can pick up and drop off vehicles in any service region at any time. Such convenience often leads to a severe imbalance between the vehicle supply and demand in different regions. We consider that micromobility platform operators can crowdsource individual riders (who is willing to conduct relocation task because the relocation trips may be close to the riders' original travel routes or they may simply use this opportunity to exercise) to relocate vehicles, besides relying on the third-party logistics provider (3PL). That is, some riders conduct the ride for satisfying their own demands while other riders conduct the ride for helping the operator. We then formulate the operator’s integrated vehicle allocation and relocation problem as a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program on a time-space network. We show that introducing rider crowdsourcing in addition to the 3PL can significantly increase profit, reduce demand loss, and improve the vehicle utilization rate of the system without affecting the existing commitment with the 3PL. The 3PL is more efficient in mass relocation than rider crowdsourcing, whereas the latter is more efficient in handling sporadic relocation needs. Furthermore, rider crowdsourcing relocates more vehicles under a unimodal customer arrival pattern than a bimodal pattern, whereas the reverse holds for the 3PL. We also notice that customers have different price and time sensitivities. Some customers are price-sensitive but time-insensitive. They are willing to purchase the service early for a cheaper rate. The other customers are time-sensitive but price-insensitive. They generally purchase late because of tight schedules and are willing to pay a high fare. Motivated by such customer heterogeneity, firms such as airline companies have adopted the early-bird booking discounts to motivate the price-sensitive customers to purchase early. To maximize the firm revenue, the company needs to appropriately allocate its capacity between the two types of customers, for which demand learning is essential. We consider that the company learns about the demands for both early-bird-discount and regular-price service/product and the buy-up substitution probability. We then construct the Bayesian updating mechanism for learning about demand parameters and substitution probability. We show that when the buy-up substitution probability is known, one may stock less, as one can infer some information about the primary demand for the discounted product from the customer substitution behavior. We also find that to learn about the unknown buy-up substitution probability drives the company to stock less so as to induce more substitution trials. Last, we consider that the service provider offers two kinds of service options: a regular service and a priority service. Customers are delay-sensitive and queues are unobservable. Customers make their joining decisions by choosing from the following three options: balking, joining the regular queue or joining the priority queue with an additional fee. We then characterize the equilibrium customer joining behavior for the two services, and the system performance. Based on the findings in this research project, we have completed four academic papers which are listed as follows: Y. Tang, P. Guo, C. Tang, and Y. Wang. 15505318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505318.value: The PI has trained one PhD student, and the research results have been presented at four conferences and several universities. Our main findings are as follows: Female user safety has become a serious concern for on-demand ride-hailing platforms. We show that when safety-concerned female users’ mismatch cost is above a certain level, switching from a gender-neutral pooling system to a hybrid system with a “female-only” option can result in a win-win outcome for safety-concerned female users and the platform. However, male and safety-unconcerned female users might be worse off due to this change in the system configuration. Unexpectedly, in the pooling system, reducing the mismatch cost associated with safety-concerned female drivers may not lead to more female riders joining the pooling system, even though it boosts the platform’s profit in general. Related results are published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 1. When riders are incentivized to help the platform micromobility operator to relocate vehicles, we show that introducing rider crowdsourcing can significantly increase profit, reduce demand loss, and improve the vehicle utilization rate of the system without affecting any existing commitment with the 3PL. To serve a region, the 3PL often relocates vehicles in batches from faraway, low-demand regions around peak hours of a day, whereas rider crowdsourcing relocates a few vehicles each time from neighboring regions throughout the day. Related results are published on Manufacturing & Service Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 2. To achieve market segmentation between early-bird price-sensitive customers and regular time-sensitive customers, an advanced purchase deadline is usually set, and the discount fare is available only before such a deadline by service providers such as airline companies. Learning about these two types of customers’ demands and their substitution rate can help the service provider better allocate its capacity to maximize revenue. We develop a dynamic inventory management model with Bayesian learning about both demand parameters and substitution probability and provide a SoftMax algorithm to solve the problem. Related results are published on Manufacturing & Service Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 3. The service provider sometimes offers both regular service and priority service with an additional fee. Queues of online service providers are often unobservable. We characterize customers’ optimal joining decision for such a setting, which helps the firm to learn the customer joining rate. Related results are published on Operations Research Letters; See Part C (8) Item 4.

15505318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505318.value: There are some related research topics that are worth exploring. For example, conducting some empirical analysis to verify our analytical results could be an interesting direction for further study. Also, we notice that on-demand platforms have started conducting the A/B testing to understand customer behaviors to identify better operational and service designs. We would like to explore the possibility of collaborating with some on-demand platforms to conduct the A/B testing to validate our results.

15505318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505318.value: We show that when on-demand ride hailing platforms adopt a pooling system that matches users regardless of their gender, reducing the mismatch cost for those safety-concerned female users has an increasing marginal effect on the platform’s profit. It is beneficial for the ride-hailing platform to develop initiatives for reducing the mis-match cost and safety concern. We find that when the platform offers dedicated male-driver- and female-driver-subsystems, female riders do not necessarily pay a higher price when they opt for female drivers instead of male drivers. Offering such dedicated services increases both the accessibility of safety-concerned female users and the platform profit, and it can benefit male and safety-unconcerned female users as well. We also show that platform micromobility operators can adopt the rider crowdsourcing to handle sporadic relocation needs. Introducing rider crowdsourcing to the micromobility system can significantly increase profit, reduce demand loss, and improve the vehicle utilization rate of the system. We find that when customers’ demand distribution and substitution probability are unknown, stocking less to induce more substitution trial can help service providers to better infer demand information.

15505518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505518.value: 許多研究表明，較小的股票，價值股票，更賺錢的公司和投資更保守的公司往往會獲得更高的平均股票回報率。有兩個主要的解釋。 Fama和French（FF，1993; 2015）認為，這些特徵的回報可預測性是因為這些特徵是系統風險的代表。根據這一風險論點，並以剩餘收益模型為動力，Fama和French（2015）通過在FF（1993）三因子模型（市場，規模，和市賬率）中增加兩個額外因素（投資和盈利能力）來提出五因子模型。在q-theory的基礎上，Hou，Xue和Zhang（HXZ，2015）提出了一個由市場，規模，盈利能力和投資因素組成的q因子模型。 另一種解釋將特徵與回報之間的關係歸因於投資者的行為偏差。根據這一論點，Daniel和Titman（DT，1997）反駁並提出了一種特徵模型，即規模和價值特徵的回報可預測性不是來自協方差，而是來自這些特徵本身。然而，關於特徵與協方差辯論的證據仍然處於FF三因子模型的階段，特別是價值或賬面對市值效應，結果證據錯雜。此外，在一系列研究中，FF發現，美國的賬面對市值因子是FF五因子模型中的一個冗餘因素。 雖然FF五因子模型和q因子模型在捕獲平均收益方面表現相當不錯並且優於FF三因子模型，但它們無法解釋某些特定股票組的一些異常或極端回報。由於特徵和因子載荷高度相關，兩種模型的強解釋力是否來自協方差或與投資和盈利能力相關的特徵仍然是未知的和未開發的。 為填補這一空白，本研究提案檢驗協方差與特徵的爭論，重點關注投資和盈利因子。我們遵循DT（1997）建議的方法來進行協方差與特徵的測試。我們首先研究美國市場。然後，由於數據的可用性，我們擴展到全球市場，重點關注由FF（2017）研究的四個地區（北美，歐洲，日本和亞太地區）。 本研究項目將提供證據，證明哪種模型能夠更好地捕捉全球平均股票收益。此外，結果不僅有助於國際資產定價的文獻，也有助於區域或國內資產定價。更重要的是，調查結果還可以為全球和國內投資組合經理提供有價值的指導。

15505518.label: Realisation of objectives
15505518.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to comprehensively examine whether the covariance risk model or the characteristics model is better in explaining the cross-section of stock returns in the international setting; (ii) to provide an alternative methodology to test the covariances-versus-characteristics debate. So far, our results in general have clearly achieved the objectives of the proposal. Using a large sample of global stock returns, we find new evidence that contributes to the covariances-versus-characteristics debate. In particular, we find that the short-term reversal effect supports the characteristic argument and not the covariance risk argument. The past 6-month and 12-month momentum effects appear to be related to both covariance risk and characteristic arguments. Among all effects, the past 12-month momentum effect provides the strongest support for the covariance risk argument. The value effect measured by annual BE/ME is consistent with both arguments, but when measured by monthly updated BE/ME, this effect is only related to the characteristic argument. We use various measures of investment and profitability effects. Although the investment effect measured by annual asset growth or quarterly investment-to-capital ratios is consistent with both arguments, when measured by quarterly asset growth, the effect lends more support to the characteristic argument. For profitability, the conclusion depends on how to measure profitability. We also examine the performance of traditional and new factor models to explain the cross-section of stock returns after controlling for characteristics. Among all risk factors proposed, the momentum factor measured by past 12-month returns is the best factor to explain stock returns. The most striking finding is of a strong negative relation between stock returns and short-term reversal factor loadings. We note that most other factor loadings suggested in traditional factor models are not related to stock returns. Instead, characteristics can predict stock returns after controlling for factor loadings in traditional models. In another paper, I also completed a paper partially related to this GRF project, which is also associated with the performance of Chinese versus global ADRs. We focus on the performance of these ADRs of firms from countries around the world in terms of risk and return. We find that overall, ADRs improve investors’ wealth by $1.03 trillion during the period between August 1954 and September 2020, with more than a third of this amount attributable to ADRs associated with Chinese firms. A value-weighted portfolio of ADRs associated with Chinese firms earned 14.1% per year since the first Chinese ADR was created in 1993, as compared to 9.9% per year for the overall U.S. stock market over the same period. The results are summarized in two papers. The paper on “Chinese and Global ADRs: The U.S. Investor Experience” has been published at Financial Analysts Journal (2021). The paper on “Determinations of cross-sectional international stock returns: Covariances or characteristics” has been presented in many international academic conferences, including at the 2019 China Financial Engineering Annual Meeting in Fuzhou, China, the 2020 Conference on the Theories and Practices of Securities and Financial Markets (SFM) in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and the 2021 Asian Bureau of Finance and Economics Research (ABFER) conference at National Chiao Tung University, Taiwan, and currently under review at Management Science. The outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

15505518.value: This project has generated the following two papers. The first paper has been published at Financial Analysts Journal and the second paper was presented at many international conferences. 1. Te-Feng Chen, Andy C.W. Chui, and K.C. John Wei, 2022, “Determinations of cross-sectional international stock returns: Covariances or characteristics” Summary: Using a large sample of global stock returns, we provide evidence that is in general more consistent with the characteristics argument, especially for the short-term reversal effect. In contrast, the momentum effect provides more support for the covariance risk argument, although is also consistent with the characteristics argument. Meanwhile, we also observe a strongly positive relationship between stock returns and loadings on the investment and profitability factors, as measured by cash-based earnings. The Fama–French (2015) five-factor model can best explain the cross-section of stock returns when using cash-based earnings as the measure of profitability, after controlling for characteristics. 2. Hendrik Bessembinder, Te-Feng Chen, Goeun Choi, and K.C. John Wei, 2021, Chinese and global ADRs: The U.S. investor experience, Financial Analysts Journal 77 (3), 53-68. Summary: We study outcomes to ADR investments between August 1954 and September 2020, with attention to ADRs associated with Chinese firms. Overall, ADRs improved investors’ wealth by $1.03 trillion, with more than a third of this amount attributable to ADRs associated with Chinese firms. A value-weighted portfolio of ADRs associated with Chinese firms earned 14.1% per year since the first Chinese ADR was created in 1993, as compared to 9.9% per year for the overall U.S. stock market over the same period. These data are relevant to current policy discussions focused on Chinese firms listed in the U.S.

15505518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505518.value: We find that in general our evidence tends to be more consistent with the characteristics argument. However, we also find some weak evidence to support the covariance argument. Although we cannot conclude whether our findings support the behavioral or rational argument, our finding is useful and valuable for investors to use the characteristic model to evaluate fund performance. The potential for further development of the research centers on linking the time-varying factor loadings to firm characteristics such as using the instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA) suggested by Kelly, Pruitt, and Su (2019). Moreover, this covariances-versus-characteristics debate can be extended to the bond market or options market.

15505518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505518.value: Do investors and fund managers care about what drive the cross-section of stock returns? We find that stock returns are more driven my firm characteristics than covariances (i.e., factor loadings). Therefore, it is suggested that investors should better to use the characteristic model such as Daniel, Grinblatt, Titman, and Wermers (1997) instead of factor model such as the Fama-French five factor model to evaluate the performance of mutual funds, hedge funds, pension funds, and their own investment portfolios.

15506018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506018.value: 信息技術（IT）投資占公司資本支出的重要且不斷增加的比例。在當今不斷變化的業務環境中，IT在轉變業務流程，實現競爭優勢以及協調關鍵的內部和外部活動方面對企業具有戰略重要性。儘管IT對企業至關重要，但由於所有權和控制權分離導致的共同代理問題經常導致管理人員對IT投資不足或過度投資，因為擁有分散所有權的現代企業長期缺乏對管理的充分監控（Berle and Means 1932）。資本市場可以解決IT治理效率低下的一個解決方案是依靠大型機構投資者的存在，他們有動力和能力監督和建議管理人員進行IT投資，以確保公司的可持續性足夠和適當IT投資。 該擬議研究旨在調查機構投資者參與IT投資治理。我們的計劃如下。 一世。我們首先將研究機構投資者對IT投資水平的影響。 II。然後，我們將研究機構投資者對IT投資業績的影響，或IT投資回報。 III。為了理解影響的機制，我們將探討三種不同類型的機構投資者（準指數/被動，專用和瞬態）對IT投資和IT績效的不同投資視角的差異效應。 III。為了解決內生性問題，我們採用回歸不連續性設計（RDD），並利用企業增加羅素1000和2000指數引發的準指數/被動機構所有權的外生衝擊。這種識別策略將使我們能夠建立機構所有權對IT投資和IT績效影響的因果關係。

15506118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506118.value: The prices of financial assets are forward-looking and contain information about future events. However, what information and to what extent the information are incorporated in the prices of financial assets are not well understood. This project proposes to use a comprehensive database of news events to examine the information related to stock return volatility. I focus on options since option prices are particularly sensitive to the volatility related information. I extract the volatility information from option prices, commonly referred to as implied volatility, and examine how well it predicts the arrival and impact of future news events. This study sheds light on what types of and the extent to which volatility related information are reflected in option prices. This study also helps understand why the option implied volatility outperforms historical volatility in forecasting future volatility, a well-known but not well explained empirical result in the literature. 金融資產的價格具有前瞻性，包含未來事件的信息。 但是，金融資產的價格包含哪些信息以及包含信息的程度還不清楚。 該項目使用一個全面新聞事件的數據庫研究與股票回報波動率相關的信息。該項目研究期權,因為期權價格對波動率相關的信息特別敏感。 我從期權價格中提取波動率信息，通常被稱為隱含波動率，並研究它預測未來新聞事件的到來以及影響。 這項研究揭示了期權價格反映什麼類型的信息以及反映的程度。 這項研究也有助於理解為什麼在預測未來波動率方面,期權隱含波動率優於歷史波動率,這樣一個眾所周知但未充分解釋的實證結果。

15506118.label: Realisation of objectives
15506118.value: To achieve the first objective, we conduct the empirical analysis on the US stock market for the period of January 2004 to June 2019. The data on public announcements of news events is from RavenPack Analytic 1.0, and the options data is from the OptionMetrics IvyDB US. From the news events, we measure monthly total news variation for each stock, a quantity conceptually similar to the realized return volatility. We also measure the variations of scheduled news and unscheduled news separately, and decompose each type of news variation measure into two components, the arrival intensity of news (i.e., the number of news in a month) and the magnitude of news (i.e., the average expected impact per news event). We further classify news events into fundamental news and non-fundamental news. We find that these news measures are positively associated with contemporaneous stock return volatility for most of the stocks. The arrival intensities of scheduled news and of unscheduled news and the magnitude of unscheduled news have the strongest associations with the stock return volatility. We also find that variations of fundamental news have greater explanatory power for stock return volatility than those of non-fundamental news have. These results indicate that the first objective is achieved. To achieve the second objective, we conduct regression analysis of news measures on lagged implied volatility for each stock. We find that the implied volatility positively predicts news measures and the predictability is the strongest for the arrival intensity of scheduled news. There is also clear evidence of the predictive power of implied volatility on the unscheduled news. The result indicates that the predictability of implied volatility on future realized volatility is partially through the channel that the implied volatility predicts these news measures. We quantify the importance of the channel via a mediation analysis with the news measures as mediators. The results indicate that the news channel accounts for about 28% of the overall predictive power of implied volatility on future realized volatility. The strength of the channel is greater for the arrival intensity of news than for the magnitude of news, and is greater for the fundamental news than for the non-fundamental news. These results indicate that the second objective is achieved.

15506118.label: Major findings and research outcome
15506118.value: We construct news measures from various dimensions, namely, arrival intensity of news vs. magnitude of news, scheduled news vs. unscheduled news, and fundamental news vs. non-fundamental news, and find that these news measures are positively associated with contemporaneous stock return volatility for most of the stocks. Among the news measures, the explanatory powers of the arrival intensities of scheduled and unscheduled fundamental news are the highest. We find that the implied volatility positively predicts many of these news measures for most of the firms, and the predictability is particularly strong for the news arrival intensities. We also find strong predictive power on the arrival intensity of unscheduled fundamental news. The magnitudes of news are generally more difficult to predict, however, we find a relatively strong predictability on the magnitude of unscheduled non-fundamental news. These results suggest that option prices incorporate both public and private information related to underlying stock return volatility. Using a mediation analysis with these news measures as mediators, we quantify the strength of the news channel through which the implied volatility predicts the realized volatility. We find that about 28% of the overall predictive power of implied volatility on the future realized volatility is through the channel that the implied volatility predicts the news measures. The strength of the channel is greater for the arrival intensity of news than for the magnitude of news, and is greater for the fundamental news than for the non-fundamental news. The time-series analysis suggests that the average strength of the news channel is negatively related to the market volatility and the strength of the non-fundamental news channel relative to that of the fundamental news channel increases over time. A paper based on this project has been presented at The 32nd Australasian Finance and Banking Conference and 2021 World Finance Conference.

15506118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15506118.value: The current analysis is based on monthly data whereas some studies in the literature suggest that the predictive power of implied volatility exists merely a few days prior to the announcement of the news events. It is interesting to extend the analysis to the daily frequency. News events and stock return volatility can be endogenously related. In months with volatile returns, news stories could be written about stocks because their returns are so volatile. Additional analysis on the scheduled news can help controlling for this endogeneity as news stories in response to scheduled news events are likely to be written regardless of the stock price reaction.

15506118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15506118.value: Numerous studies in the literature suggest that the volatility implied from option prices forecasts future stock volatility better than other forecasting approaches, such as the historical volatility or model-based approaches. This study sheds light on why the option implied volatility outperforms in forecasting future volatility, a well-known but not well explained empirical result in the literature. We use a comprehensive database of public announcements to identify news events. Some public announcements are scheduled in advance, such as earnings announcements, and other news is unscheduled, such as analyst recommendations. Since the implications of these two types of news in terms of predictability are very different, these two types of news are examined separately. We further classify news events as fundamental news and non-fundamental news. Fundamental news is related to earnings, revenues, and analyst ratings etc., and non-fundamental news include equity actions, stock prices, and investor relations etc. We find that these news measures are all positively associated with contemporaneous stock return volatility and many of them can be predicted by implied volatility. We find that a large fraction of the predictive power of implied volatility on future realized volatility is due to its ability to predict the news events. The predictability of timing of new events plays a more important role than that of the impact of new events, and the predictability of fundamental news contributes more to the overall predictability than that of non-fundamental news.

15507118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507118.value: The research evaluates a general accounting precept: balance sheet accruals, as opposed to non-accruals, reflect a firm’s “investment for the future”. In practice, GAAP subsumes the idea that a change in the net accruals, over two periods, implies subsequent growth in revenues (sales) and expenses. The accounting for inventories provides a compelling illustration. If one further adds the accounting precept of matching, an even sharper hypothesis follows: the effect of an increase in the balance sheet accruals on future revenues and expenses will be approximately the same, keeping the current revenues and expenses fixed. Changes in non-accrual accounts differ. That is, a dollar increase in passive marketable securities (or debt) differs markedly from a dollar increase in inventory because the former lacks material forecasting implications. These suggestions as to the workings of traditional accounting are familiar from many accounting texts (e.g., Penman, 2009), but they may not hold up as an empirical matter. It appears that the pre-existing research on accruals, though extensive as it is (see Larsen et al., 2017), has not considered this particular problem, that is, how accruals and their changes over time can be used to forecast future changes in revenues and expenses and whether approximate matching applies so that expenses can be deducted from revenues without information loss. Using data related to large and mature firms (S&P 1500), we estimate forecasting equations one year ahead for the two variables: revenues and expenses. Aside from the two RHS starting points: current revenues and expenses, the issue centers on accruals vs. non-accruals as predictive information. For both equations, we expect the effect of the net change in balance sheet accruals to be positive. This contrasts to changes in non-accruals such as financial assets. We hypothesize that the latter variable loads much less in the forecasting equations. We further expect the matching concept to hold up reasonably, that is, the right-hand sides of the two forecasting equations load up with quite similar coefficients. Additional empirics provide detailed analyses by splitting the accruals into those related to assets and those related to liabilities, and firms into those with above and those with below average accounting conservatism. We expect results related to the estimated coefficients to be consistent with the following traditional accounting theoretical precepts: Operating liabilities tend to be similar to financial liabilities, and unconditional conservative accounting magnifies the estimated coefficients. 待定.

15507218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507218.value: With sophisticated designs and high technical requirements, firms usually produce multiple components to assemble their final products, such as consumer electronics, automobile, etc. Benefiting from the trend of globalization, firms often procure those needed components from a global network of suppliers, which offer attractive manufacturing costs. They may also outsource their entire production and assembly of final products to some manufacturers that operate throughout the globe. For example, Apple Inc. outsources its iPhone components worldwide and subcontracts its final assembly to Foxconn, one of the world's largest contract electronics manufacturers. Such global sourcing strategy significantly reduces firms’ manufacturing costs and enhances their competitive advantages in today’s global market. However, it also exposes firms to various kinds of risks, out of which supply risk is a common one and is listed as top three most significant threats facing by global firms. For instance, due to sophisticated design, Apple Inc. faces low yield of 3D sensors, which is a key component used in the TrueDepth camera module of its newly launched iPhone X. Such supply shortage significantly restricts Apple’s ability to fully fulfill iPhone X’s pre-orders (Wu 2017). Consequently, it is important for global assemblers to take into account of potential supply risks in making their component procurement decisions in order to make timely delivery of their assembled products to the end consumers. The central theme of the proposed project is to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the interactions of supply risks in a multi-component assembly system and for designing effective mechanisms to mitigate the adverse impact of such risks. We first investigate the impact of supply uncertainty on the assembler’s optimal procurement decisions, and then evaluate two practical risk mitigation methods: (1) deploying back-up suppliers when component supply shortage occurs; and (2) shortening lead-time to resolve supply uncertainty of some components before making procurement decisions of others. We would like to understand the effectiveness of these risk mitigating strategies, and provide decision rules to prioritize components for deploying back-up supplier/or shortening lead-time. The proposed project will enhance the understanding on the impact of supply risks in a multi-component assembly system and provide useful information on prioritizing efforts to reduce such risks. Moreover, as the two strategies investigated are commonly adopted in practice, our analysis would offer useful insights and guidelines on how to effectively deploy them to manage assembly system and to stay competitive in today’s global market. 凭借先进的设计和严格的技术要求，公司通常设计和生产多种组件来组装其最终产品，如消费电子产品，汽车等。受益于全球化趋势，公司通常从全球供应商网络采购所需的组件，这提供了诱人的制造成本。他们还可能将其最终产品的整个生产和组装外包给在全球运营的一些制造商。例如，苹果公司（Apple Inc.）在全球范围内外包其iPhone组件，并将其最终组装分包给中国制造商。 这种全球采购战略显著地降低了公司的制造成本，并增强了其在当今全球市场中的竞争优势。然而，全球采购战略也使公司面临各种风险，其中供应风险最为常见，并被列为全球公司面临的三大最重要威胁之一。例如，由于设计复杂，苹果公司面临低产量的3D传感器，这是其新推出的iPhone X的TrueDepth相机模块中使用的关键部件。这种供应短缺严重限制了苹果公司满足iPhone X订单的能力。因此，全球装配商在制定零部件采购决策时要考虑潜在的供应风险，以便及时将其组装的产品交付给最终消费者。 此研究项目的核心主题是理解多组件装配系统中供应风险的相互作用以及设计有效机制为减轻此类风险的不利影响提供理论依据。我们首先研究供应不确定性对装配商最优采购决策的影响，然后评估两种实际的风险缓解方法：（1）在零部件供应短缺时部署备用供应商; （2）缩短交付时间，以便在做出其他部门的采购决策之前解决某些部件的供应不确定性。我们希望了解这些风险缓解策略的有效性，并提供有关部署备份供应商/缩短交付周期的组件的决策规则。 此研究项目将加强对多组件装配系统中供应风险影响的理解，并提供有关减少此类风险的优先次序的有用信息。此外，由于所研究的两种策略在实践中被普遍采用，我们的分析将为如何有效地部署它们来管理装配系统，并在当今的全球市场中保持竞争力提供有用的见解和指导。

15507218.label: Realisation of objectives
15507218.value: All the three research objectives have been fully investigated. This research project focuses on both understanding the impact of supply yield uncertainty on a multi-component assembly system and evaluating the effectiveness of two commonly adopted risk mitigating strategies, namely, backup sourcing and procurement postponement. In the former strategy, the assembler could diversify the component sourcing from a major supplier and a backup supplier to mitigate the potential yield shortage. In the latter strategy, the assembler could postpone the procurement of some components after the yield risks of other components are fully resolved. To address our main research objectives, we have developed stylized models, in which a multi-component assembler procures components from suppliers, whose productions suffer from supply random yields. The assembler sells the product to a market with fixed sales price, and we model the market demand as either deterministic or random. On the one hand, if backup sourcing strategy is deployed, there exists an alternative supplier for each component who has a higher cost but ensures a full reliability. The assembler could place emergent order to the backup suppliers to make up for the realized component shortage. On the other hand, if sequential ordering strategy is adopted, the assembler could postpone the procurement of some components to the later stages after the realization of the yields of other components. To evaluate the performance, we adopt two commonly used measurements: (1) threshold price, i.e., the minimal market price demanded by the assembler to ensure a positive profit; and (2) profit, i.e., the maximal profit the assembler could gain for a given price. The former helps evaluate whether a strategy could help the assembler to expand its business feasibility and reduce the minimal level of price demanded for a positive profit, whereas the latter measures how much the assembler could strive to earn in a given environment with a feasible market price. We evaluate the performance on the assembly system under the two measurements and, more importantly, identify the components which the assembler should prioritize to deploy the backup supply/delayed procurement. In what follows, I will elaborate how we achieve each objective and what are the findings. 1. Objective 1: For the first objective, we analyze optimal procurement decisions in a multi-component assembly system with component random yield, and understand the impact of supply uncertainty on the optimal decisions and the corresponding system performance. Specifically, we fully solve the assembler’s optimal sourcing decision for three models: (1) the benchmark model of simultaneous procurement; (2) the model with backup supplier; and (3) the model with sequential procurement. We further investigate how the component supply uncertainty would affect the performance measures, especially the threshold price (For details, please refer to papers 1 and 2 in Part C). 2. Objective 2: For the second objective, we evaluate the potential benefits of deploying back-up suppliers for mitigating the adverse impact of supply uncertainty in a multi-component assembly system. Specifically, we focus on a 2-component assembly system and investigate the settings when the assembler adopts backup supply for either or both components. For each setting, we quantify the value of backup supply and investigate how the characteristics of the operating environment could affect such benefits. In addition, we also investigate the setting where backup supply is added to the reliable component (For details, please refer to paper 1 in Part C). 3. Objective 3: For the third objective, we evaluate the performance of a sequential procurement to tackle supply uncertainty in a multi-component assembly system. Specifically, we start from a 2-component assembly system and provide conditions to identify the optimal postponement sequence. In addition, we also quantify the value of sequential procurement and how such value is affected by the characteristics of the operating environment. Then, we extend the analysis of threshold price to the general n-component assembly system under sequential procurement and provide an effective algorithm to identify the optimal procurement sequence that leads to the lowest threshold price (For details, please refer to paper 2 in Part C). We have fully analyzed our proposed three research objectives and derived rich managerial insights. To better present our derived results, we have separately grouped them into two academic papers to study each strategy. Specifically, paper 1 in Part C addresses the research objectives 1 and 2 by investigating the impact of backup supply on the performance of multi-component assembly system, and paper 2 in Part C addresses the research objectives 1 and 3 by investigating the impact of procurement postponement on the performance of multi-component assembly system. In addition, our studied two strategies belong to two general categories of risk hedging strategies. That is, backup supply is a special case of the general strategy of supply diversification, whereas sequential procurement is a special case of the general strategy of operational flexibility via postponement. To enhance the impact of this project, we have further extended our analysis to investigate the effect of these two general categories of strategies on mitigating the supply yield risk. Specifically, paper 3 in Part C investigates the effect of correlated supply diversification on mitigating supply yield risks, and paper 4 in Part C evaluates the impact of price postponement, rather than procurement postponement, in hedging against supply random yield for both risk neutral and risk averse firms. The above four papers jointly fulfill our three research objectives and enhance our understanding on mitigating supply yield risk via multi-sourcing and postponement strategies in managing assembly systems and other operation systems.

15507218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507218.value: We have delivered four papers to fulfill our three research objectives, three of which have been published and one is undergoing the review process currently. Specifically, focusing on mitigating yield risks in assembly systems, paper 1 in Part C studies the effectiveness of backup sourcing, addressing objectives 1 and 2; and paper 2 investigates the role of sequential procurement, tackling objectives 1 and 3, respectively. In addition, extending the previously studied risk mitigating strategies to their general categories, papers 3 and 4 evaluate the role of diversified sourcing and postponement in hedging against supply yield risk, respectively, which strengthen the understanding on how to tackle yield issues. Next, I summarize the major findings for each research objectives with more details relegated to the four papers in Part C. Objective 1: we characterize the assembler’s optimal component sourcing decisions for both our benchmark cases and the cases with each strategy adopted. For the backup supply case, we reveal how the assembler could allocate orders between the primary and the backup suppliers. For the sequential ordering case, we show that the order in each stage is a linear inflation of all the previously realized component supplies. In addition, we provide further discussions on how the yield characteristics and component costs would affect the orders and the threshold price. Objective 2: we show that the availability of backup supplier for the component with supply uncertainty can provide very substantial benefits, especially when the unit cost of this component from the primary supplier is high relative to the extra unit component cost from the backup supplier for high-margin products in an environment with high supply uncertainty and low demand uncertainty. In addition, the availability of backup suppliers for the component with no supply uncertainty can provide additional significant benefits when extra unit component cost of backup supplier for the unreliable component supplier is high for low-margin products with high demand uncertainty. Objective 3: we show that the assembler tends to postpone the procurement of more expensive and/or more reliable component, which leads to a lower threshold price and wider business feasibility. The procurement sequence generated through profit maximization is, to a large extent, consistent with that generated from threshold price reduction, especially when the product margin is relatively thin. In addition, we extend our results on threshold price to general n-component assembly system and provide effective method to identify the optimal procurement sequence.

15507218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507218.value: Around the theme of this project, there are many related research topics that are worth studying in the future. For example, for a multi-component assembler, how would backup sourcing and procurement postponement interact together in hedging against yield risk? Are they complement or substitute for each other? If the assembler is capable in setting sales price, then how would the adoption of price postponement affect the value of these two strategies? In addition, how would these risk mitigation strategies be adopted in a competitive market? All the above questions are not only relevant in practice, but also not well investigated in the existing literature. Our current results lay a solid foundation for further exploring these questions.

15507218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507218.value: In competitive global markets, firms are usually exposed to various kinds of risks, out of which supply yield risk is a significant one in many industries. Not only the frequent occurrences, but also the detrimental consequences of yield losses reemphasize the importance of supply risk management for both business practitioners and researchers. Our research provides theoretical frameworks for understanding the interactions of supply uncertainty in a multi-component assembly system and for devising effective mechanisms to manage and improve the procurement process of components in assembly systems under supply uncertainty. The research outcomes have been written into 4 academic papers, out of which three are published in high quality academic journals. Our research could provide relevant managerial insights regarding how to reduce the adverse impact of supply yield uncertainty by using either a backup supply or a sequential procurement strategy. In addition, our results can offer useful guidance regarding which component(s) the assembler should prioritize to either deploy backup supply or postpone order timing, when it has limited resource so that not all components can adopt the selected strategy. To enhance the impacts, we have also disseminated the findings to both academic and industry community, and have received many valuable comments.

15507318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507318.value: Crowdfunding has emerged as a crucial funding method for entrepreneurs with innovative ideas, especially for early-stage startups. There are different types of crowdfunding such as debt-based, equity-based, and reward-based. This proposed project focuses on reward-based crowdfunding, in which a startup promises the funder a reward in exchange for funding and the reward is usually the startup's completed product. Through running a reward-based crowdfunding campaign, a startup solicits financial contributions, which can be used to cover setup and production costs, from consumers in the form of pre-selling a product. Pre-selling a product in a crowdfunding campaign also provides information on potential demand. Although the incentives to use crowdfunding are compelling, crowdfunding also presents certain challenges. One of the big disincentives of crowdfunding for startups is that crowdfunding requires disclosing product information in public when the production innovation might be at a very early stage — thus vulnerable to poaching by potential competitors. Traditional sources of funding such as bank financing allow the startup to keep her innovation secret from the public prior to selling the product. When facing the threat of potential competitor’s imitation, whether a startup with an innovative idea should raise funds through reward-based crowdfunding or other traditional financing sources such as bank funding? What is the startup's optimal information disclosure strategy in a crowdfunding campaign? How is the outcome affected by the factors such as the demand uncertainty, the startup's initial budget, and the competitor’s imitation efficiency? To answer those questions, we develop a game-theoretical model in which a startup with an innovative idea for a new product and limited budget can strategically choose whether to raise funds through reward-based crowdfunding or bank financing. We will first study the startup’s optimal decisions and corresponding profits in the crowdfunding case and the bank financing case. Then, we will compare the outcomes in the two cases to examine under what conditions the startup prefers crowdfunding. Finally, we will conduct comparative statics to examine the impacts of the key parameters on the outcomes, especially the startup’s financing preference and information disclosure strategy in crowdfunding. 众筹已成为具有创新想法的公司的重要融资方式，特别是对于早期创业公司而言。众筹有多种不同类型，例如有的基于债务，有的基于股权，也有的基于奖励。此科研项目将重点研究基于奖励的众筹。一家创业公司在基于奖励的众筹活动中向投资者承诺奖励以换取资金，通常奖励即该创业公司的产品。通过运行基于奖励的众筹活动，创业公司以预售产品的形式从消费者处融资，用于支付设备及生产成本。在众筹活动中预售产品还可以为公司提供有关潜在需求的信息。尽管众筹有诸多好处，但也会带来一些挑战。对于创业公司而言，众筹的一个主要障碍在于，众筹要求在产品创新的初期阶段公开披露产品信息。 而此举可能导致潜在竞争者模仿生产相似产品。银行融资等传统融资方式则可以允许创业公司在销售产品之前将其产品创新想法保密。 面对潜在竞争对手模仿的威胁时，具有创新想法的创业公司是否应该通过基于奖励的众筹或其他传统融资方式（如银行融资）来筹集资金？在众筹活动中，创业公司的最佳信息披露策略是什么？这些结果将如何受到需求不确定性、创业公司初始资金和竞争对手模仿效率等因素的影响？为了回答这些问题，我们建立了一个博弈理论模型。在模型中，有创新想法和有限预算的创业公司可以策略性地选择是否通过基于奖励的众筹或银行融资来筹集资金。首先，我们将分别研究选择众筹或银行融资之后，该创业公司的最优决策及相应的利润。然后，通过比较两种融资方式的结果，我们将研究在何种情况下创业公司应选择众筹。最后，我们将进行比较静态分析，以研究关键参数对结果的影响，尤其是对创业公司的融资偏好和众筹中的信息披露策略的影响。

15507318.label: Realisation of objectives
15507318.value: All the four objectives have been fully achieved. The main purpose of this project is to study a startup firm’s optimal funding choice (crowdfunding or bank financing) and information disclosure strategy when it has an innovative product and faces the threat of a potential competitor's imitation. In a reward-based crowdfunding, the startup promises the funder (or backer) a reward in exchange for funding and the reward is usually the startup’s completed product. However, crowdfunding requires the startup to disclose product information in public when the production innovation might be at a very early stage—thus vulnerable to poaching by potential competitors. By contrast, traditional bank financing allows the startup to keep the innovation secret from the public prior to selling the product. In this project, we target to answer the following questions: (1) What is the startup’s optimal information disclosure strategy in a crowdfunding campaign when facing the threat of potential imitation? (2) What is the startup’s optimal financing choice (crowdfunding or bank financing)? (3) Which financing choice would benefit consumers or social welfare? (4) How are the results affected by the competitor’s imitation efficiency or demand risk? To answer the above questions, we have developed a game-theoretical model, in which the startup can either choose the bank financing without learning demand information or elect the crowdfunding strategy by disclosing product information to public. We consider there exists a copycat, who can decide whether to create a similar product with lower quality and compete with the startup in the regular market after observing the information disclosed by the startup in the crowdfunding platform. We have thoroughly analyzed the game model and achieved all the four objectives. The main findings have been summarized in the paper, titled “Innovation Against Imitation: Crowdfunding Strategy to Compete with Copycats”, which will be submitted to the journal Manufacturing and Service Operations Management soon. Please see the attached paper in part C for details. In what follows, we will elaborate how and to what extent the four project objectives have been achieved: 1. Objective 1: Though analyzing the game model, we have solved the startup’s optimal disclosure and pricing strategies in the crowdfunding campaign. Particularly, we find that the startup may fully or partially disclose the product quality information in the crowdfunding campaign, depending on the market condition and the copycat’s imitation efficiency. When there are limited consumers in the crowdfunding market and the copycat’s imitation efficiency is high, the startup will strategically choose to hide some information, which can help either mitigate or prevent the copycat’s imitation. Otherwise, the startup may choose to disclose full information in order to take the advantage of selling products through crowdfunding stage. That is, we identify the conditions under which the full or partial information should be disclosed in the crowdfunding campaign. 2. Objective 2: We have also studied the startup’s optimal strategy and profit when it chooses bank financing, which serves as our benchmark case. We find that bank financing is feasible if and only if the product demand risk is low. 3. Objective 3: After solving the equilibrium outcomes in the crowdfunding and bank financing cases respectively, we compare the two cases to derive interesting results. First, through comparing the startup’s profits in the two cases, we can identify its optimal financing strategy: It should choose bank financing when the demand risk is low and imitation efficiency is high, and it should choose crowdfunding otherwise. Moreover, we compare consumers’ total surplus and social welfare in the two cases; and we find that compared to the bank financing, the crowdfunding strategy always (weakly) benefits consumers and leads to higher social welfare. 4. Objective 4: We have also conducted detailed sensitivity analysis to understand how the key factors, including demand risk and imitation efficiency, affect the results. First, we find that the startup’s profit decreases as the copycat’s imitation efficiency increases or as the demand risk increases. Moreover, the startup’s optimal information strategy, consumer surplus, and social welfare are all non-monotone in the imitation efficiency. Our research contributes to the literature by studying crowdfunding and bank financing from a novel perspective. We have obtained interesting results and useful managerial insights. We show how a startup can strategically reveal product information on the public crowdfunding platform to mitigate or prevent potential imitation, and we also identify the conditions under which using crowdfunding to raise funds is more beneficial than bank financing. In addition to the above four objectives, during the project process, we have also generated some other related research ideas and extended our model to study other related questions. The original focus of this project is comparing crowdfunding with bank financing with the consideration of quality competition between an innovative startup and a copycat. We generated two related extensions: One is about the comparison between crowdfunding and bank financing under the word-of-mouth (WoM) effect, and the other one focuses on duopoly quality competition with the consideration of social interactions. Specially: 1.We have studied a very related topic about crowdfunding and bank financing with the consideration of WoM effect. On this topic, we have published one book chapter in 2022, titled “Crowdfunding Adoption in the Presence of Word-of-Mouth Communication”; and we have also completed one working paper, titled “Crowdfunding Strategy with Word-of-Mouth Communication”, which will be submitted to the journal Manufacturing and Service Operations Management soon. In the fast-growing markets of crowdfunding, firms launch projects not only to raise funding directly from the crowd to cover early-stage investment, but also to expand product awareness via WoM communication. In the book chapter, we investigate a firm’s optimal funding choice when launching an innovative product in the market with WoM communication. We characterize the firm’s optimal quality and pricing strategies under both crowdfunding and traditional bank financing, and we compare these two funding choices and their corresponding welfare implications. In the working paper, we investigate the equilibrium relationship between a firm’s funding choice and WoM communication among consumers, and its consequent impact on product quality, consumer surplus, and social welfare. Please see the attached book chapter and paper draft in Part C for details. 2.Inspired the quality competition considered in this project, we have extended our study to consider a related topic on duopoly quality competition under social interactions. The findings are summarized in the published paper, titled “Impact of Social Interactions on Duopoly Competition with Quality Considerations”, which has been published on Management Science in 2022. In this study, we investigate the impacts of social interactions on competing firms’ quality differentiation, pricing decisions, and profit performance. Our results provide important managerial insights for firms in competitive markets and suggest that they need to not only be aware of the consumers’ social interactions, but also, more importantly, distinguish the predominant form of the interactions so as to apply proper marketing strategies. Please see the attached paper link in Part C for details.
