15507318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507318.value: In this project, we have obtained fruitful results and interesting managerial insights. To summarize those findings, we have published one book chapter (“Crowdfunding Adoption in the Presence of Word-of-Mouth Communication”) and one academic paper (“Impact of Social Interactions on Duopoly Competition with Quality Considerations”) on Management Science, and we have also completed two working papers (“Innovation Against Imitation: Crowdfunding Strategy to Compete with Copycats” and “Crowdfunding Strategy with Word-of-Mouth Communication”), which will be submitted to the journal Manufacturing & Service Operations Management soon. Next, we briefly summarize the main findings. The detailed findings about Objectives 1-4 can be found in the paper “Innovation Against Imitation: Crowdfunding Strategy to Compete with Copycats”, and the other findings are summarized in the other papers attached in Part C. 1.Objective 1: We find that the startup may fully or partially disclose product information in the crowdfunding campaign, depending on the market condition and the copycat’s imitation efficiency. 2.Objective 2: We have studied the startup’s optimal strategy and profit in the bank financing case and found that bank financing is feasible if and only if the product demand risk is low. 3.Objective 3: We have compared the startup’s profits in the crowdfunding and bank financing cases, and we show that the startup should choose bank financing if the demand risk is low and imitation efficiency is high, and it would prefer crowdfunding otherwise. Moreover, we examine consumer surplus and social welfare, and we find that compared to the bank financing, the crowdfunding always (weakly) benefits consumers and also leads to higher social welfare. 4.Objective 4: We have also conducted detailed sensitivity analysis to understand how the key factors, including demand risk and imitation efficiency, affect the results. First, we find that the startup’s profit decreases as the copycat’s imitation efficiency increases or as the demand risk increases. Moreover, the startup’s optimal information strategy, consumer surplus, and social welfare are all non-monotone in the imitation efficiency. 5.Other Results: Besides the four objectives, we have also generated two related extensions. In the book chapter (“Crowdfunding Adoption in the Presence of Word-of-Mouth Communication”) and the working paper (“Crowdfunding Strategy with Word-of-Mouth Communication”), we compare crowdfunding with bank financing in the market with WoM communication. In the published paper (“Impact of Social Interactions on Duopoly Competition with Quality Considerations”), we investigate the impacts of social interactions on competing firms’ quality differentiation, pricing decisions, and profits. Please see Part C for details.

15507318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507318.value: There are many related research topics that are worth studying in the future. For example, collecting suitable date and conducting empirical analysis to verify our analytical results could be an interesting direction for future research. Moreover, there are many other issues about crowdfunding, copycat, or quality competition, which deserve further exploration. We believe this research project can motivate more researchers and students to explore those related topics in the future.

15507318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507318.value: All the proposed objectives in this project have been successfully completed. Besides the proposed objectives, we have also generated other related studies and obtained additional results. In recent years, reward-based crowdfunding has experienced dramatic growth. However, crowdfunding is a double-edged sword: On the one hand, releasing more information can induce more contributors to pledge and increase the chance of surviving in the campaign; on the other hand, more public information lowers the barrier to entry and attracts opportunistic copycats. The findings from this research project are very useful and could provide valuable managerial insights and guidance to global companies who have innovative products and need to raise funds to support the production process. Based on our findings, we have published one book chapter and one high-quality paper on the top-rank journal Management Science (UTD 24 list) in the operation areas. We have also completed two high-quality working papers, which will be submitted to the top-rank journal Manufacturing and Service Operations Management (UTD 24 list) soon. We have disseminated the findings from this research project to the peers in our research community and have received a lot of valuable comments and compliments from them.

15507718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507718.value: Currently, in China's booming bicycle-sharing industry, there are two priorities for the companies: One is to improve the slim profit margins, which are due to the fierce competition and the huge operational cost. The other one is to expand into new markets, such as the second-tier or third-tier cities. Therefore, these companies often grapple with those questions such as: When should I enter this new market that has uncertain demand? Should I wait until the market is good enough? How many bicycles should I have? How to get better profits? How to reduce costs? These questions are crucially important to a company, but they have not been fully answered by the existing literature. Hence, this project aims to examine these questions by investigating two different models. The purpose of the first model is to provide managerial insights into the entry timing decision and capacity choice for those companies that consider pursuing the growth opportunities in emerging markets. Although the combination of investment-timing decision and capacity determination has been studied in the literature, most of the previous studies on this subject focus on either decision-theoretical or static game-theoretical models. Hence, some key conclusions from those studies may not apply to the bicycle-sharing industry, in which the new markets are often characterized by intense competition, growing but uncertain demand, and positive externalities between investments. We propose a continuous-time game-theoretical model to complement this strand of research. Meanwhile, this study can also advance the literature on strategy theories and industrial organization by examining the trade-off between flexibility and commitment under uncertain environment. The results of this model not only provide managerial insights for companies but also give policy-makers a clue on how to control the number of bicycles in cities. The goal of the second model is to provide a practitioner's guide to capacity building and bicycle relocation. In the current bicycle-sharing industry, companies tend to over-invest in capacity due to the uncertain demand and the fierce competition, but building capacity is costly considering the low revenue in this industry. To address this issue and to reduce the total cost that includes both the cost of operations and capacity building, we propose a novel strategic cost reduction approach that allows two companies share their capacities while still engaging in competition. With this idea, we consider a stochastic optimization model to develop an implementable plan for capacity building and bicycle relocation. 共享单车模式的出现不仅满足了用户短距离出行的需求，也有助于改善环境污染和交通拥堵等问题。但目前这个行业遇到了两个难题：一方面运营成本高利润率低，另一方面面对激烈的竞争各个单车公司过度投放单车数量，造成了新的城市管理问题。在这个项目中，我们首先将探索公司在面对激烈竞争和快速上升的市场需求下的最优产能决策。其次，我们也将探索单车公司之间产能共享的可能性以解决产能过剩和高成本的难题。我们希望能为管理者管理并促进这个行业的发展提供一些启示。并且，我们计划为单车公司提出一个可实现的产能建设和日常车辆管理的运营计划。

15507718.label: Realisation of objectives
15507718.value: All five objectives have been achieved. The fierce competition among bicycle-sharing firms operating in a city brings significant operational challenges to the firms and the regulator. On the one hand, such a competition, along with the unique features of a bicycle-sharing system, requires the firms to carefully decide the market-entry timing and efficiently perform initial allocation and subsequent relocation of bicycles to ensure commercial sustainability. Specifically, different from other shared mobility systems, a bicycle-sharing firm often (i) bears the high investment cost of heavy assets (e.g., bicycles) while charging a low rental price, (ii) offers the convenience of bicycle pick-ups and drop-offs that may lead to a severe imbalance between supply and demand under uncertain consumer demands though, and (iii) provides bicycles not on an on-demand basis like ride-hailing while the bicycles can be centrally managed and even shared with the competitors to serve demands. On the other hand, the competition often drives the bicycle-sharing firms to allocate many bicycles in the city. The regulator is challenged to regulate these lightweight bicycles that may clutter streets and sidewalks and cause safety issues while maintaining the benefits of the bicycle-sharing services to citizens. In this project, we would like to understand the impacts of competition on firms' strategies (i.e., market-entry, initial capacity allocation, and bicycle relocation) and profitability and provide managerial guidance to the regulator on balancing the social welfare and the industry's economic viability. We consider two bicycle-sharing firms competing in the same service area over an operational horizon, and each firm provides bicycles to satisfy uncertain demands. The service area is divided into a set of neighboring service regions and the bicycle movement is modeled as a spatial-temporal network. We formulate the competition as a duopoly game-theoretical model where each firm solves an integrated bicycle allocation and relocation problem toward a Nash equilibrium. Each firm's decision-making problem is modeled as a two-stage stochastic program on a spatial-temporal network. In the capacity-development stage (1st stage), each firm decides on initial bicycle allocation for service regions. In the operation stage (2nd stage), the firm makes subsequent bicycle decisions as recourse across service regions to match supply with demand after the demands are realized in each period. Specifically, the consumer demands depend on the capacity decisions (i.e., the number of allocated bicycles), capturing the demand features in the bicycle-sharing market. The game-theoretical model is highly complicated and nonconvex, creating significant computational challenges. We reformulate the model into a tractable formulation by exploring the optimality condition of each firm's decision-making and designing various optimization algorithms. We then seek the Nash equilibrium by optimizing certain objectives (i.e., criteria for selecting an equilibrium) over the joint optimality conditions of both firms. We also consider several variants of our game-theoretical model. (1) We incorporate the market entry decisions of both firms in the model and help each firm derive the entry strategies, which include entry timing and capacity choice. (2) We consider a simplified and preliminary version of our model to help us estimate some critical parameters that cannot be estimated with real-world data. We examine the feasibility and impact of demand uncertainty and potential capacity-sharing agreement in the relatively new bicycle-sharing market. Meanwhile, the structure of the preliminary model allows us to obtain some theoretical results, which shed some light on the analytical impacts of some critical parameters, such as the renting fee, which are difficult to obtain in our base model. (3) We consider each firm provides bicycles to satisfy the uncertain demands of two types of consumers: loyal consumers and disloyal consumers, capturing the demand heterogeneity in consumer loyalty. A loyal consumer of a firm always chooses that firm to rent bicycles from regardless of the rental prices. The reasons for such a preference are various. For instance, the consumer may prefer the firm's bicycles if the two firms offer different ones, or the consumer is ineligible to rent the other firm's bicycles if he has not paid a deposit fee yet. We assume that the remaining consumers are disloyal to both firms and choose the firm with more available vehicles. The assumption comes from the phenomenon that many consumers are more likely to choose a bicycle-sharing firm due to easier access to the bicycles instead of lower rental prices because the price difference is usually insignificant across firms. (4) We consider the bicycle scheduling model in a service network to help each firm efficiently manage the bicycle fleet operations. Specifically, we explore exact optimization algorithms (including branch-and-price) to support efficient fleet operations. (5) We investigate the fundamental stochastic integer programming model induced by our game-theoretical model under uncertainty and derive optimization algorithms to help solve our model more efficiently. Specifically, we investigate the two-stage stochastic integer programming approach and adopt it in our base game-theoretical model to support each firm's decision-making. We also investigate the multistage stochastic integer programming approach and adopt it in our preliminary and simplified model to derive some analytical results. (6) To address the incentive misalignment between the firms and the regulator, we propose an innovative capacity-sharing agreement between the two bicycle-sharing firms. Under this agreement, each firm can share its abundant bicycles with another firm for a fee when competing in the same market. That is, we consider transferred bicycles when both firms share their capacities (i.e., bicycles). To the best of our knowledge, our formulated spatial-temporal network is the first that incorporates the flows between the two firms. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the capacity-sharing agreement. Finally, we perform extensive numerical experiments based on real data from several companies in China and the United States to obtain managerial insights. We use the trip data of Meituan in Zhuhai and Beijing, China, to (i) demonstrate our model in operating a bicycle-sharing system of a single firm; (ii) test our derived algorithms, and (iii) test our game-theoretical model. We also use the trip data of Citi Bike in New York City, United States, to test our game-theoretical model. Fruitful results and findings are obtained. All the above activities help us achieve all the five objectives.

15507718.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507718.value: We test our derived integer programming algorithms in the Paper 1 of Par C to help solve the bicycle fleet operations in a service network. We also test the stochastic optimization approaches in the Paper 2 and Paper 3 of Part C to help model demand uncertainty in the bicycle-sharing system. Using these solution approaches, we can solve our reformulated game-theoretical models. Then, based on real data in China and the U.S., we perform numerical experiments to obtain managerial insights for the regulator and the firms (see details in Paper 4 and Paper 5 of Part C). Specifically, we are concerned with two criteria for selecting an equilibrium: (i) maximizing the total profit of both firms and (ii) minimizing the total number of allocated bicycles. Our results suggest that, under significant demand uncertainty, an early market entry may not benefit the bicycle-sharing firm and fiercer competition between two bicycle-sharing firms may or may not be detrimental to firms' profitability. They are due to the nuanced impact of competition on the firms' bicycle allocation decisions. Meanwhile, increasing the renting fee does not always reduce the number of bicycles. We show that pursuing more loyal consumers may not bring more profit for a firm, whereas it can even improve the competing firm's profit under some circumstances. We find that the incentive misalignment between the regulator and the firms can arise: while the regulator may reduce bicycles in a city, the firms have incentives to pursue more loyal consumers and allocate more bicycles to satisfy the demands. To address such an incentive misalignment, we propose an innovative capacity-sharing agreement between the two bicycle-sharing firms and demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the agreement. Specifically, when considering the first criteria for selecting an equilibrium, we find that the capacity-sharing agreement improves the firms' profitability and service level and reduces the total number of bicycles in the city when the firms are asymmetric in terms of their loyal consumer percentages. Meanwhile, under some circumstances, the regulator may provide some incentives (e.g., reducing the plate registration cost or providing subsidies) for the firm that suffers higher costs to share its capacity under the capacity-sharing scheme. When considering the second criteria for selecting an equilibrium, we further observe that each firm can reach a capacity-sharing agreement without any interventions because capacity sharing always helps reduce the total costs and the total number of allocated bicycles.

15507718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507718.value: This project studies an important problem in operations management of shared mobility. There are several potential directions for future research. First, our numerical experiments are based on given sets of data, but our proposed game-theoretical models and the corresponding solution approaches are sufficiently general for any typical bicycle-sharing market with two or more competing firms. As the data we use is quite representative, we believe our insights for the firms and the regulator shall also hold for other service areas in the bicycle-sharing industry with similar operational features. Second, as we simplify the cost structure of the bicycle-sharing firms because of the limited information available, we believe the results may be improved if more information is provided. Third, it will be appealing to integrate both individual bicycle routes and accurate trip duration into our spatial-temporal network to provide a more practical operation plan. Fourth, as we consider the exogenous transfer price between two bicycle-sharing firms, it will be interesting to consider it as an endogenous variable and investigate how the firms set their transfer prices. Finally, we can further improve the representation of demand uncertainty, by which the results can also be improved. We leave these for future research.

15507718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507718.value: There are often several bicycle-sharing firms operating and competing in a city. Such fierce competition brings significant operational challenges to the firms and the regulator. On the one hand, along with the unique features of the bicycle-sharing system, the competition requires the firms to effectively decide market-entry timing and efficiently perform initial allocation and subsequent relocation of bicycles to ensure commercial sustainability. On the other hand, the regulator is challenged to regulate these lightweight bicycles that may cause traffic chaos and safety issues while maintaining the benefits of bicycle-sharing. In this project, we understand the impacts of competition on firms' strategies and profitability and provide managerial guidance to the regulator. We consider two bicycle-sharing firms competing in the same service area, and each firm provides bicycles to satisfy uncertain demands. We formulate the competition as a game-theoretical model where each firm solves an integrated bicycle allocation and relocation problem toward a Nash equilibrium. Each firm's decision-making problem is modeled as a two-stage stochastic program on a spatial-temporal network. Various model variants are established, optimization algorithms are developed to solve the models, and extensive insights are provided for the firms and the regulator to help operate and manage bicycle-sharing firms.

15508318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508318.value: Workplace anxiety is a common workplace experience, yet there is a lack of research on the impact of workplace anxiety on workplace outcomes. Existing research argues that anxiety is detrimental for employee performance (Ford, Cerasoli, Higgins, & Decesare, 2011). However, recent theoretical and empirical work shows that workplace anxiety can enhance performance (PI & McCarthy, in press, Journal of Applied Psychology; PI & co-I, under review). While valuable, this work does not account for momentary experiences of workplace anxiety, yet employees frequently wake up feeling nervous about the uncertainty of their upcoming work day. We propose a comprehensive research plan to continue addressing how workplace anxiety can enhance employee productivity, by considering how and when daily levels of workplace anxiety can enhance daily task and creative performance. Grounded in our past theoretical work demonstrating that workplace anxiety can enhance performance through self-regulatory processes (PI & McCarthy, in press; PI & co-I, under review), we propose a dual-process model depicting how daily workplace anxiety can enhance task and creative performance through two state-based regulatory motivational routes, prevention-focused and promotion-focused regulatory motives. Specifically, we argue that feeling anxious at the start of the work day triggers a self-regulation process that can lead to one of two paths. First, it can trigger motivation to protect current resources and avoid further loss (prevention-focus) which can enhance task performance through the enactment of safe, responsible, and vigilant behaviors at work. Second, it can trigger motivation to actively approach and meet challenges (promotion-focus) which can enhance creative performance through the enactment of growth and innovative behaviors (Lanaj, Chang, & Johnson, 2012). Extending our model, we identify critical factors guiding daily workplace anxiety to each path. Individual differences in goal orientations (VandeWalle, 1997) serve as drivers of motivated behavior, such that performance-avoid goal orientations guide daily anxiety towards enhanced task performance through prevention-focused regulatory motives. Learning goal orientations guide daily anxiety towards enhanced creative performance through promotion-focus regulatory motives. Finally, we propose a state-based, situational intervention to help employees cope with daily workplace anxiety by triggering daily goal orientation mindsets (safety vs. mastery) in a sample of employees to induce each regulatory motive that can enhance task or creative performance. We propose two empirical studies using varied methodologies (experience sampling field survey, field experiment) and industries (call center, R&D) to progressively test our model. This research has significant implications for transforming daily anxiety towards driving productivity. 工作焦虑是一种常见的职场体验，然而，鲜有研究探讨其对工作结果的影响。以往的研究显示，焦虑会降低员工的绩效(Ford, Cerasoli, Higgins, & Decesare, 2011)。然而，最近的研究却表明，工作焦虑能够提高工作绩效(PI & McCarthy, in press, Journal of Applied Psychology; PI & co- I, under review) 。这些研究虽然有价值，但并未对工作焦虑的短期体验进行有效解释；如雇员在睡眠中频繁醒来，并伴随着对即将到来的工作日中的不确定性的焦虑。因此，借助于探讨日常发生的工作焦虑是如何及何时能提高员工的日常工作和创新绩效，本研究提出了一个全面的研究计划来进一步探明工作焦虑如何提高员工的工作效率。 我们以往的理论研究表明，工作焦虑可以通过自我调节过程提高工作绩效(PI & McCarthy, in press; PI & co-I, under review) 。据此，本研究提出双路径模型，即日常工作焦虑如何分别通过防御性调节聚焦和促进性调节聚焦这两个状态性调节动机来提高工作和创新绩效。具体而言，我们认为，个体在工作开始时所感受到的焦虑会触发自我调节过程，从而使个体进入两种状态性调节动机中的一种。第一，工作开始时感受到的焦虑会触发动机采取措施保护现有资源并避免进一步损失（即防御性调节聚焦），该行为会通过实施安全、负责任和警惕性行为来提高工作绩效。第二，工作开始时感受到的焦虑会触发主动接近并迎接挑战的动机（即促进性调节聚焦），该动机可以通过从事成长和创新行为来提高创新绩效 (Lanaj, Chang, & Johnson, 2012) 。 对上述双路径模型，我们进一步找到了对日常工作焦虑有重要影响的变量。目标导向的个体差异(VandeWalle, 1997)是动机行为的重要诱因。例如，绩效回避目标导向的个体，其日常焦虑会更易引发防御性调节聚焦动机，进而提高工作绩效。学习目标导向的个体，日常焦虑会加剧促进性调节聚焦动机，进而提高创新绩效。最后，我们提出一个基于状态的情境干预来帮助雇员应对日常工作焦虑，即在员工样本中，触发每个目标导向心态（安全 与 掌握），进而调动调节动机，最终促使员工提高任务或创新绩效。本研究拟通过两个实证研究，并用多种研究方法（体验取样现场问卷调查法、现场实验法），在多个行业（呼叫中心、R&D）来逐步验证我们的研究模型。本研究将对日常焦虑转化为工作绩效动力有重要的理论和实践意义。

15508318.label: Realisation of objectives
15508318.value: All project objectives are achieved. Current narrative on workplace anxiety overwhelmingly points to negative effects. Yet, my conceptual work (Cheng & McCarthy, 2018) suggested the possibility for workplace anxiety to exert beneficial effects. The current project examined how daily workplace anxiety can promote enhanced performance (Objective #1). Moreover, based on our collective data and research findings resulting from this project, it demonstrated that the experience of workplace anxiety fluctuates day to day. First, with respect to the process through which workplace anxiety can enhance proactivity (Objective #2), we theorized, based on my theoretical foundational work on workplace anxiety (Cheng & McCarthy, 2018), alongside the proactive motivation model (Parker, Bindl, & Strauss, 2010), that workplace anxiety initiates a desire for control, which simultaneously prompts excitement and role breadth self-efficacy for proactive action, aligned with the three motivators of proactivity. Adopting a generalization and extension approach and incorporating experience sampling methodology with over 100 employees, as well as in experimental studies, results supported the theorized model. Combined, these results challenge consensus surrounding the detrimental effects of workplace anxiety. This work is under review at Journal of Organizational Behavior. Second, with respect to the process through which workplace anxiety can enhance task and contextual performance (Objective #2), we took a further step to contribute to literature on workplace anxiety. Despite workplace anxiety being a common experience of daily work life, we lack knowledge on factors that lead to its daily occurrence, and a balanced understanding of how employees may adaptively manage their work performance on days they experience workplace anxiety. Drawing from my theoretical framework of workplace anxiety (Cheng & McCarthy, 2018), which depicts job demands as important sources of workplace anxiety, we theorized and found that telepressure and normative response pressure are relevant internal and external sources of daily workplace anxiety. We examined adaptive vs. maladaptive responses to daily workplace anxiety, aligned with our objective of developing a comprehensive dual-process model of how workplace anxiety can enhance and impair performance (Objective #2). We theorized that anxiety prompts work e-mail activity as a self-regulatory behavior facilitating performance, and non-work e-mail activity, reflective of a behavior that disengages employees from their work, debilitating performance. Utilizing a multi-level, time-lagged experience sampling field study across 10 workdays, we found support for our dual-process model. On days employees experienced workplace anxiety, their task and contextual performance were enhanced through behavioral regulatory activity manifested in work e-mail activity. In addition, to address Objective #3, we theorized and found that motivation orientation shapes the boundaries of daily workplace anxiety and regulatory motivational states. This research shifts contributes to a conversation where workplace anxiety can be adaptive, such that employees are active drivers of their daily workplace anxiety. It also points to motivational elements as shapers of whether workplace anxiety is directed towards adaptive or maladaptive strategies. This work also addresses Objective #4 by presenting timely and relevant interventions for organizations, who are experimenting with how to best structure work schedules as they adapt to a “new normal” post-pandemic. As this work suggests that pressure to respond immediately to work e-mails contributes to greater levels of workplace anxiety, managers are encouraged to provide clear-cut guidance to employees, and implement policies to protect employees’ non-work time. In addition, given that work e-mail may be one behavioral regulatory activity that can aid employees’ performance on days they feel anxious about work, our results carry the potential for providing targeted, individual-based approaches to helping anxious employees. This work will be presented at a prestigious international conference, the Academy of Management conference, in August 2022. This work is under review at Journal of Organizational Behavior. Third, to further address Objectives #3 and 4, factors were examined to help employees who experience workplace anxiety better manage their daily experiences. First, we considered employees’ off-work activities as an important facilitator impacting employees’ next-day mindsets, which intersects with motivation orientation (Objective #3). Specifically, we investigated key recovery experiences such as mastery (e.g., effortful activities that build resources such as learning a new language or volunteering), agency (e.g., having autonomous choice over activities pursued during off-work time), hassles (e.g., participation in chores and errands during off-work time), relaxation (e.g., low-effort passive activities such as watching TV or reading during off-work time), and detachment (e.g., cognitively detaching from thoughts of work during off-work time) and their effect on next-day motivational states (Objective #3) that impact employees subsequent performance. Tracking approximately 200 employees across 10 workdays, we found: mastery activities in the evening contributed to next-morning high-activated positive affect and role breadth self-efficacy; having agency in the evening contributed to next-morning role breadth self-efficacy and desire for control; and engaging in hassles in the evening negatively impacted next-morning high-activated positive affect. These motivational states in turn enhanced next-day proactive behavior. Interestingly, while relaxing in the evening contributed to next-morning low-activated positive affect, and detaching in the evening had a curvilinear relationship with next-morning low-activated positive affect, these motivational orientations (Objective #3) did not have an impact on next-day proactive behaviors. This work, published in Journal of Applied Psychology, was awarded “Best Competitive Conference Paper” in the Organizational Behavior Division, Australian and New Zealand Academy of Management conference. It was also judged as the top 10% of papers in the Organizational Behavior Division, Academy of Management. Finally, it was broadly disseminated in mainstream media through South China Morning Post. Importantly, this research points to interventions (Objective #4) that can help employees’ motivational states (Objective #3), lowering anxiety and boosting performance. Finally, following from our findings that employees’ activities during non-work periods are an important period for employees to recover from workplace anxiety, to further achieve Objectives #3 and 4, we considered additional factors that help employees better transition to work in the morning. Recent work identified reattachment to work as a relevant factor - the process of mentally reconnecting to one’s work after a non-work period. We theorized and found support for a dynamic resource allocation process of reattachment to work, as a daily resource allocation activity, where sleep quality promotes next morning reattachment to work, and reattachment to work promotes proactive behaviors at work through three motivational states (Objective #3) – high-activated positive affect, autonomous motivation, and organization-based self-esteem, aligned with my theoretical framework on workplace anxiety (Cheng & McCarthy, 2018), and intersecting the proactive motivational model (Parker et al., 2010). We further identified perceived supervisor support as a critical motivational factor shaping the effect of reattachment to work on daily proactive behaviors (Objective #3). This model was tested across two time-lagged experience-sampling studies over a two-week period. The contribution of this work to applied practice surrounds encouraging employees to allocate a few minutes each morning reattaching to work, as this represents an important process that promotes proactive behaviors, through mobilizing energy and motivation for work (Objective #3). It is also imperative that organizations invest in leadership training, as providing support and motivation to team members aids performance. We further recommend managers to adopt sleep awareness training for employees, such as sleep hygiene counseling to help employees attain quality sleep. This work was presented at a prestigious international conference, the Academy of Management conference, in August 2021. It is under review at the Journal of Management.

15508318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15508318.value: This research laid a solid foundation for building additional research programs on workplace anxiety, workplace wellness, and helping employees manage their anxiety at work. Despite being labelled the “second epidemic”, we lack knowledge on how workplace anxiety unfolds over time. One avenue for future research programs examines temporal trends in workplace anxiety. Better understanding the trajectory of workplace anxiety will promote targeted interventions geared towards particular periods in which workplace anxiety peaks. A second avenue is to examine top-down strategies to complement bottom-up strategies that were the focus of the completed project. My future work in this area consists of developing a series of leadership trainings. This includes examining how CEO anxiety trickles down to middle-level managers, and providing targeted training focused on how to help leaders lead through anxiety. Drawing on clinical and positive psychology, I place gratitude priming (Fredrickson, 1998), expressive writing (Pennebaker, 1997), and principles of positive self-talk (Latham & Frayne, 1989) as core pillars helping leaders broaden positive emotions, increase self-efficacy, and focus on goal attainment. Findings of this research will carry significant impact for managers who are struggling to lead teams during anxious and uncertain times while dealing with their own anxieties.

15508318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15508318.value: This program of research created impact by addressing the well-being of anxious workers, a timely and relevant topic during the height of the pandemic. First, it identifies concrete actions employees may take to recover during off-job times to facilitate their work next day. Evening activities that promote the generation of additional resources best contribute to resource recovery that prompts well-being, such as next day proactivity at work. Spending the evening completing daily chores are, in contrast, detrimental to recovery. Employees are encouraged to make smart choices in how they spend their evening, as these choices have important impacts on resource generation, feelings of anxiety and worry, and perceptions of work capability, which affects workplace productivity. Second, this research identifies strategies employees can take during the workday to facilitate performance on days they experience workplace anxiety, including cognitive strategies focused on reattachment to work and behavioral regulation strategies focused on work email activity that aids goal progress and enhances performance. Combined, this research extends theory on the bright side of workplace anxiety, as a force that can boost performance, while providing practical and tangible suggestions for employees, managers, and companies to address workplace anxiety.

15508418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508418.value: Corporate tax avoidance has attracted enormous attention from the academy and the practitioners (note, we use the terms “tax avoidance” and “tax planning” interchangeably throughout this proposal). The literature defines corporate tax avoidance as any corporate activity, legal or illegal, designed to reduce the corporate tax burden (Dyreng et al. 2008; Hanlon and Heitzman 2010). Prior studies show that CEOs play important roles in tax avoidance by setting the “tone at the top”. Due to effort and expertise constraints, CEOs seldom design and implement tax strategies by themselves. Instead, CEOs have to collaborate with other top executives to effectively reduce the corporate tax burden. However, the existing literature provides limited insights on how the interaction between a CEO and other executives in the same firm influences corporate tax planning. This study aims to address the gap in the literature by examining whether a CEO’s connections with other executives, which are referred to as a CEO’s internal connections, facilitate the collaboration of executives in corporate tax avoidance. A CEO can develop connections with other executives through several means, such as appointing the executives to senior positions and sharing social networks with them. We predict that CEOs’ internal connections lead to more effective corporate tax avoidance. Specifically, the connections can facilitate information sharing among executives and encourage cooperative effort. Therefore, the connections can benefit the coordination of executives in tax planning. In this project, we will first provide empirical evidence on the predicted positive effect of CEOs’ internal connections on corporate tax avoidance. Next, we will examine what factors strengthen the impact of CEOs’ internal connections. In responding to Hanlon and Heitzman’s (2010) call for more research on the determinants of corporate tax avoidance, we will extend the research on this issue to include CEOs’ internal connections. The extension is important because prior studies on tax avoidance often neglect the collaborative nature of corporate tax planning and thus fail to consider the role of the connections among executives. In addition, this project will shed light on the economic effect of CEOs’ internal connections, which is not well understood in the current literature. Furthermore, the project can also have implications for practitioners. The positive effect of CEOs’ internal connections on tax planning will suggest that firm management aiming to reduce corporate tax burden can benefit from enhancing the internal connections. 公司的避税行为一直被学术界与实务界所关注。公司避税一般被定义为公司通过合法或非法的活动来降低其税负。之前的研究发现公司首席执行官通过确立高层基调，在公司避税中发挥重要作用。因精力与专长所限，首席执行官很少亲自设计与执行避税策略。他们通常需要与其他高管合作来有效的减少公司税负。然而现有文献很少研究首席执行官与高管的互动如何影响公司避税。为填补这一研究空白，该研究探讨首席执行官与高管的关系（即首席执行官的内部关系）是否会有利于他们在公司避税上的合作。 公司首席执行官能够通过多种方式与其他高管建立关系。这些方式包括任命高管、社交网络中的互动等。我们预测首席执行官的内部关系会带来更加有效的公司避税。具体而言良好的内部关系有助于管理层的信息分享与合作，因此内部关系有助于管理层在公司避税上的合作。 在该研究项目中，我们将首先提供首席执行官的内部关系对公司避税的经验证据。然后我们将检验哪些因素会强化内部关系的作用。 该项目通过考察首席执行官的内部关系，拓展了关于公司避税的研究。之前的公司避税研究常常忽略了公司纳税筹划离不开团队合作，因此这一扩展具有重要意义。另外该项目也有助于加深对于首席执行官内部关系经济后果的理解。此外该研究也有一定的实践意义。首席执行官内部联系对于公司避税的积极作用表明希望降低税负的公司可以考虑加强公司的内部联系。

15508418.label: Realisation of objectives
15508418.value: The research objectives following have been accomplished. 1) We examined whether the internal connections of CEOs facilitate corporate tax avoidance. We find that more social connections between a CEO and other top executives in the same firm are associated with more effective tax avoidance by the firm. This effect holds when several alternative measures of corporate tax avoidance are used, and it also persists in a subsample of firms that experience exogenous shocks to CEOs’ internal connections. 2) We investigated which factors strengthen the effect of CEOs’ internal connections. The impact of a CEO’s internal connections on corporate tax avoidance is more pronounced when the firm operates in a more uncertain environment and when the CEO has a shorter tenure. Overall, our findings are consistent with the notion that the internal connections of CEOs facilitate collaboration in tax planning within the management team.

15508418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15508418.value: This study adds to the literature on the role of executives in corporate tax avoidance (Dyreng et al. ,2010; Chyz 2013; Christensen et al. 2015; Law and Mills 2017). Despite the progress made in this stream of research, the existing literature does not consider the interactions among executives. As a CEO typically cannot design and implement corporate tax planning by herself, her connections with other executives in the firm can be a crucial factor for corporate tax avoidance. This study thus advances the literature by shedding light on the influence of CEOs? internal connections on corporate tax planning. This study also contributes to the literature on the economic effects of CEOs’ social connections. Prior studies have found that CEOs’ connections with external parties such as banks, analysts, and auditors influence business decisions (e.g., Engelberg et al. 2012; Brochet et al. 2014; Guan et al. 2016). However, there is limited research on whether the connections between a CEO and other internal executives can impact business outcomes.

15508518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508518.value: At the end of each sales period, inventory managers often offer price discounts on perishable products to clean up the leftover inventories. For example, bakery stores offer price discounts near the evening for those day-old unsold breads. Consequently, the sales period is composed of both the regular-sales phase and the clearance phase. Customers, on the other hand, can be divided into two types. One type highly cares about the breads' quality and is willing to pay high price for the freshness. The other type is price-sensitive and would like to check the availability of discounted products at the clearance phase to save money. Only when discounted products are stocked-out would the second-type customers consider the products at the regular price, causing one-way intertemporal substitution. Managers need to decide not only the optimal ordering quantity for perishable products in each sales period but also the amount of inventory to be marked down at the end of the regular-sales phase within each sales period. Such joint inventory and markdown decisions are explored by some researchers in recent years. However, in those studies, customer demand distribution is exogenously given. In this project, we aim to study a more realistic situation where demand distribution is unknown. Managers have to make the joint inventory and markdown decisions by learning about demand and intertemporal substitution rate through observed sales data. We plan to consider three information scenarios: fully unobservable, partially observable and censored observation. Under the first scenario, not only the realized demands for both regular-sales and clearance phases are known, but also the amount of customers who choose the regular-price products due to the stockout of clearance products (intertemporal substitution) is also known. Under the second scenario, the realized demands are known but the amount of intertemporal substitution is unknown. Under the last scenario, managers only observe the sales amount for each phase. Thus, the composition of the two types of demands for the regular sales is unknown. When stockout occurs, the lost sales are unobservable. We plan to use Bayesian updating to estimate both the demand parameters and the substitution rate. Based on that, we shall build up a dynamic programming decision model for the joint inventory and markdown decisions. This research will contribute at least in two aspects: the joint inventory and markdown decisions with demand learning and the estimation of demand and intertemporal substitution rate with censored demand data. 在每个销售期结束时，库存经理通常会提供更低的价格折扣处理易腐产品，以清理剩余的库存。例如，面包店的一天未售出的面包在傍晚会进行折扣销售。因此，销售期是由常规销售阶段和清理阶段组成。客户，另一方面手，可分为两种类型。一种类型高度关心面包的质量和愿意为新鲜面包付出高的价格。另一种类型是价格敏感的， 会考虑打折产品以节省资金。只有当打折产品缺货时，第二类客户会考虑购买正常产品，造成单向跨期替代。经理不仅需要决定每次销售中易腐产品的最佳订购数量期间以及在常规销售结束时要打折的库存量。通过以下方式探讨此类库存和降价决策。 本研究不同于以前的那些研究， 那些研究通常假设客户需求分布是外生的。 在本研究中， 经理必须做出库存和降价决策，通过观察到的销售数据了解需求和跨期替代率。我们计划考虑三种信息情景：完全不可观察，部分观察和没有观察。在第一种情况下，常规销售和清库存阶段销售都是已知的，也是真实的客户需求。 由于清仓产品的缺货选择正常价格的产品（跨期的替代）也是已知的。在第二种情况下， 每期的需求是已知的但是跨期替代的数量是未知的。在最后一个场景下，经理们 仅能观察每个阶段的销售额。因此，两种类型的销售和替代都不知道。当缺货发生时，失去的销售额是观察不到。我们计划采用贝叶斯更新来估计需求参数和替代率。在此基础上，我们将建立一个动态决策模型来解决联合库存和降价决策。这项研究至少会在两个方面有所贡献：联合库存和降价决策，和通过需求数据估计需求和跨期替代率。

15508518.label: Realisation of objectives
15508518.value: The full objectives are fully achieved. Specifically, we have set-up an dynamic programming model to capture the optimal inventory decisions in a multi-period setting. The difference from the literature is that during each period, there exist two sales phases, an early-bird discount phase and a regular-price phase. The demand parameters for the two phases and the buy-up substitution rate parameter have to be learned through observed sales data. We have derived the Bayesian updating formula for them. We designed heuristics algorithms to find the optimal inventory decisions. We then conduct numerical studies to obtain managerial insights. These results are very valuable for airline companies and could help them to achieve great profit gains for them. In another work, we have set up inventory decision models for managing emergency inventories such as water or medicines in preparing for disasters such as hurricanes or earthquakes. We have shown that the optimal deployment policy is a “nested” policy with respect to the shadow price at each location, where a shadow price represents the marginal reduction of the expected total unmet demand due to a marginal increase of inventories. These results are helpful for governments and organizations such as Red Cross.

When the early-bird-discount seat is stocked-out, an early-bird customer either purchases the regular-price seat as the substitute or simply leaves. Our work sets up a dynamic programming model to find the optimal inventory decisions with learning on those parameters, which could greatly benefit airline companies. 2. Guo, P., F. Liu and Y. Wang. 2020. Pre-positioning and deployment of reserved inventories in a supply network: structural properties. Production and Operations Management, 29(4), 893-906. We solve the optimal deployment of emergency inventories given that disasters have occurred at some locations. We show that the optimal deployment policy is a “nested” policy with respect to the shadow price at each location, where a shadow price represents the marginal reduction of the expected total unmet demand due to a marginal increase of inventories.

15508518.value: Inventory managers often need to learn market demand from past sales. However, those sales data may be censored. The sold out of 100 seats could tell the manager that the demand is at least 100 but the manager has no exact information on that. When the sales information on the early-bird discounted seats is available, things become more complex because the regular-price sales could come from the regular demand or unsatisfied early-bird customers. Our work solves this problem by setting up Bayesian updating mechanism for the manager to learn different types of demands and the substitution rates, and we also set up the dynamic programming model for optimal inventory decisions. The numerical studies show that the profit can be greatly improved if airline companies could adopt our model to improve their decision.

15509218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15509218.value: 公司債券市場對不良盈余消息的策略性擇時的關注

15509218.label: Project Objectives
15509218.value: To examine whether the corporate bond market is attentive to firms’ strategic timing of bad earnings news and whether its attentiveness is higher than that of the stock market. To examine whether the corporate bond market is overly attentive to firms’ strategic timing of bad earnings news.
rows: To examine whether the corporate bond market is attentive to firms’ strategic timing of bad earnings news and whether its attentiveness is higher than that of the stock market.
To examine whether the corporate bond market is overly attentive to firms’ strategic timing of bad earnings news.

15509218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509218.value: Investors have limited attention and processing power (Hirshleifer and Teoh, 2003; Lim and Teoh, 2010). Institutional investors, as professionals, are less prone to limited attention than individual investors (Barber and Odean, 2008). However, they are not entirely immune from limited attention (Corwin and Coughenour, 2008; Kempf, Manconi, and Spalt, 2017). To what extent are institutional investors attentive to news? This study sheds light on this question by exploring investor attention in the corporate bond market, a market dominated by institutional investors. Specifically, we examine whether bond investors are attentive to strategic timing of bad earnings news and how much attention they extend to it. Firms strategically time earnings announcements to hide bad news by announcing in periods of low attention or delaying scheduled announcements and the stock market generally cannot see through the strategic timing (Hirshleifer, Lim, and Teoh, 2009; deHaan, Shevlin, and Thornock, 2015; Johnson and So, 2017). The majority of bond investors are institutions. On the one hand, institutional investors can give attention to and process a much larger set of information than individual investors. On the other hand, out of concern for downside risk, bond investors may pay excessively high attention to bad news. Devoting too much attention to information can lead to an overreaction (Barber and Odean, 2013). Combined, we hypothesize that the corporate bond market is attentive to strategic timing of bad earnings news but the attentiveness is so high that there exists an overreaction. We utilize three settings of strategic timing of bad earnings news: (1) announcing after hours; (2) announcing on busy reporting days; (3) delaying expected announcement dates. In each setting, both bond return reaction in the window of strategic timing and subsequent returns in the post-event window are examined. We expect to find: (1) negative bond price reaction to strategic timing of bad earnings news; (2) stronger negative reaction in bond price than in stock price; (3) a reversal in subsequent bond returns. This study contributes to the literature in three ways. First, it explores the impact of limited attention on the corporate bond market and thereby generates new insights on the attentiveness of institutional investors. Second, it provides implications for managers’ strategic timing decisions conditional on the existence of another group of information users—bond investors. Lastly, it adds to our knowledge of corporate bond investors’ reaction to managers’ strategic actions to manipulate market perceptions. 投資者往往會受限於其固有的有限關註和處理能力 (Hirshleifer and Teoh, 2003; Lim and Teoh, 2010)。相較於個人投資者，機構投資者作為專業人員，會較少地受限於有限關註的影響 (Barber and Odean, 2008)，但仍不能完全避免 (Corwin and Coughenour, 2008; Kempf, Manconi, and Spalt, 2017)。那麽，機構投資者會在多大程度上關註消息呢？研究將通過探索機構投資者對企業債券市場的關註，來闡述該問題。而企業債券市場的投資者主要是機構投資者。研究將重點考察，債券市場的投資者是否會關註到企業策略性擇時發布“壞消息”的行為，以及投資者對該行為的關註程度如何。 企業為了隱藏壞消息，會策略性選擇盈余公告發布時間，主要通過選擇在市場關註較低的時間發布，或延後預期發布時間。股票市場的投資者通常並不會發現企業這種策略性擇時行為 (Hirshleifer, Lim, and Teoh, 2009; deHaan, Shevlin, and Thornock, 2015; Johnson and So, 2017)。然而，債券市場的投資者多為機構投資者，一方面，機構投資者相較於個人投資者，會更多地關註企業的行為，同時也會擁有更多的信息；另一方面，忌憚於下跌風險，債券投資者會更多地關註“壞消息”。而過度關註往往會導致過度反應 (Barber and Odean, 2013)。綜合兩方面因素，我們提出假設，認為企業債券市場會關註到策略性擇時發布“壞消息”的行為，且關註程度較高，甚至會導致投資者的過度反應。 研究將以下三種情況確定為企業策略性擇時發布“壞消息”：（1）在非工作時間發布；（2）在公告頻繁的時間段發布；（3）推遲預期發布時間。針對每一種情況，我們都會分别檢驗擇時發布時和發布後兩個窗口期的債券回報。研究預期會發現：（1）針對企業策略性擇時發布“壞消息”的行為，債券市場會有負向反應；（2）相較於股票市場，債券市場的負向反應會更加強；（3）債券市場的負向回報會在一段時間後回升。 研究貢獻主要集中於以下三個方面：第一，研究探索了企業債券市場上有限關註的影響，並提出了關於機構投資者關註的新視角；第二，研究為企業管理人員在進行擇時發布“壞消息”的決策時，提供了新的啟示，使管理人員考慮到債券投資者這部分信息使用者的反應；第三，研究拓寬了對債券投資者反應的認知，了解到當他們面對企業管理層意圖操縱市場認知的策略性行為時，將如何反應。

15509918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15509918.value: 偏黨派新聞媒體也對盈餘新聞有偏差嗎？對股價有影響嗎？

15509918.label: Project Objectives
15509918.value: To investigate if a corporation’s affinity with a political party has an effect on partisan media’s bias in providing earnings news and the tone of reporting the news. To examine whether the partisan bias has an effect on the earnings response coefficient (ERC) surrounding earnings announcements.
rows: To investigate if a corporation’s affinity with a political party has an effect on partisan media’s bias in providing earnings news and the tone of reporting the news.
To examine whether the partisan bias has an effect on the earnings response coefficient (ERC) surrounding earnings announcements.

15509918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509918.value: This proposal will first study if there exists any partisan bias in US media with respect to earnings news surrounding earnings announcements. Past studies find that partisan bias exists in media when reporting political issues, and the bias extends to economic news. Existence of the bias stems from the partisan media’s traditional political ideology and from catering to their partisan readers to attract readership and gain profits. Since earnings news is not directly linked to political ideology, it is not clear if partisan media bias will exist with respect to earnings news. However, if a partisan media outlet caters to its partisan readers, it is likely that a partisan bias exists toward corporations that show strong political preferences. After identifying the partisan bias in earnings news, we will then test if such bias has a price effect. Studies have found that the media, serving as an information intermediary, have significant price impact. However, the price effect of partisan media bias is an open question. We will examine the earnings response coefficient (ERC) surrounding earnings announcements to show if the partisan bias, if any, has an effect on ERC. It is likely that the price effects from different partisan media outlets may cancel each other out so that we cannot find any price effects. Accordingly, we will conduct subsample analyses to avoid the potential canceling effect, e.g. focusing on media, corporations, geographical areas and industries with high partisan bias. Our anecdotal evidence suggests that the partisan media differ as to how they comment on corporate earnings news. We find that they seem to strategically choose when and how (e.g. using a positive or negative tone) to comment on corporate earnings news. This evidence implies that corporate earnings news may be selectively covered by the partisan media with a bias. Research shows that investors are likely to choose their favorite information sources; hence, the partisan media bias may have a price effect. However, whether the effect is significant is strictly an empirical question. This project will be the first study to provide large-sample evidence on whether the partisan media bias exists with respect to corporate news surrounding earnings announcements and if such bias affects firm values. The findings will shed light on the role of politically-biased media in the capital markets. The project will contribute to the growing literature on media slant and the capital markets. 本研究計畫首先會研究探討美國的新聞媒體是否對盈餘公開期間的盈餘新聞存在任何政黨偏差。過去的文獻發現偏黨派新聞媒體在報導政治議題甚或是經濟議題時存在政黨偏差。此偏差根植於新聞媒體傳統上的政治意識，以及為了吸引讀者和獲利而迎合讀者政治傾向的行為。不過由於盈餘新聞和政治意識無直間關聯，偏黨派新聞媒體是否對盈餘有偏差報導，此一議題尚未清楚。然而，如果偏黨派媒體為了迎合偏黨派讀者，則有可能對具政治偏好的公司產生政黨偏差。 驗證盈餘新聞裡的政黨偏差後，我們會接著測試此偏差對股價是否造成任何影響。文獻已經發現新聞媒體作為訊息傳遞媒介，對股價有顯著的影響。但是，新聞媒體政黨偏差對股價的影響還是一個待研究的問題。我們將透過檢驗盈餘公開期間的盈餘反應係數證明政黨偏差對股價的影響。不同篇黨派新聞媒體帶來的股價效果可能會相互抵銷，我們因此可能無法發現任何股價效果。所以，我們將會進行小樣本分析以避免可能的抵銷消果，例如：聚焦在呈現高度政黨偏差的新聞媒體、公司、地理區域和產業。 我們的觀察性證據顯示偏黨派媒體在評論公司盈餘新聞的方式上有所不同。我們發現它們似乎策略性地選擇評論公司盈餘新聞的時間和方式（例如：使用正面或負面的語氣）。此證據意味著公司的盈餘新聞可能被偏黨派新聞媒體選擇性地報導。過去的研究顯示，投資者有可能選擇他們喜好的訊息來源，因此媒體的政黨偏差可能有股價效果。這個效果是否顯著則是一個實證問題。 本研究計畫將會是第一個提供關於政黨偏差存在於公司盈餘新聞，以及，此偏差對於公司價值影響證據的研究。我們的研究發現將會闡明偏黨派新聞媒體在資本市場裡的角色。本研究計畫將會貢獻於媒體偏差和資本市場等日益增長的文獻。

15509918.label: Realisation of objectives
15509918.value: During the project period, we have collected all data, including firms’ related news articles, historical headquarter information, money contribution to political parties, and geographic political preference. We have also constructed all variables of interest and conducted empirical tests to achieve the proposed research objectives. For research objective 1, we measured a corporation’s political preference based on its political contribution to the Democratic Party relative to the Republican Party. We view Fox News and its associated news outlets as Republican-leaning news media, as prior studies suggest that most news media, except Fox News, are leaning toward the liberal party. For robustness tests, we have also tried to rank the political-leaning degree of each media following the 2014 survey report conducted by the PEW Research Center. Using the political preference we identified, we identified the political affinity between the news media and the firm it reports for each earnings-related news article. Next, we collected the tone of each earnings-related news article around earnings announcement dates from the RavenPack database and examined whether the tone the media uses in their reports of a firm’s earnings differs when the firm has the same political preference and when the firm has a different political preference. For research objective 2, we retrieved stock returns data and calculated the cumulative abnormal returns surrounding earnings announcement dates. We examined how investors price earnings-related news provided by politically biased media. Based on the home-bias assumption that investors tend to invest more in the companies located in their home states, we identified investors’ political preferences by looking into the political preference of each firm’s headquarter state. For the political preference of people living in each state, we collected the information of the presidential election results from 2000 to 2018 to determine which party more people have voted for in each state. We have conducted the main tests to fulfill the above research objectives. However, while we were refining our empirical results by conducting further analyses, we recently noticed the following paper accepted for publication at The Accounting Review: Rees, L., & Twedt, B. 2021. Political Bias in the Media's Coverage of Firms' Earnings Announcements. The Accounting Review, Forthcoming. Unfortunately, Rees and Twedt (2021) examine the set of research questions that are very similar to ours. They find that media outlets negatively slant their coverage of earnings announcements when the political leanings of the outlet are incongruent with the political ideology of the firm. In addition, they show that the price reaction to good (bad) earnings news is decreasing (increasing) in the percent of incongruent media outlets covering the earnings announcement. Overall, these two findings have covered the research objectives of our projects, and hence we are no longer able to generate a publishable paper based on our original research objectives. Therefore, we have to alter our original research objectives. Instead of focusing on the effect of biased media on firms’ earnings-related news, we plan to shift our focus to biased media’s coverage of environmental issues and firms’ climate risk disclosures.

15509918.label: Major findings and research outcome
15509918.value: We find that Fox News tends to cover more earnings news of Democratic-leaning firms than those of Republican-leaning firms regardless of good or bad earnings surprises. In terms of the tone used in the news article, we find that for positive earnings surprises, Fox News does not significantly bias the media sentiment of Democratic-leaning firms and Republican-leaning firms. However, Fox News tends to bias the media sentiment upward more significantly for Republican firms when there are negative earnings surprises. Our finding provides some evidence showing that partisan media may bias corporate earnings news when the political affinity does not match between the media and the firm, and the media tend to weaken the negative impact of poor performance of the firm with the same political preference by using less negative tone in news articles. Next, we find that Republican-leaning firms with Fox News covering their earnings news have lower earnings response coefficient (ERC), especially when they have negative earnings surprises. This result, combined with what we find for the first research objective, suggests that when there may be some politically biased earnings news, investors may be affected and not be able to appreciate the earnings information correctly. Next, we partition our sample based on the political preference of firms’ headquarter location. We find that for pro-Republican counties (pro-democratic counties), Democratic-leaning firms (Republican-leaning firms) have significantly lower ERC. This result somehow contradicts our prediction, and we have to conduct further research. Finally, we partition our sample based on the institutional ownership, and we find that the lower ERC for negative earnings surprise due to political affinity between media and firms tends to concentrate on a low institutional ownership sample. This result is consistent with the notion that investment decisions of individual investors are more easily biased by the news media. Due to the forthcoming publication of Rees and Twedt (2021), we are not able to generate a significant research output for conferences or journals based on the original research questions.

15509918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15509918.value: Due to the forthcoming publication of Rees and Twedt (2021), we are not able to generate a significant research output for conferences or journals based on the original research questions. Therefore, we plan to shift our focus to biased media’s coverage of environmental issues and firms’ climate risk disclosures. We will collect environmental-related news articles and conduct a text analysis on firms’ climate risk disclosures. Based on the data of the firms’ and media’s political preference we gathered before, we could examine the impact of politically biased media on firms’ climate risk disclosures.

15509918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15509918.value: In this research project, we plan to provide empirical evidence on how news media’s political ideology (e.g., leaning toward the Democratic or Republican Parties) affects their reporting of firms’ earnings information. It has been discovered that partisan media tends to cater to their readers’ political preferences by biasing information in their news reports. Our research finding will offer new insight into whether political bias exists for earnings news. Given that news media profoundly impact investors’ decision-making, we further plan to show how investors react to potentially biased information provided by politically biased news media. Our research findings will show whether investors are misled by biased information provided by news media. Overall, this project will shed light on the role of politically biased media in the capital markets. This project will also contribute to the growing literature on media slant and the capital markets.

15600218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600218.value: 1949年中華人民共和國成立，新政權旋即與1947年從英國獨立的印度共和國建立密切的夥伴關係。在1959年達賴喇嘛流亡達蘭薩拉和1962年中印邊境戰爭爆發以前，印度廣泛輿論對「新中國」持具批判性卻不失同情的理解。學者一般以國際關係的角度關注中印兩國政府的互動，卻較少研究印度社會內部對「新中國」的認知。本項目針對民族主義精英，探討一個剛獲得獨立的非社會主義國家如何理解並論述新興起的中華人民共和國。本項目尤其關注1950年代初期曾訪問中國的印度人士，梳理他們以印度解殖過程和正在冒起的非結盟運動解讀毛時期中國的各種觀點。1950年代中國共產黨自認為統領一個兼容並包的反殖運動，取得許多印度民族主義份子的認同並鼓舞著他們想像免除歐美霸權的世界。對不少印度民族主義精英而言，「新中國」提供有別於蘇聯共產主義和以資本主義「自由世界」的可行道路；中華人民共和國儘管由共產黨執政，但其捍衛國家主權、驅除西方勢力 、維持國際和平及動員社會大眾的決心策略足以為印度和其他仍在歐美列強勢力之下的亞洲國家仿效。 本項目利用檔案及已出版的文獻，重構印度民族主義精英有關中華人民共和國的論述，其中雖有與印度政府官方立場重疊之處，但本項目旨在探討印度民間社會輿論同情「新中國」的相關言論，說明1950中印友好確有民間思想基礎，並非兩國政府及其領導人的獨特想法。本項目亦將重構一股印度獨立政治人物參與塑造的思潮，即爭取亞洲各國團結、共同探索不受蘇聯和歐美大國支配的發展模式。具體操作而言，項目關注中華人民共和國政府對外宣傳，印度的國家建設方略和印度知識份子對「新中國」認知三者的辯證關係。項目尤其集中解讀1951和1952年兩次中國友好訪問團成員的大量論著及印度國內主要的英文報刊，探討印度輿論如何解讀中共、親中共人士及中國對外宣傳刊物營造的人民共和國。總括而言，本項目闡釋在亞洲區內尋求超越共產主義和資本主義二元對立的社會發展策略及國際合作的氛圍下，印度民間認同「新中國」的前提為人民共和國被理解成一個正在擺脫殖民歷史和進行民族復興的國家。

15600218.label: Realisation of objectives
15600218.value: Archival research grinded to a halt due to the Covid pandemic and travel outside of Hong Kong remained unviable throughout the project period since 2020. In addition, in various locations, depositories were shut down for extended periods from time to time. The PI was unable to consult unpublished documents in India and Mainland China. Having extended the project for six months to 30 June 2022, the PI decided that further extension was of little use as the prospect of regular international travel was then nowhere in sight. To compensate for lack of access to unpublished primary materials, the PI relied on published materials and those held by Hong Kong-based depositories, in particular the Universities Service Centre for China Studies Collection held by The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library. The PI examined Neibu cankao, an internal Chinese state publication that provided relatively candid descriptions of how foreigner reacted to sites shown during their trips in Communist China. This allowed the PI to contextualize and compare Indian intellectuals' observations of the early PRC. One main strategy to counter the lack of access to sources in India was to join with colleagues who were willing to share materials they held. The primary example was the post-1947 Jawaharlal Nehru Papers, covering the prime minister's tenure since India achieved independence, declassified by the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in New Delhi. Colleagues now based in Mainland China and the United States were able to reproduce materials from the collection pertaining to China and India's interactions with its eastern neighbor before the pandemic's onset. These materials include telegrams, meetings minutes, memoranda, reports, correspondence, press clippings, photographs, etc. This collection allows me to tease out the various approaches to which Indian observers understood the new order unfolding in the People's Republic.

15600218.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600218.value: Research outcomes include one journal article, one book chapter, an edited special collection of research notes, and one conference presentation. Three features of Indian perceptions of "New China" were found to be salient. First, while Indian intellectuals were by no means of one mind on the nature of the PRC, many displayed palpable sympathy for the new state and the society it governed. Second, Indian intellectuals sympathetic to “New China” did so not because, or indeed in spite of, the fact that the state was Communist-led. Instead, they empathized with China’s nationalist aspirations and identified with “New China” as Asian nation undergoing decolonization. This anticolonial solidarity echoed that of Jawaharlal Nehru and his government. Third, Indian observers demonstrated interest not only in the politics and leaders of the PRC but a whole array of issues including gender and ethnic relations, education and public health, industrial and agricultural development, art and literature, etc. This broad interest reflected the obsessions of the Indian nationalist elite insofar as their own country was concerned and those of nationalist elites in other postcolonial societies after the Second World War. In this sense, while the project was no doubt about China and India, the themes that run through the research outcomes have clear regional and global relevance in the postwar, decolonizing world.

15600218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600218.value: This project forms part of my longer-term quest to examine what “New China” meant for societies in Britain and its crumbling Asian empire, focusing on those who had firsthand experience of the PRC in the 1950s. An ongoing GRF-funded project (Project No. 15602321) studies the experiences and writings of the English cleric Hewlett Johnson, whose socialist sympathies and peace activism during the Korean War brought “New China” to bear in the United Kingdom, a power coming to terms with its diminished imperial might. These two projects form the basis of a monograph that studies the PRC’s place in the production of decolonial knowledge and nation-building strategies in the 1950s. The monograph also sheds light on travelogue as a medium through which China was represented before cameras were widely used by travelers.

15600218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600218.value: This project explores how the People’s Republic of China, often styled as “New China,” was understood by Indian observers, especially those who visited the country in the 1950s. It demonstrates that rather than seeing their eastern neighborhood as a looming threat, many Indian intellectuals held affinities with the Communist-led state and the society it was building. Through published works and conference presentation, this project demonstrates that rather than simply a top-down process led by prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, bonhomie between China and India had basis in general goodwill at least among the Indian educated class.

15600418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600418.value: Schizophrenia is severe chronic disease. Cognitive impairments, a core feature of schizophrenia, is the strongest predictor of functioning and psychosocial outomes and single most important factor in determining a patient's ability to engage in daily life and adhere to treatment. Prior approaches to improve functional outcomes in schizophrenia are limited in their efficacy and they have high dropout rates. Recent studies have already shown that cognitive impairments in patients with schizophrenia could be improved by cognitive remediation therapy, which is designed to improve attention, memory, and problem solving. Meta-analytic data delivered from clinical studies about cognitive remediation combined with recent results from neuroscience have increased understanding of the critical elements contributing to improvement in cognitive deficits for persons with schizophrenia. These are using computerized repetitive practices, high dosing schedules, a sensory processing, and individually adapted learning. On the other hand, video gaming has opened new opportunities for patients in improving attention, working memory, problem-solving, feedback, emotional expression, and socialization. If video gaming is targeted in a brain-disorder-specific manner to improve dysfunctional brain circuits and renormalizing healthy brain dynamics, it might be suited to be a well scaling and low-cost therapeutic intervention. In this randomised, exploratory, single-blind, pragmatic, three-arms parallel-group trial, patients with schizophrenia will be enrolled and randomly assigned using an internet-based randomisation and stratification across study sites with a computer-generated block randomisation to either (1) Cognitive training (Cognifit, intervention group with computerized exercises), (2) entertainment gaming (Angry Birds, active control group), or (3) non-gaming “treatment-as-usual” (passive control group). The primary outcome will be working memory. Secondary outcomes will be cognitive and social functioning, experience of pleasure, self-efficacy, psychotic, anhedonia and avolition symptoms, and neurocognitive outcomes measured at 3-month and 6-months follow-ups (3-months follow up for neurocognitive outcomes only). The analysis plan (a priori) has directly aimed at testing the hypothesis on primary outcomes, i.e. intervention effects of verbal working memory at 3 and 6 months in comparison with two other groups with two key steps: (1) identify potential confounding factors at the baseline, and (2) multilevel modelling analysis for the main effects with adjustment for time effects (repeated measures) and confounding factors. Missing data handling and sensitivity analysis will be performed according the guideline of statistical analysis for RCT. 精神分裂症是嚴重的長期疾病。認知障礙，精神分裂症的一個核心特徵，是最能有效預測患者其功能和社會心理發展的因素，亦是測定患者日常生活參與度和治療依從性的單一最重要因素。結合現今關注認知功能的臨床研究和神經科學的反覆研究結果，我們了解更多有助於改善精神分裂症患者認知缺陷的關鍵因素。視頻 (電動) 遊戲亦為患者提供了新途徑以改善注意力、工作記憶、解決問題、意見反饋、情緒表達和社交。因此，在這項隨機試驗中，我們將測試娛樂遊戲予改善認知功能的有效性。如實驗成功，我們預料參加者在體驗遊戲後可找到正向結果，例如提升參加者的工作記憶、認知和社交能力，以及在三個月和六個月的精神病症狀跟進測量中有顯著改善。如果成功，該研究將具有顯著影響社會的未來潛力，以改善精神健康服務的治療方針和文化。

15600418.label: Realisation of objectives
15600418.value: Between 16 May 2019 and 30 October 2020, we assessed 1,432 potential participants for their eligibility, of whom 956 were not eligible. Towards the end of the recruitment process (autumn 2019), recruitment was halted temporarily due to the widespread social unrests in Hong Kong. Recruitment again ceased in February 2020 because of COVID-19 lock down at multiple study sites. We were left with 476 (33.2%) eligible patients who were invited to participate in the study. Amongst them, 144 provided their informed consent (30.3%) (332 did not consent, 69.7%). As 13 (2.7%) patients were further excluded (8 not reachable due to COVID-19, 3 withdrew before allocation, 1 participant was dropped after being confirmed to be over 60 years old, 1 participant was dropped for as his/her primary diagnosis was confirmed to be depression), we enrolled 131 (27.5%) participants with schizophrenia: 45 were assigned to the CogniFit group, 43 to the SIMS 4 group, and 43 to the TAU group. After baseline and before the 3-month follow-up, we lost a total of 41 participants (n=12 [26.7%] CogniFit; n=18 [41.9%] SIMS 4; n=11 [25.6%] TAU). Afterwards, further losses of participants were recorded (n=2 CogniFit [4.4%], n=2 SIMS 4 [4.7%], n=3 TAU [7.0%]), but some participants returned for the 6-month follow-up (n=5 [11.1%] CogniFit, n=6 [14.0] SIMS 4, n=4 [9.3%] TAU). Hence, at 6-month follow-up, there were 31 (68.9%) participants in the CogniFit group, 27 in the SIMS 4 group (62.8%), and 33 (76.7%) in the TAU group for a primary endpoint. The final intervention was administered on 25 July 2021. The secondary measures of brain function (EEG and fMRI) are still undergoing data processing. Preliminary analyses have not yielded any clear difference between groups. We are seeking collaboration with interested groups to conduced more advanced analyses. In conclusion, we have achieved 100% of the stated four objectives. Although we did not reach the intended number of samples due to external unforeseen circumstances, we were able to answer the four objectives set out in this study as summarized above. Emergence of some significant effects attributable to our gaming interventions showed that our study was not entirely under-powered. At the same time, the effect sizes of other hypothesized improvement may be underestimated due to the smaller than intended sample sizes, which call for further investigation with larger sample sizes. This is in keeping with the fact that the study had been conducted with a highly unusual period, and any results would warrant further validation by replication in the Hong Kong or elsewhere at a different time. A three-arm trial was conducted in Hong Kong to examine whether gaming interventions are effective in improving cognitive and clinical outcomes in the treatment of schizophrenia. First, political demonstrations in the region prohibited access to some areas and study settings, affecting patient recruitment, implementation of the intervention, follow-up outcome assessments, and access to the research laboratory. The situation caused practical and safety challenges. The study was interrupted at various periods depending on safety measures in specific areas of the city. Some participants continued after a break while some could not be reached anymore and were listed as lost to follow-up because they could not access the assessment facilities per protocol. Later, COVID-19 caused a total lockdown and access to the study sites was impossible. The authors interpreted these extenuating circumstances as a threat to the analysis plan. As the project was supposed to end in December 2021, the recruitment of new participants was stopped before the planned sample sizes could be achieved. Attempts were made to overcome the impacts of the above in terms of safety challenges for study participants and research staff, participants lost to follow-up, intervention postponed, recruitment was stopped early. Mitigating strategies included revised sample size calculations, outcome assessment procedures, revised analysis plan incorporating additional sensitivity analyses for participants lost to follow-up in extenuating circumstances. Additional sub-group analysis (not planned in the original study protocol10) was also conducted for the two primary outcomes considering gender, usage of the internet, and age of the participants. Overall means of primary outcomes by level of variables and by treatment group and change of outcomes by level of variables overtime were compared. These variables were adjusted in the final model to test the possible impact of gender, internet usage, and age on the treatment effects. However, no changes in results were found. These modifications had meaningful effects for the practicality, feasibility, acceptability of the intervention, analytical methods, and statistical power of the study. Therefore, this study might be best considered as a preliminary study during an unusual period of time (political and pandemic).
