15605118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605118.value: 導言 敘事性的信息具強大的說服力，並可影響讀者的態度和行為。作為企業話語的一種類型，企業領導者的敘事性信息有助與持份者的關係發展，並展示公司的正面形象。許多大中華區（包括香港）的指數成份公司通過在網站上發佈敘事性的信息與持份者溝通。由於持份者對企業的看法、在溝通過程中的參與對企業的形象和績效有著重大影響，因此全球領先企業越來越關注如何有效地與持份者溝通。 以往的研究發現中國的企業領導在敘事信息中重視關聯性的建立，表現出開放和感性的說話風格，以便與持份者建立密切的關係，並減少不確定感。儘管先前關於敘事信息研事的文獻指出在敘事過程中，信息的特性、故事的一致性、人物設計、說服的意圖和格式可能會影響讀者對信息的認同及情緒，甚少研究涉及企業領導在敘事信息的說話風格對信息傳播，以及持份者的影響。鑑於企業領導和持份者的溝通在大中華區的重要性日益增加，我們的研究旨在通過是剖析企業領導信息中的詞語、風格和特徵，如句子長度，詞長和詞性（POS）去了解中國企業領導的敘事及溝通方式，以及其敘事及溝通方式對持份者的影響，尤其在認同感和情感兩方面。 由定量和定性方法組成的兩階段研究將在兩年內完成。第一階的研究旨在確認企業領導信息中哪些詞和語言特徵與關聯性，開放性和感性的交流有關。通過在中國的學術和校友網絡，我們將邀請企業持份者參加第二階段的主要實驗。主要實驗涉及不同層次，不同溝通方式的信息設計和測試，探討溝通方式對持份者的影響。通過互聯網絡，我們將邀請參與者評估關聯性，開放性和感性溝通方式的績效及影響。 該項目旨在揭示企業領導者與企業持份者在溝通過程中使用的敘事性信息的說服力，探究各種溝通方式的說服效果。我們的實證研究將進一步確定溝通風格在敘事性信息研究的角色及影響，並為從業者和領導者提供有關如何增強大中華地區企業信息說服力的建議。

15605118.label: Realisation of objectives
15605118.value: Objective 1 is fully addressed. The content theme, content words, style words and linguistics characteristics (intertextuality) of the corporate leaders’ messages were carefully reviewed in the pre-experimental study. We first collected the high visible and accessible Chinese leaders’ messages from corporate websites of Chinese corporations (108 companies) listed in Global 500 2018. In total, 49 out 108 (45%) corporate leaders’ messages were yielded. Next, we reviewed the linguistics features of the messages to uncover the formal/ informal writing style adopted. We scrutinized number of word and POS as linguistic means (Hou et al., 2014) for the delivery of the informal communication style which possess similar linguistics characteristics (e.g. frequent use of pronoun, pronoun-beginning sentences and adjectives) to affective communication style with involved in Chinese corporate leaders’ messages. We have also examined the use of intertextuality in the Chinese corporate leaders' messages and reported the findings in another journal paper published in English for Specific Purpose. Then, we examined the structure of these leaders’ messages to ensure that they have temporal or spatial sequences and revealed the leader’s feeling or thoughts (e.g. Escalas, J. E., 2004; Georgakopoulou & Goutsos, 2000; Shen, F., Sheer, V. C., & Li, R.,2015). Lastly, we identified 9 out of 49 messages that have employed salient narrative structure and affective communication style from our data pool for further examination. To ensure a consistent interpretation of the narrative structure and affective communication style between the research team and real-life stakeholder, we have to further examine how the real-life stakeholder perceive these messages. Consequently, we designed a short survey to invite the real-life stakeholders of the Global 500 companies to evaluate the structure and communication styles of the nine messages where sensitive corporate information, including the name of the company and leader, will be removed from the messages to avoid perception bias. The pre-experimental study was conducted via a popular Internet survey platform-wenjuan.com in China (de Wit, Das, & Vet, 2008) with 80 invited participants on Feb, 2019. These participants, who are prospective dominant stakeholders including customers, employees and shareholders (Mitchell, Agle, & Wood, 1997) of the Chinese corporations listed on Fortune Global 500, were recruited through our academic, students and alumni network in China. They were contacted by e-mail, providing a survey link to an online pre-experimental study accessible from any computer with Internet access (Dahlstrom, 2010). To avoid causing reading fatigue, each participant was required to read one 400–600 words anonymized leader message and, to complete a questionnaire in which they were asked to rate whether the message has a narrative structure and whether it adopts affective communication style on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much). They were also asked to identity the content and style words, and sentences that exhibit the affective communication style. Lastly, participants were thanked for their participation. Measurement items and open-ended questions. The measurement items on salient narrative structure were adapted from Escalas’s Narrative Structure Coding Scale (2004), which includes whether: NS1- the message reveals the leader’s feelings or thoughts, NS2- the message has a clear structure d introduction, middle, and end , and NS3- the message focuses on specific events. Next, the participants were asked to rate whether the message exhibits affective communication style using a 7-point Likert-type scale that ranges from 1 (not at all) to 7 (very much). Then, they were asked to identify the content words, style words, and sentences that contribute to the affective communication style in the open-ended questions. The descriptors of content and style words adapted from previous studies (e.g., Cho et al., 2012; Hou et al., 2014; Lugwig et al., 2013; Ngai & Singh, 2014; Tausczik & Pennebaker 2010) were provided to the participants as reference. By Mar 15, 2019, 59 (74%) qualified survey response were collected. Only ratings provided by the qualified participants who are the stakeholders of the Global 500 corporations were harvested and analysed. We noted that stakeholders perceived verbs and adjectives that expressed strong emotions, four-character, six-character parallel slogans and Chinese proverbs as prominent features in affective messages. 3 (Message no. 4, 5 and 7) out of 9 messages which have a salient use of style words, parallel slogans and Chinese proverbs received a significant higher ratings on affective communication style comparing to the remaining messages, F(8,50)=8.914, p<0.0001). Objective 2&3 are addressed via an experimental study. We have identified the structure, content and style words, as well as linguistic features that contribute to the construction of leaders’ narrative writing (see the above) for the creation of stimuli in the experiment. Before moving onto the between-groups factorial design, the team has conducted a pilot to ensure that the presence of narrative structure and affective communication style are identified in the simulated messages naturally by the target participants (de Graaf et al., 2012). Manipulation check were also conducted in the pilot study to examine whether the independent variables and mediator variables are related to the outcome (Hauser, Ellsworth and Gonzalex, 2018). In the main experiment, a 2 (presence/ absent narrative structure) x 2 (presence/ absent affective communication style) between-groups factorial design was developed. Four stimuli messages with presence/ absent of affective communication style and narrative structure were created and posted on wenjuan.com, a e-survey platform for experimental testing. 400 participants from a variety of prospective dominant stakeholder groups including customers, employees and shareholders of the Chinese corporations listed on Fortune Global 500, were recruited through our academic, student and alumni network. We have also employed snowball sampling method by inviting our contact to refer their acquaintances viz. friends and relatives who are the prospective stakeholders to participate in the experiment (Handcock and Gile, ). This group of salient stakeholders were contacted by e-mail on Jul, 2019 providing a web link to wenjuan.com where the online experiment were accessible from any computer/ mobile with Internet access. Participants were informed about the procedure of the study and their consent were sought. First, they were presented with a set of questions to measure their stakes and standard demographics (Dahlstrom, 2010). They were then asked to identify their stakeholder group(s) before comprehending the stimuli. The 400 participants were randomly assigned to read and rate one stimulus message. Similar to the pilot study, participants were required to answer a questionnaire consisting of a series of 20 measurement items to examine the effects of the affective communication style and narrative structure on identification, emotional involvement, and attitude after reading the message. At the end of the experiment, participants were thanked for their participation. In total, there are 323 valid survey responses, 134 (42%) respondents are male and 189 (58%) are female. Our findings confirmed that 1) narrative structure has a direct impact on identification; 2) the mediating role of identification between narrative structure and attitude; 3) affective communication style has a direct effect on emotional involvement and 4) emotional involvement is a strong mediator between affective communication style and attitude. The results from our study revealed stakeholder’s perception on persuasive narrative structure and style of communication in leaders’ messages and the impact of using persuasive narrative structure and affective communication style on stakeholders’ identification, emotional involvement, and attitude. Objective 4 is fully addressed. Pls refer to Part C for more info.

15605118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605118.value: Since our experimental study confirmed that salient narrative structure in leaders’ messages has a positive effect on stakeholders’ identification and attitude, further research on the specific effects of various elements in CEO narrative including sequence, plot and valence on stakeholders' emotional engagement and attitude is highly warranted.

15605118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15605118.value: This project was able to shed light on leader–stakeholder communication and narrative persuasion by unveiling the persuasive effects of various communication styles that can be inferred from the dialectical preferences in corporate leaders’ communication on stakeholders’ identification, emotional involvement, and attitudes. Our empirical study generated a new perspective on the role of communication styles in narrative persuasion in the Chinese corporate context, and provided useful advice to practitioners and leaders on how to enhance the persuasiveness of messages in corporations in the Greater China region.

15605318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605318.value: With the overwhelming success of Airbnb and Uber in the accommodation and transportation service fields, dining with strangers is considered the next frontier of the sharing economy. What opportunities and threats are presented by the development of social dining in Hong Kong? Food consumption and culinary experiences are central to tourism consumption, and cuisine is a critical attribute attracting international visitors to Hong Kong. With the rise of the sharing economy, private social dining emerged as an advanced version of Hong Kong’s private kitchen trend in the late 1990s. Private social dining provides new opportunities for unique tourist experiences in Hong Kong. Input from consumers, providers of social dining, and the traditional restaurant sector will contribute to the development of social dining for the Hong Kong tourism sector. In this project, a sequential exploratory approach with mixed methods will be used to funnel down and ascertain the opinions and thoughts of both operators and diners on the development of private social dining and the opportunities and threats it presents to the tourism sector and local residents. In Phase One, a comprehensive review of the literature on private social dining will be conducted with attention to both operators and diners. The NVivo software package will be used to perform content analysis of the online comments left by diners on social dining websites. In Phase Two, an onsite observational approach will be taken by the Principal Investigator, who will participate in several private social dining events in Hong Kong. Short interviews will be conducted to gain an in-depth understanding of diners’ experiences and intentions. On the basis of Phases One and Two, a survey questionnaire will be developed as the basis for Phase Three, which will involve a quantitative approach. Questionnaires will be distributed to local residents and tourists selected by convenience sampling. Multi-group analysis of the results of a structural parameter invariance test will be conducted to examine the differences between local residents and tourists in the relationships between antecedents of customer experience, expectations, and dining intentions in the context of private social dining. By identifying the key features of customer experience in the private social dining setting, this project is expected to help increase the competitiveness and innovativeness of the Hong Kong tourism industry. The project will also provide recommendations for policymakers and the Hong Kong Tourism Board on the future planning and development of the Hong Kong tourism industry.

15605318.label: Realisation of objectives
15605318.value: RQ1: To identify diners’ motivations for selecting private social dining services in Hong Kong • Two-stage analysis of semi-structured interview data yielded two factors (i.e., word-of-mouth and publicity) linking up three push dimensions (i.e., seeking variety, gaining authentic experience, and enhancing social circle) and six pull dimensions (i.e., food items, atmosphere, relationship with the host, value perception, service quality, and type of food) for private social dining. • Motivations vary across different locations of the private social dining events. Along the Product-Service continuum, tourists visiting Hong Kong focus more on the product content and local tourists in Hong Kong focus more on the service content. In other words, tourists visiting Hong Kong consider private social dining events in Hong Kong as consumption of tourism products more than a close interaction with locals. RQ2: To evaluate the satisfaction and characterize the experiences of diners engaging in private social dining • Thematic analysis demonstrates that the dimensions of authenticity, culinary, relationship, unrestrained, adventure, and personalization represent valuable additions to Pine and Gilmore’s framework of the experience economy • The result clearly shows the rule change in delivering tourist experience caused by private social dining because four out of the six newly developed experiential dimensions (i.e., authenticity, culinary, relationship, and unrestrained) account for 68.8% of the total text units, indicating that private social dining event largely outperforms traditional restaurants in some experiential areas that are originally not focused or recognized by traditional restaurants. RQ3: To investigate the effects of the sharing economy on the restaurant industry from the perspective of operators • The identification of six pull motivational factors highlights that private social dining services improve the current offerings in several areas, especially the food items, the atmosphere, and the relationship with the host. However, traditional restaurants perform better in regulatory fields, such as food hygiene and fire safety. These are common in sharing economy businesses, but private social dining remains slightly different. Personal apartments or cars are periodically regulated by government authorities to ensure safety even if the owners do not have an eligible business license, but food hygiene or fire safety is not the responsibility of government authorities if it is not a registered catering business. In other words, participating in private social dining events involves more risks than staying at a stranger’s house and riding in a stranger’s car. This relatively high risk is expected to obstruct private social dining services from capturing mainstream consumers who value safety, encroaching the existing business market to maintain a perfect competition market structure. • Private social dining events are not attractive to budget travelers who are the largest customer base for the sharing economy. Private social dining services are more likely to be an advanced form of traditional restaurants that satisfy tourists’ needs for high-quality foods and special catering experiences. It definitely stages an authentic experience, but treating it as an alternative to the traditional restaurants is less likely for tourists. Although the effect of the sharing economy on the restaurant industry is found limited currently, fine dining restaurants that share a similar target market with private social dining services should be ready for challenges. RQ4: To develop recommendations for the future development of the Hong Kong tourism industry for various policymakers and stakeholders • We affirm that private social dining services are a new product mix in food tourism, suggesting that those destinations with rich food cultural backgrounds such as Hong Kong should attract luxurious food tourists by marketing private social dining events. • Private social dining service providers should be aware of diner’s dissatisfaction with the excessive entertainment elements. • restaurant operators are encouraged to be proactive and expansive in designing compelling tourist experiences that go beyond dining satisfaction and the experiential dimensions originally suggested by Pine and Gilmore.

15605318.label: Major findings and research outcome
15605318.value: This study achieved four research objectives by producing three published articles, 2 A+ and 1 B+ ranking. Based on objective 1 (To identify diners' motivations for selecting private social dining services in Hong Kong), this study identified diner's motivation in using peer-to-peer dining. In addition, by investigating tourists' private social dining experiences, this outcome presents an important role for operators (in both restaurants and private social dining) to know tourists' preferences. Lastly, this project also compares both private social dining and restaurant from users' perspectives which can shed some light on the government policy and private social dining health and safety.

15605318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605318.value: Future studies may take these variables into account before generalizing the study’s findings into a broader context. The 10 identified experiential domains were treated as second-order constructs of the dining experience to be incorporated into the SOR model. This project reveals potentially distinct effects of each experiential domain on diners’ psychological and behavioral responses. Subsequent work should aim to model all experiential domains as first-order constructs to illuminate clear relationships. Finally, an importance-performance analysis is recommended to prioritize the importance of the 10 experiential domains across dining settings and to help practitioners determine which experiential domains are worth a deeper investment. Lastly, sharing economy has been playing an important role in the tourism industry. The future study can investigate food tourism-related fields, for example, foodie tours and sustainable food tourism.

15605318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15605318.value: The private kitchen sector has a long history in Hong Kong. With the overwhelming success of Airbnb and Uber in the accommodation and transportation service sectors, the private kitchen sector turns into an online operation that offers an opportunity for worldwide tourists to try and dine in a private kitchen. This project investigates from local and international diners' perspectives to understand their motivation and experience in the private social dining sector. In addition, comparing their experiences in restaurants and private social dining sectors provides an overview of this particular sector and an understanding of both local and international diners' experiences. Lastly, the outcome of this study also can be shared with relevant stakeholders, namely, government, restaurant operators, private social dining operators, and users for their reference. .

15606018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606018.value: 據估計，美國的住宿護理設施（RCF）中有五分之一的院友在一個月內遭受了其他院友的侵略行為(RRA)（Lachs等，2016）。目前還沒有研究記錄香港RRA的情況，然而，一些案件導致了嚴重的傷害和因果關係引起了公眾的廣泛關注--- 2016年4月，一名87歲的院友據稱被殺他80歲和84歲的室友睡覺時，用井蓋擊打他們的頭; 2017年7月，一名90歲的男性院友據稱脫掉所有衣服對一名女性院友進行性騷擾。解決RRA是必不可少的。擬議的研究旨在確定香港住宿護理設施（RCF）院友侵略行為（RRA）的普遍性，並確定與此類侵略相關的風險和保護因素。充分了解與RRA相關的普遍性，因素和背景情況將協助提高RCF護理質量。 RRA指的是“長期護理院友之間的負面和激進的身體，性或言語互動”，“在接受者身上造成身體或心理困擾的可能性很大”（Rosen，Pillemer＆Lachs，2008）。這是一個複雜多變的現象，涉及侵略者，受傷院友及其環境之間的多方面互動（Caspi，2015）。以前的研究已經確定男性，行為障礙，功能依賴和認知障礙是RRA受害的危險因素（Shinoda-Tagawa等，2004）。然而，在以往的研究中尚未解決與RRA相關的因素和環境特徵。 這項擬議的研究是首次使用個體，人際和環境因素的獨特組合來檢驗RRA風險和保護因素。擬議的模型將試圖解決犯罪者的特徵和環境因素，這兩個因素在以前的研究中都未得到充分研究。研究發現將有助於全面了解RRA，從而院友更有效和有針對性的預防和乾預工作。 在研究RRA時，使用院友和家庭成員作為線人是有問題的。一方面，院友的聽力或視力缺陷可能會阻止他們目睹RRA。他們也可能經歷認知障礙，從而使他們成為不可靠的線人。特別是對於參與RRA的院友：由於有罪或害怕受到懲罰，發起暴力的院友可能不誠實;由於害怕遭到報復，受害者或證人可能不誠實。另一方面，家庭成員可能只見到一小部分院友互動，院友在家庭成員在場時可能表現得不同。因此，使用家庭成員作為RRA線人可能無法獲得可靠的信息。由於工作性質，個人護理工作者每天都與居民密切互動，並且最有可能目睹RRA。因此，本研究將針對為老年院友提供護理的個人護理員作為線人。 數據將從30個RCF的800名個人護理員的配額樣本中收集。可靠和有效的工具將用於收集個人層面的數據，包括受害者和犯罪者特徵（認知和日常功能，行為問題），環境特徵（密度，員工與居民比率，隱私，舒適度等）和RRA。據推測，受害者和犯罪者的特徵將對RRA產生直接影響。但是，這種關聯將由RCF環境主持。線性混合效應建模和結構方程建模將用於識別各種因素對RRA的各自貢獻以及不同類型的RRA之間的關聯。

15606018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15606018.value: We completed data collection from 800 personal care workers across 70 residential care facilities in Hong Kong. Participants provided information on the types of resident-to-resident aggression (RRA) they witnessed in the past month. Our results show that resident aggression was common in this sample: verbal RRA was reported by almost all participants (99.9%). Physical RRA was witnessed by 11.8% of the participants; while sexual and unprovoked RRA were observed by 3.1% and 18.0% of the participants. Different factors were associated with respective types of RRA: Physical RRA was associated with greater victim behavioral disturbances, victim diagnosis of dementia, greater perpetrator behavioral disturbances, and workers' insufficient training; Sexual RRA was positively associated with higher perpetrator everyday functioning; Unprovoked RRA was more likely to occur inside the resident's room than in common areas, and was positively associated with greater perpetrator behavioral disturbances and perpetrator diagnosis of dementia. RRA probably represents the unmet personal needs of the perpetrators, thus a client-centered approach with a tailored care plan for individual residents would be beneficial for RRA prevention.

15606018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15606018.value: We have been carrying out training programs to assist personal care workers in residential care facilities to better understand residents' behavioral disturbances and ways to prevent resident aggression. We are in the process of adapting an education intervention protocol developed in the US for use in Hong Kong to help workers better detect and manage resident aggression in residential care facilities.

15606018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606018.value: Resident aggression is common in residential care facilities in Hong Kong. Efforts is much needed to address residents' unmet needs to prevent such aggression.

15606818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606818.value: Industrial Trainees from China and Vietnam in Japan: An Entry Point into the Key Issues of International Labour Migration and Skill Transfer Abstract Since 2016, Japan’s foreign workforce has exceeded 1 million, twenty percent of whom are so-called technical interns. A great majority of these foreign workers and interns come from China and Vietnam. Previous studies have shown that foreign workers and interns have diversified migration experiences and outcomes in terms of skill enhancement, working and living conditions, labour rights violations and maltreatment, socio-economic status and career development. But no systematic research has yet used a comparative perspective to examine the relationship between this rapidly expanding international labour migration and skill transfers. Nor are there any studies systemically comparing the changing roles of the Chinese, Vietnamese and Japanese states in recruitment, placement and monitoring of trainees/interns. This research project will identify the similarities and differences in the international trainee migration systems of the two dyads (China-Japan and Vietnam-Japan), and will isolate the factors that engender different patterns of migration experiences, skill enhancement and outcomes. Specifically, it will explore the roles and impacts of the market and state, and we will also closely examine the impacts on the young trainee participants. We will use Hangzhou in China and Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) in Vietnam as our major field sites in the sending countries, and Shizuoka Prefecture in Japan as one of the major field sites in the receiving country to conduct this comparative study. Hangzhou and HCMC send many interns to Japan while Shizuoka Prefecture has many Japanese enterprises hosting Chinese and Vietnamese workers and interns. We will focus in particular on Japanese enterprises having manufacturing facilities in both China and Vietnam, in order to keep the corporation and industry constant in our comparison of trainees from China and Vietnam and the national/local institutional and cultural factors that affect management-trainee/worker relations. Methods used for data collection will include documentary research and a large number of semi-formal interviews and observations. As part of the research, a total of sixty Chinese and Vietnamese interns (thirty from each sending country) will be interviewed annually over a period of three years, starting with their initial selection in Hangzhou and HCMC, through their 3 years of traineeship and factory work in Japan, and then again when back at work at the Japanese employer’s factories in Hangzhou and HCMC. Managerial staff will also be interviewed at factories in all three countries. While the focus of this study is on the interns, another thirty Chinese and Vietnamese workers (15 from each sending country) will also be interviewed in Japan in the project’s second year to compare their working and living experiences with the interns’. This is relevant given some studies have suggested that some of the interns sent to Japan are actually being used as cheap labour alongside the labour migrants sent to be fulltime workers. This research will contribute to current debates on international labour migration, human capital formation, and skill transfer. The research findings will be presented at migration, labour studies and development studies conferences and will be published in scholarly journals and potentially as a scholarly book. 在日本的中國及越南工業實習生：國際勞工移民與技術轉移的重點議題切入點 摘要 二零一六年以來，在日本工作的外地勞工突破一百萬，其中有百分之二十是所謂的「技能實習生」。這些外勞和實習生大部分都來自中國和越南。過去相關研究指出，移民及實習生的移民經驗和結果都不盡相同，其中包括：技能提升、工作及生活條件、勞動權利的保障、社經地位、事業發展。然而，現存文獻既未能系統地比較急速增長的國際勞工移民與技術轉移的關係，更沒有分析中國、越南和日本政府在輸出／入技能實習生時招募、安置、訓練及監督的角色。有見及此，本研究計劃旨在分析及比較兩對國際實習生移民系統（中國—日本；越南—日本），找出不同移民經驗、技能提升及移民結果的背後因素。本計劃更會重點探索巿場與國家的角色，如何影響年青的實習生。 現時，中國的杭州及越南的胡志明巿輸出為數不少的實習生到日本，而日本的靜崗縣則接收大量中國及越南的工人及實習生。故此，我們會在杭州、胡志明巿及靜崗縣收集數據。我們會集中在一些同時在中國及越南有生產設施的日本企業，致使比較中、越實習生時不受公司、行業不同的因素所影響。研究方法包括文獻研究、深入訪談及田野考察。本研究會訪問六十位中國及越南實習生（每個國家各三十位），追蹤他們三年的實習過程。本研究亦會訪問來自中、越、日的管理人員。不少文獻指出在日本的實習生只被充當廉價勞工，而他們的情況與外勞無異。故此，雖然本研究重點是實習生，我們亦會訪問三十位在日本工作的中國及越南工人（每個國家各十五位），從中比較他們與實習生在工作和生活條件上的差異。 本研究將有助了解現時國際勞工移民、人力資本的形成及技術轉移的討論。研究結果將刊載於與移民、勞動關係及社會發展相關的國際知名期刊中。

15606818.label: Realisation of objectives
15606818.value: This project was conducted during the COVID-19 period which posed great challenges for the PI and his research team to conduct fieldworks in China, Vietnam and Japan, especially under different waves of COVID-19 infection and respective strict quarantine policies in the three countries. Fortunately, despite these huge challenges, all research objectives have been achieved. Since this project is an extension of the PI’s ECS project (project title: Exit, Voice, and the Family/Work Dynamics of Married Migrant Factory Workers in China and Vietnam)by extending the scope from internal labour migration within China and Vietnam to international labour migration and skill transfer among China, Vietnam and Japan, it explored how the state, market and civil society impact on temporary international labour migration and skill transfer among China, Vietnam and Japan (objective 1), on migration experiences, skill enhancement and outcomes of Chinese and Vietnamese workers and interns in Japan (objective 2), the PI has conducted extensive fieldwork research and intensive case studies in several cities in Hangzhou City in China, in northern and southern cities in Vietnam, and Shizhioka City in Japan. The PI has conducted fieldwork by visiting a group of Chinese and Vietnamese migrant intern trainees in their home cities and receiving city in Japan; and engaged in in-depth interviews with over forty migrant trainees and returnees, factory owners, managers, government officials, labour recruitment agencies, trade unionists, labour NGO organizers, and news media reporters. Many of these informants met with me on multiple occasions over many years, allowing me to delve deeper into issues as time went on. The PI has also collected voluminous archival materials written by workers and statistics published by 3 local governments. This research has culminated in the PI’s two journal publications, two conference presentations, one book manuscript and one work-in-progress paper. Through intensive interviews with migrant families in comparable industrial cities (e.g. Hangzhou City, Ho Chi Minh City, etc.) as well as interviewing local government officials in China, Vietnam and Japan, the PI has been able to understand how different state policies have been influencing migrant workers’ strategies. Having discovered this major differences, the PI specifically has looked at how the different countries’ labour export/import policies have been impacting on migrant interns’ migration experience, adaptation strategies and livelihoods in cities (objective 4), as well as the extent of skill transfer from Japan to China and Vietnam (objective 3). Through investigations in this project, the PI has been able to develop a new perspective to analyze the complexity among internal and international labour migrations, local labour regimes, and global value chains, especially the characteristic how socialist developmental states in China and Vietnam involve in shaping the process and outcomes of different forms of international migrations. Furthermore, these investigation and research findings also enable the PI to explore the future pathways which labour migration in Asia may develop (objective 5). 15606818.label: Major findings and research outcome
15606818.value: a) The three countries’ national objectives and discourses on temporary labor migration greatly impact individual migrant trainees’ perceptions and expectations to go overseas. The perceptions of Vietnamese and Chinese trainees stem in part from the effort and strategies of local government or local labor-sending companies to make them cognizant of their migration experiences as “money-making” or “self-investment” opportunities; b) Institutional factors contributing to Vietnamese and Chinese trainees’ perceptions have also been explored. Of particular importance are the differences in the Vietnamese and Chinese governments’ national development goals and how the governments considered sending temporary labor migrants a means of “poverty alleviation” or “modernization;” c) We discovered how and why the career and labor market prospects of Vietnamese and Chinese technical internee training returnees have been constrained by the two countries’ local labor regimes, i.e. while Vietnamese returnees faced an “ethnic glass ceiling” in transnational companies limiting their chance being promoted to managerial levels, young Chinese returnees encountered an “age glass ceiling” greatly constraining their opportunities being promoted to managerial ranks; d) We examined how the Vietnamese and Chinese institutional arrangements differed in TITP trainees’ migration experiences and outcomes. We highlighted the differences of two recruitment channels in TITP (private intermediate agent vs. government-regulated) and the respective underlying reasons contributing to the failure of skills transfer from the temporary labor-receiving country to labor-sending countries. e) There are differences in the policy orientations of Beijing and Hanoi having a noticeable effect on the implementation of TITP to achieve its original objective—skill transfer. We have highlighted the responsibility of the governments of the temporary labor-sending countries to have adequate socio-technical infrastructural governance to ensure that the temporary labor migration process provides an adequate level of skill transfer back to their countries’ national skills development systems and adequate demand in the domestic labor market for these technical skills. More importantly, this sort of governance cannot be done without relevant industrial policies to unlock the constraints embedded in local labor regimes exercised in transnational companies. f) We discovered that in Japan the policy discourse of “development through migration” served as a morally superior argument in the migration debate helping to swing the veto of policy actors where in opposition to lesser skilled labor migration. Such discourse became an instrument in creating and justifying institutions that limited the agency of migrant workers by demanding “loyalty”, while restricting “voice” and “exit”.

15606818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15606818.value: The research findings of this project have great potential for further development. Particularly, through observing Chinese and Vietnamese migrant workers’ migration flow and directions, as well as the locus of capital flight, the PI has been able to explore different new patterns of industrial relations and family relations in China, Vietnam, and Japan which has great research significances in enriching the literature in terms of diversity of industrial models, international labour and family migration patterns in from socialist developing countries (China and Vietnam) to capitalist developed economies (e.g. Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan). Based on these insights, the PI is developing a journal paper trying to understand how Vietnamese women migrants using marriage migration to go to South Korea while using temporary labour migration to go to Japan.

15606818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606818.value: Since 2016, Japan’s foreign workforce has continually exceeded 1 million, and 20% of these workers are so-called technical intern trainees. These technical intern trainees migrate to Japan temporarily through Japan’s Technical Intern Training Program (TITP)—a short-term labor rotation system that originated in 1993—with a stated objective of transferring Japanese skills and techniques to these workers and their countries of origin. Today, the vast majority of foreign workers and trainees come from China and Vietnam. This project showed how Vietnam’s and China’s temporary labor-export institutional arrangements differed, and contributed to the two countries’ intern trainees having varied migration experiences and outcomes. We also explored the reasons TITP failed to achieve its stated objective—international skill transfer. The project also attempted to make sense of the different migration expectations and experiences of Vietnamese and Chinese trainees under different institutional arrangements and contribute to the debate of temporary labor migration and international skill transfer. We argued that the government of a temporary migrant labor-sending country must exercise sufficiently good socio-technical infrastructural governance to steward labor-export policy and industrial policy to match national development goals in order to make international skill transfer possible.

15607518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607518.value: The mapping from physical speech signals to abstract mental representations remains a highly challenging task, due largely to the acoustic variability of speech signals within and across individual speakers. At the population level, acoustic variations can even obscure phoneme boundaries. How listeners resolve the huge variability of speech input and whether they rely on speech-specific or general-purpose auditory mechanisms are therefore core issues in the field of speech perception. In this project, we revisit these questions by re-examining the behavioral and neural correlates of talker normalization — the process whereby listeners map acoustically overlapping stimuli produced by different talkers onto the same phonemic category with the help of contextual cues. A major argument for categorizing talker normalization as a domain-specific process is the superiority of speech contexts to nonspeech analogs in normalizing speech targets. However, the selection of stimuli might have led previous studies to overestimate the efficacy of speech contexts, biasing the empirical results toward the speech-specific hypothesis. On the other hand, participants’ mixed music backgrounds might have caused the overestimation of normalization performance in nonspeech contexts, biasing researchers toward the general-purpose auditory hypothesis. With the aim of addressing the influence of these potential biases, while evaluating the reliability of conceptual models developed thus far, we propose to investigate the cause of the superiority of speech contexts by manipulating the familiarity of contexts on which talker normalization is based, at both the input and subject levels. We will adapt the Cantonese level tone identification tasks to enhance the task comparability within the speech and nonspeech contexts. The hypothesis will also be tested that cognitive load and perceptual expertise in music or language can modulate talker normalization performance and the nature of the normalization mechanisms that are utilized. We will also test our conjectures at the neurological level with high temporal resolution electroencephalography (EEG). Through this study, we will provide more definitive evidence regarding the nature of talker normalization mechanisms. Findings obtained here will further enrich our understanding of the perceptual and cognitive constraints on talker normalization, contributing to the development of more robust models that may be readily generalized to populations with different perceptual experience in the linguistic and non-linguistic domains. Given the ubiquity of talker normalization and the popularization of music and second language education, this project will also offer practical implications for researching communication sciences more generally. 由於說話人自身和不同說話人之間言語信號的聲學差異，從物理言語信號到抽象心理表達的映射仍然是一項具有高度挑戰性的任務。在群體水平上，聲學變化甚至使得音素之間的邊界變得模糊不清。因此，聽者如何解決言語輸入的巨大聲學差異以及他們是否依賴特定言語亦或通用聽覺機制是言語感知領域的核心問題。在本項目中，我們通過重新審視說話人歸一化的行為和神經關聯—聽者藉助於語境線索將不同說話人產生的在聲學上混淆的刺激映射到同一音素類別的過程。 將說話者歸一化納入為言語特定感知過程的一個主要論點是言語上下文相對於非言語上下文在歸一化言語目標中的優越性。然而，刺激的選擇可能導致先前的研究高估了言語上下文的功效，使實證結果偏向於言語特定感知的假設。另一方面，部分實驗參與者的音樂背景可能導致在非言語上下文功效的高估，使一些研究人員偏向於通用聽覺感知假設。 為了解決這些潛在的偏誤，並同時評估已有感知機制的可靠性，我們將通過在實驗刺激和被試兩個層面來操縱說話者歸一化所基於的語境的熟悉度來探討言語上下文優越性的原因。我們將採用粵語水平調識別任務，以提高言語和非言語上下文的可比性。考察認知負荷、音樂和語言感知專長對說話人歸一化性能的影響，及其所涉及的機制。我們還將使用高時間分辨率的腦電圖（EEG）在神經學水平測試我們的推測。 通過這項研究，我們將提供關於說話人規一化機制方面更明確的證據。實驗結果將進一步豐富我們對説話人規一化的感知和認知約束的理解，有助於提出更魯棒的模型，以便較容易地推廣到在言語和非語言領域具有不同水平感知經驗的群體。鑑於説話人歸一化的普遍存在以及音樂和第二語言教育的普及，該項目還將為更廣泛層面的通信科學研究提供實際指引。

15607518.label: Realisation of objectives
15607518.value: To date, the mechanisms of talker normalization remain a question of debate, and it is still unclear whether such a process is motivated by speech-specific or general-purpose auditory processes. In support of the speech-specific account, researchers have observed that speech samples were easier to normalize when embedded in speech contexts than synthesized nonspeech analogs containing analogous formant or F0 cues. Nonetheless, we have more exposure to speech than to synthesized signals. This inherent familiarity gap might have biased the results toward the speech-specific hypothesis of talker normalization. The auditory account is inconclusive as well due to similar reasons: Musicians are more adept at processing non-linguistic sound patterns than non-musicians, and yet related studies often failed to control for participants’ music backgrounds. Hence, the auditory account of talker normalization might have also been founded upon biased data. In this project, we have re-examined the nature of talker normalization mechanisms while controlling for familiarity biases. On the one hand, we varied perceptual familiarity at the input level, presenting speech, music analogs, and synthesized nonspeech to non-musicians to investigate the influence of the acoustic nature on talker normalization. On the other hand, familiarity may activate higher-order perceptual processes in expert individuals. Having access to sound representations established through long-term perceptual experience, be it music or speech, give rise to behavioral and neurological advantages. To contrast higher-order perceptual familiarity, we have invited Cantonese musicians, Cantonese non-musicians, and Mandarin learners of Cantonese (non-musicians). Cantonese musicians and non-musicians allowed us to assess the modulation effects of music expertise, while performance differences between the two non-musician groups shed light on the effects of native linguistic experience. Both may offer direct support to the speech-specific hypothesis of talker normalization. Furthermore, listeners frequently need to tackle heightened cognitive load caused by multitasking. However, the relation between talker normalization and cognitive load is still poorly understood. By exploiting the fact that load may modulate both early (low-level sensory) and late (high-level speech-specific) stages of speech processing, results obtained here also help ascertain the nature of talker normalization mechanisms, extending our understanding of talker normalization mechanisms to more complex but true-to-life situations.

15607518.label: Major findings and research outcome
15607518.value: a.) The behavioral results showed that musicians and nonmusicians were equally well in using the pitch cues in speech contexts to normalize lexical tone variability. However, the advantage of music training was observed at the cortical level. The time-domain ERP analysis suggested that musicians normalized lexical tone variability much earlier than nonmusicians (N1: 70-175 ms vs P2: 175-280 ms). An exploratory source analysis further revealed that two groups probably use different cortical regions to normalize lexical tones. Musicians dominantly use left BA41 to normalize lexical tone variability, but nonmusicians rely on more cortical regions, including right BA 41, 42 and 22 to achieve the same purpose. b.) The results from native speakers as well as L2 learners suggested that only speech contexts are effective in normalizing lexical tone variability, indicating a speech-specific processing underlying perceptual normalization. Mandarin speakers, i.e., learners of Cantonese as L2, showed significant normalization process but the effect size is significantly smaller than Cantonese speakers. The correlation analysis indicating that the effect size of normalization process was positively correlated with their Cantonese immersion. The longer the L2 immersion, the better the normalization process. Together the results suggested that although Mandarin speakers are highly experienced at normalizing lexical tones in Mandarin, the normalization strategy cannot be transferred directly from one tonal language to another, and it is acquired gradually during the L2 immersion. c.) Subjects’ performance of the pattern searching task was significantly worse in the higher-cognitive load searching task (0.7 vs 0.91, p < 0.01; chance level = 0.5), indicating that the secondary task did consume more cognitive resources in the higher-cognitive load condition. However, to our surprise, the results suggested that at the behavioral level, the lexical tone normalization task was not affected by either the low- or high-cognitive load secondary task. Subjects’ performance was comparable (ps > 0.05) in the no load condition (M = 0.83, SD = 0.1), the low load condition (M = 0.84, SD = 0.09), and the high load condition (M = 0.83, SD = 0.09). The behavioral results suggested that subjects can successfully normalize the lexical tone variability even when the cognitive resources were reduced.

15607518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15607518.value: Normalization of speech variability is an important aspect to guarantee effective communication. By far, when and how a child acquires such an ability is unknown. Our further effect will consider looking at the time stamps of the development of this ability in our future research proposals.

15607518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15607518.value: The mapping from physical speech signals to abstract mental representations remains a highly challenging task, due largely to the acoustic variability of speech signals within and across individual speakers. At the population level, acoustic variations can even obscure phoneme boundaries. How listeners resolve the notorious variability of speech input and whether they rely on speech-specific or general-purpose auditory mechanisms are therefore core issues in the field of speech perception. In this project, we have revisited these questions by re-examining the behavioral and neural correlates of talker normalization (i.e., the process whereby listeners map acoustically overlapping stimuli produced by different talkers onto the same phonemic category with the help of context cues). This project revisits the nature of talker normalization mechanisms using behavioral and EEG measurements. Results obtained here will help adjudicate between competing accounts (speech-specific vs. general-auditory) of talker normalization, contributing to the development of more inclusive and readily generalizable speech perception theories across populations with distinct linguistic and non-linguistic perceptual experiences. The ascertaining of the nature of normalization mechanisms may also be useful for identifying potential neural networks underlying talker normalization, therefore benefiting future fMRI studies searching for the loci of auditory (non-linguistic, linguistic) normalization.

15608318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608318.value: 本研究旨在針對自閉症譜系障礙文獻中的兩個經典發現提出新的見解：一、自閉症兒童呈現心智理論能力缺陷，二、自閉症兒童難以掌握心理狀態詞彙。心智理論指的是推斷自己和他人心理狀態（例如：慾望、思想和錯誤信念）的認知能力。錯誤信念的理解被視為心智理論發展的一個重要里程碑。近期有關心智理論的發展順序的研究表明，自閉症兒童的心智理論的發展順序與正常兒童不同，而且正常兒童的心智理論的發育順序往往受地域和文化差異的影響。最近的一項薈萃分析進一步顯示，與中國內地的正常兒童相比，香港的正常兒童對錯誤信念的理解有顯著的延遲。這些研究結果促使本研究探索香港自閉症兒童和正常兒童的心智理論的發展順序，從而揭示地域和文化對心智理論發展的影響。 至於心理狀態詞彙，儘管有相當多的證據表明，香港正常兒童對非事實性的心理狀態詞彙（例如：以為）的理解能夠促進他們對錯誤信念的理解，但是迄今還沒有任何研究探索過香港自閉症兒童的心智理論與和掌握心理狀態詞彙之間的關係。本研究通過調查香港自閉症兒童和正常兒童對不同事實性（例如：知道）和非事實性的心理狀態詞彙的理解和其與心智理論的關係，從而以探索自閉症兒童難以掌握心理狀態詞彙的原因。 本研究的一個創新點是調查香港自閉症兒童和正常兒童對六種預設觸發詞的理解，其中包括調查他們對事實性和非事實性的心理狀態詞彙的理解和其與心智理論的關係。鑑於我們的初步研究結果已顯示，香港自閉症兒童對預設觸發詞的理解能力比較同齡的正常兒童弱，本研究不僅能闡明自閉症兒童難以理解預設觸發詞的原因，還能為對自閉症兒童的心智理論、心理狀態詞彙和預設觸發詞之間的關係提供帶來新的見解。

15608618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608618.value: Mandarin alphabetical words (MAWs 字母詞) are typically written with the 26 English alphabetical letters and can consist of alphabetic letters only (e.g., KTV, PK) or in combination with Chinese characters in different positions (e.g., AA制, 阿Q). The first MAW (X光線, X-ray) was documented in 1903, yet their numbers have increased significantly over the last 20 years. Currently, hundreds are listed in dictionaries, and thousands are found in corpora. MAWs pose challenges to our understanding of how language is processed because they seem to follow Mandarin word formation rules while violating phonological rules at the same time. Empirical evidence gives conflicting signals as to whether they belong to the linguistic system of Chinese or not. First, they are pronounced without a lexical tone ([eɪkʰs] or [eɪkhʊ̯sʊ̯] for ‘x’ in X-光 x-guāng ‘x-ray’). Second, they are often favored over alternatives that conform to Chinese linguistic rules. For instance, the alphabet-character form X-光 and x-guāng pronunciation is preferred over the mixed transliteration plus semantic translation 愛克斯光 aìkèsīguāng ‘x-ray’. Third, pronunciations of letters are approximations of their English forms that critically cannot be transliterated into Pinyin Romanization as the pronunciations often cannot be mapped to Chinese phonemes. Fourth, although alphabetical letters in MAWs eschew available phonologically adapted pronunciations, they seem to follow Mandarin morphological rules as aspectual marks can be attached to MAWs (e.g., PK過) and some alphabetical letters can be involved in word formation. For example, MAWs containing ‘K’ (for ‘ketamine’) include: 拉K, K仔, K粉, K膏, K毒, K癮, K他命, etc. Lastly, some MAWs are not loanwords and cannot be traced to a source language word: e.g. AA制, QQ, 阿Q. In sum, MAWs are words with sounds that are not in the Chinese phonological system. This puts them in contrast with the two other types of language units: words with sounds in the sound system, and non-words with atypical sounds (including conversational sounds, such as [m/n], [em/n], and [um/n] in many languages). The fact that MAWs are exceptions to the phonological system but conform to the morphological system poses a great challenge both to our understanding of linguistic systems and to theories and applications for language processing. We tackle the above challenges by experiments involving different linguistic modules. Built upon solid empirical evidence for complex yet subtle adaptation at different linguistic levels involving MAWs, the project aims to account for the hitherto unexplored interaction between orthography, morphology and phonology. 漢語字母詞 (Mandarin alphabetical words, MAWs) 通常以 26 個英文字母書寫; 詞可以全由字母組成(如 KTV, PK)，或由字母與漢字一起組成 (如AA制, 阿Q). 第一個漢語字母詞(X光線, X-ray) 出現於1903年, 但過去 20 年新的字母詞急速增加. 當代詞典中有數百個字母詞，語料庫中可找到上千個。 漢語字母詞的有好幾個意料之外的語言特性。第一，字母詞的發音沒有固定的詞調 (X-光 中的X 可以是[eɪkʰs] or [eɪkhʊ̯sʊ̯]， 但無聲調). 其次, 字母詞通常比同義的非字母詞更容易廣為接受/使用。 例如，字母與漢字組成的‘X-光’ 與其發音，遠比混合音意譯詞愛克斯光 aìkèsīguāng ‘x-ray’常用。第三，字母詞中字母的發音通常近似英語的字母發音，但是並無法直接轉成音譯漢字，主要是這些英語發音不但沒有聲調，而且常有漢語音韻系統外的發音，無法直接轉成漢字。第四，字母詞長期以來抗拒融入漢語音韻系統，而且並無統一標準發音，, 他們卻似乎遵循漢語的構詞規律。動詞性字母詞可接動詞語態標記 (如 PK過) X-光。特定字母詞甚至能參與構詞。 如含‘K’ 的字母詞包括: 拉K, K仔, K粉, K膏, K毒, K癮, K他命。最後，字母詞並非借詞，如AA制, QQ, 阿Q. 長久以來並未經過語音改變，並帶有許多漢語音韻系統外的特徵。本研究將針對字母詞特徵，設計多種實驗，以探索字母詞在漢語詞彙音韻系統中的地位。

15608618.label: Realisation of objectives
15608618.value: We have achieved the object (Object 6) of compiling a comprehensive linguistic database of MAWs by having extracted and constructed 406,739 MAWs from Sina Weibo (SMAW; Xiang et al., 2020). This is a more updated and balanced MAW list in simplified Chinese since the 2010s. Based on this database, we have validated and confirmed the four main types of word formation of the MAWs proposed by Huang and Liu (2017), including AC, CA, CAC, and others, according to the position of the alphabet (A) and consonants (C). It is found that most MAWs are disyllabic compound words, which mostly follow the Mandarin lexical word formation rules (Xiang et al., 2020). Object 2 is partially achieved in this sense. To achieve Object 3, we explored the influence of Mandarin speakers’ native dialects on phonetic variations in Dong and Huang (2019). For example, 感觉 (gan3jue2, feeling) in Mandarin Chinese is found to be affected by some of the dialects, and a new MAW is thus coined, 感jio. This phenomenon indicates that alphabetical words might be used to transcribe the pronunciation and create a MAW due to the phonetic differences between Mandarin and the dialect. Finally, a linguistic account of MAWs is proposed. The analysis of the database shows that MAWs, especially related to a loan word, undergo partial morphological adaptation to the Mandarin Chinese linguistic systems. However, more studies are needed to show the phonological adaptation of MAWs. Despite the above achieved objects, we have encountered difficulties conducting experiments due to Covid-19 since the end of 2019. We have designed an experiment collecting data on the use of MAWs of native Mandarin speakers to compare MAWs with lexical items with typical phonology and extraordinary sound. The experiment has unfortunately not been completed because of Covid-19. First, there was a high risk of visiting mainland China to recruit native Mandarin speakers during that time; and secondly, a technical issue was faced by the project assistant. Unavailable accessibility of Hong Kong and the policies of the University raised difficulties for the overseas project assistant to complete either data collection or data analysis without technical support of the language lab from 2019 to 2021. We have also planned the data collection process of Mandarin speaker’s speech. However, the experiment of modelling the phonological neighbourhood behaviour of MAWs with alternative tonal and segmental presentation paused because of the Covid-19.

15608618.label: Major findings and research outcome
15608618.value: We have constructed a database of Sina Mandarin Alphabetical Words (SMAW) including 406,739 MAWs which were extracted from Sina Weibo (Xiang et al., 2020). It is a more updated and balanced MAW list in simplified Chinese since the 2010s. This paper records the data retrieving technique and an elementary classification and analysis of the database MAWs. In this SMAW list, we have exhibited more diversified and productive lexical characteristics as compared with the existing corpora database. Compared to MAW in the 1990s (i.e. Chinese Gigaword Corpus), SMAW shows a higher diversity of word formation, grammatical roles and lexical meaning, and a wider range of syllables of a word. Comparing their length distribution, the mean length of MAWs in Gigaword Corpus is 3, but in SMAW in Web, the mean length is 5. We have also validated and confirmed the four main types of word formation of the MAWs proposed by Huang and Liu (2017), including AC, CA, CAC, and others, according to the position of the alphabet (A) and consonants (C). It is found that most MAWs are disyllabic compound words, which mostly follow the Mandarin lexical word formation rules (Xiang et al., 2020). However, SMAW may account for a wider grammatical roles since more verbs are found in the new list. In order to tackle the under-representation problem of MAW resources, this database also utilised search engine (i.e. Baidu), for MAW collection and refinement apart from the social media (i.e. Sina Weibo). This work proposes an innovative method of leveraging search engine (Baidu) for MAW candidates validation without manual mediation, and provides a unique MAW dataset that is most updated, scaled and comprehensive for adding into the existing lexicon and for enhancing the performance related NLP tasks, such as word segmentation. Overall, 1 journal article and 2 conference papers have been published. They focused on the data analysis of MAW (Xiang et al., 2020), Sentence Boundary Detection in Natural Language Processing from a financial perspective (Wan et al., 2019), and the formation of new Mandarin words (Dong & Huang, 2019).

15608618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15608618.value: For the development of the SMAW database, more information could be added to compile an integrated database. Data can be categorised by the MAW types in terms of its sources (loan words, Pinyin, brand names, etc.), grammatical categories (nouns, verbs, adjectives, etc.), IPA (onset, rhymes, etc.). Other than the SMAW database, an extension of our analysis of the data from Google is also valuable for the study of MAW. Google is a potential platform providing abundant data to support the modification of the constructed database. A further discussion on MAW phonologically could be conducted. The differences of both typical lexical units and non-lexical extraordinary units of MAW could be compared. Also, since this study shows that dialect influences the construction MAW, we should collect speech data from different dialect users. Moreover, the experiments that were affected by the Covid-19 can be conducted now, to further compare MAWs with lexical items with typical phonology and with extraordinary sound units, and to model phonological neighbourhood behaviour of MAWs, in terms of alternative tonal and segmental presentation, vis-à-vis the phonological neighbourhood of other attested Mandarin phonemes.

15608618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15608618.value: A database of Mandarin Alphabetical words (MAW), alphabetical words partly or fully used in Mandarin, has been constructed. It includes 406,739 MAWs extracted from Sina Weibo (SMAW). 2 experts verified by selecting a list of sample words to ensure the high preciseness of the database. Our study also identified the key vocabulary, length of the word, types of word formation and lexical diversity. It reflects the change of MAWs and identifies the differences among the words in newspapers and on social media by comparing the data with 2 MAWs databases, Web (SMAW) and Gigaword (constructed in the 1990s). A higher diversity and productiveness of MAWs could be found in the newer database.

15609018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609018.value: 本研究以兩本獨立刊物--《70年代雙周刊》和《黑鳥通訊》為主線，試圖深入討論1970年代到1990年代之間香港的文化與藝術生產中一條尚未細查的支流。在當時香港社會的背景之下，這條支流代表了一個由獨立出版物和社會運動團體構建起來的異議空間，這個空間不僅挑戰英國殖民主義和帝國主義的政治文化主導權，也同時挑戰由中國共產黨所定義的“左派思想”，以及以資本主義消費文化和大眾娛樂所佔領的“香港文化”。 初版於1970年，《70年代雙周刊》與同時期眾多獨立出版物的不同之處，在於其將各種內容融合在一起，包括介紹激進政治理論、社會運動動員、前衛藝術和本地藝術文學創作。雜誌於1970年代末期解散後，部分曾經的編輯人員加入了黑鳥樂隊，該樂隊於1984年成立。1990年，樂隊出版了一本名為《黑鳥通訊》的雜誌。一方面，《黑鳥通訊》繼承了《70年代》的反體制精神，內容繼續糅合政治討論和藝術。另一方面，黑鳥的成員還進一步在不同的傳播領域，如劇場、電影，當然最重要的是音樂領域活躍。 從《70年代》到《黑鳥通訊》的這二十年間的各種變化很好地體現了香港一段重要的另類文化歷史的形成過程。本研究以這兩本雜誌作為香港這一時期另類政治文化運動的匯合點，各種行動、辯論、感性共同體、藝術創作圍繞著這兩本雜誌生產、發生。這一研究將彌補目前有關香港反體制青年文化運動和文化政治空間產生的研究空白。借用Michael Warner的“反公共”（counterpublics）（2002）這一概念，即“一種與主流的文化環境和脈絡相左的公共領域”（Warner 2002:63），作為主要理論框架，本研究試圖探討在香港的語境中，這兩組活動者是如何在殖民主義、民族主義和主流左派佔主導地位的情況之下形成自己的認同，又是如何在消費主義的大眾媒體的影響下抵抗政治冷感的社會現實，以及如何為香港的年輕一代開創出新的共同體和獨立思考與行動的空間的。

15609018.label: Realisation of objectives
15609018.value: The project objectives 1-3 were well achieved. I have published an article titled "New Left without Old Left: The 70’s Biweekly and Youth Activism in 1970s Hong Kong" in one of the top China studies journals Modern China (48:5 (2022), 1080-1112.) I am also the chief editor of an edited volume "The 70's Biweekly: Social Activism and Alternative Cultural Production in 1970s Hong Kong", which is going to be published by Hong Kong University Press in 2023. In this volume, a wide range of topics related to the research are covered, thus fulling in all the revised objectives. I was responsible for writing an introduction and one of the chapters on the visual strategy of The 70's magazine. Another article on the group's cinematic practices is under review with the journal Cogent Arts & Humanities. The reason why the last objective was not fully achieved is because a more comprehensive and similar archive (https://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/mok/home/languages/en) was launched by HKBU shortly after I started my project. However, I have built up a private digital archive of all the materials (e.g. journals, student newspapers, pamphlets) published by young people in the 1970s Hong Kong based on my collection. I am happy to share it with any other scholars who would like to view them.

15609018.label: Major findings and research outcome
15609018.value: The major finding of the research is that the members of The 70’s could act together not because they embraced each other’s positions completely but because they found the great common ground behind these ideas. In the process of gathering, acting, and creating cultural entities such as magazines or films, they not only developed themselves outside the existing educational system, but they were also exploring and finding ways for young people to come together. In this sense, rather than searching for a clear definition of Hong Kong identity, they were forming a space of their own that belonged to their particular time and place. Another outstanding feature about The 70’s and its contemporaries was that its activities were not limited to textual debates or discussions but also included various direct political and cultural actions. The magazine had long positioned itself as an action-oriented magazine, for example, by organizing and encouraging the public to participate in protests, holding screenings of films related to social issues or politics, producing their own films, and running bookstores. The research outcomes after the mid-term report include: 1."New Left without Old Left: The 70’s Biweekly and Youth Activism in 1970s Hong Kong." Modern China 48:5 (2022), 1080-1112. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1177/00977004221091924 2.The 70's Biweekly: Social Activism and Alternative Cultural Production in 1970s Hong Kong, Hong Kong: Hong Kong University Press, in press, 2023. 3."Repertoire of Youth Activism in 1970s Hong Kong: The 70s Biweekly and Experimental Cinema", Cogent Arts & Humanities, under review.

15609018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15609018.value: The research project can develop further to pursue a broader picture of youth activism and alternative cultural production in the 1960s and 70s Hong Kong. As this is an understudied area of study, more research initiatives may benefit from the current research.

15609018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15609018.value: The 70s crystallises an important alternative cultural history of Hong Kong and its identity formation in the 1970s and beyond. By taking the magazine as a nodal point of social and cultural activism, from and around which actions, debates, community of sense and affect, artistic practices are formed and generated, this research fills the gaps in the studies on how Hong Kong young cultural producers carved out an alternative creative and political space to speak against the established authorities. The magazine’s efforts in challenging the political and cultural dominance of British colonialism and imperialism, Chinese nationalism and leftism as defined by the Chinese Community Party, and a Hong Kong culture forged largely by capitalistic consumerism and mass entertainment.

15609818.value: 1850年以來越南北方的客家社區：政治互動與民族關係

15609818.label: Project Objectives
15609818.value: To write a journal article to analyze the impact of bilateral relations between China and Vietnam on the Hakka in northern Vietnam, focusing on how the Hakka managed and manipulated the triangular interactions among the Hakka community, the Northern Vietnamese government and the Chinese government; To write a second journal article about the Hakka general Vong A Sang, analyzing his rise and fall as well as his ethnic and national identity in terms of his interactions with the multiple external forces: the Japanese invaders, the French Colonialists, the Chinese Nationalists, the Vietnamese Nationalists, and the Vietnamese Communists.

15609818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609818.value: This project intends to analyze the history of the Hakka community in northern Vietnam, focusing on its interactions with successive governments and other ethnic groups and its involvement in global historical events. Most members of this community were immigrants or their descendants who entered northern Vietnam after the outbreak of the Taiping Rebellion in the 1850’s, where they formed the largest Chinese subgroup. In the 19th and 20th centuries, they were involved in the war against the French conquest, the Pacific War, and all three Indochina wars. For political reasons, the French colonialists and the Vietnamese Communists worked hard to reshape the identities of the Hakka and to separate them from other Chinese subgroups. The French identified them as the Nung people and even allowed them to create their own autonomous region. In the late 1950s, the Vietnamese Communists decided to rename them the Han people to differentiate them from the urban Chinese, who were known as Hoa Kieu. After the exodus of many Chinese from Vietnam in the late 1970s, those Hakka who chose to stay in Vietnam were officially re-identified as the Hoa people. The unique features and experiences of the Hakka community in northern Vietnam will form the central themes of this project. Specifically, I will analyze the reasons behind the Hakka’s move to Vietnam, and examine the motivations of the French colonialists and the Vietnamese Communists to separate them from other Chinese subgroups. I will trace the origins of the alliance between the Hakka community and the Vietnamese Nationalists and Communists, and explore how the changing relationship between the People's Republic of China and Vietnam impacted on the Hakka community. I will analyze the relations between the Hakka community and other subgroups of Chinese in northern Vietnam as well as the influence of such interactions on the Hakka identity. This project will result in four journal articles, a continuation of the series of articles about the Chinese in northern Vietnam that I have already published. They eventually will form part of a book manuscript I will prepare on the history of the Chinese in northern Vietnam. The experience of the urban Chinese has been sufficiently studied, but that of the rural Hakka has remained a missing piece in the narrative. As I will explain below, it is now time to fill this important void. 本項研究的主題為越南北方的客家社區，重點分析客家群體與中越歷屆政府和其他族群的關係，以及他們在全球性歷史事件中的作用。客家人主要在太平天國之後陸續移居越南北方，並成為當地最大的華人群體。在19和20世紀，他們參與了反法戰爭、太平洋戰爭和三次印度支那戰爭。 出於政治考量，法國殖民政府和越南共產黨政府都曾致力於重塑客家人的認同以便把他們與其他華人群體分開。法國人稱他們為儂人并允許他們建立自治區。二十世紀五十年代末，北越政府稱他們為漢族，以便把他們和城市中的華僑分開。二十世紀七十年代末大批華人離開越南后，留在越南的客家人被重新識別為艾族或華族。 本項研究將重點考察北越客家社區的特點和特殊經歷，包括客家人移居越南的原因，法國殖民政府和北越共產黨政府重塑客家認同的動機，客家社區與越南民族主義運動和共產主義運動的關係，中越關係對客家社區的影響，以及客家人與其他華人群體的關係及其對客家認同的影響。 本研究項目為作者已經發表的相關研究的繼續，預期成果為兩篇論文。這些論文最終將發展為一部有關北越華僑華人歷史的專著。北越都市的華僑華人已經得到研究者的重視，但農村地區的客家人則尚未得到應有的關注。本項研究將有助於填補這項空白。

15610218.label: Project Objectives
15610218.value: to identify the social needs of the elderly, their preferences and usage patterns of community facilities in the local neighbourhood; to evaluate the key urban planning parameters (availability, diversity, accessibility) of community facilities to enhance their utilization and their satisfaction level of the local neighbourhood by the elderly; to formulate a framework of key planning considerations for community facilities to support ageing in place by involving elderly people, professionals in related fields and urban planners; to develop a set of factors to provide guidance for planners to enhance the planning of community facilities to encourage ageing in place

15610218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610218.value: Given the trend of rapid population ageing, existing community facilities in a neighbourhood often do not fully support the needs of the elderly people and their desire to age in place. Current planning and design guidelines primarily focus on the quantity of community facilities and little is known about elderly preferences, use patterns and how satisfied they are with their neighbourhoods. Previous studies found that certain built environment attributes have been associated with elderly neighborhood satisfaction. However, the majority of these studies were conducted in western cities which have very different urban densities, degrees of car dependence, and culture compared to Asian cities. In addition, few studies have investigated the lifestyle patterns and special needs of the elderly and specifically focused on how the planning of community facilities can enhance neighbourhood satisfaction to support the concept of ageing in place. Hong Kong is one of the Asian dense urban cities facing immense pressure on redevelopment. High proportion of the elderly population is concentrated in old urban districts, largely because the housing is relatively affordable and where they have familiar social connections developed over their lifetime. Thus, responsive planning and design to enhance accessibility to diverse community facilities in old neighbourhoods is extremely important. This proposed study focuses on the role of community facilities in enhancing the local neighbourhood to facilitate the preference of ageing in place. It intends to identify the key planning considerations of community facilities that can enhance elderly neighbourhood satisfaction. This study will employ objective methods using GPS tracking device and GIS mapping to capture and analyze the use patterns of community facilities by the elderly and their spatial characteristics in the neighbourhood. Subjective evaluation of neighbourhood satisfaction with both the physical and social aspects of the neighbourhood environment will conducted via a questionnaire survey. The study will contribute to a better theoretical understanding of the association between the planning of community facilities and the elderly neighbourhood satisfaction, particularly in dense old urban areas. It will provide a framework of key planning considerations for community facilities to support ageing in place.The findings of this study will establish a set of key factors that can provide guidance for urban planners and decision-makers to make better planning of community facilities to meet the citizens' desire to age in place. 當前快速老齡化的背景下，現有鄰里中的社區設施通常無法完全滿足長者的需求以及對居家安老的期望。現有的規劃標準與準則主要關注社區設施的數量，而較少關注長者的喜好，使用模式以及他們對社區的滿意度。 過去的研究發現，某些建成環境要素與長者的社區滿意度息息相關。然而，大量的此類研究是在西方城市進行，這些城市在城市密度、汽車依賴度和文化上與亞洲城市有著很大差異。此外，很少有研究調查長者的生活模式和特殊需求，並特別關注社區設施的規劃如何提高社區滿意度以支持居家安老。 香港是亞洲高密度城市之一，並面臨巨大的重建壓力。大量的長者生活在城市舊區中，很大程度上因為相對可負擔的房價以及熟悉的社會關係。因此，通過回應式規劃設計來提高舊社區中多種社區設施的可達性至關重要。 本研究關注社區設施在改善當地社區並促進居家安老的喜好中的作用。本研究旨在發現可以提高長者社區滿意度的社區設施規劃的關鍵因素。本研究將採用客觀方法，使用GPS追蹤設備和GIS來捕捉和分析長者社區設施的使用模式及其在社區中的空間特徵。同時，本研究也將通過問卷調查對社區環境的物理與社會層面進行社區滿意度的主觀評價。 本研究有助於更好地理解社區設施規劃和長者社區滿意度之間的關係，特別是在高密度的城市舊區中。本研究將會提供一個社區設施規劃考量因素的框架以支援長者居家安老。本研究的結果將建立一系列關鍵因素，為城市規劃者和決策者提供指導，以便更好地規劃社區設施，以滿足市民對居家安老的需求。

15610218.label: Realisation of objectives
15610218.value: Objective 1) The research project has identified the social needs of the older people, their preferences and usage patterns of community facilities in the local neighbourhood. 9 expert interviews were conducted to shortlist the key planning considerations of community facilities to support ageing in place in local neighbourhood. In addition, 15 focus groups in elderly centers in Kwun Tong and Shum Shui Po in Hong Kong to identify elderly needs and preferences on ageing in place in local neighbourhood. NVivo 10 software was used to analysis the results from the focus group meetings. Besides, 105 elderly from Kwun Tong and Shum Shui Po district were participate in the GPS tracking exercise and their out-of-home daily travels routes and destinations were tracked. The GPS tracking shows the usage patterns and moving patterns of the older people, in particular, the specific community facilities they visit in their daily lives. The travel patterns of the elderly also show the distance from their home which they travel for different activities. This study found that older people most frequently visit elderly centers and open space. In addition, for the purpose of using community facilities, doing physical exercise or gaining knowledge were found as two most frequently mentioned purposes. Regarding the spatial-temporal characteristics of using community facilities, older people mostly walk to the community facility in the local neighborhood. 30 minutes’ walking distance is acceptable. In addition, older people usually visit open spaces in the morning and the activity duration is around 1 to 2 hours. Furthermore, older people were found to usually visit elderly center in the morning or depend on the activity organized by the center. Thus, their visiting time and stay length both depend on the activities. Planning and design of community facilities was found to be the main concern for older people when deciding whether to visit community facilities, and they mainly focus on the diversity (42.1%) and size (26.3%) of the community facility. Built environment is another important issue that may affect older people’s use of community facility, especially the walking environment around community facility, such as pedestrian safety (31.6%) and barrier free design (26.3%). Objective 2) The key urban planning parameters (availability, diversity, accessibility) of community facilities to enhance their utilization and their satisfaction level of the local neighbourhood by the elderly were evaluated. The questionnaire survey with 509 older people, and the GPS survey with 105 older people were conducted to evaluate different planning parameters. Moreover, the key characteristics of the older people participants’ neighbourhoods including Availability: number and location, spatial concentration; Diversity; and Accessibility were recorded and analyzed by GIS spatial analysis using ArcGIS software. This set of spatial data provides better understanding of the urban planning parameters for planning and design of community facilities in the neighbourhood. This study found that older people’s usage and frequency of visiting community facilities mainly depended on the purpose of the visits and the activities the facilities provided rather than the planning and design quality variables. In addition, the factors explaining older people’s length of stay varied across the different types of community facilities. This study also suggested that older people’s satisfaction level with using community facilities was mainly associated with the planning and design quality of the facilities rather than the purpose of visitation or usage pattern. It identifies the walking environment and public transport as key mobility elements that support older people’s usage of community facilities. In addition, older people’s individual consideration, age and gender are associated with older people’s usage and satisfaction with community facilities. Furthermore, this study highlighted that older people’s physical and psychological well-being was more clearly and more strongly related to their satisfaction level with using different types of community facilities. The perceived built environment of community, land use diversity and elderly proportion of neighborhood may affect older people’s neighborhood satisfaction and well-being through affecting their usage of community facility resources. Objective 3) A framework of key planning considerations for community facilities to support ageing in place was formulated by involving elderly people, professionals in related fields and urban planners has been developed. Interviews with 7 participants including researchers, planners and policy makers from architecture, urban planning, public health and gerontology area were conducted at the final stage of the research. Key findings from the different stages of the research including questionnaire surveys, GPS tracking were the basis for discussion and refinement of the framework. The study proposes a comprehensive framework of community facility to support aging-in-place. It was indicated that the provision of community facility resources indirectly affects older people’s well-being through affecting their usage of and satisfaction with community facility. The planning and design quality of community facilities were associated with older adult’s satisfaction levels with community facilities and well-being. Mobility has been identified as an important capability element that affects older people’s use of community facilities and well-being, especially walking environment and out-of-home activity level. The perceived built environment is identified as the significant conversion factor that helps older people to convert community facility resources to well-being. Thus, the community facility planning should not only focus on the provision of community facilities, but also the planning and design quality of community facilities. Mobility (mainly walking environments) and the built environment of community should also be paid attention to. Objective 4) The study developed a set of factors to provide guidance for planners to enhance the planning of community facilities to encourage ageing in place. Through survey and discussion with older people, experts and policy makers, the study proposed the specific planning and design factors of six types of community facilities to promote older people’s usage of community facilities and well-being. The six types of community facilities are commercial facility, community service facility, cultural facility, municipal facility, leisure facility and religious facility. Planners should also pay attention to mobility, especially planning and design of walking environments and public transport, to support older people’s access to community facilities. Regarding built environment, planners could focus on barrier-free design, design for all-weather conditions, cleanliness, aesthetic, land use diversity and elderly proportion of the neighborhood.
