16101418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101418.value: 在真核細胞中，微管作為細胞質結構體系的組織者排列成高度有序的陣列，從而在多種細胞活動中發揮關鍵作用，其中包括細胞內運輸，細胞器定位，細胞分裂和形態形成。微管的組織由復雜的機制調節，而該機制依賴於被稱為γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物的一種環狀結構。這種環狀復合物由多個γ-微管蛋白和其他γ-復合蛋白（GCPs）組成，其功能是啟動微管生長並介導微管附著於微管組織中心（例如中心體）。到目前為止，對γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物的結構和調節特性仍然知之甚少。 在過去幾年中，我的研究室發現了幾種參與調控γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物的亞細胞定位和活性的蛋白質，其中包括CDK5RAP2和DNA聚合酶δ催化亞基，這兩種蛋白質分別被鑒定為γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物的活化劑和抑制劑。我們近期的研究發現，γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物的組分蛋白質GCP6充當該復合物誘導微管成核的抑制劑，然而該環狀復合物的其它特異性GCP組分並沒有這樣的功能。我們還發現當細胞從分裂間期進入有絲分裂期時，γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物經歷GCP6化學計量的增加以及微管成核活性的降低。值得注意的是，在細胞分裂周期的間期中相當一部分γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物並不含有GCP6。綜上所述，我們的研究結果顯示GCP6是一種新的γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物抑制劑，並以依賴於細胞周期的方式調節該復合物的活性。在本項研究計劃中，我們提出以下研究來分析GCP6在γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物中的調節作用：（1）解析GCP6對該復合物抑制作用的特性，（2）揭示GCP6對該復合物抑制的機制，（3）闡明該GCP6介導的抑制在細胞周期中對微管組織的作用。 本項計劃中提出的研究旨在揭示一種先前未知的抑制γ-微管蛋白環狀復合物活性的機制，從研究中獲得的信息將使我們能夠更好地了解該復合物在細胞周期中功能和調節的特性。由於該復合物是細胞微管的主要成核體，本項工作將推進我們對依賴於微管的多種細胞活動的分子機制的認知。此外，微管組織的缺陷涉及許多疾病，而微管已成為癌症的主要治療靶點，本項計劃工作中獲得的知識具有確定新靶點、從而發展新治療方法的潛力。

16101418.label: Realisation of objectives
16101418.value: Objective #1. To characterize the inhibitory effect of GCP6 on γTuRCs We have fulfilled this objective by characterizing the association of GCP6 with γTuRCs and the inhibition of γTuRCs by GCP6. First, we examined whether the addition of GCP6 affect γTuRC assembly in a reconstitution assay. After incubation of isolated γTuRCs with and without recombinant GCP6 at an excessive amount, we centrifuged the γTuRCs over a sucrose gradient (5-40%). After centrifugation, γTuRCs incubated in the absence of recombinant GCP6 appeared as ~2.2-MDa species; this agrees with that in the published reports. The incubation with recombinant GCP6 did not change the migration behavior of γTuRCs over the gradient, indicating that the reconstitution with recombinant GCP6 did not affect the integrity of γTuRC structure. To examine whether GCP6 overexpression alters the nucleation activity of γTuRC, we first performed microtubule on-beads nucleation assay in vitro. We isolated γTuRC from cells with or without induced GCP6 overexpression by utilizing the specific interaction with CDK5RAP2 1–100. The overexpression of GCP6 and integrity of γTuRC were checked by western blotting. We then test the effect of GCP6 on γTuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation. Notably, overexpression of GCP6 inhibited γTuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation. We further assessed the potency and specificity of the inhibition in microtubule nucleation assay of isolated γTuRCs. Recombinant GCP6 was expressed in HEK293T and isolated at high purity through its affinity tag, and γTuRCs were purified from mammalian cell cultures using our reported protocol (Choi and Qi, Methods Enzymol., 540:119-30). In the nucleation assay, GCP6 inhibited γTuRCs in a dose-dependent manner, with the IC50 value being ~12 nM and ~80% of the nucleating activity being inhibited at 20 nM GCP6. As comparison, we prepared recombinant GCP4 in the same manner as GCP6 and tested the GCP4 protein in the nucleation assay; we found that GCP4 did not affect the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs even if the GCP4 protein was added at 40 nM. This result agrees with those obtained from a microtubule regrowth assay in which we overexpressed GCP 4-6 and found that overexpressed GCP6 blocked centrosome-based microtubule regrowth, but overexpressed GCP4 and GCP5 did not. Among γTuRC-specific GCP proteins, GCP6 possesses the unique property of inhibiting γTuRC activity. Objective #2. To identify the mechanism by which GCP6 inhibits γTuRCs We have fulfilled this objective by carrying out the following assays. GCP 2-6 harbor the GRIP1 and GRIP2 motifs located at the amino- and carboxy-termini, respectively. GCP6 contain a long middle region (~800 a.a.) that is absent in other GCPs. We investigated the function of this middle region and found that in immunoprecipitation assays, the construct of this middle region bound to Nme7, a γTuRC component that is required for the microtubule-nucleating activity. Furthermore, our binding assays showed that within γTuRCs, Nme7 binds to GCP6. To find out how γTuRCs are regulated by GCP6, we isolated γTuRCs by exploiting the specific interaction with CDK5RAP2 1–100 and Nedd1 579–667, which are the γTuRC binding domains of CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1, respectively. The amount of Nme7 was decreased upon GCP6 overexpression in both CDK5RAP2 1–100 and Nedd1 579–667 binding γTuRCs. To narrow down the binding site of Nme7 in GCP6, we tried a series of GCP6 fragments for binding assay. The binding region could be locked within 760–1502. Based on the sequence information of GCP6, around 990–1415 were the 9 internal repeats. Therefore, we divided 760–1502 into three parts 761–1040, 1041–1273, 1274–1505 and tested their binding ability to endogenous Nme7 (Figure 5A). The GFP tagged fragments transiently expressed in 293T cells were immunoprecipitated through the ectopic tag, and the coimmunoprecipitated Nme7 was examined. Fragment 760–1040 displayed strong binding activity to Nme7. These results suggest that Nme7 localizes to γTuRC through binding to GCP6 and delocalizing Nme7 from γTuRCs to reduce γTuRC activity. γ-Tubulin has the intrinsic self-polymerizing property, and 3D reconstructions have revealed that γ-tubulins interact laterally within filaments which closely match the lateral interaction of tubulins in microtubule lattice. We found that the C-terminal region containing GRIP2 motif of GCP6 promotes γ-tubulin polymerization in vivo and in vitro. In full-length GCP6, this promotional function is blocked by the N-terminal region. For the first time, we showed that the GRIP2 motif is not only responsible for the binding to γ-tubulin but also regulate the function of γ-tubulin. CDK5RAP2 is a γTuRC stimulator and contains a γTuRC-stimulating domain that is conserved in the γTuRC-binding proteins of lower eukaryotes, and this CDK5RAP2 domain was referred to as the γTuRC-mediated nucleation activator (γTuNA). In addition, Nedd1 is an anchoring protein of γTuRCs on centrosomes and harbors a γTuRC-binding region that is different from the γTuNA. To probe whether γTuRC saturation with GCP6 affects the γTuRC binding to CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1, we induced GCP6 overexpression in the above-mentioned hTERT RPE-1 cell lines and then tested the binding of the CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1 to the γTuRCs in a pulldown assay. As control, we performed the pulldown of γTuRCs from the extracts of cells without induced GCP6 expression. By comparing the amounts of γTuRCs pulled down from these cell extracts, we found that the GCP6 overexpression did not affect the binding of γTuRCs to CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1. Therefore, CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1 bind to GCP6-saturated γTuRCs. Objective #3. To reveal the role of GCP6-mediated γTuRC inhibition in microtubule organization during the cell cycle We have fulfilled this objective by examining the effects of altering GCP6 expression levels on cellular microtubules. To investigate the function of GCP6 to γTuRC, we analyzed the effect of GCP6 on centrosomal microtubule regrowth. GCP4 and GCP6 were ectopically expressed in cell cultures. The expression levels were detected by western blotting and were significantly higher than endogenous proteins. Microtubule regrowth assay was performed after cold-induced depolymerization. At 8 s of regrowth, an obvious centrosomal microtubule asters formed in control cells and cells overexpressed GCP4. However, only sparser microtubules were found in GCP6 overexpressed cells and the centrosomal microtubule intensity was ~50% less compared to control cells. To rule out the possibility that GCP6 overexpression delocalizes γTuRC from centrosome. We overexpressed GFP tagged GCP6 in hTERT-RPE1 cells, and checked the centrosomal intensity of γ-tubulin. The quantification result showed that it was similar to control group. Taken together, overexpression of GCP6 inhibits centrosomal microtubule regrowth without disrupting the integrity and centrosomal localization of γTuRCs. To determine whether GCP6 controls microtubule regrowth at the Golgi complex, we performed Golgi-based microtubule regrowth assay. Because cell-cell variation of Golgi-based microtubule regrowth was large, we used inducible expression cell line here to minimize the experimental error. After ~20 h induction of GFP-GCP6 by doxycycline, the microtubule regrowth assay was performed. At 5s of regrowth, multiple Golgi-derived short microtubules were observed in control cells. Nevertheless, in GCP6 overexpressing cells, only few microtubules were observed. This result indicates that GCP6 controls the γTuRC nucleation activity at Golgi complex. In summary, the presence of an excess of GCP6 inhibits the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs through sequestration of Nme7, a peripheral factor of γTuRCs that promotes γTuRC activity. The inhibition compromises the microtubule-organizing function of centrosomes and the Golgi, which are the major organizing centers of cellular microtubules.

16101418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101418.value: γTuRCs are the principal microtubule nucleator in animal cells. Being the longest GCP, GCP6 plays a vital role in several cellular processes, including the attachment of γTuRCs to intermediate filaments. Our work here identified a previously unknown function of GCP6 and a mechanism by which γTuRCs are regulated. We found that GCP6 acts as an inhibitor of γTuRC. Ectopically expressed GCP6 inhibits centrosome-based and Golgi-based microtubule regrowth while GCP4 and GCP5 do not have such function. Furthermore, GCP6 overexpression inhibited γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation by in vitro assay. Based on these results, it is proposed that GCP6 can regulate γTuRC activities through delocalizing peripheral components. We found that GCP6 is the binding site of the γTuRC regulator Nme7 and the binding site locates between 760-990 in GCP6. We also found that Nme7 was delocalized upon GCP6 overexpression, which indicates that some peripheral components might be recruited to γTuRC by GCP6. This idea was supported by the binding assay which confirms the binding site of Nme7 in GCP6 is 761-1040 which does not contain the published phosphorylation sites. Therefore, the middle part of GCP6 may serve as the scaffold and recruits other peripheral components during γTuRC assembly process. GCP6 overexpression inhibited centrosome- and Golgi-derived microtubule regrowth in vivo. γTuRCs isolated from GCP6-overexpressed cells also shows a low microtubule nucleation activity in vitro. And this inhibition function is not caused by delocalizing or disassembly of γTuRC. Collectively, these results suggest that GCP6 performs crucial role in γTuRC assembly process and also in the regulation of γTuRC function. γ-Tubulin complex proteins (GCP2–6) belongs to a conserved family which contain two homologous GRIP motifs. Here, we show that the C-terminal region of GCP6 which contains GRIP2 motif, promotes γ-tubulin polymerizing to a filament structure. In full-length GCP6, this function of the C-terminal region is autoinhibited. Using a chimera that combined of N- and C-terminal regions from different GCP6, we showed that the C-terminal function is controlled by N-terminal region. Notably, the GCP6 N-terminal binds to C-terminal region to inhibit its function. Collectively, these results indicate that the C-terminal region of GCP6 regulates the function of γ-tubulin and controlled by N-terminal region. Overall, this study provides new molecular insights into a wide variety of cellular functions including cell division, movement, and morphogenesis. In addition, this work reveals a new function of GCP6.

16101418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101418.value: It has been shown that GCP6 is a substrate of Polo-like kinase 4 (Plk4) and the phosphorylation regulates centriole duplication. The findings of this project also warrant further investigation of the GCP6 phosphorylation in the regulation of GCP6 function. In addition, systematic identification of proteins that interacts with GCP6 will help in understanding how GCP6 exerts its function. We will then demonstrate the identified interactions in vitro and in vivo and assemble protein networks associated with GCP6 in certain cellular contexts. Demonstration of the identified interactions will delineate the functional networks in which GCP6 participates. Our current findings warrant the investigation of GCP6 expression in different cell types and tissues. It is likely that the level of GCP6 is relatively low in certain cancer cells, which allows an active nucleation activity of γTuRCs for cell proliferation. The aberrant expression of GCP6 in cancer may serve as a biomarker. With such information, one would analyze the deregulation of GCP6 in carcinogenesis and cancer development. Results derived from such analysis would facilitate understanding of the molecular basis of cancer progression.

16101418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101418.value: In animal cells, γ-tubulin ring complexes (γTuRCs) are the principal nucleators of cellular microtubules and mediate microtubule nucleation and anchoring at microtubule-organizing centers, such as centrosomes and the Golgi complex. γTuRCs are assembled as a macromolecular structure whose core components are γ-tubulin and five other γ-complex proteins (GCPs), GCP 2–6. By using a wide range of approaches, we investigated the function of GCP6, which is the largest GCP and contains a middle region that is absent in other GCPs. We demonstrated that GCP6 inhibits the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs. Furthermore, GCP6 controls microtubule growth at centrosomes and the Golgi complex. Mechanistically, we revealed that the unique middle region of GCP6 interacts with Nme7, which is a regulator of γTuRC activity, and that the presence of an excess of GCP6 sequesters Nme7 from γTuRC, which interferes with γTuRC activation. Overall, the functional determination of GCP6 allows us to progress on understanding the control mechanisms of microtubule nucleation and array organization during various cellular activities. Moreover, understanding the molecular mechanisms that control microtubule organization may lead to new drug targets for various human diseases, including cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.

16101518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101518.value: Neurodegenerative disease is characterized by incurable, progressive diseases with similar pathogenic features, including protein aggregation and neuronal death. Huntington’s disease (HD) is a neurodegenerative disease caused by the expansion of CAG repeats in the huntingtin (HTT) gene, leading to the loss of neurons initially in the striatum and cortex. Given the extremely high penetrance of the underlying genetic abnormality, HD is a robust model disease for investigating common neurodegeneration mechanisms and testing new therapeutic targets. However, the mechanism underlying the selective neurodegeneration in the striatum and cortex in HD is poorly understood. Recently, we found that the release of presynaptic neurotransmitters from cortical and striatal neurons is altered in a mouse model of HD prior to the onset of symptoms, suggesting a causative role of synaptic transmission in HD. However, the dynamic properties of single synaptic vesicles in HD have not been investigated. We built a state-of-the-art tracking microscope with real-time three-dimensional (3D) nanometer-accuracy, enabling us to track a single synaptic vesicle loaded with a single fluorescent quantum dot (QD) with ~20-30-nm accuracy in the x-y plane and along the z-axis. Using this microscope, we investigated the exocytosis (i.e., release) and mobility of single synaptic vesicles in live neurons. We found that synaptic vesicles from the readily releasable pool (RRP) of most excitatory synapses reside close to their fusion site, and we found that the fusion mode depends largely upon the vesicle’s location relative to the active zone. Our next step is to use this powerful setup to measure the dynamics of single synaptic vesicles in HD. Our hypothesis is that in HD, the dynamics of single synaptic vesicles are altered in the most vulnerable neurons. To test this hypothesis, we will measure synaptic vesicle dynamics in both striatal and cortical neurons in two mouse models of HD using a real-time 3D tracking microscope, electron microscopy, and electrophysiology. Using these tools, we will measure the exocytosis and mobility of single synaptic vesicles in mature cortical neurons in HD mice, as well as single inhibitory synaptic vesicles in striatal neurons, which are primarily inhibitory. Our results will provide key insight into an important—yet currently unanswered—question in HD: how are the dynamics of single synaptic vesicles altered in the earliest affected neurons? Our results will also increase our understanding of the mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration and will be used to identify novel therapeutic targets for HD and other neurodegenerative diseases. 神經退行性疾​​病的特徵在於具有相似致病特徵的無法治癒的進行性疾病，包括蛋白質聚集和神經元死亡。亨廷頓病（HD）是由亨廷頓（HTT）基因中CAG重複的擴增引起的神經退行性疾​​病，導致最初在紋狀體和皮質中的神經元丟失。鑑於潛在遺傳異常的極高外顯率，HD是一種強大的模型疾病，用於研究常見的神經變性機制和測試新的治療靶點。然而，人們對HD中紋狀體和皮質中選擇性神經變性的潛在機制知之甚少。最近，我們發現在症狀出現之前，HD小鼠模型中皮質和紋狀體神經元的突觸前神經遞質的釋放被改變，這表明突觸傳遞在HD中的致病作用。然而，尚未研究HD中單個突觸小泡的動態特性。 我們建立了具有實時三維（3D）納米精度的最先進的跟踪顯微鏡，使我們能夠跟踪單個突觸囊泡，其中裝載有單個熒光量子點（QD）在xy平面和沿Z軸有20 – 30 nm 的精度。使用該顯微鏡，我們研究了活神經元中單個突觸小泡的胞吐作用（即釋放）和移動性。我們發現來自大多數興奮性突觸的易於釋放的池（RRP）的突觸小泡位於其融合位點附近，並且我們發現融合模式在很大程度上取決於囊泡相對於活性區的位置。我們的下一步是使用這個功能強大的設置來測量HD中單個突觸小泡的動態。 我們的假設是，在HD中，單個突觸小泡的動力學在最脆弱的神經元中發生改變。為了驗證這一假設，我們將使用實時3D跟踪顯微鏡，電子顯微鏡和電生理學測量兩種HD小鼠模型中紋狀體和皮質神經元中的突觸小泡動力學。使用這些工具，我們將測量HD小鼠成熟皮質神經元中單個突觸小泡的胞吐作用和移動性，以及紋狀體神經元中的單個抑制性突觸小泡，其主要是抑制性的。 我們的研究結果將提供關於HD中一個重要但尚未解決的問題的關鍵見解：在最早受影響的神經元中，單個突觸小泡的動力學是如何改變的？我們的結果還將增加我們對神經變性潛在機制的理解，並將用於鑑定HD和其他神經退行

16101718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101718.value: Cells employ an elaborate set of processes by which they transport proteins between their various functionally interconnected organelles. Central to these processes is the requirement to discriminate among the many hundreds of proteins present in one location in the cell and to selectively transport only a small fraction of them to another location. This process or phenomena is called protein sorting. We are particularly interested in the process of protein sorting at the Golgi – an organelle found in all cells (excluding bacteria) – which functions as the cells protein sorting “hub”. We propose to investigate features of a central player in protein sorting at the Golgi – a protein known as Sed5p. Sed5p functions together with a small group of similar proteins called SNAREs. The role of SNAREs is to act as organellar gate keepers – as SNAREs are required for protein transport from one location to another. With a more complete understanding of the function of Sed5p, we hope to be able to better grasp how the cells establish and maintain the compositional and functional integrity of its organelles as abnormalities in the underlying processes are often the hallmarks of human disease. 细胞中各种细胞器会采用一系列精密复杂的蛋白质运输通路来达到各细胞器之间功能的协同。 这些细胞内蛋白转运通路需要从细胞内的一个位置的成百上千的蛋白质中准确挑选出其中很小的一部分蛋白质并将其转运到其他位置。这个过程就叫做细胞蛋白分选。该过程是细胞蛋白转运通路的核心。在众多的细胞器当中，我们对于高尔基体当中的蛋白质分选机理尤其感兴趣。高尔基体是细胞里蛋白分选的枢纽，它广泛分布在各种真核细胞当中。我们提议对于在高尔基体上蛋白分选过程中发挥核心作用的一个蛋白Sed5p开展研究。Sed5p隶属于可溶性N-乙基马来亚胺敏感受体（SNAREs）蛋白质家族，它与其他的可溶性N-乙基马来亚胺敏感受体共同作用，来完成蛋白质从一个地方运输到另一个地方的过程。因为其在细胞蛋白转运中的不可或缺性，可溶性N-乙基马来亚胺敏感受体也被认为是细胞器蛋白转运的守门人。因此，我们想更加详尽地探究并了解Sed5p的功能，从而更好地了解细胞是如何达到各个细胞器成分上的动态平衡从而建立功能上的完整性。很多人类疾病都是因为标志性的细胞器功能完整性缺失而造成的，我们也希望通过对于Sed5p的研究来了解并最终治疗一些人类疾病。

16101718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101718.value: This research proposal has led a detailed molecular insight into the mechanisms by which the Golgi resident syntaxin SNARE is sorted to and retained in the Golgi. This work has been published by the journal Traffic in 2020. Part of this study examined the role of the syntaxin binding protein – Sly1p – in the retention of Sed5p and the relationship between these two proteins was used to make the unexpected finding that the Sly1p-binding domain of Sed5p can function in trans with the remainder of Sed5p. This work, the resulting collaboration with the Merz laboratory at the University of Washington in Seattle has been reviewed, revised and in now undergoing an addition round of review with the Journal of Cell Biology.

16101718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101718.value: One of the principal reasons for using yeast as a model organism with which to study fundamental questions in Cell Biology lies in its tractable genetics. Over the last 25 years my laboratory has leveraged the genetics of budding yeast cells to great effect. Using a conditional allele of SED5 the Golgi SNARE SFT1 was identified, and with SFT1 we were able to identify (amongst other genes) VPS74. Vps74p functions as a receptor for certain Golgi resident membrane proteins – many of which are enzymes that function in this organelle. With VPS74 we were able to identify novel machineries that function similarly encoded by the BRE5 and UBP3 genes which together encode a de-ubiquitinase that acts on the Golgi vesicle coat complex termed coatomer. We have and will continue to leverage yeast genetics and the genetic interactions between the genes that encode important functional constituents of the Golgi to fuel a deeper understanding the organization and function of the Golgi and how membrane protein residents are retained there.

16101718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101718.value: Cells are comprised of several membrane-delimited comparts each of which harbors a unique collection of proteins and lipids which confer compositional identify as well as define the biochemical function of the compartment. An intracellular compartment of particular interest is the Golgi. The Golgi functions as the protein sorting / logistics hub of the cell. Protein retention and the transport of proteins and lipids into and out of the Golgi is intimately linked to the biogenesis and homeostasis of this sorting hub of eukaryotic cells. Of particular importance are membrane proteins that mediate membrane fusion events with and within the Golgi—the Soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs). In the Golgi of budding yeast cells, the syntaxin SNARE Sed5p oversees membrane fusion events. Determining how Sed5p is localized to and trafficked within the Golgi is critical to informing our understanding of the mechanism(s) of biogenesis and homeostasis of this organelle. Here we establish that the steady-state localization of Sed5p to the Golgi appears to be primarily conformation-based relying on intra-molecular associations between the Habc domain and SNARE-motif while its tribasic COPI-coatomer binding motif plays a role in intra-Golgi retention.

rows: Investigation of the role of E2F4 in BAT formation in vivo.

16101918.label: Realisation of objectives
16101918.value: 1. To investigate the role of E2F4 in brown adipose tissue (BAT) development and activity, we first tried to delineate cell fate determination mechanisms of Pax7+ mesoderm progenitors that give rise to both skeletal muscle and BAT in embryonic mice. In our collaboration with Prof. Angela WU (HKUST), we profiled single cell transcriptomics of YFP+ cells sorted from tamoxifen-treated Pax7CreER:R26R-stop-EYFP embryos at E12.5, E14.5, and E16.5. We found that within Pax7+ progenies, the myogenic lineage first arises at E12.5 while a newly-characterized bipotent cell population (Pdgfra+/Thy1+) commits into dermal lineage with Twist2 expression at E14.5 or brown adipogenic lineage with Ppara expression at E16.5. This study provided detailed temporal characterization of fate switch patterns of Pax7+ progenitors during development (Fung, et al., Cell Discovery, 2022). Next, we generated Pax7-Cre:E2F4flox/flox mice as Pax7-expressing cells were able to commit into brown adipogenic lineage as shown above. Interscapular BAT in both control and E2F4 knockout (KO) mice were examined but no obvious difference was found. By lineage tracing, we and others found that Myf5- expressing cells contributed to BAT more efficiently than Pax7-expressing cells (Berry, et al., Nat Commun. 2016). Thus, we also generated Myf5-Cre:E2F4flox/flox mice. Briefly, BAT samples were dissected from new born E2F4-KOMyf5 and Ctrl mice and subjected to weight measuring and H&E staining. No obvious difference was observed in BAT development in both E2F4 KO and the control mice. Moreover, adult E2F4- KO(Myf5) and Ctrl mice were subjected to cold treatment for 7d (6°C) and subsequently BATs were isolated and subjected to H&E staining or RT-qPCR for measurement of mRNA levels of selected thermogenic genes (e.g. Prdm16, Ucp1). No significant difference was observed. The above results suggest that the embryonic development of BAT or its activation upon cold stimulation in adulthood is not affected by E2F4 deletion. 2. To examine the role of E2F4 in white adipose tissue (WAT) browning under cold stimulation, we also generated Adiponectin-Cre:E2F4flox/flox mice (E2F4-KO(adq) to induce E2F4 deletion in mature adipocytes of both BAT and WAT. We analyzed inguinal WAT (ingWAT) after subjecting E2F4-KOadq and Ctrl mice to 6°C cold treatment for 7d. H&E staining showed similar browning effect (i.e. appearance of multilocular beige adipocytes). RT-qPCR measurement of selected thermogenic gene expression (e.g. Prdm16, Ucp1) revealed no obvious difference in ingWAT between E2F4-KO(adq) and Ctrl mice. 3. Since PDGFRa+ adipogenic progenitors (APCs) residing in stromal vasculature of fat tissues also contribute to white fat browning, we next generated PDGFRa- Cre:E2F4flox/flox line (E2F4-KO(PDGFRa) to investigate the role of E2F4 in APCs. Briefly, cold treatment of control and E2F4-KO(PDGFRa) mice at 6°C for 10d resulted in more multilocular beige adipocytes formed in ingWAT of female E2F4-KO(PDGFRa) mice than in sex- and age-matched control mice as evidenced by H&E staining. By RT-qPCR, selected thermogenic genes (e.g. Cidea, Ucp1, Cox8b) were also significantly upregulated in female rather than male KO ingWAT after cold exposure. To confirm whether E2f4-null APCs promote beige adipogenesis in a cell-autonomous manner, we FACS-isolated CD31-CD45-Sca1+ ingWAT APCs and cultured them in adipogenic differentiation medium (ADM) to evaluate their beige adipogenesis capacity in vitro. Oil Red O (ORO) staining showed no obvious difference between E2f4-null and control APC-derived adipocytes suggesting E2f4 does not affect the general adipogenic potential of APCs. However, RT-qPCR and Western blot measurement of UCP1 level showed female E2f4-null APC-derived adipocytes are slightly more prone to beige adipogenesis than female control APC-derived adipocytes. The weak phenotype could be due to the compensatory effect of E2f5, another transcription repressor of the E2f family. We are in the process of generating an inducible E2f5 knockout mouse line and an E2f4/E2f5 double knockout mouse line to experimentally test this hypothesis. Furthermore, detailed mechanisms of sex-dependent differences of E2F4-KO(PDGFRa) phenotypes and the role of E2f5 in WAT browning requires further investigation.

16101918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101918.value: During mouse embryo development, mesodermal Pax7+/Myf5+ progenitors give rise to both skeletal muscle and BAT in adult mice. Single cell transcriptomic analysis reveals detailed lineage progression patterns of Pax7+ progenies during brown adipogenic commitment. E2f4 is known to function as a transcriptional repressor in association with Rb family proteins to regulate wide-ranging cellular processes including adipogenesis and cell cycle progression. The Pax7/MyoD-E2F4/p107/p130 axis was reported previously by us to repress the expression of Prdm16 – a lineage-determination factor of BA – in APCs to suppress their brown adipogenic fate in culture. However, it remains unclear whether E2F4 knockout indeed promotes BAT development or white fat browning in vivo. We found that deletion of E2f4 in Pax7+/Myf5+ BAT embryonic progenitor cells in developing embryos was insufficient to promote brown adipogenesis during development. Nor was the ablation of E2F4 in differentiated adipocytes in WAT sufficient to promote white fat browning. However, deletion of E2f4 in Pdgfra+ preadipocytes in female mice enhanced ingWAT browning after cold stimulation suggesting inhibition of E2f4 could be beneficial for metabolic health. The single cell study was published this year on Cell Discovery.

16101918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101918.value: Although we showed that E2f4 knockout in preadipocytes could promotes ingWAT browning in female mice under cold stimulation, we could not explain why the phenotype is not as strong as previously reported in p107 or Rb knockout mice (Rudnicki et al., 2005, Cell Metabolism). Therefore, we will investigate the role of E2f5, another E2f member associated with the DREAM complex. Preliminary data shows knockdown of E2f5 enhanced brown adipogenesis of APCs in vitro. Currently, we are also generating APC-specific E2f5 KO and E2f4/5 double KO mice which will be subjected to cold stimulation as well as histological and molecular assays to determine if more multilocular UCP1+ adipocytes are produced in WAT. On the other hand, we found E2F4-KOPDGFRa mice are more resistant to high fat diet (HFD) induced obesity evidenced by lower body weight, fat weight as well as smaller adipocyte volume in various fat depots after HFD treatment. Mechanistically, we will examine transcriptomic profiles of E2F4-KOPDGFRa and control mouse adipocytes by RNA-seq and particularly look for metabolic gene expression altered by E2f4 knockout to explain the observed phenotype. Further work will involve ChIP-seq to identify direct E2f4 target and potentially uncover novel regulators of obesity.

16101918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101918.value: Brown adipose tissue is capable of generating heat in response to neurological stimulation under specific conditions including coldness in surroundings, a process also known as non-shivering thermogenesis. Brown fat cells usually contains multiple lipid droplets in contrast to white fat cells which only contain one. Moreover, distinct from white adipose tissue, brown fat cells contain more mitochondria which process fuel molecules such as fatty acids to generate heat instead of ATP. Hence, brown adipose tissue provides obvious benefits in the fight against nutrition overload. Fascinatingly, brown adipocyte-like cells can also appear in white fat in a cold environment or after genetic manipulation thus turning the white fat brownish or beige. We are interested in how this beiging process is regulated and we found that by getting rid of a gene called E2f4 in mouse white adipocyte progenitors the white fat are more beige after cold treatment. This manipulation enables us to investigate further what E2f4, a versatile protein, does in particular to control this process and fortunately we will identify its target and facilitate drug development to counter metabolic diseases such as obesity.

16102018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102018.value: The human brain contains approximately 100 billion neurons and roughly the same number of glial cells. Although glial cells do not function as excitable cells for the transmission of nerve impulses, they are critical in regulating the microenvironment and maintaining homeostasis. Glial cells are generally classified into astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and microglial cells, with the astrocytes being most abundant. Intercellular communication between neurons and astrocytes has long been recognised as a potential mechanism which contributes to brain development, neuronal survival, neuroinflammation and, more recently, synaptic transmission. The astrocytes have been demonstrated to release various transmitters and cytokines in the vicinity of neurons, thereby modulating the functions of the latter. Conversely, neurons can release cytokines that modulate the functions of astrocytes. Bidirectional interaction and communication between neurons and neighbouring astrocytes constitute an essential aspect of normal brain function. Given the large number of neurotransmitters and signaling molecules known to be expressed in the brain, intercellular signaling between neurons and astrocytes is highly complex and extremely difficult to tease out. The neural circuits in the central nervous system (CNS) are often characterized by the neurotransmitters that are released by the neurons, and many of these molecules bind to the G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Defects in GPCR signaling can lead to neuro disorders such as depression, Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. The Principal Investigator (PI) has recently shown that many GPCRs possess the ability to stimulate the production of specific cytokines in a variety of cell types including neurons. Interestingly, cytokine production is most effectively stimulated by GPCRs that utilize members of the Gαq subfamily, and there appears to be specificity in the types of cytokines being regulated. Neurotransmitters released from neurons can conceivably act on astrocytes as well as other neurons to produce cytokines that alter the microenvironment. The use of neurotransmitters and cytokines for intercellular communication between neurons and astrocytes is both logical and practical, but the biological relevance of this type of communication is rather difficult to ascertain. By leveraging on the PI’s discovery that activation of distinct Gq-coupled receptors stimulates the release of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) in astrocytic cells, the present proposal aims to examine how cytokines produced by astrocytes can regulate neuronal functions. Since LIF is a cytokine involved in the survival and differentiation of neural cells, modulation of its expression may yield protective and beneficial effects against neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases.

16102018.label: Realisation of objectives
16102018.value: The first objective aims to elucidate the mechanism by which G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) stimulate the production of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF). This objective constituted the major effort as it entailed the screening of multiple GPCRs that are known to be expressed in neurons and astrocytes. Upon testing a panel of 23 GPCR ligands against receptors known to be expressed in multiple human neural and astrocytic cell lines, the bradykinin B2 receptor was identified as one of the most robust GPCRs in releasing LIF; this receptor is expressed in glial cells. Although several other Gq-coupled receptors including bombesin, histamine H1, and muscarinic receptors are similarly capable of inducing LIF production, only the bradykinin B2 receptor-mediated response was consistently detected in multiple astrocytic cell lines (U87-MG, 1321-N1, and T98G) and in primary astrocytes. In the U87-MG astrocyte model system, detection of LIF by ELISA revealed that bradykinin stimulated LIF production in a concentration-dependent manner, and was correlated with bradykinin-mediated Ca2+ mobilization. Similar results were obtained with primary cortical astrocyte cultures, where bradykinin-induced LIF secretion exhibited an EC50 value of 23 nM. Given that the unstimulated levels of LIF in both U87-MG and primary astrocytes were negligible, the notion of bradykinin acting as a paracrine signal was pursued. We investigated whether neurons can indeed produce bradykinin. The presence of kinin-like peptides in the CNS has long been noted, however, production of bradykinin by specific cell types in the brain remains ellusive. Thus, we assessed the ability of the human SK-N-MC neuroblastoma cells and U87-MG astrocytic cells to produce kinins. The two major components of the kinin-generating system, kininogen (KNG-1) and tissue kallikrein (KLK-1), were detected in SK-N-MC cells by RT-PCR; KNG-1 is the precursor of bradykinin whereas KLK-1 is the serine protease which generates bradykinin-related peptides from KNG-1. In contrast, KNG-1 and KLK-1 transcripts were almost undetectable in U87-MG cells. These results tend to suggest that synthesis and release of bradykinin are more likely to occur in neurons rather than in astrocytes, with bradykinin constituting a paracrine signal for the astrocytes. Indeed, endogenous expression of bradykinin B1 and B2 receptors in both U87-MG and primary cortical astrocytes was demonstrated by Western blot analysis, albeit the level of B2 receptors in cultured primary astrocytes was lower as compared with U87-MG. Since the B1 receptor is predominately stimulated by Des-Arg-9-bradykinin, a metabolic by-product of bradykinin, we focused on characterizing the B2 receptor in astrocytic cells. By means of HOE-140, a B2-selective antagonist, bradykinin-induced [Ca2+]i mobilization in both U87-MG cells and cultured astrocytes was found to be mediated predominately via the B2 receptor; pre-treatment of cells with 5 μM HOE-140 completely abolished the Ca2+ response by bradykinin. Moreover, HOE-140 effectively blocked bradykinin-induced LIF production in both cell types, suggesting that bradykinin released by neurons might stimulate LIF production in astrocytes via activating their B2 receptors. Unequivocal demonstration of the release of bradykinin by neurons was fraught by supply issues of bradykinin ELISA kits due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Nevertheless, we were able to demonstrate that the conditioned media of SK-N-MC cells contained bradykinin-like components, because the conditioned media stimulated the phosphorylation of mitogen-activated kinases (MAPKs) in U87-MG cells, and these responses were completely blocked by HOE-140. These findings support the specific involvement of bradykinin B2 receptors, since activation of their coupled Gq proteins will lead to stimulatory phosphorylation of MAPKs. Indeed, the bradykinin-induced LIF production in U87-MG cells was sensitive to specific inhibitors against MAPKs, including PD98059 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase) and SB202190 (p38 MAPK). In the second objective, we attempted to characterize the functional role of LIF in regulating neuron-astrocyte communication. RT-PCR analyses revealed abundant LIF receptor (LIFR) transcripts in U87-MG and SK-N-MC cells, as well as in primary astrocytes and cortical neurons. However, expression of LIFR was substantially lower in astrocytic cells than in neuronal cells as determined by an anti-LIFR antibody. LIF released from astrocytes is thus expected to exert both autocrine and paracrine effects, perhaps with the latter being more prominent because of higher LIFR levels in neurons. To examine potential paracrine effects of LIF on neurons, we applied conditioned media from U87-MG cells (with or without bradykinin treatment for up to 24 hours) onto SK-N-MC cells and determined the activation status of STAT3 (which lies downstream of the LIFR). Conditioned media from U87-MG cells which had been treated with bradykinin significantly stimulated STAT3 phosphorylation (maximal by 12 hours of incubation) in SK-N-MC cells, and this response was partially inhibited when the conditioned media were pre-treated with anti-LIF antiserum. Pre-treatment of the conditioned media with anti-LIF and anti-IL-6 antisera completely abolished the STAT3 responses, indicating that bradykinin treatment may also induce the release of IL-6 from astrocytes. To recapitulate paracrine signaling by LIF in a more physiological condition, we co-cultured SK-N-MC and U87-MG cells in transwell chambers with 0.4 μm membrane pore size (large enough for passage of proteins but not cells). U87-MG cells were placed in the upper chamber and stimulated with or without 100 nM bradykinin, while SK-N-MC cells in the lower chamber were collected after various time points for determination of STAT3 phosphorylation. As compared to the negative controls without bradykinin treatment or with SK-N-MC seeded in the upper chamber, the level of STAT3 phosphorylation in SK-N-MC cells was elevated upon co-culture with bradykinin-treated U87-MG cells. However, attempts to replicate similar observations with primary cortical neurons and astrocytes were met with limited success. The experimental conditions for co-culturing primary cortical neurons and astrocytes will need to be established empirically, and a STAT3 reporter gene driving the expression of GFP has been constructed to facilitate the continuous detection of cytokine-induced STAT3 activation. Lastly, we investigated whether activation of GPCRs can affect the proliferation and differentiation of neural stem cells. We employed human ReNcell VM cells (an immortalized neural progenitor cell line derived from the ventral mesencephalon region) as a model system. We have established a protocol by which growth factor withdrawal can trigger the differentiation of ReNcell VM within 7-10 days, resulting in a mixed culture (ReNcell-derived immature neurons; RDIN) composed of immature neurons (80%), astrocytes (15%), and oligodendrocytes (5%). Presence of cholinergic neurons in the RDIN culture was confirmed by the detection of choline acetyltransferase with a specific antibody. Although both ReNcell VM cells and the differentiated RDIN culture express a number of functional Gq-receptors, agonist-induced LIF release was only observed in undifferentiated ReNcell VM cells. Activation of these Gq-coupled receptors (e.g., histamine, endothelin, ATP, and muscarinic receptors), however, did not significantly stimulate the proliferation of ReNcell VM or RDIN cells. Because ReNcell VM cells do not respond to bradykinin, the kinin can serve to trigger the release of LIF from astrocytic cells in a co-culture system. In a transwell co-culture system with astrocytes (either U87-MG or primary astrocytes) placed in the upper chamber, no change in proliferation of ReNcell VM or RDIN cells could be discerned over a period of 7 days despite evidence of STAT3 activation in these cells. Disappointingly, LIF also failed to stimulate the proliferation of ReNcell VM cells or primary cortical neurons. Manpower cost was reduced because an experienced researcher joined the project as a collaborator (please see Section 11) while higher general expenditure was needed to cover increased work in primary cultures.

16102018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102018.value: The overall project goal was to demonstrate the involvement of GPCRs, particularly the group of Ca2+-mobilizing Gq-coupled receptors, in intercellular communication between astrocytes and neurons. To this end, we have successfully identified several GPCRs on astrocytes that can efficiently trigger the secretion of several cytokines of the IL-6 family, with LIF being the most strongly induced cytokine (Abstract 1). One of the most effective GPCR ligands turns out to be bradykinin. This kinin is traditionally considered as a mediator of inflammation and is known to be expressed in the CNS. Recent studies suggest that bradykinin may possess neuroprotective effects and can regulate the proliferation and differentiation of neural stem cells. The present study provides evidence that bradykinin can be synthesized and released by neurons, whereas astrocytes utilize the bradykinin B2 receptor to stimulate the production of LIF. We have further demonstrated that LIF secreted from astrocytes can activate LIFR and stimulate STAT3 phosphorylation in neurons, thus completing a bi-directional signaling circuit between astrocytes and neurons (Abstract 1). Although we were not able to observe LIF-induced proliferation of neural progenitor cells (exemplified by ReNcell VM or RDIN cells), we have ascertained that neural progenitor cells express LIFR and can respond to LIF with elevated STAT3 phosphorylation (Abstracts 2 and 3). We have put forth the tantalizing idea of GPCRs being important players for regulating autocrine and paracrine signals in a recent publication (Publication 1 in Part C), which highlighted their roles in maintaining homeostasis in the CNS. We are in the process of compiling the experimental findings into a manuscript for a major publication (Publication 2 in Part C); it should be noted that extensive supportive results from primary astrocytes and neurons are needed for such a publication and the generation of these data was hampered by the COVID-19 pandemic, hence the delay in submission. One final piece of the puzzle is whether LIF can protect neurons from insults, and this is currently being addressed by determining the effects of conditioned media from astrocytes on hypoxia- or NMDA-induced neuronal cell death. These studies will be completed in the first quarter of 2023 for inclusion into the manuscript under preparation (Publication 2 in Part C).

16102018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102018.value: Due to limited supplies of mouse embryos during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, many experiments requiring the use of primary cultures could not be performed in adequate trials. Since conditioned media from primary astrocytes that had been treated with bradykinin was found to stimulate STAT3 phosphorylation in primary cortical neurons, and that the response could be suppressed by anti-LIF and anti-IL-6 antisera, co-culturing of these primary cells in transwell chambers may help to verify bradykinin/LIF-mediated intercellular signaling between astrocytes and neurons. The potential involvement of IL-6 is rather intriguing because activation of Gq-coupled receptors can also stimulate the secretion of this cytokine by astrocytes, albeit at levels significantly (~10-fold) lower than that LIF. It has been reported that LIFR/STAT4 can induce the production of IL-6 in fibroblasts, and this possible action of LIF should be further explored via RNA-seq and gene silencing approaches in selected cellular models. The autocrine function of LIF on astrocytes has yet to be fully appreciated, and its potential regulation of IL-6 (as well as other cytokines) may help to elucidate the role of astrocytes in health and in disease, since the induction of astrocytes into M1 and M2 phenotypes has functional significance on neuroinflammation.

16102018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102018.value: The brain is a highly sophisticated organ composed of multiple cell types but most neurobiological studies are heavily focused on neurons, the excitable cells responsible for neurotransmission. Astrocytes, the other major cell type in the brain, are undeniably crucial in the maintenance and functioning of our central nervous system. However, the mechanisms by which neurons and astrocytes communicate with each other remain largely unexplored. In this project, a bi-directional signaling pathway between neurons and astrocytes has been unraveled. Neurons can apparently release signaling molecules that target Gq-coupled receptors on astrocytes. Activation of these receptors can subsequently induce the production and release of cytokines such as LIF from the astrocytes. The cytokines can in turn act on their corresponding receptors on the neurons in a paracrine fashion to complete the bi-directional signaling cycle. Although the precise functional importance of such a signaling cycle has not yet been elucidated, it provides clear evidence that intercellular communications between neurons and astrocytes exist in multiple spatial and temporal dimensions. A thorough understanding on how the functional status of one cell type affects the function of another cell type in the brain may provide novel insights on the pathogenesis of neuro disorders.

16102118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102118.value: Metabolic activities and environmental factors can cause oxidative stress through the production of reactive oxygen species. Oxidative stress has been linked to cellular malfunction and organismal aging. Therefore, multiple defense mechanisms have evolved to limit the damage induced by reactive oxygen species. These include antioxidants and enzymes that neutralize toxic metabolites. For example, aldehyde dehydrogenases turn toxic fatty aldehydes into fatty acids. Although most of them are cytosolic, a sub-family of membrane-associated aldehyde dehydrogenases is dedicated to neutralize phospholipid-derived fatty aldehydes. Despite the importance of these enzymes, open questions remain regarding the molecular mechanisms for their organelle-specific membrane anchoring, and the functional significance of such membrane association. Lipid droplets are evolutionarily conserved organelles for cellular fat storage. Recently, lipid droplets are found to shelter fatty acids that may be derived from fatty aldehydes. This blunts the propagation of oxidative damage by reactive oxygen species. The fatty acid products of aldehyde dehydrogenases can also be broken down and used as substrates for energy production in mitochondria. Our long-term goal is to understand how systemic oxidative stress can be resolved in a tissue-specific, and organelle-specific manner. Our central hypothesis is that the subcellular localization of membrane-bound aldehyde dehydrogenases dictates the sites of processing and disposal of toxic lipid species. From a forward genetic screen, we isolated multiple mutant strains that are deficient in the C. elegans membrane-bound aldehyde dehydrogenase. These strains show signs of oxidative stress under basal condition. In the intestine, this enzyme is localized to the endoplasmic reticulum and lipid droplets. However, it is localized to mitochondria and peroxisomes in the hypodermis. In this proposal, we will determine how tissue-specific organelle targeting is accomplished by the C. elegans aldehyde dehydrogenase and investigate the functional consequences of mis-targeting. We will also determine how its dimerization and association with other proteins at inter-organelle junctions link substrate acquisition and product channeling. 16102218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102218.value: 真核細胞的關鍵特征是每個真核細胞被細分為各種膜封閉的細胞器，例如內質網（ER），高爾基體，內涵體和溶酶體。這種分化增加了膜區域的面積從而進行有效的生化反應，同時這種化分產生特定的空間以執行不同的功能。然而，也許作為這些優點的成本，真核細胞的這些化分也為分泌運輸途徑提供了重大挑戰。 在分泌運輸途徑中，蛋白質運輸的準確性依賴於將特定貨物蛋白質精確的分選到運輸囊泡中的貨物分選過程。外殼蛋白復合物II（COPII）調節貨物蛋白在ER中的被包裝入囊泡中的過程。 COPII外殼由五種胞質蛋白組成：小GTP酶Sar1，Sec23 / 24異二聚體和Sec13 / 31異二聚體。 Sec24是COPII外套中的主要亞單位，用作捕獲貨物蛋白質的貨物適配器。哺乳動物細胞有四種同種型的Sec24，稱為Sec24A，Sec24B，Sec24C和Sec24D。鑒於其在介導ER輸出中的重要作用，每種Sec24同種型的突變會引起各種生理和發育缺陷。ER腔中的可溶性貨物蛋白不能被COPII外殼直接識別，目前認為這些蛋白質是通過跨膜受體與COPII外殼連接。 雖然已經取得了重大進展，但依賴於特定Sec24同種型或特定貨物受體的貨物蛋白譜仍然很不清楚。揭示這些將提供貨物蛋白分選過程的生理功能和分子機制的重要見解。此外，運輸囊泡不僅應包含正確的貨物分子，還應包含正確的SNARE蛋白和運動蛋白，以確保將囊泡靶向正確的目的地。一些貨物蛋白質需要與其他貨物蛋白在一起從而被COPII識別裝入囊泡。盡管它們具有重要性，但在COPII囊泡中與特定貨物蛋白特異性共富集的蛋白質仍然沒有被充分的研究。 在這裏，我們的目標是利用體外囊泡形成法重建COPII介導的來自ER的囊泡形成的過程，從而系統地揭示依賴於特定Sec24同種型或特定貨物受體裝入囊泡的貨物蛋白質譜。此外，我們將利用囊泡形成法來揭示在COPII囊泡中與特定平面細胞極性（PCP）蛋白特異性包裝在一起的蛋白質。我們的分析將提供COPII介導的轉運過程的全面視圖，並提供調節PCP蛋白ER輸出的分子機制的新見解。

16102218.label: Realisation of objectives
16102218.value: The fidelity of protein transport in the secretory pathway relies on accurate sorting of specific cargo proteins into transport vesicles. Coat protein complex II (COPII) regulates packaging of cargo proteins into vesicles at the ER, the first step of the secretory transport pathway. COPII coat is composed of five subunits, SAR1, SEC23/24 heterodimer and SEC13/31 heterodimer. COPII coat, particularly the inner COPII coat formed by SAR1 and SEC23/24 heterodimer, functions as cargo adaptor to capture cargo proteins thereby enriching them into budding vesicles. Soluble cargo proteins in the ER lumen cannot be directly recognized by the COPII coat and those proteins are thought to be linked to the COPII coat by transmembrane cargo receptors. Although significant progresses have been achieved in understanding the COPII-mediated ER export process, the spectrum of cargo proteins that depend on a specific factor to be efficiently packaged into COPII vesicles is unclear. Moreover, protein profiles of COPII vesicles enriched with a specific cargo proteins are also unclear. In this project, we aim to utilize an in vitro vesicle formation that reconstitutes COPII-mediated vesicular release from the ER to systematically reveal the spectrum of cargo proteins that depend on a specific COPII subunit or a specific ER-located cargo receptor to be efficiently exported out of the ER in mammalian cells. Moreover, we aim to utilize the vesicle formation assay to reveal and characterize proteins that are specifically packaged together with specific planar cell polarity proteins in COPII vesicles. Realisation of Objective 1 (To investigate the functional roles of cargo adaptors and cargo receptors that participate in the COPII-mediated vesicular transport process): In collaborations with Prof. Zhongping Yao’s lab at PolyU and Prof. Liwen Jiang’s lab at CUHK, we developed a large scale vesicle formation assay in combination with label-free quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to analyze the protein profiles of transport vesicles. for proteomic analysis. Using this approach, we identified specific cargo proteins that are dependent on a COPII subunit, Sar1A, to be enriched into transport vesicles. We also identified novel cytosolic proteins that are recruited by GTP-bound SAR1A on vesicle membranes. One of the identified cytosolic protein, PRRC1, contains proline-rich domains and regulate anterograde trafficking. Further analyses revealed that PRRC1 is recruited to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites, interacts with the inner COPII coat, and its absence increases membrane association of COPII. The cargo clients of SEC24 isoforms have been published before this project started. Therefore, we did not perform our approach to analyze roles of SEC24 isoforms in COPII-mediated ER export. Using this approach, we compared the protein profiles of vesicles produced by control cells with those produced by cells depleted of the cargo receptors, SURF4 or ERGIC53. This analysis revealed specific clients of each of these two export adaptors. Our study provides novel insights into COPII-mediated vesicular transport process. This study also indicates that the vesicle formation assay in combination with quantitative MS analysis is a robust and powerful tool to uncover novel factors that mediate vesicular trafficking and to uncover cargo clients of specific cellular factors. This work has been published in PNAS in 2021. The technique uncovered cargo clients of a GTPase, Atlastin which is published in PNAS 2019. The technique has also been successfully utilized to establishing an in vitro COPII vesicle reconstitution system in plant. This reconstitution assay identified a novel class of giant COPII vesicles induced by an Arabidopsis-specific COPII paralogue in response to stress. This work has been published in Nature Plant in 2021. Realisation of Objective 2 To reveal and characterize proteins that are specifically co-enriched with Vangl2 or Frizzled6 in COPII vesicles: We have reconstituted vesicular release of FLAG-Vangl2 and HA-Frizzled6-FLAG at the ER. In addition, we have immunoisolated Vangl2-enriched and Frizzled6-enriched vesicles in a large scale and performed a label-free quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to identify proteins that specifically co-enriched with Vangl2 vesicles or Frizzled6 vesicles. Although we did not identify specific transmembrane proteins that are co-enriched with Vangl2 in ER-derived vesicles, we found a group of transmembrane cargo proteins that are co-enriched with Frizzled6 vesicles. One of the transmembrane proteins that are specifically enriched with Frizzled6 vesicles is another PCP protein, Celsr1. Our study indicates that Celsr1 and Frizzled-6 associate with each other in the secretory transport pathway. When associated with the immaturely glycosylated form of Frizzled-6, Clesr1 is retained in the ER. After correct glycosylation and folding, Frizzled-6 in association with Celsr1 is released from the ER quality control machinery and then interacts with the COPII machinery to be packaged into COPII vesicles. At this step, Celsr1 promotes the anterograde transport of Frizzled-6 possibly by providing additional binding sites for COPII. This study reveals novel insight into the molecular machinery that regulates ER export of Frizzled-6. Our study also provides a mechanism whereby Frizzled that are associated with Celsr1 can be effectively delivered from the ER to the downstream compartments suggesting a quality control mechanism to ensure the stoichiometry of Frizzled-6 and Celsr1 on cell boundaries. This work has been published in JBC 2020. In summary, we have addressed all of our objectives utilizing the vesicle formation assay as well as other biochemical and cell biological approaches, which revealed novel insights into COPII-mediated ER export process.

16102218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102218.value: In this study, we have developed a large scale vesicle formation assay in combination with quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to profile proteins associated with transport vesicles. Our study indicates that this approach is a powerful tool to reveal cargo proteins that depends on a specific cellular factor to be packaged into transport vesicles. This approach is also powerful to uncover novel factors that are associated with vesicles to mediate trafficking. This approach has a lot of applications. In future, we will use this approach to analyze to perform the following analyses: 1) To analyze protein profiles of vesicles generated from cells that have high capacity of secretion such as pancreatic cells and liver cells; 2) To analyze protein profiles of vesicles generated by cells under stress or under differentiation; 3) To analyze cargo proteins that depends on specific cellular factors that regulate the morphology of the endoplasmic reticulum to be enriched in vesicles; 4) To identify and characterize proteins co-enriched with a specific cargo in transport vesicles.

16102218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102218.value: Coat protein complex II (COPII) regulates packaging of cargo proteins into vesicles at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the first step of the secretory pathway. In this study, we utilized an in vitro assay that reconstitutes packaging of human cargo proteins into vesicles to quantify cargo capture. Quantitative mass spectrometry (MS) analyses of the isolated vesicles revealed cytosolic proteins that are recruited to vesicle membranes by GTP-bound form of the COPII subunit, SAR1A. One of them, PRRC1, interacts with the inner COPII coat, and its absence increases membrane association of COPII. In addition, we uncovered cargo proteins that depend on GTP hydrolysis of SAR1A to be captured into vesicles. Comparing control cells with cells depleted of the ER cargo receptors, SURF4 or ERGIC53, we revealed specific clients of each of these two export adaptors. In addition, we found two planar cell polarity proteins, Frizzled6 and Celsr1, are associated with each other and co-enriched in COPII vesicles. This association promotes surface delivery of Frizzled6. Our results reveal novel insight into COPII-mediated ER export process and indicates that the vesicle formation assay in combination with quantitative MS analysis is a robust and powerful tool to uncover novel factors that mediate vesicular trafficking.

16102518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102518.value: Functions of the brain, the most critical and complex organ, can be adversely affected by a variety of pathological conditions. In vivo high-resolution optical imaging of biological structures and processes in small animal models provides a novel means for the study of brain diseases and disorders. The open-skull and thinned-skull protocols for the preparation of cranial windows are mostly used for live imaging of the mouse brain. However, the open skull procedure permanently alters the neuroimmune system in the brain. The major limitation of the thinned-skull technique is that an exceedingly thin skull is required to achieve high-quality imaging due to the optical irregularity of the skull itself, the skull/brain interface and the mechanically thinned skull surface. In addition, an overly thinned skull is not suitable for chronic in vivo imaging because newly regenerated bone layer must be constantly removed to ensure the optical quality of the cranial window. In the proposed research, we will develop an adaptive optics (AO) technology to correct the optical aberration from the thinned skull of a significantly greater thickness to achieve both chronical and high-resolution imaging of the brain in vivo. We will demonstrate the use of this technology to study the development and treatment of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Accumulation of β-amyloid (Aβ) is the pathological characteristics in AD and the dysfunction or depletion of microglia, the resident immune cells in the brain, is linked to an altered Aβ plaque load and increased risks for AD. We have conducted a pilot study that successfully demonstrated the feasibility of proposed research project. We will further develop a fast AO-TPEF microscope system to achieve near diffraction-limited imaging in the live mouse brain through a relatively thick thinned-skull. We will conduct chronic brain imaging in the transgenic AD mouse model with administration of potential AD drug candidates. Through the analysis of morphological and biochemical changes in microglia and amyloid plaques, we will identify how the potential AD drugs influence the neuroimmune system and decrease the amyloid plaque load. The structural and functional brain imaging aims to provide new biological insights into AD progression and treatment. Success of the proposed research will lead to a better understanding of the disease and the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting microglia for AD treatment and prevention. The total requested funding for the three-year project is HK$1,759,220 (US$225,493). 大腦是人體最關鍵和最複雜的器官，是我們身體的控制中心。大腦的功能會受到各種病理狀況的不利影響。近年來，小動物成像已成為藥物開發和人類疾病無創診斷的重要研究工具。在小動物模型中實現亞細胞分辨率的生物結構和過程的光學成像特別為研究腦疾病和病症提供了新的方法。在這項擬議的研究中，我們的目標是開發一種先進的光學成像技術，以可視化活小鼠大腦皮質中的生物活動。我們證明該技術可用於研究世界上最流行的神經退行性疾病，阿爾茨海默病（AD）的發展和治療。 能夠用於重複對活體動物大腦進行光學成像的手術方案是實現腦疾病追蹤研究的先決條件。開放式顱骨和變薄顱骨手術是目前用於製備顱窗以實現活體小鼠大腦成像的主要方案。然而，開放式顱骨手術將不可避免地激活免疫細胞並永久改變大腦中的神經免疫系統。減薄顱骨技術的主要限制是，由於顱骨本身，顱骨/腦界面以及機械磨薄的顱骨表面的光學不規則性，需要打磨非常薄的顱骨（5-10微米）來實現高分辨率和深部組織成像。此外，過薄的顱骨不適合長期活體成像，因為必須不斷地移除新生長的顱骨以確保顱窗的光學質量。在所提出的研究中，我們開發了一種自適應光學（AO）技術，用於校正打磨后厚度明顯較厚的顱骨的光學像差，以實現大腦的長期和高分辨率活體成像。這項新技術有望推動活體光學顯微成像技術在大腦研究中的應用。 越來越多的證據表明，β-澱粉樣蛋白（Aβ）的積累是阿爾茨海默病的病理特徵。小膠質細胞（大腦中的常駐免疫細胞）的功能障礙或數量減少會改變大腦內Aβ斑塊的負荷，並且增加阿爾茨海默病風險。在一項初步研究中，我們在轉基因AD小鼠中通過變薄的顱骨顱窗展示了綠色熒光蛋白標記的小膠質細胞和染料標記的Aβ斑塊的體內雙光子激發熒光（TPEF）成像，儘管由於相對較厚（> 40微米）的變薄顱骨引入的像差而導致圖像質量受到影響。此外，我們將AO系統與TPEF顯微鏡結合在一起，以校正由約40微米厚的分離的小鼠顱骨引起的像差。AO校正後，熒光強度和成像分辨率得到顯著改善。結果證明了所提出的AO-TPEF顯微鏡系統通過相對較厚的變薄顱骨在小鼠腦中實現近衍射限製成像的可行性。在擬議的研究中，我們將在轉基因AD小鼠模型中使用潛在的治療AD的候選藥物，并進行長期活體腦成像追蹤研究。通過分析小膠質細胞和澱粉樣斑塊的形態和生化變化，我們將確定潛在的AD藥物如何影響神經免疫系統並減少澱粉樣蛋白斑塊負荷。結構和功能性腦成像旨在為AD病發和治療提供新的生物學見解。所提出的研究的成功將使得更好地理解該疾病並開發針對小膠質細胞用於AD治療和預防的新型治療策略。

16102518.label: Realisation of objectives
16102518.value: The project objectives were accomplished in three distinct phases of research, and the goals established in the original proposal were exceeded. The successful completion of the project was due to a meticulous and well-structured approach that was designed to optimize the performance of optical microscopy in deep-tissue imaging. The first phase of the research was focused on optimizing the configuration of an adaptive optics two-photon microscope system and developing an improved wavefront sensing algorithm for accurate correction of aberrations induced by the thinned skull window and brain tissue. This phase led to subcellular resolution transcranial imaging of layer 5 pyramidal neurons up to 700 μm below pia in living mice, and the investigation of microglia-plaque interaction in the living brain of Alzheimer's disease. In details, we developed an AO two-photon microscope system for transcranial brain imaging by underfilling the back aperture of a high-NA objective. The effective NA for excitation path and wavefront sensing was optimally reduced to mitigate optical scattering of a fluorescent guide star signal and enable direct wavefront sensing in the deep brain region. After wavefront measurement and correction, the full NA of the objective was then used for fluorescence collection. To examine the effectiveness of this approach, we conducted Monte Carlo simulation to evaluate the performance of wavefront sensing under different effective NA conditions. The results showed that, with the same amount of photons collected by the SHWS, the signal-to-background ratio (SBR) of the guide star images on SHWS was significantly increased when reducing the effective NA. It was found that the configuration of effective NA at 0.7 produces a good balance between wavefront sensing accuracy and diffraction-limited resolution. Next, we conducted in vivo imaging of yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) labelled neurons in Thy1-YFP mice through a thinned-skull window of 50 μm thickness using the overfilled and underfilled configurations. We demonstrated that the quality of the SHWS images was greatly improved by reducing the NA for excitation and wavefront sensing, consistent with the simulation conclusions. Furthermore, the two-photon excited fluorescence intensity was enhanced up to twofold when reducing the excitation NA from 1.05 to 0.7. In the rest of this work, we adopted the underfilled configuration with effective NA of 0.7 to improve the accuracy of direct wavefront sensing as well as the efficiency of two-photon excitation. In the second phase, we developed a two-photon endomicroscopy system by incorporating adaptive optics based on direct wavefront sensing. This allowed for the recovery of diffraction-limited resolution in deep-brain imaging and the implementation of a new precompensation strategy that corrected aberrations over large volumes and achieved rapid random-access multiplane imaging. This phase led to the investigation of neuronal plasticity in the hippocampus and the revelation of the relationship between somatic and dendritic activity of pyramidal neurons. To evaluate the efficacy of our approach, we first characterized the intrinsic aberrations of the GRIN lens using an in vitro setup. The point-spread-function (PSF) of the endomicroscope was evaluated by imaging the individual fluorescent bead. We found that despite the aberrations increasing rapidly and the PSF becoming severely distorted when the imaging position deviates from the center point, AO correction can effectively increase the fluorescence signal and recover the diffraction-limited performance at various depths. We next applied the AO approach to the in vivo imaging of the mouse hippocampus, in which a subset of pyramidal neurons expresses green fluorescent protein (GFP) under thy1 promoter (Thy1-GFP mice). The CA1 pyramidal neurons are vertically oriented with a typical laminar organization spanning hundreds of microns in depth. We demonstrated that after full AO correction and subsequent deconvolution from the local PSF, not only is the fluorescence intensity drastically improved, the dendrites and spines can also be clearly visualized owing to the substantially enhanced resolutions. The spectral power shows that the higher spatial frequency can be notably recovered by applying full AO correction with subsequent deconvolution. Quantitative measurement from individual dendritic spines shows that both lateral and axial resolutions approached diffraction-limited performance for the GRIN lens with NA of 0.8. Furthermore, even for the on-axis scenario where the GRIN lens was designed to yield the best performance, we still achieved tremendous improvement in resolution after full AO correction, with dendritic spines as deep as 300 μm clearly resolved. These results demonstrate that AO based on direct wavefront sensing can effectively correct the aberrations of the GRIN lens and recover the diffraction-limited resolution during in vivo imaging. In the third phase, we developed an adaptive optics three-photon microscope based on analog lock-in phase detection for focus sensing and shaping (ALPHA-FSS). This technology accurately measured and effectively corrected both aberrations and scattering induced by specimens, recovering subcellular resolution at depth. Moreover, the conjugate adaptive optics configuration with remote focusing enabled in vivo imaging of fine neuronal structures in the mouse cortex through the intact skull up to a depth of 750 µm below the pia, enabling near-non-invasive high-resolution microscopy in the cortex. This technology also demonstrated high-sensitivity functional calcium imaging and high-precision laser-mediated microsurgery through the intact skull, and achieved in vivo high-resolution imaging of the deep cortex and subcortical hippocampus up to 1.1 mm below the pia within the intact brain. Our conjugate α-FSS–3PM system consists of three key modules—that is, direct focus sensing, conjugate AO and remote focusing modules. The system aberrations are corrected by the deformable mirror (DM) using a simple sensorless AO method. The direct focus sensing in tissue is based on a phase-modulation and lock-in detection scheme. To measure the scattered and aberrated E-field PSF, a weak scanning beam raster scanned over a small field of view (FOV) is introduced to interfere with a strong stationary beam. Owing to the high sensitivity provided by our phase modulation and lock-in detection, the E-field PSF can be determined reliably by scanning a single frame of the FOV, regardless of the large DC background from the stationary beam. By measuring the aberrated E-field PSF, the desired corrective wavefront can be derived by using phase conjugation of the measured PSF. Then, a high-pixel-count spatial light modulator (SLM) acting as the wavefront corrector is employed to correct the aberrations over a large number of modes. To evaluate the efficacy of our α-FSS–3PM and characterize its performance in through-skull imaging, we first conducted an in vitro experiment by imaging fluorescent beads embedded in agarose below an excised intact skull. To measure the wavefront distortions, the strong beam was parked at the brightest regions—for example, the center of fluorescent bead— whereas the weak beam was used to scan over a 16 × 16-µm2 FOV to capture the complex E-field PSF. The overall aberrations can then be accurately determined and effectively corrected by using the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the measured E-field PSF, in a fast manner with only 2–3 iterations. We demonstrated that the fluorescent bead image recorded with system aberration correction only was highly distorted, and the appearance of the side lobes indicated the high-order aberrations induced by the thick skull. In contrast, by applying the corrective phase pattern to the SLM to compensate for specimen-induced aberrations, we effectively recovered high imaging resolution, and improved the fluorescence intensity more than 200-fold.

16102518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102518.value: This GRF project has been completed successfully with three publications in the first tier journals (Nature Biotechnology, Science Advances and Photonics Research). High-resolution optical imaging deep in tissues is challenging because of optical aberrations and scattering of light caused by the complex structure of living matter. First, we optimized configuration of an adaptive optics two-photon microscope system and an improved wavefront sensing algorithm were proposed for accurate correction for the aberrations induced by the thinned skull window and brain tissue. Using this system, we achieved subcellular resolution transcranial imaging of layer 5 pyramidal neurons up to 700 μm below pia in living mice. In addition, we investigated microglia–plaque interaction in living brain of Alzheimer’s disease and demonstrated high-precision laser dendrotomy and single-spine ablation. Next, we developed a two-photon endomicroscopy by adding adaptive optics based on direct wavefront sensing, which enabled recovery of diffraction-limited resolution in deep-brain imaging. A new precompensation strategy played a critical role to correct aberrations over large volumes and achieved rapid random-access multiplane imaging. We investigated the neuronal plasticity in the hippocampus, a critical deep brain structure, and revealed the relationship between the somatic and dendritic activity of pyramidal neurons. Finally, we invented an adaptive optics three-photon microscope based on analog lock-in phase detection for focus sensing and shaping (ALPHA-FSS). ALPHA-FSS accurately measures and effectively compensates for both aberrations and scattering induced by specimens and recovers subcellular resolution at depth. A conjugate adaptive optics configuration with remote focusing enables in vivo imaging of fine neuronal structures in the mouse cortex through the intact skull up to a depth of 750 µm below the pia, enabling near-non-invasive high-resolution microscopy in cortex. Functional calcium imaging with high sensitivity and high-precision laser-mediated microsurgery through the intact skull were also demonstrated. Moreover, we achieved in vivo high-resolution imaging of the deep cortex and subcortical hippocampus up to 1.1 mm below the pia within the intact brain.

16102518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102518.value: The technologies developed in this project, encompassing wavefront sensing-based adaptive optics two-photon microscopy, adaptive optics two-photon endomicroscopy for deep brain imaging, and deep tissue multi-photon imaging using adaptive optics with analog lock-in phase detection for focus sensing and shaping (ALPHA-FSS), have significant potential for adoption into standard multiphoton microscope systems and commercialization. ALPHA-FSS-based multiphoton microscopy offers minimally invasive capabilities for through intact skull deep brain imaging in various animal models, thereby enabling investigations into the neonate and infant brain development, an important research area hindered by the lack of non-invasive imaging tools. Such studies may lead to the unraveling of fundamental questions concerning the construction of the human brain.

16102518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102518.value: Optical microscopy has played a pivotal role in numerous biological discoveries. However, aberrations and scattering occur when light travels through biological tissues, fundamentally limiting the performance of optical microscopy in both resolution and depth. To overcome these limitations, adaptive optics (AO) techniques were employed to accurately measure the aberrant electric-field point-spread function of a laser in tissue and to quickly correct the aberration over a large imaging volume in the brain. Our study presents the first in-vivo imaging of fine neuronal structures in a mouse cortex through the intact skull at an unprecedented depth, making high-resolution microscopy in the cortex nearly non-invasive. This technological breakthroughs not only significantly facilitate the fundamental study of the living brain but also hold immense potential for adoption into the standard multiphoton microscope system and commercialization. This minimally invasive technology for deep brain imaging in various animal models will be used in future investigations of neonate and infant brain development, which is currently hindered by the lack of non-invasive imaging tools. The successful implementation of these technologies may ultimately lead to the unraveling of fundamental questions concerning the construction of the human brain.
