16102918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16102918.value: Nanotechnology has a wide spectrum of applications in electronics, water purification, medicine, and therapeutics. A great concern for the application of nanotechnology is the potential release of nanoparticles (NPs) into the environment, causing unwanted human exposure and environmental risks. We thus need a fundamental understanding of the impacts of metallic-based NPs on the environment and living systems. Estuaries are often the entry sites of NPs into the marine environments, and consequently there is a major need to study the transport, route/rate of exposure, transformation, as well as the response of estuarine systems to such exposure. However, estuarine nanotoxicology has not been well developed, and the interactions between bivalves as an important component in estuarine ecosystems and NPs are not well understood, which severely limits the environmental risk assessment of NPs in estuarine systems. In this project, we will focus on the biokinetics and subcellular/cellular localization of silver and zinc oxide NPs in estuarine oysters. We will: 1) study the bioaccumulation of these NPs in oysters using unique radiotracer methodology; 2) study the subcellular/cellular distribution and chemical bindings of NPs in oysters using Nano Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (NanoSIMS); 3) study the organ distribution and dissolution kinetics of metal ions and NPs in oysters using the novel Aggregated-Induced Emission (AIE) technique. Throughout these studies we will quantify the influence of NP size and surface coating, and environmental factors such as salinity and dissolved organic matter on the bioaccumulation, distribution and dissolution of NPs. One critical question to be addressed is the comparison between NPs themselves and ionic forms of metals. Radiolabeling NPs allows an accurate quantification of the bioaccumulation of NPs. Importantly, we will employ Nano-SIMS to examine and contrast the subcellular/cellular localization and binding of NPs and ionic metals in oysters. We will also for the first time examine the dissolution kinetics of NPs inside organisms using the novel AIE technique. The applications of these novel techniques will enable us to answer some of the most pressing questions surrounding nanotoxicology, including the quantitative assessment of the importance of NPs and dissolution of NPs in the overall accumulation and fates of NPs in organisms. We expect to produce one of the first biokinetic and bioimaging data of NPs in estuarine bivalves, and provide robust data for the risk assessment of NPs in estuarine environments. 納米技術在電子、淨水、醫藥和治療等領域有著廣泛的應用。對納米技術應用的極大關注是納米顆粒 (NPs) 在環境中的潛在釋放, 造成不必要的人類暴露和環境風險。因此, 我們需要對金屬基納米顆粒對環境系統的影響有一個基本的瞭解。河口經常是納米顆粒進入海洋環境的入口點, 因此, 我们需要研究它們的運輸途徑和速率、以及河口系統對這種暴露的反應。然而, 河口納米毒理學還沒有得到很好的發展, 而貝類作為河口生態系統的重要組成部分和納米顆粒的相互作用我們還不清楚, 這嚴重限制了河口納米顆粒的環境風險評價。在這個項目中, 我們將重點研究納米銀和氧化鋅納米顆粒在河口牡蠣中的生物動力學過程和亞細胞/細胞定位。我們將: 1) 利用獨特的放射性方法研究牡蠣中NPs 的生物積累; 2) 利用納米二次離子質譜 (NanoSIMS) 研究牡蠣中納米顆粒的亞細胞分佈和化學結合;3) 採用新型聚合誘導發光 (AIE) 技術, 研究牡蠣中金屬離子和納米顆粒的器官分佈和溶出動力學。在這些研究中, 我們將量化NP大小和表面塗層, 以及環境因素, 如鹽度和溶解有機物對納米顆粒的累積, 分佈和溶解的影響。這些新技術的應用將使我們能夠回答圍繞納米毒理學的一些最緊迫的問題, 包括定量評估納米顆粒的重要性。我們期望在河口雙殼貝類中產生第一個相關的生物成像資料, 為河口環境中納米顆粒的風險評估提供可靠的資料。

16102918.label: Realisation of objectives
16102918.value: Objective 1: To study the bioaccumulation and biokinetics of NPs. In this objective, we studied the bioaccumulation and biokinetics of NPs in biota using many novel technologies. Yang and Wang (2019) investigated the behavior of CuNPs in seawater, as well as the toxicity and bioaccumulation of CuNPs in barnacle larvae. Our results indicated that the toxicity of CuNPs could not be solely explained by the released Cu ions, and both CuNPs and the released Cu ion contributed to their toxicity and bioaccumulation in barnacle larvae. Shao & Wang (2020) used a radio-synthesizing method to trace the behavior of AgNPs with two sizes and two coatings in an estuarine oyster. This method was sensitive to detect the bioaccumulation and depuration of AgNPs in the oysters over a short period of exposure. Through radioactive AgNPs tracing and biokinetic modeling, we for the first time demonstrated the differential uptake mechanisms of different-sized AgNPs in the oysters. Yan et al. (2020) for the first time visualized and quantified the maternal transfer of AgNPs in a model zooplankton. AgNPs were transferred from mother to offspring and mainly accumulated in the lipids due to the strong colocalization with lipid droplets. Our bioimaging finding demonstrated that AgNPs could be maternally transferred to next generation. Along this line, Yan & Wang (2021) demonstrated that AgNPs were internalized in the phytoplankton species. These trophically transferred AgNPs experienced a complicated behavior such as dissolution in the acidic gut microenvironment and depuration. Li and & Wang (2021a) evaluated the uptake and depuration kinetics of AgNWs at various exposure concentrations. Rapid accumulation of AgNWs was observed, and the steady-state concentration was obtained within 24-h. The slow depurations of both AgNWs and Ag+ in D. magna may thus contribute to their joined chronic toxic effects. In another study, Li & Wang (2021b) investigated the uptake, intracellular dissolution, and cytotoxicity of silver nanowires (AgNWs) in two cell models. Cellular uptake of AgNWs occurred mainly via pathways of clathrin-dependent endocytosis, caveolae-dependent endocytosis, and phagocytosis. Objective 2: To study the subcellular/cellular localization and binding of NPs. In this objective, we studied the subcellular and cellular localization of NPs in biota using novel technologies. Yan et al. (2018) directly visualized and quantified the time-dependent release of Ag+ from different sized AgNPs in an in vivo model zooplankton (Daphnia magna). We demonstrated that the ingested AgNPs were dissoluted to Ag+, which were heterogeneously distributed in daphnids, with much higher concentrations in the anterior gut. Li et al. (2019) investigated the interactions between gut microbiota and zooplankton, under AgNPs exposure through bioimaging, metatranscriptomic and gut microbiota translational techniques. The results demonstrated that the toxic symptoms of zooplankton were mediated by gut microbiota at low concentrations of AgNPs. In two exciting NanoSIMS studies, the subcellular behavior of AgNPs was comprehensively studied. Shao et al. (2020) coupled high-resolution NanoSIMS elemental mapping and successfully visualized the subcellular localization as well as the potential toxicity effects of AgNPs in the oyster gill filaments. Stable isotope tracing method was also adopted to investigate the respective uptake and transport mechanisms of differently labeled 109AgNPs and 107Ag+ ions. For the first time, we provided visualized evidence of AgNPs induced autophagy in the oyster gill cells. Zhang et al. (2020) investigated the subcellular localization of Ag and in situ chemical distribution in the oyster larvae Crassostrea angulata after exposure to isotopically enriched 109AgNPs. The results collectively showed that AgNPs were much less bioavailable than Ag+, and the intracellular Ag was mainly originated from the soluble Ag especially those dissolved from the ingested AgNPs. AgNPs formed inorganic Ag-S complexes extracellularly, while Ag-organosulfur complexes were predominantly formed intracellularly. Ag was also occasionally incorporated into the phosphate granules, rough endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. Yan et al. (2021) quantitatively monitored the AgNPs and their intracellular dissolution by coupling novel aggregation induced emission (AIE) method with flow cytometry analysis. Bioimaging showed that AgNPs were mainly distributed in the lysosomes, whereas Ag+ (both the directly accumulated and dissolved Ag+) was concentrated in the mitochondria as the major storage site and potential acting target in ZF4 cells. These AgNPs accumulated in lysosomes induced the alkalization with a pH shift from 4.55 to 4.94, facilitating the dissolution of AgNPs. We found that both AgNPs and Ag+ triggered mitochondrial specific toxicity. Objective 3: To map the organ distribution and dissolution kinetics of NPs in the oysters In this objective, we studied the organ distribution and dissolution kinetics of NPs in biota using many novel technologies. In an earlier study, the dissolution kinetics of NPs was monitored by a novel probe. Leung et al. (2019) reported a fluorescence method for monitoring the rapid dissolution kinetics of nano-ZnO in aquatic environments. Sun et al. (2021) then examined the different dissolution potentials and subcellular behaviors of nZnO in fish cells. Yan et al. (2019) employed two AIEgens for the in situ visualization and quantitative analysis of distribution patterns of AIE-AgNPs and corresponding dissolved Ag ions in different organs of medaka larvae. Such novel AIE method simultaneously analyzed the quantitative distribution patterns of AIE-AgNPs and corresponding Ag ions in different organs of medaka larvae. AIE-AgNPs and Ag ions showed distinct distribution patterns, in which AIE-AgNPs were concentrated in intestine and liver. Luo & Wang (2022) then clarified the different immune responses of hemocyte subpopulations to silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and Ag ions in the oyster hemocytes. In another important work, Luo et al. (2022) employed two aggregated-induced emission (AIE) fluorogens AgNPs and Ag+ to study the intracellular behavior of AgNPs in oyster hemocyte subpopulations composed of agranulocytes, semigranulocytes, and granulocytes. Zhang & Wang (2022) investigated the toxicity of AgNPs to the veliger larvae of oyster Crassostrea angulata, with a specific focus on the possibility of the involvement of in vivo dissolution of AgNPs in the toxicity via an aggregation-induced emission luminogen (AIEgen)-based imaging technique. The results collectively implied that apart from the Ag released in the medium, the Ag dissolved from the ingested AgNPs may also greatly contribute to the toxicity of AgNPs toward the oyster larvae. Finally, Wang (2022) examined the various modern technologies for nanoscale (subcellular) or macroscale (tissues or individuals) imaging of metals in aquatic organisms. Weng et al. (2022) summarized the recent progress on the interactions of metals and nanoparticles with bivalve hemocytes, with emphasis on the involvement of hemocytes in metal regulation and detoxification, the interactions of hemocytes and nanoparticles at eco/bio-nano interface and hemocyte-mediated immune responses to the exposure of nanoparticles.

16102918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16102918.value: Overall, this project has resulted in numerous research findings and publications in highly profiled journals in the field. In total, 19 papers were published and most appeared in the top tiered international journals. 1. We have developed many novel techniques to study the biokinetics and bioaccumulation of NPs. For example, Shao & Wang (2020) developed a radio-synthesizing method to trace the behavior of AgNPs in an estuarine oyster. This method was sensitive to detect the bioaccumulation and depuration of AgNPs in the oysters over a short period of exposure. Through radioactive AgNPs tracing and biokinetic modeling, we for the first time demonstrated the differential uptake mechanisms of different-sized AgNPs in the oysters. 2. A major technology advancement in this project is the application of AIEgens, which can be used to actually visualize the nanoparticles and metal ion in organisms. With the application of these techniques, we have indeed achieved a few milestones in this project. We for the first time visualized and quantified the maternal transfer of AgNPs in a model zooplankton (Yan et al. 2019). We also demonstrated that trophically transferred AgNPs experienced a complicated behavior such as dissolution in the acidic gut microenvironment and depuration (Yan & Wang 2021) 3. We have thoroughly evaluated the uptake mechanisms of NPs in the biota. Li & Wang (2021) demonstrated that cellular uptake of AgNWs occurred mainly via pathways of clathrin-dependent endocytosis, caveolae-dependent endocytosis, and phagocytosis. 4. With the application of novel AIEgens, we are probably the first one to actually quantified the cellular dissolution (or animal dissolution) of nanoparticles. For example, Yan et al. (2018) directly visualized and quantified the time-dependent release of Ag+ from different sized AgNPs. We demonstrated that the ingested AgNPs were dissoluted to Ag+, which were heterogeneously distributed, with much higher concentrations in the anterior gut. 5. We are also probably the first to use cutting-edge NanoSIMS to reveal the subcellular behavior of AgNPs in any animal tissues (and cells). Shao et al. (2020) successfully visualized the subcellular localization as well as the potential toxicity effects of AgNPs in the oyster gill filaments. This study demonstrated that AgNPs induced autophagy in the oyster gill cells. Zhang et al. (2020) then showed that AgNPs were much less bioavailable than Ag+, and the intracellular Ag was mainly originated from the soluble Ag. AgNPs formed inorganic Ag-S complexes extracellularly, while Ag-organosulfur complexes were predominantly formed intracellularly.

16102918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16102918.value: There are vast potentials for the further development of this research line. One of the most important outcomes of this project is the application of novel technologies such as radiolabeling, AIE imaging, as well as NanoSIMS imaging. These technologies allow us to study the dissolution, bioaccumulation, transformation, transfer, as well as subcellular fates of nanoparticles in the organisms. We are basically dealing with the nanoworld, thus bioimaging is critical for the further development. The proposed course of action will be to setup cutting edge bioimaging facility in Hong Kong which enables to visualize the nanoworld in action. Furthermore, since nanotoxicology is a combined field of biology and chemistry, chemical techniques are also indispensable for future study. It is suggested that we should further study the nanoparticles/nanomaterials from the organismic perspectives, which are indispensable for the environmental risk analysis of nanoparticles.

16102918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16102918.value: A great concern for the application of nanotechnology is the potential release of nanoparticles (NPs) into the environment, causing unwanted human exposure and environmental risks. Many aquatic animals are able to ingest and accumulate NPs at extraordinarily high concentrations. The kinetic behavior of NPs including their dissolution once inside organisms remains very elusive. There has been a longstanding argument on the cellular/subcellular localization of NPs in aquatic organisms. We thus need a fundamental understanding of the impacts of metallic-based NPs on the environment and living systems. This research took the advantage of cutting-edge methodology to provide fundamental yet critical information about the fate, transport, and toxicity of NPs in aquatic ecosystems. With the application of these novel technologies, these studies provide fundamental information on the kinetics, accumulation, dissolution and exposure of NPs in aquatic biota for a better understanding of the fate and potential toxicity of NPs in organisms. This project is the first to visually and quantitatively monitor the dissolution kinetics of AgNPs in oysters. The information on the transformation of AgNPs gathered from this study will fundamentally improve our understanding of the unique behavior of NPs. This project will contribute significantly to the future development of nanotoxicology.

16103118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16103118.value: 斑馬魚視覺跟踪行為的神經迴路

16103118.label: Project Objectives
16103118.value: Characterization of pursuit eye movements. Identification of the visual areas and neurons underlying ocular pursuit.
rows: Identification of the visual areas and neurons underlying ocular pursuit.

16103118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103118.value: To examine an object in detail, an animal must position it on the fovea or high-resolution area of their eye via pursuit eye movements. Pursuit is a natural, ecologically relevant visual behavior that is conserved across many species, although most thoroughly studied in primates. Still, large gaps in our understanding of the neural circuits that generate this behavior remain. This project addresses pursuit eye movements in a simple vertebrate visual system, that of the zebrafish larva. These animals use their visual system to hunt prey, and have mobile eyes which they actively move as they hunt. In this model organism, we can take advantage of an array of genetic tools to label and manipulate neurons. In addition, the larvae are transparent, which allows for functional imaging in the intact behaving organism. We will first characterize the kinematics of pursuit eye movements in larvae, and determine which aspects of a visual stimulus drive the behavior. We will then use functional imaging to identify brain areas and neurons that respond during pursuit and characterize their anatomy. Overall, this project will allow us to understand a fundamental visual behavior at the cellular level in a simple vertebrate brain. 為了詳細的檢視物體，動物必須通過跟踪性眼球運動將其定位在視網膜的中央窩或類似的高視覺分辨率區域。視覺跟踪是一種重要的自然行為。該行為在許多物種中都是保守的，之前的研究主要以靈長類動物為對象展開。即便如此，我們對產生該行為的神經迴路還有待深入了解。 該項目致力於簡單脊椎動物(斑馬魚幼魚)視覺系統的跟踪性眼球運動。斑馬魚幼魚依賴視覺系統捕獵獵物，並在捕獵過程中主動轉動眼睛。在這個模式生物中，我們可以利用一系列遺傳學工具來標記和操縱神經元。此外, 幼魚是透明的，我們可以在清醒的運動的動物上進行功能成像。我們將首先描述幼魚的跟踪性眼球運動的動態變化，並確定視覺刺激的哪些要素驅動該行為。然後，我們將使用功能成像來識別在視覺跟踪過程中響應的腦區域和神經元，並描述其解剖結構特徵。總的來說，該項目將使我們在細胞水平上理解簡單脊椎動物大腦的一個重要的視覺行為。

16103118.label: Realisation of objectives
16103118.value: The goal of objective one was to characterize pursuit eye movements in zebrafish larvae, which have been studied mainly in cats and primates and had never been described in this system. We had sporadically observed pursuit-like movements in our head-fixed behavioral assay, where we project moving dots on a screen to evoke the characteristic eye convergence and tail movements of prey capture. We saw that larvae would sometimes converge their eyes and then move both eyes conjugately to slowly pursue the moving dot. However, saccade-like movements were much more common. One goal of this objective was to try to increase the number of smooth pursuit-like movements by using step-ramp stimuli, where the target jumps to a new location and then moves smoothly, and also trying a range of target speeds to find those that the larvae would smoothly follow. These approaches unfortunately did not significantly increase the amount of smooth pursuit that we observed during prey capture. Therefore, we decided to focus more on the convergent saccades, as mentioned in the potential risks and mitigation section. Specifically, we have been studying how the motor signal generated by the eye convergence is broadcast to the main visual areas of the brain. In order to stabilize the visual world and continuously track objects during self-motion, animals must have a copy of the intended motor output, called an efference copy, which is sent to visual areas. We reasoned that there should be an efference copy of the intended prey capture motor output (eye convergence and swim) sent to the optic tectum and tectum of zebrafish to allow them to continuously track the prey. Typically, larvae first spot prey in the lateral visual field, which is monocular, and then converge their eyes and orient toward the prey in order to bring it into the binocular, central visual field. Therefore, the expectation is that the prey will be able to activate both eyes and both hemispheres of the brain after the first bout. The convergent saccade motor efference copy should thus activate both hemispheres and alert these areas to expect the incoming prey stimulus. We reasoned that by blocking the input to one eye, we might be able to observe this interhemispheric input. We designed and 3D printed a device to selectively and reversibly block one eye by laterally moving one arm in front of the eye. We tested the completeness of the block by recording visual responses in AF7, a retinorecipient region that responds to prey stimuli, and found that blocking one eye completely blocked the input to AF7 in the hemisphere contralateral to that eye. We then presented prey at different azimuths of the visual field while recording calcium responses in 10 planes of the brain, and moved the eyeblocker to record the response to each stimulus in the left eye, right eye, and binocular condition. We found that, while the majority of the response was in the hemisphere contralateral to the unblocked eye, we also observed responses in the hemisphere ipsilateral to the unblocked eye, and we termed these neurons “ipsi neurons”. Towards the goal of objective 2, we mapped these neurons onto a zebrafish brain atlas to characterize their anatomical locations, and found that the ipsi neurons were located in the optic tectum, pretectum, dorsal thalamus, and nucleus isthmi. We looked at the response of these neurons when the contralateral eye was unblocked, and found that the vast majority also responded to prey input from the contralateral eye. We next began to characterize the sensory-motor properties of the ipsi neurons. While imaging we simultaneously recorded eye and tail movements, so we could classify each trail as having prey capture behavior or not. We found that the ipsi neurons in every anatomical region were strongly modulated in a positive direction by prey capture behavior. We hypothesized that this could indicate that they are receiving the motor efference copy of the eye convergence. The Nucleus Isthmi has been shown to provide bilateral excitatory input to the pretectum, tectum and thalamus, so we theorize that it could receive the motor efference copy and broadcast excitatory input to the midbrain in order to alert those visual areas to the initiation of prey capture. In some species, the Nucleus Isthmi contains a topographic map of the visual field, so we next analysed the tuning curves of those neurons. We found that the majority of Nucleus Isthmi neurons were broadly tuned, with a few responding more to the central visual field, but overall, no evidence for a topographic map. This suggests that the Nucleus Isthmi neurons are alerting the visual areas to the presence but not the specific location of prey. At this point, we have achieved the goal of objective 2 of identifying visual areas that are activated by prey capture eye movements. Due to the difficulties encountered in the first phase of the project, we do not have an accepted publication yet, but we have a manuscript which is attached in Part C, and will be submitted upon completion of a few final experiments. Regarding the grant budget, the equipment items were needed in the lab before the funds were available, so existing funding was used to purchase these items. A larger portion of the budget than anticipated was used for Research Staff, due to the need to use RGC funds for HKUST’s PG matching, and the lack of other GRF funds at the time.

16103118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103118.value: We developed a novel paradigm to study the contribution of each eye’s input to brain activity. Using this paradigm, we identified four brain areas that receive indirect input from the ipsilateral eye, the pretectum, tectum, dorsal thalamus, and Nucleus Isthmi. The ipsi neurons in all of these areas responded much more during trials where the eyes converged. Thus, we found that convergent eye movements activate visual areas bilaterally, and this input may be important to alert these areas to the prey capture motor plan, so that they are more likely to respond to the prey stimulus and trigger a second prey capture bout, ensuring the continuation of hunting and eventual consumption of the prey. These results are summarized in the manuscript attached in Part C.

16103118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103118.value: We will next use Granger Causality to identify the directionality of the input. This method allows us to whether the activity in one neuron is helpful to predict the activity of another, and thus whether they are likely to be connected. We will look for the inputs to the ipsi neurons in the midbrain to see if these areas receive input from the Nucleus Isthmi. We will also search for the source of the motor command to the Nucleus Isthmi. We will confirm these results by using laser ablation to test whether the Nucleus Isthmi is providing the excitatory input to activate ipsi neurons. Another line of research will ask whether the bilateral excitatory pathway we observed is prey capture specific. We will present a looming stimulus, which evokes escape behavior, and ask whether a separate population of Nucleus Isthmi neurons is activated, and whether the pattern of activation is different, for example unilateral instead of bilateral. These experiments will shed light on how motor activity is used update the expectations for visual stimuli, and how this is mediated by the Nucleus Isthmi, a brain area that is conserved up to humans.

16103118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103118.value: Our visual world appears stable, but it is constantly in motion due to our own movement of our eye, head, and body. Visual areas of the brain must take into account this self-motion in order to ignore self-generated whole field motion and continuously track objects of interest. In mammals, the source of the self-motion signal remains unknown. We have used eye convergence in zebrafish larvae as a model to understand how the motion signal influences visual areas. We found that visual areas that would be expected to respond to an object after the movement were activated by the movement signal, and this activation could be important for spotting the object after the movement. This research will allow us to better understand how we take into account our own planned movements in constructing our visual world.

16103718.label: Realisation of objectives
16103718.value: In mammals, it is known that hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise from the hemogenic endothelium in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM), subsequently migrate to the fetal liver, and finally home to the bone marrow, the adult hematopoietic organ. The ontogeny of HSC development is evolutionarily conserved. Like mammals, HSCs in zebrafish are also derived from the hemogenic endothelium in the AGM, subsequently home to the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT), and finally colonize the kidney, the adult hematopoiesis organ in zebrafish. However, our recent lineage tracing study have shown that this AGM-CHT-Kidney migration route may not be correct. To track the behaviors of HSCs, we generated a Tg(coro1a:LoxP-DsRedx-LoxP-GFP;hsp70:mCherryT2A-CreER) reporter zebrafish line, in which HSCs and their progenies are marked by DsRed but can switch to GFP+ upon light-induced CreER expression. Using this light-controlled cell labeling, we have been able to demonstrate that the AGM-born HSCs do not migrate to the CHT as reported by previous study, but rather they migrate to the kidney directly from the AGM where they are born. Remarkably, we have further found that the endothelium-born hematopoietic precursors (EHPs), which are also born in the AGM, are the hematopoietic cells that colonize the CHT where they undergo further proliferation and differentiation. To dissect molecular basis underlying the retention and mobilization of AGM-born HSCs, we have tested Cxcr4/7-Sdf1 pathway and cMyb, both which have been previously shown to play a role in the regulation of HSC mobilization. To do so, we designed specific morpholinos to knockdown the expression of the Cxcr4/7-Sdf1 or cmyb as well as overexpression of these molecules, and then asked whether it would affect the migration of HSCs and EHPs. Our study has shown that, while the mobilization of EHPs from the AGM to the CHT is moderately affected, the retention of HSCs remains intact. Collectively, these results indicate that, while Cxcr4/7-Sdf1 pathway and cMyb play critical role in the migration of EHPs, the retention of HSCs in the AGM region appears to be mediated by different pathways. Previous studies indicated that the integrin α4 (ITGα4) and its cognate receptors, the vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM-1) are involved in HSC homing to the fetal liver and bone marrow in mammals. We therefore speculated that perhaps the Itgα4-Vcam-1 pathway may also play a role in the regulation of the mobilization of HSCs and EHPs. To test this hypothesis, we knocked down the expression of Itgα4 and Vcam-1 by specific morpholinos. Results showed that, while the mobilization of EHPs from the AGM to the CHT is severely disrupted, it had little on the mobilization of HSCs. Token together, these observations indicate that Itgα4-Vcam-1 pathway is critical for the migration and colonization of the EHPs to the CHT region, but this pathway is not involved in the mobilization and migration of HSCs from the AGM to the kidney.

16103718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103718.value: In this proposed study, we have shown that hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) do not migrate to the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) as reported previously, but rather they migrate to the kidney directly from their birthplace, the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM). Intriguingly, we have found that it was the endothelium-born hematopoietic precursors (EHPs), which are also born in the AGM, migrate to the CHT, where they undergo further proliferation and differentiation. Moreover, we have further documented that Cxcr4/7-Sdf1 pathway and cMyb is critical for the mobilization of EHPs to egress from the AGM to the CHT, but they are dispensable for the retention of HSCs in the AGM, indicating that the mobilization of HSCs is mediated by different pathways. Finally, we have also demonstrated that Itgα4-Vcam-1 pathway is critical for the colonization of the EHPs from the AGM to the CHT, but this pathway is not involved in the mobilization and migration of HSCs from the AGM to the kidney.

16103718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103718.value: We will continue to employ genetic, cellular, and molecular approaches to explore the mechanisms governing the migration and homing of HSCs using zebrafish model system. To achieve these goals, we have recently performed single cell RNA-seq analysis with HSCs isolated from the AGM region and identified several candidate genes potentially involved in this process. We are currently generating specific mutants defective in these candidate genes with the hope that er can reveal the underlying mechanisms.

16103718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103718.value: In vertebrates, the blood cells are known to have a relative short lifespan and are required to be continuously replenished through the differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) or blood stem cells. The establishment of HSC pools in adult animals requires not only the initial formation of the HSCs but also depends on their ability to home to the suitable environment during development. Hence, a comprehensive elucidation of the mechanism underlying HSC mobilization will improve our understanding the formation of HSC pools. In this proposal, we utilized zebrafish to tackle this issue. We have successfully defined the migratory rout of HSCs and revealed the molecular basis underlying their mobilization.

16103918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103918.value: In eukaryotes, the initiation of DNA replication takes place in two well-separated steps: replicative helicase assembly and activation. Multiple overlapping mechanisms are employed to guarantee that these two steps occur in a sequential manner. In the G1 phase, the origin recognition complex (ORC), together with Cdc6 and Cdt1, assemble two copies of the Mcm2-7 complexes, the core of the eukaryotic replicative helicase, onto the replication origin as an inert head-to-head MCM double hexamer (DH). Upon entering S phase, DH is activated through recruitment of two accessory factors, namely GINS and Cdc45, to form the active helicase called CMG (Cdc45-MCM-GINS). DH activation is driven by the Dbf4-dependent kinase (DDK) that phosphorylates the Mcm2/4/6 subunits to signal recruitment of other helicase-activating factors. As such, DDK is critical for genome replication and stability. On the other hand, negative regulations of DH activation to prevent premature CMG assembly in G1 or at late origins in S phase are equally important for genomic stability. A recent study from Xiaolan Zhao’s group found that DH SUMOylation constitutes one of the negative regulatory pathways. It was shown that DH SUMOylation acts partly by interacting and promoting the Rif1-Glc7 phosphatase complex that antagonizes DDK in G1 phase, and SUMO-based MCM inhibition was removed as cells entering and progressing through S phase. Currently, the molecular mechanisms underlying the functions of SUMO in keeping the DH inactive are largely unknown. In our long-term effort to understand how the replicative helicase functions, we have solved the structure of an MCM DH isolated from yeast G1 cells at 3.8 Å using cryo electron microscopy (cryo-EM). This was the first structure of eukaryotic MCM complex solved at near-atomic resolution, and has since been used widely to various analyses of MCM-related structures and functions. As our DH preparation was performed without inhibiting deSUMOylases, known to remove majority SUMOylations during purification, no SUMO modification was observed in our DH structure. In the proposed project, we will collaborate with Profs. Xiaolan Zhao, Dirk Remus, and Ning Gao to isolate SUMOylated DH for structure determination. Because the SUMOylated DH is capable of interacting with Glc7, we will also aim to solve the cryo-EM structures of the SUMOylated DH in complex with Rif1-Glc7. The outcomes of the proposed research are expected to provide critical insights for understanding the mechanisms that underlie the regulation of helicase activation and the establishment of replication timing across genome. 真核生物DNA複製起始的過程可以分為兩個步驟：複製解旋酶的組裝和激活。多個重疊的調控機制被用以確保此過程的有序進行。在細胞週期的G1期，複製起點識別複合物（ORC），在Cdc6和Cdt1的幫助下，將MCM雙六聚體（DH）組裝到DNA上。進入S期，Cdc45和GINS被加載到MCM DH上，從而激活MCM解旋酶活性。在此過程中，DDK磷酸化Mcm2/4/6亞基，以此招聚其他蛋白因子到DH上。所以，DDK在DNA複製以及保持基因組穩定性方面，扮演重要角色。另外，調控DH的激活過程，以避免CMG複合物在G1期以及在較晚開始複製的起始位點上提早組裝，也同樣至關重要。DH類泛素化修飾（SUMO）是其中一種DH激活負調控的機制。這種修飾被發現可以促進Rif1-Glc7磷酸酶複合物與DH的結合，從而有效限制DDK在G1期的作用。目前，DH SUMO在抑制解旋酶激活過程中作用的分子機制還很不清楚。 為了深入理解DNA複製解旋酶，我們解析了MCM DH 3.8Å的冷凍電鏡結構。這是第一個真核生物MCM複合物近原子分辨率的高清結構。目前，此結構已經被廣泛用於分析MCM相關複合物的結構和功能。在之前DH純化的過程中，去SUMO化酶的活性沒有被抑制，所以，在DH結構中，我們沒有在DH中找到SUMO的修飾位點。在此項目中，我們會與Xiaolan Zhao, Dirk Remus, 以及Ning Gao教授合作，研究DH SUMO的結構。由於SUMO化的DH可以結合Glc7磷酸酶，我們也會解析相關的結構。本研究將會使我們進一步了解解旋酶的激活以及基因組複製次序建立的機制。

16104018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104018.value: Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts delaminate from a cluster of cells that express proneural genes. The fate determination process of neuroblast fate vs. epiderm cell fate is a classical example of the Notch signaling-mediated lateral inhibition process. We have previously successfully developed Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts as a system to study single-cell delamination, which is also termed ingression. We have demonstrated that an apical contractile myosin network is organized to drive neuroblast delamination. Importantly, we have found that the neuroblast delamination process is dependent on Notch signaling-mediated transcription. How differential Notch signaling activity in a proneural cluster is interpreted to regulate single-cell delamination remains unclear. In our preliminary work for this proposal, we compared transcriptomes from control embryos and Delta RNAi embryos at the onset of neuroblast delamination and identified three actin cytoskeletal regulators, Spire, Moesin, and Schip1, as Notch transcriptional targets. Depletion of these cytoskeletal regulators phenocopies the delamination defects observed in Delta RNAi embryos. In our proposed study, we will mechanistically dissect how down-regulation of Spire, Moesin, and Schip1 promotes delamination in neuroblasts. We hypothesize that down-regulation of Spire, Moesin, and Schip1 is critical for assembling a dynamic and polarized apical actin meshwork that supports pulsed myosin contractions. This work will allow us to start building the genetic regulatory network between upstream Notch signaling activity and the highly ordered morphogenetic events of single-cell delamination. 果蠅胚胎神經元幹細胞起源於表達proneural基因的神經表皮細胞團，神經元幹細胞和表皮細胞的命運分化由Notch信號活性決定的相鄰抑制調控。我們在前期工作中發現神經元幹細胞離層的形態發生過程也是有Notch信號活性調控的，但Notch信號活性如何調節形態發生過程中高度有序和動態的細胞骨架運動並不清楚。我們通過轉錄組分析和遺傳學篩選，尋找到Spire，Moesin和Schip1三個細胞骨架調節分子，位於Notch信號通路下游，調控神經元幹細胞離層過程。本項目將在機理層面研究這三個分子在神經元幹細胞離層過程中的作用。

16104018.label: Realisation of objectives
16104018.value: Aim 1: Quantitative analysis of dynamics and polarity of the apical actin meshwork in the neuroectoderm. (1.1) Quantitative measurement of apical actin dynamics in the neuroectoderm We have imagined the apical actin dynamics using a Utrophin:Venus transgenic line, in combination with an acute:7xHalotag line we developed to visualize neuroblast fate at the onset of delamination. Quantification analysis demonstrates that the actin meshwork undergoes a more frequent tear and refill process in the delaminating neuroblasts in comparison with the neighboring cells. (1.2) Investigation of the apical actin polarization in delaminating neuroblasts We examined whether the apical actin filaments display medioapical cell polarity in delaminating neuroblasts by examining actin filament polarity markers Adducin and Tmod. With the acute:7xHalotag line to distinguish early neuroblasts from their neighboring cells, we find that the degree of medioapical polarization for apical actin filaments in delaminating neuroblasts is modestly higher than that in their neighboring cells. Aim 2: Investigating the function of Spire, Moesin, and Schip1 in neuroblast delamination. (2.1) Investigation of Spire, Moesin, and Schip1 protein dynamics during neuroblast delamination. We generated endogenously superfolderGFP-tagged Spire, Moesin and Schip1 line through CRISPR-mediated genome editing. Moesin-GFP localizes at both the medial and junctional regions in the neuroepithelial cells. Both Moesin junctional spots and medial dots show pulsatile behavior with fluorescence coalesce and disassemble. We were unable to observe endogenous Spire-GFP and Schip1-GFP in live embryos probably due to their relatively low expression level. Llama-Tags have recently been adopted to visualize transcriptional factor dynamics in live fly embryos. Specifically, a Llama tag is inserted into the endogenous gene loci of interest to image the target protein in combination with preloaded cytoplasmic GFP. We decided to adopt this method to see if it is sensitive enough for visualizing cytoskeletal proteins like Spire and Schip1 that form discrete structures. (2.2) Investigating the mechanism by which down-regulation of Spire, Moesin, or Schip1 promotes delamination. We found that overexpression of Dia[CA] phenocopies spire RNAi phenotypes and promotes clusters of cells attempting delamination, supporting the model that Spire and Dia bind actin monomers competitively and down-regulation of Spire increases Dia activity to promote neuroblast delamination. We found that overexpression of Moesin and Schip1 dampens the actin meshwork tear and refill process in the delaminating neuroblasts, supporting that down-regulation of Moesin and Schip1 in the neuroblasts enables the remodeling of a static actin-AJ linkage into a linkage with rapid turnover. The pandemics in the past two years have caused several rounds of lab closures and delay in our normal research work. The findings summarized here are unpublished. In particular, we would like to confirm that Spire, Moesin and Schip1 are indeed downstream transcriptional targets of Notch signaling. For this, we have developed platforms with the goal of obtaining single-cell transcriptomics embryo atlases at neuroblast delamination stage and comparing transcriptomes between single delaminating neuroblasts and their neighboring cells. Our newly developed expertise in single cell transcriptomics have successfully lead to two publications in Development and Current Opinion in Cell Biology.

16104018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104018.value: Ingression or single-cell delamination is a key morphogenesis process for organ formation during embryo development. We have previously successfully used Drosophila neuroblast delamination as a model to study single-cell delamination. In this project, we have quantitatively analyzed the dynamics of apical actin meshwork in neuroepithelial cells. We have also developed an acute:7xHalotag line to mark and visualize neuroblasts at the onset of delamination. We found that actin regulators including Spire, Moesin and Schip1 are likely mediators of differential Notch signaling and the underlying actomyosin network that drives delamination. We also developed platforms to directly compare transcriptomes between delaminating neuroblasts and their neighboring cells in single-cell embryo atlases. This newly developed expertise in single cell transcriptomics have successfully lead to two publications in Development and Current Opinion in Cell Biology from my group.

16104018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104018.value: Drosophila neuroblast delamination remains as one of the few models to study single-cell delamination developmental process with access to genetic and live imaging tools. The majority of findings from this project remains to be polished and published. Recent work from Sarah Bray group demonstrated that morphogenetic movements can modulate Notch transcriptional activity through unclear mechanosensitive mechanisms. We would like to pursue if the delamination process can potentially amplify differential Notch signaling activities in proneural clusters and help to solidify neuroblast differentiation path.

16104018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104018.value: Morphogenesis, or form formation, is essential for cells to assemble into organs and then into an embryo with precise structures. Although multicellular organisms vary greatly in appearance and form, they all use a limited number of cellular morphogenetic movements to build various organs and embryos. We have previously used Drosophila neuroblast delamination as a model to study single-cell delamination. Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts delaminate from a cluster of cells that express proneural genes. The fate determination process of neuroblast fate vs. epiderm cell fate is a classical example of the Notch signaling-mediated lateral inhibition process. How differential Notch signaling activity in a proneural cluster is interpreted to regulate single-cell delamination remains unclear. In this project we started to build the genetic regulatory network between upstream Notch signaling activity and the highly ordered morphogenetic events of single-cell delamination.

16104518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104518.value: DISC1 (Disrupted in schizophrenia 1), a risk factor implicated for multiple psychiatric disorders, has been shown to regulate key aspects of neural development, ranging from proliferation and differentiation of neural progenitors, neuronal morphological development, and synaptic development and function. DISC1 protein has an unusual large interactome with over a hundred binding partners and is hypothesized to function as a major hub protein for signal integration of neurodevelopmental and disease-related pathways in a cell-type and context dependent manner. The majority of interactions identified in the interactome, however, are yet to be validated and the functional outcome of such interaction remains to be determined. Activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), also known as CREB-2, is one of such DISC1 interacting protein. ATF4 has been shown to play an important role in synaptic plasticity, memory suppressing or memory in various animal models. Whether DISC1 and ATF4 interact with each other in human neurons and play a functional role in regulating gene expression and contribute to disease relevant phenotypes are unknown. In collaboration with Drs. Hongjun Song and Guo-Li Ming (our collaborators as proposed in the grant application), we have made major progresses in studying the role of DISC1 in neurogenesis and psychiatric disorders. Patient iPSC-derived neurons with a rare frame-shift DISC1 mutation have previously been shown to exhibit aberrant gene expression and deficits in synaptic functions. How DISC1 regulates gene expression is largely unknown. We show that activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), a DISC1 binding partner and a potential risk factor for schizophrenia, is present more abundantly in the nucleus and exhibits enhanced binding to a collection of dysregulated genes identified in DISC1 mutant human neurons. Functionally, transcriptional and synaptic deficits are rescued in DISC1 mutant neurons with CRISPR mediated heterozygous ATF4 knockout, while overexpressing ATF4 in control neurons recapitulates deficits seen in DISC1 mutant neurons. By solving the high-resolution atomic structure of the DISC1-ATF4 complex, we show that mechanistically, the mutation of DISC1 disrupts normal DISC1-ATF4 interaction, and results in excessive ATF4 binding to DNA targets and deregulated gene expression. Together, our study identifies the molecular and structural basis of DISC1-ATF4 interaction underlying the transcriptional and synaptic dysregulation in an iPSC model of mental disorders. This part of the study has been published in Mol Psychiatry in 2021.

16104518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104518.value: We have made very good progresses in the structural investigations of the DISC1 tetramer, we have been able to obtain crystals of the DISC1 tetramer. Although the crystals diffracted the highest resolution of ~5 A, this low-resolution crystal indicates that we have homogeneous preparation of the DISC1 tetramer, which has laid a foundation for further optimization of crystallization conditions for obtaining high resolution structure of the full-length DISC1. This finding also encourages us to try using cryo-EM to solve the structure of DISC1 in complex with different binding targets. Such biochemical and structural studies of DISC1 alone and in complex with it targets will be valuable for understanding DISC1's involvements in various psychiatric disorders.

16104518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104518.value: Major mental disorders, including schizophrenia, are neurodevelopmental disorders resulting from genetic interruption and synaptic dysfunction. With the rapid progress in the identification of genetic variants conferring risk for psychiatric disorders, it becomes evident that the genetics of most psychiatric disorders are complex due to co-occurrence of multiple susceptibility variants with low penetrance, which in turn contribute to highly variable clinical phenotypes. A major missing link remains to be addressed is how genetic mutations manifest clinical phenotypes in patient. DISC1 is a representative example. DISC1 is known to bind to numerous target proteins with very diverse functions. However, the functional connection of the interactions of DISC1 and its identified targets are poorly understood. Not surprisingly, it is difficult to understand why different mutation of DISC1 may alter its function in neurons and eventually manifest into different psychiatric disorders. In this project, we examined the relationship between DISC1 gene mutation and ATF4 through assessing the transcriptional and functional consequence of ATF4 manipulation in neurons. We also reported the molecular and structural basis governing the specific interaction between DISC1 and ATF4. Together, we unravel a novel mechanism of action by DISC1-ATF4 and provide insight into the pathogenesis of psychiatric disorders.

16200118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200118.value: 為了幫助聽障人士和健聽人士之間的溝通，這個研究項目的首席研究員(PI)希望開發基於視覺的大詞彙自動手語識別和翻譯（ASLRT）系統。儘管現在已經有不少關於手語識別研究，但它們通常只輸出手語符號，而不會將它們翻譯成手語者的地方語言。 PI認為，把手語翻譯成自然語言對於促進聽障人士和健聽人士之間的交流非常重要。 口語依賴聲音和聽覺， 但手語是依靠視覺及手勢的。每一個手語詞彙的產生涉及手動信號，例如手指，手掌和手臂的運動和配置，以及諸如面部表情，眼睛和嘴巴的移動等非手動信號。我們雖然可以使用一些傳感器來追踪每個參與手語製作的身體部位的位置，但PI認為使用單個相機而基於視覺的ASLRT在目前更實用。 ASLRT和機器翻譯（MT）是類似的問題，因為兩者都可以被視為序列轉換問題 --- 兩者的輸出都是一個單詞/字符的序列，但MT的輸入是另外一個語言的單詞序列而ASLRT的輸入是圖像序列。然而，ASLRT問題更具挑戰性，因為（1）很多自然語言資源豐富，但大多數手語的語言資源很少; （2）由於手語製作涉及三維空間中各種身體部位的運動和配置，使用單個攝影機來捕捉手語意味著必須能夠從每幀視頻輸入中識別出相關信息並處理在圖像中可能會出現遮擋和照明及陰影產生的噪音; （3）每種手語都有自己的語法結構，與大多數自然語言相比，它們的研究資料比較少，但ASLRT必須考慮到手語與被轉換為自然語言之間的不同語法。 PI會將ASLRT視為端到端的序列到序列學習問題，並將使用當前最先進的神經機器翻譯框架來解決它。這包括源手語的編碼器，目標自然語言的解碼器以及用於從輸入獲得顯著語義的注意機制。因為香港立法會每週會議提供即時手語翻譯和文字紀錄，PI計劃從香港立法會每週會議錄像中收集大量香港手語（HKSL）數據來訓練ASLRT模型。以這種方式收集手語數據有幾個優點。首先，可以在相對短的時間（幾個月）內收集到數百小時的手語數據。其次，這些會議涵蓋了廣泛的主題，因而收集到的手語詞彙也更多樣化。第三，除了手語數據之外，這些會議錄像還附帶有相應視頻和文字紀錄以及唇讀數據。PI 計劃以師生培訓方法 （student-teacher training method），利用這些額外（音頻和唇讀）數據來優化ASLRT學習。 雖然這個研究項目致力於HKSL的識別和翻譯，但研究結果將為其他手語的識別和翻譯提供一般的學習框架。

16200118.label: Realisation of objectives
16200118.value: All the ideas and tasks described in the 5 objectives are investigated. However, due to the unexpected social movement and COVID-19 pandemic in the last few years, the method of collecting the Hong Kong Sign Language (HKSL) corpus mentioned in objective #1 is changed as soon as we realized that the original method was no longer feasible given the circumstances at that time. As a result, most of the investigations in the first two years of the project were focused on a new automated method of collecting an HKSL corpus with the least human intervention, and the original research ideas were performed on publicly available corpora of other sign languages. We also find that information other than speech and lipreading data may be more helpful for sign language recognition (SLR) and translation (SLT) since during inference, speech and lipreading information are not available (even though they may be still utilized during training via, e.g., multi-task learning or as auxiliary tasks as suggested in the original proposal). Specifically, we replace the use of speech and lipreading data by (body) keypoints and language information instead. For objective #1, we successfully built the TVB-HKSL-News corpus from 206 episodes of the TVB Pearl’s News Report with Sign Language program aired from Jan 16 to Aug 17, 2020. The program features real-time sign interpretation carried out by professional sign interpreters. The corpus consists of 15.85 hours of sign videos with a vocabulary of 6,490 sign glosses (for SLR) and 2,847 Chinese characters or 18,000 Cantonese Chinese words (for SLT). In terms of vocabulary sizes of its glosses and words, it is the largest Chinese continuous SL corpus and is the second largest after the BBC-Oxford British Sign Language Dataset (BOBSL). More importantly, most parts of the data collection pipeline are automated with little human intervention: (1) the videos are automatically downloaded from TVB’s website; (2) sign activity detection is performed by a binary classifier using a ResNet18+TCN model; (3) transcriptions of the collected sign videos are obtained from the subtitles shown on the screen during the news broadcast by text recognition using Google’s OCR API; and (4) automatic alignment between the sign videos and extracted subtitles. The processed sign videos are then annotated by professional signers manually. Gloss annotation is the only part in the collection pipeline that requires human effort. Nevertheless, our collection method can be easily scaled up to collecting more sign language data for SLT. A paper describing the new corpus was submitted to the International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV 2023 under review), and permission has been sought from TVB for its release to the public for research. While we were collecting the TVB-HKSL-News corpus, we successfully built several SLR and SLT models or systems that achieved state-of-the-art performance in various SL corpora for objective #4. In our paper, “Stochastic Fine-grained Labeling of Multi-state Sign Glosses for Continuous Sign Language Recognition” (ECCV 2020), we first established the basic architecture of an SLR system which consists of three modules: the visual module, sequential (or contextual) module and alignment module. Then we proposed stochastic modelling of these modules with stochastic frame dropping, stochastic gradient stopping and stochastic fine-grained labelling. In “Local Context-aware Self-attention for Continuous Sign Language Recognition” (Interspeech 2022), we proposed local context-aware self-attention to leverage both local and global contexts in a transformer-based SLR model. In “C2SLR: Consistency-enhanced Continuous Sign Language Recognition” (CVPR 2022), we proposed two auxiliary constraints to enhance the SLR backbones from the perspective of consistency. The first constraint aims to enhance the visual module by inserting a keypoint-guided spatial attention module to enforce it to focus on the informative regions. The second constraint requires sentence embedding consistency between the output features from the visual and sequential modules to enhance the representation power of both features. This is the first time we make use of keypoints information in SLR, which are extracted from the raw video inputs. In “Two-Stream Network for Sign Language Recognition and Translation” (NeurIPS 2022), RGB sign video and the keypoints sequence extracted from the raw sign video are presented as two input streams which are modelled with dual visual encoders and sign pyramid network with bilateral interconnection. The SLR features are also fed into a translation network to perform SLT. The resulting TwoStream-SLR and TwoStream-SLT models achieved state-of-the-art performance across a series of continuous SLR/SLT datasets in DSG (German SL) and CSL (Chinese SL) including Phoenix-2014, Phoenix-2014T, and CSL-Daily. Recently, in “Natural Language-Assisted Sign Language Recognition” (CVPR 2023), we improved the recognition performance on visually indistinguishable signs (VISigns) in sign languages by leveraging semantic information in the corresponding natural language. First, for VISigns with similar semantic meanings, we proposed language-aware label smoothing by generating soft labels for each training sign whose smoothing weights are computed from the normalized semantic similarities among the glosses to ease training. Second, for VISigns with distinct semantic meanings, we presented an inter-modality mix-up technique which blends vision and gloss features to further maximize the separability of different signs under the supervision of blended labels. (Notice that the mix-up technique was investigated earlier in our paper, “Mixup Learning Strategies for Text-independent Speaker Verification” (Interspeech 2019).) The resulting models again achieved state-of-the-art performance on three widely adopted isolated SLR benchmarks in ASL (American SL) and CSL: MSASL, WLASL, and NMFs-CSL. Finally, we apply the best continuous SLR and SLT model above on the newly collected TVB-HKSL-News corpus and achieve the following performance: for SLR, the gloss error rate (GER) is 35.97%; for SLT, the BLEU-1 to BLEU-4 scores are 46.8, 36.9, 29.3 and 24.2, respectively, and the ROUGE score is 42.48. These are good results considering that the vocabulary size of our dataset is large. As a reference, for the largest sign language dataset, BOBSL, which contains 1,497 hours of sign videos with a vocabulary of 2,281 sign glosses and 78,000 English words, its GER is 24.2% and its BLEU-1 and BLEU-4 scores are 12.78 and 1.0, respectively. Before we adopted the use of keypoints and language information for SLR/SLT, we have investigated various issues in automatic speech recognition (ASR) and lipreading. For objective #2, we investigated the use of the pre-trained model plus fine-tuning framework for rapid prototyping an ASR system for Hong Kong Cantonese elderly. We took the XLS-R pre-trained model, which was developed by Meta and trained with 500 thousand hours of speech from 128 languages, and fine-tuned it with 54 hours of local elderly speech collected for a clinical study ourselves. The fine-tuned model obtains a character error rate (CER) of 15%. For comparison, a conventional neural ASR model trained with the data obtains a CER of 24.4%. The work is submitted to Interspeech 2023 and is under review. For objective #3, we investigated an alternative to lipreading: instead of recognizing spoken words from lip movements, we synthesize speech from lip movements in a silent video. In a paper submitted to ICCV 2023 and is under review, we present a novel lip2wav model that can mitigate the adverse effect of asynchrony between lip movements and the corresponding speech in a video. Our new model achieves the best overall performance on three common lip2wav datasets.

16200118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200118.value: First, we create a large-vocabulary continuous Hong Kong sign language (HKSL) corpus, called the “TVB-HKSL-News corpus,” from 206 episodes of the TVB Pearl’s News Report with Sign Language program. The corpus consists of 15.85 hours of sign videos with a vocabulary of 6,490 sign glosses (for sign language recognition (SLR) research) and 2,847 Chinese characters or 18,000 Cantonese Chinese words (for sign language translation (SLT) research). In terms of vocabulary sizes of its glosses and words, it is the largest Chinese continuous SL corpus to date. Most parts of the data collection pipeline are automated with little human intervention: (1) automatic downloading of news videos, (2) sign activity detection, (3) generation of transcriptions from subtitles, and (4) automatic alignment between the sign videos and extracted subtitles. Gloss annotation is the only part in the collection pipeline that requires human effort but it is only needed for SLR and not SLT research. Our collection method can be easily scaled up to collecting more sign language data for SLT. Second, we have developed several SLR/SLT models using machine learning methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance in various SLR/SLT datasets. We first established in (ECCV 2020) the basic architecture of an SLR system which consists of three modules: the visual module, sequential (or contextual) module and alignment module. Then we proposed stochastic modelling of each module. In (Interspeech 2022), we proposed local context-aware self-attention to leverage both local and global contexts in transformer-based SLR model. In (CVPR 2022), we proposed two auxiliary constraints to enhance the SLR backbones: (1) a constraint that enhances the visual module by inserting a keypoint-guided spatial attention module to enforce it to focus on the informative regions; (2) another constraint requiring sentence embedding consistency between the output features from the visual and sequential modules. In (NeurIPS 2022), RGB sign video and the keypoints sequence extracted from it are presented as two input streams which are modelled with dual visual encoders and sign pyramid network with bilateral interconnection. The SLR features are also fed into a translation network to perform SLT. In (CVPR 2023), we improved the recognition performance on visually indistinguishable signs by leveraging information in the corresponding natural language and proposed the Natural Language-Assisted Sign Language Recognition (NLA-SLR) framework. Finally, we apply the best modelling methods from above on the newly collected TVB-HKSL-News corpus to provide the SLR/SLT performance benchmark for future research on the corpus.

16200118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200118.value: Further development may be sought in two directions: expanding the current HKSL corpus and making use of the recently successful “pre-training plus fine-tuning” modelling method. First, although the newly collected HKSL corpus, “TVB-HKSL-News corpus,” is already the largest Chinese SL corpus to date in terms of its vocabulary size, there are only two signers. The problem is that there are only around 60 professional sign interpreters in Hong Kong. With the fully automated sign language collection pipeline developed for SLT in the project, one may easily expand the current HKSL corpus by collecting similar videos (that contain real-time sign language interpretation and subtitles) from different sources at different times so that the sign interpreters will be different to get data from more signers. Second, in our current SLR/SLT work, we train our own visual module. Recently, pre-trained feature embedding model has been successfully developed and used in many areas, from natural language processing to speech and vision tasks. It is worth exploring the use of pre-trained visual encoder such as AV-HuBERT (which was trained on 1,752 hours of videos) to replace our visual module and then fine-tuning the whole SLR/SLT model with task-specific data to further improve the SLR/SLT performance.

16200118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200118.value: To bridge the communication gap between the deaf minority and the hearing majority, we have developed a vision-based large-vocabulary automatic sign language recognition (SLR) and translation (SLT) system in this project. The system only requires sign video inputs from a common camera. We have developed several end-to-end SLR/SLT models that make use of keypoints and natural language information, and local and global contexts to achieve state-of-the-art performance on various SLR/SLT datasets of Chinese, German, and American sign languages. As there is a lack of a similar dataset in Hong Kong sign language (HKSL), we designed a highly automated collection method to collect HKSL videos from TVB Pearl's News Report with Sign Language program. The collected videos are automatically processed, and each sign video clip is provided with its text transcription in Cantonese and its corresponding gloss transcription in HKSL glosses, obtained from manual annotation by professional HKSL signers. The resulting dataset is called the TVB-HKSL-News corpus. We have obtained permission from TVB to release the corpus to the public for research purposes. Additionally, we have run our currently best SLR/SLT model on the corpus to provide a baseline SLR/SLT performance on the corpus, enabling future research on the corpus to be benchmarked.

16200518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200518.value: 空調製冷耗費大量的能源，亦是造成電力需求高峰的其中一個重要成因。不需要電力驅動的被動式輻射冷卻可被視為其中一個解決方案應用於智能綠色建築。透過選擇性地反射及散發不同波長範圍的光子，當物體所散發到外太空的紅外線輻射高於所吸收的太陽熱輻射和環境熱輻射，淨冷卻效果便可達到。近來，一款被動式輻射冷卻器可以在日間乾燥氣候環境下將大氣溫度降低約5攝氏度。本團隊曾經測試同款的輻射冷卻器在香港炎熱潮濕氣候下的性能。雖然該輻射冷卻器的表面溫度在夜間可實現低於大氣溫度，但在日間卻一直高於大氣溫度。這是由於輻射冷卻器的性能受天氣狀況（即濕度）所影響。當空氣中的水汽過多時（即潮濕環境），位於8至13微米波長的大氣窗區的透明度下降，使大氣中8至13微米波段的熱輻射增加和透射減少。因為輻射冷卻器對於水汽所散發的熱負荷的吸收力強，其冷卻能力在潮濕氣候下有顯著的下跌。故此，本團隊提議使用一款不對稱電磁傳輸窗以改善被動式輻射冷卻器的冷卻效果。不對稱電磁傳輸窗一方面容許輻射冷卻器向外散發熱輻射傳輸，另一方面反射可見光及近紅外光的熱輻射。此研究旨在建立不對稱電磁傳輸輻射冷卻器的理論框架，和在潮濕氣候下實現白天輻射冷卻。經初步的模擬結果顯示輻射冷卻器的冷卻功率在使用不對稱電磁傳輸窗後提升了140％（即由每平方米21瓦提升至每平方米50瓦）。但是，不對稱傳輸的原理和性質仍未被充分了解。另外，高正向傳輸的超寬頻不對稱電磁傳輸設備還未被開發。有見及此，是次研究將建立一個多重反射模型以確認影響不對稱電磁傳輸輻射冷卻器的冷卻效能的因素（例如：不對稱電磁傳輸頻寬，正向和反向的透射率），以及為不對稱磁傳輸輻射冷卻器提供設計指導。有關實驗將被開展作為此模型的驗證理據。通過研究光子能帶結構，不對稱傳輸的微觀及基本理論亦能被了解。時域有限差分法模擬及傅裡葉轉換紅外光譜可被用來了解不對稱電磁傳輸窗的構成。最終，本團隊將設計，製造，組裝及測試不對稱電磁傳輸輻射冷卻器在香港不同天氣狀況下的性能。此研究鼓勵被動式輻射冷卻技術的研發，加強對不對稱電磁傳輸的理解和促進亞熱帶城市景觀及建築環境的發展。

16200518.label: Realisation of objectives
16200518.value: To achieve objective 1, we mathematically proved that asymmetric transmittivity (AT) of reciprocal optical devices is only realized by limiting incident light modes, reciprocal optical devices cannot guarantee AT in real applications. Nonreciprocity is necessary for optical devices to be optical diodes. The thermodynamics related with the AT of optical devices was also discussed to explain the validity of the second law of thermodynamics. Additionally, it explains why calling reciprocal optical devices as optical diodes, even when it can have AT conditionally, is inaccurate through the comparisons with electronic diodes and thermal diodes. The key difference is that travelling light has different modes, which may have different optical transmittivities in optical devices, but flowing electrons do not have such difference as travelling light, so flowing electrons make no difference in electric devices. When a reciprocal optical device is shown to have AT under incident light with certain modes, it will not necessarily have AT under incident light with other modes. But electric diodes will have this property consistently. Therefore, reciprocal optical devices cannot function as optical diodes. Only nonreciprocal optical devices that have asymmetric scattering matrix, i.e., the asymmetrical modal transmission can be called optical diodes. The idea of electronic diodes and the unawareness of the difference in the physical quantifies, i.e., travelling light and flowing electrons, might cause the incautious use of the terminology of “optical diode” for reciprocal optical device with conditional AT. This study can help to avoid the futile efforts of developing optical diodes with reciprocal materials and avoid the wrong use of reciprocal optical devices to have AT function in real applications where incident light can be arbitrary. Also, this study can help settling the dispute over the inaccurate use of “optical diode” for reciprocal optical device with conditional AT. To achieve objective 2, we propose to integrate an asymmetric electromagnetic transmission (AEMT) device with a radiative cooler for subtropical passive radiative cooling. The theoretical ground has been discussed quantitatively, in which the role of the AEMT window is two-fold. On one hand, it permits outgoing transmission of thermal radiation emitted by the radiative cooler. On the other hand, it reflects incoming radiation from the sky that lies within the same wavelengths. The underlying principle of cooling power recovery can be interpreted as follows. In humid climates, the transparency of the atmospheric window is partially lost. Without an AEMT window, intensive atmospheric thermal emission lying within the 8–13 μm spectrum results in a heavy heat load acting directly on the radiative cooler. With the AEMT window, incident 8–13 μm thermal radiation is partly reflected and the heat load is alleviated. As a result, the cooling power can be partly recovered. The cooling power of an AEMT enhanced radiative cooler, comprising a radiative cooler with emissivity of 1 within 8–13 μm and emissivity of 0.05 elsewhere and an AEMT window with forward and backward transmittances of 0.8 and 0.4 respectively, is quantified. Theoretical prediction reveals that cooling power of 50 W/m2 can be restored, corresponding to a power recovery of 57% under a humid semi-transparent sky. Also, it has been demonstrated by FDTD simulations that near-wavelength tapered metallic gratings can be a feasible AEMT device, displaying ultra-broadband asymmetric transmission with high forward transmittance of 0.8 and intermediate contrast ratio of 2 within 8–13 μm. To achieve objective 3, we built an in-lab testing facility based on a hybrid refrigerative thermoelectric cooling system, which can artificially simulate the equivalent radiative cooling effect. We characterized the system performance and preserved the temperatures of the equivalent thermal reservoir at -19.9°C and -12.7°C steadily at ambient temperatures of 25°C and 45°C respectively. Under a reference atmospheric transmission spectrum featuring a high 8–13 μm transparency, we measure the cooling powers of a representative radiative cooler and compare them with the theoretical values for ambient temperatures between 25°C and 45°C. Measured cooling powers range from 108 W/m2 to 141 W/m2, which exceed the theoretical values by 17 - 33% due to excessive heat flow through the testing cavity and heat lost to the surroundings. The method can be extended to examine thermal and energy associated performances of derivative radiative cooling devices and systems. Besides, it should be also noted that the in-lab testing facility and its simulation model can well predict the cooling power with different coolers’ emission profiles and window's transmission profile. Additionally, a selective thermal emitter is fabricated based on the optimized prismatic structure from FDTD simulations. The average emissivity within the 8–13 μm spectrum was enhanced to 0.98 by the gradient refractive index effect, while the average solar reflectivity in the visible and near-infrared spectrum was measured to be 0.95. The net radiative cooling power is estimated to reach 144 W/m2. In addition, a relatively cheap metal oxide material, TiO2, which lowers the cost but is highly emissive in the mid-infrared range has been used, also improving the cooling performance of the photonic daytime passive radiative cooler. Its net cooling power is estimated to be 136.3 W/m2 at ambient air temperature of 27°C. To achieve objective 4, a flexible passive radiative cooling sheet (FPRCS) by coating PDMS polymer on a reflective layer is studied. The cooling performance of the FPRCS, in terms of the sub-ambient cooling and net cooling power, is theoretically analyzed, and it is found that the FPRCS can achieve ~ 4.7°C sub-ambient cooling with a net cooling power of 68.3 W/m2 in a condition of clear sky. Notably, for the first time, a model considering sky view factor is built to numerically investigate the impact of obstructions, such as walls, on the radiative cooling performance, revealing that reduced cooling power can be attributed to a decreased sky view factor causing thermal emission blocking from the FPRCS and unwanted thermal absorption from the obstructions. Moreover, we have developed an efficient all-inorganic narrowband emitter for daytime radiative cooling. It shows strong solar reflection (96.4%) and highly selective IR emission (94.6%) within the atmospheric window, rendering it suitable for radiative cooling in hot humid climates. The excellent UV and water resistance of this inorganic emitter also enable its excellent durability in a harsh outdoor environment. What’s more, a dual-layer daytime radiative cooling coating featuring high optical performance and good applicability is studied. By experimentally investigating monolayer and dual-layer design, we optimized the solar reflection of the daytime passive radiative cooling coating to 92.2%, along with a strong emission of 95.3% in the mid-infrared range. In comparison with commercial white paint, the daytime passive radiative cooling coating helped to reduce the inner wall and indoor air temperature of the model house by 10.2°C and 5.6°C, respectively. Additionally, a large-scale demonstration was conducted on the roofing of a site office with an application area of 50 m2. In the midday, the daytime passive radiative cooling coating reduced the roof surface temperature by 30°C, along with a maximum temperature reduction of 6.4°C of the attic air. Finally, considering the steady state energy balance within the radiative cooling panel integrated HVAC systems, the cooling performance and indoor air temperature are evaluated by numerical analysis. A 100 m2 passive radiative cooling panel could chill water for the cooling of air, reducing indoor air temperature by 10°C, equivalent to a net cooling power of 1600 W.

16200518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200518.value: A theoretical model on the basis of conservation of energy is developed for the prediction of cooling performance of the asymmetric electromagnetic transmission (AEMT) enhanced radiative cooling systems. Cooling power is solved for a humid semi-transparent sky condition numerically, which shows that an AEMT window with forward and backward transmittances of 0.8 and 0.4 respectively could restore the cooling power of the passive radiative cooler by 57%. Second, validated finite-difference time-domain simulations reveal that an AEMT window implemented by near-wavelength tapered metallic gratings could meet the desired transmission ratio (i.e. contrast ratio of 2 within 8–13 μm spectrum) for radiative cooling. However, in the FDTD simulations, the incident light only consists certain modes in the two opposite directions, so the AEMT is not guaranteed in the real application [Item 6 in table in Part C]. On the other hand, a new cooling scheme that integrates a passive radiative cooler (PRC) in a conventional HVAC system is proposed. Under a clear sky, the system can provide a maximum air temperature reduction of 11 °C. The maximum cooling capacity of 1600 W is achieved. It can provide a cooling capacity of 23% of a 2-ton air cooling system, with a potential saving in energy consumption of 35% by supporting a conventional space cooling system [Item 5 in table in Part C]. In addition, a photonic multi-layered PRC with optimized alternating TiO2-SiO2 sub-layers has been developed, showing enhanced mid-infrared emissivity of an average value of 0.84. Its net cooling power is reached to 136.3 W/m2 [Item 3 in table in Part C]. Inspired by Saharan silver ants, we also present a geometrically modified polymer-based PRC. Its net radiative cooling power is estimated to reach 144 W/m2, exceeding records of previously reported PRCs [Item 1 in table in Part C]. What’s more, a hybrid refrigerative thermoelectric cooling system is built to generate radiative cooling effect artificially, so that radiative cooling power can be measured under prescribed and controlled environmental conditions [Item 9 in table in Part C]. Moreover, a flexible and scalable PRC in the form of a sheet that consists of a reflector layer and a PDMS layer is demonstrated to achieve promising sub-ambient cooling in Hong Kong climate. Under a clear sky condition, cooling powers of 52.4 W/m2 and 84.7 W/m2 are measured at noontime and night, respectively [Item 12 in table in Part C]. Furthermore, an all-inorganic narrowband emitter comprising a solution derived SiOxNy layer sandwiched between a reflective substrate and a self-assembly monolayer of SiO2 microspheres is reported. Remarkable sub ambient cooling of up to 5 °C in autumn and 2.5 °C in summer are achieved under high humidity without any solar shading or convection cover at noontime in a subtropical coastal city, Hong Kong [Item 15 in table in Part C].

16200518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200518.value: In this project, a number of various daytime passive radiative coolers (DPRCs) are studied. Unfortunately, current DPRCs lack cooling power modulation, leading to undesirable cooling in winter. To resolve this, it is proposed to develop a self-adaptive DPRC with solar reflectivity regulation induced cooling power modulation ability. The self-adaptive DPRC displays pure-white and possesses high solar reflectivity in summer, achieving self-cooling for saving air-conditioning energy. Conversely, for warmth in winter, the self-adaptive DPRC can automatically switch to a dark color to absorb solar heat. Light propagation mechanism with Mie scattering effects for the self-adaptive DPRCs should be investigated. In addition, current DPRCs also have the problems of UV degradation and poor aesthetics. Adding photoluminescent carbon dots (CDs) into DPRCs could be one of the solutions. The CDs can selectively absorb visible light to reveal color, and also they can convert the absorbed excitation light into emission light to reduce solar heat gain for photoluminescent cooling. Fundamental understanding of light scattering and heat transfer towards nano/micro-porous structures with photoluminescent CDs is lacking, so, this could also be a future research direction in relation to the study of DPRCs.

16200518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200518.value: In this study, we fundamentally understood that reciprocal optical devices cannot function as optical diodes. Only nonreciprocal optical devices that have asymmetric scattering matrix, i.e., the asymmetrical modal transmission can be called optical diodes. So, this study does help to avoid the futile efforts of developing optical diodes with reciprocal materials and avoid the wrong use of reciprocal optical devices to have asymmetric transmittivity (AT) function in real applications where incident light can be arbitrary. On the other hand, different photonic-based daytime passive radiative coolers are studied and developed. Remarkable sub-ambient cooling is achieved under high humidity without any solar shading or convection cover at noontime in a subtropical coastal city, Hong Kong. In addition, we also present a simple and scalable method to fabricate a dual-layer nanoparticle polymer hybrid daytime passive radiative cooling coating. The cooling coating exhibits great reliability and cooling effect when applied as an exterior coating on the roof of a real building. Overall, applying the proposed material as a roofing material is capable to save cooling energy across various climate zones, especially in the hot climate, which confirms the material’s possibility for carbon reduction and tackling global climate change.

16200618.value: 近幾十年以來量子信息科學與技術的發展揭開了量子加密領域的奧秘,在自然安全通信，量子計算和量子計量等新興領域有著極大的應用前景。 單光子作為信息載體，在這些突破中扮演著核心角色。 利用晶體、光纖、量子限制結構以及集成光學中的光學非線性特質, 大量的方法被用於產生單光子或是光子對。與散體和分散元件相比，集成光子芯片(PICs)以其良好的緊密度、可擴展性、機械穩定性以及現存半導體加工工藝優異的兼容性，是非線性和量子光源極具前景的技術平台。光子集成技術的量子限制效應和波導特性可以提升非線性光學頻率轉換的效率，並促進光子對的自激發。 在眾多的非線性和量子集成光子技術的材料平台中，閃鋅礦結構的III-V半導體鋁鎵砷具有各向同性，和較高的二階非線性，其高折射率可用於光學限制與波導。它還具有成熟的生長與製作工藝技術，是非常適用於非線性光學與量子光學集成電路的材料平台。最新研究顯示鋁鎵砷的4 ̅3 mm點群對稱性可用於幾何準相位匹配，也稱作4 ̅-QPM。這項技術避免了較為複雜的外部誘導疇反轉。當光沿著一個彎曲的軌道繞4 ̅軸[001]旋轉了90度以上就會有效的遇到一個倒置的晶格。在一個鋁鎵砷音壁模微諧振腔裡，光在一圈的運行中會有效地遇到了準相位匹配時周期性反轉域的一階光柵。此外，鋁鎵砷有與電泵光源單片集成的可能性，從而能以光泵在1550nm通信波段因其非線性光學特質產生單光子。 在這項擬議計畫裡，我們會進一步利用鋁鎵砷來探究集成非線性與量子光源。我們會研究在方形微諧振腔裡的4次或多次反彈往返軌跡引起的一階與更高階的4 ̅-QPM。多次反彈往返軌跡能在單腔往返中遇到至少兩周期的疇反轉，從而達到高階4 ̅-QPM。為了做到高效的非線性光學頻率變換與光子對的自激發，我們會利用集成波導和外加調制在方形微諧振腔裡示範模態依賴的4 ̅-QPM。
