16202918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202918.value: Below is a brief summary of some the major contributions in this project. [Journal Paper 1] This paper built off preliminary results outlined in the original proposal to develop, for the first time, a theoretical framework that describes the spectral properties of sample correlation matrices with low rank “spiked” structure, under high dimensional settings. Sample correlation matrices are used pervasively in signal processing applications, but their stochastic spectral properties were not understood for high dimensional data. A key contribution was to precisely describe the behavior of both the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of sample correlation matrices. This was achieved by using RMT to develop results analogous to conventional laws of large numbers and central limit theorems. These results present a fundamental contribution by describing classical objects (sample correlation matrices) under modern high-dimensional settings that are relevant to data science and “big data” applications. [Journal Paper 2] This paper presented significant technical contributions by describing the asymptotic spectral properties of advanced random matrix models that are encountered in canonical correlation analysis; an important data analysis method used in statistics. For these random matrices, referred to as “double Wishart” matrices, we presented exact and asymptotic results for the largest and smallest eigenvalue distributions. Our technical advances established, among other results, deep connections between double Wishart ensembles and Legendre polynomials, familiar in classical orthogonal polynomial theory. [Journal Paper 3] This paper employed random matrix theory to infer spectral properties of high-dimensional correlation matrices. Algorithms for systematically filtering out statistical noise from the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of correlation matrix estimates were synthesized into a flexible, easy-to-use software package that is applicable to diverse data sets. [Journal Paper 4] This paper exploited robust covariance matrix estimation to develop solutions for statistical classification based on linear discriminant analysis (LDA). LDA relies heavily on the estimation of covariance matrices and their spectral properties (eigenvectors and eigenvalues). Random matrix methods and algorithms were proposed to evaluate the performance of robust LDA under high dimensional, data-limited settings. This led to new insights and revealed the influence of key parameters, such as the choice of regularization and the robust weighting function. The results led to optimized algorithms that yielded superior performance to conventional “non-robust” solutions. They were also shown to provide robust classification of numerical digits based on the MNIST data set.

16202918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202918.value: There are various avenues for further development. Here we briefly indicate a few such directions. The analysis of high dimensional spike correlation matrices was performed under some key assumptions that could be generalized. Most notably, it was assumed that the ?signal? component of the correlation matrix being estimated was constrained to the top few eigenmodes. In practical applications, such signal may also be present in the low eigenmodes, and theoretical adaptations are necessary to account for these. The LDA analysis has been restricted to two-class classification problems. An important extension will be to relax this assumption to develop an analysis and design framework for an arbitrary n-class system. This extension is non-trivial and will require the development of additional random-matrix-based tools. In addition, a simple (but standard) regularization strategy was assumed, which linearly transforms the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix estimates for each class. More advanced non-linear eigenvalue shrinkage methods may also potentially lead to enhanced performance, and this would be a worthwhile future direction to pursue.

16202918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202918.value: This project has produced new statistical theory and algorithms for studying correlation patterns in large-dimensional data sets. These patterns can be very complicated and clouded by statistical noise. By introducing advanced mathematical approaches from the area of random matrix theory, this project has produced novel theory that can precisely evaluate the statistical noise present in conventional correlation estimators. By understanding this noise, the project has also led to the development of new robust estimation methods, that can better deal with statistical noise and better identify true correlation ?signals?. The proposed methods were demonstrated for various applications, including in signal processing and machine learning, and their performance was benchmarked on simulated and real-world data sets, and through comparison with previous competing methods. One of the algorithms was incorporated into a flexible and easy-to-use software package to help facilitate practical translation and promote broad application in different areas.

16203518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203518.value: 研究与探索适当的特征表达是计算机视觉领域中重建与识别任务的基础。如今，基于卷积神经网络（CNN）的深度特征已经在图像识别与分类任务上取得了重大突破。然而，传统的人工设计的特征，例如SIFT，依然在三维重建任务上发挥着主导作用。在本研究提案中，我们将基于之前对大规模图像三维重建的研究，探索新的CNN框架去辨认相似图片，以及学习适合于运动恢复结构（SfM）的深度特征。为此，我们提出了一个CNN框架去利用SfM重建结果进行局部特征描述子的学习。先前，由于缺少高质量的训练数据，仅基于学习的方法并未超过诸如SIFT的传统方法。最近，大量带标注的数据的获取，使得新一代的描述子和度量的学习成为了可能。这些学习方法通常利用了大量可匹配的局部图像数据，去训练一个高复杂度的非线性模型，例如多层神经网络。在此过程中，最大的难点之一，便是获取高质量带标注的数据。然而，在局部描述子这一相似度学习的任务中，所需求的标注并非仅在一个单独的样本上，而是在可匹配的图片对上。在之前的研究中，这一学习过程仅依赖于小规模的公开数据，从而无法保证学到的特征的表述能力能应对复杂场景下光照、视角、尺度、旋转、畸变的变化。得益于我们既有的大规模三维重建平台带来的大量数据，这一问题有望被更好的解决。我们的目标是通过深度特征，从准确率和效率两方面显著提高图像匹配的效果。其中，对于大规模图片匹配，基于学习或CNN的方法可以同时被用于相似图片的检索。初步结果已经证实了本提案的可行性。集成了深度特征的三维建模系统将会为更大规模的三维生产带来进一步的可靠性和几何细节的提高。

16203518.label: Realisation of objectives
16203518.value: We have achieved the five objectives of the project. We have developed a series of learning-based feature detectors and descriptors in Contextdesc, which started as learned local descriptors with geometry constraints integrated into, then evolved into learned and augmented local descriptors with cross-modality contextual integration. We have proposed and developed a GL3D database to effectively train and learn the descriptors. We have developed a fast image matching approach and algorithms with metric learning methods for large-scale datasets based on the learned feature descriptors. We have also proposed and developed a retrieval searching algorithm for visual similarities that integrate the vocabulary tree and the convolutional neural networks, which significantly improve the retrieval robustness and accuracy in many very large-scale data sets. In addition, we have investigated and developed the matching of different images, one from aerial and the other from ground-level positions. We have relied on the learned deep features and descriptors from these two types of reconstructed data as the training data sources. This kind of integration has been effectively demonstrated in practical large data sets. Finally, these developments have been integrated into a large-scale 3D reconstruction approach that has achieved high efficiency, accuracy and robustness.

16203518.value: There are three major research outcomes of this project. The first is the Contextdesc of learned local descriptors that is augmented with cross-modality contextual constraints (CVPR 2019). 16203518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203518.value: In many computer vision applications, it is fundamental to be able to establish the pixel correspondences between two different images of the same object or scenery. The correspondences are computed through similarities between the two images in that area, and these similarities could be learned from lots of prior data in the modern approach to computer vision. This learning of local image characteristics is called the local descriptors of the images, and this study advanced the state of the art of the local descriptors for matching different images. One of the most important applications of image matching is the first stage of 3D reconstruction from multiple views.

16203718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203718.value: A proximity graph models the similarity between discrete samples in many applications. It is formed by mapping the discrete samples to a point set in a d-dimensional space, where d is the number of data attributes, and then connecting neighboring points by weighted edges. A proximity graph is useful in applications such as classification, regression, and clustering. Although the graph construction can be formulated as a quadratic or convex program, it is time-consuming to solve such a program for a large instance and this prompts researchers to propose heuristics to accelerate computation. However, these heuristics do not offer any mathematical guarantee on the running time or solution quality. This project aims to develop algorithms for proximity graph construction with provable bounds on running time and solution quality. 許多應用都利用鄰近圖來摸擬離散樣本之間的相似性。鄰近圖嵌於d-維空間，頂點代表離散樣本，相鄰的頂點用加權邊連結，參數d是數據屬性的數量。鄰近圖常用於分類，回歸和聚類等。雖然鄰近圖可以經二次或凸面程序來建造，但耗費很多時間去解決大型實例，故此研究人員提出很多方法去加速運算。可惜這些方法不保證運算時間的上限或答案的質量。這項目旨在開發新的鄰近圖建造算法，為運算時間和答案質量作出保證。

16203718.label: Realisation of objectives
16203718.value: Given a set of points p_1, …, p_n in d dimensions, there is an implicit complete graph of n(n-1)/2 edges that connect all pairs of points. We want to assign positive weights to a subset of edges to define a proximity graph that is useful for applications such as clustering, regression, or classification. It would also be desirable for the proximity to be sparser than the complete graph which makes its processing more efficient. The edge weight assignment is performed via solving an optimization problem with the edge weights as non-negative variables. Several versions have been proposed which are convex programming or convex quadratic programming with linear inequality constraints. However, it is challenging to solve these optimization problems because there is a huge number of n(n-1)/2 variables despite that the proximity graph resides in d dimensions. Although the number of positive variables in the solution is usually substantially less than n(n-1)/2, no better upper bound is known in general. The only exception is the proximity graph defined by Daitch, Kelner, and Spielman which can have up to (d+1)n edges; however, the authors reported that it is still challenging to solve large instances in this case. In one dimension, we considered the optimization problem of Daitch, Kelner, and Spielman. The resultant vector at each point p_i is the sum of w_{ij}*(p_i – p_j) over all other points p_j’s, where w_{ij} is the weight of the edge connecting p_i and p_j. The problem is to choose non-negative w_{ij}’s so that the sum of squared norms of all resultant vectors is minimized. The dimension can model time, so the one-dimensional problem has potential applications in detecting change points in time series. We show that only the edge that connects consecutive points matter, reducing the number of variables from n(n-1)/2 to n-1. Nevertheless, standard convex quadratic programming still requires O(L*n^3) time, where L is the number of bits in the input. We designed a dynamic programming algorithm that solves this problem in O(n^2) time, which is at least an order of magnitude faster. This dynamic programming approach does not seem applicable in two and higher dimensions. It is also unclear how to solve the problem when the objective function is different from the one proposed by Daitch, Kelner, and Spielman. However, it is often true in experiments that the final solution contains substantially fewer than n(n-1)/2 positive variables. This motivates us to study a general scheme for solving convex quadratic programming problems with linear inequality constraints. We target applications in which there are many variables as in the case of proximity graphs, but many of them turn out to be zero in the end. Our idea is to iteratively solve the convex quadratic programming problem when relatively few variables are free and most other variables are constrained at zero. As the algorithm iterates, we need a strategy to free up some variables to improve the solution value, but we also need to prune the set of free variables to maintain efficiency. We experimentally determine an effective strategy for updating the set of free variables for this purpose. When compared with a single run of a convex quadratic program solver, our iterative scheme is much more efficient. Moreover, we can prove convergence if certain assumptions are satisfied. We cannot prove that these assumptions hold unconditionally; nevertheless, they are verified to hold in our experiments on the proximity graphs. Using our scheme, we can efficiently construct proximity graphs in two and higher dimensions whenever the objective function can be written as a convex quadratic function. Due to the connection of our scheme to convex optimization and the sparsity of solutions, we also adapt our scheme to solve some compressed sensing, Lasso regression, and logistic Lasso regression problems, which find usage in various applications in health informatics and business data analysis. In some problems, the objective function is quadratic, and there is an inequality constraint on the sum of the absolute values of some variables. As a result, there is an additive convex, non-quadratic component in the Lagrange dual. We extend our strategy for updating the set of free variables to handle this convex, non-quadratic component in the Lagrange dual. Our experimental results indicate that this method is more efficient than some existing solutions. As a result, quite unexpectedly, our research in proximity graphs has produced results that are useful in other applications. Once we obtain a graph that represents connections among a set of entities, we can associate the edges with time ranges that model the evolution of the connections over time. Specifically, an edge is present during the time ranges (possibly many) associated with it, but the edge is absent at other times. The time dimension raises many interesting questions about some conventional graph problems. A basic one is the shortest path problem. With the time constraints on the edges, when going from a source to a destination, we can only traverse an edge at a time when the edge is present. Moreover, the traversal time of an edge may be different for different time ranges associated with that edge. After arriving at a vertex, one may want to wait for an edge with a smaller traversal time to leave that vertex, but then this will result in a larger arrival time at the destination. Let N be the total number of time ranges associated with the edges. Let s be a fixed source vertex. We designed an algorithm to compute a data structure in O(N^2 * log N) time so that for any vertex v and any time t, we can report the journey from s to v with arrival time no later than t that minimizes the minimum total traversal time. Such a journey can also be output in time linear in the number of vertices on it.

16203918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203918.value: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) based on resistance-switching “memristive” devices is a promising memory candidate to fill the large gap in terms of speed, energy and cost, between main memory and storage. ReRAM offers memory densities comparable to NAND flash memory and fast random access comparable to DRAM. ReRAM has also been recognized as a favorable technology for neuromorphic computing and computing-with-memory applications. However, ReRAM also faces several challenges. First, when organized in high-density crossbar arrays, ReRAM suffers from the “sneak-path” problem which reduces the read margins and significantly increases the system’s power consumption. Second, the memristors’ resistance-switching mechanism is intrinsically stochastic, resulting in large variations. We have been exploring a ReRAM cell design and an information encoding scheme that together solve the sneak-path problem and significantly improve ReRAM’s tolerance to memristors’ variations. Specifically, we are proposing a hybrid memory cell, called “H3 cell”, which consists of two memristors and a minimum-sized transistor. We propose to use the ratio of the two memristors’ resistances in an H3 cell, instead of directly using the resistance values to encode information. Our preliminary results indicate that an H3 cell can achieve significantly greater data reliability under various sources of variations in memristors. We plan to implement a prototype system which will consist of an H3 cell-based memory array subsystem monolithically integrated on top of a standard CMOS subsystem. Our goals are to validate and characterize such a memory system, demonstrate its superiority over existing ReRAM solutions, and to configure it to efficiently implement dot-product operations, the dominant operations in artificial neural networks (ANNs), as well as some logic functions. Our effort will consist of three main tasks. The first will focus on the design and characterization of the proposed H3 cell, and on how to effectively use it as a memory element, as an analog dot-product element, or as a computing element. Our goal is to identify key cell-level design parameters critical to optimizing the system’s power consumption, performance, and energy efficiency. In the second task we will study the properties of an array of H3 cells, investigating its architectural issues and scalability. One objective is to explore and prototype a hybrid CMOS/ReRAM reconfigurable system that can be used as a scalable memory unit, a high-bandwidth dot-product unit, or as reconfigurable logic. In our last task, we will use the prototype for implementation of ANNs and evaluate its energy efficiency and performance.

16203918.label: Realisation of objectives
16203918.value: Our project uses the ratio of the resistances of the two ReRAMs to encode information, instead of the absolute resistance of a single memristor. Such ratio-based encoding (RatioBE) results in a much lower bit error probability (BEP) than a single resistance-encoded memristor since the chance of two memristors malfunctioning is much lower than just one. Since most of the existing ReRAM devices are binary cells, applying the 2T2R idea to the multi-level cell will justify the overhead of one transistor and memristor. The realization of objectives can be divided into three stages: cell design, multi-level cell (MLC) design space exploration, and CMOS/RRAM integration tapeout. Cell Design The first memory cell we proposed is called 1T2R, which is also known as the H3 cell. The two memristors in an H3 cell are anti-serially connected, forming a three-terminal device with two external electrodes and one internal, shared electrode. The external electrode of the left memristor is connected to the word line, and the external electrode of the right memristor is connected to the bit line. The gate electrode of the transistor is connected to the enable line, the drain terminal is directly connected to the internal electrode of the memristors, and the source terminal is connected to the sense line. An H3 cell’s logic 1 is encoded with the left memristor in an HRS and the right memristor in an LRS (HRS|LRS configuration). Similarly, an LRS|HRS configuration represents a logic 0. The state of an H3 cell is read by enabling its transistor, then applying a read voltage Vr (which is small and non-destructive) across the left and right memristors (through their word and bit lines), and finally sensing the voltage Vs at the internal electrode with a high-impedance sense amplifier at the end of the sense line. Although the H3 cell reduces the sneak-path problem, the leakage current still exists. And it is hard to integrate with the CMOS layer. To solve these issues, we proposed a modified H3 cell. Since there are 2 transistors and 2 RRAMs per cell, we also refer to this configuration as 2T2R. The two memristors in a 2T2R cell are serially connected, with two transistors in between. The external electrodes of the memristors are connected to the left and right bit lines respectively. The gate electrodes of the two transistors are connected to the enable lines, and the shared terminal of the two transistors is connected to the sense line. The two transistors must be turned on both when writing and reading. Logic 1 is written by applying a Vw on the sense line and grounding the left and right bit lines. Similarly, a logic 0 is written by applying Vw on the left and right bit lines and grounding the sense line. The cell is read by applying a small read voltage across the left and right bit lines and sensing the voltage at the sense line. If we do a quick comparison between the two proposed cells, we will see that the original H3 cell has a compact layout as it only uses 1 transistor in each cell. And a small transistor is possible because there is no need to turn on the transistor when writing. However, there is still a half-select problem and a sneak-path problem. Moreover, because the word lines and bit lines are made of metal, and because the word lines are going horizontally and the bit lines are going vertically, we need to use a higher layer of metal, which is an overhead for layout. On the other hand, for the 2T2R, as we can cut off the leakage current path by turning off the transistors of the 2T2R when the cell is not in use, there is no half-select problem or sneak-path problem, which makes it the best option energy-wise. And the left and right bit lines will not cross each other, only one layer of metal is needed, so the RRAM layout will be simpler. But the footprint of the cell is much larger not only because we use two transistors in each cell, but also because we use large FET to allow enough current to flow through when writing. MLC Design Space Exploration Once we have a solid memory cell structure for binary cells, the next problem is how to design a multi-level cell. For a resistance-based (ReBE) MLC, the information is encoded based on the resistance of a single device. If the device has the same variance across all targeted resistance values, the optimal values for the n levels and their optimal references would be uniformly distributed between the minimum and maximum resistance values. This is not true, however, for a ratio-based MLC which consists of two devices per cell. Since the probability distribution of a state s under RatioBE depends on the distributions of R1 and R2, the n states would have different variances, even when R1 and R2 have the same variance for any target resistance value they are programmed to. This makes the search for optimal references a non-trivial problem. When determining the target mean resistance values of these two devices for an optimized MLC, the objective is to maximize the separation of the resulting n ratio-based states while minimizing the variances of these n states. Given a set of physical device parameters, such as the lowest and highest resistance values (Ron and Roff), ON/OFF ratio α, and their intrinsic variability (represented as the standard deviation σ of the states of the device), we need to address a series of design issues and tune specific parameters for designing an optimized ratio-based MLC system. Our analysis is conducted on three merits: (1) The bit error probability phi, (2) the memory capacity or the number of levels n per memory cell, and (3) the programming effort or PE. Assuming an iterative write-verify programming scheme, the PE is proportional to the number of iterations used to program the device. A higher PE increases the programming time and/or energy but results in sharper distributions of the device’s states. To obtain an optimal configuration concerning a given figure of merit, we have to deal with some design tradeoffs. For instance, for a target bit error probability (BEP), maximize n; for a given n, minimize BEP; or for a given n and target BEP, minimize the programming energy (PE). We employ a rigorous mathematical approach that results in a compact model for BEP that enables (1) a quantitative comparison of how much better the proposed RatioBE is against the traditional ReBE, and (2) the effect assessment that each parameter has on the BEP, and the relationship among them. CMOS/RRAM integration tapeout To achieve our ultimate goal of ReRAM chip demonstration, four major endeavors have been made and achieved major milestones: 1) searching for RRAM fabrication partners, 2) searching for CMOS foundries that meet the requirements of the RRAM partners, 3) RRAM device characterization, 4) design of read/write peripheral circuitries to support the entire memory system.

16203918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203918.value: Adopting large resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) crossbars arrays is challenging due to the leakage currents (the sneak-path problem), and the large device-to-device and cycle-to-cycle variations of memristors. Our research mitigates the variation of ReRAM incrementally by proposing a ratio-based encoding (RatioBE) single-level cell (SLC) followed by a multi-level cell (MLC) and reduces the programming energy (PE) and time (PT) using a fine/coarse programming scheme. First, we have developed and reported an SLC comprised of two serially-connected ReRAMs (R) and two transistors (T), called 2T2R. We use the ratio of the resistances of the memristors to encode information, rather than the absolute resistance of a single memristor, as is traditionally used in resistive-based (ReBE) memories. RatioBE cell solves the sneak-path problem and results in a more than two orders of magnitude reduction in bit error probability (BEP) compared to the traditional ReBE, or up to 6 orders of magnitude reduction when combined with standard error correcting codes. Based on the RatioBE, we demonstrated its advantages over the ReBE for designing MLC systems. We derive an expression for the BEP of RatioBE and ReBE as a function of the number of levels of the cell, the variance of the resistive states’ distribution, and the ON/OFF ratio of the memristor. We validated these findings on multiple devices and showed that, compared to the ReBE on the same devices, RatioBE achieves up to 3 orders of magnitude lower BEP, or alternatively it could reduce the cell’s PT and PE by up 5–10× while achieving the same BEP. Different programming schemes can be applied to each memristor of the RatioBE 2T2R to save PE and PT. The traditional iterative write-and-verify scheme programs the memristor using incremental pulses with fixed delta voltage, which is time- and energy-consuming. Because we only care about the ratio of two memristors, one is programmed with a coarser delta voltage to save PE and PT. Once we know the variation of the first memristor, the other is programmed accordingly with a finer delta voltage. The results showed that RatioBE 2T2R using 30mV/60mV fine/coarse programming consumes 23.5% less PE than 30mV programming on ReBE while achieving 2.57x greater window size .

16203918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203918.value: 1. Design reliable voltage-sensing read-out and fine/coarse programing peripheral circuitries for the RatioBE 2T2R cells to validate the benefit of the BEP reduction and programming energy savings. 2. Design and fabricate a sizable 2T2R crossbar array with necessary control logic and read/write peripheral circuits fully integrated on chip to evaluate the potential of RatioBE 2T2R as memory. 3. Build a memory system by interconnecting multiple ReRAM memory chips and run demo applications on off-chip computing logic.

16203918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203918.value: The analog switching characteristics and non-volatility make the ReRAM crossbar array the perfect solution for DNN acceleration and high-density data storage. However, variations due to the intrinsic stochasticity of the ReRAM will incur DNN inference accuracy loss and data contamination. Thus, the variation must be tackled before the adoption of this technology. We proposed a new memory cell architecture that encodes multi-bit information using the ratio of two memristors that results in significant improvement of the BEP or higher memory density despite the ReRAM variations, and/or drastic reduction of the energy or time needed for programming the devices. Lower BEP means higher inference accuracy and less storage data loss. Higher memory density enables the chips to store larger volume of data at the same cost while the reduction of programming energy and time helps the mobile devices to last longer. Using the ratio-based encoding, we expect the ReRAM technology will achieve sufficiently high reliability and cost-effectiveness for consumer and enterprise applications.

16204018.label: Project Objectives
16204018.value: Objective A: Cache-Enabled UAV Networking Architecture Design: The limited backhaul in a team of UAVs jeopardizes the effectiveness of the proposed solution, due to the cut-set bound of the information flow. However, for content-centric applications, cached packets at the UAVs may be re-accessed in the near future, according to the temporal and spatial correlations between user requests for content. As such, the requested content can come directly from the cache of the UAV (instead of from the limited backhauls), and this approach can substantially enhance the effectiveness of the UAV network. We will therefore develop caching and UAV networking architecture, with system models that exploit the line-of-sight propagation channel to the users. We will also explore the potential for flexible configurations among the UAVs. Objective B: Optimization of Caching, UAV positions and UAV Networking: Building on the work to achieve Objective A, we will develop a framework to jointly optimize the caching parameters (i.e., what to cache, when to cache and where to cache), the UAV positions and the UAV networking among those systems. Our objective will be to maximize the end-user experience in multimedia streaming. This optimization problem is quite challenging, due to the inherent coupling of the caching and the positions among the teams of UAVs. However, by exploiting stochastic majorization-minimization theory, we will derive a low-complexity closed-loop algorithm, so that the UAV network will be capable of adapting to variations in traffic loading, user mobility and content popularity.

16204018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204018.value: 在未來，隨著通信技術的發展，無線網絡將需要不斷擴增網絡容量。各種研究表明，大量網絡容量的需求將來源於高質量的多媒體流應用。因此，內容中心無線網絡研究將是一個熱點課題。在此提出的研究項目中，針對高質量多媒體流應用，我們將考慮建立基於無人機輔助的內容中心網絡。使用無人機輔助的無線網絡進行內容流傳輸可以有以下幾個優點。首先，相對於地面基站 – 用戶鏈路中不佳的非視距傳播，此研究提出的方法允許我們充分利用無人機用戶無線鏈路中更有利的視距傳播。無人機可以通過補充地面無線網絡獲得更好的覆蓋範圍和容量，以實現更高的傳輸效率。 此外，部署無人機（在數量和位置方面）的靈活性使其成為滿足大型音樂會或體育賽事等特殊需求的理想選擇。應對具體情況，無人機可以在微型機到巨型飛行氣球或其設備組合中進行選擇。 然而，在應用無人機到內容中心無線網絡的過程中，會出現各種技術挑戰。首先，無人機沒有任何固定線路回程，所以構建從基礎設施到無人機的回程網絡很容易造成系統性能瓶頸。因此，無人機很可能在無線網絡中充當中繼節點，然而中繼節點將限制其在為高質量視頻流用戶提供服務的有效性。其次，系統需要仔細設計無人機的位置，並且應該適應用戶的實時需求。這些優化問題非常具有挑戰性，特別是當應用多個無人機進行操作。因此，在此研究項目中，我們將專注於開發核心技術以應對以上技術挑戰。該研究項目將充分挖掘無人機輔助無線網絡的潛力，並且將包含以下實際目標。 （1） 支持緩存的無人機網絡架構設計：為了克服第一個技術挑戰（針對當前可用無人機中缺少高網絡容量的回程），我們將充分利用內容中心網絡的特殊細微性質。在這種網絡中，數據內容可被緩存，並且它們同時具有時間和空間相關性。因此，無人機緩存的數據包可能會被其他用戶隨後請求。所以網絡中請求的數據內容可以來自無人機的本地高速緩存，而非來自有限的回程網絡。由此，支持緩存的無人機可以有效地增大網絡容量，並且繞過有限回程的瓶頸。 （2） 緩存，無人機位置和無人機網絡的閉環優化：因為數據內容的流行度分布具有區域差異，緩存設計將與無人機位置設計自然地聯繫在一起。 因此，此研究項目的第二個目標是開發一種有效的算法，用於聯合優化緩存內容和無人機位置。 我們的目標是將這種聯合優化問題建模為稀疏重構問題。 通過使用隨機Majorization-Minimization理論，我們將尋求開發一種低複雜度算法來解決優化問題。 該項目提出的基於無人機輔助的內容中心無線網絡解決方案可以通過大幅提高未來無線系統的覆蓋範圍和性能而產生巨大影響。 由於所提出的解決方案的部署靈活性，此類網絡也可被證實非常適合覆蓋大規模事件和沒有高容量基礎設施的服務區域。

16204018.label: Realisation of objectives
16204018.value: In this project, we have investigated the problem of cached enable UAV networking design. We have successfully realised objective A by proposing a cache-enabled UAV networking architecture, which breaks the cut-set bound of traditional relay network and successfully utilised the built-in cache at the UAV to achieve superb performance gain in both coverage and capacity for content access. By leveraging on the temporal and spatial correlation in the content access, the requested information can be coming directly from the UAV cache instead of having to fetch from the server via the limited backhaul. The proposed solution is shown to effectively enhance the capacity of the UAV network. The proposed solution also can take advantage of the more favourable line of sight propagation from the UAV to the user as well as flexible configuration and positioning of the UAV according to the dynamic distribution of the hot spots in the user requests. We have also achieved objective B and formulated the UAV position, cache placement and UAV radio resources design as a stochastic optimization problem using infinite horizon Markov Decision Process. We propose a novel concept of energy recharging station, which will substantially extend the flight time of the UAV. Using deep reinforcement learning, we have achieved low complexity and robust solution and the solution will be able to adapt to user traffic, user mobility and content popularity autonomously. In the project, we have trained one PhD student and one Postdoc (Dr. An LIU), produced 3 IEEE journal papers and 1 IEEE conference paper.

16204018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204018.value: In this project, we have verified the feasibility of UAV wireless networking and we have overcome the bottleneck of limited backhaul capacity in traditional UAV networking problems. Utilising content cache with the UAV, information request maybe served directly at the UAV without involving the backhaul link from the BS to the UAV and thus substantially enhanced the effectiveness of the UAV in assisting cellular networks. Specifically, the proposed solution can substantially enhance the coverage and capacity of the cellular network by leveraging on the more favourable propagation channel between the UAV and the users. Furthermore, the UAV is flexible to move to the user request hot spots dynamically and can therefore adapt to the dynamic loading, user mobility and changes in content popularity. To extend the flight time of UAV, we have proposed a charging station in the network so the UAV can choose to return to the charging station for recharge of the battery and update of the UAV cache occasionally. The solution is also extended to multi-UAV system. The investigation demonstrated the huge potential of UAV networking in assisting future 6G cellular systems.

16204018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204018.value: The proposed solution can be further extended to consider heterogeneous UAV with different cache capacities and different battery capacities. Furthermore, the individual UAVs may form adhoc networking within themselves for more effective information exchange.

16204018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204018.value: This project has investigated the feasibility of UAV assisted wireless networking. Utilising low cost UAV with built in cache, the UAV network can substantially improve the coverage and throughput of existing cellular network and it is a solution with huge potential for future 6G wireless systems. The solution will integrate the terrestrial (land) and the UAV (sky) in providing wireless networking services.

16204218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204218.value: The objective of the proposed project is to conduct a comprehensive study of the sensor scheduling problems by using a Markov decision process (MDP) and an index theory approach. This approach will enable us to derive the optimal scheduling policies in a unified framework. Sensor scheduling problems arise frequently in modern large-scale cyber-physical systems as the number of sensors involved to provide real-time measurements is huge but the communication resources (network bandwidth and communication energy) are limited. Based on the information for decision making, existing sensor scheduling strategies can be mainly categorized into two classes, namely, offline scheduling and online scheduling. Offline schedules are easy to design and implement, but the network resource is not fully utilized and the performance tradeoff is not desirable. Online schedules use real-time data for the scheduling decisions; however, most designs assume a fixed event-triggered form. As a result, no optimality can be guaranteed. Furthermore, because of the exponentially growing computational complexity, the design of optimal schedules for multiple sensors has been rarely touched. We will build a general MDP framework to study the sensor scheduling problem. To avoid a brute-force numerical computation for the optimal solution and facilitate online implementation, we will investigate which type of scheduling problems can be solved by using the index theory which provides a scheduling policy in a closed form and hence considerably reduces the computation overhead. For these problems, we will further develop methods to systematically compute the indices. For the other non-indexable problems, we will adopt other efficient numerical methods, such as reinforcement learning and distributed optimization, to numerically compute the optimal scheduling problems. The expected results will provide standard design procedures for general sensor scheduling problems, transforming large-scale sensor deployment and the resulting system performance analysis from impractical to practical, and from a tedious case-by-case study to a streamlined systematic study for a wide range of applications. 本項目的目標為運用馬爾科夫決策過程和指標理論方法，對傳感器調度問題進行全面研究。該方法使我們能夠在統一的框架裏得到最佳的調度策略。現代大規模網絡物理系統應用了大量實時測量的傳感器，然而通信資源（如網絡帶寬和通信能量）的限制使得傳感器調度問題的研究變得越來越重要。 基於決策信息，現有的傳感器調度策略可以主要分成以下兩類：離線調度和在線調度。離線調度易於設計和實施，但是由於沒有充分利用網絡資源，導致系統性能並不理想。在線調度根據實時數據進行決策分析，然而由於大多數設計均采用了固定事件的觸發模式，系統性能也無法達到最佳。此外，由於計算復雜度呈指數增長，很少有研究涉及多個傳感器的最佳調度的設計。 為了研究此類問題，我們擬建立一個通用的馬爾科夫決策過程框架。 我們首先研究可以用指標理論解決的問題。這些問題的調度策略具有閉式表達式，避免了暴力求解帶來的計算資源消耗，而且便於在線實現。針對此類特定調度問題，我們將進一步提出系統化計算其指數的方法。 對於其他不可被指標理論解決的問題，我們采用其他有效的數值方法，如強化學習和分布式優化，來尋找最佳調度方案。 預期成果將為傳感器調度問題提供標準的設計流程，使大規模的傳感器部署以及相應的系統性能分析在一系列廣泛的應用場景下由難以實行變得切合實際，由繁瑣的個案分析統一為流線型的系統化分析。

16204418.label: Project Objectives
16204418.value: To discuss the potential threats to on-body wearable communications. To systematically characterize on-body radio propagation signatures. The human body is mainly a low-loss dielectric medium at microwave frequencies, including Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequency bands. Thus, the human body has a significant impact on radio propagation between two devices carried by a user. Antenna polarization also has a significant impact on on-body propagation. To design SecureTag, which will leverage the characteristics of creeping waves to improve security of on-body wearable devices. To construct a propagation profile to authenticate on-body devices by decomposing RSS traces into different levels of variations for radio propagation feature extraction. To design SecureScatter, which will take advantage of the received data information and the radio propagation signatures described above to authenticate on-body backscatter devices. To implement SecureTag as a background service on Android-based smartphone. To implement the prototype of SecureScatter using Universal Software Radio Peripherals (USRPs)[45] and backscatter tags. To evaluate the performance of SecureTag and SecureScatter in indoor and outdoor areas in an uncontrolled manner.

16204418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204418.value: The Internet of Things (IoT), through which all the smart objects in our daily life become part of the Internet, has become one of today's most promising communication paradigms. An essential part of the IoT vision is to deliver human-centric services by sensing users’ biometrics and activities by leveraging on-body wearable devices. Ultra-low power communication technologies, such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and battery-free backscatter communication [1], have drawn significant attention to on-body wearable communications. However, those communications are also vulnerable to malicious attacks. Recent studies have shown that wireless connectivity can be compromised to send unauthorized commands to make wearable devices malfunction[2, 3]. Due to their resource-limited nature, wearable devices lack sophisticated user interfaces and powerful computational capabilities, which prevents the direct adoption of the traditional Pre-Shared Key (PSK) security protocols and device authentication methods. In this project, we propose to design new technologies to enable authentication of on-body wearable devices without hardware modification. One of our key insights is that on-body radio propagation is dominated by creeping waves diffracted from human tissue and trapped along the body’s surface [4, 5], whereas the radio waves of off-body links are mainly composed of direct line-of-sight and multi-path propagations. Our preliminary study [6] demonstrated that the received signal strength traces from commercial off-the-shelf wearables can be used to recognize wearers. Motivated by this observation, in this project, we will develop SecureTag, an on-body detection framework that can exploit the distinct radio propagation signature of the typical wireless transmission technology (e.g., BLE) to discern on-body devices. An approach with a low hardware cost will be proposed to improve security protection for on-body wearables by extracting the distinct creeping wave propagation features. Backscatter has become a compelling technology for on-body wearable devices due to the battery-free communication nature. However, the security dimension of backscatter remains unexplored. In this project, we will take the first step to explore the feasibility of authenticating on-body backscatter devices without modifying them. We propose to develop SecureScatter, a physical-layer solution that will exploit the distinct on-body backscatter propagations to verify a sender’s identity. SecureTag and SecureScatter will be evaluated in various environments to demonstrate their effectiveness against different attackers. Wearable technology is making inroads into many facets of our lives. It is essential to have a secure communication solution to fully support versatile IoT devices to maximize the likelihood of its widespread acceptance, which has tremendous technological and social significance. 通過物聯網技術的發展，我們日常生活中所有的智慧物品都成為互聯網的壹部分。物聯網願景的壹個重要部分是利用可穿戴設備, 通過感知使用者的生物特徵和活動來提供人性化的服務。超低功耗通信技術, 如低能耗藍牙(BLE) 和無電池反向散射通信, 引起了人們的高度重視。但是, 這些通信也容易受到惡意攻擊。最近的研究表明, 通過利用無線連接發送未經授權的命令，可以使可穿戴設備出現故障 。由於其資源有限, 可穿戴設備缺乏複雜的使用者界面和強大的計算能力, 這就阻礙了傳統的事先共享密鑰(PSK)的安全協定和設備身份驗證的直接採用。 在這個項目中, 我們建議設計新的技術, 以便在沒有硬體修改的情況下對人體可穿戴設備進行認證。我們的壹個關鍵見解是, 人體表面的無線電傳播主要是由人體組織衍射的爬行波控制, 並沿著身體表面發生, 而離體鏈路的無線電波是由直接視線和多徑傳播組成的。我們的初步研究表明, 從目前市面已有的可穿戴設備收到的信號強度情況可以用來識別佩戴者。根據這壹觀察, 在這個項目中, 我們將開發SecureTag, 壹個人體檢測框架，可以利用典型無線傳輸技術(如BLE)獨特的無線電傳播特徵來辨別身體上設備。通過提取不同的爬行波傳播特徵, 提出了壹種低成本的方法, 以提高在人體上的可穿戴設備的安全級別。 由於無電池通信特性, 背向散射已成為壹種引人註目的可穿戴設備通信技術。然而, 背向散射的安全性質仍未充分探索。在這個項目中, 我們將首次探索並驗證在不修改設備的前提下進行後向散射設備的安全驗證。我們提出開發SecureScatter, 壹個物理層的解抉方案, 將利用身體反向散射傳播的特性來驗證發送者的身份。我們將在不同的環境下驗證SecureTag和SecureScatter, 以證明它們面對不同攻擊者的有效性。 可穿戴技術正在進入我們生活的方方面面。壹套安全的通信解抉方案對於可穿戴設備的大規模接受和推廣至關重要，具有巨大的技術和社會意義。

16204418.label: Realisation of objectives
16204418.value: All the objectives proposed in this project had been achieved. 1) discuss the potential threats for IoT devices and communications Recently, the link establishment and data sharing IoT devices and AP have become more and more indispensable. In a smart home, an IoT device needs to establish the connection with an AP when they are trying to share message with each other. However, this establishment process is easily attacked by an active attacker. For example, when initializing the pairing with a challenge response protocol, this device who intends to share information with an AP sends a message (Message 1) for request. If the AP receives this message, it sends an acknowledgement message (Message 2) back. Finally, the IoT device receives Message 2 and feeds back the message (Message 3). However, during this process, an active attacker can launch two types of attacks to this AP and break the establishment:  In a basic attack. An attacker can impersonate the legitimate IoT device with the same MAC address and login credential. Then, it can be placed at different locations to send the same packets as the legitimate IoT device to the AP. If we lack a reliable secure scheme, this attacker will fool the AP to establish a malicious connection.  In an advanced attack. If an attacker is equipped with powerful hardware and process ability, the system would be easily attacked. In particular, a powerful attacker who has the prior knowledge of the protocol and the legitimate IoT device (e.g., the MAC address, the coding scheme, the carrier frequency, the backscatter sequence, and signal strength) can successfully detect the initialization of the communication and estimate the channel state between itself and the AP. Then, based on the estimation and the priori knowledge, this attacker can craft a multi-path signal similar to the legitimate IoT device. Finally, the attacker sends this well-designed signal with a directional antenna directly to spoof the AP. Accordingly, the AP receives the signal from the attacker and believe that this fake message is from a legitimate IoT device, which leads to unauthorized access to the AP. Considering the nature of IoT devices, which include single antenna design and sparse traffic, proper threat model is discussed in this project. Specifically, it is assumed that an attacker has some prior knowledge of the protocols and legitimate devices, such as SSID, MAC address, secret credentials, carrier frequency, coding scheme, etc. The attacker may sniff traffic to get basic information of legitimate devices (e.g., device type) and further infer more from the Internet. Thus, it can assemble packets following the well-known Wi-Fi protocol or copy one legitimate device's identity but include fake command/data to fool the other. 2) Securing IoT Devices by Exploiting Backscatter Propagation Signatures The low-power radio technologies open up many opportunities to facilitate Internet-of-Things (IoT) into our daily life, while their minimalist design also makes IoT devices vulnerable to many active attacks. In this work, we first discussed the potential threats to the IoT devices and argue that a lightweight mechanism designed for securing these devices is critical. We also investigated the fine-grained signatures of radio propagations used to defend against active attacks, which motivates our design of using backscatter tags to secure IoT devices. In this work, we proposed ShieldScatter, a lightweight system that attaches low-cost tags to single-antenna devices to shield the system from active attacks. The key insight of ShieldScatter is to intentionally create multi-path propagation signatures with the careful deployment of tags. These signatures can be used to construct a sensitive profile to identify the location of the signals’ arrival, and thus detect the threat. In addition, we also designed a tag-random scheme and a multiple receivers combination approach to detect a powerful attacker who has the strong priori knowledge of the legitimate user. We prototyped ShieldScatter with USRPs and tags to evaluate our system in various environments. The results shown that even when the powerful attacker is close to the legitimate device, ShieldScatter can mitigate 95% of attack attempts while triggering false alarms on just 7% of legitimate traffic. 3) Improving Wireless Security of Single-Antenna IoT Devices With the arrival of the Internet-of-Things era, IoT devices and the services built on them make our lives more convenient and raise public concerns on their vulnerability to attacks. There are still no satisfying solutions for IoT devices with a single antenna and sparse traffic. In this work, the threat model we introduced assumed that an attacker has some prior knowledge of the protocols and legitimate devices. In this work, we introduced SecurePilot, which is an unsupervised and plug-and-play solution which works without an attacker's knowledge in advance. It leverages the strengths of two orthogonal physical-layer information, propagation signatures and device signatures embedded in pilot signals to enable effective attack detection. It could work on single-antenna IoT devices with sparse traffic and also work compatibly with communication protocols. The experimental results show that SecurePilot can successfully detect 99.6% of attacks. 4) Single-Antenna Device-to-Device Localization in Smart Environments With Backscatter In this work, we ask the following question: can we localize the more generally used single-antenna devices (e.g., IoT) using another single-antenna device (e.g., smartphone or smartwatch) in a smart environment where low-cost backscatter tags are widely deployed on walls or smart objects? In this work, we present TagLoc, a lightweight system that enables D2D localization without relying on large antenna arrays. Our observation is that the reflected signals from the ambient smart environment can be exploited to eliminate the requirement of bulky antenna arrays that are unachievable for the simple-designed IoT devices. Specifically, TagLoc creates multiple direction signatures using backscatter arrays in smart environments. Then, the receiver can accurately estimate the direction signatures from the transmitter to the arrays and then localize the target by cooperating all tag arrays. We prototype TagLoc using two single-antenna Intel NUCs with off-the-shelf Intel 5300 WiFi cards and customized backscatter tags. The results show TagLoc can achieve robust performance in a real indoor environment with a median localization error of 0.82 m. 5) Forgery Attack Detection Using Wi-Fi Channel State Information The cybersecurity breaches expose surveillance video streams to forgery attacks, under which authentic streams are falsified to hide unauthorized activities. The recent work correlates time-series camera and wireless signals to detect looped videos but cannot realize fine-grained forgery localization. To overcome these limitations, we propose Secure-Pose, which exploits the pervasive coexistence of surveillance and Wi-Fi infrastructures to defend against video forgery attacks in a real-time and fine-grained manner. We observe that coexisting camera and Wi-Fi signals convey common human semantic information and forgery attacks on video streams will decouple such information correspondence. Particularly, retrievable human pose features are first extracted from concurrent video and Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) streams. Then, a lightweight detection network is developed to accurately discover forgery attacks and an efficient localization algorithm is devised to seamlessly track forgery traces in video streams. We implement Secure-Pose using one Logitech camera and two Intel 5300 NICs and evaluate it in different environments. Secure-Pose achieves a high detection accuracy of 98.7% and localizes abnormal objects under playback and tampering attacks.

16204418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204418.value: IoT, especially Wearable devices play important roles in many applications. Ultralow power communication technologies, such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and battery-free backscatter communication, have drawn significant attention to IoT devices and wearable communications. In this project, we have proposed several designs to significantly enhance the security of communication between IoT and especially wearable devices. With more application scenarios being considered and with more diverse IoT devices and communication manner, we can further explore the direction for future research.

16204418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204418.value: The Internet of Things (IoT) has become one of today's most promising communication paradigms. Ultra-low power communication technologies, such as backscatter communication, have drawn significant attention. However, those communications are also vulnerable to malicious attacks. Due to their resource-limited nature, many IoT devices lack sophisticated user interfaces and powerful computational capabilities, which prevents the direct adoption of the traditional security protocols and authentication methods. In this project, we discussed the threat models for IoT communications and proposed several novel solutions accordingly. Specifically, we proposed ShieldScatter, a lightweight system that attaches low-cost tags to single-antenna devices to shield the system from active attacks. We introduced SecurePilot, which is an unsupervised and plug-and-play solution which works without an attacker’s knowledge. It leverages the propagation signatures and device signatures embedded in pilot signals to enable effective attack detection. We also developed TagLoc, a lightweight system that enables D2D localization without relying on large antenna arrays. Moreover, we proposed Secure-Pose, which exploits the coexistence of surveillance and Wi-Fi infrastructures to defend against video forgery attacks in real-time. It is essential to have a secure communication solution to fully support versatile IoT devices, which has tremendous technological and social significance.

16204518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204518.value: Traffic signal control is one of the most cost-effective means for managing urban congestion. The average benefit-to-cost ratio of traffic signal projects is estimated to be 40 to 1, indicating that significant benefits can be gained from traffic signal improvements. This is easier said than done, however, as most signals are operated offline, with limited ability to adapt to traffic conditions, and existing adaptive signal systems developed in the 1980s and 1990s are based on decades-old technologies. Recently, the advancement of connected vehicle (CV) and navigation technology has produced large amounts of vehicle trajectory data. This, together with recent efforts in traffic flow modeling and control methods, makes now an opportune time to combine these advances, to substantially improve traffic signal control. A proper traffic control model must incorporate three fundamental characteristics of traffic flow: dynamic, spatial, and stochastic. This project will develop a signal control approach that encapsulates a dynamic traffic model (DTM) to capture the temporal and spatial dimensions of queuing, including queue spillback and blockage, which are critical for managing oversaturated traffic. To address stochastic traffic demand, we will embed the DTM within a stochastic programming approach. The objective of the stochastic program will be to minimize expected traffic delay as demand varies stochastically and dynamically. Integrating a DTM within a stochastic programing approach will open up new ways of developing adaptive signal control systems. Adaptive traffic control requires real-time demand and queuing information as feedback. This proposed project will investigate the fusion of vehicle trajectory data, detector data, and DTM output to estimate key parameters for real-time traffic control. Based on the expectation-maximization (EM) approach, the key parameters will be estimated by maximizing the likelihood of observing the trajectory data given the model output. To investigate how the estimation procedures and control scheme can be integrated, this project will develop a software-in-the-loop system by linking the adaptive control scheme and real-time estimation procedure to a refined traffic simulation platform. This software-in-the-loop system will be instrumental for evaluating different kinds of estimation and adaptive control strategies. The adaptive traffic control system and data fusion procedure will be evaluated in a real context. We have been working with Didi Chuxing (http://www.didichuxing.com/en/), the largest ride-sharing company in China, and gained their consent to use some of their trajectory data collected in some major cities in China, to calibrate the procedures and evaluate the performance of the system. 交通燈信號控制是道路擠塞管理的最經濟有效的方法之一。據估計，交通信號項目的平均收益成本比率可高達40比1，這表明交通燈信號控制可帶來顯著效益，然而實際應用中遠遠未達到這樣的效果。大多數的交通信號是離線操作，限制了對實時交通條件的自適應調節能力。另一方面，目前已有的自適應信號控制系統基本上是基於80和90年代的傳統技術發展而成的。近年來，車聯網技術和導航技術的發展帶來了大量的車輛軌跡數據， 結合交通流動模型和控制方法上的進步，這為交通信號控制的實質性提高提供了非常好的機遇。 交通控制模型應當考慮交通流動三個方面的基本特性：動態性、空間性和隨機性。這個項目將會創建一種新的信號控制的方法，通過這方法結合一個動態交通模型來描述排隊的時間與空間的特性，包括排隊溢出和阻塞上游路口等的現象，這對飽和狀態下的交通管理至關重要。考慮到交通需求的隨機性，我們將隨機規劃的方法嵌入到動態交通模型中。隨機規劃的目標是在需求隨機、動態變化的條件下達至最小化期望交通延誤。在動態交通模型中整合隨機規劃模型將為發展自適應信號控制系統開辟全新的方法。 自適應交通控制需要實時的交通需求和排隊信息的反饋。這個項目將會研究如何融合車輛軌跡數據、檢測器數據、以及動態交通模型的輸出數據，來估測實時交通控制的關鍵參數。基於最大期望算法（expectation-maximization），在給定模型輸出條件下，關鍵參數將通過對觀測數據的最大似然估計獲得。為了研究參數估測方法和控制方案如何整合，這個項目會建立一個軟件在環（software-in-the-loop）系統。該系統會將自適應控制方案與實時參數估測方法連結作為一個改良的交通仿真平台。這一軟件在環系統將對評估不同估測方法和自適應控制策略起重要作用。 協調自適應交通控制系統和數據融合將會進一步在實際應用背景下進行評估。我們已經同滴滴出行（中國最大的共享乘車公司，http://www.didichuxing.com/en/）建立了合作，允許使用在中國一些主要城市收集的軌跡數據，用以校準估測方法並評估系統性能。

16204618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204618.value: Cyclic liquefaction refers to dramatic loss of stiffness and strength of soils during earthquake shaking. During the past earthquakes, significant structural and ground damages were associated with large deformation in post-liquefaction and excessive ground settlement after reconsolidation. Yet, granular soils are different from classical continuum media in that they are neither fluid nor solid. Recent laboratory and field observations demonstrated that internal soil structures play an important role in liquefaction initiation and the development of large deformation in post-liquefaction processes. Therefore, knowing the particle-scale information of granular particles and void space, collectively termed as “fabric”, is crucial for obtaining a fundamental understanding of liquefaction in granular soils. While the geotechnical community has long known that liquefaction results in significant changes in soil fabric, a clear characterization of these changes has been lacking. Present methods for liquefaction triggering and post-liquefaction behaviors are mainly based on back analysis of limited field observation without explicit consideration of soil fabrics. Existing constitutive models for cyclic liquefaction are mostly phenomenological in nature without incorporating particle-scale information. As a result, it is still a big challenge to realistically predict large post-liquefaction flow deformation and subsequent settlement using existing models. This proposed project aims at improving fundamental understanding of the soil liquefaction mechanism through particle-scale investigation using the state-of-the-art laboratory tests and numerical modeling. In the proposed project, X-ray tomography will be used to probe microstructure of 3D granular packing during the liquefaction processes (Task 1). The experiment will generate unique data for direct observation of soil fabrics and their evolution during liquefaction processes. To validate various hypothesis in the micromechanical study, 3D discrete element simulations will be conducted. The numerical simulation, once calibrated from the laboratory tests, will be used to trace movement of millions of grains by considering realistic particle shape, different packing density and various loading conditions (Task 2). Based on extensive numerical simulation, new fabric indices will be proposed to quantify the evolution of the particle-void distribution within the granular packings under various condition (Task 3). As the overarching goal of the research will be to provide micromechanical basis for constitutive modeling of cyclic liquefaction, the study will link microscale information to macroscale behaviors by studying the relationships between stress, strain, mircostructure change, fabric evolution and energy consumption in the liquefaction processes, with a particular focus to improve modeling of post-liquefaction large deformation (Task 4). 砂土液化指在地震動力荷載作用下土體完全喪失剛度和承載力。在過去的地震中，液化後的大變形流動及固結沉降造成了嚴重的地基失穩和結構破壞。然而，顆粒土體與連續介質不同，它既不是流體也不是固體。最近的實驗和現場觀測表明，砂土的內部結構在液化誘發和液化後大變形過程中起重要作用。因此，研究砂土的顆粒尺度特性和孔隙結構，統稱為微觀結構，對於深刻理解砂土液化機理至關重要。雖然岩土工程界早已了解砂土液化會導致土體微觀結構發生顯著變化，對這種變化卻缺乏明確的表徵。目前的研究主要通過反演有限的現場觀測來研究砂土液化誘發和液化後的大變形行為，並沒有考慮土體的微觀結構。而現有的砂土液化本構模型本質上是基於表象的，而不包含砂土顆粒尺度的信息。因此，使用現有模型準確預測液化後的大變形流動和固結沉降仍是巨大的科學挑戰。 本研究項目旨在通過先進的顆粒尺度實驗測試和數值模擬，提高對砂土液化機理的基本認知。本研究的第一項課題將使用X射線掃描探測砂土液化過程中顆粒體的三維微觀結構特徵，這些實驗為直接觀測砂土液化過程中的微觀結構及其演化提供獨有的數據。本研究的第二項課題將通過三維離散元模擬驗證微觀力學中的各種假設。這些數值模擬經實驗數據校准後，將考慮顆粒體真實形狀、不同密度及各種加載條件，追踪數以百萬計的顆粒運動軌跡。在大量數值模擬的基礎上，本研究第三項課題將提出新的微觀結構指標以量化各種條件下的顆粒、孔隙分佈和演化規律。本項目將通過研究砂土液化過程中的應力、應變、微觀結構演化、能量耗散等關係，建立宏微觀跨尺度模型，特別是液化後的大變形機制，最終為發展砂土液化本構模型提供微觀力學基礎。

16204618.label: Realisation of objectives
16204618.value: Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI and his coworkers have successfully conducted a series of cyclic liquefaction tests using Cyclic Torsional Shear Apparatus at HKUST (Task 1). More than 60 liquefaction/reliquefaction tests were conducted on medium/dense Toyoura sand of relative density of 40-70% at various loading intensities (cyclic stress ratios are 0.15, 0.2, 0.25). We are able to quantify soil structure (termed as soil fabric) directly from laboratory tests. We discovered that soil samples develop different anisotropic fabric during post-liquefaction shearing and reconsolidation consolidation, which will significantly influence their liquefaction resistance. The laboratory tests have successfully quantified effects of strain history and induced anisotropy on liquefaction resistance of Toyoura sand. A journal paper [J5] (Fardad Amini et al. 2020) has been published in ASCE Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering, a top journal in the field. The dynamic properties of Toyoura sand in liquefaction/reliquefaction process have been summarized in a paper published in Géotechnique Letter [J7]. In this project, X-Ray tomography data on Toyoura sand particles has been collected (Task 1). The tomography data is very important to model realistic particle shapes and study the microstructure of the granular packing. Based on X-ray tomography data, we developed a computational framework for simulating complex shaped particles using spherical harmonics [J1] and clumped-DEM [J8]. A series of 3D Discrete Element Method (DEM) simulations were conducted to simulate cyclic liquefaction (Task 2). The DEM provides a convenient and cost-effective numerical approach to trace individual sand particles directly. In the DEM simulation, clumped particles have been constructed to model non-spherical sand grains in accordance with X-Ray tomography data. The results have been published in ASCE Journal of Engineering Mechanics [J8], a top journal in the field. Project objective 2 has been fully achieved. According to the research plan (Task 3), fabric anisotropy and fabric evolution in soil liquefaction have been investigated through the DEM, with an aim to connect microstructure information to macroscopic behaviors to improve liquefaction modeling. These major results have been summarized in a journal paper [J4] (Wei et al. 2020) published in Acta Geotechnica. Through the DEM simulation, it is demonstrated that granular soils have vastly different liquefaction resistance under different loading conditions. The evolution of anisotropy in contact-based fabric and void-based fabric was systematically quantified. We verified that the hypothesis stated in the proposal, that the same ‘‘stable state’’ of soil fabric will be reached under different multidirectional loading paths. Through the DEM simulation, we studied the evolution of void-based fabric indices from flow to jamming state. A Hardening State Line (HSL) is defined for jamming transition for each 3D packing. Interestingly, we found that the HSL appears to be unique and independent of loading paths for a given packing. The DEM study provides a new perspective in terms of microstructure evolution of granular soils under a variety of loading conditions. Some important results are also obtained regarding Task 4, linking microstructure information to macroscopic behaviors. In the laboratory tests, we found that the liquefaction/reliquefaction resistance of Toyoura sand can be quantified using an energy-based criterion with consideration of the integrated effects of strain history and soil fabric [J5] (Fardad Amini et al. 2020). Through DEM study, we developed correlations to connect the soil fabric, namely, the coordination number and fabric anisotropy (Z, ac), to macroscopic behaviors such as soil liquefaction resistance (Yang et al. 2022 [J8]). The DEM simulation generates data that are consistent with laboratory tests and provides micromechanical insights into the liquefaction/reliquefaction phenomenon. In this project, we also developed a new void-based fabric based on 3D Voronoi tessellation [C1, C2] (Bokkisa et al. 2019) to better characterize complicated soil packing. The results have been presented in the 7th International Conference on Earthquake Geotechnical Engineering held at Roma, Italy in June 2019 [C1] (Bokkisa et al. 2019). Many researches have also been conducted to improved numerical modeling of discrete bodies. A journal paper has been published in Computers and Geotechnics [J1] (Fan et al. 2020a). We also proposed the so-called cone-complementary algorithm to handle various numerical challenges associated with inter-particle contact. Two journal papers on this topic have been published in Computers and Geotechnics [J2] (Fan et al. 2020b) and International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering [J3] (Fan et al. 2020c), and Applied Mathematical Modeling [J6] (Fan et al. 2021). 16204618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204618.value: Major findings: 1. A series of (more than 60) laboratory tests were conducted to study the liquefaction and postliquefaction behavior of loose and medium dense Toyoura sand. The tests were conducted by using torsional shear apparatus, with a relative density 40-70%, under various loading intensities (cyclic stress ratios are set as 0.15, 0.2, 0.25). The laboratory tests showed that liquefaction/reliquefaction resistance of Toyoura sand is influenced highly by the strain history and fabric anisotropy developed. The liquefaction/reliquefaction resistance of Toyoura sand can be quantified using an energy-based criterion considering the integrated effects of strain history and soil fabric. [J5, J7] 2. Combining X-ray tomography data with advanced DEM simulation can greatly improved the quality of numerical simulation. We conducted 3D DEM simulation with realistic shaped soil packing. The DEM simulation is quantitatively comparable with the experimental tests, making it useful to study fabric evolution in a more realistic setting [J8]. 3. The DEM simulation examined fabric evolution of the soil packing under multidirectional loading [J4], and during liquefaction and post-liquefaction processes. Correlations have been developed to connect the liquefaction resistance to the soil fabrics [J8]. The study provided micromechanical insights to the study of soil liquefaction. Research Outcome In summary, to date, 8 journal papers have been published in top international journals [J1-J8], including Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering (ASCE), Journal of Engineering Mechanics (ASCE), Acta Geotechnica, Computers and Geotechnics, and International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, and Géotechnique Letter. The research findings have been actively disseminated in various local and international conferences [C1-C5], including an oral presentation in The 7th International Conference on Earthquake Geotechnical Engineering (7ICEGE), Roma, Italy, 17-20 June 2019, which is a leading conference under the auspice of International Society for Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering, and The 23rd Annual Conference of HKSTAM in Hong Kong (April 2019). A conference paper [C5] has been orally presented ub The 17th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering in September 2021 in Japan, which is the most prestigious earthquake engineering conference held every four years and attended by 3000+ researchers around the world. Mr. Srinivas Vivek BOKKISA has completed his M.Phil. thesis on this topic; Mr. Pedram FARDAD AMINI has completed his Ph.D. thesis on this topic. A visiting PhD student, Mr. YANG Siyuan from Tsinghua University, and a postdoctoral scholar Dr. FAN Huo, have worked on developing numerical method for this project.

16204618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204618.value: Although this study has investigated fabric evolution during the liquefaction process, yet, it is still a challenge how to incorporate these information to improve macroscopic constitutive modeling of soil liquefaction. In addition, modeling soil liquefaction and soil-structure interactions requires improvement of both constitutive models and numerical schemes. Many existing constitutive models for soil liquefaction have been established on the framework of small-deformation theory. These models can reasonably capture the liquefaction triggering, but to a lesser extent, the cyclic mobility or large deformation of liquefied soils. For numerical schemes, the material point method (MPM) shows promise for simulating large deformation problems without mesh distortion issues recently. Therefore, it is a great promise to develop an MPM-based computational platform for simulating soil liquefaction and more complicated seismic soil-structure interaction problems.

16204618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204618.value: Cyclic liquefaction refers to dramatic loss of stiffness and strength of soils during earthquake shaking. During the past earthquakes, significant structural and ground damages were associated with large deformation in post-liquefaction and excessive ground deformation. Yet, the design methods used for liquefaction are mainly empirically based. This proposed project aims at improving fundamental understanding of the soil liquefaction mechanism through particle-scale investigation using the state-of-the-art laboratory tests and numerical modeling. We have conducted a series of laboratory tests on loose and medium dense Toyoura sand specimen under various loading intensities. We demonstrated how the soil liquefaction resistance is related to fabric anisotropy. Further more, 3D discrete element modeling were developed to simulate soil packing with realistic shapes. The numerical simulation, calibrated from the laboratory tests, were used to trace the fabric evolution of the particles during the liquefaction and postliquefaction processes. The research provides scientific basis for linking microscale information to macroscale behaviors in the liquefaction processes.

16204718.label: Project Objectives
16204718.value: Perform heavy traffic analysis of the full flexible networks model for the manufacturing application where both production speed and status (on/off) are decision variables to obtain insights and benchmarks of performance. Identify a sparse network structure and design an implementable matching policy that can performance close to a fully flexible network. Incorporate the distance dimension into a stochastic network model that can be applied to logistic applications. Design near-optimal matching policies in the logistic applications to strike the proper balance between transportation costs and matching. Build a stochastic network to model regeneration of resources as in ride sharing applications (drivers become available resources again after dropping his passengers in the destination region). Perform heavy traffic analysis to study the interplay between the matching policy and true demand (those who do not abandon) and apply it to study economics of such networks.

16204718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204718.value: Demand and supply mismatch caused by randomness has been a major challenge in managing systems in modern business activities. The rich literature developed in our area has contributed tremendously to solving this challenge by developing methods, which have been successfully applied to various applications and have significantly improved the efficiency and reduced the cost. New applications, arising as society rapidly evolves, bring new challenges and necessitate the further development of existing and new methods. For example, Huawei manages a wide range of products with dozens of modularized components. Such components can be manufactured by several production lines and are used in different products. How to jointly manage production and inventory in such a network? In modern logistics, it is important to design and manage a network of distribution centers and regions to consider both transportation cost and loss (or delay) of sales. As another example, ride sharing has reshaped the way people travel. A key question for the ride sharing platforms, such as Didi and Uber, is how to assign passenger requests to available drivers, both of which show up randomly across regions. We need to take both spatial dimension and the demand and supply into account to minimize delay and empty car routing while maxmizing the matching. Motivated by these applications, we propose to study a general network with multiple types of resources and requests, which is often ``sparse'' since it may be too expensive, or impossible, to enable every resource to cater to every request. The literature has revealed that ``a little flexibility goes a long way'', with some even indicating ``exactly how much flexibility'' is needed. Based on this, we plan to investigate the following questions. For manufacturing applications, we are interested in finding out the optimal policy for jointly determining the production plan and inventory. For logistics applications, only transportation costs prevent resources in a certain region from serving requests in another one. The question is how to optimally construct and operate a sparse network to strike the balance between transportation cost and loss of sales. In addition to taking spatial information into account, it is important in the ride sharing application that after a driver and a passenger are matched, possibly from different nearby areas, the driver will become available later at the destination. 由随机性引发的需求与供应不匹配一直是现代商业活动管理系统中的主要挑战。本领域建立的良好学术框架对解决这一挑战已经做出极大的贡献，这些方法已经被成功运用到多种场景，显著地提升了效率、降低了成本。随着社会快速发展，新应用带来了新挑战，现有的和新的方法必须有更加深刻长远的发展。 一个例子是，华为通过数十种模块化组件管理各种产品，这些部件可以由几条生产线制造，并用于生产不同的产品，在这样一个网络中如何协同地管理生产和库存？在现代物流系统中，设计和管理配送中心和地区网络以考虑运输成本和销售损失（或延迟）非常重要。另一个例子是，乘车共享改变了人们的出行方式。对如滴滴、优步等乘车共享平台的关键问题是，如何将乘客的请求分配给现有的司机，他们都是随机出现在各个地区的。我们需要同时考虑空间分布和供求，最小化乘客等车时间和汽车未载客行驶时间，同时最大化匹配乘客与驾驶员。 在这些应用的推动下，我们提议研究具有多种类型的资源和请求的通用网络。这样的网络通常是“稀疏的”，因为使每个资源满足每个请求可能太昂贵或不可能实现。文献显示增加一点灵活性就能适用很久，有些甚至能定量给出灵活性的大小。基于这一点，我们计划调查以下问题。对于制造业应用，我们有兴趣找出同时确定生产计划和库存的最优政策。对于物流系统的应用，只有运输成本会阻止某个地区的资源在另一个地区提供服务。问题是如何优化构建和运营稀疏网络，以在运输成本和销售损失之间取得平衡。除了考虑空间信息之外，在乘坐共享应用中重要的是，尽管驾驶员可能来自不同的附近区域，但是在他和乘客匹配之后，驾驶员稍后可以在目的地提供服务。

16204718.label: Realisation of objectives
16204718.value: The objectives in the proposal have been achieved with great success. In paper #1, we have developed a novel stochastic network modeling framework to incorporate the spatial factor that can be applied in various logistic applications such as ride-hailing, achieving Objective 3. Moreover, we couple an open and a closed queueing network to model the regeneration of resources as in ride-sharing applications (drivers become available resources again after dropping their passengers in the destination region), achieving Objective 5. We analyze the dynamics of such a queueing model where the platform can control the matching process by setting a threshold on the expected pick-up time. Applying fluid approximations, we obtain accurate performance evaluations and an elegant optimality condition, based on which we propose a policy that adapts to time-varying demand. This achieves Objective 4. Paper #3 studies approximations and control of a parallel service system where the service rate depends on the number of jobs served in parallel, which is applicable in various manufacturing and service systems. The control of such a system is implemented by imposing a limit on the number of jobs that can share the resource concurrently, with the rest of the jobs waiting in a first-in-first-out buffer. A desirable control scheme should strike the right balance between efficiency (operating at a high service rate) and parallelism (preventing small jobs from getting stuck behind large ones). We employ the framework of heavy-traffic diffusion analysis to devise control heuristics for such a queueing system. We engineer a method to obtain a drift function starting from the discrete (pre-limit) state-dependent PS server to obtain a control policy for the latter. We also derive the steady-state distribution of the resulting diffusion limit, and use it to obtain insightful and closed-form approximations for the original system under a static concurrency control policy. This achieves Objectives 1 and 2. Paper #4 introduces a structure for the directed acyclic graph (DAG) and a mechanism design based on that structure so that peers can reach a consensus at a large scale based on proof of work (PoW). We explore the sparsity of the DAG to enhance the connectivity of the graphs; the result is a significant scale-up of the capacity without sacrificing security and decentralization. This achieves Objective 2. Additionally, Paper #3 proposes a method to simulate multi-asset class prices using Wasserstein generative adversarial network. This work contributes to quantitative analysis methodology for generated and original data quality. Achieving the objectives was not an easy task. It took tremendous effort from myself and my PhD students. All of them have already graduated. One got a nice job offer from Alibaba, working on supply chain projects which share the similar theoretical challenges. Another joined the finance industry in Hong Kong working as a data analyst. The papers produced in this project were much improved by hiring research assistants and communicating with top researchers in the field. The grant allowed me to have English editors improve the exposition of all my papers. The travels made possible by this grant also enable me to collaborate extensively with my collaborators and consultant around the world, and present the research outcomes in major conferences and workshops.
