16204718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204718.value: This project leads to significant development in both theory and application. Papers 1 and 3 developed a framework and necessary theory to support it. All papers are motivated by practical applications such as service centers, and ride-hailing systems, and applied the framework to obtain insightful results as well as practically implementable near-optimal policies. The major findings of this project are as follows: Paper #1 proposes a novel stochastic network model and advances an analysis method based on the new challenge brought by this model. Most queueing systems follow a classical Skorohod type reflection mapping. However, due to our control policy and the spacial factor, the reflection boundary is a curve rather than a horizontal line. Paper #3 provides a theoretical framework for optimal control in a stochastic system where the speed depends on the number of tasks that is running concurrently. The varying speed also makes traditional analysis methods fails. Papers #1 and #3 provide an effective and easy-to-implement policies for control and capacity sizing of a multi-class service networks with different customer classes. For example, Paper #1 shows that an optimal control policy need not estimate primitive parameters such as arrival rate and abandonment rate. All we need to know is the system status. Thus it is possible to construct adaptive policy without too much burden on learning or estimating parameters. Paper #2 demonstrates that it is possible to use Wasserstein generative adversarial network to simulate multi-asset classes prices, and the result is on par with real data. This can result in a systematic method for testing trading strategies.

16204718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204718.value: In this project, we have solved several major research challenges completely. For example, we develop a theoretical framework to analyze stochastic control spatial factors and varying service power depending on status. We also applied our method to several models that are widely used in many real applications, e.g. logistics and ride-sharing. In this way, there should not be much left to do in the scope of the proposed research. This project has excellent potential for future research in applications. We only demonstrate the application of the theory we develop in the optimal control of several applications in ride-hailing and resource management. However, there are broader aspects that can be studied. For example, how can we incorporate pricing strategies in the ride-hailing platform? In other words, how to use pricing as an additional control. Of course, this is beyond the scope of this project since pricing has a different implication than the matching distance. One way to model is to split customers into multiple classes, leading to a multi-class queueing network; another way is to incorporate a pricing elasticity model. In either direction, a substantial analysis will be required to tackle the new challenges.

16204718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204718.value: This project demonstrated both theoretical and application significance. On the theoretical side, we advanced the state of art of analysis method by proposing new stochastic models to incorporate spatial factors into classical queueing models. We develop a framework for both fluid and diffusion approximations for a stochastic system with varying service capacity depending on the number of concurrent jobs in service. We demonstrate the applicability of our theoretical analysis by solving challenging problems motivated by real applications in emerging areas. Many of these models are new in the research literature and have their distinctive features, necessitating the development of new methods. Beyond theoretical contributions, we have obtained operational insights into many real applications, and this insight leads to easy-to-implement and effective control policies. For example, we propose easy-to-implement control policies for ride-hailing applications, which need not estimate various parameters, making the policy robust and adaptive. We also apply stochastic analysis and explore the sparsity in a stochastic graph to enhance the connectivity to improve the efficiency and efficacy of the stochastic system.

16205018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205018.value: Thermal management has become a critical issue for high-heat flux electronics and energy systems. Phase change heat transfer in integrated micro-scale cooling channels has been envisioned as a promising solution. However, the technique entails great challenges in bubble dynamics, interfacial transport and flow instability. It has been demonstrated that chemically-patterned surfaces can be used to manipulate the density of nucleation sites and bubble detachment and thus significantly enhance the heat transfer coefficient and the critical heat flux. At micrometer scale interfacial tension, viscous forces and surface wettability come to dominate inertia and buoyancy forces. Because microbubble nucleation, growth and detachment are all sensitive to shear forces, specifically the flow velocity and the capillary force, and the surface’s wettability, it is important to understand the effects of chemically patterning the surface on bubble nucleation, contact line dynamics and heat transfer. Furthermore, vapor bubbles generated on a chemically-patterned surface may create two-phase flow which may enhance heat transfer coefficient and at the same time enhance the critical heat flux. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the effect of chemically patterning the surface with different pattern fractions and geometries to manipulate flow boiling processes. In this research, multiphase transport in mini- and micro-channels with chemically-patterned surfaces will be investigated. Mini- and micro-channels with different wettability will be fabricated using micro- or nano-fabrication technology. A wettability-patterned surface is advantageous for manipulating nucleation sites and generating instability, bubble breakup and convective flows that have the potential to maximize heat and mass transfer. Experiments will be conducted using micro-machined mini/micro-channels. Micro-scale sensor arrays will be fabricated on the channels’ substrates to measure the experimental conditions. A transparent indium tin oxide surface with chemical patterns will be used to form hydrophobic and hydrophilic patterns in the channels. Micro/nanofabricated pillars will also be used to further enhance the surface wetting/non-wetting effects. The bubble nucleation, contact line dynamics and bubble detachment in the channels will then be studied. The bubble dynamics will be documented using a high-speed camera and a recently-developed laser interference technique. The flows will be measured utilizing micro-resolution particle image velocimetry. The resulting wetting patterns, temperature gradients and flow velocities will be related to the patterning, the liquid’s surface tension and the channel dimensions. Model will be formulated and its predictions will be compared with the experimental data.

16205018.label: Realisation of objectives
16205018.value: To study bubble dynamics and heat transfer in flow boiling with chemically patterned surfaces, transparent, rectangular mini- and microscale channels with various hydrophilic networks, hydrophobic islands and temperature sensor arrays using recently-developed micro-fabrication techniques have been built. The chemically patterned (wettability-patterned) microchannel, which contains three layers. The top layer, a Pyrex glass was first anodic bonded with a silicon wafer. The silicon was then patterned with photoresist using the standard lithography method and etched through with deep reactive-ion etching (DRIE). The remaining silicon served as two side walls of the microchannel. Then the sample was anodic bonded again with the bottom Pyrex glass, which has a platinum heater, two heater pads and Teflon patterns on it. The morphology of the microchannel was measured by the Keyence VK-X260K 3D Laser Confocal Microscope. We applied standard fabrication techniques for micro-electrical-mechanical systems (MEMS) in the Nanosystem Fabrication Facility at The Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST). The heater and the pads were fabricated with a typical lift-off metallization method. The Pyrex glass was first patterned with photoresist. Then a 10 nm adhesion layer of Titanium and 300 nm of Platinum were deposited on the surface in sequence. After lift-off in acetone, a similar process was repeated with 10 nm of Titanium and 300 nm of Gold to form the heater pads. Finally, a 100 nm of silicon oxide layer was deposited on the metal surface to protect the heater and function as an insulation layer. The rectangular heater, being 700 µm in width and 10 mm in length, was placed in the center of the microchannel. The Teflon patterns were formed on the silicon oxide surface. A 330 ℃ baking for 10 min procedure in the process greatly enhances the adhesion between the substrate and the Teflon patterns, which ensures the Teflon patterns not to be peeled off during the experiment. The thickness of the Teflon patterns was measured with a Surface Profiler (KLA-Tencor P-7), which is around 110 nm. The measured roughness of the Teflon and the patterned surface are only 10 nm and 60 nm, respectively. As the roughness is quite small, the effect of it on the flow boiling is negligible. The side length of the rectangular dot is 72 µm and the respective pitch distances between two adjacent dots are 122, 144 and 172 µm. These three types of channels were used in the studies. An array of fast-response temperature sensors has been integrated into the channels’ substrates for temperature measurement. To understand and document the chemically patterned surface on three-dimensional contact-line pinning during pool boiling and flow boiling, hierarchical superbiphilic micro/nanostructures with chemical patterns were also fabricated utilizing micro/nanofabrication techniques. It is important to predict contact line dynamics under different surface wetting conditions in order to understand their effects on the response of evaporation/boiling. We also studied the liquid evaporation and contact-line dynamics on wettability patterned surfaces. The effects of different pattern sizes and pitch distances and the hydrophobic/hydrophilic fraction ratio were investigated. The effects of flow velocity and surface temperature on the heat transfer performance were documented. The flow velocity field were measured using high speed flow measurement techniques. To understand and demonstrate control of microbubble generation and behavior using surface patterning, directional control of bubble movement in flow boiling was investigated. The surfaces’ heterogeneity and hierarchical superbiphilic micro/nanostructures with chemical patterns were exploited as the basis micro-bubble control. Two mechanisms are probed: (i) the formation and subsequent pinning of bubbles atop symmetrically superbiphilic (SsBPi) micropillar arrays using superhydrophobic (sHPo) nanostructures. Bubble generation atop micropillars increases the encountered drag and lift forces due to the higher velocity of impinging liquid, and the relocation of vapor generation away from the channel base increases the rewetting potential; (ii) the orientation of sHPo patches on either the upstream or downstream facing surfaces of a micropillar (denoted by u-Janus and d-Janus, respectively) to manipulate bubble coalescence characteristics. The interplay of drag forces and bubble pinning is used to limit coalescence, which can increase both the heat transfer coefficient and maximum sustainable heat flux. To model the critical heat flux (CHF) and heat transfer coefficient (HTC) and relate them to the geometry and hydrophobic/hydrophilic fraction of a chemically-patterned surface, experiments were conducted utilizing above developed microchannels. The experimental data were used to correlate the heat flux with the surface’s properties, the surface temperature, the flow rate and the channel dimension and aspect ratio. An experimental facility for studying bubble dynamics, and heat transfer with different transparent wettability-patterned hydrophobic/hydrophilic surfaces under different pitch sizes and distances and integrated fast response temperature sensors has been developed. The effects on bubble nucleation, departure and liquid flowrate on chemically patterned surfaces in different heat fluxes under flow boiling conditions have been quantified. Microchannels composed of a hydrophilic heater with hydrophobic dots were applied to characterize the effect of pitch distance of adjacent dots on flow boiling heat transfer and pressure drop. Using deionized water as the working fluid, subcooled flow boiling experiments were conducted at different mass fluxes and bubble dynamics and flow patterns were visualized with a high-speed camera. Bubbles coalescence and flow patterns in the microchannel with different dot pitch distances were investigated. Heat transfer coefficient (HTC), critical heat flux (CHF) and pressure drop were measured in correlation with the pitch distance of dots and surface temperature. Numerical study has been conducted for studying dynamic wetting on patterned surfaces.

16205018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205018.value: In this research, it is found that bubbles coalesced more easily, and flow patterns transited faster in the microchannel with smaller pitch distance. Heat transfer coefficient (HTC), critical heat flux (CHF) and pressure drop were found to significantly rely on the pitch distance of dots and the mass flux (Wang et al. 2022). Furthermore, based on a force-balance model, bubble detached diameters were predicted in hydrophilic, hydrophobic and wettability-patterned microchannels, respectively. Effects of non-wetting fraction and pitch distance plays an important role in flow boiling heat transfer in a wettability-patterned microchannel. This provides a useful insight to optimize the wettability pattern design and then improve flow boiling heat transfer in a microchannel. A constant critical receding contact angles was found that it is determined mainly by the surface pattern fraction and independent from the surface pattern size. A proposed model for the total evaporation duration gave out reasonable consistency to the experimental data which could provide important insights to the functional surface design for the evaporation/boiling enhancement and evaporation/boiling control (He et al. 2022). For multiscale systems, integrating wettability-patterned surfaces into a multiscale micro/nanostructured evaporator has demonstrated promising thermal performance enhancement in microscale. It is found that the wettability-patterned surface can increase the length of the triple contact line, which enhances the evaporation process. Specifically, the optimum hydrophobic area fraction was found at around 34% (Yang et at. 2020, Yang et al. 2021 and Yang et al. 2022). For 3D directional chemically patterned surfaces, it is found that with three-directional hierarchical superbiphilic micro/nanostructures can enhance flow boiling heat transfer facilitating the transportation of large quantities of heat at near-constant temperature and in a small form factor (Christopher Salmean and Huihe Qiu 2022). It is possible to utilize the strong capillary forces generated by nanostructures to pin the liquid/vapor interface in three dimensions and thereby control the coalescence and flow interactions of developing bubbles. We demonstrate this principle on both symmetrical and asymmetrical superbiphilic microstructures, showing enhancement of peak heat transfer coefficient by 81% and 113%, respectively, when compared to the best superhydrophilic and superhydrophobic analogues. Our approach shows a potential future direction for engineered boiling micro/nanostructures, wherein bubble dynamics are directly manipulated on bespoke, three-dimensional substrates.

16205018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205018.value: The newly developed wettability-patterned hydrophilic/hydrophobic surfaces can control bubble dynamics and heat transfer in microscale. The pattern size, pitch distance and pattern fraction ratio are three key parameters affecting the contact line dynamics which need to be optimized. The question is whether a three-dimensional wettability patterning shape with smooth curvature like a circle or with sharp curvature like a triangle confines the bubble better if we use the bubble array to form a high numerical dot array based for ultrahigh heat flux electronic chip cooling. The pattern size confines the size of the bubble and the pitch distance controls the interaction of the adjacent bubbles. Since the heat transfer efficiency changes with the heat flux, the patterns with different sizes and pitch distances should have different optimal working conditions. Although we studied the optimum wettability fraction ratio in two-dimensional condition, optimization of these two variables in three-dimensional is a complicated but interesting topic. Systematic research on this topic would provide key parameters for better control of bubble dynamics, contact line pinning/depinning and irregular bubble shape and bubble array formation which have promising potential in microelectronics cooling and other microfluidic applications.

16205018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205018.value: Contact line dynamics and coalescence of micro-bubbles at the microscale is relevant to electronics cooling, microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip devices, energy research and industrial applications. The current project focused on the fundamental phenomena of bubble dynamics, contact line behavior and flow boiling in wettability-patterned microchannels that affect nucleation boiling, heat transfer coefficient and critical heat flux, and bubble interaction in mini/micro spaces. This is the first time that a wettability-patterned surface is found to have a significant impact on the manipulation of bubble dynamics in microchannel flow which resulted in a significant improvement in boiling heat transfer. The effects of surface wetting, contact line length, bubble pinning and depinning on bubble dynamics and heat transfer are investigated. A novel visualization technique for a mini/micro space measurement has been developed. We found an optimized design for the wettability fraction ratio which can maximize the cooling performance under giving conditions. Based on our findings, because surface-wettability patterns have a significant impact on the bubble dynamics, pinning/depinning, coalescence, heat and mass transfer processes, the technique helps to better design and optimize electronics cooling devices, such as micro-chip cooling systems, data center cooling and power battery thermal management, etc.

16205118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205118.value: Internal erosion refers to the loss of soil particles in the matrix of a soil mass under the influence of seepage flow. It is the cause of failure in 37% of failed earthen dams. When internal erosion occurs in a soil mass, the void ratio and permeability will increase but the soil dilative tendency, stiffness and shear strength will decrease, eventually leading to either shear failure or the formation of flow channels in the soil mass. Extensive laboratory tests have been performed to investigate the mechanics and hydraulic conditions of internal erosion under monotonically varying hydraulic gradients. However, in many engineering situations the hydraulic conditions are not constant but cyclic, for instance in the filter soil layer behind a leaking clay core in an earthen dam or soil around a leaking water-supply pipe embedded in a soil slope, which is subject to turbulent seepage conditions caused by flow from the leaking hole. The cyclic hydraulic gradients may promote rotational movement of fine soil particles so that a larger number of soil particles erode compared with those eroded under constant gradient conditions. However, no experimental study of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradient conditions has been reported in the literature. The primary objective of this research project is to investigate the physical mechanisms of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradients and complex stress states through a comprehensive experimental program. An existing triaxial internal erosion testing apparatus will be modified to enable the modelling of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradients and controlled stress states. Then extensive internal erosion tests will be conducted to capture the initiation and progression of internal erosion in a representative soil under cyclic hydraulic gradients with varying cyclic gradient amplitudes and frequencies. Internal erosion tests under the influence of monotonic hydraulic gradients will also be performed to provide a benchmark against which to determine any special responses under cyclic gradients. In each of the tests, the erosion rate, soil permeability, local specimen deformation, pore water pressures and critical hydraulic gradients will be measured. The dependency of the critical hydraulic gradients on the stress state, cyclic gradient amplitude, and frequency will be quantified. The outcome of the research will advance our understanding of the fundamental behaviour of internal erosion in soils under cyclic hydraulic gradients, and facilitate the rehabilitation of a large number of distressed dams, dikes and slopes and the construction of new dams and dikes. 內侵蝕是指在滲流作用下土顆粒從土體骨架中流失的現象。當土體發生內侵蝕時，其孔隙率和滲透性會增加，但剪脹性、剛度和抗剪強度卻降低，最終導致剪切破壞或形成滲流通道。內侵蝕是37%的土石壩失事的原因。 目前已就土體在單向遞增水力梯度下的內侵蝕過程及其後的力學及水力特性進行了大量實驗研究。然而，在許多實際工程中，水力條件不是單向遞增而是循环的。比如在土石壩粘土心牆後方反濾層中，或在發生滲漏的埋管四周的邊坡土壤中，都會面臨由小裂隙滲流引起的湍流作用。與恒定水力梯度情況對比，循环水力梯度可產生細顆粒的旋轉運動從而促使更多的土顆粒流失。但目前尚未開展循环水力梯度下土體內侵蝕的實驗研究。 本研究課題的主要目的，是通過實驗研究在循环水力梯度及複雜應力環境下土體內侵蝕的物理機制。首先將改進現有的三軸滲流儀，使其可以控制循环水力梯度和複雜應力狀態。接著，將用該改進後的儀器開展大量土體內侵蝕實驗，研究循环水力梯度的幅度和頻率變化時，特定土體內侵蝕的發生和發展規律。同時，也將進行土體在單向水力梯度作用下的內侵蝕實驗，為循环水力梯度作用下土體的特別行為提供參照基準。在每個實驗中，將測量土體的侵蝕速率、滲透性、局部變形、和孔隙水壓力的變化規律以及臨界水力梯度，以量化臨界水力梯度與應力水準和循环水力梯度的幅度及頻率的關係。項目的研究成果將加深我們對於土體在循环水力梯度作用下發生內侵蝕的物理機制的理解和定量評估，有助於大量現有水壩、堤壩及邊坡的維護以及新水壩和堤壩的建設。

16205118.label: Realisation of objectives
16205118.value: (1) Development of a triaxial apparatus to investigate the physical mechanisms of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradients (Chen et al., 2020a,b; Xu et al., 2022) A novel triaxial apparatus has been developed to investigate the physical mechanisms of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradients. The apparatus consists of four components: a pressurized water supply system with cyclic gradient control, a triaxial stress-controlled system, a soil collection system and a water collection system. An automatic pressure controller is adopted in the water supply system to pressurize the upstream water tank, imposing designated cyclic hydraulic gradients to the soil sample in the triaxial system. Once internal erosion is initiated, eroded fine particles are allowed to drop into a detachable soil collection container through the perforated pedestal. To realise hydraulic gradient reversal, a two-way seepage system taking advantage of two three-way valves is installed in the apparatus. The two valves connect the two ends of the specimen to the water supply system and to the water collection system, respectively. By switching the two three-way valves at certain frequencies, the direction of the applied hydraulic gradient can be reversed. (2) Benchmark internal erosion tests under monotonic hydraulic gradient conditions (Chen et al., 2020a,b; Zou et al., 2020) Benchmark tests were conducted first to study deformation characteristics and critical states of soils subject to internal erosion with monotonic hydraulic gradient conditions. Three stress conditions were considered: isotropic, triaxial compression and triaxial extension stress states. Soil deformations were measured using a photographic method. With a gradual loss of soil particles, both the axial and radial strains and the void ratio increase. Greater soil deformations develop under a larger shear stress ratio or a higher mean effective stress. Additional tests were further conducted to investigate soil behaviours after experiencing a substantial loss of particles by salt dissolution. After the salt dissolution, the material grading becomes narrower, the grading state index decreases and the specific void ratio increases, leading to an upward shift of the critical state line. Since the increase in the void ratio is more than the upward shift of the critical state line, the stress state changes from the dense side to the loose side, accompanied by a change of shearing behaviour from strain-softening to strain-hardening. As the critical friction angle is dominated by the inter-particle contacts among coarse particles, with almost no change in the coarse content of the post-dissolution materials, only a slight decrease of 2.3° in the critical friction angle is found. The evolution mechanisms of suffusion in gap-graded sandy gravels were verified using numerical simulations of coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and discrete element method (DEM). When the fine particle content is the same, the total fine erosion ratio is larger when the stability index of the gap-graded sandy gravel is lower. The porosities of five layers of the gap-graded sandy gravel change continuously with infiltration time. A slight decrease in the fine grain content appears in the upper layers, while a sharp reduction in the fine grain content occurs in the bottom layer. (3) Investigation of the effect of the magnitude of cyclic hydraulic gradient on internal erosion (Chen and Zhang, 2021; Xu et al., 2022) Extensive laboratory tests were conducted to investigate the development of internal erosion and changes in hydraulic conductivity under one-way cyclic seepage, and the post-erosion stress-strain behaviour. The erosion development is significantly influenced by the initial grain size distribution and the pattern of the imposed cyclic hydraulic gradient. The cyclic seepage promotes the loss of fine particles and leads to larger hydraulic conductivity. The eroded soil mass and hydraulic conductivity of internally unstable soils increase significantly with increasing cyclic gradient amplitude, while the internally stable soils experience a small amount of particle loss even under large cyclic gradients. For both types of soils, a larger cyclic gradient amplitude leads to stronger post-erosion contractive shearing behaviour and a smaller critical friction angle. The first batch of internal erosion tests was performed, which allow two-way alteration of seepage direction and hydraulic gradient reversals. Three different schemes of hydraulic gradient application, namely monotonic stepwise loading, cyclic reversal after monotonic loading, and direct cyclic loading, were adopted. In each test, the cumulative particle loss, deformation, hydraulic conductivity, and post-erosion shearing behaviour were evaluated. The cyclically reversed hydraulic gradient results in more severe erosion at the same level of the mean hydraulic gradient. Microscopic analysis was also conducted to investigate the mechanism of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal, in which mitigation of clogging within the soil matrix was observed and found to facilitate the progression of internal erosion. (4) Investigation of the effect of both the frequency and number of cycles of the hydraulic gradient on internal erosion (Chen and Zhang, 2021; Xu et al., 2022) Tests were conducted to define an appropriate number of gradient cycles in a cyclic stage that is required to eliminate the loading frequency effects and the number of total stages of a cyclic seepage test. At a fixed average hydraulic gradient, the peak gradient of each cycle is first kept the same until no further erosion is observed. Then, the gradient amplitude is increased while the mean gradient level is maintained. After the equilibrium is reached, the erosion test would go to the next stage by increasing the mean hydraulic gradient but maintaining the gradient amplitude. Based on the calibration tests, three cycles at each cyclic stage and a total of five cyclic stages are recommended. In internal erosion tests under cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal, the amount of particle loss declined significantly with the increase in the number of cycles. Especially for the test with direct application of cyclic reversal at a hydraulic gradient level of 12, 5.8% of soil particles eroded in the first cycle, whereas only 1.5% in the second cycle. The effect of frequency on cyclic internal erosion was also investigated following similar procedures. When the cyclic hydraulic gradient is applied at a very high frequency (a few seconds per switch), much more severe internal erosion can happen. This could be attributed to the excess pore pressure generation induced by the highly fluctuated water flow, which results in a transient or even turbulent movement of fine particles. 16205118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205118.value: This research project produced the first batch of experimental data on internal erosion under cyclic gradients, and made four significant technical contributions: (1) A novel modified triaxial internal erosion apparatus is developed to conduct one-way and two-way internal erosion tests under cyclic hydraulic gradients (Chen et al., 2020a,b; Xu et al., 2022). The mechanical consequences due to cyclic hydraulic gradient during internal erosion can be measured, including changes in eroded mass, soil deformations, hydraulic conductivity, and post-erosion stress-strain behaviour. It provides a powerful tool for studying the mechanisms involved in internal erosion under complex conditions. (2) Hydro-mechanical behaviour of soil experiencing seepage erosion under one-way cyclic hydraulic gradient has been studied (Chen and Zhang, 2021). A considerably larger amount of soil particles is eroded under cyclic gradients than under monotonic gradients. Erosion occurs most significantly in the first cyclic stage and decreases in the subsequent cyclic stages. When the mean hydraulic gradient is the same, the eroded soil mass increases significantly with increasing cyclic gradient amplitude. A larger cyclic gradient amplitude corresponds to stronger contractive shearing behaviour, and smaller peak and critical friction angles. (3) Experimental tests were performed to study internal erosion in granular soil subject to cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal (Xu et al., 2022). At all hydraulic gradient levels, a larger amount of particle loss in a gap-graded granular soil is observed when subject to cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal than to monotonic seepage. Given the same hydraulic gradient level, the cumulative eroded soil mass increases with the gradient reversal ratio. The particle loss increment during each cyclic stage declines as the gradient cycling proceeds. As loss of soil particles continues, the soil under cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal experiences larger lateral and axial deformations. The soil under a larger stress ratio experiences greater axial and radial strains and the soil has larger deformations in the compression stress states than in the extension stress states (Chen et al., 2020a,b). The hydraulic conductivity of the eroded soil subject to cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal is nearly twice that under monotonic internal erosion. Cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal results in a more contractive post-erosion drained shearing behaviour. (4) The influence of cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal on internal erosion is attributed to easier elimination of clogging due to decreased effective stresses and reversed dragging forces (Xu et al., 2022). The mitigation of clogging is also responsible for the larger reduction in the post-erosion soil stiffness.

16205118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205118.value: There are still challenging tasks on testing internal erosion tests under more realistic conditions on the basis of this completed project: (1) Erosion from two ends of the sample. In this project, the test apparatus did not allow eroded soil particles to exit from the top end of the sample, which suppressed the progression of internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal. In the future, the exit of soil particles at both ends of the specimen can be attempted. (2) Effects of random cyclic gradient waveforms. In this project, only the double-sided trapezoidal wave was applied to facilitate equilibrium within each gradient cycle. In the future, other types of waveforms (e.g., sinusoidal or random) may be attempted to study soil responses under complex transient cyclic gradient conditions. (3) CFD-DEM coupled analysis of internal erosion under cyclic gradients. CFD-DEM coupled analysis provides a sound theoretical approach to modelling of internal erosion under transient hydraulic conditions. In the future, CFD-DEM analysis can be performed to look into the physical mechanisms in the cyclic internal erosion tests. The test results in this project provide data to calibrate such advanced numerical analysis.

16205118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205118.value: Internal erosion is one of the major failure causes of earthen dams, river dikes and soil slopes. Existing experimental studies on internal erosion only address the soil response under monotonic hydraulic gradient conditions. In many practical engineering problems, such as a leaking pressurized pipe in a soil slope, seabed under wave loading, and soils around a water passing tunnel, the soil is subject to turbulent seepage and hence cyclic hydraulic gradients. No experimental studies on internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradient conditions have been reported in the literature, and the mechanisms of such internal erosion are poorly understood. This research project aims to advance the understanding of the fundamental behaviour of internal erosion in soils under cyclic hydraulic gradients. The project led to a novel triaxial internal erosion apparatus and produced the first batch of experimental data on internal erosion under cyclic hydraulic gradients and complex stress conditions. Cyclic hydraulic gradient reversal results in larger loss of fine particles and more contractive post-erosion drained shearing behaviour. Such influence is attributed to easier elimination of clogging due to reversed dragging forces. The project promotes new geotechnical engineering designs and facilitates the rehabilitation of distressed dams, dikes and slopes.

16205418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205418.value: Debris flows are among the most frequent and deadly natural hazards around the world, causing numerous fatalities every year, significant destruction and damage to infrastructure including buildings, roads, railways and pipelines, and disruption of critical supply lines of water, power, traffic and communication. Hong Kong is highly vulnerable to debris flow impacts due to its steep, hilly terrain, dense population, fast urban development that encroaches debris-hazard zones, and frequent extreme rainfalls. Our current understanding of the mechanics of debris flows remains poor, leading to largely empirical design and practice in debris flow mitigation. A physically based, robust predictive approach with full appreciation of the complex nature of debris flows is urgently needed to advance the understanding of these events to allow effective and efficient design of countermeasures. This project aims to develop a new predictive numerical framework to model debris flows as a gravity-driven motion of solid-fluid mixtures, based on a coupling of the computational fluid dynamics and the discrete element method (CFD-DEM). The new computational framework will quantitatively consider the key characteristics of debris flows necessary their modeling, including inter-particle interactions in the debris solids and their interactions with the interstitial fluid, basal entrainment, inter-phase mass exchange, and induced phase-property changes. This will empower us to simulate surges, a signature feature of debris flows that is critical for accurate quantification and assessment of their dynamics and impacts but is notoriously difficult to characterize and model. Importantly, the proposed framework also offers an innovative, integrated pathway to simulate both rigid and flexible barriers and their interaction with debris flows. Flexible barriers have become increasingly popular as an economical, non-intrusive, environmentally sustainable alternative to conventional rigid barriers for debris flow mitigation, but there is no scientific basis guiding their design. The proposed research offers a new-generation, continuum-discrete coupled computational tool to capture the multi-scale, multi-physics processes exhibited in complex dynamic systems such as debris flows. It may not only help to advance our theoretical understanding of the mechanics of debris flows, but also foster accurate predictions of their impact on debris-resisting barriers. This may potentially lead to the establishment of scientifically based design guidelines for flexible barriers, which will produce immediate impacts, both in Hong Kong and worldwide, on debris flow hazard mitigation. 泥石流是全球發生最頻繁的致命自然災害之一，每年在世界各地造成了大量的人員傷亡和財產損失。泥石流嚴重損壞眾多基礎設施，包括建築、公路、鐵路及管道，直接影響日常生活中的供水、供電、交通及通訊。香港多陡峭山地，隨著城市化的發展和人口密度的增加以及因全球氣候變化導致的暴雨頻繁，使得香港成為泥石流災害高發地區。由於對泥石流基本動力學的認識不足，現存泥石流防禦措施的設計主要基於經驗模型。泥石流災害的防治急需一種能考慮泥石流復雜自然特性、基於基本物理規律的有效預測方法。 本項目基於計算流體動力學和離散元耦合的方法，用重力驅動的固液混合物來模擬泥石流，旨在建立泥石流模擬和預測的一個全新的數值框架。該數值框架可定量考慮泥石流的關鍵特徵，包括泥石流中顆粒間的相互作用、顆粒和流體間的相互作用、河床侵蝕、泥石流中固液相物質交換及其引起的固液相性質變化。基於這些考慮，該數值框架可以模擬泥石流中常見的陣性波狀運動（陣流）。陣流是泥石流的主要運動形式，模擬陣流泥石流十分困難，準確模擬陣流對於泥石流動力性質及沖擊行為的準確量化和評估非常重要。除了陣流的模擬，新建立的數值方法位模擬剛性攔擋壩和柔性防護網以及它們與泥石流的相互作用提供了一個統一框架。相對於傳統的剛性壩體，柔性防護網是一種經濟實用、對環境影響小的新型泥石流防護措施。柔性防護網在泥石流防護中愈發受歡迎，然而其係統科學的設計指南仍然缺失。 該研究將提供一種全新的連續-離散耦合計算方法來模擬泥石流的複雜動力系統中的多尺度、多重物理過程。該研究不僅能推進對泥石流力學性質的理論認識，更能促進對泥石流沖擊防護措施行為的準確預測。本項目將為香港及世界範圍內泥石流柔性防護網的設計提供科學依據 。

16205418.label: Realisation of objectives
16205418.value: All three objectives proposed in the project have been successfully achieved. (1) We have developed an unresolved, coupled computational fluid dynamics and discrete element method (CFD-DEM) to consider the particle-fluid mixture nature of debris flow. In this method, the grains are modeled by the DEM, whereas the fluid flow is modeled by CFD to solve the locally averaged Navier-Stokes equation for each fluid cell. The coupling of CFD and DEM is considered by exchanging interaction forces such as drag and buoyancy between the grains and the fluid. The coupled CFD-DEM has been shown to capture major features of a variety of different geophysical flows including debris flow and debris avalanche. (2) We have further proposed a unified CFD-DEM framework to handle the complicated three‐way interactions among the fluid, the particles, and the flexible barrier structure for debris flow impact simulations. The flexible barrier structure is modeled by DEM in the same framework, by using bonded particles or particles with remote bond connection. Both twisted net barrier and ring net barrier, including its other components such as energy dissipator and cables, can be modeled. The same framework of coupled CFD and DEM enables rigorous consideration of the in-barrier component interactions, barrier-debris particle interactions, and barrier-debris fluid interactions. The unified framework has been validated by both experiments and the theoretical solutions. (3) We have further used data of large-scale laboratory and full-scale field flume tests reported in the literature to validate our numerical model. The numerical predictions capture experimental and field observations on fundamental flow-barrier interactions and barrier deformations reasonably well. Further fundamental physical laws are proposed and discussed based on the simulation results. Overall, we are happy and proud with what we have achieved from this project and appreciate the support of RGC through this project to make this research possible.

16205418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205418.value: The project has led to a total of 14 high-quality journal publications, 6 conference papers, over 10 keynote lectures, 3 PhD and 2 MPhil students graduated whose work was fully or partially relevant to the project, and among other recognitions. These research activities help us to make the following major findings relevant and beyond the project objectives: [A] Major research findings directly relevant to the project goals: (1) We have developed an unresolved CFD-DEM approach for modeling debris flow as a mixture of debris particles and fluids where the interaction of the fluid-particle is considered by exchanging interaction forces of the two phases. The classical dam break problem has been simulated using different mixtures of non-Newtonian liquids and particles where fluid-particle interaction is found to play a pivotal role in dictating the collapse behavior. (2) A unified CFD-DEM framework has been developed to further consider both rigid and flexible barriers. Special models based on DEM are developed to simulate various barrier types, including twisting wire-net and ring-net barriers and other associated barrier components such as brake cables and energy dissipators. This framework enables a unified treatment of fluids, debris particles and either rigid or flexible barrier and their components, and more importantly their complex interactions including interparticle, particle-channel wall, particle-fluid, fluid-wall, particle-barrier, fluid-barrier, in-barrier component interactions. Both barriers and the interactions have been rigorously validated against analytical and experimental data. A physically based impact model has been proposed based on both historical data and CFD-DEM simulation result of debris flow impact on rigid barriers [J3, J11, J13, C1, C6]. (3) Based on the unified CFD-DEM framework for debris flow and barriers, systematic studies have been performed to gain better understanding of the impacting process of debris flow on a barrier system and entrainment (C2, C3). We have specifically studied the transition of impact mechanisms of different geophysical flows against flexible barrier (J7), rigid barrier and slit barrier (J13), and the characteristics of hydrodynamic dead zone formed before a rigid barrier during the impact of debris flow (J8, C5). We have also identified a bi-linear laws that govern the impacts of different geophysical flows on a flexible barrier and how the loading deflection mechanisms works during such impact processes (J14). (4) We have developed a poly-superellipsoid-based approach for effective particle morphology characterization and modeling for DEM (J1). Based on the poly-superellipsoidal DEM, we have further investigated the universal laws governing the internal fabric structure of granular media during shearing process (J2) and how the particle shape affects the multiscale thermos-mechanical behavior of granular media (J4). Multiscale modeling frameworks that rigorously consider the intertangled effect of grain crushing and particle shape on the overall behavior of granular media (J6, J9, C4). [B] Further findings achieved beyond the original project objectives: (5) The unresolved CFD-DEM approach for debris flow has been further extended to a semi-coupled resolved formulation to solve a class of granular media problems involving thermal-induced phase changes and particle-fluid interactions (J5, J10).

16205418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205418.value: The research achieved from this project may be extended to the following aspects: (1) More rigorously integrate particle morphology and crushing into the CFD-DEM framework to develop fully resolved formulation for better reproduction of their realistic impact on geophysical flows. (2) Develop appropriate numerical methods and damage criteria to simulate the barrier damage caused by the impact of geophysical flows for practical barrier design. (3) Develop high-resolution, high fidelity flume tests to offer more rigorous validations on the proposed framework. The above three future developments are indeed promising and may deserve to be developed into a future RGC/GRF project to further enhance the impact of this line of research.

16205418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205418.value: The project offered a new computational tool to model the process when a debris flow impacts on a high deformable, flexible barrier structure. The computational tool enables physics-based considerations of complicated three‐way interactions among the debris particles, the fluids, and the flexible barrier structure which have long been considered challenging to model. The numerical predictions have been systematically benchmarked by experimental results and analytical solutions, showing desirable accuracy and rigor of the proposed framework. The CFD-DEM computational framework and its predictions have greatly advanced our understanding of the impact behavior of debris flows against flexible barriers. The research findings of this project offer an important new source of reference for establishing debris flow mitigation systems than traditionally empirical approaches. The project has also contributed to our capability of simulating particle fragmentation, multi-physics, and thermal-induced phase changes. These new findings of this project help advance our fundamental understanding of granular materials and their interactions with fluids in a general setting. The numerical methods newly developed in this project greatly enhance our ability to overcome engineering challenges relevant to geohazard mitigation.

16205818.label: Project Objectives
16205818.value: To develop a well-controllable device with unified micro-nanochannels for real-time monitoring of the DNA–peptide co-assembly dynamics. Fabrication and operation techniques will be developed to achieve a multilayer device in which DNA molecules will be confined and linearized in the nanogroove arrays, and peptides will be delivered through the connecting nanoslits and microchannels to interact with DNA molecules to form DNA–peptide co-assembly. To develop protocols for dynamic characterization of DNA–peptide co-assembled viral mimics. The nanofluidic device will be coupled with a pressure control system for sample solution handling and a fluorescence microscope for observing the DNA-templated structures. The conformational change of the DNA–peptide co-assembly will be recorded by measuring the extension of YOYO-1 labeled DNA. To understand the mechanisms of packing and release of nucleic acids for the DNA–peptide co-assembly. We will further explore peptide designs and triggering systems to regulate the assembly/disassembly process.

16205818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205818.value: 病毒是最簡單的生物系統之一，因其特異的結構，可以非常有效的將基因傳遞到細胞中。合成技術可以製造病毒模擬物來模仿和擴展病毒功能。研究表明通過短肽與DNA模板共同組裝的病毒模擬物可以作為可靠的模型去研究天然病毒。迄今為止，病毒模擬物的合成是在試管中將DNA和肽溶液混合而成。然後在靜態條件下可以觀測到合成物的納米結構的形態。然而，在目前的實驗裝置下還無法觀察研究DNA與肽合成物的組裝途徑和動態相互作用。 納米流道結構和微流體相結合的平台為研究這些相互作用提供了一個獨特的平台。此前，納米流動平台已被用於單個DNA分子研究包括在納米流道的空間局限中DNA-蛋白質的相互作用到基因組測序。在此提案中，我們將進一步採用類似的納米流道結構來研究自組裝過程中的動態結構變化。我們會定義一個明確的實驗系統，作為研究DNA與肽共組裝病毒模擬物的合成與釋放的基礎。更具體地說，我們首先將開發允許實時觀測自組裝過程中動態構象變化的裝置和方法。在這個裝置中，我們將設計納米結構用於捕獲和拉伸DNA，以便在可控的條件下促成DNA和肽相結合。我們將微納米通道整合到裝置中以用於交換溶液和模擬細胞內環境。我們將優化用於病毒模擬物形成的參數，如納米結構的尺寸和幾何形狀，傳輸介質的組成，以及肽分子結構和功能設計。我們將利用該平台探索DNA與肽共組裝的折疊和展開的原理。我們將嘗試把氧化還原或pH敏感單元引入肽序列中，通過改變肽骨架完整性或改變肽鏈的疏水/親水平衡來切換自組裝的狀態。 在此提案中，我們致力於開發可用於動態評估形貌如納米粒子的病毒的自組裝的合成技術，以建立有效的基因傳遞的病毒模型來揭示病毒中基因保護和釋放的可能機制。此項研究的結果也將幫助我們認識一系列天然和合成的裝配系統。

16205818.label: Realisation of objectives
16205818.value: (1) Objective 1 was fully realized. DNA combing strategy is applied to fix and stretch DNA molecules in the micro/nanofluidic devices. PEG-silanization is applied to coating a layer of PEG-silane on the channel surface. The surface treatment greatly reduces the electrostatic interaction or nonspecific adsorption of molecules. The device is also comprised of channels for DNA and peptide delivery and interaction. DNA molecules are confined in nanochannels or stuck to the wall of the channel, after which peptide molecules are introduced to initiate the co-assembling process. (2) Objective 2 was fully realized. We developed protocols for fluorescent labeling of DNA and peptide, and applied the stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) coupled with micro/nanofluidic device for imaging DNA labelled with YOYO-1 and peptide with Alexa Fluor 647. DNA-peptide co-assembled particles can be identified and distinguished from the loose complex using STORM. (3) Objective 3 was mostly realized. We investigated the assembled nanoberry particles composed of a short peptide H4K5-HCBzlCBzlH and DNA. Through the dynamic imaging of the endocytosis process of nanoberry and DNA release, we show that the super-resolution imaging technology has the potential to reveal the mechanism underlying the endocytosis process and guide the viral mimicry design with higher gene delivery efficiency. However, we have not varied the peptide design and investigated different triggering mechanisms. Because we discovered a deep-learning based super-resolution technology which is a novel method to resolve the dynamic process at sub-cellular level, we shifted our focus on the technological development. But with the limited time and budget, we have not extended our work to different peptide designs and triggering systems to regulate the assembly/disassembly process.

16205818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205818.value: (1) We developed a novel platform based on a multi-color stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) and a size-tunable nanochannel device for super-resolution genome mapping. By using the fluorescent barcodes on DNA backbone as references, we overcome the thermal fluctuations along the DNA chains both globally and locally. We demonstrate that our platform can improve the resolution of optical maps to ~100 bp (MicroTAS 2018, US 10,722,888 B2 2020, CN 107614675 B 2021). (2) We performed super-resolution imaging to visualize the assembly of labeled DNA molecules with YOYO-1 and H4K5-HCBzlCBzlH, and revealed the morphological changes between the assembled nanoparticles and loose complex structures (Yuzi Zhang Thesis 2021). (3) We designed a droplet-based microfluidic device that enables the mixing of two hydrogel precursor materials in discrete droplets and cross-linking into particles via click chemistry. The manipulatable concentration of precursor polymers and the mixing ratio of each were first characterized to allow the formation of hydrogel microparticles for controlled release of proteins, in the device. Typical biocompatible materials, including polyethylene glycol (PEG), dextran (DX), and sodium hyaluronate (HA), were tested for their manipulatable concentrations in the device. Fluorescein-labeled immunoglobulin G (F-IgG) and bevacizumab (an anti-VEGF IgG) were encapsulated as the model drugs. The release profiles from hydrogel microparticles with different formulations and sizes were obtained and compared (ACS Applied Bio Materials 2021). (4) Based on deep learning networks, we developed a single-frame super-resolution microscopy (SFSRM) approach that reconstructs a super-resolution image from a single frame of a diffraction-limited image to support live-cell super-resolution imaging at 30-50 nm spatial resolution and up to 10 ms temporal resolution over thousands of time points. We demonstrate that our SFSRM method enables the super-resolution imaging of subcellular dynamics involving various organelles such as the vesicle transport along microtubules, the endosome fusion and fission, and diverse interplays between mitochondria with endoplasmic reticulum in live cells (doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.10.08.463746, US Provisional Patent Application No. 63/252,181). (5) We applied confocal imaging and SFSRM to sonic hedgehog (SHH) protein exocytosis process and revealed the millisecond dynamics of cargo trafficking in live cells. The newly synthesized SHH protein in the perinuclear region of the cell is continuously delivered to the cell periphery after the biotin treatment. We were able to capture the entire generation process of a microtubule bundle that facilitates vesicle transport (PNAS 2022, doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.10.08.463746).

16205818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205818.value: Suggested work for further development: (1) Further exploration of the developed SFSRM in other applications such as neurodegeneration and mitochondrial diseases. (2) Potential improvement on higher spatiotemporal resolution and signal-to-noise ration could be achieved with better quantum-yield labels, e.g., structural modification of fluorescent dyes and quantum dots.

16205818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205818.value: Fluorescence microscopy has been an indispensable tool for biological studies, but its spatial resolution is limited by the light wave diffraction effect and thus it is unable to resolve subcellular structures smaller than 200 nm. Many types of super-resolution microscopy have merged bypassing the diffraction limit; however, at the cost of increased phototoxicity and decreased imaging speed. In this project, we address the technical problem by developing micro/nanofluidic devices and deep-learning-based imaging reconstruction tools. Our single-frame super-resolution microscopy (SFSRM) approach that reconstructs a super-resolution image from a single frame of a diffraction-limited image such that it pushes the limit of fluorescence microscopes to an unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution with a limited photon budget, and circumvents the possible tradeoffs among the spatial resolution, imaging speed, and light dose, thus enabling live-cell imaging at a state-of-the-art resolution, an unprecedented speed, and reduced phototoxicity levels. We demonstrate that SFSRM enables the super-resolution imaging of subcellular dynamics in live cells.

16206618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206618.value: Probabilistic selling is now widely applied in travel and retail industries. For example, Hotwire and Priceline offer airline tickets and hotel rooms containing hidden attributes that are not revealed until after their purchase has been confirmed. A key feature of probabilistic selling is product assignment uncertainty. That is, customers who purchase probabilistic goods (PGs) may end up acquiring any of the products that are used to create PGs. Because a PG is usually offered at a discounted price, it can attract purchase from price-sensitive customers while those who have strong preferences for a specific product are less likely to purchase a PG due to uncertainty about product assignment. Therefore, probabilistic selling serves as an effective way to price discriminate customers and segment a market. The practical popularity of probabilistic selling has engendered increasing attention to this phenomenon in academic research. However, most of the existing literature considers a single PG. That is, customers who purchase PGs all face the same set of products that are used to create a PG. This implicitly assumes that all the customers who do not have strong preferences for a specific product share the same consideration set of products. Most studies have focused on two products and, naturally, a single PG is created. However, in observable empirical contexts, more than two products are substitutable, and more importantly, customers may have different consideration sets of products. This project will attempt to study a more general setting of probabilistic selling under which the seller offers multiple PGs that are created by different sets of products. In the context of revenue management, the seller dynamically controls the set of PGs being offered. We will analyze the seller’s optimal control policy over time. Due to the complexity of the problem, we will develop various heuristics to generate the control policy, and compare their performance. We will evaluate the performance of probabilistic selling of multiple PGs, benchmarking against (i) traditional selling without PGs, and (ii) probabilistic selling with a single PG only. These results will generate insights on the value of probabilistic selling for multiple PGs. To the best of our knowledge, the dynamical management of multiple PGs has not hitherto been considered in the existing literature. Successful completion of the project would guide online sellers to develop a novel selling strategy for probabilistic selling of multiple PGs, and provide insights into how to benefit from such a strategy. 概率销售已经在旅游和零售行业广泛的应用。譬如：美国网站 Hotwire 和 Priceline 在销售机票和酒店房间时，有意识地隐藏了产品的部分描述性信息。概率产品的购买者只有在购买产品后，才可以获得产品的全部确定性信息。因此概率销售的一个重要特征是产品分配的不确定性。概率产品的购买者可能被分配任何一个用于组成该概率产品的实体物品。由于购买概率产品一般享有折扣，它对价格敏感的消费者有很强的吸引力。但同时概率产品的分配有不确定性，有强烈产品喜好的消费者更倾向于购买实体物品。因此，概率销售可以做为一种市场细分的有效工具。 概率销售的实践应用引起了学术界与日剧增的研究兴趣。但目前的研究局限于单一的概率产品销售，也就说概率产品的设计是基于所有的实体物品，所有对概率产品有兴趣的顾客有相同的喜好。并且目前的研究大多只考虑两个实体物品，和基于两个实体物品的单一概率产品。但是在现实的应用中，不同的顾客可能对基于不同实体物品的概率产品有不同的喜好。我们的研究项目就是考虑更广泛的概率销售模式，零售商可以根据不同的实体物品创建不同的概率产品。 据我们所知，动态管理多概率产品在目前的研究还是空白。此项目如顺利完成，可以为零售商提供一种新型的销售策略和有益的管理启示。

16206618.label: Realisation of objectives
16206618.value: Motivated by popular opaque selling practices, this project studies how a seller manages sales of multiple products via opaque selling. Much of the literature on opaque selling assumes that there are only two physical goods and a single opaque good. However, we consider opaque selling with more than two physical products, aligned with opaque selling practices in travel and online retail industries. To address this problem, we consider a seller with a fixed capacity/inventory for each physical good prior to a finite selling horizon. Customers arrive sequentially during the horizon. The seller dynamically controls the set of products being offered to customers, and determines which physical good is used to fulfill the demand of OGs. We formulate the seller's problem as a continuous-time, discrete-state, finite-horizon stochastic dynamic program. Due to well-known curse of dimensionality, the optimal policy is computationally infeasible. To overcome this difficulty, we study the corresponding deterministic version of the problem, known as the fluid control problem. The optimal offer and fulfillment policies are generally both time-dependent. Nevertheless, we show that it is optimal for the firm to adopt a stationary (time-independent) fulfillment policy in the fluid control problem. This result enables us to solve medium sized problems efficiently. We also show that the optimal revenue of the fluid control problem serves as an upper bound for the optimal revenue of the stochastic dynamic program. This result can be used to evaluate the performance of different heuristic policies proposed later. The optimal solution of the fluid control problem can be implemented as a heuristic control policy, which is shown to be asymptotically optimal when both inventory and demand are scaled up. However, the fluid policy is static and lacks the flexibility to match supply with demand dynamically. It also does not specify the order of each set being offered. To overcome these problems, we propose a decomposition approximation of the problem to generate a dynamic control policy. This decomposition heuristic approximates the original dynamic program with a collection of single-dimensional dynamic programs, which can be efficiently solved. Extensive numerical studies show that the decomposition heuristic outperforms the fluid policy. We conduct a simulation study to evaluate the performance of regular selling (with no opaque goods) and opaque selling under different demand loads. The revenue improvement from opaque selling under both fluid policy and decomposition policy is more significant when demand is relatively low. We also investigate how the degree of inventory imbalance among different physical goods affects the performance of the fluid policy and the decomposition policy. The fluid policy and the decomposition policy can improve the seller's revenue substantially when the inventory levels are more imbalanced. We conclude that opaque selling with either the fluid policy or the decomposition policy, has great potential to improve the seller's revenue, especially when the demand is relatively low and/or when the seller has imbalanced inventory for the physical goods.

16206618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206618.value: There are several major findings from this project. First, we consider multiple opaque goods that are created using multiple physical goods. Much of the existing literature considers situations with only a single opaque good, which is a restriction for practical implementation and can lead to substantial missed revenue opportunities. Our project fills this gap by considering multiple physical goods and opaque goods and exploring how to manage opaque selling in this general and realistic environment. Second, we propose a decomposition method where the original Markovian dynamic program is decomposed into a collection of single-dimensional Markovian dynamic programs. The decomposition method generates a dynamic policy that adjusts with the remaining inventory levels and remaining time. We show that decomposition method provides a tighter upper bound than the fluid control problem for the Markovian dynamic program. Third, our modelling framework also allows us to investigate the value of opaque selling with multiple opaque goods. The revenue improvement from opaque selling is more significant when product supply is not tight relative to demand. This result can be explained as follows. With relatively low demand, the seller should try to sell to each arriving customer by offering OGs. On the contrary, when the demand is high, the supply becomes tight. Then the seller should sell each product at a high price. Since an opaque good is sold at a discount, one can expect that fewer opaque goods should be offered by the seller when the demand is high. We also find that opaque selling is more valuable when the inventory levels are more imbalanced. This can be attributed to the fulfillment flexibility rendered by opaque selling. In particular, the seller has the flexibility to fulfill the demand of opaque goods using the physical good that has a high inventory. Importantly, we show that even offering a single opaque can achieve large benefits. This suggests that implementing opaque selling is feasible in many practical settings.

16206618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206618.value: There are several future research directions. First, prices of opaque goods are fixed in our project. It is an interesting direction to study the dynamic pricing decision with endogenous fulfillment. Second, our numerical experiments show that opaque selling with a single opaque good can significantly boost the revenue under certain conditions. However, whether a small set of opaque goods suffices remains a question to be investigated. With a moderate/large size of physical goods, what is a good number of opaque goods to be created? Third, consumer behavior modeling is an important aspect of the literature on opaque and/or probabilistic selling. How to incorporate various consumer behavior such as strategic behavior, bounded rationality, and collaboration among strategic consumers into our work is another fruitful avenue of future research. Furthermore, this project proposes a decomposition heuristic that decomposes a network revenue management into a collection of single-leg revenue management problems. There are several related approaches to solving high-dimensional dynamic programs, such as Lagrangian relaxation, which deserve further exploration.

16206618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206618.value: This project studies opaque selling in a revenue management setting where a seller offers multiple substitutable products in a finite horizon. In addition to selling each physical good, the seller creates virtual products, opaque goods, to offer over time. The seller dynamically controls the offer set and fulfillment of opaque goods over time to maximize the expected total revenue. Because the optimal control policy is too complex to characterize, we propose two heuristics including a fluid policy and a decomposition method to generate the control policy. The decomposition method generates a dynamic policy that adjusts with the remaining inventory levels and remaining time, and provides a tighter upper bound than the fluid control policy. We numerically show that opaque selling with either the fluid policy or the decomposition policy, has great potential to improve the seller's revenue, especially when the demand is relatively low and/or when the seller has imbalanced inventory for the physical goods. Particularly, the decomposition policy performs much better than the fluid policy when the demand is medium and low. Importantly, this benefit can be achieved with a relatively small collection of opaque goods, potentially reducing the burden of implementing the opaque selling strategy.

16206918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206918.value: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are airborne particles with diameters less than 100 nm. The development of a personal UFP measurement technique draws the utmost attention in the field of air quality because adverse health effects are strongly associated with exposure to UFPs. However, considerable uncertainties in the correlation and the mechanisms causing health problems still remain because the ability to measure a person’s individual exposure level is limited. A person visits different places and is involved in various kinds of activities daily, thus actual personal exposure cannot be measured by stationary field testing, which is the primary monitoring method at present. Most current monitoring devices are bulky and even contain hazardous (e.g. radioactive) components. Handheld devices without hazardous components are available but they are still too large and cannot provide the size information of UFPs, which is very important for exposure investigation. Compact and convenient personal UFP measurement devices, as small and convenient to carry as a mobile phone, are currently unavailable, which hinders the relevant epidemiologic study. Recently, the sorting of nanometer-sized particles was shown to be possible in a microchannel by applying low-energy ultrasound. Microfluidics is a promising route to miniaturizing a device and low-energy sound fields are harmless to humans, so this project proposes to develop a personal UFP sensor by using the particle separation technique in microfluidics. To develop this technology, understanding how nanoparticle motion is affected by sound and examining how to realistically apply a microfluidic device for air quality measurement are crucial. This project will first study the effect of fluid flow driven by sound waves at different frequencies and in microchannels of different geometries. Then, the effect of nanoparticle motion due to the sound wave-driven flow will be investigated. The results will be used to design and fabricate a microfluidic nanoparticle sorting device, and the performance of the separation efficiency in relationship to the flow rate and particle size will be examined. Based on the optimized microfluidic device, a UFP sensor will then be developed by analogy. The sensor will be calibrated and compared to existing UFP measurement instruments. This proposed project will enhance knowledge of particle manipulation by sound fields and demonstrate how technologies can be bridged across disciplines. The findings will also determine a new direction for the development of personal sensors for better air quality. 超細顆粒（UFP）是直徑小於100nm懸浮空氣中的顆粒。人類健康與暴露於UFP中有著密切的關係，所以在空氣質量領域的研究內，個人化的UFP測量技術的發展備受關注。然而，其中的關係和引起健康問題的機制仍然存在相當多的未知領域，其原因為現在測量個體UFP暴露水平的能力仍然非常有限。目前主要的測量方法是通過靜態現場測試來測量，但一個人每天到不同的地方參與各種活動，因此，此法並不能反映實際的個人暴露水平。而且，大多數現有的監測裝置體積龐大，甚至含有危險組件（例如放射性），市面上雖然也有不含危險組件的手提設備，但它們的體積仍然很大，且無法提供UFP的尺寸信息，可是，這對於暴露水平的研究非常重要。總括來說，目前並沒有如同移動電話般小巧及便於攜帶的個人UFP測量設備，這阻礙了相關的流行病學研究。最近的研究顯示，在微通道中通過應用低能量超聲波，微流體能分選不同尺寸的納米顆粒。低能量聲場對人類無害，而微流體是使設備小型化的可行途徑，因此本項目提出通過在微流體中使用粒子分離技術來開發個人UFP傳感器。為了開發這項技術，必須先了解納米粒子運動如何受聲音影響，及如何實際地把微流體裝置應用在空氣質量測量中。本項目將首先研究不同頻率和在不同幾何形狀的微通道中，聲波如何驅動流體的流動，接著研究由聲波驅動的流體如何影響納米顆粒的運動。該結果將用於設計和製造微流體納米顆粒分選裝置，並檢視其分離效率及流速和顆粒尺寸的關聯性。通過優化微流體裝置的參數，以類推開發UFP傳感器。傳感器將被校準並與現有的UFP測量儀器進行比較。本項目將增加聲場對粒子操縱的認識，展示跨學科技術研發，並確定個人傳感器發展的新方向，以改善空氣質量。

16206918.label: Realisation of objectives
16206918.value: The overall objectives have been achieved. The dynamics of nanoparticles in liquid (i.e. nanofluid) were extensively studied first. Then, the effect of acoustophoresis on nanoparticles in microchannels was investigated. The roles of acoustic radiation and acoustic streaming, together with the streaming patterns in different cross-sectional shapes, were studied. A nanoparticle separation method by acoustophoresis was developed, by which a microfluidic device was designed and optimized. An ultrafine particle sensor based on the microfluidic nanoparticle separation device was developed, and the performance of the sensor under different operating conditions was evaluated. Some key results are shown below. The forces exerted on particle suspensions in microchannels include the gravitational force, the buoyancy force, the Brownian motion force, and the particle interaction force. When an acoustic field is applied to the microchannels, particles also experience the acoustic forces which are mainly the acoustic radiation force (ARF) and the Stokes drag force induced by the acoustic streaming effect (ASE). As the buoyancy force usually balances the gravitational force, the resultant force can be neglected. Brownian motion affects small particles. In microfluidics and ultrasound regime, it affects particles less than 100nm. For the particle interaction, when the particle concentration is less than 0.01%, it is reasonable to neglect the particle interaction force. Therefore, when considering particles larger than 100nm with the concentration less than 0.01%, the particle motion is dominated by the acoustic forces. While micron particles can be directed to the pressure node by ARF, nanoparticles are affected by ASE and circulate according to the streaming vortices. A numerical model was developed to calculate the acoustic pressure field, the streaming velocity and the acoustophoretic motion of nanoparticles, ranging from 100nm to 900nm in diameter, in microchannels with different cross-sectional shapes, from rectangle, to trapezoidal and triangle. The model is 2D, with the cross-sectional area as the simulation domain. The results show that, as the wall inclination increases, the pressure amplitude increases on the top wall but decreases on the bottom wall, indicating that the geometry has the potential to concentrate the acoustic field. The narrower top wall generates a stronger pressure field. However, it comes with a weaker field on the bottom half, leading to a reduction in the overall average pressure. The geometry also alters the streaming pattern. In the studied cases, four vortices are generated in the bulk, two above the pressure node line and two below, which are counter-rotating compared to the neighboring vortices. They are Rayleigh’s streaming. The highest streaming velocity is found near the sidewalls. It may be explained by the fact that Rayleigh’s streaming is induced by the strong streaming vortices formed inside the viscous layer (Schlichting streaming), and the streaming velocity is the largest at the point where the streaming flow is initiated. The flow becomes weaker as it moves away from the sidewalls. In the rectangular case, the four vortices are identical in size and magnitude. They occupy the sides of the microchannel, leaving the center lightly affected by the ASE. As the sidewall inclination increases, the center of the vortices moves towards the vertical centerline, especially the top vortices. Hence, the fraction of the computational domain affected by the ASE increases. The resulting movement of nanoparticles was studied. It can be characterized as ARF- and ASE-dominant. In the model, the threshold is set at 800nm, which is independent of the microchannel geometry. Particles larger than that are considered as ARF-dominant, while particles smaller than that are ASE-dominant. The movement of ARF-dominant particles depends on the particles’ location. The computational domain is divided into two sections: 1) the center and 2) near sidewalls. Particles in the center are driven to the pressure node and stay there. Particles near sidewalls move in the direction of the streaming flow. They are found coming to the sidewalls and settled, either on the pressure node line or at the sidewalls. In contrast, the ASE-dominant particles do not stop even after a significant long time but circulate in the streaming vortices. They seem to be trapped by ASE inside a certain region defined by the particle size. Bigger particles flow into a smaller region close to the sidewalls, and smaller particles circulate the streaming vortices in a wider area. The wall inclination enhances the ASE-driven particle movement. A novel approach of nanoparticle sorting by ASE was developed. Since ASE-dominant particles can be directed outside the settling location of ARF-dominated particles, the separation of 400nm and 900nm particles can reach 100% and 98.9% purity, respectively, in a non-rectangular microchannel. Notably, separating ASE-dominant particles of different sizes is also possible as they are confined in different regions. In the triangular case, the purity of 100nm and 400nm particles achieves 92.2% and 75.6%, respectively. A two-step separation process was developed to separate multi particle sizes simultaneously. In the first step, ARF- and ASE-dominant particles are first separated by ASE. Then, in the second step, the ARF- dominant particles and ASE-dominant particles are separated by ARF and ASE, respectively. At the end of the system, there are four outlets. The optimal cross-sectional shape is selected for the ultrasonic zones. The effect of microchannel height on ASE-induced particle motion was investigated experimentally. It was observed that nanoparticles were in swirling motion shortly after switching on the acoustic excitation. They then moved into the streaming vortices. With the channel width equalling two wavelengths, a row of eight streaming vortices appeared with the axis of rotation parallel to the flow direction, which is independent of the channel height. In thin microchannels, the streaming vortices appeared in pairs. The adjacent vortices were initiated at the pressure node and circulated in opposite directions. The size of the vortices was nearly constant. In thick microchannels, the streaming vortices moved apart from each other. These vortices have different particle-capturing effect, which is affected by the channel height, meaning that adjusting the channel height can direct nanoparticles to designated locations. The ASE-induced particle focusing effects were investigated. In the streaming flow, nanoparticles experience an inward radial force induced by the shear gradient and an outward centripetal force. While the shear-induced radial force scales with the particle’s surface area, the outward force scales with the particle’s volume. Thus, the inward and outward forces affect the smaller and larger particles, respectively. The inward force can focus particles, as small as 310nm in diameter, to the vortex center. The shear-induced focusing effect can be enhanced by using a taller microchannel. In contrast, the outward force directs particles to the outer radius of the vortices. At specific channel heights, the outward force was large enough to detach particles from the rotational flow and concentrate them to specific positions. This focusing mechanism was newly discovered in our study. For the new focusing effect to occur, particles need to be small enough to avoid the influence of ARF and to be driven by the Stokes drag force into the streaming vortices, but large enough that the centripetal force is adequate to drive them away from the streaming vortices to the region of low streaming velocity. The concentration spots were independent of the size of particles that fall into this category. The spatial distance between them and the particles focused at the vortex center can potentially lead to a new separation strategy for nanoparticles.
