16206918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206918.value: The parameters that influence the acoustophoretic particle motion were investigated. The effects of microchannel’s cross-sectional geometry on ASE-induced particle motion were studied numerically and experimentally. Two ASE-induced separation methods were developed, the first one relies on the combination of ARF and ASE and the second one employs solely ASE. By employing the developed 2D numerical model, the impacts of microchannel’s cross-sectional shape were investigated. As the pressure wave and streaming flow are reflected by channel boundaries, changing the cross-sectional shapes from rectangular, to trapezoidal and triangular affects the acoustic fields and streaming velocity, thereby altering the particle’s trajectory. ASE in a non-rectangular microchannels can drive sub-micron particles away from the pressure node, enabling the separation of ARF- and ASE-dominated sub-micron particles. Furthermore, ASE-dominant particles are trapped by the streaming flow inside a certain area defined by the particle size. Larger ASE-dominant particles move in a narrower region close to the sidewalls and smaller particles occupy a wider area, thereby allowing the separation of ASE-dominant particles of different sizes. With these separation methods, a two-step separation process was developed to separate multi particle sizes simultaneously. In the first step, ARF- and ASE-dominant particles are first separated by ASE. Then, in the second step, the ARF- dominant particles and ASE-dominant particles are separated by ARF and ASE, respectively. The effect of microchannel height on ASE-induced particle motion was investigated experimentally. The number of streaming vortices is defined by the channel width, which is independent of the channel height. However, the channel height changes the streaming pattern and the particle-capturing effect of each streaming vortex. Adjusting the channel height can direct nanoparticles to designated locations. Besides, streaming vortices can induce two focusing effects, namely the shear-induced focusing and the newly discovered focusing caused by an outward centripetal force. The shear-induced focusing is caused by an inward radial force that directs particles as small as 310nm in diameter to the vortex center, while the newly discovered focusing detaches larger particles from the swirling flow and concentrate them to a specific region of low streaming velocity. The concentration spot is independent of the size of particles that fall into this category. The spatial distance between them enables the separation of nanoparticle. However, the new focusing effect only occurs at specific channel heights. Overall, the findings indicate that ASE can be the mechanism for sorting nanoparticles.

16206918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206918.value: This project focused on the particle motion in streaming vortices, investigated the particle motion inside streaming vortices, and developed separation methods for nanoparticles. To develop a portable ultrafine particles (UFPs) measurement device, a miniature particle counter is required after the separation process. Yet, concentrations of the sorted particles can be measured using acoustics, i.e., surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices. In an SAW device, two interdigital transducers (IDTs), two interlocking comb-shaped electrodes, are fabricated on a piezoelectric material with a sensing region between them. A sinusoidal electricity signal is applied to one IDT to generate an SAW passing through the sensing area to another IDT. Since the SAW will be distorted by the object in the sensing region, analyzing the received signal can give information about the object. To employ this technology, the microchannels containing the sorted particles simply go through the IDTs, then the IDTs will measure the concentration. To realize that, understanding how the particles affect the propagation of SAW is crucial. Parameters like wave speed, phase shift and attenuation, under different wave frequencies will be studied. By using the correlation between the characteristics of the wave and particle concentration, the device will be optimized for UFP measurement.

16206918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206918.value: The development of a personal UFP measurement technique draws the utmost attention in the field of air quality because adverse health effects are strongly associated with exposure to UFPs. To miniaturize a particle measurement device, microfluidics is a promising route, together with acoustics, which can effectively control nanoparticles in microchannels. To develop this technology, how nanoparticle motion in microchannels is affected by sound wave was understood. Then, the effects of microchannel’s cross-sectional geometry on the acoustic fields, the acoustic streaming velocity, and the acoustophoretic motion of nanoparticles, especially the ASE-induced particle motion, were studied. This project demonstrated how the streaming vortices concentrate nanoparticles to the vortex center, and discovered a new ASE-induced focusing effect occurred to slightly bigger particles. As the two particle focusing mechanisms happened concurrently, the spatial distance between them enables nanoparticle separation. The results were used to design a microfluidic nanoparticle sorting device, whose performance of the separation efficiency in relationship to the microchannel’s geometry and particle size was examined. The findings of this project will enhance the knowledge of nanoparticle manipulation by acoustic streaming vortices, and also determine a new direction for the development of personal sensors for better air quality.

16207118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207118.value: 隨著建築成本和人口密度的不斷增加，人們對超高層建築的需求越來越大。現今，世界上最高的建築——迪拜塔(Burj Khalifa Tower),其高度已經達到828 米。各式各樣的地標性建築，如別具特色幾何外形和功能的超高層建築，正受到建設者們的青睞。這些‘下壹代’地標性超高層建築是典型的風敏感結構，尤其是地處臺風帶上的超高層結構。 近年來，學者們開展了超高層結構的氣動特性、振動控制和結構抗風優化設計等相關研究來抑制超高建築結構的風致振動。這些研究大多針對某壹特定超高層建築，對於復雜幾何外形超高層建築結構風振抑制的系統研究較少。目前，針對地標性超高層建築開展的風洞試驗很少，風振抑制措施的應用也非常有限。迪拜塔和臺北101中心采用了調諧質量阻尼器來減振，但受保密條款的約束，這些減振措施沒有對外公布。此外，這些研究和應用大多僅關註對結構的影響，很少或沒有考慮其經濟性。同時考慮使用性和經濟性的超高層建築結構的抗風設計相關研究幾乎沒有。 本課題研究的目標是提出基於綜合成本效益的超高層建築結構抗風設計研究框架，實現地處臺風地帶上超高層建築結構的低成本優化設計。研究目標通過建立抑制風致振動的經驗成本模型，並將其與超高層建築結構設計的數值模擬優化算法相結合的方法實現。課題開發基於數值模擬的超高層抗風優化設計平臺，以輔助超高層建築結構的規劃、設計和施工。同時，課題研究成果可為平衡超高層建築結構的工程成本、壽命周期成本和結構的經濟性提供參考，從而保證超高層建築的耐久性和經濟性。

16207118.label: Realisation of objectives
16207118.value: A higher-order dynamic mode decomposition (HODMD) that equipped with a high-dimensional spectral decomposition functions to reveal the spatial-temporal evolution characteristics was developed in this study to analyze the wind-tunnel-measured building surface pressure. The HODMD analysis technique can successfully extract the modes and corresponding frequencies from the random pressure field, hence effectively reveal the physical meaning of each mode. This technique is applicable to analyze structures with closely-spaced natural frequencies and nonlinear mode shapes. Skyscrapers, in particular those with closely-spaced natural frequencies and nonlinear mode shapes, are susceptible to wind excitation, and hence are prone to have excessive building responses, i.e. tip lateral and torsional displacements and accelerations. Structural links between two adjacent building towers can be seen as a motion reduction technique to mitigate the excessive responses. The optimal location, i.e. between 0.7 to the top of the building, and the properties, i.e. mass and stiffness, of structural links were computed via an integrated performance-based optimization design framework. A novel life-cycle cost analysis (LCCA) framework, that simultaneously accounts for the non-stationary statistical characteristics of wind loading in association with the climate change, and stationary stochastic quantification of structural properties, were designed so as to achieve the project objectives. In order to deliver a reliable LCCA for the coastal buildings under the influence of the climate change, the integrated LCCA framework firstly predicts wind speeds in a coastal region considering global warming, and subsequently adopts the stochastic modeling of structural properties, and ultimately estimates the life-cycle cost of a target building—the second-generation wind-excited benchmark building. Specifically, the LCCA framework considers: • The latest climate change scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways) with future socioeconomic impacts and climate policies were applied to predict the stochastic wind field in future tropical cyclones; • Non-homogeneous Poisson processes were employed to model tropical cyclone intensities and occurrence rates, which led to more accurate estimates of uncertainties in the LCCA of tall buildings; • A stationary stochastic model for structural properties was adopted to estimate the life-cycle loss of the building, resulting in the suggested LCCA framework being regarded as a stochastic process; • The structure performances and the economic impacts in association with the installation of a motion reduction technique (e.g., a smart tuned mass damper and structural links) to a tall building under climate change effects. A baseline building erected along the coast of Hong Kong was analyzed considering its performance in the life cycle. In the LCCA processes, the influences of the climate change were evaluated via the predictions on the stochastic wind field from future tropical cyclones, and the performance of the building was assessed through the cost associated with the entire life cycle. In detail, the cost covers three major components within the life cycle of the building as, (a) the initial construction cost, which includes the cost of construction material, labor and transportation cost; (b) the serviceability failure cost, which seeks to quantify the losses of tall buildings out of operations under tropical cyclone winds; and (c) the maintenance cost, which is estimated by combing the ordinary maintenance services and the environmental impacts. The integrated LCCA framework combines three typical costs to comprehensively evaluate the total cost of the tall building in its life cycle. At the final stage of the project, a few motion reduction strategies were developed to enhance the performance of tall buildings under extreme winds, as well as to estimate the uncertainties related to the wind loads acting on structures under climate change impacts. The integrated LCCA framework and a finite element model that can estimate the dynamic performance of tall buildings were combined, to evaluate the economic and sustainability of a specific retrofit method. Consequently, structural optimization was performed to identify the optimal design of high-rise buildings subjected to various wind excitations.

16207118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207118.value: The influence of global climate change on the predicted typhoon wind field in Hong Kong was first evaluated by combining the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways climate scenarios, the Monte-Carlo Simulation method, and the refined wind field model with probability density functions of typhoon key parameters. It was found that the sea surface temperature near Hong Kong would increase by 2.24°C in the next 60 years (2021–2080) in the most severe climate condition (SSP5-85). The simulation results produced from the Monte-Carlo Simulation approach illustrated that the warmer climate in the future would raise the peak value of wind speed distribution to different extents according to variations of climate scenarios. These results pointed to one message: climate change was not to be ignored when predicting the wind fields of future typhoons, especially since future typhoons were predicted to be more severe than historical ones and were likely to cause unprecedented damage. Based on the aforementioned wind field predictions, a novel life-cycle cost analysis (LCCA) framework considering the climate change was proposed, which included the estimates of the initial cost, serviceability failure cost and maintenance cost of tall buildings. The probabilities of wind speeds induced by tropical cyclones were then combined with the fragility curve of the building to show the probability of a certain building failing to meet predefined criteria, which in turn led to the estimates of the cost associated with the serviceability failure. In the modeling of the fragility curve, the uncertainty concerning the damping of the building was taken into consideration via a pseudo-stochastic model of the structural damping ratio. Consequently, the life-cycle cost evaluation was delivered in a statistical sense integrating the probabilistic characteristics of tropical cyclone wind speeds and structural damping effects. It was found that global warming induces higher sea surface temperature and increases the occurrence rate and intensity of tropical cyclones, which have impacts on the failure loss of the benchmark building. In addition, the threshold values of the dynamic indicator have more significant impacts on the total cost of benchmark building compared to the damping ratio. As revealed using the optimal LCCA design, the motion reduction techniques can obviously reduce the maximum displacement and root-mean-square acceleration of structures, and also make the building paid-off period occur earlier.

16207118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207118.value: Considering the importance and benefits of the life-cycle cost assessment in the construction industry, the life-cycle cost analysis (LCCA) attracts attention from scholars with different backgrounds. Structural performance against wind hazards is necessary for modern tall building design, especially for structures close to the shore that have suffered substantial damage from tropical cyclone threats. In addition, global warming increases the occurrence rate and intensity of tropical cyclones, which also has positive impacts on the failure loss of the benchmark building. The major outcomes of the research project include successfully developing a refined typhoon wind field model to estimate the climate change impacts on typhoon performance in the near and far future, as well as establishing a novel integrated LCCA framework to evaluate the financial loss of tall structures in coastal areas while taking the effects of global warming into account. In addition, the predicted benefits and pay-off period from the integrated LCCA, as well as the optimal performance-based design, can provide guidance to structural engineers on designing a cost-effective high-rise building concerning the life-cycle cost during the entire design stages.

16207318.label: Project Objectives
16207318.value: Objective 1: A Framework to Assess the System Value of MDF from EVs It is envisioned that recent and future advances in the EV charging infrastructure will considerably relieve the range anxiety from the energy-critical EV owners and hence relax their energy demand during a single charging period. Therefore, EVs can take advantage of the energy-flexibility by adjusting their energy demands for the sake of economic benefits. Besides, for the EV drivers without critical deadline requirements, they can delay their charging deadlines to some extent as well. Such deadline-flexibility can significantly facilitate the operators to maintain the reliability and reduce the energy cost during the peak hours of power systems. To rigorously characterize the multi-dimensional flexibility (MDF) of EV charging, the first objective of this project is to propose a computational-tractable model that can quantify the system value of MDF in the competitive electricity market. Based on this model, i) we will theoretically prove the existence of competitive equilibrium, ii) we will also propose a distributed algorithm to calculate the market equilibrium price, and iii) further analytically characterize the relationship between the system-wide benefit and the flexibility level of the MDF. Objective 2: Mechanism Design to Elicit the Private Information of MDF from EVs The second objective is to propose an auction mechanism to elicit the truthful information of MDF from EVs. Efficient algorithms will be proposed to guarantee the mechanism's truthfulness, economic efficiency and computational efficiency. In particular, following the Vickrey-Clark-Groves mechanism design procedure, the resulting combinatorial auction requires to solve a mixed integer convex program efficiently. To tackle such a complicated problem, we will first design an exact algorithm for a small group of EVs based on generalized Benders decomposition. As for the large-scale EV setting, we will propose a perturbation-based randomized algorithm to achieve an (1 − ε)-optimal solution. Moreover, we will rigorously prove that the randomized algorithm will run in polynomial time in expectation based on the smoothed analysis. Objective 3: Harnessing MDF from EVs for Sustainability in Smart Cities In the previous two objectives, we mainly focus on how to model, assess, and exploit the value of MDF in smart grids without location-flexibility. Built upon the models in the previous two tasks, the third objective of this project is to further investigate the impact of location-flexibility of EVs on the vehicle-to-station assignment (VoSA) as well as the charging scheduling of EVs. First, we will propose an efficient offline algorithm to solve the static VoSA problem when all the EVs' charging requests are given. Second, we will propose an online algorithm for the dynamic VoSA problem when the EVs' charging requests are revealed to the system operator sequentially. Based on the proposed online algorithm for the dynamic VoSA problem, we will propose a joint VoSA and charging scheduling strategy, which can assign EVs to suitable charging stations and control the charging processes of EVs in an online fashion. Based on the joint VoSA and charging scheduling model, for the first time, the allocation of MDF to different charging stations to optimize the city-level performance will be investigated, which will help bridge the planning and operation of transportation system with power system in future smart cities.

16207318.label: Realisation of objectives
16207318.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: The Objective 1 of this project is to propose a computationally-tractable model that can quantify the system value of the multi-dimensional flexibility (MDF) of electric vehicle (EV) charging in competitive electricity markets. Specifically, we consider a strategic aggregator (e.g., a company who manages the charging of a fleet of EVs) who derives the optimal bidding strategy of the flexibility bounds (for cumulative energy and instantaneous power limits) and trades electricity in a pool. A multi-period bi-level program with a direct current power setup is considered. The upper-level problem represents the aggregator’s cost minimization, and the lower-level problem represents the market’s clearing process. Based on this bi-level formulation our theoretical analysis shows that EV aggregators can benefit from the MDF of EV charging via strategic bidding; however, the MDF will also bring negative impacts on the system generation cost, the payments of fixed loads and the non-strategic aggregators. Furthermore, these negative impacts depend on the locations of both the strategic and non-strategic aggregators. We have proposed to additionally charge the strategic aggregator for the newly introduced congestion to avoid the system performance degradation. The analytical results are validated based on extensive simulations. In summary, Objective 1 of this project has been completed. (100%) (2) Realization of Objective 2: The focus of Objective 2 is to design a mechanism that can elicit and exploit the MDF of EVs to maximize the social welfare of the overall system. We have investigated the following aspects to complete this objective. First, we have designed an online mechanism that can elicit the MDF from EVs to benefit the overall system. The key algorithmic challenges lie in the strategic nature of EVs and the incomplete knowledge of the future (e.g., arrivals and departures of EVs). To tackle these two challenges, we propose a posted-pricing mechanism (PPM) for the real-time EV charging without future information. In PPM, the charging station publishes the energy prices (that may be different from the prices of the power grids and vary over time) for EV charging. The EVs arrive sequentially and decide to either purchase a certain amount of energy based on the posted prices or leave without buying. By carefully designing the posted prices, the PPM is shown to be truthful, economic efficient and computationally efficient. In particular, the proposed PPM is optimal under the competitive analysis framework in the sense that no other online algorithms can achieve a better competitive ratio. In addition, we prove that the PPM is truthful, i.e., EV owners maximize their own utilities if they follow their true preferences. We also show that the PPM can be implemented in polynomial time. By extensive numerical experiments, we demonstrate the proposed PPM is robust against system uncertainties and outperforms the state-of-the-art benchmarks for real-time control of EV charging. Second, we have extended the PPM designed for the real-time EV charging problem to a more general online resource allocation problem. In this problem, a provider allocates multiple types of capacity-limited resources to customers that arrive sequentially. Each customer has a private valuation on the bundles of resource. The provider charges the payment from the customer who purchases a bundle of resources and incurs a supply cost with respective to the allocated resources. The goal is to maximize the social welfare, i.e., the total valuations of the customers minus the cost of the allocated resources. We have proposed a unified approach for the design of the posted prices and the analysis of the competitive ratios such that the PPM can achieve the best possible competitive ratios for setups with different supply cost functions (e.g., zero, linear and convex supply costs). This general resource allocation problem finds more real-world applications. Beyond the real-time EV charging, we have validated the empirical performance of the proposed PPM in cloud job scheduling and demonstrated that the PPM outperforms all the existing benchmarks. In summary, Objective 2 of this project has been finished. (100%) (3) Realization of Objective 3: The Objective 3 of this project is to further investigate the impact of location-flexibility of EVs on the system value in sustainable smart cities. We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 3: First, we have studied the impact of location-flexibility on the planning and operations of a network of geographically-distributed EV battery swapping stations (BSSs). We focus on two important decisions being made in two timescales, namely, a long-term decision on planning the initial inventory in each individual BSS, and a short-term decision on real-time vehicle-to-station (V2S) routing of EVs. We formulate a two-stage optimization problem and design a two-step solution scheme. In the first step, we plan the long-term initial inventory by sample average approximation to maximize the total expected revenue of BSSs. Based on the inventory planning, we further propose an online algorithm to determine real-time V2S routing without assuming any future information about the EV arrivals. We rigorously show that the worst-case performance of this online routing algorithm is guaranteed by a closed-form competitive ratio. Second, we have extended our study on the location-flexibility from BSSs to a network of EV charging stations. Unlike the BSS setting where the V2S and the EV charging decisions can be decoupled in two timescales, we must account for both decisions simultaneously in the EV charging setting. Therefore, we consider an online decision-making problem that makes V2S recommendations and schedules the corresponding charging allocation to maximize the expected total revenue of EV charging stations. Upon receiving a charging request from an EV, we offer the EV a station-price pair, which indicates the energy price if the EV charges at this station. The EV then decides whether to accept it or not. If the recommendation is accepted, the EV will arrive at the recommended station and pay for the charging service with the fixed price. We propose an online algorithm that decides the recommendations and charging schedule for sequential EV arrivals. We rigorously prove that the worst-case performance of this algorithm is guaranteed by bounded competitive ratios. In a case study based on the transportation network of Hong Kong, we show the proposed algorithm can achieve significant increase of revenues compared to benchmark online algorithms. In summary, Objective 3 of this project has been completed. (100%)

rows: Objective 1: A Framework to Assess the System Value of MDF from EVs It is envisioned that recent and future advances in the EV charging infrastructure will considerably relieve the range anxiety from the energy-critical EV owners and hence relax their energy demand during a single charging period. Therefore, EVs can take advantage of the energy-flexibility by adjusting their energy demands for the sake of economic benefits. To rigorously characterize the multi-dimensional flexibility (MDF) of EV charging, the first objective of this project is to propose a computational-tractable model that can quantify the system value of MDF in the competitive electricity market. Based on this model, i) we will theoretically prove the existence of competitive equilibrium, ii) we will also propose a distributed algorithm to calculate the market equilibrium price, and iii) further analytically characterize the relationship between the system-wide benefit and the flexibility level of the MDF.

Objective 2: Mechanism Design to Elicit the Private Information of MDF from EVs The second objective is to propose an auction mechanism to elicit the truthful information of MDF from EVs. Efficient algorithms will be proposed to guarantee the mechanism's truthfulness, economic efficiency and computational efficiency. In particular, following the Vickrey-Clark-Groves mechanism design procedure, the resulting combinatorial auction requires to solve a mixed integer convex program efficiently. To tackle such a complicated problem, we will first design an exact algorithm for a small group of EVs based on generalized Benders decomposition. As for the large-scale EV setting, we will propose a perturbation-based randomized algorithm to achieve an (1 − ε)-optimal solution. Moreover, we will rigorously prove that the randomized algorithm will run in polynomial time in expectation based on the smoothed analysis.

Objective 3: Harnessing MDF from EVs for Sustainability in Smart Cities In the previous two objectives, we mainly focus on how to model, assess, and exploit the value of MDF in smart grids without location-flexibility. Built upon the models in the previous two tasks, the third objective of this project is to further investigate the impact of location-flexibility of EVs on the vehicle-to-station assignment (VoSA) as well as the charging scheduling of EVs. First, we will propose an efficient offline algorithm to solve the static VoSA problem when all the EVs' charging requests are given. Second, we will propose an online algorithm for the dynamic VoSA problem when the EVs' charging requests are revealed to the system operator sequentially. Based on the joint VoSA and charging scheduling model, for the first time, the allocation of MDF to different charging stations to optimize the city-level performance will be investigated.

16207318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207318.value: Major findings and research outcome in this project are summarized as follows: First, we have proposed a multi-period bi-level optimization model for accessing the value of multi-dimensional flexibility (MDF) from the electric vehicle (EV) aggregators in competitive electricity markets. This bi-level model captures the aggregator’s cost minimization in the upper-level problem and the market clearing process in the lower-level problem. Our theoretical results show that the EV aggregator can benefit from the MDF via strategic bidding; however, the strategic behaviour will also bring negative impacts on the system generator cost, payments of fixed loads and non-strategic aggregators. Thus, we additionally propose a pricing scheme for the strategic aggregator to mitigate the negative impacts from the strategic behaviour. The research outcomes of this part have been published in the journal paper [4] listed in Part C. Second, we have proposed a posted-pricing mechanism for eliciting and exploiting the MDF of EVs to maximize the social welfare in the real-time EV charging problem. We rigorously prove three key properties of the proposed mechanism: (i) truthfulness, i.e., all EVs maximize their own utilities if they reveal their true preferences; (ii) economic efficiency, i.e., the online mechanism achieves the optimal competitive ratio under the competitive analysis framework; and (iii) computational efficiency, i.e., the mechanism can be implemented in polynomial time. Moreover, we have shown that the PPM can be extended to solve more general online resource allocation problem that can find a wide array of real-world applications (e.g., cloud job scheduling). The research outcomes of this part have been published in journal papers [1, 2, 3] and conference paper [1] listed in Part C. Third, we have proposed an online recommendation and charging schedule algorithm to jointly decide vehicle-to-station (V2S) assignment and the corresponding charging allocation in a network of EV charging stations. Theoretically, we rigorously prove that the worst-case performance of the proposed algorithm is guaranteed by bounded competitive ratios. Practically, we conduct a case study based on the transportation network of Hong Kong and show the algorithm can achieve significant increase of revenues compared to existing benchmark algorithms. Further, in a simpler setting for EV battery swapping stations, we can decompose the V2S assignment and charging schedule into decisions in two timescales. We have proposed a two-step algorithm to decide the long-term planning and short-term real-time control, respectively. All those results show the benefits of utilizing location-flexibility of EVs in sustainable smart cities. The research outcomes of this part have been published by journal paper [5] and conference paper [2] listed in Part C.

16207318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207318.value: This project mainly focuses on harnessing the multi-dimensional flexibility of electric vehicles to optimize the city-level performance in real-time charging problems. Our key outcome of this project is to propose a posted-pricing mechanism that can elicit and exploit the flexibilities with guaranteed worst-case performances. We also propose a unified approach for design and analysis of the proposed mechanism. Thus, the mechanism has great potentials to be deployed in broader applications in the general online resource allocation problems. Thus, it is a promising direction to further extend the mechanism to more general online problems in sustainable smart cities (e.g., resource allocation in cloud data centers and transportation systems). In addition, we make no assumptions on future knowledge about the EV arrival sequence in this project and our proposed mechanism provides guarantees on the worst-case performance. However, in practice, additional information about the future may be predicted based on the powerful machine learning tools and historical data. Thus, further investigations are needed to study how to incorporate predictions into the design of the mechanism to obtain beyond-the-worst-case results.

16207318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207318.value: Recent years have seen the trend that electric vehicles will replace gasoline and diesel vehicles to become mainstream of urban transportation in the coming decades. However, the huge charging demand from electric vehicles greatly increases the burden of the current electricity grids. To mitigate the negative impacts from electric vehicle charging, this project studies how to incentivize electric vehicle owners to provide their flexibilities by adjusting their charging requests (e.g., charging location, energy demand and departure time) in charging infrastructures. Towards this end, this project proposes new models to access the value of the flexibilities from electric vehicle owners in the electricity markets, and further designs novel mechanisms to harness the flexibilities to improve the stability and economic efficiency of the electricity grid. The outcomes of this project can lead to rich insights into the planning and operation of charging infrastructures, and further promote the penetration of electric vehicles in green and sustainable cities.

16207518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207518.value: The emerging use of Gallium Nitride (GaN) device is leading a high speed revolution for high voltage (HV) power circuits. Compared to their conventional slow silicon counterparts, GaN devices simultaneously offer fast switching and improved efficiency due to the significantly reduced parasitics. Thus, power adapters, chargers, LED drivers and other power circuits that use GaN can be smaller and lighter. Depletion-mode (D-mode) GaN transistors, which feature higher robustness and lower fabrication cost than enhancement-mode GaN switches, are widely used in HV applications. However, these D-mode transistors have a negative threshold voltage and lack a body diode for reverse current operation. Therefore, a special GaN driving circuit is necessary to ensure the fast and completed turning-on and turning-off of the transistor and to provide reverse current conduction with low energy loss. The direct driving scheme, with a negative voltage to turn off the D-mode GaN transistor, is an effective solution for driving the main switch of the power converters because it provides high reliability and almost zero reverse recovery loss. However, it is not suitable to configure the GaN as a power diode with this scheme to conduct reverse current, due to the high voltage drop on the GaN device. In addition, it is challenging to operate HV GaN-based power converters in a synchronized configuration with accurate dead-time control, because of the delay in signal level shifting. In this project, a novel D-mode GaN driver will be developed to address the above issues together with a proposed pseudo-synchronous scheme in which the turning the rectifier switch on/off will be determined locally without HV signal level shifting. In addition, techniques for precise switching timing control will be investigated to achieve almost perfect dead time in different operation modes. These techniques will help to further improve the system efficiency for a variety of GaN-based switching power converters with high operation frequency. A closed-loop HV bidirectional buck converter will also be implemented with the proposed GaN drivers to verify the effectiveness of the proposed techniques. 氮化鎵器件的應用使得高壓功率電路向著更高的速度發展。與傳統的矽器件比較，氮化鎵功率器件的寄生顯著降低，具有更高的開關頻率和效率，因此可以有效减少包括功率轉接器、充電器、LED驅動器在內的功率電路的體積和重量。 與現時增强型氮化鎵開關相比，空乏型氮化鎵電晶體具有更高的穩定性和更低的製造成本，因此在高壓應用中得到廣泛採用。但是，空乏型電晶體的閾值電壓為負，同時缺少反向二極體導通特性。這些新的特徵需要設計相應的驅動電路來保證快速可靠的功率管開關控制以及提供低損耗的反向電流傳輸。直接控制方案採用負電壓來關斷空乏型氮化鎵功率管，同時具有較高的可靠性和零反向恢復功耗。因此，這種方案非常適合用於驅動功率電路中作為主開關管的氮化鎵器件。但是，這一方案難以同時用於驅動作為整流管的氮化鎵電晶體。過高的反向導通壓降會產生顯著的導通損耗。此外，電壓位準轉換電路的延時給精確控制同步高壓功率轉換器的死區時間帶來了更多的設計挑戰。 在這一項目中，我們將開發一個全新的空乏型氮化鎵器件驅動電路以解決上述問題。同時，這一電路結合準同步控制方案可以去除低速的電壓位準轉換電路，實現開關時間的局部精確控制。此外，我們還將研究和改良不同工作模式下死區時間控制的解決方案，從而進一步提高採用氮化鎵的高速功率轉換電路的系統效率。最終，我們將基於提出的氮化鎵驅動電路，設計並實現一個閉環的高壓雙向功率轉換電路來驗證提出方案的有效性。

16207518.label: Realisation of objectives
16207518.value: The main goal of this project is to develop gate drivers for Gallium Nitride (GaN) HEMT power devices to improve the overall power conversion efficiency of switching converters. We worked on Objectives 1 through 4 together to get a clear overall picture to optimize overall power efficiency. Objectives 1 and 2 are related to improving the accuracy of the dead-time between the turn-on and turn-off of the high-side and low-side power switches. Several on-chip current sensors have been investigated to sense GaN HEMT current. A slope sensor was developed to detect the rising or falling slope of the current. The slope sensor and two sample-and-hold (S&H) circuits form a zero-voltage switching detection circuit, enabling more accurate turn-on and turn-off of the power GaN HEMT switches. This forms the basic building block of a GaN driver circuit. In Objective 3, negative voltages are critical to turn off the D-mode GaN devices. We found that negative voltages are very useful to ensure turn-off of E-mode GaN devices and prevent false turn-on during switching. This is one of the main reasons why E-mode GaN devices are not used in the design instead of D-type devices, although E-mode devices outperform D-type devices. We have developed an on-chip negative voltage generator with -4 V to -5 V to turn off the GaN device. Our design shows that the negative voltage generator has enough drive capability to pull down the gate voltage within 10 ns. A bidirectional converter was developed in Objective 4 that can be configured as Buck converter with input voltage range of 20 V to 40 V and as Boost converter with input voltage range of 12 V to 20 V, depending on the switching sequence of the power switches. The bidirectional converter was used to test the power conversion efficiency of the converter using two off-chip GaN devices. The design of the bidirectional converter with our designed monolithic controller chip and off-chip GaN HEMT has been implemented successfully and published in the IEEE Trans. on Circuits and Systems – I [J1].

16207518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207518.value: To make this project a success, several novel ideas and techniques have been researched, analyzed, simulated and developed. The key consideration is how to accurately control the dead-time between the turn-on and turn-off of the high-side and low-side power GaN switches. Instead of using conventional voltage detection, a slope detector is proposed to detect the slope of the switching node and is used to control the zero-voltage switching with less than 3ns deviation. To eliminate switch false turn-on due to the induced pulse on the gate from the high dv/dt slew rate of the switching node, a three-level gate driver that provides a negative voltage close to VDD is developed. With these novel ideas, a GaN driver for a bi-directional Buck/Boost converter with near optimal-point tracking dead-time control was developed. The detail design of this GaN drive is published in a journal paper [J1].

16207518.value: In this project, a slope detector is developed to detect the slope of the switching node and control the zero-voltage switching. This technique can be further applied to other zero-voltage switching converter applications. The developed three-level gate driver providing positive, zero and negative voltages can also be applied to other high frequency switching converter designs for better performance.

16207818.label: Realisation of objectives
16207818.value: TCP congestion control relies on a crucial observation - packet loss is used as the primary indication of network congestion. Under this observation, senders adjust sending rates upon packet loss. The Internet has adopted such a congestion control for the past 30-40 years. However, with network bandwidth from a few Mbps to today’s tens of Gbps and on-board memory from a few hundreds of KB to hundreds of GB, the corelation between packet loss and network congestion becomes weakening. Specifically, a loss-based control congestion either causes bufferbloat under large buffers or leads to poor throughput with small buffers, respectively. Bottleneck Bandwidth and RTT or BBR was recently proposed by Google with the promise of converging to the optimal operating point by maximizing delivery rate and minimizing roundtrip time (RTT). Drastically different from the conventional loss-based congestion control, BBR does not passively react to packet loss. Instead, it proactively measures the bottleneck bandwidth and minimum round-trip time. Based on those measurements, BBR aims to deliver at full bottleneck bandwidth without creating an excess queue in the pipe. For any TCP connection, there always exists a slowest link at a time, known as the bottleneck link, which dictates a connection’s maximum delivery rate and is the only place where a persistent queue can build up. Ideally, a connection should (1) send at a rate matching the bandwidth available at the bottleneck (denoted as BtlBw), and (2) maintain the amount of data in flight that matches exactly one bandwidth-delay product (BDP), i.e., inflight = BtlBw x RTT, where RTT is the round-trip time. It has been proved theoretically that this operating point maximizes a connection’s throughput (fill the pipe) while minimizing RTT (keeping queues empty), and is optimal for both individual connections and the entire network. However, conventional congestion control delivers at full pipe bandwidth at the cost of bufferbloat. When the buffer is large, the resulting bufferbloat can easily cause excessive queueing delay in the order of seconds. Converging to the optimal operating point is particularly challenging, because BtlBw and RTT cannot be measured at the same time. To measure BtlBw, the pipe must be overfilled, and in persistent queue form; to measure RTT, on the other hand, all queues must be empty. BBR finds the optimal operating point by sequentially probing a connection’s maximum delivery rate and minimum RTT. In a nutshell, BBR estimates BtlBw as the maximum delivery rate in recent 10 round trips and RTT as the minimum RTT measured in the past 10 seconds. The max-filtered bandwidth and the min-filtered RTT can accurately model the pipe. BBR governs its sending behavior through two control parameters: pacing rate and congestion window (CWND). BBR cycles through different pacing rates to probe for more bandwidth, drains off excess queues, and cruises at the current MaxBw to fully utilize bandwidth. BBR also sets CWND as a small multiple of BDP (2× by default), so as to bound the volume of inflight data without creating long persistent queues. In the steady state, a BBR flow alternates between ProbeBw and ProbeRTT phases to dynamically characterize the pipe’s BtlBw and RTT, based on the recently measured delivery rates and RTTs. Our preliminary study shows there exists a strong bias against short-lived RTT flows. At a first glimpse, this appears to be counter-intuitive as BBR flows probe for more bandwidth in consecutive round trips. When additional bandwidth becomes available, flows with short RTTs would respond to this environmental change more quickly, and hence have the advantage to claim more bandwidth. In reality, however, it turns out to be not the case. In this project, we first investigate the root cause of BBR’s bias against short RTT flows by closely examining the behaviors of competing flows. Based on that, we design our new congestion control mechanism. In summary, there are two major findings in our investigation. The first finding attributes to how persistent queues are formed on the bottleneck. Specifically, when a long RTT flow returns to ProbeBw phase, it resumes with its previous MaxBw. Because a short RTT flow detects a higher MaxBw when the long RTT flow is in ProbeRTT phase, the aggregated MaxBw of flows exceeds the bottleneck capacity, and thus a persistent queue is formed. After the long RTT flow exits ProbeRTT phase, the RTTs of both flows explode until the surging inflight is bounded by congestion control. Noticing that a persistent queue has drastically different impact on the throughput of flows with different RTTs. Through analysis on the persistent queue, the bandwidth allocation for competing flows is primarily determined by their backlog. We measure the instantaneous queue backlog of flows by instrumenting the kernel functions on the bottleneck. The results show that the short RTT flow quickly occupies all queue slots when the long RTT flow enters ProbeRTT phase. This implies that it has probed for more bandwidth. The short RTT flow then drains off queues and tries to transmit at the new bandwidth. However, when the long RTT flow returns to ProbeBw phase, the short RTT flow quickly recedes, and never finds a chance to reclaim the bandwidth. The second finding attributes to the fact when the queue builds up, the backlog of the flow with shorter RTT is reduced, so is its bandwidth share. We examine the instant when the long RTT flow completes ProbeRTT phase, in which both flows enter ProbeBw phase. Initially, flows detect roughly the same MaxBw, thus they send at roughly the same rate. As the long RTT flow has a larger MinRTT, it injects far more packets into the queue over time, which operate at a much higher delivery rate. Unable to probe a higher bandwidth, the short RTT flow quickly expires its MaxBw and replaces it with a smaller value. This, in turn, forces the short flow to send less amount of data, which results in an even smaller queue share and a lower delivery rate. This motivates us to design a congestion control mechanism that reacts to the persistent queue build-up earlier. Specifically, it should constantly detect if an excess queue is formed on the bottleneck link. When it happens, it has to quickly intervene and refrain long RTT flows from pouring too much traffic into the pipe, so as to protect short RTT flows from being pushed out. Our proposed congestion control scheme, called BBQ, follows exactly this intuition, in which it properly regulates the excess traffic injected into the pipe. The highlight of our proposed BBQ is as follows. BBQ flows continuously monitor the presence of a persistent queue during RTT measurements. When the pipe is full, BBQ flows probe for approximately the same period of time, so as to maintain an equal share of the queue backlog. When the pipe is underutilized, BBQ simply behaves like BBR, in which flows can quickly probe and utilize the available bandwidth. We design and implement BBQ, which is shown to provide significantly better RTT fairness without compromising full delivery rate or low latency. The evaluation shows that BBQ outperforms BBR with respect to RTT fairness by up to 6.1×, while achieving essentially the same link utilization with shorter end-to-end latency.

16207818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207818.value: We started by designing and implementing a new network instrumentation that can produce all the internal network status (Objective 1). We built an in-house cluster of 20 blade servers, and each has a Xeon E5-1410 8-thread CPU, interconnected through 1 Gbps NIC. We used Linux 4.9.18 with the latest BBR kernel module, and sch_fq module for flow pacing. We constructed different network topologies, in which senders connect to receivers with a configurable RTT governed by NetEm tools. The server running on Linux acts as a bottleneck switch for controllable bandwidth with buffer size per port set to 2 MB. We developed a dedicated framework to coordinate and synchronize the measurement. We used Netperf tools to generate flows, and used the Linux tc tool to control packet delay, bottleneck bandwidth, and AQM deployment. We further optimized our framework so that TCP small queues, a flow control enhancement in Linux kernel, will not interfere with NetEm in Linux tc. We conducted theoretical and experimental analysis on the BBR flow dynamics with focuses on the correlation between flow performance and RTTs, and interactions among different flows (Objective 2). We are particularly interested in finding out whether the bias towards long-lived RTT flows is an intrinsic problem of BBR. We carried out theoretical analysis and conducted a variety of benchmark experiments under different network configurations. We confirmed that BBR flows with longer RTT dominate flows with shorter RTT, irrespective of configurations. We further demonstrate, through in-depth analysis of flow behaviors, that such a bias incurs in two phases: (1) when probing for more bandwidth, a persistent queue forms on the bottleneck due to the excess traffic; (2) the long RTT flow probes for longer time, and hence injects more traffic to dominate the queue backlog. Based on the insight from the analysis and experimentation, we proposed and implemented a new fair congestion control mechanism, called BBQ, and further illustrate that it can be incorporated at the hypervisor for transparently upgrading (Objectives 3 and 4). We implemented BBQ in Linux kernel 4.9.18 and evaluated its performance in the cluster we built. The extensive evaluation show that BBQ delivers at full bandwidth with near-optimal latency, while it can reduce the queueing delay by 64% and consistently outperforms BBR with better RTT fairness by improving the bandwidth share of a short flow by up to 6.1×.

16207818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207818.value: Congestion control is essential in achieving high throughput and low latency, while enabling a fair share of network bandwidth allocation among multiple traffic flows. BBR periodically and proactively estimates the available bandwidth and round-trip time (RTT), which effectively eliminates the formation of persistent packet queues, thus in theory can deliver at the maximum rate with the minimum latency. However, BBR is still largely a work in progress. There are many details that have not been worked out. Its performance and behaviors have not been properly analysed in practical networking scenario. Our investigation in this project demonstrates there exist crucial fairness problem in BBR, in which flows with different RTTs exhibit inadequate bandwidth allocation. One aspect worth further exploration is the design and implementation of an open framework, which is capable of accurately reproducing the measurement results by incorporating and comparing different congestion mechanisms. It should be flexible in adapting to different networking configurations (e.g., Wi-Fi, wide-area networks), and tailoring for different application scenario such as machine learning jobs, video broadcast and search. The significance of such investigations is to provide an open platform which can captures the interplay of the different components and traffic behavior in practice.

16207818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207818.value: Congestion control is at the center of the network design. For over three decades, we have used a loss-based congestion control mechanism or its variants widely adopted in TCP. The central idea is to adjust sending rates by using packet loss as the congestion indication. This often results in long response time and low throughput, commonly observed from mobile applications to parallel data processing frameworks. A new congestion control algorithm, named Bottleneck Bandwidth and Roundtrip time or BBR, has recently been proposed, which adopts a completely different design philosophy by proactively measuring the bottleneck bandwidth and roundtrip delay, and adjusts the sending rates accordingly. This has been shown to approach the theoretical optimal by maximizing delivery rate while minimizing roundtrip time. The significance of this project and its outcomes are primarily two-folded: (1) through rigorous theoretical analysis and experiments, we demonstrate that there is an inherent fairness problem in the proposed BBR algorithm, in which flows with long-lived RTT dominate flows with short-lived RTT, irrespective of network configurations; (2) we designed and implemented a new version of BBR that provide significantly better fairness while achieving the same link utilization and shorter end-to-end latency.

16207918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207918.value: Methane hydrates are ice-like inclusion compound with methane molecules trapped in water molecules. They are widely found in thermodynamically favourable conditions of high pressure and low temperature such as marine and permafrost deposits. Globally, methane hydrate-bearing soils (MHBS) sequester more than 10 trillion tons of carbon, which is about twice as much as in coal, oil and conventional gas reserves. The harvest of methane hydrates for energy use requires driving hydrates out of their thermodynamically stable conditions (dissociation) by heating or depressurization. During the dissociation process, methane hydrates convert to methane gas and water, inducing significant soil deformation and instability. The deformation and instability of MHBS may trigger underwater landslides, cause extraction wellbore collapse, release a huge amount of methane into the atmosphere, and damage underwater infrastructures such as pipelines and cables. To date, there has not been any long-term extraction of gas from these abundant resources due to the complexity of MHBS behavior. Consequently, the design of extraction wellbores for long-term production is still a challenge. Some researchers have investigated the behaviour of MHBS prior to dissociation, while few studies focus on the deformation and instability behaviour of MHBS during dissociation. The proposed project will address this challenge through laboratory testing and theoretical constitutive modelling with reference to MHBS in marine deposits. Unlike previous studies, methane hydrate will be synthesized in soil specimens with different clay types and clay contents. The corresponding hydrate pore habit and morphology will be investigated through high resolution X-ray CT tests. Triaxial tests will be carried out using a new environmental triaxial system able to control high pressures (up to 20 MPa) and a wide range of temperatures (-20 to 60 degrees Celsius). The project will focus on the deformation and instability of MHBS during dissociation. To assist in the interpretations of dissociation test results, triaxial tests will be also conducted to investigate the small strain stiffness, dilatancy and shear strength of MHBS with various micro-structures. Based on new experimental results, an advanced constitutive model will be developed. Different from existing models, the new model will be able to predict the behaviour of MHBS with different micro-structures using a single set of parameters. The success of this project will improve our fundamental understanding and theoretical modelling of the behaviour of MHBS. The new test results and theoretical model will enable researchers and engineers to improve the design of extraction wellbores for long-term production scenarios. 甲烷水合物是由水分子和甲烷分子構成的固態化合物，廣泛存在於海底土層和陸地永凍層等高溫低壓環境中。在全球海洋中，甲烷水合物蘊含的碳超過10萬億噸，大約是煤，石油和常規天然氣含碳量總和的2倍。在溫度升高或壓力降低等條件下，固態水合物會分解為甲烷氣體和水，並伴隨土體變形甚至失穩。若開採不當，含水合物土的變形和失穩會誘發海底滑坡，破壞開採井和海底電纜等基礎設施，並向大氣釋放大量甲烷氣體。迄今為止，由於含水合物土性質的複雜性，人類尚未實現甲烷水合物的商業化開採。一些學者已經研究了含水合物土開採之前的性質，而土體在水合物分解過程中的變形和失穩規律尚不清楚。 本項目將針對海底含甲烷水合物土開展室內實驗和理論模擬研究。室內實驗部分，研究團隊將通過三軸實驗研究水合物分解過程中的土體變形和失穩規律，考慮不同黏土含量的影響。並將通過高分辨率X射線CT實驗研究水合物生成過程和分解過程中土體微觀結構的變化規律，以解釋含水合物土的宏觀性質。基於全新的實驗結果，研究團隊將開發先進的理論模型，用於預測開採過程中含水合物土的變形和失穩。本項目的實驗和理論成果有利於提高人類對含水合物土的認知，幫助工程師設計更加安全高效的甲烷氣開採方案。

16207918.label: Realisation of objectives
16207918.value: This project investigated the dissociation-induced deformation and instability of methane hydrate-bearing soils (MHBS) with various microstructures using laboratory testing and theoretical constitutive modelling. All of the proposed four objectives have been achieved through the following activities along with the original plan: (1) Some new testing systems were developed to study the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of MHBS and the interaction between MHBS and extraction wellbores. An advanced high-pressure and low-temperature triaxial system was developed for MHBS and hydrate-free soil (as a reference) with various microstructures. Novel in-flight centrifuge modelling was developed to study the effects of hydrate dissociation on vertical wellbores. [Objectives 1, 2 and 3] (2) Extensive tests were carried out to study the influence of microstructure on the mechanical behaviour of MHBS and hydrate-free soils, including compressibility, dilatancy and shear strength. Specimens with different microstructures were prepared with different clay contents and specimen preparation methods. Their compressibility was determined from isotropic compression tests, while the dilatancy and shear strength were studied through triaxial compression tests. The influence of microstructure on the compressibility, dilatancy and shear strength of soils, which govern the dissociation-induced deformation and instability of MHBS, was revealed. In addition, microstructural analysis was conducted to determine soil microstructure and explain the macro-behaviour. [Objectives 1 and 3] (3) Triaxial tests were carried out to investigate the dissociation behaviour of MHBS with different degrees of hydrate saturation and clay contents. The high-pressure and low-temperature triaxial apparatus was used. Toyoura sand with and without adding kaolin clay was tested. The data are useful for revealing the influence of microstructure on the dissociation-induced deformation and instability of MHBS. To better understand the relationship between micro and macro behaviour, discrete element method (DEM) simulations were also carried out to study the dissociation behaviour of HMBS with various pore habits and morphologies. [Objective 2] (4) The effects of hydrate dissociation on vertical casing-sediment interaction were revealed through novel in-flight centrifuge modelling. The centrifuge tests monitored variables like temperature and wellbore force distribution. The results illustrate the impacts of dissociation-induced deformation and instability on wellbore performance. The results are useful for the design of gas production. [Objectives 1 and 2] (5) A state-dependent constitutive model was developed for the thermos-hydro-mechanical behaviour of MHBS. The bounding surface plasticity rather than the classical elastoplasticity was used to better simulate the progressive degradation of the hydrate-induced structure. The uniqueness of this model is the incorporation of a phase parameter, which can account for the coupled effects of temperature and pore pressure on the mechanical behaviour of MHBS. This new model was validated using the measured results of MHBS with different microstructures. Test data from this project and literature were both used. [Objective 4]

16207918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207918.value: Key findings and outcome related to Objective 1: The microstructure of MHBS and its influence on the macro-behaviour were studied through X-ray CT tests, DEM simulations, geotechnical centrifuge modelling and constitutive modelling. For instance, the results indicate that adding a small amount of clay content (e.g., 15% by mass) can significantly alter the microstructure and temperature-pressure response of MHBS during dissociation. (Reference: Journal paper 1 and Conference paper 2 in the list shown below; more papers will be published in the near future) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 2: An advanced triaxial system was developed to control a high confining pressure (up to 20 MPa) and a wide temperature range (-30 to 90 degrees Celsius). Triaxial tests were conducted to obtain unique data about the dissociation-induced deformation and instability behaviour of MHBS specimens. Novel in-flight centrifuge modelling was conducted to reveal the effects of hydrate dissociation on vertical casing-sediment interaction. Test results show that the progressive hydrate dissociation could induce large axial compressive and tensile loads within and above the perforated interval of wellbores, respectively. Both of them should be carefully considered for safe gas production. (References: Journal paper 5; more papers will be published soon) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 3: The influence of microstructure on the compressibility, dilatancy and shear strength of soils, which govern the dissociation-induced deformation and instability of MHBS, was revealed. In addition, both water and methane gas are present in MHBS after dissociation. Soil water retention ability greatly affects the flow of methane gas. The research team studied the water retention ability of soil specimens with different microstructures and developed a theoretical model. (References: Journal papers 2,3,4) Key findings and outcome related to Objective 4: A state-dependent bounding surface model was developed for the hydro-mechanical behaviour of MHBS. A phase parameter was newly incorporated to account for the coupled effects of temperature and pore pressure on the mechanical behaviour of MHBS. This unique feature of the model enables it to capture the behaviour of MHBS inside the hydrate stability region. A modified dilatancy was proposed considering the degree of hydrate saturation, phase parameter and stress state. This new model was validated using the measured results of drained and undrained triaxial tests on MHBS with different microstructures and states. Furthermore, a material point method formulation was developed for large-deformation analysis. (References: Journal paper 1 and Conference paper 1)

16207918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207918.value: The particle size distribution and properties of natural MHBS can vary greatly. Previous studies of MHBS mainly focused on coarse-grained sand with very few silt and clay particles for simplicity. However, it is reported that 90% of hydrates are buried in ﬁne-grained sediments, like the marine sediments in the South China Sea and many other areas. According to the site investigation results, fine particles would significantly alter the multi-scale properties of MHBS, such as its hydrate morphology and THMC behaviour. Moreover, the current project has preliminarily investigated the influence of clay content on the behaviour of MHBS and soil-wellbore interactions. The importance of clay content is significant based on the test results. There is an urgent need to improve the fundamental understanding and modelling of fine-grained MHBS and the design method of extraction wellbores for harvesting methane hydrate safely and efficiently. One PhD student trained in this project plans to work on these problems as a postdoctoral fellow.

16207918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207918.value: Methane hydrate is a promising alternative energy source, but it is very challenging to harvest them. Any design failure in extraction wellbores may induce serious consequences like underwater landslides and extraction wellbore collapse. Up to now, there has not been any long-term gas extraction from these abundant resources due to the complexity of MHBS behaviour. The project was carried out to improve the understanding and modelling of MHBS through advanced testing and theoretical modelling. In the laboratory testing, a new pressure and temperature-controlled triaxial system was adopted to investigate (1) the deformation and instability of MHBS during dissociation; (2) small strain stiffness; (3) dilatancy and shear strength of MHBS. Furthermore, the effects of hydrate dissociation on vertical casing-sediment interaction were revealed through novel in-flight centrifuge modelling. Based on experimental results, a novel constitutive theoretical model for MHBS was developed to capture the effects of various factors, including stress, density, clay content and type, and hydrate saturation. The results of this project, no doubt, extend our fundamental understanding and improve the modelling of the hydro-mechanical behaviour of MHBS. This project can also benefit society by helping engineers harvest energy from marine deposits safely and efficiently in the future.

16208218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208218.value: Aluminum is among the most widely used materials in industrial and commodity applications. As a major producer of aluminum, China pays a very heavy toll in terms of environmental destruction and public health deterioration. In one locality, we found evidence that suggests an association between the high levels of air pollution, underground water pollution and land pollution from the electrolytic aluminum industry, and higher cancer rates and reduced average life span. Given the serious drawbacks with the traditional Hall–Héroult method of electrolytic aluminum production, we aim to introduce a novel and ‘greener’ technique, using ionic liquids (ILs) as the electrolyte in the production of aluminum. The process is more energy efficient, with low (practically zero) pollution. Our preliminary investigation of the structures and properties of ILs revealed that, when using ILs, the reaction temperatures used for aluminum electrolysis could be reduced to below 100°C, and that energy consumption levels would remain below 10kW·h/kg-Al, thereby significantly reducing the emission of greenhouse (e.g., CO2) and hazardous (e.g., HF) gases. Our proposed work will involve an in-depth investigation of the relationship between structures of ILs and the raw materials used in electrolytic systems. 16208218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208218.value: At present, the Hall-Héroult method, which is also referred to as cryolite-alumina molten salt electrolysis, has been widely adopted in modern electrolytic Al industrial production in China and globally. This is the only method that can be applied to the large-scale industrial production of metal Al. Although the exhaust emissions from electrolytic Al plants are able to meet the permitted environmental emission standards, the total volume of these emissions still far exceeds the environmental carrying capacity of the production areas due to the high density of production facilities. These exhaust emissions not only severely restrict the sustainable development of Al production companies but also place a heavy burden on the local environment. Therefore, there is an urgent demand to develop innovative, environmentally friendly methods with a higher energy efficiency for the production of Al, such as low-temperature or room temperature (RT) Al electrolysis, which could significantly reduce the energy consumption required for Al production. As such, based on a detailed investigation and preliminary experiments, it is proposed in the present study that ionic-liquid-based Al electrolysis can provide a feasible solution to the problems associated with conventional Al production. Through this research project, we found that ionic liquid electrolytic Al technology is feasible and has significant industrialization potential. Compared with the chloroaluminate-based ILE system, [Emim][Tf2N]/AlCl3 and [Bmim][Tf2N]/AlCl3 are less sensitive to water and air, thus showing promise for use in low-temperature Al electrolysis. However, their high viscosity and low solvent power for Al raw materials remain significant disadvantages. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the underlying mechanisms of non-chloroaluminate-based ILEs and how their properties are affected by the electrolysis conditions. Their physical and chemical properties could thus be continuously optimized with the aim to improve the quality of the Al deposition layer and the electrolysis efficiency and thus facilitate their practical implementation. Benzene and toluene were used as additives in the electrolyte system and significantly improved the electrolyte properties and the quality of the Al deposition layer. On the other hand, because they are volatile organic compounds, they have a toxicity and corresponding environmental risk that makes them unsuitable for future large-scale applications. Therefore, safer and more reliable electrolyte additives are required. We have found the low energy, low cost, and more efficient method to do the electrolytic aluminum. 10 patents filed, four granted, and 2 journal papers published.

16208218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208218.value: The refining reaction for waste Al alloys is affected by both cathodic Al deposition and anodic Al alloy dissolution. There remains a gap in the research regarding the dissolution process of the Al alloy anode and the influence of impurities on the refining reaction. In the future, more in-depth research is required on the effects of reaction conditions such as temperature, stirring, and electrolysis and the influence of different ILE systems on the anodic dissolution process, and the influence of impurities in the anode Al alloy on the overall electrolytic refining process. If this is achieved, a more comprehensive and systematic Al refining system could be established, providing a more solid theoretical foundation for the future application of this technology in the industry. In terms of industrial implementation, research on low-temperature ILE-based electrolysis and Al refining technology has been conducted in the laboratory stage, but the relevant industrial pilot studies have yet to be launched. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out technological integration and scaling-up research by combining governmental (Liaocheng government), industrial (Xinfa Group), and research team (Professor Mi’s team) efforts.

16208218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208218.value: The proposed technology can produce high-quality, high-purity, and high-value-added Al products and is thus a very promising electrochemical metallurgy technology. Its emergence provides a new direction for the global electrolytic Al industry toward an environmentally friendly and sustainable industrial model. The technical and economical indices for the ILE system were superior to the traditional electrolyte system. In addition, the low operating costs of the proposed ILE system increase its potential industrial value. Furthermore, this method reduces the emission of gas pollutants (e.g., CO and CF4) and solid waste (e.g., anode slime) and could thus help enterprises meet local environmental regulations and facilitate further industrial development.

16208618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208618.value: Water is perhaps our single most vital resource. Yet, globally, we waste huge volumes through aging, inefficient delivery systems. Identifying deficiencies in pipes is difficult because they are buried beneath towns and cities (nearly 8,000 kilometers in Hong Kong and two million kilometers in the US), making them relatively inaccessible for inspection, remediation, repair, or replacement. Worldwide losses of potable water losses range from 30% – 40%, enough treated water to annually supply 160 cities the size of Hong Kong. Transient-based leakage detection methods are a very promising technique for leak identification and localization. Prior investigations of these methods based on classical waterhammer theory (like the studies of virtually all researchers in the field), suggest that small and difficult to detect leaks induce small frequency shifts in the transient probing wave, and this shift becomes smaller as frequency of the probing wave increases. Surprisingly, simple experiments conducted by the PI now demonstrate that (small) leaks induce significant shift once probing wave frequency increases and excites radial wave modes. The aim of this proposed research, then, is to understand the interaction between the leak and these three- dimensional (radial mode) probing waves in a pipe system. The results of the proposed work are expected to (i) provide insights that explain the unexpected significant shift that occurs when the Helmholtz number is of order one and (ii) lead to derivation of a leak-impedance relation valid for three-dimensional wave conditions. This objective will be accomplished using in-depth physical and mathematical analysis informed and confirmed by laboratory and field experiments. The proposed theoretical investigation comprises (i) the derivation of an analytical solution for the pressure and velocity fields with and without a leak, where an impedance relation represents pipe wall dynamics, and (ii) numerical investigations. The experimental investigation will be conducted in an existing, modern experimental pipe system at HKUST that is equipped with laboratory precision piezo-electric hydrophones capable of producing acoustic waves in the range from 5 to 50 kHz. Tests will be conducted with, and without, a leak so that frequency shifts due to the presence of leaks are evaluated. The effect of pipe wall-water interaction will be measured using high sensitivity charge accelerometers. Pressure measurements will be used to examine whether the much-used standard orifice relation represents an actual leak and, if indicated by lack of validity in the results, guide the formulation of a new, frequency-dependent leak relation.
