16208718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208718.value: An ever-increasing demand for renewable energy and electric vehicles has driven the development of state-of-the-art energy storage systems consisting of electrode materials that enable high energy densities at low cost. Although lithium ion batteries (LIBs) currently dominate the battery market because of their high energy densities, low self-discharge rates, and negligible memory effects, the surge in lithium prices due to the increasing consumption of LIBs and limited Li reserves has drastically limited the application of LIBs in large-scale energy storage. Among many alternative energy storage systems, sodium-based batteries—in particular, sodium ion batteries (NIBs), sodium sulfur batteries (NSBs), and sodium oxygen batteries (NOBs)—are potential candidates for large-scale energy storage, due to the much lower cost of sodium compared to lithium. However, making such batteries with high energy densities is a challenging task because of the lack of high capacity anode materials. In this project, we propose to develop dendrite-free Na metal anodes containing carbon nanofiber (CNF) mats filled with Na metal, so that the exceptional capacities of Na metal (1166 mAhg-1) and the capability of CNFs to suppress dendrite growth will be fully exploited. Once successfully developed, the advanced Na metal anodes will replace conventional carbon anodes not only in NIBs, but also in NSBs and NOBs, leading to new battery systems, namely, Na metal batteries (NMBs). CNFs with different types of defects (e.g., surface functional groups, lattice disorders, pores and heteroatoms) will be prepared using a one-pot electrospinning process long established in our lab. Polyacrylonitrile and polyvinyl alcohol will be selected as carbon precursors, from which N heteroatoms will be in situ doped. The content of N-heteroatoms and the crystallinity of CNFs will be tailored by tuning the carbonization temperature and duration. The CNFs thereby produced will be treated to generate oxygenated functional groups on their surface, while hierarchical porosity containing both micro- and mesopores will be created using the Fe sacrificial catalyst method. The correlation between the degree of suppression of Na dendrites and the aforementioned defects in CNFs will be investigated via the combination of experimental measurements such as in situ and ex situ electron microscopy, together with multiscale theoretical simulations. The outputs arising from this project will provide new insights into Na dendrite suppression mechanisms, and enable us to build NMBs with high energy densities and safety using the easy and cost-effective electrospinning process.

16208718.label: Realisation of objectives
16208718.value: Significant progress has been made, producing many original and interesting results that are published in high-impact journals. The major outcomes from the project are discussed in the following. (1) Developing methods to synthesize CNF matrices with different types of defects, such as surface functional groups, lattice disorders, pores and heteroatoms (Objective 1) We used several new, well-established approaches to generate defects in carbon nanofibers (CNFs). The electrospinning technique has been well established to prepare freestanding electrodes and carbon films with tailored structural and functional traits (C01, J01). The first approach was based on the use of sacrificial particles, such as Fe3C nanoparticles, in CNFs which were etched using either concentrated HNO3 or HCl to obtain highly porous PCNFs. The pore volume of PCNFs was tailored by adjusting the precursor ratio of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) to Fe(acac)3. The oxygenated functional groups were created on PCNFs through oxidation of carbon using HNO3 while PCNFs without any functional groups were prepared by replacing HNO3 with HCl (J02). The conceptually-new second approach to synthesize CNF current collectors was by incorporating uniform-sized, bimetallic ZnNi metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoparticles into the PAN polymer precursor. Instead of using chemical etching, the porous structure with large surface areas and abundant functional groups were achieved by decomposing MOF particles at elevated temperatures ranging 700-1000 ℃ for an hr in an Ar environment. By doing so, the inherent robustness and flexibility of CNF films were maintained (C02, J03). The third approach was to coat the carbon nanofiber (CNF) host with Zn or ZnO which functions to minimize local currents and offer sodium a large and favorable deposition surface. The ZnO@CNFs act not only as a high affinity current collector with a large surface area, but also as a 3D scaffold to contain the plated sodium. It is proven that ZnO has a higher affinity to sodium than copper, aluminum and other commonly used metallic materials (C03, J04) Another important approach was to design coaxially electrospun, hollow and mesoporous carbon nanofiber (HpCNF) hosts possessing strong affinity with Na. The highly sodiophilic HpCNFs with abundant defects and nitrogen functional groups enabled compact, uniform plating of Na with excellent reversibility aided by the resilient, fluorine-rich SEI layer (C04, J05). We also successfully fabricated a supersodiophilic, defect-rich and hierarchically porous skeletal carbon nanofiber (SCNF) host for SCNF@Na anodes using electrospinning of the low-cost, renewable lignin biopolymer. The defect-rich porous structure plays an important role in mediating dense Na nucleation, planar growth, and electrochemical stability according to the depth profiling experiments and density functional theory calculations. (J06) (2) Fabrication of Li/CNF and Na/CNF composite anodes by electrodeposition process for metal battery applications (Objective 2) We initially studied the energy storage performance of Li/CNF composite electrodes prepared by controlled electrodeposition of Li onto the electrospun PCNFs because the underlying energy storage mechanisms of Li metal batteries are much the same as the Na metal batteries (J01). In a typical setup, the PCNF electrode was paired with a thin Li or Na foil and a fixed amount of metal was deposited onto the PCNF electrode at a low current density of 0.1 mA cm-2. For Li/CNF, 1M lithium bis(trifluromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) dissolved in dioxolane (DOL)/ dimethoxyethane (DME) with 1 wt% of LiNO3 was used as the electrolyte. (J02) For Na/CNF setup, 1M sodium trifluromethane sulfonate (NaCF3SO3) dissolved in diethylene glycol (DEG) / dimethoxyethane (DME) served as the electrolyte. The electrodes with electrochemically deposited Na were obtained after disassembling the cells in an Ar-filled glovebox. Meanwhile, a setup to facilitate direct infiltration of molten Na into the PCNF electrode was also demonstrated. In principle, the Na metal was melted at 200°C inside an Ar-filled glovebox and Na was rapidly permeated upon the contact with PCNF with molten Na due to the enhanced sodiophilic nature of the electrodes. (J03, J04, J05) In addition to CNFs, other forms of carbon materials have been successfully applied to achieve desired effects. For example, to improve the deposition behavior of Na metal, a 3D carbon foam is developed that was sputter-coated with gold nanoparticles (Au/CF), forming a functional gradient through its thickness. The highly porous Au/CF host is proven to have gradually varying sodiophilicity, which in turn facilitated initially preferential Na deposition on the gold-rich, sodiophilic region in a “bottom-up growth” mode, leading to uniform plating over the entire Au/CF host (J07). An artificial NaF-rich protective layer was also applied in situ on Na metal. The protective layer facilitated the formation of highly stable, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) capable of preventing continuous electrolyte depletion during charge/discharge cycles (J08). (3) Establishing correlations between a variety of defects and Li/Na deposition behaviors behaviors using advanced characterization techniques. (Objective 3) By using the first approach, a 30-fold increase in surface area was achieved for the PCNF (408.4 m2g-1) using sacrificial Fe3C particles. The open pores served as active sites for controlled initial nucleation of Li. The optimization of these surface properties allowed the best performing electrode (PCNF-0.5-HNO3) to retain excellent electrochemical stability for 300 hr in a symmetric cell configuration and achieve the retention of an excellent energy density of 385 Wh kg-1 after 100 cycles in a lithium sulfur full battery. (J02). Carbonization of MOF-PAN electrospun mat generated abundant pores, nitrogen and oxygenated functional groups on the CNFs. The uniform mesoporosity enabled homogenous Na nucleation and effective utilization of the entire CNF matrix. An extremely stable Na-PCNF/Na3V2(PO4)3 full cell with Coulombic efficiencies greater than 98% for 1,000 cycles was also realized. A direct validation of the sodiophilic nature of the electrode was confirmed by a melt infiltration experiment. (J03) The introduction of oxygenated functional groups facilitated homogenous nucleation and growth of Li on the PCNF surface by greatly reducing the energy barrier required for Li nuclei formation as verified by XPS and ex-situ SEM/TEM analysis (J02). We applied the depth profiling experiments based on XPS and SIMS analysis to confirm the gradually varying sodiophilicity enabled by the gold coating, which in turn facilitated initially preferential Na deposition on the gold-rich area (J07), as well as the functional gradient of SEI through its thickness with wealthier NaF species towards the Na metal (J06, J08). (4) Verification of the proposed Na deposition mechanisms by theoretical calculations. (Objective 4) We extensively employed the density functional theory (DFT) calculations to verify the Li and Na deposition mechanisms on the proposed host (J02, J03, J05, J06, J07, J08) The DFT was used to model the initial nucleation process and verify the advantageous role of oxygenated functional groups in stable and uniform Li metal deposition (J02). The DFT calculations confirmed that the defect-engineered MOF electrode with abundant functional groups was responsible for the much-improved electrochemical performance (J03). To explore the relationship between the surface functional groups and their roles in dictating Na desorption, nucleation and growth processes, a theoretical study based on DFT calculations was successfully carried out (J05). The DFT calculations along with depth profiling XPS verified that the defect-rich porous carbon structure played an important role in mediating dense Na nucleation, planar growth, and electrochemical stability (J06). To investigate the ability of different SEI constituents to inhibit the formation of Na dendrites, the interfacial energies of NaF/Na and Na 2 O/Na were successfully estimated based on the DFT calculations (J08).

16208718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208718.value: Developing new battery structures and improving their performance in terms of energy and power densities are of great importance for maintaining a sustainable energy economy. Carbonaceous materials are widely employed to host energy source metals for stable and safe metal batteries, but relatively little effort has been devoted to tailoring the surface properties of carbon to facilitate uniform metal plating. Defect-engineered, porous carbon nanofibers (PCNFs) produced by electrospinning is a low-cost alternative to other expensive substrate materials. This project is dedicated to developing three-dimensional host structures with high wettability with plating metals so that the harmful dendrite formation can be avoided to achieve long-term cyclic performance at high energy densities. We successfully developed several different carbon structures using the electrospinning technique, including defect-engineered, porous carbon nanofibers (PCNFs), hollow and mesoporous carbon nanofiber (HpCNF), supersodiophilic, defect-rich and hierarchically porous skeletal carbon nanofibers (SCNFs) as hosts for metal plating. They all deliver exceptionally high Coulombic efficiencies (CEs) and electrochemical reversibility in long-term cycles of charging and discharging, realizing potentially useful battery anodes for real world applications like large-scale electrical grids.

16209218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209218.value: 近年来，在诸多储能电池技术中，全钒氧化还原液流电池（VRFB）得到广泛关注，成为研究热点。然而，因钒金属稀缺且价格高昂(仅钒盐的成本占整个系统的50％以上)，使全钒电池成本居高不下，成为限制其规模化应用的瓶颈。本项目旨在设计、制造、优化并示范应用一种新型氧化还原液流电池，其储能密度将高于常规液流电池两倍，而成本仅为当前VRFB的一半。这种新型液流电池将使用多硫化物和二茂铁作为氧化还原电对，与钒盐相比，该电对材料储量丰富、成本低、更易溶解，因此能够在降低成本的同时实现更高的能量密度。此外，因多硫化物和二茂铁无腐蚀性，尺寸比金属离子大，本研究将使用低成本的烃基膜或多孔隔膜代替昂贵的全氟聚合物膜，以进一步降低系统成本。同时，我们采用非水电解质，不但能够实现电池在高电压下的高效运行而无任何副反应发生，同时可取消昂贵的耐酸基础结构，节约成本。初步实验结果表明，该新型氧化还原电对具有极佳的反应动力学特性。通过本项目的研究，预期在如下方面取得突破：i）在二茂铁的环戊二烯基环上设计出装饰性官能团，以获得更高的氧化还原电位、更大的溶解度和良好的稳定性; ii）优化辅助电解质成分，以实现多硫化物和二茂铁在高电压下的溶解度最大化; iii）设计并制造出合适的碳基电极，使电子、离子和质量的耦合传输最大化。该项目所提出的新方法有望大幅提高电池功率密度和效率，减小电堆体积，降低电池成本。更重要的是，本项目的实现将为新型低成本、高能量密度和高效率液流电池的开发提供新思路，其所研发的核心技术将为解决储能问题提供有力保障，使香港乃至全世界受益。

16209218.label: Realisation of objectives
16209218.value: To achieve high electrochemical potential and high solubility of the electrolyte, we have developed an electrolyte modulation method to simultaneously suppresses polysulfide the shuttle effect and lithium dendrite formation. The sluggish S redox kinetics, especially under high S loading and lean electrolyte operation, has been ignored, which dramatically limits the cycle life and energy density of previous S-based batteries. Herein, we demonstrate that a rational combination of selenium doping, core–shell hollow host structure, and fluorinated ether electrolytes enables ultrastable Li stripping/plating and essentially no polysulfide shuttle as well as fast redox kinetics. Thus, high areal capacity (>4 mAh cm−2) with excellent cycle stability and coulombic efficiency were both demonstrated in Li metal anode and thick S cathode (4.5 mg cm−2) with a low electrolyte/sulfur ratio (10 μL mg−1). This research further demonstrates a durable Li-Se/S pouch cell with high specific capacity, validating the potential practical applications. The second effort we have made to achieve the project goal is to develop a new sulfur host to improve the lifespan of the S-based batteries. The unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Si anode and its side reactions with highly soluble polysulfides limit the lifespan of lithiated Si–S batteries. To simultaneously address the issues, we developed a lithiated Si–S full battery by developing pomegranate-structured hosts for both the anode and cathode. The pomegranate-like sulfur host with titanium nitride-carbon dual-layer hollow nanospheres (Pome-TiN@C) not only effectively suppresses the polysulfides diffusion by multiple layers of chemical and physical barriers, but also facilitates their conversion reactions. In the meantime, Si nanoparticles are encapsulated in an integrated pomegranate-like carbon framework (Pome-Si@C), which accommodates the large volume variation of Si and guides the formation of stable SEI to prevent undesired side reactions. As a result, the newly developed lithiated Si–S full battery achieves a high reversible capacity (940 mAh g−1 at 300 mA g−1), a superior rate capability (537 mAh g−1 at 2 A g−1), and long cycle life (508 mAh g−1 remains after 300 cycles at 500 mA g−1). To achieve a safe, energy-dense electrochemical storage device, we have also developed two solid-state electrolytes. The state-of-the-art solid-state electrolytes are hindered by two critical issues: the narrow electrochemical window, which prevents the pairing of a lithium metal anode with a high-voltage cathode, and the large thickness, which leads to a huge internal resistance and a significant sacrifice in energy density. To simultaneously address both issues, we developed a poly(acrylonitrile) (PAN)–LiClO4–boron nitrite nanoflake (BNNF) composite electrolyte modified with a BNNF layer (PBCEB). The PAN–LiClO4–BNNF composite can sustain an oxidation voltage of up to 4.5 V vs. Li/Li+ while the BNNF modifying layer prevents the PAN–LiClO4–BNNF from the reduction reaction with the lithium metal anode. In the meantime, thanks to the BNNFs, the PAN–LiClO4–BNNF possesses a strong tensile strength (16.0 MPa) and Young's modulus (563.7 MPa), which enables the PBCEB to be as thin as 13.5 μm (12.0 μm for the PAN–LiClO4–BNNF and 1.5 μm for the BNNF modifying layer). As a result, a Li/PBCEB/LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full battery delivers a high specific capacity of 173.6 mA h g−1 at 0.2C and achieves a remarkable capacity retention of 68.1% after 350 cycles at 1C. This work provides an effective approach to develop high-performance composite solid electrolytes for high-voltage lithium metal batteries. The other solid-state electrolyte developed in this project is a composite solid electrolyte (CSE) that inherits desirable features from both ceramic and polymer electrolytes are promising to realize all-solid-state Li metal batteries with enhanced energy density and safety. Conventional CSEs formed by mechanically mixing ceramics and polymers not only suffer from low ionic conductivity but also trigger a non-uniform ion distribution at the interface, resulting in a large internal resistance and severe dendrite growth. To address these two issues simultaneously, here, we develop a novel CSE with an asymmetric dual-layer Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 ceramic framework (dual-layer CSE). The vertically-aligned porous layer of the framework provides expressways for Li+ ion conduction, endowing the CSE with a high ionic conductivity of 0.101 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, while the thin dense layer is designed to homogenize the ion distribution at the interface facing the Li anode, allowing uniform Li electrodeposition. As a result, a dendrite-free Li metal anode with stable stripping/plating for over 500 h at 0.4 mA cm−2 is obtained, and the assembled all-solid-state Li/dual-layer CSE/LFP battery achieves a high capacity of 143.5 mA h g−1 at 1C without obvious decay even after 500 cycles. This work offers not only an innovative design but also fundamental insights into novel CSEs with high conductivity and dendrite suppression capability, which paves the way for the development of dendrite-free, long lifespan all-solid-state Li metal batteries. Finally, to demonstrate the proof-of-concept non-aqueous redox flow battery system, we have synthesized a covalently linked bipolar molecule 1-(2-(4-methoxy-2,5-dimethylphenoxy) ethyl)-1′-methyl-[4,4′-bipyridine]-1,1′-diium hexafluorophosphate (VIODAMB) and apply this new compound to a nonaqueous organic redox flow battery (NAORFB) as both the anolyte and catholyte. We demonstrated that this symmetrical electrolyte could mitigate the cross-contamination issue in the flow battery. The compound exhibits an enhanced solubility of 0.66 M in acetonitrile. The flow cell delivers a capacity retention rate of 80% and an energy efficiency of 85% over 35 cycles at a current density of 1.5 mA cm–2 in the cycling test.

16209218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209218.value: The project aimed to develop safer, more efficient, and long-lasting batteries, and several methods were explored to achieve this goal. One approach involved developing a new electrolyte modulation method to simultaneously suppress polysulfide shuttle effect and lithium dendrite formation in sulfur-based batteries. The method involved a rational combination of selenium doping, core-shell hollow host structure, and fluorinated ether electrolytes, which enabled ultrastable Li stripping/plating and fast redox kinetics. Another approach involved developing a pomegranate-structured host for both the anode and cathode in a lithiated silicon-sulfur battery, which effectively suppressed polysulfide diffusion and facilitated their conversion reactions, while also accommodating large volume variation of Si and guiding the formation of stable SEI to prevent undesired side reactions. Two solid-state electrolytes were also developed to address the issues of narrow electrochemical window and large thickness in high-voltage lithium metal batteries. One electrolyte was a poly(acrylonitrile)–LiClO4–boron nitrite nanoflake composite electrolyte modified with a BNNF layer, which enabled the composite to be thin and delivered a high specific capacity and capacity retention rate. The other electrolyte was a composite solid electrolyte with an asymmetric dual-layer Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 ceramic framework, which provided expressways for Li+ ion conduction, resulting in a dendrite-free Li metal anode with stable stripping/plating and high capacity. Finally, a non-aqueous organic redox flow battery was developed using a covalently linked bipolar molecule as both the anolyte and catholyte, which mitigated the cross-contamination issue in the flow battery and delivered high capacity retention rate and energy efficiency over multiple cycles. Overall, these methods demonstrated effective approaches to developing high-performance batteries with enhanced energy density, safety, and lifespan.

16209218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209218.value: The potential for further development in this research lies in refining and optimizing the various innovative materials and methods presented. By continuing to improve the performance and safety of these novel battery technologies, we can create energy storage devices with increased energy density, longer lifecycles, and better overall safety. The proposed course of action involves building upon the successes and findings of these studies to optimize and scale the technology for real-world applications. In particular, development should focus on electrolyte modulation methods, new sulfur host materials, solid-state electrolyte designs, and non-aqueous redox flow battery systems. In layman terms, this research report describes the development of several new battery technologies. It addresses the problems that limit the performance and safety of existing batteries. The researchers developed a method to improve the performance of sulfur-based batteries, which can store a lot of energy, but have issues with stability and lifespan. They also created two types of solid-state electrolytes, which are safer than liquid electrolytes and can enable batteries to hold more energy. One of these electrolytes is very thin, allowing for high energy density and long-lasting performance. Another electrolyte has a unique design that prevents the growth of harmful structures called dendrites, extending the battery's lifespan. Finally, the researchers developed a new type of non-aqueous redox flow battery, which has a special molecule to prevent contamination and improve efficiency. Overall, these advancements could lead to better, safer, and more efficient batteries for various applications.

16209418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209418.value: 移動數據流量的指數級增長對無線行業來說是一個重大挑戰。這驅使研究人員不斷開發先進的無線傳輸技術以提高無線網絡的容量，但目前的設計方法已經接近其理論極限。傳統的設計理念由香農在其經典論文中首先提出，他指出移動數據可被視為二進制數字序列，而無需考慮具體語義。這個洞見極大地方便了系統設計，但它無法利用如今移動數據中存在的獨特模式。隨著最近移動應用的創新，我們正目睹從傳統的“以連接為中心”的通信，例如電話呼叫和文本消息，逐漸轉向“以內容為中心”的模式，例如多媒體文件共享和視頻流。思科預測，到2021年，視頻將佔據全球78％的移動數據流量。流行的視頻文件會被不同用戶重複請求，這種需求可以通過大數據分析很好地預測。考慮到這類文件傳輸的特性，在無線網絡邊緣，包括接入點和用戶設備，部署存儲單元和緩存流行內容成為支持無線內容分發的有效技術。 緩存在因特網中已被廣泛部署用於內容分發，它可以有效地減少網絡擁塞和通信延遲。無線邊緣緩存會帶來額外的好處，包括顯著減少下載延遲和回程流量，支持個性化服務，並協助物理層傳輸。與有線網絡相比，無線緩存有其獨特之處，也會帶來額外的設計挑戰。用戶移動性是無線網絡的一個差異化因素，將顯著影響緩存性能，特別是在新興應用場景下，如自動駕駛汽車和無人機。但目前無線緩存的設計通常假設固定的用戶位置，因此具有固定的網絡拓撲結構。這使得緩存設計更容易處理，但所獲得的算法在實際系統中可能不適用。 在這個項目中，我們將研究用戶移動性對無線緩存系統的影響，以及利用用戶移動性信息制定合作策略以提高緩存效率。首先是系統性能分析，這將揭示移動性的影響，並指導系統設計。為了克服有限的緩存存儲空間和單個基站的有限覆蓋範圍，我們將提出有效的基站端的移動感知協作緩存技術。用戶設備端的緩存，同時配合設備到設備（D2D）通信的輔助，可以提供另一種有效的無線內容分發方法。因此，我們將開發有效的基於移動性的D2D緩存技術，同時考慮移動設備的實際資源限制。最後，我們會考慮基站端和設備端的聯合緩存技術以進一步提升緩存性能。

16209418.label: Realisation of objectives
16209418.value: This project investigated a critical challenge in broadband wireless networks, namely wireless content delivery. It was motivated by the exponential growth of mobile data traffic, especially the recent shift from the conventional “connection-centric” communications (e.g., phone calls and text messages) to a “content-centric” mode (e.g., multimedia file sharing and video streaming). As popular content such as video files is likely to be repeatedly requested by multiple users, while such requests can be well predicted through new developments in big data analytics, deploying storage units and caching popular content at the edge of the wireless network stands out as a promising technology for effective wireless content delivery. Compared with content caching in wireline networks, wireless caching faces a unique challenge, i.e., the mobility of end devices. This project carried out a thorough investigation of the effects of user mobility on wireless content delivery, and developed effective methods for mobility-aware caching. Our investigation went beyond content delivery, to more general mobility-aware intelligent service provision via edge computing platforms. This is motivated by the recent trend in the convergence of communication, computing, and caching (3C), to meet the requirements of diversified mobile service, with edge AI as a prominent example. Meanwhile, wireless caching-based services have emerged in new application scenarios, such as smart UAVs, Internet of Vehicles (IoV), etc. To adapt to the latest development, we have also investigated these new application scenarios, where edge information systems (EIS), consisting of edge caching, edge computing, and edge intelligence, play a critical role. Thus, in our investigation, “edge caching” becomes a broad concept, including the provisioning of storage, computing, and algorithm/software at the wireless network edge. The research objectives of this project focused on the two key aspects. Research Objective 1 investigated the effects of user mobility, while Objectives 2-4 developed mobility-aware caching techniques to improve the efficiency of content delivery. Our investigation closely followed the stated research objectives, which led to fruitful research outcomes. In particularly, research results of this project have been reported in 5 journal papers and 3 conference papers. Following is the detailed description of the realization of the objectives. • Research Objective 1, which is to analyze and characterize the effects of user mobility on cache-assisted wireless content delivery, forms the foundation of this project. We first took vehicular communications as a test example, where vehicles are regarded as mobile users. The investigation was based on Veins, an open source and event-based network simulation tool. We developed a vehicular caching framework in Veins based on the IEEE 802.11p protocol, where roadside units (RSUs) have caching capabilities. It turned out that the traffic flow is quite dynamic, and the mean arrival rate is time varying. Thus, it is inaccurate to model the arrival process as a stationary process such as the most commonly used Poisson process. These findings provided key insights for us to develop mobility-aware caching algorithms. Furthermore, we also analytically investigated the performance of content delivery with cellular-connected UAVs as mobile users. A tractable framework was developed based on a powerful analytical tool, stochastic geometry, which allows us to quantify the content delivery performance. For example, it can be used to investigate the impact of the ground base station density on wireless content delivery. • Research Objective 2 is to develop mobility-aware cooperative base station caching techniques. Our investigations focused on two typical use cases, namely, edge video analytics and cooperative edge inference. For edge video analytics, where edge servers assist the mobile users to perform video analytics tasks, edge platforms need to adaptively change the placements of video analytics applications to cope with the mobility of users or to improve resource efficiency. We investigated the live application migration problem. Based on a breakdown analysis of the memory states of video analytics applications, we proposed different techniques for different types of states, i.e., warm-up, sync, and replay, in order to minimize the negative influence of migrations on application performance. We also implemented a prototype system which achieves near-transparent live migration. For cooperative edge inference, where multiple edge servers cache service models to assist multiple mobile users for low-latency inference, we investigated a loading cost-aware joint model caching and request routing problem. We proposed a randomized rounding-based online algorithm with a proved approximation ratio to solve the problem. Extensive experimental results demonstrated that our algorithm achieves more than 42.7% throughput gain than baseline algorithms. • Research Objective 3 is on mobility-aware cooperative device caching. Due to mobility, edge servers may not be always accessible, and thus cooperation among devices becomes imperative for wireless content delivery and other mobile edge services. Our investigation focused on two application scenarios: intelligent Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) and wireless emergency networks. In IoVs, each device, i.e., an intelligent vehicle, is relatively powerful, so we proposed two different scenarios: Vehicle as a Client (VaaC) and Vehicle as a Server (VaaS). Thanks to the high mobility of vehicles, frequently changing content requirements, and harsh communication environments, the design of caching algorithms in IoV is highly challenging. Leveraging two possible roles of each vehicle, i.e., VaaC and VaaS, we proposed different mobility-aware caching methods, including temporal-locality-aware caching, and spatial-locality-aware caching. For wireless emergency networks, which are of critical importance in disaster rescue scenarios, we proposed to deploy UAVs as caching and communication nodes. We investigated cooperative caching enabled by device-to-device communications, and its applications in wireless emergency networks, including cache-assisted HD mapping, object recognition and quick rescue, public safety service and medical response, etc. • Research Objective 4 is on mobility-aware joint base station and device caching methods. During our investigation, to handle user mobility more effectively, we proposed to exploit the abundant resources at the cloud, resulting in device–edge–cloud cooperation. Most existing works regard the remote cloud server as a special edge server. Consequently, the service quality cannot be met when some of the edge servers cannot be connected. By explicitly considering the powerful cloud node, our architecture becomes more robust to user mobility. Specifically, we developed an on-line offloading decision and computational resource management algorithm to jointly consider collaborations between device–cloud, edge–edge and edge–cloud. Moreover, there is inherent dependency among different tasks in many applications, and we proposed a dependency-aware offloading scheme taking advantage of edge-cloud cooperation. Our results demonstrated the effectiveness of device-edge-cloud cooperation in edge information systems, and revealed the critical role of the remote cloud resources. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project (Research Objectives 1 to 4), we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area. As a result of this project, an MPhil student, Hongyu Yang, has been trained and graduated. Our investigation on general edge information systems has led to innovative ideas and methods that can effectively handle and exploit user mobility patterns for providing various mobile services at the wireless network edge. Moreover, our results have cast new light in designing mobility-aware techniques for mobile edge application scenarios such as Internet of vehicles and smart UAVs. We envision the outcome of this project will also be helpful to support emerging AI-enabled mobile applications.

16209418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209418.value: Major findings and research outcomes of this project are summarized as follows. For references, [C1] and [J1] represent conference paper #1 and journal paper #1 in Part C, respectively. • Mobility-aware Edge-Cloud Cooperation: Cooperation is important to effectively handle user mobility. Previous works considered edge-device cooperation, but the abundant resources in the cloud has not been fully exploited. In [J3], we developed an on-line computational resource management algorithm that jointly considers collaborations between device–cloud, edge–edge and edge–cloud to minimize the total energy consumption. In [J4], we proposed a dependency-aware offloading scheme considering edge-cloud cooperation under task dependency constraints. Moreover, in [C3], we studied the joint model caching and request routing problem for cooperative inference where edge servers are coordinated by a macro base station. • Effective Content Delivery for Mobile Users: While user mobility patterns could be exploited to develop effective caching algorithms for content placement, high mobility also causes difficulties for content delivery. In [C1, C2], we investigated effective content delivery in UAV communication networks. UAVs can either act as users to request content or as aerial base stations to cache and deliver content for other users, and thus it is of critical importance to develop effective UAV communication mechanisms. Our main results include a tractable analysis framework for cellular-connected UAVs [C1] and an effective algorithm to exploit controllable mobility of UAVs for more efficient content delivery [C2]. • Live Migration for Edge Video Analytics: Due to user mobility, edge platforms need to adaptively change the placement of edge applications, including cached content and analytic models. In [J5], we investigated the live migration problem for edge video analytics. We conducted a breakdown analysis of the memory states of video analytics applications, and proposed to treat different types of states separately to minimize the negative influence of migrations on application performance. Our implemented system achieves seamless application migration and does not trade much resources for migration performance gains. • Edge Information Systems for Intelligent Mobile Applications: We investigated the application of edge information systems (EIS) in intelligent Internet of Vehicles (IoV) [J1] and wireless emergency networks [J2]. In [J1], we introduced two different models, i.e., vehicle as a client and vehicle as a server, and proposed different mobility-aware caching methods, including temporal-locality-aware caching, and spatial-locality-aware caching. In [J2], we investigated cache-enabled applications in wireless emergency networks, including cache-assisted mapping, object recognition and quick rescue, public safety service and medical response, etc.

16209418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209418.value: With the convergence of communication, computing, and caching (3C), wireless networks become capable of providing more diversified mobile applications. This project has demonstrated the important role of user mobility in designing such systems, and there is great potential for further development. One important future direction is to consider AI-enabled applications at the wireless network edge. While there has been lots of recent interest in edge AI, the issues caused by user mobility have not received much attention yet, which are critical to provide low-latency and reliable performance. It is important to first analyze the effects of mobility on AI model training and inference. For instance, user mobility will highly affect the training performance and convergence of federated edge learning, which is privacy-preserving framework to train powerful AI models from distributed data. Moreover, user mobility will severely affect the performance of edge-assisted inference, as the connectivity to powerful edge servers will become intermittent. Furthermore, it will be interesting to apply mobility-aware design methodologies developed in this project to improve the efficacy and efficiency of edge training and inference.

16209418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209418.value: With the recent innovations in mobile applications, we are witnessing a gradual shift from the conventional “connection-centric” communications (e.g., phone calls and text messages) to a “content-centric” mode (e.g., multimedia file sharing and video streaming). Popular content such as video files is likely to be repeatedly requested by different users, and such requests can be well predicted through new techniques of big data analytics. Inspired by these features, deploying storage units and caching popular content at the edge of the wireless network, including access points and user devices, emerges as a promising technology for effective wireless content delivery. User mobility is a differentiating factor of caching in wireless networks, which brings challenges as well as opportunities. This project investigated the effect of user mobility on wireless cache systems, and developed effective cooperation strategies to improve the efficiency of cache-assisted wireless content delivery by exploiting user mobility patterns. Analytical performance evaluation was firstly carried out. To overcome the limited cache storage and limited coverage range of individual edge servers, we developed effective device-edge-cloud cooperation techniques. Moreover, we investigated cache-enabled use cases in key application scenarios, including intelligent Internet of vehicles, smart UAV systems, and wireless emergency networks.

16209918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209918.value: 全球公共醫療系統正面臨著以有限資源提供高質量醫療服務的巨大挑戰。在門診診所，患者的等待時間，即請求日期和預約日期之間的差别遠非令人滿意。這種漫長的等待時間可能產生惡性循環，因為由於等待時間長而惡化的健康狀況可能消耗更多的資源。因此，如何在缩短等待時間的同時有效地利用資源是從業者和研究人員非常關注的問題。許多國家已製定等待時間目標政策作為其醫院的營運績效指南。 這項工作的目的是改善門診診所的患者预约排程问题，以便提供及时有效的服务。我们尤其关注多个时期的动态预约排程问题当患者的到達是動態的，不確定的而且有不同优先级的要求。在每個時期的開始，根據患者的等待名單，我們將有限的資源分配給不同類型的患者，以保證每個患者在等待時間要求之前接受诊疗。作为一个多階段決策問題， 我們在保证每個患者的等待時間不能超過他/她相應的可接受等待時間的同时，最小化所有時期的預期等待成本和資源利用成本的總和，然後我們探索最優政策的結構結果。 為了克服這個動態規劃問題中的維數災難，我們將使用兩種不同的方法來近似解決。第一種方法是近似動態規劃方法，它被廣泛用於解決高維問題。第二個是決策規則方法，它將決策限制為不確定參數的特定函數，以便獲得計算易處理性。我們會通过從香港大型公立醫院收集的實際數據，進行數值試驗，以測試這兩種方法的表現。此外，由於成本參數可能無法輕易量化，我們將提出一項新的績效衡量指標，以說明資源利用所涉及的風險。 假設結果可行，此项目所開發的模型和算法可以为實踐提供明確的指導，以確定每個優先級的預訂。它還可以豐富當前動態預約排程問題的文獻。

16210418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210418.value: Gas turbines are used to generate electricity and power aircraft. They are reliable and efficient but produce harmful pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOx), endangering public health and the environment by contributing to respiratory disease and climate change. An effective way to reduce NOx emissions is to switch to lean premixed combustion, but this tends to provoke thermoacoustic oscillations in the combustor. These are pressure oscillations caused by feedback between unsteady heat release and acoustic waves. If severe, they can increase noise and pollutant emissions, accelerate thermal-mechanical fatigue, and even cause catastrophic structural failure. There is an urgent need to be able to predict thermoacoustic instability at the design stage so that it can be engineered out. However, computationally simulating the compressible turbulent reacting flows in a combustor is costly. A cheaper alternative is low-order network modelling, in which the system is approximated as a network of linear acoustic elements coupled to a nonlinear flame model. That approach predicts the deterministic features well, but its modelling of the stochastic features remains largely qualitative, with most studies relying on the use of generic white Gaussian noise. Nevertheless, stochasticity is a defining feature of real combustors. For example, their stability boundaries have been observed to shift randomly between tests and between systems of the same design operating under the same conditions. In developing the next generation of low-emissions gas turbines, it is therefore essential to have quantitative methods for predicting and controlling thermoacoustic instability in the presence of noise. We propose to develop a method for quantitatively predicting and controlling the effects of turbulence-induced noise (TIN) in thermoacoustic systems. We will replace the conventional (deterministic) flame describing function used in low-order network models with a flame random-input describing function (FRIDF) that has been shown to be able to quantitatively predict the dynamics of stochastic systems. We will calibrate the FRIDF using lab-scale experiments on an open premixed flame subjected to combinations of harmonic forcing, natural TIN, and artificial noise. We will insert the flame into a combustor to build a thermoacoustic system and measure its dynamics using microphones. We will use the resulting statistics to develop stochastic low-order network models of the system, and then analyze those models to find new ways of controlling the noise-induced dynamics. This study will improve our ability to quantitatively predict and control TIN effects in thermoacoustic systems, advancing the development of the next generation of low-emissions gas turbines. 燃氣輪機廣泛地用於發電和航空推進系統。它們雖然可靠和高效，但會產生有害污染物，如氮氧化物（NOx）。這會引起呼吸道疾病和氣候變化從而危害公眾健康和環境。減少NOx排放的有效方法是改用貧油預混燃燒，但這往往會引起燃燒室中的熱聲振盪。它是由不穩定的熱釋放和聲波之間的反饋引起的壓力振盪。如果嚴重，它們會增加噪音和污染物排放，加速熱機械疲勞，甚至導致災難性的結構故障。 因而，在燃氣輪機的設計階段，設計人員迫切地需要一種能夠預測燃燒不穩定的方法從而能將其解決。然而，模擬可壓縮湍流反應流需要耗費大量計算資源。一種更簡便的替代方案是低階網絡建模，其中系統會被近似為多個線性聲學模型與一個非線性火焰模型相耦合的網絡。該方法能夠很好地預測確定性特徵，但其對隨機性特徵的模擬很大程度上還是定性的，並且大多數研究依賴於使用高斯白噪聲。然而，隨機性是真實燃燒器的一個定義特徵。例如，觀察發現，穩定性邊界會在相同運行條件下、設計相同的多個系統和多次測試中隨機變化。因此，在開發下一代低排放燃氣輪機時，需要一個定量方法來預測和控制系統中存在噪聲時的熱聲不穩定性。 我們提出開發一種嶄新的方法, 以實行定量預測和控制經由湍流引起的噪聲(TIN)對熱聲系統的影響。我們將用火焰隨機輸入描述函數（FRIDF）代替低階網絡模型中使用的傳統（確定性）火焰描述函數。該函數（FRIDF）已被證明能夠定量地預測隨機系統的動力學特徵。首先，我們將採集受到諧波振動、自然湍流引起的噪聲和人工噪聲作用下的開放預混火焰的實驗數據，並將其用來校準FRIDF。而後，我們將火焰放入燃燒室以構建熱聲系統並使用麥克風測量其動態響應。最後，我們將使用得到的統計數據來開發系統的隨機低階網絡模型，並分析這些模型以找到控制噪聲引起的動力學特徵的新方法。這項研究將提高我們定量預測和控制熱聲系統中TIN影響的能力，推動下一代低排放燃氣輪機的發展。

16210418.label: Realisation of objectives
16210418.value: To achieve the project objectives, we conducted experiments on both laminar and turbulent thermoacoustic systems, using a flame-driven Rijke tube and a swirl-stabilized premixed methane-air burner with a variable-length combustor, respectively. We collected pressure time-series data under different noise intensities as the systems transitioned from a fixed-point state to a limit-cycle attractor. Using this data, we developed a novel stochastic framework that can accurately identify and forecast nonlinear self-excited instabilities arising from a supercritical or subcritical Hopf bifurcation. The framework is designed to use the noise-induced dynamics in the unconditionally stable regime (i.e. the fixed-point regime, prior to the bifurcation itself) to quantitatively predict dynamical properties such as the locations of the bifurcation points, the order of nonlinearity, and the limit-cycle amplitudes. Our framework operates in input-output mode for laminar systems and in output-only mode for turbulent systems. For both types of systems, the framework captures the system oscillations using a low-order oscillator model based on a van der Pol-type equation perturbed by additive white Gaussian noise. The framework then identifies the system parameters (the drift and diffusion coefficients) using the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation, and then optimizes the extracted model terms via the adjoint Fokker-Planck equation. To validate the framework, we applied it to both laminar and turbulent thermoacoustic systems and demonstrated that it can quantitatively predict the order of nonlinearity, the locations and types of the bifurcation points, and the corresponding limit-cycle features using only the noise-induced dynamics in the pre-bifurcation regime. Crucially, this represents the first experimental demonstration of system identification and early warning detection using the noise-induced dynamics in only the unconditionally stable regime, i.e. away from the regimes where limit-cycle oscillations may occur. Overall, this project has opened up new pathways for the analysis, prediction and control of nonlinear dynamical systems in noisy environments.

16210418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210418.value: We have developed a novel stochastic framework for system identification and early detection of nonlinear self-excited instabilities. Specifically, our framework can identify and detect such instabilities arising from a supercritical or subcritical Hopf bifurcation, in both laminar and turbulent systems. Compared to existing methods, our framework offers three distinct advantages. First, it does not presume a specific order of nonlinearity, enabling it to predict whether a Hopf bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. Second, our framework requires only pre-bifurcation data in the fixed-point regime, eliminating the need to bring the system to the high-amplitude limit-cycle regime where potentially destructive self-excited oscillations occur. Third, our framework does not require ad-hoc instability thresholds to be arbitrarily chosen by the user, making it highly versatile and applicable across a wide range of nonlinear dynamical systems in nature and engineering. Overall, we have developed a quantitative stochastic framework for system identification and early detection of nonlinear self-excited instabilities that uses only pre-bifurcation data, without the need for arbitrary instability thresholds. This work has led to several journal publications, conference presentations, and a US patent.

16210418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210418.value: The success of this project has opened up several directions for future research. One promising direction is to build upon the proposed framework by incorporating critical transitions involving intermittency. This is a crucial aspect that plays a significant role in various natural and technological systems, and thus warrants further investigation. Moreover, we aim to expand the scope of our research by testing the proposed framework on other nonlinear dynamical systems. For example, we plan to analyze the behavior of airfoils experiencing stall, flutter, and/or gallop. This will enable us to assess the effectiveness of our proposed framework in other real-world scenarios and potentially identify new applications. Overall, these future directions hold significant potential for advancing our understanding of complex systems and their behavior.

16210418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210418.value: Gas turbines are widely used in power generation, aviation, and other industrial applications due to their high efficiency, reliability, and versatility. Unfortunately, even when 'clean' fuels like hydrogen are used, gas turbines still emit nitrogen oxides (NOx), which are harmful to people and the environment. To reduce NOx emissions, one can modify the way gas turbines burn fuel, but this can give rise to intense pressure oscillations in the combustion chamber. These oscillations, called thermoacoustic oscillations, can make gas turbines less efficient and less reliable. In this project, we tackled this problem by using a combination of laboratory experiments and low-order stochastic modeling to predict when thermoacoustic oscillations might emerge before they even start. This early warning system gives gas turbine operators more time to stop the oscillations from happening. When combined with automated control algorithms, our method could expand the operating envelope of gas turbines. This would make these machines last longer, work better, and emit less pollutants, ultimately improving air quality and helping to fight climate change.

16210718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210718.value: Free-hand sketching is frequently adopted as an efficient means of visual communication. However, semantically recognizing roughly-sketched objects remains an algorithmic challenge. Humans abstract objects in many different ways and introduce large variations in the final depictions. A robust sketch recognition approach can make human-computer interaction more natural and thus easily find its way to rich applications in fields as various as education and design. Most existing work simply casts the recognition of sketched objects as an image classification task and applies available techniques from the natural image domain, such as utilizing local image features or deep neural networks. However, unlike natural images, sketch images are typically simple black-and-white line drawings that lack texture details, rendering the adapted techniques less robust for resolving recognition ambiguity. In this project, we will explore semantic recognition of sketched objects in a vectorized form. Free-hand sketches are often collected and stored as sequences of 2D points, which contain grouping and ordering information naturally imposed by humans and encode cues of stroke importance. In contrast, vectorized form provides a dense representation of sketches and enables more direct extraction of geometric patterns for hierarchical recognition. However, it is not a straightforward task to seamlessly incorporate and fully utilize such information cues for sketch recognition. The first task of this project will be to design a novel sketch recognition framework for a single sketched object in a vectorized form. The key idea will be to view a vectorized sketch as 1D signals and to use 1D convolution neural networks for a hierarchical recognition analysis. To fully leverage the grouping and ordering information, our recognition framework will contain one sub-network for stroke-level analysis and two sub-networks for sketch-level analysis. Incorporating more human factors, such a framework is expected to recognize sketched objects more accurately. In the second task, we intend to build upon the single-object recognition framework to develop a co-classification method that jointly recognizes all the objects in a scene sketch. Scene sketches are often composed of multiple sketched objects and inter-object relations can alleviate individual recognition uncertainty. The major challenges will consist of determining how to extract and quantify the relation priors, optimize jointly and evaluate the proposed method, given that no large-scale scene-sketch dataset is available for use. We will show that our method can enable various downstream sketch-based applications. We believe that this work will serve as an important stepping stone towards more intelligent human-computer interaction. 徒手繪製草圖經常被視為一種高效的視覺溝通方式。然而，從語義層面上識別粗略繪製的物體在算法上仍面臨挑戰。一般人會以不同的方式對所畫物體進行抽象並在最終的繪圖中引入很大的形變。魯棒的草圖識別方法能夠讓人機交互更加自然並可以被運用到諸多領域中，例如教育或設計。現有的研究工作中大多數只是先簡單地把草圖物體識別問題轉化成圖像分類問題，然後再採用自然圖像領域中現有技術，例如局部圖像特徵或深度神經網絡，進行識別。然而，相較於自然圖像，草圖圖像只是簡單的缺乏紋理細節的黑白線條描繪，這使得那些即使經過適配的自然圖像技術也無法魯棒地解決草圖的識別歧義問題。在這個項目中我們會探索以矢量化形式存在的草圖物體的語義識別方法。徒手繪製的草圖經常以二維點序列的形式被收集與存儲，這種形式很自然地包含了人為的分組和順序信息，並編碼了筆劃重要性的信號。相較於圖像形式，矢量化形式是草圖的一種稠密描述，這可以讓我們更方便直接地提取其中的幾何模式以進行階層式識別。然而，現有的草圖識別方法無法直接地無縫引入並充分利用這樣的矢量化信息。在這個項目中，我們的第一個任務是設計一種全新的，基於矢量化形式的，對於單個草圖物體的識別框架。我們的主要想法是將矢量化的草圖視作一維信號然後使用一維卷積神經網絡進行階層式識別分析。為了充分利用矢量草圖中的分組和順序信息，我們的識別框架將包含一個在筆劃層面進行分析的子網絡和兩個在草圖層面進行分析的子網絡，這樣的一個引入更多的人為因素的框架將會更準確地識別草圖物體。我們的第二個任務是基於前面的單個草圖物體識別框架提出一個共同分類方法，該方法能夠對一個草圖場景中的所有物體進行聯合識別。草圖場景經常是由若干草圖物體組成，而物體間的語義關係能夠減少單獨識別的不確定性。鑑於目前沒有大規模草圖場景數據集可以使用，我們需要解決的具有挑戰性的問題將包括如何提取和量化物體間關係的先驗知識，如何優化以及評估我們所提出的聯合識別方法。在完成方法的基本實現後，我們會將我們的方法運用到諸多的基於草圖的應用中。我們相信這個項目會對推進更智能的人機交互邁出重要一步。

16210718.label: Realisation of objectives
16210718.value: We fulfilled the first objective by designing a novel network architecture named Sketch-R2CNN that fully leverages the vector format of sketches for recognition. To fulfil the second objective, we conducted experiments on existing crowd-sourced datasets to show that our architecture can consistently improve the recognition performance of CNN-only methods. Particularly, on the million-scale testing dataset of QuickDraw, Sketch-R2CNN outperforms CNN counterparts by 19K - 31K recognition successes. We fulfilled the third objective by designing a context-based classification framework that classifies a sketched object in a scene by considering its surrounding context. Our classification framework is endowed with relations of object categories to better address ambiguity issue. As there is a lack of large-scale datasets of sketched scenes, we resorted to extract relation priors from existing image datasets that contain rich annotations of objects in real-world scenes, and showed that it is a viable solution to transfer and apply the learned relation priors across different domains (i.e., image to sketch). Specifically, to fulfil the fourth objective, we learned context knowledge from a database of scene images by summarizing the inter-object relations therein, such as co-occurrence, relative positions and sizes. Finally, we fulfilled the last objective by integrating our incremental context-based classification framework seamlessly to an interactive drawing system. We presented two context-based sketch classification algorithms that target different sketching scenarios: an incremental algorithm for recognizing a new object given the confirmed categories of existing objects as context, and a co-classification algorithm for jointly identifying the categories for all the objects in the scene at once. These contributions are elaborated in Section 6.1. In view of these results, we consider that the objectives of the project have been fulfilled.

16210718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210718.value: Sketches in existing large-scale datasets like QuickDraw collection are often stored in a vector format. However, most existing sketch recognition methods rasterize vector sketches as binary images and then adopt image classification techniques. We proposed a novel end-to-end single-branch network architecture RNN-Rasterization-CNN (Sketch-R2CNN for short) to fully leverage the vector format of sketches for recognition. We performed experiments on existing large-scale sketch recognition datasets and showed that substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art methods [Li et al. TVCG 2020] We proposed a novel context-based sketch classification framework that considers the surrounding context of a sketch to alleviate its recognition ambiguity. Such context knowledge is learned from a database of scene images by summarizing the inter-object relations therein. We showed that the context information can be used for both incremental sketch classification and sketch co-classification. We also integrated our incremental context-based classification framework to an interactive drawing system to better support human-computer interactions. A preliminary version of this work was presented at Expressive 2018 and the extended version is presented in an MPhil thesis [Zhang MPhil Thesis]. Our sketch classification work led to designing an efficient deep-learning method to automatically segment sketched objects into semantically valid parts. We train a deep neural network to transfer existing segmentations and labelings from 3D models to freehand sketches without requiring numerous well-annotated sketches as training data. The improved performance in terms of labeling accuracy and speed, enables further integration into interactive drawing systems [Li et al. CG&A 2019] We developed a 3D sketching system where existing 3D objects form the basis for conceptual re-design or further design exploration. We contributed a novel workflow that exploits the geometry of an underlying 3D model to infer 3D planes on which 2D strokes drawn on and around the 3D model should be meaningfully projected. This provides users with near mode-less fluidity of a sketching interface [Xu et al. TVCG 2019]. Finally, we presented an interactive system that allows novice users to easily add vivid virtual objects interacting with a moving subject in an input video. We designed a user interface to facilitate editing of keyframes and previewing animation results [Liu et al. UIST 2020].

16210718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210718.value: Our RNN-Rasterization-CNN design allows CNNs to leverage the per-point features in vector sketches at early stages, which is enabled by a differentiable NLR module. Our idea of in-network vector-to-pixel sketch conversion with NLR can be beneficial to other sketch-related tasks like sketch retrieval, sketch synthesis or sketch simplification. Our sketch classification method can facilitate transforming a sketch into other interesting forms, such as clip-art illustrations. More specifically, given a user-sketched scene, multiple objects can be more reliably recognized and then replaced with homogeneous clip-art pieces to synthesize artistic images. Our approach could also be extended to enable a suggestive interface, where users can specify a location in the scene with simple gestures and compatible objects will then be automatically suggested. Such suggestive interfaces would be of help to design exploration.

16210718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210718.value: Freehand sketching is an easy and quick means of communication because of its simplicity and expressiveness. While human beings have the innate ability to interpret drawing semantics, it is still a challenging task for machines. Sketch analysis has been an active research topic in the computer vision and graphics fields, spanning a wide spectrum including sketch recognition, sketch segmentation, sketch-based retrieval and modeling. Thanks to the ubiquity of input devices, sketches are often acquired digitally and stored in a vector format. By leveraging the vector format of sketches, our RNN-Rasterization-CNN architecture consistently improves the recognition performance of CNN-only methods. Most existing methods perform sketch classification by considering individually sketched objects and often fail to identify their correct categories, due to the highly abstract nature of sketches. Our context-based sketch classification framework alleviates recognition ambiquity and is useful for integration with interactive sketching interface to support better human-computer interaction.

16211118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211118.value: Consumers now have more choices than ever before, as manufacturers and service providers strive to offer greater product variety to better compete in the market place. At the same time, product life cycles are shorter, making it more difficult to predict what consumers will buy when faced with substitute products or services. A retailer can offer a narrow assortment with deep inventories or a wider assortment with shallow inventories. The former strategy may miss what consumers want, and result in unsold inventories, while the latter strategy will please consumers that arrive early but displease those that arrive late and find the inventories of popular items depleted. Retailers must decide not only the depth and breadth of their assortments, but also their pricing strategy. A range of strategies are possible, including posting manufacturer-recommended prices, optimally setting fixed prices, and adjusting prices periodically during the sales horizon. This complex problem is relevant to both large retailers such as Amazon and Alibaba, and smaller retailers around the world. A variant of this problem is relevant to airlines that must assign planes to different markets depending on seasonal demands. The goal of this project is to use discrete choice models to develop near-optimal breadth and depth inventory decisions together with dynamic pricing decisions. Our preliminary results indicate that for large-scale systems, a heuristic based on solving a deterministic non-linear program to determine retail prices and initial order quantities is near-optimal in optimizing profits over the sales horizon. This result essentially ignores the end-of-horizon, ramp-down problem of dynamic stockout substitution effects. As such, the heuristic may be ineffective for moderate-size retails for which the ramp-down problem cannot be ignored. In this project, we will consider a new linear program to decide order quantities that captures most of the stochastic dynamic stockout substitution effects for given product prices for a large class of discrete choice models. The linear program takes as input simulated or real demand and takes into account stockout based demand substitution. We will also consider a finite number of opportunities for price updates during the sales horizon. This project has the potential to be of enormous value to retail firms that need to select products, inventories and prices for products with a short life cycle. 消費者現在擁有比以往更多的選擇，因為製造商和服務提供商努力提供更多的產品種類，以便更好地在市場中競爭。同時，產品生命週期更短，使得更難以預測消費者在面對替代產品或服務時會購買什麼。 一個零售商可以提供一個狹窄的分類，包括深度庫存或更廣泛的庫存。前一種策略可能會錯過消費者想要的東西，並導致未售出的庫存，而後一種策略會讓那些提前到達的消費者滿意，但會讓那些遲到的人感到不快，並且會發現流行商品的庫存耗盡。零售商不僅要決定其分類的深度和廣度，還要決定其定價策略。可以採取一系列策略，包括發布製造商建議的價格，優化設定固定價格，以及在銷售期間定期調整價格。這個複雜的問題與亞馬遜和阿里巴巴等大型零售商以及世界各地的小型零售商都有關。這個問題的一個變體與必鬚根據季節性需求將飛機分配到不同市場的航空公司相關。 該項目的目標是使用離散選擇模型來開發近乎最佳的廣度和深度庫存決策以及動態定價決策。我們的初步結果表明，對於大規模系統，基於解決確定性非線性程序以確定零售價格和初始訂單數量的啟發式方法在優化銷售期間的利潤方面接近最優。

16211118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211118.value: A pervasive problem for retailers is to make assortment and inventory procurement decisions of substitutable products with the goal of maximizing expected profits over a pre-defined selling horizon. Multiple inventory replenishments are not allowed. This problem is challenging because of demand substitution effects that are driven initially by the assortment decision and later by stockouts. We propose intuitive and easy-to-implement heuristic based on the sample average approximation method coupled with the Markov chain approximation to discrete choice modelling. We further show that our heuristic is asymptotically optimal with regret of the order of the square root of the number of products multiplied by the number of customers. These results cover objectives 1-3. In a separate document, we examine the revenue–utility assortment optimization problem with the goal of finding an assortment that maximizes a linear combination of the expected revenue of the firm and the expected utility of the customer. This criterion captures the trade-off between the firm-centric objective of maximizing the expected revenue and the customercentric objective of maximizing the expected utility. The customers choose according to the multinomial logit model, and there is a constraint on the offered assortments characterized by a totally unimodular matrix. These results expand the scope of applications to the models developed earlier for the special case of the MNL, which is a special case of the MC-model. To make the model more operational in an environment where demand must be learned on-line, we published an additional paper that shows that by observing the personalized information of each arriving customer, the firm needs to set a price accordingly based on the covariates, such as income, education background, and past purchasing history, to extract more revenue. Finally, in a working paper we also study the sequential offerings. Our results indicate that in this case assortment optimization is a monotone submodular function, so it can be efficiently approximated within a factor of 1−1/e. Moreover, we offer a faster approximation with the same worst-case guarantee. In complex choice models such as Markov Chain, the problem is APX-hard, and there is no hope of obtaining a fully polynomial time approximation (FPTAS).

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211118.value: We looked at complex problems for which traditional models can fail by not taking into account substitution, particularly during stockouts. The most intuitive finding is that by first optimizing over assortments (whereby some products may be purposely excluded) and then using traditional stocking policies can lead to near-optimal performance (when the parameters are known) showing that the assortment step is crucial. Are additional findings have to do with the complexity of the models and the learning that has to happen when parameters are unknown.

16211218.label: Project Objectives
16211218.value: To develop mathematical models and solution methods for the optimal design of the FRS in general transit networks. System performance will be optimized by determining shoulder intervals for free ride rewards and a reward ratio in light of commuters’ responses and the need to maintain the transit operator’s revenue. Commuters’ route and departure time choices in response to the FRS will be modeled based on the trade-off between the rewards and costs incurred by time loss, queuing and crowding. To explore a hybrid scheme that combines the FRS with a normal non-rewarding uniform (time-invariant but entry/exit-dependent) fare scheme tailored to commuters with and without flexibility in their departure times. 16211218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211218.value: Peaks and valleys in demand during peak and off-peak hours, respectively, have negative effects on both transit operators and users. The capacity required to fulfill peak demand is inefficiently utilized during off-peak periods, and peak congestion decreases the stability and reliability of transit services, reducing user satisfaction. Transit demand management strategies take two main forms: increasing service supply and reducing travel demand at peak times. It is not always feasible to increase service supply because transit lines with peak overcrowding usually operate at maximum capacity. Reducing peak demand is often done through fare differentials to spread demand. Temporally differential fares are easy to implement but politically unpopular: peak surcharges penalize peak-hour commuters and off-peak fare-discounts or rewards usually come at the expense of the government or transit operator. To address these problems, this proposed project aims to develop a new Fare Reward Scheme (FRS) to manage commuters’ departure time choices in a rail transit system. Essentially, a commuter will be rewarded with a free ride during periods preceding or following a given peak period (shoulder peak periods) after taking a certain number of paid rides during the central peak period. For a given number of peak-hour commuters and an ex ante time-invariant uniform fare, the FRS will determine the free fare intervals, the reward ratio and the new fare for paid rides during the central peak period to maintain the revenue of the transit operator. The proposed FRS will be not only revenue-preserving but also Pareto-improving, because all commuters will enjoy improved services due to peak spreading without paying more on average. In the first part of the project, a theoretical FRS model will be developed to optimize transit system performance based on commuters’ departure time choice in a transit network. In the second part, a hybrid scheme combining the FRS with a normal non-rewarding uniform fare scheme will be developed to cater to commuters with and without flexibility in their departure times. In the third part, in collaboration with the Beijing Transportation Information Center, smart card data will be used to characterize commuters’ travel patterns and stated preference techniques will be adopted to investigate commuters’ responses to the proposed FRS. The proposed FRS will offer a valuable incentive-compatible solution to peak overcrowding. It will be applicable to not only urban rail but also public transport in general, with the potential to benefit commuters, transit agencies and society as a whole. 高峰期与低峰期的需求不平衡对运营商和乘客都有负面影响，带来诸多问题。为了解决公共交通早晚高峰的拥挤和等待的问题，针对高峰期的需求管理主要有二个方面：提升运营能力以及降低高峰需求。由于公共交通设施在高峰期通常以最大容量运行，提升运营能力并非可行。降低高峰需求的方法包括高峰期附加费、低峰期折扣和低峰期免费出行。这些方法在应用中存在着诸如降低公众接受度、营收损失、低峰期出行的拥挤和不便等不利影响。 针对以上问题，本项目提出了一种新的票价奖励机制——客票奖赏机制（FRS）。在奖赏机制下，乘客在完成指定数量高峰期出行后，将会获得一次在次高峰期内的免费出行。高峰期因此被划分为中心高峰期和次高峰期 ，部分乘客改变出发时间到次高峰期从而平滑高峰期出行客流及等待时间；同时，通过提高高峰中的高峰期票价，保证了运营商的利益不受损失。FRS 奖赏机制主要考虑的是最小化系统总成本，同时具有营收平衡、公平性、可行性、高效性的特点。 项目的第一部分研究了FRS的理论模型，根据通勤人群的出发时间选择来优化公共交通系统的性能。第二部分深入探讨混合奖赏机制，将FRS和均一票价机制相结合以满足不同通勤人群的需求。第三部分与北京市交通信息中心合作，使用一卡通数据分析乘客出行行为并通过问卷调查研究乘客对奖赏机制的期望与看法。本项目所提出的FRS奖赏机制促进了社会公平，促进乘客出行选择多元化，降低公共交通高峰期运营风险，提高运营效率，能为乘客，企业和整个社会带来潜在效益。

16211218.label: Realisation of objectives
16211218.value: Throughout the three and half years of the research period, we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the peak demand management through the surcharge together with the reward scheme in the original proposal were addressed and the objectives were fully achieved. Demand for public transportation is growing faster than transit capacity in metropolises. Mass transit railway (MTR) operators are thus facing the significant challenge of finding feasible solutions to peak rail overcrowding. Most strategies for managing transit queuing and crowding have focused on transit service supply and fare pricing. Strategies for expanding capacity or adjusting scheduling (e.g., reducing headway) are limited because most transit lines already operate at maximum capacity or minimum headway during peak hours. Yet, fare differential strategies are often regarded as publicly and politically unacceptable. Any peak fare surcharge imposed must be significant enough to be effective, but this may drive peak transit users not to use off-peak services but to shift to other modes such as private cars, which is counterproductive in terms of broader sustainability objectives. Meanwhile, off-peak fare discounts or rewards are likely to increase off-peak ridership but incur revenue loss. This project developed a novel new Fare Reward Scheme (FRS) that is incentive compatible and balances the competing claims of efficiency, simplicity and fairness. It is an individual-based charge and reward strategy rather than an anonymous fare-differential pricing policy of the kind described above. In essence, a commuter is rewarded with a free ride during periods preceding or following a given peak period (shoulder peak periods) after a certain number of paid rides during the period central to peak hours. The FRS can determine appropriate shoulder intervals for free rides, a new fare for paid rides during the central period and the reward ratio (the ratio of a commuter’s free rides to the total number of paid and free rides during the peak hours), with the following advantages. First, the scheme maintains the transit operator’s revenue, offering no monetary compensation or other incentives that incur costs for the government or transit authority. Second, rewarding eligible commuters with free trips in prescribed shoulder periods not only smooths out peak-hour demand but also prevents excessive ridership in off-peak hours by untargeted customers who would otherwise use other modes of travel, such as bicycles. As a result, the FRS created a revenue-preserving win-win situation for both the transit agency and commuters. Commuters enjoy a reduced travel time without paying more on average. Current smart card systems record commuters’ full travel information and can thus easily be used to implement the proposed FRS. To cater to commuters with and without flexibility in their departure times, a hybrid scheme was also proposed by combining the FRS with a normal non-rewarding uniform (time-invariant but entry/exit-dependent) fare scheme. The paid ride fare under the FRS and normal uniform fare during peak hours are determined to incentivize commuters with departure time flexibility to join the FRS. Both commuters who join the FRS and commuters who continue paying the normal uniform fare can benefit from the overall improvements to peak hour transit services. The feasibility of the FRS and hybrid scheme was demonstrated through case study in collaboration with the Beijing Transportation Information Center (BTIC). The scheme can attain multiple policy objectives relating to peak transit demand management, such as smoothing out peak hour demand, increasing peak commuters’ satisfaction and enhancing capacity utilization. It provides an informative and in-depth point of reference for researchers and practitioners in transportation analysis and modeling.

16211418.label: Project Objectives
16211418.value: Holistically modeling MPSoC power conversion, delivery, and consumption at system level: We will systematically model MPSoC power delivery networks, on-chip and off-chip voltage regulators, processing units, memories, and NoCs with different configurations. We will analyze the close interactions between power conversion, delivery, and consumption, and study their impact on the overall system energy efficiency and the performance of processing units, memories, and NoCs. A parameterized power conversion, delivery, and consumption simulation and analysis platform will be developed. The platform will holistically model multiple design dimensions, including (i) on-board, in-package, and on-chip voltage regulators, (ii) power grid structures on die, package, and PCB, (iii) DVFS, clock gating, power gating, and other low-power techniques, (iv) processing unit types, functions, power consumptions, and locations, (v) on-chip memory sizes, power consumptions, and locations, (vi) NoC topologies and protocols, and (vii) package pins and die bumps. Establishing runtime holistic power co-management protocols and corresponding scalable low-cost system architectures: We will establish light-weight runtime protocols and develop corresponding low-cost scalable system architectures to holistically co-manage power conversion, delivery, and consumption. The runtime protocols will monitor and control power conversion, delivery, and consumption through efficient hardware-software collaborations. They will dynamically match power conversion, delivery, and consumption to minimize performance impacts on processing units, memories, and NoCs. The holistic power co-management will incorporate existing low-power techniques, such as DVFS. Developing a light-weight transfer-learning based multi-device collaborative power management scheme: We will develop a low-cost transfer-learning based multiple-MPSoC-collaborated power management scheme including an offline power co-management planning algorithm and a light-weight transfer-learning based online adjustment algorithm to co-optimize power conversion, delivery and consumption with task mapping and scheduling. The first stage will optimize power conversion, delivery, and consumption plans and task mapping and schedule based on system architectures during product development periods. In the second stage, the static power co-management plan and task schedule will be adjusted at runtime. Evaluating the holistic power co-management method and scalable system architectures and runtime protocols: We will perform rigorous evaluations of the holistic power co-management method and the scalable low-cost system architectures and runtime protocols in multiple embedded application domains. We will compare the co-management method with existing methods in terms of energy efficiency, application performance, and area overheads under different MPSoC usage scenarios.

16211418.label: Realisation of objectives
16211418.value: Multiprocessor systems-on-chip (MPSoCs) have become an attractive platform for high-performance embedded systems, because integrating a system or a complex subsystem on a chip provides better performance and lower cost per function. As application complexity and versatility burgeon, MPSoC energy efficiency stands out as a challenging issue and attracts enormous attention at circuit, architecture, and system levels. Numerous low-power techniques, such as dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, clock gating, power gating, gate sizing, near-threshold voltage, and voltage/frequency islands, have been studied. Existing low-power techniques optimize the designs and activities of MPSoC processing units, memories, and network-on-chips (NoC) to consume less energy. However, the overall energy efficiency of an embedded system is determined not only by power consumption but also by power conversion, delivery, and more importantly by their close interactions with power consumption. A substantial percentage of the energy is wasted by mismatches between power conversion, delivery, and consumption. Current power conversion and delivery systems are designed to minimize energy loss under average workloads. However, modern applications have a wide range of behaviors, and average workloads only account for a small portion of the total MPSoC runtime. Furthermore, it has become increasingly difficult to determine the exact workload at design time due to the burgeoning complexity of MPSoC and broad usage scenarios of embedded systems. Co-design and dynamic co-management of power conversion, delivery, and consumption could potentially maximize energy efficiency while minimizing performance impacts and cost overheads for embedded systems. This project systematically develops a holistic power management method, scalable system architectures, and runtime protocols to co-design and co-manage power conversion, delivery, and consumption for energy-efficient embedded systems. Both industry and academic researchers showed strong interests on the research results. The objectives of the project have been completed. We systematically developed a holistic power management method, scalable system architectures, and runtime protocols to co-design and co-manage power conversion, delivery, and consumption for energy-efficient embedded systems. The holistic method can dynamically match power conversion, delivery, and consumption according to runtime system status. Multiple embedded systems collaboratively optimize power management protocols through light-weight transfer learning techniques. Our results show that the method can significantly improve energy efficiency comparing to traditional methods. One PhD student was graduated based on this project. Four referred journal and conference papers were published in the leading journals and international conferences. Project results are being integrated into one open-source research and development tool and will be publicly released online for academic and industrial projects. Additionally, parts of the project are being integrated into JADE heterogeneous multiprocessor design and simulation platform and will be publicly released online as an open-source research and development tools for academic and industrial projects.
