Multiple embedded systems collaboratively optimize power management protocols through light-weight transfer learning techniques. Our results show that the method can significantly improve energy efficiency comparing to traditional methods. One PhD student was graduated based on this project. Four referred journal and conference papers were published in the leading journals and international conferences. Project results are being integrated into one open-source research and development tool and will be publicly released online for academic and industrial projects.

16211418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211418.value: The project is interested by both industry and academic researchers. We plan to continue on this direction if possible.

16211418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211418.value: Embedded systems, such as smart phones and tablets, offer a personal, portable, and intuitive form factor to access information freely. As application complexity and versatility burgeon, multiprocessor systems-on-chip (MPSoCs) have become an attractive platform for high-performance embedded systems, because integrating a system or a complex subsystem into a single chip improves performance and energy efficiency and lowers the cost per function. As application complexity and versatility burgeon, MPSoC energy efficiency stands out as a challenging issue. Existing low-power techniques optimize the designs and activities of MPSoC processing units, memories, and network-on-chips to lower energy consumption. However, the overall energy efficiency of an embedded system is determined not only by power consumption but also by power conversion, delivery, and more importantly, by their close interactions with power consumption. A substantial percentage of energy is wasted due to mismatches among power conversion, delivery, and consumption. This project systematically develop a holistic power management method, scalable system architectures, and runtime protocols to co-design and co-manage power conversion, delivery, and consumption for energy-efficient embedded systems. Both industry and academic researchers showed strong interests on the research results.

16211618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211618.value: 利用全球定位系統（GPS）和谷歌地圖等系統來評估位置經已徹底改變了我們的生活。這些系統增強了個人的導航功能，並可根據位置信息來提供不同的服務。然而，這些方法都存在著一定的局限性，例如要定位的對象必須配備有諸如RFID標籤，GPS，WiFi或移動電話的協作設備。因此，它們並不適合用來映射或定位一些沒有合作設備的任意對像或結構。這包括檢測入侵者，定位丟失的物體或估計位於某個區域的人數。推而廣之，使用不需依賴協作設備的方法來對室內環境成像可開闢許多創新的服務和應用。此領域的先前研究包括被動相干定位和穿牆雷達。這些方法雖然取得了良好的效果，但它們一般需要有大量的測量數據集，或需要對無線通信基礎設施進行修改或需要專有的硬件來配合。 在這裡的提案中，我們希望通過研究來使諸如WiFi的現有無線通信基礎設施能直接對室內環境進行成像。我們的研究重點是針對那些可以對室內環境中的變化進行成像的成像方法，因為它們有可能使成像技術更加直接地應用並只需要使用小型測量數據集。這是因為僅需要處理RF信號的差異，並且室內環境的變化通常很小，從而允許應用稀疏圖像重建技術。僅在室內環境中的成像變化也具有許多應用，包括檢測已被移除或添加的對象，檢測入侵者，人和群眾。對於這裡提出的方案，我們將特別針對兩種用於室內環境的成像變化的新技術。第一種方法是僅基於使用信號強度測量，並利用衍射層析成像。第二種方法是充分利用接收信號的知識，並利用與被動相干定位相關的方法來進行成像。特別一提，這裡提出的兩種技術僅利用現有的無線通信基礎設施而不會對其基站進行任何修改。這項研究的長期意義在於它可以開發基於人群和人員檢測以及基本庫存控制的新穎服務和應用。

16211618.label: Realisation of objectives
16211618.value: All objectives have been met. The first part of this investigation developed methods that could be utilized to image change and we settled on a phaseless version of the Rytov approximation [J1-J2]. Phaseless data is very useful in settings such as indoor imaging because synchronization is not needed between nodes. The Rytov approximation is the only approximation that has a linear form when using phaseless data and it is therefore important for our investigation and its use has allowed us to met objective 1. However the Rytov approximation reconstruction quality is not ideal [J2] and therefore methods needed to be developed to improve reconstruction quality. We performed this by developing a new extended Rytov approximation (xRA) [J3] that used lossy forms of rays. xRA provides excellent reconstructions and is a significant breakthrough in terms of quality for a linear inverse scattering technique and is ideal for indoor imaging. Indoor imaging has a wide range of objects with relative permittivity ranging from 1-80 and large electrical sizes of up to 30 wavelengths. xRA however can handle this wide variety of environments and is therefore perfect for indoor imaging [J3]. xRA satisfies objective 2. We have also utilized RA and xRA in experimental settings to show their full potential and verify and characterize its accuracy [J2,J3,J6] and these results meet objective 3. In particular the work in [J6] provides estimates of accuracy utilizing the corresponding direct problem. Furthermore we have analyzed the performance of xRA in several further modifications. The first is to reduce the number of antennas by using frequency diversity [J4]. While these results are for the Rytov approximation it reveals the potential of the technique. Further, in publications [J5-J6] we analyze the quality of xRA by using its direct problem configuration. This shows that the xRA is extremely accurate in both forward and backward configurations. In publication [C1] we have compared our technique with a conventional RF tomography approach (RTI). Over all we believe the technique we have developed, xRA, is a breakthrough for indoor imaging as it provides a linear approach while maintaining very good accuracy [J3,J6].

16211618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211618.value: The major finding of this work was the development of a new linear image reconstruction technique referred to as the extended Rytov approximation (xRA). Its novelty is based upon incorporating a lossy ray formulation of scattering into the Rytov approximation (to include neglected terms) while maintaining a linear formulation. Furthermore, in a phaseless form it also retains its linear form. This makes the technique computationally efficient and also allows temporal subtraction to be included straightforwardly. We believe the xRA results represent a significant breakthrough in inverse scattering and indoor imaging in that it can perform reconstruction when objects having relative permittivity ranging from 1-80 and large electrical sizes of up to 30 wavelengths are considered. No other linear technique has been shown to perform this accurately or over this validity range. It far exceeds previous linear approaches. Furthermore, nonlinear approaches such as subspace and contrast source inverse approaches even struggle to obtain the same kind of image reconstruction quality for the object types considered. We have also investigated the accuracy of xRA by studying the corresponding direct problem. This reveals that xRA is indeed accurate for a wide variety of object types including inhomogeneous objects. Furthermore the phase estimation of xRA is in excellent agreement with the exact results. We have also performed experiments using straightforward and inexpensive WiFi boards to demonstrate xRA in indoor image reconstruction. These results validate the theory and simulation results to show that xRA can also be applied in practice. In particular we have shown that objects, such as books, containers filled with water and people can be accurately reconstructed even when occluded behind wall partitions, book shelves and office desks. The key publications that detail xRA are [J3] and [J6] and build on the work in the other publications.

16211618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211618.value: There is significant scope for further development of xRA and given the accuracy and validity range of the technique it is important it be developed further. There are several areas for further investigation. The most important area for improvement is to reduce the number of measurement nodes. Two methods can be investigated for performing this and they include incorporating pattern diversity and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS). Other areas for development include extensions to 3D, extensions to wide frequency bands and integration into joint communication and sensing systems. I have submitted a GRF in the latest round to investigate these extensions so the full potential of this technique can be established.

16211618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211618.value: We have developed a new indoor imaging technique based on an extended Rytov approximation. The technique represents a breakthrough in indoor imaging using radio frequencies. It can provide a straightforward, inexpensive and practical technique for imaging change in the indoor environment. It provides accurate reconstructions of the indoor environment over a wide range of materials and sizes. The technique is practical because it only relies on phaseless data that does not need to be synchronized and only requires straightforward linear processing techniques. It has significant potential for integration with joint communication and sensing systems.

16212218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212218.value: It is generally accepted that the climate is changing due to anthropogenic activity. In recent years the unequivocal warming of the earth has brought about significant changes in the climate system and this reality has forced researchers and geotechnical engineers to enhance their fundamental understanding of soil-atmosphere processes. Anticipated changes in climate conditions such as extreme rainfall and temperature will be likely to lead to changes in soil conditions which will influence geotechnical structures such as embankments, comprising fill material placed to maintain the vertical alignment of highways and railway lines, which are needed for sustainable and economic developments worldwide. Slope failure of embankments may result in loss of life, incur significant damage to infrastructure and substantial disruption of economic growth. Long-term seasonal deformations caused by climate change may lead to severe safety and maintenance problems. This will have significant economic consequences for infrastructure owners and cause disruption to the public. These long-term impacts in the wake of climate change are neither well studied nor well-understood. For example, it is not clear how pore water in the soil will change in response to likely changes in the water cycle, i.e., relative humidity (RH) and temperature. In this proposed project, a newly developed environmental chamber with the ability to control climate variables including RH, rainfall and temperature independently will be employed to simulate the effects of credible but undesirable climate conditions on unsaturated earthen embankments. Deformation and possible failure mechanisms will be investigated under cyclic wetting and drying and heating and cooling over both the short- and long-term. High quality, reliable physical test data will be obtained to reveal deformation and failure mechanisms likely under future unfavourable climate conditions. In addition, new insights into the performance of embankments will be obtained by back-analysing the tests using a new constitutive soil model which is capable of simulating the coupled cyclic thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils. We expect to establish design guidelines through numerical parametric studies to assist practicing engineers in designing safer and more economical transport embankments, taking into account future possible changing climate conditions. Moreover, infrastructure owners and governments will benefit from this research as our new insights and design guidelines will allow safer, more economical and inclusive maintenance to be carried out to mitigate ongoing deterioration, improving sustainability for future generations.

16212218.label: Realisation of objectives
16212218.value: Although all the stated objectives have been achieved, the PI has encountered difficulties in acquiring needed equipment and consumables. This was due to the social unrest in Hong Kong between 2019 and 2020 and the COVID-19 pandemic spreading from early 2020 until 2022, resulting in severe delay in procurement and delivery of equipment and goods. By implementing good time management strategy and control, the progress of the project has been greatly improved.

16212218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212218.value: Based on temperature- and suction-controlled tests in the project, it is found that the shear strength and stiffness of saturated and unsaturated soils are fundamentally governed by soil suction (or moisture content) and temperature. The properties of clayey soil such as shear strength and volume change are more vulnerable to temperature changes (please see the first three journal papers in Part C for details). These findings have assisted in the interpretation of centrifuge model tests. High-quality of centrifuge model test data were obtained (see the 2022 keynote paper and Wang’s PhD thesis for details). Key findings can be summarised as follows: • As compared with silt embankments, clay embankments settle excessively during seasonal thermal cycles because of their higher thermal volumetric strains. Also, more water evaporates from clay embankments, resulting in more shrinkage. • The service life of clay embankments can be reduced to ¼ of the design life due to thermal cycles, while the effect on silt embankment may not be as significant. The design of clay embankments should allow for temperature effects on secondary consolidation, i.e., Cα values, while typical values for silt may be acceptable. • A distinctly different differential settlement trend is identified for clay embankment, where the crest settles more during wetting-drying cycles. A silt embankment shows much less significant differential settlement. • Freeze-thaw cycles can impose severe adverse effects on embankments and slopes. Both experimental and numerical studies show that, when embankments and slopes freeze, negative pore water pressure is developed in the freezing front which draws water from the unfrozen zone. As embankment slopes thaw progressively, the drainage of excess water is suppressed by the underlying frozen layer that is yet to thaw. The rise in pore water pressure softens the surface layer of the slope, which induces the downslope movement and detachment of active layer. Numerical parametric studies reveal that the extent of pore water pressure rise and the reduction of the factor of safety become more significant with lower ground surface temperature and higher ground water table. • Poorly compacted embankment slope (85% of maximum dry density, MDD) tends to experience deeper frost penetration during freezing. As a result, the frost heave of the 85% MDD embankment is about 160% higher than that of 95% MDD ones. Embankments in the unfrozen area may have severe serviceability problems once freezing is imposed under unprecedented extreme cold events. Freeze-thaw cycles also develop cracks, which threatens the stability of slopes under rainfall events.

16212218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212218.value: To account for the effects of unexpected weather conditions such as extreme temperatures, humidity, and rainfall, the formation of significant fractures at soil surface after freeze-thaw cycles should be further explored and investigated. Fundamental understanding and quantitative measurement regarding the governing parameters of the freeze-thaw induced fractures should be improved. As cracking is one of the key factors to evaluate the serviceability of highway and railways, it is necessary to conduct more physical tests to reveal the mechanism of fracture formation in cold regions. To start with, freeze-thaw tests on soil columns can be carried out by controlling different water supply, freezing rate and void ratio. The ice segregation phenomenon in the vertical direction during freezing and the remaining fractures after thawing should be measured. One typical feature of freeze-thaw action on embankments and slopes is that the temperature gradient is unidirectional. As a result, the formation of ice lenses alters soil structure even after the soil is completely thawed. These periodic, orientated ice lenses make the soil tend to become anisotropic in terms of both stiffness and strength. Element tests (e.g., triaxial tests) should be conducted to further explore the stiffness and strength of soils in different directions.

16212218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212218.value: It is widely recognised that climate changes affect everyone on the Earth. Based on temperature- and humidity-controlled laboratory element tests, state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge model tests using the advanced environmental chamber in flight, which can simulate various events due to climate changes, and advanced numerical simulations, it is found that the service life of clay embankments can be reduced to ¼ of the design life due to thermal cycles. The future design of clay embankments for roads and high-speed railways must allow for temperature effects on secondary consolidation. The distinctly differential settlement trend identified for clay embankment, where the crest settles more during wetting-drying cycles, must be addressed. As embankments and slopes thaw, the rise in pore water pressure softens the surface layer of the soil. The extent of pore pressure rise and the reduction of the factor of safety become more significant with lower ground surface temperature and higher ground water table. Embankments in the unfrozen area may have severe serviceability problems once freezing is imposed under unprecedented extreme cold events. Freeze-thaw cycles also develop cracks, which threatens the stability of slopes under rainfall events. The adverse effects due to soil thawing and freezing must be addressed in future designs.

16212318.value: 先进微纳米制造技术的发展，使得开发具有独特性质的多功能新型材料成为可能。然而，这些多功能新型材料通常具有多层尺度结构，材料性质与其多尺度结构的复杂关系极度增加了材料设计的困难。常规的设计方法通常基于物理模型与高维计算方法，因此需要相当大的计算时间， 从而无法被应用到实际问题中，在很大程度地限制了材料结构设计的范围与性能。 结构化材料，就是一种通过它自身内部结构而非组分，来实现独特力学特性的人工制造材料。拓扑优化正是一个系统地设计这类材料的方法，在设计过程中，材料的结构连通性会不断地发生变化，最终达到最优设计。由于在每一步的循环迭代中都需要对当前结构的特性进行模拟，因此在整个优化过程中需需要大量的此类计算分析。同样的问题也存在于对分层结构异质材料的模拟与设计中，为得到宏观尺度下材料的应力应变关系，需要对材料微观结构进行大量的不同边界条件下的应力计算分析。如果使用高维计算方法（例如有限元法）来模拟计算材料的力学性质，则需要巨大的计算时间从而无法应用到现实问题中。为减小计算量，人们发展了一系列降阶模型。其中大多数的模型是基于一种投影变换的思路得来，即先找到问题中的一组低维降阶的基，再将控制方程投影到这个低维子空间上。尽管如此，对低维子空间的最优选择以及有效超降阶方法，仍然是两个尚未解决的问题，特别对于非线性问题。 这一项目中，我们将用深度学习算法来构造问题的代理模型，这些模型能对任意结构进行快速准确的线性或非线性力学特性分析。这项工作将特别关注于，建立用来预测任意微结构有效力学特性和宏观应力应变关系的代理模型。这些模型将被用于替代结构化材料设计以及分层结构模拟中的有限元计算，从而极大的加速材料设计过程。此外，这一方法在其他使用降阶模型的多种领域内也有着巨大的应用潜力。

16212318.label: Realisation of objectives
16212318.value: The two objectives proposed in the project have all been realized. In addition, additional examples on different fields have been conducted to further demonstrate the proposed approach, that is, using artificial neural networks (ANN) as the surrogate models to rapidly predict the effective properties/mechanical responses of a composite material/structure. We have successfully developed convolutional neural networks (CNN) which takes the image of an 2D structure/layout as the input and outputs its corresponding mechanical responses/properties. Specifically, we have constructed CNNs to predict the compliance tensors of 2D porous materials with elliptical holes of randomly distributed size and orientation. Compared to the results obtained from Finite element analysis (FEA), the average relative prediction error over 2000 testing data is less than 5%. Regarding the computational time, the prediction time of CNN model is on the order of milliseconds, three orders of magnitude smaller than the CPU time required in FEA. In addition to porous materials with elliptical holes, we have also successfully developed CNNs to predict the compliance of an arbitrary structure represented by connected solid elements/pixels randomly distributed within a rectangular void domain under a fixed loading condition. This further demonstrates the capability of CNNs of directly linking the structure with its mechanical properties/responses. Regarding the prediction of effective quantities such as macro-stress or macro strain of microstructures, we have successfully developed CNN-based surrogate models to predict Poisson’s ratio and effective Young’s modulus of an arbitrary transversely isotropic microstructure which serves as the unit cell of a metamterial. These surrogate models again can give accurate predictions in a much short period of time. Typically, two or three orders of magnitude reduction in computational time can be achieved. With these fast surrogate models, the design of composite materials such as metamaterials with desired effective properties can be conducted readily. We have developed an ANN-based design network consisting of a generative adversarial network (GAN) and a CNN. The GAN is used to generate microstructures, that is, design candidates, and the CNN is used to predict the effective properties of the design candidate outputted from GAN. To perform the inverse design, an optimization scheme such as a gradient-based scheme or genetic algorithm is employed. With this approach, we have successfully designed many metamaterials /architectured materials with desired (1) negative Poisson’s ratio, (2) bulk and shear modulus and (3) highest Young’s modulus. Detailed description of these methods and results can be found in the journal papers attached in this report. To further demonstrate the generality of the method, we have also constructed ANN-based surrogate models to predict the temperature field and wave properties. Specifically, we have constructed CNN to predict the temperature field of an electronic chip with distributed heat sources. This problem is an important task in the design of efficient layout to reduce hot spots and minimize temperature of the chip. We also used CNN to predict the transmission coefficient of an elastic plane wave propagating through a metamaterial and the phase shift induced by the metamaterial. These two quantities are important quantities in the design of elastic metamaterials to control wave propagation. Results show that ANNs are powerful approximation tools that work for general problems.

16212318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212318.value: Artificial neural networks are powerful approximation tools that can be well utilized to construct efficient surrogate models for a wide range of physical problems including, but not limited to, various mechanical problems. Compared to numerical analysis, the typical saving in the computational time achieved by these surrogate models is at least two or three orders of magnitude. Hence, these models would be valuable in applications where many evaluations are required such as parametric study and design. Another finding is that to train ANN well, sufficient number of training data is required. Usually, the scope of the ANN is positively correlated to the number of training data. Since the training data of physical problems is obtained either through experiments or number simulations, methods to reduce the required training data need to be developed for problems in which training data is difficult or expense to obtain. The specific research outcome of this project includes the following items: 1. CNNs for predicting effective compliance tensor of 2D porous solids with randomly distributed elliptical holes of different size and orientation. 2. CNNs for predicting the strain energy of 2D arbitrary structures with one side fixed and the other side subject to a distributed load. 3. CNNs for predicting effective mechanical properties such as Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratio, bulk and shear moduli of 2D single and two-phase composite materials.

16212318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212318.value: Given the promising results of this project, there are lots to be and can be done. For example, one could develop ANN-based surrogate models to rapidly predict the acoustic wave field scattered from or transmitted through various structures/devices. This is a crucial element in the development of various acoustic metamaterials and holograms. Unlike the applications in image and speech recognition, one issue in the application of machine learning models in solving physical problems is the lack of training data. Hence, another future development should be on the reduction of training data. In fact, this is the topic of our next GRF project which fortunately was funded (Thank you!).

16212318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212318.value: With their novel properties and unprecedent performance, manmade materials such as architectured materials or metamaterials, have attracted a great attention and have been developed and applied in various fields. The design of these materials, however, has become increasingly difficult, largely due to the complex relationships between the material’s properties and its structures at multiple length scales. Conventional design approaches based on physics-based models and high-dimension simulations are too time-consuming to be of practical use in many cases, which significantly limits the range and performance of the materials that can be designed. In this project, deep learning models have been used to construct surrogate models that allow rapid yet accurate mechanical analysis, linear or nonlinear, of a given structure. In particular, surrogate models based on convolutional neural networks have been developed for the prediction of effective mechanical properties and the macroscopic stress-strain relationship of any given microstructure. These models have been used to replace FEM calculations in the design of architected materials and metamaterials, which have drastically shortened the design cycle.

16212518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212518.value: A drinking water treatment train typically consists of coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, granular activated carbon (GAC) adsorption, and chlorine disinfection, of which the GAC adsorption step has been recommended by the U.S. EPA as one of the best available technologies for removing natural organic matter (precursor of disinfection byproducts, DBPs). In a recent study on controlling halo-DBPs in drinking water, the PI found that aromatic halo-DBPs formed from chlorination of natural organic matter could be more effectively removed by GAC adsorption than their precursor natural organic matter; thus, the PI developed a new approach to controlling halo-DBPs by reversing the GAC adsorption and chlorine disinfection steps (i.e., chlorine+GAC rather than GAC+chlorine) in the drinking water treatment train. This approach has been presented at the Gordon Research Conference and published in Environmental Science & Technology. Pharmaceuticals are major emerging micropollutants in source waters for drinking water production. As these contaminants may have potential adverse effects on human health, they have aroused great concern over recent years. Because pharmaceuticals in source waters must go through the drinking water treatment train to possibly form halopharmaceuticals, an immediate question is whether the new approach (i.e., chlorine+GAC) could provide better control of (halo)pharmaceuticals in finished drinking water than the traditional approach (i.e., GAC+chlorine). Recent research has shown that most of the pharmaceuticals in source waters are aromatic compounds with electron-rich moieties, which can react with chlorine during drinking water disinfection to generate aromatic halopharmaceuticals. According to the calculation of the PI, these halopharmaceuticals have substantially higher octanol-water partition coefficients than the corresponding pharmaceuticals, indicating that halopharmaceuticals could be removed more preferentially by GAC adsorption than corresponding pharmaceuticals. Accordingly, this proposed project will aim to investigate a new approach for better controlling (halo)pharmaceuticals in the drinking water treatment by reversing the GAC adsorption and chlorine disinfection steps. Specifically, in the proposed project, the new approach will be compared with the traditional approach in terms of controlling the overall toxicity and concentrations of (halo)pharmaceuticals under different chlorination scenarios, to determine the feasibility and effectiveness of the new approach in drinking water treatment. 飲用水處理過程通常包括凝結、絮凝、沉澱、活性炭吸附和氯消毒，其中活性炭吸附這一步已被美國環保署推薦為除去天然有機物（消毒副產物的前體）的最佳可行技術之一。在最近一項關於控制飲用水中鹵代消毒副產物的研究中，該項目負責人發現，活性炭吸附對於天然有機物氯化形成的芳香性鹵代消毒副產物的去除比對其前體天然有機物的去除更加有效；因此，該項目負責人開發了一種通過對調飲用水處理過程中的活性炭吸附和氯消毒（即“氯+活性炭”而不是“活性炭+氯”）來控制鹵代消毒副產物的新方法。該方法已在戈登研究會議上作特邀報告，並在頂級環境期刊《環境科學與技術》發表。 藥物是飲用水源水中一類主要的新興微量污染物。由於這些污染物可能對人類健康產生潛在的不利影響，近年來引起了人們的广泛關注。由於源水中的藥物在通過飲用水處理時可能形成鹵代藥物，因此一個當前極待回答的問題是新方法（“氯+活性炭”）能否比傳統方法（“活性炭+氯”）更好的控制飲用水中的鹵代藥物。最近的研究表明，源水中的大多數藥物都是富含電子的芳香族化合物，它們可在飲用水消毒過程中與氯反應生成芳香族鹵代藥物。根據該項目負責人的計算，這些鹵代藥物具有比其相應的母體藥物高得多的辛醇-水分配係數，表明活性炭對於這些鹵代藥物的吸附與去除更優先于其相應的母體藥物。因此，該擬議項目旨在通過對調活性炭吸附和氯消毒步驟，研究一種在飲用水處理中更好地控制鹵化藥物的新方法。具體而言，在擬議項目中，通過比較新方法與傳統方法在不同氯化方案下對於鹵代藥物的總體毒性和濃度的控制，以確定新方法在飲用水處理中的可行性及有效性。

16212518.label: Realisation of objectives
16212518.value: (1) To understand the role of (halo)pharmaceuticals in a pool of disinfection byproducts (DBPs) from chlorinated drinking water, the contributions of pharmaceuticals to DBP formation and developmental toxicity during chlorination of drinking water containing natural organic matter (NOM) was first investigated. A stock solution of a pharmaceutical mixture containing 10 different pharmaceuticals (i.e., ciprofloxacin, sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, acetaminophen, diclofenac, salicylic acid, propranolol, gemfibrozil, carbamazepine, and caffeine) was prepared as representative pharmaceuticals in a simulated source water. The 10 pharmaceuticals were selected based on their functional diversity and high occurrence in source waters. Simulated source waters were prepared by dissolving 2.0 mg/L Suwannee River humic acid as C and 90 mg/L sodium bicarbonate in ultrapure water, and with/without the pharmaceutical mixture (i.e., “NOM only” and “NOM + Phar”). Chlorination was carried out by dosing 5.0 mg/L NaOCl as Cl2 into the sample at pH 7.0, with contact times of 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 h. The species and concentrations of DBP precursors in the “NOM only”, “Phar only” and “NOM + Phar” samples were different, resulting in different chlorine consumption patterns during chlorination of the samples. To accurately quantify the relative contributions of pharmaceuticals and NOM to the halogenated-DBP formation, chlorine exposures in the “NOM only” and “Phar only” samples were normalized to that in the corresponding “NOM + Phar” sample by multiple additions of predetermined amounts of ascorbic acid at different contact times. Specifically, ascorbic acid was added at different time intervals during chlorination of the “Phar only” sample to mimic chlorine consumption by NOM in the “NOM only” sample. By innovatively “normalizing” chlorine exposure, we were able to differentiate and evaluate the contributions of NOM and pharmaceuticals to the formation of overall halogenated DBPs (represented by total organic halogen (TOX)). Using the experimental data and the quantum chemical calculations, a kinetic model was constructed to quantitatively predict the contributions of NOM and pharmaceuticals (at low initial concentrations) to the TOX formation during chlorination of source waters. Moreover, via an in vivo bioassay with the embryos of a high-salinity-tolerance marine polychaete, we studied the developmental toxicity of the pharmaceutical-derived DBPs and NOM-derived DBPs, and their combination effects. In summary, the contributions of emerging pharmaceuticals to DBP formation and toxicity during drinking water chlorination were systematically revealed using both experimental and modeling approaches. Considering the non-negligible role of pharmaceuticals in DBP formation, the feasibility of the new approach (i.e., sequential use of chlorination and GAC adsorption) and the traditional approach (i.e., GAC adsorption prior to chlorination) in controlling chlorinated DBPs from pharmaceuticals was investigated. A chlorine contact time of 30 min was used to simulate the situation in a drinking water treatment plant. The performance of the new and traditional approaches to control pharmaceutical-derived DBPs was investigated using the source water containing a single pharmaceutical. Two pharmaceuticals (i.e., trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole) were selected as representatives for feasibility testing. The source water was treated with chlorination only (i.e., control), the traditional approach, or the new approach. For the traditional approach, GAC was added to the source water at 66 mg/L with sufficient mixing for a 30-min adsorption (batch adsorption). The sample was then filtered using a 0.45-µm membrane. The filtered sample was chlorinated for a 30-min contact time, followed by 100% stoichiometric quenching. For the new approach, the source water was chlorinated for 30 min; After quenching, a 30-min adsorption (batch adsorption) was conducted followed by filtration. The finished water with the traditional approach or the new approach was subjected to TOX analysis. Compared with the traditional approach, the new approach was found to have higher efficiency in removing (halo)pharmaceuticals at the given chlorine to pharmaceutical ratio. Accordingly, the new approach proved to be feasible in controlling (halo)pharmaceuticals. (2) The percent removal of TOX by the new and traditional approaches in the chlorinated trimethoprim sample was examined under different chlorine to pharmaceutical ratios. The new approach generally exhibited higher TOX removal than the traditional approach, except at high chlorine to pharmaceutical ratios (e.g., chlorine to carbon mass ratio of 100:3). The decrease in the TOX removal efficiency at high chlorine to pharmaceutical ratios was mainly due to the increased transformation of aromatic products to aliphatic compounds, and the latter generally have lower affinity for GAC. To explain the trend of TOX removal by the new approach, the transformation pathway during chlorination of trimethoprim was revealed by ultra performance liquid chromatography/electrospray ionization-triple quadrupole mass spectrometry. It was found that the levels of most detected aromatic compounds either decreased or initially increased and then decreased with increasing the chlorine to trimethoprim ratio, implying that the aromatic compounds were transformed to aliphatic compounds or even volatile compounds at high chlorine to trimethoprim ratios. A similar phenomenon was also observed in the chlorinated sulfamethoxazole samples. Moreover, the effect of pH on the performance of the new and traditional approaches was evaluated. Based on the results, the optimal chlorination condition (i.e., a chlorine dose of 5 mg/L at pH 7.0) was determined for the control of aromatic (halo)pharmaceuticals using the new approach. (3) Since NOM naturally coexists with pharmaceuticals in source waters, it may affect the adsorption of pharmaceuticals and their derived DBPs. For instance, NOM itself and/or the intermediate DBPs from chlorination of NOM may compete with pharmaceutical-derived DBPs for active sites in GAC adsorption. The effectiveness of the new and traditional approaches to remove DBPs in chlorination of source water containing both NOM and pharmaceuticals was further investigated. Lab-scale microcolumn tests were conducted using an adsorption module consisting of a piston pump, Teflon tubing, and a glass microcolumn (with a length of 20 mm and an inner diameter of 3 mm). The column was prepacked with 40 mg of fresh GAC with particle sizes of 100 × 200 mesh. The flow rate of a water sample through the GAC column was set to 3 mL/min. In the microcolumn tests, all materials in contact with the water consisted of Teflon or glass. For the traditional approach, an aliquot of 180 mL of source water sample was first passed through a GAC column and the collected effluent was chlorinated for a 30-min contact time, followed by 100% stoichiometric quenching. For the new approach, a 180-mL aliquot of the source water sample was chlorinated for a 30-min contact time in the dark and quenched, and then passed through a GAC column. The finished water with the traditional approach or the new approach was subjected to TOX analysis. In addition to TOX, 20 commonly known DBPs (including 13 volatile DBPs and 7 haloacetic acids) were also determined to compare their removals by the traditional and new approaches. Furthermore, a sensitive in vivo toxicity bioassay was performed to evaluate the developmental toxicity of chlorinated water samples that were treated with the traditional and new approaches. The results proved that the new approach (i.e., sequential use of chlorination and GAC adsorption) successfully reduced DBPs in chlorination of source waters containing both NOM and pharmaceuticals and significantly lowered the developmental toxicity of the chlorinated water samples. Therefore, the efficacy of the new approach in controlling (halo)pharmaceuticals was validated in the lab-scale GAC column tests.

16212518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212518.value: (1) The formation of DBPs depended on both contact time and initial concentrations of NOM and pharmaceuticals. The contribution of pharmaceuticals to the formation of total organic halogen (TOX) was 0.5%–20.2% and 0.41%–16.5% in bromide-free and bromide-containing water samples, respectively, at initial pharmaceutical concentrations of 0.006–0.31 mg/L as C. Although the contribution of pharmaceuticals to the halogenated DBP formation was relatively small compared with NOM, they exhibited much higher mass-weighted toxicity (~40 times) in chlorination than NOM. An antagonism on the developmental toxicity was observed with simultaneous exposure of NOM-derived DBPs and pharmaceutical-derived DBPs. Two models (a kinetic model and a toxicity model) were established by integrating experimental results, literature information and quantum chemical calculations. The models allow researchers and water practitioners to estimate the DBP formation and developmental toxicity index during chlorination of pharmaceuticals and/or NOM at various environmentally relevant concentrations. (2) Compared with the traditional approach (i.e., GAC adsorption prior to chlorination), the feasibility of the new approach (i.e., chlorination prior to GAC adsorption) was validated in the control of (halo)pharmaceuticals. For the chlorinated trimethoprim sample, the new and traditional approaches removed TOX by 29–63% and 33–60%, respectively, at different chlorine to trimethoprim ratios. For the chlorinated sulfamethoxazole sample, the new and traditional approaches removed TOX by 32–59% and 0.7–42%, respectively, at different chlorine to sulfamethoxazole ratios. (3) The practical application of the new approach was further validated using lab-scale micro-column tests. For the sample containing both NOM and pharmaceuticals, the new approach showed substantially higher efficiency in removing volatile DBPs, HAAs, and TOX than the traditional approach. That is, the new approach successfully reduced halogenated DBPs formed during chlorination of source waters that contained both NOM and pharmaceuticals. In addition, the new approach successfully reduced the developmental toxicity of the chlorinated water samples, and the extent of toxicity reduction was significantly higher with the new approach than with the traditional approach. The results have been published in top environmental journals including Environmental Science & Technology, Water Research, and Chemosphere. The results have also been presented in prestigious international conferences.

16212518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212518.value: (1) To more fully represent the composition of micropollutants in real waters, other types of micropollutants (not just pharmaceuticals) could be added to the source water for further study. (2) Both GAC adsorption and chlorination can alter the structural and elemental composition of NOM, which could be linked to DBP speciation and toxicity of the finished water. PI would propose to further investigate the change in structural and elemental composition of NOM and DBPs before and after treatment with the new and traditional approaches using ultrahigh resolution mass spectrometry (e.g., Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer). (3) To further validate the performance of the new approach for effective DBP control in drinking water treatment, PI would also propose to scale up and establish a pilot-scale treatment system using the new approach at a typical drinking water treatment plant. If possible, this new approach can be extended for other applications for DBP control in wastewater or reclaimed water treatment.

16212518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212518.value: Pharmaceuticals are an important class of emerging contaminants due to their recalcitrant nature in aquatic environments. Pharmaceuticals are partially removed at wastewater treatment plants and continuously discharged to receiving water bodies, and they are frequently detected in drinking water sources at ng/L to μg/L levels. Chlorine is widely used in drinking water disinfection and can react with dissolved organic matter (e.g., natural organic matter and pharmaceuticals) and bromide in source water to produce undesired halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs), which are associated with adverse health effects. This project was the first to systematically investigate the contribution of pharmaceuticals to DBP formation and toxicity during drinking water chlorination. To effectively address the toxic DBPs (i.e., (halo)pharmaceuticals) formed from pharmaceuticals, a new approach (i.e., sequential use of chlorination and GAC adsorption) was developed by removing intermediate halogenated aromatic DBPs via GAC adsorption. Compared with the traditional approach (i.e., sequential use of GAC adsorption and chlorination), the new approach proved to be substantially more effective in removing (halo)pharmaceuticals and reducing the toxicity of the chlorine-disinfected water.

16212618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212618.value: 地质灾害流由土壤，岩石和水的复杂混合物组成。这些流体高速冲下坡，每年在世界各地的山区经常会夺去数千人的生命并摧毁他们的财产。为了防治地质灾害流，通常沿预测的流动路径安装刚性障碍物。在这些刚性屏障的前面，通常安装缓冲层，例如石笼，以保护屏障并进一步减弱地球物理流动的负荷。 目前，对这些刚性障碍产生的冲击载荷的估计在很大程度上依赖于经验主义。我们对地质灾害流冲击的了解有限，因此很难确定设计是否稳固，是否足够，或者设计是否过度设计。估算冲击载荷的任务本质上是经验性的，因为地质灾害流对刚性障碍的影响很少在现场得到，并且没有系统的大规模物理实验数据可用。缺乏基本数据阻碍了我们对影响机制的基本理解。更复杂的是，对于地质灾害流中固体与流体的不同比例，流体的流动特性可以产生巨大差异。鉴于此，对于如此大变化范围的地质灾害流组成成分，目前还没有方法来研究地质灾害流对刚性障碍的冲击行为。此外，缓冲材料是用于优化地质灾害流障碍的有前景的解决方案。然而，它们对地质灾害流，土壤和水的混合物的影响机制尚未得到阐明。显然，迫切需要进行新的基础研究，以便更好地了解有和没有缓冲材料对刚性屏障冲击问题的影响。 该拟议项目将包括三个独特的组成部分，以研究地质灾害流对刚性障碍的基本冲击机制。该项目将涉及：（i）使用世界上最大的水槽模型之一进行大规模物理实验，（ii）使用耦合有限元方法进行数值模拟，LS-DYNA，以及（iii）开发一个新的冲击框架来概括不同种类地质灾害流的冲击机理。使用现有28米长水槽的大规模物理实验将成为本研究的主要组成部分。在这些实验中，将改变流体成分，固体与流体的比例，以研究各种地质灾害流对具有和不具有缓冲材料（石笼网;蜂窝玻璃）的刚性障碍物的冲击行为。这些大规模物理实验将产生一组世界仅有的可靠数据，用于校准LS-DYNA模型以进行数值反分析，以研究在物理实验中无法测量的能量和应力变化。大规模物理实验和LS-DYNA模型的结果将用于开发一个新的框架，该框架统一和表征广泛的地球物理流动的冲击行为。该项目的成功将有助于更好地了解在地球物理流对刚性障碍物冲击下，使用缓冲材料的保护机制。由此产生的独有的大规模数据，校准的LD-DYNA模型和新的统一框架将提出科学建议，改善对各种地质灾害流的冲击载荷的预测，并促进世界各地设计稳定和可持续的阻挡物。

16212618.label: Realisation of objectives
16212618.value: Revised objectives 1, 2, and 4 have been realised by completion of the proposed field-scale flume experimental to model debris flows, with different solid fractions, and with and without hard inclusions impacting a rigid barrier. The field-scale flume at the University of Hong Kong Kadoorie Centre was used to carry out the experiments. A model rigid barrier was developed for the field-scale flume tests. In addition, a series of 20 additional laboratory-scale flume experiments were conducted to fill in the gaps in the data, and, numerical back-analysis of the field-scale tests were carried out. Eight numerical simulation runs that varied the slope were carried out. Revised objective 3 was completed with a new impact equation to predict the impact force exerted by a wide range of flow types impacting a rigid barrier. The impact equation was evaluated using the experimental data of different debris mixtures with different solid fractions, including dry sand flow, water flow, and debris flow. Revised objective 5 was completed based on recommended dynamic and static pressure coefficients for the impact equation for objective 3.

16212618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212618.value: a) A new impact equation is proposed for predicting the impact force on rigid barriers. A dynamic impact coefficient of 1.5 is recommended to provide conservative impact estimates. The recommendation from this study offers an of 40% if the impact load. This implies that there is room to reduce the foot-print of visually intrusive reinforced concrete structures on the vegetated hillsides in Hong Kong. b) Measurements from the instrumentation cells indicate that the debris flow impact in this study was an undrained process due to the high rate of loading and low permeability of the debris material. The nearly liquefied state induces less energy dissipation during impact compared with that of dry granular flows, which readily dissipate flow kinetic energy as grains shear and the granular assembly compresses. The liquefied flow may also be the reason that an equivalent fluid approach is suitable for predicting the impact load of a debris flow. By treating debris flow that can maintain high excess pore pressure as an equivalent fluid, the major remaining challenge in estimating the impact load is the effects caused by the large and hard inclusions, which generate sharp impulses during impact that must be considered separately. c) A set of unique field-scale experimental data that is crucial for the research community to calibrate numerical models and evaluate analytical models. d) A unique instrumentation cell that can be used to estimate the solid fraction of the flow.

16212618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212618.value: It was determined that boulders induce short duration transient impulse loads on rigid barriers. However, the particle size to define a boulder remains unsolved. This can be resolved without additional physical model tests that vary the particle size of the large and hard inclusions based on a normalised length scale. The results in this study are for a fully closed rigid barrier without overflow or barrier deformation. Although a main objective of the original proposal was to look at cushioning materials, the objectives were revised because the budget was reduced. Therefore, a study on deformable rigid barriers to mimic cushioning materials was carried out. For open structures, such as baffles and slit dams, debris may discharge through and around these structures. For flexible barriers, the deformation of the barrier may lead to a different debris reflection compared with rigid barriers and alter the boulder-flow-barrier interaction process. Additional experiments that model different types of engineering countermeasures in terms of different stiffness and perviousness can be conducted. We have already started to look at the behavior of impact dynamics on different structure types (i.e., slit structures and deformable walls).

16212618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212618.value: Debris flows, which travel at high speeds and are often enriched with large boulders, may impact and destroy downstream facilities such as buildings and bridges. To protect human lives and infrastructure in mountainous regions from debris flow, engineering countermeasures such as barriers and dams are typically installed along the predicted flow paths. The design of safe countermeasures relies on robust predictions of the impact force. However, the impact force is difficult to estimate owing to the limited field evidence associated with the prevailing impact mechanisms, diversity of flow types that may exist (e.g., stony and muddy debris flows), and scale-dependent nature of debris flows. Consequently, the recommendations provided by design guidelines in different countries may differ. In this project, we reveal the impact behaviour between debris flows and rigid barriers using unique field-scale experiments. We evaluate the findings against existing design practices, including the commonly used impact models and assumed impact scenarios. We provide state-of-the-art research findings that enable the optimization of the design of engineering countermeasures against debris flow impact.

16212818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212818.value: The global climate is changing, and this change is irreversible. Climate change means that more extreme climate conditions will be anticipated, such as temperature rise, more frequent and intense rainfall and typhoons. For instance, in 2017, Hong Kong Observatory has issued typhoon signals number eight (i.e., storm force wind with sustained speed of 63 – 117 km/h) for five times – the highest annual frequency in the Hong Kong history. Apparently, the increased frequency and intense typhoons have led to an increased number of fallen trees over the last decade, bringing huge socio-economic and life losses. Vegetation thrown by wind occurs in many tropical and subtropical regions that are frequently hit by tropical cyclones such as southern China including Hong Kong and Macau, Singapore, Philippines and parts of the U.S.A. Existing urban forestry management strategies use the developed knowledge of forest arboriculture, ecology and pathology to protect vegetation against strong wind. These address mainly above-ground vegetation problems such as cracks on branches/trunks and loss of wood strength due to brown stump rot disease. However, below-ground problems, such as wind-induced plant uprooting, especially under the negative impact of climate change, have not received adequate attention. Accurate prediction of uprooting resistance of plant under wind loading condition requires input from researchers and geotechnical engineers to derive new and improved knowledge of cyclic plant root-soil mechanical interaction. In the project proposed, new understanding of the cyclic mechanical interaction between plant roots and soil will be provided. This project is, for the first time, to systematically investigate the fundamental cyclic behavior of individual plant roots and their cyclic interaction with soil. Effects of soil drying due to plant transpiration on cyclic hydro-mechanical behavior of unsaturated rooted soil will be explored. High-quality and original experimental data will be obtained to develop new predictive models of cyclic soil-root interaction. The new model will be able to quantify changes in mechanical root reinforcement to soil due to cyclically-induced change of root strength. The model will hence provide practicing engineers new abilities and a more scientific approach to determine the anchorage resistance of the complex below-ground plant root “foundation” through rigorous engineering principle. The new knowledge developed from this project will help decision-makers and governments to devise improved urban forestry management strategies, enhancing the sustainability and resilience of ecosystems and landscaping in urban areas – one of the key initiatives of the Paris Agreement. 全球氣候正在經歷不可逆轉的變化。氣候變化意味着極端天氣情況更頻繁出現，包括氣溫上升，降雨量增加，颱風變得強烈及頻密，以及海平面上升。2017年，香港天文台發出5次8號颱風預警，這是香港史上發布8號颱風信號最多的一年。在過去的十年間，颱風頻率和強度增加，導致樹木倒塌數目上升，當樹木壓毀電纜，會導致電力損失，另外亦會阻塞交通，甚至造成嚴重人命傷亡，社會承受巨大經濟損失。在許多經常遭受熱帶氣旋襲擊的熱帶和亞熱帶地區，例如香港、澳門、新加坡和美國部分地區，颱風吹至樹木連根拔起也時有發生。現行的城市林業管理策略，主要通過樹藝、生態學、景觀設計、病理學和土壤學，解決地面上的植被問題，例如樹枝和樹幹上的裂縫以及褐根病而導致木材強度衰減。然而，由於風荷載而引致的地底問題並未得到足夠的重視，例如植物根系在土壤中的抗錨力。為了能更精確預測在風荷載影響下植物根系的抗風能力，我們需要研究更先進的根部循環力學特性，以及加深對土根系循環力學相互作用機理的認識。 此項目提出有關循環荷載下紮根土力學的新知識，有系統地研究植物根系的基礎循環受力表現，以及根部受循環力下與土的相互作用。此項目同時亦研究由植物蒸騰作用導致土壤乾涸，以及此情況對非飽和紮根土的循環水力學特性的影響。高質量的原始實驗數據將用作開發新模型，預測循環受力下的根土力學相互作用。此模型可以定量分析由循環受力引起的根系強度變化，並通過嚴格的工程原理，為工程師提供新的工具，以更科學的方法來計算複雜的植物根系的抗錨力。開發此項目所得的研究成果，有助決策者和當局制定出更先進的城市林業管理策略，增強生態系統的可持續性和恢復能力，改善城市地區的景觀。

16212818.label: Realisation of objectives
16212818.value: Objective 1: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings were disseminated in a top-tier, high-impact-factor journal (IF = 10.75), Science of the Total Environment (see publication J4 in Part C). We first investigated the variability in biomechanical properties of Chrysopogon zizanioides L, by testing the effects of growth condition, water content, and loading speed on the biomechanical properties of vetiver roots (n = 344). The variability of the tensile strength of the fine roots of vetiver was more significant than that of the coarse roots. Root water content primarily introduced variability to the tensile strength of the fine roots, whereas growth conditions and the rate of tensile loading played a smaller role. We identified variability of other root biomechanical traits, including Young’s modulus and breakage strain, because of root water content. Dried roots had higher tensile strength and higher Young’s modulus but smaller breakage strain than hydrated fine roots. Strength and modulus had a negative power law relationship with root diameter (R2 = 0.54 and 0.69, respectively), whereas strain was positively and linearly related with diameter but with a relatively low R2 of 0.21. After characterising the variabilities of root biomechanical properties, a series of cyclic tests were conducted on the vetiver roots. The first loading path to examine was to apply pre-cyclic loading of 50 cycles at different intermediate strains, followed by monotonic axial tensile loading to breakage. We observed significant reduction of the tensile properties including the breakage strength, tensile modulus after the pre-cyclic loading and breakage strain (p-value < 0.05). The strain where the pre-cycle loading was applied also affected these three tensile properties significantly (p-value < 0.05). The reductions of the tensile properties can be explained by root diameter and root density (R2 = 0.45 and 0.56, respectively). The second loading path was to apply cyclic loading of 50 cycles at five different strains continually on the same root samples without breaking them. We discovered for the first time the drops of peak tensile stress, tensile modulus (both loading and unloading) and the area of hysteresis loop with cycle number. The drops were always more evident during the first 10 cycles. Interestingly, the change of these parameters between the 50th and 1st loading cycle has weak to no correlation with any root trait chosen for investigation including diameter, specific root length and moisture content (p-value > 0.05). However, the changes in loading tensile modulus has significant correlation with the changes in unloading tensile modulus and the changes in peak tensile stress (p-value < 0.05). A strong positive linear correlation can be found (R2 > 0.89). Objective 2: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings were disseminated in two top-tier journals in geotechnical engineering, Canadian Geotechnical Journal (refer to the publication J3 in Part C). A series of undrained triaxial tests has been carried out to investigate the monotonic and cyclic behaviour of rooted soil. Vetiver roots were used in this experiment. The root diameter ranged between 0.3 and 2 mm, while the root volume ratios tested were 0.23%, 0.45% and 0.67%. The key conclusions are: a) The root reinforcement effect is anisotropic because the root-induced change in soil friction angle is found to be path-dependent. While the friction angle change is minimal upon compression, the friction angle upon extension increased significantly by about 10o (from 41.9o (bare specimen) to 51.5o (rooted specimen) at low confining pressure of <100 kPa. b) Along the extension path, the presence of the roots changed the stress-strain behaviour from strain-softening (in the case of bare soil) to hardening. Compared to the compression path, the rooted specimens displayed more significant dilative behaviour upon extension due to the greater mobilisation of root reinforcement. c) Roots can effectively increase the liquefaction resistance, primarily because of the mobilisation of root tensile properties during the extension part of cyclic loading. The presence of roots changed the failure mechanism from limited flow (in the case of bare soil) to cyclic mobility. d) Although pore-water pressure ratio can be used to indicate the occurrence of the liquefaction of bare soil (when reaching 1.0), it does not apply to root-reinforced soil. When the roots were present, the double-amplitude axial strain continued to increase, even the pore-water pressure ratio has reached 1.0. e) The improvement of liquefaction resistance increased with an increase in RVR, and this improvement is a function of CSR; that is, the higher the CSR, the greater the root reinforcement effects would be. The liquefaction resistance (measured by the number of loading cycles required to reach failure) has an approximately linear relationship with RVR at low CSR, but the relationship became exponential when CSR exceeded 0.2. Objective 3: This objective has been achieved 100%. The findings were disseminated in two top-tier journals in geotechnical engineering, J. Geotech & Geoenviron. Eng. and Geotechnique (refer to the publication J1, J5, J7 in Part C). The model development was approached by two steps. The first step was to capture the effects of principal stress direction owing to the anisotropy in soil structure and root system. We present a new generalised 3-D anisotropic failure criterion for rooted soils on the basis of the cross-anisotropic SPM failure criterion. The theory of this criterion employed the projection of the microstructure fabric tensors of soil and root network on stress tensors to address the anisotropic effects of root network and soil fabric on the shear strength parameters of rooted soils upon various effective stress paths. The predictions made by the calibrated failure criterion showed that cohesion and friction angle are highly anisotropic and the degree of anisotropy depends on stress paths and the relative orientation of principal stresses and root distribution. The maximum shear strength of rooted soil occurs when roots are orientated along the soil tensile strain, which implies that the major principal stress is perpendicular to the predominated root orientations. The model explained that following the direct shear path, the effects of soil anisotropy are not evident, and the variation in friction angle is almost negligible, which explains why most of the existing data of direct shear tests showed remarkable changes in cohesion (root cohesion). On the basis of the first model, we developed the second model to take into account the effects of plant roots on the improvement of the soil resistance against liquefaction upon cyclic loading. The effect of roots and their orientations on any changes in soil anisotropy and the mechanisms of dissipated energy involved at liquefaction state were considered. We applied the energy-based method to evaluate the liquefaction behavior of rooted soils of varying root volume ratios. Results of 12 undrained cyclic triaxial tests on rooted soils obtained from objective 1 were reinterpreted under this energy framework. The assessment showed that the normalised cumulative dissipated energy (∑ΔW/σc) of rooted soil at liquefaction state may be related with the cyclic resistance ratio at the cycle number of 15 (CRR15). It was discovered that roots that were predominantly orientated in the direction perpendicular to the major principal stress of extension path reduced soil anisotropy. Besides, the ∑ΔW/σc’ was linearly correlated with the normalized cumulative strain energy (∑4W/σc’) with a gradient of approximately 2, which implies that any recycling and recovering of strain energy was minimal in rooted soils.

16212818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212818.value: Objective (1): we discovered that although the strength and modulus followed a negative power law relationship with root diameter, the strain–diameter relationship was linear. We observed significant reduction of the root tensile properties after subjecting to pre-cycle loading. The strain where the pre-cycle loading was applied also affected these three tensile properties significantly. We discovered the drops of peak tensile stress, tensile modulus and the area of hysteresis loop with cycle number. The changes in loading tensile modulus has significant correlation with the changes in unloading tensile modulus and the changes in peak tensile stress (p-value < 0.05). A strong positive linear correlation was found. (Reference: Journal paper 4; some of the data will be further published in the next one or two years). Objective (2): we discovered that the root reinforcement effect was anisotropic and path-dependent. Along the extension path when the major principal stress was perpendicular to the predominant root orientation, the root-induced increase in soil friction angle was approximately 10 degree. This increase was much greater than the case along the compression path where the change was minimal. The presence of roots prevented the limited flow failure (which occurred in the unreinforced sand), and the failure mode of root-reinforced soil switched to cyclic mobility. The liquefaction resistance was improved with an increase in root volume, and this improvement was more remarkable at higher cyclic stress ratios. (Reference: Journal papers 1, 2 and 3). Objective (3): we developed two models. The first one is a generalised 3-D anisotropic failure criterion for rooted soils. The model explained that following the direct shear path, the effects of soil anisotropy are not evident, and the variation in friction angle is almost negligible, which explains why most of the existing data of direct shear tests showed remarkable changes in cohesion. The second model considers the root effects on the soil resistance upon cyclic loading. The normalised cumulative dissipated energy (∑ΔW/σc’) of rooted soil at liquefaction state may be related with the cyclic resistance ratio at the cycle number of 15. Roots that were predominantly orientated in the direction perpendicular to the major principal stress of extension path reduced soil anisotropy. Besides, the ∑ΔW/σc’ was linearly correlated with the normalized cumulative strain energy (∑4W/σc’) with a gradient of approximately 2, which implies that any recycling and recovering of strain energy was minimal in rooted soils. (Reference: Journal papers 5 and 7).

16212818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212818.value: Cyclic behaviour of rooted soils is complicated. This project pioneers the testing and modelling of the strength anisotropy of rooted soils through both monotonic and cyclic test conditions. Further work is needed to explore the effects of roots on the stiffness anisotropy from very-small-strain to large-strain ranges, which are crucially important to the analysis and design of earthquake-related engineering problems such as the seismic stability of rooted soil slopes. Moreover, to more realistically simulate the loading conditions of earthquake to the rooted soils, future experiments will focus on the use of large-size simple-shear apparatus to further explore the cyclic behaviour of rooted soils and to further validate the two theoretical models developed from this project. Two PhD students trained in this project plan to work on these problems as postdoctoral fellows.

16212818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212818.value: Tropical cyclones in subtropical to tropical regions of the globe have become more extreme and intense in recent years. Vegetation in urban cities has increasing risks of collapse and uprooting under strong wind. Up to now, it is still a great challenge for engineers and landscape architect to assess and predict the performance of the vegetation uprooting resistance, because of generally lack of knowledge and reliable test data. There is an urgent need to improve our fundamental understanding of complex soil-root mechanical interaction. In this project, a series of advanced laboratory testing has been carried out to systematically quantify and investigate the cyclic biomechanical properties of plant roots and the cyclic behaviour of rooted soils. The new test data has been used to derive new theoretical models that can explain and predict the cyclic soil-root mechanical interaction. The new experimental observation and models obtained from this project will provide new scientific tools for engineers to carry out more quantitative analysis of the anchorage resistances of a complex plant root “foundation” below-ground under cyclic loading, potentially assisting decision-makers to devise improved urban forestry management strategy.

16212918.label: Project Objectives
16212918.value: Identify and overcome the conceptual and computational challenges of the original Bayesian formulation and develop an advanced novel methodology to yield reliable and robust results. The Bayesian framework offers a rigorous mathematical formulation for treating the uncertainties due to measurement noise and modeling error, as well as incomplete data. However, in its current formulation, the methodology presents significant limitations and shortcomings. These shortcomings, which have hindered the Bayesian framework from becoming the mainstream, will be explored in detail. Develop a holistic hierarchical Bayesian approach for model updating as well as robust prediction of the system output, performance, and reliability using input-output/output-only/modal data in the time/frequency domain. We aim to introduce new hierarchical probabilistic models to enhance modeling assumptions and to describe the inherent variability of model/modal parameters when considering different datasets. This variability may be due to unmodeled nonlinearities, environmental/temperature effects, etc. We will also use hierarchical probabilistic models to consider the nonstationarity of the prediction error covariance matrix. Develop efficient computational algorithms to implement the new Bayesian methodologies for model updating and robust response and reliability prediction to overcome the computational challenges encountered when dealing with high dimensional problems. Conduct a series of experiments in the structural engineering laboratory of HKUST using a shaking table and perform field measurements of ambient and free vibration of a campus pedestrian bridge to investigate the efficiency and reliability of the proposed methodology for model updating and robust predictions.

16212918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212918.value: This project aims to develop a reliable probabilistic methodology for structural monitoring and various related applications in civil structures, such as model updating, health monitoring, robust reliability and response prediction, and structural control. This methodology has its roots in a general Bayesian framework that the PI, the Co-I, and their co-workers have been developing and refining over the past 20 years. The framework forms the foundation of most Bayesian-based algorithms developed to date. Undoubtedly, the Bayesian framework offers an indispensable and powerful mathematical tool for treating and propagating uncertainties. However, it will only earn credibility and acceptance by the engineering community if it can demonstrate the ability to produce realistic and meaningful uncertainties. The current formulation has consistently underestimated the uncertainties. In this project, we aim to address and resolve some of the major shortcomings encountered by the current formulation and unleash the full power of Bayesian methodologies. We plan to develop a holistic hierarchical Bayesian approach for model updating as well as robust prediction of the system response and reliability. New hierarchical probabilistic models will be introduced to enhance modeling assumptions and to describe the inherent variability of model/modal parameters when considering different datasets. We will also use hierarchical probabilistic models to consider the non-stationarity of the prediction error covariance matrix. Moreover, a training scheme will be established to calibrate the posterior distributions of model parameters at the undamaged state of structures using long-term monitoring data and to develop a spatially-sparse damage detection method to identify localized damage reliably and to eliminate false damage alarms produced by current state-of-the-art techniques. Different model reduction techniques, high-performance computing methods, Markov-chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and surrogate models will be combined and used to lighten the computational burden of high dimensional data and to reduce the model complexity. The methodologies and algorithms developed under this project will be extensively tested numerically using a number of different damage scenarios under measurement and modeling errors assuming known and unknown dynamic loadings. They will also undergo extensive experimental verification using a series of laboratory tests and field measurements to assess their accuracy and robustness. 這個研究項目的目的是開發一個可靠的概率方法論以用於結構監察及一系列與土木結構有關的應用，例如模型更新、健康監察、穩健的可靠度及反應預測以及結構控制。這方法論源於貝氏推論的架構，而負責此項目的研究人員已從事相關理論的研究多達二十年。這個架構亦被應用於現今大部分以貝氏理論為基礎的演算法中。 無可置疑，當要處理及傳播不確定性時，貝氏理論架構是一個強大而不可少的數學工具。不過要得到工程界的信任和認同，我們須演示出其能力，尤其是其能計算出真確而有意思的不確定性。然而原有的立式會低估了所要計算的不確定性。 因此此研究項目是要解決現有立式上的一些主要缺點，從而令貝氏方法發揮其功用。我們計劃開發一套全面的階層式貝氏方法以應用於模型更新以及系統反應和可靠性的預測。這個新開發的階層式概率方法能加強建模假設以及能考慮模型或模態參數固有的可變性。我們亦會使用此方法去計算非平穩的預測誤差協方差。 此外，我們會建立一套訓練方案以利用長期監察未受損結構得到的數據校準模型參數的後驗分佈，繼而開發一個空間上稀疏的損壞檢測方法以可靠地辨認局部的損毀，以及減低現有技術誤報損毀的機會。 為了減低高維數據以及複雜結構模型所造成的計算負擔，此研究項目會整合利用不同的模型降階法、高性能計算法、馬可夫鏈蒙地卡羅法(MCMC)和代理模型。 最後研究項目中開發的方法論及演算法會通過大量測試。我們會利用電腦模擬建築物不同的受損情況，在受到建模及測量誤差，以及已知和未知的動負載情況下進行電腦模擬驗證。我們亦會進行一系列的實驗測驗以真實數據去進行實驗驗證。

16212918.label: Realisation of objectives
16212918.value: Regarding the first objective, we have developed a new Bayesian methodology based on Gaussian process discrepancy models (Journal Papers #8 and #9; Conference Paper #7). These papers discuss the choice of prediction error models thoroughly, and new methods are introduced to consider non-stationarity effects and spatial-temporal correlations of prediction errors. The uncertainty associated with the prediction error parameters is quantified considering a hyper distribution with some free parameters. These parameters capture the non-stationary effects associated with the prediction error parameters. The proposed methods were tested using both numerical and experimental examples. With regard to the first and second objectives, a hierarchical Bayesian modelling framework is successfully developed for uncertainty quantification and propagation in structural dynamics inverse problems. This framework has appeared in Journal Paper #2 for the time-domain problems, where input-output data is available. In Journal Paper #1 and Conference Paper #1, we further developed it to address the frequency-domain problems, particularly for output-only modal identification. Concerning the second and third objectives, a great deal of research effort has been devoted to formalizing the mathematical formulation of the hierarchical Bayesian framework and developing efficient computational algorithms. A few algorithms using asymptotic approximations and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling methods have been developed to reduce the computational cost. In Journal Paper #5, further developments to the hierarchical framework have been proposed to address structural model updating based on modal statistical information. Journal Paper #10 showcases a simplified version of this framework applied to the FINO3 offshore platform, validating and verifying it with real data. The variability of structural and dynamical parameters is quantified through the hierarchical approach, and additional robustness in quantifying uncertainty bounds is offered. Unlike the hierarchical framework, which treats the model inference problem in an offline manner, our recent research activities have focused on developing real-time Bayesian methods. Therefore, in line with the first objective, new Bayesian methods are developed for real-time system identification and damage detection using output-only vibration measurements. A novel sequential probabilistic method is proposed in Conference Paper #2, which resolves existing deficiencies of filtering techniques when dealing with acceleration response measurements. Along this direction, a Bayesian Expectation-Maximization approach is proposed for real-time identification of state, input, and parameters in linear dynamical systems (Journal Papers #6 and #7; Conference Papers #4, #5, and #6). It is shown that the introduced method offers robust estimations along with reasonable uncertainty bounds. The proposed real-time methods have been applied to evaluate the accumulation of fatigue damage in wind turbines (Journal Paper #4; Conference Paper #3). For the fourth objective, a series of shaking table tests and ambient vibration measurements have been performed to demonstrate the efficacy and efficiency of the framework using realistic examples (Journal Paper #2). It is demonstrated that the hierarchical Bayesian framework provides a reliable approach to account for the variability of the inference results observed when using different data sets. It also yields analytical insights into how the variability due to modelling errors can be separated from the identification uncertainty. We also demonstrated that the uncertainty obtained using the hierarchical Bayesian framework is robust with respect to the modelling errors when compared with the existing methods. Propagating this more realistic assessment of the response prediction uncertainty results in more reliable uncertainty bounds for observed and unobserved response quantities of interest. In journal paper #2, we demonstrated how variability can be captured by breaking a long-time history vibration response into multiple segments. In addition to developing the hierarchical framework, we have developed a new Bayesian mode shape assembling formulation and have obtained analytical insights into the propagating properties of constructing global mode shapes from non-synchronous measurements. This method is tested and verified using numerical and experimental examples, including the ambient vibration data of the Metsovo Bridge located in Greece. This study is published in journal paper #3.

16212918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212918.value: A great deal of research efforts has been devoted to developing new Bayesian methods for structural dynamics inverse problems (Journal Papers #1, #2, and #5). Numerous formulations and computational algorithms are proposed to elevate existing methods to a new level of accuracy and robustness, offering reliable estimations and more realistic uncertainty bounds (Journal Papers #5 and #10). A series of laboratory and in-situ tests have been performed to provide measured data for the validation and verification process of the proposed methods (Journal Papers #1 and #5). Measured responses from the Metsovo bridge and FINO3 offshore platform have been used to strengthen the findings of this research and better understand how these methods compare with the existing ones (Journal Papers #3 and #10). It is shown that the variability of structural parameters across different data sets predominantly exceeds the identification uncertainty calculated from the classical Bayesian approach (Journal Paper #2). From this viewpoint, new approximations and more efficient formulations have been proposed to simplify the application of these methods to structural health monitoring problems. Real-time system identification and damage detection of structural systems have been addressed by leveraging Bayesian filtering techniques (Journal Papers #6 and #7). More specifically, a novel Bayesian Expectation-Maximization methodology is offered, which has opened up new opportunities for performing uncertainty quantification in real-time and identifying state, parameters, and input forces simultaneously. This method is shown to be successful in calibrating the noise parameters based on data and offering reliable uncertainty bounds for the estimations.

16212918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212918.value: Despite the advancements achieved in this research, some challenges remain open, requiring further investigation. In Particular, one of the drawbacks of Bayesian methods is their high computational cost compared to less involved non-probabilistic methods. Therefore, an interesting research direction to explore in the future can be the development of new approximations and computational algorithms, which reduce the computational costs effectively to make Bayesian methods competitive with other techniques in terms of computation. In this regard, the integration of Bayesian techniques with high-performance computing techniques can be significantly beneficial and recommended for future studies. Another potential research direction can be the application of the proposed Bayesian framework to wind turbines and demonstrate its capability for handling the challenging task of system identification and damage detection.

16212918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212918.value: The construction of complex structures has progressively grown to increasingly advanced levels. As time goes by, such structures will age and become commercially more demanding from a monitoring and inspection point of view. Therefore, the structural safety and reliability assessment of these complex structures throughout their lifespan would mandate allocating considerable financial recourses. From this perspective, it is necessary to develop cost-effective structural condition monitoring and inspection methods that can reliably identify the presence of damage in structures. In this regard, probabilistic methods have shown great promise in not only indicating damage in structures but also offering the uncertainty associated with the outcome of damage detection, reflecting the degree of belief in the output of the method. This completed project has devoted enormous theoretical efforts to provide a good foundation for such techniques and demonstrated these methods through numerical and experimental studies.
