16213118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213118.value: 开发缓存一致性异构CPU-FPGA平台的潜力

16213118.label: Project Objectives
16213118.value: We will develop several source code level optimization techniques and an automated source transformation flow to improve the data locality and achieve the maximum overall benefits from HLS computational parallelism and cache performance improvement. We will develop a detailed cache management scheme to reduce the FPGA cache miss rate. First, we will design a compile-time static analysis algorithm, which analyzes the data reuse distance of the cache lines based on the memory trace of AFUs and extracts their locality parameters. A dynamic cache bypassing mechanism is then developed to select the cache lines to allocate in the cache according to the static analysis parameters. The combined effect of static and dynamic schemes will improve the cache performance. We will develop an efficient cache contention model for the performance of the shared L1 and L2 cache, which is based on the task level modeling and avoids the repetitive memory trace profiling used in the previous work. The cache model can be integrated in the task partition algorithm to achieve the optimal workload distribution between the CPU and FPGA, and hence improve overall system performance.

16213118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213118.value: Heterogeneous computing, comprised of processors and hardware accelerators, is a very promising direction for performance and power efficient computing, which enables us to overcome traditional performance and power walls. CPUs combined with FPGA-based accelerators are becoming increasingly popular recently – attracting interest from both academia and industry due to the overall advantages of the FPGA in terms of performance, power, and reconfigurability. Existing systems with CPUs and FPGA-based accelerators have been generally used for computing in the cloud and for acceleration of cloud-based algorithms. However, in order for it to become mainstream, several challenges need to be overcome. One of the primary challenges is related to long data transfer time between CPUs and accelerators. While Direct Memory Access (DMA) has been used to reduce this delay, it still has problems because an external memory needs to be set up and written with data before the direct transfer can take place. This also very much reduces the chance of fine-grained acceleration that could be possible if accelerators and CPUs could share data in each other’s memory spaces more efficiently. Therefore, in this proposal we investigate cache-coherent design and interaction between CPUs and FPGA-based accelerators. Cache coherency guarantees that both the CPUs and the accelerators act as peers and use the most recent data for all computation. This is guaranteed by access to caches on the CPU side as well as on the FPGA side. The sharing of memory space between the CPU and FPGA can also significantly simplify the programming model, which eases the utilization of the heterogeneous system in the mainstream. Specifically, this proposal contributes to significantly improving the performance of design implementation in cache coherent CPU-FPGA systems from three perspectives: (1) a code transformation flow to optimize the C/C++ code of the accelerated functions to reduce the FPGA cache miss; (2) a cache management scheme with static analysis and dynamic control at the architectural level to further improve the cache performance; (3) a detailed and efficient modeling method to analyze competition for a shared cache between CPUs and accelerators, and aid proper task partition between CPUs and accelerators considering shared cache performance. With the proposed work, we aim to significantly ease the design, development, and deployment of systems comprising of CPUs and FPGA- based accelerators, either in the cloud or for embedded systems. 由处理器和硬件加速器组成的异构计算是性能和节能计算的一个非常有前景的方向，这使我们能够克服传统的性能和功率墙。 CPU与基于FPGA的加速器相结合最近变得越来越流行 - 由于FPGA在性能，功耗和可重新配置性方面的整体优势，吸引了学术界和工业界的兴趣。具有CPU和基于FPGA的加速器的现有系统通常用于云中的计算和用于加速基于云的算法。但是，为了使其成为主流，需要克服一些挑战。主要挑战之一与CPU和加速器之间的长数据传输时间有关。虽然已使用直接内存访问（DMA）来减少此延迟，但仍然存在问题，因为在进行直接传输之前需要设置外部存储器并使用数据写入。如果加速器和CPU可以更有效地在彼此的存储空间中共享数据，这会极大地提高细粒度加速的可能性。因此，在本提案中，我们研究了CPU和基于FPGA的加速器之间的缓存一致性设计和交互。高速缓存一致性保证CPU和加速器都充当对等体并使用最新数据进行所有计算。通过访问CPU端和FPGA端的高速缓存可以保证这一点。 CPU和FPGA之间共享存储空间也可以显著简化编程模型，从而推动异构系统在主流中的利用。 具体而言，该项目从三个方面有助于显著提高缓存一致CPU-FPGA系统中设计实现的性能：（1）通过代码转换流程来优化加速函数的C / C ++代码，以减少FPGA缓存未命中率; （2）在架构层面采用静态分析和动态控制的缓存管理方案，进一步提高缓存性能; （3）开发详细而有效的建模方法，用于分析CPU和加速器之间共享缓存的竞争，并在考虑共享缓存访问延迟的情况下帮助CPU和加速器之间正确的分配任务。 通过这个项目工作，我们的目标是显著简化包含CPU和基于FPGA的加速器的系统的设计，开发和部署，无论是在云中还是在嵌入式系统中。

16213118.label: Realisation of objectives
16213118.value: Three objectives have been realized. For the first objective, we refer to previous papers’ methods and realize the source code transfer to increase the efficiency of data reuse. We have implemented this method in the CNN accelerator design and stereo vision accelerator design, and published the results in the papers “Optimizing OpenCL-based CNN Design on FPGA with Comprehensive Design Space Exploration and Collaborative Performance Modeling” and “FP-Stereo: Hardware-Efficient Stereo Vision for Embedded Applications”. For the second objective, we have developed a hybrid cache management scheme combined with static locality characteristics analysis based on data reuse distance and dynamic cache bypassing control based on the static analysis results. We implemented this scheme in the Intel HARP2 system and achieved significant cache miss rate improvement and overall performance improvement. This work is published in the paper “LAMA: Link-Aware Hybrid Management for Memory Accesses in Emerging CPU-FPGA Platforms”. We also extended the cache bypassing method to GPU and developed an effective array-level bypassing for GPUs. We make the cache bypassing decision based on array level granularity, which prevents the data with low reuse from polluting the cache, as well as avoiding a large profiling overhead and maintaining the ease of programmability. In this work, to validate the effectiveness of array-level bypassing, we extend the detailed GPU cache model in previous work to collect the cache metrics for each array. Next, based on the metrics we just obtained, we propose an effective heuristic algorithm to judiciously select arrays for cache access or bypass. Experimental results on NVIDIA Titan X using a variety of benchmarks show that our approach for cache bypassing can effectively improve the overall performance for GPU applications by a 1.28X speedup. Due to the student's graduation, the work is only formed in a technology report. For the third objective, we try to address the challenge of analyzing the trade-offs of multiple coherency strategies available for CPU-FPGA communication and partitioning the task between CPU and FPGA with the most suitable communication strategy. In this part, we model CPU-FPGA communication relevant to task partitioning, proposing performance metrics, and profiling such communication with synthetic benchmarks using a comprehensive set of coherency strategies. We further analyze the profiling results and propose design guidelines for selecting the most suitable coherency strategy for task partitioning with different CPU-FPGA interaction features. We verify these guidelines with a set of real-world benchmarks, revealing a performance difference of up to 66.1% when the most suitable coherency strategy is selected. This paper is still under review because unfortunately, it was not successfully published in the previous rounds.

16213118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213118.value: In this work, we first propose a static analysis and dynamic control combined framework for memory access management in CPU-FPGA cache-coherent systems to further enhance memory access efficiency and maintain data consistency. Based on implementation results on the real Intel HARP2 platform, our memory management method is shown to improve performance by 34% on average with very low overhead of less than 1%. Then we continue to develop a simulation model to estimate the cache miss rate. Based on it, we develop an effective array-level cache bypassing for GPUs. In the first step, we characterize every array in an application to attain its cache usage features, such as compulsory miss rate, capacity miss rate, hit rate, and a total number of transactions. Then, we propose a heuristic algorithm to determine whether to bypass or cache each array based on its cache characteristics. As the last part to fully evaluate the trade-off of all the commonly used interfaces of CPU-FPGA integrated systems, we use ZCU102 as an example to profile its communication ports between CPU and FPGA with synthetic benchmarks. We further analyze the profiling results and propose design guidelines for selecting the most suitable coherency strategy for task partitioning with different CPU-FPGA interaction features. We verify these guidelines with a set of real-world benchmarks, revealing a performance difference of up to 66.1% when the most suitable coherency strategy is selected. Our work provides valuable insights into selecting the most efficient coherency strategy for CPU-FPGA collaboration scenarios, particularly for task partitioning schemes with frequent CPU-FPGA communication.

16213118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213118.value: The automatic CPU-FPGA partition is still challenging and currently mainly depends on manual efforts. Although there are some automatic partition methods proposed in previous academic works which our works are based on, there is a large room to further improve the efficiency of the partition algorithms. In addition, the partition and implementation flow on CPU-FPGA SoC is still complicated and not easy to use. But it is mainly due to the inconvenience of the commercial toolchain.

16213118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213118.value: To meet the rapidly increasing demands for computation capabilities, CPU is commonly worked with the hardware accelerators, such as FPGA. There are different communication interfaces between CPU and FPGA. Some favor large block data communication and some favor fine-grained communication. Selecting a suitable interface between CPU and FPGA is very important for the system performance. In this project, we have done a thorough profiling and analysis of the interface performance trade-off for different CPU-FPGA communication patterns. Based on it, we developed the guideline for port selection and task partition. For the system using a full coherent cache system that FPGA also has its one cache, to improve the cache miss rate of FPGA cache, we also developed a hybrid cache management strategy combing static pattern analysis and dynamic cache bypassing control to store only frequently used data in the FPGA cache and prevent cache pollution. Experimental results showed the efficiency of our proposed methods which greatly facilitated the application implementation in the CPU-FPGA system.

16213318.value: Develop Efficient Algorithms for constructing Dynamic Alphabetic Trees : These would be algorithms with quick data insertion/deletion/access times whose cost for a sequence of operations would be almost optimal for that sequence of operations. "Optimality" would be defined using a variety of metrics, including both static and dynamic optimality. "Almost" optimal would be defined using both additive and multiplicative approximations to the optimal solutions. Develop fast algorithms for constructing useful variants of optimal and almost optimal Alphabetic Trees, e.g., non-binary and length-limited Alphabetic Trees. Re-examine old open problems such as the verification of optimal Alphabetic Trees, using "new" data structure tools that have been developed over the last thirty-five years and were never previously applied to studying this problem.

16213318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213318.value: The purpose of this proposed study is to revisit Alphabetic Trees, an old data structure, with the dual goals of creating new fast data structures for current applications and revisiting old unsolved problems from a new perspective. The Dictionary Problem of storing data to permit efficient lookup is one of the oldest and most studied problems in computer science. One of the major techniques for solving it is to store data in search trees and in particular in Binary Search Trees (BSTs). Prefix-free codes, also known as Huffman Codes, are a classic and well-studied technique for storing and transmitting compressed data via codewords. Their underlying premise is that frequently occurring data will be assigned a short codeword; infrequently occurring data, a long one. The prefix-free coding problem is to find a prefix-free set of codewords that provide maximum compression. Every Huffman code has an associated Huffman (binary) tree. Alphabetic Codes are prefix-free codes obeying an additional constraint that their codewords must satisfy a type of dictionary order. The tree associated with these codes is known as an Alphabetic Tree and is also used to solve the Dictionary Problem. Alphabetic Trees were introduced more than 50 years ago, concurrently with standard BSTs. Even though they were introduced at around the same time, alphabetic trees are usually analyzed using information-theoretic tools; binary search trees using very different data-structure ones. Surprisingly, while the last 35 years have seen continued research into extensions of BSTs there has been little published concerning extensions of Alphabetic Trees. This is doubly surprising because almost-optimal Alphabetic Trees are currently still used in many practical applications, such as routing tables. We propose to re-examine Alphabetic Trees using a combination of classic information theoretic tools and new data-structure techniques developed over recent decades. An example of the type of problem to be addressed would be the development of almost-optimal dynamic Alphabetic Trees, i.e., where the tree modifies itself to fit current data access patterns and allows insertions of new items and deletions of old ones. While there has been a plethora of work on almost-optimal dynamic Binary Search Trees there has been almost nothing published on almost-optimal dynamic Alphabetic Trees. Other examples of problems to be worked on are the construction of optimal Alphabetic Trees in the non-binary case, length limited trees and verification of the optimality of Alphabetic Trees. This is a proposal in the subarea of theoretical computer science. 這項擬議研究的目的是重新審視一種舊的資料結構－字母樹，目標是為當前的應用創建新的快速資料結構，並從新的角度重新審視未解決的問題。 以字典形式儲存數據從而允許有效地翻查資料的問題是計算機科學中最古老和研究最多的問題之一，解決它的主要技術之一是將數據存儲在搜尋樹中，特別是二元搜尋樹（BST）。 無前置碼代碼，也稱為霍夫曼編碼，是一種經典且經過充分研究的技術，用於通過代碼字以存儲和傳輸經壓縮過的數據。它的基本前提是：頻繁出現的數據將被分配一個短代碼字；不常出現的數據則被分配一個較長的代碼字。無前置碼代碼探討的問題是：找到能提供最大壓縮效果的無前置碼字集。每個霍夫曼編碼都有一個對應的霍夫曼（二元）樹。 字母代碼也是無前置碼代碼，但其代碼字必須額外滿足一種字典形式的順序。與此對應的樹稱為字母樹，也用於解決字典問題。字母樹於50多年前首次被引入，與BST同期。 儘管它們大約在同一時間被引入，字母樹通常以信息理論工具來分析，而二元搜尋樹則以非常不同的資料結構作分析。令人驚訝的是，儘管過去35年間擴展BST的研究不斷地進行，但關於擴展字母樹的文章郤很少。這是非常令人驚訝的，因為接近最優化的字母樹目前仍然在許多實際應用中使用，例如路由表。 我們提議使用經典信息理論工具和近幾十年來開發的新資料結構技術的來重新審視字母樹。要解決的問題的一個例子是：開發接近最優化的動態字母樹，亦即是，字母樹能自身作出修正，以適應當前數據提取模式，並允許插入新項目和刪除舊項目。雖然在接近最優化的動態二元搜尋樹的問題上已有大量文獻，但幾乎沒有文章發表關於接近最優化的動態字母樹。 另外可研究的問題包括，在非二元情形下構建最優化的字母樹、構建長度受限的樹和核實字母樹是否最優化等。 這篇文章屬於理論計算機科學的一個分區。

16213318.label: Realisation of objectives
16213318.value: We start by noting that the project was unable to fully meet its stated objectives. This was due to an unfortunate confluence of personal, professional, and objective-related reasons. - The personal was that PI’s youngest child fell ill with an auto-immune disease and was hospitalized multiple times during 2019-20, requiring care then and afterwards. This slowed down the PI’s progress. - The professional was the difficulty, mentioned in the progress report, in recruiting research students to work on the project. The PI did successfully recruit a new PhD student, but due to Covid restrictions, the student was unable to physically come to Hong Kong. After a year of attempting to work online, the student decided to leave the program. The PI did manage to then recruit an MPhil student but that was late in the project. - The objective-related reason was that the major primary goals and line of inquiry described in Section 6.3 of the progress report turned out to be unachievable. As stated, we had developed a family of heuristics for efficiently dynamically maintaining almost-optimal alphabetic search trees i.e., trees that change to fit the empirical probability distribution induced by key accesses. These heuristics worked well in practice. As planned, we attempted to formally prove that they always performed well. Unfortunately, working with the project supported MPhil student, we managed to develop provably bad counterexamples that would force each heuristic in the family to run badly in the worst case. This line of inquiry therefore had to be abandoned. ----------------------------------------------------------- Despite these setbacks we were in the end able to achieve good results on three related problems, described below. 1) Almost Optimal Dynamic Binary Search Trees using Morris Counters After determining that the approach discussed above was unlikely to be successful, we redirected the focus of the project-supported MPhil student’s research to the related problem of developing better randomized almost-optimal binary search trees (AOBSTs). One classic approach to solving the dynamic AOBST problem is the use of TREAPS. These assign each search key a “priority” and build the unique binary search tree which is also a maximum-heap on the priorities. Let F be an item’s frequency, i.e., the number of times it has been previously accessed. The treap algorithm first generates F random real numbers from the unit interval and then assigns their maximum as the priority. This provably guarantees that the treap is an AOBST and leads to efficient dynamic algorithms for maintaining them. Surprisingly, the use of other priorities for treaps do not seem to have been previously studied. While treaps are easy to program and work well their weakness is that they require log_2(F) bits to store priorities. This space usage can blow up after many accesses. A similar problem arises in data-streaming applications where maintaining an exact count F of the appearances of an item in the stream also require log_2(F) bits. In data streaming, this weakness is alleviated by using approximate counters, such as the “Morris counter”, which use log_2(log_2(F)) or even fewer bits. This stores a randomized counter whose expected but not exact value is guaranteed to be the exact count. In our research we examined the use of Morris counters and other functions as priorities. This required developing a theory of what types of priorities could yield almost optimal dynamic search trees. It also required developing a better understanding of Morris counters; the extensive previous studies on them had analyzed their concentration properties; those are what are needed for streaming algorithms. Their use as priorities required a better analysis of their anti-concentration properties. We proved that, if the search keys have a random ordering, then using Morris counters (and some other random variables) as priorities, does yield dynamic AOBSTs. We also provided a taxonomy of such priorities. But, if the keys are not randomly ordered, then we showed arbitrarily long access sequences for which Morris counters are provably not AOBSTs. 2) Optimal Binary Comparison Trees. In Objective 3 we have worked on an old open problem in the study of Optimal Binary Search Trees. Historically, such trees assumed that a query for element x in a tree performs a ternary comparison against a key K stored in an internal node; branching left or right if xK, and terminating if x=K. An open question raised by Knuth in 1998 was how to efficiently build optimal search trees if only binary comparisons are permitted (hardware usually only permits binary comparisons; ternary comparisons are wasteful since they require two binary comparisons). A complicated O(n^4) algorithm was published in 2002 for a very special case of this problem (in which all queries were assumed to be in the key set) but the general case was still open. In 2015, the PI with coauthors described an O(n^4) dynamic-programming algorithm that worked in both the special and general case, but with very long and complicated analysis. Under this project we developed a much simpler practical algorithm with a very short analysis. This settled the open question and was published (J3 in Part C) in 2021 in the ACM Transactions on Algorithms as “A Simple Algorithm for Optimal Search Trees with Two-way Comparisons”. 3) Optimal Algorithms for AIFV coding trees: Alphabetic coding trees are special cases of Huffman, i.e., prefix-free, coding trees. Working on this project we developed new results on a different recently developed class of coding trees. Specifically, we developed the first polynomial time algorithms for constructing AIFV-m codes. AIFV-m (Almost Instantaneous Fixed to Variable) codes were developed over the past ten years. They are a new type of lossless code that approaches even closer to the entropy lower bound on compression than the ``optimal’’ Huffman codes. They do this by coding with m trees rather than just one tree and allowing a bounded decoding-delay. The description of the codes includes a process that determines which code trees will be used to encode the next message symbol. It can be shown that the average cost of using a specific AIFV-m code is the gain of an associated “Markov chain with rewards”. The problem of finding a min-cost AIFV-m code is the problem of finding the cheapest associated Markov Chain. All previously known algorithms for solving this problem required exponential time. They were iterative algorithms that utilized a “fastest descent” technique. The new project-supported result showed, for AIFV-2 codes, how to map the two state Markov chains into an arrangement of lines in 2-dimensional space and then use geometric properties to binary search for the solution. This led to the first polynomial-time algorithm for constructing optimal AIFV-2 codes and appeared in the IEEE Data Compression Conference in 2019 (C1). An extended journal version of this result is currently in submission (J1) to the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. Both the old and new algorithms for AIFV coding utilize a dynamic programming (DP) step. Two new project-supported results showed how to improve these DPs. The first, in the journal Theoretical Computer Science in 2021 (J2), used range minimum-queries to batch dynamic programming calculations, decreased the running time for the AIFV-2 DPs from O(n^5) time. down to O(n^3) time. The second, in the 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory (C2), decreased the running time for the AIFV-m DPs from O(n^{2m+1}) time down to O(n^{m+2}) for all m>2, through the development of a new DP algorithm.

16213318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213318.value: As discussed in 5.3, the first major research finding was negative. It was that many heuristics for maintaining alphabetic trees dynamically using local tree manipulations were shown to be bad. More specifically, while they all worked quite well on random data, for each heuristic examined, we were always able to develop specifically crafted arbitrarily long counterexamples that forced the heuristic to behave badly, i.e., these provided proofs that the heuristics did not provide almost optimal behavior for all access sequences. A second major research finding had both positive and negative outcomes. This was the analysis of treap data structures using different priorities. As discussed earlier, this was the thesis research of the project supported MPhil student which initiated the study of treaps with different priorities. The positive research outcome was a study of which random functions of frequencies being used as priorities would guarantee that treaps would provide almost optimal access times for randomly ordered keys and which would not. This also proved that using Morris counters (a random variable) as priorities would also guarantee almost optimal behavior in this case. The negative result was a counterexample access sequence that shows that, for fixed orderings of keys, the use of Morris counters as priorities would not yield almost optimal search trees. A third major research finding was the development of tools for constructing AIFV-2 codes. These are a new form of lossless compression that had recently been shown to beat Huffman coding compression but for which no polynomial time construction algorithm was known. The problem of constructing the best such AIFV-2 codes was equivalent to finding a minimum cost 2-state Markov chain with rewards among an exponentially sized set of such Markov chains. Our major result here was a transformation of the problem into a two-dimensional linear programming problem (with an exponential number of constraints). This geometric interpretation led to a simple binary-search based procedure for solving the linear program and finding the best such code.

16213318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213318.value: Two of the outcomes of this project have potential to be developed further. The first outcome is the use of Morris Counters and other random variables as priorities in treaps for dynamically maintaining almost optimal binary search trees. The results so far have only been published in Mr. Siu-Chung Chan’s MPhil thesis. They need to be further refined and submitted for publication. Our research showed that Morris counters do not work well. This raises the question of what other random priorities would work well. More specifically, it raises the question of how many bits of randomness WOULD be needed to construct random priorities guaranteeing almost optimal performance. We propose continuing this study. The second is the further development of AIFV codes. The AIFV coding problem is a special case of finding a minimum cost Markov chain from a collection of Markov chains with rewards. We developed efficient algorithms for solving this problem for two state Markov Chains. They worked by transforming the problem into a geometric one. The obvious course of action is to extend this to arbitrary length Markov Chains, which we have already started working on.

16213318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213318.value: “Trees’’ are an abstract way of storing or representing data in computer science. They are often used to implement dictionaries or to represent ways of compressing data. Theoretical computer science has a long history of developing different tree structures that can be useful in different contexts. In addition to being immediately practical, this research often serves as the starting point for new applications that appear many years later. This project worked on three different tree problems, developing new techniques. The first was answering a long-standing question of how to efficiently construct a static “binary comparison search tree” that would answer data search queries in minimal expected time. The second was showing how to efficiently construct the best Almost-Instantaneous Fixed-to-Variable (AIFV) codes for performing lossless compression on given data. AIFV codes are a relatively new approach for lossless compression that have been shown to have good performance. Their weakness was the lack of efficient algorithms for constructing them. This project developed the first such algorithms. The third was an analysis of a specific type of data structure, known as treaps, for storing dynamically changing data. We extended previous work work on treaps to show when they can or cannot be improved.

16214118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214118.value: Amplification of seismic waves due to surface topography is regarded as one of the major causes of extensive damage in past earthquakes. Due to focusing or defocusing of seismic waves, strong motions are usually amplified at convex features such as ridges and hill tops, and deamplified at concave features such as canyons and valleys. Observations during past earthquakes have demonstrated the importance of incorporating topographic amplification in the seismic design procedure of earth structures, foundations and buildings. It is particularly meaningful for seismic practice in mountainous cities, such as Hong Kong. However, numerical studies in the past on topographic amplification were primarily based on simple 2D topography and homogeneous soil profiles, and significantly underestimate ground amplification. Due to its complexity, topographic amplification has not yet been incorporated in most seismic design codes. In the proposed project, three interrelated tasks are planned to address the open challenges: First, a high-resolution 3D subsurface model will be developed based on the most extensive geotechnical investigation including 34,000 borehole logs in Hong Kong Island and a digital terrain model. The abundance of subsurface data makes the project a unique opportunity to study the characteristics of nonlinearity and uncertainty in subsurface soils, leading to realistic 3D numerical modelling of regional topography and soil conditions. Since the coupling effect between topography and subsurface soils under earthquakes is not yet well understood, the second task of the project is to develop simple parametric models to quantify 3D topographic amplification based on simple proxies of terrain topography, soil profiles and input waves. The project aims to improve scientific understandings and to advance the state-of-the-art to incorporate 3D topographic amplification in earthquake design in this region and beyond. Validation and calibration of the parametric models against historic field data are critical, although they have rarely been performed due to the lack of well documented data. In the third task of the project, instrumented field data on pronounced topography during historical earthquakes will be used to validate and calibrate the developed parametric models. The field data include the KiK-Net downhole array in Japan and Lanzhou loess field data from China models. These case studies will provide valuable opportunity to revisit the key factors that influence topographic amplification. 在以往的地震中，地震波在三維地形上的放大效應是引起大規模破壞的主要因素之一。由於地形的聚焦和散焦效應，地震波在山脊等凸地形中往往被放大，而在山谷等凹地形中被縮小。歷史地震觀測表明，考慮地震波地形放大效應對土工結構、基礎工程和建築物的抗震設計具有重要意義，對香港這類山地城市尤為重要。然而，以往的地震波地形放大效應的數值研究主要基於二維地形和均質土層假設，而這些假設往往會低估地形放大效應。由於其複雜性，地形放大效應尚未被納入大多數抗震設計規範中。 本研究項目針對未解決的科學挑戰展開研究，包括以下三個相互關聯的課題：首先，利用香港島區域豐富的地質鑽孔資料和數字地形構建高分辨率的三維地形、地層模型。這些豐富的地質勘探資料為研究土層的非線性和不確定性提供了獨特的機遇，以此構建的區域化地形、土層三維數值模型更為真實可靠。由於強震作用下地形和土層的耦合作用規律尚不清楚，本研究的第二項課題將提出簡化參數來反映地形、土層及地震波輸入的特性，發展地震波三維地形放大效應的量化參數模型，以提高科學認知，促進香港及其他地區的抗震設計。由於應用歷史地震觀測數據對參數模型進行驗證和校準至關重要，本項目的第三個課題將利用日本KiK-Net地震記錄台站網和中國黃土丘陵地區的地震觀測數據，系統地驗證所提出的參數模型，為深入研究影響地形放大效應的關鍵參數提供寶貴的實例。

16214118.label: Realisation of objectives
16214118.value: Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI, Co-I and their coworkers have successfully collected and reviewed high-resolution 3D digital terrain model and borehole logs in order to model the near-surface geology of the study areas. We constructed 3D spectral element models for Hong Kong island [J1], Kowloon [J5] and Tuen Mun-Yuen Long areas [C1], Hongshiyan landslide area in mainland China [J1][J6], and Aso caldera region in Japan [J8]. The constructed numerical models were used to simulate large domain (30~50 km) wave propagation in complex topographies with an accuracy up to 5~10 Hz. In particular, we studied the effects of spatial variation and uncertainty of the soil profile on seismic amplification of the soil ground (Huang et al. 2021 [J4]). In Kato and Wang (2022) [J5], we studied the complex wave interaction in subsurface soils with buildings and underground structures. To improve the efficiency of numerical analysis, we proposed a new family of high-order weight functions for mass lumping in dynamic analysis. The work is under review (Fan et al. 2022 [J7], under major revision). Project objective 2 has been fully achieved. Parametric models are developed to quantify 3D topographic amplification based on simple proxies. We discovered that amplifications of Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA), Peak Ground Velocity (PGV) and Arias Intensity (Ia), are strongly correlated with smoothed topographic curvatures or the relative heights of terrain under different smoothing lengths. The topographic amplification is frequency-dependent and scale dependent. We developed explicit equations to predict the topographic amplification of PGA, PGV and Ia (Huang et al. 2020 [J1] and Chen et al. 2022 [J8]). In addition, we found that the topographic amplification pattern is polarized in different directions, which can be parameterized using directional curvature. We found that topographic amplification pattern changes under oblique incident waves. The work has been orally presented in ICOLD 2019 Symposium of International Commission on Large Dams in Ottawa, Canada (Chen et al. 2019 [C1]). Another paper on coupling effect of topography and subsurface soil has been presented in the 17th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering (17WCEE) held in Sendai, Japan on September 2021 [C5, Chen et al. 2021], which is the top conference in earthquake engineering. Based on strong motion database, we further developed a vine copula-based dependence model to quantify multivariate random nature of PGA, PGV and Ia, which was published in (Wang et al. 2020b [J3]). We also developed a machine-learning algorithm to improve empirical prediction of landslide based on ground motions (Wang et al. 2020a [J2]). Project objective 3 has been fully achieved. we actively developed numerical models to validate and calibrate the parametric model using instrumented earthquake data in Japan and China. We incorporated topographic effects and soil nonlinearity in the simulation of the 2016 Mw7.0 Kumamoto earthquake in Japan (Chen et al. 2022 [J8]). The numerical simulation was thoroughly validated using six strong motion stations in KiK-Net. Through the simulation, we found that the unique topographic setting of volcanic caldera leads to significant amplification of ground motions around the central cone and caldera edge. The proposed parametric model could be used to predict the strong motion on topographies. The paper is currently under review. Another validation case study is the 2014 Ms 6.5 Ludian earthquake in China (Huang et al. 2020 [J1]). We developed a large-scale model to simulate fault rupture and wave propagation process. The numerical simulation agrees well with recorded ground-motion time histories and observed landslide pattern in this region. Recently, we further developed a physics-based multiscale framework (Feng et al. 2022 [J6]). At a regional scale, Spectral Element Method (SEM) is used to model elastic wave propagation from a seismic source to a local site with complex topography. At a local scale, the topographic amplification of motions and coseismic landslide process are simulated by a nonlinear Material Point Model (MPM). The study revealed that the Hongshiyan slope, located at the terminal portion of an elongated mountain ridge, was particularly susceptible to significant topographic amplifications during an earthquake. 16214118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214118.value: Major findings: 1. The project performed large-scale 3D simulations of topographic amplification of ground motions based on high-resolution borehole data. The characteristics of ground motions, influence of nonlinearity, spatial variation/uncertainties in soil profiles are quantifies. 2. Through numerical simulations, the project identified that the smoothed curvature and relative heights on a certain length scale show strong coloration with topographic amplifications of key ground motion intensity measures. Accordingly, the project developed parametric models to quantify the 3D topographic amplification based on these simple proxies. The project discovered the topographic amplification of ground motions are frequency dependent and scale dependent. The influence of soil profiles and input waves are also studied. 3. The numerical simulations have been extensively validated through several earthquake case studies in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan. In-situ ground motion recordings have been used to calibrate and validate these numerical models. Research Outcome The research findings have been published as 6 SCI journal papers in top international journals, including Engineering Geology, Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering, Journal of Earthquake Engineering, Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering, Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, and Bulletin of Earthquake Engineering. In addition, 2 papers are currently under review or re-review (after major revision). The research findings have been actively disseminated in various local, national and international conferences, including an oral presentation in 17th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering in September 2021 in Japan, which is the most prestigious earthquake engineering conference and attended by 3000+ around the world; International Commission on Large Dams 2019 Symposium, held in Ottawa, Canada on June 9-14, 2019; 7th International Conference on Earthquake Geotechnical Engineering (7ICEGE), held in Rome, Italy on 17-20 June 2019. The research work has also been delivered as a keynote in IACGE International Conference on Geotechnical and Earthquake Engineering (IACGE2018) organized by International Association of Chinese Geotechnical Engineers, October 19-22, 2018, Chongqing, China, and as a Theme Lecture in The 10th National Conference on Soil Dynamics, November 2-4, 2018, Nanjing, China, which is the biggest conference on soil dynamics in China. Three PhD students, Dr. KATO Bence (graduated in June 2020), Dr. FENG Kewei (graduated June 2021), Mr. CHEN Zhengwei (estimated to graduate in August 2022) have been trained; two Postdoc Fellow Dr. DU Chunyang, Dr. Huo Fan, have been working on this project. An exchange student, Mr. WANG Maoxin from Wuhan University, has been trained through the project.

16214118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214118.value: Although we have conducted numerical simulation and validation study of topographic amplification of ground motions through several earthquake case studies in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan, significant efforts are still needed to collect strong motion data on topographies. Such kind of in-situ strong-motion data on topographies is very valuable to further validate and refine the prediction model, yet they are still quite rare in reality. Such needs should be seriously considered in strong motion monitoring programs. Although prediction models for topographic amplification has been developed in this project, the prediction will be less robust on soils as compared to that on rocks. It is due to very complicated soil amplification and wave interaction patterns, when the subsurface soil conditions are complex. Multiscale models need to be further developed to couple regional scale wave simulation with local scale soil amplification, with an emphasis on the effect of strong soil nonlinearity and wave interaction.

16214118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214118.value: Amplification of seismic waves due to surface topography has often been observed to cause intensive damage in past earthquakes. Due to its complexity, topographic amplification has not yet been incorporated in most seismic design codes. In this research, we conducted the state-of-the-art numerical simulation to quantify the amplification of earthquake ground motions due to coupled 3D topography and subsurface soil conditions. In this project, we developed details model based on a high-resolution digital terrain model and subsurface soil data. The developed numerical models are able to simulate earthquake rupture and wave propogation in a large simulation domain. The models are validated by using serval earthquake case studies in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan. The project developed parametric models to predict the topographic amplification of ground motions using simple topographic features. The model is most useful and can be easily incorporated into seismic hazard assessment and design maps. As it is well known that Hong Kong is a mountainous region with many buildings and infrastructure built on hill tops and steep slopes due to the paucity of land, the study will immediately benefit the ongoing efforts in developing the seismic code for buildings in this region and beyond.

16214318.label: Realisation of objectives
16214318.value: We have conducted two lines of research efforts in identifying a suitable topology to implement a power converter with ultra-low voltage conversion ratio (VCR), which is the ratio of the output voltage (Vo) over the power supply voltage (Vin), that is, VCR = Vo/Vin << 1 (e.g. VCR = (1/12)X, (1/24)X, etc.). Our exhaustive construction method of switched-capacitor converters (SCCs) was reported in [1], and we identified two candidates (Fig. 1.) The first SCC uses 3 flying capacitors (C1, C2 and C3, along with the load capacitor CL) and 4 topological phases (phi1, phi2, phi3, phi4), and achieves a minimum VCR of (1/10)X (Fig. 1(a)). However, C1 is left unconnected in phi4 = 1, and an idling capacitor means inefficient use of capacitance. The exhaustive search also identifies a (1/16)X SCC that uses 4 flying capacitors (C1, C2, C3 and C4) and only 3 topological phases (phi1, phi2, phi3), and the obvious advantage is that there is no idling capacitor (Fig. 1(b)). The second approach is to find a novel topology of a hybrid power converter: an integration of a switched-capacitor converter (SCC) and a switched-inductor buck converter, as shown in Fig. 2(a) [2]. We use VCR = 1/24X as an example. In phi1, CF is serially connected to C1, C2 and C3 that are connected in parallel; and in phi2, CF is connected in parallel to C1, C2 and C3 that are connected in series. This action gives a SCC with VCR = (1/4)X. When turn to the buck converter, in phi1, the input voltage is then (1/4)Vin = 6V for charging the inductor; and in phi2, the inductor gyrates the current from ground to the output voltage of Vo = 1V. Hence, the ideal duty ratio of the buck converter is D = 1/6 = 0.167. This duty ratio allows the buck converter to be more efficient. It is also clear that the duration of phi1 is DT, and that of phi2 is D’T = (1–D)T. More importantly, careful examination shows that the inductor current, which is also the load current and is thus the largest current, passes through only one switch for both the charging and discharging phases. We adopted the second approach and designed an integrated hybrid converter. The first prototype has latch-up issues, and after debugging, the converter was redesigned that has the latch-up issues fixed, and the switched-capacitor converter front-end served as a reliable input source to the embedded buck converter. The second prototype also implement circuit improvements with a different layout. The layout of the first prototype was like a square, and the chip exhibited high-voltage latch-up. The chip was sent to the IC Failure Analysis Laboratory in Hong Kong Science Park and was examined using the thermal emission electronic imaging method. It was found that latch-up occurred at the bootstrapping gate drivers of the switched-capacitor circuit, located at the center of the chip, where the substrate tub and the guard ring were far away from the bonding pad. For the second IC prototype, the latch-up issue was mitigated by redesigning the IC floorplan to be an elongated rectangle, to make sure that substrate tubs and guard rings were shortest from the bonding pad. We have conduct temperature measurements for the temperature sensor, and will perform the same measurement for the hybrid converter. Spatial temperature sensor that monitors on-chip thermal status of a power converter chip has been developed. Thermal sensor and its localized readout circuit are distributed to each pre-defined hot-spot monitoring region to act as a local temperature sensor. A hardware sharing scheme is invented so that the readout circuits of adjacent sensors can be reconfigured to form a higher resolution readout circuit which gives a better temperature sensing resolution. The results have been published in [3]. One research plan was to send a research assistant traveling to CERN in Genova, Switzerland to study the actual engineering requirement of DC-DC converters used in the LHC-b (Large Hadron Collider beauty) upgrade project. Air tickets were booked and accommodation reserved, but due to covid-19, the trip to Switzerland has to be cancelled in early Feb 2020. CERN and Switzerland imposed traveling warning and suggested to stall as many on-site visits as possible. Although the traveling plan was aborted, our research assistant was invited to join the electronic test board design team for the RPC (Resistive Plate Chamber) project. The RPC project also uses many DC-DC converters, and we were able to get information on how DC-DC converters integrate into the RPC electronic board. The test board was focused on both analog and digital testing of the front-end time-to-digital converter (TDC). We were responsible to design PCB layout floor-planning, and were asked to design the power and ground planes carefully because the chip prototype of RPC’s high speed TDC was sensitive to noise. The four layers test board layout floor-planning was proposed and applied to the final test board design. [1] Y. 16214318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214318.value: Multi-level hybrid converters can reduce the voltage conversion ratio (VCR) by stacking up power switches to accommodate more charge-pump (switched-capacitor) stages. The floating voltage supplies for bootstrapping gate drivers are not easy to design, especially when the stack-up level is more than 3. It is required to use additional high-voltage regulators in higher stack-up levels. Our proposed asymmetric 3-level buck converter can avoid the mentioned technical challenge. The VCR can be reduced by extending with more switched-capacitor stages. More importantly, no matter how many stages are added, the topology still allows the inductor current, which is also the load current and is thus the largest current, to pass through only one switch for both the charging and discharging phases, thus maintaining a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) even for very low voltage conversion ratio. For example, our latest fabricated version of the integrated hybrid converter measured the peak PCE of 93% when the supply voltage is Vin = 12V, the output voltage is Vo = 1V and the output current is Io = 3A (VCR = (1/12)X). The A3L converter also worked for the case of Vin = 54V and Vo = 1V (VCR = (1/54)X). The PCE at Io = 2.25A is simulated at 89%, and measurement is underway.

16214318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214318.value: The proposed A3L hybrid buck converter could be implemented using off-chip power switches, to cater for large output current such as IO = 5A. Off-chip implementation could make use of HEMTs (high electron mobility transistors) such as GaNFET. They can sustain a high breakdown voltage and is suitable for high input voltage (Vin > 54V).

16214318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214318.value: There is high demand for power converters to have ultra-low voltage conversion ratios (VCRs) with wide input voltage (Vin) range (12V ~ 54V) that realize low output voltage (Vo) for Point-of-Load (PoL) applications. A simple buck converter has low power conversion efficiency (PCE) because the duty ratio D is too small, with D < Vo/Vin << 1. Using a hybrid power converter with a step-down switched-capacitor converter (SCC) could increase the duty ratio of the buck converter, but existing topologies require using two power switches in the main current path. Our proposed asymmetric 3-level (A3L) hybrid buck converter attains high PCE by having only one power switch in the main current path that charges and discharges the inductor of the buck converter. While two power switches are needed in charging and discharging most of the flying capacitors, these power transistors can be smaller as the time available is longer, which is equal to D'T = (1-D)T ~ T, as D << 1. The A3L converter was designed using 0.18um BCD (bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) process, and measurement results shows that it attains the peak PCE of 93% when Vin = 12V, Vo = 1V, and the output current Io = 3A.

16214418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214418.value: The ongoing transition from batch-wise to continuous manufacturing (CM) in the pharmaceutical industry offers many opportunities to reduce the cost and environmental impact of pharmaceutical manufacturing. CM has several inherent advantages over batch-wise processing. Furthermore, the transition to CM offers potential advantages for specific processing steps through the development of novel technologies that work particularly well in continuous flow mode. Anti-solvent crystallization is an important component of pharmaceutical processing, involving the separation and purification of active ingredients. A feed stream with the dissolved active ingredient is mixed with a miscible solvent (the so-called anti-solvent) that lowers the solubility provoking crystallization of the active ingredient. The properties of the produced crystals need to be uniform and predictable. Therefore, mixing must be sufficiently fast to create homogenous conditions for crystal nucleation and growth. However, conventional well-mixed vessels still produce a non-uniform product quality due to the broad residence time distribution of the crystals. Tubular crystallizers have the ability to operate under plug-flow conditions enabling a uniform product quality for anti-solvent crystallization if mixing in the radial direction within a tube is sufficiently fast, which is an obstacle due to the laminar-flow conditions. Internals, such as those used in static mixers, have been used, but lack flexibility of optimization during operation and are sensitive to fouling. Active mixers based on electric fields are non-invasive and flexible in operation. However, although such mixers have received applications in microfluidics, their use for continuous anti-solvent crystallization has not been tested. The objective of the proposed research will be to develop an active mixer for the continuous anti-solvent crystallization of pharmaceuticals based on induced-charge electro-osmosis (ICEO). A flow device with micro-patterned electrodes will be developed. The electrodes will generate a low-voltage alternating-current electric field and act as polarizable surfaces that can produce fluid vortices when an electrolyte is present via dynamic changes in electric double-layer formation. The flow device will be optimized to suit typical crystallization conditions and will be integrated with a segmented-flow tubular crystallizer. The experiments will reveal how design variables related to the ICEO-based mixer can influence the final product quality by creating homogeneous and predictable conditions for crystal nucleation and growth. Finally, a design tool for process optimization and solvent selection will be developed. The successful development of the proposed ICEO-based continuous anti-solvent crystallization process will be a major step forward in realizing the full potential of pharmaceutical crystallization in continuous flow mode.

16214518.label: Project Objectives
16214518.value: Develop efficient algorithms for approximating Minkowski sums. Develop efficient algorithms for generating approximate solutions to single-shot proximity queries involving multiple convex bodies. Develop efficient data structures for generating approximate solutions to repetitive-mode proximity queries involving multiple convex bodies.

Develop efficient algorithms for generating approximate solutions to single-shot proximity queries involving multiple convex bodies.
Develop efficient data structures for generating approximate solutions to repetitive-mode proximity queries involving multiple convex bodies.

16214518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214518.value: Problems involving the proximity of convex bodies have been extensively studied due to their applications in computational geometry, robotics, pattern recognition, machine learning, and computer-aided design. As most formulations of these problems are hard to solve exactly, except in very low dimensions, it is natural to consider approximations. There has, however, been only limited work in that direction. In contrast, approximation problems involving a single convex body have been heavily investigated, culminating in results by the PI and others in the past year that have led to some dramatic improvements. Single-body approximation turns out to have many rich connections with approximate proximity problems for multiple convex bodies. In this study, we therefore propose to design efficient data structures and algorithms for generating approximate solutions to proximity problems involving multiple convex bodies. 因其在計算幾何、機器人學、模式識別、機器學習和計算機輔助設計中的應用，凸體間的接近度問題得到了廣泛的研究。除非在非常低的維度下，這類問題大多難以精確求解，所以近似求解成為一種很自然的選擇。然而，在這方面的工作卻十分之有限。相比之下，涉及單個凸體的近似問題得到了大量的研究，並在過去一年中因本項目負責人和其他人的研究成果而取得顯著進展。單個凸體上的近似問題和多個凸體間接近度的近似問題有著豐富的聯系。因此，在本研究中，我們設計了一些高效的數據結構和算法。它們可以有效地找到凸體間接近度問題的近似解。

16214518.label: Realisation of objectives
16214518.value: We have successfully achieved the objectives of this project. There are a number of works that study how to solve computational problems approximately on a single convex polytope in d dimensions. In J1, we consider approximation in a context where multiple objects are involved. These problems arise in numerous applications such as motion planning, collision detection, and computer-aided design. Given an approximation parameter eps, we show how to independently preprocess a collection of convex polytopes so that each is associated with a data structure of size O(1 / eps^{(d-1)/2}) such that, given any two preprocessed polytopes A and B, it is possible to determine whether A and B intersect approximately. More generally, after this preprocessing we can answer this query even if A and B are independently modified through affine transformations. We also show how to approximate the Minkowski sum of two given polytopes, assuming they are represented as the intersection of n halfspaces. Our approximation runs in roughly O(n + 1 / eps^{(d-1)/2}) time. A surprising consequence of our results is that it allows us to approximate the width of a convex polytope in roughly O(n + 1 / eps^{(d-1)/2}) time. This is a major improvement over the previous best bound, halving the exponent in the eps-dependent term. Our algorithms and data structures for these problems are based on a data structure defined by a hierarchy of a Macbeath regions which answers approximate directional width queries efficiently. Given a point x in a convex body K, the Macbeath region M(x) is a maximal centrally symmetric convex shape centered at x and contained within K. Macbeath regions are fundamental to convex approximation and, consequently, to the research problems involving approximate proximity problems we are investigating in this grant. In spite of their obvious importance, there is still much that is unknown about Macbeath regions. In the context of convex approximation, the number of disjoint Macbeath regions that can be placed within distance eps of K's boundary is closely related to the complexity of approximating K. For a convex body of unit diameter, such a set is known to have size O(1 / eps^{(d-1)/2}). The volume distribution of such a set turns out to be a question of vital importance, but previously there were no non-trivial results on this. We obtain a volume-sensitive bound on the number of Macbeath regions, based on a new relationship between eps-width caps of a convex body and its polar [C1, C2, J2]. We then use this result to obtain an asymptotically optimal bound of O(1 / eps^{(d-1)/2}) on the total combinatorial complexity of approximating convex bodies, settling a problem that had been open for over 40 years [C1, J2]. As another consequence, we improve the dependency on dimension of the number of Macbeath regions from 2^{O(d log d)} to 2^{O(d)}, impacting the space and preprocessing time of all our data structures. Further, our techniques yield an optimal approximation of convex bodies with respect to the Banach-Mazur distance and a fast approximation algorithm for the closest vector problem that works in any norm [C2].

16214518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214518.value: We have developed algorithms for computing Minkowski sums and detecting intersection of convex bodies. As these problems are hard to solve exactly, we have considered approximations in our work. Our algorithms offer speedups for both single-shot and receptive-mode queries. We are writing up these results for journal publication [J1]. Our data structures are based on a data structure defined by a hierarchy of Macbeath regions. Our work has led to a much richer understanding of the properties of Macbeath regions, enabling us to reduce the space and preprocessing time of our data structures. Additionally, it has led to an optimal bound on the total combinatorial complexity of approximating convey bodies. We published this result in the Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA), 2020 [C1]. The best papers in this conference were invited to a special issue of the ACM Transactions on Algorithms (TALG); our paper received this honor and has been accepted for publication [J2]. Finally, in the coming month, we will be submitting our result on Macbeath-based coverings [C2] to the Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA), 2023.

16214518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214518.value: In the future, we will consider the problem of approximating the separation distance of the polytopes if they do not intersect, and approximating their penetration depth if they do. Another question we will consider, in the context of repetitive-mode queries, is whether it is possible to store approximations of the input polytopes in a way that all subsequent proximity queries are answered exactly with respect to these approximations. For many applications, it would be an advantage if each query is not just answered correctly in the approximate sense, but all queries are answered consistently with respect to the approximate polytopes fixed at the time of preprocessing.

16214518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214518.value: Problems involving the proximity of convex bodies are fundamental in many applications such as geometric packing and covering, geographic information systems, motion planning, and collision detection. These problems can be hard to solve exactly. In this project, we presented efficient approximate solutions for these problems.

16215018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215018.value: Strain hardening cementitious composites (SHCC) are a class of fiber reinforced materials exhibiting hardening behavior up to tensile strain of several percent, accompanied by the formation of fine multiple cracks with openings below 50 microns. With their excellent crack control ability, SHCC has great potential for enhancing the long-term durability of concrete structures. In conventional durability design, concrete mixes with low water/binder ratios and incorporation of pozzolans are used to control the resistance to water and chemical transport. However, once cracking occurs under service conditions (where crack width is allowed to reach 0.2mm or above for reinforced concrete structures), water/chemical transport is greatly accelerated. As SHCC limits the crack width to very small values, their transport properties are not significantly affected by tensile deformation. The use of SHCC can therefore ensure long-term durability of structures. To facilitate the practical implementation of this concept, a durability-based design guideline for SHCC needs to be developed. The objective of the proposed research program is to establish the scientific basis for developing such a guideline. The main goal is to develop a micromechanical model for predicting the relation between crack width and tensile strain at strain levels corresponding to service loading. With this model, micro-parameters such as fiber, matrix and interface properties as well as fiber size and volume can be selected to fulfil requirements regarding allowable crack width. One major challenge in developing the model is to quantify the variations of first cracking strength and crack width in various cross sections of SHCC, as these variations govern the formation of multiple cracks and their effects on water/chemical transport. Physically, such variations are governed by the variations of flaw size and fiber content within the SHCC, which are not yet fully understood. The proposed research tasks will therefore include: (i) studying the variations of flaw size and fiber number in SHCC with different compositions and fresh properties, and developing a suitable approach for modeling such variations; (ii) developing a new micromechanical model for predicting crack width vs. tensile strain, with proper consideration of the variations in cracking strength and fiber number, and (iii) verifying the applicability of the new micromechanical model for predicting the crack widths in SHCC through simulations and additional testing. Successful completion of this project will provide a systematic approach for designing SHCC with good crack control capability, which can enhance the durability and sustainability of concrete infrastructure.

16215018.label: Realisation of objectives
16215018.value: The three objectives of the proposed study have been fully achieved. For the first objective, we have studied the effect of various processing and material parameters on (i) the pore size and fiber distributions in the SHCC, and (ii) the tensile behavior of the SHCC. SHCC were prepared from mortar matrix with Marshall flow time ranging from 15s to 43s. The full tension stress versus strain behavior and the crack width versus strain relation were measured. Various sections were cut from both tested members and virgin members prepared from the same batch to obtain the distributions of pore size and fiber volume over the sections. To find the fiber volume, fluorescence microscopy was conducted to reveal the polymeric fibers. A machine learning approach was developed to automatically detect fibers from the image. SHCC with intermediate viscosity (flow time = 30s in our case) gives the best tensile performance. This finding is consistent with observations from microscopy. When viscosity is low (i.e. short flow time), there is insufficient shear stress to separate the fibers so the fiber dispersion is relatively poor (i.e., some fibers say as bundles). When the viscosity is too high, it is difficult for fibers (which are added to the top surface of mortar after it has been well-mixed) to distribute uniformly inside the SHCC. This will lead to high variation in fiber content among different sections. As a result, the tensile performance is degraded. A mixing process with part of the water and superplasticizer withheld and added later can lead to more uniform fiber and flaw distributions, and hence better tensile behavior. This is because a higher viscosity in the beginning facilitates the dispersion of fibers while a lower viscosity at the later stage (after all the water/SP are added) enables better fiber mixing. Based on experiments on mixes with different fiber content and fiber length, the optimal flow time is higher for longer fiber and higher fiber volume as higher viscosity is required to disperse the fibers properly. A micromechanical model for predicting the tensile stress versus strain relation and crack width versus strain relation has been developed in our previous work, based on assumed fiber and flaw size distributions. The second objective is to develop a new model for the tensile behavior of SHCC that accounts for the actual flaw size and fiber distributions resulting from different processing parameters. With this new development, the link between processing, microstructure and properties can be established. To relate the cracking strength of a section to the microstructure (which includes the flaw and fiber distributions), fracture mechanics analysis was carried out on the largest penny-shaped crack on a section, formed by intersection of pores on the section and with equivalent radius calculated from the intersected area. The calculated cracking strength was in agreement with test results if an effective fracture toughness (instead of the value measured from a notched member) was used. In existing micromechanical models, the fiber orientation is assumed to follow theoretical 2D and 3D distributions or the average between the two. Our experimental results indicate that such an assumption is not realistic as the fiber orientation in real tensile specimens is biased towards smaller angles. This is believed to be caused by a flattening effect during processing, because the height of SHCC piece added to the mold is often taller than the depth of the mold. The SHCC will have to flow sideways to fill the mold and this will lead to rotation of the fibers. By considering this effect, the calculated fiber angle distribution is much closer to the experimental value. In the literature, the uniformity of fiber distribution is often characterized by the dispersion coefficient obtained from the variation of fiber content in different regions of a single section. In this study, we conducted the first comprehensive study on the variation of fiber contents among different sections of the composite. With such a variation, the minimum fiber content among all sections was derived and found to be in very good correlation with the maximum tensile strength (which should be dominated by the section with the smallest number of fibers). On the other hand, the dispersion coefficient and maximum tensile strength do not show high correlation. To properly model SHCC behavior, the determination of fiber content distribution among different sections is hence very important. A new stochastic model for predicting the tensile behavior of SHCC is then proposed. Different to existing micromechanical models which employ assumed fiber and flaw size distributions, the experimentally determined distributions were employed. The effect of processing parameters (e.g., matrix flowabilities) on the distributions can hence be considered. As an additional enhancement, while conventional models assume internal flaws to be spherical (although micro-tomography reveals most flaws to be elliptical), a new method to account for the effect of ellipticity on cracking strength was proposed. For various micromechanical parameters, instead of simply assuming their mean values and variations, new fitting approaches were proposed based on statistics or mechanics to provide better estimation. The third objective is to use the new stochastic model to derive the tensile behavior as well as crack width development in SHCC specimens. Before the specimens were tested, X-ray micro-tomography was carried out to obtain the internal flaw size distribution. With the 3D distribution, the size of 2D flaws on each plane and the corresponding ellipticity of the flaws could be obtained. Knowing these parameters for the flaw, the fracture toughness was obtained from fitting of the measured first cracking strength. The fiber distribution was obtained from samples prepared from the same batch as the tensile specimens. Instead of assuming the interfacial friction, it was obtained from fitting of the maximum bridging stress provided by the fibers according to a micromechanical model. Using the stochastic model, the tensile stress vs strain relation was generated for SHCC with different flowabilities ranching from 19s to 48s. For each case, 20 simulations were carried out so the theoretical variation can be studied and compared to experimental results. The simulated and experimental curves were found to be within a similar range. Specifically, three key parameters, namely the strain capacity, the ultimate strength and the crack width at 0.5% strain (which is slightly beyond the serviceability state so it is a conservative value for durability design) are considered. The results correctly capture the trend of mean strain capacity and mean ultimate strength with flow time, but the variation is underestimated. A plausible explanation is the presence of large pores in some specimens, leading to significantly reduced fiber content which was not considered in the model. The particularly low strength and strain capacity of such specimens result in large variations. The modeling of crack width and its variation is a very challenging task but the stochastic model was able to predict a range of crack width that is very similar to the test results. However, the distribution tends to be clustered at lower values in comparison to the experimental results. This may be due to the limit of the photographic technique for crack detection. Only the larger cracks that have been fully developed on the surface can be observed while small cracks are ignored, so the crack size is biased toward a larger value.

16215018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215018.value: Among the many findings of the project, the following can be highlighted. (1) There exists an optimal flowability of the mortar to achieve the best SHCC performance. By fitting the experimental tensile curves with a conventional micromechanical model based on assumed flaw size distributions, the mean and deviation of flaw size are found to be consistent with physical intuition. The results provide preliminary understanding of the processing-microstructure-properties relation in SHCC. Details can be found in the first conference paper in Section C. (2) The first cracking strength of a section in the SHCC is conventionally derived by assuming the presence of penny-shaped cracks in the material to simplify the analysis. We found that such as approach can provide good results as long as an effective fracture toughness (instead of the value obtained from testing of a notched member) is employed. This finding is of practical significance as simplified analysis can be carried out once the effective fracture toughness is obtained from a proper fitting method. Details can be found in the first journal paper in Section C. (3) In the interpretation of laboratory-determined tensile behaviors, fibers are usually assumed to be randomly oriented. In this project, a deep learning-based image processing workflow for obtaining fiber orientation distribution over the whole section is developed. The experimentally obtained fiber orientation distribution in PVA-SHCC tensile samples was found to differ significantly from the random distribution, and it can be derived by considering the flattening effect of fresh material during the processing. This work (which is presented in the second journal paper in Section C) enables the proper interpretation of the results from small laboratory specimens and the extrapolation of results to larger structural members. (4) The uniformity of fiber distribution has a large effect on SHCC behavior. Conventionally, fiber uniformity is studied with a dispersion coefficient derived from the number of fibers in different parts of a single section. We found that the variation of fiber content among different sections has higher correlation with SHCC behavior and should therefore be measured instead. Details are in the third journal paper in Section C). (5) Based on the measured pore and fiber distributions in SHCC specimens, a new stochastic model (presented in the fourth journal paper in Section C) was developed and the predicted strength, strain capacity and crack development for SHCC with matrix exhibiting different flow properties are in good agreement with test results.

16215018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215018.value: The completed project established an approach to relate material processing to fiber and flaw size distributions in SHCC and then to material properties. The current study only covered normal casting process and is limited to laboratory specimens. A logical step is to extend it to other processing methods, such as 3D printing and spraying which will lead to different fiber distribution and flaw sizes. Also, as fiber distribution is affected by boundary effect and flattening effect (which occur when material flows with reduced thickness), the size of specimen and the way it is prepared are factors that should be further studied. To complement experimental work, computational analysis can also be carried out at two levels. At the continuum level, the flow direction and velocity of fresh SHCC under various processing conditions are derived. With this information, the rotation and alignment of fibers can be studied through discrete element methods. The combined experimental/numerical study would facilitate the development of a new SHCC design framework which can provide guidelines for optimizing both the material constituents and processing parameters to achieve specific performance requirements. We plan to prepare a RGC GRF proposal or RGC-NSFC proposal for this study in the coming years.

16215018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215018.value: With high energy absorption and excellent crack control ability, strain hardening cementitious composites (SHCC) have high potential for enhancing the resilience and durability of concrete structures. To facilitate the design of SHCC for various applications, micromechanical models have been developed to relate material/structural behavior to properties of the fiber, matrix and fiber/matrix interface as well as fiber size, geometry and volume. SHCC performance is also significantly affected by the fiber and pore size distributions inside the composite, but these distributions are assumed in existing models without experimental verification. To address this research gap, a comprehensive study was carried out to study the effect of material processing on the pore size and fiber distributions and the use of measured (rather than assumed) distributions in the micromechanical modelling of SHCC behavior. The fiber and pore size distributions are found to be governed by the sample preparation process and matrix flow properties respectively. Using the measured distributions, the predicted tensile stress vs strain relation of SHCC is found to be in good agreement with test results. The results of this study lay the groundwork for developing a framework for optimizing SHCC performance through the proper selection of both material constituents and processing parameters.

16215218.value: Superelastic nanocrystalline NiTi plates with well controlled grain size (GS), volume fractions and textures of B2 and B19’ will be fabricated by cold rolling and annealing. 16215218.label: Realisation of objectives
16215218.value: We overcame many difficulties during the project period in the performing research (e.g., material processing, sample preparation, microstructural characterization and macroscopic property testing, as well as attending conferences) during the societal unrest in 2019 and during the COVID pandemic period of 2020-2022 in Hong Kong. The project objectives are eventually realized through the following three parts of the research works. In the first part, we successfully fabricated superelastic nanocrystalline NiTi plates with well controlled grain size (GS), volume fractions and textures of B2 and B19' phases by controlled cold rolling and annealing. The temperature dependence of the elastic modulus of the cold rolled plates are characterized and modeled. In the second part, we successfully identified the key fabrication parameters and the resulting microstructure factors such as initial phase, temperature and direction of rolling, thickness reduction, grain size and texture. The impacts of these fabrication parameters on the obtained microstructures are revealed. In the third part, we performed mechanism-based simple modelling and estimation to understand and to get insight into the obtained Elinvar, Invar and Rinvar properties of the novel superelastic NiTi alloys.
