16215218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215218.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized as the following two aspects. (1) We have tailored the temperature dependence of elastic modulus (TDEM) of polycrystalline NiTi plates by cold rolling up to 60% thickness reduction. In-plane Elinvar property is obtained with a low elastic modulus temperature coefficient of 6.0 × 10−5 K−1 over a temperature range of 192 K. It is found that the microstructure mainly consists of approximately equal volume fractions of {111}-oriented B2 and {102}-oriented B19 nanocrystals of high thermal stability due to defect pinning and grain refinement. The opposite TDEMs of the two phases can compensate each other and cause the Elinvar behavior. Such mechanism can also be used to obtain Elinvar property for other shape memory alloys. One paper is published in Scripta Materialia. (2) We have successfully fabricated a multifunctional NiTi alloy with Invar (dimension-invariant), Elinvar (elastic modulus-invariant) and Rinvar (resistivity-invariant) properties over the temperature range from 125 K to 375 K through cold rolling of 60% thickness reduction. It is found that the underlying microstructure of such multifunctional NiTi alloy mainly consists of B2 and B19′ nanocrystals which can continuously undergo a small fraction of thermally induced B2↔B19′ phase transition over a wide temperature range. Such phase transition can induce a negative thermal expansion to compensate for the positive expansions of the B2 and B19′ phases and thus yield the Invar property. Meanwhile, the opposite temperature dependences of elastic modulus of the B2 and B19′ phases can compensate each other and cause the macroscopic overall Elinvar property. In addition, the presence of nanocrystals enhances the negative temperature dependence of resistivity (TDR) caused by boundary scattering, which compensates for the positive TDR due to background scattering and thus leads to the Rinvar behavior. It is expected that the three compensation mechanisms in the dual-phase nanostructure can also be exploited in other shape memory alloys to obtain the Invar, Elinvar and Rinvar properties so as to broaden their applications. One paper is published in Journal of Alloys and Compounds.

16215218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215218.value: The project is motivated by the scientific and practical importance of developing novel NiTi SMA materials with unique combination of Invar, Elinvar, Rinvar and large linear superelasticity using Material-by-Design approach. The results of this project open a way to achieve novel temperature independent SMA materials for niched applications.

16215218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215218.value: Elastic constants or elastic tensors are fundamental properties of matters and play important roles in behavior and performance of materials. For NiTi shape memory alloys (SMAs), the elastic constants of austenite (cubic B2) and of martensite (monoclinic B19') crystals intrinsically depend on temperature but with opposite trends near the phase transition point. The overall macroscopic Youngs modulus of a NiTi polycrystal thus has V-shaped variation with the temperature. Such strong temperature sensitive elastic property of SMAs can often be a significant problem for devices that work under temperature variation. This project successfully tailored the temperature dependence of the macroscopic Youngs modulus of NiTi by nanostructure hierarchical design and control. Novel fabrication method is developed and mechanism-based modelling framework is established to achieve the project objectives. Cold rolled NiTi plates with well controlled grain size (GS), volume fractions and textures of B2 and B19' is fabricated. Key fabrication parameters and the resulting microstructure factors such as initial phase, direction of rolling, thickness reduction, grain size and texture are identified. The project is motivated by the scientific and practical importance of developing novel NiTi alloys with unique combination of Invar, Elinvar and large linear superelasticity using Material-by-Design approach.

16215618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215618.value: Chlorine is commonly used in disinfection processes in water and wastewater treatment plants. At the Stonecutters Island Sewage Treatment Works (SCISTW) under the Hong Kong Harbour Area Treatment Scheme (HATS), sodium hypochlorite solution at a high concentration (10%) is discharged into primary treated effluent in the form of multiple turbulent dense jets to achieve the intended mixing effect. The organic (nitrogenous) compounds in the treated effluent react with chlorine at a rate critically dependent on the local chlorine concentration. Given the importance of sewage disinfection to treatment performance and environmental impact, it is vital to understand the mixing of chemically reacting dense chlorine jets. When a chlorine jet is discharged into an ambient flow of treated effluent, the chlorine concentration in the jet decreases rapidly with distance from the source due to (i) turbulent entrainment with the surrounding fluid; and (ii) chemical reaction with the chlorine-demanding substances in the effluent. Recent field experience has shown that significant chlorine demand can take place within a short distance (in the order of a meter or several seconds of travel time) downstream of the dosing point. It is of fundamental value to study the physical-chemical chlorination process at a high chlorine concentration in the initial jet mixing region. The proposed research will comprise systematic experiments involving the mixing of a dense, chemically reacting chlorine jet discharged into a treated sewage flow. The experiments will be performed in a unique field scale experimental flume inside the treatment plant (SCISTW). Real primary treated effluent and chlorine solution from the sewage works will be used. The experiments will be designed to simulate chlorine jets over a wide range of jet to ambient flow velocity ratios. The cross-sectional distributions of total residual chlorine, organic, ammonia and nitrate nitrogen, sulphide and Escherichia coli concentrations will be measured at key locations in the near field of the jet. The resulting water quality data will be used to develop a chlorine jet model that accounts for both the turbulent dense jet mixing with the crossflow and local chlorine consumption by sewage organics. This research will build on existing extensive site-specific physical model studies of chlorine jets in sewage flows. The findings will aid in chlorine dosage optimization for water and wastewater treatment operations in Hong Kong and worldwide. 氯常用於水和污水處理的消毒過程。在香港淨化海港計劃(HATS)下的昂船洲污水處理廠(SCISTW)，高濃度（10％）的次氯酸鈉溶液以多股重射流的形式排入經初級處理的污水中，以達到預期的混合效果。污水的有機（氮）化合物與氯的反應率主要取決於氯濃度。鑑於消毒在污水處理的重要性和對環境的影響，了解氯射流與污水的混合和化學反應十分重要。 當氯溶液以重射流的形式排放到經處理的污水中時，與周圍流體產生湍流卷吸。氯與污水中的氮化物產生化學反應，射流中的氯濃度隨著距離迅速減少。現場觀測表明，距離排放點下游大約一米內可以產生顯著的氯消耗。因此，在射流初始混合區域內高濃度氯的物理和化學反應過程極具基礎研究價值。 本項目建立在廣泛現場物理模型研究的基礎上，以系統性實驗，研究氯射流在污水中的混合和化學反應。實驗將在污水處理廠(SCISTW)內獨特的現場規模的水槽中進行，使用經初級處理的污水和氯溶液，模擬不同射流與環境流速的比例。在射流近場的關鍵位置測量總殘餘氯、有機物、氨氮、硝酸鹽、硫化物和大腸桿菌濃度的橫截面分佈。測得的水質數據將用於開發數學模型，以預測氯射流與污水的湍流混合下，污水中氮化合物對氯的消耗。研究結果將有助於優化香港以至全球水和廢水處理的氯劑量。

16215618.label: Realisation of objectives
16215618.value: We carried out a series of experiments of the chlorine jet of different source concentrations (100-100,000 mg/L) discharging into ammonia solution and Chemically-Enhanced Primary Treatment (CEPT) effluent flow in stagnant and coflowing conditions. The Total Residual Chlorine (TRC) concentrations and ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) concentrations of the jet flow are measured at various positions in the jet flow. A theoretical jet model is developed based on the reaction mechanisms between the dosed chlorine and the ammonia and organic matters entrained from the ambient sewage effluent. A. Experiments of chlorine jet discharging in stagnant CEPT effluent and integral jet model of reacting chlorine jet (Yang et al. 2019). The structure of a chlorine jet in stagnant treated primary effluent is measured for the first time. A mathematical model for a reacting chlorine jet with ammonia nitrogen in CEPT effluent has been developed to predict the mixing and chlorine demand accounting for the fast stoichiometric reaction between chlorine and ammonia nitrogen. The stoichiometric mass reaction ratio is determined from extensive measurements of jet centerline TRC. The model is validated against laboratory experiments of chlorine jet discharging into stagnant ammonia solution and CEPT effluent. The following can be concluded: - The cross sectional TRC concentration profiles of chlorine jet in sewage are self-similar and can be well-approximated by Gaussian profiles. The spreading of chlorine jet is not significantly affected by chemical reaction. - Based on experiments of chlorine jet discharging in NH3-N solution, the overall stoichiometric reaction ratio of chlorine to ammonia nitrogen at the jet centerline under dynamic jet mixing process is 7.48, very close to the theoretical value of 7.6. - Significant chlorine demand can occur within a short distance in the order of 0.1 m (or travel time in the order of a second or less) from the dosing point due to the turbulent entrainment and reaction. In CEPT effluent, the chlorine consumption depends on the corresponding local TRC concentration. The chlorine consumption increases with higher TRC concentration. At a low TRC concentration (TRC < 2000 mg/L), the chlorine demand of CEPT sewage is mainly due to ammonia nitrogen (>60% contribution). At a high TRC concentration (>2000 mg/L), the oxidation of complex organic compounds contributes to about 2/3 of the overall chlorine consumption. B. Experiments of chlorine jet discharging in coflowing CEPT effluent (Qiao et al. 2019; Chan et al. 2020; Qiao et al. 2021) 1) Bench scale flume experiments A flume model was set up to observe the kinetics of exertion of the chlorine demand when concentrated chlorine is added into an ammonia water flow and CEPT sewage flow. The bench-scale model mainly consisted of a transparent test flume 0.015 m width with ambient flow supplied from a stock tank. The chlorine jet was fed from a constant head tank, and discharged into the coflow (velocity about 0.1 m/s) through a stainless steel nozzle of 4 mm inner diameter. The kinetics of the breakpoint reaction between dosed free chlorine and entrained ammonia was investigated using ammonia solution of 30 mg/L. When the jet source chlorine concentration is less than 800 mg/L, the test results show that there is no loss of the chlorine mass flux in the mixing process. When the source concentration increases to 10,000 mg/L, about 10% of the dosed chlorine has disappeared in the mixing process on a time scale of several seconds. Based on the flume experiment results, a two-step breakpoint reaction mechanism in the mixing process is proposed: 1) At low hypochlorite concentration, hypochlorite ions react with ammonia ions to form combined chlorine (mainly monochloramine NH2Cl), causing no residual chlorine loss; 2) for high hypochlorite concentration, the breakpoint reaction forms nitrogen gas and chloride ions, causing the chlorine loss. These results unravel the kinetic characteristics of chlorine jet mixing with ammonia water flow, and provide the data set for calibration of the kinetic model of the breakpoint chlorination. The flume model was relocated in the Stonecutters Island Sewage Treatment Work (SCISTW) for experiments using CEPT effluent of NH3-N concentration ~30 mg/L and total organic carbon (TOC) of ~50 mg/L. The test results show that even at source chlorine concentration of 800 mg/L, nearly half of the dosed chlorine mass flux has been consumed in the mixing process. Similar chlorine consumption features are confirmed by the tests with high source concentration of 5,000 mg/L. As compared to the ammonia water flow tests at the same source concentration, it is justified that the organic debris accounts for most of the chlorine demand. A simplified organic reaction model is proposed to account for the overall chlorine reaction with TOC in the mixing process. 2) Field scale model tests The purpose of the field scale physical model experiments inside the Stonecutters Island Sewage Treatment Works (SCISTW) is to study the mixing and reaction of a chlorine jet with CEPT treated sewage effluent very close to the dosing position to confirm the reaction mechanism proposed (Qiao et al. 2021). Fresh CEPT effluent is pumped into the field-scale model from a neighboring sedimentation tank. A broad crest weir is installed in the flume. The 10% sodium hypochlorite solution (density=1.2 g/mL) is discharged in vertically downward direction or in horizontal direction via a round nozzle of 10 mm diameter into the sewage flow. The excess momentum flux of the chlorine jet is dissipated quickly very near the source; the buoyant chlorine jet behaves as a linear advected thermal. Due to the social unrest in July-November 2019 and the outbreak of COVID-19 in February 2020 (SCISTW prohibited our researchers to work there for health and safety reasons since the beginning of 2020), only one series of experiments of dosing concentrated chlorine in high-speed sewage effluent flow was carried out from October 2019 to May 2020. Nevertheless, the high-speed sewage flow environment provided by the physical model yielded useful results. The TRC and NH3-N concentration profiles are measured at different distances from nozzle with aid of 2-D traverse, using standard chemical measurement method. The chlorine and ammonia nitrogen mass flux of the jet flow are evaluated. The model tests show that the mass flux of the residual chlorine decreases rapidly with a contact time of less than 0.1 s. The near full scale experiments reveal the rapid consumption of reacting chlorine in extremely short contact time of 0.1 s in wastewater stream near the dosing position in a crossflow for the first time. The experiments further confirmed that the organic reaction is responsible for most of the chlorine demand in the jet mixing process, consistent with the small flume test results. C. Theoretical modeling of reacting chlorine jet Based on the test results above, a theoretical model is developed to compute the concentration of four reactants in the jet flow including OCl-, NH2Cl, NH4+ and TOC as a function of the distance from the source, accounting for the jet mixing in cross flow and chemical kinetics. The predictions of the theoretical model for the ammonia water flow and sewage flow cases agree well with the measurements accordingly. Overall, from these extensive experimental works, we have obtained a better understanding of the chemical kinetics of chlorine jet near the dosing position for disinfecting CEPT sewage effluent. This has led to significant impact for the chlorine disinfection operation of the Harbour Area Treatment Scheme.

16215618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215618.value: Extensive experiments have been carried out to study reacting chlorine jet mixing with the ammonia water and CEPT effluent in stagnant and coflowing conditions, using bench-scale models and a near full-scale physical model in SCISTW. The TRC and ammonia nitrogen concentration distributions in the near field of the chlorine jet are measured under a series of different parameters (source concentration, jet flow rate, coflowing jet or cross-flow jet and sewage quality). The results provide the basis to develop a theoretical integral jet model for a reacting chlorine jet, and the measured data set is used to calibrate the rate constants of the chemical reactions proceeding in the mixing process: 1) The exertion of the chlorine takes place in a very short distance from the jet source on time scale of one second. 2) The breakpoint reaction can occur in the region near the source due to relatively small proportion of the ammonia nitrogen entrained from ambient sewage effluent into the chlorine jets. In principle, the chlorine consumption by the breakpoint reaction is limited. Most of the entrained ammonia is used to convert the free chlorine into the combined chlorine rather than to be oxidized to nitrogen gas. 3) The organic reaction accounts for most of the chlorine demand in the mixing process with CEPT sewage effluent. Organic particulates in the sewage effluent can be readily oxidized by the high concentration chlorine. 4) The field-scale experiments further show that the most of the chlorine demand takes place rapidly - within a time scale in the order of one second or less in high-speed sewage flow. To control the chlorine demand, the key is to decrease the time of exposure of sewage to high concentration chlorine near the source (Lee et al. 2019 (Conference Paper 1) and 2021 (Journal Paper 3)). The implementation of this idea can be achieved with our knowledge of turbulent jet mixing in a crossflow. The main research outcomes: 1) A theoretical reacting jet reaction model is incorporated into the VISJET model to compute the concentrations of four reactants along the jet flow. 2) The mechanism of the chlorine reactions in the mixing process is applied to optimize the chlorine dosage at the SCISTW. The proposed dosing approach has been adopted at SCISTW and the in-plant tests show that it can reduce the chlorine demand in the FDC significantly in field condition (Lee et al. 2019, Conference Paper 1)) and save much chemical costs for the disinfection operation. 3) One journal paper and four conference papers published; two journal papers to be submitted (see Section C).

16215618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215618.value: Based on extensive experiments of reacting chlorine jet mixing with ammonia water and CEPT sewage flow, we have better understood the reaction mechanisms of reacting chlorine jet to design new dosing approach to decrease the exertion of the chlorine demand in the mixing process. Yet due to the complexity of organic compounds in the primary treated sewage, the chemical nature of participating organic matter remains much unknown. It is proposed to carry out the following research work: 1. To further study the chemical nature of the organic reaction causing chlorine loss. Currently over 50% of the dosed chlorine has disappeared in the mixing process even with improved jet mixing efficiency. Only after having the knowledge of such oxidizable matters in the sewage effluent, additional steps could be adopted to fundamentally solve the chlorine loss problem in initial mixing stage. 2. To study automatic control mechanism for chlorine dosage. A closed-loop automatic control system is currently applied to control the dosage in SCISTW. Due to the significant time lag between the dosage change and responding TRC change at the end of chlorination, the control system tends to result in undesirable large oscillations in dosage and TRC, and its performance largely depends on operator experience. Artificial intelligence–based control methods can be investigated to improve the control process.

16215618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215618.value: Chlorine is commonly used in disinfection processes in wastewater treatment plants. The chlorine solution is typically dosed by turbulent mixing; the chlorine reacts with the inorganic and organic nitrogenous compounds at a fast rate (in the order of 0.1 second). A significant portion of the dosed chlorine can be rapidly consumed by the reactions instead of destroying the pathogens – a waste of chemicals and energy. Despite decades of use of chlorine for sewage disinfection, the interaction of turbulent mixing with chlorine consumption in the complex sewage remains an elusive problem. We carried out comprehensive laboratory and field scale experiments to understand the rapid chemical reactions of the chlorine jet into sewage flow. A theoretical integral jet model is developed to simulate the chlorine reactions under different mixing conditions. The insights obtained has led to a proposal to optimize chlorine disinfection operations that has been applied in practice in the Stonecutter’s Island Sewage Treatment Works (serving a population of 5.7 million) with significant savings in chemicals, energy, and reducing the harmful effect of chlorine to the environment.

16215718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215718.value: We propose a novel multi-pronged attack on the representation learning problem of category formation in transduction grammar induction via simultaneous tree-structured and neural approaches to machine translation. Despite significant recent advances in machine learning for natural language interpretation and translation, especially using deep learning approaches, current models still lack a strong enough sense of correct versus incorrect syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic structure — due to the (1) lack of explicit structure in implicit representations, (2) insufficient use of biases from linguistic sources, and (3) difficulty of significantly expanding and guiding search within tractable training complexity. To tackle these problems, our new approach combines significant strengths across three previously unintegrated modeling techniques: (1) new architectures for gated generative bilingual recursive neural networks, (2) integration of symbolic biases from semantic frames and language translation universals, and (3) forest based deep learning for combinatorial hypothesis expansion with controlled search complexity. Because our approach combines explicit symbolic structure with distributed concept representations, the models’ performance on learning representations can be evaluated not only via extrinsic end-to-end task-based measures such as machine translation accuracy, but also on intrinsic knowledge acquisition oriented model-based measures such as parse tree, grammar rule induction, or category formation accuracy. 对于如何在翻译语法的学习过程中，进行类别学习的问题，我们通过同时探索树状结构模型和神经网络模型，提出了全新的多角度解决方案。 尽管在自然语言理解领域，尤其是神经网络相关方面，近年来进展颇丰， 现有的模型在正确地辨别语法、语义及实际含义上依然不尽人意。这是因为—— (1) 在模型的数据结构中，缺少明确的语义结构， (2) 语言学特征被不当使用， 以及(3)对于如在大范围准确搜索，缺乏可行的训练方案。 为了解决以上问题，我们的这项研究创新地结合了3种建模方案的长处。 (1)全新的门控生成型双语递归网络， (2)将语义框架和语言翻译普遍性结合， 以及(3)可以在有限的复杂度内完成的，基于丛林深度学习的大范围准确搜索方案。 因为我们的方案结合了明晰的的结构式表示和模糊的分布式表示。 所以在学习的过程中，不但可以利用诸如翻译准确度等评分进行端对端指引， 亦可以利用更为详尽的结构式知识进行指引，例如语法树、语法推断准确度和类别形成准确度。

16215718.label: Realisation of objectives
16215718.value: Inversion transduction grammars (ITGs) are capable of symbolically representing a transduction relationship with much more explanatory power compared to mainstream neural network approaches. However inducing ITGs from parallel corpora still remains a challenging problem, with the main bottleneck lying in nonterminal category induction. The main obstacle is that the space of possible ITG rules grows exponentially with the category size, making symbolic search infeasible. Later TRAAM models showed the possibility of hypothesizing useful categories with the help of the recursive neural network, but the quality of the produced categories were far from ideal. In this work we discovered that TRAAM suffers from vanishing gradient problems, and that the self-reconstruction training objective of TRAAM does not align well with bilingual categories. For vanishing gradient problems, most mainstream training methods for LSTM, GRU, skip connections and gated linear units either require sequential input topologies or have unbounded output range, and thus cannot be used for with TRAAM. In this project we developed a new recursive network architecture that overcomes the problems. For training objectives, we found that context-aware objectives is better suited than self-reconstruction objectives. Among common context-aware objectives, sibling token prediction can be more easily generalized to work with biparse trees than autoaggressive objectives used in GPT or sibling sentence prediction objectives used in BERT. Another major advance of this work tackles the problem that even with our improved method to hypothesize bilingual categories, inducing a categorized ITG still remains challenging because TRAAM based bilingual category hinting relies on high quality biparse tree topologies, whereas high quality biparse tree topologies relies on high quality categorized ITG. We solved this chicken-and-egg problem by developing a new training pipeline that co-trains both the categorized ITG and our improved TRAAM.

16215718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215718.value: We have developed new inversion transduction grammar (ITG) induction methods that avoid the computational complexity of generating bilingual categories with the help of recursive neural network. Inducing ITGs with good differentiated nonterminal categories has long been a challenging problem because of the computation complexity of evaluating ITG rule hypotheses for different bilingual categories. Our new methods differ significantly from sequential attention-based models, which are more traditionally found in neural machine translation in three aspects. First, our model is enforcing compositional constraints. Second, our model has a much smaller search space in terms of discovering bilingual relationships from bilingual sentence pairs. Third, the end product of our model is an ITG, which is a much more transparent and interpretable representation of bilingual relationship when compared to a black box neural network. Our recursive neural network improved upon TRAAM, solving its vanishing gradient problem and mismatched training objectives. We developed a solution to the vanishing gradient problem by designing a new own network architecture based on Mixture of Experts, rather than using a mainstream solution like LSTM, GRU, skip connection or gated linear unit because they either only work with sequential input topologies or have unbounded output range. Our experiments showed that the quality of induced bilingual categories improves significantly after solving vanishing gradient problem. For training objective, we analyzed theoretically and verified empirically that using a context-based objective produces contextually more appropriate bilingual categories than using a self-reconstruction objective as in TRAAM. We chose to use a sibling token prediction objective, which is a very simple but effective objective. Other context-based objectives like autoaggresive ones or sibling sentence prediction task do exist but cannot be applied to work with biconstituents. We also introduced a new training pipeline called a feedback training pipeline, that co-trains both the categorized ITG and our improved TRAAM. Our training pipeline solves the chicken-and-egg problem in which TRAAM based bilingual category hinting relies on high quality biparse tree topologies, but high quality biparse tree topologies relies on high quality categorized ITG. Our feedback training pipeline integrates our improved TRAAM training with symbolic ITG induction algorithm, incrementally refining both the neural network and the ITG at the same time. A significant amount of new architectural work has been done since mainstream deep learning frameworks like Tensorflow and Pytorch lack the flexibility needed for the fine integration of neural and symbolic methods.

16215718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215718.value: Future work will incorporate this into training of larger models upon larger datasets. We also envision applying this to other tasks in which the frame structure of the input and/or output is central to the task, as the explicit compositional structures in our model allow for direct application of structural constraints.

16215718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215718.value: We have shown that by combining recursive neural network and symbolic ITG biparsing algorithm, bilingual categories and biparse tree topologies can be effectively and efficiently induced from a word-aligned ITG-generated corpus. This research is also an advancement in explainable deep learning research, indicating that it is possible to make a neural network explainable, and to make the error analysis transparent, by combining the neural network with symbolic machine learning algorithms.

16215818.value: 與大多數半導體器件類似，半個多世紀以來，電力電子一直由矽基功率器件占主導地位。如今，大多數Si器件技術已接近成熟，器件性能基本上受材料特性的限制。電力系統的效率，佔地面積和功能的進一步改進將強烈依賴於由具有固有優勢的其他材料製成的功率器件。受益於更大的能帶隙，更高的電子遷移率和臨界電場，基於III族氮化物的功率器件脫穎而出，並且明顯優於最先進的Si對應物。特別地，基於GaN的高電子遷移率晶體管（HEMT）已經證明了用於功率開關應用的優異性能。在過去十年中，器件物理和技術取得了巨大進步，導致GaN功率晶體管在實際應用中迅速商業化。然而，進入已經成熟數十年的矽基功率器件領域仍然具有挑戰性，不斷開發成本更低，效率更高，更可靠的元件。使電路設計者更優選的常關E模式設備的解決方案仍存在問題。它們要么採用Si元件級聯，要么採用p型柵極，但都不是理想的解決方案。由於各種原因，在九十年代試圖提供具有小占地面積和速度的優點的類似於雙極結型晶體管（BJT）的垂直結構。結合NMOSFET的優異特性和垂直配置，垂直GaN基NMOSFET可能是最終可行的解決方案。傳統Si MOSFET中的雪崩擊穿能力可以在垂直GaN MOSFET中獲得，以及具有高閾值電壓的常關特性。還允許大門擺動和高電流操作（> 100 A）。 在我們的實驗室中，我們在過去十年中為LED和晶體管開發了非常高品質的 GaN技術。這些器件的結晶質量已通過各種材料表徵技術得到驗證，並通過出色的器件性能得到證明。我們還展示了單片集成的GaN基晶體管和LED，以實現一種新穎的三端電壓控制LED（HEMT-LED），其可以比分立LED更高的頻率進行調製。利用我們的內部增長能力，我們開發了選擇性生長的漏極/源極和原位SiN柵極，用於高性能GaN基橫向晶體管。在這個項目中，我們提出了一種新型的Si基GaN結構的垂直結構，帶有用於開關應用的溝槽柵極。溝槽柵極結構和垂直側壁溝道將通過乾蝕刻形成。為了調節擊穿電壓，可以在n-GaN體和n-GaN漏極之間插入輕摻雜的n-GaN漂移層。在矽上成功開發這種垂直晶體管將允許GaN晶體管的低成本和批量製造，以用於未來的集成電源電路和系統。

16215818.value: We GaN quasi-vertical trench MOSFETs grown on 6-inch Si substrates. The device with single-trench design shows a specific ON-resistance of 0.84 mΩ·cm2, a maximum drain current density of 5.0 kA/cm2, and a breakdown voltage of 320 V, after fine tuning of the channel doping and employment of a thick bottom dielectric process. 16215818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215818.value: Lower leakage current and higher breakdown voltage can be achieved by: (1)introducing a thicker drift layer with lower Si doping; (2) optimizing the edge-terminal near the mesa region; (3) optimizing gate trench etching, gate dielectric deposition and thick bottom dielectric processes to achieve a more stable gate MOS stack; (4) optimizing GaN-on-Si buffers to reduce the dislocation density. Stable gate MOS stack for avoiding drain-to-gate hard breakdown, combined with high-quality epilayers with low dislocation density and advanced edge-termination techniques are critical to achieve avalanche capability in GaN-on-Si vertical trench MOSFETs.

16215818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215818.value: Vertical GaN transistors are attracting extensive attentions in high voltage with breakdown voltage applications. Because of the vertical topology, a higher breakdown can be effectuated by introducing a thicker drift layer without increasing the device area. In the past decade, high-performance GaN vertical transistors, including current aperture vertical electron transistors, fin power FETs, and trench MOSFETs have been demonstrated. Compared with other types of vertical transistors, GaN trench MOSFETs have advantages of simpler fabrication process and larger Vth. High-performance GaN trench MOSFETs with VBR over 1 kV have been successfully demonstrated based on bulk GaN substrates. However, the high-cost and limited size of low-defect-density GaN substrates has limited the scaling of volume production. As a more cost-effective platform, GaN-on-Si has been explored for GaN vertical device. Recently, quasi- and fully-vertical GaN trench MOSFETs with large Vth have been reported on Si substrate. The reported GaN-on-Si trench MOSFETs showed relevantly high specific ON-resistance. We report GaN-based quasi-vertical trench gate MOSFETs on cost-effective Si substrate with ON-current exceeding 1 A. The best device with single-trench design shows a low RON,sp of 0.84 mΩ·cm2, a high maximum drain current density (ID,max) of 5.0 kA/cm2, a high Vth of 5.3 V (at ID = 1 A/cm2) and a VBR of 320 V, after fine tuning of the channel doping and adoption of a thick bottom dielectric process. The fabricated large-area (~0.54 mm2) device with multiple-finger design presents a maximum drain current of 1.1 A.

16300018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300018.value: The Ricci flow is a central topic in differential geometry. It was used by Hamilton-Perelman to resolve the long-standing Poincare conjecture. In Hamilton-Perelman's approach, the analysis of singularity development forms a substantial part in the resolution of the Poincare conjecture and many other related problems. Singularity develops when the curvature of a Ricci flow blows up, so it is crucial to understand at what rate and on what region it does so. In this proposed study the PI and his collaborators will analyze the curvature blow-ups of the Ricci flow on compact Kahler manifolds (i.e. Kahler-Ricci flow) in the cases of both finite-time and infinite-time singularities. In case of finite-time singularities, the Riemann curvature must blow up in finite time by a classic result due to Hamilton, yet there are still many questions concerning at what rates it blows up in the case of Kahler-Ricci flows. For infinite-time singularities, the Riemann curvature may not blow up, and whether it will be or not depends very much on the topology. The PI and his collaborators will deepen the understanding of the analysis of the Riemann curvature for long-time solutions of the Kahler-Ricci flow. We will address questions such as whether the set of points on which the curvature blows up also depends only on the topology. It is expected that the research outcomes will further advance the knowledge about the singularity development of the Kahler-Ricci flow, and will constitute steady progress toward a deeper understanding of some important and central issues involved. The subject to be investigated lies at the interface of differential geometry, partial differential equations, and algebraic geometry. 瑞奇流 (Ricci flow) 是當代微分幾何的重要課題之一，他被Hamilton及Perelman用作解決龐卡萊猜想(Poincaré Conjecture)。在分析瑞奇流的奇異點的問題中，我們需要掌握其曲率的變化和奇異性。 在這個研究項目中，我們會關注瑞奇流在凱勒流形(Kähler manifolds)中有關的曲率問題。過去的研究成果指出，曲率的奇異性（例如在那裹變得奇異和變化的速度等問題）和流形的拓撲結構有很密切的關係。我們會對這些關於曲率和拓撲的關係作出深入的研究，和對過去的結果推廣。

16300018.label: Realisation of objectives
16300018.value: Objectives 1 and 2 have been well addressed in my paper with Yashan Zhang "Local Curvature Estimates of Long-Time Solutions to the Kahler-Ricci Flow", published by Advances in Mathematics. In the paper, we proved that the set of singular fibers on which the Riemann curvature blows up is independent of the choice of the initial Kahler metric -- addressing Objective 1 -- and we also determined the exact blow up rates near any regular fiber, and hence addressing Objective 2. We also proved some related results in the paper "Higher-order Estimates of Long-Time Solutions to the Kahler-Ricci Flow", jointly written with Man-Chun Lee and published by Journal of Functional Analysis. In the paper, we proved the smooth convergence of the metric on the regular set when the fibers are biholomorphic, hence also estimating the Ricci curvature bound on the regular fibers. Objective 3 has been addressed by my MPhil student's (FUNG Cheuk Yan) thesis. He proved a convergence result about the Ricci curvature when the Kodaira dimension is 1.

16300018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300018.value: In the paper "Local curvature estimates of long-time solutions to the Kähler-Ricci flow", jointly written with Yashan Zhang, published in Advance in Mathematics, we study the local curvature estimates of long-time solutions to the normalized Kähler-Ricci flow on compact Kähler manifolds with semi-ample canonical line bundle. Using these estimates, we prove that on such a manifold, the set of singular fibers of the semi-ample fibration on which the Riemann curvature blows up at time-infinity is independent of the choice of the initial Kähler metric. Moreover, when a regular fiber of the semi-ample fibration is not a finite quotient of a torus, we determine the exact curvature blow-up rate of the Kähler-Ricci flow near the regular fiber. In the MPhil Thesis written by FUNG Cheuk Yan, supervised by me during 2020-2022, we proved that in the same setup as the above paragraph, with an additional assumption of Kodaira dimension 1, we identify the C^0-limit of the Ricci curvature. Also, in the paper "Higher-order Estimates of Long-Time Solutions to the Kahler-Ricci Flow", jointly written with Man-Chun Lee, we proved the Ricci curvature bound on the regular fibers.

16300018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300018.value: More in-depth studies on how the Riemann/Ricci curvature blows up at the singular fibers would be a good direction to go forward. The boundedness/convergence of the Ricci curvature is also important in studying the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the Kahler-Ricci flow. We shall investigate further.

16300018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300018.value: In this project, we deepen the understanding of the blow-up behavior of the Kahler-Ricci flow. The technique used cross-overs both geometry and analysis, promoting an even greater integration of the two subjects. We also produced some results which could be interesting to algebraic geometers, as it is motivated by the Mori Minimal Program.

16300118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300118.value: 1) We synthesize four‐ and six‐member cyclic products via sequential multi‐step aryl‐aryl coupling reactions of 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexabromotriphenylene molecules on a Au(111) surface. By adjusting reaction temperature and post‐annealing temperature, we enhance/suppress the yields of the four‐member and six‐member cyclic products. We propose an underlying mechanism which is associated with different reaction kinetics of the first‐order and second‐order reactions. This work exemplifies intricate kinetically‐controlled on‐surface synthesis when multiple reactions of different reaction order are involved. 2) We investigate the on‐surface [2+2] cycloaddition reaction of 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexabromotriphenylene (HBTP) on Ag(111), Cu(111), Au(111), and Cu‐dosed Au(111) surfaces using STM and DFT simulation focusing on the organometallic intermediates. The fully debrominated HBTP molecules form an organo‐silver framework on Ag(111) and an organo‐copper framework on Cu(111), both incorporating multinuclear metal adatom clusters. The organo‐silver framework is converted into porous covalent networks via [2+2] cycloaddition above 240 °C. In contrast, the organo‐copper framework is very stable and does not undergo [2+2] cycloaddition even at 300 °C. On Au(111), no organo‐gold intermediate of [2+2] cycloaddition is observed. After loading Cu onto Au(111), the partially debrominated HBTP molecules bind to Cu adatom dimers to form multinuclear organo‐copper complexes at 100 °C which undergo [2+2] cycloaddition at 140 °C. This study shows that the choice of surface can direct the reaction pathway. 3 We employ an on-surface Cu-catalyzed dehydrogenation reaction to synthesize a single layer 2D-MOF on epitaxial graphene, in which Cu atoms play dual roles in triggering the dehydrogenation of BHO molecules and participating as metal centers in the coordination network. This structure, as confirmed by the high-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and density-functional theory (DFT) calculation, is Cu_2 (C_6 O_6). We use the DFT calculation to study the electronic properties of this structure and find the free-standing structure is a conventional semiconductor with a narrow indirect band gap of 0.485 eV. The narrow band gap behavior of this 2D-MOF makes this structure a potential infrared-active material that can be used in organic light-emitting device, chemical and biological sensing, or solar cell. 4 We employ on-surface synthesis to grow single-layer frameworks of M3(HAT)2 (M=Ni, Co) on two Van dee Waals substrates of HOPG and MoS2. In contrast to the same frameworks that are grown on metal substrates, the frameworks grown on the Van der Waals substrates exhibit electronic properties of the free-standing layers, indicating very weak substrate influences. Interestingly, Ni3(HAT)2 is metallic while Co3(HAT)2 is semiconducting.

16300118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300118.value: Our findings of 3 and 4 are particular interesting since the intrinsic electronic properties of these systems are almost preserved because of very weak substrate influences. In light of the vast amount of 2D Van der Waals materials discovered in this fast growing field, we expect that using other 2D materials as substrates to grow 2D frameworks will be equally successful. These frameworks represent promising systems for functional materials.

16300118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300118.value: 2D materials of single-atom thick exhibit rich new physical and chemical properties and represent as next generation functional materials. However, one big problem is 2D materials are very fragile. Scientists have been working very hard to find different ways to stabilize 2D materials. One way is to graft the 2D materials on a substrate, in the meanwhile, to prevent the substrate alter the intrinsic properties of the 2D materials. Our research has opened a new way by using inert Van der Waals materials as substrates to support and stabilize the 2D materials. In doing so, we successfully minimize the substrate influence.

16300218.label: Project Objectives
16300218.value: This project will derive a new set of extended saddlepoint approximation formulas for tail expectations and Expected Shortfall under non-Gaussian base distributions using the Esscher exponential tilting technique. It will also explore the general principles for guiding users in the choices of non-Gaussian base distribution in approximating the thick tail distribution of the underlying state variable. This project will derive analytic saddlepoint approximation formulas for pricing of VIX futures and options under stochastic volatility models and Levy processes. Numerical assessment of the new saddlepoint approximation formulas and comparison of performance with other numerical methods will be made. It will also conduct sensitivity analysis of the VIX derivatives with respect to pricing model parameters. Based on the new set of saddlepoint approximation formulas for Expected Shortfall, the project will derive the corresponding formulas for risk contributions of obligors in credit portfolios. The performance of the saddlepoint approximation formulas will be tested using two popular default correlation models: CreditRisk+ and Gaussian copula models with multiple risk factors. In particular, the robustness of the saddlepoint approximation approach to risk measures calculations for credit portfolios with high risk concentrations will be examined.

16300218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300218.value: Many problems in pricing financial derivatives and risk measures calculation in credit portfolios involve computation of the tail expectations of the corresponding underlying state variables. Financial institutions always strive to effectively valuate prices of exotic financial derivatives and risk positions of the credit portfolios of risky instruments. It is desirable to derive effective, reliable and accurate analytic approximation formulas for derivatives pricing and risk measures computation. The saddlepoint approximation approach is a versatile tool in statistics based on the steepest descent method to derive an analytic approximation of the Laplace inversion integrals for density functions, tail probabilities and tail expectation of a sum of independent and identically distributed random variables. Most of the existing results on the saddelpoint approximation methods are based on the use of the Gaussian base distribution as the approximation of the underlying state variable. However, the probability distributions of jump-diffusion processes of asset price dynamics and the loss distributions of credit portfolios are highly skewed, so the use of the Gaussian base distribution may lead to significant errors for tail probabilities and tail expectations. In this project, using the Esscher exponential tilting technique, I propose to derive extended saddlepoint approximation formulas for tail expectation and expected shortfall under more general base distributions that are beyond the usual Gaussian base distribution. It would be difficult to extend other derivation approaches, such as the local quadratic approximation and Edgeworth expansion, to derive the approximation formulas for tail expectation and expected shortfall under the non-Gaussian based distribution. However, it is quite convenient to employ the exponential tilting technique to derive the tail expectation approximation formula by differentiation of the saddlepoint approximation for distribution under the general base distribution. The extended saddlepoint approximation formulas for tail expectations and expected shortfall will be used to price VIX futures and options under stochastic volatility with jumps and general Levy processes. Also, they are used to compute various risk measures, like Value-at-Risk and expected shortfall, and risk contributions of obligors in credit portfolios under default correlation models. The numerical accuracy and reliability of the extended saddlepoint formulas in these two financial engineering applications will be assessed by making benchmark comparisons with other numerical algorithms, such as the Fourier transform methods and Monte Carlo simulation. The pricing behaviors of the VIX derivatives under different model parameters in the jump-diffusion processes and risk characteristics of credit portfolios with different risk concentrations will be examined. 定價金融衍生產品和信貸投資組合中風險計量計算的大多數定價問題涉及計算相應基礎狀態變量的尾部期望。金融機構一直致力於對金融衍生品的價格和風險工具組合的風險頭寸進行有效估值。我希望為衍生產品定價和風險度量計算導出有效，可靠和準確的近似公式。鞍點近似方法是統計學中的通用工具，是基於最速下降方法來導出用於密度函數的拉普拉斯反演積分的近似公式，尾部概率和獨立且相同分佈的隨機變量之和的尾部期望。在這個科研項目中，我希望導出超越通常的高斯基分佈的更一般基本分佈的尾部期望的擴展鞍點近似公式。我將檢查新鞍點近似公式的準確性，然後使用鞍點近似公式為隨機波動率模型和一般Levy過程下的VIX期貨和期權定價。

16300218.label: Realisation of objectives
16300218.value: The three objectives as stated in the project proposal have been realized fully, the details of the related research activities to achieve the objectives are summarized below. To address the first objective, I have derived the generalized saddlepoint approximation formulas for calculating tail expectations from the usual Gaussian base distribution to an arbitrary base distribution. Specific attention has been paid on the criteria of choosing the base distribution that fits better the underlying distribution. In the derivation procedures, I adopted two different analytical approaches: (i) Esscher exponentially tilting technique based on Zheng-Kwok (2014), (ii) local approximation of the exponent in the Laplace integral based on Huang-Oosterlee (2011). Though the two approaches employed in deriving the Huang-Oosterlee formula and Zheng-Kwok formula for tail expectations are very different, the analytic expressions of the two saddlepoint approximation formulas are identical under the Gaussian base distribution. However, the saddlepoint approximation formulas using these two approaches differ under a non-Gaussian base distribution. Our numerical tests reveal higher level of numerical accuracy in the Zheng-Kwok saddlepoint approximation formula, even under an extreme scenario of high kurtosis when other saddlepoint approximation formulas do not perform well. Also, I have proposed an effective set of criteria for matching better the underlying distribution. The fourth order standardized cumulant is proven to be the best statistics used for matching the underlying distribution and base distribution in determining the shape parameter when the Gamma distribution or inverse Gaussian distribution is used as the base distribution. Detailed numerical comparison of accuracy and reliability are made among different saddlepoint approximation formulas. Improved accuracy of the saddlepoint approximations to tail expectations is revealed when the proper base distributions are chosen. In addressing the second objective, I have performed numerical tests to reveal enhanced numerical accuracy of the saddlepoint approximation formulas under non-Gaussian base distribution in pricing European options on continuous integrated variance under the Heston stochastic volatility model. Instead of pricing VIX derivative products as proposed in the project proposal, I found that it is more preferable to consider a related option product that considers realized integrated variance (from initiation to maturity date) to demonstrate more vividly robustness of the saddlepoint approximation techniques. A simple explanation can be offered as follows: VIX derivative pricing depends on single variance process while variance derivative pricing relies on joint process of variance and stock price process. My work is built upon Carr and Madan (2009), where they pioneer the use of the Gaussian less exponential base distribution. They show that this choice of base distribution performs better than the Gaussian base, which provides high numerical accuracy in option value calculations (typically within 0.1% in percentage error). By employing the share measure where the asset price is used as a numeraire, they manage to represent the European call prices as tail probabilities. In pricing exotic variance derivatives, it is necessary to derive saddlepoint approximation formulas for tail expectations under non-Gaussian base distributions, together with some nice choice of base distribution. I choose the non-Gaussian base distributions to be (i) Gaussian less exponential, (ii) Gamma distribution. I manage to demonstrate enhanced accuracy and efficiency of the generalized saddlepoint approximation formulas under non-Gaussian base distributions in pricing European options on continuous integrated variance under the Heston stochastic volatility model. The third objective is related to the development of new saddlepoint approximation formulas for calculating various risk measures in industrial credit risk models, including the CreditRisk+ model and Gaussian copula models. I have developed and implemented the saddlepoint approximation and some other numerical algorithms for calculating the common risk measures (Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall) and risk contributions from risky obligors in credit portfolios under the enhanced common background vector framework in the CreditRisk+ model. Besides analyzing the established saddlepoint approximation approach and its application in the two-step importance sampling algorithm, I have also studied the detailed implementation of the less popularly known Johnson curve fitting algorithm and check function formulation. I have compared the performance of these numerical algorithms for calculating risk measures and risk contributions using both stylized credit portfolios and complex industrial credit portfolios. In most of my risk measures calculations, the saddlepoint approximation method and Johnson curve fitting algorithm were seen to perform very well in terms of accuracy, efficiency and reliability. In many cases, these two numerical methods showed very good agreement of numerical results up to 3 significant figures and revealed no reported cases of numerical failure even for complex industrial credit portfolios. Besides comparison of numerical performance, practical implementation issues for finding the saddlepoint in an appropriate domain are explored. I also performed the theoretical analysis on the issue of existence of saddlepoint in numerical implementation. Other than the CreditRisk+ model, I have also performed the numerical calculations of marginal risk contributions of Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall in the popular Gaussian copula model and t-copula model. In these copula risk models, dependence between defaults are modeled via conditional independence given a set of common risk factors. I showed that the exponential twisting method in the importance sampling algorithm has close link with the saddlepoint approximation method. I take advantage of analytical tractability exhibited by the saddlepoint approximation framework and develop the hybrid saddlepoint approximation method to compute marginal risk contributions in the copula models. The hybrid saddlepoint approximation method contains two parts. The first part applies the saddlepoint approximation methods to obtain the conditional risk measures given the systematic risk factor; and the second part requires additional integration techniques to get unconditional measures by integrating over the systematic factors. Under the hybrid saddlepoint approximation framework, instead of performing subsequent Monte Carlo simulation, we approximate the exponential twisting distribution by the normal distribution and perform the analytic derivation of the saddlepoint approximation formulas. The computational efficiency is much enhanced since the computation involves only numerical evaluation of the analytic saddlepoint approximation formulas. Further enhancement in efficiency is achieved via an interpolation scheme that helps reduce the computational effort in searching for the saddlepoint in each simulation path. Detailed numerical comparison of performance of the enhanced hybrid saddlepoint approximation with other Monte Carlo simulation algorithms in calculating risk contributions in the copula risk models reveal very good performance of my proposed saddlepoint approach in terms of computational efficiency, accuracy and reliability.

16300218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300218.value: Three papers that report the major research findings in this project have been written, two of them have been published and one is a working paper. The details of these three papers are listed below. 1. “Saddlepoint approximations to tail expectations under non-Gaussian base distributions: option pricing applications,” by Yuantao Zhang and Yue Kuen Kwok (2020). In this paper, I generalize the saddlepoint approximation formulas for calculating tail expectations from the usual Gaussian base distribution to an arbitrary base distribution. Specific discussion is presented on the criteria of choosing the base distribution that fits better the underlying distribution. Numerical performance and comparison of accuracy are made among different saddlepoint approximation formulas. Improved accuracy of the saddlepoint approximations to tail expectations is revealed when proper base distributions are chosen. I also demonstrate enhanced accuracy of the generalized saddlepoint approximation formulas under non-Gaussian base distributions in pricing European options on continuous integrated variance under the Heston stochastic volatility model. 2. “Efficient risk measures calculations for generalized CreditRisk+ model,” by Zhenzhen Huang and Yue Kuen Kwok (2021). In this paper, I consider several developments of new saddlepoint approximation formulas for calculating the common risk measures (Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall) and risk contributions from risky obligors in credit portfolios under the enhanced common background vector framework in the CreditRisk+ model. I have compared the performance of several numerical algorithms for calculating risk measures and risk contributions using both stylized credit portfolios and complex industrial credit portfolios. In most of my risk measures calculations, the saddlepoint approximation method is seen to perform very well in terms of accuracy, efficiency and reliability. In addition, practical implementation issues for finding the saddlepoint in an appropriate domain are explored in the paper. I also performed theoretical studies on existence of saddlepoint in numerical implementation. 3. “Efficient importance sampling algorithms for calculating risk contributions in copula credit models,” by Zhenzhen Huang, Ziqing Xu and Yue Kuen Kwok (2020). In this paper, I performed the numerical calculations of marginal risk contributions of Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall in the popular Gaussian copula model and t-copula model. I showed that the exponential twisting method in the importance sampling algorithm has close link with the saddlepoint approximation method. I take advantage of analytical tractability exhibited by the saddlepoint approximation framework and develop the hybrid saddlepoint approximation method to compute marginal risk contributions in the copula models. Further enhancement in efficiency is achieved via an interpolation scheme that helps reduce the computational effort in searching for the saddlepoint in each simulation path. I have performed a detailed numerical comparison of performance of the enhanced hybrid saddlepoint approximation with other Monte Carlo simulation algorithms in calculating risk contributions in the copula risk models, which reveals the very good performance of my proposed saddlepoint approach in terms of computational efficiency, accuracy and reliability.

16300218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300218.value: We may consider further development of saddlepoint approximation methods in pricing exotic variance derivatives under a wider range of stochastic volatility models, beyond the Heston models. We may also explore the use of the hybrid saddlepoint method in other importance sampling algorithms, like the cross entropy method, in risk measures calculations in a wider range of credit risk models.

16300218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300218.value: Financial institutions always strive for effective valuation of prices of financial derivatives and risk positions of portfolios of risky instruments, like hedging strategies in trading options, risk measures assessment as quantified by Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall. It is desirable to derive effective, reliable and accurate analytic approximation formulas for derivatives pricing and risk measures computation. The saddlepoint approximation approach is a versatile tool in statistics that is used to derive an analytic approximation of density functions, tail probability and tail expectation of the underlying random variables in option pricing models and credit risk models. In this project, I have derived extended saddlepoint approximation formulas for tail expectation under more general base distributions that go beyond the usual Gaussian base distribution. This aims to enhance numerical accuracy and computational efficiency. I then employed the saddlepoint approximation formula to price variance derivative options under stochastic volatility models. In addition, I used the saddlepoint approximation formulas to compute risk contributions from risky obligors in a credit portfolio under the industrial CreditRisk+ credit risk model. The saddlepoint algorithms developed in this project are seen to compete favorably among various other algorithms in the literature in terms of efficiency, accuracy and relaibility.

16300418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300418.value: Linear codes have wide applications in communication systems, computer systems, data storage systems, and consumer electronics. They are related to many areas of mathematics, such as algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic function fields, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorics, finite fields, finite geometry, graph theory, and group theory. A fascinating and challenging topic of combinatorics is t-designs, which are closely related to coding theory. On one hand, a number of families of linear codes hold t-designs, and have been used to construct t-designs. On the other hand, the incidence matrix of a t-design generates a linear code over every finite field. These interplays between linear codes and t-designs have been a very interesting research topic for many years. Recently, exponentially many infinite families of t-designs held in linear codes have been presented in the literature. The first objective of the proposed project will be to determine the parameters of the linear codes generated by the incidence matrices of these t-designs. The second will be to study properties of these linear codes, which may be useful for decoding purpose. The output of the proposed project will enhance both coding theory and the theory of combinatorics, and will have applications in engineering. 線性碼在通信系統，計算機系統，數據存儲系統和電子消費品中有廣泛的應用。線性碼與數學的許多分支有密切的關系， 例如，代數，代數幾何，代數函數域，代數數論，結合方案，組合設計，有限域，有限集合，圖論和群論。 t-設計是組合學的一個既有挑戰又有魅力的分支。t-設計與編碼學有密切的聯系。一方面一些線性碼能生成t-設計。另一方面，t-設計的關聯矩陣能在任何有限域上生成線性碼。t-設計和線性碼的這種相互作用是多年來的研究熱題。近年來，文獻中報道了許多類從線性碼中構造的t-設計。 本項目的第一個任務是確定這些t-設計生成的線性碼的參數。第二個任務是研究這些碼的性能和性質。預期本項目的成果會加強編碼學和組合學的理論和應用。

16300418.label: Realisation of objectives
16300418.value: The objectives of this project have been fully achieved. Two research breakthroughs have been made. Details are the following. We solved a conjecture, and constructed a family of 2-designs contained in a family of ternary linear codes. We studied the linear codes of 2-designs associated with subsets of the ternary generalised Reed-Muller codes. We generalised the Assmus-Mattson Theorem, established a link between 2-designs and differentially delta-uniform functions, and obtained binary codes with new parameters and weight distributions. We established connections between t-designs and special functions. Two 70-year research breakthroughs were made in this project. The first one was the discovery of an infinite family of near MDS codes supporting 2-designs and an infinite family of near MDS codes supporting 3-designs. The second one was the discovery of infinite family of linear codes supporting 4-designs. Cyclic bent functions were introduced and their applications in sequences and codes as well as t-designs were found. Linear codes of length 2^m+1 over GF(2^m) supporting 3-designs were discovered. We studied the linear codes of t-designs held in the Reed-Muller and Simplex codes. We obtained some general theory for the linear codes of t-designs held in linear codes. Since the funding amount is very small, we were not able to support a Ph.D student with this project.

16300618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300618.value: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is a standard method in multivariate statistical analysis. It is used to study the correlation of two random vectors, or two sets of data in practice. Nowadays, CCA has become an indispensable part of nearly all monographs on multivariate statistical analysis. However, the existing results on CCA are mostly on the classical dimension setting, namely, the dimensions of two random vectors are fixed, while the sample size is considered to be very large. Due to the "curse of dimensionality", these classical results often fall short when the random vectors are also high-dimensional, which is unfortunately a typical situation for big data set. Therefore, in response to the prevalence of the big data analysis, pushing forward a systematic theory on high-dimensional CCA is much needed. In this project, we will mainly use the recently developed approaches in random matrix theory to establish a high-dimensional CCA theory. Especially, we aim at deriving the asymptotic behaviour of the largest canonical correlation coefficients and the corresponding basis vectors of the sample CCA matrix, under various assumptions. 典型相關性分析是多元統計分析中的一種經典方法，幾乎是所有多元統計分析專著裏不可或缺的一部分。它主要用於研究兩個隨機向量之間的相關性。然而， 目前已知的理論主要是在經典的固定維數的假設下得出的。這些經典假設下的結果往往不能用於高維情形。由於目前高維數據分析的重要性，系統地建立一套高維設定下的典型相關性分析理論是極其必要的。在這個項目中，我們將把最近發展的一些隨機矩陣的工具應用於高維典型相關性分析的研究。我們將特別集中研究在不同假設下高維典型相關矩陣的最大特征根和相應特征向量的極限性質。

16300618.label: Realisation of objectives
16300618.value: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is a fundamental part of the multivariate statistical analysis. It is used to detect the correlation between two random vectors or two data sets. More specifically, given two random vectors X and Y, CCA aims at finding the linear combination of the components of X and that of Y which have maximum correlation with each other. Mathematically, it boils down to finding the largest eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of the CCA matrix, which is the symmetrized version of the product of two projection matrices. The sample counterpart of the CCA matrix is called sample CCA matrix. In the low-dimensional setting, the canonical correlation coefficients computed from the sample CCA matrix can be used to estimate the population ones. However, in the high-dimensional case, due to the curse of dimensionality, such estimation is very much biased. Although estimation is generally impossible in high-dimensional setting, it is possible in some cases. Especially, when the population has a few spiked canonical correlation coefficients and they are sufficiently large, it is expected that the estimation is still possible. On the other hand, even when the model does not have large spikes, and the canonical correlation coefficient cannot be detected effectively, one may still use the spectral statistics of the sample CCA matrix for various hypothesis testing problems. These motivate us to investigate the limiting behavior of the leading eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of the high-dimensional sample CCA matrix. In order to establish a spectral theory for the high-dimensional sample CCA matrix, the first step is to find the limiting distribution of the largest eigenvalue of the CCA matrix and also the related models. The largest eigenvalues undergo a phase transition called BBP transition depending on the size of the spikes of the population matrices. In a previous work, we establish such a phase transition for the sample CCA matrix, and recently we also establish the Tracy-Widom distribution for the largest eigenvalue of the Kendall’s rank correlation matrix. This solves Objective 1. The second step is to extend the analysis from eigenvalues to eigenvectors. In two of our recent works, we study the limiting behavior of the eigenvector and singular vector of large-dimensional random matrices. Especially, we discover a non-universality phenomenon for the limiting distribution of the eigenvector, when there is an additive spiked part. Moreover, we study the joint distribution of the leading eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors. These works address the Objective 2. We then turn to study the central limit theorem of the linear spectral statistics. In a recent paper, we establish such a CLT for the sum of two random matrices, which can be extended to the sum of two tensor product of deterministic matrix and random matrix. The latter is a linearization of general polynomial in two random matrices. It contains the CCA matrix as a special case. Hence, this work addresses Objective 3. Finally, in a very recent work, we consider the correlation among more than two sets of random variables. Specifically, we raise the so-called Sample Block Correlation Matrix, and establish the CLT for its linear spectral statistics. When we choose the test function of the linear spectral statistics to be x^2, the statistics can be interpreted as a linear spectral statistics of a generalized CCA model for more than two sets of random variables. This exactly solves Objective 4.

16300618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300618.value: First, we find the eigenvector distribution of two classes of large-dimensional random matrices when there are spikes. Especially, in the critical regime of BBP transition, we combine the recently rediscovered eigenvector-eigenvalue formula with the determinantal representation of the spectral minor process of Gaussian random matrices. These results are published in Annals of Statistics (2022), and Probability Theory and Related Fields (2022). Then, we also derive the mesoscopic CLT for the linear spectral statistics for sum of two random matrices. Especially, we prove a CLT for the mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for this model. The CLT matches those for the classical random matrix models such as Wigner matrices, and thus it is universal. We introduce a high order subordination system to tackle this problem. This result is contained in the paper published in International Mathematics Research Notices (2020). Last, we introduce the sample block correlation matrices and study its limiting spectral distribution and the CLT for the linear spectral statistics. The results are described with the aid of the Free Probability Theory. It turns out that the CLTs do not depend on the 4th cumulant of the matrix entry, due to a self-normalizing effect. The result has been submitted to Annals of Statistics, with a preprint on ArXiv (arXiv: 2207.06107).

16300618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300618.value: In Objective 4, we consider the correlation among more than two sets of random variables. To this end, we consider the sample block correlation matrix and establish its limiting spectral properties. However, we assume the matrix entries have light tail. Especially, we require the 4th moment to exist. The existence of the 4th moment is usually required for the CLT of the linear spectral statistics for many random matrix models, since it will show up in the limiting variance as a parameter. However, we find that the limiting formula of the CLT for linear spectral statistics of the sample block correlation matrix does not depend on the 4th moment. This indicates that the 4th moment may not be needed for this model. This new feature is essentially due to a self-normalizing effect of the correlation type of matrices. Hence, a nature further direction is to explore the spectral statistics of this type of self-normalized random matrix models under heavy-tailed assumption.

16300618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300618.value: In this project, we work on the spectral properties of the sample CCA matrix and related models. More generally, we use the spectral statistics of various random matrix models to investigate the correlation among two or more sets of random variables, under the high-dimensional setting. We have successfully established the limiting laws of the largest eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors for various models. We have also proved the CLTs for linear spectral statistics for various related random matrix models. We further apply our results to real applications. The results of this project are important in the fields of Random Matrix Theory, Free Probability Theory, and High-Dimensional Statistics.

16300818.label: Project Objectives
16300818.value: To investigate the localized-metallic phase transition versus energy in anti-dot graphene, by using the analytical approach with the self-consistent Green’s function method. Self-consistent Born Approximation (SCBA) would be employed to describe the disorder potential scattering, and maximally crossed diagrams (MCD) would be used to describe the coherent backscattering processes. Berry phase variation would be explicitly taken into account, to predict the critical doping level and disorder strength of the MIT. To carry out numerical simulations by using recursive Green’s function method, so as to obtain the size dependence of conductance as function of energy, disorder strength, gap width, etc. Simulation results would be compared with the analytical results to further identify the presence of the MIT in 2D anti-dot graphene.

16300818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300818.value: In two-dimensional (2D) electronic systems, traditional scaling theory predicts that arbitrarily weak disorder should localize the electronic states. No metallic state should survive in a large enough 2D system, regardless of the strength of disorder. This is quite different from the three-dimensional case, where a critical conductance, denoted the mobility edge, separates the Anderson localization (AL) phase and the metallic phase. In recent years, the advent of graphene has re-ignited interest in this paradigm. Owing to its honeycomb lattice structure, graphene’s electronic wave-function displays a particular geometric phase, called the Berry phase, with a value of π when electrons propagate along a closed loop. The implications of this additional phase have been widely investigated, and anti-localization behavior has been shown to be an inevitable consequence. The focus of this proposed study will be to search for possible Berry phase-induced metal-to-insulator transitions (MIT) in 2D anti-dot graphene. Here “anti-dot” means the graphene layer is nanostructured with a periodic array of holes, thereby modifying the electronic band-structure. We have recently published (Phys.Rev.X 7, 031043 (2017)) a 4-by-4 effective matrix Hamiltonian derived for this system and shown that contrary to the conventional wisdom, there can be interesting topological electronic properties. Besides opening a bandgap around the Dirac point, we also identified a 0 to π variation in the Berry phase as a function of the energy, measured with respect to the band edge. Since a Berry phase of 0 means a reversion to the conventional 2D electron gas where the traditional scaling theory applies, and a Berry phase of π can induce anti-localization, a natural question arises: Can the 0 to π variation of the Berry phase result in an MIT in 2D? We have carried out some preliminary work on the 2D massive Dirac equation, which has a simpler 2-by-2 matrix Hamiltonian, and found evidence of a similar electronic bandgap as well as the 0 to π Berry phase variation. Both the analytical and numerical simulation results show the potential existence of the proposed MIT. Hence it’s highly probable that the anti-dot graphene will exhibit similar features. Success in this proposed research will put in place a crucial piece of the puzzle for 2D localization, not only by identifying the existence and the attendant conditions for the MIT in 2D anti-dot graphene systems, but also by providing a theoretical basis for understanding the electrical transport properties of 2D topologically-nontrivial material systems.

16300818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300818.value: The two main objectives are to (1) search for a 2D localized to delocalized electronic transition in anti-dot graphene, and (2) verify the theory prediction by simulations. These are worthwhile objectives because in the classical theory of Anderson localization, all wave functions in 2D are localized. Therefore such a finding would be in direct contradiction to the classical prediction. However, the discovery of graphene and other 2D materials has injected the possibility of a 2D localized to delocalized electronic transition, mainly owing to the existence of the Berry phase, which can invert the effect of the localization mechanism—the coherent backscattering effect, to anti-localization. The objective is accomplished. We started with a simpler system, which is the two-dimensional massive Dirac fermions. Such system can be described with a 2 by 2 Hamiltonian, which avoids the complicity of the two valleys in graphene, but still holds the 0 to  variation in Berry phase. We developed a density response theory to analyze the electronic transport properties in this system. The breaking of time-reversal symmetry gives rise to the diffusive wave propagation, which is different from both the localization phase in classical 2DEG and the super-diffusive phase in massless Dirac fermions, like surface states of topological insulators. Our results have been published in Phys. Rev. B 104 (7), 075427. Based on the results derived in the 2 by 2 Hamiltonian, we next extend it to the anti-dot graphene system, which is described by a 4 by 4 massive Dirac Hamiltonian. We identified that in the vicinity of the band edge, a localized phase occurs, and at high doping level the transport is diffusive. Therefore, a localization to delocalization, or a metal-insulator, transition has indeed been found. The localization length exhibits a divergence at a critical doping level, with a divergence exponent of -0.5. A manuscript has been organized and submitted (preprint attached). For the second objective, we have done better than the originally stated goal of using simulations to verify the localization to delocalization transition. Instead, we have carried out experiments, by measuring square samples of varying sizes with different doping levels, to see the predicted transition. Indeed, a localization to delocalization transition was observed. Divergence in the localization length in the vicinity of the critical doping level was also seen and measured. The divergence exhibits an exponent of -0.4, fairly similar to what was predicted. The experimental results were also included in the preprint that is attached. In short, we have more than achieved our stated objectives.

16300818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300818.value: The results found in this research proposal can actually be of practical use. This is because if there is a localized (insulator) and delocalized (metal) transition at a critical doping level, that means one can manipulate the conductance at the mesoscopic level by just varying the gating voltage. This is because the doping level in 2D materials can be easily controlled by gate voltage. And since electrical signals can be extremely fast, it means that locally, the control on the conductance can open and shut current flows, to simulate input signals. However, since I am retiring at the end of June, 2022, this stated course of action will be left to future researchers.

16300818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300818.value: The discovery of 2D graphene has generated great excitement because its properties can be tuned by a gate voltage. However, its practical application has been hindered by not having a gap in its bandstructure, i.e., an energy range without any electronic state. However, by nanostructuring the graphene, a small bandgap can be artificially generated. This research is about the search for a drastic change in the conductance of the nanostructured graphene, by tuning the gate voltage. We have succeeded in doing so. In technical terms, we have found a gating voltage level below which the electronic states are localized, i.e., unable to move, and above that level the electrons can move freely, like in an ordinary metal. Therefore just by altering the gate voltage, one can change the conductance of the nanostructured graphene drastically. That is an exciting development.
