16300918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300918.value: 理解和分类各种可能的物态是凝聚态物理研究中的关键问题。在传统凝聚态理论中，物态是按照不同的对称性来分类的，朗道相变理论就是在此基础上建立起来，并取得了极大的成功。在最近十几年的研究中，研究人员发展出了一种分类多电子体系中不同物态的新方法。在这一新方法中，物态的分类不仅依照其所具有的对称性，还考虑其电子结构的拓扑性质。沿着这一方向，实际材料中的各种拓扑物态相继被提出和发现。例如拓扑绝缘体、量子反常霍尔效应、拓扑半金属和拓扑超导体等。 目前发现的绝大多数拓扑材料都属于弱关联材料。在弱关联材料中，电子间的库仑相互作用能够被采用局域密度近似方法(LDA)的密度泛函理论(DFT)很好的描述，同时其能带的拓扑性质主要是由于强自旋轨道耦合效应所导致的。与之相对应的是强关联材料。在强关联材料中，电子间库仑势导致的关联效应太强以至于局域密度近似方法(LDA)失效。与弱关联材料相比，强关联材料所能实现的量子物态更加丰富，其中会有许多是拓扑物态。 在本申请中，申请人(PI)提出研究一类具有强自旋轨道耦合和库仑相互作用引起的关联效应的材料体系的电子结构性质。主要的研究工作将集中于寻找受到自旋轨道耦合与关联效应共同影响导致具有拓扑物态的材料，例如拓扑绝缘体、外尔半金属、Dirac半金属和具有量子反常霍尔效应的Chern绝缘体等。沿着这一方向，将重点关注两类材料：含有稀有元素的重费米子系统和4d/5d重过渡金属化合物，例如铱(Ir)、锇(Os)和钌(Ru)化合物。在方法论部分，我们将对这类材料应用LDA+DMFT和LDA+Gutzwiller方法。这两种方法经过在学术带头人(PI)的研究组中超过十年的发展，计算程序具有很高的效率，可以用于研究本项目所关注的材料。

16300918.label: Realisation of objectives
16300918.value: The present proposal is devoted to the research of possible new topological states in strongly correlated materials. In the first decade of the research on topological states in condensed matter physics, most of the topological materials studied in detail belong to weakly correlated materials, where the Coulomb interaction among electrons can be well treated by density functional theory (DFT) under local density approximation (LDA). Thus the topological nature of the band structures can be mainly ascribed to the strong spin-orbital interactions, which have been overlooked for many decades in condensed matter physics. However, there are many interesting materials studied in condensed matter belonging to another class, the strongly correlated materials, where the correlation effects caused by Coulomb repulsive interaction cannot be treated well by the mean-field type approximation. Since there are already many topological materials being discovered in the weakly correlated system, it is natural to expect more exotic topological states to be found in the strongly correlated systems, which is the main goal of this project. After three years of hard-working, we have reached the following research outputs about the correlation-generated topological states in several different types of systems. 1) We have discovered the first Stoichiometric axion insulator state in a rare earth compound EuIn2As2. Our first-principle calculation shows that this interesting material can accommodate several different types of topological states by tuning the magnetic orders, which are mainly contributed by the Eu ions. Most importantly, if the system is in the antiferromagnetic state with the magnetic moments being tuned along the c direction, all the crystal surfaces are fully gapped. In such a situation, this material is also a high-order topological insulator with one-dimensional chiral states located right at the hinges between those gapped surfaces. These exotic phenomena have been discussed theoretically in condensed matter physics for many years, but our study proposed the first realistic single crystal material to possible realize the topological magneto-electric effect, axion insulator, and high order topological insulator states in a single material, which will have a big impact for the future experimental studies in this field. Our paper has been published in Phys. Rev. Lett. (doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.122.256402), and already received more than 120 citations in less than three years. 2) We have discovered a ferromagnetic rare-earth compound EuB6, where several different types of topological states including the topological nodal ring, Weyl semimetal, and quantum anomalous Hall effect can all be possibly realized in such material. Through the first-principle calculation, we found that the ferromagnetism in this material is very soft and its magnetization can be easily tuned along different crystal directions generating different topological states mentioned previously. The compound has been studied in the heavy fermion community for almost a half-century, our study finally reveals the topological features of its electronic structure, which generates lots of research interest recently. Our paper has been published in Phys. Rev. Letters in 2020 (doi.org/10.1103/PHYSREVLETT.124.076403) has already received more than 30 citations in two years. 3) We have published a series of papers to reveal both the origin of the topological band structure and strongly correlated effects in the Twisted bi-layer graphene (TBG). In our first paper, which is published in Phys. Rev. B in 2019 (doi.org/10.1103/PHYSREVB.99.155415), we proposed the pseudo-Landau level (PLL) description for the low energy flat bands in TBG systems. Based on the PLL description, the non-trivial topological nature of its band structure can be well understood and the possible quantum anomalous Hall states can be expected after the ferromagnetic order is established by the strong Coulomb interactions. Our paper provides a clear and straightforward way to understand the otherwise complicated physics behind it. In the second paper of this series, we extended our theoretical study from TBG to twisted multi-layer graphene systems. We predicted in the paper that various topological states can be realized in such systems by changing the twisting angle, layer number, and stacking chirality. Our paper has been published in Physical Review X in 2019 (doi.org/10.1103/PHYSREVX.9.031021) and has already received more than 110 citations by now. In the third paper of this series, we further included the strong Coulomb interaction among the flat band electrons of TBG and studied its mean field phase diagram. Our results indicate that several different topological states including the valley polarized, inter-valley coherent, and quantum anomalous Hall states can be stabilized in these systems by varying the gate, Coulomb screening, and substrates. Our paper has been published in Physical Review B in 2021 (doi.org/10.1103/PHYSREVB.103.035427) and already received about 50 citations in a year. Due to the impact of the above papers, we received an invitation to write a review article on this fast-developing research field for a newly founded Nature sub-journal Nature Review Physics. The review article has been published in 2021 (doi.org/10.1038/S42254-021-00297-3). In summary, we have done great work in the scheme of “search for topological states in correlated systems” as listed above. In addition to that, we have also finished several good works on other related topics including the magnetic field-induced topological phases, Majorana zero modes in iron-based superconductors, and the chiral zero sound effects in Weyl semimetals. It is no doubt that this is a very successful project.

16300918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300918.value: From the research work supported by this grant, we have developed a comprehensive understanding of how the correlated effects and topological physics can interplay and generate fruitful physical phenomena in condensed matters. We now have several such material platforms, where very exotic quantum orders can be induced due to the correlation effect cooperated with the spin-orbital coupling. These systems include twisted bi-layer and multi-layer graphene, twisted TMD materials, and iron-based superconductors with magnetic impurities. The next step is to further study these systems with quantitatively reliable numerical tools to study the detail physical properties of these systems. In the next three years, the research efforts of our group will be focused on two aspects, the first one is to develop a real computational scheme that can do the first principle Gutzwiller variational calculation for realistic 2D materials. And the second is to study the strongly correlated physics in TBG and instead TMD using both the dynamical field theory and Gutzwiller variational methods.

16300918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300918.value: Correlation and topology are the two most important keywords in modern condensed matter physics. The former effect is mainly caused by the mutual interactions between two electrons when they are getting very close in real space. And the latter effect is mainly about the unique contains contributed by the crystal environment to a single electron, which usually happens in momentum space. Then how these two effects can interplay and give rise to some more exotic states is a very important subject in condensed matter physics. Supported by the present grant, my research group has finished a series of good works in this field, which clearly demonstrate how these two effects can interplay and generate fruitful physics in several different material systems including the twisted bilayer graphene, where several interesting topological states can be stabilized by the correlation effect, the rare-earth compound EuIn2As2, EuB6, where the magnetization provided by the 4f electrons on Eu atoms significantly modify the topological states in these materials, and in iron-based superconductors, where the Majorana zero mode, a new type of emergent particle, can be induced from the correlation effects.

16301018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301018.value: Sewage contains a large quantity of pathogens. To protect public health, treated effluents are often disinfected prior to the discharge to the receiving waters. Chlorine is one of the most commonly used disinfectants in the sewage treatment process due to its advantages of being high in efficacy and low in operational requirements. The impacts of chlorine on the metabolism, physiology and survival of effluent-associated bacteria have been an area of active research. However, the investigations have been largely focused on a small number of pathogens or indicator bacteria (pathogen surrogates) that are readily culturable in the lab. It is well-known that the vast majority of the bacterial cells living in the environment, including sewage, are in the viable-but-non-culturable (VBNC) state. Even E. coli, which is a readily culturable bacteria typically used by regulatory agencies as an indicator of effluent quality and water sanitation, could enter the VBNC state upon chlorination, resulting in an overestimation of disinfection efficacy. What has been lacking in the current knowledge is a culture-independent, holistic understanding of the impacts of chlorine disinfection on the entire bacterial microbiome of treated effluent as a genetically and functionally diverse community of hundreds to thousands of species. The response of effluent-associated bacteria to the post-disinfection discharge to the aquatic environment is another important issue that has not been investigated at the microbiome level. To fill the knowledge gap, we propose a culture-independent investigation on (i) the lethal and sublethal impacts of chlorine on the bacterial microbiome of treated effluent, and (ii) the potential bacteriological threats associated with the disposal of the disinfected effluent to the aquatic environment. To achieve this, effluents that are going through actual chlorine disinfection in sewage treatment facilities will be investigated for changes in community composition, functional repertoire and gene expression profile, particularly for the diversity and quantity of pathogens and genes of public health concern (e.g. virulence factors and antibiotic resistance). After that, undisinfected effluents will be brought to the lab to receive chlorine disinfection followed by field mesocosm experiments to simulate the discharge to coastal seawater; the impacts on the community composition of the bacterial microbiome in general and the population dynamics of pathogens in particular will be investigated. Overall, the knowledge obtained in this proposed project will provide for the first time a culture-independent, microbiome-level insight to the bacteriological outcomes of one of the world’s most commonly used effluent disinfection and disposal strategy. 污水中含有大量的病原體。為保障公眾健康，經處理的污水在排放到河流或大海之前一般會被消毒。由於氯是高效而毋須特別操作要求的消毒劑，因此被常用於消毒經處理的污水。氯對於污水中細菌的代謝，生理及存活的影響一直是活躍的研究領域，但有關研究主要集中在少數易於在實驗室培養的病原體或指示菌（病原體替代物）。眾所周知，絕大多數生活在環境（包括污水）中的細菌是處於可存活但不可培養的（VBNC）狀態。大腸桿菌因易於培養而成為各監管機構常用於污水質量和水衛生的指標，然而大腸桿菌亦會於污水被加氯消毒時進入VBNC狀態，以致高估消毒處理的效果。經處理後污水中的整個細菌微生物組是一個由數千百個物種組成遺傳及功能多樣化的群落，目前有關研究領域缺乏的是透過非培養方式了解加氯消毒程式對整個細菌微生物組的影響。另外，有關研究領域亦缺乏於微生物組層面上瞭解污水中的細菌經消毒後被排放到水生環境後的反應。為了填補有關研究領域上的知識空缺，我們提議透過非培養方式研究（i）氯對經處理後污水中的細菌微生物組的致命和亞致命的影響，以及（ii）排放經消毒處理的污水對水生環境在細菌學層面上的潛在威脅。為實現此目標，我們將調查於污水處理設施中正被加氯消毒的污水中微生物的群落組成，功能多樣性及基因表達模式的變化，特別是病原體和與公共衛生相關的基因（例如致病和抗生素耐藥性因數）的多樣性和數量。其後，未經消毒處理的污水將會於實驗室接受加氯消毒程式，並利用戶外中型生態池模擬排放污水到沿海海水中，以調查有關污水排放對細菌微生物組群落組成及病原體種群動態的影響。總括而言，該項目將首次透過非培養方式於微生物組層面上深入瞭解世界上其中一種最常用的污水消毒和排放策略的效果。

16301018.label: Realisation of objectives
16301018.value: Objective 1 has been successfully achieved through the analysis of the microbiomes in the effluents of two local sewage treatment works collected before and after chlorine disinfection over one year of bimonthly sampling. One facility, namely Stonecutters Sewage Treatment Works (SC), receives saline influent for chemically enhance primary treatment; the other one, namely Shatin Sewage Treatment Works (ST), receives freshwater influent for secondary treatment. The effluents were analysed using cultivation as well as quantitative PCR (qPCR) and amplicon sequencing of the 16S gene markers coupled with propidium monoazide (PMA) treatment to investigate the impacts of chlorine disinfection on the total, viable, and culturable populations of indicator bacteria, pathogens, and bacterial communities. Through these analysis, we determined (i) the temporal variability of the community composition of the bacterial microbiome in the undisinfected effluents of the two treatment facilities, (ii) impacts of chlorine disinfection on the community composition, (iii) how effectively the concentrations of indicator bacteria (i.e. E. coli, Enterococcus and Bacteroidales) could serve as predictors of pathogen loads in disinfected and undisinfected effluents. The results have been published in Tang and Lau (2022). Briefly, chlorine disinfection significantly reduced the culturable counts of E. coli and Enterococcus in the effluents in both sewage treatment works. But PMA-qPCR revealed considerable amounts of viable cell equivalents remaining after disinfection even when culturable E. coli and Enterococcus was undetectable. This suggests that the culture-based methods adopted by regulatory agencies underestimates the concentrations of bacterial indicators that remained alive in the disinfected effluents and hence overestimates disinfection efficacy. The differences between the culturable counts and the concentrations of viable cell are in part attributable to the presence of viable-but-non-culturable cells. The microbiomes in the effluents of SC and ST had substantial compositional differences, which could be explained as due to the salinity in the influents and operational parameters in the two sewage treatment works. Chlorine disinfection significantly reduced the richness, diversity, and evenness of the viable bacterial communities in the effluents of both sewage treatment works. Nonetheless, over 20 pathogenic bacterial species were found viable after disinfection, many of them belonged to the genera Enterobacter and Vibrio. Although chlorine disinfection reduced the total concentrations of viable pathogens, their concentrations remained over 8 log10 16S rRNA copies ml-1 in SC and 6 log10 16S rRNA copies ml-1 in ST. The culturable counts of E. coli and Enterococcus had poor correlation with pathogen load. In contrast, the viable concentrations of indicator bacteria measured using PMA-qPCR showed the best correlations. The disparity between the performances of culturable and viable indicator bacteria suggested that the presence of VBNC cells significantly weakens the correlations between the indicator bacteria and pathogens. These results have been published in Tang and Lau (2022). Objective 2 has been completed successfully through metagenomic and the metatranscriptomeic sequencing of a subset of the effluent samples collected in objective 1. The subset samples were collected in three months from each of the sewage treatment works that had the largest differences in bacterial community composition before and after chlorination. Comparative metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses revealed: (i) how the disinfection process impacts the functional repertoire of the bacterial microbiome, (ii) how the global gene expression profile of the bacterial microbiome changes in response to chlorine, and (iii) which functions and metabolic pathways in specific are filtered / suppressed and which are enriched / promoted during the disinfection process. Briefly, the composition of the gene repertoire and expressed pathways varied across effluent types and between months of sampling. Genes in functional pathways related to signalling and cellular processes, genetic information processing, and carbohydrate metabolism were highly abundant and highly expressed in unchlorinated effluents from both sewage treatment works. Although many of the genes and their transcripts had significant changes (increased or decreased) in abundance after chlorination in each treatment work, those that had significant changes in both treatment works were scarce. The mapping of gene and transcripts to metabolic pathways suggested that the microbiome in the chlorinated effluents had higher resistance to several antimicrobial drugs, larger amounts of virulence factors related to bacterial and parasitic infectious diseases, higher activities in the repairing and degradation of genome materials, and higher activities in sensing and reacting to the external environment as well as cooperating with the community to enhance survival. These results are being prepared as manuscripts for submission. Objective 3 has been successfully completed by using microcosm experiments to simulate the discharge of chlorinated effluents into coastal seawater. Undisinfected effluents collected from SC and ST were treated with different chlorine doses and subsequently incubated in the seawater microcosms for 3 days. The changes in the concentrations of total, viable and culturable E. coli and Enterococcus as well the community structure of total and viable portion of the microbiome in the microcosms were monitored to determine (i) how the exposure to seawater impacts the community composition of the bacterial microbiome in disinfected effluents, (ii) whether the concentration of culturable E. coli or other bacterial indicators in disinfected effluent is a good predictor of the potential bacteriological threats associated with the discharge of the effluents to the marine environment. Same as the observation in objective 1, chlorine disinfection in the lab resulted in large differences between the concentrations of viable and culturable indicator bacteria. The differences widened upon dilution with seawater and over three days of incubation in the microcosms. In the community level, chlorine disinfection substantially reduced the viable population of the whole bacterial community but enriched the relative abundance of pathogenic chlorine resistant bacteria (CRB). Most of these pathogenic CRB had weak correlation with the concentrations of viable or the culturable fecal indicator bacteria. Nonetheless, the concentrations of viable Enterococcus in the effluent of ST appeared to be strongly correlated with concentrations of most pathogenic CRB. These results shed light to how chlorine disinfection and the subsequent discharge to the impacted survival of sewage bacteria, particularly the lack of correlation between the concentration of indicator bacteria and pathogenic CRB. These results are being prepared as manuscripts for submission. Additionally, we analyzed the genome sequences of E. coli strains collected from fecal and environmental sources around Hong Kong. The results indicated that some of the strains should belong to cryptic clade II of Escherichia, and they warrant the designation of a novel species. Cryptic clade II strains are widespread in Hong Kong in the aquatic environments with or without no apparent fecal pollution. Since their genomes carry signature of adaptation to both enteric and external environment, cryptic clade II may have evolved cycle between the two environments through the fecal oral route. Their presence in the aquatic environment may further weaken the correlation between the concentrations E. coli and sewage pathogens because the cultivation method that regulatory agencies use in water quality monitoring is not able to differentiate E. coli and cryptic clade II. These results have been published in Shen et al. (2019, 2020) and Koh et al. (2022). The vast majority of the works in this project involve DNA extraction, purification, amplification and sequencing, which are costly. Therefore, the entire budget of the project was channeled to the consumables and DNA sequencing charges.

16301018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301018.value: Chlorine disinfection in the two sewage treatment works (STWs) reduced the concentrations of culturable E. coli and Enterococcus in the effluents to meet the standard for discharge into the local marine environment, but considerable amounts of the viable cells of the two indicator bacteria remained after disinfection (Tang and Lau 2022). The differences between the culturable counts and the viable counts were in part due to chlorine triggering the bacterial cells into the viable-but-non-culturable state, leading to an overestimation of disinfection efficacy and hence underestimation of the potential health risks in the disinfected effluents. Indeed, high concentrations of viable pathogens were detected in disinfected effluents, which exhibited strong correlations with the viable counts, but not the culturable counts, of the indicator bacteria. At the microbiome level, undisinfected effluents in the two STWs differed substantially in bacterial community structure, which could be explained as due to the differences in the salinity in the influents and in the operational parameters in the two sewage treatment works (Tang and Lau 2022). Despite the differences observed in the undisinfected effluents, chlorine disinfection selected for similar gene repertoire in both types of effluents. These genes are related to antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, DNA repairing, chemosensing, and community functions to enhance survival (Tang and Lau in prep.). In the microcosm experiment to simulate the discharge of chlorine disinfected effluents into seawater, the discrepancy between the culturable count and the viable count of the two indicator bacteria widened over the three days of incubation (Tang and Lau in prep.). At the microbiome level, disinfection selected for chlorine resistant pathogenic bacteria. These bacteria remained detectable throughout the incubation period and their concentrations did not correlate with the culturable count or the viable count of the two indicator bacteria, highlighting the inadequacy of using indicators to assess potential health risks of sewage discharge in the aquatic environment. In addition to bacteria entering the VBNC state, the accuracy of cultivation based methods in the numeration of culturable E. coli could be impacted by the presence of the cryptic clade II of Escherichia, which may have evolved to survive in both enteric and external environment but are indistinguishable from E. coli using conventional taxonomic criteria (Shen et al. 2019, 2021). The cryptic clade II of Escherichia is widespread in the aquatic environment of Hong Kong, which further question the use of cultivation method in water quality monitoring (Koh et al. 2022).

16301018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301018.value: The results in objective 1 indicated that the concentration of viable pathogens in sewage effluents correlated with the viable counts, but not the culturable counts, of indicator bacteria. However, the determination of concentration of viable indicator bacteria require the PMA-qPCR procedures, which is too time-consuming for routine monitoring of sewage effluents. Methods that enable rapid enumeration of viable indicator bacteria within the complex effluent microbiome could be a breakthrough in the monitoring of effluent quality. A possible direction is to develop a biosensing system that specifically target viable cells of E. coli. Indeed, the PI of this project is currently in a collaboration to develop a label-free biosensing system for fish pathogens. The system may be further developed to detect viable E. coli. The results in objective 3 is another possible direction for further development. Chlorine resistant pathogenic bacteria were observed to remain viable in the microcosms throughout 3 days of incubation. But this observation was based on the relatively low taxonomic resolutions of 16S amplicon sequencing. Further investigations using metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing would be needed to determine the identity, activities and potential threats of pathogens that survive chlorine disinfection and subsequently the seawater environment after effluent discharge.

16301018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301018.value: Chlorine is a commonly used disinfectant in the sewage treatment process due to its advantages of being high in efficacy and low in operational requirements. However, the impacts of chlorine on the metabolism, physiology and survival of effluent-associated bacteria remain under-investigated, leaving a knowledge gap in the understanding of the microbiological risks associated with the discharge of disinfected effluents into the aquatic environment. The results of this project indicated that, although chlorine disinfection could reduce the total bacterial community in the effluents, chlorine resistant pathogenic bacteria and genes of public health concerns could persist. Additionally, the cultivation methods commonly used in effluent quality monitoring could overestimate disinfection efficiency due to the methods’ inability to detect E. coli and Enterococcus, which are fecal indicator bacteria, in the viable-but-not-culturable physiological state. Nonetheless, the concentration of viable fecal indicator bacteria, which was detected using quantitative polymerase chain reaction, correlated well with the pathogen load in the effluents. But the method did not yield satisfactory correlations in microcosms that simulated the discharge of disinfection effluent into the marine environment. Further investigations are needed to develop methods to accurately evaluate the potential health risks in the discharge of chlorine disinfected effluents into the marine environment.

16301218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301218.value: There have been significant interest and advances in computational fluid–structure interaction (FSI) research recently, but FSI remains as one of the most challenging problems in computational mechanics and computational fluid dynamics. FSI is a class of problems with mutual dependence between the fluid and structural mechanics components. It finds important applications in engineering, sciences, medicine, and our daily lives. The pumping of blood by the ventricles of the human heart, accompanied by the opening and closing of the heart valves, and blood flow and arterial dynamics in cerebral aneurysms, inflation of automobile airbags, and deflection of wind-turbine blades are all examples of FSI. Therefore, effective, efficient, stable, and accurate FSI numerical methods and robust FSI simulation systems are in high demand in industry, research laboratories, the medical field, space exploration, and many other areas. FSI is modeled by a mixed partial differential equation system with local models of fluid dynamics and structural mechanics in different regions, coupled through interface conditions that describe the compatibility of the kinematics and tractions at the fluid-structure interface. The structure domain is in motion, and the shape of the fluid domain also changes to conform to the motion of the structure, which accordingly results in a moving interface. It is a typical multi-modeling problem, where the local models differ substantially and are coupled together through interface-matching conditions, which leads to complex interactions and interfacial structures at the moving interface. The coupling also results in a lack of flexibility, and thus substantial difficulties in all aspects of numerical computation. On the other hand, the mathematical theory and numerical analysis for each local model are well developed, and efficient and reliable legacy codes are available. Therefore we propose to investigate effective decoupling techniques for the FSI model such that the decoupled problem can be efficiently solved, yet the decoupled algorithms ensure the added-mass free stability, and the computed solution of the decoupled model would still approximate the original solution of the coupled FSI model accurately. The proposed investigation will result in innovative decoupled methods so that the existing most effective and efficient local solvers may be easily applied and integrated for the coupled FSI model. Comprehensive numerical experiments and theoretical analysis will be carried out on the devised methods to investigate their approximation accuracy, computational efficiency, and stability. A robust and efficient software system will be developed for three-dimensional FSI simulation. Large-scale FSI simulation will be conducted for real applications.

16301218.label: Realisation of objectives
16301218.value: We have studied decoupled numerical methods for multi-domain, multi-physics applications. We have investigated the scalar coupled heat flow model as a typical multi-modeling model problem in detail. By investigating numerical approximations in space and time separately and the interface decoupling afterwards, as well as tracking how the information and errors are transmitted across the interface and how the numerical instability may be induced, we have derived an inertial-type of, or the so-called intrinsic Robin interface conditions for its semi-discrete model. This new interface conditions are justified both mathematically and physically in contrast to the classical Robin interface conditions conventionally introduced for decoupling multi-modeling problems. Based on the new intrinsic Robin conditions, an equivalent semi-discrete model is introduced, which leads to a general framework for devising effective and stable decoupled numerical methods, particularly aiming at the added-mass free stability related to the FSI applications. The decoupled numerical methods based on the new intrinsic Robin conditions have been implemented, and the developed software has been used to conduct numerical experiments for validating the efficiency and effectiveness of the decoupling approach based on the new intrinsic Robin interface approach. All project objectives have been achieved. There is certain spending deviation with more staffing cost and less general expenses as budged in the proposal, which is due to substantial numerical experiments and research collaboration are required to achieve the project objectives that leads to more cost of student support, research assistant and visitor expenses being charged to General Expenses.

16301418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301418.value: During the past decade, the study of matter’s topological aspects has been a top priority among researchers in condensed matter physics and materials sciences. Following the success in research of topological insulators, the family of topological materials has recently expanded to include semimetals known as Dirac/Weyl semimetals. These materials can be considered as three-dimensional (3D) analogs of graphene, having a gapless, linear dispersion of electronic states, protected by both topology and symmetry. The nontrivial electronic band characteristics of these semimetals cause protected, peculiar surface states such as the so-called Fermi arc. These characteristics also cause unusual magneto-electric responses to applied electric and magnetic fields, such as the so-called chiral anomaly. The experimental investigation of these exotic and peculiar properties has attracted a great deal of attention. In this project, we propose to experimentally explore the novel transport properties in Dirac/Weyl semimetals. The typical Dirac/Weyl semimetals will be synthesized by the chemical vapor transport method to obtain single-crystal 3D samples. In addition, the chemical vapor deposition technique will be applied to obtain single-crystal micro-/nano-structured samples. We will carry out a systematic magneto-transport investigation of these samples at various temperatures, under applied electric and magnetic fields. Our aim will be to reveal and demonstrate the features produced by the chiral anomaly and the Fermi arc. We believe that the fulfillment of this project will advance our understanding of the exotic and peculiar properties of Dirac/Weyl semimetals. We expect that the project’s successful outcome will pave the way for further exploration into the potential applications of Dirac/Weyl semimetals. 在過去十年中，拓撲物質方面的研究一直是凝聚態物理和材料 科學研究人員的首要任務。隨著拓撲絕緣體研究的成功， 拓撲材料家族最近擴展到包括稱為Dirac/Weyl的半金屬。 這些材料可以被認為是石墨烯的三維（3D）類似物，具有 無間隙的線性電子色散關係，受拓撲和對稱性的保護。 這些半金屬的非平凡電子能帶特性會產生受保護的特殊的 表面電子態，例如所謂的費米弧。這些特性還會對所施加 的電場和磁場產生不尋常的磁電響應，例如所謂的手徵異常。 這些奇異和具特殊屬性的實驗研究引起了極大的關注。 在這個項目中，我們建議通過實驗探索Dirac/Weyl半金屬中 的新型輸運性質。典型的Dirac/Weyl半金屬將通過化學氣相 傳輸方法合成以獲得單晶3D樣品。此外，化學氣相沉積技術 將用於獲得單晶微/納米結構樣品。我們將在不同的溫度下， 在施加的電場和磁場下對這些樣品進行系統的輸運性質研究。 我們的目標是揭示和展示手性異常和費米弧產生的特徵。 我們相信，這個項目的實現將推動我們對Dirac/Weyl半金屬 的奇異和特殊屬性的理解。我們預計該項目的成功結果將為 進一步探索Dirac/Weyl半金屬的潛在應用鋪平道路。

16301418.label: Realisation of objectives
16301418.value: We have observed an enhanced superconductivity in Bi2Se3/Nb heterostructures. The superconducting transition temperature and the critical field of Bi2Se3/Nb heterostructures are higher than those of the pristine Nb thin films. Such enhanced superconductivity is due to the improved superfluid stiffness in Nb thin films as it is in proximity to the metallic Bi2Se3 flakes. This work is published in Applied Physics Letters. We demonstrate that we can analyze quantitatively and accurately the weak antilocalization (WAL) effect of topological surface states in topological insulator, BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS), by measuring the anisotropic magnetoconductance. The anomalous conductance peaks induced by the WAL effect of topological surface states of BSTS together with the anisotropic magnetoconductance of bulk states have been observed. By subtracting the anisotropic magnetoconductance of bulk states, we are able to analyse the WAL effect of topological surface states using the Hikami−Larkin−Nagaoka expression. This work is published in Nano Letters. We demonstrate that 2D superconducting (SC) also appears in another TI/Fe1+yTe system, the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe heterostructure. We have systematically studied how the quality of the 2D SC of this heterostructure depends on the fluctuation of the antiferromagnetic (AFM) order of the Fe1+yTe layer and the thickness of the Sb2Te3 layer. Particularly, the results from the former study provide a deeper understanding on the correlation between SC and AFM in this heterostructure, while the results from the latter study support that the topological surface states may be involved in the induction of SC. This work is published in PNAS. We have fabricated the TI thin films of Bi2Te3 with different thicknesses using the molecular beam epitaxy method, and found that these thin films exhibit high electro catalytic activity in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The 48 nm Bi2Te3 thin film has the best performance, which is attributed to its largest active area arising from the spiral growth mode of triangular domains as revealed by atomic force microscopy imaging. Particularly, this work demonstrates that the topological surface states play a key role in enhancing the HER performance. Our study offers a direction to design cost-effective electro catalysts. This work is published in ACS Catalysis. We have performed a systematic magnetotransport study of thick MnBi2Te4 (MBT) flakes with low electron density. A positive linear magnetoresistance (LMR) is observed in high perpendicular fields up to 14 T. Tilted field measurement further reveals the two dimensional nature of this LMR. A two-band analysis of the measured nonlinear Hall effect relates this phenomenon to the high-mobility surface states of MBT. This work is published in PRB and in a PhD thesis. We prepared SnTe (111), SnTe (001) and SnTe (211) topological crystalline insulator (TCI) thin films by molecular beam epitaxy for studying the role of topological surface states and mirror symmetry in electro catalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance. It is found that SnTe (001) and (111) surfaces exhibit intrinsic activities significantly larger than the (211) surface. The high HER activity of SnTe (001) and (111) is attributed to the enhanced charge transfer between H atoms and topological surface states (TSSs). Our study demonstrates that the TSSs and mirror symmetry of TCIs expedite their HER activity. This work is published in Nanoscale. We grown metallic topological material ZrTe2 on STO by pulsed laser deposition. A multilayer structure of ZrTe2/ZrO2/STO due to interface redox reactions was obtained and implied a conductive STO surface. The Shubnikov–de Haas oscillations, observed in angular dependent magnetotransport measurements, revealed a high mobility quasi-2DEG in the STO-based interface. The thickness dependence study suggested the charge transfer effect existing between the capping ZrTe2 and the interfacial 2DEG. This work is published in APL. We directly observed Shubnikov–de Haas (SdH)oscillations in high-quality undoped MnBi2Te4 (MBT). It is shown that the SdH oscillations begin to appear when the MBT is in the canted AFM state. But with increasing fields, the oscillation period decreases. Only in high fields when the FM state is stabilized, single-period SdH oscillations are obtained. By analyzing these high-field SdH oscillations, a nontrivial Berry phase and a small effective mass can be extracted. More importantly, tilting the magnetization direction of ferromagnetic MBT is found to result in a splitting of the SdH oscillations. Such a behavior is believed to arise from the enhanced asymmetry of theWeyl cones in tilted fields. Our work thus reveals the close connection between the band structure of MBT and its magnetic state through the SdH oscillation measurement, demonstrating the effective manipulation of the band structure by external magnetic fields. This work is published in PRB and in a PhD thesis. The old sample preparation setup, which is essential for research activities in relation to Objective 1&2, was broken and a new one was acquired (Metatest E1-G 2D Materials Microscopic Transfer/Stacking System). As a result, a relatively large expenses for "Equipment" was generated in comparison to the approved budget.

16301418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301418.value: We demonstrate that we can analyze quantitatively and accurately the weak antilocalization effect (WAL) effect of topological surface states in topological insulator, BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS), by measuring the anisotropic magnetoconductance. The anomalous conductance peaks induced by the WAL effect of topological surface states of BSTS together with the anisotropic magnetoconductance of bulk states have been observed. By subtracting the anisotropic magnetoconductance of bulk states, we are able to analyze the WAL effect of topological surface states using the Hikami−Larkin−Nagaoka expression. Our findings offer an alternative strategy for the quantitative exploration of the WAL effect of topological surface states in topological insulators. This work is published in Nano Letters. Interfacial superconductivity (SC) is found in the Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructure system, of which neither the Sb2Te3 topological insulator (TI) nor the FeTe parent compound of iron chalcogenides is superconducting. We have systematically studied some factors that are responsible for inducing the 2-dimensional SC, including the spin fluctuation of antiferromagnetic ordering in Fe1+yTe layer and the thickness of Sb2Te3. These findings help us understand the mechanism of the unconventional SC at the interface of TI/FeTe heterostructures. TI/FeTe heterostructures provide a new platform for trapping and controlling Majorana fermions. This work is published in PNAS. The transport properties of MBT thick flakes with low carrier densities is studied. An unsaturated linear magnetoresistance is observed in high fields and persists up to 260 K. Tilted magnetic field measurement also reveals the 2D nature of this phenomenon. The observed nonlinear Hall effect further suggests that this 2D LMR is associated with the high-mobility surface states of MBT. The failure of both the classical and quantum LMR model indicates that new physics must be invoked to understand this phenomenon. This work is published in PRB. Observed SdH oscillations in undoped MBT show sensitively dependence on the magnetic states of MBT. Single-frequency oscillations can only be obtained when the fully polarized FM state is stabilized in high fields. The analysis of these high-field oscillations also yields a nontrivial Berry phase and a small effective mass. Furthermore, rotating the direction of magnetization in tilted fields can lead to a splitting of the SdH oscillation peak, suggesting the enhanced asymmetry of the Weyl cones in MBT. Therefore, our study clearly demonstrates magnetically tunable SdH oscillations in MBT and reveals the important role of magnetization or field in tuning the band structure of MBT. This work is published in PRB.

16301418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301418.value: What we have achieved so far indicate that the existence of novel transport properties in topological materials including topological insulators and Dirac/Weyl semimetals. These novel properties are originated from the gapless, linear dispersion of electronic states, protected by both topology and symmetry. All these results allow for further study of the topological materials especially their heterostructures. Their superconducting and magnetic heterostructures are expected to show many interesting phenomena and worth for further exploration. These should be the future focus of the research and actions to take.

16301418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301418.value: The family of topological materials is expanding to include topological insulators and Dirac/Weyl semimetals. These materials, as three-dimensional analogs of graphene, have gapless and linear dispersion electronic states protected by both topology and symmetry, leading to exotic and peculiar properties. The studies carried out in this project have explored the quantitative analysis of the weak antilocalization effect, interfacial superconductivity, unsaturated linear magnetoresistance, and magnetically tunable SdH oscillations. These results enrich our understanding on topological materials.

16301518.label: Project Objectives
16301518.value: To find a general and unified theory of dissipative toques in antiferromagnets (AFMs) of N-sublattices based on the Rayleigh dissipation functional and general physics principles. For example, the system energy should always dissipate to its environment for any magnetization motion when there is no external energy sources. For an AFM, we should also expect all sublattices equivalent. The theory should explain the first-principle facts in a two-sublattice antiferromagnet that the damping coefficient for the net magnetization motion is one to three orders of magnitude larger than that for the motion of the Neel order parameter. To investigate whether a non-homogeneous static magnetic field can be an efficient and effective knob for manipulating an AFM domain wall. It is well known that an antiferromagnetic order parameter is not sensitive to a homogeneous magnetic field. However, a spatially varying field can be viewed as a constant field plus a Neel field so that an inhomogeneous field might interact with the spins in AFM. Furthermore, one can show that AFM spin textures like DWs and skyrmions have net magnetization so that it can also feel a homogeneous field. The purpose is to find proper inhomogeneous magnetic field that could drive an AFM domain wall moving fast.

16301518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301518.value: There is a reviving interest in antiferromagnetic physics since spin-transfer torque (STT) and anisotropic magnetoresistance were discovered in antiferromagnets (AFMs). These discoveries make AFMs promising spintronic materials beside their only traditional application as a pinning material for ferromagnets. Compare with ferromagnetic devices, AFM devices would have no cross-talking problem and can operate at high speed because AFMs have no stray field and terahertz resonance frequency. However, one needs enough manipulating methods for AFM states first before utilizing the superb properties of AFMs. Thus, the future development of AFM spintronics relies on our detail understanding of antiferromagnetic properties and dynamics so that one may find efficient ways of manipulating spin textures such as AFM domain walls (DWs) and AFM skyrmions. The issues of how to properly describe AFM dynamics and how to control AFM states are the focus of this theoretical proposal. There is little doubt that the magnetization dynamics of ferromagnetic systems is governed by the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation or its generalization with various possible spin torques. In contrast, there are several sets of dynamic equations with different forms of dissipative torques for antiferromagnets (AFMs) in literature. The goal here is to understand the recent first-principle results in a two-sublattice antiferromagnet that the damping coefficient for the net magnetization motion is one to three orders of magnitude larger than that for the motion of the Neel order parameter. Here we intend to derive a unified theory on the dissipative torque for AFMs from the general Rayleigh dissipation functional. So far, the STT is the only confirmed efficient control knob of AFM single domain, and it is important to find other efficient control methods for controlling AFM spin textures such as DWs that are useful in spintronic applications. We shall try to see whether an inhomogeneous magnetic field can drive a DW to propagate at a high speed. It is expected that the outcomes of this study will significantly impact on condensed matter physics in general and the field of spintronics in particular. 自从反铁磁中的自旋转移力矩和各向异性磁电阻被发现以来，反铁磁重新引起了人们的兴趣。反铁磁除了用交换偏置来固定铁磁体磁矩方向这些传统应用之外，亦能通过这些新发现应用于自旋电子器件中。相比于铁磁材料，反铁磁体没有外泄静磁场且其共振频率高达太赫兹量级，从而能够避免磁器件中的串扰问题并且能使之具有极高的操作速度。然而，为了使反铁磁的上述优势能够在器件中得到充分利用，我们首先要掌握如何控制反铁磁的多种状态。因此，反铁磁未来的发展趋势依赖于我们对反铁磁性质及动力学的细致理解，从而使我们能够找到足够有效的方法来控制反铁磁中诸如反铁磁磁畴壁和反铁磁斯格明子的自旋结构。在本理论项目计划中，我们重点关注如何更好地描述反铁磁动力学以及如何控制反铁磁的多种状态。毫无疑问，铁磁系统中的磁动力学能够被朗道-利夫希兹-吉尔伯特方程或其带有多种自旋力矩的普适形式很好地描述。与之不同，在过往的文献中描述反铁磁动力学的运动方程就有多种形式，其耗散力矩也各不相同。这里我们的目标是理解近期双晶格反铁磁的第一性原理计算结果，其结果显示净磁矩的耗散系数相比奈尔序参量下的耗散系数小一到三个量级。我们希望从普适瑞利耗散泛函导出反铁磁耗散力矩的统一理论。到目前为止，仅有自旋转移力矩被证实为控制反铁磁单畴粒子的有效手段，这就迫使我们去寻找其它有效的方法去控制反铁磁里的多种自旋结构，比如在自旋电子器件中十分有用的磁畴壁。我们将去探究反铁磁中的非匀强磁场能否驱动磁畴壁的高速运动。我们相信该项目的研究成果将会对凝聚态物理特别是自旋电子学领域产生重要的影响。

16301518.label: Realisation of objectives
16301518.value: We have largely realized our objectives. The outcomes are more than we expected. We have successfully derived a set of dynamical equations applicable to both anti-ferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic materials, no matter collinear or non-collinear and with any number of sublattices. Anomalies in the switching dynamics of C-type antiferromagnets and antiferromagnetic nanowires were found. AFM order parameter switches away from the easy axis below a critical anisotropy strength when an AFM is properly tailored into a nanostructure. The switching time first decreases and then increases with the damping. Above the critical anisotropy, the AFM order parameter is stable and precesses under a microwave excitation. However, the absorption peak is not at resonance frequency even for magnetic damping as low as 0.01. Furthermore, various interesting AFM domain wall motion under non-uniform magnetic field and current-driven skyrmion motion in granular films as well as interesting wiggling skyrmion motion under parametric pumping have been uncovered.

16301518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301518.value: We have launched investigations in areas related to our objectives. We have found a general and unified theory of dissipative toques in antiferromagnets (AFMs) of N-sublattices based on the Rayleigh dissipation functional and general physics principles. Our general formulation satisfies the second law of thermodynamics that the system energy always dissipates to its environment for any magnetization motion when there are no external energy sources. In our theory, all sublattice of an AFM are equivalent. The theory naturally explains the first-principal facts in a two-sublattice antiferromagnet that the damping coefficient for the net magnetization motion is one to three orders of magnitude larger than that for the motion of the Neel order parameter. These results were published in Europhysics Letters. We have also found Anomalies in the switching dynamics of C-type antiferromagnets and antiferromagnetic nanowires. It is found that AFM order parameter switches away from the easy axis below a critical anisotropy strength when an AFM is properly tailored into a nanostructure. The switching time first decreases and then increases with the damping. Above the critical anisotropy, the AFM order parameter is stable and precesses under a microwave excitation. However, the absorption peak is not at resonance frequency even for magnetic damping as low as 0.01. These interesting studies result in several publications in Physical Review B and Physical Review Research. We wrote an invited review for Europhysics Letters on our findings in anti-ferromagnetic systems. We have also studied the dynamics of skyrmions in granular AFM films under electric current. Interestingly, the transverse motion is a random walk. The work was recently published in Phys. Rev. B. Related to this project, we have also wrote a book chapter for a book entitled Chirality, Magnetism and Magnetoelectricity by Springer. Recently, we have also reexamined our current understanding of anisotropic magnetoresistance (MR). It is predicted that such a MR for anti-ferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic materials, especially those of non-collinear ones, should be very interesting. The paper is published in Chinese Physics Letters. We reexamined another interesting phenomenon called spin-Hall MR. Interestingly, the anomalous angular dependences of MR have nothing to do with spin-Hall effect.

16301518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301518.value: Recently we were awarded a new RGC grant for studying magnetic domain wall (DW) motion of ferrimagnets near the angular momentum compensation point. The dynamic equations obtained in the current project are the starting point of the new project. The new project aims to understand the high DW speed of over thousand meters per second observed in recent years. Also, we are exploring other aspects of magnetic systems and their dynamics. We will also consider their experimental realization and applications.

16301518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301518.value: The studies of anti-ferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic materials have a very long history. Surprisingly, there were no well-established dynamical equations suitable for anti-ferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic materials. For a long time, people have used the LLG equation used for ferromagnetic materials to study anti-ferromagnetic dynamics. In this project, we have found a general and unified theory. The set of dynamical equations fully satisfy the second law of thermodynamics so that the energy of a system without external driving forces always dissipates to its environment. The theory allows us to investigate dynamics of various spin textures such as DW, skyrmions, or single domains. Use the theory, we obtained a number interesting and novel results in reversal of anti-ferromagnetic domain, AFM skyrmion motion in granular media, and high speed ferrimagnetic DW motion near the angular momentum compensation point. These investigations results in a number of publications including invited reviews.

16301618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301618.value: This proposal aims at two subjects. The first one is the spectral statistics of the Laplacian matrix and normalized Laplacian matrix of the inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi random graph. The other concerns the kernel of random matrices. The classical Erdos-Renyi random graph falls short of modeling the real-world networks. For instance, it does not allow the appearance of communities. In order to approach various situations of many complex networks, we consider a more general graph model, the inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi random graph. The matrices associated with random graphs are random matrices. There are different types of matrices for a graph, i.e. the adjacency matrix, the Laplacian matrix and normalized Laplacian matrix. With the remarkable development in the area of random matrix theory, the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix of the classical Erdos-Renyi random graph have been well-studied. The Laplacian matrix and normalized Laplacian matrix are much harder to study because of the complicated dependence among their entries. Much less is known about both. The PI is going to study the extreme eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix and normalized Laplacian matrix of this model. Such results have broad applications in graph partitioning, data clustering, network robustness and synchronizability in complex networks. The study of kernels of random matrices has a long history dating back to the 1970s. Kashin and Garnaev-Gluskin used the kernels of special random matrices to study the Gelfand balls. Their results turned out later to have many applications in compressive sensing. In a series of works by Rudelson-Vershynin and Tao-Vu on the least singular values of random matrices, one essential step is to understand the structure of the kernels of random matrices. On the application side, a fundamental question in the heart of many areas such as signal processing and applied mathematics is to understand whether or not the kernel of random matrices intersects a feasible set. The question turns out to be equivalent to studying the restricted smallest singular value of random matrices on this set. For Gaussian matrices, the analysis is relatively easy due to the rich algebraic structures of Gaussian distributions. Recently, Oymak and Tropp established a striking universality result about the restricted smallest singular value. The PI proposes to further investigate the restricted smallest singular values, study the structure of the kernels and prove universality results on the limiting distribution of kernels of random matrices. 在本项目，我们考虑两类问题。第一类问题是关于ER 随机图模型的拉普拉斯矩阵和规范拉普拉斯矩阵的谱性质的研究。另外一类问题是关于随机矩阵的核的研究。 关于随机图的研究， 其重要的一个分支是，利用谱方法来研究图的性质。具体来讲，我们研究随机图所对应的关联矩阵，拉普拉斯矩阵或者规范拉普拉斯矩阵的特征值和特征向量， 这些参数包含了随机图的很多信息。ER 随机图模型所对应的矩阵是随机矩阵。ER 随机图模型的关联矩阵是一类结构比较简单的随机矩阵：它是对称矩阵，并且上三角的元素是独立随机变量，因此和Wigner矩阵有着直接的联系。随着近几年在随机矩阵方向的研究的飞速发展，ER 随机图模型的关联矩阵的特征值和特征向量的很多性质都得到了证明。相对来说，ER 随机图模型的拉普拉斯矩阵或者规范拉普拉斯矩阵具有更复杂的结构，因此它们的谱性质还没有被充分研究。在本项目中，我们将侧重于研究ER 随机图模型的拉普拉斯矩阵以及规范拉普拉斯矩阵的极端特征值，它们的性质在图论和理论计算机科学等领域有着重要的应用。 随机矩阵的核的研究可以追溯到上个世纪七十年代，比如Kashin, Garnaev和Gluskin等数学家利用随机矩阵的核来得到Gelfand球的性质。在最近几年，随机矩阵的核在压缩感知方向有了广泛的应用，其中一个重要的问题是随机矩阵的核是否和给定的一个凸集合有交集。这个问题等价于研究随机矩阵限制在这个凸集合上的最小的奇异值是否为零。对于高斯随机矩阵，人们已经得到了对于限制在凸集合的最小奇异值的估计，这是非渐进性的结果。在Oymak和Tropp最近的一篇论文中，他们把结果从高斯随机矩阵推广到更广泛的随机矩阵。我们计划推进建立随机矩阵的核的理论基础，侧重于得到渐进理论方面的结果。

16301618.label: Realisation of objectives
16301618.value: Both objectives of the project have been fully achieved. We have demonstrated that the adjacency matrix $A$ of an inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi random graph can be modeled as a perturbative random matrix, where $A$ is decomposed as $A = MA + E$, with $MA$ representing the expected matrix of $A$, and $E$ being a centered random matrix. The perturbative random matrix model is a powerful tool for analyzing the spectral properties of the adjacency matrix $A$. By leveraging the perturbative nature of the model, we have shown that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $A$ can be approximated by those of $MA$ plus small perturbations from $E$. We have also employed tools from random matrix theory to explore the distribution of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $A$, by considering the distribution of the eigenvalues of $MA$ and the distribution of the entries of $E$, which are modeled as independent and identically distributed random variables. In addition, we have carried out a systematic study on the statistical behavior of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors and singular values and singular vectors of different perturbative random matrix models. By using tools from random matrix theory, we have obtained a comprehensive understanding of the spectral behavior of the perturbative random matrix models, thereby addressing the first objective of the project. Furthermore, we have shown that the tools and methods developed in our works apply to understanding the limiting distribution of the null subspaces of random matrices, which can be thought of as spanned by the singular vectors corresponding to the zero singular values. Thus, we have achieved our second objective as well. I was not able to travel or invite visitors to Hong Kong because of the travel restrictions.

16301618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301618.value: In our paper published in Annals of Statistics (2021), we analyze the perturbative random matrix model $Y = S + X$, where $S$ is a low-rank deterministic signal matrix and $X$ is a random noise matrix with dimensions $M imes n$. We investigate the behavior of outlier singular vectors of $Y$ under general assumptions on the structure of $S$ and the distribution of $X$ when $M$ and $n$ are comparable and the signals are supercritical. Our results include the limiting distribution of the angles between the principal singular vectors of $Y$ and their deterministic counterparts, which are the singular vectors of $S$, as well as the distribution of the distance between the subspaces spanned by the principal singular vectors of $Y$ and those of $S$. Although this paper was submitted before the grant start date, the revisions and final publication were made possible through the support of this grant. The research described in the paper is closely linked to the work conducted under the grant, and the findings and conclusions of the paper are integral to the overall research project. Therefore, I believe it is appropriate to acknowledge the grant in this paper, as it played a significant role in its revision and finalization. In another paper published in the Annals of Statistics (2022), we extend our research to a multiplicative perturbation model. In particular, we consider the spiked covariance matrix model and establish the joint distribution of the extreme eigenvalues and their associated eigenvectors in the supercritical regime, which is important in Principal Component Analysis from a statistical perspective. In our paper published in CSIAM Trans. Appl. Math. (2021), we investigate the applications of random projections in deep neural networks. Specifically, we analyze the expressive power of fully connected neural networks when the input data are either sparse vectors or from a low-dimensional smooth manifold. Our results demonstrate that the number of neurons needed to approximate a Lipschitz function with a specified precision is dependent on the sparsity or the dimension of the manifold, and only weakly dependent on the dimension of the input vector.

16301618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301618.value: The PI has undertaken a study of the Laplacian matrix $L=D-A$ of the Erdos-Renyi random graphs $G(n,p)$, where $D$ is the diagonal degree matrix and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of the graph. At the edges of the spectrum, $L$ can be viewed as $D$ perturbed by a smaller noise $A$, leading us to expect that the extreme eigenvalues of $L$ are dominated by those of $D$. However, obtaining a clear picture of the extreme eigenvalues of $D$ is challenging due to the discrete and correlated nature of its diagonal entries. To address this issue, we have extended 2-dimensional strong approximation results to study the order statistics of the diagonal entries of $D$. Another challenge is to decouple the dependence between $D$ and $A$. During our exploration, we discovered that Andrew Campbell and Sean O'Rourke had achieved such results in their paper (arXiv:2211.17175), where they assumed that $A$ has Gaussian entries. We believe that the method used in their paper could potentially be useful in obtaining more general results when $A$ is discrete and sparse, which is of significant interest.

16301618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301618.value: In this project, we have also conducted a thorough investigation into the statistical behavior of the eigenvalues, eigenvectors, singular values, and singular vectors of different perturbative random matrix models using tools from random matrix theory. Additionally, we have demonstrated that the methods developed in our work can be applied to understand the limiting distribution of the null subspaces of random matrices.

16301718.label: Realisation of objectives
16301718.value: We investigated an equivariant system of the Euler-Poincaré presentation of the r-depth Berstein projector and investigated a refined version of the system, for each depth r, which is a non-negative rational number. One of our main tools is a notion of associate classes of cuspidal pairs for Moy–Prasad quotients. We also investigated decompositions of an equivariant system of idempotents indexed by facets in a refined Bruhat-Tits building associated to a simple p-adic group, into more atomic equivariant systems. We apply these new Euler–Poincaré presentations to obtain decompositions of the resolutions of Schneider–Stuhler and Bestvina–Savin. All the objectives have been achieved.

16301718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301718.value: For k is a non-archimedean local field and G is an absolutely quasi-simple linear algebraic group defined over k. Let G be the group of k-rational points, and B = B(G) the Bruhat–Tits building of G. For N a positive integer, let BN be the refined building, and suppose C is the equivalence class of a cuspidal associate pair of depth r. We introduced and studied a certain alternating sum D(C) of the equivariant system of idempotents. We proved the properties of the sum D(C) and finally, we prove that the depth r-Berstein projector is a sum of D(C) for C over depth r. The resolutions of Schneider–Stuhler and Bestvina–Savin played important roles in the theory of representations of simple groups over p-adic fields. We applied our results about the decomposition of depth r Bernstein projector to obtain a decomposition of the resolutions.

16301718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301718.value: Our method and results can be extended to non-split groups. For simplicity, we proved our main results under the assumption that the groups are split, but we indicated how minor modifications were needed to prove our main for the non-split case.

16301718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301718.value: The representations of simple groups over non-archimedean fields are important objects in representation theory. The notions of r-depth of the representations and the associated Berstein projector are canonical concepts much used in the study. On the other hand, there are Bruhat-Tits buildings associated with such groups. The decomposition formula we proved in this project connects two types of invariant distributions on the groups: one type of distribution is from representations of the groups, and the other type is from the Bruhar-Tits buildings. We established the connections of them in terms of the Euler-Poincaré sum.

16301818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301818.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study negative nonlinear friction induced by two-phonon processes in micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators. In resonant sensors, vibrations of the micromechanical element are often excited by a periodic drive near the resonance frequency. By tracking changes in the resonance frequencies, the devices can be used in applications that range from inertial sensing to high-sensitivity force and mass detection. When a mechanical resonator is coupled to an optical, microwave or phonon cavity, the effective linear damping can be modified by one-phonon processes with pumping at the primary sideband of the cavity. By changing the pumping to the secondary sideband to induce two-phonon processes, the damping can be made nonlinear. Both the sign and magnitude of the nonlinear damping is tunable by the pumping. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the various mechanisms by which nonlinear friction can affect the driven and self-sustained vibrations. Two vibrational modes of a micromechanical resonator will be involved, with driving applied to the secondary sidebands of the mode at the higher frequency. Preliminary measurements indicate that negative nonlinear friction on the low frequency mode can be made strong enough to overcome the energy loss due to the intrinsic, positive linear friction so that self-sustained vibrations occur. Remarkably, excitation of these self-sustained vibrations requires a large initial perturbation. We propose to explore the conditions for which self-sustained vibrations can be excited. Furthermore, we plan to investigate how negative nonlinear friction can stabilize large-amplitude vibrations when the low frequency mode is subjected to resonant or parametric driving. Unlike system with only conservative nonlinearity, the response can be large and multi-valued even with weak driving, with the emergence of new bifurcation points. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but could also lead to micromechanical detectors of improved sensitivity and functionality. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. In the past few years, his group performed a comprehensive investigation of the switching between coexisting vibration states induced by Gaussian and Poisson noise on a nonlinear micromechanical torsional oscillator under strong periodic drive. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors in the phase fluctuations of self-sustained oscillations in micromechanical resonators. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究微機械諧振器中由雙聲子作用導致的負非線性阻力現象。微機械諧振器被廣泛應用于傳感器和致動器。在諧振傳感器中，微機械元件的振動通常由共振頻率附近的週期性驅動力所激發。通過監測共振頻率的變化，器件可被應用于從慣性傳感到高靈敏度的力與質量的測量。當一個微機械諧振器與光腔，微波腔，或者聲子腔相耦合時，在腔的一級邊帶泵浦所引起的單聲子作用可以改變諧振器的有效線性阻尼。把泵浦頻率改成二級邊帶則會引起雙聲子作用，使阻尼被變成非線性。非線性阻尼的正負和大小都可以通過泵浦來調節。 提案中研究的重點在於揭示非線性阻力能夠影響受迫振動和自激振動的多種機制。實驗包含微機械諧振子的兩種震動模式，並且在高頻模式的二級邊帶上施加驅動力。初步的測量結果表明，低頻模式上的負非線性阻力可以被增強到能夠克服固有的正線性阻力所造成的能量損失，進而產生自激振動。值得注意的是，激發這種自激振動需要一個較大的初始擾動。我們打算探究能夠激發這種自激振動的條件。此外，我們計劃研究當低頻模式被施加了諧振驅動力或者參數驅動力時，負非線性阻力如何穩定大振幅的振動。不同於只有保守非線性的系統的是，即使驅動力較弱，也可以得到較強而且多值的響應，而且有新的分岔點出現。提案中實驗的成功實施不僅能夠推動新的理論研究，驗證多種理論方法的正確性，還能夠促進微機械探測器的發展，提高其靈敏度和功能性。 主要研究者在微機械器件的波動現象這一領域有豐富的經驗。過去幾年中，他的團隊在強周期性驅動力下，非線性微機械扭轉諧振器受高斯噪聲和泊松噪聲的激發而在多個并存振動態之間相互切換方面做了大量的研究。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的理論物理學家Mark Dykman教授緊密合作，揭示微機械諧振器中自激振蕩的相位漲落現象。

16302018.value: To investigate the nature of topological superconductivity in NbxBi2Se3 and related compounds to clarify whether it is in the nematic or chiral topological superconducting phase. To study the mechanisms that cause the pinning of the two-fold order parameter symmetry along a particular crystalline direction in the basal plane of doped Bi2Se3 in the nematic superconducting phase through uniaxial strain. To test whether the nematic superconducting state in NbxBi2Se3 can be driven into the chiral superconducting state or vice versa by applying external control parameters such as pressure, strain, magnetic fields or temperature. To clarify the nature of the topological order in anomalous quantum Hall insulator - superconductor heterostructures by nano-point-contact spectroscopy at the sample edge in different applied magnetic fields to find the characteristic fingerprints of the topological surface states with one and two Majorana fermions. To investigate whether the high magnetic field Ising superconducting state in mono- or few-layer NbSe2 represents the theoretically predicted nodal topological superconducting state. To investigate whether the proximity-induced superconductivity at low temperatures in the Bi2Te3 layer of an FeTe/Bi2Te3 exhibiting intrinsic interfacial superconductivity is a topological superconducting phase and to clarify its nature (e.g. nematic or chiral).
