16302018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302018.value: Topological condensed matter systems are a focus of recent research because of the rich variety of novel electronic states they host - in particular their topologically-protected unusual edge states. In this proposed study, we will investigate a variety of topological - or potentially topological - superconductors. These materials feature a superconducting energy gap in their bulk, but have gapless states at the edge, which are considered to be condensed matter quasiparticle analogs of Majorana fermions in fundamental particle physics. We will use the rich variety of experimental tools in our laboratory to study a selection of 2D and 3D topological superconducting materials. The doped topological insulator Bi2Se3 was theoretically predicted to host two distinct topological superconducting states: the nematic and the chiral Weyl superconducting phases, which spontaneously break the crystalline and time-reversal symmetry, respectively. We will clarify the nature of the topological superconductivity using magnetic field-angle-resolved and linear thermal expansion experiments in combination with experiments that are sensitive to time-reversal symmetry breaking, such as DC magnetization and the Hall effect. We will also work with high pressure as a control parameter to determine whether one topological phase can be driven into another. When superconductivity is induced in a quantum anomalous Hall insulator, it has been argued that there exist two different topological superconducting phases with one or two Majorana fermionic edge states that can be switched by the reversal of the magnetization in the anomalous quantum Hall insulator by a sweep of an applied perpendicular magnetic field. However, the topological nature of these phases has recently been questioned by some theoretical work. We will clarify this phenomenon evaluating the spectroscopic signature of the different Majorana edge states using a nano-point-contact technique applied to the sample edge. Another topological superconducting state was theoretically predicted in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides such as NbSe2, which enters in an unusual Ising superconducting state in high parallel magnetic fields. With field-angle-resolved experiments and tunneling experiments, which we will realize in a graphene-NbSe2 junction, we will look for characteristic fingerprints of topological superconductivity. Finally, we will apply our field-angle-resolved experiments to a FeTe/Bi2Te3 interface in which we have observed a proximity-induced superconductivity at low temperature to clarify the possible topological nature of the superconductivity. 拓扑凝聚态物质，由于其具有丰富的奇特的电子态，尤其是受拓扑保护、非寻常的边界态，使其成为最近研究的重点。在这份研究计划中，我们将探究一系列的拓扑，或潜在的拓扑超导材料。这类材料在块材时具有超导能隙，而在其边界处超导能隙为零，这种边界态被认为是基础粒子物理学中的马约拉那费米子的凝聚态准粒子对应。我们将采用我们实验室里丰富的实验方法，对一系列特定的二维和三维拓扑超导材料展开研究。掺杂的拓扑绝缘体Bi2Se3，理论上预测具有两个不同的拓扑超导相：拓扑向列相和手性外尔超导相，前者将自发地破坏晶格对称性，后者将自发地破坏时间反演对称性。为了研究清楚这种拓扑超导体的性质，我们将使用诸如磁角分辨，线性热膨胀等实验方式，并结合对时间反演对称性破缺敏感的实验手段，比如直流磁化率和霍尔效应。我们还将采用高压作为一种控制参数，来探究是否可以实现两个拓扑超导相之间的转变。当超导效应引入至量子反常霍尔效应绝缘体时，有争论认为将存在两个不同的拓扑超导相，并拥有一个和两个马约拉那费米子边缘态。这些边缘态可以通过磁化率的反转而进行转换，而磁化率的反转可以通过对量子反常霍尔效应绝缘层施加一个垂直方向的扫描磁场来实现。然而，这些超导相的拓扑性质近期遭到了一些理论工作的质疑。我们希望能通过在样品边缘的纳米级点接触技术得到的谱信号来探究这个问题。另一种理论预测的拓扑超导态存在于二维的过渡金属二硫化物中，例如NbSe2，在施加一个强的平行方向磁场时会进入一种非寻常的伊辛超导相(Ising superconductivity)。通过磁角分辨和隧穿谱实验，我们将制备石墨烯-二硒化铌异质结，并探究拓扑超导相存在的特征信号。最后，我们还将利用磁角分辨实验去探究Bi2Te3—FeTe（拓扑绝缘体-铁基超导体）界面的拓扑超导性质，而对于这一体系我们已发现在低温下由邻近效应导致的超导态。

16302018.label: Realisation of objectives
16302018.value: Objectives 1 - 3 focus on nematic superconductivity in the doped topological insulator Bi2Te3. They have all been achieved and are addressed in our publication in Nat. Commun. 11, 3056 (2020) with the details described below. NbxBi2Se3 and CuxBi2Se3 were investigated by specific heat, thermal expansion, DC magnetization and electrical transport with high magnetic fields along different crystal directions and uniaxial pressure as additional control parameters. All experiments confirmed that all investigated compounds are in the nematic superconducting state, regardless of the exact Nb or Cu content, thus achieving objective 1. Our thermal expansion data showed that a crystalline deformation occurred 0.5 K above the critical temperature for superconductivity. The crystalline deformation occurred together with the onset of superconducting fluctuations, which became visible in the form of a very weak Meissner contribution, a tiny drop in resistance and a small anomaly in the specific heat above Tc, which confirmed the connection between the crystalline deformation and the appearance of phase incoherent Cooper pairs. With our theoretical collaborator J. Schmalian from Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, we were able to explain this by a multi-component order parameter, where superconductivity is the primary order parameter and the nematic order causing the deformation is a vestigial order. In the presence of strong fluctuations, caused by the low-dimensional layer structure, this can lead to a vestigial phase in which the primary order loses phase coherence but leaves a residual symmetry breaking above the superconducting order, represented by the breaking of Z3 rotational symmetry in the form of a twofold distortion. Cooper pairs above Tc thus fluctuate in a way that breaks the crystalline rotational symmetry, which, together with microscopic parameters such as lattice defects or strain, dictates the orientation of the twofold nematic superconducting order parameter below Tc, thus fulfilling objective 2. To achieve objective 3, we have used uniaxial pressure, doping concentration and high magnetic fields as control parameters to influence the superconducting order parameter. Moreover, the combination of thermal expansion and specific heat provides the initial uniaxial strain dependence of the phase transitions through thermodynamic relations without the need to apply real strain. For all investigated samples with different dopants (copper and niobium) in which superconductivity existed, only nematic superconductivity was observed. We found that strain and high magnetic fields stabilized the nematicity even further. For example, we were able to induce traces of nematic superconductivity in a non-superconducting, underdoped CuxBi2Se3 sample by applying uniaxial pressure. The only remaining path to chiral superconductivity in doped Bi2Se3 would require even stronger magnetism than in NbxBi2Se3, which could be achieved by intercalating elements with stronger magnetic moments. We have tried to obtain Fe-doped Bi2Se3 samples from our collaborators, but so far, they have not been able to produce superconducting samples. Objective 4 was achieved and focuses on chiral Majorana modes in a quantum anomalous Hall insulator/superconductor heterostructure. It is covered in our publication in PNAS 117 (1) 238-242 (2019). We have fabricated nano-point contacts at the edge of a quantum anomalous Hall insulator/superconductor heterostructure and performed Andreev reflection spectroscopy to investigate the characteristic fingerprint of chiral Majorana modes. We reproducibly observed the predicted Andreev reflection signature of two different topological superconducting phases with two and one chiral Majorana modes, respectively, which formed a dip-like structure around the zero-bias surrounded by two peaks, as well as a plateau-like structure in the differential conductivity as a function of bias voltage. Our theory collaborator K. T. Law from HKUST provided the corresponding theoretical simulations, which were adapted to our device geometry in excellent agreement with the experimental data. Since an earlier publication claiming the observation of chiral Majorana modes was withdrawn, our work remains the only reported observation. As a continuation of the project, we had successfully applied for an ongoing GRF follow-up proposal in which we are trying to localize these chiral Majorana modes at the ends of narrow ~100 nm wide nanoribbons and search for them with Andreev reflectance spectroscopy. Objective 5 was achieved and will is covered in our paper in Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 087002 (2022). While we already reported the first results in the midterm report, we spent the second period producing more data of higher quality in order to be able to publish the data in this high-impact journal. We performed a very detailed series of field-angle-resolved measurements of the upper critical field (Hc2) by rotating a magnetic field strictly parallel to 2D samples of NbSe2 and measuring the electric transport. The angular dependence of Hc2 in the plane of single-layer NbSe2 revealed a sixfold nodal symmetry of the superconducting order parameter near the upper critical field transition, which was not present in thicker samples with multiple layers. This confirms the theoretical prediction of a topological Weyl superconducting state in the superconducting Ising phase of single-layer NbSe2 with six point-node pairs. However, we also found that at lower temperatures and fields, the nodal order parameter was replaced by a distinct nematic superconducting order, which was unexpected. While the nodal phase was consistent with the predictions, with the help of our theoretical collaborator J. Schmalian at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, we were able to explain the latter unexpected phase by the existence of several competing superconducting channels consisting of a primary single component order parameter competing with a sub-leading unconventional two-component order parameter. Objective 6. has been covered in our accepted manuscript in Advanced Electronic Materials to appear in 2023. In this project, we first searched for evidence of a nematic and chiral superconducting state in two-dimensional FeTe/Bi2Te3 heterostructures by performing field-angle resolved Hc2 measurements. Hc2 did not exhibit significant angular changes when a magnetic field applied strictly parallel to the basal plane was rotated in-plane. Therefore, a nematic superconducting order parameter can be excluded. The DC magnetization showed a pronounced paramagnetic Meissner effect, i.e. positive magnetization at relatively weak magnetic fields instead of the usual negative diamagnetism. This is almost certainly related to the interaction of superconductivity with the local magnetism of clusters of interstitial Fe, which appear to be on the borderline of ferromagnetic ordering. However, magnetism is probably not strong enough to form a chiral state. We have therefore searched for topological superconductivity in a different way, by looking for the spectroscopic signature of localized Majorana modes in narrow nanoribbons of this heterostructure. We have fabricated 100 nm wide nanoribbons extending from a region of bare FeTe to a region of a FeTe/Bi2Te3 heterostructure. The FeTe portion of the nanowire served as a normal conducting lead for Andreev reflection spectroscopy at the interface with the FeTe/Bi2Te3 nanoribbon. Theory predicts that for a topological insulator nanowire in proximity contact with an s-wave superconductor, a Majorana mode should form and localize at the end of the nanowire when a magnetic field is applied parallel to the nanowire. We observed a zero-bias conductance peak with a height close to the quantization of 2e2/h, which can be controlled by a parallel magnetic field, consistent with the predictions. Further confirmation is needed through collaboration with other groups. We see the purpose of our publication as providing a new platform for the search for Majorana physics, as our device contains a particularly clean, epithelial-grown tunneling interface that avoids shortcomings of other approaches.

16302018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302018.value: We could show that NbxBi2Se3 and CuxBi2Se3 superconductors are always in the nematic superconducting phase. A crystalline deformation above the superconducting transition temperature was observed, which is associated with the appearance of phase incoherent preformed Cooper pairs due to superconducting fluctuations in the low-dimensional layered sample. We have proposed a theoretical framework to describe this in the context of a multi-component order parameter, where the superconductivity is the primary order parameter and the nematic order causing the deformation is a vestigial order (see part C 8, no. 2, C 9, no. 3). Using nano-point contacts at the edge of a quantum anomalous Hall insulator/superconductor heterostructure, we found the theoretically predicted Andreev reflection signature of two different topological superconducting phases with two and one chiral Majorana modes, respectively, forming a dip-like structure around the zero-bias surrounded by two peaks and a plateau-like structure, respectively, in the differential conductivity vs. bias voltage (see part C 8, no. 1, C 9, nos. 1-4). Using field-angle-resolved upper critical field measurements, we found a sixfold nodal symmetry of the superconducting order parameter of a topological Weyl superconducting state, which is supposed to form in the Ising superconducting phase of single-layer NbSe2. We also found that at lower temperatures and fields the nodal order parameter was replaced by a nematic superconducting order, which was unexpected. We could explain the latter by the existence of several competing superconducting channels consisting of a primary one-component order parameter competing with a sub-leading unconventional two-component order parameter (see part C 8, no. 3). We fabricated narrow nanoribbons from a FeTe/Bi2Te3 heterostructure and performed Andreev reflection point contact spectroscopy. We observed a nearly quantized zero-bias conductance peak whose height could be controlled by a magnetic field applied parallel to the nanoribbon. This is consistent with theoretical predictions for a topological insulator nanowire in proximity contact with an s-wave superconductor, where a Majorana mode is localized at the end of the nanowire. In this way, we were able to present a new platform for the search for Majorana physics using an intrinsic, particularly clean, epitaxially grown tunneling interface that avoids many shortcomings of other approaches to the search for Majorana zero modes based on free-standing nanowires (see part C 8, n. 4).

16302018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302018.value: With Objectives 1-3, we have gathered important information about the nature of the nematic superconducting state in the form of a multicomponent order parameter scenario that answers the most important remaining questions about this state. This knowledge can now be applied to other nematic superconductors, which we have already done when we found another nematic superconducting state in single-layer NbSe2 (Objective 4). The spectroscopic evidence for chiral Majorana modes in a heterostructure of quantum anomalous Hall insulator and superconductor (QAHI/SC), addressed in Objective 4, motivated us to successfully submit a GRF follow-up proposal to search for localized Majorana modes in narrow QAHI/SC nanoribbons. The detection of a topological Weyl superconductor phase with six pairs of point nodes in single-layer NbSe2 (Objective 5) encourages further experiments to search for the predicted Majorana arcs connecting the Weyl points. For this purpose, we have developed a special scanning tunneling probe. In addition, this work has inspired us to investigate NbSe2 and NbS2 in the bulk, where we found an unusual Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov state (which became the subject of another successful GRF application). Finally, narrow FeTe/Bi2Te3 nanoribbon heterostructures proved to be a promising new platform for the search for topological superconductivity, which we will pursue further.

16302018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302018.value: Topological materials are classified as materials in which the electronic wave functions have a different symmetry than the crystalline structure. They are of great fundamental and technological importance for new device applications. In a solid, electrons often mimic the properties of other elementary particles called quasiparticles. In a topological superconductor, the main interest is not only the disappearance of electric resistance, but also the prediction that they host Majorana quasiparticles. These are of great interest for future quantum computers as they allow for more fault-tolerant operation. Potential topological superconductors are rarely found, and our work has provided evidence for at least four different topological superconducting phases and contributed to the understanding of their fundamental properties. These include nematic superconductors, where superconductivity breaks crystalline rotational symmetries, chiral superconductivity in a superconducting quantum anomalous Hall insulator, where electrons circulate without loss around the edge of a thin film sample, an unusual topological field-induced state in two-dimensional layers of a transition metal dichalcogenide superconductor, and superconductivity occurring at the interface when two non-superconducting materials are grown on top of each other to form a heterostructure.

16302218.label: Project Objectives
16302218.value: To extend the classical thin plate theory to include Willis coupling between the velocity and stress fields and between the strain and momentum fields. The new plate theory will provide a macroscopic description of metamaterial plates with Willis coupling. To develop a structural design supporting Willis coupling and to develop the homogenization theory for such a metamaterial plate. To fabricate elastic metamaterials using 3D printing techniques with multi-material extrusion. To develop an experimental setup for measuring elastic wave fields on a plate, from which we will be able to extract the transmission and reflection spectra of an elastic metamaterial plate. To accomplish the first experimental proof of metamaterial plates with Willis coupling and to demonstrate the associated asymmetric reflection properties. To explore associated applications of Willis coupling, such as coherent control, sensing and asymmetric wave-front control.

16302218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302218.value: The recent development of mechanical metamaterials has freed us from the limited palette of elastic material parameters provided by the conventional composite approach. A negative refractive index and cross-polarized Fabry-Pérot resonance are some of the newly established concepts in this regard. Specifically, Willis and Milton predicted that proper micro-structured elastic material, now termed Willis media, could realize an analog of bianisotropy. This has been investigated in-depth in electromagnetic materials, but has never been accomplished in conventional elastic materials. In the past 2 years, we have witnessed rapid theoretical development and very recent experimental demonstrations of its acoustic counterpart, but not in the full-wave elastic case. We will extend the concept of Willis media to the plate theory for the propagation of bending waves using theoretical and experimental techniques. We will seek to (i) extend the classical plate theory to describe Willis media, (ii) design relevant microstructures to generate the required Willis coupling, and (iii) experimentally demonstrate wave phenomena and applications specially tided with the media. We will focus on asymmetric wave propagation and the possible appearance of exceptional points, which will be used as a new recipe for sensing with enhanced sensitivity. Given that classical plate theory has been widely used in mechanical engineering from the very large wings of aircrafts to the micro-sized cantilevers of atomic force microscopes, the extended plate theory with microstructures and Willis parameters will unlock the potential of the metamaterials approach to elastic wave applications including non-destructive testing and sensing. The understanding gained from the proposed project will also facilitate the application of Willis media to surface acoustic wave devices and seismic wave control. 機械超材料的最新發展使我們擺脫了傳統複合材料提供的有限的彈性材料參數。彈性波負折射率和涉及交叉偏振的法布里－珀羅共振是其中一些在這方面新建立的概念。此前，威利斯和米爾頓預測，通過適當的微結構彈性材料可以實現雙向各向異性，被稱為威利斯介質或威利斯耦合。雙向各向異性在電磁材料中存在已久。在過去的兩年中，我們見證了其空氣聲學對應的實驗演示，但在固體彈波性材料中從未實現過。在這個項目中，我們將同時使用理論和實驗將威利斯介質的概念擴展到彈性板波傳播理論。我們將尋求（i）擴展經典板理論以描述威利斯介質，（ii）設計相關的微結構以產生所需的威利斯耦合，以及（iii）通過實驗演示與威利斯耦合相關的現象。我們將專注於非對稱波傳播和特殊點的出現，可以應用於傳感裝置靈敏度的增強。經典板理論一直被廣泛應用於從大型飛機機翼到原子力顯微鏡的微尺寸懸臂不同種類的的機械結構中，具有微觀結構和威利斯參數的板理論將釋放超材料對彈性波的潛力，應用包括無損檢測和傳感。從這項目中獲得的理論也將有助於威利斯介質在聲表面波裝置和地震波控制中的應用。

16302218.label: Realisation of objectives
16302218.value: 1. We have extended the classical Timoshenko-beam and Mindlin-plate theories to include Willis coupling term for flexural waves. As a result, we have found that there is a new constitutive parameter, i.e. the Willis coupling, between shear force and out-of-plane velocity or equivalently between out-of-plane momentum and shear strain. Together with bending stiffness and density, all these three parameters have to be used to describe a plate or beam with mirror-symmetry breaking. In the later part of the project, we further extend the concept of Willis coupling from flexural waves to torsional waves and also water waves; basically cover different kinds of mechanical waves. Objective 1 is fully implemented. 2. We have designed several metamaterial structures with mirror-symmetry breaking to give a significant Willis coupling term in the constitutive parameters. It turned out a cantilever-type resonating structure serves such a purpose, for both flexural and torsional waves. For water waves, we have developed resonators (for wave shoaling) with mirror symmetry breaking to achieve Willis coupling. Regarding homogenization theory, we have developed a field-averaging technique based on the numerically simulated eigenmodes to extract the constitutive parameters. The field-averaging technique is then applied to Willis metamaterials on torsional waves and water waves as well. Objective 2 is fully implemented. 3. 3d-printing has been used to fabricate the Willis metamaterials from collaborator in Shenzhen University and also our own machines. Finally we have adopted only single-phase materials for simplicity while soft rubber materials, from collaborator in France, are used as loading for additional tuning of constitutive parameters. Objective 3 is fully implemented. 4. Scanning laser vibrometry, together with signal amplification in excitation are used to measure elastic field profile on the metamaterial beams. We have also established post-processing techniques in extracting transmission, reflection coefficients on the metamaterial beams. Objective 4 is fully implemented. 5. Experimental proof of Willis coupling on both flexural waves and torsional waves are achieved in terms of the extraction of the constitutive parameters. Asymmetric reflection from the metamaterials are also demonstrated. Objective 5 is fully implemented. 6. Asymmetric wave control and also non-Hermitian exceptional point on the scattering matrix are demonstrated as possible applications of the Willis coupling. Such asymmetric control is also extended from the investigation in reflection to non-reciprocal transmission and amplification as well.

16302218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302218.value: 1. We have formulated the effective medium representation of Willis metamaterial on three scenarios: flexural waves, torsional waves and water waves. The specific meaning of the cross-coupling between different fields are formulated as the analogy of bianisotropy of electromagnetic waves. These results is first published in Physical Review X (2019) for the flexural waves. Around 30 to 40% of the work (theory part) in the Physical Review X (2019) paper were done within the period of the project period in developing an effective medium theory common for both flexural beam and flexural plate to explain the experimental results in the initial submission. The subsequent results are published in New Journal of Physics (2021) for water waves and Wave Motion for torsional waves (2022). Further modeling and analytic formulation have been done as well. 2. In these works, we have also designed metamaterial structures to achieve the Willis coupling. A universal approach is established by designing resonating structures with mirror symmetry breaking in the propagation direction. 3. We have developed a field-averaging technique based on the numerically simulated eigenmodes or scattered fields to extract the constitutive parameters. The field-averaging technique is applied to the different scenarios. 4. We have experimentally realized Willis coupling for the first time in flexural waves and torsional waves. The associated phenomena demonstrated includes asymmetric reflection, unidirectional zero reflection (related to exceptional point). We also demonstrate non-reciprocal transmission through a collaboration. 5. Alongside developing the experimental techniques with the PhD student in training, we also develop collaborations with other groups to help characterizing elastic wave samples from other groups, resulting in a publication in Physical Review Applied (2021).

16302218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302218.value: One further development will be to explore applications, such as polarization conversion. As we have already successfully explored the concept of Willis coupling on both torsional waves and flexural waves by adopting resonators with mirror symmetry breaking in the propagation direction. A further mirror symmetry breaking in the transverse direction is expected to couple the torsional and flexural waves for polarization conversion applications. We have already developed the theoretical design with numerical simulations performed for Willis coupling for water waves. A possible next step is to seek experimental realization.

16302218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302218.value: The recent development of mechanical metamaterials has freed us from the limited palette of elastic material parameters provided by the conventional composite approach. It allows us to explore complex constitutive parameters which are not possible previously. Here, we target to realize a concept in elastodynamics called Willis coupling, which is the analog of bianisotropy in electromagnetism. Before the current project, such a concept has only been realized in air-borne acoustics. We have now established the detailed meanings of Willis coupling in three different scenarios: flexural waves, torsional waves and water waves. A universal approach in realizing Willis coupling is developed by designing resonating structures in breaking mirror symmetry. Numerical approaches are developed to extract the effective constitutive parameters from full-wave simulations and experimental realizations have been performed as well. These investigations lead to a consolidation of the concept of Willis coupling in different kinds of mechanical waves and also lead to special wave phenomena including unidirectional zero reflection, non-Hermitian exceptional points, etc. The understanding gained from the current project will also facilitate the application of Willis media to surface acoustic wave devices and seismic wave control.

16302318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302318.value: Indole is not only an important molecule in organic synthesis with versatile reactivity, but also a privileged structural motif widely present in numerous natural products and synthetic molecules with significant importance for drug discovery. As “the Load of the Rings” in drug discovery, indole has attracted substantial long-standing interests from the organic chemistry community regarding its direct and selective functionalization reactions for rapid access to important molecules. However, significant challenges remain. In this proposal, we intend to further advance this area, with emphasis on previously less addressed or unprecedented types of functionalization processes using organocatalysis as a versatile approach. Our proposal includes three parts. The first part focuses on previously unprecedented asymmetric C(sp3)−H bond functionalization of 2-alkyl-substituted indoles. In contrast to the widely studied indole C(sp2)−H functionalization, the current project represents a new dimension in asymmetric functionalization of indole. The second part is asymmetric intramolecular cyclization of indoles tethered with an oxetane. This process is the first catalytic asymmetric desymmetrization of 3-oxetanes using a carbon-based nucleophile. The success will lead to not only indole functionalization, but also efficient synthesis of diverse polyheterocyclic alkaloid-type molecules that lack rapid access before. Lastly, we will probe an interesting series of regiodivergent asymmetric functionalizations of 2,3-disubstituted indoles with (aza-)quinone methides. The mechanistic studies will potentially lead to generalization of an intrinsic rule for regioselectivity control of indole functionalization. These catalytic symmetric processes are not only fundamentally important in organic synthesis and asymmetric catalysis, but also versatile bridges to link organic synthesis to drug discovery and other aspects of human life. 吲哚不僅是有機合成中具有多種反應性的重要分子，而且是廣泛存在於許多天然產物和合成分子中的特殊結構单元，對藥物开发具有重要的意義。作為藥物研发中的重要杂环，吲哚吸引了有機化學界長期以來對其快速和選擇性功能化反應的興趣。但是，这一领域仍存在重大挑戰。本研究将進一步推進這一領域，特别是使用有機催化这一以前较少使用的方法实现前所未有的新型反应。第一部分将实现前所未有的2-烷基取代吲哚的不對稱C（sp3）-H鍵官能化。與廣泛研究的吲哚C（sp2）-H官能化相反，當前項目代表了吲哚不對稱官能化的新維度。第二部分是对携带氧雜環丁烷结构的吲哚分子的不對稱分子內環化。該過程是使用碳基親核試劑進行的3-氧雜環丁烷的首次手性去對稱化。该反应可以快速合成各種多雜環生物鹼類分子。最後，我們將探討一系列有趣的2,3-二取代吲哚與邻亚甲基苯醌和对亚甲基苯醌类化合物的區域选择性不對稱官能化，同时也对这些反应的机理进行深入理解。這些反應不僅在有機合成和不對稱催化中具有重要意义，从长远来看更重要的是能够进一步促进藥物研发，从而提高人類生活水平。

16302318.label: Realisation of objectives
16302318.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a range of catalytic asymmetric processes for the selective functionalization of indoles. Specifically, three major sub-areas have been explored, including asymmetric C(sp3)-H bond functionalization of 2-alkyl-substituted indoles, asymmetric intramolecular cyclization of indoles tethered with an oxetane, and regiodivergent asymmetric functionalization of 2,3-disubstituted indoles. Other than these reactions, we also explored additional functionalization reactions involving indole and related molecules, which provide rapid access to previously in accessible indole-containing molecules. The objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. We have developed the first catalytic asymmetric functionalization of unactivated benzylic C(sp3‒H) bonds of indoles. Unlike the previous examples of asymmetric C(sp3‒H) functionalization of α-azaarenes, this process does not require the use of a strong base or an electron-deficient substrate to facilitate deprotonation. With the proper choice of a uniquely effective chiral urea catalyst in combination with a phosphoric acid additive, the intermolecular C‒C bond formation reaction between unactivated alkyl indoles and trifluoropyruvates proceeded under mild conditions with high efficiency and enantioselectivity. The good enantiocontrol is particularly noteworthy in view of the severe background reaction as well as the complete inability of other type of catalysts for asymmetric induction. It was proposed that the pyruvate electrophile plays an important role in activating the indole toward enamine formation. DFT calculations and kinetic studies further supported this mechanism and provided important insights. We also studied the kinetic and thermodynamic features of indole N1- and C6-alkylation reactions of indoles. The electrophilic reactivity of these quinone methides have also been compared for the first time by both experiments and DFT calculations. The indole N1-alkylation is typically kinetically favorable, but the C6-alkylation is more thermodynamically favorable. With suitable conditions, the C6-alkylation could be achieved with high efficiency and selectivity. Among these quinone methides, the reactivity increases from aza-p-QMs to o-QMs. The results not only provide access to a range of valuable triarylmethanes, but also guide future development of new reactions with these versatile electrophiles. Asymmetric intramolecular cyclization of indoles with oxetanes has also been achieved with good selectivity and efficiency. The reaction processes via indole attack at the 3-position followed by 3- to 2-migration, leading to diverse cyclic tetrahydrocarbazoles. Chiral phosphoric acids have been identified as optimal catalysts for these reactions. Other studies include the remote asymmetric 1,8-addition of the in situ-generated indole imine methide and synthesis of crowded tetraarylmethanes containing an indole unit. These reactions have been achieved with high enantioselectivity.

16302318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302318.value: In this project, we have developed a wide range of asymmetric processes by proper design of the conditions and catalytic systems. These reactions provided rapid access of highly functionalized heterocycles, including indoles and related structures. Oxetanes have also been studied in terms of the selective opening reactions. (1) We developed a new approach for the efficient synthesis of eight-membered lactams featuring formal [6+2] cyclization between siloxy alkynes and vinylazetidines. (2) We have developed the first catalytic asymmetric functionalization of unactivated benzylic C(sp3‒H) bonds of indoles. (3) We developed a catalytic enantioconvergent House‒Meinwald rearrangement for the synthesis of both cyclic and acyclic ketones bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. (4) We achieved a new catalytic asymmetric approach for the synthesis of chiral tetrahydrothiophenes and tetrahydroselenophenes, both are highly useful structures with limited efficient access previously. (5) A highly efficient synthesis of hydrodibenzofurans has been developed, which is a new addition to the small family of general strategies available for this useful target. (6) We have discovered a new skeletal reorganization process of oxetanes leading to the unexpected 1,2-dihydroquinoline products. It represents an unprecedented reactivity pattern of the oxetane functional group. (7) We studied of the reactivity and selectivity of (aza-)quinone methides in selective C6-alkylations of indoles (8) We have developed an organocatalytic enantioconvergent synthesis of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes by means of remote asymmetric 1,8-addition of the in situ-generated indole imine methide. (9) We developed the first catalytic enantioselective synthesis of chiral tetraarylmethanes, a unique family of spherical molecules without direct access previously. With this new process, two libraries of structurally distinct CTAMs were efficiently synthesized with high enantioselectivity. Preliminary biological activity study indicated that these spherical molecules are highly promising anticancer agents. This study is expected to revitalize a more systematic exploration of this important chemical space. (10) We demonstrated that oxetane can serve as a useful electrophile for the mild efficient C–C bond formation with soft carbon nucleophiles silyl ketene acetals, providing expedient access to a wide range of 1,5-oxygenated molecules. (11) We developed an efficient organocatalytic enantioselective dearomatization of thiophenes in the context of asymmetric 1,10-conjugate addition. (12) We developed a new chiral framework, SPHENOL. A highly selective and efficient catalytic asymmetric protocol was also developed to allow expedient access to enantiopure SPHENOL. Further applications of SPHENOL as a chiral backbone in diverse chiral ligands and organocatalysts have also been demonstrated.

16302318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302318.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful catalytic asymmetric processes of indoles and oxetanes will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will continue to explore and push the boundary of remote stereocontrol and synthesis of sterically congested chiral centers in the context of indole functionalizations and oxetane opening. We will spend more efforts in this direction in the future.

16302318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302318.value: Indoles and oxetanes are useful heterocycles in pharmaceutical chemistry. In this project, we have discovered a range of new organic processes involving indoles and oxetane structures with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes utilized organocatalysts that do not involve metals, which are environmentally friendly. These catalysts showed excellent performance in the construction of highly useful structural motifs in many drug molecules. Many of the synthesized products from these reactions show interesting anticancer activities. These findings will contribute to the advances in drug discovery and environmental protection.

16302418.label: Project Objectives
16302418.value: To investigate systematically the mechanisms involving reactions of multiynes catalyzed or mediated by transition metal complexes. To examine factors, such as the metal center, the ligands, and the substrates influencing the reaction pathways of the abovementioned reactions.

To examine factors, such as the metal center, the ligands, and the substrates influencing the reaction pathways of the abovementioned reactions.

16302418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302418.value: Chemical synthesis of complex molecules has important impacts in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. Utilization of multiynes for the synthesis of complex molecules, especially conjugate organic systems and natural products with challenging structural features, has attracted considerable research. In particular, reactions of multiynes catalyzed or mediated by transition metal complexes allow construction of various cyclic compounds. To date, important progress has been made regarding these cyclization reactions involving multiynes. Multiyne substrates each contain many triple-bond units, and therefore their reactions often lead to various cyclization products, many of which are not necessarily desired products. In view of this, extensive and systematic understanding of their reaction mechanisms is highly desired to achieve target synthesis. In this proposal, we propose to carry out theoretical studies via density functional theory calculations to explore the related reaction mechanisms. We hope that this research work will provide potential guidance for the experimental work and develop new or improved processes for target organic synthesis. 複雜分子的化學合成在藥物和農藥製造工業有重要的作用。利用多炔來合成複雜且難得到的分子吸引了很多研究。 過渡金屬催化或輔助多炔反應可讓我們合成得各種各樣環狀的複雜分子。迄今，已經有很多多炔反應的報導。這些反應通常得到混合的環化產物。為了得到期望的產物，需要對其反應機理進行系統的研究，從而調控反應條件使其得到期望的產物。本計畫主要是對最近發現的多炔反應的反應機理進行理論研究。 由此，希望對一些重要的實驗現象進行解釋，從而對發展更好的催化劑提供理論基礎。

16302418.label: Realisation of objectives
16302418.value: In this project, we carried out DFT calculations to study reaction mechanisms involving transition metal complexes and various unsaturated organic substrates. Here is the realisation of the two objectives listed in 5.1. Objective 1: Mechanisms have been investigated for a number of transition metal mediated or catalyzed reactions involving various unsaturated organic substrates containing C-C/C-O double and/or triple bonds with the aid of DFT calculations. Detailed mechanistic insights/impact into the catalytic reactions studied have been identified and thoroughly discussed. Objective 2: Through our DFT studies, we have been able to explain the origin of the reaction pathway selectivity observed experimentally and understand how various factors influence the reaction outcomes.

16302418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302418.value: The detailed reaction mechanisms for (1) the rhodium-catalyzed cycloisomerization of homopropargylallene-alkynes involving C(sp3)-C(sp) sigma bond activation/cleavage and (2) gold-catalyzed reactions of 2,1-benzisoxazoles with propiolates and ynamides have been investigated with the aid of DFT calculations. New reaction mechanisms have been established, from which we were able to explain the origin of the reaction pathway selectivity observed experimentally (see 8(1) and 8(6)). Through our DFT studies, we have explained how substituents affect the reaction selectivity in reactions of OsCl2(PPh3)3 with various o‑ethynylphenyl carbonyl compounds and how different phosphine ligands influence the reaction pathways in the rhodium-catalyzed regiodivergent synthesis of alkylboronates via deoxygenative borylation of ketones (see 8(2) and 8(5)). We have also discovered a two-state reactivity for a previously reported iron diimine catalyzed hydrovinylation. We have confirmed the role of the non-innocent diimine ligand being one-electron reduced throughout the course of reaction, thus maintaining a Fe(I)/Fe(III) catalytic cycle (see 8(3)). We have also studied an unprecedented Rh(III)-catalyzed molecular oxygen mediated three-component coupling and acylmethylation macrocyclization via C–H/O2 dual activation strategy. We found that the O2 insertion process is the most crucial for the reaction, in which the triplet O2 interacts with the Rh-C σ bond via an SN2-like fashion leading to the formation of a triplet diradical species (a radical Rh(I) metal center and a radical peroxide) from which the two radical moieties couple via a minimum energy crossing point (see 8(4)). In collaboration with Professor M Yamashita, we reported joint experimental and theoretical studies on the reactivity of the borylgold complex (IPr)AuB(o-tol)2 toward alkynes. We for the first time found an alkyne insertion to an Au–B bond. At the same time, we observed an unusual retro-1,2-metalate shift that involves the cleavage of the C–C/C–Si bond trans to the Au–C bond of the 2-borylalkenylgold complex (see 8(7)).

16302418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302418.value: Over the years, transition metal-catalyzed reactions of multiyne substrates have found applications in organic synthetic chemistry. New catalytic processes continues to be developed and explored. The insights obtained from this project contribute significantly to this expanding development. We are continuing to focus our effort to understand recently reported reactions of multiynes.

16302418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302418.value: In this project, we've investigated issues related to transition metal catalyzed reactions of multiynes, which produce chemical species with new frameworks for the synthesis of pharmaceutical products. The results and insights obtained are useful for researchers to find better catalysts for the related chemical reactions.

16302518.label: Project Objectives
16302518.value: To study dynamic phase coexistence using small colloidal clusters experimentally and through simulation. We will measure the single-particle kinetics and investigate the boundary effects.
rows: To study dynamic phase coexistence using small colloidal clusters experimentally and through simulation. We will measure the single-particle kinetics and investigate the boundary effects.

16302518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302518.value: Phase transitions are ubiquitous in nature and important for science and technology. However their microscopic mechanisms are usually not well understood. A major challenge is that the rapid motions of tiny atoms or molecules during a phase transition can hardly be measured by conventional techniques such as calorimetry, electron microscopy or X-ray diffraction. Colloids are excellent model systems for the process because the micrometer-sized particles can be observed by optical microscopy and their thermal motions can be tracked by image processing [1]. Recently, we have been studying the melting of conventional colloidal crystals [2–5] and solid-solid transitions [6,7] between different lattice structures. We now propose the studies of two unconventional phase behaviors using colloids: (1) the order-disorder transition of a crystalline lattice [8–10]; (2) the dynamic phase coexistence of crystal and liquid in a small system [11–13]. The order-disorder transition of the same lattice is a special type of solid-solid transition, in contrast to the conventional solid-solid transitions between different lattice structures [10]. It is common in alloys. Here we design a very simple two-dimensional colloidal crystal composed of same-sized paramagnetic and nonmagnetic spheres which can exhibit such a transition. Increasing the magnetic field can drive the randomly-distributed paramagnetic particles to form a superlattice embedded in the original lattice. Our preliminary simulations have revealed a novel cascade of transitions. We will systematically study the microscopic kinetics and the effects of some key parameters to better understand the nature of the transition. The results can cast light on the order-disorder transitions in alloys and the general solid-solid transitions. When a crystal is small enough, it may spontaneously melt and re-crystallize under equilibrium thermal fluctuations. Such dynamic phase coexistence has been predicted in theory [14,15] and simulations [16,17], but only experimentally detected by indirect evidence in atomic nanoclusters [18,19]. Our preliminary experiment has directly shown such dynamic phase coexistence for the first time using colloids confined in small cavities. Further studies will deepen the understanding of this phenomenon which is useful for controlling the stability of nano-clusters. These two phenomena are not well understood in atomic systems and have not been explored in colloids before. Our proposed experiments and simulations can provide unprecedented information at the single-particle level for future refinement of the underlying theory. These understandings are of fundamental importance in condensed matter physics, and of practical interest for materials science, nanotechnology, metallurgy and related technologies. 相變在自然界中广泛存在，對科學和技術很重要。然而，它們的微觀機制通常不是很清楚。一個主要原因是相變过程中原子或分子的快速運動很難通過常規技術如量熱法，電子顯微鏡和X射線衍射來測量。膠體是優秀的模型系統，因為微米胶体粒子可以通過光學顯微鏡觀察，其熱運動可以通過圖像處理來跟踪 。最近，我們研究了膠體晶體熔化和不同晶格之間的固 - 固轉變。這裡，我們提出利用膠體研究兩種非常規相转变：（1）同一晶格上的有序 - 無序轉變; （2）小系統中晶體和液體的動態共存。 與傳統固 - 固轉變相比，同一晶格上的有序 - 無序轉變是一種特殊類型的固 - 固轉變。它廣泛存在於合金中。在這裡，我們提出一種非常簡單的二維膠體晶體，它由相同尺寸的順磁性和非磁性球體組成，它們可以表現出這種轉變。增强磁場会使原本隨機分佈的順磁顆粒变成超晶格。我們的初步模擬揭示了此過程。我們將系統地研究其微觀動力學和一些關鍵參數的影響，以更好地了解中间過渡态的性質。該結果可以揭示合金中的有序 - 無序轉變和更一般的固 - 固轉變。 當晶體足夠小時，它可以在平衡态熱涨落下自發熔化並重結晶。這種動態相位共存已在理論和模擬預測，但僅通過原子納米糰簇中的間接證據進行實驗檢測。初步實驗首次使用限制在小腔中的膠體直接顯示出這種動態相共存。進一步的研究將加深對動態相共存的理解，對控制納米粒子的穩定性有一定的用处。 上述兩種現像在原子系統中尚未得到很好的理解，之前尚未在膠體中進行過探索。所提出的實驗和模擬可以在單粒子水平上提供前所未有的微觀信息，以用於未來對基礎理論的改進。這些理解在凝聚態物理學中具有基础重要性，對材料科學，納米技術，冶金學和相關技術具有實際意義。

16302518.label: Realisation of objectives
16302518.value: We have achieved the objective and further focused on the more fruitful extensions of the objective. For objective 1, we have fabricated various sized and shaped cavities and successfully assemble colloidal spheres into crystals even in very small cavities. This improves the quality of the dynamic phase coexistence. We observed much better spontaneous fluctuations between crystal and liquid at the dynamic phase coexistence. The main problem is the blurry image of particles in the liquid phase. To better track them, we developed a machine learning algorithm which greatly improved the image processing result. We also measured the melting temperature vs the crystal size and shape, but the fluctuation is strong because of the large density variation among samples. The student has graduated last year and a new student will continue the experiments in order to obtain more data. The boundary effect is important for solids and phase transitions. To this end, we extend the study to the surface effects of crystals, including their roughening premelting and melting behaviors. This part of research has been published on Soft Matter in 2020. Although objective 2 was removed because the project is only partially funded, we made substantial progresses on it. We performed systematic simulations on the magnetic-field-induced disorder-to-order and the reverse order-to disorder transitions in binary colloidal crystals, and observed three types of behaviors under different mixing ratios, i.e. order-disorder, solid-solid, and solid-hexatic liquid-solid transitions. We focused mainly on the latter one because it is counterintuitive. We have successfully explained its mechanism and a manuscript is in preparation. We also measured the other two types of transitions. In the experimental part, we tried air-water interface or two-wall confinements for making 2D samples which encountered various problems. In particular, the applied magnetic field expands the colloidal solids and causes melting instead of solid-solid transition. We have fabricated cavities to overcome this difficulty. The student has graduated last year and a new student continued the experiments in order to obtain more data to better compare with the rich simulation results. During solid-solid transitions, the motions of grain boundaries and dislocations play a key role. Thus we extend the research to the study of defect motions under a shear. Our colloid experiment observed the kinetics of disconnections on grain boundaries for the first time and provide the first experimental test for the previous theory and simulation about grain boundary migration via disconnections. We also observed how individual dislocations move during the rotation of a crystalline grain. These results are published in the top journal PNAS in 2020.

16302518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302518.value: We performed systematic computer simulations for solid-solid transitions in binary colloids, and discovered some interesting results. For example, the binary crystal can transform to liquid and hexatic phase, and then to a new crystal as the interparticle repulsions increases in a certain parameter regime. Such melting is induced by increasing the effective volume fraction which is counterintuitively. We find that it is due to the competition between the different lattices of the parent and product lattices; when none of them dominates, the system becomes disordered and may form a fluid phase. Under another mixing ratio for the paramagnetic and non-magnetic particles, particles experience intense local rearrangements among the first and second-nearest neighbors and form small triangular superlattice domains. After this partially ordering transition, the superlattice domains expand and merge, resulting in a completely ordering transition at a higher magnetic field. We studied small crystal melting at the single-particle level for the first time. When the crystal diameter is less than 10 particles or so, the crystal can spontaneously melt and recrystallize over time. Such dynamic phase transition has rarely been observed in experiment. Due to the lack of quantitative analysis method or theoretical predictions in literature, we mainly focus on the observation for crystals in various sized and shaped cavities. Their boundary can promote or suppress melting, depending on the coherency to the lattice. We further discovered distinct surface roughening and premelting behaviors for monolayer and bilayer colloidal crystals, which demonstrates that 2D is a critical dimension with surprising impacts on crystals’ surfaces. We also find that the surface roughening process is interrupted by the premelting. These results are published in Soft Matter in 2020. We also discovered very rich critical behaviors in the glass transition of colloidal monolayers composed of ellipsoids. Critical behaviors have been found in glass transition of systems composed of various spherical particles by other group and their paper was ranked as the top 20 landmark papers in the history of Nature Materials; We further show that such critical behaviors also exist in glasses composed of non-spherical particles for the first time and the result is published in a top journal Science Advances in 2021.

16302518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302518.value: The order of the phase transition and the discovered stick-slip behaviors in the mixture of magnetic and non-magnetic particles need further studies. More experimental data are need to compare with the results in simulations. We have systematically studied the transition under some mixing ratios, while other ratios are worth to be further explored because they may produce new transitions or kinetic pathways beyond the three types that we have observed. Moreover, expanding the grain boundary thickness can change a polycrystal to a glass, which is another route of order-disorder transition which has rarely been explored. Some of the analysis in this study can be similarly applied to this new route. For the melting of small crystals, more theoretical analysis is needed to quantify the size and boundary effects on melting. The small crystal melting can generalized to the melting of small glasses. The phase transition behaviors in small systems are different from those of bulk materials, but have been much less studied. In fact, even bulk glass melting has rarely been experimentally observed at the single-particle level. Colloids can provide single-particle kinetics, and thus could reveal important microscopic information for these transitions.

16302518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302518.value: Surface effects are important to small systems. In particular, small crystals (e.g. diameter < 100 particles) melt differently from large bulk crystals. Their melting behaviors are not well understood due to the experimental challenges for the observations at small spatial and temporal scales. Micrometer sized colloidal particles can be directly visualized and their Brownian motions can be tracked by optical microscopy. Thus colloids are excellent model systems to provide microscopic kinetics that are not measurable in atomic systems. We fabricate small thermal-sensitive colloidal crystals confined in micro-cavities and observe the melting kinetics at the single-particle level by video microscopy for the first time. Generally, the melting volume fraction is lower for smaller crystals. In small hexagonal or triangular cavities, the defect-free triangular lattices spontaneously fluctuated between a single crystal and a liquid state, resulting in a novel dynamic phase transition. We also drive solid-solid transitions in colloidal crystals composed of magnetic and non-magnetic particles by increasing the magnetic field. Counterintuitively, the parent crystal under certain mixing ratio firstly melt into a hexatic liquid and then recrystallize into the product crystal as the effective density increases. We attribute the melting to the incompatibility between lattices and mixing ratio.

16302618.label: Realisation of objectives
16302618.value: Aim 1: To develop a novel assay for real-time detection of multiple steps during RNA synthesis of influenza polymerase: The completion of this aim led to the award of three PhD student’s theses and their publications in the top journal Nucleic Acid Research (Impact Factor 19.16) (Xu et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2021; 49(15):8796) with the PI (Peter Pak-Hang Cheung) and collaborator (Xuhui Huang) of this grant and supervisors of both students being the corresponding authors. We aimed to develop the Sequence-specific Wide-spectrum in vitro Fluorescent Transcription) SWIFT assay to monitor the evolution of sense-specific RNA product synthesized by influenza A virus (IAV) polymerase. Hence, for our preliminary results reported in the grant proposal to serve as the foundation to develop of the SWIFT assay, we conducted radioisotope-based assay that measures the full-length products of influenza A virus (IAV) polymerase activity. The shortcoming of this assay lies in the inability to determine the precise number of nucleotides being added into the nascent RNA by IAV polymerase so kinetic information is lost. This information is critical as it allows us to elucidate the mechanisms of inhibition by nucleoside analogs (for Aim 2 and 3). Hence, for this grant, we have developed a novel single-turnover NTP incorporation assay to obtain enzymology details, thus allowing precise calculation of transcriptional accuracy by computing the incorporation specificity of cognate (correct) and non-cognate (incorrect) NTP from a single round of nucleotide-addition reactions, with emphasis on the elongation step. Moreover, the developed kinetic assay will overcome the existing challenges in biochemical assays, which is the inability to reveal enzyme kinetics data for IAV polymerases. We overcame the challenges in the grant to achieving large quantities of highly pure IAV RdRp complex using the insect cell expression system to replace the human cell system shown in the grant proposal and resolved the lack of the gel’s resolving power of incorporating single cognate or non-cognate NTP. Published in our Nucleic Acids Research paper, our novel single-turnover NTP incorporation assay was able to quantify the incorporation rate constant (kpol) and the apparent substrate dissociation constant (Kd, app) for the site-specific incoming cognate and non-cognate NTP. To our knowledge, this would be the first time that a quantitative measurement of fidelity is carried out for the IAV heterotrimer polymerase complex. Specifically, kpol is contributed by the catalysis and associated isomerization of the RdRp active site, while Kd, app results from NTP loading and binding to the active site. We calculated the substrate specificity (kpol/Kd,app) to measure the polymerase transcription efficiency and discrimination factor (substrate specificity of cognate over non-cognate NTP) in both wild-type and mutant RdRps to complete Aim 2 and 3. This assay has helped us develop a real-time kinetics assay based on fluorescence polarization (FP), as outlined in Aim 1 of our proposal. We measured the initiation step of IAV transcription using a fluorescent capped RNA primer. As the polymerase elongated with the fluorescent-capped primer, the product RNA’s FP increased with its molecular weight. FP detection can measure the initiation or cap-binding step as the PB2 domain of the polymerase binds to the probe, increasing molecular weight and FP. After transcription, polymerase dissociates from the product, reducing FP. Without NTP, IAV polymerase cannot initiate elongation, so FP remains static. Aim 2: To identity potential sites for influenza polymerase inhibition using synthesized natural compounds The completion of this aim has led to two PhD students’ theses, one publication in Biophysical Chemistry (with the PI and the collaborator as the corresponding authors), and three patents being granted. Natural compounds have shown many advantages in developing new drugs. They are good structural scaffolds for inhibitor designs due to their high chemical diversity and mild side-effects. Meanwhile, most of the natural compounds can be obtained by simple methods in chemical synthesis, which means the cost of prospective drugs can be significantly reduced. Our grant proposal aimed to verify several potential candidates that can significantly inhibit the IAV activities from nature compounds derivatives synthesized and provided by the collaborator of this grant, Prof Rongbiao Tong. Tong has already achieved total syntheses of complex natural products with diverse novel molecular architectures and functionalities. The Tong group has contributed to our compound library of heterocyclic natural products, their analogues, and synthetic intermediates. We have further validated these compounds using both mini-genome luciferase assay and radioisotope-based in vitro transcription assay. In mini-genome luciferase assays, three compounds from two different scaffolds (Musellarin and Berberines) exhibit strong inhibitory effect on influenza polymerase activity, in which their IC50 values were significantly lower than that of T-705 but with only slightly higher level of cytotoxicity. We then further performed the radioisotope-based in vitro transcription assay to confirm its inhibitory effects on polymerase activity. This work has resulted in three patents being granted. Aim 3: To study the functions of critical amino acid residues of influenza polymerase identified by inhibitors The completion of this aim has led to two publications, one in Nucleic Acid Research (Xu et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2021; 49(15):8796) and one in Biophysical Chemistry (Wang et al., Biophys Chem, 2021, 277, 106652) with the PI and collaborator being the corresponding authors, and the graduation of two PhD students. We have identified a number of critical amino acid residues of IAV polymerase. K235R and R239K. IAV RdRp active site residues interact with NTP triphosphate during RNA elongation. Unknown how they control NTP rate and fidelity. R239 and K235 in RdRp's PB1 subunit control transcription activity and fidelity. A single lysine-to-arginine mutation on K235 increased RdRp fidelity and activity compared to wild-type. The K235R mutant had 1.9-fold more transcription activity and 4.6-fold more fidelity than wild-type. K235R's higher activity is due to its closer proximity to NTP's triphosphate moiety than wild-type. These results reveal NTP incorporation and fidelity control mechanisms, enabling rational vaccine and antiviral target design. We tested K235R's NTP analog discrimination. Guanosine and 3'-dCTP or 2'F-dCTP started the reaction. K235R mutant RdRp less efficiently incorporates 3'dCTP and 2'F-dCTP. The K235R mutant has higher transcription fidelity than the wild-type to distinguish the cognate NTP from mismatched NTP and NTP analogs. In another paper (our Biophysical Chemistry paper) stemming from this Aim, we successfully revealed the mechanisms by which Favipiravir (T-705) inhibit IAV polymerase. Favipiravir (T-705) is a potent anti-influenza drug that inhibits RNA viruses. Its active form, T-705-RTP, is a competitive substrate for influenza A virus RdRp (IAV). T-705’s inhibitory mechanisms remain elusive and debated. T-705 may inhibit transcription by acting as a chain terminator, but its ambiguous C-U base pairing may also make it a mutagen for IAV RdRp. We used biochemical assays and molecular dynamics simulations to determine how T-705 inhibits IAV RdRp. MD simulations show that two T-705 destabilize the active site and disrupt nascent RNA base stacking. Integrating computational and experimental methods, we found that T-705 inhibits IAV RdRp. Our study offers a platform to study antiviral inhibition and a novel explanation for designing anti-influenza drugs.

16302618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302618.value: As proposed in our Aim 1, we successfully developed a novel single-turnover NTP incorporation assay to obtain enzymology details, enabling the precise calculation of the incorporation specificity of cognate and non-cognate NTP from a single round of nucleotide-addition reactions (Xu et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2021; 49(15):8796). This innovative kinetic test enables the determination of the discriminating factor as a quantitative measure of fidelity for both the wild-type (WT) and mutant IAV polymerases. Moreover, our new kinetic assay has overcome the present obstacles for assessing the fidelity of influenza A virus, as biochemical assays are incapable of revealing enzyme kinetics data for influenza viruses. Next, complemented with Molecular Dynamics simulation we have elucidated the molecular mechanism of the mutations that have exhibited higher activity and fidelity in our experimental measurements. Understanding the molecular mechanisms can significantly accelerate the mechanistic investigation of further mutations of key residues that affect transcriptional fidelity and efficiency. For our Aim 2, we have demonstrated through mini-genome assay, several nature compound derivatives show great inhibitory effects on the viral polymerase activity. To further test if the candidate compounds can direct inhibit the transcription of the IAV RdRp, various concentrations of compounds were added to the reaction to see if they can inhibit our purified IAV polymerase to extend the product RNA strand. As a result, HKUST-A from Musellarin family shows significant inhibition effect on the IAV RdRp, with an in vitro IC50 significantly lower that of T-705. This work has led to two awarded patents. For Aim 3, we have successfully adopted our novel kinetic enzymology assay to elucidate the precise mechanisms by which T-705 inhibit IAV polymerase activity (Wang et al., Biophys Chem. 2021;277:106652). Our successful completion of all the aims in the proposal has impacted has lay a solid foundation to study detailed enzyme kinetics of IAV, such as the elongation rate along any point of the RNA template, and the mechanisms of inhibition as determined by inhibitors’ effect on the rate constants of individual steps of RNA synthesis. We have successfully identified critical amino acids residues that can reveal the mechanisms of action of NTP analogues and natural compounds. Furthermore, we have identified novel mutations in IAV polymerase that impacted antiviral drug resistance of NTP analogues and coincided with enhances transcriptional accuracy and activity. Our platform can further reveal novel binding sites for our synthesized natural compounds inhibit polymerase activity.

16302618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302618.value: Our two publications that documented the three completed aims of our study allow us to develop a novel assay that can be used to replace traditional radioisotope assays that are unable to accurately gauge NTP incorporation in real time and provide indirect and unreliable NTP incorporation measurements (based only on gel band intensity with few data points). Our developed novel fluorescently-label 5’cap primer allows for the first time the creation of a high throughput real time fluorescence-based assay. This can overcome the limitation of fluorescence-based assay where limited sensitivity for polymerase is due to IAV polymerase replicating only once. Our future work will improve our proposed SWIFT assay that rely on probes that bind to the product for activity measurement have a binding constant and hence adversely impact readouts for polymerase kinetics. We have also discovered novel natural compounds and NTP analogues we synthesized that can inhibit IAV polymerase. In the next stage, we will try to solve the bound structures of IAV polymerase and compound candidates by using Cryo-EM to look deep into the structural basis, including the possible mechanism of compounds targeting and inhibition by studying the kinetics for further functional groups optimization.

16302618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302618.value: We have developed a state-of-the-art assay to monitor and quantify RNA synthesis in real time. Our assay can monitor RNA synthesis, in particular NTP incorporation at single nucleotide resolution. Our assay can monitor in real-time individual steps of RNA synthesis of viral polymerases perturbed by inhibitors (e.g. NTP analogues and nature compounds) and amino acid substitutions. Using this system, we successfully quantified detailed enzyme kinetics, such as the incorporation specificities of correct versus incorrect NTP, and the inhibition mechanisms determined by inhibitors' effect on RNA synthesis rate constants. Our platform has successfully revealed novel binding sites for our synthesized natural compounds to inhibit polymerase activity. It also successfully resolved the long-standing puzzle of how T-705 can be both a mutagen and a RNA chain terminator. Long-term, we can systematically modify compounds through our synthetic routes to improve drug efficacy by increasing stability and half-life, reducing toxicity, increasing cell permeability, and increasing solubility. Our work has long-term implications for understanding influenza polymerase structure and function. This motivates us to use experiments and molecular dynamics simulations to study viral, bacterial, and yeast RNA polymerases to better understand influenza polymerase function and inhibition.

16302718.value: 活性膠體，也稱為自驱动顆粒，作為一个簡單的模型系統，具有與許多生命系統，例如分子馬達，細胞和細菌，類似的動態行為。這些微/納米尺寸的“游動者”也為廣泛的生物醫學應用帶來了巨大的希望，從定向的細胞器的貨物運輸，藥物輸送和活組織檢查，到清潔堵塞的動脈和靶向癌症的治療。作為一類新型的膠體系統，活性粒子在微觀尺度上持續消耗能量，並且表現出豐富的新興行為，這些行為只能在非平衡物理學的框架內來理解。雖然最近在該方面取得了一定進展，但目前我們對活性膠體的理解仍處於起步階段。尚未開發出用於理解其相行為和動態特性的一般理論框架。因此，通過可良好控制的活性膠體實驗可以提供當前所需的實驗數據以及對活性膠體統計特性的新見解，這仍然是非平衡統計物理學中的巨大挑戰。 在這個項目中，我們將研究稀疏的單層活性顆粒的新興動力學行為及其對複雜環境的響應，這些複雜環境通過施加可良好控制的外部勢場來模擬具有光活化特性的二氧化鈦-二氧化矽非對稱小球被選擇為該研究的活性膠體顆粒，其自推進速度隨紫外光強度而增加。我們使用光學顯微鏡和多粒子跟踪技術來獲取大量單個粒子運動的二維軌跡，之後將對其速度分佈，速度自相關函數以及位移矢量的平方矩，概率密度函數和“瞬時”擴散係數的分佈進行全面的統計分析。然後，我們將利用底部的膠體模板在活性粒子上施加不同的外部勢場，例如水平和傾斜的週期勢場和隨機勢場，研究它們的動力學如何隨外場參數來演變。 該項目的成功完成將為活性膠體在複雜外場中的動力學提供新的理解以及標度規律。擬開展的研究涉及非平衡態活性系統中新物理的探索和對複雜環境中主動運輸的研究，這些在細胞生物學和生物醫學的應用等許多方面發揮著重要作用。該項目具有科學意義和技術相關性，涉及樣品合成，精密實驗，模擬和理論建模，需要一個團隊的協作。我們已經組建了一個這樣的團隊。

16302718.label: Realisation of objectives
16302718.value: To fulfill the two research objectives, we carried out two sets of experiments to study the statistical properties of active (or self-propelled) colloids and transmembrane proteins in living cells and quantify their transport dynamics over complex energy landscapes. In one set of experiments, we carried out a comprehensive study of the lateral motion of acetylcholine receptors (AChRs), which are well-characterized ion-channel proteins on the plasma membrane of live Xenopus muscle cells, and their response to well-characterized potential (or free energy) landscapes. How a protein molecule wades through and functions in the tightly packed crowd either inside the cell or on the cell membrane is a fundamental issue in biological physics and cell biology. Two main mechanisms have been recognized for intracellular transport over different distances. At large distances up to the size of a cell, the cell utilizes motor proteins to drive directed transport of cargos along the cytoskeletal filamentous tracks. At small distances, the cell utilizes a different mechanism for molecular transport. For example, rapid communication in the brain relies on the release and diffusion of small neurotransmitters across the synaptic cleft of 15-20 nm in width. In a confined gap region, diffusion is very effective to provide targeted transport across the gap. There are other cellular processes, which require transport of molecules over distances in mesoscale (say, 20 nm - 1 um), in which these two mechanisms are not effective. An example is the lateral motion of transmembrane proteins in the plasma membrane. In the experiment, we used a micro-patterned substrate to generate a nonuniform concentration field n(x) of anchored integrins, which in turn creates a spatially varying and temporally stable potential (free-energy) landscape U(x) to other (nonmotor) mobile proteins in the region. This entropy-driven potential field offers a novel way for directed molecular transport in the mesoscale, which complements the conventional methods of directed molecular transport by diffusion at short distances and motor-driven cargo transport over long distances. We constructed two types of patterned surfaces: one with identical cylindrical holes (micro-wells) of diameter d = 2 um and depth = 1 um arranged on a hexagonal lattice of 2.5 um in lattice constant and the other with parallel grooves of height = 1 um and separation s = 2 um. From a careful analysis of a large volume of AChR trajectories obtained over a wide range of sampling conditions and long durations, we obtained the trapping potential U(x) and its effects on the drift velocity V(x) and diffusion coefficient D(x) of AChRs. Our findings suggest an important and biologically tunable mechanism for intracellular transport, protein trapping, and protein-protein interactions initiated not by specific chemical signaling, as is usually assumed, but by nonspecific physical forces that yield remarkably simple universal laws. This work thus demonstrated the third way for molecular transport in mesoscale. This work was published in Physical Review Research (2021). In the second set of experiments, we conducted a combined experimental and numerical study of the lateral motion of a dilute monolayer of self-propelled particles (SPPs) over parallel microgrooves made by photolithography. The SPPs chosen for the study are uniform SiO2 microspheres, whose half surface is coated with a thin layer of platinum (Pt) of thickness 5 nm via sputter coating. The 5-nm coating allows the Pt-SiO2 Janus particles to rotate freely in 3D with minimal influence from an uneven gravitational torque. When dispersed in an aqueous solution of H2O2, the self-diffusiophoresis of the Janus particles gives rise to a self-propulsion speed v_0 (or self-propulsion force F_0), which increases with the H2O2 concentration. With a large volume of the SPP trajectories obtained using optical microscopy and multi-particle tracking, we are able to provide a statistical description of the non-equilibrium distribution of the SPPs over a 1D periodic potential landscape. In particular, from the well-characterized particle trajectories, we obtain the population probability density function (PDF) P(x;v_0) of finding a Janus particle of velocity v_0 across the position x normal to the microgroove. By averaging the particle trajectories along the microgroove (y-axis) and over different grooves, we obtain the effective potential, U_eff(x;v_0)/k_BT = − ln[P(x;v_0)]. A central finding of our investigation is that the non-equilibrium behaviors of the SPPs in the limit of very slow particle rotation can be approximated by an effective equilibrium theory of passive particles moving in an activity-modified potential. Specifically, we found the PDF P(x;F_0) takes a Boltzmann-like form if an effective modified potential, U_eff(x;F0) is introduced by including the effect of self-propulsion force, F_0 (proportional to v_0), under the fixed angle approximation. It was also found that the PDF of escape time of the SPPs from the mircrogrooves takes a simple exponential form and the mean escape time follows a Kramers-like expression with the potential barrier given by the effective potential, U_eff, at the middle of groove ridges. This work thus provided a new understanding as well as scaling laws describing the dynamics of active colloids over complex free-energy landscapes. This work was submitted to Physical Review E Letters for publication. With the above two sets of experiments, the two project objectives were fully achieved. Because of the social unrest and pandemic situation in Hong Kong, we were unable to spend all the funds for conferences and equipment, as originally budgeted. The equipment fund was used only for maintaining the existing equipment. HKUST has banned all business trips for more than two years since 2020. As a result, I was unable to attend any international conference in person during this period. Nonetheless, we were able to overcome the difficulties and complete the research project as planned.
