16302718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302718.value: 1. Directed motion of membrane proteins under an entropy-driven potential field generated by anchored proteins. Directed transport of proteins and other molecules in a crowded living cell is often carried out by diffusion at short distances and by motor-driven cargo transport over long distances. Here we demonstrate, by both experiments and theory, that anchored proteins inside the cell can generate a spatially varying and temporally stable potential (free-energy) landscape for intracellular or membrane transport in the mesoscale. By using a micropatterned substrate, we introduce a periodic array of anchored integrins on the basal membrane of cultured Xenopus muscle cells. This patterned array of anchored integrins imposes a periodic potential U(x) to the lateral motion of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) on the cell membrane. From a thorough analysis of a large volume of AChR trajectories obtained over a wide range of sampling conditions and long durations from 385 cells, we find the trapping potential U(x) and its effects on the drift velocity and diffusion coefficient of AChRs. Our findings suggest that anchored proteins may play an essential role in generating an effective potential landscape to guide molecular motion in the mesoscale ranging from protein trapping and directed motion to enhanced protein-protein interactions over a long range. This work was published in Physical Review Research (2021). 2. Activity-assisted barrier-crossing of self-propelled colloids over parallel microgrooves. Self-propelled particles (SPPs) are intrinsically in a non-equilibrium state, in which detailed balance and Boltzmann distribution do not apply in general. Here we report a systematic study of the transport and escape dynamics of SPPs over a periodic free-energy landscape. A microgroove-patterned polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate is constructed to provide a gravitational potential landscape U_0(x) for the individual SPPs. From the measured non-equilibrium population probability density function P(x;v_0) of the SPPs, we find the escape dynamics of the SPPs across the potential landscape can be described by an effective potential U_eff(x;v_0), once the self-propulsion velocity v_0 is included into the potential under the fixed angle approximation. This work demonstrates that the parallel microgrooves provide a useful platform for a quantitative understanding of the interplay among the self-propulsion velocity v_0, spatial confinement by U_0(x) and thermal noise, and its effects on activity-assisted barrier-crossing and transport of the SPPs. This work was submitted to Physical Review E Letters for publication (under review).

16302718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302718.value: Our quantitative description of the effective potential U_eff(x;F_0) for active colloids was obtained under the fixed angle approximation, which assumes that the persistence time tau_R of the active particles is longer than their diffusion time t_0 across the potential U_0(x). In this case, the particle's orientation remains unchanged during an escape attempt, and thus the self-propulsion force F_0 will assist the barrier-crossing of the active particles. In many practical situations, however, such as cytosolic proteins in the cytoskeleton of a living cell, the active stress acting on the cytoskeleton often imposes a random force field to the mobile proteins, so that persistence time tau_R of the resulting force is shorter than the protein diffusion time t_0. It would be very interesting to know if an activity-modified effective potential can be used to describe the statistical properties of the active colloids in this limit complement to what we have studied. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research along this direction.

16302718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302718.value: Self-propelled colloids are synthetic micro-swimmers that can take up energy from the surrounding environment and converting it into directed motion. They are developed as simplified model systems that feature similar dynamic behaviors of various living systems, such as molecular motors, cells and bacteria. The micro/nanoscale swimmers hold great promise for a wide range of biomedical applications, ranging from directed cargo transport and drug delivery to targeted cancer therapy. These applications require a better understanding of the dynamics of individual active particles and their response to complex environments, which can be modeled by imposing well-characterized external free-energy landscapes. In this project, we carried out a comprehensive study of colloidal transport over complex free-energy landscapes: from self-propelled active colloids to transmembrane proteins in a living cell. With a large volume of single-particle trajectories obtained using optical microscopy and multi-particle tracking, we are able to provide a quantitative statistical description of the non-equilibrium distribution of the active particles over a one-dimensional periodic potential landscape. A central finding of this investigation is that the non-equilibrium transport and escape dynamics of the active particles can be described by an effective equilibrium approach, once the self-propulsion velocity v_0 is properly included into the effective potential U_eff(x;v_0).

16302818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302818.value: Grain boundaries are the interfaces of grains with different orientations in polycrystals. Energetic and dynamic properties of grain boundaries play essential roles in the mechanical and plastic behaviors of the materials. These properties of grain boundaries strongly depend on their microscopic structures. The classical grain boundary dynamics models are based on the motion by mean curvature to reduce the total interfacial energy (with fixed energy density). Such models neglect detailed microscopic structures and mechanisms of the grain boundaries. Experiments and atomistic simulations have shown that the grain boundary normal motion always leads to tangential motion due to the underlying microstructure (the coupling motion), which cannot be described by the classical models. Although some available models further include the decrease in grain boundary energy density by change of misorientation angle (sliding motion), these models are still not able to describe the grain boundary coupling motion in which the grain boundary energy density may increase. Cahn and Taylor described the coupling motion by a coupling coefficient. Despite a few attempts in the literature, a continuum grain boundary dynamics model that incorporates the underlying microstructures and the associated microscopic mechanisms is still lacking. In this proposed project, we will systematically develop continuum models for the energy and dynamics of low angle grain boundaries incorporating the underlying structure of line defects (dislocations), based on the discrete dislocation dynamics model. These continuum models will consist of evolution of both the grain boundaries and the dislocation densities on them, which determine their misorientation angles and the energy densities during the evolution. The long-range elastic interaction between dislocations is included in the continuum models to maintain stable dislocation structure on grain boundaries during the evolution. The continuum models will be able to describe both normal motion and tangential translation of grain boundaries and grain rotation due to both coupling and sliding effects, and will naturally accounts for the grain boundary shape change by motion and reaction of the constituent dislocations. Preliminary results have been obtained on the energy and structure of planar low angle grain boundaries and dynamics of a finite grain embedded in an infinite one in two dimensions. In this project, we will continue to derive continuum models for polycrystals and in three dimensions. We will also generalize the continuum models to high angle grain boundaries based on the line defects of disconnections (which have both the characters of dislocations and steps). 晶界是多晶材料中具有不同取向的晶粒之間的界面。晶界的能量和演化性質對於材料的機械和塑性行為起著至關重要的作用。晶界的這些特性很大程度上取決於它們的微觀結構。 經典的晶界動力學模型是基於以減少總界面能量（具有固定的能量密度）的平均曲率運動。這樣的模型忽略了晶界的微觀結構和運動機理。實驗和原子模擬表明，由於晶界的微觀結構，晶界的法向運動總是導致它們的切向運動（耦合運動）。這種運動是經典模型無法描述的。儘管一些已有的改進模型進一步考慮了由於晶界能量密度的降低引起的晶界取向偏差角的變化（滑動），這些模型仍然無法描述晶界的耦合運動，因為在耦合運動中晶界能量密度可能會增加。 Cahn和Taylor通過定義耦合係數來描述耦合運動。儘管在已有的文獻中有一些嘗試，但是仍然缺乏結合晶界的微觀結構和運動機理的連續的晶界動力學模型。 在本項目中，我們將系統地建立基於位錯 （晶體中的線缺陷）的小角度晶界的能量和動力學的連續模型。這些連續模型將從離散的位錯動力學模型推導出來。這些連續模型將包括晶界和它們上的位錯密度的演化。晶界上的位錯密度決定了演化過程中的晶界取向偏差角和晶界能量密度。位錯之間的遠程彈性相互作用也包含在連續模型中，它的作用是在晶界的演化過程中維持穩定的位錯結構。這些連續模型將能夠描述由於耦合和滑動效應引起的晶界的法向和切向運動以及晶粒旋轉，並且能夠描述由於晶界的位錯運動和反應引起的晶界形狀的變化。 我們已經獲得了一些關於平面小角度晶界的能量和結構以及二維空間中單個晶界 的動力學的初步結果。在這個項目中，我們將繼續推導出多晶體和三維空間中的的連續模型。我們還將連續模型推廣到基於斷接（同時具有位錯和階梯的特徵的一種線缺陷）的大角度晶界。

16302818.label: Realisation of objectives
16302818.value: Objective 1: We have developed a continuum model to determine the dislocation structure and energy of low angle grain boundaries in three dimensions [1]. The equilibrium dislocation structure is obtained by minimizing the grain boundary energy that is associated with the constituent dislocations subject to the constraint of Frank's formula. The orientation-dependent continuous distributions of dislocation lines on grain boundaries are described conveniently using the dislocation density potential functions, whose contour lines on the grain boundaries represent the dislocations. The energy of a grain boundary is the total energy of the constituent dislocations derived from discrete dislocation dynamics model, incorporating both the dislocation line energy and reactions of dislocations. The constrained energy minimization problem is solved by the augmented Lagrangian method and projection method. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions of the energy and dislocation densities of both planar and curved low angle grain boundaries. We have also developed a continuum model for dislocation structures of semicoherent interfaces [2]. In order to relieve the misfitting elastic energy, the hetero-interfaces become semicoherent by forming networks of dislocations. We develop a continuum model for the dislocation structures of semicoherent interfaces. The classical Frank-Bilby equation that governs the dislocation structures on semicoherent interfaces is not able to determine a unique solution. The available methods in the literature either use further information from atomistic simulations or consider only special cases (dislocations with no more than two Burgers vectors) where the Frank-Bilby equation has a unique solution. In our continuum model, the dislocation structure of a semicoherent interface is obtained by minimizing the energy of the equilibrium dislocation network with respect to all the possible Burgers vectors, subject to the constraint of the Frank-Bilby equation. The continuum model is validated by comparisons with atomistic simulation results. Objective 2: We have developed a continuum model for the dynamics of grain boundaries in three dimensions that incorporates the motion and reaction of the constituent dislocations [3]. The continuum model is based on a simple representation of densities of curved dislocations on the grain boundary. Illposedness due to nonconvexity of the total energy is fixed by a numerical treatment based on a projection method that maintains the connectivity of the constituent dislocations. An efficient simulation method is developed, in which the critical but computationally expensive long-range interaction of dislocations is replaced by another projection formulation that maintains the constraint of equilibrium of the dislocation structure described by the Frank’s formula. This continuum model is able to describe the grain boundary motion and grain rotation due to both coupling and sliding effects, to which the classical motion by mean curvature model does not apply. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions of evolutions of low angle grain boundaries and their dislocation structures. We have also developed a continuum model for the concurrent evolution of the grain boundary/triple junction network based upon the microscopic mechanisms of motion [4]. We have also performed rigorous partial differential equation analysis for the weak solutions of the proposed continuum grain boundary dynamics model [5]. We first prove the global-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solution to the initial-boundary value problem with positive equilibrium disconnection density parameter B, and then investigate the asymptotic behavior of the solutions as B goes to zero. Objective 3: We have proposed a continuum model for the grain boundary migration based on the underlying microscopic disconnection structure and mechanisms (thermally-activated nucleation and kinetically-driven motion of disconnections), in which multi disconnection modes are considered [6]. We performed continuum numerical simulations for investigating the grain boundary migration behavior in single and multi-mode disconnection limits in both a bicrystal under various conditions (two types of boundary conditions, finite-length grain boundaries with pinned ends, etc.). The results clearly demonstrate the significance of including the coupling and competing between different disconnection modes and driving forces for describing the complex and diverse phenomena of grain boundary migration within polycyrstalline microstructures. The microstructure of polycrystalline materials consists of networks of grain boundaries and triple junctions, along which three grain boundaries meet. We have also developed a continuum model for the concurrent evolution of the network of grain boundaries (GBs) and triple junctions (TJs) based upon the microscopic mechanism of motion of disconnections in the grain boundary that have both dislocation and step character [4]. The evolution involves thermally-activated disconnection formation/annihilation and migration of multiple disconnections modes/types. We proposed this crystallography-respecting continuum model for the disconnection mechanism of GB/TJ dynamics derived with a variational approach based on the principle of maximum energy dissipation. The resultant GB/TJ dynamics is reduced to an optimization problem with constraints that account for local microstructure geometry, conservation of Burgers vectors, and thermal-kinetic limitations on disconnection fluxes. We presented analysis of and numerical simulations based upon our model to demonstrate the dependence of the GB and TJ mobilities and the TJ drag effect on the disconnection properties. We also validated the continuum model predictions with molecular dynamics and experimental observations [7]. The continuum approach provides a means of reducing the complexity of the discrete disconnection picture to extract the features of disconnection dynamics that are important for microstructure evolution. 16302818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302818.value: We have developed a continuum model to determine the dislocation structure and energy of low angle grain boundaries in three dimensions [1]. The equilibrium dislocation structure is obtained by minimizing the grain boundary energy that is associated with the constituent dislocations subject to the constraint of Frank's formula. The energy of a grain boundary incorporates both the dislocation line energy and reactions of dislocations. The constrained energy minimization problem is solved by the augmented Lagrangian method and projection method. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions. We have also developed a continuum model for dislocation structures of semicoherent interfaces [2]. In order to relieve the misfitting elastic energy, the hetero-interfaces become semicoherent by forming networks of dislocations. The continuum model is validated by comparisons with atomistic simulation results. We have developed a continuum model for the dynamics of grain boundaries in three dimensions that incorporates the motion and reaction of the constituent dislocations [3]. The continuum model is based on a simple representation of densities of curved dislocations on the grain boundary. Efficient numerical formulations based on projection methods are developed to fix the illposedness due to nonconvexity of the total energy to avoid the computationally expensive long-range interaction of dislocations. This continuum model is able to describe the grain boundary motion and grain rotation due to both coupling and sliding effects, to which the classical motion by mean curvature model does not apply. Comparisons with atomistic simulation results show that our continuum model is able to give excellent predictions. We have also performed rigorous partial differential equation analysis for the global-in-time existence and uniqueness of the weak solutions of the proposed continuum grain boundary dynamics model [5]. We have proposed a continuum model for the grain boundary migration based on the underlying microscopic disconnection structure and mechanisms, in which multi disconnection modes are considered [6]. Simulation results demonstrate the significance of including the coupling and competing between different disconnection modes and driving forces. We have also developed a continuum model for the concurrent evolution of the network of grain boundaries and triple junctions based upon the motion of disconnections [4]. Variational approach based on the principle of maximum energy dissipation is employed in the derivation, leading to continuum dynamics with constraints. We also validated the continuum model predictions with molecular dynamics and experimental observations [7].

16302818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302818.value: The continuum models obtained in this project provide a basis for continuum simulations of grain boundary networks at larger length scales, to account for the effects of the underlining microscopic structures of grain boundaries which have been shown to play essential roles by recent experiments and atomistic simulations on the mechanical and plastic properties of the crystalline materials. More robust numerical methods can be further developed based on the obtained continuum models. Partial differential equation analysis can also be further performed to examine the nature and properties of the solutions of the proposed continuum models.

16302918.value: Our study revealed, for the first time, the exposure time and dosage-dependent formation of N6‑Formyl-Lysine (FLys), an abundant and lasting protein adduct formed when formaldehyde generated by nitrosative/oxidative stress and inflammation reacts with lysine residues in proteins, in cells and rat tissues after AA-I exposure. Because protein adducts were associated with altered protein functions and accelerated protein degradation, it is possible that the AA-I mediated N6-formylation of lysine may have played an important role in the renal fibrotic process induced by AAs. Moreover, lysine acetylation and methylation in histones are known to perform cell signaling functions, thus it is possible that AAs exert their toxicity by interfering with normal cell signaling processes. Because PTMs of proteins are major epigenetic mechanisms for controlling gene expression and aberrant modifications have been linked with carcinogenesis, it is likely that FLys formation is also linked with the observed toxicity of AAs. In another study, we discovered AA-I exposure induced GSH depletion in rat serum, which was accompanied by a parallel concentration-dependent formation of AA-cysteine and AA-N-acetyl-cysteine conjugates. These newly identified phase II metabolites shed light on a previously unaware protective role of endogenous aminothiols in protecting human from aristolochic acids nephropathy (AAN). The exposure-induced formation of AA-DNA adducts is well-studied for its association with both the carcinogenic and mutagenic properties of AA. With accumulating evidence showing that AA is an emerging class of environmental pollutant, we then investigated, for the first time, the effect of co-exposure to other co-existed environmental pollutants on the DNA adduct formation of AA. Results showed that co-exposure to naphthalene, acenaphthene, fluorene, phenanthrene, fluoranthene, or pyrene, diethyl phthalate, dibutyl phthalate, and benzyl butyl phthalate can interact synergistically with AAs to form elevated levels of AA-DNA adducts. These results provide direct evidence that prolonged co-exposure to the above-mentioned environmental contaminants may accelerate AAN development. Lastly, we investigated the potential causative role of AA-induced mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) damage and dysfunction in the observed toxicity of AAs. Our findings revealed AA exposure induces an exposure concentration and duration dependent lowering of ATP in both human kidney and liver cells, highlighting an AA exposure effect on mitochondrial energy production in the kidney and liver. We also detected high levels of mutagenic 8-oxo-dG and AA-DNA adduct on mitochondrial DNA isolated from AA-treated cells, unmasking a potentially important causative, but previously unknown role of mitochondrial DNA mutation in the pathophysiology of AAN.

16302918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302918.value: With the observations stated in Section 6.1, it is apparent that, despite decades of research, the toxicological mechanism of AA is complicated by its interactions with endogenous and exogenous factors, and the full picture awaits to be elucidated. Potential future research includes studying of other protein modifications, e.g. nitration and crosslinking in the observed toxicity of AA.

16302918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302918.value: The Project revealed previously unaware role of aminothiols conjugation, N6-formylation of lysine residues in proteins, and mitochondria dysfunction in the development of aristolochic acid nephropathy.

16303118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303118.value: 本项目将系统地发展重尾向量误差校正ARMA模型的统计推断过程。我们将首先发展重尾随机向量的极限理论, 然后建立条件满秩最小二次乘估计 (FLSE)的渐近理论。当尾部指数在0 与2之间,我期望能够证明长期参数的FLSE 的收敛速度是n (样本个数)与它的极限分布将是关于两个稳定随机过程的随机积分。当尾部指数丶在1 与2之间, 短期参数的FLSE 的收敛速度极可能是比n 慢与它的极限分布将是关于两个稳定随机过程的函数。但是当尾部指数在 0与1之间, 短期参数的FLSE 的收敛速度预期极可能仍然是比n 与它的极限分布不但依赖平稳成份而且也依赖非平稳成份.在此基础上, 我们期望导出条件减秩最小二乘估计(RLSE) 的极限分布。比较文献中关于重尾时间序列的成果, 我们关于短期参数的FLSE 和RLSE 的成果将会有显著的不同。这些可能的成果有可能为重尾时间序列的未来研究提供一个新的视角。以我们所知, 我们可能的渐近理论将是在重尾协整时间序列领域第一㳄获得的成果。本项目将用大量电脑模拟以评估 FLSE 和RLSE 在有限样本下的表现, 并用实际的例子说明我们的理论的可能应用。如果时间允许, 我们将提出一个重抽样 或Bootstrap 方法以取得极大似然比统计量的分布的近似分位点。

16303118.label: Realisation of objectives
16303118.value: We first studied the Whittle estimation for vector autoregressive and moving average (ARMA) models with heavy-tailed noises. It is shown that the Whittle estimator is consistent with the rate of convergence $n^{1/alpha} ilde{L}(n)$ and its limiting distribution is a function of two stable random vectors, where $ ilde{L}(n)$ is a slowly varying function and $alpha in (0,2)$ is the tail index of heavy-tailed vector noise. A simulation study is carried out to assess the performance of this estimator in finite samples and a real example is given. We then showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters in vector error correction (VEC) model is n (sample size) and its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when the tail index α ∈ (0, 2). Furthermore, we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n1/α ̃L(n) and its limiting distribution is a functional of two stable processes when α ∈ (1, 2). Simulation study is carried out to demonstrate the performance of both estimators. A real example with application to 3-month Treasury Bill rate, 1-year Treasury Bill rate and Federal Fund rate is given. We next proposed an automated approach that uses adaptive shrinkage techniques to determine the cointegrating rank and estimate the parameters simultaneously in a VEC model with unknown order p when its noise is represented by independent and identically distributed heavy-tailed random vectors with tail index α ∈ (0, 2). We showed that the estimated cointegrating rank and order p are equal to the true rank and the true order p0, respectively, with probability trending to one as the sample size n → ∞. The other estimated parameters achieve the oracle property. Finally, we studied the full rank least squares estimator (FLSE) and reduced rank least squares estimator (RLSE) of the heavy-tailed and partially nonstationary ARMA model with the tail index $alpha in (0,2)$. It is shown that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters is $n$ (sample size) and that related to the short-term parameters are $n^{1/alpha} ilde{L}(n)$ and $n$, respectively, when $alpha in (1,2)$ and $ in (0,1)$.Its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when $alpha in (0,2)$ for the long-run parameters and is a functional of some stable processes when $alpha in (1,2)$ for the short-run parameters. Based on FLSE, we derive the asymptotic properties of the RLSE. The finite-sample properties of the estimation are examined through a simulation study and an application to three U.S. interest rate series is given. To explore the possibility of using Lasso method to select variables in the heavy-tailed and partially nonstationary ARMA model, threshold s, the Lasso-based approach for variable selection of ARMA models was studied. We showed that the Lasso estimator has the Knight-Fu'slimit distribution under a general tuning parameter assumption. With a special restriction on tuning parameters, we showed that the Lasso estimator can achieve the oracle" properties zero parameters are estimated to be zero exactly and other estimators are as efficient as those under the true model. To explore the model checking of the heavy-tailed and partially nonstationary ARMA model, we proposed several tests for detecting serial correlation and ARCH effect in high-dimensional data. The dimension of data p = p(n) may go to infinity when the sample size goes to infinity. It is shown that the sample autocorrelations and the sample rank autocorrelations (Spearman’s rank correlation) of the L1-norm of data are asymptotically normal. Two portmanteau tests based, respectively, on the norm and its rank are shown to be asymptotically Chi—square istributed, and the corresponding weighted portmanteau tests are shown to be asymptotically distributed as a linear combination of independent Chi-square random variables. These tests are dimension-free, that is, independent of p, and the norm rank-based portmanteau test and its weighted counterpart can be used for heavy-tailed time series. Finally, to understand the possible effect of the change-point and threshold in the heavy-tailed and partially nonstationary ARMA model, we proposed a new approximation of a CPP by a Brownian motion and illustrated the above approximation in applications, such as the construction of confidence intervals of threshold parameters in threshold models. Furthermore, we investigated two test statistics for testing structural changes and thresholds in predictive regression models. The generalized likelihood ratio (GLR) test is proposed for the stationary predictor and the generalized F test is suggested for the persistent predictor. Under the null hypothesis of no structural change and threshold, it is shown that the GLR test statistic converges to a function of a centered Gaussian process, and the generalized F test statistic converges to a function of Brownian motions. A Bootstrap method is proposed to obtain the critical values of test statistics. Simulation studies and a real example are given to assess the performances of the proposed tests.

16303118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303118.value: This project has developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the heavy-tailed vector error correction autoregressive moving-average (ARMA) models. We established the asymptotic theory of its full rank LSE (FLSE) and reduced rank LSE (RLSE). We have obtained the rate of convergence of the FLSE and RLSE and their limiting distributions. It was conformed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters depends on the tail index. When the tail index is in (0,1), the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n and its limiting distribution not only depends on the stationary component itself but also depends on the unit root component. The results related to the short-term parameters of both FLSE and RLSE is significantly different from those of heavy-tailed time series in the literature. To the best of our knowledge, our asymptotic theory is the first time to obtain in the literature for the heavy tailed co-integrating time series. Extensive simulation studies have been carried out to access the performance of our procedure, and real examples have been given to illustrate their potential applications in practice. Some results have been published in the leading international journals.

16303218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303218.value: Harish-Chandra關於李群的表示理論是Langlands計劃的分析基礎。在他的理論中，幾何對像是與共軛相關的軌道積分，譜對像是表示的全局特徵。Harish-Chandra模的Dirac上同調為一個具有許多應用的群表示的內在不變量。 Vogan猜想揭示了Harish-Chandra模的狄拉克上同調与極小特徵的關繫。這個猜想由Pandzic和我证明。 Kostant擴展了狄拉克上同調的概念和Vogan猜想到更一般的立方狄拉克算子。與Pandzic和其他合作者一起我們確定了几种Harish-Chandra模的狄拉克上同調，包括上同調誘導模塊和最高模，並理解狄拉克上同調與李代數上同調的聯繫。我們建議使用最近開發的Dirac上同調理論研究表徵理論中的以下兩個相關問題：一個是通過辛的狄拉克上同調获取相關的李超代數和Weyl代數的表示，另一種是使用Dirac上同調的內窺鏡轉移中的表達和同调誘導模與亞瑟包一起使用。兩個問題都有明顯的幾何穩定共軛的背景，它對應於雙重橢圓元素上軌道積分的對象。狄拉克指數是自然的與表徵和內窺鏡轉移表现在常規橢圓元素上。在擴展設置中李超代數我們證明了辛狄拉克上同調正交補李超代數是一種自然的設置來獲得Adams提升正交全局特徵的傳遞因子和辛群。我們也將繼續研究這種聯繫在普通狄拉克上同調和辛狄拉克上同調之間與穩定共軛內的普通共軛相關。

16303218.label: Realisation of objectives
16303218.value: Many important questions on non-commutative Lie groups boil down to questions in invariant harmonic analysis: the study of distributions on groups that are invariant under conjugacy. The fundamental objects of invariant harmonic analysis are orbital integrals as the geometric objects and characters of representations as the spectral objects. The correspondence of these two kinds of objects reflects the core idea of harmonic analysis. In the formulation of central problems in Langlands program, the stable conjugacy plays a pivotal role. The theory of endoscopy investigates the difference between orbital integrals over ordinary and stable conjugacy classes. As Dirac cohomology of a Harish-Chandra module determines its K-character proved by PI and his collaborators, it corresponds to the dual object of the orbital integrals on elliptic elements. By using Dirac cohomology, the transfer factor is expressed as the difference of characters for the even and odd parts of the spin module, or Dirac index of the trivial representation. A lifting of characters on orthogonal groups and nonlinear metaplectic groups over real numbers was defined and studied by Jeff Adams and it was extended to the p-adic case by Tatiana Howard. This lifting is closely related to the endoscopic transfer in Langlands functoriality and the theta correspondence in Howe's reductive dual pairs. We determined the endoscopic transfer factors in many important cases. A related work is to understand the Fourier transform in the framework of the oscillator representation and the dual pair correspondence. This work was done in collaboration with Ling Zhou a former postgraduate student under my supervision. It offers the understanding of lifting of characters from a different perspective.

16303218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303218.value: The transfer factor of the Adams lifting is the difference of two irreducible components of the oscillator representation. This transfer factor is equal to the symplectic Dirac index of the trivial representation for the Lie superalgebra osp(1|2n). This is analogous to the fact that the endoscopic transfer factoras the difference of characters for the even and odd parts of the spin module is equal to Dirac index of the trivial representation as observed by PI. The corresponding Vogan's conjecture for symplectic Dirac operators of Lie superalgebras was established by PI and his collaborator. Let Mp(2n,R) denote the nonlinear two-fold covering group of the symplectic group Sp(2n,R). By formulating the Adams lifting in the framework of symplectic Dirac cohomology, we obtain direct lifting of characters from the linear group Sp(2n,R) to the nonlinear group Mp(2n,R). This lifting gives a bijection between the discrete series of Sp(2n,R) and the genuine discrete series of Mp(2n,R).

16303218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303218.value: The determination of the endoscopic transfer factors is an important step for understanding Langlands functoriality. Our usage of Dirac cohomology provides a new tool for study important problems in the Langlands program and this approach is under further investigation now.

16303218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303218.value: The Langlands program is a far-reaching and influential conjectural formulation of connections between number theory, algebraic geometry and representation theory. Proposed by Robert Langlands in 1960's, it seeks to relate Galois groups in algebraic number theory to automorphic forms and representation theory of algebraic groups over local fields and adeles. Widely seen as the single biggest project in modern mathematical research, the Langlands program is regarded as "a kind of grand unified theory of mathematics." We use the the new machinery Dirac cohomology to study the central problem the Langlands functoriality in the Langlands program.

16303318.label: Project Objectives
16303318.value: Analyze the behavior of the threshold dynamics near the contact line. We will perform a careful asymptotic analysis to study the behaviour of the minimizer near the contact line. We will identify the appropriate scaling factors for the heat kernels for different interface energies. We believe that this additional freedom to choose scales allows us to adjust the behavior near the contact line and remove the discrepancy between the computed contact angle and the Young's angle. We will also derive a dynamic law of the contact line motion. Develop an improved threshold dynamics method for simulating the motion of the interface on solid surface. The method will be implemented in both 2-dimensions and 3-dimensions and for geometrically rough as well as chemically rough surfaces. An adaptive mesh strategy based on the theory of a posteriori error estimates will also be implemented. Numerical experiments will be performed to verify the accuracy of the scheme and show that the improved method has better behavior near the contact line.

16303318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303318.value: Interface motion on a solid surface is an important problem in in the field of wetting and material science. The contact line behavior of the interface is of particular importance for understanding the characteristics of the surface. The threshold dynamics method developed by Merriman, Bence and Osher (MBO) is an efficient method for simulating the interface motion by mean curvature. The method has subsequently been extended to handle many other applications, including multi-phase networks with arbitrary surface tensions, wetting on a solid surface, image processing and auction dynamics. However, the contact line behavior and its dynamics are still poorly understood in the context of the threshold dynamics. In this proposed research, we intend to study the behavior of the interface near the contact line for the threshold dynamics method. We intend to derive a dynamic law of the contact line motion. The results will be used to develop an improved threshold dynamics method for the interface motion on a solid surface. 固體表面上的界面運動是潤濕和材料科學中的重要問題。界面的接觸線行為對於理解材料表面特別重要。由Merriman，Bence和Osher（MBO）開發的閾值動力學方法是一種通過平均曲率流模擬界面運動的有效方法。該方法隨後被擴展到處理許多其他應用，包括任意表面張力的多相問題，固體表面的潤濕，圖像處理和拍賣動態。然而，對於閾值動力學方法，仍然很難理解接觸線行為及其動態。在這個項目中，我們建議研究閾值動力學方法接觸線附近界面的漸近行為。結果將用於提高方法的準確性和效率。

16303318.label: Realisation of objectives
16303318.value: In this project, we first perform asymptotic analysis and show that, to remove the boundary layer near the contact point, we can modify the Gaussian Kernel variance for each surface energy term to obtain the correct Young's angle. We then derive the dynamic of the contact point which is consistent with the dynamic of the interface away from the contact point. We show that the improved threshold dynamics method still enjoys the energy-decaying property and is unconditionally stable. Numerical results confirmed the analytical results. Therefore both objectives are fully realized.

16303318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303318.value: We proposed a modified threshold dynamics method for wetting dynamics, which significantly improves the behavior near the contact line compared to the previous method. The new method is also based on minimizing the functional consisting of weighted interface areas over an extended domain including the solid phase. However, each interface area is approximated by the Lyapunov functional with a different Gaussian kernel. We show that a correct contact angle (Young's angle) is obtained in the leading order by choosing correct Gaussian kernel variances. We also show the Gamma convergence of the functional to the total surface energy. The method is simple, unconditionally stable with O(NlogN) computational complexity per time step and is not sensitive to the inhomogeneity or roughness of the solid surface. It is also shown that the dynamics of the contact point is consistent with the dynamics of the interface away from the contact point. Numerical examples have shown significant improvements in the accuracy of the contact angle and the hysteresis behavior of the contact angle. The results are published in a paper in Journal of Computational Physics, v. 392, September 2019, p. 291-310.

16303318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303318.value: The improved threshold dynamics method gives much better accuracy at the contact line (point). However, it seems the order of accuracy is still at half order. In the future, we will try to look for better scheme that can improve the order of accuracy at the contact line.

16303318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303318.value: We have resigned an improved numerical method to simulate the droplet motion on the solid surface with correct behavior near the contact point. The improvement is made based on a mathematical analysis to better choose the parameters used in the method.

16303418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303418.value: 在温度降低到接近玻璃化温度（Tg）时，聚合物分子的运动速率显著衰减。当温度降到低于玻璃化温度时，分子更达到几乎完全束缚状态。然而，最近研究发现，即使当测试温度低于玻璃化温度，聚合物薄膜贴近空气一侧的表面（自由表面），仍能观测到分子运动。利用局部标签法，可以得到聚合物薄膜沿厚度方向上的玻璃化温度分布，发现自由表面的玻璃化温度比本体材料的玻璃化温度小数十度。但是，基于该法所报导的数据，目前仅限于厚度大于12 nm及分子量大于临界缠结分子量（~20 kg/mol）的薄膜。因此，在表面灵敏度上及在样品分子量的自由度上该方法都有局限。 在香港研究资助局的支持下（项目编号：600513），本项目的其中一位研究员及他在香港科技大学的合作者最近成功研制了一种测量聚合物自由表面玻璃化温度的新技术。该技术基于飞行时间二次离子质谱法(ToF-SIMS)，现已于多种聚合物本体材料中得以验证。其中包括聚苯乙烯和聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯。 所涵盖的分子量达到3至405 kg/mol。由于飞行时间二次离子质谱法拥有次纳米级的采样深度，它能为任意分子量的聚合物单分子表面层的玻璃化温度, 提供前所未有的检侧机会。 在本项目中，我们提出利用飞行时间二次离子质谱法的表面高灵敏度，侧量聚合物薄膜自由表面单分子层的玻璃化温度。焦点将放在研究该玻璃化温度会否在相对表面临近时出现变化。如果会，在变化出现时两表面之间的距离是多少。目前对聚合物自由表面分子运动能力增强的物理机制仍然不太理解。尽管现有理论可以对大部分现象提供定性描述，但是对悬空聚合物薄膜的数据结果却并不适用。关于此，我们拟通过具策略性的计划调整聚合物薄膜材料或基底表面的属性，然后研究这些调整对相对表面临近效应的影响。通过这样的研究， 我们希望验证de Gennes的滑动运动模型（这是目前唯一可以解释悬空聚合物薄膜实验数据的模型）的有效性。我们相信，这样的研究结果将为进一步探究界面对聚合物分子运动速率沿厚度方向的分布的影响提供有效信息。同时也会为构建聚合物自由表面运动能力增强的模型提供有效的指导和借鉴。

16303418.label: Realisation of objectives
16303418.value: We have developed a new method in our lab. that employs Time-Of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) to study the surface glass transition temperature (Tg,s) and transition width (W) at the surface of polymer films. To make the method more accessible, we have also adapted it to employ contact angle measurement and had verified that it gave identical results to those obtained by TOF-SIMS. Objective 1: We have measured the Tg,s of polystyrene (PS) films on different substrates of oxide-covered silicon (SiOx) and soft polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer. By varying the film thickness (h) between ~5 and 100 nm, we examined the proximity effects on Tg,s from the SiOx and PDMS surfaces. In Publication No. 3, we have shown that the relaxation properties of PS next to PDMS were the same as those of PS next to a free surface. Therefore, the PS-PDMS surface can be used as a substitute for the free (i.e., PS-air) surface of PS. Our data showed that the proximity effects varied depending on whether the films had been pre-annealed at 343 K for 5 h or not. If the films were not pre-annealed, Tg,s and W of PS-SiOx and PS-PDMS were identical within experimental uncertainty, with Tg,s showing a decrease with decreasing film thickness below h ~ 100 nm, while W showing an increase with decreasing film thickness when h was smaller than an onset thickness equal to the radius of gyration (Rg) of the polymer. If the films had been pre-annealed, Tg,s and W of PS-SiOx became independent of film thickness, while Tg,s of PS-PDMS continued to decrease with decreasing film thickness and W became independent of film thickness. Tg,s of either preannealed or unannealed films with h > 100 nm were ~25 K below the bulk Tg (Tg,bulk). These results suggest that the proximity effects of the PS-SiOx and PS-PDMS interfaces were the same and equal to those of the free surface before pre-annealing. After preannealing, the nature of the PS-PDMS interface changed, which we surmised to be caused by interpenetration between the PS and PDMS chains across the interface. A primary goal of this experiment was to clarify if the sliding motion model of de Gennes could explain the molecular weight (MW) dependence of the reduction in Tg of freestanding polymer films. According to this model, a section of polymer chains can slide rapidly along its own contour if both ends of the section terminate at a free surface. This sliding motion enhances mobility and reduces the Tg of freestanding polymer films. However, the length of the polymer chains must be sufficient for two of its chain segments to simultaneously touch the opposite surfaces of a freestanding film for this motion to be feasible. Our measurements showed that the Tg,s of unannealed PS-SiOx and PS-PDMS films started to decrease with film thickness at the same thickness of ~100 nm, independent of MW. Therefore, de Gennes' model cannot be relevant to the Tg of freestanding films. However, we observed that the transition width W broadened when h was <= Rg, suggesting that sliding motion had occurred. This sliding motion caused the chain to bring varying mobilities from different depths of the polymer to the free surface, which explained the broadening in the glass transition. These findings were published in Publication No. 4. To better understand the difference in results between preannealed and unannealed films, we conducted a thorough investigation into the preannealing time dependence of Tg,s of PS-SiOx films with varying thicknesses. Our finding revealed that the time scale for Tg,s to recover the long-time value increase with the square of the film thickness. This suggests that the preannealing effect on Tg,s was caused by the diffusion of a quantity from the PS-SiOx that could lower Tg,s if present. Based on the suggestion of Colmenero and Cangialosi, we hypothesized that excess free volume existed at the PS-SiOx interface, which diffused out of the films upon thermal preannealing. We developed a model based on this idea that accurately described the preannealing time dependencies of the Tg,s of our films. These results were published in Publication No. 5. Objective 2: We have conducted experiments to compare the proximity effect of polymer films grafted to a solid substrate versus another polymer. We measured the Tg,s of PS grafted to SiOx with varying grafted density and hence film thickness, PS irreversibly adsorbed to SiOx, PS films supported on a PS brush grafted on SiOx, and PS layer formed by the self-assembly of a diblock copolymer film of PS and polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) on SiOx. We found that the Tg,s and W of all these films were identical and equal to those of the 100 nm thick PS-SiOx films. Since preparation of all these films involved preannealing, we interpreted the similar Tg,s found among these films to the absence of excess free volume in these films, which dominated the measurement. The small W of these films is attributed to the inhibition of the chain sliding motion in these films. Most of these results have been published in Publication No. 4. Objective 3: We have conducted experiments to investigate how chemical modifications affect the proximity effects of Tg,s. We measured Tg,s of PS films supported on hydrogen terminated silicon (HSi), PMMA, poly(acetoxy styrene) (PAS) films supported on SiOx. By confirming that the Tg of these films increased with decreasing film thickness, while those of PS-SiOx and PS-PDMS decreased with decreasing film thickness, we determined that the polymer-substrate interactions were strong in the PMMA, PAS and PS-HSi films but weak in the PS-SiOx and PS-PDMS films. Studying the Tg,s as a function of film thickness of these films allow us to verify that the strength of the polymer-substrate interaction correlates with the size of the proximity effect. Additional measurements have been made on the Tg,s measurements of poly (ethylene terephthalate) (PET), PS doped with dioctylphtalate (DOP), poly(4-methyl styrene) (P4MS), poly(bisphenol-A-carbonate) (PC), polysulfone (PSF), and poly (vinyl chloride) (PVC) to study the variation of Tg,s with the chemical species of the polymers and reported in Publication No. 6.

16303418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303418.value: In this project, we developed a new method to measure the surface glass transition of polymer films within 1 nm of the surface. This allows us to measure the proximity effect down to an unprecedented short distance of 5 nm. Our findings showed for the first time that de Gennes’ sliding motion model can cause broadening in the width of the surface glass transition but grafting to a substrate or entanglement suppress this motion effectively. We also found that Tg,s decreases with decreasing film thickness for PS films supported on either a solid (SiOx) or a soft elastomer (PDMS) substrate (Publication 4). The PS-PDMS interface was verified to be equivalent to the free surface as it produced the same perturbations to the dynamics of the PS films as the free surface did. (Publication 3) However, thermal pre-annealing caused the reduction of Tg,s in the solid-supported films to diminish but not in the PDMS-supported PS films. A model based on the diffusion of excess free volume holes from the solid substrate explained the result of the solid-supported films. For the PDMS-supported films, we hypothesize that thermal pre-annealing caused the PS and PDMS chains to interpenetrate, which sustained the excess free volume originally present at the PS-PDMS interface (Publication 5). Our research has also shown that the Tg of end-grafted single polymer chains is lowered by the free surface effect although end-grafting has an opposing effect on the Tg (Publication 2). Additionally, chemical modifications can be used to produce designable Tg-confinement effect in polymer films (Publication 1). We have also discovered that the shift in Tg,s relative to Tg,bulk correlates with fragility of the polymer. This is probably due to the energy landscape of fragile polymers being more heterogeneous, while that at the free surface is more uniform, allowing for bigger reductions in Tg,s in more fragile polymers (Publication 6). This paper has been selected as an Editor’s Pick for The Journal of Chemical Physics.

16303418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303418.value: The success of this project presents a new opportunity to tackle the challenging task of estimating the thickness of the mobile surface layer. One approach we are considering is to measure the thickness-dependence of the average Tg of polymer films with weak polymer-substrate interactions. This result will be mainly determined by the combined influences of Tg,s and the thickness of the mobile surface layer. By using the method we developed to measure Tg,s, we can differentiate the contribution from the thickness of the mobile surface layer. Our recent research has shown that Tg,s is linked to the fragility of the polymer. It would be interesting to explore whether the thickness of the mobile surface layer also correlates with fragility, providing valuable insight into the physics of this layer. We are currently conducting experiments to investigate these ideas.

16303418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303418.value: The primary objective of this project is to verify the validity of the sliding motion model proposed by de Gennes, which is a crucial model for explaining deviations in the dynamic properties of freestanding polymer films from the bulk polymer. Our results demonstrate, for the first time, that the physics underlying this model can significantly increase the dynamic heterogeneity of the films. This phenomenon is not limited to freestanding polymer films but also occurs in polymer films supported on substrates that do not immobilize the polymer chains relative to the substrate by chemical bonds or entanglement. Furthermore, we have developed a method to measure the glass transition temperature within 1 nanometer from the surface of polymers. This new capability will enable us to determine the thickness of the surface region of the polymer that exhibits anomalous dynamic properties, which would otherwise be challenging to obtain. Ultimately, these new findings will allow us to develop better theories to understand the dynamic properties of polymer films, which are essential for their efficient usage in various applications.

16303518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303518.value: The string theory of high energy physics is having a tremendous impact on current mathematical research such as that in mirror symmetry on algebraic geometry. Some correlation functions in string theory can be formulated in terms of algebraic geometry such as the Gromov-Witten (GW) invariants and Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten (FJRW) invariants. The computation and the understanding of these invariants are important for both mathematics and physics. Among many attempts to calculate GW invariants, we set up a theory of mixed-spin P-fields of stable maps and spin curves to effectively calculate GW invariants and FJRW invariants of all genera. This method has been used by several research groups of to compute these invariants. This theory also provides a platform for understanding the Calabi-Yau and Landau-Ginzburg correspondence predicted by string theory. In mathematics, a theory of stable quotients was established and has recently been found to play an important role in understanding the mirror symmetry of Calabi-Yau three-folds. In this project, we will set up a theory of mixed-spin P-fields of stable quotients and spin curves. We will perform the computations on moduli spaces of this theory. These results should give us a deep understanding of stable quotients invariants and their relations with FJRW invariants. 高能物理中的超弦理論對現代數學研究產生了巨大的影響，譬如鏡像對稱對代數幾何的影響。 超弦理論中的某些函數可以用代數幾何的量來表述，譬如Gromov-Witten不變量和Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten不變量。 這些不變量的計算和研究在數學和物理上都有重要的意義。 在眾多Gromov-Witten不變量的計算方法中，我們建立了穩定影射和帶旋曲線的混合帶旋P場的理論，這個理論提供了所有虧格的GW不變量和FJRW不變量的有效計算方法。這個方法已被幾個研究小組用來計算這些不變量，同時也提供了一個平台來研究物理上預測的Calabi-Yau和Landau-Ginzburg對應。 數學家們建立了穩定商的理論，而最近也發現了它在Calabi-Yau三維流形的鏡像對稱的研究的作用。在這個研究項目裡，我們會在此理論的模空間上做計算。這些研究結果會很好地幫助我們理解穩定商的不變量以及它與Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten不變量的關係。

16303518.label: Realisation of objectives
16303518.value: The main objective is to use some variant of mixed spin-P field theory (MSP for short) developed by us to study higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau quintic three-fold hypersurfaces. In our previous work on genus one Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau quintic three-folds, we used the localization technique on the moduli space of mixed-spin-P fields to carry out the calculations. It is demonstrated there that the MSP theory can effectively compute Gromov-Witten invariants. However, the combinatorics used there are quite involved. We had to use various methods beyond the traditional ones to get the needed formula. Bumsig Kim and his collaborators showed that they can get the same result for genus one Gromov-Witten invariants of the quintic Calalbi-Yau threefolds by working on quasi-maps and wall-crossings in the theory of quasi-maps. The theory of stable quotient is a special case of quasi-maps. Therefore, it is reasonable to work on stable quotient version of MSP theory. When we applied MSP theory to higher genus situation, we encountered several difficulties such as that the degree of the stable map has to be bigger than some number dependent on the genus of the domain curve. One possible solution is to modify fields there. There are several fields such as mu-fields and nu-fields that we can modify. A suitable modification might lead to workable moduli space. However, when we modify the mu-fields by replacing the line bundle associated to the mu-field with the tensor power of the line bundle in order to increase the degree, the moduli space of these new fields are not compact, and hence we were forced to work on quasi-map situation. Instead, we increased the number of mu-fields to N-many mu-fields where the original MSP theory has one mu-field. We call this new setup N-MSP theory. In the paper ``The theory of N-mixed-spin-P fields" written with H.L Chang, S. Guo and J. Li, we showed that N-MSP theory behaves the same as the original MSP theory. For example, its obstruction sheaf has a co-section. The degenerate locus of the cosection is a proper stack. Therefore, meaningful calculations can be done on the compact moduli space. It admits an N-dimensional torus action. We also worked out all the necessary torus localization calculations. In the subsequent papers written by Chang-Guo-J..Li, using the platform of NMSP, further calculations were carried out such as R-matrix etc. Several key conjectures for higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of quintic Calabi-Yau threefolds are proved, such as Yamaguchi-Yau finite generation conjecture and Bershadsky-Cecotti-Ooguri-Vafa conjecture on Feynman summation formula. It can be stated that the NMSP theory developed in this project leads to the solution of several most important and fundamental conjectures for Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau quintic three-folds. In this regard, we have achieved far more than the original objective of the project.

16303518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303518.value: The paper ``An effective theory of GW and FJRW invariants of quintic Calabi-Yau manifolds" is a sequel of the paper ``Mixed-Spin-P fields of Fermat polynomials", where we defined the mixed-spin-P fields (MSP fields for short) which geometrically combine Gromov-Witten theory and FJRW theory in one platform. The obstruction sheaf of the moduli stack of MSP fields admits a co-section. The main result of the paper``Mixed-Spin-P fields of Fermat polynomials" is to prove that the degenerate locus of the co-section is proper and of finite type. The properness of the degenerate locus enables us to use the moduli space to solve many key conjectures in Gromov-Witten theory and Landau-Ginzburg theory. In the current paper, we studied in more details about the moduli spaces of MSP fields and carried out all the computations in torus localization. In the paper ``The theory of N-mixed-spin-P fields", we modified the MSP fields by introducing N many mu fields. Before, we used MSP fields to reprove the formula of genus one Gromov-Witten invariants of the quintic threefold conjectured by physicists and first proved by Zinger. We knew that MSP fields theory can be used to study higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants. However, when we applied the localization method, some combinatoric difficulties emerged. It was found out that, if one introduce N many mu-fields in the definition of MSP fields and made some clever choice of weights, the combinatoric difficulties disappeared. This paper contains the theoretical part of a series of papers and all the localization computations. In the subsequent papers by my collaborators, several key conjectures for higher genus Gromov-Witten theory of Calabi-Yau threefolds, such as Yamaguchi-Yau finite generation conjecture and Bershadsky-Cecotti-Ooguri-Vafa conjecture, are all solved using N-MSP theory developed in this paper. In the paper ``A genus-one FJRW invariant via two methods", using the results in the previous two papers on MSP theory, we considered genus one FJRW invariants of the Fermat polynomial of degree three of three variables. Such an invariant was computed explicitly and was used in another paper by my collaborators for a complete understanding of FJRW invariants of the Fermat polynomial.

16303518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303518.value: In our previous work, we studied hypersurfaces of a projective space. One natural generalization is hypersufraces of toric varieties and complete intersections of toric varieties. These will cover most of Calabi-Yau manifolds in the existing literature. One of the key parts is to give a correct definition of MSP fields in such a way that the moduli stack of degenerate locus of the co-setiton of the theory is proper. This is contained in my next two GRF grants.

16303518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303518.value: Since the seminal work of physicists Candelas, dela Ossa, Green, and Parkes, Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau quintics has been one of the hottest research topics for the last thirty years. Genus zero and genus one Gromov-Witten invariants are completely understood by mathematicians. Higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants pose a serious challenge to mathematicians due to the fact that the methods for genus one and genus one won't work for higher genus case. We developed a mixed-spin-P fields theory (NMSP for short), which combines Gromov-Witten invariants and FJRW invariants in one geometric setup. We also showed that it provides a platform for effective computations which led to the reprove of the formula of genus one Gromov-Witten invariants first prove by Zinger. Pushing to higher genus cases, we met some serious combinatoric difficulties. In this project, we discovered that, if we enlarge the number of mu-fields in the definition of MSP theory to N many mu-fields and cleverly choose parameters, we can overcome the combinatoric difficulties. We studied this variation of MSP theory, called N-MSP theory. Based upon computations in N-MSP theory carried out in this project, my collaborators proved several most important conjectures in Gromov-Witten theory of Calabi-Yau quintics.

16303918.label: Realisation of objectives
16303918.value: We have fully realized the objectives of this research proposal in two stages, reported in two Physical Review E publications. The abstracts of the two publications can best summarize the manners in which the objectives have been addressed and attained. Abstract of the first publication (Physical Review E 101, 063104 (2020)): We have obtained analytically the complete set of hydrodynamic modes (HMs) for a two-dimensional (2D) fluid confined within a channel with the Navier slip boundary condition at the hydrodynamic boundary. The HMs are orthogonal to each other and hence each represents an independent degree of freedom. We show that the HMs can be used to recursively generate a time series of random thermal fluctuations of displacement velocity, with identical statistical distributions as those obtained from MD simulations. By projecting the HMs onto molecular dynamics (MD) configurations and evaluating the resulting decay time from the autocorrelation function, we obtain from MD the eigenvalues of the HMs. Multiplying two different HMs and integrating as a function of z from center of the channel towards the fluid-solid interface, the position of the hydrodynamic boundary (HDB)is unambiguously identified as the point at which the integral vanishes. Invariably the HDB is located inside the fluid domain and not on the liquid-solid interface. With the knowledge of the HDB position, the value of the slip length can be obtained directly from HM’s dispersion relation. We show that in terms of the complete set of HMs, the fluctuation-dissipation theorem may be expressed in a simple expression involving the average of the inverse of the eigenvalues. Besides offering an alternative perspective on thermal fluctuations and hydrodynamic boundary, the present work opens the possibility of using modulated boundary conditions to manipulate thermal fluctuations in mesoscopic channels, which can lead to interesting statistical mechanical consequences. Abstract of the second publication (Physical Review E 103, 053106 (2021)) Thermal fluctuations constitute a fundamental equilibrium phenomenon whose spatial and temporal correlations are governed by the relevant scales of molecular collisions. From the continuum point of view, thermal fluctuations in a fluid can be regarded as comprising a multitude of hydrodynamic modes (HMs) with random phases, each one having one degree of freedom. We show that in a two-dimensional fluid channel with the Navier slip boundary condition, in which the HMs are represented by periodic arrays of vortex and anti-vortex pairs, periodic modulation of the slip boundary condition can selectively suppress non-commensurate HMs while phase lock the remaining eigenmodes. As a result, thermal fluctuations would exhibit mesoscopic-scale spatial correlations, manifest as a spatially varying diffusion constant when evaluated from the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Good agreement is shown with the molecular dynamics results. Such manifestation of equilibrium collective motion implies that instead of just being an alternative mathematical basis for expressing thermal fluctuations, in mesoscopic systems the HMs may be manipulated to have physical consequences very different from those expected in bulk fluid.

16303918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303918.value: The major findings are (1) the formulation of thermal fluctuations in terms of the eigenmodes of the Navier-Stokes equation, i.e., the hydrodynamic modes, as opposed to the molecular Brownian motion point of view as offered by the traditional kinetic theory of gas; and (2) the discovery that in mesoscopic fluid systems, the consequences from the long-range correlation of the hydrodynamic modes can be made manifest through the modulation of the liquid-solid boundary condition, e.g., by periodically alternating between the slip and nonslip boundary conditions. The latter can have profound consequences, since thermal fluctuations constitute a fundamental element of the thermal equilibrium condition. These two major findings are reported in two separate publications.

16303918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303918.value: Since I will be retired at June 30, 2022, there will not be any further development of this research from my group. However, I would like to mention that due to the work of this project, an analytic solution for the 3D eigenfunctions of the Navier-Stokes equation in the channel flow geometry has been obtained. This represents a major breakthrough. By using the 3D analytic solution, combined with the previously obtained 2D and 1D solutions, the whole Navier-Stokes equation can be reduced to an autonomous system of coupled ordinary (matrix) differential equations, with time being the only independent variable. The nonlinear term in the Navier-Stokes equation is represented by a tensor, which couples two hydrodynamics modes to effect the time variation on the third. By using this formulation, my postdoc and I have already obtained some remarkable results on the channel flow and Darcy Law behavior beyond the critical Reynolds number for the channel flow. The manuscript is presently being written up to be submitted soon.

16303918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303918.value: The main outcome of this project is to offer an alternative perspective on the traditional kinetic theory view of thermal fluctuations, with important consequences for mesoscopic fluid systems. Whereas the traditional view is that thermal fluctuations are a fact of nature that can only be regulated by temperature, with our new formulation we show that in mesoscopic systems thermal fluctuations can also be manipulated by modulating the liquid-solid boundary conditions. This is something totally unexpected previously.

16304218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304218.value: The development of low-cost solar cells is crucial for sustainable power generation. Organic solar cells (OSC) are low-cost and environmental-friendly alternatives to conventional silicon cells. Current OSC exhibit efficient photocurrent generation, reaching over 12% efficiency. Nevertheless, such performance remains modest compared to silicon cells, and further improvement is required for OSC to compete commercially. The key limitation of OSC is the low open-circuit voltage due to large photovoltage loss. A key breakthrough was achieved recently by our group at HKUST. As published in Nature Energy and in JACS, we have developed two non-fullerene OSC systems that operate efficiently yet with only small photovoltage losses. These systems (named P3TEA:SF-PDI2 and PvBDTTAZ:O-IDTBR) have negligible donor-acceptor energy offset that allows charges to be generated at the interface with very small energy loss. Crucially, these systems are special because most other OSC systems (including both fullerene and non-fullerene OSC) do not operate well with such small energy offset. Previous studies attributed the high performance of these systems to their ability to create free charges at ultrafast timescales. However, the small photovoltage losses of these unique systems must also be strongly related to how charges recombine after they are created, and this has not been accounted for in earlier studies. In fact, the charge recombination processes in these systems must be different compared to other OSC systems, as evidenced by their high electroluminescence yields (at least 100 times higher than in conventional systems). Developing a fundamental understanding on charge recombination in these unique systems is crucial for further development of OSC with small photovoltage loss. Furthermore, these systems have very small Urbach energy (25 meV) compared to other OSC systems (>40 meV), indicating low degree of energetic disorder that may help suppress recombination. In this project, we will study the mechanism of charge recombination in these unique systems and its relationship with the small Urbach energy. For the first time, we will characterise the charge recombination dynamics in these systems using time-resolved optical and electrical techniques, and relate it to the high electroluminescence yield. We will then systematically vary Urbach energy by fine-tuning the processing conditions and changing the molecular acceptor involved, and identify how charge recombination is affected. The outcome of this project will provide valuable insights on the control of charge recombination in OSC with small photovoltage loss, and thereby promote the development of OSC with over 15% efficiency. 低成本太陽能電池的開發對於可持續發電至關重要。有機太陽能電池（OSC）是傳統矽電池的低成本和環保替代品。目前的OSC表現出有效的光電流產生，效率超過12％。然而，與硅電池相比，這種性能仍然適中，並且OSC需要進一步改進以進行商業競爭。 OSC的關鍵限制是由於大的光電壓損失導致的低開路電壓。 我們最近在香港科技大學取得了重大突破。正如Nature Energy和JACS中所公佈的那樣，我們開發了兩種非富勒烯OSC系統，它們只需很小的光電壓損失即可高效運行。這些系統（稱為P3TEA：SF-PDI2和PvBDTTAZ：O-IDTBR）具有可忽略的供體 - 受體能量偏移，其允許在界面處產生具有非常小的能量損失的電荷。至關重要的是，這些系統是特殊的，因為大多數其他OSC系統（包括富勒烯和非富勒烯OSC）在如此小的能量偏移下運行不佳。以前的研究將這些系統的高性能歸因於它們在超快時間尺度下產生自由電荷的能力。 然而，這些獨特系統的小光電壓損失也必須與電荷在產生後重新組合的方式密切相關，而這在早期研究中尚未得到解決。事實上，與其他OSC系統相比，這些系統中的電荷重組過程必須是不同的，正如它們的高電致發光產率（至少比傳統系統高100倍）所證明的那樣。在這些獨特系統中對電荷重組進行基本了解對於進一步開發具有小光電壓損耗的OSC至關重要。此外，與其他OSC系統（> 40 meV）相比，這些系統具有非常小的Urbach能量（25 meV），表明低程度的能量障礙可能有助於抑制重組。 在這個項目中，我們將研究這些獨特系統中電荷重組的機理及其與小Urbach能量的關係。我們將首次使用時間分辨光學和電學技術表徵這些系統中的電荷重組動力學，並將其與高電致發光產率聯繫起來。然後，我們將通過微調處理條件和改變所涉及的分子受體來系統地改變Urbach能量，並確定電荷重組如何受到影響。該項目的成果將為OSC中電荷重組控制提供有價值的見解，光電壓損失小，從而促進OSC的發展，效率超過15％。

16304218.label: Realisation of objectives
16304218.value: We have successfully completed all four of our objectives in this project, and our results have led to five publications in peer-reviewed journals (see full list below and in Part C). First, we used ultrafast optical spectroscopy methods to study charge recombination dynamics in the model non-fullerene organic solar cell (OSC) blends: P3TEA:SF-PDI2 and PvBDTTAZ:O-IDTBR (Ref. [1]). By quantifying the absorption tail using sensitive photocurrent measurements, we found that both blends exhibit an Urbach energy of around 27-30 meV, which is significantly lower compared to polymer:fullerene blends (>40 meV). This indicates that the degree of energetic disorder at the non-fullerene interface is much lowered. We found that the lowered Urbach energy is crucial for enabling long charge-transfer (CT) state lifetimes, thus reducing the rate of charge recombination at the donor:acceptor interface. It is also shown that the small energy offset between singlet exciton and CT states enable charges to thermally populate the emissive singlet exciton state and recombine radiatively, thus promoting solar cell efficiency. However, such radiative process is much slower compared to the non-radiative relaxation pathway despite the lowered Urbach energies in these non-fullerene blends, as evident by the modest electroluminescence yields (~0.02%). Since the lower-gap polymers in these blends have photoluminescence quantum yield of ~2%, the radiative recombination rate is determined to be about 1% of the non-radiative recombination rate (Objective 1). Based on our results on the model P3TEA:SF-PDI2 and PvBDTTAZ:O-IDTBR blends, we then went on to study the effect of blend ratio and other similar non-fullerene blends to further understand charge recombination processes in these materials (Objective 2). In Ref. [2], we studied charge recombination dynamics in P3TEA:SF-PDI2, P3TEA:di-PDI, and P3TEA:PCBM (fullerene), particularly focusing on recombination via the spin-triplet states. We found negligible triplet recombination in both non-fullerene blends regardless of blend ratio, while the fullerene-based P3TEA:PCBM blend showed substantial charge losses via the spin-triplet pathway (occurs on the nanosecond timescale). Since both non-fullerene blends showed much reduced Urbach energies compared to the fullerene blend, our results support the notion that reducing energetic disorder at the interface is needed to limit charge recombination via both spin states. In addition to the higher Urbach energy, it is important to note that the inclusion of fullerene acceptors also leads to a much higher triplet exciton energy than the two non-fullerene acceptors with respect to the CT state. The lowered energy difference between CT and T1 state at the interface is likely to cause faster CT to T1 transition, in agreement with Marcus theory. This result highlights the importance of engineering the energetic levels of both spin-states at the donor-acceptor interface in order to achieve efficient interfacial charge generation. Furthermore, we found that OSC blends with very small or negative interfacial energetic offsets suffer from rapid (~1 ps) CT state recombination that would lead to poor photocurrent generation unless a strong electric field is applied across the organic layer (Objective 3). During the course of this project, a new high-performance non-fullerene OSC blend named PM6:Y6 has been developed, leading to the first OSC device with over 15% efficiency. In Ref. [4], we carried out ultrafast optical spectroscopy to study charge dynamics in this blend, and compared it to the aforementioned P3TEA:SF-PDI2 blend. Our results show that both blends exhibit similar charge generation dynamics at the interface, involving an initial fast electron/hole transfer (~1 ps) followed by a much slower and thermally-activated separation of CT states to form free charges (~100 ps to complete). Instead, the key difference between the two blends lies in the charge recombination rate at later times (~100 ps onwards), with PM6:Y6 showing much longer charge lifetime which is in agreement with the higher device performance. It is shown that OSC blends based on Y6 acceptors have the lowest Urbach energy levels among all OSC blends developed to date (below 25 meV), and this is consistent with our hypothesis that a low Urbach energy helps to reduce non-radiative recombination rates at the donor-acceptor interface. We also studied charge recombination dynamics in ternary OSC blends based on Y6 acceptors (Ref. [5]), also showing extended charge lifetime due to suppressed interfacial charge recombination. Crucially, the Y6-based blends show >90% photocurrent generation yields and low voltage losses (~0.55V; defined as energy difference between open-circuit voltage and optical edge) at room temperature, with reducing charge separation efficiencies at lowered temperature. This result indicates that an Urbach energy below thermal energy (~25 meV at room temperature) is needed to promote interfacial charge separation and therefore achieve high device performance (Objective 4). Overall, our results lead to a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between interfacial disorder (Urbach energy) and charge recombination rates in OSC blends. It is found that a low Urbach energy below thermal energy (~25 meV at room temperature) is needed to enable efficient electron-hole separation at the donor-acceptor interface. The large degree of energetic disorder (high Urbach energy) in fullerene-based OSC blends is a key factor driving fast non-radiative recombination at the interface (CT state), while the much improved interfacial order in non-fullerene blends (such as Y6-based blends) can exhibit much longer interfacial charge lifetimes. 16304218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304218.value: Our results lead to a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between interfacial energetics and charge recombination rates in OSC blends. By studying charge recombination dynamics in a range of OSC blends based on both non-fullerene and fullerene acceptor molecules, it is found that a low Urbach energy below thermal energy (~25 meV at room temperature) is needed to enable efficient electron-hole separation at the donor-acceptor interface. The large degree of energetic disorder (high Urbach energy) in fullerene-based OSC blends is a key factor driving fast non-radiative recombination at the interface (CT state), while the much improved interfacial order in non-fullerene blends (such as Y6-based blends) can exhibit much longer interfacial charge lifetimes. In addition to interfacial energetic disorder, the alignment of donor-acceptor energy levels as well as spin-triplet exciton levels are also found to play important roles in determining the overall charge recombination rate. Furthermore, the effects of temperature and electric fields on the charge dynamics were studied in a range of OSC blends with varying interfacial energetic properties. Our results from this project have led to five publications in peer-reviewed journals. These fundamental results will help promote rational design of high-performance OSC materials and devices for use in future clean solar energy applications.

16304218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304218.value: While the combination of new material development and fundamental photophysical studies have led to a big improvement in the efficiency of solution-processed OSC devices (from ~13% in 2018 to ~18% in 2021), their efficiencies are still lower than that of commercial silicon cells which require high-temperature processing. The key limitation lies in the much faster non-radiative recombination rate compared to the radiative recombination rate, leading to a relatively large reduction in open-circuit voltage with respect to the absorption energy. In order to further improve OSC performance, it is crucial to engineer organic donor-acceptor heterojunctions with sufficiently slow non-radiative recombination rates, such that the probability for charges to undergo radiative relaxation is improved.

16304218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304218.value: Harvesting clean solar energy is crucial for sustainable development. Current solar cells are based on inorganic crystalline silicon that needs to be processed at very high temperature, thus leading to long energy-payback time. The development of solution-processed organic solar cells (OSC) at low temperature is therefore highly desirable, but the efficiency of OSC have remained inferior to their inorganic silicon counterparts. Understanding the fundamental electronic processes that limits the efficiency of OSC materials is needed to improve the performance of this promising technology. This project studies the fundamental relationship between interfacial energetics and charge recombination rates in a range of OSC material systems. Our results highlight the importance of minimising energetic disorder at the interface in order to promote thermally-activated electron-hole separation, as well as the need of optimising interfacial energetic levels of both spin-states.
