16305418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305418.value: Receptor models are essential and effective tools in producing quantitative source information in tackling air pollution problems (Wong Y. K. et al., 2020). In this project we have addressed a few data generation and data analysis issues pertinent to source apportionment through reception modeling. The major findings include: (1) It is feasible to deploy the in-situ Thermal desorption Aerosol Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analyzer for organic molecular source markers (i.e., TAG-GC/MS system) (Wang Q. Q. et al., 2020; He X et al., 2020; Wang S. et al., 2022). This system provides bihourly monitoring of 130+ PM2.5-borne individual organic compounds, many of which are characteristic tracers for combustion sources and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) of different precursors. (2) The high-time resolution nature of the organic markers allows capturing the dynamic change of source emissions and atmospheric aging, providing observational evidence to support their use in source apportionment (Wang Q. Q. et al., 2021). (3) The TAG-GC/MS has generated bihourly data of long-chain unsaturated fatty acids (uFAs) and saturated fatty acids, which are excellent tracers for cooking emissions in urban environments. uFAs, such as oleic acid, undergo rapid degradation via heterogeneous reactions with atmospheric oxidants upon emission. We obtained the nighttime decay rates of three cooking-related uFAs using a relative rate approach applied to bihourly measured data in urban Shanghai (Wang and Yu, 2021). The decay rates of elaidic and linoleic acid are determined to be 0.62 and 1.37 that of oleic acid, respectively. Our work provides the first kinetic data pertaining to real-world conditions. They are valuable for constraining the modeling of heterogeneous aging of ambient organic aerosols. (4) The TAG-GC/MS allows us to examine the abundance and variations of the SOA tracers in five PM2.5 episodes in urban Shanghai. Among them the SOA attributed to monoaromatic compounds (e.g., toluene) accounted for a noticeable portion of the total OM, implying that control strategies targeting local anthropogenic emissions would be effective in reducing the severity of episodic PM pollution. (5) The incorporation of detailed organic tracer data, along with other PM2.5 constitutes, has enabled us to produce unprecedently detailed source apportionment results for an urban site and a suburban site in Shanghai (Li R. et al, 2020; Wang, S. et al., 2022). Up to 14 PM2.5 sources are identified. Comparison of before and during COVID lockdown reveals that the formation change in secondary inorganic and organic compounds in response to substantial reductions in urban primary precursors are different for urban and suburban environments. (6) Degradation of organic molecular markers posts a challenge for receptor modeling. We have demonstrated the existence of atmospheric degradation and characterize the impact of ignoring degradation in source attrition results (Wong et al., 2019, 2021). (7) Rapid source apportionment has been demonstrated to be feasible via rolling positive matric factorization analysis of the hourly chemical composition data (Wang Q. Q. et al, 2022).

16305418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305418.value: This research can be further developed in the following four perspectives. First, the online TAG-GC/MS system can be expanded to include a second channel to analyze the suite of organic compounds in either total quantity (gas phase + PM phase) or in the gas-phase. This expansion allows source apportionment to tap into those organic compounds that significantly partition to the gas phase. It also enables the studies of gas-particle partitioning chemistry of the semi-volatile organic compounds. Second, it is worth exploring adapting the online TAG-GC/MS system for off-line analysis of filter samples. Sampling on filters is a reliable mean to provides PM2.5 materials for chemical analysis in routine monitoring program. This add-on feature will increase our ability in obtaining long time-series of composition data through analyzing archived filters. Third, the rapid source apportionment method for secondary sources is inferior in performance to that for primary sources. Further efforts are needed to work out a solution for the secondary sources. Fourth, we have identified organic tracer degradation has impact on the accuracy of receptor models-based source apportionment. How to address this issue in PMF-based receptor modeling needs to be studied.

16305418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305418.value: Accurate identification of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) primary and secondary sources and quantification of their contributions shapes the scientific basis underlying pollution control policies. Past measurement-based efforts rely on long-time integration of sampling and off-line analysis, severely constraining our ability in getting timely pollution source information. In this project, we have demonstrated the technical feasibility of lifting the data constrain through field testing and deploying an online PM2.5 chemical composition monitoring platform. One center piece of instrument is an in-situ Thermal desorption Aerosol Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analyzer for organic molecular source markers (i.e., TAG-GC/MS system). We have resolved multiple key operational issues of this instrument. The source-specific tracers, together with other PM2.5 constituents, have been shown to be effective in identifying sources, up to 14 sources at an urban and a suburban site in Shanghai. This level of source differentiation could not have been achieved without the suite of molecular and elemental source markers. We also developed a rapid source apportion approach based on receptor modeling of the above-obtained hourly chemical composition data. The results from this project provide policy makers with valuable information to enable a faster response to pollution events and to formulate timelier PM2.5 emission control strategies.

16305518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305518.value: There is now great interest in generating luminogenic materials for circularly-polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CPOLEDs). CPOLEDs can deliver high contrast in 3D images and reduce the perceived distortion at some angles to enhance the outdoor viewing of laptops and smartphones. They also exhibit greater brightness than non-polarized diodes and depress the reflection of ambient light. To fabricate efficient CPOLEDs, luminogenic materials with strong luminescence quantum yield and dissymmetry factor are needed. Finding such materials is still challenging as there is no clear design strategy. But the luminescent materials currently used such as chiral organometallics, small molecules and polymers suffer from high cost, poor stability and aggregation-cased quenching. The development of new circularly-polarized luminescent (CPL) materials without these problems is of both fundamental importance and commercial value. Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) from some propeller- or shell-shaped molecules has been observed in our laboratory. They show no emission or only weak emission in dilute solution but emit intensely when aggregated. That property makes them excellent candidates for fabricating thin-film optoelectronic devices. Non-doped OLEDs based on AIE luminogens (AIEgens) have already demonstrated high current and external quantum efficiency (59 cd/A and 18%) with a small efficiency roll-off. Incorporating chiral moieties into AIEgens was found to generate materials with a helical conformation with efficient CPL. Such AIEgens may well serve as promising light-emitting layers of CPOLEDs. However, that possibility is still virtually unexplored. In this study we propose to develop new chiral AIEgens for fabricating efficient CPOLEDs. New AIE-active molecules and polymers with different luminogenic skeletons and chiral groups will be designed and synthesized. Their photophysical and chiroptical properties will be systematically investigated to gain insight into their structure-property relationships. Promising candidates will be chosen for fabricating CPOLEDs by vacuum deposition and solution processing. Their device performance will be optimized. It is expected that new chiral AIEgens for efficient CPOLEDs will be generated in this research. 現在研究人員對於發展用於圓偏振有機發光二極管（CPOLEDs）的發光材料興趣濃厚。CPOLEDs能夠在3D圖像中提供高對比度，並減少某些角度的感知失真，從而增強筆記本電腦和智能手機的戶外觀看效果。它們還表現出比非偏振二極管更高的亮度，並抑制環境光的反射。為了製備有效的CPOLEDs，需要具有強發光量子產率和不對稱因子的發光材料。由於沒有明確的設計策略，因而尋找此類材料仍然具有挑戰性。並且目前使用的發光材料如手性有機金屬化合物，小分子和聚合物具有成本高，穩定性差和聚集熒光猝滅的缺點。因此開發消除這些問題的新型圓偏振發光（CPL）材料具有基礎性的重要意義和商業價值。 一些螺旋槳式或殼形分子具有聚集誘導發光（AIE）特性在我們實驗室被發現。這類分子在稀溶液中不發光或僅微弱發光，但分子聚集時卻發光很強。該特性使其成為製造薄膜光電器件的理想選擇。基於AIE發光材料（AIEgens）的非摻雜OLEDs具有高的電流和外量子效率（59 cd/A和18％），同時擁有小的效率滾降。將手性基團引入到AIEgens中能夠製備出具有有效CPL特性的螺旋構象材料。這種AIEgens能夠作為有潛力的發光層應用於CPOLEDs中。然而這種可能性實際上仍未得到探索。 在本研究項目中我們提出開發新型的手性AIEgens，用於製造有效的CPOLEDs。具有不同發光骨架和手性基團的新AIE活性分子和聚合物將被設計和合成。它們的光物理和手性光學性質將被系統地研究，從而獲得這類材料的結構–性能關係。選擇有前景的材料通過真空沉積和溶液加工來製備CPOLEDs。優化器件性能。期望通過本研究項目獲得用於高效CPOLEDs的新型手性AIEgens。

16305518.label: Realisation of objectives
16305518.value: The objectives of this proposed research project are to design and synthesize new aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogens (AIEgens) for the fabrication of efficient organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), particularly those showing circularly polarized light (CPL). Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goal, we introduced chiral units to AIEgens to generate new chiral molecules that can self-assemble into well-defined architectures. These molecules exhibit stronger CPL and larger dissymmetry factors in the solid state than single molecules in solutions, demonstrating a phenomenon of aggregation-enhanced circularly polarized luminescence. The well-ordered helical architectures are important to enhance the CPL and dissymmetry factor of chiral AIEgens. Through host–guest interaction, supramolecular materials have been successfully used to construct light-harvesting platforms or as reactors to accelerate the reaction rate. On the other hand, achiral AIEgens in co-assembly systems can also exhibit CPL when they are embedded in confined chiral nanostructures. Through such a co-assembly strategy, numerous CPL-active materials based on achiral AIEgens can be generated. We also synthesized discrete platinum(II) metallacycle with deep-red/near infrared (NIR) emission for the first time for constructing solution-processed OLEDs by mixing a 180° di-Pt(II) acceptor with a pyridyl-decorated ligand functionalized by a deep-red fluorescent emitter. The platinum(II) centre harvests the triplet excitons and transfers the energy to the fluorescent ligand containing the luminophore to give the resulting OLED with a high external quantum yield (EQE) and an excellent exciton utilization efficiency that overcomes the theoretical limit of conventional fluorescent emitters. As light-emitting SCCs are attracting intense attention, the triplet harvesting, and intramolecular FRET mechanism realized here should aid in enlightening the application of SCCs in the field of solid-state optical materials. We further designed and synthesized two green (BDMAC-XT) and sky-blue (BDPACX-XT) luminogens showing aggregation-enhanced delayed fluorescence characteristics. These molecules enjoy high thermal and electrochemical stabilities. The rigid xanthen-9-one core endows the luminogens with high quantum yields of 96% and 94% in neat films. The non-doped OLEDs of BDMAC-XT display green light with high EQE values of up to 21% and extremely small efficiency roll-offs of ∼0%, 4.8%, and 14.3% at 1000, 5000, and 10,000 cd m-2, respectively. Sky-blue non-doped OLEDs are fabricated using BDPAC-XT as the emitting layer that show impressive high EQE values of up to 21%. Such best performance is rarely reported. Both luminogens can also serve as dopants in doped OLEDs with impressive high EQE values of up to 27% and very small roll-offs down to 3.7% at 1000 cd m-2. They can further function as efficient host materials for phosphorescent OLEDs (PhOLEDs). By using BDPAC-XT as the host, the maximum EL efficiencies of 26% and 20% are attained for orange and red PhOLEDs, respectively. Two red and NIR AIEgens (DCMa and DCIs) with simple donor–π–acceptor structures are further prepared for fabricating non-doped solution-processed OLEDs. DCMa and DCIs exhibit a high QY of 13.2% and 7.8% in the thin-film state and good thermal stability in the crystal state. Simple and efficient non-doped OLEDs are fabricated, which emit electroluminescence at 625 and 711 nm, respectively, with a maximum EQE of up to 1.95%. The CIE coordinates are (0.63, 0.36) and (0.64, 0.35), which are close to the primary red color (0.63, 0.34) according to the digital television standard. Two new luminescent molecules called Cz-TAn-DMAC and TPA-TAn-DMAC comprising tert-butyl-modified anthracene, dimethyl acridine and carbazole or triphenylamine groups are successfully synthesized and utilized for fabricating OLEDs. They exhibit efficient deep blue emissions in neat films. The non-doped OLED based on TPA-TAnDMAC provides bright deep-blue light (CIEx,y = 0.14, 0.18) with a high EQE value of 4.9%, while the doped OLED of Cz-TAn-DMAC radiates blue light (CIEx,y = 0.15, 0.08) with a EQE value of 4.8%. In addition, two-color hybrid warm white OLEDs with high-performance are fabricated by using TPA-TAn-DMAC as the blue emitting layer, which show ultra-high stability, efficiency, and color at high luminance over 10000 cd m2, indicative of its promising OLED application prospect. A hierarchical polarizing system of “chiral polymer spherulite + AIEgens” that can realize CPL switching simply by film tilting was developed. The AIEgens are confined between twisted crystallites, which greatly enhance the emission efficiency of the polarizing composites due to the restriction of the intramolecular motions. Based on selective reflection and transmission, the hierarchical structure chirality of the polarizing matrix can achieve handedness switchable CPL within a single material upon the sample tilting. The glum values of the systems follow the trend of the tilt angles and is dependent on the reflection activity. The maximum value can reach 10-2. Full-color CPL generation is easily achieved by incorporating various AIEgens. We also found that the introduction of 4-(phenoxazin-10-yl)benzoyl to conventional chromophores of carbazole-substituted fluorene derivatives can generate robust luminogens with aggregation-induced delayed fluorescence (AIDF) characteristics. The obtained new AIDF materials exhibit high thermal and electrochemical stabilities. Non-doped OLEDs are fabricated, which show EQE values ranging from 19.0% to 3.3%. Much higher EQE values of 21.7-24.4% are achieved in doped OLEDs because of the enhanced fluorescence efficiency and/or improved exciton recombination efficiency. Both non-doped OLEDs and doped OLEDs at high doping concentrations enjoy very small efficiency roll-offs. We also prepared two new compounds called 35DCPP-BP-PXZ and 26DCPP-BP-PXZ by grafting functional groups with AIDF properties to bipolar carrier transport materials. Both compounds enjoy high thermal and electrochemical stabilities and show strong delayed fluorescence and high photoluminescence efficiencies in neat films. In addition, they possess excellent bipolar carrier transport abilities with almost identical hole and electron mobilities in neat films. Efficient non-doped OLEDs using both compounds as light-emitting layers are fabricated, affording high external quantum efficiencies of up to 17.3% and 16.1%. Notably, the device of 35DCPP-BP-PXZ has a tiny efficiency roll-off of 0.6% at 1000 cd m2 and the efficiency roll-off is only 16.2% even at an extremely high luminance of 10000 cd m2, demonstrating the superb efficiency stability. It is noteworthy that the approved equipment budget is intended to replace the worn out of laboratory equipment parts. In the past three years, most of the instruments are operated in normal condition. As a result, the remaining budget has been spent in other categories. The decrease in equipment expenses has no impact on the original research plan or methodology.

16305518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305518.value: Organic luminogenic materials showing strong emission in the solid state are promising candidates for fabricating high-performance OLEDs. Traditional luminophores usually show high quantum yields in solutions but such values are dramatically decreased in the aggregate state. Such a behaviour has limited their full potential for practical applications. In contrast, AIE luminogens (AIEgens) are weakly emissive or non-emissive in dilute solutions but are induced to emit intensively by aggregate formation. Therefore, AIEgens are ideal building blocks for preparing efficient solid-state luminescent materials. Through careful design on the molecular structure, several new blue-and red-emissive AIEgens are generated in this report. Some of these molecules can be facilely synthesized through simple procedures. These molecules are well soluble in common organic solvents and show high thermal and electrochemical stabilities. They can emit strong light in the solid state with high quantum yields. Non-doped and doped solution-processable OLEDs using these molecules as emitters show strong electroluminescence with high EQE values with CIE coordinates close to the values of their primary colours. Because these molecules all emit fluorescence upon photoexcitation, the EQE values of their OLEDs are hardly exceeded the theoretical limit of 5%. To overcome such a limitation, we thus designed and synthesized several rigid, twisted molecules with AIDF characteristics as they can harvest the triple excitons to make fully use of the excitation energy. Indeed, OLEDs fabricated using these molecules as emitters show high EQE values (>20%) and extremely small efficiency roll-offs at high luminance. These AIDF molecules can be further used as materials for constructing high-performance phosphorescent OLEDs and white OLEDs, playing various roles in OLEDs. On the other hand, AIEgens can emit CPL when chiral units are incorporated into their molecular structures. The well-ordered helical architectures of these chiral AIEgens are found to be important to enhance the CPL and dissymmetry factor. While the synthesis of such kind of materials requires chemistry knowledge and organic synthetic skill, achiral AIEgens can also exhibit CPL when they are embedded in the confined chiral nanostructures. Another strategy is to construct a helical molecular conformation through the restriction of intramolecular motion of AIEgens. As you can see in part C of this report, 20 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful results.

16305518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305518.value: Organic luminogenic materials have found potential applications in optics and electronics. Unfortunately, most of the traditional luminophores show weak emission in the solid state due to aggregate formation. Such a behaviour has seriously affected their device performance and applications in the practical useful solid form. In this reporting period, we found that AIEgens are ideal building blocks for the construction of efficient luminogenic materials for various applications as they show no such aggregation-caused emission quenching effect in the solid state. Non-doped or doped OLEDs using AIEgen-based luminogenic materials as emitters show strong electroluminescence with high EQE values and low efficiency drop at high luminance. These materials can be further utilized for making POLEDs and WOLEDs. While the incorporation of AIDF units into AIEgens can greatly enhanced their device efficiency, the introduction of chiral units can make these molecules to show CPL with high dissymmetry factors. Because of the academic importance and application implication, we are still working on the synthesis of new systems although the project completion date has passed. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore the applications of these molecules in optical information storage and processing, optical recognition sensors, etc.

16305518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305518.value: The development of efficient solid-state luminogenic materials for fabricating high-performance OLEDs is academic importance and application implication. Unfortunately, the strong emission of traditional luminophores in solution is weaker when they are fabricated into thin films. Such a behaviour has lowered their OLED performance. In this project, we designed new luminogenic materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics. These molecules can be synthesized through simple procedures. They show high stability to heat and electricity and emit intensely upon photo-irradiation. OLEDs fabricated using these molecules show strong light with high efficiencies. They can be also utilized for making other devices such as white OLEDs. If they possess chiral units, they can emit circularly polarized light as well. Such materials are expected to show an array of applications in optics and electronics.

16305618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305618.value: Developing new techniques for synthesizing polymers with novel structures, broad monomer scope and unique properties is a fundamental goal of polymer science. Multicomponent polymerization (MCP) is an emerging synthesis technique for preparing functional polymers with complicated structures and controlled sequences. It enjoys the advantages of good atom economy, simple procedure and high efficiency. Thanks to the versatility of alkyne chemistry, MCPs based on alkyne monomers have attracted intense interest and developed rapidly in recent years. Although considerable progress has been made in the development of metallic catalysts with high catalytic activity, the intrinsic toxicity of metal species has inevitably limited their application in the synthesis of polymers for biological and photoelectronic applications. Therefore, the development of metal-free and “green” MCPs of alkynes is the next research frontier in polymer chemistry. In recent years, the three-component coupling of an aldehyde, an alkyne and an amine, commonly known as A3 coupling, has been established as a convenient and general approach for the preparation of propargylamines. Some small molecule reactions are reported to have achieved metal-free A3 or even modified four-component coupling by utilizing a strong acid, a strong base or alkynylcarboxylic acid. Those studies demonstrated the advantages of metal-free conditions, high efficiency, excellent yield and a wide monomer scope. We aim to develop in this proposed study metal-free MCPs for the construction of functional polymers. To achieve that goal, new monomers such as diynes, dialkynylcarboxylic acids, diamines and dialdehydes will be designed and synthesized. The polymerization conditions such as reaction time, temperature, solvents and additives will be systematically optimized to achieve polymers with high molecular weights. Different functional substituents will be incorporated into the monomers’ structures to endow the resulting polymers with novel electronic, optical and photonic properties. Their applications in chemosensors, gradient-index optics and polymer light-emitting diodes will be investigated. It is anticipated that this research will develop convenient tools for both synthetic polymer chemists and non-experts seeking to synthesize metal-free functional polymers. That would help sharpen the competitive edge of our local technology industries. 開發新的聚合技術用於制備結構新穎、單體範圍廣泛和性質獨特的高分子材料是高分子科學的基本目標。多組分聚合（MCP）是壹種用於制備結構復雜和序列可控的功能聚合物的新興合成技術。它具有原子經濟性好，工藝簡單，效率高的優點。由於炔烴化學的多樣性，基於炔烴單體的MCP近年來廣受關註且發展迅速。盡管在開發具有高催化活性的金屬催化劑方面已經取得了相當大的進展，但金屬物質的固有毒性不可避免地限制了所得聚合物在生物和光電領域的應用。因此，開發無金屬、“綠色”的炔烴MCP是高分子化學的下壹個研究前沿。 近年來，醛、炔烴和胺的三組分偶聯，通常稱為A3偶聯，已成為壹種制備炔丙胺的便捷和通用的方法。據報道，壹些小分子反應已通過利用強酸、強堿或炔基羧酸實現了無金屬A3及改性的四組分偶聯。這些反應均具有無金屬參與、效率高、產率優異、單體範圍廣泛的優點。 本研究旨在開發出不含金屬的MCP用於構建功能性聚合物。為了實現該目標，我們將設計合成壹系列新型單體，例如二炔、二炔基羧酸、二胺和二醛等。優化聚合反應條件如反應時間、溫度、溶劑和添加劑等將會被系統地優化研究以獲得具有高分子量的聚合物。為了賦予所得聚合物新的電學、光學和光子性質，不同的功能性取代基將被結合到單體結構中。在功能方面，我們將會研究所得聚合物在化學傳感器，梯度折射率光學器件和聚合物發光二極管中的應用。我們預期該研究將為高分子合成化學家和尋求無金屬功能高分子合成的非業內專家提供便捷的制備工具。這將有助於突顯我們當地科技產業在相關領域的競爭優勢。

16305618.label: Realisation of objectives
16305618.value: The objective of the present project is to develop metal-free multi-component polymerization (MCP) routes for the preparation of functional polymers and exploration of their potential applications. We believed through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goal, we developed a facile and efficient multicomponent tandem polymerization (MCTP) to transform commercially available dimethylacetylenedicarboxylate and diamines into functional poly(aminomaleimide)s (PAMIs) under mild reaction conditions. Through amino-yne click reaction and ring-closing reaction, polymers with AMI segments are generated in situ along the backbones. Through systematic optimization of the reaction conditions, soluble and thermally stable PAMIs with satisfactory molecular weights and well-defined structures are obtained in excellent yields. The obtained PAMIs can be used as macromonomers for further polymerization to give macromolecules with extended chains or to produce block copolymers. The resulting PAMIs exhibit non-traditional intrinsic luminescence) and emit intensely in both dilute solution and aggregate state. The PAMIs exhibit low cytotoxicity and can be used as fluorescent bioprobes for bioimaging. We further developed a straightforward C–H-activated polyspiroannulation to transform the readily available and inexpensive 2-naphthols and diynes into photoresponsive spiropolymers with complex structures and multifunctionalities. The present polyspiroannulation can be further applied for the preparation and post-functionalization of spirocyclic telechelic polymers to further expand the libraries of functional spiro-polymers. The obtained polymers show high thermal and morphological stability and interesting photoresponsive properties. Well-resolved fluorescent images with both turn-off and turn-on mode can be readily fabricated from the polymer films under strong UV irradiation. The change of the refractive index of the polymer films to photo-irradiation can be utilized to permanently modify the resonance wavelengths of microring resonators. The performance could be further enhanced by using polymer materials with a larger refractive index change in response to UV irradiation or using polymer substrates to extend the application to flexible photonics. A facile and efficient metal-free polymerization method for the autonomous visualization of mechanical damage in polymeric materials was developed. The 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (DABCO)-catalyzed polymerizations of colorless activated alkynes proceeds quickly at 0 °C or at room temperature in air, producing a series of colored polymers. Based on the microcapsulation technique, this polymerization system was successfully applied for the autonomous damage visualization of polymers. Stable microcapsules containing the solution of reactive triyne monomer are prepared. These colorless microcapsules show immediate color change upon rupture in the presence of DABCO catalyst due to the polymer formation. By dispersing the alkyne-containing microcapsules and DABCO catalyst in poly(vinyl acetate) films, the external scratch and internal damage regions of the composite films can be readily visualized once the reaction is initiated from the ruptured microcapsules. Meanwhile, the cracks in the scratched PVA films are filled by the newly formed polymeric materials due to the damage-triggered polymerization. Therefore, this work provides a promising built-in indicating system for the design of autonomous self-reporting polymer coatings with potential self-protection function. A facile and efficient polyannulation reaction of dual-activated alkyne and pyridines was developed to construct novel N-heterocyclic poly(quinolizine)s. This polymerization can proceed smoothly under catalyst-free conditions with 100% atom economy to furnish poly(quinolizine)s with high molecular weights and well-defined structures in acceptable yields. The resulting polymers show good solubility, high thermal stability, and strong red emission. Moreover, they exhibit low cytotoxicity and can selectively label lysosomes in live cells. Metal-free multicomponent polymerizations of readily accessible diynes, diamines, and glyoxylates are successfully developed for in situ generation of poly(quinoline)s with high molecular weights in nearly quantitative yields. By tuning the electron distributions of the polymer backbones, the resulting poly(quinoline)s show various aggregation-induced behaviours and photoresponsive abilities. The good film-forming ability and divergent photosensitivity of the poly(quinoline)s enable their thin films to fabricate high-resolution 2D fluorescent photopatterns. Some of the poly(quinoline)s can serve as fluorescent indicators for the visualization of phase separation of polymer blends and differentiate the crystallites and amorphous parts of polymer spherulites. The nanoparticles of the tetraphenylethene-containing poly(quinoline)s show sensitive and selective fluorescence sensing properties to highly toxic Cr(VI), which enables the development of a flexible and straightforward technique for the differentiation of Cr(VI) and Cr(III) in a simple biological algae system. We also developed an efficient multicomponent polymerization for in situ generation of functional heteroaromatic hyperbranched polyelectrolytes using readily accessible internal diynes and low-cost, commercially available arylnitriles, NaSbF6, and H2O/AcOH in a one-pot manner. The polymerization can proceed efficiently with a broad spectrum of monomers to afford functional polymers in excellent yields and extraordinary high molecular weights. All the polymers show high solubility in common organic solvents and efficient emission in the solid state, which enable them to fabricate highly ordered fluorescence photo-patterns at different scales. Upon white-light irradiation, these polymers can generate reactive oxygen species to kill bacteria. The possibility of the hyperbranched polyelectrolytes for the creation of customizable living bacterial patterns via photodynamic therapy was demonstrated for the first time. We developed a catalyst-free spontaneous polymerization for the facile synthesis of photoresponsive polysulfonates in 100% atom economy. The polymerization proceeds efficiently at room temperature in air within a short reaction time, generating polysulfonates in excellent yields and high molecular weights with a wide monomer scope and excellent solubility. The obtained polymers can further undergo various efficient post-functionalization to give polymers with new structures and functionalities. They show extraordinarily high and tunable refractive indices and can undergo photodegradation with remarkable fluorescence change and photoacid generation. Such a property allows the fabrication of 3D or dual-emissive photopatterns with only a single optical material. Because of the light-induced acid generation, the polysulfonates can realize the UV-triggered, irreversible, and broad-spectrum bacteria killing and show hypotoxicity in high dosage under natural light. Some of the polymers was demonstrated to be a highly efficient bactericide as an antibacterial layer or spray in two practical models. It is noteworthy that the approved equipment budget is intended to replace the worn out of laboratory equipment parts. In the past three years, most of the instruments are operated in normal condition. Thus, the remaining budget has been spent in other categories. On the other hand, some monomers that we propose to synthesize in this project will be prepared via chemical reactions. Additionally, we have purchased biological reagents to explore the biological applications of the synthesized polymers and most of them are expensive. As a result, more funding has been spent on general expenses. The decrease in equipment expenses and the increase in general expenses have no impact on the original research plan or methodology.

16305618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305618.value: The development of new methodologies for the synthesis of polymers with novel structures and unique properties is a fundamental important research area in polymer science. Multicomponent polymerization (MCP) is an emerging technique for preparing functional polymers with complicated structures and controlled sequences. Thanks to the versatility of alkyne chemistry, many MCPs based on alkyne monomers have been developed. However, most of them involve the use of toxic metallic catalysts, which has inevitably limited the applications of the prepared polymers in the biological and photoelectronic fields. Therefore, the development of metal-free and “green” MCPs of alkynes is the next research frontier in polymer chemistry. In this project, we successfully developed several atom-economical MCPs for the preparation of polymers with well-defined structures and multifunctionalities from some commercially available monomers under metal-free and mild reaction conditions. Novel functional units can be generated in situ in the polymer backbone, which are hard to be accessed by conventional polymerization methods. Through the optimization of the reaction conditions, all the polymerization methods developed give polymers with high molecular weighs in high yields. The obtained polymers are soluble in common organic solvents, showing high and morphological stability. Some polymers can undergo further post-polymerization to generate new polymers with enhanced and new functionalities. Non-traditional intrinsic luminescence was observed in some polymers and some exhibit aggregation-induced emission characteristics with strong fluorescence in the aggregate state. They also show higher refractive indices than commercially used polymers and high photosensitivity, which enable them to generate well-resolved fluorescent patterns through the photolithography technique. Some polymers can serve as fluorescent sensors for bioimaging and metal ion detection, agents to kill bacteria, indicators to study the phase separation of polymer blends and visualize the mechanical damage in polymeric materials, etc. Thus, the results obtained in this project offer great opportunities for preparing functional polymers for applications in diverse areas. As you can see in part C of this report, 17 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful results.

16305618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305618.value: Multicomponent polymerization (MCP) is an emerging synthesis technique for preparing functional polymers with complicated structures and controlled sequences and enjoys the advantages of good atom economy, simple procedure, and high efficiency. Thus, exploration of new MCPs, especially those that can be carried out in the absence of metallic catalyst, is academic importance and application implication. In this project, we developed several MCPs based on alkynes with high atom economy that can be carried out under metal-free and mild reaction conditions. Polymers are obtained in high yields with high molecular weights. The obtained polymers are soluble and are thermally and morphologically stable. They show novel properties such as aggregation-induced emission, high refractive index, high photosensitivity, etc., which enable them to find potential applications such as fluorescent bioprobes, chemosensors, photoresists, photosensitizers, indicators to study the phase separation of polymer blends and visualize the mechanical damage in polymeric materials, etc. Because of these promising results, we are still working on the exploration of new MCPs although the project completion date has passed. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to further explore the applications of these molecules in disease theranostics, biochips, biopattern fabrication, chemosensors, optoelectronics, etc.

16305618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305618.value: Polymers with special structures and properties are promising for an array of high-technological applications. In this project, we developed several multicomponent polymerization routes that can generate polymers from commercially available monomers under mild reaction conditions in the absence of metallic catalysts. All the polymers are obtained in high yields with high molecular weights. They are soluble and degrade at high temperatures. They can emit strong light emission in the solid state, showing high refractive index and high sensitivity to light emission. Such properties are hard to be found in commodity polymers and enable these polymers to find potential advanced applications such as photopattern fabrication, fluorescent bioprobes and chemosensors, antibacterial agents, etc.

16306218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306218.value: As humans have two copies of each gene, multiple mutations in different loci may or may not be found on the same strand of DNA (i.e., inherited from one parent). When a person is heterozygous at more than one position, the placement or the “phase” of these mutations (cis for the same strand and trans for different strands) can result in the expression of different amounts and types of proteins. Clinically, the phase of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) is associated with varying disease risk, severity of disease phenotype, and drug response. Despite the importance of SNP phasing, this information is often missed out in routine DNA sequencing technologies because the DNA is randomly fragmented prior to sequencing. At present, if phasing were to be deemed necessary, both parents would have to be sequenced in addition to the patient. The alternative is additional long-range sequencing tools or other laborious and expensive procedures. In this proposal, we present a strategy based on nucleic acid self-assembly processes to resolve the phase information of multiple SNP (Single Nucleotide Polymorphism) sites. By leveraging the specificity of Watson-Crick hybridization, we are able to design probes that can detect mutations up to single-base specificity. Although several studies have reported the simultaneous detection of multiple mutations, there are very limited studies using this technology for determining SNP phase. This is because most biosensors rely on a binary signal (i.e., on or off) for each SNP, leading to only four possible outcomes when interrogating two sites. Conventional hybridization assays are therefore able to differentiate a target DNA containing the first SNP, second SNP, none of the SNPs, or both of the SNPs from each other, but not detect targets that contain both SNPs in cis and trans orientations. The proposed project will develop a two-step oligonucleotide probe-based hybridization assay, where the first step is a toehold-mediated strand displacement reaction to interrogate the presence of the two SNPs; this then undergoes a second reaction dependent on the first, to differentiate cis and trans SNPs. The additional step will be either due to a conditional extension by a DNA polymerase or through a conditional separation by magnetic beads. The mechanism will also be used in conjunction with a universal probe-based platform for which a versatile design could phase different pairs of SNPs simultaneously. 人类每个基因有两个拷贝，因此不同基因上的多个突变位点可能或可能不会位于同一条DNA 链（即，从一个亲本遗传）。当基因组在一个以上的碱基位置是杂合时，这些突变的位点或“相位” （顺式为同一链，反式为不同链）可导致表达出不同类型和产量的蛋白质。临床上，单核苷酸多态性（SNP）的相位与多种疾病风险，疾病表型的严重程度以及相应的药物反应相关。而该信息在常规DNA测序中难以获得，因为在测序之前DNA样品需要首先被片段化。基于当前技术如需获得此相位信息，除了患者之外，父母双方也都必须进行测序。除此之外，也可以利用长片段测序工具或其他复杂且昂贵的分析方法。基于此，我们提出一种简单的基于核酸链自组装的方法用来解析多个SNP位点的相位信息。 利用Watson-Crick杂交的特异性，我们设计出能够检测单碱基突变的探针。尽管一些研究报道了可同时检测多个突变位点的方法，该技术却极少被用来解析SNP位点的相位信息。这是因为大多数方法依赖于每个SNP位点的二进制信号（即，开或关），所以当分析两个位点时，有且仅有四种可能的结果。因此，常规杂交测定能够区分靶向DNA上是否有第一个SNP位点，第二个SNP位点，没有SNP位点或同时两个SNP位点，但却不能区分同时有两个SNP位点时的顺式和反式排列结构。 我们提出的方法基于寡核苷酸探针杂交反应，且分为两个步骤，其中第一步是通过DNA介导链置换反应来定位两个SNP位点; 然后第二步顺延第一步反应结果，可区分顺式和反式SNP位点分布。其中，第二步反应将基于DNA聚合酶的条件延伸或通过磁珠的条件分离。通用探针也将与该方法结合，以实现同时对多个SNP位点对的相位分析。

16306218.label: Realisation of objectives
16306218.value: This research aimed to develop, characterize, and apply nucleic acid assays to phase single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), which haplotype determination has great implications in molecular and clinical diagnosis of diseases such as cancers and alpha thalassemia. This project has contributed to the output of several high-quality journal papers, two awarded patents, one presentation in an international conference, and the training of two PhD students. We completed the four proposed objectives with corresponding modifications, which successfully satisfied the expected outcomes, as it will be outlined below. In Objective 1, we used a method called Conditional Displacement Hybridization Assay (CDHA) to identify the presence and the phase of two SNPs. The system is based on the enzyme-based displacement of toehold-exchange DNA probes labelled with different fluorophores and quenchers upon the correct hybridization of one probe to a specific SNP. The CDHA assay is reliable over short distances between the SNPs pair, but not it is not so over longer distances. Additionally, we hypothesized that the complicated and stable secondary structure of long, single-stranded DNA sequences at room temperature limits the use of the displacing enzyme. Therefore, we developed a strategy for determining the phase information that is not affected by the length of the target and the distance of the SNPs. We used a probe-and-sink strategy that relies on a competitive inhibitor strand in the SNP interrogation step. Importantly, the assay can be performed at elevated temperatures to decrease the steric hindrance during probe hybridization caused by the complex secondary structure of long DNA strands. We successfully phased two SNPs sites separated by 1377 nucleotides in the heat shock 70 kDa protein 1 (HSPA1) gene, exceeding the proposed objective of SNPs separated by 700 nucleotides. Aligned to Objective 2, this strategy leverages the use of an unlabelled “sink” strand that competitively hybridizes to the wild type sequence (not SNP) to suppress false-positive results. Overall, this method addresses the secondary structure issue and utilizes the simplicity and efficiency of the displacement assay abovementioned. As we progressed towards Objective 3 and 4, we developed an enzyme-free probe hybridization method leveraging conditional magnetic separation in lieu of the addition of a displacing enzyme. The assay consisted of two steps: 1) two rationally designed initially quenched toehold exchange probes are added to interrogate the presence of two SNPs. If hybridization occurs, different emission fluorescent signals will be measured, where the intensity of the signal is proportional to the number of SNPs present (0, 1 or 2); 2) to differentiate between diplotypes , one of the probes is biotinylated, thus when captured and removed from the solution by streptavidin-coated magnetic beads, it results in the solution fluorescence change that determines the phase of the SNPs. Through in silico thermodynamic calculations for probe design in this two-step assay, we successfully identified the haplotype information of 10 different pairs of haplotypes (i.e. diplotype). Notably, during the development of Objective 1 and 2, we devised another nucleic acid hybridization-and-displacement circuit to transduce and amplify a fluorescent signal in the presence of targets leveraging a highly processive endonuclease enzyme. This resulted in the creation of two methods to detect small molecules, using allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) as the sensor molecule and the abovementioned signal transduction and amplification circuit. We developed three biosensors that successfully detected the antibiotics tetracycline and erythromycin spiked in local surface water samples at nanomolar concentrations, and the metabolite uric acid spiked in serum and saliva samples at low micromolar concentrations, consistent with the clinically relevant levels. All these strategies are documented in the research output articles #1, 2, 4, 5.

16306218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306218.value: Significant contributions were made through the completion of our research project. We developed enzyme-based and enzyme-free nucleic acid-based circuits to transduce and amplify analyte detection signals that resulted in several molecular methods. First, we established two methods to determine the haplotype phase of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), which has relevant importance in clinical diagnosis and genetic research. We developed an enzyme-free method based on exchange DNA probes and conditional-magnetic separation to successfully determine the phase of 10 different diplotypes when SNPs span over short distances within the DNA. To determine the haplotype information of SNPs located from each other (e.g. greater than 1000 nucleotides), we designed and characterized a “probe-and-sink” strategy to phase SNPs that is not affected by the length of the target and the distance of the SNPs, and demonstrated its potential by using it to phase two SNPs sites separated by 1377 nucleotides in the heat shock 70 kDa protein 1 (HSPA1) gene. During the development of these rationally-designed displacement-based nucleic acid reactions, we also established a novel and patentable signal transduction and amplification mechanism that leverages toehold-mediated strand displacement reactions sustained by a highly processive endonuclease enzyme. We interfaced this circuit with allosteric transcription factors to build small molecule biosensors that we used to detect antibiotics in environmental samples and metabolites in biological fluids. Importantly, this mechanism can be coupled with other sensor biomolecules, such as functional nucleic acids or aptamers.

16306218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306218.value: The methods we developed offer a direct method for phasing of two SNPs already associated to some altered disease risk or severity. Furthermore, they have the potential for multiple SNP diagnostics and phasing by incorporating more probes with different fluorophores. The later allows straightforward applications in clinical diagnosis and genetic research. Additionally, as shown in articles 4 and 5, the strand displacement-based signal amplification platform can lead to the development of biosensors for small molecules and proteins leveraging other sensor molecules such as aptamers.

16306218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306218.value: With the support of this GRF grant, we have developed several diagnostic and detection technologies that have an impact in areas such as clinical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. We developed molecular assays to obtain genetic information beyond what current methods are capable of. Our assays not only interrogate the presence of genetic mutations in the DNA, but also determine their location, which has implications on the differential expression of proteins that are associated to diseases such as cancer and inflammatory diseases. A better understanding of these mutations allows genetic counselling and evidence-based treatment options for such diseases. Additionally, we also established a novel molecular reaction that allows the detection of small molecules, such as antibiotics and metabolites, for multiple applications in human health and environmental monitoring. Importantly, our developed platforms have the potential to expand the repertoire of detection methods to many other clinically relevant genetic, protein and metabolite targets, as well as pollutants of environmental importance.

16306318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306318.value: The interaction of light with subwavelength structures such as holes and slits has drawn increasing interest in recent years because of significant applications in biological and chemical sensing and near field spectroscopy. The study of this interaction has boomed since the experiment on extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) carried out about two decades ago ( Ebbesen et. al, Extraodinary optical transmission through sub-wavelength hole arrays, Nature, Vol 391, 1998). By exploring the optical properties of a variety of two-dimensional arrays of subwavelength cylindrical holes in a metallic film, it was observed that highly unusual transmission of light occurs at certain frequencies. The authors argued that the EOT is due to the coupling of light with plasmon which is the electronic excitation on the surface of metals. The original EOT experiment has motivated much research on the transmission of light through metallic slabs with various subwavelength structures. In addition to EOT, local field enhancement (LFE), which often occurs near the boundary of the subwavelength structures, and which also has many exciting applications in sensing and the design of novel optical devices, was also investigated. New physical mechanisms, such as cavity-induced surface modes and spoof surface plasmon, were discovered and proposed to explain the observed phenomenon of EOT or LFE. However, due to the complexity and the multiscale nature of the underlying metallic structures, each mechanism can contribute constructively or destructively to these phenomenon, or even not at all. Even today, there is still debate on which mechanism is dominant. This proposed project is devoted to resolving the debates concerning the mechanism of EOT and LFE via rigorous mathematical modeling and analysis. The principal investigator will analyze the light scattering problem by subwavelength slit structures in a metallic slab. Two cases, a single slit and a periodic array of slits, will be investigated. The key will be to characterize the resonance modes or surface modes for the underlying structures by taking advantage of the simplicity of the geometry in appropriate asymptotic regimes. To this end, the principal investigator will formulate the scattering problem by boundary integral equations, and then apply layer potential techniques, asymptotic analysis and Gohberg-Sigal theory for operator-valued analytical functions. Under such a framework, the resonance modes or surface modes are equivalent to the characteristic functions of the associated boundary-integral-operator-valued analytical functions. 近年來，由於其在生物和化學傳感以及近場光譜儀中的重要應用，光與諸如孔和狹縫之類的亞波長結構的相互作用引起了越來越多的關注。該研究的蓬勃發展起源於二十年前物理學家 Ebbesen 等人發表在自然雜誌上的的一個光學超透射實驗。在實驗中通過探索金屬膜中的各種二維次波長圓柱孔陣列的光學特性，Ebbesen 等人觀察到在某些頻率下有非常不尋常的光透射現象發生。為了解釋這種現象，他們提出這是由於光與等離子體的耦合，而等離子體是金屬表面上的電子激發產生的。 這個光透射實驗推動了許多後續的光透射研究。這些研究考察了具有各種亞波長結構的金屬膜。除了超透射，物理學家們還發現了局部場增強的效應。這種效應經常發生在亞波長結構的邊界附近，並且在新型光學器件的感測和設計中也具有許多令人興奮的應用。他們同時還發現了新的物理機制，如空腔誘導表面波模式和偽表面等離子體波模式，也可以解釋觀察到的超透射和局部場增強的現象。然而，由於金屬結構的複雜性和多尺度性質，每種機制的作用可以是建設性或破壞性，或者不起作用。截至今天，哪種機制占主導地位仍有爭議。 該提案致力於通過嚴格的數學建模和分析來解決有關超透射和局部場增強機制的爭論。 主要研究者會圍繞金屬膜中亞波長狹縫結構的光散射問題進行研究。兩種情況會被考慮：單個狹縫和周期狹縫陣列。而研究的關鍵是通過簡化所考察問題的幾何並且採用適當的漸近分析來刻畫該幾何結構的共振模式或表面波模式。為此，主要研究者先把散射問題轉化成邊界積分方程問題，然後應用層勢技術，漸近分析和Gohberg-Sigal理論來分析其中所涉及到的解析算子。在這樣的框架下，共振模式或表面波模式等同於相關的邊界積分算子函數的特徵函數。

16306318.label: Realisation of objectives
16306318.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. We give more detail below. For a single-slit in a perfectly conducting metallic slab, we have derived the asymptotic for the resonances and resonant modes. Moreover, we quantitatively analyzed the EOT and LFE. We further analyzed the case when the metal's dielectric coefficient is modeled by the Drude model where it is not perfectly conducting anymore. For this more complied model, we derived a mathematical theory for the excitation of surface plasmon resonance induced by the slit structure. We further quantitatively analyzed EOT and LFE due to the plasmonic resonance. With these results, we have a complete theory for the resonant scattering by a single-slit structure. For a periodic array of slit structures where each period cell contains one slit, we have proved the existence of surface modes and derived their asymptotic expansion, using the small parameter which is the size of the slit structure. EOT and LFE are also analyzed. We have further investigated the case when a period cell contains two slit structures. Depending on the distance or the interaction between the two slit structures in a period cell, we considered both strong interaction regimes and weak interaction regimes. In both regimes, we have characterized the surface modes and resonant modes. We have paid special attention to the emergence of Fano resonance. With these results, all the interesting phenomena from the resonant scattering by periodic slit structures are well explained. We have also considered the perturbation of resonances of a single slit structure and a periodic array of structures. which has important applications in the field of bio-medical sensing. We are able to characterize the shift in the resonant frequency due to the perturbations. The result is a natural extension of the proposed research objectives.

16306318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306318.value: 1. For the scattering by a slit structure in a thick metallic slab that is modeled by the Drude model, we have characterized the leading-order term of the surface plasmonic waves, and derived sharp estimates for both the plasmonic and nonplasmonic parts of the solution，which shows their explicit dependence of the surface plasmon resonance on the size of the slit, and the real and imaginary parts of the metal-dielectric constant. 2. For the resonant scattering by a perfectly conducting slab with periodically arranged two slits in a period. We have proved that there are two classes of resonances. A sequence of resonances has an imaginary part that is nonzero and is associated with Fabry-Perot resonance. The anther class of resonances contains the so-called embedded eigenvalues. When perturbed, the real embedded eigenvalues will be perturbed as complex-valued resonances, which induce the Fano resonance. We have shown that the field enhancement induced by Fano resonance can be stronger than Fabry-Perot resonance. Moreover, in the case of strongly coupled slits in a period cell, the Fano resonances persist in the whole radiation continuum of the grating structure as long as the slit aperture size is small compared to the incident wavelength. 3. We have derived the formulas for the resonance frequencies and their sensitivity when slit structures (including the case of a single slit and the case of a periodic array of slits) are used in the detection of thin layers. It is shown that the sensitivity of the resonance frequency highly depends on the effect of evanescent wave modes on the tiny slit apertures.

16306318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306318.value: Design slit structures for various applications which are related to their distinguished properties of enhanced transmission of energy and local field enhancement. Efficient optimization can be developed to maximize the functions of these materials. The rigorous results developed in the proposal can be used to provide guidance on the design. The simple structures used can serve as a good initial configuration for the optimization solver.

16306318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306318.value: The completed project has provided a mathematical foundation for resonant scattering by various slit structures. The mechanism of enhanced transmission and local field enhancement in various cases and regimes are all well explained by using rigorous mathematical analysis. Quantitative analysis of these interesting phenomena is derived as well. The results can help us to understand in a better and clear way the complex interactions of waves and structured materials. They also can provide useful guidance on the design of these materials that have applications in various fields such as waveguides and bio-medical sensing.

16306418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306418.value: Living cells exhibit both viscous and elastic characteristics when undergoing deformation and dynamically regulate these mechanical properties together with the cell shape and volume through a variety of cellular activities. A remarkable example is mammalian cells, which become near-spherical in shape and mechanically stiffer (more elastic) during the mitotic phase of cell division. Accurate measurement of the morphology and viscoelastic properties of living cells is essential for understanding the microscopic origin of cell mechanics and its relation to cell responses and functions. Although considerable effort has been devoted to developing various techniques to measure the mechanical properties of living cells, the available technology still faces many challenges and has considerable limitations in accurately determining the absolute value of the elasticity of living cells and imaging its spatial distribution. A major challenge to measuring the mechanical properties of living cells is that the cells are extremely soft and delicate and are surrounded by a liquid medium. Thus, a noninvasive and ultrasensitive method of simultaneous imaging the surface topography and viscoelasticity of living cells is urgently needed to accurately study mitotic cell rounding and other interesting phenomena in cell mechanics. We recently designed a novel technique of long-needle atomic force microscopy (AFM) that overcomes all of these experimental difficulties. In the proposed study, we will systematically investigate the volumetric and viscoelastic properties of mitotic cells and examine their responses to external mechanical cues using this newly developed AFM technique. In the first set of experiments, we will study the variations in the cell volume and viscoelastic properties during the shape transition of the mitotic cells. Accurate measurement of these properties will allow us to understand the interplay between the cell morphology, volume, and mechanical properties. In the second set of experiments, we will measure the topographic and elastic responses of living cells to external mechanical cues. We will study how the change of the mechanical microenvironment from isotropic to polarized affects the shape and elastic distribution of living cells. This will enable us to gain a better understanding of the mechanisms of cell migration and asymmetric cell division. The proposed study will make a fundamental contribution to our general understanding of cell mechanics and active soft matter system. It will also provide a solid foundation for further research on a common class of problems relating to the volumetric and mechanical properties of cellular activities such as cell contraction, spreading, differentiation, and cancerization. 活細胞在經歷形變時同時具有粘性和彈性的特徵，並通過各種細胞活動動態調節這些力學性質以及細胞的形狀和體積。一個顯著的例子是哺乳動物細胞，其在細胞分裂的有絲分裂期期間變成近球形並且在力學上表現得更硬（更有彈性）。準確測量活細胞的形態和粘彈性對於理解細胞力學的微觀起源及其與細胞反應和功能的聯繫至關重要。儘管各方在研發各種活細胞的力學性質的測量技術中已經付出了很大的努力，但是現有的技術仍然面臨許多挑戰，並且在準確測定活細胞彈性的絕對值和空間分佈與成像等方面仍有相當大的局限性。測量活細胞力學性質的主要挑戰源於細胞非常柔軟和脆弱，並被液體介質包圍。因此，我們迫切需要一種非侵害性的和超靈敏的成像方法同時測量活細胞的表面形貌和粘彈性，以準確地研究細胞在有絲分裂期變圓的現象和細胞力學中其他有趣的現象。 最近，我們設計了一種新的長針型原子力顯微鏡（AFM）技術，克服了以上的實驗難題。在擬開展的研究中，我們將系統地研究細胞的體積和粘彈性在有絲分裂期的特性，並使用新開發的原子力顯微鏡技術檢測它們對外部力學信號的反應。在第一組實驗中，我們將研究有絲分裂期細胞形狀轉變過程中細胞體積和粘彈性的變化。精確測量這些特性將使我們能夠理解細胞形態，體積和力學特性之間的相互作用。在第二組實驗中，我們將測量活細胞的形貌和彈性對外部力學信號的響應。我們將研究力學微環境從各向同性到極性的變化是如何影響活細胞形狀和彈性分佈。這將使我們更好地了解細胞遷移和細胞非對稱分裂的力學機制。 擬開展的研究將為我們對細胞力學和活性軟物質系統的一般性理解做出重要的貢獻。它還將為進一步研究與細胞體積和力學性質相關的一大類細胞活動問題提供堅實的基礎，例如細胞收縮，擴展，分化和癌變。

16306418.label: Realisation of objectives
16306418.value: To fulfill the two research objectives, we carried out two sets of experiments to study the viscoelastic properties of living cells and their responses to external mechanical cues. In one set of experiments, we carried out a comprehensive study of the multiscale mechanics and viscoelastic properties of living cells. Mechanical stresses and response of living cells to the resulting deformations play important roles in cell contraction, spreading, crawling, wound healing, invasion, and division. While considerable efforts have been made to measure the viscoelastic property of living cells, the available technology still faces many challenges and has considerable limitations in accurately determining the absolute value of the Young's modulus E of living cells and imaging its spatial distribution. To solve this problem, we performed force-relaxation measurements using a newly developed atomic-force-microscope (AFM) probe. In the experiment, a live cell was subjected to a fast deformation applied by a glass sphere, which is glued onto an AFM cantilever. At the same time, the AFM recorded the force generated by the cell deformation. After the initial fast indentation, the height of the AFM cantilever was held constant and the AFM recorded how the force F(t) relaxes with time t. The measured stress relaxation of living cells reveals a time-dependent compressive modulus E(t). To further quantify the time-dependent modulus of living cells, we systematically measured the force-indentation curve on living cells at different indentation speeds v. The force-indentation measurement was performed at a constant v by moving the colloidal probe vertically up and down on the top of cell. The obtained force-distance curves featured a speed-dependent approaching curve and a retraction curve with a hysteresis, indicating the viscoelastic nature of the cell. Furthermore, a modified Hertz model with a time-dependent modulus E(t) was developed to quantitatively describe the force-distance curves of different types of living cells. Our results establish a unified description of the compressive modulus E(t) of living cells, which is applicable to 10 different cell types studied, ranging from epithelial, muscle, and neuronal cells to blood and stem cells. The cell modulus E(t) is found to have three relaxation modes with different timescales: an initial exponential decay at short times t followed by a long-time power-law decay together with a persistent modulus. The exponential decay at short times indicates a diffusive relaxation of confined proteins in cytoskeleton. The power-law decay at long times reveals slow relaxation of deformed cytoskeletal network. Finally, the time-independent persistent modulus results from active stress of living cells. This work thus provided a unified description of multiscale mechanics and active stress of living cells. We have finished all the measurements and are in the final stage to analyze the data and prepare a manuscript for publication. This work was published in Physical Review Research (2021). Recent studies have shown that the cellular microenvironment with mechanical variations can influence the mechanical state of living cells. To find how the mechanical properties of the substrate, on which the cell is cultured, affect the cellular mechanics, we conducted the second set of experiments to study the mechanical interaction of a thin polymer film with a liquid droplet, which has a circular contact line with the polymer substrate. Specifically, we conducted a systematic study of the pinning-depinning dynamics of a contact line between a liquid interface and an aging polymer substrate. State- (or time-) and rate- (or speed-) dependent pinning-depinning is often observed in out-of-equilibrium disordered systems as a yield response to an external forcing. However, the microscopic mechanism responsible for this time- and speed-dependent increase of pinning strength, or contact ageing, is not well understood, because of its complexity and the lack of direct measurement of the pinning-depinning events. In the experiment, we conducted systematic measurements of the contact line pinning-depinning dynamics in a well-characterized model system, namely, the moving contact line between a liquid interface and a micro-sized glass fiber. We used a recently developed ``long-needle" AFM to directly measure the capillary force acting on a circular contact line formed on the long needle (made of a thin glass fiber), which is coated with a thin layer of temperature-sensitive polymer film (Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide, or PNIPAM for short) and intersects a water-air interface. The measured capillary force hysteresis shows a distinct overshoot for the depinning of a static contact line, and the overshoot amplitude grows logarithmically with both the hold time t and fiber speed v. A unified model based on the slow growth of a wetting ridge and force-assisted barrier crossing is developed to explain the observed time- and speed-dependent contact line depinning over an aging polymer surface. The experiment thus demonstrated that the aging effect of the wetting ridge causes the depinning force to exhibit a logarithmic growth in time for a static contact line and speed weakening for a moving contact line. We expect that these features are also applicable to other soft viscoelastic substrates, as the formation of a wetting ridge introduces an extra viscoelastic dissipation for all soft materials. This work was published in Physical Review Letters (2020). With the above two sets of experiments, the two project objectives were fully achieved.

16306418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306418.value: 1. Unified description of compressive modulus revealing multiscale mechanics of living cells. How to accurately characterize the modulus of living cells at the whole-cell level with a well-defined measurement geometry and precise mathematical modeling of viscoelastic relaxation is an ongoing challenge in biophysics and mechanobiology. In this project, we conducted combined atomic-force-microscopy (AFM) measurements of stress relaxation and indentation force for 10 cell types ranging from epithelial, muscle, and neuronal cells to blood and stem cells, from which we obtain a unified quantitative description of the compressive modulus E(t) of individual living cells. The cell modulus E(t) is found to have an initial exponential decay at short times t followed by a long-time power-law decay together with a persistent modulus. The three components of E(t) at different timescales thus provide a digital spectrum of mechanical readouts that are closely linked to the hierarchical structure and active stress of living cells. This work provides a reliable experimental framework that can be utilized to characterize the mechanical state of living cells and investigate their physiological functions and diseased states. This work was published in Physical Review Research (2021). 2. State and rate dependent contact line dynamics over an aging soft surface. Dynamics of a moving contact line between a fluid interface and a solid surface is an outstanding problem in interfacial dynamics and has been with us for many years. The main issue for moving contact lines is that their motion is strongly influenced by the physical roughness and/or chemical heterogeneities on the solid surface. In this project, we conducted direct atomic-force-microscope measurements of capillary force hysteresis of a circular contact line formed on a long glass fiber, which is coated with a thin layer of soft polymer film and intersects a water-air interface. The measured capillary force hysteresis shows a distinct overshoot for the depinning of a static contact line, and the overshoot amplitude grows logarithmically with both the hold time t and fiber speed V. A unified model based on the slow growth of a wetting ridge and force-assisted barrier crossing is developed to explain the observed time (or state) and speed (or rate) dependent contact line depinning dynamics over an aging soft surface. The experimental findings have important implications to a common class of problems involving depinning dynamics in a defect or roughness landscape, such as friction of solid interfaces. This work was published in Physical Review Letters (2020).

16306418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306418.value: Our quantitative description of multiscale cell mechanics provides a reliable experimental framework that can be utilized to analyze the viscoelastic properties of healthy and diseased cells extracted from the same type of tissue and investigate in what ways a specific disease affects cell’s physical properties. In particular, the three components of the cell modulus give a quantitative readout of the mechanical state of living cells, which may have broad applications in characterizing certain aspects of the physiology of living cells in relation to their healthy and diseased states. Unlike previous studies which only provide a single value of modulus, our combined stress relaxation and indentation force measurements provide a set of six parameters to characterize the moduli of two passive components and one active component. These six parameters can be used as effective indexes for “mechanical profiling” of living cells. For example, with a proper calibration, the six parameters can be used to characterize the structural singularity of cancer cells that is responsible for their unique mechanical properties. Our study of single cell mechanics thus paves the way forward for future studies of cancer cell mechanics. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research along this direction.

16306418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306418.value: Living cells are squishy and exhibit both fluid-like and solid-like behaviors across different spatial and temporal scales. The multiscale mechanics of such soft glassy materials have recently attracted much attention, given their important biological implications and immense practical applications in cell division, organ formation, wound healing and cancer metastasis. Despite the large number of experimental and theoretical investigations made in recent years, a comprehensive integrated model of cell mechanics has not yet been established. For example, the Young’s modulus of living cells measured by using different techniques can vary by three orders of magnitude. In this project, we developed a new atomic-force-microscopy (AFM) technique with combined AFM measurements of stress relaxation and indentation force for 10 cell types ranging from epithelial, muscle and neuronal cells to blood and stem cells, from which we obtained a unified description of the compressive modulus of living cells. Our results showed that the cell modulus contains three relaxation modes at different time scales that are closely linked to the hierarchical structure and active stress of living cells. This work provides a reliable experimental framework that can be utilized to characterize the mechanical state of living cells and investigate their physiological functions and diseased states.
