16306818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306818.value: Compared to conventional metal-nanoparticle catalytic systems, single-atom catalysts (SACs) can enormously increase the atom utilization rate of expensive noble metals and their catalytic efficiency. SACs have attracted considerable attention from the catalysis community in recent years, particularly in the fields of CO oxidation, hydrogenation, electrochemical synthesis and water-gas shift reactions. However, isolated atoms in SACs always tend to lower their surface energy by aggregation or by sintering to form crystallites, which results in degradation of their catalytic performance. To prevent degradation of SACs, various synthetic strategies have been developed, through which dispersed metal atoms are tightly bonded to dedicated supports by strong electronic or covalent interactions to form thermodynamically stable SACs. Stability is a critical issue for the practical implementation of SACs. However, thus far, few reports on high-resolution transmission electron microscopy studies on the stability and the deterioration processes of SACs at an atomic-scale in real-time under practical reaction conditions have been published, mainly because of the difficulties in applying an atmospheric heating environment inside an electron microscope’s high-vacuum column without adversely affecting the single-atom-resolved abilities. In our newly-established aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) facility, we successfully observed the atomic distribution of platinum on unique graphene-nanodiamond hybrid structures, which shows promising thermal stability and regenerable catalytic performance only when the supports are integrated with few-layered graphene-coating. However, the atomic dynamics correlating these heterogeneous structures with their layer-dependent catalytic characteristics remain unknown. In-situ STEM with single-atom-analysis capabilities is recognized to be a powerful and straightforward approach for studying the underlying mechanisms of the stability and the enhanced catalytic performance of SACs. In the proposed project, we will investigate the thermal and chemical stability of SAC materials via in-situ gas-cell STEM experiments and analyze their interfacial behaviors with the help of first-principles calculations. We will concentrate on (1) the atomic-scale STEM characterization of few-layer-structure-supported SACs under analogous realistic conditions to identify their active sites, catalytic cycles and possible reaction mechanisms; (2) the strong metal-support interactions induced by different support modification and metal dispersion methods; and (3) the SACs deactivation and regeneration by designing in-situ thermal and chemical processes. The outcomes of this research will not only deepen our knowledge of strong metal-support interaction effects lying behind SAC systems, but also help us formulate valuable guidelines on designing new SAC material systems with enhanced stability and remarkable efficiency for practical applications. 與傳統金屬納米粒子催化劑相比，單原子催化劑可以最大程度的發揮貴重金屬的使用效率，特別是在一氧化碳的氧化，氫化以及水汽相反應等領域有極大應用。 由於表面能的作用，單原子傾向於形成大晶體顆粒而導致催化失效。為了防止催化失效，目前人們採取了各種方案，比如使用具有較強相互作用的基體穩定單原子。單原子催化的穩定性是一個非常關鍵的問題，目前很少有高分辨電子顯微學的研究發表， 特別是在原子尺度下實時觀察化學反應的動態過程。其主要困難在於原位高溫反應在高分辨電子顯微鏡的真空環境裡很難實現原子分辯成像。目前我們應用最新建立的球差矯正電子顯微鏡實現了對鉑金原子在石墨烯和金剛石載體上的原子分佈觀察，這些原子有很好的穩定性。這些穩定原子結構與這類特殊的基體的關係以及機制還不清楚。原位電子顯微鏡配以強大的分析功能對研究單原子的穩定性顯然有極大優勢。 在本項目中，我們計劃使用原位電子顯微鏡內建反應器研究單原子催化劑的熱穩定性和化學穩定性，同時配以第一性原理計算，針對下列問題開展深入研究：（1） 原子尺度下單原子真實氣體催化反應下的機理問題；（2）樣品分散方法對單原子與基體的強交互作用原理；（3）單原子催化失效和激活的化學過程。預計本項目將對單原子與基體交互作用關係給出深入理解，同時對設計新型高效單原子催化系統給出新的方向。

16306818.label: Realisation of objectives
16306818.value: Our first stage of research focused on the atomic structural characterization of SAC reactions in order to understand the active sites, catalytic circles and reaction mechanisms. We therefore started research on atomic structural characterization of single atom catalysts even before the approval of the proposal in 2018. As planned, we first characterize the atomically dispersed Pd on nanodiamond and graphene for selective hydrogenation acetylene. This is a collaborative research together with our partner, Prof. H.Y. Liu as listed in the proposal. Our findings in this research is that the catalyst we prepared exhibits remarkable performance for the selective conversion of acetylene to ethylene, high conversion (100%), high ethylene selectivity (90%), and good stability. The unique structure of the catalyst blocks the formation of unselective subsurface hydrogen species and ensures the facile desorption of ethylene against the over hydrogenation to undesired ethane, which is the key for the outstanding selectivity of the catalyst. Due to the Covid-19 outbreak, our joint research with Prof. H.Y. Liu in mainland China became difficult. The main difficulty is that the samples treated by Prof. H.Y. Liu in mainland China cannot be quickly sent to Hong Kong. We have to put more manpower to do some sample treatments and preparation work in Hong Kong. This is the main reason that there is relatively large expense for research staff which vary significantly from the approved budget. On the other hand, it was not possible to attend international conferences during that period. We therefore transfer the conference budget to the staff cost. We also rearranged our research and focused our study on tin-Assisted fully exposed platinum clusters which are stabilized on defect-rich graphene for dehydrogenation reaction. Our super-resolution transmission electron microscopy images uncovered a number of interesting catalytic structures. We observed that atomically dispersed Pt clusters, with an average Pt atom number of 3, were anchored over the carbon support by the assistance of Sn atoms as a partition agent and through the Pt–C bond between Pt clusters and defect-rich graphene nano-shell. The atomically dispersed Pt clusters guaranteed a full metal availability to the reactants, a high thermal stability, and an optimized adsorption/desorption behavior. This research was published in ACS Catal. 2019, 9, 5998. In the study of atomically dispersed copper (Cu) catalyst supported on a defective nano-diamond-graphene, we used transmission electron microscopy to verified that this special catalysts exhibit excellent catalytic performance for the selective conversion of acetylene to ethylene, i.e., with high conversion (95%), high selectivity (98%), and good stability. The unique structural feature of the Cu atoms anchored over graphene through Cu-C bonds ensures the effective activation of acetylene and easy desorption of ethylene, which is the key for the outstanding activity and selectivity of the catalyst. This work has been published in Nat Comm. 2019; 10: 4431. We therefore have achieved the objectives for atomic structure and active site characterization of three types of catalysts. Our second stage research focused on direct observation of formation and stabilization of unsaturated metal atoms and activation and deactivation through in-situ electron microscopy technique. We first revealed the atomic-scale observation of the thermal stability and surface reconstruction of palladium nanoparticles supported on carbon-coated zinc oxide nanowires (PdNPs/C&ZnO-NWs). Our in-situ high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) studies discovered the high-temperature resistance to PdNPs aggregations with aids of carbon-coated low-dimensional nanostructures C&ZnO-NWs. We elucidated the interesting findings by ripening dynamics of PdNPs and the surface reconstruction of C&ZnO-NWs. The subsequent atomic-scale observation revealed the surface reconstruction of ZnO-NWs in the form of ZnO encapsulation over PdNPs and carbon-coated layers during the thermal process, which showed the microscopic evidence of potential deactivation of ZnONW-based nanocatalysts in thermal reactions. This important research results was published in Materials & Design 209 (2021) 109947. In addition, the high temperature stability and the active/inactive sites of platinum nanocatalysts deposited on graphene oxide was studied by in-situ TEM techniques. The statistical data of in-situ time-lapsed TEM images demonstrate the size variations of the sintering Pt nanoparticles which are in accordance with the Ostwald ripening process. We further discover the tendency towards the preferential exposure of high-index Pt nanocrystal facets (higher surface energy sides) for the PtNPs/GO under thermal treatment from 25 ◦C to 400 ◦C, which leads to accelerate the nanoparticle aggregations, providing microscopic evidence of the catalyst instability at high temperatures. This work was published in Materials Characterization 170 (2020) 110706. Through the studies for the thermal stability, ripening dynamics and coalescing microstructures of reduced graphene oxide-based (rGO) platinum nanocatalysts by real-time in-situ TEM techniques, we found that platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) exhibited superior thermal stability on the rGO flat surface than on the wrinkle one, indicating that improving the surface flatness of graphene-based supports can increase the thermal stability of deposited metal nanocatalysts. The time resolved analysis demonstrated that the thermal-induced microstructural transformation (graphitization) of the rGO support caused the discrepancy of PtNPs coarsening from the Ostwald ripening model. The in-situ high-resolution images further revealed the coalescing microstructures of PtNPs on the graphitized rGO, which validated the previous simulation research by real-time experimental observations. Our in-situ TEM research has demonstrated experimental evidences for revealing and elucidating the physiochemical natures, in particular the strong metal-to-support interactions of the nanocatalysts. These results have been published in Diamond & Related Materials 120 (2021) 108690. Through collaborative research with our mainland partner (Prof. H.Y. Liu) we have studied the catalytic active sites by electron microscopy and found that they are pivotal in the design of highly effective heterogeneous metal catalysts, especially for structure-sensitive reactions. Downsizing the dimension of the metal species on the catalyst increases the dispersion, which is maximized when the metal exists as single atoms, namely, single-atom catalysts (SACs). SACs have been reported to be efficient for various catalytic reactions. We show here that the Pt SACs, although with the highest metal atom utilization efficiency, are totally inactive in the cyclohexane (C6H12) dehydrogenation reaction, an important reaction that could enable efficient hydrogen transportation. Instead, catalysts enriched with fully exposed few-atom Pt ensembles, with a Pt–Pt coordination number of around 2, achieve the optimal catalytic performance. Our first-principles calculations have supported the experimental findings. The superior performance of a fully exposed few-atom ensemble catalyst is attributed to its high d-band center, multiple neighboring metal sites, and weak binding of the product. This work was published in J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 8, 3535–3542. The Co-I, Prof. Ding Pan and his group members have also performed first-principles calculations for different 2D semiconductor layered materials as the supports for different metal structures. Their main results are very useful for understanding the work function matching between metals and 2D semiconductors and also useful for building up metal-2D semiconductor electrical contacts for application of 2D nanodevices. One paper about atomic-scale study of nanostructured interfaces will be prepared for submission in 2023. By the end of 2022, we have achieved all objectives for this project.

16306918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306918.value: 在这里我们主要研究在零曲率的共形流形上的等周问题。古典的等周问题指的是在欧几里得平面上所有周长一定的封闭曲线中，是否有一个围成的面积最大？如果有的话，是什么形状？我们知道确实是有这么一个曲线围成的区域面积最大，而且这个区域一定是一个圆。尽管这个等周问题在一般曲面上不一定有答案，但是在极小曲面上，我们依然有等周不等式。Hang-Wang-Yan研究了在零曲率共形流形上的一个规范化的等周比。他们证明了如果这个等周比在零曲率共形类上的上确界严格小于标准球的等周比，那么这个上确界一定能被一个共形度量所达到。他们猜想如果这个共形流形不是标准球的话，那么这个等周比在零曲率共形类上的上确界一定严格小于标准球的等周比。在高维情况下和一些额外的曲率条件下，我们证明了这个猜想。在此，我们想要继续研究低维情况下的这个猜想，以及一些相关的加权等周比问题。

16306918.label: Realisation of objectives
16306918.value: The classic isoperimetric inequality in a plane is a sharp inequality that relates the length of a closed curve and the area of the planar region that it encloses. Carleman proved that the same inequality still holds on a minimal surface by using a sharp inequality for harmonic functions on the two dimensional unit Euclidean ball. Hang-Wang-Yan obtained a generalization of this inequality on higher dimensional Euclidean balls and on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundaries, respectively. On the Riemannian manifold (M,g), they considered the normalized ratio of the volume of M and the area of its boundary under a metric that is conformal to g and has zero scalar curvature. They investigated the supremum of this ratio over all such metrics and conjectured that the supremum is always achieved. In an earlier work of the PI, we proved this conjecture in higher dimensions under some additional curvature assumptions. The PI proposed here to continue this study in low dimensions and for a weighted isoperimetric ratio, and obtained two results which directly addressed the objectives. In research output 1, we successful proved the conjecture in low dimensions using the proposed method in the research plan. More precisely, we prove that the supremum of the isoperimetric ratio over scalar-flat conformal classes is achieved if either (i) the dimension is larger than 8 and the boundary of the manifold has a nonumbilic point, or (ii) the dimension is larger than 6, the boundary of the manifold is umbilic, and the Weyl tensor does not vanish on the boundary. The method we used is to find subsolutions of some specific equations in the half space. The PI also proposed to add corrections to the test functions of the cut-off rescaled bubbles. Surprisingly, we discovered that these two ways are essentially equivalent. It is not trivial at all to find useful subsolutions, since whenever one has a candidate, one has to go over the whole delicate calculations for verification. Moreover, we also found that the dimension assumption in (ii), that is larger than 6, is the best one can do under the current framework. In research output 2, we studied the existence of solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equation of a weighted generalized isoperimetric ratio on the unit ball. The equation is a conformally invariant nonlinear integral equation involving Poisson-type kernels. It has a stronger nonlocal featurr, is not the dual of any PDE, and is a critical equation in the sense of embeddings. We considered antipodal positive weight functions, and proved the existence of regular solutions if the weight function does not oscillate too much. The proof of our results uses blow up analysis for this nonlinear integral equation. In this investigate, we discovered a notable difference between this variational problem on the isoperimetric ratio and the Yamabe problem (or the boundary Yamabe problem), that is, the antipodal symmetric does not give any positive mass in this problem. This was not expected, and it makes the compactness problem much harder to study, even though we have proved the required important ingredients such as Harnack inequality and Pohozaev identity.

16306918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306918.value: First, we considered the isoperimetric ratio over the scalar-flat conformal class on a given smooth Riemannian manifold (M,g) with smooth boundary. We proved that the supremum of the isoperimetric ratio over scalar-flat conformal classes is achieved if either (i) the dimension is larger than 8 and the boundary of the manifold has a nonumbilic point, or (ii) the dimension is larger than 6, the boundary of the manifold is umbilic, and the Weyl tensor does not vanish on the boundary. We found examples showing that the dimension in (ii) is the best one can do using the method proposed in the research plan. Second, we considered a weighted generalized isoperimetric ratio over the Euclidean unit ball, which covers the classic isoperimetric ratio as a special case, and studied its Euler-Lagrange equation. This equation is a conformally invariant nonlinear integral equation involving Poisson-type kernels. Therefore, the equation may not have solutions due to Kazdan-Warner type conditions. We considered antipodal positive weight functions, and proved the existence of regular solutions if the weight function does not oscillate too much. We also found that the antipodal symmetry does not give the positive mass, which is unexpected and is different from the Yamabe problem. The method we use is blow up analysis for nonlinear integral equation.

16306918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306918.value: One potential future development could be some kind of compactness results for the Euler-Lagrange equation of the weighted isoperimetric ratio over the scalar-flat conformal class on the unit ball of low dimensions. Low dimension is a desirable starting point, considering the extra difficult we found during the investigation and the experience that there could be at most one blow up point in low dimensions. Furthermore, we have obtained several important ingredients such as the Harnack inequality for this nonlinear integral equations and the Pohozaev identity. Nonetheless, there are still some missing pieces such as Bocher type theorem or some other kind of positive mass. The PI would like to continue this study with collaborators.

16306918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306918.value: This research project deals with a fundamental mathematical inequality called the isoperimetric inequality, which relates the length of a closed curve and the area of the planar region it encloses. There have been generalizations of this inequality on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundaries (such as surfaces), that is the normalized ratio of the volume of the manifold and the area of its boundary under a metric that is conformal to the original metric and has zero scalar curvature. It has been conjectured that the supremum of this ratio over all such metrics is always achieved. We successfully proved the conjecture in low dimensions using a proposed method in the research plan. In addition, we also considered a weighted generalized isoperimetric ratio and proved the existence of solutions to its Euler-Lagrange equation. These results provide new insights into mathematical inequalities. Furthermore, the techniques and methods developed in this research project, such as the blow-up analysis for nonlinear integral equations, are powerful tools and have broader applications beyond the specific problems studied here.

16307618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307618.value: Water, essential for all known forms of life, exists not only near the Earth's surface but also largely inside the Earth. In the deep water cycle, water travels between the interior and surface for millions to billions of years, and critically influences the structure and dynamics of the entire Earth. In the Earth’s crust and mantle, silicates are the most important minerals. The interactions between aqueous solutions and silicates are of great importance in geoscience. However, because of the extreme pressure and temperature conditions found in the deep Earth, many fundamental properties of water confined by silicates are poorly known. In the proposed project, we will use first-principles molecular dynamics methods to study aqueous solutions nanoconfined by silica. We will focus on how the confinement alters the physical and chemical properties of supercritical aqueous solutions. We will study the structural and electronic properties of supercritical water under confinement: self-ionization and dielectric properties. In particular, we will use a new first-principles method recently developed by us to calculate the molecular polarizability of water under confinement. These properties are essential to the solvation ability of water. A specific aqueous solution, oxidized carbon in water, will be investigated in the confined water, which is an important part of the deep carbon cycle. To make strong connections with experiments, we will compute the Raman and infrared spectra of confined aqueous solutions at high-pressure and high-temperature conditions to search for the experimental fingerprints of confinement and guide experiments. The obtained data from the first-principles methods will be used to revise the current models for water-rock interactions. The atomistic understanding brought about by the proposed project will shed new light on the deep water and carbon cycles inside the Earth, which ultimately influence the sustainable development of human beings. 水乃生命之源，它不仅存在于地球表面，而且大量储藏在地球内部。在地球内部水循环的亿万年过程中，水往返穿梭于地表和内部，深刻地影响了地球的结构和动力学性质。在地壳和地幔中，硅酸盐是最常见的一类矿物。水与硅酸盐的相互作用对地球科学极其重要。但是，因为地球内部的极端高温高压环境，我们对硅酸盐受限情况下的水的性质还知之甚少。 在本项目中，我们将主要采取第一性原理分子动力学的方法去研究二氧化硅纳米受限环境下水溶液的性质。我们将集中研究纳米尺度受限环境如何影响超临界水溶液的物理化学性质：水的电离和介电性质。特别之处在于，我们将应用刚刚由我们发展的第一性原理方法计算受限条件下水的极化率。这些性质对水的溶解能力至关重要。我们将研究在受限条件下含碳的水溶液，它是地球深部碳循环的重要组成部分。为了加强同实验工作的联系，我们将计算受限体系水溶液在高温高压条件下的拉曼和红外光谱，寻找实验可观测到的受限体系效应，从而指导实验。第一性原理计算得到的数据将被用来改进当前的水-矿石作用模型。本项目将从原子尺度上对地球内部的水和碳循环进行理解，对人类可持续发展有重要意义。

16307618.label: Realisation of objectives
16307618.value: 1. Simulate supercritical water nanoconfined by silica. Understand how confinement affects the self-ionization of water. Calculate the molecular dipole moments, and polarizability of water near the interfaces. The physical and chemical properties of water under confinement can help us better understand the water-rock interactions in the deep Earth. We performed extensively long ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the chemical reactions and speciation of aqueous carbon solutions nanoconfined by graphene and stishovite at 10 GPa and 1000 ~ 1400 K. We found that the graphene nanoconfinement promotes the CO2(aq) reactions. When graphene is replaced by stishovite, less CO2(aq) reacts, but still more than in the bulk solutions. We found that contacting the stishovite (100) surface makes the solutions more acidic, which shifts the chemical equilibria, though the stishovite surface also catalyzes the CO2(aq) reactions by adsorbing HCO3- and H+. The enhanced reactivity of CO2(aq) in nanoconfinement has important implications for carbon transport and fluid-rock interactions in deep Earth. Aqueous fluids located at grain boundaries in minerals can either exist in isolated fluid-filled pores, or form a connected network of channels along grains facilitating fluid transport. It is known that adding molecular CO2(aq) to water increases the rock-fluid-rock dihedral angle θ, which inhibits fluid flow. However, our study shows that CO2(aq) reacts with water under nanoconfinement and also reacts with the solid interface, which may decrease θ and promote the interconnectivity of fluids. Our study also sheds light on atomistic mechanisms of CO2 storage through mineral carbonation. CO2 reacts more in nanoconfined water, which benefits CO2 mineralization. If we choose minerals with larger points of zero charge than that of SiO2, such as forsterite and magnesium oxide, the CO2 reactivity may be further enhanced. The paper was published in Nat. Commun. 13, 5932 (2022), and Featured by Editors’ Highlights “Inorganic and physical chemistry”, where I am the only corresponding author. We introduced a neural network dipole model, which combined with molecular dynamics, can be used to compute P–T dependent dielectric properties of water as accurately as first-principles methods but much more efficiently. We found that ϵ0 may vary by one order of magnitude in Earth’s upper mantle, suggesting that the solvation properties of water change dramatically at different depths. Although ϵ0 and the molecular dipole moment increase with an increase in pressure along an isotherm, the dipolar angular correlation has its maximum at 5 GPa–7 GPa, which may indicate that hydrogen bonds become weaker at high pressure. We also calculated the frequency-dependent dielectric constant of water in the microwave range, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not been calculated from first principles, and found that temperature affects the dielectric absorption more than pressure. Our results are of great use in many areas, e.g., modeling water–rock interactions in geochemistry. The computational approach introduced here can be readily applied to other molecular fluids. The frequency-dependent dielectric constant can be directly related to IR spectra. The paper is published in J. Chem. Phys. 153, 101103 (2020), where I am the corresponding author. 2. Compute the Raman and IR spectra of aqueous solutions nanoconfined by silica to make quantitative connections with experiments. Understand how vibrational peaks vary under confinement. Help to interpret experimental data and guide experiments. We presented a strategy, based on first-principles simulations, to determine ratios of Raman scattering cross-sections of aqueous species under extreme conditions, thus providing a key quantity that can be used, in conjunction with Raman measurements, to predict chemical speciation in aqueous fluids. Due to the importance of the Earth’s carbon cycle, we focus on carbonate and bicarbonate ions. We found that the ratio of the Raman scattering cross-sections of carbonate and bicarbonate ions in water decreases with increasing pressure, while it increases with increasing temperature, up to ~10GPa and 1000K. Our results indicate a higher concentration of bicarbonates in water than previously considered at conditions relevant to the Earth’s upper mantle, with important implications for the transport of carbon in aqueous fluids in the Earth’s interior. The paper is published in Nat Commun 11, 421 (2020), where I am the corresponding author.

16307618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307618.value: The reactions of CO2 in water under extreme pressure-temperature conditions are of great importance to the carbon storage and transport below Earth’s surface, which substantially affect the carbon budget in the atmosphere. Previous studies focus on the CO2(aq) solutions in the bulk phase, but underground aqueous solutions are often confined to the nanoscale, and nanoconfinement and solid-liquid interfaces may substantially affect chemical speciation and reaction mechanisms, which are poorly known on the molecular scale. Here, we apply extensive ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study aqueous carbon solutions nanoconfined by graphene and stishovite (SiO2) at 10 GPa and 1000 ~ 1400 K. We find that CO2(aq) reacts more in nanoconfinement than in bulk. The stishovite-water interface makes the solutions more acidic, which shifts the chemical equilibria, and the interface chemistry also significantly affects the reaction mechanisms. Our findings suggest that CO2(aq) in deep Earth is more active than previously thought, and confining CO2 and water in nanopores may enhance the efficiency of mineral carbonation.

16307618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307618.value: In this completed project, we found that both spatial confinement and solid-liquid interfaces would substantially affect the physical and chemical properties of aqueous solutions. Our current study is at a fully oxidized environment. With increasing depth, Earth's internal environment becomes more reducing, so in the future we would like to see how nanoconfinement would affect the hydrocarbon reactions in water, which would be of great implications for abiotic hydrocarbons in deep Earth.

16307618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307618.value: Dissolving CO2 in water is an everyday process, but its ubiquity belies its importance. Previous studies more focus on properties of dissolved carbon in bulk solutions; however, in deep Earth or underground carbon storage, aqueous solutions are often confined to the nanoscale in pores, grain boundaries, and fractures of Earth's materials, where spatial confinement and interface chemistry may make the solutions fundamentally different. Here we applied long-time ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the CO2 reactions in water. They found that CO2 reacts more in nanoconfinement than in bulk. Their research suggests that CO2 may be more active than previously thought in Earth's deep carbon cycle, which greatly influence the carbon budget in Earth's near-surface reservoirs. Confining CO2 and water in suitable nanoporous minerals may enhance the efficiency of underground carbon storage. This study provides a fundamental step toward unveiling the mysteries of carbon bearing fluids in Earth's interior.

16307718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307718.value: Proteins and other biomolecules often perform their functions via conformational changes, i.e. dynamic transitions between different conformations. Understanding these functional conformational changes is thus essential for understanding numerous fundamental biological processes such as gene transcription. In complement to experiments, Markov State Models (MSMs) based on extensive molecular dynamics simulations is a promising approach to study dynamics of functional conformational changes at atomic resolution. In this approach, searching for initial paths connecting different conformations of interest is prerequisite for successful MSM construction. However, the accuracy and efficiency of existing algorithms to generate initial paths remain inadequate. We propose a new algorithm: Travelling-salesman based Automated Path Searching (TAPS), to efficiently obtain optimized paths for functional conformational changes of biological macromolecules. The novelty of our proposed algorithm is twofold: (1) choosing an iteratively updated path-collective-variable (PCV, defined from a path consisting of a series of conformations) to avoid non-trivial selection of fixed structural-based collective variables; (2) performing non-local sampling perpendicular to the path to avoid localized optimization. As non-local sampling often complicates the update of PCVs, we propose a Travelling-salesman scheme that can automatically reorder the path nodes, enabling efficient on-the-fly update of PCVs. Our preliminary results on two peptide systems show that TAPS can achieve a 5-8 times speedup over the popular String Method with Swarms of Trajectories when searching for optimized paths. We will employ the TAPS algorithm to help construct MSMs to elucidate molecular mechanisms of the bacterial RNA polymerase clamp motion, and further reveal the impact of an antibiotic inhibitor binding on this functional conformational change. Elucidation of such mechanism is crucial for understanding the fundamental basis of bacterial transcription. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate hypotheses that will be tested by our experimental collaborator, and these experiments will further help refine our theoretical models. 蛋白質和其他生物分子通常通過構象變化即不同構象之間的動態轉變來發揮其功能。因此，理解這些功能性構象變化對於理解諸如基因轉錄的許多基本生物學過程是必不可少的。作為實驗的 補充，基於大量分子動力學模擬軌跡構建的馬爾可夫狀態模型（MSM）是研究原子分辨率下功能構象變化動力學的有前景的方法。在這種方法中，搜索連接不同構象的初始路徑是成功構建MSM的先決條件。然而，用於生成初始路徑的現有算法的準確性和效率仍然不足。 我們提出了一種全新的類比於旅行推銷員方案的自動路徑搜索算法（TAPS），它能有效地獲取生物大分子功能構象變化的優化路徑。我們提出的TAPS算法的新穎性有兩個方面：（1）在選擇用於描述路徑的變量上，避免使用傳統的基於分子結構的固定變量，轉而選擇使用迭代更新的用路徑上一系列分子構象定義的集體變量（PCV）; （2）垂直於路徑進行非局部採樣，以避免僅僅取得局部優化的效果。由於非本地採樣通常使PCV的更新變得複雜，我們提出了一種類比於旅行推銷員常採用的方案，該方案 可以自動對路徑節點進行重新排序，從而實現PCV的高效動態更新。我們在兩個蛋白質體系上的初步結果表明，當搜索優化路徑時，TAPS可以比流行的基於軌跡群的弦方法實現5-8倍的加速。 我們將採用TAPS算法幫助構建MSM以闡明細菌RNA聚合酶箝位運動的分子機制，並進一步揭示抗生素抑製劑結合對這種功能性構象變化的影響。闡明這種機制對於理解細菌轉錄的基礎至關 重要。我們理論工作的一個重要重點是產生可以被我們的合作者用實驗測試驗證的假設，這些驗證實驗也將進一步幫助改進我們的理論模型。

16307718.label: Realisation of objectives
16307718.value: Proteins often perform their functions via dynamic transitions between different conformations (i.e., conformational changes). Markov State Models (MSMs) built from extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide a promising approach to study dynamics of these functional conformational changes at atomic resolution. However, a major challenge for the MSM approach is to obtain initial paths connecting different conformations of interest efficiently and accurately. Research supported by this grant aims to address this challenge by developing a new path searching algorithm. For the first objective, we have developed the novel Travelling-salesman based Automated Path Searching (TAPS) method that can efficiently obtain optimized paths for functional conformational changes of biological macromolecules (J. Chem. Phys. 150, 124105 (2019)). In TAPS, we chose an iteratively updated path-collective-variable (PCV, defined from a path consisting of a series of conformations) to avoid non-trivial selection of fixed structural-based collective variables. We demonstrate that PCVs can be computed on-the-fly and used as a coordinate system, minimizing the necessary prior knowledge about the system. Furthermore, we pursue a non-local perpendicular sampling in TAPS to accelerate the search, provided that all nodes are reordered thereafter via a traveling-salesman scheme. We show that our TAPS method achieves significant speedup over the popular string method with swarms-of-trajectories for two peptide systems. We further integrated our newly developed TAPS method into our protocol tailor-made for the construction of MSMs to study protein functional conformational changes (Curr. Opin. in Struc. Bio. 67, 69, (2021) & JACS Au 1, 1330, (2021)). Using this protocol, we have constructed MSMs to study how a DNA motor protein translocates along dsDNA to search for the DNA damage (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 117, 21889, (2020)). In addition to protein dynamics, our developed protocol has shown to be efficient in elucidating dynamics of heterogeneous ice nucleation on the surface (Nat. Commun., 12, 1, (2021)). For the second objective, we have followed our protocol to successfully construct quasi-MSMs (qMSMs) from extensive MD simulations to elucidate the mechanism of the Thermus aquaticus RNA Polymerase (RNAP) clamp closing. Using qMSMs, we identified two intermediate states with partially closed clamps and identified a millisecond timescale for the clamp to close. We also found that the switch-2 region (located at the base of the clamp domain) is mostly correlated with the clamp opening, while the β-lobe oscillates four orders of magnitude faster than the clamp (the gate of RNAP consisted of beta-lobe and clamp domains) (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 118, e2024324118, (2021)). Importantly, we reveal a critical but undiscovered role of β-lobe, whose opening is sufficient for DNA loading even when the clamp is partially closed. For the third objective, we successfully revealed a conformational selection recognition mechanism of the antibiotics: Myxopyronin (Myx). In this mechanism, Myx initially binds to the partially unfolded Switch-2 region in one of the partially closed clamp intermediate state, where Switch-2 spontaneous undergoes partial unfolding. The binding of Myx will confine the clamp in a partially closed clamp conformation and hinders it to either close or open. This will eventually lead to the abolishment of bacterial transcriptional initiation (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 118, e2024324118, (2021)). These findings open the opportunity for the new development of antibiotics targeting RNAP. In addition, we have also elucidated the dynamics of RNA Polymerase II responding to various DNA modifications (J. Biol. Chem., 294, 4924, (2019) & J. Biol. Chem., 296, 100735, (2021)). Finally, with the onset of COVID-19 pandemic, this grant has also partially supported our study to elucidate the role of the ribose cyano-substitution of Remdesivir in its inhibition on SARS-CoV-2’s RNA dependent RNA polymerase (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 23, 5852, (2021)).

16307718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307718.value: With the support of this grant, we have developed a new path searching algorithm (i.e., TAPS) for efficiently identifying optimized paths connecting protein conformational states of interest. Our developed protocol to construct MSMs for conformational changes holds great promise to be widely applied in elucidating dynamics of protein conformational changes, and even dynamics underline numerous chemical processes such as self-assembly and phase transition. In our studies of bacterial RNAP, we showed that the opening of beta-lobe is orders of magnitude faster than that of the clamp. This observation highlights beta-lobe’s critical role allowing DNA loading during initiation. Thus, beta-lobe is a promising target for future development of antibiotics targeting RNAP.

16307718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307718.value: Proteins perform their functions through numerous conformational changes. Markov State Models (MSMs) provide a powerful tool to investigate the dynamics of these conformational changes. However, the application of MSMs to conformational changes is often limited by insufficient quality of initial paths. To address this challenge, we have developed a path search algorithm (TAPS) to facilitate the MSM construction. We show that our TAPS method can greatly accelerate the search for the optimal paths compared to the popular string method in several peptide systems. We further integrated TAPS into a new protocol that is tailor-made for constructing MSMs for protein functional conformational changes. Using this protocol, we have successfully construct qMSMs to elucidate the mechanism underlying the clamp opening of the bacterial Thermus aquaticus RNAP. Using qMSMs, we discovered two intermediate states with partially closed clamps, and found that the Switch-2 region plays an important role in the clamp opening. We further revealed the conformational selection mechanism for the antibiotics: Myx, in which Myx binds to the Switch-2 region, trap the clamp in a partially closed form, and eventually leads to the transcriptional inhibition. These findings provide insights into the development of novel antibiotics.

16307818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307818.value: 虽然全基因组关联研究在鉴定与复杂性状相关的遗传变异方面非常成功，但这些变异与复杂性状之间的机制联系仍然很大程度上未知。 一种科学假设是遗传变异通过影响细胞特性（例如，调节基因表达和改变蛋白质丰度）来影响生物体层面的复杂性状。 然而，如何系统地检验这一假设仍然是一个开放的问题。 最近，大型基因组联盟正在产生大量的基因组数据，以全面刻画遗传变异的调节作用。 例如，基因组 - 组织表达项目收集了449个个体的基因组谱，包括来自多种组织和约1250万个DNA碱基的基因表达的测量，为解剖复杂性状的遗传贡献提供了前所未有的机会。 有效利用多层数据（遗传变异，细胞特征和生物特征）进行机制解释的统计方法要求很高。 遗传变异对生物体层面性状的多基因效应使得统计建模非常具有挑战性，因为它要求所开发的模型能够以低信噪比方式有效地提取信息。 在该研究中，我们的目标是开发统计方法以促进机制上理解相关变异在复杂性状中的作用。关键思想建立在新的科学证据之上，即细胞水平上的遗传效应比生物体层面上的遗传效应强得多水平。我们提出了统计方法利用基因调控信息剖析遗传对复杂性状的贡献，并且充分考虑到数据集成分析中的不确定性。这项研究的新颖之处在于，研发了一种统计学上有效且计算上可行的框架，以剖析遗传对复杂性状的贡献。

16307818.label: Realisation of objectives
16307818.value: 1 Develop statistically efficient models to study the regulatory role of genetic variants in complex traits. To study the regulatory role of genetic variants in complex traits, we have developed statistical models from several different perspectives. (1) To have an overall estimation, we developed IGREX [1] to quantify the impact of genetically regulated expression on phenotypes. (2) To characterize the putative causal relationship between molecular traits and complex traits, we developed the BWMR model [2] to infer their causal effects. (3) To make our methods applicable to summary-level data, we developed several methods based on summary statistics to understand regulatory effects on complex traits, including COMM-S2 [3], LPM[4], REMI[5], GECKO[6]. These methods are not only statistically accurate, but also computationally efficient. (4) To deeply characterize the regulatory effects, we further developed two models, BOLT-SSI [7] and TisCoMM [8], where BOLT-SSI enables fast screening of interaction effects in the high dimensional settings, and TisCoMM allows the characterization of regulatory role of genetic variants at the tissue level. 2 Implementation of the proposed algorithms. We have implemented all the proposed algorithm in R packages. IGREX [1] https://github.com/mxcai/iGREX BWMR [2] https://github.com/jiazhao97/BWMR COMM-S2 [3] https://github.com/gordonliu810822/CoMM LPM[4] https://github.com/mingjingsi/LPM REMI[5] https://github.com/gordonliu810822/REMI GECKO[6] https://github.com/borangao/GECKO BOLT-SSI [7] https://github.com/daviddaigithub/BOLTSSIRR TisCoMM [8] https://github.com/XingjieShi/TisCoMM/ 3 Evaluate model performance using comprehensive simulation studies and compare analysis results with other related methods. When we developed our models, we always use comprehensive simulation studies to compare our methods with related methods. For example, we compared IGREX [1] with RhoGE which is a related statistical method developed by a group at UCLA. IGREX can provide an unbiased estimation of variance explained by genetically regulated expression, while RhoGE often makes underestimation because it ignored the estimation uncertainty at its first step. We also compared our causal inference method BWMR [2] with existing methods, including RAPS, GSMR and Egger. The comparison of the remaining methods COMM-S2 [3], LPM[4], REMI[5], GECKO[6], BOLT-SSI [7] and TisCoMM [8] were also done. To ensure the reproducibility, we provided more details of simulation studies and codes in the corresponding software websites. 4 Apply the proposed methods to real data. We have applied the proposed methods to real data, demonstrating their effectiveness. For example, using eQTL data of 48 tissue types from the GTEx project as a reference panel, we evaluated the tissue-specific IGREX [1] on a wide spectrum of phenotypes. We observed strong GREX effects on immune-related protein biomarkers. By incorporating trans-eQTLs and analyzing genetically regulated alternative splicing events, we evaluated new potential directions for TWAS analysis. We also applied BWMR [2] to make causal inference between 130 metabolites and 93 complex human traits, uncovering novel causal relationship between exposure and outcome traits. Regarding LPM [4], we applied it to analyze 44 GWASs with 9 genic category annotations and 127 cell-type specific functional annotations. The results demonstrate the benefits of LPM and gain insights of genetic architecture of complex traits. All the remaining methods, including COMM-S2 [3], REMI[5], GECKO[6], BOLT-SSI [7] and TisCoMM [8] were applied to real datasets, as detailed in the papers. 5 Investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed methods from both computational and statistical perspectives. We have investigated the theoretical properties of these methods from both computational and statistical perspectives. For example, detecting the interaction effects among the predictors on the response variable is a crucial step in our real data application. We first propose a simple method for sure screening interactions (SSI). Although its computation complexity is O(p^2 n), the SSI method works well for problems of moderate dimensionality (e.g., p = 10^3 ∼ 10^4), without the heredity assumption. For ultrahigh-dimensional problems (e.g., p = 10^6), motivated by a discretization associated Boolean representation and operations and a contingency table for discrete variables, we propose a fast algorithm, called “BOLT-SSI”. The statistical theory is established for SSI and BOLT-SSI [7], guaranteeing their sure screening property. We evaluate the performance of SSI and BOLT-SSI using comprehensive simulations and real case studies. Our numerical results demonstrate that SSI and BOLT-SSI often outperform their competitors in terms of computational efficiency and statistical accuracy. The proposed method can be applied to fully detect interactions with more than 300,000 predictors. Based on our findings, we believe there is a need to rethink the relationship between statistical accuracy and computational efficiency. We have shown that the computational performance of a statistical method can often be greatly improved by exploring the advantages of computational architecture with a tolerable loss of statistical accuracy. 6 Make developed software publicly available We have made all the developed software publicly available. The software links have given in the response to object 2 as well as in the original papers. Importantly, we provide detailed documentation such that interested readers and users can easily reproduce the results in our papers. They can also easily use our software to analyse their own datasets to generate new scientific hypothesis.

16307818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307818.value: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have been successful in identifying many genetic variants associated with complex traits. However, the mechanistic links between these variants and complex traits remain elusive. A scientific hypothesis is that genetic variants influence complex traits at the organismal level via affecting cellular traits, such as regulating gene expression and altering protein abundance. Through statistically rigorous analysis, our research outcomes indicate the following results. First, we show [1] that genetically regulated effects have significant impacts on a wide spectrum of cellular and organismal phenotypes. We also demonstrate that the genetically regulated effects are highly replicable. Second, the genetic effects on cellular phenotypes are often context-dependent. For example, we estimate [1,8] the tissue-specific genetic effects for seven diseases including bipolar disorder (BD), coronary artery disease (CAD), Crohn’s disease (CD), hypertension (HT), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). The top genetically regulated components explain a significant proportion of variance: 12.8% for BD in amygdala, 21.2% for CAD in spinal cord, 18.4% for CD in amygdala, 16.7% for HT in spleen and 17.9% for T2D in anterior cingulate cortex. Third, through real data analysis, we find [4] that there exist a large proportion of genetic variants which can affect multiple phenotypes. This phenomena is referred to “pleiotropy”. Statistical methods and computational algorithms can explore the pleiotropic effect to identify more risk variants by simultaneously analysing multiple phenotypes. Fourth, the existing genetic data can greatly help to perform causal inference between exposure traits and outcome traits. For example, our BWMR method [2] shows that there exists a causal relationship between LDL (low-density lipoprotein) cholesterol and Coronary Artery Disease with an effect size (⁠βˆ=0.13,p−value=2.41×10^−9). Our results will motivate further development of statistical methods to strengthen causal inference using genetic data.

16307818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307818.value: Our research outcomes suggest two important further directions. First, most current GWASs have been performed on samples with European ancestry (about 89% of GWAS participants to date have been of European ancestry whereas fewer than 8% of the participants have been of East Asian ancestry). Such an unbalanced sample makeup across global populations may exacerbate the disparities in genetic studies of non-Europeans. How to leverage the results derived from European samples to other populations, such as East Asian population, is a promising direction. Statistical methods for cross-population analysis will be highly appreciated. Second, we show that genetically regulated effects can be context-dependent. This fact will motivate more comprehensive study to integrate single-cell genomics with human genetics, where statistical and computational methods will play a critical role. Third, due to the presence of pleiotropy and population structure in GWAS, more sophisticated methods are needed to handle the complexity of human genetic data to perform causal inference.

16307818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307818.value: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been successful in identifying genetic variants associated with complex traits, but the mechanisms linking these variants and traits are not fully understood. A hypothesis suggests that genetic variants influence complex traits by altering cellular traits like gene expression and protein abundance. This research found that genetically regulated effects significantly impact a wide range of cellular and organismal phenotypes and are highly replicable. Additionally, genetic effects on cellular phenotypes often depend on the context. Furthermore, a high proportion of genetic variants can affect multiple phenotypes, known as pleiotropy. Statistical and computational methods can explore the pleiotropic effect to identify more risk variants by analyzing multiple phenotypes simultaneously. Existing genetic data can also help perform causal inference between exposure and outcome traits. Our research outcomes also suggest two crucial areas for further study. The first direction is leveraging GWAS results in European populations for other populations. The second direction is integrating single-cell genomics with human genetics to study context-dependent effects. Addressing these issues with statistical and computational methods will deepen our understanding of human complex traits and diseases.

16308018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308018.value: 科學研究經常會遇到不動點。許多問題，例如動力系統或經濟活動中的平衡點，都可以被歸結為有關系統中的不動點。此外，許多系統具有對稱性，而對稱系統的不動點比一般的不動點往往具有更強的性質。本課題試圖回答如下的反問題：如果某拓撲空間具有在對稱系統中比較強的性質，是不是真的可以成為某對稱系統的不動點？ 關於不動點的拓撲性質的研究，起始於Brouwer關於在一定拓撲條件下不動點存在性的定理，Lefschitz進一步給出了不動點的個數，然後Smith發現了對稱系統的不動點必須滿足的更強的拓撲性質，Smith的發現可以被認為是Lefschitz數個數的高級同調論版本。 我們的反問題從Smith發現的拓撲性質出發。許多拓撲學家，特別是Jones、Oliver、Petrie，證明了在單聯通的假定下Smith的拓撲性質可以成為有關對稱的不動點。在不是單聯通的假定下，就我們所知至今還沒有太多類似的結果。但許多有關的對稱拓撲空間的問題往往不是單聯通的，因此有必要將單聯通的假定下的結果推廣到一般的空間，這種推廣將會加深我們關於對稱性和不動點的拓撲性質之間關係的理解。

16308018.label: Realisation of objectives
16308018.value: Let F be a finite CW-complex, let Y be a finite G-CW complex, and let f be a map from F to the fixed part of Y. The problem is to extend F to become the fixed set of a finite G-CW complex X, and extend f to G-map from X to Y, such that g is a non-equivariant homotopy equivalence (i.e., pseudo-equivalence). The classical results by Jones and Oliver discussed the case Y is a single point, when the problem becomes realising F as the fixed point set of a finite contractible G-CW complex. (1) Pseudo-equivalence extension for non-simply connected case. Applying the general theory in (2), we determine the criteria for the semi-free pseudo-equivalence extension from various mapping tori of self map of sphere, which naturally maps to the circle. For example, for a prime number p, the mapping torus T(p^k) for a self map of degree p is fixed set of a Z/p^nZ-action if and only if k is not smaller than n. We also considered the case the fundamental group of Y is torsionless and the Farrell-Jones conjecture holds for the fundamental group. We get some cases that the Smith conditions are satisfied, but the semi-free pseudo-equivalence extension does not exist. Applying the general theory in (3), for a group G of not prime power order, we proved that, if the fixed set of a finite G-CW complex Y is non-empty and connected, then a finite CW complex F is the fixed set of a finite G-CW complex pseudo-equivalent to Y if and only if the Euler number condition is satisfied. Note that the result allows the “zig-zag” version of the pseudo-equivalence. In other words, there is no need to have a G-map from the extension to Y. We also applied our theory to construct a G-action on compact aspherical manifold with centreless fundamental group, such that the induced map from G to the outer isomorphism group of the fundamental group lifts to the automorphism group, and yet the G-action has no fixed point. (2) Semi-free group action. In the classical theory by Jones, a finite CW-complex F is the fixed set of a semi-free cyclic group action on a finite contractible CW-complex if and only if the Smith condition is satisfied. We proved that, for semi-free pseudo-equivalence extension of general group (not necessarily cyclic) action, the Smith condition is necessary for each connected component of the fixed set of Y. Conversely, if the action on Y is semi-free, then there is semi-free pseudo-equivalence extension if and only if some K-theoretical obstruction vanishes. Moreover, the obstruction is the sum of similar obstructions on individual connected components. We also obtain variations of our theory by considering simple homotopy or G-ANR category. (3) General group action. In the classical theory by Oliver, for any group G of not prime power order, there is a number n(G), such that a finite CW-complex F is the fixed set of a G-action on a finite contractible CW-complex if and only if Euler number of F is 0 mod n(G). We proved that, for general pseudo-equivalence extension, the answer depends on the mod n(G) Euler numbers of the connected components of the fixed set of Y. In particular, it is necessary for the total Euler number condition to be satisfied, and it is sufficient for the Euler number condition to be satisfied on each connected component. The general answer lies somewhere in between, and is characterised by an abelian group formed by these Euler numbers. We explored the role the fundamental group of Y in the “obstruction abelian group”. For the case of cyclic group G and rational pseudo-equivalence, and the case of group G with n(G)=0, we may distinguish connected components of the fixed set of Y by the conjugation classes of the liftings of the G-action on Y to G-actions on the universal cover of Y. Then the Euler number condition needs to be satisfied for each conjugation class, for the two cases. In particular, if the G-action on Y is weekly G-connected, in the sense that liftings given by different connected components are not conjugate, then the pseudo-equivalence extension is possible if and only if the mod n(G) Euler number condition is satisfied for each component. Finally, our results also applies to the case G is a compact Lie groups, and to the G-ANR category.

16308018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308018.value: We successfully extended the classical theories by Jones (for semi-free action) and Oliver (for group of not prime power order) on fixed points of contractible spaces to non-simply connected case (the classical theories were about a single point). The extension of Jones’ theory keeps the Smith condition, and introduces an additional K-theoretical obstruction. The extension of Oliver’s theory is still based on Euler numbers, but over connected components of fixed sets. In particular, Oliver’s mod n(G) Euler number condition is extended to a suitable obstruction abelian group formed by the Euler numbers over connected components. Moreover, both extensions are valid for G-ANR-category, and the extension of Oliver’s theory is valid for compact Lie group. Then we applied our theory to get interesting examples, and prove some interesting results. For semi-free complexes pseudo-equivalent to the circle, we have some examples satisfying the Smith condition, and the existence of pseudo-equivalence extension depends on some numerical conditions. For the case the fundamental group is torsionless and satisfies the Farrell-Jones conjecture, we pinpoint the homological condition for those satisfying the Smith condition to have pseudo-equivalence extension. For general G-CW complexes, we find more refined information about the obstruction abelian group for the pseudo-equivalence extension, using the effect of fundamental group on the liftings of the G-actions to the universal covers. In the weekly G-connected case, this implies the condition for the pseudo-equivalence extension is exactly the component wise Euler number condition. On the other hand, in case the fixed set is non-empty and connected, we showed the Euler number condition is necessary and sufficient for the weak “zig-zag” version of the pseudo-equivalence extension.

16308018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308018.value: For general group action, we need to further study the obstruction abelian group. The first step would be to find some examples that the obstruction is not the extreme cases that we already know about, i.e., the Euler numbers over connected components can be traded to some extent. We should consider pseudo-equivalence extensions, such that the isotropies are confined to certain families of subgroups. Oliver and Petrie already had some theory for the so called quasi-equivalence extensions. However, pseudo-equivalence extensions is the more natural problem. Finally, we should study the manifold version of the pseudo-equivalence extension problem.

16308018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308018.value: The pseudo-equivalence extension is a fundamental problem for geometrical topology. For the case of single point, the problem is to find the condition for a finite CW-complex to be the fixed point of some group action on finite contractible CW-complex. Jones and Oliver answered this simplest case quite some time ago. Their theories have been quite useful for solving some related problems in geometric topology. To solve more problems, however, we need to develop the similar theory beyond the case of single points, especially the case the complex is not simply connected. We have developed such a theory and provided some interesting examples. Moreover, we applied the new theory to get some interesting results about group actions.

16308118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308118.value: Classical heat engines (CHEs) described by classical thermodynamics, such as cars, refrigerators, air conditioners, and power plants, have revolutionarily improved humans’ quality of life. A quantum heat engine (QHE) governed by quantum thermodynamics may function significantly differently and reach unusual regimes unachievable by CHEs. While CHEs have completely changed our lifestyles in the past centuries, the study of QHEs has mostly been theoretical, with very few experimental demonstrations. Here we propose to investigate QHEs using the quantum coherence of photons and atoms, with a strong focus on experimental demonstrations. Particularly we will construct atom-photon heat engines that cannot be described by classical thermodynamics, such as QHEs violating detailed balance and Kirchhoff’s law and QHEs extracting work from a single heat reservoir. The proposed project will lead to improvements in various energy conversion processes that cannot not be achieved by CHEs. 由經典熱力學描述的經典熱機，如汽車，制冷機，空調，發電機等， 已經革命性的改進了人類的生活品質。而由量子熱力學規律主導的量子熱機的表現則可以完全不同於這些經典熱機。雖然經典熱機的發展在過去幾個世紀已經完全改變了我們的生活方式，但是對量子熱機卻大多侷限於理論研究，而很少有實驗驗證。在這裡我們提出一個利用原子光子量子相干性來研究量子熱機的實驗方案。我們將構造無法用經典熱力學來描述的原子光子熱機，其性質包括不遵循細緻平衡和基爾霍夫定律，以及利用單一熱源做工等。本研究將有助于探索發現超越經典熱機的能量轉換過程。

16308118.label: Realisation of objectives
16308118.value: [Objective 1] The thoery of quantum heat engine in the atom-photon interface was systematically developed, which lays out the foundation of the experimental demonstration. More deteails can be found in the following references [PhD Thesis, Mei Yefeng 2020 ; PhD Thesis, Jiang Yue 2020]. [Objective 2] We successfully demonstrated the generation of directional thermal radiation with a spectral brightness that was 9 times greater than that of the ambient pumping reservoir, which represents a nontraditional coherence-based quantum heat engine. The most attractive feature of quantum thermodynamics is that a quantum heat engine may overcome the limits of a classical counterpart since a quantum system may be able to deliver the amount of work that a classical system has difficulty achieving or reach high efficiency levels approaching the ideal Carnot engine. Currently, we are tyring to demonstrate a theoretical understanding of atom-photon quantum heat engine without lasing without the inversion and also aim to generalize the scheme to the atomic system in the ultracold regime.

16308118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308118.value: Conventionaly, an optical system with parity-time or anti-parity-time symmetry has to be involved with gain and loss. If such a system is extended to quantum regime, the gain/loss-induced noises do not preserve the parity-time or anti-parity-time symmetry. We find out in our optical four-wave mixing (FWM) system, the anti-parity-time symmetry can be realized without gain and loss by carefully engineering the phase mismatching. Driving by a pump laser beam and a coupling laser beam, we generate an anti-Stokes light beam by seeding a Stokes laser beam, or generate the Stokes light beam by seeding the anti-Stokes laser beam. This is the first time we realize anti-parity-time symmetric optics without involving gain and loss. This system can be extended to quantum optics regime without introducing additional noise and will have applications in quantum information science. This work was published in Physical Review Letters [Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 193604 (2019).] To better enderstanding comprehensive theoretical description of the optical FWM process, we looked deep into the theory of quantum heat engine. We investigated the Langevin quantum theory of optical four-wave mixing with atom-photon coherence. Dephasing caused noise is an important problem in a quantum system. Conventionally, driving the noise properties and correlations from microscopic atomic states coupled to light and environment is a standard but lengthy method which is difficult for experimentalists to follow. We found it is possible to develop a Langevin quantum theory from the system global linear and nonlinear properties without looking at the microscopic details of the atoms. The new approach dramatically reduces the complexity of the theoretical calculation and make it accessible for experimentalists. During the project, three PhD students were trained.

16308118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308118.value: Our demonstration of quantum heat engine in atom-photon interacting systems can be generalized to ultracold atoms. For this end, it will be necessary to implement tailored quantum control for inducing heat transfer via inelastic spin-exchange collisions. Then, full-counting statistics of atomic ensembels will allos us to monitor heat exchange betewen the system and bath, leading to the full characterisation of the quantum engine. Based on the preliminary development of various tools in the PI's group, we envision demonstrating such a quantum heat exchange process in the near future.

16308118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308118.value: We have recently witnessed how quantum technology stands to change the way we look at problems encountered in science and society. Among the many applications of quantum technology, we investigate how atoms - the most fundamental quantum objects - interact with photons. In particular, we experimentally examined the coherent atom-photon interaction process and theoretically understand how such a process can be interpreted as a quantum heat engine. Our work laid out the foundation for exploiting atomic quantum systems leading to various applications in quantum information science.

16308518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308518.value: The traditional framework for solving unknown through its linear measurements is ubiquitous in science and engineering, and it is no exaggeration to view solving Ax=b as the foundation of computational mathematics and engineering. Recently several new related classes of problems have emerged, where we no longer have the luxury of linear measurements Ax=b. In one such case we can measure only the amplitude of the entries of Ax, namely |b| where the absolute value is taken entry-wise. In other words, we have the amplitudes of the linear measurements but have no phase information. Known as the Phase Retrieval Problem, the goal is to recover the signal x by recovering the phase information. In another setting we still have the linear measurements Ax=b, however the system is vastly under-determined but we have the a priori knowledge that the solution x lies on a lower dimensional manifold. We shall refer to such a problem as a Manifold Recovery problem. It turns out that phase retrieval can be reformulated as a special case of the manifold recovery. Phase Retrieval has important applications in many fields. In fact the classic phase retrieval problem is to recover a function from the magnitude of its Fourier transform, which comes naturally from X-ray diffraction imaging. Of particular interest also is the case when the coefficients are obtained from a Windowed Fourier Transform (also known as Short-Time Fourier Transform), or an Undecimated Wavelet Transform (in audio and image signal processing). A similar problem appears in Quantum Information. Other applications are found in wavefront reconstruction, terahertz imaging, holography, communication, and more. Phase retrieval is closely related to the broader problem of recovering data on a manifold, an example of which is the low rank matrix recovery problem. Significant progress has been made on phase retrieval and related data recovery problems, especially in the past few years, both theoretically and computationally. We shall discuss many of the progresses in the main body of the proposal. Still there remains many challenges and unanswered questions. Here we shall focus on phase retrieval but will also touch on related recovery problem. Of the specific areas, we shall focus on building a theoretical framework for phase retrieval, including the minimality of measurements needed for phase retrieval, algorithms, measurements designs that allow for fast and robust phase retrieval, with applications for scattering transform. We will discuss some preliminary results and ideas for further tackling of the problems. 通過線性測量解出未知變量作為一個傳統的方法在科學和工程中無處不在。可以毫不誇張地說，解 Ax = b 是計算數學和工程的基礎。 最近出現了幾個新的相關類問題，多數來自應用。我們不再擁有線性測量Ax = b的值了，而是在很多情況下，我們只能測量到 Ax 的幅度，即 | b |，這裡絕對值是對每項求。換句話說，我們有線性測量的幅度但沒有相位信息。這就是我們說的相位恢復問題，目標是通過恢復相位信息來恢復信號 x。在另一種設置中，我們仍然具有線性測量值 Ax = b，但是系統非常不確定。變量個數遠遠多於觀測。但我們具有先驗知識，即解 x 位於較低維度的流形上。我們將把這樣的問題稱為流形恢復問題。事實證明，相位恢復問題可以重新擬定為低維度流形恢復的特例。 相位恢復在許多領域都有重要的應用。事實上，經典的相位恢復問題是從其傅立葉變換的幅度大小中恢復一個函數，這自然來自 X-射線衍射成像。另外特別有興趣的是從窗口傅里葉變換（也稱為短時傅里葉變換）或未解碼小波變換（在音頻和圖像信號處理中）獲得係數時的情況。量子信息中也出現類似的問題。其他應用包括波前重建，太赫茲成像，全息，通信等。相位恢復與在流形上恢復數據的更廣泛問題密切相關，其中一個例子是低秩矩陣恢復問題。 相位恢復和相關數據恢復問題已取得重大進展，特別是在過去幾年中，無論是在理論上還是在計算上都是如此。我們將討論提案主體中的許多進展，當然現在依舊仍然存在許多挑戰和未解決的問題。在這裡，我們將重點關注相位恢復，但也將涉及許多相關的恢復問題。在具體領域中，我們將重點建立相位檢恢復的理論框架，包括相位恢復所需的最小測量，高效算法，允許快速和穩健的相位恢復的測量設計，以及散射變換的應用。我們將討論一些初步結果和想法，以進一步解決問題。

16308518.label: Realisation of objectives
16308518.value: The PI has achieved the objectives of the proposed research. One of the objectives is to study phase retrieval using non-Gaussian random measurements. Current literature focuses entirely on Gaussian measurements. But there are clearly advantages if we can obtain the same results using non-Gaussian, such as Bernoulli measurements for practical applications. The difficulty is that without the Gaussian assumption, random measurements do not have the isotropic property. We have employed a novel technique to get around this difficulty. In the end we are able to show that with O(n log^2(n)) measurements with any sub-Gaussian measurements we can achieve full reconstruction. In another paper, we have designed a new objective function for solving the phase retrieval problem without the need to do spectral initialization. The method, which we call SAF, yields a very fast convergence for phase retrieval. Furthermore, the convergence is completely guaranteed theoretically using a comprehensive landscape analysis. It is one of the very few simple algorithms without the need for spectral initialization and a complete theoretical proof. On the minimality of measurements, we have focused on the case of "almost everywhere" phase retrieval. This is a well known topic on the theoretical side of phase retrieval. In the conventional phase retrieval setting one seeks to be able to reconstruct ALL signals from a set of measurements. In the "almost everywhere" setting, the objective is to be able to reconstruct "almost all" signals. There is a precise mathematical definition of it. We have now completely solved the problem for random and generic measurements, obtaining a precise formula for how many measurements are needed. For the classical minimality problem without the "almost everywhere" setting, the problem is very hard and so far this problem has even attracted researchers from areas such as algebraic geometry, and it is unlikely the problem will be solved soon. However, for random measurements we did make progress on sub-gaussian measurements and the number required to allow convergence of fast algorithm. Generally speaking, while random measurements work, achieving the same kind of results using deterministic measurements has eluded mathematicians and engineers for over 20 years, with still no solution on the horizon. One area we plan to pursue in the future is to consider deterministic measurements in phase retrieval that are not necessarily minimal in number, but just "a little bit worse'' than minimal. Scattering transform is valuable for applications where the data set is small. We have been working with Shanghai Renmin Hospital to apply scattering transform for ECG signal. Early results are promising although far from conclusive, and more data will be needed. It is for this application that we looked into the development of frame-related scattering transform. It is known that scattering transform works well for small data set, and is more competitive against traditional neural network in terms of feature selection. This makes it a good tool for medical data analysis since unlike ImageNet or some other standard data sets, medical data sets are typically much smaller. We have successfully applied the traditional scattering transform for our collaboration with Renmin Hospital. The application of scattering transform is deeply related to machine learning and even neural networks. On this front we have made major progress. The VGrow (Variational Gradient Flow) method we have developed offers improved training stability with much less occurrence mode collapse. Furthermore we have recently improved the VGrow further using Schrodinger Bridges, achieving state-of-the-art results.

16308518.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308518.value: One major finding is that we can efficiently perform phase retrieval from non-Gaussian measurements, something that hasn't been done before. This was presented in the paper with GAO Bing and LIU Haixia. We have employed a novel technique to get around this difficulty. In the end we are able to show that with O(n log^2(n)) measurements with any sub-Gaussian measurements we can achieve full reconstruction. Our study has completely solved the "almost everywhere" phase retrieval problem. This was also a classical problem in phase retrieval. We employed techniques from algebraic geometry to overcome the difficulties. This is presented in the paper with HUANG Meng, RONG Yi and XU Zhiqiang. We have obtained a provisional US Patent for using scattering transform and other machine learning techniques to forecast heart disease risk. We hope this would lead to a much cheaper and noninvasive method for detecting heart disease.

16308518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308518.value: The phase retrieval problem has a wide array of applications. While we know how to perform phase retrieval effectively for Gaussian random measurements, in may applications the measurements are not random Gaussian. There are many applications that are closely related to phase retrieval, such as Ptychography. We are now working in this direction, hoping to develop effective and fast algorithms. Another potentially fruitful area is the application of machine learning/neural networks for phase retrieval. While there is already some work in this area, they are still far from completely solving the problem. Deep learning has completely changed the landscape of research in related areas such as compressive sensing and image processing. Phase retrieval, while more challenging, will almost certainly go through a similar transition. For example, Ptychography is an area that is naturally suited for the interplay of phase retrieval and deep learning. Other related areas include molecular imaging. These are fruitful areas to pursue in the future.

16308518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308518.value: Many of you have seen very striking pictures of a protein or a virus. But do you know that these pictures are not taken using an optical microscope? This is because the structures are too small to be seen by even the most powerful optical microscopes. Instead they are obtained often by a process call phase retrieval. Other applications include X-ray crystallography etc. Instruments such as X-ray and electron microscope only measures the amplitude of Fourier transforms. The process to reconstruct the structure from such measurements is exactly phase retrieval. In other words, we try to retrieve lost phase information from amplitude measurements only. The question is: how can one do this? If there is a way to do it, how do we know it always works. The project is focused on addressing these questions for phase retrieval, both theoretically and algorithmically. For example, can we solve the phase retrieval problem very quickly. Also, how many measurements do we need to allow us to do phase retrieval reconstruction? These are the questions we try to answer in this project. We have made progress on many important questions in this area.
