16308818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308818.value: Trapping and manipulating cells with high temporal and spatial resolution is critical for single-cell analysis and achieving isolated cells. Researchers have used cell traps to measure nucleic acids and proteins in single cells, perform cell pairing in cell communication studies, conduct high-throughput screening and engineer tissue applications. Such studies have been critical in unveiling new insights into how cells signal pathways and communicate with other cells. Cell trapping and printing technology has a number of applications related to human health, especially with regard to probing why single cells behave differently than genetically similar cells. Such technology is also applicable to immunological studies for disease response and drug efficacy testing. A comprehensive understanding of how cell-signaling pathways and cell communication work is necessary to create new drugs, personalized medicine and targeted disease therapies. Current cell-trapping techniques can be divided into three categories. The first category concerns the use of external fields, such as optical tweezers, acoustic traps, dielectrophoresis and magnetic fields. Their major limitations are that they require expensive and sophisticated facilities, they cause damage or stress to cells and most of them are not point-source techniques, but array techniques. In the second category, substrate surfaces are chemically patterned with cell-adhesion promoters or antibodies to form cell arrays. Although the method is simple and scalable, it has low resolution and lacks versatility in cell manipulations. In the last category, hydrodynamic traps, such as microwells and microdams, in microfluidic devices are used to capture single cells. However, such methods have low single-cell capture rates and cannot manipulate cells spatially. Although resistive-based hydrodynamic trapping can capture single cells with high efficiency, it is non-trivial to release the cells safely. It is also impossible for existing devices to build 3D cell structures. In the proposed project, we will adapt the resistive-based hydrodynamic trapping mechanism to create a single-cell pipette that can selectively capture single cells with high efficiency and transfer and precisely deposit the captured cells on 2D substrates or in 3D space. A microfluidic controlling system will be integrated with the pipette to accurately control cell release. This single-cell pipette will be very easy to use and, by combining it with microfluidic components, will be adaptable to various forms to fulfill different task requirements (e.g., high-throughput, multiplexity, 3D cell printing and droplet formation with 1 cell/drop). We will further explore the applications of this single-cell pipette technique in cell studies, tissue engineering and analytical science. 高時間和空間分辨率的捕獲并操縱細胞對於單細胞分析和提取單細胞是非常重要的。研究人員使用細胞陷阱來測量單細胞中的核酸和蛋白質，在細胞通信研究中進行細胞配對，進行高通量篩选以及在組織工程中應用。這些研究對於揭示細胞信號通路以及如何與其他細胞通信提供了新的理解。細胞捕獲和打印技術在與人類健康相關的領域有許多應用，特別是關於探測為什麼單個細胞，即使遺傳上相似，也具有不同的行為。該技術也可適用於疾病響應和藥物功效測試的免疫學研究。全面了解細胞信號傳導途徑和細胞通訊如何發揮作用對於創造新藥，個性化醫療和靶向疾病治療是非常必要的。 目前的細胞捕獲技術可分為三類。第一類需要使用外場，例如光學鑷子，聲學陷阱，介電電泳和磁場。它們的主要缺點是它們需要昂貴和復雜的設備，它們對細胞造成損害或壓力，並且它們中的大多數不是點源技術，而是陣列技術。在第二類中，基質表面用細胞粘附促進劑或抗體來進行化學圖案化以形成細胞陣列。雖然該方法簡單且可放大，但它具有低分辨率並且不太容易進行多功能細胞操作。在最後一類中，微流體裝置中的流體動力學陷阱（例如微井和微型閘門）用於捕獲單個細胞。然而，這些方法的單細胞捕獲率不高並且在空間上操縱細胞比較困難。儘管基於流體阻力的流體動力學捕獲方法可以高效捕獲單個細胞，但安全地釋放捕獲的細胞並非易事。現有的技術也無法構建三維細胞結構。 在擬議的項目中，我們將採用基於流體阻力的捕集機制來創建單細胞移液器，該移液器可以選擇性地高效捕獲單個細胞，並可將捕獲的細胞精確地沉積在2D基板或3D空間中。該移液器還可以和微流控制系統集成，以精確控制細胞釋放。這種單細胞移液器將非常易於使用，並且通過與不同微流體器件相結合，將可以以各種形式來滿足不同的任務要求（例如，高通量，多重性，3D細胞印刷和形成只含單個細胞的液滴）。我們將進一步探索該單細胞移液器技術在細胞研究，組織工程和分析科學中的應用。

16308818.label: Realisation of objectives
16308818.value: Let me show the realization of the objectives below: Objectives 1&2. Design and fabricate a single-cell pipette and optimize its function; & Design and fabricate a cell-locking single-cell pipette and a cell-releasing single-cell pipette with microfluidic controlling components. We have successfully fabricated a single cell pipette device as designed, two pieces of master molds were fabricated by photolithography and different ratios of PDMS prepolymers were cast into both molds and then thermally bonded together. In our work, Quake valves and a simple mild negative pressure system controlled by Arduino were employed to precisely control the flow of cell suspension in the device. We tested more than thirty geometric designs to confirm the best one that trap cells. Using HepG2 cells as model, we found that when the width and length of bypass area were set at 900 um and 20 um, respectively, an trapping efficiency of almost 100% was reached. Moreover, we were able to release only one single cell per droplet after replacing the cell suspension with phosphate-buffered saline. The Objectives are successfully completed. Objectives 3&4. Design and fabricate a high-throughput single-cell pipette; & Design and fabricate a multiplex single-cell pipette that can simultaneously manipulate different types of cells. In our work (mainly from Qiaoyi Wang’s PhD thesis work, which has not been published yet), we constructed a microfluidic single-cell array chip that can realize addressable cell release at low cost. With rational geometric designs, we realized high cell capture efficiency (~90%) and release of a single cell in a 10 x 10 array. Asymmetric microelectrode pairs were devised to produce addressable electrolytic bubbles in the 10 x 10 microelectrode array (MEA). This platform combines both passive and active manipulation techniques to control the motion of a single cell. This device will be coupled with a downstream single-cell module and form a cost-economical single-cell analysis platform. In addition, we constructed a high-throughput, open-space and reusable microfluidic chip for combinational drug screening on tumor spheroids. This microchip is straightforward to fabricate, compatible with standard spheroid cultures, and friendly for end-users. The device consists of an inlet layer and multiple dispersing layers. In the inlet layer, different samples can be loaded into the chip simultaneously. The sample solutions flow into the dispersing layers to generate various combinations based on the specific design-of-experiment (DOE) principle. We demonstrated that the chip performance is in quantitative agreement with the design, using water and doxycycline combinations as models. As a proof-of-concept study, we constructed a HeLa reporter cell line to quantify the autophagy of tumor spheroids and used the chip to identify critical factors relating to the growth of the spheroids. Specifically, we used L-glutamine, D-glucose, FBS, and cisplatin as the factors and studied the autophagy, growth curves, and spheroid sizes in response to different combinations of the four factors. We found that D-glucose can inhibit the effects of cisplatin on tumor spheroids, and cisplatin caused severe autophagy in 3D tumor spheroids compared to 2D monoculture cells. Our method has the potential to allow more drug combinations to be examined, and it can be extended to DOE approaches with seven or more inputs. The Objectives are successfully completed. Objectives 5 & 6. Explore and demonstrate single-cell pipettes for different bio-applications; & Explore and demonstrate single-cell pipettes for the generation of droplets. We have explored possible applications of our technology in different bio-applications. In the first example, we developed a controllable, centrifugal-based single-cell microfluidic pipette for cell-pairing and used it to study long-term communications between single cells. Investigation of cell–cell interactions between individual cells in a well-defined microenvironment is critical for the understanding of specific intercellular communications and interactions. However, most current studies in multicellular systems are often overwhelmed by additional complicated interactions. Cell-pairing based on a microfluidic chip provides a potential strategy to simplify the studies. Here, we report a robust and straightforward method, relying on a combination of hydrodynamic single-cell capture and centrifugation-assisted relocation of individual cells, which can be applied, in general, to various cell types for cell-pairing and studying cell interactions at the single-cell level. This microfluidic chip is simple to operate and easily controlled, which requires only two operational steps—capturing individual cells with hydrodynamic traps and subsequently relocating the capture cells by centrifugation. With this microfluidic chip, we demonstrated homotypic cell-pairing, heterotypic cell-pairing, and long-term cell coculture, which exhibited better or comparable performance compared with previous cell-pairing methods. Its single-cell trapping and cell-pairing efficiencies are ∼74% and ∼20%, respectively. As a proof of concept, we paired individual dHL-60 cells and HeLa cells (HeLa-IL8, HeLa-IL10, and wild-type HeLa cells) in multiple cell chambers. The HeLa-IL8 and HeLa-IL10, both engineered with a light-induced gene expression system, can secret interleukin-8 and interleukin-10, respectively, under blue light illumination. We found that these three HeLa cell lines have very different influences on the migration of dHL-60 cells. This platform demonstrates its potential applications in studies of intercellular communication (paracrine), and it can be extended to trap three or more individual cells for more complex biological systems. In addition, we developed a design-of-experiment microfluidic chip that applied the single-cell pipette basics for the optimization of factor combinations for stem cell differentiations. Directed differentiation of stem cells plays a vital role in cell replacement therapy. Many activators and inhibitors targeting different signaling pathways have been identified to contribute to each step of differentiation. Most studies relied on empirically optimizing the combinations of the aforementioned factors for each step to optimize the efficiency of differentiation, which are time-consuming and nonsystematic. Design-of-experiment (DOE) is a powerful strategy to identify the critical combinations from multiple factors systematically. However, it is prohibitively complicated for typical laboratories, given a large number of potential combinations. Here, we develop a multilayer polymethyl methacrylate-based, reusable microfluidic chip to directly facilitate the DOE in the differentiation of stem cells. The chip consists of an inlet layer and multiple disperse layers. Different solutions are injected simultaneously to the chip through the inlet layer. Subsequently, the channels in the disperse layers split and recombine the flow streams to generate solution combinations based on hard-wired DOE designs. We demonstrated that it is in quantitative agreement with the designs using fluorescent dyes. Moreover, we constructed a human-induced pluripotent stem reporter cell line to improve the consistency of the cellular state measurements and use the chip to identify critical factors for cell differentiation to definitive endoderm (DE). We found that the differentiation efficiencies under various factor combinations are significantly different, and CHIR99201 and GDF8 are the most critical factors for differentiation to DE. Our method is potentially applicable to the optimization of factor combinations for multi-step stem cell differentiation and combinatorial drug screening. The Objectives are successfully completed. We planned only a small budget in the proposal for equipment. Later we found that there was no need for us to purchase the proposed parts. Instead, the cost of chemicals was increased more than what we planned in the proposal. That's why we spent large expenses for General Expenses and no equipment expenses.

16309018.label: Project Objectives
16309018.value: To develop a scalable, inexpensive, and reliable approach to fabricate organometal halide-perovskite NW arrays with precisely controlled geometries. The goal here is to obtain large-scale, high-density, geometry-controllable perovskite NW arrays. To understand the degradation mechanisms of perovskite materials under different ambient conditions, and to compare the difference in degradation behavior of perovskite NWs versus thin films. With this mechanistic study, we will further understand the role of alumina templates in hindering water and oxygen diffusion among NWs. We can also develop an effective approach to achieve long-term, stable, lead-free perovskite NW arrays. To investigate the factors that affect the optical properties of perovskite NWs, including composition and geometry. 16309018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309018.value: Metal-halide perovskite materials have attracted enormous attention in recent years for their applications in high-performance optoelectronic devices, including solar cells, photodetectors, and light-emitting diodes (LEDs). The high performance of perovskite materials can be attributed to their excellent material properties, including a high light absorption coefficient, wide-range tuned optical property, and micrometer-scale charge carrier diffusion length. Another key advantage of perovskite materials is the easy and inexpensive fabrication process, which does not require high temperatures or a vacuum. Thus a wide range of substrate materials, including flexible plastic substrates, can be used. Despite the advantages of perovskite materials, however, there are still challenges to tackle before they can be used for practical applications. They are prone to decompose when exposed to air and moisture, leading to significant device performance degradation. Because degradation is a major bottleneck challenge for perovskite materials, there is an urgent need to address it for future optoelectronic device applications. In the proposed project, semiconductor nanowires (NWs) made of metal-halide perovskite materials will be fabricated in chemically and mechanically robust nanoengineering templates, which will serve as effective protection and passivation material to block lateral diffusion of water and oxygen molecules and thus greatly improve stability. The potential of these NW materials for applications in high-performance optoelectronic devices, such as photodetectors and LEDs, will be explored. In particular, perovskite material compositional tuning and NW geometrical optimization will be studied to achieve rational device structure designs for high performance. In addition, device performance degradation mechanisms will be studied to identify approaches to further improve material and device stability. 近年來金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料引起了極大的關注，它們在高性能光電器件中有廣泛的應用，包括太陽能電池，光電探測器和發光二極管（LED）。鈣鈦礦的高性能材料可歸因於其優異的材料特性，包括高光吸收系數，寬範圍調諧光學特性和微米級電荷載流子擴散長度。鈣鈦礦材料的另一個關鍵優勢是易於使用廉價的製造工藝，不需要高溫或真空。因此，可以使用各種基板材料，包括柔性塑料基板。儘管鈣鈦礦材料具有各種優點，但仍然存在許多的挑戰。當暴露在空氣和濕氣中時，它們容易分解，會導致器件性能顯著下降。因此分解是鈣鈦礦材料的主要瓶頸挑戰，所以有迫切需要來解決它在光電器件應用。此項目提出用化學和機械性能穩定的納米工程模板作為有效的保護和鈍化材料來組裝半導體鹵化物鈣鈦礦納米線，以阻止橫向擴散水和氧分子，因而大大提高穩定性。這些納米線材料有很大潛力適用於高性能光電器件，如光電探測器和LED。我們將研究鈣鈦礦材料組成調整和納米線幾何尺寸優化來實現合理的器件結構設計，實現高性能。另外，我們將研究材料改性機制，以探測進一步提高材料和器件穩定性的方法。

16309018.label: Realisation of objectives
16309018.value: The objectives have been accomplished. We have developed two kinds of vapor-phase methods to fabricate large-area organometal halide-perovskite (perovskite) NW arrays: vapor-solid-solid reaction (VSSR) method and close-spaced vapor reaction (CSVR) method. Maximum 4-inch wafer-scale perovskite NW arrays have been successfully fabricated with excellent uniformity. The NW geometry can be precisely controlled with NWs diameter varying from ~ 500 nm to ~5 nm, where NWs with 5 nm diameters are considered as quantum wires (QWs). It benefits from the precise nanoengineering property of anodic alumina oxide (AAO) templates. After systematically study the degradation behavior of the obtained perovskite NW arrays and perovskite thin films under different ambient conditions, we have clarified the underlying degradation mechanism that is water and oxygen-induced self-sustaining and self-accelerating process. It can be significantly hindered by the AAO templates, which results in NWs stability improvement. One step further, we have grown perovskite NWs in hydrophobic AAO templates, which increases the water contact angle from 14.3o to 117.3o and hence further improves the NWs humidity stability. We have generalized our growth methods to various perovskite NWs, such as MAPbX3, MASnX3, FAPbX3, and CsPbX3 (X= Cl, Br, I, or mixed). Especially, we have successfully fabricated lead-free perovskite (MASnI3) NW arrays with good long-term stability, which reduces the toxicity issue of perovskite materials. We have studied the factors affecting optical properties of the fabricated perovskite NW arrays, such as NWs diameters and pitches. Specifically, perovskite NWs have higher photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) than thin film counterparts. And smaller diameter NWs, namely QWs, have much higher PLQY than large diameter NWs. Meanwhile, we have found that the NWs pitch significantly affects the light out-coupling efficiency. It has inspired us to finely tune and optimize the optical properties of NWs. We have also studied the physical reasons behind the high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of perovskite NWs over thin-film counterparts, which can be attributed to the higher materials crystallinity, AAO surface passivation, and quantum confinement effect. It has become a critical motivation for us to fabricate perovskite NW arrays-based high-performance optoelectronic devices. We have also successfully fabricated and characterized the integrated photodetector devices and full-color image sensor with the grown perovskite NW arrays.

16309018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309018.value: Our major findings can be summarized as: -We have utilized AAO templates to fabricate ultrahigh-density (∼1012 cm−2) vertical MAPbI3 NW arrays with controllable diameters from 250 nm down to 5.7 nm, via a VSSR method. We have found that quantum confinement, together with a nanophotonic effect, results in 130-fold substantial boost in PLQY for perovskite QWs versus thin-films. We have also discovered that the QWs have a low SRV of 18 cm/s which is comparable to state-of-the-art well passivated Si. -We have demonstrated the growth of large-area, highly-uniform, and crystalline perovskite QW arrays in hydrophobic AAO templates via a CSVR method. We have demonstrated the growth of various perovskite QWs with PL colors covering the whole visible range. They are found to have a PLQY of up to 92% and a PL lifetime (TPL50) of 5,644 hours. They have been further applied to large-area light-emitting diodes (LEDs) applications with good device performance. -We have demonstrated the fabrication of perovskite NWs array-based LEDs with a capillary-effect-assisted template method. We have found that the nanostructured device demonstrates 45% improvement of external quantum efficiency from 11% to 16% owing to substantial enhancement on device light extraction efficiency. We have also discovered that the nanostructured device possesses 3.89 times lifetime improvement due to effective template passivation. -We have fabricated an electrochemical eye with a hemispherical retina made of perovskite NWs mimicking the photoreceptors on a human retina. we have demonstrated the image-sensing function of our biomimetic device by reconstructing the optical patterns projected onto the device, which leads to biomimetic photosensing devices with high integration density. -We have developed a flexible resistive-random access memory (Re-RAM) with perovskite QWs as the switching matrix. The devices demonstrated a high ON/OFF ratio of ∼1E7 and an ultra-fast switching speed of ∼100 ps which is among the fastest in literature. The devices also possess a long retention time of over 2 years and record high endurance of ∼6 × 106 cycles for all perovskite Re-RAMs reported. We have also demonstrated an ultra-small cell effectively having 76.5 nm2 area for single bit storage, which also exhibits unique optical programmability among the low resistance states. -We have fabricated electrochemical metallization Re-RAMs based on different perovskite NWs array as the switching layer. Ultrafast switching speed (200 ps) for MAPbI3 NWs and ~7E9 s ultralong extrapolated retention time for MAPbCl3 NWs devices have been demonstrated.

16309018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309018.value: -We have found that the device performance still has room to improve, such as the external quantum efficiency and lifetime of LED devices. We have explored nanoengineering approach to improve the materials PLQY and stability. In the future, device structure optimization, such as carrier injection layers, can be explored to further improve the device performance. -In this project, we have successfully demonstrated perovskite NWs-based large-area LEDs with good uniformity. In the future, fabrication of LED pixel arrays can be further explored for display applications. -Here we have demonstrated perovskite NWs-based green color LEDs with good performance. We have also demonstrated various perovskite NWs with different PL colors. In the future, the fabrication of perovskite NWs-based blue and red color LEDs can be explored, towards full-color displays and lightings.

16309018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309018.value: In this project, we have explored the fabrication of large-area metal halide perovskite nanowires in nano-porous alumina templates with tunable geometry and composition. We have clarified the materials degradation mechanism, which has inspired us to utilize hydrophobic templates to significantly improve the nanowires stability in ambient environment. To reduce the toxicity of perovskites, we have explored the growth of lead-free perovskite NWs with much improved stability. We have systematically studied the optical properties of the grown perovskite nanowires and found the factors affecting the photoluminescence and light extraction efficiencies. We have also studied photocarrier dynamics inside NWs and discovered the physical mechanism for higher photoluminescence efficiency than thin-film counterparts. We have applied the obtained perovskite NWs into various optoelectronic applications, such as photodetectors, gray-scale and full-color image sensors, light-emitting diodes, and resistive random-access memories. Benefiting from the high crystal quality and nanophotonic effect of perovskite NWs, the performance of those optoelectronic devices has been largely improved, such as efficiency and operation lifetime. The results of the project help researchers in the field to obtain a better understanding of perovskite nanowires growth, physical and chemical properties, as well as achievement of high-performance devices that will have great impact on the optoelectronics.

16309218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309218.value: 疊層有機太陽能電池（OSC）由兩個串聯的子電池組成，因其可以擴大光吸收並顯著提高器件的開路電壓（VOC）而引起了很多研究的關注。理論計算預測，與單結對應物相比，理想串聯OSC的功率轉換效率（PCE）提高了約35％。傳統的基於富勒烯的疊層OSC具有有限的材料選擇，特別是在近紅外（NIR）區域，例如， 1000-1100納米，因為富勒烯具有弱吸收性能，並且開發低帶隙聚合物具有挑戰性，所述低帶隙聚合物可以吸收超過1000nm並且仍然可以實現高性能。結果，這些疊層OSC中的大多數對於前電池具有300-650nm的吸收，對於後電池具有~650-900nm的吸收。 然而，隨著非富勒烯受體（NFA）的快速發展，後電池的吸收可以擴展到1000-1100nm。因此，傳統的基於富勒烯的前電池材料（350-650nm的吸收）不再足以產生足以匹配NIR吸收反電池的光電流。這需要為下一代疊層OSC設計兩套全新的前後材料。 在該項目中，我們的目標是選擇或開發非富勒烯材料組，以構建有效的非富勒烯疊層OSC。首先，通過將具有高吸收係數的新型PDI基小分子受體與300-500 nm的高吸收係數和高性能中間帶隙聚合物（稱為P3TEA）相結合，設計出吸收範圍為300-750 nm的前電池。在400-750 nm處有強吸收。其次，將為背部電池設計吸收NIR的稠環NFA（覆蓋800-1050 nm）。接下來，將使用在750和950nm之間具有強吸收但在750nm以下可忽略的吸收的聚合物作為背部電池的供體，以最小化與前電池的光譜重疊。 這種疊層OSC系統可以實現高JSC（> 13 mA / cm2），因為兩個子電池的吸收範圍都比先前報導的系統更寬，而且VOCs（~1.7-1.8 V）高，因為P3TEA已經證明有創紀錄的VOC（> 1.1 V）。 遵循此設計規則，我們獲得了疊層OSC的初步結果，效率約為14％。鑑於我們以前的成功和有希望的初步結果，所提議的方法應該是可行的，並且如果充分探索，應該導致疊層OSC的效率在15-17％的範圍內。

Percentage achieved: 100% The growth of the internet of things (IoT) is creating a demand for convenient energy sources, like organic photovoltaics, to power various small IoT devices. We report a highly crystalline small molecular acceptor (named FCC-Cl) with an optical band gap of 1.71 eV suitable for indoor applications. The FCC-Cl neat film shows an intense absorption in the range of 450–720 nm, and a 41-nm bathochromic shift of absorption onset from solution to the film was observed, implying the strong intermolecular π-π stacking in the solid state. The important design rationale of FCC-Cl is the combination of a weak electron-donating core and a moderate electron-withdrawing end group, which leads to needed band gap and high crystallinity. The OPVs based on D18:FCC-Cl achieved a high external quantum efficiency up to 85% and a high fill factor of 80% due to the high absorption coefficient and strong crystallinity of FCC-Cl. It was also demonstrated that PM6:FCC-Cl-based devices can achieve high efficiencies over a wide range of active-layer thicknesses, which is a feature necessary for large-scale roll-to-roll printing processes. Objective2. Design back-cell materials with a target absorption range of 750-1100 nm and Objective3. Design novel recombination layer that does not require harsh post-treatments Percentage achieved: 100% Polymerization sites of small molecule acceptors (SMAs) play vital roles in determining device performance of all-polymer solar cells (all-PSCs). Different from our recent work about fluoro- and bromo- co-modified end group of IC-FBr (a mixture of IC-FBr1 and IC-FBr2), in the paper of Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 10137-10146, we synthesized and purified two regiospecific fluoro- and bromo- substituted end groups (IC-FBr-o & IC-FBr-m), which were then employed to construct two regio-regular polymer acceptors named PYF-T-o and PYF-T-m, respectively. In chloroform solution, PYF-T and PYF-T-o show comparable maximum absorption peaks centered at 798 and 800 nm, respectively, while PYF-T-m exhibits an obviously hypochromic absorption peak centered at 758 nm. In comparison with its isomeric counterparts named PYF-T-m with different conjugated coupling sites, PYF-T-o exhibits stronger and bathochromic absorption to achieve better photon harvesting. Strikingly, we observed a dramatic performance difference between the two isomeric polymer acceptors PYF-T-o and PYF-T-m. While devices based on PM6:PYF-T-o can yield power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 15.2 %, devices based on PM6:PYF-T-m only show poor efficiencies of 1.4 %. This work demonstrates the success of configuration-unique fluorinated end groups in designing high-performance regular polymer acceptors, which provides guidelines towards developing all-PSCs with better efficiencies. Objective4. Reduce voltage loss and increase Voc of the tandem OSC through the use of non-fullerene based active layers Side-chain engineering has been shown to be an important strategy to optimize Y-series nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs). Most previous reports were focusing on changing the branching positions and size of the alkyl side chains on Y6. In the paper of Energy Environ. Sci., 2021,14, 3469-3479, we investigate the influence of the orientation of side chains on the properties of NFAs and the performance of the organic solar cells (OSCs). Three isomeric NFAs named o-BTP-PhC6, m-BTP-PhC6, and p-BTP-PhC6 are designed by changing the substitution positions and thus orientations of the side chains attached to the central core. Our studies show that the optimal side-chain orientation can be achieved by the meta-positioned hexylphenyl group (of the m-BTP-PhC6 molecule), which introduces significant beneficial effects on optical absorption, intermolecular packing and phase separation of the NFAs. By pairing a donor polymer PTQ10 with m-BTP-PhC6, device efficiencies of 17.7% can be achieved, which is among the best values for PTQ10-based nonfullerene OSC devices so far. These results reveal that regulating side-chain orientations of Y-series NFAs is a promising strategy to achieve favorable morphology, and high charge mobility and solar cell performances.

16309218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309218.value: Good result has been obtained in this project. First, we report an acceptor-donor-acceptor (A-D-A)-type non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) named FCC-Cl (Figure 1A), using a fluorenedicyclopentathiophene core with TIC-Cl end groups (2-(2-chloro-6-oxo-5,6-dihydro 4Hcyclopenta[b]thiophen-4-ylidene)-malononitrile). This molecule exhibits an absorption onset of 725 nm with an optical band gap (Egopt) of 1.71 eV. The FCC-Cl acceptor can be combined with two reported donor polymers (D18 and PM6) and achieve efficiencies of above 13% under one-sun conditions. Furthermore, D18:FCC-Cl blends display several benefits: a high EQE of >85%, a matching absorption spectrum, a relatively low voltage loss, and a low extent of charge recombination. As a result, an impressive indoor PCE of 28.8% was achieved under a 2,600 K LED at 500 lux, which is one of the highest reported efficiencies for indoor OPVs. We also demonstrate that the performance of PM6:FCC-Cl-based devices is insensitive to active-layer thicknesses. The PCEs of the PM6:FCC-Cl-based devices were only reduced by 5% (from 27.9% to 26.5%) when the thickness of the active layer was increased from 100 to 300 nm. This is an imoprtant feature for the large-scale production of OPV devices. Our work provides effective OPV material-design guidelines for developing high-performance indoor OPV devices and proves the feasibility of practical applications for indoor OPVs. Second, two configurationally unique comonomers and the resultant regular polymer acceptors (PYF-T-o & PYF-T-m) were prepared and compared with a reported random polymer (PYF-T). When blended with PM6, morphology studies revealed that the PM6:PYF-T-o blend formed ordered interchain packing and suitable fiber-like phase separation relative to the PM6:PYF-T one, while the PM6:PYF-T-m blend suffers from oversized phase segregation. Consequently, the PM6:PYF-T-o all-PSC achieved the highest PCE of 15.2 %, with a VOC of 0.901 V and a remarkably enhanced JSC of 23.3 mA cm−2, which was superior to PM6:PYF-T (14.0 %) and PM6:PYF-T-m (1.40 %). Third, three isomeric NFAs named o-BTP-PhC6, m-BTP-PhC6, and p-BTP-PhC6 were synthesized by changing the side-chain substitution positions on the phenyl rings attached on the central core. Relative to o-BTP-PhC6 with the vertical orientation and p-BTP-PhC6 with the horizontal orientation, the hexyl chains of m-BTP-PhC6 show a “tilted” orientation. Because of this unique orientation, m-BTP-PhC6 exhibits the most ordered intermolecular packing among three isomers, resulting in the enhanced electron mobility. When blended with PTQ10, the PCE of the m-BTP-PhC6-based devices reached 17.7% with a VOC of 0.883 V, JSC of 25.3 mA cm−2, and FF of 79.3%, which is superior to those of the o-BTP-PhC6 (16.0%) and the p-BTP-PhC6-based ones (17.1%).

16309218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309218.value: 1. To date, the choice of polymer donors for tandem organic solar cells has been very limited. Common design of NFAs usually has low LUMO and HOMO levels. In order to match the energy levels of The NFA, the donor should have a low HOMO level to maintain good VOC of the device to improve performance. Therefore, the development of high-performance tandem organic solar cells requires the development of narrow band gap polymer donors with low HOMO levels. 2. Acceptors with "ADA", "A-π-D-π -a" and "A-D-A-D-A" molecular structures have been shown to reduce the band gap and redshift the absorption spectrum to the near-infrared region. So far, only a limited number of NFAs have been incorporated into tandem organic solar Cells. Therefore, the appropriate combination of NFA and matched donor can be used as back-cell materials, which could take the advantages of harvesting NIR solar photons for high efficiency tandem organic solar cells.

16309218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309218.value: In the past few years, the field of bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) organic solar cells (OSCs) has witnessed significant progress with power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) surpassing 18%. The tandem cell strategy is an effective way to simultaneously address issues like s the low charge mobility of organic materials, and furthermore, is probably well suited for OPV. First, the use of tandem cells would overcome the thickness constraint of single-junction cells due to the low mobility of organic materials because wide absorption could be achieved by stacking the active layers with complementary absorption. Moreover, tandem cells can take advantage of one of the most important features. In addition, benefiting from this, the thermalization and transmission loss can be reduced in the tandem cells.

16309418.value: 鈀基二氧化碳還原電催化劑

16309418.label: Project Objectives
16309418.value: To develop Pd-based defect-rich bimetallic nanocatalysts that have high activity and nearly 100% CO selectivity in the CO2 electrochemical reduction reaction. To correlate the activity and product selectivity with the structure and composition of catalysts and provide guidelines for developing more advanced and robust catalysts for CO2 reduction. 16309418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309418.value: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is one of the major greenhouse gases. Its continuously increasing concentration in the atmosphere has caused global temperatures to rise, leading to climate change. The electrochemical conversion of CO2 into value-added fuels (CO, CH4, C2H4, etc.) in an electrolyzer using excess renewable energy is a promising technology to both reduce the global carbon footprint and store renewable energy. The wide adaption of this technology, however, has been hindered by the unsatisfactory performance of catalysts due to their low catalytic activity, poor product selectivity, and limited lifetime. Among the products that can be generated via the electrochemical reduction of CO2, CO has received considerable attention, as it can be readily used as feedstock in the well-established Fischer–Tropsch process to generate various chemicals. The activity of the CO2 reduction and selectivity of CO in state-of-the-art electrocatalysts is too low to be considered for real applications. The proposed study will aim to develop Pd-based nanocatalysts, including nanowires and core-shell structures with a CO selectivity close to 100%. These nanostructures have a high density of structural and surface defects, on which the binding energies of CO2 and reaction intermediates are optimized. We will conduct a systematic study of the structural and composition effects on catalytic activity and product selectivity. In the proposed research, we will be able to detect reaction intermediates and their dynamic evolution during CO2 reduction using powerful surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy with an attenuated total reflection configuration. Combining experimental data and theoretical modeling results, we will evaluate the reaction mechanisms of CO2 reduction on various catalysts. 二氧化碳是一種主要的溫室氣體。其在大氣中的濃度日益增加，造成全球氣溫上升。利用可持續能源和電化學方法可將二氧化碳轉化為有價值的化學物質。但是這種技術受制於催化劑的活性、持久性及產物的選擇性。在所有的二氧化碳還原產物中，一氧化碳可以直接作為費-托反應的反應物而備受關注。但是現有的催化劑對於一氧化碳的選擇性和活性都偏低，不適合實際應用。本課題將致力於發展基於鈀的納米催化劑，包括納米線、核-殼等結構。這些催化劑有很多表面缺陷，有利於二氧化碳還原，對於一氧化碳等選擇性可達到接近100%。我們將系統地研究催化劑的結構、成分和活性、產物選擇性的關係。我們還將利用表面增強紅外光譜檢測反應過程中的活性中間產物，結合理論計算，提出合理的反應機理。

16309418.label: Realisation of objectives
16309418.value: 1. To develop Pd-based defect-rich bimetallic nanocatalysts that have high activity and nearly 100% CO selectivity in the CO2 electrochemical reduction reaction. This objective was fully achieved. We have developed two types of Pd-based bimetallic nanocatalysts, including defect-rich Pd-Au nanowires and Pd-Au core-shell nanoparticles. These nanocatalysts achieved a maximum CO faradaic efficiency of 94% to 97% in CO2 electrochemical reduction. The optimized Au-Pd core-shell nanoparticles can achieve a CO faradaic efficiency of 94.7% and catalyst mass activity of 99.8 A/gcatalyst simultaneously at 390 mV overpotential, which was among the top three records in literature reports. 2. To correlate the activity and product selectivity with the structure and composition of catalysts and provide guidelines for developing more advanced and robust catalysts for CO2 reduction. This objective was fully achieved. By using in situ infrared spectroscopy, we have successfully studied the adsorption behavior of reaction intermediates on the developed Pd-Au nanocatalysts, and uncovered how the core-shell structure, defective morphology, and composition affect their generation on the surface. A unique *CO adsorption site distribution determined CO2 reduction selectivity and activity mechanism was revealed, which is a useful guideline to the rational development of more advanced catalysts. 3. To propose reaction mechanisms of CO2 reduction by different catalysts by combining experimental and theoretical studies. This objective was fully achieved. By combining in situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculation, we have systematically studied CO2 reduction and the hydrogen evolution side reactions processes on the developed nanocatalysts. Through simulating the thermodynamic parameters of elementary steps and their dependence on the catalyst structure and composition, we successfully revealed the reaction mechanisms with molecular-level information provided. Please note that the purchase of the stirring hot plate budgeted in the original proposal (HKD5,000) was found to be unnecessary as the old one has been working well.

16309418.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309418.value: 1. A series of twisted and ultrafine Pd-Au nanowires with different compositions were successfully synthesized through the co-reduction of Na2PdCl4 and HAuCl4 precursors by NaBH4 with the presence of sodium citrate capping agent. Detailed characterizations demonstrated the presence of a large number of grain boundaries, and a unique structure with a Pd shell and Pd-Au alloy core in this material. In CO2 electrochemical reduction, the maximum faradaic efficiency of CO reached over 94%, and CO can even be generated at merely 90 mV of overpotential. The CO faradaic efficiency and partial current density on Pd-Au nanowires were both significantly higher than those of Pd nanoparticle and Pd nanowire counterparts. In situ infrared absorption spectroscopy demonstrated the twisted morphology can accelerate the CO2 activation, and the core-shell structure can increase the surface population of weakly adsorbed *CO and accelerate its desorption to form CO gas. This work revealed a unique *CO adsorption configuration determined selectivity and activity mechanism, and provided new directions in the development of more advanced CO2 reduction catalysts. (S. Zhu, et al., Advanced Energy Materials 2018, 8, 1802238) 2. A series of Pd-Au nanoparticles with different compositions were successfully synthesized through the co-reduction of Na2PdCl4 and HAuCl4 by oleylamine at 200 oC. The nanoparticles showed an average diameter of 7-8 nm and the size distributions were narrow. The nanoparticles were of core-shell structures with an atomically thin Pd shell and Pd-Au core. By adjusting the composition, the Pd shell thickness can be tuned. In CO2 electrochemical reduction, the maximum faradaic efficiency of CO reached 94% to 97% depending on the composition, and the optimized catalyst can achieve 94.7% faradaic efficiency and ~100 A/gcatalyst mass activity simultaneously toward CO production, which were among top records in this research area. Combined in situ infrared spectroscopy and theoretical calculations found the core-shell and alloy structure can facilitate CO2 activation and *CO desorption simultaneously by tuning the electronic and geometric structures of catalyst surfaces. (S. Zhu, et al., Journal of Materials Chemistry A 2019, 7, 16954-16961)

16309418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309418.value: The combination of Pd with other transition metal elements (e.g., Ag, Ni, Fe, etc.) is of great interest. Using the same methodology by incorporating in situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations to study mechanisms on other Pd-based nanocatalysts can provide more useful guidelines for the rational design of more advanced catalysts. In addition, the developed catalysts in this project can be put into laboratory-scale devices to evaluate their practical applications in CO2 reduction electrolyzers.

16309418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309418.value: In this project, several Pd-based bimetallic nanocatalysts, including defect-rich Pd-Au nanowires and Pd-Au core-shell nanoparticles are successfully developed through one-pot co-reduction methods. All the bimetallic nanocatalysts show a superior CO faradaic efficiency (94% - 97%) during CO2 electrochemical reduction reaction. In addition, the optimized Pd-Au core-shell nanoparticle can achieve a 94.7% CO faradaic efficiency and ~100 A/gcatalyst mass activity simultaneously, which is among the top three records in the research field. Through combining in situ infrared spectroscopy and theoretical calculations, the CO2 reduction mechanisms are systematically studied. A unique *CO intermediate adsorption configuration determined selectivity and activity mechanism is reported for the first time, which can be tuned by the catalyst structure and composition. These findings are very important guidelines for the rational development of more advanced CO2 reduction catalysts.

16309518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309518.value: Partial differential equations describe many phenomena in nature such as light, wave, sound, heat, rigid body motion, and fluid dynamics. In this proposal we will study several fundamental models in fluid dynamics such as the incompressible Euler equations, Navier-Stokes equations and surface quasi-geostrophic equations. The mains questions we plan to address concern the regularity of the solution operators in different functional spaces, and sharp regularity criteria involving only one component of the velocity vector. Progress on these questions may lead to deeper understanding of the delicate nonlinear and nonlocal dynamics in these equations, and hopefully one can unravel some deep mystery relating various notions such as weak and strong solutions. 偏微分方程作为一个强有力的工具可以描述很多美妙的自然现象比如声，光，电， 波，热，固体力学以及流体力学。在这个研究中我们考虑几个重要的流体力学方程 比如欧拉方程，纳维尔斯托克斯方程等等的解算子的在不同函数空间的正则性问题。 同时我们考虑速度向量场的单方向正则性准则问题。对于这些基本问题的研究有助 于深刻理解非线性非局部动力学之间的微妙联系，以及揭示相关弱解和强解的 深刻联系。

16309518.label: Realisation of objectives
16309518.value: This project was initially awarded to Prof. Dong Li. However, following his departure from Hong Kong in August 2021, I took over this project. Prof. Li continued working on the project towards its original objectives, and along with his collaborators, published several papers addressing the regularity of Euler and Navier-Stokes equations and related problems. 1. We have shown the strong Ill-Posedness of the 3D Incompressible Euler Equation in Borderline Spaces. 2. We have systematically investigated the property of frequency-localized operators and the limitations of the powerful Bernstein inequalities which a play important role in fluid equations such as fractional Navier-Stokes and quasi-geostrophic equations. 3. We developed a new approach to the construction of steady-state weak solutions to fluid equations. The method unravels some new understanding of the solution operator of nonlcal nonlinear transport equations in low regularity spaces. 4. We developed several new delicate regularity estimates for the pressure term in the incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes in various Besov and Sobolev type spaces. Several original counterexamples are constructed using harmonic analysis tools. 5. We consider a two dimensional molecular beam epitaxy equation with biharmonic dissipation. We give an improved gradient bound, which removes the logarithmic dependence on the dissipation coefficient previously shown in the literature. 6. We consider a one dimensional nonlocal transport equation and its natural multi-dimensional analogues. We also proved several weighted inequalities for the Hilbert transform and various nonlinear versions. 7. We give the first rigorous result for the semi-implicit discretization of the Cahn-Hilliard equation with singular potentials. In addition, Prof. Li and I investigated phase retrieval, a research area of our common interests and expertise. Jointly with other collaborators, we published three papers on this research topic: 1. We proposed three novel nonconvex optimization models for the numerical solution of phase retrieval. Numerical experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the new models. 2. Under the Gaussian random model, we analyzed the geometric landscape of the proposed nonconvex optimizations. We have found that, under the optimal sampling complexity, our new models have good landscapes --- all local minima are global, and all other critical points are strictly saddle. Due to the pandemic, no visitor is coming to Hong Kong, and there is no traveling to other universities for collaboration and research purposes. So all the general expenses budget is spent on hiring RAs or postdocs.

16309518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309518.value: In this project, we have developed several new approaches to studying the regularity of Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. We hope that these approaches can be integrated into a new theoretical framework for investigating the regularity of solution operators for general nonlinear partial differential equations with nonlocal interactions. The newly developed harmonic analysis tools can be exploited and further strengthened in several related hydrodynamical models arising from geostrophical equations and turbulence. Similarly, regarding our work on phase retrieval, the new techniques we have developed hold promise for analyzing nonconvex optimization landscapes for phase retrieval in more realistic settings, such as Fourier measurements and sparse phase retrieval. We believe that these techniques have the potential to advance the field of phase retrieval and lead to new insights into the fundamental properties of this important problem. The PI plans to investigate these directions in future research.

16309518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309518.value: This research project aims to understand how fluids, like air and water, flow and behave. Euler and Navier-Stokes equations are mathematical models representing fluid motion, and their regularity refers to the smoothness or predictability of their solutions. Solving these equations is essential for predicting weather, designing vehicles, and understanding natural phenomena, but their behavior is notoriously complex. This project seeks to unravel their mysteries, potentially leading to more accurate predictions and improved engineering designs in various fields.

16309718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309718.value: Superconductors can conduct electricity with zero resistance. In the beginning of last century, many superconductors, such as mercury, aluminum and niobium were discovered. Almost fifty years since the experimental discovery of superconductors, it was found that theoretically the superconducting states are realised when electrons with opposite spins are glued together to form Cooper pairs. Cooper pairings can be broken by several effects, such as thermal effects and magnetic fields. One of the effects of magnetic fields is to align electron spins to the same direction and break the Cooper pairs. Very recently, it was shown that an atomically thick transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) layer, such as MoS2 and NbS2, can be superconducting. More surprisingly, it was shown in a collaboration between the PI and experimentalists that monolayer TMD can survive extremely high magnetic fields and remain superconducting. We explained that this is due to a special type of spin-orbit coupling which protects the spins of Cooper pairs from being changed by external magnetic fields. We called such monolayer TMD Ising superconductors. In explaining the superconducting phenomenon at high magnetic fields, we assumed that the pairing between electrons is conventional. Surprisingly, in a very recent experiment in Switzerland, it was shown that gated MoS2 are gapless superconductors. This is similar to the case of high-temperature superconductors discovered in the 1980s which are the so-called d-wave superconductors. However, the lattice structure does not allow ordinary d-wave superconductivity to appear. In this proposal, we suggest that gated MoS2 can be a special (spin-triplet) gapless superconductor which is even more exotic than d-wave superconductors. The superconducting TMD described above has the so-called 2H structure. Interestingly, TMD materials have several chemically stable forms. Another stable structure is called the 1T-structure. Among all the 1T-structure TMDs, TaS2 is special. According to band theory, 1T-TaS2 is metallic. However, TaS2 becomes insulating at low temperatures due to electron-electron interaction. In a recent work, the PI and collaborators proposed that 1T-TaS2 is a quantum spin liquid state by analysing past experimental data. However, spin liquids can be classified as gapped or gapless. One question remains. Is the spin liquid phase gapped or gapless? The second objective of this proposal is to study the spin property of 1T-TaS2. More interestingly, 1T-TaS2 becomes superconducting under gating or pressure and the system behaves in a similar manner as high-temperature superconductors. The third objective of this proposal is to study the novel superconducting properties of 1T-TaS2. 超導體可以實現零電阻導電。在上個世紀初，人們發現了許多超導體，如汞，鋁和鈮。在實驗發現超導體近50年後，人们意識到理論上當具有相反自旋的電子粘在一起形成庫柏對時會形成超導態。而庫柏對可以通過熱效應和磁場等幾種效應來破壞。磁場的作用之一是使電子自旋指向相同的方向並破壞庫柏對。 最近，實驗表明原子級厚度的過渡金屬二硫族化物（transition metal dichalcogenide, TMD）層，例如二硫化鉬(MoS 2) 和二硫化鈮（NbS 2），可以是超導的。更令人驚訝的是，項目負責人與實驗家合作研究表明，單層TMD可以承受極高的磁場並保持超導。我們解釋這是由於一種特殊類型的自旋軌道耦合保護庫柏對的自旋不被外部磁場改變。我們稱單層TMD 為 Ising 超導體。 在解釋高磁場下的超導現象時，我們假設電子之間的配對是常規的。令人驚訝的是，在瑞士實驗家最近進行的一項實驗中，結果表明門控MoS2是無間隙超導體。這類似於20世紀80年代發現的高溫超導體，即所謂的d波超導體。然而，晶格結構不允許出現普通的d波超導性。在本份提議中，我們認為門控MoS2可以是一種特殊的（自旋三重態）無間隙超導體，它比d波超導體更具奇異性。 上述超導TMD具有所謂的2H結構。有趣的是，TMD材料具有幾種穩定的化學形式。另一種穩定的結構稱為1T結構。在所有1T結構TMD中，TaS2是特殊的。根據能帶理論，1T-TaS2是金屬。然而，由於電子間的相互作用，TaS2在低溫下變成絕緣體。在最近的一項工作中，項目負責人和合作者通過研究過去的實驗數據，把出1T-TaS2是所謂的自旋液態。然而，自旋液體可以分類為有間隙或無間隙。1T-TaS2的自旋液相是否有間隙或無間隙？這是一個疑問。該提議的第二個目的是研究1T-TaS2的這種自旋特性。

16309718.value: We thank the support of RGC which allowed us to explore topics related to the objectives of this GRF proposal which are related to the study of transition metal dichalcogenides. Item 1 and Item 2 below addressed the question posted in Objective 1 and Item 3 below addressed the question posted in Objective 2. This exploration resulted in the following publications: 1. Spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductivity in topological monolayer WTe, Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 107001 (2020). In this work, we predicted a few novel properties of superconducting WTe2 and related transition metal chalcogenide in the same class such as superconducting MoS2 and WS2. We predicted the enhancement of in-plane upper critical field (Hc2) beyond the Pauli limi and the anisotropic Hc2. We called these superconductor spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductors. Importantly, we discussed the possible spin-triplet pairing in these superconductors. The spin-triplet pairing is indeed needed to explain the excessive enhancement of Hc2 in the experiments. Our prediction is verified in a very recent experiment as shown below ( Nature Physics 2022). This work addressed the question posted in Objective 1 of the proposal. 2. 16309818.label: Realisation of objectives
16309818.value: The goal of this project is to investigate self-assembling peptides for the delivery of multiple types of therapeutics against tumor cells. To this end, we have first confirmed the potential of a 22- amino acid self-assembling peptide sequence, termed H4, for the co-delivery of plasmid DNA and paclitaxel. While capable of co-assembling with plasmid DNA and delivering DNA to cells for transfection, the same peptide sequence was proven to form nanostructures with paclitaxel (PTX). A spectrum of morphology, ranging from long filaments to nanospheres, could be obtained by varying the peptide to PTX ratio. Strong presence of beta-sheets were found in peptide-PTX elements, in contrast with the more disordered peptide conformation in the nanospheres. While both structures displayed acid-sensitive release, the structural difference appeared to influence the release profile of PTX. Prominent uptake by breast cancer cells (MDA-231 and MCF-7) was observed for both types of peptide-PTX nanostructures. The IC50 against cancer cells after 72h of incubation in ascending order was PTX < peptide-PTX filaments< peptide-PTX nanospheres. Despite the higher IC50 value, it was evident from confocal microscopy that the nanostructures served as intracellular depots of PTX, thus prolonged efficacy against cancer cells was expected by delivering PTX with nanostructures. To further improve the transfection efficiency from the peptide-DNA co-assembled nanostructures, the peptide sequence has been further optimized by incorporating additional functional peptides modules. A fusogenic peptide, L17E, was attached the nanodisks formed by H4 peptides prior the co-assembly with plasmid DNA. The modification enhanced the endosomal escape and increased the transfection efficiency. A modular approach was taken to systematically generate a small library of oligopeptides designed for DNA delivery. The screening effort led to a 26-amino acid sequence, named H10, which was found to be effective for transfection in serum-containing medium and attained transfection efficiency higher than commercially available lipid-based transfection reagent. In the last part of this project, the investigation was expanded to mRNA delivery. H10 and a variation of H10 (with the removal of nuclear localization sequence) were found to be effective for mRNA transfection on a panel of cell lines. The stability of peptide-mRNA structures was further optimized, by the pre-incubation with salt, which led to a fluid-like micron-sized assemblies with superior transfection efficiency.

16309818.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309818.value: 1) The ability of self-assembling peptide sequence (H4) to form tunable nanostructures with chemotherapeutic drug paclitaxel (PTX) was confirmed. Such nanostructures could replace conventional surfactant to form a depot of poorly soluble PTX for intracellular delivery. 2) The peptide sequence (H4) has been further optimized to enhance the ability for DNA transfection, in particular, by enhancing the endosomal escape via the modification by fusogenic peptide L17E 3) The peptide sequence has been further updated to incorporate additional modules (e.g. improved acid-sensitivity and redox-sensitivity). The new peptide (H10 and its variation) was found to be effective for mRNA delivery, thus expanding the spectrum of anti-cancer therapeutic agents to be delivered by the co-assembly with peptides. The research outputs of this project include 4 journal papers (3 published and 1 accepted), 1 conference paper, 1 patent and 3 manuscripts (under preparation).

16309818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309818.value: Animal study is warranted to demonstrate the efficacy of the co-delivery of multiple anti-tumor agents via their co-assembly with designer oligopeptides. This requires the selection of an animal tumor model, and the corresponding choice of DNA and mRNA targets.

16309818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309818.value: We have demonstrated that short peptide sequences are capable of co-assembly with multiple therapeutic modalities, including chemotherapeutic drug paclitaxel, plasmid DNA, and mRNA molecules. The co-assemblies enabled effective delivery to cancer cells, creating prolonged depot of chemotherapeutic drug on one hand, and providing non-viral transfection by nucleic acid on the other. The same peptide vehicles therefore have the potential to serve as a versatile platform to deliver combination anti-tumor therapy.

16309918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309918.value: Organic light emitting diode (OLED) is a premium display technology for a wide range of consumer electronics applications, such as cell phones and high-definition televisions. However, the cost of OLED displays remains high due to the high cost associated with the deposition and patterning of organic thin films in manufacturing such displays. This proposal aims to develop an alternative deposition and patterning method (close-space sublimation or CSS) as a cost-effective means of fabricating full-color, high-resolution OLED displays. To achieve this goal, which has the potential to transform the OLED industry, a detailed investigation of the CSS method will be carried out, and its utility in the deposition and patterning of RGB emitters will be systematically assessed. 有機發光二極管（Organic light-emitting diode，OLED）作為一項先進顯示技術，如今被廣泛用於智能手機以及高清電視等消費電子產品。但是目前OLED顯示屏生產過程中涉及昂貴的真空熱蒸發技術和圖案化步驟，推高其製作成本。本研究計劃的目的是研發一項低成本的熱蒸發圖案化技術冀望替代目前的生產方法。該技術將以近距離升華（close-space sublimation，CSS）為理論基礎，務求實現全彩OLED器件的高性價比製備。本研究將探索近距離升華成膜過程，開發相關的真空組件以及篩選適合CSS過程的發光材料。

16309918.label: Realisation of objectives
16309918.value: After three years of research, both objectives of this project have been achieved fully. The specific methodology and experiments conducted to realize the objectives are detailed below. To realize the first objective, we have characterized the CSS profile of a wide range of OLED materials, particularly those used for the emitting layer (EML), as a function of donor temperature and established the correlation between the molecular structure of materials and evaporation temperature of donor films. All tested materials showed drastically reduced evaporation temperature in CSS compared to their evaporation from bulk using vacuum thermal evaporation (VTE) sources. Most donor films can be evaporated below 200 degrees Celsius, representing a decrease of as much as 50% from the bulk. The decreased evaporation temperature in CSS dramatically reduces the thermal stress on the donor films and is particularly advantageous for depositing the EML. Based on the established CSS profiles, we identified several host-dopant pairs with matching evaporation characteristics to yield well-doped EMLs. TOF-SIMS analysis revealed that the host-dopant composition can be further fine-tuned to achieve EMLs with uniform or gradient dopant distributions. We also discovered that the efficiency and lifetime of CSS-deposited devices were significantly affected by the exposure of the donor films to ambient. Hydrophobic treatment and in-situ baking of the silicon donor substrate before donor film deposition effectively eliminated the adsorbed moisture on the donor surface, resulting in a substantial improvement in the device performance. An in-situ donor preparation was demonstrated to achieve a long-lasting OLED device fabricated by CSS. Under optimized CSS conditions, we successfully fabricated blue, green, and red OLED devices with CSS-deposited EMLs at low temperatures. These devices exhibited comparable efficiencies and lifetimes as reference devices made by conventional VTE methods, validating the applicability of CSS to OLED fabrication. In pursuit of the second objective, we studied the thin-film morphology, photoluminescence (PL), and transport properties of CSS-deposited films under various CSS conditions using model materials and devices. The CSS-deposited film of NPB, an archetypical OLED material, exhibits morphological characteristics comparable to the reference film deposited by VTE under various evaporation rates and donor-substrate spacings. The PL of emitting layers with a host-dopant composition is mainly determined by the sublimation characteristics of materials. Host and dopant materials with similar evaporation temperatures in CSS tend to form well-doped EMLs with PL intensities comparable to VTE-deposited references. On the other hand, a donor film comprising host and dopant materials of largely different evaporation temperatures usually forms segregated EMLs of little to no PL due to concentration quenching of the dopant. The co-evaporability of a given host-dopant pair in CSS is not affected by the processing time (from 10 ms to 1 min) or the donor film’s structure (mixed or stacked). The transport property of CSS-deposited films is greatly influenced by donor film exposure to ambient. An NPB hole transport layer deposited by a donor film exposed to atmospheric conditions increases the driving voltage of a blue OLED device by 2.5 V at 60 mA/cm2. The device using exposed donor films also saw a faster voltage rise during operation compared to devices using donor films prepared in-situ. A similar phenomenon was also observed in CSS-deposited EMLs. Our study suggests that evaporation characteristic matching between the host and dopant and in-situ donor film preparation are the two key film growth factors crucial to the performance of CSS-deposited OLEDs.

16309918.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309918.value: 1. CSS is an efficient and effective thin-film deposition method for fabricating OLED devices. RGB OLED devices with CSS-deposited EMLs showed comparable performances to reference devices made by conventional VTE methods. 2. CSS drastically reduced the evaporation temperature of organic donor films compared to their evaporation from bulk in a conventional point source. The study of donor films’ evaporation behavior revealed that materials with lower molecular weight and weaker intermolecular interactions tend to have lower evaporation temperatures in CSS. Furthermore, we also demonstrated that CSS could be used to determine the enthalpy of sublimation for organic thin films. 3. The co-evaporability of the host and dopant from the donor film is crucial to the efficiencies of OLED devices. Host and dopant combinations with matching evaporation characteristics in CSS produce a well-doped emitting layer with high electroluminescent efficiencies. Some host-dopant pairs produce gradient-doped emitting layers, a feat hard to realize via conventional vacuum deposition methods. 4. The lifetime of CSS-deposited devices is significantly reduced by the exposure of donor films to ambient and residual contaminants in vacuum chambers. Physio-adsorbed moistures on the donor substrate and trace halogenated organics desorbed from the chamber interior are identified as two leading causes of device degradation. By implementing in-situ donor preparation and chamber interior passivation, the lifetime of CSS-deposited OLEDs was greatly improved and comparable to VTE-deposited references. Other remarks: The expenses of the conference we attended in 2019 were covered by other sources of funding since we wanted to save the conference fund in this project for potential conferences in the future. Unfortunately, the COVID-19 pandemic hit soon after and significantly affected the execution of this project and our ability to travel abroad. We then used the conference budget to cover other expenses in the project, such as manpower and consumables.

16309918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309918.value: 1. Within the CSS process time (10 ms to 1 min) investigated in this project, host and dopant materials need to have similar evaporation temperatures to yield a well-doped film. This requirement, however, greatly limits the choice of materials. We will investigate CSS in time scales shorter than 10 ms, aiming to achieve ultra-fast evaporations that could co-deposit materials regardless of their evaporation temperature and form well-doped EMLs. To realize faster CSS process, we will develop freestanding silicon nitride membranes with a thickness of one micron or less as the donor substrate. The reduced thickness will result in extremely low thermal mass and faster donor temperature rises in CSS. 2. State-of-the-art blue OLED devices often use co-hosts or assist dopants in the emitting layer, requiring co-deposition of three or four materials. This requirement is very difficult to realize by linear sources in mass production but could be readily achievable by CSS regardless of the substrate size. We will develop donor films with stacked structures for depositing ternary and quaternary emitting layers. 3. We will explore using CSS with a high-resolution shadow mask for patterning RGB side-by-side pixel arrays.

16309918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309918.value: Close-space sublimation (CSS) is a promising thin-film deposition method for fabricating organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display panels. CSS can potentially lower the production cost of OLED display panels, currently manufactured by conventional vacuum thermal deposition (VTE), which is a slow thin-film deposition process and requires expensive capital equipment of large footprint. CSS presents numerous advantages over conventional VTE, such as high material utilization, short process time, low evaporation temperatures, smaller deposition equipment footprint and less downtime for deposition chamber maintenance. This project investigated the evaporation characteristics of key OLED materials, particularly those used for the emitting layer (EML), under various CSS conditions and identified process parameters crucial to the efficiency and lifetime of CSS-deposited OLED devices. Under optimized CSS conditions, we successfully fabricated blue, green, and red OLED devices with CSS-deposited EMLs that exhibited comparable efficiencies and lifetimes as reference devices made by conventional methods, validating the applicability of CSS to OLED fabrication.

16500018.label: Project Objectives
16500018.value: The first objective of our project is to develop and fully solve a formal theoretical model to study the practice of referral to medical labs and the medical labs' practice of sending kickbacks to the referring doctors. By exploring extensions and comparative statics of the model, we would draw conclusion on the effects of feasibility of kickbacks on the laboratories', the doctor's and the patient's payoffs. Do doctors and the laboratories necessarily earn higher profits in equilibrium when kickbacks are allowed? By considering different levels of consumer awareness, we study how kickbacks may impact the market outcome differently depending on whether consumers are aware or not aware of the kickbacks? Our analysis also allows us to access the effectiveness of anti-kickback law and characterize the optimal anti-kickback law. By comparing with an alternative model of kickbacks from drug companies to doctors, we can analyze how different types of kickbacks may impact the market outcome differently.

16500018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500018.value: In the relationship between the doctor and the medical laboratory, both the doctor and the medical laboratory are sellers of services as well as information intermediaries. They're both sellers because the doctor sells treatments and the medical laboratories sell laboratory tests. They are both information intermediaries because only the doctor knows whether it is cost effective to refer a patient to the laboratory and the laboratory test improves the accuracy of the doctor's diagnosis and makes the doctor's diagnosis verifiable, reducing the information asymmetry between the doctor and the patient. We study doctors' incentives to over- and under-prescribe laboratory tests, and investigate how the incentives are compounded by the kickbacks doctors receive from medical laboratories. We examines how these kickbacks impact the doctor and other players' payoffs. We also examine how the effects of kickbacks differ depending on consumers' awareness of the kickbacks. Finally, we look at how kickbacks from drug companies impact the doctor' behavior differently from the kickbacks from medical laboratories. 在醫生和醫學實驗室的關係中，醫生和實驗室都同時扮演著服務的銷售者和信息中介的角色。 他們都是服務的銷售者：醫生銷售的是醫療服務而實驗室銷售的是醫學檢驗服務。他們都是信息中介，因為只有醫生了解真實成本，知道把病人轉到實驗室是否能節約成本，而實驗室檢驗結果提高了醫生診斷的準確性，驗證了醫生診斷的正誤，從而減少了醫生與病人之間的信息不對稱。我們研究了醫生過量轉診病人到實驗室以及轉診不足的動機，並探討了醫生從實驗室獲得回扣是如何使這些動機複雜化的。我們分析了回扣是如何影響醫生及其他利益相關方的收益，並研究了病人對於回扣的認知怎樣改變回扣的這些影響。最後，我們分析了製藥公司的回扣與醫學實驗室的回扣對醫生行為的影響有何不同。

16500018.label: Realisation of objectives
16500018.value: We have accomplished in full all the last stated project objectives. 1. We have developed and fully solved a formal theoretical model to study the practice of referral to medical labs and the medical labs' practice of sending kickbacks to the referring doctors. 2. We show that the doctor does not necessarily earn a higher profit in equilibrium when kickbacks are allowed. In fact, we should that when the cost of the lab test is not high, in equilibrium, the doctor is always truthful. In terms of profits for labs, since we study a setting with competitive labs, their profits are zero whether kickbacks are allowed or not. 3. By considering different levels of consumer awareness, we show that kickbacks impact the market outcome differently depending on whether consumers are aware or not aware of the kickbacks. We should that the most efficient outcome is achieved when an intermediate fraction of consumers are aware. 4. To assess the effectiveness of anti-kickback law and characterize the optimal anti-kickback law, note that positive kickbacks raise the acceptance rate of lab tests in equilibrium, resulting in more serious-problem patients being treated. At the same time, the percentage of the minor problem being treated may decrease when the doctor cheats on the severity of the problem. Some costs are also wasted on the wrong tests and unnecessary tests. More patients being treated means more cost is wasted. These effects have the opposite impact on social welfare. Assuming that the cost of lab test is small, kickback sufﬁciently alleviates the problem of under-provision of lab test and treatment, banning kickback aggravates the problem of underproduction and hurt social welfare. In that case, it is optimal not to ban kickbacks. 5. As stated in the progress report, given that substantial work has been done, we didn't develop a different model and write a second paper to accomplish Objective 5. Instead, we only discuss how to do that in our paper's discussion.

16500018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500018.value: This paper considers a market of healthcare services. Independent laboratories are prevalent, and they are an integral part of many medical services. We study the patient-doctor-laboratory relationship in a setting where competitive laboratories can pay the doctor kickbacks to encourage him to prescribe inappropriate or unnecessary laboratory tests. While both laboratories' briberies and inappropriate prescriptions are not observable, some patients are aware of the possibility that such actions may be taken while some patients are not aware of such possibility. We find that aware patients reject the doctor's recommendations with a positive probability to protect themselves against overcharging. When more patients become aware, in response to the higher rejection rate, the doctor charges smaller kickbacks and induces a higher acceptance rate of lab tests. The paper finds that banning kickbacks can hurt social welfare when under-provision of health services is severe. A moderate level of patient awareness can be optimal for social welfare.

16500018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500018.value: The main model concerns kickbacks medical laboratories send the doctors who may referrals. Studying of kickbacks paid by specialists to general practitioners or by pharmaceutical companies to doctors are also important to study. We may also analyze kickbacks within the financial industry.

16500118.label: Project Objectives
16500118.value: To confirm a preliminary finding of the PI and his co-author. The finding is that the stock market reaction at the announcement of a proposed merger and acquisition (M&A) deal has moderate power in forecasting the probability of impairment and poor power in forecasting the magnitude of impairment. If confirmed, the study will contribute to the literature on the measurement of deal quality. Once the above finding is confirmed, to answer the natural question that then arises. Which institutional investors – mutual funds or hedge funds or some other types – are better at this long-term prediction? If answered, the study will contribute to the literature on institutional investor heterogeneity. To study whether regulators, when approving proposals by firms for (M&A) deals, should put less weight on the market reaction at the date of the announcement and more weight on the order flows of certain institutions. If answered, the study will contribute to the public policy literature on M&A approvals. To study whether the managers of acquirers and their targets about to complete a deal should care less about the stock market reaction to the deal and care more how some of their institutional shareholders trade at the time of deal completion. If answered, the study will contribute to the literature on corporate governance. To create a database of firm impairments and link it directly, as much as we can, to the original merger.

16500118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500118.value: Preliminary research conducted by the PI and his co-author shows that the stock market reaction at the announcement of a proposed merger and acquisition (M&A) deal has moderate power in forecasting the probability of impairment and poor power in forecasting the magnitude of impairment. The natural question then arises: which institutional investors – mutual funds or hedge funds or some other types – are better at this long-term prediction? This research question is important because a fundamental issue in M&A transactions is the measurement of value added in a deal. The stock market reaction at the announcement of a proposed M&A deal, which in finance is almost universally accepted as a measure of the quality of a deal for good reasons, may be an under-reaction or an over-reaction. If so, regulators – who, when evaluating proposals from firms for mergers or acquisitions – should put less weight on the market reaction at the date of the announcement and more weight on the order flows of certain institutions. If so, the managers of acquirers and their targets about to complete a deal should care less about the stock market reaction to the deal, and care more how some of their institutional shareholders trade at the time of deal completion. An important aspect of our study is our measure of long-term value added in a deal outcome. We have utilized an ex-post realized measure of deal outcome, the write-down of acquisition goodwill, to define deal failure. This seems intuitive because goodwill is the excess of the purchase price less the fair value of the target’s identifiable net assets, i.e. current assets, property, plant and equipment, patents and so on. As goodwill impairments may arise as a result of unrealized or overestimated synergies or growth expectations, or because of industry or economy-wide negative shocks affecting the target business or the business as a whole, goodwill impairment events are an ideal variable for measuring deal outcomes. 主研究者和他的共同作者進行的初步研究表明，股票市場在宣布擬議的併購交易時的反應對於預測減值概率具備穩健的檢定力，但對於減值幅度的預測則檢定力不足。自然地人們會問：哪個機構投資者 - 共同基金或對沖基金或其他類型 - 在這個長期預測中會更好？ 本項研究課題很重要的原因是，併購交易中的一個基本問題是衡量交易中的附加值。在宣佈擬議的併購交易時的股票市場的反應（在金融業中幾乎被普遍接受為衡量交易質量的一個標準）可能是反應不足或反應過度。如果是這樣，監管機構在評估公司提出的兼併或收購方案時，應該減少公告發布之日的市場反應的權重，並且更加重視某些機構的交易訂單流量。如果是這樣，收購方的經理及其即將完成交易的目標應該更少關注股市對交易的反應，並更關心機構股東在併購完成時是如何交易。 我們研究中的一個重要方面是衡量併購交易結果中的長期增值。我們利用事後實現的交易結果作為衡量標準，即收購商譽的減值來定義交易失敗。這似乎是直觀的，因為商譽是指購買價格減去併購目標可識別淨資產（即流動資產，固定資產，專利等）的公允價值。由於未實現或過高估計的協同效應或增長預期，行業或者整體經濟中影響併購目標業務或整體業務的負面衝擊，都可能使商譽發生減值。因此商譽減值事件是衡量交易結果的理想變量。

16500118.value: Objective 5 was 100% achieved. We created a database of firm impairments and linked it directly to the original merger in the period 2003-2013. Of 1967 deals, 600 were potentially impaired. After screening for missing data, our final sample was 1553 deals, of which 355 were impaired.
