16506018.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506018.value: We have investigated the joint evolution of SDF's across 10 developed economies. For this purpose we have modeled SDF's as per the LRV model of Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan (JFE'2014). Using exchange rate data, we have found that a major structural break in exchange rates, and hence SDF's, was observed at the end of the year 2005. This is a novel finding which distinguishes our results from previous related studies that typically see the global financial crisis of 2008 as the watershed event. Therefore, the structural breaks in 2005 that we find present a new challenge to currency research. We find support for a common framework for understanding of the reversals in several currency puzzles that have been documented recently, and make a first step towards rigorous modeling of these changes in the currency market. The key element in this framework is the interplay between global and local currency risk factors, which we uncover using the SDF's within the LRV model. We show that these reversals/changes can be explained by a diminishing impact of a global risk factor and an increasing role for local factors. Specifically for the U.S., such a local factor can be the oil price. We also find that the relations between exchange rates and the oil price on one hand, and inflation, real interest rates and economic growth on the other change also change around the end of 2005. Overall, our findings indicate that the observed changes in several currency market puzzles reflect a concurrent realignment among various macroeconomic variables in multiple economies. The findings in this project have been incorporated is my current working paper "Currency Puzzles and the Oil Connection". It has been presented at a few conferences and submitted to one top-level journal in finance (the Journal of Finance), but was rejected there.

16506018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16506018.value: The key element that is missing from our analysis is a rigorous structural model that ties together all our findings. Accommodating these findings will require various departures from the parsimony of the LRV model. For example, some links between OIL, interest rates, and inflation (and possibly one of the global factors) can be formalized following Backus et al. (2013), who explain the forward premium puzzle relying on a Taylor rule for the nominal interest rates, where inflation arises endogenously in equilibrium. Such a link to U.S. monetary policy and its global spillovers can be key in addressing the challenging interplay between local and global risks that are examined in this project. This is a challenging direction for future research which I am planning to explore in the coming years.

16506018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506018.value: Several long-standing currency puzzles have been reversed in recent years, including the forward premium puzzle (FPP), carry trade profitability, and the exchange rate ``disconnect''. FPP refers to the stylized fact that currencies with high interest rate do not tend to depreciate (which would offset the interest rate gains of a currency investor and thus conform to a standard notion of market efficiency), but in fact appreciate. The carry trade puzzle is that simple currency trades that exploit interest rate differentials have been profitable over many decades. The "disconnect" puzzle is that currency returns do not seem to be related to economic fundamentals, which is prescribed by most of the classic exchange rate models. We provide a common framework for understanding these reversals, which have been documented recently in the currency literature. Our approach relies on the structural breaks that we find in currency returns in 2005, and on a concurrent shift in the relative importance of global and local currency risk factors. We associate this shift with the growth in the U.S. oil sector, stronger impact of the oil price on U.S. inflation, and weaker link between the real interest rates in the U.S. and other advanced economies since 2005.

16600218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600218.value: School segregation, as a result of children from different socioeconomic backgrounds attending different schools, not only separates children but also leaves disadvantaged ones in inferior schools, generating great educational inequality. The literature generally reveals a positive association between school segregation and residential segregation, as where children study is largely determined by where they live. To break this education-location link, many countries have adopted school choice policies that allow children to choose schools outside their neighborhoods. However, Hong Kong presents a particularly interesting case where the expansion of school choice may have elevated, instead of reduced, socioeconomic segregation between schools. We suspect this could be because upper-middle-class parents have been more committed to and more capable of sending their children to high-performing schools concentrated in certain areas. This project will directly examine this research hypothesis by investigating the complicated dynamics among education, location, and school choice in Hong Kong. We will make use of multiple datasets to investigate whether access to school quality has changed for students from various family and neighborhood backgrounds and if so, the causes and the consequences. At the macro level, we will document the patterns of and trends in school segregation, residential segregation, and inter-district school choice in Hong Kong, using data from various rounds of population census/by-census and the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). At the micro level, we will explore the determinants and mechanisms of families’ school choices by linking three datasets: the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics (HKPSSD), census/by-census, and a constructed school information dataset containing detailed information on all the primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong. The potential contribution of this project is threefold. Theoretically, we will fill an important gap in existing studies on educational inequalities by bringing a socio-spatial perspective to the empirical analysis. The case study of Hong Kong will also deepen our understandings of the interrelation between school and residential segregation; Methodologically, taking advantage of the precise locational information of children's schools and homes, we will for the first time apply geographical methodology, the Geographic Information System (GIS), to delineate the spatial patterns of educational inequality in a major Chinese metropolis. Practically, findings of our project will provide evidence-based policy suggestions regarding Hong Kong's recent marketization of schools and expansion of unrestricted school choice. 不同社會經濟背景的學生就讀於品質不一的學校，即形成了學校隔離。它不僅把學生分為三六九等，更容易把那些本身來自弱勢家庭的孩子局限在教育品質很差的學校。以往的文獻通常揭示出學校隔離與居住隔離具有正相關關係，因為學生往往是就近入學。為了打破這一教育機會與地理位置之間的緊密聯繫，很多國家都採取了擇校政策以允許學生選擇他們居住社區以外的學校就讀。然而香港代表了一類特例 —— 在這裡擇校政策的推行可能不但沒有改善學校間的社會經濟隔離，反倒是使其更惡化了。我們猜測，這可能是因為中上階層父母往往更熱衷於且更有能力利用擇校機會把他們的孩子送入那些集中於某些區域的好學校。我們的這一研究將會直接來驗證這一研究假設，以釐清香港的教育，區域，以及擇校三者之間的複雜關係。 我們會利用多個不同的資料庫來檢驗進入好學校的機會對於來自不同家庭和社區的學生是否有隨時間變化，如果是的話，這一變化的原因及後果。在宏觀層面，我們會利用多輪的人口普查資料和PISA資料來記錄香港的學校隔離，居住隔離，以及跨區擇校的模式和趨勢。在微觀層面，我們會通過串聯HKPSSD，人口普查以及全港中小學校資訊這三個資料庫來挖掘影響家庭擇校的因素及機制。 本項目具有三方面的潛在貢獻。從理論層面來說，我們將通過在實證分析中引入社會 — 空間的視角來填補目前教育不平等研究中的一個理論空白。尤其是對香港的個案研究將會進一步加深我們對學校隔離和居住隔離二者之間關係的理解；從方法層面來說，我們將充分利用資料中關於學生學校和家庭位址的詳實資訊，並運用GIS地理資訊技術來描述一個重要的華人都市中教育機會的空間分佈；從應用層面來說，我們項目的研究發現可以針對香港近年來的教育市場化改革和跨區擇校的普及提供基於經驗的政策建議。

16600218.label: Realisation of objectives
16600218.value: The PI and Co-Is have achieved all the project objectives as stated in the proposal. In total, we have published three papers out of this project. We also have one manuscript under review, and one working paper to be refined and submitted to a peer-reviewed journal. Corresponding to the project objectives, our summary is listed as below. 1. The research team has successfully constructed a database comprising all the elementary and secondary schools in Hong Kong using open data sources. Specifically, we have collected information on each school’s name, geocoded address, funding source, school level, religion, single-sex/co-educational, number of classes/students, and various school quality such as school banding, teacher-student ratio, teacher qualification, school popularity, tuition fees, school tradition, and school neighbourhood environment, etc. 2. The research team has successfully completed the fourth wave of HKPSSD survey in May 2019 and a new round of refreshment survey in Nov 2020. Together with previous waves of survey data, we have collected, processed, and cleaned available school-level and family-level information for all children under age 15 in the HKPSSD sample. We have also linked the HKPSSD dataset to the constructed school dataset via school names to obtain information on the schools children attended, and also linked to the population census via geocoded addresses to obtain contextual information on children’s neighbourhoods and schools. 3. The research team has documented the levels of and trends in income segregation between neighbourhoods among families with and without children, and to investigate the changing patterns of children’s mobility between district of residence and district of study using the Hong Kong census data. We have also sketched the trends in social segregation between schools and investigate the extent of disparities in quality between schools attended by children with various family backgrounds using the PISA data. The analysis is included in one of the reported published papers. 4. The research team has explored the determinants and mechanisms of parents’ school choice practices and investigated the impacts of these parental practices on various child development outcomes, such as their academic performance and non-cognitive skills. The analysis is included in one of the reported published papers.

16600218.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600218.value: 1. In the CJS paper (see Part C), we examined the academic performance and non-cognitive skills of the children of Chinese migrants in Hong Kong. We found that the poorer academic performance of Chinese migrants’ children results mainly from disadvantageous family background and parenting practices. Children of crossborder and migrant families do not differ from children of natives in Chinese, mathematics, or English, once parental education and parent–child communication about school life are controlled for. Children from migrant families have significantly higher levels of non-cognitive ability than children of natives. 2. In the CER paper (see Part C), we examined the impact of a major policy change in school allocation on gender disparity in academic achievement in Hong Kong. We found that the policy change towards equal opportunity has led to an enlarged gender gap in academic achievement in favor of girls. The reverse gender gap due in large part to the fact that girls are increasingly more likely to secure enrolment in better-quality secondary schools than boys. 3. In the CSR paper (see Part C), we examined the school segregation faced by migrant children in urban China and may offer a comparative understanding of the situation in Hong Kong. We found that migrants are disproportionally sorted into low-quality schools, which contributes to a sizeable achievement gap between migrants and locals. We further adopt school and individual fixed effect models to disentangle the influence of peer exposure from that of school quality and find no adverse impact of migrant concentration per se on student outcomes. 4. In the APER paper (see Part C), we examined the family SES-achievement gaps in seven Asian education systems, including Hong Kong, mainland China, Macao, Taiwan, Singapore, South Korea, and Japan. We found that in mainland China the gaps are most pronounced, whereas in Macao, they remain consistently modest. Hong Kong and other systems fall in between these two extremes.

16600218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600218.value: The school-level dataset generated from this project contains rich information that can be further used to reveal the geo-spatial inequality of educational resources in Hong Kong, or be linked to other individual-/household-/neighbourhood-level data to examine the inequality in access to educational opportunities.

16600218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600218.value: Children’s access to good schools has a profound impact on their educational attainment and later life chances. In Hong Kong, the rapid increase in the socioeconomic segregation of schools has raised serious public concerns on educational equity. However, despite the importance of this issue, relevant empirical studies have been severely limited. Making use of multiple datasets (i.e., HKPSSD, PISA, Census), our studies can fill the research gap in Hong Kong by revealing the complicated dynamics among education, location, and school choice. In addition, the investigation of other Chinese societies (e.g. urban China, Macao, Taiwan) and their respective education systems provides an important comparative perspective, which can help to deepen our understanding on the current educational inequality issues in Hong Kong. Findings from this project only respond to the recent public concerns on school segregation in Hong Kong, but also can provide evidence-based policy suggestions to government for designing better school choice and allocation policies that offer equal educational opportunities to children regardless of their social origins.

16601118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601118.value: A recurring observation in the field of political economy is that authoritarian regimes with abundant natural resources have low levels of industrialization. Furthermore, by relying on the sale of commodities rather than collecting taxes from private industry, such regimes are likely to remain authoritarian because the citizens lack the basis for demanding political participation in the spirit of “no taxation without representation.” In theory, resource-rich countries can provide higher quality public services than those without lucrative natural reserves. However, the research in China has revealed that resource-dependence may actually lead to lower levels of public investment in human capital. This is puzzling given the apparent availability of resources to finance such investments. In the proposed study, I will use subnational statistical data (1993-2016) and case studies of resource-abundant localities in China to analyze the factors that influence the provision of social services. I will hypothesize that due to the strong pressure for economic growth from the upper-level governments, the leaders of resource-abundant localities tend to neglect investing in areas that enhance the quality of labor, such as public education and healthcare. In this study, I will endeavor to show that the governments in these areas fail to invest in social welfare because the revenues derived from natural resources do not require large-scale labor participation, particularly skilled labor. To evaluate the implications of resource abundance at the subnational level, I will collect prefecture- and county-level data on Chinese cities and recent data on resource production and reserves. I will investigate how resource abundance affects the social policies, expenditure, and welfare outcomes, including education, healthcare, family subsidies, and other indicators in local areas. I will also collect detailed data on political leadership to examine how the career incentives of local leaders in resource-rich cities differ from those in manufacturing cities. To identify the mechanisms underlying the hypothesized “subnational resource curse,” I will also conduct field research in three resource-abundant cities, namely, Datong in Shanxi province for coal, Daqing in Liaoning for oil, and Dazhou in Sichuan for natural gas. I will then conduct comparative case studies to examine how the different resources affect the cities and their citizens, given their various histories, local industrial structures, and the extent of labor participation in three mineral industries. Based on empirical evidence using a mixed-method design, the proposed study will add to the literature by identifying a new mechanism of the subnational resource curse. 政治经济学研究中反复出现的观点是，拥有丰富自然资源的专制政权地区工业化水平较低。此外，一个地区的经济依赖于商品销售但不从私营企业征税，这种制度可能是专制的，因为公民没有参与政治的行为缺乏“不征税就没有民主主义”的精神。理论上，资源丰富的国家与没有利润丰厚的自然禀赋的国家相比，可以提供更高质量的公共服务。然而，中国的初步研究表明，资源依赖实际上可能会导致人力资本的公共投资水平降低。令人费解的是它有资源为此类投资提供资金。 根据地方统计数据（1993-2014）和中国资源丰富地区的案例研究，本研究将分析影响提供社会服务的因素。我假设，由于政府为促进经济增长而施加较大压力，资源丰富地区的领导人倾向于忽视提高劳动力质量的投资，包括公共教育和医疗保健。这是因为资源开采为这些地区的领导者提供了不涉及大规模劳动参与的经济收入，特别是熟练劳动力的参与。 为了评估对地方一级资源丰富的影响，本研究将采用中国城市的县级和县级面板数据，以及最近的资源生产和储量数据集。我将研究资源丰富程度如何影响社会政策，支出和福利结果 - 包括教育，医疗保健，家庭补贴和其他指标。还将纳入详细的政治领导数据，以研究资源丰富城市的地方领导人的职业激励与制造业城市的不同。 为了找出假设的“地方资源诅咒（危害）”背后的因果机制，我还将在三个资源丰富的城市进行实地调查：山西省大同的煤炭，黑龙江省大庆的石油和在四川达州天然气。由于历史的变迁，当地的产业结构以及石油，天然气和煤炭行业的劳动参与程度，比较案例研究将研究不同的资源如何影响城市及其公民。 通过混合方法得出的经验证据，本研究将揭示一个新的地方资源诅咒渠道，迄今为止文献尚未引起足够的重视。

16601618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601618.value: 中國新經濟的一個令人費解的現像是，儘管政治和法律制度存在嚴重腐敗，但法院越來越多被用作商業活動中解決衝突的途徑。誰傾向於使用法院解決糾紛？在何種情形下參與訴訟的人可能會達到相對穩定的解決方案？以及原因何在？這些問題可能會為理解中國的經濟治理提供有用的線索。 本項目尋求這些問題的答案。研究的前提是，中國的法律制度是一個富有競爭性操縱、沒有高門檻（正式或非正式）的領域。 原因有三。首先，儘管內部人和外人嚴重濫用，但中國的列寧式國家機器在尋求通過在基本經濟轉型、全球化和技術變革中引入法律制度改革來重塑自身的過程中，仍然具有巨大強制力。因此，法院成為解決衝突的潛在有效途徑。其次，由於歷史原因，中國沒有制度化的社會隔離去有系統地阻礙私人（網絡）進入政治制度。容納廣泛的參賽者的這種多孔性使得操縱法院的努力具有競爭性。第三，毛澤東時代的工業化遺產和後毛時代大規模城市化導致中國的新經濟形成多元化、多中心的空間集聚。大量交易（以及於此相關的合同糾紛及對其的法律管轄權）經常發生在同一地方或區域空間。法官在各種地方網絡縱橫交錯中的嵌入性增加了獨家利益主導法院操縱的難度。 在上述背景下，基於我對中國資本主義治理的持續研究，我提出了若干個工作假設作為搜索工具來調查相關訴訟參與者的行為和策略、以及他們互動的結果。調查的重點是社會關係網絡如何塑造司法操縱的競爭，以在不同背景下對法院施加私人影響。我用來分析合同糾紛訴訟中的參與傾向，過程和後果的變量包括地點、族群、經濟活動空間集聚度、所有權類型和爭議金額大小。信息來源包括（1）與經歷過商業糾紛的律師進行深入訪談，（2）調查研究的相關企業調查數據，包括將納入2018年全國民營企業調查的訴訟相關問題，以及（3）法院審判記錄的“大數據”挖掘。時間跨度從2000年到現在。 研究結果將（1）揭示中國經濟制度演變的法律機制，（2）豐富資本主義治理另類模式的研究，（3）進一步理解經濟活動空間集聚與契約治理之間的關係， （4）促進關於經濟發展中制度“包容性”和“排他性”的爭論。

16601618.label: Realisation of objectives
16601618.value: Below is a summary of the work carried out under the project. 1. Archival and documentary research Efforts were made to compile a comprehensive bibliography of relevant literature on law and economic governance in post-Mao China. The materials assembled for this listing include scholarly publications, media reports, legal statistics and official accounts of legal reforms. Also, an extensive search was made to identify publicized cases of legal corruption during 1985-2021. A list of 682 judges (together with their background information) who had been exposed, dismissed and disciplined/punished for involvement in corruption was compiled based on online media news, printed publications and party/government reports. It provides the basis for further updating with newly available information and for the analysis of the contractual dispute cases tried by these judges before their dismissal. 2. Fieldwork and interviews with lawyers and other informants Field trips were made to mainland China before February 2020 for in-depth interviews with lawyers, legal officials, and parties involved in contractual disputes. Unfortunately, the outbreak of COVID-19 in early 2020 and the subsequent travel restrictions made it impossible to continue face-to-face information collection. Even though a six-month extension of the project completion deadline was requested in hopes of a relaxation of restrictions, the original plan for fieldwork could not be fully implemented due to the persistence and further spread of the pandemic. The total number of lawyers I interviewed, for example, was 28, which fell short of the target of 60. There are also some locales (especially county seats) that I had planned to visit but in the end was unable to set foot on. Nonetheless, very useful information was obtained during the trips I had been able to make. I will have to wait until the pandemic subsides before resuming this line of work. 3. Data scraping and extraction As indicated in the grant proposal, a major part of the project is to acquire Chinese court trial records from open and proprietary sources. We devoted a sizeable amount of resource and time to this undertaking. In total 63.17 million full-text records were scraped and downloaded from the site of “China Judgments Online” (https://wenshu.court.gov.cn/) maintained by the Supreme People’s Court. Of these, 12.14 million are identified as contractual dispute cases. The records span the entire post-Mao era, though the vast majority of them are for the past two decades (up to mid-2020). To supplement this source of information, we made use of our subscription to the proprietary database of PKULaw (北大法宝) (https://www-pkulaw-com.lib.ezproxy.ust.hk), which has more comprehensive coverage of case records in the early years of China’s economic reforms. From this database we identified and extracted 700,487 full-text records of contractual dispute cases for 1983-2010. 4. Data mining From the vast and diverse text records of court trial of contractual dispute cases we constructed a wide range of numerical and categorical variables for systematic analysis. This was done with the aid of computer algorithms developed from extensive iterations of trial and machining learning. The variables we have constructed thus far illuminate (a) the basic profile of each case (e.g., court location, time of trial, court officials, judgment date, etc.), (b) the personal particulars of disputing parties (e.g., resident status, ID number / social credit number, gender, age, ethnicity, occupation, position, organizational affiliation, etc.), (c) the legal representatives of disputing parties, (d) the focal issue(s) of dispute, the redress sought by the plaintiff, (e) the timeline of escalation from dispute occurrence to initiation of court proceeding and to delivery of court outcome, (f) the type of court procedure used (i.e., small claims, simplified, or regular trial), (g) the type of outcome (i.e., ruling, mediation, withdrawal, dismissal, and other), (h) the direction of court ruling (e.g., favorable, unfavorable, mixed, etc., as benchmarked to the original claim[s] of the plaintiff), (i) the definitiveness / conclusiveness of court outcome (e.g., whether ruling was appealed, (j) whether implementation of court ruling was withheld or impaired, (k) whether case was re-tried, and so on), (l) the statutory basis of court ruling, among other issues. 5. Data analysis The data from textual mining were then integrated with data from other sources, including the above-mentioned list of judges involved in corruption (who, by our latest count, had presided over or took part in the trial of a total of 17,365 contractual dispute cases), basic socioeconomic indicators (mainly from local statistical yearbooks) of the prefectural level jurisdiction where each court is located, the organizational profiles of the disputing parties as recorded in the database of the Company Registry of the State Administration of Industry and Commerce (SAIC) before 2018 and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) thereafter. The resultant data set was then analyzed together with three other data sets. They include: (a) a 2004 private enterprise survey (n=511) conducted by a team of CASS and HKUST researchers (http://privatizationinchina.ust.hk/Augus_Post/survey_2004.pdf); (b) a 2005 survey (n=12,400) of China’s investment environment conducted by the World Bank and the National Bureau of Statistics (http://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/602); and (c) a bi-annual tracking survey (1997-2016) of private enterprises sponsored by the All China Federation of Industry and Commerce (ACFIC) and some other organizations (http://ww2.usc.cuhk.edu.hk/DCS/DCS31-16.aspx). Our data analyses were driven by clues and insights derived from interviews, case materials, and academic and media accounts of conflict resolution through the court. Among the key questions that the analyses shed light on are when and why a contractual dispute case is brought to court, how far a court trial tends to proceed, where manipulation of the court is likely to concentrate, what factors may constrain rule-bending by judges for private considerations, what legal and extra-legal factors may affect court outcomes, and where relatively stable court outcomes are likely to obtain and hold.

16601618.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601618.value: Initial findings from the project include an overview of the impact of legal reforms on the use of the court for contractual dispute settlement, descriptive statistics from various datasets, case materials, and data analysis results. Some of these findings are being reported in a chapter on contractual dispute in a book entitled "Weak Institutions, Strong Organizations: Governance of Capitalism in China". The book project is currently under review at Cambridge University Press. As is often the case, a book project takes much longer time to complete and get published than journal articles. RGC funding will nevertheless be acknowledged in any future publication using materials generated from this project.

16601618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601618.value: The data work we have done so far is highly labor-intensive. Given the large amount of information under processing, much remains to be done to make the quantitative data fully ready for comprehensive statistical analysis for hypothesis testing. Specifically, more efforts are needed to carry out further textual data mining, to improve the variables constructed, and to match and merge data from different sources. There is also considerable space for the expansion of the qualitative information we have collected. In particular, a search for additional documentary and archival material pertaining to the contexts of contractual dispute trials is necessary. Also needed is further collection of first-hand accounts by parties involved in contractual dispute resolution. It will take sometime for the potential of the information generated from the project to be fully explored and turned into publishable works.

16601618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601618.value: This project aims to seek clues to explaining the puzzling phenomenon that despite endemic legal corruption the court has been extensively used for contractual dispute settlement in China’s new economy. The investigation uses a mixed method to derive insights from qualitative and quantitative evidence. Findings from the study will (1) cast new light on the legal mechanisms of China’s evolving economic institutions, (2) enrich the research on alternative modes of capitalist governance, (3) further the understanding of the relationship between agglomeration and contractual governance, and (4) contribute to the debate on institutional “inclusiveness” and “exclusiveness” in economic development.

16601718.value: 清代有出身官員之家庭背景對任職與仕途的影響

16601718.label: Project Objectives
16601718.value: Construct a degree holder database of the family backgrounds, including the patrilineal ancestry, of Qing officials who held jinshi (进士) or juren (举人) examination degrees and were also included in surviving records of degree holders such as zhujuan (朱卷), xiangshilu (鄉試錄) or xiangshi tongnian chilu (鄉試同年齒錄). Identify the fathers and paternal grandfathers and great-grandfathers and possibly other kin of the Qing officials recorded in the jinshenlu (缙绅录) by nominative linkage to the degree holder database, then identify whether these ancestors served as officials or held degrees by another round of linkage back to the jinshenlu and the degree holder database. Estimate the share of officials who are descended from officials or degree-holders, and compare with previous estimates of the share of jinshi degree holders who were descendants of jinshi to assess whether focusing on officials rather than degree-holders yields a different picture of permeability among elites. Assess whether a family history of holding office or exam degree was associated with performance on the metropolitan exam (會試) that was the basis for the jinshi degree, and then conditional on exam performance, whether family history influenced the chances of appointment to a position and subsequent career trajectory. Assess temporal trends and regional variation in the association between family background and the chances of appointment and subsequent career trajectories, with emphasis on whether the importance of family background increased during the 19th century. Examine whether there were specific families that were persistently successful over multiple generations, or dominated specific offices, and assess the implications of the prevalence of such families for any general conclusions from #3-#5 about the permeability of elites. Prepare the database constructed for #1 for public release in stages after the completion of the proposed project.

16601718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601718.value: We will examine how family background interacted with exam performance and other characteristics to shape the careers of officials who were appointed on the basis of a jinshi or juren examination degree during the Qing (1644-1911) dynasty. For family background, we consider family history of attainment of examination degree, service as an official, and degree or office purchase. We focus specifically on how these features of family background interacted with individual characteristics such as attainment of examination degree and membership of groups defined by common teacher, examiner, or exam year to influence initial appointment and subsequent advancement. While the relationship between family background, education and career mobility is a central concern of contemporary social science research, until now the lack of appropriate data means that there are few opportunities to study these relationships in a historical setting, especially for an elite subpopulation like the one we propose to study. Goals include examining how career trajectories differed according to family background for the degree holding officials for whom we have information on ancestry. A basic question is whether conditional on exam performance and network membership as defined above, officials whose ancestors or other kin were degree holders or officials had more favorable career trajectories. We will also investigate whether the influence of family background led to the domination of specific offices by particular families. We will make use of a linked database described career trajectories and family background. For career trajectories, we will use an existing database constructed from surviving editions of the jinshenlu (縉紳錄), a complete list of almost all civil officials published every three months during the Qing. By fall 2018 we expect it to contain 3,000,000 records of 375,000 officials. We may supplement the existing database with editions that we have recently located. For family background, we will create and link new databases from records of exam degree holders that record ancestry and kinship. To analyze these linked data, we will apply quantitative methods specifically developed by social mobility researchers to study the role of family background and other characteristics on education and employment. This will be one of the first studies of family background influences on career mobility in a national government bureaucracy over an extended period of time. As such, it will be a major contribution not only to our understanding of Qing China, but to our understanding of careers, and the structure and organization of bureaucracies more generally. 我們將檢驗清代（1644-1911）家庭背景與科場表現等其他因素的互動關係，及其對擁有科名（進士、舉人）的官員仕宦生涯產生的影響。家庭背景方面，我們考慮的因素包括家族歷史上曾經考取功名、就任官職、以及捐納出身或者官職。我們尤其關注這些家庭背景特征如何與官員個人經歷交互作用并對初仕職位和後來的遷轉產生影響，這些個人經歷包括同場科考的士子、考官、授業師、肄業師等。儘管家庭背景、教育和職業流動的關係已經是當代社會科學研究的核心話題，但是迄今為止，尤其是在一個類似於我們計劃研究的人口群體中，合適的數據的匱乏導致了在歷史背景中研究相關問題的機會寥寥。研究目標包括檢驗有祖輩信息的有科名官員之仕因家庭背景的關係引起的差異。其中一個基本的問題是根據上述定義的科場表現和關係網絡，祖輩或其他親屬擁有科名或官職的官員是否更傾向於擁有更順暢的仕途。我們也會考察家庭背景的影響是否會導致特定的家族主導某些特定官職。 我們計劃使用一個可以反映仕途和家庭背景的匹配數據庫。仕途方面，我們會用由存世的縉紳錄構建的數據庫。縉紳錄是清代每三個月按季出版的完整官員名冊。截至2018年秋季我們預計將完成37.5萬官員的約300萬條記載。我們會用近期新發現的版本對既有的數據庫進行補充。家庭背景方面，我們將利用包括祖輩和親屬信息的科名錄創建新的數據庫并進行數據匹配。為分析這些數據，我們會應用社會流動學者們專門發展并用於分析家庭背景和其他特征對教育和就業影響的定量方法。 這將是第一項關於在相當長的一段歷史時期內，家庭背景對于國家政府官員之職業流動的影響的研究。因此，這不僅將對我們理解清代中國有重要貢獻，更有助於我們理解廣義的官僚政治中的職業生涯、組織及構成。

16601718.label: Realisation of objectives
16601718.value: 1. We completed construction of a degree holder database in late 2021 by transcription of all the huishi and xiangshi tongnianchilu that we could find in libraries or published collections. We call the resulting dataset the China Government Employee Dataset-Examination Records (CGED-ER). For the CGED-Q ER, as of February 2022 we have 5,724 and 26,870 tongnian chilu records of jinshi and juren. We also have 11,990 records of gongsheng and other categories degree holders that provide family background and other information. These were recorded in mingjing tongpu. 3,574 jinshi records were transcribed directly from huishi tongnianchilu for 15 sittings of the exam in the 19th century: 1829, 1833, 1835, 1859, 1865, 1868, 1871, 1876, 1877, 1880, 1886, 1889, 1890, and 1895. We synthesized another 2,174 by combining information about huishi exam year and performance in the jinshi timinglu with information on ancestry from their xiangshi tongnianchilu records. The xiangshi tongnianchilu are from 28 different exam years. For 13 of these exam years (1810, 1816, 1821, 1825, 1828, 1832, 1835, 1840, 1844, 1849, 1855, 1870, 1879), we located and transcribed compendium volumes listing xiangshi degree holders from all provinces. For the remaining exam years, we have entered data for the subsets of provinces for which we were able to locate xiangshi tongnianchilu. We located a vendor to carry out the necessary data entry. We had originally intended to hire an RA to do the data entry, and used those funds to pay the vendor. This resulted in us being able to enter much more data than would have been possible with an RA. 2. We completed this linkage after we finished construction of the CGED-Q JSLin 2021 by transcription of the last remaining available Jinshenlu and Zhongshubeilan, and completed creation of the CGED-Q ER. We experimented with different approaches to linkage before 2021 using the partial dataset, and finalized our linkage in late 2021 once both datasets were completed. We settled on the use of probabilistic record linkage which scores possible matches based on criteria we specify and then picks the best fit in terms of match. 3. We completed this calculation. Our findings for the ancestry of degree holders were similar to those reported by Ho Ping-ti. We found that officials were even more likely to have a family history of degree attainment, and that higher officials were the most likely to have such a history. We had done the calculations on the partial dataset before 2021, and redid them at the end of 2021 after we completed entry of all the data and we are now preparing the manuscript with these results (#1 in C.8) for submission to a major journal. 4. We found that a family history of degree attainment was positively associated with performance on the Metropolitan Exam, but less strongly associated with performance on the provincial exam. It was strongly associated with age at passing the provincial exam. Net of performance on the exams, family background influence career attainment. We redid all the calculations at the end of 2021 after data entry was complete, and we are preparing the relevant manuscript (#1 in C.8) for submission to a flagship journal. 5. We have carried out the relevant calculations while we were still entering data. The results will be the basis of a new manuscript on time trends in the late Qing. We have also published a series of case studies of appointment, promotion and exit of specific groups officials in particular periods, including officials in the Ministry of Personnel (吏部) (C.8 #7), Prefects (知府) (C.8 #9), Department Prefects (C.8 #10), Exam-Degree Holders before and after the abolition of the examination system in 1905 (C.8 #6). We also collaborated with a PhD student in computer science at HKUST who developed a visualization platform that allowed for examination of changes over time and comparisons between different groups of officials (C.8 #8). 6. We have confirmed that there were families that were persistently successful. We have been redoing the analysis since we completed data entry at the end of 2021 and are finalizing the manuscript that includes these results. We have also shared CGED-Q data with other researchers doing case studies of specific lineages. We have provided data on officials surnamed Cen to Kenneth Pomeranz, and provide CGED-Q data to Li Changkun, formerly an MA student at Central China Normal University, and Hu Sijie, at the time a PhD student at LSE, both of whom had created databases out of lineage genealogies. They linked the CGED-Q data to their genealogies. Their analysis is ongoing. 7. We publicly released CGED-Q Jinshenlu data for the periods 1900-1912 and 1850-1864. These are available for download at Lee-Campbell Group Dataverses at DataSpace @ HKUST and at Harvard. We have harmonized the contents of the degree-holder database described in Objective #1 and plan to release it in stages in the coming years.

16601718.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601718.value: A research outcome has been the completion of the China Government Employee Databases-Qing (CGED-Q) Jinshenlu (JSL) and Examination Records (ER) by entry of all available Jinshenlu and Zhongshubeilan editions listing civil and military officials, respectively, as well as all of the xiangshi lu and tongnianchilu that we could find. These will be important resources not only for our own research, but that of other scholars, especially as we proceed with the public release. In C.8 #1 we confirm Ho Ping-ti's (1962) findings on the family backgrounds of degree holders, and show that family background mattered for officials even after controlling for exam performance. Higher officials were more likely to have a family history of exam or purchase degree attainment. Such results challenge the claim that the bureaucracy was 'meritocratic' and that promotion was based on ability, without regard for family background. C.8 #6 shows that the abolition of the examination system in 1905 had little effect on officials who already had degrees. Officials who already had degrees continued to be appointed after 1905. Their chances of appointment actually increased slightly because there was no longer a supply of new degree holders competing with them. Such results challenge claims that the abolition of the examination system in 1905 was a massive disruption to current or aspiring degree holders. C.8 #3 included novel and important descriptive findings on the composition of Qing officialdom. It showed that in the central government, Bannermen dominated the highest positions right up to the end of the Qing. Nearly all the central government officials who were not Bannermen held the highest exam degree, the jinshi. Outside the central government, non-Bannermen (mostly Han Chinese) dominated. Holders of purchased degrees accounted for a steadily rising share of local officials during the 19th century, with a corresponding decline in the share of local officials who held exam degrees. Collaborations with Qing historians on case studies of specific categories of officials (C.8 #7,9,10,11) have shed new light on the workings of the bureaucracy, especially processes of appointment and promotion, in the late Qing. #7 examined officials in the Ministry of Personnel in the central goverment, #9 and #10 examined prefects and departmental prefects, respectively, and #11 examines holders of gongsheng degrees. Such studies are notable because they integrate traditional approaches to Chinese history with quantitative approaches, and along with #6, have helped showcase to traditional historians the potential for such a hybrid approach.

16601718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601718.value: Re #3 and #4, we are revising C.8 #1 to reflect results from the complete CGED-Q JSL and CGED-Q ER and will submit it to a major journal in the coming months. Re #5, following up on our published case studies of appointment and promotion for specific groups of officials and time periods, we will use the complete CGED-ER to extend analysis to account for the role of family background. We will continue collaborating with Qing historians who can help interpret time trends and other observed patterns. For #6, we are currently redoing earlier calculations to make use of the complete CGED-Q JSL and EQ, developing plans for manuscripts based on our findings on multi-generational persistence. We are also looking for additional opportunities to collaborate with scholars studying specific lineages or places for more in-depth studies.

16601718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601718.value: This project has produced large datasets that will be important resources for the study of Chinese social and political history in coming decades. By recording the civil and military officials who worked for the Qing state completely and in great detail, and for a subset of them providing information on family background, we will be able to study a variety of topics in social mobility and stratification. The data will be released in portions so other scholars can pursue research related to their own interests. Collectively, the research results of this project shed new light on the late Qing state, in some cases challenging widely common assumptions. The abolition of the exam system in 1905 was less disruptive for degree holders than commonly thought. The highest positions of the central government were dominated by Bannermen right up to the end of the Qing. Family background played a role not only in the attainment of exam degrees, but on the chances of appointment and promotion, and eventually reaching high office. Working with traditional historians, we have also conducted case studies of specific groups of officials and time periods that have advanced our understanding of the Qing bureaucracy.

16601818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601818.value: 情感的主觀體驗在不同的心理現象中都擔當著很重要的角色，但是情感的結構一直都是心理學上的難題。究竟情感結構的基本因子是什麼？這些因子又會否隨著文化和心理健康而有所改變？過往有不少的理論和研究以探討前者為主，而近年越來越多人對後者的議題感興趣。 過往的理論和研究指出，愉快程度和喚醒程度是情感結構的基本因子，不過這些因子的本質仍尚待研究。我們在這個研究建議書著重於測量愉快程度。在環狀情感模型中，愉快程度是由愉快和不愉快雙極情感定義（喚醒程度則由喚醒和不喚醒雙極情感定義）。這意味著快樂和悲哀是不能同時發生的; 換句話說，一個人快樂的時候是不會感到悲哀的。不過，有些人卻認為快樂和悲哀是兩個獨立的個體，也就是說一個人可以同時感到快樂和悲哀的。在是次跨文化研究中，我們將會利用經驗抽樣方法來了解日常生活中愉快和不愉快的共存程度。 近年的研究顯示，愉快和不愉快情感在東方文化中是可以同時發生的，但在西方文化卻沒有這種現象。至於這共存現象對心理健康是否有正面的影響，各研究結果並不一致，這可能是因為這些研究所使用的樣本太小或不夠多元化，不足以得出可信的結論。因此我們建議把樣本擴大並包含更多不同文化的受訪者。更重要的是，我們必須利用其他方法（如經驗抽樣方法）作交叉驗證，這樣我們才能進一步了解在日常生活中的個人情感狀態以及不同人之間的情感差異。 我們現存的研究網絡包含50個不同的地區，它們的代表性和重要性已備受肯定。我們會在這些地區收集問卷數據。問卷語言包括印歐語系、閃米特－含米特語系 、漢藏語系、壯侗語系、烏拉爾語系、馬來－波里尼西亞語系、德拉維達語系、阿爾泰語系。這些地區不但代表著六大洲，也覆蓋了Schwartz (2006) 界定的國際區域。我們亦會在每個區域收集多個樣本以確保研究結果的可信性。我們會測量愉快和不愉快情感的共存程度與心理健康的關係，以及這些關係在不同文化中的差異程度。過往的研究因為樣本太小未能解答這些問題，我們將會以實證研究來了解愉快程度的本質，以及它們與文化及其他因素的關係。

16602118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602118.value: For most of its existence, the civil service of late imperial China was the most complex and sophisticated bureaucracy in the world. Although scholars have studied it from a variety of angles, we still know relatively little concerning the actual careers of officials who served in this system. This project will construct a dataset using the personnel files (lüli 履歷) of the Qing dynasty to study one group of officials in particular: those who used office purchase (juanna 捐納) at some point in their official career. It will first collect and input the data from the personnel files into a digital database. Information collected will include personal information, history of appointment for the official, and also the rationale and reasons for such appointments. Using the information collected, this project will analyze the data with three objectives in mind. First, it will undertake to analyze how officials were appointed and selected in mid to late career. In contrast to the early career of officials, for which there is much research because of its close proximity to the civil service examination system, mid to late career officials, especially those in middling ranks, have generally been neglected by scholarly research. This group of officials deserve more attention because they formed the backbone for the civil service and many fulfilled important tasks for the government, even if they never reached national level positions. Secondly, the project will analyze how purchase affected the age of those who were appointed. Using of purchase to buy appointments and promotions would, theoretically, speed up appointment processes. Did this result in a relatively young group of officials reaching higher ranked positions than otherwise possible compared with the examination population? Information from this database will be able to yield answers to this question. Finally, in conjunction with the two previous points, it is important to also pay attention to interruptions in officials’ careers. These include but were not limited to parental mourning, sickness, and dismissals. Purchase regulations include provisions for paying for fast-tracked reappointment after such interruptions, and the database will provide answers as to how these regulations were used. Combined, these three topics of inquiry will reveal how actively serving officials in the Qing dynasty may have used office purchase to further enhance their career and show the importance of wealth in maintaining an active and successful career in the civil service at the time. 在同期的歷史中， 明清的文官制度可以說是世界上最複雜的官僚體制。 雖然史學界一直有研究明清官僚體制的各個層面，當中涉及官員流通，陞遷，降貶的實際個案卻並未受重視。此課題會以北京第一歷史檔案館所出版的清代官員履歷檔案為基礎去研究曾經利用捐納的官員之官運。計劃的第一步是將履歷檔案中明確有使用捐納的官員的資料數據化。這些檔案中包括了官員的出身，官職，年齡等。本計劃會使用已收集的資料來分析清代捐納官員的陞遷模式。計劃的第一個目標是分析官員在任命期的中後期的陞遷過程。與初任的官員比較，有關中級官員的研究比較貧乏，但這群體是清代官僚體制的骨幹，也可凸顯捐納官員在這群體中的重要性。第二個目標是以官員的年齡作為變數去分析官納對官員的入仕和陞遷過程有何影響。理論上捐納是應該有增加升遷速度的功用，但實際上是否有這樣的效果仍需實體個案來演示。第三個目標則是以官員陞遷的障礙，包括病假，丁憂，降革等。捐納在這幾方面亦可以幫助官員重新得缺，但實際上的運作如何仍有待大量的資料支持才能作出定論。本計劃希望利用履歷檔中的資料對以上三點詳加分析，為我們對清代捐納的使用情況作出更深入的理解。

16602118.label: Realisation of objectives
16602118.value: Over the course of the project I have entered about 60,000 lines of data, which come from about 6,100 individuals throughout the history of the Qing dynasty. The data has been entered onto excel spreadsheets including every piece of available information in the personnel files. While some statistical studies have been done in the past on these files by other scholars, this is the first attempt to systematically digitize all the information contained in these personnel files for future analysis. As such, the project was able to input 9 volumes out of 30 of the available personnel files. In the proposal stage it was never envisioned that it would be possible to enter all 30 volumes as the amount of data was deemed too much for both the amount of time available and the funding requirement. In the intervening time between 2021 and the end of the project there was a period when coordinating data entry became impossible due to the Covid pandemic as some of my data entry workers were located in Wuhan. That we were able to enter this much data within the research timeframe, especially given the disruptions posed by the pandemic, has exceeded expectations. Data entry is ongoing in a continuing collaboration with the Lee-Campbell group, who have taken over the data entry for the rest of the personnel files. Their experienced coders have taken over the coding of the rest of the data, thus the deviation in the budget from RA expenses to "general expenses" as the Lee-Campbell Group coders are paid via vendor billing. This GRF project has therefore seeded the complete digitization of the personnel files in the future. This will be a tool that will become available to other researchers once entry is complete and verified, and will be an indispensable tool for the study of Qing bureaucracy. Due to various disruptions throughout this research period, there were interruptions in the coding process especially since the onset of the pandemic. Nevertheless, I have been able to use some of the data entered early on in the project to enhance my ongoing research into the system of office purchase in the Qing dynasty. This data, especially comments by emperor on individual officials as well as the ratings in aggregate from the Yongzheng emperor have been utilized in both my monograph titled "Power for a Price" as well as my co-authored chapter in the book "Making Meritocracy." The data collected showed decisively how the Qing emperors were much more ecumenical about the qualification origins of their officials, and did not really consider origin as a factor in evaluation existing officials' promotion paths. There has been a bit more difficulty in using the age data gathered as the data is less reliable than previously expected. The initial batch of materials coded was insufficient to perform proper analysis for this purpose, and with the interruption in coding arrangements in the GRF progress was stalled for a while. As a result, my own analysis of the data collected so far is ongoing, especially since the more abundantly detailed information coming from the later periods are still being entered by the Lee-Campbell group. However, I have conducted some analysis of the information available to us in conjunction with my graduate student Li Chong, who is finishing an MPhil thesis with me on the topic of the retirement and forced-retirement of officials during the Qing. The age data present in the personnel files that we have entered has been useful in parts of his thesis, and the sickness and retirement information contained within the files have also been used to help study those whose careers were cut short or interrupted in some fashion. We have found that contrary to common assumption, there was in fact no fixed retirement age in the Qing and officials often worked till very late in their age, well past the age of 70 in some extreme cases. The retirement of officials was entirely at the discretion of the emperor and was granted on a case-by-case basis. The lack of institutionalization of such an arrangement is unusual, especially given that so much of the rest of the civil service was highly regimented. It suggests perhaps a more paternalistic and personal control of the lives and careers of officials, especially senior officials, than previously assumed. Once he completes his thesis this year, Li Chong will continue to study with me as a PhD candidate in my division working on a broader themed topic related to his current research. His progress has been good so far and I expect no delay in his graduation. Also, I expect to continue to work on this set of data for years to come especially as we gather more materials, and am looking forward to work on and publish co-authored pieces with my graduate student on topics related to the mid to late career of Qing officials and their retirement and exit from the civil service.

16602118.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602118.value: The data collected from this project has informed my research in both my book "Power for a Price" as well as my co-authored chapter in the book "Making Meritocracy." In both cases, the data is used to help enhance my study of the institution of office purchase during the Qing dynasty and its relation to the topic of meritocracy during this period. In particular, the comments from emperors in the early Qing suggest that imperial decision making on individual career moves (promotion, demotion, etc) were largely independent of one's qualification for office, whether through exam, purchase, or other paths. Rather, one's performance on the job, family background, and other factors such as appearance were emphasized. This suggests that there were different metrics that were used to recruit officials vs metrics used to evaluate existing officials. Overemphasis of examination success in the literature in the past has blinded the field to these nuances in the ongoing evaluation of officials. Also, in collaboration with my postgraduate student Li Chong, we have been examining the process and policy changes in retirement during the Qing. We have found that there was no firm retirement date, and that retirement cases were done on an individual, case-by-case basis. Some officials were forced to retire by the emperor if deemed to be incompetent, or simply dishonest. This study will be extended to mid-career interruptions such as mourning, sickness, etc as Li continues his study with me to pursue his PhD. The data entered in this project will also form the basis of a much larger, comprehensive database of all personnel file information from the Qing dynasty. Data entry for this project is currently underway and will become an important tool for those of us who study the Qing.

16602118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602118.value: At the moment one of my MPhil student, Li Chong, is using the data collected to study the issue of retirement, dismissal, and punishment in the Qing civil service. His main focus of the MPhil thesis is on the issue of retirement, but my department has also just accepted him to be a PhD student in the coming year and he will continue his study of this topic and extend it into the question of age and mid-career move. In conjunction with the Lee-Campbell group, we are also moving ahead to continue inputting data from the personnel files that began under this project using other funding sources. The database from the personnel files will thus continue to be built up, eventually hopefully encompassing all of the files that have been published in the 30 volume set. This process will take some time but we have plans to take it to completion.

16602118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602118.value: In the past studies of the Qing civil service have overwhelmingly focused on the question of entry - the examination system and the selection system that determine who gets to become an official. Equally important, however, is the reverse, which is the issue of how people move through and up in the civil service and how people leave. This is obviously a broad topic, but one point where we can begin to understand this issue is from the data present in the personnel files of the Qing government, which include a lot of data of officials' careers throughout the Qing. By inputting this data into a useable database format, we thus have a way to begin analyzing this data systematically and reach a better understanding of how officials advanced, and also left, the civil service. This would help us construct a more complete picture of the dynamics of personnel appointments and thus gain a broader understanding of the issues underlying the debate about meritocracy in the Qing.

16602318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602318.value: TTechnological change is inextricably linked with sustainable development – improving human well-being across present generations without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Marshaling innovation to meet sustainable development goals will require reorienting innovation systems to better serve the needs of poor and marginalized populations as well as future generations. Yet the levers of change available remain poorly understood both in academic and policy circles. This project will seek to develop a stronger, policy-applicable understanding of the role of innovation systems in advancing sustainable development, with a focus on the role played by public actors. Technologies are increasingly emerging within transnational innovation systems, as realizing sustainable development is a global task that involves linking global challenges to local contexts. Yet innovation policy is a strongly nationally oriented activity. How policy actors have been able to reconcile national needs and strategies within larger, more globalized innovation systems, is an underdeveloped area in scholarship and practice. The project will be spearheaded by a group of scholars with globally recognized contributions in this area. Building on our previous research on transnational innovation systems for sustainable development, this project will further our understanding of the role played by public policy actors. The project overall will help policy actors understand the types of interventions that are most effective in supporting the innovation system for sustainable development. It will also query the linkages between national and international innovation systems. Theoretically and empirically, the findings will guide countries with limited resources to better utilize and allocate their innovation resources for sustainable development from the policy perspective. Based on a previously developed innovation systems framework, we will review key policy documents and develop a set of novel case studies across five technology sectors (health, energy, manufacturing, water and agriculture) to meet our research objectives. We will focus on three core research questions: 1. Where in the innovation systems do, and should, governments intervene to support sustainable development (with a focus on energy, health, agriculture/food, water, and manufacturing)? 2. How do these interventions by policy actors at different geographical and political scales integrate into transnational systems of innovation? 3. How can policy actors better target their policy interventions to support technologies for sustainable development? Our findings will fill important gaps in the scholarly literature. It will also provide policy makers practical lessons to improve their innovation systems for sustainable development. 技術變革與可持續發展密不可分，然而為實現可持續發展目標而進行的技術創新，則需要重新調整創新系統, 以便更好地滿足貧困和邊緣化人口、以及子孫後代的需求。現如今，學術界和政策界對可用的調整創新系統的手段卻缺乏瞭解。本項目將針對政策參與者研發有效的、政策上可執行性強的引導創新系統來推動可持續發展。可持續發展已成為一項全球性的任務，並涉及將全球共享的挑戰與地方的特殊環境聯繫起來，技術也越來越多地出現在跨國創新系統中。然而, 制定創新政策卻是一項強烈圍繞著國家而進行的活動，因此，政策參與者如何能夠在更廣闊、更全球化的創新系統內調和世界與本國的需求，成為極為重要但仍缺乏探索的領域。本項目通過重點研究創新政策參與者中的公共參與者，力求加深對創新系統在促進可持續發展方面的政策適用性理解。項目將由一批在創新和可持續發展領域全球公認具有積極貢獻的學者牽頭，這批學者之前已對可持續發展的跨國創新系統有研究基礎。整個項目將幫助政策參與者進一步瞭解支持可持續發展創新系統最為有效的干預措施類型，還將探索國家和國際創新體系之間的聯繫。從理論和經驗上講, 研究結果將從政策角度指導資源有限的國家更好地利用和分配其創新資源, 以促進可持續發展。基於項目牽頭學者之前已制定好的創新體系框架，本項目將仔細審查關鍵的政策文件，並開展一套涵蓋五個技術方向（衛生、能源、製造業、水和農業）的新案例研究。項目將重點關注三個方面的核心問題：1、在創新體系中（重點放在能源、保健、農業/糧食、水和製造業），政府應該在哪個環節對支持可持續發展的進行干預？2、在不同地理和政治尺度上的政策參與者所做的干預措施應如何融入跨國創新體系？3、政策參與者如何能夠更好地針對政策干預措施來支持可持續發展的技術？我們的研究結果將填補學術文獻中的重要空白，還將為決策者提供實際經驗從而為支持可持續發展提供更好的創新體系。

16602318.label: Realisation of objectives
16602318.value: Overall, we were able to successfully accomplish our research objectives. The greatest challenge was that from our initial project design, we assumed that the policies would be much more technology-specific than they actually are. We were able to identify patterns at sectoral or aggregate levels, but not into technology characteristics. This is balanced by an incredibly successful data collection effort. We collected over 2200 policies across the 14 countries that we identified in different parts of our study. As far as we can tell, this is the only comparative policy tool database (focused on innovation and sustainability) of this size and richness, and the work has been very well received by colleagues. Thus the detail and richness of what we were able to accomplish across (and beyond) our objectives exceeds our expectations at the start of this project. Objective 1: Using an extensive literature review, we identified articles and reports discussing and analyzing barriers to innovation in all five of the sectors in this study (drawing from examples globally, not just limited to the countries in this study). From this, we were able to identify 54 specific barriers, which we grouped into eight categories (Economic & Financial, Technical, Regulatory & Policy, Standards, Market Entry, Knowledge & Capacity, System & Structural, Social & Behavioral). Each of these 54 barriers was then mapped onto the innovation system stages in the FAMIS Mode, which gave a more robust picture of when in the innovation process these occur. Related to Objective 2, the three most common stages for barriers to occur are in production, initial adoption, widespread use, and adaptation. Yet these are the very areas where we identified the FEWEST policies. This would indicate that more policy attention is needed here (see Objective 2). The nature of the existing research, and the nature of how (as we discovered during data collection) policies tend to be sectorally focused (as opposed to technology-specific), made it impossible for us to do a more granular linkage between a specific set of socio-technical characteristics and barriers. Thus we focused more on overall patterns in sectors and in aggregate. Objective 2: In practice, our research showed that both the relevant literature to barriers to innovation related to sustainability, and also the policies, are sectorally, rather than specific-technology focused. This means that they are not, in fact, linked to specific socio-technical characteristics at the granular level, but in fact more towards sector dynamics (i.e. health vs. agriculture vs. energy), and the structures of technology (and problems) in those areas. We also found that while there are certainly differences in the sectoral profiles of common tools in the water, health, energy, agriculture, and manufacturing sectors, within (and across) those sectors there are clear national-level patterns (please see Objective 3). To establish this, we used correspondence analysis at the country-sector level, as well as correspondence analysis at the national level (aggregate of all sectors). We used the FAMIS model to map these policies against innovation stages, and were able to identify three key gaps. (1) Misalignment between national innovation strategies and concrete implementation places, (2) A lack of policy to move technologies from prototype to commercialization (sometimes called “the Valley of Death”), and (3) lack of policies focused on technology adoption (other than in energy), which runs counter to policy literature that emphasizes government roles in market co-creation and co-shaping. Objective 3: From our data, the vast majority of the policies to support innovation for sustainable development were very broad, and not focused on a specific technology. However, we were able to establish different policy ‘styles’ in the countries that we were studying, linked more closely to political preference and market features. To accomplish this, we used correspondence analysis as a novel tool to visualize associations between policy instruments employed by our subset of ten countries through which we identified five distinct policy instrument mixes (or innovation strategies). We found that countries with a mixed economic system generally used more sustainability-related policy interventions and predominantly focused on targeted R&D funding and market creation (e.g., Denmark, Sweden). Whereas countries with a market economic system largely focused on policies that support firm innovation – either through direct economic tools especially providing high-risk early stage and expansion financing (e.g., Israel, New Zealand) or through enabling a conductive environment for innovation through creating spaces, building networks and capacity (e.g., Switzerland). Objective 4: It was very clear that the Visegrad Four (Central EU) countries we analyzed heavily relied on EU funding for energy technology adoption. The data collected on the policy interventions and their sources of financing clearly shows that the EU plays an important role in terms of financing as well as providing a direction towards carbon neutrality. In general, out of 236 interventions in total, 66 were co-financed by the EU. This shows that all four countries heavily depend on EU structural funds, where most of these funds are used on the initial and widespread adoption of technologies – especially initial and widespread adoption of renewable energy technologies and energy efficiency improvements of buildings. In comparison to the Central EU countries, EU structural funds were rarely mentioned. The more innovative EU countries are guided by renewable energy targets, energy efficiency targets, and GHG reduction targets, but they seem to be more proactive. In terms of EU and non-EU countries, the most striking difference is related to venture capital/high-risk early-stage funding where the landscape in both Israel and New Zealand is much more open to this compared to the EU. Objective 5: We collected data on Hong Kong’s innovation policies in the energy sector – including those related to the GBA. We also included Singapore in this analysis, to allow for comparison with an economic and regional peer (alongside the other countries in Objectives 2-4). We found four key points. (1) Hong Kong lacks an innovation strategy targeted at specific clean energy technology or clean energy technologies in general. (2) Hong Kong’s energy innovation strategy is characterized by heavy reliance on technology adoption policies, which has only been seen in the policy mixes of Hong Kong and Slovakia (which is a geographically large, highly industrial, and agricultural economy, very different from Hong Kong’s). (3) By contrast, the other 10 small economies examined (except Norway) tend to adopt strategic R&D and market creation policies. (4) Singapore shares features with the countries that focus on firm support, and facilitating knowledge development and diffusion. From this, we argue that Hong Kong. Thus, the policy mix and innovation strategy the government has adopted between 2008 and 2020 seems to present an inconsistent message that is still limited by the non-interventionist mindset leading to an overlook of targeted policy supports where they are most needed for technological innovation to take off and prosper domestically for sustainability transitions. A transition into new policy regimes is essential to Hong Kong’s successful socio-technical transitions. To make sure that the implications for Hong Kong are clearly highlighted, we broke them into a separate journal manuscript -these results are reflected in a paper under review (Please see Section C).

16602318.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602318.value: By mapping sustainability-related policies onto the analytical framework of FAMIS, we established that there is currently still an overall relative policy focus on the supply of inventions, knowledge, and skilled workforce by the small, developed, and innovative countries. While the theoretical suggestions on policies needed for sustainability transitions are rapidly advancing, novel policy tools are being picked up slowly in practice, and only among ‘innovation leaders.’ This implies that there are opportunities for policy learning from countries that were so far able to implement such novel policies, but also that there is a need to better connect practice with theory and to offer recommendations for governments in terms of their transition towards a more active, risk-taking and innovative roles. We also found that there are three significant policy gaps that currently hinder innovation for sustainable development. These gaps include the misalignment of concrete policies and innovation priorities, the near absent support for the production of technologies, and the limited support for technology adoption, adaptation, and retirement of technologies. Using correspondence analysis, we systematically assess the policy mixes and innovation strategies of top small country innovators and find that countries with a mixed economic system generally used more sustainability-related policy interventions and predominantly focused on targeted R&D funding and market creation (e.g., Denmark, and Sweden), whereas countries with a market economic system largely focused on policies that support firm innovation. In terms of strategies supporting firm innovation, one strategy that we observed focused on direct economic tools, especially providing high-risk early stage and expansion financing (e.g., Israel, New Zealand), while the other strategy focused on enabling a conducive environment for innovation through creating spaces, building networks and capacity (e.g., Switzerland). We also found that there is a relationship between the level of sector focus and related strategic capabilities, and the extent to which innovation strategies address the whole innovation system. Generally, government efforts are more balanced when sectors are of strategic importance, whereas public policy support is more haphazard when strategic priorities and capabilities are weaker depending on the sector. For example, in the case of the agriculture, water, and manufacturing sectors, policy efforts are mostly focused on invention and selection, while in the energy sector, technology adoption is a primary focus. These findings are reflected in two major papers currently under review, and one recently accepted (see Part C).

16602318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602318.value: Regional specific investigations with a stronger qualitative element: the Nordic countries have an especially identifiable set of strategies, and many regional policies, worth taking up as a group (including some of the larger countries, i.e. the Netherlands). After the PIs seminar with the Asian Productivity Organization, there is clear interest in investigations of whether there are similar policy tool choice models at play in south and south-east Asia, in middle-income countries with a different underlying context. This is an important possible extension to move beyond the OECD. Finally, we collected a great deal of data on the actual ministries involved. There is a potential for extension to move beyond cataloguing this data, and to engaging in a new round of data collection about the bureaux and ministries themselves, and the backgrounds of key innovation policy actors at the level of policy implementation, to better understand the nature, make up, and potential skills/knowledge gaps, and the implications for future sustainable innovations policy support. This would be especially useful in tandem with qualitative case studies and more detailed budget and outcome data (where available), for a more nuanced investigation of innovation policy dynamics that links implementation capacity and policy tool choice strategy.

16602318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602318.value: Sustainability is a major focus of policymakers around the world. Governments use innovation policy to support domestic environmental, social, and economic strategies. Many small, economically advanced countries are consistently ranked as leaders in innovation and sustainability. This research project focused on these countries to try and identify the policies their governments use to support ‘green’ or sustainable technologies. Through comparison of more than 1700 policies in 12 countries, we identified three areas as challenges for new, green technologies that have relatively few policies targeted to alleviate them. They are a gap between innovation strategy documents and concrete plans to implement them, a lack of attention to production needs as technologies transition from lab prototypes to commercialization, and too few policies to support actual adoption/market uptake of these technologies. This analysis is useful for countries that are working towards improving their use of innovation policy to support social needs. While there is not a ‘one size fits all’ answer to how countries can be both innovative and sustainable, this research provides needed context to help governments, experts, and also the private sector, make useful decisions about how to deploy their resources to better meet their strategic goals.

16602918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602918.value: In 2017, there are an estimated 21 million refugees in the world, and an additional 42 million forcibly displaced persons. While displacement due to war, famine, and natural disasters is a long-standing historical phenomenon, a formal definition of 'refugee' by the United Nations has only existed since 1951. Furthermore, the number of refugees worldwide has increased tenfold since the 1970s. Since 1974, approximately 50% of all refugees have resided for at least some period of time in a refugee camp. Few refugees simply pass through the camps on their way to more secure living situations; refugees who become camp residents spend an average of 17 years in camps. The number of people who have been born, passed their entire lives within the confines of a refugee camp, and then perished there is approaching one million. Originally, refugee camps were repurposed prisoner of war camps or barracks once used by active-duty soldiers in the first years of the Cold War. Initially imagined as temporary structures, the word 'camp' is misleading: over half of all refugee camps ever constructed – usually in haste – remain in operation today. A spike in the number of refugees between 2012-2016 has led to an increased interest in the experience of refugees, both contemporary and historical, but there has been comparatively little research into the role that refugee camps, as an administrative structure and physical space played in this process. The proposed project offers an in- depth history of six refugee camps that operated during the course of the 20th Century, with a focus on their story of origin, location, construction, the pattern of daily life for refugees living within the camps, the control, security, and administration of the camps, and the political and social controversies surrounding these camps. The camps selected are meant to represent an evolution in the size, scale, implementation, and purpose of refugee camps between 1948 (the year the United Nations began defining 'refugee') to 2010, when the refugee population, after hitting an all-time high in 1992, was (incorrectly) believed to be in permanent decline. The chosen camps are in Israel, Sudan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Tanzania, and Iran. 按2017年的估算，全球定義為「難民」的數字達到二千一百多萬人；另外，被迫流離失所的人口達四千二百萬人。因為戰爭、饑荒、天然災禍的原因而離開家園的人，在悠長歷史上一直出現，但是要到1951年，聯合國才正式確認「難民」的定義。時至今時今日全球的難民人口，比起上世紀七十年代，多達十倍。自1974年起，所有難民之中，有大約50%曾經住在某種形式的難民營內：只有少數難民是短暫居住，繼而轉到其他更安穩的居住環境；但是，難民滯留於難民營內的統計平均年期，長達17年。那些一生困在難民營內出生、長大及生存至死的人數，接近一百萬。 初期的難民營，是由冷戰時期早年，服役士兵使用過的戰地軍營或營房改建而成。本來這些臨時搭建的建築物，也算不上是什麼「營」；但是，包括那些匆匆建造，超過半數營運過的難民營，迄今仍在使用中。 2012年至2016年間全球難民數字飆升，針對難民親身體驗的當代及歷史資料，被受更多關注。可是，有關難民營裡的行政管理或空間運用及其角色意義的研究，的確相對較少。這個研究計畫，正正是要對準出現在二十世紀之中6個難民營的深度史料，尤其集中其起源、位置、建築、難民在營內的日常生活、監管、保安、行政措施，與及關於這些難民營的政治及社會爭議。我特意選擇研究1951年至2010年期間的這6個難民營，皆因在過去的60年間，它們在其大小、規模、建築及用途的變遷，均具有其代表性的歷史地位。 本研究計畫中的6個難民營，位於以色列、蘇丹、香港、泰國、坦桑尼亞及伊朗。

17100218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100218.value: Silver nanomaterials including silver nanoparticles, resin with silver nanoparticles, glass ionomer with silver nanoparticles and nano silver fluoride can be used to prevent caries progression. Silver nanomaterials have low cytotoxic effect on human cells. Silver nanomaterials can inhibit the growth of cariogenic bacteria and the adhesion of biofilm. They hinder the demineralisation of enamel and dentine and degradation of collagen. We have successfully synthesized chitosan-silver nanoparticles with epigallocatechin gallate and chitosan. Our study showed that the chitosan-silver nanoparticles have lower cytotoxicity towards human gingival fibroblasts and stem cells from human teeth than silver nitrate. Besides, the chitosan-silver nanoparticles had profound inhibition effect on growth of Streptococcus mutans and adhesion of biofilm. In addition, we found Chitosan-silver nanoparticles decreased production of lactic acid of Streptococcus mutans biofilm. Our studies also demonstrated chitosan-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride could remineralise dentine caries and reduce exposure of collagen. The addition of sodium fluoride did not influence the effect of silver nanoparticles on dentine caries in bacteria model. Besides, we also found the combination of silver nanoparticles and sodium fluoride did not stain carious lesion black. Hence, chitosan-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride can be a potential therapy to treat dental caries. Further clinical studies to substantiate our findings. We found the antibacterial concentration of developed polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles against Streptococcus mutans was lower than its cytotoxic concentration towards human gingival fibroblasts. The addition of sodium fluoride did not influence the antibacterial effect of polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles. Furthermore, polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride remained stable over 18-month store. We applied the polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride on dentine caries and found that thdy could promote remineralisation and protect the dentine collagen from degradation. In addition, the polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride did not stain teeth black in our laboratory study. Further research is necessary to evaluate the effect of polyethylene glycol-silver nanoparticles with sodium fluoride in clinical trials.
