17106718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106718.value: We have listed two major findings and research outcomes as follows. 1. We have adopted the most cutting-edge single-cell RNA sequencing technology to characterize every cells in nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) tumours, including cancer cells, tumour-infiltrated lymphocytes and other stromal cells. According to our data from droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on over 150000 cells from 17 newly diagnosed NPC patients, a total of 23 sub-clusters were discovered by unsupervised clustering. Normal tissue was also found to contain large number of epithelial cells that clustered with primary tumour and lymph predominant sub-clusters, which may indicate early development of tumour. Then we identified the sub-clusters that expanded and they were classified as Category 1. Most of the expansion were found to continue in neck lymph nodes. Sub-cluster 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 10, 15, 17 and 19 were found to belong to this category. Trajectory of cancer evolution was computed using Monocle 3 software and functional enrichment of each sub-clusters were analysed using Enrichr software. We found that category 1 sub-clusters were originated from normal tissue and included two particular evolution paths. Path 1 passed through sub-cluster 17 and developed to sub-clusters such as sub-cluster 7 and 10, which are mainly associated with locoregional spread, an indicator of high aggressiveness. Path 2 developed into sub-cluster 15 which are mainly related to immune response. Interestingly, sub-cluster 17 is mainly related to EBV signalling, indicating the important role of EBV in evolutionary development of aggressive subclusters, and EBV intervention may be important to terminate evolutionary development of aggressive cancer cells and unfavourable clinical prognosis. In summary, EBV is essential in evolutionary development of aggressive cancer sub-populations. 2. Copy number variation (CNV) analysis using inferCNV software identified clonal evolution of cancer cells from scRNA-seq data. Our findings showed highest degree of heterogeneity of cancer clones at T1 stage of NPC, indicating selection force existed in tumour that led to more homogenous clones. Our findings suggested that the homogeneous clones were likely originated from heterogenous clones and this re-enforced the possibility of identifying prognosis-predicting aberration at early diagnosis. Then we attempted to identify the CNV aberrations that might be correlated with clinical parameters. According to previous reports, TP53 is one of the gene most common for CNV loss in NPC. According to our scRNA-seq data, TP53 was not the most common. There are quite a number of genes with ≥ 13 patients out of 15 patents with primary tumour-normal tissue pair with primary tumour-to-normal tissue fold change ≥ 1.5. In contrast, TP53 was only found in 3 out of 15 (20%) patients having tumour-to-normal tissue fold change ≥ 1.5, cut-off for significantly higher CNV expression, although successful detection of cells harbouring TP53 mutation in patient samples was common. It was found that the percentage of patients with significantly higher level of TP53 CNV loss in tumour sample was quite consistent with previous report. Our results showed that scRNA-seq is capable of revealing previously overlooked mutated cells that harbour TP53 CNV loss.

17106718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106718.value: Based on the results of this study, we have already identified important genomic aberrations responsible for the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Besides, we have also identified important tumour cell subpopulations which correlate with more advanced clinical presentation of NPC. More importantly, we have proven that Epstein-Barr virus plays an essential role in the development of more aggressive cell types of NPC. We shall submit our research outcomes to high-impact peer-reviewed journals in the first half of 2022. In the future, we shall focus on the exact mechanisms of the clonal evolution and tumour heterogeneity of NPC development, which will provide us precious information on how to better treat and manage the more locoregionally advanced NPC in routine clinical practice. In addition, we will also investigate how immune cells and surrounding supporting cells interact with the tumour cells and decipher the mechanisms of tumour cell response or drug resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors in NPC and other types of solid cancers.

17106718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106718.value: In summary, we have adopted the most cutting-edge single-cell RNA sequencing technology and identified important clusters and subclusters of tumour cells and immune cells which are responsible for development of aggressive nasopharyngeal cancer cells which lead to an unfavourable clinical presentation and presentation. Furthermore, we have confirmed that Epstein-Barr virus is essential to the evolutionary development of aggressive cancer subpopulations. Besides, we found that copy number variation (CNV) aberrations are corrleated with the clinicopathological characteristics of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This provides us important information on the underlying oncogenic process of development of locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

17106918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17106918.value: 猩紅熱在兒童間的傳播以及其決定因素

17106918.label: Project Objectives
17106918.value: To develop a transmission model for scarlet fever and estimate the plausible range of epidemiological parameters that characterize the model To identify determinants of transmissibility in order to recognise high-risk and pivotal schools, and hence examine the impact of various targeted interventions
rows: To develop a transmission model for scarlet fever and estimate the plausible range of epidemiological parameters that characterize the model
To identify determinants of transmissibility in order to recognise high-risk and pivotal schools, and hence examine the impact of various targeted interventions

17106918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106918.value: 猩紅熱是一種通過直接接觸感染者的唾液和鼻液傳播、主要影響兒童的傳染病。猩紅熱個案於2011年在中國和2014年在英國達到了近期的高峰。在香港，2011年亦爆發了猩紅熱，導致兩名患者死亡；在這一年期間，有超過1,400個病例通報，超過了過去六年的總數。自此，通報數目一直維持在高水平。從2005 年至 2015 年期間超過 7,500 個猩紅熱通報病例中，我們發現在幼兒園和小學就讀的兒童發病率最高，但在長假期，特別是暑假之後，病例數會減少。這些觀察結果表明，幼兒園和小學在猩紅熱的傳播中有著重要的影響。 以往，大多數關於猩紅熱傳播動態的研究模型中，都假設了所有兒童有相似的人羣接觸模式，卻少有研究考慮到個別兒童的特定社交網絡。而社交網絡模型就是處理這問題的一個替代方法。一般來說，兒童與同一所學校的許多其他兒童有很多接觸和互動，但在學校以外和在學校假期時，與其他兒童的聯繫就會少得多；與其他網絡相比，一個具有「班級-學校-社區」這個結構的階層式分群網絡，可以更適合地去描述兒童的社交接觸模式。 因此，我們建議使用階層式分群網絡模型去研究兒童之間的猩紅熱傳播，從而幫助預測這個病的流行病學模式。這個傳播模型會先以電腦模擬構建，然後根據香港 (2000年後最早報告猩紅熱激增的其中一個地區) 在2011年爆發以後出現的案例來進行調校模型的參數，之後我們就可以通過模擬，估算出猩紅熱持續傳播和疫症爆發的可能性和潛在規模。我們還可以利用這個社交網絡模型的網絡中心度來找出猩紅熱病菌傳播的決定因素，從而辨別出被傳染風險較高，或是在猩紅熱的傳播中起著關鍵作用的學校特徵。以這些結果作為基礎，學校可以實施針對性校本控制措施，例如改善學童衛生，增加學童之間的社交距離，或學校停課等，去防止猩紅熱進一步傳播。

17107218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17107218.value: 利用放療前和放療中吞嚥治療來減低鼻咽癌病人放療後的吞嚥功能障礙

17107218.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17107218.value: Prof Chan, Ying Kuen Jason Dr Lee, Ho Fun Victor Dr Poon, Ming Chun Darren Dr Tsang, Raymond King Yin

17107218.label: Project Objectives
17107218.value: To determine the effectiveness of pre-treatment and in-treatment swallowing therapy in reducing swallowing dysfunction in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients treated with radiotherapy To determine the feasibility and compliance of nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients on swallowing therapy while undergoing radiotherapy
rows: To determine the effectiveness of pre-treatment and in-treatment swallowing therapy in reducing swallowing dysfunction in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients treated with radiotherapy
To determine the feasibility and compliance of nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients on swallowing therapy while undergoing radiotherapy

17107218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107218.value: Introduction - Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is the 7th commonest cancer in Hong Kong. With advances in radiotherapy, survival of early cancers is now over 80%. Unfortunately, radiotherapy still has long-term side effects including dysphagia and aspiration. Dysphagia and aspiration affect quality of life and can lead to life threatening chest infections. Traditionally, NPC patients will only be referred to speech therapist when swallowing dysfunction developed. Recently, the concept of preemptive swallowing exercise to reduce the development of swallowing dysfunction has emerged. Small-scale clinical trials in US and Europe have shown swallowing exercise during radiation treatment for head and neck cancer reduced the development of swallowing dysfunction. Similar strategy of preemptive swallowing exercise should be feasible in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients and should reduce swallowing dysfunction. Objectives of the study:- Primary Objective - To determine the effectiveness of pre-treatment and in-treatment swallowing therapy in reducing swallowing dysfunction in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients treated with radiotherapy. Secondary Objective - To determine the feasibility and compliance of nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients on swallowing therapy while undergoing radiotherapy. Study Design – The study is 3-year multi-centre prospective randomized trial recruiting 126 newly diagnosed NPC patients. Assessment tools for swallowing function include subjective “Functional Oral Intake Score” and quality of life assessment using “MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory”. Objective assessment will rely on videofluroscopic swallowing studies. Patients in the treatment arm will receive instructions to perform swallowing exercise at home during radiation treatment, while a speech therapist employed by the study will monitor the function and performance of the patients weekly during the treatment period. Patients in the control arm will received the conventional management of swallowing disorders for new case NPC patients and will be referred to speech therapist for assessment if the clinicians detect swallowing problems. All patients will have subjective and objective assessments of swallowing function before the start of radiotherapy, 6 months and 12 months after radiotherapy. Long-term assessment of swallowing function of this cohort is planned and will apply for a research grant in the future. Expected results and future research directions – the present study will determine the feasibility and magnitude of improvement of swallowing function when patients receive swallowing therapy during the period of radiotherapy. The results can help in deploying swallowing therapy for NPC patients during the period of radiation therapy before they develop swallowing dysfunction. Future research direction would include the type and intensity of swallowing therapies that would be most beneficial.

17107218.label: Realisation of objectives
17107218.value: The project aimed to recruit 126 newly diagnosed nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) patients from Queen Mary Hospital and Prince of Wales Hospital. Subject recruitment at Queen Mary Hospital started from mid-May 2019. The subject recruitment was soon disrupted by HKU campus closures and road closures in late 2019 and different pandemic measures from 2020. In response to the pandemic measures, subject recruitment could not take place at the Prince of Wales Hospital. The team worked closely with the Department of Surgery and Department of Oncology at the Queen Mary Hospital and in the end, a total of 78 newly diagnosed NPC patients were recruited. The project proposed to follow the participants from diagnosis to 1 year post-cancer treatment. Before the start of cancer treatment, all participants were assessed by a speech language pathologist on their swallowing functions clinically and through videofluoroscopic swallowing studies (VFSS). Participants were also invited to complete a swallowing-related quality of life questionnaire. Sixty-six participants completed all pre-treatment assessment, six only consented to complete the questionnaire by phone (refusing to return to hospital for the VFSS session), two did not complete the pre-treatment assessments and four withdrawn from the study after giving consents. In total, there were 72 participants who completed part or all pre-treatment assessments and were randomized into two groups: a treatment group (N = 37) and a control group (N=35). The treatment group were instructed by a speech language pathologist on how to conduct a series of swallowing exercises, that involved the jaw, lips, tongue and larynx. They were encouraged to download the 'Keep on Talking and Eating' app, which was developed by the project team to include videos of the swallowing exercises. The participants were encouraged to practice daily before and during the cancer treatment period, regular phone calls were made by the team to the treatment group to encourage exercise adherence. The control group received conventional care, which did not involve any consultation with a speech language pathologist unless swallowing difficulties occur during cancer treatment. All participants were invited to return for a VFSS session six months post-completion of cancer treatment. Among the 72 participants, 34 returned (treatment group N=21) and completed all assessment tasks, 11 only completed the questionnaire by phone (treatment group N=5), 25 did not return for any assessment (treatment group N=11) and 2 passed away. Participants were invited to return for a final assessment 1 year-post completion of cancer treatment. Among the 70 participants, 55 returned and completed all assessment tasks (treatment group N=29), 2 only completed the questionnaire by phone and 11 failed to return for final assessment (treatment group = 8). In the end, after taken into account of missing data, a total of 44 participants (treatment group N=24; control group N=20) were included in data analysis. Both groups had significantly poorer self-reported swallowing functions and related quality of life after cancer-treatment. In addition, the treatment group also had significantly more pharyngeal residue post-treatment with small to medium effect size when compared with the pre-treatment condition. The control group did not have any significant changes in the pharyngeal residue after treatment. No significant changes in penetration and aspiration was observed in both groups 6-months after cancer treatment. The effect of pre-treatment and in-treatment swallowing therapy in reducing swallowing dysfunction could not be clearly observed in the current study. It is hypothesized that the results were impacted by a number of factors: 1. the attendance rate for the follow up assessments were greatly impacted by COVID measures at the hospital. While the participants did not withdraw from the study, they did not or could not attend the post-assessments in person. For patients who did not wish return to the hospital, we completed the questionnaire data by phone. 2. it is not known how many of the participants were infected by COVID, however, it is clear from the literature and from clinical experience that there are post-COVID symptoms that would affect the NPC survivors' swallowing functions. Therefore it is not know to what extent the current observations were affected by COVID. 3. treatment compliance was also affected by the pandemic measures. Our research staff could not have frequent face-to-face interactions with the treatment group to monitor and encourage them to continue with the swallowing exercises during cancer treatment. It is clear that this reduced the treatment compliance in the treatment group. Some of the treatment group participants reported that they did not remember how to do the exercises by the time they returned for their 6-month post follow up assessment. The project team is now making use of the VFSS videos collected from this study to support a larger project on developing automated processing for detecting swallowing dysfunctions from VFSS examinations. It is anticipated that results will be available in 2025, which may help to improve the reliability and accuracy of identifying swallowing dysfunctions from VFSS examinations.

17107218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17107218.value: The current study confirmed that nasopharyngeal cancer survivors have reduced swallowing functions from 6 months post-cancer treatment. Participants have shown increased pharyngeal residue post-swallows 6-months post-cancer treatment. Such residue will increase their risk of aspiration, which may then lead to aspiration pneumonia. The results also showed that NPC survivors have poorer self-reported swallowing functions 6 months-after cancer treatment. At the same time, the NPC survivors reported that their diet required special preparation and limited choices due to the changes in their swallowing functions after cancer treatment. The current study supports the need to provide swallowing training and support to NPC survivors from cancer diagnosis. Participants in the treatment group of the study only received one session of swallowing therapy before cancer-treatment and did not have other face-to-face sessions with a speech language pathologist afterwards. The results showed that this may not be enough to promote better swallowing outcomes in the NPC survivors. It is recommended that future study may develop more intensive swallowing therapy to prevent NPC survivors from developing swallowing disorders.

17107218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17107218.value: Further study is needed to confirm the effect of pre-treatment and in-treatment swallowing exercises to reduce swallowing dysfunction in nasopharyngeal cancer survivors. Recent studies have confirmed the importance of prophylactic swallowing exercises to prevent long-term swallowing dysfunctions in head-and-neck cancer survivors. Future studies may focus on more effective way of delivering such prophylactic swallowing exercises. Our current study made use of a simple app for showing videos of swallowing exercises. The current study suggests that a more interactive app is needed to motivate patients to conduct the swallowing exercises, especially when the patients may not have access to seek face-to-face speech language pathology support. The team is currently developing swallowing-related interactive games to improve exercise adherence. It is anticipated that the games will be available in 2024 and will be piloted on different populations, including NPC survivors.

17107218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17107218.value: The project aims to investigate whether conducting swallowing exercises during the cancer treatment period would help to reduce swallowing dysfunctions in nasopharyngeal cancer survivors in the long-run. The project was impacted by the pandemic and could not fully reach its objective. The project confirmed that nasopharyngeal cancer survivors would start to experience reduced swallowing functions as early as 6-months post-cancer treatment. It is important to provide appropriate education and swallowing therapy to these cancer patients from cancer diagnosis, in order to increase their awareness and take measures to prevent long-term swallowing disorders. Future studies may consider providing regular swallowing therapy to NPC survivors from diagnosis to throughout the cancer treatment period to maximize the effect of such therapy on preventing long-term swallowing disorders.

17107718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107718.value: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 viruses continue to transmit zoonotically, with mortality higher than 60%. H5N1 patients developed severe viral pneumonia and progressed to respiratory failure. The underlying mechanisms of influenza-induced acute lung injury have not been well defined and there is no effective drugs currently available. Antivirals remain the primary choice of treatment but only effective to be administered at early stage of infection. Besides, antiviral-resistant strain continues to emerge. Significant improvements in survival rate and the pathogenesis of H5N1-infected mice were observed by combination treatment of antiviral and immunomodulatory drugs. These results suggest that antiviral, in combination with immunomodulatory intervention may be beneficial to human H5N1 disease. Platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR), is a receptor-tyrosine kinase, expressed in a number of cell types. There is very limited study on PDGFR’s role in influenza virus infection and cytokine induction. Up to now, there is one study reported the antiviral effects of a PDGFR inhibitor in influenza A virus infection. Tyrphostin A9, blocked three post-entry steps of the H1N1 virus life cycle in a cancer cell line. However, the levels of PDGFs and PDGFR activation have been associated with clinical severity and mortality of ARDS patients. Both alveolar epithelial cells and macrophages are the target cells of H5N1 virus infection within the human lung in autopsy studies and in ex vivo cultures. The dysregulation of immune response is believed to contribute to the pathogenesis of human H5N1 disease. Both cell types infected with H5N1 viruses elicit markedly stronger responses of proinflammatory cytokines than does seasonal influenza virus. Therefore, we propose to investigate the role of PDGFR in cellular entry, virus replication and cytokine induction during influenza A virus infection in physiologically relevant cell models—human primary alveolar epithelial cells and peripheral blood monocyte derived macrophages. We also propose to examine the therapeutic effects of combination therapy of a PDGFR inhibitor with an antiviral in treating severe human influenza disease in a mouse model. The elucidation of how PDGFR inhibitor exhibits antiviral and immunoregulatory effects not only defines a novel role of PDGFR in influenza infection but also uncovers more potential cellular molecules for future development of host-targeted anti-influenza therapy. The evaluation of the mouse study on therapeutic potential of a FDA-approved PDGFR inhibitor provides important information for future clinical study against severe human influenza disease and repurposing existng drugs could be a more rapid path to direct application for human health. 高致病性禽流感H5N1病毒持續在人畜傳播，人類患者死亡率高於60％。 H5N1患者發展為嚴重的病毒性肺炎並引致呼吸衰竭。而流感誘導的急性呼吸窘迫綜合症的機制尚未明確定義，目前尚無有效的藥物治療急性呼吸窘迫綜合症。抗病毒藥物仍然是治療的主要選擇，但必須在感染的早期階段服用才有成效。而且，抗病毒耐藥株持續出現。有H5N1感染小鼠的研究顯示，通過抗病毒藥物和免疫調節藥物的組合療法顯著改善小鼠的存活率和病理狀況。這些結果表明，抗病毒藥物與免疫調節干預相結合或可改善治療人類H5N1疾病的成效。 血小板衍生生長因子受體（PDGFR）屬於酪氨酸激酶受體的一種，許多細胞類型都會表達這種受體。關於PDGFR在流感病毒感染和細胞因子產生的研究非常有限。到目前為止，有一項研究報導了PDGFR抑製劑在甲型流感病毒感染的癌細胞起了抗病毒作用。這種抑製劑於H1N1病毒進入細胞後抑製了病毒複製週期的三個不同步驟。然而，PDGF和PDGFR活化水平與急性呼吸窘迫綜合症患者的臨床嚴重程度和死亡率相關。在屍檢研究和離體培養研究指出，肺泡上皮細胞和巨噬細胞都是人肺內H5N1病毒感染的靶細胞。據信免疫系統的過度反應是引致人類H5N1疾病的發病機制的原因之一。當H5N1病毒感染此兩種細胞引起的促炎細胞因子反應比季節性流感病毒更明顯更強。因此，這個研究計畫將評估PDGFR和甲型流感病毒感染期間的細胞進入，病毒複製和細胞因子產生的作用。病毒感染將會在最接近人類的人類原發性肺泡上皮細胞和巨噬細胞中進行。另外，我們將會測試PDGFR抑製劑與抗病毒劑聯合療法對於H5N1及嚴重流感的治療成效。 闡明PDGFR抑製劑如何表現出抗病毒和免疫調節的作用不僅定義了PDGFR在流感感染中的新角色，而且揭示了更多潛在的細胞分子，有助開拓未來宿主靶向抗流感治療的研究。利用現有FDA認可的PDGFR抑製藥物，研究對嚴重人類流感疾病的治療，為將來嚴重人類流感疾病的臨床研究提供了重要基礎，並且為藥物重新定位是直接應用於人類的快速途徑。

17108218.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17108218.value: Dr Fuente, Adrian Prof McPherson, Donald Bradley

17108218.label: Project Objectives
17108218.value: To determine whether there is general association between auditory status and blood group, using a comprehensive range of tests of cochlear function. To determine the specific blood group(s) associated with differences in auditory status.
rows: To determine whether there is general association between auditory status and blood group, using a comprehensive range of tests of cochlear function.
To determine the specific blood group(s) associated with differences in auditory status.

17108218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108218.value: Blood group is a factor that leads to greater risk of a wide range of health disorders. The four ABO blood groups (A, B, AB and O) have been linked with different pathologies. Individuals with blood group A are more prone to gastric cancer than those with other blood groups while individuals with blood group O have an increased risk of gastroenteritis and peptic ulcers than those with other blood groups (Rizzo, Caruso & Vasto, 2014). On the other hand, individuals with blood group O have a significantly decreased risk of developing coronary heart disease compared to those with other blood groups. AB blood group individuals are significantly more likely to experience heart disease and dementia than those with blood group O. The reasons for blood group antigen effects are thought to be diverse and not always related to their role in blood alone. Several studies have found an increased risk of noise-induced hearing loss in noise-exposed workers with blood group O. Globally, hearing loss is now the fourth leading cause of years lived with disability (Vos et al., 2016). Noise-induced hearing loss is a principal cause of hearing loss, with one-third of all cases of adult hearing loss attributed to it (NIH, 1990). Recent exploratory work done by our research group was the first to discover that blood group O individuals have a reduced inner ear response to sound compared to individuals with other blood groups. Our findings, if confirmed, will signpost new directions in the study of the inner ear and its vulnerability to hearing loss. Strong evidence of blood group-inner ear effects will show the need to consider the effects of blood antigens on the development and function of the inner ear. In addition, for workers exposed to noise, blood group will therefore need to be considered in risk assessment and hearing conservation programs. Our proposed research project therefore seeks to assess the hearing status of a large sample of participants and more fully explore the association between hearing status and blood group. The research project will involve the detailed assessment of human hearing function using series of specialised auditory tests. The proposed study will provide stronger evidence to support our hypothesis that blood group O is linked to differences in inner ear function compared with the three other major ABO blood groups. 血型是多種健康問題風險增加的因素。四種ABO血型（A，B，AB和O）已被證實與不同的病理有緊密關聯。例如A血型的人比其他血型的人更容易患上胃癌，而O血型的人患有胃腸炎和消化性潰瘍的風險比其他血型的人更高（Rizzo，Caruso和Vasto，2014）。另外，與其他血型的人相比，O血型的人患上冠心病的風險顯著較低。與O血型相比，AB血型的人患上心臟病和腦退化的可能性更大。血型抗原效應是有多種原因，並不單與它們在血液中的作用有關。一些研究發現，O血型的工人暴露於噪音引致的聽力損失風險會增加。現時，聽力損失是導致殘疾的第四大因素（Vos等，2016）。噪聲是引致聽力損失的主要原因，其中三分之一的成人是由於噪聲而損害聽力（NIH，1990）。我們研究小組最近的探索性研究首次發現，O血型與其他血型相比，內耳對聲音的反應降低。我們的研究結果如果得到全面證實，將會在內耳及其易受聽力損失方面找到新的研究方向。血型引至內耳對聲音不同反應的論據，表明需要考慮血液抗原對內耳發育和功能的影響。此外，對於長期暴露於噪音下的工人，需要在風險評估和聽力保護計劃中考慮血型的因素。我們提出的研究項目將評估大量參與者的聽力狀況，並全面探索其聽力狀況與血型之間的關聯。此研究項目將涉及使用一系列專業聽力測試對人類聽力功能進行詳細評估。擬議的研究將提供更有力的證據來支持我們的論據，即與其他三個主要ABO血型相比，O血型與內耳功能的差異有關。

17108618.value: 肥胖誘導的異常脂肪堆積是慢性肝病 (包括胰島素抵抗和非酒精性脂肪肝）的誘發因素之一。 儘管增加肝臟轉脂肪酸運體(CD36)促使的脂肪酸吸收已經被認為是導致非酒精性脂肪肝的主要原因，但是為何CD36的活性在非酒精性脂肪肝中會增加卻尚不清楚。從我們的初步數據顯示，有一種未知功能的新蛋白 (SH3 結構域結合蛋白激酶，SBK1) 可以調節肝臟中的脂質代謝。不僅如此，我們還發現了轉錄因子Nur77 是SBK1 的第一個蛋白底物。鑒於Nur77是肝臟脂質和葡萄糖代謝的重要調節因子，我們因此提出「SBK1-Nur77-CD36信號通路是增加脂肪酸在肥胖肝細胞中積累的新機理， 也是導致非酒精性脂肪肝出現的關鍵通路」的假設。為了驗證這一假設，我們將會（1）在肝細胞中詳細探討SBK1介導的相關分子變化，（2）確定Nur77是SBK1控制的其中一條代謝通路，（3）研究過量Nur77表達在肝臟中的代謝結果。綜上所述，我們的研究將揭示一種新分子機理來解釋異常脂質代謝如何形成非酒精性脂肪肝，並對於研發治療這種疾病的新策略具有重要意義。

17108618.label: Realisation of objectives
17108618.value: In this proposal, we hypothesize that high circulating lipid content in obese subject upregulates hepatic SBK1 expression and promotes the cytoplasm-nucleus shuttling of SBK1. Nuclear-residing SBK1 phosphorylates Nur77 to enhance its transcriptional activity on genes involved in lipid metabolism. To test this hypothesis, we have performed a variety of molecular, biochemical, and cellular assays in cultured hepatocytes. We have also performed in vitro assays to determine the molecular details of SBK1-Nur77 interaction, Moreover, the physiological parameters, energy and glucose homeostasis, and signaling mechanism were examined in SBK1 transgenic mice. Specific assays done are listed below: To achieve the Specific aim 1 “Studying the role of SBK1 in hepatic lipid and glucose metabolism in vitro”, we have (1) proved the regulatory role of fatty acid on SBK1 expression in the cultured hepatocytes; (2) determined the fatty acid uptake, lipid metabolism gene expression, and fatty acid accumulation in the cultured SBK1-deficient hepatocytes, and (3) evaluated the glucose production and related gene expression in the cultured SBK1-deficient hepatocytes. To achieve the specific aim 2 Delineating the functional outcomes of SBK1-mediated Nur77 phosphorylation, we have (1) identified the phosphorylation site of Nur77 by SBK1, (2) examined the effect of SBK1 phosphorylation on the transcriptional activity of Nur77 (3), tested the Nur77 phosphorylation status in obese liver, and (4) studied the Nur77-regulated genes in the liver-specific SBK1 knockout (LSKO) mice. To achieve the Specific aim 3 “Evaluating the role of SBK1 in promoting hepatic steatosis in vivo”, we have (1) developed the model liver-specific SBK1 transgenic mice; (2) Determined the physiological parameter including blood chemistry, tissue morphology, metabolite content, body weight, etc in the high fat diet-fed liver-specific SBK1 transgenic mice; and (3) insulin sensitivity of Ad-SBk1 mice. In summary, we have performed a large number of assays that have thoroughly addressed all Specific Aims set in the proposal.

17108618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108618.value: This study demonstrates that SBK1 is a novel regulatory kinase in the liver that protects against metabolic stresses via Nur77-mediated gene expression. Our data proposed that the ectopic accumulation of FA in the liver induces SBK1 transcription and its cytosol-to-nucleus shuttling. Nuclear SBK1 phosphorylates Nur77 and decreases its transcriptional activity to modulate the expression of genes for lipid anabolism (CD36, DGAT2, LDLR, etc.) in the liver. SBK1-mediated Nur77 phosphorylation is also critical for hepatic FGF21 production, which is responsible for inter-organ communication. When SBK1 was ablated in the liver of HFD-fed mice, reduced Nur77 S344 phosphorylation diminished the suppressive effect of Nur77 on hepatic genes for FA uptake and lipogenesis, leading to the development of hepatic steatosis. The Fgf21 production was also impaired in the liver of HFD-fed LSKO mice, leading to defective insulin sensitivity in these tissues and failure to disseminate the hepatic metabolic status to other tissues. Hepatic insulin signaling was also lower in the LSKO mice, possibly resulting from higher lipid accumulation in the tissue. In contrast, increasing the hepatic SBK1 expression via adenovirus-mediated gene delivery in the mice with fatty liver resulted in several beneficial outcomes, including alleviated hepatosteatosis, relieved hyperlipidemia, and reduced hepatic glucose output. Moreover, browning of gonadal white adipose tissue (gWAT) was also observed in the mice with high hepatic SBK1 content, which we rationalize as the consequence of FGF21-induced PPARa expression in the adipose tissue. In all, our data strongly suggest that the hepatic SBK1-Nur77 signaling has a dual role in protecting systemic metabolism during energy surplus - it prevents excessive FA uptake and TG synthesis in the liver on the one hand and promotes the production of hepatic FGF21 for inducing WAT browning on the other hand. Our findings were reported in 2 international journals “Current Topics in Medicinal Chemistry (Chan et al. 2019 19: 2188, 2022 impact factor: 3.400)”, and “Hepatology (Ahuja et al 2023 77: 213; 2022 impact factor: 13.5)”. Moreover, the projects have provided training opportunities to 2 Ph.D. candidates and 1 undergraduate student at the University of Hong Kong. Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, overseas traveling was hauled between 2019 to 2022. Hence, the PI has no opportunity to present his findings at any international conference.

17108618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108618.value: This project identifies SBK1 as a novel signaling molecule controlling lipid metabolism and systemic insulin sensitivity in obese animals. We have also proved that enhancing the expression of SBK1 in the liver of obese mice can significantly improve their liver from developing hepatosteatosis and increase systemic insulin sensitivity. Hence, pharmacological manipulation of SBK1 activity may represent a feasible method to treat obesity-related metabolic diseases such as diabetes and fatty liver disease. Therefore, more studies are needed to delineate the complete functional spectrum of SBK1 in the liver and other tissues to set the foundation for the future development of SBK1 activity.

17108618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108618.value: Obesity-induced lipid deposition in the liver is detrimental as it is strongly associated with severe health problems like fatty liver disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, and liver cancer. While the outcomes of fat accumulation in the liver have been well established, it remains unclear if the liver possesses any defensive mechanism to work against the damage. This project identified and proved that a novel protein called “SH3 domain binding kinase 1” is an important regulator of lipid metabolism. Using a variety of methods in cultured cell and knockout mice models, the project has revealed the action mechanism of SBK1 in protecting the liver from developing excessive lipid accumulation. Moreover, the project has also proved that increasing the amount of SBK1 in the liver can alleviate obesity-related metabolic problems in mice. These findings provide the foundations for further developing SBK1-based drugs to treat obesity-induced disorders.

17109918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109918.value: 標題 ：膽道閉鎖基因組：使用全基因組測序數據模擬疾病的先導性研究 摘要： 圍產期膽道閉鎖（PBA）是一種罕見，嚴重和復雜的疾病，其特徵是肝外膽管系統在嬰兒出生後的最初數週內會逐漸纖維硬化和炎性閉塞。唯一的治療方法是外科手術（門靜脈造口術 - Kasai手術），不幸的是，即使膽汁流恢復，在許多患者中，病情仍然會演變成漸進性的膽管炎症和硬化，導致繼發性膽汁性肝硬化，最終要進行肝臟移植。 PBA仍然是兒童中最嚴重的肝臟疾病，特別是在中國，其發病率高於其他國家。 PBA是一種非綜合徵型的疾病且以散發為主。 PBA的發病機制理論認為，在圍產期，一種未知的外源因子與遺傳易感個體的免疫系統接觸，觸發無法控制的免疫反應，導致肝臟纖維化和肝外膽管閉鎖。遺傳學上，免疫化學和基因表達研究表明，患者的遺傳易感性對PBA的發展至關重要。常見（存在於> 1％的人群中）和罕見（存在於<1％的人群中）的DNA變異都會導致包括PBA在内的複雜疾病。據推測，常見變異賦予一般人群易感性的背景, 而環境和/或罕見變異提供驅動易感個體患病的額外刺激。通過全基因組關聯研究（GWAS; N = 180），我們確定了第一個PBA基因位點，ADD3，並證明ADD3的常見變異不僅賦予對PBA的易感性，而且還解釋了亞洲PBA高發病率的原因。基於我們的假設，即罕見變異（新生- 非遺傳-或隱性遺傳）可能是那些罕見，嚴重疾病的發病基礎，我們建議對30個PBA核心家系進行全基因組測序（WGS）試點研究。這個假設有助於解釋PBA的散發性，嚴重性及其罕見性。我們將綜合分析 GWAS和正在進行的外顯子組測序（N = 80核心家系）的研究數據。此外，我們將利用我們實驗室特有的人體BA器官系統來測試所篩選的有害變異/基因的功能 。七百名BA患者將被納入後期的複製研究階段。 由於基因表達的時空控制在發育過程中至關重要，干擾非編碼調控區的DNA變異可能會導致先天性疾病。因此， 我們採用全基因組測序 (WGS) 這個方法。 這將是PBA的第一個WGS研究。综合PBA的遺傳結構以及使用人體器官系統來驗證DNA變異功能，將有助於闡明PBA的潛在機制。了解這種疾病是尋求治療的第一步。

17110818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110818.value: 巨結腸病（HSCR）是一種複雜的先天性疾病，因缺乏結腸神經，引起功能性腸梗塞。有部分HSCR患者也患有心室間隔缺損（VSD）。這種綜合症狀相信是由於腸道（ENCC）和心臟（CNCC）神經嵴細胞在腸道和心臟流出道（OFT）發育途中出錯，從而影響腸神經系統（ENS）和心臟的發育。儘管醫學界對此綜合症有相當多的臨床知識，但這種綜合症狀的成因仍未有確實的了解。 Vinculin（Vcl）通過影響介導粘著斑（FA）組裝來調節各種細胞運作。我們小組最近在HSCR患者中發現了7個新的VCL基因突變。更重要的是，在其中三個患有VSD-HSCR綜合症的患者中，都發現帶有影響VCL蛋白結構的M209L VCL基因突變。使用患者特異性誘導的多能幹細胞（hiPSC）模型，我們進一步證實M209L扞擾FA組裝，而損害hiPSC衍生的NCC的遷移和其神經元及平滑肌譜系分化。而校正此VCL突變便有效地恢復NCC功能。在小鼠實驗中，當Vcl在NCC中被敲除時（VclKO），小鼠在出生後幾小時死亡，並有OFT，VSD和結腸神經發育畸形。我們的數據還表明，丟失了Vcl不僅擾亂了NCC的遷移，而且破壞其後的細胞分化。但VclKO小鼠沒有明顯的顱面缺陷。我們相信Vcl對腸道和心臟神經嵴細胞有特定的功能。擾亂Vcl會同時破壞腸道的神經元和心臟的平滑肌譜系的分化，從而導致HSCR / VSD綜合症狀。我們建議用利用VclKO小鼠模型來研究Vcl 在NCC中的功能，並特別關注Vcl是如何影響1）腸神經系統的發育；2）心臟流出道的發育、心室分隔和大血管的形成; 3）分析ENCC和CNCC分化的分子機制，以找出引致心臟和ENS缺陷的基因和病因。值得注意的是，建立這種罕見的遺傳疾病模型將有助我們對各種先天性疾病的研究，從而為這些複雜的先天性疾病找出新的診斷方法。

17110918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110918.value: The relapse rate is high in patients with psychosis. Even with maintenance medication treatment, relapse occurs in 40% of the recovered patients. The consequences of relapse including hospitalization and financial burden can be substantial. Unfortunately, some of these consequences can be irreversible and may lead to treatment refractory. Relapse prevention planning is therefore crucial. Existing clinical guidelines suggest maintenance antipsychotics treatment should be continued for at least 1 year following remission from first episode psychosis. Although continuing treatment can reduce the risk of relapse by approximately 2-fold, antipsychotics treatment is not without side effects, and the psychological burden of needing to take medication long-term is demoralizing to patients. On the other hand, non-pharmacological interventions such as cognitive behavioral therapy require substantial resources and professional training, and is difficult to implement in countries where resources are limited. One key precipitating factor of psychotic relapse is stress. Studies have shown that relapsed patients had experienced more stressful life events at 2- to 4-week prior to its occurrence; and negative comments from their carers can also incur stress in patients leading to a relapse. We believe that the exploration of non-pharmacological intervention that modulates stress, such as mindfulness intervention, is key to relapse prevention in psychosis. Nowadays, practicing mindfulness is popular and well-accepted for its benefits in improving mental and physical health. In particular, its benefits in promoting resilience to stress and well-being have been shown in studies involving different psychiatric conditions, as well as preventing relapse in patients with depressive disorders. However, its role in relapse prevention among patients with psychosis has not been tested. We therefore propose a multi-site, single-blind, 12-month randomized controlled trial (RCT) in Hong Kong to examine the effectiveness of mindfulness intervention in prevention of relapse among 152 remitted psychosis patients. Through mindfulness (no equipment needed, not costing any money to practice, and can be practiced at any time and place convenient to patients), we hope to alter and provide patients with an alternative response in face of stressful situations, and thus reduce the risk of relapse in psychosis. 思覺失調患者康復後仍有機會復發。研究發現即使是康復中而又維持藥物治療的病人，復發率可高達四成。復發的後果包括住院，經濟上的負擔，甚至可能遇上一些不可逆轉的後果，以及導致身體內產生抗藥性的情況。 預防復發是重要的一環。現時臨床指引建議，首發性思覺失調患者在康復後至少一年仍需繼續使用抗思覺失調藥物，以防止復發。雖然康復期間維持藥物治療可減低大概兩倍的復發率，但長期服食抗思覺失調藥會對患者會帶來副作用及心理上的負擔。 於是不少提出非藥物治療，例如認知行為治療，可是這些都需要巨大資源及專業訓練，在資源有限的國家便難以實行。 壓力是其中一個導致復發的因素。研究顯示思覺失調患者復發前兩至四個星期經歷了更多生活壓力事件。些外，照顧者的負面評語亦會增加患者的壓力，從而提高復發的機會。我們認為非藥物治療，例如靜觀練習，可幫助病人面對及處理壓力，是預防思覺失調復發的關鍵。 現今，靜觀練習是一種有效及受歡迎的訓練。在不同類型的精神病研究顯示，靜觀練習能有效提升抗壓能力及有助身心健康，也可預防抑鬱症復發。但靜觀練習在預防思覺失調症復發的成效還未試驗過。 在各區醫院，通過爲期一年的單盲及隨機分派的臨床研究，我們將152名思覺失調患者分組，並研究靜觀練習對預防思覺失調復發的成效。我們希望透過靜觀練習 (這項不需設備及金錢，亦可在任何時間地點使用的訓練) 去提升患者面對及處理壓力的能力，從而減低思覺失調復發的風險。

17111118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111118.value: Lysine succinylation is a newly discovered post-translational modification with distinctive physical properties. However, to date rarely have studies reported effectors capable of interpreting this modification on histones. Following our previous study of SIRT5 as an eraser of succinyl-lysine (Ksuc), we have recently identified the GAS41 YEATS domain as a pH-dependent reader of Ksuc on histones. Biochemical studies showed that the GAS41 YEATS domain presents significant binding affinity towards H3K122suc. Furthermore, cellular studies showed that GAS41 had prominent interaction with H3K122suc on histones, and also demonstrated the co-enrichment of GAS41 and H3K122suc on p21 promoter. The YEASTS domains have previously been reported to function as an acetyl (Kac) or crotonyl-lysine (Kcr) reader. In this application, we propose to investigate the molecular mechanism of how the YEATS domain of GAS41 recognizes different histone modifications by solving the crystal structures of the GAS41 YEASTS domain in complex with an H3 Ksuc, Kac or Kcr peptide, respectively. We will also comprehensively profile GAS41 readouts of histone Ksuc and other acyl-lysines. As GAS41 is amplified in many types of human cancer, the molecular mechanism revealed by the complex structures will be utilized to develop specific inhibitors against GAS41 and thus provide a potential therapeutic target for cancer treatment. 賴氨酸琥珀酰化是一種新發現的具有獨特物理特性的翻譯後修飾。然而，迄今為止很少有研究報告能夠解釋對組蛋白的這種修飾。延续我們之前SIRT5作為琥珀酰賴氨酸（Ksuc）eraser的研究，我們最近確定了GAS41 YEATS結構域作為Ksuc對組蛋白的pH依賴reader。生化研究表明GAS41 YEATS結構域對H3K122suc具有顯著的結合親和力。此外，細胞研究表明GAS41在組蛋白上對H3K122suc具有顯著的相互作用，也證明了GAS41和H3K122suc在p21啟動子上的co-enrichment。之前已報告過YEASTS結構域与乙酰基（Kac）或巴豆酰基 - 賴氨酸（Kcr）的作用。在這個课题中，我們建議通過解析GAS41的YEASTS結構域分別與H3 Ksuc，Kac或Kcr肽複合的晶體結構來研究GAS41的YEATS結構域的分子機制。我們還會全面描绘GAS41識別組蛋白Ksuc和其他酰基賴氨酸的模式。由於GAS41在許多類型的人類癌症中被擴增，通過複合結構顯示的分子機制將用於開發針對GAS41的特異性抑製劑，從而為癌症治療提供潛在的治療靶點。

17111118.label: Realisation of objectives
17111118.value: Objective 1: To analyze the structural basis of GAS41 as a Ksuc, Kac or Kcr reader. YEATS domain-containing proteins have been reported as readers of acetyl lysine (Kac) or crotonyl lysine (Kcr) on histones. Our previous biochemical and cellular studies revealed that GAS41 is a pH-dependent lysine succinylation (Ksuc) reader. Succinylation is a newly discovered PTM with distinct structural and chemical properties. In the current study, GAS41 and H3K122suc peptide co-crystallization was attempted to investigate the underlying binding mechanisms. We obtained crystals in plate shape from new crystallization condition compared to that rod-like in our previously reported data. Crystals were then taken to the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility (SSRF) and X-ray diffraction data were collected and processed. We determined the structure. However, the H3K122suc peptide was not observed in the structure and instead an oligermeric state formation of GAS41 was seen. Ten molecules were discovered in an asymmetric unit with head to tail binding manner. Interestingly, the readout pocket of GAS41 was occupied by several residues from the N terminus of the neighboring GAS41 molecule mainly by hydrogen bonds, indicating a new inhibition mechanism of GAS41. Objective 2: To profile GAS41 readouts of histone Ksuc and other acyl-lysines Currently there are more than 20 Ksuc sites identified on various histones in cancer cells, which urges further investigation on profiling GAS41 readouts of other potential histone Ksuc sites and other types of acyl-lysines with a terminal carboxyl group including malonyl- (Kmal) and glutaryl-lysine (Kglu), to comprehensively elucidate GAS41-mediated epigenetic regulation. In order to understand the mechanism of human GAS41 readout of potential acyl lysines, we have tried to co-crystallizes GAS41 with Ksucc, Kmal and Kglu modified H3K9 peptides. Crystals were then obtained by using crystallization screening. Next, the crystallization conditions were further optimized. Unfortunately, the Covid-related travel restrictions between Hong Kong and Mainland China have prevented us from taking these crystals to SSRF for X-ray diffraction data collection. Objective 3: To develop structure-based inhibitors for GAS41. As GAS41 is amplified in many types of human cancer, enriches on the promoter region and participates in transcription activation of p21 oncogene upregulated in cancer, the structural studies on GAS41 in complex with its binding partners may provide a promising direction of designing inhibitor used for cancer therapy. In collaboration with Professor HZ Sun’s group in the HKU Department of Chemistry, we used the swiss-ADME program to do virtual screening of potential inhibitors for GAS41. The GAS41 oligomeric structure was used as the search model. In consideration of the p-value in the virtual screening result, a promising compound Trichostatin A (TSA) was chosen as a potential inhibitor. We then compared the binding capabilities of TSA with human GAS41 and other human YEATS domains-containing protein AF9 and ENL. The MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrum result shows TSA could bind to GAS41 and also in a concentration dependent manner while no capacities to others. This indicates the specificity of TSA to GAS41. The measurement of this binding affinity by SPR was 167μM. Furthermore, we co-crystalized GAS41 in complex with TSA. Crystals were obtained and X-ray diffraction data were collected at SSRF. We then solved the complex structure of GAS41 and TSA at 2.4 Angstrom resolution to illustrate the inhibition mechanism. We superimposed the structure of GAS41/TSA complex with Yaf9/H3K122suc complex structure. In the structure of GAS41/TSA complex, TSA anchored in the readout pocket of GAS41 for the accommodation with succinyl lysine. The distinct residues on the flexible loops may explain the binding specificity of TSA towards GAS41 rather than the other human YEATS domains. Our findings have establish the potential of TSA as a GAS41 inhibitor.

17111118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111118.value: In this project, we used virtual screening, MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrum, binding affinity by SPR and co-crystallization to identify and characterize a small molecule, Trichostatin A (TSA), as a novel GAS41 inhibitor. We solved a crystal structure of decamer GAS41. Interestingly, the protruding N-terminal of each monomer interacts into the reader pocket of the adjacent monomer mainly by hydrogen bonds. Moreover, the N-terminal was well superimposed with acyl-lysine in other published GAS41 structures. The decamer structure reveals a new insight for developing peptide-based inhibitors of GAS41. In a related project, we worked with our collaborators (HY Sun and L Zhang) at CityU of Hong Kong on profiling the proteins that interact with a dual-function lipoylation probe developed in HY Sun’s lab (See Output #1 - JACS, 2019, 141(46), 18428-18436). In a related project, we developed a general method to utilize cryo-EM maps for X-ray crystal determination (see output #2, Acta Cryst D, 2020, 76 (1), 63-72). The preliminary data that led to this project on the identification of the YEATS domain of GAS41 as a pH-dependent reader of histone succinylation were published (see output #3, PNAS, 2018, 115(10), 2365-2370).

17111118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111118.value: 1. Based on the crystal structures of GAS41-H3K122suc, GAS41-H3K122cr and GAS41-H3K122ac complexes, mutagenesis can be used to validate if the elimination or impairment on the binary interaction between mutated GAS41 and histone H3 with K122suc, K122cr or K122ac also occurs at the cellular level. 2. To fully understand the regulation on epigenetic codes by GAS41, SPR can be used to measure the binding constant between GAS41 and different peptides with Ksuc, Kcr, Kac, Kmal or Kglu modifications. 3. The gene expression level of the genes with and without inhibitors (such as TSA identified in Objective 3) can be compared via ChIP-qPCR assay. The results will show if the inhibitors will indeed affect the interaction between GAS41 and those modifications and their potential impact on cancer development.

17111118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111118.value: Glioma amplified sequence 41 (GAS41) is highly expressed in several tumor cell lines and promotes oncogene transcription via recognition of particular histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) including Ksuc, Kac and Kcr. We have identified the GAS41 YEATS domain as a pH-dependent reader of Ksuc on histones. Biochemical studies showed that the GAS41 YEATS domain presents significant binding affinity towards Ksuc. In this project, we have investigated the molecular mechanism of how the YEATS domain of GAS41 recognizes different histone modifications by solving the crystal structures of the GAS41 YEASTS domain in complex with Ksuc, Kac or Kcr peptides, as well as promising small molecule inhibitors. As GAS41 is amplified in many types of human cancer, the molecular mechanism revealed by the complex structures can be utilized to develop specific inhibitors against GAS41 and thus provide a potential therapeutic target for cancer treatment.

17111518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111518.value: With the advancement of information communication technologies (ICTs), instant messaging applications (IM Apps, e.g. WhatsApp and WeChat) can be used for providing synchronous, personalized, interactive interventions for health promotion. We propose to apply IM Apps for enhancing our tested brief smoking cessation (SC) intervention model from AWARD to e-AWARD (AWARD: Ask, Warn, Advise, Refer, Do-it-again,) without medications to increase SC in smokers proactively recruited in smoking hotspots in Hong Kong. Such smokers are the majority and have low quit rate. IM Apps allows trained SC advisors to proactively deliver personalized SC advices, response to smokers’ needs promptly, and provide psychosocial support. No similar trials are found in PubMed, Cochrane Library and trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov & ISRCTN) (except our pilot trial). The present proposal is based on the success of our pilot qualitative study and feasibility trial. Smokers regardless of their intention to stop or reduce smoking will be proactively recruited at smoking hotspots and individually randomized into the Intervention or Control group (n=348 each group). Both groups will receive face-to-face brief advice using the AWARD model at baseline and actively refer to SC service if preferred. The proposed 12-week intervention guided by Social cognitive theory and Transtheoretical model consists of (1) proactive regular personalized (based on gender, occupation, motivation to quit, nicotine dependence and self-efficacy of quitting) messages and (2) synchronous IM Apps psychosocial support, delivered by trained SC advisors. Regular messages (including text, picture, animation and video) are important as probes to initiate and maintain the IM Apps conversation or interaction with smokers. IM Apps will be used to provide synchronous, personalized, interactive SC advices, psychosocial support and active referral to SC service providers. The Control group will only receive similar intensity regular messages on general health and reminders on follow-up surveys. Primary outcomes include exhaled carbon monoxide validated abstinence at 6-month and 12-month. Secondary outcomes include self-reported past 7-day abstinence, 24-week continuous abstinence, smoking reduction, self-efficacy of quitting, intention to quit, quit attempts and SC medications and services use at 6-month and 12-month. Qualitative interviews, mediation and economic analyses will be done to study the intervention mechanisms and cost-effectiveness. Outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group allocation. We will follow CONSORT strictly. This world’s first RCT will provide much needed timely evidence on using IM Apps for SC. The intervention is highly applicable to reduce smoking prevalence and related harms in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

17111518.label: Realisation of objectives
17111518.value: We have organized a smoking cessation (SC) training workshop in September 2018 for 30 undergraduates (mostly from nursing major) and all of them passed the examination and become SC advisors. The recruitment lasted for a year from December 2018 to November 2019. We recruited 700 participants from community settings, slightly larger than the planned sample size of 696. Half (350) were individually randomized to the Intervention group and the remaining were assigned to the Control group. Experienced SC counselors supervised the intervention delivery at recruitment sites and through WhatsApp on smartphones as planned. By October 2020, we finished all 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups with retention rates of 69.3%, 65.1%, and 63.7%, respectively, which are comparable to many other SC trials. No significant difference in attrition was observed between groups. Ten calls and 1 reminder message were made to boost up response before a case was dropped as unsuccessful. After the completion of last follow-up, we have conducted individual in-person interviews with 38 participants (both quitters and non-quitters) from the Intervention group to understand user experience. Among 700 participants, 24.2% were aged 40-49 and 72.1% were male. 43.6% smoked their first cigarette within 5 mins after waking, 44.6% smoked ≤10 cigarettes daily and 77.2% planned to quit within 30 days (intent to quit). Baseline characteristics were similar between the two groups except for fewer intervention group participants had previous quit attempts (37.3% vs. 45.4%, P=0.04). Many participants (95.6%) were referred to SC services at baseline and in the first 3 months after randomization. Objective 1: The interventions have been delivered to participants smoothly without any adverse event reported. The main effect has been assessed according to the registered protocol (NCT03800719). Self-reported quitters at 6- and 12-month joined biochemical validations to test exhaled carbon monoxide (CO). The corresponding participation rates were 41.0% and 43.8%, which were comparable to those of the previous trials. Only 2 self-reported quitters at 12-month had relapsed before joining the CO tests. We have followed the intention-to-treat approach (e.g. not joining the test as smoking) to compare the rates of validated smoking abstinence between groups and calculated relative risks (RRs) using Poisson regressions, with and without adjusting for imbalanced baseline characteristics. Objective 2: All planned secondary outcomes were collected including self-reported past 7-day abstinence, 24-week continuous abstinence, smoking reduction, self-efficacy of quitting, intention to quit (planned quit date), quit attempts and SC medications and services use at both 6- and 12-month. Missing data were mostly from participants who refused the entire follow-up surveys (34.9% and 36.3%, respectively). Similar to main analysis, intention-to-treat approach and RRs from Poisson regressions were used with or without adjusting for imbalanced baseline characteristics. Subgroup analyses based on intention to quit at baseline and whether participants had chatted with SC advisors on WhatsApp were also conducted. Among all secondary outcomes, the self-reported past 7-day point prevalence abstinence was similar between the Intervention (9.1%) and the Control (8.3%) group at 6-month (P>0.05). The corresponding rates of smoking reduction by 50% or more of the baseline daily cigarette consumption (28.6% vs 23.1%), accumulated quit attempts (14.0% vs. 10.3%) and service use (25.7% vs 24.0%) were also similar (all Ps>0.05). The corresponding figures at 12-month were similar between groups: 13.1% vs. 14.3% for self-reported abstinence, 6.3% vs. 6.0% for 24-week continuous abstinence, 31.7% vs. 34.9% for smoking reduction, 20.6% vs. 18.0% for quit attempt. In participants who remained smoking at 6-month, 36.7% smoked their first cigarette within 5 mins after waking, 53.7% smoked ≤10 cigarettes daily, 7.7% had quit attempts in the past 30 days, and 27.8% planned to quit within 30 days. These outcomes were similar between groups. The corresponding figures at 12-month were: 36.8% first used cigarettes within 5 mins after waking, 56.1% consumed ≤10 cigarettes daily, 4.3% tried to quit in the past 30 days, and 22.7% planned to quit within 30 days, and these outcomes were similar between groups. Objective 3: Data of all planned mediators have been collected. We have used quit attempt and service use at 3-month as mediators to explore the potential mechanism between intervention effect on 6-month validated quitting. We have also conducted a similar casual mediation analysis on 12-month quitting outcomes using 3- and 6-month factors. We regressed the group allocation on mediators and calculated the inverse of the treatment-mediator odds ratios, which was used to weight the regression of the outcomes on group allocation. The weighted regressions estimated the natural direct effects, and indirect effects were identified by subtracting direct effects from total effects. Objective 4: We estimated the cost of the interventions from the following 3 components: (1) training, including cost for a research nurse to introduce smoking cessation and counseling skills, a professor for delivering knowledge in tobacco control, research staff for project introduction and training notes; (2) recruitment and baseline intervention delivery, including the cost of trained SC advisors for recruitment, the health warning leaflet distributed, smokerlyzer mouthpiece for exhaled CO test, and manpower for transferring smokers’ information to SC service providers; (3) follow-up interventions, including the cost of trained SC advisors for sending personalized regular messages and providing synchronous psychosocial support to the Intervention group participants through conversations on WhatsApp, sending messages on general health through SMS to the Control group participants, and a short booster at 3-month follow-up before the administration of the survey. The costs per participant and per quitter were compared between groups. The total operating cost for the Intervention group was US$ 7152.6, which equals US$ 20.44 per participant, US$ 510.9, and US$ 376.5 per validated quitters at 6 and 12-month, respectively. The corresponding costs for the Control group were US$6160.9, US$ 17.6, US$ 560.1, and US$ 293.4, respectively. We have administered the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire (measuring problems in mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression on 5-point Likert-like scales) at baseline and the 12-month follow-up. Missing data at baseline (<10%) were mostly due to time constraints (e.g. the participant needed to catch a bus or return for work). At 12-month, they were mostly from participants who refused the follow-up. The responses have been transformed using the standard Hong Kong value set to assess participants’ value of health state (quality of life). The valued of adults in Hong Kong ranged from -0.865 (the worst) to 1 (the best). The transformed values at baseline and 12-month were used to construct the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) and the area under the curve (AUD) was compared between groups. We have consulted the Co-I with health economic analysis background. Markov simulation model to assess the long-term cost-effectiveness were not used as quit rates and the value of health state were similar between the two groups at the 12-month follow-up. Using similar inputs in the models is unlikely to find a significant difference in simulation outcomes. Objective 5: We have individually interviewed 38 participants in person of the intervention group, including 16 quitters and 22 non-quitters using a semi-structured interview guide. Of these 38 interviewees, 15 had replied on WhatsApp while 23 had not. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The transcripts were analyzed following the thematic analysis approach to understand participants' experience of the intervention. The results have been confirmed by the qualitative researcher Co-I.

17111518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111518.value: At 6- and 12- month follow-up, the corresponding validated abstinence was 4.0% and 5.4% in the Intervention group, and 3.1% and 6.0% in the Control group (both Ps>0.05). Compared with the Control group, RRs of validated abstinence were 1.27 (95% CI 0.59-2.77) at 6-month and 0.92 (0.63-1.33) at 12-month. The corresponding RRs were 1.31 (0.60-2.85) and 0.95 (0.52-1.75) adjusting for quit attempts at baseline. Compared with the Control group, the Intervention group showed a higher 24-week continuous abstinence (3.1% vs. 0.9%; RR 3.74, 95% CI 1.07-13.12) at 6-month, and more service use (35.1% vs. 28.0%; RR 1.26, 1.01-1.57) at 12-month. In smokers without intention to quit, the intervention had no effects on all quitting outcomes (all Ps>0.05). In smokers with intention to quit, the intervention had effects on self-reported quitting at 6-month (RR 1.74, 95% CI 1.10-2.76) and service use at 12-month (1.31, 1.03-1.67). Marginally significant effects were also observed for 24-week continuous abstinence (2.97, 0.82-10.76) and smoking reduction by at least 50% (1.29, 0.96-1.73) (both Ps<0.10) at 12-month. Intervention group participants who had chatted with SC advisors on WhatApp had a higher validated abstinence (3.13, 1.25-7.81), 24-week continuous abstinence (8.09, 1.97-33.17), smoking reduction by at least 50% (1.85, 1.33-2.57), quit attempt (1.99, 1.14-3.45) and service use (1.84, 1.34-2.53) at 6-month, compared with the Control group participants. Significant effects were also found on smoking reduction by at least 50% (1.41, 1.07-1.86), making quit attempt (1.77, 1.18-2.65), and service use (2.08, 1.61-2.69) at 12-month. Casual mediation analyses did not identify significant mediators. Participants had only minor problems in their health status at baseline (0.973) and did not differ between groups (P=0.17). The values of health (0.964) were also similar at 12-month (P=0.91) with only a minimal decrease from baseline in both groups. AUDs of ROCs were 0.971 for the Intervention group and 0.967 for the Control group. The intervention was not associated with changes in values of health. Regular messages and interactive chatting on WhatsApp were well received by most of the interviewees. They found it a flexible way to interact, especially those who were used to communicate by voice messages instead of texts. WhatsApp messages were generally regarded as providing relevant information, warm support, encouragement, and friendly reminders. Non-responding to messages were due to not used to do so or not trying to quit. Regardless of smoking status, nearly all interviewees considered messages not the most important determinants of quitting.

17111518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111518.value: More studies are need to understand the long term effects of using instant messaging (IM) apps to promote smoking cessation. We found IM intervention may be effective for smokers who were interested in interaction and intended to quit. IM apps can be cost-effective to reach many community smokers with automated regular messaging and responses to frequently asked questions by an automated system (e.g. chatbot). The system can be supplemented by experienced SC advisors/counselors providing more in-depth psychosocial support for those needed. Built on the results of this project, we have collaborated with the main cessation service provider in Hong Kong to provide a chatbot on WhatsApp promoting the service and debunking the myths of pharmacological treatments for smoking. Further studies should improve the engagement of smokers on responding to messages and interacting with SC advisor in IM app as more interaction with increased the likelihood of quitting. Initial face-to-face engagement and subsequent compliance to IM messages and chatting with SC advisors should be better measured and improved. Providing incentives to increase engagement may be helpful as shown in another trial. We will further investigate how to optimize mHealth intervention for addictive behaviors by enhancing engagement, compliance and automated personalized responses.

17111518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111518.value: We conducted the world’s 1st trial to evaluate whether regular personalized messages and synchronous psychosocial support by smoking cessation (SC) advisors through WhatsApp increase quitting (vs. regular messages on general health through SMS). All smokers received brief advice on SC and referral to SC services at baseline. Participants were followed up at 3, 6, and 12-months. Self-reported quitting was biochemically validated. The quitting results were generally similar between 2 groups, except for more service use in the intervention group. The WhatsApp intervention was effective in smokers with intention to quit and in smokers who chatted with SC advisors. The intervention was well received by participants, which was flexible and provided relevant information, warm support, encouragement, and friendly reminders. Non-responding to messages were due to not used to do so or not trying to quit. These results suggest the intervention supported smokers in quitting, particularly in those who were interested in interaction. Instant messaging apps can be a cost-effective way to reach many community smokers and help those who intend to quit. Automated regular messaging and responses by a smarter chatbot could reduce the manpower burden, while SC advisors/counselors can chat with smokers who need more in-depth psychosocial support.

17111618.label: Realisation of objectives
17111618.value: Objective 1: To dissect the interaction between p85β and AXL. We have constructed multiple cell lines stably expressing p85β shRNA or p85β overexpression plasmid. Complementarily, we also performed gene silencing experiment using p85β-specific siRNA. Using these cell line models, we have confirmed the regulation of AXL by p85β. Essentially, p85β depletion led to reduced expression level of AXL, wherease p85β overexpression caused enhanced AXL level. In addition to cell lines, we assessed the correlation between the expression of p85β and AXL in ovarian cancer patient samples using immunohistochemistry. The analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation between the two proteins (Pearson correlation coefficient r=0.6, P<0.0001). Further, the regulation of AXL by p85β was independent of p110. Inhibition of p110 by pan-110 inhibitor (PIK-90), p110α-specific inhibitor (BYL719) or p110β-specific inhibitor (TGX-221) could not abolish p85β-induced expression of AXL. After establishing that p85β regulates AXL expression, we then investigated the potential role of AXL in the oncogenicity of p85β. Strikingly, our data indicated that AXL mediates the oncogenic activities of p85β. We investigated the involvement of AXL in p85β-induced phenotypes and p110 activity. AXL was inhibited by dominant negative AXL or AXL inhibitor (TP-0903). Cell proliferation, colony formation and cell invasion induced by p85β were all abrogated upon inhibition of AXL by the two approaches. The induced catalytic activities of p110α and p110β were also abolished by AXL inhibition. Together, these data indicated that p85β induces AXL protein expression to promote p110 activities which may in turn initiate downstream oncogenic signaling. Objective 2: To elucidate the regulatory mechanism of AXL by p85β. We found that p85β regulates AXL via post-translational mechanism. AXL mRNA level and promoter activity were not changed in PIK3R2-depleted cells. Cycloheximide chase experiments revealed that PIK3R2 depletion reduced the half-life of AXL protein. We observed an accumulation of ubiquitinated AXL in the presence of PIK3R2 siRNA. Further, PIK3R2 depletion failed to decrease AXL protein level upon treatment with chloroquine, but not with MG132 or lactacystin, suggesting that AXL is regulated by p85β via the lysosomal pathway. Accompanied with AXL degradation was an increased co-localization between AXL protein and key autophagy/lysosome markers. Autophagic flux was also induced upon p85β silencing. To further identify the potential mediators of the lysosomal regulation of AXL, we performed detailed mechanistic analyses that involved proteomics and biochemical experiments. Intriguingly, TRIM2 (an E3 ligase) and optineurin (an autophagy receptor) were identified to mediate the entry of AXL into the autophagy pathway. Importantly, p85β likely regulates the activities of TRIM2 and optineurin by altering the phosphorylation of these two molecules. Objective 3: To delineate the AXL signaling axis induced by p85β. To elucidate the downstream signaling events that mediate the effects of p85β, we performed protein array analysis and subsequent Western blotting validation in multiple cell lines. p85β did not activate the classical AKT pathway but unexpectedly PDK1/SGK3. Phosphorylation of AKT, PRAS40, mTOR and p70S6K was not changed by p85β. In contrast, PDK1, SGK3 and NDRG1 (a marker of SGK activity) was remarkably phosphorylated in p85β-expressing cells. Next, we assessed the contribution of each of these molecules to the effects of p85β on SGK3 signaling by inhibiting AXL (TP-0903), p110 (GDC-0941) or PDK1 (GSK2334470). All the inhibitors suppressed the induction of PDK1, SGK3 and NDRG1 phosphorylation by p85β expression. These results collectively indicate activation of the AXL/p110/PDK1/SGK3/NDRG1 signaling cascade by p85β in ovarian cancer. Notably, these inhibitions had no effect on the induction of AXL protein levels by p85β, concordant with the notion that the regulation of AXL by p85β is independent of p110 activity. Objective 4: To examine whether p85β confers sensitivity to inhibitors along the AXL signaling axis. p85β could confer sensitivity to inhibitors targeting molecules in the AXL/p110/PDK1/SGK3/NDRG1 signaling cascade. p85β-overexpressing 3D spheroids were treated with serial dilutions of inhibitors of AXL and PI3K/PDK1 signaling to obtain IC50 values in the presence and absence of p85β expression. Strikingly, p85β-overexpressing 3D spheroids displayed significantly higher sensitivity to AXL (BGB324 and TP-0903), pan-PI3K (GDC-0941), p110α-specific (A66), p110β-specific (TGX-221) and PDK1 (OSU-03012 and GSK2334470) inhibitors than control spheroids. Drug sensitivity was also assessed in spheroids of PIK3R2-depleted cells. In contrast to the results for the overexpression spheroids, PIK3R2 siRNA-mediated knockdown led to reduced sensitivity to all of these inhibitors. We also investigated the in vivo antitumor effect of AXL inhibition (TP-0903) on p85β-overexpressing or vector control-expressing ovarian cancer xenografts. The p85β-overexpressing tumors showed significant growth inhibition after treatment with TP-0903 compared to the control tumors, which were not responsive to TP-0903. Together, these findings suggest that therapeutic blockade of AXL signaling may be an effective strategy for ovarian tumors with PIK3R2 amplification.

17111618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111618.value: The p85 regulatory subunit of PI3K is thought to be dependent on the p110 catalytic subunit for downstream functions. There are several PI3K isoforms. Our group has reported the tumor suppressive activities of p85α (encoded by PIK3R1). However, the p85β isoform (PIK3R2) is little understood. In particular, the signaling mechanism and therapeutic implication of p85β had never been investigated. In this study, we established a previously unappreciated function of p85β, using ovarian cancer as model because PIK3R2 amplification occurs most frequently in this cancer type (49% of TCGA serous ovarian cancer patients). We discovered that: (1) p85β, but not p85α, increases the protein level of AXL (a receptor tyrosine kinase; RTK). p110 activity is not involved in this AXL regulation, but AXL activates p110 activity to mediate the oncogenicity of p85β. p85α or p85β had never been reported to regulate the expression of any RTK. RTK was solely known to be upstream of PI3K, our data reveal for the first time a bi-directional regulation. AXL has received more attention in recent years because it is often overexpressed and causes poor prognosis in cancers. (2) Detailed mechanistic studies revealed that the regulation of AXL involves an autophagic-lysosomal pathway through TRIM2 which is a novel E3 ligase of AXL and optineurin (an autophagic receptor). p85β modulates the phosphorylation and activities of TRIM2 and optineurin. p85 was not known to impinge on the autophagic-lysosomal machinery. Also, the phosphorylation changes of TRIM2 and optineuin have not been previously reported. (3) p85β does not activate the classical AKT pathway but unexpectedly PDK1/SGK3. This represents another novel piece of evidence that p85α and p85β induce different downstream signaling. (4) AXL inhibitors exert anti-tumor effect in p85β-expressing ovarian cancer models. AXL inhibitors are in cancer clinical trials, the incorporation of PIK3R2 amplification as biomarkers will potentiate the application of the drugs in cancer patients. Together, we discover that p85β controls ubiquitin signal and autophagic machinery to selectively upregulate AXL expression, thereby inducing the p110/PDK1/SGK3 axis to promote tumorigenesis. The findings have been published in Nature Communications. A invited commentary paper focusing on the major findings of this study was also published. A PhD student supported by this fund has successfully graduated. The student had received multiple scholarships and award because of her research achievements. The thesis entitled ‘Oncogenic Signals Driven by PIK3R2 in Ovarian Cancer’ was rated ‘outstanding’ (top 5%) by the thesis examining committee.

17111618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111618.value: Our drug response data revealed that p85?-expressing tumors were more vulnerable to inhibition of AXL than control tumors. Therefore, PIK3R2 amplification or p85? level could be a potential biomarker of responsiveness to AXL-targeting therapy in ovarian cancer. Future steps to take these findings to the next level include examination of drug responses using patient-derived cancer models. Second, PIK3R2 amplification is also frequent in glioblastoma (40%), breast carcinoma (20%) and endometrial carcinoma (17%) in the TCGA cohorts. The functional impacts and therapeutic implications of PIK3R2 amplification in these cancer types remain to be explored.

17111618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111618.value: Ovarian cancer is the 6th most common cancer among women in Hong Kong. The causes and the molecular events that lead to the development of the disease remain largely unknown. This study has revealed a signaling pathway triggered by a protein called p85? to promote the growth and progression of ovarian cancer cells. p85? is often overexpressed in ovarian cancer cells, for example, through gene amplification. Interestingly, the data obtained in this study revealed that ovarian cancer cells with high levels of p85? showed cancer properties. Through proteomic profiling and subsequent validation, a cell surface signaling receptor protein called AXL was found to be activated by p85?. p85? protects AXL from degradation through selective autophagy which is a cellular process to target and degrade specific proteins. Being an initiator of cellular signaling, the activated AXL thereby causes a stimulation of downstream AXL/p110/PDK1/SGK3/NDRG1 signaling pathway to promote cancer phenotypes. Ovarian cancer cells expressing p85? were more sensitivity to inhibitors targeting molecules in the AXL/p110/PDK1/SGK3/NDRG1 signaling cascade. Together, these findings suggest that therapeutic blockade of AXL signaling may be an effective strategy for ovarian tumors with PIK3R2 amplification.
