17112018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112018.value: Children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD), who comprise about 6% of the primary school population, display marked movement and balance difficulties. Reduced limits of stability (LOS), the maximum spatial area in which a standing person can lean, in these children is a major concern because it predisposes them to falls and affects their motor development. Our recent studies demonstrate the underlying causes of impaired LOS in children with DCD to include suboptimal volitional control of the center of gravity (COG) and reduced leg muscle force production speed. Tai chi (TC) is a particularly suitable exercise for improving COG control, yet the speed of movement is too slow to improve muscle power. Hence, muscle power training (MPT), which can hasten leg muscle force production, in conjunction with TC (TC-MPT) may be an ideal therapy for improving LOS, preventing falls, and improving functional performance in children with DCD. In the proposed study, we will pioneer the treatment of both COG control and leg muscular deficit in children with DCD by incorporating MPT into TC. We hypothesize that the LOS of balance control in these children can best be improved by treating both their COG control and muscular deficits. This hypothesis is supported by the prediction that TC-MPT is superior to either TC or MPT alone in improving LOS balance performance. Furthermore, improved LOS is associated with fewer fall incidents and better functional performance in children with DCD. Objectives: To compare the effectiveness of TC-MPT, TC alone, MPT alone, and usual care (as a control) for improving the LOS of balance control in children with DCD and to explore the relationship among LOS, falls, and functional performance in this population. Design: A randomized controlled trial. Sample: 156 children with DCD. Interventions: TC-MPT, TC alone, MPT alone, or usual care for 12 weeks. Major outcomes: Outcomes will be evaluated at baseline, post-intervention, and a 3-month follow-up. An LOS test will give a dynamic LOS score, an isokinetic test will quantify leg muscle force production speed, Movement Assessment Battery for Children–2 will be used to assess functional motor performance, and fall history will be obtained via interviews. Anticipated results and significance: The TC-MPT group is predicted to display the best LOS balance performance, which is associated with reduced fall incidents and improved functional performance. This novel training regime could be readily adopted into school or clinical settings to improve physical well-being in children with DCD, an outcome with positive socioeconomic implications. 發展協調障礙兒童（DCD）佔小學生人口的6％左右，這些兒童有明顯的運動和平衡困難。他們狹窄的有限穩定性平衡能力（LOS）(即是一個站立的人可以傾斜的最大空間區域)是一個令人擔憂的問題，因為這會導致這些兒童跌倒及影響他們的運動功能發育。 我們最近的研究顯示，DCD兒童LOS受損的潛在原因包括：控制重心（COG）不佳和腿部肌肉力量生產速度較慢。太極拳（TC）是一種特別適合改善COG控制的運動，但運動速度太慢，無法提高肌肉力量生產速度。因此，肌肉力量訓練（MPT, 用以加速腿部肌肉發力）與TC相結合（TC-MPT）或許是一種理想的療法，用來改善DCD兒童的LOS，預防跌倒和改善功能表現。 在這擬議的研究中，我們開創性地將MPT融合TC，來治療DCD兒童的COG控制和腿部肌肉發力的缺陷。我們假設：通過治療他們的COG控制和肌肉發力的缺陷，可以大大改善這些兒童的LOS平衡表現。如果TC-MPT在改善LOS平衡功能方面優勝於TC或MPT，便支持了我們的假設。此外，我們相信改善LOS與減少DCD兒童的跌倒次數和有更好的功能表現有關。 研究目的：比較TC-MPT，TC，MPT和常規護理（作為對照組）對改善DCD兒童LOS平衡控制的功效；和探討LOS，跌倒和功能表現之間的關係。 設計：一個隨機對照試驗。 樣本：156名患有DCD的兒童。 干預：TC及MPT，只用TC，只用MPT或常規護理(12週)。 主要結果：評估結果將在干預前，干預後和干預後3個月進行。 透過LOS測試得到動態LOS評分，等速肌肉力量測試將量化腿部肌肉力量產生速度，使用MABC-2評估功能運動表現，並通過訪問獲得跌倒的紀錄。 預期的結果和意義：預計TC-MPT組將顯示最佳的LOS平衡表現，這與減少跌倒次數和改善功能表現相關。這種新穎的訓練可以很容易地應用於學校或臨床環境，以改善DCD兒童的身體健康，研究結果具有正面的社會經濟影響。

17112018.label: Realisation of objectives
17112018.value: This project was completed successfully, and the objectives were achieved. The following summary describes how and to what extent the project objectives were realised. Objectives: This study aimed to: (1) compare the effectiveness of tai chi-muscle power training (TC-MPT), tai chi (TC) alone, muscle power training (MPT) alone, and usual care (control) in improving the limits of stability (LOS) of balance control in children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD), and (2) explore the relationship among LOS, functional motor performance, and falls in these children. Methods: This was a single-blinded and randomized controlled trial. A total of 159 children with DCD were recruited and screened for eligibility; 121 qualified (age range: 9-12 years) and underwent randomization – 30 to the TC-MPT group, 30 to the TC group, 30 to the MPT group, and 31 to the no training control group. The TC-MPT group received both TC training (including five basic TC movements and their applications) and MPT for the lower limbs [including the gluteus maximus (squatting), iliopsoas (resisted hip flexion), quadriceps (resisted knee extension and squatting), hamstrings (hamstring curls), gluteus medius and minimus (resisted hip abduction), tibialis anterior (resisted ankle dorsiflexion), and gastrocnemius and soleus (calf raises and squatting) muscles] three times per week for 3 months; the TC group received TC training only for 3 months (three times per week); the MPT group received MPT only for 3 months (three times per week); and the control group received no training (but can continue usual medical care and daily activities) for 3 months. Outcomes were evaluated at baseline and shortly after the intervention period by blinded assessors. The primary outcomes were the LOS completion time and dynamic limits of stability (DLOS) scores as measured using a BioSwayTM computerized dynamic posturography system. The secondary outcomes included the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-Second Edition (MABC-2) total test score and percentile rank, knee muscle peak force and time to peak force as assessed using a Lafayette Manual Muscle Test System, and the self/parent-reported number of falls in the past 3 and 12 months. In addition, the expectation about treatment credibility and educational impact of the intervention were measured post-intervention using a questionnaire (maximum score = 10 for each domain). SPSS version 27 software (IBM, Armonk, NY, USA) was used to analyze the data based on the intention-to-treat principle. The alpha level was set at 0.05 (two-tailed). A repeated-measures analysis of covariance (group × time) was used to compare the outcome variables of the four groups across the two time points, with adjustment for baseline covariates. A Bonferroni adjustment of the alpha level was applied to the post hoc multiple comparisons. Pearson’s correlational analysis was performed to explore the association between the DLOS scores, MABC-2 scores, and falls in the four groups. Results: Twenty-two, 22, 23, and 21 participants from the TC-MPT, TC, MPT, and control groups, respectively, completed the study. The average attendance rates at the training sessions were 60%, 61%, and 83% for the TC-MPT, TC, and MPT groups, respectively. All participants complied with the home exercise programs. No adverse events were noted. The baseline demographics (TC-MPT group: mean age = 9.5 years, 25 boys and 5 girls; TC group: mean age = 9.9 years, 26 boys and 4 girls; MPT group: mean age = 9.8 years, 25 boys and 5 girls; control group: mean age = 9.7 years, 25 boys and 6 girls) were similar between the four groups (all p > 0.05). Major results revealed that none of the interventions affected the LOS completion time and DLOS scores. Improvements in the peak forces of the knee extensors and flexors were found in the TC (p = 0.006) and MPT groups (p = 0.032), respectively. The number of fall incidents also decreased in these two groups (p < 0.001). No changes were found in other secondary outcome measures. In addition, no associations were found between the primary and secondary outcomes. Expectation about treatment credibility scores (TC-MPT group: 10/10; TC group: 9/10; MPT group: 9/10) and educational impact scores (TC-MPT group: 10/10; TC group: 10/10; MPT group: 9/10) were also analyzed. All participants and their parents agreed that the interventions (including the frequency of training) were reasonable and can improve their children’s motor performance and learning in general. Conclusions: Three months of TC training could strengthen the knee extensor muscles and 3 months of MPT could strengthen the knee flexor muscles of children with DCD. Either TC or MPT alone could effectively decrease the number of falls in this group of children. However, TC and MPT combined did not improve lower limb muscular performance, motor performance, or the LOS of balance control or decrease the number of falls in these children. In addition, no associations were found between LOS, functional motor performance, and falls in these children. Thus, clinicians and physiotherapists may prescribe TC or MPT as a stand-alone intervention for children with DCD to increase their knee muscle strength and reduce their risk of falls.

17112018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112018.value: (1) Investigating the biomechanics of TC and MPT is important to further understand their clinical efficacy in improving leg muscle strength and motor control in children with DCD. Our research team intends to use a motion analysis system to further examine the kinematics of TC and MPT in these children. (2) It is still uncertain that whether the improved knee muscle strength after TC or MPT in children with DCD could be carried over to daily activities (e.g., walking) and physical education (PE) classes in school. This topic is important and should be further examined because most children with DCD demonstrate an awkward gait pattern and usually underperformed during PE classes. A grant proposal is being prepared to investigate the effects of physical training (including TC and MPT) on leg muscle strength, dynamic postural control, gait pattern and performances during PE classes in children with DCD. (3) Further research work could also investigate the effectiveness of TC and MPT in other pediatric populations such as children with autism spectrum disorder.

17112018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112018.value: This study compared the effectiveness of a novel tai chi (TC) muscle power training (MPT) program, TC program, MPT program, and no training for improving the limits of stability (LOS) of balance control and motor and leg muscular performance and decreasing falls in children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD). This investigation is important because children with DCD often exhibit motor and postural control difficulties that predispose them to falls and injuries. It was a randomized controlled trial – 121 children with DCD were recruited and randomly assigned to the TC-MPT, TC, MPT, or control group. The three intervention groups received TC-MPT, TC, or MPT 3 times/week for 3 months. Body balance, motor performance and fall-related measurements were taken before and after the intervention period. Results revealed that TC training strengthened the knee extensor muscles and MPT strengthened the knee flexor muscles of children with DCD. Either TC or MPT alone could effectively decrease the number of falls in this group of children. However, TC and MPT combined did not improve motor performance, balance control, or decrease the number of falls in these children. Thus, clinicians may suggest TC or MPT as stand-alone interventions to children with DCD and their parents.

17113718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113718.value: Influenza virus is a public health threat, infecting over 1% of the global population annually and contributing to substantial deaths worldwide. The current vaccine has limited capacity to combat new influenza viruses which continue to emerge every year and even jump from animal reservoirs. By re-focussing our immune response to conserved regions of the virus we may be able to pre-arm the immune system in the long term against influenza infection. The inside of the virus and functional domains on the outside of the virus have remained constant, providing us with stable and suitable targets for a universal influenza vaccine. These key conserved antibody targets include the HA-stem (necessary for virus entry), the viruses internal NP (which is present on infected cells), and polymerase proteins needed for viral replication. These antibodies have substantial protective capacity to reduce viral burden by interfering with the virus life cycle and recruitment of immune cells. Antibodies contain a variable binding domain which interacts with the virus, and a constant domain which interacts with the immune system. The addition of sugars to the antibody constant region enable it to recruit different immune cells, and either activate or suppress their responses. We will use a mouse animal model to determine the comparable efficacy of anti-influenza antibodies that target the internal viral proteins and determine the recruitment of effector cell as a mechanism of action. HA-stem specific antibodies are currently in clinical vaccine and therapeutic development, and will be used as a benchmark in our study for comparative efficacy of alternate vaccine targets. Protective potential of different viral targets will be determined by vaccinating mice with a representative influenza protein panel and followed by infection with high doses of lethal influenza viruses for similar viruses and distant viruses, to determine the breadth of antibody cross reactivity. Antibodies from vaccinated mice will then be used recruit different immune cells and where in the virus life cycle they are effective. Human serum after naturally acquired influenza infection will be assessed to determine the frequency of these responses, their constant region profile, their role in limiting viral loads, symptom severity and risk of infection. Therefore, by fingerprinting the specificity of the binding domain in combination with the interaction domain of different antibodies we can determine what constitutes a protective antibody response. 流感病毒每年感染百分之一的世界人口，在世界範圍內造成大量死亡，是公共衛生的巨大威脅。現有的流感疫苗不足以應對每年新出現的或是從動物宿主轉移至人類宿主的新病毒株。通過重新研究人類免疫系統對病毒保守抗原的反應，我們或許可以為免疫系統提供針對流感病毒感染的長效保護。病毒的內部和病毒表面的某些功能性蛋白保持著恆定，這為我們研發全效的流感疫苗提供了穩定和合適的標靶。這些關鍵的保守標靶包括：在病毒入侵宿主细胞時至關重要的血凝素蛋白茎秆部、感染后呈现在宿主细胞表面的来自病毒内部的核蛋白、以及病毒複製不可缺少的病毒聚合酶。針對這些標靶抗原的抗體可以阻礙病毒的複制週期並且召集免疫細胞，從而为宿主提供有效保護 ，降低血液中的病毒數量。這些抗體有兩個蛋白結構域：一個可變的病毒結合結構域和一個固定的免疫系統作用結構域。在抗體的固定結構域上連接不同的糖分子可以令抗體得以召集不同的免疫細胞，從而激活或者抑制這些免疫細胞的反應。我們将会利用一个小鼠动物模型，来測試和比較针对病毒内部蛋白的流感疫苗的效力，同時我們還會測試這些疫苗对免疫细胞的激活效力。針對病毒血凝素蛋白茎秆部的抗體现正处于临床治療的研究中。而我們會用該種抗體作為基準，來衡量其他疫苗標靶的效力。通過向小鼠先註射一組有代表性的流感病毒蛋白，再用高劑量的同種或異種致死流感病毒對注射後的小鼠進行感染，我們會對不同病毒標靶的保護效力和抗體間的交互作用進行評估。來自接種小鼠的抗體會被用於體外實驗中測試其在各種免疫細胞於不同病毒複製週期中的保護作用。來自流感感染個體的人類血清將會被用於同樣的體外實驗中以評估其對感染的保護作用、恆定抗原的組成、對病毒濃度的限制作用、病症的嚴重性、以及感染的風險。通過細緻辨識不同抗體病毒結合結構域的特異性，和其免疫系統作用結構域，我們將會對有效的保護性抗體的組成有更清晰的認知。

17113718.label: Realisation of objectives
17113718.value: This project aims to determine the role of multiple influenza proteins in immune mediated protection by vaccination of mice with single proteins, and further assessing these specific antibodies in human serum before and after infection. We had custom recombinant proteins made for IAV polymerase proteins, and sourced remaining proteins commercially or from collaborators. Our protein panel included HA, H1stem, NA, M1, NP, PA, PB1, PB2, NS1 and NS2 proteins from A/H1N1 of A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8, for M1, NS1, NS2 proteins) and A/California/04/2009 (H1N1pdm, for other remaining proteins) and, and PBS+adjuvant controls. This enabled, objective 1, mouse vaccination, and objective 2 and 3 immune assay with human serum to be performed. For objective 1, there were some unforeseen project difficulties in mouse vaccination, which resulted in us adapting our vaccination approach from a recombinant vaccinia panel to protein panel to generate Single Protein Immune Serum (SPIMS). As PA, PB1, PB2 proteins exist as a complex and recombinant purified proteins are not commercially available, we first explored the option of vaccinating mice with a panel of recombinant vaccinia viruses (rVV) from collaborators with novel reagents: Jonathan Yewdell (NIH, USA) and Weisan Chen (LaTrobe University) that included major influenza proteins, including the polymerase proteins. However, mice failed to seroconvert against the rVV backbone even and no specific antibodies were detected despite 2 dose vaccination and a high dose titration (1x108 p.f.u) of rVV doses. Moving forward, recombinant polymerase proteins (PA, PB1 and PB2) were custom ordered from MyBiosource (by Baculovirus expression) which took nearly 2 years for production (quoted January 2020, arrived late 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic) for a limited amount of 250ug protein (cost $65k HKD), thus mouse protein vaccination experiments were conducted over 2 vaccination batches based on available proteins. The H1Stem as a headless trimer was kindly supplied from Raghavan Varadarajan (Indian Institute of Science, India). For Objective 1, mice were vaccinated twice intra muscularly with a panel of recombinant proteins, set 1: HA, H1Stem, NA, NP, NS2, M1 and set 2: HA, NS1, PA, PB1, PB2, with an oil in water adjuvant (Addavax, Invivogen), PBS+adjuvant negative control, and H1N1pdm convalescent controls (day 28 post infection) and subsequent vaccine SPIM serum harvested for downstream in vitro assays. Vaccinated mice were challenged with PR8 and subsequent viral load, survival, and pre vaccination and recall (day 7 post infection) antibody responses during infection assessed. Vaccination generated detectable antibody responses to all proteins, excluding NS2, PB1 and PB2, and infection rapidly recalled these antibody responses, that were not present in infection alone (NA, M1, PA, NS1 and NS2). Mouse antibody tools generated in this project resulted in further publications, and were used to assess immunopathology of a next generation vaccine response with heterologous HA (Bull et al., CTI 2022) and repeat influenza vaccination (Kavian et al., CTI 2021). To address issues of limited influenza polymerase protein availability described above for objective 2 characterization of mouse and human immune serum, the Luciferase immunoprecipitation system (LIPS) assay, an unbiased and quantitative tool to screen antibodies against cell expressed protein antigens tagged with luciferase, was adopted to the Valkenburg laboratory in 2019. An MTA was established with Peter Burbelo from the NIH, USA, to enable the import of plasmids needed for the LIPS assay. Cell lines proved difficult to sustain, (Cos1 cells from ATCC), and had to be reordered 3 times from ATCC during the study. Mouse LIPS system had high background for naïve immune serum, and alternate cell lines were tested, but the mouse LIPS assay was not used further due to high background. The establishment and trials of the human LIPS assay for a representative influenza virus: A/California/04/2009 (H1N1pdm) in 2019 and early data of human immune serum, was rapidly adopted to the COVID-19 pandemic. In early February 2020, a project application to a COVID-19 commissioned grant call from the HMRF was submitted using data from our 2019 influenza trials using the LIPS assay for novel antigen discovery of SARS-CoV-2. This led to a major study (senior author publication by the Valkenburg group to Nature Immunology 2020, 206 citations), patent filing, and further work in the pandemic response. Objective 2 to determine influenza specific antibodies isotype and Fc modifications with effector functions we adopted the LIPS and Luminex bead based assays. Antigen specific pulled down and purified human immune serum was sent to collaborators, Daniel Kolarich, Griffith University, Australia, for mass spectrometry to determine Fc glycan patterns however no results were generated due to loss of staff in the Kolarich team during the COVID-19 pandemic. Cellular assays to determine SPIM specific serum for complement binding and phagocytosis function were also unsuccessful at troubleshooting stages. We collaborated with Amy Chung from the University of Melbourne to adapt the Luminex bead based assays with FcR dimers from Mark Hogarth and Bruce Wines (by MTA with Burnet Institute, Australia) and expressed in house. A decommissioned Bioplex machine was serviced and relocated to the HKU-Pasteur to conduct these experiments. The SPIM panel specific antibody response of IgG, IgG1, IgG3, IgA, FcgR2a (for ADCP) and FcgR3a (for ADCC) have been performed from index infected, and their contacts were sampled before infection enabling baseline samples to be collected and follow up to the household 4 weeks later. This will be integrated to clinical data to realize objective 3, data analysis is in process. We found polymerase proteins had opposing trends to HA stem antibodies for protection. Furthermore, objective 1 mouse serum has also been in used in a multi-stage infection assay to determine the impact on viral entry versus viral replication and release. Only HA-specific immune serum limited viral entry, whilst no virus replication was detected with other SPIMS specificities limited viral replication and release. A HA-focused related study of the 2009 H1N1 pandemic with seasonal vaccination in children used the Luminex approach developed with this grant, and a manuscript is under review at Nature Communications. Further, final human LIPS experiments are still being completed in process, as staff proficient in the LIPS technique relocated in late 2021 due to pandemic impact. A further publication is planned based on these human results, and mouse challenge work. There were several problems encountered during this project that have curtailed the project and delayed final analysis and publication of results. These include the Hong Kong protest events of 2019 over at least 6 months of project onset, and the COVID-19 pandemic which impacted access to the laboratory, delivery of reagents and mouse breeding. Custom protein synthesis took nearly 2 years. Collaborations and techniques were impacted by staff relocation due to the pandemic. In addition, the original PI Valkenburg was on maternity leave from February to August 2020 and relocated to Australia at the end of 2022. Therefore, a 1-year extension was granted for this project. However, this project has resulted in 3 peer-reviewed publications, 1 submitted publication and 1 further publication of our exciting research findings directly from this research project will be submitted as soon as possible.

17113718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113718.value: To determine the priority targets of influenza proteins we used a mouse vaccination model and clustered cohort study with baseline pre infection at exposure sampling. Our investigation panel included internal functionally conserved polymerase proteins which have not been previously characterised in this manner. We found the current priority target, surface HA, remained more protective than alternate targets. However we also found additional proteins that contributed to viral clearance, namely the polymerase submit 1 (PB1). Whilst in a complementary human study we found that H1-stem IgA was elevated in exposed but not infected participants and is thus a protective immune correlate, whilst infected participants had elevated IgG, IgG1 and FcgR2a (ADCP function) to the polymerase proteins (PA, PB2, NS2), thus a risk immune correlate. These markers could be monitored in at risk groups and support the use of the HA stem as a universal vaccine target. At least 5 publications (Nature Immunology, CTI and ICB published, Nature Communications under review, and 1 in preparation), 2 completed PhD students (Bull and Li), 1 international conference award (with award for best oral presentation, Italy), and international collaborations (Australia, USA, India: Chung, Yewdell, Chan, Varadarajan, Hogarth, Wines and Burbelo) came from this project.

17113718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113718.value: This research project could be further developed through new vaccine targets to include the polymerase protein targets as monoclonal treatment options. Further establishment of antibody glycan modifications, cellular complement and phagocytosis assays at the group would be useful for future projects.

17113718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113718.value: The influenza A virus encodes at least 11 different proteins or domains that could be used for vaccine or therapeutic development. We investigated which of these proteins were protective in a mouse model and increased by recent influenza infection in a human household cohort study. Antibodies stimulated by these proteins were assessed at various timepoints, and new targets identified to enhance reduced viral load including the polymerase basic subunit 1, that could be incorporated to new vaccines due to high conservation with new influenza viruses to generate universal vaccines. Whilst current targets based on the surface haemagglutinin, HA, continue to provide both protection from lethal infection and increased viral clearance, and remains our best target compared to others tested here.

17113918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113918.value: Spexin (SPX) 是一種由GalR2 / GalR3受體介導的多功能多肽，已被確定為魚類模型中的飽食因子。最近，由餵食引發的SPX表達已經在魚類中得到驗證，但是SPX在肝臟的功能仍有待研究。以草魚為動物模型，我們克隆了草魚SPX及其受體GalR2b，並驗證了它們在草魚肝臟中的轉錄和蛋白表達。在草魚肝細胞中，我們初步研究結果顯示：（i）SPX可以上調生長激素 (GH) 受體 (GHR) 的成熟mRNA和初級轉錄物，並引發細胞內cAMP和Ca2+信號的上升和肝臟富集的轉錄因子FoxA1-3的表達，（ii）GH處理可以誘發SPX mRNA表達，而與SPX共處理可以增強GH誘發的IGF-I和GHR基因表達，以及（iii）免疫中和去除內源性SPX可以減少基礎水準與GH誘發的IGF-I和GHR mRNA表達。在具有草魚GalR2b表達的HEK293細胞中用攜帶草魚GHR啟動子的Luc報告基因轉染，SPX能誘導GHR啟動子激活，阻斷cAMP合成與Ca2+調動亦可抵消SPX的作用。此外，FoxA1表達也可抑制基礎和SPX誘導的GHR啟動子活性。這些結果表明，GH在草魚肝臟中能通過轉錄激活上調SPX表達，而SPX作為自分泌/旁分泌信號通過cAMP和Ca2+與GalR2b偶聯來促使GHR表達，這種機制對於GH誘導肝臟IGF-I表達是必需的。在草魚肝臟，SPX還可以觸發FoxA表達作為終止GHR反應的細胞內回饋信號。為了驗證我們的假設，我們將開展研究：（i）確認SPX對GHR和IGF-I肝臟表達的影響，並通過整個動物實驗檢查其對血漿IGF-I水準和生長性能的可能作用，（ii）通過體外培養方法闡明GalR2/GalR3的受體特異性和受體相應信號參與SPX誘導的GHR表達與轉錄，以及（iii）闡明SPX誘導的草魚肝臟FoxA1-3表達的信號傳導和FoxA1-3在SPX誘導的GHR信號終結功能。我們的研究不僅能為SPX作為肝臟中的新型自分泌/旁分泌調節因子提供證據，而且為魚類模型中飼喂和生長軸之間的資訊交聯提供了新的研究方向。

17113918.label: Realisation of objectives
17113918.value: As a first step to study the hepatic action of spexin (SPX) in grass carp, grass carp SPX & its receptor GalR2 were cloned. Phylogenetic analysis & sequence alignment have confirmed that grass carp SPX & GalR2 are members of their respective gene families in fish species. Using HEK293 cells stably transfected with carp GalR2 (referred to as “HEK293-GalR2 cells”), the newly cloned GalR2 was shown to have receptor binding property typical of the GalR2b subtype. Using RT-PCR & LC/MS/MS, SPX & GalR2 signals were detected in the carp liver. Using immunocytochemical staining, SPX & GalR2 co-expression was noted in individual hepatocytes, implying that SPX produced locally within the carp liver may have hepatic function(s). In grass carp hepatocytes, growth hormone (GH) treatment could induce IGF-I expression and elevate GH receptor (GHR) & SPX mRNA levels. SPX co-treatment, interestingly, could enhance GH-induced IGF-I & GHR mRNA expression and these stimulatory effects were blocked by removing endogenous SPX using immunoneutralization with SPX antiserum. In the same cell model, GH was effective in triggering rapid phosphorylation of JAK2, STAT1, STAT3. STAT5, MEK1/2, ERK1/2, P38 MAPK, PI3K and Akt. Meanwhile, IGF-I & SPX mRNA expression induced by GH were also reduced/abolished by the inhibitors targeting (i) JAK/STAT pathway (with AG490 for JAK2, FA for STAT1, ETDDC for STAT3 & IQDMA for STAT5), (ii) PI3K/Akt pathway (with Ly294002 for PI3K, HIMOC for Akt & Rapamycin for mTOR), and (iii) MAPK pathway (with PD98059 for MEK1/2, FR180204 for ERK1/2 & SB 239063 for P38 MAPK). These results indicate that hepatic expression of SPX is under the control of GH via activation of the JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades and probably play a role in maintaining/enhancing IGF-I responsiveness to GH via GHR regulation. For the receptor specificity & signal transduction for SPX-induced GHR expression in the carp liver, SPX induction could up-regulate GHR mRNA expression with a parallel rise in GHR primary transcript in carp hepatocytes. Along with the GHR signals, a transient increase in FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3 mRNA levels was also noted. In the same cell model, SPX immunoneutralization was effective in reducing the transcript levels of GHR & FoxA1-3 while the stimulatory effects of SPX on GHR & FoxA1-3 expression could be mimicked by the GalR2 agonist M1896 and blocked by the GalR2 antagonist M871. At the hepatocyte level, SPX treatment was shown to increase cAMP production & cytosolic Ca2+ level with rapid phosphorylation of MEK1/2, ERK1/2, P38 MAPK, PI3K and Akt. In parallel experiments, transcript expression of GHR & FoxA1-3 induced by SPX could be reduced/totally negated by the inhibitors for (i) cAMP/PKA pathway (with MDL12330A for AC & H89 for PKA), (ii) Ca2+/CaM/CaMK pathway (with Nifedipine for voltage-sensitive Ca2+ channel, Calmidazolium for CaM & KN62/KN93 for CaMK-II), (iii) PLC/IP3/PKC pathway (with U73122 for PLC, 2-APB for IP3-sensitive Ca2+ channel & Calphostin C for PKC), (iv) MAPK pathway (with PD98059 for MEK1/2, FR180204 for ERK1/2 & SB239063 for P38 MAPK), and (v) PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway (with Ly294002 for PI3K, HIMOC for Akt & Rapamycin for mTOR). These results indicate that SPX produced locally in the carp liver via GalR2 activation can induce GHR & FoxA1-3 expression through the cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK, PI3K/ Akt & MAPK cascades. To study the role of gene transcription in the GHR response induced by SPX, a Luc reporter with a 1756 bp grass carp GHR promoter was constructed and used in transfection study with HEK293-GalR2 cells. In this cell model, SPX treatment was found to up-regulate GHR promoter activity with parallel rises in cAMP production & cytosolic Ca2+ signals. GHR promoter activation caused by SPX was also sensitive to the blockade with the inhibitors for cAMP/PKA, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK, PLC/IP3/PKC, MAPK & PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathways. Using 5’ deletion analysis of the GHR promoter within the Luc reporter used in transfection study, the responsive sequence for SPX induction could be mapped to the proximal promoter region downstream of position -331 of the grass carp GHR promoter. Our results based on transfection studies in HEK293-GalR2 cells imply that GHR gene transcription via promoter activation is involved in SPX-induced GHR mRNA expression at the hepatic level. Consistent with the results for GHR expression in carp hepatocytes, GHR promoter activation can be induced by SPX via GalR2 coupled with the cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades. In carp hepatocytes, SPX not only could induce GHR mRNA expression but also trigger a transient rise in the transcript levels of FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3, which are the liver-enriched transcription factors involved in embryo development, glucose homeostasis, and lipid metabolism. In parallel study with the same cell model, co-treatment with SPX was shown to potentiate GHR mRNA expression induced by GH. In the same experiment, transient rises of FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3 mRNA levels were also noted after GH treatment and these FoxA responses were found to be additive to the corresponding responses induced by SPX, suggesting that FoxA1-3 may be involved in GHR regulation caused by functional interaction between GH & SPX. Since HEK293-GalR2 cells have been confirmed to faithfully mimic the post-receptor signaling coupling to carp GalR2 and proven to be very useful in our study for GHR promoter activity of carp origin, the cell line was used to examine the functional role of FoxA1-3 in SPX-induced GHR gene transcription. As a first step, the ORFs of grass carp FoxA1-3 were PCR isolated & subcloned into pcDNA3.1(-) to generate the expression vectors for the respective FoxA. As revealed by the results of co-transfection studies in HEK293-GalR2 cells with Luc reporter carrying the carp GHR promoter and the expression vector for individual isoforms of carp FoxA, over-expression of FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3 respectively was found to suppress basal promoter activity of carp GHR in a time- and dose-dependent manner. In parallel experiment, over-expression of individual isoforms of carp FoxA was also effective in blocking the stimulatory effect of SPX on GHR promoter activation. In our previous study, we have established a line of CHO cells with stable expression of carp GHR (referred to as the “CHO-GHR cells”) and used for promoter study of grass carp IGF-I gene. In CHO-GHR cells transfected with Luc reporter carrying the carp GHR promoter and the expression vector for individual isoforms of carp FoxA, GH treatment was effective in elevating GHR promoter activity and this stimulatory action was blocked by over-expression of carp FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3, respectively. In parallel study with CHO-GHR cells transfected with a Luc reporter carrying a 1077 bp of the carp IGF-I promoter with/without the co-transfection of FoxA expression vector, GH treatment also induced a rise in IGF-I promoter activity and this stimulatory effect was totally abolished with over-expression of FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3, respectively. These findings, as a whole, suggest that FoxA1-3 up-regulation by SPX produced locally within the carp liver may form a negative feedback for GHR gene transcription induced by SPX, which may be a part of the intrinsic system acting in an autocrine/paracrine manner to fine-tune GH-induced IGF-I expression at the hepatic level.

17113918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113918.value: Using primary culture of carp hepatocytes as a model, we have the novel findings as follows: (i) SPX and its receptor GalR2 are co-expressed in carp hepatocytes and form the basis of an autocrine/paracrine system for the local actions of SPX within the carp liver. (ii) SPX expression in carp hepatocytes can be induced by GH via activation of the JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades and play a role in IGF-I regulation via modulation of GHR expression. (iii) SPX produced locally in the carp liver can stimulate GHR expression in carp hepatocytes by increasing its gene transcription via promoter activation and this stimulatory action is mediated by GalR2 activation coupled with the cAMP/ PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades. (iv) SPX produced locally can also induce FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3 expression in carp hepatocytes via GalR2 activation coupled with the cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC & PI3K/Akt pathways and these FoxA responses can act as feedback signals to inhibit SPX-induced GHR expression by interfering with GHR gene transcription at the hepatic level. Our findings, as a whole, provide the first evidence that SPX can act as an autocrine/paracrine factor within the liver of a carp species to maintain/modulate GHR expression at the hepatic level, which is assumed to play a key role in regulating the hepatic responsiveness for GH-induced IGF-I expression/ secretion. For the local induction of GHR expression, a novel feedback loop via SPX-induced FoxA1-3 expression has also been demonstrated. This adds another layer of “system complexity” to maintain/ modulate GHR expression in the carp liver, which is highly relevant for fine-tuning the somatotropic axis in fish model. Despite the fact that our SPX project has been delayed by the riot in Hong Kong & the lockdown caused by COVID pandemic, the results obtained are highly novel and have not been reported previously. The first half of the project composed of SPX & GalR2 co-localization in carp hepatocytes and the novel actions of SPX on GHR expression has been packaged into a manuscript in the process of journal submission (manuscript attached in Part C). The manuscript for the second half of the project with focus on the feedback action of FoxA expression and its functional relevance to GH-induced IGF-I expression is still in preparation. Hopefully it will not be a long wait for the publication of these two papers.

17113918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113918.value: Our findings based on carp hepatocytes are novel and have not been reported in mammalian species. Given that our study on GHR regulation by SPX was based on grass carp (mainly for the concern of potential application for growth enhancement in finfish culture), it will be of interest to see if our project can be extended to mammalian models with biomedical implications (e.g., rodents). In our previous study in goldfish for the role of SPX as a novel satiety factor after a meal in fish model, we have successful extended our project on feeding regulation by SPX to the mouse model and the results have been published recently in 3 consecutive papers published in Frontiers in Endocrinology (Papers attached in Part C). This approach for sure will help to broaden the impact of our findings in the field comparative endocrinology.

17113918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113918.value: Stimulation of IGF-I production in the liver by growth hormone (GH) via activation of GH receptor (GHR) expressed in hepatocytes represents a key component of the somatotropic axis in vertebrate species. In our study with the function of the novel peptide Spexin (SPX) in grass carp hepatocytes, we have demonstrated for the first time that (i) SPX expression in the carp liver can be up-regulated by GH along with GH-induced IGF-I expression at the hepatic level, (ii) SPX by acting as an autocrine/paracrine factor in the carp liver can induce GHR expression in hepatocytes by increasing GHR gene transcription via promoter activation and this stimulatory action is mediated by GalR2 activation coupled with the cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK, PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades, and (iii) Through similar GalR2 activation & post-receptor signaling, SPX can also stimulate FoxA1, FoxA2 & FoxA3 expression in carp hepatocytes, which then act as the feedback signals to inhibit GHR expression induced by SPX at the hepatic level. These findings indicate that SPX by acting locally within the liver can serve as a novel regulator for GHR expression in carp species and the process may involve the local feedback via FoxA expression.

17114818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114818.value: 鼻咽癌的發生（NPC）與EBV感染密切相關, 尤其高發與居住在香港和南方其他地區的粵語人群。EBV 感染引起鼻咽癌的根本原因尚不明確。 研究結果顯示從NPC病人分離得到的EBV病毒株和其他疾病分離得到的EBV病毒株存在著顯著差異。這些觀察結果表明感染NPC的EBV 病毒很可能存在不同的致病機制。 EBV容易感染未活化的B細胞並建立潛伏感染，促進被感染過的B細胞進入可無限增值的淋巴母細胞。相反的， EBV主要以裂解性感染方式存在於原發性口咽上皮細胞，而不是持續感染。然而，在近100％的鼻咽癌中檢測到EBV的持續感染，主要是潛伏感染，這暗示著EBV在NPC發病機制中起著重要的作用。由於缺乏NPC來源的EBV病毒株以及能夠持續感染EBV的上皮細胞模型，這嚴重的阻礙了EBV 感染在NPC發病機制的作用的研究。從NPC中分離得到的EBV 病毒株是否在具有不同的致病機制仍然沒有明確定義。最近，HJ-Delecluse教授（德國）成功的從中國的NPC病人中分離出的M81-NPC 病毒株，並研究顯示該EBV病毒株具有不同的生物學特性。M81-EBV可高效的感染上皮細胞，並且很容易誘導B細胞中的溶解性感染。我們課題組與HJ-Delecluse教授合作，在我們早期建立的永生化的鼻咽上皮細胞系統中建立了穩定的M81-EBV感染。有趣的是，我們將穩定感染M81-EBV的永生化細胞注射到NOD / SCID小鼠中時，結果顯示M81-EBV感染的鼻咽上皮細胞具有致瘤的特性。這些研究首次證明了NPC來源的EBV病毒在癌前期鼻咽上皮細胞模型中的致瘤性質。因此，該模型為我們提供了研究中國鼻咽癌和其他疾病起源的EBV病毒株的致病性的研究工具。此外，我們最近建立了3個新的EBV陽性的NPC細胞系（NPC43，C17和NPC47），這使我們能夠分離更多的NPC來源的EBV病毒株用於支撐該研究。與HJ-Delecluse教授合作，我們還將使用EBV特定基因缺失的突變體病毒株來確定特定EBV編碼基因在NPC發病過程中的作用。我們的研究還將確定M81-EBV再激活缺陷型病毒株的致瘤特性。我們將通過NGS測序手段來研究野生型和突變體M81-EBV中​​細胞信號通路傳導途徑的改變，以了解EBV感染與NPC發病機制中宿主的相互作用。

17114818.label: Realisation of objectives
17114818.value: Aim 1: To define the pathogenic properties of EBV isolated from NPC. The role of EBV has been long postulated in NPC pathogenesis. Genomic clustering demonstrated a close similarity of EBV strains identified in the endemic area. EBV from distinct geographic regions with high NPC incidence may have distinct pathological properties. In this project, we have generated an EBV-infection cell system for understanding the tumorigenic property of EBV derived from NPC. A panel of nasopharyngeal epithelial cell lines, including the hTert immortalized NPE cells (NP460hTert), NPC cells which lost their EBV (NPC43-EBV negative), EBV-negative undifferentiated NPC cell line (HK1), EBV-negative gastric cancer cells (AGS) and others were established and well characterized. These cell lines represent different stages of malignant transformation. During the investigation period, we have infected these lines with different EBV strains (e.g. Akata-EBV and M81-EBV) and examined for their malignant transformation properties. Notably, stable and latent infection of Akata-EBV (B-cell lymphoma origin) and M81-EBV (NPC-origin) were established in the NP460 cells (a well-characterized hTert immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells). It was non-tumorigenic when injected into nude mice. Yet, after it had been infected with M81-EBV (named as NP460-M81), this cell line exhibited enhanced anchorage-independent growth phenotype, as well as tumor formation capacity when inoculated in NOD/SCID mice. This is, for the first time, a direct evidence of EBV-induced transformation in NPE cells. Interestingly, the B-cell lymphoma derived Akata-EBV did not confer in vivo tumorigenicity to hTert immortalized NP460 cells, indicating the differences among EBV strains on their functional roles in transforming premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Importantly, we have isolated the subclones of NPC43 which have lost the EBV genomes. The NPC43 is a recently generated EBV+ve NPC cell line derived from recurrent NPC patient sample. 6 EBV-negative NPC43 sublines were isolated from different colonies and their tumorigenicity was examined in immune deficient mice. Interestingly, all these isolated lines of EBV- negative NPC43 exhibited significantly decrease tumorigenicity. In the second part of this project, one of these clones, NPC43 clone 7 (named as NPC43-C7), was used to examine the tumorigenicity of different strains of EBV. We have also compared the tumorigenicity of NPC43, NPC43-C7 as well as the reinfected NPC43-C7-AkataEBV and the NPC43-C7-M81EBV. NPC43-C7 did not show in vivo tumorigenicity when subcutaneously injected into the flank region of NOD/SCID mice. In vivo tumor growth was observed for both NPC43-C7-AkataEBV and NPC43-C7-M81EBV when subcutaneously inoculated in NOD/SCID mice. We also performed phylogenetic study of EBV sequences identified from NPC PDXs/cell lines derived from patients from different geographical regions. The whole-genome sequences of EBV in the newly established NPC PDXs (Xeno23, 32, 47 and 76) and cell line (NPC43) clustered with the Asian EBV strains, especially those sequences from Chinese NPC (M81, C666-1, HKNPC1-9 and GD2). AG876, a type II EBV strain, clearly segregated from the other type I EBV strains. The LMP1 and EBNA1 sequences from NPC EBV also clustered as a distinct category. It may suggest EBV retained in NPC may possess distinct biological property contributing to NPC pathogenesis. Aim 2: To determine the role of specific EBV genes in the tumorigenic transformation of precancerous nasopharyngeal epithelial cell model. Through collaboration with Prof. Delecluse (University of Heidelberg, Germany), we have obtained mutant EBV with deletion of regions of miR-BARTs (M81-ΔBART), LMP1 (M81-ΔLMP1) and BZLF1/BRLF (M81-ΔZR). In this research, a set of EBV-positive cells lines were developed by infecting wildtype and mutant M81-EBV strains in NP460hTert and in NPC43-EBV negative (NPC43-C7) cell lines. It is believed that expression of EBV latent and lytic genes is control by epigenetic mechanism. Establishment of persistent and latent EBV infection is one of the prerequisite steps for cellular transformation. Interestingly, compared to the WT, cells infected with M81-ΔBART showed higher degree of methylation for a set of lytic genes, indicating that miR-BARTs may control the switch from latency to lytic cycle. Additionally, cells infected with M81-ΔLMP1 demonstrated lower degree of DNA methylation for BART cluster 2 promoter. By performing functional assay, higher expression of BART miRNAs was observed in the M81-ΔLMP1 cells, compared to the WT. This research concludes that EBV genes may regulated their own genes by DNA methylation. Numerous evidences suggest that EBV expressed BamH I-A region rightward transcript (BART) microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate the gene expression of the host cell, particularly in immune evasion and tumorigenesis. BART contains 2 clusters that encodes a total of 22 miRNA precursors (ebv-miR-BART1-22), but the functions of the miRNAs are not fully understood. We found that EBV-BART microRNAs enhance aerobic glycolysis which increase chemoresistance in NPC. Our results showed that BART miRNAs enhanced glucose metabolism and increased the resistance to cisplatin treatment in NPC EBV+ve cells. Importantly, we have also compared the tumorigenicity between the NPC43-C7-M81EBV and NPC43-C7-M81EBVΔBART. The tumorigenicity capability of M81 was downregulated when the regions of miR-BARTs were deleted. The expression profiles of EBV gene and microRNA have also been compared between the NP460hTert-M81 and -Akata cells. Latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1) was expressed at high levels (~50 folds) in NP460hTert-M81 cells compared to NP460hTert-Akata cells. The highly expressed LMP1 may support the enhanced tumorigenic properties of M81-EBV compared to Akata-EBV. Moreover, M81-infected NP460hTert cells exhibited high expression of cluster 1 BART miRNAs (including miR-BART3-3p, miR-BART4-5p). These microRNAs were previously identified to have oncogenic roles in NPC. Enhanced activation of MEK/Erk signaling was also found in NP460hTert-M81 cells. Aim 3: To define the interplay of EBV infection and host cell factors in the tumorigenic transformation of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Another major finding regarding NP460-M81 came from the primary culture of the tumor tissue of NP460-M81 subcutaneously grown in NOD/SCID mice. After explantation and culture for several passages, tumorigenic NP460-M81 cell (labelled as NP460-M81-T cells) were generated and its origin from the parental hTert NP460was confirmed by STR analysis. Further cell sorting was performed and two cell populations were generated, namely NP460M81-T-GFP(EBV)-ve and NP460M81-T-GFP(EBV)+ve. Interestingly, tumors in vivo grown by EBV-ve population exhibited well-differentiated histological features, as compared to the EBV+ve counterpart, suggesting (a) EBV inhibited epithelial cell differentiation and/ or (b) EBV transformed undifferentiated NP460 cells. These two effects of EBV may not be exclusive. In this section, we have also quantitated gene expression levels of EBV+ve and EBV-ve NPC xenografts and cell lines by RNAseq and GSEA. Activation of NF-κB and PI3K pathways were observed in EBV+ve NPC xenografts and cell lines. Upregulated gene expression in epithelial-mesenchymal transition, Notch and Wnt signaling pathways in EBV+ve cohorts was also revealed. In this project, we also found that EBV infection can sensitize the cells to TNFα for invasive properties. The NPC43EBV+ve, NPC43EBV-ve, and NPC43EBV-M81 cell lines were used to examine the effect of TNFα on the formation of invadopodia, which are invasive structures which can degrade extracellular matrix. TNFα could greatly enhance the invadopodia formation in NPC43EBV+ve and NPC43EBV-M81 but not in NPC43EBV-ve. We also performed RNAseq to assess the expression profiles of genes associated with invadopodia formation in NPC43EBV-ve and NPC43EBV+ve cell lines under TNFα treatment. Genes that are known to be crucial to invadopodia formation and activity, including TLN1, WAS, MMP9, and MMP14, were upregulated in TNFα-treated NPC43EBV+ve cells, while these genes were only slightly upregulated in the TNFα-treated NPC43EBV-ve cells. These results suggests that EBV infection modulates the ability of TNFα to induce invadopodia formation.

17114818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114818.value: In this study, we have examined the tumorigenicity and biological properties of EBV from different disease origins, particularly those from Chinese NPC origins (e.g. M81). We have also got a subclone of NPC43 which has lost the EBV genome (NPC43-C7). Using the immortalized NP460hTert and EBV-negative NPC43-C7, a panel of EBV-positive cell lines was established by infected them with wildtype and mutant EBV with deletion of regions of miR-BARTs (M81-ΔBART), LMP1 (M81-ΔLMP1) and BZLF1/BRLF (M81-ΔZR). The background and establishment of these cell lines can be found in the attached Research output 1: Valsempy S et al. Manuscript attached; Research output 2: Lin W et al, Nature communications, 2019. Furthermore, miR-BARTs promote glycolysis of NPC43 cells with an upregulation of extracellular acidification ratio (ECAR) and oxygen consumption ratio OCR. [Research output 3: Zhang J et al. Manuscript attached]. This manuscript also reports the impact of miRBARTs in resisting chemodrug-induced apoptosis by enhanced glycolysis in NPC cells. Tumorigenic property of M81-EBV has been demonstrated in our immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell model. Besides, the miR-BARTs are expressed at high level in NPC and has been postulated to play an important role in promoting tumorigenic growth of EBV-infected epithelial cancers in vivo. We could confirm the expression of miR-BARTs could promote tumorigenicity in NPC43-C7 [Research output 3]. We have established and analyzed three-dimensional (3D) spheroid models of EBV-positive and EBV-negative NPC cells and compared these to classical two-dimensional (2D) cultures in various aspects of tumor phenotype and drug responses. EBV-positive 3D spheroids were demonstrated to have features that resemble advanced and metastatic NPCs. Furthermore, we show that NPC spheroids have potential use in identifying new drug targets [Research output 4: Yi C et al., Journal of Cell Science, 2021]. We have also studied the invasive properties among the EBV-negative NPC43 (NPC43-C7), NPC43 and NPC43-C7-M81. EBV infection sensitizes the NPC cells to form mobilizing invadopodia when encountering a TNFα-rich tumor microenvironment. This study unveils the interplay of EBV and stromal components in driving the invasive potential of NPC via unleashing the propulsion of invadopodia in overcoming matrix hurdles [Research output 5: Tang WC et al., Journal of Pathology, 2022]. The continuous investigation in understanding the pathogenic roles of EBV and its encoded viral genes have provided direct and indirect druggable targets for effective NPC therapies [Research Output 6: Bruce JP et al., Nat Comm, 2021; Research output 7: Tsang CM et al, Semin Cancer Biol, 2020].

17114818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114818.value: The full characterization of newly established EBV-positive NPC models will provide valuable resources for NPC and EBV research. The experience and knowledge gained from this study will also contribute to the future success in the establishment of more representative NPC models, which are important for understanding the properties of NPC and the roles of EBV in NPC pathogenesis. The elucidation of interplay between host cell factors and EBV in driving NPC pathogenesis may identify therapeutic targets to suppress growth of EBV-infected NPC in patients. Targeting host cell factors supporting latent EBV infection may drive them to undergo lytic infection which may have therapeutic application in NPC treatment. Focused preclinical and clinical investigations on these new directions will provide insight for novel strategies to further improve survival of NPC patients.

17114818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114818.value: Examination of sequence homology of EBV strains from different geographical regions and EBV-associated diseases has revealed a homogeneous clustering of EBV genomes among NPC specimens from southern China (including Hong Kong) which distinguishes them from EBV genomes isolated from other geographical regions. However, the tumorigenic properties of EBV in epithelial cancer are poorly understood due to the lack of appropriate EBV-infection epithelial cell system for investigations. In this study, we have compared and evaluated the property of different EBV strains (e.g. Akata, M81) in NP460hTert and EBV-negative NPC43. The findings indicated the malignant transformation capacity of EBV infection in NPC. M81-EBV with NPC origin exhibited more potent pathogenic roles in the transformation of NPC cells than Akata-EBV. Furthermore, miR-BARTs promote the resistance of NPC43 cells to the treatment of cisplatin by enhancing glycolysis. Interestingly, the promoters of miR-BARTs were shown to be methylated more in NPC43-M81 than NPC43-M81ΔLMP1, indicating the LMP1 may suppress the expression of miR-BARTs by promotor methylation. Besides, in the TNFα-rich tumor microenvironment of NPC, the power for dissolving matrix will be highly upregulated in EBV-positive or LMP1-positive NPC cells. The understanding of the pathogenicity of EBV infection provides the basis for developing effective treatment to NPC.

17115218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115218.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. It has a mortality-to-incidence ratio almost reaching 1 as a result of late symptom presentation and absence of curative treatments. Deconvolution of the metabolic routes favoring HCC growth and their underlying molecular mechanisms will provide invaluable insights for the design of novel therapeutic. HCC invariably experiences inadequate O2 (hypoxia) and nutrient supply, due to outgrowth of cancer cells which do not have sufficient access to functional vasculature. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) mediates cascades of molecular events that enable cancer cells to adapt and propagate under this metabolically hostile environment. In our study, we provided initial evidence that hypoxia instigated a unique metabolic mechanism called macropinocytosis in HCC cells. Macropinocytosis is an endocytic process initiated by membrane ruffling, causing the engulfment of extracellular fluids (proteins) and formation of macropinosomes, followed by lysosomal digestion of ingested proteins and subsequent incorporation into biomass. Macropinocytosis has been shown to be driven by KRas and metabolically supports pancreatic cancer proliferation. Here, we show that this process is governed by HIF which activates the transcription of membrane ruffling protein, EHD2. Over-expression of EHD2 by CRISPR/dCAS9 activating system promotes actin-induced membrane ruffles formation, the first step of macropinocytosis. Knockout of HIF or EHD2 in a HCC cell line represses hypoxia-induced macropinosome formation and dampens HCC growth. Intriguingly, EHD2 is over-expressed in our discovery cohort of HCC patients. Our preliminary data suggest that macropinocytosis not only occurs in KRas mutated cancers but rather occurs universally in hypoxic condition. HCC cells are in close proximity to hepatocytes which avidly produce albumin, the major protein constituent in our body. We posit that hypoxia facilitates macropinocytosis through HIF/EHD2 pathway in HCC cells, harnessing extracellular albumin as nutrients to survive. In our study, we will interrogate the clinical significance and regulation of the HIF/EHD2 pathway in HCC, substantiate the mechanistic roles of HIF/EHD2 pathway in macropinocytosis, and examine the effects of therapeutic agents perturbing macropinocytosis in HCC.

17115218.label: Realisation of objectives
17115218.value: We have achieved all of the project objectives and there are no under-achievements or problems. Objective 1: To investigate the clinical implications of EHD2 in HCC: We found that EHD2 was the most highly over-expressed member of the EHD family (EHD1-4) in HCC cells under hypoxia (1% O2). Moreover, transcriptome sequencing data available from TCGA on 49 pairs of human HCC and nontumorous (NT) tissue showed that EHD2 was the only EHD family member overexpressed. EHD2 was overexpressed in other cancer types such as esophageal carcinoma (ESCA), kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC), and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) from TCGA database. We further performed RT-qPCR in a cohort of 80 HCC patients admitted to our institute QMH-HKU which confirmed the significant overexpression of EHD2 in HCC tumor tissues. Upregulation of EHD2 mRNA expression of at least 2-fold in HCC tissues relative to corresponding NT tissues from TCGA database and QMH-HKU cohort were found in 38.8% and 48.8% of HCC patients, respectively. Clinicopathological analysis further demonstrated that EHD2 over-expression was significantly correlated with a large tumour size in human HCC patients. Objective 2: To delineate the regulation of EHD2 in HCC: We asked if EHD2 is a direct transcriptional target of HIF-1. A putative HRE (-A/GCGTG) was found in the promoter of EHD2. A chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay confirmed the binding of HIF-1α and HIF-1β to the HRE of EHD2. RT-qPCR and Western blotting confirmed that hypoxia-induced EHD2 mRNA and protein expression in MHCC97L cells was abolished upon knockdown (KD) or KO of HIF-1α and slightly attenuated upon KD of HIF-2α. A HIF inhibitor, digoxin also abrogated hypoxia-induced EHD2 expression. Our data confirm that EHD2, a gene important for the actin remodeling involved in membrane ruffling, is a direct transcriptional target of HIFs. Objective 3: To unravel the mechanistic roles of HIF/EHD2-mediated macropinocytosis in HCC: We first studied the effects of hypoxia on macropinocytic capacity of HCC cells by evaluating HCC cells’ ability to form macropinosomes and degrade engulfed proteins under 20% and 1%. Upon pre-exposure of HCC cells to 20% and 1% O2 with TMR-dextran, a standard macropinocytosis marker, and DQ-BSA which emits fluorescence only upon proteolytic degradation of BSA through lysosomal pathway, confocal imaging showed increased dextran uptake and BSA proteolysis under hypoxia. Interestingly, hypoxia did not increase macropinocytic index of immortalized liver cell line MIHA. We next showed targeting different steps in micropinocytosis using IPA-3, BafA1, and CQ could block hypoxia-induced micropinocytosis as hypoxia-induced dextran uptake and BSA degradation were blocked in HCC cells. Hypoxia-induced macropinosome formation and BSA degradation were abrogated by HIF-1α-KO or treatment with HIF inhibitor digoxin (Dig). These findings suggest that macropinocytosis is induced by hypoxia through HIF-1. We next explored whether macropinocytosis facilitates hypoxic HCC cells survival. HCC cells were cultured with low-glutamine and exogenous BSA dose-dependently increased HCC cell viability exposed to 1% O2 but not those exposed to 20% O2. Exogenous BSA consistently restored hypoxic HCC cell growth in different nutrient deficient conditions, including glutamine depletion (-Gln), essential AA depletion (-EAA), non-essential amino acid depletion (-NEAA) or 0.2 Q conditions. EIPA, a macropinocytosis inhibitor abolished the growth-promoting effects of exogenous BSA in a dose-dependent manner. BSA failed to rescue cell growth in 1% O2 when HIF-1α was knocked out, suggesting HIF-1 plays an important role for protein scavenging-dependent cell survival in hypoxia. We next speculated that EHD2 may be responsible for hypoxia/HIF-induced macropinocytosis We established EHD2-KO and -KD subclones and evaluated their macropinocytic capacities under 20% and 1% O2. EHD2-KO/ KD greatly suppressed hypoxia-induced dextran uptake and BSA degradation. Furthermore, we generated EHD2-OE cells and observed enhanced dextran uptake and degrade BSA capabilities under 20% O2 in HCC cells which was further enhanced under 1% O2. Immunofluorescence staining with phalloidin and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) both revealed enhanced macropinosomes encapsulation of particles in EHD2-OE HCC cells. We have provided evidence that HIF-1/EHD2 pathway facilitates macropinocytosis and subsequent protein degradation in hypoxic HCC cells. We showed that extracellular proteins rescue hypoxic HCC cell growth but a missing link is whether HIF-1/EHD2-mediated extracellular protein scavenging fuels hypoxic HCC cells metabolically to facilitate their growth under O2 depletion. Metabolic incorporation of scavenged proteins was studied by pre-labeling all amino acids in cells using stable isotope-containing medium, followed by treatment with unlabeled albumin. Since scavenged proteins are the only source of unlabeled amino acids (12C-amino acids), macropinocytosis would decrease the ratio of isotope-labeled amino acids to total amino acids. Interestingly, hypoxia markedly reduced the ratio of isotope-labeled amino acids to total amino acids (the 13C,15N-labeled fraction), indicating metabolic incorporation of macropinocytosed proteins into the intracellular amino acid pool under hypoxia. Moreover, HIF-1α or EHD2-KO restored the ratio of isotope-labeled amino acids to total amino acids, suggesting metabolic incorporation of scavenged proteins was dependent on the HIF-1/EHD2 pathway in HCC cells. Objective 4: To evaluate the therapeutic potentials of targeting macropinocytosis in HCC: Pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1 using digoxin suppressed the growth of orthotopic tumors and lung metastasis in vivo. Ex vivo analysis showed that macropinocytic index in HCC tumors from mice administered with digoxin was significantly reduced. Consistently, IPA-3 blocked the growth of subcutaneous xenografts and macropinocytosis without affecting mouse body weight. To ensure that the effect is not model-specific, we induced HCC by hydrodynamic tail-vein injection (HDTVi) with the deletion of Tp53 and OE of c-Myc in liver of immunocompetent mice. Strikingly, IPA-3 profoundly suppressed the growth and macropinocytosis of HDTVi-induced HCC tumors without affecting mouse body weight. We showed that exogenous proteins benefit the growth of HCC and that the growth-promoting effect could be abolished by HIF-1 inhibitor or IPA-3. Next, we elucidated the roles of EHD2 in macropinocytosis and HCC in vivo. EHD2-KO dramatically suppressed HCC tumor growth, lung metastasis, and macropinocytosis. To investigate the correlation of hypoxia/HIF and dextran uptake in vivo, we performed in vivo dextran labeling together with a widely employed hypoxic marker pimonidazole and costained tumors with GLUT1. In EHD2-KO tumors, dextran labeling was significantly decreased, while pimonidazole and GLUT1 signals reduced slightly. By HDTVi, somatic KO of Ehd2 drastically repressed the growth and macropinocytic capability of HCC tumours. To obtain direct evidence of macropinocytosis induction in HCC tissue, we injected dextran through tail vein and collected tumor and NT tissues to evaluate dextran uptake capacity as direct indication of macropinocytosis in vivo. In both orthotopic and HDTVi models, tumor tissue demonstrated higher level of dextran labeling, while NT tissue was barely labeled with dextran. EHD2-KO in orthotopic and somatic Ehd2 KO tumors by HDTVi in vivo suppressed macropinocytic capacity. Third, we established a transgenic Ehd2-KO (Ehd2−/−) mouse line. Ehd2-KO mice (Ehd2−/−) exhibited no obvious defects during their normal life span. Similar to somatic Ehd2-KO, germline Ehd2-KO repressed the growth and macropinocytosis of HCC induced by HDTVi. Since human HCC is often preceded by fibrosis, we induced HCC in Ehd2-KO mice via hepatocarcinogen DEN and fibrotic agent CCl4 exposure. Consistent with all other mouse HCC models, Ehd2-KO (Ehd2−/−) mice had smaller tumors with weaker macropinocytic capability with the fibrotic background than Ehd2-wild-type (WT) mice (Ehd2+/+). These findings strongly indicate EHD2-mediated macropinocytosis is not restricted to any specific oncogenic mutations but is a general phenomenon in HCC.

17115218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115218.value: 1. We found over-expression of EHD2 at the mRNA level in HCC samples relative to their corresponding NT tissues from a cohort of human HCC patients. EHD2 over-expression was also found from transcriptome sequencing data on HCC available from TCGA. In addition to HCC, EHD2 over-expression was also found in esophageal carcinoma, kidney renal clear cell carcinoma, and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Clinicopathological analysis showed the over-expression of EHD2 to be significantly correlated with larger tumour size in human HCC patients. 2. We found EHD2 to be the most highly over-expressed member of the EHD family in HCC under hypoxia. HIF is the master regulator of hypoxia mediated responses. We located a putative hypoxia response element (HRE) region in the promoter region of EHD2. We confirmed the binding of HIF-1α and HIF-1β to the HRE region using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) in a human HCC cell line MHCC97L under hypoxia. The expression of EHD2 was attenuated upon knockdown and knockout of HIF-1α at the mRNA and protein level. Treatment of HIF inhibitor Digoxin also abrogated the expression of hypoxia-induced EHD2. Our data confirm that EHD2, a gene important for the actin remodeling involved in membrane ruffling, is a direct transcriptional target of HIFs. 3. To unravel the mechanistic roles of HIF/EHD2-mediated micropinocytosis in HCC, we first confirmed that hypoxia induces macropinocytosis through HIF-1. We found macropinosome formation was abolished in MHCC97L cells upon HIF-1α knockout and upon treatment of HIF inhibitor digoxin. We further demonstrated inhibitors which target different steps of micropinocytosis including EIPA, IPA-3, BafA1, and CQ could abolish hypoxia-induced micropinocytosis in MHCC97L cells. We then confirmed the role of EHD2 in macropinocytosis in HCC under hypoxia. EHD2-KO or EHD2-KD demonstrated the abolishment of hypoxia-induced macropinocytosis in HCC cells while EHD2-OE demonstrated enhanced macropinocytotic activities under hypoxia. 4. To evaluate the therapeutic potential of targeting macropinocytosis in HCC, we first demonstrated that pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1 using Digoxin suppressed the growth of orthotopic HCC tumours and lung metastasis. Ex vivo analysis also showed that mice HCC tumours treated with digoxin had significantly reduced macropinocytic index than control tumours. Furthermore, treatment of IPA-3 also inhibited macropinocytosis and growth of HCC tumours in multiple HCC tumour models.

17115218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115218.value: Our data supported the role of HIF-1/EHD2-induced macropinocytosis as a metabolic adaption mechanism in HCC with different genetic backgrounds, providing an important molecular basis for the design of future targeted therapies against macropinocytosis in HCC. We demonstrated HIF inhibitor (digoxin), PAK1 inhibitor (IPA-3) and BafA1 (lysosomal inhibitor) abolished HIF-induced macropinocytosis in HCC. Further, digoxin and IPA-3 suppressed HCC growth in vivo. Although more specific macropinocytosis inhibitors have yet to be developed, our data encouraged that these inhibitors may have therapeutic potential and we may test them in clinical setting as there are no effective molecular targets in HCC currently. In addition, since hypoxic HCC cells undergo macropinocytosis for nutrients in order to survive, we may explore treatment potential of albumin-conjugated chemo-or targeted therapies. For example, albumin-conjugated paclitaxel (Abraxane®), an FDA-approved drug for treating metastatic breast, non-small-cell lung, and pancreatic cancers. HCC cells are expected to uptake these drugs through macropinocytosis. It may also enhance specificity of these drugs. Furthermore, as hypoxia is a common phenomenon in solid tumors, we may extend our study to other cancer types with solid tumors to explore targeting macropinocytosis as a new therapeutic approach.

17115218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115218.value: Hypoxia, the lack of oxygen, is commonly found in solid cancers including liver cancer due to abnormal vasculature and insufficient blood supply. Hypoxic cancer cells have limited nutrients which renders greater reliance on extracellular proteins. Macropinocytosis is a process cancer cells rely on to scavenge extracellular nutrients as fuel under limited nutrient. We found macropinocytosis to be universally induced in liver cancer cells under hypoxia. Cells adapt to hypoxia through HIFs, the master regulator for adaptation and response to hypoxia. We found EHD2 to be a transcriptional target of HIF-1. EHD2 drives membrane ruffle formation and macropinocytosis for protein scavenging to support liver cancer cell growth. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1α and EHD2 converged to demonstrate the inhibition of hypoxia-induced macropinocytosis and suppressed HCC tumour growth in vivo. EHD2 was found to be over-expressed in various solid tumours, including HCC. The upregulation of EHD2 was correlated to poor prognosis in HCC patients. Our study demonstrates macropinocytosis mediated by the HIF/EHD2 pathway as an important survival mechanism in hypoxic HCC and represents a novel therapeutic target for HCC treatment.

17115618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115618.value: Introduction Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is an extraordinary surgical procedure that involves removal of up to 70% of liver mass from healthy live donors and its implantation to an adult recipient. The minimum graft size for LDLT has been a subject of controversy for nearly 20 years and it is directly related to donor safety. We have previously demonstrated excellent outcomes when we lowered the minimum graft size from graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) 0.8% to 0.7%. Based on our center’s data, outcomes after LDLT were excellent even with GRWR of 0.6%, in recipients with model for end stage liver disease (MELD) score ≤30. Objective This study aims to investigate the outcomes after adult-to-adult LDLT, using a minimum GRWR 0.6% in recipients with MELD ≤30. Study Design This is a 3-year prospective study, at Queen Mary Hospital, the University of Hong Kong. Consecutive adult-to-adult LDLT patients will be recruited if they fulfill trial criteria. Potential recipient will be eligible for LDLT, if either donor’s right/ left lobe has GRWR ≥0.6%. If both right and left lobe is greater than our minimum requirement, the smaller lobe (always the left lobe) will be chosen for the sake of donor safety. Portal pressure and flow will be kept <20mmHg and within 100-300ml/100g/min. Portal flow modulation will be performed should any of the parameters deviate from our standard. Our primary outcome is to determine the risk of small for size syndrome (SFSS) after LDLT. We hypothesize with our protocol we can avoid SFSS and even if it occurs, SFSS will not impact on recipient hospital mortality. We will also evaluate the risk of graft failure, overall complication rate and hospital mortality. Because donor safety is the primary reason for lowering graft size limit, we will look into graft size and its relation with donor complication and recovery of biochemistry. Anticipated results and long-term impact Our hypothesis will revolutionize the practice of LDLT. Donor safety is the caveat of LDLT; every effort should be made to ensure donor safety. If we can lower the minimal graft size requirement to GRWR 0.6%, there are 2 important implications. 1) It widens applicability of LDLT, as donors who were ineligible for live donation due to small graft size will become eligible; 2) It greatly enhances the safety of LDLT as it is well known that donor complication and mortality is proportional to the amount of liver donated.

17115618.label: Realisation of objectives
17115618.value: Study screening and enrolment During study period, 577 patients were referred to our center for consideration of liver transplant (LT). Among them, 430 patients (79.5%) were accepted for LT but only 196 patients (45.6%) intended for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). Majority of the patients were waitlisted for deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) only. Our study hypothesized that the minimum graft size requirement, graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) can be lowered to 0.6% selectively in LDLT. Seventy-five patients (38.3%) underwent LDLT based on the protocol. Despite our protocol of using a small liver graft for LDLT, there was no restriction on the indication with high MELD patients (defined as MELD >20) accounting for more than half of the transplanted population and 17.3% were transplanted for acute or acute-on-chronic liver failure. As the predicted GRWR was lowered to 0.6% in this study, the actual GRWR was 0.89% with a range of 0.61% to 0.96%. Majority of patients were transplanted with right lobe with middle hepatic vein grafts 67/75 (89.3%), 6 patients had left or left with caudate graft (8%), 2 patients had right posterior section and left lateral section graft. The latter were rare in adult LDLT and would not be possible if not for our study proposal. Our study recruitment was severely affected during COVID period as non-urgent, elective LDLT was delayed due to manpower and operating theatre arrangement. The social distancing and isolation protocol during COVID was another barrier for potential donors to commence living donor evaluation and study enrolment. Nonetheless, with an extension of study period by 6 months, our team has surpassed our initial recruitment target and eventually 75 patients underwent LDLT. Primary outcome: To determine the risk of SFSS after LDLT 10/75 (21.3%) patient developed biochemical small-for-size syndrome (SFSS) but none died within 30 days after LDLT. In addition, 8 patients (10.7%) had portal flow modulation, 4 were performed intraoperatively [3 splenic artery ligation (SAL) and 1 ligation of portosystemic shunt) as pre-emptive measurement and 4 were rescue splenic artery embolization (SAE). Of the 8 patients who had portal flow modulation, 5 fulfilled the biochemical criteria of SFSS (one in SAL and 4 in SAE). Secondary outcomes - To evaluate the risk of graft failure at 90 days after LDLT The risk of graft failure/ loss at 90 days were 9/75 (12%). Of these 5 were due to patient death, 2 due to hepatic artery thrombosis (HAT), 1 because of hepatic vein thrombosis and one due to severe acute cellular rejection. None of the graft loss was a result of SFSS. One potential complication of SAL or SAE was reducing the portal flow might lead to portal vein thrombosis but this is not observed in our cohort. Again, this showed that our hypothesis was safe. - To describe the risk and cause of recipient mortality after LDLT As of 31 Dec 2023, 9 LDLT patients (12%) died, only one died of technical complication (hepatic vein thrombosis) and none died of SFSS. Majority of the patients died of sepsis or multiorgan failure. - To evaluate recipient complication after LDLT The overall recipient complication rate was 69.3%, which is consistent with what’s reported in literature. Severe complications defined as Clavien > grade 3b was uncommon [11/75 (14.7%), and there was no difference between right and other recipients (9/67, 13.4% and 2/8 25%, P=0.987). The hospital and ICU stay were 21 and 3 days respectively, which are consistent with our center’s standard. The overall vascular complication rate is low, 4 patients developed HAT, 5.3% and 3 (4%) patients had hepatic vein thrombosis. Among recipients with small-for-size graft, HAT is a concern due to portal hyper-perfusion and it might trigger a reflex that lead to HAT. Our data has shown that HAT rate remains low using a minimum GRWR requirement at 0.6%. (Table 3) - To evaluate donor complication after right vs. left lobe LDLT The overall donor complication rate was low at 20/75 (26.7%) and most were minor complications including wound infection, thrombophlebitis and pneumonia. There was no severe postoperative complication/ mortality in donor. There were 4 grade 3a complication (2 small postoperative collection, 1 duodenal ulcer and 1 bile duct stricture), all occurred in right lobe donors. - To describe relationship of right vs. left lobe LDLT and biochemical recovery There was no difference in terms of graft function recovery including bilirubin, INR, AST and creatinine after right/ left lobe LDLT. Invariably, graft function normalized by the end of 1st week after LDLT. Long-term outcomes Although long-term outcomes were not our proposed study endpoints, these are important outcomes assessment in adult LDLT. The long-term patient and graft survival rates were excellent. The 5-year patient and graft survival rates were 87.7% and 83.7% respectively. There were no difference in terms of patient and graft survival after right and left lobe LDLT. The 1- and 3- year patient survival rates were the same for both right and left lobe LDLT, at 87.7% and 83.3% respectively (P=0.670). Similarly, there were no difference of 1- and 3- year graft survival rates after right and left LDLT, both were 83.2% and 83.2% respectively.
