17122918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122918.value: The major research findings are highlighted as follows: 1). A theranostic nanoplatform has been well constructed from the red-emissive CDs with guanidine modification and conjugation of amphotericin B (AmB). The resultant nanoplatform (CD-Gu+-AmB) possesses potent effects against the common pathogenic yeast - Candida albicans. Notably, the accumulation of CD-Gu+-AmB in the 3-D human oral epithelial tissues model can effectively protect the fungal (C. albicans) infection (Li et al, ACS Appl Mater Interfaces 2019). 2). The cell-penetrating poly(disulfide)s (CPDs)-coated silica-based nanosystem with encapsulation of baicalein has been established to enhance the therapeutic efficacy precisely via intracellular drug delivery. As the CPDs-coated red-fluorescent MSNs exhibit limited penetration in the reconstructed human gingival epithelia (RHGE), the anti-inflammatory effects and fast internalizations of CPDs-coated and baicalein-encapsulated nanoparticles are assessed in human gingival epithelial cells. The novel nanosystem per se, particularly its combination with the encapsulated baicalein, can synergistically downregulate immuno-inflammatory responses in gingival epithelial cells via the NF-κB signaling pathway (Li et al, J. Colloid Interf Sci 2022). 3). We have successfully synthesized the multifunctional metallic particles with loading capacity for effective antimicrobial/anti-inflammatory treatments. Importantly, two novel metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have been developed and well characterized, including i) the micronized bismuth-doped MOFs (CAU-17) (Huang et al, Mater Today Bio 2022, in revision) and ii) nanosized zinc-doped MOFs (ZIF-65). The as-synthesized CAU-17 demonstrates potent antibacterial effects on periodontal pathogens, while ZIF-65 can greatly suppress the growth of the keystone periodontal pathogen - Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) and yet completely eradicate its persisters. 4) P. gingivalis (Pg) is the keystone pathogen of periodontitis. In a previous GRF-funded project, our research group has identified for the first time the existence of Pg persisters (Li et al, 2018; doi: 10.1111/jcpe.13002). Essentially, we have recently made a comprehensive review and given a scientific update on microbial persisters and their interactions with host cells (Wang & Jin, Crit Rev Microbiol 2022). During the extended study of the current project, we have further shown that Pg persisters are able to maintain their capability to invade into human gingival epithelial cells, and significantly disrupt the innate host responses through upregulation of the FOXO signaling pathway (Wang et al, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2020; Wang et al, Int J Mol Sci 2022). Importantly, these novel findings can greatly facilitate the development of novel approaches like zinc-doped MOFs (ZIF-65 as shown above) for tackling microbial persisters including Pg persisters and effectively managing the resultant inflammatory diseases.

17122918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122918.value: According to the scientific rationales and the current findings from our project (Li et al, 2019, 2022; Huang et al, 2022, in revision; Wang & Jin, 2022; Wang et al, 2020, 2022), the following research potential and directions could be proposed: 1). Following our discoveries on i) the identification of Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) persisters and their significant perturbation of immuno-inflammatory responses, ii) significant effects of the metallic bismuth drugs on Pg and the dysregulated host responses, and iii) complete eradication of Pg persisters via the synergized use of metronidazole and bismuth drugs. Next, we aim to develop multi-functional metallic nanomedicines to eradicate Pg persisters and appropriately modulate host responses through targeting certain signaling pathways (e.g., NF-kB and pyroptosis) for optimal healthcare. 2). Currently, there are huge challenges and technical limitations in highly mimicking oral/periodontal microenvironment for understanding the dynamic interactions of Pg with the host. We realize from this project that it is rather tough to develop a well-defined host-microbe interaction model for evaluating the therapeutic effects of our synthesized nanomedicines. As such, the construction of oral mucosal organoids as an ex vivo platform with microinjection of Pg could greatly facilitate future studies and implementation of personalized medicine.

17122918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122918.value: Gum (periodontal) disease is a major global health burden with unbelievably high socio-economic impacts. Severe gum disease (periodontitis) is the leading cause of multiple tooth loss (edentulism) in adults, and it is strongly linked to various systemic diseases and conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, dementia and COVID-19. This project aims to develop new multifunctional nanomedicines for tackling the keystone pathogen and the resultant immuno-inflammatory responses in periodontitis. Herein, we have successfully developed four nano/microparticles for further translational studies and potential clinical applications. Our findings highlight that these constructed nanomedicines can potentially protect oral tissues from the invasion of various oral pathogens, and appropriately modulate immuno-inflammatory responses. Moreover, we have further developed two types of metallic micro/nanomedicines to eradicate the major pathogens of periodontitis. These research findings may inspire the future development of antibiotic-free agents for precise delivery of oral/periodontal healthcare, in line with WHO?s global oral health strategies and personalized medicine approach.

17123718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123718.value: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) caused by partial or complete blockage of coronary arteries is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Clinically, the most effective intervention to reduce ischemic injury is restoration of blood flow, but reperfusion itself may cause additional injury called “ischemia/reperfusion injury (I/RI)”. The aging heart is more vulnerable to ischemic injury. Although the mechanism is still largely unknown, mitochondria alterations in aging heart have been suggested to play an important role in its pathology. With aging, the heart exhibits reduced adenosine triphosphate generation, increased reactive oxygen species, impaired oxidative phosphorylation and decreased mitochondrial biogenesis. These mitochondrial defects lead to cardiac remodeling and dysfunction, further increasing aging heart susceptibility to I/RI. Thus, identifying a potential central controller that reverses mitochondrial defects may provide new strategy to combat I/RI in aging heart. The telomeric protein repressor activator protein 1 (Rap1) is essential for the maintenance of telomere length and structural integrity. In the absence of telomerase, Rap1 knockout mice display more pronounced telomere shortening and increased expression of p53 (the senescence marker) when compared with counterparts. Of note, p53 can directly bind to the promoter of PGC1α and suppress its expression at transcriptional level. PGC1α, the coactivator of PPARγ, has been demonstrated to drive virtually all aspects of mitochondrial biogenesis and function and its enhancement protects against myocardial I/RI. Furthermore, Rap1 can bind to PGC1α loci in the liver, and regulate transcription of PGC1α. Indeed, our preliminary studies indicate that in aged mice, Rap1 deficiency leads to pronounced mitochondrial dysfunction, cardiac dysfunction, with concomitantly enhanced p53, reduced PGC1α level and increased susceptibility to myocardial I/RI when compared to age-matched counterparts. We therefore postulate that in aging heart, which partly mimics the defective telomerase, Rap1 deficiency may down-regulate the expression of PGC1α in p53-dependent and -independent pathways, and thereby lead to mitochondrial dysfunction and increased susceptibility to myocardial I/RI. The proposed research aims, therefore, to 1. Investigate if Rap1 deficiency increases the susceptibility to myocardial I/RI in aging heart; 2. Determine whether or not Rap1 deficiency precipitates cardiac aging and increases the susceptibility of aging heart to I/RI via p53-PGC1α signaling. The proposed work will improve our understanding on the telomere-associated protein Rap1, which forges a link between telomere homeostasis and mitochondrial function during aging and may help facilitate the development of better therapies for the management of IHD in elderly in whom this disease is very common. 部分或完全性冠脈阻塞導致的缺血性心臟病在全球範圍內都是患病和死亡的主要原因。臨床上，及時的心臟再灌能夠最有效地降低心肌缺血損傷，但再灌注本身能夠引起進一步的損害，稱為“心肌缺血再灌注損傷”。老化的心臟對於缺血性損傷更為敏感。儘管再灌注損傷的機制尚不完全明確，但老化心臟中的線粒體改變可能起到至關重要的作用。隨著年齡增長，心臟呈現出如ATP生成降低、活性氧增加、氧化磷酸化功能損傷和線粒體生物合成減少的變化。這些變化導致心肌重塑及心功能不全，進一步增加了老化心臟對於缺血再灌注損傷的易感性。因此，確定一個能夠逆轉線粒體功能損傷的中心控制靶點可能對老化心臟的缺血再灌注損傷提供新的治療思路。 端粒結合蛋白Rap1作為端粒蛋白複合體中的一個蛋白，對於端粒結構的完整性和端粒長度的維持都有至關重要的作用。在端粒酶缺乏時，相比野生型小鼠，Rap1敲除小鼠呈現出更顯著的端粒縮短和p53（衰老標誌物）表達增加。同時，p53能夠直接與轉錄因子PGC1α結合，從轉錄層面抑制PGC1α的表達。PGC1α作為PPARγ的共啟動物，被證實對線粒體生物合成、線粒體功能和的心肌缺血再灌注的保護的多方面具有推動作用。有研究發現，Rap1在肝臟中可以與PGC1的基因位點結合從而起到轉錄調控作用。我們前期的研究顯示，相對於同年齡的野生型小鼠，年老的Rap1敲除小鼠顯示出更顯著的線粒體功能障礙和心功能不全，伴有p53表達上調、PGC1α降低和心肌缺血再灌注易感性增加。因此我們假設在心臟中，老化部分類比了端粒酶缺陷，Rap1缺失通過p53依賴和不依賴的途徑下調了PGC1α表達，從而導致線粒體功能障礙和心肌缺血再灌注的易感性增加。 因此，本研究的主要目的有： 1， 研究在老化心臟中Rap1缺失能否增加心肌缺血再灌注損傷的易感性； 2， 明確Rap1缺失是否加劇了心臟老化和通過p53-PGC1α信號通路增加老化心臟的缺血再灌注損傷易感性。 端粒相關蛋白Rap1建立起了線粒體功能和端粒穩態之間的聯繫，本課題將增進對Rap1的瞭解，為我們針對年老人群建立更好的缺血性心肌病治療方案提供理論依據。

17123718.label: Realisation of objectives
17123718.value: The three objectives are fully realized and extended to some extent as reflected in the published and yet to be published work (not listed). Our study identified the role of Rap1 in myocardial I/RI in relation to aging and showed that Rap1 deficiency protects the heart from ischemic damage through STAT3-dependent reduction of cardiomyocyte apoptosis, which may yield viable target for pharmacological intervention in ischemic heart disease. This part of work (Objective 1, mainly) was published in 2020 (FASEB J. 2020 Mar;34(3):4482-4496.). Further, we identified that Rap1 may link telomere biology to fatty acid metabolism and aging-related cardiac pathologies via modulating the p53/PPARα signaling pathway, which could represent a therapeutic target in preventing/attenuating cardiac aging. These findings answer what were questioned in Objective 2 & 3, and was published in early 2021 (Theranostics . 2021 Mar 4;11(10):4710-4727.). Our findings regarding the impact of mitochondrial mechanism on myocardial I/RI in aged or in diabetic hearts has lead to a comprehensive viewpoint review which was published in 2021 (Cardiovasc Diabetol . 2021 Jan 4;20(1):2. ) and attached good attention. Given that our project is regarding the impact of ageing on myocardial function or resistance to ischemic insult, we extended the study to the impact of aging on the mortality of COVID-19 in collaboration with the Mainland colleagues, at the time of pandemics. The related study was published in 2020 ( Aging (Albany NY) . 2020 Jul 11;12(13):12504-12516) and in 2021 (Aging (Albany NY). 2021 Sep 22;13(18):21903-21913.). Mechanistically, we also extended our study to the impact of non-coding RNAs on myocardial I/RI under normal and aging conditions and related work was published in 2020 (Oxid Med Cell Longev. 2020 Jul 25;2020:7913418. ). We also further explored the metabolic impact on myocardial I/RI in aging related diabetic models and the work in 2020 (J Cell Mol Med. 2020 Dec;24(23):13727-13738. ; J Cell Mol Med. 2020 Jul;24(14):7850-7861).

17124218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124218.value: Cells are the fundamental building block of the living organism. Cells can move, communicate, and assemble proper organizations to maintain the structure and function of the tissue. Enclosed by lipid bilayer membranes, cells synthesize important protein receptors on the plasma membrane to orchestrate a wide variety of functions. Integrin receptor, a transmembrane protein plays a vital role in how cells migrate, adhere, and assemble the multicellular tissue. Specifically, integrin serves as the physical link between cell and extracellular matrices. As a result of integrin-matrix interaction, activated integrin can translate the extracellular signals across the cell membrane and trigger important physiological processes, including cytoskeletal reorganization and GTPase regulation. On the other hand, misregulated integrin-matrix interaction has often linked to various diseases, such as cancer development. Previous work and our pilot studies have indicated that Dab2/clathrin-mediated endocytosis of integrin-beta3 can cause prolonged integrin activation and alter cell migration. However, the regulation of integrin endocytosis remains poorly understood. In this proposal, we will firstly focus on the molecular mechanism of integrin endocytosis. Our pilot study suggests that activated integrin-beta3 receptors are locally removed during the F-actin polymerization at the invadosome. Dynamin2 GTPase plays the key role at the endocytosis site and becomes enriched prior to the scission event. Dominant-negative dynamin2-K44A mutant blocks the endocytosis. Based on these preliminary findings, we seek to identify the regulation of dynamin2 in integrin-beta3 endocytosis by examining the upstream activation signaling of BAR-domain protein and GTP biogenesis in the invadosome. In addition, we will reveal the impact of activated integrin-beta3 endocytosis in cellular physiology, as well as the endocytosis specificity of other integrin receptors. With our expertise in adhesion signaling, we will apply modern molecular cell biological approaches, advanced high-resolution fluorescence microscopy techniques, and quantitative imaging analysis to carry out the scientific investigation. Taking together, our finding will provide a better understanding of cell biological mechanisms in integrin-related diseases. Pharmaceutical and biotech industries will be potentially interested in applying our findings to develop new compounds and technologies to ameliorate patient’s condition. 整合素是連接细胞及细胞外基质的跨膜蛋白受體，在許多腫瘤細胞中，存在著異常的整合素轉運。侵襲小體是腫瘤細胞轉移過程中形成的重要黏附結構。它通過降解細胞外基質幫助腫瘤細胞穿越機體屏障實現轉移。然而，整合素內吞對腫瘤細胞遷移的作用，以及與侵襲小體的功能，還有待深入的探討。我們的初期研究指出，使用RGD配體激活整合素，可在侵襲小體形成過程中檢測到RGD的內吞。當侵襲小體形成被抑制，RGD內吞減少。在侵襲小體形成初期，DNM2蛋白有非常顯著的增加，而RGD及整合素逐漸降低，表明它們在逐漸被內吞。DNM2顯性失活突變體（DNM2-K44A）的引入，可有效地減少RGD的內吞。此計畫將深入研究DMN2在侵襲小體形成初期的啟動機制，以及整合素內吞對細胞遷移的作用。

17124218.label: Realisation of objectives
17124218.value: Summary of the investigation: In this investigation, we combine quantitative fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology to reveal the molecular mechanism of integrin-beta3 endocytosis at the invadosome. Specifically, F-actin assembly at the invadosome core exhibits protrusive contact towards the substrate and results in the plasma membrane invagination at the invadosome ring. We identify that BAR-domain protein BIN1 spatially associates with the region of invaginated membrane and is responsible for the spatiotemporal recruitment of dynamin2 via the SH3-PRD interaction. During the invadosome formation, BIN1 and dynamin2 synchronously enrich at the invadosome ring and trigger RGD ligand internalization and integrin endocytosis. Blockages of invadosome formation by pharmacological inhibition of PI3K and Src abolish the internalization of RGD ligand and the endocytosis of integrin. Knockdowns of BIN1 and dynamin2 do not suppress invadosome formation, but effectively suppress RGD ligand internalization and integrin endocytosis. Thus, plasma membrane invagination caused by F-actin polymerization promotes BIN1-dependent dynamin2 recruitment and facilitates integrin-beta3 endocytosis at the invadosome. This work has been published in a peer-reviewed journal^. ^Fakun Cao, Yuhuan Zhou, Xiaoting Liu, Cheng-Han Yu*. Podosome Formation Promotes Plasma Membrane Invagination and integrin-β3 Endocytosis on a Viscous RGD-membrane. Commun Biol. 2020 Mar 13;3(1):117. doi: 10.1038/s42003-020-0843-2. *corresponding author [Objective 1] Define the regulation mechanism of dynamin2-mediated endocytosis of integrin-beta3 at the invadosome. Percentage of completion: 100%. While the knockdown of dynamin2 and the overexpress of dominant-negative mutant dynamin2-K44A block the endocytosis of integrin and its RGD ligand, we seek to reveal the spatial and temporal regulation of dynamin2’s activity at the integrin-mediated adhesion. First, we find that the PRD domain of dynamin2 is essential for the recruitment to the adhesion site. Dynamin2 mutant without PRD domain are non-specifically distributed in the cytoplasm. Next, we combine fluorescence microscopy and interference reflection microscopy and identify that protrusive F-actin polymerization at the invadosome core results in the invagination of the surrounding plasma membrane. The concave profile of the deformed plasma membrane around the invadosome core is also demonstrated by the enrichment of plasma membrane markers and the specific recruitment of BIN/Amphiphysin/Rvs(BAR) domain proteins that recognizes and binds to lipid membrane with high curvature. Various of BAR-domain proteins, including BIN1, CIP4, FBP17, and syndapin2, contain the SH3 domain and can potentially interact with the PRD domain of dynamin2. After thorough examinations, we find that BIN1, a N-BAR domain protein, is specifically recruited around the invadosome core and is absent from non-invadosome adhesions. In addition, we reveal that BIN1 localizes at the membrane invagination via its N-BAR domain, as the BIN1 mutant without N-BAR domain is mostly cytosolic and diffusive. Therefore, we identify that BIN1 locally acts as the key curvature-sensing factor to probe the membrane invagination resulted from F-actin protrusion and to recruit membrane fission regulator dynamin2 to the invadosome. Thus, we have achieved the investigation of Objective 1. [Objective 2] Investigate the functional role of dynamin2-mediated integrin endocytosis. Percentage of completion: 100%. We previously found that endocytic protein clathrin and its adaptor Dab2 are colocalized with a subpopulation of integrin-beta3 at the invadosome ring. As F-actin increasingly polymerizes at the invadosome core, the intensities of BIN1 and dynamin2 at the invadosome ring increase. The elevation of BIN1 and dynamin2 recruitment is followed by the gradual intensity loss of Dab2, integrin-beta3, and RGD ligand. We apply time-lapsed imaging with a spinning disc confocal microscope and find that the lost RGD puncta are subsequently observed above the adhesion plane and internalized into the cell. Internalized RGD puncta colocalize with the confirmation-specific antibody of activated integrin-beta3 and are dynamically sorted into Rab5, Rab7, Rab11, and Rab4 positive endosomes. In addition, we find that autophosphorylated focal adhesion kinase (pY397-FAK) colocalizes with integrin-beta3/RGD puncta in the endosomal compartment. FAK is one of the key factors to promote downstream adhesion signalling, including activation of ERK and PI3K. Endocytosis of activated integrin can retain the activity of FAK in the endosomal compartment and promote the anchorage-independent cell survival of cancer cells. Indeed, we find that the levels of endosomal pY397-FAK in invadosome-positive cells are significantly higher than those in invadosome-negative cells. In summary, BIN1 and dynamin2 mediated integrin endocytosis promotes cytoplasmic FAK activation and support anchorage-independent integrin signalling. Thus, we have also achieved the investigation of Objective 2.

17124218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124218.value: Integrin receptor plays an essential role in regulating cell motility and tissue organization. In particular, disassembly and turnover of integrin-mediated adhesion is needed to facilitate cell migration. Abnormal integrin endocytosis has been reported to promote cell migration and cancer metastasis. Here, we reveal the molecular mechanism of integrin-beta3 endocytosis at the invadosome adhesion. We find that invadosome adhesions are the major sites where the clathrin-mediated endocytosis of integrin-beta3 and its ligand RGD takes place. Intense F-actin polymerization at the invadosome core exhibits protrusive contact towards the substrate and results in plasma membrane invaginations at the invadosome ring. BAR-domain protein BIN1 acts as the key curvature-sensing factor to probe the membrane invagination and recruits the membrane fission regulator dynamin2. Knockdowns of BIN1 and dynamin2 effectively suppress RGD ligand internalization and integrin endocytosis. Thus, plasma membrane invagination caused by F-actin polymerization promotes BIN1-dependent dynamin2 recruitment and facilitate integrin-beta3 endocytosis at the invadosome. These results have been published in a peer-reviewed journal, and here are the major findings. 1) Dab2 localizes at integrin-beta3 in the invadosome ring 2) Integrin-beta3 and RGD ligand are internalized at the invadosome 3) Inhibitions of invadosome formation suppress RGD endocytosis 4) Dynamin2 recruitment to the invadosome ring triggers RGD endocytosis 5) Protrusive F-actin polymerization causes plasma membrane deformation at the invadosome ring 6) BIN1 is recruited to the deformed plasma membrane at the invadosome ring 7) BIN1 recruits dynamin2 to the invadosome ring and promotes RGD endocytosis

17124218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124218.value: Integrins are a large family of transmembrane receptors and act as the biophysical link between the cell and extracellular matrix. The trafficking of integrin receptor, including endocytosis, endosomal sorting, and exocytosis (recycling), orchestrates the spatiotemporal distribution of adhesion signalling and cell motility. In particular, metastatic cancer cells often form the invadosome adhesion, a type of specialized integrin-mediated adhesion that facilitates invasive migration across tissue barriers. Here, we identify that the dynamical recruitment of BIN1 and dynamin2 to the invadosome adhesion triggers the endocytosis of integrin-beta3. In addition, we find that endocytosed integrin-beta3 remains in the activated confirmation. Activated integrin in the endosomal compartment can retain the activity of focal adhesion kinase in an anchorage-independent manner and promote the survival of cancer cells. While our work here focuses on the endocytosis, the sorting and recycling of integrin also play critical roles in cell migration and cancer metastasis. Further studies are required to extend these findings and investigate the recycling mechanism of integrin-beta3 (and other integrin family) and its implication to new adhesion formation and overall cell motility.

17124218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124218.value: Cell adhesion plays an important role in benign tissue regeneration, as well as malignant cancer metastasis. Integrin receptors are the key transmembrane protein family that facilitate the cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix. Receptor endocytosis is a cell biological process in which receptors are internalized and removed from the cell membrane. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanism of integrin-beta3 receptor endocytosis is largely unknow. Here, we find that invadosome adhesions are the major sites where the endocytosis of integrin-beta3 and its ligand RGD occurs. BIN1 acts as the key factor to recruit the membrane fission regulator dynamin2 that triggers the endocytosis of integrin-beta3. In addition, we find that endocytosed integrin-beta3 remains active, supports the sustained activation of focal adhesion kinase, and promotes the survival of cancer cells in an anchorage-independent manner. Thus, our investigation reveals the regulatory pathway of invadosome-dependent integrin endocytosis and sheds light on the innovation in the pharmaceutical development to block cancer metastasis.

17124718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124718.value: 地球上的大多數生物都有24小時內部生物鐘，以適應環境變化。內源分子鐘，如CLOCK，BMAL，PER和CRY，協調中心和外圍對外部環境的反應，從而提供不同生物的生理和行為的晝夜節律性。在哺乳動物中，晝夜節律鐘的網絡非常複雜。例如，心血管和代謝功能的24小時波動不僅受到晝/夜循環的驅動，還受到食物，溫度和身體活動等其他外部線索（Zeitgebers）的驅動。Period是20世紀80年代中期克隆的第一個時鐘基因。 PER（蛋白質產物）的積累通過以循環模式在細胞核和細胞質之間穿梭來負調其自身的基因表達。與其他中心時鐘相比，PER2獨特地參與食物預期活動的外圍調節，與日夜週期無關。我們之前的實驗表明，PER2突變小鼠的動脈壓和能量代謝的日夜週期都消失了，而內皮細胞中人SIRT1的選擇性過表達恢復了血管和代謝的晝夜節律，從而阻止了這些動物的高血壓的發展。本研究旨在檢驗內皮SIRT1獨立於PER2起作用的假設，通過調節氨基酸代謝和/或體溫的晝夜節律來實現動脈血壓和能量代謝的24小時振盪並通過翻譯後反饋迴路調節SIRT1表達和活性。此項目將使用我們建立的幾種基因修飾小鼠模型在不同的器官，細胞和分子水平上進行測試，以揭示內皮SIRT1介導的晝夜節律性的機制。晝夜節律性隨著年齡逐漸喪失，導致心血管事件和代謝功能障礙的風險增加。預計該結果將為針對衰老相關疾病的治療預防和/或乾預提供有價值的創新見解和策略。

17126118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126118.value: 椎間盤退化（IDD）是腰痛的主要原因，在漸趨衰老的社會中影響著數百萬人的生活質量並造成不斷增長的社會經濟負擔。許多患者無法忍受腰痛，病情嚴重時外科手術成爲最後一個補救選項。環境、生活方式及衰老對IDD都有影響，但遺傳的作用更爲重要，可提高IDD的易感性，導致其更早發生及更嚴重。確定並了解遺傳風險因子的作用，是診斷IDD並確定其愈後與治療方案之關鍵所在。以往我們已經確定椎間盤的一種胞外基質（ECM）蛋白Asporin (簡稱ASPN)是IDD的遺傳風險因子。 同時，ASPN表達的增高與IDD的發生有關聯性。在轉基因小鼠的椎間盤中過表達ASPN可誘導細胞和基質成分的改變以及炎症，與人類IDD中所見的漸進式病變相仿。因此，ASPN在IDD發生與發展中均有作用，但其退化機理與分子基礎尚待闡明。 我們在ASPN轉基因小鼠中的研究表明TGF-β信號轉導有所增強，這與體外實驗中所擬議的ASPN對TGF-β信號通路的負調控作用截然不同。有趣的是，我們對ASPN轉基因小鼠椎間盤蛋白質組的初步分析顯示，最顯著的變化在於原纖蛋白1（FBN1）的檢出水平。FBN1是胞外基質的一種微原纖維蛋白，可通過阻隔TGF-β的無活性大複合體而限制TGF-β的激活。FBN1的突變確實可引起馬方綜合症，表現爲TGF-β信號通路的過度激活。抑制TGF-β信號轉導的藥物可用於治療此症。我們發現，如果將小鼠的遺傳背景從CB57B6轉變爲LG/J，ASPN對IDD的作用有所減緩。有意思的是LG/J修複受損組織的能力特別強，被稱爲“超級自愈小鼠”。如果將小鼠的遺傳背景從CB57B6轉變爲LG/J，ASPN所引起的IDD病變可被阻止，由此正可揭示獨特的保護性機理。我們的研究目標是利用創新的小鼠模型剖析ASPN誘導IDD病變發生及發展的分子基礎並闡明其與FBN1和TGF-β信號轉導的關系。從機理上了解與人類遺傳風險因子相關的退化或保護因子，對於IDD的病因學研究及治療將有更深遠的意義。如果能夠在退化發生之前采用藥物預先干預風險因子，我們就能預防或減輕退化。

17126118.label: Realisation of objectives
17126118.value: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is a major cause of back pain, affecting quality of life in an ageing society. Genetics have a significant contribution for an individual to develop IDD. Our team has identified a major genetic risk factor is Asporin (ASPN), an extracellular matrix component of the intervertebral disc (IVD). How ASPN acts as genetic risk factor is not known. A hypothesis is that it influences TGFb signalling by direct binding, regulating availability to the receptors from studies on osteoarthritis, carried out in chondrocytes in vitro. How ASPN behaves in vivo in the IVD is not known, and is the aim of this project. We generated transgenic mouse model (ASPN-Tg) over-expressing the human ASPN gene to study the in vivo impact. Specific objectives are: 1. To decipher the progressive molecular and cellular changes induced by ASPN in relation to TGF-β signalling. 2. To determine the intrinsic/extrinsic contributions of ASPN as a risk factor in IDD progression. 3. To assess the potential of modifiers in ameliorating ASPN-induced IDD onset and progression. We want to understand the impact of this risk factor in IVD homeostasis and function, and to performed transcriptomic and proteomic assessments to gain insights into the gene and protein expression profiles, respectively. Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) was used to assess changes in the cell population, or subtle changes in genes within cell population(s), such as molecular signals or expression of ECM molecules. From this, we identified activated TGFb signalling as a target, and test the possibility of modulating the disease outcome using Losartan, an inhibitor of TGFb signaling. Funding received was 700K, representing 60% of the original requested fund of 1.2M. Thus, while we have maintained the original objectives, the scope for objectives is reduced accordingly. Further, the restrictions imposed by the COVID19 pandemic spanning across the entire period of this project has further impacted on efficient use of research funding, acquisition of reagents, handling and breeding of mouse colonies, and human capital. For mouse husbandry, as researchers were restricted from entering the mouse facility in numerous occasions, we have lost critical experiments. Further, an international PhD student from Pakistani had to withdraw from her candidature as travel restriction had prohibited her return to Hong Kong at a critical time. These unfortunate situations were beyond our control. Nevertheless, we have completed the project in full as listed below. For objective 1, we have systematically assessed the IVD phenotypic outcome with studies on more than 50 mice with histological scores across three age time points showing a gradual progression of disc changes in the mouse. These include cell content and characteristics, ECM distribution and NP and AF organization. This was a major undertaking but important to evaluation the overall outcome of the impact on IVD function. We further performed systematic assessment of the changes in the NP, using histology and specific molecular markers. We showed that ASPN had an impact on ECM deposition and distribution, likely related to direct changes in ECM production, altering the relative composition. There was an increase in Collagen II and Aggrecan production by cells resided in the NP expressing the transgene, associated with an up-regulation of Sox9, and TGFb signalling. Evidence of increased expression was clear, but not in all NP cells. We propose that there could be a change in the ECM niche for progenitor cells in the NP, and assess two markers, Tie2 and GD2, and showed indeed to be the case. Single cell RNA sequencing was used to gain insights to the overall cell populations in the NP,. Given the budget constrain, we only analyse mice at 10-weeks of age with 3,000 cells from each of WT and ASPN-tg mice. There were two major clusters of NP and AF cells. There was clear evidence for the transgene expression in a population of NP cells, but not all. We reason that this may be due to that fact in the transgene expressing cells, the overall genes that are expressed are not significantly different, but rather, subtle differences in the level of some of the genes that are expressed; in particular some of the ECM genes. Further, changes in genes associated with TGfb signaling was not different. Again, this may reflect a subtle change in the level of gene expression difficult to differentiate by scRNA-Seq. This is supported by the immunostaining for pSMADs and increased nuclear localization of the in some of the NP cells in the ASPN-tg mice that has provide a more direct indication. The above findings, in particular the sc-RNASeq data supports a cell autonomous outcome, although not definitive. Given the reduced funding, as well as the COVID19 restrictions on the transgenic core facility, we did not proceed with the generation of chimeras as stated in the original objective 2, and leverage on the single cell data to provide some clues. We have however, generated the ES cells for this purpose and can used in the future. As a function test, the proteome would be more direct, especially the ECM within the IVD. We performed several rounds of LC MS/MS analyses for 23 samples over 3 timepoints (WT=12, ASPN = 11). Minor changes in the ECM were detected, a major change was a decrease in the level of Fibrillin-1 (FBN1), a micro-fibril forming ECM protein that limits TGFb. Indeed, genetic mutations in FBN1 are associated with the Marfan syndrome, causing excessive TGFb signaling, consistent with our hypothesis. It is possible that over-expressing ASPN in the NP could lead to a destabilization of FBN1, and increase degradation, as the peptide recovery of FBN1 in ASPN-tg mice was reduced in some but not in all time points analysed, indicating a dynamic outcome and detection is context dependent. We argue that Asporin could be involved in the organization the Fibrillin-1 microfilaments localized within the pericellular space, and coordinate the appropriate levels of TGFb signals to NP cells. Interesting, we did not observe detectable changes in the network by immunostaining, or changes in the intensity. It is possible that macroscopic changes may not be detectable higher resolution electron microscopy imaging is needed, but not within the scope of this project. Further, to functionally test whether an inhibition of TGFb signaling using Losartan as part of objective 3. Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor type 1 (AT1) antagonist which inhibits SMAD2/3 signalling and can be administrate via the drinking water (0.6g/L). We selected 3-week-old mice, a time point close to the onset of degeneration and assess whether treatment for 2 weeks has a potential preventative outcome. We perform a study of 6 mice in each group and analysed 7 levels (C4/C5-C10/11) of the tail discs. However, we did not observe any improvement on IVD score of the treated ASPN-tg mice over this treatment period, comparing the IVD histology and an IVD degeneration scoring system. This outcome suggests targeting AT1 may not be effective as IVD is an avascular structure. There may be a need to perform specific molecular markers as further validation. Alternative can also be consider to improve drug delivery in future studies. In summary, we have addressed all objectives as stated in the proposal within the limitation of the reduced funding and scope of this project.

17126118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126118.value: In completing this project, we have generated mouse models to understand the impact of a human genetic risk factor, ASPN, on intervertebral disc degeneration, a major cause of back pain. While ASPN is upregulated in degenerative IVDs, its over-expression in normal discs can induce a degenerative change. Thus, it can be involved in both induction and process, and in combination with other risk factors, adds to the onset and severity of the disease. We showed that ASPN impacts on matrix organization and in part, cellular homeostasis as a functional outcome, possible via alterations in TGFb signaling. While we have yet to identify a potential modifier of TGFb signaling that could be beneficial to reduce the effect of ASPN in the degenerative process, it is a major step in the right direction for more precise investigation using this mouse model, or additional models to be generated. Overall, we have completed all the stated objectives of the proposal. So far, two publications are relevant to this project. First is a major proteomic atlas of the mouse IVDs in the lumbar and tail regions of the mouse spine. This is key paper providing the basis for a comparative assessment of the ASPN-tg mouse (this was published in Matrix Biology Plus). A second, a proteomic atlas of the human IVDs, as this is necessary to demonstrate the relevance of the mouse work to human (this was published in eLife). A third paper is in preparation describing the findings of the ASPN-tg mice. However, we were unable to have this completed for submission in time for this final report. Update of the draft can be provided when available. It was unfortunate that the PhD student involved in this work had to withdrew due to the pandemic. This work was presented in major international conferences as oral presentations.

17126118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126118.value: There are further developments of this project that would enhance the basic understanding of genetic risk factors and the pathway to translation. The approach we have taken using a transgenic approach has its advantage in the generation of a mouse model at the initiation of the project. However, the finding indicates a gene-target approach may be more beneficial in the long-term as it will provide a more stable expression pattern. Thus, directly replacing one allele of the mouse Aspn gene with the human gene using the CRISP-Cas9 system would be an advantage, with more precise expression pattern with the endogenous gene in the relevant tissues. The key findings from the ASPN-tg mice can be confirmed in this new model and further detailed assessments can be continued with this gene targeted mouse model, such as the cellular and molecular changes in older mice. Further, this will provide the most appropriate models for preclinical studies to assessment pharmacological interventions, as additional drugs modulating TGFb signalling are available. As additional risk factors will be identified, and new mouse models generated, the opportunity to study genetic interactions is possible through breeding strategies in mice, which is not possible in human studies.

17126118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126118.value: Back pain is a major burden in society. Many factors can cause back pain. A major reason is degeneration of joints in our spine, the intervertebral discs. A young disc is hydrated, to absorb and protect the spine against mechanical loadings in our daily life. Unfortunately, the discs can become dehydrated, losing its function as it degenerates that can cause excruciating pain. Some of us gets this earlier, while others may be protected due to our genetic makeup. There are genetic risk factors for disc degeneration, and a factor we discovered is Asporin, a disc protein needed for proper function. However, we don’t know why it is the case. To study this, we made a mouse model expressing Asporin and analyse the outcome. One of the changes is more active TGFb signaling. This is interesting as TGFb signaling can be modified by drugs. While we have yet to provide a complete answer, we are on track to understand how this risk factor works, and perhaps insights into other risk factors also, and how risk factors may work together affecting back pain. Intervention is possible through changes in lifestyle and perhaps assisted with pharmacological means.

17126518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126518.value: Tissues under sustained injury or disease state without resolution undergo chronic inflammation and eventually fibrosis, where activity of fibroblasts that are normally induced for wound healing become excessive. Addressing the source and regulation of such abnormal fibroblastic activity is therefore pivotal to the understanding of tissue homeostasis and repair. Intervertebral discs (IVD), as the major articular components in vertebral column, have a central function in spinal motion. Degeneration of IVD is associated with chronic neck and low back pain, and in severe cases may lead to neurological deficit due to nerve compression. The etiology of IVD degeneration is still not well understood to date. IVD degeneration has been regarded as a chronic inflammatory disorder. Consistent with this school of thought, our previous findings and other reports in human and animal models of disc degeneration have consistently implied elements of fibrosis in the core compartment of IVD tissue, the nucleus pulposus (NP), that is known to confer essential biomechanical function to the disc. Such deterioration of biomechanical function is believed to aggravate the inflammatory response and hence degeneration progression. Our recent data indicated a remarkable increase of fibroblasts and its activated form myofibroblasts in degenerative IVD. Moreover, we found that NP cells may directly acquire a phenotype resembling fibroblast/ myofibroblast-like cells in mouse model of induced IVD degeneration. Interestingly, our data also suggested that a specific biglycan proteolytic fragment may induce fibroblast-like phenotype in NP cells in vitro. Our pilot data therefore support a role of fibroblast activation in the course of IVD degeneration and a function of biglycan associated metabolites in the process. Based on these discoveries, we propose to address the following important but yet to be explored questions: Do biglycan fragments per se have a function in inducing NP cell-to-fibroblast conversion in vivo? Can modulating the activity of these fragments alleviate joint degeneration? To address these questions, we plan to utilize an array of established methodologies in our team, including human IVD samples and mouse models that enable lineage tracing in context of induced disc degeneration. The novelty of this proposal lies in the investigation of concept of how matrix degradation product, in particular biglycan, may mediate the fibrotic process via regulating cell phenotype conversion. We envisage that the outcome may provide an alternative perspective on the pathomechanism of IVD degeneration. 17126518.label: Realisation of objectives
17126518.value: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is an irreversible condition and associated with low back pain. IDD is associated with chronic inflammation, involving excessive degradation and remodeling of the extracellular matrix. Etiology of IDD is thought to be multi-factorial and its pathophysiology of IDD remains largely unknown. Studies of biological treatments suggest that modulating the matrix metabolism and inflammatory environment may alleviate IDD. Our previous findings in human and animal models of IDD have implied a role of fibrosis in the nucleus pulposus (NP), the core compartment of the disc that confers key biomechanical function. In previous studies, we have revealed profibrotic events in the NP of human IDD as well as in animal models of injury-induced IDD. However, the regulation of initiation and progression of these profibrotic events is not clear. Our pilot data have implicated a role of fibroblast activation in the course of IDD and a function of biglycan associated metabolites in the process. In this study, we hypothesize that a biglycan neopeptide Bgm1 derived from MMP-12 degradation may positively contribute to the NP fibrosis and the progression of IDD by modulation of fibroblastic activity. Objective 1 aimed to investigate the expression of the biglycan neopeptide Bgm1 (YWEVQPATFR) in disc cell cultures and human IVD specimens. A custom rabbit polyclonal antibody that recognizes Bgm1 (named Bgm1 Y-R) was generated. The specificity of Bgm1 Y-R was verified by immunostaining in a biglycan knockout 293 cell line. Staining in human NP tissues indicated that the expression of Bgm1 was significantly higher in non-degenerative human NP than in degenerative human NP. In mouse, biglycan expression was faintly detected in the notochord at E12.5 and gradually increased in cartilaginous tissues, including the NP, endplate, and annulus. In contrast, Bgm1 expression was detected specifically in the NP region at E15.5, and negatively shown at E12.5 and E14.5. By P15, Bgm1 was expressed in the cartilaginous elements of the disc, particularly the NP. Interestingly, Bgm1 was specifically expressed in the normal NP but the expression was lost by 2-8 weeks of puncture induced IDD, whereas biglycan was expressed in both normal and degenerative conditions. Altogether our data indicated that, unlike biglycan, Bgm1 is preferentially expressed in the NP and its expression is decreased in IDD along with abnormal collagen deposition. This objective was completely achieved. Objective 2 aimed to investigate the function of Bgm1 in NP cell phenotype regulation. The cellular uptake capacity of Bgm1 peptide was examined. We found that fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated Bgm1 could enter the human NP cell cytoplasm after 72 hr treatment, and by 120 hr, most of the FITC-Bgm1 signal could be detected in the nucleus. In a 3D alginate NP cell culture system, COL1A1 expression could be significantly downregulated after 14 days of Bgm1 treatment compared with non-treatment group, whereas treatment with full length BGN did not cause significant alterations. In a 2D monolayer culture system, Bgm1 not only could suppress COL1A1 gene expression compared with non-treatment group, but also significantly inhibited TGF-beta1 induced COL1A1 expression. By transcriptome profiling with RNA sequencing, we found that the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) upregulated by TGF-beta1 correspond to genes related to translational initiation, ribosome biosynthesis, mitochondria-related biological composition and NADH dehydrogenase activity. TGF-beta1 treatment significantly upregulated genes related to collagen deposition, myofibroblast differentiation, matrix catabolism but downregulated chondrocyte markers. Collectively, these data implied that TGF-beta1 may upregulate a fibroblastic phenotype in human NP cells along with increased translational activity. We further tested the effect of Bgm1 on TGF-beta1 treated cells. Under TGF-beta1 treatment, Bgm1, but not biglycan, could significantly downregulate DEGs enriched in inflammatory response and pain perception pathways. Genes related to inflammation and pain sensation were significantly inhibited by Bgm1. RT-qPCR confirmed the gene expression trends. Furthermore, GSEA analysis revealed that compared to the TGF-beta1 -treated group, TGF-beta1 +Bgm1 significantly inhibited ribosome biosynthesis and cell metabolic pathways such as adipogenesis, glycolysis, cholesterol homeostasis and fatty acid metabolism, whereas TGF-beta1 +biglycan did not show any significant alterations. Therefore, our results demonstrated that Bgm1 has a function in inhibiting inflammatory pathway and possibly modulate pain perception. This objective was completely achieved. Based on the initial perception that Bgm1 might promote fibrosis, Objective 3 was originally set out to test if inhibiting Bgm1 may modify IDD. However, our findings indicated a contrasting action of Bgm1 where it may exert an inhibitory effect on fibrosis and hence potential function to alleviate IDD. In the meantime, outbreak of COVID has also led to limited support of animal facility to conduct animal experimentation. We therefore moved forward with Objective 4 as an alternative. In view of the interesting findings in vitro and in vivo, we studied the potential mechanism of action of Bgm1 as Objective 4. Consistent with the in vivo staining data, we examined the Bgm1 expression in JHC7 cell line (which resembles notochordal cells) and primary human NP cells and observed positive signals. Western blot demonstrated that Bgm1 was predominantly expressed intracellularly rather than extracellularly at a size of ~34 kDa. By immunoprecipitation, this ~34 kDa band was specific detected in the Bgm1 pull-down group but not in the IgG group, suggesting that the~34kDa protein contained a Bgm1 sequestered protein complex. Further proteomic analysis by LC-MS/MS identified eIF6 (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 6) as a binding protein of Bgm1. Co-immunoprecipitation study suggested that the ~34kDa band pulled down by Bgm1Y-R antibody could also be detected by anti-eIF6 antibody. Similar eIF6 and Bgm1 expression pattern in induced mice IDD and in developing mouse discs was found. In silico modelling indicated that the potential binding region of eIF6 is at the C-terminus of biglycan, which is consistent with the Bgm1 position. These data therefore indicated that Bgm1 may interact with eIF6 intracellularly in notochordal cells. The capacity of Bgm1 in interacting with eIF6 is consistent with its effect on ribosome production and cell metabolism observed in the human NP cells (in Objective 2).

17126518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126518.value: In this study, we found that intact biglycan and its C-terminal Bgm1 fragment are differentially expressed during intervertebral disc development. Biglycan was found expressed in the notochord whereas Bgm1 was preferentially detected in the postnatal NP. In adult human and mouse discs, Bgm1 is preferentially expressed in the NP, whereas biglycan is more widely expressed in the disc and in the growth plate. Bgm1 expression is reduced in both human IDD and injury-induced mouse IDD model. These findings implicate an important role of Bgm1 in regulating disc homeostasis. We further found that eIF6 may interact with Bgm1 in notochordal cells. TGF-beta1 is a pro-fibrogenic factor. We found that TGF-β treatment could increase eIF6 and COL1A1 expression in human NP cells, while Bgm1 could significantly reduce TGF-β-induced COL1A1 expression, implying that Bgm1 may counter TGF-β signaling. In addition, transcriptome profiling indicated that TGF-β treatment may cause an upregulation of glycan production but downregulation of lipid and fatty acid degradation. Interestingly, exogenous Bgm1 could significantly inhibit changes in genes related to glycolysis, adipogenesis and fatty acid metabolism induced by TGF-β treatment. These results are consistent with the previously reported activity of eIF6, inferring that Bgm1 may interact with eIF6 to regulate NP cell phenotype and metabolism. Previous studies attributed inflammation and fibrosis to IDD. Consistent with the role of biglycan in coordinating the formation of collagen network, we found that the expression pattern of biglycan coincides with the region of collagen deposition in the disc. In contrast, Bgm1 was found negatively correlated to collagen deposition. Addition of exogenous Bgm1 in NP cell culture could upregulate fibrosis and inflammation-related pathways. However, in TGF-beta1 treated degenerative NP cells, Bgm1 could suppress genes related to inflammatory response. Together with the finding of eIF6 as a partner of Bgm1, we hypothesize that Bgm1 and eIF6 may co-regulate NP cell phenotype and function, and hence contribute to homeostasis of intervertebral disc.

17126518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126518.value: Our results provide new insights into the function of biglycan in intervertebral disc and its potential contribution to the etiology of IDD. This study gives rise to knowledge about the unidentified roles of degraded proteoglycans in molecular pathomechanism of IDD beyond the structural and mechanical attributes of their native forms. While our findings are indicative for a role of Bgm1 in the regulation of disc homeostasis, further studies are required to determine if Bgm1 can be a therapeutic target of IDD. While injury-induced mouse IDD model has shown relevance to human IDD, investigation of Bgm1 in large animal models is desirable for its translation in future. Moreover, in the present study, the biological function of Bgm1 was achieved by in vitro analysis of exogenous Bgm1-treated cells. The precise mechanistic pathway in particular the interaction between Bgm1 and eIF6 awaits to be elucidated. Further investigation may also focus on the processing and role of endogenous Bgm1 in IDD.

17126518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126518.value: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) causes back and neck pain, which has become a global public health concern and seriously impacts quality of life and healthcare system worldwide. Biglycan is a proteoglycan molecule which has a function not only as an extracellular matrix but also in regulating cell-matrix communication. The degradation of biglycan has been implicated in IDD. In this study, we found that a conserved C-terminal fragment of biglycan peptide, termed Bgm1, and intact biglycan are expressed in different manner during disc development. Human and mouse studies demonstrated that Bgm1 is preferentially expressed in the postnatal nucleus pulposus and is reduced in IDD. Bgm1 could counter the effect of profibrotic regulator and may interact with eIF6, a translational initiation factor to regulate the protein synthesis. In conclusion, this study implies a role of Bgm1 in IDD progression and implicates an active role of proteoglycan in maintaining disc homeostasis. Together with eIF6, Bgm1 may exert a function in modulating disc cell metabolism and profibrotic activities. Our findings provide new insights into the etiology and potential therapeutic option for IDD.

17126618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126618.value: Posttranslational modifications (PTMs) of histones, for example, methylation, acetylation, phosphorylation, and ubiquitylation, play essential roles in regulating gene functions. Other than directly changing the physicochemical properties of the modified residues, histone PTMs (or marks) can serve as the docking sites for effector proteins ('readers') that specifically recognize them. By recruiting readers to the chromatin, histone PTMs signal the downstream biological events (e.g., gene transcription, DNA replication and repair), which underlies one of the key cellular mechanisms for epigenetic regulation. Given their importance in maintaining normal cell physiology, dysregulation of histone PTMs and their 'readers' may lead to the pathogenesis of human diseases, such as cancer. The identification and characterization of 'readers' of histone PTMs, and the development of chemical probes that target the 'readers', are important to decipher their biological significance. The proposed research will focus on the development of chemical tools for the identification and interrogation of histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) 'readers'. Although several Kcr 'reasers' have been reported, but a systematic profiling is still lacking. To fulfill this knowledge gap, we will develop a chemical proteomics approach to comprehensively profile the 'readers' of two Kcr mark (i.e., H3K9cr and K3H27cr) at whole cell proteome level, and characterize how the 'readers' recognize Kcr using multiple methods. We will also develop chemical inhibitor for YEATS domain, a newly identified 'reader' of Kcr, as chemical probes to interrogate the roles played by YEATS domain-containing proteins in gene transcription. The completion of this project will help us understand the roles of histone Kcr and their 'readers' in gene regulation. In the long term, the findings from this project will lay the foundation for elucidating how histone Kcr contributes to human health and disease, and provide leads for the development of therapeutic agents for the treatment of human diseases associated with improper ‘reading’ of histone Kcr marks. 組蛋白的翻譯後修飾（例如：甲基化、乙酰化、磷酸化和泛素化）在基因功能調控中扮演者重要的角色。除了直接改變所修飾殘基的物理化學性質之外，組蛋白修飾（或稱標記）也為一些具有特異性識別能力的效應蛋白（即“閲讀器”）提供了停靠位點。通過把這些“閲讀器”招募到染色質上來，組蛋白修飾可以引發信號以啟動下游的生物事件（例如：基因轉錄、DNA複製與修復）。這就成為了表觀遺傳學調控中一種關鍵的細胞機制。由於組蛋白修飾及其“閲讀器”在維持細胞正常生理過程的重要性，其失調可能導致很多人類疾病的產生，例如癌症。因此，鑒定和表徵組蛋白修飾的“閲讀器”，並開發靶向這些“閲讀器”的化學探針，對於解密其生物學重要性有著極其重要的意義。 本研究將聚焦於開發化學工具以鑒定並探究組蛋白賴氨酸巴豆酰化（Kcr）的“閲讀器”。雖然已有幾個組蛋白Kcr的“閲讀器”被報導，但對這類“閲讀器”系統的搜尋鑒定卻仍未有先例。為了填補這一認知空白，我們將要開發一種化學蛋白組學方法，在全細胞蛋白質組水平，系統全面的鑒定兩個組蛋白Kcr標記（即H3K9cr 和 K3H27cr）的“閲讀器”，並運用多種方法以闡明這些“閲讀器”是如何識別相應的Kcr標記的。此外，我們也將開發靶向一類新發現的Kcr“閲讀器”（YEATS結構域）的化學抑制劑，並用於研究含有YEATS結構域蛋白在基因轉錄中扮演的角色。這個課題的完成將幫助我們理解組蛋白Kcr修飾及其“閲讀器”在基因調控中的角色。長期來講，這個課題的發現將成為闡明組蛋白Kcr對人類健康和疾病意義的基礎，併為開發治療由組蛋白Kcr“閲讀”調控異常所引致的人類疾病的藥物提供先導化合物。

17126618.label: Realisation of objectives
17126618.value: Objective 1: To comprehensively identify histone crotonylation ‘readers’ using a chemical proteomics approach. In order to identify proteins that specifically recognize Kcr mark (i.e., ‘readers’) at histone H3 Lys27 (H3K27cr), we have designed and synthesized two complementary photoaffinity probes (probe 1 and 2) based on the sequence of a histone H3 peptide (L20-G34) carrying K27cr. In probe 1, a diazirine-based photo-cross-linker was introduced to replace the original A29 residue (C-terminal to K27), while in probe 2, the A24 residue (N-terminal to K27) was replaced. The application of two probes may avoid the loss of target proteins that can result from the disruption of Kcr-mediated PPIs caused by the introduction of a photo-cross-linker at one site. Each of the probes also carries a terminal alkyne group to facilitate biorthogonal ‘click’ chemistry-mediated conjugation of reporter tags for the affinity enrichment (via affinity purification tag, e.g., biotin) of the captured proteins. We carried out cross-linking-assisted and SILAC-based protein identification (CLASPI) to capture potential ‘readers’ of H3K27cr in the whole-cell proteome. To identify proteins that bind H3K27cr with high selectivity and high affinity, we performed two types of CLASPI experiments. Briefly, in the ‘selectivity filter’ CLASPI experiment, the ‘heavy’ and ‘light’ cell lysates were photo-cross-linked with probe 1 (or probe 2) and unmodified probe C1 (or probe C2), respectively, and pooled for the subsequent steps. In the ‘affinity filter’ CLASPI experiment, both ‘light’ and ‘heavy’ lysates were photo-cross-linked with probe 1 (or probe 2), but the ‘light’ sample will also have added H3K27cr peptide as a competitor. We designated proteins that show high SILAC ratios of heavy/light (H/L) in both ‘selectivity filter’ and ‘affinity filter’ as selective and tight H3K27cr binders, which included YEATS4, TRIP10, DMAP1, CTDP1, BCLAF1, NDRG1, FOLR1, TAF15. The identification of YEATS4, a known H3K27cr ‘reader’, indicated the reliability of the data. Objective 2: To develop chemical probes against YEATS domains for interrogating their roles in gene transcription. The YEATS domain was recently identified as a novel ‘reader’ of histone lysine acetylation (Kac) and Kcr marks. The human genome encodes four YEATS domain-containing proteins, which are AF9, ENL, YEATS2, and Gas41. The AF9 YEATS domain was found to mediate active transcription through reading the histone Kac and Kcr marks. The YEATS-dependent association of ENL with acetylated histone H3 was reported to be essential for oncogenic gene expression in aggressive leukemia. Despite these discoveries, we have limited knowledge of the functional outcomes of YEATS-Kac/Kcr interactions in epigenetic regulation. The development of YEATS domain inhibitors should provide useful tools to fill such a knowledge gap, and could offer potential therapeutic agents for the treatment of diseases associated with the abnormal ‘reading’ of histone Kac/Kcr marks by YEATS domain-containing proteins. We developed the first class of YEATS domain inhibitors by targeting a unique π-π>-π>stacking interaction at the proteins’ Kcr recognition site. Further structure optimization resulted in the selective inhibitors preferentially binding to individual YEATS-containing proteins including AF9 and ENL with submicromolar affinities. We demonstrate that one of the ENL YEATS-selective inhibitors, XL-13m, engages with endogenous ENL, perturbs the recruitment of ENL onto chromatin, and synergizes the BET and DOT1L inhibition-induced down-regulation of oncogenes in MLL-rearranged acute leukemia. However, the reported YEATS domain inhibitors developed by us and others often have a general preference toward AF9 and ENL YEATS domains, and selective inhibitors targeting either YEATS domain are challenging to develop as these two proteins share a high structural similarity. Crystal structure analysis revealed that inhibitors with proper functional groups approaching the Loop 8 region in YEATS domains should show selectivity between AF9 and ENL. We reasoned that cyclization of the original linear peptides by replacing the hydrogen bond with covalent linkages could rigidify the inhibitors to the AF9 YEATS-favored conformation. Based on the structures of previously reported inhibitors, we first developed four cyclopeptide inhibitors (JYX-1 to JYX-4) carrying either a furan or an oxazole ring at the lysine side chain. We adopted a fluorescence-based competitive photo-cross-linking assay to estimate the inhibitory activity of these four cyclopeptides on AF9 YEATS. The results showed that all of the four inhibitors could efficiently block the interaction between AF9 YEATS and a crotonylated peptide probe 1. Specifically, JYX-3 (IC50 = 0.41 uM) and JYX-4 (IC50 = 0.56 uM) exhibited higher potencies than JYX-1 (IC50 = 1.78 uM) and JYX-2 (IC50 = 2.23 uM), and more importantly, JYX-3 and JYX-4 showed 31-fold and 19-fold decreased inhibitory activity on ENL YEATS (JYX-3, IC50 = 12.80 uM; JYX-4, IC50 = 10.84 uM) than that on AF9 YEATS, respectively, indicating a substantially increased selectivity toward AF9 over ENL compared with the linear precursor. We next monitored the engagement of JYX-3 with endogenous AF9. To this end, we proceeded to examine the performance of JYX-3 in living cells. Using the immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography and the parallel artificial membrane permeability assay (PAMPA), we first demonstrated that the cyclization indeed increased the lipophilicity and passive transport rate of the inhibitor. Although there would still be a large space to improve, JYX-3 behaved comparably to theophylline, a model drug known to have relatively low cell membrane permeability39. In addition, JYX-3 exhibited higher stability than its linear precursor. We next applied the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) to determine whether JYX-3 could target AF9 in living cells. HeLa cells treated with or without 20 uM JYX-3 were heated at different temperatures. Soluble proteins were then extracted and analyzed by immunoblotting. As expected, JYX-3 helped AF9 resist the high temperature-induced denaturation, while the thermal stability of ENL remained unchanged upon the inhibitor treatment. The CETSA results indicated that JYX-3 could traverse the cell membrane and selectively engage with the endogenous AF9, but not ENL, under the tested condition. We next sought to explore the effects of JYX-3 on the AF9 YEATS-dependent regulation of gene expression. By performing chromatin immunoprecipitation and quantitative PCR (ChIP-qPCR) in HeLa cells, we detected reduced abundances of AF9 and H3K79me3, but not ENL, on MYC and PABPC1 upon JYX-3 treatment, suggesting that the cyclopeptide could disrupt the YEATS-dependent enrichment of AF9 on its target genes and could further prevent the recruitment of DOT1L. In addition, exposure of HeLa cells to JYX-3 induced significant losses in the transcription levels of MYC and PABPC1, which was in good accordance with the unloading of AF9 from these two genes. Our observations agree with the previous discoveries that AF9 downregulation or Kac-binding-impairing mutations in AF9 YEATS led to transcription defects of its target genes. For the developed AF9 YEATS domain-selective cyclopeptide inhibitors, the cumbersome and time-consuming synthesis of the cyclopeptides limited further structural derivatization and applications. One more step forward, we developed a concise solid-phase synthesis of cyclopeptide inhibitors targeting YEATS domains. This new route outcompetes the previously reported approach by substantially reducing the synthesis time and increasing the overall yield. We also showed that the proper selection of orthogonal protecting groups allowed derivatization of the cyclopeptides. As proof of concept, we successfully obtained the cyclopeptide inhibitor carrying either a TAT cell-penetrating peptide or a fluorescence tag at the original Ala position. Although not yet tested, we believe further modifications of the cyclopeptide at other sites, for example, the current Cbz moiety, can be achieved by introducing protecting groups with additional orthogonalities.

17126618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126618.value: With the support of this GRF, we systematically profiled histone crotonylation ‘readers’ using a chemical proteomics approach, and have developed chemical probes against YEATS domains for interrogating their roles in gene transcription. The major findings and outcomes are: (1) YEATS domains are newly identified epigenetic ‘readers’ of histone lysine acetylation and crotonylation. Guided by the structural analysis of a YEATS-Kcr complex, we developed the first class of peptide-based inhibitors of YEATS domains by targeting a unique π-π>-π >stacking interaction at the proteins’ Kcr recognition site. Further structure optimization resulted in the selective inhibitors preferentially binding to individual YEATS-containing proteins including AF9 and ENL with submicromolar affinities. We demonstrated that one of the ENL YEATS-selective inhibitors, XL-13m, engages with endogenous ENL, perturbs the recruitment of ENL onto chromatin, and synergizes the BET and DOT1L inhibition-induced down-regulation of the oncogenes in MLL-rearranged acute leukemia. (Nat Chem Biol 2018) (2) Selective inhibitors targeting either AF9 or ENL YEATS domain are challenging to develop as these two proteins share a high structural similarity. To address this challenge, we identified a proximal site outside the acyllysine-binding pocket that can differentiate AF9 YEATS from ENL YEATS. Combinatorial targeting of both the acyllysine pocket and this additional site by conformationally preorganized cyclopeptides enabled the selective inhibition of AF9 YEATS domain. The most selective inhibitor, JYX-3, showed a 38-fold higher binding affinity toward AF9 YEATS over ENL YEATS. Further investigations indicated that JYX-3 could engage with AF9 in living cells, disrupt the YEATS-dependent chromatin recruitment of AF9, and suppress the transcription of AF9 target genes. (J Am Chem Soc. 2020) (3) For the developed AF9 YEATS domain-selective cyclopeptide inhibitors, we reported a concise method for the solid‐phase synthesis of the cyclopeptides, which substantially reduced the amount of time required for the preparation of the cyclopeptides and led to a higher overall yield. Moreover, we demonstrated that the conjugation of the cyclopeptide with cell-penetrating peptide TAT led to a significantly increased cellular uptake. (Bioorg Med Chem. 2021) (4) We also expanded our study to lysine acetylation. Bromodomains, epigenetic "readers" of lysine acetylation marks, have emerged as therapeutic targets for drug discovery. We developed a photoaffinity probe, photo-bromosporine (photo-BS), that enables comprehensive evaluations of bromodomain inhibitors in terms of their selectivity against endogenous bromodomain-containing proteins in living cells. (J Am Chem Soc. 2019)

17126618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126618.value: For future perspectives: 1. To validate and characterize the identified potential ‘readers’ of histone Kcr marks at the single protein level and in living cells using multidisciplinary methods. We will measure the binding affinities of these protein targets toward the corresponding Kcr peptides using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), and fluorescence polarization (FP) assay, followed by performing X-ray crystallography analysis of the protein-Kcr peptide complexes to determine the molecular basis for the recognition. Based on the structures, we will carry out site-directed mutation of residues in both proteins and peptides to evaluate their contribution to the Kcr-mediated protein-protein interactions. 2. To develop small-molecule inhibitors of YEATS domains. Compared with peptide-based inhibitors, because of the high structural diversity and better physicochemical properties, small-molecule inhibitors are widely used in biological studies. To identify the candidates of small molecule YEATS inhibitors, we will use a fluorescence polarization (FP)-based method to perform the high-throughput screening (HTS) against the library of FDA-approved drugs, the commercial small-molecule library from ChemBridge, and the small molecule library from National Cancer Institute (over 1 million compounds in total) using individual YEATS domain. Peptide-based inhibitors developed in this project will be used as the template for the FP probe design.

17126618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126618.value: Histone PTMs can recruit specific effector proteins (‘readers’) to the chromatin to signal the downstream cellular events, such as gene expression, DNA replication, and repair. Improper ‘reading’ of histone PTMs has been implicated in human diseases such as cancer. Thus, the identification and characterization of 'readers' of histone PTMs, and the development of chemical probes that target the 'readers', are important to decipher their biological significance. Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) was discovered in 2011, and very recently, YEATS domains have been identified as novel ‘readers’ of histone Kac and Kcr marks. In this project, we systematically profiled histone crotonylation ‘readers’ using a chemical proteomics approach, and have developed chemical probes against YEATS domains for interrogating their roles in gene transcription. Our results greatly expand the repertoire of ‘readers’ of histone Kcr and provide critical information on how this new histone PTM is ‘translated’ during gene expression. The findings could also help us to unravel how malfunctions of YEATS domains mediate pathogenic transcriptional programs, which may eventually lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of human diseases associated with improper ‘reading’ of histone marks by YEATS domains.
