17126918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126918.value: Plant biomass represents an abundant and sustainable raw material for biofuel ethanol production. However, the presence of lignin impedes the release of sugar (saccharification) from cellulose for fermentation. Lignin is a phenolic polymer interspersed extensively with polysaccharides in plant cell wall. In most plants, lignin is primarily derived from oxidative couplings of monolignols. Recently, a wide range of monocots were discovered to utilize a member of flavonoid, tricin, as a natural co-monomer with monolignols for cell wall lignification. Our recent studies indicate that disruption of a gene encoding flavone synthase II (FNSII) in rice results in reduced cell wall lignin content which is devoid of tricin but incorporated with another flavonoid (naringenin). FNSII is a key enzyme for the biosynthesis of tricin in grasses. The rice fnsII mutant was further demonstrated to have enhanced enzymatic saccharification efficiency without negative impacts on biomass production and grain yield. Hence, it is hypothesized that manipulation of flavonoid biosynthesis represents a novel strategy to improve the efficiency of grass biomass as feedstocks for ethanol fermentation. Using rice as a model system, this project takes a comprehensive approach to manipulate a number of reaction steps in flavonoid biosynthesis by targeted mutation or ectopic expression through transformation. Subsequently, a combination of metabolite, chemical, histochemical, and NMR analyses will be conducted to determine the flavonoid profile as well as lignin content and composition in the transgenic rice biomass, followed by enzymatic saccharification assays. We expect to reveal new molecular targets useful for genetic engineering to improve the cell wall digestibility of grass biomass for ethanol biofuel production. Discoveries from this work can be directly applied in rice straw or translated to other cereal residues and biofuel grass crops (e.g. sorghum, switchgrass, bamboo), which all accumulate substantial amounts of tricin-bound lignin. This work will also advance our understanding on the relationships between flavonoid biosynthesis and lignification in the grass family.

17126918.label: Realisation of objectives
17126918.value: Rice mutant lines for characterization Rice genes encoding chalcone synthase (OsCHS1), chalcone isomerase (CHI), chalcone isomerase-like proteins (OsCHIL1 and OsCHIL2), apigenin 3’-hydroxylase/chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase (CYP75B4), and 5-hydroxyconiferaldehyde O-methyltransferase (OsCAldOMT1) were selected for analysis in this study. T-DNA insertion mutants were available for OsCHS1 and CYP75B4 (Huazhong Agricultural University, China) and OsCAldOMT1 (Kyung Hee University, Korea). Homozygous mutant and near-isogenic wild-type lines were isolated for subsequent analyses. Knockout mutants of OsCHI and OsCHIL were generated by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis. For OsCHI, a CRISPR/Cas9 vector harboring a single-guide RNA (sgRNA) specific for the second exon of this gene was transformed into rice. Two homozygous OsCHI-CRISPR mutant lines (T2 generation) with different mutations (OsCHI-CRISPR-a and OsCHI-CRISPR-b) were isolated. We also generated OsCHIL1 and OsCHIL2 double-knockout mutants using a multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 construct harboring two sgRNAs that target different conserved sequences in OsCHIL1 and OsCHIL2. Two homozygous mutant lines (T2 generation) with different mutations (OsCHIL-CRISPR-a and OsCHIL-CRISPR-b) were obtained. All the mutant plants (T2 and T3 generations) used for further studies were genotyped and confirmed to harbor consistent mutations without off-target mutations for each sgRNA. Multiple sequence alignment suggested that the indels in the mutant lines resulted in frameshift mutations, leading to truncated non-functional proteins, and loss-of-function mutations were expected. Analysis of mutant flavonoid profiles We have published the flavonoid profiles for CYP75B4 and OsCAldOMT1 previously. In this study, we determined the effects of CHS, CHI, and CHIL genetic mutations on the biosynthesis of soluble flavonoids. Metabolites extracted from the leaves of the mutant and wild-type seedlings were analyzed by LC-MS/MS. Various flavones, such as apigenin, luteolin, chrysoeriol, and tricin, and flavone C-glycosides, including vitexin, isovitexin, orientin, and isoorientin, were detected in the wild-type plants. Compared with wild-type plants, flavone and flavone C-glycoside contents in the OsCHS1-TDNA plants decreased by more than 81%. The contents of most flavonoids in OsCHI-CRISPR-a and OsCHI-CRISPR-b plants decreased by more than 79%, relative to the wild-type control. Additionally, naringenin chalcone, the CHI substrate, accumulated substantially in the OsCHI-CRISPR-a and OsCHI-CRISPR-b plants, but barely detectable in the wild-type control and other mutant lines. Collectively, these results demonstrate that OsCHS1 and OsCHI are respectively the predominant CHS and CHI responsible for the biosynthesis of the major soluble flavones in rice. Similar to the OsCHS1-TDNA and the OsCHI-CRISPR lines, flavone and flavone C-glycoside contents were much lower in the OsCHIL-CRISPR lines than wild-type controls, demonstrating that, together with OsCHS1 and OsCHI, CHILs play key roles in the biosynthesis of the soluble flavones in rice. Meanwhile, similar to the OsCHS1-TDNA line but in contrast to the OsCHI-CRISPR lines, the OsCHIL-CRISPR lines did not accumulate naringenin chalcone. These findings are consistent with the previous reports that CHIL serves as a non-catalytic enhancer of CHS, but not of CHI. Tricin biosynthesis in Medicago legumes: convergent recruitment of chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase activities. We also examined the functions of CYP75B enzymes in a rare group of tricin-accumulating dicot, the Medicago legumes (Medicago truncatula and alfalfa). Five Medicago cytochrome P450 CYP75B FBHs were found to be phylogenetically distant from other legume CYP75B members. Among them, MtFBH-4, MsFBH-4 and MsFBH-10 were expressed in tricin-accumulating vegetative tissues. In vitro and in planta analyses demonstrated that these proteins catalyze 3´- and 5´-hydroxylations critical to tricin biosynthesis. A key amino acid polymorphism, T492G, at their Substrate Recognition Site 6 domain is required for the novel 5´-hydroxylation activities. We obtained seeds of two independent M. truncatula mutant lines for MtFBH-4 which harbor transposable element of Nicotiana tabacum cell type 1 (tnt1) insertions from the Noble Research Institute. LC-MS/MS analyses showed that M. truncatula mtfbh-4 mutants are tricin-deficient, indicating that MtFBH-4 is indispensable for tricin biosynthesis. Objective 2: Characterization of cell wall properties for the transgenic rice lines Cell wall properties for the different transgenic rice mutants were analyzed in comparison to their respective wild-type controls. Histochemical staining of transverse sections using phloroglucinol-HCl and vanillin-HCl were performed on culms and sheaths. Extractive-free cell wall residues (CWRs) for chemical analyses were prepared from dried culms and sheaths. For two-dimensional (2D) NMR analysis, CWRs were further ball-milled and digested with crude cellulase to give lignin-enriched CWRs. Thioglycolic acid lignin content assay, Klason lignin analysis, thioacidolysis, cell-wall-bound p-coumarate (pCA) and ferulate (FA) content analysis, and amorphous and crystalline neutral sugar composition assay were also performed. The enzymatic saccharification efficiency of destarched CWRs was determined by hydrolysis with a cellulolytic enzyme cocktail. Concentration of glucose released at each incubation time point was determined. CYP75B4 mutant Secondary thickened cell walls of cortical sclerenchyma and vascular bundle cells in both culm and leaf sheath sections of wild-type and CYP75B4 mutant were stained positive for lignin but there was a strong depletion of wall-bound flavonoids, presumably tricin-lignins, in the mutant cell walls as revealed by histochemical staining. In addition, thioglycolic acid assay and the Klason method revealed significant reduction of cell wall lignin content in mutant culm and leaf sheath. 2D-NMR analyses revealed that aromatic signals from G, S, H lignin units are present in the mutant lignin but not those from tricin units. Instead, apigenin was incorporated as a non-canonical monomer. Further structural analyses suggested that CYP75B4 disruption also affected cell wall components including monolignol-derived lignin fractions and hemicellulosic arabinoxylans. Significant enhancement of the saccharification efficiency was recorded for the mutant over wild-type CWRs at all time points when glucose released is expressed per mass of CWR (12-26% enhancement), and also after 12 h when expressed per total glucan (15-19% enhancement). Thus, CYP75B4 disruption reduces cell wall recalcitrance and boosts the production of fermentable sugars from rice lignocellulose. OsCAldOMT1 mutant The mutant is largely depleted in S units and partially incorporated with atypical 5H units. These results collectively support the notion that OsCAldOMT1 is a predominant CAldOMT functioning in S lignin biosynthesis in rice. Importantly, histochemical and 2D NMR analysis also established that lignin-bound tricin was drastically reduced in the OsCAldOMT1-deficient rice cell walls (Figs 3 and 4), demonstrating the crucial role of OsCAldOMT1 in the biosynthesis of not only the sinapyl alcohol but also the tricin monomers for lignification. In fact, our NMR data suggested that lignin-integrated tricin units were nearly absent in the mutant cell wall. The mutant also displayed enhanced biomass saccharification efficiency over the wild-type controls by around 60% after 24 h incubation. OsCHS1, OsCHI, and OsCHIL mutants They showed different changes in lignin contents when compared with their respective wild-type controls. While OsCHS1 mutant showed no significant difference in lignin content, OsCH1 mutant showed 33.6% reduction and OsCHIL mutant showed 12.6% increase. Meanwhile, thioacidolysis-released S, G, H units were unchanged in OsCHS1 mutant, but significantly decreased in OsCHI mutant and increased in OsCHIL mutant. 2D-NMR analysis revealed the depletion of tricin units in lignins from all three mutants. Surprisingly, none of the mutants exhibited any significant enhancement in the enzymatic saccharification efficiency expressed either as glucose released per mass of CWR or as glucose released per total glucan. These findings sharply contrasted with our above results regarding tricin-depleted rice mutants defective in CYP75B4, OsCAldOMT1 as well as our previous study on OsFNSII mutant (Lam et al. 2017 Plant Physiol 174(2):972-985. doi: 10.1104/pp.16.01973). Collectively, our results reflect the complexity in the metabolic consequences of tricin pathway perturbations and the relationships between lignin profiles and cell wall properties.

17126918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126918.value: Pub no. 1: We have established the indispensable role of the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP75B4 in the generation of tricin-lignin in rice. CYP75B4 serves as a bifunctional hydroxylase in tricin biosynthesis: apigenin 3’-hydroxylase and chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase. CYP75B4 is co-expressed with OsFNSII (CYP93G2) which catalyzes the first committed step for tricin biosynthesis. CYP75B4 mutation results in tricin-depleted lignin which in turn improved the cellulose digestibility of rice biomass. Pub no. 2: In collaboration with Kyoto University (Y Tobimatsu and T Umezawa), we demonstrated that OsCAldOMT1 is involved in production of tricin-lignin in rice. OsCAldOMT1 is a bifunctional enzyme which catalyzes O-methylation reactions in both monolignol and flavone pathways. Consistently, we found that OsAldOMT1 mutation resulted in altered lignin which is depleted in both syringly and tricin unit. We further demonstrated that OsAldOMT1 deficiency could enhance cellulose digestibility of rice biomass. Pub no. 3: We demonstrated that Medicago legumes, including M. truncatula and alfalfa, recruited CYP75B proteins to catalyze 5’-hydroxylations of chrysoeriol independent from that of CYP75B4 and orthologs which are highly conserved in the grass family. In particular, MtFBH-4 is indispensable for tricin biosynthesis in M. truncatula. The Medicago legumes are rare examples of tricin-accumulating dicots. We further demonstrated that the 5’-hydroxylation activity requires a key amino acid substitution (T492G) in the SRS6 site. This paper was featured in a commentary (https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.16827) by John Ralph who is a renowned lignin biochemist. Pub no. 4: We demonstrated that CHS and CHI as well as the non-catalytic CHS enhancer CHIL are all involved in the generation of tricin for lignin formation in rice cell wall. While lignin composition and content are differentially altered in the CHS, CHI, and CHIL mutants, their cell wall lignins were nearly devoid of tricin units. Surprisingly, cellulose digestibility of the biomass of these mutants did not show significant differences from wild-type controls. Pub no. 5 and conference meetings no. 1, 2, and 3: We were invited to write a review article on flavonoid biosynthesis for Frontiers in Plant Science. In this paper, we reviewed our work on CYP75B4, MtFBH-4, OsCAldOMT1, CHS, CHI, and CHIL derived from this GRF project along with other recent literatures on related work. In addition, results from this work were presented as seminars at three international conferences. Two PhD students: Dr. Lanxiang Wang was working on the CHS, CHI, and CHIL experiments. Dr. Cheuk Woon Lui was working on the CYP75B4 and MtFBH-4 experiments.

17126918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126918.value: We have successfully identified two additional molecular components, namely CYP75B4 and OsCAldOMT1 that can be manipulated genetically to enhance biomass digestibility (i.e. enzyme saccharification), potentially improving the quality of grass biomass for use as bioenergy feedstock. Meanwhile, they represent targets for investigation of molecular regulators that control the biosynthesis of tricin. Accordingly, we submitted the GRF application (project no. 17104720) which was funded with HKD 1,195,542 in 2020-2021.

17126918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126918.value: Feedstocks for cellulosic bio-ethanol production are derived from agricultural residues or biomass crops. However, the major barrier for cellulosic ethanol production is the presence of lignin which is a complex polymer providing mechanical support in plants. In grasses, tricin is used as a co-monomer for lignification and its biosynthesis was elucidated by our laboratory previously. In this study, disruption of genes encoding CHS, CHI, CHIL, CYP75B4, or OsCAldOMT1 for tricin biosynthesis was achieved in transgenic rice which were subject to different chemical analyses. We demonstrated that disruption of CYP75B4 or OsCAldOMT1 resulted in reduced production of lignin which is devoid of tricin. On the other hand, the disruptions did not alter growth and productivity. Importantly, the transgenic biomass materials showed enhanced enzymatic saccharification efficiencies, meaning that more glucose could be released by digestion of cellulose from cell wall. Hence, CYP75B4 and OsCAldOMT1 represent promising targets for genetic manipulation to improve the digestibility of grass biomass for use as feedstock in bio-ethanol production. Meanwhile, we discovered that MtFBH-4 shared the same function as CYP75B4 during tricin biosynthesis in Medicago legumes including alfalfa which is an important forage crop. MtFBH-4 may be manipulated to improve forage digestibility for livestock feeding.

17127218.label: Realisation of objectives
17127218.value: Our study objectives as originally planned were not realized due to sequential rounds of unanticipated events throughout the study period. In our protocol, we have originally proposed a study period of 30 months from Oct 2018 to Mar 2021, and later on with a revision of a 6-month extension to 36 mouths until Sept 2021. As proposed in the grant application, recruitment was planned to take place during influenza seasons in various university health clinics of local universities, where have previously successfully collaborated with us, and have kindly agreed to support this project. On issuance of the grant, relevant preparatory works were initiated and implemented, including ground work of relevant approval application, trial medical production with regulatory certification, and liaison with working out of the relevant workflow plans with all involved stakeholders, including the University Health Service (UHS) of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) and the Health Centre at the Hong Kong Community College for participant recruitment, the virology laboratory in the Division of Public Health Laboratory Sciences of HKU School of Public Health for virological testing, and the HKU Department of Medicine for serological testing. Despite all these successful preparatory works, the actual field works of participant recruitment, however, was never able to get started. This was due initially to the territory wide social event since mid-2019, leading to the severe disruption to social order and public transportation, and damage caused to the UHS clinic and other campus facilities at PolyU with resultant prolonged school suspension and facility repairment. This was, however, followed closely by the arrival of the novel COVID-19 pandemic in the local community since December 2019, which have resulted in the ever tightening infection control and social distancing restrictions necessitated by the ongoing waves of the pandemic. As explained continuously in our submitted progress reports, the project implementation and timeline was severely disrupted during the whole study period as a result of the above explained unexpected social event and COVID-19 pandemic. Although we have once remained optimistic and hoping that the delayed progress can ultimately be catched up, with the anticipated further lessening of community lockdown restrictions in the later part of our original planned study period, this has turned out not to be the case with the worsening pandemic situation, evolving local pandemic waves with emerging variants, and related governmental anti-pandemic policy in the local community. As of today (November 2022), access to the campus and facilities in PolyU, including the UHS, were still tightly controlled by pre-registration and event-based specifically-issued QR codes by the relevant units. On the other hand, under the tight infection control consideration, activities that are not considered absolutely essential, including recruitment work for individuals with respiratory symptoms for research study, is deemed inappropriate and thus not allowed in all public and private outpatient settings we continuously explored, making the implementation of recruitment and sampling as required in our originally planned study never impossible. No In view of the fluctuating pandemic situation and the lack of any concrete plan of the Government to relax the pandemic control strategy, no promise can thus be given by any of our collaborating centres for when the face-to-face recruitment field work of patient with respiratory symptoms may become permissible. On the other hand, the wide spread usage of facemask and large-scale social distancing has also resulted in a total absence of local influenza activity during the usual seasons epidemic period since February 2020, as reported officially by the Centre for Health Protection (Appendix 1: Flu Express, Centre for Health Protection, Figure 2), thus adding to the hurdle for any material progress of the study to be anticipated over the coming one or two years even if recruitment can be started in the near future. We decided not to apply for any further extension of the project period when the original project period was coming to an end, as the above risk assessment has made it impossible for the team to have any realistic planning for the way forward under all the logistical, manpower and financial limitation, which thus had made any consideration of further extension of our project period impractical. The recent arrival of the sixth wave and the current persisting access limitation to our planned recruitment site has further confirmed the difficult decision based on our ongoing situation assessment. With the termination of the study, we would like to return the total of the unspent balance of the funding (HK$877,176.13, constituting 76% of the original budget) to the RGC. As explained above, only 24% of the funding have spent (HK$274,131.87) on essential expenditure required by initial ground work and preparatory steps, including general expense required for the sourcing and purchase of clinical items (swabs & influenza rapid test), purchase of clinical trial insurances, application of required regulatory approvals e.g. clinical trial certificate from Drug Office DH, and the related staff cost to support these works, and the manufacturing, packaging and safety testing of our clinical trial medication. The medication production was done by Unicorn Laboratories Ltd., a local GMP pharmaceutical manufacturer which is experienced in producing clinical medication and its corresponding placebo for clinical trial. The production process involved the manufacturing of the active macrolide medications and placebo in identical outlook and packaged in identical blistered packs for achieving the proper blinding of participant and investigator. The manufactured products were tested for component and quality and with the issuance the documents of Certificate of Analysis, which were subsequently endorsed by Drug Office, DH as part of the application process of the clinical trial certificate and the trial insurance arrangement. The total cost of medication production was approximately HK$130,000 (constituting close to 45% of the total incurred expenditure). Although the project has been impacted by such an external situation totally unexpected and out of our control, we are still grateful and fascinated for this interesting project to be recognized and funded by the RGC, and would really hope to see its result in fruition. On behalf of the study team, we regret to have the termination of the study without achieving our original planning and we wish this completion report can be kindly approved by the RGC review board.

17127518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127518.value: Cardiovascular diseases, including heart failure, remain the top causes of death and disability among the senior citizens in Hong Kong. Type 2 diabetes, which has reached epidemic proportions globally, is an important risk factor for heart diseases by triggering metabolic disturbance, mitochondrial oxidative stress, defective energy production, cardiomyopathy and mechanical dysfunction of cardiomyocytes. Physical exercise has long been established as one of cheapest and most effective non-pharmacological interventions for prevention and treatment of diabetic heart diseases. However, the molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced cardiac protection remain poorly understood. Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21), a stress-responsive hormone with multiple salutary effects on obesity-related cardiometabolic complications, has recently been shown to possess potent cardio-protective activity in diabetic mice. We found that physical exercise-induced improvements in cardiac structure and function in type 2 diabetic mice are associated with a drastic induction of cardiac β-klotho (a co-receptor of FGF21 which determines the tissue selectivity of the hormone). On the other hand, the cardiac benefits of exercise in alleviation of diabetes-induced oxidative stress, defective mitochondrial complex activity and cardiac dysfunction are largely compromised in FGF21 knockout mice. Furthermore, we have identified the mitochondrial deacetylase SirT3 as a novel intracellular signaling effector of FGF21 in response to exercise. Therefore, we propose that the cardiac protection of physical exercise is mediated in part by enhancing myocardial FGF21 sensitivity through upregulation of β-klotho in cardiomyocytes, which in turn exerts induces mitochondrial SirT3, thereby leading to improved mitochondrial function and energy production, and reduced accumulation of toxic lipid intermediates in the hearts. This study aims to test this hypothesis using several tissue-selective knockout mouse models established in our laboratory, and to employ both hypothesis-driven and “omics-based” approaches to tease out the detailed intracellular signaling pathways of FGF21 which mediate the effects of exercise on improvement of mitochondrial function, ATP production, metabolic and structural remodeling, and contractile activity of cardiomyocytes. The results will not only help to rationalize and promote exercise as a preventive medicine for heart diseases, but also facilitate the development of “exercise mimetics” or biological interventions which can recapitulate the cardiovascular benefits of physical exercise. Furthermore, it will provide knowledge base for development of FGF21 agonists as a therapeutic agent for obesity-related cardiovascular complications.

17127518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127518.value: In this study, we have obtained a series of clinical, animal and cellular evidences for the obligatory role of FGF21 signaling in mediating the protective effects of exercise against diabetic heart disease, as summarized below: 1. In overweight/obese Chinese men with prediabetes, 12-week supervised exercise intervention lowers circulating FGF21 levels, which is correlated with improvements of cardiometabolic indexes. In high fat diet feeding and streptozotocin injection (HFD/STZ)-induced diabetic mice, long-term exercise significantly decreases circulating FGF21 level but selectively upregulates the expression of the FGF21 coreceptor β-Klotho in cardiomyocytes, remodeling the heart as an FGF21 sensitive target organ. 2. FGF21 knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice exhibit similar symptoms of diabetic cardiac dysfunction, as determined by echocardiographic assessments for ejection fraction, fractional shortening, stroke volume, and cardiac output. 6-week treadmill exercise significantly attenuates diabetes-induced cardiac dysfunction in WT mice, accompanied by reduced mitochondrial damage and increased activities of mitochondrial enzymes in hearts. However, such cardioprotective benefits of exercise are largely abrogated in mice with global or hepatocyte-selective ablation of FGF21, or cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of β-klotho. 3. Histological and biochemical analyses revealed that exercise alleviates diabetes-induced mitochondrial dysfunctions, including accumulation of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid droplets, as well as impairments in fatty acid oxidation and ATP production in the hearts of WT mice, whereas FGF21 KO mice are resistant to such beneficial effects of exercise on mitochondrial functions. Further biochemical screening demonstrated that exercise reverses diabetes-induced impairments of mitochondrial complex II&V, long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD), and superoxide dismutase-2 (SOD2) activities in WT mice, but not in FGF21 KO mice. 4. Mechanistically, we identified the mitochondrial deacetylase sirtuin-3 (Sirt3) as a novel FGF21 downstream effector to modulate deacetylation and activity of mitochondrial enzymes under exercise intervention. Exercise-induced sirtuin-3 (Sirt3) expression is severely compromised in the hearts of FGF21 KO mic, while restoration of cardiac Sirt3 reverses compromised cardioprotective benefits of exercise in mice lacking FGF21. 5. In vitro experiments demonstrated that FGF21 induces Sirt3 expression through activation of AMP-activated protein kinase and forkhead box O3a (AMPK-FOXO3a) pathways in H9C2 cardiomyocytes and in human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived cardiomyocytes. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays revealed that FOXO3a binds to the proximal Sirt3 gene promoter regions and enhances transcriptional activity of the Sirt3 promoter. Based on these findings, we have published three papers in top-ranked journals including Circulation and Annual Reviews in Pharmacology and Toxicology (see part C, section 8, items #1 and #2).

17127518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127518.value: This study uncovered FGF21 signaling axis as a novel molecular transducer mediating the protective effect of physical exercise against diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM). Our findings raise the possibility of (1) using FGF21 as a biomarker to evaluate the efficacy of exercise intervention for prevention and alleviation of diabetes and its complications; (2) development of long-acting FGF21 analogs or agonists as exercise mimetics for treatment of DCM. To this end, we have already developed a high sensitive FGF21 immunoassay for clinical validation in collaboration with several medical centers in mainland China to further evaluate its utility for assisting implementation of personalized exercise intervention for management of diabetes and its complications. We have also obtained further funding support from Croucher Foundation and Hong Kong ITC to develop lipidated long-acting FGF21 as a therapeutic agent for DCM. We are applying for patent protection for our inventions and will initiate preclinical studies in humanoid animals (such as monkey), which will set the foundation for commercialization and licensing of our products.

17127518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127518.value: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), characterized by cardiac hypertrophy, altered metabolic energetics diastolic and systolic dysfunction, is a major cause of heart failure. Exercise is an effective nonpharmacological strategy to alleviate DCM, but its clinical implementation was hindered by lack of understanding of molecular mechanism underlying exercise-mediated heart protection. In this study, we identified liver-secreted hormone FGF21 as exercise-responsive factor conferring such a beneficial effect of exercise. Exercise induces the expression of FGF21 co-receptor (named as beta-klotho) in heart cells, and thus rendering the hearts sensitive to FGF21 actions in protection against diabetes-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and damage. In wild-type mice, treadmill exercise significantly attenuates diabetes-induced cardiac dysfunction accompanied by reduced mitochondrial damage and increased activities of mitochondrial enzymes in hearts. However, such cardioprotective benefits of exercise are largely abrogated in mice with genetic ablation of FGF21 or cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of β-klotho In human-like heart cells, FGF21 can mimic exercise to prevent toxic lipids-induced cell damage through maintaining mitochondrial integrity. These findings uncover the FGF21 signaling axis as a novel molecular transducer mediating the protective effect of exercise against DCM, and provide scientific base for development of FGF21 analogues or sensitizers for treatment of this heart disease.

17127718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127718.value: Water/salt homeostasis is one of the three fundamental issues in biology, in addition to reproduction and growth/metabolism. Terrestrial animal including humans are always under risks of dehydration and salt deficiency. Consequently, sophisticated physiological and behavioral responses are evolved so as to ensure the constancy of milieu interieur. Water and salt contents in our bodies are meticulously maintained within narrow physiological range by neural and endocrine mechanisms via complementary ingestion and excretion adjustments of water and sodium. Among all mechanisms, it is well accepted that angiotensin II (ANGII) is the most important peptide responsible for the homeostatic control of water and salt in our body. Recently, there is an increasing body of evidence indicating SCT’s osmoregulatory action at multiple levels from kidney, adrenal, pituitary to the central nervous system. Our laboratory, in fact, is largely responsible for generating key findings showing the functions of SCT in this water/salt homeostatic axis. In the brain, we showed that SCT is the missing link that connects ANGII with its effects. Among the network of central osmoregulatory sites, subfornical organ (SFO) is the most upstream regulator with stimulatory and inhibitory efferent projections to other brain regions. Hence, SFO is the key control in our body to switch on and off water and salt appetite. We have previously shown that both SCT and ANGII are capable of stimulating SFO and water intake while the mechanism remains largely unknown. In this study, we aim to initially investigate SCT-specific actions in SFO by using mouse model with SCT or SCTR gene ablation in a SFO cell-specific manner. In addition, we will perform studies to look at changes in the gene expression profiles of excitatory and inhibitory neurons in SFO under osmotic and hormonal challenges. Finally, by electrophysiological recordings of individual SFO cells, we will study effects of SCT in neuronal excitability and pre-synaptic mechanisms. All these data will be analyzed and integrated to provide a comprehensive picture on the cellular and physiologic actions of SCT in the excitatory and inhibitory neuronal populations of SFO to stimulate water and salt appetite. As SFO is the most upstream site that acts as a on/off switch to osmoregulation, findings in the proposed studies are clearly important in providing information to understand one of the fundamental issues in survival: water/salt balance. 除了生殖和生長代謝外, 水/鹽穩態是生物學中的三個基本生存問題之一。由於包括人類在內的陸生動物總是面臨脫水和缺鹽的風險，這些動物因而進化出複雜的生理和行為反應以維持內環境穩定。透過神經、內分泌機制、水和鈉的補充和排泄, 我們體內的水和鹽被精心地調節和維持在一個狹窄的生理範圍內。在所有機制中，人們普遍認為血管緊張素II(Angiotensin II，ANGII)是最重要的肽, 主要負責體內的水/鹽平衡。最近，越來越多的證據証明胰泌素(Secretin，SCT)在腎，腎上腺，垂體及中樞神經系統的多個層面上發揮滲透壓調節作用。目前，本實驗室主要負責探究SCT在水/鹽穩態軸中的功能。在大腦中，我們發現SCT是連接ANGII及其下游作用的重要環節。在參與中央滲透壓調節的神經網路中，穹窿下器(Subfornical Organ，SFO)是最上游的調節位點，並向其他大腦區域發出興奮和抑制性投射。因此, SFO是負責控制水和鹽攝入行為的關鍵區域。儘管在具體機制上仍有很多未知，我們之前的研究已經證明SCT和ANGII 都能刺激SFO的神經元活性以及水的攝入。在本研究中，我們的目標是通過使用SFO 特異性SCT/SCTR基因敲除的小鼠模型來初步研究SCT對SFO的作用。此外，我們將研究在滲透壓和激素挑戰下,SFO內興奮性和抑制性神經元基因表達譜的變化。最後，通過電生理記錄，我們將研究SCT在SFO神經元興奮性和突觸前機制中的作用。我們將對所有資料進行分析和整合，以在細胞和生理層面上深入瞭解SCT如何透過SFO的興奮性和抑制性神經元群體影響對攝入水和鹽的需求。由於SFO作為滲透壓調節中最上游的位點，所以此擬議項目中的發現對於闡明其中一個基本生存問題—水/鹽平衡是非常重要的。

17127718.label: Realisation of objectives
17127718.value: All objectives have been achieved. The published paper in "The FASEB Journal" and "Current Biology" acknowledge the completion of these objectives. Objective 1 Using SCT and SCTR knockout mouse models, we found that the absence of either SCT or SCTR results in an abnormal water/salt appetite under dehydration, confirming the function of SCT signaling in body fluid homeostasis. For local ablation of the Sctr genes in the SFO, we injected an AAV1-GFP-Cre virus into the SFO of Sctr fl/fl mice. Then we found that specific deletion of SCTR in SFO resulted in a selective reduction of water intake, but not salt-water intake, in mice. Exogenous SCT administration elevated water intake in WT mice but not in SCTRSFO-/- mice, showing that the dipsogenic effect of SCT depends on the SCTR in SFO. Furthermore, specific deletion of SCTR in SFO did not alter salt intakes under Na-depleted conditions. In addition, we show that SCTR deletion in SFO also decreases Ang II-induced water intake, suggesting that the SCT plays an indispensable role in Ang II dipsogenic effects. Taken together, our results suggest that SCTR in the SFO is involved in thirst but not salt appetite (this part was published in Current Biology, see Part C). We delved into the in vitro heteromer formation between angiotensin II receptor type 1a subtype (AT1aR) and SCTR, and its involvement in water intake behavior. We modulate SCTR-AT1aR heteromeric function by I.C.V.-transmembrane peptides. We found that the SCTR-AT1aR heteromer mediates the stimulatory effects of SCT and ANGII in hypothalamic Vp expression and release through cFos/cAMP/CREB pathway. This study is the first to suggest that SCT and ANGII interact at the receptor level to mediate their dipsogenic effects. We also provide evidence for the involvement of cross-class GPCR heteromer in specific physiological functions (the SCTR-AT1aR study was published in The FASEB Journal, see Part C). Objective 2 Unfortunately, the import of Vglut2-Cre and Vgat-Cre mice strains was postponed due to the Covid-19. In order to minimized the impact of lacking mouse models and to distinguish SFOnNOS from SFOGABA neurons, we combined single-cell reverse transcription PCR (sc-rtPCR) with whole-cell patch clamp recording to identify specific SFO neuronal subtypes by examining the Nos1 and Gad1 gene expression in recorded cells. We collected four passive membrane parameters of SFOnNOS and SFOGAD neurons and found that SFOnNOS neurons have a larger membrane capacitance than SFOGAD67 neurons. We then analysed the gene expression of several presynaptic and postsynaptic markers in dehydrated SCTSFO-/- or SCTRSFO-/- mice. Consistent with electrophysiological results, we found that compared with sham-operated control mice, the vesicular glutamate transporter 1 (Vglut1) but not Vglut2 mRNA expression was significantly down-regulated in SCTSFO-/- and SCTRSFO-/- mice, while the vesicular GABA transporter (Vgat) mRNA expression was not significantly different. This data suggested that local ablation of the SCT/SCTR axis in the SFO may alter glutamate release mainly by downregulating the transcription level of Vglut1in presynaptic. On the other hand, the gene expression of excitatory postsynaptic related protein (postsynaptic density protein 95, PSD95) and inhibitory postsynaptic related protein (gephyrin) did not show differences among the sham-operated control, SCTSFO-/- and SCTRSFO-/- mice, implying that SCT/SCTR axis in the SFO may not participate in excitatory or inhibitory synaptic transmission through postsynaptic mechanisms. Taken together, we concluded that presynaptic SCTR regulates excitatory transmission in SFO by facilitating glutamate release and enhances the excitability of SFOnNOS neurons under dehydration. Objective 3 We next examined the effects of SCT on SFOnNOS neurons by conducting whole-cell patch clamp recording coupled with sc-rtPCR. Under current-clamp mode, bath-applied SCT (300 nM) increased the excitability of SFOnNOS neurons by eliciting reversible membrane depolarization, but no significant SCT effects were observed in the SFO of Sctr-/- mice. These results show that SCT depolarizes SFOnNOS neurons in an SCTR-dependent manner. Next, we analyzed SCT-elicited currents in voltage-clamp mode. Experiments were performed in the presence of glutamate receptor antagonists (CNQX and D-APV), which were used to block glutamatergic neurotransmission in direct and indirect circuits. Bath application of SCT (300 nM) induced a reversible inward current in SFOnNOS neurons of WT (-10.3 ± 1.6 pA) but not Sctr-/- mice (-1.3 ± 0.4 pA). On the other hand, no significant responses were observed in the SFOGAD67 neurons. These results show that the SCT can induce inward currents via SCTR to increase the intrinsic excitability of SFOnNOS neurons. We then examined the direct effects of SCT in MnPOnNOS neurons using whole-cell patch clamp, and biocytin-filled brain slices were collected for neuronal subtype identification. Under current-clamp mode, we found that bath-applied SCT (300 nM) elevated the excitability of MnPOnNOS neurons by eliciting reversible depolarizing effects. Our data confirmed that MnPOnNOS neurons respond to direct or indirect SCT signals. To further investigate the role of SCT signaling in the SFO→MnPO pathway, we adopted a two-virus system for projection-specific gene deletion using AAV1retro-EF1a-mCherry-IRES-Flpo (a retrograde AAV expressing yeast flippase, FLP) and AAV9-EF1a-fDIO-Cre, in which the expression of Cre is dependent on FLP-mediated recombination at the two Frt sequences. When these viral vectors were injected into Sctr fl/fl, the expressed Cre deleted the Sctr gene in SFO neurons that project to MnPO [here referred to as SCTR(SFO→MnPO)-/-)]. We then performed a one-bottle test for the dehydrated SCTR(SFO→MnPO)-/- and SHAM mice and found that the water consumption of SCTR(SFO→MnPO)-/- mice was significantly reduced compared to that of SHAM mice. These results suggest that SCTR in SFO neurons projecting to MnPO is necessary for regulating water intake under dehydration (this part was published in Current Biology, see Part C).

17127718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127718.value: This study resulted in two peer-review research articles, published in "The FASEB Journal" and "Current Biology", respectively (see Part C). Our research yielded the following findings: 1. We found that the SCTR-AT1aR heteromer mediates the stimulatory effects of SCT and ANGII in hypothalamic Vp expression and release through cFos/cAMP/CREB pathway. It is the first to suggest that SCT and ANGII interact at the receptor level to mediate their dipsogenic effects. We also provide evidence for the involvement of cross-class GPCR heteromer in specific physiological functions (the SCTR-AT1aR study was published in The FASEB Journal, see Part C). 2. We found that specific deletion of SCTR in SFO resulted in a selective reduction of water intake, but not salt-water intake, in mice. Exogenous SCT administration elevated water intake in WT mice but not in SCTRSFO-/- mice, showing that the dipsogenic effect of SCT depends on the SCTR in SFO. Our results suggest that SCTR in the SFO is involved in thirst but not salt appetite. 3. We showed that SCTR-expressing neurons in SFO were primarily excitatory neurons. 4. We showed that exogenous SCT administration elevated water intake in WT mice by activating SFOnNOS neurons in an SCTR-dependent manner. Electrophysiological experiments found that SCT increased the intrinsic excitability of SFOnNOS neurons through SCTR in a cell-autonomous mechanism. 5. Using the fiber photometry approach, we recorded the real-time calcium dynamics of SFOnNOS neurons in SCTRSFO-/- and SHAM mice under different internal conditions. We found that the lack of SCTR in the SFO blunts the activation of SFOnNOS neurons under both osmotic thirst and hypovolemic thirst. 6. We found that SFO-specific SCTR knockout reduced the expression level of cFos in MnPOnNOS neurons under WD conditions. Using projection-specific gene deletion methods, we showed that SCTR in SFO neurons projecting to MnPO is necessary for regulating water intake under dehydration (findings 2-6 were published in Current Biology, see Part C).

17127718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127718.value: To illustrate the central-peripheral role of secretin in modulating hydromineral homeostasis in response to different metabolic challenges. A novel perspective is that we suggest an intrinsic role for drinking water in reducing the risk of metabolic disease. Drinking water reduces plasma vasopressin levels, which is causally linked to obesity, heart disease and type-2 diabetes. The potential roles of hydration and salt reduction via SCT in the treatment of obesity and metabolic syndrome warrants further investigation. Analysis 1.1 To understand specific actions SCT signaling on water/salt intake of diet-induced obesity (DIO) mice, we will generate SFO-specific SCTR knockouts (SCTRSFO-/-) and NTS-specific SCTR knockouts (SCTRNTS-/-). DIO mice will be fed with high-fat diet for 8 weeks, followed by the monitor of daily water/salt intake. Analysis 1.2 To investigate the possibilities of SCT signaling-mediated hydration and salt reduction in the treatment of obesity and metabolic syndrome. We will activate or inhibit SFO and NTSSCTR+ neurons and observe the effects on hydromineral balance and obesity-related syndrome in DIO mice. The water/salt intake profile will be monitored. Long-term intervention experiments will be conducted to examine the ameliorating effects of hydration and salt reduction on obesity-related phenotypes.

17127718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127718.value: Animals instinctively find and consume water when feeling thirsty in order to restore body fluid osmolality and plasma volume to their set points. The feeling of thirst is strongly influenced by the subfornical organ (SFO), a forebrain structure that integrates circulating signals, such as osmotic pressure and sodium contents, to stimulate thirst. While Secretin (SCT), a classical gastrointestinal hormone, has been implicated as a humoral factor regulating body-fluid homeostasis. As known that the mundane behavior of drinking water is actually governed by the complex neural mechanisms of SCT in the central nervous system, but how the signalling is involved in this process was unclear. Our team adopted a specific gene deletion approach, demonstrating the neural mechanism for the first time, which reveals the important role of SCT Recepter (SCTR) in regulating drinking behaviour under thirst. This study not only expands the functional boundary of SCT, but also puts forward new insights into the regulation of the gut-brain axis in maintaining body fluid homeostasis, which provides new ideas for solving hydromineral imbalance symptoms (e.g., fatigue, headaches, arrhythmia, nausea, and vomiting etc.). Our findings have been published in the top journal The FASEB Journal and Current Biology.

17127918.value: 鼠傷寒沙門氏菌是最常見的引起人畜腸胃炎症的病原菌，全球范圍內每年導致約28億例腸道感染疾病。雖然多數沙門氏菌病（Salmonellosis）無需入院治療，但是隨著越來越多的沙門氏菌感染大爆發）的發生和抗生素耐藥菌的泛濫，對沙門氏菌的抗感染和預防仍然是公共衛生領域具有挑戰性的課題。我們亟需新的藥物靶點和新型的、區別於傳統抗生素的干預手段來應對這一挑戰。 鼠傷寒沙門氏菌是一種侵入性的胞內病原體，也是研究細菌病理學的模式細菌。近來的研究顯示該病原菌可以自身獨特的代謝能力作為一種新型毒力因子，在腸道炎症環境中以連四硫酸鹽作為末端電子受體進行厭氧呼吸，從而以顯著超越腸道菌群的速度繁殖和轉染。鼠傷寒沙門氏菌如何在腸道炎症的復雜環境中行使這一毒力因子的分子機制尚不清楚。 在前期研究中我們通過定量蛋白組學和分子生理學研究，首次發現兩個屬於催化二硫健形成酶家族的蛋白ScsB和ScsC在這個過程中發揮重要作用。本項目則擬通過系統研究ScsBC 蛋白的功能和在厭氧連四硫酸鹽呼吸脅迫反應中的作用，揭示利用生理代謝優勢作為毒力因子的分子機制。這些分子層面的研究不僅可以揭示新型二硫健形成酶ScsBC 的功能，而且還將揭示鼠傷寒沙門氏菌在病原-宿主相互作用中的脅迫反應機制，從而給藥物研發指明方向和靶點。

17128518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128518.value: 幹細胞具有不對稱細胞分裂（ACD）的能力，它們自我更新和同時分化，產生兩個不同命運的子細胞，一個保留為幹細胞，另一個成為具有特化功能的細胞。 用於研究ACD的現有實驗模型主要是體內發育模型。然而，這些模型幾乎無法控制幹細胞微環境，因此很難確定這些微環境因子在ACD中的作用。因此，具有可控微環境因子的基於單細胞的體外模型對於ACD研究是非常有價值的。 幹細胞微環境包括相鄰細胞，生長因子，細胞外基質，拓撲和機械信息。越來越多的證據證明了局部因素對影響幹細胞命運的重要性。幹細胞進行ACD需要不對稱信號，如微環境因子密度和位置。 能夠在體外重建幹細胞微環境的技術是ACD研究的重要平台。目前可用的微加工技術遠非理想，特別是在對多種類型的生態因子的定量和空間控制方面。 雙光子微加工是一種新興的光交聯技術，競爭優勢包括（1）納米級特徵的亞微米分辨率; （2）3D微加工的深度光學穿透; （3）對多種因素的獨立，定量和空間控制的可控性; （4）保持拓撲特徵，並使表面與整體性能分離; （5）優異的生物相容性。 我們的實驗室開發了一種多光子微加工平台，特別是用於細胞研究的蛋白質微結構和微觀模式。我們的平台能夠精確控制拓撲特徵，孔隙度，機械和基質特性，並應用於研究生物學問題，如機械剛度相關的細胞粘連。 尚未完成的研發挑戰包括：（1）微圖案可溶性因子和（2）具有定量和空間控制細胞之間相互作用; （3）為基於單幹細胞的ACD研究製作不對稱微環境因子。初步數據證明了實現這些關鍵能力的可行性，促使我們填補了該提案中ACD研究的技術空白。 該項目的即時重要性是開發基於單細胞的體外模型，以確定影響ACD的微環境因子。長期重要性是合理化組織工程的支架和生物反應器設計。

17128918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128918.value: Stem cells and technologies to program cellular states have the potential to transform clinical diagnostics and regenerative medicine. However, before clinical translation efficiency, quality, reproducibility and safety issues have to be addressed. The forcible expression of transcription factor cocktails is a powerful method to epigenetically reprogram cells leading to drastic conversions of cellular states in vitro and in vivo. We have developed a novel method designated directed evolution of reprogramming factors by cell selection and sequencing (DERBYseq). This method takes advantage of the finding that modifying endogenous reprogramming factors by the engineering of their molecular interfaces can switch and enhance their functions. We have benchmarked DERBYseq in pluripotency reprogramming and identified several artificially evolved synthetic transcription factors (eTFs) that outperform their wild-type counterparts in terms of reprogramming speed and efficiency. This work is a ‘first-of-a-kind’ and a ‘proof-of-concept’ and a critical step forward in applying directed evolution in the context of mammalian cells. In somatic cell reprogramming to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) with defined factors a proprietary eTF combination generates up to 100-time more iPSC colonies than wild-type cocktails with profoundly accelerated kinetics in a near deterministic manner. Moreover, the eTF combination allows the omission of potentially harmful oncogenes. However, the molecular basis for the improved activity of eTFs is unclear. We surmise that the improved function could rely on (1) changes to DNA recognition alone or with dimerization partners; (2) changes to the recruitment of co-activators; (3) changes to protein stability and DNA binding kinetics; (4) changes of the binding to nucleosomes. The goal of this proposal to test these hypotheses using a series of biochemical, biophysical and proteomic approaches. To this end we propose to (i) combine biochemical assays with next-generation sequencing (Spec-seq and Coop-seq) to identify and contrast DNA sequences bound by wild-type TFs and eTFs in vitro; (ii) study the thermal stability, folding kinetics and DNA binding kinetics; (iii) apply nucleosome binding assays to probe changes to their ‘pioneering activity’; (iv) perform proteomics to compare their interactomes; (v) perform pluripotency reprogramming experiments combined with epigenetic assays to test functional consequences of the altered molecular properties of eTFs. This project will elucidate fundamental aspects for the mechanism of TF mediated cell fate conversions. These insights will guide and accelerate follow up studies to further improve the design of artificially evolved TFs that will allow the production of functional cells for regenerative medicine. 幹細胞和細胞狀態重編程技術具有改變臨床診斷和再生醫學的潛力。然而，在實現臨床轉化前，重編程的效率、品質、可重複性和安全問題仍有待解決。外源表達轉錄因子可以實現在表觀遺傳上重編程細胞，介導體內和體外不同狀態下細胞狀態的大幅度轉化，是一種有力的細胞重編程手段。在先前的研究中，我們對內源重編程因子的功能位點進行改造，實現了其功能的轉換和增強。根據此發現，（DERBY-seq）。我們測試了DERBY-seq在多能性重編程過程中的作用，並發現幾種人工進化的轉錄因子（eTF）在重編程過程的速度和效率上都優於其野生型轉錄因子。在重編程體細胞產生誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）的實驗中，含有三種eTF的組合可以產生相較於野生型誘導因子組合約100倍的iPSC細胞克隆，並且能以一種幾乎決定性的方式加速此過程。此外，eTF組合可以使誘導過程無需添加潛在致癌基因。這些發現是史無前例的，也是實現將蛋白質定向進化技術應用於哺乳動物細胞的關鍵一步。然而，eTF增強誘導效率的分子機制尚不清楚。我們推測eTF功能的增強可能基於：（1）eTF單體或二聚體對DNA序列識別的變化；（二）共激活因子招募的變化；（3）蛋白穩定性和DNA結合動力學的變化；（4）與核小體結合的變化。此研究計畫的目標是通過一系列生物化學、生物物理學和蛋白質組學的方法來驗證以上這些假設。為此，我們計畫：（一）結合生化分析與下一代測序的方法（如Spec-seq和Coop-seq），在體外鑒定和對比野生型TF和eTF結合的DNA序列；（二）研究eTF的熱穩定性、折疊動力學和DNA結合動力學；（三）應用核小體結合分析方法檢測eTF“重編程先驅性能力”的改變；（四）應用蛋白組學的方法比較eTF的相互作用;（五） 進行多能性重編程實驗，並結合表觀遺傳分析方法檢驗eTF分子特性改變後的功能。本專案將闡明轉錄因子介導的細胞命運轉換機制。這些見解將指導並促進後續的研究，以進一步改進人工進化轉錄因子的設計，用以生產再生醫學研究所需的功能細胞。

For objective 1, we purified recombinant proteins of WT Oct4 and ePOU DNA binding domains (DBDs). To analyse the specificity for a large set of DNA sequences, we performed two complementary high-throughput assays. We first performed Specificity by sequencing (Spec-seq) for the quantitative profiling of the relative binding affinities octamer-like sequences in parallel through gel shift assays {Stormo, 2015 #106}. Using this, we obtained quantitative binding data of Oct4 and ePOU to 736 sequences. Both proteins retain similar binding specificities with a minutely altered preferences at position 4 and 5 of the octamer for ePOU. In collaboration with Prof Jian Yan at the City University of Hong Kong, we performed High-throughput SELEX (systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment {Jolma, 2015 #123}. We performed four cycles of HT-SELEX using a 40N library (40 randomised nucleotides) and purified Oct4 and ePOU DBDs. We recovered a similar set of top-scoring motifs from the sequence sets enriched by ePOU or Oct4, respectively, albeit with varied ranks. Together, this showed monomeric octamer binding is unchanged between Oct4 and ePOU. We, then, proceeded to perform dedicated gel shift assays motifs known to be dimerically bound by Oct4 and other POU family factor such as the MORE, NORE and PORE. Through this we found key differences between ePOU and Oct4 binding preference. ePOU preferentially binds all three palindromic motifs MORE, NORE and PORE with increased homodimer cooperativity. Of note, ePOU has a significantly higher homodimer cooperativity on a variant of MOREA4+1 variant of the MORE motif. We also performed binding assays to nucleosome core particles assembled in vitro but could not observe major differences between ePOU and Oct4. For objective 2, we have performed label free proteomics at day 7 of iPSC reprogramming with either Oct4 or ePOU to contrast the co-factor recruitment. We find that a majority of co-factors are similar between the two albeit some key pluripotency factors like EpCam, CDK5 and Kif11 was shown to be more enriched in ePOU. The Sox family key partner factor of the POU family to determine target gene selection and cell fate determination. Oct4 forms DNA-dependent heterodimers with Sox2 in pluripotent cells and with Sox17 in the extraembryonic endoderm {Jauch, 2011 #130; Aksoy, 2013 #135}. The dimerization in pluripotent cells is driven by a composite canonical SoxOct element. We performed gel shift assays with Sox factors-Sox2 and Sox17 with Oct4 and ePOU to investigate dimerization patterns. We found that patterns between Oct4 and ePOU were retained although with moderately elevated cooperativity constants for ePOU. In sum, core functions of the POU domain in pluripotency are largely preserved between ePOU and Oct4. For objective 3, we extensively performed RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and ATAC-seq at various day of iPSC reprogramming with Oct4 or ePOU. For RNA-seq, we analysed samples collected from reprogramming cells at days 0, 2, 3, 6, and 13 expressing ePOU or Oct4 with Sox2, Klf4 and c-Myc. We observed that the overall trajectory of global gene expression profiles was similar albeit faster for ePOU. Notable pluripotency related genes are upregulated include Lin28a, Mycn, Oxt2, Sall4, Tfcp2l1, and Utf1 for ePOU. To identify individual genes that are activated, we performed differential gene expression analysis and identified genes previously not implicated to play a role in pluripotency (Shisa3, Avil, Eya2, Fetub, Olfm1, Strip2, and Trh). Of note was the Trh gene, which encodes for the precursor of a secreted tripeptide that is a neurotransmitter in the hypothalamus, contributes to metabolic regulation. We further investigated Trh in overexpression and knockdown experiments. We find that overexpression improves reprogramming efficiency and knockdowns observed a 2–3-fold reduction in iPSC colony numbers. Next, we supplemented reprogramming media with the processed TRH peptide and found that reprogramming efficiency increases as well. Next, we profiled different reprogramming stages and transduction of different factor combinations using ATAC-seq. We find that less than 10% of the loci were differentially opened with most sites opening concurrently. Without Sox2 or Klf4, the chromatin state at day 3 of reprogramming was barely altered in comparison to MEFs for both Oct4 and ePOU. ChIP-seq revealed that ePOU not only bound the majority of Oct4 targeted loci, but also bound a sizable number of unique sites. 17128918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128918.value: Cellular reprogramming has the potential to revolutionize medicine through personalized disease models, ex vivo drug testing and regenerative therapies. Our group engineered the scaffold of Pit-Oct-Unc (POU) factor in the context of iPSC reprogramming and identified an enhanced POU factor (ePOU) that substantially outperforms wild-type Oct4 in terms of speed and efficiency. Here, we decode the basis of enhanced reprogramming activity ePOU. Biochemical assays combined with genome-wide analyses showed that ePOU possesses a new preference to dimerize on palindromic DNA elements. Yet, the core functions of Oct4 as pluripotency factor is unchanged for ePOU. The moderate capacity of Oct4 to function as a pioneer factor, its preference to bind octamer DNA and its capability to dimerize with Sox factors remain unchanged. ePOU: 1) differentially activates several genes previously not implicated in reprogramming, 2) reveals an unappreciated role of thyrotropin-releasing hormone signalling, and 3) binds an variant of the MORE motif MOREA4+1. Collectively, these features enable ePOU to accelerate the establishment of the pluripotency network.

17128918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128918.value: The characterization of ePOU presented here hold several lessons for protein and stem cell engineering, as well as the mechanism of biomolecule driven reprogramming. The results described here provides a basis for engineering of transcription factors towards other cell fate conversion strategies like lineage reprogramming or forward programming of stem and progenitor cells. In a follow up project we will explore whether the ePOU could support the reprogramming of human cells towards different stem cell types (i.e. stem cells with totipotency features and tissue specific stem cells of the brain). In addition, in collaboration with a group from Australia we will evaluate whether the ePOU can generate iPSC from endangered species which or otherwise difficult to reprogram.

17128918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128918.value: Cellular reprogramming has the potential to revolutionize medicine through personalized disease models, ex vivo drug testing and regenerative therapies. To ensure the safe and effective implementation of this technology from the bench to bedside therapies, we must understand the underlying mechanisms that drive it. Here, we decode the mechanisms that enable an enhanced POU factor (ePOU) to substantially outperforms wild-type Oct4 in terms of speed and efficiency in pluripotency reprogramming. We find that ePOU even with a 17 amino acid difference from WT Oct4 follow similar core patterns and relatively subtle changes drive the enhanced activity. We reveal access to a subset of additional sites and an unappreciated role of thyrotropin-releasing hormone signalling underly the enhanced performance of ePOU. Collectively, lessons learned here inform the next generation of artificially evolved biomolecules that will advance cell fate conversions towards translational applications.

17129118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129118.value: The Sox10 gene is required for mammalian enteric nervous system development. Sox10 mutation will lead to colonic aganglionosis which is characterized by the absence of ganglia in the distal region of the gut. We have generated a Sox10-NGFP mutant in which the N-terminal of Sox10 is fused to the EGFP reporter. Our phenotype analysis shows that the Sox10 mutant enteric neural crest cells have impaired cell adhesion and abnormal interaction with the extracellular matrix components. By transcriptome analysis using RNA-Seq data obtained from Sox10-NGFP mutant neural crest cells, we have observed that genes involved in cell-cell interaction and for the Eph receptor tyrosine kinases and their ephrin ligands are dysregulated, suggesting that Sox10 could function as a regulator of cell migration processes through direct and indirect network of gene regulations. We hypothesize that Sox10 may may cooperate with Ephs and ephrins to regulate cell-cell communications, thereby affecting the enteric neural crest cell-cell interaction and migration processes in the developing gut. The aim of this project is to decipher the roles of Sox10 and Ephs/ephrins in controlling the cell adhesive capacities of the enteric neural crest cells during their course of migration and colonization of the developing mouse gut. Specifically, (1) we will perform imaging analysis of Sox10 mutant neural crest and study the cellular behaviour using Sox10-NGFP:Lifeact-mRFP double mutant mouse line; (2) we will investigate the expression of Ephs and ephrins in the developing enteric nervous system, and examine their roles in enteric neural crest cell-cell interaction; (3) by genetic mutant analyses we will decipher the pathways of Sox10 and Ephs/Efns gene regulation, and identify the cascade of gene interactions for controlling enteric neural crest cell migration. As the contribution of Eph-ephrin signaling in the developing enteric nervous system is not known, to the best of our knowledge this is the first study of their functions in the enteric neural crest. In this study, we will investigate how Sox10 orchestrates multiple gene expression changes that lead to delayed enteric neural crest cell migration. As the regulation of cell-cell signaling are important for cell migration as well as cell proliferation and differentiation, the results obtained from this study will have a broad implication on our understanding of the functions of Sox10 in the neural crest.

17129118.label: Realisation of objectives
17129118.value: Objective 1. To investigate the roles of Sox10 in enteric neural crest cell adhesion, cell-matrix interaction and directional migration To investigate how Sox10 may control enteric neural crest cell (ENCC) adhesion and migration, we examined interaction of Sox10 mutant ENCCs on different extracellular matrix molecules. We found that in gut explant culture, Sox10NGFP/+ mutant ENCCs formed compact cell aggregates, indicating increased cell adhesion. We characterized the cellular behaviour by time-lapse imaging using Sox10NGFP/+ and Wnt1-Cre;Z/EG explants. Analysis and tracking of the movement of individual cell from multiple explants showed that mutant cells consistently displayed a reduction of persistence. To investigate the abnormal cellular behavior in vivo, time-lapse video microscopy was performed using Wnt1-Cre;Z/EG and Sox10NGFP/+ guts. The migration speed, persistence and directionality of the leading cells were recorded and analyzed. We showed that the migration speed and the persistence of the leading cells in mutant guts were significantly reduced. The leading cells in the control migrated towards the caudal end of the gut, whereas the cell migration directionality was erratic in mutant guts. To address how Sox10 affects ENCCs adhesion at the cellular level, the formation of focal adhesion and adherens junction were analyzed. We cultured neurospheres derived from E12.5 ENCCs and used vinculin immunostaining to visualize the focal adhesion complexes. Elongated focal adhesions with increased number and size were observed in Sox10NGFP/+ ENCCs. To investigate the cell adhesion properties of ENCCs, pan-cadherin and β-catenin antibodies were used in immunostaining. In the Sox10 mutant ENCCs, thickened, larger and more condensed adherens junctions could be observed. These results suggest that Sox10 mutation could alter the formation of adhesive complexes and affect ENCC cell adhesion. In this study, we have investigated the roles of Sox10 in enteric neural crest cell adhesion, cell-matrix interaction and directional migration using in vitro and in vivo platforms. Our findings are consistent with other published findings (Huang et al 2022). We have achieved Objective 1 completely. Objective 2. To investigate the roles of Ephs and ephrins in enteric neural crest cell-cell communication and cell migration To understand the expression and functions of Ephs and ephrins in the developing gut, we made use of single cell transcriptome data available in public databases. We have examined the transcription profiles of Ephs and ephrins in developing human, mouse and zebrafish guts (Elmentaite et al., 2020; Kastriti et al., 2022; Howard IV et al., 2021). We constructed specific expression signatures of Ephs and ephrins across various cell types of the developing guts. The cell type-specific expression patterns of Ephs and ephrins among the progenitors, neuroblasts, neuronal cells and glial precursors; as well as their co-expression with Ret, Sox10 and p75 were characterized. To complement the transcription profiles observed in the scRNA transcriptomes, we have examined the in vivo expression profiles of Ephs and ephrins in embryo sections. We found that ephrinA1 was expressed in both ENCCs and mesenchymal cells as early as E10.5. EphrinA5 and ephrinB2 were found in the neuronal cells from E12.5-E16.5. For the receptors, EphB2 was expressed in ENCCs and mesenchyme, EphA5 was expressed only in enteric neurons at late stages. To investigate the requirement of Eph-ephrin signaling and potential cross-talks with Ret and p75, we generated a series of expression and reporter constructs as well as ephrinA1-H135Q and EphB2-S421L mutant expression vectors for cell function analysis. By Co-IP and antibody pull-down assays, we clearly demonstrated that ephrin-A1 could form protein complexes with Ret and p75. Interestingly, we found that both wildtype and mutant ephrinA1 could form protein complexes with p75 and Ret. However, interaction with ephrinA1-H135Q mutant led to aberrant phosphorylation of p75 and Ret and affect their downstream signaling activities. To test the requirement of Eph-ephrin signaling in cellular interaction, cell segregation assay was developed to investigate cell attraction or repulsion behavior. Cell lines stably transfected with wildtype and mutant ephrinA1, EphA4, ephrinB2 and EphB2 with GFP or tdTomato reporter were generated. Ephrin-A1/EphA4, and ephrin-B2/EphB2 cell lines were co-cultured for 48 hours, the cell segregation patterns were captured by fluorescent microscopy. We found that both wildtype ephrinA1/EphA4 and ephrinB2/EphB2 co-cultures displayed as regular patterns of small cell clusters. However, when ephrinA1 or EphB2 were mutated, the cell clusters became interconnected and larger clusters were formed. Our results suggest that ephrinA1-H134Q and EphB2-S421L mutant signaling might lead to weakened repulsive cell-cell interaction, allowing the mutant cells to form larger clusters. Taken together, our results clearly indicate interactions between p75 and Ret with Eph-ephrin signaling and affect cell-cell interactions. We have achieved Objective 2 completely. Objective 3. To elucidate the hierarchy of Sox10 and Ephs/Efns gene regulatory network for controlling enteric neural crest cell-cell interaction and cell migration To investigate the gene regulatory relationship between Sox10 and Eph/ephrin genes, we performed RNA-Seq transcriptome analysis using ENCCs isolated from E12.5 Wnt1-Cre;Z/EG and Sox10NGFP/+ guts. Characterization of differentially expressed genes showed that among the most significant changes were those involved in cell adhesion and cell migration. We also analyzed single cell RNA-seq dataset of E12.5–13.0 Sox10Cre; Rosa26tdTomato ENCCs and found that the transcriptome profiles of ENCCs were mostly similar with our RNA-seq data. To validate the differential expression of EphA4 and EphB2, which were significantly changed in Sox10NGFP/+ ENCCs, we performed qRT-PCR using sorted ENCCs as well as immunofluorescence analyses of mouse gut samples. Although qRT-PCR experiments using sorted ENCCs confirmed their differential expression in the mutant cells, we did not observe significant difference in expression between wildtype and Sox10NGFP/+ E12.5 gut sections. We explored the functions of Ephs and ephrins in mediating ENCCs cell migration by binding assay using Fc protein in gut explant culture. However, we could not observe significant difference between wildtype and Sox10NGFP/+ gut explants. Our functional experiments indicate that Sox10 probably regulates Ephs and ephrins indirectly through cross-talks with Ret and p75, or other cell-cell interaction mechanisms. On the other hand, our analysis of Sox10NGFP/+ RNA-Seq and other publicly available human and mouse single cell transcriptome datasets have allowed us to isolate Sox10-positive ENCCs and their derivatives in lineage reconstruction experiments, and to examine the Sox10 regulon to identify downstream targets. To this end, we discovered that Notch signaling factor genes were significantly changed in Sox10 mutant ENCCs, and DLL3 was among the top differentially expressed genes. To validate the transcriptome data in vivo, we examined the expression of Notch signaling factors in wildtype and Sox10NGFP/+ mutant ENCCs. Our qRT-PCR analysis using EGFP-sorted Sox10+ ENCCs confirmed that Notch signaling genes were largely affected in Sox10NGFP/+ mutant ENCCs. Dll3 and Jag2 were downregulated, while Dll1 and Jag1 were upregulated in Sox10 mutant cells. As the expression levels of Jag1 and Jag2 were very low in ENCCs, Dll3 was the most likely functional ligand in the developing gut. We examined the expression of Dll3 in wildtype E12.5 and E14.5 guts and found that Dll3 was indeed expressed in the ENCCS, overlapping with the expression of Phox2b. In Sox10NGFP/+ mutant, Dll3 expression was similar to that of Phox2b and absent in the distal hindgut. Furthermore, Dll3 expression was completely abolished in E12.5 Sox10NGFP/NGFP homozygous mutant gut. Our results demonstrate that Dll3 is a novel Notch signaling ligand in the developing ENS, and Dll3 could be a downstream target of Sox10. We have achieved Objective 3 completely.

17129118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17129118.value: Analysis of the Sox10NGFP mutant generated in our laboratory showed that Sox10 mutant enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs) have impaired cell-cell interactions and contribute to abnormal cell migration processes. By transcriptome analysis using RNA-Seq data obtained from Sox10NGFP mutant neural crest cells, we found that genes involved in cell-cell interaction, Eph receptors and their ephrin ligands, as well as Notch signaling factors were dysregulated, suggesting that Sox10 could function as a regulator of cell migration processes through direct and indirect network of gene regulations. In this project, we have made the following discoveries: 1. Mutations of EFNA1 and EPHB2 have been identified in Hirschprung disease patients, but the role of Eph/ephrin signaling in ENS development is unknown. By single cell transcriptome analysis, we provided the cell type specific expression signature of Ephs and ephrins during human and mouse ENS development. We characterized the spatiotemporal distribution of Ephs and ephrins in developing mouse gut. We showed that abnormal ephrinA1-H134Q/EphA4 and EphB2-S421L/ephrinB2 signaling interactions reduced cell-cell repulsion in cell segregation assays. Importantly, we demonstrated that ephrinA1 could physically interact with two ENCC receptors, Ret and p75. Interaction with mutant ephrinA1 led to phosphorylation of Ret and aberrant activation of Ret-mediated MAPK signaling. Our study uncovered a novel mechanism regulating ENCC interaction and the Ret-mediated ephrinA1 reverse signaling in ENCCs. (This part of the findings are summarized in the manuscript by Lui et al.) 2. By transcriptome and Gene Regulatory Network analysis, we discovered that Notch signaling is downstream or cooperative with Sox10 function in the ENCCs. Analysis of lineage-specific expression profiles of the Notch signaling factors showed that SOX10 and NOTCH1 were highly expressed in ENCCs and downregulated in differentiating neurons, consistent with their roles in maintenance of progenitors. DLL3, a Notch-inhibiting ligand, and ASCL1 were highly expressed in the neural progenitors, suggesting that DLL3 could be required during neurogenic differentiation. We showed that Dll3 is specifically expressed in Sox10-positive ENCCs in developing gut, and is downregulated in Sox10 mutant. We identified multiple putative SOX10 binding sites at the DLL3 promoter regulatory region, suggesting that SOX10 could directly regulate DLL3 expression. The interactions between Sox10 and Notch signaling is likely to contribute to the maintenance of progenitors and their differentiation. Our results suggest that Dll3 is the ligand that mediates the Notch1-Sox10-Ascl1 regulatory axis in the developing ENS. (This part of the findings are summarized in the manuscript by Li et al.)

17129118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17129118.value: 1. Our study has revealed the extensive expression and requirement of Ephs and ephrins in enteric neural crest cell interaction. Our findings have provided the basis for further studies along the following lines: 1) the forward and reverse signaling mechanisms of Ephs/ephrins in the differentiation of ENCCs and in formation of functional enteric ganglia during ENS development; 2) our results on protein interactions between ephrinA1 and Ret receptor suggest cross-talks between Eph/ephrin and GDNF/Ret signaling in the ENCCs. The complex molecular signaling and pathogenic mechanisms underlying the defective ENCC colonization of the distal colon will require further investigations. 2. Our discovery of the Notch1-Sox10-Ascl1-Dll3 regulatory axis in ENCC progenitor maintenance and neuronal differentiation will allow further studies on Notch1-Dll3 signaling functions in ENS development. As modulation of Notch signaling level has significant implications on disease and developmental processes, characterization of Notch1-Dll3 functions will not only provide further understanding of pathogenic mechanism, but also potential therapeutic strategies. We will apply for research grant supports to continue the various directions of study. The new research opportunities will also allow us to continue our collaborations with Profs. Urban Lendahl and Woody Chan on Notch signaling mechansims and ENS development.

17129118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17129118.value: Sox10 mutations lead to colonic aganglionosis which is characterized by the absence of ganglia in the distal gut. We showed that Sox10NGFP mutant enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs) have impaired cell-cell interactions. Based on our analysis using RNA-Seq data obtained from Sox10NGFP ENCCs as well as single cell transcriptome datasets in the public domain, we investigated the expression profiles of Ephs receptors/ephrin ligands and Notch signaling factors. By co-culture assays, we showed that Eph/ephrin interaction was required in cell-cell communications. Furthermore, ephrinA1 could form protein complex with Ret and affect Ret-mediated signaling. As the contribution of Eph-ephrin signaling in the enteric nervous system (ENS) is not known, this is the first study of their functions in the enteric neural crest. In this study, we also identified that Dll3, a Notch signaling ligand with unknown function in the ENS, was specifically expressed in Sox10-positive ENCCs. Expression of Dll3 was downregulated in Sox10 mutant. The interactions between Sox10 and Notch/Dll3 signaling is likely to be required for the maintenance of ENCC progenitors and their differentiation. Our results suggest that Sox10 could function as a regulator of cell migration processes through direct regulation of Notch1-Dll3-Ascl1 axis and indirect network of Eph/ephrin regulations.
