17129218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17129218.value: DNA damage occurs frequently in human cells due to constant challenges from both environmental insults and endogenous toxins. Failure to properly respond to DNA damage can lead to genome instability that has been regardsed as a hallmark of human cancers. To combat DNA damage, cells evolve multiple DNA repair and checkpoints pathways to accurately and efficiently repair the damaged DNA. Human protein Timeless has been extensively charaterized as a critical replisome component. Timeless and Tipin (Timeless interacting protein) heterodimer was shown to physically interact with other components of replisome such as RPA, MCM complex, DNA polymerases and Claspin to maintain replisome integrity and activate the replication checkpoint in response to genotoxic stress. Timeless-deficient cells exhibit defects in both the intra-S-phase and G2/M checkpoints and elevated levels of phosphorylated γ-H2AX foci formation that is normally regarded as a marker of DNA double-strand breaks. Timeless can also function independent of Tipin. Recently we had an unexpected finding that Timeless interacts with DNA damage sensor protein PARP1 to promote DNA double-strand break repiar. In this project we will continue to investigate how exactly PARP1, Timeless and Tipin dynamically interact to ochestrate a proper response to damaged DNA, especially at stalled replication forks. In line with our recent observation that PARP1 dependent recruitment of Timeless but not Tipin to laser-induced DNA DSB sites, our preliminary data suggest that Tipin and PARP1 cann’t bind to Timeless simultaneously to form a ternary complex although Timeless does form a stable binary complex with Tipin or PARP1 respectively. We will expand upon our our previous studies by proposing the following specific aims: (i) To provide a mechanistic understanding of mutual exclusivity of the Timeless/Tipin and Timeless/PARP1 complexes. (ii) To decipher structure and function of Timeless DUF1 domain. Our study should provide important and novel insights into the regulatory mechanisms of Timeless complexes in maintenance of genome stability and tumor suppression. Considering PARP1 is a promising therapeutic target, and Timeless overexpression has been observed in various cancers, our research should lay a solid foundation for developing potential inhibitors to block Timeless and PARP1 interactions, the potential inhibitor can be used together with PARP inhibitor to achieve higher efficacy against BRCA-deficient cancers. 由於來自外源環境和內源毒素的持續挑戰，DNA損傷在正常細胞中經常發生。未能正確應對DNA損傷可導致基因組不穩定，這已被視為癌症的標誌之一。為了對抗DNA損傷，細胞進化出多個DNA修復和細胞週期檢查點通路，以準確有效地修復受損DNA。人類蛋白質Timeless已經被廣泛地描述為關鍵的複制組件。 Timeless和Tipin形成的異源二聚體同replisome的其他組分如RPA，MCM複合物，DNA聚合酶和Claspin有直接的相互作用來維持replisome的完整性，並參與激活複製叉檢查點以響應遺傳毒性應激。Timeless缺失細胞在S期內和G2 / M檢查點都表現出缺陷，並且磷酸化的γ-H2AX水平明顯升高，這通常被認為是DNA雙鏈斷裂的標誌。 另外，Timeless也有獨立於Tipin的功能。不久前我們意外地發現Timeless與DNA損傷傳感器蛋白PARP1相互作用從而促進DNA雙鏈斷裂修復。在這個項目中，我們將繼續研究PARP1，Timeless和Tipin如何動態相互調節以應對DNA損傷, 特別是對停滯的複制叉進行適當的響應。最近我們利用活细胞成像觀察到Timeless而非Tipin依賴於PARP1招募到激光誘導的DNA 雙鏈斷裂位點。与此一致的是，我們发现儘管Timeless能夠分別與Tipin或PARP1形成異源二聚體，但Tipin和PARP1不能同時與Timeless結合形成三元復合物。在這個項目中，我們將提出以下具體目標來擴展我們之前的研究：（i）為Timeless / Tipin和Timeless / PARP1複合物的互斥性提供機理解釋。 （ii）解析Timeless DUF1模塊的結構和功能。我們的研究應該為Timeless複合物在維持基因組穩定性和腫瘤抑制方面的調控機制提供重要並且新穎的見解。考慮到PARP1是一種有潛力的癌症治療靶點，並且在多種癌症中觀察到有過表達，我們的研究應該為開發可阻斷Timeless和PARP1相互作用的潛在抑製劑奠定堅實的基礎。我們認為潛在的抑製劑可以與PARP抑製劑聯合使用以獲得更高的療效對抗BRCA缺陷的癌症。

17129218.label: Realisation of objectives
17129218.value: Human Timeless and Tipin (Timeless interacting protein) heterodimeric complex protein has been extensively characterized as critical replisome components that physically interact with other components of replisome such as MCM complex, RPA, DNA polymerases and Claspin to maintain replisome integrity and activate the replication checkpoint in response to genotoxic stress. Timeless-deficient cells exhibit defects in both the intra-S-phase and G2/M checkpoints and elevated levels of phosphorylated gymma-H2AX foci formation that is normally regarded as a marker of DNA double-strand breaks. My group has first demonstrated that human Timeless interacts with DNA damage sensor protein PARP1 to promote DNA double-strand break repair. Intriguingly, our preliminary data suggest that Tipin and PARP1 can’t bind to Timeless simultaneously to form a ternary complex although Tipin and PARP1 bind to different regions of Timeless, and Timeless does form a stable binary complex with Tipin or PARP1 respectively. We aimed to provide structural insights into mutual exclusivity of the Timeless/Tipin and Timeless/PARP1 complexes. Therefore, we aimed to determine the structure of Timeless/Tipin complex. To complete this research objective, we have established a co-expression & purification strategy to obtain large amounts of Timeless/Tipin heterodimeric complex proteins. We successfully crystalized Tim_S(aa:1-810)/Tipin_HD (aa: 66-176) complex and determined the crystal structure recently (Figure 1). Tim-S adapts alpha-solenoid conformation with nine heat repeats. Tipin_HD forms a five-helical bundle and has a direct interaction with the 9th heat repeat of Tim_S through both hydrophobic interactions and electrostatic interactions. The crystal structure provided the detailed molecular foundation for Timeless and Tipin complex formation, but it can’t explain why Timeless/Tipin and Timeless/PARP1 complex are mutually exclusive. We have put lots of efforts into optimizing crystals of Tim_NP(aa:1-1098)/Tipin_HD(aa: 66-176) complex but the diffraction of crystals is poor. We attempted to apply cryo-EM for structural analysis of Tim_NP/Tipin_HD complex structure. We are currently facing the challenge to obtain high-resolution cryo-EM map, probably due to the following reasons: (1) the relative small size of Tim_NP/Tipin_HD complex; (2) the large portion of Tim_NP/Tipin complex seems degraded during the sample freezing process. We are still putting efforts to solve these issues. Hopefully we will make significant progress given that our Faculty has just established Cryo-EM facility and we can systematically screen a variety of freezing conditions. We have also successfully determined the crystal structure of Timeless DUF1 domain spanning from residue 540 to 665 (Figure 2). This DUF1 domain is newly evolved and not found in yeast orthologs. It contains four alpha-helices in which alpha1 and alpha4, alpha2 and alpha3 form two antiparallel helices respectively. This domain is invisible in recently determined cryo-EM structure of human replisome, likely it lacks molecular interactions with other neighbouring domains. We previously applied tandem affinity purification (TAP) with mass spectrometry to identify the potential interacting protein partners of this novel domain. Afterwards we performed co-immunoprecipitation to validate a number of potential partners. So far, our data suggested that DBF4 is likely a binding protein of Timeless DUF1 domain. DBF4-dependent CDC7 kinase (DDK) is critical to initiate replisomome assembly by phosphorylating MCM complex. DDK is also involved in replication checkpoint signalling under conditions of replication stress. To explore how DDK and Timeless orchestrates S-phase checkpoint signalling, we are currently collaborating with Dr Thomas Helleday’s group to systematically carry out structural and functional analysis.

17200218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200218.value: Symmetry is fundamental in nature, science, engineering, and art. Perception and recognition of symmetries influence not only our understanding of the world but also our design processes. Symmetry is also ubiquitous and continuous in architecture, appearing in all places over the world and at all times throughout history, for example, the Great Wall of China, the Parthenon of Greece, the Taj Mahal of India, ‘The Gherkin’ in London, and the Sydney Opera House in Australia. The ubiquity of symmetry in architecture is far from accidental, rather it is the result of considerations relating to function, economics, mechanics, manufacturing, and aesthetics. Recent advances in sensing technology, such as laser scanning and photogrammetry, provide increasingly available 3D point clouds of architectures and cities. Detection of architectural symmetries from 3D point clouds is not only an intriguing inquiry in its own right, but also an effective and essential step in creating accurate and informative digital building/city models for various applications such as architectural design, computer vision, construction management, heritage conservation, and smart and resilient city development. However, as it is too time-consuming, tedious, and costly to manually recognize and segment architectural symmetries from 3D point clouds, the challenge is to devise an automated detection of architectural symmetries. To meet this challenge, the proposed research project aims to apply modern derivative-free optimization (DFO) algorithms, which have been successfully used to solve many science and engineering problems, to automated architectural symmetry detection from 3D point clouds. Extending the mathematical definition of symmetry, this research proposes a general formulation of detecting symmetry in architecture. The major innovation here is an elegant means of detecting all types of architectural symmetries, including reflection, translation, rotation, uniform scaling, or combinations thereof, as a unified nonlinear optimization problem which is solvable by modern DFO methods. Our recent pilot study, involving a dense cloud of over one million points from a neoclassical building, has confirmed the technological feasibility of this proposed DFO approach. The project offers both academic insights and practical benefits. The findings will extend knowledge of how modern mathematical methods can be used to discover symmetry in architecture or related areas. The outcomes may lead to a breakthrough in theoretical explanation of the challenges in architectural symmetry detection. Practically, the research will offer a useful methodological tool for the creation of accurate and informative building/city models from inexpensive point clouds for industries related to architecture, construction, engineering, automobiles, and robotics. 對稱性普遍存在於世界各地各時期的建築中，例如長城、帕特農神廟、泰姬陵、倫敦“小黃瓜”及悉尼歌劇院。無處不在的對稱性并非意外使然，而是綜合功能性、經濟性、結構、可生產性及美觀性的全面考量的結果。目前，測量建築物及城市的三維點雲已變得日益準確、全面及廉價。三維點雲中的對稱性識別不僅是一種知識獲取，更是創建智慧城市所必須的建築和城市信息模型的必要步驟。然而，人工識別費時費力且成本高昂；因此，需要研究自動化對稱性識別技術。 本項目將運用最新的無導數優化（DFO）算法，自動化三維點雲中的建築對稱性識別過程。在本項目中，不論是鏡像、平移、旋轉、等比縮放或是它們的各種組合，都會被統一地形式化為一類非綫性優化問題。進而采用無導數優化算法來求解此類問題。本項目兼具學術及實踐意義。預期結果料將拓展運用當代數學方法發現建築及相關領域的對稱性的研究，亦可識別建築對稱性識別的理論難點。在實踐影響力方面，本研究將為建築和城市信息模型提供一套有效的方法論工具。

17200218.value: 5.1 Scope of investigation -- The 3D point cloud is a popular means of measuring the 3D geometry of a city. Yet, it is challenging to detect the architectural symmetries within millions or billions of points for understanding the data and creating meaningful city models. -- This project presents a novel optimization-based method to automate architectural symmetry detection in urban point clouds. -- We apply the modern DFO (derivative-free optimization) algorithms in Applied Mathematics to realize a fully automatic point cloud processing. -- Furthermore, we looked into the Gestalt design laws for systematic symmetries and integration of semantics and BIM for urban facilities. 5.2 Objectives achieved -- Objective 1 achieved. The formulation of automatic symmetry detection in point clouds was first presented as ODAS (Optimization-based Detection of Architectural Symmetries) in journal paper [1] (as listed in Sect. 8, Section C) and furthered in [2] and [3]. The paper [1] won HKU Research Output Prize 2018/19. -- Objective 2 achieved. In journal paper [1], the experimental results showed that our ODAS method was 1,000 times faster – while with less error – than conventional voting methods. The ODAS was also 10 times faster and more accurate than the preliminary work in our 2019 conference paper [1]. -- Objective 3 achieved. The ODAS is open-sourced for worldwide researchers; freely available at: https://github.com/ffxue/odas. We further investigated the Gestalt law-based systematic symmetries, presented in a journal paper [3]. 17200418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200418.value: This project will explore the theoretical foundations and applications of private data structures and algorithms, whose goal is to prevent the leakage of sensitive information through the data access pattern, which cannot be obscured by just using encryption. We will extend existing private storage models to capture practical aspects such as concurrency and I/O (input/output)-efficiency. Since the design of modern architectures ubiquitously employs parallelism and memory hierarchy, our models will have impacts on real-world applications such as multi-core processors and outsourced cloud platforms. Moreover, we will develop more relaxed security notions to achieve tradeoffs between performance and privacy levels. The classical oblivious RAM (ORAM) proposed by Goldreich and Ostrovsky allows data to be accessed obliviously such that the access pattern does not leak any information other than the length of the operation sequence. Even though the performance of ORAM has been improved in the past decade, the model does not readily support parallel architectures. To rectify the situation, the oblivious parallel RAM (OPRAM) has been proposed in a recent TCC 2016 paper. In our preliminary results that will appear in the upcoming TCC 2017 and ASIACRYPT 2017, we have achieved OPRAMs whose performance matches the state-of-the-art ORAMs. Our preliminary results inspire us to go beyond OPRAMs and further investigate private concurrent data structures supporting multiple requests and their parallel implementations. Besides parallelism, memory hierarchy plays a major role in practice. Our preliminary results on I/O-efficient cache-agnostic oblivious sorting algorithms, which will appear in the upcoming SODA 2018, equip us with powerful techniques to further explore the I/O-efficiency of our private mechanisms. Furthermore, we will also explore new notions of privacy in storage schemes that allow users to balance between their privacy preference and performance guarantee. Specifically, our recently developed techniques enable us to tackle the following challenging areas: (1) Explore concurrency and parallelism in private data structures and algorithms. We will design some basic oblivious parallel algorithms as fundamental building blocks for storage schemes, and study the tradeoff between depth and total work. (2) Achieve I/O-efficiency for private mechanisms. For instance, we will consider cache-agnostic subroutines in our private schemes that can achieve optimal I/O-efficiency without explicitly knowing the parameters of the underlying architecture. (3) Study more general notions of security in storage schemes. Going beyond conventional ORAMs, we will consider differential privacy as a more relaxed security requirement to allow better performance in practice. 此項目將探索隱私數據結構與算法的理論基礎與應用，旨在通過數據存取模式防止敏感信息的洩露，該目標不能僅通過加密完成。我們將延展已有的隱私存儲模型來刻畫實際應用中的特徵，例如並行性與輸入/輸出高效性。由於現代結構設計普適採用了並行性與分級存儲器體系，我們的模型將對包括多核處理器、外包雲平台在內的多項實際應用中產生重要的影響。此外，我們發展更鬆弛的安全概念，以在性能與隱私級別中進行平衡。由Goldreich和Ostrovsky提出的經典不經意隨機存取器(ORAM)使得數據可以被不經意的存取，其中存儲模式不會洩露除運算序列長度以外的任何信息。 儘管在過去的十年中，ORAM的性能被提升，該模型並不能直接的支持並行結構。為了改變以上情況，不經意並行隨機存取器（OPRAM）在最近的TCC2016論文中被提出。在我們即將發表的TCC2017及ASIACRYPT2017論文中，我們得到了與最先進ORAM性能相同的OPRAM。這些初步成果啓發我們在OPRAM之外進一步探索支持多任務的隱私並行數據結構與他們的並行實現。除了並行性，分級存儲器體系在實際應用中也發揮著重要的作用。在即將發表的SODA2018論文中，我們提出了輸入/輸出高效、緩存不可知不經意排序算法，該成果給與我們強大的技術以繼續探索隱私機制中的輸入/輸出高效性。進一步，我們將探索在存儲方案中的新隱私概念，允許用戶在隱私偏好與性能保障中進行平衡。特別的，我們最近發展的技術使得我們可以克服以下挑戰：（1）在隱私數據結構與算法中探索並行性。我們將設計基礎的不經意並行算法作為存儲方案的基石，並研究深度與總工作之間的平衡。（2）在隱私機制中達到輸入/輸出高效性。例如，我們將考慮隱私方案中緩存不可知子程序，使得算法可以在沒有底層結構變量信息的情況下達到最優輸入/輸出高效性。 （3）研究存儲方案中更一般的安全概念。超越傳統ORAM，我們將考慮可微分隱私作為更鬆弛的安全要求，以在實際應用中取得更好的性能。

17200418.label: Realisation of objectives
17200418.value: Objective 1 We have explored concurrency and parallelism in private data structures and algorithms. One notable example is our study of Oblivious Parallel RAM (OPRAM). Our scheme, which offers perfect security, has demonstrated improvements in total work overhead and parallel depth compared to previous works. This advancement can be attributed to the use of special expander graphs for derandomizing earlier statistically secure OPRAM techniques, presenting a novel approach in the construction of ORAMs/OPRAMs. Our findings were published in TCC 2018. Moreover, we have developed distributed algorithms to compute approximate solutions for several related graph optimization problems. Our algorithms feature round complexity that is logarithmic in the number of nodes in the underlying graph, independent of the graph diameter. By utilizing a primal-dual approach, our algorithm can compute coreness values of nodes with approximation ratios close to 2. Additionally, our distributed algorithm can solve the min-max edge orientation problem with a similarly close approximation ratio. We have provided lower bounds that demonstrate the tightness of our approximation guarantee and round complexity. This research, which explores a weaker version of the densest subset problem, was published in IPDPS 2019 and the Journal of Parallel Distributed Computing 2021. Our work on Byzantine Agreement (BA) has also contributed to a better understanding of its round complexity. Despite previous research, significant gaps remained in comprehending BA under a corrupt majority. We have made progress in this area by developing a corrupt-majority BA protocol with sublinear round complexity, consistent with a high probability, and capable of tolerating a substantial fraction of corrupt nodes. Our protocol is secure against adaptive adversaries and offers an upper bound that is optimal up to a logarithmic factor. These results were published in PKC 2020. Objective 2 We have focused on achieving I/O efficiency for private mechanisms. To address this challenge, we have explored various approaches, including multi-server settings in the context of Oblivious RAM (ORAM). Traditionally, ORAM has been studied in a single-server setting with tree-based approaches that offer good bandwidth overhead but lack I/O efficiency. By considering a multi-server setting, we have developed a 3-server ORAM scheme that not only achieves I/O efficiency but also provides perfect security and O(log^2 N) total work overhead. This performance surpasses the best-known single-server scheme by a logarithmic factor. Our study also demonstrates that specific problems, such as obliviously merging two sorted arrays, can benefit from multiple servers in overcoming known lower bounds in the single-server setting. Our findings were published in ASIACRYPT 2018. We have also investigated locality-preserving ORAMs to address the issue of conventional ORAM schemes disrupting the locality of data accesses. Our research has led to the development of a locality-preserving ORAM with poly-logarithmic overhead in terms of both bandwidth and locality. By examining the trade-off between locality, bandwidth, and leakage, we have discovered that schemes preserving locality without revealing the lengths of contiguous memory regions accessed suffer from prohibitive bandwidth. Our approach utilizes a locality-friendly oblivious sorting algorithm, and the results were published in EUROCRYPT 2019 and the Journal of Cryptology 2022. We have revisited the problem of low-memory robust simulation of interactive protocols over noisy channels, particularly in the context of client-server interactive protocols and multi-server Private Information Retrieval (PIR) schemes. Our proposed information-theoretic technique converts any correct PIR protocol that assumes reliable channels into a protocol that is both correct and private in the presence of a noisy channel while minimizing space complexity. Our technique addresses the challenges of previous approaches by saving hashes of prefixes of past transcripts, resulting in a more robust simulation. These results were published in SODA 2020. Furthermore, our research has led to the development of bucket oblivious sort and bucket oblivious random permutation algorithms, which offer a conceptually simple and efficient approach to oblivious sorting. The bucket oblivious sort algorithm demonstrates a runtime that is only three times slower than a non-oblivious merge sort baseline, making it significantly faster than the bitonic sort. Our results were published in SOSA 2020. Objective 3 We have investigated more general notions of security in storage schemes. Moving beyond conventional ORAMs, we have explored differential privacy as a more relaxed security requirement, which allows for improved performance in practice. Our work considers the notion of oblivious simulation, which prevents the access pattern from revealing any information about the input. However, due to the well-known logarithmic ORAM lower bound by Goldreich and Ostrovsky, achieving this strict notion presents certain limitations. Inspired by differential privacy, we have introduced the concept of differential obliviousness, which ensures that the distribution of the access pattern does not change significantly when the input is slightly altered. By examining classical problems such as sorting small-length keys, merging two sorted lists, and range query data structures, we have demonstrated that adopting differential obliviousness with reasonable parameters can circumvent several impossibilities related to full obliviousness. Conversely, we have shown that for more stringent parameter choices, the same lower bounds for oblivious algorithms still apply. Our findings have been published in SODA 2019 and JACM 2022. In addition to differential obliviousness, we have investigated Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) as a model of computation that captures realistic parallel computing architectures, such as large-scale MapReduce and Hadoop clusters. Given that many data analytics tasks on these platforms involve sensitive user data, our research has explored how to leverage MPC architectures for efficient, privacy-preserving computation over massive data sets. We have established that any task that can be efficiently computed on MPC can also be securely computed with comparable efficiency. Specifically, we have shown that any MPC algorithm can be compiled into a communication-oblivious counterpart, preserving its round and space complexity. Communication-obliviousness ensures that any network intermediary observing the communication patterns learns no information about the secret inputs. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that, assuming the existence of Fully Homomorphic Encryption with a suitable notion of compactness and other standard cryptographic assumptions, any MPC algorithm can be compiled to a secure counterpart that defends against adversaries controlling not only intermediate network routers but also up to a less than 1/3 fraction of machines. This compilation preserves the round complexity tightly and the space complexity up to a multiplicative security parameter-related blowup. These results have been published in ITCS 2020.

17200418.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200418.value: For Objective 1, we have investigated concurrency and parallelism within private data structures and algorithms, including Oblivious Parallel RAM (OPRAM) with perfect security, showcasing improvements in overhead and parallel depth (TCC 2018). We have also devised distributed algorithms for graph optimization issues featuring logarithmic round complexity and tight approximation guarantees (IPDPS 2019, Journal of Parallel Distributed Computing 2021). Our research on Byzantine Agreement (BA) has enriched our comprehension of its round complexity by formulating a corrupt-majority BA protocol with sublinear round complexity and optimal upper bounds (PKC 2020). Addressing Objective 2, we have attained I/O efficiency for private mechanisms by examining multi-server settings in Oblivious RAM (ORAM) and creating a 3-server ORAM scheme with perfect security and enhanced performance (ASIACRYPT 2018). Furthermore, we have designed locality-preserving ORAMs, generating a scheme with poly-logarithmic overhead in both bandwidth and locality (EUROCRYPT 2019, Journal of Cryptology 2022). We also revisited low-memory robust simulation of interactive protocols over noisy channels, introducing an information-theoretic technique for multi-server Private Information Retrieval (PIR) schemes (SODA 2020). Finally, we designed bucket oblivious sort and bucket oblivious random permutation algorithms for a more efficient oblivious sorting approach (SOSA 2020). Regarding Objective 3, we have delved into differential privacy in storage schemes and utilized differential obliviousness, illustrating its potential to overcome full obliviousness limitations (SODA 2019, JACM 2022). We have also explored Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) for privacy-preserving computation on vast data sets, demonstrating that any MPC algorithm can be transformed into a communication-oblivious counterpart while maintaining similar efficiency and security (ITCS 2020). This project has also mentored two PhD students. One thesis examined concurrency and parallelism in combinatorial problems in graphs and hypergraphs, emphasizing well-connected parts detection and algorithm development for various problems, including k-core decomposition and the k-clique densest subgraph problem. The other thesis concentrated on communication-efficient low-memory robust simulation of client-server interactive protocols over noisy channels. Lastly, this project has fostered collaboration with global academic institutions in the US, Europe, Israel, and Asia, as well as industry research labs.

17200418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200418.value: Future research will continue to refine Oblivious Parallel RAM (OPRAM) and other private data structures and algorithms for enhanced security and efficiency, potentially incorporating machine learning techniques. Expanding distributed algorithms for graph optimization, such as community detection and network flow, will facilitate applications in real-world scenarios like social networks and transportation systems. Investigating the scalability and adaptability of Byzantine Agreement (BA) protocols in various network conditions and applications, including blockchain and secure multiparty computation, should continue to be investigated. For instance, optimizing I/O efficiency for private mechanisms can be achieved by exploring server configurations and access strategies in Oblivious RAM (ORAM). Developing novel privacy-preserving techniques and tools for handling sensitive data can be accomplished by applying concepts of differential privacy and differential obliviousness to domains like machine learning and data analytics. Creating a comprehensive framework for Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) algorithms that integrates with existing data processing systems can ensure privacy-preserving computation without sacrificing performance and scalability. Moreover, establishing collaborations with research groups and industry partners can facilitate real-world applications, such as finance, healthcare, and smart cities. For example, engaging with regulatory bodies and policymakers is vital for promoting privacy-preserving computation and developing implementation standards and guidelines across sectors.

17200418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200418.value: This project aimed to protect sensitive information in computer systems by researching and developing advanced data storage methods and algorithms. The primary focus was on enhancing the way data is accessed and processed while maintaining privacy and security. We have designed innovative techniques for handling data, allowing multiple tasks to be performed simultaneously, thereby increasing efficiency without compromising privacy. This has improved our understanding of securely processing data in complex systems such as cloud platforms. We have achieved enhanced efficiency in managing data input and output, which is crucial for modern computer systems. By creating new, more efficient algorithms, sensitive data remains secure even when accessed by multiple users. We have explored novel ways of securing data that balance privacy and performance. By considering alternative privacy models, we have been able to develop more efficient and flexible solutions for real-world applications. In summary, this project has made significant advancements in the field of data security, with wide-ranging applications in modern computing systems, such as multi-core processors and cloud platforms. The research has provided valuable insights and practical solutions for maintaining privacy and security while optimizing the performance of data storage and processing systems.

17200518.label: Project Objectives
17200518.value: Understanding and realization of ultra-small and ligand-free ternary MONPs. The present synthesis method of ultra-small MONPs mainly includes the precipitation reaction for intermediates and the decomposition of the intermediates for MONPs, and no exotic ligand will be used throughout the process. We propose the new “molecules pre-nesting mechanism” as the NP refinement mechanism. Based on our achievements in ultra-small NiOx NPs, together with the very recent demonstration of ultra-small NiCo2O4 NPs, we aim to achieve a series of ultra-small ternary MONPs. Specifically, we will identify and establish the new mechanism through studying NP size when water is pre-nested in the intermediates. We will also adopt other pre-nesting molecules to pursue ultra-small MONPs for reinforcing the proposed mechanism. With the fundamental understanding of NP refinement, we will offer new ligand-free strategies to synthesize a series of ultra-small ternary MONPs (e.g. NiCo2O4, SrTiO3) by introducing and manipulating extra molecules in the intermediate mixtures. Unveiling the mechanisms of ligand-free MONP monodispersion and its relationship with film formation from MONP inks. We will investigate the dispersity of ligand-free MONPs and unveil the mechanism of film formation with MONP inks. Specifically, we will reveal the MONPs dispersity from the viewpoint of interactions between NPs and between NP and disperse molecules. We will study the effect of varying the concentration of surface ions and functional groups on the surfaces on the dispersity status (i.e. precipitated suspension, disperse collection with mildly-aggregated NPs, and monodisperse collection). Based on the acquired results, we will gain the fundamental knowledge of the monodispersity of ligand-free MONPs and develop monodisperse MONP inks in different disperse media (e.g. water, chlorobenzene (CB), dichlorobenzene (DCB), chloroform (CF), alcohols and toluene). Realizing post-treating-free MOPN CTLs for high-performance OSCs/PVSCs. In order to obtain efficient MONP CTLs, we will theoretically and experimentally optimize the band-structure, optical and electrical properties of MONPs. Meanwhile, in order to show the potential of scalability, we will achieve uniform and compact CTLs, taking the advantage of ultra-small size of the MONP inks. We will fabricate organic/perovskite solar cells using MONP CTLs to show the advantage of post-treatment-free from the ligand-free MONPs. Through the decent electrical and optical properties, good band-alignment in device, and ultra-small and post-treatment-free advantages of MONPs, we aim to improve performances of OSCs and PVSCs by the integration of MONP CTLs. ***To show our capability to manage the project, we have started to work on the project. The preliminary results of 5 nm NiCo2O4 NPs have been achieved through using a new ammonia pre-nesting strategy (see “Research Plan and Methodology” for details).

17200518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200518.value: 有機/鈣鈦礦太陽能電池（OSC / PVSC）是有前景的溶液處理光伏電池。為了充分發揮溶液工藝的潛力，開發高性能溶液處理載流子傳輸層（CTL）至關重要，因為CTL對於有效提取光生載流子具有決定性作用。溶液處理的金屬氧化物納米粒子（MONP）是有希望的CTL候選物，不僅因為它們的低成本，良好的穩定性和在金屬氧化物半導體中發現的有利的電學/光學性質，而且因為預成型MONP解耦納米粒子（NP）的合成和成膜，從而為CTL製備提供更多自由度。特別是溶液處理的超小（<10 nm）MONP對於MONP分散體系列（稱為墨水）的長期均勻性以及典型的薄CTL（幾十納米厚）的緊湊性和平滑性非常有吸引力，這是高性能溶液處理光伏產品中備受追捧的產品。 溶液處理的MONP CTL中非常重要的特徵是無後處理，這可以有效地避免對易受影響的底層的損害，例如，柔性基板和易受攻擊的活性層。目前，外來有機配體，例如，烷基膦氧化物，烷基膦酸，烷基膦，脂肪酸和胺通常用於通過連接到MONP表面來穩定MONP分散。 然而，大多數配體的導電性差阻礙了MONP之間的載流子傳輸，並且去除配體需要單獨分隔的後處理（例如高溫退火和等離子體）。實現無後處理的挑戰是避免在合成和分散中添加配體。 除了實現無後處理之外，簡單的MONP合成方法對於實際的MONP CTL特別有吸引力。雖然MONP合成通常涉及復雜的工藝和苛刻的要求（例如高壓和有害的原材料）導致高成本，低重複性和環境問題，我們最近開發了一種簡便的合成方法，用於無配體的NiOx-NP墨水。 ~5 nm NP直徑作為OSC / PVSC中的高效NiOx CTL，無需任何後處理。隨著之前對NiOx-NP的探索，由於三元金屬氧化物帶隙可調性和良好的導電性，我們將研究三元MONP（例如Zn2SnO4，CuGaO2），以及它們作為CTL的有限成功應用。為了實現理想的三元MONP CTL，其具有無後處理，低成本（即簡單）和可擴展性（即溶液處理）的特點，在本項目中，我們將解決以下挑戰：（1）理解和實現超小三元具有無配體和簡單/綠色方法的MONP; （2）揭示MONP油墨中無配體MONP單分散機理及其與成膜的關係; （3）實現高性能OSC / PVSC的無治療後MOPN CTL。 因此，這項工作對於實現OSC / PVSC的有效解決方案處理的MONP CTL以及多樣化策略以改善器件製造和設計中的光伏性能從根本上和實際上的重要性。

17200518.label: Realisation of objectives
17200518.value: In objective 1, we continue to synthesize ultra-small and ligand-free MONPs. Notably, CuGaO2 ternary metal oxide synthesized from the conventional hydrothermal route usually yield large and agglomerated particles, where the diameters can be as large as from a few hundred nanometers to about 1 μm. We propose to incorporate a Cr-doped strategy under hydrothermal synthesis conditions together with controllable intermediates and surfactants’ assistance to synthesize Cr-doped CuGaO2 ternary nanoplates [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 16611]. The obtained Cr/CuGaO2 nanocrystals with a diameter of 48.3 nm are much smaller than the undoped CuGaO2 (78.9 nm), which is the smallest among reported doped CuGaO2 samples. The size reduction can be explained that part of Ga atoms (0.62 Å) are easily substituted by small ionic radius Cr (0.52 Å), which is similar to other doped CuGaO2. The function of the surfactant is to create a barrier for nanoparticles by binding on particle surfaces and prevent the nanocrystals from growing into larger nanocrystals. Apart from CuGaO2, we also we demonstrate the first kind of room-temperature solution-processed and post-treatment-free Li and Cu co-doped NiOx nanoparticle [J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 371-379]. A smaller grain size of 4.28 nm on average is obtained for the co-doped NPs, which is smaller than pristine NiOx (5.62 nm on average), which is attributed to the smaller size of hydroxide intermediates. We further developed a low temperature synthesis approach for obtaining Sn:In2O3 nanoparticles [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. The Sn-doped In2O3 NPs synthesized by our low-temperature strategy show a high crystallinity and small size distribution. In objective 2, we focus on the film-formation quality from the MONP inks. The Cr-doped CuGaO2 ternary nanoplates can serve as excellent expressway for improving hole extraction properties, we then employed ultrasmall-sized NiOx nanoparticles to modify the surface for achieving unique surface properties [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 16611]. The HTL formed from the designed hybrid 3D-nanostructured system exhibits the advantages of smooth and full-covered surface, the RMS roughness was significantly decreased from 23 nm to 14 nm. Simultaneously, the co-doping strategy also helps to flatten the film surface (pin-hole/crack free) and improve film optical transmittance [J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 371-379]. The surface roughness has been reduced from 3.09 nm of Li and Cu co-doped NiOx NPs to 4.00 of un-doped NPs. We also found the Sn-doped In2O3 NPs film helps to improve the device stability [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. Following that, we realized that pristine NPs films will easily have pin-holes or defects, which is detrimental to device stability and performance. To improve the MONPs film quality, we also developed passivation strategies on the MONP films. Potassium slat (KSCN) is adopted to passivate the NiOx NPs film [Small Methods 2020, 4, 2000478]. In addition to potassium passivation, the thiocyanate showed good passivation effects on MONP films. The strong Ni-N bonding exhibited strong polar covalent bond properties to make the electron deviate from the Ni side and finally leads to a more compact surface. Moreover, we applied imidazole bromide functionalized graphene quantum dots (I-GQDs) to modify SnO2 film [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. The functional groups on the surface of GQDs could reduce the interface trap states and the metal oxide film roughness was obviously decreased from 1.38 nm to 1.06 nm. In objective 3, since the hole/electron transport properties of the MONPs are critical and their enabled device performance is essential. The approaches that can improves quality of the NPs and the corresponding films introduced in objective 1 and 2 were also adopted to fabricate OSCs/PVSC devices. The Cr-doped CuGaO2 together with NiOx presented remarkable charge collection efficiency, energy level alignment between the electrode and perovskite layer, and the promotion of perovskite crystal growth [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 16611]. Consequently, nearly 20% of power conversion efficiency with negligible hysteresis is achieved in inverted perovskite solar cells (PVSCs). Moreover, it is found that the Li and Cu codoped NiOx HTL exhibited improved electrical conductivity, favored large grain-size perovskite film formation and wide-range thermal stability up to 250 °C. With these interesting multiple functions, PVSCs with Li and Cu codoped NiOx HTLs achieve a PCE of 20.8% and 18.2% on rigid and flexible substrates, respectively [J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 371-379]. Notably, doping strategy also improved the energy level alignment in In2O3 with PVSK [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. Sn-doped In2O3 NPs combined with pristine In2O3 double layer formed a gradient potential structure, which featured enhanced built-in potential, high electron extraction, low interfacial recombination and offered a PCE of 20.65% in PSVCs. The defect alleviation of the PVSK films brought by the MONPs films was further investigated. It is found that, by KSCN modification on the NiOx ultra-small NPs, the strong electrostatic force between S and Pb in MAPbI3 makes the Pb atomic layer closer to perovskite to restrain the I atom [Small Methods 2020, 4, 2000478]. The modification also led to better valence band alignment, which achieved a high efficiency of 21.23% with open-circuit voltage of 1.14 V and improved operational stability of PVSC devices. Further, GQDs modified SnO2 film not only reduced the interface defects for achieving a better energy level alignment between ETL and perovskite, but also improved the film quality of FAPbI3 perovskite including enlarged grain size, lower trap density, and a longer carrier lifetime, which realized a higher efficiency of 22.37% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. Because of the facile film-formation, excellent electrical and optical properties of MONPs, they have been widely applied to fabricate photovoltaic devices without further post-treatment. Ultra-small NiOx NPs had been applied to fabricate different PVSC devices with efficiency of 20.64% [Small 2020, 16, 2002628], 21.2 % [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 57165] and 21.52% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 2105290]. Due to excellent film quality, ultra-small NiOx NPs had also been adopted in blue light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), and achieves brightness of 1765 cd/m2, EQE of 7.51%, low turn-on voltage of 3.07 V, and long operation lifetime of 3961 s under constant driving current without any shift of the electroluminescence spectra [ACS Energy Lett. 2020, 5, 2569]. Except for NiOx, ultra-small ZnO and MoOx had been employed as top ETL and sintering media, respectively, in evaporation-free OSCs, and contributing to a high efficiency of 15% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 2010764].

17200518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200518.value: In the period of the project, 17 research articles and 7 review articles have been published in international peer-reviewed journals. The best-performed PVSC and OSCs based on ultra-small MONPs reached PCE of over 22.3% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438] and 15% [Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 2010764], respectively. Particularly, with the doping optimization of the ultra-small MONPs carrier transport layer, the stability of PVSCs reached an operation lifetime of over 2000 hours [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. (1) Different doping or even co-doping strategies have been developed to decrease the ligand-free MONP size (<8 nm) and to flatten the corresponding films. The improved surface morphology also contribute to electrical/optical properties and improves the perovskite film quality including organic and inorganic Pb and Pb-Sn-based perovskites. The results are been published in [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 16611; J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 371-379; ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27179]. (2) New approaches of ligand-induced surface passivation of ultra-small ligand-free MONPs. Since the as-cast NPs films may have pin-holes, surface passivation helps to reduce the traps and bridge the NPs with perovskite, and ultimately improve the perovskite grain size, device performance and stability. Theoretical studies using DFT method had been conducted to simulate the interaction between MONPs, passivation media and perovskite to unveil the underlined mechanism. The results have been published in [Small Methods 2020, 4, 2000478; Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101438]. (3) A series of devices including PVSCs, OSCs and LEDs based on ultra-small ligand-free MONPs had been fabricated and shown excellent performance. Importantly, the MONPs in these devices demonstrate wide versatility varies from deposition solvent, hole/electron transport to top/bottom deposition technique, which features different application occasions. The results are reported in [Small 2020, 16, 2002628; ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2020, 12, 57165; Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 2105290; ACS Energy Lett. 2020, 5, 2569; Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 2010764]. It should be noted that the outputs stated in this progress report are achieved through the financial support from this GRF fund together with some other grants from RGC as stated in the acknowledgement of the publications.

17200518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200518.value: With the proposed strategies and the investigation of their effects on size and film quality of ultra-small ligand-free MONPs involving particle dispersity and film deposition kinetics, our work offers methodology for scientific and industry society to deposit low-cost, high conductivity/transmittance and smooth metal oxide semiconductor layers. Importantly, its correlation with the active layer performance such as perovskite is also essential to improve the stability and performance of optoelectronic devices. The series of low-temperature solution-processed MONPs semiconductor materials can be further investigated to improve electrical/optical properties and also applicable in flexible and semitransparent devices such as photovoltaic window, semi-transparent display and integrated wearable electronics.

17200518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200518.value: In this period, we have introduced and investigated different strategies to decrease the size, improve the monodispersity, optimize the corresponding film surface of solution-processed metal oxide nanoparticles semiconductor materials. The doping or intermediate effects on the final particle size are fully studied. We successfully reduced the nanoparticle size to lower than 8 nm and smoothen the surface (root-mean-square roughness of 1.06 nm), which is critical for the electrical and optical properties of the obtained films. Then, we applied the synthesized or optimized metal oxide nanoparticles to fabricate different types of optoelectronic devices. The perovskite solar cell device performance is significantly boosted to over 22.3% and operational stability is also prolonged to over 2000 hours. The mechanism and correlation between the nanoparticles with the perovskite films are thoroughly and systematically uncovered via experimental and theoretical tools. The project covering semiconductor synthesis, materials property modeling and device physics studying offers new insights for the design and fabrication of low-cost, scalable, high-performance and stable optoelectronic devices.

17200618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200618.value: Taxis offer round-the-clock, comfortable, and direct transportation services. However, they often cruise and circulate around a city to search for customers because after dropping off their customers, drivers cannot find a new customer straightaway at the drop-off location. The total travel distances of vacant taxis can be great. Consequently, taxis can use up much road space and capacity, and can worsen traffic congestion and roadside air quality. To tackle these problems, taxi regulation policies have been established. The effectiveness of these policies can be evaluated by a taxi network traffic assignment model. However, the existing models have not simultaneously considered the following. First, e-hailing has become popular. Second, there are multiple taxi classes (e.g., taxis with different fare structures and taxis serving different regions) and heterogeneous customers. Third, customer demand and traffic conditions change over time. Fourth, demand for taxi services is elastic. It is therefore important to develop a methodology to consider the abovementioned factors simultaneously for taxi policy evaluation. Moreover, the current taxi policy studies do not consider the following new regulatory policies: providing incentives in the form of origin-based surcharges to vacant taxi drivers to go to the areas with a low taxi supply to search for customers, offering peak-hour taxi licenses to allow the fleet size to vary during the day, allowing the operating area of each taxi type to change during the day, and dynamic pricing for multiple e-hailing services. It is crucial to develop a tool to evaluate the effectiveness of these policies. The proposed project will develop methodologies for the dynamic modeling and management of taxi markets with multiple taxi classes, heterogeneous travelers, different e-hailing platforms, and elastic demand using the bi-level optimization theory and the continuum modeling approach. It will analyze the aforementioned regulatory policies, evaluate their effectiveness, and clarify policy implications, which will help governments to manage taxi markets with third-party hailing services (e.g., Uber and Lyft). The project will include a case study for providing new insights to the Hong Kong government for deciding the fleet size and the dynamic pricing strategies of new taxi services under the impact of Uber. The proposed research will contribute to the literature by introducing new taxi market management concepts and problems and advancing the theory of taxi network modeling and solution methods. The proposed modeling framework is expected to be used to assess regulations for different services (taxis, Uber, etc.), including non-cooperative pricing strategies. 出租車能夠提供全天候，舒適且便捷的運輸服務。但因為出租車司機往往不能在完成一次乘客出行後在出行目的地直接尋找到新的乘客，他們需要駛往別處尋找新的乘客。而由此產生的空載行駛距離可以是很長的。這將導致大量的道路空間被擠占，道路的通行能力也將受到影響，進而加劇了交通擁堵和道路周邊的空氣污染。為了解決上述問題，相關管理部門製定了許多與出租車有關的政策法規。這些政策法規的有效性則可以通過出租車網絡交通分配模型進行評估。但是，現有的模型並不能同時考慮到下列因素。首先，網約車服務已經十分普遍。其次，出租車和乘客是各種各樣的。 （例如，出租車可能存在不同的收費標準和服務區域）。再次，乘客對出租車的需求以及道路交通狀況是隨著時間變化的。最後，乘客對出租車的需求是彈性的。因此，提出一種能夠同時考慮到上述因素的方法以評估出租車政策是十分重要的。此外，現有的出租車政策研究也沒有考慮到下列出租車新規：通過對乘客徵收基於出行起始點附加費以鼓勵空載出租車前往需求較低的區域搜尋乘客；允許發放出行高峰期出租車牌照從而實現出租車數量在一天中的不同時段發生變化；允許不同種類出租車的運行區域在一天中的不同時段產生變化；對各種網約車乘客實行動態定價。對上述新政提出行之有效的評估方法同樣是很重要的。 本項目擬提出基於雙層優化理論和連續建模方法的出租車市場動態建模與管理方法。項目將同時考慮多種出租車和乘客種類、不同網約車平台以及對出租車的彈性需求並對上述出租車政策的有效性進行分析，明確政策的意義，從而幫助政府部門在第三方召車服務（例如，Uber、Lyft）存在的情況下管理出租車市場。同時，本項目將包括一例個案研究以為香港政府在Uber進入市場的情況下重新擬定出租車數量和製定動態收費政策時提供深入的參考意見和建議。本項目研究所提出的新型出租車市場管理問題和概念將豐富現有的出租車政策研究並推動出租車網絡建模與求解的發展。項目提出的模型框架將會被用於評估針對不同類型出租車（例如，常規出租、Uber等）服務的政策，包括非合作定價策略等。

17200618.label: Realisation of objectives
17200618.value: The first objective is to propose a dynamic taxi network modeling framework for the studied taxi market with multiple e-hailing and taxi services. To achieve this objective, a dynamic taxi network modeling framework was proposed based on a time-space network [J3]. This modeling framework was used to model the temporal dynamics of a taxi market, and can be extended to consider multiple taxi classes [J1, J2] such as restricted area taxis, urban taxis, premium electric taxis, and conventional liquefied petroleum gas taxis. [J8] and [J9] provide frameworks to model and manage the real-time operation of multiple e-hailing services with multiple classes of e-hailing vehicles (e.g., electric, premier, and express ride-hailing vehicles) and multiple user classes. This objective has been completely achieved. The second objective is to examine various dynamic pricing and fleet size control strategies for the taxi market whereas the third objective is to develop and analyze different novel dynamic management strategies for the taxi market. To achieve these two objectives, the following tasks were done: First, a new dynamic pricing and fleet size control strategy for managing a taxi market was studied. The associated problem is called a peak-period taxi scheme design problem [J3], which was proposed to simultaneously determine the peak-period taxi surcharge and the optimal fleet size/shifts of peak-period taxis (PTs) in a regulated taxi market. The problem was formulated as a bi-level program, in which the upper level is the government problem and the lower level refers to the taxi driver problem. The upper-level objective is to maximize social welfare and it is required that customer waiting time for taxis in each period of a day must be lower than a maximum acceptable value to guarantee the taxi service quality. The lower level is an equilibrium problem that describes the scheduling behaviors of taxi drivers working in different shifts. A time-expanded network was used to depict the time-of-day dynamics of demand for and supply of taxis. The model was solved by a brute force method combined with the Frank-Wolfe algorithm. Numerical experiments were conducted to give policy implications and managerial insights into the regulation of dynamic taxi markets. Next, a taxi market regulatory problem called the taxi service area design problem was studied. The service area of a taxi is a region of the city in which taxis are allowed to run and provide services to customers. Conventionally, taxis are allowed to operate anywhere in a city. However, in some cities, taxis are classified into different types according to their confined service areas. Taxis with a service area restriction are only allowed to provide their service within the designated area. A mixed integer nonlinear optimization model was developed to determine the service area of each type of taxi with the objective to maximize social welfare [J1]. The taxi service area design problem contains two sub-problems. The first one is a combined network equilibrium problem; the second one is a regulatory problem, which is to select a specific region from the entire network as the service area of each type of restricted area taxi. A greedy heuristic was proposed to solve the model. Numerical experiments were conducted to examine the performance of the proposed heuristic and to provide insights into taxi service area design and management strategies. Then, the PI focused on emission surcharges, optimal fare, and fleet size regulation in two market regimes [J4]: (i) market with gasoline taxis and gasoline ride-sourcing vehicles and (ii) market with electric taxis and electric ride-sourcing vehicles. Moreover, a taxi market with a monopsony taxi owner and multiple rentee-drivers was modeled and analyzed in [J5], which focused on taxi rent control and the effect of fare adjustment by the government on different stakeholders. Furthermore, the effects of accessible taxi service and taxi fare subsidy scheme on the elderly’s willingness-to-travel was examined in [J6] and presented in an annual international conference held in Hong Kong [C2]. In addition, the effects of peak hour and congested area taxi surcharges on customers’ travel decisions were analyzed and the policy implications were discussed in [J7]. Finally, the PI proposed introducing taxi surcharges under extreme weather conditions [J10] and presented the findings virtually [C1]. All these studies focus on the analysis of management or control strategies, and provide managerial suggestions to the government. To sum up, the second and third objectives have been achieved successfully.

17200618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200618.value: The research outcomes (in forms of the modeling frameworks, solution methodologies, and properties of studied models) and major findings were published in 10 journal papers [J1]-[J10]. Some of them were presented at international conferences [C1]-[C2]. The following summarizes the major findings and managerial insights. 1. More impatient passengers imply the need for more PTs to improve the taxi waiting time and service quality, but lower social welfare. Therefore, there is a trade-off between social welfare maximization and taxi service quality. Empirical evidence for taxi passengers’ preference for waiting time is critical to support the government in the decision-making process. 2. The optimal PT shifts become shorter and social welfare is smaller if PT drivers are more sensitive to work duration. Therefore, it is suggested that some full-time drivers (who are less sensitive to work duration) should be hired as PT drivers, but the government should work out some methods (e.g., subsidizing the PT drivers) to balance the profit levels between full-time and PT drivers. 3. Introducing restricted area taxis properly can reduce the customer waiting time inside the service area of restricted area taxis but increase the customer waiting time outside that area. 4. Under social welfare maximization, the optimal restricted taxi service area may shrink as the total taxi fleet size or the fare level of restricted area taxis decreases, or as the total demand increases. 5. The total emissions from taxis and ride-sourcing vehicles can be reduced by the regulation of taxi/ride-sourcing fare and fleet size. At social optimum, a taxi or ride-sourcing passenger should pay for the emission surcharge equal to the marginal emission cost incurred by his/her ride. The emission surcharge in the market with only gasoline taxis and ride-sourcing vehicles can be much higher than that in the market with only the electric counterparts. 6. Rentee-drivers can benefit from a fare adjustment if and only if it brings a higher marginal taxi revenue at the current level of employment. A fare adjustment likely benefits the monopsonist only if it only leads to an increase in taxi revenue but does not improve marginal taxi revenue. 7. A rent control can benefit both taxi customers and rentee-drivers but incurs a profit loss to the monopsonist. There is a chance that social welfare is improved by the effective rent control. 8. A fleet size control can harm monopsony and driver profits, customer demand, and social welfare.

17200618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200618.value: The proposed frameworks and the analyses did not consider competition between taxis and ride-sourcing vehicles. Therefore, one future research direction is to extend the proposed frameworks and the analyses to consider such competition.

17200618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200618.value: The proposed project developed methodologies for the dynamic modeling and management of taxi markets with multiple taxi classes and heterogeneous taxi customers. It analyzed different regulatory policies in various market regimes, evaluate their effectiveness, and clarify their policy implications, which will help governments to manage taxi markets with e-hailing services. The proposed research contributes to the literature by introducing new taxi market management concepts and problems and advancing the theory of taxi network modeling and solution methods.

17200718.label: Project Objectives
17200718.value: To conjecture on the correlation between points of maximum displacements of rogue waves physically with locations of poles in the complex plane, by taking the spatial coordinate to be complex by analytic continuation. To confirm that this conjecture can be verified for widely studied deterministic dynamical systems, and to conduct further trials for more complicated evolution equations. To understand how rogue waves or breathers can arise from special initial conditions, by starting the simulations with a long wavelength disturbance or a mode with the optimal modulation instability growth rate, and comparing the eventual outcomes. To formulate evolution equations for wave groups in the coastal waters in Hong Kong by analyzing the local marine condition and wave data; To assess the likelihood of occurrence of unexpectedly large amplitude waves from these dynamic factors.

17200718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200718.value: 背景：最近很多科學家在 ‘物理學中的極端和罕見事件’ 主題方面進行了深入研究。這些問題最初在海洋環境中出現，超出正常的大浪對海洋船隻和海上建築物構成了巨大危險。當這超常大波動在光纖波導中也被發現後，現在很多研究人員都在科學和工程學的許多領域中尋求和嘗試預測這種現象, 俗稱 ‘流氓波’, 也被稱為 ‘怪異波’ 或 ‘魔鬼波’ 。 目標和關鍵問題：除了在應用科學上的巨大潛力之外，流氓波已經引起了許多研究人員的注意，因為優雅的數學分析方法已被應用於非線性動力系統上, 從而獲得精確解。值得注意的是，這些流氓波類型在流體動力學水通道以及光波導中也已經獲得實驗上的驗證。我們的目標是利用動力系統知識對流氓波的動力學進行聯合的理論和計算研究。這項工作的另一個方向，是測試這些知識和結果是否適用於香港的本地環境。 研究方法: 我們首先推導或識別動力系統的代數精確解作為流氓波的模型, 接著推測物理空間中最大位移的時間和位置。從另一個角度來看, 我們將空間坐標視為複變量, 從復數平面中極點的動力學和軌跡, 然後計算極點的實部, 用來推測流氓波的振幅。這兩種方法的計算值是相等的。從電腦模擬來看, 我們利用最佳不穩定模式用作初始條件, 來預測流氓波的發生。 初步結果和擬議工作：這個推測在非線性薛定諤方程已經過驗證並測試, 但我們需要面對更複雜和更高階的薛定諤方程, 數值模擬也將會是同時進行。我們也會思考這些概念可否在香港應用, 包括查看波浪數據等工作。 重要性和意義：流氓波最大位移的振幅位置和發生的時間是科學與工程上的主要考慮因素, 這裡擬議的方案可以減少為流氓波尋找此類信息所付出的努力, 時間和資源，研究工作產生的新知識並可對香港和世界海上作業提出有價值的貢獻。

17200718.label: Realisation of objectives
17200718.value: (Objective1) The correlation between the points of maximum displacements of rogue waves and the locations of poles in the complex plane was first proposed by our group in a paper in 'Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science' in 2017. We provided strong evidence that the spatial locations of the maximum displacements were identical to the real parts of the poles at the turning points of the trajectories in the complex plane. These statements were verified for the widely studied systems like the cubic nonlinear Schrodinger equation. We extended this idea to more complicated systems like the complex modified Korteweg-de Vries equation in a paper in 'Nonlinear Dynamics' in 2020. (Objective2) Further tests were indeed conducted for other evolution systems. In 2020-2022, we were studying the possibility of 'internal rogue waves' in the interior of the oceans. In particular, excitation of internal waves could be triggered by three-wave resonance. While mathematical expressions of rogue waves were given in the literature, the study in terms of fluid dynamics and oceanography had not been performed. We derived the coefficients of the triad resonance equations in the context of a sharply varying density profile, a case of practical importance in the coastal and deep oceans. We then studied the movement of poles from the known analytical expressions. The conjecture on the correlation between locations of maximum displacements of rogue waves and the real parts at the turning points of the trajectories in complex plane was verified for the first order rogue waves. For the second order rogue waves, the matching was not completely exact and was off by about 1% or 2%. The results were published in 'Acta Mechanica Sinica' in 2023. (Objective3) The occurrence of rogue waves was often preceded by the growth of small amplitude disturbances due to modulation instability. Subsequent excitations of higher harmonics produced intriguing dynamics. The 'cascading mechanism' gave a reasonably simple picture to describe the phenomenon. Higher order harmonics exponentially small initially would grow at a higher rate than the fundamental mode. Eventually all modes would attain the same order of magnitude at one instant in time or one spatial location. For unbounded domains, this would signify the occurrence of rogue waves. For periodic boundary conditions, this would imply the formation of 'breathers'. The idea was first proposed by an American group in a paper in Physical Review E in 2015. We dramatically expanded this explanation for many dynamical systems in many leading journals, e.g. 'Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science' in 2021 and 'Physica D' in 2022. (Objective4) During 2020-2022, our conference attendance and site visits were affected by COVID-19. Nevertheless, we had still made substantial progress in aspects of practical applications, in terms of local marine conditions in Hong Kong. In Spring 2019, we were invited by the Drainage Services Department (DSD) of the Government to conduct a feasibility study of floating breakwaters as a temporary coastal protection mechanism against typhoons. This issue was made more acute by the widespread damages caused by super typhoon Mangkhut in 2018. The facilities near the shore of Ap Lei Chau (an island in the southern part of Hong Kong) were severely affected. DSD had initiated the deployment of floating breakwaters there in early 2019. Subsequently we conducted theoretical modeling studies as well as experimental investigations. Firstly, the water channel at the Polytechnic University was utilized. However, that channel had a length limitation of 25 meters. We then started a collaboration with the Shanghai Jiao Tong University, using their 100-meter channel. However, the COVID-19 pandemic prevented us from visiting there in 2020-2022, and the main communications were conducted mostly online. Nevertheless, the Hong Kong and Shanghai groups had measured and analyzed a tremendous amount of data. The results were filed in technical reports to DSD, and also presented in District Council meetings in Hong Kong by DSD engineers.

17200718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200718.value: We shall concentrate on the findings in 2021 and 2022, as works of 2019 and 2020 were at least partially covered in the progress report filed earlier. (A) Nonlinear Dynamics: Cascading Mechanism (A1) Background - Our contribution is to elucidate the cascading mechanism of 'integrable' as well as 'non-integrable' dynamical systems. A USA group first discussed such mechanism for the widely applicable nonlinear Schrodinger equation in 2015. (A2) Physical Basis - For a nonlinear system with a plane wave background, properties of small amplitude disturbances can be handled by classical methods of linearization. The nonlinear evolution will typically be a more difficult problem. One scenario is the excitation of the higher harmonics, which may be exponentially small initially. These higher harmonics may grow at a rate higher than that of the fundamental mode. Eventually, all harmonics attain roughly the same order of magnitude. A 'breather' (pulsating mode) is formed. (A3) Subsequent Development - Typically many such breathers decay, through mechanisms not fully understood. When the amplitude becomes sufficiently small, modulation instability is triggered again. Amplification resumes. The whole pattern may repeat indefinitely, provided that dissipation is negligibly small. This thus constitutes an illuminating example of the classical problem of 'Fermi-Pasta-Tsingou-Ulam' recurrence (FPUT). (A4) Our contribution is significantly expand this concept to many other nonlinear dynamical systems, e.g. (i) Coherently coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations (Chaos 2021) - optical fibers with weak birefringence. (ii) Schrodinger equation with self-steepening nonlinearity (Physica D, 2021) - 'short' optical pulse with the frequency in the femtosecond regime. (iii) Discrete systems (Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation, 2022) - using the widely studied Ablowitz-Ladik equation as example. (iv) Coupled waveguides (Physica D, 2022) - two-core fibers governed by linearly coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations as example. (B) Applications: Coastal and Marine Engineering (B1) We study triad resonance of oceanic waves, special interaction of three waves where the sums of frequencies and wave numbers of two waves are equal to the frequency and wave number of the third wave (Journal of Marine Science & Engineering, 2021). (B2) We develop numerical wave tanks with fifth order Stokes waves as inlet condition and absorbing boundary conditions at the other end (Ocean Engineering, 2022). These formulations serve as foundations for studies in breakwaters and coastal defense mechanisms in 2023 and 2024.

17200718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200718.value: (A) Scientific Aspects (A1) Nonlinear Dynamics - The repeated occurrence of breathers typically leads to doubly periodic patterns. These patterns will be periodic in the transverse variable by the formulation of the problem (spatial / temporal variable for fluid mechanics / optical waveguides respectively), and repeating in the propagation variable (temporal / spatial variable for fluid mechanics / optical waveguides). This scenario constitutes a manifestation of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou recurrence (FPUT). These studies lead to the award of another RGC GRF grant in 2022, and further nonlinear developments of instability will be reported in the next few years. (A2) Stability Properties - In addition to the direct numerical simulations, stability considerations in terms of eigenvalues and eigenvectors are also fruitful. Linearized stability equations and the periodic nature of the basic states dictate the occurrence of a 'monodromy matrix'. We have computed the maximum eigenvalues for these doubly periodic patterns (which are expressed in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions). Preliminary comparisons with results of simulations are very encouraging. (B) Application Floating Breakwater - Computational investigations of the dynamics of floating devices will be performed using volume of fluid scheme for free surface flows and turbulence models.

17200718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200718.value: Rogue waves are unexpectedly large displacements from an otherwise tranquil background. In the oceanic wave setting, rogue waves cause extensive damages to ships and have been known to sailors for nearly a century. Since 2007, surprising huge amplitude events are detected in optical waveguides and other physical fields too. The generation mechanism is still controversial and not fully understood. Deterministic approaches using special dynamical systems will be adopted here. Small amplitude disturbances on a plane wave background will grow from an interplay of dispersive and nonlinear effects, a mechanism known as modulation instability. Higher order harmonics exponentially small initially will grow at a higher rate. Eventually all modes attain the same order of magnitude at one time instant or one spatial location. A rogue wave or a breather will then be formed. This description is known as a cascading mechanism. Analytically, a conjecture on the locations of the maximum displacements of the rogue waves are correlated with the trajectories in the complex plane, by extending the time or spatial variable as a complex coordinate. These ideas and schemes of investigation are also used to investigate large amplitude waves in the marine neighborhood of Hong Kong.

17200918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200918.value: 近年來，網路化動態系統受到越來越多的關注。在該系統中，感測器，控制器和執行器通過網路交換資訊。網路的引入帶來了諸多優勢，如安裝和維護成本的降低，系統靈活性的增加，以及連線的顯著減少。這些優勢極大地推動了網路化系統在汽車工業、程序控制、遠端遙控等領域的應用。但隨著惡意網路攻擊的持續增多，以及國家和個人的資訊在網路中廣泛地傳播，網路化系統存在洩漏國家機密以及公民敏感資訊的風險。因此，隱私保護已經成為一個至關重要的問題，受到廣泛的關注。很多隱私保護技術方面的文獻已經發表，然而現有的隱私保護技術主要應用於資料統計和資料採擷領域。針對系統狀態估計、控制以及一致性設計的隱私保護技術很少，針對動態系統提出的隱私的數學表述也很少。鑒於網路化系統廣泛的使用以及對隱私的考慮，亟待有效的網路化系統的隱私保護機制。該機制能夠確定多少的隱私可以受到保護，同時能使得估計器具有較好的性能，控制器能夠穩定系統，以及多智慧體可以達到一致性。由於涉及到很多新的技術難題，實現該機制不僅僅是估計和控制性能與隱私保護程度之間的權衡問題。因此，從理論和應用的角度，需要新的技術來設計能夠保護隱私的估計器和控制器，這是本專案的主要目標。本專案也將擴展所得的成果到多智慧體，使得它們在隱私保護的情況下能很好地協同合作。本專案所得的成果將為智慧交通，智慧電網，多機器人合作等網路化系統的應用領域提供一個安全且具有隱私保護的環境。
