17201318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201318.value: Crowd disasters occur frequently in places and events with high densities of pedestrian movements, such as religious pilgrimages and large entertainment events, leading to compressive asphyxiation, stampedes and crushing with huge death tolls and serious injuries. The dynamics of pedestrian crowds have been widely studied, but most of them are concerned about the normal operating conditions. In a panicked situation, pedestrian behavior and interaction within a crowd are very different from those under a normal condition. When people try to escape from a hazardous situation, they push and squeeze their way to the exit, resulting in a sizable physical contact force between pedestrians. This pushing force can accumulate to a high level in a large crowd, leading to the possibility of compressive asphyxiation and an increased possibility of human stampedes and crushes. While the pushing intention and effort may be tampered by the release of panic through appropriate information passage, it is often hindered by impaired visual and audio conditions due to infrastructure constraints and noisy environments. In the proposed project, we will conduct control experiments to extract relevant data and information about the characteristics and behavior of a high-density crowd, and the internal interaction mechanisms such as force aggregation and information propagation in the crowd. On the basis of these data and information, we will develop a dynamic macroscopic model to describe pedestrian movements with a continuum modeling technique for a two-dimensional spatial domain, in which we will explicitly consider the pushing force, super density, hazard stimulus, and route choice behavior of a crowd under panic conditions. The problem will be formulated as an initial value problem with a set of partial differential equations with appropriate boundary conditions. We will also rigorously investigate the analytical properties of the model and develop efficient numerical schemes to solve the model. The methodology will also be tested using examples of recent crowd disaster events. 人群災害頻繁發生在行人密度高的場所和事件中，如宗教朝聖和大型娛樂活動等，這可導致行人壓縮窒息、踩踏，造成巨大的死傷人數。人群動力學已被廣泛研究，但大多僅關心正常情況下的行人流動。恐慌情況下行人的行為以及在人群中的互動與正常情況下是非常不同的。當人們試圖逃離危險時，會推擠到出口處，這可導致行人間產生相當大的推力。這種推力可在大型人群中積累到很高的程度，從而可能導致行人壓縮窒息，以及增加人群踩踏和擠壓受傷的可能性。雖然通過適當的信息渠道發布恐慌信息可能在一定程度上影響人們擠推的意圖和力度，但由於基礎設施的約束和嘈雜的環境，行人的視覺和聽覺經常會被削弱。在這項目中，我們將進行可控實驗，以提取有關高密度人群的特徵、行為以及人群積聚推力和信息傳播等內部相互作用機制的相關數據和信息。在這些數據和信息基礎上，我們將利用二維空間連續建模技術，構建動態宏觀模型來描述行人運動，其中將明確地考慮人群在恐慌狀態下的推力、超密度、危險信息傳播和路徑選擇行為。該問題將通過採用一組具有適當邊界條件的偏微分方程被表述為初值問題。我們還將縝密地分析模型的特質，並建立有效的數值方案來求解該模型。並會使用近期的人群災難事件作為此方法的測試例子。

17201318.label: Realisation of objectives
17201318.value: In order to accomplish Objective 1, several control experiments were carried out to gather data and information regarding pedestrian traits and actions, with the aim of comprehending the dynamics of high-density crowds, which are linked with elevated risks such as stampede accidents during panic situations. To disclose pedestrian interactions within a crowd, two sets of control experiments were designed to exhibit their walking behavior, consisting of a 1.5-meter-wide ring corridor and a single-file circular track. A variety of pedestrian densities were established, with a maximum of 9 pedestrians per square meter, a figure frequently seen in crowd disasters. To gain a deeper understanding of body motion and walking style of pedestrians in a crowd, another set of control experiments, single-file and two-way, were conducted. In these experiments, pedestrians walked in a 0.5-meter-wide circular corridor, rotating their bodies to prevent collisions. This set of experiments reveals pedestrians' micro-characteristics at the step level, which also exposes their reactions to nearby individuals, thereby offering insights into the macroscopic characteristics of a large crowd. In many crowd catastrophes, pedestrians often experience panic in walking environments with limited visibility, such as during dark hours or in a smoke-filled room during emergency evacuations. To comprehend pedestrian responses and behavior in such unfavorable conditions, a series of control experiments were carried out in a 6.8 m x 10.0 m room. In these experiments, participants wore baseball caps with two layers of opaque veil coverings to simulate limited visibility conditions and were instructed to exit the room in situations with different geometric settings and varying density levels. Through these controlled experiments, valuable insights into pedestrian flow dynamics in high-density situations were obtained. Moreover, the findings contribute valuable information for the development of crowd models in Objective 2. To achieve Objective 2, the analytical properties of dynamic continuum models for pedestrian flows were initially reviewed. This helped in understanding the rationality of continuum approaches in describing panicked crowd models in high-density situations where crowd disasters frequently occur. A model based on this approach, which views pedestrians as a continuous flow rather than individual agents, was developed. This model explicitly considered the effect of crowd force based on the formation mechanism of force chains in a dense crowd, where pushing forces could propagate through persistent physical contact. This pushing behavior, which depended on the panic sentiment, could lead to sudden changes in pedestrian movement patterns. The crowd model was formulated as a second-order pedestrian model consisting of two types of equations: a continuity equation and a set of transport equations. Eikonal equations were employed to explicitly consider the effects of the collective decisions of individuals and the development of crowd pressure on pedestrian dynamics. Mathematically, this model takes the form of a set of partial differential equations under appropriate initial and boundary conditions. Stability requirements, derived through a standard linear stability analysis, provided guidelines for selecting suitable parameters for the developed model. Moreover, the linear stability analysis elucidated the relationship between collective movement patterns and crowd characteristics, such as the connection between observed instabilities and the behavioral parameters introduced in the model. Empirical studies of large gatherings and stampede disasters have highlighted two crucial features of dense crowds: extremely high crowd pressure and crowd turbulence. The aforementioned model has successfully represented crowd behavior under extremely high crowd pressure in a unidirectional pedestrian flow. However, modeling crowd turbulence in a high-dimensional hyperbolic system remains challenging. Consequently, the model was extended to incorporate a mixed-type system for multidirectional pedestrian flow, which explicitly considered the phase transition of different anticipation characteristics under varying densities. Non-hyperbolicity was utilized to model the strong instabilities during crowd turbulence. Additionally, by estimating the aggregated crowd pressure in a heterogeneous crowd, the proposed model was able to elucidate the effects of both force chains and panic sentiment, phenomena commonly observed during crowd disasters. This model was formulated as a non-hyperbolic partial differential equations system embedded with an appropriate set of eikonal equations. To achieve Objective 3, efficient numerical schemes were developed to solve the dynamic macroscopic models. Both aforementioned models are systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) that describe the evolution of pedestrian density and velocity fields over time and space. The continuity equation set in the unidirectional model, which strictly adhered to the hyperbolic law, was numerically solved using the characteristic-wise third-order Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory (WENO3) scheme with flux splitting to discretize space. Meanwhile, the third-order total variation diminishing (TVD) Runge-Kutta method was employed for time integration. The aggregated pressure equation consists of two eikonal equations corresponding to different regions based on the movement characteristics. The solution of the eikonal equation set is not unique. Therefore, the fast sweeping method was initially applied to seek an approximation of the continuous solution, which is the physically relevant solution, and then the Gauss-Seidel iterations could be applied simultaneously to the two eikonal equations, as the pushing pressure term is continuous when sweeping from one region to another. Numerical examples demonstrated that the computational scheme was convergent and capable of effectively describing the evolution of pedestrian dynamics, analyzing pushing pressure in panic states, and verifying the stability condition. In the case of modeling crowd pressure and crowd turbulence in multidirectional scenarios, traditional numerical methods were not applicable for solving the PDE sets due to the presence of non-hyperbolicity. To address this challenge, the numerical solver was extended to incorporate the mixed-type finite difference method. This method, which considers the phase transition between hyperbolicity and non-hyperbolicity, was used for the approximation of the numerical fluxes. In the hyperbolic region, the eigenvalues of the Jacobi matrix are real and unique, and the numerical fluxes are approximated through the traditional local Lax-Friedrichs scheme on the characteristic space. In the non-hyperbolic region, the Jacobi matrix becomes singular, and the traditional Lax-Friedrichs splitting is not applicable. Therefore, in order to capture instability in this multidimensional problem, a new splitting scheme was developed based on the requirements of non-singularity after Lax-Friedrichs splitting. The above numerical schemes were developed for rectangular grid mesh, which limits their applications to real-world geometric settings with non-rectangular domains. To efficiently model real-life complex computational regions, high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods on unstructured triangular meshes were developed to solve the conservation law, and a second-order fast-sweeping scheme was employed to solve the eikonal equations. In general, numerical schemes commonly applied to low-density regions may yield negative pedestrian density, leading to nonphysical solutions and simulation blow-ups. To address this problem, a high-order positivity-preserving limiter was incorporated while maintaining the order of accuracy for the numerical scheme. Numerical examples were shown to demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed solution algorithm. The numerical results validated the reliability of the proposed numerical method and highlighted the advantages of triangular meshes. The effectiveness of the dynamic continuum models was validated through their application to real crowd disasters. The multidirectional model was applied to the 2010 Love Parade crowd disaster, which occurred on July 24, 2010, in Duisburg, causing 21 fatalities and 652 injuries. This application demonstrates the model's effectiveness in reproducing the important features of the observed crowd: high density, high pressure, and crowd turbulence in the real-world context. The simulation results were consistent with the empirical observations.

17201318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201318.value: A critical review of the existing literature on crowd force was conducted, which provided useful guidance for experiment design, model development, and practical applications related to crowd force [C1]. Control experiments were performed on a 1.5-m-wide ring corridor and a single-file circular track to investigate the observational characteristics of pedestrian flows under high-density conditions [J1]. Interesting properties of high-density crowd, such as lane formation processes, were observed. To further understand the interactive mechanisms among pedestrians and their interactions with cyclists in a crowd, experiments were conducted at the micro-characteristics level [J4, J9]. To describe panicked crowd behavior in a walking environment with reduced visibility, such as during the dark hours or in a smoke-filled room during emergency evacuation, control experiments were conducted in a confined space. These experiments provided valuable insights for the design of evacuation scenarios [J2]. These experimental works offered insights into the development of dynamic macroscopic models for high-density crowds under panicked conditions. Critical reviews on the analytical properties of dynamic macroscopic models were conducted, offering useful insights about the capability of the continuum approach to pedestrian modeling [J6]. A dynamic macroscopic model that explicitly considered psychological pressure and physical pressure was developed and solved using an efficient numerical scheme based on WENO3 and fast sweeping methods [J5]. The pedestrian route choice decisions can be effectively described based on the concept of potential field for overcrowded pedestrian flow [J3], an important concept that is effective in guiding both pedestrian movement directions and aggregated pushing forces along a force chain in a high-density crowd. To address the challenging problem of crowd turbulence in real crowd disasters, this model was extended to a mixed-type continuum model for multidirectional pedestrian flow, which explicitly considered the phase transition of different anticipation characteristics under various densities [J8]. Non-hyperbolicity was used to model the strong instabilities during crowd turbulence. The resulting non-hyperbolic partial differential equations were solved using the mixed-type finite difference method. The case study of the 2010 Love Parade crowd disaster further demonstrated the usefulness of the developed dynamic continuum crowd model in unraveling the causes of crowd disasters in panic situations. To enhance the applicability of these models for real-world scenarios, numerical schemes based on a more general triangular mesh structure were established [J7, C2]. This provides a versatile and useful tool for formulating effective risk management schemes to reduce the chances of stampede crowd disasters in mass gatherings.

17201318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201318.value: This study demonstrated the significance of pedestrian dynamics and behavior in crowd disasters during panic situations. While the developed models and solution algorithms offer valuable tools, further research is necessary. Ethical constraints preclude field experiments on panicked crowds, so some parameters in this study were based on empirical studies that did not explicitly explain the causes of panic sentiment. To enhance applicability, these parameters must be calibrated through carefully designed control experiments that effectively capture pedestrian behavior in extreme yet safe conditions. These experiments allow the examination of pushing capacity and physical pressure using stationary and wearable pressure sensors, and the monitoring of crowd movements. This information can reveal the specific conditions that give rise to panic in diverse crowd density and pressure scenarios. The models and numerical procedures that will be developed to encompass crowd dynamics in the process of building up panic conditions will enable the formulation and evaluation of risk-level indicators. This will assist implementation of effective crowd management strategies. Drawing on the knowledge acquired from this project, a research proposal addressing these issues in panicked crowd dynamics research will be submitted to the Research Grants Council's General Research Fund.

17201318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201318.value: As cities grow and more people gather for big events, large crowds are becoming increasingly common. These crowds can be dangerous, making it difficult to walk and sometimes even leading to disasters. When too many people gather in one place, they can push against each other, creating significant force and pressure. In smaller crowds, the force from people pushing against each other may not be a problem. However, in larger crowds, the combined force can be overwhelming for an individual to handle. This research examines how forces and pressure build up in crowds, helping to predict when dangerous situations, such as suffocation from being crushed or stampedes, might occur. The study focuses on how people in a crowd behave when they panic, using a method that helps to understand the crowd as a whole. This method can aid in finding solutions for controlling crowds and evacuating people safely during emergencies. The findings from this research can be utilized to create improved ways to manage crowds and design spaces for large events, reducing the chances of stampedes, crushing, and other crowd disasters. This will ultimately help save lives and lessen the suffering of those who survive such incidents.

17201818.label: Project Objectives
17201818.value: Our first, and main, objective is in the development of advanced computational algorithms to enhance the image quality. In particular, we will focus on increasing the spatial and depth resolution, and suppressing the noise contamination to the holograms. The challenge involves not only in formulating the appropriate inverse imaging problem and incorporation of the image prior, but also in efficient iterative schemes for practical convergence and robustness. We target to achieve this objective through accurate mathematical modeling of the imaging system, extensive simulation to compare different algorithms and parameter choices, and experiments with real data, with appropriate metrics to measure resolution and noise levels. Our second objective focuses on the digital inline holography system capability. Since it may be the only microscopic imaging tool available in many deployment scenarios, we want to make it as versatile as possible. One aspect of this objective is to achieve high dynamic range imaging, enabled by a combination of controlling the light source and experimenting with new electronic sensors, such as the quanta image sensor with single-photon sensitivity. Another aspect is the imaging speed. We target to shorten both the capture time and the data processing time, where the former requires extensive investigation in the tradeoff with the signal-to-noise ratio, and the latter needs exploration with dedicated computing hardware such as graphical processing units. Our third objective is on deployment of our computational holography system for an actual application. Our target is for water quality assessment, and to achieve this objective we aim to collect a variety of water samples, with different levels of cleanliness and amount of microbiological organisms, and benchmark with lab-based tools. The comparison will be qualitative or subjective in nature; if time permits, we will begin to explore an automated system that has the potential for round-the-clock monitoring.

17201818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201818.value: Digital holographic imaging systems capture the complex optical wavefront of an object, preserving valuable information in the hologram for visualization and analysis. Many digital holography configurations have been developed over the years; unfortunately, most require advanced optical instrumentation, confining their use primarily to scientific research in laboratories. In recent years, digital inline holography (DIH), arguably the simplest holographic setup, has found its way in portable systems, with the goal of providing point-of-care diagnostics. DIH only requires a spatially coherent light source and an electronic detector but no lenses, making it an attractive option for an inexpensive imaging system. In essence, DIH records the interference of the wave from the light source and the object wave, and computational algorithms are used subsequently to recover a digital image from the hologram. Image quality and system capability are two critical areas we aim to improve in this research proposal. For the former, we develop advanced computational techniques to tackle two main problems: resolution and noise. DIH is capable of providing wide field-of-view imaging, but its resolution is limited by the detector pixel size, because the object is placed almost directly atop the sensor surface. While recent research indicates that fusing multiple observations or making use of image prior can increase the spatial resolution, there is room for further improvement by leveraging on recent advances in inverse imaging. With regard to noise, speckle is a ubiquitous phenomenon with coherent imaging. It can be suppressed by optical or digital means, where the latter involves modeling it as a multiplicative Rayleigh-distributed noise, which is then log-transformed to additive noise for removal. Similarly, we aim to achieve better speckle suppression by direct methods taking advantage of recent development in Gaussian denoising. For the latter, which is on expanding DIH system capability, we have a custom design in mind with a twofold focus. The first is to deliver a high dynamic range holographic imaging, through a combination of controlling the light source and experimenting with new electronic sensors, such as the quanta image sensor with single-photon sensitivity. The second is on imaging speed, where we seek to minimize both the capture time and the data processing time. The former requires extensive experimentation in the tradeoff with noise, and the latter needs exploration with dedicated computing hardware. The target application for our DIH system will be in water quality assessment through imaging the microbiological contaminants. 數字全息成像系統記錄物體的複雜光學波，保留全息圖中有價值信息以用於可視化和分析。多年來，許多數字全息系統已經開發，可惜大多數都需要先進的光學儀器，以致主要只能用於實驗室的科學研究。近年來，數字在線全息術，可以說是最簡單的全息設置，已經在便攜式系統中確立目標提供即時診斷。這技術僅需要同調光源和電子探測器，但不需要透鏡，這使其成為有吸引力的廉價成像系統。本質上，數字在線全息術記錄來自光源和物體波的干擾，並且隨後使用計算算法從全息圖恢復數字圖像。 圖像質量和系統能力是我們在本研究計劃中旨在改進的兩個關鍵領域。對於前者，我們開發先進的計算技術來解決兩個主要問題：分辨率和噪聲。數字在線全息術能夠提供寬視場成像，但其分辨率受探測器像素大小的限制，因為物體幾乎直接放置在傳感器表面的頂部。雖然最近的研究表明融合多次觀察或利用先前的圖像可以提高空間分辨率，但通過利用逆成像的最新進展，仍有進一步改進的空間。關於噪聲，散斑是相干成像普遍存在的現象。它可以通過光學或計算來抑制，後者包括將其建模為乘法瑞利分佈噪聲，然後將其轉換為加性噪聲以便去除。同樣，我們的目標是利用最近在高斯去噪中的發展，通過直接方法實現更好的散斑抑制。對於後者，即擴展全息系統能力，我們有兩個目標。第一是通過控制光源和試驗新的電子傳感器，例如具有單光子靈敏度的量子圖像傳感器，提供高動態範圍的全息成像。第二是成像速度，我們尋求最小化捕獲時間和數據處理時間。前者需要在與噪聲的權衡中進行廣泛的實驗，而後者需要使用專用計算硬件進行探索。數字在線全息系統的目標應用是通過對微生物污染物進行成像來進行水質評估。

17201818.label: Realisation of objectives
17201818.value: This project consists of 3 objectives: development of advanced computational algorithms to enhance the image quality of lensless digital inline holography, increasing both the spatial and depth resolution as well as suppressing the noise contamination; enhancing the holographic system capability through increasing the detector sensitivity and imaging speed, which includes both capture and data processing time; and application of the lensless digital inline holography system for imaging of micro-organisms and objects. These objectives have been realized with the conclusion of this project. Regarding the first objective, we reported a 75% completion in the mid-term progress report. Specifically, we have developed computational algorithms that could effectively suppress the speckle noise that was common in digital holography. Further work during the second half of the project focused on improving the image quality under various conditions. Robustness is an important aspect, as practical systems invariably need to deal with various imperfections. We investigated and developed methods to enhance the robustness of lensless imaging by explicitly taking the model mismatch into account in the algorithm, and pushed the incorporation of the physics of imaging systems and the learning-based methods that could further strengthen the holographic reconstruction. The results were published in an IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging paper (see the list of publications in the section below). Regarding the second objective, we reported a 20% completion in the mid-term progress report. We had envisioned the use of an advanced imaging sensor to increase the detection sensitivity. Unfortunately, due to the unforeseen global pandemic, much of the experimental work in the lab was met with delays. Nevertheless, in the meantime, we were able to adjust our work plan to first push forward different computational schemes to improve the data processing. Subsequently, we also developed learning methods that were particularly tuned to low light imaging, and handled the difficult scattering issue through a novel polarization multiplexing scheme in holography, effectively enhancing the sensitivity of existing imaging detectors. These were reported in the two conference papers presented in 2021, with journal papers reporting our continuous development in these areas currently underway. Regarding the third objective, we reported a 30% completion in the mid-term progress report. Further along our earlier investigations, we had focused on imaging microplastics using digital holographic microscopy. This turned out to be a very fruitful study, and through this we had attracted collaborations with many domain experts who advised us on the importance and challenges of combating microplastic pollution. One of the first work we published was on microplastic pollution monitoring with holographic classification and deep learning, in collaboration with a colleague in the Centre for Water Technology and Policy in the Department of Civil Engineering. We reported on a deep learning-based holographic classification method that computes directly on the raw holographic data to extract quantitative information of the microplastic pollutants in order to classify them according to the extent of the pollution. Because our system does not contain bulky optical devices, it has the potential to be further developed into a portable microplastics detection system, facilitating the monitoring of microplastic particle pollution in the ecological environment.

17201818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201818.value: In this project, the major findings and research outcome center on demonstrating that computational optical imaging approach can greatly benefit lensless digital inline holography. It is generally accepted that this holographic setup is simple and can be built without bulky or costly optical devices, yet the resulting holograms suffer from some image quality degradations such as speckle noise. Consequently, its use is rather limited. Here, we show with a series of work that by explicitly taking into account the physical imaging process in a learning-based reconstruction scheme, we are able to suppress such noise while also enhancing the resolution of the reconstruction images. We developed various possible algorithms for different situations, and in particular, we also demonstrated that we could explicitly incorporate the model mismatch in the algorithm as well to enhance its robustness. In terms of applications, we have focused on imaging micro-objects, specifically microplastics, and argued that its simple design would facilitate the development into a portable system, which could benefit a lot in field study.

17201818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201818.value: The research has room for further development on a couple of directions. In terms of computational algorithms, there remains a lot of work that can done, particularly in reducing the data-driven training. In recent years, there have been various approaches in the artificial intelligence and computer vision community in generative model, zero-shot learning, and transfer learning, all aiming to reduce the need for a large amount of data. Adapting these approaches for holographic imaging will be a promising direction. In terms of applications, we have only touched the surface of harnessing holographic imaging for microplastics. Further development will focus on obtaining more parameters of the microplastics, such as the size, density, morphology, etc, under more challenging aquatic environments. In addition, the ultimate goal is to build a portable holographic system that can be brought to field use, which will further its impact on environmental protection and sustainability.

17201818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201818.value: Digital holography is a special form of imaging that can provide a volumetric information of an object. There are various holographic setups, with a lensless inline holography being one of the simplest, which does not require bulky or costly optical components. However, the image quality is usually less satisfactory. This project seeks to develop a set of computation methods to achieve higher resolution and less noise in the reconstructed images. These methods combine the modeling of the imaging system with various data used to training the processing. Furthermore, we also incorporate model mismatch to enhance the system robustness. The resulting system is being demonstrated in imaging microplastics, which shows its advantages in assessing pollution due to these small plastic fragments.

17202318.label: Project Objectives

We will make Kakute support diverse big-data queries on large, popular datasets, and we will make Kakute incur reasonable performance overhead compared to native, insecure queries. [To create a Fine-grained Differential Privacy (FDP) technique for private clouds] We will leverage Kakute to develop FDP and its new algorithms, which will only add noise to sensitive data fields or query results, preserving strong differential privacy for sensitive data and good accuracy for most results. [To construct the first compiler for big-data privacy in public clouds] Our compiler will support unmodified big-data frameworks by creating a thin, verified translator that automatically translates Java bytecode to SGX-compatible code. We will quantitatively evaluate the performance overhead of our compiler and whether it can protect data privacy against real-world privileged attacks.

17202318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202318.value: 在这个大数据的时代，很多商业公司（比如Uber）存储他们的数据在云上。同时，商业公司和他们的第三方合作伙伴用自定义查询（比如MapReduce）来处理数据，导致了两个严重的大数据隐私泄漏问题。第一，第三方公司容易把数据记录中的敏感字段（比如Uber记录中的信用卡）通过查询而偷去。第二，粗心或者恶意的云提供商（比如Amazon）可以偷看正在查询的数据。 这个计划目的就在于提升大数据的隐私。我提出一个全盘策略：用户们仍然可以使用以往的大数据查询，而我这个计划会在运行时自动地防止大数据隐私的泄漏。我提出三大目标。 第一，为了约束恶意的第三方公司，我会构建Kakute，第一个大数据的流跟踪系统。Kakute将会提供容易使用的API给商业公司标记他们认为是隐私或者敏感的数据字段，然后Kakute会自动地运行以往的大数据查询，自动地跟踪敏感字段的流向，从而避免敏感数据流向查询结果。目前的流跟踪系统的一个挑战就是，跟踪计算密集型的查询的敏感字段是非常低效的（比如，一个有名的流跟踪系统在运行大数据查询时，性能落差是不安全的查询的128倍）。我将会挖掘大数据查询中的一些深度的特性，创建两个新的标记传播和跟踪技术。我们的Kakute原型已经发表在ACSAC 2017国际会议上，发表结果表明，我们的技术的性能落差仅比不安全的查询满了32.3%。 第二，我将会构建一个新的“精细化差分隐私”技术和它的新算法。在约束第三方公司方面，Kakute和差分隐私技术是互相促进的，因为查分隐私技术允许数据的聚合计算，通过在计算结果添加随机噪声，而避免单个人的数据暴露在查询结果中。不幸地是，已有的差分隐私技术是粗糙的：他们经常会很保守地添加过多的噪声在数据结果中，使得结果不可用，因为他们不知道是那些敏感的数据字段流向了哪些计算结果。通过把Kakute和差分隐私技术相结合，我们的精细化查分隐私技术将会只在计算结果的敏感部分添加噪声，既有效地隐藏了敏感数据，有极大地提升了计算结果的可用性。 第三，为了约束恶意的云提供商，我将会利用先进的Intel SGX安全硬件技术来构建第一个隐私保障的大数据查询引擎。这个引擎可以使用已有的查询，不需修改。已有的基于SGX的大数据查询引擎有两个问题。第一，他们不得不重新编写已有的Java查询来符合SGX的C++标准。第二，他们运行在SGX的可信模块过大（比如需要把整个JVM跑在SGX里面），使得安全隐患大。为了解决这些挑战，我的新系统将只会把大数据查询本身一小段代码跑在SGX里面，使用一个小型的运行时翻译引擎。这个新系统既可以重用已有的Java大数据查询，又可以保证很小的可信模块。 这个计划的成功，将会极大地提升云中大数据计算的隐私和性能，使得绝大多数人受益。

17202618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202618.value: One of today’s major environmental challenges is the occurrence of heat waves or extreme heats in many large cities. Urban extreme heat events have already become the most prominent weather-related hazard. Although heat wave atmospheric conditions are mainly caused by large-scale circulations, the urban thermal climate is also known to be significantly affected by local urban factors such as the city’s morphology and anthropogenic heat and moisture, otherwise known as the urban heat island phenomenon. We propose to study how a newly identified local warming mechanism worsens the local effects of regional warming in the urban areas of Kowloon, Hong Kong, a dense high-rise city. A surprising characteristic was observed in the daily urban temperature profiles during some recent extreme heat events in Kowloon. The urban daytime maximum air temperature there is known to be generally lower than that in rural areas due to the significant urban thermal storage effect. In the June 2016 extreme heat event, however, the opposite occurred, that is, the city’s maximum air temperatures increased and became greater than those in rural areas. Our preliminary studies revealed a possible new synergistic warming mechanism. The increasing urbanisation in Kowloon in the 2010s has produced an urban heat/moist island circulation or heat dome that is sufficiently large to enhance the foehn wind – a downslope warm and drying mountain wind – from Lion Rock Mountain. The foehn wind is assisted by the heat dome to overcome the cooler westerly sea breeze, which provides additional urban heating and has led to record high temperatures in Kowloon. We propose to carry out detailed laboratory modelling and numerical simulations under ideal two-dimensional settings to explore and isolate the major influencing factors and parameters in the interaction of the wind trio: a sea breeze, a foehn wind and a heat dome. We will also consider three-dimensional ideal settings with gap flows, and with realistic morphology under both ideal and realistic weather conditions. We will use forward- and backward-trajectory methods to investigate the origin of the foehn air and the contribution of adiabatic and diabatic processes for the suspected foehn events. We will also explore one possible mitigation method to weaken the heat dome circulation and thereby weaken the synergistic warming, namely, reduction of anthropogenic heat sources with the use of alternative air conditioning systems and electric vehicles. Our study will illuminate the mitigation of urban heat waves in cities with similar coastal settings. 當今的主要環境挑戰之一是許多大城市出現熱浪或極端高溫。城市極端高溫事件已成為最突出的與天氣有關的危害。雖然熱浪大氣條件主要是由大尺度環流引起的，但城市熱氣候也受到當地城市因素的顯著影響，如城市形態和人為熱量，比如城市熱島現象。我們將研究一個最近發現的局部變暖機制是如何影響香港九龍城市地區的極端高溫事件。 在九龍最近發生的幾個極端高溫事件中，日城市溫度曲線出現了奇怪的特徵。由於城市蓄熱效應顯著，九龍市區白天最高氣溫一般都低於農村地區。然而，在2016年6月的極端高溫事件中，相反的情況發生，即市區白天最高氣溫增加並且大於農村地區。我們的初步研究揭示了一種可能的新的協同變暖機制。 2010年以來，香港城市化程度不斷提高，城市熱/濕島環流或熱穹窿不斷增大，達到足以增強來自獅子山的焚風 。即一個下坡溫暖和乾燥的山風 。焚風通過穹窿風而加強，抵禦涼爽的西向海風，這提供了額外的城市暖化，從而導致九龍極端高溫紀錄。 我們建議首先在理想的二維設置下進行詳細的實驗室建模和數值模擬，以探索和分離三重風（海風，焚風和熱穹窿）相互作用中的主要影響因素和參數。我們還將考慮具有間隙流的三維理想設置，以及在理想和真實天氣條件的作用。我們將使用前向和後向軌跡方法來研究焚風的起源以及絕熱和非絕熱過程對可疑焚風的貢獻。我們還將探索一種可能減緩方法，以減弱城市熱/濕島環流，從而減弱協同變暖機制，即使用替代空調系統和電動車輛減少人為熱源。我們的研究可能將有利於相似沿海城市的城市熱浪緩解。

17202618.label: Realisation of objectives
17202618.value: Objective 1: To understand the interaction of mountain flows, sea breeze and urban heat/moisture island circulation at ideal settings (Tasks 1 - 3) Our conceptualized simple model of the interacting mountain flows, sea breeze and urban heat/moisture island circulation represents a costal hilly urban setting such as Kowloon in Hong Kong. The most significant finding is the recent identification of a new potential “downstream blocking” synergistic mechanism for urban warming in such as setting. The interaction of the downward mountain flows and the urban circulation “blocks” the urban air flows at the downstream flow of the mountain at certain background winds. Certain background winds transform mountain slope winds to foehn-like winds. These adverse effects are exacerbated in the presence of urban heat island circulation (UHIC) and sea breezes in Kowloon. This potential warming mechanism would lead to long-lasting high temperature afternoons in urban areas, during which the region with the highest temperature experiences the lowest wind speed. Our new theory termed “downstream blocking” clarifies how air masses descend after passing a mountain ridge when a downwind urban heat island exists. This study follows an earlier finding of the urban circulation blockage due to upstream wind. Here the UHICs were simulated over circular cities of the same size arranged in tandem or side by side with respect to the background wind direction, at different spacing distances. The study analyzed the flow structures and city ventilation arising from thermally driven UHICs and background wind. The arrangements of the cities have a significant modifying effect on the interaction between UHICs and winds. As the spacing distance increases, the city ventilation improves slightly. In the tandem arrangement, a chain flow is formed between UHICs at a spacing distance of between 0.5 and 1.5 times the city diameter. An upstream UHIC blocks the incoming wind flow to the downstream city, which results in a ventilation deficiency. This somehow resembles the “downstream blocking” synergistic mechanism as discovered later in Zhang et al (in review). A journal paper has been published, Wang Q, Fan Y, Hang J & Li Y 2019. Interacting urban heat island circulations as affected by weak background wind. Building and Environment, vol. 160, 106224. The second journal paper is submitted to Urban Climate, in review. Zhang C, Wang Q, Chan PW, Li Y*. Potential “downstream blocking” synergistic mechanism for urban warming in kowloon Peninsula, Hong Kong. Urban Climate. In review Objective 2: To investigate the development of foehn winds in semi-ideal settings by exploring the gap flows and wind blocking in the complex morphological setting of Hong Kong. (Tasks 4-5) In Objective 1 and an earlier GRF project, we presented related findings on various “complex” urban shape on UHICs. Here we analzyed the complex 3D settings of Kowloon peninsula with mountains and gaps to the east and northeast under various background wind conditions. The evolution and interaction of UHICs, sea-land breeze circulation and mountain circulation under calm weather conditions were also studied and compared. We also examined a large number of weather photos of Kowloon to identify cloud locations and evaluate our predicted urban plumes and explored the association between background wind and spatial air temperature distribution in Kowloon. Northeasterly wind conditions can lead to high temperatures at the foothills of mountains situated northeast of Kowloon due to the downstream blocking synergistic mechanism; a streamline analysis showed that heat advection accounts for this phenomenon during the day, while a possible foehn-like wind plays an important role at night. One journal paper has been recently submitted to Urban Climate (in review). Zhang C, Wang Q, Chan PW, Li Y*. Why do northeasterly winds make Kowloon warmer? Urban Climate, in review. Objective 3: To evaluate air conditioning and electric vehicle options as possible mitigation methods. (Task 6). Our major contribution is in discovering the urban warming is not due to higher air temperature, but more importantly the related urban moisture island (UMI). This has important implication in mitigation. In Wang et al (2019), we found a more significant rising trend in humidity than in temperature in Hong Kong. We analyzed the change in the equivalent temperature which reveals a larger contribution by moisture than sensible temperature. This is done by developing a new and integrated simple lumped moisture/heat model for the hourly urban air humidity. The effect of anthropogenic heat/moisture such as due to buildings and vehicles is considered. In addition to the anthropogenic heat/moisture, a weakened wind environment increases urban air moisture. Following our new downstream blocking mechanism, the wind weakening is not only due to urban building blockage, but due to UHIC blockage. Larger building anthropogenic heat increases UHI and UHIC, while UHI impacts on building energy use. The two cannot be isolated. We examined how the climate and building cooling load in summer interact in a collaborative effort (Shi et al., 2019). Our heat/moisture combined approach is applied. In Shi et al (2019), we recognized that the UMI effect on latent energy was underexplored. We thus investigated the intensity of UHI and UMI, and its impacts on the sensible and latent cooling demand of residential buildings in summer in Hong Kong. Firstly, a ten-year weather dataset from 2004–2013 for the six stations selected based on the local climate zone (LCZ) scheme was analysed. Both UHI and UMI coexist during summer nights but as cooling and dry islands during daytime, and the nocturnal UHI and UMI intensity vary significantly with different LCZs. The urban building shows a higher sensible cooling demand, approximately twice that of the comparative rural one, and the latent cooling demand could be up to 96% higher. 17202618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202618.value: The urban heat island (UHI) phenomenon is known to be caused by the anthropogenic heat, trapped solar heat, weakened wind removal due to blockage and other factors. In this project, we explored the interaction of sea-land breeze, and mountain (foehn) winds and UHI circulation (UHIC). When there is sea breeze (mainly southwest) and mountain (foehn) winds (mainly northeast), interaction with UHIC occurs with diurnal variation. Our major new finding is “downstream blocking” synergistic mechanism for urban warming in such as a setting. Certain background winds transform mountain slope winds to foehn-like winds. Our new finding clarifies how air masses descend after passing a mountain ridge when a downwind UHI exists. These adverse effects are exacerbated in the presence of UHIC and sea breezes in Kowloon. This potential warming mechanism seems to lead to long-lasting high temperature afternoons in urban areas, during which the region with the highest temperature experiences the lowest wind speed. Hence a new urban-scale factor for the occurrence of urban warming is identified, which weakens the urban wind and trapped urban heat/moisture. Such “downstream blocking” does not exist when UHIC is weak. The blocking effect of UHIC at intermediate wind was already found in our early study, and in this project, we also explored two circular cities at various distance as affected by background winds. In the tandem arrangement, a chain flow is formed between UHICs at a spacing distance of between 0.5 and 1.5 times the city diameter. An upstream UHIC blocks the incoming wind flow to the downstream city. Our second major contribution is the co-occurrence of UHI and urban moisture island (UMI). Urban warming is not only due to higher air temperature, but more importantly the related urban moisture island (UMI). We found a more significant rising trend in humidity than in temperature in Hong Kong. Analysis of the yearly change in the diurnal equivalent temperature reveals a larger contribution by moisture than heat. In addition to the anthropogenic heat/moisture due to buildings and vehicles, a weakened wind environment increases urban air moisture. Larger building anthropogenic heat increases UHI and UHIC, while UHI impacts on building energy use. Following our new downstream blocking mechanism, the wind weakening is also due to UHIC blockage. This has important implication in mitigation. Our study reveals the need of not only reducing anthropogenic heat/moisture, improving urban ventilation, but also considering the urban scale air flow interaction.

17202618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202618.value: Close building plumes interact and produce urban plumes. Stratification further leads it to urban dome (urban heat island circulation). Urban heat island circulation interacts with sea breeze and mountain (foehn) winds of similar length scale. The synergistic city scale “downstream” blockage provides a new mechanism for weakening urban wind weakening and trapping urban heat/moisture. One immediate implication lies in the city scale mitigation, i.e. reducing urban heat island circulation for urban heat island mitigation. Our development has the potential to be used for city planning and design. Urban heat island phenomenon cannot be mitigated by considering each individual building and vehicle and urban planning alone, but considering the local and regional climate interaction with urban climate. The downstream blockage impacts not only the urban heat/moisture island, but also air pollution. Different what commonly believed that zero background winds lead to the worst urban warming and polluting, but immediate winds interact with urban heat island circulation with wind blockage. Rapid coastal urbanization in China mean an increased number and intensity of large city heat domes. These heat domes might explain the wind weakening phenomenon in parts of China. Further study is being planned on how to design and build a city.

17202818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202818.value: Effective integration of transit and land-use is considered an important component in accomplishing a sustainable urban future for both developed and developing cities. Urban leaders are encouraged to invest in metro systems in order to reduce car-dependency, promote low carbon mobility and boost smarter urban growth. Transit investment is also expected to reshape urban form by encouraging transit-oriented development (TOD), enhancing compact development, and reducing urban sprawl. However, past research on global experiences has indicated that these land-use outcomes may not happen as expected. Although Hong Kong has run a relatively young metro system (called mass transit railway - MTR) since 1979, the World Bank praises it as one of the ‘global best-case examples of transit and land-use integration’. This, however, refers to the approach of value capture by the MTR Corporation in aggressively engaging in joint development around its metro station areas and using property incomes to subsidize metro investment. What has been less examined is about how the MTR has influenced private land development near but outside the metro station areas. The metro system is widely believed to have transformed the urban land-use pattern of Hong Kong during the past four decades. Is this belief valid? Spatial clustering and interdependence of land-uses in an urban environment imply that private land development decisions are subject to a complex influence of many factors, in addition to site accessibility to metro services. Recent advancement in spatial modelling techniques enables a more rigorous investigation of these issues. This research aims at evaluating private land-use development decisions along three urban metro corridors in Hong Kong. This proposal expands the dataset of a previous GRF study completed by the Principal Investigator, and uses new quantitative methods (supplemented by expert consultations) to identify the real impacts of metro transit in reconfiguring the land-use structure of the main urban districts in Hong Kong. This study will contribute to the spatial econometrics literature and enrich our understanding about the transformative effects of metro system on the urban built environment and property development. Insofar as Hong Kong is concerned, this research has some practical values as new metro lines are being proposed under the government’s “Railway Development Strategy”. Metro lines are widely expected to be able to combat urban decay by encouraging urban regeneration and redevelopment of urban sites. This investigation can provide useful insights in informing policy about the connection between metro transit and urban renewal. 交通運輸和土地使用的有效整合，被認為是實現可持續未來城市發展的重要組成部分。城市領導者往往希望通過投資地鐵系統，以減少對汽車的依賴，促進低碳出行，促進智慧城市發展，並通過鼓勵公交導向型發展（TOD），促進緊湊型發展和減少城市擴張。然而，預計公交投資可以重塑城市形態的想法，在過去不少城市的研究中表明，這些土地利用結果可能不會按預期發生。 香港自1979年以來開始運行地鐵系統，世界銀行稱讚它是“全球最佳運輸和土地使用一體化案例之一”。然而，這是指地鐵公司積極參與其地鐵站區域的聯合開發，以及利用房地產收入補貼地鐵投資的價值捕獲 (value capture) 營運方法。較少受到關注的是地鐵如何影響地鐵站附近但在地鐵站外的私人土地開發。人們普遍認為，地鐵系統在過去四十年中改變了香港的城市土地利用格局。這種信念有效嗎？除了地鐵效應之外，城市環境中土地利用的空間集聚和相互依賴意味著私人土地開發決策受到許多複雜的因素影響。 空間建模技術的最新進展可以為這些研究問題進行更嚴格的分析。這項研究旨在評估香港三條城市地鐵走廊的私人土地用途發展決策，通過擴大了首席研究員先前完成的GRF研究的數據集，並使用新的定量方法（輔以專家諮詢），來確定地鐵運輸在重新配置香港主要城區的土地使用結構方面的實際影響。 這項研究將不僅充實有關於空間計量經濟學文獻，並豐富我們對地鐵系統如何影響城市建築環境和房地產開發的理解。就香港而言，這項研究也具有一些實用價值，因為在政府的“鐵路發展策略”下提出了新的地鐵線路。人們普遍預計地鐵線路可以鼓勵城市更新和城市重建來對抗城市衰退，這項研究可以為有關地鐵交通與城市更新之間聯繫的政策提供有用的見解。

17203418.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203418.value: 電子廢棄物之金屬零排放處理目標: 控制金屬於陶瓷玻璃中的分化型態

17203418.label: Project Objectives
17203418.value: This project aims to control metal speciation and distributions of Cr, Cu, Pb and Zn by thermal reactions to enhance the metal recovery and stabilization of e-waste residue. The main challenge is the identification of metal hosting phases derived from the complicated matrix reactions in e-waste residue. High resolution X-ray diffraction and electron diffraction skills will be the keys to reveal the reaction processes among different metal hosting phases and to utilize the partitioning of glass and ceramic phases to separate target metals. Based on the high resolution X-ray diffraction data, atomic structure models needed for quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis will be constructed for the start-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analyses (fundamental parameter approach and precise amorphous content quantification with internal standards) to quantify the metal distributions in the systems. Our new technical development of combining the Rietveld refinement results and the elemental information from transmission electron microscopy will further quantify metal occupancy ratios in the different coordination positions of the crystalline and glass phases. The stability of target metals in their hosting phases is closely related to the crystal parameters. The modeling of Rietveld structural refinement and the measurement by electron diffraction technique will provide the lattice parameters, cation distributions, crystal sizes, defects, and impurities of the metal phases generated from thermally treating the e-waste residue with different glass-ceramic precursors. The roles of sintering additives will also be evaluated to observe their influences on the crystal structures of metal hosting phases and their effects on the promotion of metal speciation in glass-ceramics. Metal extractability and immobilization effects will be quantified by phase separation outcomes and leaching experiments. Characterization tools targeting on probing surface and interfacial reactions, such as small-angle X-ray diffraction, atomic force microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, will further delineate the metal leaching behavior and reaction pathways. The relationship between the glass-ceramic microstructures and the resulting grain boundary features will be investigated by high resolution electron microscopy (FESEM and HRTEM) to assist the control of metal release and incorporation behavior. The preferred nano- and micro-structural features will be designed for the intermediate and final products in e-waste recovery and immobilization processing. With the unambiguous understanding of the reaction mechanisms, phase compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics in this study, the control of metal speciation and grain boundary features will provide new opportunities for reaching more reactive sites and larger available surfaces to optimize metal recovery efficiency and stabilization effect.

17203418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203418.value: The unprecedented manufacture and use of electrical/electronic devices has generated a significant amount of electronic waste (e-waste), and the associated discharge of hazardous metals such as chromium (Cr), copper (Cu), lead (Pb) and zinc (Zn) has created a new and urgent environmental problem. The global generation of e-waste has reached 50 million tons annually and is continuing with a strong increasing trend. Mechanical separation and solution leaching methods are currently used to achieve ~80% recycling efficiency for e-waste, but this is still far from the goal of zero pollutant discharge to safeguard our environment. Continuing technological development to recover valuable materials is a must, but many recovery methods also generate treatment residue laden with hazardous metals. Therefore, technological breakthroughs to further extract metals from e-waste processing/treatment residue and to reliably stabilize metals in final products are needed to achieve zero pollutant discharge. Under different thermal conditions, crystalline (ceramic) and non-crystalline (glass) phases have been found to release or incorporate certain hazardous metals at the atomic and nanometer scales. This finding provides us with opportunities to further extract metals unreachable by conventional solution leaching methods (mostly relying on heterogeneous surface-limited reactions) and securely incorporate metals by the more durable mineral phases and the double-barrier (through both ceramic and glass structures) immobilization mechanism. Metal speciation behavior and metal hosting phases are highly relevant to matrix compositions and thermal conditions. For example, we found that metallic lead could be successfully extracted from the lead glass network at 700C when zero-valent iron presented, but lead could also be securely stabilized in the melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9) structure at 850C when both iron and silicon oxides were available in the matrix. This project will identify the key mechanisms of controlling Cr, Cu, Pb, and Zn speciation in glass-ceramic systems. We will start experiments by incorporating the shredded residue of different e-waste components (printed circuit boards, capacitors, cathode ray tubes, etc.) into glass-ceramics with different matrix compositions and thermal conditions. The high resolution X-ray diffraction technique and a state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification capability will be implemented to quantify different metal hosting phases and their crystalline parameters. By identifying the grain boundary features and evaluating the metal leachabilities of product phases, the flexibility to design a variety of nano- and micro-structural features to further facilitate metal recovery and residue stabilization will be explored to move toward the goal of zero metal discharge from e-waste treatment. 快速進步的電子產品已令電子廢棄物造成世界性的環境問題，尤其是其釋出的有害金屬如鉻、銅、鉛與鋅等污染物。目前世界上電子廢棄物的產生量約為每年五千噸，並以極快的速度在增加。常用的機械處理法僅能達至約百分之八十的金屬回收成果，無法有效的竭止金屬釋出的環境問題。因此對於金屬零排放處理目標的追求，將有賴於新處理技術的開發，其中包括更有效的金屬回收方法與更可靠的金屬穩定策略。熱處理方法在此一方面展現了新的應用潛力，然而現今各種熱處理方法常要面對金屬在結晶相(陶瓷)與非結晶相(玻璃)中的分化型態問題。這些問題的答案常決定著是否該利用液相萃取法(大多依賴固液界面的非均相反應)以提高金屬回收量，或利用礦物結構達至雙重(藉由陶瓷相與玻璃相)穩定機制以可靠地抑制金屬的釋出行為。金屬的分化型態與其賦存基質及熱處理條件密切相關。例如金屬鉛可於攝氏700度時由含零價鐵的基質中獲得，但於攝氏850度如有矽同存時將轉變為矽鉛鐵礦 (Pb2Fe2Si2O9)。本研究將致力於解開鉻、銅、鉛與鋅在陶瓷玻璃基質中的分化機理。研究中將觀察電子廢棄物主要元件(如電路板、電容器、陰極射線管等)其金屬於陶瓷玻璃基質中熱處理過程的分化行為。利用高解析X射線衍射技術與最新的Rietveld結構分析方法，本研究將進一步量化金屬存於各結晶相與非結晶相的結果。以此訊息配合晶界特徵之觀察，一系列納米及微米級結構的設計將更有助於金屬回收與穩定的處理目地，並藉此邁向金屬零排放的技術目標。

17203418.label: Realisation of objectives
17203418.value: The global generation of e-waste has reached an unprecedented amount annually and is continuing with a strong increasing trend. Mechanical separation and solution leaching methods are currently used to achieve ~80% recycling efficiency for e-waste, but this is still far from the goal of zero pollutant discharge to safeguard our environment. The associated discharge of hazardous metals from such sources has created a new and urgent environmental problem. The implementation of this project has reached the objectives of exploring the release or incorporation of hazardous chromium (Cr), copper (Cu), lead (Pb) and zinc (Zn) metals in the e-waste residues using crystalline (ceramic) and non-crystalline (glass) phases under different thermal conditions. Metal incorporation experiments with the targeted metals were conducted in this project, and the outcomes have identified promising metal hosting phases, like melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9), double orthophosphate (PbZr(PO4)2), spinels (CuAl2O4 and MgCr2O4), and zinc-manganese oxide solid solution (MnMn2-xZnxO4), through sintering with commonly available and non-hazardous ceramic precursors. The formation of these phases can achieve the control of metal speciation to create opportunities for metal recovery during the transformation process of the targeted metals. High-resolution X-ray diffraction and electron diffraction techniques were used to collect data for identifying the appearing mineral phases and to analyze their relationship and partitioning behavior with the surrounding glass phases. We have established structure models for the metal hosting phases and used our unique Rietveld refinement analysis technique (fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through CaF2 and LaB6 internal standards) to quantify the metal distributions in the systems. The results have also been compared with the information from transmission electron microscopy to ensure the derived metal occupancy ratios in the targeted metal phases are of good accuracy to discuss the impact of their coordination positions on the phase stability issues. Following the results from the Rietveld structural refinement, the diffraction data of the metal hosting phases have also provided information on the lattice parameters, cation distributions, crystal sizes, and the amounts of the impurity phases. The structure and texture variabilities found in the final products also revealed the hazardous metal transform pathway and the product properties when thermally treating the e-waste residue with different glass-ceramic precursors. Our laboratory experiments first revealed that the iron oxide sintering additive could enhance the sinterability and influence the metal incorporation of Pb, Cu and Zn ceramic phases but not of the Cr-spinel phase. The results of prolonged leaching experiments further reflected the different acid attack resistance of the multi-metal oxide structures found in the sintering experiments, compared with the amorphous phase and their single oxide forms. Surface characterizations to discuss the observed leaching data were one of the focused tasks in the project, and multiple characterization techniques were utilized to cross-examine the observed outcomes. Small-angle X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy were used to ensure the surface phases and elemental compositions largely responsible for the observed leaching performance to be consistent with the bulk phases. The atomic force microscopy was used to monitor the surface roughness which enhanced the metal leaching rate. Samples after leaching processes were subject to high resolution electron microscopic investigations on their grain boundaries to help explain the behavior and metal destabilization sequences. As an example, to elucidate the leaching behavior of PbZr(PO4)2, we used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to detect the variation of surface element composition in the leaching process. After 28 days of leaching, the intensities of Pb and Zr were both reduced in the PbZr(PO4)2 sample. Our quantitative analysis collected O signal assigned to the lattice oxygen and surface oxygen, and a reduced intensity was observed for O lattice after the leaching process, indicating mineral phase depletion by acidic attack. Additionally, the peaks observed at the binding energies of 183.8 and 186.2 eV in the raw PbZr(PO4)2 sample correspond to Zr 3d spin-orbit doublets of the Zr-O bond in the ﬁtted spectra. However, prolonged leaching resulted in the transformation of surface compositions, and the split peaks of the Zr 3d proﬁle showed the presence of Zr-O and Zr-OH bonds. The variation of surface element composition indicated that an amorphous Zr(OH)4 layer might have been formed on the outer surface of PbZr(PO4)2, as the crystalline Zr(OH)4 was easily transformed into an amorphous structure through incorporating water molecules into the polymerized structure. The results were consistent with the Inductively coupled plasma analysis outcome and suggest that the low zirconium leachability may also be due to the low solubility of Zr(OH)4 generated in the dissolution process. The presence of Zr(OH)4 from precipitation might further aﬀect the Pb release rate from the target structure in the later stages of the leaching process, which provided a second barrier beneficial to the Pb stabilization. As the final goal, the nano- and micro-structural features of the generated metal hosting products and their raw waste residues were compared. By clearly delineating the phase transformation processes during the designed thermal treatments, intermediates relevant to the targeted metals were identified with the reaction mechanisms proposed. Further controls of the product designs through optimizing phase compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics for the preferred products were carried out. The metal speciation and grain boundary features were found to be crucial in the metal reactivity under the leaching environment and subsequently the metal stability performance for either the recovery or the stabilization purpose in the separation and purification processes. This finding provides us with opportunities to further extract metals unreachable by conventional solution leaching methods (mostly relying on heterogeneous surface-limited reactions) and securely incorporate metals by the more durable mineral phases and the double-barrier (through both ceramic and glass structures) immobilization mechanism. By identifying the grain boundary features and evaluating the metal leachabilities of product phases, the flexibility to design a variety of nano- and micro-structural features to further facilitate metal recovery and residue stabilization was realized.

rows: Metal incorporation experiments with the targeted metals, representing the metal pollutants discharged from electronic waste and/or its treatment residues, were conducted in this project. We have identified promising metal hosting phases, like melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9), double orthophosphate (PbZr(PO4)2), spinels (CuAl2O4 and MgCr2O4), and zinc-manganese oxide solid solution (MnMn2-xZnxO4) that can be generated with other common non-hazardous precursors under different thermal conditions to from ceramic matrices. The formation of these phases can achieve the control of metal speciation to create opportunities for metal recovery during the transformation process of the targeted metals. High-resolution X-ray diffraction and electron diffraction data were collected for those phases to analyze their relationship and partitioning behavior with the surrounding glass phases.

We have established structure models for the metal hosting phases and used our Rietveld refinement analysis technique (fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through CaF2 and LaB6 internal standards) to quantify the metal distributions in the systems. The results have also been compared with the information from transmission electron microscopy to ensure the derived metal occupancy ratios in the targeted metal phases are of good accuracy to discuss the impact of their coordination positions on the phase stability issues.

The results of Rietveld structural refinement on diffraction data collected from the metal hosting phases have also provided the lattice parameters, cation distributions, crystal sizes, and the amounts of the impurity phases. The structure and texture variabilities found in the final products also revealed the hazardous metal transform pathway and the product properties when thermally treating the e-waste residue with different glass-ceramic precursors. The iron oxide sintering additive was found to enhance the sinterability and influence the metal incorporation of Pb, Cu and Zn ceramic phases but not of the Cr-spinel phase.

The results of prolonged leaching experiments further reflected the superior resistance of the multi-metal oxide structures reported in Task 1 as the final stabilized products to acidic attack compared with the amorphous phase and their single oxide forms. Surface characterizations to discuss the observed leaching data have been carried out. Small-angle X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy were used to ensure the surface phases and elemental compositions largely responsible for the observed leaching performance to be consistent with the bulk phases. The atomic force microscopy was used to monitor the surface roughness which enhanced the metal leaching rate. Samples after leaching processes were subject to high resolution electron microscopic investigations on their grain boundaries to help explain the behavior and metal destabilization sequences.

The nano- and micro-structural features of the generated metal hosting products and their raw waste residues were compared. By clearly delineating the phase transformation processes during the designed thermal treatments, intermediates relevant to the targeted metals were identified with the reaction mechanisms proposed. Further controls of the product designs through optimizing phase compositions, metal distributions, and crystalline characteristics for the preferred products were carried out. The metal speciation and grain boundary features were found to be crucial in the metal reactivity under the leaching environment and subsequently the metal stability performance for either the recovery or the stabilization purpose in the separation and purification processes.

17203418.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203418.value: The hazardous metals are commonly found in the e-waste residues and among those concerned hazardous metals, Pb, Zn, Cu and Cr often play major roles in the compositions. This project used the commonly available raw materials to incorporate the targeted metals into the crystalline (ceramic) and non-crystalline (glass) phases under different thermal conditions to control their mobility for metal recovery and stabilization purposes. The outcomes have identified promising metal hosting phases, like melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9), double orthophosphate (PbZr(PO4)2), spinels (CuAl2O4 and MgCr2O4), and zinc-manganese oxide solid solution (MnMn2-xZnxO4), through sintering with the non-hazardous ceramic precursors. The formation of these phases can achieve the transformation of targeted metals to create opportunities for our observation of metal speciation during the reaction processes. High-resolution X-ray and electron diffraction techniques were used to identify the appearing mineral phases and to analyze their relationship and partitioning behavior with the surrounding glass phases. We have established structure models for the metal hosting phases and used our unique Rietveld refinement analysis technique (fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through CaF2 and LaB6 internal standards) to quantify the metal distributions in the systems. The results have also been compared with the information from transmission electron microscopy to ensure the derived metal occupancy ratios in the targeted metal phases are of good accuracy to discuss the impact of their coordination positions on the phase stability. The laboratory experiments first revealed that the iron oxide sintering additive could enhance the sinterability and influence the metal incorporation of Pb, Cu and Zn ceramic phases but not of the Cr-spinel phase. The results of prolonged leaching experiments further reflected the different acid attack resistance of the multi-metal oxide structures found in the sintering experiments, compared with the amorphous phase and their single oxide forms. Multiple surface characterization techniques were utilized to cross-examine the observed outcomes. For example, in addition to the intrinsic stability of PbZr(PO4)2, the presence of low-leachable Zr(OH)4 may provide a second barrier beneficial to Pb stabilization. Samples after leaching processes were subject to high resolution electron microscopic investigations on their grain boundaries to help explain the behavior and metal destabilization sequences. The metal speciation and grain boundary features were found to be most crucial in the metal reactivity under the leaching environment and subsequently the metal stability performance. Such know-how further assisted the design of nano- and micro-structural features of the generated metal hosting products.

17203418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203418.value: The implementation of this project has sufficiently used the experimental resources in a laboratory-scale facility. Further scientific research development can be planned with the synchrotron-based characterization techniques to further understand the changes of atomic coordination and occupancy when the targeted metals were going through different leaching processes. Additional development direction can be additional theoretical thermodynamic calculations to model the behavior of metals when subjected to different acidic attack conditions and verified by the experimental outcomes. Both future developments can further confirm the product phase stability results presented in the current project outcomes. Another direction of development is to refine the parameters and processing procedure generated from our laboratory-scale experiments through the industrial scale operation to fully realize the actual treatment process for e-waste treatment facilities.

17203418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203418.value: The unprecedented manufacture and use of electrical/electronic devices has generated a significant amount of electronic waste (e-waste), and the associated discharge of hazardous metals has created a new and urgent environmental problem. The research project aimed to treat the concerned hazardous metals commonly found in e-waste residues, and the research work has successfully incorporated the targeted metals into the crystalline (ceramic) and non-crystalline phases (glass) through the designs of thermal treatment processes and choices of precursors to control the metal mobility for metal recovery and stabilization purposes. The project results identified a few promising metal hosting phases and used substantial leaching experiments coupled with surface characterization techniques to explore the metal leaching behavior. The metal speciation and grain boundary features were found to be most crucial in the metal reactivity under different leaching environments and subsequently the metal stability performance. Such know-how generated from this project further assisted the design of nano- and micro-structural features of the metal-bearing products to achieve the control of metal mobility and to realize the recovery and stabilization, as the key technology toward the zero metal discharge goal for e-waste.

17203518.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17203518.value: 電商物流自動化進退兩難之博弈分析

17203518.label: Project Objectives
17203518.value: To propose a new modeling approach based on game theory for automated ecommerce warehousing services involving key stakeholders including warehouse property owner, warehouse operators, ecommerce businesses and automation technology provider. To develop a method to determine the optimal operational strategy through game equilibrium and examine the boundaries of the equilibrium. To study pricing mechanisms for the property owner to charge the warehouse operators and for ecommerce businesses to subscribe automated warehousing services from the warehousing operators, and to examine the revenue sharing mechanism between the warehouse operators and the automation technology provider. To examine potential strategic partnerships between stakeholders under different scenario settings to best address the “to automate or not to automate” dilemma faced by Hong Kong logistics industries. To test and evaluate the proposed models and findings through several Hong Kong logistics business associations among their members.

17203518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203518.value: This project has been motivated through extensive exchanges with members of five main logistics business associations in Hong Kong, especially through a series of focus group discussions recently. Logistics businesses expressed their strong desire to seize the opportunity that booming ecommerce created. Knowing characteristics and challenges of ecommerce logistics, they realize that they have to automate warehouse operations to the extent to achieve cost-effectiveness. Many of them are willing to invest, particularly through recent efforts made by world leading ecommerce businesses such as Amazons (Kiva robotized warehouses), JD.Dom and Alibaba. However, there has been a critical hurdle - lease period. That is, warehouses are typically rented from property owners to small-medium-sized (SME) warehouse operators for 2~5 years. This period is not adequate to justify investment of automating warehouses – the period is shorter than the lifespan of automation equipment even if it is long enough for a breakeven. When a lease expires, the tenant faces dilemma to accept a possible rental rise or rent another warehouse by moving automation equipment from expired warehouse to newly-rented warehouse. The cost of uninstalling, moving and reinstalling become prohibitively high – not to automate warehouses. This “to automate or not to automate” dilemma now becomes deadlock, unique with SME warehouse operators (Amazons, JD.Com and Alibaba have strength to own warehouse properties). This project is among the first attempt to study a novel business model of automated ecommerce warehouse services. While property owner invests in property development, automation technology provider invests in automating warehouses. Warehouse operators rent automated warehouses and ecommerce businesses subscribe automated warehousing services. Automation provider recovers its investment by sharing revenues collected by warehouse operators from ecommerce businesses without charging property owner. Game theory is used to study theoretical feasibility of this “all win” model by testing if equilibrium exist and examine boundaries of equilibrium. Pricing mechanisms are studied for property owner to charge warehouse operators and for ecommerce businesses to subscribe operator’s automated warehousing services. Revenue sharing mechanism is examined between warehousing operators and automation provider. Sensitivity analyses are conducted to examine how factors affect pricing and revenue sharing mechanisms and to identify dominating factors. Several typical scenarios are considered to evaluate if warehouse operations and maintenance are carried out either by warehouse operators or automation provider or both. The project outcomes is expected to break the “to automate or not to automate” ice for Hong Kong logistics and automation industries. 該項目是與香港五大主要物流業協會的成員進行廣泛交流下形成的，特別是最近通過一系列焦點小組討論豐富了下面的内容、強化了必要性和緊迫性。了解電子商務物流的特點和挑戰後，物流企業意識到必須實現倉庫運營的自動化，以提高效益降低成本。他們中的許多人都願意投資自動化，特別是最近世界領先的電子商務企業，如亞馬遜（Kiva自動化倉庫），JD.Dom和阿里巴巴。然而，倉庫自動化受制于一個關鍵的障礙 - 租賃期，租賃期一般是2〜5年。這段時間不足以證明自動化倉庫的投資是合理的 - 即使它足夠長以達到盈虧平衡，這段時間也比自動化設備的壽命短。當租約到期時，租戶面臨兩難境地，即通過將自動化設備從過期倉庫移動到新租用的倉庫來接受可能的租金上漲或租用另一個倉庫，卸載，搬移和重新安裝的成本非常高。這種“自動化或不自動化”的困境現在變成進退兩難的僵局。 該項目是首次嘗試研究自動化電子商務倉庫服務的新型商業模式。物業所有者投資房地產開發，自動化技術提供商投資自動化倉庫，倉庫運營商租用自動化倉庫和電子商務企業訂購自動化倉儲服務。自動化提供商通過分享倉庫運營商從電子商務企業收集的收入來恢復其投資，而無需向業主收取費用。博弈論用於研究這種“全贏”模型的理論可行性，通過測試均衡是否存在並檢驗均衡邊界。為房產所有者研究定價機制，以便為倉庫運營商和電子商務企業收取訂購運營商的自動化倉儲服務。在倉儲運營商和自動化提供商之間檢查收益共享機制，進行敏感性分析以檢查因素如何影響定價和收益分享機制以及確定主導因素。如果倉庫操作和維護由倉庫操作員或自動化提供商或兩者執行，則考慮幾種典型方案來評估。預計項目成果將打破香港物流和自動化行業的“自動化或不自動化”進退兩難的局面。

17203518.label: Realisation of objectives
17203518.value: All research objectives have been generally achieved through a series of research activities. Dr Yang was the post-doctoral research fellow recruited with partial financial support from this grant and initiated the development of the game theoretic models. Miss Wang was a student researcher supporting Dr Yang and Miss Wang became a PhD student working on the project. Game theoretic analysis was a major chapter of Dr Wang's PhD thesis while Dr Yang led the publication in RCIM Journal. These paper and chapters have examined and discussed Objectives 1-4 in detail. In responses to interactions with Hong Kong warehousing and logistics industries, our research activities have been extended along several lines. Firstly, Miss Wang worked on first-mile and last-mile ecommerce logistics operations supported by automated warehouses. Secondly, Miss Jiang Min joined the project by focusing on automated forward warehouses supported by reserve warehouses. This project was a result of industrial collaboration with a major warehousing and logistics operators in Hong Kong for pharmaceutical and cold chain products. Thirdly, Dr Leung and Mr Ouyang started community research resulted from automated warehousing and delivery operations. Resulting research outputs have been published in top journals such as EJOR, RCIM, TRE, and IJPR.
