17203518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203518.value: One major research finding is that there is an equilibrium of the warehousing automation partnership game. This implies that there is a theoretical foundation for different stakeholders to work together automating warehousing operations and services. Another research finding is that a forward-reserve warehouse configuration is advantageous. Forward warehouses are more automated mainly for order picking, sorting and packing, while reserve warehouses are operated in more traditional ways mainly for storage. Both forward and reserve warehouses are interoperated and synchronised through replenishment strategies and operation in between the two parts. The third research outcome is that automated warehouses / distribution centers support a new approach to ecommerce logistics and we call this approach community logistics. By this approach, ecommerce orders are delivered to consumer communities instead of routing through large areas. These new research findings / outcome open up new research areas. We have included warehouse automation local area network and spatial-temporal relativity identified from community logistics research in our theme-based research proposal which was successful in 12th round (2022-2023). We are applying patents for cellular warehousing and potentially this will become another hot and key and new research area for major proposal. This project provided funds to partially support PhD students and researchers.

17203518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203518.value: One of the most important areas identified for further research and development is Cellular Warehousing and Warehousing Cells (similar to cellular manufacturing and manufacturing cells). Different cells are dedicated to sets of SKUs that share products packaging features or logistics operations. They can be automated with specific technologies. This is a much effective and efficient approach to warehousing automation. Several PhD research students are working on the concept and proposals for major funding may be submitted in 2-3 years. A patent application has also been submitted. Another area worth further investigation is to develop local area network (LAN) for automated and digitised warehouses in what has been called Cyber-Physical Internet for global cross-border logistics. This is one of the research tasks in the proposal under Theme-based Research Scheme and this proposal has been successful in 12th round (2022-2023) for funding (HK$33.6M). Finally, it is still not clear how different stakeholders should share the costs and benefits of warehousing automation and automated warehousing services.

The project allows the research team to explore innovative warehouse configurations such as forward-reserve warehouses and cellular warehousing, and innovative logistics / delivery operations such as community logistics and first-mile / last-mile door-step logistics. Research findings and outcome have provided foundation for new large-scale research efforts for future explorations.

17204218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204218.value: Nano-structuring of InGaN/GaN quantum wells leads to a spectral blue-shift of the emission spectrum, which is usually attributed to strain relaxation. However, with recent observations of spectral red-shifts arising from nano-structuring using high-spatial-resolution techniques such as catholuminescence spectroscopy and near-field optical spectroscopy, the mechanisms and effects of nanostructuring to InGaN/GaN quantum wells certainly needs revisiting. Using a range of advanced theoretical and experimental techniques, the exact origins of strain relaxation are to be identified in this project, so that the spectral characteristics of nano-LEDs can be accurately predicted. The observations of spectral red-shifts further suggest that strain in InGaN/GaN quantum wellscan be induced by nano-structuring, something that has not been thought of before. The next objective of this project is to examine the possibility and feasibility of doing so, and to design and optimize nanostructures to achieve this goal. Comprehensive theoretical and experimental studies will be carried out to determine the methods, extents and limits of strain induction through nanostructures. Most importantly, solutions that exploit both strain relaxation and induction phenomena will be developed for solving some of the most pressing issues facing GaN technology today. This includes making use of strain induction to lengthen the emission wavelengths of InGaN/GaN LEDs as opposed to the conventional approach of increasing In content in the wells, which would otherwise drastically degrade material qualities and thus quantum efficiencies, commonly described as the “green gap” phenomenon. Using this approach, high IQE green LEDs, or long wavelength orange-red can be achieved without having to increase In content in the wells, preserving the IQEs of their lower wavelength counterparts. Phosphor-free white LEDs can also be realized using the approach of monolithically integrating strain-induced and strained-relaxed nanostructures which would emit above and below the nominal emission wavelength. With demonstrated blue-shifts of 80 nm and projected red-shifts of 30 nm, broadband emission with spectral widths exceeding 100 nm can readily be achieved. In particular, the red-shifted spectral components will contribute significantly to color qualities that excel over their phosphor-converted counterparts. Full-color microdisplays based on the monolithic integrated of matrix-addressable arrays of red, green and blue light emitting pixels will be enabled with the findings of this study, which could well become the next generation of displays given the efficiencies and longevities of inorganic LEDs compared to existing display technologies. The possibilities with the strain-induced red LEDs are endless, as they constitute important building blocks in the GaN integrated-circuit (GaN-IC) platform.

17204218.label: Realisation of objectives
17204218.value: In this project we carried out an in-depth study of relative spectral red-shift at the edge of a micro-sized structure. Strain relaxation of InGaN/GaNmultiple quantum wells (MQWs) by geometrical shaping is a common technique to blue-shift the initially fixed, narrow bandwidth light emission spectrum, and has important applications in monolithic integrated optoelectronic devices. Even though there have been numerous previous studies on the origin of the blue-shift mechanism, there has been little attention to the change in photoluminescence (PL) maps across an individual micro-structure. In this work, we have employed advanced scanning near-field optical spectroscopy (SNOS) to systematically study near-field photoluminescence map across micropillars, and discovered that the relative spectral shift at the edge of a micropillar depends on the Indium composition of MQWs. We proceed on to investigate the strain relaxation mechanism by comparing the results from molecular dynamics simulations of micropillars with low and high Indium composition. From our theoretical studies, a relative red-shift in nf-PL can be observed at the edge of micropillars having MQWs with low Indium content despite the overall blue-shift in PL. It is believed that this work would potentially open up new routes of design strategy for these applications, including but not limited to broadband micro-/nano sized LEDs, as well as colour tunable laser diodes, since the sizing effect increases with decreasing sizes. Based on the study, we have designed a nanostructure that is capable of incurring a spectral red‐shift on a conventional LED wafer, without any colour conversion agent such as quantum dots or phosphor. In the past, nanostructuring was commonly employed as a technique for colour tuning of light‐emitting devices through spectral blue‐shifting by strain relaxation of multiple quantum wells (MQWs). In fact, strain relaxation of InGaN/GaN MQWs by geometrical shaping is a common technique to blue‐shift the initially fixed, narrow bandwidth light emission spectrum, and has important applications in monolithic integrated optoelectronic devices. As such, we are of the opinion that the project objectives have been fully achieved, if not exceeded.

17204218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204218.value: A primary objective of the work is to explain the mechanism of the relative spectral redshift. We are able to observe an increase in out-of-plane strain at the edge of low Indium composition micropillar, which is verified experimentally from atomic spacings determined using calibrated diffraction patterns taken with transmission electron microscopy (TEM). This implies that the relative spectral red-shift is due to an interplay between strain relaxation mechanisms and the quantum confined stark effect (QCSE). The large scale molecular dynamics simulations, which use 96 million atoms to simulate half the micropillar with a dimension of 1μm × 1μm. The strain field is used in k∙p calculation to solve the Schrödinger equation for MQWs. We are able to reproduce, using the simulated strain fields from the above molecular dynamics simulations to calculate the emission wavelengths, the relative spectral shift with respect to the distance from the centre of a micropillar, showing red-shift and blue-shift of emission wavelength at the edge of micropillars with low and high Indium composition, respectively. We have also demonstrated that the MQWs with 18% Indium composition can exhibit a spectral shift of 50nm with only out-of-plane strain relaxation, and up to 90nm when it becomes fully relaxed in the in-plane direction as well. Experimentally, we demonstrated a nanostructure configuration that produces the spectral red-shifting effect, by increasing the strain in the quantum wells through the formation of an inverted nanoconical-frustum array over the quantum wells, without allowing the nanostructures to penetrate through the quantum wells. Under such conditions, spectral red-shifting of the photoluminescence spectrum can be observed, consistent with the prediction of strain induction in the quantum wells by molecular dynamics simulations. Experimentally, spectral red-shift of the photoluminescence spectrum by up to 7.6 nm has been observed, when the proposed nanostructures are fabricated on InGaN/GaN quantum wells grown on a c-plane sapphire substrate with a nominal emission wavelength of ∼560 nm. We have also proven that at the same emission wavelength, the IQE of samples with strain‐inducing nanostructures is higher than that of the as‐grown counterpart that has a higher Indium incorporation. This implies that the strain‐inducing nanostructures would also help in solving the “green gap” problem, which has been a bottleneck to the III‐Nitride research field and industry.

17204218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204218.value: Having established and verified the mechanism of spectral red-shift, it is imperative to develop applications based on the findings. One important application would be that of monolithic color displays. Currently LED displays are assembled from multiple LED chips, introducing many issues including yield, costs and reliability. If the colour display can be fabricated from a single wafer, all these concerns can be alleviated. Using the currently developed spectral red-shifting technology, combining with previously-developed spectral blue-shifting technology, it would be possible to realize multiple-colour emitting LEDs from a single wafer. This is an innovative solution that promises to compete with existing display technologies such as LCD and OLED displays.

17204218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204218.value: It is known that nanostructuring of InGaN/GaN quantum wells, which are responsible for light emission in light-emitting diodes, results in spectral blue-shifting. This means that the emission wavelengths become shorter after formation of the nanostructures. However, can the emission wavelength be red-shifted, which is that the wavelength becomes longer? In this project we carried out theoretical and experimental investigations to explore this intriguing topic. It was found that spectral red-shifting is possible, by inducing strain into the nanostructure. In fact, we designed a nanostructure that induces strain into the quantum wells, and experimentally demonstrated such spectral red-shifting effect. Using these results, it would be possible to realize multi-colour emission from a single LED wafer. In other words, a single chip colour LED display can be developed based on this technology.

17204318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204318.value: Nowadays, wireless power transfer technologies have been gaining increasing traction in a broad range of practical applications, which include the charging of low-power electronic devices such as smartphones, tablets, laptops, wearables, and biomedical implants to high-power charging of electric vehicles. The multi-coil wireless power transfer (MCWPT) system is becoming an attractive solution due to its flexibility, scalability and cost-effectiveness of charging multiple devices concurrently. Primarily driven by the fast-growing market demand and more stringent design constraints, there is a strong motivation in R&D works to develop a compact, efficient, low-cost inverter for future generations of MCWPT systems. Nevertheless, the design of such inverters poses two new challenges. (i) Existing inverter topologies for simultaneously charging multiple devices require an excessive number of power switches and passive components, which are bulky, costly and inefficient. These inverters are unacceptable for many space- and cost-stringent applications. In addition, they only support charging of a limited number of devices at a time because of relatively low power ratings. This is insufficient to satisfy the ever-increasing power demands from many newer types of consumer electronic devices. To attain truly cost-effective and high-power-density inverters for medium-to-high power wireless power transfer, further investigations are required to explore new topologies that use fewest components while achieving a wide output power range. (ii) Cross-coupling among transmitter coils in MCWPT systems has always been a major issue. It becomes more pronounced when the transmitter coils are located in close proximity to one another. For example, such problem is observed in the prior art of a low-power single-inductor three-output inverter whose outputs are oscillating at the same frequency. Hence, it is essential to operate the output channels at different frequencies in order to mitigate undesirable cross-interference between coils. Currently, there is no reported research work on such inverters with different output frequencies and related investigations are therefore important. With rapid market penetrations of MCWPT technologies, an increasing number of high-frequency inverters for powering multiple transmitter coils will be required. Investigations into advanced topologies and control methods of inverters for MCWPT systems will be important. Successful completion of this project will lead to greater interests in and wider use of such inverters. The outcomes will be an enrichment of the theory of power electronics (e.g. new single-inductor-multiple-output-based inverter topologies, new switching sequences for variable frequencies, and control techniques for independent power regulation with good dynamics), and practical results verifying their potential for applications. 近年來，無線電力傳輸技術在廣泛的實際應用中愈來愈受到重視。其中包括為智能手機，平板電腦，筆記本電腦，可穿戴設備和生物醫學植入物等低功率電子設備充電，以至為電動汽車等高功率設備充電。由於多線圈無線功率傳輸(MCWPT)系統能同時為多個設備充電, 其靈活性、可擴展性和成本效益，令它成為一種極具吸引力的解決方案。於市場需求快速增長和嚴格的設計限制所驅使下，我們將致力為未來的多線圈無線功率傳輸系統研發體積小、效率高及成本低的逆變器。然而，這種逆變器的設計給我們帶來了兩個新的挑戰。 (i) 現有的逆變器縱使能同時為多個設備充電，但它們需要過多的電源開關和無源元件，導致這些逆變器體積大，成本高且效率低，並不適合應用於對空間和成本有嚴格要求的產品上。此外，由於它們的輸出功率相對較低，僅容許對有限數量的設備進行充電，實在不足以滿足許多新型消費電子設備不斷增長的電力需求。為了實現具有成本效益和高功率的逆變器，讓它們能應用在中至高功率無線功率傳輸，我們需要進一步研究及探索使用最少組件而同時能達到功率範圍廣的新電路拓撲。 (ii) 在MCWPT系統中，發射器線圈之間的交叉耦合一直是一個主要問題，尤其是當發射器線圈彼此靠近時，這種現象變得更為嚴重。譬如，我們已經在低功率單電感器三輸出逆變器中觀察到此現象，主要原因是其輸出通道都是採用相同的振盪頻率。因此，最有效的解決方法是對輸出通道採用不同的頻率，以大大減輕線圈之間的交叉干擾。據了解，目前並沒有關於具有不同輸出頻率的單電感器多輸出的逆變器之研究報導，因此，我們認為相關研究是重要的。 隨著MCWPT的市場滲透率持續提升，我們預期為多個發射器線圈供電的高頻逆變器將變得愈來愈普遍。對這種逆變器的高階拓撲和控制方法之研究將顯得更為重要。成功完成該研究項目將引起人們對這類逆變器的更大興趣和更廣泛的使用。其研究成果將豐富了電力電子理論（例如，基於單電感器多輸出的逆變器之新拓撲，用於可變頻率的新開關序列，及具有獨立功率調節和良好動態的控制技術），我們並會附上實際測試報告以驗證它們的應用潛力。

17204318.label: Realisation of objectives
17204318.value: With reference to the proposed objective 1, our target was to derive the switching sequence and control scheme for independent frequency control and/or power level regulation of individual AC outputs of the SITO boost inverter. For independent frequency control and its related switching sequence, we have achieved this by using a new type of gallium nitride (GaN)-based single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) dc–ac inverter that generates multiple frequencies at the ac outputs. The proposed time-multiplexed switching sequences enable the SIMO inverter to simultaneously generate sinusoidal-like outputs with different frequencies. In the absence of a parasitic body diode in the GaN transistor and with correct bias voltage, the proposed inverter requires no additional blocking diodes and/or cascaded power switches while still ensuring unidirectional flow of the inductor current for proper circuit operation. Compared with its silicon counterpart, this GaN-based inverter achieves a simplified circuit structure, reduced component count, small form factor, increased power density, and high efficiency. A practical application of this inverter is to act as a single wireless power transmitter which concurrently drives multiple transmitter coils at different frequencies for multi-standard wireless power transfer. A hardware prototype of a single-inductor three-output inverter producing three distinct resonant frequencies, namely, 100, 200, and 300 kHz, is constructed. The effectiveness of the proposed switching sequences and control method for this inverter is experimentally verified. No cross regulation is observed across the three individual ac outputs. This work has been published as "A gallium nitride (GaN)-based single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) inverter with multi-frequency AC outputs" in IEEE Transaction on Power Electronics. Nonetheless, for the work above and also that of all previously reported SIMO inverters, the works have been focused on deriving solutions with open-loop switching schemes and sequences. They do not incorporate the subsequent necessary closed-loop control scheme for achieving a truly robust and independent frequency control and power level regulation of individual AC outputs of the SITO inverters that have external changes. For all practical purposes, a controllable output voltage at the transmitting coil is essential in real WPT applications because a constant voltage (CV) in the primary coil at the transmitter infers a constant current (CC) in the secondary coil at the loaded receiver, such as the Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery in a mobile device. For this reason, the subsequent task was to incorporate feedback control into the SIMO inverter. This is especially useful for the wireless charging of rechargeable batteries when they act as a CC load in the CC charging phase. By precisely regulating the source voltage at each transmitting coil, a constant load current at the corresponding receiver can be achieved at a particular resonant frequency and mutual inductance between the transmitting and receiving coil. Here, the closed-form expressions of the sinusoidal-like output voltage and resonant inductor current as a function of the duty ratio of the main switch was analytically derived. Then, an experimental prototype of a SITO inverter with a single time-multiplexed analog-based controller employing the type II compensation is implemented. It is experimentally verified that the individual ac outputs can be accurately and independently controlled. The maximum error between the target and measured peak voltage values is shown to be within 1.14% This work has been published as "Single-Inductor Multiple-Output Inverter With Precise and Independent Output Voltage Regulation" in IEEE Transaction on Power Electronics. With both the tasks above completed, objective 1 as stated in the original funding application has been fully achieved. With reference to objective 2, we have developed a non-isolated medium power SIMO buck hybrid converter that can simultaneously supply multiple independent AC and DC loads from a single DC input. Compared with the existing hybrid converter topologies, the proposed SIMO based hybrid converter achieves a simplified circuit structure, smaller component count, fully independent power control of its outputs, and better scalability of a larger number of AC and DC outputs and at a higher power level. A useful application of this hybrid converter is to drive multiple transmitting coils and USB charging ports in a multi-device Qi-compliant hybrid wireless charger. This work has been presented as "Single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) buck hybrid converter with simultaneous AC and DC outputs for multi-coil wireless power transfer applications,” at IEEE APEC Anaheim, California. The extended journal version of this work is published as "Single-Inductor Multiple-Output (SIMO) Buck Hybrid Converter for Simultaneous Wireless and Wired Power Transfer" in IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics. Additionally, we also developed a type of non-isolated buck-boost SIMO dc–ac inverter for driving multiple independent high-frequency ac outputs of medium power. Compared with traditional bridge-type inverters, the proposed buck-boost SIMO inverter achieves 1) a smaller component count, 2) fully independent power control of its outputs, 3) better scalability in increasing the number of ac output channels, and 4) higher power efficiency. Operating in pseudo-continuous conduction mode, the rated power of each output channel of this inverter can be high while attaining zero cross regulation. The scalability factor of the proposed inverter is formally investigated and the theoretical maximum number of ac outputs is analytically derived. A hardware prototype of a SITO buck-boost inverter delivering a medium power of 8.4 W per output channel has been constructed. It is experimentally verified that precise and independent current regulation of individual transmitter coil is achievable. This work has been published as “Buck-boost single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) high-frequency inverters for medium-power wireless power transfer” in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. With both the tasks above completed, objective 2 as stated in the original funding application has been fully achieved. For completeness of the overall target of WPT, we extended our work to include its receiver counterpart. Aiming at low-cost applications, our anticipated system involves only a single-switch class-E resonant rectifier a frequency synchronization circuit, and a microcontroller. The number of power semiconductor devices required is minimal. Only one active switch is used, with no diode. This simplifies circuit implementation, improves reliability, and lowers the hardware cost. A prototype is built and experimental works are performed to verify the features: achieving 93% efficiency single-switch ac–dc rectification, −7.17-dB total harmonic distortion ac voltage waveform, ZVS turn ON and turn OFF over wide load range, 0.4% output voltage regulation error, 79% cost reduction as compared with the Qi- compliant receivers, 2.5% overshoot/undershoot after load disturbances, and 1% overshoot after line disturbance. This work has been published as “Single-Switch-Regulated Resonant WPT Receiver,” in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. The abovementioned solution is only applicable to applications where operating line voltage and load are fairly constant. The ZVS operation is highly sensitive to may be lost if line voltage and load changes. Moreover, ac voltage waveform of its circuits contains both even- and odd-order harmonic components, which limits their THD performance and filter size is substantially large. Subsequently, we proposed a receiver system that utilizes the differential resonant topology, which can provide low THD ac waveforms, continuous dc current, and ground-referenced switches. This also reduces the EMI filter and output capacitor size. Experimental results showed that it can achieve single-stage ac rectification and dc regulation while attaining low harmonic distortion in its ac output voltage, continuous dc current, and ZVS operation over a wide operating range. This work has been published as “Single-Stage Regulated Resonant WPT Receiver With Low Input Harmonic Distortion,” in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics.

17204318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204318.value: A GaN-based dc/ac SIMO inverter with multiple output frequencies has been proposed. With no transistor's body diode, the proposed circuit requires no blocking diode or back-to-back MOSFETs. It has a reduced component count, smaller form factor, and higher efficiency. It is capable of generating similar or different frequencies across independently driven output channels. It benefits applications by allowing interoperability of different wireless standards and concurrent power transfer across multiple power channels with minimum cross interference. A single-stage dc–ac buck-boost SIMO inverter, which employs one single inductor to generate multiple independent sinusoidal outputs, has been proposed. By adjusting the inductor's peak and valley current, the output power of each channel can be independently controlled. Compared with boost-only SIMO inverters, this inverter can achieve a significantly higher output power of 8.4 W per channel, which is useful for low-to-medium power applications. A boost-type SIMO inverter with precise and independent control of the output voltage under closed-loop control, has been proposed. The relationship between the output voltage and the ON-time duty ratio of the switch of this inverter has been derived. It is shown that the output voltages are well regulated with high precision and the closed-loop system remains in stable condition in both line and load transients. A single-stage SIMO dc–ac buck based hybrid converter has been proposed. By operating in PCCM, it can achieve a rated output power of 20 W (or 5 W per output channel). An application of this converter is as a versatile multidevice hybrid charger or power bank with multiple wireless charging pads and USB charging ports. It is experimentally confirmed that this converter is effective in performing independent dc–ac and/or dc–dc power conversions without cross regulation. We has also derived a single-switch-regulated resonant WPT receiver using the active class-E rectifier topology. By adopting phase-shift control and our proposed design, the system can simultaneously achieve high-frequency rectification, wide-load-range ZVS operation, and accurate output regulation, without needing post regulator. The system involves one power semiconductor device (no diode required). Lower cost and higher reliability as compared to existing WPT receivers is possible. A single-stage regulated WPT receiver with low input harmonic distortion is proposed. The receiver is based on the differential resonant rectifier topology and adopts the phase-shift control. Low input harmonic distortion and accurate out voltage/current regulation of the receiver is achievable, making it a promising solution for simple, compact, and reliable WPT battery charging.

17204318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204318.value: It is interesting to investigate more advanced controllers (e.g. Type-III or pseudo-Type III), which can possibly lead to faster transient response while maintaining closed-loop stability across a wider load range. Hence, a more robust dynamic performance can be achieved in SIMO inverter, which is useful for quick and safe charging of batteries. By far, the maximum output power per channel achieved is around 8.4 W. In the future, it would also be crucial to investigate the possibility of achieving a higher output power level (e.g. beyond 25 W) without compromising the overall efficiency. This would allow quick and simultaneous charging of a larger number of unidentical electronic devices. To further improve the efficiency and minimize the form factor, there is still plenty of room to optimize the key passive components in terms of their size and ESR. Finally, since all the experiment prototypes in this work are implemented as single-inductor three-output (SITO) inverter, future work may be needed to extend it to more outputs. For future investigations, it is equally important to keep pace with any latest changes in the wireless power standard.

17204318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204318.value: The wireless power transfer technology is becoming popular in a broad range of practical applications, This includes the charging of low-power electronic devices such as smartphones, tablets, laptops, wearables, and biomedical implants to high-power charging of robots and electric vehicles. The use of multi-coil wireless power transfer system is attractive due to its flexibility, scalability and cost-effectiveness of charging multiple devices concurrently. Nevertheless, conventional inverter topologies for simultaneously charging multiple devices require an excessive number of power switches and passive components, which are bulky and costly. These inverters are unacceptable for space-and-cost-stringent applications. In addition, they only support charging of a limited number of devices at a time. This is insufficient to satisfy the increasing power demands from newer types of consumer electronics. To attain cost-effective and high-power-density inverters for wireless power transfer, new topologies that are low cost and use fewest components are needed. The research work completed in this project enables the development of the single-inductor-multiple-output inverters that meet the requirement of low cost and low component counts. The publication of these works has also led to greater interests in and wider use of such inverters. The outcomes also provide an enrichment of the theory of power electronics.

17204418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204418.value: In 1972, the government of Hong Kong undertook an ambitious housing development plan that would radically alter the city’s geography, reshape its economy, and transform its natural and cultural environments. It was one of the most ambitious infrastructure and urban development projects in the world (Hills and Yeh, 1983), drawing in professionals from around the world to participate in the planning, design, and construction of three ‘new towns’ in the low valleys and waterways of Hong Kong’s New Territories (Garrett, 2015). This research traces the experience of one these groups—the landscape architect—to illuminate its contribution to the larger ecological and social reconfigurations of the territory. The story of this transformation has been examined largely as a product of centralized colonial statecraft (Castells et al., 1990). Yet in reality, the scale and pace of the program triggered a much messier process in which the multidisciplinary project teams of professionals exercised uncommon levels of autonomy (Lewis, 2016). The practices of these “experts”—either as they reproduced or, as some lines of scholarship suggest (Rose and Miller, 1992; Rueschemeyer, 1983), contravened, centralized authority—has received little attention in academic literature. There is less still on how these experts, in situations of uncertainty, construct and adapt their professional belief-systems and self-image for new contexts (Howe and Kaufman, 1981; Lipman, 1969; Thomas and Healey, 1991). Given the global image of Hong Kong today, one might not expect that landscape architects had any mark on the growth of the city. Yet, the influence on much of the city’s urban environment is significant (Bristow, 1989). This project will explore how a young discipline, wielding a new body of expertise engaged with local and international knowledge networks to enact urban and environmental change. It will examine how a new language and discourse influenced the ongoing narratives of urban development and quality of life in the city. The research will contribute new perspectives to scholarship on the dynamics of lesson-drawing and exchange in the dynamic context of colonialism cum globalism. Through first-hand interviews with the individuals involved, the research will contribute new detail to Hong Kong’s housing and urban development histories, recovering the roots of the landscape profession locally, and revealing the foundations of contemporary forms of practice in China and the around the world. The project continues the researcher’s larger interest in seeking the under-explored histories of landscape architecture and revealing new paradigms for nature in the city. 1972年，香港政府实施了一项雄心勃勃的住房发展计划，这将剧烈改变城市地理，重塑经济，并转变其自然和文化环境。它曾是世界上最宏大的基础设施和城市发展项目之一，吸引了来自世界各地的专业人士参与。这项研究追溯了其中一个专业群体 - 景观建筑师 - 的经验，以阐明其对该地区的更大的生态和社会重构的贡献。这个转变的故事被广泛视为中心化殖民统治战略的产物。然而实际上，该计划的规模和速度引发了一个更加混乱的过程。在此过程中，多学科的专业项目团队行使了罕见水平的自治。本项目将探索一个年轻的学科，如何利用一种与当地和国际知识网络相连的新专业知识，来促使城市和环境变化的发生。一种新的语言和论述如何影响城市发展的持续叙事与生活质量是本文研究的内容。本项目延续了研究者对更大范畴学术问题的关注，即寻求未充分发掘的景观建筑历史，并揭示城市自然的新范式。

17204718.value: 疏液表面：微流控液滴法製備跳蟲表皮狀多孔表面

17204718.label: Project Objectives
17204718.value: To develop a general microfluidics approach for large-scale low-cost fabrication of well-defined porous surfaces with robust liquid repellency and strong mechanical stability; To reliably correlate processing parameters, surface structures, liquid repellency, and mechanical stability; To develop and characterize two kinds of liquid-repellent surfaces using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and PVA/silica nanoparticle composites as the surface materials.

17204718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204718.value: 疏液材料具備排斥任何液體而表面不被粘附的功能。這類材料的重要用途包括防水衣物、防汙廚具、強化傳熱及防汙、防腐、減阻塗層（例如用於大型船隻以提升速度、節省燃料)等。理想的疏液材料應同時滿足這些要求：疏液功能強、耐用程度高、製備面積大、製造成本低。然而，目前的疏液材料並未能齊備上列四大條件，原因是傳統疏液結構的設計和微結構的精確加工及表面性能調控尚有不足之處。 我們提出一種低成本的可擴展方法，用於製造具有良好疏液性和高機械穩定性的多孔表面。該多孔疏液表面的結構設計受啟發於跳蟲表皮，可有效地解決疏液性和機械穩定性之間的矛盾。跳蟲是棲息於土壤中的節肢動物，其棲息地經常遭遇雨水和洪水的沖洗或者淹浸。因此，這些節肢動物續漸進化出具有強機械耐久性和優異疏液特性的角質表皮以抵抗土壤顆粒的摩擦並在水環境中呼吸生存。我們設計的多孔表面由具有互連凹角特徵的蜂窩狀微腔組成：互相連接提高機械穩定性，凹腔結構加強疏液性能。充分利用微流控的可擴展性和對微量流體的精確控制能力，該跳蟲表皮狀多孔表面可通過微流控液滴的自組裝來製造。微流控法將會是一種製備仿跳蟲表皮結構多孔表面的精確、可控、可擴展且廉價的製造方法。 我們的目標是檢驗微流控液滴法在製備疏液性好和機械強度高的疏液表面及其用於商業化大規模製造上的潛力。本專案設計的疏液表面將能夠同時排斥各種液體，故而又被稱為“全疏表面”。我們將使用聚乙烯醇（PVA）和PVA/二氧化矽納米顆粒複合材料製造兩種全疏表面來研究所提出的微流控制備法：PVA具有優異的成膜、乳化以及機械性能，如高拉伸強度和柔韌性；添加二氧化矽納米粒子則能夠製造納/微米層級結構，進而增強疏液特性。 該項目的成功施行將改變疏液表面的製造方式，為大面積低成本製備機械性和疏液性皆優的疏液表面提供有效的解決方案。該項目還將研發出革命性的疏液表面，並加深我們對潤濕現象和固液相互作用的理解。專案的研究結果將為合理設計表面結構，精確調控表面形貌、疏液性和機械穩定性以滿足特定的應用需求提供良好的借鑒思路。

17204718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204718.value: This project developed a low-cost scalable approach for the fabrication of well-defined porous surfaces with robust liquid repellency and strong mechanical stability. The design of the liquid-repellent surfaces is inspired by structures on springtail cuticles, which can effectively resolve the longstanding conflict between the liquid repellency and the mechanical stability. Springtails are soil-dwelling arthropods whose habitats often experience rain and flooding. As a consequence, springtails have evolved cuticles with strong mechanical durability and robust liquid repellency to resist friction from soil particles and to survive in watery environments. The porous surfaces are designed to be composed of interconnected honeycomb-like microcavities with a re-entrant profile: the interconnectivity ensures mechanical stability and the re-entrant structure yields robust liquid repellency. The cuticle-like porous surfaces is fabricated by self-assembly using microfluidic droplets, which takes full advantage of the capabilities of microfluidics in terms of scalability and precise-handling of small fluid volumes. The generation of these cuticle-like porous surfaces using microfluidics led to precise, controllable, scalable, and inexpensive fabrication. This project changes the way liquid-repellent surfaces are fabricated for robust liquid-repellency, strong mechanical stability, and economical production at a commercial scale.

17205318.label: Project Objectives
17205318.value: Investigation of optical resonances in 2D photonic crystal nano-cavity: this includes optimization of the periodic dielectric nano-structures with the aid of simulations and theoretical calculations. A point defect induced into a photonic crystal exhibits a strong localization of the light at a wavelength within the photonic bandgap. Design and fabrication of monolithic nano-cavities for a stable lasing operation in the broad visible band: this includes the optimization of photonic crystal structure and dimension and of point defect that satisfy the resonance condition. This also includes the optimization of the fabrication sequences and processes. Realization of a single-chip multi-colour semiconductor laser: the project aims at demonstrating multi-color lasing emission. The resultant device, which is designed to be optically/electrically pumped, produces laser emission of different colours from different regions.

17205318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205318.value: 三族氮化物半導體的顯著進步使得通過紫外到可見光譜帶的直接帶隙發射成為可能，因此出現了全新的固態發光體系列。能夠在整個可見光譜上發射的多色激光器可以實現光電子學的許多重要應用，例如固態照明、全色顯示器、可見顏色通信和多色熒光傳感。它還可以提供產生白光的巨大潛力，從而使該技術更接近成為主流光源。 雖然乾式激光現在可用於全色激光，但激光配置涉及非線性頻率轉換，這是一種高度複雜且能量低效的過程。此外，乾式激光器一次只能發出一種顏色，其色彩調節過程非常慢。顯然，長期前景是通過採用三族氮化物半導體用於激光應用來消除對頻率轉換的需求，這提供了許多優點，包括高能量效率，低發熱，簡單的製造和組裝過程以及微型佔用面積。然而，開發緊湊的基於多色半導體的激光源受到極大限制，因為傳統的邊緣發射激光器和電流表面發射激光器需要半導體帶隙和腔長度的突然變化以改變它們的發射波長。因此，激光源通常發射單一顏色，特定波長的電磁波譜，而不是寬範圍的不同波長。 最近，我們的各種實驗結果使我們想到了在不使用外部頻率轉換介質的情況下從單芯片產生多色激光的新思想。通過系統研究光子晶體納米腔的激光作用和通過納米結構化氮化銦鎵/氮化鎵量子阱的應變弛豫，可以確定實現單晶片激光發射的寬光譜範圍的條件。所提出的激光器結構將由具有單點缺陷的二維週期性納米柱陣列組成，通過電子束光刻圖案化並通過等離子體蝕刻轉移。這種在大面積氮化鎵薄膜上製造納米柱陣列的單片工藝將提供許多有吸引力的優點，包括簡單的工藝流程，緊湊的尺寸和超低功耗，並使新一代電子注入半導體激光器具有多色操作波長。

17205318.label: Realisation of objectives
17205318.value: Extensive theoretical and experimental work has been conducted to realize the objectives of the project. Multiple approaches have been devices, based on the manipulation of an optical cavity, including the photonic crystal cavity and the whispering gallery mode cavity. The theoretical investigations have been carried out with the aid of Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) simulations in order to predict the cavity modes of the cavities. This is followed by the experimental investigations. The patterning of the cavities relies heavily on microspheres and nanospheres; due to their sphericity and hardness which facilitate pattern transfers. For the photonic crystals, ink-jet printing is adopted for the printing of nanosphere arrays with varying pitches designed according to FDTD simulations. For the whispering-gallery mode cavities, the microspheres and nanospheres are mixed before being coated over the wafers. The subsequent steps follow standard III-nitride fabrications procedures. The fabricated devices are then characterized by optical pumping. Optical-pumped single-chip multi-colour (multi-wavelength) lasing is demonstrated with wavelengths ranging from 473.9 nm to 516.9 nm.

17205318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205318.value: Multiple routes have been explored for achieving multi-color (multi-wavelength) emission and lasing from GaN microcavities. The methods can be grouped into two major categories, namely photonic crystal cavities and strain relaxation. In the photonic crystal method, arrays of GaN nanopillars are formed by firstly ink-jet printing of nanospheres into domains, followed by dry etching in GaN. The dimensions and pitch of the nanospheres in a domain is varied by changing the nanosphere suspension and/or the printing parameters. As such, the different domains printed onto the same GaN sample will have different photonic crystal effects. On the other hand, whispering-gallery mode microdisk cavities of different dimensions can be formed on a single GaN wafer to achieve multi-color emission making use of the Quantum Confined Starch Effect (QCSE). This is realized by the spin-coating of a mixture of microspheres and nanospheres having diamters of 950 nm, 1 micron and 10 micron. The pattern is transferred onto the wafer by dry etching, resulting in the formation of microdisks of different dimensions. As the differently-sized microdisks are strain-relaxed to different extents, their emission wavelengths are shifted. Upon optical pumping, the microdisks laser at different wavelengths, giving rise to multi-wavelength lasing, with lasing thresholds of 15.1 mJ/cm2, 2.9 mJ/cm2 and 5.3 mJ/cm2 with Q factors of 2370, 2060 and 4308. The extent of wavelength shift has been correlated to the Raman shift, which measures the extent of strain relaxation in the GaN microdisks.

17205318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205318.value: There are many applications that would benefit from multi-wavelength lasers, including solid-state lighting, laser displays, visible light communications and fluorescence excitation. Having multi-color or multi-wavelength capabilities would improve the performance or usability of such applications. As such, there is great potential for further development of multi-wavelength lasers based on the findings in this work. For instance, the range of lasing wavelength can be increased to achieve a broader spectrum and thus colour gamut. This would call for additional investigations into the material and processing aspects of the device design and structures.

17205318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205318.value: We have investigated the topic of multiple wavelength (or multiple colour) emission and lasing from a single device. Such monolithic emission relies on optical microcavities of different optical properties that are monolithically integrated onto the same chip. The different optical properties have been achieved by changing the parameters of the optical cavities, which can either by photonic crystals or whispering gallery mode microdisk cavities. By integrating optical cavities with different optical properties, multiple wavelength lasing has been demonstrated, with emission ranging from blue to green.

17205518.label: Project Objectives
17205518.value: Develop novel dual-rotor stator-permanent-magnet motor topologies for electric vehicles (EVs), which can offer higher reliability and safety than the state-of-the-art electronic differential using the two-motor arrangement. Formulate the design equations and analytical models of the proposed motors, hence identifying the key design parameters and performance indices. Analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motors, hence assessing the torque ripple during cornering, the thermal instability of permanent magnets, and the mechanical integrity of the axial-field structure. Develop the power converter topologies for the proposed motors, which can conduct power regulation for dual-rotor propulsion and steering. Devise the control strategies for the proposed motor drives, which can achieve the desired propulsive torque with minimum torque ripple, especially during cornering. Evaluate the performance indices of the proposed motor drives in terms of the reliability and safety under various failure modes as well as the efficiency, torque density, manufacturing complexity and cost as compared with the state-of-the-art electronic differential for EVs.

17205518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205518.value: Electric vehicles (EVs) are the cleanest and greenest road transportation. The use of direct-drive motors for individual driving wheels is attractive to provide the action of electronic differential, which can eliminate the bulky and heavy mechanical differential. However, the electronic differential suffers from some fundamental problems – reliability and safety concerns – that hinder its practical application to EVs. In particular, if there is an unpredictable error in controlling one of the motors during cornering, the consequence will be disastrous. In recent years, the development of dual-rotor machines is becoming active, which can improve the overall torque density as compared with the use of two individual machines. Taking into account the increased complexity, this kind of integration may not be justifiable unless there is a necessity to combine the two machines. The use of dual-rotor motor for EV propulsion is highly justifiable because it not only improves the overall torque density, but also provides a way to improve the electronic differential – both are highly desirable for modern EVs. However, the available dual-rotor motors for electronic differential still suffer from the same reliability and safety concerns as the use of two motors. In order to possess the advantages of dual-rotor motors and electronic differential while retaining the reliability of mechanical differential, the concept of magnetic steering mechanism is proposed. In essence, the motor for the left wheel can be integrated with the motor for the right wheel to form a novel structure with two rotors, which are magnetically coupled together to ensure the reliability and hence safety. Meanwhile, in order to provide a robust structure for direct drive, the two rotors should be free from copper windings or permanent magnets (PMs). The purpose of this proposal is to develop a novel class of dual-rotor stator-PM motor drives for EVs with electronic differential. The objectives are: (1) develop novel dual-rotor stator-PM motor topologies which can offer higher reliability and safety than the state-of-the-art electronic differential; (2) formulate the design equations and analytical models of the proposed motors; (3) analyze the electromagnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motors; (4) develop the power converter topologies to conduct power regulation for dual-rotor propulsion and steering; (5) devise the control strategies to achieve the desired propulsive torque with minimum torque ripple, especially during cornering; (6) evaluate the performance indices of the proposed motor drives, especially reliability and safety under various failure modes. 電動汽車是當今最清潔、最環保的公路運輸。將直驅電動機用於電動汽車的驅動輪以提供電子差速器作用是十分吸引的，這可以消除龐大且重的機械差速器。然而，電子差速器存在一些基本問題──可靠性和安全性──阻礙了其在電動汽車中的實際應用。特別是，如果在轉彎期間控制其中一個電動機存在不可預測的錯誤，則後果將是災難性的。近年來，雙轉子電機的發展變得活躍，與使用兩台電機相比，這可以改善整體扭矩密度。除非有必要將兩台電機組合在一起，否則這種組合大大增加其復雜性，雙轉子電機便變成不合理。將雙轉子電機用於電動汽車是非常合理的，因為它不僅提高了整體扭矩密度，而且提供了一種有效改善電子差速器的方法──這兩者都是現代電動汽車非常需要的。然而，用於當今電子差速器的雙轉子電動機仍然帶有與使用兩個電動機相同的可靠性和安全性問題。為了在保留機械差速器可靠性的同時具備雙轉子電動機和電子差速器的優點，我們提出了磁轉向機制的概念。即用於左輪的電動機可以與用於右輪的電動機結合，以形成具有兩個轉子的新穎結構，這兩個轉子磁耦合在一起以確保其可靠性並因此確保其安全性。同時，為了提供用於直接驅動的堅固結構，兩個轉子應該沒有銅繞組或永磁體。本項目的目的是為具有電子差速器的電動汽車開發一種新型的雙轉子定子永磁電動機。我們的目標是：（1）開發新型雙轉子定子永磁電機結構，與現有技術的電子差速器相比，可提供更高的可靠性和安全性。（2）制定所提出電動機的設計方程和分析模型。（3）分析所提出的電動機的電磁場、熱場和結構性能。（4）開發功率變換器結構，對雙轉子電動機的驅動和轉向進行功率調節。（5）設計控制策略，以最小的轉矩波動達到所需的驅動力矩，特別是在轉彎時的驅動。（6）評估所提出的電動機的性能指標，特別是在各種故障模式下的可靠性和安全性。

17205518.label: Realisation of objectives
17205518.value: The 1st objective has been fully completed. Firstly, a new stator-permanent-magnet (PM) motor topology has been proposed, termed the parallel-hybrid-excited (PHE) machine with harmonic-shift (HS) structure. This HS-PHE motor topology is particularly attractive for direct-drive electric propulsion. The key is to alternately place the dc-field pole-pair and PM pole-pair in the stator, thereby achieving the dc-field harmonic shift from the PM-field harmonics. Consequently, the dc-field harmonics interact with the PM harmonics to regulate the resultant effective harmonics in the air-gap while the parallel flux paths of PM flux and dc-field flux can also be obtained, leading to more effective flux regulation ability. Secondly, a new PHE machine with harmonic-differential (HD) effect has been proposed. The key is to place the dc-field windings in the dc pole sandwiched by two adjacent PM poles, thereby realizing the parallel flux paths of PM-flux and dc-field flux. The corresponding HD effect is created so that the dc-field harmonics can differentiate the effective and ineffective harmonics in the airgap to weaken the resultant effective magnetic field. Hence, attractive flux-weakening ability and extended speed-operating range can be achieved for EV propulsion. Consequently, by incorporating the PHE concept into the dual-rotor structure, various dual-rotor stator-PM motor topologies can be derived, which can realize differential action without using the bulky differential gear, making the propulsion system more compact, better reliability and higher safety than the state-of-the-art electronic differential using the two-motor arrangement. The 2nd objective has been fully completed. In order to have a deeper insight into the flux regulation principle as well as the torque production mechanism of the proposed motors, the airgap harmonics have been analytically derived. Hence, the design equations can be formulated and the performance indices can be quantitatively assessed. Namely, the machine has been analyzed from the perspective of the field-modulation effect based on the air-gap field harmonics. It reveals that the dominant effective harmonics are those even harmonics with specific pole-pairs contributing to the most of total torque. Consequently, the torque-sizing equations of the resulting dual-rotor stator-PM motor system are derived to provide the key design parameters. These torque equations are particularly essential to assess the cornering performance under differential action. Meanwhile, a nonlinear varying-network magnetic circuit method has been developed to analytically calculate the electromagnetic performances. The key is to divide the machine model into different elements reasonably, hence deducing the reluctances and magnetomotive force sources in each element. While taking account of magnetic saturation in the iron region, the proposed method can accurately predict the three-dimensional magnetic field distribution, hence determining the corresponding back electromotive force and electromagnetic power. Apart from offering fast calculation, this analytical method can provide physical insight on how to optimize the design parameters of the machine. The 3rd objective has been fully completed. By using finite element analysis based on a commercial software package JMAG, multiphysics simulation including magnetic, thermal and structural performances of the proposed motors have been analyzed. In particular, the flux regulation capability, back electromotive force, torque ripple and the unbalanced magnetic force of the proposed motors have been assessed. Consequently, the resultant torque, differential torque and torque ripple of the proposed motor systems during cornering are evaluated. For the axial-field sandwiched stator-PM motor structure, the thermal instability and mechanical integrity are critically assessed. Moreover, the effect of different PM arrangements on various stator-PM machines have been comprehensively analyzed. Hence, the corresponding back electromotive force, steady torque, cogging torque, efficiency, PM utilization ratio, and immunity of PM demagnetization are optimized. The 4th objective has been fully completed. The power converters of the proposed motors and the proposed dual-rotor stator-PM motor systems have been developed. In particular, two types of power converters are required to feed the motor system: namely, a three-phase full-bridge inverter is designed to feed the armature windings for propulsion while a full-bridge dc-dc converter is designed to feed the magnetic coupling windings for steering. This dc-dc converter can feed a positive current to the magnetic coupling windings to strengthen the air-gap flux density of the left rotor and to weaken that of the right rotor for right-hand cornering, and can feed a negative current to the magnetic coupling windings for left-hand cornering. Meanwhile, to achieve straight movement, the magnetic coupling windings are not injected with currents so that only the same PM flux exists in the two rotors, thus creating the same torque and speed at the two rotors. The 5th objective has been fully completed. Based on the Ackerman-Jeantand geometry model for steering maneuver and the vehicle dynamic model for electric propulsion, the control strategies for the proposed dual-rotor motor system have been devised. In the angle-speed controller, the outputs of the left and right wheel speed references are compared with the speed differential feedback from two wheels to regulate the magnetic coupling current. Meanwhile, the differential signal between the vehicle speed reference and feedback is fed into the field-oriented control controller to regulate the armature current. As a result, by properly controlling the magnetic coupling current while keeping the same armature current, the left rotor torque and right rotor torque can be differentiated during cornering. Compared with the existing electronic differential system using two motors, the proposed system can produce the desired torque with minimum torque ripple, especially during cornering. In case of any motor fault, the proposed system can maintain the correct angle for cornering with reduced speed, whereas the existing electronic differential system cannot maintain the desired turning angle which may cause a fatal accident during cornering. Hence, the proposed system can provide higher reliability and safety than the existing electronic differential system. The 6th objective has been fully completed. To verify the merits of the proposed dual-rotor motor system with the capability of magnetic differential, the vehicle steering performances of the conventional mechanical differential, the state-of-the-art electronic differential and the proposed magnetic differential under various failure modes are simulated and quantitatively compared. It confirms that the proposed system can offer much higher efficiency and compactness than the mechanical differential system, while can offer higher efficiency, higher torque density, lower complexity and lower cost as well as higher reliability and safer operation than the state-of-the-art electronic differential system. Additionally, the proposed dual-rotor motor system has been further extended to the flywheel energy storage machine system for EVs. By incorporating the slotless, coreless and Halbach-PM features, it can offer high power density, good dynamic performance and low eddy-current loss, leading to a promising energy storage technology.

17205518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205518.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 8 international journal papers [J1]-[J8] and 4 international conference papers [C1]-[C4]. Meanwhile, 2 PhD students have been trained. Concerning the machine design for this project, we have conducted a critical review of various electric machines for electric vehicles (EVs) [J5]. A novel parallel-hybrid-excited permanent-magnet (PM) machine with harmonic-shift structure has been proposed for EVs with electronic differential, in which the dc-field harmonics can interact with the PM harmonics to regulate the resultant effective harmonics in the airgap, leading to more effective flux regulation ability [J1]. Then, another novel parallel-hybrid-excited PM machine with harmonic-differential effect has been proposed, in which the dc-field windings in the dc pole are sandwiched by two adjacent PM poles so that the dc-field harmonics can differentiate the effective and ineffective harmonics in the airgap to weaken the resultant effective magnetic field, hence achieving excellent flux-weakening ability and wide speed-operating range [J2]. Moreover, a new flux-reversal PM motor with magnetic differential (MagD) has been proposed, in which the dual-rotor structure can realize electronic differential action, making the system more compact and reliable [C4]. Concerning the machine analysis for this project, we have newly analyzed the parallel-hybrid-excited PM harmonic-shift machine from the perspective of field modulation, which reveals the relationship among the effective harmonics, dominant harmonics and pole-pairs [J3]. On the other hand, a new nonlinear varying-network magnetic circuit method has been proposed for various hybrid-excited PM machines, which can analytically calculate the three-dimensional magnetic field distribution and hence the machine performance, while taking account of magnetic saturation [J6], [C2]. Moreover, the effect of different PM arrangements in stator-PM machines has been comprehensively analyzed, which reveals that the positions and polarities of PMs can significantly affect the torque, cogging torque, efficiency and immunity of PM demagnetization [J7]. Concerning the system control for this project, we have proposed a novel dual-rotor flux-switching PM motor based MagD system to generate the differential torque between wheels for accurate cornering, which can offer higher efficiency and compactness than the mechanical differential system, while providing higher reliability and safer operation than the existing electronic differential system [J4], [C1]. Various MagD systems have been quantitatively evaluated, revealing that the flux-switching PM version can offer the best overall performance [J8]. Furthermore, the concept of dual-rotor machine system has been extended to flywheel energy storage for EVs, hence achieving high power density and good dynamic performance [C3].

17205518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205518.value: The project has been focused on developing the machine topologies of the dual-rotor stator permanent-magnet (PM) motor system that can offer magnetic differential for electric vehicles (EVs). The corresponding power converters only serve to conduct power regulation for dual-rotor propulsion and steering. These power converters should be further developed in such a way that they can offer independent flux strengthening and flux weakening for individual rotors, hence achieving instantaneous torque boosting for EV acceleration and high-speed constant-power operation for EV cruising. This is one of the areas that needs further development for the proposed dual-rotor motor system. Another important area that needs further development is the fault-tolerant control and limp-home mode of operation for the proposed motor system. Although the dual-rotor system can inherently alleviate the consequence of various failure modes during cornering, the fault-tolerant control should be activated to enable the EV operating at the limp-home mode until reaching home or a service station, which is crucial to success of the proposed system.

17205518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205518.value: The use of direct-drive motors for individual driving wheels of electric vehicles (EVs) is attractive to provide the action of electronic differential, which can eliminate the bulky and heavy mechanical differential. However, this electronic differential suffers from two fundamental problems – reliability and safety concerns – that hinder its practical application. In particular, if there is an unpredictable error in controlling one of the motors during cornering, the consequence will be disastrous. The use of dual-rotor motors for EV propulsion is becoming attractive because it not only improves the overall torque density, but also provides a way to improve the electronic differential. The project has successfully developed a novel class of dual-rotor stator-PM motor systems for EVs with the magnetic differential action. The key is the concept of magnetic steering mechanism in which the motor for the left wheel can be integrated with the motor for the right wheel to form a novel machine structure with two rotors, which are magnetically coupled together to ensure the reliability and hence safety. Hence, this magnetic differential can retain the reliability of mechanical differential, while offering higher reliability and safety than the state-of-the-art electronic differential.

17206218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206218.value: Creating 3D digital contents, including 3D object and scene models, from scratch is often a labor-intensive and time-consuming task. In certain application scenarios such as role-playing games, social media and 3D printing, amateur users wish to prepare custom-made avatars and object models themselves. Due to the massive demand of personalized 3D contents generated by amateur users in such scenarios, low-cost modeling tools with user-friendly interfaces are still much favored. Sketch-based 3D modeling tools belong to this category and have been paid much attention in the research community. Since there exist correlations between different components of a certain type of objects, it is crucial to employ machine learning to understand such correlations from data and let them guide labor-efficient sketch-based modeling. As a type of machine learning methods, deep learning has a strong generalization capability and can robustly handle rough and noisy sketches created by amateur users. Deep learning is also capable of inferring semantic meanings. In this project, we propose a hybrid approach for sketch-based 3D modeling. We treat a 2D sketch as an image, and first run a deep neural network on the raw pixels to recognize the shape in the sketch and meanwhile generate an initial 3D model according to the correlations between sketched lines and the rest of the model surface. However, although deep neural networks are very good at high-level inference, we do not expect them to be very precise in terms of feature localization and local shape reconstruction. Our hybrid approach improves the model generated by the DNN in these aspects by explicitly enforcing shape constraints imposed by the lines and curves in the input sketch through deformation. In this project, we plan to focus on objects characterized by curvilinear structures, including faces and a large subset of man-made objects, and investigate single-view and multi-view sketch-based modeling based on this hybrid approach. The outcomes of our proposed research will significantly advance the state of the art of sketch interfaces for modeling objects characterized by curvilinear structures. We also plan to improve relevant deep learning and 3D computer vision algorithms and make them better suited for sketch-based modeling. The proposed research has important practical impact. If our project is successful, publications resulting from our work will likely have influence on future versions of commercial interactive modeling software. 從零開始創建3D數字內容，包括3D對象和場景模型通常是一個勞動密集和耗時的任務。在諸如角色扮演遊戲、社交媒體和3D列印等特定應用場景中，業餘用戶希望自己製作定制的化身和物件模型。由於這種場景下業餘用戶產生的個性化3D內容的巨大需求，具有用戶友好介面的低成本建模工具仍然備受青睞。 基於草圖的三維建模工具屬於這一類，在研究領域備受關注。由於一類模型的不同組件之間存在相關性，從數據中學習這種相關性是至關重要的，並且讓它們指導高效的基於草圖的建模。傳統的機器學習算法通常難以處理業餘用戶創建的粗略和嘈雜的草圖，而深度學習具有很强的泛化能力，並且可以更可靠地處理雜訊輸入。此外，眾所周知，深度學習能够推斷語義。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種基於草圖的三維建模的混合方法。我們將2D草圖作為影像，首先在原始像素上運行一個深度神經網络來識別草圖中的形狀，同時根據草圖線與模型表面的其餘部分之間的關係生成初始3D模型。然而，雖然深度神經網络非常擅長高級推理，我們並不期望它們在特徵定位和局部形狀重構方面非常精確。因此，我們的混合方法改進了DNN在這些方面所產生的模型，通過變形顯式地執行輸入草圖中的線條和曲線所施加的形狀約束。在這個項目中，我們計畫著眼於人臉和人造物體，研究基於這種混合方法的草圖建模技术。 我們的研究成果將推進人臉和人造物體的基于草圖建模的研究現狀。我們還計畫改進相關的深度學習和3D计算机視覺算法，使之更適合於基於草圖的建模。这项研究具有重要的實際影響。如果我們的項目获得成功，從我們的工作產生的论文可能會影響未來的商業互動式建模軟件。

17206218.label: Realisation of objectives
17206218.value: During this project, we have investigated and completed the three revised objectives. 1) As the outcome of the first objective, we have fully developed a novel sketching system for 3D face and caricature modeling. This system has a labor-efficient sketching interface, and automatic 3D face model inference is based on both deep learning techniques and constraint-based surface deformation techniques. We have constructed a significantly expanded version of a public face database called FaceWarehouse. To increase the diversity of expressions, we chose 11 expressions with relatively noticeable mutual differences from the original 20 expressions, and asked an artist to create 14 new expressions in caricature styles on a neutral face. We apply three different scaling factors to the original shapes to obtain shapes at three higher levels of exaggeration. In summary, our database has 15,000 meshes, which include 150 identities, 25 expressions and 4 levels of exaggeration. All meshes are well registered with exactly the same topology. The user interface of our sketching system supports the following three interaction modes for coarse-to-fine face modeling: initial sketching mode, follow-up sketching mode and gesture-based refinement mode. A complete interactive modeling session in our system only requires drawing, erasing and clicking. Our sketching system takes a hybrid approach and integrates deep learning based high-level 3D model inference with more precise handle-based shape deformation techniques. As the deep learning component, a novel CNN based deep regression network has been designed for inferring 3D face models from 2D sketches. The input to our deep regression network is a 256x256 binary sketch image. The output from our deep regression network is a pair of u and v vectors for the bilinear face representation, which eventually reconstructs all 3D vertices of a face mesh. Our regression network includes multiple convolutional layers to extract features from the input sketch image. These convolutional layers are set up in the same way as in AlexNet. To avoid interference between the identity mode and the expression mode, our deep network has two independent branches with different numbers of fully connected layers for generating the u and v vectors. The branch for generating the u vector has three new fully connected layers while the branch for the v vector only has one new fully connected layer as the complexity of the identity mode (600 shapes) is much higher than the complexity of the expression mode (25 types). Each fully connected layer in both branches has 1024 neurons, which was set empirically to achieve the optimal performance. 2) As the outcome of the second revised objective, we introduce the first real-time sketching system for interactive personalized and photorealistic face caricaturization. Given a real image of a human face as the input, the user can create personalized caricature photos by manipulating its facial feature curves. Our system first reconstructs an underlying 3D face model for the input image using an existing approach. Then our system produces a photorealistic 2D caricature in three steps: texture mapping the 3D model using the input image, 3D textured face exaggeration, re-rendering the exaggerated face as a 2D image. To tackle the core problem of sketch-based face exaggeration, we introduce a deep learning based solution, where the training data consists of differential encodings of both the input sketches and their corresponding exaggerated 3D face models. Since meshes have irregular connectivities unsuitable for efficient deep learning algorithms, these encodings are defined as images over a 2D parametric domain of the face, and face exaggeration is cast as an image-to-image translation problem. To support network training, a large synthetic dataset of sketch-to-exaggeration pairs is created. We also propose effective solutions to address technical problems encountered during face image re-rendering. First, to fix incorrect shading effects due to facial geometry changes, an optimization algorithm is developed to find an optimal pixel-wise shading scaling field in the nose and cheek regions where the normal undergoes large changes. Second, insufficient texture resolution caused by face exaggeration usually makes certain local regions in the re-rendered image blurry. Deep learning based image-to-image translation is exploited again to handle this problem by learning to infer missing high-frequency details in such blurry regions. To achieve real-time performance required by our sketching interface, we divide the input photo into overlapping patches and run a lightweight pix2pix network by Isola et al. on individual patches separately. Third, inconsistencies between regions with underlying 3D model and those without result in artifacts especially on facial boundaries, ears and hair regions. To remove such artifacts, we first generate two images, one obtained by applying 2D warping guided by the underlying 3D mesh deformation and the other obtained by re-rendering the deformed 3D textured model. These two images are then seamlessly integrated to produce our final output. 3) As the outcome of the third revised objective, we introduce a sketch-based modeling system for generic man-made objects characterized by curvilinear structures. Such objects often have complex structures which consist of many parts. The user interface of our system decomposes the task of sketch-based modelling into two interaction phases, namely, part sketching and part assembling. In the part sketching phase, users can sketch and create each part of an object separately through interacting with the frontend of the system running in the browser using a mouse or a graphics tablet. In the part assembly phase, users can tune the translation and scale of each object part starting from an automatic assembly inferred by the backend of the system. To support the aforementioned user interface, we propose a deep learning method for sketch-based part generation and assembly. The pipeline of our algorithm consists of two parts: 1. a part generation module to produce a 3D mesh for each single part sketch; 2. a part assembly module to recover the position and scale of each part mesh with respect to the complete 3D object. The part generation module takes a part sketch as input and estimates the corresponding 3D mesh. We represent 3D shapes as occupancy fields in space. For each 3D object, we provide our network with the sketches of part shapes and the segmented ground-truth part shapes for training. For each part sketch, we crop the sketch content and move it to the centre of the image, then resize the image to the size of 224 × 224, and train a ResNet18 to encode the image into a 256-d feature, which is subsequently concatenated with sampled 3D points in the shape space and fed into OccNet to predict the occupancy probability of each point. The input of the part assembler consists of three portions: the whole sketch, the part sketch, and the part shape produced by the above generator. We concatenate the whole and part sketches, and use ResNet18 to extract the sketch feature. Then a 3D CNN encoder is applied to the occupancy prediction of the part shape to obtain the geometric feature. The sketch and geometric features are concatenated and fed to an MLP network to regress the 3D assembly information (i.e. part centre position and the radius (scale) of the part bounding box). Once all parts have been scaled and translated to the specified position, a holistic mesh can be extracted from an implicit field by the Marching Cubes algorithm.

17206218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206218.value: 1) The first research output in Part C introduces the first comprehensive easy-to-use sketching system for interactive creation of personalized and photorealistic caricatures from photographs. Our system is made possible by a suite of novel techniques for 3D face exaggeration, exaggerated face re-shading, and artifact-free caricature synthesis. Two datasets are built for training and testing deep neural networks used in our sketching system. The first one is a large synthetic dataset for training the deep network that maps sparse sketches to a dense exaggeration map. The second one is a dataset of high-resolution (1080p and above) portrait photos for training the deep network that synthesizes high-frequency details for facial textures with insufficient resolution. 2) The second research output in Part C introduces a novel and easy-to-use sketching system to model part-composited man-made objects, which helps users freely design models with complex structures and detailed geometry. This system decouples the task of sketch2shape into a part generation module and a part assembling module, and deep learning methods are leveraged for the implementation of both modules. 3) The third research output in Part C introduces a novel easy-to-use sketching interface for modeling animal-like 3D character heads. Our system allows users to draw on canvases from scratch to obtain quality synthesized results with instant feedback. It also provides plentiful tools to post-manipulate generated surfaces. It also includes the first 3D animal head model dataset, containing 220 well-collected models in 19 animal categories. The number of further augmented models is 16,800. Each model is also associated with line-drawing renderings in orthographic views, and 1,200 models with hand-drawn sketches. 4) The fourth research output in Part C introduces a sketching system that enables amateur users to model high-fidelity 3D faces in minutes. First, curvature-aware strokes are adopted in the system to better control facial detail carving. Second, we develop a novel learning-based method termed "Implicit and Depth Guided Mesh Modeling" (IDGMM) for mapping a 2D sketch to a 3D model. It fuses the advantages of mesh, implicit, and depth representations to achieve high-quality results with high efficiency. In addition, to further support usability, we design a coarse-to-fine 2D sketching interface and a data-driven stroke suggestion tool. User studies demonstrate the superiority of our system over existing modeling tools in terms of the ease to use and visual quality of results. Experimental analyses also show that IDGMM reaches a better trade-off between accuracy and efficiency.

17206218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206218.value: Creating 3D digital contents, including 3D object and scene models, from scratch is often a labor-intensive and time-consuming task. In application scenarios such as role-playing games, social media and 3D printing, amateur users wish to prepare custom-made avatars and object models themselves. Due to the massive demand of personalized 3D contents generated by amateur users in such scenarios, low-cost modeling tools with user-friendly interfaces are still much favored. Thus sketch-based modeling is an important research topic in computer graphics, and has been paid much attention in the research community. The proposed approach for modeling objects characterized by curvilinear structures, including faces and a large subset of man-made objects, promotes a labor-efficient sketch interface, and advances the state of the art of sketch-based modeling. Our project also has important practical values and is likely to have a positive impact on the industry. The sheer demand of massive user-generated 3D contents has pushed the industry to release all sorts of user-friendly modeling software, including Autodesk Tinkercad and Trimble SketchUp (previous Google SketchUp).
