17206418.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206418.value: The project has resulted in high-quality first-hand data and new findings as summarized below. Nine papers have been published in reputable journals and one paper published as a book chapter, with another two papers under review by international journals. The results also contribute to a number of invited talks by the PI at international conferences/workshops and universities. Three PhD students (two graduated and one to submit the thesis in a few months), two post-docs and one undergraduate student have been trained in the framework of this project. • For all clean sands and sand-fines mixtures investigated, four distinct failure patterns have been consistently observed from the undrained cyclic triaxial tests, namely flow-type failure, limited flow failure, plastic strain accumulation, and cyclic mobility. For a given type of sand–fines mixture, the failure pattern can turn from cyclic mobility to flow-type failure by varying the percentage of fines while the void ratio is kept the same. • For both clean and silty sand specimens, the liquefaction resistance in terms of CRR can be well related to the state parameter defined in the context of critical state soil mechanics. A significant advantage of the state parameter-based framework is the capability to unify different material properties such as fines content and particle characteristics. In addition, the effect of the initial static shear stress can also be taken into account in a rational way. • For each of the tested clean sand, the shear wave velocity of sand is affected by the quantity of fines apart from the void ratio and confining stress. Under similar confining pressure and void ratio, the shear wave velocity decreases with fines content. By using the state parameter and by correcting shear wave velocity for stress level, a unique relationship can be established between the corrected shear wave velocity and the state parameter which is independent of fines content. The relationship contains three constants that reflect the influence of particle characteristics of the material. • The relationship between liquefaction resistance and state parameter is approximately the same for different sand-fines mixtures tested, but the relationship between liquefaction resistance and the stress corrected shear wave velocity appears to be slightly dependent on the grain characteristics of the material. The experimental data suggests that, different from the current empirical chart, no upper limiting value of the stress corrected shear wave velocity exists.

17206418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206418.value: Most of the laboratory experiments were conducted on specimens prepared using the moist tamping method. Since the liquefaction resistance is affected by sample preparation methods, further extensive research to investigate the effect of sample preparation on the shear wave velocity of both clean and silty sands as well as on the relationship between liquefaction resistance and shear wave velocity would be worthwhile. The effect of sample preparation method is associated with the fabric effect which is a fundamental issue in the mechanics of granular materials. Given the difficulties in laboratory quantification of the fabric, extensive theoretical and numerical studies are needed.

17206418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206418.value: Seismic soil liquefaction remains an area of great difficulty in earthquake engineering. It may cause huge damage to infrastructure systems that are vital for the safety and economy of our societies. In the 2010-2011 Christchurch, New Zealand earthquake and the 2011 East Japan earthquake, the financial losses caused by the liquefaction hazard exceeded billions of dollars. This project was aimed at developing a new approach to evaluating the liquefaction potential of silty sand depositsa major concern arising from recent large earthquakes. The new approach is based on measurements of shear wave velocity and is developed from a comprehensive experimental program comprising small-strain shear wave testing and large-strain undrained shear tests for sand samples with varying fines contents. A novel point of the method is the unified characterization of shear wave velocity for both clean sand and silty sand through a state parameter defined in a sound theoretical context. As modern technology has made it more convenient and reliable to measure the shear wave velocity both in the laboratory and in the field, and since the state parameter is a rational index for characterizing soil behavior, the new approach is promising in a wide range of geotechnical applications.

17206518.label: Realisation of objectives
17206518.value: This project supported us to develop a TEC, named direct thermal charging cell (DTCC), using graphene oxide/platinum (GO/PtNPs) anode and polyaniline PANI cathode and aqueous Fe2+/Fe3+-based redox electrolyte for heat-to-electricity conversion, achieving a ηE of 2.8% at 70 °C (21.4% of ηcarnot). DTCC has a unique feature of thermal charging and electrical discharging under high temperatures and then can be self-regenerated when cooled down to realize the cycle. In the configuration of DTTC, using PANI with positive α as the anode would decrease thermal-voltage generation when heating at open-circuit potential. Additionally, the relatively low conductivity of the reduced form of PANI hinders the electron transport during oxidation process when discharging, thus limiting the discharge capacity. Moreover, PANI with multiple oxidation states may be over-oxidized when operating at a higher potential, so it is difficult to return to its original and consistent status by chemical reduction in each cycle. Accordingly, we further employed FeII-based nickel hexacyanoferrate (NiHCFeII) as a battery-like anode because it is a highly reversible material with negative α and an electrochemical potential lower than GO, which fits the design configuration of DTCC. Nickel hexacyanoferrate (NiHCFe) is a Prussian blue analogue with an open framework that allows the redox reactions to occur through ion (i.e. Na+ and K+) intercalation/extraction and produces a large current.14 Therefore, the formulated Fe2+/Fe3+-based redox electrolyte can be replaced by a neutral, safe, and environmentally friendly KCl or NaCl solution, which is cheap and easily obtained in daily life. This new configuration (denoted as DTCCNCF) enables the green recycling of DTCCs after long-term cycling because NiHCFeII can be quickly regenerated by immersing in NaBH4 solution, and then reassembled into a pouch cell by adding salt water as the electrolyte to realize the next life cycle.

17206818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206818.value: 摘要 膀胱癌的全球死亡率排名第八，其中非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌（NMIBC）佔所有確診膀胱癌病例的80％，一年復發率高達61％，五年復發率達到78％。 NMIBC的標準治療途徑是經尿道切除術（TUR），並且通常與膀胱腔內化療聯合使用。對複發風險高的病例，需要通過膀胱鏡進行嚴格的手術監測。檢查頻率高達每3個月一次，持續2年，然後每6個月一次持續3年，之後每年一次。如果癌症發展為肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌，通常需要完全切除膀胱（根治性膀胱切除術）。手術後，患者的尿液必須通過導管轉移到一個外置泌尿道包中。雖然用新膀胱在體內收集尿液也是可能的，但它需要使用患者50-60cm的小腸來重建。就健康相關的生活質量而言，這兩種尿液導流方式都會造成對患者造成極差的影響。這一事實帶來了對更完整可靠的NMIBC的一線治療的巨大需求。 近年來，納米金（GNP）技術由於其在癌症診斷和治療方面的潛力而得以廣泛應用。腫瘤表現出的脈管系統擴大為藥衣包被的GNP提供了切入點，並使得GNP在腫瘤內的滲透和積聚成為可能。其中，GNP被發現在稱為光熱療法（PTT）中發揮出消融腫瘤細胞的能力。GNP粒子在近紅外（NIR）光譜中具有很強的吸收能力，因此，當NIR激光照射到腫瘤內積聚的GNP上時，GNP產生的熱量可以破壞癌細胞。但是，由於NIR激光器的穿透深度低，將NIR激光器輸送到身體內更深處的區域（例如膀胱）是個較難解決的問題，而且PTT對附近健康組織的熱擴散控制尚未得到很好的研究。為此，我們提出採用機器人輔助內窺鏡技術和消融控制方法，借助於術中MRI來發揮GNP對膀胱目標區域的消融能力。 這個項目的總體目標是開發並驗證一種磁力共振(MR)條件下可用的膀胱鏡機器人系統。這套系統可以將NIR激光能量傳遞到膀胱中的特定腫瘤目標。這套機器人系統將由流體和肌腱驅動，並將由基於磁力共振掃瞄儀(MRI)的手術路線圖引導。這套系統將首次協同結合小型化射頻線圈跟踪和光纖布拉格光柵(FBG)形狀識別技術，以增強術中MRI下膀胱鏡的三維位置追踪。應用於GNP的MRI對比劑還將能夠在手術中有效定位消融目標。在膀胱鏡頂端的新型軟體線性驅動器能夠實現可調的激光投射。通過結合高保真膀胱鏡、基於學習的反饋控制方法和MR環境下的組織熱擴散模型，可以實現精確而完整的腫瘤消融，同時令過熱傳導對附近健康組織造成的損害減至最低。對於這套系統的驗證將會在實驗室環境和MRI環境下進行，並分別使用膀胱模型，離體豬膀胱和活豬樣本。 該研究可作為MRI引導機器人輔助PTT的第一步，為推進其在身體其他區域（不限於膀胱）的癌症治療上的應用提供技術支撐。成功引入PTT作為標準治療將可以減少對化學治療劑的依賴，減少治療持續的時間，改善患者的生活質量。

17206818.label: Realisation of objectives
17206818.value: 1) MR-conditional robotic laser steering platform for photothermal ablation: The major objectives of this project are to enable the plan for cystoscope/endoscope navigation and accurately steer/sweep the implemented laser (e.g., near-infrared (NIR) laser) for photothermal ablation. PI and his collaborators have developed an MR-conditional soft robotic system for MRI-guided transoral laser microsurgery with an optical endoscopic camera, as a similar platform for photothermal therapy of bladder cancer. Owing to its miniature size (Ø12 × 100 mm), inherent compliance, and five degrees of freedom (DoFs), the soft robot ensures zero electromagnetic interference with MRI and enables safe and dexterous operation within the confined oral and pharyngeal cavities. The laser manipulator was rapidly fabricated with hybrid soft and hard structures and enables laser steering with enhanced stiffness and lowered hysteresis. A learning-based closed-loop controller accommodates the inherent nonlinear robot actuation, which was validated with laser path–following tests. Submillimeter laser steering accuracy was demonstrated with a mean error < 0.20 mm. MRI compatibility testing demonstrated zero observable image artifacts during robot operation. A cadaveric head-and-neck trial and ex vivo tissue ablation tests were carried out under MRI, where MR thermometry was employed to monitor the tissue ablation margin and thermal diffusion intraoperatively. 2) Visual servoing closed-loop control scheme for cystoscope tip: The team also proposed an epipolar-geometry-based visual servoing algorithm for soft endoscopic/cystoscopic manipulators, and had it tested for laser photothermal ablation. The visual servoing controller allows automatic laser spot steering using soft manipulators. The epipolar geometry model was established to acquire the inverse transition mapping from image to actuation. With this mapping, a closed-loop controller was derived without prior information of tissue surface geometry. Experimental validation demonstrates accurate path following using an MR-conditional manipulator, with root-mean-square (RMS) tracking errors <4 pixels (140 μm) in the camera view. This is maintained even throughout 70 repeated cycles, with a maximum tracking error <11.32 pixels (~396.2 μm). The controller enables laser spot following of the mouse cursor with a root-mean-square (RMS) tracking error of 3.97 pixels (~180.5 μm). Ex vivo tissue ablation tests were conducted to validate the photothermal ablation pattern, with an RMS tracking error of about 5.75 pixels (~201.3 μm). A laser ablation test was conducted under MRI to validate the feasibility of MRI-guided laser photothermal ablation. 3) Shape tracking and closed-loop control under MRI: To achieve 3D shape and positional tracking under MRI, the team designed a shape-tracking system that integrates a multicore fiber Bragg grating (FBG) fiber and miniaturized wireless radiofrequency (RF) coils, and tested it using a standard cardiac catheter. A learning-based modeling method was proposed for continuum manipulators (e.g., cystoscopes), which uses FBG-reconstructed three-dimensional curvatures for model initialization. The modeling method was implemented on an MRI-guided robotic platform to achieve closed-loop control of a cardiac catheter. The shape-tracking performance was experimentally verified, demonstrating a 2.33° average error for each sensing segment and 1.53 mm positional accuracy at the catheter tip. A corresponding closed-loop control performance was tested by autonomous targeting and path following (average deviation of 0.62 mm) tasks, proving the ability to be implemented on cystoscopes in the future. The overall performance of the integrated robotic system was validated by a pulmonary vein isolation simulator with ex-vivo tissue ablation, which employed a left atrial phantom with pulsatile liquid flow. Continuum robot tracking and closed-loop control tests were conducted in an MRI scanner, demonstrating the capability of the proposed system under MRI. 4) MR-conditional FUS robotic platform for photothermal ablation: Focused ultrasound (FUS) technology has also been accredited for the non-invasive and painless treatment of tumors deep inside the body. The high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) spot could be “steered” to ablate large (>Ø 3.5 cm) or multiple tumors (e.g., in liver). The team has developed a hydraulic-driven teleoperated robot platform that enables 5-DoF manipulation of the FUS transducer. Even operated close to the MRI iso-center, the robot can guarantee zero electromagnetic (EM) artifact to the MR image. The proof-of-concept robot prototype can offer a large workspace (100 mm × 100 mm × 35 mm) for FUS foci steering. Accurate manipulation (0.2 mm in translation, 0.4° in rotation) of the FUS transducer holder was achieved using rolling diaphragm-sealed hydraulic actuators. The robot control responsiveness (from 0.1 to 4 Hz) was also evaluated to show the potential to compensate for the spot-tracking error induced by respiratory motion. The use of wireless radiofrequency (RF) markers was demonstrated to continuously register the robot task space in the MRI coordinates. 5) Miniature robotic arms for ESD and ERBT The team developed the first surgical robotic instruments in Hong Kong to target endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and en bloc resection of bladder tumor (ERBT) procedures. The long, flexible, and miniature robotic arms with five DoFs have enhanced tissue traction and instrument triangulation. Since the robotic arms also include a variety of end effectors, they can complete a wide range of intricate tasks. They realize seamless compatibility as each robotic arm is less than 2.8 mm in diameter, therefore they can directly channel through or alongside conventional endoscopes currently used in clinical practice. The extremely narrow diameter of the robotic arms allowed their compatibility with traditional urology telescopes and sheaths, and the arms were able to clamp and cut tumor tissue. The surgeon console is both compact and mobile, allowing for its placement within close proximity to the patient. Furthermore, with free-floating pen controllers, seamless transition from endoscope/cystoscope controls can be achieved. Live animal trial and cadaveric tests have been completed, which involved artificial bladder tumor resection.

17206818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206818.value: A miniature MR-conditional endoscopic robotic system and its visual servoing controller for photothermal steering have been developed, which enables precise steering. Cadaveric trial and ex vivo ablation tests were conducted under MRI, using MR thermometry to monitor the ablation margin and thermal diffusion intraoperatively. The closed-loop controller needs no prior knowledge of tissue-surface geometry and demonstrates robustness to actuation disturbances. Accurate path following was accomplished, with RMS errors <4 pixels in camera view (physical errors <140 μm). It brings new opportunities for precise photothermal ablation using soft manipulators, which could be equipped on endoscope/cystoscope tips. Its MRI compatibility enables MRI-guided photothermal treatments, enhancing the intra-op monitoring of ablation outcomes. Shape tracking and closed-loop control for continuum manipulators under MRI have been established. The flexible configuration can be obtained from a multicore FBG fiber and positional (MRI-based) tracking coils, and was subsequently incorporated with an MR-conditional robotic system for testing. Learning-based modeling uses FBG for characterization, resolving uncertainties from parameter tuning and tendon backlash. Shape sensing achieves a 2.33° average error and 1.53 mm tip positional error. Path following accuracy is 0.62 mm (max. 2.34 mm). A study with a pulmonary vein isolation simulator and ex-vivo tissue ablation shows its feasibility in dynamic environments. Such shape tracking can be further implemented on any continuum manipulators under MRI. Periodic motions of robotic systems have been analyzed and feedback algorithms have been developed for stabilization/tracking control. The periodic piecewise time-varying modeling method can accommodate nonlinear robot actuation and periodic disturbances. A polynomial blossoming approach is proposed to design stabilizing controllers, proven effective in tackling multiple time-varying coefficients. The proposed method provides an alternative when complex time-varying structures are involved. A general safety framework based on reachable set estimation is proposed, where a Bernstein polynomial approach is first applied to estimate the safety constraints. The proposed approach has been proven less conservative in reachable set estimating and boundary optimization. The first surgical robotic instruments in Hong Kong for ESD and ERBT have been proposed and tested. The long flexible arms with five DoFs enhanced tissue traction and instrument triangulation. Each robotic arm is less than 2.8 mm in diameter, allowing its compatibility with conventional standard urology telescopes and sheath. The arms were able to clamp and cut tumor tissue. Compact and mobile surgeon console enables the placement within close proximity to the patient. Live animal trial and cadaveric tests have been completed, including bladder tumor resection.

17206818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206818.value: In future work, we will investigate the influence of MRI sequence parameters on imaging of tissue being photothermal ablated. Real-time tracking under MRI will be incorporated to enable registration between MRI images and robotic navigation. We aim to incorporate the fast streaming of MRI scanning data, thus interfacing with various types of MR imaging feedback (e.g., MR thermometry) in real time. It would give additional information for monitoring the heat diffusion process, thus further enhancing the photothermal ablation safety. Visual servoing based on MR-thermometry will also be of our interest. Proper surgical laser sources, e.g., pulsed laser and NIR laser, will be investigated to achieve tissue cutting or photothermal ablation in cooperation with laser beam manipulation. We also intend to improve the laser spot control performance by decoupling the velocity profile and path following. In the aspect of sensing, the proposed shape tracking and closed-loop controller will be adapted to commercial MR-conditional systems and robotic cystoscopes that deliver NIR laser energy for photothermal therapy of bladder cancer. The proposed shape tracking method would provide sufficient feedback for visualization and robotic control under MRI, potentially reducing workload of the surgeon as well as postprocedural disease recurrence.

17206818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206818.value: The proposed MR-conditional soft robotic system for MRI-guided laser microsurgery can adapt to the confirmed workspace in human body and conduct precise laser steering and ablation to deal with tumors. The miniature design can be equipped on endoscope/cystoscope tip. Owing to MRI compatibility, the soft laser manipulator can be guided by intra-operative MRI, which could enhance the visualization and monitoring of laser ablation outcomes. The proposed epipolar-geometry-based visual servoing control scheme can be used to steer the laser projection, thus enabling complicated laser ablation patterns. The pattern can even be customized in situ by the cursor in the camera view, facilitating the surgeon’s operation. No prior information of tissue surface geometry will be needed, even when the tissue surface is extremely uneven. 3D shape tracking of long flexible manipulators under MRI is accomplished by a type of optical fiber and miniaturized thin-film coils, providing both intuitive visualization and quantitative positional feedback for real-time closed-loop control of the manipulator body. The thin (diameter 0.2 mm) fiber can be integrated into any interventional manipulator without being limited by size, while the coils (6.7×1.5×0.3 mm3) for localization can be easily attached on the manipulator body.

17207018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207018.value: 我們的世界充滿了數據，這些數據通常出現在高維結構中 。例子包括社會科學，醫學，藥理學和環境監測方面的數據 。為了理解多維數據，我們需要先進的計算工具來找出數據背後隱藏的規律。這正是張量子空間學習發揮作用的地方。張量子空間學習是一個新興研究題目，研究從多維數據中提取低維但基本信息。由於過去十年張量子空間學習算法的進步，以及其相對傳統矩陣數據處理的優越性能，張量子空間學習在不同的工程領域中找到了許多應用，包括醫學圖像處理，電路設計，無線通信網絡，金融數據分析和社交網絡研究。 目前，大多數張量子空間學習算法是以批量處理模式操作。但是在大數據時代， 數據集非常龐大， 以至於它們無法被放入計算機的內存中，使得批量處理算法在面對大量數據時無用。這只留下一個選項：開發在線張量子空間學習算法。在這些算法中，開始時只會用少量數據，然後每當新數據到來，子空間會被更新。這需要一種嚴格的更新機制, 但當前的張量子空間學習方法無法提供這種機制，特別是當我們對子空間的秩（或維度）不確定時。 事實上，確定子空間的秩是子空間學習問題的一部分，但是目前該領域的大多數研究只是假設秩已知。為了克服這一挑戰，本項目負責人最近探索了張量子空間學習的概率模型，並以批量處理模式規範多元分解（CPD）為例，成功地證明了秩的確定可以完美地合併到子空間學習過程中。 加上概率模型推理具有新數據的更新能力，因此非常適合於在線子空間學習。 憑藉這種相對於當前方法的範式轉移優勢，此項目提出從概率模型框架開發在線張量子空間學習算法，其中自動秩確定是一個重要特徵。在所有張量子空間模型中，CPD被選擇作為此項目的焦點，因為它是一個基本模型，並且在CPD上開發的見解可以很容易被擴展到其他模型。此項目的結果不僅代表了張量子空間學習的最新技術，而且算法的軟件也將在互聯網上共享，令 任何對張量子空間學習感興趣的人都受益。

17207018.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207018.value: We have successfully formulated and derived a Bayesian Canonical Polyadic Decomposition (CPD) with non-negative factors with the ability to automatically identify the rank. Due to the inadequacy of the current probabilistic modeling on handling non-negative values, we have established the non-negative Gaussian gamma distribution, and investigated its properties. Furthermore, to handle large-scale data, we also make use of projected gradient and Nesterov acceleration scheme to speed up the algorithm. After published the above work in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, we further identified a link between the proposed method and the inexact block coordinate descent (BCD) framework. This relationship is non-trivial as our developed model is based on Bayesian method while inexact BCD is based on optimization theories. Despite the difference, we managed to show that the expectation of the variational distribution in our method is exactly the result from BCD update step. With this newly established link, we applied inexact BCD to our method so that the algorithm is accelerated 5 to 6 times without loss of performance. The corresponding result was published in the journal Signal Processing. We have applied the developed algorithm to different applications, including fluorescence data analysis, and ENRON e-mail data mining. Furthermore, we have applied the Bayesian framework to the channel estimation problem of massive MIMO communication systems. It is for the first time, such problem is connected with tensor CPD modelling. A tailored algorithm is derived such that the number of paths in the channel can be identified. Simulation experiments show that the proposed CPD model exhibits better performance than state of the arts methods. The results on massive MIMO communication systems were published in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing. All the related Matlab codes have been released in the PI’s website.

17207018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207018.value: The proposed research topic Canonical Polyadic Decomposition (CPD) has been well investigated. But in general, there are other tensor decomposition format, such as Tucker, PARAFAC2 and Tensor Train. These formats also lack Bayesian treatment. Based on the insights developed from this project, we are ready to tackle other decomposition formats. In fact, we have started some of the studies, and preliminary results have been reported in recent conference papers. Further investigation will be carried out and journal papers are aimed for the more complete results.

17207018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207018.value: This project developed a machine learning model for discovering the hidden pattern of data appearing in three or more-dimensional structure. Due to the potentially large-scale data in the real world, this project emphasizes on low-complexity algorithms. The developed methods have been applied to fluorescence data analysis, e-mail data mining, and 5th generation wireless communication system, to show their effectiveness. The developed software is also open to public so that other researchers can directly make use of the results as off-the-self programs, without being impeded by the theory and implementation details.

17207518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207518.value: Investigation of an actual man-made slope failure disaster is important for us to learn more lessons for understanding failure mechanism, for designing slopes better, and for clarifying responsibilities for different parties involving the failure case. This study aims to further investigate a catastrophic man-made slope failure disaster, occurred on December 20, 2015 at Hengtaiyu Industrial Park, Shenzhen, PR China. Fill soils 2.7 million m3 in volume forming the upper portion of the slope rapidly slipped in a motion resembling a huge mass of fluid material flowing out of a narrow gate from a gourd-shaped reservoir. The soil debris buried 33 buildings on the vast area of flat ground in front of the slope toe, which resulted in 73 fatalities, 4 missing, and 17 injured. The disaster was investigated by a government team on behalf of the State Council of PR China. The official forensic investigation report was published by State Administration of Work Safety of PR China on July 15, 2016. The government report is mainly concentrated on the presence of excessive pore water (pressure) in the fill soils for the failure mechanism. This report led to the sentencing to up to 20 years in jail of 45 individuals involved in the design, construction and management of the slope by Shenzhen municipal courts on May 5, 2017. The PI has also investigated the disaster and his preliminary results indicate much more lessons can be learned in addition to those given in the government report. They include (1) the slope failure occurred in the middle of the dry-season; (2) prior to the slope failure from December 10 to 20, 2015, the slope site almost had no rainfall; (3) the overall angle of the fill slope was between 9 and 15 degree and is less than the 15 degree minimum angle for registration as potentially dangerous fill slope in Hong Kong Slope Safety System; (4) The fill soils are common in Shenzhen and Hong Kong and; (5) similar soils have formed many man-made slopes with steeper angles here. Recognising its importance to science, engineering and society, therefore, the PI will undertake further investigations in this study for learning more lessons from this disaster case. They would benefit people in Hong Kong and globally. 對人造斜坡破壞災難事件的調查研究是非常重要。它可使得我們在更好地理解斜坡破壞機理、更好地設計斜坡、和澄清與斜坡破壞事件相關各方責任等方面獲取更多的科學新認識。 本研究旨在進一步調查一次特別重大的人造填土斜坡破壞災難事件。它于2015年12月20日發生在深圳恒泰裕工業園區。災難發生時，計有270萬立方米的渣土從人造極緩傾角填土斜坡上部快速下滑，土體如同流體一樣從葫蘆形填土庫的狹窄閘口快速流出滑下。快速運動的大量渣土有力地推倒並掩埋了在斜坡前方、遠方開闊平地上的33座建築物，導致了73人死亡，4人失踪，17人受傷。 針對這場重大災難，國務院成立了事件調查組。2016年7月15日，國家安全生産監督管理總局公布了事件調查組的調查報告。該報告主要關注填土斜坡中存在超孔隙水（壓力），認爲地下水是導致斜坡破壞的原因。2017年5月5日，深圳市法院依據該事故調查報告，判處45名相關責任人最高20年不等的有期徒刑。 本項目負責人也調查了這次災難事件。初步研究結果表明，除調查組報告中的經驗教訓外，還有更多的經驗教訓可以吸取。它們包括，（1）這次斜坡破壞發生在乾旱季節中期；（2）從2015年12月10日到20日破壞發生前，該地區幾乎沒有降雨；（3）該填土斜坡的整體坡度在9至15度之間、小於香港斜坡安全系統所規定的潛在危險填土斜坡15度坡角下限值；（4）在深圳和香港，這樣的填土斜坡很常見；（5）並且，這裏有大量用同樣土構成的、坡角大於15度的人造斜坡。 在認識到這次斜坡破壞災難在科學、工程和社會重要性的基礎上，本項目將做進一步調查研究，以從這次災難事件中獲取更多科學新知識。這些科學新知識會使得包括香港人民在內的全球人民受益。

17207518.label: Realisation of objectives
17207518.value: Objective 1: The research team carried out site assessments, soil sampling, gas sampling, topographical survey and the buried gas pipeline assessment at the landslide site on the following dates: 2015 (December 23), 2016 (January 4 and 9; March 8; April 8; June 8; November 23), 2017 (April 8; September 17; October 9; November 4), 2018 (September 30), 2019 (October 5). Laboratory tests were conducted for the soil shear strength and soil permeability for water seepage under a series of water contents from shrinkage, to plastic, to liquid limit. Slope stability assessment were carried out using both other and our soil parameter values. The rapid and long run-out debris flow was re-simulated and back-analyzed using the 2D Debris Mobility Model developed by GEO. The research team carried out a comprehensive literature review about the landslide and other relevant landslides. The research team summarized the triggering factors, especially water triggering factor from the literature. The team found that the water infiltrated into the fill slope from rainfall was estimated to be about 4.8% to 8.8% volume of the fill soil volume, which is far less than the required water volume of 19 to 21% volume of the fill soil volume estimated with the initial solid volume in fraction dynamic analysis model in literatures. The average water content was from 3.2% to 5.8% under the assumption that all the accumulated rainfall water was infiltrated into the fill soil with an average dry density of 1.5 g/cm3. This water content was far less than the water content in the slope stability analysis model (10% to 23%) and the liquid limit of the fill soil. The research team further proposed and developed a new slip depth plot algorithm for determining the smallest factor of safety (FOS) for soil slopes and analyzed the stability of the fill slope. The research team found that the stability of the fill slope is high for normal soil parameters and it could not be failed without large and dramatic triggering force and energy. The smallest FOS value was obtained using the curve between the potential slip depth and its associated FOS value. The FOS value of a potential slip decreases first and then increases as the slip depth increases from the slope surface to deep depth. This finding is due to the opposite contributions of the soil internal cohesion and the soil internal friction angle to the FOS value with respect to the potential slip depth. The contribution from the internal cohesion decreases rapidly and the contribution from the internal frictional angle increases slowly, as the potential slip increases. Objective 2: The research team carried out a series of small-scaled flume tests to demonstrate the landslide on the gentle soil slope. Three different flume test models are design and tested. The first model A was a 2D model with 1: 900 small scales. It was designed based on the most critical cross-section of the fill slope and the gourd-shaped granitic aggregate quarry pit. Six model tests were carried out for the triggering with gas injection. Each test used different soil models and/or different water contents. The second model B was 3D model with 1:1000 small scales of the actual fill slope. It was designed based on three longitudinal cross-sections and two transverse cross-sections. The small-scaled slope fill soil profile geometry was also determined based on the actual slope geometry. Nine tests were carried out using the 3D model. B-a1 to B-a3 were triggered by gas injection at the slope bottom. B-h1 to B-h6 were triggered by mixing 32% H2O2 solution and with cement. The third model C was a one-dimensional flume test model. The first part was a 650 mm long, 200 mm in width flume with the sliding base of a small (10 to 15 degrees) angle to horizontal line. The second part was a horizontal base. Three triggering factors were used in the experiment. The first triggering factor was a small mass of gas injection. The second triggering factor was water injection. Three tests were done for different soil models and/or different water contents and/or different water injections. The third triggering factor was the 35% H2O2 solution injection. Seven tests were done. Each test used different soil models, different H2O2 solution injections. The soil slope models were constructed by upper dry sand layer, a middle clay layer, and a bottom dry cement core. The H2O2 solution was injected into the cement core for generation of the new oxygen gas mass since the cement acts as a catalyzer. Furthermore, more than 10 calibration tests were designed and carried out for determining the generation rate of the new oxygen mass with time from H2O2 solution in the flume tests. Each calibration test used different cement powder mass and different H2O2 injection rates and masses. Objective 3: Further examination of the gas observed in the fill soils were undertaken. The conditions of the buried pipeline in the adjacent hillside slope were examined. Some records of gas transmission operation in the pipeline before and after the landslide were found in open literature and media. Observation of gas emission in the drillholes indicate that the upper strata of fill soils can become a gas-impermeable layer covering the gas in the lower strata of the saturated fill soils. The permeability of the fill soils for the seepage flow of water or air was carried out using the soil samples from the site. Using the small-scale laboratory experiments for Shenzhen Hengtaiyu slope and flume tests, the actions of water and gas/or were tested. Some important phenomena were observed. It can be sure that the compressed gas in the saturated fill can cause the fill forming the gentle slope to flow down for a distance. Analytical and boundary element methods are further developed and used to examine the elastic stress and displacement fields in soil or other solid materials due to internal and/or external loading. These capabilities and results can quantify and predict the effect of new gas in the soil slope. Objective 4: At present, fourteen papers were published in peer-reviewed journals and one was submitted. Four papers were published in recognized international conference proceedings. Eleven research project reports on this landslide were prepared by HKU BEng students for their final year projects. One MPhil thesis on this landslide was completed. Three PhD thesis were completed. One PhD student is being trained under this project. In total, 15 students were trained. The principal investigator delivered nine keynotes at international conference and two invited seminars at HKIE and Geotechnical Engineering Office of HKSAR Government. More publications will be produced.

17207518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207518.value: This project is the only project which proposed and demonstrated that the pore-gas with high pressure was the dominant factor triggering the catastrophic landslide on December 20, 2015 in man-made fill soil slope at Hengtaiyu Industrial Park, Shenzhen, PR China. All the other researchers believed and adopted that the conventional porewater or porewater pressure was the dominant factor. Furthermore, the pore-gas with high pressure is a new triggering factor of originality and can be responsible for many landslides. It is new to the international community of landslides. See output: journal papers nos. 8, 13 to 15; conference papers nos. 1 to 4; students’ theses nos. 1 to 12. The laboratory flume tests conclude that a deep-seated landslide in gentle soil slope triggered by groundwater alone required a large mass of water. Such required water mass has to equal to 16% to 70% of the total mass of the sliding soil debris since the soil liquid limit is usually higher than 16%. The laboratory flume tests further conclude that a deep-seated landslide in gentle soil slope triggered by pore-gas alone required only a small mass of pore-gas. Such required pore-gas mass can be less than 0.1% of the total mass of the sliding soil debris since the pore-gas with high pressure has high expansive power for uplifting and pushing the slope soil and reducing the soil resistance. Such triggering factor of pressurized pore-gas is generally not noticeable since its mass can be very small and disappeared rapidly without tracing. See output: journal papers nos. 8, 13 to 15; conference papers nos. 1 to 4. The project further discovers that the two shear strength parameters show opposite contribution manner to the stability of soil slopes. The contribution by internal cohesion decreases rapidly but the contribution by internal friction angle increases slowly and linearly as the slip depth increases. Such opposite contributions lead to the existence of a global minimum value of the factor of safety for general soil slopes. The contribution of the internal cohesion to the slope stability associated with Shenzhen landslide is very limited. See output: journal paper no. 8 and conference paper no. 4. The project developed many new solutions for elastic stress and displacement fields in solid materials due to internal and external loadings and new results with the drilling process monitor method. These new findings can offer solid foundations for slope stability and landslide investigation. See output: journal papers nos. 1 to 7 and 9 to 12; conference paper no. 3.

17207518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207518.value: The triggering factor of pore-gas with high pressure for landslide is a new triggering factor that is examined and demonstrated with laboratory test. Due to the fact that the mass of the pore-gas can be very small, this cause or triggering factor for slope failure or landslide was not observed and examined. Further development to understand, detect, quantify, and prevent this factor are needed to reduce and prevent landslide hazards. The test method for using H2O2 solution to generate pore-gas in Portland cement can be further developed to examine and investigate other types of landslides including rock and ice avalanches since underground pore-gas is newly discovered triggering factor. This factor can cause sudden and rapid and huge landslide in mountainous slopes and marine slopes. The test method for using H2O2 solution to generate pore-gas in Portland cement can be further applied to examine other geotechnical and geological phenomena including fault, co-seismic surface rupture and fold. The mechanical modelling and prediction methods and techniques that were developed and used in this project can be further applied to address and solve many other landslide and other geotechnical and geo-scientific problems. More publications and presentations are needed to disseminate the most important finding of this project.

17207518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207518.value: The project investigated triggering factors responsible for the catastrophic landslide on December 20, 2015 in man-made fill soil slope at Hengtaiyu Industrial Park, Shenzhen, PR China. The rapid sliding of the soil debris swept and buried 33 buildings on vast flat ground and resulted in 73 fatalities, 4 missing, and 17 injured. The landslide was huge but unusual. It occurred in dry-season. The site had no rainfall before disaster. The fill was common excavated soil. The failed slope had a very gentle angle between 9 to 15 degrees. Sliding debris was huge (2.7 million m^3 and traveling distance very long (608 m) on flat ground. The project examined conventional triggering factors including groundwater, rainfall infiltration, excess porewater pressure and soil liquefaction and found they were not the dominant factors. The project found that the dominant factor was the pore-gas with high pressure in the lower portion of the saturated fill soil. The pore-gas could be the leaked gas from the natural gas pipe buried in nearby ground. The project designed and carried out laboratory test. The results demonstrated that the mass of the pore-gas with high pressure could be less than 0.1% of the mass of the landslide debris.

17207818.label: Realisation of objectives
17207818.value: We have successfully accomplished all tasks during the period of this project. Some research aspects beyond what is described in the proposal. During the past years, the research accomplishments have been summarized in 18 top-tier Journal Papers and 8 top IEEE Conference Papers with acknowledgement of the support of this RGC GRF project. The Journal papers include thirteen papers published in the IEEE Trans. on Smart Grid, two papers published in the IEEE Trans. on Power Systems, one paper published in the IEEE Trans. on Sustainable Energy, and one paper published in the Applied Energy. The PI was invited as the panellists to share the research accomplishments on the resilience of power-electronics-enabled power systems at several prestigious conferences, including (i)Panel Chair “Electric Grid Resilience Metric with Uncertainty” in PSCC 2020 (Power Systems Computation Conference). (ii) Panel Chair “Renewable Energy Planning and Operation with Decision Dependent Uncertainty”, 2021 INFORMS Annual Meeting. (iii) Panel Chair of “Converter-Interfaced Devices for Power System Restoration with high penetration Renewables” in 2022 IEEE PES General Meeting. (iv) Panel Chair “Strategic Behavior in Renewable-dominated Energy Systems”, 2022 INFORMS Annual Meeting. The PI was also invited to share the latest research accomplishments in resilience-related panels in IEEE PES GM and INFORMS from 2018-2022. For the implementation of the proposed methods, a project entitled “Key Technology, System Development and Application of Large-scale Renewable Energy Power Prediction under Complex Weather Conditions” was awarded the Second Prize for Scientific and Technological Progress by the China Electrotechnical Society at the end of 2019. The PI is the key member. The National Natural Science Foundation of China and Guangzhou Zhaohe Power Technology Co., Ltd. have commissioned RMB 3.8M and HKD 1M to PI to extend the theory and applications of this project, respectively. The PI was appointed as the leader of some prestigious organizations in academia and industry, including (i) Chair of IEEE PES Task Forces “Power System Restoration with Renewable Energy Sources” in 2021. (ii) Co-Chair, IEEE PES Working Group “Power System Restoration” from 2022. (iii) Expert, IEC SC8A Working Group-Terms Definition for Renewable Energy Generation, from 2020. The research findings are summarized as follows: -Developing resilience metrics and operating strategies to enhance the survivability of critical loads with multi-resources and dynamic microgrids formation (i) Resilient operation strategy aims to enhance the performance of a power system during the entire process of extremely severe operating scenarios. We proposed a mobile power sources dispatch method to enhance the survivability of critical loads. The survivability of critical loads and the ability to reduce the duration of unsupplied loads are integrated into resilience metrics as the objective of the decision. We proposed a two-stage framework for resilient routing and scheduling of MPSs to enhance both the survivability and recovery of a distribution system. This paper was identified as an ESI Highly Cited Paper [Part C J2]. (ii) Resilient disaster recovery logistics with co-optimizing dynamic microgrid formation. The model incorporates different timescales of DS restoration and RC/MPS dispatch, the coupling of transportation and power networks, and topology constraints based on the concept of spanning forest. The model is convexified equivalently and linearized into mixed-integer linear programming. This method has been widely applied in other areas with topology constraints, and this paper awarded the 2021 Best Paper in IEEE Trans. on Smart Grid [Part C J1]. (iii) To implement dynamic microgrids formation and ensure topology constraints, we proposed a method for radiality constraints formulation. A new model for post-disturbance microgrid formation is proposed. This method enables the topological and some other related flexibilities so that the reconfiguration-related optimization problems can have extended feasibility and enhanced optimality. Graph-theoretic supports are provided to certify their theoretical validity. We also analyze the issues of tightness and compactness [Part C J17]. (iv) We develop a special strategy to enhance resilience in a kind of critical load: a data centre. A post-event restoration method for power distribution systems with Internet data centres as critical loads is proposed. The proposed method considers emergency operation decisions in IDCs and restoration decisions in power distribution systems and minimizes utility loss [Part C J5]. - Enhancing resilience of a power-electronics-enabled microgrid with a collaborating strategy (i) We introduced electric springs (ESs) to implement the transacitve energy of a microgrid. The non-critical loads (NCLs) in microgrids are installed with ESs. A mathematical model was proposed to quantify the feasible operating trace of the ES. An optimization method was developed to determine the optimal operating points for multiple ESs in the microgrid under normal and outage operating scenarios. This work, as well as our series of research results in this area, provide systematic methods to enhance resilience and flexibility with power-electronics-based demand response. [Part C. J4]. (ii) We proposed an optimal placement model for ESs in a radial distribution network against potential extremes. The operation characteristics of the individual ESs are investigated and linearized. Distflow equations are used to model the network. The proposed planning problem is solved by a mixed integer linear program problem. [Part C, J13]. (iii) We proposed a series of technologies to equip power-electronics-enabled devices to contribute to resilience enhancement. To mitigate electromechanical oscillations, we proposed frequency control and drivetrain dynamics of the mechanical system [Part C, J6]. For grid-connected VSCs in DC voltage control, we proposed a net damping criterion dedicated to a multi-VSC system [Part C, J18]. For islanded systems, we developed an optimization-based autonomous operation control strategy that is implemented through a continuous-time alternating direction method [Part C, J12]. -Developing resilience enhancement strategies under decision-dependent uncertainties (i) A novel structure of decision-making under uncertainty, decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU), has been identified. It has been demonstrated that the uncertainty of a system depends upon the decision when there are decision variables associated with uncertainties. During system restoration, we identified that decision-making on the timing of integrating uncertain renewable energy sources and picking up cold loads (CLPU) are DDU problems. A two-stage stochastic decision-dependent service restoration (SDDSR) model is constructed, and the progressive hedging algorithm decomposes the original model into scenario-wise subproblems [Part C, J10]. (ii) DDU significantly aggregate the computational burden. To establish sequential operating decisions, we proposed an approximate dynamic programming method. [Part C, J7]. Besides, convex hull [Part C, J9], and network reduction [Part C, J15] methods were also tested. -Implementing the proposed methods in a high-performance software-hardware parallel computing platform We proposed an enumeration model predictive control of pumped storage to enhance resilience and flexibility. To overcome challenges from heterogeneous resources, we established pumped storage systems with different operational modes. The proposed model optimizes the switching time subject to the complexities and non-linear characteristics of different modes. A software-hardware parallel computing platform was developed. A parallelly accelerated computing method was proposed for multiple pumped storage units. We found that with an increase in the length of the control horizon, the calculation time on the hybrid platform becomes nearly proportional to the length of the control horizons. It can reduce the computational complexity of the proposed strategy from O(n^2) to O(n) with an increase in the length of the control horizon. The accomplishments include a flexible software-hardware parallel computing platform and some highly efficient algorithms. The platform and algorithms are portable and used in other decision-making problems with a large number of uncertain scenarios [Part C J3].

17207818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207818.value: This research addresses the most critical challenging topic during the energy transition, i.e., constructing resilient operating strategies for the emerging energy system with a high percentage of power-electronics-interfaced (PEI) devices and renewable energy sources (RESs). This project proposed a systematic method to operate a PEI device and RESs-dominated system against extreme weather events under the new paradigm. First, we proposed new operating strategies for PEI devices under extreme conditions. (i) For PEI wind generators, to mitigate electromechanical oscillations, we proposed frequency control and drivetrain dynamics of the mechanical system [J6]. For PEI grid-connected VSCs in DC voltage control, we proposed a net damping criterion dedicated to a multi-VSC system [J18]. For islanded systems, we developed an optimization-based autonomous operation control strategy that is implemented through a continuous-time alternating direction method [J12]. (ii) For PEI loads, we proposed a coordinating strategy to implement the required transacitve energy [J4]. The optimal planning for PEI responsive loads is also established [J13]. (iii) For large-scale systems, not only the resilience of physical systems but also the cyber systems are discussed to coordinate multi-infeed HVDC [J8]. Second, we proposed resilient operating strategies with large-scale RESs and diverse loads. RESs are considered the dominant sources for constructing resilient operations [J3, J4, J5, J13, J16]. To enhance resilience for a system with RESs, more resources were integrated, including data centre [J5], transportation systems and mobile generations [J1, J2]. In particular, the networks were also involved in providing flexible resources. A topology modelling method was proposed and used in resilience enhancement [J1, J2, J17]. Third, we revealed a new structure of decision-making under uncertainties, i.e., decision-dependent uncertainties (DDU). For the problem with decision variables associated with uncertainties, the uncertainty of the system is dependent on the decision. We revealed that decisions on the timing of uncertain RESs integration and cold loads pick-up (CLPU) during system restoration are DDU problems. We established a two-stage stochastic decision-dependent service restoration model and solved it with a progressive hedging algorithm for a multi-microgrid system with RESs and CLPU [J10]. Complicated uncertainties can be quantified with data-driven methods [J14, J16]. Finally, to solve the complicated decision problem, we proposed several highly efficient methods, including approximate dynamic programming [J7], constructing a convex hull [J9], and network reduction [J15]. Notably, a hardware-software hybrid parallel computing platform was constructed to make decisions under uncertainties parallelly.

17207818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207818.value: This project systematically established resilience enhancement strategies for a power system with dominated PEI devices and RESs. As key technologies for emerging energy systems, the accomplishments of this project provide many applications with future development potential, including but not limited to (i) Decision-making for interdependent systems. Future energy systems will evolve from the current power system to multi-energy systems with many heterogeneous components. These heterogeneous components are coupled through networks with different timescales and spatiotemporal properties. The method for decision in transportation systems, power systems, and gas systems [J1, J2, J9] with different timescales can be extended to new components. Notably, the method to integrate network constraints [J17] can be generalized to all networked systems. (ii) Decision-dependent uncertainties (DDUs) are general characteristics of the future energy system. System operation and planning for RESs generally introduce DDUs. Characteristics of components determined by the timing of integration, such as responsive loads, should also be modelled as DDUs. The method proposed in [J10] can be extended. (iii) A hardware-software hybrid parallel computing platform explores new tools for a system with a high percentage of uncertain components. The platform and methods proposed in [J3] can be extended to parallel Monte Carlo simulations with detailed models.

17207818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207818.value: To curb global warming, attain and attain sustainable development, and ensure affordability, power-electronics-interfaced (PEI) devices and renewable energy sources (RESs) have been well-identified to dominate the future energy system. However, PEI devices and RESs, cannot be integrated into the current power system operating methodology, which was designed for controllable synchronous generators and predictable loads. Furthermore, global climate change results in the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events have increased. This project systematically addresses this critical challenge. First, we established models for future systems with electrical power systems, gas systems, transportation systems, etc. The new interdependent energy system with heterogeneous multiple timescale components. We established a set of sequential decision algorithms against extremes with acceptable risks. The characteristics of extremes, PEI devices, and RESs, were integrated into the decision-making process. Second, new control methods for RESs were proposed to equip the wind generators with the required controllability. This will be the key technology for the emerging RESs-dominated system operation. Finally, a new computing platform was established to meet the requirements. It is believed that the success of this project will significantly benefit Hong Kong, a coastal international financial centre whose prosperity is strongly reliant on the consistency of energy supply.

17207918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207918.value: The provision of secure electrical energy has been a slowly evolving engineering subject for over 100 years. However, the pressure to replace fossil fuel based generation has led to an upheaval of thinking about what future grids could look like. At the centre of this discussion is the concept of a microgrid, roughly defined as a cluster of power devices which can operate autonomously or in grid-connected modes to supply the demand within. While the subject of power system stability is well-developed, there are many new features in microgrids, which require new analysis. The key ones in many are the short network distances with high losses, plug-and-play nature, novel converter control dynamics and use of new technologies like storage and demand-response. The theoretical difficulties raised by these new issues have not yet been satisfactorily overcome. This proposal will draw on our past work and stability theory expertise to address them. 自20世紀以來，電能的安全可靠傳輸備受業界關注，在實際電網中亦隨著時代發展的需求而逐步演化和完善。然而，近年來由清潔能源替代傳統化石燃料發電的需求日益迫切，未來的電能傳輸模式將發生重大變革，這也掀起了對未來電網形態的探討熱潮。本項目以微電網為主要對象，研究微電網的穩定性問題。微電網本質上由一群可自主/並網運行、能滿足自身用電需求的電力設備組成。儘管電力系統穩定性的研究已相對成熟，但伴隨著微電網中出現的諸多新特徵，如線路距離短、網絡損耗高、設備即插即用、變換器動態控制複雜等，同時受儲能和需求側響應等新技術廣泛滲入的影響，現代電網的安全穩定運行正面臨著一系列新挑戰。本項目將以項目組過去在系統穩定性方面的專門知識和研究成果為基礎，從理論角度深入研究微電網的穩定性問題，全面建立微電網穩定性分析的新方法和體系。

17207918.label: Realisation of objectives
17207918.value: This project has proposed a new stability analysis framework for a special type of power network, i.e., microgrids, under different scenarios. The four objectives of the project have been divided into small targets accomplished step by step. The following are the details of the realization of each small target. Impact of network topology on microgrid stability. The standard topology for distributed generators (DGs) is proved to be harmful to the microgrid's small-disturbance stability, where the algebraic connectivity of a graph will approach zero in case of inappropriate expansion of nodes and lines. Furthermore, it is shown that the zero algebraic connectivity leads to a zero eigenvalue of the microgrid’s dynamic Jacobian matrix and thus deteriorates stability. These results reveal the importance of careful planning for DG connection topology, especially when many DGs are to be integrated. It also suggests that forming loops by linking the nodes close to feeder terminals could be an effective way for stability enhancement. Impasse surface on voltage stability. A necessary condition under which a system trajectory hits the impasse surface is established. It applies to generic DAE models featuring high-order synchronous generators, static loads, induction motor loads, and lossy power networks. A class of static load parameters that prevent power systems from hitting the impasse surface is also identified, which proves an unsolved conjecture in power system studies for decades. Moreover, the obtained results lead to an early indicator of voltage collapse and a novel viewpoint that inductive compensation to the power network has a positive effect on preventing short-term voltage collapse. Stability analysis using the extended effective resistance and conductance. The definitions of effective resistance and conductance are extended to characterize the overall relation between any two disjoint sets of nodes in a signed graph. It is proved that the Laplacian matrix of a signed graph is positive semi-definite with only one zero eigenvalue if and only if the effective conductances between some specific pairs of node sets are positive. Further, the number of Laplacian negative eigenvalues is upper bounded by the number of negatively weighted edges. New conditions for the small-disturbance angle stability, hyperbolicity, and type of power system equilibria are established. These results can be further tailored to microgrid stability analysis by considering the particular characteristics of microgrids. Power flow routers (PFRs) for transient stability-constrained optimal power flow (OPF). A robust transient stability-constrained OPF problem is proposed. The original robust optimization problem is simplified to a scenario-based semidefinite programming (SDP) problem. An offline–online solution framework is developed to solve the problem efficiently. Under this framework, the time-consuming transient stability analysis and scenario reduction are carried out at the offline stage. Only a lower-dimensional deterministic problem is solved at the online stage based on the information obtained offline, which achieves fast implementation of PFR parameter tuning and generation re-dispatch. These results can be used for microgrid stability analysis by taking microgrid’s particular features into account. Stability enhancement by BESS droop gain tuning. A BESS droop tuning scheme in an inverter-based microgrid is established to enhance its stability under small disturbances. A droop control scheme for BESS is introduced so that they can provide both power injection support under steady-state conditions and dynamical support under disturbances. A small signal stability-constrained optimal power flow (SSSC-OPF) problem is formulated to tune BESS droop gains for minimizing the system generation cost while ensuring system stability by applying the linear power flow model. The Benders decomposition-based method with sensitivity analysis is applied to solve the optimization model. Distributionally robust OPF for grid-connected microgrids. A conditional value at risk (CVaR)-averse distributionally robust chance-constrained OPF (CVaR-DRCC-OPF) is proposed. The problem considers voltage regulation from a risk perspective. Compared to the conventional chance-constrained OPF, the CVaR-averse penalty term quantifies the voltage violation better, especially for the uncertainty distribution function with a long tail. A moment-based ambiguous set of uncertainty distribution functions is proposed. The proposed OPF is reformulated as a second-order cone programming (SOCP), which can be solved in polynomial processing time. Stability and control of power grids survey. Power grids, including transmission systems, distribution systems, and microgrids, are critical infrastructures in modern society, and there are well-established theories for the stability and control of traditional power grids under a centralized paradigm. Driven by environmental and sustainability concerns, power grids are undergoing an unprecedented transition, with much more flexibility and uncertainty brought by the growing penetration of renewable energy and power electronic devices. A new paradigm for stability and control is under development that uses graph-based, data-based, and distributed analysis tools. The classic and novel results on the stability and control of power grids are surveyed to provide a perspective on both old and new subjects. Chance-constrained OPF in droop-controlled microgrids. A chance-constrained OPF (CC-OPF) problem with PFRs is investigated to regulate microgrids’ voltage profile. Compared with the normal CC-OPF that relies on node power flexibility only, the proposed model introduces a new dimension of control from the power network to enhance system performance under renewable uncertainties. A linearization method and an iterative algorithm are adopted to address the CC-OPF problem by iteratively solving a subproblem. Flexibility enhancement at the transmission-distribution (T-D) interface. A chance-constrained optimization model is proposed to estimate the flexibility area at a T-D interface. Network flexibility is, for the first time, involved and facilitated by introducing PFRs into distribution systems or grid-connected microgrids. The chance-constrained flexibility area (CCFA) given by the proposed model describes the aggregated power dispatchability of the system with the guarantee of low risks of voltage violations under renewable uncertainties. It is shown that network flexibility significantly reduces the voltage standard deviations. To evaluate the CCFA, an efficient two-layer iteration algorithm is designed. The inner layer finds the boundary point of CCFA. The outer layer determines key directions to be included in the estimation. Ambient-signals-based load modeling (ASLM). A hierarchical framework with two layers for ASLM is proposed, which explores the hidden quasi-convexity of the load modeling problem for the first time. At the upper level, the identification of dynamic load parameters is regarded as an optimization problem. At the lower level, the optimal static load parameters are obtained through linear regression for a given group of dynamic load parameters. Afterward, the regression residuals are regarded as the objective function of the upper-level optimization problem. This load model will be further used for microgrid stability analysis to study the impact of the load dynamics on the system stability. Optimal admittance matrix of DC networks. A general framework for the optimal admittance matrix (OAM) problem in DC systems is established, which aims to find the OAM that minimizes power loss given the power injection information. An algorithm based on successive linear programming is designed to solve the proposed problem efficiently. Two numerical rules: the sparsity and proportionality rules, are discovered from the optimal admittance matrix of the OAM problem. The former tells that the optimal admittance matrix is sparse. The latter reveals that the optimal nodal self-admittance is nearly directly proportional to its power injection in absolute value. The results show how to coordinate the network and power injections for better system performance. These results can be used for DC microgrid design.

17207918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207918.value: The research accomplishments are summarized in ten journal papers and one conference paper. Among the journal papers, three were published in IEEE Trans. on Power Systems; one in IEEE Trans. on Smart Grid; one in IEEE Trans on Automatic Control; one in IEEE Trans. on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers; one invited paper in Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems; one in International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems; and two in Electric Power System Research. The conference paper was presented in IEEE PES ISGT Europe. The major findings of the project include four aspects with respect to the four objectives. First, the project provides new insights into power network stability analysis by extending the effective resistance and conductance definitions to characterize the overall relation between any two disjoint sets of nodes in a signed graph. New stability conditions are established, which intuitively interpret instability as the electrical antagonism between two certain sets of nodes in an active power flow graph. Second, the project studies the impact of distributed generator (DG) connection topology on microgrid stability and finds that the common connection topology that new DGs are connected to nearby nodes via a single line is harmful to microgrid stability. Such a connection will lead to zero algebraic connectivity of the network topology, which deteriorates the stability. The results suggest the need for careful planning for DG connection topology and that forming loops by linking the nodes close to feeder terminals may enhance stability. Third, the project establishes a hierarchical framework for load modeling. The hidden quasi-convexity of the load modeling problem is explored for the first time, which allows more complicated static load model structures. The case study using the Guangdong Power Grid shows that the objective function is mostly quasi-convex after the transformation of induction motor models, which provides the basis for the application of the proposed framework. Last but least, a new droop-tuning scheme is designed for battery energy storage systems (BESSs) to enhance microgrid stability. The designed droop control scheme makes BESSs provide power injection support under steady-state conditions and dynamical support under disturbances. In addition, a new chance-constrained optimal power flow problem is proposed, which introduces a new dimension of microgrid control from the network topology point of view to improve the control performance and enhance stability under renewable uncertainties.

17207918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207918.value: With the new stability criteria for microgrids established in the project, a natural development and extension of the research is the controller synthesis to stabilize unstable microgrids or improve control performance with guaranteed stability of the closed-loop systems. Particular characteristics of microgrids, such as the high R/X ratio of distribution lines and low inertia of the entire system, should be fully considered and combined with the new stability criteria in the controller synthesis.

17207918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207918.value: To save the environment, countries worldwide announced to increase in renewable capacities. These renewables challenge the limits of the traditional power system control paradigm and possibly make the system less robust and more fragile to contingencies. How to operate a reliable power system and deliver uninterruptible, clean, and cost-effective power to customers is becoming an increasingly important issue. The concept of microgrids provides new opportunities to solve all of these issues. In particular, the islanded microgrids can continue to provide power service to end-users in case of main grid failures, and hence can increase the operability of the power system and improve the power supply reliability. Then, the key issue becomes how to run a stable microgrid. This project proposed a new stability analysis framework for microgrids. Particularly, novel stability criteria and droop control methods were established to guarantee the stability of different microgrids by integrating ideas of control system theory, power system theory, network science, and optimization theory. These novel stability criteria and control methods will guide us to build more stable and cost-effective microgrids with high renewables in practice.

17208218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208218.value: 溫度是表示物體冷熱程度的物理量，在日常生活，科學研究和工程生產中是重要的參數。溫度計是用來準確測量物體溫度的傳感器。由於世界市場與科學研究的需求，更高溫度精度和空間精度的溫度傳感器在不斷的被研發出來。從集成光電器件到活細胞，超高空間精度溫度傳感器對於研究在不同系統中的微觀熱力學問題至關重要。常規溫度傳感器，包括熱成像溫度傳感器和熱電偶溫度傳感器，其空間精度極限是數十微米，並不足以用來研究微觀熱力學問題。 過去十年中，諸如量子點和納米鑽石這樣的發光納米材料由於具有在不同的溫度下發出不同波長的光的能力被提議用作局部溫度傳感器。其小尺寸和光學尋址能力使得無接觸，納米級別空間精度溫度測量成為可能。為了讓此類納米探測器準確的反映空間溫度分佈，我們需要操控它們並讓其能在三維空間中運動。近年來我們研發了自驅動納米鑽石，其可以在粘性液體中自我驅動並感應局部磁場。這項研究給了我們控制納米溫度傳感器的啟發。 在這項研究提案中，我們計劃開發能夠無線運行並在流體環境中導航的“自主”納米溫度傳感器。每個溫度傳感器由兩個部分組成，第一部分是感應溫度的量子點，第二部分是能被磁場磁化和控制的螺旋推進器，螺旋推進器可以使量子點能在三維空間運動並擁有納米級別的位置精度。對於這些運動的納米溫度傳感器 的光譜分析 - 在程序設計下運動 – 可以高分辨率的映射溫度在粘性流體中的分佈。我們將利用噴嘴式3D納米打印技術來製造具有指定形狀和材料的納米溫度傳感器。 這項研究旨在（1）建立製造納米溫度傳感器的方案（2）探索需要表徵高溫度精度和空間精度所需的物理學。擬議的研究範圍是建立工程基礎，以便納米傳感器設備可以無線測量流體內的微觀物理量。此外，我們期望該項目可以為等離子體加熱，微流變學和定向生物醫學傳感器等研究主題提供有趣的發現。

17208218.label: Realisation of objectives
17208218.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1) In this project, we have mainly developed nanoscale printing protocols of functional materials that can be used for the fabrication of micro-thermometers. A key technological scheme was to exploit the on-demand dispensing of very small material-laden ink to print materials. First, nanoscale printing of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center nanodiamonds and semiconducting quantum dots, which are emerging as promising optical temperature sensing materials, has been demonstrated. Second, a nanoscale 3D printing method for metallic materials has also been devised. These research works pave the potential way for producing temperature sensing components based on temperature-dependent luminescence or thermoelectric effect with programmed size and shape. 2) We performed basic research to understand the active propulsion of small-scale objects. As a result, we for the first time discovered that X-rays act as a stimulus energy source to propel colloids in an aqueous solution. The result opens new potentials to remotely steer our active sensors inside the opaque biological bodies.

17208218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208218.value: Printing of Nanodiamonds at the Quantum Level [Advanced Science 9, 2103598 (2022)]: The practical realization of quantum temperature sensors calls for the placement of individual qubits on circuits. However, this prerequisite continues to suffer from coarse positioning accuracy, low throughput, and process complexity. We developed a novel nanoprinting scheme that allows the controllable placement of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center nanodiamonds which are emerging as a potential optical temperature sensing probe. The scheme enables remarkable achievements that are not attainable by other approaches: (1) single-quantum level quantity control, (2) sub-wavelength positional accuracy, and (3) scalable, ‘lithography-free’ patterning capability. We believe this work to be a game-changer, as it directly addresses the key technological challenge associated with the realization of quantum sensing devices. A US patent for this invention has been filed (US 63/236,411). These NV center nanodiamonds can be combined with active matters for moving by themselves in fluids for nanoscale quantum sensing, as demonstrated by our preliminary study [Adv. Mater. 29, 1701024 (2017)]. X-ray-Powered Micromotors [ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 11, 15727 (2019)]: We for the first time discovered that X-rays can act as a stimulus energy source to propel colloids in aqueous solution. We can exploit bubble growth by radiolysis of water to propel small objects in water. This initial finding successfully tackles a longstanding challenge in existing approaches that exploit UV-Vis-IR light with a limited penetrating power. The result opens new potentials to remotely steer our active sensors inside the opaque biological bodies. Furthermore, the project extended the scope of our research to develop various 3D-printed sensing probes for nanoscale topography, virus detection, moisture detection, and so on. Most of the results have been published in internationally recognized journals (e.g., Advanced Science, Small, Nano Letters, ACS Nano, ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, etc.)

17208218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208218.value: The completed research project contributed to the development of nanoscale 3D printing methods for various functional materials from metals, semiconductors, to quantum qubits, that can sense small physical/chemical quantities. Based on this, we have further developed the first 4D micro-thermometry by using 3D-printed thermocouples and the manuscript is in preparation. This completed project is directly related to the practical use of 3D printing techniques for real production and the developed techniques/protocols will facilitate a broad range of materials and applications, not limited to specific materials and structures.

17208218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208218.value: In this project, we explored strategies to develop 3D printing methods for creating micro-sensors. The research delivered some clever ideas on how to utilize 3D printing for manufacturing of high-added-valued quantum, semiconducting materials which are potential sensing materials for diverse physical/chemical quantities such as temperature, humidity, biomolecules, and so on. These results suggest a number of interesting applications of 3D printing for real devices.

17208918.value: 高速旋轉成像細胞力學儀 (SIMeC) - 用於大規模多參數細胞力學分析

17208918.label: Project Objectives
17208918.value: - Develop the microfluidic spinning disk assay platform for SIMeC – We will design and fabricate a microfluidic spinning-disk adherent-cell assay platform that harnesses the centrifugal microfluidic concept to enable both shear-stress flow cell assay for measuring cell stiffness; and traction force microscopy for quantifying cell traction force. - Establish the SIMeC prototype: from instrumentation to phenotypic analysis – We will develop a multi-modal (quantitative phase and fluorescence) ultrafast FACED microscopy system and combine it with the spinning-disk assay platform for ultralarge-scale SIMeC. We will perform proof-of-principle experiments to evaluate the robustness of high-dimensional image-derived cellular phenotyping by SIMeC. - Explore the potential applications of SIMeC – We will employ the SIMeC prototype for exploring its utilities in clinical diagnostic (label-free screening of T-cell activation for cancer immunotherapy) and basic biology research (ultralarge-scale mechanophenotyping of stem cell differentiation).

17208918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208918.value: 此項研究主力開發一種新型量化細胞分析儀 ，名為「旋轉成像細胞力學儀」（SIMeC）。SIMeC結合兩種技術於一身：離心微流體 及 全光學激光掃描成像，以達至能夠仔細深度細胞表型。對比現有技術，SIMeC 能夠做出超高速細胞成像 （包括螢光及量化相位差成像），從而可大規模地計算一系列單細胞的力學表徵。此技術能有系統地開拓了解細胞運作的新知識，特別在於研究細胞生物力學上的特性。在醫學診斷中，此類生物力學特性更可用作新型生物標記，例如癌症腫瘤標記。

17208918.label: Realisation of objectives
17208918.value: Objective 1 - We have designed and fabricated a microfluidic spinning-disk adherent-cell assay platform. We also combined the imaging system with SIMeC (with 96 chambers) as well as other microfluidic flow cytometry platforms (Two US patent applications filed). Objective 1 and 2 - We have successfully developed a multi-modal ultrafast FACED microscopy system that could deliver quantitative phase, and fluorescence live-cell imaging (APL Photonics, 2021, Nature Protocols, 2021). The imaging throughput is at least 100 times higher than any existing imaging cytometer (10MHz imaging rate). The microfluidic spinning disk assay platform allowed us to probe the mechanical, biophysical, and morphological phenotypes of cells at high throughput. Objective 3- We have successfully explored different biological and clinical applications of the integrated system, including the originally proposed T-cell activation assay (SPIE BIOS 2023). This pilot study enabled us to initiate a new collaboration with Hong Kong Children's Hospital for further studies in the area of T-cell immunotherapy monitoring. Instead of exploring stem cell differentiation experiments which were not available due to COVID-19-interrupted lab suspension, we explored other more suitable applications and succeeded in demonstrating the experiments including cell-based drug assays (Lab-Chip 2020, SPIE BIOS 2022), viral infection assays (SPIE BIOS 2022, manuscript in preparation), preliminary CRISPR-perturbed cell assay (SPIE BIOS 2023).
