17208918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208918.value: We have successfully developed a multi-modal ultrafast FACED microscopy system that could deliver quantitative phase, and fluorescence live-cell imaging (APL Photonics, 2021, Nature Protocols, 2021). The imaging throughput is at least 100 times higher than any existing imaging cytometer (10MHz imaging rate). And we have combined the imaging system with different large-scale cell assay platforms, including microfluidic imaging cytometry, as well as SIMeC. We have developed the microfluidic spinning disk assay platform for mechanical, biophysical, and morphological phenotyping of cells at high throughput (Two US patent applications filed). We have further developed unsupervised image analytical tools (PARC, VIA) (Bioinformatics 2019, Nature Communicatons 2021) that are used to analyze large-scale (>> millions of cells) single-cell morphological features (biophysical and mechanical) and infer the underlying biological processes. We have performed pilot studies of T-cell activation assays using the FACED imaging system. The key novelty is the label-free single-cell imaging methodology for assessing the activation subtypes and pathways. We discovered that the label-free quantitative phase imaging has the specificity to differentiate different activation subtypes (CD4+ and CD8+), as well as their activation progressions. The experiments have also been validated with standard flow cytometry with known CD markers (e.g. CD25, and CD69) (SPIE BIOS 2023, paper #12390-35). The imaging system and the label-free imaging concept have also been tested with other cell-based assays, including cell cycle assay, as well as targeted drug assay (Nature Protocols 2021, LabChip 2021). We have also conducted preliminary clinical studies using single-cell biophysical morphological analysis based on our large-scale FACED imaging assay platform (Journal of Thoracic Oncology 2021). In total, 16 journal publications ( and more than 10 conference publications/presentations) directly related to this project have been published (in the areas of imaging development, cell assay development, image analytic tool development, as well as clinical exploration). Two US patent applications have been filed regarding the SIMeC development.

17208918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208918.value: The imaging assay platform developed in this project will be further extended to other applications where cell-based assays are essential. One of the on-going effort is to combine CRISPR gene editing technology with our imaging platform for exploring basic understanding of how each genetic variant dictate different image contrasts of the cellular morphology/biophysical/mechanical properties and thus the corresponding morphological profiles. The scale and throughput provided by our system represent the unique opportunity to address this long-standing challenge.

17208918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208918.value: In this project, we developed an integrated imaging technology that allows massive and high-resolution read-out of human cell morphology (1-10’s millions cells per assay) indicative of health and diseases. This represents a one-of-a-kind capability that could be translated to the clinical studies as well as biological discovery.

17209018.label: Project Objectives
17209018.value: To design a MIR-TIP based on second-order nonlinearity. It is specifically about establishing the simulation model to design and numerically investigate the performance of a MIR-TIP based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) in nonlinear crystals (e.g. periodically-poled lithium niobate, PPLN). Multiple performance parameters require to be scrutinized, which include spectral resolution and measurement range, temporal resolution and recording length, detection sensitivity etc. Based on these parameters, the required parametric-conversion bandwidth in nonlinear crystals, the appropriate pump power and pump bandwidth of the time lens and the amount of dispersion can be determined, which help to identify the most appropriate components to construct the MIR-TIP. To construct and optimize the system performance of MIR-TIP through a tailor-made MIR fiber laser. Based on the identified optical components and designed performance parameters, the MIR-TIP will be experimentally implemented. Furthermore, a tailor-made MIR fiber laser will be constructed based on erbium-doped ZBLAN (ZrF4-BaF2-LaF3-AlF3-NaF) fiber, which provides a probe to characterize and optimize the MIR-TIP through the ultrafast spectral-temporal measurement. It will operate in a wavelength-tunable continuous-wave regime to test the MIR-TIP’s spectral resolution and measurement range. Subsequently, a saturable absorber will be further incorporated to the laser cavity to realize mode-locking. The resulting mode-locked pulses thus enable performance test for the MIR-TIP in the temporal domain. To measure the spectral and temporal dynamics of MIR frequency comb. The MIR-TIP will be subsequently applied in the ultrafast spectral-temporal measurement on the microresonator-based MIR frequency comb fabricated by our Co-I. Leveraging the large conversion bandwidth and high conversion efficiency of the nonlinear-crystal-based time lens, the large spectral observation range and high spectral-temporal resolution will provide a comprehensive characterization of the MIR frequency comb. Such characterization is expected to reveal intriguing spectral and temporal dynamics, which leads to deeper understanding and optimization of MIR frequency comb.

17209018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209018.value: Optical spectrum and waveform act as essential information carriers in many different fields. For example, optical signal measurement in both temporal and spectral domains provides complete characterization of light-matter interaction, which plays a critical role in probing the frontier of fundamental physics. However, most of the state-of-the-art measurement techniques such as pump-probe spectroscopy and frequency resolved optical gating (FROG) only work on repetitive processes, while valuable information will be missed for transient and non-repetitive events. Therefore, ultrafast real-time and single-shot spectral and temporal acquisition is highly demanded for analyzing numerous dynamic physical processes. Such capability is particularly desired in the frontier regime of mid-infrared (MIR) wavelength window for its unique fingerprints of materials among myriad applications such as material analysis, environmental sensing and healthcare diagnosis. Furthermore, as an indispensable tool of MIR research, ultrafast MIR laser sources such as mode-locked quantum cascade lasers (QCL), mode-locked diode lasers, Kerr frequency combs etc. are comparatively immature compared to the near-infrared (NIR) counterparts. Thus dynamic optical signal characterizations in both temporal and spectral domains are essential to fully advance the MIR ultrafast laser technology, which brings significant benefits to all the related applications. In a three-phase approach, we will demonstrate our proposed temporal imaging platform (TIP) as a core technology to address some of the critical challenges in observing and characterizing ultrafast dynamic phenomena in the MIR regime. First, we will design a MIR-TIP based on second-order nonlinearity to simultaneously achieve efficient wavelength conversion from the MIR wavelength window to the telecommunication window and ultrafast time-lens-based signal processing. Specifically it can realize optical Fourier transform for spectral analysis and time magnification for waveform measurement in the order of 100-MHz frame rate. Second, we will construct and optimize the system performance of MIR-TIP through a tailor-made MIR fiber laser that operates from the wavelength-tunable continuous-wave regime to passive mode-locked regime to test the MIR-TIP’s performance in spectral-temporal measurement. Third, the MIR-TIP will be used for ultrafast spectral-temporal characterization of a microresonator-based MIR frequency comb to obtain comprehensive understanding of its underlying physical mechanism and to facilitate its performance optimization. The proposed project and its synergy will transform various ultrafast applications, including ultrafast spectroscopy for capturing dynamic phenomena and real-time full-field information characterization in the MIR regime. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry. 光信號的頻譜與波形在很多領域中都是重要的信息載體。比如，光信號的時域及頻域測量可以完整表徵光與物質相互作用的過程，從而推動基礎物理的研究前沿。然而，目前最先進的測量技術，例如泵浦探針光譜測量技術，頻域分辨光學開關技術等只適用於重複過程。而對於瞬態非重複過程，關鍵信息將會在測量中丟失。因而，實時單次的超快時頻測量在研究很多瞬態物理過程的研究中都有著很大需求。這種測量功能在中紅外波段的研究前沿顯得尤其重要：很多材料在中紅外波段有著像指紋一樣的特徵性光譜吸收峰，因而中紅外波段的信號在材料分析，環境傳感以及健康監測方面都有著廣泛應用。另一方面，作為中紅外光學研究中不可或缺的工具，超快中紅外光源例如量子級聯鎖模激光器，半導體鎖模激光器，克爾光頻率梳等等相比於近紅外波段都處於相對不成熟的階段。因而，頻域及時域的動態信號測量將會推動中紅外超快光源的發展，進而為光源的應用帶來幫助。 通過三個階段的工作，我們將會在實驗上實現研究計劃中所提出的時間成像系統。它將成為中紅外波段超快瞬態測量的核心技術。首先，我們將會利用二階非線性過程，在將中紅外信號高效轉換到近紅外通信波段的同時進行二次時域相位調製（時間透鏡），從而搭建出一個中紅外時間成像系統。這個系統可以提供的功能具體包括用於頻譜分析的光學傅里葉變換以及用於波形測量的時間放大，測量的幀速率可以高達100兆赫茲。其次，我們將會利用一個特製的中紅外光纖激光器對系統進行優化。這個激光器既可以工作在鎖模狀態也可以工作在波長可調的連續光輸出狀態。最終，最優化的中紅外時間成像系統將會被用於諧振微環中紅外光頻率梳的超快時頻測量。該測量將使我們對中紅外光頻率梳的物理機制獲得全面深入的理解，進而優化其工作性能。 我們提出的研究項目以及相關技術將會為眾多應用帶來革新，其中包括捕捉動態過程的超快光譜分析以及中紅外波段的實時全光場測量。與此同時，該研究項目所衍生的相關知識也會對科研界乃至工業界帶來積極影響。

17209018.label: Realisation of objectives
17209018.value: 1. To design a MIR-TIP based on second-order nonlinearity. We have established the simulation model to design and numerically investigate the performance of a MIR-TIP based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) in nonlinear crystals (e.g. periodically-poled lithium niobate, PPLN). Multiple performance parameters require to be scrutinized, which include spectral resolution and measurement range, temporal resolution and recording length, detection sensitivity etc. Based on these parameters, the required parametric-conversion bandwidth in nonlinear crystals, the appropriate pump power and pump bandwidth of the time lens and the amount of dispersion can be determined, we managed to identify the most appropriate components to construct the MIR-TIP. 2. To construct and optimize the system performance of MIR-TIP through a tailor-made MIR fiber laser. We demonstrated experimentally a shortwave infrared (SWIR) fiber laser as a transition stage for the MIR fiber laser, specifically through a gain-switched thulium-doped fiber laser with continuous tuning from 1690 to 1765 nm by using an electrically driven acousto-optical tunable filter. In addition to that, we have also demonstrated a temporal imaging platform (TIP) based on on a gating-assisted electro-optic time lens. Operating at the repetition rate of 10-MHz, a 10-dB spectral measurement range of more than 70-nm is achieved with a resolution of up to 42.5-pm in the near-infrared regime. To demonstrate its performance in applications, real-time spectral observation of broadband wavelength sweeping of a Fourier domain mode-locked laser and a 32.4-GHz optical frequency comb is presented. Finally, we expanded further by demonstrating a parametric time magnifier to characterize automatically synchronized noise-like pulses (NLPs) and then demonstrated a novel self-starting mid-infrared laser scheme with simplified alignment, and yielding a state-of-the-art 37-nm bandwidth and 2.2-nJ pulse energy output. 3. To measure the spectral and temporal dynamics of MIR frequency comb. We have unraveled the transitional dynamics of frequency microcombs from chaotic background routes to femtosecond mode-locking in real time, enabled by our ultrafast temporal magnifier metrology and improved stability of dispersion-managed dissipative solitons. Through our dispersion-managed oscillator, we further report a stability zone that is more than an order-of-magnitude larger than its prior static homogeneous counterparts, providing a novel platform for understanding ultrafast dissipative dynamics and offering a new path towards high-power frequency microcombs in the future.

17209018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209018.value: In this project, we proposed and demonstrated a temporal imaging platform for ultrafast shortwave-infrared (SWIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) spectral-temporal observations particularly the laser dynamics. First, we established a simulation model to design and numerically investigate the performance of a MIR-TIP based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) in nonlinear crystals. It helped to identify the most appropriate components to construct the MIR-TIP. Second, we constructed and optimized the system performance of MIR-TIP through a tailor-made SWIR and MIR fiber laser by demonstrating a parametric time magnifier to characterize automatically synchronized noise-like pulses (NLPs) etc. Third, we unraveled the transitional dynamics of frequency microcombs from chaotic background routes to femtosecond mode-locking in real time, enabled by our ultrafast temporal magnifier metrology and improved stability of dispersion-managed dissipative solitons. With these efforts, this project thus will transform various ultrafast applications, including ultrafast spectroscopy for capturing dynamic phenomena and real-time full-field information characterization in the MIR regime. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry.

17209918.label: Realisation of objectives
17209918.value: Plasmonic nanoantennas made from nanostructured metals have attracted significant attention in nonlinear optics, due to their unique properties. For this part of the research efforts, a novel numerical solution based on the nonlinear PMCHWT integral equation method is proposed for the second-order surface nonlinear scattering problems that could be further used for nonlinear OAM analysis. The proposed method is efficient with a surface discretization, and it can directly employ experimentally tabulated material parameters. The method was validated by comparing far-field sum-frequency and second harmonic scattering patterns with Mie theory solutions. The sum-frequency generation from the multi-resonant nano antenna, where two incident frequencies corresponded to the fundamental resonances of the two arms, was analyzed by the developed method. The nonlinear second-harmonic generation from the particle-in-cavity nanoantenna was also modeled using the developed method. Unidirectional radiation of asymmetric particle-in-cavity nanoantenna was realized, and the radiation direction could be controlled by the position of the nanoparticle. This developed method enables us to conduct the theoretical study of the characteristics of the nonlinear spin-orbital angular momentum coupling induced by second-harmonic generation in plasmonic and dielectric nanostructures. To handle the electromagnetic interactions between nano particles in a capsuled approach, the conventional equivalent principle algorithm (EPA) uses rectangular equivalent surfaces to partition interacting objects and use equivalent sources on these equivalent surfaces to calculate the interactions through the "divide and conquer" strategy. However, these artificial surfaces introduce high order discontinuities in the interaction operators. Consequently, they generate certain complexity that was not physical. For this part of the research efforts, we propose a novel relaxed hierarchical equivalent source algorithm (RHESA) for integral equations. Compared with the conventional methods, the equivalent sources in RHESA residing on smooth spherical equivalence surfaces (ES) are established by exact integral operators rather than numerical approximations, following the equivalence principle strictly. Using the meshless integral scheme on the spherical ES, the equivalent sources at quadrature points can represent the internal primary sources with a higher order accuracy. Unlike EPA in which the equivalent sources are taken as unknowns, the equivalent sources in RHESA act as the intermediate sources to compute the far-field interactions efficiently. To weaken the singularities in integral operators, the spherical ESs are “relaxed” hierarchically. The term “relaxed” refers that a spherical ES will not touch the internal primary sources, ESs of its far-field groups, and ES of its parent in the hierarchical algorithm. Combing one-group-buffer scheme, the tap basis functions are avoided. Another effort we did for this period of research is that we present a quasi-continuous metasurface for OAM generation. The metasurface contains an anisotropic perfect electric conductor (PEC) layer and an isotropic perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) layer. It reflects the incident left circularly polarized (LCP)/right circularly polarized (RCP) plane wave to a RCP/LCP wave, along with a locally modulated geometric phase. The phase distribution on the whole metasurface satisfies the requirements so that an OAM of order l can be generated at the k-space position (kx, ky), where kx and ky are the transverse wave numbers. The PEC layer presents a quasi-continuous pattern and the PMC layer can be realized using any artificial high impedance surface. Patterning of the metal strips is accomplished with the assistance of grating vector, which offers a simple and effective way to the design of the whole metasurface. Different from existing design protocols for geometric-phase based metasurfaces, complicated optimization process of single scatterer is not needed. Furthermore, thanks to the quasi-continuous geometries, high-order diffraction from discrete scatterers are avoided. To enable more flexible fast multipole algorithm (FMA) acceleration, a novel hybrid translation computation method for the fast multipole algorithm is proposed based on the machine learning method. The new method combines both generalized regression neural network (GRNN) and artificial neural network (ANN) to replace the traditional translation procedure during the solving process of the FMA. Based on the data corresponding to every one of the interaction list boxes at each level, a hybrid neural network can be trained. Comparing with the previous methods in this field, the proposed model is more general and has lower complexity because it inherits the accuracy of GRNN as well as the efficiency of the ANN. To the best of our knowledge, it is for the first time that the ANN is integrated into FMA. The proposed method has tremendous flexibilities that overcomes the difficulties in construction FMA translators. This made the FMA acceleration for nonlinear analysis more convenient, especially during the setup stage. It is also possible to be used for solving similar problems during the fast inhomogeneous plane wave algorithm in the complex multilayered medium. We also demonstrated chiral surface states along the zigzag edge of a valley photonic crystal in the honeycomb lattice. By decomposing the local fields into orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, we find that the chiral surface states present OAM-dependent unidirectional propagation characteristics. Particularly, the propagation directivities of the surface states are quantified by the local OAM decomposition and are found to depend on chiralities of both the source and surface states. These findings allow for the engineering control of the unidirectional propagation of electromagnetic energy without requiring an ancillary cladding layer. We furthermore examine the propagation of the chiral surface states against sharp bends. It turns out that although only certain states successfully pass through the bend, the unidirectional propagation is well maintained due to the topology of the structure. Nanoantenna supporting localized surface plasmon-polaritons (SPP) has been exhaustively utilized in the transformation of nonlinear optics. By collaborating with HKUST Nanosystem Fabrication Center and Zhejiang University, experimentally we focused on the study of nanoantenna's potential in the mixing of spin angular momentum (SAM) and orbital angular momentum (OAM) via second-harmonic generation (SHG). At this stage, the nanoantenna array for linear response study has been designed and fabricated. By using the measurement platform, the nanoantenna sample is place in between two objective lens. The optical beam scans across the antenna surface with the aid of the rotary scanner and the transmission light is collected by the photodiode that is utilized for imaging. Before measurement, the magnified view of the antenna arrays with different length L (from 140 nm to 220 nm) is captured by 150x microscope. Since the nanoantennas have different resonant frequencies due to their various physical sizes, the absorption rate is different as can be seen from the brightness of different arrays from experiments. At this stage, the response frequencies cannot be detected by the optical spectrum. For one possible reason, due to the very limited area of each antenna array, it is difficult for the beam to be focused. Multiple polarizations and incident angles would simultaneously exist, resulting in the bandwidth increment. The detected power is then averaged and hard to be sensed by the spectrometer. Hence, a revised nanoantenna design and more experiments would be conducted.

17209918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209918.value: In this project, we have developed a novel numerical solution based on the nonlinear PMCHWT integral equation method for the second-order surface nonlinear scattering problems that is further used for nonlinear OAM analysis. The proposed method is efficient with a surface discretization, and it can directly employ experimentally tabulated material parameters. This developed method enabled us to conduct the theoretical study of the characteristics of the nonlinear spin-orbital angular momentum coupling induced by second-harmonic generation in plasmonic and dielectric nanostructures. To handle the electromagnetic interactions between nano particles in a capsuled approach, we proposed a novel relaxed hierarchical equivalent source algorithm (RHESA) for integral equations. Compared with the conventional methods, the equivalent sources in RHESA residing on smooth spherical equivalence surfaces (ES) are established by exact integral operators rather than numerical approximations, following the equivalence principle strictly. Combing one-group-buffer scheme, the tap basis functions are avoided. To further enable more flexible fast multipole algorithm (FMA) acceleration, a novel hybrid translation computation method for the fast multipole algorithm is proposed based on the machine learning method. The new method combines both generalized regression neural network (GRNN) and artificial neural network (ANN) to replace the traditional translation procedure during the solving process of the FMA. The proposed method has tremendous flexibilities that overcomes the difficulties in construction FMA translators. This made the FMA acceleration for nonlinear analysis more convenient, especially during the setup stage. By collaborating with HKUST Nanosystem Fabrication Center and Zhejiang University, experimentally we have tried to experiment mixing of spin angular momentum (SAM) and orbital angular momentum (OAM) via second-harmonic generation (SHG). A revised nanoantenna design and more experiments would be followed. Using knowledges developed from this project, we also demonstrated chiral surface states along the zigzag edge of a valley photonic crystal in the honeycomb lattice. By decomposing the local fields into orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, we find that the chiral surface states present OAM-dependent unidirectional propagation characteristics. We also demonstrated the coexistence of pseudospin- and valley-Hall-like edge states in a photonic crystal with C3v symmetry. The system can support triband pseudospin- and valley-momentum locking edge states at properly designed domain-wall interfaces. Our work combines the pseudospin and valley degrees of freedom in a single configuration and may provide more flexibility in manipulating electromagnetic waves with promising potential for multiband and multifunctional applications.

17209918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209918.value: In this project, we developed the nonlinear PMCHWT (Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai) surface integral equation method. It is efficient for the surface nonlinearity of centrosymmetric materials in general shape nanoparticles since no volumetric mesh is needed. We further studied the nonlinear response to beams carrying OAM. The vortex beam excitations with OAM in nonlinear analysis provide a convenient and powerful tool for investigating complex nonlinear angular momenta interactions in plasmonic nano structures. We developed a new relaxed hierarchical equivalent source algorithm to group interactions and accelerate the whole computation process. To further enable more flexible fast multipole algorithm (FMA) acceleration, a novel hybrid translation computation method for the fast multipole algorithm is proposed based on the machine learning method. The new method combines both generalized regression neural network (GRNN) and artificial neural network (ANN) to replace the traditional translation procedure during the solving process of the FMA. This made the FMA acceleration for nonlinear analysis more convenient, especially during the setup stage.

17210218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210218.value: Cold-formed high strength steel sections are increasingly popular in structural applications. By using high strength steel materials, the size of sections and number of members in structures can be numerously reduced due to its advantages of high strength-to-weight ratio, aesthetic appearance and ease of construction. More importantly, it can also reduce carbon footprint and construction time. Therefore, the society will benefit from using high strength steel materials in terms of energy efficiency and sustainable development. Despite the interest in adopting high strength steel materials in design and construction, the investigation on high strength steel structural members, especially for hollow section joints, is very limited. In addition, structural design of high strength steel hollow section joints with steel grade beyond 700 MPa is not covered by any existing international design specifications. The welding of cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints is currently an urgent issue that needs to be tackled due to the weldability and ductility of high strength materials. Therefore, it is necessary and urgent to investigate cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints in order to fully utilise the potential structural efficiency offered by high strength steel materials in construction. X- and T-joints are basic and essential components in structural systems. However, previous investigations on hollow section joints are mainly focused on materials with steel grade of S460 (nominal yield stress of 460 MPa) or lower. The structural response of high strength steel hollow section joints is different from that of normal strength steel hollow section joints. Therefore, investigation on cold-formed high strength steel hollow section X- and T-joints under axial compression is proposed in this research project. The objectives of this research project are to conduct a series of experiments on cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints under axial compression and perform numerical investigation as well as propose new design rules for high strength steel hollow section X- and T-joints. 冷彎高強鋼構件在結構中應用日益廣泛。高強鋼材不僅強重比性能優越，作為結構材料可以顯著減小構件截面尺寸、降低構件數量，而且其美學價值突出。更重要的是，由於施工便捷，高強鋼的應用可縮短施工周期，減少碳排放總量，在建築節能和可持續發展方面，其工程應用具有重要社會意義。盡管高強鋼已在結構設計中引起廣泛關註，但目前關於高強鋼結構的研究十分匱乏，尤其是針對高強鋼管節點的性能研究非常有限。迄今為止，國際上尚未有規範可適用於名義屈服強度超過700MPa的鋼管節點設計。此外，由於高強鋼材的可焊性和延展性特殊，高強鋼管節點的焊接也是一個亟待解決的難題。為充分利用高強鋼的結構高效性，基於冷彎高強鋼管節點的研究需求十分迫切。X型和T型節點是結構體系的基礎構件，現有基於鋼管節點的研究主要針對名義屈服強度不高於460MPa的鋼材，而高強鋼管節點的結構性能與常規強度的鋼管節點差異顯著。因此，本課題將開展軸力作用下冷彎高強X型和T型鋼管節點的性能研究。旨在通過一系列針對軸向受壓冷彎高強鋼管節點的試驗研究和數值模擬，提出適用於高強X型和T型鋼管結構的設計準則。

17210218.label: Realisation of objectives
17210218.value: The behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints under axial compression has been investigated. A series of tensile and compression coupon tests was conducted. Therefore, the material properties of the high strength steel hollow sections were determined. Furthermore, a series of cold-formed high strength steel tubular X- and T-joints tests under axial compression was also conducted. The test strengths and failure modes of the high strength steel tubular joints were obtained. The load-deformation curves of the tubular joints were also obtained. The weldability of the high strength steel materials was examined. In addition, finite element models for high strength steel X- and T-joints were developed. The finite element models were also verified against the test results obtained from this project. An extensive parametric study of the cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints under axial compression was performed. Hence, a large data pool of numerical data was obtained. The high strength steel X- and T-joints with wider range of brace and chord dimensions, ratios of brace-to-chord width, brace-to-chord thickness and chord width-to-thickness as well as different steel grades were examined. The test and numerical results obtained from this project were used to compare the current design strengths calculated from international design standards. Generally, it is shown that the existing design provisions are not capable of providing accurate and reliable predictions for the design of cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints under axial compression. Therefore, new design rules for cold-formed high strength steel tubular X- and T-joints under axial compression have been proposed. It should be noted that the objectives of this project have been achieved.

17210218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210218.value: Owing to the rapid development of technology and architectural requirements, the infrastructure sector requires high performance materials in constructions. The demand of high strength steel in construction is growing due to its excellent strength-to-weight ratio. However, the use of high strength steel is limited due to the lack of available design rules in current international specifications. In this project, structural behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel tubular X- and T-joints under axial compression has been thoroughly studied through both experimental and numerical investigations. New research data and knowledge on this important topic have been generated from this project. Furthermore, new design equations for cold-formed high strength steel tubular X- and T-joints under axial compression have been proposed. More importantly, the newly proposed design equations can be adopted by international specifications. This will definitely benefit the steel industry and construction using high strength steel materials. Therefore, a more economical, reliable and safer design for cold-formed high strength steel tubular joints can be used by engineers and designers. The findings of this research project are able to enhance the understanding on the behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel hollow section joints under axial compression.

17210418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210418.value: Strength and ductility are the key mechanical properties of metallic materials for lightweight structural applications in the aerospace and automotive industries. However, improving the strength of such materials frequently results in a reduction in ductility, which is known as the strength-ductility trade-off in metallic materials. Hence, pathways to increasing dislocation density can significantly increase material strength but often with a concomitant loss in ductility. In recent work published in Science, we demonstrated that high dislocation density can not only increase strength but also improve ductility in steels. High dislocation density is mainly responsible for improved yield strength through dislocation forest hardening, whilst improved ductility is achieved by the glide of intensive mobile dislocations and well-controlled martensitic transformation, both of which are governed by the high dislocation density resulting from warm rolling and displacive shear transformation. In this project, we propose a new strategy that combines the concept of high dislocation density with the room-temperature quenching and partitioning process to design novel steels with ultrahigh tensile strength, i.e. 2 GPa or higher, and total elongation of 15-20%. High dislocation density can be introduced by a warm rolling process at appropriate temperatures, at which dynamic recrystallisation and dynamic recovery are considerably restricted. These dislocations are inherited by the martensite matrix and retained austenite after subsequent water quenching down to room temperature. They can refine the martensite block size, as well as increase the dislocation density in the martensite matrix. In addition, the dislocations can also enhance the mechanical stability of the retained austenite grains, providing an improved transformation-induced plasticity effect. It is expected that such dislocation engineering in both the martensite and austenite phases will allow the manufacture of strong, ductile steels. In addition to the fabrication of new ultrahigh-strength steel, the proposed project will also thoroughly investigate its deformation mechanism and microstructure-property relation through comprehensive experimental and modelling work. In particular, the effect of dislocation density on the martensitic transformation kinetics during the plastic deformation of the ultrahigh-strength steel will be investigated. It is worth noting that the new ultrahigh-strength steel can be manufactured using conventional production methods compatible with existing industrial production lines, which will facilitate its industrial application. 航空和汽車工業所采用的金屬材料必須同時兼備高強度和高塑性。然而，金屬材料的強度和塑性是兩個互斥的力學性能。一般而言，通過提高金屬材料的位錯密度可以大幅提高其強度，但會導致其塑性下降。 然而，我們最近發表在《科學》雜誌上的研究結果表明，提高鋼鐵材料的位錯密度不僅可以提高其強度，同時還可以提高其塑性。強度的提高的主要依靠林位錯強化機制，高塑性則是通過大量的可移動位錯的同時開動及合適的馬氏體相變所獲得。高位錯密度是通過溫紮和室溫冷軋馬氏體相變所獲得。 在本項目中，我們提出一種全新的鋼鐵材料設計理念，即同時采用高位錯密度和室溫淬火配分工藝兩個概念，設計高強高塑鋼鐵材料。本項目提出的新型鋼鐵材料的目標強度是2 GPa或更高，塑性達到15-20%。高位錯密度通過溫紮來獲得。溫紮的溫度選擇必須要適當，要最大限度控制動態再結晶和動態回復的發生，以便獲得最高的位錯密度。溫紮所獲得的高位錯密度將會保留在隨後生成的馬氏體基體和殘余奧氏體中。這樣可以使馬氏體基體的晶粒更細小，位錯密度也更高。此外，高位錯密度也可以使殘余奧氏體具有更高的機械穩定性，從而獲得更優的相變誘發塑性效果。我們預計，通過此位錯工程的設計調控，我們可以制備出高強高塑的鋼鐵材料。除了設計和制備這些新的高強高塑鋼鐵材料之外，本項目還將研究這些新型鋼鐵材料的微觀組織結構與力學性能之間的關系，研究計劃包括詳細的實驗和理論模擬研究。位錯密度對變形過程中的馬氏體相變的影響將得到特別關註。值得提出的是，該新型高鐵材料可以采用常規的鋼鐵生產設備來制備，這可以加速該新型鋼鐵材料的工業化進程。

17210418.value: For objective 1, the following achievements have been completed and this objective is fully achieved. A novel steel subjected to warm-rolling, cold-rolling and partitioning obtains a tensile strength of 2144 MPa, a uniform elongation of 19%, a total elongation of 22%. The tensile properties are better than the ones listed in the objective 1. In addition, this steel obtained an excellent fracture toughness of 101 MPa m-0.5. This steel creates a world record on the combination of yield stress-fracture toughness, and was published in SCIENCE in 2020. The first author of this paper is PI's PhD student, and PI is the leading corresponding author. For objective 2, new constitutive models including martensitic transformation and dislocation density evolution were developed, and implemented in CPFEM simulations. These models were used to simulate new high-strength steels. For objective 3, systematic experiments including dislocation density measured by synchrotron XRD and martensitic transformation are obtained for samples deformed at various temperatures and strain rates. These data were used to calibrate the CPFEM simulations which agree well with experimental findings.

17210618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210618.value: By anchoring cells to their micro-environment and serving as hubs for signal exchange, cell-ECM (extracellular matrix) adhesion plays essential roles in processes such as cell migration, proliferation and differentiation. Interestingly, recent evidence has indicated that the adhesion and spreading of cells can all be enhanced by stress relaxation in the substrate. Given that most natural and synthetic ECMs are known to be viscoelastic, a precise knowledge of such viscosity-regulation of cells will not only be the key for our understanding of how they execute different biological duties in vivo but may also provide critical clues for the development of biomaterials and regenerative medicine in the future. However, several important issues remain unsettled here. First of all, almost all the previous experimental investigations in this area are qualitative in nature while quantitative data illustrating exactly how the formation and growth of close cell-ECM contact regions, often referred to as focal adhesions (FAs), are influenced by material viscosity are still lacking. In addition, the fundamental question of whether the observed enhancing effect of substrate viscosity on cell adhesion and spreading can be attenuated/modulated, as indicated in our preliminary study, by other key viscoelastic parameters such as the rigidity level and characteristic relaxation times of the material remains largely unclear. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address these outstanding issues. Specifically, on the basis of our pilot studies, methods for fabricating substrates with distinct viscoelastic properties will be developed. The growth dynamics of FAs as well as spreading of cells on these viscoelastic ECMs will then be systematically and quantitatively examined with confocal and total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) imaging. Data to be generated here in conjunction with subsequent theoretical modeling, taking into account important features that were neglected in previous investigations, will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that the regulation of ECM viscosity on the adhesion and spreading of cells is both rigidity- and relaxation timescale-dependent. If successful, this study will greatly enhance our basic understanding of the mechanism by which surrounding viscoelasticity affects cells, and hence shed lights on the design of new materials for biomedical applications. In addition, the comprehensive data to be generated by this study are also expected to be extremely useful in guiding/assisting the development of future theories. 通過將細胞固定于它們的微環境中並充當信號交換的中樞，細胞与胞外基質的黏附在細胞遷移，增殖和分化等過程中起着重要作用。最近的證據表明，細胞的黏附和延展都可以通過材料中的應力鬆弛來增強。鑑於大多數天然和合成的胞外基質都是粘彈性的，关于材料粘度对細胞行为調控的精確认识不僅是我們理解細胞如何在體內執行不同生命職責的關鍵，而且還可能為未來生物材料和再生醫學的發展提供關鍵線索。然而，许多重要的問題尚未被厘清。首先，幾乎所有在該領域的现有實驗研究都是定性的，而关于材料粘度对細胞黏附區域形成和生長影響的定量數據則仍然缺乏。此外，对于所觀察到的基質粘度對細胞黏附和延展的增強效應是否可以通過其他關鍵粘彈性參數，例如材料的剛性水平和特徵弛豫時間，進行調節这一基本問題仍不清楚。 在本項目中，我們計劃对這些問題進行實驗与理論的綜合研究。具體而言，在我們前期研究的基礎上，製备不同粘彈性基質的方法将会被開發出来。同时，細胞黏附班在這些粘彈性材料上的生長動力學，以及整个細胞的延展，都将被共聚焦或全內反射熒光顯微鏡所精确的观测。此外，相应的理論模型也将会被提出以明確地證實或駁斥我們的主要假設，即基質粘度對細胞黏附和延展的影響都是同材料的剛度以及鬆弛時間尺度相关的。如果成功，這項研究將大大增強我們對材料物理性能对細胞行为影響機制的基本理解，從而為新生物材料的設計提供线索。此外，本研究所產生的數據也有望在未來相关理論的發展上發揮作用。

17210618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210618.value: 1. We have identified protocols to fabricate polyacrylic acid (PAA) and hyaluronic acid (HA) based viscoelastic hydrogels. Specifically, by changing the concentration of polymerized acrylamide within a covalently crosslinked PAA network, we were able to vary the storage (elastic) and loss (viscous) modulus of the fabricated PAA gels. Similarly, distinct levels of viscosity can also be introduced by adding adamantine groups in the norbornene-modified hyaluronic acid and then mixing it with mixing β-cyclodextrin-modified hyaluronic acid (refer to item 8-5 in Part C). In addition, methods have also been developed to insert functionalized nanoparticles into dynamic hydrogels (see item 8-8 in Part C) or introduce mobile adhesion molecules on the surface (item 8-9 in Part C). 2. Using techniques such as TIRFM (total internal reflection fluorescence microscope) and confocal imaging, we have systematically examined the adhesion, spreading and related activities of cells cultured on viscoelastic gels. It was found that maximum cell spreading will be achieved at intermediate substrate viscosity (item 8-5 in Part C) or when the viscous resistance experienced by mobile ligands, responsible for cell-material adhesion, is at an optimal level (item 8-9 in Part C). In addition, we also demonstrated that the presence of gold nanorods, with large aspect ratios and bearing αCD3 or αCD28 antibodies, in the viscoelastic hydrogels significantly enhances the activation of human T cells (item 8-8 in Part C). 3. By considering the stochastic dynamics of motor clutches formed between the cell and outside, we have developed a model to elucidate the influence of substrate viscosity on cell spreading. Specifically, it was found that the presence of viscosity can stiffen soft substrates on a timescale faster than the clutch off-rate which enhances cell−ECM adhesion and ultimately promotes cell spreading (item 8-5 in Part C). In the case of mobile ligands, the random movement of ligands becomes so severe in the high mobility regime that eventually leads to vanishing total resistance against actin retrograde flow. On the other hand, when the viscous resistance against ligand movement is very large, the system behavior becomes friction-slippage like and which also results in weak cell adhesion and limited cell spreading (item 8-9 in Part C). Finally, a computational model has also been developed to elucidate the physical origins of the viscoelastic response of biopolymer gels or cell cytoskeleton (refer to item 8-4 and item 8-6 in Part C).

17210618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210618.value: 1. Our findings that cell adhesion, spreading and related activities can all be regulated by material viscosity, along with the functionalized nanoparticles inserted or mobile adhesion molecules coated, may provide insights for the development of new strategies for tissue engineering and cancer therapy. 2. The stochastic and computational models developed could be extended to examine other interesting phenomena like topography-assisted cell migration and cancer metastasis.

17210618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210618.value: We have developed novel methods to fabricate hydrogels with distinct viscoelastic properties, containing functionalized nanoparticles or coated with mobile adhesion ligands. Utilizing these substrates, it was found that maximum cell spreading will be achieved at an optimal level of material viscosity or intermediate ligand mobility. In addition, related cellular activities like the immune response of T cells can also be regulated by the viscoelasticity and inserted functionalized gold nanorods of hydrogels. Findings from this study shed lights on the design of future biomaterials as well as the development of new strategies for tissue engineering and cancer therapy.

17210718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210718.value: Commodity RGBD cameras are now widely used in many fields. These cameras are accessible and portal, and most important of all, can capture in real time the depth information of a 3D environment. There is now increasing research effort to harness the power of RGBD cameras for fast 3D reconstruction, which is the key technology to applications of augmented reality (AR) and robotics. Existing reconstruction methods based on commodity RGBD camera produce compelling results in real time 3D reconstruction. However, limited by their design choices that are primarily made for processing extended surfaces, these methods fail badly in reconstructing thin objects, such as cable wires and wire frame furniture, which are frequently encountered in daily scenes. At the present there is also a lack of basic research in the literature on using RGBD cameras for real time, high quality reconstruction of thin objects. In view of the ubiquity of thin structures and the importance of their 3D reconstruction, in this project we will tackle the problem of real time high, quality reconstruction of 3D thin structures with commodity RGBD cameras. We propose a new 3D geometry representation, called {em skeleton transform}, that is particularly suited for representing and processing 3D thin structures. We also propose a new fusion framework that can achieve real-time and accurate reconstruction of a thin structure by building up its skeleton transform in a progressive manner. Our key insight is to utilize the RGB images, which contain accurate 2D images of the thin structure, and multiple RGBD image frames from nearby views to facilitate fast and robust reconstruction. The outcome of the project will be the first system for real-time reconstruction of thin structures, which will represent a major contribution to the state of the art of 3D reconstruction technology. 消費級RGBD相機在許多領域得到廣泛應用，它們不僅方便攜帶並可實時地獲取三維環境的深度信息。作為增強現實與機器人應用中的關鍵技術，如何更好地發揮RGBD相機的快速三維重構能力吸引了越來越多的研究。然而，現有的基於消費級RGBD相機的重構方法可實時獲得一般較大物體的三維重構結果，但難以用於重建細線物體，如常見的電纜線或細絲裝飾。同時，亦缺少如何實現實時、高質量細線物體重構的基礎研究工作。 鑑於細線物體的普遍性及其三維重構在應用中的重要性，本項目將以基於消費級RGBD相機實現實時、高質量的細結構物體三維重構作為關鍵研究問題，提出了一種新的三維幾何表示方法，稱為骨架變換，適於表示並處理三維細線物體。同時，我們提出了一種新的融合框架，採用一種漸進方法建立細線物體的骨架變換，實現對該類結構的實時精準重構。其中的關鍵在於採用多張包含細線物體的精確二維RGB圖像，以及從鄰近視角採集的多張RGBD圖像，達到快速魯棒的重構。本項目成果將是首創的細線物體實時重構系統，將大大改進目前的三維重構技術。

17210718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210718.value: We have developed a system for 3D thin structure reconstruction using a depth camera. The reconstruction quality is satisfactory in general and outperforms previous imaged-based method. However due to the use of infrared light and low-resolution of the commodity depth cameras we use, the method cannot reconstruct thin structures of diameters less then 2mm or that have black surface, The work is published at SIGGRAPH Asia 2018. Furthermore, we improve the reconstruction quality further by using an RGG video sequence. That work is published at SIGGRAPH 2020. The drawback of this work is the assumption that the scene background needs to be simple enough to be segmented so to extract the thin structure as the foreground. Moreover, so far we cannot reconstruct dynamic structure, since we assume that all the thin structures to be static during image acquisition,

17210718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210718.value: We are now studying the following outstanding challenges: (1) The reconstruction of dynamic thin structures, such as waving tree branches or moving wires involved robotic surgery; (2) reconstruction of thin structures against a natural background. These issues need to be addressed in order to support robotic operation. Our approach will be based on integrating event cameras as additional image input.

17300018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300018.value: 本項目旨在研究（1）含有弱化學鍵的複雜半導體晶體中的聲子散射機制；（2）通過調控能帶結構提高硫銀鍺礦化合物Cu8GeSe6、Ag8SnSe6與Ag9GaSe6的熱電能量轉換效率。聲子散射可以有效降低晶格熱導率；然而由於實驗設備與理論方法的限制，人們對硫銀鍺礦化合物中的聲子散射微觀機制仍未充分理解。在本項目中，我們將通過結合中子散射、衍射、高溫熱電輸運性能測量、電子與原子尺度的量子模擬等先進的實驗與理論方法進行研究。 申請人的前期研究結果表明硫銀鍺礦化合物Ag9GaSe6具有所有緻密固體中近乎最低的熱導率 ~0.15 W/m-K，與木頭的熱導率相當。低熱導率材料在不同工程領域有重要應用，包括熱障塗層、光相變與熱電設備等。前期實驗結果表明硫銀鍺礦化合物Ag9GaSe6由於具有極低的熱導率，其最高熱電優值可達1.5。研究還表明Ag9GaSe6中的Ag原子與周圍其它原子之間所成的化學鍵較弱，因此可以猜想該弱相互作用將導致強聲子關聯效應。在本項目中，申請人將通過開發新的理論方法計算有限溫度下的振動譜與聲子壽命並對聲子相互作用進行深入探討。該項目與申請人的前期研究工作緊密相關，切實可行。 研究結果表明硫銀鍺礦化合物的熱電效率可以通過能帶工程進一步提高。在本項目中，申請人將系統地研究摻雜與合金化對能帶結構與電輸運性能的影響。通過第一性原理計算篩選合金元素優化合金成分，為進一步實驗研究提供方向指導。該項目的執行將有助於對半導體材料中聲子散射機制的更全面理解。同時，該項目還將提高半導體熱電輸運性能的可調控性。通過載流子濃度與組分的優化，我們將基於硫銀鍺礦化合物合成高性能的熱能轉換與利用新材料。

17300018.label: Realisation of objectives
17300018.value: Objective 1: We have studied the lattice dynamics of the orthorhombic and cubic phases of argyrodite Ag8GeSe6 from both first-principles calculations and inelastic neutron scattering experiments. To simulate the partial occupation of the Ag lattice sites in the cubic phase, we perform ab-initio molecular dynamics simulations using a 240-atom supercell, where 32 Ag atoms randomly take up 120 lattice sites. The atomic distribution was obtained with a special quasi-random structure algorithm. Ag atoms are found to be loosely bonded and have a larger atomic displacement parameter in the orthorhombic phase. In the cubic phase, Ag atoms become diffusive and exhibit a liquid-like behavior. The diffusion coefficient increases significantly as temperature rises. Objective 2: We have obtained the phonon density of states of argyrodite compounds from molecular dynamics simulations and inelastic neutron scattering experiments using powder samples. The initial configuration of atomic partial occupation used in our simulation was constructed using data from X-ray diffraction refinement experiment. Via the Fourier transform of the velocity autocorrelation function, which was obtained based on molecular dynamics simulations under the NVT ensemble, we calculated the temperature-dependent phonon density of states taking into account the phonon-phonon interactions. The theoretical data were directly compared with experiments, and the results were found to be in reasonable agreement. Objective 3: We have studied the high-temperature thermoelectric transport properties of argyrodite compounds. Electrical resistivity and Seebeck coefficient were simultaneously measured as a function of temperature under a vacuum environment. Thermal diffusivity was measured using the laser flash method. Thermal conductivity was evaluated based on the Dulong-Petit limit of heat capacity. The thermoelectrical figure of merit of argyrodite compounds, which is directly related to the energy conversion efficiency, was found to be enhanced by proper doping and alloying. A more complete understanding of the improved electrical transport properties was obtained based on the measurements of the carrier concentration and mobility. The thermal transport mechanisms were unveiled via the study of the lattice dynamics and phonon scattering.

17300018.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300018.value: Argyrodite compounds including Ag8GeSe6 and Ag9GaSe6 have been systematically studied based on first-principles calculations, transport property measurements and inelastic neutron scattering experiments. By calculating the phonon dispersions of these argyrodite compounds, we found that the group velocities of the acoustic phonon modes are strongly suppressed, while the optical phonon modes only have an insignificant contribution to the heat transport. The phonon density of states of Ag8GeSe6 was obtained from both theory and experiment. We found that phonon modes in the low-frequency region are mostly dominated by Ag atoms, which become diffusive at high temperatures, resulting in a superionic structural phase transition. The partial occupancy of the Ag lattice sites at high temperatures was also confirmed in X-ray diffraction experiments. From ab-initio molecular dynamics simulations, we also observe consistent results, i.e., Ge and Se atoms oscillate around their equilibrium lattice sites while Ag diffuses. The diffusive behavior of Ag atoms in these argyrodite compounds originates from the weak chemical bonding formed with the neighboring atoms. The thermal conductivity, electrical resistance and Seebeck coefficient of these argyrodite compounds were also investigated from both theory and experiment to achieve a more complete understanding of the transport properties.

17300018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300018.value: This study of the lattice dynamics and transport properties of argyrodite compounds suggest novel phonon scattering and heat conduction mechanisms. The atomic diffusive behavior indicates potential alternative thermal transfer channels at high temperatures. Further study of the heat transfer mechanisms using advanced theories is needed for better insight into the effects of atomic diffusion. Results of this project also suggest that some argyrodite compounds can have promising thermoelectric properties with proper doping and alloying. Future study of the influences of atomic diffusion on the long-term material performance is also needed for practical device applications.

17300018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300018.value: Some of the argyrodite compounds have low thermal conductivities and narrow band gaps. These materials have potential applications in thermoelectric devices, which can convert heat into electricity or vice versa. To promote the practical applications, the thermoelectric energy conversion efficiency needs to be further enhanced. The issue of atomic diffusion may also affect device performance in long-term service. To tackle these problems, a better understanding of the thermal and electrical transport mechanisms and the lattice dynamics of the materials need to be studied in-depth. In this project, we carried out a systematic investigation of the fundamental electronic structures and phonon properties to better understand the transport properties of these compounds, paving the path for their thermoelectric applications.

17300318.label: Project Objectives
17300318.value: We aim to develop efficient numerical methods for solving multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs. We shall construct localized adaptive basis functions and explore low-dimensional structures in their Green's functions using the hierarchical matrix approximation approach. We aim to develop efficient numerical methods for solving Helmholtz equations in random media. We shall construct localized adaptive basis functions and explore low-dimensional structures in their Green's functions using the hierarchical matrix approximation approach. We shall study the numerical accuracy, convergence, and stability of the proposed numerical methods. In addition, we shall carry out numerical simulations to solve some application problems, such as reservoir simulation and seismic inversion. We aim to gain critical insights about the properties of these two challenging SPDEs, including the effective dimension of the SPDE solution space (i.e., Kolmogorov n-width of the solution manifold), the separability of their Green's functions, and the stability estimate of the Helmholtz equations in random media.

17300318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300318.value: 科学和工程中的许多实际问题都充满不确定性，例如流动（地下水，石油和天然气等）在非均质多孔介质中的传输和声波在随机介质中的传播。建立数学模型来描述这些问题的不确定性，并且量化分析这些不确定性因素对人们关心的计算量的影响是非常重要的研究方向。比如量化分析多孔介质中的流体传输中的不确定性因素的影响可以帮助石油公司在石油和天然气的生产中做出更好的决策。准确计算声波在随机介质中的传播，能够帮助科学家从观测到的回波中重构关于地下结构的高质量图像。不确定性量化是研究这些问题的一个新兴研究领域。 随机偏微分方程， 由于方程中包含随机变量或随机过程，在复杂问题建模以及不确定性量化研究中发挥着重要的作用。很多研究工作者已经付出大量的努力，从理论分析和数值计算的角度来研究随机偏微分方程，成功地发展了很多有效的算法。 然而，由于其复杂的性质，特别是当方程的随机维数很高时，解空间的维度很高，这个研究领域仍然存在着许多值得研究的难题。这极大地限制了我们解决许多具有挑战性的问题的能力。 在这个研究课题中，我们将探索两类随机偏微分方程的解空间中的低维结构，并设计有效的数值方法来计算它们。 具体来说，我们将研究两个问题：（1）带随机系数的多尺度椭圆偏微分方程；和（2）随机介质中的亥姆霍兹方程。 对于每个问题，我们将构造自适应基函数来逼近它们的解空间，并研究其格林函数的低秩逼近方法。我们还将研究几个重要的问题，包括证明自适应基函数的指数衰减性质，估计格林函数的近似可分性，从解的不完整的测量信息中估计解的性质，以及计算高频振荡积分等等。 我们相信，本课题发展的方法和用到的想法，有可能应用于解决其他高维随机偏微分方程的计算，例如对流占优型的对流扩散随机偏微分方程。 然后，我们将进行许多数值模拟实验，以测试本课题得到的数值方法的收敛性和计算效率。 此外，我们将研究该项目中的随机偏微分方程的几个理论问题，例如解空间的有效维数估计（即解空间的柯尔莫哥洛夫 n-宽度），格林函数的可分性，以及随机介质中的亥姆霍兹方程的解的稳定性估计等。我们期望通过这些数值结果和理论分析，能够使我们更好地理解这些高维随机偏微分方程的解的性质。 这个研究课题的成功完成将使我们在高维随机偏微分方程的数值计算领域取得新的进展，尤其是带高波数的亥姆霍兹方程。 通过这些新方法，我们可以计算许多来自物理和工程中的实际问题，例如油藏模拟和地震波反演等。 因此，课题的顺利完成将有望在科学和工程界产生广泛的影响。

17300318.label: Realisation of objectives
17300318.value: We have dedicated significant efforts towards achieving the objectives proposed in this project, and we are delighted that all of the objectives outlined in the proposal have been accomplished. Thirteen papers have been published and one paper is under review in the second round. Many papers were published in top journals of computational mathematics. I have successfully developed several efficient numerical methods that effectively tackle the challenges posed by multiscale stochastic elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs). These methods leverage the low-dimensional structures inherent in the solution spaces, enabling more accurate and computationally efficient solutions. In paper [1], I introduced the proper orthogonal decomposition-based method, which effectively captures and utilizes the dominant modes of the solution space. In paper [2], I further expanded on this approach by introducing the multiscale multilevel Monte Carlo method, which combines the benefits of both multiscale and multilevel Monte Carlo techniques. Additionally, in paper [5], I proposed a data-driven approach that utilizes intrinsic dimension reduction techniques, offering an innovative perspective for addressing the challenges associated with these PDEs. Lastly, in paper [12], I introduced the stochastic domain decomposition method based on the variable-separation approach, which provides a powerful tool for addressing the multiscale and random nature of these PDEs. These works collectively contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the challenges posed by multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and offer effective solutions from various angles, significantly advancing the field. Building on the efficient methods developed for solving the forward problems of multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs, I also developed model reduction methods to solve the inverse problems associated with these SPDEs. Specifically, in paper [10], I introduced a proper orthogonal decomposition-based method for solving parabolic inverse source problems and provided a rigorous convergence analysis of this method. In the paper [13], I developed a data-driven and model-based accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method for solving Bayesian elliptic inverse problems. Additionally, in the paper [14], I proposed a reduced-order model-based variational inference with normalizing flows for solving Bayesian elliptic inverse problems. These works represent significant progress in the development of model reduction methods for solving the inverse problems associated with multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs. I have also made significant progress in developing efficient numerical methods for solving Helmholtz equations in random media. In the paper [8], I introduced a quasi-Monte Carlo-based model reduction method specifically tailored for solving the Helmholtz equation in random media. Furthermore, in [6], I proposed a novel Clenshaw-Curtis Smolyak rule for high-dimensional oscillatory integrals, which can also be applied to solve Helmholtz equations in random media. This work is currently in the second round of the review process in the Journal of Mathematics of Computation. Inspired by the model-reduction idea, we proposed a deterministic-statistical approach for an inverse acoustic source problem using multiple frequency limited aperture data in [11]. These works represent significant contributions to the field of efficient numerical methods for solving Helmholtz equations in random media. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in applying deep learning methods to scientific computation, including using deep neural networks to approximate multivariate functions and solve differential equations. In line with this trend, I have also made progress in this direction. In the paper [3], I proposed a mesh-free method for interface problems using a deep learning approach. This method leverages the benefits of deep neural networks to achieve efficient and accurate solutions for interface problems without the need for a mesh. In the paper [4], I developed a QMC-deep learning method for estimating the diffusivity of elliptic PDEs in random domains. This method combines quasi-Monte Carlo techniques with deep learning methods to achieve more efficient and accurate solutions for this challenging problem. In addition to the aforementioned research works, I also developed a second-order accuracy-preserving method for moving contact lines with Stokes flow in [7] and studied the convergence analysis of the localized orthogonal decomposition method for the semiclassical Schrodinger equations with multiscale potentials in [9]. Some research outputs were presented by myself and my student in invited talks at six international and regional conferences. Joining these conferences allows us to present our research findings to a wider audience and engage in discussions with experts in the field. This exposure helps to disseminate our research and foster collaboration opportunities. Two Ph.D. students, Dr. Dingjiong Ma and Dr. Sijing Li were trained with support from the project. Dr. Ma joined the HUAWEI Theoretical Research Lab in Hong Kong and Dr. Li joined a financial company in Beijing. They will apply their expertise in computational mathematics to solve real-world problems.

17300318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300318.value: Stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), which incorporate random variables or stochastic processes, are crucial in modeling complex problems and quantifying associated uncertainties. Extensive efforts have been dedicated to studying the solutions of SPDEs, both analytically and numerically. With the successful development of numerous efficient numerical methods, researchers have made significant progress in solving SPDEs. However, the high dimensionality of solution spaces in many challenging real-world problems presents ongoing difficulties, limiting our ability to tackle them. Hence, there is a pressing need to investigate these complex problems and develop innovative approaches to overcome the limitations imposed by high dimensionality. In this project, our objective is to investigate low-dimensional structures in two types of high-dimensional stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), namely multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and Helmholtz equations in random media. Our goal is to develop efficient numerical methods to solve these SPDEs. To address the challenges associated with multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs, I have explored the low-dimensional structures in the solution spaces and developed several efficient numerical methods. In paper [1], I introduced the proper orthogonal decomposition-based method, which effectively captures and utilizes the dominant modes of the solution space. Building on this approach, paper [2] presents the multiscale multilevel Monte Carlo method, which combines the benefits of both multiscale and Monte Carlo techniques. To provide a novel perspective on these PDEs, the paper [5] proposes a data-driven approach employing intrinsic dimension reduction techniques. Lastly, in paper [12], I introduced the stochastic domain decomposition method, based on the variable-separation approach, which offers a powerful tool for addressing the multiscale nature of these PDEs. Together, these works contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the challenges associated with multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and present effective solutions from various angles, significantly advancing the field. Regarding the Helmholtz equations in random media, I have made significant progress in developing efficient numerical methods. In the paper [8], I introduced a quasi-Monte Carlo-based model reduction method specifically tailored for solving the Helmholtz equation in random media. Additionally, in [6], I proposed a Clenshaw-Curtis Smolyak rule for high-dimensional oscillatory integrals, which is designed to solve Helmholtz equations in random media. Building on the idea of model reduction, I further proposed a deterministic-statistical approach for an inverse acoustic source problem using multiple frequency limited aperture data in [11]. These contributions provide novel and effective approaches to solving the challenging Helmholtz equations in random media, and their potential applications are promising. The successful completion of this project marks a significant advancement in the development of numerical methods for high-dimensional stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), specifically for multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and Helmholtz equations in random media. They have the potential to be applied to solve other high-dimensional SPDEs, such as convection-dominated SPDEs. The newly developed methods now enable us to efficiently compute a wide range of real-world problems, including reservoir simulation and seismic inversion. As a result, the proposed project has the potential to generate broader impacts within the sciences and engineering community, offering valuable tools for tackling complex problems and advancing research in various fields.

17300318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300318.value: Based on the findings of this project, several potential research directions emerge for the future: (1) Developing adaptive basis functions and model reduction methods to solve convection-dominated stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). The inherent challenges posed by strong convection dominance and high-dimensionality of randomness necessitate novel approaches in designing adaptive basis functions and numerical methods. (2) Establishing efficient methods to solve the inverse problems associated with multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and Helmholtz equations in random media. This entails focusing on estimating random coefficients for the former and inferring the random refraction index for the latter. (3) Exploring the application of deep neural network-based methods in solving multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and Helmholtz equations in random media. Building upon the insights gained from this project, our understanding of the approximation properties of high-dimensional SPDEs will aid in the design of improved neural networks and facilitate the development of more accurate deep-learning methods for solving these complex high-dimensional SPDEs.

17300318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300318.value: Uncertainties abound in various scientific and engineering problems, including the transport of flow (such as groundwater, oil, and gas) in heterogeneous porous media and the propagation of acoustic waves in random media. Constructing mathematical models to describe these uncertainties and quantifying their impact on the quantities of interest is of utmost importance. Stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), which incorporate random variables or stochastic processes, play a crucial role in modeling complex problems and assessing their associated uncertainties. Thanks to the successful development of numerous efficient numerical methods, researchers have made significant progress in solving SPDEs. However, the high dimensionality of solution spaces presents ongoing challenges, limiting our ability to address many demanding real-world problems. This project involved the exploration of low-dimensional structures in two types of high-dimensional SPDEs: multiscale stochastic elliptic PDEs and Helmholtz equations in random media. We developed efficient numerical methods to solve these problems by constructing adaptive basis functions for their solutions and employing model reduction techniques. Our investigations also included studying important issues such as proving the exponential decay of adaptive basis functions, estimating the approximate separability of Green's functions, extracting solution information from incomplete measurements, and computing highly oscillatory integrals. We have carried out many numerical simulations to test the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods. The successful completion of the proposed project represents a significant advancement in the development of numerical methods for high-dimensional SPDEs. With the introduction of these new methods, we are now able to effectively compute a wide range of real-world problems, including reservoir simulation and seismic inversion. As a result, the proposed project holds great promise for generating broader impacts within the sciences and engineering community.

17300518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300518.value: 眾所周知，金和金類化合物是小分子活化和有機合成常用的催化劑，同時它們在材料科學和藥物化學的應用也引起了人們越來越多的興趣。與銥、鉑、銠等鉑族金屬相比，地球上金的儲量更為豐富。因此，為了揭示新的科學技術以及基於使用鉑族金屬的現有技術的可持續發展，對金化學的基礎研究，包括開發新的金基分子材料、催化劑和藥物的新策略，將是一個非常有吸引力的研究方向。到目前為止，金化學的應用研究主要集中於金（I）和納米金材料，與發光鉑配合物相比，發光金配合物的研究相當有限。隨著最近對金（I）和金（III）配合物的光譜性質及其激發態性質的理解更加深入，以下趨勢是很明顯的：（i）發光金（III）配合物在薄膜中的發光量子產率高達80％以上，極有潛力被開發成類似於磷光鉑（II）和銥（III）的具有實用前景的有機發光二極管(OLED) 發光材料；（ii）金配合物可以用作光誘導活化的光催化劑，在電子激發態下通過外球機制和/或內球原子提取途徑進行C-H和C-X鍵的活化。由於金離子對硫醇具有強結合親和力，可以開發對癌細胞所具有細胞毒性的金配合物，根據文獻報導，已經有一些金配合物體內抗腫瘤的活性比順鉑更有效。將具有細胞毒性的金配合物加入發光特性將帶來新的抗癌治療藥劑，開發這些治療藥劑在藥用無機化學領域是令大家感興趣的研究方向。本申請中用於治療和診斷的金配合物的抗癌特性將在化學生物學中心的相關平台進行評估測試，該化學生物中心的主任也是本申請的首席科學家。本項目的一個主要方向是開發新型的穩定的發光金配合物，包括具有橋接雙（N-雜環卡賓）配體的金（I）和具有四齒配體的金（III）配合物，這些配合物均被設計為具有長壽命激發態，具有在光氧化還原催化以及材料科學中的潛在用途。我們將通過使用微波等技術手段獲得新的金（III）配合物，以實現（i）具備高穩定性的發光金配合物材料；（ii）通過熱激活延遲熒光途徑實現具有較快輻射衰減速率的金配合物。這種金（III）配合物也可以用於能量下轉換反應以及單電子和雙電子 [Au（III）-Au（I）] 氧化還原催化。通過利用橋接二膦和/或雙（N-雜環卡賓）配體的電子和空間特性，我們擬在溶液中實現具有高量子效率的長壽命 [5dσ*6pσ] 三重激發態的雙核金（I）配合物，並以其作為內球氧化C-H鍵活化的強氧化劑和/或還原性C-X鍵裂解反應的強還原劑。我們擬通過各種方法包括超快速時間分辨吸收和發射光譜檢測單電子氧化的Au2（I，II）和雙電子氧化[Au2（II，II）]以及單電子還原[Au2（I，O）]。一般認為[Au2（I，II）H]和A-框架[Au2（II，II）X3]具有足夠的穩定性，能夠進行表徵、反應性研究和/或分離。本研究內容是金化學領域的最新進展，研究成果可進一步在應用領域帶動技術革新。如獲得資助，本研究結果將有助於提升香港在過渡金屬化學領域的卓越全球聲譽，促進發光金材料的實際應用。考慮到中國大陸地區黃金礦藏豐富，本研究所得的成果將在該地區具有重要的戰略意義。

17300518.label: Realisation of objectives
17300518.value: During the project period, we have developed and prepared new classes of luminescent gold(I) and gold(III) complexes and examined their excited state dynamics and photophysical properties. The photochemistry and photo-catalytic properties of these newly prepared gold(I) and (III) complexes have also been investigated. Six papers have been published in peer-reviewed journals: 4 in ACIE, 1 in Adv. Mater., 1 in PNAS. One book chapter was published in Adv. Inorg. Chem. Three presentations were delivered in international conferences. The support from this GRF grant has been acknowledged in these contributions (papers, book chapter and presentations). The manuscripts for the completed yet unpublished works, being extracted from PhD thesis and patents (filed application) are also attached. The findings are summarized below: [1] Objective 1: We prepared cyclometalated Au(III) hydride complexes supported by C^N^C ligands. These complexes display triplet intraligand (3IL) phosphorescence with quantum yields and lifetimes of up to 0.093 and 89 μs, respectively, featuring rare examples of luminescent metal-hydride complexes. Upon light excitation, the Au(III) hydride complex is converted to a Au(III) aryl complex, with the aryl ligand being the phenyl moiety of a free C^N^C ligand, and with its structure determined by X-ray crystallography Mechanistic studies revealed homolytic cleavage of Au(III)-H bond in the excited state. This work is published as a chapter in the PhD thesis of Dr. Zhou Dongling (https://hub.hku.hk/handle/10722/313725). A manuscript to be submitted for publication is also attached. [2] Objective 1. We have prepared a series of cyclometalated Au(III) dimers supported by bridging ligands such as pyrazolate, N,N'-diarylformamidinate and pyridin-2-olate. These complexes display short intramolecular Au-Au distances of down to 2.92 Å, and are emissive in degassed solution at room temperature with emission quantum yields and emission lifetimes in the range of 0.0005–0.14 and 0.67–85.9 µs respectively. With the use of 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole and 4,4'-(5-methyl-1,3-phenylene)bis(3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole) as bridging ligands, trinuclear and tetranuclear Au(III) complexes were obtained. This work is included as a chapter in the PhD thesis of Dr. Lo Kar-Wai. [3] Objective 1. Tetradentate Au(III) complexes having diarylamino donor group have been prepared. These complexes show intense thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in solutions and in thin films at room temperature with quantum yields and radiative decay rate constants (kr) of up to 0.98 and 1.93×10^6 s^-1, respectively. Femtosecond time-resolved absorption difference and emission (fs-ta) spectroscopy revealed intersystem crossing (ISC) rates ranging from 4.88×10^10 to 1.52×10^11 s^-1. OLEDs fabricated with these Au(III) emitters showed EQEs of up to 27% and efficiency roll-off <6%. The device operational lifetime LT90 at 1000 cd m^-2 reached 1820 hours, which is the highest value among Au(I) and Au(III) OLEDs. One of these Au(III)-TADF complexes can undergo energy transfer with a multi-resonance TADF emitter BN2, and the OLED fabricated with these Au(III)-TADF sensitizer and BN2 emitter in the emissive layer displayed narrowband emission with EQE of up to 29.4%. [Adv. Mater. 2022, 2206598] [4] Objective 1. In the course of our study, we found that attachment of Au atom to rigid B- and N-(O-) doped polyaromatic hydrocarbons (abbreviated as “BN”) leads to enhancement of ISC and reverse ISC (RISC) rate constants. These as-prepared Au-BN complexes display emission with quantum yields up to 0.93 in degassed THF at room temperature. fs-ta and femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-trf) measurements were conducted to study the excited state dynamics of these compounds. OLEDs fabricated with these Au-BN complexes as emitters showed EQE of up to 30.3 %. [ACIE 2022, 61, e202213392] [5] Objective 1. In the course of our investigation on Au(III) thiolates and acetylides, Au(I) thiolates and Au(I) acetylides were found to undergo self-assembly reactions to give “ring-in-ring” Au(I) clusters and trefoil knot structures, respectively. These luminescent Au(I)-self-assemblies display novel structures and we examined their excited state properties and photochemical properties. By fs-ta spectroscopy, a Au9Cu6 trefoil knot was found to sensitize the formation of singlet oxygen with quantum yield of 5%. [ACIE 2019, 58, 16297-16306; ACIE 2022, 61, e202200748] [6] Objectives 2 and 3. A series of binuclear Au(I) bis-NHC complexes with short intramolecular Au-Au distances ranging 3.01-3.07 Å have been synthesized and characterized by single crystal X-ray crystallography. In degassed MeCN, all these complexes display a high-energy emission with peak maxima at 442-475 nm, quantum yields of 0.25-0.62 and lifetimes of 0.7-12.7 μs. Some of them display an addition low-energy emission with peak maxima at 565-622 nm and lifetimes of 2.5-6.5 μs. The high- and low-energy emission are respectively assigned to [5dσ*6pσ] excited states and anion-exciplex. fs-ta and fs-tre measurements conducted on Au-1 as a representative example revealed the ISC rate constant of Au-1 to be 1.6×10^10 s^-1. Importantly, Au-1 was found to catalyze the dehydrogenation of benzylic alcohols upon 390 nm LEDs irradiation to give diols or ketones under oxygen-free, acceptorless condition. Under the same condition, 1,4-cyclohexadiene was converted to give benzene, cyclohexene, cyclohexane and hydrogen. The formation of cyclohexene and cyclohexane is indicative of the presence of gold-hydride intermediate(s), and this has been confirmed by HR-ESI MS analysis of the reaction solution obtained by photolysis of Au-1 with 1,4-cyclohexadiene. Complex Au-1 was found to generate the corresponding Au(II)-Au(II) dihalide complexes ([Au2X2]2+; X = Cl, Br, I) upon photolysis in the presence of alkyl/aryl halides. Notably, [Au2X2]2+ complexes undergo reductive elimination under 390 nm LEDs irradiation to generate their [Au2]2+ counterpart in alcohols (methanol, ethanol and IPA) without addition of external halogen trap. This work is included as a chapter in the PhD thesis of Tang Rui (just submitted for examination). [7] Objectives 2 and 3. A series of binuclear Au(I) diphosphine complexes with different substituents on the diphosphine ligands have been synthesized. The one functionalized with morpholine ligand (bis(bis(4-morpholinophenyl)phosphanyl)methane) displays singlet LMMCT absorption that tails to the visible spectral region. This complex exhibits phosphorescence from LMMCT excited state with anion-exciplex formation, and with quantum yield of 0.59 and lifetime of 2.0 μs in degassed MeCN. It can activate aryl/alkyl halides under 405 nm LEDs irradiation. Upon laser flash photolysis in the presence of halocarbons, long-lived ns-ta signal that last for >90 µs is generated, which could be attributed to the formation of [Au(I)-Au(II)-X]2+. Another Au(I) complex with a bulky diphosphine ligand (bis(bis(4,4''-di-tert-butyl-[1,1':3',1''-terphenyl]-5'-yl)phosphanyl)methane) displays higher activity in photodehydrogenation of allylic C-H bonds (e.g. 1,4-cyclohexadiene) among this Au(I) diphosphine complexes. A patent application based on this work has been filed and an unpublished manuscript for this work is attached. [8] Objective 4. We discovered a previously unknown biomolecular binding interaction between Au(III)MesoIX and cysteine thiols of cancer-associated proteins (thioredoxin, peroxiredoxin, and deubiquitinases). The electrophilic Au(III) center is proposed to activate the meso-carbon atom of the ligand, leading to the formation of covalent thiol adduct. [PNAS 2020, 117, 1321-1329] [9] Objective 4. We published a book chapter summarizing the recent advances on anti-cancer gold, platinum and iridium compounds with porphyrin and/or N-heterocyclic carbene ligand(s). [Adv. Inorg. Chem. 2020, 75, 87-119] [10] Objective 4. We recently prepared a cyclometalated Au(III) NHC complex supported by a doubly-deprotonated C^N^N ligand. This complex forms nanoparticles in solution (PBS with 0.25% DMSO), displays potent cytotoxicity towards all tested human cancer cell lines (10 to 100-fold more toxic than cisplatin), and binds with the mitochondrial chaperone HSPD1 in NCI-H460 and induces morphology change in mitochondria. Part of this work was published in the undergraduate research thesis of Mr. Wong Kwan-Yuen [unpublished]
