17300518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300518.value: The studies conducted in this project are instrumented to the development of new classes of luminescent Au(I) and Au(III) complexes showing long-lived excited states that can be harnessed for various applications. In essence, we have accomplished the followings: [1] 6 publications in international chemistry journals including Angewandte Chemie International Edition and Advanced Materials, and 1 book chapter. [2] 3 presentations on this research topic were delivered in international conferences. [3] An important breakthrough in luminescent Au(III) complexes is the realization of a tetradentate gold(III)-TADF emitter displaying 98% emission quantum yield and radiative decay rate constant of 1.75×10^6 s^-1 in thin film, which is unprecedent in gold chemistry. More importantly, the OLEDs fabricated with this emitter showed EQE up to 24.9% and LT90 up to 1820 hours at 1000 cd m^-2, the latter of which is the best value in literature among gold(III) emitters.[Adv. Mater. 2022, 2206598] [4] Au(I) multi-resonance TADF emitters have been realized by incorporating rigid B- and N-(O-) doped polyaromatic hydrocarbons as an auxiliary ligand to Au(I)-NHC. High luminance of up to 2.53×10^5 cd m^-2, and EQE of up to 30.3% have been achieved with the OLEDs fabricated with these Au(I) emitters. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202213392] [5] Rare “ring-in-ring” and trefoil knot structures have been prepared by self-assembly of Au(I) thiolates and acetylides, respectively. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2019, 58, 16297–16306; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, 61, e202200748] [6] Gold(I) bis-NHC complexes could undergo self-assembly with multiple kinetic aggregation states. Some of them exhibit nonlinear optical response of second harmonic generation (SHG) and function as optical waveguides. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2022, accepted, DOI:10.1002/anie.202216523] [7] Cysteine thiol conjugation to the Au(III)-activated porphyrin scaffold through nucleophilic aromatic substitution was discovered for the first time. Such reactivity serves as an alternative modality for cysteine targeting and for the development of cancer therapeutics. [Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U. S. A. 2020, 117, 1321-1329] [8] With the use of a new morpholine-functionalized diphosphine ligand, we developed a new class of highly efficient binuclear Au(I) photo-catalysts that absorb in the visible spectral region and efficiently catalyze visible light (LED light) driven C-C bond formation reactions from aryl/allyl bromides even at a very low catalyst loading. [Unpublished] [9] Binuclear Au(I) bis-NHC complexes displaying emission from 3[5dσ*6pσ] excited state and/or anion-exciplex are efficient photocatalysts for organic transformations, some of which involve H-atom abstraction by the Au(I) complex. Photolysis of binuclear Au(II) bis-NHC dihalide complexes in MeOH regenerates the parental Au(I) bis-NHC complex, opening up the possibility of photocatalysis without the need for sacrificial electron donor and/or electron acceptor. [Patent application filed] [10] A cyclometalated Au(III) NHC complex supported by a doubly-deprotonated C^N^N ligand was prepared which forms nanoparticles in solution (PBS with 0.25% DMSO), displays potent cytotoxicity towards all tested human cancer cell lines (10 to 100-fold more toxic than cisplatin), and binds with the mitochondrial chaperone HSPD1 in NCI-H460 and induces morphology change in mitochondria. [Unpublished]

17300518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300518.value: The results of this project have further enlightened the great potential of luminescent Au(I) and Au(III) complexes in the design and synthesis of photo-functional materials that could have profound applications in organic display technology and in visible-light-driven organic synthesis. The rich excited state properties of the Au complexes demonstrated in our works, especially the establishment of Au(I) and Au(III) complexes as new avenues for developing highly emissive TADF emitters, suggest that Au complexes can be designed to display electroluminescence properties comparable to those of the state-of-art Pt(II) and Ir(III) emitters by employing a judicious choice of ligands. With the insight gained from these studies, we will continue to do molecular engineering on luminescent Au(I) and Au(III) complexes, such that their photophysical and photochemical properties can be tailored for specific applications in diverse areas. Besides, the use of binuclear Au(I) complexes as photocatalysts opens new avenues for photochemical activation and functionalization of unreactive C-H and C-X bonds at the inner coordination sphere without the need of sacrificial oxidant and/or reductants. Luminescent Au complexes have a very bright prospect and further studies in this area would unearth gold-based molecular materials and photo-catalysis with practical industrial application.

17300518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300518.value: Molecular phosphorescent materials have potential applications in OLEDs, photocatalysis and biomedicines. However, as up to now, these materials are largely based on platinum and iridium, both of which have low earth abundance. In comparison, gold has a higher earth-abundance than Pt and Ir, but the practical applications of gold complexes are far fewer than these two noble metals. This project has been successful to unearth new photophysical and photochemical properties of luminescent gold complexes that could be harnessed for applications. With suitable structural design, the gold complexes developed in this project display outstanding photophysical properties with emission quantum yields and radiative decay rate constants that are hardly achieved by the luminescent platinum and iridium complexes. We also developed gold(I) complexes that can act as photocatalysts for a broad range of organic transformations at low catalyst loadings. Studies on the interaction of gold(III) complexes with biomolecules revealed a previously unknown covalent binding mode. The findings in this project clearly establish the bright prospect of gold complexes in light-related and chemical biology applications.

17300718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300718.value: Burmese amber, also known as burmite, has been mined by humans since 600 BC. Burmese amber from the Hukawng Valley in northern Myanmar was once thought to be Miocene or Eocene in age, but is now known to be the only Cretaceous amber deposit in the world available for both commercial purposes and scientific research. Due to changing political conditions, northern Myanmar has become more accessible to international researchers and numerous research groups are now studying inclusions found in Burmese amber. Burmese amber may host the largest variety of Cretaceous plant and animal found in a single deposit. With their exceptional preservation, the amber inclusions specifically provide a window into tropical forest ecosystems of ~99 million years ago. The amber deposits however are not well constrained in terms of their geologic age or context. We propose to investigate stratrigraphy and establish a robust age determination for the fossil-bearing amber from the Hukawng Valley of Kachin Province, Myanmar. This research will answer several fundamental questions: 1) What is the oldest stratigraphic evidence of damselfly courtship behavior? 2) During what time frame did the toothed birds Enantiornithes exist? 3) When did feathered dinosaurs migrate to northern Myanmar? 4) What is the evolutionary tree of mushrooms? 自古以來，緬甸產的琥珀就以漂亮的色澤和質地聞名，是收藏家們爭相收藏的珍寶。自從近幾年緬甸的政治情勢漸趨穩定之後，來自全世界的琥珀愛好者紛紛到這裡尋寶，近期，科學家們在緬甸琥珀中發現許多保存完整、種類繁多的動物和植物化石，目前已經被報導的化石包括有羽毛的恐龍尾巴、型態奇特的蜻蜓、和熱帶植物，因為緬甸琥珀的生成年代大約是白堊紀，建立精確的琥珀年代，能夠讓我們對白堊紀的生態環境和物種演化更深入的認識。

17300718.label: Realisation of objectives
17300718.value: 1. During the first part of this study, we obtained more than ten datable samples from Central and Northern Myanmar. After the preliminary U-Pb ICP-MS studies, inclusion-free volcanic zircons were sent to MIT for high-precision CA-ID-TIMS U-Pb dating. Results indicate an Albian to early Cenomanian age for the (northern) Burmese amber (~112 Ma for Khamti amber and ~100-98.8 Ma for Kachin amber). Biostratigraphic analyses of all recently reported fossil inclusions from Burmese amber show that its biota, although confined to the southern hemisphere, strongly resembles that found in ambers from Spain. Burmese amber (senso lato) appears to have a protracted depositional history ranging from at least early Albian to late Campanian in age. 2. Burmese amber from the Tanai and Khamti deposits has been sold on gem markets for the past few years. The similar physical character, especially of polished amber pieces makes it difficult to distinguish between the two source sites. In our study, we investigated amber inclusions from both sites. We also established biostratigraphic correlations from both locations. The distribution and duration of shared Cretaceous genera were examined to establish biostratigraphic age. Biostratigraphic analysis of all 1574 species found in described specimens indicates a late Albian age. The Burmese amber genera shared with other Cretaceous fossil sites include those belonging to the taxa Entomobryomorpha, Archaeognatha, Ephemeroptera, Odonata, Dictyoptera, Hemiptera, Psocoptera, Thysanoptera, Coleoptera, Diptera, Hymenoptera, Neuroptera, and Raphidioptera. The orders Diptera and Hymenoptera dominate the shared taxa. In Burmese amber, the Coleoptera are the most diverse group, but most of the described genera belong to new taxa and thus cannot provide biostratigraphic constraints. Burmese amber contains Cretakarenni and Prosolierius, which also occur in the late Albian Álava amber, and Paleoripiphorus, which occurs in the late Albian Charentese amber of France. Our study has allowed to understand the Mesozoic biodiversities. 3. The Kachin amber deposits lie ca. 20 km southwest of Tanai Town and served as a significant source of amber for Burmese gem markets. Previous researchers have provided detailed descriptions of the excavation of Burmese amber, which occurs mainly in the area near a northerly hill referred to as Noije Bum. During colonial times, the largest amber deposit occurred at the Khanjamaw site, which was located at ca. 1.5 km northeast of Nojie Bum. In the past several years, research into Burmese amber has expanded, especially near Noije Bum. Amber in this area appears in tuffs or tuffaceous clastics (mudstones, sandstones, and coal seals) and within thin limestone beds. The Khamti amber deposits are located ca. 80 km southwest of Nojie Bum, especially at Pat-tar bum (Pat-ta bum) near the Nampilin stream of Khamti Town. Ngaw reported an amber site named Nam Sakhaw, which overlaps regionally with the Khamti site. The amber from the Nam Sakhaw site probably represents the first record of Khamti amber. The Khamti amber occurred in Cretaceous Orbitolina limestone and was extracted between 1948 and 1961 (colonial era). Khamti amber was rediscovered around 2012–2013 by local miners. With the closure of the Tanai sites in 2017, more than 1000 miners now excavate amber in open and underground pits accessing the Khamti deposits. The Khamti deposits have thus become the primary source of amber for the gem market in the past two years. The Khamti amber occurs in tuffs, tuffaceous sandstones, and shales, interbedded with calcareous sandstones and limestones. Recent investigations have confirmed the occurrence of Khamti amber in Orbitolina-bearing limestones. The Albian to Cenomanian age Orbitolina limestones occur widely throughout northern Myanmar. Our dating results carry implications for locating additional deposits. 4. This project supported two Ph.D. students, Daran Zheng and Yuling Li. Daran has graduated from HKU and now is a researcher at Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology. Since Yuling Ph.D. study in the summer of 2019, she has been trained to be a paleontologist with geochronologic skills. Now she is able to interpret geochronologic data well. This project also provided an opportunity for undergraduate students in EASC3417 "Earth Through Time" to learn Mesozoic ecosystems, tectonic history, and geochronology. In the first and sixth lectures of EASC3417, students observed amber pieces from Myanmar and elsewhere. Students discussed how the amber formed and why amber inclusions are important to understanding Earth's history.

17300718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300718.value: This project is successful as we established high-precision ages for amber sites from Myanmar. Our ages indicated that there was a biological hotspot in Myanmar during the mid-late Cretaceous time period. Our study further allows understanding of the formation and preservation of amber in the past. We summarise that Burmese amber shares typical genera with late Albian Álava, San Just, and EI Soplao ambers from Spain, and with the Charentese amber from France. Burmese amber shares the largest number of shared genera with the Álava amber. A late Albian biostratigraphic age comports with geochronologic constraints discovered in our collaborative study. Along with a late Campanian U-Pb zircon age estimate for the Tilin amber from central Myanmar, data obtained in our study indicate a protracted depositional history for Cretaceous amber in Myanmar spanning from the early Albian to the late Campanian. Burmese amber (sensu stricto) previously only referred to as amber found near Tanai in the Hukawng Valley, northern Myanmar. Here we demonstrate that Khamti amber (~112 Ma; early Albian) and Kachin amber (~100-98.8 Ma; early Cenomanian) formed during a similar time frame. The new geochronologic constraints elucidate the origin and early evolution of some important biologic elements and animal behavioral indicators recorded in Burmese amber. These include the earliest documented lizard assemblage in amber, the earliest evidence of insect pollination of flowering plants, and morphological specialization of insects showing sociality and social parasitism. We included this research topic in one book chapter that was published in Geological Society, London, Special Publications 521. Based on our high-precision TIMS U/Pb data and fossil records from Myanmar, we are preparing the manuscript which will be submitted to Geology in a few months.

17300718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300718.value: With further studies, we will investigate more Cretaceous amber sites from South and East Asia. Our goals are to establish high-precision ages for important amber outcrops and to further understand the bio-diversities during the middle and late Mesozoic. For example, we recently started working on new amber outcrops in China. Our discovery of in situ ambers from the Yimin and Zhalainuoer coal fields in the Hailar Basin extends the geographic distribution of amber outcrops into northeast China. Stratigraphic correlation and U/Pb geochronology indicate the Hailar ambers formed in the Early Cretaceous and thus represent the oldest known amber in China. Further investigations into the amber-bearing Yimin Formation will advance understanding of Cretaceous biota, local ecosystems, global environmental change, and the link between biology and climate. We are preparing a manuscript that will be submitted to Palaeogeography, Palaeoclimatology, Palaeoecology soon.

17300718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300718.value: Amber is a fossilized tree resin ranging from a few million to 320 million years. Amber is found worldwide, from the Arctic to Antarctica. Dating at least back to the Neolithic period, around 13,000 years ago, humans have valued amber for its color and natural beauty. In the past three decades, scientists started working on ambers as they provide secrets to the Earth's history. Amber-bearing deposits are among the most essential Konservat-Lagerstetten, providing unique windows into past ecosystems. The variety of biological inclusions preserved in pristine, three-dimensional conditions within amber can contain different lines of evidence. Studies demonstrate that delicate organisms are preserved in amber with life-like, microscopic fidelity. Sometimes even complex behavior is preserved. As phylogenetic precision depends on the number of preserved taxa, fossils in amber have considerably resolved evolutionary parameters and relationships. Our study from Myanmar has revealed the biodiversities, ecosystems, and evolutionary history of many groups of animals.

17300918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300918.value: Quantum clocks and quantum gyroscopes have the potential to measure time and orientation with unprecedented precision, which could revolutionize GPS technology and navigation systems. Recent advances in quantum communication suggest that quantum clocks and gyroscopes could be connected into networks, allowing a number of distant parties to establish a common time standard and to align their reference frames with unprecedented accuracy. Similar advantages can be envisaged for a variety of quantum sensors, which could be linked up into networks for the ultraprecise measurement of various quantities such as temperature, particle density, electromagnetic fields, and gravitational fields. The realization of quantum sensor networks, however, is limited by the low transmission rates and by the high costs of quantum communication. These limitations make the transmission of quantum bits a precious resource, which must be used in the most efficient way. In this project, we will apply methods of quantum Shannon theory to design sensor networks that achieve quantum-enhanced precision while requiring the minimum amount of quantum communication. More broadly, we will develop a general theory of communication efficiency in quantum sensor networks, and we will devise testable criteria to validate the first experimental demonstrations of quantum advantages in realistic networks. This research will build upon techniques developed by our group in a series of recent works, which offer a systematic method to construct data compression protocols for quantum sensors and benchmarks for the demonstration of quantum advantages. In addition to optimizing the communication efficiency of quantum sensor networks, we will explore their security. We will develop cryptographic protocols whereby the nodes of a network can establish a private time reference or a private frame of spatial directions, accessible only to authorized parties. We will also develop protocols that are robust to errors and can deal with faulty behavior of certain nodes. Such protocols will be useful in situations where some of the communication links are disrupted, or where some of the nodes have fallen under the control of an attacker. This project will contribute to the design and experimental demonstration of future quantum sensor networks. In the long term, the realization of large-scale quantum networks will have powerful applications to geodesy, electrometry, magnetometry, and fundamental physics, enabling tests of quantum mechanics in previously unexplored spacetime scenarios. 量子鐘和量子陀螺儀有著以突破性精度測量時間和空間信息的潛力，可以從根本上革新GPS等定位技術。量子通訊方向的最新進展表面量子鐘和量子陀螺可以被接入網絡中，從而使得相互距離很遠的一組用戶可以以更高精度建立共同的時間標準或參照系。可以預期的是，類似的優勢也存在於其他種類的量子傳感器中。這些傳感器也可以建立起用於測量一系列物理量的高精度網絡，如溫度、粒子質量、電磁場和引力場。 然而，量子傳感器網絡的實現會受到低傳輸效率以及高傳輸成本的制約。基於這些限制，量子通訊比特應被看作一種寶貴資源并被以最高效方式利用。在本項目中，我們將運用一系列量子香農理論中的手段，在保持量子傳感器網絡高精度的同時最小化其所需的通訊資源。更廣泛地，我們將發展量子傳感器網絡通訊效率的一般理論，并設計可測基準來驗證首批量子傳感器網絡的實驗展示。本研究將建立在項目組近期發展的一系列技術上。這些技術提供了構建量子數據壓縮協議以及驗證量子優勢的基準點的系統化手段。 在優化量子傳感器網絡的通訊效率以外，我們還將探討它們的安全性問題。我們將研發一系列安全性協議，使得同一網絡中的節點可以建立私有的時間或空間參照系。我們也將研發可以抵抗噪聲和某些節點的惡意行為的協議。當網絡中某些通訊鏈接被干擾或某些節點被劫持時，這類型通訊協議會變得十分有用。 本項目將為量子傳感器網絡的設計及實驗實現做出貢獻。從長期看，這類大規模量子網絡的實現將在測地學、電磁學測量以及基礎物理方向產生強有力的應用，使得在某些前所未見的時空場景中測試量子理論變為可能。

17300918.label: Realisation of objectives
17300918.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved to a major extent, and the corresponding research has resulted in the publication of 10 research papers, of which 1 in Nature Communications, 2 in Physical Review Letters, 2 in Proceedings of the Royal Society A, and 2 in Quantum. Objective 1: communication-efficient quantum sensor networks. This objective was the most foundational of the project, and has been achieved through a series of works that connect the precision of quantum sensing with the communication capacity of quantum communication links. The starting point of our work has the observation that the interference among multiple paths in a network can increase the amount of information that is reliably transferred from one point to another, thereby increasing the sensing performance when quantum communication is used to transfer information about physical parameters. This work has been done in collaboration with PhD student Hlér Kristjánsson from Oxford University, who has been co-supervised by the PI, The results have been published in Proceedings of the Royal Society A. The second step of our work has been the development of a framework for measurement on dynamical processes, such as the estimation of a parameter of the dynamics of a physical system. This framework is suitable for analytical and numerical optimization, and can be applied to a variety of sensing problems. Our work has been published in Proceedings of the Royal Society A. The combination of the two ingredients described above has then been used to design a new type of sensing protocol, where multiple sensors are combined in a coherent superposition of different configurations. The idea is that each sensor is probing a parameter of a dynamical process, and that the quantum communication links between the sensors can be used to connect these dynamical processes in a coherent superposition of multiple configurations. In our concrete example, the order of the processes ends up being in a quantum superposition, giving rise to a feature known as "indefinite causal order." The superposition of causal orders gives rise to a precision scaling that could not be achieved if the dynamical processes where probed in a fixed order, as in most of the existing quantum sensing protocols. In the specific problem considered in our work, we have shown that the total precision with N sensors can grow as the fourth power of N, whereas every protocol where the processes are probed in a definite order could only give a precision growing as the square of N, which is known as the Heisenberg limit. The work has been published in Physical Review Letters. In addition to the above results, we developed a number of results on the foundations of quantum measurement, tomographic, and sensing protocols, and on the theory of quantum protocols that connect multiple dynamical processes in a quantum network. At the fundamental level, this included a substantial part of research on the use of causal connections as resources for quantum communication and sensing. Objective 2: Benchmarks for the demonstration of quantum advantages. This objective has been fully achieved and, in addition, has stimulated experimental work based on our results. We provided to main benchmarks. The first benchmark refers to the superposition of configurations exploited in our PRL paper "Quantum Metrology with Indefinite Causal Order," whose results are summarized in the previous point. Specifically, we have showed that, for the problem under consideration, the super-Heisenberg scaling can be achieved only through a coherent superposition of the order in which the processes are probed. As a consequence, the observation of a precision scaling better than the Heisenberg scaling can be regarded as a witness of the ability to coherently control the connections between the sensors. In other words, the Heisenberg scaling can be regarded as the benchmark that has to be surpassed in order to demonstrate the genuine implementation of quantum sensing with coherent superposition of configurations. This benchmark has been used in a recent photonic experiment, performed by the group of Prof. Biheng Liu at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei, where super-Heisenberg scaling has been observed to a high degree of statistical significance. While the previous benchmark applied to a specific sensing problem, a general technique for deriving benchmarks has been developed later in our work, where we established a number of advantages of coherent quantum information processing in terms of the thermodynamic resources needed to achieve a desired level of accuracy. Building on our results, we showed that, for a broad set of tasks, coherent quantum information processing is necessary in order to achieve the ultimate limit. In contrast, classical information processing schemes, based on measurement and classical data processing on the measurement outcomes, are necessarily thermodynamically inefficient. The maximal efficiency achievable by classical, incoherent schemes, can then serve as a benchmark to witness the use of genuinely quantum resources. We developed this idea explicitly in the case of quantum communication from one node to another of a quantum network, and we established the maximum fidelity of transmission achievable with a given budget of thermodynamic resources. The results of this paper have been published in Nature Communications. Objective 3: secure distributed sensing. This objective has been achieved to a substantial extent, although we expect that further results could be obtained, and for this reason we ranked the achievement as 90%. In collaboration with co-PI Prof. HK Chau, we developed a new protocol for quantum communication through N nodes of a quantum network, arranged in a cyclic configuration. The connection between each node is described by a completely depolarizing channel, which is generally regarded as the prototype of an extremely noisy channel that prevents any form of communication, including, of course, secure quantum communication. Despite the presence of extremely noisy channels, we have shown that the possibility to coherently control the transmission of information through the nodes of the network enables a transmission of quantum data in the scenario where the number of parties, N, becomes large. This effect remains valid also for finite values of N, in which case we have shown a lower bound to the amount of quantum data that can be safely transmitted from one point to another. This work has been published in Physical Review Letters. In a subsequent work, we explored the use of accurate quantum sensing for the development of quantum error correcting schemes. We considered a particular type of error correcting protocols, known as transversal error correcting codes, which are known to be valuable for quantum computing. Exact transversal codes are forbidden by a general result, known as the Eastin-Knill theorem. In our work, we developed a new construction that takes an arbitrary code and converts into another code that is approximately transversal. The technique is based on the idea of appending a sensor to the encoding qubits, and the quality of the approximation improves with the precision of sensing at a quadratic rate that is reminiscent of the Heisenberg limit. We applied our technique to the development of error correcting schemes for various types of erasing errors, corresponding to faulty nodes of a network in which information can be lost. This work has been published in Quantum.

17300918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300918.value: This project achieved three major outcomes, the first two published in Physical Review Letters and the third in Nature Communications. The first major outcome is an enhanced sensing scheme using a network of quantum devices in a coherent quantum superposition of alternative configurations. We found that the coherent superposition of configuration allows us to overcome the so-called Heisenberg limit, which is generally regarded as the ultimate precision limit set by quantum mechanics. In our work, we considered a sensor network scenario where different local sensors collect information about some physical parameters (specifically, displacements of a harmonic oscillator) and the goal is to evaluate a quadratic function of these parameters. The result is that by transferring quantum information from one sensor to the other, and controlling the paths of the communicated information in a coherent fashion, the desired function can be measured with a precision that scales like the quartic power of the number of sensors. Notably, we showed that this scaling is impossible to achieve without coherent control on the communication paths in the network. This result establishes the superposition of configurations as a new resource for quantum sensing. The second major outcome is a demonstration that the coherent superposition of configurations permits secure quantum communication even in noisy scenarios where security could not be achieved in standard quantum communication protocols. Our protocol enables a nearly noiseless transmission of quantum bits even in the presence of completely depolarizing noise, which in normal conditions would replace every signal with white noise. Finally, our third major result is a fundamental limit on the accuracy of general information processing tasks, including (but not limited to) sensing. We discovered a universal relation that connects the achievable accuracy with the amount of thermodynamic resources invested in the realization of the desired information processing task. In addition, we established an advantage of coherent quantum information processing over protocols that convert data into a classical form. To certify the advantage we developed benchmarks that can be used in realistic scenarios, such as the transmission of quantum information over noisy channels.

17300918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300918.value: this project opened up two new research directions that we plan to further explore in the coming years. The first direction is the study of new sensing protocols boosted by coherent superpositions of multiple configurations. The idea is that the sensors in a quantum sensor network can be connected by sending quantum data through multiple paths. The availability of multiple paths then enables interference effects that can boost the precision in the estimation of physical parameters, sometimes beating the limits of traditional quantum sensing schemes. An important open question we are currently studying concerns the maximum achievable advantages, and their robustness in realistic scenarios where the visibility of interference is reduced by noise and loss. The second main direction is the study of the relation between the precision of sensing and the physical resources used in the process. Previous works focussed on the energy initially present in the sensors. The techniques developed in this process enable us to study the total amount of resources, including those associated to the realization of the detectors, and those associated to the transmission of quantum signals within the sensor network. We plan to exploit these techniques in a forthcoming project.

17300918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300918.value: This project developed measurement schemes that achieve superior precision through the transmission of quantum systems in a network of sensors. The working principle of our protocols is the ability of quantum particles to travel simultaneously through multiple paths. By taking advantage of this feature, our schemes achieve a level of precision that could not be achieved by the previous measurement schemes. The use of quantum communication between sensors also offers a number of security features, which enable precise measurements with the guarantee that the measurement parameter remains hidden from malicious third parties. To enable the demonstration of the above advantages in realistic scenarios, we developed a number of benchmarks that can be used to certify the use of coherent communication among sensors. One of these benchmarks been already been used in a photonic demonstration, and other experimental realizations are expected to be possible in the near term. In the longer term, our results provide the foundation for a new generation of quantum precision measurements boosted by communication between different sensors, and could eventually give rise to technological applications in the field of quantum sensing, which is generally regarded as one of the most promising quantum technologies.

17301018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301018.value: Ring structures abound in bioactive compounds and natural products. The ability to exploit and develop these compounds for therapeutic purposes is contingent on the ability to asymmetrically synthesize functionalized ring structures bearing various substituents effectively and efficiently. Cycloadditions are therefore excellent strategies for the construction of ring compounds, and for the synthesis of seven-membered rings that are found in many bioactive natural product frameworks, the (4+3) cycloaddition represents one of the most convergent approaches. However, although there has been much research done on (4+3) cycloadditions, the range of dienes used has been limited to largely endocyclic and the more reactive dienes. In this project we seek to challenge and engage typically unreactive aromatic compounds such as arenes and thiophenes as dienes in the (4+3) cycloaddition of epoxy or aziridinyl enolsilanes. This novel reaction would allow us to devise a new route towards tubingensin B, an anti-cancer and anti-viral natural product. Cycloadducts derived from substituted benzenes and thiophenes would also allow us to exploit derivatizations that cleave the bridges, for obtaining unbridged cycloheptanoids that are found in many natural product frameworks. This proposal has both method development and application aspects, and overall could greatly increase the utility of (4+3) cycloadditions to the synthesis of a broader range of optically enriched cycloheptanoids and bioactive natural products. Furthermore, the successful synthesis of tubingensin B will allow us to study the chemical biology of this compound and possibly harness its anti-cancer and anti-viral properties for therapeutic purposes in the form of derivatives. 環狀結構廣泛存在於生物活性化合物及天然產物當中。這類化合物的製備和開發依賴於如何高效地，不對稱地構建含各種官能團的環狀結構。環加成反應是合成環狀化合物極佳的策略。而對含七員環的天然產物來説，（4+3）環加成反應是最直接和高效的途徑。 儘管學界已經做了多年關於（4+3）環加成反應的研究，能夠發生有效反應的二烯至今依然局限於一些持高反應活性的，如環内二烯。 本課題以研究通常反應惰性的芳香化合物，如芳烴和噻吩的(4+3)環加成反應，並採用環氧和氮雜環丙烷烯醇硅醚為親二烯體。這新型的反應可以應用於抗癌，抗病毒的天然產物tubingensin B的全合成新路綫。苯和噻吩的環加成產物通過斷裂橋鏈，可以得到非橋接的環庚烷類化合物，具備在天然產物中常見和重要的骨架。 本課題既有方法學的探討，也有其應用，能夠增加(4+3)環加成反應的應用範圍，合成一系列具有光学活性的環庚烷類，具有生物活性的天然產物。如能成功完成tubingensin B的全合成，我們便能夠探究其化學生物活性，從而找到具有更好抗癌，抗病毒活性的衍生物。

17301118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301118.value: 整合素 (integrin) 是一類通過結合多種蛋白質配體，實現細胞內外信號傳導的重要膜蛋 白。整合素調控細胞與環境、細胞與細胞之間的相互作用，影響細胞增殖、分化、遷移、形態變化、免疫應答等重要生命活動，從而在多種惡性腫瘤中高度表達，是抗腫瘤藥物研發和疾病診斷的一類重要靶標。本研究項目提出一種新穎的基於 DNA 光活分子探針的蛋白質標記方法，能夠在活細胞表面實現對蛋白質-蛋白質相互作用的標記、識別、表徵。因此本方法對整合素這一類與抗腫瘤藥物研發密切相關的膜蛋白的胞外配體的標記與識別，將會起到重要的推進作用。由於整合素與胞外配體的相互作用對其在細胞中的生物功能至關重要，因此本項目的研究內容對探索癌症分子機理、抗腫瘤藥物研發、腫瘤類型診斷、以及腫瘤成像方面，具有重要的科學和實際意義。

17301118.label: Realisation of objectives
17301118.value: This project has four objectives. We have been successful with the methodology development and had some difficulties with the method’s application to integrins, but eventually the problem was circumvented by switching to an antibody-mediated approach in protein labeling. Overall, as originally proposed, we have developed a DNA-based protein labeling method for profiling protein complexes; moreover, the method could be used for profiling protein complexes both in cell lysates and on the surface of live cells. In one of the major publications supported by the GRF grant, we applied this method and realized, for the first time, ultra-high throughput screening at multi-million compound scale against membrane protein on live cells. However, this method requires a known ligand to guide the initial DNA tagging of the target. We have found the reported small molecule ligands of integrin showed poor binding affinities and/or specificities to the targets, whereas antibodies could be used to guide the labeling but they suffer from target specificity, the large molecular weight, high cost, and variable antibody quality from different vendors. However, the developed method has seen good results with other types of proteins and protein complexes. For Objective 1, we have developed a DNA-mediated method that can specifically label the protein targets either in cell lysates and on live cells. By controlling the DNA-based probe hybridization, this method can be used to profile large protein complexes. Besides the direct protein binders, other proteins that indirectly interact the target in the same complex may be captured and identified, and a set of probes with different lengths present a multitude of probe configurations to profile hundreds of proteins in a family of protein complexes. The method has been used to profile the binding ligands of integrins and histone deacetylases. Furthermore, we have realized, for the first time, ultra-high throughput screening of DNA-encoded chemical libraries against membrane proteins on live cells. In addition, this method has also been used to screen non-DNA-conjugated natural product libraries on live cells. For Objective 2, we have encountered some technical difficulties when we applied the labeling method to integrins, specifically in using the RGDfK-based affinity probes for integrin labeling. RGDfK peptides, either in the cyclic or linear form, are known binders for integrins. However, DNA-conjugation appeared to be quite detrimental for RGDfK-integrin binding on the cell surface. We have attempted to use different types of probes, e.g., other peptides and non-RGDfK small molecules (more than 15 small molecules tested), and we have also tested more than 10 cell types. However, the results were roughly the same. In most cases, these probes appeared to have insufficient affinities to guide the labelling or the labelling was not target-specific with high background signal. To circumvent this problem, we moved onto antibody-based probes. We have successfully used antibody-DNA conjugates to capture the binding ligands of integrin αvβ3 on live A375 cells. However, antibodies are more expensive, have varied quality of different batches or from different vendors, and require considerable efforts and resources to the prepare, characterize, and validate the antibody-DNA conjugates. Nevertheless, using the antibody-mediated labeling method, we have identified ~74 putative novel binders of integrin αvβ3 and characterized the interactions of several representative interactors. For Objective 3, we have applied the method to lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 (LFA-1). Unexpectedly, we discovered that LFA-1 interacts with thrombopoietin receptor (TPOR), which also belongs to the receptor tyrosine kinase superfamily. Moreover, the LFA-1/TPOR interaction appeared to be important for the activation of TPOR, which is implicated in cell viability and growth, megakaryocyte maturation, and platelet production. Leveraging the LFA-1-mediated TPOR activation, we screened a 30-million compound library and identified a series of tripeptides as novel TPOR agonists. This research finding has significance in understanding the crosstalk between the integrin-RTK families of proteins and also provided novel chemotypes for developing TPOR agonists for the treatment of thrombocytopenia and malignant cancers. For Objective 4, we have summarized the research in this report. Among the research outputs, the major ones that directly arise from this grant are listed below: 1. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 17525-17532; 2. Nat. Chem. 2021, 13, 77-88; 3. Chem. Commun, 2021, 57, 3769-3772; 4. Acc. Chem. Res. 2021, 54, 3491-3503 (review); 5. Nat. Chem. 2022, 14, 129-140 (perspective article); 6. ACS Omega 2022, 7, 11491-11500; 7. ChemRxiv 2022, doi: 10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-hg2x8 (under revision). The other research outputs are also related to this project. The manuscript describing the research findings of LFA-1, TPOR, and the discovered agonists are under preparation. Since we have also applied the method to two additional membrane proteins: epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and insulin receptor (INSR), we would like to publish the results collectively to enhance the impact of the publication. In addition, we have submitted three patent applications for internal review before formal submission.

17301118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301118.value: a) We developed a novel protein labeling method capable of profiling protein complexes. We have identified 112 novel binders of histone deacetylases, which include indirect interactors intractable to traditional small molecule probes. The method has been applied to the integrins αvβ3 and LFA-1. For integrin αvβ3, a set of probes have collectively identified ~74 novel binders. For LFA-1, we have identified that TPOR binds to LFA-1 on cancer cells, and the interaction is synergistic with thrombopoietin (TPO) in activating the receptor and the downstream pathways. The results revealed the crosstalk between integrin-RTK proteins and a new way to modulate TPOR via integrin signaling. b) We screened a 30-million-compound chemical library and identified novel TPOR/LFA-1-agonists. The TPOR agonists are synergistic with TPO and bind to an allosteric site. Since TPOR is positively associated with primary tumors, these findings may provide opportunities to inhibit cancer cell growth by targeting TPOR. Intriguingly, the TPOR agonism is mediated through LFA-1, a pro-tumorigenic factor in cancer metastasis and angiogenesis. Collectively, these results provide new opportunities to inhibit cancer cell migration via LFA-1 signaling, and the agonists identified may be considered for anti-cancer drug development. The results in a) and b) lead to two major publications: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020 and Nat. Chem. 2021. The manuscript describing the LFA-1/TPOR agonists are under preparation, which will include the results of two additional proteins. A patent application has been submitted for internal review. We have also been invited to write review articles on the research topics (Nat. Chem. 2022; Acc. Chem. Res. 2021) c) We further developed the method to enable on-cell screening of chemical compounds, especially structurally complex one such as natural products. We have screened a library of ~200 natural products and identified novel ligands for two membrane protein targets (Chem. Commun, 2021). d) Cell-based protein labeling is inherently noisy, which makes accurate target identification quite difficult. On the one hand, we systematically optimized cell-based experiments to minimize non-specific labeling; on the other hand, we developed a machine-learning (ML)-based computational method to denoise cell-based datasets. These works have facilitated the applications of the methods in not only protein labeling and profiling, but also in the screening of chemical libraries. The results have been published on ACS Omega 2022, 7, 11491-11500 (experimental protocol) and a preprint article ChemRxiv 2022, doi: 10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-hg2x8, which describes the ML-based data denoising method and is under revision for formal publication.

17301118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301118.value: We will complete the LFA-1/TPOR study and publish a manuscript in early 2023 to collectively report the research findings. The inclusion of more targets and more data would better demonstrate the generality and performance of the method. We intend to perform medicinal chemistry optimizations of the agonists. The more downstream drug development would require collaboration/funding from external agencies and/or companies. We have recently submitted an ITF application to conduct drug development on the agonists. A technical barrier we have encountered is that the DNA-small molecule conjugates had poor ability in recognizing integrins. Although we circumvented the problem by using antibodies, small molecules are still more desirable; thus, we plan to further investigate this technical issue and find out whether it is integrin-specific or more general to a range of membrane proteins. Finally, we envision this method to be extended to other protein complexes and protein-protein interactions (PPIs) of biological and therapeutic significance. Future research efforts may be dedicated to the discovery of protein-complex- or even pathway-specific ligands, which remain largely underexplored in this field. For example, using the same principle, complex DNA architectures with multivalent display capabilities could be used to target protein complexes with distal binding pockets.

17301118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301118.value: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are important molecular interactions underlying many fundamental cellular processes, which also represent a major class of therapeutic targets for drug discovery. During the past decades, a multitude of methods have been developed to interrogate PPI targets, but most of them are not compatible with the native cellular environment, which is often required by the PPIs. In this project, a novel DNA-based affinity labelling method has been developed to characterize PPIs in cell lysates and on live cells. The developed strategy is generalizable and has added a unique tool to the existing toolbox for not only studying the molecular mechanisms underlying the biological functions of PPIs, but also facilitating the development of novel therapeutics and diagnostics for the treatment of human diseases.

17301518.label: Realisation of objectives
17301518.value: The main objective of the project is Objective 1, since that provides the basis for functional transcendence theory for general situations including the Ax-Schanuel conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties and for period domains. For Objective 1, with my collaborators Jonathan Pila and Jacob Tsimerman we completely resolved the arithmetic case in [Publ.1, 2019], proving the Ax-Schanuel theorem for all Shimura varieties, i.e., completely resolving the hyperbolic Ax-Schanuel conjecture for arithmetic lattices. This is a landmark paper published in the flagship journal Annals of Mathematics which is the culmination of the cross-fertilization between the perspective of my collaborators from o-minimal geometry in mathematical logic and Hodge theory, and the perspective from complex analysis, algebraic geometry and complex differential geometry as illustrated in my work [Compostio Math., 2019] in the solution of the Ax-Lindemann conjecture in the rank-1 case. Although a certain amount of complex differential geometry was already necessary in earlier works on hyperbolic Ax-type results in works of Ullmo-Yafaev, Pila-Tsimerman and Ullmo-Yafaev (notably volume estimates on subvarieties of bounded symmetric domains), my perspective is to make use of complex geometry in order to exploit meromorphic foliations on fibered spaces over finite-volume quotients of bounded symmetric domain, which provides a new source of techniques to overcome difficulties in solving the outstanding conjecture, after work already done by Pila-Tsimerman in the case of the j-function, i.e., the special case of products of modular curves. In the final solution, tame complex geometry of Peterzil-Starchenko was brought in as that gave a more efficient way of proving algebraicity of complex spaces constructed in the case of noncompact Shimura varieties. Tame complex geometry could be made use of because of the counting theorem of Pila-Wilkie applicable to arithmetic lattices. As to the situation of nonarithmetic lattices, which occurs with rank-1 irreducible factors which are either the unit disk or the complex unit ball of dimension > 1, with Shan-Tai Chan [J. Differential Geom., 2022] we proved a general uniformization theorem for algebraic subsets of bounded symmetric domains covering projective varieties, obtaining in particular the characterization of bi-algebraic varieties with compact quotients, opening up the path for the eventual resolution of the hyperbolic Ax-Schanuel conjecture in the more difficult cases of nonarithmetic lattices. The solution of the Ax-Schanuel theorem for Shimura varieties has taken a decade starting with earlier works, and it was not to be expected that a final solution could come in a short spell of time for the nonarithmetic cases, given that the most fundamental technique of the counting theorem of Pila-Wilkie is absent, especially in the cases where the lattice contains factors which are generic lattices in SL(2,R), which are not even defined over the field of algebraic numbers. The aforementioned result of Chan-Mok, which was an application of hard-core complex differential geometry (relying on the study of asymptotics of holomorphic curves exiting bounded symmetric domains) published in the top journal of differential geometry, is an important starting point for the eventual resolution of the hyperbolic Ax-Schanuel conjecture in the case of nonarithmetic lattices. For Objective 2, as soon as the proof of Mok-Pila-Tsimerman on the Ax-Schanuel theorem was available in the public domain, Gao has started to work on the generalization of the theorem to the situation of universal families of polarized families of abelian varieties over Shimura varieties. Shortly afterwards, Gao already produced an affirmative solution of the Ax-Schanuel conjecture for universal families of polarized abelian varieties by a combination of the methods of Mok-Pila-Tsimerman and his earlier work on the Ax-Lindemann conjecture for universal families of polarized abelian varieties. From my perspective our methodology has already proven to furnish the basis of the solution to the problem I have listed as Objective 2, although the work was done by Gao. At that juncture I looked at applications of Ax-Schanuel for universal families of polarized abelian varieties and related problems, and, given that the Betti map had played an important role in remarkable applications by Gao and his collaborators to number theory, I resorted to work on the Betti map. Consider a holomorphic section of an elliptic surface p: E --> B over a projective curve B, and a holomorphic section s: B --> E of infinite order. The work [Publ.3, 2023] of myself with Sui-Chung Ng yields an effective estimate on the size, counting multiplicities, of points where the Betti multiplicities of s exceeds 1. Our approach recovers a recent result of Ulmer-Ursua, and our effective proof has the advantage of being applicable to families of polarized abelian varieties, which will be followed up in my research work on a newly approved GRF grant of mine. My role in achieving Objective 2 was to provide the fundamental basis upon which the problem was finally resolved by Gao, and to work on related problems on the Betti map with effective estimates on Betti multiplicities. As regards Objective 3, shortly after Mok-Pila-Tsimerman [Publ.1, 2019], Benjamin Bakker (2019) collaborated with Jacob Tsimerman to generalize MPT to period domains. The scheme of proof followed that of MPT, with the new input in proving definability of the uniformization map restricted to the fundamental domain, and a volume estimate for horizontal subvarieties of period domains which replaces the analogous result of Hwang-To in the case of bounded symmetric domains. The breakthrough result of MPT was the fundamental basis of Bakker-Tsimerman. Given that the problem had already been solved, it was natural for me to tackle the not necessarily arithmetic case using analytic methods, starting with attempting to prove a generalization of Chan-Mok [Publ.2, 2022]. The work Mok-Wong [Publ.4, 2023] is meant to give a basis for the dilatation argument which is expected to eventually give a characterization of weakly special subvarieties with compact quotients among horizontal subvarieties in terms of bi-algebraicity. The articles [Publ.1, 2, 3] are deep results which have taken a long time to develop and finalize. Time was not enough to fully generalize the dilatation argument of Mok [Compostio Math. 2019] in the rank-1 case to handle the cases of horizontal algebraic subvarieties covering projective varieties. A simplified proof using dilation arguments (in place of stability and canonical metrics) of the uniformization theorem of Chan-Mok [Publ.2] for compact quotients of algebraic subvarieties of bounded symmetric domains is now being written up and it is expected that the new proof will work for period domains with some modifications. In other words, the remaining work is being pursued and expected to work out. The limitations in achieving Objectives 2 and 3 is primarily due to the fact that our landmark paper MPT had immediately been applied by other researchers to yield the results expected from Objective 2 and 3, which fully illustrated the impact and importance of MPT. Objective 1, which has been fully achieved, is the single most important objective, of significantly higher weight than the totality of the other two objectives. It is also a very positive outcome that functional transcendence theory has related itself in the case of families of polarized abelian varieties to the analytic study of the Betti map for which Ng-Mok [Publ.3] in the case of elliptic surfaces is the starting point. The methodology of [Publ.3] strongly suggests generalizations to families of polarized abelian varieties.

17301518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301518.value: The Ax-Schanuel theorem for Shimura varieties has been proven by Mok-Pila-Tsimerman [Publ.1]. This was achieved by combining the perspectives from Mok and Pila-Tsimerman. Here over finite-volume quotients X of bounded symmetric domains D, Mok formerly considered meromorphic foliations on holomorphic fiber bundles over X arising from quotients by lattice actions of restrictions to D of universal families U over Chow schemes K on dual Hermitian symmetric spaces M, and Pila-Tsimerman had developed a strategy using o-minimality, Hodge theory and complex geometry which already led to the affirmative solution of the conjecture on products of modular curves, and [Publ.1] resulted from a cross-fertilization of both perspectives. Without the counting theorem of Pila-Wilkie from o-minimality, generalizations to the case of not necessarily arithmetic lattices require a different approach. The study of functional transcendence theory in the general case was initiated by Chan-Mok [Publ.2] using methods of complex differential geometry and the study of holomorphic curves exiting bounded symmetric domains. For mixed Shimura varieties, earlier works of Gao, Chiu and Gao-Klingler have led to a proof of the Ax-Schanuel theorem for mixed Hodge structures, and in the case of mixed Shimura varieties of abelian type, it was revealed by Gao that Betti maps played a crucial role in applications of the Ax-Schanuel conjecture. I re-examined the theme of the Betti form which I introduced (without the name) in 1991 and which has recently become popular due notably to works of Zannier et-al., and, using differential geometry Mok-Ng [Publ.3] gave a new proof of an effective estimate of the locus where Betti multiplicities exceed 1 in the case of holomorphic sections of elliptic schemes over algebraic curves, with a method that generalizes to the case of abelian schemes. Fibers of first partial Cayley transforms are isometric embeddings of the ball. These algebraic subvarieties play an important role in the approach for Ax-Lindemann for non-arithmetic lattices, and by analogy we sought to construct non-trivial horizontal isometric embeddings of the ball into flag domains in preparation for functional transcendence theory for horizontal varieties on quotients of flag domains D. As generalizations to holomorphic isometric embeddings of the ball in the case of irreducible bounded symmetric domains of rank > 1, Mok-Wong [Publ.4] constructed such examples for flag domains in rational homogeneous spaces G/P of Picard number 1, reaching in the long-root case the same dimension p+1 where p is the dimension of the VMRT at any point of G/P.

17301518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301518.value: Prompted by the success of the current project, I have written up and obtained a GRF grant starting January 2021 entitled "Reconstructing distinguished subvarieties on bounded symmetric domains from families of totally geodesic holomorphic curves". It is a project inspired by the theory of varieties of minimal rational tangents which I have been pursuing through a number of approved GRF projects and by the rescaling argument which I had carried out in various places before and during the current project. Illustrated by the effective estimates obtained in the current project on the locus of higher Betti multiplicities of a holomorphic section of infinite order on an elliptic scheme, the study of holomorphic sections of abelian schemes from the differential-geometric perspective is another potentially fruitful direction of research which will lead to interaction between complex differential geometry, algebraic geometry and number theory.

17301518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301518.value: Our project sprang from exchanges between myself and specialists in mathematical logic, number theory and arithmetic geometry, culminating in the resolution of Mok-Pila-Tsimerman of an important conjecture in arithmetic geometry, viz., the Ax-Schanuel conjecture on Shimura varieties, with plenty of applications to central problems in number theory, including significant works on the Shafarevich conjecture and the uniform Mordell-Lang theorem for counting rational points on higher-genus algebraic curves C in their Jacobian varieties. (The Mordell theorem for a single C was the principal work leading to Falting's Fields Medal 1983.) The work of Mok-Pila-Tsimerman has been recognized as a milestone for successful collaboration between complex geometry and number theory, and it was an important component of 3 academic awards I was bestowed in 2022, including the Chern Prize at ICCM, the Future Science Prize (also known as China's Nobel Prize) in Mathematics and Computer Science and the Tan Kah Kee Science Prize in Mathematics and Physics of CAS. Results of the project provided in-roads for tackling the Ax-Schanuel conjecture for non-arithmetic lattices, and for bringing forth the importance of the Betti form for the study of abelian schemes and for their applications to the study of rational points on algebraic varieties.

17301618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17301618.value: 年輕脈衝星風雲的射電研究

17301618.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17301618.value: Dr Dodson, Richard Prof Roberts, Mallory S. E.

17301618.label: Project Objectives
17301618.value: To map the radio structure of young PWNe at high resolution. The new observations will provide radio images of PWNe at a level of detail not available before. We will perform a systematic comparison to determine their general characteristics. The comprehensive sample will set the stage for further theoretical studies to understand how these features are generated in relativistic shocks. To test the shock acceleration theories using the injected particle spectra. We will use the multi-wavelength observations to constrain the broadband spectra of PWNe, in order to infer the particle energy spectrum for detailed comparison with theoretical models. To characterize the PWN magnetic field configuration. We will obtain high resolution polarization maps to reveal the intrinsic nebular B-field in details. This will give unique information to distinguish different origins of the small scale features and confirm if radial diffusion is the primary mode of particle transport in PWNe. In addition, our high resolution maps will provide useful inputs for X-ray polarization measurements in near future.

17301618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301618.value: 當大質量的恆星死亡時，會產生超新星爆炸及脈衝星。脈衝星有很強的磁場，可將電子加速，產生脈衝星風及脈衝星風星雲。 脈衝星風雲可以產生PeV的高能粒子，但其加速機制仍然是一個謎。由於距離較近，脈衝星風雲是研究相對論衝擊波的重要對象，高解像觀測可解開脈衝星風雲的詳細結構，從而了解粒子加速機制。之前的研究主要集中在X射綫波段，射電觀測可以追溯到星雲的長期演化。結合兩者，可以對星雲的同步輻射作全面研究。我們之前的項目對年老的脈衝星風雲進行了一系列的射電研究，但類似的工作在年輕的星雲則不多。之前的樣本顯示了豐富小型結構，包括磁圈和細絲狀結構等，但目前尚不清楚它們是如何產生的。 我們將以此為基礎展開全面研究，以擴大樣本，並進行系統性比較。我們的團隊由專家組成，並已經穫得了新的觀測數據。此項目將揭示年輕脈衝星風雲的詳細結構，及磁場分佈。結果將有助理解這些結構的性質和形成過程。我們將結合多波段觀測去測量粒子的能量分佈。這提供了一種新方法去直接測試粒子加速度的理論。最後，我們獲得的偏震分佈圖對於NASA新的X射綫望遠鏡的規劃與調試將會很有用。

17301618.label: Realisation of objectives
17301618.value: In this project, we have made new observations of three pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) using the VLA and the ATCA radio telescopes. We analyzed new and archival data of G343.1-2.3, G21.9-0.9, and the Dragonfly to produce high resolution radio images. We discovered diverse morphology and magnetic field geometry in these sources, and developed new models that can successfully explain our new findings.

We found a diverse magnetic field structure, including a radial field in G21.5-0.9, a toroidal field for G343.1-2.3, and a complex field in the Dragonfly. As a toroidal field is generally expected for young sources, our finding for G21.5-0.9 is difficult to explain with current theory. 17301618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301618.value: 1. For G21.5-0.9, we found a radial B-field structure with significant internal Faraday rotation within the PWN. The latter could imply mixing of the supernova material and pulsar wind. The results are published in Lai et al. (2022). 2. For the Dragonfly, we discovered that the radio PWN consists of an elongated main body and a thin arc like structure ahead of the pulsar. The magnetic field has complex geometry and we showed that it can be a toroidal field distorted by the pulsar motion. The results are published in Jin et al. (2022). 3. For the PWN powered by PSR B1706-44 inside G343.1-2.3, we found a double lobed structure and has successfully developed a thick torus model with Doppler boosting to explain the feature. The results are published in Liu et al. (2022).

17301618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301618.value: 1. The thick torus model we developed can be applied to other radio PWNe. 2. The diverse magnetic field configuration we found will need further simulation works to explain. 3. Deeper radio observations are needed to confirm some putative small scale structure and the single power-law multi-wavelength spectrum.

17301618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301618.value: Pulsar wind nebulae are important particle accelerators in our Galaxy. In this project, we reveal the radio emission structure and magnetic field configuration of these sources in details, using high resolution observations. The results set the stage for further theoretical modeling works.

17301718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301718.value: Today, the surface of Mars is a frozen, rusted desert. Some of the landscapes are familiar – the surface contains dormant volcanoes, ancient sedimentary layers, and dried river channels. But, for the most part, these landforms are fossils landscapes from an era long gone. Though the planet appears frozen and life-less now, abundant evidence indicates that the surface environment was much warmer and wetter in the past – at least for some period of time. In fact, some scientists have argued that the planet’s climate was earthlike billions of years ago, though the timing of when that happened and the questions of how long it lasted remain open. Evidence for a warmer ancient climate comes in many forms. On Earth, it is common knowledge that rainfall erodes the landscape, creating networks of river channels that form over geologic time. Also, the rainfall results in surface and near-surface water that interacts with rocks through chemical weathering reactions to form soils and aqueous alteration minerals. In surveying the Martian crust, it is clear that these types of geologic activity did occur. However, only the most ancient parts of the Martian crust (over ~3.6 billion years ago) contain evidence for rainfall or snow-melt/ice-melt that resulted in the erosion of channels and the chemical weathering of surface rocks. The goal of this project is to investigate the geomorphological (landscape) and mineralogical (chemical) evidence for a warmer and wetter ancient climate on Mars (the climate from ~3.6-4.1 billion years ago). Previous work by other researchers have produced global-scale surveys of the mineralogy and morphology of water-related features on Mars. This work will focus on one aspect of those results for further, detailed analysis. My team will investigate sites on Mars where Al-rich clays are found because aluminium is an element that is a strong indicator of aqueous chemical weathering processes. My team will characterize the detailed mineralogy and geologic context of ~200 sites where evidence for Al-rich clay minerals has been documented. Those early results lack the mineralogical detail to understand the environmental conditions. And, because those results were intended as a global survey, the early results lack necessary details to constrain the timing and geological context of many of the deposits. In this work, my team will use remote sensing analysis and laboratory analyses to better constrain the type, timing and duration of surface alteration on ancient Mars. 今天，火星表面是一片冰凍，生鏽的沙漠。一些景觀很熟悉 - 表麵包含休眠火山，古代沉積層和乾河 通道。但是，在大多數情況下，這些地貌是一個時代的化石景觀 不見了。雖然這個星球現在顯得冰凍而且沒有生命，但是充足的證據表明 過去表面環境溫暖多雨 - 至少對於 一段時間。事實上，一些科學家認為這個星球的氣候是 數十億年前的地球般的，雖然發生的時間和時間 關於它持續多久的問題仍未解決。古老氣候變暖的證據 有多種形式。在地球上，眾所周知，降雨侵蝕了地球 景觀，創建在地質時期形成的河道網絡。而且， 降雨導致表面和近地表水與岩石相互作用 化學風化反應形成土壤和含水蝕變礦物。在 在調查火星地殼時，很明顯這些類型的地質活動確實發生過。 然而，只有火星地殼最古老的部分（超過35億年前） 包含導致土壤侵蝕的降雨或融雪/冰融的證據 通道和表面岩石的化學風化。這個項目的目標是 調查a的地貌（景觀）和礦物學（化學）證據 火星上的溫暖和潮濕的古老氣候（氣候從大約35-4億年前）。 其他研究人員以前的工作已經對火星上與水有關的特徵的礦物學和形態進行了全球尺度的調查。這項工作將側重於這些結果的一個方面，以進行進一步的詳細分析。我的團隊將調查火星上發現富含鋁的粘土的地點，因為鋁是一種元素，是水化學風化過程的有力指標。我的團隊將描述約200個地點的詳細礦物學和地質背景，其中記錄了富含Al的粘土礦物的證據。這些早期結果缺乏了解環境條件的礦物學細節。而且，由於這些結果旨在作為一項全球調查，早期結果缺乏必要的細節來限制許多礦床的時間和地質背景。在這項工作中，我的團隊將使用遙感分析和實驗室分析來更好地約束古代火星表面蝕變的類型，時間和持續時間。

17301718.label: Realisation of objectives
17301718.value: The goal of this project was to investigate evidence for ancient climate change on Mars through the study of compositional stratigraphy related to Al-rich clay minerals detected on the martian surface spectroscopically. The ancient climate of Mars is important for an number reasons, not the least of which is because the warmer and wetter ancient surface would likely have been habitable to microbial life. Furthermore, ancient mechanisms by which planetary climates change dramatically are not well understood, but these processes are relevant to our own past and future on this planet. Our goal in this project was to investigate the geologic context clay deposits on Mars using remote sensing data, to study the mineralogy of the deposits, carry out several major tasks related to the identification and cataloguing of such clay deposits, constraining the mineralogy of the deposits using infrared spectroscopy, characterizing the geologic context of the deposits, delineating the thicknesses and morphologies of the deposits, and constraining the timing of the deposits using relative age constraints and crater counting. Our last goal was to summarize the results and produce high quality publications in international journals. We are pleased to report that we have successfully carried out of these tasks on time. The results of the study have been published in multiple papers, but the summary of the results occurs in a comprehensive paper submitted to Nature Communications. The main results of that capstone paper are as follows: Chemical weathering profiles on Mars consisting of an upper Al clay-rich, Fe-poor layer and lower Fe/Mg-clay-rich layer provide an important record of the planet’s climate history. Here we explore the geological characteristics, stratigraphy and relative age of >200 weathering profiles across the southern highlands to evaluate connections to past climate. Almost all (>99%) examples show show a similar, single stratigraphic relationship of Al over Fe/Mg clays rather than multiple interbedded mineralogical transitions suggesting either one single climate transition or chemical resetting of weathering horizons during multiple events meaning they only record the latest event. While the absolute amount of time required for form a typical martian weathering profile may have been only ~106-107 years, the profile occurred in deposits over >7 x 108 years from the Early Noachian into the Hesperian. This global view of martian weathering profiles shows the compositional stratigraphy occurred over a range of geologic units, at wide range of elevations, over a large range of geologic time, though chemical weathering may have peaked c.a. 3.7-3.8 billion years ago. The conditions required for martian weathering profiles to have formed are seemingly driven by chemical mobility of Fe. We therefore conclude that reducing atmospheric conditions facilitating Fe-mobility prevailed throughout the Noachian and into the Hesperian on Mars. The funding for this work was used to train a PhD student, Binlong Ye, who will graduate this coming spring or summer. He has produced a significant amount of Mars climate research from this project, some of which is contained in his Geophysical Researcher Letters publication and some contained in the submitted Nature Communications paper. Further results are forthcoming in another paper about carbonate rocks on Mars. A pleasantly surprising element of this work is that, in addition to being able to carry out all of the anticipated research objectives without much complication, we discovered some spinoff projects along that way that were not anticipated. For example, some of the work related to past ground ice and volcanic processes turnout out to reveal further hidden volcanic features, which turned into another GRF (funded this past year). Also, we were able compare some of the Mars remote sensing work to features observed in the Qaidam basin of western China. Further, the study of climate-related features on Mars led to a review paper on martian dry lake beds by the PI in review at Nature Geoscience, and this topic has been further developed into a CRF proposal that is now in final stages of consideration at RGC.

17301718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301718.value: In addition to the spinoff activities described aove in section 5.3, there is another major outcome of this work which is that I have submitted a follow-on GRF proposal this recent cycle. While this GRF project focused on Al-rich clays as they are related to climate, the future one, if it is funded, will focus on sulfates on Mars. These types of sulfur-rich minerals also form as a function of climate, but it seems that many of them are geologically younger than the clays, and it seems they might have formed in colder, drier conditions. Therefore this work led directly not only to highly productive scientific papers, but also to new insights and updated questions that can be addressed through future studies of comparable scope and style.

17301718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301718.value: Soils on Earth typically contain clay minerals, a type of mineral that forms through interaction between rocks, water, atmosphere and sometimes microbial life. Geologists study the chemistry, crystal form, abundance, occurrence and character of clays on Earth in part as a way to trace past climate on this planet. The same is true for Mars where we can study the occurrence of clays formed in the distant past using satellite data. Our study carried out a global analysis of 100s of sites of ancient clays on Mars, producing the most comprehensive view of links between clays and climate. The key results are that we were able to show examples of the oldest and youngest clay deposits on Mars, illustrating how warm, wet climate conditions occurred over >700 million years, through a wide range of elevations, within a huge range of geologic units around the globe. This indicates that the planet Mars, which is frozen and dry today, experienced long lived, warm, wet conditions over 3 billion years ago driven by greenhouse conditions associated with reduced volcanic gasses (such as methane and hydrogen).

17301818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301818.value: 由於北極氣候變暖的速度是地球的兩倍，自上個世紀格，格陵蘭地區的冰蓋一直融化，是海平面上升的30％左右。格陵蘭冰蓋融化導致融水輸送的潛在影響尚未清楚。我們並不了解淡水輸送的強度，時間和位置對海洋對流帶來的影響。學界普遍認為淡水輸入會急劇減少甚至完全關閉北歐海域的對流，但最近的研究與此觀點相矛盾。研究顯示，一個相對較厚，寒冷，清新的夏季表面混合層來源於冰蓋融化，其特徵是過去的間冰期，稱為海洋同位素11期（約40萬年前）。因此，這種具有活躍海洋對流的間冰期是以海洋上層為條件，其被認為是阻止對流混合和深水形成。因此，從格陵蘭冰蓋的融化揭開淡水輸入的影響對於更有效地預測近期氣候至關重要。再者，北大西洋上層海洋分層的變化有可能對對流過程和北大西洋環流產生重大影響，更對氣候造成嚴重干擾，包括降雨和乾旱的頻率，北極海冰，甚至颶風在大西洋形成。 本研究記錄全新世和海洋同位素11期的亞極地和北大西洋極地中的高熔融水通量對上層海洋分層演變的影響。我們將分析南北橫斷面沉積物岩芯的樣本，以重建氣候期間地表分層的潛在緯度變化。我們測量有孔蟲殼體中有機物的氮同位素，這化石可反映該地方的硝酸鹽消耗和上層水分層。本研究將探討有關淡水輸入何時影響該地區的上層海洋分層，以及對海洋環流的影響。這將提高我們預測當前氣候的趨勢及格陵蘭冰蓋融化的影響的能力。

17301818.label: Realisation of objectives
17301818.value: We reconstructed the spatiotemporal evolution of nitrate utilization during MIS 11 as expected. Due to COVID restriction we didn’t manage to go in Germany to sample the core we were supposed to do for MIS 1, but we replaced this with some samples covering the common area from a collaborator in Canada. Therefore, the time period studied is not like exactly we initially planned, but we manage to cover the most critical period despite the issue we faced. Moreover, we wanted to reconstruct nitrate utilization to infer the upper-ocean stratification, so we decided to use another proxy that can be used to reconstruct upper-ocean stratification instead of nitrate utilization. So we produced new stable isotope data from two planktic foraminifera living at different depth to replace the missing nutrient utilization data, this was published alongside our main results. For the first time, we showed high-resolution variation in the nutrient utilization over these crucial climatic periods (obj. 1). We also manage to show enough supporting evidence to validate, that these variation in the isotopic signal were not due to other factor like iron concentration or phosphorous input (obj. 2). In our publications and PhD thesis, we compared our data to existing data on paleotemperature, salinity and deep-water renewal to display the important link between upper ocean stratification and regional oceanography and deep-water renewal (obj. 3). Finally, we have included in our publication a new model integrating the impact of freshwater release on open-ocean convection and global climate using our newly produced data and existing data from the literature (obj. 4). Therefore, we fully achieved our objectives (all included in publications).

17301818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301818.value: The major finding of this study is the fact that freshwater input from ice-sheet melt did not necessary inhibited the formation of deep water in the Nordic Sea 400,000 years ago. Indeed, we explained that despite the release of freshwater the change in gradient of salinity between the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic was such that it was still promoting deep-water formation (Doherty et al., 2021, QSR). Moreover, we highlighted that the timing of the onset of deep-water formation in the Nordic Seas may be the trigger to extend the duration of the MIS 11 interglacial into what is often called the ‘super interglacial’, which is a long-lasted debate (Doherty et al., 2021, QSR). We also provided evidence that nutrient supply in this region is highly dependent on climate-driven change in oceanic currents, which may even have consequences on the fisheries industry (Doherty et al., 2021, PP).

17301818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301818.value: The next step will be to integrate these results into broader, more complex coupled-climate models. While our results with our box-model are reliable, it is important to place these results into a larger perspective to fully understand the interplay between climate and ocean regarding these very important climatic events that may have a strong impact on near-future weather conditions on Earth. We are connecting with internationally renowned ocean modelers in order to test our hypothesis with their model. The challenge is that there are not many data to define robust ‘boundary conditions’ for MIS 11.

17301818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301818.value: Ocean circulation is weakening, and this may lead to dramatic consequences in some regions (change in climate and weather, droughts and floods, stronger typhoons, etc). One potential cause for this weakening is the release of freshwater due to melt of the Greenland icesheet. Here, we demonstrated that 400,000 years ago, similar freshwater release did not shutdown oceanic circulation but rather displaced the locus of deep-water formation and strengthened it. While the climatic consequences of such changes are not as dramatic as a shutdown, it enhanced the heat transport and thus may have prevented an ice-age. While the modern conditions are different, these results may call for caution when inferring the impact of freshwater release on climate.
