17301918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301918.value: The therapeutic potential of small interfering RNA (siRNA), which inhibits specific gene expression through RNA interference (RNAi), has been demonstrated in animal and clinical studies, including the treatment of lung diseases such as cancer, infections and inflammatory diseases. The lack of a safe and efficient delivery system is one of the major barriers to the translation of this novel RNAi therapeutics, which could fulfill the unmet need for effective therapy in many lung diseases. There are limited studies that investigate inhaled siRNA formulation for clinical application. We aim to address this issue by developing inhaled dry powder formulations of siRNA that exhibit excellent dispersibility and aerodynamic properties with good safety profile. We are the first to report the production of inhaled ‘naked siRNA’ dry powder by spray drying. Under optimised operation parameters, the integrity of siRNA was successfully preserved. To further enhance the lung deposition efficiency for clinical use, one of the strategies is to incorporate an effective dispersion enhancer. Our preliminary study suggested that when small nucleic acids were co-spray dried with albumin, the surface of the particles was modified and became corrugated, leading to a significant improvement in aerosol performance. It is hypothesized that during the drying process, the macromolecular albumin competed with siRNA to stay on particle surface, forming an elastic shell which restricts the escape of solvent. Once the solvent becomes exhausted, the shell collapses to form particles with wrinkled surface and reduced cohesiveness, and the resultant powder exhibit high dispersibility, improving delivery efficiency. In this project, the effect of human serum albumin in siRNA dry powder formulation will be systematically investigated. A full factorial design approach will be employed to carefully examine the effect of albumin content, siRNA dose and solute concentration on the aerosol performance of the spray dried powder. The aerodynamic properties will be assessed using cascade impactor. The integrity and recovery of siRNA will be evaluated by gel electrophoresis and high-performance liquid chromatography. The morphology and structural characteristics of the powder will be thoroughly examined by physical methods (electron microscope, atomic force microscope, powder X-ray diffraction etc.). Finally, the biological activity and toxicity of the siRNA powder will be evaluated in animal model of acute lung injury following pulmonary delivery. The outcome of this project will provide a new platform for future development of inhaled RNA therapeutics. Moreover, the potential of co-spray drying RNA with a protein therapeutics can be explored. 在RNA干擾(RNA interference)中，小分子干擾核糖核酸(siRNA)能夠抑制特定基因的轉譯。科學家們嘗試利用這一機制，研究使用siRNA作為藥物的可能。動物和臨床實驗的結果顯示，siRNA具有治療不同疾病的潛力，包括各種呼吸系統的疾病，如肺癌、傳染病、哮喘和慢阻肺病等。現時，很多呼吸系統的疾病都欠缺有效的治療方法。儘管siRNA為治療這些疾病帶來曙光，但要將siRNA發展成藥物，我們仍然缺乏一種有效而且安全的給藥系統(delivery system)。此外，研究將siRNA製成吸藥劑型的報告亦十分有限。 有見及此，是次研究的目的是製作出siRNA的乾粉吸劑。這款吸劑需要安全，同時具備優異的分散能力(dispersibility)以及空氣動力學的性質。我們曾首次報告利用噴霧乾燥法將未有與給藥系統結合的無遮蓋siRNA (naked siRNA)製成乾粉吸劑。在合適的運作環境下，乾粉中的siRNA在噴霧乾燥後仍保持完整。為了提升乾粉在肺部沉積的效率，我們在乾粉中加入分散增強劑(dispersion enhancer)。初步實驗顯示，在噴霧乾燥細小核糖核酸時加入白蛋白(albumin)能使乾粉粒子的表面起皺褶，並顯著改善乾粉的氣霧性能。我們假定，巨大分子如白蛋白在水滴乾燥時會和siRNA互相爭奪在水滴的表面上滯留，並在過程中形成具彈性的外殼，從而限制溶劑揮發。當大部分溶劑揮發後，這層外殼會向內塌陷，使粒子的表面形成皺褶。褶痕能降低乾粉粒子間的黏着力，增加乾粉的分散能力並改善乾粉的給藥效能。在是次研究中，我們會系統地分析人類血清白蛋白(human serum albumin)對siRNA乾粉吸劑的影響。我們將利用因子設計(factorial design)實驗來探討白蛋白的份量、siRNA的份量以及溶質的濃度對乾粉的氣霧性能的影響。我們會使用階式撞擊取樣器(cascade impactor)來測定粉劑的空氣動力學性質。我們會透過凝膠電泳和高效液相色譜法去檢查siRNA在噴霧乾燥後的結構完備性和回收效率，並以各種物理分析技術如電子顯微鏡、原子力顯微鏡(atomic force microscopy)及乾粉X光繞射(powder X-ray diffraction)等研究粉劑的形態和結構特徵。此外，我們亦會利用急性肺部損傷(acute lung injury)的動物模型來測定經肺部給藥的siRNA亁粉的生物活性及毒性。我們期望此研究項目能為日後使用肺部給藥的基因藥物提供藥劑劑型上的設計方向，同時探索將基因藥物以及蛋白質藥物共同噴霧乾燥的可能。

17301918.label: Realisation of objectives
17301918.value: Three factors were chosen for investigations in the factorial design study. The first one was siRNA concentration. As the active drug in the formulation, it would be of primary interest to study the effect of siRNA composition on the particle properties. The low level of the siRNA concentration was set at 2% w/w. To the best of our knowledge, 2% w/w was the highest siRNA concentration reported for inhalable siRNA dry powder prepared by spray drying at the time of experiment. Here, the high level of siRNA concentration was ambitiously set at 8% w/w, the highest siRNA loading yet to report. The second factor studied was the concentration of human serum albumin (HSA). Based on our unpublished preliminary data, powders comprising 20% w/w HSA and 80% w/w mannitol exhibited satisfactory aerosol performance. Thus, the centre point of HSA concentration was set to 20%. It was extended to 5% and 35% as the low and high level, respectively, for a wide range of coverage. The last factor included in the model was the total solute concentration. The solute concentration of the feed solution has high influence on particle size distribution. Essentially, it determines the amount of solid mass in each droplet during spray drying. HSA demonstrated the ability to modify the surface properties of the spray dried powder. HSA containing particles exhibited corrugated surfaces, and the extent of corrugation increased with HSA composition. Analysis of surface composition also reflected that HSA was enriched on the particle surface. In general, the fine particle fraction (FPF) of the formulations ranged from 53% to>70%. These aerosol performances were considered to be excellent as the FPF values of commercial dry powder inhaler products typically ranged from 20% to 40%. Since siRNA is a relatively expensive molecule compared to most small drug molecules, it would be desirable to achieve FPF as high as possible. Although varying the level of HSA in the formulation did not significantly affect the FPF according to the factorial analysis, it had a linear relationship with EF, showing that increasing HSA could improve powder dispersion, albeit only modestly. Interestingly, the physical size of the powder formulations at the centre point was considerably smaller than the other formulations, and the factorial analysis showed that the effect of curvature for median diameter was significant. It would require further investigation to dissect why this specific combination of factors would result in smaller particles. Furthermore, it has been reported that a moderate degree of surface corrugation was sufficient to considerably enhance powder dispersion, and excessive surface corrugation would not further improve aerosol performance. The combination of small particle size with corrugated surfaces contributed to the higher FPF of the centre point formulations. While only formulation parameters were varied and the spray drying conditions were kept unchanged in the current investigation, the presence of curvature in the model highlighted the complexity and challenges in optimizing the formulation parameters.

17301918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301918.value: The development of small interfering RNA (siRNA) formulation for pulmonary delivery is a key to the clinical translation of siRNA therapeutics for the treatment of respiratory diseases. Most inhalable siRNA powder formulations published to date were limited by the siRNA content which was often too low to be clinically relevant. This study aimed to prepare inhalable siRNA powder formulations that contained high siRNA loading of over 6% w/w by spray drying, with human serum albumin (HSA) investigated as a dispersion enhancer to improve the aerosol performance. The effect of siRNA, HSA and solute concentrations in the formulations were evaluated systemically using factorial analyses. All the spray dried siRNA powders exhibited excellent aerosol performance with fine particle fraction (FPF) consistently over 50% in all the formulations. An enrichment of HSA on the particle surface was observed. Surface corrugation was more prominent as HSA composition increased. Importantly, the bioactivity of siRNA was successfully preserved upon spray drying as demonstrated in the in vitro transfection study, and up to 78% of intact siRNA retained in the spray dried powder. Overall, HSA is an effective dispersion enhancer and spray drying is an appropriate technique to produce inhalable dry powder with high siRNA loading for further investigation.

17301918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301918.value: The objective of future study is to develop this delivery system as a platform technology so that it can be applied to a wide range of RNA therapeutics, including messenger RNA (mRNA), for different therapeutic indications such as respiratory infections, vaccines, lung inflammatory diseases, acute lung injury/ pulmonary fibrosis and lung cancer. In addition, the formulations will be evaluated with different inhaler systems and different inspiratory flow rate in order to assess their suitability for use in patients with different pulmonary function/ disease conditions. Pharmacokinetic studies will also be performed to gain a better understanding on the performance of the inhaled dry powder formulations as compared to other routes of administration.

17301918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301918.value: The current study successfully demonstrated the preparation of inhalable dry powder containing high siRNA content using spray drying technique with human serum albumin (HSA) as dispersion enhancer. The highest siRNA loading achieved was 6.24% w/w, which was also the highest loading reported so far for inhaled siRNA dry powder formulations. Both the physical integrity and the bioactivity of the siRNA were preserved after spray drying, even in the absence of any protecting agents. It is anticipated that the demonstrated physical robustness of siRNA could encourage further formulation development. Further study will be carried out to explore the use of HSA as dispersion enhancer to other inhaled powder formulation of nucleic acids including messenger RNA (mRNA) and macromolecules (proteins and antibodies).

17302218.label: Project Objectives
17302218.value: Study the spectroscopic properties of selected diarylnitrenium ions by femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA) and time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) spectroscopies in a variety of solvents. Compare the differences between the diarylnitrenium ions with the more well-studied arylnitrenium ions, especially for their high reactivity toward nucleophiles. These results will be utilized for benchmarks to better understand the reaction mechanisms of the diarylnitrenium ions that will be studied further. Investigate the reactions of selected diarylnitrenium ions with Guanosine, Adenosine, 5-Methyluridine and Cytidine in aqueous solutions using nanosecond transient absorption (ns-TA) spectroscopy. This part of our project will focus on the reaction rates. Additional experiments like ground state UV-vis absorption, resonance Raman spectroscopy, NMR and mass spectroscopy will be used to analyze the photo-induced products resulting from the reactions of the nitrenium ions and the DNA bases studied. Ns-TR3 will be employed to obtain vibrational spectra information for the short-lived intermediates involved in the reactions between the diarylnitrenium ions and the DNA bases. The Raman spectra will enable more detailed information to be determined for the involved transient species, especially for the reactions towards guanosine. One may expect that there will be some different reactivity and properties between the diarylnitrenium ions and their arylnitrenium ions may result in some different alkylated transient species and final products and this will be explored as part of this objective. DFT and time-dependent DFT calculations will be employed to predict the reaction pathways for the diarylnitrenium ions reacting with selected DNA bases. These results will help better elucidate the photoreaction mechanism of DNA damage process(es) induced by diarylnitrenium ions. Time-resolved spectroscopy (ns-TA and ns-TR3) and product analysis experiments will be employed to investigate the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. DFT calculations will also be employed to predict the intermediates involved in the reactions of interest. These results will bring us new insights into the mechanisms for the nitrenium induced reactions with nucleobases and amino acids and insight into possible protein damage by nitrenium ions. Similar time-resolved spectroscopy, product analysis experiments and DFT calculations will also be used to study selected diarylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. These results will be used to compare with results found in objective 5 above and help to better understand the reaction mechanisms between the different these different kinds of nitrenium ions with amino acids. If time and resources permit, we will synthesize some new precursors for selected diarylnitrenium ions and employ similar time-resolved spectroscopy methods mentioned above to study the photochemistry and electrophilic reactions of these diarylnitrenium ions. These experiments will provide deeper insights into the geometries, properties and chemical reactivity for these intermediates and reactions.

17302218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302218.value: Nitrenium ions have been proposed as intermediates in reactions that damage DNA which may lead to conversion of a normal cell into a cancer cell. It has been known for many years that nitrenium ions formed from metabolism of aromatic amines and amides, have mutagenic properties and implications as “ultimate carcinogens” which cause DNA damage. Thus, nitrenium ions have interest from both chemical and biochemical aspects. Previous studies have indicated that arylnitrenium ions, such as the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion and 4-biphenylnitrenium ion are able to selectively react with guanine derivatives in DNA to form C8-intermediates. However, only a few studies have been conducted for reactions between diarylnitrenium ions and DNA bases. Thus, we propose to study the alkylation reactions between selected diarylnitrenium ions and DNA bases so as to characterize the intermediates formed and deduce their alkylation reaction mechanisms. The results of the proposed research will be compared with previous results observed for arylnitrenium ions to gain further insight and a deeper knowledge on how the different structures and properties of diarylnitrenium ions relative to arylnitrenium ions influences their electrophilic reaction towards DNA bases. Since there has been limited study so far between nitrenium ions and amino acids, we will also study the reactions between both the arylnitrenium ions and diarylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. These proposed studies will help us to better understand the mechanisms for the nitrenium ions reactions with amino acids and consider how they may induce protein damage. We propose to employ femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy to directly observe the generation of the nitrenium ions in different conditions and characterize the absorption properties of the transient nitrenium ions and then utilize nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption to study the reactions of the nitrenium ions of interest towards different nucleophiles, such as DNA bases and amino acids. This work will provide the reaction rates of the nitrenium ions under different solution conditions and give key information for future work. We plan to use picosecond and nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations to gain important fingerprint information of the intermediates produced from the reactions of nitrenium ions with the DNA nucleobases and amino acids of interest in this project. These new data will help to insight and a better understanding for how nitrenium ions cause DNA damage or protein damage in aqueous solution environments. 氮賓離子已經被提出是導致正常細胞轉化為癌細胞的DNA突變反應的中間體。多年來已知由芳香胺和醯胺代謝形成的氮賓離子具有誘變性質并且被定義為會引起DNA損傷的“終極致癌物”。因此，氮賓離子不僅僅吸引了化學家的興趣，也引起了生物化學家的極大關注。先前的研究表明，例如在2-芴基氮賓離子和4-聯二苯氮賓離子中，芳基氮賓離子能够選擇性地與DNA中的鳥嘌呤衍生物反應形成碳8（C8）中間體。然而，幾乎沒有研究報道二芳基氮賓離子和DNA碱基之間的反應。因此，我們計劃有選擇性地研究二芳基氮賓離子與DNA碱基之間的烷基化反應，以表徵形成的反應中間體并推斷它們的反應機理，這將給研究致癌機理提供更堅實的證據。以上計劃的研究結果將與之前單芳基氮賓離子的研究結果進行比較，從而讓我們可以更深入地瞭解二芳基氮賓離子相對于單芳基氮賓離子的不同電子結構和性質如何影響它們與DNA碱基的親電反應。此外，由于目前對氮賓離子和氨基酸的反應研究也很有限，所以我們還將研究芳基氮賓離子和二芳基氮賓離子與部分氨基酸之間的反應。這些擬執行的研究將有助于我們更好地理解氮賓離子與氨基酸反應的機理，并探究這一反應是如何導致蛋白質損傷的。我們建議采用飛秒時間分辨瞬態吸收光譜技術直接觀察不同條件下的氮賓離子的産生，并表徵瞬態氮賓離子的吸收特性，然後利用納秒時間分辨瞬態吸收光譜來研究感興趣的氮賓離子與不同親核試劑的反應，例如DNA碱基和氨基酸等。這項工作將提供不同溶液條件下的氮賓離子的反應速率，并為今後的工作提供關鍵信息。更多地，我們還計劃使用皮秒和納秒時間分辨共振拉曼光譜實驗與密度泛函理論計算相結合的方式，更精細地確證出由該項目中氮賓離子與DNA核碱基和氨基酸反應産生的中間體。這些新數據將大大加深我們對在水溶液環境中氮賓離子如何導致DNA突變與蛋白質損傷的理解。

17302218.label: Realisation of objectives
17302218.value: For Objectives 1, 2 and 3 we have performed femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA), nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption (ns-TA), time-resolved resonance Raman (nsTR3) and other methods to characterize the spectroscopic properties of selected diarylnitrenium ions in various solvents and also their reactions with nucleobases like guanosine time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA) and spectroscopies in a variety of solvents. We also compared these new results to investigate the differences between the diarylnitrenium ions with the more well-studied arylnitrenium ions literature results. We have demonstrated that diarylnintreniums react with guanosine at a different position (N7) to form a different intermediate compared to singlet arylnitrenium ions studied in the literature which attack guanosine at the C8 position to produce C8 intermediates. However, these different reaction pathways and intermediates both lead to formation of C8 adduct final products. In addition to address Objective 4, we have done DFT and time-dependent DFT computations to examine the reaction pathways for the diarylnitrenium ions reacting with selected DNA bases and compared these results to the experimental data above. These new experimental and computational results for diarylnitrenium ions have addressed Objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 and have been reported mostly in publications 1, 2 and 3 of this report. For Objectives 5 and 6, we performed time-resolved spectroscopy (ns-TA and ns-TR3) and product analysis experiments to explore the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions and diarylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. In addition, DFT computations were done to predict the intermediates involved in the reactions of interest. These new results will bring us new insights into the mechanisms for the arylnitrenium and diarylnitrenium ions induced reactions with nucleobases and amino acids and insight into possible protein damage these arylnitrenium and diarylnitrenium ions. We are still in the process of analyzing these results and preparing manuscripts for publication in due course. This work was slowed down by the effects of the pandemic on movement of chemicals and people. An interesting question for Objectives 1-7 is that all the arylnitrenium ions and diarylnitrenium ions examined so far are singlet in nature and no triplet arylnitrenium ion has been directly generated photochemically and characterized so as to better understand how the electronic configuration (triplet versus singlet) affects the structure, properties and chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions. An important finding in our project was the discovery of a precursor compound that was able to effectively photochemically generate a triplet arylnitrenium ion intermediate and characterize it with time-resolved spectroscopy methods. Using this new photochemical precursor compound, we were able to observe both the triplet p-iodophenylnitrenium ion and the singlet p-iodophenylnitrenium ion which were produced after about 10-50 ps, and their reactivities were greatly influenced by their electronic configurations. The triplet arylnitrenium ion decayed via ISC to form the closed-shell singlet ground state ion that then underwent proton and electron transfer reactions to form a radical cation species which generates the p-iodoaniline as the major photoproduct. In contrast to this, the singlet arylnitrenium ion produced the p-phenylenediamine through a dication species. Importantly, being able to control the electronic configurations of arylnitrenium ions has potential for the development of new synthetic transformations as well as how electronic configurations influence the chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions. This new work on triplet arylnitrenium ions helps to partially address Objectives 1-7 and was reported in publication 6 of this report. .

rows: Study the spectroscopic properties of selected diarylnitrenium ions by femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA) and time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) spectroscopies in a variety of solvents. Compare the differences between the diarylnitrenium ions with the more well-studied arylnitrenium ions, especially for their high reactivity toward nucleophiles. These results will be utilized for benchmarks to better understand the reaction mechanisms of the diarylnitrenium ions that will be studied further.

Investigate the reactions of selected diarylnitrenium ions with Guanosine, Adenosine, 5-Methyluridine and Cytidine in aqueous solutions using nanosecond transient absorption (ns-TA) spectroscopy. This part of our project will focus on the reaction rates. Additional experiments like ground state UV-vis absorption, resonance Raman spectroscopy, NMR and mass spectroscopy will be used to analyze the photo-induced products resulting from the reactions of the nitrenium ions and the DNA bases studied.

Ns-TR3 will be employed to obtain vibrational spectra information for the short-lived intermediates involved in the reactions between the diarylnitrenium ions and the DNA bases. The Raman spectra will enable more detailed information to be determined for the involved transient species, especially for the reactions towards guanosine. One may expect that there will be some different reactivity and properties between the diarylnitrenium ions and their arylnitrenium ions may result in some different alkylated transient species and final products and this will be explored as part of this objective.

DFT and time-dependent DFT calculations will be employed to predict the reaction pathways for the diarylnitrenium ions reacting with selected DNA bases. These results will help better elucidate the photoreaction mechanism of DNA damage process(es) induced by diarylnitrenium ions.

Time-resolved spectroscopy (ns-TA and ns-TR3) and product analysis experiments will be employed to investigate the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. DFT calculations will also be employed to predict the intermediates involved in the reactions of interest. These results will bring us new insights into the mechanisms for the nitrenium induced reactions with nucleobases and amino acids and insight into possible protein damage by nitrenium ions.

Similar time-resolved spectroscopy, product analysis experiments and DFT calculations will also be used to study selected diarylnitrenium ions with selected amino acids. These results will be used to compare with results found in objective 5 above and help to better understand the reaction mechanisms between the different these different kinds of nitrenium ions with amino acids.

If time and resources permit, we will synthesize some new precursors for selected diarylnitrenium ions and employ similar time-resolved spectroscopy methods mentioned above to study the photochemistry and electrophilic reactions of these diarylnitrenium ions. These experiments will provide deeper insights into the geometries, properties and chemical reactivity for these intermediates and reactions.

17302218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302218.value: Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA), nanosecond transient absorption (ns-TA), nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) spectroscopy and density function theory (DFT) calculations were done to characterize the spectroscopic characters of the N(4,40–dibromodiphenylamino)–2,4,6–trimethylpyridinium BF4- salt (1) in an acidic aqueous solution. The ultrafast dissociation of the N–N bond (4 ps) produces the N,N–di(4–bromophenyl)nitrenium ion (DN) in the acidic aqueous solution and in turn can form a dication intermediate 4 after abstracting a proton from DN in the acidic solution followed by an electron abstraction to produce the radical cation intermediate 3. These new time-resolved spectroscopic data are helpful to better understanding the identity, nature, and properties of nitrenium ions involved in reactions under acidic aqueous conditions. Next, we used, ns-TA and ns-TR3 spectroscopic methods to study the reactions between the diarylnitrenium ion and guanosine. The attack position of arylnitrenium ions toward guanosine derivatives are important to understand, and our time-resolved spectroscopy data and photochemical product analysis results demonstrate that the reaction of guanosine with the diarlynitrenium ion forms the N7 intermediates (which is different from other arylnitrenium ions studied in the past) which then undergo rearrangement and deprotonation to generate the C8 adduct. The major finding from the preceding work is that the structure and properties of the arylnitrenium versus diarylnitrenium ions can influence the reaction intermediate structure. Another major finding was our discovery of a new precursor that could form the triplet p-iodophenylnitrenium ion. This precursor 2-(4-iodo-phenyl)hydrazin-1-ium tetrafluoroborate 1, was examined by using fs-TA, ns-TA and nsTR3 time-resolved spectroscopic experiments and results from theoretical calculations. We observed both the triplet p-iodophenylnitrenium ion and the singlet p-iodophenylnitrenium ion that were formed after around 10-50 ps, and their reactivities were strongly affected by their electronic configurations. The triplet arylnitrenium ion decayed via ISC into the closed-shell singlet ground state ion, which could then undergo proton and electron transfer processes to produce a radical cation species that then produces the p-iodoaniline as the main photoproduct. In contrast, the singlet arylnitrenium ion formed the p-phenylenediamine via a dication species. Interestingly, control of the electronic configurations of arylnitrenium ions has potential for useful new synthetic transformations. Thus, further investigations for how the structures and electronic configurations of the initial arylnitrenium and diarylnitrenium ions influence the reaction intermediates can help gain deeper insights on how these addition reactions work to damage DNA.

17302218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302218.value: In this GRF project a major finding was the discovery that the alkylation reactions between selected diarylnitrenium ions and DNA bases proceed via a different N-7-intermediate species than arylnitrenium ions like 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion that form a C-8 intermediate species although both kinds of reaction pathways end up producing the same C-8 adduct final product. There is still further work that can be done to better understand why the singlet diphenylnitrenium ions react differently than the singlet arylnitrenium ions with guanosine bases and related oligomers. Additional experimental and computational can help acquire further insight into how the different structures and properties of diarylnitrenium ions relative to arylnitrenium ions influences their electrophilic reaction towards DNA bases. Another major finding of this GRF project was the discovery of a suitable precursor compound that was able to photochemically generate a triplet arylnitrenium ion intermediate and allow its direct observation and characterization for the first time. This opens up many new directions for further research to study a range of triplet arylnitrenium ions and their reactions for the first time and also enable a more detailed comparison of the structures, properties and chemical reactivity of triplet arylnitrenium ions compared to singlet arylnitrenium ions.

17302218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302218.value: Arylnitrenium ions are key intermediates in reactions that damage DNA that may induce a normal cell to become a cancer cell. Previous research found that singlet arylnitrenium ions, like 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion and 4-biphenylnitrenium ion are able to selectively react with guanine derivatives in DNA to form C8-intermediates that lead to C8-adduct final products. However, not much is known for reactions between singlet diarylnitrenium ions and DNA bases. Our research in this project directly investigated reactions of singlet diarylnitrenium ions and DNA bases and found that they react selectively with guanine derivatives to form N7-intermediates that then form C8-adduct final products. This work demonstrated that the different structure and properties of diarylnitenium ions react differently with guanine derivatives than singlet arylnitrenium ions but both produce C8-adduct final products. Our research on this project also discovered a new way to photochemically generate a triplet arylnitrenium ion that enabled the first direct observation and characterization of a triplet arylnitrenium ion intermediate. This new discovery opens up new avenues to observe and characterize triplet arylnitrenium ion and their reactions with DNA bases in the future so as to better understand the structures, properties and reactivities of triplet versus singlet arylnitrenium ions.

17302518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302518.value: It is known that marine biodiversity is much higher in certain places than other places. These high biodiversity locations are known as biodiversity hotspots and are important for ecological and conservation research. The Hopping Hotspots Hypothesis, arguing that Cenozoic tropical biodiversity hotspots have been shifting from Eocene Tethys (ancient Mediterranean), through the Miocene Arabia, to the Miocene–Recent Indo-Pacific (known as IAA, Indo-Australian Archipelago, hotspot), was proposed ~ 10 years ago. There is general agreement in these Cenozoic tropical diversity dynamics, but it remains uncertain if biodiversity hotspots really "hopped". Paleobiogeographic data tend to show similarity of taxonomic composition among the hotspots (i.e., Tethyan, Arabian, and IAA hotspots) supporting the Hopping Hotspots Hypothesis, but the data remain limited and primarily based on literature survey of often old references. The Cenozoic tropical diversity dynamics can also be explained simply by a rise and fall of diversity in each region without biogeographic shifts between hotspots (=hopping). We call this null hypothesis "Whack-A-Mole", in which moles (=biodiversity hotspots) will just rise and fall individually, without moving from hole to hole. Here we will test the relative importance of these two hypotheses by using fossil ostracods as a model system, by taking advantage of their continuous and abundant fossil records. More specifically, we will investigate Eocene and Miocene fossil samples from three regions of Pakistan (the place of Eocene Tethys and Miocene Arabian hotspots), southern Australia (fossil ostracod diversity known to be high; Australian hotspot hereafter), and the Indo-Pacific (IAA hotspot). We will compare fossil ostracod fauna between the Eocene and the Miocene, before and after the establishment of the IAA hotspot, respectively, and among Pakistan, Australia, and the Indo-Pacific. If biodiversity hotspots hop, the Miocene IAA fauna should be mainly composed of the elements from the previous hotspot(s) of the Eocene Tethyan (=Pakistan) region related to the Tethyan pathway to the Indo-Pacific and its closure (and perhaps southern Australian hotspot related to the collision of Australia with Pacific arcs and the southeast Asian margin). These relationships will be investigated by comparing diversity, faunal composition, and number of common species and genera among the regions. The results will give us a better understanding of the mechanisms that maintain biodiversity hotspots, which will help to manage and conserve biodiversity hotspots under various human-induced changes. 很多研究表明，某些海域的海洋生物多樣性顯著高於其他海域。這些擁有豐富海洋生物多樣性的海域被稱為生物多樣性熱點，對於生態與保育的研究具有重大意義。大約十年前提出了“跳躍式”轉移理論，指的是新生代的熱帶生物多樣性熱點從始新世的特提斯海（古地中海），於中新世轉移至阿拉伯半島，而後至今，移至印度洋－太平洋海域（通常被熟知為”印澳群島”熱點; IAA）。儘管新生代生物多樣性熱點的動態變化得到廣泛認可，其“跳躍式”轉移的理論仍具有爭議性。古生物地理的數據表明各個熱點（如特提斯海，阿拉伯半島和印澳群島）之間有相似的生物分類組成，但這些數據主要來源於早期的文獻調查，具有一定的局限性。實際上，“新生代熱帶生物多樣性熱點的動態變化”也可被簡單地認為是每個地域生物多樣性的增減，而非在不同熱點之間的生物地理轉移（“跳躍式”）。我們把這個假設稱為“閃現式”，意為每個熱點的生物多樣性是獨立地增加或減少，而非相互轉移。因此，鑑於介形類擁有連貫和豐富的化石記錄，本研究以介形類為研究對象，測試兩種理論的相對重要性。具體地說，我們將分析三個地區中始新世和中新世的化石樣品，包括：巴基斯坦（始新世特提斯海及中新世阿拉伯半島熱點），澳洲南部（已知介形類的多樣性很高；以下簡稱為澳洲熱點），以及印澳群島（IAA熱點）。 我們將分別對比介形類組成的化石記錄在始新世和中新世的差異，在IAA熱點形成前後的差異，以及在巴基斯坦，澳洲和印度洋－太平洋熱點海域的區別。如果多樣性熱點是跳躍式的， IAA熱點的中新世介形類組成理應與始新世的特提斯海（今巴基斯坦地區，其形成與特提斯通往印度洋的路徑及關閉有關）相似，也可能與澳洲南部熱點（其形成與澳洲和太平洋弧及東南亞邊緣的碰撞有關）相似。因此，我們將分析各個熱點間的介形類種類、組成以及常見種屬的數量差異。此研究結果將揭示生物多樣性熱點的維持機制，對於在人類活動干擾下如何管理和保育生物多樣性熱點具有重要的环境和生态学意義。

17302518.label: Realisation of objectives
17302518.value: 1. To obtain comprehensive Cenozoic ostracod data from Pakistan and Australia. We have obtained many Cenozoic samples and ostracod data, and we published 17 papers as seen in the Part C. 2. To compare diversity and faunal composition among the Indo-Pacific, Pakistan, and Australia. Detailed comparison of diversity and faunal composition among hotspots has been conducted as detailed in Yasuhara et al (2022, Oceanography and Marine Biology: An Annual Review; see Part C), supporting the Hopping Hotspots model. 3. To elucidate the number of species and genera that are common among these three regions, based on our own robust taxonomic harmonization, to evaluate paleobiogeographic affinities among the hotspots. These Tethys taxa were identified and the comparison of paleobiogeographic affinities among the hotspots have been conducted as detailed in Yasuhara et al (2022, Oceanography and Marine Biology: An Annual Review; see Part C), again supporting the Hopping Hotspots model. 4. To test Hopping Hotspots and Whack-A-Mole Hypotheses. As above, we evaluated these two hypotheses rigorously and supported the Hopping Hotspots model (as full details shown in Yasuhara et al 2022, Oceanography and Marine Biology: An Annual Review; see Part C). 5. To better understand how marine biodiversity hotspot has been developed. We now much better understand global dynamics of Cenozoic tropical biodiversity hotspots and we proposed Global Hopping Hotspots Model to explain them. A summary is given below in the Sections 6 and 7.

17302518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302518.value: In this project, we conducted the detailed investigation of tropical biodiversity in the broad Into-Pacific and globally. Our project supports the Hopping Hotspots model, which proposes that the locations of peak biodiversity are related to Tethyan faunal elements and track broad-scale shallow-marine habitats and high coastal complexity created by the collision of tectonic plates. The ‘Whack-A-Mole’ model can be useful as a null hypothesis, which proposes that hotspots occur in habitats suitable for high diversity regardless of taxonomic identity or faunal elements. It was, however, also revealed that human-induced disturbance is massively disrupting these natural patterns. We produced 17 papers. Through these, we increased biodiversity and faunal information of these regions substantially, and synthesized global patterns and mechanisms of Cenozoic tropical biodiversity hotspots successfully. As emphasised in Yasuhara et al (2020 Oceanography; see Part C), paleobiology (recently I dub it as Time Machine Biology) is essential to understand not only deep-time past biodiversity and ecosystems but also to use such information to understand the present and prepare for a coming future. We also conducted 5 oral presentation in international conferences.

17302518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302518.value: We are interested in whether the same mechanisms work in older time period such as Mesozoic and Paleozoic. Also more rigorous comparison with tectonic and climatic modelling data will aid better understanding of global biodiversity and the mechanisms behind. In addition, an important next step will be re-investigation of western Tethys ostracod taxonomy and faunal composition in details in classic Paleogene European localities (such as Paris Basin) to uplift and update the taxonomic and paleobiogeographic information, leading to a next-stage synthesis.

17302518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302518.value: Tropical marine seas are known to support a large number of species, with about 30% of all marine species being found in coral reefs alone. Within this, there are particular regions that show exceptionally high biodiversity, known as biodiversity hotspots. In the present day the Indo-Australian Archipelago is one of these hotspots, however this has not always been the case. Biodiversity hotspots have changed in both richness and location across geological time. In this study, we used fossil records and tracked the rise and fall of these hotspots through the last 66 million years, and examine how this happens. The data showed that tropical shallow marine biodiversity hotspots across the 66 million years all occur in similar tectonic settings with complex coastlines and numerous islands related to continent-continent collision. This tectonic-induced process known as "Hopping Hotspots" explains the relationship between biodiversity hotspots: the hotspot location "hopped" to track such tectonically-active regions.

17302918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302918.value: The rational design of materials with controlled dimensions, shapes, architectures and topologies is of crucial importance in advanced materials synthesis. However, most materials consist of molecules that are randomly oriented and packed by intermolecular forces. The control of these non-covalent intermolecular interactions will help to align and pack the molecules into a more ordered structure with improved desirable properties. In this project, we will mainly focus on the use of supramolecular assembly processes to manipulate the molecular packing and to create nanoscale architectures in a controllable manner, which has been a major challenge in materials synthesis. In sharp contrast to the well-established development of polymer synthesis and living polymerization that has led to widespread use of polymers with profound impacts, supramolecular polymerization is less extensively studied and living supramolecular polymerization is still at its infancy. As most of the works on supramolecular assembly and polymerization are focused on simple amphiphilic molecules such as lipids, peptides and molecular surfactants, and more recently π-conjugated chromophoric motifs and polymers, to form micellar-type of structures and aggregates as well as supramolecular polymers, we will focus on the less explored metallosupramolecular motifs. In particular, efforts will be made with the use of the low-coordinate metal-ligand motifs that have the advantage over the more commonly employed octahedral metal complex building blocks by allowing columnar stacking. Despite scattered examples of supramolecular assembly and polymerization involving low-coordinate metal-ligand motifs leading to well-defined nanostructures known, all of them are confined to single-component supramolecular self-assembly with two-component supramolecular co-assembly to generate well-defined nanostructures essentially unknown and unexplored. In this project, we will focus our efforts on the exploration of the virtually unexplored two- to multi-component supramolecular co-assembly as well as living supramolecular polymerization based on low-coordinate metal complexes and various diblock and triblock copolymers. These, together with a systematic study of the strategies and underlying factors that govern their controlled dimensional growth, would also be pursued. It is envisaged that with judicious design and choice of the block copolymers as well as the discrete target low-coordinate metal complex monomers or unimers with unique structural properties, novel classes of two- and multi-component metallosupramolecular co-assemblies with novel nanostructures or networks of controlled dimensional growth and interesting optical, luminescence and morphological properties would be obtained. This may open up new, simple one-pot strategies for the fabrication of unique two- and multi-component metallosupramolecular co-assemblies with controlled dimensional growth. 形狀、尺寸、構造和拓撲結構可控的材料的合理設計對於先進材料的製備至關重要。然而，大多數材料是由隨機取向的分子組成，在材料內部，分子之間存在非共價相互作用。對分子間非共價相互作用的控制有助於將材料內部的分子排列成更有序的結構，進而獲得所需的材料性能。本專案的關注點為運用超分子組裝過程來操控分子的堆積，進而可控制備納米結構，這也是目前材料合成領域中的主要挑戰。對共價聚合物而言，聚合方法的發展已經比較完善，而且，聚合方法的發展促進了共價聚合物的廣泛使用。與共價聚合不同，超分子聚合方法的研究相對較少，其中，活性超分子聚合仍處於起步階段。目前，超分子組裝和超分子聚合的研究工作大多集中在比較簡單的兩親性分子的溶液行為的研究上，如脂質、肽和小分子表面活性劑，以及最近的共軛發光分子和共軛聚合物的溶液行為的研究，這些兩親性分子的溶液組裝可形成各種膠束或超分子聚合物。本專案將專注於目前研究較少的金屬配合物組裝單元的超分子組裝和超分子聚合，特別地，將研究低配位元金屬配合物組裝單元的超分子性質。低配位元金屬配合物可堆疊成柱狀超分子聚集體，這是常用的八面體金屬配合物所不具備的優點。儘管有低配位元金屬配合物通過超分子組裝和超分子聚合形成規整納米結構的零星報導，但這些報導都局限于單一組分的超分子自組裝，文獻上基本沒有通過雙組分體系的超分子共組裝而形成規整納米結構的報導。本專案將致力於探索雙組分和多組分超分子共組裝體系的組裝行為，以及探索基於低配位元金屬配合物和兩嵌段共聚物或三嵌段共聚物的活性超分子聚合體系，也將系統研究控制超分子體系的尺寸增長的策略和潛在因素。我們預期，通過對嵌段共聚物的合理設計以及選擇具有獨特結構和性質的低配位元金屬配合物，本專案可製備獲得維度和尺寸可控，具有有趣的光學、發光和形貌特色，具有新型納米結構和網路結構的雙組分和多組分金屬-超分子共組裝體。本項目可開闢一條用簡單的一鍋法製造尺寸可控的獨特的雙組分和多組分金屬-超分子共組裝體的全新策略。

17303418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303418.value: 最近人们对研究三维（3D）Dirac半金属（一种新的电子状态物 质）感兴趣。它与石墨烯的3D类似，具有独特的电子结构，其 中传导和价带能量仅在动量空间中的孤立点处相互接触，在所 有三个动量方向上具有线性色散关系。如果时间反演或空间反 演对称性被破坏，则Dirac半金属的双重带简并性被破坏，导致 另一个称为Weyl半金属的拓扑相。在Weyl半金属中，每个触点 都具有一定的手性，可以看作动量空间中的磁单极子（Berry通 量的源或汇）。预计Weyl半金属具有许多独特的性质。例如， 它具有拓扑保护的无能隙新型费米弧面状态。该体系被预言显 示负磁阻，异常霍尔效应，非局部输运和普通电流的局部非守 恒性。在表面上的费米弧状态可以在隧道光谱学中引起磁输运 和量子干涉效应的新的量子振荡。通过量子场理论预测，直流 磁场可以在Weyl半金属中产生特殊的纵向电流密度，这种效应 被称为手性磁效应，被认为是Weyl节点独特手性异常的特征之 一。一系列的角分辨光电子能谱学实验已证实外尔半金属的能 带结构的存在以及对系统如TaAs，TaP，NbAs，NbP，MoTe2， WTe2具有上述非常规特征。 特别是在NbP中，Weyl半金属的 候选物，在高达9T的磁场中及温度为1.85K（室温下250％）时 观察到8500000%的极大的磁阻。 Weyl半金属所具有的这些独特性质表明Weyl半金属有望用于拓 扑量子比特，低功率电子器件和自旋电子学等应用。 众所周知， 这种无序普遍存在于所有固态系统中，它可以将Weyl半金属驱 动到不同的量子相中。 由于Weyl半金属的学术意义和实际应用 价值，研究Weyl半金属对抗无序的鲁棒性非常重要。 此外，研 究无序对Weyl半金属的运输特性的影响将是有趣的。

17303418.label: Realisation of objectives
17303418.value: In order to achieve our goal, which is quantum transport through disordered WSM modeled by a particular Hamiltonian, we first want to develop necessary machinery to tackle the general systems in the presence of disorders. For instance, we need to develop formalism to treat frequency dependent conductance and shot noise in the presence of disorders, as well as the formalism for the transient dynamics. We have done several works along this line. (1). We have developed general full counting statistics formalism for frequency dependent transport. This formalism can be coupled with coherent potential approximation so that the ac transport in the presence of disorders can be dealt with analytically. This formalism can also be used to study ac shot noise and full counting statistics as well as transient dynamics. (2). We have also explored transient dynamics in the presence of quantum trench with temperature gradient. (3). We have also studied the phase diagrams for ac transport in the presence of disorders. (4). In WSM systems, phonon transport is also important. One of my M.Phil students, Mr. C. Zhang, has developed a general formalism of full counting statistics for phonon transport in the presence of disorders within coherent potential approximation. (5). In quantum transport field, most of the work focused on diagonal disorders. Less attention has been paid on more general problems, i.e., diagonal disorders as well as off-diagonal disorders. One of my M.Phil students, Mr. Z.Y. Yu, together with my collaborators, has developed a general formalism using full counting statistics language with coherent potential approximation that can investigate quantum transport through disordered systems.

17303418.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303418.value: Specifically, we have predicted transport properties of disordered systems, especially ac transport properties. To do so, one has to calculate the disorder average of the correlation of the multiple Green's function at different energies. To avoid brute force calculation, diagrammatic perturbation expansion must be used along with the coherent potential approximation (CPA). We developed a theoretical formalism based on the non-equilibrium Green's function that maps the average of the correlation of the multiple Green's function into an average over a single generalized Green's function. After the mapping, this formalism is structurally very similar to the CPA and completely eliminates the need to perform diagrammatic expansion. As a demonstration of our theory, the dynamic conductance, frequency-dependent shot noise under dc bias, and frequency-dependent noise spectrum under ac bias in the presence of Anderson disorder are calculated by directly taking the disorder average of the generating function of full counting statistics (FCS) within the CPA. Our numerical results on dynamic conductance, frequency-dependent shot noise under dc bias, and frequency-dependent noise spectrum under ac bias show remarkable agreement with that obtained by the brute force calculation. The phase diagram in the frequency versus disorder strength plane has been efficiently calculated using the generalized FCS-CPA method. We investigated the transient behavior of the quantum transport in mesoscopic systems under a quantum quench within the Caroli scheme. Using the nonequilibrium Green's function approach, an exact solution of the transient electric current, energy current, and its fluctuation in the presence of both external bias and temperature gradient are presented that goes beyond the wide-band limit. The exact solution of the time dependent Seebeck coefficient in the linear response regime is also obtained. This formalism is applied to study the transient behavior of a single-level quantum dot with Lorentzian linewidth induced by the temperature gradient. The damped oscillatory behavior is found in the transient electric and energy currents, as well as their fluctuations. The oscillation frequency of electric and energy currents increases with the increasing energy level of quantum dot and the decay rate of oscillation decreases as the bandwidth increases. A significantly enhanced Seebeck coefficient is generated in the transient regime. We find the maximum value of the time dependent Seebeck coefficient can be enhanced by increasing the energy level of the quantum dot and the reference temperature of leads.

We proceed to calculate ac transport properties in the presence of disorders including full counting statistics. 17303518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303518.value: The family of atomically thin two-dimensional crystals has grown rapidly since the discovery of graphene, displaying a broad range of electronic properties that hold promises for hosting versatile electronics and optoelectronics. Different 2D crystals can be vertically stacked and glued together by the van der Waals force to form heterostructures that can combine and extend the distinct properties of the building blocks. Owning to the flexibility in forming vdW heterostructures, various types of vertical heterostructure devices constructed with distinct building blocks and geometries are being actively studied experimentally. Spintronics is another highly active research frontier with the similar goal of improving efficiency and enriching functionalities of future electronics, but taking a different approach focused on the exploitation of magnetization and spin for information storage and processing. 2D atomic crystals with intrinsic magnetism are thus of great interest that can allow spintronic manipulations on the versatile platform of vdW heterostructures and devices. Very recently, 2D magnets in truly 2D limit have been successfully exfoliated from the layered bulk magnets, allowing the integrating of atomically thin magnetic information storage unit into vdW heterostructure devices. This project will exploit this opportunity and theoretically investigate quantum manipulations of magnetizations and spins in vdW heterostructure devices consisting of 2D chromium triiodes and other trihalides - a family of ferromagnetic semiconductors/insulators in monolayer form - for new concept spintronic devices. Based on the intriguing magnetic properties experimentally discovered in mono- and few- layer chromium trihalides, we plan to investigate a number of novel spintronic controls, including: manipulations of the layered magnetic configurations in these 2D magnets; engineering of in-plane magnetic textures in incommensurate heterstructures that may arise from the interlayer magnetic coupling; and engineering of the magnetic proximity effect from adjacent 2D magnets for control of carrier spin in the non-magnetic building blocks of the vdW heterostructures. 從石墨烯的發現以來，原子厚度的二維材料家族日益壯大，各種不同電子物性的家族成員不斷被發現，為實現新型的多樣化電器件及光電器件提供了平臺。不同的二維材料可以通過範德瓦爾斯力結合，堆垛成各種異質結，來組合並拓展不同單元的各不相同的屬性。由於通過範德瓦爾斯力相結合組成異質結所具有的靈活性，各類不同的異質結器件正在被廣泛的研究。自旋電子學是當下另一個熱門的研究領域，著眼於通過利用磁性及電子自旋來存儲和處理信息，以實現拓展電子器件的功能和提高性能。具有本征磁性的二維原子晶體使得範德瓦爾斯異質結器件能夠為自旋電子學探索提供一個全新的多樣化的平臺，成為當下矚目的一個熱點。最近，幾個實驗組通過對層裝的磁性材料進行機械剝離得到了原子厚度的二維磁性晶體，這個關鍵的突破給將磁性存儲和範德瓦爾斯異質結器件相結合帶來了契機。這個研究項目將從理論上探索在三鹵化鉻範德瓦爾斯異質結器件中的對磁性和電子自旋的量子調控。三鹵化鉻是首先發現原子厚度下本征二維鐵磁性的一種層狀絕緣材料，在單層及多層的厚度下，表現出豐富的奇特磁性結構。 我們計劃探索一系列的自選電子學調控，包括：對這類材料中的層狀磁性的操控；在晶格不匹配的異質結中利用不同層間的磁耦合來實現平面內的各種磁性紋理；在異質結中通過磁性近鄰效應來實現相鄰的非磁性二維材料中的自選調控。

17303518.label: Realisation of objectives
17303518.value: Objective 1: Achieved. We have explored few layer chromium trihalides in vertical tunneling heterostructure devices, together with our experimental collaborators. Possibilities to access the various layered magnetic configurations and to utilize them for functional devices are demonstrated, including: (1) voltage control of tunnelling magneto resistance in few layer CrI3 sandwiched by graphene contacts in a dual-gated structure, where the device can be switched reversibly – by gate voltage at fixed magnetic field - between bistable layered magnetic configurations with the same net magnetization but remarkably different resistance; (2) spin photovoltaic effects in few layer CrI3 sandwiched by graphene contacts, where the photocurrent can be controlled by light helicity and frequency, as well as the layered magnetic configurations in varying magnetic field; (3) finding of the layered antiferromagnetic order in CrCl3 with an easy-plane normal to the c-axis, where the tunnelling current as function of magnetic field shows distinct behavior from that in CrI3. These findings point to exciting opportunities to explore emergent spintronics and photospintronics by engineering atomically thin chromium trihalides heterostructures (c.f. publications #2,4,10). Our theoretical study has also discovered a giant spin transfer torque in the coherent tunnelling through a magnetic bilayer - a regime that becomes relevant with the atomic thickness of 2D magnets - using a model we previously adopted for describing the giant tunneling magneto-resistance through bilayer CrI3. We find that the spin transfer torques per electron incidence can become orders of magnitude larger than hbar/2, made possible by electron’s multi-reflection path through the ferromagnetic monolayers as an intermediate of their angular momentum transfer. This points to exciting possibilities for highly efficient current control of layered magnetic configurations in few layer 2D magnets. The results are published on Chin. Phys. Lett. 37, 107201 (2020), as an Express Letter (c.f. publication #7). Objective 2: Achieved. We have investigated the magnetic proximity effect in a van der Waals heterostructure formed by a monolayer semiconductor stacked on a two-dimensional ferromagnet. We find that the magnetic proximity field from the spin-dependent interlayer coupling depends sensitively on the interlayer atomic registry. The general presence of lattice mismatch and twisting between the layers will lead to the formation of a moiré pattern, and consequently the spatial variation of the atomic registry leads to a lateral periodic modulation of a magnetic proximity field. Such a moiré modulated magnetic proximity effect manifests as a miniband spin splitting that strongly depends on the moiré periodicity, which can be mechanically tuned by a relative twisting and/or strain between the layers. We also show, because of the moiré modulation on the interlayer distance, a perpendicular electric field can be used to control the miniband spin splitting. Our results suggest potential nanodevices where the moiré modulated magnetic proximity effect can lead to unique spin controllability. The results are published on Phys. Rev. Applied 12, 024031 (2019) (publication #1). Objective 3: Achieved. We find that the sensitive dependence of interlayer magnetic coupling between 2D magnets in vdW heterostructure on the interlayer stacking registries can be exploited to realize various magnetization textures such as magnetic bubble phases and skyrmion lattices. In the long-period moiré pattern of 2D magnets, we show that the formation of magnetization textures can be rooted in the local-to-local variation of atomic registry in the moiré and the registry dependent interlayer magnetic coupling, which favors periodic domain structures, whereas interlayer dipolar coupling can wind domain boundaries to form skyrmions. An external magnetic field can switch the vorticity and location of skyrmions in the moiré, and the skyrmion lattices can be dramatically tuned by small interlayer translation and strain through the moiré magnification effect. At weaker interlayer coupling or small moiré period where the monolayer remains in FM phase, we find that local magnetization reversal can generate and erase metastable skyrmion excitations that behave like quasiparticles trapped in a superlattice potential. Current pulses can deterministically move such skyrmion excitations between the ordered trapping sites. These control possibilities point to potential use of 2D magnets moiré as a lateral register array using skyrmion excitations as information carriers. The results are published on Nano Letters 18, 7194 (2018) (publication # 3). Based on the example of the recently discovered 2D magnetic topological insulators MnBi2Te4, we also explored the interplay of such magnetization textures with topological surface states, where sign flip of the exchange gap across a magnetization domain wall gives rise to a single in-gap chiral channel on each surface. In the periodic magnetization textures, such chiral spin channels at the domain walls couple to form a network and superlattice minibands emerge. We find that in magnetization textures with closed domain-wall geometries, the formed superlattice miniband is a gapped Dirac cone featuring orbital magnetization from the current circulation in the closed loops of chiral channels, while in magnetization textures with open domain wall geometries, a gapless mini-Dirac cone is found instead. The miniband Bloch states feature a spatial texture of spin and local current densities, which are clear manifestations of the spin-momentum locked chiral channels at the domain walls. The results suggest a platform to engineer spin and current flows through the manipulation of magnetization domains for spintronic devices. The results are published on Phys. Rev. B 102, 125409 (2020) (publication #6).

17303518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303518.value: (1) We explored magnerization textures in moiré pattern of 2D magnets. Using example of ferromagnetic monolayer on antiferromagnetic substrate, we demonstrate a new origin of skyrmions from the spatial modulation of interlayer magnetic coupling in moiré, with periodicity dramatically tunable by strain. At relatively strong interlayer coupling, the ground states are skyrmion lattices, where magnetic field can switch skyrmion vorticity and location in the moiré. At weak interlayer coupling limit, we find metastable skyrmion excitations on the ferromagnetic ground state that can be deterministically moved between the ordered moiré trapping sites by current pulses. See publication #3. (2) We studied the effects of the periodic magnetization textures in 2D magnetic topological insulators MnBi2Te4 that can be generated by moiré pattern. For the surface Dirac cone gapped by exchange field, sign flip of the gap across a magnetization domain wall leads to a chiral channel inside the exchange gap. In the periodic magnetization textures, such chiral spin channels form a network and superlattice minibands emerge out of their coupling. The miniband Bloch states feature a spatial texture of spin and local current density, where the spin momentum locked chiral channels pinned to the domain walls are clearly manifested. These results suggest a platform to engineer spin and current flows through the manipulation of magnetization domains for spintronic devices. See publication #6. (3) We investigated the magnetic proximity effect in moire superlattice formed by CrI3 and a semiconductor monolayer (BAs). Our first-principles calculations show a strong dependence of magnetic proximity field on the interlayer registry, which, in the moire superlattices, leads to a strong lateral modulation of the magnetic proximity field, giving rise to spin splitting in minibands. We show remarkable tunability of the spin splitting by a perpendicular electric field, which can be utilized for engineering programmable spin polarized quantum dot arrays. See publication #1. (4) We found in the quantum coherent tunneling through atomically thin magnetic bilayers, the scattering wavefunctions at the tunneling resonances have a spin current density profile peaked between the two ferromagnetic monolayers, resembling the intra-cavity field for a resonant photon. As a result, the torque per electron incidence becomes orders of magnitude larger than hbar/2. Electron’s role as an intermediate for angular momentum transfer is radically amplified through its multiple reflections between the two monolayers. This finding points to highly efficient manipulation of 2D magnets by tunneling current for spintronics applications. See publication #7.

17303518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303518.value: Findings of this project have pointed to some interesting directions for further development. We have shown that the coherent resonant quantum tunneling through magnetic bilayers can lead to a field-like torque that is equivalent to the RKKY interaction mediated by the quasi-bound electron, as well as a damping-like torque that tends to align downstream layer parallel to upstream layer, and upstream layer anti-parallel to downstream one. This points to rich possibilities to drive magnetization dynamics by tunneling current for spintronics manipulations, under various scenarios where 2D magnets have either in-plane or out-of-plane anisotropy, and interlayer interaction being either ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic. Under the situation where one layer has much larger anisotropy than the other (free layer), we plan to investigate the magnetisation dynamics with the free layer being in either upstream or downstream side. We also plan to investigate a more intriguing scenario when the two magnetic layers have comparable anisotropy, i.e. both upstream and downstream layers can have active magnetization dynamics driven by current. The coherent quantum tunneling regime is likely applicable to a thicker limit (e.g. 8 to 10 layers), where more complex current driven layered magnetization dynamics is expected.

17303518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303518.value: Atomically thin 2D crystals with intrinsic magnetism are of great interest for spintronic manipulations. The orientation of magnetization in an individual layer can be used to encode information. The possibility to manipulate the layered magnetic configurations in van der Waals layered structures of 2D magnets, and the possibility to manipulate spin in non-magnetic layers by the proximity field from adjacent magnetic layers can potentially lead to miniaturised devices for future information technology. This project has theoretically investigated various possibilities for manipulations of magnetizations and spins in heterostructures consisting of 2D chromium trihalides as well as other magnetic and nonmagnetic 2D crystals for spintronic applications, including: manipulations of the layered magnetic configurations in these 2D magnets; engineering of in-plane magnetic textures in incommensurate heterstructures that may arise from the interlayer magnetic coupling; and engineering of the magnetic proximity effect from adjacent 2D magnets for control of carrier spin in the non-magnetic building blocks of the vdW heterostructures.

17303618.value: Construct a family of L-functions which have an additional parameter (a certain complex number) and yield the Riemann zeta function as a limit. Compute the regularized Mellin transform on the family of weight 1/2 forms; construct a family of L-functions related to the Riemann zeta function. Consider applications of the properties of the L-functions constructed in previous steps on the L-series obtained in the limit. Investigate any possible implications about the zeros of L-series. 17303618.label: Realisation of objectives
17303618.value: A paper was produced where the regularized Mellin transform of polar harmonic Maass forms were computed, achieving objective 2. This was then applied to the family of weight 2 polar harmonic Maass forms given in objective 3. The limit of the family of polar harmonic Maass forms yields a weight two Eisenstein series, which is known to be connected to the product of two zeta functions. However, due to technical complications, the limit inside the integral and outside of the integral give different values. Through analytic techniques and careful meromorphic continuation, the difference between the limit inside and outside of the integral was evaluated and turns out to be related to an explicit finite sum of polylogarithm functions. After this technical modification, objective 1 could be realized by subtracting the extra terms and then taking the limit. A paper, joint with Kathrin Bringmann, was completed and has recently been accepted for publication in the Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications. Following the completion of the aforementioned paper, similar techniques were applied in the weight 1/2 case. The first task, objective 4, was to construct a family of meromorphic modular forms whose limit is precisely the classical theta function. A modification was made that involved what is known as a Hauptmodul for the theta subgroup (upon which the classical theta function is modular). The limit inside and outside of the integral is again different due to the technical issues that arise from the regularization process for the Mellin transform. Similar polylogarithm functions appear in the difference between these two limits, and it was again shown that after subtracting these polylogarithm terms, the limit precisely yields the Riemann zeta function precisely, giving objective 5. The resulting paper is in preparation. After completing the first 5 objectives, we have been looking for applications of these generalized L-functions/regularized Mellin transforms for meromorphic modular forms and polar harmonic Maass forms. Along this vein, we have been looking for another perspective on the polylogarithm functions, rewriting them in another form that reveals more information about the Riemann zeta function and possibly its zeros. This has partially succeeded in objective 6, although we still lack a full understanding of what we are looking at. Over the previous summer, a team of two undergraduates worked on a twisted version of the results contained above, following the techniques in the accepted paper. This partially succeeded in objective 7, although the applications are as of yet unknown. It should also be noted that another undergraduate was also trained in the techniques and generalized the results in a different direction the summer before that; the student produced a preprint from this, which is currently submitted for publication and under review in a journal.

17303618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303618.value: The major findings are the construction of generalized L-functions and the realization of the limit (after an appropriate subtraction of "simpler" terms) as a classical L-function related to the Riemann zeta function (it is the product of two zeta functions). Moreover, it is likely that the regularization which was constructed to find a meromorphic continuation that gives the generalized L-functions as a regularized Mellin transform will have applications in other settings. Regularized integrals have appeared in a number of settings, including theta lifts, and a regularization of the Mellin transform for functions that have singularities may similarly appear in those settings. The construction resulted in a paper, joint with Kathrin Bringmann, which has been accepted for publication in the Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications. The generalization to weight 1/2 has also been fruitful, as it resulted in similar functions appearing but the limit is now precisely the Riemann zeta function. The resulting paper is still under preparation, but may help to further enlighten us about the nature of these new functions.

17303618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303618.value: There are still interesting questions about the possible applications of there generalized L-functions. Due to the technical nature of the construction, not enough time has been spent thinking about how to use these new functions, although they do seem to give some new structure around well-known classical L-functions.

17303618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303618.value: Certain integrals of highly symmetric functions with many "bad points" were studied. The naive definitions of these integrals give infinite answers, but they were "regularized" to give finite answers. These finite answers were then investigated and shown to be related to well-known functions related to the zeta function that was studied by Riemann. The points where the Riemann zeta function vanish are of particular interest, and properties related to the symmetries of the functions that were integrated is being investigated at points where the Riemann zeta function vanishes.

17303918.label: Project Objectives
17303918.value: Fieldwork: collect high-resolution, biostratigracphically constrained samples from middle Cambrian-early Ordovician carbonate platform deposits of North America that record mass extinction events. 17303918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303918.value: This project will investigate mass extinctions during the early evolution of animals. Specifically, we will take a multi-disciplinary geochemical and paleontological approach to understand the underlying mechanisms behind environmental perturbations of the Cambrian “dead interval”– the intervening ~40 million-year gap between the Cambrian "explosion" and the Great Ordovician Biodiversificiation Event. This “dead interval” is characterized by low biodiversity, widespread deposition of organic-rich black shales, selection against hypercalcifying organisms and the longest 'reef-gap' of the Phanerozoic, as well as numerous mass extinction events that yield faunal turnovers comparable to the Phanerozoic "Big Five" mass extinctions. We will investigate three of these upper Cambrian mass extinction events, which are mostly seen in trilobite communities, in two paleogeographically distinct terranes: Laurentia (North America) and North China/Sino-Korea. We will 1) utilize large biostratigraphic data compilations to establish whether these extinctions were global events; 2) construct high-resolution coupled carbon and sulfur (δ13C and δ34S) isotopic records to assess oceanic anoxia as a potential “kill-mechanism” during these extinctions; and 3) use high-resolution strontium and lithium (87Sr/86Sr and δ7Li) isotopic records to evaluate paleo-weathering responses to possible climatic perturbations throughout this interval. Furthermore, these combined biostratigraphic and chemostratigraphic data will help to properly correlate Laurentian and North China/Sino-Korean stratigraphic records, thus improving our broader understanding of the Cambrian period. 该项目将研究动物早期进化过程中的大规模灭绝。具体而言，我们将采用多学科的地球化学和古生物学方法来理解寒武纪“死区”的环境扰动背后的潜在机制 - 寒武纪“爆炸”与大奥陶纪生物多样性事件之间的间隔约为4千万年的差距。这种“死亡区间”的特点是生物多样性低，富含有机质的黑色页岩的广泛沉积，对高钙化生物的选择和显生宙最长的“礁间隙”，以及产生与其相当的动物群失调的大量灭绝事件。显生宙“五大”灭绝。我们将研究这些上寒武纪大规模灭绝事件中的三个，这些事件主要见于三叶虫群落，在两个古地理上不同的地体：Laurentia（北美）和华北/中韩。我们将1）利用大型生物地层数据汇编来确定这些物种灭绝是否是全球事件; 2）构建高分辨率耦合碳和硫（δ13C和δ34S）同位素记录，以评估海洋缺氧作为这些灭绝期间潜在的“杀灭机制”; 3）使用高分辨率锶和锂（87Sr / 86Sr和δ7Li）同位素记录来评估整个间隔内可能的气候扰动的古风化响应。此外，这些组合的生物地层学和化学地层学数据将有助于将劳伦森和华北/中韩地层记录正确联系起来，从而提高我们对寒武纪时期的更广泛理解。

17303918.label: Realisation of objectives
17303918.value: This project was adversely affected by the Covid-19 pandemic. We conducted a single field season during January 2020 approximately one week before the first reported Covid case in Hong Kong. The subsequent covid outbreak resulted in major travel restrictions that prevented us from completing any additional fieldwork — we had planned for extensive field seasons in Summer 2020 that we could not execute. The pandemic also caused the extended closures and long -running restrictions of many analytical facilities. My student was only just finally able to visit Yale to conduct analyses in December 2022 (~2.5 months ago). Our key analytic facility at HKU (MC-ICP-MS lab) has been down since before the outset of Covid due to our inability to receive engineers from abroad to conduct repairs given Hong Kong’s Covid restrictions — we are now finally scheduling these visits. Accordingly, progress on this project has been very slow. However, we redirected our efforts to aspects of project that could be complete under the limitations of Covid and have made significant “catch up” on this project in recent months. Firstly, we greatly refined the biostratigraphic database on two fronts: one highly focused on the upper Cambrian—lower Ordovician record, and the other on the Ediacaran—middle Cambrian. The upper Cambrian–Ordovician work was spearheaded by collaborator Dr. Shelly Wernette, which included our new fossil collections made in Southeast Asia – notably specimens collected during our joint collaborative work in Myanmar and Thailand – along with the incorporation of my older database. Dr. Wernette completed her PhD in 2020 and she was potentially going to come do a postdoc with me at HKU to work on this project; however, the Covid-19 pandemic prevented her from moving here, so she took another opportunity and remained in the USA. We have maintained ongoing collaborations for this work and are making progress. The other front was led by my current postdoc, Dr. Qing Tang (HKU Presidential and RGC Postdoctoral Fellow) who started in June 2021. In addition to Dr. Tang’s databasing work, he was also able complete independent fieldwork this past late summer-fall 2022. Collectively, this comprehensive work will continue to produce new research outputs. We have generated new detrital zircon U-Pb data from fossiliferous Cambrian sandstones and compiled a large database of published U-Pb zircon data that we are incorporating with the biostratigraphic data to test models on trilobite provincialism and paleogeography. This work has variably involved my former PhD students Cody Colleps and Hangyu Liu, along with multiple HKU undergraduates. While the database is continuously growing, this work has contributed to 2 manuscripts (one having gone through review, one in prep circulating amongst the coauthors), with more to follow. As noted above, by my PhD student (HKPF student Chris Cheung) visited Yale for ~3 weeks this December 2022 when he set up and generated new lithium (Li) isotopic data. 17303918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303918.value: We were not able to fully complete the extensive field work we anticipated given the extent of the Covid-19 pandemic, which had downstream implications for our other objectives given we could not generate the extensive geochemical records we planned (this is indicated by the less than 100% completions noted above). However, we were able to expand our efforts to work collaboratively within the Covid constraints to achieve results following the overarching goals of the project, i.e., to enhance the biostratigraphic resolution of early Paleozoic mass extinctions and develop a better understanding of environmental conditions during this interval. Biostratigraphic databases were vastly extended during this project, via work with HKU researchers and external collaborations to produce records beyond those initially expected (objective 2). Importantly, through our collaborative work we generated new geochronologic data both from detrital zircon from sandstones interbedded withing fossiliferous horizons, and importantly, from ash beds dispersed within select horizons. This provides important numerical ages to further anchor our biostratigraphic records in time and enhance global correlations beyond what would have been capable from chemostratigraphy alone (objectives 4 & 5). This even more significant as this particular interval has very few existing numerical age constraints and these new data greatly enhance our over construction of our geologic timescale. These combined records further elucidated the presence of multiple previously hypothesized mass extinction events and supported the global correlation of these biospheric perturbations. Therefore, this work added fare more perspective to the extent of environmental turmoil during this enigmatic interval of Earth history. While we could not generate the amount of geochemical data we planned, what we have generated was quite intriguing. Notably, our C and S isotopic data (objective 5) identified coupled perturbations at independently correlated extinction horizons, thus enhancing the strength of these global correlations and demonstrating perturbations to the carbon and sulfur cycles in relation to the mass extinctions. The most parsimonious explanation for the isotopic data would be that enhanced ocean anoxia, specifically expanded euxinia, was linked to the extinctions. The magnitude and duration of the sulfur isotopic excursion presents further evidence of very low seawater sulfate, illustrating the dramatic differences in seawater chemistry during that time of extreme greenhouse conditions compared to the rest of the Phanerozoic.

17303918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303918.value: The elucidation of late Cambrian-early Ordovician global-scale mass extinction events warrants further exploration of the geochemical records during this interval in order to better understand the drivers of these biospheric perturbations. This will need to be accomplished through the development of more extensive biostratigraphically constrained geochemical records. As noted above, we are in the process of vastly enhancing our Li and Sr isotopic datasets. These data are used as proxies that can potentially track enhanced chemical weathering following rapid climatic warming form CO2 fluxes from volcanic activity, which is a hypothesized “kill mechanism” given the extreme greenhouse conditions during the Cambrian. These new data will be generated by Summer 2023. We have additional plans to explore calcium (Ca) isotopes as a potential proxy to identify ocean acidification during these mass extinctions (work to funded with a future seed grant on our existing samples that is beyond the primary scope of this project). The extensive biostratigraphic databases generated need to be qualitatively assessed with appropriate software (CONOP) and calibrated/anchored with our new numerical dates to better resolve the Cambrian geologic time scale. This work is currently being carried out with anticipated completion later this year (2023).

17303918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303918.value: This project explored environmental conditions during an interval in Earth history characterized by an extreme greenhouse climate and major turnovers in biological diversity during the early evolution of animals some ~500 million years ago. Through the development of global databases of fossil occurrences integrated with new geochronologic age data, we enhanced the resolution of our geologic times scale during this interval, and identified global-scale mass extinctions events that occurred in continents where they had not been previously recognized. Our new geochemical data illustrated major perturbations to the global carbon and sulfur cycles corresponded with these extinction events, perturbations that may be linked to widespread ocean anoxic events. Collectively, our findings further demonstrate the biological turmoil experienced during one of the most dramatic greenhouse climates witnessed by animals, and adds important perspective to how major climatic variations can influence the evolution of Earth’s biosphere.
