17305718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305718.value: The most significant findings were: (A) A vertical tectonics "heat-pipe" model passed a series of prediction tests at the Isua supracrustal belt, whereas plate tectonics models for this area (at least in terms of their currently published specific predictions) did not. Plate tectonics presents such a diverse and flexible set of overall tectonic environments that it is not possible to rule it out, but the published specific applications of plate tectonic environments to this environment (i.e., terrane collision, or an accretionary prism) are not supported. (B) A side project that grew from / within this project context developed a new exciting model for the initiation of plate tectonics that was published in Nature Communications (Tang et al., 2020) and won the Research Output Prize of the Faculty of Science (HKU). (C) Another side project led by the principal PhD student on this project, Jiawei Zuo, led to the first preliminary exploration of detrital zircons in pre-plate tectonic settings, in terms of models and data, published in Earth and Planetary Science Letters (Zuo et al., 2021). Breaking these findings down with respect to the project objectives, we published the prediction tests in the following works: 1) strain distributions: Webb et al., 2020 Lithosphere; Zuo et al., 2021 Tectonics; Ramirez et al., 2022 Tectonics. [Note that the 2022 contribution is a peer-reviewed Reply to Comments on our two Tectonics papers in 2021]. 2) metamorphism and deformation: Webb et al., 2020 Lithosphere; Zuo et al., 2021 Tectonics; Ramirez et al., 2021, 2022 Tectonics. 3) Age control: Webb et al., 2020 Lithosphere; Ramirez et al., 2022 Tectonics (both reinterpretations of published data); new data is about 1 month and 3 months away from submission for contributions led by A. Ramirez-Salazar and J. Zuo, respectively. 4) Reconstruction: Webb et al., 2020 Lithosphere; Zuo et al., 2021 Tectonics; Ramirez et al., 2021, 2022 Tectonics.

17305718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305718.value: We hope to pursue these works further. We used internal funding to return to Isua in summer 2022 and delved deep into records of metasomatism. These are disputed, but suggest that the protolith rocks of many key lithologies may be grossly misunderstood. These rocks are our best window into Eoarchean time, the oldest period for which we have rock records, and yet we can't yet even define the original rock types! Through future funding, some hopefully from RGC, we hope to explore the textural relationships and mass balances of metasomatic reactions in order to enable new mapping of the Isua region and new understanding of the rocks developed at the Earth surface in the Eoarchean.

17305718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305718.value: Earth's earliest rocks can tell us about the evolution of our home planet. However, few of them are preserved to the present day. Other than tiny grains of the mineral zircon, the oldest rocks are from the Eoarchean period, 4 to 3.6 billion years ago. Of these, the best preserved rocks that record Earth surface conditions are at the "Isua supracrustal belt", a ~35 km strip of layered rocks in southwestern Greenland. We explored these rocks because there is much evidence suggesting that plate tectonics - Earth's current mode of heat-loss and planetary dynamics - started at around ~3.2-3.0 billion years ago, yet all prior teams exploring Isua interpret that these rocks also record plate tectonics half a billion years earlier. Could alternative pre-plate tectonic models dominated by volcanism be possible? We tested plate tectonic and pre-plate tectonic models, focusing on chronological, metamorphic, and deformation predictions of the models. Plate tectonic models did not pass; pre-plate tectonic models did. New plate tectonic models could be devised for Isua (plate tectonics is flexible), but the new project findings drastically change the range of permissible options, showing viability of pre-plate tectonic models here for the first time.

17306018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306018.value: Podiform chromite deposits are mostly hosted in mantle peridotites of ophiolites and include both high-Cr and high-Al varieties that are believed to have formed from different magmas under different tectonic settings. Varieties of mineral inclusions in chromite of chromite ores are proved to have different origins, suggesting that the formation of chromite ores may involve more complex mantle processes than previously thought. Although this complexity makes it difficult to determine where in the mantle such bodies formed, the contradictory evidence must be reconciled in order to develop a satisfactory model for the origin of podiform chromite deposits and their hosting ophiolites. Parental magmas of two types of chromite ores are particularly critical for establishing a new model for the formation of ophiolites and can be examined using melt inclusions in minerals. The Zambales ophiolite in the Philippines contains both high-Al and high-Cr chromite ore bodies in the Acoje and Coto blocks, which have affinities of island arc and back-arc basin in a supra-subduction zone environment (SSZ), respectively. Studies of melt inclusions in these blocks could provide detailed information about the genesis of different types of chromite ores and the geological evolution of the Zambales ophiolite, which is also critical to reconstructing the framework of SSZ environments in general. In this project, we plan to undertake systematic studies of melt inclusions in minerals from chromite ores and associated dunites of the Acoje and Coto blocks. Such studies will be based on field investigation, petrographic observations, and whole-rock and mineral analyses. We will determine major and trace elemental and Sr-Pb-Li-O isotopic compositions of homogenized melt inclusions. Our goals are to unravel the genetic relationship between chromite ores and their hosting peridotites; to determine melt/fluid processes that control the formation, compositions and distributions of high-Cr and high-Al chromite ores; and to understand the multi-stage processes that are linked to the evolution of ophiolites. With these messages, we finally hope to reconstruct the tectonic evolution of the Zambales ophiolite and to establish a geodynamic model for SSZ processes. 豆荚状铬铁矿矿床主要赋存于蛇绿岩层序中地幔橄榄岩里面。它们在成分上可以划分为高铝和高铬两大类型，通常被认为是超俯冲带背景（SSZ）下不同岩浆作用的产物。近年来，详细地观察发现矿石里的铬铁矿往往包含有类型丰富的矿物单晶或集合体。这些矿物包裹体具有明显差异的成因，暗示了铬铁矿矿床的形成过程可能比之前提出的模型更为复杂。鉴于豆荚状铬铁矿矿床的成因对于研究蛇绿岩的起源以及超俯冲带的演化有重要的启示意义，我们亟需提出一个新模型来更好地解释它们的形成过程。矿物中包含的熔体包裹体直接捕获于岩浆作用阶段，它们的化学成分有效地记录了寄主矿物的母岩浆信息。因此研究矿物熔体包裹体为了解豆荚状铬铁矿矿床的形成及其背后所蕴含的地质过程提供了重要的手段。菲律宾吕宋岛西北部的三巴礼士（Zambales）蛇绿岩同时包含有高铝和高铬两种类型的铬铁矿床，它们分别主要产出在该蛇绿岩的阿科杰（Acoje）和科特（Coto）两个块体之中。前人研究表明，这些高铝和高铬类型的矿床在构造背景上分别表现了出了岛弧和弧后盆地的特征。它们在成分和成因上的显著差异性非常有利于我们开展熔体包裹体相关工作的研究。在该项目中，我们计划针对不同类型矿石及其纯橄岩围岩中的铬铁矿和橄榄石，进行系统性的熔体包裹体研究。具体包括有野外地质调查，镜下岩相学观察，全岩及单矿物的主微量成分分析，矿物熔体包裹体的均一化实验，熔体包裹体原位的主微量元素和Sr-Pb-Li-O同位素测试分析。通过这些研究，我们有望更好地了解铬铁矿矿体及其围岩之间的内在联系，确定控制铬铁矿床形成和分布的主要因素，揭示相关熔流体活动和蛇绿岩演化过程中多期次地质事件。在综合这些信息的基础上，我们期待能够完整地恢复三巴礼士的构造演化历史，并建构一个SSZ过程相关的地球动力学模型。

17306018.label: Realisation of objectives
17306018.value: This project involved the work of two PhD students, Zhang Pengfei and Hu Wenjun, who were then research assistants with the PI for this project. Since the start of this project, we have carried out field and extensive lab work both in Mainland and HK. Extensive collaboration with geologists from Mainland and Philippines was part of the project. This includes work with Prof. Jun Yumul (Philippines), Prof. Julian Pearce (UK), Prof. John Malpas (emeritus professor of HKU), and Prof. Paul Robinson (Canada). Although the studies were partially based on the previous findings of the PI, we have also generated many new ideas in this project with a focus on chromite deposits in the Philippines, Cyprus and Tibet. Specifically, Dr. Zhang worked on the Philippines and Tibet and Dr. Hu has focused on Cyprus and melt inclusions with in-situ isotopes. With new observation and lab work, we reached the objectives with 5 papers published. Some results were presented in international conferences and were well received. Overall, all of our objectives proposed in the projects have generally been realized. 1. to characterize the general features of the Zambales ophiolite and to examine the field relationships between chromite ore bodies and their hosting peridotites in the Acoje and Coto blocks. We observed the two ophiolitic blocks, including the spatial distributions of each lithology. The mantle sequence of both blocks become more and more depleted from their bottoms upward, featured by decreasing vol.% of pyroxenes in the peridotites. We discovered that chromite deposits were mainly hosted in the dunitic Moho transition zones of the two blocks, different from the previous concept that chromite orebodies are mainly distributed in the mantle sequence of ophiolitic blocks. Moreover, abundant cpx-rich harzburgites and cpx-poor lherzolites were identified in the mantle sequence of the Acoje block, and such rocks were also found at the topmost part of the mantle sequence and even near the high-Cr chromite orebodies. By contrast, the mantle sequence of the Coto block is mainly made of cpx-poor harzburgites. Such regular spatial distributions of different lithologies in the two blocks allow us to restore the general mantle processes related to different types of chromite mineralization in the ophiolite. 2. to observe carefully multiple solid phase inclusions in chromite and olivine from high-Cr and high-Al chromite ores and identify mineral grains with melt inclusions for homogenization experiments. We carefully observed the mineral phases included in chromite and olivine grains in different ore rocks from the Zambales ophiolite and lavas from the Troodos ophiolite. The results show that chromite from both types of ores have inclusions of olivine, orthopyroxene, clinopyroxene and amphibole, either mono- or poly-mineralic. However, chromite grains in the high-Al ores were specially found to have plagioclase inclusions at times, supporting the traditional viewpoint that the parental magmas of high-Al chromitites are more Al-rich than those of the high-Cr chromitites. In addition, olivine grains from the upper pillow lavas of the Troodos ophiolite were seen to have inclusions of mixed glass and clinopyroxene crystals. Relevant inclusion-bearing phases were picked up for homogenization experiments of melt inclusion already. 3. to obtain a dataset of trace elemental and Sr, Pb, Li and O isotopic compositions of melt inclusions. We have carried out in-situ trace element analysis for chromite and olivine grains in different types of lithologies. Combined with major element compositions of both mineral phases, the data helped us to better understand the parental magma compositions of different chromitites and their mantle sources. Moreover, we also conducted in-situ Sr, Pb, Li and O isotopic analyses for olivine grains and their hosted melt inclusions from the Zambales and Troodos ophiolites. Such data allow us to identify the contribution of different components in the mantle sources of different magmas. 4. to retrieve the nature and origin of the parental magmas of high-Cr and high-Al chromite ores through integration of bulk, minerals and melt inclusion data. One main purpose is to determine the exact nature and origin of the parental magmas of different chromite ores. With the combined petrological observation and chemical analyses, we were able to claim that the parental magmas of the high-Al chromitites have transitional MORB-boninitic and arc picritic compositions, respectively. Both types of parental magmas originated from depleted harzburgitic mantle regions, but the former ones were generated under lower temperature conditions than the latter ones. Relevant conclusions have been published already and can be particularly found in the papers below. Zhang, P.F., Zhou, M.F. and Yumul Jr, G.P., 2020. Coexistence of high-Al and high-Cr chromite orebodies in the Acoje block of the Zambales ophiolite, Philippines: Evidence for subduction initiation. Ore Geology Reviews, 126, p.103739. Zhang, P.F., Zhou, M.F., Yumul Jr, G.P. and Wang, C.Y., 2021. Geodynamic setting of high-Cr chromite mineralization in nascent subduction zones: Li isotopic and REE constraints from the Zambales ophiolite, Philippines. Lithos, 384, p.105975. 5. to explore the possible contribution of fluid/melt activities to the formation of chromite ores. The in-situ isotopic data obtained for mineral separates and their hosted melt inclusions were used for investigating the contribution of fluid/melt activities in the mantle sources of different chromite ores. According to our data interpretation, the mantle sources of both types of ores had been modified by slab components to varying degrees, but the source regions of some high-Cr chromitites kept normal mantle-like isotopic features. Moreover, we also did numerical calculations to constrain the amounts of slab contributions quantatitively, which had never been done in previous studies. More details regarding relevant studies can be found in the papers below. Zhang, P.F., Zhou, M.F., Malpas, J. and Robinson, P.T., 2020. Origin of high-Cr chromite deposits in nascent mantle wedges: Petrological and geochemical constraints from the Neo-Tethyan Luobusa ophiolite, Tibet. Ore Geology Reviews, 123, p.103581. Zhang, P.F., Zhou, M.F. and Yumul Jr, G.P., 2020. Coexistence of high-Al and high-Cr chromite orebodies in the Acoje block of the Zambales ophiolite, Philippines: Evidence for subduction initiation. Ore Geology Reviews, 126, p.103739. Zhang, P.F., Zhou, M.F., Yumul Jr, G.P. and Wang, C.Y., 2021. Geodynamic setting of high-Cr chromite mineralization in nascent subduction zones: Li isotopic and REE constraints from the Zambales ophiolite, Philippines. Lithos, 384, p.105975. Hu, W.J., Zhou, M.F., Malpas, J. and Ren, Z.Y., 2021. High-Ca boninitic melt inclusions in lavas of the Troodos ophiolite and a reappraisal of genetic relationships between different lava types. GSA Bulletin. 6. to reconstruct the evolution of the Zambales ophiolite and propose a possible model for the geodynamic evolution of newly-initiated subduction zones. The Zambales ophiolite is an oceanic fragement generated during subduction initiation in the Western Pacific, and it can be effectively used for studying how intra-oceanic subduction initiation is developed. Different from traditional works that took volcanic rocks as the research tools, we used mantle rocks preserved in the mantle sequences of the ophiolites in our studies, which preserved multiple stages of melt events compared to the erupted lavas. With the obtained petrological and geochemical information, we provided more details for the geochemical and geodynamic evolution of the newly-initiated subduction zones. In particular, we found that the nascent mantle wedges experienced a relatively cold stage during the transitional MORB-boninitic magmatism, which was never been found previously. Details of relevant conclusions can be found in our accepted papers. Moreover, we are still composing more papers on the Zambales ophiolite, which will be published soon.

17306018.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306018.value: Our previous objectives set in the proposal are all reached. Our activities related to the project have been productive. The project was actually a continuation of previous studies of our research group at the HKU but tackled new issues with significant implications. In this project, we have made a series of progresses for the origin of podiform chromite deposits and their hosting ophiolites. To achieve the objectives, we have done field excursions worldwide including those to the Philippines, Tibet, Cyprus, Oman and etc. To clarify the mutual relationships among different lithologies, petrography of each lithology, and solid-phase inclusions in chromite grains, we conducted careful observations not only on outcrops but also using microscopes and SEM. On the basis of our detailed peotrographic observation, systematic geochemical analyses were further carried out for the in-situ major-trace element and Sr-Pb-Li-O isotopic compositions for phases such as chromite, olivine, pyroxene and homogenized melt inclusions included in some of the minerals. This work allowed to better understand the compositions and origins of the parental magma of high-Al and high-Cr chromite ores. Moreover, we also improved the model of chromite mineralization and linked their tectonic settings to the process of subduction initiation, which was among the earliest batch of studies in the world claiming the genetic relationship between podiform chromite mineralization and subduction initiation. Our discoveries generally overcome the problems encountered in previous studies and can explain most features observed for podiform chromite deposits and supra-subduction zone (SSZ) ophiolites. Currently, we have published 5 papers in high-level international journals, including and 1 psper in GCA (IF, 5.010), 1 paper in GSAB (IF, 4.40), 1 paper in Lithos (IF, 4.0004), and 2 in Ore Geology Reviews (IF, 3.809). We also attended international conferences, such as the world-famous Goldschmidt held at Barcelona in 2019 and some high-level geosciences-related workshops in China. According to the citation records, some of the papers have received notable attention from colleagues across the world, and the overall feedbacks were positive and pleasant. In addition, we are still keeping working on the obtained data and possibly will have 2-3 papers completed in the coming year.

17306018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306018.value: Our research group has been working on podiform chromite deposits for over 30 years and has always been one of the leading groups on relevant topics in the world. In this project, we have made some major achievements on the origin of podiform chromite deposits, including the general compositions of their parental magmas and mineralization settings of different types of chromitites. Despite such novel findings, some conclusions are still at their preliminary stages and have not been defined quantitatively, enlightening us that detailed investigations remain to be done on podiform chromite deposits and their SSZ ophiolites. Accordingly, more experimental studies with modern technologies such as micro-analysis using nano-SIMS, high P-T experiments and numerical simulation, are highly needed, and we anticipate to eventually establish an integrated generic model for podiform chromite deposits and their ophiolite hosts quantitatively. Overall, our previous work on these deposits of this project has made a major impact internationally. At the moment, our research group are collaborating with Chinese and oversea colleagues to continue our studies on these well known deposits. We are confident that more and more critical details would be reconstructed in the future.

17306018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306018.value: Podiform chromite deposits are important source of chrome for industrial productions. This project aims to better understand the origin of podiform chromite deposits and ophiolites, the hosting bodies of chromite deposits. The research outcomes would provide valuable information for chromite exploration in the field. The project was mainly undertaken by Prof. Meifu Zhou (PI) and his two research assistants, Dr. Pengfei Zhang and Wenjun Hu. The collaborators, Jun Yumul from Philippines and John Malpas from the University of Hong Kong, were also involved and offered us instructions on field work, data interpretation and paper writing. Since the start of this project, the research group has organized field trips in Philippines, Tibet, Cyprus and Oman for times and conducted extensive laboratory work in Hong Kong and Mainland China. Up to now, the research group have published 5 papers in prestigious journals and also attended high-level conferences for times, e.g., the world-famous Goldschmidt held at Barcelona in 2019, receiving postive feedback from colleagues on relevant topics. The findings of this projects are overall inspiring and enlightening. In the future, the research group will continue working on relevant topics to deepen the knowledge of chromite mineralization in ophiolites.

17306718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306718.value: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the CERN lab is the world’s largest and highest- energy particle accelerator for studying fundamental particles and their interactions. The ATLAS is one of the two general purpose particle detectors at the LHC, belonging to an internationally collaborated particle experiment. The Muon Spectrometer of the ATLAS accurately measures the tracks of highly penetrating muons, which provides key information for the Standard Model precision measurements and various new physics searches. The LHC is planed to operate until the year 2030 or beyond. The particle physics researches will greatly benefit from increasing the luminosity and collision energy of the LHC. Maintenance and upgrades the ATLAS detector are necessary to meet the challenges brought by increasing the luminosity and energy of the LHC. One of the incoming events for major detector maintenance and upgrades is the phase 1 upgrade which will happen in 2019 and 2020. The PI proposes the projects which are the parts of the muon detector electronics upgrade and the muon detector control system development. The projects are within a time window covering the end of RUN II, the phase 1 upgrading period and the beginning of the Run III of the ATLAS experiment. The projects will last from September 2018 to August 2021. 位於歐洲核子中心（CERN）的世界最大和最高能量的大型強子對撞機（LHC）正在研究基本粒子以及它們之間的相互作用。 ATLAS是LHC的兩個通用粒子探測器之一，同時它也是一個以ATLAS命名的國際合作粒子物理實驗。ATLAS探測器的MUON譜儀可以精確的測量大動量的MUON在探測器中的軌跡，這是可以用於粒子物理標準模型精確測量和新物理探測的關鍵信息。 LHC計劃運行到2030年或2030年之後結束。 粒子物理研究將會收益於LHC對撞亮度和能量的增加， 而增加LHC亮度和能量會給ATLAS粒子探測器的升級維護帶來新挑戰。 在2019和2020年，ATLAS探測器計劃實施PHASE 1 升級維護工作。 PI建議的項目是MUON探測器的電子學升級以及控制系統發展的一部分。整個項目時間跨度是從RUN 2 末尾階段， PHASE 1升級， RUN 3 初始階段，從2018年9月到2021年8月。

17306718.label: Realisation of objectives
17306718.value: For the objective 1 “commissioning the sTGC sub-detector Front End Electronics System in Phase I upgrade at the ATLAS experiment”, we help to: 1. prepare the Felix system for chamber testing. 2. setup TTC system for the Felix 3. develop and test the MINIDAQ firmware 3. apply noise measurement on the sTGC Wedges. 4. test the monitoring and controlling tools for digital DC power supply. 5. optimize the threshold settings for the VMM chips according to individual channel’s baseline and noise level. 6. design and produce cooling cages. All of sTGC wedges have been integrated and tested, in which less than 2% channels observed with defects in high voltage operation. Recently, a successful integration of NSW MMG & sTGC DCS into ATLAS Muon Central DCS is achieved. The sTGC successfully took data in self-trigger mode during the LHC beam splashes run. For the objective 2 “developing the Detector Control System (DCS) for the Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) detector”, we help to: 1. develop standardised display histograms for parameters under monitor such as high voltage , low voltage, electronics, gas, and cooling systems. 2. develop the operator panel to control and monitor the system in the Felix. 3. update the map with the new EASY crate that will be controlled from the MainFrame via the branchController for the system 4. the post-doc becomes RPC DCS on call expert.

17306718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306718.value: The LHC started the phase I upgrade in 2019. My group is involved in the upgrade of electronic system for the Muon New Small Wheel small Thin-Gas-Chamber ( NSW sTGC) detector. We have been one of the most active groups in commissioning the sTGC Front End electronics system. The muon detector is one of the most important sub-detector of the ATLAS. The performance of it has significant effects on the signal significance of new physics searches and the precision of the Standard Model measurements. The upgrade of the muon trigger detectors is going to reduce the large event rates while maintaining high efficiency for processes of interest. As part of this upgrade, the NSW will replace the inner detectors of the end-cap muon spectrometer, such that the Level-1 trigger rate can be reduced significantly. Our work contributes to provide precision muon measurement for new physics discovery and the Standard Model measurements with muons in the final states at the LHC.

17306718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306718.value: Currently the sTGC integration is in the final stage such the beam tests and data analyses are carried out. One crucial part of the integration procedure is to validate the electronics for a system with more than two million electronic channels. We can use our experiences for developing the operator panel to control and monitor the detector system in the Felix to help the construction of the readout chain for sTGC which is based on the FELIX too .

17306718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306718.value: Fundamental particles are basic elements of matter and the fundamental force carriers in the universe. The ATLAS experiment is one of the major particle experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. All particle scattering experiments require particle detectors to reconstruct and identify all the particles emerging from a scattering event. A detector is a system, at least including sensors and readout electronics which sense small signals, amplify them to a usable level with a sufficiently good signal-to-noise ratio and then transform the signal into some form usable by computers over a relevant time of period. Due to this reason, particle physics has grown together with the electronics technologies. Due to unique requirements on function and performance, most electronic systems for modern detectors can only be built with custom designs. Our group is actively involved in the detector electronics commissioning and detector control system developing work. The detector we help to built will be used in the Atlas experiment at the Large Hadron Collider.

17306818.label: Project Objectives
17306818.value: To study the MDDM-based testing method for multivariate MDS hypothesis. Some new MDDM-based tests will be constructed for the testing purpose, and their limiting null distributions will be established. These MDDM-based tests will be shown to be consistent and have non-trivial power to detect local alternatives. A wild bootstrap method will be given to obtain their critical values, and its validity will be justified. Simulations will be conducted to assess their finite-sample performance. Extension work to the MDDM-based spectral test will be attempted if time allows. To develop the HSIC-based testing method for independence hypothesis. Some new HSIC-based tests will be proposed to examine the independence of two model innovations, and their limiting null distributions will be derived. The consistency and local power of these HSIC-based tests will be studied. A residual bootstrap method will be offered to obtain the critical values of these HSIC-based tests, and its validity will be justified. Simulations will be given to examine the performance of these HSIC-based tests in finite-sample. Extension work to the HSIC-based spectral test will be considered if time allows. To apply the proposed MDDM-based tests and HSIC-based tests in various applications. The existing well-known prediction models for many important fundamental variables will be examined by all newly proposed tests. Insightful prediction models will be expected.

17306818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306818.value: Testing for martingale difference sequence (MDS) hypothesis is important to see whether the user-specific multivariate time series model is appropriate for prediction. However, all existing tests are only applicable for univariate time series models, and they could result in misleading conclusions by overlooking the information of some endogenous variables. To overcome this deficiency, this project constructs some new novel tests for multivariate MDS hypothesis by using the martingale difference divergence matrix method. Moreover, it is crucial to determine whether the user-specific multivariate time series model can enhance its prediction ability, by making use of the information from the other multivariate time series model. Testing for independence of their model innovations can give us insightful evidence towards this goal. However, most of existing tests are only investigating the linear dependence of two model innovations. This project proposes some new novel tests for independence of two model innovations by using the Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion method, and these tests can detect the general (including both linear and non-linear) dependence of two model innovations. Finally, this project establishes the properties of all newly proposed tests, and demonstrates their importance by a myriad of applications. 检验一个多元时间序列是否为鞅差对于模型预报具有重要意义。但是，现有方法仅仅对于一元时间序列模型适用，因而在外生变量存在时，这些方法可能给出错误的结论。为了克服这些不足，本项目借助鞅差发散矩阵，构造了一类新的检验方法来检验多元时间序列是否为鞅差。 进一步，一个关键的问题是我们是否可以利用其它模型信息来提升目标模型的预测能力。两模型的独立性检验可以为此问题的解答提供有用信息。本项目利用希尔伯特-施密特独立性准则，构造一类新的关于两多元模型误差独立性的检验；这些新的检验可以检验一般性的误差相依结构（包含线性及非线性结构）。 最后，本项目将研究上述检验方法的性质，并在大量实际例子中验证这些方法的重要性。

17306818.label: Realisation of objectives
17306818.value: 1. My published paper Wang, Zhu, and Shao (2022, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics) has achieved the Objective 1. In this paper, my co-authors and I have proposed several MDDM-based tests to examine whether the error term in a multivariate parametric time series model is a martingale difference sequence. Under some regularity conditions, we have established the asymptotic null distributions of these MDDM-based tests. Since the null distributions are not asymptotically pivotal, we have provided a fixed design bootstrap method to compute their critical values and proven its validity. Moreover, we have shown that our MDDM-based tests are consistent to detect a broad class of fixed alternatives, and they have nontrivial power against local alternatives of order n^{-1/2}, where n is the sample size. In simulation studies, we have demonstrated that our MDDM-based tests have accurate sizes and good power. 2. My published paper Wang, Li, and Zhu (2021, Statistica Sinica) has achieved the Objective 2. In this paper, my co-authors and I have proposed some one-sided omnibus HSIC-based tests for independence between innovation vectors of two multivariate stationary time series. Under regular conditions, we have established the limiting null distributions of our HSIC-based tests. Next, we have proven the consistency of our HSIC-based tests. Moreover, we have provided a residual bootstrap method to obtain the critical values for our HSIC-based tests, and justified its validity. Our simulation studies have found that compared with the existing cross-correlation-based tests for linear dependence, our tests can have the decent power to examine the general (including both linear and non-linear) dependence. 3. I have achieved the Objective 3 by applying the MDDM-based tests and HSIC-based tests to study some real data sets in the aforementioned two papers. Specifically, the MDDM-based tests have been used to check whether the U.S. monthly interest rates can be adequately fitted by a multivariate threshold autoregressive model. This is a benchmark interest rates data set and has been studied by Tsay (1998, Journal of the American Statistical Association 93, 1188–1202). Our testing results have revealed that the multivariate martingale difference assumption assumed by Tsay (1998) is valid, so the multivariate threshold autoregressive model is correctly specified to study this interest rates data set. Moreover, the HSIC-based tests have been used to examine whether there has a causal relationship between Chinese stock market and Russian/Indian market. Our testing results have indicated that there is a strong contemporaneously causal relationship between these two markets, which, however, have an asymmetric non-contemporaneously causal relationship. The Russian/Indian market has a quicker impact to Chinese market. On the contrary, the Chinese market is more localized, and its influence to Russian/Indian market tends to be slower but can last for a longer term.

17306818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306818.value: This project has delivered 10 published papers, including 1 paper in Annals of Statistics (AoS), 3 papers in Journal of Econometrics (JoE), 2 papers in Journal of Business & Economic Statistics (JBES), 3 papers in Statistica Sinica (SS), and 1 paper in Journal of Time Series Analysis (JTSA). The first major research outcome from my published paper Wang, Zhu, and Shao (2022, JBES) is that our MDDM-based tests provide formal tools to test the multivariate martingale difference hypothesis in the literature for the first time. Testing for univariate martingale difference hypothesis has been widely studied, however, none of attempts has been made for the multivariate counterpart. Our study has filled this gap, and it is expected to have a large application scope. The second major research outcome from my published paper Wang, Li, and Zhu (2021, SS) is that our HSIC-based tests are applicable to model residuals rather observed data. As is well-known, the tests based on model residuals have to account for the model estimation effect, making the null distribution of test become complicated. If we ignore the estimation effect, the testing results tend to be wrong, leading to some incorrect conclusions. Our results in this paper have shown how the estimation effect affects our HSIC-based tests, and provided a valid way to compute critical values based on the bootstrap. Owing to the financial support from this project, I also have many other interesting research outcomes for various statistical tests in my other published papers. In Zhu (2019, AoS), I have proposed a sign-based test to check the adequacy of heteroscedastic autoregressive (AR) model. In Jiang, Li, and Zhu (2020, JoE), we have studied the non-standard asymptotics of Wald, LR, and LM tests for the augmented double AR model. In Wang and Zhu (2020, SS), we have studied the asymptotics of portmanteau tests for the nonlinear co-integrating regression with correlated errors. In Jiang, Li, and Zhu (2021, JoE), we have shown how the time-varying structure of long-term variance affects the asymptotics of portmanteau tests. In Wang, Zhu, Li, and Li (2022, JoE), we have proposed several quantile-based tests to check the stationarity of GARCH model. In Liu, Zhu, and Zhu (2022, JBES), we have constructed wavelet-based tests to check the white noise hypothesis for the non-stationary data. In Zhou, Jiang, Zhu, and Li (2022, SS), we have formed some new tests to check the adequacy of matrix time series model.

17306818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306818.value: Rooting in the current outputs from this project, I expect some further related research developments in future. For example, one of my on-going project is to construct the estimation for the multivariate regression model based on MDDM. The advantage of this new MDDM-based estimation method over the traditional instrumental variable estimation is that it is applicable even when the model is under-identifiable. Another possible future study is the extend our HSIC-based tests to study the non-stationary data. This extension seems attractive but challenging at this stage. It may require some new technique treatments to study the statistical inference of non-stationary time series model.

17306818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306818.value: Testing for martingale difference sequence hypothesis is vital to see whether the user-specific multivariate model is appropriate for prediction. However, all existing tests are only applicable for univariate models, and they could lead to wrong conclusions by overlooking the information of some endogenous variables. The MDDM-based tests in this project overcome this deficiency successfully. Moreover, our HSIC-based tests in this project help us to determine whether the user-specific multivariate model can improve its prediction ability, by making use of the information from the other multivariate model. Overall, both MDDM-based tests and HSIC-based tests could help practitioners to get more efficient models for prediction.

17306918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306918.value: In the theory of random matrices, the class of so-called Wigner matrices is particularly important. Historically pioneers in random matrix theory such as the mathematical physicist Eugene Wigner studied these matrices in the late 1950’s. Wigner discovered the celebrated semi-circle law and these matrices are thus named after him. These matrices have been studied intensively in the literature since then. In particular, an important result establishes the so-called central limit theorems for linear statistics, that is, for any smooth function say f(x), if we denote by a1, …, an the eigenvalues of an n by n Wigner matrix, then when n grows to infinity, the sum f(a1)+…+f(an) will converge to a Gaussian distribution. However, in such exiting central limit theorems, the entries of the matrix are required to have a common fourth moment. This project is motivated by the study of large networks such as friend networks on Facebook, network of scientific collaborators in mathematics, network of research papers connected by citations. A current and challenging problem here is to group different members into communities, that is sub-groups of members who are more likely connected each other. Network data directly point to connections between all the members, but the structure of communities is not observed and has to be identified (detection of communities). Notice that any network is characterized by its adjacency matrix which is symmetric with binary entries 0 and 1. In fact such an adjacency matrix can be modeled as a random Wigner matrix and the investigation of its spectral properties leads to many powerful inference tools for the structure of the network. In particular, one can test various hypotheses on this structure by examining linear spectral statistics of the adjacency matrix. However, the particularity of such adjacency matrices is that their entries do not have a common fourth moment. Following our previous studies in random matrix theory, we propose in this project to establish new central limit theorems for linear spectral statistics of a general Wigner matrix without a common fourth moment for its entries. This theory, once completed, can be directly used to address the problem of detection of communities in a large network. The advantage of such linear spectral statistics over those already proposed in the literature is that they are believed to be more robust against estimation errors. Therefore, this project will leads to innovative and promising tools for analysis of large networks. 在隨機矩陣理論中，Wigner矩陣的研究非常重要。歷史上隨機矩陣理論的先驅，如數學物理學家Eugene Wigner在20世紀50年代後期研究了這些矩陣。Wigner發現了著名的半圓律；這些矩陣因此以他的名字命名。從那以後，專家們對這些矩陣進行了深入的研究。尤其重要的一個結果是關於線性統計量的中心極限定理。也就是說，對於任何平滑函數，如 f(x)，如果我們用a1,...,an表示一個 n x n Wigner 矩陣的特徵值，那麼當n增長到無窮大時， f(a1) + ... + f(an) 將收斂到一個高斯分佈。但是，在這樣的中心 極限定理中，矩陣的元素需要具有相同的四階矩。 該項目的動機是研究大型網絡，如Facebook 裏的朋友網絡， 數學科學合作者網絡和學術論文通過引用連接起來的網絡。這里具有挑戰性的問題是將網絡的不同成員分組，即同組的成員會更多的相互聯絡。網絡數據直接指出來了成員之間的連接，但沒有觀察到羣組的結構； 而這個羣組的結構是我們要確定的（ 羣組鑑定）。請注意，任何網絡都可以用它的鄰接矩陣來刻劃；這個對稱矩陣的元素是 取值0和1的變量。實際上這樣的鄰接矩陣可以是個特殊的隨機Wigner矩陣；對其譜的研究為網絡結構分析帶來了許多強大的工具。特別是，人們可以用鄰接矩陣的線性譜統計量來檢查測試對網絡結構的各種假設。但是，此類鄰接矩陣有個特殊性， 即是它們的元素沒有共同的四階矩 。基於根我們之前在隨機矩陣理論中的研究，我們在此項目中提出建立一般Wigner線性譜統計的新中心極限定理；這裏的矩陣元素不需要具有相同的四階矩。這個理論一旦完成，可以直接用於解決大型網絡 中的羣組鑑定問題。 這種線性譜統計的據會有優勢超越已知文獻中的方法， 即是它們會對估計誤差更具魯棒性（robustness)。 因此，該項目將帶來創新和有前景的關於大型網絡的分析工具。

17307118.label: Realisation of objectives
17307118.value: Objectices Theme1: Our research group has made significant progress in achieving the objectives outlined in the original proposal for Project # 17307118. P17307118 focuses on understanding the abundance and composition of cadmium and mercury halide clusters, as well as their solvation and hydrogen-bonding properties, both in laboratory and natural enviroments. In particular, for objective T1, we have successfully characterized a wide range of cadmium halide clusters using ESI FT mass spectrometry. Our investigation included clusters with and without water solvation shells, as well as mono- and poly-nuclear cadmium halide species with varying numbers of water molecules in their hydration shell (the analysis of these CdCl clusters has provided quite valuable insights into the composition and abundance of these Cd clusters in aqueous media, which are also of great importance for the understanding of their role in volcanic water vapor). We have also complemented our FT mass spectrometry measurements with infrared multiple photon dissociation (IRMPD) spectroscopic studies at HKU and FELIX, NL. This technique has allowed us to examine the stretching and bending vibrations in the water shell surrounding CdCl+ ions, thus providing a deeper understanding of the hydrogen-bonded network in these solvated clusters. These experimental results have shed light on the position of specific vibrational frequencies for free and hydrogen-bonded stretching modes of H2O molecules solvating the cadmium chloride ion core, thereby addressing the second part of objective under T1. Our experimental work on cadmium chloride clusters has also been supported by state-of-the-art ab initio theoretical calculations using second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and density functional theory (DFT) methods. These calculations have been performed at the Hong Kong University's high-performance computing center HPC2016/2021, to which we have been granted access. The computational results have allowed us to predict individual IR stretching frequencies, the magnitude of the band shifts, and the nature of the solvent molecules giving rise to individual IR bands, as outlined in the third part of objective T1. These theoretical predictions have been instrumental in guiding our experimental work and interpreting our observations. The integration of experimental and theoretical approaches in our research has led to a comprehensive understanding of the cadmium halide clusters and their solvation properties. This work is currently being compiled and written up, with the aim of submitting a manuscript detailing our findings within the next 3 to 4 months. We believe that our study will make a significant contribution to the field of metal speciation in volcanic vapors, and will provide valuable insights for future research in this area, in particular, in the field or hydrothermal ore deposits. In summary, we believe that our group has successfully addressed the objectives outlined in the original proposal for Project # 17307118. We have employed a combination of experimental and theoretical techniques to characterize the abundance and composition of cadmium halide clusters, record their IRMPD spectra, and undertake ab initio calculations to determine the global minima structures for each cadmium ion cluster. Our work has provided valuable insights into the solvation and hydrogen-bonding properties of these clusters, which are essential for understanding their role in volcanic vapors. With the completion of our manuscript in the coming months, we will be ready to share our findings with the scientific community. Objectices Theme2: The second theme of Project # 17307118 focuses on mercury halide clusters, their structure, and spectroscopic properties. This part of the project has proven to be more challenging due to the difficulties encountered in isolating and measuring Hg clusters using FT mass spectrometry. Despite these challenges, our research group has made significant progress in characterizing the abundance and composition of mercury halide clusters through the application of electrospray ionization (ESI) mass spectrometry. Initially, we were able to mass isolate clusters such as Hg2Cl3+ and corresponding larger clusters. To address some of these challenges, we have initiated a short proposal in preparation for submission to FELIX in the Netherlands to re-probe hydrated clusters of the type Hg2Cl3+. Our group is quite proficient in dealing with such systems theoretically, using quantum chemical simulation techniques. To compensate for the shortcomings encountered with the IRMPD spectroscopic analysis of these clusters, we have reweighted some of our work and undertaken a more in-depth theoretical approach in analyzing the structure, energies, and spectroscopic properties of clusters such as HgCl+ and Hg2Cl3+, as well as larger species. We have conducted a detailed survey of the structures and energies of these clusters using density functional theory (DFT) and higher correlated techniques such as second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and coupled cluster with single, double, and triple excitations (CCSDT) theory. The second part of objective T2 aims to probe the hydrogen-bonding environment in water-solvated Hg clusters, such as Hg2Cl3+(H2O)n, using FT-MS mass isolation and IRMPD spectroscopy. Despite the experimental challenges, our theoretical work has allowed us to characterize the solvation shell structure and assign individual IR bands. This has provided valuable insights into the hydrogen-bonding environment and the propensity of H2O to bind to Hg and/or halide centers in mercury-chloride clusters. In the third part of objective T2, we have explored the capacity of these volatiles to establish a complete hydrogen bonding network around the mercury-halide ion core using quantum chemical methods. Our theoretical investigations have shed light on the nature of the hydrogen-bonded network and the factors that govern the stability and spectroscopic properties of these solvated mercury-halide clusters. Given the challenges faced in analyzing these mercury clusters, we anticipate that our work will be published in a geochemical (GCA) and physical chemistry (PCCP) journal within the next 9 to 12 months. In conclusion, despite the experimental difficulties, our research group has made significant progress in deepening our understanding of mercury halide clusters and their properties through a combination of experimental and theoretical approaches. This work will contribute to a better understanding of the role of heavy metals in volcanic vapors and provide valuable insights for future research in this area.

17307118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307118.value: Major findings and research outcomes for Theme 1: Our research group has successfully isolated and analyzed a broad range of cadmium chloride clusters using FT-MS due to the high mass accuracy of this technique. We discovered that water molecules preferentially attach to smaller Cd clusters with one and two cadmium atoms. The solvation shell around these smaller cadmium complexes and clusters usually contain between 1 to 5 water molecules. In the case of the mononuclear complex CdCl+, we mass-isolated this species in preparation for infrared spectroscopic dissociation at FELIX in the Netherlands and measured the infrared spectrum for the water molecule in the wave number range of 1600 to 3600 cm-1 (this work is currently in preparation for publication in PCCP) Due to the relatively weak interactions between subsequent water molecules, particularly for hydration numbers beyond three, we focused on the single water molecule attaching to the double ion complex CdCl+. This work is currently in preparation for publication and represents a significant breakthrough for our research group, as we were able to combine mass spectrometric and infrared spectroscopic work together with quantum chemical calculations for a geochemically important complex. Altogether, these techniques provide a robust and comprehensive picture of the interactions between small cadmium complexes and water molecules. In terms of larger cadmium chloride clusters, particularly those without water, we were able to easily mass-isolate these, however, we were unable to monitor the solvation shell in these clusters using infrared dissociation spectroscopy, mainly because the water molecules are weakly attached to these larger clusters. Major findings and research outcomes for Theme 2: The most significant finding in this part of the project was the challenge in mass spectrometrically analysing mercury chloride clusters. This challenge exists because the water solvation shell around these mercury halide clusters is less well developed than in the case of cadmium chloride. However, the major findings in this part of the work stem from a mixture of mass spectrometric studies that we conducted on the system and a very detailed computational study of the structure, charge distribution, spectroscopic and energetic properties of these mercury chloride clusters. This work was designed to compensate for some of the challenges that we faced when undertaking IRMPD spectroscopic studies of these clusters. Such challenges are not uncommon, particularly when exploring a system, such as mercury chloride, in more detail following some of our preliminary experiments that led up to the original proposal. These challenges can be compensated by relatively accurate spectroscopic calculations, particularly for the infrared spectroscopic properties of these systems. As a result, the major outcome of this work will be primarily theoretical. In other words, these results will be cast in the context of density functional and MP2 theory, providing a deeper understanding of the structure and affinity of water molecules to specifically sized mercury chloride clusters

17307118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307118.value: Project #17307118's results indicate further development in two main research themes: cadmium halide and mercury halide systems: in the case of cadmium halide, future studies could should focus on examining larger cadmium chloride clusters, exploring other cadmium halides (e.g., bromide, iodide), and investigating their geochemical potential and environmental implications, particularly in volcanic vapors and, somewjat overseen, the potential impacts on ecosystems and human health. For the mercury halide system, despite some experimental challenges that we faced in analyzing mercury halide clusters, progress in characterizing their abundance, composition, structure, and properties suggests further research strategies would be to explore experimental techniques to overcome difficulties in isolating and measuring mercury halide clusters using the FELIX FT mass spectrometry and IRMPD spectroscopy system, investigating other mercury halides (e.g., bromide, iodide) and exploring their role in atmospheric chemistry, especially in volcanic emissions.

17307118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307118.value: This research project focuses on examining 2 types of heavy metal clusters, i.e. cadmium halide and mercury halide clusters, which are well known play a significant role in volcanic vapors and are therefore of heightened interest to Earth scientists working on hydrothermal ore deposits. By studying these type of clusters, we aim to deepen our understanding of their properties and interactions with water molecules, which can help us better comprehend their potential environmental and health impacts. In Theme 1, we successfully analyzed and characterized various cadmium halide clusters using advanced techniques such as FT mass spectrometry and infrared dissociation spectroscopy. This allowed us to gain new insights into the solvation properties of these complexes, which is essential in understanding their role in volcanic emissions and fumarolic gases. In Theme 2, we measured the mass spectra of mercury halide clusters, and made significant progress by employing theoretical methods to study their molecular configuration and spectroscopic properties, upon interaction with water molecules. This novel approach has provided us with new critical information on the hydrogen-bonding environment within these clusters, and their potential involvement during the vapor phase transport and deposition of this economically important metals

17307218.label: Project Objectives
17307218.value: To develop estimation and clustering procedures for grouping the continuously monitored blood pressure curves whiling taking into account the outcome information. The semiparametric efficient estimating equation will be used for the parameter estimation. The clustering step will apply the k-means centering algorithm introduced in Chiou and Li (2007). The goal is to develop a method that will yield clustering labels that are consistent with the patients’ outcomes. Further, we will study whether including the patients’ outcomes improves the clustering efficiency. To develop a multi-scale change point detection method to identify the change points in the blood pressure curves. We will use the Haar wavelet to transform the blood pressure sequence in different scales. The multi-scale procedure allows us to evaluate the blood pressure changes in different resolutions. Further, the non-local priors help to reduce the false discovery of the change points. We will introduce a complete multi-scale Bayesian framework for the change point detection, including identification, post-processing, and selection of the optimal number of change points. The procedure can be used in the early prevention of the stroke onset. To develop a censored regression model between the stroke recurrent survival time and the continuous monitored blood pressure. The blood pressure curves are measured with missing segments. We propose to impute the missing segments through the B-spline method. After the imputation, the resulting curves are contaminated by the imputation errors. Hence, we propose an estimation under the measurement error model. The procedure will be used to identify the patients with high risk of stroke recurrence and adjust the medicare plan according.

17307218.value: 中风是全球死亡的主要原因 - 包括中国 - 并且高血压已被确认为关键风险因素，导致全球约一半的中风。在美国，欧洲和日本，连续血压监测已被证明可有效控制高血压，但中国的研究受到限制。 BOSS（短暂性脑缺血发作或缺血性卒中的血压和临床结果）是一项基于医院的前瞻性队列研究，旨在评估缺血性卒中/短暂性脑缺血发作患者持续监测的血压和临床结果。持续监测血压和临床结果为本项目的分析提供。 拟议的项目有三个主要目标：（i）聚集血压曲线，（ii）确定血压的变化，以及（iii）检查卒中复发与血压轨迹之间的关系。为了实现第一个目标，我们将开发响应辅助聚类方法，该方法将在考虑结果信息的同时执行功能聚类。为了实现第二个目标，我们将构建一个多尺度贝叶斯变换点检测框架，该框架将评估不同分辨率下的功能曲线，并能有效地控制错误发现率。为了实现第三个目标，我们提出了一种插补方法，然后进行删失分位数回归，以评估血压对卒中复发时间的影响。我们将推导出三种方法的渐近性质，包括估计，聚类一致性和估计的渐近正态性。将进行数值实验以评估所提出的方法，并且用这些方法分析BOSS数据。该方法可以扩展到分析其他合作项目中的数据，例如磁共振成像引导的放射治疗数据和遗留女孩数据。

17307318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307318.value: Clinical trials in cancer new drug development are becoming much more complicated due to onerous procedures and strict regulations as well as prohibitive expenditures of time and cost. To expedite drug development and enhance precision medicine, we propose three novel statistical designs for early-phase clinical trials, which make the study design and trial conduct more efficient, flexible, and ethical. First, we will modify the nonparametric overdose control design by introducing two new models for trial early stopping due to under- or over-dosing and developing a new sampling scheme for ordered uniform random variables. We further adopt the bootstrap aggregating ensemble method to boost the estimation of the order in the two-dimensional drug combination space. Second, we propose a new dose-finding method for cytostatic agents in phase I/II trials. Targeted agents utilize novel biomarkers to identify patients who are most likely to benefit from certain treatment and thus patients can be treated with individually tailored medicine. These types of agents are cytostatic and generally tolerable, and finding the dose with the highest efficacy level is the primary objective. However, most of the dose-finding methods in the literature are for cytotoxic agents, such as chemotherapies, and there is a lack of statistical methods for cytostatic agents. We construct curve-free models for both toxicity and efficacy and introduce correlations through latent variables, and dose finding is cast in a Bayesian model selection framework. Our proposal is robust as it does not utilize any parametric modeling structures and the latent Student t distributions have heavy tails than the commonly used normal distribution in probit models. Third, we will investigate basket trials by developing a two-stage trial design with futility stopping and homogeneity testing at the interim stage for one drug but with multiple biomarkers. In addition, we will explore the case with multiple drugs and multiple biomarkers, and apply adaptive randomization to enhance trials’ ethics by assigning more patients to better treatment arms. 在癌症新藥的研究領域，臨床試驗由於其手續繁瑣、監管嚴格、 耗時耗資巨大，因而其執行越來越複雜。為了加快新藥研發的 進程、提升精準藥物療法的準確度，我們提出三種新型的早期 臨床試驗的統計設計方法，其能夠令試驗研究更加靈活有效且 符合道德倫理。首先，我們對控制過高劑量的非參數方法進行 修正，提出一種新的針對均勻分佈的有序隨機變量的抽樣方法， 并引入兩種新的模型分別用於在劑量過高與過低的情況下提前 終止試驗。此外，我們通過抽樣聚集方法，提高二維劑量探尋 空間的估計準確度。其次，我們提出一種新的針對一期二期臨 床試驗下非細胞毒性藥物的劑量探尋方法，靶向藥物通過生物 標記來確認最有可能受益于某個療法的病人群體，這種靶向藥 物往往細胞毒性較弱，能夠被病人承受，因此尋找該類藥物最 具療效的劑量等級是其臨床試驗的首要目標。然而，現有的大 多數劑量探尋方法主要針對于細胞毒性類藥物，針對於非細胞 毒性藥物的劑量探尋研究則較少。我們構建一種不依賴于參數 曲線的模型，用來刻畫毒性與有效性之間的關係，并通過引入 潛變量來對兩者之間的相關性進行建模，劑量探尋的過程則基 於貝葉斯模型選擇的框架。我們提出的模型具有穩健性，不依 賴于任何參數型的模型假設，而且潛變量服從t分佈，與通常的 正態分佈模型相比，t分佈具有厚尾的特征。第三，我們對具有 多種生物標記的單一藥物的籃型試驗進行研究，提出一種二階 段的設計，該設計在中期檢驗包含了無效性停止界限，并能夠 檢測多個藥物之間的同質性。此外，我們進一步研究當多個藥 物存在多種生物標記的情況，并通過適應性隨機化機制将更多 的病人分配至更有效的療法組中，以令試驗更符合倫理道德層 面的考慮。

17307318.value: We developed new dose-finding methods for drug-combination trials, including the dynamic ordering design and non-parametric overdose control design. Both methods are efficient and can identify the maximum tolerated dose accurately. We also proposed subgroup analysis in censored linear regression which can identify a particular subpopulation with biomarker expression that is more susceptible to treatment. In related machine learning research, we developed the Delaunay triangulation learner which is shown to be superior to decision trees or random forest in classification and regression analysis.

17307318.value: The Delaunay triangulation learner can be further extended to two-layer crystalization learning that can overcome the computational challenge in high-dimensional cases for which the Delaunay triangulation is computationally costly.

17307418.label: Realisation of objectives
17307418.value: Dr. Kwan-Ming Ng was the original PI when the project began in August 2018. In August 2019, Dr. Ng left HKU to take up the post of Professor at the Department of Chemistry of Shantou University, and Dr. Ho Yu Au-Yeung, has kindly agreed to take up the role of PI of the project. Nevertheless, Dr. Ng was appointed as an Honorary Assistant Professor of the Department of Chemistry of HKU and became a co-investigator of this project to work closely with Dr. Au-Yeung to complete this project. All stated objectives have been achieved, including publication of six research articles and delivery of one presentation at an international conference. The important findings are summarized below: Objective 1: Different types of antibodies-conjugated spherical gold and silver nanoparticles (with diameter from 20 to 80 nm) have been successfully prepared via coupling of N-hydroxysuccinimide activated gold nanoparticles (NHS-PEG-AuNPs) and N-hydroxysuccinimide activated silver nanoparticles (NHS-PEG- AgNPs) with the antibodies, including anti-β-hCG, anti-PML, anti-mouse IgG and anti-rabbit IgG. Moreover, a seed-mediated approach followed by a successive growing method was successfully adopted to synthesize 20nm gold nanoparticles for the surface functionalization with different ratios of antibodies and PEG ligands to compromise specific versus non-specific interaction. The synthesized antibodies-conjugated nanoparticles were characterized using UV-visible spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), gel electrophoresis, and dynamic light scattering. The data have been published in Analytica Chimica Acta (2019, 1055, 1-6). In addition to that, four different types of gold@metal sulfide nanoparticles, including AuNP@PdS, AuNP@AgS, AuNP@ZnS and AuNP@CdS nanoparticles have also been successfully synthesized. The size and morphology of the synthesized gold@metal sulfide nanoparticles were examined using a transmission electron microscope. The size of the AuNP core was characterized to be 20.6 ± 0.6nm while the shell was 8.3 ± 2.5nm for Ag2S, 7.1 ± 1.6nm for CdS, 6.4 ± 2.5nm for ZnS, and 5.6 ± 2.1nm for PbS. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy was used to analyze the elemental composition of the NPs. The cation exchange efficiency (%mole cation : (%mole Ag+%mole cation)) from Au@Ag2S to Au@CdS, Au@ZnS, and Au@PbS NPs was measured to be 95%, 90%, and 80% respectively. The effect of these gold@metal sulfide nanoparticles on the desorption and ionization efficiency has been studied and the results are published in Analytical Chemistry (2020, 92, 10262-10267). Objective 2: Different experimental conditions, including GOPTS derivatization time and glass drying temperature, have been optimized for the preparation of antibody array to maximize the density of capturing antibodies to enhance the detection sensitivity of the method. Moreover, the effect of different sizes (20 to 80nm) of gold nanoparticles and silver nanoparticles on the detection sensitivity of immune-capture laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry for analysis of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) hormone has been systematically investigated. Increasing the size of the nanoparticles not only increases the detection sensitivity but also lowers the detection limits. Moreover, for the comparable particle size (80nm), the sensitivity of AgNPs is 9 times higher than that of AuNPs. The data has been published in Analytica Chimica Acta (2019, 1055, 1-6), Chemical Communications (2019, 55, 2761-2764), and Analyst (2020, 145, 6237-6242). Moreover, we developed a facile means to optimize antibody-conjugated gold nanoparticles for molecular biomarker analysis. Surfaces of gold nanoparticles were modified via PEGylation using different ratios of (i) antibody-capped and (ii) carboxylate-capped PEG in solution to provide both functionalization and stabilization of the nanoparticles in biological media. By varying the ratio between carboxylate-PEG and antibody-PEG, up to 7 times improvement in the performance was observed by reducing non-specific bindings, i.e. noise, whilst retaining sufficient sensitivity, ultimately achieving a detection limit down to 35 amol. The optimized gold nanoparticles mass tags were applied to detect HPV18E7 in HeLa cell lysate. The result is published in Analyst (2020, 145, 6237-6242). Objective 3: The optimized antibodies-conjugated gold nanoparticles and silver nanoparticles have been applied to the detection of protein markers in different complex biological samples. For instance, using antibody-conjugated AuNPs, the detection limit of hCG hormone in urine by SALDI-MS could be as low as 5 attomole, which was significantly lower than that achieved by conventional fluorescence detection (i.e. 75 femtomoles). This result indicated antibodies-conjugated AuNPs with SALDI-MS could be applied to improve common diagnostic screening tests. Apart from biological fluids, we have also developed the detection of protein markers in cancer cell lysates, especially those that could not be easily detected by conventional fluorescence detection, which could benefit the early screening and treatment of cancers. Detection of HPV18E7 marker protein (14kDa) in HeLa cell lysate was achieved down to low attomole level, which was 2 orders of magnitude lower than conventional fluorescence detection (Analyst, 2020, 145, 6237-6242). Detection of high molecular weight PML-RARA fusion protein (120 kDa) in NB4 leukemia cell lysate was also developed, which could be useful for screening and monitoring of cancer, and previously could not be achieved by conventional Western Blot Assay with chemiluminescence. Moreover, the antibodies-conjugated gold nanoparticles and silver nanoparticles could be utilized for the duplex imaging of high molecular weight proteins, megalin (522 kDa) and podocin (42 kDa), in rat kidney tissue. Our results revealed that plasmonic AuNPs conjugated with antibodies allow indirect detection of trace proteins in complex biological matrices, which could not be achieved by conventional MALDI-MS detection, fluorescence detection, or Western blotting method. Overall, we have demonstrated that plasmonic AuNPs can be utilized as a multifaceted probe for direct chromogenic imaging (i.e. characteristic red/blue color due to the plasmonic absorption band), enhanced fluorescence (i.e. plasmon-enhanced fluorescence for neighbouring fluorophores) and strong MS ion intensity for biological tissue imaging. The results have been published in Analytica Chimica Acta (2019, 1055, 1-6) and Chem. Commun. (2019, 55, 2761-2764).

Ultrasensitive detection of protein markers in complex biological samples has been achieved, including urine, cancer cell lysate, and animal tissue samples. An attomole level detection sensitivity can be achieved by this method which is 2 orders of magnitude lower than conventional fluorescence detection. 2. A facile method has been developed to optimize antibody-conjugated gold nanoparticles for molecular biomarker analysis. By conjugating the gold nanoparticles with an optimal ratio of antibodies and stabilizing ligands, non-specific bindings to biological samples can be significantly reduced. The signal-to-noise ratio was increased 7 times and ultimately achieved a detection limit down to 35 attomoles of protein. 3. Silver nanoparticles can also be used as the mass spectrometric reporting group for protein detection in laser ionization mass spectrometry. With comparable particle sizes, silver nanoparticles can provide a 9-time higher sensitivity than gold nanoparticles. 4. On top of providing mass spectrometry signal readout in laser ionization mass spectrometry, the plasmonic gold nanoparticle has been successfully developed as a multifaceted probe for tissue imaging, providing optical, electron microscopic, and enhanced fluorescence signal readouts. 5. The above major findings and research outcomes have been published in the leading international chemistry journals, including Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Communications, Analytica Chimica Acta, Analyst, Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry. Two research articles have been selected as front covers. One presentation has been made at an international conference.

17307418.value: With the high sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio, the laser ionization mass spectrometry method can be applied for clinical samples analysis for disease diagnosis.

17307418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307418.value: Attributed to the low ionization efficiency of macromolecules, single protein biomarker detection remains challenging for mass spectrometry, although scientists have invested great effort into maximizing the efficiency of various ionization methods, optimizing ion optics for better ion collection and transmission efficiency. In this project, the “dual-functional” antibodies-conjugated noble metal NPs has been developed and applied for (i) specific capturing of target proteins; and (ii) generation of reporter metal ions to amplify ion signals for mass spectrometric detection. Our study successfully applied antibodies-conjugated AuNPs and AgNPs to develop a sandwich-type immunoassay for attomole-level biomarker detection in tissue sections, urine samples and cell lysates, which could not be achieved by most analytical techniques. Moreover, the method can be applied to image spatial distribution of high-mass proteins (~ 500kDa) in animal tissues which cannot be detected using standard MALDI-MS method. The mechanisms behind laser desorption ionization has also been studied, aiming at developing a more effective nanoparticle for amplifying ion signals for mass spectrometric detection and achieve single protein detection, which is important for proteomic studies and early disease diagnosis. These findings have been published in international journals including Analytical Chemistry, Chemical Communications, Analytica Chimica Acta, Analyst, and Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry.

17307518.value: In the general field of organic synthesis the use of organic molecules to catalyze reactions has emerged as a powerful method for complex molecule synthesis, and numerous classes of such organocatalysts have been developed for use in a wide range of organic reactions. In the proposed research project we aim to expand the utility of organocatalysis by examining the use of organic halides to activate substrates through halogen bonding in order to determine the scope of reactions such halogen bond catalysis is applicable in. Additionally, we plan to study the use chiral halogen bonding catalysts in order to attempt to develop the first examples of highly enantioselective halogen bond catalysis. 17307518.label: Realisation of objectives
17307518.value: Numerous organic halides, including some self-supported ones, were synthesized and used as organocatalysts in transformations such as immine formation, Diels-Alder reactions, Povarov reactions, Mannich reactions, Friedel-Crafts reactions and various tandem processes. We chose to synthesize and study racemic examples of axial chiral organic halides based on a 2,2'-bipyridal platform to study the effectiveness of this architecture in organocatalysis before devoting resources to the preparation of chiral (enantioenriched) versions. While these non-enantioselective studies were successful, we did not have an opportunity to move on to the analogous enantioselective versions.

17307618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307618.value: Pulsars are rapidly spinning, highly magnetized neutron stars created in the deaths of massive stars. Since their 1967 discovery (1974 Physics Nobel Prize), >2600 pulsars have been detected, across the electromagnetic spectrum. In addition to being interesting in their own right, pulsars are excellent tools to study physical phenomena in extreme environments; the (indirect) detection of gravitational waves (1993 Physics Nobel Prize) being probably the most famous such example. Recent advances in gamma-ray astronomy have provided a renewed impetus to pulsar research. Explaining the high-energy emission is critical to understanding the pulsar mechanism, since pulsars convert a significant fraction of their rotational kinetic energy into gamma-ray photons. The Large Area Telescope (LAT), on the Fermi satellite, has been scanning the >100 MeV gamma-ray sky since 2008, detecting >200 gamma-ray pulsars (compared to < 10 previously known). These span a broad parameter space and, surprisingly, about half of them are millisecond pulsars (MSPs), very old systems spinning with periods shorter than 10 ms. Most gamma-ray pulsars have energy spectra that peak in 1-10 GeV range and exponentially drop off. Two pulsars, however, have been detected at energies exceeding 100 GeV. Above 50 GeV, the limited collecting area of the LAT (~1m^2), hampers its sensitivity. Fortunately, at such high energies, ground-based observations become viable. The Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov (MAGIC) telescopes, the world’s most sensitive in the 50-100 GeV range, first reported the detection of >25 GeV pulsed emission from the Crab in 2008, recently extending its detection up to TeV energies, something completely unexpected and challenging to explain with standard models. We propose using Fermi and MAGIC observations of three MSPs to probe the highest-energy emission from these systems, so far never detected above 100 GeV. Our targets are carefully chosen, based on empirical and theoretical grounds, as well as their locations in the sky. We aim to address some key questions: Can MSPs emit photons above 100 GeV, like some of their younger counterparts (e.g. Crab and Vela)? What mechanism can explain this emission? How does it relate to the lower-energy keV–GeV emission? In the event of non-detections, we will establish, via simulations, upper limits for individual systems and the MSP population as a whole. In the case of detections, we will explore their usefulness to probe fundamental physics questions, such as Lorentz invariance violation. Our results will also guide future pulsar observations with next-generation instruments like CTA. 脈衝星高速旋轉，這種高度磁化的中子星是在大質量恆星的消亡中產生。自1967年發現以來（1974年諾貝爾物理學獎），已有> 2600個脈衝星在電磁波譜中被檢測到。除了自身有趣之外，脈衝星還是研究極端環境中物理現象的絕佳工具; （間接）探測引力波（1993年諾貝爾物理學獎）可能是最著名的例子。伽馬射線天文學的最新進展為脈衝星研究提供了新的動力。解釋高能發射對於理解脈衝星機制至關重要，因為脈衝星將其旋轉動能的很大一部分轉換成伽馬射線光子。 費米衛星上的大面積望遠鏡（LAT）自2008年以來一直在掃描> 100 MeV的伽馬射線天空，已探測到> 200個伽馬射線脈衝星（相比之前只知道少數幾個）。它們具有廣泛的參數空間：年輕，毫秒脈衝星，無線電靜音等。大多數伽馬射線脈衝星具有光譜峰值，且在1-10 GeV範圍內指數切斷。然而，現有兩個脈衝星已被檢測到能量超過100 GeV！若能量高於50 GeV，LAT的有限收集區域（~1平方公尺）會阻礙它的靈敏度。幸運的是，地面基礎觀察在如此高能量下變得可行。主要的大氣伽瑪成像Cherenkov（MAGIC）望遠鏡是世界上50-100 GeV範圍內最敏感的望遠鏡，它首次報告了2008年從Crab發現的> 25 GeV脈衝發射，最近其檢測擴展至高達TeV能量，完全出乎意料且難以用標準模型解釋。 我們建議使用費米和MAGIC觀測伽馬射線脈衝星（年輕及毫秒脈衝星）來探測這些系統的最高能量發射。我們的探測目標是根據它們在天空中的特徵和位置而精心挑選的：所有這些目標都在LAT的25 GeV以上，並且可由MAGIC觀察到。我們的目標是解決一些關鍵問題：其他脈衝星（除了Crab和Vela）輻射量是否會發出超過100 GeV？ 毫秒脈衝星是否以這些能量輻射？什麼機制可以解釋這種輻射？它與低能量keV-GeV輻射有何關係？在未檢測到的情況下，我們將通過模擬確定單個對象和群體的上限。在已檢測到的情況下，我們將探索它們用於探測基本物理問題的有效性，例如洛倫茲不變性違規。我們的結果還將指導未來脈衝星觀測與下一代儀器如CTA。

17307618.value: We analyzed 11.5 years of Fermi LAT data, carrying out a spectral analysis, as well as a pulsar timing analysis, obtaining a pulse profile for our pulsar of interest, contemporaneous with our MAGIC observations. We obtained ~100 hours of MAGIC data on PSR J0218+4232 and carried out two independent analyses, both a spectral analysis, and a search for pulsations above 100 GeV. We performed broadband modelling of PSR J0218+4232, using all available data, from X-ray to GeV and TeV gamma rays, and interpreted the results using two theoretical models (one led by Co-I Diego Torres, the other led by co-I Alice Harding). We published our results in a refereed journal article, in The Astrophysical Journal (Volume 922, Issue 2, id.251, 14 pp. Pub Date: December 2021)

17307618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307618.value: Despite PSR J0218+4232 being one of the most energetic millisecond pulsars known, we have shown that its high-energy emission extends only up to about 25 GeV. Despite a deep observation with MAGIC, no emission is found above 100 GeV.

17307618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307618.value: Although MSPs like J0218+4232 appear challenging for MAGIC, the future Cherenkov Telescope Array is expected to have significantly better sensitivity than MAGIC in the 10?100 GeV range, and this and other pulsars will thus be prime targets for observation. In addition, pulsars like J0218 are also good sources for MeV telescopes, such as the All-sky Medium Energy Gamma-ray Observatory that can detect the predicted peaks around 1?10 MeV.

17307618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307618.value: Since their discovery, in 1967, pulsars have continued to fascinate physicists due to their extreme properties (spin periods, magnetic fields, surface gravity). In the last 15 years, the number of pulsars known to emit gamma rays has increased from only a few to several hundred. Some pulsars have even been detected at energies above 100 GeV. However, only "young" pulsars have so far shown emission up to these high energies. In this project, we used the most sensitive ground-based Gamma-ray telescope to search for pulsed emission from an "old" millisecond pulsar, PSR J0218+4232. In combination with satellite observations from Fermi-LAT, we concluded that the highest energies reached by this pulsar are ~25 GeV, setting important constraints on the acceleration mechanism for such systems. Future, more sensitive, ground-based telescopes will be needed to explore this and other pulsars at such high energies.

17307718.value: PI建议探讨Poisson-Ore 延拓的一些基本问题. 其中包括基本定义, Lie理论中的例子, 以及Poisson-Ore结构的分部突变. 这将是第一个系统地统一地研究此类问题的项目. 该项目与代数几何，表示理论，代数和组合密切相关。

17307718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307718.value: We have shown that a large class of Poisson varieties from Lie theory, such as Bott-Samelson varieties, flag varieties and certain sub-varieties of twisted products of flag varieties admit Bott-Samelson atlases and are thus Poisson-Ore varieties with compatible totally positive structures. Such varieties also carry closely related groupoid structures. Objective 2 has been carried out but final results have not been written up. Partial results on Objectives 3 and 4 have been published in the paper "Bott–Samelson atlases, total positivity, and Poisson structures on some homogeneous spaces" in Selecta. One more manuscript has been written up, but due to re-organization, that manuscript will be submitted after another paper which contains more background investigation and will also open up new directions based on the currect project.

17307718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307718.value: The research outcome of the project leads directly to a future study of cluster sub-varieties of cluster varieties via Poisson geometry.

17307718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307718.value: A Poisson-Ore variety is a Poisson variety covered by coordinate charts parametrized by affine spaces, in which the Poisson structure has the special property of being an iterated Poisson-Ore extensions. Together with former students, PI has successfully identified and examined several examples from Lie theory, which will lead to further studies on cluster sub-varieties and cluster covers.
