17307918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307918.value: Recent studies have shown that most East Asian blocks (North China, South China, Tarim, Qaidam, Indochina, Sibumasu, Qiangtang, Lhasa, etc) were once part of Gondwana during end-Neoproterozoic to Early Paleozoic time, but controversy has surrounded the time of collision of these East Asian blocks with the northern margin of Gondwana, and their paleo-geographic reconstructions in Gondwana. Sedimentary provenance analysis of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata from major blocks in East Asia can provide important insights into resolving the above issues. As one of major blocks in East Asia, the Tarim Block was widely exposed with Neoproterozoic and Early Paleozoic sedimentary strata on its southern margin, which are ideal targets for sedimentary provenance analysis. This proposal focuses on the Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic sedimentary strata in the Tiekelike and Altyn-Tagh areas at the southwestern and southeastern margins of Tarim, respectively, and plans to carry out systematic sedimentological investigations and detailed detrital zircon provenance analysis on these sedimentary rocks. The whole-rock geochemistry and modal detrital content will be investigated in order to infer the tectonic settings of these Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata. Paleocurrent direction data will be collected from the field and are combined with U-Pb dating results of detrital zircons in order to constrain the time of provenance transition. The hafnium (Hf) and oxygen (O) isotopes of zircons will be determined and linked to age data to reveal subduction and accretion processes. Through a comprehensive comparison with detrital zircon data from other components (e.g. Australia, India, etc) of Gondwana and combined with available magmatic, metamorphic and structural data, this project is aimed to constrain the paleogeographic-position of Tarim with respect to Gondwana and their amalgamation time in the Early Paleozoic. The results of this project will provide new insights into the reconstruction of East Asian blocks in Gondwana. 最近的研究表明大多数东亚陆块（华北、华南、塔里木、柴达木、印度支那、滇缅泰、羌塘、拉萨等）在晚元古代末至早古生代曾经是冈瓦纳大陆的一部分，但有关这些陆块在冈瓦纳北缘的位置以及古地理重建却存在争论。这些东亚陆块上的晚元古代至古生代沉积物物源分析可以为解决上述争论提供依据。作为东亚主要陆块之一的塔里木陆块的南缘出露大量的晚元古代至古生代沉积岩，因而成为物源分析的理想靶区。本项目集中对塔里木陆块的东南缘和西南缘铁克里克和阿尔金地区所出露的晚元古代至古生代沉积地层开展系统的沉积岩石学研究和详细的碎屑锆石物源分析，同时通过全岩地球化学分析和碎屑物含量去探讨该区晚元古代至古生代沉积地层形成的大地构造环境。此外，通过野外斜层理和波痕确定古水流方向，并结合碎屑锆石U-Pb年龄限定物源转换时间。锆石的铪（Hf）和氧（O）同位素将用来揭示陆块俯冲和增生过程。通过与冈瓦纳大陆上其它陆块（如澳大利亚，印度等）碎屑锆石数据综合对比并结合已有的岩浆、变质和构造数据来限定塔里木陆块在冈瓦纳大陆上的古地理位置和古生代的拼合时间。该项目研究结果将对东亚陆块在冈瓦纳大陆上的重建提供重要限制。

17307918.label: Realisation of objectives
17307918.value: We have successfully completed all seven objectives designed for this project as follows: Objective 1 is to determine the spatial distribution and relationships of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Block. This objective was completed by three times of fieldwork that was carried out on 27 July-26 August 2019, 1-19 August 2020; 19 August 19-27 September 2021, of which the first and second fieldwork was focused in the Altyn-Tagh area at the southeastern margin, and the third fieldwork was focused in the Tiekelike area at the southwestern margin of the Tarim Craton, where Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata are widely exposed. In these areas, we did large-scale (1:50000) mapping through which we have determined the spatial distribution and relationships of different Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic sedimentary sequences. The results were shown in Figures 1 and/or 2 of Publication Nos. 1-2, 4-6, 8, 10 and 16-18 (see Part C). In the field, we have totally collected 1028 samples for further petrographic, structural, whole-rock geochemical and zircon U-Pb age dating and Hf isotopic studies. Objective 2 is to determine the nature of the major structural episodes at the southern margin of the Tarim craton. This objective was completed by detailed structural investigations in the Altyn-Tagh area at the southeastern margin and the Tiekelike area at the southwestern margin of the Tarim Craton. In the field, we took statistics and measurements of various foliations, lineation and various senses of thrusting and shearing by which we identified three episodes of deformation (D1 to D3) of which D1 is represented by small isoclinal and recumbent folds, D2 produced large-scale asymmetric folds and an associated penetrative axial planar foliation, a mineral stretching lineation and regional-scale ductile shear zones, and D3 is indicated by open to tight folds of varying scales, axial crenulation cleavages and EW-striking thrust faults, involving broadly N-S compression. Combined with the results of Objective 3, the results of this objective will be published in a paper entitled “Reconstructions of polyphase deformation and paleocurrent direction of Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Block and tectonic implications”, authored by Peng Wang, Guochun Zhao (corresponding author), Jian Zhang, Yigui Han and Jinlong Yao (submitted to Sedimentary Geology). Objective 3 is to restore the paleocurrent direction and it was completed by studying asymmetry wave ripples, oblique beddings and cross beddings of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata in the Altyn-Tagh area at the southeastern margin and the Tiekelike area at the southwestern margin of the Tarim Craton, on the basis of eliminating structural effects in the field. Our results show that the paleocurrents along the southeastern margin and the southwestern margin of the Tarim craton were mostly northward before Early Devonian but changed to southward direction after the Early Devonian. The tectonic implication of such a paleocurrent direction shift has been discussed in a paper entitled “Reconstructions of polyphase deformation and paleocurrent direction of Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton and tectonic implications”, which has been just completed by Peng Wang, Guochun Zhao (corresponding author), Jian Zhang, Yigui Han and Jinlong Yao and submitted to Sedimentary Geology. Objective 4 is to discriminate the tectonic settings of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata in the Tiekelike and Altyn-Tagh areas. This objective was completed by studying detrital components of sandstones combined with whole-rock geochemical analysis. During the fieldwork that was carried out on 27 July-26 August 2019, 1-19 August 2020; 19 August 19-27 September 2021, we have collected 620 geochemical samples, of which 286 samples were finally selected for whole-rock analysis. The results of our study suggest that the southern margin of the Tarim craton represented an active continental margin arc during Neoproterozoic and Early Paleozoic times but changed to a passive continental margin since the Late Silurian when the southern margin of the Tarim Craton collided with the northern margin of Gondwana. The research outcomes of this objective have been reflected in Publication Nos. 1-2, 6, 10, 11 and 16-18 as listed in Part C. Objective 5 is to constrain the age of the provenance transition based on U-Pb dating results of detrital zircons combined with paleocurrent direction data. We completed this objective by utilizing the SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating techniques to determine U-Pb ages and εHf values of detrital zircons from the bottom to top sequences of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton. During the fieldwork, we have collected 280 samples from the Tiekelike and Altyn-Tagh areas for SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating. Our results indicate that detrital zircon grains from Neoproterozoic–Silurian strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton display two dominant populations at 950–750 and 550–450 Ma, both of which lag two global peaks at 1200–1000 and 650–500 Ma, respectively, most likely reflecting the Rodinia and Gondwana assembly. The results of this Objective have been highlighted in Publication Nos. 2, 6 and 11 in Part C. Objective 6 is to reveal subduction and accretion processes at depth via zircon hafnium (Hf) isotopes linked to age data. We completed this objective by analyzing hafnium (Hf) isotope on detrital zircon grains that have been done for SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating. Our results demonstrate that in the Neoproterozoic and Early Paleozoic strata at the southern magin of Tarim, the εHf(t) values of detrital zircons with two prominent peaks at 950–750 and 550–450 Ma range from − 20 to 10 and 12 to 5, respectively. Considering the 487 ± 7 Ma andesitic lava sample with εHf(t) values clustering 10 to 15 forming during retreating subduction, we proposed that the northward subduction of the Proto-Tethys oceanic lithosphere must have occurred at some time prior to 487 ± 7 Ma. The results of this objective have been reflected in Publications Nos. 2 and 11 in Part C. Objective 7 is to determine the paleogeographic position of the Tarim Block with respect to Gondwana and their amalgamation time in the Early Paleozoic. We have completed this objective through a comprehensive comparison with detrital zircon data from other components of Gondwana, combined with available magmatic, metamorphic and structural data. Our results indicate that detrital zircons from Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton are characterized by two prominent peaks at 950–750 and 550–450 Ma, with εHf(t) values ranging from − 20 to 10 and 12 to 5, respectively, which largely match two prominent peaks at 1000–800 and 600–490 Ma with εHf(t) values ranging from − 20 to 10 and − 15 to 5 from Neoproterozoic-Ordovician strata in North India, but are not consistent with those of other continental fragments such as West Australia and Arabia-Iran, etc. This led us to have proposed a close linkage of South Tarim and North India in Gondwana. The results of this Objective have been published in Geology (2022, v. 50, p. 131–136), Nature Communications (2021, v. 12, 4189) and Tectonophysics (2021, v. 803, 228741) (see Publications 1-2 and 11 in Part C).

17307918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307918.value: More and more evidence indicates that most continents in East Asia were added to the northern margin of Gondwana with the closure of the Proto-Tethys Ocean in the Early Paleozoic. However, it still remains unknown or controversial about when and where these East Asian blocks collided with the northern margin of Gondwana. This is particularly the case with the Tarim Craton that still remains as one of the poorly understood continental blocks in East Asia in terms of its Neoproterozoic and Early Paleozoic paleo-geographic position and its relationship with Gondwana. This formed the justification for this project in which we have carried out systematic sedimentological investigations and detailed detrital zircon provenance analysis on Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic sedimentary strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton, and produced large amounts of new data and interpretations as reflected in 20 refereed papers that we published in leading international journals including Nature Communications, Geology, Tectonics, GSA Bulletin, American Journal of Science, etc (see Publications listed in Part C). We summarize our major findings and research outcomes as follows: 1. We demonstrated that the southern margin of the Tarim Craton represented an active continental margin developed by northward subduction of the Proto-Tethys Ocean during Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic times, and finally collided with the northern margin of Gondwana at 500-460 Ma (See Publication Nos. 1-2, 6, 10, 11 and 16-18 as listed in Part C). 2. Our results show that the paleocurrents along the southern margin of the Tarim craton were mostly northward before Early Devonian but changed to southward direction after the Early Devonian. 3. Our study have recognized two prominent age peaks at 950–750 Ma and 550–450 Ma from detrital zircons of Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton, which remarkably match two prominent peaks (1000–800 and 600–490 Ma) recognized from Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic strata at North India, but are inconsistent with those of other continental fragments in the northern margin of Gondwana such as West Australia and Arabia-Iran, etc. (See Publication Nos. 1-2 and 11 in Part C). 4. Through a comprehensive comparison with detrital zircon U-Pb age and Hf data from other components of Gondwana and combined with available magmatic, metamorphic and structural data, we have proposed a close linkage of South Tarim and North India in Gondwana (See Publication Nos. 1-2 and 11 in Part C).

17307918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307918.value: Our results from this project confirm that the southern margin of the Tarim Craton represented an active continental margin developed by northward subduction of the Proto-Tethys Ocean during Neoproterozoic and early Paleozoic times, and finally collided with North India in the northern margin of Gondwana at 500-460 Ma. Whether or not our model established in this project can be tested with paleomagnetic data for Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic rocks at the southern margin of the Tarim Craton and age-similar rocks from the northern margin of the Indian Block. In future, we plan to apply for a Hong Kong RGC GRF project entitled “Paleomagnetic study on the Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic rocks from the Tarim and Indian blocks”.

17307918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307918.value: Gondwana is a large landmass that was traditionally considered to be assembled by South America, Africa, Australia, Antarctica and India about 650-530 million years (Ma) ago, and more and more evidence indicates that most East Asian continental blocks were welded to the northern margin of Gondwana with the closure of an old ocean (Proto-Tethys Ocean) around 500-460 Ma ago. However, there is a hot debate regarding issues of when and where these blocks were added to the northern margin of Gondwana. This is particularly the case with the Tarim Block in terms of its relationship to Gondwana. To resolve these issues, Prof. Guochun Zhao from University of Hong Kong and his collaborators undertook a Hong Kong RGC GRF project (17307918) to carry out zircon U-Pb dating and Hf isotopic studies combined with magmatic, sedimentary and structural investigations on the 650-500 Ma sedimentary strata and relevant rocks at the southern margin of the Tarim Block. Their results indicate that the southern margin of the Tarim Block developed as an active continental margin through the northward subduction of the Proto-Tethys Ocean during the period of 650-500 Ma, and finally collided with North India at the northern margin of Gondwana at 500-460 Ma.

17308018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308018.value: 隨著大數據的興起，現在越來越普遍遇到以下情形:數據集包含數百萬個數據點或每個數據依次記錄, 而同時存儲整個數據集可能是不可行的。許多傳統統計數據的方法是建立在存儲整個數據集的基礎之上的, 不能很好地擴展。理想情況下，方法應該是單程的，每個數據依次記錄處理一次，然後丟棄。本項目提出了針對分位數回歸和最優決策的單程方法，以獲得有效的計算和推斷方法。 可擴展的分位數回歸是由大量實際數據應用所推動的。比如，美國1990年人口普查數據的1％樣本包含2,458, 285個觀測值，包括教育水平，種族，收入，性別等。目前，能應用於大數據的分位數回歸方法很少, 且缺乏理論上的推斷程序。我們提出了一種基於隨機梯度的可擴展分位數回歸的單程方法。將發展一個統一的理論 用於估計回歸分位數函數以及可縮放的重採樣相關統計推斷的程序。 最優決策制定中，最優個性化決策是為在實踐中使預期結果最大化，這在應用上越來越受歡迎。例如，在醫療保健領域，醫生可以根據患者生物標誌物和臨床病史選擇個性化治療。在市場營銷中，公司可能會根據用戶人口統計信息定位廣告或搜索關鍵字實現利益優化。 現有最佳決策估計方法需要同時獲得整個數據集。這帶來兩個限制。一，方法不可擴展。其次，但更重要的是，它會導致樣本中個體的次優結果，因為最優決策只是從樣本中估算,但沒有為他們實施。為了解決這些問題，我們提出了單程自適應方法。一方面，在將決定分配給新到個體時，擬議的方案利用最新信息和最佳個性化決策。另一方面，新的樣本數據有效更新最優決策的估計。

17308518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308518.value: In nature, complex structures consisting of several compartments of different characters are ubiquitous. The most known example is the cells, which contain many physically isolated units that store a variety of biomolecules separately and perform distinct biological functions simultaneously. While this “multicompartment” feature is essential for natural systems, it is largely missing in synthetic materials. Amphiphilic molecules and polymers automatically form nanostructures with a hydrophilic and a hydrophobic region (e.g., micelles and vesicles); however, these compartmentalized regions have low specificity towards guest molecules. For example, the hydrophobic region cannot distinguish hydrophobic molecules of different sizes. In contrast, compartmentization in biological systems often works together with highly specific molecular recognitions. Until now, it remains a formidable challenge to create artificial nanomaterials possessing multiple compartments with tunable yet specific characteristics. Such materials hold great promise in advancing important applications such as catalysis, drug delivery, and separations, etc. To tackle this challenge, this project aims to develop a new class of materials, which we termed BCPMM (block co-polymer metal-organic-cage micelles). BCPMM integrates metal-organic cages (MOCs) with amphiphilic block copolymers (BCPs), resulting in hybrid nanoparticles (NPs) with several distinct compartments derived from the MOC, the hydrophobic polymer and the hydrophilic polymer. The key to our design is that by taking the advantage of MOCs, which are discrete coordination complexes with well-defined geometries and intrinsic cavities, BCPMM is able to encapsulate guest molecules with high specificity. At the same time, other types of molecules can be accommodated in the compartments made by the polymers. The ability to uptake multiple including both specific and general molecules in isolated compartments makes BCPMM highly promising candidates for catalyzing incompatible tandem reactions, or for carrying multiple drugs for combination therapy. The thrust of our BCPMM strategy is its versatility, as a wide spectrum of MOCs and BCPs can be combined, so the NP’s size, morphology, and compartment properties can all be finely tuned. Coupled with the power of directed self-assembly, an easy and convenient strategy employed for its fabrication, BCPMM is expected to serve as a modular platform for synthesizing multicompartment NPs with hierarchical structures for targeted functions. As a proof of concept, we will explore the possibility of using a customized BCPMM as water-stable, multicompartment drug carriers. 在自然界中，由幾個不同特徵的區室組成的複雜結構無處不在。最著名的例子是細胞，它含有許多物理上分離的單元來存儲各種生物分子並可同時執行不同的生物功能。雖然這種“多室”特徵對於自然系統至關重要，但在合成材料中卻很少見。兩親性分子和聚合物能夠自發形成具有親水和疏水區域的納米結構（例如，膠束和囊泡）;然而，這些區域對客體分子的特異選擇性很低。例如，疏水區域不能區分不同大小的疏水分子。相反，生物系統中的各區域通常能夠協同工作並且具有高度特異性的分子識別能力。到目前為止，製造具有可調節並且高特異選擇性的多室人造納米材料仍然是一項艱鉅的挑戰。這些材料在推進催化，藥物輸送和分離等重要應用方面具有很大的前景。 為了應對這一挑戰，該項目旨在開發一種新型材料，我們稱之為BCPMM（嵌段共聚物-金屬有機籠型膠束）。BCPMM將金屬有機籠（MOC）與兩親性嵌段共聚物（BCP）結合起來，產生一種具有金屬有機籠，疏水聚合物和親水聚合物的多室混合納米粒子（NPs）。我們設計的關鍵是利用了金屬有機籠的特征，這是一種具有明確幾何形狀和固有空腔的離散配位絡合物，BCPMM因此能夠特異性地封裝客體分子。同時，其他類型的分子可以容納在由聚合物製成的隔室中。在隔室中容納多種包括特異性和一般性分子的能力使得BCPMM非常有希望用於催化不相容的串聯反應，或用於攜帶多種藥物的聯合治療中。 我們的BCPMM具有多功能性，因為一系列不同性質的MOCs和BCPs可供組合，因此納米粒子的尺寸，形態和多室的屬性都可以被微調。結合這種簡單方便的定向自組裝策略，BCPMM有望成為一種模塊化的平台，可用於合成具有多級分層結構和目標功能的多室納米粒子。首先，我們將探索使用BCPMM作為一種水相穩定的多室藥物載體的可能性來驗證這一概念。

17308518.label: Realisation of objectives
17308518.value: Objective 1. This objective aims to develop synthetic protocols for ligand functionalized block copolymers (BCPs), crucial for the implementation of the whole project. The task includes the selection of the BCPs and the ligand and investigate protocols for the materials synthesis and purifications. The objective has been successfully realized (100%). Additional design beyond the original proposal has also been demonstrated. Synthesis of the block copolymer. As planned, we have designed and synthesized amphiphilic BCPs containing a hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG) block and a hydrophobic block. We have examined the synthesis of multiple hydrophobic polymers including poly(L-lactide) (PLA), poly(caprolactone) (PCL). We have successfully synthesized BCPs of various molecular weights and block ratios. PCL-PEG was found suitable for the subsequent applications. In the later stage of the project, we have expanded the scope of polymers to peptoid, which has rendered the system more precise, tunable, and functional. Functionalization of block copolymer with ligand. We have synthesized small-molecule ligands needed for functionalizing the BCPs. The original proposal was to use click chemistry (copper-catalysed cycloaddition) to couple the ligand onto BCPs, yet the chemicals and condition needed can degrade the BCP we choose such as PLA. The use of copper is also not ideal for the proposed application in biological settings. We have switched to EDC-mediated coupling to link the ligand. This method proved effective, which produced the final ligand-functionalized block copolymer (BCP-L). The same protocol was later applied for polymers with different molecular weights and various types of ligands. Thus, the synthetic aspect of this project is successful, laying foundation for self-assembly and application. Objective 2. This objective is the key step for the formation of the proposed BCPMM nanoparticles. Using self-assembly and various characterization methods, we have successfully construct the BCPMM and investigated their structures and how different components play a role. The objective is 100% achieved. Self-assembly of micelles and their morphology. We have investigated the self-assembly of BCP-L, first forming the cage and then the BCPMMs. The first step produces start polymer with a defined number of arms. It has been proved that the assembly works for all polymers investigated. We have subsequently studied the formation of BCPMMs by transferring polymer functionalized cages to aqueous solution by dialysis. This has led to the micellar nanoparticles BCPMMs, which were characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS), transmission electron microscopy, etc. The results were compared to traditional micelles (without the cage inside), block copolymer micelles (BCPM) and with polymeric particles with different types of cages. We have discovered that the presence of cages can, as we proposed, greatly influence the morphologies of the nanoparticle formed. Stability of BCPMM nanoparticles. We have investigated the stability of BCPMM in aqueous solution as well as in buffers, with and without strong competing ligands, using various techniques (UV-Vis spectroscopy, DLS, and transmission electron microscope). We have proved that the designed BCPMM particles are stable than traditional micelles particles; the integrity of the cages were preserved or prolonged. We have also used fluorescence spectrometry to study the critical micelle concentration, CMC, of BCPMMs, which revealed a much smaller value confirming the increased micelle stability. This property is the most important discovery that makes BCPMM a promising candidate for delivery systems with increased efficiency. The properties is presumably due to the special structure of the BCPMM, having a core-shell architecture with metal-organic cages and polymers having a synergistic effect. Objective 3. Having demonstrated the structure and stability of BCPMMs, we have investigated the loading of anticancer drugs in the nanoparticles. With the special design and the ability to tune the composition and architecture, we have explored different ways for drug loading. The objective is 100% realized. Encapsulating the hydrophobic drug. We have tested the encapsulation of a hydrophobic anti-cancer drug, DOX, into the BCPMMs. We focused on particles made by PCL-PEG and with the large Fujita-type cages. We found that the drug could be successfully encapsulated into the particles, with a loading of 19.6% and a loading efficiency of 65%, which is similar to BCPM. The encapsulation was also verified by using hydrophobic dye molecule Nile Red. We have also explored the encapsulation of inorganic drugs such as cis-platin into the cage as a second drug, to realize multi-drug loading and delivery. In the peptoid-based BCPMM system, a CPT drug has been incorporated to the polymer chain via covalent linkage. Also, we have preliminarily investigated the introduction of drug molecules into the MOC by a ligand functionalization method. These studies are beyond the scope of this proposal but important extension of it. This capability will ensure great flexibility in designing similar systems for other applications. Objective 4. The final objective of this project is to apply the developed BCPMM nanoparticles for biomedical applications, in this case, delivery of anticancer drugs. Working together with collaborators, we have thoroughly investigated the performance of BCPMMs for the purpose. The particles with advantages in structures and stability have shown outstanding/improved efficacy in cancer delivery and treatment. This objective has been well executed (100%). Drug release profile. We have studied the releasing profile of the drugs loaded in BCPMMs using UV-Vis and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Results show that BCPMMs have sustained release compared to BCPM under various different conditions (e.g., pH values). In vitro cell viability and cellular uptake. We have studied the cell viability of the obtained BCPMM nanoparticle as well as other particle formulations as controls. Experiments showed that the BCPMM without drug have a low toxicity proving that it can be used as a good platform for carrying and delivering drugs. We have also tested BCPMMs that carries DOX, and found that they are more acute to cells. The cellular uptake was observed by confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM) at different intervals. The uptake of BCPMM is more effective than BCPM (particles without cage). In vivo experiments. We have done tests in vivo for BCPMM nanoparticles, showing promising results as revealed in the attached manuscript. The pharmacokinetics of DOX−BCPMMs was examined. The circulation half-life for BCPMM is about 38 hours, about twice as much as that of BCPM, which can be ascribed to the stability of the particle. The biodistribution is also studied, and results show that BCPMM particles more like to accumulate in the cancer area. Finally, the antitumor efficacy of BCPMM loaded with DOX is studied, as compared to different control groups, such as PBS, free DOX, DOX-BCPM, etc. Remarkably, the DOX-BCPMMs show the highest antitumor efficiency. The body weights did not show evident fluctuation during the treatment, indicative of little systemic toxicity (including BCPMMs). Yet, compared to the controls, the BCPMMs with DOX can reach a mouse survival rate of 75% after 30 days. For the peptoid-based BCPMM systems, a superior anticancer efficacy has also been realized. In summary, we have developed a new composite nanocarrier BCPMM by integrating large-sized metal−organic cages with BCPs using a self-assembly strategy. With structural synergy by design, the unimolecular, multi-compartment, core−shell nanoparticle presents a remarkable stability against dilution and a moderate stability to strong nucleophiles, making them a suitable candidate as drug carriers. The objectives listed in the proposal have been well investigated and realized.

17308518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17308518.value: The major findings of the project is that a new type of composite nanoparticles called BCPMMs have been introduced. The particles are made by a stepwise self-assembly strategy yet has remarkable stability as well as unique structural features, stemming from the combined advantages of block copolymers (BCPs) and metal-organic cages (MOC). Among many good merits, the BCPMMs particles are monodisperse with unimolecular architecture. When carrying anticancer drugs, they have shown negligible systematic toxicity but superior anticancer efficacy, revealed in a mouse model. These explorations and findings will/have led to three publications in peer-reviewed international journals (one paper under review). First, the thorough investigation of literature in the field has been reviewed by us in “Molecular Engineering of Metal-Organic Cycles/Cages for Drug Delivery” published in Macromolecular Research. Second, the main findings about the BCPMMs and their biomedical applications have been reported as an research article “Block Co-PolyMOC Micelles and Structural Synergy as Composite Nanocarriers” in ACS Applied Materials and Interface (Impact factor 10.38). Finally, the BCPMM system has been extended to peptoid-based polymer systems, which endow such particles with extra new functionality and ever more precise nanostructures. This has led to a high-quality paper currently under review. The title of the paper is “Atomically Precise and Highly Addressable Nanoparticles by Integrating Metal-Organic Cage and Peptoids”. These research outcome have also been list in Pat C, Research Output, 8). By working on the project, post- and undergraduate students have been trained (Part C, Research Output, 10). One student Dr. Lang WANG, who primarily worked on this project, has graduated with PhD in Materials Chemistry. Another two students, Mr. Yannis Ho and Mr Jiayu Zhou, has also gained vigorous training. They have also extended the BCPMMs systems to the design of asymmetrically functionalized nanoparticles or particles that carry biomolecules such as proteins. In addition, many undergraduate students have been partly involved in the project, obtaining academic trainings. With its interdisciplinary nature, working on this project has helped the establishment of many collaborators, both in and out of Hong Kong. Through such collaboration, our team has learned the related knowledge and improved the infrastructure in our lab. Finally, the results of the project have been discussed in local and international meetings (Part C, Research Output, 9). We note that due to the pandemic, the PI and students could not participate in many conferences and visits.

17308518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17308518.value: In this project, the concept of integrating block copolymer and metal-organic cages to create composite nanoparticles have been proved, and the application of a specific system (drug delivery) has been demonstrated. The design of such system is modular, and can be extended to other polymers, cages, and targeted for many applications. For example, we have already extended this idea to peptoid, which is sequence-defined with accurate molecular weight. This leads to atom-precision soft nanoparticles, which has been a challenge to fabricate. Because the narrowly dispersed particles size, one of the future exploration can be how size influence the biodistribution and accumulation of particles in biological systems. In previous systems, nanoparticles always have large size variation, so there is no clear answer about the optimal size of nanoparticles for drug delivery and to test the debatable EPR effect (enhanced permeation and retention effect). Another direction currently under our investigation is to make asymmetrically functional nanoparticles, or Janus nanoparticles, by utilizing MOC ligand with exo- and endo functionalization. This would enable the site-specific installation and release of drug molecules. Depending on the nature of these further development, it would take 1-3 years for completion.

17308518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17308518.value: This project introduces a new type nanosized particles made from polymers and metal-organic cages that possess several distinct features. They are equally sized and having multiple compartments, core-shell architecture, and exceptional stability. These advantages stem from the structural synergy between the polymer and metal-organic cages, combined via a stepwise directed self-assembly strategy. The types of the polymers and the metal-organic cages can be tuned to adjust the morphology and functions of the nanoparticles. The new particles can carry anticancer drugs and deliver them to the diseased tissue with preference. According to our experiment, the particles also have a sustainable release of the carried drugs, which is desirable for such application. When tested in a mouse model, the drug-loaded particles show superior efficacy in inhibiting the growth of the tumor and increasing the survival rate of the mice. On one hand, the project provides a means of engineering nanostructure and nanomorphology of particulate materials. On the other hand, it?s flexibility and outstanding performance for biomedical purposes is significant regarding to the practical applications.

17308618.label: Project Objectives
17308618.value: To develop novel unified ab-initio quantum chemistry tools that can capture the many-body nature of transient excitonic states and the bulk effects in a given singlet fission material at a low computational cost. In particular, we shall establish active space partitioning and reordering schemes to allow a rapid recovery of electron correlations in the local region, and implement a local correlation version of expeditious stochastic second-order Møller-Plesset method for treating the surrounding environment of singlet fission materials. To elucidate the mechanism of correlated triplet-triplet exciton generation in typical inter- and intra-molecular singlet fission materials using proposed high-fidelity quantum chemistry simulations. To elucidate the significance of the long-range environment effects in regulating the singlet fission pathway. To compute linear optical spectral and kinetic transportation properties associated with singlet fission mechanistic hypothesis that can be tested by experimental collaborators to further refine our computational models.

17308618.label: Realisation of objectives
17308618.value: Objective 1. This objective has been fully achieved. We developed a comprehensive tool set for analysing the many-body wavefunction of molecular excited states based on two-particle spin descriptors of the numerically exact ab-initio density-matrix renormalization group method, by incorporating a rather large number of correlated electrons and active orbitals. Our formulation and implementation enable to characterise the nature of electronic spin states over molecular units from many-body electronic structures, track their state progression along important vibronic directions, as well as identify the important normal modes tuning/promoting electronic transitions. These methodologies are of general purpose and their application is not limited to singlet fission systems as proposed here, and can be also used for computing and understanding the photophysical details in other photofunctional systems. Yet, the full development of the stochastic MP2 approach for describing the bulk impact on the locally excited molecules demands substantial efforts beyond the normative period of this project, and will be carried out in future. Objective 2. The objective has been fully achieved. By advancing and applying high-level ab-initio quantum chemistry techniques, we revealed the coexistence and role of both lower- and higher-lying charge transfer (CT) states in vibronically modulating the triplet pair state in pentacene. The indirect CT interactions are shown to delocalise the triplet pair state and reduce the binding energy of the triplet pairs through the out-of-phase vibronic modulations, thus providing clear implications of triplet-triplet pair separations in pentacene dimer. Our work substantiates the importance of the many-electron vibronic process for governing singlet fission pathways, as the triplet pair is vibronically bundled with energetically close singlet states via multimode interactions in the distinct vibronic region of compression and stretching, respectively. Objective 3. We systematically investigated the efficiency of the pentacene dimer separation in yielding the triplet-triplet pair state. We showed that the ability of generating the pure correlated triplet-triplet pairs in pentacene dimer is bounded to a narrow range of 6.1-6.5 Angstrom, given its proper herringbone configuration. Beyond this range of inter-dimer distance, the singlet fission is predicted to be poor for pentacene. More importantly, as we move to multiple chromophore units, considerably more low-lying singlet states come closer and can be found within a smaller energy window than the dimer. In trimers and tetramers, the close-lying adiabatic states interact rather strongly via intramolecular and intermolecular electron-vibration couplings. The molecular packing in trimers and tetramers induces very significant intermolecular vibronic interactions via C=C stretching modes leading to the stabilisation of a triplet-triplet pair state both in low and high-frequency regions. Objective 4. This objective has been mostly addressed. We performed a high-throughput virtual screening procedure to discover azaborine substituted organic singlet fission materials by tuning the S-T gaps and other charge transport properties in the parent acene ring. To enhance the singlet fission performance, the structural packings were modified to yield the local maxima of fission rates in a six-dimensional space as computed using Marcus theory for studying the electron transfer kinetics. After an extensive exploration and screening using a simplified frontier orbital model, we identified many potential dimer geometries for newly developed singlet fission chromophores and reported their Davydoy splitting, binding energies and enhanced singlet fission rates. These dimer structures can be utilised as new targets for crystal engineering and possible chemical synthesis of covalently linked dimers. In contrast to the prevailing energetic criterion based on chromophore monomers commonly adopted in literature, our results highlight that these monomer-based SF metrics provide only a general guideline, and it is the molecular packing as revealed in the minimum dimer model that can dictate the singlet fission kinetics and should be managed together with the monomer-based excitonic properties for developing new singlet fission materials. In our future works, our computational results for identifying efficient singlet fission materials will be tested in collaboration with synthetic and spectroscopic studies.

17308618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17308618.value: This project innovates and applies the many-body ab-initio electronic structure tools for studying photofunctional systems with unconventional excited state property such as singlet fission. Our major findings center on two general aspects: (i) delivering new excited state computational tools for routine applications as demonstrated to our benchmark study of discovering exciton duplication channels in pentacene, and (ii) extending these methodologies to computationally design efficient singlet fission chromophores. (1) We put forth extensive wavefunction methodologies, based on the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method for the first time, for quantifying the spin state nature of molecular excitonic states [R. Walia, Z. Deng and J. Yang Chem. Sci. 2021,12, 12928-12938]. (2) We came up with a detailed high-level analysis of relevant charge transfer states in pentacene, and quantified the vibronic coupling strengths between multiple low-lying singlet states and normal modes, at the ab-initio DMRG level for the first time [R. Walia, Z. Deng and J. Yang Chem. Sci. 2021,12, 12928-12938]. (3) We explored a variety of optimal BN-doped dimeric configurations in a parent perylene molecule, and showed that in case of a few BN-doped perylene systems, the vibronic influence stabilises the multi-excitonic state and promotes the population transfer with other charge transfer states. These computationally identified configurations can serve as starting points for the synthesis and experimental exploration of new novel singlet fission candidates [R. Walia and J. Yang Photochem. Photobiol. Sci. 2022, 10.1007/s43630-022-00251-x]. Our main research findings were also presented as invited and contributed talks at several international/regional conferences, including "the 10th Biennial International Conference of The Asian Consortium on Computational Materials Science", "NSFC/RGC Joint Conference On Advanced Materials For Energy Related Applications", "the 30th International Conference on Photochemistry" and so on.

17308618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17308618.value: In this project, we have devoted to sharpen new numerical tools for simulating singlet fission systems and performed with these tools the benchmark mechanistic studies on prototypical singlet fission system as well as the digital discovery of new BN-doped perylene derivatives by virtual screening. Our simulations generated interesting findings from high-level ab-initio computation, but were still limited to dimer models to reduce the computational complexity. Moving forward, there are many more to explore in this fascinating field with major challenges. For instances, the morphological requirements are less clear for efficient singlet fission in realistic bulky systems; how inhomogeneous environment may fundamentally revise the nature of highly packed low-lying states and the singlet fission pathways (eg, the long-range vibronic decoherence). Moreover, the quantum dynamics simulation on the kinetic process of diffusion and separation of the loosely correlated triplet-triplet pair states is desired to produce more insights beyond dimer model. Finally, the computational design and exploration of vibronically modified molecular-spacer based intramolecular singlet fission candidates is another direction to be taken as well, although it is commonly realised that practically achieving the high light-electricity conversion efficiency has still remained difficult in real materials.

17308618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17308618.value: During the light conversion into electricity in traditional solar cells, only one electron can be excited by one photon, and solar cell efficiency is intrinsically capped by Shockley-Queisser limit: only about 33% of the total incident sunlight can be harvested and converted due to spectrum losses. The theoretical work by our research team has discovered that the efficiency limit can be removed by opening novel quantum channels of electron-hole pair duplication in an optimal structural conformation. That is, upon absorbing light energy, the materials relay the energy from one photoexcited singlet exciton of higher energy to at least two triplet excitons of lower energy. As a result, the exciton generation is boosted at the expense of only one photon energy to double electric currents in solar cells, which holds a great potential to substantially improve the light-electricity conversion efficiency. For revealing such complex electron and energy transfer pathways in photophysical processes, our research team developed an extensive and widely applicable computational technique using high-level quantum chemistry algorithms. Our findings in understanding and discovering new singlet fission systems would promote the optimisation of the performance of photofunctional materials towards enhanced solar panel efficiency.

17308818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308818.value: This project studies the Poisson geometry of meromorphic endomorphism algebras of elliptic curves and their quantizations. Meromorphic endomorphism algebras are a class of infinite dimensional algebraic Poisson manifolds associated to complex elliptic curves, equipped with associative products. They were first studied by Sklyanin and Cherednik in early 80s. Meromorphic endomorphism algebras and their quantizations give examples of integrable Hamiltonian systems and their quantum analogies associated to elliptic curves. The construction of Sklyanin and Cherednik is based on Belavin’s elliptic solution of classical (and quantum) Yang-Baxter equation. One may obtain rational and trigonometric solutions of Yang-Baxter equation from Belavin's elliptic solution via a degeneration process. Meromorphic endomorphism algebra can be embedded into the formal loop Lie algebra. Its quantisation is closely related the quantised universal enveloping algebra of the formal loop Lie algebra. In the joint work with Alexander Polishchuk, using the method of derived algebraic geometry, the PI constructed a Poisson structure on moduli space of complexes of vector bundles over an elliptic curve. And it is observed that meromorphic endomorphism algebras are components of this moduli space. The derived geometry method also provides a new tool to show the existence of symplectic foliation on the moduli space. In this project, the PI aims to apply the method of derived algebraic geometry to the study of meromorphic endomorphism algebras. To be more specific, we plan to study the symplectic foliations of them and give a coordinate-free construction of quantizations via algebraic geometry. Moreover, we will study the conjectural correspondence between symplectic leaves on meromorphic endomorphism algebras and irreducible representations of their quantizations. The topics of the proposed project lie in the interface of various active subjects including algebraic geometry, symplectic geometry, representation theory and mathematical physics. We believe the new method of derived geometry will shed some lights for some old problems in these subjects. 17308818.label: Realisation of objectives
17308818.value: Object 1 is completed. In the paper joint with Polishchuk, published on Selecta, we classify the symplectic leaves of the meromorphic matrix algebra over elliptic curves. It turns out the moduli stack of symplectic leaves admit discrete parameters and continuous parameters. The discrete parameter is a pair of partitions. Fixing a discrete parameter we get a moduli space that are strata of symmetric power of elliptic curves. We have studied Object 2 for a while and realized that it is better to put that in a bigger framework, i.e. finding algebraic geometric way to quantize all Feigin-Odesskii Poisson manifolds, where meromorphic endomorphism algebra is a special example. Now we have extended this to a long term project. We have made significant progress on Object 3. In a joint work with Polishchuk (submit to Journal of Topology), we prove all Feigin-Odesskii manifolds of rank 1 are bihamiltonian. We have also constructed bihamiltonian structure on another class of higher rank. Recently we have also studied the symplectic leaves on Kodaira cycles, an important class of degeneration of elliptic curves.

17308818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17308818.value: In the paper "Shifted Poisson geometry and meromorphic matrix algebras over an elliptic curve" joint with Polishchuk, published on Selecta Math., we have classified the symplectic leaves of the matrix algebra over the field of meromorphic functions on elliptic curves. This is an ind-scheme that can be written as direct limit of moduli space of meromorphic endomorphisms of stable vector bundles with poles on a fixed divisor. The poisson structure on these spaces are originally defined via Belavin-Drinfeld elliptic r-matrix. Our main contribution is that we give a geometric construction of this Poisson structure based on our previous work on shifted Poisson structure on moduli stack of complexes. Moreover, using derived algebraic geometric techniques we reduce the classification problem of symplectic leaves to a classification of torsion sheaves with certain properties. This result has found some applications in the theory of AS regular algebras. In the work "Elliptic bihamiltonian structures from relative shifted Poisson structures" joint with Polishchuk, we have constructed bihamiltonian structures on several classes of Feigin-Odesskii elliptic manifolds, including all FO manifolds of rank 1. Integrability is very closely related to existence of bihamiltonian structures. This paper has been submit to Journal of Topology. We have studied the symplectic (leaves) foliation on certain moduli space of complexes on Kodaira cycle, i.e. cyclic chain of projective lines. It turns out that the symplectic foliation is closely related to certain Lie theoretical stratification. This is a work in progress.

17308818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17308818.value: We plan to extend Object 2 into a long term project on setting up a geometric framework to quantize Poisson structure on moduli stack of complexes of Gorenstein curves. This has been made precise in my RGC proposal for year 2023.

17308818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17308818.value: Our construction of shifted Poisson structure on moduli stack of complexes of Gorenstein curves have so far found many applications in algebraic geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. First, many interesting Poisson structure that appears in these subjects fit into this class. Moreover, our construction and techniques make it possible to translate some problems regarding the the symplectic leaves to questions about vector bundles on curves. Following this methodology, we are able to solve several problems in these subjects. And recently we have found a new link to the theory of cluster algebra.

17309018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309018.value: Cardiolipin (CL), a unique family of phospholipids found in energy-producing membranes of mitochondria, plays vital roles in mitochondrial biology and energy metabolism. In healthy normal cells, CL interacts intimately with protein members of the mitochondrial respiratory chain to maintain optimal ATP synthesis. Under oxidative stress or cellular injury, CL undergoes peroxidation and translocation, which are critical steps in the initiation of programmed cell death. Given its prominent roles as a lipid regulator of mitochondrial bioenergetics and apoptosis, CL is a highly significant molecular determinant of mitochondrial health and dysfunction. Indeed, a wide spectrum of human diseases has been associated with CL alternations, including cardiomyopathies, metabolic disorders, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Detection of CL has previously depended on mass spectroscopic methods or staining with fluorogenic dyes of unsatisfactory selectivity. A lack of small-molecule probes for CL suitable for live cell imaging and quantitative fluorescence measurement has hampered progress in CL biology and the study of related diseases. In our previous research funded by RGC, we have a track record in development of practical fluorescent probes for selective detection and imaging of specific reactive oxygen species and application in biological systems. In an effort to extend our expertise to CL detection, we have developed a green fluorescent turn-on probe based on a novel detection strategy, and applied it in live cell imaging. In this proposal, we will focus on optimizing the performance in terms of selectivity/sensitivity, excitation/emission wavelength, mitochondria targeting, and cell imaging. In addition, we plan to use our new CL fluorescent probes to tackle questions related to the roles of CL in mitochondria function. This project is of fundamental interest as it attempts to overcome an age-old technical challenge of providing facile and robust fluorescent probes for live cell imaging and quantitative measurement of CL, which should prove useful to investigation on the complex roles of CL in mitochondrial function and disorder. 心磷脂（cardiolipin）是磷脂中一個特殊的家族,它主要發現于線粒體的內膜中， 並對於線粒體生物學及能量代謝起重要作用。在正常健康細胞中, 心磷脂與線粒體的呼吸鏈中的蛋白緊密作用以維持其正常的能量合成。而在氧化應激和細胞損傷情況下, 心磷脂會被過氧化或發生移位,並進一步觸發程式性細胞凋亡。由於其線上粒體能量學和細胞凋亡中起到的獨特的調節作用, 心磷脂是決定線粒體的健康或失活的重要因素。事實上,人類的許多疾病已經被發現與心磷脂的變異有關,這些疾病包括心肌萎縮,代謝紊亂,神經變性及癌症等。目前心磷脂的檢測主要依靠質譜和選擇性不理想的螢光染料。 由於缺乏可用於活細胞並作定量檢測的小分子螢光探針,心磷脂生物學及相關疾病的研究受到了阻礙。我組在以過RGC資助的研究中, 開發了一系列可選擇性檢測生物體系中的活性氧物種並成像的螢光探針。為了進一步拓展心磷脂的檢測手段, 我們利用新穎的檢測理念, 開發了一種綠色螢光探針,並成功用於細胞成像。在本課題中我們將致力於優化該探針的表現(就其選擇性/靈敏度, 激發和發射波長, 線粒體靶向性及成像效果而言), 並使用這些新穎的螢光探針探究心磷脂在程式性細胞凋亡中起到的作用。 提供便利和高效的螢光探針用於活細胞成像並定量分析心磷脂一直是一個亟待攻克的難題, 而該研究課題正要解決這個難題, 並進一步探究心磷脂線上粒體的功能和紊亂中起到的作用。

17500618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500618.value: Uncertainty and information frictions are everywhere. If you run a firm and have to make investment decisions, the first thing you should consider is the forecast for your firm sales in the next few years. If you have to decide whether to enter a foreign market which requires a substantial amount of investment in advance, the first thing you should think of is the forecast for your products' (in the foreign country) for the next few years. For my profession, whether or not hiring or promoting an academic staff crucially depends on how the school or department forecasts the scholar's performance and productivity in the future. In short, uncertainty is important for decision making. In most cases, economic agents make imprecise forecasts as they face information frictions (or rigidity). For instance, a firm sometime cannot receive precise information about the popularity of its products due to random noises. Moreover, firms can make systematic mistakes when forecasting, if there is an unexpected shock that happens after the forecasting period. In our profession, every school/department head wish to know the true productivity or ability of every job candidate. However, the reality is that we can only extract information about this candidate's quality from his or her files or presentation. And, all these information has noises in it. In many cases, we, as economists, make bad hiring decisions. All these examples show the importance of information frictions (or rigidity) for decision making. Naturally, studying patterns of firms' forecasts and forecast errors is important for us to understand how information frictions affect firm-level decisions as well as aggregate efficiency of the economy. In this project, we utilize two unique panel datasets from Japan to systematically study these important issues. Specifically, our study studies how and why firms make systematical errors when making their forecast. For instance, how does the precision of forecasts vary with firm age and size? How do firms update their forecasts over time? How do the forecast errors evolve over time? Importantly, we are going to study how the recent financial crisis affected firms' forecasts and the precision of the forecasts. We plan to study how the crisis affected firms' investment, hiring and exiting choices through influencing their forecasts and confidence for the future. 我们的研究是关于企业预期的形成。在现实生活中，企业如何 预期自己将来的销售收入和利润情状况将在很大程度上决定它的 投资，雇用和科研投入。这些企业层面的行为加总起来又会影 响经济整体的波动和经济体的长期增长。本研究利用日本政府 的数据和本研究小组将要在日本收集的企业层面数据对企业 预期形成的成因以及它对经济体的整体影响做研究。 本研究首先会分析企业的预期形成的因素。即企业是否是根据 自己的经营历史和经验来形成对将来的预期。其次，本研究将探讨 经济总体的波动对企业预期的影响会有多大。在此，不同规模和 年龄的企业的预期形成是否有所不同。同理，不同产业的企业的 预期形成是否会有不同。最后，本研究将分析企业在形成预期 的时候是否受困于所掌握的信息不够充足和完全。这将会对政 府的信息公开以及政策透明等方面提供意见。

17500618.label: Realisation of objectives
17500618.value: The objectives proposed in the original application have been realized in our complete working paper entitled: "Information Rigidity and Elastic Attention: Evidence from Japan." Specifically, in the paper we examined how information rigidities behave differently when forecasting firm-level variables. Using a panel dataset containing quantitative forecasts of the GDP growth rate, inflation rate, and firms’ own cost, we present evidence of more pervasive information rigidity when forecasting macro targets than when forecasting firms’ own cost. This finding supports the argument of state-dependent information rigidities, as the cost process is estimated to be more volatile than macro variable processes.

17500618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500618.value: In this study, we empirically investigate the information rigidities that firms face with regard to forecasting both macro targets and firm-level variables. We carry out this using a merged panel dataset from Japan (2004 − 2018) containing firms’ forecasts of both macro targets (i.e., the inflation rate and nominal GDP growth rate) and firm-level variables (i.e., firms’ own sales and cost). We find the information rigidities related to forecasting macro variables far more pervasive than those associated with the forecasting firm’s own cost. Moreover, when estimating the three target variables’ dynamic processes, we find the cost process much more volatile than the GDP growth and inflation processes, rationalizing our empirical finding. In summary, we find evidence consistent with the predictions of rational inattention (RI) models with elastic attention in Sims (2010) and Ma ́ckowiak and Wiederholt (2015). In the empirical section, we evaluate the performance of our model in terms of calculated sensitivity parameters and non-targeted moments. We find the parameter of sensitivity to firm’s marginal cost 3.5 to 4 times higher than the implied parameter of sensitivity to the two macro targets. In order to gauge the plausibility of the calculated sensitivity parameters, we match the three target variables’ estimated Kalman gains (and thus sensitivity parameters) by choosing two parameters: the constant marginal cost of acquiring and processing information, and the Frisch ELS.5 The calibrated model matches the three Kalman gains well, while the implied Frisch ELS (0.91) is in line with the estimates in the literature (e.g., Kneip et al. (2020)). Moreover, we do not try to match the standard deviations of the three FEs in our calibration exercise, but the standard deviations of the three FEs implied by our calibrated model are quite close to those calculated using the data, with the percentage difference ranging from zero to 25%. In sum, we can conclude that our empirical results support the RI model predictions with elastic attention and the argument of state-dependent information rigidities.

17500618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500618.value: Our study is related to the literature on elastic attention; see Sims (2003) and Sims (2010). We contribute to this literature by presenting evidence that the attention paid to macro and firm-specific target variables is heterogeneous and thus state dependent. The state-dependent nature of information rigidities has important implications for the effectiveness of monetary policies over business cycles. In the future, we will apply the results obtained in this project to study how the interaction of the state-dependent feature with the elastic attention theory affects optimal adjustments and the effects of monetary policy.

17500618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500618.value: This study utilizes a merged Japanese firm-level panel dataset containing the quantitative forecasts of three target variables to infer the corresponding degree of information rigidity at the macro and firm levels. We find that the degree of information rigidity concerning forecasting macro targets is much higher than that associated with forecasting the firm’s own cost. This is consistent with the predictions of the rational inattention (RI) model with elastic attention proposed in Sims (2010) and supports the argument of state-dependent information rigidities.

17500918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500918.value: A rapidly growing literature in accounting has studied firm’s cost behavior and cost variability, shedding light on managerial decisions relating to cost management (e.g., Anderson, Banker and Janakiraman 2003). Firm’s cost behavior has an impact on analysts’ forecast accuracy and investors’ interpretation of earnings conservatism (Weiss 2010; Banker et al. 2016). Cost variability and stickiness are often estimated by the correlation between the changes of total costs and the sales growth. Such an estimation requires the historical data of firm’s operation and does not apply to the initial public offering (IPO) firms which are young firms without a track record of firm performance. More importantly, Balakrishnan, Labro and Soderstrom (2014) argue that the observed cost behavior is determined by firm’s innate cost structure which illustrates the cost components of direct materials, direct labors and indirect manufacturing overheads and hence identifies the costs controllable for firm’s management. The lack of cost structure data implies that the documented cost behaviors might not pertain to managerial decisions. In 2012 China Securities Regulatory Committee (CSRC) required the disclosure of product cost structure in the annual reports for listed firms and in the IPO prospectus for the IPO issuers. Such a mandatory disclosure of firm’s cost structure allows us to investigate the role of cost information in the price formation of IPOs. Based on the two theories of IPO underpricing phenomenon (i.e., the closing price of the first trading day is usually higher than the offer price), the information asymmetry theory and agency friction theory, we expect that the extent of IPO underpricing is positively correlated with the proportion of indirect cost in the cost structure. Such an expectation relies on the basic managerial accounting fact that the indirect costs (e.g. manufacturing overheads) consist of depreciation expenses, the allocated costs of service departments and indirect labor costs, many of which are sunk costs and uncontrollable for managers. Therefore, the component of indirect cost increases the break-even point of sales revenues and exaggerates earnings sensitivity to business condition. The proportion of indirect cost is also expected to be positively correlated with post-IPO stock return volatility and the upward revision of offer price in support of, respectively, the information-based and agency-based theories of IPO underpricing. Furthermore, we will examine whether the documented effect is less pronounced for firms with higher-quality disclosure of cost structure and for IPO firms selling a larger slice of ownership. 會計研究中的一个快速發展的方向是研究公司的成本行為和成本變異性，從而揭示了與成本管理相關的管理決策 (如Anderson, Banker and Janakiraman 2003)。公司的成本行為對分析師的預測準確性和投資者對盈餘穩健性的解釋有影響 (Weiss 2010; Banker et al. 2016)。过往的研究往往采用總成本的變化與銷售增長之間的相關性來估算成本變異性和粘性。這種估算需要公司運作的歷史資料, 因而不適用於公開募股 (IPO) 公司。這些IPO企業是年輕的公司, 还沒有一個長時間的公司業績記錄。更重要的是, Balakrishnan, Labro and Soderstrom (2014) 認為, 觀察到的成本行為是由企業固有的成本結構決定的, 它能說明直接材料、直接人工和間接製造費用的成本構成, 從而確定了企業的成本可控性。由於缺乏公開的企業成本數據，過往研究中的成本行為也許並不能用來反映公司管理決策。 在 2012年, 中國證券監督管理委員會 (證監會) 要求在上市公司年度報告和 IPO 發行人招股說明書中披露產品成本結構。這種強制披露公司的成本結構使我們能夠調查成本資訊在 IPO價格形成中的作用。基於IPO抑價現象的兩種理論 (即第一交易日的收盤價通常高於要約價格), 包括資訊不對稱理論和代理摩擦理論, 我們預期IPO抑價的程度是與間接成本的比例呈正相關。這種預期是依賴于基本的管理會計事實, 即間接成本 (例如製造費用) 包括折舊費用、服務部門的分配成本和間接人工成本, 其中許多是沉沒成本和管理人員無法控制。因此, 間接成本增加了銷售收入的平衡點, 並加大了業務狀況的收益敏感性。同時, 間接成本的比重也與IPO後股票收益波動率和報價價格上調呈正相關。这两个预期分別支持資訊不对称和代理摩擦的IPO抑價理論。此外, 我們將研究是否我們的預期結果，對於成本披露質量較高的企業和出售更大一部分擁有權的 IPO 公司來說, 是否更不明顯。

17500918.label: Realisation of objectives
17500918.value: In our GRF project, we aim to investigate the role of newly-disclosed cost information in shaping the trade-offs in the managers’ decision-making and triggering the responses from market participants. However, after collecting the sample of Chinese IPOs, we realize that the traditional research design of IPO under-pricing model is not well-suited for China’s capital market. In particular, for almost all IPOs, the stock returns are 44% in the first day of IPOs, reaching the highest limit of stock returns as set by the regulator, CSRC in China. Without observing much variation in the first-day IPO returns, we face the difficult in documenting any effect of firm’s cost structure. In an attempt to overcome this problem, we turn to the post-IPO period and examine how the improved disclosure of firm’s cost items affects managers’ decision to adjust cost structure accordingly. Our initial evidence suggests that the cost stickiness of some major cost items (COGS, S&G, and R&D costs) experiences a salient change in response to the enhanced disclosure of individual cost items in annual reports. This evidence, however, is not very robust to sample selection or the choice of control variables used in the cost-stickiness models. After further investigating into the underlying factors, we figure it out that there is one confounding event occurring in 2018: the CSRC mandated all firms to clarify the details of the costs contained in the account “management expenses” in the income statement by explicitly reporting the “R&D expenses” as a standalone item (i.e., improved cost details). This regulation significantly improves the disclosed cost structure of a firm in the annual reports. In addition, we understand that it is not appropriate to examine the cost behavior of the aggregate amount of total cost. Instead, we should rely on the disclosed individual cost items and separately study the cost recognition and enhanced disclosure of these individual cost items which have different natures and characteristics in view of firm’s different business models. Therefore, we focus on the three major cost items such as the R&D cost, investment cost and the management compensation costs. I develop this GRF research by conducting multiple projects wherein my coauthors and I focus on one specific cost item for each project. To utilize the unique setting of the new regulation for enhanced disclosure of R&D costs in 2018, Dr. Yifei Xia (the Co-I) and I invited Prof. Yutao Wang from Renmin University of China to join the research. Yutao has an expertise in collecting and cleaning the hand-collected patent data for Chinese firms. In the paper “R&D Disclosure Change and Innovation Investments: Evidence from Retroactive Adjustments in R&D expenses” we hand-collect the retroactive adjustments made by firms to their 2017 reported R&D expenses in the footnote; such adjustment is available in the 2018 annual reports, corresponding to the first year of adopting the new presentation format of standalone line item for R&D expenses in the income statement. This paper is now under preparation for journal submission and is attached to this report (See Part C, the “under preparation” research output). In this study, we manage to document the relation between the retroactive R&D cost adjustments and firm’s future R&D investment. In addition, the over- and under-statements of 2017 R&D costs shed lights on managers’ incentive to pursue their private benefit when there is no such requirement of separate disclosure of R&D costs. Moreover, we also pin down some scenarios where managers try to avoid providing sophisticated information about R&D in view of the proprietary disclosure cost derived from competitors’ learning about firm’s R&D projects. In sum, our findings largely speak to several GRF project objectives: the objective (1) (although it is not IPO price but the stock price performance), objective (3) (managerial incentives pertaining to cost information disclosure) and objective (4) (cost and benefit of enhanced cost information). Another important cost item pertains to firm’s investment. I am particularly interested in the cost structure of investments within a firm (i.e., how investment costs distribute across divisions of a conglomerate firm). In the paper “Division Managers’ Private Information and Capital Investment: Exploiting External Social Connections as an Information Source,” I work with my HKU colleagues on the idea of firms allocating investments among divisions in response to the perceived local information advantage of divisional managers. We also investigate the market consequences of this investment cost allocation. Please see the paper attached to this report in Part C (“under review” research output & the conference paper). This study helps to realize the GRF project objective (2) (market impact) and objective (3) (managerial incentive). As the corresponding author of this study, I submitted this paper for journal review at Journal of Accounting and Economics (See the JAE manuscript # in the attached PDF file in Part C). Although it was rejected by JAE last month, we have already submitted this manuscript to Contemporary Accounting Research (CAR) and now it is still under the journal review at CAR. This paper was also accepted for presentation at the HARC conference (see Part C). In the third project, I coauthored with Chen Xia, Cheng Qiang and Alvis Lo. This paper was recently accepted by Journal of Business Finance & Accounting (JBFA) which is a decent “B+” journal at HKU. The paper is titled “CEO contractual protection and debt contracting” (see Part C for the journal publication). I submitted to JBFA in 2019 and received the acceptance letter in in 2022. For the purpose of full disclosure, this project was originally a concurrent project with the GRF proposal when I started to write the proposal in 2017 (recall that GRF outcomes were announced in 2018). In its first version in 2017 (i.e., before the GRF announcement), we only simply extended the other journal publication (Chen et al. 2015) by examining the cost of debt. With the GRF project going on, I realize that the cost disclosure for management severance package is a vital factor for the framework of this story. We hand-collected several key cost items for the severance package offered to firm CEOs as disclosed in the firm’s filings, including the monetary terms of the severance payment and the contingent non-monetary benefits. The sample size is significantly extended to S&P 1500 firms. The collection of compensation cost items greatly improves the sophistication of the cost proxy, leading to significant results consistent with our expectations. The new version tells that the disclosed compensation costs affect loan lenders’ response to the perceived managerial risk-taking incentives. Without this knowledge developed concurrently from the GRF proposal and also the RAs hired under this GRF project, we will not be able to further develop this project of CEO contractual protection into a journal publication. This paper realizes several objectives of this GRF proposal, including the role of cost information disclosure in the pricing (of the loans) and loan lenders’ conservatism (objectives (1) and (2)) and the trade-off the costs and benefits of compensation disclosure transparency from the perspective of firm’s access to debt market (objective (4)). Collectively, the abovementioned papers (working paper, conference paper and journal publication) help to realize all the objectives of our GRF proposal to a great extent.

17500918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500918.value: I developed three papers from the funding of this GRF project. I am the corresponding author for all the three papers. In the paper “R&D Disclosure Change and Innovation Investments: Evidence from Retroactive Adjustments in R&D expenses” (it is an “under preparation” paper in Section 8 of Part C), we find that the retroactive adjustment to R&D costs, as mandated by the new disclosure regulation, has an impact on managers’ risk-taking. We further show that the upward (downward) adjustments reflect managers’ differential incentives to understate (overstate) the R&D costs in the previous year. The second paper “Division Managers’ Private Information and Capital Investment: Exploiting External Social Connections as an Information Source” is currently under journal review and was accepted for conference presentation (it is an “under review” paper and also a conference paper in Section 8 of Part C). Our results suggest that headquarters CEOs of conglomerates strategically allocate higher costs of investment to the business divisions with divisional managers being socially connected with the CEOs of industry peers. I submitted this paper to a top accounting journal as the first try and it is now under the review of the journal Contemporary Accounting Research. In the third paper, titled “CEO contractual protection and debt contracting,” we examine how the disclosed details of management compensation costs affect the lenders’ debt pricing. Compared with other loans, loans issued by firms with CEOs being protected by higher severance payment costs (and better employment contracts) on average contain more performance covenants and performance-pricing provisions. Please note that this paper was originally a concurrent research in 2017 when I was preparing the GRF proposal in the same year (and submitted the GRF proposal in 2017). The on-going GRF projects also bring the great opportunity to significantly re-write this concurrent paper. We explicitly incorporate the concept of disclosed firm cost (i.e., the detailed cost items related to CEOs’ severance package) and expand the scale of sample collection to include the whole group S&P1500 firms. This paper was submitted to Journal of Business Finance & Accounting (JBFA) in 2019 and accepted for publication in 2022 (it is the journal publication in Section 8 of Part C). Furthermore, a case is developed for the Asia Case Research Center (case title: MADISON HOLDINGS: ACCOUNTING FOR A CRYPTOCURRENCY MINING BUSINESS). This case demonstrates the costing method for a HK-listed firm’s cryptocurrency asset and managerial incentives underlying accounting choices.

17500918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500918.value: The 2018 regulation requires Chinese listed firms to present R&D expenses in the income statement as a separate line item. The change in R&D reporting provides unique research opportunities for future study. Specifically, we can investigate how such a mandatory change in the presentation format of firms’ R&D expense affects the valuation of the reported R&D expense from investors’ point of view. Such a change in the valuation of R&D costs should have considered the potential changes in managerial behavior induced by this format change. To conduct this research, we need to hand-collect the R&D expenses as disclosed in the footnotes of the annual reports in the pre-2018 period. Our traditional CSMAR database often omits the data in the footnote disclosures and hence we have to rely more on manual collection.

17500918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500918.value: A series of research findings are derived from this GRF project. We find that the enhanced disclosures of firm’s cost items, especially those pertaining to R&D activities, investments, and management compensations, have an impact on managers’ risk-taking and within-firm capital allocation. In addition, such an enhancement in cost disclosure affects the stock performance from the equity investors’ perspective and the loan pricing from the creditors’ perspective. Accordingly, in view of the costs and benefits induced by the cost structure disclosures, managers tend to make accounting discretions in their decisions on cost recognition and disclosures.

17501518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501518.value: It has become increasingly popular for investors to seek information from social media when they make investment decisions. Although previous research has shown that sentiment analysis in social media may help predict future stock returns, inconsistent results have been reported and there is a lack of research in applying data analytics on understanding the effect of moderators in stock opinions on future stock performance. Investigating such effect can be crucial in understanding why inconsistent results exist and creating a strategic value for investors and shareholders. Using social media data from an investment forum, we propose to explore the effect of moderators in stock opinions on stock returns in terms of three aspects involving the quality of article, author’s position, and author's popularity. We will also propose and evaluate trading strategies based on these moderators. The results of our findings and applications will be useful for both researchers and practitioners. 投資者依靠社交媒體中的信息進行投資決策已經變得愈發流行。儘管先前的研究表明社交媒體中的情緒分析可以預測股票收益， 但所得結論並不一致。運用數據分析的方法探究股票觀點與未來股票收益關係中的調節因素仍值得研究。這對於解釋之前研究中存在的不同結論，以及幫助投資者和利益相關者創造有價值的策略都意義重大。利用投資論壇中社交媒體的數據，我們提出研究股票觀點與股票收益關係中的調節變量。 這些調節變量包括文章質量、作者的持倉狀況、和作者的受歡迎程度。我們將評估基於這些調節變量的不同交易策略。我們的研究成果對研究者和從業者都有一定的貢獻。

17501518.label: Realisation of objectives
17501518.value: Both project objectives have been successfully achieved. We have comprehensively studied the moderating role of article quality, author’s position, and author’s popularity, on the effect of sentiment level in social media on predicting stock return using data from various sources. Statistical tests were conducted to validate our hypotheses. We also devised a trading strategy using sentiment level in social media and the proposed moderators, and used simulation to show that the proposed strategy achieved better potential trading profits than using only sentiment.

17501518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501518.value: Literature has shown the sentiment of social media articles is associated with stock return. Using data from SeekingAlpha, we study find that the author’s current position (i.e., a long or a short position on the specific stock involved) can have a substantial effect on future stock performance. It also moderates the relationship between sentiment level and future stock return. We also found that the author’s popularity has a significantly positive effect on the stock performance in the short term. It also partially moderates the relationship between sentiment level and future stock performance. In addition, we found that when we combine these variables, a simple trading strategy can achieve a better potential profit than using sentiment level alone.

17501518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501518.value: While the current trading strategy is based on simple rules, it is possible to devise more advanced trading strategies using machine learning methods. We are currently working on this direction. A journal paper will be submitted for publication shortly.

17501518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501518.value: Our study investigates how social media articles can predict stock return. Besides the sentiment level expressed in the text of these articles, our study has found that author's attributes, such as author's declared holding position and popularity, are also important in the prediction and can moderate the prediction power of the sentiment level. It is also possible to devise a simple trading strategy using these variables that is more profitable than using the sentiment level only.
