17603918.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603918.value: China’s rise and its accession to global trade rules have become the subject of much commentary, but there has yet to be a comprehensive and in-depth study of China’s impact on global antirust policy. This research identifies the idiosyncrasies underlying China’s enforcement of antitrust law. It reveals that agencies are particularly adept at applying media strategies to strategically deter firms from challenging the authority and enticing them to cooperate. And while agencies are largely free of judicial constraints, they remain subject to severe bureaucratic constraints. The missions, cultures and the structures of the agencies have a significant impact on the enforcement priority, regulatory approach and the final outcome of a case.

17603918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603918.value: I am applying my findings of this research to a new setting relating to Chinese regulation of big tech. I will explore the bureaucratic incentives in responding to the top leadership’s call to tighten regulatory scrutiny over big tech. I will also continue with this research by examining the reputation sanctions placed on big tech, as well as the strategies of big tech in responding to government regulation.

17603918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603918.value: Antitrust first originated as policies designed to correct market failures in western democracies. However, this research finds that antitrust has become a multi-functional regulatory tool in the hands of the Chinese government. In relentless attempts to expand their bureaucratic turf, Chinese administrative agencies have deployed the Anti-Monopoly Law to not only tackle monopolies but also to achieve their policy objectives to control and stabilize prices. At the same time, Chinese antitrust agencies are seldom challenged in court as they possess vast administrative discretion and are adept at applying media strategies aimed at enticing firms to yield to their demands. The Chinese example of enforcing antitrust law demonstrates the importance of having adequate institutional safeguards for antitrust enforcement. This research has proven incredibly timely and attracted media inquiries from numerous media outlets including the Wall Street Journal, Financial Times and the Economist. Commentaries based on this research have also appeared in Nikkei Asia Review, Bloomberg and Project Syndicate.

17604318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604318.value: In recent years, a rich body of work examining how ‘legal norms are developed, conveyed and settled transnationally’ has emerged, ‘integrating both bottom-up and top-down analyses’ (Halliday & Shaffer, 2015). This growing body of work on ‘transnational legal ordering’ (Halliday, 2015) is significant given the increasing involvement of public and private actors in the creation of legal norms beyond the nation state (Twining, 2000; Zumbansen, 2010; Tamanaha, 2000; Halliday & Shaffer, 2015). At the same time, it has been recognised that participation in global norm-making has not, in many cases, been representative of the diversity of global actors, with historically limited representation by non-western states. The aim of the proposed research project is to address this gap by systematically analysing the role of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law Regional Centre for Asia and the Pacific (UNCITRAL RCAP), established in 2012, in coordinating with private and public sector institutions in East Asia in the development, interpretation and application of global cross-border dispute settlement guidelines. Since the mid-1950s, UNCITRAL has engaged in a process of global model law drafting, including most recently its revised Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration and Rules on Transparency in Treaty-based Investor-State Arbitration. While such guidelines provide for regional adaptation, the extent to which they reflect expanded representation in global law-making at both the vertical (between global institutions and individual citizens) and horizontal (between states and international organisations) levels requires further examination. Drawing on a mixed empirical methodology, this study will seek to distil positive lessons from UNCITRAL RCAP's efforts at ‘decentralized transnational law engagement’, elucidate regional dynamics, and glean best practices in the form of law and policy recommendations. 近年出現了一系列豐富的研究，研究「如何跨國發展、傳達和建立法律規範」，並「整合自下而上和自上而下的分析」(Halliday & Shaffer, 2015)。由於公共和私人人士在製定跨越國家之法律規範中的參與日益增加(Twining, 2000; Zumbansen, 2010; Tamanaha, 2000; Halliday & Shaffer, 2015)，此類越來越多的「跨國法律秩序」 (Halliday, 2015)研究意義重大 。與此同時，我們意識到在許多情況下，制定全球準則的參與過程並不代表全球的多樣性，如歷年非西方國家的代表性有限。建議研究項目的目的是通過系統分析於2012年成立的聯合國國際貿易法委員會亞洲及太平洋區域中心(UNCITRAL RCAP)在協調東亞私營和公共部門機構製定、解釋和應用解決全球跨境爭端指南的角色。自20世紀50年代中期以來，貿易法委員會參與了全球法律範本的起草，其中包括最近修訂的“國際商事仲裁示範法”和“投資人與國家間基於條約仲裁透明度規則”。雖然這些指南容許區域適應微調，但越來越多的研究工作正在倡議在縱向（全球機構和個別公民之間）和橫向（國家和國際組織之間）兩個層面擴大全球立法的代表性（Alvarez，2007），以通過更有效的參與（Alvarez，2007）、外來保證（Halliday和Carruthers，2007）、區域適應微調（Ali，2010）和跨界別代表（Wheatley，2010）加強合法性。為了回應這種倡議，本研究將尋求從“分散的跨國法律參與”中汲取正面教訓，闡明區域動態，並以法律和政策建議的形式得出最佳做法。

17604318.label: Realisation of objectives
17604318.value: Each of the research objectives of this project has been achieved. They will be discussed in detail below: I. First Objective: To analyze contributions from Asia Pacific members, alongside other members of the global community, in the development and refinement of UNCITRAL dispute settlement instruments including its Model Law on international arbitration and transparency rules based on regional case interpretation and practice insights. The chief culminating output of the project, Forming Transnational Dispute Settlement Norms: Soft Law and the Role of UNCITRAL's Regional Centre for Asia and the Pacific (Edward Elgar, 2021) provides in depth analysis, through survey data, case studies and UNCITRAL working group participation records, of the contributions of Asia Pacific states in the development and refinement of UNCITRAL dispute settlement instruments. According to one reviewer, Professor Kevin E. Davis of NYU School of Law, “This study of the growing role of Asia-Pacific countries in the governance of international dispute resolution combines sophisticated treatments of the relevant legal instruments and theoretical literature with rigorous empirical analyses." In reference to the work, Professor Simon Chesterman of NUS Law notes that "International law poses a dilemma for emerging markets. Politically, former colonies rightly expect more of a say in its content; economically, stability and consistency may be more conducive to development. This illuminating new book describes decentralised transnational legal ordering as one outcome of this tension, tracking the activities of UNCITRAL’s Regional Centre for Asia and the Pacific and the manner in which it has enhanced the legitimacy — and, perhaps, the effectiveness — of global norm-making." Professor Hiroshi Fukurai observes that the research provides "vital alternatives to the hegemonic narrative of International arbitration and mediation. Not only a “must-read,” but of urgent relevance to democratic resolutions of disputes in Asia and across the globe." II. Second Objective: To examine whether, and if so how, decentralised engagement in soft law-making through UNCITRAL RCAP is helping to overcome the vertical and horizontal representational deficits in the global soft law-making process. The second objective is addressed in the Edward Elgar publication. According to another reviewer, Anselmo Reyes of the Singapore International Commercial Court, the book "considers the importance of soft law in developing transnational commercial legal norms... and examines how Asia Pacific states have shaped and are being shaped by those norms. The book achieves its objectives through empirical and theoretical analyses and concludes by reflecting on the balance to be struck between centralised and regional approaches to globalisation." III. Third Objective: To test the proposition that the presence of regional centres has the potential to expand participation in global soft law-making processes. The second and third part of the book respectively address whether and to what extent regional centres expand participation in global soft-law making. Part II of the book presents RCAP case studies by examining Asia Pacific state participation through tracking oral contributions made during UNCITRAL Working Group meetings focused on the development of the: Singapore Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation (Ch. 5); UNCITRAL Working Group III deliberations on investor–state arbitration reform (Ch. 6); Transparency rules (Ch. 7); Online dispute resolution (Ch. 8); the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration (Ch. 9) and Conciliation Rules (Ch. 10). Part III of the book presents further empirical findings from survey data of Asia Pacific dispute resolution practitioners regarding the contribution of the RCAP in extending regional representation. João Ribeiro-Bidaoui, First Secretary at the Permanent Bureau of the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH); Head of the UNCITRAL Regional Centre for Asia and the Pacific (2013-2018) notes that: “It is rare to have 5 years of our work performance scrutinized academically, and peer-reviewed. I cannot escape a sense of relief after reading this remarkable work by Professor Shahla Ali. Her work shows the importance of having more Regional Offices, not only of UNCITRAL, but, I dare to say, also of the HCCH and UNIDROIT. This book demonstrates how they are key enablers of legal reforms and relevant platforms to ensure equal access to legal knowledge. One of the possible conclusions reading this book, is that such work reduces non-tariff (sometimes invisible) trade barriers, and has tremendous side effects like levelling the playing field for practitioners and legal educators from parts of the world often meriting less attention and resources. For example, without such work, we would have never seen DPR Korea or Laos adopting the CISG and its core value: party autonomy. This book is indispensable for any one engaged with legal reforms based on international cooperation.” Professor Kevin E. Davis of NYU Law adds that "it is impossible to ignore this evidence of decentralized transnational legal ordering and how it might be fostered by regional institutions.” IV. Fourth Objective: To suggest revisions to UNCITRAL’s assessment indicators measuring regional engagement to reflect emerging insights regarding best practices in decentralised engagement. The fourth chapter of the book considers "Indicators of representation in global governance: assessing regional engagement, representation and diversity through UNCITRAL RCAP" (Ch. 4) and suggests revisions and recommendations for the design of a new set of indicators to track regional participation. V. Fifth Objective: To contribute to the ongoing theoretical discussion on the role of regional actors, including courts and arbitral institutions, in transnational norm formation. The final two chapters, "Extending soft law representation through regional centres:empirical analysis (Ch. 11) and "Conclusions" (Ch. 12) address the role of regional actors including courts and arbitral institutions in transnational norm formation. International arbitration practitioners have noted the value of the work. Professor William W. Park of Boston University and a practicing international arbitrator notes that the study is an "impressive work on a vital subject," and Anselmo Reyes of the Singapore International Commercial Court notes that, "at a time when many Asia-Pacific jurisdictions are seeking to transform themselves into international commercial dispute resolution hubs for the post-COVID-19 era, [the book] deserves a wide readership." Scholarly contribution: The The project resulted in 1 book (ranked A by RQF), 1 edited volume, 7 journal articles/book chapters and 17 conference contributions. Under-Expenditure of Budget/COVID-19: Given the outbreak of COVID-19 two thirds of the way through the project time line, data collection, research and conference participation was conducted virtually, where possible, in order to achieve the research objectives in light of public health guidelines. This accounts for the overall project cost savings.

17604318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604318.value: The study’s key findings, drawing on in-depth case studies, a survey and quantitative analysis of UNCITRAL working group participation logs suggest that regional centers, such as the UNCITRAL Regional Centre for the Asia-Pacific while still in their infancy, have corresponded with the emergence of a new form of “decentralized transnational legal ordering” associated with growing regional engagement and participation in global soft law design. This is evidenced by a 63% increase in the frequency of Asia-Pacific regional input in WG II meetings, an 8% increase in official Asia-Pacific representation in the WG II, a 6.2% increase in the number of observers from the Asia-Pacific region, and an average increase of 32% in perceived levels of engagement and participation amongst regional stakeholders over a 7 year period. Specifically, survey respondents reported an increase of 34% in the ‘presence of mechanisms allowing a wide range of voices to be heard,’ an increase of 35% in ‘pro-active engagement with relevant stakeholders,’ an increase of 25% in perceived ‘participation of delegations in the sessions of Working Group II’, and a 34% increase in ‘understanding of UNCITRAL instruments amongst diverse stakeholders for enactment of legislation based on the Model Law’ since the establishment of the RCAP in 2012. For each of UNCITRAL’s dispute resolution instruments, following the opening of the Regional Centre, increased adoption trends in the Region are also evident. This has included an increase of 100% in adoption of the Conciliation Rules and an increase of 38% in adoption of the Model Law. To date, 21 regions in the Asia-Pacific are amongst a total of 53 states on a global level to have adopted the Singapore Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation. The study finds that the direction of decentralized transnational engagement is mutual – it moves both from the global to the regional and vice versa. In addition to regional adaptation of UNCITRAL text, nearly a quarter of respondents, or 24% believed that unique approaches to the interpretation and implementation of the UNCITRAL model instruments in the Asia-Pacific have informed UNCITRAL developments in other regions and globally.

17604318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604318.value: There is a strong potential for further development of the research. In particular, much remains to be examined regarding prospects for the further development and expansion of regional centres and the nature and dynamics of 'decentralised transnational legal ordering.' Specifically, given the backdrop of historically uneven representation in global institutions, efforts to expand engagement and inclusivity in global law making aims to strengthen legitimacy through more inclusive representation and regional adaptation. The substantive findings of this book provide useful insights supporting the expansion of regional centres in areas with historically limited representation in global law making including from within Africa, the Middle East and South America. From a methodological perspective, the study contributes to the development of a new approach to tracking the frequency of participation in global soft law making bodies through coding Working Group participation records. Future studies by a growing number of researchers will no doubt advance insights into the application of this new set of indicators by tracking the dynamics of diversity, participation and voice in global governance institutions.

17604318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604318.value: This study examines whether regional centres associated with global legal institutions facilitate expanded citizen engagement in global soft law making. It carries out a novel analysis of the influence of regional centres on overcoming representational deficits in the design of global cross-border dispute settlement norms. It does this by comparing the impact of two forms of engagement in the Asia-Pacific region, traditional ‘centralised’ engagement, and a ‘decentralised’ form, on the soft law-making process over a 10 year period. Through an analysis of empirical research into the role of decentralized soft law making in the East Asian region, the project investigates the influence of such regional centres in overcoming representational deficits. Analysis of survey data, case studies and UNCITRAL participation records, provide a comprehensive view of the contributions of Asia Pacific states in the development and refinement of UNCITRAL dispute settlement instruments. The formation of a regional centre of UNCITRAL in the Asia Pacific has corresponded with the emergence of a new form of decentralized transnational legal ordering, advancing representation and legal innovation at both regional and global levels. The study concludes that these findings support the expansion of regional centres in areas with historically limited representation in global law making.

17605118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605118.value: 听觉康复的目标是帮助听障儿童获取言语语言的最大潜能，使之融入主流社会，并使其对社会的贡献最大化。听觉康复主要包含了调试助听器或人工耳蜗，随后是多年的听觉训练和言语语言治疗。研究已经证实英语国家听障儿童使用人工耳蜗的有效性，因此中国政府和慈善机构在本国致力于资助人工耳蜗。然而普通话听障儿童使用人工耳蜗的长时效用还鲜少知晓，部分原因归咎于缺少标准的言语感知测试工具。临床工作者缺少系统的方式来确定言语感知特定领域或进行言语训练和助听设备的调试。 现有的普通话言语感知测试有较多不足。他们没有全面测试言语感知或测试花费的时间太长，因此不适用于注意力时间短的孩子。最为重要的是，没有评估心理测量学性能，也没有评估代表日常生活环境的噪声下言语感知。由于测试项和测试方式不同，朱等人报导了不一致的结果(Zhu, Wong, Chen et al., 2015a)。 因此，该研究项目会开发一套普通话声母韵母分辨测试并验证其有效性。与之前由朱等人开发的普通话声调识别测试一起组成一款普通话言语感知量表(the MTIT, Zhu, Wong, & Chen et al., 2014a)。研究方法基于研发人员开发普通话声调测试和普通话言语感知与发音的经验(Li & To, 2017; Zhu, Wong, Chen et al., 2015b)。初期的研究已经开发并评估了声母分辨测试材料。该研究包含了七个阶段的开发和录制测试项，收集3-6岁健听儿童的正常数据。通过测试听障儿童来评估该量表的敏感度、信度和效度。基于之前此项目主要负责人的研究，此项目会招募656名儿童，这将会是第一个评估听障孩子普通话言语感知量表。该研究的结果将会报导助听设备的效果，为临床工作者确认需要提高的领域，帮助决定基金的分配以及政策的制定。

17605118.label: Realisation of objectives
17605118.value: Objective 1: To continue developing a Mandarin consonant discrimination test to evaluate consonant perception in children with hearing impairment (HI). Test items were chosen from kindergarten textbooks and evaluated for age appropriateness, to create the materials for the Mandarin Consonant Discrimination Test (MCDT). Minimal pairs of the same tones, same syllabic structure and same vowels were formed. Two native and standard Mandarin-speaking male voice actors recorded the test materials and the best recordings were selected based on ratings from native speakers. A speech spectrum-shaped Noise (SSN) that has the same long-term average spectrum and level as the test words, was created. A custom software program was created to control the signals, administer the tests in quiet and in noise and score the tests. The test program was refined throughout the research to ensure the test could be administered most efficiently and in a user friendly manner. The program reports findings on individual speech sounds, categorize results according to place and manner of articulation as well as aspiration for consonant discrimination, and allows comparison of findings to children with normal hearing. Objective 2: To develop a Mandarin vowel discrimination test to evaluate vowel perception in children with hearing impairment (HI). The procedures used above to develop the MCDT were also used to develop materials for the Mandarin Vowel Discrimination Test (MVDT), except the contrastive pairs in the MVDT were made according to Lee’s criteria of low contrast vowel identification test (2003), as described in the proposal. Vowel discrimination was evaluated in native Mandarin-speaking children aged 4 to 6. Ceiling performance was observed in quiet, but Mandarin vowel discrimination in noise is not fully mastered by children aged 4 to 6. Future studies with larger samples at more adverse noise levels should be conducted to evaluate the developmental trends of Mandarin vowel perception. A manuscript describing the development of vowel discrimination in normal hearing children is being prepared. Objective 3: To evaluate the sensitivity, reliability and validity of these test materials to ensure repeatable results and these are appropriate measures of consonant and vowel perception. Tests for evaluating consonant and vowel discrimination have been developed and data collected on normal hearing children showed good test sensitivity and face validity. The relationships between performance and age as well as aided hearing level and test conditions suggest that this newly designed test battery is able to reflect the impact of the degree of hearing loss and test conditions on speech perception, consistent with good predictive validity. The difference in performance between children with normal and impaired hearing also suggests good discriminant validity. The evaluation of test-retest reliability and concurrent validity was planned by relating results on the MCDT and MVDT to those obtained on the MPSI. These evaluations could not be carried out as testing was interrupted by the pandemic. Reduction of the number of items using Rasch model and item analysis was attempted to reduce test items and time without losing the ability of the test to evaluate performance. Item analysis was conducted. Due to the small samples that these results are based on, the investigators are not completely confident about these results. More testing will be conducted post pandemic to increase the sample size. Objective 4: To document the development of consonant perception in children with normal and impaired hearing. Performance on the MCDT was obtained in children with NH (ages 4;0 to 8;9). The custom program randomized the order of minimal pairs and S/Ns, administered the test as planned in the research proposal and recorded participant responses. Consonant discrimination in quiet and in noise improved as normal hearing children became older. The discrimination of consonants varied and listening in noise is more difficult. These results can serve as normative reference for comparison with children with hearing loss. Two other manuscripts focusing on the development of consonant and vowel discrimination in children with hearing loss will be written. Consonant discrimination was evaluated in children with hearing loss and compared to normative data obtained on children with normal hearing. As expected, despite being fitted with hearing devices early, children with hearing loss were performing poorly compared to aged peers with normal hearing. The ability to discriminate consonant pairs varied with age and noise level. A stepwise multiple linear regression analysis years of education and aided hearing thresholds related significantly to consonant discrimination ability. Once these factors have been included, hearing age, unaided hearing and maternal education level were not significant factors, which differs from findings from previous research (e.g., Chen, Wong et al, 2015). The small sample size might have contributed to the non-significant relationships. Interestingly, children using cochlear implants performed better than those using hearing aids despite having poorer unaided hearing. The hearing level of children using cochlear implants was comparable to those of children using hearing aids. In fact, children using cochlear implant were better at discriminating speech sounds than those with hearing aids, suggesting not only positive effects with cochlear implants but also the importance of early implantation despite the dubious costs involved. Government agencies as well as ENTs and audiologists should actively recommend the use of cochlear implants for better hearing among children with severe to profound hearing loss. Conclusion The sample sizes at various stages of the study were smaller than planned as initially there were difficulties recruiting schools to participate in the research because regulations on school participation in research project has been tightened in mainland China. Participants were recruited via personal contact and referrals. Data collection was later disrupted by the pandemic, due to lockdown and closure of schools and hearing clinics. Despite these challenges, developmental changes in the ability to discriminate speech sounds were revealed among children with normal hearing and hearing loss. When the situation allows, more data will be collected to better address some of the objectives above (e.g., normative data can be reported in 6-month intervals, instead of 1-year; test-retest reliability). Together with the Mandarin Tone Identification Test (MTIT), they will make up a battery of Mandarin segmental perception tests for evaluating children with HI and possibly those with other speech perception problems. Further research will apply the battery to the evaluation of Mandarin speaking children. The battery will be made available to clinicians and researchers via a material transfer agreement. They will be trained to use it via workshops and feedback will be collected to improve the test and its administration via the custom program. References Chen Y, Wong LLN, ..., & Xi, X. (2015). 17605118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605118.value: The recent pandemic has restricted data collection to a large extent because school principals and clinicians hesitated in referring children for testing and parents also did not feel comfortable attending test sessions. Thus, we were not able to collect all data needed to meet the objectives of the study. Nonetheless, based on the data we collected prior to the pandemic, we were able to examine consonant and vowel perception in normal hearing children as well as consonant perception in a small group of children with hearing loss. The study was the first to reveal typical perceptual development of Mandarin consonant and vowel discrimination in children and can serve as a reference for comparison with children with disordered perceptual development, such as those with hearing loss. A significant main effect of age, test conditions, and an interaction effect between these variables was noted. Consonant discrimination in quiet and in noise improved as children became older. Consonants that were difficult to discriminate in quiet and in noise are mainly velar contrasts. Noise seems to have less effect on the discrimination of affricates and fricatives, and plosives seem to be more difficult to discriminate in noise than in quiet. Place contrasts between alveolar and palato-alveolar consonants were difficult in quiet. Discrimination of nasalized high front vowels in quiet were significantly worse than other types of vowels, among young children aged 4 to 6 with normal hearing. In noise, performance was similar among vowel pairs with similar or distinct vowel heights. Although performance in quiet were near ceiling among many children, they have not fully mastered the discrimination of Mandarin vowels. Mid to high front vowels with nasal finals were difficult even in quiet. In noise, developmental improvement was observed across the age range for /i-u, ai-iao, an-un/ (which were vowel pairs with similar vowel heights). Surprisingly, the presence of noise did not greatly impact the discrimination of vowels in noise, and previous research from our lab suggests that the tonal nature of the language could contribute to better discrimination, compared to English. Among children who use hearing aids and cochlear implants, developmental improvement was observed across the age groups. While the discrimination of consonants was more difficult compared to children with normal hearing, results showed benefits from the use of bimodal (hearing aid on one ear and cochlear implant on the other ear) listening.

17605118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605118.value: Speech discrimination is affected by hearing loss but little research has been performed to understand Mandarin consonant and vowel discrimination in children with hearing loss. Although hearing aids and cochlear implants have been proven effective means of rehabilitation clinically, little is known about whether the effectiveness of these devices on enhancing Mandarin discrimination is optimized. Although data collection of this research was impacted by the pandemic, test stimuli and software to run the tests have been prepared and ready for future testing should funding be available after the pandemic. Funding from hearing device industry, GRF, and/or other sources will be sought. Future studies with larger groups of younger children at more adverse noise levels and degrees of hearing loss will be conducted to evaluate the developmental trends of Mandarin consonant and vowel development. Their performance can be referred to that of aged peers with normal hearing, to suggest areas of rehabilitation for clinicians to work on and to inform the design of speech processing algorithms and prescription methods to target better speech understanding. With these data, the tasks developed in the present research can be shortened for use in clinical situations.

17605118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605118.value: Speech discrimination is affected by hearing loss but few research has been performed to understand Mandarin consonant and vowel discrimination in children with hearing loss. This research is the first to systematically examine Mandarin consonant and vowel discrimination in quiet and in noise and provides information on the types of consonants and vowels that maybe confusing to children with hearing loss, while considering the impact of age and development. With this information, clinicians will be able to identify speech sounds that require more attention and appropriate training could be provided to address the specific needs of individual children. Although hearing aids and cochlear implants have been proven effective means of rehabilitation clinically, little is known about whether the effectiveness of these devices on enhancing Mandarin discrimination is optimized. Hearing device manufacturers have modified prescriptive methods and signal processing algorithms to cater for Mandarin speakers, assuming that certain features should be enhanced but direct evidence on the effectiveness of these modifications has not been examined. The present research thus provides an efficient tool to assess outcomes with these devices and provides information to manufacturers to improve their devices.

17605518.value: Prof Benson, Philip Prof Ma, Qing Dr Wang, Qiu

17605518.label: Project Objectives
17605518.value:  To identify key dimensions of technology-enhanced out-of-class language learning experience that are critical to vocabulary knowledge and to understand how these key dimensions are associated with and predict learners’ vocabulary knowledge.  To understand what and how learner factors and learning context factors may moderate the influences of these key learning experience dimensions on learners’ vocabulary knowledge.
rows:  To identify key dimensions of technology-enhanced out-of-class language learning experience that are critical to vocabulary knowledge and to understand how these key dimensions are associated with and predict learners’ vocabulary knowledge.
 To understand what and how learner factors and learning context factors may moderate the influences of these key learning experience dimensions on learners’ vocabulary knowledge.

17605518.label: Realisation of objectives
17605518.value: Objective 1: A taxonomy of the key dimensions of technology-enhanced out-of-class language learning experience that are critical to vocabulary knowledge is developed based on a synthesis of relevant literature and an interview and diary study with 47 English language learners from two universities. This taxonomy consists of six dimensions (balance of medium used; balance of contextualized learning; balance of attentional focus when interacting with the resources; dual attention to both meaning and language focus; depth of lexical information learners attend to; and involvement load). Mann-Whitney U tests of the manifestation of the six dimensions among learners with high and low vocabulary knowledge suggests that access to multimedia resources, dual attention to both meaning and form, and deeper processing of the vocabulary correlated significantly with vocabulary scores. This research finding is report in a paper published in Language Learning & Technology. In addition, 695 survey responses and vocabulary and reading tests were collected from English language learners from three universities to test the conceptual model revealed from the qualitative phase of the study. A structural model has been generated through analyzing structural equation modeling of the survey and test data. A journal paper is in preparation and plans to be submitted Computers & Education. Objective 2: Analysis of the 695 survey responses and test scores revealed a few learner and contextual factors that influence self-directed technological experience and its relationship with vocabulary and reading. A few learner factors have been identified through a structural equation modeling analysis, including subject-matter interest, the integration of personal interest with subject learning and self-regulation. These three learner factors are found to interplay with each other to shape different types of self-directed technolgoical experiences differently. This research findings is reported in a paper currently under review at British Journal of Educational Technology. Moreover, vocabulary learning strategy is found to moderate the link between information-oriented technological expeirence and learners' vocabulary knoweldge. This finding is to be reported in a paper under preparation that is planned to be submitted to TESOL Quarterly. The project further revealed that different types of teacher support influenced different types of self-directed technological activities differently via self-efficacy, enjoyment and perceived usefulness. The research finding is in preparation and plan to be submitted to Computer Assisted Language Learning.

17605518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605518.value: Major research findings: a taxonomy of key dimensions of technology-enhanced out-of-class language learning experience that are essential to vocabulary knowledge is developed and empirically tested. Relevant research findings are reported in a journal paper published in Language Learning & Technology and another paper in preparation to be submitted to Computers & Education). Statistical modeling of the survey data and vocabulary and reading test scores revealed some essential learner variables and learning context variables that are critical to the relationship including interest and self-regulation. Relevant research findings are reported in a journal paper under review at British Journal of Educational Technology, one research paper being drafted to be submitted to TESOL Quarterly and another paper in preparation to be submitted to Computer Assisted Language Learning.

17605518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605518.value: As this study revealed a few learner and learning context variables that influence the relationship of self-directed technological experiences and vocabulary knowledge, further development of the research will focus on delving deeper into these learner and learning context variables. Specifically: Since vocabulary learning strategy is found to be a significant moderator of the relationship between self-directed technological experience and vocabulary knowledge, further development of the research will focus on examining the efficacy of relevant vocabulary learning strategy training. Furthermore, as different types of teacher support influenced different types of self-directed technological experience, further development of the research will focus on examining the longitudinal interaction of teacher support and self-directed technological expeirences over time.

17605518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605518.value: Out-of-class learning constitutes an important context of second language development, and the quality of learners’ out-of-class learning experience directly influences their language gains and confidence and enjoyment of learning. It is thus important to understand what constitutes quality out-of-class autonomous language learning. This project focused on identifying important characteristics of out-of-class learning experience that are essential vocabulary knowledge development. It found that access to multimedia resources, dual attention to both meaning and form, and deeper processing of the vocabulary correlated significantly with vocabulary scores. Moreover, it revealed that learners' English learning interest, the integration of personal interest into English language learning and self-regulation are important learner variables and teacher support is an important learning context variable that influence learners' technological experiences.

17605618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605618.value: BACKGROUND: The consequences of stigma and discrimination on persons with mental illness and their family caregivers are so pervasive that they may become the main impediment to rehabilitation and recovery of persons with mental illness. Although evidence shows that increasing contact with people with mental illness can reduce stigmatizing attitudes and behaviors in general public, it is uncertain whether increasing contact interventions for family caregivers of relatives with schizophrenia may reduce family caregivers’ self-stigma and burden of care, and improve patients’ treatment and recovery. Moreover, there is no study to explore the long-term (e.g., 9-month follow-up) effectiveness of anti-stigma intervention for family caregivers through increasing contact with persons with schizophrenia, especially in Chinese context. OBJECTIVE: The proposed randomized controlled trial will test the short (post-intervention) and long-term (9-month follow-up) effectiveness of a newly developed Enhancing Contact Model (ECM) Intervention for reducing self-stigma in family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia, and will examine whether ECM is more effective on reducing self-stigma than Psychoeducational Family Intervention (PFI). METHOD: We will recruit 231 family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia identified in the mental health survey (2015) in six townships in Xinjin, Chengdu, China. The family caregivers will be randomly assigned to 1) ECM group, 2) PFI group, or 3) Control group. The ECM groups will receive enhancing contact model intervention from health professionals using ECM plan to improve their knowledge of schizophrenia, and enhance their positive contact with relatives with schizophrenia (individual contact) and other peer family caregivers with relatives with schizophrenia (group contact). The PFI groups will receive psychoeducational family intervention from health professionals using PFI plan to improve their knowledge of schizophrenia on causes, treatment and recovery. The Control groups will be visited regularly without any further interventions. All participants will complete questionnaires (e.g., self-stigma, burden of care, quality of life) at 4 times points: baseline prior to randomization, post-intervention, 3-month post-intervention, and 9-month post-intervention. Relatives with schizophrenia will also be assessed, such as their treatment compliance and psychiatric symptoms. IMPACTS: This study will generate new knowledge of new ECM intervention for family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia that will significantly extend and refine the existing literature on contact model in reducing stigma of mental illness. This study will also identify the different effects on reducing stigma of mental illness between ECM and PFI that will improve knowledge and develop better holistic methods on anti-stigma interventions.

17605618.label: Realisation of objectives
17605618.value: In this GRF project, we have two research objectives: 1) The primary objective is to investigate the short- (post-intervention) and long-term (9-month follow-up) effects of the newly developed enhancing contact model (ECM) on the family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia in rural Xinjin District, Chengdu, China using an RCT design; and 2) The secondary objective is to examine whether the ECM is more effective in reducing self-stigma than the psychoeducational family intervention (PFI) in the family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. From September 2019 to August 2022, our research team has tried our best to conduct and finish the GRF project accordingly to the GRF proposal. Based on our work, we have achieved 100% of these two project objectives. First, we have finished all the research activities according to the GRF project. The research activities include: 1) Literature review and refinement of research proposal; 2) Preparation and liaise with collaborated organization; 3) Finalize questionnaires; 4) Conduct pilot interview and revise materials; 5) Appoint health professionals and training; 6) Recruitment of participants; 7) Baseline assessment (T0); 8) Randomization and intervention (12 weekly); 9) post-intervention assessment (T1); 10) 3-month follow-up assessment (T2); 11) 9-month follow-up assessment (T3); 12) data entry and cleaning; 13) data analysis; and 14) report writing and publication. Even though we met many problems and challenges during the project, we have solved all the problems and challenges encountered. One example, the post-intervention assessment (T1), the 3-month follow-up assessment (T2), and the 9-month follow-up assessment (T3) were very difficult. Although some family caregivers who participated in the interventions could not finish these assessment, especially the 3-month and 9-month follow-up assessments, our research team had tried our best to successfully follow-up these family caregivers via various methods (e.g., multiple visits family caregivers, collaboration with local professionals to follow-up them, providing health services plus visits, etc.). Thus, the final attrition rate was not so high, which is very helpful for our final data analysis. Another example, in general, the quality of data is very high according to our repeatedly checking. However, in order to further improve the quality of the project, some data of a few subjects/participants may need further follow-up and re-check. Although we could not go to conduct the follow-up assessment in Xinjin, Chengdu, China because the pandemic of COVID-19, we contacted with local collaborators and health professionals and asked them to help to follow-up the subjects/participants and re-check the relevant data. Second, as the high quality of this study, we have successfully investigated the short- (post-intervention) and long-term (9-month follow-up) effects of the newly developed enhancing contact model (ECM) on the family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia in rural Xinjin District, Chengdu, China using an RCT design, and examined whether the ECM is more effective in reducing self-stigma than the psychoeducational family intervention (PFI) in the family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. The high quality of this study may reflect in the followings. 1. The number of participants in the three groups was higher (91 in ECM; 81 in PFI, and 82 in Treatment as Usual (TAU) group), the average attendance rates of family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia were above 95% in both the ECM and the PFI groups each session, and overall retention rate was above 92% and these were similar across groups at all follow-ups. 2. The major findings in the article of ‘Effectiveness of enhancing contact model on reducing stigma of mental illness among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia in rural China: A cluster randomized controlled trial’ have been published by The Lancet Regional Health-Western Pacific 2022; 22: 100419. This first trial in rural China shows that ECM intervention, a new anti-stigma intervention model, is a promising method for reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. The ECM intervention is more effective and stable than the PFI on reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. 3. Except testing the effectiveness of ECM and PFI on reducing stigma of mental illness, this study has further firstly tested the effectiveness of ECM on reducing family caregiving burden and improving psychological wellbeing among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia in rural China. The article of ‘Effectiveness of enhancing contact model on reducing family caregiving burden and improving psychological wellbeing (e.g., quality of life, hope) among caregivers of persons with schizophrenia in rural China’ has been accepted for publication by Psychological Medicine (2022, in press). The results of this study indicate that the ECM intervention, a comprehensive and multifaceted intervention, is more effective than the PFI in various aspects of mental wellbeing (e.g., reducing family caregiving burden and improving hope and QOL) among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia.

17605618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605618.value: The major findings and research outcome in two major studies of the project: First study: In April 2019, 253 family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia from 8 townships were randomly assigned to receive either ECM (cluster=3, n=90), PFI (cluster=2, n=81), or TAU (cluster=3, n=82). Compared with participants in the TAU group, participants in the ECM group had statistically significantly lower affiliate self-stigma scale (ASSS) scores at 9-month follow-up (estimated parameter [EP]= -5.51, 95% CI -10.27 to -0.74, p=0.02). There were no statistically significantly different ASSS scores at 9-month follow up between ECM and PFI groups. Compared with participants in the PFI group, younger (<60 years old), with higher monthly income and other caregiver (e.g., parent, sibling, child) participants in the ECM group had statistically significantly lower ASSS scores in the 3-month follow-up (EP= -5.66, 95% CI -10.13 to – 1.19, p<0.01; EP = -7.82, 95% CI -11.87 to -3.78, p<0.001; EP = -6.79, 95% CI -10.69 to -2.90, p<0.001, respectively). This first trial in rural China shows that ECM intervention, a new anti-stigma intervention model, is a promising method for reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. The ECM intervention is more effective and stable than the PFI on reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia (see detail in paper published by The Lancet Regional Health-Western Pacific 2022; 22: 100419. Impact factor: 8.559, 2021). Second study: Compared with participants in the TAU group, participants in the ECM group had statistically significantly lower caregiving burden scores both at T1 and T2 (p=0.0059 and 0.0257, respectively). Compared with participants in the TAU group, participants in the PFI group had statistically significantly higher QOL scores in T1 (p= 0.0406), while participants in the ECM group had statistically significantly higher QOL scores in T3 (p = 0.0240). Participants in both ECM and PFI groups had statistically significantly higher hope scores than those in the TAU group at T1 (p=0.0160 and 0.0486, respectively). This is the first study to explore the effectiveness of ECM on reducing family caregiving burden and improving hope and QOL in rural China. The results indicate the ECM intervention, a comprehensive and multifaceted intervention, is more effective than the PFI in various aspects of mental wellbeing among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia (see detail in paper published by Psychological Medicine, In press. Impact factor: 10.592, 2021).

17605618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605618.value: The results of this study indicate that the ECM intervention, a new anti-stigma intervention model, is a promising method for reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. The ECM intervention is more effective and stable than the PFI on reducing affiliate stigma among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. Further research needs to explore whether a long-term intervention (e.g., 6-month or 1-year intervention) could produce a more positive anti-stigma outcome trajectory. The results of this study also indicate that the ECM intervention, a comprehensive and multifaceted intervention, is more effective than the PFI in various aspects of mental wellbeing (e.g., reducing family caregiving burden, improving hope and quality of life) among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia. Future research needs to confirm ECM?s effectiveness in various population (e.g., primary health professionals, general people, etc.). Relevant mental health policies should be developed for emphasizing the contact, especially positive contact, between family caregivers and persons with schizophrenia in community. The Mental Health relevant courses in various schools (e.g., middle schools, high schools, colleges, universities) should include and emphasize the importance of contact, especially positive contact, on reducing stigma of mental illness among family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia.

17605618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605618.value: In order to test the effectiveness of Enhancing Contact Model (ECM) intervention, a new anti-stigma intervention model emphasizing positive contact, a cluster randomized controlled trial in family caregivers of persons with schizophrenia (FCPWS) was conducted in eight rural townships in Xinjin district, Chengdu, China. The FCPWS were randomly allocated to the ECM, Psychoeducational Family Intervention (PFI), or Treatment as Usual (TAU) group. FCPWS in three groups were provided specific interventions and follow-ups. This first trial in rural China shows that ECM intervention is a promising method for reducing affiliate stigma among FCPWS. The ECM intervention is more effective and stable than the PFI on reducing affiliate stigma among FCPWS. Moreover, this study also indicates the ECM is more effective than the PFI in various aspects of mental wellbeing (e.g., reducing family caregiving burden, improving hope and quality of life) among FCPWS. This study generates new knowledge of the ECM intervention, extends existing knowledge of the contact model in reducing stigma of mental illness. Our findings are important for facilitating the development of mental health policy and national evidence-based anti-stigma campaign on reducing stigma of mental illness, enhancing family caregiving quality and improving treatment and recovery of persons with schizophrenia.

17606318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17606318.value: Background: Electronic devices are frequently used by young children despite concerns over their potential adverse effects. Empirical studies have identified the overuse of electronic devices without proper supervision to be associated with a number of suboptimal childhood outcomes, including reduced cognitive ability, academic achievement, and psychosocial well-being and behavioural problems. Nonetheless, concrete evidence of such outcomes remains elusive, and a good-quality cohort study is thus necessary to examine the long-term effects of early electronic device exposure. Objectives: The proposed study will examine the impact of electronic device use during early childhood on long-term cognitive and psychosocial development. It will also investigate the cumulative effect of exposure to electronic devices throughout early and middle childhood, the potential moderating role of family socioeconomic background, and the relationship between electronic device use patterns during early childhood and adolescence. Study Design: The study will constitute the second follow-up of a Chinese kindergarten cohort initially recruited in 2011/12 from 22 kindergartens (3rd year of kindergarten, aged 5-6). The subjects and their families were first reassessed in 2014/15 (Grade 3, aged 8-9). The key variables collected in the previous assessments included time spent on various electronic devices (television, game consoles, smartphones, etc.), parental supervision, family socioeconomic status, school readiness, academic ability and behaviours. Both the baseline and first follow-up studies were funded by RGC GRF grants. The proposed study will revisit the cohort in 2018/19 (Grade 7, aged 12-13) to examine the patterns of electronic device use and such outcomes as academic performance, mental health, behavioural problems and social connectedness in adolescence. Our experience in the previous follow-up suggests that we should be able to recruit at least 70% (n = 583) of the initial cohort. Study Contributions: The proposed cohort study will be among the first to investigate the long-term health and developmental impact of electronic device use on children. It will provide concrete evidence of the effects of early electronic device exposure, cumulative exposure over the different stages of childhood, and the influence of family socioeconomic status on children’s cognitive and psychosocial outcomes. The study’s findings will help to guide relevant policymaking and form an empirical basis for future epidemiological research. 背景： 現今幼兒已經常使用電子設備，即使社會上不同聲音關注其潛在之不良影響。實證研究顯示，若幼兒過度使用電子設備，而沒有適當監督，他們的早期兒童發展會出現各種問題，包括較差的認知能力，學業成績，社會心理健康和行為問題。儘管如此，使用電子設備之長遠影響還未有足夠證據支持，因此我們提議進行本項為期7年的追蹤研究。 目標： 本研究將探討兒童早期使用電子設備對長期認知、心理和社交發展的影響，也會研究使用電子設備的累積效應及家庭社經背景的影響。研究亦會檢視早期使用電子設備和青少年時使用電子設備之關係。 研究設計： 本研究的對象是在2011/12年度從22所幼稚園（幼稚園第3年，5-6歲）招募的華人幼兒及其父母。孩子和他們的父母已於2014/15年進行首次跟進評估（小學3年級，8-9歲）。在之前兩次評估中收集的關鍵變量包括在各種電子設備（電視、遊戲機、智能手機等）上花費的時間、父母監督、家庭社會經濟狀況、在學準備、學術成績和行為問題等。基線和首次跟進研究均由RGC GRF撥款資助。本研究將於2018/19（中學1年級，12-13歲）對參加者進行第二次跟進，以檢視電子設備使用的模式如何影響學業成績、心理健康、行為問題等。我們在之前跟進中的經驗表明，我們能夠招募至少70％（n = 583）參加者。 研究貢獻： 本追蹤研究將是第一個研究電子設備使用對兒童的長期健康和發展影響的研究。它將提供具體證據，了解早期電子設備使用、兒童不同階段的累積使用，以及家庭社會經濟狀況對兒童認知和心理社交發展的影響。該研究的結果將有助於指導相關政策制定，並為相關流行病學研究奠定基礎。

17606318.label: Realisation of objectives
17606318.value: A total of 623 parent-child dyads from our original cohort have been successfully followed up and reassessed. Children’s academic achievement, psychosocial well-being, cognitive outcomes were assessed using validated instruments. Their pattern in electronic device usage was also assessed. The data collected sufficiently and satisfactorily achieved all the four proposed objectives. Objective 1 - To examine whether exposure to electronic devices at age 5 is associated with children’s cognitive and psychosocial development at age 12 After adjusting for child age and gender and family SES at K1, duration of exposure to electronic devices at age 5 was not associated with mathematics score (β = 0.04, p=0.567) and Chinese score (β = -0.04, p=0.636). More externalizing problems at time 2 were signiﬁcantly associated with more time spent by children on screen activities (β = 0.15, p = 0.007) at time 1. However, after further controlling for children’s gender, age, and time 1 socioemotional competence and family SES, the association between screen time and later externalizing problems remained signiﬁcant (β = 0.12, p = 0.038). Screen time was not associated with internalizing problems. Objective 2 - To investigate the cumulative effect of exposure to electronic devices from the ages of 5 to 12 on children’s cognitive and psychosocial development Cumulative effect was measured by the high/low screen time exposure status at age 5 and age 12 according to the international guidelines for pre-schoolers and teenagers. There was no significant cumulative effect on Chinese and Math scores and internalizing problems. Although the cumulative effect on externalizing problems was not significant, significant differences in externalizing problems were observed between those exceeding 2 hours of screen time at age 12 and those low in screen use at both assessment phases (B = 2.05, p = 0.033). Objective 3 - To examine whether family socioeconomic status moderates the relationship between early exposure to electronic devices and developmental outcomes in adolescence Family SES did not moderate the relationship between early exposure to electronic devices and internalizing problems in age 12. However, for externalizing problems in adolescence, longer duration of exposure to electronic devices at age 5 was associated with more externalizing problems in age 12 only in middle SES families (β = 0.17, p = 0.032). Objective 4 - To explore whether the use of electronic devices in early childhood predicts the pattern of electronic device use in adolescence There was a significantly positive correlation between the use of electronic devices at age 5 and at age 12 (r=0.25, p<0.001). Participants with high use of electronic devices in early childhood was 3.43 times more likely than other participants to have high use of electronic device in adolescence (p=0.016).

17606318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17606318.value: This project is one of the first studies in Chinese community to longitudinally examine the influence of early exposure to electronic devices on the cognitive and psychosocial development of the children. In this study, we identified a significant impact of exposure to electronic device on the psychosocial outcomes of the children. Specifically, our study found a positive association between the duration of exposure to electronic devices at age 5 and severity of externalizing problems at age 12. Cumulative effect of exposure to electronic devices was also examined. Although the cumulative effect on externalizing problems did not reach statistical significance, child participants with more than 2 hours of daily screen time at age 12 were found more prone to have externalizing problems than those with low screen use at both assessment phases. However, no significant impacts were observed in the academic performance (including the test scores in Mathematics and Chinese) and internalizing problems. The potential role of family socioeconomic status (SES) was also studied. It was found that the impact of longer exposure duration to electronic devices at age 5 on externalizing problems at age 12 was only observed in children from middle SES families. Family SES has no moderating effect on the relationship between early exposure to electronic devices and internalizing problems in adolescence. In addition, this study also identified a positive correlation between the use of electronic devices at age 5 and at age 12, in which those with high use of electronic devices in early childhood was 3.43 times more likely to have high use of electronic device in adolescence.

17606318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17606318.value: The findings of this study lay an important foundation for future epidemiological research on electronic device use in young children by identifying a long-term impact of early exposure to electronic device on the psychosocial outcomes of the children. Even more importantly, this study examined the cumulative effect of exposure to electronic devices and identified an increasing trend in the externalizing problems among those with high daily electronic device usage. Since this study also identified that those with high use of electronic devices in early childhood are more likely to have high use in adolescence, future longitudinal studies can be designed to study whether the usage pattern would continue until adulthood. The results of this study also suggest the necessity of examining the long-term behavioural outcomes at adulthood among those with high use of electronic device in early childhood. Given that most electronic devices have become popular in the past decade, this study can help to guide the formulation of policy pertaining to electronic device use among children and adolescents in Hong Kong. Guidelines and recommendations based on the findings can be issued to schools, parents and professionals, alerting them the adverse consequences of early exposure to various electronic devices.

17606318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17606318.value: This research study examined the impact of early exposure to electronic devices, which has become common in our daily life over the past decade. Results indicate that children with high use of electronic devices in early childhood are more likely to have behavioural problems with a potential cumulative effects observed. In addition, children with high use of electronic devices in early children are more likely to continue their high use pattern in adolescence. These findings add to the limited current evidence over the long-term impact of early exposure to electronic devices. This suggests the importance of prompt action by the government and healthcare providers to address the increasing trend and impacts of early use of electronic devices. More resource should be allocated to promoting the knowledge of proper usage of electronic device especially among children and adolescents.

17606518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17606518.value: With the adoption of the Anti-Monopoly Law (“AML”) in 2007, China officially joined the global competition law community. In the space of ten years, China has quickly established itself as one of the most prominent competition law jurisdictions, especially as far as merger review is concerned. However, the path to prominence has been rocky at times. The country has been accused of allowing political bias or protectionist instinct to seep into its AML enforcement. Foreign observers have argued that China has pursued industrial policy objectives through its merger review enforcement in particular. While political bias is difficult to prove without access to closed-door deliberations of the enforcement authorities, it would be helpful to examine whether China’s enforcement record is consistent with established competition law principles. To the extent that cases have been decided in accordance with such principles, then charge of political bias becomes less damaging. Another issue that is worth examining in AML enforcement thus far is the dual track enforcement system consisting of the enforcement authorities and the courts. Due to the lack of discovery procedures in Chinese courts, the ability of the courts to handle certain cases, such as cartels, is necessarily limited. Therefore, the Chinese courts are likely to focus on cases in which availability of evidence, at least evidence on the existence of the conduct, is less of an issue, namely vertical agreements and abuse of dominance cases, especially the ones that the authorities have refused to take. This is potentially problematic because the enforcement authorities and the courts have adopted different approaches to the same conduct, such as resale price maintenance. Therefore, this proposed project will examine this issue and put forward possible solutions. Lastly, this proposed project examines whether China needs a contextualized approach to competition law enforcement that takes into account its somewhat unique domestic socio-economic circumstances. These include the need to incorporate development considerations, especially technology catch-up, and reflect the complex and omnipresent interaction between the state and markets. A contextualized approach will in turn affect China’s treatment of the intellectual property-competition interface, merger review, conduct enforcement, and regulation of abuse of administrative monopoly. This proposed project will suggest ways in which the above four areas of AML enforcement will need to be adjusted as a result of the aforementioned socio-economic circumstances if a contextualized approach is deemed more appropriate for China. 隨著2007年反壟斷法（“反壟斷法”）的通過，中國正式加入了全球競爭法界。在十年的時間裡，中國迅速成為最重要的競爭法司法管轄區之一，特別是就合併審查而言。然而，一切並非一帆風順。該國被指控允許政治偏見或保護主義滲透其反壟斷法執法。外國觀察家認為，中國通過合併審查實施了產業政策目標。雖然如果沒有執法機關的閉門會議紀錄，很難證明政治偏見，那麼檢查中國的執法記錄是否符合既定的競爭法原則將會有所幫助。如果案件是根據這些原則決定的，那麼對政治偏見的指責就不確立了。 反壟斷法執法中另一個值得研究的問題是由執法當局和法院組成的雙軌執法系統。由於中國法院缺乏搜證程序，法院處理某些案件（如卡特爾）的能力必然受到限制。因此，中國法院可能會把重點放在縱向協議和濫用支配地位的案件。採取。這可能產生問題，因為執法機關和法院對同一行為採納了不同的態度，例如維持轉售價格。因此，該項目將研究這一問題並提出可能的解決方案。最後，這項目會考察中國是否需要考慮到其獨特的社會經濟環境執法。其中包括需要納入發展考慮因素，特別是科技發展，並反映國家與市場之間複雜的關係。

17606518.label: Realisation of objectives
17606518.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved overall. The one objective where effort may have fallen short (Objective 2) is the examination of political biases in Anti-Monopoly Law (AML) enforcement. The difficulties were foreseen when the project was conceived. The PI was aware that it may not be possible to find definitive evidence on political interference in competition law enforcement, given the opaque nature of the PRC bureaucracy. Effort was made to speak to practitioners and others who would be in a position to comment on the issue. Thankfully, this problem has been somewhat alleviated by the overtly politically driven enforcement against the Big Tech companies such as Alibaba, Meituan and Tencent. There was an almost unanimous consensus in the international media and among commentators that this constituted a government crusade against the Big Tech companies. There has been a deliberate effort by the PRC government to weaken the Big Tech companies and to diminish their influence in Chinese society. And because recent enforcement under the AML has been so dominated by Big Tech issues, the scope of the project has shifted to devote greater attention to the industry. This shift in focus is fully justified because digital economy issues have taken over the field of competition law in the last few years, especially after the original proposal was prepared in 2017. There were already signs that digital economy issues were becoming increasingly important in 2017. But subsequent development globally and in China means that a project on competition law enforcement in China cannot afford to overlook this sector. Therefore, a number of research output focus on digital economy issues, some specifically on China and some on more general theoretical issues that illuminate the analysis on China. Another important objective (Objective 5) that has become a main focus of the project is the intellectual property-competition interface, especially the patent-competition interface. This area of law has taken on greater importance in the Mainland due to its implications for technology transfer and acquisition. With the increasing political tension between the US and China and the growing focus on technological self-sufficiency, the role that competition law can play to facilitate technology transfer has taken on extra importance. Therefore, a considerable part of the project is devoted to developing a theoretical framework for approaching the patent-competition interface in China in light of its political, developmental, and technological considerations. The remainder of the objectives (Objectives 1, 3, 4, 7) have either been subsumed under the discussion of digital economy issues and the patent-competition interface, or dealt with separately, for example, in the book chapter on cartel enforcement in Mainland China. The objective of delving into industrial policy considerations in merger review (Objective 6) has been somewhat scaled back because merger review tends to play a less important role in the digital economy and the patent-competition interface in China. With the shift in focus of the project to these two topics, less attention was paid to merger review.

17606518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17606518.value: 1. While there are some notable divergences between the decisional practices and jurisprudence in China and those in the established jurisdictions of the US and the EU, AML enforcement is by and large consistent with the international mainstream. Take the most prominent enforcement cases in recent years, the cases against Alibaba and Meituan, for example. While there is little doubt that these two cases were politically driven, the analysis and the outcome of the two cases was hardly surprising. Both cases featured fairly run-of-the-mill exclusive dealing by dominant firms that clearly had an exclusionary impact in the market. The decisions by SAMR, the PRC enforcement authority, against these two companies were justified under conventional competition law principles. 2. While the role played by political considerations was perhaps not as apparent in the initial years of AML enforcement, there is no question that politics have come to dominate the recent enforcement agenda of the AML. However, with the recent announcement by the government on the easing of the tech crackdown, it remains to be seen whether SAMR will gain more autonomy in its enforcement activities. 3. China will need to adopt a development-stage specific and industry-specific approach to the patent-competition interface. There are some industries, such as ICT, where China is already a leading innovator globally. In these industries, the interests of both the innovators and the imitators will need to be taken into account and balanced against one and other. There are other industries, such as pharmaceuticals, where China is still very much a technological laggard and a recipient of foreign technology. The approach to the patent-competition interface in these industries is necessarily to facilitate technology transfer. The patent-competition rules will need to be crafted with these considerations in mind. 4. Whether one thinks it appropriate or not, AML enforcement already reflects the unique socio-economic and political environment of China. Given the government's views of the relationship between law and politics, it is inevitable that law enforcement is informed by political considerations. And AML enforcement also needs to reflect China's status as a middle-income developing country with a continental-sized economy and world-leading innovation capacity in some industries.

17606518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17606518.value: AML enforcement will continue to evolve. Digital economy and patent-competition issues will continue to remain at the forefront while other issues of interest may arise. The PI plans to continue to pay attention to future development in AML enforcement and produce further research output that builds on the research done for this project, which has given the PI a very good foundation for and understanding of AML enforcement.

17606518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17606518.value: This project has examined the enforcement of the Anti-Monopoly Law in China, with a special focus on digital economy issues and the patent-competition interface. The findings of the project are: (1) Politics have played an important role in driving the enforcement agenda in recent years, especially in the digital economy, and will probably continue to do so in the future. (2) While recent enforcement in the digital economy may have been politically driven, the analysis and outcome of the decisions made by SAMR, the PRC enforcement authority, were largely sound and consistent with conventional competition law principles and economic learning. While China continues to find its own voice and approach to competition law enforcement, its approach has not diverged too significantly from that in other jurisdictions. (3) China will need to adopt a development stage-specific and industry-specific approach to the patent-competition interface taking into account its technological capacity in different industries. In industries where domestic innovation is taking place, it may need to pay greater attention to protecting innovation incentives.
