17609518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609518.value: Because of impairments in understanding independent mental states (such as belief, desire, and intention) of self and others, children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have difficulty explaining and predicting other people’s behaviors. This deficit is known as theory of mind (ToM) or mind reading deficit (Baron-Cohen, Leslie, & Frith, 1985). Our recent study has shown a significant link between ToM deficit and reading comprehension difficulty in normally intelligent Chinese children with ASD (Tong & Wong, submitted). However, the nature of this link and the underlying factors affecting it remain unexplored. This study aims to address these issues by focusing on two key factors that are critically related to both ToM and reading comprehension: executive function (EF) and pragmatic language comprehension (PLC). EF refers to inter-related, higher order cognitive control processes, such as inhibition, flexibility, and planning, that are responsible for goal-directed behaviours (Miyake et al., 2000). PLC is the utilization of context to infer the meaning of utterances (Loukusa & Moilanen, 2009). The goals of the proposed study concerning ToM, EF, PLC, and reading comprehension are threefold: 1) to examine whether children with ASD demonstrate separate specific deficits in ToM, EF, PLC, and reading comprehension; 2) to explore longitudinally developmental relationships among ToM, EF, and PLC; and 3) to evaluate the relative contributions of ToM, EF, and PLC to reading comprehension development and difficulties in Chinese children with ASD and their peers. A group of 120 Chinese children of normal intelligence with ASD and 120 typically developing controls (ages 8-13 years), all studying in Hong Kong mainstream primary schools, will be recruited and tested on an annual basis for three years on multiple measures of ToM, EF, PLC, oral language skills, word reading, and reading comprehension. Logistic regression and multivariate analysis of variance will be used to examine research goal 1, while latent growth curve model analysis using structural equation modeling will be employed to examine research goals 2 and 3. The proposed longitudinal study will inform critical cognitive and linguistic components of a reading comprehension model, and can thus shed light on the development of optimal tools for the diagnosis of and intervention for reading comprehension difficulties. In addition to the theoretical and clinical implications, results of this study will be practically relevant to the design and implementation of more effective intervention programs to assist Hong Kong Chinese children with ASD who study in mainstream schools.

17609518.label: Realisation of objectives
17609518.value: Despite the disruption of school and lab closure caused by the unprecedented social movement and the COVID-19 pandemic, we have successfully completed this project by fully achieving three intended objectives. The details are described in terms of each objective. With regards to the first objective concerning the specific and separate deficits in cognitive function, pragmatic language comprehension (PLC), and reading comprehension, our results have found that Hong Kong Chinese children with high functioning autism exhibited deficits in advanced theory of mind (ToM) and executive function (EF) and overall reading comprehension skills. These findings have reported in our recently published peer-reviewed journal article (see Lee, Chan, and Tong, 2022). Additionally, by assessing simple and complete PLC and receptive prosody, we have found that Hong Kong Chinese children with autism showed more difficulties in answering pragmatically complex questions and providing explanations for their answers, and these difficulties were significantly associated with their impairment in receptive prosody language skills (Tong, under reviewed). For the second objective, we have successfully administered ToM, EF, PLC and reading comprehension tasks across three years. While most tasks have been administered identically across all phases, reading comprehension was revised across each phase to account for more sophisticated language and cognitive abilities, such as the inclusion of more challenging Chinese passages and addition of English passages. Specifically, as of March 2023, a total of 205 TD children (Grade 3: N = 116; Grade 4: N = 89) and 189 ASD children (Grade 3: N = 124; Grade 4: N = 65) were tested at phase 1. At phase 2, 155 TD children (Grade 3: N = 88; Grade 4: N = 67) and 145 ASD children (Grade 3: N = 94; Grade 4: N = 51) were tested. Finally at phase 3, 105 TD children (Grade 3: N = 62; Grade 4: N = 43) and 78 ASD children (Grade 3: N = 51; Grade 4: N = 27) were tested. Despite multiple city-wide disruptions, such as the social movement and ongoing COVID-19-related disruptions to in-person testing and vaccination requirements, we have achieved a retention rate of 51% for TD children and 41% ASD children from phases 1 to 3. This was largely due to our dedicated effort and flexibility in adapting our tasks to an online format during the critical stages. Regarding the third objective, we have demonstrated that both advanced EF and ToM deficits exhibited by Chinese children with autism were significantly related to different components of reading comprehension deficits and language abilities in children with autism (see Lee, Chan and Tong, 2022). Furthermore, our longitudinal data analysis showed stable relationships between EF and PLC, as well as PLC and reading comprehension, further details of which will be explained in the research outcome section.

17609518.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609518.value: Our analysis of the large-scale dataset contributed to two publications and three under-reviewed manuscript thus far. In a study comparing ToM and literal and non-literal reading comprehension abilities of TD and ASD children, we addressed objectives 1 and 3 (Tong et al., 2020). Children with ASD performed less well in both literal and non-literal question types, meaning they were less able to extract information from texts directly, as well as make inferences. More importantly, ToM was found to mediate the relationship between children’s ASD status and non-literal reading comprehension in middle childhood. Our most recent publication continued to build on these findings (Lee et al., 2022). First, relative to TD peers, ASD children displayed deficits in advanced ToM. Second, ASD children experienced specific EF and ToM deficits that varied in their contribution to reading comprehension. For example, while the same condition of the EF task, Hearts and Flowers task, measuring shifting and flexibility, contributed to literal and non-literal reading comprehension, their relationship with other ToM subtasks, vocabulary and nonverbal intelligence differed. In an under-reviewed manuscript, we compared the performance of TD and ASD children in ToM, PLC and receptive prosody. Our findings demonstrated that those skills were correlated in ASD children but not in TD children, indicating the greater relevance for ASD children. Furthermore, regardless of ASD or TD status, ToM predicted PLC among school-age children, suggesting that an understanding of mental states is critical to applying this knowledge in social interactions. In addition to publications and under-reviewed articles, our longitudinal analyses generated several consistent findings. Among those who had completed all testing phases, EF consistently predicted PLC development from middle childhood to early adolescence. Furthermore, PLC was found to significantly predict reading comprehension between each phase, indicating a stable longitudinal relationship. After separate analyses for TD and ASD children, however, different patterns emerged. While for TD children, the aforementioned relationship remained, for ASD children, these longitudinal relationships were only found between phases 2 and 3. This suggests that the predictive roles of EF to PLC and PLC to reading comprehension becomes more critical for ASD children in later development. For ASD children, ToM appears to explain more of the variance in reading comprehension, especially at phases 1 and 3. These preliminary findings characterize differences in the skills that contribute to reading comprehension among these populations.

17609518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609518.value: Findings from the current project highlight the importance of ToM, EF and PLC for reading comprehension for children from middle childhood to adolescence. As such, we propose three clear directions for future research and application. First, the extension of our assessment to both pre-school and early primary school students, as well as adolescents, would be insightful towards examining the developmental trajectory of the three core skills studied. Second, while our project examined children’s ToM and PLC comprehensively through several self-developed tasks, our behavioral assessment focused on academic applications of these skills. Future research should focus on real-life events or scenarios. Third, following comprehensive assessments of the three core skills, intervention is critical, especially for our young participants with ASD. By targeting EF and PLC, while integrating aspects of ToM into intervention programs, we aim to observe improvement in reading comprehension, a framework we are already testing [GRF 17620520].

17609518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609518.value: By testing a large group of Hong Kong school-age Chinese children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and their typically developing (TD) peers for three consecutive years, we have demonstrated that relative to TD children, those with ASD exhibit weaknesses in 1) understanding the mental and affective states of themselves and others (theory of mind, ToM); 2) inhibiting irrelevant information to achieve the goals in daily life (executive function, EF); and 3) using appropriate language according to a given context (pragmatic language comprehension, PLC). Furthermore, these weaknesses directly contributed to their reading comprehension difficulties, especially for inferential questions that require the use of context to derive unwritten meanings. These findings suggest that parents, clinical and educational practitioners should target advanced cognitive and language skills, especially ToM, EF and PLC, for improving reading comprehension difficulties in children with autism.

17609818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609818.value: Despite the extensive history of social movements around the world, their impact on population mental health remains largely unknown. By comparison, the psychiatric sequelae of other population events such as natural disasters and terrorist attacks have been much better documented. These studies indicate a significant toll of psychopathology associated with mass community trauma; however whether similar findings apply to social movements is unclear. The threat of harm or death - a defining feature of disasters - is absent in nonviolent movements, suggesting that alternative mechanisms are operating. Natural disasters which threaten the entire community can be occasions for increased solidarity, whereas social movements could exacerbate ideological divisions. Theoretical frameworks such as the social support deterioration model could therefore be relevant. In 2014, a massive civil disobedience campaign, Occupy Central/Umbrella Movement (OCUM), took place in Hong Kong. We have shown that OCUM was associated with substantial and persistent increases in depressive symptoms. Three years after the protests, we have demonstrated a re-emergence of sociopolitical conflicts and that social ties have not yet healed. Several unresolved questions therefore remain: What is the causal effect of long-term sociopolitical conflicts on mental health? When will the mental health consequences of OCUM abate? What are the underlying mechanisms for the psychiatric sequelae? Drawing from the disaster-related literature, state-of-the-art evidence would be derived from 1) a longitudinal study with multiple assessments before, during and after the event, 2) long-term psychiatric outcomes, and 3) the application of latent class trajectory and time-varying analyses. We accordingly propose to take advantage of an ongoing prospective cohort, where we have administered interviews at several time points before, during and after OCUM, to obtain long-term psychiatric diagnoses (five years before and after OCUM). Our proposed research would achieve the following objectives:- 1. Assess the cumulative impact of sociopolitical conflicts on common mental disorders over a 10-year study period using marginal structural modelling. 2. Examine long-term patterns and predictors of depression trajectories of OCUM using latent growth curve analysis. 3. Test the social support deterioration model in OCUM using causal mediation analysis. With the rise in protests globally, social movements and sociopolitical conflicts could emerge as an important social determinant of mental health. Our proposed longitudinal study with pre-event data and long-term outcomes is therefore uniquely positioned to inform public health and social policies to protect mental health in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

17609818.label: Realisation of objectives
17609818.value: Using a large population-based prospective cohort with more than 10 years of longitudinal data, we have achieved all the project objectives with additional important analyses to provide timely and critical evidence for the mental health impact of the Hong Kong social unrest during 2019-20. Social unrest has been rising around the world, including in large prosperous cities such as Paris, Santiago and Barcelona. Prior to COVID-19, the 2019-20 social unrest in Hong Kong had spread to key cities internationally with rallies having taken place in Australia, Canada, France, South Korea, UK and US, amongst others. In fact, mass conflicts and collective actions have continued to take place in more than 190 countries during the pandemic. Yet the impact of social unrest as an emerging social determinant of population mental health remains largely undocumented. To date, this is the largest and longest prospective cohort study on collective actions and mental health. In addition to the stated objectives, we assessed the population mental health burden, risk factors, and health-care needs of the 2019-20 social unrest and compared the findings with those of the 2014 Occupy Central/Umbrella Movement (OCUM), with baseline data from 2009-14. We showed an alarming five-fold increase in probable depression during the 2019-20 social unrest (from 1.9% to 11.2%) compared to the baseline. Similarly, prevalence of suicidal ideation and PTSD symptoms had increased to 4.3% and 31.6%, respectively. These levels remarkably exceed those following the OCUM, and the mental health burden was comparable to those experiencing large-scale disasters. While mental health deterioration transcended sociodemographics, we showed that heavy social media use was associated with probable depression and suspected PTSD. In contrast, family support mitigated against probable depression. Please kindly refer to the attachment with full manuscript and appendix published in The Lancet (leading medical journal; Impact Factor: 79.3). Realisation of the objectives: Please see attachment for supplementary methods, figures, tables and references. Objective 1: To assess the cumulative impact of sociopolitical conflicts on common mental disorders over a 10-year study period using marginal structural modelling. Figure 1 shows the weighted prevalence of conflict with family members, and friends and colleagues due to sociopolitical reasons in the Hong Kong adult population over a ten-year period. We investigated the impact of the cumulative interpersonal conflict due to sociopolitical reasons from the Occupy Central in 2014 to the social unrest in 2019 on probable depression. We also assessed the impact of the cumulative sociopolitical conflict with family members in the last decade from 2011 to 2021 on probable depression. We showed that participants with 1-unit higher score of cumulative conflict with family members from 2014 to 2019 were estimated to have a 42% higher odds (OR, 1.42; 95% CI 1.20-1.67) of probable depression, adjusted for baseline socio-demographics, prior conflict with family members, family support and probable depression. The estimate remained robust (OR, 1.42; 95% CI 1.20-1.69), when additionally adjusted for political participation, time spent on sociopolitical news/events on social media, and prior conflict with friends and colleagues (Table 1). Sensitivity analysis with inverse probability of censoring weighting to account for attrition bias yielded similar results (Table 1). Adjusting for age and sex, participants with 1-unit higher score of cumulative conflict with friends and colleagues due to sociopolitical reasons from 2014 to 2019 were found to have a 27% higher odds (OR, 1.27; 95 % CI 1.04-1.56) of probable depression. However, additional adjustments resulted in the estimate being attenuated to the null (Table 1). In examining the follow-up from 2011 to 2021, cumulative conflict with family members was also found to be associated with probable depression, and the association remained robust (OR, 1.45, 95% CI: 1.22, 1.74) with further adjustment for the sources of stress and anxiety level during the COVID-19 pandemic (Table 2). In the stratified analyses, associations were detected among both males and females, those aged below 60 years, unmarried, widowed/divorced/separated, and with lower household income at baseline (Figure 2). Individuals experienced a monotonic increase in interpersonal conflicts, both with family members and friends/colleagues, with more time spent on social media during the 2014 protests and the 2019 social unrest, which was not observed for traditional media (i.e. TV, newspaper and radio) (Figure 3). Individuals who spent 1-2 or ≥2 hours per day on social media for sociopolitical news/events were associated with higher interpersonal conflicts compared to those spending <1 hour per day (Table 3). In contrast, no associations were detected between exposure to sociopolitical news/events via traditional media with interpersonal conflicts (Table 3). In the multivariable adjusted model, individuals who spent ≥2 hours had higher odds of probable depression (Table 4). Time spent on television, newspapers, radio for sociopolitical news/events were not associated with probable depression. Objective 2: To examine the long-term patterns and predictors of depression trajectories of Occupy Central/Umbrella Movement using latent growth curve analysis. We fitted models with one to seven latent classes and identified a four-class model for depressive symptoms (Figure 4). Majority of respondents (61.6%) had minimal depressive symptoms throughout the 10-year prospective study and were thus classified as either resistant (19.9%) or resilient (41.7%). Almost one-third of respondents (30.8%) had been suffering from mild depressive symptoms. Less than one-tenth of respondents (7.5%) had persistent moderate depression. Compared with the resistant group, those who had depressive symptoms at baseline were more likely to have persistent moderate depression (Table 5). Those who had better self-rated health and higher levels of resilience, family harmony, and family support were less likely to be in the persistent moderate depression group (Table 5). Objective 3: To test the social support deterioration model in Occupy Central/Umbrella Movement using causal mediation analysis. We used marginal structural models to estimate the “natural direct effect” of the intrafamilial conflict and depression from 2014 to 2019, and the “natural indirect effect” by family support. (1,2) Inverse probability weighting techniques were used to adjust for potential confounding. The results of the complete case analysis are presented in Table 6. Both natural direct effect of the intrafamilial conflict and natural indirect effect of family support on depression were not statistically significant. However, due to the monotonic missing data in the follow-up, we used multiple imputation to handle the missing data to increase the statistical power and reduce bias. Similar results were found for the associations of intrafamilial conflict and family support on depression (Table 6).

17609818.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609818.value: Using a large population-based prospective cohort with more than 10 years of longitudinal data, we examined the impact of major protests and sociopolitical conflicts on mental health. Evidence from two consecutive social movements suggests that substantial mental health burden was associated with major protests, with about 40% of respondents having mild depressive symptoms and persistent moderate depression following OCUM and the 2019-20 social unrest. In late 2019, prevalence of probable depression and suspected PTSD reached 11.2% and 12.8%, respectively. One in five adults reported probable depression or suspected PTSD during the social unrest, which is comparable to those experiencing large-scale disasters, armed conflicts, or terrorist attacks. Heavy social media use (≥2 h per day), particularly social media apps widely used by protesters, was associated with both probable depression and suspected PTSD, while family support mitigated against probable depression. We estimated that the mental health burden identified would translate into an excess 12% service requirement to the public sector queue or equivalent. While the mental health consequences of social unrest transcended sociodemographics, we found those with higher levels of individual resilience, family harmony, and family support were less likely to be in the persistent moderate depression group. Using marginal structural modelling, we showed that those with higher level of cumulative conflicts with family members due to sociopolitical reasons had increased risks of probable depression, and the associations remained robust after adjustments for multiple covariates and confounders. Similarly, those with higher level of cumulative conflict with friends and colleagues due to sociopolitical reasons were more likely to suffer probable depression. However, the associations attenuated after additional adjustments for covariates. Further analyses of data from 2011 to 2021 showed that the association between cumulative conflict with family members and probable depression remained significant with additional adjustment for the sources of stress and anxiety level during the COVID-19 pandemic. Thus, our findings indicate a significant role of family support in protecting population mental health during major protests.

17609818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609818.value: Our findings show a major mental health burden associated with the 2019-20 Hong Kong social unrest, as well as persistent moderate depression in a significant portion of respondents. This will require substantial increases in service surge capacity in both the health and social sectors, and in real time. Health-care and social care professionals need to be vigilant in recognising possible psychiatric sequelae during and after widespread unrest, opportunistically during routine interactions and systematically through deliberate planning. This includes potential spillover effects, where those who have not participated in the protests can also be affected. The high prevalence in probable depression and suspected PTSD could result in functional impairment for parenting and work, as well as substantial economic costs. In particular, our trajectory findings suggested that baseline depressive symptoms and poor self-rated health predicted worse mental health outcomes. Mental health preventive interventions may be usefully targeted at these vulnerable groups. Our findings also suggest that interventions should enhance individual resilience, family harmony, and family support, which help buffer against probable depression. At the population level, public health measures during an unrest include health needs assessment, ensuring safety, and restoring the population’s ability to engage in daily routines and community activities. This would require a major planning exercise across the health-care and social care sectors, involving both public and private providers in the mixed health-care and social care economy of Hong Kong. In a world of increasing unrest, our findings may have implications for service planning to better protect population mental health globally. In future, ongoing surveillance and monitoring of the mental health consequences of major social unrest, in addition to current conventions for infectious epidemics, wars and natural disasters, should become routine as part of preparedness efforts worldwide.

17609818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609818.value: Collective actions have been documented to be rising globally, yet the impact of social unrest on mental health remains largely unknown. Here, we conducted the largest and longest prospective cohort study on collective actions and mental health to date, and examined the associated population mental health burden, risk factors, and health-care needs. We found a major mental health burden during the 2019-20 Hong Kong social unrest, which will require substantial increases in service surge capacity. Health-care and social care professionals should be vigilant in recognising possible mental health sequelae, including potential community spillover effects. Thus, we showed compelling evidence that protests even when nonviolent can be associated with adverse mental health outcomes. In contrast, proper and adequate social support and reducing intra-familial and society-wide socio-political conflicts may mitigate these adverse mental health effects. In a world of increasing unrest, our findings might have implications for service planning to better protect population mental health globally.

17610018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610018.value: We live in an age in which virtually all goods and services are merchandized through trademarks. Thus, the economic and cultural value of trademarks has increased significantly, as they have become part of our daily lives and core assets for many companies. While trademark law protects the exclusive right to use a trademark, it also carves out limitations on that exclusive right. These limitations entitle the public to use a trademark without obtaining permission from, and paying remuneration to, the trademark owner. They are of critical importance to the protection of consumer welfare and cultural freedom. Despite the crucial importance of limitations on trademark rights to protecting the public interest, the Chinese law governing those limitations remains woefully underdeveloped. The Chinese Trademark Act, for example, permits only the descriptive use exemption without protecting other types of non-infringing trademark uses such as nominative use and parodic use. The Trademark Act also lacks necessary instructions on how to deal with the relationship between descriptive use and the protection of trademark rights against the likelihood of confusion or dilution. Through investigation of statutory provisions and judicial rulings, my project will identify the major problems with the existing limitations on trademark rights under Chinese law. In examining ways to address those problems, it will then explore how China can reform its trademark law by establishing a new trademark fair use mechanism. Legally, the project will suggest that the new mechanism should broadly permit not only descriptive trademark use but also other types of fair use such as nominative and parodic use. It will also shed new light on what China can learn from the European Union and United States in crafting proper legal standards for a finding of fair trademark use. Culturally, the project will examine the extent to which the proposed new mechanism will better protect the public interest and how it can promote two forms of cultural freedom in China, namely, freedom of expression and freedom to participate in cultural life. It will further demonstrate that the promotion of both forms of cultural freedom could effect positive change in the identity of both consumers and corporations, thereby fostering ethical branding and consumerism in China. 在我們生活的這個時代裏，實際上所有的產品和服務都是經由商標作買賣的。因此，商標的經濟和文化價值都被顯著提高了，因爲商標已經成爲了我們日常生活中的一部份和很多機構的核心資產。商標法一方面保護運用商標這獨一無二的權利，一方面也開闢出關於這種獨家權利的種種限制。這些限制使得公衆既不需要從商標權人手上拿到允許，也不需要付酬金給商標權人就能運用商標。它們對於保護消費者福祉及文化自由方面尤為重要。 儘管商標權的限制對於維護公衆利益有莫大的重要性，有關規管那些限制的中國律法發展仍然嚴重地滯後。例如，《中華人民共和國商標法》只允許豁免描述性的合理商標使用，而沒有保障到其他非侵權性的商標使用方式，比如指示性之合理使用及戲謔仿作。該《商標法》也缺乏應有的指引去處理描述性商標使用和保護商標權此兩者關係對於引起混淆或淡化商標的可能性。 通過研究法律條款和法治管理方式，我的課題將指出在中國律法下，目前商標權的限制所衍生的主要問題。此課題將檢測不同的方法去解決那些問題，並探索中國如何可以通過成立一個全新的商標公平使用機制從而改革國家的商標法。 在法律層面上，此課題將建議新機制應該廣泛地允許描述性的合理商標使用，以及其他商標使用方式比如指示性之合理使用及戲謔仿作。它亦將啓發中國在哪些方面可以向歐盟和美國學習制定一套用於裁決公平商標使用時的合適的法律標準。 在文化層面上，此課題將檢驗建議的新機制有多大程度可以更好地保護公衆利益，以及它如何能夠促進中國國内的兩種文化自由模式，分別是表達的自由和參與文化生活的自由。此課題將進一步地證明促進此兩種文化自由模式可以正面地改變消費者和機構的身份認同，從而培育國内合乎道德的品牌創建和保護消費者權益。

17610018.label: Realisation of objectives
17610018.value: I looked into the major Chinese statutes, administrative regulations, and interpretations issued by the Chinese Supreme Court. I analyzed the nature and scope of the descriptive use exemption under the Trademark Act, and also thoroughly examined whether other exemptions such as nominative use and parodic use have already been accepted by the relevant administrative regulations, and Supreme Court’s interpretations. I also examined the nature and scope of the descriptive use, nominative use, and parodic use exemptions by studying judicial rulings by Chinese courts. I collected a large number of rulings, sorted out influential ones, and analyzed their implications for Chinese courts to decide the nature and scope of these exemptions. I collected the major statutes and judicial rulings concerning trademark fair use in the European Union (EU) and the United States (US), and then examined the nature and scope of the fair use exemptions under these statutes and rulings. In particular, I studied how fair use exemptions have promoted freedom of expression and the freedom to take part in cultural life in the EU and the US. Based on these studies, I further considered how China could learn lessons from the EU and the US to improve its trademark fair use mechanism. I focused on two research questions. First, how China could learn lessons from the EU and the US about whether it should statutorily adopt nominative use and parodic use exemptions. Second, how China could learn lessons from the EU and the US about how to promote freedom of expression and cultural life through trademark fair use exemptions. I organized an international conference Limitations on Trademark Rights from Comparative and Interdisciplinary Perspectives on January 7-8, 2019 under the auspices of the Law and Technology Center at the University of Hong Kong Faculty of Law and the Engelberg Center on Innovation Law & Policy at New York University School of Law. The conference brought together leading trademark experts from around the world to explore the nature and scope of those limitations from comparative and interdisciplinary perspectives. Base on this conference, I co-edited a book on the limitations on trademark rights with Professor Barton Beebe, John M. Desmarais Professor of Intellectual Property Law at New York University School of Law. The editing process helped me gain a better understanding of trademark fair use from comparative and interdisciplinary perspectives. I also presented my research papers at various international conferences such as the EUPLANT Seminar: EU-China Round Table on IP at the City University of Hong Kong School of Law, the Annual Congress organized by the International Association for the Advancement of Teaching and Research in Intellectual Property (ATRIP), and the Privatizing, Quantifying, Performing and Transforming the University conference at the University of California, Davis, School of Law. I also gave a public lecture on Chinese trademark law at Waseda University School of Law. I received very helpful comments and feedbacks for my research project.

17610018.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610018.value: Despite the crucial importance of trademark fair use, Chinese trademark law governing this type of limitations on trademark rights is woefully underdeveloped. The Chinese Trademark Act merely permits only the descriptive use exemption. It does not expressly recognize nominative use and parodic use exemptions. However, a closer look into the rulings made by Chinese courts shows that there is a robust judicial recognition of the nominative use exemption. Although the Chinese Trademark Act allows only for descriptive use, the Chinese courts have relied on nominative use in deciding cases without any statutory basis. In such cases, the courts have protected the interests of consumers and businesses by holding that the nominative use of a trademark can be fair despite not being an existing statutory exception to infringement. My latest search of Beida Fabao, a legal database, showed that as of January 2021, Chinese judges had applied nominative fair use to settle 172 trademark cases. Based on these research findings, I argue that China should revise its Trademark Act to expressly recognize the nominative use exemption. I also examine the implications of trademark fair use for protecting luxury brands. Although Chinese judges have used creative methods to proactively protect the public, they have not relied on freedom of expression to decide trademark fair use cases. The Chinese courts have not yet recognized parodic use as a legal limitation, even though disputes involving parodic use have increased dramatically in China in recent years owing to the rise of social media. In response, I put forward a proposal for how judges could cite the Chinese constitution’s free speech clause to uphold a ruling that limits trademark rights. Rather than adopting free speech solely as an individual liberty, I suggest that Chinese judges should view free speech as having a major function in promoting the public interest in a tolerant, pluralistic society. 17610018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610018.value: Legal disputes over parodic trademark uses are on the rise, posing challenges for the courts in the absence of any statutory guidance under Chinese trademark law. Further research will be needed to examine the growing number of parodic use cases. While the statutory recognition of the nominative use exemption is very likely in the near future, it would be difficult for the Chinese legislature to adopt parodic use as a statutory limitation on trademark rights. Based on the new developments in parodic use in China, further research is needed to study the political and legal hurdles for the statutory recognition of the parodic use exemption and how to pave the way for such a statutory revision.

17610018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610018.value: Trademark fair use is of vital importance in protecting the public interest. The trademark fair use mechanism in China, however, remains underdeveloped. The Chinese Trademark Act permits only the descriptive use exemption without recognizing the nominative use and parodic use exemptions. Through investigation of statutory provisions and judicial rulings, my project has identified the major problems with the existing trademark fair use mechanism under Chinese law. The project focuses on the role of Chinese courts in dealing with trademark fair use cases. It identifies two important contributions that Chinese courts have made to protecting the public interest. First, when interpreting the nature and scope of limitations on trademark rights, they have made appropriate deviations from the civil law tradition to proactively protect the public interest. Second, in doing so, they have developed creative legal methods to ascertain the myriad public interests implicated in limitations on trademark rights. Nonetheless, Chinese judges have not yet relied on the right to free speech in their trademark rulings. This article suggests that to better protect the public interest Chinese judges should cite the Chinese constitution’s free speech clause to highlight its public interest function of fostering a tolerant, pluralistic society.

17610418.label: Realisation of objectives
17610418.value: The study adopted a multi-site randomized controlled trial (RCT) design. We aimed to recruit integrated community centres for mental wellness (ICCMWs) in this workplace well-being intervention study. At each site (i.e. an ICCMW), the study lasted for 6 months (3-month intervention and 3-month follow-up). Measures were administered at 1-month intervals. Intensive work at each site was required in engagement, training & coaching onsite group facilitators, and implementing the 2-arm RCT. Because the huge amount of work at each site, our original plan was to implement the study at the pace of adding 1 new site per month, starting from April 2019. Unfortunately we came across extended social unrest in the second half of 2019. The operation of many ICCMWs were frequently disrupted. After that, COVID-19 pandemic broke out in February 2020. Prolonged stringent infection control and social distancing regulations have been enforced in Hong Kong. ICCMWs experienced continuous disruption, and virtually ceased their operation during multiple waves of the pandemic. As a result, the implementation of study has been severely affected. Nevertheless, with our persistent effort, we managed to engage 13 ICCMWs covering the whole territory of Hong Kong, which are: 1. The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong-Jockey Club Amity Place-Kwun Tong South 香港心理衞生會-賽馬會恆健坊 2. Caritas Wellness Link 明愛全樂軒 3. Baptist Oi Kwan Social Service 浸信會愛羣社會服務處 4. Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui Welfare Council Limited-The Club 香港聖公會福利協會有限公司-樂喜聚 5. Caritas Wellness Link - North District 明愛樂晴軒 6. Fu Hong Society Sunrise Centre 扶康會康晴天地 7. Tung Wah Group of Hospitals-Lok Hong Integrated Community Centre for Mental Wellness 東華三院-樂康軒 8. MHAHK-Amity Place (Kwun Tong North) 香港心理衛生會恆樂坊 (觀塘北) 9. New Life Psychiatric Rehabilitation Association- The Wellness Centre (Tin Shui Wai) 新生精神康復會-安泰軒 (天水圍) 10 Richmond Fellowship of Hong Kong -ALOHA (Eastern) 利民會-友樂坊 (東區) 11 Richmond Fellowship of Hong Kong-ALOHA (Wong Tai Sin) 利民會-友樂坊（黃大仙） 12 Stewards Ltd. --Take Your Way Clubhouse(Ma On Shan) 香港神託會--創薈坊（馬鞍山） 13 New Life Psychiatric Rehabilitation Association --The Wellness Centre (Shatin) 新生精神康復會--安泰軒（沙田） Initially 265 staff of these 13 ICCMWs joined the research. Because of the adverse disruptions of COVID-19 pandemic, interventions at 3 sites (n =64) had to be stopped. Excluding those not doing baseline measures and not joining the interventions, we achieved an effective sample size of 175. Considering the extreme challenges we faced, our success in engaging 13 ICCMWs into the study is an amazing result. For a 2-arm RCT, assuming a mid/moderate effect, an effective sample size of 175 is adequate for core statistical analysis. Another major challenge we experienced was that review process in many journals experienced severe delay during COVID-19 pandemic. For example, in one of our target journals, the first review alone took about half a year. Nevertheless, we managed to produce 3 papers in good, relevant journals, which are: - Occupational & Environmental Medicine (2021 IF: 2.306) - Frontiers in Psychology (2021 IF: 4.232) - Asia Pacific Journal of Social Work and Development (2021 IF: 1.433) Overall, despite all the unprecedented challenges, we have satisfactorily achieved the study objectives.

17610418.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610418.value: 1. EFFICIACY OF OUR NOVEL INTERVENTION Grounded in an integrative body-mind-spirit (BMS) approach, a brief daily workplace well-being program has been developed for community mental health workers (CMHW) who were vulnerable to burnout. Aiming to evaluate the program’s efficacy, this study adopted a multi-site randomized controlled trial design. Primary outcome measures included work engagement and burnout. The data analysis included 175 participants from 10 community mental health centres. ANOVA revealed significant group x time interaction effects on work engagement (η2 = 0.037, p = 0.039) and one of its sub-scores: absorption (η2=0.048, p=0.014). Regarding burnout, ANOVA revealed that at T4 there were significant group x time effects on burnout total score and all its three sub-scores, including work-related burnout, client-related burnout, and personal burnout. Partial eta squared ranged between 0.028 and 0.071, suggesting a small to medium effect size. Overall findings demonstrated the protective effect of the Brief Daily BMS program in preserving work engagement during challenging conditions, and to a lesser extent in reducing burnout among CMHW. 2. WORK ENGAGEMENT NOT NECESSARILY THE HIGHER THE BETTER We examined the effects of interventions on well-being among highly engaged workers. Of the whole sample, we examined participants’ work engagement and positive affect from the highest quarter (HWE) and the lowest quarter (LWE) of work engagement at baseline. Measures were taken at baseline and 1-month intervals during 3-month programs and 3-month follow-up. Repeated measures analysis of variance and paired sample t-tests were carried out to test our hypotheses. The interventions had decreasing effects on work engagement in the HWE subgroup. There was an increasing trend of positive affect on the HWE group only in the BMS program. The trajectories of work engagement in the HWE moved towards a moderate level. Our results suggest that the work engagement’s decrease in the HWE group could be a sign of recovery and relaxation. Work engagement is not necessarily the higher the better. There seems to be an optimal, sustainable range of work engagement. The findings have significant theoretical and practical implications.

17610418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610418.value: The findings have significant theoretical and practical implications to workplace well-being strategies and practices. First, regarding workplace well-being program, the findings suggest a feasible, efficacious design can be: 1. Mode: A brief daily mode over an extended period (c.f.: Previous interventions tend to be one off programme, for example, a whole day retreat) 2. Content: An integrative body, mind and spirit approach (c.f.: Previous interventions tend to separate mental and physical health) 3. Facilitators: Members of the work unit can be coached to do the job (c.f. Previous interventions tend to use outside experts) In view of the favourable findings, the novel workplace well-being intervention can be adapted and transferred to other work settings, for examples, in commercial and government work units. Application of the intervention in other cultures is also worth pursuing. Second, findings of the current study support our hypothesis that work engagement is not necessarily the higher the better. There seems to be an optimal, sustainable range of work engagement. This is an important contribution to our current understanding of this important construct in workplace well-being. Further basic and intervention research on this area is worth pursuing, and will help optimize our workplace well-being strategies.

17610418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610418.value: Grounded in an integrative body-mind-spirit (BMS) approach, a brief daily workplace well-being program was developed for community mental health workers (CMHW) who were vulnerable to burnout. To evaluate the program’s efficacy, this study adopted a multi-site randomized controlled trial design. Data analysis included 175 participants from 10 community mental health centres. Overall findings demonstrated the protective effect of the Brief Daily BMS program in preserving work engagement and reducing burnout among CMHW. We also examined the effects of interventions on highly engaged workers. Of the whole sample, we examined participants’ work engagement and positive affect from the highest quarter (HWE) and the lowest quarter (LWE) of work engagement at baseline. The interventions had decreasing effects on work engagement in the HWE subgroup. There was an increasing trend of positive affect on the HWE group only in the BMS program. The trajectories of work engagement in the HWE moved towards a moderate level. Our results suggest that the work engagement’s decrease in the HWE group could be a sign of recovery and relaxation. Work engagement may not be necessarily the higher the better, but has an optimal, sustainable range. The findings have significant theoretical and practical implications.

17610818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610818.value: 單性別學校對學生社交發展的影響是個爭議性的話題。本研究將測試單性別學校的學生是否比男女校的學生更具性別顯著性(即在認知基模上傾向于聯繫到性別相關的概念) 及更不擅長與兩性相處。測試這些假設有相當重要性。第一、高性別顯著性會令人們更容易性別定型、對異性持更負面的態度及、更不願意與異性相處，及迴避做與自身性別定型不符的個人選擇；第二，要游刃於無可避免的混合性別世界，必須與同性及異性建立良好關係。性別隔離會影響性別顯著性及人際關係。單性別學校的支持者和反對者都引用發展性群際理論 (重點探討環境條件如何影響性別顯著性及性別分化) 及社會認知理論 (重點探討社會化及性別基模)去預測這些結果，但是這些預測並不一致。支持者認為結果是正面的，例如單性別學校會減低性別顯著性及性別定型；而反對者認為結果是負面的，例如單性別學校會增加性別顯著性，亦因限制與兩性相處的經驗而妨礙了與異性的互動。以前的研究很多時候忽略了測試這些結果及沒有控制其他混淆因素。而且，前瞻性的研究忽略了單性別及男女校的學生在入學及畢業這些關鍵過渡期的發展。因此，是次研究旨在運用交叉遞延方法，以實測證據直接比較單性別學校和男女校的學生在高中畢業時前後的性別顯著性和人際關係。性別顯著性及異性關係將會以多個量表量度。並且，是次研究將會第一次測試單性別學校和男女校學生有異的原因，即不同類型學校是否通過影響性別顯著性進而影響人際關係。是次研究計劃運用數個現進方法 (包括前瞻性跟進及配對技巧) 來達成這些目標。是次研究結果將會在研究及實用性上具有重要意義。首先，研究能就現時對於單性別學校在性別顯著性和人際關係上有好處還是壞處這個爭議性的話題上提供實質證據；另外，只有實質證據能幫助了解哪個理論在影響性別隔離的結果上是最重要的；最後，是次探究結果將有助設計介入策略以令學生在混合性別世界中游刃有餘。

17611318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611318.value: Since the constitutional movement of the late Qing dynasty, the quest for constitutionalism had been an important theme in modern Chinese political and legal developments. There were three eras of constitution-making: the last decade of the Qing (1901-11), the republican era (1911-1949), and the communist era (1949-). Dr Sun Yat-sen, founding father of the Republic of China (RoC), developed a three-stage theory of the Chinese republic’s political development: military rule, 'political tutelage' and 'constitutionalism' (xianzheng, alternatively translated as 'constitutional governance'). Although China in theory entered the third stage when a new RoC Constitution was enacted in 1946, this Constitution became largely suspended as the RoC regime moved to Taiwan and introduced martial law upon its defeat in the Chinese Civil War. The establishment of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) in 1949 inaugurated a new era of constitution-making under the Soviet Union’s influence. The ‘Western’ or ‘bourgeois’ idea of constitutionalism was however rejected, despite the making of several Constitutions of the PRC since 1954. Under the Xi Jingping regime, the very discourse of ‘constitutionalism’ (xianzheng) has been suppressed, even though the concept of ‘ruling the country according to law’ (which was constitutionalized in 1999) has been re-affirmed. Despite setbacks in the project of constitutionalism in mainland China, Taiwan has since the 1990s realized the constitutionalism that was promised by the 1946 Constitution. At the same time, constitutional governance has also been practiced in the Special Administrative Regions of Hong Kong and Macau under the ‘One Country Two Systems’ framework in accordance with their Basic Laws. The experience of Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau in constitutional governance and the practice of constitutionalism in a Chinese society may serve as a valuable resource for mainland China to draw on should it pursue political and constitutional reforms at some point in the future. This project seeks to describe, analyze, explain and compare the institutions and dynamics of constitutional governance and the practice of constitutionalism in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau, and explore their implications for the possible development of constitutionalism in mainland China. It also reviews the constitutional history of China since the late Qing attempt at constitutional reform, and examines the current practice and discourse of the Rule of Law and public law in mainland China, for the purpose of exploring the possibilities of constitutional reform in the future. 晚清的立憲運動以來，追求憲政是中國現代政治和法律史的一個主題。現代中國的憲法發展包括三個時期，即（1）晚清（1901至1911年）、民國時期（1911至1949年），以及中華人民共和國時期（1949年至今）。孫中山先生提出了中華民國的政治發展的三個階段的理論，即“軍政”、“訓政”和“憲政”。1946年《中華民國憲法》的制定，理論上把中國帶進憲政的階段，但由於國共內戰，這部憲法未能在中國大陸實施。1949年中華人民共和國成立以後，憲法的制定受到蘇聯的憲法思想的影響，尤其是在1954年《中華人民共和國憲法》的制定的時候。另一方面，西方“資產階級”憲法思想則被堅決否定。2014年以來，“憲政”成為討論的“禁區”，但“依法治國”的構想卻已經在1999年修憲時寫進了憲法，並在習近平執政的新時代得到重視和提倡。 雖然“憲政”的事業在中國大陸的前途未卜，但在台灣， 1990年代以來已經在台灣地區範圍內實現了1946年憲法的憲政構想。同時，在“一國兩制”的憲制框架下，香港和澳門特別行政區已經實行以《基本法》為依據的憲政管治。台灣地區和香港及澳門特別行政區的憲政實踐，對中國大陸來說應算是寶貴的資源；如果中國大陸在未來進行政治和憲政改革，台、港、澳的經驗將具有參考價值。 本研究項目的目的，在於敘述、分析，解釋和比較台灣地區和港澳特別行政區的憲政實踐，並探討此實踐對於中國大陸未來憲政發展的意義。本研究項目並將回顧晚清以來中國的憲政史，並審視當前中國大陸關於法治和公法的理論和實踐，從而探索其未來的憲政改革的可能性。

17611318.label: Realisation of objectives
17611318.value: Objective one. I have reviewed the existing literature in English in Chinese on the history of the development of constitutionalism in China since the late 19 century, the drafting of the 1954 PRC Constitution and the subsequent constitutions including the current constitution of 1982, the major amendments to the 1982 Constitution, and the current practice and discourse of the Rule of Law in China. The relevant rules and practices of the Chinese constitutional system, and the writings of leading scholars of Chinese constitution law have been studied, with a view to extracting resources for the possible development of Chinese constitutionalism in the future. The theory and practice of constitutionalism originated in the Western world and were ‘imported’ into China and in the late 19 century. I have researched into the multiple purposes behind the project of constitutional reform in the late Qing and the early Republican periods. Unlike the situation in many Western states in which the constitutional project was largely shaped by the Enlightenment ideas and ideals of protecting liberties and rights, designing a rational system of government and subjecting political power to legal control, the constitutional projects in early modern China was partly for the purpose of bringing China in line with international practices, and also for the purpose of strengthening the nascent Chinese nation-state to ensure its survival in the age of Western imperialism. In Chinese constitutional history of the communist era, the 1954 Constitution was of fundamental importance. This constitution was actually to a significant extent modelled on the Stalinist constitution of the USSR. PRC constitutional developments have been much shaped by path-dependency; the Soviet constitutional model adopted by the PRC in 1954 still dominates the Chinese constitutional system even today. At the same time, the various subsequent amendments to the 1982 Constitution demonstrated the influence of global constitutional values and trends in China in the era of ‘reform and opening’ inaugurated by Deng Xiaoping. Objective two. I have studied the history of the enactment of the 1946 Constitution of the Republic of China (ROC) and the different phases of its implementation since 1946. I have investigated into the guiding ideology behind this constitution, which was Dr Sun Yat-sen’s political thought. After the retreat of the Kuomintang (KMT) government to Taiwan in 1949, the ROC Constitution experienced a phase of authoritarian constitutionalism, with the imposition of martial law and the introduction of the ‘Temporary Provisions for the Period of National Mobilization to Suppress the Communist Rebellion’. I have researched into the subsequent transition to liberal democratic constitutionalism that began in the late 1980s and was speedily completed in the 1990s. One primary focus of my study has been the operation of the Council of Grand Justices as the constitutional court of the ROC regime. I have studied the 1946 Constitution in considerable details. The Constitution reflected Sun Yat’sen’s constitutional thought. Sun’s most significant contributions include the development of the theory of the three-stage process of China’s constitutional development, and the theorizing of the institutional framework of the five ‘yuans’, which show upon which represented a synthesis of Western separation of (three) powers and the traditional Chinese institutions of the censorate and the civil service examination system. The 1946 Constitution was also shaped by the constitutional thought of Zhang Junmai (Carson Chang), who was familiar with German as well as Anglo-American constitutionalism. Even though the 1946 Constitution had not been fully put into practice during the authoritarian era of KMT rule in Taiwan, post 1987 developments have realised the promises of this constitution. The case of Taiwan demonstrates that the 1946 Constitution, made in mainland China and designed by thinkers committed to the Chinese nation-state and its future, can sustain a Western-style liberal constitutional democracy. On the other hand, I have also examined and evaluated the criticism that because of the pernicious political struggles between the KMT and the Democratic Progressive Party, Taiwan after democratization has been beset by populism and purely electoral democracy (rather than genuine liberal constitutional democracy), sometimes in disregard of the constitutional values of toleration, pluralism, and respect for different views. Objective three. I have reviewed the history of the drafting of the Basic Laws of the Special Administrative Regions of Hong Kong and Macau, with a view to identifying the basic elements of the original design of the constitutional arrangement known as ‘One Country, Two Systems’. I have studied the history of the implementation of the Basic Laws, particularly the Hong Kong Basic Law. Elements of the practice of the constitutional arrangement of ‘One Country, Two Systems’ in Hong Kong and Macau that demonstrate constitutionalism at work have been studied and identified. In the case of Hong Kong, the fundamental change to the constitutional system brought about by the enactment of the national security law in 2020 and the electoral reform in 2021 have been analysed. British colonial rule in Hong Kong resulted in the transplant of the common law and the values of the Rule of Law and judicial independence to Hong Kong. Hong Kong before the handover was more Westernised than either mainland or Taiwan in terms of its legal and constitutional culture. After the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration in 1984, the British Hong Kong government introduced democratic constitutional reforms and enacted a bill of rights. The latter inaugurated the era of constitutional judicial review in Hong Kong. After the handover in 1997, significant progress in the practice of constitutionalism had been made in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), at least until the enactment of the National Security Law in 2020 and the electoral reform in 2021. Before the introduction of these measures in the HKSAR by the PRC authorities in response to the ‘anti-extradition bill’ movement of 2019, Hong Kong may be considered a showcase of the synthesis of Western and socialist Chinese ideas and practices of constitutionalism, as exemplified by the interaction between the Hong Kong courts and the National People’s Congress Standing Committee, and the use of legal and constitutional means by the PRC authorities to shape constitutional developments in Hong Kong. The political struggles between the ‘pro-Establishment’ camp and the ‘pan-democrats’, like the struggles between the ‘blue’ and the ‘green’ political forces in Taiwan, exemplified the vibrant constitutional dynamics of a pluralistic political system and an autonomous civil society. Objective four. In order to investigate into the prospects for the development of Chinese constitutionalism in the future, I have studied the theoretical contributions of leading scholars such as Larry Backer, Jiang Shigong, Chen Duanhong, Gao Quanxi, Qin Qianhong, Ke Huaqing, Tong Zhiwei, Han Dayuan, Lin Laifan, Zhang Qianfan, Ren Jiantao, Tian Lei, etc. I have also reviewed the major schools of thought regarding Chinese constitutionalism, such as liberal constitutionalism, Confucian constitutionalism and socialist constitutionalism. The significance of the official rejection of ‘constitutionalism’ (xianzheng) discourse since 2013, and the implications of Xi Jinping’s ‘Rule of Law’ thought for the development of constitutionalism in the foreseeable future, have been investigated into. Furthermore, I have also identified the concept, doctrines, principles, rules, institutions and practices that have evolved within the PRC constitutional, political and legal systems in the era of ‘reform and opening’ that may provide a foundation for the development of constitutionalism in China in the future.

17611318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611318.value: Since the late Qing Dynasty, China has accumulated significant amounts of experience in developing constitutional theories and constitutional doctrine, and in drafting constitutions and seeking to implement them. The various exercises in Chinese constitutionalism include the late Qing constitutional reform, the early Republican experiments in Chinese constitutionalism, and the subsequent constitutional exercises conducted by the Chinese Nationalist Party regime and the Chinese Communist Party. After 1949, the Chinese constitutional experience has continued to develop in Taiwan under the 1946 Constitution of the Republic of China, and in mainland China under the 1954 PRC Constitution and its successors. The enactment of the 1982 Constitution of the new era of ‘reform and opening’ inaugurated a new stage in the development of Chinese constitutionalism. At around the same time, the constitutional project of ‘One Country, Two Systems’ was conceived; it was then mapped out in the two Basic Laws of the Special Administrative Regions of Hong Kong and Macau, which have been implemented since 1997 and 1999 respectively. Since Taiwan’s democratisation began in the late 1980s, the liberal-democratic promises of the 1946 Constitution have been largely realised in Taiwan. The constitutional project of ‘One Country, Two Systems’, which entailed a synthesis of elements of liberal democratic constitutionalism and Chinese socialist constitutional practice, was originally promising, but suffered a significant setback after the ‘anti-extradition bill’ movement of 2019. In the Chinese mainland under Xi Jinping, ‘ruling the country according to law’ continued to be emphasized, but the discourse of constitutionalism was rejected and banned. The prospects for the development of constitutionalism in mainland China are not promising in the short term. However, the legal reforms that the PRC has continuously and consistently engaged in since the late 1970s, as well as the theories developed by Chinese scholars of constitutional law and constitutionalism, collectively constitute resources that can serve as the foundation for the future development of Chinese constitutionalism. Furthermore, the constitutional experience that has been accumulated in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau may also contribute to this development.

17611318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611318.value: Using the dichotomy between ‘political constitutionalism’ and ‘legal’ or ‘judicial constitutionalism’, it can be said that mainland China practised the former, while Taiwan and also to a considerable extent Hong Kong practised the latter. Judicial constitutionalism began to develop in Taiwan even before its democratisation in the late 1980s, and paved a good foundation for its subsequent liberalisation and democratisation. In Hong Kong, constitutional judicial review subject to the possible intervention of the NPCSC also flourished under the constitutional framework of ‘One Country, Two Systems’. Drawing from such experience in Hong Kong and Taiwan, it is possible and practicable for judicial constitutionalism to evolve in mainland China even under one-party rule. Further investigations into this potential should be viable and promising. Other potential areas for further research include the possible revival of the movement for separation of party and state proposed in the charity young area in the 1980s, and the possibility that existing institutional mechanisms within the People’s Congress system (such as its power of scrutiny of the administration) may be activated in a liberalised political atmosphere in the future to achieve the checks and balances, pluralism and the expression of diverse interests and opinions that are required by constitutionalism.

17611318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611318.value: Achieving constitutionalism in the Chinese nation-state has been a fundamental aspiration of the Chinese people since the late Qing dynasty. Significant amounts of experience in developing constitutional doctrines and building constitutional institutions has been accumulated in the Republican era and in the PRC. The essential elements of constitutionalism include the Rule of Law, separation of powers, political checks and balances, judicial independence, and the protection of civil liberties and human rights. These elements have been largely realised in Taiwan since the political reform of the late 1980s, and also to a significant extent in the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau. In mainland China, significant progress has been made in the development of the Rule of Law in the era of ‘reform and opening’ since the 1980s. In addition to the Rule of Law, the concept of supervision of the exercise of power has also been increasingly recognised in contemporary China. These developments, together with the strengthening of the institutional capacity of the People’s Congress system (at the national and local levels) and the court system, provide a good foundation for the realisation of constitutionalism in mainland China in the long-term.

17611718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611718.value: Inflation is a fundamental risk in asset markets. The usual measure of inflation, Consumer Price Index (CPI), is composed of core, food, and energy inflation. It is largely unnoticed that these price indices have distinct statistical properties and implications on asset returns. This project studies how risks of different inflation are priced differently in asset markets. We show that core inflation is far more persistent and less volatile than energy inflation. The two types of inflation have a low correlation of 0.2, even though both are highly correlated with CPI. Given this important difference, we further document novel facts that asset returns have qualitatively different exposures on core and energy inflation. We estimate the risk exposure (beta) of stock, bond, currency, and commodity returns to unexpected inflation shocks. Equity market portfolio has a negative CPI beta, a negative core beta, but a positive energy beta. Treasury bonds have a negative CPI beta that emerges mainly from core inflation. The energy beta is tiny and insignificant. In contrast to bond, currency returns have a positive CPI beta that comes solely from energy inflation. Finally, commodity futures load unambiguously on energy but has little correlation with core. Beyond these preliminary findings, we will further explore implications on (1) cross section of stocks, currencies, and commodities; (2) time-varying exposures; (3) PPI inflation; (4) TIPS; (5) changing inflation target. We will build a general equilibrium model to interpret the facts. Considering energy inflation will introduce two key novelties into a standard production-based asset pricing model. Fist, the energy price is close to be flexible and much less rigid than core goods empirically. The Phillips Curve applies to core goods but not to energy. Energy inflation is driven by energy supply and demand shocks. Moreover, the central bank responds to core and energy inflation differently, since the main objective is to fight against core inflation that has non-neutral effects. This is consistent with the practice in the US. Introducing these new features, we expect the model to generate different core and energy inflation risks. We will estimate the model by Bayesian methods and replicate the asset loadings on risks of core and energy inflation, and the correlation structure of returns of different asset classes. Finally, we will conduct monetary policy experiments involving differential responses to core and energy inflation. 通货膨胀是资本市场中最根本的风险之一。通常的通货膨胀度量是消费价格指数。其中包含核心商品、食品和能源通货膨胀。不同通胀风险的不同作用在通胀和资产价格的文献中几乎没有被研究过。 我们发现核心通胀比能源通胀更持久，而两者的相关性很低。基于这些差异，我们进一步发现资产收益于受到核心通胀和能源通胀的影响不同。这些不同反应在股票市场，债券市场，汇率市场和大宗商品市场。 我们建立了一般均衡模型来解释这些新的发现。我们引入了两个能源通胀的关键特征到带有生产的宏观金融模型中。首先，能源价格的价格刚性程度远小于核心商品。其次，中央银行的货币政策对能源价格的反应更小。这个模型可以解释核心通胀和能源通胀风险的不同。

17611718.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611718.value: Do “real” assets protect against inflation? Core inflation betas of stocks are negative while energy betas are positive; currencies, commodities, and real estate also mostly hedge against energy inflation but not core. These hedging properties are reflected in the prices of inflation risks: only core inflation carries a negative risk premium, and its magnitude is consistent both within and across asset classes, uniquely among macroeconomic risk factors. While high core inflation tends to be followed by low real output, consumption, and dividend payouts, it impacts asset prices through both cash-flow and discount rate channels. The relative contribution of core and energy changes over time, helping explain the time-varying correlation between stock and bond returns. A two-sector New Keynesian model qualitatively accounts for these facts and implies that the changing stock-bond correlation can be attributed to the shifting importance of supply and demand shocks in driving energy inflation over time.

17611718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611718.value: The current model delivers the results qualitatively consistent with the data. The next step is to bring the model to data and build a quantitative model to match the facts. In this way, the model can address important questions about inflation and monetary policy.

17612118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612118.value: Background Negative symptom is a core feature of schizophrenia that is strongly linked to poor outcomes in patients. Current pharmacological treatments have limitations and many patients are in need of adjunct treatment for their negative symptoms. There is growing evidence to suggest transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is effective in improving negative symptom, but critical issues remain unanswered concerning the duration of effects in patients with schizophrenia. Aim A double-blind, randomized, controlled trial was designed to address these issues. We will compare the effect of 20 sessions of active tDCS vs. 10 sessions of sham tDCS plus 10 sessions of active tDCS vs. 20 sessions of sham tDCS in improving negative symptoms in patients with schizophrenia. We hypothesize that patients who receive twenty sessions of active tDCS will have more reduction in negative symptoms over 12 weeks when compared to other groups. Methods Ninety-three patients with schizophrenia with predominate negative symptoms will be randomly assigned to receive either a) 20 sessions of active tDCS, b) 10 sessions of sham tDCS plus 10 sessions of active tDCS, or c) 20 sessions of sham tDCS over 4 weeks. Symptom, cognitive function, social functioning and side effects will be assessed at baseline, then bi-weekly. The effect of tDCS on negative symptoms over time will be compared in the different treatment groups using analysis of variance with repeated measures to examine the group, time and their interaction effects. Possible results and implications This study will provide us with information on whether twenty sessions of active tDCS will have the greatest improvements of negative symptoms over 12 weeks than other group and how the negative symptoms change after tDCS treatment. Data from this study will enrich our understanding towards the optimal interval of tDCS treatment. This has potential to become a useful non-invasive adjunct treatment to improve negative symptoms and promote recovery in patients with schizophrenia. 背景 陰性症狀是思覺失調的核心特徵之一，與患者的康復有密切的關連。目前藥物治療對減輕患者的陰性症狀仍有其局限，所以需尋找其他輔助治療幫助。現在有越來越多文獻顯示經顱直流電治療能有效減低陰性症狀，但對於療效的持續性等重要資料仍需進一步研究了解。 目的 我們將進行一項雙盲隨機對照臨床研究，比較進行二十次直流電治療、十次直流電治療和十次對照直流電治療，及二十次對照直流電治療對減輕陰性症狀的效果。我們假設接受二十次直流電治療的患者相將會比其他組別的患者其陰性症狀會在十二週有較大改善。 方法 九十三名有明顯陰性症狀的思覺失調患者將被隨機分配在四個星期內將接受(1)二十次直流電治療，(2)十次對照直流電治療和十次直流電治療，或(3)二十次對照直流電治療。患者的症狀、認知和社交功能及副作用將於第一次及其後每兩週評估一次。 直流電治療治療對陰性症狀的效益將會用重複測量變異數分析法去研究不同治療組別，時間與其相互作用的影響。 可能的研究結果和啟示 本研究將幫助了解二十次直流電擊治療是否比其他組別較能於十二週改善陰性症狀，以及直流電治療對陰性症狀的效果。本研究將豐富我們對直流電治療效用的理解。這種非入侵性治療有機會成為一種有效改善陰性症狀的輔助治療方法，促進思覺失調患者的康復。

17612118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17612118.value: The baseline characteristics of the three groups were similar with no significant difference between symptoms, cognitive functions and social functioning. When comparing the negative symptoms with a mixed-model, Group×Time interactions, no statistical significant difference was found between the three groups. The effects on cognitive functions were significant for short-term memory and executive function. The effects of immediate recall of logical memory test (P<0.05) and animal naming of category fluency test (P<0.05) for the 20 active and 10 active tDCS groups remained significant after controlling for age, gender and education years as covariates. The effects on cognition observed at week 2 in both intervention groups were maintained at week 12 follow-up. There were no significant changes in other domains of cognitive functions, including attention, speed of processing, visual learning and social cognition between the 3 groups. We did not find any significant change in either positive symptoms (P=0.542) or social functioning between the 3 groups (P=0.485).

17612118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17612118.value: The current research project did not find significant change in negative symptoms to support the application of tDCS as an adjunctive treatment for negative symptoms in psychosis. Further research is needed to explore usual treatment for negative symptoms.

17612118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17612118.value: Negative symptom is a core feature of schizophrenia that is strongly linked to poor outcomes in patients. Current pharmacological treatments have limitations and many patients are in need of adjunct treatment for their negative symptoms. In a group of stable, medicated patients with psychosis, we explored whether participating in a noninvasive brain stimulation intervention (transcranial direct current stimulation, tDCS) improve negative and positive symptoms, cognitive functions and social functioning. A total of 93 patients with psychosis joined a 12-week randomized controlled study of 20 active tDCS or 10 active tDCS sessions compared with control group (20 sham tDCS sessions). No significant changes were found in negative symptoms, positive symptoms and social functioning. However, both 20 active and 10 active tDCS groups demonstrated significant improvements in short-term memory (P<0.05) and executive function (P<0.005) when compared with the control group. The current research project did not find significant change in negative symptoms to support the application of tDCS as an adjunctive treatment for negative symptoms in psychosis. Further research is needed to explore usual treatment for negative symptoms. This study was supported by RGC funding (17612118) by the University Grants Committee, Hong Kong.

17612218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17612218.value: 近代東亞企業的誕生: 醬油業的例子, 1880-1960

17612218.label: Project Objectives
17612218.value: To trace the transformation of traditional soy sauce from a home- or community-made, handicraft product to an industrial one with modern mechanical and chemical technologies in East Asia (Japan, China, Korea, Taiwan) from 1880-1960. To explore technological choices that increased production to industrial scale, enhanced hygienic standards and reduced production time and costs. To explore the emergence and background of soy sauce entrepreneurs by studying the first successful global enterprises, focusing on their technological decisions, their marketing strategies, labor organization in face of increasing competition in a growing global market. Regional differences will be highlighted. To study the changing role of the modern East Asian state and related institutions (tariff and taxation systems, universities, research institutions, vocational schools, training programs etc.) in soy sauce making, and the training and impact of new state agents (scientists, technocrats, institutions) on the development of new soy sauce industries. To explore how new soy sauce making technologies transformed traditional values attributed to a product defined by its nutritional content, smell, color, and taste, branding, packaging, local character, “authenticity” etc. that reflect both regional coherence and differences. In other words, to analyze what modern soy sauce has “gained” or “lost” in cultural and dietetic terms after being technologically transformed into a modern product. This issue is central in the construction of soy sauce today as a “cultural heritage” product, a genuine, “traditional” East Asian food to be distinguished from the “fake” or the “chemical”. To explore technological choices that increased production to industrial scale, enhanced hygienic standards and reduced production time and costs.

To explore the emergence and background of soy sauce entrepreneurs by studying the first successful global enterprises, focusing on their technological decisions, their marketing strategies, labor organization in face of increasing competition in a growing global market. 17612218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612218.value: This project aims to construct the first integrated East Asian history of modern soy sauce, exploring the transformation of this ancient condiment into a global product. Soy sauce is an East Asian identity food—a product that embodies and symbolizes the biological, socio-cultural, and historical makeup of East Asian cultures. That soy is an East Asian crop par excellence, and qu/kōji/nurukgyun (麴as pronounced in Chinese, Japanese and Korean), the key ferment type needed to make soy sauce and other traditional alcoholic drinks and medicines, containing specific enzymes and organisms, is one that can develop only in East Asia, makes soy sauce a uniquely informative vehicle for understanding the region and its intraregional exchanges and connections. This collaborative study allows for a new understanding of East Asia as a region by focusing on the circulations of individuals, knowledge, and practices related to soy sauce making in Japan, Taiwan, the Korean peninsula, and China from ca.1880 to 1960. Modern soy sauce began with the introduction of new mechanical and chemical technologies to accelerate and increase soy sauce production first in Japan, and later in the rest of East Asia, with different cohorts of experts being trained in the West or in Japanese universities and institutions. Some of these became entrepreneurs — “fixers” as defined by Harvard economist Joseph Schumpeter — innovators who technically and managerially refashioned the local and regional product into a modern one that conquered regional and global markets. Soy sauce presents a significant story that illustrates not only the typical narrative of technological breakthrough and market expansion, but provides possible answers to the following questions: 1)what does it take to become the modern, East Asian soy sauce “fixer,” and what are the historical ramifications to contemporary entrepreneurship? 2) how does the flow and circulation of new technological knowledge, practices and products enable the reconfiguration and reconceptualization of East Asia as a culture region? 3) In what ways were modern food technologies and marketing strategies part and parcel of state and empire building in East Asia in this period?

17612318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17612318.value: 我將會考究有否支持侵權賠償制度的非後果性理由。 侵權賠償制度有以下兩個特點： (a) 一個人如因另一人不當行為蒙受損失，則(如一些其他條件也被滿足下)前者有法律權利向後者得到賠償； (b) 如前者的損失不是由其他人不當造成(如因意外造成),他不會得到一樣的賠償。 如同一般普通法制度，香港有一套侵權賠償制度。然而, 侵權賠償制度不是對損失和傷亡的唯一應對。舉例，我們可改為用一套使受害者不論損失是否由他人不當行為造成也得到一樣賠償的制度，[1]或一套要求所有行為不當的人，不論他們的行為有沒有造成他人損失，都要交錢進一個中央基金以作將來賠償其他人損失之用的制度。[2]有什麼原因我們要選擇侵權賠償制度呢？如Patrick Atiyah說，侵權賠償制度好像優待某些受害者(其損失是由其他人不當行為造成，而不是由其他原因如意外造成，的受害者)和某些行為不當的人(其不當行為幸運地沒有造成他人損失的人)。[3]如此，不是代表侵權賠償制度是不公義及隨意的嗎？ 以往支持侵權賠償制度的理由一般是通過指出它會帶來的好後果。然而,近來有論認為有好的非後果性理由支持侵權賠償制度。[4]我希望考究此是否真確。 [1] See, e.g., M Franklin, “Replacing the Negligence Lottery”, (1967) 53 Virginia Law Review 774 and the New Zealand Accident Compensation Scheme. [2] C Schroder, “Corrective Justice, Liability for Risks, and Tort Law”, (1990) 38 UCLA Law Review 143. [3] P Atiyah, The Damages Lottery (Oxford: Hart Publishing, 1997). [4] See the works referred to in the Background of Research below
