17613818.value: 兒童早期逆境與其身心發展影響 ： 追蹤青年從社交，認知，行為及免疫途徑中的前瞻性研究

17613818.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17613818.value: Dr Chan, Sherry Kit-wa Prof Chang, Wing Chung Prof Chen, Eric Yu Hai Prof Hui, Christy Lai-ming Prof Ip, Patrick Dr Lee, Edwin Ho-ming

17613818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613818.value: Background. Mounting evidence across countries indicates that childhood adversity, namely child maltreatment and a socioeconomic disadvantage, instantiates the development and progression of mental health difficulties and chronic health conditions in adolescence plus adulthood. Local evidence suggests a widening gap in development between youth from underprivileged vs. resourceful backgrounds. How exactly does early adversity become embedded to shape these developmental and health outcomes, throughout the lifespan? The interactive pathways underlying long-arm effects of childhood adversity remain unclear. The proposed study will utilize an existing cohort of children with ample baseline data, and aims to elucidate how the broader childhood environment can disrupt multiple psychosocial and bio-behavioral systems during adolescence. Unmasking such interactive pathways across systems may shed light on plausible resilience elements that can buffer deleterious implications associated with childhood adversity. Method. This study will draw an existing cohort of ~500 families that already have two time points of data on childhood environment and development. The sample of youth will be on average age 12 during this third visit. Changes in parental and family circumstances will be probed. Youth psychosocial measures include life events and coping responses, mental health symptoms (with a focus on mood disorders), emotion processing, social relationships, and cognitive performance. Bio-behavioral measures include anthropometric measures, pubertal stage, and health practices. A peripheral blood sample will also be collected by antecubital blood draw to examine systemic and genomic immune activation. Significance. Disparities in emotion disorders and age-related diseases remain a growing concern globally and locally, and evidence on the etiology of social health disparities point to roots in early childhood circumstances. Results from this study will link childhood environment characteristics with adolescent functioning across psychosocial, behavioral, and biological domains. Findings will help build a longitudinal model of risk and resilience trajectories to shed light on the interactive pathways across multiple health regulatory systems, and the respective juncture points that serve as viable targets for early intervention.

17614118.label: Project Objectives

17614118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614118.value: The scale of migration has increased exponentially in recent decades in much of the Southeast Asian region. While the impact of migration on the wellbeing of left-behind children has been well studied, there is little systematic research on (1) the impact of migration patterns on the longer-term socioeconomic consequences, in terms of education attainment and employment outcomes, of these left-behind children as they transition into young adulthood and (2) how these impacts vary based on whether the parent(s) are international or internal domestic migrants The proposed study will capitalize on two existing complementary baseline surveys of international and internal migration within one Southeast Asian country, Thailand, to address these significant research gaps and systematically examine the causal relationships between childhood experiences of parental migration, alternative caregiving arrangements and health and human capital in young adulthood. This study will collect survey data on young adults aged 20 to 22 years old in 2019 on key outcome variables of health (physical, psychological, risk behaviour) and human capital (education and employment). Longitudinal data analysis methods will be used to examine the impact of parental migration during childhood and young adulthood outcomes. The study will be the first to establish a unique longitudinal dataset that will allow for investigating the influences of parental migration on a range of health and socioeconomic outcomes for their left-behind children, while taking into account diverse parental migration patterns. Thailand is one of several countries in the Southeast Asian region—a major source region of global migrants including to destinations such as Hong Kong. As a middle income country and source of internal, international and in-migration Thailand provides an excellent case study to inform development policy and practice for other countries with similar economic and migration profiles. Findings generated from this study will therefore contribute empirical evidence to enhance understanding of longer-term consequences, both costs and benefits, of parental migration for children who grew up in transnational and/or internal migrant households, further expand our theoretical understandings on the complex relationships between migration and development, and contribute to national, regional and global policy development on migration. 東南亞的移民規模在近幾十年來不斷增大。雖然有大量關於移民活動給留守兒童身心健康帶來影響的研究， 但它們大多缺乏對以下兩點的系統性梳理：首先是關於不同的父母移民模式給逐漸進入成年期的留守青少年帶來的長期性社會經濟方面的影響，例如他們的受教育程度以及就業機會。其次是細緻比較這些不同移民模式，例如國内流動或跨國流動，給子女帶來怎樣不同的影響。使用來自兩項分別對泰國移民群體中國際流動和國内流動進行的補充性基綫調查所得到的數據，本研究不僅將回應前述研究缺口，并且還將系統地分析童年經歷父母移民，非傳統照顧安排，留守兒童成年後的健康及人力資本狀況三者之間的關係。 本研究計劃于2019年在目標群體中，蒐集年齡介乎20至22嵗年輕人關於健康和人力資本的數據指標。這些長期性研究的數據將用于檢驗父母移民對留守兒童在童年以及成年后不同時期的不同影響。這些數據將首先構建一個獨特的長期性數據庫。以此爲基礎，一系列關於父母移民經歷及不同移民模式對於留守兒童在社會經濟方面影響的分析將會逐步展開。 泰國是東南亞主要的移民輸出國之一，其目的地就包括香港。作爲一個國際移民和國内移民同樣活躍的中等收入國家，泰國不僅可以爲政策制定提供多元的個案，其經驗還可以應用於類似國家和地區的分析及實踐當中。因此，研究結果將增進我們對成長于跨國或國内移民家庭的留守兒童的理解，理解父母移民經歷對他們的成長帶來怎樣正面或負面的長期影響。同時，研究結果還將有助於拓展我們對移民與發展之間複雜關係的理論構建，從而為地區性以及國内國際移民政策的制定，提供依據。

17614218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614218.value: 中国城市更新中的公众参与：货真价实还是形式主义？

17614218.label: Project Objectives
17614218.value: To determine the nature and extent of public participation in China’s urban redevelopment; To investigate the new social and political conditions upon which participatory urban redevelopment has been brought about; To evaluate the effects of participatory urban redevelopment upon urban economic growth, spatial inequality, and social justice.
rows: To determine the nature and extent of public participation in China’s urban redevelopment;
To investigate the new social and political conditions upon which participatory urban redevelopment has been brought about;
To evaluate the effects of participatory urban redevelopment upon urban economic growth, spatial inequality, and social justice.

17614218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614218.value: 一般认为，社会主义国家的城市规划由政府统一制定而缺少市民参与。然而，近年很多中国城市的住房拆迁项目开始引入社区参与决策。这种尝试为城市研究提出了新的研究问题：这种公众参与究竟有多深入？它对于我们重新认识中国不断变化中的国家与社会的关系有什么启示？本研究旨在探索近年来中国城市更新中公众参与的性质，背景和效应。研究的目的包括：界定公众参与在城市更新过程中的性质和程度；揭示这种它的政治和社会根源；评估它对城市经济发展，地区差异，和社会公正所产生的影响。本研究重点放在北京，上海和深圳三个在城市更新方面领先的都市区。研究方法包括对全国二百多个地级及以上的城市统计资料的定量分析和对野外考察及面谈所得到的详尽信息做定性分析。本项目建基于多年积累的实地研究经验和当地研究网络，研究成果将促进中外理论界对中国不断变化中的国家与社会的关系有新的认知；提高中国的城市规划与管理水平；同时为关心中国内地城市发展的香港政府，商人及其他有识人士提供重要信息。

17614218.label: Realisation of objectives
17614218.value: The objectives of this research are basically to determine the nature and extent of public participation in urban redevelopment; investigate its social and political motivations; and evaluate its effects upon urban economic growth, spatial inequality, and social justice. We are pleased to report that these three objectives have been successfully and fruitfully achieved thanks to the unwavering supports and collaboration of a whole team of experienced local Chinese researchers mobilized from the field sites of this project, namely Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen. We have mobilized some of the best experts in the field, including Professor LIU Tao, (Peking University), Professor TIAN Li (Tsinghua University), Professor CHEN Jie (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Professor LI Guichai (Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School), and their post-doctoral as well as graduate students. A summary of what and how we have done is provided as follows: Objective 1 is to determine the nature and extent of public participation in China’s urban redevelopment. This seemingly straightforward task of social survey has turned out to be more challenging and complicated than our original thoughts. At the macro level, Chinese authorities under the new leadership of Xi Jinping have in recent years tightened up control over the release of sensitive data and information to foreign sources. For the nature of this research, determination of participatory urban redevelopment to be genuine engagement or symbolic governance obviously sounds too critical and cynical to warrant any enthusiastic collaboration from local Chinese researchers let alone positive responses from planners, professionals, and local cadres. The difficulty encountered in data collection has been further compounded by the fact that different organizations, state agencies and localities tended to have the information collected and presented in different manners without consistency and comparability. More problematic has been a large discrepancy found between the data and information gathered from different sources for the same case. Furthermore, the absence of a national standard for citizen participation in urban redevelopment has meant that there exists a great variation among localities in terms of the extent and manner of community participation. After serious consultation and discussions with experienced local Chinese collaborators, we have decided to undertake detailed and in-depth investigations in six cases carefully chosen from the three cities, namely 丰台区西铁营村亚林西改造项目 and 石景山区首钢改造项目 in Beijing, 虹口区 and 黄埔区露香园街道 in Shanghai, and 南山区大冲村改造项目 and 福田区赛格日立工业区改造项目 in Shenzhen. Our approach has uncovered a fascinating pattern and process of participatory urban redevelopment in which the nature and extent of citizen participation vary depending on location, property rights, local culture and the state-market portfolio. More specifically, citizen participation is found to be relatively limited, rhetorical and symbolic for those projects involving redevelopment of the (land) property that is state-owned, remotely located, and heavily intervened by the local state in a top-down fashion. By comparison, citizen participation has turned out to be better organized and more genuinely carried out if the redevelopment projects involve a central location, collectively owned property, sophisticated residents, advanced economy, and high degree of marketization. For examples, in the Hongkou District (虹口区) in Shanghai, resident committees were formed at the grassroots level to take the lead in community participation and organize opinion surveys as well as voting for the bidding firms to be entrusted for the appraisal of demolition, compensation and resettlement. However, community participation in the Luxiang Yuan Neighborhood (黄埔区露香园街道) was found to be heavily handed and manipulated by the district government with the affected residents and developers effectively marginalized. Community participation has demonstrated certain elements of genuine engagements in the case of the Hongkou District (虹口区) with a central location, advanced economy and a group of sophisticated residents, but it has become rhetorical, superficial and symbolic in the case of the Luxiang Yuan Neighborhood (黄埔区露香园街道) whose location is relatively remote, its economy less advanced, and the affected residents less sophisticated. A similar pattern is found from Beijing and Shenzhen. In call cases, migrant population are invariably excluded from participatory decision-making even though they take a sizable share of affected residents. Objective 2 has been accomplished satisfactorily through in-depth field investigations conducted in the study sites carefully chosen from Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen as originally planned. Our field investigations have involved extensive and deep collaboration between the PI/Co-I from Hong Kong and the three research teams mobilized from the three cities to conduct field surveys, including a) questionnaire survey: To understand the motives, consideration, and concerns of different stakeholders in the process of participatory urban redevelopment, we have administered a questionnaire survey targeting local cadres, city planners, developers, and affected residents inclusive of the migrant population; b) semi-structured interviews: To understand the role played by central and local policies, city planning, governments of different levels, developers, existing land users and the migrant population, we have conducted personal interviews; and c) documentary research of relevant government policies, laws, directives, and internal reports written by professional planners. Questionnaire survey respondents and interviewees are chosen from the six field sites listed above. Our detailed field investigations have enabled us to obtain insights into the strategic interests, individual concerns and considerations of the different stakeholders involved in the practice of participatory urban redevelopment under different local contexts. Our detailed investigation has unfolded an interesting and sophisticated dynamic in which citizen participation has been brought about superficially and symbolically by local governments primarily as a means to expedite housing requisition and avoid social unrests rather than any genuine awareness of rights and entitlements. Moreover, the notion of “public interests” stipulated in the Chinese Constitution (Article 10) and the Land Management Law (Article 2) is found to have been ambiguously (mis)interpreted and effectively manipulated by local authorities in the practice of participatory urban redevelopment. Objective 3 has been successfully achieved in accordance with the original plan. We have collected and analyzed regional economic data such as per capita GDP, per capita income, level of urbanization, FDI, exports, and municipal revenue since the year 2010 at the district and county level for the three city-regions in which Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen are located. For consistency and comparability, we have adopted a classification scheme that categorizes all urban districts in Beijing (12 districts), Shanghai (16 districts) and Shenzhen (10 districts) into “city-center”, “inner-suburb” and “outer-suburb”. This has enabled us to analyze the impacts of participatory urban redevelopment upon the redistribution of local residents and migrant population as well as economic activities over time and across space. Changes in land use efficiency are analyzed on the basis of floor area ratio (容积率), building coverage ratio (建筑密度), green space ratio (绿化率) and housing value as well as rental per unit. Changes in spatial inequality are measured by Coefficient of Variance using per capita GDP at the district level for the time period of 2010-2020 and mapped out into the consistent scheme of upward converging/diverging and downward converging/diverging. We have also gathered information about the incidents of social discontents, grievance and protests against the project of urban redevelopment. Our research has generated novel research findings, some already published and others submitted for publication in leading internationally refereed journals (see Research Outcome and Research Output below for details). Overall, we are highly satisfied with the results of our research as what we have originally planned.

17614218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614218.value: This project has generated a large number of important findings, some of which have already been published in leading internationally refereed journals and presented in international conferences whilst others are in the pipeline for submission and publication. Our research findings include: 1) Contrary to the popular belief and conventional wisdom that citizen participation is often marginalized if not completely excluded in urban redevelopments in the context of a command economy, many projects of housing requisition for urban redevelopments in Chinese cities have since the 2010s introduced the scheme of community participation. 2) At the absence of a national standard for citizen participation in urban redevelopment, there exists a great variation among Chinese cities in the extent and manner of community participation. The nature and extent of citizen participation in urban redevelopment hinge upon the location of the project, property rights involved, local culture and tradition, and the degree of marketization and openness. 3) Citizen participation is found to be relatively limited, rhetorical and symbolic for those projects involving redevelopment of the (land) property that is state-owned, remotely located, and heavily intervened by the local state in a top-down fashion. By comparison, citizen participation has turned out to be better organized and more genuinely carried out if the redevelopment projects involve a central location, collectively owned property, sophisticated residents, advanced economy, and high degree of marketization and openness. 4) The new fashion of participatory urban redevelopment has been introduced rhetorically and symbolically by local governments as a tactic to expedite housing requisition and avoid social unrests rather than any genuine awareness of rights and entitlements. As the Chinese proverb runs: “[T]he drunkard’s real intention lies not on the wine” (醉翁之意不在酒). 5) In all cases, the affected migrant population who are residents of the locales for years without the local household registration status have never been consulted and their interests completely ignored from the process of participatory urban redevelopments. 6) The Chinese Constitution (Article 10) and the Land Management Law (Article 2) stipulated “the public interest” as the rationale for the state to justify property requisition, demolition and resettlements. Our research has found that the notion of “the public interest” has been ambiguously defined and effectively manipulated by local governments in the process of participatory urban redevelopment. Public opinions may have been heard through community participation, but “the public interest” has been arbitrarily (mis)interpreted and determined primarily by the powerful authorities while the actual rights and responsibilities among major stakeholders remain unchanged before and after consultation. 7) In contrast to the dominant theory of neoliberalism that describes the pattern and process of China’s urban (re)development as the outcome of a changing interaction between the state and market forces (i.e. the “hollowing out” of the state vis-à-vis “rolling out” of market forces), our research has found that the nature and dynamics of participatory urban redevelopment depend primarily upon the contestation, negotiation, and mediation between an authoritarian state and an increasingly sophisticated society.

17614218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614218.value: This project has helped push forward research frontier in urban China studies. Three important issues arisen from this project are believed to have significant potentials for theoretical and methodological advancements as well as planning and policy formation: 1. Existing research on China’s urbanization has been based upon a widely made assumption that the mechanism of decision-making in Chinese cities is monopolized by a powerful state with little space for citizen participation. This project has identified an intriguing pattern and process of participatory urban redevelopment characterized by spatial variation. Is this new fashion of participatory urban redevelopment a signal of long term trend shifting from central planning top down into participatory decision-making bottom-up or simply a temporary and ad hoc tactic that will not last long? Further research is needed to answer this question. 2. The prevalent theory of neoliberalism is built upon the re-interpretation of state-market relations (i.e. the “hollowing out of the state” and the “rolling out of market”). This project has identified state-society interplay as the key to understanding the pattern and process of China’s participatory urban redevelopment. Does state-society interplay represent an alternative lens and analytical tool to study urban transformation not just in China but beyond China as well? Further studies are needed to address this theoretical concern. 3. This research has found the disturbing evidence showing the complete exclusion of the migrant population from the process of citizen participation in urban redevelopment. We have provided another case to illustrate the continuing battle of millions of migrant population in their contest for citizenship. For China to pursue sustainable urbanism, the current practice of participatory urban redevelopment will have to be critically re-evaluated and reformed along the line of equity, inclusiveness, justice, and social cohesion taking on board the interests of the migrant population as the indispensable stakeholders of China’s continuing urban transformation.

17614218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614218.value: This research investigates how and why participatory urban redevelopment has recently been practiced in Chinese cities and what social, economic and spatial effects this new practice has had focusing on the cases of Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen. Contrary to the conventional belief that citizen participation is usually alienated in a command economy such as China, many Chinese cities have since the 2010s practiced in various degree and manner the scheme of community participation in urban redevelopment. This new fashion has been introduced by local governments more as a tactic to expedite housing requisition and avoid social unrests than any genuine recognition of rights and entitlements. The nature and extent of citizen participation in urban redevelopment hinge upon the location of the projects, property rights involved, local culture and tradition, and degree of marketization and openness of the local economy. Citizen participation is found to be limited, rhetorical and symbolic for those projects involving the (land) property that is state-owned, remotely located, and heavily intervened by the local state in a top-down fashion, but it has turned out to be better organized and more genuinely carried out if the projects involved a central location, collectively owned property, sophisticated residents, and a local economy with a high degree of marketization and openness. In call cases, migrant population are invariably excluded from participatory decision-making even though they take a sizable share of affected residents.

17614318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614318.value: 改革持久授權書：比較法研究

17614318.label: Project Objectives
17614318.value: To thoroughly examine the legislation, subsidiary legislation, case law, and administrative infrastructure with regards to enduring powers of attorney in England, Ireland, Australia (Victoria and New South Wales), Hong Kong, and Singapore. To devise a model for enduring powers that aligns with best international practice and suits the cultural needs of Asian jurisdictions. To identify ways to align the supervision of attorneys with guardianship and trusteeship, and propose measures to cater for the informal family context of durable powers.
rows: To thoroughly examine the legislation, subsidiary legislation, case law, and administrative infrastructure with regards to enduring powers of attorney in England, Ireland, Australia (Victoria and New South Wales), Hong Kong, and Singapore.
To devise a model for enduring powers that aligns with best international practice and suits the cultural needs of Asian jurisdictions.
To identify ways to align the supervision of attorneys with guardianship and trusteeship, and propose measures to cater for the informal family context of durable powers.

17614318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614318.value: 我的首要研究目的是設計一個既符合最佳國際慣例，但同時適用於香港等亞洲司法管轄區的社會背景的持久授權書模式。持久授權書（也稱為永久/持續/耐久授權書）允許個人在他們仍然健康的時候任命他們自己選擇的人在他們喪失行為能力時開始管理他們的事務。 該項目特別及時，因為香港政府正在考慮改革其持久授權書法例。該法例在1997年根據在1985年已廢除的英國法例而制定。由於全球社會急速老化，並迫切需要改善與認知障礙者相關的規劃工具，我的研究結果將會在香港及國際層面上有著重大影響 。 我將會進行首個比較英格蘭，愛爾蘭，澳洲（維多利亞和新南威爾士），新加坡和香港的持久授權書的理論，實踐和挑戰的系統性研究。我將針對解決該範疇三個迫切的問題。第一，持久授權雖然為信託和監護提供了一種非正式和可負擔的替代方案，但諷刺地，這些特質同時也令持久授權書容易被濫用成財政剝削的工具。第二，實施適用於香港的“聯合國殘疾人權利公約”（CRPD）第12條所載的支持性決策原則需要龐大的資源，並需要受權人作出重大的承擔。第三，持久授權根據私法概念改編，通常供有資源在法院提起訴訟的商業單位所使用。然而，持久授權中弱勢的授權人在尋求公義時面臨的障礙使其權利顯得不切實際。此問題在注重家庭和諧的亞洲社會尤其嚴重。我的比較研究將更深入地探討受權人與監護人之間相同的作用和角色 。於此同時，為了滿足持久授權在不拘形式的家庭事宜當中，可能需要採取一些預防措施來指導受權人履行他們的職責，並且可能需要將製裁違法行為的權力交給非正式法庭或類似司法機構處理。 我將至少撰寫3篇期刊文章，以發放我的研究成果，以及把一些政策性的文章交給立法者和香港公眾以作參考 。

17614318.label: Realisation of objectives
17614318.value: All three objectives as per the original application have been completed in full. Please see below for details. Objective 1: I have conducted a thorough study of the legal rules (i.e. the statutes, subsidiary legislation, and relevant case law) and administrative infrastructure of durable powers of attorney in the jurisdictions selected. In addition, I went beyond the objective to consider government reports, law reform consultation papers, and academic commentary about durable powers in these jurisdictions. In particular, I have conducted a close, comparative analysis of the durable power regimes in Hong Kong and Singapore. Objective 2: Based on examples of international best practice and a close comparative study with Singapore, which is the most similar to Hong Kong in terms of legal tradition and cultural norms, I have made a number of law reform recommendations with respect to a model for durable powers that is suitable to Hong Kong. Specifically, I considered several crucial aspects of the durable power regime, such as the requisite capacity thresholds (in the context of similar significant lifetime decisions such as wills and large lifetime gifts in elder years), formality requirements, prevention of abuse, and administrative implementation. I have proposed a model for assessing the capacity of the donor in order to prevent the execution of durable powers as the result of abuse, undue influence and other forms of exploitation rather than the expression of the autonomous wishes of the donor (see item C.8.2). I have also proposed an appropriate level of formality requirements for durable powers that are more stringent than those in western jurisdictions, but suitable for Hong Kong in safeguarding donors from abuses (item C.8.1). Finally, I have argued that Singapore’s success shows that cultural taboos about incapacity can be overcome by a rigorous public awareness campaign and the adoption of administrative measures to promote the use of durable powers amongst the general population (item C.8.1). Objective 3 I have closely examined the current legal regime in Hong Kong for safeguarding donors from financial abuse through duress and undue influence. Taking into account current legislative measures adopted in Singapore for preventing such abuses as well as the cultural contexts and judicial practices in Hong Kong and Singapore, I have made observations on the ways to strike a balance between over-paternalistic judicial intervention and the prevention of abuse (see item C.8.3).

17614318.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614318.value: I have presented draft papers of the published outputs and parts of my research in London, Singapore, and Seoul, as well as in an online workshop (see items listed in C.9). I have also shared my recommendations with government officers in charge of the law reform process of the regime of enduring powers in Hong Kong. The study has shown that even though Hong Kong has started the process of reforming its regime of enduring powers of attorney, the reform process is very slow and lags behind the monumental advancements that have taken place in other jurisdictions. My research has also shown that despite being a latecomer to the durable power regime, Singapore has surpassed Hong Kong in enacting a modern regime in 2010, and has since then made numerous significant amendments to improve it (see items C.8.1 and C.8.3). It has also demonstrated that cultural taboos do not account for the low uptake of enduring powers in Hong Kong, and that with appropriate institutional measures in implementing the law and promoting durable powers, the general public is receptive to durable powers (item C.8.1). Based on these observations, I have made recommendations on key strategic areas of reform of the durable power regime in Hong Kong and published my proposals internationally and locally (see items listed in C.8) Item C.8.1: Lusina Ho, ‘Durable Powers of Attorney: A Tale of Two Cities’ (2021) 12 Journal of Comparative and International Aging Law & Policy 39 Item C.8.2: Lusina Ho, ‘An Asian Approach to Mental Capacity for Wills and Lasting Powers’ in Richard Nolan, Tang Hang Wu and Yip Man (eds), Trusts and Private Wealth Management: Developments and Directions (Cambridge: CUP, 2021)(forthcoming) Item C.8.3: Lusina Ho, ‘Assessing Capacity for Lifetime and Testamentary Dispositions’ (2021) 51 Hong Kong Law Journal (forthcoming)

17614318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614318.value: The project has demonstrated at least three important areas for further development. First, the development of measures to facilitate supported decision-making and the need to review substitute decision-making, of which durable powers are an example. Second, the importance of a coherent capacity law, which is currently lacking in Hong Kong. Third, the need to devise practical measures to support the implementation of durable power regimes. In order to pursue further work on these three important aspects, I have teamed up with colleagues in the field of medical law and submitted an application for an RGC Research Impact Fund. The proposed research will collaborate with the College of Psychiatry and has received policy support from the Advisory Committee on Mental Health established by the Hong Kong government. I am glad to report that the application has been shortlisted by the RGC, and hope I will be able to conduct an inter-disciplinary study of the law and bring practical impact to the community.

17614318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614318.value: The nature of the research: This project is a doctrinal and comparative research that examines the shortfalls of the current regime of enduring powers of attorney in Hong Kong, and offers recommendations on legal reform. The project conducts a close comparison of the durable power regimes in Hong Kong and Singapore to identify the reasons for the success of the latter system as opposed to that in Hong Kong. The significance and value of the research: With a rapidly ageing population and significantly higher instances of dementia amongst the elder population, Hong Kong faces an urgent and compelling challenge in improving its laws in facilitating people to plan for their incapacity. The current enduring power regime is out-of-date, because it was enacted in 1997 based on an English legislation that was enacted in 1985. It is commendable that the government has begun the process of reforming this regime. Accordingly, this project is very timely and significant in providing research findings and making law reform recommendations that assist the government in the law reform process. Another significance of the project lies in its being the first comprehensive comparative study of the durable power regimes in Singapore and Hong Kong, which have very similar cultures. The research has shown that cultural taboos about incapacity planning can be overcome by a rigorous promotion campaign. The long term value of the research lies in identifying the features of a durable power regime that suits Chinese culture and draws an appropriate balance between respecting the autonomy of the donors and protecting them from financial abuse through the use of durable power instruments.

17614618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614618.value: 整合流行文化：以「一塊」專輯和流行音樂中的再版選集為例

17614618.label: Project Objectives
17614618.value: - to carry out new research on the history of the Nuggets album and on the role of reissue anthology compilation albums in the cultural production of popular music. - to produce a scholarly monograph based on this research.
rows: - to carry out new research on the history of the Nuggets album and on the role of reissue anthology compilation albums in the cultural production of popular music.
- to produce a scholarly monograph based on this research.

17614618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614618.value: The reissue anthology compilation is a media form that has been largely overlooked in popular music studies despite the important role these albums have played in the circulation of Anglo-American popular music from the second half of the 20th century. This project explores the role of anthology compilation albums in the cultural production of rock music, focusing on the seminal anthology compilation, "Nuggets: Original Artyfacts from the First Psychedelic Era, 1965–1968." I argue that this album presents an invaluable lens into a larger story of popular music media, one that foregrounds the diffuse, complex mediations through which audio media circulates in the late 20th and early 21st centuries. This entails not just the album and its reception, but the original recordings and their (re-)circulation, the rise of “do-it-yourself” (DIY) reissue anthology compilations in the album’s aftermath, the growth in rock connoisseurship from the 1970s, and the changing media ecology of popular music from the 1960s through to the present. Drawing on archival work and ethnographic interviews with label owners, record collectors, and producers, this project explores the technical practice of producing anthology compilations, including the work of tracking down obscure recordings, acquiring their rights, compiling discographical information, and curating this material in album form. From questions that concern the production of these albums, I ask, what kinds of media entities are reissue anthology compilations, and how do they serve to mediate the past and present? Building on recent trends in the humanities and social sciences towards the material domains of sociocultural life, this research project presents a unique theoretical and methodological framework for approaching the study of albums in popular music scholarship. 儘管再版選集在二十世紀下半業英美流行音樂的傳播中發揮了重要作用，作為媒介的一種，這些專輯在流行音樂研究中卻鮮受重視。本研究聚焦《Nuggets: Original Artyfacts from the First Psychedelic Era, 1965–1968》這張意義重大的選集，由此探索再版選集在搖滾樂的文化生產中承擔的角色。該專輯為理解流行音樂媒介背後更廣闊的語境提供了珍貴視角，此語境中，二十世紀後期和二十一世紀初期聲音媒介的傳播與斡旋均被置於顯著位置。這要求研究者不僅關注專輯本身和人們對它的接納，同時也應看到原始錄音及其（再）傳播、基於原版專輯的DIY再版選集的興起、始於1970年代的搖滾樂鑒賞文化的盛行、以及從1960年代至今不停改變著的流行音樂媒介環境。藉助檔案研究和民族誌訪談——與唱片公司經營者、唱片收集者、音樂製作人，本研究將從技術層面探索再版選集的製作，包括追寻罕見錄音、獲取其版權、匯總音樂人的作品目錄，以及將這些材料整合為專輯。這些圍繞專輯製作的問題旨在回答再版選集究竟是何種媒介實體，又怎樣在過去與現在中斡旋？緊隨近年來人文與社會科學從物質領域探尋社會文化生活的趨勢，本研究為流行音樂學中的專輯研究帶來了一種獨特的理論和實踐框架。

17614618.label: Realisation of objectives
17614618.value: The objectives of the project have been partly completed. I have carried out the research that had planned to conduct (objective 1). For example, I had conducted ethnographic and archival research during the course of the project up until January of 2020. This entailed meeting with interlocutors and working through archives in Kentucky, Iowa, Portland, Massachusetts, as well as other places. I have completed over 60 hours of formal interviews with artists and musicians in USA. That doesn't include informal and non-structured interviews that have conducted over the course of my fieldwork. I have also documented important materials and media objects in archives and in people's personal collections during my research. The second part of the project (objective 2)--i.e. writing the monograph--is mostly completed, with the plan that the monograph will be completed by the end of 2022. In the interim, I have published an article out of the research conducted on this project. The article was published at the end of 2021 in the peer-reviewed popular music journal, Volume! (full citation: “‘Original Artyfacts’: Rethinking Object Biography in Popular Music Studies,” Volume! The French Journal of Popular Music Studies, 18 (2), 33-51 (2021)). I have also presented a research paper at an academic conference in 2021, at the KISMIF conference in Porto, Portugal (full citation: “The Social Lives of Reissues: Object Biography in Popular Music Studies,” KISMIF: DIY Cultures and Global Challenges, Porto, Portugal, 7-10 July 2021. ) There have been two big setbacks that have slowed down the completion of the project. Firstly, my position at the university has changed since the start of the project, from research faculty (assistant professor) to teaching staff (lecturer). The implication has been that I could not access most of the funds once I had switched to teaching staff (as per HKU policy), and so I have only spent a small portion of the funding for my research. Likewise, I have had less time and resources within the university to devote to the research, as my teaching duties have increased. (I took up the lectureship at HKU in the fall of 2019). Another key setback has been the fact that I am unable to travel for research on account of the COVID crisis. As my research mostly entails fieldwork and archival work, my plans have been seriously hampered due to the fact that I have not been able to travel to the United States since January 2020. While I have resorted to conducting ZOOM interviews and other online research, this has nonetheless slowed the progress of the project significantly. My current plan now is to submit a book proposal in the spring of 2022 to Bloomsbury publishing. I am planning to propose a monograph for their 33 1/3rd series. This series is specifically devoted to books on popular music albums, and I feel this is the best home for the project. In the end, I anticipate that the outcome of the project will have changed slightly: 1) monograph 2) an article (as noted above), and hopefully a second peer-reviewed article (currently in progress, planned for the Global Punk series by Intellect Books.)

17614618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614618.value: -- a monograph (in progress) -- an article (published in 2021, full citation: “‘Original Artyfacts’: Rethinking Object Biography in Popular Music Studies,” Volume! The French Journal of Popular Music Studies, 18 (2), 33-51 (2021)) -- a research conference paper (full citation: “The Social Lives of Reissues: Object Biography in Popular Music Studies,” KISMIF: DIY Cultures and Global Challenges, Porto, Portugal, 7-10 July 2021. ) A key finding of the research has been to show that the album is a unique media product that underwent a series of transformations over time, from a cult object to an iconic object, until it had been turned into a brand object in more recent years. This has important methodological implications in how we study popular culture, particularly in terms of emphasising the material aspects of the cultural objects we consume.

17614618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614618.value: As noted above, the research has led to an article (published in 2021). I anticipate one or two more articles that will emerge from the research, specifically, on the topic of how the album is entangled in the early history of particular genre of music called punk. Here, I plan to make the case that the album's history has implications for understanding processes of genre formation, specifically, I argue that the album is best understood as an adumbration of changes in the media ecology of popular music in North America in the 1970s and 1980s.

17614618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614618.value: This research has helped to uncover details about an important cultural object in the history of Anglo-American popular music, an influential compilation album called Nuggets: Original Artyfacts from the First Psychedelic Era, 1965-1968. Focusing on the material history of this album--the way it has circulated over time, as well as the particular media formats it has assumed--opens up new ways to understand popular music as a distinct cultural formation in contemporary life.

17615218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615218.value: At Hong Kong universities, the student experience has generally been assessed as satisfaction with course learning environments (Student Learning Theory; e.g., Entwistle & Ramsden, 1983). Parallel to this approach to assessing the student experience, student engagement (students’ participation in activities during university which enhance learning outcomes) became central to American university quality assurance. The use of the student engagement framework has steadily expanded globally, with the development of the Chinese College Student Survey (CCSS) during the past decade. This framework, while useful as a broad measure of university engagement, fails to capture lecture/tutorial/lab experiences. Capturing these experiences and assessing their impact on the development of students’ engagement with their domain of study is essential for the assessment of university engagement. The proposed research into student engagement in Hong Kong (HK) higher education is necessary for two key reasons. First, our understanding of the student experience must include student engagement as part of the broader university experience within HK higher education. Second, HK and Mainland China each have much to learn from a shared student experience framework. Further to these two practical needs, and following the development of a HK Survey of Student Engagement (HKSSE), we propose addressing two theoretical gaps in this field. First, this project will conduct inter-institutional adaptation/validation of students’ self-reported university engagement. This work will be supplemented and integrated with an examination of lecture/tutorial engagement. Second, empirical and then theoretical work towards the development of a framework integrating the best of Student Learning Theory and Student Engagement Theory will be undertaken. The proposed project will begin with the adaptation/validation of CCSS at HKU, expanding to three more HK universities (Baptist University, Chinese University and the Polytechnic University). Following intra-/inter-institutional validation of the inventory (HKSSE), studies at HK universities, focus group interviews to will be used to triangulate the new inventory’s results. The finalised inventory will then be tested at Mainland universities to begin to map the diversity of student university engagement with a group of Chinese Universities comparable in quality to Hong Kong universities (Tsinghua University acting as research hub). The proposed study (24 months) will be punctuated by two research-symposia generating discussions on student engagement in the HK and Mainland Chinese higher education community. Symposia will draw attention to the importance of student engagement at HK universities and establish an international network for the long-term development of student experience research across Greater China. 17615218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17615218.value: 1. Programme and university student experiences can be integrated and understood together as a pair of indicators of university quality assurance. 2. The paired measure of quality assurance integrated in the current study is useful across Hong Kong and Mainland Chinese universities. 3. Bringing these broader measures into alignment with course evaluations necessitates serious revisions to how higher education understands quality assurance and quality enhancement. Essentially, unlike programme and university student experience measures, course evaluations need to integrate meaningful and understandable feedback for students and teachers. 4. Most of the projects findings have been replicated beyond Greater China. Parallel research in Korea and Japan specifically suggest that an at least partially shared measure of quality assurance has the propensity to meaningfully benchmark student experiences across the region.

17615218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17615218.value: We are currently finalising a book of edited chapters with studies based on this project from universities across Pacific Asia (Phillipines, Macao, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Japan, Taiwan, Korea and Japan). This will be followed by a symposium with participating universities at HKU. As a followup to this project (the book and the symposium) we will be both expanding and narrowing the project in two directions. Expanding: Building on the international cooperation, we will be recruiting a larger sample of universities to participate in a 2024 benchmarking of student experience across Pacific Asia. Narrowing: We will also be initiating a Greaterbay project to focus on student experiences in universities in and near Hong Kong. We are continuing to work on bringing course evaluations closer to programme/university experiences but with institutional involvement, this is extremely difficult to move meaningfully forward.

17615218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17615218.value: Society needs to ensure that one of its chief drivers of economic prosperity (education broadly) and innovation (higher education specifically) continues to improve. Sustained improvements to individual institutions are only possible with robust information about how students are experiencing these environments. As the world continually grows together, additional opportunities for improvement to institutions are available by learning from one another. This is made much easier and effective if institutions share consistent information about these student experiences. While this is done nationally in some cases (e.g., UK, USA or Mainland China), there are largely unexplored opportunities for sharing and learning across national borders. The present project and parallel studies across Pacific Asia suggest that approach to university quality enhancement is possible and should be pursued.

17615618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615618.value: When people are objectified, they are denied of personhood and are treated merely as things or tools that can aid others’ goal achievement. A large body of research has examined the precedents, processes, and consequences of sexual objectification. The literature, however, lacks causal evidence on how people respond to non-sexual forms of objectification. The present investigation aims to contribute to the literature by testing how and when objectification impacts prosocial behavior. Building on theoretical and empirical research development, we propose two mechanisms for the effect of objectification on prosocial behavior. First, when people are objectified, they will engage in self-objectification, which decreases empathy and prosocial behavior. We propose self-affirmation as an effective way to counter the negative influence of objectification on self-objectification, thus reducing the negative effect of objectification on prosocial behavior. In addition, as objectification deprives people’s entitlement to autonomy, equality, and opportunities for growth and development, objectified individuals are likely to experience relative deprivation, which decreases empathy and prosocial behavior. The mediating effect of relative deprivation can be weakened by strong just-world beliefs. People with a strong just-world belief are motivated to view the world as a just place where people get what they deserve, and they tend to make internal attributions when facing negative experiences. Therefore, perceived relative deprivation as well as prosocial behavior of people with strong just-world beliefs, compared to those with weak just-world beliefs, will be less influenced by objectification. Further, we will directly compare how our two proposed mediators contribute to the negative effect of objectification on empathy and prosocial behaviors. Although we expect self-objectification and relative deprivation to function as two parallel mechanisms, different potential pathways of these variables will also be examined. A series of experimental and correlational studies will be conducted to provide systematic examinations of our hypotheses. Given that objectification is commonly experienced, a better understanding of the psychological consequences of objectification will not only help uncover the detrimental effects of objectification but will guide the development of intervention programs aiming to forge social bonds and to reduce the negative influence of objectification on individuals’ well-being. The present research can also benefit society, as it may inform efforts to promote a positive social environment and to provide guidance for facilitating social interactions among members in local and international communities, schools, and organizations. 當人們被物化時，他們被剝奪了人格，並被視為可以幫助他人實現目標的事物或工具。大量現有研究關注性別物化的誘因，過程和後果。然而，對於人們如何應對非性別物化，現有文獻中缺乏相應的因果證據。本研究填補文獻在方面的空白，關注物化是否以及如何影響親社會行為。 基於現有的理論和實證研究，我們提出了兩種物化影響親社會行為的機制。首先，當人們被物化時，他們會進行自我物化，因此降低同理心和親社會行為。我們進一步提出，自我確認能有效的對抗物化對自我物化的影響，從而減少物化對親社會行為的負面影響。此外，由於物化剝奪了人們享有自主權，平等權和增長與發展機會的權利，物化的個體可能會體驗到相對剝奪感，這也會減少同情和親社會行為。同時，公正世界信念可以影響相對剝奪的中介作用。具有強烈的公正世界信念的人在面對負面體驗時傾向於做出內部歸因。因此，與具有弱公正世界信念的人相比，具有強烈的公正世界信念的人所感知的相對剝奪以及親社會行為更少受到物化的影響。此外，我們將直接比較這兩種調解機制的相對作用。我們預測自我物化和相對剝奪是兩個平行的機制，但同時， 我們也將關注這些變量其他關聯的可能性。 我們將通過一系列實驗和相關研究對我們的假設進行系統的檢驗。鑑於物化體驗的常見性，更好地理解物化的心理後果，不僅有助於揭示物化的不利影響，還可用於指導干預方法的推進，減少物化對個人的負面影響。本研究也可以為促進積極的社會環境提供信息，並為促進當地和國際社區，學校和組織成員之間的社會互動提供指導。

17615618.label: Realisation of objectives
17615618.value: This project overlaps with some challenging times, including the 2019 social movement as well as the coronavirus pandemic. Nevertheless, the project objectives have been achieved. Objective 1: We tested whether objectification decreases empathy and prosociality. We have sufficient evidence supporting our prediction that objectification decreases empathy and prosocial intention, although the finding regarding prosocial behavior turned out to be more complicated (see 6.1 for more details). Objective 2: We tested and found that self-dehumanization, one key component of self-objectification, contributes to empathy and prosociality. Objective 3: We tested and found that people’s perceived relative deprivation contributes to empathy and prosociality following objectification. Objective 4: We tested and found self-objectification and perceived relative deprivation can function as two parallel mechanisms for the negative effect of objectification on empathy and prosociality, although self-objectification plays a more prominent role than relative deprivation. Objective 5: We tested and did not support the proposed moderating roles of just-world beliefs as well as self-affirmation (i.e., fortifying one’s core values).

17615618.label: Major findings and research outcome
17615618.value: Our major findings are below: We found, with converging evidence, that objectification contributes to prosociality. In assessing prosociality, we measured people’s behavioral intentions as well as actions. Although the main effect of objectification on prosocial behavior was not significant, our research suggests that objectification can still contribute to prosocial action through various psychological processes. Our research showed that relative deprivation is one process through which objectification contributes to prosocial behaviors. We suggest that there are alternative processes, which may work against the influence of relative deprivation in shaping prosocial behavior following objectification. Further, we found that objectification decreases people’s prosocial intention (i.e., intention to help others). And the effect of objectification on prosocial intention can be accounted for by both relative deprivation and self-dehumanization, although the later process (i.e., self-dehumanization) plays a more prominent role. Major research outcome: The project has led to a paper published at the Frontiers in Psychology and another manuscript that is currently under review (see Part C). In addition, findings of the project have been presented at international conferences, including the 2022 and 2023 SPSP annual meetings (see Part C). Finally, with the support of this project, one Mphil student (i.e., Chan Sze Yu) and one PhD student (Jiaxin Shi), finished their trainings and successfully graduated from The University of Hong Kong.

17615618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17615618.value: Our research suggests that objectification contributes to prosociality, including prosocial intentions and prosocial acts. More importantly, our research showed that the mechanism through which objectification impacts prosociality is complicated, involving psychological processes that work in opposite directions. Our research only focused on processes that limit prosociality following objectification. Future research should examine the processes through which objectification may boost prosociality. For instance, after being objectified, people might be more likely to help others when such acts could reduce their objectification concurrently or in the future. In addition, one major limitation in the literature of helping is the predominance of self-report measurements. Future research needs to develop paradigms that can be easily used in the laboratory settings, which allow the examination of causal effects. In addition, it is still unclear at this stage how to counter or reduce the negative effect of objectification on prosociality. Recent dissertational work by Dr. Jiaxin Shi, supervised by the PI of this project, showed that humility is effective in reducing objectification. Future research can test whether humility could also be effective in reducing the negative impacts of being objectified on prosociality and other psychological outcomes.

17615618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17615618.value: Objectification is a common experience. Employees can be treated as mere instruments to aid the financial success of their employers, students can be treated by their classmates as note-takers, and so on. When people are objectified, they are treated merely as things or tools that can aid others’ goal achievement, and their autonomy, needs, feelings, and opportunities are neglected. Aside from affecting intrapersonal processes, objectification can also impair people’s interpersonal relations by increasing external aggression. The present research aimed to further investigate the impact of objectification on interpersonal processes. In particular, we focused on whether and how objectification influences prosociality, which plays an important role in promoting positive interpersonal relations. Our research showed that objectification impacts prosociality through several distinct psychological processes. In particular, both people’s sense of relative deprivation and their self-dehumanization play important roles in shaping people’s prosociality after they are objectified. And self-dehumanization is more prominent than relative deprivation. This research is among the first to test how people interact with others after they are objectified. Findings and insights gained through this investigation could guide future research for a deeper and more comprehensive understanding regarding how objectification change our interpersonal interactions and relations.

17615818.value: 在奈良（710–794）與平安（794–1185）時代，佛教的新宗派與中國文學的新技巧都同時流傳到日本，產生了重大影響。雖然平安文化中最典型的文學作品（如《源氏物語》及《古今集》等）由日語白話文（即平假名）寫成，但是當時的官方公文及男性文人大多數的著作則由漢文與漢詩寫成。兩種文字的同時並存被一些現代學者看成「意義分岔」或「漢日對立」的狀態。實際上，平安時代文學中的矛盾或分岔並不嚴重，只是因為文學研究者的眼光限於俗文學和純文學的領域。如果我們追溯佛教思想與禮儀流傳到日本的過程，對平安時代的文學作品也會達到更完整的理解，並更完整地重構這些文本原來的歷史語境。而且，這種研究方法也可以幫我們重新了解漢文在平安時代文化的意義。漢文當然是儒家意識形態的重要載體，如同朝廷所編輯的幾本漢詩集；不過，同時也是佛教思想的各種嶄新概念的媒介物，如同律宗、密宗、天台宗、以及禪宗。因此漢文在平安時代日本的文化含意與當時佛教思想的新趨勢都不能分開。 本研究項目擬對這些長年被討論的難題以雙重方法（文學與宗教兩學科並用）進行新的考察。研究對象就是佛教（尤其是密教與天台宗）與純文學（主要指六朝及唐代詩文）在日本的接受史交叉點。以近年對平安文學與對中國古典文學的新研究為基礎，筆者會對中日文化交流的一些個案進行文學史和宗教史的雙重研究。研究的核心是日本的僧人、詩人、哲學家、及書法家空海（774–835）。對空海產生遠大影響的中國文獻有敦煌願文、昭明文選等。筆者會對這些文本進行詳細研究和新的翻譯，以便使國際學術界重新認識空海和他在世界文化史的崇高地位。空海研究則可幫我們對平安時代後期的文學作品也進行新的研究，以了解漢文著作和佛教思想在《源氏物語》等傑作的背後影響。

He has acknowledged the support of the UGC funding for both of these papers: 1. “Beyond Arbitrariness: Kūkai’s Theory of Languages and Scripts.” Journal of the Pacific Association for the Continental Tradition 4 (2021): 77–94. 2. “Kūkai’s Transcultural Rhetoric of Prayer: on his Writings Inspired by the Chinese “Prayer Rext” (yuanwen 願文).” Studies in Chinese Religions 8 (2022): 1–27. Dr Williams is also planning to produce a monograph building on this research and in the next 1-2 years. This is a long-term project and so the monograph has not been completed within the time frame for the initial research project, but he will acknowledge the UGC funding when it is complete.

17617118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617118.value: This research project explores the history of beauty and cosmetics in Chinese communities across Asia. It aims to transform how we understand the transregional and global contexts of modern Chinese history. During the twentieth-century, global markets and new technologies of photography and cinema facilitated the circulation of mass-produced beauty commodities and images. Beauty and its technologies became global: American film star Jean Harlow was admired across the world, and US-based Pond’s cold cream tailored its product and advertisements to local markets in India and China. But beauty and cosmetics were also trans-regional: Chinese women in Singapore viewed photographs of movie star Ruan Lingyu in Shanghai-published magazine Ling long, and Guangzhou cosmetic companies produced face powder for Chinese women in Hong Kong and Penang. How did the global and regional circulations of beauty products and images shape the gendered subjectivities and the Chinese identities of women living across the Sinophone, from Shanghai and Hong Kong to Taibei and Jakarta? Moreover, did this female visual and material culture of beauty shape an idea of Chineseness beyond the boundaries of the nation? During the twentieth-century, the reproduction and circulation of visual and material culture related to beauty expanded the geographic reach of shared beauty ideals, while also bringing people closer together. Technologies of photographic and cinematic reproduction, along with mass-produced branded commodities travelled along steam shipping, and later air, routes creating a time-space compression. Images and goods could travel widely, expanding space, but they also travelled more quickly allowing consumers to feel as though they were sharing the same time and space as people far away. Thus, did print culture and mass-produced cosmetics forge an “imagined community”? I hypothesize that the global and regional circulations of print culture and commodities related to beauty and cosmetics did not expand the boundaries of the Chinese nation, but instead forged a female Chinese trans-regional community as an alternative to the Chinese nation-state in which a woman living in British colonized Singapore shared Chinese beauty ideals with her counterpart in Japanese colonized Taibei even if they did not identify as citizens or members of the Chinese nation-state. Thus, through examining the history of how Chinese female identity was forged in and outside of mainland China during the twentieth-century, this project aims to contribute to understandings of Chinese identity-formation that continue to shape the Sinophone region today.

17617118.label: Realisation of objectives
17617118.value: This project could not be completed as planned due to the global pandemic, which began one year after beginning the project. Despite the disruption, I completed four of the five objectives and produced two outputs. For a year of this project, the University of Hong Kong would not allow faculty to travel for research. Afterwards, we were strongly discouraged from travelling. This is a multi-sited project that requires research in archives in Hong Kong, the ROC, the PRC, Japan, and Singapore. Singapore has only just opened up to international travellers this spring. The other locations of my archives are still closed. I do not know when they will open, and I am not sure if foreign researchers will be allowed into archives when they do. Thus, I do not know when restrictions will be lifted to allow me to complete this project. Since I could not travel, I focused my research on Hong Kong and wrote two articles that are currently under peer-review. I have been invited to revise and resubmit one article. The other article, I submitted in June 2021, and am waiting to hear back. These articles focus on gender and race in Hong Kong. I could not realise objective 1. Since I could not travel to archives in China, I was unable to re-examine Chinese women’s history as broadly as I had planned. Since I could only travel to archives and libraries in Taiwan before the pandemic, and in Hong Kong during, I am unable to write a monograph on the history of Sinophone cosmetics. Despite these restrictions and hardships, I wrote two articles about Hong Kong that realise objectives 2 to 5. The realisation of these objectives will inform future research directions as I pursue obtainable objectives in Hong Kong history. Because the pandemic has made future of archival research in other places in Asia so uncertain, I have no choice but to revise my objectives and outputs and close this grant. I appreciate the support and understanding of the Research Grants Council in this matter.

17617118.label: Major findings and research outcome
17617118.value: This research focuses on gender and race in Hong Kong through the lenses of beauty and popular culture. It explores how local and global structures of gender and race intersect and interconnect to forge concepts of Whiteness in Hong Kong, including both Western Whiteness and the Sino-Whiteness of the Han Chinese majority. I argue that Hong Kongers navigate global, regional, and local layers of racial structures through processes of erasing and racing thereby creating and perpetuating racialized hierarchies in Hong Kong. Looking at erasing and racing through Hong Kong as a case study demonstrates how majority groups in Asia are both victims and perpetrators of racialized discrimination.

17617118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17617118.value: Race in Hong Kong has been understudied, and the scholarship that does exist has largely been in in Law, Education and Sociology. A cultural studies approach to race in Hong Kong opens up new avenues to examining intersectional, racialized power structures in the city. Moreover, this research creates new pathways in Women’s Studies and Asian Studies for thinking about race in Asia. Finally, while this research breaks academic ground, it also can help improve understanding across ethnic groups in Hong Kong creating a social difference.

17617118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17617118.value: This research looks at beauty and popular culture to think about the ways in which gender and race intersect in Hong Kong. The cosmetics that people use, the novels they read, and the media they watch can reveal power and inequalities across the city. This cultural lens can help us understand how identities are forged in Hong Kong where Chinese people are the ethnic majority of a formerly Western colonized place. Looking at gender, race, and everyday life in Hong Kong, this research illuminates possibilities for progress.

17617218.label: Project Objectives
17617218.value: To offer a more comprehensive and systematic understanding of nativist writing in Taiwan, with a focus on the nativist works produced since the 1990s. To redress the common saturated optimism in which the relationship between the Han and aboriginal population is conceived. To challenge the current narrow definition of nativist writing by extending the scope to ocean-based writing. 17617218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17617218.value: This project examines Taiwan’s new nativist fiction produced since the 1990s. Nativist literature in Taiwan started as a trope for Taiwanese intellectuals’ class-sensitive nationalist consciousness in the 1930s. It became a manifestation of the writers’ political dissatisfaction with the KMT rule in the 1970s. After the lifting of martial law in 1987, it underwent a dynamic development. Adopting non-realist narrative techniques and combining with environmental awareness, as well as urban and ocean imaginings, the younger practitioners have expanded the scope of nativist fiction. The richness of those works, referred to as new nativist, however, has not yet been systematically explored. The significance of this project is threefold. First, it will add to Taiwan’s ongoing intellectual debate on indigeneity from a literature-focused perspective. Particularly, it will offer a vantage point through which Taiwan’s Han-aboriginal relations can be critically contemplated. Second, it will bring much needed stylistic and thematic study onto understudied and important creative works. Third, it has larger implications outside of Taiwan Studies, as its highly relevant case studies will add a new dimension to scholarship in the areas of eco-critical, ethnic ethics, and indigenous studies. The project will explore representative works by eight Taiwanese authors who have varied ethnic backgrounds. It will tackle the following interrelated questions: how are old nativist stories’ motifs (such as resisting Japanese imperialism, anti-Western cultural hegemony, and humanitarian concerns for the underdog in society) refashioned by the young writers’ freer place-based imagination? And, what are the literary modes employed? How can indigeneity be discussed without risking assimilation of ethnically minor groups into the Hoklo-centric Taiwanese cultural nativism? Can ocean or ecological literature offer a post-national way-out for the current discussion on nativist literature? I will first revisit the evolvement of nativist literature in Taiwan by problematizing the trend of antagonistic, exclusionist and ideologically charged practices within the nativist discourse and in valorising nativist literature. I will then investigate the new nativist fiction from four aspects—its use of history and memory, the image of wasted man and non-human, the politics of wandering and self-(alienation), and ocean as a site of nativist imagination. Finally, through close reading of my chosen works, I wish to demonstrate their diverse responses to Taiwan’s thorny identity politics and oft-politicised nativist debate. I will seek to attest that only by harbouring a more all-encompassing view on nativist writing can nativist imagination be meaningfully enacted and a Derrida-inspired inter-ethnic hospitality/friendship approximated. 本計劃檢視1990年代以來的台灣鄉土小說。台灣的鄉土文學最初在1930年代，被當作台灣具階級及國族意識的知識分子的託寓而被提出，之後於1970年代演變成對國民黨不滿的作家們的表述。1987年解嚴後，其發展又呈現新貌。年輕一輩作家們採用與環境意識結合的非寫實敘事技巧，或都會或海洋的想像，拓闊了鄉土小說的範疇。然而，這批所謂新鄉土小說作品，迄今仍未被有系統地探究。 本研究的重要性有三點。一、為台灣持續的關於本土性的討論挹注文學的視角，特別是提供一個批判性地思考原（住民）／漢（人）關係的向度。二、提供這批重要但少獲關注的作品，風格與主題上的深度分析。三、將台灣研究與更大的相關領域研究（例如環境批評、族群倫理、本土性研究）作鏈接。 本研究擬探討八位不同族群背景的當代台灣作家之作品，關注點包含：舊有的鄉土故事母題（如反日本帝國主義、反西方文化霸權、對社會上小人物的人道關懷）如何被新的作家重新演繹成更自由的，以地方為主的想像？又，他們採用何種文學敘述模式？本土性的討論如何能避免將少數族群收編進以福佬人為主的台灣文化本土主義？海洋或環保文學是否能提供現有的鄉土文學討論一個後國族的出路？ 研究首先將回顧台灣鄉土文學的演進，問題化鄉土文學論述以及評價當中的對立的、排外的、意識形態先行的狀況，然後從四個面向——其對歷史和記憶的運用、荒人與非人的形象、流浪與自我異化的政治、海洋想像來檢視所選取的新鄉土小說。透過文本細讀，本研究將展現這些新鄉土小說對台灣認同政治以及鄉土論述的多元回應，也將論證唯有對鄉土創作抱持開放態度，鄉土想像方能被有意義地啟動，而近似德希達所言的跨族群「悅納異己」概念方能達至。

17617218.label: Realisation of objectives
17617218.value: I have completed an eight-chapter book manuscript, which is currently under review by Columbia University Press. It provides a systematic and fairly comprehensive analysis on selected post-2000 well-regarded literary works from Taiwan through three critical lenses--the temporal lens, the geopolitical lens, and the ethical lens. All the works discussed were published in the past two decades, and some were published only about three or four years ago almost without existing scholarship to date. Hence, the first and fifth objectives have been realised. One of the chapters is on the indigenous ocean-centric Tao author Syaman Rapongan's recent works. In this chapter, the Han-aboriginal tension is addressed. It is also in this chapter that ocean as a borderless liminal imagination is scrutinised. The 2nd and 3rd objectives were met. As for the 4th objective, I not only problematise the Hoklo cultural nationalism, but the very essence of ethno-nationalism. My book is entitled "Post-national Articulations: Place-based Imagination in Taiwanese Literature since the Millennium" accordingly, which is what was proposed initially by this project.

17617218.label: Major findings and research outcome
17617218.value: The major findings, based on my aforementioned book manuscript, can be summarised in three points. 1) Regarding the "temporal" imagination, this project observes that authors all strive to offer multi-perspective representations of Taiwan's Japanese colonial past. More specifically, Wu Mingyi tends to “privatise” or “small-talk” (war) history. And rather than fabricating everything or being obsessed with documentary-like veracity, Gan Yaoming opts for the third way, which is a combination of both. As for Tong Weige, his writing presents an endless circuit of extracting specific fragments from the external world full of losses to construct a closed and highly personal inner universe, and this “microscopic” approach indicates the randomness of memory and urges us to redeem the remains of our life beyond politics. 2) Regarding the "geopolitical" imagination, this project demonstrates that Taiwan in fact has serves as a conducive site for non-local Sinophone authors, such as the late Li Yongping who was originally from the Borneo of Malaysia, and Lan Xiaolu who came to Taiwan because of marriage. It also argues that for Taiwanese authors, Taiwan may not necessarily feature in their works but even so, Taiwan still serves as a reference for cultural comparison. 3) Regarding the "ethical" imagination, this project posits that issues tackled by Taiwanese authors are far more universal than Taiwan-centric. In the case of Zhu Tianxin, her animal narratives can be considered an organic entity of her earlier works that deal with Mainlanders’ disappearing ethnic memory. And for the indigenous author Syaman Rapongan, it maintains that the ocean plays the most fundamental part of the Tao cultural identity as well as an effective image propelling us to reimagine Taiwan from a more fluid and open-minded “ocean-based” epistemology.

17617218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17617218.value: Taiwan's literary establishment since 2000 is still an emerging research field. With the proposed three specific tactics, more writers and literary texts can be included. For instance, under the ethical lens, literary representation of LGBQT can be included, in addition to the animal writing and eco-criticism covered by my case studies. I have published some shorter writing (e.g. book chapters and journal articles) on those authors and texts that are left out in my book manuscript. I would also like to highlight more about the "worldly" nature of Taiwanese literature. I have taken action on this by co-editing a book Taiwanese Literature as World Literature (forthcoming from Bloomsbury). A new co-edited book entitled "A Literary History of Taiwan in the New Millennium" is being planned and under contract with Cambria Press.

17617218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17617218.value: This project explores the placed-based imagination in post-2000 Taiwanese literature. By highlighting three important coordinates—the temporal, the geopolitical, and the ethical—deployed by writers since the millennium, this research explores selected authors’ rewriting of Japanese colonial memories, translocal envisioning (particularly Taiwan and the Southeast Asia), as well as animal narratives and ethnic reflections. Its significance lies in its innovative conceptualisation of Taiwanese literature not as a quasi-national one, but a place-based reference that allows Taiwanese authors to mull over relevant global issues faced by non-Taiwanese people as well enables non-local writers to sharpen their Taiwan-inspired style. This project has at least three specific values. First, it has an inclusive selection of cases, such as pays attention to multigenerational writers and even multi-genre texts. Second, it theorises three tactics for producing place-based literature. Third, this project expands the scope and definition of Taiwanese literature with its inclusion of migrant writers, and positions Taiwanese literature as world literature.

18300618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18300618.value: Marine plastic debris pollution has been identified by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) as an emerging global environmental issue. In particular, the problem of microplastics (MP), or plastic debris smaller than 5mm, has attracted increasing attention in the recent years. Because of its small size, a range of marine organisms have been observed to ingest MP particles, including commercial species intended for human consumption. Ingestion of MP can lead to physical harm, although ingestion of MPs is rarely lethal. Despite evidence documented in field studies which identified the Pearl River estuary as a hotspot for MP pollution, studies with regard to ingestion by marine organisms intended for human consumption are scarce. The proposed study will investigate the occurrence and the spatio-temporal pattern of MP ingestion by commercial fish in the Pearl River Estuary. Culture and wild fish samples of the species greasy grouper (Serranidae) will be collected from local fish rafts and fishermen respectively. MP recovered from gastrointestinal tracts of sample fish will be counted, classified and identified using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Ingestion of MP by fish is a potential food safety issue, and a matter of public concern. Data collected in the project will represent a first step to understanding potential impacts of MP on human health. 海洋塑膠污染是個被聯合國環境署確認的新興的全球性環境問題。尤其在近年來，微塑膠（粒徑少於5毫米的塑膠碎片）引起了越來越廣泛的關注。由於其體積小，學者已觀察到有一系列的海洋生物，包括供人食用的經濟物種，會誤食微塑膠顆粒。雖然海洋生物攝入微塑膠後罕有地會致命，此行為卻會對攝食者的身體造成傷害。近年有實地研究證明珠江口是微塑膠污染的熱點，但有關經濟性海洋生物誤食微塑膠的調查卻很少。是個項目將調查珠江口經濟性魚類誤食微塑膠的情況和時空分佈。研究將分別從本地魚排和漁民，收集養殖及野生的青斑（Serranidae）樣本，然後從樣本魚的胃腸道中提取微塑膠進行分類、量化、及以紅外光譜術鑑定。魚類誤食微塑膠是一個潛在的食品安全問題，亦是公眾所關注的事。此項目收集到的數據是了解微塑膠對人類健康影響的首步曲。

18300618.label: Realisation of objectives
18300618.value: Abundance and nature of microplastic (MP) in commercial fishes in the Pearl River Estuary had been assessed in collaboration with Prof Xu (Co-I). The assessment was carried out on both wild and cultured fishes. Wild fish samples were capture from outer Lingding Bay (an area south of Nei Lingding Island (內伶仃島) to Wanshan Archipelago (萬山群島), representing the outer part of Pearl River Estuary). A total of 337 fishes spanning across 26 species were collected. Cultured fishes were sampled from fish farms in eastern waters of Hong Kong (Sam Mun Tsai in Tolo Harbour and Sam Wan Tsai in Mirs Bay), and from two fish farms in Guishan Island (桂山島; 5 km southwest of Lantau Island) in Zhuhai. From each of the four farms, 60 samples of TGGG hybrid grouper (沙巴龍躉) were obtained from fish farms of Hong Kong and mainland respectively. This sampling design for cultured fishes allowed for a spatial comparison of MP abundance in fishes (Objective 3). MP were extracted from gastrointestinal tract, sorted, identified visually, and characterised instrumentally (Objective 1 & 2). Objective 1. MP were found in 42% of wild fish samples. Presence of MP varied from 15.5% to 80% among species. In terms of MP abundance, the average was 0.37 items per individual (n/ind). Likewise, abundance varied across species, ranging from 0.06 to 0.88 n/ind. There was also no significant difference observed from fishes of different living habitats and feeding habits. Results suggested that species should be controlled in investigation of MP in fishes. In cultured fishes, MP were present in all samples (100%), with a much higher average abundance of 26.6 n/ind, and a range of 4 to 147 n/ind. It should be noted that the latter is a table fish much larger in size (average weight of 2.4 kg, compared to <300g for wild samples). The relatively high abundance of MP in cultured fish should be originated from both the environment, fish feed and feeding operations of fish farms. Nonetheless, in the present study, we are unable to determine the exact sources. Objective 2. Regarding microplastic type, wild and cultured fish samples shared a similar composition of microplastic type, with fibre being the most dominant morphotype, followed by fragment and film. Pellet-shaped microplastics were only found in cultured fish. However, it should be noted that the proportion of fibres in wild fish (93.5%) was much higher than that in cultured fish (61.1%). The dominance of fibres suggests than the breakdown of fishing gears and the washing of synthetic cloths may be the major sources of microplastics in fishes. Regarding particle size, the size of microplastics detected in wild fish ranged from 0.18 to 4.90 mm in their longest dimension, while that in cultured fish ranged from 0.01 to 4.99 mm. The size distributions of microplastics were similar between wild and cultured fish, in which microplastic abundances decreased with increasing size. The majority of microplastics were in size smaller than 1 mm (wild fish: 34.8%; cultured fish: 73.6%). This indicates a serious threat to a wider range of marine organisms because their small size make them more readily ingested. Objective 3. A paired-site design was used to investigate the spatial variation in microplastic abundance in cultured fish sampled between western and eastern Hong Kong waters. The eastern Hong Kong waters was representative of conditions relatively unaffected by the Pearl River discharge, while Guishan Island is directly adjacent to the Pearl River outflow, which could reflect the input of microplastics through riverine discharge. The abundance of microplastics in cultured fish spatially varied across the PRE, with fish from Guishan Island (35.4 n/ind) being more heavily polluted than those from the eastern Hong Kong waters (17.9 n/ind). Such west-to-east pattern of decreasing microplastic abundance could imply that the Pearl River is a potential major source of plastic debris in the Pearl River Estuary, exerting influence on the uptake of microplastics by marine organisms, in particular during the wet season when the river discharge is the strongest.
