18611418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611418.value: The project examines the relationship between the local community and the asylum-seekers and refugees in post-colonial Hong Kong, in particular how the local community receives and interacts with this marginalized group, a currently understudied topic. With the backdrop of the negative news coverage in 2016 on the marginalized group and a polling that contradicts the media as over 60% of Hong Kong people are “neutral” towards the existence of the asylum-seekers and refugees, the reality in Hong Kong regarding this issue needs to be addressed. Drawing on relational ontology, I examine how the lives between the asylum-seekers and refugees and locals could relate to and affect each other’s lives throughout their life course. The crux of relation ontology is that everything is connected, dynamic and interactive. The framework shed light on the understanding of interplay among stakeholders, with relational ontology focuses on the lives as an ongoing process of the actors and how they influence each other, amidst social, structural and historical changes. A 1 ½ year ethnographic research in the ethnic cluster of rural Hong Kong and in-depth interviews and focus groups with 100 villagers who live with the asylum-seekers and refugees in the walled village and the 100 asylum-seekers who reside there., together with local human rights group, government officials and legislators will be conducted in this study. This research will provide invaluable insight on the practical policy and theoretical aspect of local’s interaction with the vulnerable group. On the practical level, understanding the lives of asylum-seekers and refugees and how local people interact with this group will advance the knowledge among the public to dispel misunderstandings about this marginalized group. On the theoretical level, adopting relational ontology in examining the locals and asylum-seekers opens a different level of application in a distinct spatial cluster. It allows the locals to be the core subject in the understanding of the refugees’ lives and they are linked together. The study also advances the knowledge on studying asylum-seekers and refugees in Hong Kong, a population as a result of the increasing connectedness due to globalization situated in a rural locale well-known for its exclusivity, a topic which is currently overlooked as studies on this group mostly focus on urban area. Being a female ethnographer studying male asylum-seekers from patriarchal communities could contribute to the understanding of positionality and power dynamics in ethnographic fieldwork. 本文旨在研究及審視香港本地社區與香港後殖民時代的尋求庇護者和難民之間的關係，尤其是本地社區與這邊緣化群體如何接收訊息與進行互動。有關學術主題目前缺乏探討。香港媒體在2016年期間以負面新聞報導針對邊緣化群體。在此氛圍下，民意調查的結果與媒體報導互相矛盾，調查顯示超過六成的香港受訪者對尋求庇護者和難民的存在表示「中立」。因此，香港必須面對並解決這個社會問題。 借鑒關係本體論，本文作者研究了尋求庇護者、難民與本地人之間的生活如何互相影響彼此的生命歷程。關係本體論的焦點在於一切都是聯繫的、不斷變化的和互動的。該框架闡明了對不同持份者之間相互作用的理解。此理論著重於以生活作為行動者的持續過程，從中了解它們如何在社會、結構和歷史的變化中相互影響。 為此，本文作者在香港農村地區進行為期1.5年的民族誌研究，對100名尋求庇護者、100名同居住在香港圍村內的村民、本地人權組織、政府官員與立法會議員等以深入訪談和焦點小組的方法進行相關研究。 本研究將為當地與弱勢群體互動的實際政策和理論方面提供寶貴、透徹的見解。在實際政策層面，從探詢當地人如何在生活中與尋求庇護者、難民這一弱勢群體的互動，有助於提升公眾對有關議題的認知及消除對邊緣化群體的誤解。在理論層面上，採用關係本體論的研究有助於在一個空間集群中以不同層面的應用去審視本地人和尋求庇護者的互動。它使本地人成為了解難民生活的核心議題，並將兩者聯繫在一起。 是次研究還推動了香港尋求庇護者和難民研究的知識。進一步的探究還推動發展香港尋求庇護者和難民研究的知識。受到全球化聯繫對人口帶來的影響，在越趨緊密的城市中，農村的排他性成為了其獨特之處。然而，這一研究主題目前被忽略。是故，作為一名女性民族誌學者，研究來自父權社區的男性尋求庇護者，有助於理解民族誌田野研究工作中的關係結構與權力變動。

18611418.label: Realisation of objectives
18611418.value: The project sets out to understand the relationship between the asylum-seeker and refugees (hereafter ASRs) in Hong Kong and the host country. The three objectives of this project are: from the legal and policy level to the day-to-day relational and livelihood levels of the ASRs with the host community, will help us understand how ASRs, as a by-product of a global humanitarian framework, survives under a local context, especially when it is in a transitory context. The project is also intended to understand migration, especially forced migration, as a complex and multilevel phenomenon. The project has succeeded in understanding how this complex phenomenon criss-crossing different levels and how this constitutes, as I would call it, an unhappy marriage, across micro- to macro level and criss-crossing each other. The project also helps advance understanding on the relational ontology between the host community and the refugees; how this relation results in [de]humanization; [dis]empowerment and social in/exclusion and how these relations could be changed when situated in different space and time. Apart from document and archival research, I had also conducted two-year ethnographic fieldwork in a walled village which has a sizable ASR population, during which I had also interviewed 37 ASRs; 33 walled villagers; three NGO workers, one legislator (there is only one who is really concerned and familiar with the refugee issue in Hong Kong). The project has achieved all the objectives: from the relational aspects between the villagers and the ASRs in the village (micro); to the local Hong Kong Chinese with the ASR (meso) and the government policy with the ASR (macro). Adopting relational ontology as the theoretical framework, I analysed the relational aspects through different space and time in each level and how each level that relations interact. The objectives direct me to look at both the macro and the micro aspects of the asylum-seekers and refugees: the inter-relations between the macro and the micro perspectives, and in each the relational aspect between the ASR. To achieve the objectives, the first four to five months of 2019 I went through the existing government documents (including LegCo minutes; media reports on the issue; as well as NGO submissions (objectives 1 and 2). I also went through literature which discusses about the group in Hong Kong and to revisit existing work on relational ontology relating to migration and forced migration and how refugees are resettled. While doing literature review, I was still committing myself to the volunteer work on the group. I had obtained consent from the Chairman of the NGO I co-founded on conducting participant observation while volunteering. My volunteer work included helping the ASRs apply Judicial Review, appealing their cases, taking them to see lawyers; mediating conflicts and liaising with Immigration Department as well as other government departments if necessary; the society also organized playgroup for the families. Both document research and volunteering activities facilitated my initial work to achieve 70% for both objectives 1 and 2 in my first year of my research. Based on the understanding I acquired from the literature, and the volunteer work I have been involving in (objectives 1 and 2), beginning in June 2019, I started arranging interviews with the villagers and the asylum-seekers living in the village (objectives 2 and 3). With the permission from the Chairman of the Pat Heung village committee and the village chiefs, I conducted fieldwork and observed the activities and interactions in the park, in the area outside the Pakistani shop. This took place around evening three times a day; and in events organized by the village council like National Day celebration with basin dish dinner (October 1, 2019) (objectives 2 and 3). Between September and October, because of the social movement in Hong Kong, the tension was also salient in the walled village where I conducted my fieldwork, when there was intergenerational conflict on how they view the social movement. This polarization also affected me and my relationship with the villagers at some point. I had to be careful when interviewing them. During that time, I still continued conducting my observation. I just needed to be more alert to the political sentiment. This also reflected the reason why I could only achieve 50% of objective 3 in the first year of my research period. On top of the political turmoil in Hong Kong, the pandemic happened since February 2020 had also disrupted my research. I had to be extremely careful in arranging interviews as the situation was unpredictable and precarious. With all the schools closed and human contact was reducing to minimal, face-to-face interviews would need to be arranged when the situation was slightly improved. Meanwhile, it gave me a window to experience and understand how the local community reacted to the ASRs over the pandemic period and how they interacted through NGOs (objective 2). While volunteering during the pandemic, I was also leading a team to conduct the third biennial survey funded by my department on gauging the local perception towards the ASRs. The survey showed that there was a staggering increase in positive and neutral public attitudes towards the ASR. Also, there was a dramatic increase in supporting refugee-friendly policy. By analysing the data, we discovered that the sudden surge in supporting ASRs and refugee-friendly policy had close relations with the time when the social movement took place. The results, together with my ongoing fieldwork and interviews provided invaluable information on achieving objective 2. As the pandemic situation continued, I had asked for six months extension to continue my interviews with the ASRs, the villagers and the NGO workers. My interviews with the ASRs currently living in the village saturated after I had interviewed 20 of them, then I started interviewing those who were living in the village and then moved out. These helped me to realize 100% objectives 2 and 3. Apart from being invited to attend a roundtable organized by OHCHR, I was also interviewed by ARIANA, an upscale English magazine featuring my research on refugees. That issue was guest edited by Zaid Ra’ad Al Hussein, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights in 2014. I have also presented in a seminar organized by SOKA university in Japan; and one in Chiang Mai University in Thailand. And one talk in my university. I have also given two talks to two different forms in a local secondary school regarding my research. Academically, I attended a conference organized by the International Political Science Association and the paper has received positive response. The panel organizer has included my paper in their planning of a Special issue. I have published one article on Journal of Asian Public Policy and submitted one article to Journal of Rural Studies to discuss about this unusual ethnic cluster in a village which is widely known for its exclusivity. I am now preparing two more articles; one article will be co-written with my research assistant and my two PhD students to explore the relational elements between the ASRs and the local population. The other one will be on children’s situation in Hong Kong. I have trained my first PhD student on how to conduct ethnography. He has completed his ethnography studying single mothers in Thailand.

18611418.label: Major findings and research outcome
18611418.value: My findings suggest strongly that inter-relations between ASRs and host community are circumscribed by the tension between the global humanitarian framework and the increasing securitization policy. I have used the concept of “politics of unhappy marriage” to describe the relationship between ASRs and the host community (i.e. Hong Kong). The concept denotes a constant struggle and tensions, and the power relations between the two. The tension explains how, from the government policy to day-to-day living, ASRs are facing in different aspects of marginalizations and discrimination. None of the ASRs, whether young or old, male or female, could escape this marginalization. They may experience different forms of such discriminations and marginalization. There is that idea of intersectional marginalizations where citizenship status, compounded with age, gender, could face different form of marginalization. And this criminalization policy constitutes to the social exclusion of the ASRs in Hong Kong. Walled village, while well-known for its exclusive nature, is surprisingly liberating to the ASRs. For those who have lived in the village before and those who are still living there, they found the familiarity with their home (South Asia and Africa) particularly attractive. Also the freedom to move around, bigger space and the possibility of informal business provides an ordinary life experience amidst their extraordinary life circumstances. The space, while local and exclusive in nature, provides a relatively inclusive environment for the group. The findings in the village also suggest that segregation is not particularly salient. Space and boundaries are also blurred in a matter of time. Walled villages and culture is a symbol of exclusivity where outsiders fear to tread. The asylum-seekers and refugees are joining their events such as national day celebration which used to be for Chinese only. Now, they have invited asylum-seekers to join their feast; compared with ten years ago when activities like these were no go zone to the ASRs. In fact, one interesting finding is that it is not the citizenship status that immediately mark the difference but the ethnicity and the race that spark off the feeling of difference. Our findings also suggest that NGO is an important mediator. While existing literature often reveals skepticism over humanitarianism organized by human rights organizations and NGOs and some studies also question NGO as a service provider to the group, our findings suggest that NGOs and churches are important to support their need and create social network for mutual support.

18611418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18611418.value: The findings, drawing on the concept of relational ontology, has facilitated the understanding of the intricate relationships between the host communities and the asylum-seekers and refugees. While in the context of global human rights framework, asylum-seekers and refugees are often being regarded as downtrodden, defenseless, marginalized and discriminated, it was through this research which I see that process of [de]humanization and [dis]empowerment is more complicated than it should be understood. From the micro aspect of the walled village to the macro aspect of the government, we notice the [un]willingness of villagers in working with the group, or in understanding the group when they discovered that it is not easy to ask them to leave. I am working on a book project which looks into that intricacies and this could answer the concern regarding the tension between global human rights and securitization policy. Findings about the asylum-seeking and children in Hong Kong in this project has also raised a number of questions regarding the relationship between international human rights framework and children rights. I am working on an RGC proposal comparing children rights policy between Hong Kong, U.S. and U.K towards asylum-seeking children.

18611418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18611418.value: In an indigenous village (aka walled village) situated at the rural part of Hong Kong, there lives a sizable population of asylum-seekers and refugees who have been residing there for over a decade or two. Once known for its exclusivity, the indigenous village has open up for rent and sale, and this in turn has become a refuge for the asylum-seekers and refugees. While their status has deprived them of a number of rights, they have found certain degree of freedom and possibility of activities in this part of Hong Kong. The analysis focused on the inter-actions and relational ontology between the asylum-seekers and the villages. I look at how these relations and interactions reflect the relations between the local community and the ASRs (meso level) to the government policy and the group (macro level). I examine how these relations results in the [de]humanization and [dis]empowerment of the group. Through exploring these relations, the findings have contributed substantially in the understanding of the relationship between the host communities and the asylum-seekers and refugees in the global migration context. The concept of “unhappy marriage” that I conclude from this study, could become a beginning of a learning process that promotes inclusiveness.

18612018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612018.value: 本研究項目旨在應對全球化時代高等教育國際化面臨的挑戰。在過去十年里，圍繞「高等教育國際化」的目標、措施等議題，研究者與決策者們主要從以下三個理論脈絡進行探討：新自由主義觀點著重研究各高校對國際學生市場的競爭；軟實力視角強調外來國際學生為本國帶來的國際聲譽；世界公民論述則關注國際學生從不同文化和社會中培養的各項能力及價值觀，尤其是這些素質如何讓國際學生更好地滿足全球化就業市場的需求。 以上研究成果對香港高等教育國際化發展的相關政策制定有著諸多啟示，但並不能夠解釋香港高等教育面臨的三個矛盾之處。首先，香港的高等教育普遍被認為是極具吸引力的，香港高校不僅擁有雄厚的師資，也擁有東西結合的學術優勢。然而，為何香港近年來迎接的國際學生人數卻不斷下降？在國際學生眼中，香港的大學真的那麼具有吸引力嗎？ 第二，香港特區政府旨在將香港打造成域內教育樞紐，對外提供高等教育服務，推動香港知識經濟發展。這一本應帶來高額利潤的產業卻始終以香港政府的財政支出作為支撐。如果香港高等教育產業採取市場化途徑發展，它能否為香港帶來如期的收益？和亞太地區其他廣泛接收國際學生的高等教育重鎮相比，香港的競爭力如何體現？ 第三，在香港政府的財政支持下，香港高校肩負著增強國際競爭力、加強與大陸交流的使命，為此香港高校推出了各種實習、遊學、交流活動，幫助香港學生拓展全球視野、深化對大陸的認識。然而，究竟學生們從各類跨境交流活動中學到了什麼，卻鮮為人討論。 本項目正欲填補上述研究盲點，通過考察學生們的交流學習經驗，對香港推動高等教育國際化的途徑作出反思。本研究捕捉了香港赴境外交換生和境外來港交換生對於香港高等教育的觀感，這一對比的視角不僅具有原創性，對於反思香港高等教育發展而言亦是正當其時。政策文件研究、問卷調查、學生訪談等多種研究形式都會被採用。 這一項目的研究結果對香港在全球高等教育體系的定位以及相關政策的制定具有重要意義。根據專家預測，目前全球高等教育的重心正逐步轉移至亞洲，未來15年里近七成高等教育生源皆來自該區域。這一背景下，學生的體認對於香港高等教育政策的制定極具啟發性，更能幫助香港把握未來的機遇。本項目的學術價值在於其研究途徑上的創新：它超越了傳統的市場理性分析路徑，從學生的視角出發，考察香港高等教育的吸引力、競爭力與全球視野這三項關鍵要素。本項目的成果對於美國、歐洲、澳大利亞同一領域的研究發展有著重要的參考價值。

18612018.label: Realisation of objectives
18612018.value: All of the five project objectives have been fully achieved. 1. To analyse policy rationale underlying HK universities’ outreach to international HEIs; This objective has been fully achieved through combined methodologies of historical review, sociological discursive analysis, and comparative policy studies. Historical review has helped to identify changing academic traditions embodied in higher education in the context of Hong Kong’s transition from a British colony to a Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Sociological discursive analysis was used to understand how the policies on internationalisation of higher education have been shaped by discourses for repositioning Hong Kong’s the political transition and the ongoing global/national/local dynamics. Comparative policy studies were conducted, to understand the international and national contexts of Hong Kong universities’ outreach to international higher education communities in the light of the UGC policy on ‘internationalisation and engagement with Mainland China’. The comparative lens has helped to identify and explain a national-local synergy in Hong Kong’s higher education coupling with the internationalisation of China’s higher education as a national strategy to rejuvenate the ‘civilisational state’ and to claim a global power status. 2. To identify students’ expectations on, and evaluation of, their international exchange experiences; This objective has been fully achieved through parallel surveys conducted to identify inbound exchange students’ experiences in Hong Kong to outbound Hong Kong students’ exchange experiences abroad. The major items in the two surveys are identical. The questionnaire include a demographics section with independent variables (gender, age, institutional affiliation, discipline area, birthplace, passport type, and length of stay in Hong Kong/abroad), and two sections posing three major questions. The questionnaire surveys were interrupted by university campus ban and global lockdown resulted from the 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests and global coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19). The period of data collection in Hong Kong universities was prolonged due to the drop in non-local applications and the suspension of exchange programmes with the international academics. I have explored diverse methods for data collection and sought help from my home institution - The Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK). From August 2019 to December 2020, with support from the Global Affairs Office, I have managed to collect adequate data for significant statistical analysis. The independent T-test was used to identify how inbound and outbound students differed in their perceived overseas exchange experience, including motivation to participate in overseas exchange, engagement within the host university, engagement in the host society, and planning for future relations with host destinations. 3. To investigate exchange students’ perceptions about the attractiveness of HK as a study abroad destination, competitive skills developed through educational exchange, and attributes associated with global citizenship; This objective has been fully achieved through the investigation into three research questions: [1] How do inbound students perceive the attractiveness of Hong Kong as a study destination? [2] How do international students perceive competitive skills developed through studying in Hong Kong? [3] How do international students perceive attributes associated with global citizenship? Combined methods of questionnaire surveys, semi-structured interviews, and participant observations were used to collect empirical data. I have followed proposal reviewers’ advice to include both exchange students and degree-seeking students in the surveys. Between 1st August 2019 and 8th March 2021, 1077 survey responses were collected, with 1031 (95.7%) completed responses from both online questionnaire (which used Google platform) and paper questionnaire. The respondents include both exchange students (63.3%) and degree-seeking students (36.7%). Among them, 54.3% are female, 45.2% are male, and 0.6% other gender identifications, showing the balance of gender representation in surveys. Participants include both undergraduate and postgraduate students aged between18 and 23-plus. The distribution of respondents’ host institution is relatively even. The survey respondents reported 79 countries of origin. SPSS software was used to analyse the data. Calculated order of mean scores of each item was corresponded with the combined percentages agreeing with the statements to denote respondents’ views. Independent-samples T-test compared how students’ responses differ by demographic factors and types of study (i.e., short-term exchange, degree-seeking). Content analysis was used to analyse interview data, delineate and cluster the units of meaning relevant to the research questions, and generate themes from the clusters for comparison with those from the questionnaire data. 4. To reflect on HK policies on HEI internationalisation by gathering and analysing factual data; This objective has been fully achieved through reflective analysis of empirical data, for understanding whether the officially-designated international exchange programmes resonate with the lived reality of what students have learned and developed. Factual data on inbound student mobility has revealed complexities that are both contradictory and complementary to the rationale-based policies, mainly in three aspects. First, the policies and strategies to internationalise higher education in Hong Kong have had positive policy outcomes in terms of rising Hong Kong universities’ international profile, still Hong Kong’s actual recruitment of non-local degree-seeking students is largely reliant upon intranational mobility. Second, to make internationalising universities in Hong Kong, institutional convergence is seen in the articulation of global outlook and domestic experiences in curricula and experiential learning. The values of these educational components were perceived differently by students’ demographic backgrounds and types of study in Hong Kong. Third, aligned with higher education policies, the Hong Kong government has made immigration policies in support of attracting talents from around the world; however, the policies were considered less important to non-local students’ determinants of studying and working in Hong Kong. Instead, their plan for future connections with Hong Kong was largely affected by their perceived value of international credentials obtained from Hong Kong universities and their cultural engagement/disengagement on and off university campus. 5. To revisit existing theoretical discourses on cross-border student mobility in the comparative contexts of HK and Asia-Pacific. This objective has been fully achieved through critical reflections on theoretical discourses of internationalization in higher education. The sociological perspective on higher education's shifting geopolitics is adopted to examine the role of geopolitical context in shaping planners' decisions to reposition higher education. This is integrated with the historical perspective examining the role of academic traditions associated with geopolitics, to identify changing academic models and political landscape. The case of Hong Kong provides a critique to rationales of neo-liberalism which are Western-centric and market-oriented. Theoretical revision has demonstrated that merely relying on neo-liberal logic cannot fully understand the meaning and utility of “internationalization” in the lexicon of higher education in the East Asian context where the universities’ international orientations are bound to the state’s directive and sponsorship. Publications based on the project findings have advanced theoretical discourses on cross-border student mobility in four aspects, by [1] identifying the limits of neo-liberalism for both theoretical advancement and practices in international higher education; [2] revealing the local-national synergy in the policies on internationalisation of higher education as soft power with ‘Chinese characteristics’; [3] exploring new determinants affecting Asian students’ decision to study within the same region in the aftermath of COVID-19, and the practical implications for East Asia (including Hong Kong) to act emerging regional hub in the intervening period; and [4] initiating the utility of a neo-statist analytical framework that is made of three conceptual dimensions – discourse, strategy, and regime – to shed light on broader social variables revealing the international landscape of higher education and student mobility in the aftermath of the global pandemic.

18612018.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612018.value: From a perspective of shifting geopolitics of higher education aligned with a historical perspective of evolving academic traditions, analysis have revealed important policy rationale underlying Hong Kong universities’ dual pathways towards the internationalization of higher education: one towards a more globalised neoliberal competition, the other towards the reconsolidation of statist nationalism (Ref: Part C 8 #1). Considering local transitions against macro-politics in the national context, a local-national synergy is seen, showing how changes to higher education in Hong Kong suited well into the pace and timing of the PRC’s strategical planning for regional leadership and global diffusion of higher education as soft power with ‘Chinese characteristics’ (Ref: Part C 8 #3, 5) and the theoretical utility of the term ‘neo-statism’ for understanding the globally-framed competitive strategies, national-oriented priorities, and local academic heritage embedded in higher education (Ref: Part C 8 #6). According to surveyed students, the top three most attractive reasons to study in Hong Kong are: gaining intercultural competency, learning from academic staff with internationally recognised qualifications, and host institution’s profile in the world university ranking. The three least important reasons are Hong Kong’s offer of financial support, immigration policy, and connection with Mainland China. Degree-seeking students rated the use of university facilities and class participation as the most engaging activities for improving academic capacities. They were more active in networking for employment in Hong Kong, but were less engaged in culture-related activities on and outside university campus. Exchange students showed higher level of cultural engagement both on and off university campus, but lower level of interest to seek employment in Hong Kong (Ref: Part C 8 #7). Students’ pre-mobility motivations, overseas engagement, and future plan after study-in-Hong Kong are statistically correlated. In particular, social integration outside of the university campuses has significant impact on exchange students’ development of sense of belonging towards the study destination. (Ref: Part C 11 #3). Studying internationalisation of higher education and student mobility from comparative lens, the Western state-supervising model and Asian statist sponsoring model are part and parcel of the globalised economy and international relations. Policies and strategies towards internationalisation and non-local student recruitments should consider such factors as travel distance and institutional support to international students, including financial support, mental care, and cultural engagement. These are becoming new determinants affecting families’ decision to invest in study abroad in the aftermath of COVID-19 (Ref: Part C 8 #2, 4).

18612018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612018.value: In the long run, the sustainability of the neo-liberalism will be tested by the geopolitical outcomes beyond COVID-19. The global pandemic has provoked a backlash against the fast-moving international higher education industry, showing the clash between economic neoliberalism and geopolitical realities. This creates a new policy challenge for considering the shifting geopolitical landscape, the resurgence of student flow, the international recruitment strategies, and the renewed significance of the state’s role in policymaking and financial undertaking, and the consequential impact on state-university relations. The future development of research is expected to further bridge the gap between higher education, international relations, and academic power studies. These interdisciplinary studies may help to open up a wider spectrum of research topics for understanding the university-state relationship, cross-border higher education, and international students’ cross-cultural experiences.

18612018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612018.value: This project seeks to reflect on the mentality, motivation, and measures that have shaped higher education institutions in Hong Kong towards “internationalisation”, which is increasingly outward-looking in international student recruitment, seeking to align Hong Kong’s educational capacity with the city’s geostrategic aspirations. It brings students’ experiences into a reflection of the policy outcomes. Mixed research methods were employed, including documentation study, questionnaire surveys, and semi-structured interviews. The results reveal complexities in non-local students’ learning experiences in Hong Kong, which are both contradictory and complementary to the rationale-based policies. Despite its rising international profile, Hong Kong’s actual recruitment of non-local students is largely reliant upon intranational mobility. Hong Kong as a study abroad destination is attractive to exchange and degree-seeking students for different reasons, which were related to their pre-mobility understanding of Hong Kong and the world. In contrast to the Hong Kong government’s immigration policies and universities’ financial support aiming to attract talents from around the world, students’ plan for future connections with Hong Kong was largely affected by their lived realities in Hong Kong, including the desire for international credential, sense of identity, and involvement in culture-related activities on and off university campus.

18612718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612718.value: With the prevalence of social pensions in the Asia-Pacific region, there is fierce debate on whether they have a positive or negative impact on older people and their family members. In 2017, one measure was implemented in each of two social pensions to improve their coverage for older adults. Then in 2018, a higher tier of assistance will be introduced in one social pension by providing a greater benefit but with a stricter asset limit. These reform measures provide a golden opportunity to examine the impact of social pensions by creating an exogenous change in the benefit level by taking advantage of an ongoing longitudinal study of older adults in Hong Kong. In this proposed study, we will examine the impact of recent changes in social pension programs on older adults and their household members in Hong Kong. Specifically, we aim to evaluate the impact of the newly introduced measures on social pensions on household income and expenditure, different measures of poverty (income-, expenditure- and asset-based poverty risk, material deprivation, social exclusion), intergenerational transfers from adult children, labor participation intensity, subjective well-being (i.e. life satisfaction and depressive symptoms) and health indicators in households with older adults. To achieve this objective, we will conduct the third and fourth wave survey of an ongoing longitudinal study of older adults in 2019 and 2021, respectively. These surveys follow on from the first and second wave surveys undertaken in 2015 and 2017. In addition to some basic socio-demographic and economic characteristics as the covariates for data analysis, we will collect data on household income, expenditure and asset, material deprivation, social exclusion, labor participation of household members, upstream intergenerational transfers, subjective well-being, and health indicators. We will use a triple-differences approach to systematically evaluate these effects by comparing the treatment and comparison groups for each reform measure using the four waves of data. The findings of the proposed study are expected to make a substantial contribution to policy debates in Hong Kong. These debates should eventually improve the living conditions of older adults in the territory by offering concrete policy recommendations to reform support for this vulnerable group of people. The research will also contribute to the theoretical literature by evaluating the impact of reform on different measures of poverty, subjective well-being and health indicators. Lastly, by examining the effect on intergenerational transfers, we will also evaluate theories or models underlying these transfers.

18612718.label: Realisation of objectives
18612718.value: We have achieved the objectives mentioned above: 1. To evaluate the impact of the newly introduced measures on social pension schemes on household income and the risk of income-based poverty, defined by the official poverty line, on the aged population in Hong Kong; 2. To evaluate the impact of the newly introduced measures on social pension schemes on household consumption among Hong Kong’s aged population, and to assess the risk of poverty using other indicators including consumption-based and asset-based poverty, material deprivation, and social exclusion; 3. To evaluate the effect of the newly introduced measures on social pension schemes on private inter-generational transfers from adult children and labor participation of older adults and their household members; and 4. To evaluate the impact of the newly introduced measures on social pension schemes on life satisfaction, depressive symptoms, and health indicators among Hong Kong’s older people. When we were collecting data in the fourth wave in 2021, pandemic was severe in Hong Kong and we encountered a lot of difficulties in contracting with our participants. However, we overcome all these challenges using a lot of measures like using phone survey.

18612718.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612718.value: This study utilized the introduction of a new higher tier of the Old Age Living Allowance (OALA) in Hong Kong in June 2018 as its experimental condition and examined the impact of the higher OALA on five poverty indicators among Hong Kong’s older adults. Supported by three waves of data, collected in 2015, 2017 and 2019 from a sample of Hong Kong’s older residents, we designed a quasi-experiment and estimated the triple differences in the five poverty indicators. The findings show that the higher OALA did not impact the institutionalized life course by reducing labour participation or financial transfers from adult children, and that it significantly reduced income-based poverty (see paper #3). The institutionalized life-course financial planning among poorer older people in Hong Kong determined that the higher OALA transferred into savings and reduced asset-based poverty but failed to affect expenditure-based poverty, material hardship or social exclusion (see paper #3). We also found that Hong Kong’s higher OALA significantly promoted engagement in cultural and entertainment activities, use of healthcare services, sleep quality, and life satisfaction but had no effect on self-rated health and loneliness (see paper #4). Lastly, we also found that an increased social pension significantly boosts older people’s expenditures on their grandchildren’s education, preventive healthcare, housing, and transportation; however, an increase does not significantly influence expenditures on family utilities, entertainment, and financial transfers to relatives (see paper #5). Another notable result was reduced expenditures on alcoholic drinks and cigarettes after a social pension expansion (see paper #5). In this study, poverty was assessed as being either income-poor, expenditure-poor, asset-poor, or as experiencing material deprivation. Social support was measured in terms of instrumental support, financial support, and informational support. When moderation and mediation were compared in the same model, only the role of moderation was identified as being significant. Instrumental support mitigated the effect of material deprivation on depression, while all three types of social support buffered the impact of expenditure-based poverty on depression (see paper #1). We also found that while material deprivation and asset-based poverty reduce life satisfaction, income-based poverty and expenditure-based poverty do not shape life satisfaction (see paper #2).

18612718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612718.value: The panel data is valuable for further investigation of older adults. One important topic is the impact of pandemic on older adults because the fourth wave of our data was collected in 2021. Moreover, we could also examine poverty dynamics using our panel data.

18612718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612718.value: With the prevalence of social pensions in the Asia-Pacific region, there is fierce debate on whether they have a positive or negative impact on older people and their family members. In 2018, a higher tier of assistance was introduced in one social pension by providing a greater benefit but with a stricter asset limit among Hong Kong older adults. These reform measures provide a golden opportunity to examine the impact of social pensions by creating an exogenous change in the benefit level by taking advantage of an ongoing longitudinal study of older adults in Hong Kong. In this study, we found that the newly introduced social pension substantially reduced income-based and asset-based poverty, but no impact was found on expenditure-based poverty, material deprivation and social exclusion. In other words, it seems that the social pension did not improve the standard of living among older adults who received it. On the other hand, it did promote older adults' engagement in cultural and entertainment activities, use of healthcare services and improved their sleep quality and life satisfaction. It seems that the new social pension enhance older adults' well-being and their participation is social activities.

18613118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613118.value: The importance of science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education has been gaining a lot of attention recently. There is a great deal of information introducing and promoting the design and implementation of STEM activities. However, during this initial stage of a new education initiative, most of the efforts are focused on mainstream students, without any attention paid to students with special educational needs (SEN), who are under-represented in the STEM education initiative. The rationale of “One Curriculum for All” put forward by the Hong Kong Curriculum Development Council in 2001 is that all children, whether they require special educational services or not, have basically the same needs and should not be distinguished from each other, and thus children with SEN should be exposed to similar learning experiences. Hence, these students should not be deprived of the opportunities to be engaged in STEM experiences. This study aims to research the under-explored area in STEM education of teacher professional development to support students with mild intellectual disabilities (ID). In the belief that individuals with disabilities should be evaluated and defined by their capacity, strengths, and broad range of interests and abilities, this proposal is grounded in research-based practices from both special and STEM education, with the main research question being: “How can teachers be well prepared for STEM education for students with ID?” Teachers will be supported in STEM education to promote students’ cognitive engagement by integrating arts, using an engineering design and inquiry-based approach to manage students’ cognitive load. Teachers working in two SEN schools will be invited to take part in this research to plan and implement STEM activities that are adapted from the mainstream schools. The model of collegial peer coaching will be used to involve other teachers in the same schools in order to improve teaching practices. Qualitative research methodology will be used for detailed analysis of teachers’ lesson planning, pedagogical concerns, and students’ cognitive engagement during lessons, as well as analysis of students’ learning outcomes and teachers’ reflection to identify good practices that help students accomplish STEM tasks. While challenging, with due consideration of the cognitive processes and functioning of teaching and learning, this study will provide useful pedagogical approaches, strategies, and resources in STEM education for teachers to meet the needs of students with ID and prepare them to be STEM-literate citizens. 最近, STEM教育（科學，技術，工程和數學教育）被廣泛關注。已有大量文獻介紹和推動STEM活動的設計和實施。然而，在STEM教育計畫的初始推行階段，大部分的工作都集中在主流學校的學生，沒有關注到特殊教育需要學生（SEN）。 “所有學童在同一課程下學習”的理念由香港課程發展局於2001年提出，這一理念指明所有的學童，無論他們需要特殊的教育服務與否，具有基本相同的需求和不應該被區別對待，從而讓有特殊教育需要的兒童應擁有類似的學習經歷。因此，不應剝奪這些學生參加STEM經歷的機會。 本計劃旨在研究STEM教育中探索不足的教師專業發展領域，以支持輕度智障（ID）學生。本著應該對殘障人士的能力，特長，以及廣泛的興趣和能力進行評估和定義的理念，以特殊教育和STEM教育的實踐出發進行研究，主要研究問題是：“教師如何能為ID學生提供STEM教育做好準備？” 教師將在STEM教育上得到支持，通過整合藝術，工程設計和探究式的方法，調控學生的認知負荷，從而促進學生認知參與。 兩所特殊教育學校工作的教師將受邀參與這項研究，以計畫和實施改編自主流學校的STEM活動。研究將基於同伴輔導模式，讓同一所學校的其他教師參與，以改善教學實踐。定性研究方法將用於詳細分析教師的教學準備，教學法的重點，學生在課堂上的認知參與度，以及學生的學習成果和教師反思分析，來確定幫助學生完成STEM任務的最佳做法。 雖具有挑戰性，這項研究基於對認知過程和教學運作的考量，將提供教師有用的教學方法，策略，和STEM教育的資源。同時亦有助於教師適應ID學生的需求 ，培養他們成為有STEM素養的公民。

18613118.label: Realisation of objectives
18613118.value: There was a teacher professional development (PD) progamme conducted with twenty teachers from different special schools who were interested in STEM education for students with intellectual disability (ID). Data were collected by open-ended questions around how STEM education can be transferred from the PD programme to special school teachers’ teaching, including (a) teachers’ perceptions of STEM education and whether they believe that there are advantages for ID students to engage in STEM, and (b) teachers’ readiness to adapt what was introduced in the PD progamme to future use for their students. Thematic analysis was used for data analysis, and the most frequently occurring items in objectives of STEM education for ID students, benefits of STEM education for ID students, how to support ID students with STEM learning, and STEM teaching design for ID students were identified. The strategies proposed to adapt the STEM activities for ID students were coded and summarized to examine predominant, consistent, and noticeable themes. Based on the data analysis, a paper entitled “Equipping Teachers in STEM Education for Intellectual Disability Students by Peer Coaching” was prepared for presentation in the ASTEM conference in December 2019, and a book chapter entitled “Teacher Professional Development for STEM Education: Adaptations for Students with Intellectual Disabilities” was submitted and accepted for publication in a book “Asia-Pacific STEM Teaching Practices”. Next, with the strong emphasis on the importance of peer coaching, STEM practices were carried out in two special schools with teachers attended the PD programme. The lesson planning and STEM activities were designed collaboratively by a group of teachers including experienced coordinator and novice teachers in the schools. Data was collected from participating teachers and students successfully. Pre- and post-lesson data were gathered by way of interviews on teachers’ pedagogical concerns during their planning of STEM education, teachers’ lesson plans, and lesson observation records (both field notes and video recording), and teachers’ reflection. Analysis of the data collected (e.g., interviews, lesson plan, reflections and lesson observation transcripts) was conducted using content analysis. The analysis of teacher data was useful for tracking teachers’ professional development to support students with ID in STEM learning. The analysis of student data reviewed the cognitive engagement and learning outcomes of students with ID during STEM learning, this also provides evidence of the effectiveness of the peer coaching in STEM activities design for improving ID students’ engagement. A paper related to the findings “Teachers’ Professional Development with Peer Coaching to Support Students with Intellectual Disabilities in STEM Learning” was prepared and published in Educational Technology & Society, 24 (4), 86–98. A paper “Engaging students with ID in STEM learning” was presented in the EASE East-Asian Association for Science Education 2021 conference, and a paper entitled “Engaging Students with Intellectual Disability in STEM Learning” was prepared and recently accepted by the Science Education International.

18613118.label: Major findings and research outcome
18613118.value: The book chapter about “Teacher Professional Development for STEM Education: Adaptations for Students with Intellectual Disabilities” reported the pedagogical concerns of twenty teachers from special schools in planning STEM activities for students with ID. Based on the findings focusing on teachers’ suggestions for adaptation, special school teachers should take into consideration two factors: First, the STEM learning activities designed should be closely related to science inquiry. Second, it is important for ID students to know more about contemporary technologies, and teachers' support with the provision of procedures of the essential/manageable steps is helpful for ID students to complete science inquiry and engineering design tasks. There are also summaries of strategies used by the special school teachers to meet the needs of students with ID in STEM education for adaptions as follows: (1) breaking down of tasks into smaller steps, (2) dividing tasks in accordance with students’ ability, (3) establishing background knowledge, (4) providing relevant tools and (5) attending to safety precautions. Peer coaching was recommended to the special school teachers in order to improve their planning of STEM learning and teaching practices for teachers’ professional development. General Studies teachers in two special schools for children with intellectual disabilities worked collaboratively with each other in their schools to plan and implement STEM learning. It was found that teachers were having pedagogical considerations during planning and implementing of STEM learning for their students with ID. Firstly, there is need to use technology for ID students in STEM learning, including the use of electronic devices and coding. Secondly, taking consideration of inquiry learning based on students’ ability with adapted strategies/steps to manage ID students’ cognitive load. And thirdly, with the support of peer coaching, teachers realized the importance of managing and balancing teachers’ disparity and school involvement when they worked collaboratively in planning and providing STEM learning for their ID students. In order to better engage students who have mild and moderate ID in the same class into STEM learning, teachers from a special school constructed a 4E model of Engaging, Exploring, Engineering, and Explaining, which emphasized inquiry and at the same time leveraged technology and engineering to integrate learning content into a purposeful and informed way to improve student engagement in lessons. Among the class of ten students involved in the research, five of them were regarded as having mild ID and the other five as having moderate ID. Lesson observations were conducted to study students’ cognitive, affective, and behavioral engagement in lessons. Results showed that ID students showed active and various degrees of cognitive engagement, positive affective engagement and reactive behavioral engagement during the four phases of Engaging, Exploring, Engineering, and Explaining of STEM learning design.

18613118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18613118.value: This research was focusing on teachers’ pedagogical concerns during planning and implementing of STEM learning for students with ID. Further research is therefore warrant to explore the ways through which teachers can be better supported to address their pedagogical concerns through more effective teacher professional development strategies. This research adopted mainly qualitative research methods with a limited sample size. In order to extend the research to other samples (for example, teachers and students of special schools at the secondary school level), it is therefore suggested that further research apply quantitative research methods to produce more generalized results by involving a large sample size of teachers or students. For instance, research can be conducted to explore the relationships between the types of teachers’ pedagogical strategies and the levels or types of students’ engagement in STEM learning, or to explore the moderating role of ID levels, to provide more insights into the effective STEM education specific to students of different ID levels.

18613318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613318.value: A growing body of literature has shown that the negative development outcome of child poverty results from the under-development of Executive Functioning (EF) in poor children, and interventions that involve physical activity, that are complex, novel and diverse, is most effective in enhancing EFs. Based on these lessons, this study seeks to investigate the effectiveness of a training programme of Cantonese opera as a culturally appropriate physical activity in enhancing EFs among Hong Kong Chinese children living in low-income families. This study will compare the effectiveness of Cantonese Opera training with the RULER Approach to Social and Emotional Learning (RULER) in classroom interactions on development of EF. We will also investigate the various mediating factors, including stress level, loneliness, quality of sleep and physical fitness, on the effectiveness of the interventions programmes. The proposed study is a 12-month cluster randomised, controlled intervention trial in which 290 primary school students aged 7 and 9 from low-income families will be recruited. They will be randomly assigned to one of the following four groups: 1) students learn and practise Cantonese opera only; 2) students’ classroom receives the RULER intervention only; 3) students learn Cantonese opera and their classroom receives the RULER interaction; and 4) students do not learn Cantonese opera and their classroom does not receive the RULER intervention. Both Cantonese opera and the RULER intervention will be implemented for one year. To assess the outcome of intervention, we will measure children’s EF using the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Batteries (CANTAB). Children’s academic attainment in Chinese, English, and Mathematics will be assessed by the LAMK. With respect to the mediating variables, we will measure children’s level of depression by the Beck Depression Inventory–II. The Chinese version of the UCLA Loneliness Scale will be used to assess children’s loneliness. Physical fitness will be measured by the Multistage 20-m Shuttle Run test. The EF, academic achievement and mediating variables will be measured three times, first during the baseline assessment before the intervention, the second immediately after the intervention, and the last one will be conducted one year after the intervention. Results from the study will inform policy makers on the effectiveness of Cantonese opera training and the RULER Approach to Social and Emotional Learning (RULER) in classroom interactions on reducing the negative impact of poverty on children’s EF. 越來越多的研究指出貧窮兒童的負面發展問題很多時是由於這些貧窮兒童的執行職能未能全面發展。研究亦發現一些多元及複雜的體育活動能夠有效提升兒童的執行職能。有見及此，是次研究希望探討粵劇訓練作為一種符合本土文化的體育活動對提升低收入家庭兒童的執行職能的成效。我們同時會比較粵劇訓練和在課堂採用RULER社交情感學習對學童執行職能的發展影響。本研究亦會探討其他因素包括兒童的壓力，孤獨程度，睡眠質量以及體能對執行職能的影響。 是次研究是一個為期12個月的隨機對照實驗，將會邀請290名小學七至九歲來自低收入家庭的小學生，並將他們隨機分派到以下四個組別：1) 接受粵劇訓練 2) 學童的課堂採用RULER社交情感學習 3) 接受粵劇訓練以及學童的課堂採用RULER社交情感學習 4) 沒有任何介入。粵劇訓練及RULER社交情感學習介入將會為期12個月。在研究的不同階段我們會評估參與學童的執行職能以及學童在中英數三方面的學習成績。同時我們亦會評估學童的壓力，孤獨程度，睡眠質量以及體能。研究的結果將有助政策制定者就粵劇訓練及在課堂採用社交情感訓練對減低貧窮對兒童的執行職能的影響。

21100818.label: Realisation of objectives
21100818.value: In this ECS project, we have tackled all 2 specific objectives and achieved 100% of both objectives 2 are completed. Specific Aim 1: To determine if CD36 can purify hPSC-CMs at the neonatal maturity stage 1. Generation of cardiomyocyte maturation systems: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) such as H9 and BJ1 cell lines were directed into the cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) lineage using small molecules (CHIR 99021 and WNT C-59). We then enriched the hPSC-CMs up to 95% by treatment with L-lactic acid. Finally, we promoted the maturation of hPSC-CMs in vitro by using two independent methods, all of which were previously reported. Briefly, we produced 3D fibrin-based cardiac tissues with day 15 (d15) hPSC-CMs and continuously cultured them until day 45 (d45). In addition, we generated an extended culture model by continuously culturing 15 hPSC-CMs up to day 100 (d100). 2. Enrichment of CD36 positive mature hPSC-CMs using CD36 antibody and their characterization: To enrich functionally mature hPSC-CMs, the hPSC-CMs dissociated from the cultured 3D cardiac tissues or the 100-day-cultured hPSC-CMs were treated with CD36 Ab, fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS)-sorted, and then subjected to various assays such as qRT-PCR, immunocytochemistry, and several functional/physiological examination including Ca2+ transient and patch clamp analysis. First, the flow cytometry analysis showed that the percentage of hPSC-CMs positive for CD36 Ab was 45.1%, and 99.5% of FACS-sorted CD36-positive hPSC-CMs exhibited TNNT2 expression in flow cytometry. Immunocytochemistry results further verified that virtually all CD36-Ab sorted hPSC-CMs stained positive for Tnnt2 and Actn2. In addition, qRT-PCR analyses demonstrated that these purified hPSC-CMs expressed at least 2 to 6-fold higher levels of genes involved in Calcium handling, CM structures, CM conduction, CM maturity, and metabolisms compared to the pre-sorted population indicating the enrichment of matured hPSC-CMs. Next, to check the functionality of FACS-sorted CD36-positive hPSC-CMs (CD36+ hPSC-CMs), we performed three analyses: i) Ca2+ transient, ii) patch clamp and iii) MEA analysis, all of which are well-known assay for evaluating the physiological function of the cardiomyocyte. As a result, in the Ca2+ transient analysis, all three types of CMs showed automaticity, but the patterns of calcium transients of CD36+ hPSC-CMs were similar to mature ventricular CMs but not atrial CMs; the frequency was slower, and the amplitude was larger in CD36+ hPSC-CMs indicating that these cells are likely to mature ventricular type CMs. In addition, we obtained stable recordings from forty-six purified CD36+ hPSC-CMs in the patch clamp analysis. Three major types of APs were observed: nodal-like, atrial-like, and ventricular-like APs. These results indicate that CD36 Ab-based purified CMs exhibit electrophysiologic characteristics of genuine mature ventricular CMs. We also performed additional experiments using multielectrode arrays (MEAs) to show the advantage of a homogeneous population of mature CMs to determine if the CD36+ hPSC-CMs displayed more synchronous electrophysiological properties. For MEA analyses, we FACS–sorted CD36+ positive and -negative hPSC-CMs and plated them on the fibronectin-coated MEA chambers. The results showed that while CD36- hPSC-CMs showed limited and non-synchronous electrical activities, CD36+ hPSC-CMs demonstrated regular and synchronous action potentials, suggesting a well-coupled syncytium of cells with appropriate CM electrophysiological characteristics. Lack of electrical activity measured in the CD36- hPSC-CMs may be due to a higher proportion of non-CM cell types in this population. Lastly, to test our central hypothesis that CD36+ hPSC-CMs will elicit better therapeutic potentials in the MI-induced hearts than immature CD36- hPSC-CMs, we performed in vivo preliminary experiments with the following experimental groups: 1) MI control, 2) Injecting 1 x 106 mature CD36+ hPSC-CMs, and 3) Injecting 1 x 106 immature CD36- hPSC-CMs at d15. Four rats per group were tested. For tracking purposes, hPSC-CMs were pre-labeled with a fluorescence dye, DiO showing a green fluorescence signal. As a result, the number of hPSC-CMs in the mature CD36+ hPSC-CMs injected hearts was substantially greater than that of the immature CD36- hPSC-CMs injected group. In addition, the results of immunohistochemistry with MYH6/7 antibody demonstrated that while the morphology of immature CD36- hPSC-CM injected heart tissues exhibited an irregular-globular shape, which is a typical immature CM phenotype, those grafted hPSC-CMs in the mature CD36+ hPSC-CMs injected heart tissues exhibited significantly larger in size and retained a rod-shaped structure resembling adult-like CMs. More importantly, concomitant staining with Gja1, a major gap junction protein, further showed that a substantial number of engrafted hPSC-CMs in mature CD36+ hPSC-CMs treated hearts formed gap junctions with the host CMs. Limited expression of Gja1 in immature CD36- hPSC-CMs injected heart tissues was detected. These results strongly suggest that injection with mature hPSC-CMs can markedly enhance cell retention and integration with the host myocardium in MI-induced hearts. Specific Aim 2: To develop methods of inducing large-scale hPSC-CM maturation While several promising approaches aiming to generate mature hPSC-CMs have been developed, none of the suggested techniques provide a solution for a large-scale generation of mature hPSC-CMs. Thus, developing new methods that can improve the maturity of immature hPSC-CMs on a large scale has been highly required. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound stimulation: The LIPU stimulation system is fabricated using 10 × 29 pMUT arrays for targeted ultrasonic cell stimulation. The fabricated pMUT array for cell stimulation is 2.27 × 6.84 mm, and the size of the AIO-LIPUSS is 13.4 × 17.3 × 2.5 cm, which is small enough to be placed in a cell incubator. Thus, the cells are prevented from exposure to the external environment, reducing the chances of cell contamination. The measured resonance frequency of a single pMUT element is 1.48 ± 0.13 MHz, and the measured acoustic intensity of the pMUT array is 0.15 ± 0.03 MPa at 1 mm away from the transducer. A pMUT array is mounted on a print circuit board (PCB), designed according to the size of a 12-well trans-well. The trans-well is placed on the PCB, and wire bonding is performed to connect the PCB and pMUT arrays electrically. After wiring, the PCB and pMUT arrays are coated with 2.6-μm thick parylene-C to ensure biocompatibility and waterproofing. To select the optimal combination of experimental parameters for inducing CM maturation, various conditions of ultrasound such as different amplitude (5Vpp Vs. 10 Vpp), frequency (680 KHz Vs. 1.5MHz), and stimulation cycle (30min × 3 times/day Vs. 30min × 6 times/day), which were selected based on the previously obtained results, were applied to cultured hPSC-CMs. After 7 days of ultrasound stimulation, the hPSC-CMs were harvested for qRT-PCR analyses. The results from qRT-PCR analyses demonstrated that the expression level of several genes involved in CM maturation, such as calcium (Ca2+) handling (RYR2, ATP2A2. CASQ2, and CACNA1C) and cardiac conduction (SCN5A, KCNJ2, and HCN4) in compared to untreated control hPSC-CMs. Particularly, the hPSC-CMs exposed to 10Vpp, 680 KHz, and the cycle for 30min × 6 times/day displayed higher expressions of CM maturation-related genes than other test groups. We also observed that the expression of CD36 and cardiac maturation markers such as MYH7 and TNNT2 were significantly elevated compared to the control groups. Based on these results, we developed a complete system that can efficiently enhance the maturity of hPSC-CMs by using LIPU via pMUT array. We demonstrated that the LIPU with pMUT array successfully increased the maturity of immature hPSC-CMs.

21100818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21100818.value: This study is timely and significant as it can provide new platforms to advance the use of hPSC-CMs for various future applications. First, a homogenous population of neonatal-stage hPSC-CMs will be more beneficial for cell-based cardiac therapy than embryonic/fetal-stage hPSC-CMs due to improved electric and mechanical properties. We anticipate that such hPSC-CMs would pose a less arrhythmic risk and have enhanced contractile performance. Second, a homogeneous population of neonatal-stage hPSC-CMs will be more useful in disease modeling since they can better reflect the native cardiac physiology. Finally, these purified neonatal-stage hPSC-CMs would better serve for testing the efficacy and toxicity of human cardiac drugs. The proposal is highly innovative as this is the first study aiming to identify surface proteins that mark neonatal-stage hPSC-CMs and to purify them via cell sorting.

21100818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21100818.value: The capacity of hPSC-CMs provides an unlimited resource for human CMs for various applications such as cell-based cardiac repair, cardiac drug toxicology screening, and human cardiac disease modeling. However, applicability is significantly limited by their immature phenotypes. Several new approaches to generate more mature hPSC-CM have been developed to overcome this critical issue. However, methodologies for maturing hPSC-CMs are rapidly improving; even these improved methods only result in heterogeneous populations of hPSC-CMs of varying maturities. Thus, developing a method that can selectively purify mature hPSC-CMs is necessary. In this ECS grand, we aimed to develop a novel system that can purify homogeneous populations of mature hPSC-CMs via the antibody targeting CD36 surface protein markers uniquely expressed in mature CMs. As a result, by using CD36 Ab, we successfully enriched the CD36-positive hPSC-CMs (CD36+ hPSC-CMs) from the hPSC-CM cultures generated by our in vitro CM maturation systems. After performing several assays examining CM identity and functional maturity, we found that these enriched CD36+ hPSC-CMs were more mature than control hPSC-CMs. Our results provide the first evidence for identifying the novel surface markers that distinguish mature CMs from a pool of immature CMs.

21101218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21101218.value: 贫血影响了世界上三分之一的人，造成了极大的经济损失。 深入理解红细胞扩增的机制有助于大量生产这种细胞。在红细胞发育的过程中， 促红素是必须的。在促红素的细胞传导途径中， 许多重要的分子，如Jak2, Stat5, PI3K, MARK, 和ERK，已被详细研究了， 但是另一个被促红素激活的激酶， SYK，还没有被研究。 为了研究SYK在红细胞发育中的作用， 我们构建了SYK全身敲除和红系特异性敲除的小鼠。 SYK敲除导致了胚胎和成年小鼠的贫血。 SYK的抑制剂导致红细胞前体的凋亡。 有意思的是， SYK的抑制造成Stat5的活性降低，和铁转运蛋白受体的降低。综上所述，我们的预数据显示了SYK对红细胞发育中的铁转运很重要。于是我们假设，在红细胞发育中， SYK对铁代谢很重要。 这里我们将研究SYK在正常和压力下的红细胞发育中的作用。 我们将研究（1）SYK在红细胞自主发育中的作用；（2）SYK是如何调控压力下的红细胞发育；（3）SYK是如何通过调节铁转运蛋白受体调节铁代谢。 我们的研究将为理解SYK在铁代谢中的作用提供坚实的基础，为未来大量生产红细胞做准备。

21103018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21103018.value: 丁香假單胞菌（Pseudomonas syringae）是全球農作物的主要病原菌之一，其致病性主要通過三型分泌系統（T3SS）的激活。雖然目前已經鑒定了一些調節T3SS的組份，但是細菌如何感應環境信號並作出相應的反應還知之甚少。我們在前期實驗中發現了第一套直接調控T3SS的雙組分系統RhpRS，並且初步分析了它的信號通路和調控機理。根據初步實驗結果推測： RhpRS和另外一套雙組分系統交聯作用共同調控T3SS，RhpR直接抑制多個T3SS基因的轉錄。本課題旨在進一步通過生化和遺傳學手段，研究假單胞菌中RhpRS系統分子作用機制和對細菌致病力的影響；通過轉錄組和蛋白組分析，探索RhpRS上下游調控關聯基因並解析T3SS信號轉導途徑。T3SS作為細菌重要的致病因子分泌系統，對其調控表達機制的研究可以為植物病原菌的防控提供新策略。

21103018.label: Realisation of objectives
21103018.value: Objective 1: To determine if RhpS senses ESA as a T3SS repressor. We proposed that ESA can help to prevent tomato from Pseudomonas prior to infection, which is of great potential of agricultural application in other crops and fruit trees. We found that three polyphenols (similar to ESA) specifically bind to the RhpS protein. Polyphenols are widely distributed secondary metabolites in plants and have been found to inhibit virulence-related phenotypes, including swarming, biofilm formation, and quorum sensing in many bacterial species. However, how polyphenols interfere with bacteria virulence and defend against pathogenic attack remains poorly understood. These polyphenols (TA, PGG, and EGCG) were found to increase the expression level of rhpR-lux in a dose-dependent manner, but suppress the transcription of T3SS genes. To explore if these polyphenols also regulate rhpR-lux via RhpS, increasing doses of polyphenols were applied to the Psph ΔrhpS strain. Results supported that these plant-derived polyphenols suppress the induction of T3SS genes in an RhpS-dependent manner. To determine whether the polyphenols affected the enzymatic activity of RhpS, we purified an inverted membrane vesicle containing a full-length RhpS protein (RhpS-FL). Phosphorylation assays revealed that polyphenols suppress both the kinase and phosphatase activity of RhpS in vitro. Objective 2: To examine the crosstalk between RhpRS and EnvZ. We have proved that EnvZ is a repressor of the T3SS by rhpS in P. syringae. Among 62 alternative kinases of RhpR, three EnvZ homologs, such as PSPPH_3550c (aa 152-425), PSPPH_3736c (aa 274-537), and PSPPH_5115c (aa 63-441), were found to show kinase activity rather than phosphatase activity on RhpR, switching off bacterial virulence via phosphorylation-related crosstalk. Deletion of these genes recovered the expression level of rhpR in the rhpS mutant. Objective 3: To study the mechanism of RhpRS-mediated regulation on hrpR and PSPPH_1805^6 (GrlP). We have suggested that the phosphorylation of RhpR promoted its binding affinity to the IR element in the hrpR promoter, thus inhibiting the transcription of hrpRS. IR is also found in the promoter of a gene coding glycine rich lipoprotein (named as GrlP). Here we reported that GrlP is located to the periplasmic side of OM, and negatively regulates the T3SS gene expression, bacterial pathogenicity, swimming motility, biofilm formation, as well as various stress resistance. GrlP increased the size of periplasmic space probably by interacting with OprI, the ortholog of lipoprotein Lpp in E. coli controlling periplasmic space and mechanical properties of OM.

21103018.label: Major findings and research outcome
21103018.value: Bacteria use a variety of mechanisms, such as two-component regulatory systems (TCSs), to rapidly sense and respond to distinct conditions and signals in their host organisms. The type III secretion system (T3SS) is a key determinant of the virulence of the model plant pathogen P. syringae and contains the TCS RhpRS as a key regulator. However, the plant-derived compound targeting RhpRS remains unknown. Here, we identify three natural polyphenols that induce the expression of the rhpRS operon in an RhpS-dependent manner. In addition, three non-cognate histidine kinases cooperatively phosphorylate RhpR and antagonize the rhpS mutant phenotype. The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria is the most front line in contact with extracellular milieu. However, whether the OM composition and mechanical properties are coordinated with the expression of the T3SS genes is unknown. Here we found that phosphorylated RhpR directly activates the expression of the OM lipoprotein gene grlP bearing a function in regulating the periplasmic space. This finding suggests a coordination between the OM properties and the T3SS gene regulation, and reveals a new target for control of the T3SS gene expression and bacterial pathogenicity.

21103018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21103018.value: To further understand the mechanism whereby these polyphenols inhibit T3SS gene expression in P. syringae, we will perform a transcriptome analysis of P. syringae in the presence and absence of them MM. According to the analysis data, we will identify the differentially expressed genes regulated by them, respectively. To test whether these polyphenols can reduce bacterial pathogenicity on host plants, P. syringae bacterial culture with all three polyphenols will be syringe-infiltrated into the primary leaves of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) plants. We predict that polyphenol can be an ideal inhibitor for P. syringae virulence, which will be tested in field study in the future. To detect whether a direct polyphenol-RhpS interaction occurred, a microscale thermophoresis assay will be used to detect if RhpS directly binds polyphenols via its specific domain. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis will be used to identify the amino acids essential for polyphenol recognition. We plan to study the molecular mechanism of the interaction between three HKs and RhpR. We also plan to identify and characterize the targets of GrlP in both bacteria and plants. Based on all the results, we will construct a polyphenol-RhpRS-PSPPH_3550/3736/5115-T3SS-GrlP pathway.

21103018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21103018.value: Pathogens use host-generated signals to gauge appropriate behavior and infection timing after invasion. However, very few natural signals of phytopathogens are currently known. In plants, a plethora of compounds defend against attack by pathogens and animals. Polyphenols have been recognized as one of the most abundant groups of plant secondary metabolites and have marked antimicrobial activities. They can inhibit multiple virulence-related pathways of pathogenic bacteria. As a master T3SS regulator, TCS RhpRS plays a crucial role in promoting the virulence of P. syringae. In this study, we demonstrated the effect of polyphenols on the T3SS and virulence of the plant pathogenic bacterium P. syringae. RhpS senses polyphenols and inhibit bacterial virulence. We also revealed the regulation of GrlP on the virulence of P. syringae. Our research not only provided new insights of signal perception of RhpS to the external environment, but also showed the role of bacterial OM in P. syringae virulence.
