21103818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21103818.value: Sensory learning in the brain involves identifying the stimulus and associating it with a positive or negative value. It is generally believed that sensing and learning occur in separate brain areas: stable representation of sensory stimuli occurs in sensory cortices, while plastic learning occurs in a downstream region. Recent studies challenge this view by showing that odor features such as odor identity, concentration, and value are multiplexedly represented in the same brain region: the primary olfactory cortex. How are neurons and circuits wired up to mediate extraction of distinct odor features in the same brain region? In layer 2 of the anterior piriform cortex (APC), one of the largest regions of olfactory cortex, our group and others have recently identified two main principal neurons that differ in input as well as output connectivity patterns: semilunar (SL) and superficial pyramidal (SP) cells. It has been shown that SL cells are better activated by direct sensory inputs while SP cells are preferentially activated by associative inputs, hence SL and SP cells are parallel output channels that extract and represent different odor features. However, the neural mechanisms that gate the activation of SL vs. SP cells are unclear. Our preliminary data suggest that GABAergic interneurons differentially regulate SL vs. SP cells. Here, we propose that the plasticity and wiring of GABAergic interneurons providing inhibition to SL vs. SP cells are a key mechanism mediating this gating. This proposal is undertaken to examine the hypothesis that activity-dependent recruitment of inhibitory circuits differentially control SL vs. SP cell function, thereby dynamically regulating the output mode of APC. To probe the contribution of inhibitory synapses to SL vs. SP activity, I will use a combination of slice electrophysiology, optogenetics, sensory activity manipulation, mouse genetics, and immunofluorescent staining. Objective 1 will physiologically determine how excitatory and inhibitory circuits are differentially wired up for SL vs. SP cells. Objective 2 will examine how sensory experience modifies excitatory and inhibitory synapses of SL vs. SP cells. Objective 3 will examine whether parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory interneurons mediate the recurrent inhibition received by SL vs. SP cells. The synaptic and circuit mechanisms uncovered in this proposal will elucidate on how cortical circuits can selectively represent distinct sensory features and provide a framework for understanding how top-down projections or neuromodulators can influence these processes. 大腦中的認知學習涉及識別刺激並將其聯繫到正或負價值。一般認為，識別和學習發生在不同的大腦區域：感覺刺激的表現發生在感覺皮層中，而關聯學習的可塑性側發生在下游區域。最近的研究反對這觀點：不同的氣味特徵，如氣味特性，濃度和價值，可以在同一主要嗅覺皮層中多重表示。同一個大腦區域內的神經元迴路是如何連接起來代表不同氣味特徵？在前部梨狀皮質（APC）的第2層，嗅覺皮層的最大區域之一，我們和其他的小組最近確定了兩個主要的神經元，它們在輸入和輸出連接模式上不同：半月和淺表金字塔（淺金）細胞。由於嗅覺球體輸入可激活半月細胞，而關聯輸入可激活淺金細胞，這兩種神經元類型是提取不同氣味特徵的平行輸出通道。然而，控制這兩種神經元類型激活的機制尚不清楚。基於我們的初步數據，我們提出抑制性中間神經元的可塑性和連接性對半月與淺金神經元的抑制作用是介導這種門控的關鍵機制。目標1將用切片電生理學確定興奮性和抑制性迴路如何差異地連接這兩種神經元。目標2將用感覺活動操作，小鼠遺傳學和免疫熒光染色檢驗感覺經驗如何改變這兩種神經元類型的興奮性和抑制性突觸。目標3將用光遺傳學檢查不同樣的抑制神經元亞型是否介導這兩種神經元所接受的複發抑制。

21103818.label: Realisation of objectives
21103818.value: The sense of olfaction is critical to animal’s survival due to its role in predator avoidance, prey capture, and mating activities. The anterior piriform cortex (APC) is the largest cortical area devoted to olfaction and is important for olfactory perception and learning. The presence of recurrent excitatory connections and robust long-term synaptic plasticity are the main features that enable the APC to achieve those functions. The main output of the APC are the layer 2 (L2) principal neurons, which can be further subdivided into the semilunar (SL) and superficial pyramidal (SP) cells due to their distinct molecular marker expression, passive membrane properties, and excitatory inputs. Due to these major differences, SL and SP cells are thought to be separate, parallel output channels of the APC. While the excitatory inputs on SL and SP cells are well studied, how well-connected and plastic their inhibitory inputs are is much less clear. Here we hypothesize that activity-dependent recruitment of inhibitory circuits differentially controls SL and SP cell function, thereby dynamically regulating the feature extraction mode of APC. We have achieved 100% of all 3 Objectives. In Objective 1, we determined the inhibitory transmission tone in SL vs SP cells. We performed whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology on SL and SP cells in the same acute APC slice and measured the spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents (sIPSCs). We found that the amplitude of sIPSCs were comparable, but the frequency was significantly higher in the SL compared to SP cells. Next, we investigated the excitation-inhibition (E-I) ratio of recurrent connections in SL and SP cells. Recurrent connections are important in context-dependent learning and memory, which is a key feature of the APC. We expressed the red-shifted channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2), Chrimson, in neurons in APC using an AAV and examined the local synaptic connections away from the injection site. Whole-field illumination (560 nm, 1 ms pulse width) of APC triggered recurrent EPSCs and IPSCs in principal neurons. While both SL and SP cells received strong evoked IPSCs of similar amplitudes, SP cells receive much stronger EPSCs than SL cells. These experiments showed that the excitatory and inhibitory circuits are wired up differently in SL and SP cells. In Objective 2, we examined how sensory experience modulates the excitatory and inhibitory synapses in APC. Ongoing learning and sensory experience regulate the strength of excitatory and inhibitory synapses anatomically and physiologically. In this Objective, we used unilateral naris occlusion (NO) to test the impact of sensory deprivation on synapses in APC. SL cells are mainly situated in superficial L2a while SP cells are mainly in deeper L2b. One of the main markers of inhibitory synapses is GAD67. We quantified the output parts of GABAergic synapses (axonal boutons). We found that NO significantly reduced the density of GAD67 synapses in L2b but not L2a, suggesting SP but not SL cells are differentially regulated. Several different interneuron subtypes exist in the APC, like the neocortex and hippocampus. The parvalbumin (PV)- and somatostatin (SOM)-expressing interneurons are the major subtypes. We quantified the PV output synapses are mainly found in the perisomatic region of SL (L2a) and SP (L2b) cells. NO significantly decreased the density of PV+ synapses in both L2a and L2b, suggesting that sensory experience modulates PV inhibition equally in SL and SP cells. Moreover, NO increased the density of excitatory synapses marked by VGluT1. These results indicate that sensory experience differentially modulates excitatory and inhibitory synapses in APC. In Objective 3, we examined the functional output of PV and SOM interneurons to SL vs SP cells. We expressed the fast Ch2, CheTA, in PV or SOM neurons using the PV-Cre or SOM-Cre transgenic mouse, respectively. We found that PV output is significantly stronger than SOM output. To address whether interneuron circuits in different layers (L1 vs L3) are wired up differently, we performed patterned illumination and activation of CheTA in L1 or L3 and mapped the PV to SL, PV to SP, SOM to SL and SOM to SP circuits. Our experiments revealed an unexpected connection motif: that PV output strength is oppositely wired up in L1 vs L3 for SL vs SP cells. These results showed that PV and SOM interneurons mediate the recurrent inhibition differently in SP vs. SP cells. Overall, our results indicate that sensory deprivation can induce target-specific modulation of inhibitory synapses structurally and functionally.

21103818.label: Major findings and research outcome
21103818.value: We found that SL and SP cells of the APC are differentially wired up for inhibition as they receive sIPSC of different strength. Moreover, patterned optogenetic activation of inhibition from different layers revealed that inhibition in SL cells is L1 > L3 while inhibition for SP cells is L3> L1. This connection motif is mirrored by the PV neuronal output, which is L1 > L3 for SL cells and L3 > L1 for SP cells. Activity deprivation using naris occlusion showed that inhibition in L3 for SP cells is selectively upregulated. This is mirrored by the specific upregulation in PV to SP cell circuit. Taken together, our findings reveal a working model where target- and layer-specific connectivity in APC differentially regulates SL vs SP cells, modulating their output as parallel channels. The major findings from this proposal have been presented at several different international conferences and published in a well-respected international journal, the FASEB Journal (Jiang et al., 2021).

21103818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21103818.value: In this project, we examined the anatomical and physiological mechanisms by which sensory experience differentially modulates the SL vs SP cells. In particular, there was a PV neuron-specific regulation that resulted in the plasticity of the PV to SP cell microcircuit. However, what is the molecular mechanism that governed this plasticity in (1) the principal neurons and (2) the interneuron subtypes? It would be interesting to determine the transcription factor(s) that mediate the regulatory control in the principal neurons or interneurons.

21103818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21103818.value: The piriform (olfactory) cortex is important for learning and perception of smells. Plasticity of piriform cortical circuitry is thought to be critical for learning, but how its underlying mechanisms work is unclear. In this proposal, we examined how two main output neurons, SL and SP neurons, are regulated by inhibitory transmission and interneuron subtypes. We found that the inhibitory synapses and circuits are differentially wired up for SL and SP neurons, suggesting that the neural signals they represent are differently processed. Olfactory experience also differentially modulates inhibitory signals in SL and SP neurons. We found that one particular subtype of inhibitory interneuron, the parvalbumin (PV) interneuron, plays a particularly important role in the experience-dependent plasticity of SL and SP neurons. We showed that the PV to SP, but not PV to SL, neural circuit is particularly plastic. Our findings uncover a new type of plasticity in the piriform cortex that is likely important for odor learning and memory.

21203318.value: 以通信達成共識:極限與實踐

21203318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203318.value: In a network in which users may have different private knowledge, how much can they agree on after some discussion? It is intuitive that more discussion generally leads to greater consensus. However, finding the precise cost-benefit trade-off between the amount of discussion and agreement is non-trivial yet essential for developing effective network communication schemes. This project considers the secret key agreement problem, where users have public discussions to generate a common secret key. The objective is to characterize the maximum amount of secret key that the users can share after a limited amount of discussion, and to develop effective discussion schemes that can approach the theoretical limit. The secret key can then be used to support provably secure communication among the users. The optimal trade-off between key rate and discussion rate is unknown, even for the two-user case. Nevertheless, with appropriate simplifications, the PI and others have made substantial progress in the more pragmatic case involving multiple users. The idea is to consider different tractable models of practical interest, derive computable bounds and optimality conditions for different discussion strategies, and identify the limitations and potential improvements with conjectures and concrete examples that can possibly be solved with the help of an automatic information inequality prover. By continuing this approach, this project is expected to generate successively more challenging and general subproblems that inspire new models, proof techniques, and discussion schemes. Partial solutions also exist that suggest interesting connections to machine learning problems. For instance, with no restrictions on the amount of public discussion, the maximum key rate can be regarded as a multivariate extension of Shannon’s mutual information: a quantity measuring the amount of mutual information in the private knowledge of the users. This has recently inspired a new framework for clustering features according to their mutual information. Additionally, with limited public discussion, the problem is related to the information-bottleneck method for feature extraction. Recently, such an information-theoretic approach has been applied to deep learning studies with promising results. Deep learning has also been used to automatically construct information-theoretically secure communication schemes. This project will elucidate such connections using the information-bottleneck method and deep learning to solve the secret key agreement problem. The network information theory developed under the secret key agreement problem will also help understand and improve machine learning techniques. 在網絡中，不同用戶擁有不同信息，通過適當的通信，用戶之間可以達成一定的共識。通常來說，用戶之間的通信越多，所能達成的共識越多，然而，兩者之間的確切關係尚無明確定論。該關係的刻畫對我們構建高效的網絡通信至關重要。本項目研究密鑰協商問題，即用戶通過通信交流產生一個共同的密鑰。項目旨在：1）刻畫出在一定通信速率下所能產生的密鑰的極限速率；2）構造一個能達到上述極限的實際可行性協議。生成的密鑰可用來實現用戶之間的安全通信。 在一般情況下，即使只有兩個用戶，密鑰速率與通信速率之間的確切關係依舊未知。基於此，研究員根據實際情況對模型進行了適當的簡化，並對該問題的研究取得了顯著的進展。基本思路：基於實際情況簡化模型，給出可計算的理論界和評價協議優劣的準則，通過實例和猜想指出現有的不足和可進一步推動的思路，以及運用信息不等式軟件進行佐證。該項目的研究有望啟發產生一些新的模型、證明思路、和可行性協議。 現有的文獻指出，密鑰協商問題與機器學習存在著一定的聯繫。一方面，當通信速率沒有限制時，所能產生的密鑰的最大速率等於用戶之間的多元互信息。在機器學習中，以該多元互信息為度量準則，我們可以對用戶的特徵進行有效的聚類。另一方面，當通信速率受限制時，密鑰協商問題與特徵提取中的信息瓶頸方法有關。最近的研究表明，信息瓶頸方法可用於研究深度學習；同時，深度學習也可用來自動地構建安全通信協議。在本項目中，通過運用信息瓶頸方法和深度學習解決密鑰協商問題，可進一步闡明他們之間的聯繫。此外，研究密鑰協商問題所揭示的網絡信息論也將有助於我們進一步理解和改進機器學習。

21203318.label: Realisation of objectives
21203318.value: Overall, all the objectives have been accomplished to a significant extent, resulting in 3 journal publications and 9 conference publications. 2 more journal submissions are under review. The first objective of the project is to derive information-theoretic limits on the trade-off between key rate and discussion rate. We gave a complete characterization of the individual discussion rates required to generate any secret key rate for sources that minimally connected hypergraphs can represent. En route to proving the results, some combinatorial properties of hypergraphs are derived, which are of independent interest in graph theory. For the so-called pairwise independent network (PIN) model in literature, we could pinpoint the trade-off between the key rate and total discussion rate by leveraging combinatorial optimization techniques. For a large class of PIN models, we obtained an explicit characterization of the individual discussion rate required for generating a secret key of maximal rate. These results have been published in prestigious journals and conferences, including IEEE Transactions on Information Theory and IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory. We have also conveyed our results to experts in the field, including Profs. P. Narayan, S. Watanabe, and H. Tyagi. The project's second objective is to develop discussion schemes that are practical and near-optimal under different scenarios. We first considered the finite linear source (FLS) model, which naturally arises in the network packet transmission scenario. We put forth a simple non-interactive protocol for this source model to generate a secret key of maximal length using the minimum number of discussions. The discussion protocol is practical since it only requires each user to do linear processing before applying the standard Slepian-Wolf scheme. We then investigated practical discussion schemes for omniscience when there is a wiretapper. To this end, we considered the tree-PIN model with a linear wiretapper that can observe arbitrary linear combinations of the source. For this source model, we constructed an optimal omniscience scheme that completely aligns with the wiretapper side information, thereby leaking as little information as possible. The scheme is practical since it is linear, non-interactive, and deterministic. These results have been presented at conferences such as the well-recognized IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory and IEEE Information Theory Workshop and submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. The project's third objective is to develop general information-theoretic tools and elucidate their connections with, or potential applications to, machine learning. To achieve this objective, we studied various mathematical structures in submodular function optimization, especially the principal and principal sequences of partitions. We found a fundamental property connecting the well-known Watanabe's total correlation and the multivariate mutual information inspired by multiterminal secret key agreement capacity. Consequently, we showed that info-clustering, an information-theoretic paradigm for data clustering in machine learning, can be solved in an agglomerative manner. Our results elucidate that divisive and agglomerative approaches result in the same hierarchy of clusters under the info-clustering framework. The agglomerative approach is an order of magnitude faster than the divisive one. These results have been published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory and IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory. The algorithms have been implemented and are now available as public GitHub repositories.

21203318.label: Major findings and research outcome
21203318.value: For minimally connected hypergraphical sources, a single-letter explicit characterization of the region of achievable secret key rate and public discussion rate tuple was established. Furthermore, we showed that the secret key could be attained non-asymptotically with zero error and perfect secrecy through linear non-interactive discussion without any additional cost in the discussion rates. We also obtained a closed-form formula for the maximum achievable secret key rate under any given total public discussion rate for such kinds of sources. For general hypergraphical sources, we derived a family of explicitly computable upper bounds on the number of bits of the secret key that can be generated per bit of public discussion. In particular, a specific instance of these upper bounds was shown to be tight for the pairwise independent network (PIN) model, a special case of the hypergraphical source when the hypergraph is a graph. Therefore, we have pinpointed the trade-off between the key rate and total discussion rate for the important PIN model. For finite linear sources (FLS), we obtained a characterization of the minimum amount of public discussion required to generate a secret key of maximum length. This was accomplished by constructing an optimal discussion scheme in which each terminal first does a linear processing of its own private observations, following which the terminals all execute a discussion-optimal communication-for omniscience protocol. For a general source model with a wiretapper, we provided a lower bound on the minimum leakage in achieving omniscience. The lower bound is expressed in terms of wiretapper secret key capacity and was identified to be tight in the two-user FLS. For tree-PIN source with linear wiretapper, we showed that the minimum leakage omniscience scheme achieves wiretap secret key capacity. This was accomplished by constructing a deterministic omniscience scheme that aligns with the wiretapper side information completely. As a result, we established a duality between secure omniscience and wiretap secret key capacity problems and a single-letter characterization of the wiretap secret key capacity. For hypergraphical sources with a linear wiretapper, we established a necessary and sufficient condition for the positivity of wiretap secret key capacity. By exploiting a duality between the principal sequence of partitions and the principal sequence in combinatorial optimization, we uncover a fundamental connection between the well-known total correlation and the multivariate mutual information (MMI). With this, we showed that the info-clustering, a data clustering framework based on MMI, can be solved in an agglomerative manner and is an order of magnitude faster than the existing divisive one.

21203318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21203318.value: Firstly, the most imminent among the several directions in which this project can be extended is to characterize the trade-off between key rate and discussion rate for hypergraphical sources, i.e., for any given total discussion rate, give a precise characterization of the maximal achievable secret key rate. To this end, we need to develop a novel technique for deriving information-theoretic upper bound and a new discussion scheme for the lower bound. Secondly, our current results on the tree-PIN model show a duality between secure omniscience and wiretap secret key capacity problems. It is plausible to show that this duality also holds for any finite linear source, potentially by constructing an omniscience scheme that aligns with the wiretapper's side information. Lastly, instead of attaining omniscience or generating a secret key, one may be interested in only computing a given function of the source. Since this secure function computation problem is closely related to the secret key agreement problem, it is promising to extend our current results and insights to secure function computation. For instance, an open problem is to characterize the discussion and leakage rates for secure function computation.

21203318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21203318.value: Considering that users possess distinct albeit correlated knowledge, how much discussion is needed to agree on some common secure knowledge independent of the entire discussion? For several scenarios of practical interest, we gave precise characterizations of the trade-off between the amount of discussion and common secure knowledge. Furthermore, we devised some simple (near-)optimal discussion schemes that are easy to implement in practice. These results provide important insights into information-theoretic problems that arise in secure communications. More importantly, the above problem also inspired a faster algorithm for data clustering in machine learning, which may have potential applications such as gene-clustering and social network clustering.

21203518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203518.value: Hybrid perovskite semiconductors have recently become promising alternatives for low-cost and high-efficient photovoltaics. Their photovoltaic efficiency has increased dramatically by more mature technologies, from 3.8% to 22.1% within a few years. Despite these advantages, the stability of hybrid perovskite photovoltaics remains the most important concern. Stability issues occur in the hybrid perovskite itself but also in other constituent materials, as well as at interfaces between different layers of solar devices. Thus, several approaches have been developed to diminish device degradation. For example, organic semiconductors were replaced by oxides at interfaces to promote moisture and oxygen stability. Central to this proposal is the design of hybrid perovskites, striving to explore fundamental properties and dynamic interactions of interfacial layers to develop efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics. The PI’s previous research experiences in exciton transfer dynamics of platinum acetylide polymers, in combination with the investigation on photoelectrochemistry at hybrid semiconductors using electrochemical techniques, has helped him gain a broad perspective on semiconductor materials for energy and environment applications alongside a deeper understanding of the challenges. To accomplish these goals, we propose the following tasks. (1) Design novel hybrid materials with stable perovskite-like structures. We will fabricate the perovskite spot array using a piezoelectric dispenser and then screen photoelectrode array by modified SECM techniques. (2) Characterize photoelectrochemical response of hybrid perovskite thin films by designed photoelectrochemical systems to confirm the result of SECM imaging. The photocurrent density of hybrid perovskites will be further optimized by morphology engineering (3) Investigate charge dynamics and transport mechanisms between perovskite film and interfacial layers (i.e. hole transport layer, electron transport layer and modification layer) utilizing photophysical, electrochemical and photoelectochemical techniques. (4) We will fabricate perovskite solar cells with the measurement of photovoltaic parameters, and then understand the relationships among exciton diffusion behaviors, photoelectrochemical response and photovoltaic performance. We believe the implementation of the proposed project could not only advance our fundamental understanding of dynamic interfacial mechanisms on hybrid perovskite solar cells, but also open a new avenue to develop novel perovskite-based solar devices with enhanced efficiency and stability for commercial applications. The results of the project will provide new classroom materials for undergraduate courses as well. The ECS project will enable the PI to continue his research work in a sustained and focused manner, laying the foundation for a lifetime of integrated research and teaching contributions in the areas of semiconductor materials, photophysics, and photoelectrochemistry. 雜化鈣鈦礦半導體已成為低成本和高效率光伏領域中極具潛力的替代材料。伴隨日趨成熟的技術，雜化鈣鈦礦半導體器件的效率在幾年內由3.8%增加到了23.3%。儘管具有這些優點，雜化鈣鈦礦光伏器件穩定性仍然是最重要的關注點。光伏器件穩定性問題不僅存在於雜化鈣鈦礦材料本身，也存在於其他的構成材料，以及光伏器件不同層的介面處。因此，幾種方法已經被採用來降低器件的退化程度。比如，使用氧化物替代介面處的有機半導體以提升器件對水分和氧氣的耐受能力。本研究計畫的核心是設計合成雜化鈣鈦礦材料，並致力於探索不同介面層的基本性質和介面層之間的動力學相互作用，以開發高效穩定的鈣鈦礦光伏器件。本專案負責人此前主要研究鉑乙炔聚合物的激子轉移動力學以及使用電化學技術研究雜化鈣鈦礦半導體的光電化學特性。這些研究經歷使他對應用於能源與環境的半導體材料具有了更廣闊的視角，同時對當前挑戰具有了更深刻理解。 為了完成目標，將展開以下計畫：（1）通過使用壓電分配器製造鈣鈦礦點陣，結合已改進的掃描電化學顯微鏡技術來篩選光電極陣列，設計具有穩定鈣鈦礦結構的新型雜化材料；（2）測定雜化鈣鈦礦薄膜的光電化學回應，使用已設計的光電化學系統確認掃描電化學顯微鏡成像結果，並通過調控形貌優化雜化鈣鈦礦光電流密度；（3）使用光物理、電化學和光電化學等技術手段，探究鈣鈦礦薄膜與介面層（包括空穴傳輸層、電子傳輸層和修飾層）之間的電荷動力學和傳輸機制；（4）製作鈣鈦礦太陽能電池並測定相關光伏參數，以理解激子擴散行為、光電化學回應和光伏性能之間的關係。 此研究不僅可增進對雜化鈣鈦礦太陽能電池動態介面機制的深入理解，還可為發展可商業化的高效能新型鈣鈦礦太陽能器件開闢了一條嶄新的道路。此外，這項研究成果也可為本科課程提供新資訊。此研究計畫可使專案負責人專注其研究方向，為其在半導體材料、光物理和光電化學領域的綜合研究和教學貢獻打下堅實基礎。

21203518.label: Realisation of objectives
21203518.value: 1. To design hybrid materials with stable perovskite-like structures based on Goldschmidt's Tolerance Factor, and then screen hybrid perovskite photoelectrode array using scanning photoelectrochemical microscopy imaging. To develop ultra-stable hybrid perovskite photoelectrodes, we initially identified a series of potential hybrid materials with perovskite-like structures by GTF, i.e., (MA)2MnCl4, (MA)2GeCl4, (MA)2EuCl4, (MA)2CdCl4, (MA)2FeCl4 and (MA)2CuCl4. Building on our previous work with the array scanning technique for the analysis of MAPbI3, we undertook a detailed study on a variety of potential hybrid perovskites using the high-throughput scanning photoelectrochemical microscopy (SPECM) system. The 2D-layered (MA)2CdCl4 perovskites (CD-4) increase up to ~ 0.30 mA cm-2 which is due to the improved perovskite crystallinity and grain size. For photoactive semiconductors, we modified a typical scanning electrochemical microscope (SECM) system by replacing the conventional working electrode with an optical fiber. By combining SPECM with time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) measurements on different molar ratios of BP/MAPbI3 halide perovskite composites, the cause-and-effect relationship between material compositions and PEC responses could be clarified by a combination of the SECM imaging technology and photoluminescence decay dynamics. We employed the SECM system to screen the BP/MAPbI3-based array photoelectrodes, detecting the photocurrent response on the compositions of MAPbI3 doped with a series of BP ranging from 0 mole% to 10 mole %. 2.0 mole% of BP to MAPbI3 exhibited the highest photocurrent under visible-light illumination. 2. To characterize the photoelectrochemical response of hybrid perovskite semiconductors by a designed photoelectrochemical system. We have a designed photoelectrochemical (PEC) system to analyze the PEC response and stability of the perovskite films. PEC cell consists of one working electrode (Cd-based hybrid material film on the fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) glass) for the production and detection of reduced species, and a platinum (Pt) mesh counter electrode to generate an oxidized mediator species Ox at a diﬀusion-limited rate from a reduced species (Red), which is formed by the working electrode in the electrolyte. The photocurrent for 2D layered (MA)2CdCl4 perovskites (CD-4) increases up to ~ 0.30 mA cm-2 (at − 0.7 V vs. Fc/Fc+) which is due to the improved perovskite crystallinity and grain size. In addition, the thin-film bulk photoelectrodes of the pure MAPbI3 and BP/MAPbI3 perovskite composites were characterized by their PEC responses to validate the experimental results of the SPECM images. By using linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) under chopped light illumination, the photocurrent densities of BP/MAPbI3 perovskite composites with a molar ratio ranging from 0% to 10.0% were obtained. The 2.0% and 10.0% BP/MAPbI3 composite photoelectrodes produced photocurrents of 6.2 × 10−5 A and 0.4 × 10−5 A at−0.6 V vs Ag/AgNO3 for the reduction reaction of BQ/BQ− redox couples. These PEC results obtained by LSV are in accordance with those of the SPECM image, thereby demonstrating the validity of using SECM imaging technology for the determination of PEC performance on BP/MAPbI3 halide perovskite composites. 3. To investigate the charge dynamics and transport mechanisms between perovskite film and interfacial layers utilizing time-resolved photoluminescence and photoelectrochemical technique. In terms of the charge dynamics, we performed a series of material characterizations, e.g., time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL). We determined optical band gaps (Eg) by Kubelka-Munk equation from UV-vis absorption spectrum. The decay dynamics was monitored by using TRPL spectra in order to understand the exciton diffusion behaviors of (MA)2CdCl4 perovskite. The 2D layered (MA)2CdCl4 perovskite crystals give rise to a longer exciton diffusion lifetime with a time constant of t PL = 1.50 ns. After 60 days exposure to 90% RH, the lifetime of CD-4 films was reduced to 0.83 ns, because the emission intensity was quenched by the formation of hydrate products, MACd3Cl7·3H2O, characterized by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD). By using a time-correlated single photon counting (TCSPC) system, we also collected time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) spectra of BP/MAPbI3 perovskite composite films to examine the PL decay dynamics. For the TRPL measurements, we utilized a pulsed laser with an excitation wavelength of 450 nm, which could provide < 200 ps pulses with the fluence of ∼30 nJ cm−2. BP/MAPbI3 perovskite films with thicknesses of about 200 nm have been used for the photophysical characterizations because this film thickness is close to the typical thickness in photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices. We monitored PL emissions at ∼775 nm to determine the PL decay dynamics of those perovskite composite films. By fitting PL decay curves using exponential functions, the PL decay lifetime, τPL, was then estimated. For 2.0 mole % BP/MAPbI3 perovskite composite films, the overall photoluminescence lifetime τPL was largest, at 0.136 μs, which is attributed to the incorporation of BP into MAPbI3 perovskite films leading to reduced charge-carrier recombination. Additionally, the efficient electron–hole separation and charge-carrier transport of photogenerated electron–hole pairs can theoretically result in enhanced PEC activity. To investigate the influence factor of the motion of electron–hole pairs of the participating perovskites, temperature-dependent TRPL was conducted with temperatures ranging from −30 °C to 30 °C. On the basis of the temperature-dependent TRPL spectral response of the MBCl-I, the activation energies of the fast and slow decay components are about 198 and 167 meV, respectively. From the pre-exponential factor, the temperature-independent coupling matrix elements were evaluated for the fast and slow decay components of MBCl-I perovskites (0.427 cm−1 and 0.234 cm−1 ), which are stronger than those of MBI (0.339 cm−1 and 0.191 cm−1 ), as the wave functions of MBCl-I are more delocalized along with the perovskite materials. 4. To fabricate perovskite solar cells and understand the relationships among exciton diffusion behaviors, photoelectrochemical response, and photovoltaic performance. Based on the studies from Task I to Task III, we confirm that Cd doping of hybrid perovskites is considered an efficient approach for enhancing the stability of solar cells. We have fabricated different doping amounts of Cd in MAPbI3 perovskite solar cells. The photovoltaic performance of Cd-doped MAPbI3 perovskites compared with pristine MAPbI3. Pure MAPbI3 has the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.38%. After doping Cd into MAPbI3, the efficiency gradually dropped. The 5% Cd-doped MAPbI3 showed an optimal efficiency of 8.33%. The unsatisfactory solar devices will be further optimized with enhanced long-term stability. We expect that the Cd-doped perovskite solar cells are more stable than pristine MAPbI¬3-based photovoltaics. It is because the Cd-based hydrate will be produced to protect the MAPbI3 perovskite layers, reducing the decomposition of MAPbI3 perovskites by water molecules. Moreover, we fabricated the inverted perovskite solar cells with poly-TPD as a hole transport layer and C60 as an electron transport layer after getting the results of material and photophysical characterizations from Task I to Task III. We measured the photovoltaic performance of a series of BP/MAPbI3-based solar cells. In comparison to pristine MAPbI3 perovskites, the 2.0 mole% BP/MAPbI3-based solar cell shows the best power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.112% with a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 23.70 mA cm−2, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.05 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.768. The self-healing property of BP is possibly beneficial for the stability of perovskite solar cells. Therefore, we evaluated the stability of as-prepared BP/MAPbI3-based perovskite solar cells with a representative inverted planar configuration of ITO/poly-TPD/perovskite composite/C60/BCP/Ag. Compared with the pure MAPbI3 counterpart, the BP/MAPbI3-based perovskite solar cells show improved stability under continuous 100 mW cm−2 illumination.

21203518.label: Major findings and research outcome
21203518.value: For the first time, we demonstrate that methylammonium cadmium halides ((MA)2CdCl4) show photoelectrochemical (PEC) response with excellent humidity and chemical resistance because the oxidation state of almost all cadmium compounds is +2. The interaction between the (MA)2CdCl4 and water vapor is studied by probing film morphology and characterizing a single crystal structure. The experimental results showed that H2O is able to complex with the perovskite, forming a hydrate product with the molecular formula of MACd3Cl7·3H2O upon humidity exposure, which causes a decrease in absorption and a recognizable change in the crystal structure of the material. To reduce charge recombination in the perovskites, we incorporate black phosphorus (BP) into methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskites, and optimize the concentration with scanning photoelectrochemical microscopy (SPECM). An optimum ratio of 2.0 mole% BP/MAPbI3 perovskite composite generates an increased photocurrent response compared to pristine MAPbI3 for 2 mM benzoquinone (BQ) reduction at −0.6 V vs Ag/AgNO3 on a spot array electrode under illumination. Finally, we demonstrate the enhanced efficiency and stability of 2.0% BP/MAPbI3-based perovskite solar cells arising from impeded Pb0-defect generation and suppressed charge-carrier recombination. In order to reduce the concerns about environmental health threats, we also developed lead-free bismuth (Bi)-based hybrid perovskite through in situ growth. The air-stable MA3Bi2I9/DMA3BiI6 perovskite heterostructure with enhanced photoinduced charge separation exhibits outstanding visible-light-induced photocatalytic activity for H2 evolution in an aqueous hydrogen iodide solution. In addition, mixed halide perovskite MA3Bi2Cl9-xIx with a bandgap funnel structure is developed. Due to gradient neutral formation energy within iodine-doped MA3Bi2Cl9, the concentration of the iodide element decreases from the surface to the interior across the MA3Bi2Cl9–xIx perovskite. A graded bandgap funnel structure is therefore formed, leading to the promotion of photoinduced charge transfer from the interior to the surface for efficient photocatalytic redox reaction. The dynamic interfacial interactions of novel bandgap funnel structure perovskite MA3Bi2Cl9-xIx in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) system are then investigated. We prepared MA3Bi2Cl9−yIy and MA3Bi2I9 perovskites (named MBCl-I and MBI)—in the presence and absence of the bandgap funnel structure, respectively. Due to the bandgap funnel structure, stronger electronic coupling arising from an enhanced overlap of electronic wavefunctions results in more efficient exciton transport. Besides, MBCl-I's effective diffusion coefficient and electron-transfer rate demonstrate efficient heterogeneous charge transfer at the solid–liquid interface, generating improved photoelectrochemical hydrogen production.

21203518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21203518.value: Based on our success in the synthesis of lead-free halide perovskites ((MA)2CdCl4, MA3Bi2I9, and MA3Bi2Cl9−xIx), in the future, we can develop more environmentally friendly halide perovskites, such as Sn, Sb, Ge-based halide perovskites, and compare their performances. We can also try to apply the bandgap funneling perovskites (MA3Bi2Cl9-xIx) to different applications, such as hydrogen production, CO2 reduction, and pollutant degradation, to explore more suitable applications for this novel perovskite. In addition, we can develop more kinds of novel perovskite structures based on this structure. The stability of perovskites in different photocatalysis systems can also be studied by combining the high-performance perovskites that we have synthesized with different other semiconductors, such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), transition metal disulfides (TMDs), MXenes, etc. to form heterojunctions. This will not only retard the decomposition of halide perovskites, but also improve the separation of photogenerated carriers and increase the number of catalytic active sites, thus greatly improving the catalytic performance. Last but not least, we can explore new methods to further investigate the photophysical and photochemical mechanisms of the dynamic transfer of photogenerated carriers at the solid-solid and solid-liquid interfaces and apply these findings to the fields of electroluminescence, photocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis.

21203518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21203518.value: Halide perovskites are promising semiconductor materials that can be widely used in the fields of electroluminescence, photoelectrocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. However, it is still challenging to design a perovskite material with a very outstanding performance and figure out the carrier transfer dynamic mechanism. Therefore, our research focused on solving these problems. At first, we design hybrid materials with stable perovskite-like structures based on Goldschmidt's Tolerance Factor, and then screen hybrid perovskite photoelectrode array using scanning photoelectrochemical microscopy imaging. And then, we characterize the photoelectrochemical response of hybrid perovskite semiconductors by a designed photoelectrochemical system. Next, we use time-resolved photoluminescence and photoelectrochemical techniques to investigate the charge dynamics and transport mechanisms between perovskite film and interfacial layers utilizing. Finally, we fabricate perovskite solar cells and understand the relationships among exciton diffusion behaviors, photoelectrochemical response and photovoltaic performance. The combination of photophysical and electrochemical techniques opens up an avenue to explore the intrinsic and interfacial properties of semiconductor materials for elucidating the correlation between material characterization and device performance. These findings will guide researchers in designing high-performance hybrid perovskites.

21211018.value: 面向大規模視覺數據分析的視覺特徵和信號可擴展表示研究

21211018.label: Project Objectives
21211018.value: Designing a scalable coding architecture for joint visual signal and feature compression; Developing efficient construction and compression schemes for the base layer based on deep feature extraction; Exploring the compression of the enhancement layer by investigating advanced coding algorithms.

21211018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21211018.value: The visual signals, such as images and videos, are increasingly becoming the “biggest big data” and spurring on tremendous growth in related technologies. Along with such explosion, for effective visual data management and manipulation, there are still fundamental and critical challenges regarding compression. In particular, with the advances in computer vision, nowadays both human beings and machines serve as the ultimate receivers of visual data. Instead of perceiving the visual content, image/video analyses are performed relying on the extracted features. The proliferation of such automatic services and unprecedented challenges in handling large-scale visual data have pushed the horizon of the visual compression paradigm, and joint visual signal plus feature compression in a scalable framework is necessary and desirable, as these functionalities provide enhancement to transmission and storage applications according to the dynamic demand and network bandwidth. Existing compression frameworks, such as image/video coding and compact feature representation, either do not fully leverage the redundancy between visual signal and feature, or largely ignore the interactions between them. To address these limitations, we will systematically develop a novel and integrated framework for joint visual signal and feature compression with deep neural networks, due to the exceptional power of deep learning in visual computing tasks. In particular, we propose to partition the representation of visual information into base and enhancement layers, where base layer conveys compact feature for analysis purpose, and enhancement layer accounts for representing the visual signals based on the fine structure prediction from base layer. Within this framework, we plan to 1) study the construction and compression of base layer, and investigate the utility of base layer for rate-utility optimization; 2) explore the enhancement layer generation based on the base layer prediction and develop advanced enhancement layer compression algorithms; 3) optimize the overall coding performance with efficient bit allocation strategy between two layers. The proposed paradigm shifts feature representation as an integrated part of visual data compression, and offloads feature extraction to large-scale edge nodes. As such, the interactions of visual signal and feature representation can greatly increase the degree of supported scalability and flexibility to meet various application requirements. In server-side processing, such scalable framework also allows the direct access to the visual feature without introducing the data redundancy. The research results will bridge the gaps between visual analysis and signal representation, and contribute to a diverse set of applications such as video surveillance, autonomous driving and augmented reality. 視覺信號如圖像和視頻等，正日益成為“最大的大數據”，並帶來相關技術的快速進步。視覺大數據對於視覺數據的高效管理，特別是數據的壓縮帶來了極大的挑戰。隨著計算機視覺技術的進步，人類和機器都成為視覺數據的最終接收和使用者。圖像/視頻的自動分析不依賴於感知視覺內容，而是依賴於提取的特徵來完成。因此，大規模視覺數據自動分析所帶來的前所未有的挑戰已經擴展了視覺數據壓縮的範疇。本項目在可擴展的框架中聯合視覺信號以及特徵進行聯合壓縮表示，從而根據動態需求和網絡帶寬的變化優化視覺信息傳輸。現有的壓縮框架，例如圖像/視頻編碼和緊湊的特徵表示，或者不能充分利用視覺信號和特徵之間的冗餘，或者在很大程度上忽略它們之間的相互作用。為了解決這些局限性，我們擬通過視覺計算任務中深度學習的強大功能，進行視覺信號和特徵的聯合表示和壓縮。特別地，我們將視覺信息的表示劃分為基礎層和增強層，其中基礎層傳達用於分析目的的緊湊特徵，而增強層根據基礎層的特徵表示來進一步表達視覺信號。在此框架內，我們計劃1）研究基礎層的構造和壓縮，並研究基礎層碼率-效用優化; 2）探索增強層生成，並開發先進的增強層壓縮算法; 3）利用兩層之間的有效比特分配策略優化整體編碼性能。所提出的方案將特徵表示轉換為視覺數據壓縮的不可分離的部分，並將特徵提取部署到大規模邊緣節點。因此，視覺信號和特徵表示的交互可以極大地增強支持的可伸縮性和靈活性以滿足各種應用的要求。在服務器端處理中，這種可擴展框架還允許直接訪問特徵而不引入數據冗餘。研究結果將整合視覺分析和信號表示在一個統一的框架中，以支持視頻監控，自動駕駛和增強現實等多種應用。

21211018.label: Realisation of objectives
21211018.value: All three major objectives are fully achieved. We developed the scalable visual representation based upon two layers, including the base layer that accounts for the compact feature representation and enhancement layer that achieves the signal level reconstruction. The interaction between two layers has been particularly designed based upon the specifically learned generative model. The entire framework has also been optimized in a scientifically sound way, and the proposed framework enjoys the advantages of highly effective, flexible and computationally efficient. The research results show that the performance of the proposed framework is superior to the traditional video coding methods, in terms of rate-accuracy and rate-distortion performance based on facial images. Moreover, we also studied the model generation, utilization and communication paradigm to further improve the representation capability of the visual data. These works have been published in IEEE ICME and IEEE Trans on Multimedia. Regarding the compact feature representation, we first developed a neuron coverage based domain generalization method, empowering the capability of extracting highly generalized features. The method was further analysed with network dissection, and the experimental results show the promise of the method in improving the generalization capability. The feature compression performance, which is critical in the compact visual representation, has been further improved based upon the teacher-student learning strategy, as well as the advanced rate-accuracy optimization with multi-granularity constraint. Significant bit rate savings have also been achieved in terms of the rate-accuracy performance. Additionally, we also studied the compression performance of the intermediate deep learning features, as transmitting the intermediate features provides the promising balance among the transmission load, computational load and generalization capability. These works have been published in IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, ICASSP and ACM Multimedia. Regarding the signal-level compression, we studied the quality evaluation of the distorted images, which leads to the Deep Image Structure and Texture Similarity (DISTS) index. The intrinsic popularity has also been studied, based on the optimization of millions of popularity-discriminable pairs. The visual signal compression performance was further optimized based upon the philosophy that the compression should be fully optimized towards the ultimate utility, and a specifically designed rate-accuracy optimization scheme was developed. This strategy leads to significant bit rate savings. The compression framework was also optimized with the advanced partitioning structure, further improving the coding performance of visual signals. These works have been published in IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, IEEE Open Journal of Circuits and Systems and ACM Multimedia.

21211018.label: Major findings and research outcome
21211018.value: In this project, we have the following key findings: 1) The scalable representation framework of visual data not only provides the significant bitrate savings in terms of rate-accuracy performance, but also delivers promising rate-distortion performance. 2) The compact feature representation performance can be greatly improved by designing effective feature extraction and rate-analysis functions to exploit the intrinsic characteristics of the visual data. 3) The ultimate utility of the visual signals plays key roles in driving the optimization of the codec. As such, the principle that optimization with the end in mind could greatly benefit the compact visual signal representation towards machine vision. The project has led to 9 publications in total, including papers published in top-venues in the field, such as IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, IEEE Transactions on Multimedia.

21211018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21211018.value: The proposed framework can be further developed to achieve cross-modality visual data representation, in which the visual data can be hierarchically represented with multimodal fusions (e.g., audio and visual). Moreover, the proposed paradigm can also be extended to the 3D geometry data, due to the increasing proliferation of multi-dimensional multimedia application systems.

21211018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21211018.value: This project focuses on compact representation of visual data towards different application scenarios. The research topic is timely and critical because the machine vision is gradually replacing the human vision as the ultimate receiver of the visual data in many applications. As such, the way of representing the visual data should be highly adapted to such evolution. We develop a principled coding framework and explore the scalable representation paradigm of the visual data, based upon the joint visual signal and feature compression. In particular, the base layer accounts for the compact feature representation while the target of the enhancement layer is signal-level reconstruction. The optimization of the framework is systematically studied, and efficient feature extraction, compression and signal reconstruction schemes are further developed. The results of the research show that the proposed representation of visual data can be highly flexible, efficient and computationally economic. Our research outcomes have potential to be applied in real-world applications such as video surveillance, autonomous driving and augmented reality.

21211518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21211518.value: Light-field (LF) data is capable of providing viewers with a realistic 3-D visual perception in glasses-free and fatigue-free manners with the help of LF display technology. Thus, LF is considered as a promising paradigm for immersive 3-D telepresence, which can be widely applied to entertainment, telerehabilitation, business, etc., to significantly reform human work and life styles. LF also facilitates/allows a wide range of interesting applications, e.g., image editing/post-capture refocus, 3-D reconstruction, etc. More importantly, recent advances in commercial hand-held LF cameras make the convenient acquisition of LF images in a single snapshot possible, which dramatically boosts LF-based research and applications. However, the astronomical amount of LF data poses great challenges to its storage, transmission, and display/rendering. Moreover, due to the challenge of characterizing the inherent structure of LF data, conventional image/video coding schemes are not well suited for LF data. Therefore, it is urgently needed to study more efficient LF data tailored compression frameworks for advancing the deployment of LF technology. Unlike conventional architectures based on predictive and transform coding, we will investigate novel frameworks from two new perspectives, which are expected to be capable of accurately characterizing the inherent structure. Specifically, from the statistical learning perspective, we will investigate computationally and memory- efficient deep learning architectures and training strategies for high-quality spatial and angular reconstruction, which are novel to address the challenge posed by the high dimensionality of LF. From the geometric modeling perspective, to explore the multidimensional correlation of LF data simultaneously for the best global performance, we propose to formulate a multi-sparsity and low-rank regularized compact matrix factorization with the assistance of proposed novel accurate depth reasoning with occluded region regularization. Moreover, in contrast to the conventional explicit model based rate-distortion-optimization (RDO), which requires time-consuming pre-encoding, it is promising to study learning based RDO with efficient random forests/trees and deep features to determine the optimal encoding parameters faster and more accurately. With our novel algorithms that cover multidisciplinary knowledge, as well as our promising preliminary experimental verification, our frameworks have great potential in achieving 30% data size reduction at the same reconstruction quality than current state-of-the-art methods, which could be a significant boost to LF-based immersive 3-D telepresence. Beyond compact representation, our algorithms can address other fundamental issues of LF acquisition and applications, including, but not limited to, compressive LF sensing, precise distance measurement/perception, etc. 光場成像能夠同時捕捉三維場景的反射特性以及幾何結構。應用光場顯示技術，光場數據能夠為觀眾提供逼真的三維視覺感受，而不需要借助3D眼鏡，也不會產生視覺疲勞。因此，光場有望為沉浸式三維遠程呈現提供有效的解決方案，將可以廣泛應用於娛樂，遠程康復，商業等領域，從而顯著改善人們的工作和生活方式。另外，光場可以應用在如圖像編輯，拍照後重聚焦，三維重建等方面。更重要的是，近年來商業手持式光場相機的發展使得光場圖像的採集非常方便，這極大地促進了對光場的研究和應用。 然而，光場的數據量非常大，這對它的存儲，傳輸和顯示/渲染都產生了很大的挑戰。並且由於表徵光場數據的內在結構具有挑戰性，傳統的圖像或視頻編碼方式不能很好的適用於光場數據。因此，更高效的光場數據壓縮框架對推動光場技術的發展十分必要。 不同於傳統的基於預測和變換編碼的體系結構，本項目將從兩個新的角度研究新的框架，從而準確地表示光場數據的內在結構。從統計學習的角度出發，本項目將研究高效利用計算和內存資源的深度學習模型和訓練方法，以實現高質量的空間域和角度域重建。這將是解決光場數據高維度挑戰的新方法。 從基於模型優化的角度出發，為了探索光場數據的多維相關性，同時獲得最佳的全局性能，本項目利用已提出的遮擋區域正則化深度估計方法，提出構造多域稀疏與低秩正則化的緊湊矩陣分解方法。 此外，傳統的率失真優化方法基於特定模型，需要的預編碼非常耗時，本項目將研究基於學習的率失真優化方法，利用高效的隨機森林/樹以及深度特徵來更快更準確地確定最佳編碼參數。 通過結合多領域知識提出新的算法，並經過初步實驗驗證，本項目的框架將有望達到與當前先進方法同等重建質量，而數據量降低30％的效果。這將極大推動基於光場的沉浸式三維遠程呈現。除了緊湊表示之外，本項目提出的算法還可以解決光場採集和應用的其他基本問題，例如壓縮光場感知，精確距離測量與感知等。

21211518.label: Realisation of objectives
21211518.value: Objective 1: to spatially super-resolve light field images, we explored the complementary information cross sub-aperture images via computationally and memory-efficient spatial-angular separable convolution, combinatorial geometry embedding and structural consistency regularization, and cross-scale information propagation. Objective 2: to angularly synthesize light field images, we studied efficient feature learning, geometry and occlusion-aware blending with optimized sampling patterns, content-aware warping operation, and coded aperture-based imaging. Objective 3: to address the occlusion issue in light field depth estimation, we explicitly modeled occlusion regions in supervised and unsupervised fashions. Objective 4: we leveraged graph learning and dictionary learning to sparsely represent light field images for the removal of structural redundancies. Objective 5: we studied a bit allocation scheme by formulating rate and distortion models and an optimization-based method to optimize the positions of input views for improving compression performance. Beyond the above five objectives, we also studied studied perceptual quality assessment towards LF images and extended the proposed methods to other low-level light field image processing, e.g., light field image denoising.

21211518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21211518.value: Further development will focus on: (1) reconstruction of unstructured light fields or light fields with wide fields of view, (2) end-to-end deep learning compression frameworks for light field data, and (3) quantitative metrics for evaluating the parallax structure of reconstructed light field images.

21211518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21211518.value: In this project, based on the philosophy of “compression by reconstruction”, we developed a series of methods of reconstructing high spatial or angular resolution light field images from low resolution ones, and occlusion-aware depth estimation methods from light field images. The solutions could advance various cutting-edge applications, such as meta-verse, immersive telepresence, and VR/AR.

21301018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301018.value: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are a class of systems with an energy gap in the bulk, just like the usual insulators, however the boundary is guaranteed to have nontrivial properties. The nontrivial boundary properties are protected by the symmetries of the system, which will be absent if the symmetries are removed. For three-dimensional (3D) SPT phases, the surface may have three different forms: (1) a gapless and fully symmetric state, (2) a state with one of the symmetries broken spontaneously, and (3) a gapped, symmetric and topologically ordered surface. Whichever it is, the non-triviality of the surface is reflected by the fact that it carries a quantum anomaly of the symmetries, i.e., the surface cannot be realized in strict 2D. In this proposal, we focus on the third type of surfaces —- topologically ordered surfaces. A topologically ordered system hosts exotic quasiparticles, named anyons. Anyons obey fractional braiding statistics and are currently under extensive search, as they can be used for fault-tolerant topological quantum computation. In the presence of symmetries, anyons can intertwine with symmetries in various ways, dubbed different symmetry-enriched topological (SET) phases. Some SET phases carry quantum anomalies of the symmetries. The purpose of this project is to carry out a comprehensive theoretical study on the correspondences between 2D anomalous SETs and 3D SPTs, namely bulk-boundary correspondences. That is, we would like to study the question of which 3D SPT can support a given 2D SET on its surface. We will emphasize the physical pictures behind these correspondences. More specifically, we will study bulk-boundary correspondences in (1) bosonic systems with both mirror-reflection and onsite unitary symmetries; (2) systems with time-reversal/mirror-reflection and Lie group symmetries; (3) fermionic systems with discrete onsite unitary symmetries; (4) systems with general crystalline symmetries; and (5) study some extensions to the similar problem of quantum anomalies in 3D SET systems. This study is of fundamental importance to the general principles of the interplay between topology and symmetry in 3D quantum many-body systems. The bulk-boundary relations are also practically useful for the ongoing search of anyons, as the anomaly-free condition or that a system must carry certain anomaly puts very strong constraints on which topological order can occur in specific systems or materials. 對稱性保護拓撲態是壹類有能隙的系統，就像普通的絕緣體，然而它們的邊界上總是存在非平凡的性質。這些非平凡的性質由系統對稱性保護，如果沒有對稱性，這些非平凡的性質就會消失。三維空間中，對稱性保護拓撲態的表面可以形成三種不同的狀態：1. 對稱的無能隙態，2. 對稱性自發破缺態，3. 對稱的有能隙的拓撲序態。不論哪種態，表面的非平凡特性體現在這個事實：表面態壹定具有量子反常，也就是說這個態不可能在嚴格的二維體系中實現。在這個提案中，我們主要研究第三種態 --- 有拓撲序的表面。壹個有拓撲序的系統可以承載壹種叫做任意子的新奇準粒子。任意子服從分數統計，正在被廣泛的研究，因為它們可以被用來做容錯拓撲量子計算。在有對稱性的情況下，任意子和對稱性的相互糾纏可以非常豐富，這些不同的拓撲序態被稱為對稱性富化拓撲態。其中，有壹些對稱性富化拓撲態具有量子反常。這個提案的主要目的是開展系統化的針對二維對稱性富化拓撲態和三維對稱性保護拓撲態之間的聯系的理論研究。兩者之間的聯系通常被稱為體表對應。換句話說，我們研究哪個三維對稱性保護拓撲態的表面可以存在壹個給定的二維對稱性富化拓撲態。我們的研究會強調體表對應的物理圖像。更具體的，我們會研究下列系統中的體表對應：(1) 具有鏡面對稱性和格點酉對稱性的波色子系統；(2) 具有鏡面（或時間反演）對稱性及李群對稱性的系統；(3) 具有格點酉對稱性的費米子系統；(4) 具有晶格對稱性的系統；(5)壹些三維對稱性富化系統。這個研究對三維量子多體物理系統中的拓撲和對稱性互相影響的壹般原則具有基本的重要性。體表對應關系對當前的任意子實驗搜索也有積極的意義，因為知道有(或者沒有)特定的量子反常，對實驗系統或者材料中可以實現哪些具體的拓撲序，是壹個非常強的約束。

21301018.label: Realisation of objectives
21301018.value: This project aims to theoretically investigate quantitative bulk-boundary relations for 3D symmetry-protected topological phases, when the surface is in a topologically ordered state. Different symmetries are considered. Overall, the objectives are achieved with satisfactory results, though some questions remain open for further study. Details are given below. 1. The first and third objectives were studied almost simultaneously, enabled by gauging the fermion parity and turning a fermionic system into a bosonic system. The case of fermionic systems with only mirror symmetry was investigated by the folding approach, proposed by the PI and collaborators in an earlier work. We obtained a Z16-valued anomaly indicator and established the correspondence, which are published in Paper 4 in Part C. When internal symmetries were concerned, we studied the bulk topological properties and topological invariants using field theoretical approach and the approach of three-loop braiding statistics. Novel types of loop braiding statistics were identified. Results are published in Paper 1 and 3 in Part C. The boundary properties and correspondence in the presence of both mirror and internal symmetries turn out technically hard. While attempted, the general cases remain unclear to us. Some explicit results were obtained on the example of a system with both the mirror and a Z2 internal symmetry. In addition, we also studied a related problem of the so-called “non-Abelian” 2D symmetry-protected topological states by the gauging and field theoretical approaches. The results are published in Paper 2 in Part C. 2. For objective 2, we worked out the quantitative bulk-boundary relations for both bosonic and fermionic systems with Lie groups U(1), SU(2) and SO(3) and mirror symmetry. The fermionic cases correspond to the mirror counterparts of the ten-fold symmetry classes in the presence of interaction. These anomaly indicators and bulk-boundary relations are published in Paper 6 in Part C.

21301018.label: Major findings and research outcome
21301018.value: 1. A series of quantitative bulk-boundary relations, serving as indicators of the quantum anomaly of the surface, were derived and published in Phys. Rev. Research 2, 023339 (2020) and Phys. Rev. B 104, 075111 (2021). Quantum anomaly and bulk-boundary correspondences are of fundamental importance in condensed matter physics. We first studied 2D fermionic topological orders in the presence of the mirror symmetry. It was known that certain mirror symmetry enriched fermionic topological orders carried quantum anomaly and had to live on the surface of 3D topological crystalline superconductors. We derived a Z16-valued anomaly indicator to quantitively characterize the quantum anomalies of fermionic mirror-symmetric topological order and the corresponding 3D bulk of symmetry-protected topological states. Then, we generalized the study to anomaly indicators and bulk-boundary correspondences of bosonic and fermionic systems in the ten-fold symmetry classes of fermions, with time-reversal replaced by mirror, which host additional continuous symmetries like U(1), SU(2), or SO(3). Bulk topological invariants and a complete set of anomaly indicators were derived. 2. New types of non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics that characterize the bulk of a class of 3D fermionic symmetry-protected topological states were identified and published in Nature Communications 12, 3191 (2021). Fractional statistics, in particular, the so-called non-Abelian statistics, is one of the most intriguing features of topological phases in 2D. In three dimensions, loop-like extensive objects can also carry fractional statistics. In this work, we systematically studied a class of three-loop braiding statistics, emerging in 3D interacting fermion systems coupled to an Abelian gauge field. We discovered new types of non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics that must come hand-in-hand with fermionic particle statistics. We also used these three-loop braiding statistics to classify fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases with Abelian unitary symmetries.

21301018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21301018.value: There are still open questions on bulk-boundary correspondence of three dimensional fermionic symmetry protected topological states. Explicit surface topological orders of those three-dimensional fermionic bulk characterized by non-Abelian three-loop braiding statistics have not been constructed, although the general formalism has recently been proposed. Looking for explicit surface topological orders and studying their properties would clarify the corresponding quantum anomaly and symmetry properties of fermionic topological order in general. In addition, recently there are theoretical interests in understanding generalized symmetries beyond group, namely categorical symmetries. I am interested in extending the current research to the quantum anomaly of categorical symmetries, as well as the analogous concept of symmetry-protected topological states.

21301018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21301018.value: Symmetry and topology can show intriguing interplay in quantum many-body systems, leading to the discovery of topological insulators, topological superconductors and many other novel quantum matter. One of the key features in topological phases of matter is the so-called bulk-boundary correspondence, a deep connection between bulk and boundary properties. While the existence of such connections is well known, quantitative relations are rare. In this regard, we worked out a series of quantitative bulk-boundary relations for a class of quantum many-body systems. That is, we obtained quantitative characterization of the bulk and boundary, and established a series of equations between bulk and boundary quantities, for the class of boundaries that themselves are also in a topological state. These relations also serve as the anomaly indicators for the boundary states, because if the bulk is nontrivial, the boundary cannot be standalone. Our results provide a quantitative way to judge if a boundary can be properly split off.

21301818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301818.value: Hybrid, low-dimensional systems are at the forefront of modern scientific research. Moreover, recent interests in novel topological states of matter have reinvigorated the field, and placed heavy interest on combining one- and two-dimensional materials with superconductivity. Graphene still remains a flagship material to form such hybrid systems as is evidenced by the strong ongoing effort towards making devices, focused in particular on breakthroughs in quantum computing and quantum information. This proposal will focus on a key element in quantum information: a reliable, on-chip source of entangled electrons. Successful previous works have used a nanowire-based, superconductor-two quantum dot Cooper Pair splitter design to generate pairs of entangled electrons. However, while efficiency has been demonstrated, such devices lack consistent tunability, scalability, and entangled pairs have only been generated at distances of few 100nm apart. Graphene devices even based on the same superconductor-two quantum dot design are capable of overcoming all of the above issues. Already, design-based tunability has been demonstrated. The roadmap towards scalability and long distance entangled pair separation is clear; with electron pair separations over 1 micron easily supported by theory. However, recent demonstration of superconductivity in the quantum Hall (QH) regime opens up a possibility of a different entangler design; one capable of generating entangled electron pairs with high efficiency on macroscopic scales. In QH regime the supercurrent is supported by counter propagating currents contained in opposite edges of a graphene crystal. Superconductivity and entanglement is facilitated via hybrid modes along the superconductor-graphene interface. Accessing the edge states would give one a source of entangled electrons. Previous work on conventional Josephson junction devices already showed that the superconducting QH edge states can be separated by up to 4.5um. While not macroscopic, such distances are already on the order of the size of modern 4-5 qubit systems. Moreover, separation distances over 100 micrometers have been postulated. This project’s ultimate goal is to demonstrate such superconducting quantum Hall edge state-based entangler. Starting with the conventional design, the project first aims to demonstrate super-micron entanglement; and to achieve near unity efficiency allowing us to evaluate the degree of entanglement. Further focus will be on QH edge state devices. The superconducting edges will be accessed by normal-metal contacts. Initially, entangled pair generation will be measured via conduction resonances corresponding to resonances of the hybrid modes. Finally, shot-noise measurements will be performed to demonstrate Cooper Pair splitting. 混合低維繫統正處於現代科學研究的最前沿。而且，近來對新穎拓撲物態的研究也使該領域重新煥發活力，並對一維、二維材料與超導的結合產生了濃厚的興趣。石墨烯仍然是形成這種混合系統的旗艦材料，目前研究人員正在投入大量持續的努力來製造相關設備，尤其試圖在量子計算和量子信息上尋求突破。本提案將重點關注量子信息中的一個關鍵要素：一個可靠的、芯片上的糾纏電子源。先前的工作成功利用基於納米線的超導體 – 雙量子點庫伯對分離器來產生成對的糾纏電子。然而，雖然這種裝置效率很好，但是缺乏一致的可調性，可擴展性，並且只能產生相距幾百納米的糾纏對。利用相同的超導體 – 雙量子點設計，基於石墨烯的器件就能夠克服所有上述問題。目前，可調性已經得到了證實。對可擴展性和長距離糾纏對產生的證實也清晰可見； 超過1微米的糾纏電子對分離也很好的獲得了理論的支持。最近，在量子霍爾（QH）體系中觀測到的超導現像開啟了一種不同的設計糾纏器的路徑；這種設計能夠在宏觀尺度上高效率的產生糾纏電子對。在QH體系中，超導電流在石墨烯晶體的兩個邊界的反向傳播。在超導體 - 石墨烯界面上，電子的混合模式促成了超導和糾纏。這些邊界態可以被看成一個糾纏電子源。以前在常規約瑟夫森結器件上的工作已經表明，超導QH邊界態可以分開高達4.5微米。雖然不是宏觀的，但這種距離已經達到了現代4-5個量子比特系統的大小。此外，超過100微米的分離也被猜想過。本項目的最終目標是展示這種基於超導量子霍爾邊緣狀態的糾纏器。從傳統設計開始，本項目首先旨在展示超微米尺度的糾纏；並實現接近百分之百的效率，使我們能夠評估糾纏的程度。進一步，我們研究QH邊緣狀態器件。超導邊緣態的測量將通過接入普通金屬觸點進行。糾纏對的產生將通過對應於混合模式共振的電導測量進行。
