21606918.label: Major findings and research outcome
21606918.value: A major goal in forensic voice comparison research is to evaluate the evidential value of various speech features under forensically relevant conditions. This project sought to determine the population statistics and evidential strength of ten voice quality (VQ) acoustic parameters (five spectral tilt parameters and five additive noise parameters, and combinations of them), using speech samples with match vs. mismatch in speech style and contemporaneous vs. non-contemporaneous recordings. Results show that 1) in general, individual VQ parameters (e.g. H1-H2, cepstral peak prominence) performed rather poorly in distinguishing speakers, with mostly high log-likelihood-ratio cost (Cllr) values and equal error rates (EERs) regardless of whether non-contemporaneous recordings or mismatch in speech style was involved. 2) No single VQ parameter appears to stand out from the others. This suggest that individual VQ parameters alone provide little speaker-discriminatory information. 3) System validity improves slightly or considerably when the five spectral tilt measures or the five additive noise measures were combined as input. These findings are in line with previous findings that maximal speaker discrimination is often achieved using a combination of complementary speech features rather than single features, and that systems with more non-overlapping parameters as input may lead to higher system validity. 4) The combined additive noise measures consistently outperformed the combined spectral tilt measures, especially when both speech style mismatch and non-contemporaneous recordings were involved (which are common in forensic contexts). This suggests that additive noise measures carry more speaker-specific information and higher evidential strength for FVC. 5) However, having more parameters as input does not necessarily lead to better performance, as reflected in our findings that adding the combined spectral tilt measures to the combined additive noise measures yielded worse system performances. This reveals that spectral tilt measures and additive noise measures may provide overlapping or even conflicting information for discriminating speakers. 6) VQ parameters performed worse in this study on Australian English than a previous study on Standard Southern British English, potentially due to methodological differences as discussed in publication #1. 7) non-contemporaneous and speech style mismatch general led to worse performance. All these key findings and relevant detailed discussion are included in publications #1 and #2.

21606918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21606918.value: This research project focused on long-term voice quality acoustics. A logical follow-up lies in how these parameters may be combined with other speech features (e.g. formant frequencies; Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients) to achieve better speaker discrimination. Preliminary analysis is in progress. Besides, during the project period, a large amount of speech samples (75 speakers x 4 recordings = 300 recordings) have already been pre-processed (segmentation, labelling, and documentation), and future studies may focus on other acoustic parameters using the same dataset in this project so that the results will be directly comparable. Preliminary data on the speakers’ fundamental frequency and formant frequencies have already been extracted fur further analysis. Another possible extension is to examine whether short-term variation in voice quality may provide sufficient speaker-idiosyncratic information for forensic voice comparison, and how the evidential strength of various short-term voice quality acoustic parameters may be affected by vowel quality. This will involve further processing of the existing recordings and formulation of new research questions. A new research proposal can be developed based on this research direction.

21606918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21606918.value: Voice quality (e.g. breathy voice, creaky voice) has been reported to be one of the most useful and popular speech features for identifying speakers in forensic cases. However, few empirical studies have tested this claim. Besides, voice quality is typically analyzed auditorily based on subjective judgements by experts, and the process is non-transparent, non-reproducible, and susceptible to cognitive bias and human errors. This project involves analysis of voice quality acoustic parameters in the hope of 1) transforming the categorical auditory-based labels into continuous variables whose evidential strength can be assessed quantitatively; and 2) determining if voice quality of our speech is sufficiently speaker-specific to be useful in forensic contexts as usually claimed. Results show that voice quality acoustic parameters generally performed rather poorly in distinguishing speakers, especially when the speech samples analyzed involved different speaking styles and were separated by approximately two weeks. The findings have clear practical implications: forensic analysts should be cautious when using voice quality acoustic parameters in forensic voice comparison casework, and these parameters may at best be used with other speech features in forensic analysis of voice.

21608818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21608818.value: In most of the literature on mechanism design, two important assumptions are made. First, agents have a given amount of private information and their incentives to acquire more information are unmodeled. Second, the payment by an agent depends only on his report and not on the realized valuation. However, in many important practical settings, these assumptions do not apply. For example, in the sale of financial or business assets, firstly potential buyers often perform due diligence to investigate the quality and compatibility of the assets before submitting offers. Moreover, it is costly to acquire information. The legal and accounting costs of performing due diligence often amount to millions of dollars. Secondly, values of the auctioned assets are contractible. Indeed, when selling a company to an acquirer or soliciting venture capital, equity and other securities are commonly used. Other examples include spectrum auctions, highway building contracts, lead-plaintiff auctions, authors selling publishing rights and sports associations selling broadcasting rights. We call mechanisms in which the payment by an agent is contingent on his ex-post payoff contingent mechanisms (in contrast to cash mechanisms). Surprisingly, few studies have considered contingent mechanisms with information acquisition. In this project, I will compare the performance of different contingent mechanisms and study the design of optimal contingent mechanisms when agents can covertly acquire information at some cost. These theoretical exercises help us understand the degree to which the characteristics of optimal mechanisms depend on the above two assumptions, and provide guidance for the use of different mechanisms in practice. More specifically, I first consider security-bid auctions in which the seller restricts the security design to an ordered set and uses a standard auction format (e.g., first- or second-price auction). The preliminary result shows that auctions using steeper securities provide lower incentives for agents to acquire information. Furthermore, this difference in incentives to acquire information may overturn the revenue ranking among security designs in earlier work. I will then study the design of optimal linear and non-linear contingent mechanisms, respectively, when information is endogenous. 研究機制設計的大部分文獻都採用了以下兩個重要的假設。首先，文獻中通常假設代理人的私有信息是外生的，且不考慮代理人獲取額外信息的激勵。其次，代理人支付的金額僅依賴於他最初的報告，而與最終實現的價值無關。但在許多重要的實際問題中，這兩個假設並不成立。 例如，在金融和商業資產的交易中，潛在的買家在競標前會謹慎調查資產的價值和兼容性。調查的成本也常常高達數百萬美元。其次，資產最終實現的價值可以被寫入合約。例如，在公司收購中，股票和其他證券常常被作為支付手段。類似的例子還有頻譜拍賣，高速公路的建造合約，書籍出版權的銷售和體育賽事轉播權的銷售等。我們把這種支付金額依賴於最終實現價值的機制稱為或有機制（與之相對應的是現金機制）。 現有文獻幾乎沒有在代理人可以以一定的成本獲取信息的情形下研究過或有機制。在這項研究中，我將在這一情形下比較不同的或有機制的表現，並研究最優或有機制的設計。這一研究可以幫助我們理解以上兩個假設對最優機制的影響，並對實際中不同機制的應用給出指導性建議。具體而言，我首先研究了證券拍賣（即拍賣的參加者只能用預先給定的證券類型競標）。初步的研究結果表明，選用更加陡峭的證券會減少競標者獲取信息的激勵，從而減少委託人的收入。其次，我將會研究如果代理人可以以一定的成本獲取信息，最優或有機制具有哪些特徵。

21608818.label: Realisation of objectives
21608818.value: The first objective of this project is to compare security-bid auctions in which the seller restricts the security design to an ordered set and uses a standard auction format (e.g., first- or second-price auction). To complete this objective, we first study agents’ incentives to acquire information under different ordered sets of securities. We show that for either first- or second-price auction, steeper securities give agents a lower marginal return to information, and all securities give agents a lower marginal return to information than cash. Next, we compare the seller’s expected revenues under different ordered sets of securities. This project is closely related to DeMarzo, Kremer and Skrzypacz (AER, 2005), who also study security-bid auctions. They show that when the information possessed by agents is exogenous, steeper securities yield higher revenues and all security-bid auctions yield higher revenues than cash auctions. However, this result may not hold with costly information acquisition. The seller’s expected revenue is given by the difference between the expected surplus and the information rents accruing to the agents. On the one hand, steeper securities yield lower information rents, given the accuracy of information. On the other hand, steeper securities lead to less accurate information, reducing the expected surplus, as the allocation becomes less efficient ex-post. As a result, steeper securities may yield lower revenues and security-bid auctions may yield lower revenues than cash auctions as the agents acquire less accurate information. We provide an example where the cash-bid auction generates higher expected revenue than the equity-bid auction. The second objective of this project is to design optimal or revenue-maximizing linear (contingent) mechanisms. In a linear mechanism, the payment by an agent linearly depends on his ex-post payoff. In other words, an agent pays in all cash, all stock, or a mixture of the two. We characterize the revenue-maximizing linear mechanism. The optimal linear mechanism allocates the asset efficiently conditional on the private information ex-post. An agent pays if and only if he wins. The winner pays in cash if their expected values are above a threshold and pays in stock if their expected values are below the threshold. The threshold decreases as the marginal cost of acquiring additional information increases. As an application, our results provide a new theoretical explanation for the choice of payment methods in mergers and acquisitions based on information acquisition. Our model predicts that the use of stock bids is negatively associated with merge synergies. We empirically test this prediction using the Securities Data Company (SDC) Platinum’s merge and acquisition data, the stock price data from the Center for Research in Security Price (CRSP), and Compustat data. Consistent with the model prediction, we find that deals paid entirely in stock have lower synergy values, measured by take-over premiums or abnormal returns around announcement dates, than the other merge deals. More importantly, our model predicts that stock payments are more likely than cash payments when it is easier for bidders to acquire information about the seller. To explore this information-based implication, we use geographical proximity and recent seasoned equity offering of sellers as proxies of bidders’ information about sellers. Consistent with the model prediction, we find all information proxies are positively associated with the use of stock payments.

21608818.label: Major findings and research outcome
21608818.value: The project has three main findings. First, we consider auctions with ordered securities in which the seller restricts the security design to an ordered set and uses a first- or second-price auction. We show that steeper securities give agents lower marginal returns to information and may yield lower revenues. Second, we study linear mechanisms in which payments linearly depend on the asset’s realized value. We show that the revenue-maximizing linear mechanism assigns the asset efficiently. The winner pays in cash if their expected values are above a threshold and pays in stock if their expected values are below the threshold. The threshold decreases as the marginal cost of acquiring additional information increases. Finally, the theoretical results about the optimal linear mechanism imply that stock payments are associated with lower merge synergies and lower information acquisition costs. We empirically test the implications and find consistent results. This project produced one research paper, “Security-bid Auctions with Information Acquisition,” which is available on SSRN. This paper has been presented at six international conferences (please see part C for details) and at seminars at Nanjing University, Indian Statistical Institute, Sun Yat-sen University, Korean University, and Seoul National University. Later, I will submit a more polished version of this paper to a journal for publication. Multiple undergraduate and graduate students worked with me as research assistants during the project to gain research experience (please see part C for details).

21608818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21608818.value: The first main finding of this project shows that security design affects the seller?s revenue. A natural question arises: Which security design maximized the seller?s revenue? In this project, we focus on linear mechanisms, which rule out some commonly used securities such as debt. Therefore, it is worthwhile to study the revenue-maximizing non-linear mechanisms in the future. Throughout the project, we assume that the seller can restrict the set of securities used by the bidders. In some applications, such as selling publishing rights or soliciting venture capitals, the bidders can choose which securities to offer. DeMarzo, Kremer and Skrzypacz (AER, 2005) studied this type of informal auction when the bidders? information is exogenous. In the future, it is interesting to understand the equilibrium of the informal auction when the bidders? information is endogenous.

21608818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21608818.value: Consider, for example, the sale of financial or business assets. First, potential buyers often perform due diligence to investigate the quality and compatibility of the assets before submitting offers. Moreover, it is costly to acquire information. The legal and accounting costs of performing due diligence often amount to millions of dollars. Second, the values of the auctioned assets are contractible. Indeed, when selling a company to an acquirer, equity and other securities are commonly used. Surprisingly, few studies have considered this type of security-bid auction where potential buyers can gather information at some cost. The current project fills this. In addition to improving our theoretical understanding of this question, the results of this project also speak to practice. In particular, the results of this project provide economic insight into the following two applications: bankruptcy procedures and mergers and acquisitions (M&A). In these two applications, earlier studies have advocated the importance of non-cash bids in relaxing potential buyers? financial constraints or raising the seller?s revenue but ignored the impacts of non-cash bids on bidders? incentives to investigate the quality and compatibility of the assets. The results of this project thus provide guidance for structuring the selling procedure of M&A and the bankruptcy procedure.

21609618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21609618.value: 專制政權中的環保示威運動與政治轉變：越南

21609618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21609618.value: The project seeks to capture the role and consequences of the growing number of environmental protests in Vietnam, which are widely reported in the local press and which suggest significant change in the state-society relationship in the 14th most populous country in the world. So far, environmental protests in Vietnam have surprisingly drawn very little attention in the academic literature. Reports about environmental protests have become common in the Vietnamese press, which is surprising in an authoritarian regime in which protests are generally viewed as a threat and the media is controlled by the state. Preliminary research shows that quite a few reports are primarily factual and are not biased against the protesters. Instead, the companies responsible for the environmental pollution or local officials are often blamed for the protests. However, in some instances, the reporting changes significantly and becomes heavily biased against the environmental activists. This demonstrates that there are different competing discourses surrounding environmental protests about which relatively little is known. The project will fill this gap. It will collect all reports about environmental protests in major Vietnamese newspapers since the early 2000s and use an interpretive content analysis to determine different discourses in the texts. This will be combined with case studies of three to four protests that were reported very differently in the press. The field research will primarily rely on interviews with journalists and editors as well as government officials and activists, who will provide background information about what may have been left out of the reports. This will allow the researcher to determine differences in the media perception from those of observers and participants. The changing discourse of environmental protests will make it possible to indicate political changes in the country and the context in which those occur. The research will make significant academic, methodological and practical contributions. Theoretically, the research will contribute to the discussion over whether protests are a threat to one-party rule or help strengthen the regime by providing important information about societal grievances. Methodologically, the research applies an interpretative framework that is particularly suited to media sources that do not reflect an authoritative source of information but are rather state-approved representation of events such as protests. Practically, the project will provide new evidence about the changing nature and discourses of environmental protests that can provide an in-depth understanding of growing contention that is useful to scholars as well as policy-makers. 是次研究嘗試探討不斷成長及增加的環保示威運動在越南的角色和影響，相關運動受到本地媒體廣泛報導，意味在全球人口排名第14的越南，國家與社會關係正在明顯變化。到目前為止，學術文獻對越南環保示威運動的關注卻少得令人驚訝。 環保示威運動經常出現在越南媒體，對於一個視抗議遊行為威脅而對大眾傳媒嚴加控制的專制政權，這實在是令人意想不到。初步研究發現，不少報導都是作事實陳述，而未對示威者存有偏見。相反，要為環境污染負責的公司或是當地官員則經常指責示威者。然而，在某些情況下，報導會徹底改變，趨向嚴厲指責環保人士。這證明了，圍繞環保示威運動有意味相悖的論述，而對有關論述卻所知甚少。 為了填補這一空白，是次研究會搜集自20年代初期，出現在越南主要報刊有關環保示威運動的所有報導，用詮釋內容研究法(Interpretive content analysis)分析不同的論述。包括研究三至四個報導截然不同的示威活動。實地考察主要是透過訪問記者、編輯、政府官員以及環保人士以取得可能遺漏未報的背景資料，使到研究員能從中確定觀察者和參與者在媒體感知(media perception)上的差異。不斷變化的環保示威運動論述，可能在暗示該國正在經歷政治轉變及其發生的背景。 本研究將對學術理論、研究方法和理論實踐均作出重大貢獻。理論上，研究有助討論示威運動是否對一黨統治構成威脅？還是給政權發放社會不滿的重要訊息從而更鞏固其權力？研究方法方面，詮釋研究模式特別適用於未能反映權威訊息的媒體資料，但到底也是國家默許報導的事件，如遊行抗議。實踐上，研究結果能對環保示威運動本質和論述上的轉變提供新佐證，令學者和政策制定者對相關爭論有更深入而實用的理解。

21614018.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21614018.value: 天崩地坼：太平天國時期的文學與文化

21614018.label: Project Objectives
21614018.value: In seeking to understand how political conflicts and cultural upheavals mutually enforce each other, I explore the dialectic relationship between utopia and dystopia, religion and violence, imagery and rhetoric, as well as trauma and memory. I study the evolution of the Taiping textual universe that offers a millenarian promise. I examine the metamorphosis of the Qing propagandistic discourse, which seeks to combat the Taiping ideology but inadvertently presents nineteenth century reality as a dystopia. I explore a late Qing elite’s response, registered through numerous temporal layers, to traumatic experiences in his multi-volume, meticulously edited, and fragmented diary manuscript written during the war. I investigate a full-length literati novel of strong autobiographical impulses, to investigate the transformation of the tradition of literati novel in mid-nineteenth century. I inquire into the liminal zone between illusion and reality in fantastic representations of the war in fiction and serialized stories on late Qing newspapers. I study numerous late nineteenth century plays that represent the war and individual’s experiences in theatrical forms to come to terms with individual’s traumatic experiences.

21614018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21614018.value: “天崩地坼：太平天國時期的文學與文化”研究中國文學與文化在十九世紀後半葉的重要轉型。太平天國戰爭與其引起的慘重傷亡使其成為十九世紀中國的一個標誌性事件。通過探討戰時與戰後產生的宣傳文學、小說、日記、戲曲等多種材料，本研究結合歷史、文學，以及書籍史的研究，著眼於敘事過程中所呈現出的時間多樣性及這些敘述作為政治與個人表述的意義。總體而言，以太平天國為中心的文學與文化對明清時期文學經典的改變與對西方文化的改寫呈現出兩個向度：一方面是明清時期文化傳統的斷裂與收束，另一方面是受西方影響下中國烏托邦話語的崛起。

21614018.label: Major findings and research outcome
21614018.value: My project is a broad-ranging, multigenre, and multimedia study of writings produced during and in relation to the Taiping Civil War. As Anders Engberg-Pedersen states, “While clearly marked as a historical event, war was nevertheless not a historical fact but an elusive phenomenon, a blurry object that required a new aesthetics, a new set of forms, new morphologies,” and thus literature should be “read as a way of dealing with the complex epistemic regime of war.” Though his observation is about the Napoleonic war, I find it is pertinent to our discussion. My research explores how narratives creatively reinvented topoi and literary themes to introduce new ideals of religious and political authorities and to make sense of individual’s existence in a tumultuous era in nineteenth century China. I have chosen to focus on texts of political, archeological, and/or literary significance. On a synchronic level, I show that as expressions produced at particular historical instances, these writings exemplify shifting expectations of the social and aesthetic functions of major narrative genres. On a diachronic level, I track networks of allusions to show that utopian and dystopian visions, nostalgic lamentations, and fantastic imaginations know no temporal and political boundaries in literary engagements with calamitous events. The conflicting yet mutually generative rhetoric and aesthetic modes in the writings I study unsettle simplistic dichotomies: if one of the modes is despair, it must be understood in the context of elation, just as orthodoxy must be seen in relation to heterodoxy, and despondency in relation to masochistic pleasure. Ultimately, we see the emergence of a culture characterized by apocalyptic sensibilities and yearnings for transcendence on both ideological and personal levels. The writings that came out of this culture are examples of what Hayden White calls the “artistic treatment of a real event … [that] transcends the truth,” in that they are allegories not only of history but also of the extensive change of the late imperial literary and cultural paradigms.

21614018.value: Based on this project, I have developed a second project titled "A Chinese Remix: Visions of the World in Early Nineteenth-Century Missionary Publications."

21614018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21614018.value: This project studies the literary and cultural aspects of the Taiping Civil War, one of the most destructive civil wars in human history, to show the unraveling of the late imperial literary and cultural tradition and to rethink the beginning of Chinese literary modernity. This book makes a significant contribution to our understanding of Chinese literature and culture from late imperial period to the modern times.

21614618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21614618.value: 此研究項目以中國西南部的的貴州省為案例，探討被視作邊远地區的內地省份如何通過文化遺產打造品牌，進行跨地域的文化推廣。自21世紀初，貴州省將“多彩貴州”作為其走向世界的文化品牌，希望通過當地的民族文化和自然景觀作為其特有的遺產，幫助貴州扭轉刻板印象、提升知名度。在過去的十年裡，政府、商界、媒體紛紛將“多彩貴州”策略性地用於發展文化創意產業，增進跨區域的聯繫。 本研究課題通過人類學的視角探究“多彩貴州”的品牌打造，尤其關注地方精英和民眾如何共同參與日常文化工作。基於參與式觀察、半結構性訪談、小組焦點座談、和媒體材料分析，此項目試圖討論少數民族文化遺產傳承人和表演者如何參與到文化產品的設計和生產當中。除了最主要的田野調查地點貴州省省會城市貴陽之外，也將放眼貴州與香港在商貿合作基礎之上的文化宣傳和交流。 在視覺識別和文化體驗最為引人注目的當下，本課題通過民族志的方式批判性地思考在後社會主義背景下當代中國的區域性文化發展問題，也將針對貧困地區的文化政策進行適時、深入的探究。此種結合了文化遺產傳承的省份品牌打造將提供一個觀察全球化語境下國家和市場力量在當地社會影響的特殊視角。

21614618.label: Realisation of objectives
21614618.value: Research objectives have been mostly met by advancing the understanding of the intertwining roles of culture and economy in contemporary China through the case of Guizhou's provincial branding, creative industries, and its bilateral cooperation with Hong Kong. However, the pandemic has forestalled the possibility of conducting fieldwork. Thus, first-hand data collection was only undertaken in Guizhou in the summer of 2019. To overcome this challenge, I could only rely on social media and online reports. In addition, I was originally planning to hire my research assistant due to her expertise on related topics for a much longer period of time. But I was not able to extend her employment due to COVID-19 as she was away from Hong Kong.

21614618.label: Major findings and research outcome
21614618.value: I have published a co-authored article in Social Anthropology at an earlier stage of this project, which critically rethinks how Guizhou’s “remoteness” is being recuperated in an age of increased connectivity in highly visual and marketable ways. I have also finished a solo-authored article that was published by the International Journal of Heritage Studies; based on my summer fieldwork in Guizhou, it argues that edutainment -- the combination of educational and entertainment activities -- offers new learning opportunities about intangible heritage to a public audience and younger generations, while it inevitably entails transformations of traditional cultural forms and practice. From 2020 to 2021 when fieldwork has not been feasible, I have used this grant to refine and finalise my book manuscript entitled "Ethnic Branding in Late Socialist China: Buyi and the Paradox of Difference" and it is now under review by the University of Washington Press.

21614618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21614618.value: Further research is needed for exploring the "outward" reach of Guizhou's local policies and its manifestation, for example, by a tendency to promote Guizhou's heritage and tourism beyond regional and national borders. In addition, since "heritage" has been a key term that local stakeholders in Guizhou engage for the past two decades, it will be important to glean out the trajectory of how this term is conceptualised and practiced over this time period.

21614618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21614618.value: This project uses China’s southwestern province Guizhou to exemplify how one of China’s most socioeconomically marginal and remote regions strategizes on cultural branding that promotes heritage-related industries. Since the early 2000s, the provincial government has officially proposed “Colorful Guizhou” as a cultural brand to “go global.” This branding aims to highlight Guizhou’s spectacular ethnic diversity and a life-nourishing environment as its distinct heritage, which could help make over Guizhou’s stereotypical image of a backwater region by gaining visibility in larger spheres. Over the past decade, the local government, business partners, and media workers have been capitalizing on “Colorful Guizhou” to create opportunities in developing cultural industries and in bolstering trans-regional connections including, most recently, the One Belt One Road Initiative. This research approaches the branding of “Colorful Guizhou” from an anthropological perspective, by focusing on the middle ground where various cultural workers engage with cultural development in contemporary China. It sheds light on the negotiations between state agendas, market forces, and local societies amid China’s globalization and socioeconomic restructuring. It contributes to a timely and in-depth understanding of cultural policies that hold special significance for a province like Guizhou striving for poverty alleviation, national integration, and global connection.

22302718.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22302718.value: 對混響聲場的主動操控

22302718.label: Project Objectives
22302718.value: To investigate and analyze the performance of the existing spatial sound modulator using both experimental and computational methods.
rows: To investigate and analyze the performance of the existing spatial sound modulator using both experimental and computational methods.

22302718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22302718.value: In this project, we apply adaptive wave shaping to acoustic sound. In particular, we aim to achieve active, reconfigurable control of reverberating airborne sound covering a reasonably broad bandwidth in the audible frequency regime. Reverberating cavity is an important class of complex medium. A cavity is in the reverberating regime when frequency is sufficiently high, so that owing to the intrinsic spectral broadening, neighboring eigenmodes can no longer be individually distinguished in measurement. Reverberating sound usually manifests as a disordered wavefield, with a spatial pattern resembling a laser speckle. This characteristic means that despite its commonplace in daily life, its control remains extremely difficult in most situations. A recent breakthrough in optics known as adaptive wave shaping brings new possibility to tackle this challenge. The complexity of reverberating sound is underlain by the richness of eigenmodes, which are in essence standing waves. The interference of these standing waves can be altered to change the spatial pattern of reverberating sound. This can be achieved by altering the phase of a sufficient number of these modes (standing waves) in specific way. To do so, we design and fabricate a device we denote “spatial sound modulator” (SSM), which is now within technological reach, thanks to the recent advance in planar acoustic metamaterials and acoustic metasurfaces. We have exploited the membrane-type acoustic metamaterial to realize an active-controlled reconfigurable acoustic metasurface as a phase-modulating SSM with two switchable states built in to each unit cell. Based on this recent development, we plan to conduct thorough study on the SSM’s capability in controlling reverberating sound, and aim to realize an improved SSM for the effective reshaping of a broadband sound field. 聲音的混響廣汎存在與日常生活中。一個足夠大的封閉腔體在頻率足夠高的情況下，其共振模態的分佈將會十分密集，相鄰共振模態對外部激勵的響應會在耗散的作用下相互重合而無法區分，這種狀態可稱之爲混響。由於一般來説混響聲場是一個在空間中無序分佈的聲場，其操控是極其困難的。 本課題的出發點是光學中最近提出的波前相位操控的方法。該方法在空間上為入射聲波的波前加入特定的相位，從而調控射后的波在空間中的干涉結果。我們將該方法拓展至聲學，進而實現對混響聲場空間分佈的調控。近期聲波超材料/超界面的發展使該目標的實現成爲可能。我們設計並製造基於聲波超材料的“空間聲場調控器”，並將對其原理、功能進行全面的探索的研究。

22302718.label: Realisation of objectives
22302718.value: The project objective is fully achieved. The project has achieved much more than the originally proposed objective. Based on the spatial sound modulator units, we have thoroughly characterized broadband phase-modulating capabilities. We have further experimentally achieved the effective control of our reverberating laboratory room’s impulse responses. In other words, we have successfully achieved the control of time-coherent transient sound at different instants and positions. We further analyzed the performance of the SSM using a numerical model derived from the properties of diffuse sound field, including mean free path, modal density, etc. The model shows that the control performance directly benefits from multiple scattering. The model is able to predict experimental results in our laboratory.

22302718.label: Summary of objectives addressed
22302718.value: Objectives Addressed Percentage achieved 1.To investigate and analyze the performance of the existing spatial sound modulator using both experimental and computational methods.Yes100%
rows: To investigate and analyze the performance of the existing spatial sound modulator using both experimental and computational methods.

22302718.label: Major findings and research outcome
22302718.value: We have thoroughly investigated the bandwidth of the existing membrane-type spatial sound modulators. We found that the units have impressive broadband phase-modulating capabilities - spanning 1/3 octave with a base frequency of 500 Hz. This broadband phase-modulating capabilities enable the experimental realization of coherent control of a transient sound field in a reverberating toom This is achieved as the reshaping of spatiotemporal impulse acoustic response of the said room. Our experiments showed that the successful suppression or enhancement of sound amplitude at any chosen time instants at any location within the room. A transient-scattering numerical model is developed to capture the time-domain multiple scattering of sound in the parametrized reverberating room. The model is based on the properties of the diffuse sound field in the room, including mean free paths, Q-factors, etc. The model shows that the control performance benefits from multiple scattering of the diffuse sound and it can predict the performance of the spatiotemporal control of the spatial sound modulators. These findings are summarized in a paper "Controlling the Spatiotemporal Response of Transient Reverberating Sound" which is now under review in Physical Review Applied (see Part C). Other than the abovementioned findings, the project funding also partially supported several other investigations in the PI's group, which are published in Nature Physics, Science Bulletin, and Physical Review Applied. See Part C for the outcomes.

22302718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22302718.value: Our results and findings show that the spatial sound modulator's capabilities in wavefield shaping go significantly beyond controlling steady-state at single frequencies, as we reported in PNAS 115, 6638-6643 (2018). By exploring them for time-coherent polychromatic manipulations, the control of transient acoustic responses is attained for the first time. We expect the results and findings in spatiotemporal acoustic wavefield shaping to lay the foundation for more advanced adaptive control of complex sound fields. It can benefit an abundance of applications in acoustic engineering, such as adaptive indoor acoustic engineering, noise suppression, real-time sound-scaping, and acoustic illusions.

22302718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22302718.value: Despite the impressive development of acoustic metamaterials in the past decade, their effects are restricted to the manipulation of steady acoustic excitations in the frequency domain. This severely limits their application potentials to real-life acoustic scenarios, wherein the sound fields are almost always time-varying. This project successfully achieved the time-domain manipulation of complex sound using metamaterial-based spatial sound modulators. We have experimentally achieved the adaptive reshaping of the transient acoustic responses, which lays the foundation for real-time sound-scaping applications, which may have tremendous potential in indoor acoustic engineering, precision noise abatement, and so on.

22303518.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22303518.value: 基於核的眾數回歸算法的數學分析

22303518.label: Project Objectives
22303518.value: A learning theory framework will be introduced to study the consistency and robustness of regularized kernel modal regression algorithms. We shall first derive fast learning rates for the excess modal regression risk when varying Gaussian kernel is employed. To handle large-scale data, we shall then consider the combination of regularized kernel modal regression with distributed scheme, localized approach or Nystroem subsampling, respectively. The rates of convergence for the induced learning algorithms will be derived and compared to the original algorithm. An additive model framework will be employed to analyze kernel modal regression algorithms for high-dimensional data, where a mixed norm penalty will be adopted to induce sparsity in the solution. We shall carry out consistency, robustness and sparsity analysis for the sparse additive modal regression scheme in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The convergence analysis of regularized kernel modal regression scheme will be extended to study infinite dimensional functional data. With the help of integral operators induced by the covariance kernel and the reproducing kernel, learning rates for prediction error will be derived. The estimation of mode function based on sparse and irregularly sampled functional data will also be considered and studied.

We shall carry out consistency, robustness and sparsity analysis for the sparse additive modal regression scheme in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.

The convergence analysis of regularized kernel modal regression scheme will be extended to study infinite dimensional functional data. With the help of integral operators induced by the covariance kernel and the reproducing kernel, learning rates for prediction error will be derived. The estimation of mode function based on sparse and irregularly sampled functional data will also be considered and studied.

22303518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22303518.value: Modal regression seeks the conditional mode of a response variable given a set of covariates, providing an alternative to mean regression and quantile regression in the presence of heavy-tailed noise, asymmetric noise or outliers. The goal of this project is to investigate theoretical properties of some kernel based modal regression schemes for large-scale and high-dimensional (even infinite dimensional) problems of learning theory. We shall first consider the large-scale problems by studying a regularized kernel modal regression scheme associated with varying Gaussian kernels and its combination with distributed learning scheme, localized approach or Nystroem subsampling method respectively, where consistency and robustness analysis for the induced learning algorithms will be carried out. We shall then study the impact of sparsity and robustness on generalization performance of sparse additive modal regression scheme in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS), which can be applied to high or ultra-high dimensional learning problems. An RKHS approach to functional linear modal regression will be studied, which allows covariates to be infinite dimensional functional data such as random curves or images. Learning rates will be derived for prediction error in terms of decay rates for eigenvalues of integral operators generated by reproducing kernel and covariance kernel. At last, the estimation of mode function based on sparse and irregularly sampled functional data will be considered. The mode function of random curves will preserve some important features that the mean function tends to average out of the data. 眾數回歸在給定一組協變量的情況下尋求反應變量的條件眾數，是存在重尾噪聲、不對稱噪聲或異常值時均值回歸和分位數回歸的替代方案。本項目的目標是研究一些基於核的眾數回歸算法在大規模及高維（甚至無窮維）學習問題中的理論性質。我們首先通過研究與變化高斯核相關的正則化核眾數回歸算法及其與分佈式學習算法、局部方法或Nystroem二次抽樣方法的結合來考慮大規模問題，并進行相應學習算法的一致性分析和穩健性分析。然後我們將考慮再生核希爾伯特空間中稀疏可加眾數回歸算法以及稀疏性和穩健性對該算法泛化性能的影響，并將其應用於高維或超高維學習問題。之後我們考慮函數型線性眾數回歸的再生核希爾伯特空間方法，其允許協變量為無窮維的函數型數據，如隨機曲線或圖像。預測誤差的學習率將依據由再生核及協方差核生成的積分算子的特征根衰減率導出。最後我們將考慮基於稀疏且不規則抽樣的函數型數據的眾數函數的估計。隨機曲線的眾數函數保留了數據中均值函數趨於平均掉的一些重要特征。

22303518.label: Realisation of objectives
22303518.value: All objectives in the development of mathematical theory for modal regression schemes have been achieved. In particular, we have introduced a novel learning theory framework to learn the conditional mode function nonparametrically based on both density kernel and reproducing kernel, which allows us to design scalable and robust machine learning algorithms to handle large-scale, high-dimensional (even infinite-dimensional) and noisy data in supervised learning problems. In regression problems, the goal is to learn an unknown function relating the response variable to a set of covariates while certain assumptions on the noise variable shall be imposed. Regression estimators usually settle for inferring a characterization of the unknown conditional distribution by shifting information based on a set of observations. Several commonly used characterizations of the conditional distribution include the conditional mean, the conditional median, the conditional quantile, and the conditional mode. It is well known that regression towards the conditional mean is effective when the noise is Gaussian or sub-Gaussian. And median or quantile regression is more robust in the presence of light-tailed noise or symmetric conditional distributions. However, modal regression has not been well understood in the statistical learning literature. In [1], we developed and analyzed learning algorithms generated by empirical risk minimization schemes, which incorporate kernel density estimation into the nonparametric modal regression problem. One of the most appealing features of modal regression lies in its robustness to heavy-tailed noise, skewed noise, and outliers. However, most existing research studies focused on modal linear regression or the estimation of local modes, which may not be enough in the current era of big data. We presented in [1] the first systematic statistical learning treatment on modal regression by devising the modal regression risk, characterizing its corresponding Bayes rule, and introducing its computationally tractable surrogates. We showed that the modal regression estimator can be pursued by maximizing a one-dimensional density estimator, while usually a possibly high-dimensional density was involved in the existing studies. We provided a detailed theoretical analysis regarding the modal regression risk consistency, the generalization risk consistency, and the function estimation ability of the proposed algorithms. All these findings unveiled that modal regression is closely related to correntropy-based regression when its scaling parameter tends to zero. In [4], we further studied modal regression when its scaling parameter tends to infinity, aiming to learn the conditional mean function robustly. We conducted the generalization error analysis of a regularized learning algorithm associated with varying Gaussian kernels to tackle supervised learning problems in the presence of heavy-tailed noise or outliers. We showed that the proposed algorithm can adaptively achieve the minimax optimal rate of convergence up to a logarithmic factor without knowing the smoothness of the regression function. We have gained insights into the theoretical properties and computational schemes of modal regression and the important roles of the two types of kernels in supervised learning algorithms. With the era of big data, we are also interested in theoretically understanding supervised learning algorithms for massive data, functional data, and high-dimensional data, respectively. In [2], we studied distributed pairwise learning algorithms with multi-penalty regularization to tackle large-scale datasets. Different from classical pointwise learning such as regression and classification, pairwise learning depends on the interaction among the sample pairs. Typical examples include ranking, preference learning, metric learning, AUC maximization, and the minimum error entropy principle. Meanwhile, the motivation for multi-penalty regularization stems from manifold learning, in which there are two regularization terms, one controlling the complexity of the hypothesis space and the other exploiting the geometry structure of the probability distribution that generates the examples. In [2], we applied the distributed learning method to reduce computational complexity caused by large-size unlabeled data and multiple parameters. Our results showed that the learning rate of the multi-penalty regularized pairwise learning algorithm can match the minimax optimal rate for classical regression if the size of subdataset is not too small and regularization parameters are chosen appropriately. For various diseases, patients may show signiﬁcant heterogeneity in response to treatments. During the past decades, biomedical research has been changing from "one-size-ﬁts-all" strategy to a precision medicine method, where the right treatment, for the right patient, and at the right time, will be prescribed. Typical tasks arising from precision medicine include individualized treatment rules, personalized dose ﬁnding, and dynamic treatment regimes. In [3], we presented an RKHS approach to learning optimal individualized treatment rules (ITR) based on functional covariates within the D-learning framework. Functional data refers to the data where each observation is a curve or a random function, which is quite common in healthcare data. The infinite dimensionality of the explanatory variable poses big challenges in both theoretical analysis and computational schemes of ITR learning algorithms. We derived fast rates of convergence for the prediction of the optimal ITR maximizing the expected clinical outcome. This deepened our understanding of kernel-based functional data learning and its application in precision medicine. In the high dimension low sample size (HDLSS) setting, the support vector machine (SVM) may suffer from "data piling" phenomena, that is, a large portion of data points are support vectors and they will pile up on top of each other while projected onto the normal vector of the separating hyperplane. Data piling may reduce generalizability and lead to suboptimal performance in the HDLSS setting, which is usually not desirable for a classifier. In [5], we considered large-margin unified machines (LUMs) for binary classification problems and investigate the consistency of kernel-based LUMs within the framework of learning theory. We provided quantitative convergence analysis for the kernel-based LUMs to estimate the excess misclassification error. We have better understood the challenges we will face in the high-dimensional classification problems.

22303518.label: Major findings and research outcome
22303518.value: In [1], we studied the problem of nonparametric modal regression within the framework of learning theory. We provided an empirical risk minimization framework for analyzing and implementing modal regression in the presence of heavy-tailed and skewed noises. We built the connection between the modal regression risk and the excess generalization error. We further showed the function estimation consistency and derived rates of convergence under mild conditions. We also discussed the implementation issues of modal regression as well as the selection of the tuning parameters. The efficiency of the proposed algorithm is illustrated by numerical experiments on real datasets. Following the idea of modal regression, we further discussed in [4] correntropy-based regression from information theoretic learning to tackle non-Gaussian noises. We investigated the theoretical properties of the learning algorithm generated by Tikhonov regularization schemes and Gaussian kernels. We derived the minimax optimal rates (up to a logarithmic factor) with the help of a tight upper bound for the uniform covering numbers of Gaussian reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and the explicit estimation of approximation error under a Sobolev smoothness condition. In [2], we adopted a divide-and-conquer strategy for pairwise learning with multi-penalty regularization to handle large-scale data efficiently. Under mild regularity conditions on the target function, we established the error bounds and derive the minimax optimal rates of the proposed distributed learning algorithms by choosing an appropriate number of local machines. We also discussed the benefit of unlabeled data to reduce the computational complexity in this setting. In [3], we considered the estimation of optimal individualized treatment rules based on infinite-dimensional functional covariates of patients, which shall be of great interest in precision medicine. We provided the rates of convergence for prediction under mild conditions, which are jointly determined by both the reproducing kernel and covariance kernel. We showed that the proposed algorithm can be conveniently implemented although the input data is intrinsically infinite-dimensional. In [5], we studied the problem of binary classification in the setting of high dimension and low sample size (HDLSS), where the classical support vector machine may suffer from data piling issues. We proposed a class of large-margin unified machines within the framework of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. We provided quantitative convergence analysis for the proposed algorithms to understand the challenges in this HDLSS setting.

22303518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22303518.value: The main component of our research is based on kernel methods, aiming to learn the conditional mode function within the framework of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. A potential further development is to investigate the theoretical properties and computational advantages of modal regression algorithms generated by deep neural networks, which is now one of the hottest topics in the community of machine learning. Another interesting topic is adopting (stochastic) gradient descent algorithms to solve the corresponding optimization problems arising in modal regression.

22303518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22303518.value: The goal of modal regression is to learn the conditional mode function based on a set of covariates, which provides an alternative to conventional supervised learning schemes such as mean regression and quantile regression. In this project, we design and study modal regression algorithms to tackle large-scale and high-dimensional (even infinite-dimensional) problems within the framework of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. We aim at a theoretically sound and computationally efficient framework for robust machine learning in the presence of heavy-tailed noises. The methods and techniques developed are applied to manifold learning and precision medicine.

22602918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22602918.value: 元代宮廷詩的特色與發展

22602918.label: Project Objectives
22602918.value: 從文學史的宏觀角度，梳理宮廷文學書寫的源流，集中討論這一書寫在詩歌如七律中的發展，以及從漢代到唐宋宮廷詩中的頌聖傳統，還有與漢賦傳統中宏大富麗特質的異同，進而揭示元代宮廷文人對文學傳統的繼承和補充。 從宮廷文化的角度，看元代宮廷詩產生的背景及其對蒙元上位者宮廷生活的反映，以及元代宮廷詩發展過程中體現的文化特色。 從兩種文化(蒙元文化與漢文化)的交疊中，看元代宮廷詩所創造的獨特的審美情趣，以及這一審美情趣在宮廷文學傳統中的價值。 從藝術層面，探討元代宮廷詩在語言運用和用典等方面的特色，特別關注其發展的階段性。 擬將所有元代宮廷詩按題材內容分類，並按詩人爵里順次排序，以及把同題或唱和作品的撰作者歸於同一標目下，彙編成冊，此外，把元代宮廷詩的總體和個別詩人用語習慣、詞彙頻率、蒙漢詞彙等語料建成資料庫，為研究中國宮廷文學、蒙元社會和文化的學者提供參考。 本課題最終成果為三至四篇專題論文，擬發表於國內外的核心期刊上。

22602918.label: Realisation of objectives
22602918.value: 本研究按照計畫書設定的研究目標順行執行，分述如下。 (1) 研究目標 計畫書有六個研究目標，按照筆者的宮廷詩定義，通覽及分析元代宮廷詩，歸納了二千首作品為研究範圍。以文本細讀為研究取向，副以數位人文研究工具，成功歸納元代宮廷詩的發展變化和時段特色[目標一及五]。 通覽全部現存元代詩文(《全元詩》[68冊]及《全元文》[60冊])，考出元代宮廷文化裡漢文化與蒙古文化的交疊，包括御書賞賜、刻本分賜、尊號分賜、上都宮殿的蒙古娛樂習俗、蒙漢風物在詩裡的呈現等等面向；並從現存文獻裡，發現元代帝王從不與宮廷文人唱酬，成為這一階段最為突出的文化現象 [目標二及三]。 通覽全部現存元代宮廷詩，勾勒出元代中後期的重大文事件與詩文創作的關係，以1294的高克恭〈夜山圖〉，1310及1323年王振鵬的〈金明池圖〉，1323年的南坡之變，1330-1333年的奎章閣，1342年的《國朝文類》編纂及出版，結合宮廷文人的詩文創作，考出各個階段，宮廷文人的關注點以及他們的詩文創作傾向[目標二及四]。 (2) 研究難處 本計畫的執行時段由2019至2023年為止，跨越了三年的新冠肺炎時段；對研究資料的獲得、對外學術交流、研究團隊的計畫目標執行都影響甚鉅，尤其本計畫需要閱讀大量一手文獻，在新冠疫情期間，難以獲取研究材料。 加上，疫情期間本地大學圖書館的有限度開放，當時只能在僅有的研究材料上整合資訊。 感謝浸會大學及研究資助局，接納並通過本計畫的延期要求，讓本計畫主持人得以在疫情完結後，重新查找一手資訊及外出訪學報告，得以順利完成計畫。

22602918.label: Major findings and research outcome
22602918.value: (1) 元代約有二千首宮廷詩，發展高峰在中期，而「蒙漢並置」是此時期的重要文化特徵； (2) 宮廷文人運用物質 (地點場所、日常生活)、社會 (政治權力)、精神層面 (生活禮儀、價值意義) 的關鍵字詞，形塑蒙元帝王的王權威儀； (3) 宮廷詩的語言運用情況，可分為「漢語借用於蒙語或其他外來語言的音譯詞」和「以漢語固有詞彙表述蒙古或外來概念」兩類，成為此一階段最為重要的語言文化現象。 (4) 宮廷詩裡的蒙漢風物，為漢詩體式裡帶來新的藝術趣味，蘊藏了典雅、粗豪、陌生的感情色彩，同時表達蒙元混一區宇、蒙古文化廣被四海的融合欣賞，宮廷文人通過此類書寫的嘗試，積極參與建構蒙古和外來概念在漢語系統內的文化積澱過程。 (5) 元代宮廷文人寫有不少作品反映時局世情之變化，例如從南坡之變的內亂視角，可知宮廷文人驚惶失措的心靈世界，以及思緒沉澱後的積極進言。在朝與退隱是宮廷詩裡抒情世界的紐結所在。

22602918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22602918.value: 全面整理元代宮廷詩的特色和內涵後，可進而擴展至明代初年的宮廷詩壇研究，考察入明後的元末文人，是如何面新新主，進而創作宮廷詩文，如所周知，蒙元自1368年退出漢地，回到漠北之後，一直與明代朝廷相對峙，而入明後的元末宮廷文人，在宮廷寫作裡呈現了怎樣的抒情特質、對時局關注的傾向以及蒙漢文化交匯的問題，是非常值得繼續探討的問題。

22602918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22602918.value: 十四世紀初的詩歌反映蒙元皇帝統領漢地及漠北的文治形象，也道出當時宮廷文人對宮廷文化活動增多、自身地位和文化日益受到重視的喜悅。元代宮廷詩的文學及文化價值體現在其創作場景上主、客的互為影響，皇帝、貴戚、宗室的文治作為，以及宮廷文人對此的積極期頒，宮廷詩便是在這些元素下互為因果的產物，可以說，蒙漢並置的視角，是了解和賞析元代宮廷詩與前朝作品同中有異的有效途徑。

22604318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22604318.value: 新香港政治漫畫運動的興起

22604318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22604318.value: During the Hong Kong Chief Executive Election in 2012, a number of online political cartoonists emerged on social media and made a huge impact on the formation of public opinion among young people. It signalled the beginning of a new political cartoon movement in the digital era with new style, aesthetics and readership. The movement reached its peak during the Umbrella Movement in 2014 when visual arts were widely adopted by protestors. While we expect the movement to continue to develop, the HKCE Election in 2017 has shown a totally different picture. The number of political cartoons on social media dropped drastically and cartoonists were struggling to gain the same level of public attention as in 2012. Despite the ups and downs, the movement has brought a lot of changes to Hong Kong’s political cartoon scene that will be decisive in future developments. This research will aim to investigate those changes with the following focuses: 1) The new ecology that transformed the mode of creation and art practices for both traditional and online cartoonists. 2) The new comics language that emerged from new tools, publication formats and the influence from other disciplines such as graphic design in visual arts. 3) The new readership that represents a new mode of social engagement that affects cartoonists’ creative directions. This research project will not approach the New Political Comics Movement as merely the transformation from print to online platforms, but also as the establishment of a hybrid environment that allows exchange between traditional and online cartoonists. This study will aim to fill the huge gap in academic studies about political comics in Hong Kong since the extensive studies on Hong Kong comics by Wendy Wong S.Y about 20 years ago. It will also attempt to continue the significant research on Hong Kong political comics by Carine Lai Man in 2006 and generate an up-to-date overview of the scene. Apart from contributing to academic literature via an analysis of cartoonists’ backgrounds and works, the research will also bring the findings to the public through the building of an online platform and a comic work. 本計劃的目的為研究自2012年香港行政長官選舉期間，大量網絡政治漫畫的出現為業界發來生態的改變。傳統報章的政治漫畫一直在製造民意上扮演重要角色。網絡政治漫畫的興起除了帶來新一輪政治漫畫運動之外，同時亦為此傳統藝術形式帶來了很大的挑戰。 2017年行政長官選舉期間，政治漫畫在網絡上雖然仍然零散地出現，但其影響力已難與2012年選舉相比。近年香港政治氣候的變遷、不同程度的政治審查以及傳統媒體的沒落等都對行業的前景構成重大的威脅。由此可見，對「新香港政治漫畫運動」的研究確實有迫切的需要。 過往學術界對香港政治漫畫的研究一直不足。約十多年前，思匯政策研究所的黎文燕曾出版《從政治漫畫分析香港政治的興起》一書，為回歸前後的政治漫畫發展留下一個註腳。自此之後，有關香港政治漫畫的研究可謂少之又少。本計劃期望能以網絡政治漫畫為切入點，為香港政治漫畫的注入新的觀點和分析，以下為計劃的重點： 1）為香港政治漫畫提供一個更新的藍圖，尤其以2012年行政長官選舉後開始創作的新一輩漫畫家為重點 2）從藝術創作模式去研究傳統與網絡政治漫畫家在創作環境、生態和方法上的相異之處 3）比較傳統與網絡政治漫畫在技巧和說故事形式上如何展現其美學 4）研究數碼科技，軟件和工具對創作，出版和發布的影響 5）透過一些跨媒體的作品的研究，去重新審視「政治漫畫」在新媒體和政治環境之下的定義 本計劃冀能透過訪問，作品的分析和與業界創作人的協作，對近年香港政治漫畫在獨特的政治環境下建立一套更完整的論述。希望藉此能為這一直被忽視的課題帶來更多的討論。

22605118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22605118.value: This project explores the intersections of intellectual discussions about race, nation, and migration in Japan and the United States from the 1920s to the 1940s. Beginning in the late nineteenth century, a portion of the Japanese population shuttled between the Japanese empire and the American West Coast and Hawaii. While their presence created racial tensions in the United States, it gave Japanese intellectuals important opportunities to reflect on race relations and migrations within the Japanese empire. Meanwhile, between the 1920s and 1940s, there were serious attempts to integrate diverse racial minorities in their own territory, spawning the idea of an expanded/multi-ethnic nation in both Japan and the United States in the context of imperial expansion, war, and the emergence of new theories of race relations. How then did the issue of Japanese transpacific migration historically intersect with or contribute to ongoing nation formation processes on both sides of the Pacific? This is the central question of this project and the importance of this inquiry lies in its introducing a unique trans-regional perspective and addressing the intersections of existing migration and empire studies. To explore the central question motivating this project, the proposed research will analyse Japanese and American intellectual discourses on transpacific Japanese migrations. Since the early interwar years, Japanese and American scholars in a variety of disciplines including sociology, anthropology, geography, medical science, and psychology had studied Japanese migrants’ racial contacts across the Pacific. Such intellectual discourses offered an authentic view of the nation behind each empire. In particular, building on the principal investigator’s past research on sociological works, this project examines the works of representative scholars who contributed to the studies of migrations, the Japanese medical scientist Ishihara Fusao, the Japanese geographer Komaki Saneshige, the American anthropologist Harry Shapiro, and the American psychologist Edward Strong, Jr., each of whom worked in broader interdisciplinary intellectual networks. The principal investigator will analyse how their works delineated the unstable borders of their own nations and consider the types of racism with which they engaged in their research. The resulting monograph will demonstrate that transpacific Japanese migration provided the basis on which Japanese and American intellectuals discussed and articulated the possibilities of extending the boundaries of their own nations. Moreover, in parallel to this research, the principal investigator will foster knowledge-sharing by creating a website that tracks and reports on this research and using materials discovered in the research in the classroom. 22605118.label: Realisation of objectives
22605118.value: Objective 1: To identify the trans-regional connections between modern Japanese and American history between the 1920s and the 1940s In my monograph, I explored Japanese and American intellectual discourses from interwar and wartime period. What I clarified in this study is that, in relation to the study of transpacific Japanese migration, there was a transnational flow of researchers and ideas. Based on such trans-regional connections, intellectuals in both countries were able to engage in the discussion of a common subject of Japanese migrations. In this way, I was able to identify the trans-regional historical connections between Japan and the United States between the 1920s and the 1940s. Objective 2: To illustrate how interdisciplinary interests were mobilised for the production of knowledge on migrations In my monograph, I examined various intellectual discourses on transpacific migrations produced during the interwar and wartime period both in Japan and the United States. In Japan, leading sociologists examined the racial/ethnic relationships Japanese migrants were involved in Hawaii during the 1930s. Also, Japanese geopoliticians discussed the Japanese migrants’ situation in Hawaii during the Pacific War. In the meantime, in the United States, American sociologists examined the Japanese immigrants’ level of assimilation in Hawaii during the 1930s. In addition, around the same time, American cultural and physical anthropologists did research on Japanese immigrants in Hawaii. In this way, my research illustrated how interdisciplinary interests were mobilized for the study of Japanese migrants. Objective 3: To elucidate the function of racism in the formations of multi-ethnic nation in Japanese and American history In my analysis of intellectual discourses on migrants, I particularly dealt with the discourses which envisioned the formation of multi-ethnic nations in Japan or the United States. However, I was very careful about how such discourses constantly reproduced the existing racial differences and hierarchies. My research particularly relied on Takashi Fujitani’s idea of “inclusionary racism” to analyze this mechanism of racism. Thus, my study elucidated the function of racism in multi-ethnic nation formation. Objective 4: To explore the intersection of migration studies and empire studies in the context of nation formation in the Japanese and American empires In my monograph, I focus on the intellectual discourses that envisioned the multi-ethnic imperial formations in Japan and the United States. However, when I selected the discourses to analyze, I particularly chose the discourses that incorporated the subject of transpacific Japanese migrations. In doing so, I was able to show how the history of migration was related to the subject of imperial nation formation. In this way, my methodology allows me to explore the intersection of migrations studies and empire studies in the context of Japanese and American imperial nation formations. Objective 5: To produce a monograph-length study and/or several articles that will enrich our knowledge of transpacific intellectual history and transpacific studies of empire and migration Based on my research, I was able to prepare my monograph and published an article on the discourse of the intellectual I dealt with in this project (Hani Goro) in a highly indexed journal. My monograph is currently under review. The reason why I have not been able to publish my monograph yet was because of the impact of Covid-19. Because of this pandemic, I have not been able to engage in archival research outside of Hong Kong for a few years. This global health crisis with a longer impact in Asia heavily affected my transnational historical research. Still, I tried to reframe my research perspective in order to finish my project. In the end, I was able to complete my manuscript and submitted it to a publisher for review.

22605118.label: Major findings and research outcome
22605118.value: Through my research, I came upon the existence of a variety of intellectual discourses on transpacific Japanese migrants in the context of multi-ethnic imperial formations in Japan and the United States from interwar and wartime periods. While those discourses shared the common subject of Japanese migration, I found a different tendency between Japanese intellectual discourses and American ones. In the case of Japanese discourses, the Japanese migrants were incorporated into the narrative of multi-ethnic Japanese imperial formation as important initiators or mediators for the ongoing Japanese imperial expansion. On the contrary, in the case of American discourses, Japanese migrants were examined and studied by American scholars as subjects to be integrated into the multi-ethnic American empire. In this way, even though the subject of transpacific Japanese migrants played an important role for both countries’ imperial formations, the way they were incorporated into the existing intellectual discourses was different. Furthermore, my research also discovered that, when both countries’ intellectual discourses approached the same subject of transpacific Japanese migration, there was an overlap of knowledge productions. It means that Japanese scholars used the results of the study produced by American scholarly research done around the same time and narrated their own vision of the formation of the Japanese empire. I also found that in this process Japanese scholars also altered the interpretation offered by American scholars. In this way, my research revealed the complicated interaction between the knowledge productions engaged by scholars in both countries. Through these examinations, I was able to address the historical connection between the intellectual history and empire history in both countries.

22605118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22605118.value: In regard to the further development of this project, first of all, I plan to share my research outcomes with a broader audience through workshops/conferences or public talk. Based on the feedback I will receive from such an exchange, I will try to expand my perspective and write additional research paper in the future. Secondly, in my monograph, I was not able to address what happened to the producers of that type of imperial knowledge about migrants during the postwar period. Therefore, I will keep tracing their career after the Pacific War and examine to what extent their perspective changed based on the effect of the ending of the war and the collapse of the Japanese empire.

22605118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22605118.value: My research project is the study of the historical relationship between Japanese migration to the United States and the imperial expansion in Japan and the United States between 1920s and 1940s. During this period, some leading intellectuals in both countries discussed the pressing issues of those migrants such as their assimilation to the host country (the United States), their experience of racial and ethnic contacts with other racial/ethnic groups, and their identity struggles. These issues stimulated the interests of both countries’ intellectuals because they were useful for them to think about the future development of their empire (Japanese and American empire). My research traces how these intellectuals discussed the issues of migration and how such discussions were related to their concern with the ongoing expansion of empires. This research is the pioneering study of such a transnational connection between two countries. By revealing such a connection, my project contributes to open a new transnational, transregional perspective for modern Japanese history and modern American history.

22608118.label: Project Objectives
22608118.value: Examine the role and evaluate the significance of the Sino-Malay corridor as a zone within the larger Maritime Silk Road. Deconstruct the Sino-Malay corridor that encompasses selected port cities in Eastern Indonesia, Sumatra, and Malaya as a culturally homogenous cultural zone by identifying differences that were uniquely developed due to political, social, economic, and ecological surroundings. Collect and analyze multi-lingual primary and secondary sources and examine multi-sited material culture regarding the forging of Sino-Malay corridor between circa 1400, when the presence of Chinese diasporas of mixed race heritage were first documented, and circa 1900, when the favorable position of Chinese mixed race communities declined. Publish two English and one Chinese single authored peer-reviewed journal articles to disseminate the project’s findings.

22608118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22608118.value: This proposed project will examine how and why the Sino-Malay cultural zone – an area that expanded from the port cities in Eastern Java to Makassar, Palembang, Melaka, and Singapore – became an important corridor within the wider Maritime Silk Road. Instead of approaching the formation of this corridor from state-centric perspectives, I will look at the history of trade exchanges, interactions, and movements of Chinese mixed race communities between 1400 and 1900. In so doing, I will question China’s role as the primary agent for developing the Maritime Silk Road throughout history. Although China’s tributary relations with Southeast Asia declined significantly since the 1400s, my proposed project hypothesizes that 1400-1900 was the formative period for shaping the Sino-Malay zone within the Maritime Silk Road. Focusing on Eastern Java as a nodal point I will examine how this zone was forged, shaped, and expanded by Chinese mixed race communities who dominated the trade networks along the Indonesian and Malaysian coasts. The geographical reach of this zone, therefore, is not formed by states’ fixity of borders but is shaped and continuously reshaped by movements of the trade diaspora and their networks. This project investigates the shaping and consolidation of the Sino-Malay zone by scrutinizing various Dutch, Malay, Indonesian, Chinese, and English textual sources and material culture from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, China, and the Netherlands. This project has two main purposes. First: to position and evaluate the significance of this Sino-Malay corridor as a unit within the larger Maritime Silk Road that stretched from China to Europe. Second: to deconstruct the Sino-Malay zone as a culturally homogenous zone from within by comparing port cities in the Eastern trade circuit (encompassing Eastern Java and Makassar) with those in the Western trade circuit (stretching from Eastern Java to Palembang, Singapore, and Melaka). I hypothesize that this zone, connected via Eastern Java, can be best understood as a unified multi-zonal system in which each port city contained both common Sino-Malay characteristics as well as distinctive traits due to political, socioeconomic, and ecological uniqueness. This distinctiveness, I suggest, can be observed by examining the histories and blended cultural heritage of trade diaspora of mixed Chinese and indigenous descent. By emphasizing their ‘mixedness’ rather than ‘Chineseness’ for forging the Sino-Malay cultural zone this proposed project will not only help shape Maritime Silk Road Studies but will also help further refine existing paradigms for Chinese Diaspora Studies. 22608118.label: Realisation of objectives
22608118.value: REGARDING OBJECTIVE 1: My research shows that the Sino-Malay corridor was a significant part of the larger Maritime Silk Road that connected the Asian with European waters. I examined the shaping of the Sino-Malay corridor by focusing on the movement of goods and human mobility, and concluded that these actors contributed to the development of the Silk Road. Focusing on the period between 1400 and 1900, my research shows that the Sino-Malay corridor flourished in from the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries, especially the networks and movements of peoples of mixed Chinese and Malayan descent were key to the development of the Sino-Malay corridor. The reasons for the growing importance include: Their connections with the Javanese and Malayan polities, China's decreased control on maritime trade, the rise of maritime routes that replaces the popularity of overland routes, and the growing demand of locale-specific products in high quantities. My research showed that the port cities along the Indonesian/ Malayan Kupang, Banda, Makassar, Banjarmasin, Surabaya, Palembang, Malacca), too, were nodal points in the global trade network. Besides being the gateway to China, the Sino-Malay corridor was connected with port cities beyond the Indonesian/Malayan archipelago, such as Pho Hien and Hoi An (Vietnam), Pegu (Myanmar), Ayutthaya (Thailand), and even the parts of what is now considered Australia. REGARDING OBJECTIVE 2: My research shows that although the Sino-Malay corridor is mainly forged by mobility, settlement, and networks by peoples of mixed Chinese and Malayan descent, this Sino-Malay cultural zone is by no means static, nor homogenous. Adopting a longue duree perspective I examined how the Sino-Malay zone emerged, evolved and further shaped between 1400 and 1900. Throughout the process of formation and shaping the role of the mixed descendants was crucial. This trade diaspora of mixed ancestry whose importance grew due to the wide trade connections that linked Java, Malaya, Borneo, Timor, Maluku together, forged trade connections through port cities and dominated the trade network across this maritime realm. Having networks extending to the coastal region in China and having access to the indigenous Southeast Asian society from whose products was the highly desired produce (such as spices, sea products, pearls, animal products etc.) as well as maintaining distribution channels of non-local products such as cotton and rice the trade diaspora of mixed Chinese and indigenous descent became a key agent to develop the Sino-Malay trade circuit. This composition and cultural identity of this mixed community was fluid. Examining its changes between 1400 and 1900, my research has identified the following broad patterns: in the periods 1400s-1500s records describe such communities as Malayanized people whose ancestry could be traced back to places in Fujian. Such descriptions were also found in records in later periods. I also examined records of 1600s that described the physical appearance of these mixed people. However, it is evident that later records (especially those from the 1800s-1900s) showed that descriptions of mixedness waned. Instead, my research shows that some peoples of mixed descent, despite its mixed ancestry became identified as native or Chinese. REGARDING OBJECTIVE 3: My goal was to collect and study Chinese, Dutch, English, Indonesian, and Malay primary and secondary sources from research sites in Europe and Asia. I planned to start with secondary sources first before embarking on field research. However, the pandemic has greatly affected my plan to collect data from research sites. The continuing restrictions on travel and access to research material caused a shift in my research. Because adopting multi-lingual and multi-sited research was challenging under such circumstances, I have mainly focused on Chinese language material and secondary sources that were accessible from Hong Kong. Although such material was useful for understanding the Chinese angle and Chinese aspects of the maritime Silk Road, it is insufficient to obtain the full picture of the forging Sino-Malay corridor and the mixed communities that helped forge this zone. REGARDING OBJECTIVE 4: In my sole-authored article “Mixed Bloods in a Plural Society: Recovering the Place of Hybridized 'Chinese' in Indonesia’s Port Communities” I have provided methodological discussions and empirical data elaborately. Therefore, instead of two articles I have decided to write one long article (39 pages in total). I am finalising one Chinese article by October 2023. The intended date of completion report is in December 2023, but due to my departure of my institution, I am submitting my completion report four months earlier.

22608118.label: Major findings and research outcome
22608118.value: This project has examined the shaping and significance and Sino-Malay maritime zone between the period 1400 and 1900, and concluded that this zone became an important corridor within the wider maritime Silk Road. My research identifies the period between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries as the flourishing period of the Sino-Malay corridor. This zone was forged, shaped, and expanded by the peoples and networks of mixed Chinese and Malayan descent. Due to its geographical location and the key position of these Sino-Malay communities, port cities in this zone, specifically Surabaya, Gresik, Tuban in Eastern Java; Batavia on Western Java; Palembang, Melaka/ Malacca, Penang bordering/ coastline of the Straits of Malacca, each in varying historical periods became important transit point and collection point of products for maritime trade between China, the Indian Ocean, and the Mediterranean. By investigating the formation and consolidation of Sino-Malay corridor, I have concluded the following: the significance of this Sino-Malay corridor within the larger maritime Silk Road that stretched from China to Europe was attributed to the following factors: flourishing global trade, China’s isolation from maritime presence, ascent of Sino-Malay communities and networks. Moreover, I also observed that connections of the Sino-Malay corridor extended to Vietnam, Thailand, and Myanmar. to deconstruct the Sino-Malay corridor as unified zone in multiple sub-sections (tentatively three sub-sections). Moreover, this corridor which is unified by shared Sino-Malay characteristics should be understood as a multi-segmented zone in which segments contain distinctive traits due to political, economic, social, and ecological uniqueness.

22608118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22608118.value: This project evoked my interest and desire to further research in mixed-race communities. During my research I notice that the Chinese and Malay mixed communities were not the sole engine for the thriving of the maritime Silk Road. Hence, I will investigate their role comparatively with other mixed communities, especially the Indian-Malayan mixed communities.

22608118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22608118.value: Most studies on the Silk Road history place China at the center of shaping the overland and maritime Silk Roads. As a result, these studies incorrectly give the assumption that the maritime silk road declined with China's isolation from the maritime waters during the Ming era. But this project shows that, instead of decline, the maritime Silk Road thrived due to the flourishing of the Sino-Malay corridor, thanks to the importance of communities of mixed Chinese and Malayan descent.

22608518.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22608518.value: 沉默發聲之間：香港日常政治的俗民志研究

22608518.label: Project Objectives
22608518.value: To examine the process generating the impetus, practice, and capital of everyday politics; To revisit the scope and meanings of political participation in Hong Kong; To advance the conceptualization of everyday politics in hybrid, urban, and cyber contexts; To explore changes in the relations of power vis-a-vis contours of sociocultural reproduction in selected groups; and To generate rich and original ethnographic data to inform political actors of the dialectics between silence and voice in contentious politics.

To revisit the scope and meanings of political participation in Hong Kong;
