To generate rich and original ethnographic data to inform political actors of the dialectics between silence and voice in contentious politics.

22608518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22608518.value: This proposed study examines the paradox of declining protest events and intensified political polarization in Hong Kong. Recently, street mobilization and parliamentary confrontation have lessened following proactive regime responses and the low-tide of a protest cycle. However, the steady rise in electoral turnouts, hateful social media debates, recurring community initiatives, and unprecedented records of public meetings indicate the growing politicization of everyday life. Silence is less informative and organized than voice. It is imperative, therefore, to explore which groups of citizens choose to engage in everyday politics, how they appropriate their practices and messages, and why they seek recognition and solidarity. Borrowing the concepts of “everyday resistance,” “movement abeyance,” and “connective action,” this study will unpack the changing processes and agency of political participation in Hong Kong. First, it examines how new community and professional initiatives can overtly or covertly transmit political messages. This focus transcends existing frameworks that regard political participation as a function of political culture and institutional constraints. Second, it analyzes why everyday practices in the civic arena may contest the distribution and relations of power in society. This process tracing reveals how strong ties and new identities are disseminated to sustain social movements. Here, everyday politics are classified into three different categories, namely casual conversations of public affairs, organized community initiatives, and professional advocacies. An ethnographic approach will be adopted to identify the impetus, practice, and capital unfolding from these lived experiences. Interviews and focus groups will be conducted with state and non-state actors to discover their nuanced perceptions of order, authority and justice to analyze the discrepancy between public statements and hidden transcripts. Public events, members-only meetings and their online interactions will be regularly documented to trace the evolution of routine and novel performances, and assess the participants’ daily interactions in terms of scale, connectivity, and durability. By offering a thick description and contextual analysis of subaltern beliefs and practices in semi-democratic, urban, and cyber contexts, this study will advance the conceptualization of everyday politics. Results will demonstrate original and uninterrupted data by unpacking the patterns, scope, and meanings of political participation, which will inform policymakers about the dialectical relationship between silence and voice in contentious politics, and pose insights for political mediation. This study will lay the groundwork to deepen our understanding of the transformative effects of personalized politics, thereby provoking international academic interest in Hong Kong politics despite the dearth of striking events. 這項研究擬考察香港抗議活動減緩，政治兩極化卻加劇的悖論。近年，基於政權的積極回應和抗議週期的低潮，街頭動員和議會抗爭相繼減少。然而，選舉投票率和社交媒體政治辯論卻穩步上升，社區倡議和公眾會議更反復出現。這些現象說明日常生活愈趨政治化。「沉默」的信息量和組織性均不如「發聲」。因此，有必要探索那些公民群體選擇參與日常政治，他們如何傳遞信息和行動，以及他們為何爭取認可和團結。 借用「日常抗爭」、「運動暫停」和「締結行動」等概念，這項研究希望揭示香港政治參與在機制和主體方面的變動。首先，它會考察新生社區倡議和專業參政，如何公開或含蓄地傳遞政治信息。這種角度超越了將政治參與，視為體現政治文化和製度約束的現有框架。其次，它嘗試分析為什麼公民的日常實踐，有可能衝擊權力在不同社會場域的分配和關係。這個跟踪過程，有效揭示強連接和新身份怎樣維繫社會運動。 在這裡，日常政治分為三個不同的類別，即公共事務的日常對話，社區倡議和專業參政。本研究將採用俗民志研究的方法，拿捏這些生活經歷中展現出的誘因、模式和資本；菁英訪談和焦點小組，將解析不同群體對秩序，權威和公義等概念的差距看法；其公共活動，僅限會員會議及在線互動等活動將被定期記錄，以追踪常規和特殊戲碼的互動，並根據規模、連通性和耐久性等指標評估各組織的參與程度和影響。 通過深入描述和分析，不同場域的基層組織的價值和行為，這項研究將推進日常政治的概念化。一方面，能夠提供原創和不間斷的數據，理解當下香港政治參與的模式、範圍和意義。這有助政策制定者理解沉默和發聲的辯證關係，並為政治調解提供切入點。另方面，這個研究將為研究個性化政治的變革告影響，奠定基礎。從而維繫國際學術界對香港研究的興趣：因為儘管香港缺乏引人注目的事件，但廣義的政治參與依然存在。

A number of research impact activities and outputs have also been disseminated in reputable academic and public venues. The details are as follows. Objectives 1 and 2. The PI has conducted more than 80 semi-structured interviews and intensive ethnography studies with community organizers, activists and ordinary citizens to survey their organizational network, social capital and diversified forms of political participation. Each interview lasted for around 1.5 hours on average. This intensive fieldwork has gathered substantial, first-hand data to assess the recurring mechanisms that accounted for the diffusion of everyday politics, by which some claims are politicized and evolved into popular events while others are not. In collaboration with three other academics, the PI conducted 25 onsite surveys and collected more than 18,000 valid responses from 9 June 2019 to 30 November 2019. In each onsite survey, around 15-20 Trained volunteers were deployed to randomly pick samples after walking a fixed number of steps in an assigned route. The respondents’ pre-exiting networks, participatory motivations, social demographics obtained from different research methods and time periods were also compared to facilitate valid and multifaceted measurements. The changing scope and meanings of political participation in Hong Kong are thus documented, enabling comparison between social groups and in different periods. Objectives 3 and 4: The findings of the project have revealed the interacted relationship between silence and voice. In terms of silence, the findings suggest that movement abeyance can be a strategic choice of activists to retreat from active political engagement under different social structures and political environments. This leads to fragmentation of inter-group coalition in civil society but also enables the preservation of group values, identity, and vision among a wider population through hidden transcripts and community networks. In terms of voice, socially engaged groups can make use of their expertise, specialized networks and institutional positions, to develop a novel form of collective action. This observation reveals the symbolic and tangible functions of social roles in various forms of voice, i.e. protests, elections and public critics. Objective 5: Findings unpack the nexus between collective memory and collective identity and find the cultural process of transforming collective memory into collective identity and actions is anything but linear. The trends and determinants of everyday politics were found to be increasingly correlated with the relational affections and informal networks commonly associated with pre-existing networks, digital information sources, and political values. Various stakeholders should acknowledge the changes in citizen values and community attachment that is not only local but also global. It should also develop new mechanisms to increase citizens' external efficacy in policymaking and everyday life to mitigate political conflicts among the population.

22608518.label: Major findings and research outcome
22608518.value: This project has resulted in three conference papers and four articles in reputable journals in the respective fields of political science, sociology, and area studies. Using a combination of interviews, ethnography, and surveys, we show how and why mixed methods and thick descriptions can enable better measurements of the nexus between silence and voice. These outputs help to provide methodological insight, empirical findings, and conceptual development in the fields of area studies and political sociology. The PI is either the first or corresponding author of all these publications. The PI has presented three papers at the annual meeting of the Association for Asian Studies, the Taiwanese Sociological Association, and the Midwest Political Science Association. These papers received good and extensive feedback from the audience and balanced the engagements with various fields and disciplines that are relevant to the research project. The PI published an article in Mobilization that examines the nexus between collective memory and collective identity and finds the cultural process of transforming collective memory into collective identity and actions is anything but linear. It highlights the performative and filtering role of repertoires in reproducing collective memory and reveals a dynamic and nuanced relationship between collective memory and identity, especially the mediating factors at work. Another article published in China Review examines how collective actions have unexpectedly emerged despite the absence of favorable conditions amidst a declining trend of political efficacy. It reveals the respective roles of formal and informal abeyance networks in the study period triggering sectorial-wide participation. Moreover, the author published an article in Social Movement Studies that examine the symbolic and tangible functions of social roles in various forms of voice. It shows that sectoral mobilization’s modes and levels are often contingent on an array of institutional constraints, informal networks, and conjunctural events in a networked movement. Another article published in the Japanese Journal of Political Science surveys the inter-group relations between different generations. The findings shed light on the affective and relational dimensions of protest participation, showing how the traumatic conditions under which different social actors are welded together by shared emotional upheavals facilitate ingroup identification and affective solidarity.

22608518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22608518.value: The current project has also inspired new projects that touch upon social network analysis and contentious politics. The PI has received two GRFs and two PPRs that aim to provide new conceptual framework and methodological tools to measure public sentiments, networked movements, and state-diasporic relations in an increasingly polarized world.

22608518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22608518.value: This project unpacks the nexus between silence and voice in a fast-changing and deeply divided society. It finds the trends and determinants of everyday politics and political identification were found to be increasingly correlated with the relational affections and informal networks commonly associated with pre-existing networks, digital information sources, and political values. Methodologically, the project has shown how and why mixed methods and thick descriptions can enable better measurements of the formal and informal networks and the discrepancy between political platforms from hidden transcripts. Empirically, our primary finding was that civic engagement is dynamic, changes over time, and varies between sectors. We found a general trend of declining trust in formal NGOs and political parties in the city, which is often mediated by pre-existing networks, social roles, political identity, and perceived efficacy. Theoretically, this project differentiates the measurements of silence and voice and unpacks their interactive mechanisms at the individual and group levels, which helps to situation the Hong Kong case to the broader inquiry between everyday politics and contentious politics. Various stakeholders should acknowledge the changes in citizen values and community attachment that is not only local but also global. They may explore ways to develop new mechanisms to increase citizens' external efficacy in policymaking and everyday life to mitigate political conflicts among the population.

22609018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22609018.value: For generations, China’s farmers have worked the land to harvest a living. Land was essential, and for the great majority, it was the only means to thrive. Today, the farmers’ offspring have uprooted themselves from the land for urban jobs. Nevertheless, most still retain the rural land and float between the urban and rural realms. Farmers can lease their land, but they are not permitted to sell it, except to the government. Despite these incomplete rural property rights, landholders tend to maximize the utility of their land to realize its potential value. As investment capital frenetically acquires rural land for development and centralized agricultural production, the value of rural land has significantly increased. In many places and for many rural households, rural landholdings have changed from being the means of livelihood into being a fixed asset whose value varies according to the type, quantity and location of the landholdings. Revenues generated from rural land often instantaneously alter the mobility choices and life outcomes of rural citizens. These new developments are almost completely absent from studies of China’s migration and social changes, where emphasis is on the role of urban employment in driving rural citizens to move across the country and up the social ladder. This research, however, will shed new light on how the countryside may also be driving the geographic and social mobility of rural citizens, thereby shaping regional social patterns. Through juxtaposing and relating rural migrants’ resources and life outcomes from both urban and rural angles, empirical analysis using two complementary approaches will unravel the effect of rural landholdings. Statistical modeling of survey data will be used to examine the causal relationships of rural landholdings, migration and life outcomes. A multi-sited ethnography approach will be used to investigate how rural landholdings influence the splitting of the family and the lives of migrants in the city and family members in the countryside. The mixed-methods investigation will be conducted in a hierarchy of urban destinations in Jiangsu and in multiple rural origins within and outside the province. In these analyses, urban livelihood and rural assets will be treated as integral components of the complex process of transregional class formation and reproduction. Scrutinizing such processes at the household level will help explain how rural land, distributed (in principle) to rural households on an egalitarian basis, may have become a source of inequality, sorting rural citizens into various localities and social classes. 世代以來，中國農民以耕地謀生。土地不僅是生存之根本，也是大多數人追求富足生活的唯一手段。時至今日，農民離開土地，遠走他鄉。他們在城市謀生，卻依然保留農村土地，遷徙於城鄉之間。農村土地可以租借，但禁止出售。這種不完整的土地產權限制了土地流轉，但土地所有者仍能儘可能最大化土地效用，以實現其潛在價值。從城市溢出的大量資本湧入農村城市化開發和集中式農業生產，助推了農村土地增值和收益。在部分地區，農村土地已經由農業生產資料轉變為固定資產，其價值由土地所有權類型和土地面積、位置等因素決定。農村土地收益常常直接影響農村居民的生活水平和空間流動。關於中國農民工和社會轉型的研究通常以城市就業作為推動農村人口流動和社會變遷的主要原因， 農村土地的作用幾乎完全被忽視。本研究探索農村土地如何推動農村人口的空間和社會流動，改變區域社會結構。研究框架整合互補的兩種實證分析方法，通過將農民工家庭在城市和農村兩地的經濟社會資源和生活狀態並置、聯繫，揭示農村土地的作用。一方面，基於問卷調查數據的統計模型用於分析農村土地所有權，空間流動和社會經濟屬性的相互影響機制。另一方面，多點民族志方法用於調查農村土地及其收益如何影響農村家庭的遷移策略，目的地選擇，以及在城市居住和在農村居住家庭成員的生活狀態。數據收集在江蘇省多個城市（農民工流入地）和該省內外多個農村地區（農民工流出地）進行。在數據分析過程中，以土地為主的農村經濟社會資源將和城市就業一起被視作決定跨地區階級形成和再生產的要素。這一新視角有助於解釋以集體平均主義為基礎的農村土地所有制，如何在經濟社會轉型過程中創造出新的不平等，將農村人口推向不同的目的地和社會階層。

22609018.label: Realisation of objectives
22609018.value: The realization of all three objectives relies on extensive primary data collection in Mainland China. The outbreak of Covid-19 significantly disrupted the fieldwork planned for 2020. Due to restrictions on cross-border travel and stringent quarantine measures lasting from the beginning of 2020 through 2022, a series of data collection activities were postponed and rearranged to cope with practical challenges. The 18-month project extension facilitated the postponed fieldwork when traveling to and within the mainland was possible. All research objectives have been realized. In the following, specific achievements are outlined with respect to each objective. Objective 1 The conventional view of China's internal migration posits that the migration and social mobility of rural citizens are driven by urban jobs. Personal disadvantages, institutional constraints, and inadequate resources typically restrain rural citizens from urban migration. This research confirms that the least endowed rural citizens are the least mobile. It further unravels that the deterrent effects rooted in rural origin cause varied degrees of (im)mobility—staying, rural-rural migration, rural-urban migration, and short- and long-distance moves. For those endowed to move, their destination choices are broadened by factors such as education attainment and family resources. However, those less endowed are apt to hold onto the safe and secure, though probably less desirable livelihood promised at home or a nearby place, following a risk-averse pathway that precludes more rewarding possibilities elsewhere. The most conspicuous deterrents for them include the inadequate provision of quality education, a predominant agricultural economy, unalienable rural landholdings, and constraints in accessing public provision of healthcare and social security outside of their native places. Negative endowments are holding them back, resulting in immobility and persistent poverty. Meanwhile, migration still makes a difference in several ways, including supporting a larger fund for rural house construction and maintenance. Households with a migrating member also spend more on children’s education, enhancing their chances for upward social mobility. Migration improves the financial capacity of a household to cope with adversity and crises, such as covering the medical expenses of sick family members when other major family events occur simultaneously. In contrast, immobile households must significantly reduce spending on some items to provide for other, more urgent needs. Nevertheless, rural migrants and their families are still trapped in substandard living conditions. Even elderly and disabled family members must often strive to be effectively self-sufficient or at least not a net drain on limited household resources. Throughout individuals’ life course, personal and familial endowments may have profound and lasting effects on mobility choices and how (im)mobility interacts with the uneven distributive outcomes of the labor market and welfare provision across localities. At a macro level, a self-reinforcing socio-spatial sorting process is likely to occur, propelling the formation and reproduction of trans-regional inequalities. Objective 2 For generations, China’s farmers have worked the land to harvest a living. Land was essential, and for the great majority, it was the only means to thrive. Today, the farmers’ offspring have uprooted themselves from the land for urban jobs. Nevertheless, most of them still retain rural land and float between urban and rural realms. The examination of both survey and interview data has confirmed that rural landholdings vary among rural migrants in terms of type, quantity, and location, exerting different effects on mobility choices and life outcomes. By and large, it is not only access to better urban opportunities but also the possession of rural land that either enables or impedes the attainment of better life outcomes and social status. The use of rural land generates revenues and affects migration decisions and urban career aspirations. The life outcomes of rural migrants in the city, in turn, determine their relative dependence on rural land and its revenue. Migration and rural landholdings are therefore no longer exogenous factors for life outcomes but are endogenous factors that have feedback effects on each other. Urban livelihood and rural assets form integral components in the complex process of transregional class formation and reproduction. In Chinese cities, institutional discrimination engendered by the hukou system has caused systematic inequalities between rural migrants and urban locals. In response, policy recommendations are often formulated in the direction of granting rural migrants urban hukou status or, at the very least, offering them access to basic welfare in the city. However, this research reveals that dramatic variations in personal and familial endowments within the rural population have led to socioeconomic disparities. Some rural citizens are endowed to move to the city and benefit from urban jobs and welfare. Some are confined by their poor health, lack of education, path dependency on agricultural livelihood, and outcomes of land requisition. These endowment factors enable or constrain the geographic and social mobility of rural citizens, sorting them into different localities and social classes. These mechanisms suggest that the differences in impoverishment and life outcome may be nuanced, and deeper structural inequalities are caused not only by institutional obstacles between rural and urban residents but also by endowed qualities and resources among the rural population. Geographical disparities across rural communities and individual differences within these communities create fine-grained patterns of advantages and disadvantages. The mutually interactive (im)mobility and divergent life outcomes of the rural population are both subject to initial inequalities in endowments. Objective 3 The industrialization and urban development in China have driven a significant portion of the rural population to its urban areas. While discriminating institutions engendered by the hukou system exclude most rural migrants from urban rights and benefits, the option of converting hukou has become increasingly available. Nevertheless, few rural migrants have chosen to settle down in cities by obtaining an urban hukou, contradicting a common perception that rural migrants desire an urban hukou. Based on both survey and interview data, the research explores rural migrants’ intention of hukou conversion with respect to the availability, type, and quantity of rural landholdings in their home countryside, as well as their socioeconomic attributes and migration patterns. The results indicate that both the possession of farmland and housing land in rural areas significantly influence the intention of rural migrants to obtain an urban hukou in their destination cities. Moreover, systematic variances in settlement intention are found between the “born-after-1980” generation and their older counterparts, as well as between migrants from the more and less affluent regions. More recently, the booming platform economy has reshaped the urban labor market, offering entry-level opportunities to urban residents, particularly rural migrant workers. Unlike traditional sectors characterized by occupational segregation between rural migrants and urban locals, platform-based gig jobs, such as food delivery and ride-hailing, have attracted both groups, creating a diverse labor force. Among these groups, rural migrant workers have the lowest socioeconomic status and worst living conditions, often perceiving food delivery as a last-resort means of livelihood. Most urban locals and urban migrants turn to food delivery to supplement their family incomes or as a temporary job while pursuing other career opportunities. Furthermore, both rural and urban migrant workers experience a higher degree of job insecurity compared to urban locals. These disparities in socioeconomic status and subjective well-being among the three groups within the food delivery labor force influence their divergent life prospects in terms of career paths and settlement intentions.

22609018.label: Major findings and research outcome
22609018.value: Existing literature on China’s social transformation has primarily focused on the role of urban areas in propelling rural citizens to move across the country and ascend the social ladder. Participation in the urban economy promotes social mobility, while rural landholdings are often expropriated at low compensation rates to provide a “hidden subsidy” for urban growth. Nevertheless, as investment capital frenetically acquires rural land for development and centralized agricultural production, rural communities are also motivated to capitalize on the potential of their landholdings. Against this backdrop, this research proposes a new conceptual framework to understand the mechanism of rural–urban migration and social mobility through the prism of rural landholdings. Drawing on multiple national and regional surveys, this research finds that the mobility choices of Chinese rural citizens are determined by rural landholdings as well as other individual and familial endowments. Good health, basic educational attainment, and non-local family livelihoods increase the likelihood of out-migration, while a lack of these endowments likely bars rural citizens from moving. The possession of rural land and other local resources, in contrast, tends to deter migration to urban destinations. Being the largest asset for most rural citizens in China, landholdings in the countryside function as a selection mechanism to sort rural citizens into various localities and social classes, propelling trans-regional class formation and reproduction. The analyses also reveal that the budgets of poor rural households in China are extremely strained, regardless of migration by any family members. The living standards of migrant households are not substantially improved in comparison with immobile households. Yet, high living costs in the city oblige them to split the family and live frugally on both sides to minimize total household expenditures. While both migrant and immobile households resort to similar strategies to cut costs wherever they can, migrant households spend significantly more to meet basic needs due to the duplication of some expenditure. Consequently, despite having relatively higher incomes, migrant households have living standards as low as those of immobile households. Both groups have a negligible budget for investment and recreation and allocate almost all their income to food, housing, education, transport, and healthcare. For the migrants, not only do living costs in the city tend to drain their urban incomes, leaving negligible remittances, but their families back in the rural home also must sacrifice by tightening their budget for healthcare, education, and daily essentials.

22609018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22609018.value: In addition to the four journal articles and three conference presentations, the quantitative and qualitative data collected in this project will be analyzed to address more relevant questions and yield at least two additional journal publications. Given the diverse properties of rural landholdings in terms of quantity, type, and location, the effects of rural landholdings on spatial and social mobility substantially vary among the rural population. Rural land has become a source of inequality, sorting rural citizens into various localities and social classes. The process of selective sorting and the resulting migration and social mobility may, in turn, determine how rural land is used or disposed of. China’s rural migrant population, though working and living in the cities, is still tied to their rural roots, either voluntarily or involuntarily. Further analyses will be conducted to inform and coordinate rural land management and demographic policies. A more flexible administration of rural land and a more inclusive provision of urban jobs and welfare should be introduced to empower rural citizens to meet migration and career aspirations. Additionally, it is time to acknowledge and respond to the rising inequality among rural citizens at the regional and national levels. Social mobility pathways for rural citizens from less developed regions should be broadened through preferential and redistributive measures.

22609018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22609018.value: For the approximately 300 million rural migrant workers in China, migrating to urban destinations offers a primary avenue for poverty alleviation and upward social mobility. Using questionnaire surveys, interviews, and extensive fieldwork, this research reveals that rural migrants, while deeply engaged in the urban economy, remain socially and economically tied to their rural origins. For rural households, ownership of rural land tends to deter migration and impede the attainment of improved life outcomes and social status. Meanwhile, although remittances from migrating members contribute to higher household incomes, elevated living costs in the city compel these migrant households to be frugal, often resulting in the family being split between the city and the rural home to minimize total household expenditures. While rural landholdings are sorting China’s rural citizens into different localities and social classes, many of the poorest rural households are on the horns of a dilemma—having a job in the city mitigates poverty but often leads to the distress of family separation and the need to endure harsh living conditions for family members in the city. These findings call for policy changes to facilitate family migration and enhance rural welfare and resource provisions for immobile households.

22610218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22610218.value: 雙重視野下的香港及其文學：香港文學英譯及法譯選本研究

22610218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22610218.value: While several monographs focus on the uniqueness of Hong Kong culture, often restricted to cinema, little attention has been paid to how Hong Kong literature is presented to international readers. However, literature has the ability to create powerful images of cultures that are globally transmitted through translation. By focusing on translation anthologies of Hong Kong literature, this project will investigate the translators’ agency and the way their choices shape the representation of Hong Kong and its literature. The project will therefore broaden the understanding of Hong Kong literary identity and the agency of translators, contributing to both Hong Kong literature studies and socially situated translation studies. Translation anthologies are an especially pertinent site for the study of intercultural representation because they can be considered a double rewriting: anthologizing involves selection, structuring and presentation, while translations are marked by the choices of translators. In addition, translation anthologies are typically used in comparative literature courses, influencing students’ understanding of other literatures and cultures. The study of 21 translation anthologies in English and 9 in French will help us examine both the image of the Self and the representation of the Other. The macro-level analysis (paratexts, content and reviews) will be followed by a detailed micro-level reading and translation comparison of three of these anthologies. The postcolonial context in which these anthologies were produced and the marginalised position of Hong Kong literature make the object of study uniquely interesting. The analysis of the paratextual elements (prefaces, notes, book covers) and reviews will inform us about the translators’ intervention at the discursive level, the way they depict Hong Kong and its literature, and the way this literature is received. Detailed analysis of a selection of translations will be conducted to study the decision-making of each translator. Special attention will be paid to translations of stories that appear both in the French and English anthologies, since they will allow us to establish a comparison. The translators’ stance will be examined in other sources, such as interviews, articles, prefaces and accounts of their own work. Interviews with the editors, publishers and a selection of ten translators who have participated in three of the anthologies will complement the data. The outcomes will be disseminated through conferences, articles and book chapters. The project’s website will give global visibility to Hong Kong literature both as an exceptional field of research and as a literature worth reading and translating. 雖然目前有幾部專著集中討論香港文化的獨特性，但範圍往往局限於電影一隅，鮮少關注香港文學以何種方式呈現給國際讀者。然而，文學能夠創造出強而有力的文化形象，更可借助翻譯傳播海外。本研究項目將聚焦於香港文學的翻譯選本，探討譯者的施為及選擇如何形塑出香港及其文學之再現。因此，本項目將深化對香港文學身份及譯者施為的認識，為香港文學研究及社會學翻譯研究同時帶來貢獻。 翻譯選本可以視作雙重的「改寫」，故對研究跨文化再現尤其密切攸關：首先，編選行為本身涉及甄選、架構和呈現，譯文則留下了譯者抉擇的印記。再者，翻譯選本通常用作比較文學課的教材，對學生瞭解其他文學與文化有一定影響。本研究將以21種英譯選本及9種法譯選本為基本文獻，借以探索自身的形象和他者的再現。對副文本、內文、書評等進行的宏觀分析，將結合對三種主要選本的微觀細讀和譯文比較，展開深入全面的研究。 這些選本生成背後的後殖民脈絡，與香港文學的邊緣化位置，都賦予了研究對象獨特的研究意義和興味。對副文本元素（如前言、注語、封面）和書評等的分析，將透露譯者在論述層面上所作的干預、怎樣描寫香港及其文學，以及香港文學如何為讀者接受。本研究將挑選一部分譯作詳加分析，藉以研究每位譯者的取捨抉擇。同時見於法譯和英譯本的故事因可資比較，故將獲特別重視。此外，通過訪問、文章、前言、譯者自述等其他來源探討譯者的立場和定位。另與編者、出版商和十位譯者進行專訪，補充文字材料的不足。研究成果將以會議、論文和專章等方式發表。項目網站將有助香港文學吸引國際注目，證明香港文學作為研究領域意義非凡，作為地方文學更是值得閱讀和翻譯。

22611818.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22611818.value: 陶藝藝術治療應用於中學生調節情緒及身心壓力: 隨機對照試驗

22611818.label: Project Objectives
22611818.value: To investigate and compare the effectiveness of CAT and control treatment in promoting the following outcomes: 1. improvement of emotion regulation strategies; 2. enhancement of positive affective states; 3. alleviation of negative affective states; 4. alleviation of deficits in the cognitive processing of affect, as in alexithymia; 5. reduction in psychological and physiological stress levels.
rows: To investigate and compare the effectiveness of CAT and control treatment in promoting the following outcomes: 1. improvement of emotion regulation strategies; 2. enhancement of positive affective states; 3. alleviation of negative affective states; 4. alleviation of deficits in the cognitive processing of affect, as in alexithymia; 5. reduction in psychological and physiological stress levels.

22611818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22611818.value: Emotional problems, such as depressive and anxious mood, are prevalent in the youth population of Hong Kong (HK) and although the etiology is complex it is widely believed that academic stress is a major factor. Locally there has been a lot of research into stress prevention but the results have been poor. A city-wide survey found that 50% of adolescents were on the brink of clinical depression. A review of the literature suggests that depression in adolescents is the result of poor emotional regulation (ER). There has been scant research on ER in HK, but in Western countries ER mechanisms and the impacts of ER strategies on psychophysiological health have been extensively and intensively researched in recent decades. ER can be divided into three components: positive and negative affective states, physiological-psychological interaction, and cognition-emotion interaction. Built on the theoretical underpinnings of ER, art therapy with clay (clay art therapy; CAT) provides the intervention that aids emotional regulation by improving emotional regulation aspects as abovementioned and facilitating mind—body interactions in the treatment processes. The aim of this study is to assess the effectiveness of CAT in improving the various respects of emotion regulation. The intervention starts with individuals interacting physically with clay and progressively integrates various psychological techniques. The objectives of CAT are to (1) improve emotional regulation strategies; (2) enhance positive affective states; (3) alleviate negative affective states; (4) reduce cognitive deficits in affective processing, e.g. alexithymia; (5) reduce psychological and physiological stress in secondary school students. The effectiveness of the CAT intervention will be tested via a randomized controlled trial comparing the CAT program with a control treatment. The sample will consist of secondary school students aged 15 to 17 years. During the time that the treatment group is receiving CAT the control group will participate in non-therapeutic activities, mainly ordinary classes organized and hosted by school teachers (e.g. remedial English and mathematics classes). The treatment group is expected to show improvement in the areas targeted by the intervention. Outcome measures as listed in the Methodology section will be used to assess improvements in affective states and cognition-emotion interaction. Salivary cortisol levels will be measured to assess physiological-psychological interactions and stress reduction resulting from after the anticipated reduction in emotional problems. 本港青少年普遍呈現與情緒相關徵狀，如抑鬱和焦慮。雖然當中原因複雜，但社會大眾普遍認同學業壓力是一個主要因素。 過去已有不少有關預防壓力的研究，但結果不如理想。 一項全港調查研究發現，半數的青少年現正處於臨床抑鬱的邊緣。 在過去的文獻中綜述，青少年抑鬱症狀是由於情緒調節（Emotion Regulation, ER）所產生的不良所影響。香港對ER相關的研究寥寥可數；然而，在西方國家，近數十年來，ER機制和ER策略對心理生理健康的影響已經進行了廣泛而深入的研究。 ER可分為三個部分：積極和消極情感狀態、生理心理相互作用，以及認知及情感相互作用。陶藝藝術治療（Clay Art Therapy, CAT）以ER的理論作為基礎，通過藝術治療師預設的藝術治療介入手法，去促進身心相互作用來幫助參加者有效地調節情緒。 本研究目的是評估CAT在改善情緒調節在以下各方面的有效程度，包括: （1）改善情緒調節策略; （2）增強正面積極的情感狀態; （3）緩解負面情感狀態; （4）減少處理情感時的認知功能缺陷，例如：述情障礙; 及（5）減少中學生的心理和生理壓力。 是次研究為隨機對照試驗，對象為15至17歲的中學生，參加者將被隨機分配到CAT 治療小組或對照組。對照組為學校指定的、提升學能的課後活動（例如英語輔導班和數學輔導班）。 本研究預計指定治療組將在藝術治療介入下，所針對的領域得到改善。研究團隊會分析參加者填寫有關情緒調節的問卷，去量度陶藝藝術治療對參加者在以上各方面的影響。另外，研究人員亦會採集參加者的唾液皮質醇樣本，以評估同學在參與小組前後的生理壓力變化，以及生理心理壓力反應的相互關係。

22611818.label: Realisation of objectives
22611818.value: The objective of this study is to investigate and compare the effectiveness of CAT and control treatment in promoting the improvement of emotion regulation strategies; enhancement of positive affective states; alleviation of negative affective states; alleviation of deficits in the cognitive processing of affect, as in alexithymia; and reduction in psychological and physiological stress levels. In order to achieve the mentioned objectives, we successfully recruited 94 participants in total, participants were randomly allocated to the intervention or the control group by a 1:1 ratio. We analysed all the data collected in this study which include quantitative psychosocial (questionnaires) and physiological (hair cortisol) data as well as qualitative (focus group) data collected at baseline and/or after the intervention. All students have achieved 80% or more attendance rate and have created multiple pieces of clay artwork during the intervention process. The objectives of this study were achieved, our research team found that treatment of clay art therapy in youth) can improve emotion regulatory (ER) abilities (obj. 1) and elevated cortisol levels hints a strengthened psychophysiological stress-coping mechanism benefiting health (obj 5). Clay art therapy (CAT) has shown significant effects on both positive and negative affective states (obj 2 & 3) and cognitive process of articulating inner eperience (improvement of alexithymia) (obj 4) by strengthening ER. Despite the objectives were achieved in different time-points of the intervention process, the effects were significant. The major quantitative findings on psychophysiological stress reactions in relation to the objectives of the research are reported in manuscripts (8.2) and conference presentations in the Society of Beh Medicine and Taiwan (9.1 and 9.2). Other supporting qualitative data, results, and theoretical underpinnings are reported in two peer-reviewed book chapters (8.3-4). As such, the research result on hair cortisol has great potential as a biomarker for evaluating stress response. We have reported the findings in the conference presentation (9.2). The elevation of hair cortisol concentration after the intervention may not be pathological but a sign of benefit to health. Studies have noted that art therapy is effective in alleviating depression and stress, promoting emotional openness, and improving general health. To supplement the results of the quantitative findings, the research team has also looked into the qualitative data generated from this study. The qualitative exploration focused on the treatment efficacy and the mechanism of art therapy with clay (CAT), on the emotional problem of youth in the context of HK. The results of the qualitative study suggested the therapeutic effects of CAT in three different themes as releasing physical tension, soothing and regulating emotion; building persistence in face of adversities and failures, and; art products as representations of new meanings of life and positive self-image. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) and the outputs (8.1) for details. To sum up, Quantitative results show significant improvements in alleviating different aspects of emotional regulation difficulties and reduction of psychological and physiological stress levels, please refer to (8.2; 9.1). Qualitative analysis showed that the intervention process has helped participants to outlet negative emotions, grow patience, increase courage to face adversity, accept discrepancies between ideal and reality, increase acceptance of imperfection, and soothe emotions, please refer to (8.1; 9.2; 9.3). Qualitative (verbal feedback and focus group) data results, it found that participants were able to relax through the art therapy process, create own meaningful clay artworks, learn different emotional regulation strategies and reflect upon their artistic experience, please refer to the book of the monograph (8.6).

22611818.label: Major findings and research outcome
22611818.value: Research data from this study demonstrated the benefits of clay art therapy on youth with emotional regulation. The finding showed that, when compared to the control group, participants in the clay art therapy showed the mean score of tracking the level of difficulty for regulating emotion in the clay art therapy group decreased significantly throughout the three time-points, suggesting a lasting effect of the intervention in this respect. The results showed that participants with a higher level of baseline depression, anxiety or stress have greater difficulty in regulating emotion. From this research, it showed that Clay Art Therapy (CAT) imbeds physical activities (kinesthetic-sensory processes) and psychological processes (perception, affection, cognition) in clay art making for enhancing emotional adaptation to adversity and coping with stress. Improved emotion regulatory abilities and elevated cortisol levels hints a strengthened psychophysiological stress-coping mechanism benefiting health. Hair cortisol has great potential as a biomarker for evaluating stress response. The Clay art therapy (CAT) process and the created ceramic artworks show powerful therapeutic effects in reorganizing and incorporating challenging experiences and failures, regulating feelings, and instilling new meanings to existential struggles and life issues. The study supports the positive effect of CAT on the emotion regulation ability of youth. What’s more, the quantitative study showed that the elevation of HCC after the intervention may not be pathological but a sign of benefit to health. The results support the significant effects of CAT on both psychological and physiological signs of emotion.

22611818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22611818.value: This study is one of the first studies applying clay art therapy to work on the emotional problems of HK secondary school students. The adoption of art therapy with clay intervention treatment methods will provide an alternative treatment to complement social work stress treatment or support group interventions for youth wrestling with stress issues. The rationale, intervention methods of art therapy, and findings of the research study will have significant implications for national and international healthcare professions, non-governmental organizations, and government bodies to adopt more effective preventive measures to cope with the challenges posed to HK youths today and the youths facing similar challenges over the globe. As such, this proposed study will potentially benefit social welfare, education systems, training of health care professionals at the university level, and continued education for professionals internationally. The research can also facilitate active collaborations among multidiscipline, especially between secondary school educators, social workers, art psychotherapists, and scientists.

Notably, this clay art therapy intervention was conducted in a research setting. The research proposes examining psychological signs of emotional issues and the association with hair cortisol concentration. The study found out that the elevation of hair cortisol concentration after the intervention may not be pathological but a sign of benefit to health.

22612318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22612318.value: The Good Friday Agreement (GFA) was signed in Belfast in April 1998 by the British and Irish governments as well as eight political parties in Northern Ireland. This historic event marks the end of the three-decade-long conflict known as “The Troubles” (1968-1998) fought chiefly among loyalist paramilitaries, nationalist paramilitaries and security forces, resulting in thousands of causalities including Catholic and Protestant civilians. The GFA also brought new institutions (most notably a new version of the power-sharing, “consociational” executive) and political commitments. With qualified and punctuated “success” (McGarry and O’Leary 2017), the GFA has heralded in a new era of relative peace and optimism quite unknown in the region torn by centuries of violence beginning with English colonialism and outliving successive waves of decolonization worldwide. Yet despite the GFA’s historic significance and initial achievements, politics in Northern Ireland has yet to enter the stage of what political theorists call “stable peace” (Kacowicz et al. 2000) or “deep reconciliation” (He 2009). The challenges of imminent Brexit, the recent breakdown of the devolved Executive since early 2017 and the persistent post-GFA “low-intensity” sectarian violence (Balcells et al. 2015) are but some of the reminders of how precarious the peace in Northern Ireland still is, which remains standing in sharp contrast to a post-Reformation, postcolonial and – to a lesser extent – postnational Europe. Beginning in 2018, that is, twenty years on since the signing of the GFA and twenty-five years since the publication of Brendan O’Leary and John McGarry’s celebrated book, The Politics of Antagonism: Understanding Northern Ireland (1993), the proposed three-year research project aims to critically assess the implementation of GFA as a constitutional framework within which various social and political actors employ different resources at their disposal to overcome past and present obstacles to political reconciliation. Adopting Colleen Murphy’s framework for evaluating processes of political reconciliation (2010), the research seeks to determine the level (or lack) of achievement in areas such as political trust and rule of law in the twenty-year period, and to answer whether the predominant political concepts of “antagonism” and “accommodation” (Lijphart 1968) suffice as conceptual opposites to measure the overall accomplishment of the Northern Ireland peace process thus far. In terms of significance and output, aside from producing a number of peer-reviewed articles for high-impact journals, the project also aims to connect and contrast experiences in Northern Ireland and Hong Kong, where some fear a politics of antagonism is fast emerging. 《貝爾法斯特協議》（下稱《協議》）於一九九八年四月由英國政府、愛爾蘭政府及八個北愛爾蘭政黨簽署。 此歷史性協議標誌着一個長達三十年 （1968-1998）、主要涉及聯合、共和兩派準軍事部隊和英軍，並導致數以千計人數死亡（包括天主教和新教基督徒的北愛人民）的衝突之終結。 此外，《協議》亦帶來了新的政治制度和承諾，當中最為顯著的是一個新的協商民主行政機關。儘管《協議》的成功並不盡如人意 (McGarry and O’Leary 2017)，但它為北愛爾蘭開拓了一個相對和平和樂觀的新時代，這在當地由英國殖民統治拉開序幕的悠長暴力史上實屬罕見。 雖然《協議》具有相當歷史意義且取得初步成功，但北愛政治並未進入政治理論家所講的「穩定的和平」(Kacowicz et al. 2000) 或「深層次和解」(He 2009)。誠言，北愛的和平仍面對著不同的威脅，包括英國脫歐、近期的地方政府行政機關癱瘓丶以及後協議時期持續不斷的「低密度」派系暴力事件等 (Balcells et al. 2015) 。在和平問題上，北愛與後宗教改革丶後殖民主義和某程度上相對後愛國主義的歐洲仍存有強烈對比。 二〇一八年是《協議》簽署二十周年，亦是 B. O’Leary 及 J. McGarry 的名著《敵對政治：理解北愛爾蘭》出版廿五載之時，本研究計劃藉此契機，以三年為期，透過批判審視《協議》的實踐，看其作為地方憲制框架如何促進或阻礙社會和政治人士與團體運用自身的資源去克服過去與現在的政治和解障礙。 本研究計劃將參照 Colleen Murphy (2010) 的理論框架去評估北愛政治和解進程，尤其著眼於探討政治互信和法治重建等不同領域在過去二十年間的成果或不足，並嘗試回答「敵對」和「協調」等主流政治概念 (Lijphart 1968) 在二十多年後的今日是否足以作為兩極概念去評定北愛和平進程至今的整體成果。 在研究意義和成果方面，本計劃除了旨在高端學術期刊發表論文，亦有意探索北愛和香港經驗的可比較性，以更好理解本土敵對政治的冒起和建議可行對策。

22613218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22613218.value: The main objective of the current project is the publication of a monograph consisting of the English translation of the recently published (2015) manuscript Zhou xun 周訓 or Instructions of the Zhou and a commentary of the text delving into its political and philosophical underpinnings. More broadly speaking, this is an inquiry into how political and philosophical ideas codified into texts were employed in early China as instruments that validated and justified shifts in power centers. The Zhou xun is part of the Peking University collection (Beijing daxue cang Xi-Han zhushu 北京大學藏西漢竹書). The principle of “elevating the worthy” (shang xian 尚賢) this text promulgates represents one of the most influential ideas in the Chinese society of the late Chuqiu 春秋 as well as Zhanguo 戰國 periods. Following deep changes in Chinese society, resulting from the gradual demise of old aristocratic families, this principle was implemented in many political reforms of the day and promoted in numerous philosophical writings. As some transmitted texts, such as the Shang shu 尚書, and, especially, a bulk of newly discovered manuscripts show, “elevating the worthy” was also applied to the issue of power transfer as the ostensive governance practice of the ancient times when the rulers established the most able men as their successors, regardless of their provenance and their relationship to the rulers’ family. The Zhou xun also contains the idea of elevating the worthy in the context of the transfer of rule. Yet, this meritocratic principle is not brought up to undermine hereditary power transfer but, on the contrary, to consolidate it. In the Zhou xun, the protagonist promulgating this principle is the Zhou monarch, Lord Zhaowen of Zhou 周昭文君. In his discussion of the concept, this monarch makes “worthiness” the main prerequisite for obtaining political power, but never mentions the main paradigm of the Zhou dynasty, the “Mandate of Heaven” (tian ming 天命). At the heart of the commentary will be determining the philosophical and political implications of Lord Zhaowen’s refusal to attach himself to the model of the former Zhou kings and, instead, to solely insist on the importance of “worthiness” for the transfer and preservation of rule. To validate his philosophical interpretation, the PI plans to engage in academic exchange with other scholars in Chinese intellectual history. The same strategy will be applied to ensure the accuracy and validity of the English translation of the Zhou xun. 本計畫旨在探討新出《周訓》中的「尚賢」思想。這部出土文獻屬於《北京大學藏西漢竹書》﹐其抄寫年代大概在公元前一世紀的前半葉。《周訓》與其他提倡「尚賢」的新出土文獻形成了鮮明的對比，因為前者提出「尚賢」的目的是為了支持傳子之制，認為應該將統治權力交給最有能力的繼承人。本計劃主持人認為《周訓》的立場達到以下幾個目的﹕首先，它解決了禪讓說中的核心問題，即「尊賢」與「愛親」之間的衝突﹔其次， 這種對「尚賢」的解釋擴大了王位候選人的範圍，挑戰了長子繼承制這種中國自古以來政治秩序的基石。這個根本性挑戰的目的﹐或許是要為周王室制定一個新的統治範式。《周訓》完全沒有提到「天命」的觀念，也說明了它已經遠離周朝對權力的固有理解。然而，鑑於《周訓》與《呂氏春秋》之間的密切關係，我們也可以說《周訓》的寫作目的是要證明秦滅周的合法性。無論如何，《周訓》給我們提供了有關「尚賢」的原則如何應用於政治的新知識

22613218.label: Major findings and research outcome
22613218.value: The rejection of the rule of primogeniture as the main instrument for determining succession found in the Zhou xun might represent an attempt to formulate a theoretical justification for the wide-spread disregard of the said rule, as many powerholders from the Warring States period and earlier ages, for one reason or another, came to dismiss their first-born sons. However, this central feature of the Zhou xun can be also understood as reflecting specific events that took place in the state of Qin after prince Zichu 子楚, a son by a concubine (nie sun孽孫), ascended the Qin throne and came to be known as King Zhuangxiang of Qin 秦莊襄王 (r. 250–247 BC). To begin with, after coming to power, he grew to become a ruler who stood out through his “virtue” and “kindness” and completed the conquest of the Zhou, effectively becoming their ideological successor. But equally intriguing in this context is his chancellor Lü Buwei 呂不韋 (292–235 BC). Not only was Lü Buwei instrumental in the establishment of Zichu as Qin ruler, he also assisted King Zhuangxiang in conquering the Zhou and, moreover, he oversaw the creation of the Lüshi chunqiu. To recall, in addition to borrowing from the Zhou xun, the Lüshi chunqiu was the only work to hail Lord Zhaowen as a worthy ruler and teacher of King Hui of Qin. While the exact correlation between these facts and the Zhou xun remains, at least under the current state of the field, an issue of speculation, their manifold correspondences cannot be treated as a mere coincidence. In light of the above, I maintain that this manuscript might very well have been created in the aftermath of the Qin’s conquest of the Zhou to assert the superiority of the Qin and praise its king.

22613218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22613218.value: The further development of the research will very much depend on the discovery of new ancient Chinese manuscripts, which deal with the Zhou-Qin transition. Furthermore, attempts to address the ideological ramifications of the Qin conquest of the Zhou, found in the Zhou xun, can be further investigated against the backdrop of other historical and philosophical texts mentioning this momentous event.

22613218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22613218.value: This research sheds light on one of the most important events in Chinese history and is, as such, highly relevant in the context of Chinese historical and philosophical studies. Furthermore, the study reflects on the significant cultural and ideological shifts that took place in the late Warring States period prior to the unification of China through the state of Qin.

23500018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23500018.value: In this study, we will examine a recent change in management voluntary disclosure practice. We notice an increasing number of firms beginning to voluntarily communicate their expected effective tax rate (ETR) with outsiders by issuing management ETR forecasts in recent years. To the best of our knowledge, no study has systematically investigated this important new form of voluntary disclosures yet. Our proposed study attempts to fill this gap by examining the characteristics, determinants, and consequences of management ETR forecast. Management ETR forecasts are different in terms of their timeliness, accuracy, and precision. We will first conduct descriptive analyses on the characteristics of management ETR forecasts to obtain a preliminary understanding of managerial voluntary disclosures of expected income tax rate. In addition, we will examine the industry and year distribution of managerial ETR forecasts and compare the timing of managerial ETR forecasts and analyst ETR forecasts. We will then examine the incentives for management to voluntarily issue ETR forecasts. Prior studies argue that the complexities of tax regulations and business operations cause a lack of understanding about corporate income taxes (e.g., Plumlee 2003; Bauman and Shaw 2005). Thus, we will examine whether external regulation complexity and internal tax complexity are associated with the tendency of managers issuing ETR forecast. In addition, as income tax is an important component of earnings, we argue that managers issue ETR forecasts to help investors better understand earnings forecasts. We thus will examine whether managers are more likely to issue ETR forecasts when the unexpected portion of earnings forecast news is greater. For the consequences of management ETR forecast issuance, we will examine whether management ETR forecasts cause any reactions from analysts and the stock market. In particular, we will examine whether analysts respond to management ETR forecast by issuing their ETR forecasts or revising their initial estimates. We will also test whether the stock market reacts significantly to the information in management ETR forecasts. We believe that an analysis of this growing form of tax-related voluntary disclosure will have a significant contribution to the literature on corporate voluntary disclosures. To the best of our knowledge, our study will be the first one to systematically investigate the characteristics, determinants, and consequences of management ETR forecasts, a new type of voluntary disclosures. In addition, our study will also contribute to our understanding of the information content of disaggregated earnings forecasts given income tax is an important component of earnings. 在此项研究中，我们将研究管理层自愿披露行为的一项近期变化。我们发现近年来，越来越多的公司开始通过发布管理层实际税率预测向投资者透露预期未来实际税率。就我们所知，至今为止没有相关研究关注这一现象。我们的研究计划试图通过检验管理层实际税率预测的特点、决定因素以及披露后果来填补学术界的这一空白。 管理层实际税率预测在及时性、准确性和精确度方面有所差异。在本研究中，为了对管理层实际税率预测取得一个初步的认识，我们首先将对收集的样本做细致的描述性统计。比如，我们将检验管理层实际税率预测的年度和行业分布，比较管理层实际税率预测和分析师实际税率预测在及时性方面的差异等。 同时，我们将会探究管理层自愿性进行实际税率预测的动机。以前文献指出，税收法规以及公司经营的复杂性导致外界对公司实际税负难以理解。因此，我们会检验外部法规的复杂性以及内部经营的复杂性是否会影响公司发布实际税率预测。同时，由于所得税是公司盈利的重要组成部分，我们认为管理层公布实际税率预测是为了帮助投资者更好的理解盈利预测。因此，我们将检验当盈利预测中非预期部分比较大时，管理层是否更有可能公布实际税率预测。 对于管理层实际税率预测的后果，我们将检验分析师以及市场对预测的反应。具体来说，我们将检验分析师是否会跟随管理层预测来发布分析师预测，以及是否会修改之前的分析师预测。同时，我们将检验股票市场是否会对管理层实际税率预测进行反应。 我们相信对管理层实际税率预测这一日益增长的自愿性披露的研究对现有文献有很大贡献。就我们所知，此项研究将会是第一篇对管理层实际税率预测特点，原因以及结果的系统性研究。同时，由于所得税费用是公司盈利的重要组成部分，此项研究也有助于我们对分项盈利预测的理解。

23500018.label: Realisation of objectives
23500018.value: In this project, all three objectives have been fully achieved. A working paper generated from the funded project once received R&R at Review of Accounting Studies. Based on the research objectives and comments received from reviewers, we focus on tax aggressiveness as an important determinant to test the cost-benefit trade-off in management voluntary ETR forecast decisions and the corresponding consequences of ETR forecast issuance. In addition to the objectives listed in the original research proposal, we also consider the role played by media and IRS on firms’ management ETR forecast decisions. We elaborate on how the project objectives have been achieved and what else we have done below. Objective 1: Conduct a descriptive analysis on the characteristics of the management ETR forecast. To achieve this research objective, we first manually collect data on management voluntary ETR forecasts from SEC 8-K filings and the Capital IQ Key Developments database. Based on the initial management voluntary ETR forecast sample, we check a variety of characteristics of the management voluntary ETR forecasts, such as the year and industry distribution, forecast horizon, forecast precision, forecast stickiness, etc. Objective 2: Investigate managers’ motivation to issue ETR forecast. In particular, we will examine whether managers are more likely to issue ETR forecasts when the unexpected portion of earnings forecast news is greater. We will also test whether firms’ tax avoidance activities influence managers’ decisions on ETR forecast issuance. The main focus of this project is to investigate whether and how tax aggressiveness influences firms’ decisions to issue management voluntary ETR forecasts. We theorize tax-aggressive firms’ voluntary ETR forecast issuance decisions as a cost-benefit trade-off. While tax-aggressive firms can enjoy the capital market benefits of improved transparency by issuing forecasts, they have to bear the costs of heightened public attention and regulatory scrutiny. Using the industry–size-adjusted three-year GAAP ETR and tax haven operations as proxies of tax aggressiveness, we find that tax-aggressive firms have a lower propensity and frequency of issuing voluntary ETR forecasts, after controlling for management earnings forecast issuance, earnings forecast surprise, tax complexity, operating complexity, and a variety of other determinants and fixed effects. To substantiate the main findings, we explore potential variations in the cost-benefit trade-off faced by managers in making decisions on ETR forecast issuance. With respect to the costs, our cross-sectional analyses show that the negative relation between tax aggressiveness and the propensity and frequency of management voluntary ETR forecasts is more pronounced for firms with ex ante higher media coverage, closer IRS attention, or greater efforts in establishing brand equity. As for the benefits of issuing voluntary ETR forecasts, our cross-sectional analyses show that the negative relation between tax aggressiveness and the forecast propensity and frequency is muted among firms with greater tax-induced opacity, proxied by tax complexity and analysts’ ETR forecast dispersion. Because our project now mainly focuses on whether tax aggressiveness affects firms’ decisions on management voluntary ETR forecast issuance, we add the unexpected portion of earnings forecast news as an important control variable in the main regressions to control for the market demand for disaggregated forecasts. Objective 3: Investigate the consequences of management ETR forecasts by examining analyst and investor reactions to the issuance of management ETR forecasts. We conduct two groups of consequence analyses to enhance our understanding of the benefits and costs of voluntary ETR forecast issuance. We first investigate whether a voluntary ETR forecast issued by a tax-aggressive firm indeed increases public attention and IRS scrutiny. We find that a voluntary forecast that estimates a lower future ETR indeed leads to more negative media sentiment, particularly for more profitable forecast issuers. In terms of IRS scrutiny, we show that issuing a low ETR forecast increases the IRS downloads of the firm’s SEC filings and the likelihood of the IRS auditing the firm, especially for firms with ex ante higher media coverage. We then provide direct evidence of the capital market benefits of voluntary ETR forecast. We find that voluntary ETR forecasts generate significant stock price reactions, improve analyst ETR forecast accuracy, and reduce the cost of equity capital.

23500018.label: Major findings and research outcome
23500018.value: In this project, we investigate a unique form of tax-related voluntary disclosures, namely, management voluntary effective tax rate (ETR) forecasts, which have been prevalent among public firms but largely overlooked by prior studies. We are particularly interested in whether tax-aggressive firms are more or less likely to issue voluntary ETR forecasts. We argue that tax-aggressive firms face a trade-off in this disclosure choice. While they can enjoy the capital market benefits of improved transparency by issuing forecasts, they have to bear the costs of heightened public attention and regulatory scrutiny. Our empirical results show that tax-aggressive firms have a lower propensity and frequency of issuing voluntary ETR forecasts, suggesting that, for such firms, managers’ concerns over public attention and IRS scrutiny dominate the capital market benefits. We also implement a comprehensive set of tests to understand more about the costs and benefits of management voluntary ETR forecasts. Our cross-sectional analyses show that the negative association between tax aggressiveness and the issuance of management voluntary ETR forecasts is stronger for firms that are more prone to media coverage, IRS attention, or loss of reputational capital, and weaker for firms with higher tax complexity or tax-induced information uncertainty. Further, we find that management voluntary forecasts that reveal a lower future ETR indeed attract negative media coverage, especially for more profitable firms. Management voluntary ETR forecasts that reveal aggressive tax strategies are also associated with greater IRS attention and higher likelihood of IRS audits, particularly for firms with higher ex ante media coverage. Finally, we provide direct evidence on the benefits of issuing management voluntary ETR forecasts by showing that voluntary ETR forecasts generate significant stock price reactions, improve analyst ETR forecast accuracy, and reduce the cost of equity capital. The working paper generated from this project once received R&R at Review of Accounting Studies. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to provide systematic evidence on whether tax-aggressive firms are more or less likely to issue voluntary ETR forecasts. In addition, we extend the literature on reputational concerns related to tax avoidance by showing that public attention and regulatory scrutiny can be nontrivial friction that deters managers of tax-aggressive firms from providing ETR forecasts. Our study also adds to the broader literature on voluntary disclosure by investigating ETR forecasts as an important but underexplored disclosure tool.

23500018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23500018.value: The area of management voluntary ETR forecast is underexplored. We are one of the first to investigate this tax-related voluntary disclosure. We expect to publish this paper in a high-quality journal. After that, we can do another paper exploring the characteristics of voluntary ETR forecast, such as the forecast accuracy/bias and timeliness, and investigate the strategic disclosure behavior of voluntary ETR forecast.

23500018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23500018.value: In recent years, whether companies pay their “fair share” of tax has become a headline issue. Companies face unprecedented scrutiny of their tax strategies by the media, activist groups, and regulators. News articles report that the media and activist groups do pay attention to corporate disclosures to obtain information to evaluate firms’ tax strategies. In this project, we show that to avoid unfavorable public perceptions and IRS scrutiny, tax-aggressive firms are less likely to communicate their future ETRs with investors by issuing voluntary ETR forecasts. Further analyses reveal that after issuing a voluntary ETR forecast, tax-aggressive firms attract more negative media coverage, IRS downloads of their financial information, and IRS audits. We also find that voluntary ETR forecasts indeed benefit firms by generating significant stock price reactions, improving analysts’ ETR forecast accuracy, and reducing the cost of equity capital. This study enhances our understanding of management voluntary ETR forecast, which has gained prevalence among public firms but has been largely overlooked by prior studies. We also extend the literature on reputational concerns related to tax avoidance by showing that public attention and regulatory scrutiny can be nontrivial friction that deters managers of tax-aggressive firms from providing ETR forecasts.

23500218.label: Project Objectives
23500218.value: To investigate effects of perspective flexibility on social behaviors in a service setting that are likely to involve a shift in perspective, and to examine the extent to which individuals with chronic and situationally activated cultural syndromes differ in their attribution and other reactions to a service failure in ways that are traceable to differences in perspective flexibility. To explain the cultural differences in susceptibility to fundamental attribution error by providing a novel perspective-flexibility-based mechanism in a service setting. To refine both the measure of perspective flexibility and the procedures for manipulating it, and to determine the extent to which it can account for the effects of cultural syndromes on various forms consumer behaviors. To differentiate perspective flexibility with a more general cognitive flexibility. Whereas perspective flexibility reflects the extent to which an individual mentally travels to multiple perspectives in making judgments on social events, cognitive flexibility determines the number of thoughts that are generated when taking a given perspective.

23500218.label: Realisation of objectives
23500218.value: The objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Related to Objective 1, our paper published at the Journal of Marketing Research (JMR, top-tier journal in business, UTD24, FT50, ABDC A*) conceptualized consumers’ ascription versus achievement mindset, a cultural syndrome-based cognitive process of applying family origin or achievement as the basis for evaluation of brand endorsers. The paper uncovered a process-transfer model, such that consumers’ ascription versus achievement mindset is flexible enough to shift to the evaluation of the products/services associated with the endorser. In one of the experiments, we used British restaurants as the stimuli to generalize the process-transfer model to services. Another paper published at the Journal of Marketing (JM, top-tier journal in business, UTD24, FT50, ABDC A*) showed that consumers interpret marketing communications that describe a reduction in a product’s negative attributes (e.g., “our mineral water now uses 34% less plastic”) in a flexible manner, depending on the perspective they take about the changeability of the world. That is, a cultural syndrome-based cognitive process, consumers’ incremental versus entity mindset, can shift to product evaluation and determine whether consumers are positively or negatively influenced by such marketing communications. Still another paper published at the Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (JEP:G, top-tier journal in psychology, ABDC A*) showed a cultural difference in consumers’ flexibility in the extent to which they pay attention to contextual information, for example, to think about stimulus elements in relation to their context and to think about stimulus elements in relation to one another. Related to Objective 2, our paper published at the JMR showed that when consumers attribute an endorser’s status to his/her origin-related (vs. performance-related) features (e.g., family background vs. achievement), they form a who-one-is (vs. what-one-does) mindset, which lead them to use a conceptually similar cognitive process to evaluate the endorsed product (i.e., evaluating based on the product’s origin vs. function related information). The effect was shown robust in both traditional goods and services settings. Another paper published at the JEP:G further found a cultural difference in considering contextual information (either self-context or self-another relationship) in making cognitive judgment, which has important implication for fundamental attribution error. Related to Objective 3, we developed/refined multiple measures that shed light on various aspects of perspective flexibility. Our paper published at the JMR developed a set of measures the flexibility consumers shift their perspective in evaluating endorsers to their perspective in evaluation of endorsed products (i.e., ascription vs. achievement mindset), as an initial step of exploring a more general flexibility of shifting various mindsets from human evaluation to product/brand evaluation. Another paper published at the JEP:G obtained a clearer picture of the multidimensionality of holistic thinking, a concept closely related to perspective flexibility. We constructed a procedure that could be used both to assess and to induce three different styles of cognitive processing that reflect different aspects of holistic thinking. Related to Objective 4, two of our papers published at JM and JMR documented the distinct effects of two pairs of conceptually similar mindsets concerning consumers’ flexibility in generalizing cognitive process to various targets. In the JM paper, a “who-one-is mindset” refers to the cognitive strategy of emphasizing a target’s inherited characteristics to evaluate it. In contrast, a “what-one-does mindset” involves the strategy of applying a target’s performance to generate an evaluation. In the JMR paper, whereas an entity mindset is characterized by the belief that traits are dispositional, an incremental mindset is associated with the belief in continual changes of traits with time and effort. We argue that an incremental mindset focuses on the change in the observed activity, which leads consumers to emphasize the trend of product improvement. In contrast, an entity mindset, which focuses on the state of an observed activity, leads consumers to interpret the communications based on the end state. In our JEP:G paper, We isolated three different components of holistic thinking: (a) a focus on global characteristics of a stimulus independently of the features that compose it, (b) a consideration of individual features of a situation in relation to their context, and (c) a consideration of features of a stimulus in relation to one another.

23500218.label: Major findings and research outcome
23500218.value: Three major findings are yielded from this project with a general focus of the role of perspective flexibility related mindsets/cognitive process in consumer judgment and decision making. One paper, published in 2020 on Journal of Marketing Research (top-tier journal in business, UTD24, FT50, ABDC A*), suggests that the way in which consumers evaluate an endorser (i.e., the cognitive process, such as applying family origin or achievement as the basis for evaluation) will carry over to the evaluation of the endorsed product (e.g., applying country of origin or performance as the criteria). Because the process transfer is not inherently associated with positive/negative valence, it provides a theoretical rationale for explaining successful endorsements involving endorsers who are less favorable/credible, less of a “fit” with the product, or associated with some negative meanings. Another paper, published in 2020 on Journal of Marketing (top-tier journal in business, UTD24, FT50, ABDC A*), focus on marketing communications that often describe a reduction in a product’s negative attributes (e.g., “our mineral water now uses 34% less plastic”). This claim may be interpreted as a trend of improving relative to previous state. However, such a claim may also call attention to a negative product feature that might have otherwise been overlooked. Our research suggests that whether consumers are positively or negatively influenced by such claims depends on whether the claims are interpreted through an incremental or entity mindset. When a reduction in negative attributes is viewed through an incremental mindset—the tendency to think of attributes as malleable—a trend-based interpretation results in improved product evaluations. In contrast, an entity mindset that emphasizes attributes are unlikely to change produces a negative effect for the claim. The third paper, published in 2021 on Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (top-tier journal in psychology, ABDC A*), obtained a clearer picture of the multidimensionality of holistic thinking. We constructed a procedure that could be used both to assess and to induce three different processing styles that reflect different aspects of holistic thinking: specifically, the tendencies (a) to respond to the configuration of a stimulus as a whole without regard to the elements that compose it, (b) to think about stimulus elements in relation to their context, and (c) to think about stimulus elements in relation to one another. Indian, Hong Kong Chinese, North American, and British participants differed in their tendency to use these types of thinking.

23500218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23500218.value: As shown from the summary of the research outcome, this project’s objectives have been successfully achieved. While the project has been productive in terms of publication, there is great potential for further development of this project. For example, (a) How does perspective flexibility influence actor-observer bias? (b) is the process-transfer model documented in our JMR paper generalizable to other cognitive processes besides who-one-is and what-one-does mindset? (c) how to identify the dimensions of perspective flexibility that our measures provide? The first priority along this line is to push the working papers forward through the review process and hopefully publish it in the coming several years. It is also our plan to further extend the findings of some of the published papers and build new research projects correspondingly.

23500218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23500218.value: A provider’s service can often fail to meet a customer’s expectations. For example, a restaurant customer might be badly treated by a waiter or the service might be exceptionally slow. The rapid growth of businesses that serve customers from diverse cultural backgrounds has amplified the need to understand cultural differences in customers’ reactions to a service failure. An emerging stream of research has examined these differences. This research provides a novel perspective to investigate how cultural differences influence reactions to services failure. Our conceptualization is based, in part, on evidence that members from different cultures differ in their perspective flexibility, or, their disposition to take an allocentric perspective (e.g., another person’s point of view) into account when they construe a social event. Consequently, this flexibility increases the customers’ understanding of the provider’s situational constraints and decreases the perceptions that the provider’ dispositional factors (e.g., professionalism) are responsible for the service failure. Eventually, flexible customers are more willing to patronize the provider in the future despite the failure that has occurred. This research provides new insights into the nature of cultural differences in consumer behavior in a service setting and also enhances the understanding of social attribution process in general.
