23500918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23500918.value: 監管機構在財務報告中的作用: 來自中國證券交易所年報問詢函的證據

23500918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23500918.value: Whether public enforcement can help protect investors is critically important in countries with weak investor protection because private enforcement mechanisms usually do not work well due to lack of an independent judiciary (La Porta et al., 2006). The proposed project will analyze the efficacy of the filing review program undertaken by the Chinese stock exchanges to enforce disclosure and accounting standards. In China, the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges regularly review corporate annual reports to ensure compliance with disclosure and accounting standards. During the annual reports review process, the exchange staff can issue letters to the company requesting supplemental information to clarify the company’s disclosure and accounting practices. This process can result in a company having to amend/restate its previously-filed annual report. Using exchange letters and companies’ response letters/amendments collected from the stock exchanges’ websites and CNINF’s website, the proposed project will first analyze the content and resolution of comment letters issued by the Chinese stock exchanges. The analysis will help researchers understand the issues that Chinese regulators are most concerned about. Next, the proposed study will investigate what kinds of companies are more like to be targeted by the Chinese stock exchanges. It will test the hypothesis that companies that are subject to heightened regulatory scrutiny and have lower financial reporting quality are more likely to receive exchange comments and incur more remediation costs. Finally, the proposed project will examine whether Chinese stock exchanges’ reviews of annual reports improve the information environment for investors. The resource constraints view suggests that the exchange staff can identify and rectify material disclosure and reporting deficiencies and violations of securities laws. Therefore, the companies will remedy the deficiencies by providing substantial disclosures and transparent financial reporting. It is possible that annual report reviews have a positive effect on the information environment. The proposed project will make two contributions to the literature on regulatory oversight. First, it will contribute to the regulation compliance literature by conducting a comprehensive analysis of the determinants of firms’ compliance with disclosure and accounting regulations in a representative weak legal regime, China. Second, the proposed project will be the first to study the effect of regulator’s filing reviews on the information environment in China. The research findings will inform the debate on whether public enforcement can help protect investors, especially in weak investor protection countries. 公共執法機制是否有助於保護投資者在投資者保護薄弱的國家至關重要，因為私人執法機制在這些國家由於缺乏獨立的司法機構，通常效果不佳 (La Porta et al., 2006)。本擬議項目將分析中國證券交易所執行信息披露和會計準則而對上市公司提交年度財務報告審閱計劃的有效性。 在中國，上海和深圳證券交易所定期審查公司年度報告，以確保上市公司遵守披露和會計標準。在年度報告審核過程中，交易所員工可以向公司發出問詢函件要求補充信息以澄清公司的披露和會計實踐。 這個問詢過程可能導致公司不得不修改或重述其先前提交的年度報告內容。 擬議項目將從證券交易所網站和巨潮網站收集證券交易所問詢函和公司回复函以及財務報告補充更正，首先分析中國證券交易所發布的問詢函的內容和上市公司相應的整改措施。該文本分析將幫助研究人員了解中國證券監管機構最關心的披露和會計問題。其次，擬議的研究將調查什麼樣的公司是中國證券交易所的披露審查目標。它將檢驗這一假設即那些面臨監管機構嚴格審查和財務報表質量較低的公司更可能收到證券交易所問詢函并發生更多的補救費用。最後，擬議的項目將檢驗中國證券交易所對年度報告的審閱是否改善了投資者的信息環境。資源限制視角表明交易所員工可以識別和糾正重大披露和報告缺陷和違反證券法的行為。因此，公司將通過提供實質性披露和透明的財務報告來彌補披露缺陷。從而，年度報告審閱可能會對上市公司信息環境產生積極影響。 擬議的項目將對資本市場監管文獻做出兩點貢獻。 首先，它將通過全面分析企業在一個具有代表性的弱法律制度國家，中國，遵守披露和會計法規的決定因素，從而充實了法律合規文獻。第二，擬議的項目將是第一個研究中國監管機構信息披露事後審閱對投資者信息環境的影響。研究結果將為關於公共執法機制在弱投資者保護制度國家是否有助於保護投資者這一爭論提供建議。

23600918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23600918.value: Political participation of the younger generation has always been a cornerstone of effective governance. Despite a chorus of worries over youth disengagement from politics, young people today have shown sustained political interest and have sought to engage in politics in innovative ways. However, while much work has focused on Western democracies, few studies have examined youth political participation in nondemocratic contexts, especially hybrid ones, where young people are partially excluded from politics and struggle to make their voices heard. Most of the limited works have focused on youth activists rather than ordinary young people. The questions of why and how ordinary youth participate, and whether they persist in political participation over their life-course, becomes particularly important when waves of political activism in such contexts have often failed to bring about genuine democratic changes. After taking part in activism and then coping with the realities of regime resilience, how do young people in non-democracies understand politics? What make them persist and what leads them to reduce participation or disengage? How do they seek new ways to involve in politics? Post-handover Hong Kong offers an ideal setting to examine these questions. As a resilient hybrid regime, Hong Kong has witnessed a growing trend in youth political participation since the mid-2000s, challenging government policies and legitimacy in the form of popular protests. While studies have analysed the causes and consequences of youth contention, none of them have thoroughly explained what drives youth political engagement, or what motivates variations in political attitudes and behaviour within the youth cohort. Nor have these works attempted to explain the continuity of participation, or how past political experiences shape subsequent participation. The protest-ridden, hybrid regime context of Hong Kong provides a fitting opportunity for researchers to understand the evolution of political participation as a dynamic and contingent process. This project aims to study the intensity and continuity of youth political participation in contemporary Hong Kong. Using both quantitative and qualitative methods, the project will 1) identify the variations in forms of political participation both within the youth cohorts and across age groups, 2) explain the variations of the intensity and continuity of participation through individual-level factors, 3) examine the endogenous impact of past participatory experiences, and 4) map new ways that youth participate in politics. In doing so, it hopes to bring theoretical insights to the scholarship of political participation, facilitate cross-national comparisons and impact policy. 青年政治參與是民主管治的重要元素。然而，學術界大部分關注這個課題的研究都集中以西方民主國家為案例，而對於混合政權下青年如何參與政治的問題，則缺乏充分的理解。在民主不健全或尚未健全的制度下，青年人如何理解政治參與？面對政治參與和抗爭的種種風險，是甚麼驅使青年持續、減少或退出參與政治事務？他們如何以創新的手法介入政治? 此研究以回歸後的香港為背景，旨在理解推動青年政治參與的深層原因。研究問題包括：1）青年以什麼樣的方式介入政治？2）甚麼個人層面的原因解釋政治參與的投入度和持續性？3）以往的政治經歷如何影響個人當下的政治參與？4）青年有何創新的手法介入政治？透過這些問題，我們希望能夠在理論層面上探尋青年政治參與的動力和變化，並在政策層面上令青年參政有助推動香港的民主管治。

23600918.label: Realisation of objectives
23600918.value: The research objectives have been achieved as planned. A range of research impact activities and outputs have also been disseminated in reputable academic and public venues. Objective 1: The PI has produced a set of original and large-n data about the patterns of political participation of citizens in Hong Kong using a mixed-methods approach. The collected data included: - A youth cohort survey (n=545) that incorporates questions concerning history and frequency of political participation, political values and attitudes, sources of information, and basic demographics. In addition, it also incorporates measures of economic precarity to investigate the impact of economic circumstances on political participation, as well as the intention of emigration to examine exit-voice dynamics. - A population survey (n=4438) that targeted all age cohorts in order to compare with the youth cohort survey. The questions included are identical. Despite the large sample size of this survey, the pollster’s database has a disproportionate number of older respondents. Therefore, a separate youth cohort survey was conducted to enlarge the sample size of younger respondents and facilitate more robust comparisons. - Ten youth cohort focus groups were conducted (n=45) to gauge youth’s understanding of politics as well as patterns of social and political participation. I focused on questions concerning when respondents first became interested in politics and first participated in protests and voting, how they perceived the meaning of politics, and how they participated after the 2019 protests. I also asked substantively about particular issues respondents are concerned with, such as community, LGBT rights, and environmental justice. Objective 2 The findings have provided persuasive evidence to identify the variations in political participation across age groups. By comparing the youth cohort survey with the population survey, the PI identified a number of empirically important and theoretical interesting patterns. - While older cohorts (aged >35) had great interest in politics, they were less active in political participation than the younger cohorts. Younger cohorts (aged 18-35) were particularly more active in non-conventional modes of participation such as protesting, sharing political information online and political consumption. But they are also similar in other aspects: low trust in government institutions, low intention to vote or contact government officials, and low external efficacy. - Compared with the older cohorts, younger cohorts were more interested in issues such as community, LGBT rights, women’s rights, fair trade, heritage, environmental justice, and data privacy. Older cohorts were more concerned with issues like economic development. However, despite their postmaterialist orientation, youth cohorts are more concerned with housing issues. This makes sense given the unaffordability of housing in Hong Kong. - Younger cohorts tended to be more postmaterialist. This explains why younger respondents show interest in the issues mentioned above. Nevertheless, the fact that the youth cohort remains concerned with housing indicates that materialist orientations remain relevant. The lingering importance of the materialist dimension is augmented by the fact that the youth cohort tended to see themselves as more economically precarious. Objective 3&4 The findings have provided evidence to identify and explain the variations in political participation within the youth cohort. Some youth are more politically active than others in terms of both conventional and non-conventional participation. We identified several important factors that cause these variations, including life satisfaction and economic precarity. For example, youth who are more dissatisfied with their lives are more likely to participate in unconventional political participation, such as political consumption and sharing political news online. They also tend to have a higher intention to emigrate. Those who are more satisfied with their lives, however, are more likely to make donations to political causes and participate in recycling. On the other hand, youth who feel more economically precarious are less likely to have participated in protests as well as other forms of conventional modes of participation. Another finding is young people’s use of social media in protest campaigns. The PI found that young people relied heavily on Instagram during the 2019 Anti-Extradition Movement to network with one another and to access social capital, which allowed them to overcome their shortage of resources. This extensive use of Instagram was not observed among the older cohorts. The finding shows that there is a clear intergenerational difference in how people participate in social movements. Objective 5 The objective was achieved through the focus groups. While the surveys provided data on respondents' political participation, focus groups offered qualitative explanations of how participants perceived politics and why they became politically involved. One significant finding was that social movements often serve as "entry points" for citizens to become interested in politics. Some participants mentioned joining annual June 4 vigils and July 1 rallies, while others referred to the 2014 Umbrella Movement and the 2019 Anti-Extradition Movement. These events became the lens through which they made sense of Hong Kong politics and shaped their political identities. For example, young people who participated in the Umbrella Movement as their first protest were more likely to identify with localist ideals. Another major finding was that contentious events had a significant impact on political participation during movement abeyance. The PI found that many participants of the Umbrella Movement continued to engage in everyday politics in territorial communities. Emphasizing "intensive cultivation," they practiced "lived citizenship" through various neighborhood initiatives, such as exposing corrupt practices in the district council, organizing walking tours, fixing home appliances for residents, screening films on the streets, and publishing community newspapers. These attempts, aiming to rescale politics to the local level and building the groundwork for democracy, were partly inspired by participatory experiences in the Umbrella Movement and the public backlash against it. Activists learned that they had to "do something" to promote their cause while seeking to rebuild relationships with grassroots citizens. Challenges and limitations The research faced two big challenges. The first was the outbreak of the 2019 Anti-Extradition Movement. Although the protests provided an opportunity to study political participation up close, they postponed the population and youth cohort surveys because they could have been biased responses toward protest participation. The second was the COVID-19 pandemic, which began around February 2020 and continued until the project's end date. Social restrictions and health concerns made it challenging to conduct the surveys. For example, the population survey was originally a telephone-based survey. However, given the difficulty for polling agencies to recruit interviewers at the height of the pandemic, conducting a telephone-based survey became impractical. Therefore, the PI had to change to an online survey (a downside being that the sample has to be weighted). Similarly, the youth cohort survey was originally designed to be a street-intercept survey. However, the pollster (Academy of Hong Kong Studies) suggested that conducting a street-intercept survey in pandemic and post-protest times might pose health and political risks to the survey helpers, and they turned down the original arrangement. Consequently, the PI decided to drop the street-intercept survey and instead conducted an online survey focused on the youth cohort. Online surveys are cheaper than the telephone-based and street intercept survey. Originally, the telephone-based survey would have cost HKD200K and the street-intercept survey HKD100K; while the new surveys only cost around HKD70K in total. This explains the budget under-utilisation. I hope the panel can take this into consideration and understand that the project was completed under challenging and changing circumstances.

23600918.label: Major findings and research outcome
23600918.value: My research has resulted in a number of outputs published in reputable venues, including five conference papers, three journal articles, and three newspaper op-eds. A book manuscript about Hong Kong’s contentious politics is currently under review by the Cambridge University Press. These outputs have provided valuable contributions to social movement studies, political sociology and area studies, while offering insights for policymaking. Five conference papers were presented, including a conference in the Australian Centre on China in the World, Australian National University (December 2022), a seminar in University of British Columbia (October 2022), the annual conference of Latin American Studies Association (February 2022), the annual conference of American Political Science Association (September 2020), and a seminar in Australian National University (November 2019). Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the PI attended most of these conferences virtually. The only exceptions are the November 2019 seminar and December 2022 conference, both of which took place in the Australian National University. The PI attended them in-person, and the travel expenses were covered by the organizer. This explained why the conference budget was not utilized. Three peer-reviewed articles have been published at highly reputable journals. The China Review article, which has been cited 182 times since publication, provided a rich descriptive account of the origins and characteristics of the 2019 Anti-Extradition Law Amendment Bill Movement. It explained how the protests unexpectedly emerged despite the absence of favourable conditions amidst a declining trend of political efficacy, and illustrated core characteristics of the protests through the survey data. The Social Movement Studies article studies how young people organized protest actions during the 2019 protests despite their lack of resources. It argues that digitally-based, informal social movement groups formed by student activists played a crucial role in unleashing their social capital. By activating their schools’ alumni networks, school reputation and joint-school ties, these digitally-based groups initiated a wide array of collective actions. This article has been awarded as the first runner-up of the Social Movement Studies Britta Baumgarten Memorial Prize 2022 and has been made open access by the journal. The China Journal article, which has been recently accepted, spotlights the "abeyance" politics of community activism, in which activists sought to make territorial communities an arena of social and political participation in quieter times after mass mobilizations. It argues that community activism served as “abeyance structures” after the mass mobilizations in the early 2010s. These abeyance structures not only allowed activists to maintain their political engagement, but also gave rise to various practices of “lived citizenship” in territorial communities that produced a changing sense of political subjectivity among citizens. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, many academic conferences/seminars were cancelled. In the context, knowledge transfer activities for this research could not be organized. The PI instead tried to facilitate knowledge transfer through publishing newspaper op-eds. All the three op-eds were published in Mingpao and made use of the survey data to illustrate the political behaviour of young citizens in Hong Kong.

23600918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23600918.value: The PI is developing two other manuscripts using the survey and focus group data – one focusing on youth precarity and political values, another related to their political participation and intention to emigrate. Given that the surveys incorporated questions regarding the socioeconomic conditions and attitudes of young people (e.g., sense of precarity, utilisation of income, views toward social equity), further research – potentially a GRF project – can be developed along this direction to study the impact of precarity on young people’s social values and behaviour. For example, one interesting question is to understand why young people still feel precarious despite being employed, and what are their strategies to overcome such senses of precarity. As a global city with high housing prices and endemic inequalities, Hong Kong provides an excellent case to examine the causes and consequences of youth precarity.

23600918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23600918.value: Youth political participation has always been a cornerstone of effective governance. Despite a chorus of worries over youth disengagement from politics, young people today have shown sustained political interest and have sought to engage in politics in innovative ways. The questions of why and how ordinary youth participate, and whether they persist over their life-course, becomes particularly important when waves of political activism in such contexts have often failed to bring about genuine democratic changes. After taking part in activism and then coping with the realities of regime resilience, how do young people in non-democracies understand politics? What makes them persist and what leads them to reduce participation or disengage? How do they seek new ways to get involved in politics? Focusing on Hong Kong, this study has examined how young people understand politics and their political role, as well as to identify variations in political participation across age groups and within the youth cohort. The project uses a mixed-methods approach and has collected original data that include two large-n surveys and focus groups with Hong Kong youth aged 18 to 35. The findings have identified patterns of social and political participation among citizens, as well as variations in political participation across age groups and within the youth cohort. The research also explores the dynamic nature of participation and the changing trajectories of young people’s engagement, the factors that motivate and enable youth political participation, as well as some of their innovative practices.

23601618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601618.value: ‘Made-in-China Nollywood’ aims to understand the connections between diasporic cultural production and regimes of transnational mobility through a focus on the migration and creative journeys of China-based West African filmmakers and musicians, within the context of China's One Belt One Road Initiative (OBOR). ‘Made-in-China Nollywood’ is an ethnographic and film analysis project that takes the production of films and music videos as its empirical focus. Firstly, the project will generate ethnographic insights into the transnational experiences of the producers of this media. Secondly, it will critically examine the meanings (e.g. imagery, narratives) embedded in their media production. Thirdly, it will link both ethnographic findings and textual analysis to historical and contemporary geopolitical conjunctures, and to theoretical understandings of transnational mobility, diaspora, migrant filmmaking, entrepreneurialism, cultural production and globalisation. Nollywood is a travelling cultural form/product identified by many Africans as ‘uniquely African’ (Makhubu 2015), and a ‘truly pan-African affair’ (Krings & Okome 2013). As a video-making practice, Nollywood is often theorised within the African context or in relation to Europe or America. ‘Made-in-China Nollywood’ opens up a new line of critical investigation into the paths that Nollywood is taking in the context of the rise of China. In the last decade, China-based artists from Nigeria, Ghana and Cameroon have been laying down the foundations of a budding filmic universe. Their cultural production often portrays China as a new ‘land of opportunity’ where novel diasporic narratives about success, failure and romance are articulated. This project will argue that cultivating the talents of these artists — instead of making it difficult for them to remain in the country — could prove beneficial to China’s attempt at tapping into African cultural industries. Recently, governments in China and Africa vowed to increase funding for the arts —filmmaking, in particular. Indeed, two of the ‘soft power’ strategies recently laid out in the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) were: promoting Chinese cinema across Africa; and tapping into the enormous economic opportunities offered by Nollywood and other regional film industries/markets. While Sino-African exchanges are not new, their recent intensification illustrates that the impacts in both regions can no longer be ignored. Arguably, the study of Sino-African exchanges is also the study of contemporary Chinese society, in that African presence in China (and vice versa) are indicative of China’s remarkable shift into becoming not only a more cosmopolitan but also a transnational, and potentially immigrant, society. 《中國製造羅里活(Nollywood)》嘗試在中國一帶一路的語境下，從在華西非電影工作者的遷移和創作歷程，理解離散文化生產和跨國移動管治(regimes of transational mobilty)之間的關係。 《中國製造羅里活》 是結合了民族誌和電影分析的研究計畫，集中研究電影和音樂錄像生產。該計劃希望增加對理解這些媒體的生產者的跨國經驗的民族誌角度。此外，計畫亦會檢視媒體生產當中的意義構成（從影像、敘事等等）。最後，計畫會把民族誌觀察和文本分析，連接現今的地緣政治形勢(conjuncture)，跨國移動，離散，移民電影生產，創業主義，文化生產和全球化的理論分析。 羅里活 (Nollywood) 是一個移動的文化形式和商品，不少非洲人認為它是「非洲人獨有的」(Makhubu 2015)和「真正的泛非洲事務」(Krings & Okome 2013)。作為一種影像生產實踐，羅里活通常是在非洲語境以及跟歐美國家的關係下給理論化的。《中國製造羅里活》開展了一個新的研究方向，把羅里活放置在中國崛起的語境下來理解。 在過去十年，來自尼日利亞，迦納和喀麥隆的在華藝術家持續建立一個電影宇宙(filmic universe)。他們的文化生產把中國描述成一個「機會之地」，接合了關於成功，失敗和浪漫的新離散敘事。這個研究計畫提出，培養這些藝術家的才能，而不是讓他們更難以居留，將會有助於中國進入非洲文化產業的嘗試。 近年，中國和非洲各國政府都增加了對藝術的資助，特別是電影創作。中非合作論壇(FOCAC) 確立了兩個軟實力策略：擴展中國電影在非洲的宣傳以及在羅里活和其他地區電影工業和市場所產生出來的巨大經濟機遇中分一杯羹。 儘管中非合作不是新事，近年的頻密發展，對兩地的影響不容忽視。研究中非交流同時也是研究現今的中國社會，非洲在中國，或中國在非洲的存在，指出了中國已經轉變成為一個不單是國際化，同時也是跨國界，和移民組成的社會。

23601618.label: Realisation of objectives
23601618.value: This research project has achieved most of its objectives, conducting a comprehensive exploration of the media representation of West African presence in China. The objective to shed light on this less researched aspect was accomplished, providing accessible and intellectually stimulating insights for scholars, students, and the general public. The examination of issues such as representation, racialization, migration, and aspiration in Sino-African exchanges was also completed. While the original plan aimed to expand existing theorizations of 'global Nollywood' from an Asian perspective, significant progress in this aspect faced challenges due to pandemic-related restrictions. The research strategies devised to overcome these obstacles led the project in a slightly different direction (still keeping in line with the original research objectives), emphasizing the theoretical exploration of representation, race, and racism, as reflected in the publications associated with this research project. Furthermore, the aim to produce a theoretically reflexive yet grounded account of how multiple regimes of mobility in Asia impact Africa's diasporic cultural production reached about 80 per cent completion, influenced by the same constraints as the previous objective. Finally, the objective to inform cultural policymakers and the general public about opportunities, possibilities, and constraints in cultural exchanges between African and Chinese communities can be considered highly accomplished, as evidenced by the impact generated through the project's publications. It is important to keep in mind that, as noted in previous reports, during most of the time planned for ethnographic research in this project there was no access to China due to China’s Zero Covid policy. This project was highly impacted by the pandemic.

23601618.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601618.value: The research yielded significant insights into the complex interplay of representation, race, and migration within the context of the West African presence in China. The exploration of issues such as racialization, migration, and aspiration in Sino-African exchanges uncovered nuanced patterns and narratives. The shift in focus towards representation and race, prompted by pandemic-related challenges, resulted in notable publications that contribute to contemporary discussions on these themes. The theoretical exploration of how multiple regimes of mobility in Asia impact Africa's diasporic cultural production unveiled valuable perspectives. The project's major findings underscore the dynamic nature of cultural interactions and highlight the evolving narratives within the global mobility landscape.

23601618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601618.value: Building on the major findings and outcomes, there exists promising potential for further development in this research. To expand on the theoretical exploration of representation, race, and racism initiated during the project, a deeper analysis of the evolving narratives within West African cultural production in China and beyond is warranted. Furthermore, considering the increasing significance of Sino-African exchanges, future research could delve into the impact on contemporary Chinese society, particularly examining the implications of African presence in China and vice versa. This multifaceted approach would provide a more comprehensive understanding of the cultural dynamics at play, extending the research's impact and relevance. The PI has already followed this lead by successfully securing a GRF project on the topic of social media representation.

23601618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601618.value: This research project, titled 'Made-in-China Nollywood,' delves into the intriguing intersection of West African presence in China and the dynamic world of cultural production. The study successfully illuminates this less-explored facet, shedding light on the migration and creative journeys of China-based West African filmmakers and musicians. Despite challenges posed by the pandemic, the research navigated a nuanced exploration of representation, race, and migration in Sino-African exchanges, leading to insightful publications that enrich contemporary discussions. The project's outcomes, though evolving due to unforeseen circumstances, present a valuable contribution to understanding the intricate dynamics of diasporic cultural production in the global context. Looking ahead, the research suggests potential avenues for deeper exploration, emphasizing the need to delve into specific media forms, reconsider the original goal of expanding 'global Nollywood' theorizations, and examining the broader impacts of Sino-African exchanges on contemporary Chinese society. In essence, this project's significance lies in unraveling the complex interplay of cultures, migration, and representation within the evolving landscape of global mobility.

23601918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601918.value: This project traces an alternate literary history in which the material labour of women—the secretaries, muses, and wives of important literary figures—has been as invisible as the labour and production of material technologies. The twentieth and twenty-first centuries saw a paradigmatic shift in content production from analogue to digital forms, as digital content—for instance, in digital image rendering—can mask its own material traces. As technological screens provide an “illusion of media immateriality” (Raley 2017), the stakes of materiality intensify: archive gives way to database, object gives way to image, and process gives way to product. Responding to these shifts, this project identifies losses tied to invisible materiality, including: i) material conditions of technological production and infrastructure; ii) material bodies of technological labour; and iii) material traces in historical objects, documents, and resources. This project argues that a renewed critical focus on materiality and material histories allows us to look backwards at the forgotten stories of people, places, and things that were never culturally significant, but that can be recovered by examining their material contexts, conditions, and politics. This project adopts a material histories framework towards literary culture and text production in order to analyze: i) the invisibility of technological labour, focusing on literary production technologies that include the typewriter, word processor, and networked online computer; ii) gendered labour in this production system through the objectification and invisibility of women’s bodies—a phenomenon that I argue is a historiocultural antecedent to the exploitation of invisible labourers within the contemporary global technocultural market; iii) the necessity for comparative approaches to studying artifacts and texts that can account for both digital and analogue forms, as well as their methods and politics of production. Towards what I am calling “comparative (or mixed-media) textual criticism,” this project develops a new method of recovering traces of material production in both digital and analogue texts. Where traditional methods of textual analysis—archival work, textual criticism, and the examination of literary forms—allow a researcher to trace the steps through which an artifact is formed, digital content production masks the processes and politics of production. By focusing on analogue and digital texts in literary culture, my new analytical method will recover material evidence of women’s invisible labour in western literary production while also accounting for the dynamic tensions between two dominant cultures of meaning making in literary history. 23602118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602118.value: In dynamic semantics, the meaning of a sentence is modeled as a rule for how a body of information changes when the sentence is accepted. Recent work in dynamic semantics has analyzed sentences involving modals (words like 'might' and 'must') and conditionals ('if ... then ...' sentences) as tests. Tests are a special type of meaning: when an agent learns a test, her information is guaranteed to either stay the same, or become absurd. The aim of this project is to critically evaluate the extent to which dynamic semantics can be separated from the notion of a test. In particular, the project will develop two new theories of modals and conditionals. On the first theory, these operators are not tests. For example, when an agent learns that it might be raining, she rules out any possibilities where the information is inconsistent with it raining. But, crucially, the information available at each possibility is itself sensitive to her overall beliefs, in a special way. In particular, the information available at each possibility must contain all of her beliefs. On the second theory I will develop, modals and conditionals are tests. But this second theory still differs from traditional kinds of dynamic semantics. In a traditional theory, different operators all update the same body of information. In this new theory, different operators update different kinds of information. The rule for updating information is then relativized to which body of information is being updated. I show that this more sophisticated model of learning has some special applications, in particular modeling rigidifying operators like 'actually'. While the theories disagree about much, they are both still irreducibly dynamic. On both theories, the meaning of sentences involving modals and conditionals cannot be represented as a rule instructing the agent to update her information with the claim that she inhabits one of a fixed set of possibilities, that a certain proposition is true. Rather, the rule for how she is to update her information must make essential reference to her current information, providing different instructions depending on what that information is like. The goal of the overall project is to critically evaluate the idea of a test by exploring the relationship between these two semantics, and exploring the extent to which various data requires each theory.

23603418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23603418.value: Night-soil, used as the valuable manure, was a contested commodity in modern Beijing. The human waste collected in the pits of these Squat-style draught latrines was scooped up by night-soil collectors, and transported to the drying yards where it was dried for use as fertilizer. The stinking but indispensable night-soil gathering was a business controlled by collectors from Shandong province since the sixteenth century. After the Boxer Rebellion in 1900, night-soil collectors came under the scrutiny of the modernization. The treatment of night-soil and its collectors were put into the political agenda. The night-soil collectors demonstrated prudence and persistence in response to challenges. However, they were also inflicted with internal disputes and factional issues. In the conventional scholarship of urban history, the wastes disposal is usually associated with health, disease and municipal infrastructure. However, waste is also a business, which had to manage product, employees and customers, fight off peers’ competition, handle public complaints, deal with state regulation, and combat modernization efforts. This is where I am placing waste disposal at the center of the story. In this project, I will position night-soil collectors in their daily settings to probe into three major questions: First, how the night-soil businessmen structured their business empires; Second, the tension between the state and the collectors including the policies of the state and the modern discourses of the urban elite on waste management and hygiene; Third, how night-soil collectors maintained their monopoly during time of regime changes from the Qing to the Communist State and in the face of political and popular criticism. By building on the primary sources housed at Mainland China, Taipei and U. S., and locating the night-soil industry as a modernizing project and a part of the endeavor of nation-building, the significance of this study lies in: first, informing us of the lives of understudied urban proletariats, and the nature of the emerging urban working class in urban China; second, illustrating the urban waste management and hygiene in the Chinese nation-building, and more importantly, presenting a bottom-up perspective on Chinese modernity and urbanization in the first half of the twentieth century.

23603418.label: Realisation of objectives
23603418.value: This research project clarifies the business structure of the night-soil collector including the drying yard owners and carriers who had ties with them. Men from Shandong began the business of collecting night-soil to sell as fertilizer in the sixteenth century and hired collectors who were also from Shandong. In 1920s, about 4,000 Shandong yard owners and carriers were engaged in the business of night-soil in Beijing. So strong were the native place connections that men from Shandong continued to monopolize the night-soil collection, drying and selling trade until the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) brought an end to their business (1950). This research illuminates the power of night-soil collector by examining the night-soil collecting territory, a substantial area over which the collectors held control and espoused the ideal that militancy was necessary to legitimize their power. As the embodiment of collectors’ power, the collecting territories laid the foundation for collectors’ monopolization. To complicate the nature of power, collectors were also inflicted with internal conflict and disputes over collecting territories and factional issues. This research demonstrates the transformation night-soil collector to lords by exploring their kinship connections and native place ties within the collecting territory. The collectors displayed cohesion and solidarity in dealing with the state by using political movements and strikes in 1920s to compel the state to compromise, which facilitated their transformation into “night-soil lords” after 1900 by building labor regime. This research elucidates urban waste management and hygiene in Chinese urbanization and nation-building by exploring the waste disposal beyond the conventional topics of health, disease and science. It takes the waste disposal as a business to manage product, fight off peers’ competition, handle public complaints, deal with state regulation, and combat modernization efforts. It also presents a bottom-up perspective on Chinese modernity and urbanization by informing us of the lives of a group of understudied urban proletariats.

23603418.label: Major findings and research outcome
23603418.value: With the generous financial support of this fund, I managed to secure numbers of primary sources on Beijing’s nightsoil and its collectors. The procured sources shed light on the many-sided narrative of constructing on the night-soil collectors and the surrounding social, political and cultural contexts. Based on these primary sources, I presented two conference papers at the Fifth Biennial Conference of East Asian Environmental History at Taiwan (10/2019) and Sixth Biennial Conference of East Asian Environmental History at Kyoto (9/2021) respectively. I am drafting a peer-reviewed article entitled “Toilet Revolution: The politics of excrement in Beijing, 1928-1937” which investigates a network of commercial night-soil collectors and reveals the strategy of nightsoil collectors using excrement as commodity to defend their enterprise and as weapon to resist the state agenda. The labor regime established by the nightsoil collectors reflects the intricate political ecology and contingent nature of enviro-social networks in modern Beijing. This article will be submitted to the Environmental History, the official journal of American Society for Environmental History and Forest History Society, in 2022.

23603418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23603418.value: Building on the collection of solid primary sources, the potential development of this research is to explore the labor regime in Beijing by examining the understudied urban laborers and the nature of the emerging urban working class in modern China. Departure from the official city envision, the proposed pathway is to put the agency of urban laborers as critical historical actors in the narrative of urbanization by focusing on the lives of ordinary people including their city sojourn and work experience to illustrate Chinese nation-building and modernization.

23603418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23603418.value: Moving beyond the studies of urban history which relied largely on the voices of urban elites, this research presented a bottom-up perspective on Chinese urbanization by focusing on a group of understudied Shandong peasants who collected night-soil in Beijing, this research further indicated that the ordinary people were not traditional and waiting to be reformed as assumed, instead, they managed to accommodate modernity by adapting to new social, economic and ideological conditions in the first half of the twentieth century.

24111818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24111818.value: Aim We aim to evaluate the immunomodulatory effects of integrative Chinese-Western medicine by studying the relationship between inflammatory cytokine and clinical marker changes of fatigue in a cohort of subjects with multiple sclerosis (MS). Project Background MS is the most common neurological disorder affecting 2.5 million young adults worldwide. Recent breakthroughs in disease modifying drugs have significantly reduced relapse rates and prevented long-term neurological disabilities. Nevertheless, fatigue impair the majority of patients and is a key contributing factor to reduced quality of life and work performance, often leading to unemployment. Our group has demonstrated a 40% increase prevalence of MS among local Chinese residents in the past decade. We found an unemployment rate of 40%, which is 10 times higher than that found in the general population. More importantly, our survey found that 60% of our MS patients actively seek Chinese medicine to relieve their disabling symptoms, among which 90% were prescribed Chinese herbal medications. In our cohort, over 90% patients reported fatigue; Chinese medicine syndrome ‘qi’ deficiency is strongly associated with objective measures of fatigue, which significantly improves with Chinese medicine that replenishes ‘qi’. We hypothesize that Chinese medicine can improve fatigue associated with MS by an immune-modulated process mediated by inflammatory cytokine changes. Brief Project Description We have launched an 8-week integrative program including Chinese medicine (herbs and acupuncture) and Western medicine to treat patients with relapsing and progressive MS. In this pragmatic clinical trial, we perform serial objective evaluation of neurological disability, fatigue, cognition, and Chinese medicine diagnoses using validated instruments. In addition, we collect blood samples at baseline and end-of-study to measure both classical and novel cytokines associated with immuno-pathogenesis of MS. In particular, we shall evaluate the responses and putative mechanism of novel cytokines, namely IL-32, IL-35, IL-36, IL-37 and IL-38. We will also explore network analysis for complex interactions between multiple herbs, clinical markers, and Chinese medicine diagnoses. Significance of Project Our study will provide critical data on the scientific basis of integrative medicine regarding the role of novel cytokines and immunomodulation in managing fatigue associated with MS. The network model may provide a framework for complex analysis of multi-herb prescription and Chinese medicine diagnoses, and their correlations with robust clinical markers of disease activity. Our results can generate further research hypotheses to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of Chinese medicine as a neuroprotective agent to halt neurodegenerative disease. 研究目的 通過研究多發性硬化症（Multiple Sclerosis, 以下簡稱MS）患者炎性細胞因子和疲勞相關臨床標記變化的關係，研究團隊旨在評估中西醫結合療法的免疫調節效用。 項目背景 MS影響全球二百五十萬年輕患者，是最為常見的腦神經系統疾病。最新研究証實，使用免疫修飾藥物不但可以顯著減少疾病復發率，而且可以減少長期神經殘疾。可是，大多數患者受疲勞影響，成為降低生活質量和影響工作表現的最主要因素，常常導致患者失業。過去十年間，香港MS的發病率增長了百分之四十，並且我們發現MS患者失業率達百分之四十，比普通人群高十倍。更重要的是，調查發現百分之六十的患者正在使用中醫療法減輕他們的殘疾症狀，其中百分之九十的患者曾使用中草藥治療。在我們的研究對象當中，超過百分之九十的患者主訴有疲勞症狀。數據顯示中醫症狀「氣虛」與疲勞的客觀評估有強烈的連繫，而患者在接受中醫補氣治療後他們的疲勞症狀得到極大改善。我們假設中醫療法可以通過改變炎性細胞因子介導的免疫調節過程來改善MS患者的疲勞症狀。 簡要項目描述 我們展開了一項長達八週的中西醫結合治療計劃，為復發型和進展型多發性硬化患者提供中醫療法（包括中草藥和針灸）和西醫療法。在這項臨床試驗中，就著神經殘疾、疲勞症狀、認知功能及中醫診斷方面，我們採用已驗證的評估測試進行一系列客觀評估。除此以外，在基線和研究結束之時均會收集患者的血液樣本，以此檢測經典和新型的炎性細胞因子；特別是IL-32，IL-35，IL-36，IL-37和IL-38等新型細胞因子，我們將針對這些與MS致病相關的新型細胞因子 的反應和機制而作詳細的研究。我們也對多種中草藥間的複雜相互反應、臨床指標及中醫診斷作深入的網絡分析。 項目重要性 這項研究計劃不但使團隊在使用中西結合治療時對新型細胞因子和免疫調節的反應和機制有更深入的了解，而且能為中西醫結合療法對改善MS相關疲勞症狀提供重要的科學數據。網絡分析可以為複雜數據的分析提供框架，如多種中草藥處方、中醫診斷，也能用於研究與疾病活動度相關關的臨床標記間的相關性分析。我們的結果可以產生更進一步的研究假說，在真實世界中評估中醫療法作為一種神經保護劑在治療神經退行性疾病中的有效性。

24115318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24115318.value: 此研究計劃目的是從人類活動的神經控制發展，以至基因對這種神經控制有多少影響，來了解嬰孩如何學習行走。 出生時，人類具有走步反射，但不能獨立行走。大人扶著6-10個月大嬰兒的腋下，讓嬰兒腳部觸及地面時，他們能做出協調良好的類似走路動作。嬰兒直到12-16個月大，他們會從需要體重支撐才可步行發展到可以獨立行走。在這幾個月中，神經系統是如何令各組肌肉配合協調來行走是在文獻中未知的範疇。最近有學者在《科學》雜誌中發表了一項橫斷性研究，他們提出當嬰兒從新生兒的走步反射過渡到幼兒步行時，除了出生時存在的2個模塊之外，中樞神經系統還啟動了神經肌肉協同的2個新的「 基本模塊」。但是，在「學會走路」的關鍵期間，這些模塊的成熟過程，以及自然（遺傳學）與培育（感覺運動經驗和神經系統狀態）的因素如何相互影響來塑造這些模塊仍未被探索。 我們希望通過縱貫性研究，三次記錄正常嬰兒的步態運動和肌電活動(28個肌肉), 來了解正常嬰兒步態的神經發展。神經肌肉協調模塊(肌肉協同)將從取得的肌電活動數據中鑑定。另外，我們與長沙中南大學湘雅醫院的遺傳學國家重點實驗室合作，記錄患有脊髓肌肉萎縮症的病人的肌電圖來評估非遺傳因素對肌肉協同的影響程度。脊髓肌肉萎縮症是一種運動神經元病變的遺傳病，這類病人呈現異常的運動神經元突觸間隙分佈，從而破壞皮質脊髓間或脊髓內神經元內肌肉協同的編碼方式，故此我們假設這類病人在非基因變異後的肌肉協同與健康組別比較會有所不同。 脊髓肌肉萎縮症病人的肌肉協同數據將能準確定義嬰兒的病理步態，從而促進早期檢測步行發展遲緩；而健康嬰孩的肌肉協同數據可用作鑑測康復進展的指標。研究結果將有助我們對人類神經系統發育的理解，以及將來研發針對脊髓肌肉萎縮症的復康機械裝置。

24115318.label: Realisation of objectives
24115318.value: The overall conceptual goal of this project is to understand how humans acquire and potentially fine-tune the muscle coordination patterns necessary for independent walking during their critical months of “learning” to walk, and to assess the importance of early sensorimotor experience around the typical walking onset for the maturation of locomotor patterns. To address these important neuroscientific questions, we recorded bilateral multi-muscle surface electromyographic signals (EMGs, 14 muscles each side) from two cohorts, including typically developing children at around walking onset (OBJECTIVE 1), and children with atypical experience due to spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) (OBJECTIVE 2), a genetic disorder associated with degeneration of lower motor neurons (motoneurons) in the spinal cord. For the first cohort, we further recorded signals at 3 time points (~6-10 mo, ~8-12 mo, and ~12-16 mo) during supported, assisted, and independent overground walking, respectively. Data from OBJECTIVE 1 were used both to assess the potential changes in the muscle patterns across the 3 stages of learning to walk, and as a baseline of comparison for EMGs we collected later from other adult subjects for evaluating the changes in locomotor muscle coordination during child-to-adult development. In addition, this normative data for OBJECTIVE 1 served as a baseline of comparison for the data acquired from the SMA subjects for OBJECTIVE 2. With these data sets, we applied factorization algorithms to the EMGs to extract “muscle synergies” – modules for the neural control of multiple groups of muscles for locomotion – and assessed how the muscle synergies differed between the different time points and cohorts. RESULTS ACHIEVED FOR OBJECTIVE 1 Overall, during the project period we succeeded in collecting longitudinal walking EMG and kinematic data at our targeted 3 stages of walking from human infants. By the end of the last progress report (April 2020), we managed to complete recordings of 16 locally recruited infants. However, the advent of COVID-19 had severely interfered with our original data recording schedule. Between April 2020 and early 2022, our laboratory was closed several times due either to university/governmental recommendations or the fact that some of our students/staff were tested COVID-19 positive. Subject recruitment was made even more difficult by the fact that until recently, it was not common for infants below age 1 to be vaccinated. To make up for the lost time, we applied for a 6-month extension of grant end date and our application was approved by RGC. We have also tried our very best to reach our targeted number of subjects (N=30). At the end, we managed to collect data from 40 infants, with 18 subjects with 3 time points of data, and 22 with 2 of 3 time points. Our subsequent analysis revealed that the spatial muscle synergies for walking remained quite constant at the individual and population levels across the 3 stages. This observation and the availability of data from 10 additional subjects suggest to us that our data set is sufficient for addressing our scientific questions even though not all subjects had all 3 time points of recordings. RESULTS ACHIEVED FOR OBJECTIVE 2 To collect data from children with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), we established a collaboration with the State Key Laboratory of Medical Genetics (directed by Prof. Liang Desheng and Wu Lingqian) in Changsha, Hunan, which has a good reputation of managing and providing genetic counselling to parents of SMA children. We arranged research trips to Changsha for collecting data from SMA patients at the Jiahui Genetics Hospital (Xiangya Medical School, Central South University) managed by the above State Key Laboratory. Also, we recruited an additional SMA subject at the Heep Hong Society, a local charity organization that offers education and rehabilitation for children. At the end, we succeeded in collecting EMG, clinical scores, genetic status (SMN1/SMN2 copy numbers), and video-based kinematics from our targeted number of SMA subjects (N=24). In our patient cohort, most subjects had a degree of motoneuronal degeneration that rendered them unable to walk independently. In fact, of the 24 subjects, only 6 came with the ability to walk either independently or with assistance. For the subjects unable to walk, we still managed to record locomotor-like EMGs through another motor task. We found that sufficient variability of EMGs could still be recorded by active assistive motions (AAM) of the lower limb, elicited by having the subject lying supine on a bed, and with the experimenter aiding the attempted cyclical and alternating leg motions. After data collection, we have performed extensive data analysis (detailed in publication 5 listed in part C) to verify that for both ambulatory and non-ambulatory SMA subjects, the muscle synergies derived from AAM EMG should be synergies related to their potential walking ability.

24115318.label: Major findings and research outcome
24115318.value: In relation to OBJECTIVE 1, we sought to formulate a mechanism that accounts for the long-term plasticity of locomotor muscle synergies during motor development and learning. We found that across the 3 time points we recorded close to walking onset, at both the population and individual levels the synergies remained constant, consistent with the recent proposal that muscle synergies are inborn or determined early in life. But development of the neuromusculoskeletal system and acquisition of new skills may demand fine-tuning or reshaping of the early synergies. We therefore further sought to understand how locomotor synergies change during child-to-adult development and training by comparing the synergies from children with those of adults (derived from running of sedentary subjects, novice runners, and elite marathoners). During development, synergies are fractionated into units with fewer muscles. As adults train to run, specific synergies coalesce to become merged synergies. Presences of specific synergy-merging patterns correlate with enhanced or reduced running efficiency. Fractionation and merging of muscle synergies may be a mechanism for modifying early motor modules (Nature) to accommodate the changing limb biomechanics and influences from sensorimotor training (Nurture). This important result was disseminated as a paper in Nature Communications (publication 4, part C). In relation to OBJECTIVE 2, we aimed to understand how genetic processes, early and later sensorimotor experiences contribute to development of locomotor synergies. We evaluated experience-dependent synergy development by studying subjects with atypical sensorimotor histories around typical walking onset due to spinal muscular atrophy (SMA, types II/IIIa), a disorder associated with degeneration and deafferentation of motoneurons. Muscle synergies of SMA children were identified from electromyographic signals recorded during active assisted leg motions or walking, and compared with those of age-matched controls. We found that the earlier the SMA onset age, the more different the SMA synergies were from the normative, consistent with a strong role of experience in the proper maturation and fractionation of synergy precursors. Our results highlight post-SMA impairment as outcome of not just motoneuronal loss, but also a dysfunctional sensorimotor circuit that emerges partly from altered experience during a critical period of locomotor development. This result was disseminated as a paper under review (currently available as a preprint at BioRxiv; attached here in this final report) (publication 5, part C).

24115318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24115318.value: In relation to OBJECTIVE 1, if the basic locomotor muscle synergies are already present by walking onset, as our findings suggest, it is reasonable to ask whether there are precursors to these basic muscle synergies that may be detectable from EMGs at an even earlier age before the onset of walking. In fact, a recent PNAS paper from an Italian group argues that precursors to locomotor synergies observed in children can already be discerned in stepping and kicking (air-stepping) performed by neonates under 1 week of age. We therefore hypothesize that the neonatal synergy precursors are transformed into the basic locomotor synergies at walking onset through both genetic processes and experience-dependent plasticity, with the latter facilitated by the performance of the many spontaneous movement between birth and walking onset. We propose recording EMGs from one such spontaneous movement most noticeable at age 3-4 months, called fidgety motion, to validate our hypothesis. In relation to OBJECTIVE 2, our finding implies that the degree of abnormality of muscle synergies can be a marker that indicates the exact motor functional status of the SMA subjects. One possibility is to extend this concept to other motoneuronal or muscular disorders (e.g., Duchenne muscular dystrophy).

24115318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24115318.value: How do human infants learn to walk? Our ability to walk is underpinned by complex activations of many leg/trunk muscles, and how the central nervous system (CNS) manages to coordinate their activities to ensure stable, yet flexible, locomotion remains unanswered. The CNS achieves muscle coordination by generating muscle patterns through the combination of a small number of motor building blocks, called muscle synergies. When recruited, each muscle synergy activates a pre-specified set of muscles together as a unit. Here, we ask how the muscle synergies for walking are formed during the months when walking emerges in humans (age 6-18 months). We found that in typically developing infants, by the time walking appears, the muscle synergies required are already in place and remain stable through the initial months of walking maturation, though they are further refined during child-to-adult development. A comparison with subjects with atypical motor experience at the same age due to a movement disorder (spinal muscular atrophy) reveals that our early sensorimotor experience is critical for the initial formation and subsequent maturation of these muscle synergies. Thus, our early sensorimotor experience around walking onset plays a strong role in the shaping of our subsequent muscle control for locomotion.

24116518.label: Project Objectives
24116518.value: This prospective, multi-centre RCT aims to compare between SR and EBR in patients with NMIBC. We hypothesized that EBR could reduce disease recurrence as compared to SR at one year. Secondary outcomes include detrusor muscle sampling rate, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative mitomycin C instillation, hospital stay, 30-day complications, any residual or upstaging of disease upon second-look TURBT and the 1-year progression rate. In addition, for the EBR group, circumferential resection margin, deep resection margin, successful EBR rate and complete tumour resection rate (i.e. successful EBR with negative circumferential and deep resection margins) would be assessed. These results would provide evidence on the basis of EBR i.e. removal of bladder tumour en bloc with histological support of a complete tumour resection. The findings of this study could establish the role of EBR in the management of NMIBC.

24116518.value: 背景 經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術是診斷和治療非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌的標準 。傳統上，我們以零碎的方式進行傳統切除術。 然而，這樣會增加在膀胱裡浮游的腫瘤細胞及其重新植入的可能性。 此外，在接受第一次傳統切除術後，多達33.3％的病例仍存在殘留病變。 整塊切除術已被提議作為傳統切除術的替代方法。 在我們的經驗中，整塊切除術的成功率為98.6％，並在所有病例中取得陰性的切緣。 這可能是治療非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌簡單而優越的手術方法。 目的和假設 本研究的目的是要比較傳統切除術和整塊切除術在治療非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌的效果。 我們假設整塊切除術可以減少非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌的復發率。 方法 這是一項涉及十一個中心的前瞻性隨機對照試驗，目的是比較傳統切除術和整塊切除術在治療非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌的效果。 所有被診斷患有膀胱腫瘤及符合研究資格的患者將被納入研究中。 研究的主要結果是一年復發率。 次要結果包括逼尿肌取樣率、閉孔反射的發生率、手術時間、術後絲裂黴素C的灌注率、住院時間、術後三十天內的並發症、二次經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術的病理報告以及疾病的一年進展率。 樣本量計算 根據以往的數據，假設一年復發率的差異為16.5％，顯著性水平為0.05，功效為80％，每組需要118名患者。 考慮到其中24％的患者會有非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌以外的組織學診斷，以及10％的患者可能中斷隨訪，每組需要174名患者，即總共348名患者。 時間表和可行性 本研究涉及十一家醫院。 我們預計納入研究時間為二十一個月，估計潛在病例的數目為1353個。 患者將隨訪一年，預計研究將在三年內完成。 未來的研究 該研究可以確定整塊切除術在治療非肌層浸潤性膀胱癌的作用。 這些結果可能為經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術提供一個新的標準，亦有助於計劃術後的輔助治療。 觀察到的複發模式也可能有助於製定整塊切除術後的膀胱鏡覆檢時間表。

24116518.label: Realisation of objectives
24116518.value: Objectives 1. This prospective, multi-centre RCT aims to compare between SR and EBR in patients with NMIBC. We hypothesized that EBR could reduce disease recurrence as compared to SR at one year. This objective was fulfilled. We completed this multi-centre RCT comparing between SR and EBR in patients with NMIBC. We demonstrated that EBR could reduce disease recurrence at one year, and therefore our hypothesis was proven. 2. Secondary outcomes include detrusor muscle sampling rate, occurrence of obturator reflex, operative time, rate of immediate post-operative mitomycin C instillation, hospital stay, 30-day complications, any residual or upstaging of disease upon second-look TURBT and the 1-year progression rate. This objective was fulfilled. Our results showed that operative time was slightly longer in the EBR group, but all other secondary outcomes were similar between the two groups. There was also a trend towards a lower 1-year progression rates in the EBR group. 3. In addition, for the EBR group, circumferential resection margin, deep resection margin, successful EBR rate and complete tumour resection rate (i.e. successful EBR with negative circumferential and deep resection margins) would be assessed. These results would provide evidence on the basis of EBR i.e. removal of bladder tumour en bloc with histological support of a complete tumour resection. This objective was fulfilled. The successful EBR rate was 88.1% in the EBR group. Clear resection margins were achieved in 82% of the cases in the EBR group. These results proved that EBR is technically feasible in the majority of the cases. 4. The findings of this study could establish the role of EBR in the management of NMIBC. This objective was fulfilled. This RCT proved that en bloc resection is a superior technique in treating patients with bladder tumour(s) of ≤3cm. EBR should be considered the new standard treatment for patients with NMIBC.

24116518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24116518.value: Introduction & Objectives: The current standard resection (SR) is performed by resecting the bladder tumour in a piecemeal manner. En bloc resection of bladder tumour (EBR) has been proposed as a potentially superior technique in treating non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), but high-quality evidence is lacking. Materials & Methods: The EB-StaR study is a multi-centre, randomized, phase 3 trial comparing between EBR and SR. Patients who were diagnosed to have bladder tumour(s) upon flexible cystoscopy were screened for study eligibility. Patients with maximal bladder tumour base dimension of >3cm were excluded. Primary outcome was 1-year recurrence rate. Main secondary outcomes included 1-year progression rate, operative time, hospital stay, detrusor muscle sampling rate and 30-day complications. A modified intention-to-treat analysis was planned for the study outcomes. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02993211). Results: A total of 350 patients were randomly assigned to receive EBR or SR. Among them, 49 patients had benign histology, 22 patients had muscle-invasive bladder cancer, and 3 patients were found to have no bladder tumour upon allocated treatment. Hence, 276 patients with NMIBC (143 patients in the EBR group and 133 patients in the SR group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. At 1 year, the recurrence rates were 28.5% in the EBR group and 38.1% in the SR group (p=0.007) (Figure 1); the progression rates were 0% in the EBR group and 2.6% in the SR group (p=0.065). The EBR group had a longer operative time (33.4±18.5 vs 24.7±12.9 minutes, p<0.001) than the SR group. Hospital stay (EBR: 2.6±1.4; SR: 2.6±1.4 days), detrusor muscle sampling rate (EBR: 83.2%; SR: 84.2%) and 30-day complications (EBR: 14.7%; SR: 14.3%) were similar between the two groups. In the EBR group, the ERB success rate was 88.1%, and clear resection margins were achieved in 82.0% of the cases. Conclusions: In patients with NMIBC, EBR led to a significant reduction in 1-year recurrence rate when compared to SR. An EBR-first approach should be considered in patients with bladder tumour(s) of ≤3cm.

24116518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24116518.value: The study findings support en bloc resection as the standard treatment for patients with bladder tumour(s) of ≤3cm. Simply by changing the surgical technique in resecting the bladder tumour, the 1-year recurrence rate can be lowered significantly. This study could potentially change the current guidelines in the management of bladder cancer. The en bloc resection procedure can be promoted and generalised to urologists worldwide, ultimately benefiting bladder cancer patients globally.

24116518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24116518.value: In this study, we proved that en bloc resection of bladder tumour (i.e. removal of bladder tumour in one piece) could led to a lower recurrence rate in patients with bladder cancer. When compared to conventional standard resection (i.e. removal of bladder tumour in multiple pieces), en bloc resection of bladder tumour had similar peri-operative outcomes and complication profile. We concluded that en bloc resection of bladder tumour should be considered the new standard in treating patients with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

24122318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24122318.value: 外周組織的生物鐘在受到下丘腦生物鐘釋放的神經遞質和激素調控的同時，本身對細胞的節律性基因表達和功能也起了主要的調節作用。Bmal1是CLOCK:BMAL1這個二聚體的一部分，參與生物鐘控制的基因轉錄調控。已知BMAL1對炎症反應時單核細胞的節律性動態變化起了主要作用。我們以往的研究提示Bmal1缺失通過上調CCL2促進了單核細胞募集和浸潤動脈粥樣硬化斑塊，加重ApoE敲除小鼠的動脈粥樣硬化。生物鐘紊亂比如輪夜班與心血管疾病的發生有顯著相關性。同時血壓和血管彈性也表現出明顯的晝夜節律。我們提出假設巨噬細胞生物鐘紊亂通過促進血管外膜炎症和血管重構，加重高血壓和血管功能障礙。我們將利用雙腎單夾模型誘導腎源性高血壓模型小鼠。觀察Bmal1敲除對血壓升高的影響和晝夜變化，檢測Bmal1敲除對血管外膜巨噬細胞募集和極性轉化的影響，是否促進血管炎症。Bmal1敲除是否能增加Smad信號通路的活性，從而增加環氧化酶-2（COX-2）和其產生的前列腺素F2α（PGF2α）的生成，直接引起血管功能障礙和加劇血管炎症反應。我們也會進一步通過體外實驗驗證BMAL1與Smad是否有相互作用。此項研究的結果將明確血管外周生物鐘通過COX-2 -PGF2α調控血管炎症的機制，幫助了解腎源性高血壓引起血管病變的發病機理和血壓的晝夜節律調控。

24122318.label: Realisation of objectives
24122318.value: 5.3.1. Myeloid selective deletion of Bmal1 enhances hypertension and vascular remodeling in hypertensive mice. We have used two experimental hypertension models in mice. Both the angiotensin infusion for 4 weeks and L-NAME (nitric oxide synthase inhibitor) with saline in drinking water for 4 weeks were used. The results showed that both models induce a steady blood pressure (BP) increase in the wild type Bmal1MWT mice, while the BP in the myeloid-selective Bmal1 knockout Bmal1MKO mice were higher, at different times of day (refer to the Figure 1-2 and Figure S1 from Huo et a., Cardiovascular Research 2022 DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336), associated with more severe vascular wall thickening in the Bmal1MKO. In addition, the vascular function was also further impaired in the hypertensive Bmal1MKO mice, with more vasoconstriction when the effect of endothelium was excluded, indicating vascular wall thickening (Figure 2, DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). 5.3.2. Bmal1 deletion enhances pro-fibrotic M2 macrophage accumulation in the vascular wall. The gene expressions showed a more obvious pro-fibrotic phenotype with high expression of MMPs and relatively less pro-inflammatory phenotype examined by expression of cytokines (Il6, Tnf, Il1b, etc.) (refer to Figure 5 and S6, DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). The infiltrating macrophages and monocytes were also profiled which showed infiltrated macrophages differentiated more into pro-fibrotic M2 macrophages rather than pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages (refer to Figure 3-4, and S2, S5. DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). The histological analysis showed that hypertensive Bmal1MKO mice have more collagen deposition, collagen I and collagen III expression, M2 macrophage infiltration, accompanied by MMP9 and MMP13 expression, suggested that these MMPs may be the key molecules involved in the vascular remodeling in both hypertension models (refer to Figure 4-5, and S10. DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). 5.3.3. Inhibition of Il4R signaling in myeloid cells attenuates M2 macrophages accumulation in the vascular wall of hypertensive mice and vascular remodeling. Due to the observation of enhanced accumulation of pro-fibrotic M2 macrophages rather pro-inflammatory macrophages, which was more consistent in several cohorts of mice, we continued to look into whether inhibiting these M2 macrophage would affect the macrophage within the vascular wall. We used myeloid selective Il4Ra knockout mice (Ilr4aMKO) because Il4R signaling is the major signaling pathway mediated the effect of Th2 cytokines Il4 and IL13 to differentiate macrophage into M2 macrophages. In the angiotensin II infused hypertensive Ilr4aMKO mice, the CD301+ M2 macrophage population was reduced. Ilr4aMKO mice also had less vascular wall thickening, resulting in less blood pressure increase upon angiotensin II infusion (refer to Figure 7, DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). 5.3.4. Bmal1 deletion enhanced STAT6 and overactivation in the macrophages. MMP enzymes are known to be involved in vascular extracellular matrix degradation, vascular smooth muscle proliferation, and outward remodeling of the vascular wall. MMP are also known to be upregulated in M2 macrophages. Therefore, we switched from further studying the COX-2 pathway to the molecular mechanism mediating MMPs in M2 macrophages. In the bone marrow derived macrophages (BMDMs), knockout of Bmal1 enhanced IL-4 induced Mmp9 and Mmp13 expression and MMP9 over-activation. Further in vitro results showed that STAT6 phosphorylation, translocation, and transcriptional activity was enhanced in Bmal1 knockout BMDMs, while inhibition of STAT6 reduced Mmp13 expression. Co-immunoprecipitation suggested a direct binding of endogenous STAT6 with BMAL1 proteins in the BMDMs (refer to Figure 6, DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). These results showed that BMAL1 inhibits overactivation of STAT6, therefore loss of Bmal1 causes enhanced STAT6 activity downstream of IL4R signaling, resulting in more MMP production and vascular wall remodeling. 5.3.5. Bmal1 knockout enhances the pro-inflammatory phenotype in macrophages during acute inflammation. Due to the concern on the lack of robustness on the pro-inflammatory phenotype of macrophages in the context of hypertension, alternatively, we examined the regulation of macrophage by Bmal1 under other conditions such as under the treatment of pro-inflammatory stimuli and in the context of acute inflammation. We found that in the Bmal1 knockout BMDMs, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induced expressions of Tnf, Il6, Il1b, and Il118 were enhanced, particular the production of mature Il-1β was increased (refer to Figure 1, Hong et al., Biochemical Pharmacology, 2021, DOI: 10.1016/j.bcp.2021.114701). Next, we showed that activation of clock gene Rev-Erbα by ligand SR9009 suppressed inflammatory responses in BMDMs independent of time-of-day difference (refer to Figure 2. DOI: 10.1016/j.bcp.2021.114701). 5.3.6. Bmal1-independent suppression of inflammatory phenotype in macrophages by Rev-Erbα by ligand SR9009. Because inflammatory responses induced by LPS was enhanced with Bmal1 knockout, we further studied whether SR9009 would inhibit inflammation depending on Bmal1 expression. Using the BMDMs from Bmal1MKO vs wild type mice, we found that the inhibition of Tnf, Il6, Il1b, Il18 transcripts were suppressed by SR9009 independent of the presence of Bmal1. However, the production of mature IL-1β was attenuated in Bmal1 knockout BMDMs. Further experiments showed that the suppression of inflammasome Nlrp3 transcript and protein by SR9009 was abolished in Bmal1 knockout BMDMs, which is responsible for mature IL-1β production (refer to Figure 3-4, DOI: 10.1016/j.bcp.2021.114701). In the mice, SR9009 supressed LPS-induced infiltration of peritoneal macrophages and the production of IL-1β in these cells, accompanied by less circulating IL-1β and IL-18 levels (refer to Figure 5, DOI: 10.1016/j.bcp.2021.114701).

24122318.label: Major findings and research outcome
24122318.value: In summary, we showed that Bmal1 is an important regulator of macrophage phenotype through various downstream molecules in different types of macrophages, either through post-transcriptional or transcriptional regulations, in response to different stimuli. Under the condition of hypertension and angiotensin II challenge, loss of Bmal1 results in the increased presence of pro-fibrotic M2 macrophages, which in response to IL-4 most likely from the increased population of infiltrating Th2 cell, producing more MMP enzymes to facilitate the proliferation of vascular smooth muscles and outward remodeling of vascular wall, therefore enhancing blood pressure increase. Such changes in the vascular macrophages is due to the loss of BMAL1 inhibition on the transcription factor STAT6 and its downstream signaling (Huo et a., Cardiovascular Research 2022 DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvab336). In addition, although the pro-inflammatory phenotype in the context of hypertension was not quite obvious after a more rigorous investigation and repeats of the experiments, we observed that the modulation of inflammation by Bmal1 was more sensitive under the context of acute inflammation, such as LPS challenge in vitro and in vivo. Bmal1 is particularly important to inhibit Nlrp3 inflammasome induced by LPS and therefore mature IL-1β and IL-18 production. However, the ligand SR9009 is able to suppress the transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines induced by LPS independent of Bmal1 expression (Hong et al., Biochemical Pharmacology, 2021, DOI: 10.1016/j.bcp.2021.114701).

24122318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24122318.value: Based on the research finding showing the significance of vascular wall macrophages in vascular wall remodeling and hypertension. This is in line with the recent research highlight on the contribution of various immune cells in hypertension and related vascular pathology. Our publication in the journal Cardiovascular Research was also picked as the "Editor's choice" in the issue. This finding showed the importance of modulating macrophage phenotype in vascular pathology, which has not be emphasised in these non-immune related diseases. Macrophage phenotype could be modulated by many different drugs or small molecules. Therefore, our results also suggested that drugs which affect macrophage phenotype could be potentially effective in treating hypertensive vascular remodeling. In addition, when testing efficacy of new drugs or new biologics in treating hypertensive vascular disease, the impact of these reagents on immunomodulation, particularly the effect on T helper cells, cytokines, and macrophage phentoype also need to be considered. The current research findings also inspire us to further study the effect of ligands such as SR9009 on hypertensive vascular remodeling, as well as the involvement of Bmal1 in other hypertension-related vascular pathologies, such as stroke, hypertensive renal damage, and aortic aneurysm, etc., as some of the future directions.

24122318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24122318.value: Circadian clock genes orchestrate biological rhythm to adapt and anticipate environmental changes, especially the 24 hour light dark cycle. Clock genes also exist outside the brain to regulate many biological function including the metabolism and cardiovascular function via circulating hormones and metabolites. Bmal1 is part of the central clock gene complex. Because blood pressure and vascular response follows circadian variation, while the disturbance of local vascular clock impairs blood pressure regulation. In this research we used cell type selective knockout of Bmal1 in mice and two experimental hypertension model to show that without the expression of Bmal1 in monocytes and macrophages, the blood pressure increase is further enhanced in hypertensive mice. The enhanced blood pressure increase is probably due to more thickening of the vascular wall. The loss of Bmal1 in macrophages causes more production of extracellular matrix enzymes to degrade outer layer of the vascular wall and stimulate vascular wall smooth muscle cell growth. The over-production and activate of these matrix enzyme is associated with cytokine interleukin-4 signaling, therefore, block the interleukin-4 receptor attenuates blood pressure increase in hypertensive mice. This project showed that immune cells are involved in the development of hypertension through interaction with vascular cells.
