24204818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24204818.value: 該項目旨在開發一種蛇形柔性機器人的磁穩定方法，並探索其在自然腔道手術（NOTES）中的應用，例如胃腸道內鏡黏膜下剝離術（ESD）。 胃腸癌在香港和全世界都很普遍。例如，在香港結直腸癌的發病率排名第一，死亡率排名第二，而胃癌則分別排在第6位和第4位。在全球範圍內，結腸直腸癌和胃癌分別是第二大和第五大癌症。通過手術切除腫瘤是癌症治療的通用方法，包括開放手術或微創手術（MIS）。在這兩種方法中，手術器械穿過消化道到達腔內腫瘤從而需要切除部分胃腸道。隨著診斷技術的進步，更多胃腸道癌症被早期發現。這使得可以通過先進的NOTES手術（例如ESD）切除早期腫瘤並保持器官完好無損。這帶來的好處是顯而易見的，包括減少失血，縮短住院時間，減少術後疼痛，提高患者耐受性，減少疤痕等。在ESD中，早期腫瘤通過使用柔性內窺鏡器械切除。由於內窺鏡器械的末端和在消化道內沒有固定以及器械靈巧性差，導致ESD手術不容易掌握。通過在內窺鏡末端添加兩個微型機械臂可以解決靈巧性的問題，而內窺鏡末端浮動依舊是一個急需解決的問題。其困境在於內窺鏡一方面需要足夠柔軟以進入胃腸道，另一方面需要大的剛度以保證手術操作的穩定。現有剛度調節的研究包括張力法以及擠壓法。由於內窺鏡下柔性機械臂尺寸小，驅動繩的張力有限，影響張力法的剛度調節性能。過高的張力還會帶來安全隱患。在擠壓法中，顆粒以及層狀結構所需要的空間更大，同時過高的壓力帶來的安全隱患更為嚴重。由此可見，一種安全有效的結構穩定方法依然是NOTES機器人發展的瓶頸。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種柔性機器人的磁穩定方法。在該方法中，機械臂的末端使用磁力穩定，而機械臂本身保持柔軟。因此，無論機械臂的長度和彎曲情況如何，其末端都是穩定的。而且，該方法消除了現有方法中的安全隱患。為了驗證所提出的方法，我們將搭建一個蛇形柔性機器人，並利用該機器人模擬ESD手術中的操作。我們預計這項研究將解決柔性機械臂的末端穩定問題，從而促進NOTES手術的推廣並為這個老齡化社會的挽救更多的生命。

24204818.label: Realisation of objectives
24204818.value: This project aims to study the stabilization of snake-like flexible surgical robots with magnetic forces. The main objectives include: 1) develop a proof-of-concept NOTES suited snake-like flexible robot with magnetic stabilization; 2) Evaluate the efficacy of the proposed stabilization technique. For the first objective, there are four sub-objectives, including: a) design and develop a proof-of-concept snake-like flexible robot with a magnetic tip; b) design and develop an electromagnetic actuation system; c) develop the dynamic model of the flexible robot in the magnetic field; d) develop the stabilizing algorithm of the distal tip. To achieve this objective, we have developed a soft-tethered endoscope robot as proof-of-concept. The soft-tethered endoscope robot contains a magnetic tip (NdFeB, N52, 10 mm internal diameter, 14 mm external diameter, length 23 mm), a multi-channel silicon-based shaft, and a handle. A camera with LED lighting (5.5 mm diameter, two million pixels, 5 mm focus), and an IMU sensor have been integrated inside the magnetic tip. The diameter and length of the magnetic tip are 14 mm and 28 mm. The total weight of the magnetic tip is 19 g. The soft tether has a diameter of 6 mm with a hardness of 73A. There are four functional channels inside the soft tether for insufflation, irrigation, instrument, and signal transmission. Then handle is 3D printed with ergonomic user interfaces, including two valves to control insufflation and irrigation. This part of work is published in TMRB. The electromagnetic actuation system is used to generate desired magnetic fields and forces to control the position and orientation of the flexible robot tip. In this project, a proof-of-concept electromagnetic actuation system is developed. It contains nine electromagnetic coils (1.8 mm wire diameter, 1620 turns, 4.0±0.2-ohm resistance) with a core (made of DT4C pure iron, 65 mm in diameter, 280 mm in length). The maximum current to the coil is 10 A. With the iron core, the magnetic field is about 20 times stronger than that of air-core electromagnetic coil. Eight electromagnetic coils are distributed symmetrically around the spherical workspace with a diameter of 200 mm. The distance between the upper electromagnet core and the lower one is 105 mm. The nineth coil is placed at the bottom center of the workspace. It helps to generate a strong magnetic gradient in the Z-axis direction. The configuration of electromagnets is optimized to generate strong magnetic gradients in X-axis, Y-axis, and Z-axis direction. In the electromagnetic actuation system, a movable platform is developed to enlarge the operating workspace. The movable platform is made of carbon fibers and plastics to avoid magnetic interference. It has 2-DOF motions in X-axis and Y-axis. To facilitate the steering of the soft-tethered endoscope robot, a feeding mechanism is designed. It is fixed at the bottom side of the movable platform. In the electromagnetic actuation system, a programmable DC power supply (Model DPM8616-485, Junce Instrument Co., Ltd., Hangzhou, China) is used to power the electromagnetic coils. It is connected to the host computer through RS485 and can provide a maximum DC output of 64V/16A. The current reversal is achieved by an H-bridge circuit module. Another power supply with a DC output of 24V/5A is used to power the motors in the movable platform, which is controlled by the host computer through a CAN bus. The developed flexible endoscope robot can be modelled as a soft beam with a magnetic tip. The magnetic force and torque are applied to the tip of the soft beam. The magnetic field of a single coil could be modelled by the dipole model. The overall magnetic field could be obtained by superposition. The force and torque are related to both the magnetic moments and currents. A 2OR pseudo rigid body (PRB) model is developed to model the bending of the soft tether. The model is composed of three rigid links joined by two orthogonal revolute joints and two torsional springs. The stiffness of the springs and the length of the links are calibrated through experiments with optimization algorithms. With the calibrated parameters and the 2OR PRB model, the soft tether could be modelled as conventional manipulators. To control and stabilize the soft tether with high accuracy, close-loop control is necessary. In this research, we investigated two approaches for position sensing, which is crucial for the control. The first one is by hall sensor arrays with an IMU sensor for orientation sensing. The magnet at the tip of the flexible robot will emit the magnetic flux, which could be modelled using the dipole model. We developed a 5 by 5 hall sensor array with a total of 25 hall sensors. Two methods are developed to calculate the position of the permanent magnet, including direct estimation method and second derivative method. For the orientation, three methods are investigated, including orientation with accelerometer, orientation with magnetic moment, and orientation with Gyroscope. The measured position and orientation are fused by complimentary filter and Kalman filter. Overall, when the distance between the permanent magnet and the hall sensor array is in the range of 25 to 72 mm, the position error is 1.46 mm and the orientation error is 0.42°, which outperforms previous methods. Optical measurement is another method to measure the shape of the flexible robot. With the soft tethered endoscope robot, we use the optical method for control. An ArUco maker is attached at the tip of the robot and used to provide the position with a frame rate of 30 Hz. A visual servo controller is developed to control the soft tethered endoscope. For the second main objective, there are two sub-objectives: a) evaluate the stabilization performance of the flexible robot in the lab tests; b) ex vivo test of the stabilization performances of the snake-like flexible robot in colon or stomach phantom. With the developed soft tethered endoscope robot platform, we performed various kinds of experiments. The magnetic tip is controlled to follow different trajectories, such as sine-wave, square, circle, and infinite-symbol. The absolute mean position error is within 0.5 mm, with a speed of 3.5 mm/s. Three kinds of disturbances are applied to the flexible robot, including impact disturbance, step disturbance, and constant disturbance. These represent the common scenarios, such as snap motion of the biopsy forceps and contact with surrounding tissue during operation. Results show that with the visual servo control, the tip could significantly reduce the oscillation and converge to the stable position within a short time. The soft tethered endoscope robot is also tested with ex vivo colon model. A silicon colon phantom is developed with embedded polyps. A deep learning neural network is trained to identify the lumen center and the polyps. Combined with the visual servo control, the soft tethered endoscope robot could take either the lumen center or the polyp as the servo target. When the lumen center is the target, the controller could orient the endoscope robot to the lumen center and the feeding mechanism could advance the endoscope robot inside the colon autonomously. Six subjects have been invited to test the robot. Results show that the visual servo based autonomous navigation could reduce 14.49% operation time compared to manual operation.

24204818.label: Major findings and research outcome
24204818.value: In this research, we developed a soft-tethered endoscope robot with magnetic actuation and stabilization, experiments are conducted to validate the proposed methods. The robot system contains two main parts, including the soft-tethered endoscope and the magnetic actuation system. The soft-tethered endoscope body is a multi-channel silicon shaft, which has large deformation during the operation. Due to the asymmetric structure, conventional PRB model could not be used, and we proposed a 2OR PRB model that could capture the asymmetric property. A balloon structure could help to anchor the soft-tethered endoscope inside the lumen. The magnetic actuation system contains nine electromagnetic coils. Each coil could be modelled by the dipole model. After superposition, the overall magnetic field could be derived. The force and torque applied to the magnet tip is related to the magnetic moment and currents to the coils. Due to the fast deterioration of magnetic field, the workspace of the magnetic actuation system is small. Therefore, a proof-of-concept prototype with reduced workspace is developed in this project. The position and orientation of the magnet tip of the robot could be measured either by hall sensor arrays or by optical methods. With the developed hall sensor arrays, the positioning accuracy is 1.46 mm and orientation accuracy is 0.42° when the distance between the magnet and the hall sensor array is 25-72 mm. By using optical measurement, the visual measurement could be easily integrated with the visual servo controller to form close-loop control. This could control the tip position accurately and stabilize the tip during operation. Typical disturbances, such as constant disturbance, step disturbance and impact disturbance could be well supressed with the close-loop control. Further, deep learning neural networks are developed to facilitate the autonomous navigation control of the soft tethered endoscope robot. This helps to save the time of navigation compared to manual control. The results have been published in top-notch peer-reviewed journals and leading international conferences in robotics as shown in part C.

24204818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24204818.value: In this project, a proof-of-concept flexible endoscope robot, its magnetic actuation and stabilization are studied. Results show that using magnetic force to steer and stabilize the flexible robots is feasible and promising. However, there are also challenges need to be further addressed, including real-time shape sensing, magnetic operating distance, and frequency. In addition, magnetic interference with other ferromagnetic instruments needs be considered. For further developments, to address the real-time shape sensing, FBG sensors, hall sensor array, or visual-based methods could be investigated. For the magnetic operating distance and frequency, efforts could be made on the electromagnetic coil array optimization. In terms of magnetic interference, isolation methods, such as new magnet configurations, magnetic shielding materials, and buffer space could be adopted. After addressing these, flexible robots could be designed for specific lumens to facilitate surgeons in their operations.

24204818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24204818.value: Endoluminal diseases, such as colon cancer, stomach cancer and lung cancer, are common and deadly. To preserve the organ and minimize the trauma to patient, surgeons would use snake-like flexible devices/robots (such as a flexible endoscope) to examine the lumen and treat the lesion. However, the operation with the flexible endoscope is challenge due to the tip is floating, which significantly affects the operating accuracy. In this project, we developed a proof-of-concept flexible endoscope robot that is actuated and stabilized by external magnetic force. With the endoscope visual feedback and stabilization algorithms, our flexible endoscope could achieve sub-millimetre accuracy. This could help surgeons to reach deep into the lumen and perform precise interventions, such as dissection, drug delivery, etc.

24208518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24208518.value: Severe outdoor air pollution, especially smog, has become a major threat to public health in China. In many buildings, a large amount of outdoor PM2.5 can enter into indoor environments through ventilation and infiltration. Most of the residential housing in China is naturally ventilated without filtration units. Therefore, when outdoor PM2.5 pollution is severe, people are inclined to close their windows to reduce the indoor exposure to some extent. However, doing so results in a low air exchange rate with poor indoor air quality. Nanofiber window screens can be potentially applied for solving this problem. The nanofiber films coated on window screens can act as air filters to capture outdoor PM2.5 from the incoming air. Meanwhile, the relatively low air resistance because of the slip effect may be able to help maintain the air exchange rate at an acceptable level for ensuring indoor air quality. However, few studies, if any, on the characteristics of air resistance of nanofiber window screens have been reported in the literature. Without the understanding of air resistance, we cannot effectively assess the performance of nanofiber window screens in buildings. Therefore, in the proposed project, we will investigate the influence of the window opening angle, dust load, and fiber diameter on the air resistance of nanofiber window screens. This project will start with experiments in a laboratory setup to measure the pressure drops of various nanofiber window screens with the window at different opening angles under different face velocities. An air resistance model will be developed and validated using the experimental data. This study will then experimentally investigate the influence of the dust load on the air resistance and PM2.5 removal efficiency for nanofiber window screens. Empirical dust load functions will be established. Both the air resistance model and the dust load functions will be implemented into an existing exposure assessment method. The developed method will then be applied to assess the performance of nanofiber window screens in residential buildings in Beijing. Finally, we will optimize the fiber diameters based on experimental results to reduce the air resistance without sacrificing the PM2.5 removal efficiency. The proposed project will enhance our knowledge of how the window opening angle, dust load, and fiber diameter affect the air resistance of nanofiber window screens. 24208518.label: Realisation of objectives
24208518.value: All of the 6 objectives have been fully achieved. This project fabricated a number of nanofiber window screens using the electrospinning technique with nylon 6 as the nanofiber material. A series of experiments were conducted with a laboratory setup consisting of a testing tunnel, a variable-speed fan, an airflow controller, a manometer, and two particle counters. The airflow rates, pressure drops, and PM2.5 removal efficiencies were measured under different window opening angles and face velocities. The obtained experimental data can be used for model development and validation. Therefore, Objective 1 “to experimentally investigate the resistance of the airflow through nanofiber window screens with the window at different opening angles” has been fully achieved. To develop an air resistance model, this project assumed the process of the airflow through a nanofiber window screen as two separate steps. First, the outdoor air moves across the nanofiber window screen. Then, the air moves through the window with an opening angle. In this hypothetical process, the air has to overcome the resistance of both the nanofiber window screen and the window with an opening angle. With this assumption, a numerical model was then developed for predicting the pressure drop. The measured data was then used to validate the model. Therefore, Objective 2 “to develop and validate an air resistance model for predicting the airflow rate through nanofiber window screens with the window at different opening angles” has been fully achieved. This project conducted a series of experiments to understand the evolution of wetting liquid aerosols, taking incense particles as an example, on nanofiber filter media and the influence of this evolution on PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop. The evolution of pressure drop may consist of two stages, i.e., a first stage with a linear relationship, and a second stage with a steep increase in pressure drop with the loading mass. This project also experimentally investigated the relationship between the pressure drop and solid particle loading mass for a number of nanofiber filters under various face velocities. The results show that the air resistance coefficient increased with the solid particle loading mass for the nanofiber filter media. Based on the experimental data, semi-empirical equations were developed for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop as a function of loading mass for both wetting liquid aerosols and solid particles. Therefore, Objective 3 “To experimentally investigate the influence of the dust load on the air resistance and PM2.5 removal efficiency, and establish empirical dust load functions” has been fully achieved. This project then implemented the air resistance model and semi-empirical dust load equations into the exposure assessment method for assessing the indoor exposure to PM2.5 of outdoor origin. The developed air resistance model improved the prediction of the air exchange rate and the particle penetration through the nanofiber window screens as the influence of window opening angles can be well considered. The semi-empirical dust load functions allowed us to consider the influence of the dust load, which is crucial for long-term performance assessment. The exposure assessment method with the air resistance model and semi-empirical dust load equations can be used for long-term performance assessment of nanofiber window screen in indoor particle control. Therefore, Objective 4 “to implement the air resistance model and dust load functions into an existing exposure assessment method for assessing the indoor exposure to PM2.5 of outdoor origin” has been fully achieved. This project applied the developed exposure assessment method to assess the performance of nanofiber window screens under various scenarios. First, we focused on a one-storey detached house. The influence of nanofiber window screen on the natural ventilation rate and the concentration ratio of indoor PM2.5 of outdoor origin to outdoor PM2.5 was numerically explored using the developed method. Second, we considered a case with kitchen ventilation using a range hood of a residential building in Beijing. A nanofiber window screen was used to filter the outdoor PM2.5 in the makeup air. The effectiveness of using nanofiber window screens on reducing the PM2.5 concentrations in the kitchen was numerically investigated. Finally, we considered a case with the nanofiber filter installed in an air cleaner. The developed method was used to estimate the indoor PM2.5 of outdoor origin as a function of filter usage time for a typical apartment in Beijing. Therefore, Objective 5 “to apply the developed method to assess the performance of nanofiber window screens in residential buildings in Beijing in terms of the PM2.5 removal and the air exchange rate” has been fully achieved. This project conducted laboratory experiments on the relationship between the fiber diameter and PM2.5 filtration efficiency and pressure drop under different face velocities for a number of different nanofiber filters fabricated using the electrospinning technique. Based on the experimental data, this project optimized the fiber diameter to minimize the pressure drop under a given PM2.5 filtration efficiency and face velocity. With the proposed approach, the fabricated nanofiber window screens can lower the air resistance, namely increase the ventilation rate, under the same PM2.5 filtration efficiency. Therefore, Objective 6 “to experimentally optimize the fiber diameters to reduce the air resistance of the nanofiber window screens without sacrificing the PM2.5 removal efficiency” has been fully achieved.

24208518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24208518.value: Major findings: 1. An air resistance model was developed for predicting the airflow rate through nanofiber window screens with the window at different opening angles. The developed model was validated by the measured data obtained in our laboratory experiments. The validated air resistance model can be used for predicting the airflow rate through nanofiber window screens. 2. The influence of dust loading on nanofiber air filter media for both wetting liquid aerosols and solid particles was experimentally investigated. Based on the experimental data, semi-empirical equations were developed for predicting the PM2.5 removal efficiency and pressure drop as a function of loading mass. The developed semi-empirical equations can be used for assessing long-term performance of nanofiber air filter media. 3. The exposure assessment method for assessing the indoor exposure to PM2.5 of outdoor origin was improved by implementing the air resistance model and semi-empirical dust load equations. The improved exposure assessment method can be used for long-term performance assessment of nanofiber window screen in indoor particle control. 4. The case studies using the improved exposure assessment method for residential buildings with natural ventilation, kitchen range hood ventilation, and portable air cleaner show that the use of nanofiber window screens can reduce indoor exposure to PM2.5 of outdoor origin but also reduce the ventilation rate. 5. The fiber diameter of nanofiber window screens was optimized based on the measured data obtained from our laboratory experiments. The optimized fiber diameter can minimize the pressure drop under a given PM2.5 filtration efficiency. Namely, the corresponding nanofiber window screens can achieve higher ventilation rate under the same PM2.5 filtration efficiency. Research outcome: This project has led to 6 journal publications in Building and Environment, Journal of Hazardous Materials, Applied Materials Today, and Building Simulation. The research results were disseminated in two ISIAQ conferences Indoor Air 2020 and Healthy Buildings 2021 America.

24208518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24208518.value: There are two directions for further development of the research. First, with the improved exposure assessment method, a large-scale simulation project can be conducted to comprehensively assess the long-term performance of nanofiber window screens in indoor particulate pollution control in different residential buildings under different climates. The gains in health benefits and the costs can be compared to assess whether this technology is suitable for applications under different situations. The results will also serve as the basis for promoting the application of nanofiber window screens in indoor particulate pollution control. Second, with the improved understanding of nanofiber window screens, a technology development project can be conducted to realize the scalable and efficient manufacturing of nanofiber window screens with high quality and relatively low costs. The development of the manufacturing technologies may facilitate the practical applications of this new technology.

24208518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24208518.value: Severe outdoor air pollution has become a major threat to public health. A large amount of outdoor PM2.5 can enter into indoor environments through ventilation and infiltration. For many residential housing, when outdoor PM2.5 pollution is severe, people are inclined to close their windows to reduce the indoor exposure to some extent. However, doing so results in a low air exchange rate with poor indoor air quality. Nanofiber window screens can be potentially applied for solving this problem as it can act as air filters to capture outdoor PM2.5 from the incoming air. Meanwhile, the relatively low air resistance because of the slip effect may be able to help maintain the air exchange rate at an acceptable level for ensuring indoor air quality. This project characterized the air resistance of nanofiber window screens for effectively assessing the performance of nanofiber window screens in buildings. The obtained results enhance our knowledge of how the window opening angle, dust load, and fiber diameter affect the air resistance of nanofiber window screens. The findings can advance the development of this novel intervention technology for reducing indoor exposure to PM2.5 of outdoor origin while maintaining adequate natural ventilation.

24209418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24209418.value: The World Wide Web has merged into our life by powering numerous applications on the Internet that we use on a daily basis. While enjoying various rich features provided by web applications, the security of our online data is also at risk. A lot of sensitive data, e.g., personally identifiable information (PII), authentication tokens, and online transaction data, is presented in modern web applications, which have become the primary targets for cyber attacks. Attackers would usually launch code injection attacks against a target website to compromise its confidentiality and integrity because the injected JavaScript code has full privilege over the victim website. To mitigate code injection attacks, modern browsers all have implemented the Content Security Policy (CSP) in addition to the Same-origin policy. CSP prevents unknown scripts from being executed but does not restrict a "trusted" script's ability to access web content, including sensitive content. Thus, compromising a "trusted" script becomes another approach to injecting malicious code. State-of-the-art security mechanisms focus on protecting mainly the confidentiality of data in web applications, leaving the integrity of data unprotected. Many proposals do not provide fine-grained data protection either, as they mostly aim to limit a script's available functionalities. The few proposals protecting individual HTML elements have limitations on deployment and compatibility. In this project, we propose Content Protection Policy (CPP), a new web security mechanism for providing both confidentiality and integrity guarantees for sensitive user data in web applications. We aim to enable object-level protection instead of page-level protection by using a data-centric approach in the design of CPP. CPP follows the fail-safe defaults and least privilege security principles. Developers need to explicitly specify only the allowed content accesses. Any unauthorized content access is automatically denied by default. CPP complements existing security mechanisms and offers web developers a much finer-grained and flexible control to protect their sensitive data. We will further develop techniques to help website administrators generate security policies to minimize the deployment cost of CPP. The outcomes of this project would help further mitigate the impact of content injection attacks to make the Web more secure. 通過驅動我們日常使用的數量衆多的應用程式，萬維網已經融入了我們的生活。當我們享受網絡應用程式的衆多功能時，我們在網絡上的數據安全也處於危險中。現代的網路應用程式包含許多敏感的數據，例如個人識別信息（PII），身份驗證令牌，以及網上交易數據。因此，這些網絡應用程式已經成爲網絡攻擊的主要目標。攻擊者通常會通過代碼注入攻擊來威脅一個目標網站的機密性和完整性，因爲注入的JavaScript代碼擁有被注入網站的全部權限。 爲了緩解代碼注入攻擊的危害，現代的瀏覽器都實現了同源策略（SOP）和內容安全策略（CSP）。內容安全策略可以防止未知腳本執行。但是，它並不限制“可信的”腳本訪問包括敏感內容在內的網絡內容。因而，控制一個“可信的”腳本成爲了注入惡意代碼的另一種方式。目前最先進的安全機制專注於主要保護網絡應用程式數據的機密性，這些數據的完整性並不受保護。許多新的研究提案也不提供細粒度的數據保護，因爲它們通常旨在限制一個腳本可使用的功能。少數保護個別的HTML元素的提案則有部署和兼容性的缺點。 我們在這項研究課題中提出內容保護策略（CPP）。它是一個新的可以同時保護網絡應用程式中用戶數據的機密性和完整性的網絡安全機制。我們旨在通過一個以數據爲中心的方法在CPP的設計中提供對象級別的保護而不是頁面級別的保護。CPP遵循失效安全默認及最低權限兩個安全原則。開發者僅需要明確地指定允許的內容訪問，任何未授權的內容訪問會被默認拒絕。CPP與現有的安全機制互補，它提供給網絡開發者一個更細粒度和靈活的控制以保護他們的敏感數據。我們將會進一步研發幫助網站管理者生成安全策略的技術來降低CPP的部署成本。這項研究項目的成果可以幫助進一步降低內容注入攻擊的影響力並讓萬維網更加安全。

24209418.label: Realisation of objectives
24209418.value: The major project objectives have been all realized. We discuss next in detail how and to what extent each objective has been achieved. 5.3.1 Allow developers to define the access permission of remote JavaScript per object using a new policy language. We have designed the policy language allowing the developers to limit a script’s access permission. In particular, the developers can specify whether a script is allowed to read and/or write the data of a DOM object, including its child DOM objects, and execute methods of a DOM object. The child DOM nodes automatically inherit the policy specified for their ancestor DOM node, unless a policy is directly defined for them. The policy can be defined as an inline HTML attribute, or defined in special HTML policy tags——that we introduce. The policies can also be defined in a separate policy file and be loaded into a tag. The objects can be selected using syntax similar to CSS selectors. We have implemented the language support in the Chromium browser parser, supporting both inline and external policies. Since our new access control policy has not been deployed by real websites yet, we implemented a proxy for dynamically injecting access control policy into matched web pages. 5.3.2 Extend protection to cover persistent client-side data. We have studied how to extend the content protection to cover persistent client-side storage, such as Cookies and Local Storage. In the current browser architecture, all scripts can access the same storage, which may include very sensitive first-party data. In our research, we focused on investigating cookie accesses. To limit third-party script’s access to first-party storage data, we can block all cookie accesses made by third-party scripts. Only if explicitly permitted by the developer, the access can be allowed. However, this design could break the functionality of third-party scripts. To preserve functionalities, we have changed the current browser storage architecture by providing isolated client-side storage in the Chromium browser. In particular, we maintain in each web frame two isolated cookie storage instances: one for first-party scripts and one for third-party scripts. The isolation is transparently provided without requiring any JavaScript code change. When a script accesses the cookies, the corresponding storage is returned based on the privilege level of the script. Consequently, the third-party scripts can still operate normally without the ability of directly accessing the first-party storage. 5.3.3 Provide support for limiting a script’s available functionalities. We have identified a list of sensitive HTML5 DOM APIs, and implemented access control mechanism for a few APIs that can be directly accessed without asking the users to explicitly grant permissions at run time. If a script is denied access according to the access control policy, the call of a particular API would result in nothing. This mechanism largely depends on the element access control mechanism that we develop for achieving the fourth objective. In particular, it shares the same logic to check the identity of an active script invoking the API. More details are discussed next. 5.3.4 Develop reference monitors to mediate resource accesses. To implement the reference monitor at the DOM layer, we have extended Observer—a browser based JavaScript analysis system—that we developed. Observer supports basic monitoring of HTMLAnchorElement, which implements the hyperlinks in a web page. We have added access control support to all HTML Elements. In particular, we modify the IDL files for all HTML Element classes to add extended IDL attributes for performing access control on their attributes and methods. Our modified IDL compiler in the Chromium browser can then automatically generate access control code in the V8 JavaScript binding layer for these classes. The automatically generated code serves as the reference monitor that can mediate direct access to resources represented by those HTML Elements. When any protected element or DOM API is being accessed by JavaScript code, the access control enforcement code inspects the JavaScript call stack to identify the accessing script and fetches the corresponding access control policy to make runtime access control decision. 5.3.5 Study ways to support JavaScript runtime isolation. We have developed an isolation mechanism for client-side JavaScript code. We designed a lightweight browser-based framework, JSIsolate, that provides an isolated and reliable JavaScript execution environment. It loads scripts into different isolated environments based on their dependency relationship. JSIsolate operates in two modes: a dynamic script-dependency analysis mode, and a policy enforcement mode that separates JavaScript in isolated execution environments (contexts) to provide higher reliability. In the first mode, JSIsolate analyzes the dependency relationship between scripts. In the second mode, for each group of functionality-dependent scripts, JSIsolate spawns an isolated execution environment. In this way, it executes scripts with independent functionalities in different contexts, effectively preventing them from interfering with each other. 5.3.6 Study policy generation techniques to help developers minimize the deployment cost. We have proposed and developed a semi-automated approach to generating DOM access control policies for web pages. We identify potentially sensitive content in a page with several heuristics and differential testing using different user profiles. We then instruct the instrumented browser to operate in the monitoring mode to collect all DOM access logs. Assuming all the scripts behave correctly during the monitoring phase, we automatically generate policies based on the collected logs to prevent any unobserved accesses that deviate from the logged ones. However, this auto-generated policy could potentially break the web page as the logs only reflect the default operations of the scripts. To avoid any potential compatibility issues, we then apply automated UI testing on the target page to trigger as much code as possible. We further expand the collected logs and refine the policy with several rounds of testing. The final policy we generate serves as a starting point for the developers, who can further fine adjust the policy according to their implementation details and security needs.

24209418.label: Major findings and research outcome
24209418.value: In this project, we investigated how to develop a fine-grained object level resource protection mechanism to provide both confidentiality and integrity protection for sensitive data in client- side web applications. Our research has led to the publication of three research papers and two poster papers at top-tier computer science conferences—CCS, WWW and ESEC/FSE, and one Ph.D. thesis and one M.Phil. thesis. We have studied some new practices of privilege abuse at client side by third-party scripts. First, we investigated an integrity problem—click interception, where malicious third-party scripts can intercept user clicks to control the navigation. Second, we studied a new threat to web users—cryptojacking, where malicious websites or scripts automatically start cryptocurrency mining leveraging a victim user’s computer browser without obtaining the user’s consent. Third, we studied another client-side integrity problem—JavaScript name conflicts, where all scripts share the same global JavaScript name space, and thus can overwrite other scripts’ objects. We have also developed the methods and system to provide fine-grained object level content protection in the Chromium browser. We have implemented a reference monitor in the browser to perform object level access control to protect sensitive content from untrusted third-party scripts. We have designed and implemented mechanisms to provide both isolated JavaScript execution environments and isolated cookie storage in the browser. Finally, we have developed a method to semi-automatically generate the access control policies for web pages.

24209418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24209418.value: As a future work, we could investigate better methods to identify sensitive client-side contents in a web application and to automatically generate and update content protection policies. We could also study and evaluate the real-world benefit and cost of deploying and maintaining the proposed content protection mechanism.

24209418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24209418.value: A lot of sensitive data, e.g., personally identifiable information (PII), authentication tokens, and online transaction data, is presented in modern web applications. Such data can be directly accessed by any untrusted third-party scripts loaded into the same web frame. In this project, we proposed and developed Content Protection Policy (CPP), a new web security mechanism for providing both confidentiality and integrity guarantees for sensitive user data in web applications. It offers a fine-grained object-level protection by using a data-centric approach. We have designed a policy language allowing the developers to limit a script’s access permission, and implemented the mechanisms to enforce their protection needs in the Chromium browser.

24209618.label: Project Objectives
24209618.value: To bridge the semantic gap and facilitate fast secure deletion for sequential-write-constrained storage, we will develop an efficient communication framework that enables file system to transmit file identification information to the storage device. We will fulfil fast secure deletion for 3D NAND flash devices. Specially, we will proactively store data in different flash blocks based on the files, so as to efficiently delete data of files by erasing the corresponding flash block. We also intend to exploit the subblock erase operations supported by 3D flash memory to reduce the data erasing unit for further reduction of secure deletion amplification. We will fulfil fast secure deletion for SMR drives. Specially, when storing data into SMR drives based on the files, we will simultaneously maintain data sequentiality and high secure deletion efficiency. Additionally, we will explore different possible methods (such as virtually creating smaller SMR zones and dynamically creating isolation) to further overcome the severer secure deletion amplification due to large SMR zone size. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework and methodologies, we will develop both experimental platforms and theoretical models to conduct performance evaluations based on realistic data workloads and average/worst-cases analysis respectively.

24209618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24209618.value: To bridge the demand-supply gap between data generation and storage production, 3D NAND flash memory and shingled magnetic recording (SMR) disk drive technology offer the promising capability of increasing the areal density for the conventional flash memory and hard disk drives, respectively. In this information age, in addition to storing data in a cost-effective way, reliably deleting data from the storage media is one of the most critical design concerns in data security. Nevertheless, because of the severe “write disturbance problem” and imposed “sequential write constraint” on these emerging high-density storage technologies, most existing secure data deletion techniques will encounter enormous difficulty in efficiently and securely deleting data, especially when the amount of data and storage capacity are still dramatically increasing. This study is strongly inspired by the urgent need to fulfil fast and secure data deletion for the two most promising high-density yet write-constrained storage technologies. To identify the root cause of inefficiency in secure data deletion, we conducted a series of preliminary evaluations and discovered that a large semantic gap between the file system and storage device may exist. That is, in most file system designs, data are managed and securely deleted in the unit of a file, but the storage device knows nothing about the files. To bridge the observed semantic gap between the file system and storage device, we propose to leverage the concept of “file stream” or “file identification” to develop an efficient communication framework for facilitating transmission of information from the file system to the storage. The ultimate objective of this framework is to enable the storage device to proactively manage its storage space based on the concept of files, so that an efficient mechanism can be developed to securely delete the files from the storage. On top of the proposed framework, we also intend to exploit the special hardware characteristics of 3D NAND flash memory and SMR technology to further improve the secure deletion efficiency. To validate the effectiveness of our framework and methodologies, we plan to conduct experimental evaluations based on realistic workloads and theoretical amortized/worst-case analysis. The success of this research will ensure that the precious data are not only stored cost-effectively but also deleted securely and efficiently. Being a crucial international trade and finance center, Hong Kong has identified ensuring data protection and secure deletion as being particularly crucial. Thus, developing reliable and efficient data storage is extremely important for Hong Kong. 為了縮小資料產生與存儲生產之間的供需差，新興之三維NAND快閃記憶體技術與疊瓦式磁紀錄硬碟技術能分別替傳統的快閃記憶體與硬碟有效地提升存儲空間密度。在這個資訊時代，除了更低成本地儲存資料，如何可靠地從存儲媒介上刪除資料也是資料安全中最關鍵的設計考量之一。然而，由於上述這兩種新興高密度存儲技術所特有之較嚴重地「寫入干擾問題」與新引發地「循序寫入限制」，大部份現有的安全資料刪除技術將會面臨無法高效率將資料安全刪除之巨大困難；尤其，快速成長的資料量和存儲容量更將可能惡化這個問題。 此研究的動機為如何能基於新興高密度但具循序寫入限制存儲裝置實現快速且安全地資料刪除技術之迫切需求。為了能找出無法高效率地安全刪除資料之根本原因，此研究進行了一系列實驗、並觀察到檔案系統與存儲裝置之間可能存在巨大的語意落差。亦即在大部份現有的檔案系統設計中，資料是以檔案為單位被管理或刪除，然而存儲裝置卻對檔案的概念一無所知。因此，為了能縮小這個存在於檔案系統與存儲裝置間的語意落差，此研究提出了利用「檔案串流」或「檔案識別」的概念來開發一個有效地資訊傳遞框架，並希望藉此框架能促進由檔案系統至存儲裝置之資訊傳遞。而此框架的最終目的是讓存儲裝置能以檔案之概念主動地管理存儲空間，並且讓資料從存儲媒介中快速且安全地刪除之技術也能得以實現。基於所提出的框架，此研究更希望能巧妙利用三維NAND快閃記憶體技術與疊瓦式磁紀錄硬碟技術之特性，來進一步地提升安全資料刪除技術之效率。為了驗證所提出之框架與資料刪除技術之有效性，此研究亦預期進行一連串基於真實工作負載之實驗測評和一般與最壞情境之理論分析。 此研究的成功將能確保具高價值之資料不僅能被更低成本地儲存著，更能有效率及可靠地從存儲媒介上被刪除。身處國際貿易與經濟中心，資料保護與安全刪除對香港而言極其重要，發展可靠且高效率之資料存儲對香港的重要性更是不可言喻。

24209618.label: Realisation of objectives
24209618.value: This project has been going very well. All the objectives stated in this project have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. For Objective 1, we have studied and implemented a method to enable the file system to transmit the file identification information to the storage device. The key idea of this method is to piggyback the file identification information (which is kept in the inode of the virtual file system) on a reserved field of both regular and queued write commands as specified in the Advanced Technology Attached (ATA) command set; consequently, the file identification can be sent along with every single write request from the file system to the storage device. Also, we have extended this method to enable applications to pass any other identification information to the file system and eventually to the storage device along with the write requests. This idea can be implemented by passing the information through the fadvise system call, which, in turn, stores the information in the inode of the virtual file system; as a result, any other identification information, specified by the applications, can be eventually pass to the storage device along with the write requests (as what we pass the file identification information). As a case study, we pick the LSM-tree based key-value (KV) store, the mainstream implementation of building KV store for write-intensive workloads, as an application to practice the extended method of information passing. In particular, we successfully pass the “level” and “invalidation” information from KV store to the SMR storage device to facilitate the data management. For Objective 2, we have proposed a semantic-aware secure deletion scheme to improve the performance and endurance of NAND flash devices for secure deletion via multi-streamed SSDs. The main idea is to utilize file semantic information by attaching them to each data access, then properly allocate the data destination based on the attached file hints. The objective is to reduce as much erasure and data movement as possible. It is remarkable that this scheme can be applied to any hardware protocol that is able to transfer secure deletion commands and coordinates interface with any block-based file system. Meanwhile, as the design concept is to bring in extra information to the core flash management via multi-stream SSD technology, there is no significant change required to the systems. It is encouraging that the evaluations based on the real-world implementation demonstrate that the proposed scheme can reduce 79.36% of erase operations and 83.4% extra data movement on average while performing the secure deletion on SSDs with confidence. Also, we have studied the special characteristics of the latest bit-alterable 3D NAND flash memory and devised a bit-level error removal (BER) scheme to remove error bits via the bit-level operations, which may reduce the data erasing unit for further reduction of secure deletion amplification. For Objective 3, we have devised a file-oriented fast secure deletion (FFSD) strategy which can securely erase a deleted file on SMR drives via a single command with the file identification specified by file systems. Specifically, to realize the FFSD strategy, we first close up the gap between the file systems and the storage devices via passing the file identification (i.e., fid) information from file systems to storage devices. Then, we present 1) an adaptive guard barrier mechanism to isolate each data chunk by inserting adaptive guard barriers in SMR zones for alleviating the sequential-write constraint of SMR drives and lower the write amplification during secure deletion; 2) a space utilization enhancement policy to avoid fragmented storage space with the concept of tail packing; 3) a file-oriented space management design to utilize the fid information specified by the file system to arrange file data and group the LBA-to-PBA mapping entries, thus avoiding the inefficient fid-to-LBA conversion in the file system; and 4) a ghost space reclamation scheme to reclaim space from the ghost space lists when SMR drives run out of free space. Based on real-world workloads, the proposed FFSD strategy can effectively reduce the secure deletion latency by 286.15x on average when compared with the conventional secure deletion approach. For Objective 4, we have developed experimental platforms for NAND flash devices by extending the public SSD simulator SSDSim to interconnect multiple control units with flash chips through high-speed interface and by implementing on a multi-channel SSD emulator. As for the experimental platforms for SMR drives, we have developed an in-house simulator to measure the performance behaviour of SMR drives and developed an emulator that can be utilized to evaluate hard disk drives based on different magnetic recording technologies. On the other hand, we have utilized a variety of realistic data workloads to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and methodologies. For example, we have evaluated the well-known file system and storage benchmarks (i.e., Filebench and Postmark), the widely adopted on-line transaction processing (OLTP) benchmarks (i.e., TPC-C and TPC-E), and the representative traces collected from 875 file system snapshots by Microsoft Research.

24209618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24209618.value: As the proposed schemes mainly focus on securely and efficiently deleting the file content, one possible direction of further development is to support the fast secure deletion of the file system metadata (i.e., inode and directory) or the journaling data in journaling file systems. On the other hand, as storage technologies keep evolving, we also believe that this research project can be regarded as an instructive role model in how to fulfil fast secure deletion for other types of emerging storage devices, such as the zoned namespaces (ZNS) SSD and Interlaced Magnetic Recording (IMR) based HDD.

24306318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24306318.value: This project aims to achieve controllable heterovalent doping of halide perovskite nanocrystals, to develop novel and efficient doping strategies for adjustable electrical and optical properties, and to demonstrate their potential applications in versatile optoelectronic devices. Halide perovskite has accomplished significant triumphs in the field of photovoltaics due to its superior electrical and optical properties. Recently, some of the research efforts have been shifted to explore the material’s potential applications beyond photovoltaics, such as in light-emitting diodes, sensors, and transistors. To this purpose, doping, as one of the most important methods offering diverse freedoms to semiconducting materials, stands out as a feasible route to modify the properties of halide perovskite materials. In this project, we will focus on the heterovalent doping of halide perovskite nanocrystals, for the following reasons. (1) Compared with isovalent doping, heterovalent doping offers a remarkably high tunability in free carrier concentration, bandgap, position of Fermi level, conductivity, and etc. Under heavy doping, wide bandgaps may even be narrowed into the infrared region. (2) Not only can nanocrystals be easily processed and incorporated into versatile materials and devices, but they also provide a handle for the modification of physical properties via the quantum confinement effect. (3) The heterovalent doping of semiconducting nanocrystals remains a challenge in semiconductor research. Its basic mechanism is not yet fully understood and therefore of great scientific merit. Our preliminary results have confirmed that heterovalent doping with Ag+ can be achieved using a colloidal synthesis method, producing desired behaviors in doped halide perovskite nanocrystals, such as changes in position of Fermi level, conductivity, and optical absorption and emission. Our trial of mixing doped perovskite nanocrystals into an organic bulk heterojunction active layer, achieved a promising increase in the photocurrent of solar cells. In the proposed research, we will carefully study the kinetics of doping reactions and develop a controllable doping strategy that can be extended to other kinds of dopants and host crystals. We will use state-of-the-art characterization methods to measure doping efficiency, doping concentration, dopant location, dopant electrical activity, etc. and correlate these characteristics with the adjusted electrical and optical properties. The successful implementation of the proposed project will provide a fundamental understanding of doping mechanisms, elucidate the intrinsic correlation between doping and the electrical and optical properties of halide perovskite nanocrystals, and pave the way for the wider application of halide perovskite in versatile optoelectronic devices.

24306318.label: Realisation of objectives
24306318.value: To develop novel and efficient doping strategies to realize adjustable electrical and optical properties in halide perovskite NCs, we constructed two set-ups for room-temperature and high-temperature synthesis of colloidal perovskite nanocrystals. We reported for the first time a successful controlled heterovalent doping of Ag+ and Bi3+ in substitution of Pb2+ in colloidal CsPbBr3 NCs via a simple room-temperature synthesis method (ACS Energy Lett. 2019, 4, 534-541). The Ag+ doping has demonstrated great potential in modulating the electrical properties of CsPbBr3 NCs. It was found that undoped CsPbBr3 NCs exhibit poor electrical conductivity and very low charge-carrier mobility. After Ag+ doping, significant improvement of both the conductivity and charge-carrier mobility by nearly 3 orders of magnitude has been achieved. Low-temperature (<230 K), demonstrating the remarkable tunability of heterovalent doping on the electrical properties of halide perovskite NCs through the feasible room-temperature doping method. To use comprehensive characterization methods to quantify dopant incorporation details such as doping efficiency, dopant concentration, dopant location, and dopant electrical activity, and to elucidate the underlying doping mechanisms, we introduce multiple characterization methods. Firstly, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) was used to characterize the relationship between the concentration in the feed solution and the concentration in the resultant quantum dot. For instance, the correlation between the Ag+ concentration in doped CsPbBr3 NCs (Cm) and the concentration of Ag+ in the feed solution (Cideal) were investigated. To confirm the existence of Ag+ in the core of CsPbBr3 NCs, all doped NC samples were washed with toluene to remove the surface adsorbed or loosely bonded dopants. It was estimated from a linear fitting of Cm versus Cideal that about 16% of the Ag+ ions in the feed solution were successfully incorporated into the CsPbBr3 NCs. Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) results demonstrated that the Ag+ doping induces electronically active impurities, which induce energy levels near the valence band of CsPbBr3 NCs. Therefore, the band structure of CsPbBr3 NCs can be readily tuned by changing the doping concentration. And furthermore, we investigated, with the assistance of in situ grazing-incidence wide-angle and small-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS/GISAXS), distinct phase behaviors of CsPbI3 QD films under two different temperature profiles – instant heating-up and slow heating-up (ref 13, manuscript submitted). Detailed studies and structural refinement analysis revealed that the black-to-yellow phase transition is triggered by the removal of surface ligands, which switches the energy landscape from the QD state to the “strained bulk” state. The lattice strain maintained in the black phase before the transition determines the transition rate and the coexistence black-to-yellow phase ratio. And the interstitial bismuth ions would decrease the lattice symmetry, therefore, stabilizing the whole lattice and preventing the phase transition. To correlate the doping characteristics with the resultant electrical and optical properties, we performed a systematic study on the ionic and electronic transport mechanism in films of CsPbBr3 NCs by using a combination of transient response characterization and thin-film transistor measurement. It was revealed that electronic current is the dominant current passing through the CsPbBr3-NC films under dark conditions. The electronic current is found to be significantly augmented when the ion migration is gradually awakened at T > 240 K. The remarkable current amplification could be attributed to a combination of factors originating from the mobile-ion-induced p-doping modification and the inefficient long-range ionic transport that avoids serious ion accumulation at the device interfaces. At room temperature, the ion-induced doping effect prevails over the gating effect in the FET measurements, resulting in no clear gate modulation of the channel current. However, at T < 240 K the electronic transport can be readily decoupled from the ionic transport in CsPbBr3 NCs, leading to a clean unipolar transport characteristic in a p-type mode featuring well-defined linear and saturation regimes. Moreover, the elimination of intrinsic doping induced by mobile ions greatly facilitates the investigation of extrinsic dopant incorporation on the electronic transport in CsPbBr3 NCs. In particular, the Bi3+ doping raises the fermi level of CsPbBr3 NCs and switches the device to a normally-off (enhancement) p-channel transistor, whereas the incorporation of Ag+ lowers the fermi level and switches the device to a normally on (depletion) p-channel transistor. Impressive hole mobility approaching 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1, the on−off ratio of ∼104, and turn-on voltage in a wide range of −30 to 20 V has been demonstrated from the CsPbBr3-NC-based FETs. It revealed a different interplay mechanism between ionic transport and electronic transport in perovskite NC films, compared with that observed in conventional semiconductor films. The current experimental progress on the ionic−electronic transport dynamics should contribute to the improvement of optoelectronic devices based on halide perovskite NCs and the design of novel electronic devices such as synaptic memtransistors through both intrinsic and extrinsic doping (ACS Energy Letters 2020, 5 (8), 2614-2623). To demonstrate the potential applications of doped perovskite NCs in optoelectronic devices, hybrid solar cells were fabricated (ACS Applied Energy Materials 2020, 3 (11), 11359-11367). We fabricated a novel hybrid organic and perovskite PV device by mixing CsPbI3 QDs into a conventional organic system PBDB-T: IT-M. The energy level alignment of QDs and OPV materials was effectively tuned by changing the QDs size and heterovalent doping to facilitate charge transfer between perovskite QDs and OPV materials. The BHJ film morphology, particularly the size of the intermixing amorphous region was also modified for more efficient exciton collection. The intensity profiles are fitted with the Debye−Anderson−Brumberger model and the fractal-like network model to quantify the correlation length (ξ) of the intermixing amorphous phase and the average domain size (2Rg) of IT-M phases. It is evident that the addition of all three types of CsPbI3 QDs could largely shrink the amorphous intermixing domain, and the organic intermixing domain sizes (ξ) are reduced after the addition of Bi-doped QDs. Although exciton dissociation was sufficient in the intermixing region, the dissociated electrons and holes were largely recombined due to the lack of connected charge transport pathways. Consequently, a smaller intermixing region was helpful to the dissociated charges transport, promoting the exciton utilization from amorphous regions. QDs did not affect the aggregation of acceptor crystalline domains. Consequently, a considerable decrease in charge recombination and in turn an increase of FF, Voc, and Jsc were achieved. Furthermore, the incorporation of CsPbI3 QDs also improves the photocurrent of the devices through Rayleigh scattering and their own light absorption. Consequently, a maximum increase of 12.2% in PCE has been achieved, compared with the control device. During the progress of this project, we also established close collaborations with several leading teams in the field and obtained interesting results in terms of perovskite solar cells (Advanced Functional Materials 2021, 31 (28), 2101287;Matter 2021, 4 (1), 313-327; Adv Mater 2021, 33 (22), e2100009; J Phys Chem Lett 2021, 12 (45), 10996-11004; Small 2020, 16 (42), e2003098; etc ) and patterned macromolecular film growth (Adv Mater 2021, 33 (29), e2006836).

24306318.label: Major findings and research outcome
24306318.value: Through this project, we published 13 publications in peer-reviewed journals and presented our results 4 times at local and international conferences (part C). Overall, our results provided guidelines and insights for efficiently doping in versatile PQD-based devices. Major finding 1: We developed novel and efficient doping strategies to realize adjustable electrical and optical properties in halide perovskite NCs. We report for the first time a controlled doping of monovalent Ag+ into CsPbBr3 NCs via a facile room-temperature synthesis method. Field effect transistors fabricated with Ag+-doped CsPbBr3 NCs exhibit 3 orders of magnitude enhancement in hole mobility at room temperature, compared with undoped CsPbBr3 NCs. Low-temperature electrical studies further confirm the influence of Ag+ doping on the charge carrier transport. Major finding 2: We used comprehensive characterization methods to quantify dopant incorporation details such as doping efficiency, dopant concentration, dopant location, and dopant electrical activity, and to elucidate the underlying doping mechanisms. We utilize the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) to successfully quantify the relationship between the concentration in the feed solution and the concentration in the resultant quantum dot. Furthermore, we successfully identify the substitutional doping and interstitial doping respectively, and further reveal the transition between the two different doping styles. Major finding 3: We correlated the doping characteristics with the resultant electrical and optical properties. We fabricate all-inorganic CsPbBr3 NCs terminated with short ligands into field effect transistors, providing a facile platform to study the electronic−ionic transport systematically. By combining with transient response characterization, we demonstrate that electronic current is the dominant current passing through perovskite-NC films under dark conditions, while mobile ions induce intrinsic doping to perovskite NCs, which gradually changes the film conductivity and thereby the magnitude of the electronic current. Major finding 4: We demonstrated the potential applications of doped perovskite NCs in optoelectronic devices. We demonstrated a novel hybrid organic and perovskite PV device by mixing all-inorganic CsPbI3 quantum dots (QDs) into the conventional organic bulk heterojunction active layer of PBDB-T: IT-M. It is found that the charge transfer properties between QDs and organic D/A interfaces can be finetuned with the size modulation and the hetero-valent bismuth (Bi) doping of perovskite QDs, leading to the increase of open circuit voltage. Besides, the incorporation of perovskite QDs with different sizes could effectively modify the nanoscale bulk heterojunction morphology towards more efficient charge collection and thus higher fill factor.

24306318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24306318.value: Heterovalent doping of halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs), offering potential tunability in optical and electrical properties, remains a grand challenge. Meanwhile, improving devices based on solution-processed halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) demands a deeper understanding of charge transport in this emerging new class of ionic semiconductor nanomaterials. This project develops novel and efficient doping strategies to realize adjustable electrical and optical properties in halide perovskite NCs. Comprehensive characterization methods were used to quantify dopant incorporation details such as doping efficiency, dopant concentration, dopant location, and dopant electrical activity, and to elucidate the underlying doping mechanisms. We correlated the doping characteristics with the resultant electrical and optical properties and further demonstrated the potential applications of doped perovskite NCs in optoelectronic devices such as hybrid solar cells. These works demonstrated the tunability of heterovalent doping on the electrical properties of halide perovskite NCs, shedding light on their future applications in versatile optoelectronic devices.

24500418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500418.value: Many organizations, from a manufacturing system to a hospital, seek to increase their productivity. For a manufacturing system, such as an automobile production line, high productivity means more products being produced and more money being made. For a hospital, high productivity means more patients being treated/cured and more lives being saved. Motivated by observations around the world and especially in Hong Kong, we propose to study how to effectively improve productivity from an operations perspective using linear/integer programming and combinatorial analysis. In the Operations Management (OM) literature, organizations can be modeled as processes, and the maximum productivity is referred to as “process capacity”. Many OM textbooks use a “bottleneck formula” to capture process capacity, and from there, derive a variety of managerial insights; in particular, a key insight is that, to improve process capacity, one simply needs to invest on increasing the processing speed of the bottlenecks. Recent research finds that this widely used formula fails to characterize process capacity in general, and moreover, can be significantly inaccurate. In particular, this finding is significantly pronounced in processes that involve human beings, like a hospital, where the collaboration and multitasking of resources are prevalent. Motivated by this finding, we expect our proposed study to provide resolutions to identify the correct “bottlenecks”, which will generate correct managerial insights, and in particular, provide the correct guidance on improving process capacity. Given the fundamental importance of process capacity in OM, we expect our proposed research to make significant contributions. 許多機構——如制造系統或醫院——追求產率。對於制造系統，如汽車生產線，高產率等價於更多的成品和更多利潤。對於醫院，高產率等價於救治更多的病人和挽救更多生命。基於對世界以及香港的觀察，我們將利用線性/整數規劃和組合分析來研究如何從運籌角度有效提高產率。在運籌管理文獻中，機構可用系統來建模，而最大產率被稱為“系統容量”。許多運籌管理教科書用“瓶頸公式”來計算系統容量，並由此推導出許多商業洞察。比如以下核心洞察：我們需要通過提高瓶頸工作速度來提高系統容量。近來研究發現，“瓶頸公式”不適用於所有系統，並且對於壹些系統十分不精確。這項研究的發現在有人參與的系統中尤為突出，因為這些系統往往需要不同人力之間的相互協作和多任務處理。由此，本項目將至力於研究如何發現正確的“瓶頸”，並由此推導出正確的圍繞“瓶頸”的商業洞察；其中特別包括提高系統容量的準則。基於系統容量在運籌管理中的根本重要性，我們預期本項目將產生重要貢獻。

24502818.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24502818.value: 國際貿易出入口商關係的形成

24502818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502818.value: Exporter-importer relationships are the foundation of international trade. While trade relationships across countries at the aggregate level are well-studied, relatively little is known about cross-border trade relationships at the micro-level. In particular, who are the importing firms that exporters sell to, and how do exporters find and locate these importers? In this project, we study the formation of exporter-importer relationships theoretically and empirically, utilizing a novel two-sided firm trade transactions dataset of Korean exporters and US importers. We present an international trade model with search, learning, export spillovers, and two-sided heterogeneity. Heterogeneous producers belong to groups and operate in different industries. A group may be a geographic city, or in the case of Korea, it may be defined by sharing an ownership structure known as a "chaebol" or business group. To sell in the foreign market, producers must match with heterogeneous importers at different locations. This requires a fixed cost, which depends on the importer's spatial relationship and value chain position relative to other importers previously sold to, either by the firm or other firms within the group. This cost falls as firms learn from exporting, or through within-group export spillovers. The model predicts firms within groups to cluster import partners by geography and industry. However, this effect is weaker for productive exporters. Furthermore, there is feedback from the relationships between import partners to producers' export activity. Thus, the model also predicts that the spatial dispersion and sectoral concentration of import partners should promote greater learning for firms within groups and encourage more exports. To test the empirical implications of the model, we construct a novel transaction-level dataset from 2005 to 2014 with US importers and Korean exporters by matching the US Customs' Longitudinal Firm Trade Transactions Database (LFTTD) with Korean firm-level data. We obtain the identities of exporters and importers and their firm characteristics, including measures of productivity, location, industry, and business group affiliation in the case of Korean firms. We propose different regressions and estimation strategies to provide empirical support for our theoretical predictions. In particular, we exploit the US-Korea Free Trade Agreement in 2012, which provides exogenous variation in the decline of tariffs, and test the model prediction that the learning and spillover effects are more pronounced for a greater fall in tariffs. Our project will contribute to a greater understanding on exporter-importer relationships, firm heterogeneity, and the networks of international trade. 出口商和進口商的關係是國際貿易的基礎。雖然學者已在宏觀的角度上對於國家與國家之間的貿易關係作出詳細研究，可是相比之下，我們從微觀的層面所了解的確是甚少。例如，出口商賣向了哪些進口商？出口商是如何尋找並定位這些進口商？在這個研究項目裡，我們利用韓國出口商和美國進口商的雙邊貿易交易數據集，從理論和實證兩方面研究出口商和進口商關係的形成。 我們提出一個具有搜索，知識轉移，溢出效應和雙邊異質性的國際貿易模型。在此模型，異質廠商是附屬於組織，並且在不同的工業中運作。組織可以是一個地理城市，或者以韓國為例，它可以通過共享被稱為“財閥”或企業集團的所有權結構來定義。要在國外市場上銷售，廠商必須在不同地點和異質進口商匹配。在這過程中，出口商需付固定成本。這固定成本取決於此進口商相對於該出口商或組織內廠商先前出售的其他進口商的空間關係和價值鏈地位。這種成本隨著廠商從出口中學習或通過組織內溢出效應而下降。該模型預測組織中的廠商通過地理和產業聚集進口合作夥伴。然而，對生產效率較強的出口商來說，這種影響較弱。此外，進口商之間的關係對於廠商的出口行為會有反饋。因此，該模型亦預測進口商的地理擴散和工業集中應促進組織內的廠商對國外市場的認識及鼓勵更多出口。 為測試模型的實證意涵，我們通過把美國海關的Longitudinal Firm Trade Transactions Database（LFTTD）與韓國的廠商數據連接，建立了一個包括2005至2014年美國進口商與韓國出口商交易的微觀數據庫。我們獲得出入口商的身份及其企業特徵，包括其生產力，地點，行業和韓國財閥中的隸屬關係。我們用回歸分析為理論提供經驗證據。特别是，我們利用提供了關稅下降外生變化的2012年美韓自由貿易協定，來測試模型對知識轉移和溢出效應在關稅更大下跌時會更為顯著的預測。我們的研究將更深入了解出入口商的關係，廠商異質性，和國際貿易網絡而作出貢獻。

24505918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24505918.value: Supply uncertainty has become an increasingly more pressing concern of many multi-national firms with global supply networks. Dual sourcing or multiple sourcing, as a natural operational hedging strategy to mitigate supply risks by diversifying supply sources, has become a common practice in supply chain management. There are many realistic situations where the firm can order from multiple suppliers, and the risks of these suppliers are dependent. Motivated by the above observations, we propose a project studying a dual sourcing inventory problem with dependent random capacities. In addition, we consider a quite general cost structure – the two-part fee structure. This cost structure allows the supply uncertainties to be shared between the supplier and the firm who places the order. We intend to provide a comprehensive understanding of this complex dual sourcing inventory systems. When analyzing our proposed model, we plan to develop an innovative method to deal with a technical challenge of minimizing a non-convex optimization problem. Our method converts the original non-convex minimization problem to an equivalent convex one while preserving some desirable structure properties, which are useful for analyzing optimal decision policies and conducting comparative statics. Our method also provides opportunities for conducting numerical studies to further generate managerial insights. In addition, we propose to design a decision rule based algorithm to compute optimal decision policies more efficiently. 對於擁有全球供應網絡的許多跨國公司來說，供應不確定性已成為一個越來越緊迫的問題。雙重採購或多重採購作為通過多樣化供應來降低供應風險的運營對沖策略，已成為供應鏈管理中的常見做法。在許多現實情況中，公司可以從多個供應商訂購，而這些供應商的風險通常具有相關性。在上述觀察的啟發下，我們將研究一個在供應不確定性影響下的雙重採購問題。 此外，我們還考慮一種相當普遍的成本結構 - 雙段成本結構。這種成本結構允許供應商和下游公司之間共同承擔供應不確定性。在分析我們的模型時，我們研發了一種創新方法來應對最小化非凸優化問題的技術挑戰。我們的方法能將問題中出現的非凸最小化問題轉換為凸優化問題，同時保留了一些理想的結構屬性，以幫助分析最優決策策略。此外，我們將設計一種基於決策規則的算法，以更有效地計算最優決策策略。

24505918.value: All objectives have been successfully achieved. For the dual sourcing inventory model, we can convert the originally nonconvex optimization problem to an equivalent convex one using a carefully developed transforming technique. Building upon this transformation, we are able to analyze the structural properties of the proposed model. We can show that the property of submodularity and L natural convexity can be preserved in this model. Monotonic properties of the decisions can be established. In terms of computational studies, we have implemented both the linear decision rule approach and LP-ADP approach. Therefore, the problem can be solved efficiently based on our transformation technique. As mentioned in the midterm report, based on the discussions with my research collaborators and the comments from review team, we also consider the inventory model from the data-driven perspective. In particular, we assume that the demand information is not known a priori and must be learned on the fly. We have designed an online learning algorithm that can achieve fast convergence rate balancing the famous exploration versus exploitation trade-off.

24505918.label: Major findings and research outcome
24505918.value: The main research outcome is a paper accepted by the journal Production and Operations Management. The paper has appeared online with the link http://doi.org/10.1111/poms.13693. A complete PDF version of the paper is attached in Part C. We consider a periodic-review multi-product inventory system where customers’ purchasing decisions are affected by the product availabilities. Demands need to be learned on the fly, through the partial and censored feedback of customers. For this learning problem, if one ignores the inventory dynamic and treats it as a Multi-Armed Bandit problem and directly applies some existing algorithms, e.g., the Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) algorithm, the convergence can be extremely slow due to the high-dimensionality of the policy space. We propose a UCB-based learning framework that utilizes the sales information based on two improvement ideas. We illustrate how these two ideas can be incorporated by considering two specific systems: 1) multi-product inventory system with stock-out substitutions, 2) multi-product inventory assortment problem for urban warehouses. We develop improved UCB algorithms for both systems, using the two improvements. For both systems, the algorithm can achieve a tight worst-case convergence rate (up to a logarithmic term) on the planning horizon. Extensive numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the efficiency of the improved UCB algorithms for the two systems. In the experiments, when there are more than 1000 candidate policies to choose from, the algorithms can achieve around 15% average expected regret within 50 periods, and continues to steadily improve as time increases.

24505918.value: We believe that more data-driven algorithms can be designed and analyzed for the proposed inventory model.

24505918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24505918.value: It is a significant and challenging task for companies to manage their inventory well, especially with multiple suppliers or products. Analyzing such a complicated inventory system often requires innovation and theoretical advancements in optimization. We have developed a general and valuable method for analyzing an inventory system with multiple suppliers or products. Moreover, facing the opportunity of big data nowadays, we further study how to develop a data-driven learning algorithm to help companies do intelligent inventory management.
