24506318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24506318.value: In mergers and acquisitions (M&A) transactions, managers of target firms often provide their forecasts of future financial performance to the acquirers and financial advisors for valuation purposes. Many target firms also subsequently include these management forecasts in M&A proxy statements for shareholder approval. While managers often claim that the projections are their “best estimate” and are prepared using “reasonable” assumptions in the proxy statements, one recent court ruling in the PetSmart case (2017) used the phrase “at best, fanciful” to describe the management projections disclosed in the M&A proxy statement of the firm involved. Although the ruling only concerns one case in particular, this leads to the question of whether management forecasts disclosed in M&A proxy statements really represent truthful projections by managers and how pervasive is the provision and usage of “fanciful” projections in M&As. While prior literature has extensively examined management guidance issued in the ordinary course of business, none of the studies have examined the management forecasts included in the proxy statements during M&A transactions. There are, however, possibly notable differences between these two types of management forecasts. In M&A situations, management forecasts provided by a target firm are potentially less verifiable by outsiders post-merger as the target firm becomes a part of merged consolidated entity and is no longer required to disclose separate financials. While management guidance during the ordinary course of business can be considered as a repeated reputation game, the provision of management forecasts by target firms in an M&A situation may resemble a one-shot game, with likely fewer reputational concerns that constrain opportunistic behaviors. The lack of ex-post verifiability and the potentially one-shot nature of the game may provide managers more room for strategic manipulation (Stocken, 2000), possibly translating into different properties and economic effect for the forecasts contained in M&A proxy statements. This proposed study will test the above predictions and ultimately aims at uncovering a “black box” in the literature through a systematic large-sample investigation into the determinants, characteristic and consequences of management forecasts disclosed in M&A proxy statements. The study will also shed some light on how these forecasts compare to those issued during regular guidance. The study also hopes to further our understanding of the information exchange process during M&A transactions, with the potential to help answer, from an informational perspective, an unsettled question in the M&A literature as to why acquirers tend to underperform after M&A transactions. 在併購（M＆A）交易中，目標公司的經理通常會向收購方和財務顧問提供其對未來財務業績的預測，以助其進行估值。許多目標公司隨後也將這些管理層財務預測納入併購文件中，以供股東投票批准時作參考。雖然管理人員經常聲稱預測是他們的“最佳估計”，並且作出使用了“合理”假設準備的聲明，但PetSmart案（2017年）最近的一項判決中法院使用了“充其量，異想天開”這一字眼來描述管理層在該公司併購文件中披露的預測。 儘管該裁決僅涉及一個案例，但這引申出一個問題，即併購文件中披露的管理層財務預測是否真的代表了管理層的對未來業務的真實預測? 同時管理層在併購中提供和使用“異想天開”的預測有是一個有多普遍的現象? 雖然先前的文獻已經廣泛研究了公司在日常業務過程中正式發佈的管理層財務預測，但是沒有一項研究探討過包含在冗長併購文件中的管理層財務預測。然而，這兩種管理層預測之間或存在顯著的差異。 在併購情況下，目標公司會在合併成功後將成為合併實體的一部分，不再需要披露單獨的財務。因此, 目標公司提供的管理預測可能不太容易由合併後的外部人員驗證。雖然在日常業務過程中的管理層預測可以被視為不斷重複並影響聲譽的博弈遊戲，但是目標公司在併購情況下提供的管理預測可能類似於一次性博弈遊戲，因對聲譽有較小的潛在影響而較難限制管理層的機會主義行為。缺乏事後可驗證性和博弈遊戲的一次性性質可能為管理層提供更多的戰略操縱空間，為併購文件中披露的預測帶來不同屬性和經濟效應。 這項擬議的研究將測試上述預測，並旨在通過進行系統性的大樣本的研究去探討披露在併購文件中管理層財務預測的前因，特徵和後果，打開文獻中相關的“黑匣子”. 該研究還將闡明這些併購文件中的管理層財務預測與常規管理層財務預測有何相似或不同的性質。該研究同時希望進一步了解併購交易中的信息交換過程，並從信息的角度去探討併購文獻中一個未解決的問題，即收購者在併購交易後往往表現不佳的原因。

24506318.label: Realisation of objectives
24506318.value: Objective 1: The PI has collected 4,393 DEFM14A filings related to shareholder approvals in statutory merger transactions by US-listed firms from 1996 to 2015. After eliminating filings that cannot be matched to GVKEYs in Compustat and transactions in which the filer is not the target firm, the PI has worked with RAs to hand-collect detailed management forecast information from a total of 3,376 proxy filings. Objective 2: The PI has estimated linear probability models to examine the determinants on the inclusion of management forecasts in M&A proxy statements. Major independent variables of interests include proxies for recent litigation rates, the issuance of forecasts in the ordinary course, whether the acquirer and target belong to related industries, as well as other transaction and target characteristics. To proxy for ex-ante shareholder litigation risks that vary over time, the PI uses two proxies: Litigation Rate(CAB), the M&A shareholder litigation rates in the prior year among the 25 largest M&A transactions using the available data from Cheffins et al. (2012), and Litigation Rate(CFST), the M&A shareholder litigation rates in the prior year among deals with over $100 million value using the available data from Cain et al. (2018). The results find a significantly positive β1, consistent with the litigation cost hypothesis. To capture managerial discretionary disclosure incentives, Regular Guidance is an indicator for whether the target provides forecasts in the ordinary course. The results find a significantly positive β2, consistent with the selective disclosure hypothesis. The study also uses an indicator Related Industry to capture whether the target and acquirer belong to the same two-digit SIC industry. Acquirers from non-related industries are likely less familiar with the target and may have heightened information demand for the target’s forward-looking information. The results find a significantly negative β3, consistent with the information demand hypothesis. To further investigate the impact of litigation concerns on the disclosure decision, the PI also employs two difference-in-difference specifications to examine whether the disclosure propensity of firms incorporated in DE is more sensitive to recent DE court interpretations. The first specification utilizes two major DE court cases that rule in favor of disclosures from In re Netsmart Technologies, Inc. Shareholders Litigation (2007) and Maric v. Plato (2010). The second specification utilizes two major DE courts cases that regard the disclosure as non-obligatory from Skeen v. Jo-Ann Stores (1999, 2000) and Dent v. Ramtron (2012, 2014). The sample includes three years before and three years after the first ruling dates. The results suggest the disclosure propensity is sensitive to recent relevant court interpretations. Objective 3: The PI has examined several characteristics of these projections, including the number of years being projected, the number of major financial items under projection, and the prevalence of each major financial item, including revenue, EBITDA, net income, capital expenditure, being projected in proxy statements. The results show that the average projection horizon in M&A proxy statements is five years. The projection contains four major financial items on average, with revenue (77%), EBITDA (62%), and net income (48%) as the top three items. The PI has also attempted to assess both the “bias” and “accuracy” of these projections. However, one big challenge is that the actual realization of financial numbers is often not publicly available once the target firm is merged in the context of M&A transactions. This challenge has also been echoed by a discussant at a conference. To mitigate this issue, the PI has utilized several benchmarking samples for evaluation. First, for a subsample of firms with analyst following, the PI compares the projections with the most recent sell-side analyst forecast consensus on the target before the proxy filing date as a proxy for market expectation. Second, for a small subsample of targets that continue to disclose their financial reports after deal consummation, the study compares the projections with their actual realization. Third, for a subsample of targets that issue forecasts in the ordinary course, the study compares the one-year projections with regular forecasts. Additionally, the PI has also computed the growth rates in each major financial item for further benchmarking comparisons. Specifically, the study compares the target’s three-year projected growth rates with the average realized industry growth rates at the four-digit SIC level as an industry performance benchmark as well as with the target’s own historical three-year growth rates before the transaction as a historical performance benchmark. A quick summary of the findings is that the projections tend to be more “optimistic” against the latest analyst forecast consensus prior to filings. The projected growth rates are also higher than each target’s average historical growth rates and the average realized industry growth rates. Such “optimism” increases with the projected horizon and is mostly attributable to expense estimation. One important caveat is that the PI cannot observe true realization of the financial projections after the entities are merged. The difference or “optimism” may not necessarily be a real bias. It is possible that some differences contain useful managerial insights on the target’s future prospects. Objective 4: The PI has attempted to assess the consequences of these management projections by examining the association with subsequent outcomes or actions taken by various stakeholders. The dependent variables represent various potential consequences to stakeholders, such as transaction pricing, shareholder voting outcomes, deal completion status, and the acquirer’s post-merger performance (e.g., long-run returns and goodwill impairments). The primary independent variables of interest are whether the target provides projections in the proxy statements and the average difference between management projections and consensus analyst forecasts. Additionally, the PI has also looked into sell-side analysts’ revisions of target financial estimates after the release of M&A proxy statements and examined whether the revisions are associated with the “optimisms” of management forecasts against analyst forecasts. A quick summary of the findings is that the actions taken by different stakeholders are generally consistent with the presence of some useful signals from management projections over consensus analyst forecasts. The “optimism” of management forecasts against consensus analyst forecasts is also not systematically associated with worse post-merger acquirer performance. A major pushback that the PI received after submitting to a journal is that management projections are among the many data points that targets provide in the proxy filings and it is difficult to attribute any consequences to management projections only. The PI acknowledges this concern as it is impossible to control for all other data points provided in proxy filings due to their non-uniform disclosure practices. The PI has decided to pivot away from “consequences”. Instead, the PI intends to use these analyses to shed light on the informativeness of the management projections to different stakeholders. This can in turn reflect whether different stakeholders regard the management projections as “credible”. Objective 5: The PI has incorporated an indicator for the provision of management forecasts issued during the ordinary course as an independent variable in various analyses and conducted additional subsampling analyses based on this indicator. The results show that the provision of regular guidance is associated with increased propensity to provide EBITDA and CAPEX projections among those that provide management projections. The provision of regular guidance is associated with reduced acquisition premium. There are no other significant associations found.

24506318.label: Major findings and research outcome
24506318.value: The PI finds that the percentage of targets’ M&A proxy filings disclosing management projections is increasing over time, from fewer than 15% before 2000 to over 75% after 2010. The trend coincides with the increasing M&A litigation rates. Findings from determinant analyses suggest that mitigating litigation risk is an important consideration in the board’s disclosure decision in M&A proxy filings. Targets are more likely provide management projections if they issue management forecasts in the ordinary course or if the acquirers are not from a related industry. Unlike management forecasts in the ordinary course, the average projection horizon in M&A proxy filings spans five years. Revenue (77%), EBITDA (62%), and net income (48%) are the top projected items. The projections tend to be more “optimistic” compared to the analyst forecast consensus prior to filings. Projected revenue, EBITDA, and net income figures are higher than the consensus by an average of 4.83%, 11.42%, and 13.84%, respectively. The “optimism” against consensus analyst forecasts increases by 2.5% per year with the projected horizon. The level of “optimism” is also higher if the acquirer is publicly listed, but lower if the acquirer is from a related industry. Target shareholders are more likely to vote in favor of the transactions if the projections are disclosed. The average difference of projections against consensus analyst forecasts also displays a negative association with shareholder support for the transaction, suggesting that target shareholders find the projections informative as they are less likely to approve the deal if projections are optimistic. Sell-side analysts also revise their estimates of target financials after the release of M&A proxy statements towards the figures in management projections. The results suggest that these stakeholders appear to find the management projections containing some useful signals. One important caveat is that the findings do not imply that these stakeholders find the projections fully credible. The analyses also fail to find significant evidence supporting the presence of a positive association between the “optimism” against consensus analyst forecasts and subsequent acquirer goodwill impairments or a negative association between the “optimism” against consensus analyst forecasts and post-announcement acquirer abnormal stock returns. The “optimism” in projections does not appear to have led to systematic overpayment by acquirers who may have anticipated and unwound the strategic “bias” in their transaction pricing. While there is no strong evidence of grossly inflated projections on average, large heterogeneity does exist among target firms.

24506318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24506318.value: The project offers unique opportunities for outsiders to catch a glimpse of managers’ long-term views on the companies. Based on current findings, there is a large gap between managerial financial projections and analyst forecasts if we take the projections at their face value. Managers are more “optimistic” relative to analysts’ expectations and such “optimism” becomes larger as the horizon increases. This raises the question whether the diverging beliefs between target managers and market (as reflected in analyst forecasts) are potential drivers of M&A transactions. The PI has analyzed the evolution of analyst expectations across the entire transaction cycle, beyond just the proxy statements in the proposed project and is preparing manuscripts to document the evidence regarding this phenomenon and its implications to the M&A literature. Separately, the PI is preparing another manuscript to document the rest of findings in this project to focus on the disclosure decision by target boards in M&A proxy statements and the implications from this disclosure decision.

24506318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24506318.value: This project investigates the determinants and characteristics of managerial projections disclosed in M&A targets’ proxy statements to shareholders for transaction approvals. The disclosures typically pertain to projections shared by target managers to its board or deal advisors. The results show that such a disclosure is increasingly common over time, with the propensity positively associated with M&A litigation rates and court interpretations. Unlike management forecasts issued in the ordinary course, these projections often span five years and offer unique opportunities for outsiders to catch a glimpse of managers’ long-term views on the companies. The results show that these managerial projections tend to be more “optimistic” relative to consensus analyst forecasts on average. The “optimism” increases with the projected horizon and is mostly attributable to expense estimation. Voting decisions by target shareholders and analyst forecast revisions after the proxy statements are consistent with the projections containing some informative signals over prevailing consensus analyst forecasts. While “fanciful” projections do exist anecdotally, the project fails to find strong systematic evidence suggesting that more “optimistic” projections are associated with worse acquirer post-merger performance. Overall, the project shed lights on the potential role of M&As in helping target firms to communicate their long-term value to outsiders.

24506518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24506518.value: Mandatory and voluntary disclosures are two primary channels through which firms communicate their private information to the market. Because the two types of disclosures do not exist in isolation, it is important to understand the relation between them. A new mandatory disclosure regulation can have potential impact on either firms’ voluntary disclosure quantity, quality, or both, but all existing studies evaluate the quantity changes of voluntary disclosures in response to mandatory disclosure regulations. Little is known about how a mandatory disclosure requirement affects firms’ quality of voluntary disclosure. In this proposal, I will use the setting of the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) to examine the impact of mandatory disclosure regulation on the quality of voluntary innovation disclosure. The AIPA is a federal law enacted in 1999 that requires all patent applications to be published on the website of the USPTO 18 months after the initial application date, which is an exogenous shock to a firm’s mandatory disclosure environment. Because the mandatory publication of a patent application presents patent information in a standard manner, it can be used as a benchmark for evaluating the quality, defined as the richness of content, of corresponding voluntary disclosures about the same patent. I propose to use a novel patent dataset, PATSTAT, to link each patent application with all its corresponding voluntary innovation disclosures released before the approval (or publication) date. PATSTAT is preferred over the most commonly used patent database NBER because NBER records application years only. The direct match will allow me to conduct analyses at both the application and firm levels. I will first use the new data to confirm the results in Wang (2017) which uses NBER data to examine the impact of the AIPA on R&D disclosure quantity. Second, I will examine the change in richness of content of firms’ voluntary innovation disclosures from the pre- to the post-AIPA period using a cost-benefit framework. Third, I will investigate cross-sectional variations in this effect by partitioning firms based on their R&D intensity, external financing need, product substitutability, and earnings performance. This study is the first, to my knowledge, to examine the impact of mandatory disclosure regulation on the quality of narrative voluntary disclosure. It is also one of the few voluntary disclosure studies that investigate an information item other than management earnings forecasts. The usage of the most comprehensive patent database PATSTAT may inspire more future research on innovations. 強制性和自願性披露是企業將私有信息傳播到市場的兩個主要渠道。由於這兩種披露並不是孤立存在的，因此理解兩者之間的關係十分重要。新的強制性披露規定可能會對公司的自願性披露數量和質量產生潛在影響，但現有研究通常只關注強制性披露規定對自願性披露的數量的改變。關於強制性披露規定如果影響公司的自願性披露質量，我們知之甚少。 在本提案中，我將使用美國發明人保護法（AIPA）作為研究設定，從而檢驗強制性信息披露規定對自願性創新研發披露質量的影響。AIPA是美國1999年頒布的聯邦法律，要求所有專利申請者在首次申請日后的18個月時將申請信息公佈在USPTO網站上。這項法律被視作對公司強制性披露環境的外部衝擊。由於專利申請的強制性披露需要遵循一定的披露標準，因此可以用作評估相同專利的自願性披露質量的基準。自願性披露質量是以披露信息內容的豐富性為定義。 我建議使用新的專利數據庫PATSTAT，從而將每個專利申請與批准（或公佈）日期之前發佈的所有相應自願性披露匹配起來。PATSTAT優於目前常用的專利數據庫NBER，因為NBER僅記錄申請年份，而利用PATSTAT的直接匹配可以讓我用專利申請及公司進行分別研究分析。我將首先使用PATSTAT的數據驗證王（2017）使用NBER數據檢驗AIPA對研發披露數量影響的結果。其次，我將使用成本效益框架來檢驗起眼自願性創新研究披露呢誒榮的豐富程度在AIPA前期和後期的改變。最後，我將根據公司的研發強度，外部融資需求，產品替代性，及盈利表現，劃分公司種類從而研究這種影響的横截面变化。 在現有文獻的基礎上，本提案將首次研究強制性披露規定對自願性披露質量的影響。它也是為數不多的使用除管理收益預測以外的信息項目的自願性披露研究之一。使用最完整的專利數據庫PATSTAT也可能會促進未來更多對創新研發披露的研究。

24506518.label: Realisation of objectives
24506518.value: Objective 1: The AIPA is an U.S. federal law implemented on November 29, 2000. It requires all U.S. patent applications to be published 18 months after the initial application date. The “18-month rule” intended to not only broaden the scope of information by publishing pre-grant patent information, but also expedite patent information flow to the U.S. market. However, not all firms with U.S. patent applications are affected by the AIPA in the same manner. First, to avoid publication, an applicant may file a “non-publication request.” Such a request must certify that the accompanying application has not sought and will not seek patent protection from any foreign jurisdiction. Second, because most foreign jurisdictions implemented an 18-month mandatory publication rule long before the AIPA in the U.S., the impact of the AIPA may differ depending on whether a patent application is first filed in the U.S. or overseas. Thus, the AIPA changes the disclosure environment of firms filing for patent applications in the U.S. but the impact may be differential across different filing scenarios, which provides a rich setting for empirical testing. I obtain a sample of 20,536 firm-years during 1997-2004 with at least one innovation-related press release or patent application in the current year, or non-zero innovation expenses in the previous three years, to ensure that the firms invest in innovation activities. Firm only with patent applications filed domestically are already excluded from this sample. I use the patent data primarily from the EPO Worldwide Patent Statistical database (PATSTAT), cross-check with patent data from NBER and Google Patents. My measures of a firm’s mandatory patent disclosure are based on the existence and number of patent applications filed during each firm-year. To measure the quality of voluntary innovation disclosure, I first expand Merkley’s (2014) dictionary of common innovation keywords and phrases by using the neural-network-based word embedding. I then use this new dictionary to identify all innovation-related press releases. Utilizing the 18-month rule, I construct the measures of a firm’s voluntary innovation disclosure by counting the total number of innovation-related press releases issued during the 18-month filing-to-publication period of each patent application filed in the fiscal year, and the total number of words in these press releases. For firm-years with no patent applications, the voluntary innovation disclosure measures are constructed using the 18-month period starting from the beginning of the fiscal year. To address the concern that firms with certain characteristics are more likely to file patent applications and have different incentives in making voluntary innovation disclosure, I also construct a propensity-score-matched sample of 10,289 firm-years, by pairing firms with patent applications (treatment group) with firms without patent applications (control group). I employ a difference-in-differences (DiD) design around the implementation of the AIPA to investigate the average effect of the AIPA on firms’ voluntary innovation disclosure. I find that firms with patent applications increase the quality of voluntary innovation disclosure during the filing-to-publication period after the AIPA. The effect is economically significant. Firms that apply for patents after the AIPA voluntarily provide 15.7 percent more innovation-related press releases and disclose 1,518 more words in these innovation-related press releases than firms that applied for patents before the AIPA. I also find that after the AIPA, firms with more patent applications are more likely to increase their voluntary innovation disclosures than firms with fewer patent applications. Beyer et al.’s (2010) call for archival researchers to investigate the relationship between mandatory and voluntary disclosures. My study complements prior studies by exploring a setting in which a major change in mandatory reporting may affect firms’ voluntary disclosure quality which predate the mandatory disclosure, and both disclosures convey disaggregated, non-financial information. Objective 2: I examine cross-sectional variations in the effect of the AIPA on the quality of voluntary innovation disclosure by evaluating which types of firms are more (less) likely to experience the decrease (increase) in costs (benefits) of voluntarily disclosing innovation information in the post-AIPA period. Before the AIPA, innovation-intensive firms incurred greater proprietary costs of disclosure than other firms because the former risked losing their patents to “submarine patent” applicants. As the AIPA eliminates the practice of “submarine patents,” I predict that after the AIPA, innovation-intensive firms are more likely to experience a decrease in proprietary costs and thus are more likely to voluntarily disclose their innovation activities than firms with low innovation intensity. In addition, firms with high product substitutability are less likely to make early innovation disclosures before the publication of patent applications because higher product substitutability means a lower degree of competitive advantage in the product market and therefore more intense product competition. These firms do not have technological advantages to deter competition, so I predict that they are less likely to benefit from and make early high-quality disclosure of innovation activities than firms with low product substitutability. The empirical results support these predictions. Objective 3: I use the PATSTAT data to investigate the underlying mechanisms driving the relation between mandatory and voluntary disclosures. On the one hand, for a firm traditionally with innovation investments, investors have their prior beliefs about the progress and outcomes of the firm’s innovation activities. In the post-AIPA regime, if the anticipation of earlier patent publications reduces uncertainty about such progress and outcomes, investors would exert less pressure on the firm to provide related information via voluntary innovation disclosures before the actual publications of patent information (i.e., information uncertainty mechanism). On the other hand, when a firm applies for a patent without the “non-publication request,” the proprietary cost of disclosing detailed patent information becomes unavoidable, unconditional on whether the patent is ultimately granted or not. The anticipated patent publication thus reduces the incremental proprietary cost of voluntarily disclosing related innovation information, resulting in a lower disclosure threshold in the equilibrium (i.e., proprietary cost mechanism). Investors may not be aware of the existence of a patent application until its publication, but when investors observe the publication, they can easily reverse-engineer the filing date from which managers certainly have the private information of the patent. Investors would rationally interpret managers’ decision of not voluntarily disclosing such information earlier less favorably. To separately examine the two countervailing mechanisms, I employ a difference-in-difference-in-differences (DiDiD) design. The results show the complementary relationship between the mandatory disclosure of pre-patent information and voluntary innovation disclosure during the filing-to-publication period after the AIPA is mainly driven by the reduced proprietary cost of voluntary innovation disclosure. This finding suggests that investors’ priors may not substantially change when they are uncertain about the existence of innovation investments ex ante. Managers, in anticipation of the mandatory disclosure of patent information, may use the voluntary disclosure to explain the upcoming mandatory disclosure when both disclosures convey disaggregated, proprietary information. Objective 4: Although my study focuses on one particular patent law change and disclosure of only innovation activities, I expect my results to be informative to accounting standard setters. The U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) has long considered a project on the disclosure of intangible assets (FASB 2004). We have limited understanding about how mandated reporting of certain intangible assets affects the voluntary disclosure of related information. My results are relevant to the FASB because patents are an important intangible asset that is not recognized in firms’ financial statements.

24506518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24506518.value: I first employ a difference-in-differences (DiD) design around the implementation of the AIPA to investigate the average effect of the AIPA on firms’ voluntary innovation disclosure. I find that firms with patent applications increase the quality of voluntary innovation disclosure during the filing-to-publication period after the AIPA. The effect is economically significant. Firms that apply for patents after the AIPA voluntarily provide 15.7 percent more innovation-related press releases and disclose 1,518 more words in these innovation-related press releases than firms that applied for patents before the AIPA. I also find that after the AIPA, firms with more patent applications are more likely to increase their voluntary innovation disclosures than firms with fewer patent applications. Next, I separately examine the two countervailing mechanisms using a difference-in-difference-in-differences (DiDiD) design. The results show the complementary relationship between the mandatory disclosure of pre-patent information and voluntary innovation disclosure during the filing-to-publication period after the AIPA is mainly driven by the reduced proprietary cost of voluntary innovation disclosure. This finding suggests that investors’ priors may not substantially change when they are uncertain about the existence of innovation investments ex ante. Managers, in anticipation of the mandatory disclosure of patent information, may use the voluntary disclosure to explain the upcoming mandatory disclosure when both disclosures convey disaggregated, proprietary information. Lastly, I conduct several additional tests to better understand the nature and timing of the two disclosures. I find that although firms may voluntarily choose pre-grant publications for their patent applications with no foreign protection, firms with patent applications published at the 18-month deadline are the main driver of the positive relationship between the mandatory patent disclosure and the voluntary innovation disclosure after the AIPA. The complementarity is stronger when the voluntary innovation-related press releases convey information directly related to at least one patent of the firm. The complementarity barely exists when the mandatory pre-grant disclosure predates the voluntary innovation disclosure. These results suggest that firms use voluntary patent-related press releases to explain the highly technical and complex information contained in the patent applications in an easy-to-understand manner before their publications, not afterwards.

24506518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24506518.value: My study focuses on one particular patent law change and disclosure of only innovation activities, but I expect my results to be informative to standard setters who are evaluating the costs and benefits of mandating reporting of certain intangible assets and to generalize to disclosures of other proprietary information. For future research, it is also interesting to investigate the broader impact of a series of actions of the USPTO to reform the patent system. For example, following the AIPA, the USPTO released a new and more comprehensive set of tools available to enable the public to view the status and history of both pending applications and issued patents. The Image File Wrapper (IFW) and the Patent Application Information Retrieval (PAIR) systems were introduced. IFW is the paperless system for handling the various papers associated with the application process for a patent; the collection of papers is referred to as the ?file wrapper.? Public PAIR is a system for viewing the status and history of a U.S. patent application or issued patent over the Internet. Examining the joint impact of the law change and the technology advancement would provide a more comprehensive understanding of the information dissemination function and disclosure environment.

24506518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24506518.value: Managers must balance the capital-market benefits with the proprietary costs of voluntary disclosure. A new mandatory disclosure requirement is likely to change this balance. In this study, I use the American Inventors Protection Act of 1999, which requires the public disclosure of firms? patent applications, to examine the impact of mandatory disclosure regulation on firms? voluntary disclosure quality. This project makes significant contributes to the literature. First, it complements prior studies by exploring a setting in which a major change in mandatory reporting affects voluntary disclosures that predate the mandatory disclosure. Second, this is the first study to examine such a relationship with a focus on narrative disclosures. Narrative disclosures are important but difficult to collect and quantify. I overcome the barrier by using advanced computational techniques to provide a large-sample study. The value of this study is to inform standard setters. The U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) has long considered a project on the disclosure of intangible assets. We have limited understanding about how mandated reporting of certain intangible assets affects the voluntary disclosure of related information. My results are relevant to the FASB because patents are an important intangible asset that is not recognized in firms? financial statements.

24601818.label: Realisation of objectives
24601818.value: Project Objective 1: To reassess the Jesuits’ accommodation policy In “Typological Figuration of Mystical Elements in Jesuit Figurists’ Re-interpretation of Chinese Classics,” the P.I. re-assessed the Jesuit Firgurists’ accommodation policy by discussing how they translated mystic creatures in Chinese classics, such as dragon, qilin, dog, and Chinese mythological figures, in their typological exegesis as a tool of proselytization. The P.I. also argued that their accommodation policy not only started from their studies of the Four Books and the Five Classics, but also might incorporate their readings and interpretations of Chinese canons of mythology, geography and witchcrafts. The P.I. continued to reassess the Jesuits’ accommodation policy by examining the Figurists’ use of sheng ren 聖人 (sage) in the paper, in “Sheng Ren in the Figurists’ Reinterpretation of the Yijing.” The sheng ren enjoys a supreme status due to his virtues and flawlessness, as described in Confucianism and Daoism; Joachim Bouvet thus describes Jesus as a Confucian sage for the purpose of proselytization and Joseph Henri-Marie de Prémare and Jean François Foucquet also applied this term to their description of Jesus in their Chinese writings and in their dissemination of the Dao to Europe. Foucquet employed his expertise of astronomical knowledge and deciphered the images of hexagrams in the Yijing, using them to draw parallels between the fall of Adam and the hexagram Yi 頤and redefined Jesus as a sheng ren. On the other hand, Prémare analyzed the compositions of Chinese characters; it was he who used the two hexagrams Tai 泰and Pi 否to indicate the image of the sheng ren. In these rarely examined Chinese, Latin, and French manuscripts, Jesus, as a sheng ren, has plural and dialogic identities, which not only mitigated the differences between Christianity and the Yijing and reflected a new facet of the sheng ren to Chinese readers but also helped communicate the Dao to Europe. Project Objective 2: To establish the Dao lineage among Jesuit translators across time and space First, in “Typological Figuration of Mystical Elements in Jesuit Figurists’ Re-interpretation of Chinese Classics,” the P.I. laid the foundation of the lineage of Figurists adopting typological exegesis in their manuscript translations, from Bouvet to Prémare and Foucquet. The examination of their manuscript translations showcased that, in their translations into Latin, the Three Sovereigns三皇and Chinese mythological figures were depicted as biblical figures or figures from Greek and Roman mythology to parallel them with the biblical stories and narrow the cultural gap; and in the opposite linguistic direction, in their translations in Chinese manuscripts, the betrayal of Satan, the fall of Adam and Eve, and the emergence of Jesus were modeled as mystical creatures in Chinese classics, to lessen their foreignness. In the paper, “The Genesis of Dao Knowledge at the Beginning of Orientalism,” it aims to analyze the flow of knowledge of the Dao and the translation of Daoist terms over several generations of Jesuits in China, from the Jesuit Figurists to the French Sinologist Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. It also aims to determine the role of the Jesuit translators in the spread of Dao and Daoist terms in China and Europe. This may prove that their focus on the Dao was no mere historical contingency, but rather that their translations helped form the genesis of Dao knowledge and presented Chinese philosophy fairly on the world stage while their contemporaries shaped prejudiced outsider-interpretations out of the cultural attitudes of European imperialism in the 18th and 19th centuries. “The Journey of the Dao from China to Europe: The Figurist Jean-François Foucquet’s Struggle with and Interpretation of the Dao” adds crucial pieces to the puzzle, forming a fuller portrait of Foucquet’s controversial role in the interpretation and dissemination of the Dao. This micro-historical case study of Foucquet’s interpretation of the Dao shows how his navigating the strait between the Scylla and Charybdis of the emperor and the Holy See factored into his trajectory of interpreting the Dao; it also demonstrates that he cleaved to typological exegesis and Confucian-Christian-Dao synthesis in response to being challenged by his own brothers in the Catholic Church. The significance of this paper lies in that the early understanding of the Dao was manipulated as a tool for proselytization and as a bridge to link the East with the West, especially among the Figurists. Project Objective 3: To map out the routes of travel and circulation of these translation manuscripts from China to Europe “The Genesis of Dao Knowledge at the Beginning of Orientalism,” maps out the routes of travel and circulation of the translations of the Dao. Prémare’s manuscript Notitia Linguae Sinicae remained buried for many years in the Royal Library of France. Abel-Rémusat later discovered the manuscript, and it became the main source of his knowledge of Chinese. The attitude of Abel-Rémusat toward Figurism was not always positive; later, in his discovery of the Dao, he followed the approach of Prémare and interpreted Yi, Xi, and Wei from Chapter 14 of the Daodejing as the first three Hebrew letters of the Tetragrammaton. The P.I. especially examined the Figurists’ Chinese, Latin, and French manuscripts, before comparing them with Noëlas’ Latin translation and Abel-Rémusat’s French translation, in order to point out the common features in the genealogy of the Dao from Bouvet to Prémare to Noëlas, and also from Prémare to Abel-Rémusat. On the other hand, among the Figurists, Foucquet was the only one to return to Rome and try to convince the Pope by use of his manuscripts. In this paper, “The Journey of the Dao from China to Europe: The Figurist Jean-François Foucquet’s Struggle with and Interpretation of the Dao,” facing refutation from the Roman Catholic Church about the Rites Controversy, Foucquet stood fast by his interpretation of the Dao in his Chinese manuscripts that he submitted to the emperor and in Latin and French manuscripts he later submitted to the Pope. These rewritings and interpretations of the Dao are scattered across European archives and these are the precious cache of materials through which this paper investigates Foucquet’s very first attempts at translating the Dao into Latin and French. Project Objective 4: To explore the emotional conflicts of the Jesuit translators and their choices of frequent emotion/emotion-less terms related to Daoist classic translations In “The Making of Jesus in the Hands of the Jesuit Figurists--Religious Emotions Transformed in the Translations of the Yijing,” the P.I. examined the Jesuit Figurists’ intralingual translations, and there are many examples which establish Jesus Christ as a Confucian sage with original religious emotions toward God, transformed into the ethical virtues of xiao 孝 (filial piety) and zhong 忠 (loyalty; treating people right). In addition, the Figurist use of sheng ren was examined in “Sheng Ren in the Figurists’ Reinterpretation of the Yijing,” to distinguish how they explained the image of Jesus and prelapsarian Adam using the ethical emotions and virtues of a sheng ren 聖人 in their reinterpretation of the Yijing and the Dao. This also led to the European people aspiring for a more in-depth understanding and more discussion of the Yijing and the Dao.

24601818.label: Major findings and research outcome
24601818.value: 1. Establish The Dao lineage among Jesuit translators The Dao lineage, the flow of knowledge of the Dao and the translation of Daoist terms over several generations of Jesuits in China, from the Jesuit Figurists to the French Sinologist Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat is established. By marking these connections from Bouvet to Prémare and to Noëlas, and describing the lineage from Prémare to Abel-Rémusat, the P.I.’s research delineates the pedigree of the Dao translators. Prémare’s prolific production of Latin, French, and Chinese translation manuscripts and his interpretation of the Dao in association with the Triune God left a lasting impact on Noëlas’ Latin translation and Abel-Rémusat’s French translation of the Daodejing. Through in-depth textual comparison and analysis, this project has demonstrated that, influenced by Prémare, both Noëlas and Abel-Rémusat adopted the same approach of associating characters and sounds with the Triune God, while Noëlas also relied on the Chinese Dao scholars’ commentaries to Christianize the Dao. The Figurist mindset focused on the mysterious glossolalia found in some commentaries of the Daodejing and treated them as keys to secret messages encoded by the Triune God. Their intense passion for the Dao prompted their translations and rewritings, which were disseminated to Europe. 2. Identify Each Figurist’s Signature Approach This project identified each Figurist’s signature approach. “Sheng Ren in the Figurists’ Reinterpretation of the Yijing,” “The Making of Jesus in the Hands of the Jesuit Figurists--Religious Emotions Transformed in the Translations of the Yijing,” and “Typological Figuration of Mystical Elements in Jesuit Figurists’ Re-interpretation of Chinese Classics,” examined each Figurist’s interpretations of sheng ren, the use of religious emotions and each approach of typological exegesis in their re-interpretation of the Dao. Especially in the last two papers, the P.I. positioned Prémare’s and Foucquet’s significance in the Dao lineage of the Jesuit translators. 3. Link the Buried Treasure with the Dao Lineage The buried manuscripts in the European archives were examined to showcase these Figurists’ reinterpretation of the Dao. For example, the manuscript with the call number Chin. Ms. H. 20 is possibly the earliest extant Latin translation of the Daodejing and it helps the P.I. build the Dao lineage and the connection between Prémare and Noëlas. In addition, Manuscript no. Borg. Cin. 109 especially helps the P.I. investigate the sources and the commentaries Foucquet consulted and thus built his own perspective of the Dao.

24601818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24601818.value: The P.I. has investigated the genealogy of translating the Dao in the 16th and 17th centuries in this ECS project. Her next GRF project continues to examine the Daoist translators over three periods: It starts from two Jesuit Figurists’ translations and reinterpretations of the Dao, those of Joseph Henri Marie de Prémare and Jean François Foucquet in the 18th century, and proceeds to their impact on Abel-Remusat, Pauthier, and Julien in the heyday of French Sinology; then the network is extended to Chalmers, Legge, and Balfour with respect to their translations of Daoist texts at the high tide of British Sinology. Having different agendas, different webs of academic resources and patronage, as well as different commentaries and tutors, each translator developed a unique trajectory of the Dao. This will be the first analysis making connections among Daodejing translators from the 17th to 19th century. This will also be the first examination of the diverging roads of the Figurist-minded, academic, and secular translators in the 19th century by investigating those translators’ texts, contexts, and paratexts of the translated Daodejing. This project will establish the significant roles of Daodejing translators and translations in translation history, religious studies, as well as Sinological studies.

24601818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24601818.value: This project presents a panoramic view of these controversial Figurists and their reinterpretation of the Dao. Their hermetic learning manifested in their translation of Chinese classics, translations which formed the backdrop for the early Sinology in the 16th and 17th centuries; their meticulous forming of links between figures from Chinese legend and biblical figures in their Latin and French manuscripts aimed to reduce the gap between Christianity and Chinese philosophy as a proselytization tool. Influenced by Western esotericism and the prisca theologia, the Figurists indulged in locating mystic messages in the Chinese classics: Bouvet’s two protégés Prémare and Foucquet inherited his mystic Hermeticism, but each with his own theological and philosophical interpretation of the Dao. The Dao, Taiji, and other symbols were employed as pre-figurations of Jesus Christ or as aliases of Deus. Their reinterpretation of the Dao and Taiji were associated with Neopythagoreanism and Neoplatonism, which was also followed by Abel-Rémusat, who continued the earlier attitude of openness toward Chinese languages and philosophy. Based on the missionaries’ religious agenda or Abel-Rémusat’s Western world views, each Dao translator introduced the Dao, re-contextualized it and re-packaged it, and thus opened the door to understand the philosophical and religious landscape of China.

24604518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604518.value: Background: Sleep disturbance is highly comorbid with a range of psychological disorders, especially major depressive disorder (MDD). MDD is a major public health concern and a leading cause of disability worldwide. A shift in treatment perspectives, from a disorder-specific approach to a transdiagnostic approach, has been proposed. While the disorder-specific approach tends to understand and treat different mental disorders as independent psychological problems, the transdiagnostic approach aims to identify common clinical features (e.g., sleep disturbances) across a range of psychological disorders. The transdiagnostic approach would potentially facilitate timely dissemination of evidence-based psychological treatments and contribute to significant public health implications. Aims: To evaluate the efficacy of a transdiagnostic group sleep and circadian treatment (TranS-C) for improving disorder-specific symptoms (i.e., depressive symptoms) and sleep and circadian functions, and to examine the relationship between depressive symptoms and sleep problems across the treatment. Methods: The proposed study will be a randomised, assessor-blind controlled trial involving 150 participants with comorbid MDD and sleep and circadian dysfunctions. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to either 6-week TranS-C group treatment or care-as-usual (CAU) control group in a ratio of 1:1. TranS-C integrates elements of evidence-based interventions, namely cognitive-behavioural therapy for insomnia, delayed sleep phase type, and interpersonal and social rhythm therapy. Based on a task-shifting approach, the treatment will be delivered by a trained psychology graduate to enhance dissemination and maintain sustainability in the long run. Major assessments will be at baseline, 1-week, and 12-week post-treatment. Primary and secondary outcomes will include depressive and anxiety symptoms, sleep disturbances, fatigue, quality of life, and functional impairment. Data analysis: Analyses will be conducted by a blinded statistician. Treatment efficacy will be compared between groups using linear mixed-effects models across time points. A hierarchical linear regression analysis will be performed to examine changes in depressive symptoms in relation to changes in sleep symptoms across the treatment. Significance: To the best of knowledge, the proposed study will be the first study examining the efficacy of group TranS-C for MDD using the task-shifting approach. Transdiagnostic sleep treatment will assist clinicians to determine treatment priority for comorbidities, shorten the time needed to train non-specialist health workers and increase help-seeking behaviours in Chinese adult population. If proven effective and acceptable, it will inform the next stage of work that applies to populations with different mental illnesses. 研究背景：睡眠障礙與不同的心理疾病有著高度的共病性，其中以抑鬱症（MDD）最為常見。抑鬱症是一個主要的公共衛生問題，也是在世界各地導致殘疾的主因。近年，改變治療方法的說法開始被提議，由疾病專有療法轉變為跨診斷方法。跨診斷方法旨在識別不同精神病之間共有的臨床特徵（例如，睡眠障礙），而疾病專有療法則視不同的心理疾病為獨立的心理問題。跨診斷方法可能有助於適時地傳播以實證為本的心理療法，並有助於在公共衛生層面產生重大的影響。 研究目的：本研究的目的在於評估跨診斷睡眠及晝夜節律治療小組（TranS-C）改善特定疾病症狀（即抑鬱症症狀）和睡眠及晝夜節律功能之療效，並探討抑鬱症狀與睡眠問題之間的關係。 研究方法：是項擬定的研究為一個評估者盲導的隨機對照試驗。150名同時患上抑鬱症和睡眠及生理節律障礙的參加者將會以1比1 的比例被隨機分配到為期6週的治療組（TranS-C）或常規護理對照組（CAU）。TranS-C整合了以實證為本的心理療法，包括失眠認知行為治療，睡眠相位後移症候群之療法，以及人際社會節奏治療。建基於任務轉移的方法，療程將由已受訓的心理學研究生負責，以加強傳播和維持長遠發展的可持續性。是項研究的主要的評估將會在基線，治療後1星期和治療後12星期。主要和次要指標包括抑鬱和焦慮病徵，睡眠障礙，疲勞，生活質素和功能障礙。 數據分析：數據將會由統計人員以盲測進行分析。通過比較治療組和對照組的數據，本研究將以時間為變項進行線性混合效果模型分析，以探討治療功效。在整個治療過程中，階層線性迴歸分析將會被用以分析抑鬱病徵和睡眠病徵之間的變化。 重要性：是項擬定的研究為首個以任務轉移為基礎，探討TranS-C治療小組治療抑鬱症療效的研究。跨診斷睡眠治療將會幫助治療師判斷共病症的治療優先次序，縮短非專科受訓的健康工作者所需的培訓時間，並增加中國成年人的求助行為。若本研究被證實為有效和可接受，它將會為下一階段的研究提供重要的基礎，並適用於患有不同心理問題的患者。

24604518.label: Realisation of objectives
24604518.value: To achieve objective 1 (to evaluate the efficacy of a 6-week transdiagnostic group sleep and circadian treatment (TranS-C) for improving disorder-specific symptoms (i.e., depressive symptoms) and sleep and circadian dysfunctions in comparison with care-as-usual (CAU) control group), we conducted the first randomized controlled trial (RCT) to examine the efficacy of TranS-C on individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD). A total of 152 adults diagnosed with MDD and at least one sleep disturbance (n = 152) were recruited on a rolling basis through the mass mailing system of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) and social media (e.g., Facebook and Instagram). Potential participants completed informed consent followed by a two-stage screening for eligibility. In the first stage, participants were asked to complete a set of online screening questionnaires on the Qualtrics platform. In the second stage, participants received a telephone-administered diagnostic interview on MDD by trained research assistants. Eligible participants who passed through the two-stage screening were invited to participate in this study by a research assistant via phone contact and instructed to download an in-house smartphone app for online data collection. Participants who completed the basely ne assessment were then randomized into the TranS-C (n = 77) or CAU group (n = 75). The block randomization was performed by an independent research assistant using a computer-generated list of numbers. The participants were not blind to group allocation in the current study design. There are no significant between-group differences in demographics, clinical characteristics, and treatment expectancy at baseline (ps > 0.5). The intervention of our study comprised six weekly two-hour group sessions with the following components: (1) motivational enhancement and goal setting, (2) education on sleep and circadian processes, (3) sleep hygiene, (4) establishing regular sleep-wake times, (5) stimulus control, (6) sleep restriction, (7) improving daytime functioning with energy-generating experiments, (8) correcting unhelpful sleep-related beliefs, and other elements in TranS-C if deemed necessary. Treatment contents were based on a manual published by Harvey and Buysse (2017), which was translated into and delivered in Chinese by our research team. The intervention was primarily conducted by a clinical psychology trainee under the supervision of a clinical psychologist. In group sessions, participants were helped to understand treatment materials through psychoeducation, discussions, videos, quizzes, and exercises. To consolidate learnings, participants were asked to complete sleep diaries, set weekly goals and implement behavioral changes as homework. Each weekly session was followed by a 15-minute individual follow-up on sleep diary review and weekly goal setting. A total of nine treatment groups were run to deliver the intervention, with each group consisting of 6–10 participants. The intervention was initially conducted face-to-face on the campus of CUHK. The venue was later changed to a community center due to tightened COVID infection control measures imposed by CUHK. Subsequent group treatment sessions were delivered online via video conferencing of Zoom Meetings due to further tightened restriction measures during COVID outbreaks. The participants were asked to turn on cameras to ensure engagement and participation. For the CAU group, participants continued to receive usual care during the 6-week period. They received no active treatment for sleep disturbance or depressive symptoms. They only filled in their sleep diaries during the period. To ensure the treatment protocol was not violated, a treatment tracking log was used. The primary outcome measure for efficacy was the self-administered Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), a 20-item questionnaire used to assess the severity of depressive symptoms. Secondary outcome measures included the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), a 14-item self-rating scale measuring anxiety and depression in both hospital and community settings; the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), a 7-item scale designed to evaluate perceived insomnia severity; the 7-day standardised sleep diary that records sleep time, wake time, perceived sleeping quality, and use of hypnotics on a daily basis; a composite sleep health score captured by the sum of the scores from six domains, including sleep regularity, satisfaction, alertness, timing, efficiency, and duration; the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-Sleep Disturbance (PROMIS-SD) and the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-Sleep-Related Impairment (PROMIS-SRI), 8-item scales to assess sleep and circadian functions; the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI), a 20-item self-reported instrument designed to measure fatigue; the Short Form (Six-Dimension) Health Survey – The Chinese (Hong Kong) Version (SF-6D), a preference-based single-index measure of health, including physical functioning, role limitation, social functioning, bodily pain, mental health, and vitality; and the Sheehan Disability Scale (SDS), a 5-item scale that assesses functional impairment in work/school, social life, and family life. All data were verified for accuracy, consistency, and completeness before the analysis. The intent-to-treat approach, which includes all randomized participants regardless of the amount of treatment they have received and/or attrition during follow-up assessments, was used in all analyses to simulate the real-world setting. The baseline characteristics of TranS-C and CAU groups were compared using chi-square test of independence or independent samples t-tests as appropriate. The efficacy of TranS-C was evaluated using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to examine changes in primary and secondary outcomes between the two groups from baseline to immediate post-treatment (Week 7) and 12-week follow-up (Week 19). The LMM uses maximum likelihood estimation and handles data that are assumed to be missing at random. To achieve objective 2 (to examine the relationship between depressive symptoms and sleep problems across the TranS-C treatment), a multiple linear regression analysis was used to demonstrate how sleep variables predict the severity of depressive symptoms. The 7-day standardised sleep diary at baseline and the PHQ-9 at immediate post-treatment (Week 7) were used to perform the analysis.

24604518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24604518.value: Treatment Efficacy (Objective 1) On PHQ-9, the TranS-C group showed significant improvement in depressive symptoms relative to the CAU group from baseline to immediate post-treatment (p <.001, d = 0.84). Further improvement was noted at the 12-week follow-up (p <.001; d = 1.09). Similarly, on HADS-D, the TranS-C group showed a significant reduction in depressive symptoms compared to the CAU group at immediate post-treatment (p = .002, d = 0.76). Further improvement was observed at the 12-week follow-up (p <.001, d = 0.93). On sleep and circadian functioning, the TranS-C group showed significantly greater improvement relative to the CAU group in insomnia severity, sleep disturbance, and sleep-related impairments at immediate post-treatment, as indicated by ISI (p <.001, d = 0.77), PROMIS-SD (p <.001, d = 1.15), and PROMIS-SRI (p <.001, d = 1.22). Further improvements were observed in ISI (p <.001, d = 1.11), PROMIS-SD (p <.001, d = 1.27), and PROMIS-SRI (p <.001, d = 1.33) in the TranS-C group at 12-week follow-up. On sleep diary measures, the TranS-C group showed significant improvements in a range of sleep parameters, including SE (p <.001, d = 0.59), TIB (p = .002, d = 0.41), SOL (p =.001, d = 0.59), WASO (p <.001, d = 0.39), NOA (p =.002, d = 0.12), SQ (p <.001, d = 0.77), and RF (p <.001, d = 0.65) relative to CAU controls at immediate post-treatment. Significant improvements relative to the CAU group were also noted for SE (p <.001, d = 0.76), TIB (p =.004, d = 0.18), SOL (p =.001, d = 0.47), WASO (p <.001, d = 0.36), NOA (p =.005, d = 0.26), SQ (p <.001, d = 0.69), and RF (p <.001, d = 0.94) at 12-week follow-up. Meanwhile, no significant improvement in TST was observed in the TranS-C group relative to the CAU group at both time points. On other secondary outcomes, participants in the TranS-C group showed significant improvements in fatigue, anxiety, and subjective health at immediate post-treatment, as indicated by MFI (p <.001, d = 1.06), HADS-A (p =.004, d = 0.67) and SF-6D (p <.001, d = 0.71). Gains in MFI (p <.001, d = 1.09), HADS-A (p <.001, d = 1.09), and SF-6D (p <.001, d = 0.59) were maintained at 12-week follow-up. Significant reductions in functional impairments measured by SDS in the TranS-C group relative to controls were also noted at the 12-week follow-up (p =.014, d = 0.57). Prediction of Depressive Symptoms by Sleep Variables (Objective 2) There was a significant interaction between treatment condition and changes in insomnia severity (i.e., ISI) from Week 0 to Week 7 for depression severity (i.e., PHQ-9) at immediate post-treatment (b = −.29, p < .05). Changes in PROMIS-SD/SRI from Week 9 to Week 7 and 19 as well as changes in ISI from Week 0 to Week 19 did not moderate depression severity (i.e., PHQ-9) at Week 7 or 19. Furthermore, changes in ISI and PROMIS-SD from Week 0 to Week 7 and 19 had a significant main effect of time on depression severity at both Week 7 and 19.

24604518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24604518.value: Despite our positive findings of TranS-C on MDD, several limitations of this study are important to note. Firstly, the present study does not involve an active control, which may inflate the effect size differences (Cunningham et al., 2013). Future studies may adopt active controls and compare the efficacy of TranS-C to other sleep interventions or depression-focused treatments. Secondly, as blinding was not possible for participants because of the nature of the study, their ratings on outcome measures could be potentially biased. Thirdly, our study included only subjective sleep measures. Future studies may include actigraphy or polysomnography for objective sleep parameters. Fourthly, the current sample excluded MDD patients comorbid with other psychiatric disorders and certain sleep disorders (e.g., narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea). The generalizability of current ﬁndings to samples with fewer exclusion criteria could be examined in future studies. Fifthly, our current study did not examine the effects of TranS-C on depressive symptoms beyond three months. As sleep disturbance is a known predictor for the recurrence of MDD (Wojnarowski et al., 2019), future studies may examine the effects of TranS-C over a longer time frame and how well it can reduce risks of relapse for MDD.

24604518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24604518.value: Sleep disturbance commonly co-occur with major depressive disorder (MDD). The Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Treatment (TranS-C) is an intervention targeting multiple sleep dysfunctions underlying a range of psychological disorders, including MDD. At present, only two clinical trials demonstrated the efficacy of TranS-C on sleep functioning and general psychiatric symptoms. The present study was the first to examine the efficacy of TranS-C on MDD. Depressed individuals who received TranS-C showed significant improvement in not only depressive symptoms, but also insomnia severity, sleep disturbance, sleep-related impairments, fatigue, anxiety, and quality of life. Compared to traditional depression-specific treatments, TranS-C has several distinctive advantages. First, TranS-C is shown to be effective in treating MDD and sleep disturbance, while traditional treatments for depression such as cognitive behavioral therapy depression (CBT-D) often leave sleep dysfunction untreated. Second, mental health stigma is a significant barrier to treatment-seeking for depression. TranS-C as a sleep-focused intervention may thus bypass the stigma and be better accepted than depression-focused treatments by certain MDD patients. Third, TranS-C offers a highly disseminable and cost-effective transdiagnostic protocol. While TranS-C was first designed as an individual treatment with a great extent of customization, our study demonstrated the comparable efficacy of TranS-C in group format with individual follow-up.

24606618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24606618.value: Venipuncture is one of the most painful and distressing procedure experienced by pediatric patients. Unmanaged pain has short- and long-term consequences to patients. Moreover, it prolongs the procedure and consumes additional manpower while decreasing the satisfaction of health-care providers. Evidence suggests that distraction combined with age-appropriate procedural information can effectively decrease procedural pain and anxiety in pediatric patients. This integrated approach, however, may be difficult to implement and consumes high amounts of manpower and time. Immersive virtual reality (IVR) has become possible with technological advancement. It can simultaneously provide complete distraction and procedural information to patients. However, its effects on pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture are unknown. Guided by the Gate Control Theory and the Lazarus and Folkman’s Theory, this study aims to examine the effects of IVR intervention on reducing the pain, anxiety and stress experienced by pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture. It will also examine the effects of IVR on the duration of venipuncture and the satisfaction of health-care providers for the procedure. Its cost-effectiveness will also be evaluated. A randomized controlled trial with repeated assessments will be conducted. A total of 200 pediatric patients aged 4–12 years will be recruited from a regional public hospital and randomly assigned to either the intervention or control group. The study will use two age-appropriate IVR modules that consist of procedural information developed by the principal investigator. The intervention group will receive IVR intervention, whereas the control group will receive standard care only. The primary outcome is child-reported pain. Secondary outcomes include child-reported anxiety, heart rate, salivary cortisol, length of procedure, and satisfaction of health care providers with respect to the venipuncture procedure. The cost-effectiveness of IVR intervention will be compared with that of standard care. Outcome evaluation will be conducted at four time points: 10 minutes before, during, and immediately after and 30 minutes after the procedure. Intention to treat and generalized estimating equation model will be used to analyze the data. This study is the first of its kind to adopt IVR intervention with age-appropriate procedural information for pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture. Findings of the proposed study may (1) provide a novel, facile, and cost-effective intervention that can be used virtually at any time and place to manage pain and anxiety; and (2) shed light on the global trends of research and clinical development of IVR as an intervention for other painful and stressful medical procedures.

24606618.label: Realisation of objectives
24606618.value: This study was a two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial aimed to examine the effects of immersive virtual reality (IVR) intervention on reducing pain, anxiety, stress, and length of procedure among pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture. The satisfaction ratings of healthcare providers toward the venipuncture procedures and the cost effectiveness of IVR interventions were also assessed. The study was conducted as originally planned without deviation from January 2019 to January 2020. However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Hospital Authority announced the activation of the Emergency Response Level in public hospitals on 25 January 2020. All visiting arrangements and research-related activities have been suspended in public hospitals. Therefore, subject recruitment and data collection of this project has been suspended since 25 January 2020. Since then, the COVID-19 pandemic situation in Hong Kong has been fluctuating. As of June 2022, Hong Kong is still experiencing the fifth wave of the pandemic. Due to increased hospital admissions of children infected with the COVID-19 in the fifth wave, it was difficult to resume subject recruitment and data collection at the clinical site of this study and elsewhere before the end of the study (i.e. June 2022). Nonetheless, all three objectives listed have been achieved. During January 2019 to January 2020, a total of 155 eligible pediatric patients and their parents were approached, which accounted for 77.5% of the original proposed sample size (n=200). Eligible pediatric patients were (1) aged between 4 and 12 years; (2) scheduled to undergo venipuncture; and (3) can understand Chinese and follow instructions. Potential participants were excluded if they had (1) identified cognitive and learning problems in their medical record; (2) identified contact precautions; and (3) history of seizures or motion sickness. Healthcare providers participating in the procedure (e.g., medical interns/officers, nurses, patient-care assistants) were also invited to rate their satisfaction with the venipuncture procedure. Of the 155 eligible patients and their parents, six refused to participate because they were in a hurry for subsequent medical appointments or investigations after venipuncture. Accordingly, 149 pediatric patients and their parents were recruited with a consent rate of 96.1%. The mean age of pediatric patients were 7.21 (SD=2.45) years. More than half were between 4 and 7 years old (59.1%) and female (57.7%), and nearly half were diagnosed with fever (44.3%). The 149 patients were randomly allocated to the control (n=74) and intervention group (n=75) in a 1:1 ratio and stratified by age group (4–7 and 8–12 years). Pediatric patients in the control group received standard care, while those in the intervention group received an age appropriate IVR intervention providing distraction and procedural information in addition to standard care. Of the 149 participants, five received multiple venipunctures, and three did not complete post-test data collection. They were all included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Pediatric patients in the intervention group did not report any adverse effects such as dizziness, nausea, headache or eye strain during and after the IVR intervention. Objectives 1 and 2 were achieved through a randomized controlled trial. For objective 1, the effects of IVR interventions in reducing pain, anxiety, stress, and length of procedure in pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture with those of standard care were compared. All planned outcomes data were collected at 10 min before (T0), during (T1), immediately after (T2), and 30 min after (T3) the venipuncture procedure. At T0, baseline data including child-reported pain, child-reported anxiety, stress level (measured by salivary cortisol), and heart rate were collected. At T1, heart-rate data was collected. At T2, child-reported pain, child-reported anxiety, heart rate, the length of procedure and healthcare provider satisfaction were collected. At T3, child-reported pain, child-reported anxiety, stress level and heart rate were collected again. For Objective 2, a total of 149 healthcare providers were recruited. Their satisfaction towards venipuncture procedures was assessed using the 8-item Staff Satisfaction Scale at T2 and compared between groups. Objective 3 was achieved by collecting and comparing the cost of implementing IVR interventions and standard care. All the cost data involved were expressed in Hong Kong dollars and valued on the starting date of the study on the basis of non-subsidized cost. All costs incurred were estimated per each participant. Specifically, the cost of human resources (e.g. doctors, nurses, phlebotomist, and health care assistants) were measured by the salary of the middle rank of the professionals and calculated based on minutes used to perform the procedures. Costs of consumables to perform the venipuncture (e.g. alcohol pad, glove, butterfly needles, and band aid) were also collected and estimated based on the retail price paid by the finance office of the hospital. The cost for development of IVR modules and VR goggles included in the intervention group were also collected.

24606618.label: Major findings and research outcome
24606618.value: This is the first randomised controlled trial to use IVR to distract pediatric patients while simultaneously offering procedural information during venipuncture. The generalized estimating equation results showed that the intervention group experienced a significantly smaller increase in pain score at T2 relative to T0 than those in the control group (β: -0.78; 95% CI: -1.21, -0.35; p<0.001). Similar results were observed in the subgroup analysis of patients aged 4–7 years (β: -1.05; 95% CI: -1.62, -0.49; p<0.001) with a large effect size (d=0.98; 95% CI: 0.53, 1.42). As for anxiety, the intervention group also showed a significant greater reduction in anxiety scores at T2 (β: -0.41; 95% CI: -0.76, -0.05; p=0.025) with respect to T0 than the control group. Additionally, independent t-test showed that the length of procedure in the intervention group (mean [SD] duration, 4.43 [3.47] minutes) was significantly shorter than that in the control group (mean [SD] duration, 6.56 [7.39] minutes, p=0.025). However, no statistically significant difference was found in stress level and heart rate between groups. For staff satisfaction towards venipuncture procedures, healthcare providers in the intervention group reported a mean staff satisfaction score of 34.45 (SD 4.50), which was statistically significantly higher than the control group (32.97 [SD 4.02], p=0.03). For cost-effectiveness of IVR intervention, the mean total cost per patient incurred in the intervention and control groups were HK$342.0 (SD 72.0) and HK$138.5 (SD 239.7), respectively. The pain level change (as assessed by the FPS-R score) at immediately post-intervention with respect to the baseline in the intervention and control groups indicating that the IVR intervention could lead to a smaller increment of the pain score by a mean between group difference of -2.63 (95% bootstrap CI: -3.87 to -1.41) when compared with the standard care. Therefore, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of the IVR intervention compared with standard care was HK$77.4 per 1 point of the FPS-R score decrease, indicating that the mean cost needed per a patient for a reduction of 1 point in the FPS-R score by the IVR intervention would be HK$77.4 (~US$10) compared with standard care. If VR development costs were excluded, the mean medical cost per patient incurred in the intervention group was HK$72.1 (SD 72.0), which was lower than standard care (HK$138.5 [SD 239.7]). This suggests that the IVR intervention would be cost-effective compared to standard care if one-off VR development cost are not accounted for.

24606618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24606618.value: The encouraging results of this study suggest that IVR interventions can serve as an innovative clinical intervention that provides distraction and procedural information to reduce pain and anxiety in pediatric patients undergoing venipunctures. Further studies should consider recruiting participants at multiple sites to validate the findings. As this study primarily focused on quantitative measures, future studies may include qualitative interviews to understand the process and mechanisms. The principles of this intervention can be generalized and extended to other pain- and anxiety-inducing medical procedures beyond venipuncture. Based on the current findings, the PI expanded the use of IVR and applied it to pediatric cancer patients to reduce their anxiety, nausea and vomiting during chemotherapy. One exploratory trial (ref: 16170321) and a full scale randomized controlled trial (ref: 18190151) were funded by the Health and Medical Research Fund. In addition, the experiences gained from this study provided insights into involving parents in the IVR intervention, and as such, another proposal related to the use of IVR to deliver mindfulness interventions to childhood cancer survivors and their parents has been submitted for seeking support from the General Research Fund (ref: 14607923).

24606618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24606618.value: Pediatric patients experienced substantial pain and distress during venipuncture. Using immersive virtual reality (IVR) to offer procedural information and distraction may reduce venipuncture-related pain and anxiety. However, the effects of such IVR on pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture are unknown. This randomized controlled trial examined the effects of an IVR intervention on pain, anxiety, stress and length of procedure among pediatric patients undergoing venipuncture. Healthcare provider satisfaction and the cost-effectiveness of the interventions were also evaluated. From January 2019 to January 2020, 149 pediatric patients aged 4–12 years who underwent venipuncture from a public hospital were recruited. They were randomly allocated to an IVR intervention or a standard care control group. Outcomes were assessed 10 min before, during, immediately after and 30 min after the procedure. Results showed that the IVR intervention significantly reduced increase in pain and anxiety immediately after the intervention, shortened the length of procedure and increased healthcare provider satisfaction compared with standard care. The IVR intervention is more cost-effective than standard care if the one-off virtual reality development costs are excluded. These results shed light on the clinical development of IVR interventions for other painful and stressful medical procedures.

24606718.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24606718.value: 中國南方的流行音樂與新流動性

24606718.label: Project Objectives
24606718.value: This project will document a flourishing and rapidly evolving music scene in southern China that has received little scholarly attention, and will analyze it in relation to broader economic, political, and cultural transformations in China. This research will contribute substantially to the completion of a monograph that is an important addition to existing scholarship on popular music in the PRC, and which addresses important lacunae in this broader scholarship in terms of research focus, methodology, and critical approach. This research will invoke “mobility” as a central analytic in understanding the music of—and the creative processes employed by—a cohort of musicians based in Guangzhou. It will explore interconnections between physical movements and migrations of people, circulations of global popular musics, emergent forms of musical creativity, and an evolving geography of contemporary China. Thus, this research will contribute to an understanding of new ways in which people, sounds, ideas, and feelings circulate to, from, within, and beyond China. By focusing on the contemporary and historical media systems through which music and other sounds circulate within and beyond China, this research will investigate how evolving modes of musical circulation and the listening practices associated with them are connected to broader transformations of state, society, and space. By offering an ethnographic analysis of the music industry in southern China, it will thus contribute to broader work on media and communications in contemporary China from the important but underrepresented perspective of popular music.
