24606718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24606718.value: Focusing on contemporary popular and independent music in southern China, this research will examine emergent forms of musical creativity and modes of circulation as they relate to shifts in conceptualizations about self, publics, space, and state instigated by China’s political and economic reforms. At the center of this research is a cohort of musicians that has coalesced in Guangzhou over the past decade. These musicians, many of whom have moved to China’s third largest city from small towns and rural areas throughout southern China, selectively draw on transnational genres of popular music and Chinese folk musics. They sing in local dialects of Chinese about themes related to urban/rural difference, migration, their hometowns, and broader changes in Chinese society. Increasingly successful commercially, these bands have become central to a new business model adopted by one of China’s largest record companies, which seeks to integrate traditional industry approaches with new strategies and new media that cater to an increasingly mobile citizenry. This research project is an ethnographic study of these musicians and the music industry in which they participate, and brings together a close ethnographic approach with detailed historical knowledge and analysis of the changing economics, politics, and aesthetics of music in China. Bridging ethnomusicology, popular music studies, cultural geography, media studies, and the anthropology of infrastructure, this research invokes “mobility” as a central analytic, exploring interconnections between physical movements and migrations of people, circulations of global popular musics, forms of musical creativity, and an evolving geography of contemporary China. By attending to the contemporary and historical infrastructures through which music and other sounds circulate within and beyond China, this research seeks to understand how evolving modes of musical circulation and the listening practices associated with them are connected to broader transformations of state, society, and space. Due to the historical centrality of sound—taken broadly to include both musical and linguistic sounds, as well as the soundscapes of which they are a part—in the affective constitution of subjectivities and nation in China, the acoustic is an important and underutilized anthropological lens on such transformations. By paying attention to the musical construction of place, space, and scale while foregrounding mobility as a central analytic, this research builds upon ethnographic studies of the ways music and sound may participate in constructions of the local in globally connected societies, while also contributing to spatially-informed scholarship of contemporary China. 本課題聚焦中國南方的當代流行音樂與獨立音樂，研究音樂創造力的表現和中國政治經濟改革下的傳播主體、時空與國家觀念。研究對象為過去十年中在廣州相識相知的一群音樂家們。他們從中國南部村鎮遷址到第三大城市（廣州），有意識地汲取流行音樂與民間音樂中的跨民族文化養分。他們以方言歌唱，主題涉及城鄉差異、移民、鄉愁以及中國社會的巨大變革。隨之而來的商業成功，使得這些樂隊逐漸成為全國最大唱片公司之一（星外星唱片）的新型商業模式的中心環節。星外星唱片公司致力於探尋傳統音樂工業運作方式與新策略、新媒體的有效結合，以迎合不斷增長的流動公民之需求。本課題是針對這些音樂家及音樂產業的民族誌研究，是對變革中的中國經濟、政治和音樂審美的歷史分析文本。本課題結合民族音樂學、流行音樂、文化地理、媒體研究及人類學研究，聚焦“流動性”，探索遷徙與移民的內在關聯，並及全球流行音樂的流通範式、音樂創造力和文化地理特徵。基於國內國外當代或歷史中諸多音樂及其他聲音實踐的經驗，本課題力圖解讀演進中的音樂流通模式，以及與聽覺實踐相關聯的廣闊的國家、社會與空間變遷。由於歷史中聲音的核心——廣義上包括音樂、語言聲響，以及它們參與建構的聲音景觀——是中國主體性與國族建構的重要一環，其演變流轉卻長久以來欠缺人類學觀照。通過著重分析時空的音樂性建構，及其流動性，本課題依託民族誌研究，觀照國際化視野下的本土音樂、聲音建構，并促進中國當代的空間研究。

24606718.label: Realisation of objectives
24606718.value: The primary research output from this project is Sonic Mobilities: Producing Worlds in Southern China, a single-author monograph published by the University of Chicago Press. This book explores the relationships between musical circulations, emergent forms of musical creativity, and an evolving geography of contemporary China. It is an ethnographic account of musical cosmopolitanism in Guangzhou as a process of knowledge making, connected both to much older forms of cosmopolitanism and routes of exchange and to contemporary experiences of mobility, migration, and urbanization. Bridging ethnomusicology, popular music studies, cultural geography, media studies, and the anthropology of infrastructure, it examines the cultural dimensions of shifts in conceptualizations of self, space, publics, and state in a rapidly transforming PRC. The ethnographic focus of the book is a cohort of musicians who have moved from smaller cities and rural areas to China’s third-largest city, Guangzhou. Wanju Chuanzhang (Toy Captain) performs a self-described “island mix” of poppy, Latin-infused music sung in the Min subdialect spoken on Nan’ao Dao, a small island off the southeast coast of China. Mabang performs a blend of folk, rock, and reggae peppered with elements from folk musics of southern China and caidiao opera from Guangxi Province. Focusing on these musicians and the music industry in which they participate, the book explores the changing economics, politics, and aesthetics of popular music in China through an ethnography of the social worlds of cultural production in Guangzhou. Offering a unique and timely perspective on contemporary culture in China while engaging active debates in ethnomusicology and related fields, this book will appeal to a wide variety of scholars and students in ethnomusicology, popular music studies, anthropology, media studies, China studies, Asian studies, and adjacent areas. The book is an important addition to the limited existing scholarship on contemporary popular music and culture in China because it addresses significant lacunae in terms of research focus, methodology, and critical approach. Employing a deep ethnographic approach, it takes as its focus diverse genres of popular music in southern China, and complicates a history of the relationships between folk, traditional, and popular musics. Furthermore, it approaches the political significance of this music not in terms of hegemony and resistance (like much of the existing work on rock and popular music in northern China), but in relation to subtle transformations of space, state, and society. This book will also be an important contribution to the field of China studies through its focus on popular music, an underrepresented and critical cultural domain where China’s shifting economics, politics, and culture are being negotiated, contested, and reimagined. More broadly, the book contributes to efforts in ethnomusicology and popular music studies to nuance understandings of the ways popular music constructs notions of the local against a backdrop of globalization, while using the particularities of the context it focuses on in order to contribute to theorizing popular music’s cultural, political, and economic significance. Through its theoretical focus on mobilities, the book stands to appeal to scholars working on music and sound in a variety of geographic contexts beyond Asia. The book is published in the University of Chicago Press’s book series, “Chicago Studies in Ethnomusicology,” one of the most prestigious book series in the discipline of ethnomusicology that has published several classics in the field. In the past two decades, book prizes awarded by the Society for Ethnomusicology have been overwhelmingly dominated by three presses, of which University of Chicago Press is one. By publishing the book in this venue, it will reach as wide a readership as possible, and will be acquired by most academic libraries who maintain collections in this field. The covid-19 pandemic impacted my ability to carry out some parts of this project. My last trip to Mainland China was in January 2020; since then, further on-the-ground fieldwork has been impossible due to travel restrictions, and because of the long-term cancellation of the kinds of events and activities that my research originally intended to focus on. While I was able to complete the book based on additional fieldwork trips in the first year of the project duration before the pandemic as well as on past fieldwork, I was forced to adjust my research plans given the situation. I underutilized funds allocated for research trips and conference travel, and a second journal article planned is delayed due to the need for additional fieldwork. In the meantime, I developed a secondary research area in online musical activities including musical diplomacy, and laid the foundation for further research that I have applied for a GRF grant for, as discussed more below.

24606718.label: Major findings and research outcome
24606718.value: Musical cosmopolitanism is a process of knowledge making, and music participates in producing worlds—in forging understandings of global connection, senses of self, and emplaced ways of being in the world. Contemporary musicians’ different modes of mobility—both actual and vicarious—enact new spatial-creative imaginaries, jump scales, make places, and reveal spatial and scalar transformations tied to broader economic, political, and cultural transformations in China, and to processes of neoliberal globalization. Creativity in popular music production is a collaborative process that occurs at various intersections between musicians, producers, corporate executives, recording engineers, audiences, and many other players. That collaborative creative process is inflected by interconnected concerns about musical genre and ideas of the local, national, and global. Understanding recording and mixing as negotiations that mediate sonic and social worlds, we may look to musical creativity as an assemblage of practices including listening, interpretation, performance, recording, mixing, and selection of instruments as they intersect with one another, with emergent genre categorizations, and with cosmopolitan circulations of knowledge. When musical genres are recombined, they hold on to certain values, meanings, and embodied practices while discarding others, and musical sounds may come to feel and sound as if they resemble certain places, identities, and sociocultural formations through repetitive acts of listening and performance. The production, circulation, and consumption of music in local dialects challenges the symbolic power of standard Mandarin by aligning local languages with alternative spatial and social imaginaries and articulates translocal geographies of southern China that stand in contrast to ways of imagining space that assume isomorphic relationships between dialect, culture, and music. Personal histories, national histories, and cosmopolitan formations intersect and overlap, and musical creativity is a means of exploring the role of individual agency and expressive culture in broader cultural shifts. The process of becoming a musical cosmopolitan in contemporary China is one that is structured by political, economic, and cultural factors but that is nonetheless profoundly personal and unique to thinking, feeling, reflecting, and listening individuals. Focusing on the infrastructural foundations of mediated circulations of sound as well as on the sonic aspects of broader infrastructures brings attention to the materialities and spatialities of the technical and cultural systems through which sounds circulate. Evolving modes of musical circulation and the listening practices associated with them reveal and contribute to broader transformations of state, society, and space.

24606718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24606718.value: A major new focus of my work that emerged through the process of carrying out this research is the proliferation in contemporary China of musical styles linked to African American, Afro-Caribbean, and Black Atlantic histories and experiences. I have submitted a new GRF proposal, “Popular Music, Minor Transnationalism, and Blackness in Southern China,” that extends this dimension of the project. In this new project, I will analyze how blackness is understood, reconfigured, and performed in a Chinese context, and explore how music and race—as well as other social constructs that negotiate difference and power—intersect in locally particular ways. My work on music in local dialects also lays the groundwork for collaborative research projects that extend this work while bridging perspectives and methodologies from the humanities, social sciences, and cognitive sciences. I have recently applied as Co-PI on an Areas of Excellence Scheme proposal and as Project Coordinator of a Young Collaborative Research Grant project related to this work. Although neither proposal was successful, I will continue to apply for funding. These collaborations are poised to contribute to generating knowledge about linguistic and musical environments of South China that have implications for child development, cultural preservation, and public policy initiatives.

24606718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24606718.value: In the past few decades, economic, social, political and cultural changes in China have meant that people are not only moving around more and in new ways, but they are also thinking differently about their relationships to places. At the same time, in our contemporary networked world, music and ideas about it travel faster than ever before, and represent another form of mobility—in this case, of sound, rather than of people. Through on-the ground research in various music-making and music industry contexts in Guangzhou and other locations, this work sheds light on the ways musicians in Southern China draw on global popular musics as well as regional traditions and ideas, and how they create music reflective of their own lives and their own mobilities. More broadly, it offers insight on the cultural dimensions of globalization in Southern China and beyond.

24607618.label: Project Objectives
24607618.value: This project will demonstrate that concepts of autonomy, such as independence and self-determination, are the leading concepts by which Ernst Cassirer’s Philosophy of Symbolic Forms, Vol. II: Mythical Thought ought to be interpreted. This project will demonstrate the immense influence G.W.F. Hegel’s philosophy of conceptual determinacy has played in the formation of Cassirer’s concept of autonomy. Accordingly, this book aims to fill a lacuna in the philosophical literature. This project aims to foster dialogue between philosophy of culture and comparative mythology. This project aims to provide a model for a philosophy of culture which is both attentive to the empirical sciences but is not reduced to an empirical science. By demonstrating how Cassirer’s philosophy of myth provides an organizational scheme for categorizing empirical research, Cassirer’s philosophy of mythology provides key insights for developing a philosophy of culture which integrates philosophy and empirical science. Cassirer's structural paradigm will offer students a compelling model for approaching comparative mythology, which deserves as much attention as more widely read authors such as Campbell, Dundes, Witzel, and Puhvel. This project will demonstrate the central role that imagination plays in Cassirer’s solution to a methodological paradox that few philosophers have recognized. Cassirer employs an apriori transcendental methodology while at the same time appealing to a posteriori empirical studies to establish the content of mythological phenomena. I aim to show that Cassirer’s appropriation of Kant’s concept of the transcendental synthetic imagination can solve this paradox. This project will demonstrate that one of the leading problems of Cassirer’s philosophy of mythology is the conflict between ‘Horizontalism’ and ‘Verticalism’. For Cassirer, the autonomy of each symbolic form signifies that no form ought to be measured by the standard of another cultural form. This is ‘Horizontalism’: each form is equally autonomous. Nonetheless, Cassirer establishes a vertical hierarchy of symbolic forms. Hence, Cassirer also advocates a ‘Verticalism’ which appears to stand in fundamental conflict with 'Horizontalism.' I will show that Cassirer solves this problem by appropriating Hegel’s concept of autonomy. This project will demonstrate the need for increased research into the philosophy of 20th century Jewish Humanism. In the 20th century Heidegger famously debated Cassirer at Davos, and for much of the remaining 20th century in Continental philosophy Cassirer’s philosophy was considered passé. With the revelation of Heidegger’s black books and the depth of Heidegger’s affiliation with National Socialism, this study will show that Cassirer’s humanism offers a new path to re-evaluate and re-appropriate 20th century German thought with a special focus on Jewish Humanism.

24607618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24607618.value: The proposed title of the book project is Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Myth. This book will investigate two central, albeit neglected, themes in Cassirer’s book Philosophy of Symbolic Forms, Vol. II: Mythical Thought: the autonomy of the cultural forms and the influence of G.W.F. Hegel on the concept of autonomy. In Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Myth I intend to investigate the autonomy of myth and Hegel’s influence on Cassirer’s concept of the autonomy of myth. Cassirer scholarship has experienced a revival in recent decades. Nonetheless, scholars have not done justice to the role of autonomy in Cassirer’s philosophy of symbolic forms. In particular, scholars have not discussed how autonomy works as a self-determining system and have not yet recognized the role that Hegel’s logic has played in the development of that system of autonomy. In Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Language I developed a novel interpretation of Cassirer’s philosophy of symbolic forms by employing the concept of autonomy to interpret Cassirer’s account of cultural forms with a particular focus on language. In Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Myth, I will apply the general interpretive framework first developed in Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Language to the cultural form of myth. By appropriating the concept of autonomy and Hegel’s concrete universal as a guiding interpretive thread, scholars shall be in a better position to appreciate and evaluate the methodological grounding of the central philosophical problems and their solutions in Philosophy of Symbolic Forms, Vol. II: Mythical Thought. Although the role of autonomy in Cassirer has not always been appreciated, Cassirer is clear that the autonomy of each cultural form (e.g. language, myth, and science) is a guiding thread by which to navigate his philosophy of culture. On the one hand, the ‘autonomy of culture’ signifies that human culture cannot be fully explained by or reduced to a principle external to culture itself. For example, culture loses its independence when one completely reduces culture to biological or neural-physiological processes. On the other hand, the autonomy of culture signifies that, although culture is not absolutely autonomous, the system of culture can account for itself as a product of the free and productive imagination. In Cassirer's concept of the autonomy of culture, scholars have an opportunity to develop more tools to advocate for the preservation of the humanities as an autonomous field of inquiry. 該項目的擬議標題是恩斯特卡西爾和神話自治。這個 本書將研究卡西爾的著作“哲學”中的兩個主要的，雖然被忽視的主題 符號形式，卷。二：神話思想：文化形式和文化的自主性 G.W.F.的影響黑格爾關於自治的概念。在恩斯特卡西爾和 神話的自主性我打算調查神話的自治和黑格爾的影響 關於卡西爾關於神話自治的概念。 近幾十年來，卡西爾獎學金經歷了復興。儘管如此，學者們 在卡西爾的象徵形式哲學中，對自治的作用沒有做到公正。 特別是，學者們尚未討論自治如何作為一種自我決定 系統並沒有認識到黑格爾的邏輯在其中發揮的作用 發展自治制度。在恩斯特卡西爾和自治中 語言我對卡西爾的象徵形式哲學進行了新穎的解釋 通過運用自治的概念來解釋卡西爾對文化形式的描述 特別注重語言。在恩斯特卡西爾和神話自治中，我會 應用最初在恩斯特卡西爾開發的一般解釋框架和 語言自治對神話的文化形態。通過挪用的概念 自治和黑格爾的具體普遍性作為指導性解釋主線，學者們應該 能夠更好地欣賞和評估方法論的基礎 符號形式哲學中的中心哲學問題及其解決方案，Vol。 二：神話思想。

24607618.label: Realisation of objectives
24607618.value: Objective One In chapter four I explicate the autonomy of mythology in terms of Cassirer’s schematism of symbolic forms. Myth is individuated from other forms by the fact that it is an objectification of the expressive function, whereby sign=signified. In chapter five I build upon this insight by showing that the independent function of myth is the law of the coincidence of the members of a relation. I demonstrate the truth of this law by appealing to anthropological material drawn from ethnological studies over the 19th and 20th centuries. In chapter six, I also show how the law of mythical consciousness is consistent with Cassirer's account of the sacred/profane distinction, and the emotional origin of that distinction. I first introduce myth as a form of self-determination in chapter four, and further develop this idea in chapters five through seven. Finally, in chapter seven, I demonstrate how mythical-religious consciousness can function as a form of self-determination and self-consciousness by transforming the sacred from a material into a trans-material domain. Objective Two In chapter four I demonstrate how the second volume of Cassirer’s The Philosophy of Symbolic Forms, Vol 2: Mythical Thinking, is an extension of Hegel’s Phenomenology of Spirit. I show how Cassirer further develops Hegel’s concept of the concept (as an autonomous self-determining totality) by applying it to the mythical world as a novel instance of the concrete universal. I show how Cassirer draws on the very specific sense of phenomenology as it is employed by Hegel. Cassirer further develops Hegel’s concept of Entäußerung to show that myth is a self-externalized form of culture. Chapter nine is further devoted to a detailed discussion of Hegel’s philosophy as a form of rational dialetheism and offers a detailed critique of his philosophy. Chapter ten shows how Hegel’s philosophy of the concept and Cassirer’s symbolic philosophy of culture can be synthesized into a novel philosophy of absolute symbolism. In this revised conception of their philosophy, I argue that the tautegorical and allegorical aspects of myth can be integrated into a novel and compelling vision of the absolute. Objective Three In chapter one I discuss some recent developments in the anthropology of myth, and the classical problem of ethno-centrism in anthropology. While acknowledging that Cassirer’s philosophy has problematic ethnocentric components, I argue that there are other aspects of Cassirer’s’ philosophy from which post-modern anthropology could benefit—especially Cassirer’s commitment to truth. For instance, by abandoning the concept of truth and the public domain of meaning, post-modern anthropology has lost its status as a scientific discipline and loses its capacity to engage in dialogue with others. Although Cassirer’s philosophy draws on some discredited material, I show that much of his work explains legitimate phenomena that are still recognized today: such as homeopathic and sympathetic magic investigated by Frazer in the Golden Baugh. Throughout the book—especially chapters five and six, I demonstrate how much of the ethnographical studies of the 19th and 20th centuries on mythical culture—from various forms of ritual and magical practices to mythical feeling and intuition, can be explained by Cassirer’s law of mythical culture. In addition to others, I consult the work of anthropologists such as Dundes, Witzel, Puhvel, Mauss, Strauss and Geertz. Objective Four In chapter one I introduce myth, unlike scientific culture, as a form of culture that thinks the totality in imaginative form. In chapter five I raise the following problem: given that Cassirer’s method is transcendental, how can he answer his questions empirically? I solve the problem by appealing to the mythical imagination. Because the synthetic imagination is a transcendental function, it is a priori. However, since the imagination’s products cannot be known except empirically, in order to know the product of the transcendental function, one must engage in empirical research. In chapter eight I further elucidate the relation of the imagination to all the forms of symbolism—expressive, representative, and significative. I show how Cassirer conceives of imagination as a unifying function active in all forms of symbolism, for it is responsible for combining sensuous signs with meaning contents. Finally, in chapter ten I give a novel argument that draws upon Cassirer’s philosophy of imagination. Here I show that only via the imagination can the absolute be successfully grasped in a particular, sensuous form. Objective Five In chapter one I argue that culture is autonomous in the sense that it is an absolute concept. I argue that because language can refer to all things, and language is a form of culture, so must culture have an absolute reference. I pick up on this theme again in chapter four, where I formulate the problem of autonomy. If each cultural form develops in total independence, then the goal of providing a system of culture is endangered. As Cassirer states, the philosopher of culture finds himself in a dilemma: either each form “stands side by side” and “they no longer express a common ideal content” or one appears forced to reduce the forms of culture to different instantiations of “one form of logic.” I tentatively solve this problem by appealing to the schematic structure of symbolism. Later, in chapter seven, I defend the autonomy of myth and language, in which I critique the view that myth is a failed form of language, and I explicate in detail the relation of myth to science. In chapter eight I address the problem of autonomy at a larger scale. First, I address the various senses of autonomy, i.e. independence, the free-signification of the imagination, and self-determination. Following this elucidation, I show how myth, language, and science can each maintain their autonomy while simultaneously being vertically ordered into a hierarchy of cultural forms. Objective Six Very little attention has been paid to Ernst Cassirer’s philosophy of mythology. While the Schelling and Heidegger connection has been deeply investigated, almost no attention has been given to Schelling’s influence on Cassirer’s thought. In order to address this lacuna in the literature I have given special focus on the way that Cassirer transformed Schelling’s project in chapters two through four. The whole book addresses the relative neglect of Cassirer research, for the whole book illuminates the importance of Cassirer’s humanism, and the way that culture can function as a path to human freedom. This progressive story of human freedom is discussed at length in chapter eight.

24607618.label: Major findings and research outcome
24607618.value: I completed a book entitled The Mythical Absolute: Schelling, Cassirer, and the Autonomy of Mythology. The book is under review with SUNY press. Two chapters of this book have been published: “The Mythical Dialetheism: The Symbolic Absolute,” and “The Place of the Sacred in Cassirer’s Philosophy of Mythology.” I collaborated with many leading scholars. I attended conferences and organized conferences, including “Negative Philosophy" and “The Philosophy of Mythology in the Continental Tradition.” The first formed the basis of a peer-reviewed edited volume with Springer that engaged Cassirer and Neo-Kantian philosophy, entitled The Being of Negation in Post-Kantian Philosophy. The second conference formed the basis of a peer reviewed volume (Mythologizing the Absolute: Studies in the Philosophy of Mythology), that will appear in the prestigious series, Reality and Hermeneutics, with Mohr Siebeck, 2024. Chapter five of the book manuscript will also appear in this book. With two edited volumes, two papers published in prestigious journals, and one book manuscript, the ECS project has been a resounding success. After integrating Schelling’s influence on Cassirer, I realized that a revised concept of Cassirer’s symbolic philosophy of culture could be employed to solve some contemporary problems in philosophy. As a result, I reorganized the book in order to show how Cassirer’s philosophy of culture could solve this problem. The Mythical Absolute argues that philosophy is fundamentally oriented towards absolute knowing. This vision of philosophy, deeply inspired by the tradition of German Idealism, leads philosophy into paradox, for absolute thinking ultimately leads philosophy into contradiction. Due to this paradox, some contemporary philosophers have cast doubt on the existence of the absolute. In order to respond to these challenges, The Mythical Absolute calls for philosophy to re-think the absolute as a true contradiction. The book explores two plausible species of absolute dialetheism: rational and mystical dialetheism. The book argues against rational dialetheism, and its main proponent, G.W.F Hegel. The book advances the claim of the mystical variety, and demonstrates that mystical dialetheism is mythical in form. The Mythical Absolute explores the form of myth by investigating F.W.J. Schelling and Ernst Cassirer’s tautegorical interpretations of mythology. The book also engages with Fichte and Hegel, and re-configures their thinking within an inquiry into the mythical absolute. In the course of the investigation, the relation of myth to other forms of culture is explored. The Mythical Absolute investigates the relationship between myth and various concepts, including the sacred and the profane, metaphor, freedom and determinism, self-consciousness, polytheism and monotheism. The philosophical discussions are always connected to issues of relevance to important topics in cultural anthropology. In its concluding chapters, the book integrates the insights of Schelling and Cassirer on myth into a symbolic metaphysics of the Absolute, that calls upon philosophy to reimagine the world in mythical terms.

24607618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24607618.value: The Mythical Absolute laid the groundwork for future research on the phenomenology of other minds and the recurrence of myth in the secular world. This research has demonstrated that consciousness of myth is grounded in the expressive function. This same function is operative in the perceptual experience of other minds. Because the bodily expression of the other person is the sign that signifies the presence of the person, and the person appears in a way that is indistinguishable from their bodily expression, the experience of the other person conforms to the form of expression whereby the sign=signified. This is the same function at work in the mythical law, or the equivalence of the members of a relation. Because the experience of other minds conforms to the expressive function, even when mythical culture has vanished from human life, forms of mythical culture have the potential to reappear in different forms. Because the expressive function of objectification is never fully absent, Cassirer’s theory of myth is fully able to account for the reappearance and transformation of mythical forms. My future research will focus on how Cassirer's philosophy of mythology can account for the re-appearance of myth in various forms of cultural life.

24607618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24607618.value: The research project, Ernst Cassirer and the Autonomy of Mythology, investigates the nature of mythology. It investigates and answers the question "what is myth?" The research investigated myth on a global scale. On the one hand, the project employed philosophy to provide a conceptual structure in which to organize the empirical data on myth provided by empirical anthropology. On the other hand, the project showed how myth is necessary for human beings to have a successful conception of the world. The latter is of great import, for all human beings have an interest in their place in the world. Without such a world-conception, the human being cannot orient themselves in the world. Thus, the research project is of value to human life, because it investigates the way that myth provides human beings with a principle by which they can orient themselves in the world.

24611118.value: 該研究項目（以下簡稱“該項目”）的目的在於探索關於 - 設計“允許之前稅務不合規的納稅人改正其稅務”的專案所應考慮的因素。許多國家已經採用了稅務特赦及自願性披露的專案（以下簡稱“規則化專案”），並且這些專案的規則之間有很大的差別。由於對稅收、執行措施以及合規程度有影響，稅務不合規的規則化是一個重要的公共政策事項。儘管許多國家面臨著如何規範稅務不合規的困境，OECD的指引及相關學術文獻對那些考慮制定新的規則化專案或修改現行政策的政府所給予的幫助少之又少。 該項目的第一部分旨在填補文獻關於如何設計規則化專案的空白。規則化專案的相關文獻通常只比較特赦模式和非特赦模式，而忽略了一個重要的事實 — 沒有規則化專案的國家經常減免對那些自願披露過去稅務不合規的納稅人的懲罰。這將會在下文的分析中與關鍵性的設計考量因素，如，永久性規則化專案的合意性一起再行探討。這部分將會給政府提供在發展及評估其規則化專案時所應考慮的建議及因素。 該項目第二部分的比較法律分析將對不同國家所代表的，不同的稅務不合規的規則化方式作出檢驗。分析將專注於這些國家所採用的專案的性質和特點，以及他們如何配合及融入相應的稅務系統。這一比較法律分析可能會顯示出不同國家在設計其規則化專案時的相似性及差異。這篇分析亦可被政府及學者用於探索不同的規則化模式，以及學習他國的相關經驗。 基於前述各部分的結論，該項目的第三部分將分析中國是否應該採用正式的規則化專案，如是的話，應該怎樣架構。和許多國家不同，中國至今未有制定關於稅務不合規的正式規則化專案。在接下來的幾年，對過去稅務不合規的規則化將在中國越來越重要，因其將會透過“促進自動資訊交換的國際規則”的執行來顯著提升自身的稅法執行力。這一規則化專案的設計將體現中國稅務體系的特點。

24611118.label: Realisation of objectives
24611118.value: The discussion below explains how these objectives were achieved in the research outputs of this project: 1. Noam Noked, Viktoria Wöhrer & Pierce Lai, Formal vs. Informal Voluntary Disclosure Policies, AMERICAN JOURNAL OF COMPARATIVE LAW (forthcoming 2023) This publication offers a comparative study of voluntary disclosure policies of various jurisdictions. It finds that nearly all countries provide noncompliant taxpayers with opportunities to rectify their noncompliance voluntarily and receive reduced penalties. This article identifies three broad categories of voluntary disclosure policies: formal and permanent voluntary disclosure programs, repeated temporary voluntary disclosure schemes, and informal voluntary disclosure practices. Importantly, the article finds that the tax authorities in countries with no formal voluntary disclosure programs frequently follow informal voluntary disclosure practices that operate as de facto substitutes for formal policies. This comparative study satisfies the second objective as it provides a comparative legal analysis of regularization programs in different countries, examining the characteristics and features of these programs in the context of the relevant tax systems. This publication also develops a set of recommendations and considerations that governments should consider when designing and assessing their regularization programs and policies. Building on the findings of the comparative analysis, the article explores the tax policy considerations in the design of voluntary disclosure policies and the choice between formal and informal voluntary policies. The article analyzes several tax policy considerations, including participation incentives, fairness, transparency, implementation and compliance costs, coordination with non-tax regulators, and other design considerations. This achieves the first objective of the project. This article has been accepted for publication in the American Journal of Comparative Law, which is internationally recognized as the preeminent peer-reviewed journal for comparative legal studies. This journal is ranked 1/37 in Comparative Law in the Washington & Lee (W&L) Law Journal Rankings. It has “A” rating in the Australian Business Deans Council (ABDC) Journal Quality List. The article was co-authored by the PI together with Dr. Viktoria Wöhrer (then-Postdoctoral Fellow at CUHK Law) & Pierce Lai (then-Research Assistant at CUHK Law). 2. Philip Marcovici & Noam Noked, Cooperative Compliance for Individuals and Trusts: A Proposal for a Compliance Passport, 6 JOURNAL OF TAX ADMINISTRATION 33 (2021) A summarized version of this article was published as follows: Philip Marcovici & Noam Noked, Passports, please!, 5 STEP JOURNAL 60-61 (Oct. 18, 2021). This publication further advances the first objective by developing a novel proposal for a voluntary cooperative compliance program for individuals, family trusts, and private investment vehicles. Under the proposed program, the authorities of the relevant jurisdictions would determine, on a joint basis, whether the participant is in full compliance with their tax obligations and whether there are any money laundering concerns. The implementation of this proposal could enhance a culture of cooperative compliance and free up enforcement resources. For participants, it could improve privacy, increase certainty, and reduce compliance costs and distortions. As this proposal has the potential to ensure compliance while reducing costs and risks for both tax authorities and taxpayers, it deserves serious consideration. This publication appeared in the Journal of Tax Administration, which is a reputable peer-reviewed journal focusing on the study of tax administration issues. It was co-authored by the PI and Philip Marcovici, a prominent expert in international tax, wealth management, and family trusts. He is the former chair of the European tax practice of Baker McKenzie. To expand the reach of this proposal, the PI and Mr Marcovici published a summarized version of this article in the STEP Journal, which is the journal of the Society of Trust and Estate Practitioners (STEP). STEP is an international professional organization with more than 21,000 members in 96 countries, comprising trustees, wealth planners, lawyers, accountants, and other professionals in the trust and wealth management industry. The PI and Mr Marcovici made a submission based on the proposal in this article as part of a public consultation of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) in August 2021. The FATF is the international policymaking organization that develops standards for anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing. Following this submission, the PI and Mr Marcovici were invited to participate and give comments in an online meeting (by invitation only) with the FATF and other stakeholders. This meeting took place in November 2021. 3. Noam Noked & Yan Xu, Proposal for Voluntary Disclosure Procedures in China, 6 JOURNAL OF TAX ADMINISTRATION 190 (2020) 4. Noam Noked & Yan Xu, A Voluntary Disclosure Mechanism: Theory, Practice and the Path in China, INTERNATIONAL TAXATION IN CHINA (2022) (in Chinese) These publications satisfy the third objective by providing a proposal for the optimal regularization of tax noncompliance in China, aiming to increase tax revenues and compliance. These publications explore voluntary disclosure policies and practices in China. They show that while China does not have formal nationwide voluntary disclosure procedures, Chinese tax authorities frequently reduce or waive penalties for taxpayers who voluntarily disclose their noncompliance and settle their unpaid taxes. This article calls for the adoption of nationwide voluntary disclosure procedures in China and explores the design considerations of such procedures. These publications were co-authored by the PI and Prof. Yan Xu (formerly an Associate Professor at CUHK Law and now at UNSW). To increase the potential impact of these publications, the PI and Prof. Xu sent them (in English and Chinese) together with cover letters to senior officials of the State Taxation Administration, China’s tax authority. The PI also shared the publications with other experts and relevant organizations. Following that, the Hong Kong Branch of STEP also sent the paper to senior officials of the State Taxation Administration and suggested that they consider the proposal for formal voluntary disclosure policies in China.

24611118.label: Major findings and research outcome
24611118.value: Increasing tax collection is a major challenge for many governments. In addition to enforcement efforts to detect and deter noncompliance, governments have long tried to incentivize noncompliant taxpayers to rectify their noncompliance voluntarily. For that purpose, most countries have adopted a general voluntary disclosure program. However, several countries — including China and other large economies — have not done so. This project examines how noncompliant taxpayers can correct their tax affairs in countries that do not have formal voluntary disclosure policies. It also explores the tax policy considerations that countries should consider when designing their voluntary disclosure policies. This project provides a comparative study of voluntary disclosure policies in 25 countries that do not have formal voluntary disclosure programs. It shows that many of these countries implement practices that reduce or waive penalties for voluntary disclosure filers. Some countries have adopted repeated temporary voluntary disclosure schemes. The result is that nearly all countries provide noncompliant taxpayers with opportunities to voluntarily rectify their noncompliance and receive reduced penalties. The observations that nearly all countries reduce penalties for voluntary disclosure filers and that informal practices operate in certain countries as de facto substitutes for formal voluntary disclosure programs have important policy implications. The project analyzes several tax policy considerations such as participation incentives, fairness, transparency, implementation and compliance costs, coordination with non-tax regulators, and other design considerations. This analysis shows that formal schemes have several advantages over informal practices. The project offers an in-depth analysis of China’s voluntary disclosure policies. It shows that while China does not have a nationwide voluntary disclosure policy, the Chinese tax authorities have been following voluntary disclosure practices under which taxpayers who voluntarily disclose their past noncompliance and pay the required taxes are subject to reduced or no penalties. Local tax authorities have been following voluntary disclosure practices that vary across localities. The project calls for the adoption of nationwide voluntary disclosure procedures by the State Taxation Administration and discusses key design features of such procedures. The project also develops a novel proposal for a voluntary cooperative compliance program for individuals and family trusts. Under the proposed program, the authorities of the relevant jurisdictions would determine, on a joint basis, whether the participant is in full compliance with their tax obligations and whether there are any money laundering concerns. The implementation of this proposal could enhance a culture of cooperative compliance and free up enforcement resources.

24611118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24611118.value: More research is needed on the optimal design of voluntary disclosure policies. This project shows that the tax policy question which has been the focus of the literature — whether governments should reduce penalties for voluntary disclosure filers — has been answered in the affirmative by nearly all countries. Thus, a key question for future research is the optimal design of voluntary disclosure policies. The PI intends to build on this project to further analyze this question in future publications. The PI is currently working on an article focusing on design features (other than the penalty level) that affect the incentives to file a voluntary disclosure. More work is also required in assessing the voluntary disclosure policies of specific countries. This project provides a detailed country-specific analysis of China. Future work could follow this approach by offering in-depth analyses and recommendations for more countries. The PI will continue working on these important aspects of tax administration and compliance

24611118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24611118.value: Some people fail to comply with their tax obligations. In addition to trying to detect and penalize noncompliant taxpayers, many governments implement policies to encourage noncompliant persons to report their noncompliance voluntarily and get back into full compliance. These policies are typically referred to as voluntary disclosure programs. Voluntary disclosure filers are usually subject to lower penalties than noncompliant taxpayers who got caught. However, several countries including China do not have voluntary disclosure programs. How can taxpayers rectify noncompliance in these countries? By studying the practices in 25 countries with no formal programs, this project shows that nearly all countries provide opportunities to rectify noncompliance voluntarily and receive reduced penalties. The project contends that, from a societal perspective, formal voluntary disclosure policies have several advantages over informal practices: they are fairer, more transparent, more cost-effective, and provide stronger incentives to participate. The project offers an in-depth analysis of China’s voluntary disclosure policies. It calls for the adoption of nationwide voluntary disclosure procedures and discusses key design features of such procedures. Lastly, the project develops a novel proposal for a voluntary cooperative compliance program for individuals and family trusts which could enhance a culture of cooperative compliance and free up enforcement resources.

24612618.label: Major findings and research outcome
24612618.value: I have written six research papers based on funding for this project, five of which have been published. The first paper investigates the role of informal networks in shaping economic falsification behaviors of Chinese local leaders. I find that local leaders with informal ties with higher-level officials are actually less likely to falsify. The second paper, building on a dataset created with the support of this project's funding, studies the economic and informational effect of leadership rotation in China. This paper is published in Journal of Development Economics. The third paper, published at British Journal of Political Science, studies how anticorruption campaign affects the quality of bureaucratic selection. The key finding is that forceful anticorruption may actually hurt bureaucratic quality by scaring away the more competent candidates. The fourth paper, published at Journal of Politics, studies the patterns of leadership style in China. I find that there exist two distinct leadership styles: an assertive, autocratic style that focuses on centralized decision-making and efficient execution and a relatively soft, collegial style that respects dissent and fosters intraelite collaboration. We further show that these two leadership styles are associated with distinct governing strategies and that they both offer viable, but different, paths to political survival. In the fifth paper, my coauthor and I examine the role of informal networks in shaping local officials' incentives in utilizing information about economic reforms. Using the liberalization of land market as a case, we show that officials with connections to higher-level authority are more likely to adopt land market reforms in face of mounting social pressure. This paper has been published in Journal of Politics. The sixth paper, which is published in Journal of Public Economics, studies the role of informal networks in shaping the distribution of fiscal transfers. My coauthor and I show that the allocation of intergovernmental transfer in China is in part shaped by vertical patron-client ties within the Chinese government, and that distributive favoritism is in part driven by greater interest alignment between higher and lower level governments. In addition to the research paper, I have also developed an original dataset on local economic falsification in China. This dataset uses GMM method to estimate the rate of actual economic growth based on presumably less manipulatable metrics such as nighttime brightness, electricity consumption, and railway freight. This dataset has the potential to enable researchers to investigate various determinants of falsification behavior in China.

24612618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24612618.value: In the next step, I will use the dataset to explore various other potential determinants of economic falsification and information distortion in China. For example, I'm currently working on a project that studies how a major statistical reporting reform that occurred after 2006 might have changed the incentive to misreport. I will also investigate how local leaders' personal background, such as their past career trajectories and promotion incentives, shape information distortion behaviors.

24612618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24612618.value: The findings of the project suggest that information distortion exists in many parts of the Chinese systems. Some of the distortions appear to have substantive economic and policy consequences. To counteract information distortion requires a combination of formal institutional building and information political maneuver.

24614518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24614518.value: Over recent decades, labor migration from less to more developed regions has been growing rapidly. More than 12% (8.5 million) of the female global migrant workforce are employed as foreign domestic workers (FDWs) in 2015. However, these FDWs are often vulnerable and deprived. They usually have alien status within the legal framework of the host countries, and their employment conditions are of particular concern. Given the complex legal, socio-cultural and economic issues related to FDWs, most of the existing research has focused on the policy and legal mechanisms of employment, the impact on their transnational families and children being left behind, as well as the gender, racial and class discrimination being encountered. However, there has been inadequate research work on the health and well-being of FDWs, despite clear evidence that they are at risk to adverse working conditions, deprivation and exploitation. While there have been studies that have investigated the association between employment conditions and health of FDWs, there is little population evidence particularly in Hong Kong which hosts a large population of FDWs. Although much of the evidence based on qualitative research have provided insights of living and working conditions of FDWs, unfortunately, these findings cannot be generalized at the population level or used for designing appropriate policy and program interventions. On the other hand, the existing quantitative data on FDWs are limited in terms of population coverage and representativeness. Furthermore, the types of questions asked in the surveys do not adequately capture the health and well-being outcomes of FDWs along with other essential social and economic information. The proposed study will address these research gaps by quantifying and disentangling the risk of employment conditions on physical and mental health outcomes of FDWs. This proposed study will implement a multi-stage cluster random sampling survey and will interview 2,000 FDWs. The analysis will identify the statistical association between different aspects of employment conditions (i.e., working/living conditions and material circumstances) and physical and mental health status among FDWs, and also examine whether social and family networks moderate the associations. The study will contribute to identifying the important risks and exposure of FDWs to adverse physical and mental health outcomes, and generating evidence for designing appropriate public policies and health promotion interventions to improve the quality of life and well-being of this uniquely vulnerable subgroup of migrant population. 近幾十年來，從發展中地區遷移到已發展地區的勞動人口急劇上升。在2015年，12%以上（即大概八百五十萬）的全球女性移民勞動人口受僱為外籍家庭傭工（外傭）。可是，這些外傭屬於社經資源較匱乏的弱勢群體。她們通常亦在當地（即工作的地區）的法律框架下只擁有外籍人士的身份地位，而她們的受雇狀況尤其受到關注。 正因為有關外傭的法律、社會文化及經濟問題存在相當的複雜性，大部份現存的研究都把焦點放在有關雇傭的政策與條例、遷移對被留下來的家人與子女的影響以及她們所遇到的性別、種族及階級的歧視之上。雖然有明顯跡象顯示外傭有頗大風險需要面對不利的工作環境、匱乏及剝削，但對於外傭的健康與生活福祉的研究卻非常不足。就算探討外傭的受雇狀況與健康的關係的研究確實存在，但在香港這個許多外傭居住的地方，基於普遍總體外傭人口作出的研究實證卻欠奉。儘管頗多的質性研究實證也對外傭的生活及工作環境提供了見解，可惜那些結果均不能夠被概括到一個普遍總體外傭人口的層面，更遑論可以用作設計適切的介入政策及計劃。再者，現有關於外傭的量性數據在人口的覆蓋面及代表性也頗為有限。此外，現有量性調查未能同時搜集外傭的健康狀況、生活福祉以及社經背景的關鍵資料。所以，本研究計劃將會把外傭的受雇狀況對她們身心健康的影響量化並作出梳理，以填補以上所提及的研究不足。 本研究計劃將會使用多重類聚隨機抽樣的調查方法，訪問2,000名外傭。分析將會對外傭的各種受雇狀況（即工作／居住環境及物質狀況）與其身心健康之間的相關性進行評估，並檢驗社會及家庭網絡會否對這些相關性產生調節效應。 本研究將會識別出不利於外傭身心健康的重要風險因素，並獲取經驗數據以利於設計適切的公共政策及健康促進計劃，從而提升這個尤為弱勢的移民群體的健康與生活質素。

24614518.label: Realisation of objectives
24614518.value: As described in the amended proposal, data was collected in two ways. The first method used a systematic random sampling approach where migrant domestic workers (MDWs) were recruited face-to-face in popular MDW gathering areas outdoors on Sunday, their usual day off. Due to strict social distancing restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic we adopted a second method by recruiting MDWs online through social media platforms. To minimize the face-to-face interaction time in the first method and remain consistent in the survey completion format of the second method, both methods used an online platform to complete the survey. In total we collected 1965 completed surveys between August 2020 and August 2021. The online survey collected the respondents’: (1) Background information; (2) characteristics of the employer’s home and basic information of the employer’s family; (3) questions related to the respondents’ employment conditions, material circumstances, psychosocial factors (i.e. job satisfaction and stress), lifestyle factors, social network, and social support received; (4) health status including anxiety using General Anxiety Disorder-7 scale, depression using Patient Health Questionnaire-9 scale, and quality of life using EQ5D-5L. The survey yields quantitative results corresponding to Objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Objectives 2 through 5 were achieved in full. Challenges in fully achieving Objective 1 and the measures taken to overcome it are discussed below; nonetheless, with the refined methodology, Objective 1 was also achieved. To measure the impact of employment conditions on MDWs’ health, 17 items covering the physical environment at home/work, workload, material circumstances such as adequate food and wages, and their experiences on exploitation and abuse by employers were asked. A summative employment conditions score (ECS) was computed (scored 0 to 17) whereby a higher score indicated poorer employment conditions (Cronbach’s alpha=0.73 for the 17-item scale). Based on the distribution of the ECS, respondents were grouped into three levels of working conditions. Those whose ECS was less than the interquartile range (IQR) (those reporting no adverse work conditions) were classified as having “good” working conditions. Those in the interquartile range were classified as having “average” working conditions, while those reporting ECS greater than IQR were classified as having “poor” working conditions. As mentioned in the first paragraph above, the strict social distancing restrictions imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic required us to adopt a second sampling method in addition to our original probability sampling method. The second method used a non-probability approach which does not allow us to generalize our findings to the entire MDW population of Hong Kong or provide representative estimates for the physical and mental health of our population (Objective 1). To address this, we have weighted our data based on 2020 census population estimates to reflect the age distribution of female MDWs in Hong Kong. For mental health, as recommended for female MDWs by Garabiles et al., 2020, we reported depression and probable anxiety using cut-off scores of ≥ 6 and ≥ 7, respectively. For physical health, the EQ5D-5L quality of life measure was used. This measure asks respondents to rate their health today under five domains (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression) on a 5-point scale from no problem (=1) to severe problems (=5). The EQ5D measure also ask respondents to rate their health today on a scale from 0 (worst health) to 100 (best health). The scales for anxiety, depression, and self-rated health were used for Objectives 3, 4, and 5. To address Objective 2, we included the employer’s home size as a proxy for employer’s socioeconomic status and number of members in the employer’s home to represent employer’s demographic background. Chi-square tests for both variables were tabulated in a crosstabs table to assess their associations with the employment conditions score. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess Objective 3. Objectives 4 and 5 were completed using PROCESS macro for SPSS which can test the mediating and moderating factors while treating the independent variable as multicategorical (as mentioned above). Reference: Garabiles MR, Lao CK, Yip P, Chan EWW, Mordeno I, Hall BJ. Psychometric Validation of PHQ-9 and GAD-7 in Filipino Migrant Domestic Workers in Macao (SAR), China. J Pers Assess. 2020;102(6):833–44.

24614518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24614518.value: Objective 1 Among 1965 respondents, 81% were Filipino and 19% Indonesian. Within the study sample, 31.8% were classified with depression and 17.1% with probable anxiety. From the EQ5D-5L measure, those reporting some problem, compared with no problem, in each domain were mobility 13.3%, self-care 5.5%, usual activities 9.8%, pain/discomfort 35.4%, and anxiety/depression 25.5%. The mean self-rated health score was 81.5 (standard deviation 20.4). Objective 2 An increase in employer’s home size was statistical-significantly and negatively associated with an increase in negative employment conditions. Employers with a family size of 5 or more people, compared to those with 4 or less, was significantly associated with increased negative employment conditions. Objective 3 Among the 17 items included in the employment conditions score, the most frequently reported conditions were 1) ever needing to work before being able to begin day off (31.9%), 2) having overcrowded home environments or lack of privacy (26.9%), 3) not always getting enough to eat (24.1%), 4) ever being woken up and asked to work in the middle of the night (23.2%), and 5) working on average 16 or more hours per day in the past month (20.8%). While controlling for sociodemographic variables, when compared with good employment conditions, those with average and poor employment conditions were statistical-significantly associated with increased anxiety and depressive symptoms and decreased self-rated health. Objective 4 & 5 Levels of stress and job satisfaction were both considered as psychosocial factors which may mediate the association between employment conditions and physical and mental health. Both factors significantly mediated the association between employment conditions score and anxiety, depression, and self-rated health. In each model, stress more strongly mediated the association between employment conditions score and the outcome. An increase in stress indirectly and significantly increased anxiety and depressive symptoms and decreased self-rated health. An increase in job satisfaction indirectly decreased anxiety and depressive symptoms and increased self-rated health. Employment conditions score was significantly directly associated with each of the outcomes in the mediation analysis. However, social support was not found to significantly moderate any of these associations. All analyses controlled for sociodemographic variables. A manuscript presenting results of employment conditions and mental health with the mediating roles of stress and job satisfaction has been submitted to Journal of Occupational Health Psychology (IF 7.707, JIF Q1 in Public Health, Environment, and Occupational Health - SSCI). Confirmation of publication will be forwarded to RGC upon manuscript acceptance.

24614518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24614518.value: We have currently submitted one manuscript on the topic of employment conditions and mental health to Journal of Occupational Health Psychology and plan to submit three more manuscripts shortly, namely 1) employment conditions and health-related quality of life, 2) caregiving intensity and distress, and 3) perceived discrimination and mental health. Further development of the research may include qualitative interviews or a Delphi study with stakeholders across the MDW community to assess the feasibility of different solutions to address the findings in our project. These stakeholders could include academics, local policymakers, leaders of MDW-focused NGOs, healthcare workers, and religious leaders within the MDW community. Our project also revealed the usefulness for creating a validated employment conditions scale for MDWs internationally. Developing such a scale could provide a quick battery to assess MDWs employment conditions status and their risk to adverse health conditions. This scale could also be used to more directly compare the conditions of MDWs in different countries and regions. Finally, a more ambitious longitudinal approach, preferably before, during, and after migration could be done to better understand the health of this population throughout the course of their migration; however, this project will require significantly greater human and financial resources.

24614518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24614518.value: This project assessed the impact employment conditions on the health of female migrant domestic workers (MDW) in Hong Kong. Hong Kong hosts approximately 370,000 MDWs, making up 5% of the total Hong Kong population. This population is unique in that they must live and work in their employer’s home, creating vulnerabilities. We found that MDWs in Hong Kong reported working long hours each week averaging 12.6 hours per day (6 days per week = 75.6 hours/week). Other negative employment conditions include needing to work before being able to begin day off, overcrowding at home or lack of privacy, occasional food deprivation, and waking up in the middle of the night to work. When we looked at the number of negative employment conditions this population faced, an increase in negative conditions also significantly increased their anxiety and depressive symptoms and decreased their self-rated health. Levels of stress and job satisfaction both partially explained the association between employment conditions and health. However, differing levels of social support did not have an effect on these associations. Better understanding the impact employment conditions has on the health of MDWs can help inform policies that can safeguard the health and well-being of this population.

24614818.label: Realisation of objectives
24614818.value: Of the 192 survivors who were screened for eligibility, 175 fulfilled the inclusion criteria and were invited to participate in the study. Subsequently, 158 survivors completed the assessments. After excluding 6 of those survivors because of missing diagnosis or treatment protocol information, the data of 152 survivors were analyzed. A subset of 102 adult survivors provided blood samples for the analysis of plasma inflammatory biomarkers, which included interleukin (IL)-8, IL-13, interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), macrophage inflammatory protein-1β, and tumor necrosis factor-α. In summary, all of the 4 research objectives have been met during the study period. Problems encountered and deviations from the original plan: 1. Change in neurocognitive tools (stated in progress report in March 2020) Our original intention is to use the NIH Toolbox to assess survivors’ neurocognitive outcomes. Certain tests within NIH Toolbox are not language dependent. Hence, we need permission from the developers to translate the instructions into Chinese. We have contacted NIH Toolbox (Washington DC, USA) to request for their permission in late 2018. However, we faced problems with receiving timely responses from them (Our earlier correspondences with them in late 2018 took almost 4 months). The developers mentioned that there is another group in mainland China who is translating the instructions, therefore we are not allowed to embark on another set of Chinese instructions. Deviation: We changed the NIH Toolbox to a traditional battery of neurocognitive tests. - Attention: Conners’ Continuous Performance Test (CPT) - Executive function: Trail Making Test A and B - Visual-motor processing speed: Grooved Pegboard - Memory: Modified Taylor Complex Figure (MTCF) - Behavioral function: Child/Adult Behavior Checklist List These tests have been previously used for research in the Chinese population with reference norms available from published literature or manuals; we reckoned that it is reasonable to replace the NIH Toolbox with these tests. 2. Recruitment of controls (stated in progress report in March 2020) Our initial plan was to recruit controls as the NIH toolbox has not been widely utilized within the Chinese population, and there is no published reference norms. However, the budget has been revised by RGC prior to initiation of this study on Jan 1, 2019. Therefore, the revised budget did not allow recruitment of controls (especially pediatric controls) as it would require additional manpower and resources. Deviation: We are no longer using the NIH toolbox for neurocognitive assessment. The revised neurocognitive battery consists of tests that have been widely used with published reference norms in the literature. This change has also been reflected under 5.2 “Revised objectives”. We recalculated the sample size and expanded the sample size to 150 survivors. We faced challenges with recruitment during the pandemic; however, we managed to achieve the targeted sample size (actual number of survivors recruited: 158). On hindsight, it was a wise decision to use reference/published norms (instead of prospectively recruiting controls) because it would have been very challenging to invite non-cancer controls to visit the Prince of Wales Hospital for research procedures during the pandemic in 2020/2021. Admittedly, the lack of a non-cancer control group is a major limitation for the assessment of chronic stress in Objective 2. However, it is well known in the literature that a compromised health status (as reflected by higher chronic stress levels and higher rate of chronic health conditions) is more prevalent among survivors of cancer than the non-cancer population. Therefore, we can still draw meaningful findings from our association analysis between chronic stress and cognitive/behavioral outcomes among survivors.

24614818.label: Major findings and research outcome
24614818.value: Objective 1: (published/discussed in Section C: Publications 1 to 3) 1.1 At an average of 17.2 years post-cancer diagnosis, survivors performed more poorly than the reference norms on measures of motor processing speed, memory, executive function, and attention. A minority of survivors demonstrated impairments in memory (9.2%), motor processing speed (36.2%), executive function (8.5%) and attention (4.0%-10.5%). 1.2 Compared with the age- and sex-matched norms, the survivors reported significantly more issues with all measures of behavioral functioning. The proportions of survivors who reported symptoms of inattention and internalizing and externalizing problems ranged from 7.9% to 17.1%. Approximately a quarter reported a sluggish cognitive tempo (23.7%). Objective 2: (published/discussed in Section C: Publications 1 to 4) 2.1 Survivors who developed chronic health conditions had more executive dysfunction than those who did not have any chronic conditions. 2.2 Survivors within top tertiles of interferon-γ and interleukin-13 demonstrated more inattentiveness. Higher monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 was associated with worse attention outcomes. More self-reported anxiety/depressive and internalizing problems correlated with higher interleukin-8. Objective 3: (published/discussed in Section C: Publications 1 to 3) 3.1 For neurocognitive outcomes, survivors who resided in <600 square feet of housing space (indicator of lower socioeconomic status) had worse performances in memory and motor processing speed than survivors who resided in larger housing spaces. Worse family functioning was associated with more executive dysfunction. 3.2 For behavioral outcomes, poorer family functioning was strongly associated with all measures on the syndrome scales. A higher level of physical inactivity was correlated with more self-reported symptoms of inattention and a sluggish cognitive tempo. Survivors who were more fatigued reported significantly worse outcomes on all measures of the syndrome scale. Among the subset of survivors who were current students, academic stress was associated with multiple domains of behavioral functioning. Objective 4: (published/discussed in Section C: Publication 2) 4.1 Mediation analysis showed that chronic health conditions were associated with self-reported attention problems indirectly through fatigue. Similar results were obtained for other behavioral measures. Summary: 1. At more than 10 years after cancer diagnosis, a subgroup of childhood ALL survivors of childhood ALL in Hong Kong demonstrated significant neurocognitive impairment and behavioral problems. 2. These functional impairment might be mediated by the socioenvironmental factors (family functioning, living environment, academic stress and physical inactivity). 3. Survivors with compromised health status, as reflected by the presence of chronic health conditions and higher levels of stress biomarkers, appeared to be more vulnerable to neurocognitive impairment and behavioral symptoms.

24614818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24614818.value: 1. While it may not be possible to fully eliminate the neurotoxic effects of cancer treatment, our results suggest that survivors may benefit from appropriate interventions to address modifiable risk factors, such as the provision of social support to families and interventions to encourage survivors to adopt a physically active lifestyle. - We are actively working with local NGOs (Little Life Warriors Society and Children's Cancer Foundation) to optimize social support for survivors of childhood cancer. - One of the collaborators have submitted a GRF grant (2021/2022 cycle) to evaluate the effect of mindfulness therapy on reducing stress and improving functional outcomes in survivors. 2. Chronic health conditions and systemic inflammation may potentially be mechanistic mediators of neurocognitive and behavioral symptoms in survivors. Future work includes understanding the underlying pathophysiology behind functional outcomes in survivors. - We have successfully obtained another GRF grant (Ref: 14605421) to investigate the mechanistic effect of "premature aging" (ie. analysis of telomere length and frailty assessment) on cognitive and behavioral outcomes in survivors. This study is ongoing. If markers of aging are associated with cognitive/ behavioral outcomes, they can potentially be applied to assess or monitor the success of both pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions, particularly behavioral interventions.

24614818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24614818.value: Survivors of childhood leukemia may develop cognitive impairment (e.g. trouble remembering, learning new things, concentrating, or decision-making) and psychological symptoms due to their previous cancer experience and treatment. This study recruited 152 Chinese survivors of childhood leukemia who completed cognitive/behavioral assessments at the Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong. We found that at more than 10 years after cancer diagnosis, around 10% to 25% of the survivors displayed cognitive impairment and behavioral problems, such as depression/anxiety symptoms and sluggish cognitive tempo. The survivors who developed chronic health conditions (e.g. heart, hormonal and neurological complications) had worse attention performance and self-reported behavioral problems than survivors who did not. Higher circulating levels of inflammatory markers (an indicator of poorer health status) were found in the blood of survivors with cognitive and behavioral impairment. Other than clinical and biological risk factors, poorer functional deficits were observed in survivors who were more physically inactive, fatigued or resided in poor living environment. Overall, our findings suggest that health behavior and socio-environment factors may be potentially modifiable risk factors associated with functional outcomes in survivors. Regular monitoring of behavioral function should be performed on survivors with compromised health status or chronic conditions.

24615218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24615218.value: Problems related to socio-spatial polarization, racial segregation, and sectarian violence trouble many cities across the world today. Considering the persistence of urbanization at a planetary scale, achieving and sustaining peaceful coexistence of culturally distinct urban communities is more urgent a task than ever. World cities are especially important sites for studying various histories, politics, and everyday manifestations of multicultural coexistence due to larger and more differentiated populations living in dense urban settings of such places. An important hub of global finance and trade with cosmopolitan outlook, Hong Kong offers social scientists fertile ground to explore cultural diversity in world cities. The city prides itself for being a meeting place of Eastern and Western civilizations with a hybrid cultural identity. Its administration has recently implemented albeit limited measures to meet multicultural accommodation of its ethnic minorities and there is relatively little conflict between minority groups and the Chinese majority. This compares favorably with the accommodation of cultural diversity in many world cities that are struggling to achieve social cohesion. However, the ways in which different groups engage in production and negotiation of multicultural coexistence through everyday encounters, or urban conviviality, remains underexplored in studies about cultural diversity in Hong Kong. Furthermore, we know little about the role played by global discourses about multiculturalism, human rights, and anti-racism as well as transnational ideas and practices in shaping everyday encounters between the minority and majority populations. This study explores the ways in which urban spaces, global discourses about cultural diversity, and transnational ethno-religious practices partake in the production of urban conviviality in Hong Kong by looking at how young South Asian Muslim men negotiate their masculinity in everyday encounters. South Asian Muslims have been present in this city since the earliest days of the colonial rule under the United Kingdom, but they are still seen as cultural outsiders today. Contemporary debates about Hong Kong’s postcolonial future, its global connections, and ambivalent national identity revolve mainly around the territory’s uneasy reintegration to mainland China. However, accommodation of non-Chinese groups is just as important to achieve peaceful coexistence in this world city. Through a multi-method approach with a strong ethnographic component, this research will examine how young South Asian Muslim men and their Chinese interlocutors articulate multicultural belonging to Hong Kong. 24616618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24616618.value: 試論專利的價值：一個關於台灣、香港、與中國大陸無形資產估價的民族誌研究

24616618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24616618.value: This Early Career Scheme application proposes a four-year research project to study current debates and discussions over how to determine the value of a patent, a set of patents, or of the patent system as a whole. The PI will conduct a series of interviews and case studies in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, three places that share a common “Chinese” cultural background and parallel efforts to increase innovation and creativity, but have very different histories (the Communist Revolution in China, British Colonialism in Hong Kong, and Japanese colonialism combined with more recent democratization on Taiwan), legal structures, and economic positions within global supply chains. While the project begins with collecting, organizing and analyzing the variety of ways that professionals themselves evaluate the value of patents, it’s primary goal is to use these techniques and debates over their relative usefulness in order to better understand the cultural conceptions of innovation, creativity, production, economies, and the law on which these are based. Finally, the project will contribute to our larger understanding of the “knowledge economies” that the governments of each of these three legal jurisdictions are attempting to create. Significantly, this understanding will come not from logical analyses of new legal structures (like Intellectual Property itself) or economic models, but rather will complement and perhaps challenge such approaches by focusing first on the actual day to day practice of patents. 論文摘要 本研藉由分析台灣、香港、與中國大陸各自如何對單一專利、一組專利與整個專利系統估價，來理解三地對無形資產估價的方法與論述。三地一方面皆為華人社會，另一方面卻有著截然不同的歷史脈絡（特別指中國大陸與中國共產黨的統治，香港與英國殖民主義，以及台灣與日本殖民主義及其近代民主化的過程）、法律架構、以及在全球經濟中不同的生產供需位置。由於三地有著截然不同的法規架構與法律傳統，再加上三地政府同時各自積極發展參與創新，對他們的綜合比較研究可以對所謂「知識經濟」產生一個更廣泛的理解。 本研究的資料採集方法以面談法與個案分析法為主。藉由收集、組織、分係三地專利估價專業人員所使用的估值方法與論述，本研究最終目的是藉由理解這些估價技術與爭論來一窺華人社會文化與創新、創意、生產、經濟與法律間的關係。更重要的是，本研究將不是從法律慣用的邏輯觀點或者經濟模型觀點來理解如知識產權這樣一個新興移入的法律概念，而是透過日常生活實踐的視角來理解。這樣一個新的檢驗視角不僅可以補充現行對知識產權的理解，甚至還有可能挑戰單從邏輯或經濟模型視角得出的結論。

24617218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24617218.value: 混合型金融監管體系和中國股市危機 2014-2015

24617218.label: Project Objectives
24617218.value: • mapping out the authority relations and control mechanisms of China’s stock market regulatory regime during China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015; • tracing and analyzing the bail-out policy making processes and implementation mechanisms by key state agencies and how they were coordinated during China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015; • examining and assessing whether and how the hybridization of Western modern stock market arrangements with Chinese Communist Party’s traditional mechanisms of governance and control has shaped the regulatory incentives, policy initiatives and responses during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015; • generating deeper theoretical understanding on the role of the state in financial market development and how political institutions and policy regime shape the effectiveness of financial regulation;
