• tracing and analyzing the bail-out policy making processes and implementation mechanisms by key state agencies and how they were coordinated during China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015;

• examining and assessing whether and how the hybridization of Western modern stock market arrangements with Chinese Communist Party’s traditional mechanisms of governance and control has shaped the regulatory incentives, policy initiatives and responses during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015;

• generating deeper theoretical understanding on the role of the state in financial market development and how political institutions and policy regime shape the effectiveness of financial regulation;

24617218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24617218.value: The development of stock market has been a key element of China’s economic reforms. However, the complex interface of regulation and control between the Chinese party-state bureaucracy and evolving stock market remains relatively under-researched. Between 2014 and 2015, China experienced a major round of stock market boom and crash, with profound implications on China’s financial stability and regulatory reforms. While state actions featured prominently in both the upturn and downturn of this so-called “national bull market”, there has been no systematic study that examines the policy making process and implementation mechanisms in China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015. This project aims at investigating this important issue by using a mixed method to analyze the role of the state in China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015. The starting point of this project is that China’s financial governance is characterized by the combination of the imported Western stock market regulatory arrangements with China’s own Leninist tradition of governance and control, which has generated a hybrid regulatory regime with unusual policy style and processes. This project aims to contribute by: A) mapping out the authority relations and control mechanisms of China’s stock market regulatory regime during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015; B) tracing and analyzing the bail-out policy making processes and implementation mechanisms by key state agencies and how they were coordinated during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015; C) examining and assessing whether and how the hybridization of Western modern stock market arrangements with Chinese Communist Party’s traditional mechanisms of governance and control has shaped the regulatory incentives, policy initiatives and responses during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015; D) contributing to deeper theoretical understanding on the role of the state in financial market development and how political institutions and policy regime shape the effectiveness of financial regulation. On the basis of its findings, this project will generate policy implications on China’s financial regulatory reform. This project will not only contribute to the literature on the political economy of China’s reform, but also relate to the wider academic and policy debates on financial regulation and economic governance in developing countries. As the financial markets in Mainland China and Hong Kong become increasingly integrated, this project is also directly relevant to Hong Kong’s policy and market development. 股票市場的發展是中國經濟體制改革的重要組成部分，但中國政府官僚體系與迅速成長的股市在監管與控制方面的互動仍然有待進一步的研究。2014-2015年，中國股市經歷了一場嚴重的泡沫與危機，對中國金融體系的穩定和金融監管體制的改革產生了重大影響。在這場所謂“國家牛市”的形成與破滅過程中，政府的政策行為起到了舉足輕重的作用，然而對這次股市危機之中與之後的政府監管與控制行為的政策過程與執行機制，學界仍有待系統深入的研究。 本項研究旨在應用綜合型的研究方法探索中國股市2014-2015年危機之中與之後的政府行為與角色。中國的金融治理體系是一種將西方現代金融市場制度安排與中國自身的列寧主義治理與控制系統的結合。這種結合產生了一種具有獨特政策風格與過程的混合型金融監管體系。本項研究試圖在如下幾個方面做出貢獻：A）揭示和分析在2014-2015年股市危機過程中中國金融監管體系的決策關系與控制機制；B）追蹤和評估2014-2015年股市危機過程之中和之後，中國政府相關部門的救市政策過程以及執行與協調機制；C）研究和評估混合型金融監管體系如何塑造了監管方的激勵機制、政策行為與危機應對方案；D）加深對轉型經濟體中政府在金融市場發展方面作用的理解，並拓展從政治經濟學視角對中國金融監管體制的研究。 本項研究不僅將對有關中國改革的政治經濟學文獻做出貢獻，也將深入涉及更廣泛的有關發展中國家金融監管與經濟治理的學術與政策辯論。由於中國內地與香港的金融市場在不斷加深融合，本項研究的成果對香港的金融政策與市場發展也當有所助益。

24617218.label: Realisation of objectives
24617218.value: 1) The project has mapped out the overall authority relations and control mechanisms of China’s stock market regulatory regime during China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015. It characterizes the crisis-management architecture of China’s stock market regulatory regime as a hierarchical institutional network, with the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges, key financial market trade associations, including the Securities Association of China (SAC) and the Asset Management Association of China (AMAC), as well as major securities firms and asset management companies, nested under the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), which is subordinate to the State Council and ultimately the Communist Party center. Its hierarchical features are apparent both in terms of the regulatory framework and political control, which stem from the top-down authority structure of China’s party-state. However, it is not a pure administrative hierarchy dominated by vertical commands as in a traditional planning system, but a complex institutional network linking multiple layers of market participants with the central party-state bureaucracy and local governments. Major stock market financial institutions are strategically linked by equity ownership with various state institutions and non-financial state-controlled enterprises at both the central and local levels. There are extensive cadre personnel-transfers, joint-appointment and rotation among CSRC, stock exchanges, major financial intermediaries, and trade associations, creating dense network linkages that facilitate information flow, relational exchanges, and collaboration across institutions. The project has investigated the state shareholding network and personnel network of China’s major securities firms and asset management companies. Based on interviews and archival materials, it has investigated the authority relations and control mechanisms in the stock market crisis management. Due to the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown in the project period, the PI was unable to conduct fieldwork in Shanghai and Shenzhen as originally planned, so the range and depth of interviews and fieldwork were limited. As a result, the mapping results are not as granular as the PI aspires to achieve. 2) The project has systemically traced and analysed the bail-out policy making processes and implementation mechanisms by key state agencies and how they were coordinated during China’s stock market crisis 2014-2015. It has applied the process tracing method to investigate the evolution of China’s stock market crisis in 2015. Process tracing helps to uncover the stimuli that regulatory actors and market actors attend to and the outcomes that occur. It has traced and analyzed the role of the state in the origin, evolution, and management of China’s stock market crises in 2015–2016, including the policy mobilization, financial innovation, and bubble formation between 2012 and 2015; and market crashes, bailout and crisis management in 2015–2016. Due to the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown in the project period, the PI was unable to conduct fieldwork in Shanghai and Shenzhen as originally planned, so the range and depth of interviews and fieldwork were limited. As a result, the results of process tracing and analyses are not as granular as the PI aspires to achieve. 3) The project has examined and assessed whether and how the hybridization of Western modern stock market arrangements with Chinese Communist Party’s traditional mechanisms of governance and control has shaped the regulatory incentives, policy initiatives and responses during China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015. It shows that China's stock market development has been governed by an evolving hybrid regulatory regime, which has used, repurposed, and refined existing governance mechanisms of socialist state control, with new forms of financial organizations, instruments, and relations layering upon existing institutional elements. Crises and elite-bureaucracy interaction in the reform process have played key roles in shaping the momentum of institutional change in China’s stock market. It has demonstrated that the hybridity between the state and market is essential to China’s stock market regime, which manifests as the intertwining of multiple ownership, control, and governance mechanisms between the public and private, the state bureaucracy and the market. While the presence of state intervention is strong, the state no longer exerts monolithic control over resource allocation, agent incentives, and information communications in the stock market governance. To the extent that the state does directly intervene and dominate, its control has become highly porous in dealing with the increasingly complex and active stock market. Due to the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown in the project period, the PI was unable to conduct fieldwork in Shanghai and Shenzhen as originally planned, so the range and depth of interviews and fieldwork were limited. As a result, the results of analyses are not as granular as the PI aspires to achieve. 4) The project has generated deeper theoretical understanding on the role of the state in financial market development and how political institutions and policy regime shape the effectiveness of financial regulation. It contributes to an emerging body of research, which takes a political economy perspective to analyze how the organizational-institutional features of China’s financial regulatory regime shape the dynamics of its crisis governance. It draws on and further develops the Legal Theory of Finance (LTF) to analyze the hybridity in China’s stock market regulatory regime. At the heart of the LTF framework lies four interwoven propositions: (i) financial market is a rule-bound system supported by laws and institutions; (ii) finance governance is essentially a hybrid between the state and market, public and private; (iii) laws, regulatory rules, and public sector institutions can be a source of financial instability; and (iv) financial governance is inherently hierarchical. The project has assessed China’s stock market regulatory regime along these dimensions. It has identified and analysed the pathological features of regulatory elasticity dilemma, and campaign-style enforcement dilemma, which have amplified policy noises and produced turbulence in the state-market interface, leading to a destabilizing feedback loop between policy-induced market turbulence and market-induced organizational turbulence inside the regulatory bureaucracy. This project has also developed an institutional logic perspective to analyze the hybridity in China’s stock market governance, deepening the theoretical understanding on organizational responses to logic multiplicity and institutional complexity in governance, highlighting the multi-task dilemma and logic volatility in China’s stock market regulatory regime as key contributing factors in China’s stock market crisis. However, given the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown and disruption in the project period, there is still space for further theoretical development based on the empirical research. Overall, the project has an unspent balance of HK$155992.09, equivalent to 20.63% of the total budget. This is because the PI was unable to conduct fieldwork in Shanghai and Shenzhen as planned, due to the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown and disruptions in the project period.

24617218.label: Major findings and research outcome
24617218.value: • The hybridization of socialist state control with increasingly complex financial markets has generated unusual features in China’s financial regulatory regime. China’s stock market governance has shifted away from traditional administrative hierarchies to more plural and hybrid forms of ownership, control, and regulatory governance. The endogenous dilemmas of regulatory elasticity and campaign-style enforcement in China’s hybrid regulatory regime have amplified policy noises and led to a destabilizing feedback loop between policy-induced market turbulence and market-induced organizational turbulence inside the regulatory bureaucracy. • While rules apparently similar to the Western regulatory practices have become increasingly important in China’s stock market governance, the ways these rules are formulated and implemented are deeply embedded in China’s indigenous policy environment and underlying distributions of power. China’s financial regulators possess pervasive discretionary authority and face only limited oversight apart from accountability to the upper-level party-state organs. Such pervasive bureaucratic power is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it enables regulators to flexibly design, experiment, and push forward reforms and policy initiatives, but on the other hand, it also generates administrative dilemmas that distort regulatory incentives, policy processes, and market dynamics. • The hybridization of multiple logics has shaped the regulatory incentives, policy process and market dynamics in the evolution of China’s stock market crisis in 2014-2015. The continuous mixing of top-down control by the party-state and bottom-up dynamics driven by market development has given rise to the hybridization of multiple regulatory logics in governing China’s stock market, creating peculiar institutional complexity. China’s stock market governance has been trapped by the multitask regulatory dilemma with logic volatility endogenous to its hybrid regime, which poses fundamental constraints on China’s financial stability and regulatory effectiveness. In China's stock market crisis 2014-15, the state regulatory bureaucracy was caught in its own trap under organizational hybridity, logic multiplicity and institutional complexity, with messy policies and porous channels of interventions.

24617218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24617218.value: Due to the Cov-19 pandemic lockdown in the project period, the PI was unable to conduct fieldwork in Shanghai and Shenzhen as originally planned, so the range and depth of interviews and fieldwork were limited. As a result, the results of analyses are not as granular as the PI aspires to achieve. The PI can further develop its empirical research with additional interviews and fieldwork as well as theoretical analyses. The current research findings have been published in two refereed journal articles. The PI is working on expanding the two articles into a book.

24617218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24617218.value: China’s stock market experienced a major boom and bust between 2014 and 2015, with profound implications on China’s financial stability and governance reforms. This project takes a political economy perspective to analyze how the organizational-institutional features of China’s stock market regulatory regime shape the dynamics of its crisis governance. It contributes to the growing literature on the political economy of China’s stock market development, and also relates to the wider academic and policy debates on financial regulation and governance in developing countries. As the financial markets in Mainland China and Hong Kong become increasingly integrated, this project is also directly relevant to Hong Kong’s policy and stock market development.

24617318.label: Project Objectives
24617318.value: To examine the effects of caregiver-delivered affective touch on the depressive symptoms, state of attachment security, self-esteem and perceived family harmony of stroke survivors. To examine whether the effect of caregiver-delivered affective touch on depressive symptoms is mediated by attachment security among stroke survivors. 24617318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24617318.value: Depression after a stroke is multiply disabling, as it complicates the rehabilitation process, increases the risk of a recurrence and jeopardises family harmony. However, supportive interventions for stroke survivors and their family caregivers show very limited effects on reducing post-stroke depressive symptoms. Recent laboratory-based studies have shown that ‘affective touch’ - a touch that includes skin-to-skin contact and an affective element involving love and care via recalling times of feeling close to and loved by another - can increase the touch recipients’ oxytocin level. Increased oxytocin inhibits the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity, in which dysregulated HPA activity is one of the etiologies of post-stroke depression (PSD). Also, the physical and emotional closeness signalled by affective touch is an important attribute of attachment security. According to attachment theory, such security is a psychological resource that enhances the positive appraisal of self and others and is associated with increased blood oxytocin level. The attachment security may play a crucial role in enhancing the psychological rehabilitation of stroke survivors. Thus, extending our knowledge of affective touch is clearly required, to reduce PSD in a day-to-day environment. This mixed-method study includes a randomised controlled trial and an exploratory qualitative study, and aims to examine the effects of caregiver-delivered affective touch on depressive symptoms, state of attachment security, self-esteem, and perceived family harmony among stroke survivors, and to explore the mediating effect of attachment security and how an intervention may affect depressive symptoms from stroke survivor’s perspective. A total of 184 survivor-caregiver dyads will be recruited from various non-governmental organisations. The dyads will be randomly allocated to intervention (IG) and control (CG) groups, stratified by the survivor’s attachment style. IG caregivers will be taught to deliver a 15-minute affective touch intervention to stroke survivors. To address the attention effect, CG caregivers will be asked to sit with the survivors during a 15-minute fine motor coordination exercise. Both activities, affective touching and fine motor exercise, will be performed for 12 weeks (3 times/week), and the outcomes mentioned earlier will be measured at baseline, 12 and 36 weeks after study entry. The present study marks the first attempt to develop a caregiver-delivered affective touch intervention and to examine its effects in a stroke-caregiving context. The findings will advance our understandings on how to enhance the attachment security to reduce post-stroke depressive symptoms, providing culturally sensitive medical-social service direction to optimise outcomes among community-dwelling stroke survivors.

24619118.value: 本研究針對中國過去幾年新興的心理相關新創公司（主要以提供心理相關服務或內容為運營範圍），結合民族誌、文本分析、與量化研究方法，力圖釐清以下幾個問題：一、了解這些新創公司的誕生過程以及創業者參與其中的生命經驗。二、檢視這些公司多半是透過數位平台所提供的服務，並探討其對心理衛生服務體系的影響。三、分析這些公司多半是透過社交媒體所散播的資訊，並了解其如何形塑大眾對心理與精神健康認知的影響。

24619118.label: Realisation of objectives
24619118.value: Throughout the research, I faced two major obstacles, both of which could not be anticipated during the planning phase. The first is the political turmoil caused by the 2019 Anti-ELAB protests in Hong Kong, which, along with the tightening of political control in China and the heightened geopolitical tensions, increased suspicion, and sometimes even hostility, toward overseas researchers like me. The second is the COVID-19 pandemic, which had made ethnographic research in its conventional form—being there in the physical world—impossible since late January 2020. Originally, I planned to spend 9 months in Beijing and Shanghai. As the pandemic lasted indefinitely, I was forced to give up the plan and applied for an extension. Eventually, I could only conduct 2-3 weeks of onsite fieldwork; most of the fieldwork for this project turned out to be conducted online. During the latter part of the research period, I resorted to online interviews to overcome the inaccessibility of field sites. Objective No.1: I have achieved 100% of the first objective—to study the development of a psy-startup scene that features digital technologies and relies on venture capital. Initially, I planned to gather information by inserting myself in this psy-startup scene as a participant observer—a standard practice in socio-cultural anthropology. This turned out to be unfeasible due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Fortunately, I could still collect enough data through the WeChat accounts of the scene’s key players. I also got to know quite a few people associated with the scene and was able to interview them online. Objective No. 2: I have achieved 90% of the second objective—to examine the services of certain highly influential psy-startups and evaluate their impacts on psychotherapy as both a mental health services sector and a profession. Again, I had to rely mostly on online fieldwork to achieve this aim. I closely followed the digital platforms of several important psy-starups and talked to many of their affiliated practitioners. I had encountered little difficulty—except for the challenge of conducting interviews online—thanks to a vast network of key informants established previously during my decade-long research on China’s psychotherapy boom. However, a crucial part of my original plan—to conduct fieldwork in the office of a psy-startup—was missing, and it was impossible to understand the company’s day-to-day operation through other means. Objective No.3: I have achieved 75% of the third objective—to investigate the ideas, narratives, and experiences disseminated by certain highly influential psy-startups and to explore how the psy-startups produce the “content” as well as how the audience receives it. I fulfilled the former part of the aim as it involved “content” that could be accessed via the WeChat public account platform. However, I encountered immense difficulty in achieving the latter part of the aim. First, as described in the previous paragraph, I couldn’t perform “office fieldwork” to examine content production, and there was no feasible backup plan. Second, understanding the reception of the psy-startups—that is, to solicit the experiences of people who had used their services—turned out to be very challenging. Recruitment was a big issue to begin with, though eventually I overcame it with the assistance of certain Internet celebrities. These interviews were conducted online, and often could not go as deeply as I wished.

24619118.label: Major findings and research outcome
24619118.value: The project has thus far resulted in one peer-reviewed journal article in History of Psychiatry (2021 Impact factor 0.579) and five conference presentations. I am working on two more journal articles based on these presentations; hopefully they will be completed and submitted to acclaimed international journals in the next year. The first, already-published article examines the evolution of entry-level psychotherapy training after the termination of the state-sponsored certification for psychological counselors in 2017. It describes psy-startups as one of the three major players in the “post-certification era”—the other two are respectively the pre-existing, old-fashioned training industry and the professional associations—and how they have become the major provider for professional training on the market. The second, still yet to be finished article examines some of the most well-known controversies that involve psychotherapy practice on the platforms created by psy-startups. It argues that while psy-startups have become the most crucial infrastructure builder in the domain of mental health services and its related profession, this “infrastructurization” comes with distinct risks with regards to the role they are supposed to play in adjudicating ethical issues. The third article will deal with the rapid growth of psy-startups during the COVID-19 pandemic, which has constituted another “peak” after the early phase of the startup frenzy (roughly 2015-2016). It looks into how the domain of mental health attracts the attention of the general public as the idea of psychic trauma prevails; venture capitalists begin to invest on psy-startups again in the backdrop of economic slowdown as they believe in the great potential of digital technology not only in the pandemic times but also in the post-pandemic future.

24619118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24619118.value: My main goal is to publish all the manuscripts derived from the current project in the next two years. Besides this, I am preparing a grant application to Taiwan’s National Science and Technology Council (the Taiwanese equivalent of Hong Kong’s Research Grants Council). The new project, tentatively titled “Reading KnowYourself: Self-Fashioning of Chinese Youth on a Digital Mental Health Platform,” would build on the current project and pick up its unfinished part—the reception of psy-startups. My inquiry highlights the experience of reading since the object of study, KnowYourself, is often hailed as a paragon of “content entrepreneurship.” Taking reading experience as an entry point into one’s psychic life, I aim to examine the self-fashioning of Chinese youth under the current Xi Jingping regime, an era defined by omnipotent surveillance and the enforcement of “positive energy.” This project may become the mainstay of my research in the next two or three years, and hopefully it will eventually lead to the publication of a monograph or a series of journal articles.

24619118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24619118.value: In China, a country that still lags behind the developed world in mental health services, the nascent field of digital mental health is growing at full speed and is particularly welcomed by the middle-class population. The trend occurs at the confluence of the “psycho-boom” that intensified after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake and a more recent “startup frenzy” that is driven by the state’s ambition to build an innovation-based economy. Its key players are startup companies that put forward products and services derived from Western psychotherapy or psychology. Situated in the distinct environment of the Chinese Internet, a vibrant parallel universe that is heavily censored, these startups function as the inventors of novel “infrastructure,” whose influence are increasingly rivalling that of more traditional players in the mental health system. They facilitate the progress of the related professions, enhance the delivery of services, and disseminate as well as create elements of the therapeutic culture that puts more emphasis on self-awareness and self-understanding.

24620618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24620618.value: After World War II, the strategic town for the Chinese-language film industry migrated south from Shanghai to Hong Kong; and the Cold War situation changed the film distribution and production model. Since the 1950s, Singapore and Malaysia had replaced Mainland China as the biggest export market for Hong Kong-produced films. To understand the postwar Chinese-language film industry’s funding cycle, production model, and film genre evolution, one cannot ignore the cultural production networks of Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia and the important influence of geopolitics behind the business. This study continues the research in the academic book I will soon publish, Hong Kong Cinema and Singapore: A Cultural Ring between Two Cities. (1950-64), (forthcoming). This study will focus on the early days of the Motion Picture & General Investment Co., Ltd. (MP&GI)—its golden age; from 1955 to 1964, MP&GI produced 152 Mandarin and Cantonese films. The Chairman of MP&GI, Loke Wan Tho, son of the richest man in Singapore and Malaysia, studied history and economics in Europe and had a Western style. In the mid-1950s, Loke imitated the Hollywood studio model by integrating three links—theater, distribution, and production, produced high-quality Chinese-language films in Hong Kong, and distributed to Singapore, Malaysia, North America, and other places. MP&GI, known as the “literati studio,” hired quite a few cultural figures, and MP&GI films were famous for approximating the Hollywood style. Besides Loke’s personal background and European flair, factors of the times and geopolitical changes also dictated MP&GI’s style. In this study, I will continue to explore the effect of the Cold War political environment on the production strategy for MP&GI films, the film genres produced, and the studio’s leading middle-brow filmmaking style. Besides concentrating research on the relationship in film culture between Singapore and Hong Kong, MP&GI’s network would also extend to Taiwan. From a political environment perspective, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia were once British colonies; in terms of official system, the United Kingdom took charge by including Hong Kong and Singapore within the scope of Southeast Asia, and both places had similar political and economic systems. On funding source, MP&GI can be seen as the paragon for early cross-regional Chinese-language cinema. Due to the Cold War situation, MP&GI was incorporated into the “right” and maintained a close relationship with Taiwan. The emphases of this research plan are MP&GI’s regional network and studio style of focusing on wen-yi films and comedies. 在二戰後，華語電影工業的重鎮從上海南移香港，冷戰形勢改變了電影的發行與生產模式，在1950年代開始，星馬取代中國大陸，成為港產片最大的出口市場。星馬地區出現三大華語院線，改變了華語電影工業的氣候：邵逸夫家族的邵氏、陸運濤家族的國泰和何啟榮家族的光藝。香港電影業亦從小公司林立的局面變成由幾間大片廠所主導。要了解華語影業的資金循環、生產模式、類型電影的演變，不能忽略香港與星馬地區的文化生產網絡，以及商業背後地緣政治的重要影響。這一項研究，是延續我將要出版的學術專書之研究《Hong Kong Cinema and Singapore: A Cultural Ring between Two Cities. (1950-64)》，(將會在2018年由香港大學出版社出版)。這項研究的重點將會放在電懋公司早期、亦即其黃金時期上，從1955到1964年，電懋製作了152部國、粵語影片。電懋公司的董事長陸運濤是星馬首富之子，曾經留學歐洲供讀歷史與經濟，作風西化。在1950年代中期陸氏仿好萊塢片廠模式，整合了戲院、發行、製作三環節，在香港生產高質素的華語電影，並發行到星馬及北美等地。電懋公司聘任不少文化人，例如是易文、宋淇、張愛玲、陶秦都曾在旗下服務，電懋的電影亦以其靠近好萊塢的美學風格著名。電懋「文人片廠」風格的建立，除了是因為董事長陸運濤的個人背景與歐化作風，還有的是時代的因素、地緣政治的改變所使然。在我將要出版的學術專著中提到冷戰的地緣政治如何在1950、60年代拉近了香港與星馬等地的電影文化連繫。這一項研究，將會繼續探索冷戰政治環境對於電懋電影的生產策略、類型電影製作、片廠主導的「中產趣味」(middle brow)的影響。 這項研究，我除了會集中在星港兩城的電影文化關係，還會把電懋的網絡伸延到台灣。從政治環境角度看，香港和星馬都曾經是英國殖民地，從官方制度上，英國把香港和新加坡納入東南亞範圍看管，兩地有相似的政、經系統。另外，電懋公司在早期曾跟英國的J. Arthur Rank Organisation合作，從其資金來源來看，電懋可以看為是早期跨區域華語電影的典範。亦因為冷戰形勢，被納入為「右派」的電懋公司與台灣亦保持緊密的關係。電懋公司的三地網絡，以及其著重文藝片及喜劇的片廠風格，都是這個研究計劃的重點。

24620618.label: Realisation of objectives
24620618.value: My main objectives on this research are to study Chinese-language film production and aesthetics from a cross-regional perspective, and to explore the Cold War situation from the geopolitics angle and discrete ethnicity by studying the film culture and interactive relationships among Hong Kong, Singapore, Malay/Malaysia, and Taiwan from 1950 to 1965. My research focused on the Singapore financial funding of a Hong Kong based film studio MP&GI which produced high quality Chinese films in the 1950s and 1960s. In order to achieve these objectives, I devoted much time scrutinizing and analysing research materials between 2018 and 2020. I viewed some 10 rare old films that could only been seen at the Taiwan Film Institute during my research visit in the summer of 2019 in Taipei. These films cannot be found in any other archives in the world, which are crucial materials in this research project. After the Taipei trip, I conducted a research trip in London. I consulted books, old movie magazines, business reports and related documents that are related to the Cathay Organisation and Rank Organisation. During my stay in London, I also visited the National Archives to collect historical and archival reports focusing on the colonial cultural policies in the 1950s and 1960s Hong Kong. This archival research helped to achieve the first, second and third objectives of my project. I was planning to arrange other research trips to Taipei and Singapore in 2020, but due to the Covid-19 pandemic situation, this hindered my chance to conduct research trips outside Hong Kong. In addition, due to the same reasons, Covid-19 also reduced my ability to attend conferences held overseas. I worked with the materials I gathered (although I could not fully utilize the grant to make more research trips to collect as much materials as I planned) and worked on my publications. I have my book monograph “From Pulp Fiction, Hollywood to MP&GI (Cathay): Adaptations and Remakes in Hong Kong Cinema during the Cold War Era”(《冷戰時期香港電懋電影的「另類改編」與「重拍」》)published by the Beijing Xinhua Bookstore in 2020. In addition, I also have two journal articles published in two different peer reviewed journals “Cultural Studies Quarterly”(《文化研究季刊》) and “Bulletin of The Department of Chinese Literature, National Taiwan University”（《臺大中文學報》） in 2019 and 2021 respectively. My book titled “From Pulp Fiction, Hollywood to MP&GI (Cathay): Adaptations and Remakes in Hong Kong Cinema during the Cold War Era”, has been published by the Xinhua Bookstore in Beijing. In this book, I discussed the process of ‘adaptation’/’remake’, the multifaceted journey and propagation of the cultural materials which were “borrowed” in different media, regions, political cultures, national cultures, and so on, thereby revealing the culture and business network of the Hong Kong film industry during the Cold War era. In the 1950s and 1960s, the concept of ‘intellectual property rights’ had not yet taken root in Hong Kong. The production of many popular literature and films actually relied on the ‘recirculation’ of cultural materials, and the ‘recirculation’ of these cultural materials was not necessarily obtained from literary works (including pulp fiction and serious literature). The material for many original versions of stories was drawn from Hollywood movies. These movie titles were not the same as their ‘remade’ films. It is difficult to judge which works were the ‘original versions’ of these films from the titles of the films alone. However, as long as we pay close attention to the contents of the plots of the films, we can find their original texts. These Hollywood stories would often undergo a ‘localisation’ rewriting process. The setting and background of the characters in the story were ones with which Hong Kong and Chinese-language film audiences could grasp and identify. Moreover, in the process of ‘adaptation’/ ‘remake’, the multifaceted journey and propagation of these cultural materials were also reflected in different media, regions, political cultures, national cultures, and so on, thereby revealing the culture and business network of the Hong Kong film industry during the Cold War era. My publications between 2019 and 2021 helped to achieve the fourth and fifth objectives of my project.

24620618.label: Major findings and research outcome
24620618.value: The 1950s was a turning point for the Hong Kong film industry. The ideological struggles between the left and right camps reached a peak during 1950-56 that directly affected the Hong Kong film industry. The Hong Kong rightist filmmakers faced political hurdles from Taiwan's government during the Cold War era. From Zhang Shankun and Li Zuyong to Loke Wan To; from Yung Hwa Motion Picture Studio and Xinhua to MP&GI; my research studied the question of how the Cold War environment impacted the existence of the Hong Kong right-wing filmmakers. 24620618.value: The period of 1950s and 1960s is a golden era in Hong Kong cinema history. MP&GI, as one of the top studio back in those days, has produced more than 150 films, but the cultural and cinematic network built by this studio has still been understudied. I will continue to explore the opportunities to make research trips to Taiwan and Singapore, and to collect more data and materials for the further research in this area.

24620618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24620618.value: My research examined the impact of the Cold War climate of the 1950s upon the Hong Kong film industry. Using the political and cultural strategies employed by the British government in Hong Kong and Southeast Asia during the Cold War period as the backdrop, my research juxtaposes and observes the cinema in Hong Kong and the rise of national cinema in Singapore as well as its cultural ties with Taiwan. This project focuses on films made by MP&GI Studio (or Cathay Studio) between 1950-1965 dealing with Southeast Asian Chinese subjects. My research examines a rarely studied area of modern Asian cultural history: the emergence and subsequent decline of the cinematic ties between Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore-Malaya in the Cold War era. It examines the Hong Kong cinema industry's parallels to the development of the Chinese-language national cinemas in Malaya/Singapore and Taiwan during the 1950s and the 1960s.

24621518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24621518.value: English language writing is an important literacy skill for learners of English as a second/foreign language (ESL/EFL). However, research shows that writing is the most difficult skill to master for English language learners and that English language teachers need guidance in instructional practices to enhance their teaching of English writing (Wang, Schwab, Fenn, & Chang, 2013). In Hong Kong, the situation is especially true because English serves as an EFL but at the same time English is an important subject in schools (Wang & Kirkpatrick 2013). This proposed study uses a quasi-experimental design and has two phases: exploration and intervention. In Phase One, think-alouds will be conducted with 20 primary school students to explore the self-regulated writing strategies used by primary students in Hong Kong. A comprehensive literature review on self-regulated writing strategies used by ESL/EFL students will also be undertaken. Based on the data from the think-aloud protocols and literature review, a questionnaire of self-regulated writing strategies will be designed and piloted with around 250 primary school students. Unreliable items will be removed to enhance the reliability. The main questionnaire survey will be administered to around 500 4th and 5th graders. This phase is to identify the self-regulated writing strategies (e.g., attending to audience and reading back what has been written, planning, text-generating and revising) that contribute to writing competence. During Phase Two, self-regulated writing strategies found significantly correlated to writing competence in Phase One will be taught to around 250 students for 10 weeks. Another 250 students of a similar English proficiency will serve as the control group. Classroom observations and meetings with the teachers will be conducted on weekdays to seek feedback and to examine their implementation fidelity. Pre- and post-intervention writing tests and questionnaires will be administered to find out if their students can achieve better writing competence and improvements in use of self-regulated writing strategies. This project will make significant contributions by adding to ESL/EFL writing research. It seeks (a) to find out what self-regulated writing strategies primary students use in an EFL context, i.e., Hong Kong; (b) to investigate how self-regulated writing strategies contribute to writing competence; and (c) to improve Hong Kong primary school students’ English language writing competence through strategy-based instruction (SBI) for self-regulated writing strategies. 對於以英語為第二語言或外語(ESL/EFL)的學習者，寫作是一項十分重要的技能。不過，研究指出對於英語學習者來說，寫作技巧是最難掌握的，而且英語教師需要切實教學實踐的指導，以提升他們的英語寫作教學(Wang, Schwab, Fenn & Chang, 2013)。在香港，情況尤其如此，因為英語不但是外語，同時亦是學校中重要的科目(Wang & Kirkpatrick 2013) 。 這項提議研究採用準實驗設計(qusai-experimental design)，分為兩個階段：探索和介入。 在第一階段，首先會邀請20名小學生參與有聲思維 (think-alouds)，從而探索香港小學生使用的自主學習寫作策略。另外會進行一個全面性的文獻回顧，探討有關以英語為第二語言或外語學習者的自主學習寫作策略。根據有聲思維法 (think aloud protocols) 所收集的數據和文獻探討，設計一份有關自主學習寫作策略的問卷，並邀請約250名小學生進行測試(pilot)。不可靠的問卷項目會被刪除，以提高問卷的可靠性。主要的問卷調查會有約500名小四和小五的學生參與。這個階段的目的是識別有助於提升寫作能力的自主學習寫作策略 (例如：關注讀者、閱讀已寫部分、計劃、文本寫作和修改)。 在第二階段，250名小學生會學習在第一階段確認與提升寫作能力顯著相關的自主學習寫作策略，為期十星期。另外，250名具有相近英語水平的學生將成為研究的控制組。觀課和教師會議將在平日進行，以便尋求反饋並檢查教師實施研究計劃時的準確度(implementation fidelity)。這研究亦會利用介入前後的寫作測試和寫作策略問卷調查，以確定學生是否可以達到更好的寫作能力和改善自主學習寫作策略的使用。 該項目將通過增加以英語為第二語言或外語寫作研究做出重大貢獻。它尋求（a）找出小學生在外語背景的地方，如香港，會使用什麼的自主學習寫作策略（b）調查自主寫作策略與於寫作能力的相關性; （c）透過以策略為基礎的教學方法 (SBI) ，讓香港小學生學習自主學習寫作策略使用，以提升他們的英語寫作能力。

24621518.label: Major findings and research outcome
24621518.value: The participants were found to use a wide range of self-regulated writing strategies, including self-initiation, planning, text-generating, self-monitoring and management, revising, acting on feedback. They reported a medium level of SRL strategy use; they used planning strategies most frequently, and self-initiation and revising strategies least frequently. Revising strategies are found less favored among Hong Kong primary students. The findings suggest that the students spent little efforts on their own to improve their English writing. The findings suggested noticeable differences among the grade levels in terms of SRL writing strategy use, but the students of different grade levels did not differ in their use of half of the strategies (i.e., planning, text-generating, and acting on feedback). The 5th graders used SRL writing strategies significantly less frequently than the 4th . In terms of motivation (i.e., interest, task values, and growth mindset), first, the participants reported a low level of interest and collaborative learning in English writing. Second, significant differences in the motivational variables and SRL writing strategy use between the high and low achievers were identified. Third, the motivational variables, especially self-efficacy and growth mindset, were crucial for SRL writing strategy use. However, it is unexpected that interest negatively predicted acting on feedback. Regarding English teachers’ writing instruction, the participants reported that their teachers executed process-based instruction (e.g., teaching writing at the three different stages) at a high frequency. In contrast, the primary school participants reported their SRL strategy use at only a moderate frequency, which indicates a general gap between teachers’ writing instruction and their students’ adoption and employment of the taught self-regulated writing strategies. The intervention phase of the project measured the changes to the participants’ level of motivation in English writing and e-learning acceptance. The findings suggest that the intervention achieved a significant effect on the participants’ use of all four types of SRL writing strategies. In terms of motivation, both their interest and self-efficacy increased although self-efficacy failed to reach a significant level (p = .052). For the four subscales of e-learning acceptance, the students’ perceived usefulness, attitude, and continuance intention improved significantly, but their perceived ease of use did not see a significant improvement (p = .16). The intervention can be considered successful. For publication 7, acknowledgement of the RGC funding was not made due to the tight publication deadline and the editor misplaced the information.

24621518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24621518.value: The participants reported that their English teachers did teach various self-regulated writing strategies at a high frequency. However, the participants reported only a medium level of use of all types of self-regulated writing strategies. Such findings highlight the importance of bridging the gap between instruction and learning. Future research should aim to investigate what instructional approaches and conditions can improve students’ adoption and employment of writing strategies besides the motivational factors (e.g., interest, self-efficacy and growth mindset) of students. Therefore, I plan to carry out some observations in different types of primary schools to find out what factors/conditions/approaches may facilitate students’ adoption and employment of self-regulated writing strategies more effectively. Special attention will be paid to English teachers’ continuing professional development, classroom routines, cultures, and actual teaching plans in order to map out the factors/conditions.

24621518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24621518.value: The project identified a wide range of self-regulated writing strategies that facilitate primary school students’ English writing, including self-initiation, planning, text-generating, self-monitoring and management, revising, acting on feedback. The more frequently students use these strategies, the better English writing results they may achieve. The project also found that students’ use of self-regulated writing strategies was influenced by a series of motivational factors (e.g., interest, self-efficacy, growth mindset and task values). In other words, all these motivational variables may result in students’ more frequent use of the strategies if English teachers use strategies to boost students’ motivation. However, there was a gap between English teachers’ instruction and students’ use of strategies. Although English teachers may teach the strategies frequently, their students’ may not use them as frequently. Therefore, it is important to find out what factors/conditions may further promote students’ adoption and use of the strategies, besides boosting their motivation.

25100818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100818.value: 作為最常見的一種關節炎，骨關節炎是老年人慢性疼痛和行動不便的主要原因。 骨關節炎的標誌是關節軟骨的破壞；最新研究成果顯示衰老細胞隨著骨關節炎的發展而在關節軟骨中逐漸積累，應用基因工程方法去除衰老細胞可以減輕骨關節炎，而去除衰老細胞的藥物正在進一步的研發當中。 高血壓是膝骨關節炎最新確立的獨立危險因素。 據報導，高血壓在人體和動物模型中可誘導腎臟和心臟細胞衰老；然而，高血壓及其致病因子是否會導致膝關節中衰老細胞的積聚並引發骨關節炎尚不清楚。內皮素-1是一種高血壓致病因子中的強效血管收縮劑和炎症促進因子。最近發現內皮素-1在體外誘導內皮細胞衰老，內皮素受體拮抗劑可以減少血管組織中的衰老細胞，從而減輕體內與衰老相關的血管病變。因此，我們有興趣知道內皮素-1是否會在滑膜關節損傷後血管翳增生時促進關節中的衰老細胞聚集。因此，我們研究了轉基因內皮細胞特異性過表達內皮素-1的小鼠模型，這是一種經過充分驗證的系統性高血壓囓齒動物模型。當比較轉基因小鼠與其同窩小鼠的膝關節組織形態時，我們發現過度表達的內皮素-1導致衰老細胞在軟骨下骨，滑膜和關節軟骨中積聚，並加速對其膝關節的破壞。我們的初步研究發現內皮素受體拮抗劑可以減少受傷膝關節的衰老細胞，減弱創傷後骨關節炎的症狀。 在此項目中，我們將通過轉基因小鼠的前十字韌帶橫斷誘導膝骨關節炎，探究系統性（高血壓和 血漿中過高的內皮素-1）和局部因素（關節創傷）在細胞衰老與骨關節炎發展之間的相互作用，並且進一步驗證內皮素受體拮抗劑在這一多因素骨關節炎動物模型中的抗衰老功效。

25100818.label: Realisation of objectives
25100818.value: For Aim 1, we investigated the role of endothelin-1 (ET-1), originally known as the potent vasoconstrictor, and its receptors in chondrocyte senescence and osteoarthritis (OA) development in a post traumatic murine model. Temporal changes of ET-1 and its receptors with OA development were characterized in a posttraumatic OA (PTOA) mouse model at time zero, 1-month and 4-month after surgical induction via destabilization of medial meniscus (DMM). A transgenic ET-1 overexpression (TET-1) mouse model was deployed to assess the impact of upregulated ET-1 on chondrocyte senescence and cartilage degradation. Effects of endothelin receptor blockade on chondrocyte senescence and OA development were further examined both in vitro and in vivo. We observed that local expression of ET-1 in subchondral bone and synovium upregulated after DMM with an increase of plasma ET-1 level from 3.18 ± 0.21 pg/ml at time zero to 6.47 ± 0.34 pg/ml at 4-month post-surgery. Meanwhile, endothelin type B receptor (ETBR) (53.31 ± 2.42% to 83.8 ± 2.65%) and p16INK4a (10.91 ± 1.07% to 28.2 ± 1.0%) positve chondrocytes accumulated in articular cartilage since 1-month prior to cartilage loss at 4-month post-surgery. Overexpressed ET-1 promoted p16INK4a-positive senescent chondrocytes accumulation and cartilage degradation in TET-1 mice. Selective blockade of ETBR, but not ETAR, lowered the expression of p16INK4a in ET-1 or H2O2-induced chondrocyte senescence model, and mitigated the severity of murine PTOA. Intriguingly, reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenger, Vitamin C, could rescue ET-1-induced chondrocyte senescence in vitro associated with restoration of mitochondrial dynamics. We concluded that ET-1 could induce chondrocytes senescence and cartilage damages via ETBR in PTOA. Under the auspices of RGC ECS and GRF, Dr. Wen and his team finally identified endothelin-1 (ET-1), the most potent vasoconstrictor in hypertension, contributing to articular chondrocyte senescence and osteoarthritis pathology (Osteoarthritis and Cartilage, 2020, impact factor 6.576, 2/82 in the category of orthopaedics). It substantiates the vascular etiology hypothesis of osteoarthritis and opens a new avenue for discovery of novel mechanism-based disease-modifying therapies against osteoarthritis. Dr. Wen was therefore being invited to review current knowledge and to discuss future development along this direction on Nature Review Rheumatology in July 2021. Publication Link: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41584-021-00650-x. Dr. Wen has also been invited to give a keynote speech in local and international conferences on the same topic. For Aim 2, we exploited the efficacy of dual blockade of endothelin receptors for rescue of OA. Human cartilage samples and chondrocytes were obtained from patients with knee OA and evaluated on its expression of endothelin receptors. To investigate the changes in endothelin system during hypertrophic differentiation, immature articular chondrocytes were isolated from mouse pulps for hypertrophic induction. The pre-hypertrophic ATDC5 cells were sorted based on its expression of ETBR, or treated with inhibitors of ETAR and ETBR to explore the function of endothelin receptors in chondrogenesis and chondrocyte hypertrophy. Mice received Macitentan treatment after sham or destabilization of medial meniscus (DMM) surgery to investigate the effects of endothelin receptor blockade in vivo. OA chondrocytes expressed high levels of ETAR and ETBR. Expression of ETAR was upregulated throughout hypertrophic differentiation, while levels of ETBR were first downregulated then upregulated. ATDC5 cells expressing high levels of ETBR appeared more hypertrophic and produced more oxidative stress. Dual blockade of endothelin receptors could significantly downregulate MMP13 and Sox9 in ATDC5 cells. Macitentan treatment to intact or OA knees resulted in proteoglycan loss in the articular surface. ETBR was identified as a mediator of chondrogenesis through Sox9. Dual blockade of ETAR and ETBR might not protect against cartilage damage as endothelin receptors were required for chondrogenesis. Through this RGC ECS project, we have established formal research collaboration with world-leading research institutes such as Kennedy Institute of Rheumatology, University of Oxford (Prof. Tonia Vincent, HMRF research fellowship) and Sorbonne University in Paris (Prof. Francis Berenbaum, PROCORE-France/Hong Kong Joint Research Scheme and INSERM International Research Program) and Saarland University Medical Center (Prof. Dr. Henning Madry and Prof. Magali Cucchiarini). Dr. WEN and team also introduced an imaging-guided nanoparticle photothermal treatment for osteoarthritis pain. The targeted osteoarthritis pain theranostics i.e., serving diagnostic and therapeutic purposes at same time, are made of gold nanorods that are fused with antibodies directed against the nerve growth factor (NGF), the pain-triggering protein. Animal testing on mice suggests the targeted photothermal treatment achieves satisfactory pain relief and improvement of motor function. It holds good promise for clinical translation to achieve long-lasting pain relief. These findings have been published in the official journal of the American Chemical Society - ACS Nano (impact factor 15. 881, top 5% in the category of material science, multidisciplinary) and were reported by Nature Reviews Rheumatology. Dr. Wen has also been invited to edit a special issue along this direction for Theranostics (impact factor 11.556, No.9 in the category of medicine, research experimental) (https://www.thno.org/si/osteoarthritis.html).

25100818.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100818.value: Dr. Wen’s research centers on vascular etiology of osteoarthritis. Dr. Wen observed a clinical association between hypertension and osteoarthritis (Osteoarthritis and Cartilage, 2013, impact factor 6.576, No.2 in the category of orthopaedics). This finding led a way in Dr. Wen’s research to searched for the underlying molecular link between these two prevalent debilitating age-related diseases (Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2017, impact factor 19.103, No.2 in the category of rheumatology; Arthritis & Rheumatology 2019, impact factor 10.995, No.3 in the category of rheumatology). Under the auspices of RGC ECS and GRF, Dr. Wen and his team finally identified endothelin-1 (ET-1), the most potent vasoconstrictor in hypertension, contributing to articular chondrocyte senescence and osteoarthritis pathology (Osteoarthritis and Cartilage, 2015, 2020). It substantiates the vascular etiology hypothesis of osteoarthritis and opens a new avenue for discovery of novel mechanism-based disease-modifying therapies against osteoarthritis. Dr. Wen was therefore being invited to review current knowledge and to discuss future development along this direction on Nature Review Rheumatology in July 2021. Publication Link: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41584-021-00650-x.

25100818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100818.value: We anticipate developing endothelin-1 as an emerging biomarker for joint ageing and disorder and its type B receptor as a promising therapeutic target for rescue of osteoarthritis. Along the same research direction, we have secured more research funding to further exploit the vascular aetiology of osteoarthritis and the other vasoactive factors in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis: 1) NFSC/RGC “Vascular ageing in osteoarthritis: from mechanism towards intervention” (N_PolyU520/20) (HK$1,154,954, RMB~1,000,000) 2) RGC GRF “Endothelial dysfunction in joint ageing and osteoarthritis: molecular mechanism and clinical implication” (15100821) (HK$997,332)

25100818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100818.value: Knee osteoarthritis is a prevalent debilitating age-related joint disorder. It is a leading cause of chronic pain and disability in the older adults. There is a famous Chinese old saying: "痛則不通；通則不痛". However, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Our research findings generated from this RGC ECS project, for the first time to our best knowledge, unravel the molecular basis of this phenomenon, i.e. endothelin-1, a potent vasoconstrictor, which plays a pivotal role in the development of osteoarthritis, a painful joint problem. We have also developed a targeted therapy to blockade endothelin signalling to attenuate this disease with proven efficacy in a pre-clinical setting. Endothelin receptor antagonists have been proved by FDA for the other vascular pathologies. It lays a solid foundation for clinical translation to repurpose this kind of medications for rescue of osteoarthritis in near future.

25101418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25101418.value: Epidemiologic studies have shown that migraine, particularly migraine with aura, was significantly associated with various cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). The migraine features (subtype, duration, frequency, and intensity), however, have not been well examined in those previous studies due to the difficulty in recording the episodic headache attacks. These migraine features are relevant for locating the subgroup of migraineurs who have the highest CVD risk, which may enable treatment to be targeted at those most likely to benefit. A few studies have found an unfavorable cardiovascular risk profile among migraineurs. Understanding the CVD risk factors associated with migraine features may not only help to further substantiate the link between migraine and CVD but also aid in the identification of high-risk individuals for early intervention. We plan to establish a cohort of women living in Hong Kong for longitudinal evaluation of migraine features in relation to cardiovascular risk profile. Our primary objectives are: 1) To characterize the migraine features and cardiovascular risk profile in a cohort of Hong Kong Chinese women; 2) To determine whether migraineurs have unfavorable cardiovascular risk profile; 3) To investigate which CVD risk factors predict certain migraine features; 4) To examine the relationship between migraine and predicted risk of developing CVD; and 5) To test whether migraine features make any difference to the progression of cardiovascular risk. Four thousand Chinese women aged ≥30 years and are free of existing CVD will be enrolled at the collaborating clinics that provide medical services to a large number of women. Data will be collected through face-to-face interview, physical examinations and laboratory tests, and medical record review and data extraction. At baseline, participants will be screened by the ID MigraineTM embedded in the questionnaire, and probable migraineurs will be confirmed using clinical diagnostic criteria. Confirmed migraineurs are asked to document their migraine features in a migraine diary. Two years follow-up will be carried out. The primary outcome is the estimated risk of developing CVD, which is evaluated by the calibrated Framingham 10-Year General Cardiovascular Risk Score. Secondary outcomes are the distribution of modifiable CVD risk factors from baseline to the end of the follow-up period, including body mass index, waist circumference, blood pressure, blood lipids, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia; as well as the stress and health related quality of life. Multiple linear mix model will be used to examine the associations between migraine features and cardiovascular risk profile. 流行病學研究已表明偏頭痛與各種心血管疾病顯著相關，特別是有先兆的偏頭痛。然而由於頭痛多為陣發性發作，難以記錄，以前的研究並沒有深入探討不同特徵的偏頭痛（類型，持續時長，發作頻率，發作強度）與心血管病發展的關係。具有某一特徵的偏頭痛患者可能有最高的心血管病風險，針對這類患者進行心血管病預防及治療可能更有效益。所以了解心血管病危險因素與偏頭痛特徵的關係，不僅可以進一步證實偏頭痛與心血管病的關連，而且能夠幫助找出有心血管病高風險的個體，以進行早期幹預。 我們計劃建立一項香港女性的隊列研究，縱向觀察偏頭痛特徵與心血管風險狀況的關係。主要研究目的包括：1）描述此女性隊列人群的偏頭痛特徵及心血管風險狀況；2）檢驗其中偏頭痛患者是否具有不利的心血管風險狀況；3）調查哪些心血管病危險因素與特定偏頭痛特徵相關；4）研究偏頭痛與發生心血管病的風險預測之間的關係；5）檢驗是否偏頭痛特徵在心血管病風險進程中起到不同作用。 四千名30歲以上、無心血管病的華人女性將在合作的臨床診所進行招募。數據收集將通過面對面訪談、體格檢查、實驗室測試以及審查和提取醫療記錄來獲得。收集基線數據時，研究人員首先將用ID Migraine對參加者進行偏頭痛的篩查，隨後基於臨床的標準診斷確認偏頭痛患者。這些患者被要求用偏頭痛日記記錄每次頭痛發作之情況。所有參加者將跟蹤隨訪兩年。本研究主要研究結局是發生心血管病的風險預測，將用校準的弗拉明翰十年心血管風險綜合評分來測得。次要研究結局是從基線到隨訪結束時各項可改變的心血管病危險因素的分佈，包括身體質量指數，腰圍，血壓，血脂，吸煙，飲酒，體力活動，糖尿病和血脂異常，以及壓力和健康相關生活質量。多元線性混合模型將用於檢驗偏頭痛特徵與心血管風險狀況之間的關係。

25101418.label: Realisation of objectives
25101418.value: From October 2019 to December 2020, 4656 women were invited to participate in our cohort study, which named “Migraine Exposures and Cardiovascular Health in Hong Kong Chinese Women (MECH-HK)”. After screening of the eligibility, 4221 women aged ≥30 years were involved in the baseline assessment. The second-round data collection started in October 2021, around one year later, 3433 women were successfully followed until December 2022. The follow-up rate was 81.3%. In fact, this round of data collection is still ongoing, several women have been successfully tracked back after the end date of the project. Women underwent a range of assessments at both waves, including questionnaires, physical examinations, and blood tests. Questionnaires were used to collect the data on socioeconomic characteristics (age, marital status, income, employment, etc.), reproduction health (menarche, menopause, pregnancy, breastfeeding, etc.), personal and family medical history, lifestyles (smoking, alcohol, physical activity, diet, etc.), sleep, fatigue, and stress. Physical examinations included weight, height, blood pressure, waist and hip circumference, and body fat. Blood tests included blood glucose and blood lipids. The International Classification of Headache Disorders 3rd edition was used to identify migraine or probable migraine cases. For those who were diagnosed with migraine at baseline, a migraine diary was used to record their migraine features monthly. In summary, we successfully established a cohort and followed it within 4 years period. The fulfillment of each objective was shown below. 1. Objective 1 (100% achieved). To characterize migraine features, women with migraine or probable migraine in the cohort were contacted monthly to provide their migraine diary for the preceding month. This diary included: 1) the date and duration of the migraine attack; 2) the intensity of the migraine attack; 3) any transient neurological disturbances; 4) any accompanying symptoms occurring concurrently with the migraine attack; 5) any medication to alleviate pain; 6) potential migraine triggers. Based on these data, we defined several metrics to describe migraine features: (1) Migraine attack frequency (MAF); (2) Migraine attack incidence (MAI); (3) Migraine duration per attack (MDA) and migraine duration per month (MDM); (4) Mean migraine intensity (MMI). Until December 2023, we have conducted around 48 months of migraine diary follow-ups and collected 7867 migraine diary reports. To characterize the cardiovascular risk profile, we calculated the Framingham 10-year general cardiovascular risk score (FRS) based on age, smoking, systolic blood pressure (SBP), blood glucose, total cholesterol (TC), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) for ALL women in the cohort. At baseline, the mean FRS of all women were 0.06±0.04. Most women (94.8%) were non-current smokers. The mean SBP, blood glucose, TC, and HDL-C were 123.68 mmHg, 6.44 mmol/L, 197.87 mg/dL, and 65.06 mg/dL, respectively. Details are shown in Paper 1 (refer to Part C). 2. Objective 2 (100% achieved). To determine whether migraineurs have unfavorable cardiovascular risk profile, we compared the baseline FRS, its components, and several other CVD-related factors between women with and without migraine. For FRS, since it was significantly associated with age, stratified analyses were conducted according to age groups. Women with migraine between 30-45 years displayed a slightly higher FRS compared to women without migraine and other headache (0.012 vs. 0.010). However, this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.150). By contrast, among those aged >45 years, migraineurs demonstrated a lower FRS than non-migraineurs (0.058 vs. 0.065, P<0.001). Additionally, compared to non-migraineurs, women with migraine had more current smokers (2.5% vs. 2.3%), more people who drunk alcohol ≥1 time/month (13.5% vs. 11.6%), lower people engaging in high level physical activity (58.3% vs. 67.1%), higher PSQI scores (7.77 vs. 6.04), higher PSS-14 scores (26.44 vs. 24.03), and higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C, 106.55 vs. 102.28 mg/dL) (all P<0.05). Conversely, women with migraine had lower ages (51.68 vs. 54.70 years), lower SBPs (118.45 vs. 124.15 mmHg), lower DBPs (74.65 vs. 76.34 mmHg), and lower hypertension prevalence (16.3% vs. 25.7%) than those without migraine (all P<0.05). Among the six components of the FRS, age and blood pressure were the top two factors with the largest weights. Furthermore, the two factors were highly related to each other, in other words, younger people typically demonstrate better blood pressure profile than older people. Consequently, in this study, the age might mask the contribution of migraine on the CVD risk among older women. Our results suggest that a longer time observation for those young women with migraine is needed. 3. Objective 3 (100% achieved). To investigate which CVD risk factors predict certain migraine features, we considered several baseline CVD-related factors as independent variables, and migraine features as the dependent variables for analysis. The overall obesity (β=1.33; 95% CI=0.26-2.40; P=0.015), PSQI score (β=0.26; 95% CI=0.13-0.39; P<0.001), PSS-14 score (β=0.08; 95% CI=0.01-0.16; P=0.030), and TC (β=0.01; 95% CI=0.001-0.03; P=0.029) were positively associated with MAF. Hypertension (β=2.55; 95% CI=0.08-5.03; P=0.045), overall obesity (β=1.73; 95% CI=0.30-3.16; P=0.019), central obesity (β=1.40; 95% CI=0.08-2.72; P=0.038), and PSQI score (β=0.27; 95% CI=0.10-0.44; P=0.002) were positively correlated with aMAF. DBP (β=0.73; 95% CI=0.01-1.45; P=0.049) and PSQI score (β=2.07; 95% CI=0.22-3.93; P=0.030) were positively associated with MDM. 4. Objectives 4 and 5 (100% achieved). To address these two objectives, all women with complete data on FRS at both waves were included. The independent variables were baseline migraine status, subtypes (with vs. without aura), and migraine severity/features. The dependent variable was the change of FRS and its components between baseline and second survey. Subgroup analyses were performed based on age groups (30-45 and >45 years). During a 1.17-year (±0.24) follow-up, women with migraine had a slightly higher FRS change than those without migraine (0.0010 vs. 0.0004). However, this difference did not exhibit statistical significance (P=0.363). When stratifying by age, among those aged >45 years, women with migraine exhibited a higher FRS change than those without migraine (0.0015 vs. 0.0004). For the components of FRS, compared to women without migraine, women with migraine had a significant decreased HDL-C (-3.08 vs. -1.35 mg/dL; P=0.036). Migraine subtype and migraine features were all not related to FRS change (all P>0.05). Notably, among women younger than 60 years, migraine with aura, higher frequency of attacks, higher intensity of headache, and longer duration of attack were all significantly associated with the higher growth of stroke risk score (all P<0.05). One plausible explanation for these findings is the short follow-up duration (1.15±0.24 years). CVDs are chronic diseases which need over ten years to develop. Therefore, it is reasonable that FRS did not have significant change between migraineurs and non-migraineurs within such a short follow-up period. In fact, although we did not observe a significant association, women with migraine displayed a faster CVD risk progression compared to those without migraine; migraine features were also significantly associated with stroke risk. Thus, extending the follow-up time (e.g., to 5-10 years) might reveal a more insightful relationship between migraine and CVD progression.

25101418.label: Major findings and research outcome
25101418.value: Until December of 2023, 5 papers are under review and 6 conference abstracts have been presented/accepted. The data mining work is still ongoing. Based on this unique women cohort in Hong Kong, we believe that more papers will be produced and published in the future. (1) The prevalence of migraine and probable migraine was 10.3% (436/4221) in this cohort. The median migraine attack frequency and duration were 0.96 attacks/month and 7.71 hours/attack, respectively. The intensity score was 5.28. The average FRS was 0.06 at baseline. The blood glucose and blood lipid levels were similar to the general HK women in the same age groups, indicating a good representativeness of our cohort data (Paper 1, please see Part C). (2) A 7-item lifestyle score was devised, where higher scores indicating better health. During a 1.17-year follow-up, 214 (10.7%) new metabolic syndrome cases occurred in the cohort. Higher combined lifestyle score was associated with lower metabolic syndrome incidence (Paper 2). A systematic review paper was then produced based on this topic (Paper 3). (3) Among women with migraine, overall obesity, central obesity, hypertension, PSQI score, PSS-14 score, blood pressure, TC, TG, and HDL-C were significantly associated with migraine features. An inverse relationship was found between a combination of lifestyle index and migraine prevalence (Paper 4). (4) The contribution of migraine on the risk of developing stroke was comparable with physical inactivity, SBP, BMI, and HDL-C (Paper 5 and Conference abstract 2). (5) Over an average 1.17-year follow-up period, women with migraine displayed a slightly faster growth of FRS and decreased HDL-C compared to those without migraine (paper in preparation). (6) Other significant findings: i. threshold effects existed in the associations of CVD risk with waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference (HC) (Conference abstract 1). ii. increased overall (when < 35%) and trunk body fat percentage (BFP) and decreased arm and leg BFP were associated with elevated CVD risk (Conference abstract 3). iii. Higher healthy lifestyle score was associated with lower risk of metabolic syndrome in the nested case-control study which integrated in the cohort (Conference abstract 4). iv. prolonged sitting time predicted higher WC, HC, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, and trunk body fat percentage (Conference abstract 5). v. women with migraine had higher progression of 10-year stroke risk than those without migraine; those with higher migraine burden (more serious migraine features) demonstrated faster progression of stroke risk (Conference abstract 6).

25101418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25101418.value: Our baseline data showed women with migraine had a slightly lower FRS than those without migraine. Paradoxically, despite this lower overall CVD risk score, migraineurs actually showed unfavourable cardiovascular health compared with non-migraineurs, including higher smoking and drinking, lower physical activity, poorer sleep, higher stress and LDL-C. The only exceptions were that migraineurs had lower ages and blood pressures than non-migraineurs in the cohort. Nevertheless, the last two factors had the largest weights when calculating FRS, which might partially explain the inverse association between migraine and FRS. Hence, it might be necessary to include more young participants to verify the findings. The growth of FRS from baseline to the second round of follow-up was higher in migraineurs than non-migraineurs, typically in those aged 65 or above. This result indicated that the progression of CVD could be faster in women with migraine, typically in old women, than in women without migraine. Although the difference in FRS growth had no statistical significance at the current stage, a plausible reason for this was the short follow-up period. CVDs typically require long-term observation for their progression. Thus, a long follow-up period will enable us to comprehensively observe the enough migraine burden on CVD progression.

25101418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25101418.value: We established a cohort of women living in Hong Kong for longitudinal evaluation of migraine features in relation to cardiovascular health. In total 4221 women aged 30 to 74 years were enrolled during 2019-2020, and 3433 of them finished the second-round survey during 2021-2022. In the first survey (baseline), 10.3% women were diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine. Half of them had at least 1 time migraine attack per month, and the headache intensity was moderate to severe. In all women, an average 6% likelihood of developing CVD within the forthcoming decade was estimated. Such CVD risk increased with age. We found a slightly higher CVD risk in migraineurs than non-migraineurs in young women group (30 to 45 years). Another interesting finding was, among old women, the progression of CVD was a little bit faster in migraineurs than non-migraineurs. In addition, obesity, hypertension, sleep, stress, blood pressure, TC, TG, and HDL-C were all significantly associated with migraine frequency, intensity and duration. Although longer term observation is needed to further verify the evidence, these findings are relevant for locating the subgroup of migraineurs who have the highest CVD risk, which may enable more effective treatment for those most likely to benefit.
