25103918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25103918.value: Gap junctions play a critical role in intercellular signal communication and modulation of visual signals in the retina. Gap junctions between amacrine cells (ACs) and ganglion cells (GCs) may tune the output signals of the GCs to the brain. There are at least 30 morphological subtypes of ACs coupled to 20 subtypes of GCs, which are independently coded to different aspects of the visual scene. However, very few of these ACs subtypes have been characterized with respect to the specific subtypes of GCs to which they are coupled in the retina, which is needed to fully understand the vision process. All basic visual information in the retina is physiologically divided into ON and OFF channels. Therefore, the first objective of this proposal is to identify the structure of the specific subtypes of ACs that are coupled to the two distinct GCs: G2(ON) and G3(OFF) GC. Using PoPro1, a novel fluorescent gap junction-permeant tracer that can be imaged in vivo, the specific subtypes of ACs that are coupled to and thereby form functional circuits with G2(ON) and G3(OFF) GC subtypes will be identified and recorded. Correlated firing in the visual system, mediated through gap junctions, transports precise information related to stimulus structure and position. The roles of coupled networks of ACs in modulating the activity of GCs are largely unknown in the retina. The second objective of this proposal is to determine the effect of coupling extent among ACs on the correlated firing of G2(ON) or G3(OFF) GCs pair and coupled G2(ON) GC-AC pair. This will be carried out by modulating ACs coupling extent with pharmacological agents to dissect out the communication pathways. Dual cell recording will be used to investigate the functional physiological properties of the coupling between ACs and GCs. Entrainment is mediated by gap junctions between adjacent cells. The role of entrainment is well known across physiological systems. The third objective of this proposal is to determine the mechanism of possible entrainment of activities between heterologous coupled ACs and G2(ON) GC. The proposed experiments focus on electrophysiological recording of retinal neurons and their labelling. The research will expand the understanding of the roles of gap junctions and amacrine cells in terms of the integration and propagation of visual signals. In addition, gap junctions have been implicated in many neurological diseases. The proposed work will nevertheless provide important insights into the roles of gap junctions throughout the brain. 電突觸在細胞間信號傳導,尤其在視網膜內視覺信號傳輸的過程中起關鍵作用。無長突細胞（Amacrine Cells, ACs）和神經節細胞（Ganglion Cells, GCs）之間的電突觸可以調控從GCs傳遞到大腦的視覺信號。至少有30種亞型的ACs與大約20種亞型，能獨立編碼不同視覺信息的GCs相藕連。這些和不同GCs亞型相藕聯的ACs的解剖和生理特性，是我們了解視覺傳導機制所必需的。 視網膜中基本的電生理信號分為開（ON）和關（OFF）通道。因此，本研究項目的第壹個目標是確定和“開”和“關”通道GCs（G2（ON）和G3（OFF）GCs）藕聯的特定的ACs細胞。使用PoPro1，壹種可以在體內成像的新型熒光電突觸滲透示蹤劑，將用來識別並記錄藕聯到G2（ON）和G3（OFF）GCs亞型的ACs的細胞解剖結構。 視覺系統中, 通過電突觸介導的細胞間協同激發可以傳遞與視覺刺激和位置相關的精確信息。而在視網膜中，我們對於和GCs 藕聯的ACs在視覺信號調節中的作用，在很大程度上是未知的。因此，本研究項目的第二個目的是確定ACs之間的藕聯範圍對G2（ON）或G3（OFF）GCs細胞之間以及G2（ON）GCs和藕聯的ACs細胞間協同激發的影響。我們將通過藥理學的方法改變ACs的藕聯來進行研究，同時應用雙細胞外膜片鉗技術研究ACs和GCs之間藕聯的電生理特性，以剖析GCs及其藕聯的ACs的視覺信號傳導。 細胞間控制激發是由相鄰細胞之間的電突觸介導。細胞間控制激發在生理系統中的功能是普遍存在。本研究項目的第三個目標是確定不同細胞間-藕聯ACs與G2（ON）GCs之間可能的細胞間控制激發機制。實驗將專註於視網膜神經元的電生理記錄及其標記。該研究將擴展我們對電突觸和無長突細胞在視覺信號的整合和傳導作用的理解。此外，由於電突觸和許多神經系統疾病相關，因此，本研究工作將對整個包括大腦在內的神經系統中電突觸的作用和功能也有重要的意義。

25103918.label: Realisation of objectives
25103918.value: 5.3 Realisation of objectives Aim 1: To characterize the various subtypes of amacrine cells (ACs) coupled to G2(ON) and G3(OFF) ganglion cell (GC) by using fluorescent gap junction-permeant tracer were achieved. The aim was achieved. To identify the subtypes of ACs coupled to G2(ON) and G3(OFF), Popro-1was injected into GCs to show the coupled ACs in living tissue. Then, Neurobiotin was injected to show the full detailed morphology of the coupled ACs. Anti-ChAT antibodies were used to determine the dendritic stratification. Regarding the ACs coupled to G2 GCs, 90% (19/21) of ACs were displaced ACs with somas located in the ganglion cell layer (GCL); only 10% of coupled ACs were located in the inner plexiform layer (IPL). 90% (19/21) of these ACs were wide-field ACs; only 10% were poly-axonal ACs. In contrast, all ACs (28/28) coupled with G3 GCs, their somas were located in INL. 96% (27/28) were wide-field ACs. All of the coupled ACs were co-stratified with dendrites of G3 GCs. The diameter of ACs coupled to G2 and G3 were 11.76±1.80 um (mean ± SEM) and 8.58±1.22 um, respectively. ACs coupled to G3 GCs were mainly round shape with 6-10 um in diameter, while ACs coupled to G2 GCs are large oval soma in diameter between 9-15 um. All these subtypes of ACs coupled to G2 and G3 GCs were located in the dendritic field of G2 and G3. Cx36 were found to co-localize in the dendritic cross between G2 and coupled ACs. The G3 GCs have homologous coupling to other G3 GCs and one type of ACs. The coupled ACs have small, round soma with 2-4 primary dendrites and ramified branches. G2 GCs have no coupling with other G3 but are coupled to 2 subtypes of ACs; most of ACs are displayed as wide-field ACs. Aim 2: To determine the effect of coupling extent among ACs on the correlated firing of G2(ON) or G3(OFF) GCs pair and coupled G2(ON) GC-AC pair. The aim was achieved. In order to test the effects of the gap junctional pathways on correlated firing between (a) the G2(ON) or G3(OFF) GCs pair and (b) G2 (ON) GC-AC pairs. The following research activities were completed: First, Neurobiotin intracellular injections were performed under light adaptation with photopic white light illumination. AII ACs injected with Neurobiotin displayed a number of coupled neighbors from approximately the first and secondary tier as the control retina group. Injection of Neurobiotin with activation of dopamine receptor 1 (D1R) by SKF38393 application (10 µM, n = 7) led to a decrease in the extent of Neurobiotin diffusion in AII–AII coupling (n = 10). In contrast, the application of low concentration D1R antagonist SCH23390 (5 µM, n = 6) dramatically increased AII–AII coupling. Dopamine receptor antagonist (SCH23390, 5 µm) application significantly increased AII ACs coupled cell numbers by Neurobiotin injection from 15 ± 3 (mean ± SD) in the control retina to 226.6 ± 43.2 µm. At the same time, the extent of the tracer coupled AII ACs rose from 77 ± 8.5 µm2 in control to 479 ± 41.5 µm2 in the SCH23390 treated retina. Second, paired recordings were performed between G2(ON)-G2; G3(OFF)-G3 GCs pair and between coupled G2(ON) and displaced AC pair in the Kcng4-YFP mice retina. At the same time, their correlated spiking patterns were analyzed and identified. Paired recording between G2 and G3 was performed as a negative control. D1R agonist-10 µM SKF38393 decreased the synchronized firing of spontaneous spikes in both ON α RGCs pairs (n=7) and OFF RGCs pairs (n=6). 6 of the ON α RGCs pairs lost their synchronized firing after 3 minutes 10 µM SKF38393 application. The spike correlation in one ON α RGCs pairs decreased 67% after 3 minutes 10 µM SKF38393 application. 6 pairs of OFF RGCs lost their synchronized firing. In contrast, 5 µM antagonist SCH23390 application (Figure 3) did not eliminate the synchronized firing of spontaneous spikes between cell pairs of ON α RGCs (n=6) after 3 minutes. After normalization, 4 of ON α RGCs decreased spike correlation by about 0.26 ± 0.1 (mean ± SEM); 2 of ON α RGCs decreased spike correlation by about 0.13. 5 µM antagonist SCH23390 application increased the synchronized firing of spontaneous spikes between cell pair of OFF α RGCs 0.37 ± 0.05 (mean ± SEM; n=7). It also revealed RGCs and displaced ACs were abolished by 10 µM D1R agonist SKF38393 after 3 minutes (n=5). D1R antagonist SCH2339 increased synchronized firing of CCFs of spontaneous spikes of the ON α RGCs and coupled displaced AC (after normalization. 0.43 ± 0.1, mean ± SEM; n=5). With the coupling of ACs increased, the synchronized cell firing pattern also changed. With the time-lapse, the synchrony of RGC-AC also increased, which might indicate more coupled ACs were involved in the synchronized firing of spontaneous spikes of the coupled ON α RGC-ACs. Aim 3: To determine the mechanism of entrainment of activities between coupled ACs and G2(ON) GC. The aim was achieved. First, The experiment further explores whether one cell could induce the spikes or drive the spike in another coupled cell between the different cell types in the retina. An ON RGC was hold with a whole-cells patch and then stimulated with a serial burst of currents with 3 and 5 Hz 10pA followed by 10Hz of 5pA and 10pA. The spikes of nearby AC were induced and recorded (n=6). The CCF computed from the pair of ON α-RGCs and AC indicated the synchronous firing relationship. The ON α RGC and the coupled ACs were double confirmed by PoProl-1 injection. Then, to test whether AC can also drive the spikes of coupled RGC. The nearby AC was patched and stimulated by a serial burst of currents of 3 and 5 Hz 10pA followed by 10Hz of 5pA and 10pA (n=5). The AC can also induce the spikes in coupled RGC and drive the firing of RGC with the synchronous pattern. The frequency tested for cell drive up to 900Hz. However, high-frequency burst of currents can't induce the spikes in the coupled cell. Second, 5 days ChR2(L132C)-AAV viral vector infected retinas were generated. The pair of coupled ON α RGC-ACs with one cell with ChR2-GFP expressing was examined to determine whether one cell spikes can drive the spikes of another coupled cell. 525nm light-induced spikes on both ON α RGC and direct-coupled displaced AC (ChR2) pairs. Then, 460 nm blue light induced the strong spikes of both cells. Displaced AC retained the light response, but the ON α-RGC with ChR2 without ChR2 lost their light response after applying the gap junction blocker 50 µm MFA. Cx36 knockout mice were tested to determine whether Cx36 played a major role in the concerted activity. There was no induced light response in ON α-RGC without ChR2. Thus, these experiments showed that one cell could drive another cell firing via gap junctions in the retina. In summary, three aims are all achieved. There are still some results from Aims that are being reviewed for publication.

25103918.label: Major findings and research outcome
25103918.value: The research investigated the anatomy of two representative retinal ganglion cells (GCs)-G2(ON) and G3(OFF)- and their coupled amacrine cells (ACs). The goal was to understand how their essential physiological functions tune the correlated firing of GCs and ACs, which transmits basic visual information to central brain structures. Aim 1 of the research is to identify the subtypes of ACs coupled to G2(ON) and G3(OFF) GC by using fluorescent gap junction-permeant tracer. The results of this research have been published or are currently under review in the following papers. 1: Cells. 2020 Mar; 9(3): 530. 2: Cells. 2019 Jul; 8(7): 640. 3: Front. Cell. The results of this research have been published or are currently under review in the following papers. 1: FASEB J. 2020 Nov;34(11):15282-15299. 2: Front. Cell. Neurosci. 14:124. 3: Vis Neurosci. 2021 May 14;38:E008. 4: "Nonlinear Dynamics in the myopic mouse retina" under review. 5: "Restoring Light Responses by Implantation of Biomimic ZnIn2S4/NGQD Microspheres-based Artificial Photoreceptors in a Retinal Degeneration Mouse Model". In preparation. Aim 3 of the research is to determine the mechanism of entrainment of activities between coupled ACs and G2(ON) GC. The results of this research have been published or are currently under review in the following papers. 1: Neuronal firing between retinal ganglion cells and coupled amacrine cells in the mouse retina. Paper presentation in 2022 "The Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO) meeting" and awarded Robert Miller Travel Grant. 2: "Cell firing between retinal ganglion cell and coupled amacrine cells in the mouse retina." In preparation. This research will help in better understanding the crucial processes involved in coding and potentially decoding visual signals. The results will also contribute to expanding our comprehension of the roles of gap junctions in the retina regarding the transmission of visual signals.

25103918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25103918.value: The future research plan aims to investigate the response characteristics resulting from different gap junctional pathways in the two basic retinal pathways, known as "ON" and "OFF," that converge onto retinal ganglion cell (GCs). Most GCs and ACs in the retina use a protein called connexin 36, while connexin 45 is only used in some GCs. The coupling between GC and AC will tune and code the visual information in GC delivered to the central nervous system. The next step of the research will focus on how different subtypes of ACs or connexin proteins affect the GC signaling. This will help us understand how visual signals are coded and decoded in the retina. Furthermore, the findings will expand our understanding of the roles of gap junctions in the central nervous system.

25103918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25103918.value: The retina is a thin tissue that lines the inner surface at the back of the eye, where all visual information is generated and sent to the brain to create the images we see. A retinal ganglion cell (GC) is a type of neuron located near the inner surface of the eye's retina that codes all visual information. This research investigates the anatomy of two representative GCs, G2(ON) and G3(OFF), along with their coupled amacrine cells (ACs) via gap junctions, and their essential physiological functions. The results from electrophysiological recording of retinal GCs and their labeling will expand our understanding of the roles of gap junctions in the integration and propagation of visual signals. Additionally, gap junctions have been implicated in many neurological diseases. The proposed work will provide important insights into the roles of gap junctions throughout the brain. Overall, this research has the potential to significantly contribute to our understanding of the retina and its neuronal networks, as well as contribute to the development of treatments for neurological diseases related to gap junctions.

25208118.label: Realisation of objectives
25208118.value: (1) The first objective: Deepening and broadening the generic life cycle sustainability assessment framework to incorporate the interactions among the criteria for sustainability assessment (rather than neglecting the interactions) for investigating the environmental impacts, economic performances, and social influences of sludge-to-energy processes simultaneously. This objective has been successfully achieved (100% achieved). More specifically, we have done the following work: (i) developing a new framework for life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA) of sludge valorization technologies, and the coupling coordination between economic development, environmental impacts and social acceptability has been incorporated in life cycle sustainability assessment; (ii) proposing a novel exergy-economic-environmental (3E) sustainability analysis model for sustainability assessment of a new sludge-to-methanol route and investigating the optimum operating conditions of this technology for better sustainability performances; and (iii) developing a quantitative and scientific framework for LCSA by combining data envelopment analysis (DEA) and life cycle thinking by quantifying both soft criteria (especially social indicators) and hard criteria, which can guarantee the accuracy of the results of LCSA. All in all, we have developed various new methods to improve the traditional life cycle sustainability assessment framework with the considerations of the interactions among the criteria for sustainability assessment. (2) The second objective: Developing the multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making methods that can incorporate the preferences of all the stakeholders (rather than only considering the preferences of a specific group of decision-makers) for prioritizing the sludge-to-energy options. This objective has been successfully achieved (100% achieved) with the completion of the following work: (i) proposing a novel sustainability-interval-index conceptual framework for multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making by developing a multi-actor fuzzy best-worst method which can integrate the preferences of multiple stakeholders in complex decision-making problems; (ii) developing a multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making framework based on game theory and multi-criteria decision-making approach to solve the decision-making problems with conflicting interests of different groups of stakeholders, and a two-player game between the sludge treatment facility and the government was selected to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework; (iii) developing a generic multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making framework based on fuzzy AHP and intuitionistic fuzzy GRA for sludge valorization technologies prioritization. All the above-mentioned methods developed in this project have been verified to be effective to address the multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making problems with flexibility and reliability. (3) The third objective: Developing a mathematical model using sustainability as the objective (rather than neglecting the social and environmental objectives) for selecting the most sustainable sludge-to-energy technology from a life cycle perspective. This objective has been successfully achieved (100% achieved). To achieve this objective, the following work has been conducted: (i) developing a novel life cycle composite footprint index with the consideration of environmental impacts and technical performance to assess and prioritize the sludge-to-energy technologies according to their sustainability performances with an estimation of the energy recovery rate around 27% for the most preferred technique route; (ii) developing an innovative life cycle sustainability-interval-index for sustainability-oriented assessment and prioritization of sewage-to-energy technologies which can not only integrate the opinions of different groups of stakeholders, but also consider the economic, environmental, technological and social indicators simultaneously; (iii) proposing different methodology frameworks to address the decision-making problems with uncertainty (such as hybrid information or missing information) for ranking different sludge valorization technologies considering the performances of four sustainability pillars, including interval analytic hierarchy process (IAHP) combined with TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution), Dempster-Shafer (DS) theory and fuzzy best-worst method (BWM), Z-number BWM together with the ELECTRE method, and an improved Grey Relational Analysis (GRA); (iv) establishing a three-layer optimization model based on mixed integer programming for sustainable sewage-to-energy supply chain design by minimizing the total costs with the consideration of environmental constraints; and (v) developing a novel decision-making framework based on process simulation and fuzzy PROMETHEE II method which incorporates the performances of environmental, economic, technical and social aspects for sustainability assessment and ranking of different sludge valorization technologies. All the above-mentioned methods have been demonstrated by case studies and analyzed in detail to verify their feasibility and robustness. The results also provided important insights to guide technology improvement and decision-making. In one word, this objective has been achieved completely by developing different sustainability-oriented assessment and decision-making methods that incorporate multiple dimensions of sustainability.

25208118.label: Major findings and research outcome
25208118.value: 13 papers and 5 book chapters have been published, and the outcomes have also been presented at international conferences. The main findings are summarized as follows: (i) The developed novel gasification-based sludge-to-methanol process was examined through process simulation and 3E (economic, environmental, and exergy) analysis. The influence of the operational parameters on economic, environmental, and exergy sustainability was investigated and the results indicated that the cost of methanol produced by using sludge valorization technology is around 579.6 $/ton with a sludge disposal cost of 39.6 $/ton. The internal rate of return (IRR) with a subsidy of 20 $/ton sludge and without support was estimated to be 10.20% and 5.48%, respectively. As for the environmental and technical aspects, results revealed that the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission was 3.21 kg eq. CO2/kg methanol and the exergy efficiency was 37.92%. These results provide significant implications for decision-makers to achieve sustainable sludge management. (ii) A multi-criteria decision-making model combined with game theory was constructed to handle the decision-making problems with multiple stakeholders. Four sludge treatment strategies were considered as the alternatives for the sludge treatment facility (STF) and the government (Gov). The environmental sustainability is the most important according to the preferences of both stakeholders, but the STF also emphasized on the importance of technological aspect while the Gov focused more on the social pillar. Results of the case study showed that the interactions between the sludge treatment facility and the government can guarantee the robustness of the decision-making results, and biogas from sludge digestion for electricity generation by fuel cells was recognized as the most suitable alternative by both the stakeholders with a consensus of tipping fee $0.19-7.59 per kWh net electricity generation in this context. (iii) Four sludge-to-electricity technologies have been studied considering four sustainability pillars, including sludge incineration for electricity generation (S1), biogas from anaerobic digestion (AD) process of sludge for power generation by fuel cells (S2), biogas from AD of sludge for electricity generation by combustion gas engine (S3), and pretreated sludge for electricity generation by microbial fuel cells (MFCs) (S4). The results revealed that the most superior technology is S1, followed by S3, and the inferior one is S4 due to technology immaturity. The ranking could be different from those studies that only considered economic or/and environmental aspects, and it also reveals the necessity of integrating other sustainability pillars to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the technologies for sewage sludge treatment.

25208118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25208118.value: The new life cycle sustainability assessment frameworks have been established for sewage sludge technology improvement and sustainability-oriented decision-making by considering the interactions between social-economic and environmental indicators. Different multi-stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making methods have been developed to effectively solve complex decision-making problems considering the preferences of different groups of stakeholders, even with conflicting interests. A composite sustainability index which integrates environmental, economic, social, and technological aspects has been developed for selecting the most sustainable sludge treatment technology. With the proposed sustainability index, the overall sustainability performance of a sludge-to-value-added-products technology can be measured, which can further provide valuable implications for technology prioritization. Although the models developed in this study have covered many kinds of complicated sustainability-oriented decision-making problems for sludge valorization technology prioritization, the temporal and spatial effects are still not discussed and integrated into sustainability assessment and decision-making. Since the sludge management facilities usually operate over decades in different regions, it is necessary to develop a dynamic life cycle sustainability assessment and decision-making framework that can incorporate temporal and spatial differences. The dynamic LCSA by combining systems dynamics and traditional LCSA for sludge treatment technology assessment will be developed in the future.

25208118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25208118.value: Sewage sludge with an estimation of around 30,000 m3/day generated in Hong Kong, can potentially cause serious environmental problems and threaten human health if treated improperly due to harmful components in sewage sludge. Sewage sludge valorization which can convert waste into value-added products has been recognized as a promising technology for sludge management. This project focused on developing advanced life cycle sustainability assessment and decision-making tools for achieving sustainable sludge management. This project established a multi-layer decision support framework from life cycle thinking to promote sustainable sewage sludge management, including a life cycle composite index for sustainability assessment, sustainability-oriented optimization model incorporating economic, environmental and social indicators, and multiple stakeholder multi-criteria decision-making framework. Case studies were carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The sustainability performance in environmental, economic, social, and technological aspects and the ranking of sludge valorization technologies were obtained. The managerial and policy implications were also proposed based on the results, and they can help to improve the sustainability performances of sludge treatment technologies and make informed decisions according to the preferences of different stakeholders. Effective measures and policies were also proposed for sustainable treatment of sewage sludge.

25208218.label: Project Objectives
25208218.value: The objectives have been reduced from originally 4 to 3 due to limited funding support (from original application HKD 1,443,400 to funding awarded HKD 700, 000). Synthesise PLLA brush-grafted MSNs and load these with drugs. We will study the effect of various parameters (e.g., chain length and grafting density of PLLA brush) on the drug release profile and fine-tune these parameters to achieve optimal drug loading capacity, efficiency and drug release rates. Fabricate drug-loaded electrospun core-shell fibres. We will load the PLLA brush-grafted MSNs with anti-scarring drugs before incorporating into electrospun core (HA) - shell (PLLA) fibres and coat the resultant fibres with bFGF. We will study the effect of various parameters (e.g., fibre diameter, MSN concentration, fibre swelling and degradation) on the drug release profile and adjust these parameters to achieve optimal drug release rates. Characterise and optimise the physical and biological properties of the drug-loaded electrospun core-shell fibres in vitro. We will establish the relationship between the biocompatibility of the core-shell fibres and how the drug release rates modulate the behaviours and functions of the fibroblasts seeded on the fibrous scaffolds to elucidate the mechanism of how long-term drug release inhibits HSc formation.

25208218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25208218.value: 增生性疤痕（HSc）的形成是皮膚修復常見的併發症，可導致生理疼痛、殘疾以及社會心理障礙。調查發現，該疾病每年在中國大陸和香港影響人數超過5000萬，給家庭和社會造成了嚴重負擔。目前的治療策略（如在病灶處注射皮質類固醇）由於不能在抑制HSc形成的同時支持傷口癒合，僅取得了有限的療效。因此，本課題組計畫研發一種電紡絲納米纖維支架，可在支持傷口癒合的情況下減少HSc的形成。該支架在結構上類似于天然細胞外基質（ECM），具有較大的表面積以促進營養交換，並且可結合各種治療藥物來調節組織細胞的行為和功能。本課題組在前期研究工作中製作了具有鹼性成纖維細胞生長因子（bFGF）塗層的載抗疤痕藥人參皂苷Rg3聚乳酸-羥基乙酸共聚物（PLGA）電紡纖維支架。實驗證明，該支架可促進傷口癒合，同時可減少HSc的形成。然而，由於藥物擴散路線太短，該系統中Rg3釋放僅持續了30天，無法達到HSc預防所需的90天持續釋放的目標。為了進一步延長藥物擴散路徑，本課題組將抗疤痕藥物載入到介孔二氧化矽納米顆粒（MSNs）中，並將其與聚乳酸（PLLA）電紡纖維混紡，將藥物釋放時間延長到70天。但是，MSNs的引入增加了纖維的疏水性，不利於細胞粘附和增殖；此外，藥物釋放的持續時間仍低於HSc預防的要求（>90天）。 鑒於此，本項目旨在提高藥物釋放持續時間的同時，保持納米纖維表面結構和性能的完整性，以實現無HSc傷口癒合。本課題中，我們提出通過嫁接不同鏈長和密度的PLLA分子刷來修飾MSN表面，從而精確調控藥物釋放速率。具體來說，我們將合成嫁接了PLLA的MSNs，將其載入抗疤痕藥物後，放入到具有核（透明質酸（HA））-殼（PLLA）結構的電紡纖維中，以延長藥物的釋放。此外，在合成纖維的表面進一步接枝bFGF，以獲得更好的細胞粘附和增殖。最後，本課題組將全面研究和優化這些纖維支架的表面形貌、疏水性、藥物釋放、吸水、降解和生物學特性以及其對早期創面癒合和晚期HSc抑制的治療效果。該項目的成功完成將促進支持細胞生長和長效藥物釋放支架體系的發展。此外，本項目的研究成果對於制定針對不同疾病狀態的早期組織再生和晚期併發症預防的綜合治療策略也至關重要。

25208218.label: Realisation of objectives
25208218.value: (1). Objective 1. PLLA-grafted MSN synthesis and drug loading In the original proposal, we proposed a long-term drug releasing electrospun fibrous scaffold with core-shell design, imbued with gatekeeping nanoparticles as condensed drug reservoirs to achieve the much-desired >90 day release profile corresponding to typical wound healing cycle. Firstly, we have successfully synthesized mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) via the Stober method. Here we made slight modifications to prepare MSN-PLA as we found the modification rate to substitute the surface groups to amine groups from hydroxyl groups is relatively low and the macromolecular reaction to graft PLA to the surface of MSN-NH2 is quite hard. We then attempted another approach towards grafting PLA on the surface commercial MSN-COOH (Sigma-Aldrich; 200 nm diameter, 4 nm pore size). Using lactide monomers and Tin(II) 2-ethylhexanoate as catalyst, we successfully grafted PLA chains onto MSN-COOH. The polymer brush length could be readily adjusted through controlling reaction time. Successful functionalization was verified using FTIR spectrometer and the amount of PLLA grafted on is quantified by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). These results collectively suggested that the pore size of MSNs can be tunably reduced through the additive grafting of polymer brushes for delaying drug release. We then took MSN-PLA to attempt loading model drug doxorubicin (DOX) owing to its small molecular size and high polarity. For drug release assessment, MSN-PLA-DOX were dispersed in PBS and released DOX concentration was quantified with UV-vis spectrometry at absorbance of 480 nm. The drug release curve shown DOX molecules were retained significantly by PLA brushes gatekeeper, which demonstrated the long-term release potential of our nanocarriers under a controlled environment. To ensure the slowly releasing DOX retains its inhibitory effect against fibroblasts, 3T3 human fibroblasts was used as a preliminary cytotoxicity test for the nanocarriers. At both 24 and 48 h after exposure to MSN-PLA-DOX infused medium, cell proliferation of 3T3s was significantly hindered even at dilution ratios up to 100x, indicating the slow release of DOX still inhibited fibroblast activity. To conclude, we have successfully synthesized MSN-PLA using the “graft-from” approach, optimized brush length and density through tuning reaction time, and loaded model drug DOX into MSN-PLA holes for inhibition of fibroblast proliferation. (2). Objective 2. Fabrication of drug-loaded electrospun core-shell fibres Following the proposal, after establishment of anti-scarring agent nanocarriers MSN-PLA-DOX, we attempted to synthesize electrospun fibres to achieve localized release and extension of drug diffusion distance. Co-axial spinning method was employed with ethanol as the core solution (MSN-PLA-DOX) to avoid direct mixing of nanoparticles with shell solution (PLA in hexafluoro-2-propanol, HFIP) to prevent the leakage of DOX into the surroundings due to the open-up of PLA brushes in HFIP. We then encapsulated different amount of MSN-PLA-DOX (10, 20, or 50 mg) to ensure appropriate drug release amount for anti-scarring therapy. The formed fibre groups were characterized after air drying by TEM. For all concentration groups, MSNs could be observed to be centered within the fibre lumen, but with vastly altered fibre morphologies owing to their occupied space within the fibres, in which 50 mg/mL exhibited clusters of MSNs within the fibre lumen with the highest fibre diameter. These varied morphologies also directly impacted the mechanical properties of the electrospun scaffolds. Naturally, the higher the solute content of an electrospun fibre, the lower the tensile stress as nanocarriers create flaws in the fibres’ cross sections. This phenomenon was observed between the pure PLA, 10 and 20 mg/mL fibre groups, while the clusters of MSNs in the 50 mg/mL simultaneously enlarged the fibre size, causing an improvement in tensile modulus instead. Nevertheless, the tensile modulus of all fibre groups well exceeded the range of healed skin tissues. Despite the large differences in morphology, the drug release kinetics of all 3 MSN fibres remain similar with the ability of long-term sustained release of encapsulated molecules presumably owing to the protection of carriers from contact from HFIP. To conclude, we have successfully fabricated MSN-PLA-DOX loaded electrospun polymeric fibres for long-term function, as well as all fibres are equipped with sufficient mechanical strength. (3). Objective 3. Characterisation and optimisation of physical and biological properties of the drug-loaded electrospun core-shell fibres in vitro. Compared with the performance of nanocarriers alone, the lengthy spinning process and the brief, partial exposure of MSN-PLA-DOX to spinning solvents at the needle tip might have led to slight blending of DOX within the fibre shell, which could possibly create concerns for excessive initial inhibition of other cell types integral to wound healing. Thus, dosage control for this long-term release strategy is extremely important to ensure the complete healing of exposed wound beds. Preliminary dosage assessment was performed by indirect contact cytotoxicity assessment at designated time points over the average wound healing cycle. Varied inhibition was observed in all fibre groups compared with pure PLA control early, but differences became less significant for later time points except for 50 mg/mL groups. Additionally, adhesion assessment was performed to ensure that the cytotoxicity was controlled as fibroblast adhesion was vital to achieving wound closure and completing the wound cycle; the DOX concentration could not be oversaturated that it rendered native cells incapable of performing reparative functions. Actin staining displayed that all groups was able to support fibroblast adhesion. Notably, less cell spreading was observed in 50 mg/mL groups and the average cell size was quantified to be nearly half of other groups on both day 0 and day 90. To conclude, results showed that the inhibitory effect of our long-term release scaffolds was able to sustain beyond 90 days without majorly hindering the basic cellular functions of fibroblasts. (4). Evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of the drug-loaded electrospun core-shell fibres in vivo. We selected rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model for further assessment to establish the scaffold clinical relevancy, owing to its scarring reproducibility and responsiveness in an in vivo setting. After establishing circular wound on the ears of New Zealand White Rabbits, the rabbits were treated with pure PLA, 20 and 50 mg/mL MSN-PLA-DOX doped scaffolds. We found that 20 mg/mL group showed the flattest wound healing, while 50 mg/mL group displayed a visible delay in the healing process. Histological analysis (e.g., H&E staining) revealed 20 mg/mL group substantially inhibited granulation tissue formation owing to scar elevation index (SEI) and epidermal thickness index (ETI) of 20 mg/mL group were the lowest among all groups. To quantifiably assess the long-term treatment efficacy of our scaffolds, the expression of typical scar-associated genes collagen-I (Col-1), collagen-III (Col-3) and transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) was characterized using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Significant reduction in expression levels for all 3 genes was observed for 20 and 50 mg/mL groups, suggesting the fundamental alteration of cellular activity at the healed tissues. However, despite the 50 mg/mL group maximumly downregulated the expression of all 3 genes, significant scar formation was still observed on the rabbit wounds. These results suggested that only at certain dosages are long-term release scaffolds effective at inhibiting scar formation, and that the cautionary signs observed during the in vitro dosage assessment were amplified when performed on a living specimen with complex physiological microenvironments. To conclude, our long-term release scaffolds could linger beyond the drug release profile within native cells and prevent a relapse of hypertrophic tissues, hence effectively inhibit scar formation during the healing process.

25208218.label: Major findings and research outcome
25208218.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a novel surface modification method that has (a) facilitated incorporation of drug-loaded MSNs into electrospun polymeric fibres and (b) enabled extended drug release over 90 days, thus suppressing hypertrophic scar formation in the later-stage of wound healing. Through manipulating the chain length and grafting density of PLA brush, the morphology and structure of PLA brush layer were readily modified to fine-tune the drug release rates. Following incorporation of a model drug DOX into the MSNs with PLA brush, cell proliferation of 3T3s was significantly hindered even at dilution ratios up to 100x, indicating the slow release of DOX still inhibit fibroblast activity. A novel co-axial spinning method exploiting the difference in solvent volatility and solubility was also developed to fabricate core-shell fibres with ethanol as the core solution (MSN-PLA-DOX) to avoid direct mixing of nanoparticles with shell solution (PLA in HFIP), which prevented the leakage of DOX into the surroundings due to the open-up of PLA brushes in HFIP. With the increase in loaded MSN-PLA-DOX content, MSN-PLA-DOX nanoparticles also aided in the increase of fibre diameter and mechanical strength. We also proved drug release kinetics of all fibres remain similar with the ability of long-term sustained release of encapsulated molecules, which assured continuous release of DOX over 90 days. Furthermore, we demonstrated the great biocompatibility of fibrous scaffolds by indirect contact cytotoxicity assessment at designated time points over the average wound healing cycle. Encouraged by the preliminary evaluation about scaffolds, we then assessed typical cellular functions and found DOX concentration (10 and 20 mg/mL MSN-PLA-DOX) had negligible impact to cell activities, including cell adhesion, cell spreading and reparative process. After the anti-scarring property has been validated at cellular level, rabbit ear wound model was employed to demonstrate in vivo anti-scarring activity of scaffolds. Wound photographs and histological staining proved 20 mg/mL MSN-PLA-DOX scaffolds could efficiently inhibit scar formation in terms of considerable downregulation of the expression of 3 typical scar-associated genes. In short, the prepared fibrous scaffolds enabled long-term drug release for inhibition of fibroblast activity without majorly hindering the basic cellular functions of fibroblasts. The related outcome was published in two papers, 1 Elsevier journal Applied Materials Today with the title of Evaporation-based, co-axial lock-and-key fibrous reservoir for long-term prevention of hypertrophic scars and 2 Elsevier journal Drug Discovery Today with the title of Petite miracles: insight into the nano-management of scarless wound healing (refers to Part C).

25208218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25208218.value: The promising results of our long-term release fibrous drug delivery system grant it great potential in combination with other therapies to achieve extended therapeutic potential. Despite the favourable cell adhesion assessment results, however, PLA was only used as a proof-of-concept for the long-term release strategy owing to its widespread usage and experimentation, as well as general spinnability. Improved scaffold properties such as tissue adhesiveness could be further achieved by co-spinning various tissue adhesive bulk polymer solutions such as gelatin methacryloyl without altering the core concept of this study. To achieve smart drug release, we can also modify our system to incorporate an enzyme-sensitive ligand on the surface of nanoparticles before grafting of PLA gatekeepers, which allows for minimal drug leakage and simultaneously activation of drug release when programmed conditions are met (cleaving of ligand by enzymes) to achieve on-demand drug delivery. In addition, the PLA gatekeepers could be substituted with positively charged polyethylenimine (PEI) to achieve gatekeeping and passive loading of negatively charged molecules. The non-rigorous requirements and simple mechanism of our long-term drug releasing electrospun fibrous scaffolds possess high adaptability and translation into clinical application and solve other tissue engineering problems including inhibition of cancer development and tendon adhesion.

25208218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25208218.value: Many diseases and conditions such as hypertrophic scarring require long-term maintenance over the healing cycle to achieve full recovery. However, there is a lack of wound dressings that can sustain over 90 days of therapeutic release. In this project, inspired by the enhancement of wound healing by the nanofibrous morphology and diverse structures of electrospinning, we fabricated an evaporation-based co-axial electrospun fibrous scaffold incorporating polymer brush gatekeeper nanocarriers for sustained delivery of therapeutics. The release rates of the system were demonstrated to be tunable through polymer graft length. As a proof-of-concept, we target hypertrophic scarring by loading the system with doxorubicin, which led to inhibition of fibroblast activity without interfering with cell adhesion. Application of our scaffolds on rabbit ear hypertrophic scar models displayed that our scaffolds effectively reduced collagen density and scar-related gene expression in healing tissues, with improved tissue elevation outcomes. We envision that our long-term release scaffolds will also be useful in combating long unresolved clinical dilemmas such as tendon adhesion and tumor regression.

25211018.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25211018.value: 考慮動態交通變化和道路之間相關性的多目標道路管理系統

25211018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25211018.value: Periodic and adequate pavement management is an important responsibility for departments of transportation (DOTs) to maintain their deteriorating pavement assets above critical service levels. This also stems from the fact that poor pavement condition has direct effects on road users, increasing their vehicle wear and tear as well as their fuel consumption associated with user costs and environmental impacts such as greenhouse gas emissions. Moreover, poorly managed pavement infrastructure may reduce system performance such as network capacity and connectivity. Thus, it is necessary to pursue multiple objectives in pavement management planning. In populated and dense cities like Hong Kong, traffic disruptions resulting from work zones are significant, so understanding the interplay between traffic dynamics and pavement management system is essential. During constructions, complete or partial roadway closures yield traffic congestions from the work zones to upstream. Moreover, detours result in extra travel time and distance across nearby networks. As opposed to this short-term adverse impact, once a managerial activity is applied, it improves pavement condition and decelerates the deterioration speed, bringing long-term benefits. The trade-offs between the short-term adverse and long-term positive impacts influence decision-making in the hierarchical levels consisting of activity-specific level, site-specific level and system level. In this proposal, we outline research into how spatial and temporal dynamics manifest themselves in the context of deterioration. We will discover how DOTs can better manage the system to make effective decisions, including the selection of maintenance, rehabilitation and reconstruction (MR&R) activities as well as inspection decisions to apply to different pavement segments during each period of a given planning horizon, in the context of multiple criteria. However, understanding the dynamic interplay and finding the optimal management planning may require high-level of computational power, thus we will introduce mathematical schemes based on practically reasonable assumptions, which can reduce the complexity of the optimization process. We will demonstrate the proposed solution methodology using real-world examples from the large-scale pavement networks in Hong Kong and the San Francisco Bay Area. 為了使路面維持壹定的服務水平，公路部門需要對路面進行定期和適當的維護管理。這是因為不良的路面狀況會導致使用者的車輛磨損，燃料消耗增加，從而造成用戶成本增加以及產生負面的環境效應。此外，如果路面系統管理不善，會使得路網的容量，連接性以及其他性能指標降低。因此，在路面管理規劃中追求多目標協同優化非常重要。 理解交通動態變化和路面管理系統之間的相互作用至關重要，尤其是對於像香港這樣的人口稠密型城市。因為路面施工維護會導致路網的中斷。這不僅僅因為道路封閉導致路網容量減小，同時也因為與之相關的車輛繞行造成的附近路網行程時間的增加。 盡管路面維修會造成短時間的路網中斷，產生額外的交通擁堵，但路面狀況的改善卻可以帶來長期效益。其中的利益權衡在多個層次影響著整個決策過程，包括施工層次，選址層次和整個道路系統層次。 在這個提案中，我們概述了時間和空間的動態變化是如何表現的。我們將探索公路部門應如何做出高效決策，更好地管理路面系統，包括給定規劃期間不同路面不同時期的維護，修復和重建，以及路段的監測檢查。然而，理解動態的相互作用並找到最佳的管理方案可能需要較高水平的計算能力。因此，我們將引入壹些數學方法以降低原問題的復雜度， 從而找到高效的優化方法以保證全局最優或至少局部最優。我們將使用來自香港和舊金山灣區路面網絡作為實例來演示我們所提出的方案，並就該路網環境和政府預算提出更好的管理方案。

25215318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25215318.value: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is an age-related progressive condition in which venous pooling reduces venous return in lower limbs. Elastic compression stockings (ECSs) have become a cornerstone to prevent and treat CVI through delivering gradient pressures to improve venous return. However, high noncompliance and poor acceptability are the major obstacles affecting effectiveness of ECSs among the seniors. The undistinguished pressure strategies with less considering seniors’ varied tolerance to pressure stimuli, and the lack of theoretical guidance for technical design of optimal pressure are the prominent limitation. To address this problem, this project aims to develop and validate a new scientific pressure design technology applying coupled fluid-solid model and optimization algorithm to achieve balanced comfort and mechanical function of ECSs for senior subjects. The essentials of design optimization involve fabric properties in elastic and shear moduli, mass density and thickness at different heights along the ECSs shells. It is challenging because interactions among elastic fabrics, comfort perception and multiple bio-components in viscoelastic legs are highly complex. Little reported work has unrealistically modeled ECSs as homogeneous shells with one single pressure level, and no referable methods are available to optimize ECSs design to attain both subjective comfort and hemodynamic improvements. This proposal will originally develop fluid-solid coupling models integrating nonlinear finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics model system to provide a quantitative insight into the mechanical responses of soft tissues and venous flows by ECSs. To realistically simulate interactions between lower limbs and stockings, the leg tissues moduli of subjects aged 60-75 years representing different leg sizes will be determined by the advanced ultrasound elastography. A series of algorithm-driven iterations of the coupling models will be run to simulate skin pressures and venous flows by ECSs with various designed pressure levels and gradient ratios. By employing optimization algorithm, the optimum fabric parameters will be determined when the simulated venous flows achieve the maximum values, and the simulated skin pressures fall within the comfort pressure range determined by the subjective assessments. Both the optimal simulated pressures and flow rates by the coupling models will be validated against the experimental data; and the determined optimal fabric parameters will be further applied into the new ECSs for the senior subjects to improve user’s compliance in practice. This advanced technology will open a new way for compression textiles design and will have profound impact on functional textiles for healthcare, medical, rehabilitation and other promising applications. 慢性靜脈功能不全(CVI)是一種隨年齡增長而加重的進展性炎症反應疾病。靜脈血流淤積影響靜脈迴流，造成下肢血循環不暢。彈性壓力襪通過施加梯度壓力於下肢改善血循環已成爲預防和治療CVI的基石。然而，在實際使用中低依從率和接受度已成爲影響長者穿用的主要障礙。目前壓力襪設計無年齡區分，缺乏對長者壓感忍受度變異的考慮，且沒有可以參考的壓力優化理論做設計指導，從而限制了壓力襪這一物理治療手段在 長者人羣中的應用。爲了解決這個問題，此項研究目的在於建立和驗證具有科學依據的壓力設計技術和系統，通過建立流固耦合模型和優化算法，探索適合於特定年齡人羣穿用的兼具舒適性與力學功能的壓力治療途徑。壓力襪彈性材料、 穿着舒適度和具有異構質粘彈性生物組織性能的下肢之間發生複雜的相互作用，有效模擬及分析其間的作用機制具有挑戰性。此項創新研究通過建立流固耦合模型提供一個能量化監測壓力紡織材料性能設計對人體軟組織力學效果和血流動力學的方法。不同位置彈性材料的楊氏模量、剪切模量、質量密度、厚度等力學性能的設計優化是研究重點。 爲了更加真實模擬年長者下肢與彈力襪間的相互作用，超聲彈性成像技術將被用以檢測受測者軟組織力學特性。一系列耦合模型和迭代算法將用以模擬和預測各種特定壓力級別 和梯度設計的壓力襪材料對皮膚壓力和血流的影響。當達到最大靜脈流速且處於舒適壓力區域時，優化的織物參數將通過優化算法確定。所模擬的壓力數值和血流值將和實驗數據進行對比，以確定優化的材料設計參數組合，並將其應用於 新的年長或特定人羣用壓力襪設計，以改善實際穿用依從性和接受度。這一增進的設計技術將爲壓力紡織服裝功能性設計開闢新路，並對功能紡織材料在健康、醫療、康復及更多領域的應用起到積極而深遠的影響。

25215318.label: Realisation of objectives
25215318.value: The proposed 4 objectives have been fully achieved. A new scientific pressure design technology through applying the coupled fluid-solid models, optimization algorithms, and experimental studies, has been developed to realize balanced comfort and mechanical function of the elastic compression stockings (ECSs). The sophisticated subject-specific geometric leg models including multi-biocomponents (soft tissues, tibia and fibula bones, and superficial and deep veins) were constructed based on the extracted magnetic resonance images (MRI). The ECS geometric models were built based on the actual ECS morphologies to fit users via the prototyping process. The built geometric leg and ECS models were meshed and set with boundary conditions for investigating their interactions and the resultant skin pressure and tissue stress of the lower limbs. Among the selected meshing sizes (ECSs: 7, 6, 5, 4, and 3mm and soft tissues: 8, 7, 6, 5, and 4 mm), the mesh sizes of 5 mm for FE ECS model and 6 mm for FE leg model were fully converged with the best meshing quality (0.839) for a desirable simulation effect. Tetrahedron and hexahedron elements were respectively used to mesh 3D leg and ECS models which produced approximately 30,000 nodes and 120,000 elements for FE model construction. The tibia and fibula bones were fixed without displacement whereas the FE ECS tubular can freely move from the ankle to the knee with customized displacement loading (e.g., 340 mm). The proposed FE leg-ECS model had approximately 650,000 degrees of freedom (DOFs) with six DOFs for every node. The boundary conditions restricted these DOFs for bones and one DOF along the longitudinal direction for each node was set. The explicit LS-DYNA dynamic solvers were used to simulate stress transmission within leg tissues. ECS prototypes made of polyamide-covered Lycra yarns with linear densities ranging from 40D to 420D were produced in 1x1 laid-in loop structures and in open-toe, close-toe, and legging styles. By regulating the knitting densities, tensions, and needle cylinder rotation cycles, the sizes and pressure levels of ECSs were engineered. The Young's moduli (E), Poisson's ratios (v), mass densities (kg/m3), shear moduli (G), and thickness (mm) of the ECS fabrics with lower and higher-pressure classes (e.g., I and III) were determined. Results indicated that E values of Class I ECS fabrics were generally 49.8% lower than those of Class III ECS fabrics. The strains of the ECS fabrics along the course direction at the ankle, brachial, and calf are approximately 25.3%, 44.3%, and 38.7%, respectively, which followed the RAL-GZ 381/1 standard for knee-high ECS. The interaction among the tension force (T) of the ECS fabrics, interface pressure (P), and the applied body with a specific radius (R) can be clarified using Laplace's Law (P=T/R) or modified equations. The penalty method was used to incorporate the contact condition into the FE discretization to prevent penetration of the two bodies (ECS and lower limb) in the interactive simulation. The frictional resistance between the two bodies is usually proportional to the force that presses to the surfaces and the roughness of the surfaces, thus influencing the easy-to-wear and comfortable performance of the ECSs. Results revealed that the simulated highest pressures 24.2 mmHg and 36.3 mmHg were at the ankle for Classes I and III ECS fabrics, respectively, and gradually decreased up to the calf with 14.6 mmHg and 26.7 mmHg for Classes I and III ECS fabrics, respectively, where the pressure gradient ratios at the ankle (B), brachial (B1), and calf (C) were 100 %, 89.0 %, and 60.3 % for Class I and 100 %, 89.0 %, and 73.6 % for Class III, respectively. The pressure profiles follow the therapeutic requirements in CVI treatment. Stress transmission behaviors from the skin to the deeper tissues were numerically analyzed using four determined cross-sectional paths, i.e., two paths towards major superficial veins (small saphenous venous (SSV) and great saphenous venous (GSV)), and two paths towards major anatomic bones (tibia and fibula). The results show the tissue stress was approximately 2525 Pa at the posterior ankle and then gradually decreased to approximately 2449 and 1478 Pa near the SSV and GSV, respectively, to 456 Pa near the deep veins (peroneal veins (PVs)), and to 449 and 783 Pa near the fibula and tibia, respectively, at the ankle level. By contrast, the tissue stress was increased from the calf periphery to the inner bones, i.e., approximately 2100 Pa at the skin surface of the calf region gradually increased to 2425 Pa near the fibula. At the ankle and brachial sections, the variation ratios (VROs) from SSV to PVs were 80% and 55%, respectively, but almost no stress decay was observed from SSV or GSV to PVs at calf section. The simulated maximum tissue deformations caused by Class I and III ECSs were approximately 2.88 and 3.60 mm at posterior ankle, respectively, and 6.01 and 9.69 mm at posterior calf, respectively. These tissue deformations gradually decayed from the periphery to the center with no deformation observed around the bones. The greater mechanical squeezing forces by ECSs were applied to the GSV and SSV than those to the PV, indicating that the pressure doses of the ECSs may have been lost or decayed during the delivery process from the periphery to the center, thereby exerting insufficient or variable pressure doses to targeted veins, which may have in turn influenced the biomechanical function of ECSs in regulating venous calibers and hemodynamics. The built subject-specific FE ECS-lower limb models were verified using pressure sensors to test skin pressures over 12-16 critical anatomic sites of leg per subject in vivo. The deviation ratios (DROs) between the measured and the simulated pressure were approximately 13.6%, 5.9%, and 15.1% for Class I ECS and 7.7%, 21.4%, and 8.1% for Class III ECSs at the ankle, brachial, and calf sections, respectively. Pearson correlation coefficient between the simulated and experimental data was approximately 0.967 and the root-mean-square deviation was approximately 2.37, indicating that the simulated and the measured pressure values have high relationships and the developed FE ECS-leg model has a preferable accuracy in prediction of pressure profiles. Moreover, the fluid-solid (FS) coupling model of the leg-vein-ECS system was developed. The venous models (involving PV, SSV, and GSV) were meshed. The velocity inlet was determined based on the Doppler ultrasound test and the venous flow pressure was set as the outlet, respectively. The results showed that the central average flow velocities of the SSV and GSV were higher than those of the PV. Based on the Poiseuille Law and Continuity equation, the increase of the external pressure applied by ECSs on the venous walls could induce increased venous flow. The comfort perceptions were significantly varied by the pressure classes applied. By employing optimization algorithms and sensitivity analysis, the parameters that mostly influenced ECS pressure function such as elastic moduli, tubular sizes, leg dimensions were determined, and the ECS pressure levels that fall in the corresponding user comfort range were quantified. Both the simulated pressures and flow rates by the FS coupling models were validated against the experimental data with preferable agreements. The outcomes facilitate us to understand in depth the biomechanical mechanisms of the ECS-leg system and provide valuable insights for ECS designs with optimized material properties, user comfort, and mechanical function.

25215318.label: Major findings and research outcome
25215318.value: This project created novel approaches to realize ECS simulation with multi-pressure levels and with heterogeneous shells (long- and short-stretches and knit-laid-in stitches) based on the realistic lower limb features that possessed more biomechanical properties. The newly developed FE leg-stocking models have been consistently improved through the optimized methods to determine the actual knitted fabric parameters (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, shear modulus, mass density, and thickness, etc) and the soft tissue stiffness of the specific subject using the advanced ultrasound elastography. The simulation precision of the FE model increased by 46.6% by applying the determined 3D material properties (involving thickness direction) compared to those traditionally used 2D material properties (along wale and course directions only). The validated FE ECS-leg models can simulate interfacial pressure magnitudes and distributions that highly agree with the experimental pressure results. It showed the applicability of the developed FE model in practical use. The FE ECS-lower limb model also numerically simulated and visualized the skin pressure, tissue stress, tissue deformation, and mechanical transmission behaviors within leg tissues under ECS application. A degressive gradient pressure was observed longitudinally from the ankle to the knee induced by ECSs, which met the gradient requirements of the RAL-GZ 387/1 standard. The inner tissue stresses induced by ECSs gradually decreased from the peripheral to the central soft tissues which could result in insufficient pressure doses delivered by the ECSs to the deeper venous system and the recurrence of venous disorders. The built fluid-solid (FS) coupling model of the leg-vein-ECS system characterized the mechanical effects of ECS on leg venous structures and venous flows, which was validated by wear trials using Doppler ultrasound tests. The increased interface pressure by ECSs produced an increasing trend in venous flow velocities. Optimized algorithms and sensitivity analysis determined the critical parameters that mostly influenced pressure performances such as material elastic modulus, tubular sizes, and user leg dimensions and their quantitative correlations. The ECS properties that fall in the corresponding user comfort pressure range were determined. The outcomes of the project enhanced the understanding of the working mechanisms underlying the interactions between ECSs and lower extremities, which contribute to new ECS design and development for CVI treatment. The obtained evidence-based design solutions also provide a valuable research framework and scientific guidance for more related compression textile products (e.g., leggings and tight-fit garments) with balanced wearing comfort and mechanical function for wide end users.

25215318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25215318.value: In the future study, the refined body structures with heterogeneous material properties will be incorporated into fluid–solid interaction models to analyze the more complex biomechanical function of ECSs and compression garments in treatment, including the effectiveness of ECSs on hemodynamics with consideration of variations in venous wall stiffnesses and venous flow viscosities as well as path mechanics characteristics of the lower limbs. Wear trials can be further carried out to assess the effects of ECSs with different pressure pattern designs on user comfortability and therapeutic efficiency in CVI. Thus, further optimize ECSs wearing and functional performances to better serve the targeted users.

25215318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25215318.value: Elastic compression stockings (ECSs) have demonstrated positive effectiveness in prophylaxis and treatment of chronic venous insufficiency (e.g., varicose veins and deep vein thrombosis). Through exerting controlled pressure from the distal to the proximal leg, the application of ECSs contributes to counteracting the gravity force and opposing the increased venous hypertension to facilitate venous return. However, ill-fitting, discomfort wearing perception, or insufficient mechanical function have hindered the ECS efficiency in use. To address these issues, this project adopted mixed methodologies of numerical simulation, optimization algorithms, and laboratory validation to systematically analyze the working mechanisms of interactions between ECSs and lower limbs and created new pressure design technologies to determine the optimal compression materials and fabrication parameters for producing ECSs with required pressure levels. This is the first study to systematically investigate such a complex compression garment and lower limb system in terms of materials, structures, biomechanics, comfort, psycho-physiological responses, and optimization strategies. The research outputs build an operable framework to visualize, predict, and evaluate pressure performances of the ECSs, and provide new insights for engineering design, development, and optimization of functional compression textiles (e.g., ECSs, leggings, tight-fit garments) for health care, medical treatments, or body support of the target users.

25215618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25215618.value: In the past decade, significant research efforts have been allocated to the so-called “Zero-Energy/Emission Buildings (ZEBs)” and “Zero-Energy/Emission Vehicles (ZEVs)”, which are perceived as ambitious outlooks for the building and transportation sectors to significantly reduce primary energy consumptions and equivalent CO2 emissions. Very often, the studies for these two sectors were isolated from each other, following separate paths towards their own zero-energy/emission balances. However, these separate paths will be increasingly challenged in the future as buildings are more interactively affected by vehicles, especially the building-charged new energy vehicles. Although some researchers have already investigated the possibility to integrate electric vehicles with building energy systems, there is still a lack of a systematic approach to appropriately integrate the ZEB(s) with the ZEV(s), and there is an urgent need for a comprehensive understanding of the interactive patterns and the resulting impacts on the technical, economic and environmental performances of the hybrid system. Furthermore, several challenges are involved for the integration, including the distinct static/mobile features of the zero-energy boundaries, different building/vehicle types, diversified energy/fuel sources, various hybrid grids interactions, and stochastic living/mobility behaviours. Therefore, the primary objective of this project is to develop a systematic methodology to optimally transit from the originally isolated elements into the future mutually integrated zero-energy unity between the ZEB(s) and the ZEV(s). In order to reach this target, this project will be logically conducted via the following research steps: (a) investigations and identifications for the characteristics of the ZEBs, the ZEVs and their integration potentials, (b) investigation of the technical solutions for the mutual integration, (c) multi-objective optimization of the integrations regarding the technical, economic and environmental objectives, (d) validation of the optimal solutions via the emulation method, and (e) theoretical thermodynamic and life-cycle analyses of the hybrid system. The outcome of this project is expected to contribute to the academic community by an integrated zero-energy concept, novelly expanding the conventional boundaries of the static ZEB(s) and the mobile ZEV(s), while sharing each other’s resources. Moreover, the developed methodology will be used as a guideline to support the integrations, enhancing the compatibilities and energy sharing features between the two sectors. Furthermore, this project will contribute to the fundamental understanding of the optimal integrations, by revealing the underlying thermodynamic principles of the integration methods as well as the critical solutions for further enhancing the overall system performance. 在過去的十年間，學術界針對“零耗能建築（ZEBs）”和“零耗能汽車（ZEVs）”開展了大量的研究，因爲這兩項零耗能技術被視爲是未來有效降低建築和交通領域的一次能源消耗和等效二氧化碳排放的重要手段。同時，我們注意到，在學術界，針對零耗能建築和零耗能汽車的研究往往彼此孤立的開展：分別遵循彼此特有的研究路徑，以期實現各自零耗能/零排放平衡的目標。然而，這樣彼此孤立的研究路徑和研究方法將在未來受到越來越多的制約和挑戰，因爲建築系統將會更多地受到汽車系統的交互式影響，尤其是受到屋宇充電式電動汽車的影響。雖然已經有部分學者開始探究電動汽車和建築系統相耦合的技術可行性，但是在學術界，仍然欠缺將零耗能建築和零耗能汽車進行有效整合的系統性方法；相應的，我們也急需全面瞭解ZEB(s)和ZEV(s)之間的交互式模式，以及這些模式所帶來的對於耦合系統在技術性、經濟型和環境性方面的影響。同時，隨著能源技術的多樣化發展，ZEB(s)和ZEV(s)之間的耦合也將遇到越來越多的挑戰：包括截然不同的零耗能邊界的靜/動態特徵，不同的建築/車輛種類，多樣化的能源/燃料供給方法，种類繁多的耦合能源網絡的交互模式，以及隨機式的居住/出行的行爲模式。因此，本項目的主要目標是開發系統性的研究方法，以期實現從過去相互孤立的建築/汽車模塊，向未來交互式耦合且統一的ZEB-ZEV零耗能系統進行優化性的轉變。 為實現前述目標，本項目將有序開展如下研究步驟：（a）探究和識別零耗能建築、零耗能汽車的零耗能特性，以及他們之間相互耦合的潛力；（b）探究交互式耦合的技術方法；（c）對於ZEB-ZEV的耦合方法進行包含技術性、經濟型和環境性的多目標優化；（d）通過仿真技術來驗證優化的耦合方法；（e）對於耦合系統進行理論性的熱力學和生命周期分析。本項目的研究成果將給學術界作出如下貢獻：提出一個新穎的耦合ZEB-ZEV的零耗能系統概念，獨創性的擴展零耗能建築的靜態邊界和零耗能汽車的動態邊界，同時共享彼此的零耗能資源。此外，本項目所開發的研究方法將會作為未來支持ZEB-ZEV耦合的指導準則，加強建築和交通領域之間的相互兼容性及能源共享性。同時，本項目將會揭示ZEB-ZEV耦合方法的熱力學機理以及優化耦合系統性能的關鍵性環節，從而有助於學術界從理論原理的層面更深入的理解ZEB-ZEV之間耦合的最優方法。

25215618.label: Realisation of objectives
25215618.value: Via this project, all the objectives have been successfully realized. We have systematically identified the similarities and differences of the characteristics between the ZEB(s) and the ZEV(s). The characteristics have been categorized into the buildings and battery-based electric vehicles, buildings and fuel-cell based electric vehicles, buildings and fuel-based vehicles, and the capabilities and potentials of the building side and the vehicle side to integrate each other as well as the techno-economic challenges. Diversified technical solutions have been investigated for the ZEB-ZEV integrations in detail in this project, covering different types of buildings and vehicles. The typical technical solutions mainly include the smart designs of the energy supporting systems and the smart controls for the B2V, V2B, G2V, and V2G interactions while comprehensively taking the mobile features of the ZEV(s) into account. The new energy vehicle is mainly considered as a mobile energy storage and an extended zero-energy boundary. This on one hand brings the challenges for the analysis of the ZEB energy balance and zero-energy system performances, while on the other hand has also brought in the benefit and opportunities to utilize the mobile energy storage capacities of the interacted ZEVs to absorb the surplus on-site renewable energy generations or to back-up the on-site energy shortage. The impact of the technical integration solutions on the energy matching, energy flexibility, and techno-economic-environmental performances of the hybrid zero-energy system have been emphasized during the investigation. Furthermore, the genetic-algorithm-based multi-objective optimizations have been systematically conducted for both the optimal design and control of the ZEB-ZEV integrations, with respect to the technical, economic, and environmental performances. The simulation, emulation and sensitivity analyses approaches have been used to support the operation and validation of the optimal solutions. Moreover, the characteristics of the groups of the optimal solutions have been analysed and achieved in detail based on this project. The fundamental principles and the most critical factors and processes have been investigated and obtained to support the optimal design and control of the building-vehicle integration as well as the optimal transition from the conventional systems towards the integrated zero-energy unity. The developed methodologies of the design and control for the ZEB-ZEV integrations have successfully provided a bridge between the building and transportation sectors, which were conventionally considered to be separated and isolated. Therefore, as a conclusion, all the objectives have been realized, and the integrated ZEB-ZEV concept and approach obtained from this project has provided a very good and referable methodology for the smart transitions towards the future carbon-neutral societies and zero-emission urban energy systems.

25215618.label: Major findings and research outcome
25215618.value: The major findings and research outcome have been mainly disseminated via the high-impact journal publications as listed in the Part C. As a summary, the followings are the most representative findings and research outcome from this project: (1) A state-of-the-art review and summary has been conducted and obtained between the buildings and vehicles, which has revealed the capabilities, potentials and challenges for the two sides to integrate each other [Paper#1 in Part C]. (2) Furthermore, by integrating the ZEV, it has been noticed that the conventional zero-energy building boundary should be revised, as the ZEB boundary should be extended to cover the mobile features of the ZEV. The expanded boundary has on one hand led to significant challenges for the ZEB analysis, whereas on the other hand the optimal utilization and control of this boundary expansion feature can be beneficial for the improvement of the zero-energy performances and the alleviation of bi-directional grid stresses [Paper#2 in Part C]. (3) Moreover, as the B(G)2V and V2B(G) interactions may degrade the batteries, we have further integrated the dynamic battery degradation models into account for the ZEB-ZEV integration. We have correspondingly obtained the updated control strategies for the ZEB-ZEV integration in order to enhance the techno-economic performances while protecting the battery conditions [Paper#3 in Part C]. (4) In addition, Paper #4 in Part C utilized the coordinated multi-criteria framework and life-cycle-based concept to analyse the building-vehicle integrations while taking the battery degradations and renewable energy depreciations into account. (5) The genetic-algorithm-based multi-objective optimizations have been conducted for the ZEB-ZEV integration, based on which the pareto-fronts (optimal fronts) have been obtained regarding the optimal design and control solutions. The characteristics of the optimal solutions have been achieved, with respect to the technical, economic and environmental performances [Paper#5 in Part C]. (6) We have also compared the impact of building performance transition on the ZEB-ZEV integration, starting from the low-performance building towards the zero-energy and positive-energy systems. The most influential factors have been obtained for the ZEB-ZEV integration during these transitions [Paper#6 in Part C]. (7) In the paper #7 in part C, we have obtained the technical solutions to integrate the zero-emission electrified metro train with the zero-energy metro train station. It has been found that the metro train battery storage can be fully utilized to enhance the techno-economic feasibility of the hybrid zero-energy train-building system with both the mobile and swappable battery technologies.

25215618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25215618.value: There are many potentials for the further research and development based on the outcome of this project. Firstly, the research concept of ZEB-ZEV integration can be further expanded to different types of transportation systems in the future, such as the aviation and navigation systems. For example, there is a good potential in the future to integrate the zero-energy airports with the zero-emission aeroplanes and zero-emission mobility systems in the airport. The boundary expansion methodology can be also applied to the zero-energy airport system, although different challenges and constraints should be considered and taken into account. Secondly, it is recommended that the research concept and methodologies developed from this project can be also applied to the large-scale urban and district energy supply and utilities to better support the planning and management of the future carbon-neutral urban and regional energy systems. There is a good research potential to further develop the large-scale urban energy management systems and unified business models to integrate the aggregated zero-emission buildings and zero-emission transportation systems in the future carbon-neutral urban systems. It is expected that the future transition towards the carbon-neutral society will be based on an integrated approach between the building and transportation sectors.

25215618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25215618.value: As the buildings are increasingly affected by the new energy vehicles, the old methodologies for treating the ZEB(s) and ZEV(s) separately were increasingly challenged by the new trend of the building integrated vehicle energy systems. However, there was a lack of a systematic approach to appropriately integrate the ZEB(s) with the ZEV(s). Correspondingly, via this project, we have developed a general and transferrable approach and methodology to integrate the ZEB(s) with the ZEV(s), and have obtained a comprehensive understanding of the interactive patterns and the resulting impacts on the hybrid zero-energy system while considering different types of buildings and vehicles. Therefore, the outcome of this project has significant value to help the academic communities obtain the updated approaches to optimally transit from the originally isolated building and vehicle elements into the future mutually integrated zero-energy unity, hereby improving the research methodologies for the design, control, operation and analysis of ZEB(s) and ZEV(s), while contributing to the enhanced compatibilities, feasibilities and flexibilities to integrate the two sectors together. Based on the outcome of this project, it is also expected that the future transition towards the carbon-neutral society will also rely on an integrated approach between the building and transportation sectors.
