25215918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25215918.value: Efficient utilizations of clean energies like solar, wind and tidal powers are highly desirable in modern society for sustainable development. Due to the intermittent nature of these renewable sources, energy storage systems are required in order to make the best use. Batteries, which convert the chemical energies into electric power, offer an effective way not only to store the energies but also to conveniently use them in various devices. As such, Li-ion batteries have gained a great success in the last two decades in portable electronics. Considerable efforts have been making to putting them into the applications of electric vehicles and stationary energy storage. Tremendous pressures are placed on the material resources. A mere 17ppm of lithium content in the earth crust has raised severe concerns on their sustainability for the upcoming unprecedentedly large markets. Moreover, the employments of high-cost elements such as cobalt make their price unaffordable for large-scale applications. Alternative technologies are therefore being intensively explored to develop low-cost and greener batteries. Na- and K-ion batteries are among the most promising candidates thanks to their similar properties with Li and elemental abundance of sodium (23,000 ppm) and potassium (15,000 ppm) over lithium. Unlike sodium ions, potassium ions are able to intercalate into graphite to form graphite intercalation compounds, which greatly expedites the development of K-ion batteries. Nevertheless, the natural graphite delivers only a modest capacity of only ~200 mAh/g in K-ion batteries currently, falling much behind 350 mAh/g – the practical capacity in Li-ion batteries. In this project, the microstructure of carbons will firstly be tailored for fully realization of its theoretical capacity (279 mAh/g corresponding to the formation of KC8). In addition, carbon materials possess a variety of mechanisms in potassium ion storage. Exploring the active sites such as defects and functional groups will lead to “extra” capacities for designing even-better carbon anodes. Furthermore, anions such as PF6-, BF4- could also be intercalated into graphitic carbon at a high potential (>4.5 V), making it feasible to build a potassium-based “dual-ion battery” utilizing anion and cation intercalations simultaneously, where carbons act as both anode and cathode. To this end, the correlation between carbon structure and their electrochemical behaviors will be established so as to accelerate the development of advanced potassium-based batteries. 清潔能源如（如太陽能、風能）的使用對於社會可持續發展有重要意義。但是由於這些資源發電具有不連續性，需要配合儲能器件如電池來有效的利用它們。在過去二十年間，鋰離子電池在便攜式電子設備中取得了重大的成功，因而人們考慮將它進一步使用在電動交通工具和靜態儲能中。然而鋰元素在地殼中含量僅為17ppm, 大規模鋰離子電池的使用勢必會帶來資源的匱乏和價格的上升。近些年來，研究人員著手開發成本更低、生產更清潔的電池技術作為鋰離子電池的替代物。鈉和鉀具有和鋰非常相似的性能，在地殼含量上比鋰更加豐富，因此鈉離子和鉀離子電池成為重要的研究對象。在負極方面，不同於鈉離子，鉀離子能夠嵌入到石墨形成石墨層間化合物。然而，目前天然石墨作為鉀離子電池負極僅有200 mAh/g的容量，遠低於在鋰離子電池中的350 mAh/g容量。本項目一方面通過調節碳材料的微觀結構來充分利用鉀離子在石墨中的插層容量，另一方面採取原子摻雜、官能團引入等手段進一步提高儲鉀能力。此外，利用陰離子如PF6-, BF4-在碳材料中高電壓下的插層和吸附，有望開發一種基於鉀離子的“雙碳”電極電池，即電池的正負極均使用碳材料。本項目將致力於探索碳材料的結構-性能關聯，為加快鉀離子電池的開發打下良好基礎。

25215918.label: Realisation of objectives
25215918.value: The three objectives have been successfully realized. (1) Using pitch-derived carbon as a model system, we have systematically explored the K ion storage behavior in the carbon materials with different microstructures by controlling the carbonization temperature from 800 to 2800 oC. We revealed the potential K ion storage sites and compared their reaction voltage, kinetics and structural stability during insertion/extraction to guide the rational carbon design. A structure-property correlation has been established, suggesting the partially graphitized carbon has the best overall performance in the capacity, rate, and lifespan. The results have been published in J. Power Sources 2021, 506, 230179. We also compared the charge storage mechanism between Li, Na and K ions through in-situ Raman tests (Carbon 2020, 157, 316). We observed a similar behavior at high voltages, but distinct mechanisms are involved at the low-voltage regime in the voltage profiles, thus calling for the customized structural design of carbon anodes for the alkali-metal ion batteries. (2) We investigated the cyclic stability and reversible capacity of nature graphite anode. A capacity close to the theoretical value (279 mAh/g corresponding to the KC8 formation) has been achieved by regulating the intercalation chemistry in various electrolytes (Small Structure 2022, 2200078). We showed that weak solvation is necessitated to prevent solvent co-intercalation in ether electrolytes for realizing the binary graphite intercalation compound KC8. Moreover, we have prepared a carbon with an exceptional reversible capacity of over 400 mAh/g (Carbon 2021, 176, 383) through the co-utilization of several active sites besides intercalation. Stable cycling of 2000 cycles has been realized with the construction of a robust electrode/electrolyte interface. (3) We examined the full K-ion batteries by coupling carbon anodes with a K3V2(PO4)2F3 cathode (J. Power Sources 2021, 506, 230179), and potassium-based dual-ion batteries utilizing a graphite cathode. We report the co-intercalation of PF6- and FSI- in the graphite to simultaneously take advantage of the fast kinetics of FSI- and robust interfaces associated with PF6-, significantly improving the capacity and stability of dual-ion batteries (Carbon 2021, 178, 363). The intercalation chemistry and electrochemical performance have been examined to promote practical application.

25215918.label: Major findings and research outcome
25215918.value: We have conducted a thorough investigation from the materials synthesis and insertion chemistry to the electrode/electrolyte interfaces. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows. i) We synthesized the hard and soft carbon anodes from lignin and pitch precursors, respectively. The synthesis approaches have been optimized. We found a pre-oxidation at 200 oC in the air is essential to the lignin-derived hard carbon to enlarge the inter-layer space (C: Research Output No. 1). Turning the pitch-derived soft carbon, a carbonization temperature at 1400 oC led to a high capacity with attractive rate capability (C: Research Output No. 3). We have disclosed the potential active sites in carbon materials, including surface adsorption, insertion between the randomly oriented graphene layers, and intercalation to form graphite intercalation compounds (GIC). The former two have fast kinetics to achieve the high power density while the GIC formation takes place at a low potential, benefiting the construction of high-voltage potassium full cells. ii) We unraveled the critical roles of the electrode/electrolyte interfaces in boosting cycling stability and developed an ethylene glycol diethyl ether-derived electrolyte (EGDEE) to build a stable interface. Under the graphite anode, this EGDEE electrolyte effectively prevents solvent co-intercalation because of the weak cation-solvent interaction (C: Research Output No. 6). Meanwhile, it maintains the advantages of ether electrolytes in building a thin and uniform solid electrolyte interphase to facilitate charge transfer and improve cyclic stability. The electrolyte could also be extended to the mesoporous carbon anode, which was synthesized by the MgO template. The synergistic effect between the optimized microstructure and well-designed interface enabled high-rate cycling at 1 A/g with an exceptional lifespan of 2000 cycles (C: Research Output No. 5). 3) We investigated the anion insertion chemistry in graphite cathode for building high-energy dual-ion batteries. It is revealed that the PF6- benefits the stability at high voltage for realizing full intercalation while FSI- has fast intercalation kinetics to boost the rate performance. A synergistic effect could be achieved using KPF6-KFSI dual salts-based electrolytes (C: Research Output No. 4).

25215918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25215918.value: The implementation of this project has substantially enhanced our understanding of the potassium ion storage mechanism, which facilitates the rational design of carbon anodes. We will further explore along this direction to develop high-capacity and high-rate carbon anodes that uptake potassium ions at an appropriate potential. This could be achieved by simultaneously utilizing diverse active sites, as we have already disclosed the charge storage behaviors in different sites. It is also important to further increase the initial Coulombic efficiency for effectively coupling with the cathode. These efforts will significantly promote the practical application of potassium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage.

25215918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25215918.value: Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) possess great advantages in sustainability and cost, making them attractive candidates for complementing lithium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage. Carbon materials are the most compelling anodes for PIBs. However, the insertion/extraction of large radius potassium ions brings grand challenges in designing high-capacity and high-stability carbon anodes. In this project, we first unravel the structure-property correlation of potassium ion storage in carbon material, leading to the discovery of several potential active sites. We disclose the detailed thermodynamic and kinetics features of these sites, based on which promising hard and soft carbon anodes are synthesized. We also regulate the solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) that cover the anode to boost the potassium ion diffusivity. The fracture of SEIs would decrease the reversibility. Through the newly developed electrolyte formulations, thin and homogeneous SEIs have been built, which show excellent electrochemical and mechanical stability upon repeated potassium ion insertion/extraction. We also examine the compatibility of as-prepared carbon in full PIBs and potassium-based dual-ion batteries. The achieved results would benefit the application of PIBs for facilitating clean energy utilization.

25216118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25216118.value: Past catastrophic events have highlighted the vulnerability of coastal bridges under typhoons, including numerous bridge failures during Hurricanes Ivan and Katrina. Due to population growth in coastal areas and climate changes, vulnerability of infrastructure to typhoons is amplified. Furthermore, both sea level rise (SLR) and increase in typhoon intensity pose a threat to coastal communities. However, the current design and management approaches rely on past climate records without considering climate change effects, which remains a significant research gap and could result in an underestimation of hazard risk. Thus, it is essential to formulate methodologies to quantify vulnerability and risk of coastal bridges under increasingly intense typhoons and SLR. Past studies have investigated the deterministic performance of bridges to typhoon-induced loads, but failed to account for uncertainties. Meanwhile, risk-informed management of infrastructures vulnerable to climate change is limited. Adaptation engineering, as an emerging research area, focuses on ensuring that existing and new assets are protected from both near- and long-term changes in climate. Currently, research in design and adaptation of bridges under climate change lags behind research in climate projection. Furthermore, knowledge is lacking on structural adaptation under deep uncertainties of future scenarios, where likelihoods of the scenarios cannot be assigned. The preliminary study has revealed that it is impossible to identify one best solution under all possible future scenarios, representing another challenge to decision makers. In order to address these challenges, in this project, an integrated and robust decision-making approach incorporating state-of-the-art climate projection models will be established to aid bridge design and adaptation in a changing climate. Effects of climate change on probabilistic loading, structural reliability, and risk will be quantified using both analytical and simulation methods. A robustness index will be developed considering both flexibility and robustness of a strategy under future scenarios. The proposed methodologies include probabilistic modeling of structural capacity and load, quantitative risk assessment, long-term loss projection in a changing climate, and improved robust decision-making. Overall, this project will advance the development of resilient bridges under climate change. The proposed methodology will be illustrated and evaluated by its application to a set of bridges in different regions, that are prone to typhoons and SLR, including Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta region. The results of developed risk-informed performance assessment and decision-making approach can further scientific understanding of robust structural adaptation, update current design and assessment specifications, and support policies and actions in hazard mitigation and adaptation. 過去的災難性事件已經凸顯出颱風對於沿海橋樑的破壞性。此外，考慮到沿海地區人口的不斷增長和全球氣候的日趨變化，可以預見颱風對於沿海地區基礎設施的影響將持續增大。然而，目前的橋樑設計和管理方法主要基於過去的氣候記錄，並未考慮氣候變化的影響，這一研究不足可能導致我們對於相應災害風險的低估。因此，在日益強烈的颱風和海平面上升趨勢下，制定相應的方法來量化沿海橋樑的易損性和風險至關重要。 過去的相關研究主要集中于颱風在橋樑上產生荷載作用的確定性分析，並未考慮到相應的不確定性及其影響規律。此外，基於風險概念的基礎設施評估理論尚未系統地建立。基礎設施氣候變化適應性研究作為一個新興的研究領域，以確保現有和新建基礎設施適應于氣候變化所帶來的影響作為主要目標，有著重大的理論意義和工程實用價值。目前，氣候變化條件下橋樑設計和評估的研究嚴重落後於氣候預測研究，且未考慮氣候變化自身深層次不確定性的影響規律。初步研究表明，若根據現有的橋樑設計和評估理論，在所有可能的未來氣候變化情景中尋求最佳的解決方案是不可行的，這對決策者來說是一個極大挑戰。為此，本項目將建立一個基於魯棒性的決策方法，確保沿海橋樑在不斷變化氣候條件下的適應性。同時，將結合基於結構可靠性和風險的評估方法對沿海橋樑的性能進行量化分析，并提出基於結構性能的魯棒性指數。擬採用的方法和理論包括結構抗力和荷載的概率化模型、定量風險評估、考慮氣候變化中的沿海橋樑結構性能退化預測以及改進的魯棒性決策。 總而言之，該項目將推動氣候變化下具有可持續性和可恢復性橋樑的設計、評估理論建立與發展。提出的方法可應用於不同地區的橋樑，包括香港和珠三角洲地區，同時，本研究還可以進一步推進在氣候變化下基礎設施結構體系的適應性調整，更新當前的沿海橋樑設計和評估規範，并為相應的防災減災決策提供理論基礎。

25216118.label: Realisation of objectives
25216118.value: This project has four objectives, and all of these four objectives have been 100% achieved. The first objective is to develop probabilistic vulnerability models of coastal bridges under typhoon-induced forces considering uncertainties of structural capacity and load effects. Our team first characterized the demand of wave and surge loads on bridge decks considering the uncertainty. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models have been established to compute the hazard-induced loads on the bridge superstructure. These results have been validated using the AASHTO empirical equations and a bias removal factor has been used to adjust the potential underestimation from these formulas. Besides, the randomness in the variables, e.g., wave height, period, storm surge, etc., have been captured in the reliability analysis. The Longuett-Higgins joint probability density function has been used to describe the correlation between wave height and period. Surge heights associated with typhoon hazards were taken from the local surge modeling and historical databases collected by the Hong Kong Observatory’s website. On the other hand, to accurately calculate the structural capacity of a specific coastal bridge, uncertainties of material strength, material density, and structural dimensions have been considered in the structural capacity assessment. The vertical resistance of the bridge deck was assessed considering the dead weight of the span and the vertical connections between the deck and cap. The weight of the bridge span was calculated considering the uncertainties of unit weight of materials and construction uncertainty, e.g., deck thickness, to represent the difference between the asbuilt from the onsite condition. The second objective is to establish a probabilistic risk assessment approach incorporating deep uncertainty and damage loss. The structural risk of a coastal bridge subjected to typhoon hazards is a performance indicator emphasizing both structural performance and the consequences of failure. In this project, the structural risk is defined as a function of the threat T, vulnerability V, and consequences C. The structural vulnerability was addressed in the tasks for objective 1, so this object mainly focused on the calculation of probabilistic threats and consequences. First, the frequency and intensity of typhoon hazards within the investigated region have been established based on current climate data using the yearly typhoon occurrence rate. Future typhoon scenarios were estimated based on the historical climate and future projections provided by HKO. The yearly rate of the Poisson process could also be assessed as a function of time, λ(t), as a non-stationary Poisson process, according to the relevant trend. To account for the underlying uncertainties, different sampling techniques, e.g., Latin Hypercube sampling, have been utilized to generate possible values. Concerning the consequence evaluation of the high-risk coastal bridges, it is defined as the sum of rebuilding/repair costs, running costs, and time costs. The outcomes of this objective then contributed to the development of the risk-informed retrofit/adaptation actions in the following tasks. The third objective is to identify the retrofit/adaptation actions and to assess the long-term loss/risk of coastal bridges in a changing climate. The developed retrofit actions can be generally divided into two categories: (a) actions to reduce the wave-induced forces on deck, such as elevation and venting holes, and (b) actions to increase the capacity of a bridge, such as steel wires. To quantify the specific effects of these retrofit actions, bridges equipped with different actions have been separately tested through experimental and numerical studies as introduced previously. For instance, we have established different CFD models for bridge decks with different types and ratios of air venting holes. The results show that these holes could reduce the total wave loads to varying degrees. Besides, the effects of climate change and future economic growth have been considered in the long-term assessment of coastal bridge risks. The changing hazard intensity and frequency of typhoons under different climate scenarios have been tested, and the long-term losses have been transferred into present value by introducing an economic growth factor for ease of comparison. The fourth objective is to propose an improved robust decision-making approach and tool for adaptation of coastal bridges vulnerable to typhoons and sea level rise. An adaptation decision consists of the type of adaptation action and the time of implementation of this action. Different strategies have been assessed within the time horizon, i.e., the service life of a specific bridge. As there is a desire to wait for more information regarding future scenarios, the flexibility of an adaptation action will be incorporated within the decision-making process. All the adaptation actions were assumed to be implemented on the coastal bridge at the first of a year when considering the flexibility. Deep uncertainties associated with climate change and future economic growth have been evaluated. To identify robust adaptation strategies, we have defined several performance metrics (e.g., benefit, cost, regret, etc.) and proposed a multi-criteria optimization framework. The robust strategies were identified by performing the Pareto Optimality process.

25216118.label: Major findings and research outcome
25216118.value: A paramount contribution of this research project is that it assists in progressing the knowledge and reducing the gap between the state-of-art and state-of-practice in the risk-informed coastal bridge design and adaptation to climate change effects, especially in the sea level rise and intense typhoons. Specifically, a probabilistic vulnerability model for coastal bridges subjected to typhoon hazards has been developed, which comprehensively considers the uncertainties of structural capacity and demand. On this basis, a risk assessment approach incorporating deep uncertainties associated with climate change and future economic scenarios has been established. Different retrofit/adaptation actions have been identified and tested. Finally, robust adaptation strategies have been formulated and a high-performance decision-making tool has been developed. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models have been established to compute the hazard-induced loads on the bridge superstructure. The established 3D models can calculate more accurate results as compared with previous empirical and analytical methods. Besides, it is more flexible and could be easily adjusted for different types of bridges. These results have been validated using the AASHTO empirical equations and a bias removal factor has been used to adjust the potential underestimation from these formulas. Based on the numerical results, the team has developed existing fragility models by incorporating the uncertainties of structural demand and capacity, as well as the performance of bridge components. Fragility, risk, and resilience models are then developed for high-risk coastal bridges under typhoon hazards. Through comparisons, it is observed that old fragility models may underestimate the potential risks induced by future hazards. Based on the developed numerical models and experimental results, our team further tested the effects of different adaptation actions and developed robust adaptation strategies. Many previous studies only tested these actions but did not assess their applicability from the economic aspect. To overcome this issue, we defined several performance metrics and developed robust adaptation strategies through a multi-criteria optimization framework. This research project has led to five publications on world well-known journals, e.g., Structure and Infrastructure Engineering; Ocean Engineering; Engineering Structures; Civil Engineering and Environmental Systems; and Reliability Engineering and System Safety; and four conference presentations on 31st European Safety and Reliability Conference; IABSE Conference Seoul 2020 - Risk Intelligence of Infrastructures; 10th International Conference on Bridge Maintenance, Safety and Management (IABMAS2020); and The 32nd European Safety and Reliability Conference (ESREL 2022).

25216118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25216118.value: Based on the outcomes of this research project, it is found that existing low-lying coastal bridges are at high-risk under extreme tropical cyclones, especially under climate change scenarios. Although this project has established a more refined model for calculating the wave impacts on superstructures, some other influences are still not clear and require further exploration. For example, the effects of wave impacts on substructures and the vibration of the main structure; the compound hazard impacts such as the sequential earthquake-tsunami hazards; experimental and numerical tests on different types and dimensions of bridges; the projection of future climate scenarios and economic scenarios incorporating government policies; fragility, risk, and resilience models for bridge networks; and the development of existing bridge design specifications. We will keep our future research studies and projects on these topics, aiming at advancing the development of resilient bridges under climate change.

25216118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25216118.value: Past catastrophic events have highlighted the vulnerability of coastal bridges under typhoons, including numerous bridge failures during Hurricanes Ivan and Katrina. Due to the population growth in coastal areas and climate changes, the vulnerability of coastal bridges to typhoons is amplified. However, current design and management approaches rely on past climate records without considering climate change effects, which remains a significant research gap and could result in an underestimation of hazard risk. Thus, it is essential to formulate methodologies to quantify the vulnerability and risk of coastal bridges. To fulfill these research gaps, this project focused on the robust adaptation of coastal bridges under typhoon hazards. Specifically, a probabilistic vulnerability model for coastal bridges subjected to typhoon hazards has been developed, which comprehensively considers the uncertainties of structural capacity and demand. On this basis, a risk assessment approach incorporating deep uncertainties associated with climate change and future economic scenarios has been established. Different retrofit/adaptation actions have been identified and tested. Finally, robust adaptation strategies have been formulated and a high-performance decision-making tool has been developed.

25220118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25220118.value: In an increasingly urbanized built environment, each additional square meter of building space gives rise to environmental and economic costs. Economic and environmental sustainability can be achieved with the aid of space-utilization prediction methods, which help architects both to modify their designs and achieve more efficient space-utilization and also to enhance end-user satisfaction by distributing well-used space across buildings. However, current methods of predicting space-utilization have limited accuracy and precision because they ignore, or over-simplify, the role of building-user preferences in spatial-choice behavior. The present study seeks to develop a method that models space preferences during the design phase by integrating discrete-choice modeling (DCM) theory with immersive virtual environments (IVEs). DCM will be used to measure the relationships between spaces, space preferences, and user space-use probabilities. For this purpose, discrete-choice experiments will be designed and conducted on the basis of important space attributes; levels comprising space options, and the design of space options, will be incorporated into the IVEs. The study will then gather users’ spatial choices between space options by requiring them to choose spaces in IVEs. The data will be used to model space-preference by estimating the parameters of space attributes through a conditional logit model. External validity of the integrated method will be tested by measuring its predictive accuracy with the Brier Score and by comparing it with the actual choices in the physical environment. Finally, an overall integrated method for modeling space preferences will be formulated. The integrated method will generate space-use probabilities on the basis of building-user space preferences. These probabilities can easily be adapted for use in current methods of utilization prediction, so that the overall aim of the study is to bring about more realistic space-utilization predictions, with greater accuracy and precision. The integrated method can be applied on a case-by-case basis when the project requires some design decision-making. In addition, modeled space-preferences can be stored according to types of activity (e.g. individual work, group work, socializing) and user (e.g. students, office workers) in different types of building (e.g. hospitals) in different regions (e.g. Europe). They can then be shared among architects and those concerned. In conclusion, the findings will enhance many other building performance analyses and, specifically, those that are greatly affected by the use of space, such as energy use and indoor air quality. 25223118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25223118.value: The electric power systems have been experiencing fast and drastic changes throughout the world mainly due to the energy policies which promotes the renewables. The competitive renewable resources are far from the load centers. Therefore, series capacitor compensation in AC transmission system and construction of new HVDC links are the typical responses of the power system operators to the large scale renewable integration. Those large scale renewables include wind parks and photovoltaic solar systems which employ electronically coupled generators (ECGs). The development of power grids goes in the direction of hybrid systems with integrated AC/DC interconnections and high ECG penetration levels. On the other hand, this transformation introduces several technical challenges in power system planning and operation including the subsynchronous interaction (SSI) problems. SSI defines two parts of a power system exchanging energy with each other at one or more of the natural frequencies of the combined system below the synchronous frequency. The SSI problems in conventional power systems have been known since 1970s. However, with the increased large scale renewable integration, the SSI problems associated with ECGs came to light with the incidents in US and China. Majority of the ECG related SSI researches are on the doubly-fed induction generator based wind parks connected to a series capacitor compensated transmission system. On the other hand, the modern power systems contain other configurations which are potentially susceptible to SSI. For example, one of the recent incidents in China demonstrated the susceptibility of conventional turbine-generators to SSI when located in the vicinity of large scale wind parks with ECGs. Due to the recent ECG related SSI incidents, the power system operators are under considerable pressure to increase the percentage of renewables in their generation fleet. The available SSI screening tools (or methods) are not able to identify all the ECG related SSI problems. The proposed project will develop an enhanced SSI screening tool for very large-scale power systems. The developed tool will be able to identify all ECG related SSI problems considering various power system operating conditions and contingency scenarios. Accuracy and efficiency will be the key factors. In addition, all power system configurations potentially susceptible to SSI will be identified and analyzed deeply on realistic benchmarks with high penetration of ECGs as well as other types of power electronics-based devices (such as HVDC terminals, flexible AC transmission system devices). This research will also propose practicable and cost-effective SSI mitigation methods. 電力系統主要因應世界各國為推行再生能源所實施的政策，迎來了快速且急劇的轉變。其中具有競爭力的再生能源產業都遠離於耗電中心區域。所以，使用交流輸電網串聯電容補償和新建高壓直流連接成為了電網運營方對大規模新能源接入的典型做法。那些大規模的再生能源包括了使用電子耦合式發電設備（ECGs）的風力發電機組與太陽能板。電網正向著具備整合交直流連接與大規模電子耦合式發電設備的混合系統而發展。另外，這種發展帶來了一些在籌劃與營運電力系統時在技術層面上所面對的的挑戰，例如包含了次同步交互問題（SSI）。 次同步交互的定義是在電力系統的兩個區域，在低於同步頻率的一個或多個固有頻率上交換能量的情况。自1970年代起，次同步交互問題所帶來的問題已在傳統電力系統中被認知。不過，隨著規模龐大的再生能源發電與現有電網的聯合發展愈來愈多，加上電子耦合式發電設備的聯動影響，次同步交互問題所帶來的問題更是於發生在中國和美國的多次事故中受到注目。電子耦合式發電設備相關的次同步交互問題的主要研究內容是關於使用雙饋非同步風機的風電場在串聯電容補償輸電網的接入。然而，現代電力系統也包含了其它對次同步交互具備潛在敏感性的配置。譬如︰最近一次出現在中國的事故印證了當傳統汽輪發電機組存在於使用大規模電子耦合式發電設備的風電場附近時，其易受次同步交互問題的影響。由於近期電子耦合式發電設備相關的次同步交互事故，電力營運者在增加再生能源的整體發電佔比時受到相當大的壓力。目前可用的次同步交互篩選工具或者方法並不能識別所有的電子耦合式發電設備相關的次同步交互問題。 這項計畫將開發一個用於超大規模電力系統的改進次同步交互篩選工具。這個工具將能夠分辨所有不同電力系統運行條件和意外事故狀態下電子耦合式發電設備相關的次同步交互問題。其準確性和效率將會是至關重要的參數。再者，所有對次同步交互具備潛在敏感特點的電力系統組態將通過對真實的且具備大規模電子耦合式發電設備的標準案例進行深入識別與分析（其它基於電力電子的設備也將包含其中，比如高壓直流輸電終端，柔性交流輸電設備）。這項研究亦將提出可行以及具高成本效益的減輕次同步交互影響的方法。

25223118.label: Realisation of objectives
25223118.value: Extension of the Scope, Reasons and Impact on Project Progress: The proposed research was supposed to focus on subsynchronous interaction (SSI) problems of inverter-based resources (IBRs). In other words, the instability problems of IBRs that had been expected to take place at subsynchronous frequency range. Unlike stated in the literature, this research has identified that the controller of IBRs can adversely interact with the weakly tied AC grids at super-synchronous frequency range. The instability risks and mechanisms of both full-size converter (FSC) and doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) based IBRs in weak grids are re-examined. The mirror frequency effect (MFE) becomes significant at super-synchronous. This produces significant errors when single-input single output (SISO) sequence impedance of IBR is used in impedance-based stability analysis (IBSA). The alternative is utilizing dq reference frame multi-input multi-output (dq MIMO) IBSA as it inherently accounts for MFE. However, dq MIMO cannot differentiate the resonance and mirror frequencies. Furthermore, it brings some complexities when the resonance frequency is beyond the double fundamental frequency. Hence, alternative MIMO impedance models of IBR and related electromagnetic transient (EMT) level impedance scanning techniques are explored. A new control interaction phenomenon between large-scale FSC-based wind park and extra high voltage level transmission system has been identified. This new interaction phenomenon was analyzed deeply considering various WP operating conditions, transmission grid topologies and FSC controller parameters. The extension of the scope resulted delay in project deliverable and achieving objectives. Impacts of Protests and Covid-19 Pandemic: In addition to the extension of scope, protests and Covid-19 pandemic had significant impacts on the delays in project deliverables and achieving certain objectives. Some of the research papers of this project are either under review or under preparation. Furthermore, most of the large-scale renewable projects had been either suspended or cancelled due to Covid-19. Therefore, our participation in actual large-scale renewable projects was realized only in research based, but not in planning and implementation (Objective-5). Summary of Research Outputs: All objectives except objective-5 have been achieved. The project outputs include 9 journal papers (except 3 journal papers under review and 2 journal papers under preparation), and 2 book chapters (in collaboration with Montreal Polytechnique and Concordia University). In addition, a PhD student has been trained (Meng Lei, expected graduation date: 2023-10-01). Realization of Objectives Objective-1: -An accurate EMT-level frequency scanning tool has been developed and implemented in EMTP as a library tool. -A grid side topology screening tool containing power system reduction and line outage scenario selection functions has been developed in Matlab which also performs phasor-domain frequency scanning on the reduced size system for the identified set of transmission outages forming either radial connections between DFIG-based IBRs and series capacitors or weak grid conditions at all type IBR terminals. -IBSA tool that uses IBR and grid side impedances. Objective-2: -Numerous comprehensive realistic benchmarks have been developed for not only SSI research, but also other type converter instability conditions. Objective-3 -The power system configurations and operating conditions not only susceptible to SSI, but also other type converter instabilities have been identified. -Effective and practicable mitigation techniques have been proposed for series capacitor compensated DFIG-based IBRs. Objective-4 -This project delivered guidelines for utilities and manufacturers to follow in the planning stage for identification and mitigation of both SSI and weak grid instability problems. Objective-5 - Strong ties have been established with Hitachi ABB Power Grids and Réseau de Transport d'Électricité. A grant application was made (Mitacs application (IT30826) with project title "Measurement-based modeling and stability analysis of voltage source converter-based power systems") under leadership of Montreal Polytechnique and our application was accepted on 25/04/2023. - Our participation in actual large-scale renewable projects was realized only in research based (see above), but not in planning and implementation mainly due to Covid-19 pandemic. It should be noted that, many large-scale renewable projects had been either suspended or cancelled due to Covid-19 pandemic. Moreover, travel restrictions limited the contact with industry. Objective-6 -Our research team delivered cutting-edge research in the field of converter instability identification and mitigation; and gained a fame internationally. Objective-7 -Strong alliances have been developed with Montreal Polytechnique, Concordia University, Réseau de Transport d'Électricité and Hitachi ABB Power Grids. Our Mitacs application (IT30826) with project title "Measurement-based modeling and stability analysis of voltage source converter-based power systems" was accepted on 25/04/2023.

25223118.label: Major findings and research outcome
25223118.value: 1. Fixing blind spots in the classification of inverter-based resource (IBR) small-signal instability: The instability risks and mechanisms of both full-size converter (FSC) and doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) based IBRs in weak grids were re-examined deeply (research outputs [7] and [13], respectively). It was demonstrated that weak grid instability takes place at super-synchronous frequency range rather than sub-synchronous. 2. Development of effective EMT-level impedance scanning techniques for the accurate impedance-based stability analysis (IBSA) of IBRs and their implementation in EMTP as library tool (research outputs [2]-[5], [9], [11], [12] and [16]): The proposed technique in [5] is superior over all the others in all aspects as illustrated in [12] and its efficiency can be improved further with the implementation proposed in [16]. 3. Stability Assessment of Inverter-based Resources in a Large-Scale Power System (research output [15]): A grid side topology screening tool containing power system reduction and line outage scenario selection functions has been developed in Matlab which also performs phasor-domain frequency scanning on the reduced size system for the identified set of transmission outages forming either radial connections between DFIG-based IBRs and series capacitors or weak grid conditions at all type IBR terminals. 4. A new control interaction phenomenon with large-scale FSC-based wind park (research output [14]): A new control interaction phenomenon between large-scale FSC-based wind park and extra high voltage level transmission system has been identified. This new interaction phenomenon was analyzed deeply considering various wind park operating conditions, transmission grid topologies and FSC controller parameters. 5. The first detailed analysis on the impact of communication delays on SSI damping controller performance (research output [1]): A novel algorithm is proposed to calculate the stability delay margin (SDM). Based on the proposed algorithm, the impacts of wind farm operating conditions and turbine control parameters on the SDM are investigated. To strengthen the SSI damping controller performance against communication delays, a Smith predictor scheme is also developed. 6. A robust and practicable SSI damping controller using H∞ technique for series compensated DFIG-based wind farms (research output [6]): The implementation of the proposed controller does not require any communication links between the wind turbines and wind farm secondary control layer. Moreover, the controller output signals are applied to the inner control loops of DFIG converters and are dynamically limited for the desired transient performance. 7. Impact of DFIG impedance model precision on IBSA is analysed deeply (research output [7]).

25223118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25223118.value: Big data processing, artificial intelligence, and machine learning (ML) can be used to design inverter-based resource (IBR) controllers to efficiently damp sub- or super-synchronous control interaction phenomena. Given the abundance of data and variety of operating conditions in the IBR-dominated grid, ML-based schemes seem promising for solving big data problems in this new energy paradigm. The voltage source converter (VSC) HVDC controllers can be designed in a similar manner for immunity to sub- or super-synchronous control interaction phenomena. The delivered instability identification tool can be also improved with the application of ML-based schemes which falls into the current Mitacs project (QC-ISDE) where PolyU is one of the participants. The research on converter instability identification and its mitigation can be extended to include networks that accomodate grid forming converters and also HVDC connected offshore wind parks. The recent developments in distribution grids (such as integration of small-scale renewables, battery storage units, electric vehicle charging stations) make distribution system vulnerable to converter instability problems. The number of converters is expected to increase further with the DC distribution paradigm. Hence, a compherensive research is required on potential converter instability problems and their mitigation considering the future of distribution grids.

25223118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25223118.value: With recent advances in wind turbine and photovoltaic cell technologies, the wind and solar power penetration levels increase as well as the sizes of wind parks and photovoltaic solar plants. These renewables are connected to electrical grids through power electronic converters, and called inverter-based resources (IBRs). The increasing generation share of IBRs causes stability problems in transmission grids which has been confirmed with several real-life incidents. This project delivered an accurate and efficient IBR instability screening tool for large-scale power systems. It is the preliminary version of an industry grade tool which can be used in planning and operation. In addition, this project proposed effective and practiciable methods for mitigation considering the implementation challenges. The ability to perform IBR instability studies is essential for utilities to increase the large-scale renewable integration in their system in a safe manner. Identifying potential instability problems will also enable manufacturers to revise their designs in the planning stage.

25300818.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25300818.value: 具有非光滑解的时间分数阶扩散方程的数值方法

25300818.label: Project Objectives
25300818.value: We intend to investigate time-fractional diffusion equations with time-dependent diffusion coefficients, which is missing in the literature although analytical works on the models with time-independent coefficients is rather extensive. The analysis in existing works is mostly based on Laplace transform, which is not directly applicable to the case of time-dependent diffusion coefficients. Meanwhile, the fractional differentiation does not satisfy many useful rules in calculus, e.g., Leibniz rule, which contrasts sharply with the integer-order differentiation. Therefore, the analysis will differ substantially from that for its parabolic counterpart and the fractional problems with time-independent diffusion coefficients. In this project, we aim at developing a new perturbation argument for this kind of problems. This part of the project consists of the following three components. First, the well-posedness and (limited) regularity property (in both space and time) will be theoretically confirmed by a perturbation argument. The methodology is expected to provide a powerful tool to analyze numerical approximations. Second, we shall analyze both spatially semidiscrete Galerkin FEM scheme and fully discrete schemes given by convolution quadrature in time. Third and last, this novel argument together with the initial correction technique will be used to develop some high-order time-stepping schemes, even though the solution is nonsmooth. We are interested in stochastic time-fractional diffusion equations, where the random noise is introduced in the model to describe random effects on particle transport in fractal media or subject to trapping. Compared with the deterministic model, the numerical analysis of the stochastic time-fractional diffusion model is more challenging, due to the additional restriction on the smoothing property caused by random noise. We firstly aim to develop numerical schemes for the linear time-fractional diffusion equations driven by additive noise, and analyze convergence rates in both strong and weak senses. The argument should rely crucially on suitable error estimates for the corresponding deterministic problem with nonsmooth data, and can be extended to the semilinear stochastic fractional diffusion equation driven by multiplicative noise. Due to the distinct smoothing property of the time-fractional diffusion model, the convergence rate could be further improved using some modified high-order schemes. For the time-fractional problem, the spatial smoothness of the solution is highly dependent on the regularity of the initial data. In contrast with its parabolic counterpart, which provides infinite smoothness in space (provided that the boundary of domain is smooth), the fractional model only provides a limited spatial regularity. However, in all existing studies, the analysis of spatially high-order schemes was done by assuming that the solution is sufficiently smooth. This motivates us to investigate high-order schemes in case that the initial data is nonsmooth. A splitting method will be introduced to separate the solution into two components, one time-dependent smooth part and one steady nonsmooth part. Then we shall develop high-order schemes for both components with a rigorous analysis, under some weak assumptions on the initial data.

25300818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300818.value: The time-fractional diffusion equation, which is used to capture the dynamics of anomalously slow diffusion, has received much attention in recent years. In contrast with its normal diffusion counterpart, the time-fractional diffusion equation involves a fractional-order derivative, which does not satisfy some classical calculus rules and often leads to limited regularity (in both time and space directions) of the solution. In case of nonsmooth data (e.g., initial data or source data), the solution will be more singular and therefore the analysis will be more challenging. In this project, we shall study numerical treatment for the time-fractional diffusion equations and derive optimal error estimates that are expressed with respect to regularity of (possibly very weak) problem data, without smoothness assumptions on solutions directly. The research will consist of three parts. First, we will investigate the time-fractional diffusion model involving a time-dependent diffusion coefficient, where existing techniques, mostly based on Laplace transform, are not directly applicable here. We shall provide sharp regularity estimates as well as the numerical analysis by a novel perturbation argument. High-order numerical methods will be discussed, using the convolution quadrature and the initial correction technique. Second, we intend to study the stochastic time-fractional diffusion model, where the additional restriction on the smoothing property is caused by the random noise. The numerical analysis relies crucially on suitable error estimates for the corresponding deterministic problem with nonsmooth data, and a careful study on the inhomogeneous part due to the stochastic process. Third and finally, we shall discuss how to improve the approximation in space, where the solution of the time-fractional diffusion model is nonsmooth in space due to the low regularity of the initial data and the presence of the time-fractional derivative. 时间分数阶扩散方程常常用于模拟反常亚扩散现象，近年来已受到广泛关注。相比于标准扩散方程，分数阶扩散方程含有的分数阶导数不满足传统的微积分运算法则并会导致解在时间和空间上均不光滑。当数据非光滑时，解则会更加奇异，因此数值方法的构造和分析就会更加困难。 在这个项目中，我们将研究时间分数阶扩散方程的数值方法，并证明逼近误差对于数据的正则性是最优的，而不需要对解得正则性做进一步假设。研究将分为三个部分。首先，我们将探讨该模型含有时间相关扩散系数的情况。现有的证明技巧大多依赖于laplace变换，将不适用于该情况。我们将提供构造一个新的perturbation argument去证明解的正则性以及数值方法的最优误差。此外，我们将进一步研究如何利用卷积数值积分和初始矫正的方法构造高阶方法。第二，我们将研究随机时间分数阶模型。随机噪声的存在将进一步影响解得光滑性。数值方法的讨论将依赖于确定性问题的误差分析以及对随机右端项的研究。最后，我们注意到时间分数阶扩散方程的解在空间上也缺乏一定的正则性，因此我将讨论如何改进空间上的逼近误差。

25300818.label: Realisation of objectives
25300818.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved. 1. For Objective 1, we investigated time-fractional diffusion equations with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. We developed a new perturbation argument and proved the well-posedness and limited regularity property in both space and time. Then we applied the methodology to analyze numerical approximations. We proved the optimal convergence rates for both spatially semidiscrete Galerkin FEM scheme and fully discrete schemes given by convolution quadrature in time. Finally, we applied this novel argument to develop high-order time-stepping schemes. In particular, we established high-order differentiability and regularity estimates. Using these regularity results and a refined perturbation argument, we proved that the convolution quadrature generated by the second-order backward differentiation formula, with proper correction at the first time step, can achieve second-order convergence for both nonsmooth initial data and incompatible source term. 2. For Objective 2, we developed and analyzed a numerical method for stochastic time-fractional diffusion driven by additive fractionally integrated Gaussian noise. The model involves two nonlocal terms in time, i.e., a Caputo fractional derivative, and fractionally integrated Gaussian noise with a Riemann-Liouville fractional integral. The numerical scheme approximates the model in space by the standard Galerkin method with continuous piecewise linear finite elements and in time by the classical Grunwald-Letnikov method, and the noise by the L2-projection. Sharp strong and weak convergence rates were established, using suitable nonsmooth data error estimates for the discrete solution operators for the deterministic inhomogeneous problem. 3. In contrast with the diffusion equation which smoothens the initial data to a infinitely differentiable function, the subdiffusion equation only exhibits limited spatial regularity. As a result, one generally cannot expect high-order accuracy in space in solving the subdiffusion equation with nonsmooth initial data. For Objective 3, we proposed a new splitting of the solution is constructed for high-order finite element approximations to the subdiffusion equation with nonsmooth initial data. The scheme was constructed by splitting the solution into two parts, i.e., a time-dependent smooth part and a time-independent nonsmooth part, and then approximating the two parts via different strategies. The time-dependent smooth part is approximated by using high-order finite element method in space and convolution quadrature in time, while the steady nonsmooth part could be approximated by using smaller mesh size or other methods that could yield high-order accuracy. Several examples are presented to show how to accurately approximate the steady nonsmooth part, including piecewise smooth initial data, Dirac--Delta point initial data, and Dirac measure concentrated on an interface. The argument could be directly extended to subdiffusion equations with nonsmooth source data. Extensive numerical experiments are presented to support the theoretical analysis and to illustrate the performance of the proposed high-order splitting finite element methods.

The scheme was constructed by splitting the solution into two parts, i.e., a time-dependent smooth part and a time-independent nonsmooth part, and then approximating the two parts via different strategies. The time-dependent smooth part is approximated by using high-order finite element method in space and convolution quadrature in time, while the steady nonsmooth part could be approximated by using smaller mesh size or other methods that could yield high-order accuracy. 25300818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300818.value: There are a lot of interesting problem still open. (1) The numerical analysis of the time-fractional model with a nonlinear diffusion coefficient is still an ongoing research topic. By combining the maximum L^p regularity and perturbation argument, it becomes feasible to investigate the sharp regularity estimates. Additionally, exploring the discrete variants of these techniques holds promise in driving the development and analysis of numerical schemes. (2) Developing a spatially high-order scheme for nonlinear time-fractional diffusion models remains an open question. In comparison to linear counterparts, this task presents additional challenges due to the change of the nonsmooth structure's profile. One potential approach is to establish a posterior error estimates and develop an algorithm to track the shifting singularities. (3) Similar to the standard parabolic equations, the time-fractional subdiffusion model also satisfies to the maximum principle. In our previous work [8], we successfully developed maximum principle preserving schemes with arbitrarily high-order accuracy for parabolic-type equations. However, the analysis heavily relies on the single-step structure of the time stepping scheme. Therefore, extending these methods to the nonlocal-in-time model poses significant challenges and necessitates further research and investigation.

25300818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300818.value: The interest in the time-fractional model stems from its wide range of applications involving anomalous diffusion, such as underground flow, thermal diffusion in fractal domains, dynamics of protein molecules, and heat conduction with memory, among others. At a microscopic level, processes exhibiting anomalously slow diffusion (referred to as subdiffusion) can be characterized by continuous-time random walks with heavy-tailed waiting time distributions. The corresponding macroscopic counterpart involves differential equations with fractional-order derivatives in time. Given the remarkable modeling capabilities, our focus lies in developing, analyzing, and testing efficient numerical methods for addressing such problems. In this project, we developed and analyzed numerical schemes for time-fractional diffusion models with nonsmooth structure. This particular case frequently arises in related inverse problems and optimal control problems. First, we investigated the model with a time-dependent diffusion coefficient. Second, we studied the stochastic model, where the additional difficulty comes from the limited regularity of stochastic process. Third and finally, we discussed how to improve the approximation in space, where the solution is nonsmooth due to the low regularity of problem data.

25300918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300918.value: 在很多聚合物材料和消費商品的合成過程中，原油和石油的轉化十分重要，其中，這些轉化中都會使用沸石分子篩催化劑。沸石分子篩在學術界和工業界都十分重要，沸石分子篩優秀的化學和物理特性，來源于其固態的酸位點，及其三維多孔結構。但是，研究人員仍然未能清楚地闡明各種反應分子與酸性位點的相附關係，及其催化反應的構效關係。本申請書擬進一步了解沸石和其他分子篩相關材料中的分子化學特性。 申請人擁有豐富沸石表徵和催化領域的經驗，亦成功闡明不少氣態氣子（如氨氣等）在沸石內部結構的原子位置。以同步輻射Ｘ射線衍射(SXRD)为主要技術的表徵方案，再结合其他表徵手段等，我們將研究不同沸石材料與反應分子的吸附特性。我們預計，此研究能為將來智能地設計新型多孔材料提供思路，以及科學的指導。

It is anticipated that the extensive fundamental understanding can advance the scientific investigation of more superior catalysts for industrially important reactions, such as methanol-to-hydrocarbons (MTH), and for more extensive applications. 25300918.label: Major findings and research outcome
25300918.value: This part elaborates on how the objectives have been fully realised: 1. Evaluation of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites in zeolites using probe-assisted synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction (Applied Catalysis A: General, 2020, 596, 117528.) The research work involves the elucidation of metal-adsorbate interactions in ZSM-5 and USY zeolites. The Rietveld refinements give both qualitatively and quantitatively the spatial arrangements and adsorption geometries of furan and dimethylfuran on the Brønsted acid sites (BAS) and metal Lewis acid sites (LAS). This descriptive study of surface acid-base chemistry on zeolites is not only merely a supplementary classification scheme on top of the traditional understanding but also provides a quantitative perspective to interrogate and optimise complex reactions catalysed by zeolites based on structural evidence. 2. Cooperative catalytically active sites for methanol activation by frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) in metal-doped ZSM-5 (Chem. Sci. 2021, 12(1), 210–219.) We have subsequently looked into how the atomistic information related to the molecular-zeolitic interactions can provide additional information to key industrial MTH reactions. It is demonstrated for the first time that active frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) within molecular distance can be created, which could lead to the initial heterolytic cleavage of small molecules such as water and methanol with subsequent reactions to form products at high selectivity. This can account for their active and selective catalytic routes of small molecule activations. 3. Differential adsorption of D-/L-Lys on achiral zeolites (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 132(3), 1109–1113.) We have also exploited our atomistic understanding of the microporous environment of zeolites to investigate the chiral chemistry within the achiral H-ZSM-5 zeolites (with MFI topology). We reported the first crystallographic observation of stereospecific bindings of L- and D-Lys in achiral MFI zeolites. The MFI structure offers inherent geometric and internal confinement effects for the enantiomeric difference in L- and D-Lys adsorption. Distinct L- and D-Lys adsorption behaviours on the H-ZSM-5 framework have been revealed by the Rietveld refinement of high-resolution SXRD data. 4. Investigation of achiral zeolites in asymmetric catalysis (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2020, 22, 18757) Thanks to the new-generation synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction (SXRD) facilities, we reveal the presence of the unique ‘chiral region’ in achiral zeolites. Both the inherent site-isolation effect of the active sites and internal confinement restraints in zeolites are critical for creating ‘chiral regions’ that can aid the design of more enantioselective catalytic reactions.

25300918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300918.value: Crystalline and porous zeolites and metal-organic frameworks are often considered a class of ideal host matrices for the immobilisation of foreign molecular metal species within the microporous ‘environments’ (cf. zeozymes). The research results obtained from the ECS project enable our team to further investigate the synergistic effect in heterogeneous catalysts, e.g., through various motifs within a microenvironment. Within the microenvironment, the interactions between proximate motifs between the inherent functionality (such as zeolitic Brønsted and Lewis acidities) and metal sites can offer interesting synergistic catalytic properties and facilitate tandem reactions. We anticipate that the synergistic effects between proximate active motifs shall result in higher reaction yield or yield transformations not possible with the bulk or ‘single-atom’ analogues. We would also aim to establish a research platform that harnesses the core concepts of inorganic chemistry and solid-state microporosity to rationally engineer potent microenvironments for the selective activation of C–H bonds. It will develop atom-efficient and highly selective heterogeneous catalytic systems to meet the challenges for the sustainable manufacture of valuable chemical products. The impact of this platform will also reveal countless possibilities for broader applications in other research disciplines.

25300918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300918.value: With a strong passion for chemistry and materials, the PI’s research vision is to tackle one of the biggest challenges in heterogeneous catalytic science – the design of catalytic landscapes with high precision and ease of green production. The ultimate goal of this project is to pave solid foundations for developing a research platform for new-generation solid atomic catalysts which will ultimately reach the molecular frontier. It is generally accepted that the elusive attributes of substrate generality and catalytic reaction efficiency cannot be anticipated, and it typically takes years of rigorous study to fully optimise the scope and reactivity of challenging catalytic processes. Our work reveals the geometric information and crystal structures of various metal-doped ZSM-5 catalysts, which form constricted frustrated Lewis pairs via the combined use of advanced characterisation techniques. The structure-activity relationships with respect to methanol (and also other small molecules) activations include (i) methanol-to-hydrocarbons, and (ii) methanol-to-aromatics. It offers a valuable platform for the further development of atom-efficient and highly selective heterogeneous catalytic systems to meet the challenges for the sustainable manufacture of valuable chemical products. The impact of this platform will also reveal countless possibilities for broader applications in other research disciplines.

25301018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25301018.value: The emergent two-dimensional (2D) crystals with atomic thickness have shown great promises in various applications. The 2D materials are special, almost all the atoms in 2D materials are on the surface. Among their wide applications, particularly, the remarkable flexibility accompanied with the ultrahigh in-plane strength in 2D materials make it suitable for stretchable/flexible devices, nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS), energy devices, lubricants, etc. As the basic mechanical tests for all materials, the tensile experiments on 2D materials have been previously conducted by either atomic force microscopy (AFM) or in situ transmission electron microcopy (TEM). In contrast, the bending properties of 2D materials are much more difficult to measure via experiments. In order to obtain the bending properties of 2D materials which is lacking in database now and serve for their future applications. In the current project our target is to obtain the bending mechanical parameters of 2D materials and understand the 2D bending by the combination of experimental and theoretical works. We will perform mechanical bending tests on several representative 2D materials like graphene and TMDs by the in situ TEM method. The atomically thin 2D materials will be bended, folded, and compressed by the atomically sharp tip mounted on the piezoelectric manipulator with nano-meter (nm) precision control in space and nano-newton (nN) resolution in force measurement. In the TEM the in-plane view and cross-section view experiments will be both conducted to see the membrane morphology change and local atomically structure variations. The bent structures of 2D will be pushed to the limit until fracture. Importantly, the ultimate bending strength which is the key parameter for future applications of 2D materials will be directly captured by our in situ TEM tests. Meanwhile, the phase stabilities of polymorphic 2D materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides will be examined under bending stress. The electronic structures of the bent structures as well as new phase information can be provided by high resolution STEM-EELS. The quantitative experimental results of current project will be rationalized by both the continuum mechanics modeling and atomic-scale simulations, moving forward the fundamental understanding of such distinct bending of 2D materials. 具有原子厚度的新興二維（2D）晶體正在各種應用中顯示出很好的效果。 2D材料是特殊的，因為幾乎所有2D材料中的原子都在表面上。在它們的廣泛應用中，尤其是 卓越的靈活性以及2D材料中超高的面內強度 使其適用於可拉伸/柔性裝置，納米機電系統（NEMS），能量裝置，潤滑劑等。作為所有材料的基本機械測試，2D材料的拉伸實驗先前已通過原子力顯微鏡（AFM）或原位透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）來完成。相比之下，2D材料的彎曲特性更難以通過實驗來測量。為了獲得現在數據庫中缺乏的2D材料的彎曲性能，並為將來的應用服務。在目前的項目中，我們的目標是獲得2D材料的彎曲力學參數，並通過實驗和理論工作的結合來理解2D彎曲。我們將通過原位TEM方法對幾種代表性的2D材料（如石墨烯和TMD）進行機械彎曲測試。原子級薄的2D材料將通過安裝在壓電機械手上的原子尖銳尖端進行彎曲，折疊和壓縮，在空間中具有納米（nm）精度控制，在力測量中具有納米牛頓（nN）分辨率。在TEM中，我們將進行面內視圖和橫截面視圖實驗以觀察膜形態變化和局部原子結構變化。 2D的彎曲結構將被推到極限直到破裂。另外，最終彎曲強度是二維材料未來應用的關鍵參數，這也將通過我們的原位TEM測試直接測量。同時，我們將在彎曲應力下檢測多晶二維材料如過渡金屬二硫屬化物的相穩定性。彎曲結構的電子結構以及新相結構可以由高分辨率STEM-EELS提供。通過連續介質力學建模和原子尺度模擬，當前項目的定量實驗結果將推進對2D材料彎曲性能的深入理解。

25301018.label: Realisation of objectives
25301018.value: All the objectives have been satisfactorily completed. (1) We have performed the in situ bending experiments by using in situ TEM on a series of 2D materials, including graphene, MoS2 and ReS2. The buckling and bending behavior have been thoroughly understood. We also addressed the critical stable properties of bended structures in 2D materials using in situ TEM and EELS. All of these findings have been published in ACS Nano, 2020, 14, 2137–2144. (2) We have completed the in situ TEM observations on the bending and related phase transitions in 2D ReS2. During the bending of 2D ReS2, we found the lattice reconstruction occur easily. The lattice reconstructions can be related to in-plane or out-of-plane strains, while the out-of-plane strain can even induce an abnormal fracture mode, which is unexpected and out of the scope of original plan. These findings have been published in Science Advances, 2020, 6, 47, eabc2282; PRL, 2020, 125, 246102. Meanwhile, we have identified the phase transition related to the the phase transition of 2D materials which are not very easily induced by pure bending. Alternatively, the phase transition can occur with the atomic defect sites. Please refer to Advanced Science, 2022, 202200702. (3) We have used the continuum mechanics model and density functional theory (atomistic model simulation) to describe the bended structures of 2D materials, and retrieved the bending properties of these 2D materials, such as graphene and 2D ReS2. It has been published in ACS Nano, 2020, 14, 2137–2144; Communiations Materials, 2021, 2, 87.

25301018.label: Major findings and research outcome
25301018.value: (1) We have synthesized 2D TMD materials like ReS2, the method and related growth mechanism by chemical vapor deposition has been published in Chemistry of Materials, 2021, 33, 17, 7039–7046. (2) We have performed the in situ bending experiments inside TEM on a series of 2D materials, including graphene, MoS2 and ReS2. The buckling and bending behavior have been thoroughly understood. We also addressed the critical stable properties of bended structures in 2D materials using in situ TEM and EELS. Our experiments, mechanical modeling, and self-consistent charge density functional tight binding (SCC-DFTB) simulations reveal that a minimum critical length is required for stabilizing the wrinkles in 2D materials. All of these findings have been published in ACS Nano, 2020, 14, 2137–2144. (3) We have successfully applied the easily bending 2D materials such as graphene, for the wrinkle pattern formation. The 1D and 2D ordered wrinkle patterns in 2D materials can be produced by by thermal straining and vertical spatial confinement. Our new approach can simplify the patterning processes on 2D layered materials, enabling numerous engineering applications that require ordered surface texturing (Nano Letters, 2020, 20, 11, 8420–8425). (4) We have completed the in situ TEM observations on the bending and related phase transitions in 2D ReS2. During the bending of 2D ReS2, we found the lattice reconstruction occur easily. The lattice reconstructions can be related to in-plane or out-of-plane strains, while the out-of-plane strain can even induce an abnormal fracture mode, which is unexpected and out of the scope of original plan. These findings have been published in Science Advances, 2020, 6, 47, eabc2282; PRL, 2020, 125, 246102. Meanwhile, we have identified the phase transition related to the the phase transition of 2D materials which are not very easily induced by pure bending. Alternatively, the phase transition can occur with the atomic defect sites. Please refer to Advanced Science, 2022, 202200702. (5) We have used the continuum mechanics model and density functional theory (atomistic model simulation) to describe the bended structures of 2D materials, and retrieved the bending properties of these 2D materials, such as graphene and 2D ReS2. It has been published in ACS Nano, 2020, 14, 2137–2144; Communications Materials, 2021, 2, 87. (6) We have completed a review work descirbing our previous researches on 2D material defects, and particularly, we addressed the relationship between bending/wrinkling and grain boudaries, please refer to Accounts of Chemical Reserach, 2021, 2021, 54, 22, 4191–4202.

25301018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25301018.value: We will continue to study the bended structures of 2D materials as it is the most important and unique property of the unique flexibilty in 2D materials. We actually found some interesting phenomena in 2D In2Se3 and the new phases emerge in bended structures of 2D In2Se3. On the other hand, we will also apply the intrinsic bending of 2D materials for activating the dynamics in 2D materials, and apply the driving force and loading for mehcanical testing of 2D materials in atomic scale by using in situ TEM. Finally, we will also search the applications for the bended structures of 2D materials, focusing on their electrical and optical properties, and we will continue to study and develop such new 2D structures. There is huge potential for further study and devleopment following this project.

25301018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25301018.value: The emergent two-dimensional (2D) crystals with atomic thickness have almost all the atoms on the surface. They are suitable for stretchable/flexible devices, nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS), energy devices, lubricants, etc. The bending properties of 2D materials are particularly important but quite difficult to measure via experiments. Here we performed mechanical bending tests on several representative 2D materials like graphene and TMDs by the in situ TEM method. The atomically thin 2D materials are bended, folded, and compressed. The bended structures of 2D usually formed wrinkles and we found there is critical length for the wrinkles to be stable. The continuum mechanics modeling and atomic-scale simulations have been performed and compared. Meanwhile, the bended 2D materials can easily trigger phase instabilities for the polymorphic 2D materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides, we have observed clear phase transition in 2D ReS2, the 2H, T' and T'' phases can be triggered under mechanical loading or under chemical excitation, and the bending behavior of these 2D materials are closely related to the mechanical loading conditons. Our work will move forward the fundamental understanding of 2D materials and promote novel applications using their intrinsic flexiblities.

25301518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25301518.value: With their exceptional structural diversity, natural products have been a treasure trove for drug discovery. Electrophilic natural products (eNPs) are of particular interest as they are naturally designed to interfere with a wide variety of biological functions by targeting nucleophilic centers like cysteines in proteins. Triptolide (TL), celastrol (Cel) and withaferin A (WA), three naturally occurring electrophiles, are promising therapeutic agents under clinical trials because of their strong inhibition on inflammation, cell proliferation, angiogenesis and tumor metastasis. Interestingly, independent studies have shown that they can exert bioactivities through the same signaling pathways. However, like many promiscuous natural products, a poor understanding of the target profiles of TL, Cel and WA has limited their mechanism studies as well as application in drug discovery. Our preliminary study has revealed that TL, Cel and WA bind the same cysteines in peroxiredoxin I through Michael addition. We hypothesize that they may share other protein targets with reactive cysteines which contribute to their bioactivities in common. We propose to design a robust chemical proteomics approach and simultaneously investigate the targets of TL, Cel and WA. We will apply two complementary “clickable” electrophilic probes to label reactive cysteines in proteins. A unique chemical proteomics protocol will be established for quantifying probe-labeled peptides as well as binding site assignment. By using an eNP-probe competition experiment combined with stable isotope labeling with amino acids in cell culture (SILAC) quantification, we will evaluate interactions between eNPs and thousands of proteins to identify their binding targets and explain their common bioactivities. The study will provide important insights into the mechanisms of eNPs with the same bioactivities and signaling pathways. Furthermore, the study can potentially generate therapeutic targets for drug discovery. 25303318.label: Realisation of objectives
25303318.value: The project objective completion was mainly successful; some results have been published in the listed journal papers. The individual materials have been incorporated individually and in pairs across textile and/or gel-based polymeric substrates, whilst a broader library of materials combinations and attendant physico-chemical data has also been built. Detailed characterisation of various, physico-chemical and mechanical properties were obtained during these investigations. Thus, the results provide foundational synthetic and mechanistic investigations, via careful characterisation, into several materials combinations of interest. However, the successful and effective combination of three-component systems in a single composite, as well as the related light-based antimicrobial testing of the three-component systems was not able to be fully completed in accordance with the initial project aims. Follow-on work will remedy this. Other related empirical extensions to the work (with partial overlaps with this project work, involving contributions from the project research assistant), are currently being composed for publication. Such results allow for improved surface control and functionalisation of polymeric substrates with various nanoparticles. This proves that the synthetic approaches and improved mechanistic understandings resulting from this project can be extended to other polymer composite systems, for effective functionalisation. By their conclusion, the synthetic aims of the project will have been fully completed, as well as the leach-resistance/durable material loading of substrates. The PI recruited a single research assistant as well as two part-time summer interns, to work on the project; all students received good training in several areas of modern science and technology in Hong Kong. The structure-property-function relationships of these composites were investigated and will form the foundation of future inorganic-polymer composites.
