25303318.label: Major findings and research outcome
25303318.value: These results show that a 2D-heterostructure-based (i.e.; reduced graphene oxide) composite exhibited a higher loading of nanoparticles onto a substrate as well as lower effective leaching, which in turn leads to higher effective (statistically significant) antibacterial activity. In all cases, leaching values were well below recognised environmental leaching limits (EPA). Materials synthesis was achieved via a two-step treatment; a substrate surface reduction process to increase the availability of hydroxyl groups, which then subsequently aid anchoring of nanoparticles to the micropores of polymeric textile substrates, upon immersion into the precursor mixture. The presence of the 2D-heterostructures seemingly aids the increased loading of the active nanoparticulate matter (e.g.; silver nanoparticles). All such experiments were done without the use of capping agents, binders or any other additional chemical component, and all matter was formed/reduced in situ, interacting with the substrate directly to form strong bonding interactions. For comparison, absent the use of the 2D heterostructures, the loading of active nanoparticles was lower, whilst the durability of the substrates to washing was also lower, as much of the nanoparticulate matter was leached away. Different photosensitiser dyes were also incorporated into various polymer substrates (unpublished), to effectively illustrate that the dyes could be effectively trapped within the polymers at high concentration. This includes photosensitiser dyes that may alternatively be classified as type I or II (Rose Bengal, R6G, Methylene Blue, etc.). This library of data, as gathered by the undergraduate summer interns for this project, will be critical to next-stage composite synthesis, comprising surface functionalisation – active compound impregnation processes, including conjugation of a relevant photosensitiser dye, for photodynamic treatments. In the second study, a series of double-network alginate-acrylamide tough hydrogels were synthesised. By varying the identity of the metal linking precursor (molar equivalents used in the experimental variants), we were able to modify the extent, onset and nature of the physical and chemical interactions between the various biomaterial components. These mechanistic changes were mapped in real-time, with bond evolution and structural rearrangements clearly visible over the course of a reaction, via a multitude of complementary spectroscopic and analytical techniques. Such physico-chemical variances resulting from simple interfacial modifications, were found to have marked effects on the eventual mechanical properties, e.g.; different stress relaxation characteristics were observed for different chemically-organised structures. Depending on the cross-linking agent, the relative contributions of these phases, and the resultant favouring of either M-group or G-group co-ordination along the alginate backbone.

25303318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25303318.value: Composite materials with light-activated properties retain a strong research interest across various disciplines and applications. This project provides a concrete and flexible framework for the further development of 2D-heterostructure-based, light-activated polymeric materials and surfaces. While the foundational studies are complete and a strong mechanistic understanding obtained, considerable follow-up work still remains (as was intended from the outset of the project). The following areas of research can be further explored: 1) The generation of phototoxic ROS, via the photosensitiser, to surface-impingent species upon exposure to environmental white light sources; 2) Elucidate the underlying mechanism of these degradative processes by using non-destructive, in situ characterisation approaches, is unusual reaction and explore its synthetic utility, and; 3) Further improve the reactive oxygen species/singlet oxygen generation quantum efficiency and/or electron transfer mechanisms (the chosen path dependent on the environmental conditions and most favourable reaction path), to expand the photodynamic process, combining the testing of different components carried out in this project (i.e.; 2D-heterostructures, metal nanoparticles, photosensitiser dyes – perhaps taking advantage of persistent luminescence, ionic- and/or covalent- cross-linking agents, etc.). It is believed that these further studies can lead to more advanced photosensitizers that can greatly assist the further development of photodynamic therapy.

25303318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25303318.value: The aim of this research was to experimentally synthesise, test and analyse multi-component composite materials, based on 2D-heterostructures and polymers, to derive stable and responsive materials. Detailed spectroscopic, thermal, structural and leaching properties of these composites were investigated in order to gain novel synthetic and mechanistic insights. The benefit of in-depth mechanistic understanding and empirical refinement is that it can lead to materials with improved physico-chemical properties as compared to literature reports to-date. The foundational results from this project have broad application and so have explanatory and predictive value when applied to large classes of overlapping multicomponent materials for use in biomedical applications. For example, our data from this project can allow for improved efficiencies in surface treatment and/or precursor control (via wet chemical routes), for enhanced attachment of nanoparticles (i.e.; higher load/less equivalent leaching), and/or improved mechanical properties of composites. Such intervention routes should serve as lead methodologies for further advancing the R&D process of materials development, including photosensitiser-based systems.

25304218.label: Project Objectives
25304218.value: We will develop association tests between incomplete genomic variables and phenotypes, where missing genomic data are imputed from the available data based on the biological associations among variables. Specifically, we will explore semiparametric methods to improve robustness against misspecification of the missing-data model. We will also develop model-selection methods for the incomplete genomic variables, which yield optimal efficiency in the analysis of the phenotype model. We will develop prediction and variable-selection methods for multiple types of incomplete high-dimensional genomic variables. Specifically, we will explore a penalized model-updating method to build a sparse prediction rule, which accounts for missing data and the differences in predictive power of the data types. We will also study variable selection under a general theoretical framework that includes multiple types of independent variables.

25304218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25304218.value: Because of recent technological advances in genomic profiling, some large-scale genomics studies have been able to collect multiple types of genomic data, including mutation, copy number variation, DNA methylation, and the expression levels of mRNA, miRNA, and protein, for patients with various diseases. These multi-platform genomic data provide unprecedented opportunities for understanding disease mechanisms and identifying molecular abnormalities associated with diseases. However, the complexity of the data poses enormous statistical and computational challenges. Conventional statistical methods fail to account for incomplete observations, high-dimensional data, or associations among different types of genomic data, and therefore are inefficient and may even be invalid. In this grant period, we will develop novel methods that integrate data from multiple genomics platforms for identifying variables associated with phenotypes of interest. In particular, we will study the association analysis between phenotypes and a set of incomplete genomic variables. We propose robust methods for imputation of missing genomic data and will develop model-selection methods for the incomplete genomic variables. Also, we will study the regression analysis of multiple types of high-dimensional incomplete genomic data. We propose a stepwise penalization-based method to accommodate missing data and the differences across data types. All proposed methods properly utilize the biological relationships among genomic variables to improve efficiency. The proposed research will enhance understanding of complex diseases, and the methods are broadly applicable to problems from other disciplines that involve multiple types of (incomplete) data. To maximize the impact of our research, we will disseminate user-friendly software to facilitate the use of the proposed methods by the research community. 基於最近在基因組分析上的技術進步，一些大規模基因組學研究已經能夠從不同疾病的病人收集多種類型的基因組數據，包括突變，拷貝數變異，DNA甲基化以及mRNA，miRNA和蛋白質的表達水平。這些多平台基因組數據為理解和識別與疾病相關的分子機制提供了前所未有的機會。然而，數據的複雜性帶來了巨大的統計和計算上的挑戰。傳統的統計方法因不能處理不完整的數據、高維數據或不同類型基因組數據之間的關聯，所以有效性低，甚至可能不正確。在這項目中，我們將開發新的方法來整合來自多個基因組平台的數據，以識別與各樣表型相關的變量。我們將特別研究表型與不完整的基因組變量之間的關聯分析方法。我們將提出穩健的方法來插補缺失的基因組數據，並會開發用於不完整基因組變量的模型選擇方法。此外，我們將研究多類型的高維不完整基因組數據的回歸分析。我們提出一種逐步的正規化方法來處理缺失數據以及不同數據類型之間的差異。所有提出的方法都利用基因組變量之間的關係來提高有效性。擬議的研究將增強我們對複雜疾病的理解，並且該方法廣泛適用於其他學科裡涉及多種類型（不完整）數據的問題。為了最大限度地發揮我們研究的影響，我們將發放容易使用的軟件，以方便研究界使用所提出的方法。

25304218.label: Realisation of objectives
25304218.value: Regarding the first objective, we have developed a hypothesis testing procedure for incomplete genomic variables and phenotypes of interest, where the incomplete variables can be predicted from available data, including auxiliary variables collected on other data types. One major advantage of the proposed methods is that we allow for the existence of high-dimensional auxiliary variables. We rigorously proved the validity of the proposed methods and also studied the power of the tests. We have performed large-scale simulation studies to investigate the empirical properties of the proposed methods and their advantages over existing methods. We also demonstrated the usefulness of the proposed methods using actual cancer genomics studies. Regarding the second objective, we have developed a penalized regression approach for relating an outcome of interest to incomplete multi-platform features. We constructed a structured factor model for the multi-platform features and developed a likelihood-based method for estimation. The factor model accounts for the differences across genomic features of different platforms. The proposed methods are computationally efficient even with a large number of missing variables and arbitrary missing patterns. We studied the theoretical properties of the proposed methods and conducted large-scale simulation studies to investigate the empirical properties of the proposed methods. We applied the proposed methods to an actual cancer genomics study. In addition, to study the relationship between disease outcomes and different types of genomic features, we developed a regression approach to relate a disease outcome with multiple types of genomics/clinical variables. We account for interaction effects among multiple types of variables using a single-index varying coefficient model. We performed simulation studies to investigate the empirical performance of the proposed methods and demonstrated the proposed methods to cancer genomics studies. Moreover, as a preliminary work on modeling disease outcomes and multi-platform genomic features under a heterogeneous population, we developed a latent class model for longitudinal measurements and survival outcomes. We devised an estimation method for low-dimensional data and established the theoretical properties of the proposed method. This is a precursor for a latent-class model for the integrative analysis of high-dimensional, incomplete, multi-omics data.

25304218.label: Major findings and research outcome
25304218.value: Four journal papers are published as the research outcome of this project. The first paper is “Score Tests with Incomplete Covariates and High-Dimensional Auxiliary Variables,” in which we studied hypothesis testing with incomplete covariates and developed a general theory that incorporates high-dimensional auxiliary variables. The second paper is “Penalized Regression for Multiple Types of Many Features With Missing Data,” in which we studied estimation and variable selection with incomplete multi-platform genomic data. The third paper is “Penalized Estimation of a Class of Single-Index Varying-Coefficient Models for Integrative Genomic Analysis,” in which we studied a single-index model that accommodates interaction effects between different types of genomics variables. The fourth paper is “Semiparametric Latent-Class Models for Multivariate Longitudinal and Survival Data,” in which we studied a flexible latent class model for longitudinal measurements and a censored survival time.

25304218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25304218.value: The published works can be extended in some of the following general directions: (1) extend the proposed methods to semiparametric models that allow for more relaxed model assumptions; (2) extend the proposed methods to different data structures, such as interval-censored survival times; and (3) specifically for the work on latent class models, incorporate high-dimensional multi-platform genomic features into the modeling framework.

25304218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25304218.value: In this project, we developed tools for addressing scientific questions that arise from analyzing modern genomic data, which are often complex and subject to missingness. In particular, we studied methods for understanding the relationship between genomic features and diseases, such as cancer. We considered problems of estimation, hypothesis testing, variable selection, prediction, and clustering. We developed effective and computationally feasible methods with rigorous theoretical justifications. Although the methods are mainly motivated by biomedical applications, the methods and theoretical innovations are nevertheless are generally applicable to other scientific studies that involve missing data, high-dimensional data, and time-to-event data.

25502318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25502318.value: The meetings, incentives, conventions and exhibitions (MICE) sector has recently been the most rapidly growing tourism sector in Hong Kong. The expansion of MICE venue space, the fourfold increase of international attendees and the consequent tremendous economic benefits testify to the remarkable growth of Hong Kong’s MICE sector in the past two decades. The increasing yield of visitor spending makes MICE an important sector for business tourism in Hong Kong. As part of an effort to liberalise trade, the latest supplement to the Closer Economic Partnership Agreement between Hong Kong and China allows Hong Kong service suppliers to provide convention and exhibition services to ten provinces, four municipalities and one autonomous region in mainland China. Such an expanding market benefits Hong Kong service suppliers, and the future of MICE sector development in the city looks promising. With full committment to strengthen Hong Kong’s appeal as the ‘Trade Fair Capital of Asia’, the government established a working group with an earmarked budget of HK$243 million to promote MICE tourism. This group is an extension of the former cross-sector steering committee, comprising representatives from the government, convention and exhibition sector, travel sector, hotel trades and tertiary and training institutions who review and formulate development strategies aimed at a continuous supply of world-class ‘professionals’ to support the rapid development of the relevant industries. However, it operates with no consistent and recognised definition of ‘professional’ attributes. While no single instrument can capture all aspects of professionalism, previous studies have not mainly focused on convention and exhibition tourism. As conventional multi-dimensional professionalism models focus largely on industry views, a study drawing on practitioner and customer (user) perspectives will fill the research gaps. Through a two-stage research incorporating a key informant approach with 20 industry leaders and attendees, and two rounds of questionnaires targeting different groups (500 business event planners at different levels and 500 local and international attendees), the aim of this study will be to develop a valid and reliable measure to rigorously evaluate and delineate professionalism for the MICE sector. This study will identify the dimensions of professionalism for individual business event planners by consolidating the viewpoints of various levels of practitioners and local and international users. Structural equation model analysis will then be used to examine the relationships between the various dimensions of professionalism and performance constructs. The work will help managers and employees to understand the aspects of performance required for professional MICE practice. N/A

25507818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25507818.value: In the proposed study, I will examine bank auditors' responses to subprime lending in the context of the 2007–2009 global financial crisis. The unprecedented growth in subprime mortgages and the fraud-laden subprime lending process prior to the financial crisis will provide unique data for this study. I will construct measures that gauge the extent to which individual banks engaged in risky mortgage lending and mortgage fraud. For mortgage fraud, I will focus on unreported second liens, owner occupancy misreporting, and appraisal overstatements. Using these measures, I will examine whether bank auditors charge higher audit fees when a bank’s subprime risk and fraud increase. To understand why audit fees increase, I will explore a novel measure that capture the ex post consequences of banks' subprime activities–non-accounting subprime fraud settlements. I will also use another two measures: bank earnings quality and bank failure. I will further investigate whether the bank’s earnings is of lower quality when its auditors charge higher audit fees. I will then examine whether the bank’s audit pre-crisis fees increase predicts the mortgage fraud-related settlements of banks and bank failure during the post-crisis period. 用最近的一次金融危機作為研究情景,我們檢驗了審計師對銀行客戶次級貸款業務的反應。在金融危機前夕，極速增長的次級按揭貸款以及舞弊盛行的次貸發放過程預示了2007-2009全球金融危機，同時也為本研究提供了獨特的數據。首先，我對每個銀行從事高風險按揭和相關舞弊的程度進行了量化。對於按揭舞弊行為，我主要關注三個方面：未告知的第二留置權，房主佔有方式的錯報以及房屋價值的高估。同時，我也對這些舞弊行為的后果進行了量化，具體包括針對相關舞弊的和解金額以及該銀行是否在金融危機爆發后破產。運用這些量化指標，我檢驗了銀行審計師是否對次貸風險和舞弊程度較高的客戶收取了更高的審計費用。進一步地，我還檢驗了這種審計師的反應能否預測舞弊和解金額以及銀行客戶的破產。

25508618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25508618.value: 接受他人帮助是否会威胁到我的社会地位:員工帮助類型及人際公平對受惠者地位及後續影響的事件採樣研究

25508618.label: Project Objectives
25508618.value: To develop a matrix of receiving help based on what help is given (i.e., dependency-oriented help versus autonomy-oriented help) and how the help is communicated (i.e., the helper demonstrates high versus low interpersonal justice). To examine how receiving help influences the recipient’s perception of threat to social status. To examine the downstream behavioral consequences of receiving help.
rows: To develop a matrix of receiving help based on what help is given (i.e., dependency-oriented help versus autonomy-oriented help) and how the help is communicated (i.e., the helper demonstrates high versus low interpersonal justice).
To examine how receiving help influences the recipient’s perception of threat to social status.
To examine the downstream behavioral consequences of receiving help.

25508618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508618.value: Do you always feel good when your coworkers help you? Scholars and practitioners alike may say yes because helping, like social support, is a valuable resource that should be encouraged in organizations. However, my previous and ongoing studies suggest otherwise, that recipients have a more ambivalent and complex experience when they receive help. The purpose of this project is to answer this question by unpacking the dynamics of receiving help and examining the influences of receiving help, as a product of what help was given and how the help was given, on the recipient’s perception of threat to social status and downstream behavioral consequences. Unlike the existing literature that focuses on the social exchange between a helper and a help recipient, I introduced the helping (receiving help) relations as status relations model (Nadler, 2002), and highlighted that the process of receiving help is a process where the help recipient loses status and experiences inferiority to the helper. I develop a typology of receiving help based on the "what" and the "how" component of helping. First, one may receive dependency-oriented help (given fish) or autonomy-oriented help (taught to fish). The status threatening effect is stronger when one receives dependency-oriented help than when one receives autonomy-oriented help. Second, help may be communicated in different ways. A helper might be polite and respectful (high interpersonal justice) or rude and disrespectful (low interpersonal justice) when s/he provides help. Thus, whether the helper demonstrates interpersonal justice when providing help is another key component to determine whether the recipient experiences the status threatening effect. Third, I further argue that the "how" component (interpersonal justice) could buffer the status threatening effect of receiving both types of help. Further, the status threatening effect of receiving help might hinder help recipients’ help-seeking behavior but encourage their learning behavior in the future, especially among those with higher status striving motive. As this study taps into the characteristics of receiving help episodes, I follow the paradigm I used in my prior studies and propose to conduct an experience sampling study to capture the real occurrence of receiving help episodes. This proposed research will contribute to our understanding of how receiving help influences the help recipients, and help us to identify practices of how help should be given at work to minimize the negative influences on the help recipient. 當同事給你提供幫助的時候，你是否總是感到開心？大部分学者与业界人士也許都會說是，因為助人行為和社會支持都是珍贵的社会資源。然而，我过去的研究發現，當人們在接受他人幫助時，会体验一种矛盾及復雜的感受。本研究旨在了解接受他人帮助的动态过程，以及在接受幫助後員工是否感到社会地位受到威胁和后续的行为反应。 以往關於助人行為的研究普遍關注施惠者與受惠者之間的社會交換，本研究則采用“帮助關係等同于地位關係”模型(Nadler, 2002)， 并强调接受他人帮助的过程是一种自我地位损失及体验到自己比施惠者弱势的过程。根據受惠过程的兩個特徵：他人所给予的帮助类型以及帮助是如何被呈现的，我建立了一個描述受惠过程的分类。首先，个体可能会接受到依賴性導向的帮助(授人以魚)或者是自主性導向的帮助(授之以漁)。當接受到依賴性導向的帮助時，個體社会地位受到威胁的程度强于当其接受到自主性導向的帮助时。其次，帮助将会以不同的方式呈现。施惠者可能会用禮貌且尊重他人的方式(高人际公平)給他人提供幫助，但也有可能用粗魯無禮的方式(低人际公平)。這兩種不同方式不僅會影响受惠者所感受到的社会地位受威胁的程度，亦会调节帮助类型与社会地位受威胁程度的关系。最後，當受惠者感到自己的地位受到威脅時，他們會減少后续求助行為并加强自我学习。对于那些有高社会地位欲望的受惠者来说，这段关系尤其强烈。 由於本研究关注每一个受惠过程的独特特性，我將採用事件採樣研究方法，以真实地捕捉每一个受惠事件发生的经过。本研究將有助於我們更了解助人行為是如何影響受惠者，并在实务上建议一种适当的助人方式，以減少助人行為對受惠者所帶來的負面影響。

25508618.label: Realisation of objectives
25508618.value: Across eight studies using different research designs, we examine whether help recipients may respond negatively and harm the help giver when they perceive helping as a status threat and experience envy. We also compare the consequences of receiving different types of help in combination with different levels of relative competence between the helper and the help recipients. Results show that only when one receives task-related help, but not person-related help, from a more competent, rather than less competent, help giver, they would perceive a higher level of threat to social status, and subsequently engage in social undermining toward the help giver. We only achieved 70% of the first objective because we developed a different matrix of receiving help based on what help is given (help type: task-related help vs. person-related help) and the relative competence of the help giver (more competent help giver vs. less competent help giver), based on the suggestions and feedback we received from participants in research seminars as well as reviewers. Nevertheless, our research achieved objectives 2 and 3 because (1) we identified a unique help type (i.e., task-related help) and a unique contingent factor (i.e., relative competence) that would result in recipient’s perception of threat to social status, as well as the downstream negative behavioral consequence of receiving help (i.e., social undermining).

25508618.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508618.value: Integrating the helping as status relations framework and the social functional perspective of envy, we examine when and why receiving help may prompt help recipients to undermine help givers. We propose that when individuals receive task-related help from help givers who are perceived to be more, rather than less, competent than them, they experience greater status threat and envy. As help recipients experience envy toward help givers, they are likely to undermine help givers, and this positive relationship becomes stronger for help recipients who have higher status striving motivation. To test our theoretical model, we conducted eight studies. First, we conducted two studies with a round robin design using two separate samples of student teams in Hong Kong. In these two studies, we examined whether receiving task-related help would result in help recipient’s status threat when the help giver is perceived to be more competent than the help recipient, and whether status threat in turn would induce envy. Second, we conducted a four-wave study with data collected from employees in the United Kingdom to constructively replicate Study 1 and test the overall model. Lastly, to replicate these results and provide support for causal relations, we conducted five pre-registered experiments. In the published article, we conducted two pre-registered experiments using an experimental causal chain design, in which we manipulated our independent, mediating and moderating variables in separate studies to test different parts of our theoretical model. Three additional experiments, which were included in the online supplemental materials, provided more robust evidence of our findings. Overall, our findings underscore the status dynamics implicated in helping interactions by highlighting that help recipients, especially those with higher status striving motivation, may paradoxically undermine help givers when they perceive status threat from and feel envious of help givers, as a result of receiving help from more competent help givers. This research was presented at the 79th Annual Meeting of the Academy of Management in 2019, with a shortened version published in the Best Paper Proceedings. The full paper was accepted for publication in the Journal of Applied Psychology in April 2022.

25508618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508618.value: Our research opens doors to new areas of inquiries about the paradoxical implications of giving and receiving help. First, one might argue that other characteristics of the help, such as help solicitation, may explain our proposed effect. Future research could directly measure the frequency of solicited versus unsolicited help and examine how help recipients react to solicited versus unsolicited help and their downstream impacts. Second, future studies could also examine other moderators of the link between receiving task-related help and status threat, such as the characteristics of the help giver. For example, when the help recipient perceives the help giver to be warm, it may weaken the status threatening effect of receiving task-related help from a more competent help giver. Lastly, although we did not differentiate autonomy versus dependency-oriented help in this study, status threat and envy resulting from receiving task-related help might predict different types of help provision in return. Given that envious help recipients with higher status striving motivation are more motivated to exercise power and influence over others, they are more likely to return the favor with dependency-oriented (but not autonomy-oriented) help to foster future dependence from the envied targets and effectively close the status gap.

25508618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508618.value: We often offer help to others at work, holding the belief that we are doing others a favor, something that is beneficial to the recipients, and expecting that the help recipient will pay us back. However, as the old saying goes, “No good deed goes unpunished,” we are sometimes punished for helping. Our research provides support for the phenomenon of “biting the hand that feeds.” In particular, we find that receiving task-related help from a more competent coworker would elicit the perception of status threat and the feeling of envy, which results in social undermining behavior toward the help giver, especially among help recipients who have a higher status striving motivation. In contrast, receiving person-related help does not lead to status threat, nor envy or social undermining. To limit the paradoxical “biting the hand that feeds” effect, we encourage help recipients to overcome their tendency of competence comparison and instead focus on processing the value of the help received. We also suggest that envious help recipients with higher status striving motivations should be mindful of how they may socially undermine envied help givers and potentially invite negative reciprocity that harms the dyadic relationship in the long run.

25600718.value: 社交媒體時代白手興家的數碼藝人：香港YouTuber博主及Facebook意見領袖的工作生活經歷

25600718.label: Project Objectives
25600718.value: Local relevance: investigate the process by which media-savvy individuals engage social media and mobile technology to pursue self-started enterprises in the digital entertainment industry, as well as how they interpret and negotiate their professional status and circumstances. 25600718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25600718.value: Recent advances in social media and mobile technology have facilitated the emergence of self-created enterprises and self-made celebrities in the digital entertainment industry worldwide. In Hong Kong, there has been a substantial growth in the number of full-time YouTubers and Facebook opinion leaders, who create and upload (video) blogs to generate revenue as a major source of income. They constitute an emerging phenomenon, in which digitally-enabled individuals translate their leisure activities and time into production activities and self-employment. A large body of literature has focused on the new reconfigurations in the so-called gig economy associated with issues such as capital accumulation by online platforms, the erosion of government’s tax basis, and the deterioration of labor rights. However, little effort has been made to examine the lived experiences of those who move into self-entrepreneurship by experimenting with new media technology. Furthermore, Facebook celebrities and YouTube video bloggers may suffer from inferiority and marginalization that are deeply tied to the milieu of Hong Kong society. Knowledge of their socio-technological practices to cope with the challenges they face is crucial if we are to understand the sustainability and potentials of the digital entertainment industry in Hong Kong. This project examines the work-life experiences of Hong Kong YouTubers and Facebook opinion leaders. By integrating two previously separate fields of study, namely the social studies of technology and sociology of work and leisure, it analyzes their pathways to entrepreneurships in the newly emerging industry. Based on interviews, participant observation fieldwork, and media content analysis, this project will provide a better understanding of (1) the process by which media-savvy individuals engage social media and mobile technology to pursue their digital entertainment careers, (2) how they interpret and negotiate their professional status and circumstances, and (3) the strategies they adopt to sustain and expand their enterprises. This project will generate empirical and theoretical insights that will be of interest to scholars and policymakers. First, it will provide timely research on the self-entrepreneurships in the growing industry of digital entertainment. Second, it will enable theorization of the changing relationship between work and leisure particularly with reference to social media environments. Lastly, it will inform policy addressing the development of the creative economy, and facilitate the government’s initiative to reinforce Hong Kong’s position as hub of digital entertainment in the region. 社交媒體和流動科技的最新進發展促進了全球的數碼娛樂產業的創業以及名人現象。香港近年YouTuber視頻博主及Facebook意見領袖的全職人數大幅增加，製作（視頻）博客成為了他們的主要收入來源。在數碼化下，他們將原本只屬於個人的休閒活動及時間轉化成為新的生產活動及自營職業，並構成了一種新興社會現象。 大量文獻都只集中討論了零工經濟中有關資本積累，政府稅收基礎的削弱，及勞工權利的惡化等題目，較少有學者探討那些嘗試通過新社交媒體技術實現創業場的數碼藝人的工作生活經歷。另外，Facebook名人及YouTube視頻博主有可能會遭受階及矮化和邊緣化等與香港社會環境息息相關的問題。因此，探討他們應對挑戰的生存策略及做法對了解香港數碼娛樂產業的可持續性和潛力至關重要。 本研究項目主要探討香港YouTuber視頻博主和Facebook意見領袖的工作生活經歷。通過整合兩個先前相對獨立的研究領域，即科技社會研究及工作與休閒社會學，本研究分析他們的創業途徑及工作經歷。基於訪談，參與觀察和媒體內容分析，本項目將對以下問題提供深入的見解:（1）精通新社交媒體的電子藝人如何追逐他們的電子娛樂事業，（2）他們如何 自我闡釋他們的專業地位並與之協商，以及（3）他們採取什麼策略來維持及擴展他們的事業。 本項目將為學術界及政策制定者提供有效的理論和見解。首先，本研究及時地對正在不斷擴展的電子娛樂產業進行深入探討。其次，它針對社交媒體環境下工作和休閒之間的關係正不斷變化的現象進行理論研究。最後，它為發展創意經濟的政策提供實用的資訊，促進政府推動及鞏固香港作為區內數碼娛樂中心的地位。

25600718.label: Realisation of objectives
25600718.value: All the three research objectives set out in the proposal were achieved. To achieve these objectives, this research project conducted 72 in-depth interviews, analysis of social media content of 87 content creators, and 5 participant observation fieldworks. These methods allow for a more comprehensive understanding of the informants’ work-life experiences. The first objective of the research project is to investigate the process by which media-savvy individuals engage digital media technology in pursuing self-started enterprises in the new creative economy, and how they negotiate their professional identity and cope with challenges. While identifying various career pathways towards digital entertainment, this research found that the informants’ family experiences of entrepreneurship (not limited to digital ones) and social class backgrounds are influential in shaping the individuals’ perceptions of and decisions on pursing digital entertainment as a long-term career. The second objective of the research is to identity barriers to the development of new creative economy by evaluating the strategies adopted by self-started digital entertainers to cope with challenges. The analysis shows that in addition to creativity and hard work, additional resources, such as cultural capital and social networks, are often mobilized and needed for pursuing the self-enterprise of digital entertainment. Business or policy initiatives that promote skillsets and know-hows for mobilizing these resources, especially among early-career content creators, may facilitate the development of digital entertainment industry. The third objective of the research is to further our theoretical understanding of the contemporary relationship between technology, economy, and society. This research contributes to the scholarship by adopting a critical lens to examine how classed-based inequality may shape people’s pathways towards the new creative economy. In particular, it contends that a Bourdieusian approach offers a useful and dynamic framework which can be used to examine how the processes of content production and audience engagement are shaped by social class origins and family backgrounds.

25600718.label: Major findings and research outcome
25600718.value: This research results in a conference paper and two journal articles. Major research findings are addressed and discussed in these academic outputs. First, this research offers insights into the career pathways and professional engagement of self-started digital entertainers. In particular, the research findings reveal the roles played by social class and family background in creating distinction in the mobilization of resources and capitals for initiating their self-enterprises. It was found that while more privileged informants tend to experience more fruitful processes of content creation and develop a stronger professional identity, less privileged informants may experience a loss of meaning and identity over time, and they sometimes learn to develop tacit tactics, such as alternative schema of interpretation of the meaning of their work, to cope with these circumstances. Second, this research reveals that content creators coming from various social class backgrounds can mobilize different sets of habitus and repertoires internalized by the youthful agents to engage audience of a respective field, as social media platform is nowadays characterized by a rather fragmented audienceship. Meanwhile, social capital is crucial to the formation of collaborative projects of content production, which constitutes a crucial strategy to maintain and expand fandom. Third, by illustrating the distinctive pathways to vlogging, this study puts forward a Bourdieusian approach that can generate nuanced understanding of how the youthful agents draw from cultural practices of their class origins with different tastes and know-hows in undertaking vlogging and entrepreneurial activities in the new creative economy. While most digital inequality research focuses on platform exploitation and gendered or racial inequality, this research explicates how tenable professional vlogging involves the mobilization of additional resources and power deeply tied to class positions, such that digital labor and professional identity can be shaped by unequal vlogging practices in the processes.

25600718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25600718.value: This project lays down a foundation for understanding the formation of work-life experiences, cultural practices and social networks underpinning the new creative industry. It has potential for further development. First, findings about the relationship between social class and content creation points out a potential direction for future research to investigate the constraints among less privileged content creators more systematically. This can become an especially important issue during economic downturns. Second, with the growing interest and increasing importance of health communication, especially during and in the aftermath of global pandemic, this research can be further expanded to identify more effective means of content creation and communication to engage audience with various social and class backgrounds.

25600718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25600718.value: This research examines the youthful agents’ pathways towards the self-entrepreneurship of digital entertainment. It aims to understand the process by which they come to engage in the new creative economy, and how they negotiate their professional identity and cope with challenges. Drawing on in-depth interviews, content analysis, and participant observation fieldworks, this research suggests that social class origins and family backgrounds are influential in creating distinction in the mobilization of resources and capitals for content production and audience engagement. While more privileged informants tend to experience a more fruitful process of content creation and develop a stronger professional identity, less privileged informants may experience a loss of meaning and identity over time, but they can also learn to develop tacit tactics to cope with these circumstances. The research findings advance our understanding of the formation of work-life experiences, cultural practices, and social networks underpinning the newly emerging creative economy.

25601618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25601618.value: 旅遊之審美體驗：遊客、居民及目的地審美特徵

25601618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25601618.value: Tourism consumption is image-oriented and aesthetic. Yet, knowledge regarding the aesthetic component of tourism is very limited. Particularly, existing research demonstrated that tourists utilize a number of criteria when judging a destination as beautiful or ugly, tested a scale to assess destination aesthetic properties, and showed that destination aesthetic qualities contribute to a vacation being perceived as restorative. Although valuable, these studies are situated in the Western context, marketing-driven and neglect the question of how destination aesthetics is actually experienced, or “lived”. This is problematic from four perspectives. First, the notion of aesthetic judgment is the outcome of an aesthetic experience. Thus, our current knowledge of tourism aesthetics is limited to inputs (destination features) and the outputs (aesthetic judgment), while the most critical understanding of how destination beauty is experienced is missing. Second, philosophers argue that aesthetically significant experiences are not limited to the beautiful and also include the sublime, the picturesque and thus, our current understanding does not capture the complexity of aesthetic responses. Third, insights obtained in the Western settings may be non-transferable to other contexts. Fourth, since many tourist attractions are in fact shared spaces, aesthetic consumption at a tourist destination must be also viewed from the perspective of residents. The proposed research sets out to address the above gaps by linking inputs (destination aesthetic qualities) to processes (aesthetic experiences). Given that tourist aesthetic experiences are subjective, this study will also explore similarities and differences in how aesthetic experiences are lived through by tourists and by residents. The study investigates aesthetic experiences set in Hong Kong, a suitable context given its popularity as a tourist destination with multiple tourist attractions (nature-based and urban). The study is interdisciplinary and is informed by the fields of the philosophy of arts, general and environmental psychology, architecture and urban design, and adopts a mixed-method approach. Phase I, designed as a descriptive phenomenological study, aims to describe tourists’ experiences of the beautiful, the sublime, and the picturesque. Phase II is an exploratory cross-sectional quantitative study, designed to empirically link destination properties with aesthetic experiences. Differences in tourists’ and residents’ data will be explored. In the long run, we will supply insights into how to design and maintain destination sites in ways that are aesthetically pleasing to residents and are attractive to tourists, which is useful in attempts to balance the interests of the tourism sector with those of the local communities. 旅遊消費是以形象為導向且具審美性。然而，關於旅遊美學成分之知識比較有限。特別是，現有研究顯示了遊客在判斷目的地是否美麗或醜陋時使用了許多標準、測試了評估目的地美學特性的尺度、並且展示了目的地美學品質有助於度假被視為能夠使人精力恢復。這些研究雖然具有一定的價值，但都以西方為背景、受營銷驅動而忽略了遊客對目的地美學的實際體驗或經歷的問題。 從四個方面分析，這些研究存在著問題。首先，審美判斷的概念是審美體驗之結果。因此，我們目前對旅遊美學的了解僅限於輸入（目的地特徵）和輸出（審美判斷），而缺乏對遊客如何體驗目的地美感最重要的理解。其次，哲學家認為，美學上重要的體驗不僅限於美麗的東西，還要包括震撼、風景如畫，因此，我們目前的理解並沒有捕捉到審美反應的複雜性。第三，在西方環境中獲得的見解未必可以轉移到其他環境。第四，由於許多旅遊景點實際上是共享空間，因此必須從當地居民的角度來看待旅遊目的地的審美消費。本研究擬通過將輸入（目的地美學品質）與過程（美學體驗）聯繫起來解決上述差距。鑑於遊客的審美體驗具有主觀性，本研究還將探討遊客和居民在經歷審美體驗之異同。本研究將調查香港的審美經驗，原因是香港它作為受人歡迎的旅遊目的地擁有大量（自然及都市）旅遊景點，因此特別適合開展研究。 本研究具有跨學科性，並且受到藝術哲學、普通心理學及環境心理學、建築學和城市設計領域的影響，採用混合研究方法。第一階段為描述性的現象學研究，旨在描述遊客對美、震撼和風景如畫的體驗。第二階段為探索性橫斷面定量研究，旨在根據實證將目的地屬性與審美經驗聯繫起來。本研究將探討遊客和居民數據的差異。從長遠來看，研究者將提出有關如何設計和維護居民及遊客都感到美觀的目的地景點之見解，有助於旅遊部門在發展的同時平衡當地社區之利益。

25602218.label: Project Objectives
25602218.value: To evaluate the degree to which extant texts display inclusionary and / or exclusionary discourse with the aim of ascertaining what kinds of barriers to social inclusion exist ‘out there’ in society; To identify disabled participants’ attitudes toward extant texts; their definitions and experiences of social inclusion (or the lack thereof), their views about what factors help, or hinder, social inclusion; and their assessments of how inclusionary-exclusionary experiences impact upon other aspects of life; To produce knowledge about inclusionary-exclusionary experiences through interaction between disabled participants and to add, check and counter themes identified in the second phase of this project; To develop, through a Community of Practice, definitions, and thick descriptions, of social inclusion (what it is and what it is not, how such definitions might be operationalized) so as to be able to elucidate upon how disabled people might better be able to derive experiences of social inclusion; To facilitate disabled persons’ attitudes, experiences, and definitions of social inclusion to ‘speak back’ to those extant texts (explored in the first phase of this project) already circulating within society; and To communicate the findings generated by this project to a local, and global, audience of persons, not only scholars and policy-makers but also disabled and ‘abled’ persons. In so doing, I hope to contribute to international debates about issues relating to disability (and especially inclusionary-exclusionary practices) and present the practical (and theoretical) implications of this research to persons working in such areas as social work, social policy and public policy in a local Hong Kong context.

25602218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25602218.value: This qualitative research will generate in-depth and holistic understandings of the lives of disabled persons in Hong Kong, focusing upon their experiences of social inclusion/exclusion. Such a holistic approach is necessary since a primary contention of this research is that social inclusion/exclusion neither results merely from factors inside persons, or subjects. Nor does it arise solely because of the world, or the structures, discourses and environments outside persons. Instead, social inclusion/exclusion arises at the intersections between subjects and the world as factors inside persons not only enmesh with those outside but also interweave with each other as outside penetrates inside and vice-versa as, for example, dis/ableist discourses are internalized; impairments constructed discursively, and so on. This project will, accordingly, not only explore external environments, paying attention to the structures, places, texts and persons and the exclusionary-inclusionary ideology and discourse therein but also how these become interwoven into the everyday lives of disabled persons. Although this project is exploratory, such focus will likely yield complicated, contingent accounts of social inclusion/exclusion. Nevertheless, this project intends to access, or map, the multifarious entanglements, or intersections, between inside and outside, and subjects and the world through, or as they become manifest in, first-hand experiences. Such focus upon subjective experience is necessary not only as an end in itself, namely to generate understandings of profound variations in the nature and degree of impairments and their impacts upon quotidian life but also to make visible a whole morass of cultural, social, economic, and discursive processes which would otherwise remain invisible. Put simply, larger processes can be traced through persons’ lived experiences, and the personal is political. Such mapping of the knot of factors conspiring to produce, maintain and consolidate social inclusion/exclusion is also important since this largely exploratory project nevertheless begins with a sense of a problem. This unease relates to a profound disconnect between, as well as contradictions within, official discourses regarding the social inclusion of disabled persons and preliminary observations of the decidedly more exclusionary (or asylum-like) real world to which such discourse refers. Consequently, social theory will be deployed to inform extant data and data generated with research participants to not only complicate but also create alternatives to dominant discourses about inclusionary society and, more generally, to explore the interstices between social inclusion/exclusion, subjects and the world, through in-depth contemplation of the experiences, and everyday lives, of disabled persons in Hong Kong. 基於質化研究方法，本研究通過關注香港殘障人士的社會包容/排斥經歷，以深刻和全面地瞭解他們的生活。這種整體法很有必要，因為本研究的主要論點是，社會包容/排斥不僅來自個體或主體內部因素，也不僅源於外部世界或個體之外的結構、話語和環境，而是產生於主體與外部世界間的互動。個體內部因素不僅與外部因素融為一體，而且隨著外部因素滲入內部相互交織；反之亦然。例如，殘障/健全話語被內化；通過話語建構殘障本身等等。 因此，本研究不僅探討外部環境，關注結構、地點、文本、個體，以及排他-包容的意識形態及內部話語，同時還關注這些因素與殘障人士日常生活的相互作用。雖然本研究為探索性研究，其研究焦點或許會為社會包容/排斥提供複雜及可能的解釋。本研究旨在通過所體現的一手經驗，認識及描述內部與外部、主體與外部世界之間紛繁複雜的交織與互動。關注主體經歷不僅是研究目的本身，即認識和瞭解殘障本身的性質與程度及其對日常生活的影響，同時也能揭示文化、社會、經濟與話語過程。簡而言之，宏觀過程可以通過追溯個人的生活經歷而得知，而個人的經歷均是政治性的。 由於該探索性研究源自於問題意識，描述產生、維持以及鞏固社會包容/排斥的各因素間的相互作用尤其重要。這種問題意識源自官方話語對殘障人士社會包容與現實中初步觀察到的現狀的嚴重脫節和衝突：現實社會中的話語明顯對殘障人士更為排斥（或類似於庇護）。因此，本研究將基於一手與現存資料，通過社會學理論將關於包容性社會的主導話語複雜化，同時構建一套替代性話語。與此同時，本研究還將通過對香港殘障人士的經歷與日常生活的深度反思，探討社會包容/排斥，主體與外部世界間的脫節。

25602218.label: Realisation of objectives
25602218.value: For objectives 1-5, all aspects were addressed. Objective 1 was realised through textual analysis and particularly my interpretation of critical discourse analysis. This resulted in a publication of an article on a specific filmic text (2021, Journal of Literary and Cultural Disability Studies) and a currently under review manuscript (for Disability and Society), with the latter exploring constructions of disability in virtual spaces. For objective 2, group interviews were conducted with five sets of participants attending interviews in three phases, so as to explore issues and build rapport between sessions. Group interviews were also used to realise objective 3 and 4. The outcomes of these objectives are also currently under review in an additional article submitted to Disability and Society. With regard to a community of practice, we have established WhatsApp groups and these are comprised of participants in my project and these are regularly used for sharing of information and expereinces. I believe this is a satisying outcome. For objective 5, I instigated a contrived conversation between "disabled" and "abled" people, asking them to provide commentary on not only extant texts but also, and especially, the way disability is produced in and through the social encounter. The results of these conversations are published in my published article in the Tizard Learning Disability Review and in a manuscript submitted to Disability Studies Quarterly. For objective 6, I attended a conference in 2019 (before Covid) and have widely published findings to audeinces with a global audience.

25602218.label: Major findings and research outcome
25602218.value: Disabled persons in Hong Kong and their family members, or intimate others, expereince a frightening amount of discrimination, on a day-to-day basis. These experiences jar with--and contradict--many of the somewhat celebratory discourses produced by government about social inclusion in Hong Kong. This project reminds us much needs to be done: social inclusion is far from a fully realised fact. Disabled persons and their family members experience feelings of community amongst people privy to the intimate details of impairment butlargely feel misunderstood by wider society. They crave opportunities to communicate, believing social inclusion can only be achieved through processes of sharing--or conscientization. Despite existing in very discriminatory milieu, disabled persons and their families find ways of navigating exclusionary environments.

25602218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25602218.value: This research must continue. There is much work to be done if socially inclusive and inclusionary environments are to be co-produced and one potential avenue to these ends is through dialogue and converstaion and this, to me, is one way to try to intervene in disabling contexts, i.e., by contriving dialogue, in as many ways as possible and by deconstructing the ostensibly robust and hierarchically arranged categories of ability/disability.

25602218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25602218.value: This research has provided a spotlight on the profound and vast day to day exclusions and discriminations faced by disabled persons and their families in Hong Kong. Disturbingly, these barriers exist in a multitude of places, even ones which might seem to be inclusive. Disabled persons and their families find ways of coping with and in such environments but it is vital that much more work is done--even through conversation and dialogue--before social inclusion can be anything than just an empty claim.

25605418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25605418.value: It is estimated that in Hong Kong, three in every 10 adolescents have experienced anxiety disorder symptoms (Mak et al., 2014) and one in every 10 is diagnosed with anxiety disorders (Lam et al., 2015). Too much anxiety is not only associated with poorer school adjustment and achievement but also related to comorbidity of other mental health issues and higher suicidal risk. Given its tremendous impact, a number of school-based programmes have been used for intervention and prevention. These programs usually include the components of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), which focuses on changing dysfunctional or distorted thoughts, and coping, which involves helping children to acquire new skills for coping with anxiety. However, whether or not students believe that their own thoughts and skills can change (beliefs of change, also refers to Implicit Theories, Dweck, 2006, 2013) may be a prerequisite for adjusting anxiety level. Beliefs of change may reduce or escalate anxiety level and influence the effectiveness of the intervention. Despite the growing literature on beliefs of change, a longitudinal study on the trajectory interplay between beliefs of change and anxiety level has yet to be conducted. In addition, because student anxiety may emerge at different times in an academic year, detecting anxiety level in time will be useful for designing timely prevention and intervention programs. The goal of this study is to examine the interplay between beliefs of change and anxiety among secondary school students at three critical timepoints in an academic year. The new arrival to school, after the mid-term test and before the end-of-term exam are more likely for emerging higher anxiety. It will also examine the potentially different impacts of beliefs of change in both psychological attributes and psychological distress. This study will be the first to examine the reciprocal relationship between beliefs of change and anxiety, leading to new methods for reducing anxiety and improving current interventions. It will also provide specific information for a timely intervention. Data will be collected in Hong Kong classroom surveys from Grade 7 and 8 students (N = 860) selected via quota sampling. Reliable and validated instruments will be used to collect data. These will include measures of social demographic (age, gender, SES), anxiety symptoms (general anxiety disorder and state-trait anxiety), beliefs of change (in attributes and distress), and other covariate factors (parental and peer influences, school, and media influences). Data will be analysed with cross-lagged regression modelling. 焦慮是最為普遍的青少年精神健康問題。在香港，每10名青少年就有3名有焦慮症狀，其中一名更是達到焦慮症診斷程度。過度焦慮不僅影響學校適應行為和成績，而且往往與其他心理健康問題，甚至自殺風險密切相關。本研究探討內隱理論與焦慮的交互影響。內隱理論由心理學家Dweck 提出，也稱為心態。它指個體認為自己的特質和能力是否可以改變；認為自己可以改變的信念稱為成長心態，認為自己不可以改變的信念成為定型心態。儘管已有不少關於內隱理論的文獻，但尚缺乏對內隱理論和焦慮之間的相互作用軌跡進行縱向研究。本研究假設，成長心態會降低焦慮而定性心態會增加焦慮水準；同時，焦慮會增加形成定型心態，減低形成成長心態的可能性。驗證這些假設，可以從成長角度，瞭解學生的內隱理論形成的影響因素，也可以為調節和干預焦慮問題提出新的方法。另外，由於學生焦慮程度可能在一學年的不同時間內變化，檢測焦慮程度變化對於設計及時的預防和干預計劃是幫助的。我們的研究通過配額抽樣在860名香港中一和中二學生中收集資料，探討他們在新學年開始，在中期考試之後和期末考試之前的三個時間點的焦慮水準以及內隱理論。我們將使用驗證了信效度的問卷收集數據，包括社會人口統計（年齡，性別，家庭社會經濟地位），焦慮症狀（一般焦慮症和狀態 - 特質焦慮），內隱理論以及其他協變因素（父母和同伴的影響、學校和媒體的影響）。通過分析縱向研究資料，我們建立模型以分析內隱理論與焦慮水準的交互影響。

25605418.label: Realisation of objectives
25605418.value: 1) Execution of the project to achieve the Research Objectives: 1.1)This research project started in January 2019. The PI carried out the study as planned to achieve the research objectives. First, the PI sent invitations to secondary schools in three main areas in Hong Kong, including Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, and New Territory and successfully recruited 12 schools with at least one school in each of three medium-of-instructions (English, Chinese, and both) in each of the three areas. Data collection started at September and October, the start of an academic year as planned. In Wave 1, 1721 participants from Grades 7 and 8 with parental consent participated the study. The questionnaire battery included general anxiety disorder symptoms (GAD7) and state-trait anxiety, depressive symptoms (PHQ9), Mindset of Depression, Anxiety, and Stress (MDASS), school climate, parental and peer influence, social demographic (age, gender, SES), other covariate factors (e.g., self-control, self-efficacy, and life-satisfaction). The questionnaire lasted between 20 to 25 minutes. It was a classroom survey administered by one or two university student helpers recruited and trained by the PI for the project to provide standardised instruction and support for participants. Despite the influence of the social unrest in 2019 in Hong Kong, the PI used rigorous survey methods and representative sampling methods to carry out the study as planned, which laid the scientific foundation for achieving the research objectives. 1.2) Wave 2 survey was planned in January and February when students know the mid-term examination results. The research team collected Wave 2 data in classrooms in two schools in early and mid-January as planned. However, the Covid-19 Pandemic outbroke in Hong Kong in late January. We had to stop data collection due to the school closures. Although we transferred to online survey mode in March to collect Wave 2 data, the Wave 2 survey was severely interfered with by the school closure. First, school schedules varied, and some schools did not release the mid-term exam results to the students. More importantly, students and teachers were busy adapting to the online teaching mode and did not respond to the online survey request. Only 566 participants responded to the Wave 2 online survey, and the response rate was only 21%. 1.3) We successfully collected Wave 3 data (N=1735) in June as planned after overcoming enormous difficulties. Due to the challenges of the pandemic to the school management and the narrow timeframe of school reopening in June, one school withdrew from the study. Having tried very hard to consolidate the collaborations with schools, eleven schools continued their participation during the difficult school management time. The PI (Zhu) and research assistant (Zhuang) trained student helpers, and the team conducted the school-based survey in June 2020, which made this study one of the rare school-based classroom survey research with longitudinal data collected pre-pandemic and during the pandemic. The matched Wave 1 and Wave 3 data have more than 1,393 participants, which is sufficient to achieve the research objectives. We found that the anxiety level increased while the depression level dropped at the end of the school year. However, anxiety may be caused by other factors, such as worry about the pandemic. Thus, this finding may not apply to a general academic year (Objective 1). The hypothesised reciprocal association between implicit theories and mental health was not supported by the cross-lagged model with Wave 1 and Wave 3 data (Objective 2). We found implicit theories of negative emotion were a significant predictor to mental health symptoms, such as anxiety, depression and suicidality (Objective 3). Findings are disseminated in journal papers listed in Part C. 2) Challenges and attempts to overcome: 2.1) Overall, the social unrest in Hong Kong in 2019 and the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021 caused unpredictable difficulties and severe interruption to the research project, especially the multiple school closures due to the COVID-19 pandemic since January 2020. Data collection in Wave 2 planned in February was seriously interrupted by the four-month school closure during the first wave of COVID-19. The PI led the team and successfully collected Wave 1 and Wave 3 data at the planned time points after overcoming many difficulties in school collaboration, student helper recruitment, and data collection. The Wave 1 and Wave 3 longitudinal data in one academic year with a relatively large representative sample have enabled the research team to examine research questions and disseminate the findings in top-tier journals. 2.2) Doing school-based surveys three times within one school year also created a few challenges for recruiting schools for the study. To attract school participation, the PI provided school-based reports to each school when the study ended. We contacted more than twenty schools and finally, 12 schools agreed to participate the study. Most schools found our study helps to promote student mental health during challenging school reopening and agreed to continue supporting the study. 2.3) Schools have different timetables for mid-term examinations, and it wasn't easy to decide a commonly suitable time for all schools to collect data after knowing the examination results. School effects should be taken into consideration for further analysis. 3) Beyond Achieving the Objectives: An extended wave of the school-based survey was conducted in June 2021, one academic year after the wave 3 data collection. This extended wave will help examine the association between implicit theory and mental health in an extended timeframe and scope.

25605418.label: Major findings and research outcome
25605418.value: Since January 2019, I have been focusing on uncovering the association between implicit theories and mental health outcomes and have completed a series of papers for journal publications. First, the first paper investigates the domain specificity and generality of implicit theory, published in Frontiers in Psychology in 2020. The findings suggested that identifying the most relevant domain of implicit theories may help better address the mechanism of mental health concerns. Based on the extant literature, I assumed that the implicit theories of negative emotional states are more relevant to depression, anxiety and stress. Then, I developed and validated the measure of Mindsets of Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (MDASS) and published the findings in the second paper in the Early Intervention in Psychiatry in 2021. The MDASS scale is used to examine the reciprocal association between implicit theories and mental health, including anxiety and depression. However, the data did not support the cross-lagged model of the hypothesis. The findings were reported in the Biennial Meeting of the Society for Research in Child Development in 2021. I further examined the cross-sectional and longitudinal association between the implicit theories of depression, anxiety and stress and mental health symptoms. The fourth paper, published in Journal of Affective Disorders in 2021, reported the association between implicit theories and the change in suicidal ideation over one academic year before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. This paper highlighted that fixed mindsets of negative emotions are a risk factor which predicts higher suicidality after nine months. Moreover, I further examined the role of implicit theories on suicidality among adolescents and published the fifth paper in Suicide and Life-Threatening Behaviour in 2022. This paper reports the findings that the fixed mindset of negative emotions mediates the association between depressive symptoms and suicidality. The mediation model was supported in both the cross-sectional and the longitudinal data over nine months. With the support of participating schools and the concerted effort of the research team, we managed to collect school-based data in classrooms during the brief school reopening after months of school closure due to the pandemic. Therefore, I also examined problem gaming behaviours and lifestyle changes during the pandemic among students. The findings were published in paper 6 and paper 7. These research findings have a practical impact on school management and promote better student support during the pandemic, and foster further research studies on intervention planning for problem behaviours caused by school closure and the pandemic. Recently, the impact of implicit theory on mental health is not confined to adolescents. With the data collected in the extended wave, I compared children and adolescents and found that growth mindset is a common protective factor for suicidality among children and youth. The manuscript reporting the findings is now under review by Psychiatry Research (revised with major revision). More research findings are coming out with ongoing data analyses and will be submitted for publication.

25605418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25605418.value: This project has great potential for further development. The PI has been moving forward in two promising directions. First, the PI is expanding the survey scope and examining the association of mindsets of depression, anxiety and stress on other mental health outcomes. Second, the PI is applying the findings of the current project to develop interventions for mental health prevention and early intervention. Two intervention projects supported by University Grants Committee are in progress and aim to promote belief-in-change of negative emotions to reduce internalising symptoms, including depression and anxiety. These further development of the research will further expand the scope and enhance the social impact of the research.

25605418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25605418.value: The proposed study will extend existing knowledge on implicit theory and mental health by providing empirical evidence of the longitudinal relations between the association of the notion of malleable negative emotion and mental health symptoms. Holding the belief-in-change of negative emotion is associated with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms concurrently and after nine months. The hypothesised reciprocal association between implicit theories and anxiety or depression was not supported in the current project as mental health symptoms did not predict belief-in-change of negative emotions. Further analysis found that fixed mindsets served as a mediator between depressive symptoms and suicidality and that belief-in-change of negative emotion is a protective factor against mental health problems, suicidal ideation, and suicidal attempt. These findings can be used in interventions to promote the efficacy and effectiveness of mental health promotion programmes. To thoroughly examine the effectiveness of intervention using belief-in-change of negative emotions on reducing common mental health symptoms, further research is needed, especially the randomised controlled trial research design.

25610118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25610118.value: 融合手机大数据及社会经济属性数据：一种面向混合物理/虚拟空间的社会分异动态度量方法

25610118.label: Project Objectives
25610118.value: Develop a data fusion approach to integrate information from mobile phone and urban socioeconomic datasets with high spatial granularities (e.g., income data, residential property price). The purpose of this step is to estimate individual phone users’ socioeconomic status and quantifies the uncertainty of these estimations. Quantify phone users’ interactions in physical and virtual space to support segregation measurement. To this end, a set of methods will be developed to: (1) quantify the potential interactions of phone users in physical space based on their movement patterns extracted from mobile phone data; (2) establish city-scale social networks that summarize the communication patterns among individual phone users in virtual space. Develop a set of indices to measure dynamic social segregation in cities in a hybrid physical-virtual space. Specifically, this step will use information extracted from objectives 1 and 2 to quantify: (1) the uneven distribution of socioeconomic classes in physical space; (2) the socioeconomic imbalances in human communications in virtual space (observed from mobile phone communications); (3) the segregation patterns of various places in cities as well as their evolutions over time. For this project, the principal investigator has obtained access to mobile phone data and socioeconomic datasets collected from cities including Singapore, Paris, Lyon, and Marseilles. These datasets will be used to assess the feasibility of the proposed approaches.
