25610118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25610118.value: Accelerated global urbanization has endowed cities with unprecedented amounts of wealth and people. Such agglomerations are beneficial to the well-being of societies, but raise issues such as income inequality and social stratification. The presence of “homophily” as human nature (i.e., the tendency of people to connect with similar others) and the physical separation of different population groups in cities have led to varying degrees of urban social segregation. These socioeconomic imbalances in human interactions are associated with crime, unemployment, deterioration of human health, and other issues. Although important to the health of cities, our knowledge of how effectively cities bring together people across different socioeconomic classes is limited. This is partially due to lack of multimodal data that could reveal interactions and socioeconomic status of the same populations. Existing research has primarily focused on investigating segregation at places of residence, which provides a static view of the uneven distribution of social groups in physical space. How human movements and their day-to-day communications affect social integration have largely been ignored. Recent technological advancements have produced many data sources that capture human movements and social interactions simultaneously. Mobile phone data, for example, has been widely used to understand different aspects of population dynamics. However, its potential in revealing urban social segregations remains underexplored, partly because of the absence of socioeconomic characteristics in the data. If coupled with other high-resolution datasets that reflect the socioeconomic characteristics of the underlying populations, the rich information embedded in mobile phone data can be fully utilized to depict a dynamic and multi-dimensional view of urban social segregation. This project aims to introduce a new method, through the integration of mobile phone and socioeconomic datasets, to measure social segregation in cities. By coupling information of human movements, social interactions (e.g., phone communication activities), and socioeconomic characteristics, the project aims to quantify segregation from three dimensions — spatial, temporal, and communication. The innovation of the proposed approach lies in its abilities to: (1) measure segregation level of different socioeconomic classes in physical space; (2) quantify socioeconomic imbalances in human communications in “virtual” space (3) monitor segregation patterns of various places in cities and their evolutions over time. The project will enable an efficient way of measuring dynamic social segregation at population scales. The findings will benefit many cities around the world including Hong Kong where timely and informed decisions on urban development are needed to maintain social cohesion and integration. 加速的全球城市化为城市带来了前所未有的财富和人口。这种聚集有利于社会的福祉，却引发了收入不平等和社会分层等诸多问题。社会人群的“同质性”以及不同人群在物理空间的隔离导致了不同程度的社会分异。这些社会经济活动的不平衡与犯罪，失业，人类健康恶化等问题具有紧密的联系。然而，我们对城市如何有效地融合不同社会阶层有着局限的认知。部分的原因是由于缺乏可以揭示相同人群社会经济状况和交互特征的多模数据。现有的研究主要侧重于分析居住分异问题，从而对物理空间中的社会分异形态提供了一个静态视角。而人类的出行以及日常的社交活动如何影响社会融合在很大程度上被忽视。最近的技术进步产生了许多能够同时捕捉人类活动和社会交互的数据来源。例如，手机数据已被广泛用于理解和分析社会人群的动态。然而，其揭示社会分异的潜力仍未得到充分发掘。部分原因是手机数据中缺乏反映人群社会经济特征的信息。如果能将手机数据与能够反映人群社会经济属性的高分辨率数据结合，那么这些融合之后的信息将能够从多维和动态的视角上反映城市的社会分异形态。该项目旨在通过融合手机大数据和社会经济数据，引入一种新的方法来量化城市的社会分异。具体的说，项目将通过耦合人类出行活动、社会交互（例如电话通讯行为）和社会经济属性信息，从物理空间、社交空间和时间三个维度来量化社会分异。该项目的创新之处在于：（1）量化不同社会阶层在物理空间的分异特征；（2）量化社交空间的分异形态，以及（3）有效地度量城市中不同地点和区域的社会分异程度以及时间变化规律。该项目将提供一种有效的衡量动态社会分异的方法。研究结果将使包括香港在内的世界许多城市受益，为城市的可持续发展和社会融合提供及时有效的决策支持。

25610118.label: Realisation of objectives
25610118.value: The grand mission of this project is to develop a new computational framework to enable fine-grained and quantitative measurements of urban social segregation in both physical and virtual spaces. The project has proposed three objectives, with the purposes to estimate the socioeconomic status of mobile phone users (objective 1), to quantify the interactions of phone users in physical and virtual spaces (objective 2), and to develop a set of indices to measure dynamic urban social segregation in a hybrid physical-virtual space (objective 3). 1. Realization of objective 1 Objective 1 aims to develop a data fusion approach to estimate individual phone users’ socioeconomic status (SES) and quantify the uncertainty of these estimations. To achieve this, the project proposed a home detection algorithm to infer each mobile phone user’s residence from call detail records (CDRs), a typical type of mobile phone data. In the dataset we use, all events are associated with a cell tower which a phone was connected to when an event (e.g., call phone call of text message) occurred. We use a Voronoi polygon as an approximation of a cell tower service area. The approach first divides a city into 500-meter grid. To estimate a user’s home location, for each grid cell we count the number of nights when at least one event occurred at this cell between 7pm and 9am. We count an event as occurring at a cell whenever it occurs at the base tower whose Voronoi polygon intersects with this cell. A cell with the events on the highest number of nights is assigned as home location. Two types of socioeconomic datasets, residential property price and Household Interview Travel Survey (HITS), were further used to estimate phone users’ SES. For every cell where we have at least one record of apartment/house purchase and for every user whose home location was assigned to this cell, we assign a user to the housing price drawn at random from the uniform distribution over the linear interpolation of the prices. This price is used as an approximation of individuals’ SES. To assess the feasibility of using housing price to infer individual SES, in the case study of Singapore, we perform a correlation analysis by relating housing price and income data from HITS. We extracted all the individuals from the HITS data who reported their monthly income, and then aggregated individuals based on the postal code of their reported residencies and calculated the average monthly income at each planning area. We find that the average monthly income matches well with the mean housing price (Pearson’s r = 0.88). The analysis suggests that it is reasonable to use housing prices to approximate the SES of the underlying populations. Since a phone user’s home location can be associated with multiple housing price values in the SES assignment model, to verify the robustness of our method, we repeated this assignment for 100 times, and every time the estimated SES were used to compute the segregation indices. The robustness checking suggests that the segregation metrics remain relatively consistent over 100 assignments. This suggests the robustness of the SES estimation and the reliability of the segregation metrics. 2. Realization of objective 2 Objective 2 aims to quantify phone users’ interactions in physical and virtual space to support segregation measurement. To quantify phone users’ interactions in physical space, this project develops an approach to estimate the co-location probability among phone users as they move around in a city. To accomplish this, we perform a high-resolution probability estimation separately on general weekdays and weekends. For each type of day, we divide the day into 24 one-hour time windows. For each time window, we estimate, for each individual x, the probability of staying at different urban locations. From these estimations, we further measure the “co-location” probability for all individual pairs in the city, The derived co-location probabilities were used as the weights when the subsequent segregation index (i.e., physical segregation index) was computed. To quantify phone users’ interactions in virtual space, we compute the total number of phone calls & text messages exchanged between any pair of phone users during the study period. The number is used as the weight when the subsequent segregation index (i.e., communication segregation index) was computed. Phone user pairs with higher co-location probabilities will have a higher impact on each other when the communication segregation index is computed. By realizing this objective, the project successfully quantified the degree of interactions for any pair of phone users in a city in both physical and virtual spaces, which were used as key input to compute the subsequent segregation indices. 3. Realization of objective 3 The objective 3 used information extracted from objective 1 and 2 to develop a set of indices to measure social segregation in a hybrid physical-virtual space. The project has developed three novel indices, namely, the communication segregation index (CSI), the physical segregation index (PSI), the place-based PSI, to quantify segregation from different perspectives. Before computing these indices, the project first developed a novel methodology to quantify the social similarity of any phone user pairs given their estimated SES (and the associated social ranks). The index ranges between 0 and 1, and a larger value indicates a higher social similarity between the phone user pairs. Building on the defined social similarity function, the project proposed a communication segregation index (CSI) to quantify the segregation level of individuals in the virtual space. The CSI of an individual x is defined as the weighted sum of social similarity between x and his/her contacts with weights being their communication strength (i.e., total number of calls/text messages exchanged). The value of CSI ranges from 0 to 1. A CSI close to 1 indicates that the individual mainly communicates with similar others, while a value close to 0 means that the person mainly interacts with very different others. If an individual communicates equally with any other person in the social network, his/her CSI would be equal to 0.5. Then, the project proposed a physical segregation index (PSI) to measure individual segregation in physical space. Compared to CSI, the PSI replaces the communication strength in the equation by the “co-location” probability (that measures interactions in physical space). Similar to CSI, PSI was calculated for each phone user. The value of PSI ranges from 0 to 1, with larger values indicating more exposure to similar others. Finally, the project proposed a place-based index to quantify the unique characteristics of various urban locations and their evolution over time. By aggregating PSI values of all users x for each place L, the project computed the place-based PSI to quantify the average level of exposure that phone users experienced at the location L during each one-hour time window. This index enables a new way to look at the changing landscape of physical segregation and its variation over time. The feasibility of all the metrics have been demonstrated and validated using real-world datasets (e.g., mobile phone and socioeconomic datasets in Singapore). In sum, all three objectives have been achieved. The project has produced several important publications that demonstrated the usefulness of these methods/metrics. The computational framework has already been used in other research to study social segregation. The major research findings, output, and academic and social impacts will be further reported in section 6.1.

25610118.label: Major findings and research outcome
25610118.value: This project demonstrated the great value of using mobile phone and socioeconomic datasets for studying social segregation. In 2019, invited by BBVA, a famous Spanish financial services company, Dr. Xu (PI) wrote a vision paper, calling for establishing individual-level and fine-grained measurements of social segregation: Xu, Y. and Ratti, C., 2019. Conquer the Divided Cities. Towards a New Enlightenment? A Transcendent Decade. (https://www.bbvaopenmind.com/en/articles/conquer-the-divided-cities) To prove the feasibility of the ideas, the project developed a novel computational framework that transcends traditional segregation metrics. The framework can be used to quantify social exposure of individuals in both physical and social-network spaces, and also provide aggregate measurements at scale of places and their evolution over time: Xu, Y., et al. 2019. Quantifying segregation in an integrated urban physical-social space. Journal of the Royal Society Interface, 16(160), p.20190536. Based on a case study of Singapore, the research discovered a higher level of segregation among relatively wealthier classes. The study also revealed the spatial heterogeneity of social segregation, time-varying roles of places, and correlation of individual segregation in physical and social-network spaces. By collaborating with MIT Senseable City Lab, the research was transformed into a big-data-visualization (https://senseable.mit.edu/singapore-calling), and received the FastCompany 2020 Innovation-by-Design-Awards (https://www.fastcompany.com/90547935/data-design-innovation-by-design-2020). Later, the PI proposed a novel concept of “homophily distance” to quantify the joint impact of distance decay and people’s socioeconomic characteristics on their communication patterns. The study found that after controlling distance, similar places tend to have relatively higher communication intensity than dissimilar ones, confirming a significant homophily effect as a determinant of communication intensity. This marks another important research outcome that revealed the interplay between physical and social-network segregation: Xu, Y., et al. 2022. Beyond distance decay: Discover homophily in spatially embedded social networks. Annals of the American Association of Geographers, 112(2), pp.505-521. The project outcome has received notable attention. The PI was invited by a research team in Texas A&M to apply the developed methodology to quantify changes of segregation in major US metropolitan statistical areas during Covid-19: Li, X., Huang, X., Li, D. and Xu, Y., 2022. Aggravated social segregation during the COVID-19 pandemic: Evidence from crowdsourced mobility data in twelve most populated US metropolitan areas. Sustainable Cities and Society, 81, p.103869. This project has also supported the PI to develop algorithms for preprocessing mobile phone data (Xu et al., 2020) and examine people’s use of public open space (Jan et al., 2021). The aforementioned research publications derived from this project are summarized in Part C.

25610118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25610118.value: As described in section 6.1, the computational framework developed in this research has already been used by other researchers to study the dynamics of social segregation. Therefore, it’s worthwhile to further promote this framework and apply it in different urban and research contexts, for example, to examine degree of social segregation in different types of cities, before and after public health crisis/disasters, and even study its long-term evolution. Second, as the metrics developed in this project can reveal the exposure that individuals experienced at different places and their evolution of time, an intriguing question is what types of places tend to bring together people with similar or very different socioeconomic characteristics. Therefore, further incorporating urban functions and built environment data may further reveal the impact of physical environments on segregation patterns. Third, since the method developed in this project could portray, at the individual level, the social exposure in physical and social-network space, an important topic is to relate these segregation metrics with individual well-being indicators (e.g., physical and mental health) to reveal their potential linkage. The PI considers the above as possible directions for future research and will actively seek research collaborations and develop new projects as a continuum of this research.

25610118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25610118.value: This project developed a computational framework to quantify segregation in an integrated urban physical-virtual space. By demonstrating the value of the developed metrics and empirical findings, the project delivered a powerful message, that segregation needs to be tracked more dynamically: across the urban environment and not just at home; through time and not just space; and by monitoring its presence in virtual space and not just physical space. With this computational framework, urban planners, social scientists, and city authorities could leverage large-scale and fine-grained mobility datasets (e.g., mobile phone data) to assess degree of social separation at individual level, to compare segregation patterns across urban spaces, and to monitor segregation in virtual and online spaces. The methodologies can be applied in any city when compatible datasets are available. The project finding on “homophily distance” revealed an important linkage between physical and social-network segregation. Namely, simply increasing social mixing in residential spaces (i.e., to reduce residential segregation) is not enough per se to achieve a high degree of social mixing in social-network spaces. A possible strategy to further reduce social segregation is to complement “place-based” practices with “activity-based” practices, where people from different social classes are actively engaged in social bonding activities.

26203218.value: 針對網絡流量分析攻擊的防禦措施

26203218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26203218.value: People want privacy on the Internet, but privacy remains an elusive pursuit, even with encryption and proxy services like Tor and VPNs. This is because malicious eavesdroppers, who can see traffic information such as the number of packets, their sizes, their timing and their ordering, can process such information using privacy-intrusive traffic analysis attacks to identify what a web user is doing on the Internet, thus compromising the user's privacy. Though these attacks have been known as a threat for more than 20 years, no practical defense has been implemented against them. We identify three main barriers that pose a challenge to a practical defense against such attacks and how they can be overcome. First, there has been a lack of understanding of how and why these traffic analysis attacks succeed. Consequently, defenses against one attack have often failed against other attacks. We propose to explore the power of such traffic analysis attacks with a precision-based methodology. Second, there has been no consistent metric to measure the success of a defense, and thus we could not know if any defense was good. We present a novel metric and show how it is intricately related to the maximum precision of any possible classifier. Third, practical limitations have inhibited the use of a defense. Many of those limitations have been lifted by ongoing implementation work by the academic community and by developers of privacy-enhancing technologies. The main goal of this project is the design, implementation, and dissemination of a practical real-world defense against these privacy-intrusive traffic analysis attacks. We propose a defense with both client-side and server-side implementations, emphasizing practical usability. On the client side, we mathematically formulate probabilistic guarantees against classification and outline them in this proposal. By combining them with half-duplex communication, we are able to create a low-cost defense with guaranteed effectiveness against real attacks. On the server side, we propose new tools to increase server resilience against these attacks. Using a novel resource tree approach, we find that random perturbations to resource size on the server side can significantly deter an attacker. We describe in detail our strategy of implementing and disseminating this work so that it may be used by individuals who need privacy on the Internet. 瀏覽互聯網的客戶平時會向中繼點的路由器宣佈自己想去的網址。這會泄漏自己的私隱，並讓第三者瞭解和收集自己的網上行爲。如果客戶想隱藏自己想去的網址，她可以用Tor或者各種的VPN。可是，研究發現，攻擊者可以用通過被動、靜態的流量分析攻擊以推導出客戶端想去的網址，從而破壞客戶的私隱。這些攻擊雖然已被證明成功有二十多年，但是防禦措施不切實際，形同虛設。 我們在這份研究提案之中，將指出已有的流量攻擊防衛措施的三個問題，並提出解決方案。其一，設計防衛措施的研究員不足夠瞭解流量分析如何和爲何成功。因此，每個防衛措施只能打敗少數的攻擊，而不能打敗所有攻擊。我們應以一個基於準確度的方式去分析流量分析攻擊，從而解釋它們的運作。其二，過去分析防禦措施並無統一的量度方式，更無法比較不同措施的優劣。我們提出一個嶄新的量度方式，而這種方式可以幫助我們推算出任何攻擊的最高準確度，以此得知防禦措施的最低效率。其三，我們將指出防衛措施的各種實際應用問題，並利用研究員和程序家最新的發現來消除這些問題。 這個研究項目的主要目的是創造一個新的、實用的防禦措施，達到保護客戶私隱的目的。我們會設計、製造、並推廣一個新的防禦措施。這個實際的防禦措施會有客戶端的服務器兩面。對於客戶端，我們會推導出對於流量攻擊達到最低保證的方式，並籍着半雙工流量的傳送而達到低負擔的目標。對於服務器，我們用新的工具加強服務器對流量分析攻擊的保護，並使用嶄新的資源樹分析來打敗流量分析攻擊。我們會詳細解釋設計、推廣的策略，讓我們的防禦措施可以得到廣泛利用，保護網民的私隱。

26208318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26208318.value: 使用高效零知识证明进行私人智能合约评估

26208318.label: Project Objectives
26208318.value: Design and implement a novel succinct NIZK scheme for private smart contracts with improved performance and without per-contract preprocessing. Develop an optimized prototype system for executing private smart contracts efficiently. Open-source said system.
rows: Design and implement a novel succinct NIZK scheme for private smart contracts with improved performance and without per-contract preprocessing.
Develop an optimized prototype system for executing private smart contracts efficiently.

26208318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26208318.value: Smart contracts are a blockchain application that allows mutually distrustful parties to execute a piece of code over their joint inputs, in a distributed and verifiable manner. Once a smart contract transaction is processed by the blockchain, it is added to a distributed ledger that provides unified, tamper-proof visibility into the transaction record; an immutable version of transaction truth that enforces the parties participating in the contract to uphold its terms. This can have profound impact on transactions for the financial sector, e.g., financial swaps and bond liquidity enforcement, without the need for third-party arbitration. One side-effect of smart contracts, which seems inherent, is the loss of privacy. For the blockchain to be able to check and enforce the contract terms, every piece of information must be published, including participants' identities, contract terms, and input records, which may be of sensitive or proprietary nature. Therein lies a major contradiction. It seems that the fields which can most benefit from smart contracts (e.g., the financial and banking sectors) have the most to lose by disclosing sensitive data. This project proposes a novel way for achieving private smart contract execution. A private smart contract can guarantee that the data placed on the blockchain as part of the smart contract execution reveal absolutely no information about the internals of the contract. To achieve this strong privacy property, we will use powerful cryptographic tools called non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZK). At a high level, NIZKs allow a party to guarantee the correct execution of a program by providing a cryptographic proof which can be then verified by anyone very efficiently (and without access to the original code). We first identify why previous approaches for private smart contracts fail to solve the problem and we propose a novel way for designing NIZKs that deviates from the literature and is specifically tailored for the problem of smart contracts. Our goal is not only to develop the necessary new cryptographic tools but also to build a prototype system that will demonstrate the practicality of our approach and will be able to execute large numbers of smart contracts in an efficient manner. Due to the necessary cryptographic operations involved, particular care will be put in optimizing its performance both at the cryptographic design and at the engineering levels. Given the increased need for privacy in blockchain applications, we expect this project to have major potential for adoption in practice. 智能合约是一种区块链应用程序，允许相互不信任的各方以分布式和可验证的方式来协同贡献并执行代码。 一旦区块链处理了一条智能合约交易，它就会被添加到分布式账本中，该账本提供对交易记录的统一和防篡改的可见性; 该账本同时也是不可改变的交易真实版本，强制参与合同的各方维护其条款。 这可能对金融部门的交易产生深远影响，例如金融互换和债券流动性执行，而无需第三方仲裁。 智能合约的一个固有的缺点是隐私的丧失。 为了使区块链能够检查和执行合同条款，每条信息都必须被公布，包括参与者的身份，合同条款和输入记录，这些记录可能具有敏感性或专有性。 这其中包含一个主要的矛盾。 通过披露敏感数据，最能从智能合约（例如金融和银行部门）中受益的领域损失最大。 该项目提出了一种实现私人智能合约执行的新方法。 私人智能合约可以保证作为智能合约执行的一部分的放置在区块链上的数据绝对不会泄露有关合同内部的信息。 为了实现这种强大的隐私性，我们将使用称为非交互式零知识证明（NIZK）的强大加密工具。 在更高层次上，NIZK允许一方通过提供加密证据来保证程序的正确执行，然后可以非常有效地被任何人验证（并且无需访问原始代码）。 我们首先确定为什么以前的私人智能合约方法无法解决问题，并提出了一种新颖的方法来设计有别于传统文献中的NIZK，以专门针对智能合约的问题来重新定制。 我们的目标不仅是开发必要的新加密工具，还要构建一个足以展示我们方法的实用性，并能够以有效的方式执行大量智能合约的原型系统。 由于涉及必要的加密操作，因此将特别注意在加密设计和工程级别优化其性能。 鉴于区块链应用程序对隐私的需求日益增加，我们预计该项目在实践中具有很大的应用潜力。

26208318.label: Realisation of objectives
26208318.value: For Objective (1), we first looked into the specific problem of transparency logs that have been proposed as a way of building accountable (and thus more secure) public key infrastructures. A transparency log is a dictionary managed by an untrusted log server or in a decentralized blockchain platform. Key-value pairs are then periodically appended to the dictionary which is queried by mutually distrusting users, who want to know certain keys’ values. All previous solutions to this problem, suffer from one of two issues: to remain secure, either their membership query resolution or their update overhead must be linear to the dictionary size. We solved this problem by proposing a new argument system that implements an append-only authenticated dictionary (AAD) primitive. An AAD maps a key to one or more values in an append-only fashion and is an abstraction for a transparency log. We are the first to give security definitions for AADs and to instantiate asymptotically efficient AADs from bilinear accumulators. At a high level, we encode the relations to be proven in terms of polynomial arithmetic and then use the bilinear group representation to succinctly prove them. Importantly, our design does not rely on collective verification by users or on trusted third parties and assumes only an untrusted log server or a decentralized blockchain protocol. It offers logarithmic-sized append-only proofs, polylogarithmic-sized lookup proofs, and polylogarithmic worst-case time appends. This line of research has led to a publication in the prestigious top-tier computer security conference ACM CCS 2019 (see C1 below). Moving on, we focused on the problem of private smart contract evaluation in the application of a decentralized data marketplace. The proliferation of Internet-connected devices with multiple functionalities and sensors, in addition to services with access to high volumes of data, has resulted in the development of data marketplaces. In a data marketplace, data owners host their data onto a service that can later sell data-related information to interested buyers. Although owners can get compensated for providing their data, privacy risks may deter them from doing so. Most data marketplaces expect owners to fully trust services by relinquishing control of their data, which functions are computed over them, and whether they are altered. Ideally, owners would like to maintain some control over the types of computations that can be performed on their data. Additionally, buyers may have security concerns of their own, e.g., they would like to be provided with a proof-of-correctness for the results they purchase. Recent proposals for privacy-aware marketplaces can offer such guarantees either by relying on trusted entities or by using secure hardware. We proposed Agora, a privacy-aware blockchain-based decentralized marketplace that achieves three key security properties: (i) Data privacy: no party can learn any information about the raw data of data generators, apart from the function output that is learned by the broker and paying consumers. (ii) Output verifiability: no data broker can successfully sell an incorrect result to a consumer. (iii) Atomicity of payments: no party can avoid paying for services, i.e., generators are always reimbursed for their data, and brokers are paid for providing function outputs. To achieve this, we combined two cryptographic techniques, lightweight NIZKs without trusted setup and functional encryption. In particular, we designed a NIZK protocol for data brokerage, where the consumer requests a specific output from the broker. To achieve atomicity of payments, we split the ZKP verification efficiently into on-chain and off-chain parts. Specifically, we offloaded the last verification step onto a smart contract which transfers the agreed funds from the consumer to the broker, only if the NIZK verifier accepts. Finally, for most applications, consumers may be interested in acquiring results from multiple time periods. If this was done by repeating our protocol for each output separately, both the cost and the delay would grow linearly with the number of outputs. In order to avoid this, we customized the NIZK used in Agora to enable batch purchases without any additional on-chain cost. This line of research has led to a short-paper publication in the prestigious top-tier decentralized systems conference IEEE ICDCS 2020 (see C2 below). Subsequently, the full version of our paper was accepted and published in the top-tier computer security journal IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing. Finally, in what we consider the main result of this project, we were able to address one of the main practical limitations of universal zk-SNARKs, i.e., the need for a trusted setup per different computation. We first explored how to enable efficient randomized checks in zk-SNARK circuits. Randomized checks can make the verification logic much faster than regular verification circuits in cases like permutation verification and others. Informally, while it is possible to ask the prover to generate randomness by committing to the witness, doing this naively would lead to having additional expensive commitment logic in the circuit. Then, utilizing this idea we looked into using this scheme for blockchain applications, evaluating in the context of privacy-preserving smart contracts to address the trusted key generation per contract issue. This has resulted in a novel protocol and full-fledged implementation called Mirage SNARK. With Mirage, a single universal verification key is hardcoded on the blockchain, and for every new computation, an untrusted computation specifier would only provide 32 bytes encoding the computation to be verified to a custom contract. Verifying our proofs on the chain is very similar to verifying "classic" zk-SNARK proofs (e.g., Groth16), e.g., it only slows down the prover by 1.4× and still keeps verification computation in the order of milliseconds. To the best of our knowledge, Mirage is still the most efficient universal zk-SNARK in terms of minimal proof size and verification. This result has been published to the top-tier conference USENIX Security 2020 (see C3 below). Regarding Objectives (2) and (3), the above works are accompanied by optimized implementations and prototype systems, and the code is open-sourced on GitHub repositories. For AAD our implementation is in C++ and the code is available at https://github.com/alinush/libaad-ccs2019. Our lookup and append-only proofs are in the order of tens of KiBs and our verification time is in the order of seconds. For example, a proof for a key with 32 values in a dictionary of 106 entries is 94 KiB and verifies in 2.5 seconds. According to our experimental evaluation, this is close to one order of magnitude better than previous solutions. We implemented Agora over Ethereum, using Solidity for developing the smart contracts and we deployed our smart contracts on the Rinkeby testnet. Finally, for Mirage our code is open-source at https://github.com/akosba/mirage together with a running prototype smart contract for secure auctions. The back-end uses the popular libsnark C library, while our front-end is written in Java.

26208318.label: Major findings and research outcome
26208318.value: This project has tried to target the problem of constructing new systems with formally-proven verifiability via two approaches: (a) develop special NIZK systems for certain applications; since these systems do not need to be universal, they can overcome the above issues by sacrificing “generality for efficiency,” and (b) propose a novel succinct NIZK argument system that is universal. The underlying context for both approaches has been the use of our cryptographic schemes in the context of decentralized/distributed systems, in particular blockchain protocols with smart contract evaluation, looking into the applications of certificate transparency, and data marketplaces. The research outcome of the above efforts can be summarized in a series of papers in top-tier compute venues (ACM CCS, USENIX Security, IEEE ICDCS, IEEE TDSC) and three implemented prototype systems: 1) Mirage is the state-of-the-art universal-setup zk-SNARK in terms of minimal proof size and verification time. Its implementation includes privacy-preserving verifiable general-purpose blockchain smart contracts, addressing the main research objective of the project (paper appeared in USENIX Security 2020, C3 below). 2) AAD is the first accumulator-based transparent log in the literature, with direct applications to key/certificate transparency (paper appeared in ACM CCS 2019, C1 below). 3) Agora is the first formally-proven secure privacy-preserving data marketplace with result verifiability (owning to efficient zero-knowledge arguments). It has been deployed on the Ethereum testnet (short paper appeared in IEEE ICDCS 2020, C2 below; full paper published at the IEEE TDSC journal).

26208318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26208318.value: The project leaves several research directions and goals for future work. While it largely addressed the main goal of eliminating the per-computation trusted setup, the bottleneck that stems from the heavy prover overhead remains. Hence, the next step is to combine zk-SNARK techniques from this project with novel ideas to reduce the prover overhead. Another direction is to explore different cryptographic techniques (such as hidden-order groups) for alternative performance trade-offs for arguments and commitments/accumulators.

26208318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26208318.value: The last few years have witnessed increasing interest in the deployment of systems with strong formal guarantees of verifiability, e.g., in the context of blockchain smart contract systems, decentralized finance, and mode. One prominent tool that has recently been considered for deployment (e.g., by the ZCash cryptocurrency, or Binance which is currently the world's leading digital asset exchange) are cryptographic proof and argument systems (NIZKs), in particular ones with zero-knowledge, succinct proofs, and efficient verification (zk-SNARKs). One of the main challenges for zk-SNARKs is the requirement of a trusted key generation phase per different computation to achieve practical proving performance. All existing systems that do not require a trusted setup or have a single trusted preprocessing phase suffer from increased proof size and/or additional verification overhead. This project has proposed novel systems with cryptographic zk-SNARKs (and one novel zk-SNARK) that overcome the above limitation. We have demonstrated the applicability of our systems for different applications, such as building secure public-key infrastructure, verifiable Ethereum smart contracts, and secure data marketplaces. Our results have been published in top-tier academic venues of computer security and our code is open-sourced and publicly available.

26213818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26213818.value: 内存内计算技术已被广泛部署于大规模分布式数据分析集群，其典型应用包括大数据分析和机器学习。使用该技术，对读写操作要求频繁的应用可以将其输入数据和中间计算结果缓存在集群内存，从而实现计算速度数量级上的提升。然而，囿于有限的内存空间和日益增长的数据规模，集群缓存通常以共享和竞争的方式分配给多种应用。基于此，一个基础性的技术难题是：如何合理而高效地决定哪些文件数据应该缓存在内存，从而实现对单个应用的性能隔离？具体而言，我们希望每个应用都能获得有保证的最小缓存分配，并对其能实现的读写性能有强预见性。与此同时，我们还要求整个集群保持高内存使用率。 然而，现有的集群缓存管理系统并不在乎单个应用的缓存表现。相反，其关注重点则是在如何优化提升总缓存命中率。为实现这一目标，这些系统使用经典的缓存淘汰算法进行缓存管理，如最近最少使用缓存置换（LRU Cache）以及最近最不常用缓存置换（LFU Cache)。于是，对于一些并不经常访问其数据对象的应用，其所需的数据将大概率被缓存淘汰，从而导致其在读写性能上严重受损。更为糟糕的是，优化总缓存命中率给其他应用操纵缓存分配带来了可趁之机：这些应用完全可以通过增加一些对数据对象不必要的访问来提升其访问频率，并最终淘汰其他应用的缓存数据，从而获得任意多的缓存分配。 为了解决这一问题，在本项目中我们将设计、分析、并开发一个以应用为中心的缓存管理框架。我们的缓存框架将为没一个单独应用提供最小缓存分配保障，从而实现可预见的性能隔离。与此同时，我们的设计也将以不牺牲总体缓存效率为目标，为集群提供近似最优的缓存命中率。我们的缓存管理框架将会为用户提供一个公用的应用编程接口（API)。通过该编程接口，用户应用可以向缓存管理框架提出注册并指定其所使用的缓存淘汰策略，如LRU、LFU甚至是用户自定义的淘汰算法。基于这些信息，我们的管理框架将会实现公平、高效的缓存共享管理，并使用单个应用所指定的缓存淘汰算法管理其在内存中的数据对象。另外，我们注意到大数据处理集群广泛使用多级缓存系统，例如使用固态硬盘（SSD）作为对内存缓存的一个次级补充。我们的缓存管理系统也将被设计成能用于管理多级缓存。 我们注意到开发这样一套缓存管理系统在理论和工程实现上都有相应的挑战。为达到高读写吞吐量，现有的数据处理集群广泛支持内存内数据共享（in-memory data sharing）模式。在这一模式下，缓存在内存中的数据对象可以被多个应用共享。然而，这一模式也给了应用以“搭便车”的方式进行缓存操控打开了方便之门。具体而言，一个应用可以“谎报”自己的内存需求，从而操控其他应用使用他们各自分配到的内存来缓存该应用所感兴趣的数据对象。该应用再以“搭便车”的方式访问这些数据对象，进而为自己节省内存开销。我们将提出一些列新颖的缓存管理方法来解决这一问题。我们将通过严格的数学推导来证明我们的算法不会给应用以“搭便车”的方式进行缓存操控的机会。我们也将证明我们的算法可以在多级缓存下实现各应用之间的性能隔离。最后，我们将在Alluxio上进行系统实现，并最终在亚马逊云平台上进行原型部署和性能测试。我们的系统将极大改善云应用的读写性能，这对于大数据处理和分布式机器学习将至关重要。

26213818.label: Realisation of objectives
26213818.value: Memory caches are being used aggressively for large-scale data analytics. Given the limited size of caches, data-intensive applications frequently contend for the main memory in a shared cloud platform. In such a multi-tenant environment, however, the problem of managing caches becomes particularly challenging. Ideally, the system should provide each application with a guaranteed minimum cache allocation for predictable performance isolation. At the same time, the system should strive to achieve optimal cache efficiency to maximize the number of requests that can be directly served from memory. Nevertheless, prevalent in-memory computing systems only focus on optimizing global cache efficiency, without any concern for performance isolation. Systems such as Spark and Alluxio employ Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Recently/Frequently Used (LRFU) algorithms to evict cached data objects. These algorithms provide no isolation but promote cheating: by making spurious data accesses, an application can easily abuse the system to cache as much data as possible for it, while evicting the others’ data out of the memory. On the other hand, simply maintaining an isolated cache for each application, though guaranteeing isolation, is highly inefficient. Data sharing among multiple applications has become commonplace in today’s production clusters. Having isolated caches leads to multiple copies of a shared file, which not only wastes the cache space, but also results in a significant drop of the system’s write performance due to frequent in-memory duplications. In this project, we have developed a new cache management framework to enforce predictable performance isolation between applications, while achieving near-optimal cache efficiency. Our cache management framework is built on top of Alluxio, a popular memory-centric distributed storage system. - Realisation of Objective-1 Unlike Alluxio that does not differentiate data accesses among different users and applications, our cache management framework provides a simple application programming interface (API) through which user applications can register and have their data access tracked by the framework. The framework consists of a centralized controller on the Alluxio master and several distributed CacheMonitors that collect cache statistics on worker nodes and report to the controller periodically. The controller has two key components: (1) an AppManager that interacts with applications through the Alluxio client, and (2) a CacheManagerMaster that implements the logic of cache management algorithms based on the cache statistics reported by CacheMonitors. Before accessing files, a user application needs to register itself with the ClientManager. In response, the ClientManager assigns it an appID to uniquely identify the application. With an appID, the application can interact with workers to read and write data, and has its data access identified and tracked by the CacheMonitor on those workers. CacheMonitor periodically communicates this information along with other cache statistics to the CacheManagerMaster. Based on those reports, CacheManagerMaster makes data eviction decisions and informs BlockMaster, which then instructs each worker to evict the corresponding data blocks. Our framework also provides applications with the flexibility of specifying their preferred eviction policies through a set of APIs. The framework currently supports classic eviction policies, including LFU, LRU, LRU-K, and ARC, and our proposed cache management policies. It also allows users to implement customized eviction policies and add them into the class. The application’s preferred eviction policies is kept by AppManager and used by CacheManagerMaster when making eviction decisions. - Realisation of Objective-2 and Objective-3 We have analyzed existing cache management policies, including recency- and frequency-based cache replacement policies, isolated caches, max-min fair allocations, and the state- of-the-art solution FairRide. Our analysis shows that these policies either result in poor cache utilization or suffer from strategic manipulations, known as a "free-riding" problem. That is, instead of using its own allocated cache to persist files it requests, a strategic application may seek to “free-ride” on others who have a strong need to cache the same dataset, and thus can save its cache space at the expense of others. We have revisited the fundamental problem of fair and efficient cache allocation in shared cloud environments, and proposed two new cache allocation algorithms. Our first algorithm provides isolation guarantee and is immune to harmful manipulations. The price paid is a slight efficiency loss. The algorithm has two stages when making the cache allocation decisions. In the first stage, it strives to share caches for high efficiency without suffering harmful manipulations. It then checks if the sharing outcome provides isolation for individual applications. If no application prefers isolation, the algorithm settles on sharing; otherwise, the attempt of sharing caches has not succeeded, and the algorithm resorts to isolated allocation in the second stage, in which each user is allocated an isolated cache of equal size. More specifically, our algorithm uses proportional fairness (PF) for cache sharing in the first stage, under which an isolation guarantee is provided while high efficiency can also be attained. A PF allocation maximizes the social welfare, but is not strategy-proof. To address this problem, we have developed a technique that frames PF allocation into the VCG mechanism (VCG-PF) assuming logarithm utility. In our design, the VCG mechanism charges each application a “tax” payment following the Clarke pivot rule, so as to ensure strategy-proofness against free-riding. Our analysis shows that in most cases, our algorithm provides isolation guarantee, thus achieving high cache utilization by avoiding reverting to the baseline isolation. Our second cache allocation algorithm considers not only the total amount of caches allocated to each application, but also the placement of its cached data. While the former determines the quantity of the allocation, i.e., how much data an application can cache in memory, the placement of cached data determines the quality of the allocation. For example, applications having input data co-located with some hot data objects in a cache server likely suffer from long latency as those objects may result in severe network congestion. Therefore, the goal of our second algorithm is to find the optimal placement for each cached data object, so as to enforce performance isolation between applications while attaining high caching efficiency. Our algorithm, called Load-Aware Cache Sharing scheme (LACS), keeps track of the load contributed by each application and jointly determines cache allocation and the file placement. To attain high efficiency, LACS shares both the cached files and the network bandwidth among applications. In case that an application contributes too much load that would compromise performance isolation, LACS quickly intervenes by throttling its cache accesses and bandwidth usage, so as to curb its negative impact on other users. LACS provides guaranteed performance isolation. We have generalized both cache allocation algorithms and our framework to multi-tiered cache storage. - Realisation of Objective-4 We have evaluated the two algorithms and our cache management framework via real cloud deployment on AWS EC2 (a cluster of 30 cache servers and 1 master node). Extensive evaluation results show that both algorithms ensure performance isolation for individual users while achieving high efficiency. Our first algorithm outperforms isolated caches by 2.45x and is 16.6% better than FairRide in terms of cache hit ratio. The performance comes close to the global optimum with a narrow gap less than 7%. In the presence of severe network congestion, our second algorithm speeds up the per-user average latency by up to 80.4% (25.3% on average) over the state-of-the-art load balancing technique. We have released our framework as open-source software in GitHub.

26213818.label: Major findings and research outcome
26213818.value: We started by studying the efficient and fair cache allocation problem in shared cloud environments, where many users and applications contend for the main memory to cache shared datasets or files. Unlike other resources such as CPUs and networks, in-memory caches can be non-exclusively shared across many users, e.g., a cached columnar dataset queried by many Spark SQL jobs. This results in a unique challenge of the “free-riding” problem, where an application lies about its caching preferences to trick other users to cache files for it, using their allocated cache space. We showed that existing cache allocation policies either suffer from such manipulations or result in poor efficiency. To address this problem, we developed a new cache management framework atop Alluxio that differentiates data accesses among different applications. Our framework provides APIs through which applications can specify their preferred cache eviction policies. We also designed two new cache allocation algorithms for efficient cache management in our framework. The first algorithm models the cache allocation problem as VCG mechanism design problem, and incorporates proportional fairness into the design. We showed that the algorithm provides performance isolation between applications and is also strategy-proof against “free-riding” manipulations. Note that an application’s caching performance depends not only on the amount of cache allocation but also the placement of its cached data. Therefore, simply providing a guaranteed amount of minimum cache space for individual applications does not translate to a performance guarantee: an application having its input co-located with some hot data objects in a cache server likely suffer from long latency as those objects may result in severe network congestion. We propose a Load-Aware Cache Sharing scheme (LACS) to enforce isolation between applications. LACS keeps track of the load contributed by each application and reins back the congestion caused by the heavy contributors by throttling their cache usage and network bandwidth. Our theoretical analysis shows that LACS provides guaranteed performance isolation. We have implemented both cache allocation algorithms as a cache manager in our framework, and evaluated their performance through real cloud deployment on AWS EC2 and trace-driven simulations. The results conclusively demonstrated the near-optimal efficiency in cache utilization, guaranteed performance isolation, and resilience to strategic manipulations. The project has led to fruitful results published in various top-tier conferences and journals (listed in the research output). The cache management framework we built in this project has also been released as open-source software (https://github.com/yhust/lacs.git, https://github.com/yhust/Alluixo-for-OpuS.git).

26213818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26213818.value: Memory cache manager is no doubt one of the most critical components in data-intensive clusters. Our focus in this project is the design of application-aware cache management for improving overall cache utilization and for achieving performance isolation between individual applications under various tradeoff such as fairness. Moving forward, there are two trends worth further investigation. The first is to leverage machine learning techniques, such as deep reinforcement learning (RL), to make more intelligent caching and placement decisions. Using the RL algorithm, the system can train an agent that automatically learns the optimal caching policy for each application based on its data access pattern. The algorithm can also be used to predict the popularity changes of the cached data objects, which allows the system to make more accurate placement decisions. We are currently investigating learning-assisted caching algorithms. The second trend is an architecture shift towards memory-disaggregated datacenters, in which the memory and compute resources are provided by the memory and compute nodes in two disaggregated resource pools, respectively. In this architecture, memory access involves network communication, making network a relevant resource for cache management. We will work with our industry partners to tailor our algorithms and framework to this new datacenter architecture.

26213818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26213818.value: Today's data analytics clusters are shifting towards in-memory computation, ranging from big data analytics to distributed machine learning. With a surging volume of data moving into the main memory, a diverse range of applications contend for limited cache spaces in a shared cloud platform. The fundamental challenge in this regard is to judiciously determine which data files to cache and which ones to evict, so that each application can expect a guaranteed minimum cache allocation for performance predictability, while the shared cloud platform can achieve highly efficient memory utilization. However, existing cache management frameworks are oblivious to the cache performance of individual applications, thus failing to provide any performance isolation. In this project, we have analyzed, designed, and developed a new cache management framework that is application-aware. Using newly developed cache management algorithms, the framework provides each application with a guaranteed minimum cache allocation for predictable performance isolation, while achieving near-optimal cache efficiency for the system as a whole. We have released our framework as open-source software. With fundamentally more efficient, predictable, and robust ways of utilizing the memory, our framework substantially improves the performance of large-scale data analytics and machine learning applications, as they routinely coexist in the public cloud.

26302118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26302118.value: 對稱性和拓撲是描述我們身邊客觀物體最深刻的概念之壹。二者都表征了物體在某種變換下的不變性：比如反射和反演這樣的對稱操作以及延展和彎曲這樣的連續變換。 長期以來，對稱性在物理學中扮演著極為重要的角色。在凝聚態物理學中，朗道在1930年左右創立了關於相變的普遍理論。人們意識到不同的相可以通過對稱性進行區分，相變過程用對稱性的破缺進行描述。和對稱性相比，拓撲的概念僅僅在1980年量子霍爾效應的發現後才被引入到凝聚態物理中用於區分物相。拓撲相的實現也非常困難，這是由於拓撲相的存在往往依賴於低溫或強磁場等極端環境。鼓舞人心的是，通過結合對稱性，2005年量子自旋霍爾絕緣體的發現迅速地擴展了拓撲相領域的研究。相應地，各種令人耳目壹新的應用在這之後被人們提出。 尋找能夠同時實現對稱性破缺和拓撲相的材料對科學價值和潛在應用都是非常重要的。在2014年，該項目負責人和其合作者預測出單層WTe2型過渡金屬硫族化合物（TMDs）可能擁有量子自旋霍爾絕緣體的拓撲相。這項工作最近被壹些獨立的研究組用包括輸運在內的各種實驗手段所證實。因此，WTe2-型TMDs已經成為壹種非常有前景的新型材料平臺的候選者。然而，現在依然存在許多遺留下來的不確定性和開放性的問題，阻礙了深入的研究和可能的應用。 這壹研究計劃的主要目的是探究所有可能在WTe2型TMD薄膜中能夠同時實現的對稱性破缺和拓撲相。我們將首先回顧各種實驗結果，結合第壹性原理計算、緊束縛近似模型、k·p方法、拓撲學分析以及平均場理論來建立壹個樣品模型用於處理這些不確定的問題。這壹模型將作為壹個穩固的基礎，從中我們可以深入地探究通過磁性摻雜或者磁性襯底在WTe2型TMD薄膜中實現量子反常霍爾態和拓撲超導的可行性。同時，不同的堆積方式會造成能否具有反演對稱性的不同晶體結構，進而引起鐵電性和鐵彈性。最後，我們能夠深入研究這些對稱性破缺和拓撲相之間的相互作用。 這壹研究會進壹步加強我們對對稱性破缺相和拓撲相以及它們相互作用的理解，同時研究它們在實際材料中地實現，從而為高效率、低功耗的量子電子器件，自旋電子器件以及容錯量子計算等應用中提供壹個合適的平臺。

26302118.label: Realisation of objectives
26302118.value: We have realized all the proposed objectives. By combing first-principles calculations with tight-binding methods and kp models and collaborating with various experimental groups, we have systematically studied the properties of monolayer and multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides with 1T’ and 1H structures including WTe2, MoTe2, WSe2, WSSe, etc. We built the complete tight-binding models and kp models that satisfy the full symmetry requirements and capture the exact features of states around the Fermi level including both topological trivial and nontrivial features and demonstrated the possible ferromagnetism and quantum Hall states, which serves a solid basis for the further theoretical and experimental studies [Physical Review B 104, 035156 (2021)]. Based on our theoretical studies, we also predicted that strain can be used to manipulate the growth and electronic properties of TMDs. All these theoretical studies have been realized in experiments through the close collaborations. We first theoretically and experimentally demonstrated that strain is a very efficient approach to control the phase transition between topological semimetallic phases, topological insulating phases, and trivial insulating phases [Physical Review Letters 125, 046801 (2020)]. We then theoretically and experimentally demonstrated that the strain can be also used to control the epitaxial growth of single-phase 1T’-WSe2 through assistance of enhanced interface interaction [Advanced Materials 33, 2004930 (2021)]. Moreover, with the solid theoretical basis and close experimental collaborations, we discovered that the ferroelectricity can indeed exist in antiparallel stacking of twisted WSe2 [National Science Open 2, 20220033 (2023)], which is very surprising since the local centro-symmetry of atomic registries at the twist interface does not favor the spontaneous electronic polarizations.

26302118.label: Major findings and research outcome
26302118.value: The major findings of this project are the clear demonstration of novel electronic properties and many novel phases in monolayer and multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides with 1T’ and 1H structures including WTe2, MoTe2, WSe2, WSSe, etc. With the support of this projects, we have been able to build the complete tight-binding models and kp models that satisfy the full symmetry requirements and capture the exact features of states around the Fermi level including both topological trivial and nontrivial features [Physical Review B 104, 035156 (2021)], which can serve a solid basis for the further theoretical and experimental studies. We theoretically and experimentally demonstrated that strain is a very efficient approach to control the phase transition between topological semimetallic phases, topological insulating phases, and trivial insulating phases [Physical Review Letters 125, 046801 (2020)] and demonstrated that the strain can be also used to control the epitaxial growth of single-phase 1T’-WSe2 through assistance of enhanced interface interaction [Advanced Materials 33, 2004930 (2021)]. Moreover, we discovered that the ferroelectricity can indeed exist in antiparallel stacking of twisted WSe2 [National Science Open 2, 20220033 (2023)], which is very surprising since the local centro-symmetry of atomic registries at the twist interface does not favor the spontaneous electronic polarizations.

26302118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26302118.value: We will continue to explore other novel properties of monolayer and multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides and search for the experimentally feasible methods to realize the dissipationless quantum transport.

26302118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26302118.value: Due topological protection of the topological nontrivial gapless edge states inside the bulk band gap, the backscattering and localization are strongly suppressed or even completely forbidden, and hence topological materials hold a great potential in next-generation low heat dissipation and power cost quantum electric devices. Up to now, hundreds of topological materials have been theoretically proposed, while only few materials systems can show the experimental evidence of quantum transport. Since the theoretical prediction in 2014 and experimental verification in 2017, monolayer WTe2-type transition metal dichalcogenides has show great promises, while the systematic studies about manipulating its structural and electronic properties have been lacking. In this work, we not only theoretically studies the novel properties of monolayer WTe2-type transition metal dichalcogenides and proposed that strain can be a very efficient approach to control their novel properties, but also experimentally demonstrated the feasibility of using strain to control the epitaxy growth of single-phase 1T’ monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides and to manipulate the phase transition between topological semimetallic phase, topological insulating phase and normal insulating phase. Our series of work has lay a solid foundation for the further theoretical and experimental study and potential application of thin films of transition metal dichalcogenides.

26303018.label: Project Objectives
26303018.value: Build and calibrate the experimental platform for single-molecule Force-coupled Raman Spectroscopy (smFRS), which would add structural resolution to current single-molecule manipulation methods and offer a new way to characterize the force-involved structural changes and elucidate the sophisticated mechanisms in protein folding. Moreover, we will push the distance sensitivity of smFRS to the cutting-edge Angstrom-level by correlating the delicate spectral features to the molecular extensions in data analysis, which would be a significant improvement of current single-molecule manipulation methods. Obtain force-dependent Raman spectra of model peptides and establish a database for common secondary structures of proteins, which would be the first spectroscopic investigation of a single protein molecule under stretching conditions. The systematic analysis on the correlation between spectral changes and structural alternations would prove the concept of smFRS and provide a convenient reference for protein design and protein folding/unfolding studies. Investigate the mechanism governing the zippering process of SNARE proteins and identify the exact structures of the intermediates by smFRS. By analyzing the correlated force, molecular extension, and Raman spectra, we expect to reveal the details of membrane fusion mechanisms for a better understanding of basic biological processes and the corresponding human diseases.

26303018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26303018.value: Single-molecule manipulation methods open up a new door to answer fundamental questions in sophisticated life processes, with unparalleled advantages to avoid ensemble (bulk) averaging, observe rare events, measure molecular force/distance directly, monitor conformational dynamics, and push the limit of small-scope characterization. In particular, optical tweezers monitor the real-time force response and molecular extensions associated with conformational changes of a single protein molecule during folding/unfolding. The force vs. extension curves can be further analyzed to define intermediate stages and conformational changes. However, it is difficult to depict the complicated molecular structures simply relying on the analysis of molecular extension. Current methods in single-molecule studies are limited by the insufficient structural resolution. Therefore, there is an urgent need to add direct structural detection to current single-molecule manipulation methods. Here, we propose to develop single-molecule Force-coupled Raman Spectroscopy (smFRS), which brings in a new dimension of information for structural characterization in a label-free manner, while still delineating the individual molecular behaviors. Integrating surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy into optical tweezers, smFRS can monitor the real-time force response, molecular extension, and Raman spectra simultaneously. The additional Raman spectra will depict the chemical structures at different force-dependent intermediate states. Furthermore, the huge amounts of spectra at the single-molecule level will enable us to paint a clearer picture of large-scale molecular populations through statistical analysis, offering the interpretation of the bulk observations for heterogeneous systems. To investigate the mechanisms of protein folding/unfolding, we will utilize smFRS to study model peptides as a proof of concept, followed by investigating soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor (SNARE) proteins to showcase the practical applications. Membrane fusion is driven by SNARE proteins through a zippering process, where three distinct stages have been identified by optical tweezers. Nevertheless, the conformational transitions are only estimated from molecular extension without chemical sensitivity. To further understand the zippering hypothesis, we will apply smFRS to obtain the complementary force-dependent Raman spectra and reveal the detailed structures of intermediates. As a highly generalizable technique, smFRS can provide new insight into important biological problems such as the force-involved structural transformations of metalloproteins, allosteric enzymes, and intrinsically disordered proteins. 新型的單分子操控方法為研究生命過程中眾多複雜的基礎問題開闢了一個新的角度，藉由在單分子尺度上的無與倫比的優勢，實驗觀測可以避免總體平均（指對大量樣品的實驗結果是統計平均而造成少量樣品的獨特信號被模糊化處理），從而觀察被忽略的稀有反應過程。通過直接測量單個分子的應力和距離，間接監測單個分子的結構變化，從而達到推動微小尺度的測量極限的目的。在具體實驗中，光鑷可以用來監測實時的應力大小和與構象變化相關的分子延展長度。進一步分析應力與分子延展曲線可以得到中間態和構象變化的信息。然而，僅僅依靠分子延伸長度的間接分析難以描繪複雜的分子結構。當前的單分子研究方法受到結構分辨率不足的限制。因此，對複雜體系的深入研究迫切需要將直接的結構檢測添加到當前的單分子操作方法中。 在這裡，我們提出開發單分子力耦合拉曼光譜（smFRS），它以無標籤的方式為以往間接的結構表徵帶來新的信息維度，同時仍然描繪了單個分子行為。將表面增強拉曼光譜儀集成到光鑷中，smFRS可以同時監測實時應力，分子延展和拉曼光譜。附加的拉曼光譜將描繪不同應力下的中間態的化學鍵結構。此外，在單分子水平上採集的大量光譜將使我們能夠通過統計分析的方法描繪出大規模的分子群體的清晰畫面，從而加深對多相系統的整體觀測結果的解釋。 為了驗證smFRS在單分子層面研究蛋白質折疊/解折疊機理的可行性， 我們將在模式肽中測試方法的穩定性。繼而，同樣的方法可以用於研究可溶性N-乙基馬來酰亞胺敏感因子附著蛋白受體（SNARE）蛋白以展示其在解決實際生物體系複雜問題中的巨大潛力。在生物學上極其核心的膜融合過程是由SNARE蛋白通過蛋白結構變化的類拉鍊過程驅動的，其中三個不同的階段已經被光鑷技術所識別。然而，這些構象轉變僅通過分子延伸長度來間接探知，而缺乏化學結構上的具體證據。為了進一步理解拉鍊假設，我們將應用smFRS來獲得互補的力耦合拉曼光譜，並揭示中間體的詳細結構。作為一種可以廣泛推廣的新型技術，smFRS可以對重要生物學問題提供新見解，例如研究金屬蛋白，變構酶和固有無序蛋白質的力相關結構轉化。

26303018.label: Realisation of objectives
26303018.value: In this project, we have developed a new single-molecule force-coupled Raman spectroscopy method and investigated the dynamic structures of selected proteins in folding and unfolding processes. Objective 1: We constructed a novel experimental platform for single-molecule Force-coupled Raman Spectroscopy (smFRS) by integrating the dual-trap optical tweezers-based force manipulations and the back-scattering geometry Raman spectroscopic measurements, which adds the extra structural resolution to current single-molecule manipulation methods and offers a new way to characterize the force-involved structural changes and elucidate the sophisticated mechanisms in protein folding [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292]. The platform was calibrated to achieve precise force manipulations [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370] and sensitive Raman spectroscopic measurements [Analyst 2020, 145, 5158-5165]. We demonstrated that this novel experimental platform could push the distance sensitivity to the cutting-edge Angstrom-level by correlating the delicate spectral features to the molecular extensions in data analysis, which would be a significant improvement of current single-molecule manipulation methods [Manuscript under review]. Besides, the instrumental configurations and experimental operations of this novel platform were explained and illustrated with details, which also showcases its setting robustness and signal reproducibility [Journal of visualized experiments, 2022, 184, e63862; Biophysical Journal 2022, 121, 3a]. Objective 2: We obtained the Raman spectra of selective model peptides at well-defined fully folded, partially folded, and fully unfolded states associated with the force-dependent manipulations, which reveals the subtle vibrational characteristic as a database regarding the structural stability for common secondary structures of proteins, i.e. alpha-helix, beta-sheet, and random coil [Manuscript in preparation]. Moreover, we demonstrated the versatile force manipulations coupled with Raman spectroscopic measurements to control the dynamic hotspot for protein structure characterizations from small size-sampling to single-molecule detections [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Manuscript under review]. Under single-molecule force manipulations, biomolecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins were stretched to straighten and, to an extent, change secondary structures. Meanwhile, the surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) measurements were conducted at the specified site of the stretched molecule, which is the first single-molecule force-correlative Raman spectral analysis to prove the concept of smFRS and provide a convenient reference for biomolecule folding/unfolding studies [Manuscript under review]. Besides, we utilized the correlative single-molecule manipulation and site-specified SERS characterization to monitor DNA-small molecule interactions, pushing the position accuracy and distance sensitivity to sub-nanometer level [Manuscript under review]. Furthermore, we performed the single-molecule force spectroscopy experiments to monitor the mechanical unfolding and refolding processes of DNA hairpins, which establishes a systematic analysis to reveal the thermodynamic and kinetic driving force [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370]. In addition, we studied the potential interactions between the metal nanoparticles and different proteins to minimize perturbation from the SERS measurements [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Chemical Communications, 2021, 57, 6979-6982]. We also shared the fabrication protocol of the silver nanoparticle-coated silica beads as SERS substrates, which determines the single-molecule SERS detection sensitivity and reproducibility for protein structural characterizations. [Protocol Exchange on Research Square 2021, PPR291931] Objective 3: We investigated the mechanisms and intermediate structures of selective membrane proteins including soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor (SNARE) proteins and surfeit locus protein 4 (SURF4) by combining the correlate force, molecular extension, and Raman spectra obtained from our novel experimental platform and the reference acquired from conventional biophysical characterization methods, which reveals the zippering process of SNARE proteins in membrane fusion mechanisms and the protein-protein interaction to release signaling molecule into vesicles and membrane transportations associated with basic biological processes and the corresponding potential human diseases [Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2022, 119, e2113991119; Manuscript in preparation]. Furthermore, since SNARE proteins and many membrane proteins contain primary alpha-helical confirmations, we compared the Raman characteristics in the folding, unfolding, and refolding processes of the selected SNARE protein and that of the alpha-helical model peptides with different lengths, which reveals their structural stabilities and dynamic transformations correlated to their potential biological functions and provides profound insights into peptide-based drug discovery [Manuscript in preparation].

26303018.label: Major findings and research outcome
26303018.value: We have developed a novel single-molecule Force-coupled Raman Spectroscopy (smFRS) platform by integrating the dual-trap optical tweezers-based force manipulations and the back-scattering geometry Raman spectroscopic measurements, which offers the unique structural resolution in addition to the precise molecular controllability to bring in a new dimension of information for direct protein structure characterization at the single-molecule level [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292]. For the first time, the vibrational features of the monomeric alpha-synuclein protein at physiological concentrations were characterized under small-size sampling measurements and large-scale molecular population statistical analysis, indicating the co-existence of low-populated, transient, and heterogeneous structures that are overwhelmed by the ensemble averaging in conventional bulk measurements but crucial for understanding the initiation of amyloid aggregations related to neurodegenerative diseases [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292]. More importantly, we have demonstrated the first single-molecule force-correlative Raman spectral analysis to prove the concept of smFRS as a highly generalizable technique to study the folding and unfolding processes of various biological macromolecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Manuscript under review]. Moreover, we have performed the single-molecule force spectroscopy experiments to monitor the mechanical unfolding and refolding processes of DNA hairpins, which establishes a systematic analysis to reveal the thermodynamic and kinetic driving force [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370]. In addition, we have studied the potential interactions between the metal nanoparticles and different proteins to minimize perturbation from surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) measurements [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Chemical Communications, 2021, 57, 6979-6982]. We have developed novel metallic nanostructures as SERS substrates [Analyst 2020, 145, 5158-5165] and shared the fabrication protocol to achieve the single-molecule SERS detection sensitivity and reproducibility for protein structural characterizations [Protocol Exchange on Research Square 2021, PPR291931]. We have illustrated the setting of our platform with details to further verify its robustness and reproducibility for easy accessibility [Journal of visualized experiments, 2022, 184, e63862; Biophysical Journal 2022, 121, 3a]. Furthermore, we have investigated the mechanisms and intermediate structures of selective membrane proteins including soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor (SNARE) proteins and surfeit locus protein 4 (SURF4), which reveals the zippering process of SNARE proteins in membrane fusion mechanisms and the protein-protein interaction to release signaling molecule into vesicles and membrane transportations associated with fundamental biological processes and the corresponding potential human diseases [Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2022, 119, e2113991119; Manuscript in preparation].

26303018.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26303018.value: As a highly generalizable technique, our platform enables the direct spectroscopic detections of endogenous molecular vibrations for structural characterizations as a new dimension of information added to the existing single-molecule force manipulation methods, thus could be adopted to investigate the force-involved structural transformations of metalloproteins, allosteric enzymes, and intrinsically disordered proteins in the future. Moreover, it correlates single-molecule force manipulations and site-specified surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) characterizations to overcome the optical diffraction limit to push the spatial accuracy to sub-nanometer for single-molecule spatial scanning measurements in solutions, which would inspire new method developments and applications in molecular interactions, encryption, and sequencing. Furthermore, our platform adds precise molecular controllability to the existing single-molecule SERS platforms, which makes it feasible to characterize the dynamic structures and interactions of various biological macromolecules including DNA, RNA, and proteins in the follow-up studies. Specifically, we would utilize our platform to apply stretching force to extend and unfold the secondary structures of DNA, RNA, and proteins to expose the site of interest for interacting with exogenous agents and unveiling buried sequence information at the single-molecule level, which might reveal hidden details in significant biological processes and provide valuable insight into the development of precision medicines.

26303018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26303018.value: Single-molecule studies have revolutionized our understanding of complex biological systems since a molecule of interest can be differentiated from surrounding molecules. To better characterize the molecule of interest, we have developed a novel method that combines the dual-trap optical tweezers-based force manipulations and the back-scattering geometry Raman spectroscopic measurements. It enables precise molecular control at sub-nanometer sensitivity while bringing in a new dimension of information for direct structural characterizations of the molecule of interest in a label-free manner, which is a powerful platform to tackle the challenging problems in heterogeneous systems. For the first time, we have characterized the low-populated, transient, and diverse structures of the monomeric alpha-synuclein protein at physiological concentrations, which are overwhelmed by the ensemble averaging in conventional bulk measurements but crucial to determine the initiation of amyloid aggregations related to neurodegenerative diseases. We also investigated the mechanisms and intermediate structures of selective membrane proteins that are associated with fundamental biological processes and the corresponding potential human diseases. As a highly generalizable technique, our platform holds great promise to study various biological macromolecules such as DNA, RNA, and proteins to decode the mystery of more complex biological processes in the future.
