26305218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26305218.value: A series of my recent papers, written with Z. Hamaker and B. Pawlowski has developed, to a significant but not exhaustive extent, the theory of involution words for permutations. An involution is a permutation that is its own inverse and that therefore acts by swapping disjoint pairs of distinct numbers. An involution word is a sequence of indices that records one of the possible ways in which one can build up an involution, in as few steps as possible, by composing a sequence of elementary transformations of a certain natural type. Some remarkable properties of these objects have been revealed by our work. There are typically many involution words that one can associate with a given involution. For the reverse permutation (the involution that reverses the numbers 1 to n), the total number of involution words coincides with the dimension of the maximal irreducible representation of a Coxeter group of type B, which is also the number of "standard shifted tableaux" of a certain shape. There are also notions of "involution Schubert polynomials," defined as certain generating functions over involutions words, and "involution Stanley symmetric functions," obtained by taking certain limits of the Schubert polynomials. It turns out that the involution Schubert polynomials are closely related to the geometry of type A flag varieties (certain important geometric spaces), while the involution Stanley symmetric functions are themselves connected to the Schur P-functions (certain symmetric functions with relevance to representation theory and combinatorics). Many of these phenomena are all the more interesting because of their formal similarity to theorems about reduced words for permutations discovered in the 1980s, despite the fact that completely different proof strategies are required to establish our new findings. The goals of the proposed project are to extend what is known about involution words, both combinatorially and geometrically, in three distinct directions. First, despite a considerable amount of recent work, several open questions remain to be addressed in the case of permutations. Second, much of the algebraic theory of Schubert polynomials, Stanley symmetric functions, and so on should extend to involutions in affine symmetric groups. Third, the notion of involution words makes sense for any Coxeter group, and there appear to be some remarkable combinatorial identities for involution words of elements of the Coxeter groups of type B. These questions are natural to explore, and their answers will most likely play a useful role in advances in representation theory, combinatorics, and geometry. 我最近與Z. Hamaker和B. Pawlowski一起撰寫的一系列論文，在很大程度上但並非詳盡無遺的範圍內，發展了用於排列的對合詞的理論。對合是一種排列，它是自己的逆，因此通過交換不相交的不同數字對來起作用。對合詞是一系列索引，它們通過組成一定的自然類型的基本變換序列，以盡可能少的步驟記錄可以建立對合的可能方式之一。 我們的工作揭示了這些物體的一些顯著特性。通常存在許多可以與給定的對合相關聯的對合詞。對於反向排列（將數字1反轉為n的對合），對合詞的總數與B類的Coxeter組的最大不可約表示的維度一致，這也是“標準移位的表格”某種形狀的數量。 還存在“對合Schubert多項式”的概念，其定義為在對數詞上的某些生成函數，以及“對合斯坦利對稱函數”，其通過取Schubert多項式的某些限制而獲得。事實證明，對合Schubert多項式與A型旗幟變體（某些重要幾何空間）的幾何密切相關，而對合Stanley對稱函數本身與Schur P函數相關（某些對稱函數與表示理論和組合學相關）。 這些現像中的許多現像都更有趣，因為它們與20世紀80年代發現的排列減少詞的定理形式相似，儘管事實上需要完全不同的證明策略來建立我們的新發現。 擬議項目的目標是在三個不同的方向上擴展關於對合詞的組合，包括組合和幾何。首先，儘管最近有相當多的工作，但在排列的情況下仍有幾個懸而未決的問題需要解決。其次，Schubert多項式的代數理論，Stanley對稱函數等的大部分理論都應該延伸到仿射對稱群中的變換。第三，對合詞的概念對於任何Coxeter群都是有意義的，並且對於B類的Coxeter群的元素的對合詞似乎存在一些顯著的組合身份。 這些問題很容易被探索，他們的答案很可能在表徵理論，組合學和幾何學的進步中發揮有用的作用。

26305218.label: Realisation of objectives
26305218.value: Objective #1 has been addressed by two of my joint papers with Brendan Pawlowski ("On some properties of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials" published in 2021 and "K-theory formulas for orthogonal and symplectic orbit closures" published in 2020), which study K-theoretic generalizations of involution Stanley symmetric functions and relate them to geometry. Objective #2 is partly addressed by the same joint papers with Pawlowski. In those works, we show that certain limits of K-theory representatives for orbit closures in type A flag varieties are also K-theory representatives for Schubert classes in orthogonal and Lagrangian Grassmannian spaces. This objective is also only half completed, however, because a significant amount of progress on this objective was carried out in independent work of Pawlowski (namely, in his 2019 paper "Universal graph Schubert varieties") before there was time to address it in this proposal. Objective #3 has been completely carried out through two papers that I finished in 2019: "A symplectic refinement of shifted Hecke insertion" and "Bumping operators and insertion algorithms for queer supercrystals". Objective #4 has also been completely carried out. The conjectural analogue of involution Coxeter-Knuth insertion for fixed-point-free involution words is described in my paper "A symplectic refinement of shifted Hecke insertion" which was finished in January 2019. The basic theory of affine involution Stanley symmetric functions, as set out in Objective #5, has been developed in two papers: one written by myself and my PhD student Yifeng Zhang ("Affine transitions for involution Stanley symmetric functions", published in 2022), and one written solely by Yifeng Zhang while under my supervision ("Quasiparabolic sets and Stanley symmetric functions for affine fixed-point-free involutions", published in 2021). However, there are still a number of mysteries and open questions that would make for excellent followup research problems in this area, although is beyond the scope of this objective. Objective #6 has been carried out in my papers "Stanley symmetric functions for signed involutions" with Brendan Pawlowski (published in 2019) and "Atoms for signed permutations" with Zachary Hamaker (published in 2021). The second paper was completed before this RGC funded project began, but was significantly revised and expanded in 2020.

26305218.label: Major findings and research outcome
26305218.value: One set of major findings concerns the development of many generalizations of involution Stanley symmetric functions. For example, new versions of these functions are explored for type B in joint work with Pawlowski ("Stanley symmetric functions for signed involutions", published in the Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A in 2019), for affine type A in joint work with Zhang ("Affine transitions for involution Stanley symmetric functions", published in the European Journal of Combinatorics in 2022), and for K-theory in more joint work with Pawlowski ("K-theory formulas for orthogonal and symplectic orbit closures", published in Advances in Mathematics in 2020). A second set of major findings is related to new geometric interpretations of involution Schubert polynomials and Stanley symmetric functions, which came to light while trying to address project objectives #1 and #2. Some relevant publications include joint work with Pawlowski ("K-theory formulas for orthogonal and symplectic orbit closures" and "Gröbner geometry for skew-symmetric matrix Schubert varieties", published in Advances in Mathematics in 2021 and 2022) and joint work with Hamaker and Pawlowski ("Involution pipe dreams", published in the Canadian Journal of Mathematics in 2021). A third set of major findings concerns the discovery of new insertion algorithms, which emerged thanks to project objectives #3 and #4, and which have led to several followup papers on novel categories of crystals. Some relevant publications here include two papers which I wrote without coauthors ("A symplectic refinement of shifted Hecke insertion", published in Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A in 2020, and "Bumping operators and insertion algorithms for queer supercrystals", published in Selecta Mathematica, New Series in 2022), along with more recently completely joint work with my PhD student Kam Hung Tong ("Highest weight crystals for Schur Q-functions", currently under review).

26305218.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26305218.value: My joint work with Pawlowski on "K-theory formulas for orthogonal and symplectic orbit closures" proposed several still open research questions about K-theory representatives for orthogonal group orbits in the type A flag variety. Studying these questions is one avenue for further research. There is also a lot of potential to further develop the theory of affine involution Stanley symmetric functions, and to provide better geometric interpretations of these functions. What has been addressed to date in my joint work in Zhang in the course of this project only uncovers the basics of this subject. Finally, the study of involution insertion algorithms via this project has directly led to some followup work on new categories of crystals whose characters are Schur Q-polynomials. I have coauthored one paper on this fascinating new topic with a current PhD student, but there are many opportunities to further develop the area.

26305218.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26305218.value: An involution is a permutation that is its own inverse, and which therefore acts by swapping disjoint pairs of distinct numbers. An involution word is a sequence of indices that records one of the possible ways in which one can build up an involution by composing certain elementary transformations. There are also notions of "involution Schubert polynomials," defined as generating functions over involutions words, and "involution Stanley symmetric functions," obtained by taking limits of the Schubert polynomials. Involution Schubert polynomials are closely related to the geometry of certain important geometric spaces called flag varieties. In this project, we resolved several open questions about involution words, involution Schubert polynomials, and involution Stanley symmetric functions. We also discovered and investigated many novel extensions of these objects to other types and to more general geometric theories. These developments are significant as they resolve open conjectures and also lay the groundwork for a lot of potential future research in algebraic combinatorics and geometry.

26309618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26309618.value: The most relevant anthropogenic activities that can significantly modify the Earth’s climate system are greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and land-use/land-cover (LULC) changes. While increased GHG emissions perturb the global energy balance, LULC changes due to urban growth alter the surface energy partitioning and the water cycle at the regional to local scale through surface-atmosphere interactions. Despite their different physical processes, both GHG emissions and urban expansion are considered as important contributors to global and local warming trends. In this regard, China is a representative region with rising concerns about anthropogenic warming, particularly along the heavily populated eastern coast with its rapid development. Studies on detection and attribution of recent climate changes evidenced the significant increase in the frequency and intensity of heat waves in China due to global warming. Observational and modelling studies also support the urban expansion’s role in exacerbating the severity of heat waves. Although the impacts of climate change and urbanization on the present climate are well documented, most climate projections have not appropriately considered future urban growth-induced LULC changes, leading to a potential underestimation of the risk of heat-related extremes. The proposed project will be the first attempt to quantify the relative contributions of anthropogenic climate change and urban growth on human thermal comfort in two vast urban agglomerations of China. An unprecedented level of dynamically downscaled climate projections will be produced within a state-of-the-art experimental framework in terms of multiple global climate models, multiple regional climate models, and multiple scenarios of both future GHG emissions and future urban growth. The factor separation method will be applied to various subsets of massive simulations, which facilitates separating the contributions of the two individual factors (GHG emissions vs. urban growth) as well as their synergetic effects on temperature, humidity, and the related thermal comfort. Not only conventional heat stress indices that measure the combined effects of temperature and humidity, but also thermophysiological indices that account for metabolic heat production depending on labor intensity, will be considered to integrate the perception of the human body’s heat strain in an outdoor working environment. This project will strengthen our understanding of the urban-atmosphere interactions under global warming conditions, with important implications for the mitigation and adaptation strategies to alleviate the negative impacts of anthropogenic warming on human thermal comfort. 溫室氣體 (GHG）排放與土地利用/土地覆蓋變化 (LULC）是對地球氣候系統影響最大的人為活動。GHG排放的增加會擾動全球能量平衡，而城市拓展所引起的LULC則會改變地表的能量分配，通過陸氣交換過程改變區域和局部尺度的水循環。 儘管兩者的物理過程有所不同， 但GHG排放和城市擴展都被視為全球與地方暖化趨勢的重要貢獻源。 而中國，尤其是在人口密度較大、發展較快的東部沿海地區，正是受到人為暖化的不斷增強影響的代表區域。 關於近來氣候變化的檢測與歸因研究證實了全球變暖在中國造成的熱浪頻率與強度的明顯增強，而觀測與模式研究則揭示了城市擴展也在不斷加重熱浪的不良影響。 儘管氣候變化與城市化對現時氣候的影響都已得到較好的記載，但大多數的氣候預估未能恰當地考慮未來的城市增長所帶來的LULC變化，從而可能低估了極端熱天氣事件所造成的風險。 本項目將首次嘗試對中國的兩個大城市群中的人為氣候變化和城市增長對人體熱舒適的相對貢獻進行量化研究,，通過多個全球氣候模型、多個區域氣候模型以及未來GHG排放和城市增長的多種情景搭建起的最先進的實驗框架，進行創新性的動態降尺度氣候預估。多個模擬中的不同子集將有助於分離兩個獨立因素 (GHG排放與城市增長) 對溫度、適度和相關熱舒適度的貢獻。 為了綜合考量人體在室外工作環境中的熱應變感知情況， 本研究將同時考慮測量溫度同濕度結合效應的常規熱應激指數以及指示基於勞動強度變化的代謝產熱的熱生理指標。 本項目將加強我們對全球變暖條件下城市-大氣相互作用的理解，對制定減輕人為變暖對人體熱舒適度的負面影響的減緩與適應戰略具有重要意義。

26309618.label: Major findings and research outcome
26309618.value: We first developed the non-hydrostatic RegCM4 (RegCM4-NH) customized over two vast urban agglomerations (i.e., the Pearl River Delta (PRD), and the Yangtze River Delta (YRD)) in China. We found that the performance of RegCM4-NH over the PRD and YRD can be the best when driven by a non-hydrostatic mother domain simulation and when turning on the Emanuel convection scheme. It turned out that the performance of RegCM4-NH was comparable to the convection-permitting the Weather Research and Forecasting simulations over the PRD and YRD. In addition, we improved the performance of RegCM4-NH by the implementation of the building energy model (BEM). Since the BEM prognostically calculates interior building temperature and considers the ventilation and heat transfer between the building and the environment, it can better estimate anthropogenic heat flux, which in turn alleviated the warm bias in urban grids observed in RegCM4-NH. Improved RegCM4-NH with BEM was used to dynamically downscale the multiple global climate projections (Norwegian Earth System Model (NorESM1-M) and Max Planck Institute for Meteorology Earth System Model-Mixed Resolution (MPI-ESM-MR)) forced by the medium and high levels emission scenarios (i.e., RCP4.5 and RCP8.5). Unlike previous studies, the transient nature of future urban expansion generated from different Shared Socio-Economic Pathways (i.e., SSP2 and SSP5) was taken into consideration for both periods: mid-future (2030-2049) and far-future (2080-2099). Changes in multiple heat stress indices, namely, wet-bulb globe temperature, humidex, and apparent temperature, which are all calculated based on both temperature and humidity, were investigated in order to quantify the relative contributions of global warming and urban growth to human thermal comfort. It was found that while the impact of urban expansion reached its peak in the mid-future period, the worsening of heat stress was much more dominated by global warming at the end of 21st century. Under the RCP8.5 scenario, the temperature is likely to increase by 6 ℃ whereas the wet-bulb temperature is projected to increase 4 ℃ due to the reduction in relative humidity. In addition, the urban expansion is able to enhance the warming up to 1.47℃ over several urban points. In general, the effect of global warming is at least twice as significant as that of unban growth alone in terms of the increase in human thermal discomfort. The impact of transient urban growth emerged in a more significant way in the YRD region.

26309618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26309618.value: The scientific knowledge and modeling techniques obtained from this project will infuse new insights and logical extensions into the following-up new projects that mainly focus on the climate change issues over the Pearl River Delta (PRD) and the Yangtze River Delta (YRD).

26309618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26309618.value: This project comprehensively estimated the combined effects of global warming and urbanization on human heat stress over the Pearl River Delta (PRD) and the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) in China. Since most climate projections have not adequately considered the synergistic effects of urbanization under global warming, it is a valuable attempt to incorporate the transient evolution of urban growth into future climate projections in response to increased greenhouse gas emissions. In addition, the comparison of diverse impacts of urban growth on human thermal comfort over the PRD and YRD regions is able to provide important insights into emerging patterns of urban heat island that interacts with different meteorological backgrounds over these regions. Although both PRD and YRD have experienced rapid urbanization over the past few decades, the effect of urban heat island appeared in a different manner and the discrepancy between urban and suburban was greater in YRD than in PRD. From a technical point of view, the first evaluation of non-hydrostatic RegCM4 will be a valuable reference to facilitate a wider use of it over monsoon-dominated regions of East Asia.

26501518.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26501518.value: 希望及其在创新过程中的角色

26501518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501518.value: The creative process requires motivation to persevere through its many challenges and setbacks and hope is often an important emotional component of this process. Yet, hope may involve different motivational forces than other positive emotions. Hope is defined as the yearning for the attainment of a desired goal (e.g., Stotland, 1969; Lazarus, 1999), yet this goal may never materialize (Lazarus, 1999). In this way, hope’s positivity is unusual because this gap between one’s current and desired states is often a distinguishing feature of negative emotions. As such, the combination of uncertainty and positivity in hope is unique and may have profound effects on people’s motivations to engage in the creative process. The proposed research aims to investigate how hope acts as a motivational force in the creative process and what factors may impact this relationship. The creative process is a long-term creative engagement in which individuals may experience challenges and setbacks with resulting high and low emotional experiences (To, Fisher, Ashkanasy, & Rowe, 2012). I argue that hope may motivate individuals to persist through the creative process through two potential avenues: increased persistence and risk-taking propensity. Furthermore, I propose that while hope may increase persistence on creative engagement, it may also make individuals respond to feedback in ways that protect them from negative feelings such that those with high hope can constructively incorporate feedback and maintain their desire to persist in their creative process. Yet, individuals with high hope receiving feedback may also decrease their risk-taking propensity. By exploring the relationships between hope, persistence, risk-taking, feedback, and creativity in two studies - one longitudinal field study using experience-sampling methodology and one laboratory experiment - this research aims to better understand how the discrete emotion of hope drives the creative process. It advances the literatures on emotions and creativity by (1) dissecting the psychological processes through which hope motivates creativity, (2) exploring the effect of external feedback on these processes, and (3) empirically examining the dynamic relationships between these variables over time. Aside from these contributions, the proposed research also has important practical implications. Findings from the proposed study will increase individuals’ understanding of how their emotions - particularly hope - affects their motivation to persist in creative endeavors and how feedback may affect these relationships. Such meta-cognitive awareness could facilitate how individuals experience the creative process and, perhaps, increase their desire to persist in their creative pursuits. 创新过程需要动力来坚持不懈地克服其中的许多挑战和挫折，而希望往往是这一过程的重要情感组成部分。然而，希望可能涉及与其他积极情绪不同的激励力量。希望被定义为对实现预期目标的渴望（例如，Lazarus，1999），但这个目标可能永远不会实现（Lazarus，1999）。通过这种方式，希望的积极性是不寻常的，因为当前和期望状态之间的差距往往是消极情绪的显著特征。因此，希望中的不确定性和积极性的结合是独特的，并且可能对人们参与创新过程的动机产生深远的影响。拟议的研究旨在调查希望如何成为创新过程中的动力，以及哪些因素可能会影响这种关系。 创新过程是一种长期的创造性参与，个人可能会遇到挑战和挫折，从而导致高低情绪体验（To, Fisher, Ashkanasy, & Rowe, 2012）。我认为，希望可能会激励个人通过两种可能的途径坚持创新过程：增加持久性和冒险倾向。此外，我建议虽然希望可能会增加创造性参与的持久性，但也可能使个人以保护他们免受负面情绪的方式回应反馈，以便那些抱有很高希望的人可以建设性地纳入反馈并保持他们坚持创新过程的愿望。然而，希望得到反馈的个人也可能会降低他们的冒险倾向。通过在两项研究中探索希望，持久性，冒险，反馈和创造力之间的关系 - 一项使用经验抽样方法和一项实验室实验的纵向实地研究 - 本研究旨在更好地理解希望的离散情绪如何驱动创新的过程。它通过以下方式推进关于情感和创造力的文献：（1）剖析希望激发创造力的心理过程，（2）探索外部反馈对这些过程的影响，以及（3）实证检验这些变量之间的动态关系。 除了这些贡献之外，拟议的研究也具有重要的实际意义。拟议研究的结果将增加个人对他们的情绪 - 特别是希望 - 如何影响他们坚持创造性努力的动机以及反馈如何影响这些关系的理解。这种元认知意识可以促进个人如何体验创作过程，并且可能增加他们坚持创造性追求的愿望。

26502418.value: 当忙碌人偏好不省时间：忙碌对节约时间产品偏好的作用

26502418.label: Project Objectives
26502418.value: To understand how busyness is viewed and appraised by consumers To understand the effect of busyness on consumer behavior and choice To examine conditions (of varying cultural and individual differences) under which the busy desire to reduce busyness versus not, and provide practical guidelines for practitioners
rows: To understand how busyness is viewed and appraised by consumers
To understand the effect of busyness on consumer behavior and choice
To examine conditions (of varying cultural and individual differences) under which the busy desire to reduce busyness versus not, and provide practical guidelines for practitioners

26502418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502418.value: The word “busy” has become one of the key descriptors of modern consumers, with an increasing number of consumers reportedly feeling busier than ever (Schlute 2014). Given the widely documented negative consequences of being busy (Svenson and Maule 1993), much effort has been invested in tempering a growing sense of busyness in society. Underlying this effort is the idea that busy people should desire to reduce busyness. In our research, we challenge this idea and demonstrate that busy people desire to reduce busyness only under some conditions, but desire not to reduce busyness under other conditions, and test this in the domain of product choices. Starting from mixed findings in the literature, which shows inconsistent results about how busyness impacts desire for means to reduce busyness, namely time-saving products (Strober and Weinberg 1980; Reilly 1982), we propose that considering both the negative and positive views of busyness is a key to this puzzle. Following the coping literature framework of threat-challenge appraisal of a stressor (Lazarus and Folkman 1984), we argue that when busyness is appraised as a threat, time-saving products are viewed as helpful tools for alleviating the aversive state, and thus desired. In contrast, extending research documenting positive perception of busyness displayed in other people (Gershuny 2005, Bellezza, Paharia and Keinan 2016) and building on the PI’s ongoing work (Kim, Wadhwa and Chattopadhyay 2017) demonstrating a unique link between busyness and enhanced self-view, we propose that busyness could also be appraised as a challenge to bolster self-value by demonstrating autonomous competence. In such a case, we propose that time-saving products are viewed as an impediment to one’s unique opportunity to be a better self, and thus not desired. Consistent with past research (Crocker and Wolfe 2001) showing that people derive self-value only in the domain relevant to self-identity, we further predict that, under challenge appraisal, busyness reduces desire for time-saving products only when the time-saving product is relevant to self-identity. In addition, we explore various cultural and individual differences and demonstrate practical guidelines for when busyness should be tempered versus encouraged. Specifically, our findings suggest interventions for reducing busyness should be helpful for those low in work ethic, living in developed country or politically conservative. Our findings will provide a comprehensive theoretical framework on busyness for researchers and provide crucial practical guidelines for practitioners concerned with busy epidemics in society. “忙碌”已经成为现代消费者的一个重要描述词，越来越多的消费者被报道说感到从未如此繁忙。因为多方面文档都反应忙碌的负面后果，大量的努力放在了减缓人们愈加繁忙的感受。支撑这些努力的肯本原因是有观点认为忙碌人应该渴望降低繁忙。我们的研究对此观点提出质疑，并论证忙碌人只有在一些条件下渴望降低繁忙，在其他条件下反而渴望不要降低繁忙。我们在产品选择上检验我们的论点。忙碌对降低繁忙的方式（即节约时间的产品）的选择，文献中说法不一。我们提议，这个谜题的关键是人们对忙碌既有负面也有正面的看法。按照应对文献中对压力源的威胁-挑战的估计构架，我们认为当繁忙被评估为威胁的时候，节约时间的产品被视为减缓厌恶状态的有利工具，从而被人渴望。与此相反，延伸研究证明其他人对忙碌有正面的看法，而且发现忙碌和提高自我认知之间存在独特的关系。建立在PI现行研究的基础上，我们建议忙碌也可以被评估为挑战，通过证明独立能力从而加强自我价值。在这种情况下，我们认为节约时间的产品会被视为成为更好自我的障碍物，因此不被渴望。过去的研究 发现只有在与自我认同领域，人们才会获得自我价值。与此一致，我们进一步预测，在挑战评估时，只有当节约时间的产品是与自我认同相关的，忙碌才会降低对这类产品的渴望。另外，我们探究各种文化和个体的不同，发现了实际的指导原则可以帮助我们判断何时应当缓和、何时应当鼓励忙碌。具体来说，我们的研究结果表示，对于职业道德低、生活在发达国家或者政治守旧国家的人，降低忙碌对他们是有所帮助的。我们的发现为研究人员提供了一个研究忙碌的综合理论框架，并且为关注忙碌疾病的实务工作者提供了重要的实际指导方针。

26502818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502818.value: The core objective of this proposal is to examine under what conditions investors benefit from indirect social ties to their investment targets. Existing research in network analysis suggests that there are two competing effects. On one hand, indirect ties to the investment target – i.e., knowing an actor who knows the target – can be sources of high-quality non-public information about the investment target’s capabilities and likely future performance, and as such allow the investor to make more informed investment decisions. On the other hand, indirect ties can reduce the quality of the investment decision if they unduly limit the breadth and the depth of the search in which investors engage. For example, investors may relax their due diligence standards and blindly herd into investments held by their peers. I aim to unpack those different processes and apply them to a rarely studied, but important setting: the investment relationships between the venture capital (VC) firms and their limited partners (LPs). Unlike prior research, which has generally only focused on a single network – such as the network of syndication ties between VC firms – I construct a multilevel network that includes: (1) the horizontal co-investment network between LPs; (2) the horizontal co-investment network between VC firms; (3) the vertical network of investment ties between LPs and VC firms. Those distinctions are important given the different roles and asymmetric strategic objectives of the VC firms and LPs, and allow me to construct two distinct kind of indirect relationships: LP-mediated relationships (i.e., an LP has co-invested with another LP that holds an investment in the target VC firm) as well as VC-mediated relationships (i.e., an LP has an investment in a VC firm that has co-invested with the target VC firm). I develop a theoretical framework predicting which kind of relationships allow LPs to cherry-pick the best possible investment opportunities, based on the type of intermediary (a fellow LP or a VC firm), the attributes of the intermediary, as well as the attributes of the investment target.

26502818.label: Realisation of objectives
26502818.value: All objectives have been achieved by the in-progress research. Below is the list of the objectives and how they were addressed. 1. Objective No. 1 was fully addressed by the study “Channel Redundancy and the Limits of the Performance Effects of Interfirm Ties” with Umit Ozmel and Valentina Assenova. In that study, we specifically modeled the effects of LP-mediated and GP-mediated ties using the methodology outlined in the proposal. In addition to identifying significant performance effects of both types of ties, we also documented important boundary conditions. For example, we showed that different types of ties are substitutes in their effect on performance (i.e., stacking different types of ties has diminishing marginal effects); GP-mediated ties have maximum effect for less experienced LPs and those evaluating geographically distant opportunities. 2. Objective No. 2 was fully addressed by the same study as well. The theoretical motivation for the study was understanding the different effects that different types of network intermediaries have, and the results directly contribute to the literature on multiplex networks. Further, Valentina Assenova and I have used the data to develop another relevant study (“Breaking into the Club: Overcoming the Liability of Being Unknown and Unconnected via Professional Service Provider Ties”) in which we examined the effects of professional service firms (placement agents and auditors) in the matching between LPs and PE firms. We show that such intermediaries are crucial for PEs without much track record or connections to find their first investors. Altogether, this project illuminates the complex multiplex dynamics between LPs, PE firms, and professional service firms. 3. Objective No. 3 was fully addressed primarily by the initial study with Ozmel and Assenova as well. We have a number of practical implications for LPs, including the importance of social connections for realizing superior returns, as well as the circumstances where social connections are especially influential. The study with Valentina Assenova, as well as a third study with Benjamin Hallen and Alicia DeSantola “Windows versus Waves of Opportunity: How Reputation Alters Venture Capital Firms’ Reactions to Resource Mobilization Opportunities?” also has rich implications from the PE firms’ perspective, including the optimal timing and social network support for fundraising from LPs.

26502818.label: Major findings and research outcome
26502818.value: The primary output of the project is the working paper (joint with Valentina Assenova and Umit Ozmel) provisionally titled “Channel Redundancy and the Limits of the Performance Effects of Interfirm Ties.” We show that both LP- and GP-mediated ties enable LPs to make more successful investment decisions, though the effects of GP-mediated ties are much stronger. Further, we find evidence of diminishing returns if an LP is connected to a PE firm via multiple different types of ties. We also document that the effects of GP-mediated ties are especially positive for inexperienced LPs with little outside sources of information and for assessing geographically distant PE firms. The paper was presented at the 2021 AoM annual meeting; a revision of the paper (under the title "Quality Uncertainty and the Performance Benefits of Social Ties in Private Markets") is under review in the Strategic Management Journal. A related project (with Valentina Assenova) is provisionally titled “Breaking into the Club: Overcoming the Liability of Being Unknown and Unconnected via Professional Service Provider Ties.” In this paper, we explored how two major types of intermediaries in the PE industry (placement agents and auditors) affect the matching of LPs to PE firms and the implications of such selection. Our major finding is that LPs are indeed more likely to invest in PE firms that use a professional service provider that the LP has interacted with in the past, especially for PE firms that have limited other connections or lack track record. However, even if professional service providers can help a PE firm get the benefit of the doubt when it lacks any track record, they cannot shield it from a poor track record. The paper is in preparation for submission to Strategic Management Journal. A final project (with Alicia DeSantola and Benjamin Hallen), titled “Windows versus Waves of Opportunity: How Reputation Alters Venture Capital Firms’ Reactions to Resource Mobilization Opportunities” zeroes in on the fundraising behavior of the VCs. We find that high-reputation VC firms are relatively more restrained than low-reputation VC firms in capitalizing on firm-specific positive shocks such as high-profile exits. A key reason for this restraint is high-reputation VCs’ confidence in their ability to attract resources at will. However, high-reputation VC firms are more aggressive than low-reputation VC firms in capitalizing on external shocks such as hot markets for raising capital. The paper is under revision (1st revise & resubmit) from Strategic Management Journal.

26502818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26502818.value: Beyond the initial paper on channel redundancy (“Channel Redundancy and the Limits of the Performance Effects of Interfirm Ties”) and its revision under review, I have pushed the project in several directions. The first direction is examining the multiplex dynamics between professional service firms, PE firms, and LPs. While I already have a working paper with Valentina Assenova on the role that professional service firms play in the matching between LPs and PE firms (“Breaking into the Club: Overcoming the Liability of Being Unknown and Unconnected via Professional Service Provider Ties”), we are also planning follow-on work on how professional service firms can facilitate information flow among PE firms and lead to herding of investment behavior. I also plan to build on the second branch of the project (“Windows versus waves of opportunity: How reputation alters venture capital firms’ reactions to resource mobilization opportunities”) with Alicia DeSantola and Benjamin Hallen. In the existing working paper, we focus on VC scaling in response to internal and external opportunities; however, we also plan to elaborate on the performance implications of such scaling. In particular, do VC firms that overscale (relative to their internal capabilities) suffer from a reduced subsequent performance?

26502818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26502818.value: The project examined how institutional investors – such as endowments, foundations, and pension funds – can improve their selection of private equity funds thanks to various kinds of social connections within the industry. My coauthors and I find that connections via other private equity funds (and, to a lesser degree, other institutional investors) improve the returns that institutional investors realize from their investments. We also find that certain circumstances increase the positive effects of social ties: for example, when the institutional investor has less private equity investment experience, or when it is investing in geographically distant funds. In separate projects, we also explore the role of professional service firms (such as placement agents and auditors) in bringing together institutional investors and private equity funds, as well as how private equity firms take advantage of various types of fundraising opportunities to scale up their funds. Altogether, our results help inform institutional investors’ due diligence practices and investment behavior by alerting them to the importance of social networks for investment performance; as well as inform private equity firms’ optimal fundraising strategies.

26504318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504318.value: The Internet and mobile technology has transformed many aspects of our society, including the way in which people find and establish romantic relationships. Online dating services such as eHarmony, Match.com, Coffee Meets Bagel, and OkCupid have become popular platforms for people to find their partners, and has fundamentally changed the dating landscape. As of 2015, 15% of adults in the United States used online dating services (Pew Research Center 2016). Two-thirds of online daters have gone on a date with someone they met through an online dating service (Pew Research Center 2016), and one-third of marriages start from online dating (Cacioppo et al. 2013). Online dating services revenue is expected to exceed US$3 billion with 5.3% of annual growth from 2012 to 2017 (IBISWorld 2017). The usage among 18 to 24 year-olds has increased three times, while that among 55 to 65 year-olds doubled during 2013 to 2015 (Pew Research Center 2016). Finding a dating partner and ultimately a marriage partner is one of the most important socioeconomic decisions, and this decision-making process is being altered. Despite the popularity of online dating services, only 1.6% of young generation users in dating apps pay for premium services (Seal 2017). For example, less than 1% of 32 million Tinder users pay for the premium service, known as ‘Tinder Plus’. The majority of online dating services adopt a freemium model where users can register and gain free access, but a premium is charged for additional features and services. Thus, online dating service providers should attract and retain their users and encourage them to convert to premium services. While there is growing interest in studying online dating, previous studies mostly focus on mate selection (Finkel et al. 2012; Hitsch et al. 2010a; Hitsch et al. 2010b). The importance of features in online dating applications (Bapna et al. 2016), and the underlying dynamics of the mate-seeking process and managing two-sided markets in online dating platforms have not been studied yet. Thus, this study 1) will identify the two-sided markets in online dating platforms by investigating access, communication, and matching patterns, 2) examine direct and indirect network effects in terms of access, communication, and matching outcomes, and 3) investigate the mechanisms of network effects. The findings of this study will ultimately provide pricing and user engagement strategies for each market of online dating platform service providers. 互聯網和移動技術改變了我們社會的許多方面，包括人們尋找和建立戀愛關係的方式。在線約會服務，如eHarmony，Match.com，Coffee Meets Bagel和OkCupid已經成為人們尋找合作夥伴的熱門平台，並從根本上改變了約會環境。截至2015年，美國有15％的成年人在線使用 約會服務（Pew Research Center 2016) 。三分之二的在線約會者與他們通過在線約會服務認識的人約會（Pew Research Center 2016)，三分之一的婚姻從網上約會開始（Cacioppo et al 2013)。在線約會服務收入預計將超過30億美元，2012年至2017年的年增長率為5.3％（IBISWorld 2017)。 18至24歲人士的使用量增加了三倍，而55至65歲人士的使用量在2013年至2015年期間上升一倍（Pew Research Center 2016)。尋找約會伴侶並最終成為婚姻伴侶是最重要的社會經濟決策之一，這一決策過程正在被改變。 儘管在線約會服務很受歡迎，但約會應用程序中只有1.6％的年輕一代用戶支付高級服務費用（Seal 2017）。例如，32百萬Tinder用戶中不足1%有支付高級服務費用，稱為“Tinder Plus”。大多數在線約會服務採用免費增值模式，用戶可以註冊並獲得免費 訪問權限，但額外功能和服務收取額外費用。因此，在線約會服務供應商應吸引並留住其用戶並鼓勵他們轉換為高級服務。雖然對在線約會的研究越來越感興趣， 以前的研究主要集中在配偶選擇上（Finkel et al;，2012; Hitsch et al，2010a; Hitsch et al，2010b）。在線約會應用程序中的功能的重要性（Bapna et al 2016），以及在線約會平台中尋找配偶過程和管理兩個市場的潛在動態尚未得到研究。因此，本研究1）將通過調查訪問來識別在線約會平台的雙邊市場，溝通和匹配模式，2）在訪問，溝通和匹配結果方面檢查直接和間接的網絡效應，3）調查 網絡效應機制。本研究的結果將最終為在線約會平台服務提供商的每個市場提供定價和用戶參與策略。

26504318.label: Realisation of objectives
26504318.value: Concurrent with advances in information technology and the en masse relocation of various activities from offline to online channels, online matching platforms have become a disruptive force in many industries. As firms can now provide various IT-enabled features to improve matching, these matching markets require new approaches to market design. Although choice capacity is a key design feature that critically affects market performance, its effect on matching platforms is woefully understudied. I conducted a novel randomized experiment that allows me to examine this question and make a causal inference. Specifically, I design four treatment groups with different choice capacities, in which users can only interact with other users in the same group. Then, I select users who are in a similar age range and live in the same geographical location, and randomly assign users to each treatment group. The design enables me to address the various challenges of the empirical analyses conducted in previous studies. First, by creating an isolated network for each group, this study eliminates potential interference between test groups, which is one of the biggest challenges in matching market experiments. Second, by randomizing the order of the profiles shown to each user in the experiment, this study disentangles the effect of choice capacity from the order effect that might alter the results. The results provide empirical evidence of the four proposed mechanisms through which choice capacity affects user engagement and matching outcomes. First, this study finds competing effects of increasing choice capacity on user engagement. Specifically, the results demonstrate that increasing the choice capacity of one side increases the engagement of that side (i.e., positive same-side effect) but decreases the engagement of the other side (i.e., negative cross-side effect). Second, this study presents different effects of increasing choice capacity on users’ choice behavior (i.e., whom users select) and matching outcomes. More specifically, presented with high choice capacity, female users become less selective (motivated by the competition effect), whereas male users become more selective (motivated by the choice effect). Finally, this study provides practical guidance for the market design of online matching platforms. This study suggests that providing a high choice capacity to the long side (e.g., male users) only is the best strategy to increase user engagement when the market is imbalanced, because the positive same-side effect is larger than the negative cross-side effect only when the choice capacity of the long side is increased. In addition, this study suggests that providing a higher choice capacity to the competition-dominant side (e.g., female users) is the most effective way to increase matching outcomes because the choices made by less selective users result in a higher conversion rate. The findings of this study have both theoretical and practical implications. First, the results suggest that firms should be aware of the fundamental trade-offs of increasing choice capacity when designing their markets. Specifically, increasing the choice capacity of both sides guarantees neither the highest engagement nor the most matching outcomes. Indeed, the findings of the experiment explain why recent dating applications, such as Bumble, have designed their choice capacity to allow only female users to make the first move. In addition, this study presents that a one-size-fits-all choice capacity design that simultaneously results in the highest engagement and most matching outcomes might not exist. Rather, the optimal choice capacity is a function of the market characteristics and motivations that manifest on each side of a platform. Therefore, firms should strategically design choice capacity for optimal engagement and matching outcomes. Second, although this study focuses on the context of online dating platforms, I believe that this work is generalizable beyond that context to other matching platforms. This generalizability stems from the identification of the underlying mechanisms that lead to changes in users’ behavior as the platform increases users’ choice capacity. Specifically, I see the mechanisms of the negative cross-side effect and competition effect happening across the board—ranging from our context of dating to college admissions and, even more broadly, to the labor market. Although the bilateral matching environment allows users to obtain matches that better account for their idiosyncratic preferences (Kanoria and Saban 2019), the literature in this area is sparse. This study spearheads much needed research in this underserved stream of the literature. In conclusion, understanding the effects of choice capacity on engagement and matching outcomes is a crucial step in developing optimal design strategies for matching markets. Through a randomized field experiment, this study enriches the literature on matching market design, two-sided network effects, and online dating by providing a framework of choice capacity and insights into the underlying mechanisms. Thus, this study identifies the two-sided markets in online dating platforms by investigating access, communication, and matching patterns and measures direct network effects and indirect network externalities in terms of access, communication, and matching outcomes. I also empirically examine the boundary conditions that mitigate or amplify direct and indirect network effects on online dating platforms. Finally, this study provides pricing and user engagement strategies of each market for online dating platform service providers.

26504318.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504318.value: I find that providing more choice capacity to male and female users has different effects on choice behaviors and matching outcomes. Although increasing the choice capacity of male users yields the highest engagement, increasing the choice capacity of female users is the most effective method to increase matching outcomes. I posit and empirically demonstrate four mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of different choice capacity designs. Furthermore, I generalize the findings of this study to other online matching platforms and discuss how choice capacity can be designed to increase engagement and matching outcomes. Based on the results of our experiments, this study offers guidelines on how online platforms can design matching markets and suggest choice capacity should be designed differently based on the relative size of the network (i.e., balanced or imbalanced) and whether each side is motivated more strongly by the choice or competition effect. 26504518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504518.value: Knowledge and technological progress are sequential and cumulative. When relevant technologies are sequentially patented, the first patent can be a 'blocking patent' for the second one. This can cause the underuse of technologies after the invention and distort ex ante incentives for innovation and entry in a fast growing technology industry such as the 3D printer industry. The formation of a patent pool, an agreement among patent holders to license their patents to each other or third parties, can resolve the problem. But the empirical model to quantify the effects is not readily available. In this research, we will develop an empirical model of patent overlaps that allows us to quantitatively predict the consequences of hypothetical policies toward patent pool formation. This project will be the first attempt to estimate the parameters of a dynamic oligopoly model with patent overlaps. The novelty will be to integrate several key features. First, complementarity between technologies will be captured by the dependency structure, which in turn will be empirically captured by the citation structure. Second, our model will allow firms to design a product by avoiding a particular set of technologies and using substitute technologies. The success of the alternative product design will eventually be tested in the product market. Third, our model will explicitly incorporate both the knowledge spillover in the upstream technology market and the business stealing effects in the downstream product market. The knowledge spillover will be empirically identified by analyzing the evolution of patented technologies, and the business stealing effects are by analyzing the demand across products. Fourth, the model will incorporate entry and exit of firms with endogenous product design. We will estimate the structural parameters of this model using data from the 3D printer industry. After estimating the model, we will conduct several policy experiments regarding patent pools such as: i) the formation of patent pools within each technology group, ii) and within some but not all of the technology groups, iii) the comparison between the cases where discriminatory pricing across members and non-members are allowed and not allowed, iv) the comparision between the cases where a grant-back policy is considered and not considered. Using this framework, antitrust authorities can assess the welfare impacts, industry groups can convince the authority and licensees of the potential benefits, and firm managers can decide whether to join a patent pool on an empirical ground. 知識和技術的進步是連續和累積的。當相關技術專利申請存在先後次序時，第一項專利可能成為第二項專利的“封鎖專利”。這會導致技術在被發明之後卻未被充分使用，並且扭曲快速增長技術行業中對創新和進入的事前激勵，如3D打印機行業。形成專利共有人聯盟可以解決此問題。專利共有人聯盟是專利持有人之間允許彼此或第三方使用其專利的協議。 但目前還未有現成的經驗模型可以量化此影響。在這項研究中，我們將建立一個關於專利重疊的經驗模型，來定量預測假設的政策對專利聯盟形成的影響。 這個課題將是對加入專利重疊的動態寡頭模型的參數估計的首次嘗試。它的創新之處在于整合了以下關鍵要素。首先，技術互補被模型的依賴結構所刻畫，而依賴結構又被引用結構所經驗地刻畫。其次，我們的模型將允許企業通過設計某種產品來避免某些特定技術並使用替代技術。替代產品的設計是否成功最終將在產品市場中進行檢驗。第三，我們的模型將顯性地結合上游技術市場的知識溢出和下游產品市場中的商業竊取效應。知識溢出將通過分析專利技術的發展演變來經驗地識別，而商業竊取效應則通過分析各類產品的需求來經驗地識別。第四，該模型將引入有内生產品設計的企業的進入和退出。 我們將使用來自3D打印機行業的數據來估計該模型的結構參數。在估算模型後，我們將對專利聯盟進行若干政策試驗，例如：i）每個技術組內專利聯盟的形成，ii) 在一些但不是所有技術組內專利聯盟的形成，iii) 比較允許和不允許成員和非成員之間歧視性定價的情形， iv）比較考慮和不考慮回贈政策的情形。 使用這個框架，反壟斷機構可以評估對福利的影響，行業團體可以使權威機構和被許可人相信潛在的益處，而企業管理者可以決定是否加入專利聯盟，這些判斷都基於實證基礎。

26504518.label: Realisation of objectives
26504518.value: We fully achieved objectives 1, 3, 4, and 5. We developed an empirical model of oligopoly pricing with patent overlaps and successfully estimated the model parameters using a dataset from the 3D printer industry. Based on the estimated model, we performed several counterfactual simulations to evaluate the impacts of patent pool formation on the welfare and the social and private return of inventing patented technologies. Because we found the variation in the data is not rich enough to identify the high-dimensional transition of patent ownership, we gave up to develop a fully dynamic model. Because we gave up to develop a fully dynamic model, the transition of patent ownership and dependency structure in the second objective became no longer relevant for the analysis. For objective 6, we evaluated the welfare impacts of the industry-wide patent pool but did not have enough time to explore a wider class of patent pools by the deadline. Currently, we are working on the evaluation of the company-to-company cross licensing.

26504518.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504518.value: A high-tech industry often suﬀers from the ineﬃciencies rooted in overlapping patent rights, such as the so-called “tragedy of anti-commons” and raising rivals’ costs eﬀects. Separating patents and forming a patent pool can resolve some problems, but doing so may also increase the licensor’s power. To evaluate these policies, we develop a Nash-in-Nash oligopoly model with patent overlaps and apply it to industrial three-dimensional (3D) printers using data for 1997–2016, a case that likely demonstrates patent overlaps. Using counterfactual simulations, we found multiple implications. 1) Setting up an independent patent pool could increase the total surplus by 5.1%. However, vertical separation increased the total surplus by 7.6% without pooling. The diﬀerence was due to the increase in the licensor’s market power in the patent pool. 2) Taking stereolithography technology as an example, we found that the social return of patented technologies was greater under vertical separation. Still, the private return to the licensor could also be greater under patent pooling depending on the transfer mechanism. 3) If the pool shared revenue according to the number of patents, the private return for the inventor was too small to prompt him or her to join the pool. As a result, the inventor would have remained an outsider to the pool. Our model thus enables the empirical assessment of various policy questions regarding patent pools.

26504518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504518.value: The paper has multiple limitations. First, the model is static, and the evaluation of ine?ciency is after the patent, its ownership, and product design are all ?xed. Although we attempted to quantify the social and private returns of inventing patents by ?xing all of the other products and patents, fully evaluating the dynamic implications of patent overlaps and patent pools would require endogenously characterizing the intensity and direction of innovation and product design. This will allow us to evaluate the total welfare impacts of a patent pool. Second, the patent royalty is estimated under the assumptions of the Nash-in-Nash model. Directly obtaining patent royalty data and evaluating the implications of patent pooling would be the next step. For example, we may be able to use data from the patent royalty information of the DVD patent pool. This will allow us to compare the actual patent royalty with the estimated patent royalty from my model.

26504518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504518.value: A high-tech industry such as the 3D printer industry is often trapped in a web of patent ownership. For many reasons, this complicated patent ownership structure can lead to excessively high patent royalty and result in the excessively high prices of products that use the patented technologies. For example, if a rival manufacturer uses your patent, you may want to raise the patent royalty to increase the rival's cost. Or, if you increase the patent royalty, a manufacturer that used your patent may stop production. This can damage other licensors whose patent was used by this manufacturer. In theory, we can use some remedies such as separating the intellectual property and production departments and pooling patents to resolve part of these problems. However, there was no way to quantitatively evaluate the impacts of these policies. We proposed an approach to assess the impacts of these policies and demonstrated using the data from the 3D printer industry that they could have substantially improved the industry inefficiency.

26504918.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26504918.value: 自由职业中的角色扩展和性别歧视：多重方法研究

26504918.label: Project Objectives
26504918.value: To understand the challenges associated with freelance careers To understand the social or structural constraints on role expansion To understand gender biases in freelance careers

26504918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504918.value: Flexible work practices, such as freelancing, have become prevalent in the past few decades. Despite this change, we know little about the challenges in these new forms of work arrangement and how individual workers navigate these challenges. In this proposal, we focus on two aspects: role expansion and gender discrimination. Expansion of work roles has been an important part of career advancement. As people develop in their careers, they expand their roles and obtain more responsibility in their work. Unlike traditional work arrangements in which organized career ladders helped workers to expand their work roles, freelancers need to claim new work roles. Yet this is made difficult because freelancers lack the legitimacy to claim new roles convincingly. This is especially so for female freelancers, who normally face discrimination in their careers. In this proposal, I document a preliminary finding in the careers of popular Korean songwriters where female songwriters consistently remain role-specialists more than male songwriters do. Then I propose multiple controlled laboratory experiments and one natural experiment in Korea that can be leveraged to elaborate the causal mechanism in which female freelancers are penalized in their effort to expand work roles. 灵活的工作方式在过去几十年里变得日益普遍，例如自由职业。尽管如此，我们对于这种新的工作形式中的挑战和个体工作者如何应对这些挑战还了解甚少。在这一研究计划中，我们主要关注两个方面：角色扩展和性别歧视。角色扩展是职业发展的重要环节。随着人们在职业路径上前进，其角色也随之扩展，并且要在工作中承担更多职责。在传统的工作形式中，既有的职业阶梯能够帮助工作者扩展其角色；与此不同的是，自由职业者却需要自己定义新的工作角色。但这对自由职业者并不容易，因为他们缺乏自我定义新角色的合法性。对于遭受性别歧视的女性自由职业者而言，这一问题尤为突出。在这一研究计划中，我记录了有关韩国流行音乐作曲家职业生涯的初步发现：相比于男性作曲家，女性作曲家的角色始终更加局限。接下来我提出多个实验室控制实验和一个自然实验的方法，用来解释女性自由职业者因角色扩展而受到惩罚的因果机制。

26504918.label: Realisation of objectives
26504918.value: Three objectives of this project have been achieved through three stages. First, I have been doing extensive interviews with Korean popular music songwriters whose career evolves as freelancing. The objective of this explorative interview format was to understand the challenges associated with their career considering that there are no firms or agencies that help them find new job opportunities. The interviews revealed that songwriters were concerned about where the next job opportunities would come from and used collaboration with other peers as a way to exchange job opportunities. In other words, freelancing songwriters were concerned about their survival in a precarious career. A primary way to navigate through this challenge was to expand work roles to access job opportunities for multiple roles. Second, we collected an extensive dataset that helped us understand the chance of songwriters' survival as a function of role expansion. The key objective, here, was to test the insights we gained from our interviews. We found that role expansion helped men's career, but not women's. Finally, we conducted a series of experiments to develop a design to test gender bias for female freelancers. We found that women who expanded their work role received discounts in explaining their extent of agency in their decision, and such a discount contributed to gender difference in the level of competence and commitment of the female freelancers. All these resulted in a manuscript titled, "The Glass Wall and the Gendered Evaluation of Role Expansion in Freelancing Careers" which is now accepted for publication in the Academy of Management Journal, a flagship journal of our field.

26504918.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504918.value: Across three studies using different methods (archival data and experiment), industries (music and film), and samples (Korean and American), I find female freelancers who expand into a new work role are less likely to get next work opportunities compared with men who did the same. Furthemore, women who expanded their roles are seen as less agentic than men who expand. Although women who pursue careers outside of organizations may become unshackled from gender biases embedded within traditional organizational hierarchies, I suggest that they still face substantial obstacles in the new forms of work.

26504918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504918.value: I believe that the next step in my research is to investigate how pervasive the glass wall is in not only freelancing careers, but also in other forms of careers that gives people greater autonomy in deciding when, what, and with whom they would work.

26504918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504918.value: While women often take freelancing careers to gain control over when, what, and with whom they would work to avoid muscular corporate culture and balance their professional and personal lives. However, in doing so, women face a new challenge. While taking multiple work roles is integral to keeping freelancing careers afloat, women who take multiple work roles are seen less agentic than men. This leads women to be seen less competent and committed, and eventually find themselves exposed more to the perils of freelancing careers than men do. We call this the glass wall, which discounts women who are trying to advance their freelancing careers and may even further prevent women from expanding their work roles.

26505518.label: Project Objectives
26505518.value: Deepen our understanding of crypto currencies. Understand how crypto currencies affect money creation.
rows: Deepen our understanding of crypto currencies.
Understand how crypto currencies affect money creation.

26505518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505518.value: The rise of crypto currencies such as Bitcoin has led to an increased level of speculation that the structure of the financial sector will soon undergo dramatic change. We examine the consequences of such upheaval. In particular, we build a general model in which fiat money and crypto currencies exist side-by-side. In the model, traditional banks and "crypto" banks compete in the credit market. Traditional banks can create money whereas crypto banks cannot. Because crypto banks' lending cannot exceed their deposits, we prove they have stronger incentives to screen their potential borrowers. Consequently, traditional banks face a lower quality borrower pool and respond by reducing their loan supply. We show there exist positive NPV projects which would be financed absent crypto banks. We characterize the environments under which the introduction of crypto banks is welfare improving. 比特币等加密货币的兴起引发越来越多的猜测，金融业结构将发生巨大变化。本文研究这种变革的结果。具体地说，我们建立一个法定货币与加密货币并存的通用模型。在该模型中，传统银行和“加密”银行在信贷市场中竞争。传统银行可以发行货币但加密银行不能。因为加密银行的贷款不能超过其储蓄，可证明加密银行有更强烈的动机对借款人进行筛选。因此，传统银行将面临资质较低的借款人群，因而减少贷款供给。我们发现存在一些NPV为正的项目，在没有加密银行的情况下获得融资。我们进而讨论了在哪些环境条件下引入加密银行可以改善社会福利。

26505518.label: Realisation of objectives
26505518.value: In our view, our research paper -- although still in the process of being finalized for submission to a top journal -- achieves both objectives laid out in the initial proposal. On the first objective, we have built a novel model of crypto currencies and the mining process (which is how money is created in the crypto-world). First, the model demonstrates that if there are small inefficiencies in the hashing algorithm that underpins crypto-mining, then large players have win rates that exceed what conventional wisdom (typically thought to be their share of aggregate computing power). That is, small imperfections in cryptocurrencies may give rise to economies of scale in crypto-mining. Second, these large players have longer solving times on average than their smaller competitors. We find supporting evidence for the latter prediction using bitcoin data (the first prediction is untestable because one cannot observe market shares of computing power). On the second objective, our model also suggests that these economies of scale may in part motivate an arms race in crypto-mining. In particular, because large players win at greater rates than their share of aggregate computing power, miners have stronger incentives to invest in computing power. However, since all miners face the same set of incentives, this leads to greater aggregate investment in computing power than what would be predicted by traditional models. Consequently, small inefficiencies in the hashing algorithm might (help) explain why massive amounts of energy are spent mining (i.e. creating money) the various proof-of-work cryptocurrencies (e.g. bitcoin) around the world. We acknowledge that the paper attached (and the model used) is quite different than what was discussed in the initial proposal and the midterm report. There are two primary reasons for the deviation. First, although we were able to put together a working model similar in spirit to the framework described in the initial proposal, (i) we found certain assumptions to be not particularly desirable, and (ii) the idea of a "crypto-bank" -- something which seemed imminent at the time of the proposal's writing -- is still yet to truly materialize in practice. Second, during the course of our research into money creation and cryptocurrencies, we uncovered a slightly different angle which in our view (i) stays true to the objectives of the project (as explained above), and (ii) produces more insightful, provocative, and potentially impactful results. Hence, we chose to go this route. However, since we made these adjustments relatively late in the process (after the midterm report), we have yet to submit the project to a journal (we are currently in discussion with cryptography experts about certain aspects of the model).

26505518.label: Major findings and research outcome
26505518.value: We find that when the hashing algorithm underpinning a cryptocurrency exhibits small inefficiencies (inefficiencies which do not necessarily violate core design principals of hashing functions) large players in crypto-mining successfully mine blocks at rates that significantly exceed traditional models. These win rates can be understood as the consequence of within-block-learning, and give rise to endogenous economies of scale in crypto-mining. Our model predicts that large players should take longer on average to mine blocks (providing inefficiencies are non-trivial), a fact we find supporting evidence for using bitcoin data. Finally, our model offers a novel explanation for the large amounts of energy that are used in mining bitcoin and other proof-of-work cryptocurrencies.

26505518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26505518.value: We are currently in the process of reaching out and talking to cryptography (i.e. non-finance) experts about our findings. We are hoping to bring one on board and add further supporting evidence to some of the assumptions that underpin our model. Once the working paper is polished we hope to submit to a top journal.

26505518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26505518.value: We challenge a common assumption made about cryptocurrencies; that hashing functions (a key technology underpinning crypto) are "perfectly random". We find that small deviations from this assumption might have large consequences. In particular, we show that inefficiencies in the hashing function favour large players, affect the timing and creation of new blocks on the blockchain, and potentially help explain why those involved in mining cryptocurrency are willing to invest such large amounts of energy resources.

26505818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26505818.value: This study will investigate the impact of borrowing managers and loan officers on debt contracting. I plan to identify borrowing managers and loan officers in corporate loans, and track their debt contracting history and contracting terms from 1994 to 2016. I propose that corporate loans have lower loan spreads, larger amounts, longer maturities, lower likelihood of being secured, and less covenant restrictions: (i) when borrowing managers have borrowing experience and financial expertise, (ii) when loan officers have lending experience and industry expertise, and (iii) when borrowing managers and loan officers have cooperated before in other loans. My study provides novel evidence that borrowing managers and loan officers play important roles to help lower information asymmetry and communication costs. 本研究将调查借款经理和贷款人员在债务契约中的作用。 我计划在公司贷款中识别借款经理和贷款人员，并追踪他们的借贷历史和合同条款。当（i）借款经理具有借款经验和财务专业知识，（ii）贷款经理有贷款经验和行业专业知识，以及（iii）借款经理和贷款经理之前曾在其他贷款中合作过时，我预期发现公司贷款的贷款利差较低，金额较大，期限较长，有更低的担保可能性和更少的契约限制。 我的研究 会证明借款经理和贷款人员可以发挥重要作用，降低信息不对称性和沟通成本。

We find that borrowing managers’ relationship with the loan officer helps to resolve information asymmetry in loan contracting, and it reduces the loan spread. 26505818.label: Major findings and research outcome
26505818.value: In this paper, we examine the significance and uniqueness of the individual-pair relationship cultivated through repeated loan interactions by the firm’s borrowing manager and the bank’s loan officer. Using a hand-collected dataset of borrowing manager and loan officer information, we find that individual-pair relationship loans reduce the cost of debt between 7-27 basis points. We also document that the economic impact of individual-pair lending relationships exists even when other types of relationships, e.g., institutional pairs, social ties, cultural proximity and gender, are taken into consideration. Lastly, we find evidence that individual-pair relationships are especially important when either the firm has a high level of information asymmetry, the bank is smaller, or loan officers have slimmer portfolios. Cumulatively, our results highlight the value of sustained professional engagement between two individuals in the lending process.

This paper also got accepted into the 2022 American Accounting Association annual conference.

26506518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26506518.value: In this project, I seek to identify the network mechanisms underlying the network formation process among Chinese suppliers in the global mobile handset industry. Given the dispersed, opaque nature of global supply chains, this project seeks to provide a better understanding about the impact of supply chain visibility, which can be defined as “the identity, location and status of entities transiting the supply chain, captured in timely messages about events” (Francis, 2008: 182). More Specifically, I will investigate how a sudden increase in network visibility – captured through a spike in the volume of social media posts about nodes or dyads in the company’s supply chain network – changes firm behavior and subsequent network structures. When a certain node or dyad of a firm’s supplier base faces such an increase in exposure, how will firms’ networking patterns change? Given the recursive nature of social actions and social structures (Giddens, 1984), I will explore how social structures constrain actors’ underlying networking patterns, and how actors modify social structures by changing their previous networking patterns. To test my arguments, I will combine social media data with original component-level supply chains data, and employ a series of stochastic actor-oriented network simulations to rigorously detect the supply chain network dynamics. Specifically, I intend to look at how posts on Chinese social media affects supply chain network dynamics among Chinese suppliers in the global mobile handset industry. This project will use social media posts, specifically co-mentions on social media posts, to capture supply chain visibility. Co-mentions, references to more than one firm in the same article, are shown to be a way of observing the association between firms. Co-mentions are a good proxy to show that covered companies are embedded in a market network, which also reflects how people are defining and interpreting the market concept as a whole (Kennedy, 2008; Navis & Glynn, 2010). The salience or strength of the association limits the dilution of information pertaining to evaluation (Vergne, 2012). In a sense, co-mentions of firms in social media posts proxy the cognitive social structure, or the perceived image of a company’s interfirm relationships. Therefore, my core argument is that the increase in co-mentions of select parts of supply chain networks may capture an increase in the visibility of the supply chain, which may lead to changes in firms’ network mechanisms. 在過去數十年的主流商業趨勢之一是將主要的業務活動外判給供應商和承判商。供應鏈逐漸變得更長、更分散和更複雜。在這個提案中，我尋求識別中國供應商在全球手機行業的網絡形成過程中的網絡機制。此提案旨在更好地了解供應鏈可視性的影響。更具體地說，我將研究網絡可視性的突然增長如何改變公司行為和後續的網絡結構。

26506518.label: Major findings and research outcome
26506518.value: In one study, using empirical data on supply chain networks of three global automotive manufacturers and a series of computational experiments, we study what makes supply chain networks robust to shocks that simultaneously disable multiple participating organizations. As the ravaging COVID-19 pandemic has illuminated, global supply chain networks can be extremely vulnerable to shocks — such as pandemics, natural disasters, or social and political unrest — that lead to the shutdown of multiple suppliers at once. This study shows how small changes in buyers’ choices of new suppliers can make the emergent global supply chain network significantly more robust to such disruptions. In doing so, we adopt a complex systems perspective in which there is no central network architect, and thousands of organizations make individual decisions regarding their suppliers without considering or even observing the robustness of the global network. Our results reveal that even when a small fraction (5%) of companies in a globally dispersed supply chain network replace one supplier per year based on geographical proximity (to the buyer or to the buyer’s current suppliers), the emergent supply chain network can become significantly more robust. Such regionalizing supplier-selection strategies largely outperform globalizing supplier-selection practices (selecting geographically distant suppliers) for shocks that diffuse through land borders (e.g., social or political unrest) or via air travel (e.g., pandemics). In another study, drawing on the extant research on attention, visibility, and reputation, I study firms’ responses to labor unrest targeting their direct component suppliers in the mobile phone industry. Recent research suggests the opacity of global supply chains, particularly firms’ inability to completely trace their production process, is the main reason firms are unable to make their supply chains accountable. Globally dispersed supply chains give firms the ability to deny or ignore labor unrest in their supply chain, since most external stakeholders do not have the ability to link a firm with its suppliers. The main findings demonstrate that social media both enables greater visibility and amplifies the potential impact of labor unrest in supply chains, as it enables external stakeholders to closely link brand names with labor issues in their supply chain, making the buyer–supplier tie salient in their mind. The study’s findings suggest that external supply chain visibility can shed light on supply chain dynamics in the aftermath of suppliers’ labor unrest.

26506518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26506518.value: Building a comprehensive strategy for supply chain network robustness and resilience should be among the firm’s central organizational objectives. Unfortunately, both research and practice on network robustness and resilience are fragmented and have yet to be interconnected. Future research can thus explore how a comprehensive strategy in this area could rest on such key formative elements as: a company’s inter-organizational relationships, both active and potentially available as substitutes; the depth and breadth of its human capital; formal systems and procedures; cultural readiness; and the organization’s financial and physical resources.

26506518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26506518.value: How can global supply chains continue operations in the face of disruptions —pandemics, natural and human made disasters, social and political unrest — that can cause multiple suppliers to shut down their operations at once? Our research indicates that even if some buyers occasionally choose geographically proximate suppliers, the resultant global supply chain network becomes significantly more likely to withstand such disruptions.
