27112518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27112518.value: Background Health care spending has increased faster than economic growth in Hong Kong and the rest of China. Identifying avoidable costs for chronic diseases such as diabetes is a pressing concern in a rapidly ageing society. Effective treatment and adherence to best practice could mitigate the future economic burden of diabetes. Objectives We aim to determine the avoidable direct health care costs of diabetes and the avoidable indirect costs in terms of lost economic output from 2006 to 2016; and project the likely avoidable health care costs and impact on economic growth over the next 20 years. Participants People with diabetes identified from the Hospital Authority Clinical Management System covering publically provided services in Hong Kong. Methods We conduct economic analysis comparing several scenarios ranging from a base case of no change to alternatives assuming full adherence to the Hong Kong diabetes reference framework risk factor targets. The avoidable health care cost of diabetes is the reduction in spending from health improvements under the alternative scenarios. We use a publically available simulation tool to estimate future health care costs accounting for demographic ageing, behavioural lifestyle changes and medical inflation. We use a human capital approach to calculate the lost economic output from 2006 to 2016 by deriving the number of sick days attributable to diabetes, and the time off work from employed care givers. We use the average wage rate to calculate the lost wages, and the GDP per employee to calculate the lost economic output. To project future economic growth, we use a production function that models the health effects on GDP output. We include health status, and government projections of labour force size, capital stock, educational level and total factor productivity in the model parameters. Health status is proxied by quality-adjusted life expectancy. The avoidable loss of economic output is the difference in economic output between the base case and alternative scenarios. Outcomes The main outcomes are the avoidable health costs and loss in economic growth due to diabetes from 2006 to 2036. Impact This study assesses the likely economic impact of clinical guidelines for diabetes, and provides direct evidence to assist local authorities in health care planning. This could guide possible population level strategies for the rest of China. 背景 近年來，中國大陸和香港的醫療開支升幅均超越經濟增長，在人口急速老化的背景下，識別出長期疾病（如糖尿病）的可避免成本急不容緩。有效的治療能令糖尿病人的病情受控並達預期指標，更可能減少糖尿病對香港未來的經濟負擔。 目的 我們希望找出香港於2006至2016年因糖尿病導致的直接和間接可避免成本，並以此預測於未來二十年，糖尿病將引發的可避免成本及其對香港經濟發展的影響。 研究數據 數據取自醫院管理局的臨床管理系統，對象為曾接受醫院管理局治療的糖尿病患者。 方法 我們將參考《香港糖尿病參考概覽》中對糖尿病風險因素的控制指引，模擬香港的糖尿病人於「維持現狀」、「部分達標」和「完全達標」等情況下引發的可避免成本，和其對本地經濟發展的影響。 可避免成本指現時情況與模擬情景中的成本差別，可分爲直接和間接兩部分：在「直接成本」方面，我們將考慮人口老化、大衆生活方式轉變和醫療費用上漲等因素，透過公開的模擬工具估計糖尿病引發的醫療開支。「間接成本」即香港因糖尿病而損失的經濟產出，我們將使用人力資本法，透過香港的平均薪金及人均國内生產總值，計算出病人和照顧者因工作時間減少而導致的工資及經濟產出損失，並以此估算由2006-16年間糖尿病對香港經濟產出的影響。 在預測糖尿病對香港未來經濟發展的影響方面，我們將考慮人民健康狀況（以素質調整壽命年估計）、政府估算的勞動人口、生產力因素、人力資本和教育水平等因素，透過生產函數估算人民健康程度對國内生產總值的影響。 研究結果 本研究旨在找出香港由2006到2036年因糖尿病導致的可避免支出及其對經濟發展的影響。 研究對社會的貢獻 本研究將探討糖尿病臨床指引對經濟的影響。研究結果能提供客觀直接的證據，以協助有關當局制定醫療政策，中國大陸亦能參考結果制定大衆層面的醫療策略。

27112518.label: Realisation of objectives
27112518.value: Objective 1: We used representative sampling of Hong Kong's territory-wide public healthcare system records (Hospital Authority) to derive incremental health spending attributable to type 2 diabetes care. We randomly sampled patients aged 30 or above, with at least one contact (inpatient, ambulatory, emergency care) with publicly provided healthcare services (in 2017). Patient data included demographic information, diagnosis dates for diabetes and comorbidities, and health utilisation (including inpatient, general and specialist ambulatory care, and emergency care). The presence of type 2 diabetes and comorbidities were based on diagnosis codes from 2007 to 2017 records. We aggregated total medical expenditures in 2017 by applying unit prices from public sector charges for non- eligible persons; these rates are set at a cost- recovery basis. Mean annual cost was capped at USD 100,000. To model annual medical spending, we fitted a generalised linear model with diabetes status, years living with diabetes and its square, age and age-squared and interaction terms between diabetes status and age and age-squared, sex and medical conditions. Specification tests supported the use of the log link and gamma distribution for the generalised linear model. We took natural logarithms of the dependent variable (healthcare expenditures) as the Box–Cox test showed the distribution is close to symmetric. We performed a modified Park test to determine a gamma variance function, this distribution accounts for increasing variance with higher medical spending. A human capital approach was used to calculate the indirect cost, measured by the lost productivity in the formal workforce. Data of labour force, monthly employment earnings, labour force participation rate, and average work day were extracted from government reports and census data in 2017. We excluded people aged 65 or above from this analysis as 65 is the official retirement age for civil servants in Hong Kong. Given the shortness of evidence on the division of the labour force into full- or part-time employment by disease status, all employees were assumed to be in full-time employment. We applied the regression model to the type 2 diabetes population in 2017 to predict annual medical spending for individuals with diabetes. By using the same sample population but setting the diabetes status variable to zero, we predict annual medical spending for these individuals if diabetes were eliminated. The mean of the difference between these two predicted values provides an estimate of per-person medical spending attributable to type 2 diabetes. This counterfactual analysis ensures comparable population characteristics between those with and without diabetes to isolate the incremental effect of diabetes on healthcare expenditure. Confidence intervals were estimated using 1000 bootstrap iterations with statistical analyses conducted using SAS and R. Objective 2: We developed a health outcomes model - Chinese Hong Kong Integrated Modeling and Evaluation (CHIME) from a population-based cohort of individuals with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes: Hong Kong Clinical Management System (CMS, 97,628 participants) from 2006 to 2017 and externally validated against CHARLS cohort and 9 published trials. CMS is one of the largest Chinese electronic health informatics systems with detailed clinical records. CHARLS was chosen for external validation as it is a nationally representative longitudinal cohort of middle-aged and elderly Chinese residents age 45 and older. We validated against 6 outcomes measures recorded in the CHARLS data and an additional 80 endpoints from 9 published trials of diabetes patients using simulated cohorts of 100,000 individuals. The CHIME simulation model comprises of 13 risk equations to predict mortality, micro- and macrovascular complications, and development of diabetes. The modelling outcomes include cumulative incidence and time to onset of complications, life expectancy, quality-adjusted life expectancy, direct costs arising from treatment of diabetes-related complications. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of articles reporting utility and disutility values for diabetes and its related complications in East and Southeast Asia. Identified studies were assessed for quality based on the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence guidelines. Utility and disutility estimates were pooled by meta-analyses with subgroup analyses to evaluate differences by nationality and valuation instrument. We identified 17 studies for the systematic review from a total of 13035 studies in the initial search, of which 13 studies met the quality criteria for inclusion in the meta-analyses. Immediate control of risk factors (American Diabetes Association guidelines) was compared to current baseline levels to estimate differences in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and treatment costs (2020 USD). Analyses were performed in the full population of people with type 2 diabetes in Hong Kong. Risk factor control was defined by Hong Kong reference framework, Chinese Diabetes Society and American Diabetes Association guidelines on glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) targets <7% (53 mmol/mol), blood pressure <130/80 mmHg, and LDL-cholesterol <2.6 mmol/L. These recommendations are comparable to Singapore and UK. Four scenarios were simulated: individual control of glycaemia, blood pressure, cholesterol and multifactorial (all three risk factors) combined. The impact of inadequate risk factor control was evaluated by comparing immediate control (values of risk factors were assumed to reach the corresponding target at the first year) to constant baseline levels over a 20-year time horizon. Quality-adjustment of life years was calculated by taking the baseline utility value for type 2 diabetes without complications and adding disutility for each occurring conditions to create annual utility values for each individual. Utility values for diabetes without complications were taken from a published meta-analysis of Asian participants. The annual direct medical costs associated with diabetes-related complications in the year of event and subsequent years in Hong Kong were derived from published sources. Direct medical costs of managing diabetes and related complications were calculated from a healthcare provider perspective and inflated to 2020 US dollars (USD) using the implicit price deflator of gross domestic product (GDP) published by Census and Statistics Department. We applied a discount rate of 3% for costs and benefits. Analyses were conducted using R (v4.0.3). Objective 3: We apply a standardized methodology for estimating the net value of changes in medical spending, with population specific risk prediction models to account for the over-prediction of cardiovascular events and death when western-based models are applied to Asian populations. This method measures value using a “cost-of-living” approach that is analogous to a cost-effectiveness analysis comparing outcomes in the baseline and final periods, assigning a monetary value to life-years gained, and then subtracting the added costs of care. We referred the indirect cost to money loss owing to absenteeism, the number of work days missed due to poor health conditions among employed individuals. Absenteeism was estimated by the length of stay (LOS) in the health care services including the accident and emergency service (A&E), the family medicine specialist clinics (FMSC), the general outpatient clinics (GOPC), the specialist outpatient clinics (SOPC), and the inpatient hospitalisation service. The total LOS of each person was calculated as the addition of days spent in each of the above services. Money loss was estimated by multiplying the individual-level LOS with the age-specific average daily wage and labour participation rate in 2017. The average daily wage was the age-specific median of monthly employment earnings dividing the monthly average work day (25 days). We applied a microsimulation modelling approach using the CHIME (Chinese Hong Kong Integrated Modelling and Evaluation) model to estimate the projected health and economic burden for each participant with diabetes.

27112518.label: Major findings and research outcome
27112518.value: 1. We developed a health outcomes model from a population-based cohort of individuals with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes. The Chinese Hong Kong Integrated Modeling and Evaluation (CHIME) simulation model comprises of 13 risk equations to predict mortality, micro- and macrovascular complications, and development of diabetes. Our study shows the CHIME model is a validated tool for predicting progression diabetes and its outcomes, particularly among Chinese and East Asian populations. 2. We developed a recommended set of pooled disutility and utility estimates for type 2 diabetes without complication and 17 diabetes-related complications for use in quality-of-life measurements and economic evaluation. The pooled utility value for diabetes without complication was 0.88 (95% CI 0.83-0.93), with the pooled utility decrement for associated complications ranged from 0.00 (for excess BMI) to 0.18 (for amputation). 3. The incremental mean annual healthcare expenditure for a person with diabetes was USD 3739. The incremental spending attributable to diabetes was 36.5% of total annual medical expenditure. In other words, spending for patients with diabetes is 1.57 times greater than for a person without diabetes. Patients with diabetes had higher annual medical expenditures than their non-diabetes equivalent groups at all ages. The annual incremental medical expenditure attributed to diabetes is greater as years since diabetes diagnosis increased: under 5 years (USD 2808), 5-9 years (USD 3297), 10-14 years (USD 3980), 15-19 years (USD 4869), and greater than 20 years (USD 5664). 4. Analyzing over 600,000 patient-years of medical utilization, spending, and biomarker-based health outcomes, we find a small but statistically and economically meaningful positive net value of spending on diabetes management across four distinct health systems: Japan, The Netherlands, Hong Kong and Taiwan. This finding implies a positive net value of diabetes care: the value of improved survival outweighs the added costs of care in each of the four health systems. 5. Analyzing a nationally representative survey conducted in 2018-19 (n = 24,319), 69.1% (95% CI: 67.7-70.5) achieved optimal diabetes control (HbA1c <7% [53 mmol/mol]), 27.7% [26.1-29.3] achieved blood pressure control (<130/80 mmHg) and 20.1% (18.6-21.6) achieved both targets. Achieving 70% control rate for people with diabetes could reduce deaths before age 70 by 7.1% (5.7-8.7), reduce medical costs by 14.9% (12.3-18.0), and gain 50.4 QALYs (44.8-56.0) per 1,000 people over 10 years compared to the baseline status quo. Substantial health gains and economic savings are potentially achievable with better risk factor control especially in rural settings.

27112518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

27124318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27124318.value: Anthropogenic climate change is predicted to be a major cause of species extinctions in the next 100 years by posing novel selection pressures for natural populations. Theoretically, species can respond to this major threat by (i) migrating to newly suitable areas; (ii) by plastic adjustments and/or (iii) by adaptive evolution. However, habitat fragmentation and the existence of great environmental fluctuations through broad geographical ranges, constrain the availability of suitable habitats to disperse, and therefore, species are forced to adjust to the shifts in environmental conditions by means of plastic or genetic responses. Under this context, broad-scale environmental changes, such as the ocean warming (OW) and acidification (OA), are of major concern due to their intensity and rapid rise during the last century. Despite of this, we know little about the potential and real capacity of marine species to cope with these changes. Mass extinction events in the past, due to the rise in CO2, temperature and the decrease of ocean’s pH, have shaped the evolution and diversification of marine species. How will these rapid environmental changes influence the ecology and evolution of marine organisms in the future?. Empirical evidences of micro-evolutionary responses (i.e., genetic) to OW and OA are scarce, mainly because most of the studies are purely phenotypic, and therefore, unable to separate plastic responses from genetic responses. In this project, I propose to study the phenotypic plasticity (thermal reaction norms and transcriptomic profiles) and adaptive potentials (genetic architectures) of tropical marine organisms under a multi-stressors context. Several authors have predicted a greater impact of climate change on tropical species because they are considered more narrowly endemic in both geographic and climatic space, likely as result of the reduced seasonality in the tropics. By integrating different approaches (comparative physiology, quantitative-genetics and transcriptomics) this project aims to identify (i) the mechanisms that help to explain the ecological and evolutionary responses of tropical marine species to climate change; and (ii) to reveal the molecular and genetic factors involved in the tolerance to environmental stress in these organisms. This information will ultimately provide tools and approaches that are required to be incorporated into management programmes designed to minimize biodiversity loss under rapid climate change. 通過對自然種群構成新的選擇壓力，人為氣候變化預計將成為未來100年物種滅絕的主要原因。從理論上講，物種可以通過（i）遷移到新的適宜區域來應對這一主要威脅; （ii）通過塑料調整和/或（iii）通過適應性演變。然而，棲息地破碎化以及在廣泛的地理範圍內存在巨大的環境波動，限制了適當的棲息地的分散，因此，物種被迫通過塑料或遺傳反應來適應環境條件的變化。在這種背景下，海洋變暖（OW）和酸化（OA）等大範圍環境變化由於其強度和上個世紀的迅速上升而成為主要關注點。儘管如此，我們對海洋物種應對這些變化的潛力和實際能力知之甚少。由於二氧化碳，溫度升高和海洋pH降低，過去的大規模滅絕事件已經形成了海洋物種的演變和多樣化。這些快速的環境變化將如何影響未來海洋生物的生態和進化？對OW和OA的微進化反應（即遺傳）的經驗證據很少，主要是因為大多數研究純粹是表型，因此無法將塑料反應與遺傳反應分開。在這個項目中，我建議研究多壓力環境下熱帶海洋生物的表型可塑性（熱反應規範和轉錄組學特徵）和適應性潛力（遺傳結構）。一些作者預測氣候變化對熱帶物種的影響更大，因為它們在地理和氣候空間中被認為是更為狹隘的地方性，可能是由於熱帶地區的季節性減少。通過整合不同的方法（比較生理學，定量遺傳學和轉錄組學），該項目旨在確定（i）有助於解釋熱帶海洋物種對氣候變化的生態和進化反應的機制; （ii）揭示這些生物體對環境脅迫的耐受性所涉及的分子和遺傳因素。這些信息最終將提供需要納入管理計劃的工具和方法，旨在最大限度地減少氣候變化帶來的生物多樣性喪失。

27124318.label: Realisation of objectives
27124318.value: This project included three main objectives that were designed for field and lab work in Hong Kong and Australia. Unfortunately, challenges due to social unrest in Hong Kong (2019-2020) and COVID (2019-2022), delayed or constrained many of the original plans. Protests erupted in June 2019 (https://time.com/5726446/cuhk-chinese-university-hong-kong) and the University was occupied by rioters, which disrupted most academic and scientific activities for several months. Then, COVID hit and travel restrictions made it impossible to visit Australia to lead the field and laboratory work comparing populations as initially planned. Despite these challenges, we were able to successfully complete the project and generate impact through the formation of new scientists, and the presentation of findings in scientific meetings and in peer-reviewed journals. All three objectives were fully completed and have deliverables associated, particularly for the first two. Papers linked to objective 3 are under development and supported by a thesis that was finalized last year. Objective three was completed and the main manuscript derived is under development. Findings from this objective have been presented in three international meetings where the PI of this project was invited as keynote speaker (12th International Phycological Congress, IPC2021; 2022 China-Norway Marine University Consortium Alliance; 58th Meeting of the Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation). For objective one, we characterise the thermal reaction norms for different marine species. We compared populations in terms of their different capacities to adjust physiologically under broader ranges of temperature conditions (e.g., Pain et al., 2021; Rodríguez-Romero et al., 2022; Britton et al., under review; Li et al., under review). We assessed the physiological cost of detrimental effects of warming in these populations (e.g., Schimd et al., 2020), and tried to explain overall patterns of thermal physiology and vulnerabilities (e.g., Hemraj et al., 2021; Arromrak et al., 2022; Li et al., under review), as well as other potential mechanisms regulating thermal plasticity in marine organisms (e.g., Gaitan-Espitia & Schmid, 2020; Arromrak et al., under review). For objective two we expanded this research by looking at the interaction of warming with other climate change stressors such as ocean acidification, comparing populations across latitudinal gradients (e.g., Hemraj et al., 2021; Rodríguez-Romero et al., 2022; Britton et al., under review) and assessing the influence of other environmental drivers in the capacity for thermal plasticity (e.g., Schimd et al., 2020; Pain et al., 2021; Li et al., under review). We then assessed the molecular regulation of physiological stress in ectotherms inhabiting thermal extreme conditions in tropical ecosystems (Leung & Gaitan-Espitia, under preparation). Using this transcriptional information, we reconstructed the genetic architecture of functional pathways involved in the thermal adaptation of tropical ectotherms and tested the influence of the rate of temperature change modulating such adaptations (Leung & Gaitan-Espitia, under preparation). We have integrated all the functional and genetic findings of this project into a broader conservation framework aiming to provide tools and a guide route to scientists, conservation managers and stakeholders interested in harnessing phenotypic plasticity into conservation efforts to mitigate climate change (e.g., Gaitan-Espitia & Hobday, 2021; Donelson et al., under review).

27124318.label: Major findings and research outcome
27124318.value: Marine ectotherms are highly vulnerable to environmental and climate change. In this ECS project, we assessed intra- and inter-species differences in the mechanisms underpinning biological responses to climate change (i.e., phenotypic plasticity and adaptive evolution). First, we found that ectothermic organisms can exhibit differential capacity for thermal plasticity (TPC) depending on their ecological backgrounds (stable vs variable environments) and range of distribution (endemic/constrained vs cosmopolitan). For instance, ectotherms with broader geographic distribution tend to exhibit greater thermal phenotypic plasticity than organisms with more narrowed distribution. This pattern, however, is influenced by the level of environmental variability experienced in which ectotherms from more variable environments tend to be more tolerant to thermal fluctuations and change (Hemraj et al., 2021; Arromrak et al., 2022; Li et al., under review). Nevertheless, and despite this general pattern, there are context specific exemptions. For instance, isolated endemic, ectothermic populations inhabiting highly variable environments in temperate zones have marked local adaptation and lower thermal optima compared to sub-tropical and tropical populations. This can result in limited capacity to tolerate increased temperatures and thus, higher vulnerability to climate change in temperate populations (Pain et al., 2021; Britton et al., under review). It is important to highlight here that the capacity for thermal plasticity is highly conditioned by the interaction with other environmental drivers (e.g., light, nutrients, pH)(Schimd et al., 2020; Pain et al., 2021; Li et al., under review) and the influence of other extrinsic biological factors (e.g., microbiome)(Gaitan-Espitia & Schmid, 2020; Arromrak et al., under review), making more challenging the accurate assessment of thermal plasticity and vulnerability in ectotherms. Contrary to our expectations, ocean acidification does not show clear geographic patters in phenotypic plasticity, performance and sensitivities for marine ectotherms. Populations show similar negative effects of OA disregarding their latitudinal distribution (Hemraj et al., 2021; Rodríguez-Romero et al., 2022). These findings suggest that warming and ocean acidification can negatively impact natural populations of marine ectotherms from the tropics to the poles. However, while the responses to OA are expected to be uniform across latitudes, responses to warming are hypothesised to differ. Therefore, planning conservation of marine ectotherms under climate change will require to consider such ecological trends and the geographic differences in adaptive capacities to cope with novel and extreme conditions (Gaitan-Espitia & Hobday, 2021). Such differences have shaped the genetic architecture underpinning gene expression and pro-survival pathways in marine ectotherms (Leung & Gaitan-Espitia, under preparation).

27124318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27124318.value: Climate change is a fact and is happening right now. We are witnessing rapid populations declines and massive die-offs in tropical marine ectotherms, mostly driven by changes in environmental temperature. This is (and will be) exacerbated by concomitant changes in pH/pCO2 and oxygen availability. Most of these multi-driver changes are rapid, unpredictable and catastrophic extreme events (e.g., heatwaves). Such events are expected to increase in frequency and intensity during the next decades, pushing tropical marine organisms beyond their limits of plastic phenotypic adjustments and reducing their potential for adaptive evolution. However, there is no empirical evaluation of the ecological and evolutionary responses of tropical ectotherms to multi-driver changes, extreme and compound events. It is unclear whether local adaptation and the capacity of these organisms to tolerate extreme events can help them in the future or act as a maladaptive response. Moreover, it is important to understand how these extreme, multi-driver events can re-shape population dynamics of ectotherms across species distribution (latitudinal ranges). To achieve this, it is fundamental to integrate climate change models with species range models informed by empirical assessments of latitudinal differences in physiological tolerances and plasticity in response to multi-driver extreme events.

27124318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27124318.value: Climate change is a major threat to marine biodiversity. However, the ecological and evolutionary responses of marine organisms to this threat will not be uniform across space and time due to differences in their capacity for plasticity phenotypic adjustments and adaptive potential. Compared to temperate and sub-tropical organisms, most tropical ectotherms are expected to be highly vulnerable to climate change. These organisms already live near their physiological limits to changes in temperature, O2 and pH. As a consequence, climate-driven changes can induce major population declines and species extinctions, particularly in the tropics. However, in this ECS project we found that tropical ectotherms can better withstand extreme thermal conditions compared to their higher latitude counterparts. Nonetheless, such greater tolerance is limited by the rate of environmental change and it comes with a trade-off evidenced by the constrained phenotypic plasticity in these organisms. This eco-physiological pattern is most likely explained by local adaptation and the evolution of regulatory mechanisms to tolerate environment stress in the highly extreme and stable tropical environments. Such physiological mechanisms are linked to the fine regulation of protein-folding genes and pro-survival pathways, aspects that reviled different genetic architectures and genetic constraints for physiological traits in tropical ectotherms.

27204518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27204518.value: Rare diseases and cancers are fundamentally diseases of the genome. In the past several years, genome sequencing has become one of the most important tools in clinical practice for rare disease diagnosis and targeted cancer therapy. However, the variant interpretation step, which inspects and organizes the candidate variants for annotation, remains the bottleneck as is not yet sufficiently automated and may take a specialist up to 10 hours of work per patient. On average, 20% of this time was spent on visually confirming the authenticity of the candidate variants, according to the Hong Kong and Mainland users of the popular variant interpretation platform named “database.bio”. Sequencing data include both systematic and random errors that hinder any of the current variant identification algorithms from working perfectly. Typically, 1-3% of the candidate variants are false positives with Illumina sequencing. With the help of a genome browser, a specialist can visually inspect a graphical layout of the sequencing read alignments around a candidate to assess supporting and contradicting evidence to make an arbitration. Undoubtedly, this is a tedious and fallible procedure and urgently needs to be revolutionized. From project MNIST to GoogLeNet, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) have drastically improved from being able to barely distinguish hand-written numbers to accurately categorizing images of thousands of different objects in the real world. As reported, GoogLeNet can perform even better than a human in edge cases. However, there has been no systematic study on how these new advancements could help tackle the variant identification problem. Can we use ANN to automate the visual validation of clinically significant genomic variants and save doctors 2 hours of work per patient? In this project, we aim to study the suitability of different ANN techniques in capturing various genomics features and use real genomic data to develop a versatile network to capture all necessary genomics features for variant identification. We will perturb the design and construct training models to maximize the precision and recall rate to exceed the current best variant identification algorithm. To transform the research outcomes into a usable product, we will implement a robust variant discriminator that can be seamlessly deployed into database.bio and other variant interpretation platforms. Finally, as no effective variant identification algorithm exists for newer third-generation sequencing (TGS) technologies such as PacBio and Oxford Nanopore, we will also investigate the possibility of extending our design to make a general variant caller for TGS. 罕見病和癌症從根本上屬於基因組疾病。過去的幾年里，基因組測序已成為了罕見病診斷和癌症靶向治療的一個非常重用的臨床工具。然而，其中一個用於組織和檢閱基因組變異注釋的重要步驟，又名「變異解讀」，缺少成熟自動化的方案並需要消耗一個專家每病人次多達十個小時。根據「database.bio」變異解讀平台在香港和內地用戶們的反饋，這其中20％的時間用於視覺檢驗變異的確實性。 測序數據中包含系統性和隨機性錯誤，導致沒有一個現有的變異檢測算法可以保證百分百的準確。通常，使用Illumina測序會導致1﹣3％左右的假陽性。通過使用基因組瀏覽器，專家可以通過肉眼觀察收集圍繞一個基因組變異的，支持或反對這個變異確實性的短序列比對信息以作出變異是否確實的決斷。毋庸置疑，這一步驟不僅繁瑣而且極易犯錯，應該被更好的方法取而代之。 從MINST到GoogLeNet項目，人工神經網絡（ANN）得到了極大的發展，並從僅僅能辨認手寫數字，到現在的可以從真實世界的圖片中準確識別出上千種類別的物體。根據報道GoogLeNet在一些極端例子中表現得比人更出色。然而當前還沒有把人工神經網絡利用在辨別基因組變異確實性的研究。我以我們提出了質疑，我們可否利用人工神經網絡使臨床顯著基因組變異的視覺檢驗自動化，以此節省醫生每病人次兩小時的工作時間？ 在這個項目中，我們將研究利用人工神經網絡捕獲多種基因組特徵的可行性，並利用真實基因組數據以知道開發一個通用的，可以捕捉變異識別所需的所有基因組特徵的人工神經網絡。我們將通過微小的調整網絡設計以最大化變異檢測的準確性和靈敏性，以超越當前最優秀的變異檢測算法。為了將研究成果轉化成切實可用的產品，我們將實現一個可以無縫部署至「database.bio」或其他變異解讀平台的，強健的基因組變異識別器。最後，鑒於當前並不存在一個可用於第三代測序技術（TGS），比如PacBio和Oxford Nanopore的變異檢測算法，我們將調研把我們的設計擴展至一個完整的，可用於TGS的變異檢測算法的可行性。

27204518.label: Major findings and research outcome
27204518.value: We established the global standard of germline variant calling using long-read. Germline variant calling is the basic step of discovering genetic differences between individuals, and its precision and sensitivity are the cornerstone of precision medicine and curing rare diseases and cancer. As benchmarked in the published papers, our method is the most precise and sensitive method that enables more clinically actionable genetic variants to be discovered. As an established standard, our method was implemented in an open-source software package of computer algorithms and deep-learning algorithms. The package has been downloaded over 110 thousand times. It has been deployed in the production environment of top bioinformatics institutes, including the National Institute of Health (NIH) of the U.S. and the European Bioinformatics Institute.

27204518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27204518.value: The project has enabled a successful GRF grant that extends this project to a harder problem, that is, somatic variant calling using long-read. With a wonderful foundation established in this project, the new GRF project is moving smoothly and achieving promising results. The project has also attracted an industrial donation from the top long-read sequencing technology company Oxford Nanopore Sequencing for us to keep maintaining the method and the software package developed.

27204518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27204518.value: The project is a grand success, with 13 publications published that accumulated over 500 citations up to date, enabled a successful GRF grant that extends the achievements of this project to an even harder problem, and attracted a one-million industrial donation to support general research from a public-listed top company in bioinformatics. The project established the global standard of germline variant calling using long-read, which is an essential step in precision medicine and curing rare diseases and cancer.

27204818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27204818.value: For concrete infrastructure exposed to marine environments, as in Hong Kong, steel corrosion can lead to concrete cover spalling, structural deterioration and even failure. Corrosion reduces safety and service life, increases maintenance costs and disruption of use, as well as adds significant environmental and economic costs. Conventional solutions include surface coatings, larger concrete covers as well as corrosion resistant reinforcements, all of which are expensive and/or environmentally unfriendly. Smart and functional concrete with spontaneous and long-lasting corrosion inhibiting capabilities can provide an economic and sustainable solution to extending the service life of concrete infrastructure. The primary objectives of this research are to elucidate the influence of microstructure and composition of concrete on corrosion kinetics of steel and to develop sustainable and functional concrete materials with smart corrosion inhibiting effects. This study will first explore parameters that control the corrosion kinetics of steel through a multi-scale characterization and modeling of the concrete-steel interface. The corrosion rate and electrical resistivity of concrete with vastly different compositions and microstructures will be measured and correlated. In parallel, the spatial rust distribution and elemental mapping at the concrete-steel interface will be studied using advanced techniques. The macro-scale properties of concrete will be linked to the microstructural information through finite element method and reactive-transport modeling. It will help identify the critical microstructural features of concrete that control corrosion development of embedded steel, as well as provide essential information for designing novel corrosion-resistant concrete with a tailored microstructure. Novel types of functional concrete with smart corrosion inhibiting effects will be formulated based on (i) modified calcined clays and (ii) innovative alkali-activated cementitious materials. The smart release of corrosion inhibitors in concrete will not rely on any encapsulation techniques and organic coatings; instead, it will fully utilize the physicochemical properties of concrete itself. In particular, clay minerals will be modified and intercalated with corrosion inhibitive ions (nitrate) or pillared with titian dioxide. The pozzolanic reaction of modified calcined clays with portlandite in concrete will generate and capture nitrate ions in the formed layered double hydroxides (LDHs) during hydration or photocatalysis, then release nitrate ions when exposed to chloride-rich environments via ion exchange mechanisms. The alkali-activation technology will be utilized to convert industrial waste materials into sustainable cementitious binders/coatings with smart nitrate releasing functions, by implementing compositionally-designed novel activators. The formation of nitrate-containing LDHs in alkali-activated materials will be enhanced through dispersing aqueous LDHs precursors in activators. 作為目前最廣為應用的結構形式，鋼筋混凝土結構的可靠性、耐久性和可持續性是當前結構工程領域的研究熱點。對於暴露在海洋環境中的混凝土結構，鋼筋鏽蝕所引起的結構失效和服役壽命縮短是當今世界上最常見的耐久性問題。侵蝕到保護層的氯離子會使鋼筋表面鈍化膜脫落，加速腐蝕速度，進而引起表層混凝土開裂和結構可靠度降低，由此造成巨大的經濟損失和安全隱患。傳統的鋼筋腐蝕控製手段包括加大混凝土保護層厚度、應用耐腐蝕鋼筋及表面塗層，不僅費用昂貴而且不環保。智能與功能化混凝土可以長期有效地控製鋼筋腐蝕速率，提供一種全新的可持續的、經濟的鋼筋阻銹技術。本項目的主要研究目的在於闡明控製鋼筋腐蝕速率的混凝土微觀信息參數並設計製備具有智能阻銹功能的新型混凝土材料。 本項目首先著重於通過多尺度表徵和鋼筋-混凝土界面模擬，探究控製鋼筋腐蝕速率的關鍵參數。測定具有不同化學成分和微觀結構的混凝土的鏽蝕速率和電阻率，進而建立兩者之間的定性關係。與此同時，應用現代先進材料表徵技術，分析在鋼筋-混凝土界面中的鏽蝕產物和化學元素分佈。依據有限元和反應-傳質模擬，建立混凝土宏觀鏽蝕速率與微觀信息參數之間的多尺度模型。所獲得的信息將有助於微觀參數優化，設計新型抗銹混凝土。 具有智能阻銹功能的新型混凝土材料將通過兩種方法製備：鹼激發材料和改進的粘土礦物。與現有方法不同，所設計的混凝土將根據所暴露的環境可控制地釋放阻銹劑，而不依靠任何有機物塗層或膠囊。一方面，將阻銹離子插入到粘土礦物夾層中，應用混凝土中的火山灰反應將煅燒的粘土轉化為具有阻銹離子的層狀雙氫氧化物。另一方面，應用改進的鹼激發技術，將粉煤灰廢渣轉化為具有阻銹離子層狀雙氫氧化物。

27204818.label: Realisation of objectives
27204818.value: We have successfully addressed all the objectives of this project. Over ten journal papers have been published or submitted for publication in the top journals, including Cement and Concrete Research, Cement and Concrete Composites, among others. Realization of Objective 1: A new mechanism is proposed to explain the influence of multiply influential factors on the R-C (electrical resistivity versus corrosion rate) relationships from ion diffusion and electrochemistry. Realization of Objective 2: The key microstructural and compositional parameters (i.e., diffusion coefficient of partially-saturated concrete and [Cl]/[OH] ratio) that that govern corrosion rate of steel embedded in concrete have been identified and verified. Realization of Objective 3: The modelling of corrosion rate of steel in concrete underlying varying climate conditions has been realised. The model allows the relating of microstructural parameters of concrete materials to the corrosion rate of steel embedded. Realization of Objective 4: The spontaneous formation and smart use of corrosion inhibitors-intercalated LDHs (layered double hydroxide, also called anionic clays) have been demonstrated. Realization of Objective 5: Low-carbon alkali-activated slag binder with smart corrosion inhibiting effect has been formulated and investigated.

27204818.label: Major findings and research outcome
27204818.value: The major findings related to each research objective are summarized as follows: Findings related to Objective 1: The R-C (electrical resistivity versus corrosion rate) relationships are primarily influenced by hydroxide ion concentration in pore solution through affecting ion conductivity and the ratio of chloride-to-hydroxide concentration ([Cl]/[OH]) of pore solution electrochemically. However, R-C relationships are limitedly affected by chloride ion concentration in pore solution and formation factor (pore structure), as a result of their combined influence on electrical resistivity and corrosion rate. Findings related to Objective 2: Diffusion coefficient of partially-saturated concrete and pore solution chemistry ([Cl]/[OH] ratio) is the fundamental parameters that govern corrosion rate of steel. Findings related to Objective 3: The change of RH has a great impact on the development of corrosion. Low resistivity of concrete is helpful for current circulation between anodes and cathodes, which can be achieved only when the environmental temperature and RH are both relatively high. The evolution trend of corrosion current density is correlated to that of temperature, indicating that temperature is the decisive factor in controlling the steel corrosion rate. Findings related to Objective 4: The direct admixing of inorganic or organic inhibitors results in spontaneous formation of inhibitors-intercalated LDHs, regardless of binder chemistry. The sequestrated anodic inhibitors in cementitious systems are released upon exposure to chloride, accompanied by simultaneous formation of Friedel’s salts (Cl-AFm). The incorporation of anodic inhibitors has little influence on the chloride binding capacity of cementitious pastes, but impacts their chloride resistance via pore structure modification. Findings related to Objective 5: Low-carbon alkali-activated slag binder with smart corrosion inhibiting effect has been formulated and investigated. It is found that upon chloride exposure, the nitrite or nitrate is released together with the increased local chloride concentration, suggesting the potential smart corrosion control ability of nitrite- or nitrate- intercalated hydrotalcite of AAS. Initially, part of nitrite and nitrate is sequestrated in hydrotalcite that prevents inhibitors leaching and rapid drop of inhibiting efficiency. As chloride ingresses, the local chloride concentration raises and hydrotalcite releases nitrite and nitrate while immobilising chloride. As such, the relative concentration of inhibitor to chloride can be maintained, contributing to the mitigation of corrosion initiation.

27204818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27204818.value: Further research regarding the chemistry and molecular-scale behaviours of LDHs (layered double hydroxide) phases in cement and concrete should be conducted. The LDHs show great promise in enhancing the mechanical and durability performance of concrete materials. Further research into other innovative application fields of LDHs in concrete construction should be explored.

27204818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27204818.value: This project aims at developing smart and sustainable concrete materials to control the corrosion of steel reinforcement in marine infrastructure. As corrosion of steel in concrete infrastructure is the most prevalent durability issue in marine infrastructure, the project aims to considerably enhance the long-term serviceability and reduce the life-cycle costs of critical concrete infrastructure. In this project, we have identified the key microstructural and compositional parameters (i.e., diffusion coefficient of partially-saturated concrete and [Cl]/[OH] ratio) that that govern the corrosion rate of steel embedded in concrete. As such, designing durable concrete with enhanced chloride resistance becomes possible. In addition, we have demonstrated that sustainable concrete based on low-carbon binders and corrosion inhibitors can demonstrate smart corrosion control capacity. In particular, the addition of corrosion inhibitors in cementitious systems leads to the spontaneous formation of inhibitors-intercalated LDHs (layered double hydroxide), which can uptake chloride while releasing corrosion inhibitive agents. The outcome of this research has led to the development of more sustainable and smart concrete for marine construction in Hong Kong.

27205918.label: Realisation of objectives
27205918.value: The three objectives of the project have been well achieved. First, we have developed novel modeling frameworks for waterless fracturing methods. These developments include a series of phase-field models for mixed-mode fracture in quasi-brittle rocks and an anisotropic and viscoplastic constitutive model for shale based on layered microstructure homogenization. Second, we have developed accurate and efficient numerical techniques for coupled geomechanics and flow in porous media. Specifically, we have spearheaded enriched Galerkin methods and material point methods for coupled poromechanics, in which the inf-sup stability problem in undrained deformation is efficiently stabilized for each kind of method. Lastly, through the application of these advanced mathematical models and numerical techniques, we have investigated how the properties of the injecting fluid controls the physical process of fluid-driven fracture for energy recovery.

27205918.label: Major findings and research outcome
27205918.value: A primary outcome of this project is a class of phase-field formulations for modeling discontinuities and fractures in geologic materials. Over the past several years, phase-field modeling has become a state-of-the-art method for computational simulation of fractures in various kinds of solids. However, the existing phase-field formulations do not incorporate several critical features of discontinuities and fractures in geologic materials: frictional contact, pressure-dependence, quasi-brittleness, and their combined impact on mixed-mode cracking. In this project, we have developed a class of novel phase-field formulations that incorporate these features in a well verified and validated manner. Remarkably, these phase-field approaches allow one to simulate the combination of cohesive tensile fracture and frictional shear fracture without any algorithms for surface tracking and contact constraints. Another key outcome related to geomechanical modeling is a two-scale constitutive model for anisotropic and viscoplsatic shale. The constitutive model utilizes semi-analytical homogenization of a bilayer microstructure comprised of soft and hard layers, such that anisotropic behavior naturally emerges in the macroscopic level even when the individual layers are isotropic. As a result, the anisotropic viscoplastic constitutive model can be calibrated with a lower number of parameters compared with existing constitutive models for the same purpose, and all the parameters have clear physical meanings. In addition, we have developed accurate and efficient numerical methods for simulating coupled geomechanics and flow in porous media. They include enriched Galerkin methods for locally conservative solutions to poromechanical problems, and material point methods for simulating fluid-saturated porous media undergoing large deformations. For both types of methods, we have developed stabilization techniques that efficiently address the inf-sup stability problem in undrained deformation. Last but not least, by applying these advanced simulation methodologies, we have investigated how the properties of the injecting fluid controls the physics involved in waterless fracturing methods for energy recovery. Our findings include that when the fracturing fluid is far less viscous than water, the breakdown pressure becomes much lower, and the rock matrix experiences much more distributed microcracking. These changes may have significant effects on the performance and environmental impacts of unconventional resources recovery.

27205918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27205918.value: The research may be further developed in the following way. Firstly, one can improve the numerical modeling methodology such that it incorporates more physical aspects in the waterless fracturing process. For example, it is highly desirable to enhance the methodology for mixed-mode fracture in anisotropic and viscoplastic shale, by combining the phase-field models and the constitutive model developed in this research. Another line of important future work improving the methodology is to include chemical and thermal effects such as adsorption into the shale matrix. Once the modeling methodology becomes improved as described above, one may use it to further elucidate the physics involved in waterless fracturing methods in more realistic settings. The improved simulation methodology and physical understanding will allow us to better deploy waterless fracturing methods in the large-scale commercial production of unconventional resources.

27205918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27205918.value: The use of unconventional resources (e.g. shale gas) is essential to meeting the ever-growing demands for energy resources until renewable energy technologies become mature enough to replace fossil fuels completely. However, the current methods for extracting unconventional resources can give rise to other environmental problems, particularly consumption and contamination of freshwater resources and induced earthquakes. These problems are mainly resulted from the use of hydraulic fracturing, in which a large volume of chemically treated water is injected into deep underground to fracture low-permeable rock formations. A promising option to counteract these problems is to use waterless fracturing methods, whereby the water in hydraulic fracturing is replaced by non-aqueous fluids such as liquid/supercritical carbon dioxide. However, to apply such waterless fracturing methods in the large-scale commercial production of unconventional resources, we should be able to understand, predict and control the complex physics involved in waterless fracturing processes. This project has developed a family of novel computational methods for high-fidelity simulation of waterless fracturing processes in shale rocks. The methods have been applied to decipher hitherto unknown aspects of the physics involved in waterless fracturing processes. The outcomes will help advance waterless fracturing technologies for more environmentally friendly recovery of unconventional resources.

27210118.value: 建立有韌性的生產網絡：系統風險和政策評估

27210118.label: Project Objectives
27210118.value: Propose an innovative tractable model that quantifies the systemic risk and contagion effect generated by shocks in production networks. This model will capture the cyclical interdependence between firms in the production network and incorporate the contingent policy each firm will take when facing supply disruptions. Investigate the impact of network structure on systemic risk in production networks. I will compare different network structures in terms of systemic risk so as to answer the questions such as whether multiple (single) sourcing for a firm is better or whether horizontal (vertical) integration is beneficial to the entire production network. Evaluate the intervention policies aimed at mitigating the impact of shocks in different production networks. Three forms of intervention will be considered: bailouts, bail-ins, and subsidized bail-ins. I plan to quantify the performance of each policy under different shock sizes and network structures. Quantify the systemic risk generated from uncertainty. I will investigate the benefits each firm can earn in terms of reduced systemic risk by knowing more about the production network. This will further bring out the managerial insights on the value of information sharing.

27210118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27210118.value: In the 2008-10 automotive industry crisis caused by the oil price shock and economic downturn, both General Motors and Chrysler faced bankruptcy and the loss of one million jobs. This created a huge demand uncertainty risk to the suppliers of these two giant automakers and prompted the U.S. government to provide financial assistant through the U.S. Treasury Department's Asset Relief Program (TARP), originally put forward to address the subprime mortgage crisis. Starting from the early 2000s and mainly after the 2008 financial crisis, systemic risk in financial networks has drawn a great deal of attention from both academia and industry. Although the gross output of the manufacturing industry is more than twice as large as that of the finance and insurance industry, only a handful of studies have focused on systemic risk in production networks. This project aims to fill this gap in the literature. My contribution in this proposed project will be twofold in both building up a tractable network model and improving the network performance. Different from the prevailing one-product and two-stage setting in the literature, I will develop a production network model where each firm manufactures multiple outputs sold to multiple customers and demands multiple inputs from multiple suppliers. This generalization is crucial for investigating how shocks propagate through the entire production network via the input-output linkages between suppliers and customers and makes it possible to study how a shock is amplified by the cyclic structures in the production network. Moreover, the network model will incorporate firms' responses to supply disruptions. When a firm observes a disruption, it will take contingent policies to mitigate the impact of the disruption. It is necessary to take into account the effect of such policies to avoid the overestimate of systemic risk. Aiming at improving the network performance, I will provide an analytical tool to compare production networks with different network structures as it has been shown in the literature that network structure significantly affects the supply disruption risk in the single-product and two-stage setting. Furthermore, I will propose a framework for a government to assess possible intervention policies that target the resolution of firm failures in manufacturing industries. I believe my combined expertise in financial networks analysis, network equilibrium models and majorization theory will guide the research efforts. 高油價和經濟不景氣造成了2008至2010年的美國汽車工業危機。當時，汽車業巨擘美商通用汽車和克萊斯勒雙雙遭遇破產危機，百萬計的工人面臨著失業的可能，這兩間汽車大廠的供應商因而面對巨大的需求不確定風險。這促使美國政府透過財政部制定的不良資產救助計劃（TARP），對這兩間企業提供財務協助。自2000年起，金融網絡中的系統風險（systemic risk）吸引了產官學界的關注，此趨勢在2008年金融危機後越發顯著。儘管製造工業的總產出大過金融及保險業總產出的兩倍，針對生產網絡中系統風險的研究確是寥寥可數。本項目將填補現有文獻中的空白。 本項目的貢獻將包含：建立一個可解的生產網絡模型，和提升生產網絡的表現。不同於現有文獻大量使用的單一產品兩階層的供應鍊，我將建立一個生產網絡模型。在這網絡中，每間製造商從多個供應商訂購多種生產原料，製造多種產品，售予多位客戶。這樣的設定，對於研究生產衝擊如何透過供應商和客戶間的輸入-輸出連結，在生產網絡中蔓延開來，至為關鍵。同時也讓我們可以研究生產衝擊如何透過生產網絡中的循環結構而增強。這個網絡模型也會一併考慮，製造商爲了降低因生產衝擊造成的供應中斷所帶來的負面影響，而採取的應對措施。如果沒有一併考慮應對措施，將有可能高估生產網絡中的系統風險。在提升生產網絡表現方面，我將開發一個能比較不同網絡結構表現的工具。現有文獻顯示，在擁有不同結構的單一產品兩階層的供應鍊中，供應中斷風險有顯著的差異。藉此工具，針對政府用以援助受衝擊製造商的政策，我將進一步開發一個可供政府監管部門評估的框架。我在金融網絡分析、網絡均衡理論，以及蓋理論（majorization theory) 的經驗，將能充分運用在本項目中。

27300118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300118.value: Fluvial networks occupy less than 0.5% of the Earth’s land surface, yet are significant components of the global carbon cycle. Recent research indicates that river systems act not only as land-to-ocean vectors, transporting, storing, and processing huge quantities of carbon, but also as dynamic conduits that relocate greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. However, current research on riverine carbon is associated with great uncertainty. Most existing studies have been conducted in tropical and arctic regions, while relevant studies in other climatic zones are lacking. The lack of a clear understanding of geographical variability across different climatic zones has been noted as an important error source in global estimates of the riverine carbon cycle. The Loess Plateau in northern China has historically suffered severe soil erosion, which has meant that large amounts of carbon have been exported into its river systems. In recent decades, however, soil conservation measures have significantly reduced this soil erosion. While extensive studies have investigated soil erosion and sediment transport, relatively little is known about the associated carbon. This proposed project is among the first to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the riverine carbon cycle of the Loess Plateau. There are three destinations for terrestrially-derived riverine carbon: downstream export to catchment outlets, burial in sediments, and evasion into the atmosphere. Through intensive field sampling in representative Loess Plateau river catchments, we will investigate spatial and temporal variations in lateral carbon export at the catchment scale. The magnitude and direction of CO2 evasion from streams and reservoirs will also be determined to explore its underlying mechanisms and response to human activity, such as land-use change and dam impoundment. In addition, the extensive construction of silt check dams on the Loess Plateau presents the opportunity to quantitatively assess carbon burial and its potential implications for regional carbon budgets. This research project is highly significant because it will be the first integrated research project undertaken to investigate the Loess Plateau riverine carbon cycle taking all three of its pathways into account. Building on our previous studies of soil erosion and sediment, we will be able to critically evaluate the re-distribution of riverine carbon among its different destinations. Our results will quantify the influence of human activity such as land-use change and dam construction on riverine carbon transport. Therefore, the proposed study will also be highly relevant and meaningful for policy-makers evaluating the carbon benefits of soil conservation and vegetation restoration programmes. 盡管全球河流系統只占據了陸地總面積的0.5%，河流系統卻是全球碳循環過程中的壹個重要組成部分。近來的研究表明河流系統並非被動地把陸地生態系統的碳輸送至與海洋系統中去，河流系統在橫向碳輸移過程也釋放大量的碳進入大氣中。然而，當前關於河流碳輸移的研究仍存在較大的誤差。現有的研究多針對熱帶和寒帶地區的河流系統開展的，而缺乏對其他氣候帶河流碳輸移過程的理解。由於不同氣候帶之間巨大的地理空間差異，針對不同氣候帶河流碳輸移過程研究的缺乏已成為當前全球尺度河流碳輸移通量估算的壹個重要誤差來源。 位於中國北部的黃土高原曾遭受嚴重的土壤侵蝕 。這意味著大量的流域坡面土壤碳經侵蝕已被搬運至河流系統中去。另外， 近幾十年來，大量的水土保持工作已顯著地減輕了土壤侵蝕強度。值得註意的是，盡管針對水土保持而引起的土壤侵蝕強度和河流泥沙輸移減少已引起廣泛的關註和研究，對於相關的碳輸移研究卻很缺乏。本項目將針對黃土高原典型流域的河流碳輸移過程首次開展相關的深入研究。河流碳在輸移過程中有三種不同的歸宿，即橫向輸移至流域出口、伴隨泥沙淤積而埋藏於流域內及經氧化分解而逸出到大氣中去。通過對代表性流域的大量野外實測工作，本項目將探討黃土高原流域河流碳輸移過程的時空變化特征，並通過定量分析CO2的逸出速率及方向進而辨析其內在影響機理及其對人類活動（比如土地利用變化和水壩建設等）的響應。另外，本項目還將定量分析黃土高原因大量淤地壩建設而導致的有機碳埋藏及其對區域碳收支平衡的潛在影響。 作為針對黃土高原流域河流碳輸移過程的首次系統性探索研究，本項目對於理解河流碳循環過程具有重要的理論意義。基於項目申請者前期關於土壤侵蝕和泥沙輸移的研究結果，本項目將系統性地探討河流碳在其輸移過程中基於三種不同歸宿的再分配過程。此外，研究結果將定量分析人類活動對河流碳輸移的影響。因此，本項目結論將有助於相關的政府決策者更準確地評估水土保持措施及植被重建項目對河流碳輸移影響的利與弊。

27300118.label: Realisation of objectives
27300118.value: River systems represent an important component in the global carbon cycle. My research team has finished five campaigns of fieldwork on riverine carbon cycle in three catchments on the Chinese Loess Plateau (CLP), including the Kuye, Wuding, and Jing catchments, during the implementation of the research project. The five campaigns were conducted in July/August 2018, October/November 2018, March/April 2019, June/July 2019, and June 2020, respectively. During each of the first four campaigns, we visited 69 sites in the three catchments. The fifth campaign was only conducted in the Jing River. We have collected >1500 samples and completed all laboratory work. The obtained datasets were stored at the HKU Library. Below, I briefly summarize the state how and to what extent the listed five objectives have been achieved. For Objective 1: Both lateral carbon export and dissolved carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the studied river catchments were found to exhibit pronounced spatial and seasonal variations. For lateral carbon export at the catchment outlet, dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is the major carbon species due largely to the unique chemical composition of loess soils (e.g., high carbonate content). DIC concentrations ranged from 35 to 98 mg L^-1 and were generally 10 times higher than dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations. Content of particulate organic carbon (POC) in sediments was extremely low, in the range of 0.2–0.5% (dry weight), which reflects the low terrestrial productivity and strong sediment mobilization through erosion (see: Chan et al., 2021. Water, 13, 1614; Ran et al., 2020. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, 45, 1777-1788; Shi et al., 2021. Arid Zone Research, 38, 369-379). While the lateral carbon concentrations were significantly lower during periods of high flow due to the ‘dilution effect’, the high flow periods (i.e., the wet season) played an important role in transporting riverine carbon. For example, an extreme flood in the Wuding River catchment in 2017 alone contributed 73.1% of the annual carbon flux in just 7 days (see: Ran et al., 2020. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, 45, 1777-1788). All the surveyed streams were net CO2 sources, exhibiting significant seasonal variabilities with substantially stronger emission rates in spring/autumn while lower rates in summer, which reflects the impact of terrestrial carbon inputs (see: Chan et al., 2021. Water, 13, 1614; Ran et al., 2021. Journal of Hydrology, 598, 126260). For Objective 2: Our study shows that lateral carbon derived from soil respiration and chemical weathering played a central role in controlling the variability of riverine CO2 partial pressure. In addition, in-stream processing was an important source of CO2 excess, modulating the inﬂuence of lateral carbon inputs. Based on the intensive sampling in the Wuding River (at Baijiachuan gauge), our stable carbon isotope (13C) analysis of POC suggested that modern soils and C3 plants were its primary sources (see: Ran et al., 2020. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, 45, 1777-1788). Radiocarbon (14C) analysis showed that the age of the degassed CO2 ranged from 810 to 1890 years. The emitted CO2 exhibited the oldest age in spring with the age in summer and autumn 36% and 29 % younger, respectively. For riverine POC, our unpublished 14C results for the Jing River show that its radiocarbon ages ranged from 5515 to 7990 years BP. These old radiocarbon ages suggest that the POC is primarily of petrogenic origin with small contributions of recently fixed atmospheric carbon. For Objective 3: Based on sediment coring data, we evaluated the organic carbon (OC) burial efficiency by check dams. Compared with the OC content of soils, the OC content in the deposited sediments showed insignificant differences (p>0.05). Our results show that the POC content in buried sediments (POC%) varied from 0.1 to 0.5 % with high POC% values in the surface sediments (0–60 cm) and it declined rapidly with depth. Building on our earlier estimate of sediment deposition by check dams, we estimated the annual OC burial behind check dams in the Wuding catchment to be (7.8 ± 4.1) × 10^10 g C (see: Ran et al., 2021. Journal of Hydrology, 598, 126260; Ran et al., 2018. Biogeosciences, 15, 3857-3871). For the Jing catchment, we found similar OC burial efficiency. Compared with soils where carbon typically has a short turnover time, the buried terrestrial carbon by check dams can more effectively escape mineralization and is thus removed from the short-term carbon cycle. Therefore, rather than a simple change in storage location, the carbon burial by check dams could be accountable as an anthropogenic carbon sink. For Objective 4: Our study shows that the combined effects of flow paths and land–river connectivity can lead to significant carbon export fluxes and CO2 emissions. Flushing of the abundant antecedent carbon in soils and groundwater by large floods sustained the dissolved carbon concentrations that would otherwise be diluted. This is especially apparent for DOC, which is primarily derived from soil organic matter that depends on overland flow for movement. In contrast, the DIC concentration remained seasonally stable, which indicates that the change in the flow paths from groundwater in dry seasons to overland flow during floods did not greatly impact DIC concentration. In addition, hydrological controls are also important for POC export. The much lower POC% during floods reflected its catchment-derived inputs, possibly from subsurface soils characterized by extremely low carbon content. Mobilization of subsurface soils by non-topsoil erosion processes have likely resulted in the low POC%, which is also evidenced by the 13C signature of POC (see: Ran et al., 2020. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, 45, 1777-1788). Furthermore, riverine CO2 degassing is highly related to discharge dynamics and hydraulic geometry. Our research suggests that the average CO2 efflux for a complete flood event was 2348 ± 664 mg C m^-2 day^-1, which was ~3 times that under low-flow conditions due to enhanced turbulence and strong inputs of terrestrial carbon (see: Ran et al., 2021. Journal of Hydrology, 598, 126260; Ran et al., 2020. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, 45, 1777-1788). Geomorphological characteristics such as stream slope and soil properties are also critical factors in regulating the CO2 emissions. For Objective 5: Our results suggest that reservoir operation will alter the riverine dynamics of gas evasion. Compared with rivers which were large CO2 sources, the magnitude of CO2 emissions from the Tumengou Reservoir (in the Jing catchment) has been greatly reduced. As a result of extensive inputs of agricultural nitrogen and phosphorus, reservoirs on the CLP are highly eutrophic with widespread phytoplankton growth, which have considerably changed the aquatic carbon cycling processes. For example, continuous addition of methane (CH4) from agriculture along the Jing River course sustained its CH4 effluxes at higher-order streams (see: Ran et al., 2021. Journal of Hydrology, 598, 126260). In addition to extensive agriculture and damming, riverine carbon cycling has also been affected by urban wastewater. Our study in the Jing catchment demonstrates that urban sewage inflows can considerably increase GHG emissions. Part of these results have contributed to our national-scale assessment of CO2 emissions from Chinese inland waters (see: Ran et al., 2021. Nature Communications, 12, 1-9). Overall, all the five listed project objectives have been successfully achieved. Our results quantitatively examined the influence of human activity and environmental controls on riverine carbon transport and CO2 emissions in the semiarid Loess Plateau.

27300118.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300118.value: Fluvial carbon cycle in semiarid river systems remain largely understudied. Our results based on the three catchments indicate that both lateral carbon export and CO2 emissions exhibited pronounced spatial and seasonal variations, which are controlled by terrestrial productivity, soil property, and hydrological regime. For lateral carbon export, DIC is the predominant carbon form due largely to the unique chemical composition of loess soils. The DIC concentrations of 35-98 mg L^-1 were generally 10 times higher than DOC concentrations. Although the content of POC in sediments was extremely low (0.2-0.5%), POC export is substantial due to high sediment yielding. While groundwater is an important contributor to runoff, large floods are disproportionately important in exporting terrestrial carbon. A case study in the Wuding catchment suggests that the three largest floods transported 41.4-77% of the annual carbon flux, and an extreme flood in 2017 alone contributed 73.1% of the annual carbon flux in just 7 days. Despite the low terrestrial organic carbon inputs, rates of CO2 emission from streams and rivers (40-135 mmol m^-2 d^-1) are comparable to these observed in tropical and temperate catchments. This is primarily because of the exceptionally high DIC input through groundwater pathways that has sustained CO2 emissions along the river course. Furthermore, reservoir operation would greatly reduce dissolved CO2 concentrations owing to enhanced primary production but increase CH4 concentrations because of anaerobic degradation of organic-rich sediments. Our study suggests that reservoirs acted as a smaller CO2 source but a stronger CH4 source than flowing rivers. Urban wastewater discharges could modify aquatic carbon cycling and create local hotspots of gas production and emissions, which will be globally important given the increasing human impacts worldwide. Meanwhile, check dams and reservoirs can efficiently sequester terrestrial carbon through sediment deposition that would otherwise be released to the atmosphere during fluvial transit. For carbon burial by check dams and reservoirs, we argue that, rather than a simple change in storage location from hillslopes to depositional environments, this carbon burial pathway could be accountable as an anthropogenic carbon sink and needs to be properly accounted for in future carbon accounting. Based on these research results, eight research articles have been published in prestigious journals in the fields of physical geography and environmental sciences. This research project has also partly funded two RPG students. An MPhil student has successfully graduated in 2021 and another PhD student will submit his thesis soon.

27300118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300118.value: Building on the preliminary results from this ECS project, I submitted a GRF proposal entitled ‘Riverine carbon cycle and greenhouse gas emissions from the Dongjiang River Basin’ to the RGC in 2018, and fortunately this proposal was supported by RGC in 2019. In this GRF project, my team aims to critically examine environmental controls on downstream carbon export from the Dongjiang River into the ocean and greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere, and further assess their biogeochemical implications for regional carbon accounting. Although this project is still ongoing, my team has made outstanding achievements regarding riverine carbon cycling in the subtropical Dongjiang River basin. Based on the findings on the importance of groundwater inflow in providing riverine DIC and sustaining high CO2 emissions, I will propose another GRF proposal this year, which aims to quantitatively understand the significance and role of groundwater pathway and lateral hyporheic exchange in aquatic carbon cycling. If funded by the RGC, this new project will be simultaneously conducted in semiarid and subtropical catchments with contrasting hydrometeorological conditions and human impacts. Continued monitoring in dry and wet seasons will be performed to elucidate how groundwater inflow and lateral hyporheic exchange regulate biogeochemical cycling of aquatic carbon.

27300118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300118.value: Recent research indicates that river systems act not only as land-to-ocean vectors, transporting and processing huge quantities of carbon, but also as dynamic conduits that relocate greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. However, most existing studies have been conducted in tropical and arctic regions, while less is known on aquatic carbon cycling processes in (semi)arid regions. Our results based on intensive sampling in three catchments on the Chinese Loess Plateau indicate that both lateral carbon export and CO2 emissions exhibited pronounced spatial and seasonal variations, which are largely controlled by terrestrial productivity, soil property, and hydrological regime. Particularly, extreme flood events played a disproportionate role in exporting terrestrial carbon, and must be fully accounted for in future annual carbon flux estimates. Furthermore, reservoir operation would significantly alter the magnitude of greenhouse gas emissions and related carbon cycling processes due to the changed physical and biogeochemical conditions. Meanwhile, the carbon burial in reservoirs represents an anthropogenic carbon sink due to its high burial efficiency. Our results reinforce the urgency to account for (semi)arid rivers in future regional or global carbon accounting. The findings have important implications for policy makers to evaluate the carbon benefits of soil conservation and to pursue environmental sustainability.

27302018.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27302018.value: The prediction of any possible hazards of space weather requires an understanding of the entire coupled geospace system since so many feedback mechanisms exist between the Earth’s upper atmosphere, ionosphere, and magnetosphere. The ability to forecast the weather of the geospace environment depends critically on the capabilities to accurately model the dynamics of the coupled geospace system. In this coupling chain, the magnetosphere-ionosphere-upper atmosphere interaction involves a set of electrodynamic and plasma transport processes acting between the magnetosphere and ionosphere-upper atmosphere system, and it is influenced by ions that outflow from the ionosphere in to the magnetosphere, which affects the whole geospace system. Satellite data show that these ion outflows include both light ionospheric ions (H+ and He+) and heavy ions such as O+. Numerical simulations of the global geospace play an important role in understanding the Earth’s space environment. A key feature of most global geospace models is the implementation of ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling, and the dynamics of ionospheric outflow is one of the most important processes to specify in such global geospace models. However, one deficiency of most community global geospace simulation codes is the lack of accurate specifications of ionospheric O+ ion outflow. Thus this project is going to investigate physical processes related to ionospheric outflow that are necessary to facilitate the understanding of the dynamics of the whole geospace system. In this project, we will investigate the impact of the global ionosphere-thermosphere system dynamics on the processes of ion upflow and outflow using high-resolution, high-performance computing based numerical simulations of the ionosphere-thermosphere system. In order to connect the source region of ion upflow/outflow to physical process of topside ionospheric plasma transport, we will couple a global-scale ionosphere-thermosphere general circulation model with a topside ionospheric polar wind mode, and will answer the following two science questions: 1) What is (are) the influence(s) of meso-scale ionospheric structures such as tongue of ionization and polar ionization patch on the dynamic evolution of high-latitude ion upflow/outflow? and 2) Which aspects of the thermospheric response during a geomagnetic storm have the largest influence on high-latitude ion upflow and outflow? These questions will be addressed using high-resolution, two-way coupled models using controlled numerical simulations. The two-way coupled model developed in this project has also the potential to become a significant part of the Whole Geospace Modeling effort, which is an on-going community model development collaboration between multiple top-tier U.S. universities and research institutes. 地球電離層熱層的空間天氣效應對於日常生活和航空航天有重要的影響。大尺度的空間天氣現象已經由全球耦合模式進行深入研究，這類模式已經被應用於全球空間天氣模擬和預測。但中小尺度上由於模式的精度限制以及物理過程的缺失，研究進展緩慢。本研究項目致力於研究電離層熱層中小尺度結構，包括高緯度區域電離層舌狀結構以及電離層塊狀結構對於頂部電離層氧離子上行和外流的影響。氧離子上行以及外流作為地球空間天氣的一個重要組成部分，受到電離層熱層大尺度以及中小尺度動力學結構的影響。本項目基於近期新開發的高精度電離層熱層全球電動力學耦合模式，以及電離層極區風模式，采用雙向耦合的方式，在模式中對電離層熱層中尺度模式進行模擬重現，並且設計對照實驗來研究這種中尺度結構對於氧離子上行以及外流的影響。研究結果將促進空間天氣的模擬和預報模式的開發和驗證。

27302018.label: Realisation of objectives
27302018.value: Object 1: Completed. The PI and collaborators have successfully developed a fully-coupled global geospace model with the capability of simulating ionospheric ion outflows, by integrating the Ionosphere Polar Wind Model (IPWM) with the multi-fluid LFM global magnetosphere model. In the coupled version of the code, the IPWM takes magnetospheric input from the LFM and provides density, velocity and temperature of ion outflow, including thermal H+/O+ and non-thermal O+, forming a self-consistent feedback loop of geospace plasma circulation. The first model has been published in the American Geophysical Union's top journal Journal of Geophysical Research - Space Physics (doi:10.1029/2020JA028656). The numerical methods associated with the model development are published in the Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series (doi:10.3847/1538-4365/ab3a4c) and computational physics related journals (doi:10.1016/j.jcp.2018.08.020, doi:10.5194/gmd-14-859-2021) Object 2: Completed. The PI and collaborators have used the coupled geospace model to study the dynamic evolution of meso-scale structures in the ionosphere, which is related to the ion upflow and outflow in the topside ionosphere. The coupled model was used to simulate several solar eclipese events, with multiple instrumental results serving as the validation of the simulation results. The solar eclipse simulation results were published in American Geophysical Union's top journal Geophysical Research Letters (doi:10.1029/2019JA027268). The influence of causally-driven ionospheric outflow on the mode of magnetospheric convection is re-visited using the coupled global model. The research team has found a new relationship between the magnetospheric sawtooth oscillation and the amount of ionospheric outflow when the source location is in the dayside cusp region. Numerical experiments have shown that the rate of cusp O+ ion outflow is not the only control factor of the sawtooth mode, as stated in the Brambles et al. [2011] Science paper. This work has been published in Geophysical Research Letters (doi:10.1029/2019GL086419). Object 3: Completed. The research team has successfully isolated the role of thermospheric wind and mass density on the generation of ionospheric O+ upflow and outflow. The research team has also demonstrated a new pathway of thermospheric influence to the geospace system: through its regulation of ionospheric outflows influences magnetosphere-ionosphere convection and the ion composition, symmetries, x-line perimeter and magnetic merging of the magnetosphere. This new finding is illustrated using controlled simulations and observation from a geomagnetic storm event, and the results were published in the American Geophysical Union's top journal Journal of Geophysical Research - Space Physics (doi:10.1029/2020JA028656).

27302018.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27302018.value: This research project has successfully developed a new global-scale computer simulation model for predicting the near-Earth space environment, including the layers of the ionosphere, thermosphere and magnetosphere driving by the solar wind. The new model includes the physical module of describing the ions outflowing from the Earth's ionosphere. The team has identified new physical pathways of how the upper atmosphere influences the near-Earth space environment, via providing additional ion composition and changing the state of the magnetosphere. The new model is expected to provide more accurate predictions for space weather events especially geomagnetic storms
