27302618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27302618.value: While the instrumental record shows a clear decrease in the Arctic sea ice cover during the last decades, it is not possible to compare this trend to the natural, pre-anthropogenic, sea ice variability since we have very limited data predating the 1970’s. It is thus difficult to assess what are the primary factors controlling the temporal and spatial extent of Arctic sea ice. Potential disruption of the intermediate water layer, called the halocline, due to ongoing climate change, is suspected to be one cause for the observed sea ice decline. The halocline isolates the surface sea ice from the warmer Atlantic water, protecting it from further melting via close contact with this warm bottom water mass. However, our limited understanding of the processes regulating the strength of the Arctic halocline restricts our ability to forecast near-future consequences of the on-going climate warming trend. Sea-ice cover plays a critical role in regulating global climate, due to its high albedo (i.e., capacity to reflect solar energy), which controls the radiative budget of the Earth. In addition, sea ice regulates the Arctic hydrological cycle through its control on evaporation and precipitation. Finally, sea ice cover influences biological activity in the Arctic Ocean since primary productivity and thus carbon export is limited under sea ice. Therefore, the recent decrease of the Arctic sea ice cover and the prospect of an ice-free summer Arctic Ocean in the near-future could dramatically affect global climate. The proposed project will document the evolution of the halocline and thus the stratification of the Western Arctic during the last climatic cycle. We will use the geochemical composition of benthic calcareous microorganisms (ostracods) to reconstruct the depth of the halocline at four key locations in the Western side of the Arctic. By comparing our stratification reconstruction to published sea ice proxies we will significantly improve our understanding of the mechanisms responsible for sea ice variability during this period. Furthermore, our findings will provide crucial information to improve the integration of sea ice dynamics in climate models and thus enhance the accuracy of sea ice cover projections. 雖有科學記錄證明在過去幾十年裏北冰洋海冰覆蓋率明顯下降，但由於1970年代之前的數據非常有限，此下降趨勢無法與有人類活動之前該處海冰的自然變化進行比較，因此難以找出影響北極海冰覆蓋時間及範圍的主要因素 。因持續的氣候變化對北冰洋中間水體（即鹽躍層）的潛在改變可能是做成海冰減少的其中一個原因。 鹽躍層將北冰洋表面海冰與較溫暖的大西洋海流隔開，避免海冰與溫暖的底部水體接觸，減緩海冰融化速度。然而，我們對北冰洋調節鹽躍層強度和深度的機制了解有限，以致我們難以預測當下氣候變暖趨勢的影響 。 海冰覆蓋在調節全球氣候方面都發揮著關鍵性的作用，其高反照率（即反射太陽能的能力）有助控制地球所接收的輻射能量。此外，海冰通過控制海水蒸發和降雨來調節北冰洋的水循環。再者，海冰覆蓋會影響北冰洋的生物活動，從而影響該海域的初級生產力，並限制碳排放。因此，近期北冰洋海冰覆蓋面的減少、甚至未來可能出現的北冰洋無冰夏季或會廣泛影響全球氣候。 此項目將會重建最近一次氣候週期北冰洋西部水體分層及鹽躍層的演變。我們通過利用底棲鈣質微生物（介形蟲）的化學成分來重建北冰洋西部四個關鍵位置的鹽躍層深度，並將我們的水體分層重建與已公佈的海冰覆蓋估算進行比較。我們的研究結果將可提供關鍵的信息，增加我們對最近一次氣候週期北冰洋海冰變化的機制的理解，以及改善海冰動力學在氣候模型中的整合，從而提升海冰覆蓋預測的準確性。

27302618.label: Realisation of objectives
27302618.value: Warming of the Arctic is occurring faster than any other region on Earth due to a variety of positive feedback mechanisms that operate in the high north. One such mechanism is the advection of relatively warm Atlantic-origin waters to the Arctic Ocean, which will likely increase under continued polar sea-ice demise and further accelerate warming throughout the region. However, climate models have struggled to capture the full magnitude of this effect, resulting in potentially underestimated projections of near-future warming and changes in other elements of the ocean-climate system such as the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC). In this project we used, paleotemperature reconstruction of the bottom water mass at different water depth of the Chukchi plateau to reconstructed the water masses stratification over the last 800,000 years. Below a summary of the findings is describe for each objective. Objective 1: To estimate the temperature of the bottom water masses from sediment cores of the Chukchi Plateau in the Western Arctic Ocean. As mentioned in the mid-term report, 618 ostracods coming from 3 sediment cores located in the Chukchi plateau were analysed for their trace element to calcium ratio in their shells. The 3 cores are located along a water depth gradient in the Chukchi plateau, in order to test water masses stratification changes. The 3 sediment cores ARC3-P31 (78.012º N, 168.016º E, 434 m water depth), ARC7-P12 (78.287ºN, 160.688ºE, 580 m water depth) and ARC6-R14 (78.637ºN, 160.448ºE, 741 m water depth) were extracted from the Chukchi Plateau in the western Arctic Ocean during Chinese Arctic Research Expeditions III, VII, and VI respectively. The chronostratigraphy of cores was established to range from the Holocene to MIS 13 by our collaborator from Tongji University based on a combination of AMS 14C dating, core correlation of ice rafted debris (IRD) record, foraminifera abundance and lithostratigraphy. From the 618 ostracods analysed, 546 were from the Krithe genus, whereas Polycope genus. This work represent the first attempt to analyses E/Ca in Polycope. Potential contamination bias in Mg/Ca and Sr/Ca from detrital material was evaluated to ensure the robustness of the proxies as well as the comparability between the genera have been published in Rodriguez et al., 2020 (See part C). Using the findings obtained from this publication (contamination, juvenile stage impact, etc.) we reconstructed the temperature from the Mg/Ca ratios of Krithe ostracods. Objective 2 and 3: To determine the halocline depth in the Chukchi Plateau and To reconstruct the variability of the Arctic water masses’ stratification over the last climatic cycle in the Western Arctic Ocean. By comparing our reconstructed temperature, we attributed a water mass for each sedimentary layer, using an average temperature of 1˚C to 2˚C for the Atlantic layer and below 0˚C for the Arctic Intermediate water. Today, cores ARC3-P31 and ARC7-P12 are located within the Atlantic Layer, whereas ARC6-R14 is located at the boundary between the Atlantic Layer and AIW and our reconstruction of the most recent sediment fit the oceanographic observation. For the three water depths (434m, 580m, 741m) represented by the three sediment cores we evaluated if the Atlantic water or Arctic Intermediate water were present for each time periods. As the halocline thickness influence the Atlantic layer depth (e.g. thicker halocline leads to deeper Atlantic water mass), being able to identified the presence of Atlantic water at a certain depth provide valuable information of the halocline depth. Based on our results we observe two scenario, one during which high supply of freshwater (river discharge, precipitation) produce a thin and strong halocline with a shallow Atlantic layer and a second scenario where low freshwater supply driven by heavy ice condition result in a weak but thick halocline and deep Atlantic layer. We identified MIS 3, 5, 7 and 9 as intensified stadial regime whereas the other time period investigated correspond to weaker stadial regime. In this regime, MIS 11 appears to be an exception in that Atlantic-layer temperatures are recorded at 951 m, which may be linked to the exceptionally strong AMOC and intensified Atlantic inflow to the Arctic region during this interval. Objective 4 and 5: To characterize the role of the water masses stratification in the sea ice variability of the Arctic Ocean over the last climatic cycle and To evaluate the role of the western Arctic Ocean stratification in the Arctic climate. We compare our data with perennial sea-ice cover and observe a clear relationship, where thick halocline reconstruction correspond to period with high sea-ice coverage. The new constraints on past Arctic BWT conditions presented here provide additional insights into the behaviour of ocean circulation and water-mass stratification along the Chukchi Plateau on inter-interglacial timescales. A key finding of our study is that MIS 5 was not an anomalously warm interval in the western Arctic, and that the general hydrographic regime of MIS 5 was similar to other late-Pleistocene interglacial periods with relatively extensive ice cover such as stages 3 and 7. Another novel finding presented here is that the AMOC may have regulated the strength and vertical position of the Atlantic inflow layer to the western Arctic throughout past interglacial periods, with the stronger AMOC of MIS 11 being associated with a deeper base of the Atlantic layer (of at least 951 m) and the weaker AMOC of MIS 9 being associated with reduced Atlantic inflow. Increased Atlantic influence in the Arctic during MIS 11 may have helped to sustain reduced perennial sea-ice cover and the inferred absence of thick ice shelves.

27302618.label: Major findings and research outcome
27302618.value: The finding of this project allowed us to present new constraints on 1) the intra valve variability of trace element to calcium ratio (Mg/Ca and Sr/Ca) in Arctic ostracods 2) the strength and depth position of the Atlantic inflow layer along the Chukchi Plateau in the western Arctic Ocean during past warm interglacial periods based on bottom-water temperature reconstructed via the Mg/Ca content of Krithe ostracod specimens. Findings on the Mg/Ca and Sr/Ca intra valve variability are important to strengthen the use of trace element to calcium ratio as paleo proxies and have been published in Rodriguez et al., 2020. Our findings highlight the clear need for an extensive cleaning of the shells to avoid bias in the paleo reconstruction. In this paper we also report for the first time trace element to calcium ration in ostracods valve from the genus Polycope. These report are the first step to extend the use of E/Ca as paleo proxies to Polycope genus and therefore refine the paleo reconstruction by 1) increasing the number of sample available, 2) allowing the comparison of paleo reconstruction obtained by different genus/species Using the data obtained in this project we are capable to provide additional support to the previously proposed hydrographic regimes of Atlantic inflow regulated by halocline variability associated with the presence or absence of thick ice shelves and perennial sea-ice cover for an extended period that previously available. Our new records, which span from marine isotope stage (MIS) 19 to 1 shows variability in the stratification of the water column in the Wester Arctic. Two novel paleoclimatic discoveries are identified from the data. First, exceptional warming and hydrographic conditions during MIS 5, typically invoked as an anomalously warm period and potential Holocene analogue, were not found to occur in the Arctic. Secondly, the available evidence supports the presence of an extended base of the Atlantic inflow layer during MIS 11, another particularly warm period and potential Holocene analogue, which may be associated with the vigorous AMOC inferred from several other independent paleoceanographic records of MIS 11. A strengthened AMOC and Atlantic advection to the Arctic Ocean could have likely been relevant for sustaining low-ice conditions, which may have also had implications for the influence of Arctic export waters on deep-water formation in the Nordic Seas as previously hypothesized. The latest part is currently in preparation for submission in Quaternary Science Review.

27302618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27302618.value: Two directions for further research has been identified from this project. First, developing calibration of E/Ca with environmental parameters to use other genus/species, which will improve our understanding of the strengths and limitations of the use of these proxies and ultimately increase the accuracy of Arctic paleo reconstructions. For example, combining paleotemperature reconstruction from different species will allow the reduction of the uncertainties on temperature reconstruction. Secondly, only limited findings on the Western Arctic stratification are available for time periods older than MIS3 and our results suggest a different climatic response of the Arctic vs the North Atlantic in older time period such as MIS5 and MIS1, therefore additional work on these time periods is needed to strengthen our understanding of the relationship between Arctic water masses stratification and global climate.

27302618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27302618.value: Using the geochemistry of ostracods, marine micro-fossil crustacean, we reconstructed the bottom water temperature of the several location with the Chukchi Shelf of the Western Arctic Ocean. Paleotemperature reconstruction cover the last 800 000 years. Based on these paleotemperature we reconstructed the depth of the Arctic water masses and linked it with the presence of sea ice and the North Atlantic input reaching the Western Arctic Ocean. We identified that in older warm periods (MIS11 and older) of the Earth, the temperature of the water masses are relatively similar as today, with relatively high impact of the Atlantic layer in the low abundance of sea-ice, however during younger period, the western Arctic was recover by a thicker sea-ice layer, probably related to the limited reach of the Atlantic layer in the Chukchi shelf.

27501618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27501618.value: This proposed project studies technology upgrading in an export supply chain of the dragon fruit industry of Vietnam. Despite demand for high-quality fruits from overseas markets, the supply of dragon fruits that meet export standards is surprisingly low. Observations on agricultural practices show persistent use of low technology along the supply chain. I hypothesize that a key reason for the lack of supply of export-quality dragon fruits is that farmers and intermediaries lack the information and technological resources that are necessary to produce and trade high-quality agricultural products. I plan to test this hypothesis through a randomized control trial that generates exogenous variation in access to information and training on an export-oriented agricultural technology for dragon fruit farmers and intermediaries in Binh Thuan, Vietnam. As part of a seed project, I have finished conducting a baseline survey with 579 farmers and 208 intermediaries across 16 communes in this province. The proposed project will use this baseline information to randomly sample, within each stratum, a subset of communes for treatment assignment. The treatment will offer farmers and intermediaries the opportunity to receive information and training on applying new export-oriented technology for growing and processing dragon fruits. I use this variation to understand whether and how technology upgrading in the supply chain occurs as a response to the information and technology intervention. To the best of my knowledge, this is the first study to exogenously generate information and technology transfers along the supply chain. Specifically, the experiment is designed to have three treatment groups, where in the first treatment group only farmers are assigned to the technology shock, in the second treatment group only intermediaries are assigned to the treatment, and in the third treatment group both farmers and intermediaries are offered the technology transfer. This will allow me to answer two questions: (i) whether technology transfer is more effective when it is simultaneously provided to both farmers and intermediaries compared with when only one group is exposed to the positive technology shock and (ii) whether and to what extent technology diffusion occurs in a vertical supply chain relationship. The findings of this research will provide useful implications for designing policies aimed at developing high-value agricultural sectors and nurturing sustainable export-oriented supply chains. 該擬議項目研究了越南火龍果產業出口供應鏈的技術革新。盡管海外市場對高品質水果有需求，達到出口標準的火龍果供應量卻出乎意料地低。對農業實踐的觀察表明，供應鏈中持續使用低端技術。我假定缺少達到出口品質火龍果供應量的一個關鍵原因是農民與中介機構缺少生產和交易高品質農產品所必需的信息和技術資源。 我計劃通過一項隨機對照實驗來驗證該假設， 該隨機對照實驗在為越南平順省的火龍果農民和中介機構提供的關於出口導向型農業技術的信息和培訓中產生了外源性差異。作為種子項目的一部分，我已經在該省份的16個社區中完成了對579位農民和208家中介機構的基線調查。我會使用此基線信息在社區下屬的每一層中隨機取樣來獲得解決方案。該解決方案將會為農民和中介機構提供獲得將新出口導向型技術應用到種植和生產火龍果進程中的信息和培訓的機會。我將此差異應用在理解產業鏈中的技術革新是否作為信息和技術干擾的回應出現，並同時理解技術革新是如何作為此回應而出現。 據我所知，這是第一項在供應鏈中產生外源性信息和技術遷移的研究。特別的是，該實驗被設計為含有三個實驗組。在第一個實驗組中，只有農民被分配至面對此技術衝擊，在第二個實驗組中，僅有中介機構被分配至此方案，而在第三個實驗組中，農民和中介機構均面臨此技術遷移。這將使我得以回答以下的兩個問題：（一）與只有一組實驗對象面臨積極的技術衝擊的情況作對比，是否當農民和中介機構同時面臨之時的技術遷移更有效果；（二）在垂直供應鏈關係中，技術擴散是否出現並且在多大程度上出現。此研究的發現將會為設計意欲發展高品質農業板塊和培育可持續的出口導向型供應鏈的政策提供一些有用的啟示與意義。

27501618.label: Realisation of objectives
27501618.value: To accomplish the five objectives, we conducted a field experiment in the dragon fruit supply chain in Vietnam. This supply chain offers an ideal context to examine the impact of technology training and buyer-supplier complementarity on quality upgrading. Dragon fruit is a popular cash crop grown in several South-central provinces in Vietnam, mostly cultivated by smallholder farmers. Farmers typically sell dragon fruit to small local collectors, who then resell to exporting intermediaries or domestic retailers. Contracts are rarely used in local trade and farmers often sell to the local collector who offers the highest price on the spot market. Due to such competition among small collectors and lack of contracts, the relationship between farmers and local collectors are largely unstable in the market. The experiment was conducted in two major districts in Binh Thuan Province in Vietnam. We formed farmer-intermediary clusters by randomly matching farmer groups and exporting intermediaries from the same commune. We randomly introduced a training intervention on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) to each cluster, which is a set of agricultural management practices designed to improve food safety and product quality. Each cluster was randomly assigned to one of four treatment arms: (1) farmer-only training, (2) intermediary-only training, (3) farmer-intermediary joint training, and (4) no training which serves as our control group. The content of the training program was identical across all training groups. In total, our sample consists of 88 farmer-intermediary clusters with 1,141 farmers and 234 exporting intermediaries participating in the experiment (Objective 5). We utilize two independent methods to obtain accurate measures of product quality. The first measure is the score from an on-farm audit on GAP compliance, which evaluates the implementation of quality upgrading practices; this measure is mandatory for most agricultural quality certificates. We conducted the GAP audit twice, 6 and 12 months after the training respectively, for every participating farmer by agronomists specializing in dragon fruit. The second quality measure is based on a pesticide residue analysis conducted by an ISO-certified laboratory. We tested the residues of 18 different types of pesticides to examine their compliance with international standards on pesticide residue limits, based on which we constructed a standardized quality index as the second quality measure. We estimate the effects of technology training on quality upgrading and market performance (Objective 2). Three main results can be drawn. First, farmer-only training improves quality upgrading substantially, by 0.43 standard deviation as measured by GAP compliance. Second, joint training generates a significantly larger effect: it increases GAP compliance by 0.64 standard deviation. Third, intermediary training has no significant impact on farmers' GAP compliance.We find similar results when using lab-tested pesticide residue as the measure for quality. The farmer-only training and joint training reduce the average pesticide residue substantially, with a stronger effect from the latter. They also reduce the incidence of violating the Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) set by European Commission by 31 and 50 percent. We find that 12 months after the intervention, farmers in joint training group receive higher farm-gate prices (by 11.5 percent), revenue (by 20 percent), and profits (by 10-14 percent). This is consistent with the finding that farmers in joint training clusters have significantly higher chances of exporting to high-price markets. Surprisingly, there is no significant effect on farm sales, profits, or export destinations for farmers in the farmer-only training group, although estimation results show they improved quality. We document two mechanisms through which the training intervention improves quality upgrading and farm-gate performance (Objective 1): knowledge transfer and linkage with downstream buyers. Using unique data on farmers' knowledge on GAP collected in the experiment, we find that farmer-only training substantially increases farmers' knowledge on GAP by 0.299 standard deviation. However, joint training does not improve farmers' GAP knowledge more. After controlling for knowledge, the effects of farmer-only training and joint training on quality upgrading decreases by 20 - 30 percent, suggesting knowledge transfer as an important mechanism. However, this result also implies that some other mechanisms associated with the training intervention---such as newly established trade linkages with downstream buyers---may have contributed to quality upgrading too, because after controlling for knowledge joint training still has a large effect. Using survey data on contract formation and trade partners, we test the second and novel mechanism of farmers' linkages with downstream buyers. The joint training provided an opportunity for farmers and exporting intermediaries to establish linkages with each other. This linkage may be responsible for the greater effect of joint training relative to farmer-only training, and the persistence of the significant effect of joint training even after accounting for an increase in knowledge. We find that joint training substantially increases trade between farmers and downstream exporting intermediaries in the same cluster by 30 percent, half of which is arranged through informal contracts. By contrast, we find no economically or statistically significant increase in trade activities for clusters assigned to farmer-only training or intermediary-only training. We provide evidence consistent with the idea that linkages between farmers and exporting intermediaries incentivize quality upgrading through overcoming asymmetric information on quality and mistrust (Objective 1). We find that farmers who trade with exporting intermediaries receiving joint training together receive a higher price premium from upgrading quality, relative to farmers who trade with other intermediaries (Objective 3). The result implies that linkage with exporter may help (partially) overcome information asymmetry on quality; thus, when the farmer improves quality, the connected exporter knows it better than non-connected buyers and, therefore, is willing to pay more. Interestingly, buyer-supplier linkage generates no additional benefit to quality upgrading along the observable/verifiable quality dimensions (e.g., color, size, sweetness, etc.), lending further support to the information asymmetry and mistrust argument (Objective 4). We also provide evidence to show that mitigation of search friction is unlikely to drive our main results. We conduct several tests on alternative explanations. We find no evidence of farmer-intermediary knowledge complementarity in driving farmers' quality upgrading (Objective 3).

27501618.label: Major findings and research outcome
27501618.value: The main finding is that while technology training promotes quality upgrading, the buyer-supplier linkages boost quality upgrading substantially. Specifically, training farmers and exporting intermediaries together generates a much larger effect on quality upgrading than that when only farmers are trained. The results are robust to different quality measures specified in our pre-analysis plan — farm audits conducted by experts and laboratory tests on pesticide residue. More specifically, we exploit our experimental design to document two mechanisms that contribute to quality upgrading: (i) knowledge transfer and (ii) linkage with downstream buyers. Training increased farmers’ knowledge on quality-enhancing technology, relaxing a supply-side constraint to quality upgrading. Interestingly, training farmers and exporting intermediaries altogether helps establish buyer-supplier linkages, as evidenced by increased within-cluster trade, of which half were based on informal contracts. The improved linkage resulted in a higher price premium to quality at the farm gate. The paper is currently under review for publication at the American Economic Review. In addition, the paper was accepted for oral presentation at several top economics conferences, including the North East University Development Consortium (NEUDC) 2020, 41st Virtual BREAD Conference on Development Economics (NYU), and 2022 AEA/ASSA Annual Meeting.

27501618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27501618.value: Our findings of the paper have important policy implications. In particular, the findings suggest that training programs, as widely adopted by many governments in developing countries, can be more effective if they can help the trainees to establish buyer-seller linkages, besides transferring knowledge. The results also suggest that in policy evaluations, we need to take into account the role of linkages in supply chains to accurately assess the impact of training programs on technology adoption decisions and business performances.

27501618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27501618.value: Farmers do not often have direct contact with larger or multinational buyers and exporters and rely, instead, on intermediaries to sell products and share information on new technologies and market factors. However, intermediaries do not always have an incentive to help farmers improve output quality due to lack of stable relationship and trust, especially if quality is costly to observe and long-term contracts are rarely used in agricultural sectors in developing countries. As a result, quality improvement is not always rewarded and farmers have low incentives to upgrade quality. But when farmers and intermediaries can build connections and trust, both are more likely to benefit from higher prices and higher quality products. Our project shows that jointly training dragon fruit farmers and intermediaries on quality-enhancing technologies created a forum for them to build trust and buyer-supplier relationships, leading to higher adoption of the training technologies, more farm investments, and higher prices paid to farmers. Our findings generate direct implications for government policy through shedding light on the importance of buyer-supplier relationships in supply chains for promoting agricultural product quality.

27502318.value: 全球化、资本偏向型技术进步和劳动收入占比

27502318.label: Project Objectives
27502318.value: Construct firm-level panels for different countries in ORBIS. Decompose changes in labor shares at country-industry level into a within-firm technological change component and a reallocation effect. Identify the impact of import, export, inward and outward multinational activities on within-firm technological changes and the reallocation effect. rows: Construct firm-level panels for different countries in ORBIS.

27502318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27502318.value: An important trend in the past 30 years is the decline in labor shares. In other words, the share of national income that goes to the workers has been declining. Given that capital is owned mainly by wealthy people, this secular trend suggests a rise in income inequality. One plausible explanation in the literature is capital-biased technological change, i.e., production technologies increasingly demand capital rather than labor. However, the literature has treated technology as a black box, and it is not well-understood why technological changes have been favoring capital. This project aims to understand how firm heterogeneity in technology choices coupled with globalization has contributed to capital-biased technological changes, therefore to the decline of labor shares. There is large heterogeneity in the proportions of capital and labor used in production even among firms in a narrowly-defined industry. Such firm heterogeneity in technologies, however, is underexplored in the literature. Globalization forces - such as international trade and multinational production (MP) - can reallocate capital and labor across firms with different technologies. If the more capital-intensive firms gain market shares after trade and MP liberalization, such reallocation will increase the demand for capital relative to labor, and lead to an increase in rental rates relative to wages and a decline in labor shares. This “reallocation effect” makes the “aggregate production technology” biased towards capital. On the other hand, individual firms may adopt capital-biased technologies over time. The “within-firm technological changes” can also contribute to the decline in labor shares. The remaining questions are the relative importance of these two effects, as well as the role of trade and multinational production in determining such effects. In this project, I will use a panel dataset on firms in different countries from 1999 to 2012 (ORBIS) to answer these questions. I first decompose the change in the labor shares into two components, the “reallocation effect” and “within-firm technological change”. I further separate the impact of multinational firms and local firms within this decomposition framework. Second, I will use an instrumental variable approach to test the impact of trade and multinational production on these two components, guided by predictions from a theoretical model I developed in an earlier paper. The results will shed light on our understanding of the labor share decline and provide guidance to redistribution policies.

27502718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27502718.value: This proposal studies how administration discretion affects the effectiveness of accounting regulation by examining determinants of SEC review outcomes and efforts in Confidential Treatment Order (CTO) reviews. Although the role of the SEC in security law execution is critical, no prior studies have investigated individual characteristics of SEC reviewers as determinants of the agency’s regulatory review process. To execute the research question, I focus on the setting of CTO reviews. CTO review is the process of deciding whether the SEC would grant a firm nondisclosure of information in a firm’s filings. This offers several advantages in studying the SEC’s decision process. First, as the process is mandatory for all firms, it effectively mitigates any endogenous concerns related to the SEC in the selection of review cases. Second, the CTO decision is based on assessing the ambiguous concept “materiality”, thus enabling the SEC staff to use discretion over the status regulation. Third, the primary purpose of the CTO regulation is to both ensure investors’ rights to access material information, as well as protect firms from possible disclosure harms. This unique setting enables testing how effectively the SEC balances the two parties’ interests. Empirically, I look into two sets of reviewer-specific factors. First, reviewers’ discretion over mechanical regulations is important, as it requires expertise to identify evidence against strategic disclosures. I thus expect more capable SEC staff may result in a higher likelihood of redaction amendments, but uses a shorter review time. I also investigate whether staff personal judgments drive the balance between the firm and investors in review decisions. The likelihood of amendments is expected to be higher if the SEC reviewers have a stronger incentive to protect investors, whereas the possibility of amendments is lower if the SEC reviewers are more sympathetic to the proprietary costs of disclosures. Finally, I expect and test whether overly loose approval of CTO applications results in higher implied volatility and cost of capital that is consistent with an opacity-imposed cost to investors. Overall, the proposal is expected to the first empirical evidence regarding front-line administration staff discretions and will contribute to the understanding of SEC administration in the process of regulation execution, which helps regulators and administrators in improving the effectiveness of accounting regulations, as well as provides investors with a deeper comprehension of the security regulation process that enables them to achieve better judgments of their investment decisions. 本研究透过分析证券交易委员会（证交会）对企业信息保密申请（Confidential Treatment Order或CTO）的审核过程，旨在研究自由裁量权与会计监管效率的关系。尽管证交会在证券监管过程中扮演重要角色，但目前尚无文献研究证交会行政人员的特征如何影响其监管过程及监管效率。 为了回答这一问题，本文实证分析了证交会审核员的CTO审核过程。具体而言，在CTO审核过程中，审核员需就企业关于在其公开文件中隐藏部分信息的申请进行审核，并决定是否批准企业的申请。就研究自由裁量权与会计监管效率的关系而言，CTO审核这一研究设定具备如下优势：第一，所有企业的CTO申请都必须经由证交会审核，这有助于解决选择性偏差这一内生性问题--即证交会选择性地审核部分具备某种特征的企业；第二，CTO审核的核心原则是“重要性”，即原则上企业只能隐藏对投资者而言并不重要的信息。但由于证交会对于“重要性“原则并无精确和严格的定义，因此证交会审核员在审核过程中具有充足的自由裁量权；第三，CTO审核主要有两方面的目的：一是确保投资者能够及时获得重要信息；二是保护企业的专有信息及降低信息披露的“专有成本”。这一特征有助于我们了解证交会如何有效地权衡投资者和企业双方的利益。 实证方面，本文重点关注审核员两方面的特征。其一，CTO审核过程中，审核员必须具备足够的专业能力去应用和执行与CTO审核相关的法规，因此审核员的专业能力在该过程中起到关键性作用。显然，专业能力较高的审核员更有可能识别企业的策略性披露行为--即企业刻意隐藏对投资者而言重要的信息。因此，本文预测专业能力较高的审核员有更高的概率否决企业的CTO申请，并且其所需的审核时间更短。其次，本文研究了审核员个体判断对审核结果的影响。具体而言，当审核员有更强的意愿去保护投资者时，企业的CTO申请被否决的概率更高。相反，当其有更强的意愿去保护企业的专有信息时，企业的CTO申请被否决的概率更低。最后，本文研究了相对宽松的审核过程是否提高了企业和投资者间的信息不对称，进而引致负面的结果，诸如提高企业价值的隐含波动率以及企业的融资成本等。综上，本研究首次对证交所一线行政人员的自由裁量权进行了实证分析。研究结论增进了我们对自由裁量权在证券监管过程中的作用的理解，并有助于监管层和行政人员改进和提高会计监管的效率。与此同时，本文增进了投资者对证券监管过程的理解并有助于他们改进其投资决策。

Understand the underlying mechanisms through which mortgage securitization influence bank portfolio management and lending strategies.
Explore the related real economic impact: how mortgage securitization affects job creation through small businesses.

27502918.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27502918.value: The popularity of mortgage securitization not only changes banks’ business model in the mortgage market, but also affects non-mortgage lending by changing the way banks manage liquidity and risk. Specifically, mortgage securitization could free up bank liquidity and allow banks to increase lending to non-mortgage sectors. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are likely among the mostly-impacted non-mortgage borrowers, as they largely rely on risky and illiquid loans from relationship banks. Since SMEs are essential growth drivers and job creators to the economy, the financial implications on SME lending could also have important real consequences. This project aims at understanding how policy shocks to mortgage securitization impact SME financing and the related real consequences. The estimation is based on changes in the securitization policy by government sponsored enterprises (GSEs) in the US. As the dominating securitization channel in the US mortgage market, GSE mortgage securitization is determined by the national conforming loan limit (CLL), which specifies the maximum size of mortgage that could be securitized by GSEs. While a uniform change of CLL is exogenous to any single market, it could have stronger impacts on mortgage securitization in markets where a larger share of mortgage loans fall close to the threshold. Given this, the effects of GSE policy change vary across banks that operates in different markets, and we could use this cross-bank variation as an instrument to estimate the causal effect of mortgage securitization on bank lending to SMEs. Based on this instrumental variable approach, I use a unique loan-level dataset of small business credit to estimate the financial and economic effects on SMEs. This dataset tracks each SME’s credit activities over time and provides information on the quantity and pricing of each loan. By controlling for firm-year fixed effect, I could cleanly identify the credit supply effect by comparing lendings to the same borrower from different banks. This dataset also allows me to estimate the real economic consequences on employment and sales of the impacted businesses. This study is expected to have three main contributions. First, it will shed light on how an important innovation in mortgage financing impacts non-mortgage financing by banks. Second, it will help us better understand the related real economic consequences. Third, the findings will allow policy makers to better evaluate the role of financial intermediaries under the related evolutions in the credit market. 过去数十年来， 美国市场住房贷款的证券化经历了飞速的发展，并对银行的资产及风险管理模式产生了系统性的影响。目前来看，已有的研究主要集中在房贷证券化对银行整体流动性和风险的影响，而尚未涉及更加围观层面的问题，如对银行在不同信贷业务领域， 尤其是流动性相对较低业务的资金配置等。 一方面来说，房贷证券化能够让银行释放更多的流动性，从而增加对非住房抵押类信贷业务的资金倾斜；另一方面，近期的一些研究提出，房贷证券化增大了银行的风险状况而这将使得银行在高风险，低流动性业务上的借款意愿下降。本研究课题希望通过基于政策变化的工具变量模型对这一问题进行仔细的实证研究。 本课题预计有以下方面的主要贡献：其一，研究结果预计能够帮助大家更好的理解金融创新的跨市场影响；其二，本课题同时希望能探索这些潜在影响对实体经济的作用；其三，本课题成果能够对政策制定者更好的评估信贷市场带来帮助。

27502918.label: Realisation of objectives
27502918.value: The most fundamental root of this project’s objectives is to obtain a more comprehensive understanding on a very important question to financial regulators and policy makers: how do banks’ liquidity conditions impact their credit allocation to small and medium enterprises (SMEs), which are the backbone of most economies’ growth and job creation, and what are the real economic impacts from the consequential changes in bank credit provision to SMEs? In the proposal, we expected to answer this fundamental question by using the expansion of mortgage securitization as an instrument, as it enables banks to free up liquidity by getting rid of mortgage assets off balance sheets. However, our early-stage empirical investigations show that securitization not only impact bank liquidity, but may also affect banks’ incentive of allocating credit resources between mortgage v.s. non-mortgage sectors. Therefore, in order to obtain cleaner understanding on the economic mechanisms and to generate unambiguous policy implications, we disentangle the fundamental liquidity-driven aspect from the cross-sector credit allocation aspect, and realize our objectives through the following research papers: In the main research paper, which is recently published in the Review of Corporate Finance Studies (Lin, C., Tai, M. and Xie, W., 2023. Credit environment and small business dynamics: Evidence from establishment-level data. The Review of Corporate Finance Studies, 12(2), pp.326-365.), we focus on the fundamental, liquidity-driven aspect and realize our first objective by directly testing how an exogenous shock that improves bank funding liquidity impacts bank credit provision across different small and medium enterprises (SMEs). By using micro-level data on small business lending by each bank to each county’ SME borrowers in different size categories, we find that in response to positive liquidity shocks, banks only increase lending to relatively larger SMEs, but not to the smallest micro businesses. We then realize our second objective by understanding the mechanism that drives such liquidity-driven lending outcomes: as the positive liquidity shock increases banks’ charter value by lowering costs of funds, the impacted banks’ risk-taking incentive is lowered, leading them to increase lending to relatively larger SMEs but not the smallest micro businesses that are much riskier. This charter-value mechanism is supported by our empirical finding that an exogenous shock that improves bank funding liquidity can significantly lower banks’ costs of funds (as measured by the ratio of average interest costs to deposits) as well as improve banks’ charter value (as measured by the market-to-book ratio of bank equity). Most importantly, we realize the third objective by showing that the disproportionate credit provision across SMEs results in unintended real consequences: a crowding-out effect on micro firms. Specifically, as larger SMEs obtain better access to credit from banks that receive positive liquidity shocks, these larger entities’ expansion stifles the development of micro firms, whose access to credit remains unchanged. As a consequence, micro businesses experience lower employment and sales growth despite the expansion of aggregate bank liquidity and credit supply. By providing concrete evidence on the real economic impact of bank credit allocation to small businesses, our findings not only enable us to well achieve the listed objectives of the project, but also generate important implications to policy makers and economists, who often do not distinguish micro businesses from relatively larger SMEs when considering supporting jobs and growth by encouraging bank lending to the real sector. According to a report by the Association for Enterprise Opportunity (2013), “If one in three Main Street microbusinesses hired a single employee, the United States would be at full employment.” The estimation is similar in other economies like Hong Kong. Given the importance of micro businesses to the economy, our research suggests that policies aiming at helping SMEs should consider the separate effects on micro businesses and larger firms. The distinction between micro and other small businesses is critical to understanding the transmission mechanisms through which SME finance affects economic development (Bernanke 2010; Beck 2013; Yellen 2013). In another research paper (Lin, C., Qin, S., and Tai, M., 2023. Regulatory-Driven Crowd Out on Small Business Lending.), we conduct complementary analyses to focus on the cross-sector credit-allocation aspect and investigate how a regulatory-driven expansion of mortgage lending can generate unintended financial and real impacts on SMEs. From this aspect, we realize the first objective by showing that in response to an exogenous positive shock to mortgage credit supply, banks actually shrink their lending to small businesses, leading to a crowding-out effect on SME credit especially in low- and moderate-income (LMI) neighborhoods. To realize the second objective and explore the underlying mechanism, we adopt a difference-in-difference-in-difference empirical strategy by interactively utilizing two regulation shocks to the mortgage and small business credit markets. We show that the crowding-out effect on SME credit is due to banks’ regulatory constraints: under the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), banks are encouraged to meet the credit needs of households and small businesses in low- and moderate-income (LMI) neighborhoods. However, when the regulatory-constrained banks can easily fulfill the regulatory requirement on credit provision to the LMI communities via the expansion of mortgage lending, they will cut lending to small businesses without jeopardizing their CRA assessment performance. This mechanism is supported by our finding that the crowding-out effect is stronger for banks facing stronger regulatory pressure (measured by their CRA examination performance). Moreover, we realize the third objective by investigating the real consequences of this regulatory-driven crowd-out effect. Using longitudinal data on the U.S establishments that includes job creation and sales, we find that the crowding-out effect on small business credit leads to a significant decline in employment and sales of the impacted SMEs. Meanwhile, bankruptcy and foreclosure rates are also significantly higher in the impacted neighborhoods after the housing market collapsed. Besides realizing the listed objectives, this second research paper also has an important policy implication: when regulators assess bank credit provision in different product lines aggregately, it may generate unintended consequences regarding the distribution of credit resources across different economic sectors. Given this, evaluating bank performance in each credit sector separately may alleviate the unintended distributional concerns and improve the effectiveness of the regulations. References Bernanke, B. 2010. Restoring the flow of credit to small businesses. Federal Reserve Meeting Series: Addressing the Financing Needs of Small Businesses. Beck, T. 2013. Bank financing for SMEs – lessons from the literature. National Institute Economic Review 225: R23–R38. Yellen, J. 2013. Interconnectedness and systemic risk: Lessons from the financial crisis and policy implications. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington, DC.

27502918.label: Major findings and research outcome
27502918.value: In the first research paper, which is recently published in the Review of Corporate Finance Studies (Lin, C., Tai, M. and Xie, W., 2023. Credit environment and small business dynamics: Evidence from establishment-level data. The Review of Corporate Finance Studies, 12(2), pp.326-365.), we first show that banks receiving positive liquidity shocks increase lending to relatively larger SMEs, but not to the smallest businesses. This finding is consistent with the view that a positive liquidity shock enhances bank charter values, thereby reducing risk-taking incentives. Moreover, such disproportionate credit allocation leads to a crowding-out effect on the real growth of micro firms. When larger SMEs grow faster and exit less because of better access to credit, their expansion stifles the development of micro firms, whose access to credit remains unchanged. In the second research paper (Lin, C., Qin, S., and Tai, M., 2023. Regulatory-Driven Crowd Out on Small Business Lending.), we provide micro-level evidence on a regulatory-driven crowd-out effect that could lead to a negative relation between mortgage credit expansion and small business lending even when lenders’ financial constraints are not binding. In low- and moderate-income (LMI) neighborhoods under the CRA assessments, a shock that leads to mortgage credit expansion results in lower small business lending growth compared to non-CRA neighborhoods, especially if lenders are under greater regulatory pressure. Moreover, it results in a negative impact on SME employment growth and ultimately leads to more intensive bankruptcies and foreclosures in the impacted neighborhoods after the market collapsed. We also find this regulatory-driven crowd-out effect is more profound in areas with a larger minority share, and minority-owned entities suffer more negative impacts on their real growth.

27502918.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27502918.value: Given the important role played by banks in providing credit resources to SMEs, and the complicated economic mechanisms and impacts on resource allocation to the real sector, the big-picture question of the project can be extended to further research topics such as how financial technology development and the recent shift of banking business model from physical brick-and-mortar branch banking to digital banking impact the retail SME credit market. We explore this extended question in a related research paper (Kwan, A., Lin, C., Pursiainen, V. and Tai, M., 2023. Stress testing banks' digital capabilities: Evidence from the covid-19 pandemic. Accepted by the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis.). We show that when retail customers face an unexpected and unprecedented shock that shifts banking services from in-person to digital due to the COVID-19 pandemic, banks with stronger IT capacities are able to originate more PPP loans to small business borrowers, especially in areas with more severe COVID-19 outbreaks, higher internet use, and higher bank competition.

27502918.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27502918.value: This research project digs into a fundamental question in finance: when banks have more free money, how do they lend the money to small businesses and how their lending decisions affect the growth and job creation by those businesses? This question is very important to policy makers because small businesses contribute a large share of jobs to our economy and they heavily rely on banks to raise funding. Looking at detailed data on how banks lend to small businesses and how small businesses grow, we find that bank only lend more to the relatively larger SMEs but not the very micro ones when they have more money. This will lead the micro businesses to end up experiencing negative growth. We also find that when banks find there are more lending opportunities in the mortgage market, they also cut lending to small businesses, which can ultimately hurt the real economy and boost housing bubbles.

27503518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27503518.value: 擁有生活的意義感對個人的身心健康十分重要。然後，有時候人們發現尋找意義感並不是一件容易的事情。而意義感的缺失會帶來一系列的負面影響，包括會引起更高的焦慮水平(Debats, Van Der Lubbe, and Wezeman 1993), 降低個人快樂的程度(Janoff-Bulman 1992), 以及甚至會導致更多的自殺意念(Harlow, Newcomb, and Bentler 1986)。這些負面影響是值得關注的，因為香港大約有11.6%的年輕人報告說感受不到他們的生活中存在意義。事實上，在不同國家進行的研究發現高達70%的人會在一生中的某個時間點感覺到缺失生活的意義 (Berman, Weems, and Stickle 2006; van Selm and Dittmann-Kohli 1998)。 儘管人們十分關心生活意義感的缺失（以及追求生活意義感的這一動機）會如何影響人們的行為，迄今為止並沒有多少研究探討人們怎樣能通過消費行為來彌補生活意義感的缺失。本研究建立在過往生活意義感缺失和偏好建構文獻的基礎上，提出人們在感受到生活意義感缺失的時候，會更有可能建構出自己的偏好（相對於沒有偏好而言），即便供他們選擇的選項並沒有多大的差異。例如，人們可能本來對某些日常產品（例如鹽）的品牌並沒有什麼偏好。但是當他們感受到生活意義感缺失的時候，他們可能會構建出一個自己喜歡的品牌。本研究認為這是因為人們相信擁有偏好代表他們的生活中有值得他們追求的東西，而這一感覺會讓他們感受到生活的意義感。本研究會同時研究這一效應的邊際條件。 本研究對文獻的貢獻有以下幾點。首先，它會加深我們對生活意義感缺失如何影響消費者行為的認識。其次，它也會發掘出影響消費者偏好建構的一個新因素。本研究也提供實務意義。根據本研究的預測，營銷經理可以通過在人們容易感受到生活意義感缺失的情況下呈現他們的產品以鼓勵這些消費者形成偏好。本研究也預測給予消費者構建偏好的機會能幫助他們提高生活意義感。

27504318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27504318.value: Hedge fund managers fear that their clients will demand their money back exactly when that capital is most valuable to the fund. In the industry, this temperamental capital is called “hot money.” It flows easily into hedge funds when times are good, but flows out quickly when times are bad. However, little is empirically known about hot money. What types of investors are responsible for hot money: individual retail investors or large sophisticated institutional investors? What is the magnitude of the hot money risk? Is this risk compensated for in equilibrium? And, does this risk impact market efficiency? Using the novel eVestment database, I identify the distribution of hedge fund clients at the fund level, and study these questions. Hot money may be driven by either retail or institutional investors. Retail investors may be responsible if they have a limited ability to Bayesian update. For example, if they extrapolate past returns, then they will rush into funds when returns are good, and they will pull out of funds when returns are bad. However, institutional investors may be responsible if they are superior at producing information. These investors may have a better ability to identify failing funds and will be the first to pull their money out when the fund gets into trouble. For this project, I will purchase, clean, and analyze the eVestment hedge fund database. This database contains hedge fund performance and fund flows, as well as fund characteristics, including information on client types. I currently do not have a license to use any hedge fund database, and this particular data will be helpful for my research agenda in the future. As a student, I cleaned a snapshot of the eVestment database and performed preliminary tests. My preliminary results suggest that retail investors are responsible for hot money. Specifically, comparing retail-focused to institutional-focused hedge funds, I find that outflows are 17.2 percentage points higher for a one standard deviation decrease in returns. I also investigate the equilibrium characteristics of hot money, and find that retail-focused funds compensate investors for this risk. On average, these funds have annual returns that are 1.47 percentage points higher than institutional-focused funds. Moving forward with this project, I will investigate the impact of hot money on market efficiency. Hot money hinders the ability of hedge funds to act as arbitrageurs, and a better understanding of this risk will lead to a better functioning financial market for all participants. 對衝基金投資經理不希望儅資金對於基金很有價值的時候，投資者將資金撤出基金。在金融領域，我們將這些錢稱之爲“熱錢”。熱錢儅市場好的時候流向對衝基金，儅市場萎靡的時候撤出基金。然而，在實證研究上，我們對於熱錢知之甚少。熱錢來源於哪一類投資者呢：個人散戶投資者還是大型機構投資者。熱錢的風險有多大？在市場均衡狀態下，這部分熱錢的風險是否被補償了？這部分風險是否影響了市場有效性？運用最新的eVestment數據庫，我能夠清楚地分析對衝基金客戶的分類并且研究這些問題。 熱錢可能來源於散戶或者機構投資者。如果個人投資者不能對金融市場做有效的貝葉斯推斷。那麽他們的錢就會變成熱錢。擧個例子，如果他們僅僅簡單運用外部插值推斷股價變化，那麽在基金表現良好的時候他們就會湧向基金，而儅基金出現了一些小問題就會撤出自己的投資。然而大型的機構投資者并不會這樣。他們會有更好的獲取信息的方式，他們能夠更好的區分哪一隻基金是因爲經營不善而不是市場起伏導致的表現不好，然後明智地撤出資金。 在這個項目中，我將會購買，清理，分析eVestment對衝基金數據庫。這個數據庫包含了對衝基金表現，資金流，甚至還有基金特徵包括客戶類型。目前我沒有權限使用任何對衝基金數據庫，這個數據庫對我以後的研究有著重要的作用。當我是學生的時候，我有過清理和分析一部分eVestment數據庫的經驗，并且得到了初步的結果。 我的初步研究結果顯示，個人散戶投資者導致了熱錢的流入。尤其是通過比較散戶主導的對衝基金和機構主導的對衝基金，我發現每當基金回報減少一個標準差，散戶集中的對衝基金會有17.2% 更多的熱錢流出。通過研究熱錢的均衡狀態，我發現，散戶集中的對衝基金補償了這一部分風險。平均來看，散戶對衝基金比機構對衝基金年化收益率高出1.47%。 在此項目之後的研究中，我將會研究熱錢對於市場有效性的影響。熱錢可以幫助對衝基金更好的套利，如果我們能夠更清楚的瞭解這部分風險，可以讓整個金融市場更好、更有效的運轉。

27504318.label: Realisation of objectives
27504318.value: The first three project objectives have been achieved. We identified retail and institutional hedge fund investors using data provided by the eVestment database. We find that retail investors are hot money, they rush into funds following good performance and rush out following poor performance (objective 2). We find that retail investors are less sophisticated than institutional investors, and that their hot money causes performance to decrease (that is, this is a funding liquidity risk) (objective 1). We find that the retail funds exposed to this hot money risk provide similar returns as institutional funds, suggesting that there is not a hot money premium or discount (objective 3). Objective four was difficult to achieve because we did not have a method to identify the impact of hot money on market efficiency. We instead changed this objective to study the inequality of investment opportunities and we demonstrated that wealthy investors, who have access to retail hedge funds, have access to a valuable opportunity that is not available to less wealthy investors.

27504318.label: Major findings and research outcome
27504318.value: We demonstrate that retail investors behave very differently from institutional investors. Our results confirm the popular belief that retail investors are ``hot money.'' Compared to institutional investors, retail investors react very strongly when performance is in the tails; outflows are 12.8 percentage points (p.p.) larger following poor performance (bottom 20%), and inflows are 6.1 p.p. larger following good performance (top 20%). We also find evidence that this hot money poses a liquidity risk. We perform a counterfactual analysis to study the effects of hot retail money on future performance, and we find evidence that a hot money liquidity risk exists and is driven by exit. We further examine investor sophistication in four ways, by analyzing differences in (1) how investors respond to risk factors, (2) selection ability, (3) risk and return, and (4) the likelihood of liquidation. First, we decompose excess returns into alpha, traditional beta, and exotic beta components and find evidence that retail investors are less sensitive to performance due to exotic risk factors. Second, we study the "smart money" effect and demonstrate that institutional investors exhibit superior selection ability. Third, we find that both retail and institutional investors earn similar risk-adjusted returns. Finally, we study whether retail investors are more likely to invest in funds that liquidate and find evidence to the contrary. The first two results suggest that retail investors are less sophisticated than institutional investors, but the latter two results imply that these investors are not harmed by their access to hedge funds. Having established that these wealthy retail investors are not harmed by access to hedge funds we next ask whether this is a valuable opportunity? We demonstrate that wealthy investors have a valuable opportunity by comparing retail hedge funds with retail actively-managed mutual funds. We find that retail hedge funds outperform actively-managed retail mutual funds by 2.4 p.p. of risk-adjusted returns annually. Furthermore, a sophisticated retail investor has more opportunity to find alpha in the hedge fund market. We find that 17.2% of retail hedge funds produce alpha, while just 0.2% of retail mutual funds do. Also, in contrast to retail mutual funds, retail hedge fund alphas are, to an extent, persistent; poor performers continue to underperform and a portfolio that longs winners and shorts losers produces an annual alpha of between 3.6 p.p. and 10.8 p.p. on average, suggesting that a sophisticated retail investor could avoid potential losses.

27504318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27504318.value: Given the limitations inherent in the data, we believe the limits of this research agenda have been reached.

27504318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27504318.value: In the interest of consumer financial protection, most households do not have access to the hedge fund market. We show that this creates an inequality of investment opportunities. Wealthy households can access this market, and while these retail investors behave very differently from institutional investors (e.g., they provide "hot money," pay less attention to exotic risk factors, and exhibit inferior selection ability), they are sophisticated enough that they enjoy comparable performance. Furthermore, access is valuable. Compared to less wealthy investors limited to actively-managed retail mutual funds, retail hedge fund investors have access to higher performance, performance persistence, and alpha.

27601518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27601518.value: Increasing numbers of students are pursuing a growing and diverse range of master’s degree programmes. The proposed study will focus on self-financed taught master’s programmes in Hong Kong. More specifically, it will identify the demographic and academic profiles of students studying for different types of master’s degrees and explore why they are pursuing master’s-level education. The analysis will focus on four main research questions: 1) What are the characteristics and profiles of students enrolled in master’s programmes in Hong Kong? 2) What are the economic, social and educational factors underpinning the decision to pursue a master’s degree? 3) How do those factors differ by student profile, such as country of origin or study mode (full-time or part-time)? 4) How do they differ by degree type, namely, research or profession-oriented? The study framework will draw on multiple theoretical approaches, including human, cultural and social capital theories, credential theory, and educational inflation and college choice models. It will follow a mixed-methods, multiple case-study design, with an exemplary case study applied to describe the distinct features of select programmes. Based on purposive maximum variation sampling, 12 master’s programmes offered by three universities in Hong Kong will be selected, ranging from research-oriented (e.g. Master of Arts and Master of Science) to profession-oriented (e.g. Master of Business Administration, Master of Social Work and Master of Architecture). The project will be conducted over a 24-month period, and will rely upon existing data and secondary documents drawn from the government, university and departmental levels, coupled with the analysis of qualitative data gathered from semi-structured interviews and quantitative data gleaned from a survey. Approximately 120 current master’s students will be identified for interviews using snowball sampling, and 700 to 800 questionnaires will be collected from current master’s students across programmes and institutions. The qualitative data will be subjected to thematic content and narrative analysis, and cross-programme analysis will be performed. The quantitative data will be analysed using hierarchical logistic regression, with disciplinary differences considered. The findings will expand our understanding of the heterogeneity of current master’s students’ backgrounds and expectations for learning and career development. In the long term, they have implications for theory development concerning students’ decision-making regarding postgraduate degree programmes and for public policy, e.g. the quality assurance of postgraduate programmes. For institutional leaders and programme managers, the findings have implications for student recruitment strategies and programme design. 目前，越来越多的学生正在追求越来越多的硕士学位课程。本项研究将集中于香港的自费教学硕士课程。更具体地说，它将确定学习不同类型硕士学位的学生的人口统计和学术概况，并探索他们为什么要进行硕士学位的教育。本项研究将集中讨论四个主要研究问题：1）在香港参加硕士课程的学生有哪些特征和概况？ 2）他们决定攻读硕士学位，受到哪些经济，社会和教育因素的影响？ 3）这些因素如何因学生而异，例如原籍国或学习模式（全日制或非全日制）？ 4）他们在学位类型方面有何差异，比如研究式或专业型导向？ 该研究框架将借鉴多种理论方法，包括人力，文化和社会资本理论，证书理论，教育通胀和大学选择模型。它将遵循混合方法，多案例研究设计，并应用示例性案例研究来描述这些项目的不同特征。根据最大变异抽样，我们将选择香港三所大学提供的12个硕士课程，包括研究型导向（如文学硕士和理学硕士）、专业型导向（如工商管理硕士，社会工作硕士和建筑硕士）。该项目将在24个月内完成，并将收集从政府，大学和学系层面的现有数据和文件，以及从半结构化访谈中收集的定性数据的分析，以及定量数据。该项研究将通过雪球抽样访谈大约120名现任硕士生，并从收集700至800份问卷。本项研究将对定性数据进行主题分析，并将进行专业项目之间的比较分析。定量数据将使用分层逻辑回归分析，并考虑学科差异。 这些研究结果将扩展我们对当前硕士研究生背景的异质性以及对其学习和职业发展的期望的理解。从长远来看，它们对于学生关于研究生学位课程和公共政策的决策的理论发展产生影响，例如：研究生课程的质量保证等。对于院校领导者和专业项目管理人员来说，这些研究发现将对学生的招聘策略和专业或者项目设计有影响。

27601518.label: Realisation of objectives
27601518.value: 1. To identify and characterise student profiles in research- and profession-oriented master’s programmes Since there was limited information on master’s programmes in Hong Kong, the first objective of the research project was to provide an overview of the current development and status of master’s degree programmes. The lack of information is mainly because most master’s programmes in Hong Kong are self-funded without UGC subsidy. Although there is some publicly available information on UGC-funded master’s programmes on the Hong Kong UGC website, most coursework-based programmes are based on self-financed programmes with a broad range of institutional and programme levels of diversity. Document analysis was applied to achieve the first objective, including publicly available and institutionally provided secondary documents. As there was limited access to the institutional documents, I relied on the open data, which is collected from programme websites of master’s programmes. With the support of a research assistant, I identified almost five hundred master’s programmes in Hong Kong. I collected information on each programme, including degree title, programme title, missions, learning outcomes, curriculum, assessment, graduation requirements, and tuition fee. Based on the content analysis, the project found the diversity of master’s programmes in Hong Kong and emerging trends in market-oriented approaches in launching and promoting such programmes. However, there were challenges in characterising the students’ profiles in master’s programmes across Hong Kong higher education institutions. As stated earlier, the master’s programmes are operated flexibly at institutional and programme levels, and there was a lack of a consistent dataset to show the entire student population in Hong Kong. I contacted individual institutions to request such student demographic information; however, there were several restrictions to obtaining such information. To overcome the underachievement, I applied the case study approach instead of collecting entire institutional information in Hong Kong. I chose the University of Hong Kong as a case, where I am employed and have better access to the information. For example, historical documents were reviewed to describe the evolution of master’s programmes within the institution. In addition, primary data on the number of master’s students and programmes were collected from the case institution’s ‘Quick Stats’ data. The study also included secondary data for 1995–2015 from the source ‘A profile of first-year postgraduate students’. Although there was limited data access, the first objective was achieved at around 80 per cent by combining the document analysis with a case study approach. 2. To explore why students pursue master’s degrees The second objective was successfully achieved with a mixed-method approach. First, the survey was implemented with the title, ‘Determinants of master’s degree pursuit in Hong Kong’. We obtained around 786 responses and analyzed them by focusing on the motivation for pursuing a master’s degree, perception of learning experiences and career plans after a master’s degree. From the quantitative data analysis part, two major factors were identified; intrinsic motivation for growth (i.e. found in the interests in the field, self-development) and extrinsic motivation to overcome deficiencies (i.e. improving institutional reputations, increasing chances for employment, promotion, and working conditions). The qualitative data confirmed and elaborated such initial findings from the factor analysis. The second objective was achieved mainly from qualitative data analysis. Comprehensive dialogue with interviewees provided rich data about individual perceptions of one particular motivation and expectations on their master’s degrees. We investigated various experiences of students’ engagement in research through broad, open-ended interview questions. The participants represented a wide range of disciplines and over 50 coursework-based master’s programmes, including some new interdisciplinary programmes such as MSc in Artificial Intelligence and Digital Media and MSc in Environmental and Public Health Management. The interview questions were developed regarding the participants’ motivations to undertake master’s studies and their learning experiences in the master’s programmes, including their coursework, research projects, and relationships with supervisors and peers. The findings showed that students decided to pursue a master's degree because of the interplay of different motivations, the patterns of which differed according to the students' particular characteristics. The study's findings expand our understanding of the heterogeneity of current students' backgrounds and their diverse demands for masters-level education. We also conducted the follow-up interview with fifteen students after one year of the initial interview by applying the longitudinal qualitative approach. Although the longitudinal qualitative approach was not part of the initial plan in the proposal stage, we wanted to understand how the students’ perceptions change during the learning journey and what changes their perceptions. The number of interviewees in the second round was small (N-15); however, we found many interesting findings, such as students’ disappointment in degree value in employment compared to their initial expectations and suggestions to improve the quality of learning experiences and career support for the master’s students. Three stages of data collection contributed to successfully achieving the second objective. One limitation was that all the interviews were conducted via an online platform (Zoom) without face-to-face interaction due to the COVID pandemic. However, we did our best to make the online interview as active as the face-to-face interview and followed the sound procedure to triangulate the interview data. 3. To implement a survey to ascertain the factors involved in master’s degree pursuit by student profile (local and non-local, full- and part-time) and degree type (research-oriented and profession-oriented) Overall, the objective of designing and implanting the survey was successfully achieved. The online survey entitled ‘Determinants of master’s degree pursuit in Hong Kong’ was conducted. The research team designed the survey based on an extensive literature review and pilot interviews, aiming to explore various aspects of master’s education. The survey was developed in early 2020 after the research team obtained ethical approval from the affiliated institution. The questionnaire was modified and its length was reduced to two stages of pilot surveys (First pilot: November 2020; Second pilot: December 2020–January 2021). The main survey was conducted online from March to June 2021 and included a consent form. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, most classes in master’s programmes were held online or in hybrid mode during the survey period. The restrictions to classroom access led the research team to identify master’s programme coordinators and teachers in Hong Kong public universities via the internet and to contact them via email. The research team invited them to distribute the survey link to their students. Eight public universities in Hong Kong offer various master’s programmes. After data cleaning, we obtained a total of 786 respondents for the analysis. The number of participants from each university was relative to the size of the master’s programme. The data analysis was conducted with different topics, with a particular focus on students’ perceived learning experience and employability. Based on the survey data, one manuscript is currently under review, ‘Perceived employability among Master’s students in Hong Kong (Submitted to Education + Training). Another manuscript, ‘Motivation, approaches to learning, and perceived employability among master’s students’ is in preparation.

27601518.label: Major findings and research outcome
27601518.value: 1) Increasing diversity in programmes, students’ profiles, and students’ motivations in master’s education The project was initiated with the question of why there was a lack of scholarly works in master’s education despite the exponential growth in enrollment. For example, new master’s degree titles have emerged and new specialised programmes have been developed in recent years to respond to the market demands. The profiles of master’s students have also changed, with an increasing number of female students, non-local and full-time students, and shorter work experience. Students’ motivation in pursuing master’s degrees has changed in current economic and social conditions. These findings were presented in the paper ‘Master’s education in Hong Kong: Access and programme diversity’ (refer to Part C). 2) Changing nature of master’s education With the increasing diversity in master’s education, the nature of master’s education has changed. In particular, the research requirement in many master’s programmes has become flexible or replaced by other learning outcomes. This raises the question: What meanings do ‘thesis’ and ‘research’ have in the context of master’s education? The project findings showed that master's students build their loose and flexible research communities due to the nature of master's programmes with their short periods of study and large numbers of part-time students. In addition, the project findings showed that the research was interpreted via multiple perspectives among the master’s students, such as learning outcomes, learning processes, and separate tasks. These findings were presented in the paper ‘Concept of research among master’s students in Hong Kong’ (refer to Part C). 3) Master’s students’ labour market transition and career development As most master’s graduates transit to the labour market after degree completion, the master’s education needs to be studied in the context of employment and career development. The project findings broadly showed that most master’s students are uncertain about their career paths and employment outcomes even if they have already completed the undergraduate degree and narrowed down their master’s studies to more specific fields. The findings argued that learning experience and approaches to learning are the most critical factor in supporting students’ career development. Four key aspects of the students’ career support need at the institutional level were also identified: information channels, relational networks, technical skills and practical experience. These findings were reported in the papers ‘Perceived employability among Master’s students in Hong Kong’, and ‘Part-time master’s students’ attitudes towards study and work’ (refer to Part C).

27601518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27601518.value: I identified several potential research topics for further development based on the current project outcomes. There is a need for further investigation of master’s degrees in economic and sociological perspectives, especially in the growing higher education systems, including China. Despite the massive expansion of postgraduate education in many countries, few studies have been performed to examine the association between graduates possessing a master’s degree and their labour market outcomes. The future research plan involves examining how the value of a master’s degree will evolve in both academia and in a fast-changing uncertain labour market. It will involve directions of curricular structure, teaching, and policies to improve postgraduate education. The long-term plan is to use empirical and comparative approaches to conceptualise the relationships between labour markets, postgraduate education, and higher education policy. The background paper on the labour market impact of a master’s degree was published in the handbook entry in 2022, entitled ‘The Expansion of Postgraduate Degrees and its Labour Market Consequences in East Asia’. The General Research Fund proposal will be submitted in 2023, with the topic ‘Effect of a master’s degree for employment outcomes in China’. Interdisciplinary and international collaboration will be extended to achieve the goals.

27601518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27601518.value: The rapid expansion of master’s education is a global phenomenon. For instance, the number of Master’s students enrolled in China reached 2.28 million in 2017. In the US, 24.1 million people aged 25 and over had a master’s degree in 2021, and 9,000 new master’s degree programmes have been launched since 2011. Hong Kong has almost five hundred master’s programmes in eight UGC higher education institutions. What are the backgrounds of the rapid expansion of master’s education? How will the expansion of a master’s degree affect graduates’ employment and the labour market? This research project aimed to provide an explanation of what factors has caused the expansion of master’s education and how master’s students perceive their learning motivations, experiences, and career plans. Based on the data from the survey and interviews among Hong Kong master’s students, the project findings have shown the students’ changing backgrounds and expectations of the master’s education and the implications of how the higher education institutions and master’s programmes can meet the changing needs and expectations.
