27601818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27601818.value: How did the Song (960-1279) literati maintain and exploit their social networks in response to drastic changes in the political arena or social environment during the Northern-Southern Song transition? By reconstructing the social networks of two prominent political and literary figures, Sun Di (孫覿, 1081-1169) and Li Gang (李綱, 1083-1140), through comprehensive analysis of their writings, the proposed project will investigate how the two men related to their contemporaries, including their relatives, friends from home, schoolmates, examination cohorts and colleagues in both the late Northern Song (960-1127) and early Southern Song (1127-1279). Its results will not only deepen our understanding of political communications and the wider literati culture, as well as elite networks and behaviour, but also offer new points of reference for evaluating historical figures from the early Southern Song. Both men joined official ranks after years of study at metropolitan schools in the Song capital of Kaifeng in the 1100s. They rapidly climbed the ladder of success to become senior court officials in the mid-1120s. After the Song court moved to the south, both men largely remained outside politics for most of the post-1130s period following discord with court officials. How did these politically ambitious men cope with the reality of failed careers? What agendas emerge in their letters to their contemporaries after they had stepped down? As interpersonal relationships are not static, how did their relationships with their contemporaries evolve over time? In what ways did they strengthen their ties with their correspondents? Despite having a similar career path, both men had differing attitudes towards the Jurchen in the mid-1120s: Li asserted the need to counter the invaders, while Sun tended towards appeasement. How did they portray their own deeds and justify their stance in their communication with their contemporaries? Given that posterity’s view of the two men has evolved in radically different ways, to what extent did their letters help shape their historical reputations? Lastly, because the two men studied at the Imperial University in the 1110s, a close examination of their relationship with their schoolmates will also help to resolve larger historical questions such as how student networks at the Imperial University helped the Southern Song regime to consolidate political power and, more broadly, how elite networks created the cohesiveness that bound the Chinese empire in the middle period. 為了應對兩宋之際政治和社會的急劇變化，宋代（960-1279）文人如何維繫和利用他們的社交網絡？這項研究計劃通過分析孫覿（1081-1169）和李綱（1083-1140）這兩位著名文士的著作，重構他們的社交網絡，進而探討兩人與北宋（960-1127）末和南宋（1127-1279）初的同時代人有何關連，當中包括他們的親戚、同鄉、同學、同年和同事等。這項研究的成果不單令我們對政治溝通、廣泛的士人文化、以至精英們的網絡和行為有更深入的了解，更為評估南宋初期的歷史人物提供了新的視角。多年在宋代首都開封的中央官學習業後，孫覿和李綱兩人均於徽宗年間入仕。其後他們在官僚的階梯上迅速爬升，成功在宣和年間晉身朝中高級官員的行列。然而自宋室南渡後，兩人由於與朝臣不和，因此在紹興年間的大部份時間均被迫遠離朝中政治。像孫覿和李綱這些具有政治野心的人如何面對失意的仕途？他們在被貶後寫給同時代人的信中又提出了什麼議程？由於人際關係並非一成不變，他們與同時代人的關係如何隨著時間的推移而演變？他們以什麼方式加強與通訊者的聯繫？儘管孫覿和李綱兩人的仕宦有著相似的經歷，但兩人在靖康年間對女真人卻持不同態度：李主張有必要對抗入侵者，而孫則傾向與敵人議和。他們如何表述自己的行為，並在與同時代人的訊息溝通中把他們的立場合理化？鑑於後世對兩人的評價截然不同，他們與友人的書信對於他們歷史形象的塑造有多大幫助？最後，因為兩人在大觀至政和年間在太學習業，仔細研究他們與其同學的關係將有助解決更大的歷史問題，如太學生網絡如何鞏固南宋政權，乃至於精英網絡如何凝聚唐、宋、元時期的中華帝國。

27601818.label: Realisation of objectives
27601818.value: The six project objectives, as originally laid out, have been fully accomplished. Thanks to the help of this ECS grant, I was able to examine sources that are unavailable in Hong Kong by visiting multiple libraries in Taipei, Japan and Europe. The completion of library research enables me, with the help of student helpers, to compile an authentic textual data set of the writings of Li Gang and Sun Di. The data set was then imported to the semi-automated tagging platform MARKUS, through which names of individuals and places have been marked up. With the help of digital tools like NodeXL and QGIS, the social networks of Li Gang and Sun Di have been reconstructed and analyzed with reference to the historical context of the Northern-Southern Song transition in the first half of the twelfth century. Hence the 1st and 6th objectives are met. I discover that both Li Gang and Sun Di held contrasting views towards student activism at the Imperial University in 1126. Whereas Li was sympathetic to the student protestors, Sun was skeptical about the motives of the students. This prompts me to further investigate how students comment on politics in response to political crises caused by the Jurchen invasion and what enabled them to do so. Through a comparison of fourteen memorials submitted by university students and personnel to Emperor Qinzong, I examine the ways in which students submitted their petitions, the responsiveness of the court towards their appeals, students’ political sensitivities as well as the channels by which they accessed political information. A close examination of the memorials reveals that students were highly responsive to the rapidly changing political circumstances. Such sensitivity suggests that students could utilize different channels to access political information. Everyday rumour, public notices, political documents sold at markets, and relatives and friends currently in office allowed students to learn of personnel movements in the civil and military services, policy deliberations at court, and even events at an imperial audience. Such a vibrant network of political communication enabled students to remain politically active, despite prohibitions under the preceding reformist administration. These findings have been published in 2020 in the article titled “Student Activism and Channels of Political Communication in 1126” in the Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies, one of the oldest and most reputable journals in sinology in the United Kingdom. This study of communication channels helps elucidate political communication, culture, elite networks and behavior in Song China and hence realize the 4th objective. The second case study of elite networks in the Northern-Southern Song transition focuses on how Sun Di wrote to his contemporaries during his exile journey to and from Xiangzhou in modern Guangxi. Sun was likely aware of his literary fame, a cultural capital that he could exploit to strengthen his network associations with his correspondents. His ambitious networking strategy not only contributed to a relatively pleasant exile journey to and banishment in Xiangzhou, but also allowed him, in the midst of everything, to help friends in government or local affairs. The above findings are presented in the article titled “Life of an Exile: Sun Di’s (1081–1169) Letters Pertaining to His Banishment to Xiangzhou”, which has been published in 2021 in the Journal of the American Oriental Society, the oldest and one of the leading scholarly journals in oriental studies in the United States. This article deepens our understanding of political culture in the Northern–Southern Song transition by showing how an individual’s literary fame could be exploited to strengthen his social ties and hence to moderate the worst in a faction-riddled political system. The analysis of the unending efforts of Sun Di at networking through correspondence meets the 2nd and 3rd objectives of the project. Regarding the realization of the 5th objective, the case studies presented in the two journal articles have strong comparative relevance for analysis of political communication and elite networks in both Chinese and global history. Large-scale demonstrations led by Chen Dong and his schoolmates in the late Northern Song, for example, can be compared with small-scale student protests in medieval universities in Europe, through which we can have a better understanding how political mobilization in Song China differed from that in medieval Europe.

27601818.label: Major findings and research outcome
27601818.value: Major findings in this research project are published in the following two articles: The first article “Student Activism and Channels of Political Communication in 1126” is of particular significance as it expands the existing research on Song political institutions by adding to our understanding of how the Song government actually functioned. Through a comparison of fourteen memorials submitted by students and personnel at the Imperial University to Emperor Qinzong, it examines the ways in which students submitted their petitions, the responsiveness of the court towards their appeals, students’ political sensitivities as well as the channels by which they accessed political information. A close examination of the memorials reveals that students were highly responsive to the rapidly changing political circumstances. It is argued that such responsiveness owes much to the presence of different communication channels that facilitated the circulation of political information within literati circles. This article provides concrete evidence of how Song government functioned in real time, as opposed to the static organization charts presented by conventional institutional history. The second article “Life of an Exile: Sun Di’s (1081–1169) Letters Pertaining to His Banishment to Xiangzhou” makes significant contributions to a robust trend in recent Song dynasty studies by focusing on letters as source of information about political and social networking. Based on letters as well as other writings by Sun Di, a prominent literary figure in the Northern to Southern Song transition, it describes Sun’s exile to the malarial south (Xiangzhou prefecture, in present-day Guangxi) during a period of factionalist infighting in the early Southern Song, as well as his journeys to and from exile. Through an in-depth analysis of the contents of his letters, the paper shows how Sun Di established ties with officials in different localities and how he responded to the humiliation of banishment. It is argued that Sun Di’s reputation as a literary stylist among his contemporaries helped him to develop a good rapport with local officials, particularly in the Guangnan West circuit, which was essential to creating a relatively comfortable exile journey and a pleasant life during his confinement. This study highlights the value of letters as historical sources pertaining to Song political and literati culture and sheds light on literati responses to life’s many challenges.

27601818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27601818.value: This study of the writings and social networks of Sun Di and Li Gang is just the starting point of a larger project, which plans to undertake a full-scale prosopographical study of members of the university community. Their lives and reconstructed social networks will then be contextualized within the broader political and social environment, which will shed light on how members of the Imperial University in the late Northern Song impacted on politics and local societies in the early Southern Song. I have successfully got a GRF grant to support this new project, which will be completed in 2024.

27601818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27601818.value: This project investigates the social networks of two prominent political and literary figures, Sun Di and Li Gang, through a comprehensive analysis of their writings, particularly their letters. Contrasting views of the two men towards student activism at the Imperial University in 1126 prompt me to investigate how students comment on politics in response to political crises caused by the Jurchen invasion and what enabled them to do so. It is found that students’ sensitivity to the rapidly changing political environment owes much to their utilization of different communication channels to access political information. A close reading of the letters of Sun Di also reveals how Sun, then on his exile journey to Xiangzhou in modern Guangxi, related to officials in different localities through which he passed and how epistolary writings were used as a channel to circulate political information. It highlights the important role that epistolary exchanges played in establishing and maintaining social networks among Song literati. Findings in this project provide strong comparative relevance for analysis of political communication and elite networks in both Chinese and global history.

27603818.label: Project Objectives
27603818.value: To collect high density brain EEG signals from 100 participants during basic learning tasks (sequence learning and reinforcement learning) and extract the single trial dynamic information of neural activities. To evaluate the reliability and validity of single trial-based neural traits during basic learning processes in predicting cognitive abilities (assessed by psychometric tasks) based on structural equation modeling.

27603818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27603818.value: Understanding and optimizing the process of learning constitute key subjects in educational research. For practical purposes, educational approaches in learning research focus primarily on optimization of macroscopic learning behaviour rather than a mechanistic understanding of fundamental learning processes. Macroscopic learning activities are composed of elementary neural dynamic events that occur in a very short time scale (within milliseconds). Therefore, knowing the neural characteristics of fundamental learning processes and their relationships with higher order cognitive performance may bring us insights on learning optimization. In this project, we aim to examine the fast temporal neural dynamics underlying two fundamental learning processes (sequence learning and reinforcement learning) and the link between the neural characteristics of learning with general cognitive abilities, to seek potential neural feedback for learning optimization. The imaging of neuro-physiological signals at high temporal resolution is thus crucially important to investigating fast time-scale learning processes. We will employ high temporal-resolution brain electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings to investigate the neural underpinnings of fast time-scale learning processes during sequence learning and reinforcement learning tasks. To capture learning-related changes and dynamic patterns across repetitions, we will perform advanced single-trial analysis in combination with neural source imaging to extract trial-to-trial neural dynamic information. Single-trial EEG characteristics that may be related to temporal learning processes and abilities will be thoroughly extracted, including component amplitude, latency, morphology, scalp distribution, spectrum, and time frequency, among others, at both the sensor level and neural source level. All of these neural characteristics will be examined in terms of their relationships with learning process and performance in a multivariate statistical framework using structural equation modeling. Linking neural correlates of learning with general cognitive abilities will frame the study into the broader arena of education. We will conduct psychometric tests to measure participants’ general cognitive abilities. The relationship between learning traits as characterized by neural dynamics during the learning tasks and cognitive abilities will be investigated within an individual differences framework based on structural equation modeling (SEM). This SEM approach will allow us to examine the link between the neural dynamics in fast time-scale learning and higher order cognitive abilities, which in turn create potential for utilizing specific neural traits as a reference for learning optimization in future research. The research paradigm will also prepare the foundation for further investigating the relationships between the neural underpinnings of other learning domains and intellectual abilities. 理解並優化學習過程一直以來都是教育研究領域的重點。而出於實用性的考慮，該領域所關注的方法主要致力於優化宏觀學習行為，而非通過理解學習過程。而考慮到宏觀學習活動也是由許多發生時間範圍極短（毫秒）的基本神經動態事件組成，我們認為尋找基本學習過程中的神經特徵與高階認知表現的關聯可能會為我們優化長期學習過程帶來新的見解。在這個項目中，我們致力於尋求可能與學習優化潛在相關聯的神經反饋。我們會研究與兩個基本學習過程（序列學習和強化學習）相關的快速時間尺度的神經動態，並尋找學習過程中的神經特徵與一般認知能力之間的聯繫。為研究快速時間尺度內的學習過程，高時間分辨率下對神經生理信號的成像是十分重要的。我們將採用高時間分辨率腦電圖（EEG）來研究進行序列學習和強化學習時，快速時間尺度學習下的神經基礎。為了捕捉在重複實驗中可能發生的與學習相關的變化與動態模式，我們將結合神經源成像進行進一步單試驗分析，通過比較試驗間變化來提取神經動態信息。對於每個單次實驗的EEG數據，我們將提取出所有可能與學習過程和能力相關的特徵，如振幅，潛伏期，形態，信號收集點在頭皮上分佈，頻譜和時間頻率等。所有這些特徵值，結合他們與學習過程、表現的關係，都會被統一使用一個多變量統計模型進行相應的分析檢查。同時，我們認為將與學習的相關的神經特質與一般認知能力聯繫起來，將使我們的研究服務於更廣泛的教育領域。為測量被試者的一般認知能力，我們會進行心理測試。而研究不同學習特徵之間的聯繫時，我們將基於結構方程模型（SEM）進行個體差異分析。這些學習特徵主要由學習、認知任務時發生的神經動態所代表，而SEM方法正能使我們能夠檢驗快速時間尺度學習中神經動態與高階認知能力之間的聯繫。從另一個角度上來說，我們的研究也使利用特定神經特徵值來作為未來優化學習相關研究的一個參考變量成為可能。研究範式還將為進一步研究其他學習領域的神經基礎與智力能力之間的關係奠定基礎。

27603818.label: Major findings and research outcome
27603818.value: The major findings are summarized below. All of the findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals. 1. The single trial EEG data encode functionally and cognitively related information, and are able to predict individual’s cognitive performance at different levels of cognitive system. 2. Different levels of cognitive processes and abilities are highly correlated, which is shown in the correlation between neural effects generated by cognitive tasks at different levels. These cross-level link provides a foundation for evaluating complex learning abilities based on basic neural cognitive processes. 3. The reliability of single trial EEG-based evaluation of neural and cognitive profiles is quite high, which provides a foundation for developing reliable neural indicators based on neural dynamics. 4. The information encoded in the single trial EEG can be extracted by sophisticated algorithms in a effective way that allow them to enable not just neural assessment of cognitive activities but also developing efficient brain-computer interface systems.

27603818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27603818.value: Based on the data and findings generated from the project, we will proceed to develop more efficient algorithms for extracting the information from the single trial neural dynamics. One direction is to apply transformer based neural network to develop models for predicting brain’s dynamic signal in a generic sense. This will undoubtedly require more data for the training. We are applying new grants to support a continuation of data collection with the expectation that a model for predicting the EEG time series can be developed and a better understanding of the dynamic system characteristics can be achieved.

27603818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27603818.value: The project has collected sufficient amount of data that led to development of algorithms to read the complex brain activity and translate them into information revealing mental activity. The data collected and the research paradigms that have been built from this project will allow for a highly sustainable line of research that further explores the brain-mind-behaviour relationships in a broader context. We are using the results and publications generated by this project to applying larger-scale grants to continue the research line described above.

27606118.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27606118.value: 探究第二語言寫作中給予和接受同儕互評對學習者社會認知動機，自我調整策略處理與寫作表現的影響

27606118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27606118.value: Peer feedback has earned an increasingly noteworthy place in second language (L2) writing research and instructional practice over the past four decades. However, issues pertaining to motivation (a crucial factor that influences learning behaviour and academic performance) and self-regulation (a reflective learner strategy that facilitates effective learning and adaptive motivation) are not yet well understood. This is largely due to a lack of in-depth, theory-driven investigations. This study aims to investigate the impact of peer feedback on L2 learners’ writing motivation, use of self-regulatory writing strategies, and writing performance. It also seeks to examine the connections between writing motivation, strategic processing of writing tasks, and writing achievement in peer feedback practice. This study will be conducted at senior secondary level in local schools and is composed of two parts. In Part 1, a self-report inventory for collection of quantitative data on writing self-regulation will be developed and validated. This will involve data collected from around 500 senior secondary students. In Part 2, an experimental intervention involving around 100 students will be conducted in a local secondary school to examine the impact of peer feedback. The treatment group (divided into feedback-giving and feedback-receiving subgroups) and the comparison group (individual writing) will participate in five writing cycles spanning two semesters. Pre- and post-intervention questionnaire data on writing motivation (collected via an existing motivation questionnaire) and use of self-regulatory strategies as well as data on writing grades will be collected. Student interview responses will also be elicited to delve into the development of their motivational attributes and self-regulatory capacity and awareness during the intervention. The quantitative and qualitative findings will unravel the relationships between motivation, strategy use and performance in the peer feedback context. The findings of this study can help uncover the operating mechanisms underlying motivational and self-regulatory processes in L2 writing and peer feedback tasks, and expand upon existing accounts of motivation and self-regulated learning in educational psychology. The self-report inventory will provide future research with a validated instrument for collection of writing self-regulation data, and offer a blueprint for developing similar inventories in other learning domains. Pedagogically speaking, this study will provide teachers with guidelines on how to cater to learners’ emerging motivational needs in peer collaborative tasks, and to potentiate collaborative learning in order to nurture active and reflective learners. 在過去的四十年裏，同儕互評在第二語言寫作研究和教學實踐中佔據越來越顯著的地位。然而，關於學習動機（影響學習行為和學術表現的關鍵因素）和自我調整（促進有效學習和適應性動機的反思學習策略）方面的問題尚未得到透徹的瞭解。這很大程度上是因為過去缺乏深入的理論導向研究。此研究目的在於探索同儕互評對第二語言寫作學習者的寫作動機，自我調整寫作策略的使用和寫作表現的影響。此研究還會嘗試了解在同儕互評中，寫作動機，寫作策略處理和寫作成就三者之間的關係。 此研究將會在本地的高中進行，並且由兩個部分組成。第一部分會用此研究設計的自評量表來收集寫作自我調整的量化數據，並且驗證該量表的效度。這將會涉及從大概500名本地高中生中獲取的數據。第二部分是用實驗介入來測試同儕互評的影響，大概需要100名本地中學生參與。實驗組（分為互評給予組和互評接受組）和對照組（獨立寫作）將會參與貫穿兩個學期的五次寫作週期。問卷將會用於實驗介入之前和之後來收集有關寫作動機（通過已有的動機問卷）和自我調整策略使用的數據。寫作成績也會被收集。學生訪談將用於深入研究在實驗介入期間動機屬性和自我調整能力與意識的發展。此研究所收集的量化和質化數據將會幫助闡明在第二語言同儕互評中動機，策略使用和寫作表現的關係。 此研究的結果會幫助揭示第二語言寫作和同儕互評中動機與自我調整的運作機制，並且對教育心理學中已有的動機與自我調整學習的闡述進行補充。此研究所設計的自我調整自評量表能為未來相關寫作研究提供有效的測量工具，也能為設計其他學習領域的類似量表提供參考。在教學方面，此研究能為老師提供指導方針，幫助他們理解如何照顧學生在同儕合作中出現的動機需求，以及如何增強同儕學習的效用和培養主動及自我反思的學習者。

27607518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27607518.value: Over the past two decades, significant changes have occurred in how men who have sex with men (MSM) find partners, moving from the traditional approach (in person at gay bars) to the Internet and now to smartphone dating applications (apps). Notably, both international and local studies have found a high prevalence of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and risky sexual behaviours, such as condomless anal sex, substance misuse in conjunction with sex (‘chemsex’) and group sex, among MSM dating app users. Although the use of dating apps is an emerging sexual risk factor, little effort has been expended on the promotion of safe sex and good sexual health among the users of those apps. Previous studies in various populations have found that interactive web-based interventions can improve sexual health knowledge, attitudes and sexual behaviours. Therefore, the aim of the proposed study is to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of an interactive web-based intervention in improving the sexual health of MSM dating app users in Hong Kong. The research will involve two phases. In Phase 1, qualitative interviews with MSM dating app users will be conducted to extract in-depth, qualitative information on their experiences of using such apps and why users are particularly likely to engage in risky sexual behaviours, which will inform the development of the intervention. In Phase 2, a two-armed randomised controlled trial will be conducted. Chinese MSM dating app users who have had sex in the past 12 months will be recruited and randomly allocated into either the intervention (n = 200) or control group (n = 200). Subjects in the intervention group will receive the web-based intervention containing interactive content that (1) encourages a positive attitude towards consistent condom use and HIV/STI testing and negative attitude towards chemsex and group sex; (2) positions condom use and regular HIV/STI testing as normative; and (3) targets improved perceived self-efficacy concerning condom use and negotiation and HIV/STI testing at baseline and at two and four months. The control group will receive only web-based information without sexual health components. Subjects in both groups will be evaluated at baseline and three and six months after baseline. The primary outcome will be the frequency of condomless anal sex. The web-based intervention, if found successful, can be adopted by the government and NGOs to reduce the growing HIV epidemic among MSM in Hong Kong. 網絡改變了男男性接觸者尋找伴侶的方式。以前，男男性接觸者多數從傳統渠道如酒吧結識伴侶。但隨着手機約會程式的普及，越來越多人是透過手機約會程式去結識伴侶。值得注意的是，國際及本地研究都發現性傳播感染及風險性行為（如無套肛交，濫藥性行為及群交）在使用手機約會程式的男男性接觸用者中都較為普遍。儘管使用手機約會程式與風險性行為息息相關，但到目前為止並沒有研究去促進使用手機約會程式的男男性接觸者的心性健康。此外，在不同人群中的研究發現，互動網絡干預措施可以改善心性健康知識，態度和性行為。本研究的目的是開發和評估一個互動網絡干預，以改善使用手機約會程式的男男性接觸用者的心性健康。本研究分為兩個階段。第一階段為定性研究，這階段對使用手機約會程式的男男性接觸用者進行訪談以了解他們使用約會程式的經驗及他們進行風險性行為的動機。第一階段的定性數據會用於建立互動網絡干預。第二階段是一項隨機對照試驗，男男性接觸者將被隨機分為干預組(n = 200) 和對照組 (n = 200). 干預的內容包括(1) 鼓勵他們使用安全套及定期進行HIV / STI測試，(2) 讓他們知道使用安全套及定期進行HIV / STI測試是十分普遍及(3) 加強安全套使用自我效能感及溝通。對照組僅接收沒有心性健康成分的信息。兩組將在基線和基線後三個月和六個月進行評估。主要成效指標將是無套肛交的頻率。如果本干預成功，它可以被政府及非政府組織採用，以減少本港愛滋病毒感染率。

27607518.label: Realisation of objectives
27607518.value: Objective 1: To understand the motives, norms, attitudes and experience of MSM dating app users and their engagement in risky sexual behaviours. To accomplish this objective, a qualitative study was undertaken in 2019. Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted with 31 Chinese men who have sex with men (MSM). The data were analyzed using the thematic analysis method suggested by Braun and Clarke. Concerning participants' experiences with dating app usage and their engagement in risky sexual behaviors, four themes were identified: Theme 1: Picking Mr. Right – Screening and Selecting a Partner; Theme 2: App-Facilitated Sexual Practices – Variations and Adaptations; Theme 3: Safe Sex Only? Navigating Protective Measures for Safer Encounters; and Theme 4: The Ramifications of Unsafe Sex. In summary, factors associated with app-based matching included sex roles, HIV serostatus, and the availability of meeting venues. These dating apps facilitated various types of sexual encounters. Condoms were generally used for safer intercourse, except by younger and inexperienced individuals or when drugs were consumed before or during sex (chemsex). A significant interest in non-penetrative sexual behaviors was expressed by our sample. Seeking post-exposure prophylaxis methods and/or sexual health screenings was common after exposure to infection risks. Sexually abusive encounters led to changes in sex-searching habits and reduced trust in relationship formation. Furthermore, four themes related to sexual violence were also identified. Theme 1: Different Forms of Sexual Violence, from Physical to Virtual; Theme 2: Inner Struggles with Fears and Worry; Theme 3: Low Awareness and Perceived Risk of Sexual Violence – ‘It Has Nothing to Do with Me’; and Theme 4: Dilemma towards Sexual Violence Prevention. In summary, physical and image-based forms of sexual violence were identified, causing participants to experience psychological distress, fear of contracting HIV/other STIs, notoriety within the gay community, and discrimination and stigmatization within their family and workplace. To minimize the risk of sexual violence, some participants were careful about the location where they engaged in sex and the practice of sharing explicit photos with others. However, some participants demonstrated low awareness and perceived risk of sexual violence. Objective 2: To develop a culture-specific, interactive web-based intervention that promotes safe sex practices among MSM dating app users. To achieve objective 2, a website intervention named "Safe Fun Battle" was developed. The website was developed in collaboration with local organizations that offer community support and HIV/STI testing services for the MSM population. The content was informed by real-life examples gathered from the qualitative interviews (Objective 1) and insights from front-line workers. The intervention aimed to enhance participants' self-efficacy and decision-making skills regarding condom use, negotiation, and HIV/STI testing in real-life contexts. The intervention consisted of two parts. 1. Interactive Game: Participants engaged with three tailored scenarios depicting potential dangers of meeting sexual partners through dating apps and risks to sexual health during encounters. In each storyline, participants made virtual decisions, with each action leading to a different outcome. 2. Knowledge-based Information: Participants received information on safer sex practices, including condom and lubricant usage, an overview of various STIs and testing methods, and general information on pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) access in Hong Kong. Additionally, participants were presented with information related to chemsex, sexual violence, and image-based sexual violence. The control group received educational content about sexual orientations, which was not directly relevant to the intervention components on dating apps and safer sex. Objective 3: To evaluate the effectiveness of the interactive web-based intervention in reducing risky sexual behaviours (condomless anal sex, group sex and substance misuse in conjunction with sex), enhancing self-efficacy in and attitudes towards condom use, and increasing the frequency of HIV/STI testing among MSM dating app users. A two-arm, assessor-blinded, randomized, parallel-group trial with a 6-month follow-up period was conducted in Hong Kong from 2020 to 2022. The trial was registered on ISRCTN (ISRCTN16681863). Participants were enrolled using convenience sampling. The intervention group received interactive game and knowledge-based information. The control group was provided with brief information and educational materials about sexual orientation and identity. The primary outcome was the occurrence of condomless anal sex in the last 3 months as measured by a self-report item. The secondary outcome included (i) occurrence of group sex in the last 3 months, (ii) occurrence of chemsex in the last 3 months, (iii) self-efficacy in condom use as measured by the validated traditional Chinese version of the Condom Self-Efficacy Scale, (iv) attitudes towards condom use as measured by the UCLA Multidimensional Condom Attitudes Scale, (v) occurrence of HIV testing in the last 3 months and (vi) occurrence of other STI testing in the last 3 months. The intention-to-treat principle was applied, with linear mixed-effects models used to assess differential changes in continuous outcomes. Generalized linear mixed-effects models with logit links were utilized to analyze binary outcomes. In total, 480 MSM enrolled in the study (240 in the intervention and 240 in the control group). Regarding the primary outcome, the generalized linear mixed-effects model found that participants in the intervention group demonstrated significantly larger reductions in the likelihood of having engaged in condomless anal sex in the last 3 months (time-by-group interaction p-value <0.05). The between-group difference at 6-month follow-up found that participants in the intervention group was less likely to engage in condomless anal sex in the last 3 month than participants in the control group with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.64 (p-value <0.05). The linear mixed-effects models found that the intervention group demonstrated a significantly larger improvement in condom use self-efficacy, as measured by the Condom Self-Efficacy Scale total score (time-by-group interaction: P<0.001), and attitudes towards condom use, as measured by the UCLA Multidimensional Condom Attitudes Scale total score (time-by-group interaction: P<0.001). However, no statistically significant differences were found in other secondary outcomes, such as group sex, chemsex, HIV testing, and other STI testing.

27607518.label: Major findings and research outcome
27607518.value: The comprehensive qualitative investigation identified eight salient themes. Theme 1: Picking Mr. Right – Screening and Selecting a Partner; Theme 2: App-Facilitated Sexual Practices – Variations and Adaptations; Theme 3: Safe Sex Only? Navigating Protective Measures for Safer Encounters; and Theme 4: The Ramifications of Unsafe Sex. Theme 5: Different Forms of Sexual Violence, from Physical to Virtual; Theme 6: Inner Struggles with Fears and Worry; Theme 7: Low Awareness and Perceived Risk of Sexual Violence – ‘It Has Nothing to Do with Me’; and Theme 8: Dilemma towards Sexual Violence Prevention. The study scrutinized factors influencing matching on dating apps among MSM and underscored the heterogeneous nature of sexual encounters facilitated via these digital platforms. Additionally, the research delved into the experiences and perceptions of sexual violence among Chinese MSM dating app users. The qualitative study results were published in the Journal of Sex Research and Journal of Advanced Nursing. A conference abstract encapsulating the qualitative discoveries has been submitted and is currently under review. The randomized controlled trial (RCT) results indicate that a web-based intervention can effectively mitigate condomless anal sex while bolstering condom use self-efficacy and fostering positive attitudes towards condom utilization. However, no statistically significant differences between the intervention and control groups were found in other secondary outcomes, such as group sex, chemsex, HIV testing, and other STI testing. The trial protocol was published in BMC Public Health. A conference abstract delineating the trial findings has been submitted and is presently under review. The manuscript of the main findings is being prepared for submission to an international peer-reviewed journal. The RCT's baseline data was analyzed to pinpoint contributing factors to the prevalence of condomless anal sex among Chinese MSM. The analysis revealed that approximately 40% of participants engaged in condomless anal sex within the past three months. Several factors were correlated with an increased propensity for indulging in condomless anal sex, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) usage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 7.33), participation in chemsex within the last three months (aOR: 3.68), involvement in group sex within the past three months (aOR: 2.41), and being in a committed relationship (aOR: 2.09). Furthermore, MSM who demonstrated greater condom use self-efficacy exhibited a decreased likelihood of engaging in condomless anal sex (aOR: 0.90). A conference abstract encapsulating these findings has been submitted and is currently under review. The manuscript is being prepared for submission to an international peer-reviewed journal.

27607518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27607518.value: The qualitative study revealed a diverse range of themes related to the experience of dating app usage among MSM, shedding light on the complexities of sexual encounters and incidents of sexual violence. As a result, these findings have significant implications for designing effective interventions aimed at promoting safer sexual practices among MSM dating app users. Additionally, the insights gained regarding sexual violence can aid in the development of tailored primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention programs for MSM and beyond. This research also lays a solid foundation for further exploration of the identified themes, uncovering additional factors that may contribute to the prevalence of condomless anal sex and sexual violence. Furthermore, the results of the randomized controlled trial (RCT) suggest the potential for enhancing the web-based intervention to address secondary outcomes such as group sex, chemsex, and HIV/ other STI testing, thus increasing its overall effectiveness. The recommended course of action includes the following: conducting additional qualitative and quantitative studies to validate and build upon the current findings; refining the web-based intervention to improve its impact on secondary outcomes; and investigating alternative intervention methods to ensure a comprehensive and tailored approach to fostering safer sexual practices among MSM dating app users.

27607518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27607518.value: The significance and value of this research project lie in its potential to improve sexual health and reduce the prevalence of risky sexual behaviors among men who have sex with men (MSM). By understanding the experiences of MSM who use dating apps, the study provides valuable insights into the factors that contribute to risky sexual behaviors and their experiences and perceptions of sexual violence. The development of a culture-specific, interactive web-based intervention offers a novel approach to promoting safe sex practices among MSM. The evaluation of the intervention's effectiveness in reducing risky sexual behaviors and enhancing self-efficacy and attitudes towards condom use provides evidence-based support for the implementation of such interventions in real-world settings. The positive outcomes observed in the study highlight the potential of interactive, web-based interventions in promoting safer sex practices and reducing the prevalence of condomless anal sex among MSM. Overall, the research project holds significant value in addressing sexual health disparities and enhancing the well-being of MSM. This project has the potential to make a positive impact on the lives of MSM, the broader LGBTQ+ community, and public health as a whole.

27607818.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27607818.value: Schooling plays an important role in nation-building, and hence state power often seeks to disperse ideas and values in favor of the national interest through it. However, what happens to schooling when the national interest crosses boundaries? Such a situation is not uncommon, particularly when it comes to the education of trans-territory ethnic groups and overseas diasporas. The Republican China-registered secondary schools in British Hong Kong from 1928 to 1949 exemplify just such a scenario. Although the Republican Chinese government recognized British sovereignty over Hong Kong, it considered all ethnic Chinese in the colony to be part of the Chinese nation. Therefore, from China’s point of view, the schooling of the majority Chinese population in British Hong Kong was a matter of the education of its overseas diaspora. Thus, although all schools in Hong Kong were required to register with the colonial government’s Education Department, one-third of secondary schools in the territory were also registered with the Republican Chinese government. The proposed research will explore (1) the factors motivating the Republican Chinese government to extend its administration to Hong Kong schools; (2) the factors constraining it from advocating nationalism in those schools; (3) how schools reacted to the two governments; and (4) how the colonial government responded to education intervention by China. Hong Kong newspapers from the 1930s and 1940s will be the major source of data for this study, although it will also utilize archival records from Hong Kong, mainland China and Taiwan. School publications and descriptive records of Hong Kong schools registered in China during the period under study will also be consulted. The study’s findings will be analysed in twofold. First there will be discussion on why and how the Republican Chinese government involved itself in the schooling of Hong Kong, as well as how both Hong Kong schools and the British Hong Kong government conflicted or compromised with the Chinese government. Second the profiles of around 10 Republican China-registered Hong Kong schools will be complied in order to understand the perspectives of the schools themselves. The study will not only provide a missing piece of Hong Kong education history, but also lay a foundation for further comparison of cross-border national influences on education and shed new light on the relationship between education and state power. 教育在國家形成的過程裏扮演重要角色，因此國家權力往往謀求透過教育傳播對國家有利的思想和價值觀。那麼，如果國家利益超越了邊界，對教育又會有甚麼影響呢？這種情況並不罕見，在涉及跨境民族和境外僑民的時候更加明顯。1928 至 1949 年間在英治香港而又向中國內地國民政府立案的中學正正是這樣的情況。雖然國民政府承認英國對香港的主權，但是也將殖民地下所有華人視為中國國民。所以，按照中國的觀點，英治香港下主流華人的教育乃是中國華僑教育的管轄範圍。正因如此，當時香港所有學校都需要向殖民地政府教育司署註冊，其中有約三分之一的學校也同時向中國內地的國民政府註冊。本研究旨在探究：一，是甚麼原因驅使國民政府延伸其管轄範圍至香港學校；二、有哪些因素妨礙國民政府在香港學校推廣國家意識；三、學校如何回應兩個政府；及四、殖民地政府如何回應中國內地對殖民地教育的干預。本研究將以 1930 及 1940 年代的香港報章為主要資料來源，同時會利用在香港、中國內地、台灣等地區的檔案文獻，也會參考這段時期的學校刊物及相關學校的記載。本研究的成果將分兩部分闡述，首先本研究將討論中國內地國民政府為何及如何參與香港的教育，而香港的學校及港英政府與中國內地政府有何矛盾又怎樣妥協，然後本研究將會選取大約十所向中國內地註冊的香港學校，為這些學校編寫傳略，從這些學校的視角考察問題。本研究將會補充過去香港教育史研究的不足，同時為進一步探究跨境教育領導權、了解教育與國家權力的關係提供新的資料。

27607818.label: Realisation of objectives
27607818.value: This project explores cross-boundary hegemony over schooling by examining the Hong Kong schools registered in Mainland China between 1928 and 1949 through archival documents, old newspapers, and school publications. The social unrest and pandemic from 2019 to early 2023 inevitably posed significant challenges to the progress of this project. The most crucial part of this project is to survey the archival documents of the Chinese Republican Government preserved in Nanjing, Guangzhou and Taipei. Unfortunately, I could not visit the archives during the original project period due to travel restrictions. I am deeply grateful to the panel for approving my applications for extension on several occasions. According to the original plan, I would have made two trips each to Guangzhou, Nanjing and Taipei. It was not until January 2023, when the first stage of border re-opening was implemented, that I could finally visit the archives in Guangzhou for the first time. In May 2023, I visited the Second Historical Archives of China at Nanjing. Since the Mainland had just recovered from the pandemic, too many people were applying to visit the Second Historical Archives of China, and I was only approved to visit the archives for two days. The most essential information was recorded. In July 2024, I will conduct another visit to the Second Historical Archives of China in Nanjing. I will also make up for my planned but never-made visit to the archives in Taipei in December 2024. Even though, the acquisition of these key archival materials has benefitted the original fragmentary information from old newspaper clippings and school publications, which can now be organically linked to form a vivid historical narrative. Thus, all three objectives of this project will be satisfactorily answered. The first objective of this project is to explore why and how the Republican Chinese government participated in schooling in Hong Kong. Official documents and archival records show that China’s participation in education in Hong Kong was part of the policy on overseas Chinese education. Several factors motivated the Chinese Government to attach importance to overseas Chinese education. Firstly, the Chinese Nationality Law at that time adopted the jus sanguinis principle, which granted all ethnic Chinese overseas with Chinese nationality. It laid the ground for the Republican Government to regard overseas Chinese education as part of national education. Secondly, overseas Chinese were very important to China’s economy and politics. Therefore, the Republican Government paid much attention to the education of overseas Chinese to maintain their Chinese identity and to cultivate the next generation. Thirdly, the ruling Kuomintang was worried about the development of opposition forces overseas. Therefore, it was considered necessary to teach overseas Chinese patriotic ideas in line with the Kuomintang’s doctrine. Within the Chinese Republican Government, overseas Chinese education was the responsibility of the Overseas Chinese Affairs Commission. However, the commission did not officially implement the policy overseas. Instead, it was through the local school principals and teachers that the unofficial Overseas Chinese Education Association was organised as an agent. The main task of the Overseas Chinese Education Association was to mobilise local schools to register in the Mainland, adopt Mainland curriculum and teaching materials, and encourage students to study in the Mainland. It also publicised patriotism in the local education sector and supported the Republican Government, especially when China struggled to resist the Japanese invasion. However, archival documents also reveal problems with the implementation at that time. For example, the Overseas Chinese Affairs Commission and the Ministry of Education sometimes had conflicts. In addition to the Overseas Chinese Education Association, the Kuomintang party organisation, as well as home region and university alumni networks, were also an essential channel for implementing education policies from the Mainland. The second objective aims to evaluate the impact of the Republican Chinese government’s participation in Hong Kong schools. The old newspapers and school publications reveal that the main motive of Hong Kong schools registering in the Mainland was to obtain recognition of their academic qualifications. In this way, students from the Mainland can be enrolled directly, and graduates of the schools can conveniently pursue further studies in the Mainland. This could help with enrollment and be attractive to these self-financing private schools. To be registered, the school had to meet the requirements of the Mainland. The school should form the board of directors, and the premises should have a science laboratory, a library, and preferably a playground. These requirements were higher than the original standards of private Chinese schools in Hong Kong, forcing these schools to improve. In terms of teaching, these schools had to meet the requirements of both the Hong Kong and the Mainland curricula. It raised the question of which curriculum should be emphasised and how the two curricula should be integrated. Because of the adoption of the Mainland curriculum, pedagogies commonly used in the Mainland were introduced to Hong Kong. The third objective aims to determine how the British Hong Kong government reacted to the Chinese government’s intervention in Hong Kong education. Since almost all of the Hong Kong Government’s pre-war education records were not preserved, it is not easy to find relevant documents. We know that the British Hong Kong Government, to maintain a good relationship with the Mainland, was very tolerant of educational intervention from the Mainland, leaving it alone as long as it was not conducted officially and did not oppose British rule. However, the Hong Kong Government also regarded the educational leadership from the Mainland as a competitor. Many of the 1935 Burney Report recommendations, including the extension of the government’s responsibility in primary education, strengthening Chinese language education, and establishing a teachers’ training college, were probably made in response to the hegemony from the Mainland. These directions continued after the war and profoundly impacted education in Hong Kong. Over the past half year, I have rewritten the early drafts almost from scratch again. One of the expected outcomes of this project is a monograph, which is now about 50% complete. This monograph will consist of 12 chapters. Chapters 1.1 and 1.2 will be the background. The following Chapters 2.1 to 2.5 will be a chronological discussion of the interaction between the Chinese Republican Government and the Hong Kong schools, and the last Chapters 3.1 to 3.5 will be case studies of individual school histories. The book is expected to be ready for publication by August 2025. This project has opened up many new academic topics for further research. In the previous studies, most writings on the history of education in Hong Kong were based on the archives of the British Hong Kong Government. As a result, the focus of the writings was inevitably skewed towards the small number of government or church-organised grant schools that taught mainly in English. Almost for the first time, this project focuses on the history of education in Hong Kong in private Chinese schools, which had been overwhelmed in number. This project reveals the rich archival collections of Hong Kong education in Guangzhou, Nanjing and Taipei. These previously under-recognised materials will give strong impetus to future research on the education history of Hong Kong.

27607818.label: Major findings and research outcome
27607818.value: Previous studies on the relationship between the state and schooling mainly discussed the relationship within one country. However, when education involves cross-boundary ethnic groups, it is possible that the schooling may encounter two nations at the same time. Our project suggests that what happens in such circumstances depends on which side, the “country of origin” or the “country or region of residence”, was stronger in nation-state awareness. In the case of Hong Kong from 1928 to 1949, China, as the country of origin for the local Chinese population, was much more assertive in nation-state awareness than British side. As a result, the hegemony of the Chinese Republican Government was able to profoundly affect schooling in Hong Kong in less than a decade. Our study draws on archives, old newspapers and school publications to explain how this hegemony came to be, how it was realised, and its impact. This will lay the groundwork for further research on cross-boundary hegemony in education in other places and times. Our project points out that the archives of the Chinese Republican Government preserved in Nanjing, Taipei, and Guangzhou have also documented Hong Kong education from 1928 to 1949 in large quantities. In addition, previous writings have mainly focused on the small number of government and church schools that taught mainly in English and seriously neglected the private Chinese schools that constituted around 90% of the total number of schools. Our project provides a new perspective by focusing, for the first time, on private Chinese schools in Hong Kong. The outcome of this project will be a monograph that includes a detailed historical account of how the Chinese Republican Government implemented educational leadership across the boundary in British-ruled Hong Kong, as well as the history of five Hong Kong schools that have registered in the Mainland. The preliminary findings of this project have been presented at two academic conferences, including the AERA Annual Meeting, one of the most prestigious conferences in educational studies. The project also gave two public academic lectures. Both of these have been uploaded to the Internet. One lecture on education during the Japanese occupation period has received over 124,000 views to date, while another on the history of textbooks in Hong Kong was selected by RTHK for public broadcasting. The PI of this project has also taken the opportunity of this project to supervise one PhD student.

27607818.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27607818.value: The findings of this project can be developed into a comparative study of overseas Chinese schooling in other regions or countries. For example, in the 1930s, the overseas Chinese education policy implemented by the Republican Government met with little resistance in Hong Kong. In contrast, it met with such fierce opposition in Thailand that the Sino-Thai diplomatic relationship broke off. The complexity of cross-boundary hegemony in schooling needs to be further investigated. In addition, the data collected during this project will form the basis of the various topics. First, a comprehensive study on the Hong Kong Student Relief Society, which was the leading student organisation in Hong Kong in support of the Chinese War of Resistance against Aggression, a student organisation unique in Hong Kong’s education history and deserves to be studied in depth. Second, Hong Kong’s education during the Japanese occupation, a period which is arguably the most under-researched in Hong Kong’s education history. Third, A database of pre-war Hong Kong schools. There were about 1,100 schools in Hong Kong in 1941, primarily small-scale private Chinese schools, which formed the mainstay of Hong Kong education at that time but were severely neglected.

27607818.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27607818.value: National boundaries often do not coincide with ethnic boundaries. Cross-boundary ethnic groups are, therefore, likely to have “dual affiliations” regarding their countries of origin and residence. It complicates their schooling because education is a means to cultivate national awareness. Between 1928 and 1949, the Chinese Government actively developed education for the overseas Chinese, including Hong Kong. The “Principle of Bloodline” in the nationality law laid the legal basis for these practices. The motivation of the Chinese Government was mainly internal. The overseas Chinese communities have made essential contributions to modernisation. Also, the ruling Kuomintang was worried about the development of opposition forces abroad. Cross-boundary education policy was often practised through unofficial organisations. Other networks, such as political parties and home region associations, were also the vehicles through which cross-boundary leadership was realised. Hong Kong schools registered in the Mainland would greatly benefit enrollment and increase revenue. The schools had to integrate the curricula of both places, and pedagogies from the Mainland were introduced to Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Government viewed the interventions from the Mainland as competitors. The educational reforms implemented in the 1930s were likely a response to the influence of the Mainland.

27608718.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27608718.value: 收編荷里活：為國家服務的電影故事

27608718.label: Project Objectives
27608718.value: To document and analyze contemporary interactions between the entertainment industry and the US military, comparing the perspectives of personnel involved. To contribute theoretical and empirical insights to anthropology and media studies by challenging the assumed divisions between military and civilian spheres, and “soft” skills and “hard” power. To record how entertainment professionals and state agencies create narratives for immersive technologies and how they apply storytelling techniques (e.g. ideation, character development, set design, prototypes, 3D modeling, animation) to better understand heterogeneous knowledge production.

27608718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27608718.value: Hollywood has long been a tool of American government propaganda and military recruitment. However, in 2014 the state and entertainment industry relationship took a new turn: the Pentagon contracted the special effects studio that designed the Ironman 3 movie's exoskeletal suit to produce a real-life robotic, weaponized suit for its commandos in Afghanistan. Costume design is just one of the “solutions” that the military describes entertainment professionals as providing them; others include imagining disaster storylines for security preparedness. Scripts for military interactive training and medical virtual reality therapy are another. Simulation technologies that the entertainment industry help develop are earmarked as dual-use: designed for military members and intended to be converted for civilian use, including student tutoring, job trainees, and PTSD sufferers. From STEM to scriptwriting, these new developments represent the application of entertainment labor from media industries into arenas beyond the realm of entertainment. My study examines contemporary interactions between Hollywood entertainment and the U.S. military, and how the perceived potential of Hollywood ideation and creativity is pursued by the state for war, security, and societal purposes. In doing so, this project aims to reveal new dimensions to the relationship between the American commercial entertainment industry and U.S. state power. This project will investigate how the talents and skills of a range of Hollywood professionals are mobilized by the state to help protect its institutions and citizens while advancing military goals. Implications of such linkages for nation-building remain under-studied in media anthropology. Importantly, as governments around the world organize policies and missions around innovation and debate the value of “creative” industries, this project will demonstrate that the skills and talents fostered by a highly commercial and predominantly male-led industry – from screenwriting to animation – are not just transferable to, but increasingly valorized by, American state agencies, even as individual entertainment professionals may hold critical stances of state policies. This project will use media and web analysis, focus groups, interviews, and participant observation with members of the Hollywood industry to grasp how they work with various state agencies. In doing so, it will track the cross-disciplinarity of knowledge production. In analyzing how Hollywood creativity is deployed by the state, this project will produce timely findings and cultural insights about the ramifications of intersections between entertainment and the military for scholars striving to understand how governments use media to secure the nation. 一直以來荷里活都有份參與美國政府的宣傳和軍事徵募，而這種國家與娛樂工業之間的關係到了2014年更進入了新里程，因爲美國國防部開始與電影《鐵甲奇俠3》（Ironman 3）的特技製作室合作，把電影中的裝甲戰衣轉化成真實的軍事機械戰衣，以供駐守阿富汗的美軍特種部隊使用。事實上，服裝設計只是娛樂業界的技術人員為國家提供的多項軍事方案的其中一種，其他的還有把虛構的災難劇情加入到安保訓練中，以及為軍事互動訓練和醫療用的虛擬實境編寫劇本。從娛樂工業中研發出來的模擬技術更被視爲具備軍民兩用的功能，其服務對象包括學生、職場上的實習生、創傷後壓力症患者等。由娛樂業界衍生出來的種種新技術，其應用範圍從教育上的科技工數（STEM）到劇本編寫，都在在顯示出媒體工業的娛樂業者，已經不僅僅是爲了娛樂大衆這麽簡單了。本人這項研究針對當今荷里活娛樂業界與美國軍事的互動關係，考證荷里活的意念構思和創意所蘊含的潛能，如何被國家所利用和開發，為戰爭、安保和社會提供服務，並以此來揭示美國商業娛樂工業與美國國家權力之間鮮爲人知的一面。具體來説，本項研究將調查荷里活一衆專業人員及其才能和技術，如何被國家驅使去參與保衛國民和國家機構，並從而幫助國家達成某些特定的軍事目的。這些關係在國家建構過程中有著怎樣的意義，在目前的媒體人類學裏仍然未有充分的研究。更重要的一點，就是正當世界各國政府致力為培養創新能力制訂政策，以及探討創意產業的價值，本項研究卻可為我們展示出，在一個以男性主導的高度商業化行業，其發展出來的人才和技術（從電影劇本編寫到動畫製作），不但具備可轉移性，且越來越得到美國國家機構的追捧；即使這個行業内有不少業者對國家政策抱持批判態度，也未能影響這個趨勢。本項研究會採用媒體和網絡分析、焦點小組、訪問、以及在荷里活電影業者之間進行參與觀察，以了解他們如何與各種國家機構合作。這些研究方法能讓我們追蹤考察跨學科的知識生產。在分析荷里活的創意如何被國家調用時，我們也能夠從娛樂業界與軍事之間的交叉關係中，獲得其後續演變的適時調查結果和文化見解，為有志研究政府如何利用媒體保衛國家這個課題的學者提供參考。

27608718.label: Realisation of objectives
27608718.value: First, I have conducted several dozen interviews, both semi-structured and unstructured, with informants in Los Angeles and throughout southern California, a few also based in other states. I conducted participant observation in Los Angeles including, invited to observe filming of videos and museum projects that entailed both the entertainment industry and the military. In 2019 I attended an international computer graphics convention in Los Angeles (Siggraph) that allowed me to observe industry workers demonstrate their products and research, some of them military-funded, and the occasion provided me with an opportunity to talk to them and follow up with interviews. I attended demonstrations at an entertainment research center that allowed me to observe creative and technical processes. I sampled various immersive technologies, and interviewed military veterans who work in Hollywood and participate in an entertainment writing mentorship program. I interviewed military members who participated in writing workshops organized by Hollywood creatives and who are part of an initiative to implement pedagogical changes in military training. I have also conducted media analysis of promotional military literature and videos co-produced with entertainment professionals, learning about the discourse of each sector. Through these research experiences, I have been able to flesh out what I refer to as the military-industrial-imagineering complex that is based in southern California. Second, part of my upcoming book discusses the dynamic character of US empire as constituted by the intermingling of soft and hard power. Soft power has been undertheorized in anthropology in particular, yet my ethnographic and textual findings document that creative professionals in what Joseph Nye considers one of the US’ key sources of soft power – Hollywood – have become a necessary asset in the actual exercise of hard power, or “warfighting” as DOD discourse and military informants refer to it. Third, I observed and interviewed film directors and computer graphics specialists as well as natural language processing engineers to understand how some of the simulation technologies are designed to create immersive and interactive experiences for the user. I found that the application of arts and humanities training demonstrates their practical relevance for the national security state, an extension of the scholarship on useful cinema. Challenges during research: Covid disrupted the progress of overseas data collection and access to informants. See Mid-Term Progress Report. HKU also granted a tenure pause due to the disruption in research and travel. In general, many informants overseas were not available for follow-up conversations during 2020 and most of 2021 due to the pandemic in the US, with people busy converting to online work and/or dealing with family concerns and/or illness. It was difficult to establish rapport when communication was solely online and not in-person. Covid also hindered establishing relationships with possible collaborators. I was supported by a senior colleague in the Dept. of War Studies at Kings College London in my November 2019 application for the reciprocal Kings/HKU (Hong Kong University) Fellowship Awards. However, the Fellowship was cancelled due to Covid travel restrictions, and has not been resumed to apply for again. Attempts to Overcome: I applied for and received a six month extension for my project to try to collect more data. This additional time, just completed, is aiding me in finalizing the book project and journal article completion. Since Covid started, I turned to relying more heavily on digital data collection efforts and textual analysis. Attending numerous webinars on Zoom organized by military and creative professionals particularly in 2021 allowed me to hear about the collaborative book stories and book projects that they have produced. I also devoted more time to analyzing the writing collaborations, the analysis of which will be a chapter in my book. Publication Objectives: I published an article in Media, Culture & Society based on this research. I am currently in talks with editors at two top university presses (U Penn Press; U Michigan Press) who are very excited about my book proposal. I am awaiting response from U Chicago Press. U Penn Press has requested chapters for review for an advance book contract, and these chapters are currently near completion. I will also in the meantime contact Duke University Press. I am completing a journal article, “Storycraft/Statecraft: ‘Useful Fiction’ and the US Military-Industrial-Imagineering Complex,” for submission.

27608718.label: Major findings and research outcome
27608718.value: First, with the help of Hollywood professionals, storytelling is mobilized as a tool for prediction, prevention, and pedagogy within military agencies. See article (Part C, #1) “Imagineering Empire,” published in Media, Culture & Society. Hollywood secures enormous benefits and power from its relationship to dominant institutions, such as the Department of Defense. This is covered in my in-progress book, Military Imagineers: Weaponized Storytelling in US Empire and my in-progress journal article, “Storycraft/Statecraft: ‘Useful Fiction’ and the US Military-Industrial-Imagineering Complex.” Third, heteropatriarchal relations remain fundamental to the maintenance of both the US military and the US entertainment industry despite #MeToo initiatives. (this is in my in-progress book, Military Imagineers).

27608718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27608718.value: In addition to the book and the article in progress (see Part C #2 and #3), I am looking further into AI-driven storytelling technologies and their impact on cultural heritage projects. I will examine the efficacy and ethics of user-driven storytelling tech. As such, I have co-organized a panel for the Royal Anthropological Institute virtual conference Anthropology, AI and the Future of Human Society on June 6-10. The panel, co-organized with Dr. Lisa Messeri at Yale University, is titled “Immersed in the Story: Narrating about and with New Technologies,” and I am presenting the paper “Siri Survivor: AI-driven Storytelling and Future-Proofing Solutions.”

27608718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27608718.value: This project examines contemporary collaborations between the US military and Hollywood creatives. The 9/11 bombings were attributed to a “failure of imagination,” and this research demonstrates that in 9/11’s aftermath, the U.S. national security state has striven to imagine more effectively, its military agencies drawing on multiple techniques of Hollywood storytelling to strengthen its fighting force. Drawing from qualitative research and textual analysis, this study found that military officials are inspired to use what they referred to as “the power of Hollywood storytelling” for internal purposes such as helping to imagine future threat scenarios and national security strategy, and to improve military instruction. Storytelling techniques and technologies are deployed within military agencies, with military members themselves becoming Disney-style imagineers. The military-industrial-imagineering complex illuminates that Hollywood’s power comes as much from relationships it forges with powerful institutions such as the Department of Defense as it does from global box office.

27610618.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27610618.value: 重新构想领袖魅力：从古典起源到当代应用​

27610618.label: Project Objectives
27610618.value: The first objective is a recovery of Weberian theory by way of close readings of his original texts. In contrast to many studies which cite Weber and ‘charisma’ in a rather totemic fashion, I make extensive use of the most original versions of Weber’s writings on the topic, at times retranslating from the original German. Beyond this fealty to his own writings, I take seriously the need to read Weber in context, tracing his inspiration by following his own references, reading his forbearers in the social sciences such as Rudolph Sohm and Karl Holl, and by seeking to understand his contemporary scholarly and political milieu. Some research employing this approach has recently been published in the Journal of Classical Sociology (Joosse 2014). The second objective builds on the first by demonstrating methods for bringing Weberian theory forward, showing how his descriptions of charisma are consonant with certain schools of social theory that post-date him. Specifically, I trace the commensurability between Weber’s writings and symbolic interactionism, while locating his approach more broadly within the ‘performative turn’ in social theory. Work that marries Weber’s model to Goffman’s dramaturgical model has already been published in Sociology of Religion (Joosse 2012) and my piece that does the same within a Bourdieusian framework is forthcoming in Sociological Theory (2017c). A piece that relates the role of Weber’s ‘charismatic hero’ to Stanley Cohen’s ‘folk devil’ from moral panic theory was just published in the British Journal of Criminology (2017b). The third objective involves verifying, refining, and elaborating upon Weber’s descriptions by empirically testing his central ideas. Inspired by Weber’s original intentions (Baehr 2008:59-114), and by the early uses of his followers (Abel 1937; Gerth 1940), the main objective here is to extend analyses of charismatic authority beyond the sectarian and cultic societal marginalia to which it is customarily applied, instead using ‘charisma’ to interpret mainstream politics: in this case the charismatic ascendance of Donald Trump. There is a burgeoning literature on Trump and charisma to which I have already contributed (eg. Meyer 2016; Joosse 2017b; Wagner-Pacifici and Tavory 2017), and new pieces in this area will surely be widely read and much discussed as researchers from across the broad spectrum of social science seek to come to terms with “the Trump phenomenon.”

27610618.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27610618.value: Nearly a century ago, Max Weber wrested the term ‘charisma’ from obscure theological discussion and placed it at the center of his enormously influential tripartite theory of social power. As Weber’s opus as a whole was becoming canonical within the social sciences, however, his scholastic heirs would level a variety of criticisms at ‘charisma’—most of them centered on the idea that it represented a recapitulation of 19th century hero-worship (Gerth and Mills 1946[1958]; Friedland 1964:20) or that it implied an overly-psychological “individualism” or “trait atomism” that stood in need of “sociologizing” (Parsons 1963:lxxiii, Bourdieu 1971[1987]). Thus, while the popularity of ‘charisma’ as a term soared in the European languages (Turner 2003:6), and while it was increasingly applied in popular discourse as a form of “star power” (Derman 2011:88) its currency in professional sociology has depreciated considerably (Joas 1992). This project seeks to redress charisma’s marginal status in social theory. Combining conceptual innovations with empirical demonstration, I make the case that ‘charisma’ should be regarded as a defining component of how social power manifests, not simply (as is sometimes thought) within the insular enclaves of alternative religions and political extremism, but also at the center of modern socio-political orders—what Geertz (1977) referred to as the cultural ‘centers’ of society (also Weber 1919[1946]:79, 296; Eisenstadt 1968). Specifically, I will draw on previous empirical and theoretical work and combine it with new data to advance a novel interpretation of how charismatic dynamics have been propitious for, a) staging Donald Trump’s ascendance during the previous electoral contest, and, b) perpetuating charismatically-devotional relationships during the Presidential phase of his political career. I have already produced series of articles about charisma for leading journals which have contributed to a resurgence of interest in charismatic authority within sociology (Joosse 2006; 2012; 2014; 2015a; 2017a; 2017c). In addition, I am an early contributor to charismatic analyses of Trump per se, having published an article (2017b) on the connection between Trump’s charisma and moral panic theory. The current project will continue this work, using the example of Trump to provide grist for the theoretical project of introducing a novel typology of “charismatic counter-roles.” The typology, described in this proposal, looks beyond mere “follower agency” (Junker 2013), combining classic Weber with contemporary theory to give a novel account of how political rivals, incredulous bystanders, and dismissive commentators produce performative contrasts with the charismatic leader in ways that actualize charismatic legitimacy. 近一个世纪以前，马克斯·韦伯从晦涩的神学讨论中获得了“魅力”一词，并将其置于其极具影响力的社会权力三方理论的中心。然而，随着韦伯作为一个整体的作品在社会科学中成为规范，他的学术继承人将在“魅力”中对各种批评进行平衡 - 其中大部分都集中于它代表19世纪英雄崇拜的重演（Gerth）和米尔斯1946年[1958];弗里德兰德1964：20）或者暗示一种过度心理的“个人主义”或“特质原子论”需要“社会化”（Parsons 1963：lxxiii，Bourdieu 1971 [1987]）。因此，虽然“魅力”作为一个术语的流行在欧洲语言中飙升（特纳2003：6），并且它越来越多地应用于流行话语作为“明星力量”的形式（Derman 2011：88）其货币在专业社会学已大幅贬值（Joas 1992。 该项目旨在纠正人格魅力在社会理论中的边缘地位。将概念创新与实证论证结合起来，我认为“魅力”应该被视为社会权力如何体现的一个决定性因素，而不是简单地（有时被认为）在另类宗教和政治极端主义的岛屿飞地内，而且现代社会政治秩序的中心 - 格尔茨（1977）所称的社会文化“中心”（Weber 1919 [1946]：79,296; Eisenstadt 1968）。具体来说，我将利用之前的经验和理论工作，并将其与新数据相结合，推进对魅力动态如何有利的新颖解释：a）在前一次选举竞赛期间演绎唐纳德特朗普的优势，以及b）具有超凡魅力 - 他政治生涯总统阶段的虔诚关系。我已经为主要期刊制作了一系列关于魅力的文章，这些文章促成了社会学中对魅力权威的兴趣的重新兴起（Joosse 2006; 2012; 2014; 2015a; 2017a; 2017c）。此外，我是对特朗普本身的魅力分析的早期贡献者，发表了一篇关于特朗普的魅力与道德恐慌理论之间联系的文章（2017b）。目前的项目将继续这项工作，使用特朗普的例子为引入一种新的“魅力反作用”类型的理论项目提供基础。该提案中描述的类型学不仅仅是“追随者”（Junker） 2013年），将经典的韦伯与当代理论相结合，对政治对手，不相信的旁观者和不屑一顾的评论家如何与具有超凡魅力的领导者形成一种表现形式的对比，以实现魅力合法性。

27610618.label: Realisation of objectives
27610618.value: Thank you very much for the opportunity to conduct this research. I can confidently say that the objectives were fully achieved, in that: A. I have produced two articles in leading journals which have extended and expanded my research program on charismatic authority. B. I have received 6 research awards from the likes of the American Sociological Association, the International Sociological Association, the Society for the Study of Social Problems, and the University of Hong Kong. C. I presented research at 8 international conferences for leading scholarly associations, in addition to several other local ones. I gave an international keynote address in Germany. D. In terms of the above three objectives, my publications have succeeded in (1) recovering a central Weberian concept through a reexamination and close reading of his texts; (2) brought Weber's theory forward, by combining it with more current social theories (particularly relating to social movements and gender); and (3) using charisma theory to interpret new empirical phenomena (particularly environmental social movements, and gender in the context of the election of Trump). E. As a note: unfortunately, due to COVID-19, four (and counting) of my forthcoming conferences were cancelled. For this reason, the travel funds in this grant were dramatically underused. I would hope that there is some possibility to still attend these conferences (or other similar makeup conferences) and, if the UGC decides it is reasonable, use the unspent funds at that future time. I had also planned to hire a research assistant during a research trip to Canada, this summer (2020). This accounts for an additional $45,000HK in unspent funds. Like many, I have retreated into my home, to do work on my own, keeping my spirits up while also reminding myself of how fortunate my circumstances are, when compared with others'. There is no need for me to keep my grant active until its original completion date (Aug 31, 2020), and so, with the promised deliverables in hand, I am submitting this early.
