rows: The first objective is a recovery of Weberian theory by way of close readings of his original texts. In contrast to many studies which cite Weber and ‘charisma’ in a rather totemic fashion, I make extensive use of the most original versions of Weber’s writings on the topic, at times retranslating from the original German. Beyond this fealty to his own writings, I take seriously the need to read Weber in context, tracing his inspiration by following his own references, reading his forbearers in the social sciences such as Rudolph Sohm and Karl Holl, and by seeking to understand his contemporary scholarly and political milieu. Some research employing this approach has recently been published in the Journal of Classical Sociology (Joosse 2014).

The second objective builds on the first by demonstrating methods for bringing Weberian theory forward, showing how his descriptions of charisma are consonant with certain schools of social theory that post-date him. Specifically, I trace the commensurability between Weber’s writings and symbolic interactionism, while locating his approach more broadly within the ‘performative turn’ in social theory. Work that marries Weber’s model to Goffman’s dramaturgical model has already been published in Sociology of Religion (Joosse 2012) and my piece that does the same within a Bourdieusian framework is forthcoming in Sociological Theory (2017c). A piece that relates the role of Weber’s ‘charismatic hero’ to Stanley Cohen’s ‘folk devil’ from moral panic theory was just published in the British Journal of Criminology (2017b).

The third objective involves verifying, refining, and elaborating upon Weber’s descriptions by empirically testing his central ideas. Inspired by Weber’s original intentions (Baehr 2008:59-114), and by the early uses of his followers (Abel 1937; Gerth 1940), the main objective here is to extend analyses of charismatic authority beyond the sectarian and cultic societal marginalia to which it is customarily applied, instead using ‘charisma’ to interpret mainstream politics: in this case the charismatic ascendance of Donald Trump. There is a burgeoning literature on Trump and charisma to which I have already contributed (eg. Meyer 2016; Joosse 2017b; Wagner-Pacifici and Tavory 2017), and new pieces in this area will surely be widely read and much discussed as researchers from across the broad spectrum of social science seek to come to terms with “the Trump phenomenon.”

27610618.label: Major findings and research outcome
27610618.value: Firstly, I attempted to work beyond the inclination to inaugurate alternative theoretical traditions alongside canonical sociology, demonstrating the value of recovering latent gender theory from within classic concepts—in this case, Weber’s “charisma.” Close readings of Weber revealed, (a) tools for theorizing extraordinary, non-masculinist agency, and, (b) clues that help to account for the conventional wisdom (popular and scholastic) that charisma is “not for women.” While contemporary movements may be tempted to eschew charismatic leadership per se because of legacies of dominance by men, there is value in Weber’s formulation, which anticipated the performative turn in social theory that would destabilize biologistic gender ontologies. Value in this exchange also flows back to Weber: by confronting his intermittent tendency to describe charisma in terms that we now recognize as “customs of manly power,” this research revealed heretofore unseen imperfections (i.e., traditionalist modes of legitimation) in his ideal-type. This engagement thus demonstrated an empowering mutuality between contemporary theory and “the classics.” The research also theorized the nexus of gender and charisma in the case of Trump, pointing to possibilities for vitiating Donald Trump’s charisma, as well as for anti-Trumpian charisma. Secondly, working from a narrative criminological framework, this research distinguished and described the ‘narrative of rebellion’ as a generic form that can be encountered widely in situations of asymmetrical struggle. Because narratives of rebellion furnish their tellers with agentic potential across various stages of the ‘rebellious career’ (from contemplation, to participation, to capture, and ultimately to peril), they are desirable cultural accoutrements for bringing into seditious struggle. Rebellion stories typically (a) subsume individuals within collective avatars that are represented as existing somehow ‘outside of life’ – often through charismatic, legendary martyrdom, (b) advance plots that draw causal connections between failure/death and regenerative proliferation ‘from below,’ and (c) promulgate of a sense of solidarity with many as-yet unseen fellow travelers. These features offer protective resources for rebels engaging in criminal resistance, while also providing a framework for sense-making that, rather than obfuscating danger (a prominent feature of existing theories of rebellious participation), offers interpretive resources for contending with the likelihood of a perilous fate.

27610618.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27610618.value: I very much look forward to continuing this area of research, both through theoretical elaboration and empirical application. Specifically, I hope to explore the "routinization of charisma" (a key, but underexplored dynamic through which charismatic performance settles into predictable social patterns) in the case of Trump, and I hope to continue to apply the concept to my research on enviromental social movements and current movement in Hong Kong.

27610618.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27610618.value: This research tries to give an answer to the question as to why some individuals can emerge and, through their leadership style, go on to fundamentally transform society. These transformations can by positive (in the case of Nelson Mandela, for example) or negative (in the case of Hitler, for example). The research itself does not engage in moral assessments of leaders, but rather attempts to show the social processes through which power comes to be concentrated in them, and the effect that such individuals have on society after they are invested with such power. In the present research, I looked at this both in the case of the election of Donald Trump, and in the case of leadership within environmental social movements. I am very grateful for the opportunity to carry out this research, and hope that my work will add to popular understandings of charismatic power.

27613118.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613118.value: Toleration is widely understood to function as an important moderator of ethical life in our global, cosmopolitan world order. In the last decade, however, with the rise of public violence linked to forms of religious fundamentalism, scholarly work in the humanities has turned an increasingly critical eye on the concept of toleration and its continuing relevance to the way in which modern societies understand and manage difference. While some scholars such as Perez Zagorin and A.C. Grayling have called for a renewed commitment to the ideals of Toleration, seeing it as a means to generate forms of mutual respect in our inevitably pluralistic world, others such as Wendy Brown, Jasbir Puar, and Judith Butler have argued that the concept of Toleration itself has a dark and repressive dimension, encouraging new forms of persecution, and surveillance, while claiming to function as a mechanism of freedom and equality. This study seeks to contribute to recent discussions of the issue by turning to the literature produced in the British Long Eighteenth Century. Beginning with the Toleration Act of 1689, the Long Eighteenth Century in Britain witnessed several attempts to institutionalise religious toleration, which in turn generated often violent public opposition. My project focuses on the literary responses to the public conflict over how to define the nature of civic life in the absence of religious hegemony. Focusing on genres of writing that emerged in the Restoration and Eighteenth Century, I trace representations of religious conflict and dialogue in relation to a reading public responding to the state’s attempts to locate the source of collective identity in diversity rather than uniformity. I focus on how emerging genres attempt to shape spaces for inter-faith conversation, as well as identity sources for the moderation of religious conflict. This project asks what existing cultural scripts require revision in order for the licensing of religious pluralism to gain cultural legitimacy. By focusing on how writers negotiated a literary inheritance traditionally invested in ideals of a spiritual monoculture, this project draws attention to the cultural dimensions of Toleration, understanding it as embodied acts that often exceed the codified meanings conveyed in political/legal theory. My project’s focus on the generic and rhetorical aspects of Toleration aims to enrich as well as modify current historical and theoretical understandings of Toleration and its potential and limitations in the ethical management of difference in contemporary society. 論文摘要題目：處理差異:漫長的十八世紀文學中宗教寬容的表達 香港大學英文學院Brandon Chua博士 論文摘要：大眾認為宗教寬容有緩和及維持全球與大都會倫理秩序的重要功能。惟最近十年，隨著與原教旨主義 (religious fundamentalism) 相關的公共暴力 (public violence) 肆虐，人文學科之學術研究遂以更批判性的角度審視「寬容」之概念及理解它如何持續地影響現今社會理解及處理差異。一方面有些學者如Perez Zagorin與 A.C. Grayling等提倡重振宗教寬容之願景，視之為在多元化世界建立互相尊重的方法；另一方面其他學者如Wendy Brown、Jasbir Puar、Judith Butler等卻爭論宗教寬容本身有其黑暗的壓制史，重振它無疑是一邊鼓吹新形式的迫害及監視，一邊卻聲稱它是維繫自由平等的工具。 有鑑於此，本研究旨在探討漫長的十八世紀的英國文學如何處理上述的相關議題，盼能為近期討論薄盡綿力。自1689年的宗教寬容法案 (Toleration Act) 起，英國在漫長的十八世紀經歷了數次嘗試將宗教寬容制度化的事件，却屢因群眾的激烈反對而告終。本研究集中探究文學如何回應大眾爭論，界定在沒有宗教霸權下公民生活的本質。以王政復辟 (Restoration) 及十八世紀的新興文學種類為本，本文追溯宗教衝突及對話的表述，及其如何影響大眾讀者回應國家嘗試尋找集體身份認同差異而非單一性的來源、探討新興文學種類嘗試創造跨信仰的對話空間 (inter-faith conversation) 、及緩和宗教衝突的認同來源。本研究提出哪些文化文本有待修改，以致宗教多元化能獲授文化的合法性。通過分析作家如何商議文學傳承中靈性的單一文化理念 (ideals of a spiritual monoculture) ，本文著重探討宗教寬容的文化層面，及理解實踐宗教寬容往往超越政治與法律理論的固有含義。本研究集中探討宗教寬容的普遍及修辭學的層面，盼能增進及改變現今歷史及理論上對宗教寬容的理解、以了解在當今社會在倫理層面處理宗教寬容及差異的潛力與局限。

27613118.label: Realisation of objectives
27613118.value: 1) The first objective of this project was to identify Toleration as a key and important concept that organised and motivated a significant proportion of imaginative writing around the periods 1660-1780. To that end, I have surveyed and catalogued an extensive body of primary printed sources relating to the issue of Religious Uniformity from the years 1660-1745, from the Restoration of the Monarchy and the Church of England to the end of the Jacobite crises in the mid 18th century. I have thus made significant inroads into understanding the place of toleration in the late 17th century and early 18th century.The significance of Toleration to this period has often been underestimated in the secondary scholarship on 18th Century Literature, which conventionally has been more focused on explicating the centrality of other related concepts like Liberty, Secularism, and Cosmopolitanism. In surveying a range of primary texts and analysing contemporary critical discourse around them, I have found that scholars tend to underestimate the significance of Toleration due to their rather limited understandings of it as a social ideal to be championed and affirmed as a platitude, or as an unequivocal and uncontroversial virtue in little need of substantial discussion or elaboration beyond a limited body of philosophical explication, and an overview of legal/governmental attempts to implement this ideal practically through policy and legislation. My project aimed to complicate our current scholarly understandings of Toleration, developing a more expansive definition of the concept by way of a genealogy that pays closer attention to the affective dimensions of the concept, and the ways in which it organises public emotions and political subjectivities. By revising our views on Toleration by uncovering its subjective dimensions, its affective range, and its ability to solicit a large variety of public emotions, my research undertaken in this project revealed the central role played by Toleration in generating a great deal of the generic innovations in imaginative writing that scholarship has conventionally underestimated. To achieve this end, I surveyed a large printed corpus featuring public debates on Religious Toleration from religious leaders, statesmen, and periodical writers in the period, focusing on the ways in which various arguments for and against the implementation of religious Toleration are conveyed and engaged with. Out of this survey of polemical texts, I have published an article with a major period-studies journal that examines the central position occupied by Toleration in the years leading up to the Glorious Revolution, and the new poetic traditions he inspired. This article will also be the basis of a book-length project that I am currently completing. This book will expand and elaborate the claims that I make in this article. My research undertaken in this project has also allowed me to complete and publish a related article on the topic of Cosmopolitanism and the ways in which it informs Women’s Writing in the early 18th century, during the period of the first Jacobite crisis. The project did not fully achieve the objective I initially envisioned, however, due to constraints that presented as a result of the Covid pandemic. I had originally intended to survey a whole range of primary documents in order to make a case for Toleration’s centrality to other arenas of civic life, such as Education, Marriage, and the organisation of Empire. I was unable to visit any of the archives that I originally planned to visit due to the considerable travel restrictions. This meant significantly reducing the scope of the project, and narrowing the range of primary sources to be examined. I was thus no longer able to explore certain key genres, such as the way toleration informs the composition of didactic, periodical literature (such as the innovative magazines and newsletters that emerged in the 18th century) as well as debates on inter-religious marriage. While this omission has been disappointing, I think the narrower scope makes for a better and more viable book length project. I hope to take up the issues of Education and Interfaith Marriages in separate projects in the future. Nevertheless, this project has given me a good foundation for the pursuit of these future endeavours. While I wasn’t able to visit certain archives for surveying of non-print, manuscript sources, I was able to use money from the grant to hire a research assistant to compile a database of primary textual materials, and for also sourcing access to some key documents from libraries and collections overseas. 2) This project has reread a number of different literary texts from the Long Eighteenth Century through the context of an enriched, expanded, definition of Toleration. My survey of an extended printed corpus has allowed me to develop a comprehensive historical understanding of how literary and other textual creations mediate public understandings of religious controversy. By proposing close analysis of the often under-explored affective dimensions of Toleration, this project has made a case for understanding Eighteenth Century Literature (often presented as ushering in new structures of feeling — ‘The Age of Satire’; ‘The Sentimental Age’) as an important forum for discussions and debates over how best to manage the relationship between private and public life, in the wake of the demands that Toleration was making in terms of regulating religious conviction and the way it can be expressed in public. 3) This project has surveyed a range of polemical discourse over the crisis of Religious Uniformity from the years 1660-1742. I have read and analysed a range of pamphlet literature, parliamentary speeches, church sermons, and royal declarations around the issue of religious diversity and the need to introduce measures for the toleration of different faiths. I bring this body of primary textual material in conversations with a growing body of secondary scholarship on the concepts of Liberalism and Cosmopolitanism. This historical detail is crucial for offering a more nuanced account of these much-studied concepts. This project’s close engagement with the polemical discourse around religious diversity enables a more contextualised account of how concepts like Liberalism and Cosmopolitanism came to be seen as social virtues in subsequent periods. The survey of printed polemic around the Restoration government’s controversial approach to change the texture of religious life in this period undertaken and completed in this project meets the objective of situating civic ideals of Liberalism within a broader history that allows us to understand better how these ideals emerged as ideals, and the kinds of subjectivities and structures of public emotions they shaped. 4) By surveying a range of primary documents related to religious controversy, and by analysing a body of secondary literature related to the dissection of Toleration, and related concepts of Secularism, Liberalism, and Cosmopolitanism, this project has shown how the literary culture of the Long Eighteenth Century was primarily interested in exploring, discussing, and debating the effects of Toleration by giving the concept embodied and subjective life through innovations in imaginative writing and key generic developments in narrative discourse.

27613118.label: Major findings and research outcome
27613118.value: The major findings of this project is that the key innovations of Eighteenth Century Literature (satirical writing, utopian literature, sentimental fiction) are all chiefly occupied by the problem of religious diversity and the institutionalisation of Toleration. The extent to which religious controversy permeates a body of writing conventionally understood as ‘secular’ is an important finding of this project. This project has also established, through a genealogical inquiry, that Toleration is fundamentally a discourse involving affect, emotion, and subjectivity. This affective dimension discloses a hitherto under appreciated role that Literary Culture, with its cultivation, solicitation and shaping of subjective responses, played with regard to the institutionalisation of Toleration in the period. My survey of primary source documents on the attempts by various government regimes to implement policies and legislation to do with Toleration has also revealed the significance of Toleration to other facets of civic life, such as the administration of an emerging Empire, diplomatic activities, and expansion of trade. I had prepared a number of conference papers documenting my findings. Unfortunately, I was not able to present most of them due to Covid restrictions resulting in cancellations. I was able to circulate drafts of my papers to other experts in my field, for informal feedback, nevertheless. I have prepared 4 articles that circulate these findings. Two of these articles have been published: the first of these is an article on innovations in satiric poetry, using the poet laureate John Dryden as a case study. The second is an article on how English engagements with China in the early 18th century grew out of domestic religious controversies over problems of diversity and toleration. I have also completed a pair of articles on how religious toleration and conviction are gendered in the period. One of these articles have been submitted for review, and the second is in its final stages of editing.

27613118.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27613118.value: I have completed a book proposal on the representation of Religious Conviction based on the findings of this project. A further development of this research will be the completion and publication of this book project. My book project aims to convey the findings of this current research, as well as develop them further by extending the scope of inquiry by looking at how Religious Toleration informed understandings of the education of children in the 18th century, as well as the practice of inter-religious marriages. My book will thus be on the effects of Religious Toleration on domestic life in the period. This project’s focus on public emotions and their reconfiguration by the institutional imperatives of religion has also led me into research on more specific religious controversies in the period, such as the Jacobite uprisings and its unleashing of anti-Catholic sentiments, the parliamentary debates on naturalising Jewish subjects in the later Eighteenth Century, and the public backlash against Methodism. These specific controversies require more focused and individual analyses, rather than the broad survey I have performed here under the general concept of Toleration. I hope to further my inquiries in these specific controversies in the future. At the moment, I am preparing a GRF application on the representation of England’s religious history in 18th Century Literature. It is my contention that the demand for Religious toleration in the 18th century influenced the way in which England’s history was represented in popular discourse. I hope to continue this research through a project that looks specifically at the genre of the Shakespearean History Play in the 18th Century — a topic that hasn’t been studied in any thorough fashion.

27613118.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27613118.value: Toleration is often presented as a cherished ideal in contemporary liberal cultures. Even today, as the world witnesses the resurgence of forms of cultural prejudice such as anti-semitism, islamophobia, and discrimination against ethnic, sexual and gendered identities, Toleration is still vaunted as a unique accomplishment of global modernity, and one we need to remain committed to. This project offers a cultural history of the idea of Toleration. This research aims to unravel the long history of Toleration discourse, starting in the Eighteenth Century, when states like England were attempting to implement legislative instruments to regulate forms of religious persecution. This project examines emergent literary forms of the period, like the novel and sentimental drama, locating them in this context of toleration, in order to understand better the stories of difference and coexistence that people told themselves and each other. The goal of this study is to offer a more complex history of toleration, one that does not see it as a straightforward solution to the problem of bigotry and prejudice, but rather as a complex set of public emotions and subjective dispositions towards religious belief that developed over time to respond to the challenges brought by global modernity.

27616418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27616418.value: 台灣即將成為亞洲第一個認可同性伴侶關係的國家。2016年5月24日，台灣最高法院作出一項支持同性婚姻的判決，判決除認定現行民法不符合憲法的自由平等原則外，同時要求立法院於兩年之內提案修改或是通過新的立法，以保障婚姻平權。這個即將來臨的法律變革，創造了一個進行前瞻性研究的機會，去探討婚姻平權政策與個人福祉間的關聯。 過去有關同性婚姻結果的量化調查研究提供了許多有力的證據，指出同性婚姻的合法化能促進個人的社會心理健康，然而探究同性婚姻的質化研究卻相當缺乏。另外雖然量化研究能提出許多有意義的結果，但卻很少能考量到文化與關係脈絡。文化關係理論指出建立雙向的關係乃是人類核心的渴望，也是個人福祉不可或缺的一環。同時我們也知道華人文化重視關係的和諧，關係的和諧往往也是個人滿足感以及認同感的主要來源。然而時至今日，尚未有研究開始探討同性婚姻與關係福祉間的關聯。此外，目前的研究文獻也未提供任何有關華人同志成年人的非親密關係 - 其父母對於同性婚姻的觀感與反應。為了要對在華人文化脈絡中的同性婚姻有更全面的了解，本研究將會收集同志成人的父母的想法，以了解同性婚姻合法化是如何影響台灣的同志成年人在原生家庭中的關係福祉。 本質性研究將招募15位15位介於18-39歲的同志成人以及他們的一位父母，每位受訪者將在同性婚姻合法化前後各接受一次訪談，總共會有60次深度訪談作為研究資料。訪談將謄為逐字稿。資料分析則採用詮釋現象學的方法，以了解受訪者在台灣社會脈絡中的內在經驗與觀感，並以多種方式來保障資料分析的嚴謹性。本研究的發現將能作為婚姻平權政策的評估參考，此外，透過發掘同性婚姻的文化意涵與對關係的影響，本研究將能充實同性婚姻的跨文化理論。

27616418.label: Realisation of objectives
27616418.value: Objective 1: To evaluate the impact of Taiwan’s legalization same-sex marriage on Taiwanese LGB young adults’ relational well-being In this project, I have collected a wealth of data through two waves of interviews with 15 dyads – an LGB young adult and a parent. These longitudinal interviews have provided rich and in-depth data to identify if Taiwan’s legalization of same-sex marriage was associated with LGB young adults’ perception of relational well-being. The dyadic data indicate that this policy change has contributed to the relationship quality, authenticity, and closeness between LGB young adults and their parents. In specific, the interviews with LGB young adults suggest that after the same-sex marriage legislation passed, these LGB young adults have noticed the shifts in their parents’ behavior and attitudes towards LGB-related issues along with a stronger bond and open communications with their parents. Although the legalization of same-sex marriage itself may not cause a drastic change in parents’ understanding and perception of LGB people, this policy change was unanimously recognized by the LGB participants as a positive contribution to their relationships with parents and sense of wellbeing. Objective 2: To theorize the policy implications of same-sex marriage beyond a Western independence-oriented paradigm The interview data have captured the culture-specific implications of same-sex marriage legalization in Chinese societies. It is known that in the Taiwanese society, many LGB young adults are heavily concerned with and driven to maintain close bonding with parents. For example, co-residence with parents is not uncommon for LGB young adults and filial piety continues to be endorsed. Yet, the prominence of filial value and the quest for bonding between parents and LGB children could intensify parents’ struggle with the child’s LGB sexuality. Many qualitative studies with Taiwanese parents have shown that parents become worried about their children’s future and had a sense of disappointment that their children could not follow the normative life path as other people could. Amid this sociocultural context, the legalization of same-sex marriage could provide a sense of reassurance for the parents, reducing their concern and the tension with the LGB children. The findings of this study shed a light into these culture-specific implications of same-sex marriage legalization and add an innovative insight into the current body of theories (e.g., minority stress theory, the theoretical notion of structural stigma) and empirical studies that were largely constructed in Western, individualistic societies. Objective 3: To illuminate the experiential and relational implications of same-sex marriage policy from the perspectives of LGB young adults’ parents This study recruited 16 parents (12 mothers and 4 fathers) and the interviews have illuminated how the legalization of same-sex marriage in Taiwan has made it easier for them to accept their children’s identities. Although nine parents stated that they had already accepted their child’s LGB identity before the same-sex marriage legal reforms in Taiwan, ten participants emphasized that legal recognition of same-sex partnerships gave them the courage to publicly support their LGB child. The legalization of same-sex marriage made many parents perceive Taiwanese society as increasingly tolerant of LGB people, providing a sense of reassurance and, in turn, increasing their level of support for their LGB children. Viewed together, parental acceptance could be shaped by the legal and social landscape of sexuality. For these parents in Taiwan, the same-sex marriage legalization served to reduce their worry about children’s lives and offered a discursive scheme to see their children’s LGB identities as normal. These experiential and relational implications of same-sex marriage policy have been documented by this study.

27616418.label: Major findings and research outcome
27616418.value: This qualitative study collected dyadic, longitudinal data from LGB young adults and their parents over the course of same-sex marriage legalization in Taiwan and provided significant and novel findings on the implications of marriage equality. Although existing studies conducted in western contexts have identified a wide range of psychosocial benefits arising from LGB-affirmative policies (e.g., same-sex marriage and anti-discriminatory laws), no studies have been done in East Asia to investigate whether marriage equality could influence relationship-related outcomes. With a focus on relational wellbeing, defined as “caring, respect for diversity, reciprocity, nurturance and affection, support, collaboration, and democratic participation in decision-making process,” this study uncovered that this policy reform has created a new relationship context for LGB young adults and their parents to resolve conflict and concerns with being a sexual minority individual in a heteronormative society. Both parties highlighted that the legislation of same-sex marriage have contributed to parental acceptance and generated open communications and support within their families. Aside from the profound implication for parent-child relationship, the LGB participants also highlighted the improvements of their relational well-being as shown in their relationships with themselves (i.e., self-acceptance), intimate relationships, and the relationship between LGB communities and the general public. These consequences were not adequately captured by previous studies and should be interpreted in the context of Taiwan where social harmony and family relationships take precedence over personal interests and goal attainment. Taken together, these results have provided compelling evidence about the effects associated with marriage equality policies in an East Asian context. The findings not only contribute to the emerging literature about same-sex marriage policy but also provide vital support for the activism towards marriage equality policies.

27616418.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27616418.value: The study provides three recommendations for future development of research on same-sex marriage policies. First, since this study only recruited parents who were already aware of and accepting the child’s sexual orientation, future research should seek to collect narratives from parents who have yet accepted an LGB child. Second, future studies can incorporate an intersectionality lens to further diversify the characteristics of participants and examine if marriage equality means differently to LGB young adults who are at various social locations or conditions. Third, accounts of other family members (e.g., siblings, grandparents) will provide important data to enrich the scope of investigations into the consequences of same-sex marriage legalization. Such expansion of data source is particularly promising given the longer-term and close bonds between family members among Chinese families. The findings of this study will be shared to the general public, LGB rights activists, lawmakers, and students through a series of lectures, posts on social media, and academic publications. The results will become important evidence for different stakeholders to envision the effects of legalizing same-sex marriage.

27616418.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27616418.value: This study sought to answer a question: does legalization of same-sex marriage have effects on LGB people’s perception of relationships in different domains? With regards to this topic, scholars from other countries that pioneer in marriage equality and equal rights, such as Australia and the U.S., have found that marriage equality has a wide range of benefits for LGB people’s health and mental health. But no studies have been done in Taiwan – the first in Asia to grant a legal status for two same-sex individuals to form marriage. Moreover, few studies have examined the outcomes related to relationship quality particularly in a family context. Coming from this unique perspective of “relational well-being,” this study found that when same-sex marriage became legal, both LGB young adults and their parents became more open and positive towards diverse sexual orientations and the relationship between them also became more genuine and mutually supportive. Such positive consequences of marriage equality suggest that this policy reform might help resolve LGB people’s family conflicts and personal struggle that are rooted in homonegativity that persists in Chinese societies. The findings lend support for policymakers and activists to continue their advocacy toward social inclusion and promote legal and institutional changes towards equal rights.

28300518.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28300518.value: In 1933, astrophysicist Fritz Zwicky studied radial velocity measurements of several individual galaxies in the well-known Coma cluster of galaxies. He noticed that the galaxies seemed to be moving too fast for the amount of visible matter in the cluster (Sanders 2010). This is the first time an astrophysicist realized that some kind of invisible matter exists in our universe. Later, the kinematic data of galaxies indicate that a large amount of invisible matter exists, the term dark matter is now used to describe this matter. Some proposals suggest that a few stable hypothetical particles, such as weakly interacting massive particles (WIMP), may be dark matter particles. Some of these proposals also suggest that dark matter particles can self-annihilate to form stable and high-energy particles such as electrons, positrons and photons. By assuming dark matter particles can self-annihilate, we can simulate the resulting energy spectrums of the produced particles. The number of particles produced in one second due to dark matter annihilation can also be calculated. There are two major parameters involved in the calculations: annihilation cross section and rest mass of dark matter particles. Moreover, the result also depends on the annihilation channels. Theoretically, dark matter particles can self-annihilate through more than 18 channels (e.g. ee, µµ). In this proposal, we propose constraining the cross section of dark matter annihilation, the rest mass of dark matter particles and the possible annihilation channels by using the latest astrophysical data. The data mainly come from the observations of galaxies. We assume that the positrons and electrons produced would quickly lose their energy to the surroundings mainly through synchrotron radiation, which can be detected by radio telescopes. We develop two new methods and use new and archival data to eliminate the cosmic ray contribution and constrain the dark matter parameters. We will apply for some radio telescopes to get the radio flux profile data which are useful for constraining annihilating dark matter. These constraints can give indirect support in finding new particles in the Large-Hadron-Collider experiment and direct detection experiments of dark matter. Moreover, the observational data can also tell us whether the cross section is velocity dependent or not (the Sommerfeld enhancement effect can produce a velocity-dependent cross section). We will use the radial distribution of dark matter mapped from the data to analyze the possible signature of Sommerfeld enhancement. Reference: Sanders, R. H. (2010). The Dark Matter Problem: A Historical Perspective. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

28300518.label: Realisation of objectives
28300518.value: Most of the objectives have been achieved in this project. For objective 1, we have developed a new method of using multi-frequency analysis and a new method of using flux profile data to constrain dark matter. Some data have been analyzed by these new methods and several papers have been published. For objective 2, we have improved the lower limits of thermal relic dark matter mass to almost TeV order for most of the channels (e.g. bb quark channel). In view of this, we have found that the analysis following four representative annihilation channels (e, mu, tau and b quark) can almost cover the limits of the 18 standard model particle annihilation channels. Therefore, most of our analyses are focussing on the four representative channels. For objective 3, we have explored our analysis of two new target objects (NGC4449 and NGC4214). One of them can help improve the constraints of dark matter. Two related articles have been published. For objective 4, we have observed the radio flux profile data of the M31 and M33 galaxies by the Shanghai Tianma Radio Telescope. Some of the data are still being analyzed. Nevertheless, we have analyzed the archival radio flux profile data of the M31 galaxy and obtained some limits for dark matter. One paper has been published. For objective 5, we have investigated the issue of velocity-dependent annihilation cross section by using the archival radio flux profile data. Although the data are not good enough to determine the velocity dependency, our results show that the flux profile data are consistent with the velocity-independent cross section. The results have been published in a journal article. All together 10 journal articles have been published to disseminate the results of this project. Due to the pandemic situation in 2020, many recognized international conferences have been canceled. We have also presented our results in a few webinars and online conferences.

28300518.label: Major findings and research outcome
28300518.value: By using galactic radio data of the M31 and NGC4214 galaxies, we have ruled out a certain thermal annihilating dark matter mass range ~ 100-500 GeV. These limits are almost the most stringent constraints for dark matter. These results have been published in 3 papers [1,6,8]. However, due to the diffusion uncertainties, dark matter mass < 100 GeV is still possible. We have also investigated the archival radio data of a few galaxy clusters, including A4038, A697, and Ophiuchus clusters. We have applied our newly developed method (the multi-frequency approach) to detect dark matter signals and constrain dark matter mass. These data suggest some possible dark matter signals with dark matter mass 30-100 GeV. These results have been published in 3 papers [3,4,7]. Another study using the method of flux profile data of the M31 galaxy also suggests a similar range [9]. In particular, based on the study of the A4038 cluster, we have found a strong signal with more than 5 sigma [7]. Further analysis and observations can verify these claims. I have combined and summarized the above results of this project in a review article published in [10]. Besides, by applying a similar technique, we have also performed some studies on the TeV dark matter model (based on the DAMPE data) [2] and a new dark matter model proposed recently (the d*(2380) dark matter model) [5]. (Please refer to Part C for the reference order)

28300518.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28300518.value: Based on our developed methods, we have claimed the existence of some possible dark matter signals based on the archival radio data. Further observations and analyses using a wide range of radio frequencies can help verify our claims. Therefore, we propose to observe and analyze galaxy cluster data in our future studies. Since we have developed two new methods to analyze dark matter annihilation signals, we will continue to apply these two methods to further analyze archival data or observed data. We have done some further observations by using the Effelsberg radio telescope in Germany and the FAST in China. The data are being analyzed and we aim at improving the current constraints by the methods developed in this project.

28300518.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28300518.value: Dark matter exists in our universe. However, the properties of dark matter are still poorly understood. In this project, we have developed two new methods to constrain annihilating dark matter properties. By using these methods, we have improved the constraints of dark matter properties by using radio data of galaxies and galaxy clusters. In particular, we have ruled out a certain range of annihilating dark matter mass and discovered some potential signals of dark matter annihilation. A certain potential mass range of dark matter particles has been identified. Further observations and analyses following our newly developed methods can verify our claims in this project and help reveal the mystery of dark matter.

28602718.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28602718.value: 十一世紀的黃庭堅（1045-1105）號山谷，是型塑北宋詩歌與禪宗形態、內涵的代表。其《山谷內集》有詩逾七百首，是今人認知山谷詩學、禪學的核心文獻。該集歷來以難解而聞名，註家甚少。自古及今的華人世界內唯宋代任淵（1090？-1164？）曾遍註內集詩，又唯錢鍾書（1910-1998）選註的逾八十首為當代學界山谷詩註的典範。然而，十五世紀室町時代的日本禪僧萬里集九（1428-1507？）曾著書《帳中香》，以漢文遍註內集。萬里獨特的知識背景、闡釋立場與心態，使得該書在詮解旨趣異於華人註家的同時，尤在認識《山谷內集》中詩禪關係的問題上，深具洞察。然此書的存在及其重要性，長期未為學界所熟知。本計劃即將針對萬里集九及其《帳中香》展開首次全面研究。筆者尤其將通過檢視該書以禪解詩的獨特路徑，反思《山谷內集》固有的內典化傾向，進而重新認識黃庭堅所引領的迥異於唐代傳統的宋型詩禪新風。同時，本計劃亦將有助學界重新探索，近古以降的中日兩國在詩禪文化上曾有的互動與共性。

28602718.label: Realisation of objectives
28602718.value: 目標一：古籍整理 日本室町時代（1336-1573）中期，京都五山學問僧群之間，存在一種研讀、講授黃庭堅詩歌（又稱「山谷詩」）的風氣，持續約百年之久。五山僧是日本中世最重要的知識精英群體之一。其致力研究並傳授宋型文化巔峰之一的山谷詩，這既是日本獨有的一種文字禪風的體現，同時也是該時代日本重要的漢學研習、傳承方式之一。五山僧所用山谷詩底本，為兩宋之際任淵（生卒年不詳）《山谷詩集註》後者簡稱「任註」。該註為「宋人註宋詩」最善本之一。上述五山僧群中，萬里集九（1428-1507？）最稱翹楚。後土御門天皇長享二年（1488），萬里時年六十一歲之際，用時三年，完成任註山谷詩補註《帳中香》二十一卷。該書媒介以漢字為主，輔以極少量古日語片假名。《帳中香》是日本室町時代最重要的漢詩闡釋學結晶。它主要有一種寫本、一種刻本存世。寫本為東京東洋文庫藏萬里自筆本（足本）。刻本多處有藏，較易獲得者為東京國立公文書館藏慶長年間（1596-1615）古活字版。 如今，在若干學生助手和研究助理的協助下，主持人已初步將該書以現代標點整理完成，篇幅約120萬字。該整理本，今已投往一家中國內陸的頂級出版社，謀求出版。 目標二：日本漢學史 自少至壯，萬里集九相繼在京都五山東福寺、相國寺修行，為「藏殿」主管而司職經藏，成為學問鴻富的五山學僧。期間他接受良好的漢詩文教養，成為五山叢林主要的漢詩人之一。其漢詩文集，名《梅花無盡藏》。中年不幸親歷應仁之亂（1467），萬里從京都流落美濃國鵜沼（今岐阜縣各務原市），依靠承國寺的幫助，營構草菴「梅花無盡藏」而隱居。文明十七年（1485），萬里東游至武藏國江戶城（今東京都）盤桓三年，在芳林寺（今埼玉縣岩槻市內）旁，再次營構草菴「梅花無盡藏」，《帳中香》即成書於此。萬里特別重視從禪宗的角度解讀黃庭堅，其閱讀山谷詩有時猶如閱讀內典，其註釋山谷詩有時則猶如註經。其註釋山谷詩用力之兢兢業業，不啻視註詩為一種特殊修行，而欲藉此達到積累功德乃至懺悔之目的。萬里的多重身份認同，充分體現在「梅花無盡藏」的多重意涵之上。 如今，主持人的論文〈複調的「梅花無盡藏」：五山僧萬里集九的身份認同〉，已獲得《域外漢籍研究集刊》（CSSCI來源集刊，北京中華書局出版）的用稿通知。預計2023年上半年，該文將登載於該刊第24輯。 目標三：宋代詩學 北宋黃庭堅（1045-1105）號「山谷道人」。其詩稱「山谷詩」，乃東亞古典時代的詩學淵藪，卻典奧難讀。山谷詩分《內》《外》《別》三集，但作者本人、子姪、門生唯重《山谷內集詩》。任淵（1090？-1164）是山谷晚年流放之際的弟子。無論詮釋力或影響力，其《山谷內集詩註》都是「宋人註宋詩」典範。二十世紀學術泰斗錢鍾書（1910-1998）撰〈黃山谷詩補註〉，分見於《談藝錄》《管錐編》《宋詩選註》，意在挑戰任註。唯其著眼任註之失，僅涉及《內集》700首不足七分之一。日本室町時代禪僧萬里集九（1428-1507？）所著《帳中香》，是成書最早、影響最廣且成就最高的五山「山谷抄物」。上述三家的身份、知識結構、歷史情境、詮釋目的迥異。任註重字面、事料之出處，重編年以示本事，但礙於政情，對詩意微言欲說還休。錢註善將山谷詩置於東西方純文學脈絡，揭示獨到詩法、曲折詩旨，但觸及政治微言之際，礙於錢氏自身的文字獄環境而多諱言，亦無視其宗教性。萬里視山谷為香嚴童子，其《帳中香》以香藥、香方博喻漢詩史，予山谷詩崇高定位。他以禪解詩亦不廢以史證詩，對文學性、宗教性和政治諷喻同等重視。三家註各有目的，效果大相徑庭，共同構成一獨特的東亞漢詩闡釋傳統。 如今，該文已寫就初稿，題為〈東亞山谷詩三家註比較：北宋任淵、錢鍾書、日僧萬里集九〉。2021年5月8日，該文已通過在線方式，由主持人口頭宣讀於「東亞文化交涉學會第13屆國際學術大會」。該會議，由東京二松學社大學主辦。 目標四：宋代禪學 「退聽堂」是黃庭堅中晚年兩度以之命名的書齋兼禪房，先在北宋元祐四年之汴京，後在元符元年之戎州。元祐、元符的十數年間，其相當比例的詩歌創作和禪修實踐，在退聽堂這一特定空間展開。《退聽堂錄》是黃庭堅在元祐年間的自編詩集，是其自認及時賢公認的山谷詩代表作，也是其甥洪炎編《山谷內集》的底本之一。黃氏親為此集撰〈退聽序〉，洪炎亦有〈豫章黃先生退聽堂錄序〉。「退聽」典出《周易》艮卦，黃庭堅在保留「取靜」主旨的同時，借用《宗鏡錄》、《楞嚴經》的觀念改造其文化語境，使該典內涵由《周易》之「時運」變為佛教之禪定。洪炎編《山谷內集》，「凡詩斷自退聽始，退聽以前概不復取」，將舅父元祐元年以前所作芟減殆盡。作為山谷晚年的入室弟子，任淵同樣不註匯集元祐元年以前詩作的《山谷外集》。從《退聽堂錄》到《山谷內集》的編撰過程，帶有政治內捲、禪修內觀的傾向。這一判斷可進而解釋，為何萬里集九等日本五山僧擁有《山谷外集》《外集註》，卻只講解、註釋《內集》。在其看來，黃庭堅其人其詩已禪化、神聖化，故內集即內典，外集即外典。 如今，該文已寫就初稿，題為〈酺池寺南，退聽堂下：黃庭堅中晚年的禪修空間與《山谷内集》的編撰意圖〉。2020年11月28日，該文已通過在線方式，由主持人口頭宣讀於「2020佛教文獻與文學國際學術研討會」。該會議，由台北國立政治大學中文系主辦。

28602718.label: Major findings and research outcome
28602718.value: 第一，作為古代日本漢學史上最重要的一部黃庭堅詩註本，《帳中香》首次得以現代標點的方式，整理出來。 第二，針對東亞香文化史上存世最早的香譜類著述，洪芻的作者身份得到確認，其書首次得以正名為《香後譜》，其北宋時代的原初結構亦得以重新勾勒。 第三，作為日本室町時代最重要的漢學家之一，萬里集九之禪林藏主、漢詩人及漢詩註家的多重身份認同，首次得以清晰揭示。 第四，以東亞為視野看待黃庭堅詩歌闡釋史，則黃氏晚年入室弟子任淵、二十世紀人文學術泰斗錢鍾書及日本室町時代禪僧萬里集九，三位註者的詮釋立場及效果，首次得以比較。 第五，黃庭堅中晚年的書齋兼禪房名為「退聽堂」，其最重視的自編詩集《山谷內集》之底本原名《退聽堂錄》，個中深藏之禪學、詩學的雙重意蘊，首次得以揭示。

28602718.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

28602718.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28602718.value: 十一世紀的黃庭堅（1045-1105）號山谷，是型塑北宋詩歌與禪宗形態、內涵的代表。其《山谷內集》有詩逾七百首，是今人認知山谷詩學、禪學的核心文獻。該集歷來以難解而聞名，註家甚少。自古及今的華人世界內唯宋代任淵（1090？-1164？）曾遍註內集詩，又唯錢鍾書（1910-1998）選註的逾八十首為當代學界山谷詩註的典範。然而，十五世紀室町時代的日本禪僧萬里集九（1428-1507？）曾著書《帳中香》，以漢文遍註內集。萬里獨特的知識背景、闡釋立場與心態，使得該書在詮解旨趣異於華人註家的同時，尤在認識《山谷內集》中詩禪關係的問題上，深具洞察。此書的存在及其重要性，長期未為學界所熟知。該計劃是針對《帳中香》其書的首次全面研究。

28603218.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28603218.value: 通過任務切換提升創造力

28603218.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28603218.value: 人們習慣採用現有的知識及方法去解決新問題, 即使現有的方法並未能有效解決問題。 過份專注現有的知識的是阻礙創意的關鍵因素, 改變這習慣是提升創造力的途徑之一。 最近的研究顯示通過任務切換戓能有效防此過份專注現有的知識, 從而提升創造力。然而這些 硏究只關注任務切換如何影響解決問題的準確性及速度,並未有更詳細了解什麼時侯及情況適合任務切換。而且，這些研究只使用單一的問題, 對於任務切換能否提升其他問題仍是未知數。 這擬議研究將評估任務切換在解決各種問題的效果。 這項目將收集定量和定性的數據以幫助更清楚了解任務切換的好處。跟據收集的數據，我們將建立一個能實針對個人解決問題的進對並按時提啟動任務切換的電腦系統。這擬議研究將在理論和實踐上有重要貢獻。這擬議項目不但有助解釋任務切換如何提升創造還能提出優化任務切換的方法。最後, 這擬議研究將會建立一個能實針對個人解決問題的進對並按時提啟動任務切換的電腦系統。考慮到人界面的使用越來越多，這系統將可應用在 許多領域。

28604318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28604318.value: 低關係流動性的環境可能促進敵對關係

28604318.label: Project Objectives
28604318.value: To test whether low-relational-mobility contexts that promote harmony can also promote the existence of enemyship gradually across time points, and whether this pattern would be moderated by interpersonal tension To investigate whether the influence of low relational mobility on the existence of enemyship will be explained by enhancing the perception of social embeddedness To investigate whether reminding people of the long-term consequences of leaving conflicts unresolved can eliminate the influence of relational mobility on enemyship
rows: To test whether low-relational-mobility contexts that promote harmony can also promote the existence of enemyship gradually across time points, and whether this pattern would be moderated by interpersonal tension
To investigate whether the influence of low relational mobility on the existence of enemyship will be explained by enhancing the perception of social embeddedness
To investigate whether reminding people of the long-term consequences of leaving conflicts unresolved can eliminate the influence of relational mobility on enemyship

28604318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28604318.value: The project aims to examine the influence of relational mobility, defined as the number of opportunities in the environment for people to freely form new social relationships and forgo undesired ones, on the existence of enemyship, a hostile relationship inducing intense negative emotions. Social relationships are important to humans. Surprisingly though, in psychological research, personal enemyship, a hostile social relationship that occurs across cultures and has detrimental influences on the well-being of individuals, has not received as much attention as positive relationships. A few previous studies have suggested that low relational mobility may promote the existence of enemies as well as promoting harmony. However, no causal evidence is available. In addition, prior work has not differentiated whether low relational mobility promotes a stronger concept of enemyship or actually increases the existence of enemies in reality. Moreover, no research examines when low relational mobility might be more likely to promote the existence of enemies than promote harmony. Little is known about the underlying mechanism of how low relational mobility leads to the existence of enemies across time points. Finally, research into how to reduce the likelihood of the existence of enemies is rare, even though the existence of enemies is associated with intense negative emotions. This project proposes to overcome these limitations. We plan to adopt manipulation designs as well as a longitudinal design to obtain causal evidence for the influence of low relational mobility on the existence of enemyship and the underlying mechanism of high social embeddedness across time points. In addition, we will test how effectively enemyship is detected in low versus high relational mobility contexts. Finally, we will also explore whether reminders of the dangers of leaving conflicts unresolved will eliminate the negative impact of low relational mobility on the existence of enemies. These proposed studies should contribute to not only a better understanding of both the bright and dark sides of social relationships but also represent an advancement of the socio-ecological approach in psychological research. Furthermore, searching for a way to eliminate the negative impact of low relational mobility on social relationships may shed light on how to improve individual well-being. 本研究項目將探討關係流動性對敵對關係產生的影響。關係流動性的定義為環境中人們可以自由形成新的社會關係或捨棄不受歡迎的社會關係的機會。社會關係對人類很重要。然而令人驚訝的是，在心理學研究中，個人的敵對關係，即一種對不同文化背景的人都產生不良影響的社會關係，並沒有像正面的社會關係那樣得到很多關注。一些研究表明低關係流動性促進和諧的同時也可能促進敵人的存在。但是以往研究沒有提供因果關係的證據，也沒有區分究竟低關係流動性會促進更強的敵人概念或是促進敵對關係的實際產生。另外，以往研究沒有考察低關係流動性何時更有可能促進敵人的存在而不是促進和諧。關於低關係流動性如何導致敵對關係產生的潛在機制，所知甚少。最後，即使敵人的存在與負面情緒有很大關連，很少研究探討如何降低敵人存在的可能性。本研究項目將會探討這些問題。我們計劃採用操縱設計和縱向設計研究以探討低關係流動性和敵對關係產生的因果關係以及其影響機制。同時，我們將探討敵對關係在低關係流動性與高關係流動性的環境中如何被探測。我們也會探討提醒人們未解決衝突的長期負面影響是否能消除低關係流動性對敵人存在的影響。這些研究將有助更好理解社會關係的明暗兩面，推進在心理學研究中使用社會生態學方法。 尋找消除低關係流動性對社會關係的負面影響也可能幫助了解如何改善個人幸福感。

28604318.label: Realisation of objectives
28604318.value: This project aims to further enhance our understanding of the effect of relational mobility on people’s interpersonal relationships. Specifically, we focused on testing whether low-relational-mobility contexts would promote the existence of enemies, and if yes, when this pattern would be stronger and what would explain these processes. Adopting a multi-method approach, we conducted different studies to examine these questions. Realization of Objective 1: We have empirically tested whether low-relational-mobility contexts (vs. high-relational-mobility contexts) would promote the existence of enemies and whether these patterns would be moderated by interpersonal tension. The results revealed some supportive evidence for the causal role of relational mobility on the formation of enemyships. Interestingly, we also found a significant moderating effect of gender, which showed stronger patterns among female participants. However, these moderation patterns were not consistently observed across studies. Regarding the moderating effect of interpersonal tension, we observed a significant negative correlation between relational mobility and the likelihood of enemyship formation in the low-tension scenarios but not in the high-tension scenarios. However, these results did not reach a statistical significance for the moderation effect of interpersonal tension. Realization of Objective 2: We measured participants’ social embeddedness and conducted analyses to explore its mediating role in the relationship between relational mobility and perception of enemyships. Some evidence demonstrated a positive relationship between social embeddedness (or interdependence) and stronger perceptions of enemyship formation. Interestingly, the results showed that participants in the high-relational-mobility contexts reported a higher level of social embeddedness (or interdependence). These results suggested that other mechanisms were involved in the influence of relational mobility on the formation of enemyships. Realization of Objective 3: In the study, we randomly assigned the participants to either the condition of reminding them of the long-term consequences of leaving conflicts unresolved or the control condition. We examined whether it would affect the relationship between relational mobility and perception of enemyships. The results did not provide reliable evidence to support the moderating effect of the provision of reminders.

28604318.label: Major findings and research outcome
28604318.value: This project aims to deepen the understanding of the effect of relational mobility on people’s interpersonal relationships with a specific focus on enemyships. First, we found some supportive evidence showing that low-relational-mobility contexts (vs. high-relational-mobility contexts) were more likely to promote the existence of enemyship. These patterns were not significantly moderated by interpersonal tension in conflict scenarios and a reminder of the long-term consequences of leaving conflicts unresolved (Li, in preparation). Second, consistent with our expectations, we found that perceived social embeddedness was positively associated with the perceptions of the existence of enemyships. Moreover, interestingly, we found participants in the high-relational-mobility contexts perceived a higher level of social embeddedness, which was supported by subjective and objective evidence (Li, in preparation; Li, Wang, & Lin, 2022). We found that participants who perceived a low level of relational mobility in a given context reported a greater level of interdependence among individuals in a given context (Li, in preparation). We also found that the manipulated high-relational-mobility contexts facilitated greater integration of multiple social networks, and these divergent patterns started at an initial stage and got stabilized very fast over time (Li, Wang, & Lin, 2022). Furthermore, we found that the effect of mobility on people’s interpersonal strategies may be shaped by other factors. The accompany of significant others was found to increase the positive affect of people with greater mobility, which was associated with their reduced motivation to expand social networks (Li, Li, & Lou, 2022). More broadly, the project also revealed evidence to support the substantial role of environmental mobility in shaping people’s psychological processes beyond interpersonal contexts. We found a significant interaction between social mobility and individual characteristics (e.g., fear of failure) in predicting people’s psychological well-being (Lou & Li, under review). These findings were published in peer-refereed international journals in psychology, including the Asian Journal of Social Psychology and Current Psychology. Some of the findings were presented at international conferences, including the 13th and 14th Biennial Conference of the Asian Association of Social Psychology.

28604318.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28604318.value: The current project showed that people from high-relational-mobility contexts reported higher levels of social embeddedness, and higher levels of social embeddedness were associated with greater perceptions of enemyship formation. In other words, social embeddedness did not help explain that participants from low-relational-mobility contexts reported greater perceptions of enemyship formation. Further studies may further explore potential mechanisms in elucidating the negative link between low relational mobility and perception of enemyship formation. Additionally, future studies may extend the obtained findings to other domains of interpersonal relationships. For instance, it would be interesting to explore whether high-relational-mobility contexts would promote higher levels of social embeddedness, thereby promoting higher levels of generalized trust in these contexts. Finally, the current project recruited only Chinese participants. With considering the powerful role of cultural contexts observed in previous studies, it would be worthwhile to examine the generalizability of the current findings in societies with different cultural heritage.

28604318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28604318.value: The current research obtained some evidence showing that lower levels of environmental relational mobility increased people’s perception of the existence of enemies in general. Moreover, perceiving greater social embeddedness was also positively associated with greater perceptions of the existence of enemies. Through exploring when and why environmental relational mobility affects the existence of enemyship, the obtained findings advanced our existing knowledge of social relationships by highlighting the power of external, socioecological environments. Specifically, the current project advanced current theories of enemyships, which received relatively little attention relative to other types of interpersonal relationships. It also created new avenues for future studies to identify psychological mechanisms as well as the boundary conditions underlying the environmental influences in social relationships.

28605318.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28605318.value: 教師領導: 華人社會學校如何通過專業學習社群增强教師領導能力

28605318.label: Project Objectives
28605318.value: Determine the degree to which teacher dispositions, PLCs, principal leadership, and school banding are linked to teacher leadership. Gain insights from principals’ and teachers’ perspectives, and teachers’ everyday PLC experiences, to explain teacher leadership outcomes. Examine the situated conceptualization of teacher leadership in the context of hierarchical cultures.
rows: Determine the degree to which teacher dispositions, PLCs, principal leadership, and school banding are linked to teacher leadership.
Gain insights from principals’ and teachers’ perspectives, and teachers’ everyday PLC experiences, to explain teacher leadership outcomes.
Examine the situated conceptualization of teacher leadership in the context of hierarchical cultures.

28605318.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28605318.value: To stay ahead of rapidly changing educational demands, Hong Kong’s schools need effective teacher leadership that can navigate professional hierarchies to improve student learning. Classroom teachers, even those without formal leadership titles, require informal leadership skills or the ability to influence educational decisions on student learning. Arguments have been made that teachers may acquire informal leadership capabilities through professional learning communities (PLCs). However, it is challenging to maximise this capacity of PLCs in highly hierarchical cultures. Studies show that informal teacher leadership eludes Hong Kong schools despite increased collaboration among teachers. This study will investigate how school type, principals, and teacher dispositions may modify the potential for teacher leadership, and aims to identify how PLCs can mediate these factors to empower the leadership skills of the classroom teacher. The mixed-methods study involves: (Phase 1) a quantitative survey of teachers to examine the interrelationship between teacher leadership and moderating factors; (Phase 2) qualitative case studies to explain these links. In Phase 1, schools will be selected to equally represent all school bands to study school differences. Structural equation modelling will analyse the moderating effects of principal leadership and teacher dispositions on teacher leadership outcomes, mediated by the teachers’ PLC participation. In Phase 2, three schools from different school bands will be selected as case studies from survey results. As part of this naturalistic case study design, schools will decide which existing collaborative practices best represent PLCs in their schools, so that principals and researchers may jointly identify suitable observation sites. Observations of teachers-in-action in PLCs will be complemented by first-hand accounts from focus groups with the teachers observed, and from interviews with principals. Qualitative data will be analysed via grounded theory approaches. The analysis will be supported by fieldwork templates and observation protocols to guide coding procedures, and will focus on the role of relationships in structuring teacher leadership outcomes. A theoretical framework will be developed from the synergized analysis of mixed-methods data to explain cultural influences that moderate teacher leadership in PLCs. This study will deepen the understanding of the challenges to empowering informal teacher leadership in highly hierarchical cultural contexts. By identifying moderating factors of teacher leadership, insights are sought regarding cultural influences on teacher leadership, and how existing PLC practices can be improved. The findings will contribute to future studies of how Chinese hierarchical school systems (e.g., self-managed Hong Kong and centralized-control Singapore) compare, building on previous studies. 香港學校需要教師領導，以助學生學習 ，並於快速變化的教育需求中保持領先地位。課堂教師雖無正式領導角色，但仍需有能力影響關乎學生學習的教學決定。然而，專業學習社群能否在香港華人社會背景下增强教師領導能力？儘管教師之間的合作有所增加，但研究指出: 課堂教師仍需要增强領導能力。我們的研究計劃從學校類型、校長領導和教師特徵三方面，了解如何協助課堂教師專業發展，從而提供有關建議，以改善香港學校的專業學習社群。 這研究涉及: (第一階段)全校教師 - 量化調查教師領導與多方面因素之間的相互關係 ; (第二階段）限定選定的學校與校內專業學習社群 - 通過對所選團隊進行錄影和焦點小組訪談，進行質性案例研究解釋這些聯繫。我們將確保每個學校組別 (第一、二、三組別學校)都有機會參加這項研究。在第一階段，我們將用結構方程模型 (structural equation modelling) 來理解校長領導和教師特徵對教師在專業學習社群內增强領導能力的影響。在第二階段，我們將從參與量度調查的學校中選擇較少數的學校作為我們的質性案例學校。我們將就學校現有有關專業學習社群的日程實踐進行錄影，以記錄教師們的日常會議日程，此不需要教師做任何額外工作（如: 進行額外的會議）。教師和校長只需要在研究的第二階段參加額外的焦點小組訪談。我們的研究組將採用紮根理論質性分析 (grounded theory analysis) 探索教師與教師之間的協作關係對於教師領導有什麼影響。我們希望通過研究成果，從中建立有關理論框架，來解釋華人社會文化對於專業學習社群內增强教師領導能力的影響。 本研究將加深對華人社會文化背景下教師領導能力所面臨的挑戰的認識。通過了解多方面影響教師領導力因素，我們探討如何改進當前專業學習社群的實踐。本研究結果將有助於未來華人社會學校系統的比較研究。

28605318.label: Realisation of objectives
28605318.value: The objectives of the study has been achieved in the following aspects: Objective 1: Determine the degree to which teacher dispositions, PLCs, principal leadership, and school banding are linked to teacher leadership. Lee (2022) employs the concept of professional capital (of which teacher leadership is a part of the measurements) to determine teachers’ values profiles of high, medium and low professional capital in the respective contexts. Medium professional capital Hong Kong teachers’ values matched Singapore’s, but teachers in other clusters are nuanced. Compared to Singapore teachers with similar levels of professional capital, high professional capital Hong Kong teachers have higher uncertainty avoidance, while low professional capital teachers are the opposite. In Hong Kong, high uncertainty avoidance values positively influence teacher leadership and focus on student learning. Nevertheless, as with their Singapore counterparts, high professional capital Hong Kong teachers have low power distance and high risk-taking values. This paper raises awareness regarding policy’s influence in cultivating teachers’ values and their transformational change capabilities. When teacher leadership in Hong Kong is promoted in a loosely defined school-based management context, teachers are more likely to feel uncertain about how change can be achieved. Those with higher uncertainty avoidance values have stronger potential to be endorsed by colleagues who need a clear purpose for collaboration, and so are more likely to be cultivated into HKPChigh teachers in a context of uncertainty. In contrast, SGPChigh teachers represent Singapore teachers who aspire to “loosen up” and embrace a diversity of professional practices with collaborative learning within a structured policy context. Lee and Ip (2021) show that PLCs are highly influential and very powerful platforms in developing informal teacher leadership. In turn, teacher leadership has a high positive influence on teachers’ focus on student learning. Importantly, the results show teacher leadership has a strong positive influence on teachers’ focus on student learning. Student achievement results can only tell a part of the story. In this study, the results directly informed what teachers are doing and can do for student learning to be improved. Principals in the study hope to do more in empowering teacher leadership to boost school improvement. Their instructional leadership has a high positive influence on PLC capacity. Middle leaders 5 (e.g., subject heads) have a moderate positive influence in this aspect. Impact: The research highlights to schools strategic areas of concern needing their attention, and concrete examples of how research recommendations can be practiced. The results support school leaders’ proposals to their school management committee for a strategic plan that develops subject heads’ capabilities. Objective 2: Gain insights from principals’ and teachers’ perspectives, and teachers’ everyday PLC experiences, to explain teacher leadership outcomes. The study discovered nuances between schools in how principals and teachers perceive and leverage PLCs, resulting in differentiated teacher leadership outcomes by school banding. Lee and Chiu (2021) found that band one principals see PLCs as platforms for developing both formal and informal teacher leaders. Middle leaders (formal teacher leaders, mostly subject heads) are not just PLC leaders who mentor other teachers in their teacher leadership and professional development. They are also learning transformational leadership by leading change collaboratively with colleagues. They likewise develop instructional leadership by learning from informal teacher leaders, who may have more solid subject knowledge and classroom experiences than formal teacher leaders who have their attention mainly on school administration. Band two principals see PLCs as platforms for developing teacher collaboration in supporting student achievement in key subjects, such as Mathematics and Science. They see the key disadvantage in students’ English proficiency, as their students may have weaker English proficiency than band one school students, as the HKDSE is administered in English. Band three principals and middle leaders experience a disconnect between their visions for teacher leadership development via PLCs and teachers’ commitment toward these initiatives. On the one hand, school leaders hope to leverage PLCs to promote teacher professional development (e.g., information sharing, analyze HKDSE results to develop relevant teaching strategies for their students, and develop teacher initiatives for promoting student whole person development). Yet, they see a lack of commitment among teachers towards these initiatives. School leaders attribute the challenges to structural issues (e.g., disadvantaged funding for band three schools, so funds for teacher recruitment are reserved for teachers who are close to retirement, while remaining funding could only be afforded for hiring young teachers on one-year contracts). Impact: There remains space for deepening the investigation of school banding effects on leadership at multiple levels, and how organizational belonging to banded schools shape the identity of educators, and how such influences are moderated by individual demographical attributes. For example, Lee (2021), and Lee and King (2021) provide initial insights into the challenges posed against change leadership capacities by teachers’ home language pose for those who lack proficiency in the dominant language(s). Objective 3: Examine the situated conceptualization of teacher leadership in the context of hierarchical cultures. In Lee and Ip (2021), we found that in Chinese hierarchical cultures, teachers look more to principals for teacher leadership development than middle leaders. Given the sensitivity of teachers in Chinese contexts toward hierarchy, principals need to explore means to level up middle leadership capacities. This will empower middle leaders to exercise their leadership to support teacher leadership development more effectively. Extending Lee’s (2021) findings that heterogeneous PLC groupings have stronger capacities than homogeneous groups in transcending hierarchical divisions between teachers and middle leaders, schools can leverage heterogeneous grouping arrangements to develop both teacher and middle leadership capacities. Principal Investigator Lee’s research interest in Chinese hierarchical societies (Lee, 2022; Lee & Lee, 2018) has given rise to a growing interest in the influence of cultural values on other aspects of teaching and learning. The findings have produced insights into comparisons on the relationships between values and levels of professional capital in segments of the teaching population in Hong Kong and Singapore, building on previous studies (Lee, 2022). Research in this study has also given rise to proposals for future studies of how Hong Kong and Singapore compare as Chinese hierarchical school systems. Impact: Applications for extended studies demonstrated through applications for research funding (RGC GRF 18616322 and RGC YCRG C8022-22Y). Research insights have been scaled and translated into professional development seminars and webinars over the course of the years of in research work on the ECS, demonstrating knowledge transfer and community engagement (see Part C). Research work on hierarchical Chinese societies also extended to other domains in the course of ECS research work, such as work on the nuanced impact of hierarchical inequality on different segments of the student population. For example, power distance do not always produce deleterious effects on all students’ financial literacy learning in Hong Kong (Ho & Lee, 2021). Nevertheless, differentiated access in financial literacy learning among students due to school banding and unequal language access are causes for concern regarding social equity (Ho & Lee, 2020; 2022). Impact: Collaboration with likeminded colleagues to grow research interest in our respective research domains gave rise to sustained new collaborations (e.g., deepening research collaboration with Ho on Hong Kong and Singapore teachers’ pedagogical identity and practice upon successful attainment of GRF 2021/22, and on developing identities that promote embracing diversity as a strength in Hong Kong and Singapore upon successful attainment of YCRG 2022).

28605318.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28605318.value: Hong Kong’s schools need effective teacher leadership that can navigate professional hierarchies to improve student learning to stay ahead of rapidly changing educational demands. However, this capacity of PLCs may be challenging to replicate in highly hierarchical cultural contexts. This proposal investigates the moderating factors of school type, principals, and teacher dispositions on teacher leadership, to identify how PLCs can mediate these factors to empower the leadership skills of the classroom teacher. This study has provided a nuanced understanding of the conditions and challenges in empowering informal teacher leadership among different population segments in highly hierarchical cultural contexts. While the medium professional capital middle majority segments tend to concur with attributes prevalently found in the literature, high and low professional teachers differ. By identifying the factors that moderate teacher leadership and distinct attributes of different segments of the teacher population, we have a better understand of how cultural influences impact on the teacher leadership of different teacher segments, and how existing PLC practices can be improved. The findings have promoted knowledge dissemination, forged further research developments, and contributed to knowledge transfer, leveraging on the insights into how Chinese hierarchical school systems compare, such as between Hong Kong and Singapore.

28606418.label: Project Objectives
28606418.value: This research aims to investigate how contemporary craft practices can be juxtaposed in the stream of the maker movement driven by the digital fabrication technologies with a focus on Hong Kong’s maker communities. The objectives of the research are: Investigate contemporary craft practices with a focus on the changes derived by the democratization of digital fabrication technologies and re-juxtapose them in new groups of makers and creative industries. Identify benefits and challenges in the integration of traditional and digital craft practice and describe the potential development of craft within the creative industry in Hong Kong. 28606418.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28606418.value: The notion of craft has for a long time been closely tied to making objects using materials produced through handmade processes. It has often been seen as activities performed by two different groups of makers: professional artisans; and do-it-yourself (DIY) amateur hobbyists. However, the emergence of new digital fabrication technologies in recent years has brought a significant shift in the maker group and culture. With the new digital means of making objects, theoretically, anyone can customize and produce one’s own goods. The concept has been embodied through the maker movement which refers to a cultural trend that places a high value on making physical things using digital technologies and craft skills. The idea of digital craft has been present for the past two decades. Individual practitioners started producing work with hybrid craft techniques, and proved the potential benefits of digital craft in expanding creativity and appealing to a wider audience. However, examinations of how the new technologies will affect the craft community and modes of production and distribution in the craft industry have been scarce. In response, this research aims to investigate how digital fabrication technologies influence craft practices as part of the maker movement. It also aims to identify challenges and opportunities for professional and amateur makers involved in conventional craft practices. Explorative qualitative studies will be carried out through digital fabrication workshops with twenty local makers. Through participant observation, pre-workshop and post-workshop interviews, and artifact (workshop outcome) analysis, the purpose of the study is to explore how different groups of makers’ practice and value perceptions are changed by the introduction of new digital tools. Additionally, the study will address issues that need to be resolved in both practical and socio-cultural contexts. It is expected that the findings from the study will have implications for the following aspects: It will provide an understanding of the significance of maker culture as socio-cultural practices and as a means to foster creativity and related industries. 長久以來，手工藝的概念和以手作材料製作物品密不可分。一般認為，手工藝實作者包含兩個群體：職業工匠和業餘DIY愛好者。然而，近年興起的數位製造技術為製造文化與實踐帶來了深刻的變革。有了嶄新的數位製造技術，在第三次工業革命的時代，理論上任何人都可以量身製作自己的產品。然而，儘管眾多媒體報導和研究皆提及新數位工具能帶來潛在機會，仍然只有少數製造者有機會學習和體驗數位製造技術。這是因為相關知識和技巧的傳播研究仍處於早期階段。尤其是具有手工藝背景的製造者通常不太有數位製造的經驗，也較少接觸近年的轉變。有鑑於當前環境，本研究試圖探討數位製作技術如何影響製作文化和實踐。另外，本研究也試圖釐清此項變革對於從事傳統手工藝實作的專業及業餘製造者而言，帶來怎樣的挑戰與機會。本研究將採質性個案研究，為二十位本地製造者舉辦數位製作工作坊。透過參與式觀察、工作坊舉行前後之訪談與工藝品（工作坊成果）分析，本研究將探討不同製造者群體在實踐與價值感知上，如何受到新進科技的影響。此外，本研究也將處理在實作情境和社會文化情境下需要解決的問題。本研究成果預期將帶來以下層向之意涵。本研究將從社會文化實踐和培育創意與相關產業的角度，闡明製作者文化的重要性。另外，由於數位素養在後數位時代不可或缺，因此本研究將分析新型數位工具所帶來的挑戰與機會，成果將有助於研發提升數位素養的教學材料。

28606418.label: Realisation of objectives
28606418.value: The PI has achieved most project objectives stated in the initial proposal. The first objective was to investigate contemporary craft practices focusing on the changes derived from the democratization of digital fabrication technologies and re-juxtapose them in new groups of makers and creative industries. The PI invited 18 craft practitioners based in Hong Kong, both professionals, and amateurs, who have no or little experience in digital fabrication technologies, and conducted a month-long workshop to identify their perception of the potential benefits and shortcomings of the DFT. The workshop consisted of 12 hrs of lecture and hands-on practice over four weeks. The interviews(pre- and post- workshop) with the workshop participants revealed that craft practitioners in Hong Kong had had little exposure to opportunities to learn DFT. However, the majority had a positive outlook on the DFT's impact on crafts. Through literature review and case studies of contemporary craft resources and exhibition records, it was found that contemporary craft practices have substantially evolved into hybrid ones. The changes were detected in several aspects. The term 'craftsperson' is no longer solely used to define craftspeople's occupation; instead, craftspeople tend to identify themselves as a designer-maker, designer, maker, or artists capable of crossing boundaries between different fields. The ways contemporary craft practitioners run businesses have extended into hybrid modes(online and offline), various scales, materials(mixed media), and manufacturing methods(handmaking & digital making). The second objective was to identify the benefits and challenges in integrating traditional and digital craft practice and describe the potential development of craft within the creative industry in Hong Kong. It was found that the craftspeople felt that DFT would be beneficial to all, especially in enhancing productivity and creativity. By shortening the time for prototyping or directly reproducing parts, labor costs can be reduced while the production quantity can be increased. The participants also mentioned the potential improvement in artistic exploration and affordable customization options. After the workshop, the participants identified the potential advantage for the craft practitioners to adopt the technologies since general makers who do not have a good understanding of materials and making processes cannot be fully benefited from manufacturing with DFT. However, in order to apply to their practice, the research participants noted that an intensive tailored training program with experienced teachers in digital crafts would be necessary for formal and informal institutes. The third objective was to explore new social, cultural, economic, and aesthetic values generated by the maker movement and how they relate to both individualistic craft practice and the community. With just a few cases of practitioners who run businesses with products made with DFT, generalizations could not be made. Also, a long-term impact could not be measured in this cross-sectional study with data derived from the one-month-long workshop. However, overall the perception of the craft practitioners on DFT's impact on economic aspects was found to be positive. In addition to the potential artistic and economic developments brought by the integration of DFT into craft practices, the research participants emphasized and anticipated the enriched value of craft labor and crafted objects amid the rise of the maker population. The craftspeople expected that the public's making experiences with and without digital technologies would enhance the value of craft in society. The PI sought to invite craftspeople to participate in the exhibition to disseminate the findings and produce local cases of craft practitioners using DFT. However, due to a small pool of potential participants in Hong Kong, local and international artists and designers were invited to showcase their work involving the creative use of digital fabrication technologies. The outputs from the exhibition, including an exhibition booklet, artist videos, artist talks, and a guided tour, were used as educational resources. To host the art exhibition, the PI received additional funding from the Hong Kong Arts Development Council since the allocated education plan budget could not cover the expenses for the exhibition implementation. The PI used the HKADC grant to cover a part of the research support staff salary and general expenses. There were two significant challenges in carrying out this research project. Due to a lack of existing documents about craftspeople and industry demographic data, and craft-focused governmental bodies, reliance on the networks based in academic institutions was inevitable. In 2019-20, due to protests in Hong Kong, it was challenging to recruit workshop participants and ask them to commute and attend the workshop for a month. The sample size and workshop duration were reduced. The PI acknowledged the RGC in the research outputs(conference paper, exhibition materials), but one acknowledgment is missing in the published research paper due to the journal publisher's mistake.
